title: Murakami’s Dream
text: # Murakami’s Dream ## The question and the knots under consideration For a knot $K$ and an integer $N\geq2$, Kashaev’s invariant $K_N(K)$ is a complex number obtained by evaluating a finite sum at a root of unity. We use the reduced normalization, in which the unknot has value one. If the knot complement admits a complete hyperbolic metric of finite volume, the volume conjecture predicts that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] The left side measures exponential growth: a value of the form $N^a e^{NV/(2\pi)}$ has limit $V$, because the polynomial factor disappears after taking the logarithm and dividing by $N$. The right side is the volume of the knot complement. The knot remains removed from the three-sphere. This project studies the conjecture by cutting knot diagrams into tangles and keeping their finite evaluations and geometric face identifications together. One construction starts from a planar diagram encoded by a simple triangulation of the sphere. Other results treat **Conway algebraic, or arborescent, knots**, built by joining and turning rational tangles. The planar construction gives broad families after a specified finite decoration; the tree results also give explicit degree and twist bounds. The [manuscript](manuscript.md) contains completed proofs with their exact scope. This guide also explains the research approaches that have not yet produced a general theorem. Start with [methods and approaches](methods.md) for the definitions, examples, and literature behind Fourier energy, weighted Cauchy, angle optimization, quantum recurrences, and torsors. The [notation chapter](notation.md) fixes the symbols and normalizations used throughout. ## A general planar construction Choose a finite simple triangulation of the sphere, and pair adjacent triangles so that each triangle occurs once. The pairs specify crossing-circle tangles and their strand connections in the three-sphere. There is an explicit procedure that adds finitely many tangles on both sides of each original crossing circle. The numbers added are even, and the new pieces have odd crossing parity, so a chosen knot pairing is preserved. For every resulting decorated diagram, independently sufficiently long positive or negative twists at all original and added regions give the volume equality above. No tree decomposition of the tangle operations is required. The added tangles generally change the knot; the theorem does not remove them from its conclusion. The [construction and proof](results.md#decorating-a-planar-diagram) explain how a common circle packing determines the decoration and how its inequalities bound the full finite invariant. The geometric part constructs the smooth fillings of the auxiliary cusps while leaving the main knot cusp complete. ![A triangle is subdivided by an added circle, preserving the old matching edge and adding a new one.](../figures/balanced-terminal-fans.png) ## The ordered-tree constructions For the specified construction with an integer braid at every vertex of an ordered tree with at least one edge, a [single twist threshold works for every finite tree](results.md#one-twist-threshold-for-arbitrarily-many-tangles): \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27}. \] The integer \(n_v\) counts signed half-twists. The actual endpoint pairing must form one knot, with no additional closed component. The threshold is independent of the size, depth and degrees of the tree. A more flexible sufficient condition lets each vertex have either this twist magnitude or degree \(d_v\ge2^{28}\). The entire diagram is still fixed before the quantum level grows. ## Stacking and turning the tree pieces A two-string tangle consists of two arcs in a ball, with four specified endpoints on its boundary. Draw the ball as a rectangle with two endpoints at the top and two at the bottom. There are two operations. To stack two tangles, put one above the other and join the adjacent pairs of endpoints without adding crossings. To turn a tangle, rotate its entire diagram through a quarter-turn. The order of the pieces matters. Start with an elementary box containing two strands with an integer number of half twists, and turn that box through a quarter-turn. Make finitely many such pieces, each with its own integer twist number. Repeated stacking and turning gives larger tangles. Finally, stack two such tangles and close the diagram by connecting the bottom-left endpoint to the top-left endpoint outside the box, and likewise on the right. This is the *cylindrical closure* used here. To decide whether the result is a knot, follow all strand connections and count any circles already closed inside intermediate boxes as well as those formed by the final closure. The construction can have arbitrarily many pieces and arbitrarily deep nesting. It is recorded by a finite ordered tree: its leaves are the elementary twist pieces, and its internal operations are stacking and turning. A tree in this description records a construction; it is not a drawing of the knot. The [manuscript guide](manuscript.md) gives drawings, worked examples, and the precise recursive class treated in the paper. The [results chapter](results.md) also explains the larger class covered by the companion theorem. ## The volume theorem and its quantifiers The [net-twist theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) first simplifies the actual tangle diagram. Integral twist boxes that can be brought together are combined by adding their signed twist numbers. Moving a twist box past a tangle carries a specified half-turn of that tangle, which the reduction retains. The result is either an elementary two-strand braid closure or a presentation passing the strict angle-feasibility test described in the [results chapter](results.md). For each fixed input construction $\mathcal E$, the reduction partitions the original pieces into disjoint groups $B_1,\ldots,B_s$. Their surviving twist numbers are \[ W_j=\sum_{i\in B_j}n_i. \] The groups are determined before the integer weights are chosen. The order of some surviving pieces can depend on their parities. There is a finite threshold $B(\mathcal E)$ such that, on a non-elementary output, the conditions \[ |W_j|>B(\mathcal E)\qquad(1\leq j\leq s) \] and the requirement that the actual closed link be a knot imply hyperbolicity and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log|K_N(K_{\mathcal E}(\mathbf n))| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathcal E}(\mathbf n)). \] The elementary output is the closure of a single two-strand braid, hence a torus link or knot; it is excluded from this positive-volume theorem. On a strict output the different net twists may have independent signs and incomparable magnitudes. Original weights within one group can cancel, so their individual largeness does not suffice. For example, two boxes with weights $a+2m$ and $-2m$ combine to the fixed weight $a$, however large $|m|$ becomes. Choose the entire construction and all twist integers first; then let $N$ grow through the positive integers. The threshold may depend on the construction, but is uniform over its finitely many parity choices. Neither the tree nor its weights grow with $N$. This covers arbitrarily large fixed compositions when their reduced twists satisfy the bound. It does not cover arbitrary short twists or classify every arborescent knot up to all possible presentation changes. The earlier chapters of the TeX manuscript prove an included family; the companion strict-tree estimates and exact tangle reduction give this extension. A further manuscript chapter proves the quantitative circle-tree result below. The [manuscript page](manuscript.md) distinguishes those scopes. The [closure extension](../../notes/actual_conway_arbitrary_closure_volume.md) also permits cap closures, which join each upper and lower endpoint pair, and twist sums that vanish exactly. Removing these zero sums can split the diagram into connected-sum factors. If the input is hyperbolic and every surviving strict factor has long net twists, the proof shows that just one strict factor remains and all others are unknots. The original knot is isotopic to that covered factor. The [results chapter](results.md#cap-closures-and-exact-cancellations) gives the precise criterion, including a sufficient condition on the original subset sums. ## Numerical conditions for trees of crossing circles In this construction every product junction contains an integer two-strand braid. To describe its geometry, place a crossing circle around that braid and retain its parity as a half twist. Let \(d_v\) be the number of incident tree edges and \(n_v\) its signed crossing power. The [directed subtree theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) proves the actual hyperbolic knot-volume equality when, independently at each vertex, \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27}\quad\text{or}\quad d_v\ge2^{28}, \] and the original strand pairing gives one knot. Its more detailed finite criterion assigns a separate decay bound to each subtree; the displayed condition is a simple consequence of that criterion. The degree alternative allows short and zero powers. For example, start with any fixed ordered core whose strand pairing is a knot. At an existing product slot at each vertex, insert an even stack of \(B\ge2^{28}\) new terminal pieces, each with an odd power of magnitude at least \(2^{27}+1\). The stack has the same endpoint pairing as two straight strands and creates no internal circle. The resulting knot satisfies the theorem. This is a way to construct new covered knots; it generally changes the knot represented by the original core. The [summed criterion](../../notes/actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) gives a different sufficient test: \[ \sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}\le2^{-25}. \] For a tree with \(E\) edges, every \(|n_v|\ge8192\sqrt E\) suffices. This can be numerically better for a particular diagram. The earlier local condition is also retained in its original note. All these theorems keep the tree and the twist integers fixed while \(N\) grows through both parities. Both the finite-sum estimate and its geometric interpretation are proved. The original octahedral pieces deform with their marked filling curves, and the final metric is smooth on the original knot complement. The main knot cusp remains unfilled. The [results chapter](results.md) gives the exact scope and the [manuscript guide](manuscript.md) locates the full proofs. ## Why the proof has both an analytic and a geometric part After the exact tangle reduction, the analytic and geometric proof begins by removing the surviving long twists and placing an auxiliary circle around the two strands in each twist region. The resulting *augmented link* remembers where the twists will be restored. Assigning integer labels, called colors, to these auxiliary circles produces a finite evaluation depending on those labels. The notes call this evaluation the *source*. At each level $N$, the source is an exact finite sum. Its leading exponential growth is described by a real function of the summation indices divided by $N$. Maximizing that function produces angles for ideal hyperbolic cells. The geometric part of the proof shows that these cells fit together with precisely the face identifications of the augmented link complement. This establishes which manifold supplies the volume. Restoring the twists requires another finite sum over the auxiliary colors. Its terms have complex phases, so their absolute values alone do not determine its growth. The analytic part proves a nonzero leading contribution and bounds the rest of this whole sum. It also follows the chosen geometric structure through the fillings that restore the twists. Filling an auxiliary crossing circle means removing that auxiliary cusp by attaching a solid torus with the specified slope. The cusp belonging to the knot is left unfilled. Consequently the final critical value is the volume of the resulting **knot complement**, rather than the volume of the augmented link used at the beginning. ![Exact tangle reduction, finite-sum estimates, and identification of the knot complement volume.](../figures/research-map.png) The [mechanism chapter](mechanism.md) develops the finite sum and its estimates. The [geometry chapter](geometry.md) explains the ideal cells, peripheral curves, and the volume comparison. These two parts are both needed: constructing a hyperbolic metric does not by itself estimate the quantum invariant, and estimating a finite sum does not by itself identify its exponential rate with the volume of a particular complement. ## The quantum A-polynomial formulation There is also a recurrence formulation. A quantum A-operator is a finite difference operator annihilating the color-dependent invariant. Its coefficients depend on the quantum parameter and a peripheral variable; a shift changes the color. An operator alone generally has more than one solution. Initial values and the prescribed behavior at singular specializations select the solution corresponding to the knot invariant. The [pointed quantum A-period theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) gives an exact reconstruction of $K_N(K)$ from this operator and finite initial data, retaining the peripheral factors. For the knots covered above, this reconstructed value therefore has the same hyperbolic volume limit. The theorem also gives a positive determinant expression whose exponential rate is the volume. For every covered strict long-filling presentation, the [geometric longitude proof](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) identifies the whole selected curve with the preferred meridian--longitude deformation of the knot complement. Junctions without crossing circles may have arbitrary valence and adjacency. The earlier summed circle-tree theorem and the local theorem with bound \(2^{-120}\) also have the required geometric identification and full expansion. The selected complex geometric irreducible factor therefore divides the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine all-level annihilator of the reduced invariant. This does not identify the other factors, their multiplicities, or the full recurrence ideal. The actual meridian state imposes a concrete constraint: its complete value has volume growth, but its value one quantum shift away is exactly one. The [nearby-zero theorem](../../notes/actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) proves that zeros approach completeness at distance $O(1/N)$. A nonvanishing scalar asymptotic for the unchanged state therefore cannot hold on a fixed neighborhood. There is now a uniform volume limit on smaller disks \(M=q_N^s\), \(|s|\le R<1\), for every fixed strict Conway tree with independently sufficiently long signed twists. Product junctions can have arbitrary fixed valence and adjacency. The ratio to the complete value tends to \(\sin(\pi s)/(\pi s)\); after division by the exact finite sine quotient, its first correction is determined by the preferred cusp shape. The [moving-meridian theorem](results.md#the-volume-limit-while-the-meridian-varies) states the normalization, the threshold and the whole-sum comparison. The same intrinsic volume, nonvanishing, cusp and selected-factor conclusions pass through the net-twist and closure reductions under their stated hypotheses. Their ambient isotopies preserve the entire zero-framed meridian family and the preferred peripheral curves. The comparison may use the reduced strict diagram to compute its factors; it does not identify the auxiliary augmented links of different presentations. The disk still stops before the ordinary-color resonances. Continuation through them and coverage of other knot classes remain further questions. ## Reading and checking the arguments Read the [manuscript](manuscript.md) for a continuous account with definitions, proof details, and illustrations. Use [the results chapter](results.md) to compare the exact families and hypotheses, and [the notation chapter](notation.md) when consulting technical notes. The [reproduction chapter](audits.md) distinguishes the finite rational inequalities checked by the supplied programs from the analytic and geometric arguments proved in writing. The [research library](../library.html) organizes the supporting notes by question. It retains the Fourier, weighted Cauchy, torsor, cube, and other approaches, including estimates that failed and the explanations of their failure. Those historical routes are useful evidence about the problem; they are not additional prerequisites for reading the main theorem. The [figure gallery](../figures.md) explains what each diagram represents and links to editable sources. The general volume conjecture remains open.

title: A guide to the manuscript
text: # A guide to the manuscript [Read the manuscript PDF](../../manuscript/build/main.pdf). The [editable sources and build instructions](../../manuscript/README.md) are available alongside it. The paper proves volume equalities for decorated planar tangle diagrams and for several ordered-tree constructions. It explains the finite quantum invariant, the hyperbolic geometry, the estimates controlling cancellation, and the passage from an augmented link to the final knot complement. The families have different hypotheses; this page introduces them separately. ## The planar decoration chapter The broadest construction begins with a simple triangulation of the sphere and a chosen pairing of its adjacent triangles. These finite data give a planar crossing-circle diagram in the three-sphere. The chapter constructs its circle packing and then inserts even terminal stacks on both sides of each crossing circle. The number of insertions is chosen by an explicit curvature recurrence. After that finite decoration, independently sufficiently long signed twists at every old and new region give the full volume equality. A specified parity pattern makes the main strands one knot. The inserted tangles preserve this pairing and generally change the knot type. The theorem does not require a tree of tangle operations or compare the relative magnitudes of the long twists. The chapter explains the local construction and the inequality it establishes. Its appendix gives the full proof: the variational packing, the exact coefficient with its original mark and parity, the local geometric contribution, all Fourier tails and boundary terms, and completion to the actual smooth knot complement. The [results page](results.md#decorating-a-planar-diagram) gives a detailed introduction with the same figure. ## The directed full expansion The final analytic chapter proves every finite order of the microscopic meridian expansion for the directed tree criterion. It works on all fixed translated nonreal charts needed by a fixed recurrence. Exact normal channels and peripheral gauge factors are retained. The first correction is the preferred cusp shape, and the highest-degree coefficients recover the full preferred longitude germ. This adds every directed certificate to the selected geometric-factor theorem. It does not identify the full A-polynomial or extend the moving-meridian theorem to the decorated planar class. ## The ordered tangle construction Start with two strands in a box whose four endpoints are labeled and kept in order. Insert an integer number of signed half-twists. A positive and a negative count give opposite crossing directions. Turn the box through a quarter-turn; this is the basic piece used in the construction. Two boxes can be stacked in order, and a constructed box can itself be turned. After finitely many such operations, join the remaining outside endpoints by the prescribed cylindrical closure. Following the strands determines whether this produces a knot or a link. The theorem requires one component, with no closed component hidden inside a box. The notation in the paper abbreviates these operations: | Notation | Meaning | | --- | --- | | $R^n$ | Two strands with $n$ signed half-twists. | | $T(F)$ | The quarter-turn of the tangle box $F$, with its endpoint order retained. | | $h_i(n_i)=T(R^{n_i})$ | The $i$th basic twist piece. Different subscripts carry independent integers. | | $FG$ | The ordered stack of $F$ and $G$. | | $C(FG)$ | The prescribed closure of the four outside endpoints of that stack. | These are operations on actual tangles. The notation does not mean that formal arithmetic with rational fractions has replaced an isotopy argument. For the paper's main family, first stack two basic pieces. Thereafter one may turn a constructed box, stack two constructed boxes, or attach one additional basic piece on either side. The technical notes call a box obtained by these rules **completed**. This is a recursive name for a class of boxes; it does not mean that a Dehn filling has already been performed. Construct two such boxes $F$ and $G$, then close $FG$. The paper also handles its stated isolated stacks of at least three basic pieces. ## The theorem and its quantifiers For each fixed permitted construction there is a threshold. Choose the twist integers independently, with either sign, beyond that threshold in absolute value, and choose their parities so that the endpoint pairing gives a knot. Fix all those integers. The theorem then proves $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). $$ Here $K$ is the resulting knot, $K_N(K)$ is the reduced Kashaev invariant at integer level $N$, and the right side is its hyperbolic complement volume. The limit includes even and odd levels and composite levels. The twist counts do not grow with $N$, and no restriction is imposed on their relative sizes. The threshold may depend on the entire construction. To analyze the geometry, the proof first places an auxiliary crossing circle around each twist region. The resulting augmented link has a convenient decomposition into ideal hyperbolic cells. Filling an auxiliary circle means attaching a solid torus along the prescribed meridian so as to insert the twists. In the knot theorem **all auxiliary circles are filled**. The cusp of the knot itself remains unfilled. Thus the conclusion is about the knot complement, not a closed three-manifold. Two companion results extend the paper's recursive family. The [strict-tree theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) proves the estimates for every expression passing a finite angle-feasibility test. The [net-twist theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) then reduces an arbitrary ordered cylindrical product closure to one of those expressions or to an elementary two-strand braid closure. In the former case, the size condition applies to the combined twist numbers produced by the reduction. The [results chapter](results.md) states that condition and gives an example. The earlier PDF chapters retain their own theorem and proof; the new quantitative chapter is described next. ## A bound independent of the tree size The chapter on directed subtree estimates gives one sufficient twist threshold for every finite ordered circle tree with at least one edge: \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27} \] at every vertex, with either sign. The actual strand pairing must give one knot without an internal closed component. A more flexible consequence lets each vertex independently have this twist magnitude or degree \(d_v\ge2^{28}\). The degree alternative permits any fixed signed power. The whole tree and all powers are fixed before the quantum level grows. The [directed criterion](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) is proved from the exact polynomial obtained by evaluating a subtree while retaining its attaching variable. The proof establishes its nonzero value at zero, normalized bounds on real and complex angles, and a nonzero first Fourier contribution to the next trace. Each error is compared with the filling at the current vertex. Different subtrees can have different decay bounds. At the final vertex there is no outgoing variable, so the proof does not impose an unnecessary outgoing bound. The chapter and its full technical appendix retain the actual finite trace, its boundary contributions and its orientation factors. The geometric path identifies the resulting action with the volume of the original knot complement. The earlier local-message chapter proves an included, more restrictive criterion, and the summed theorem below remains useful for individual diagrams. One consequence attaches an even stack of sufficiently many long odd terminal pieces at each vertex of any fixed core whose endpoint pairing is a knot. The insertion preserves the pairing but generally changes the knot type. It supplies covered knots with arbitrary prescribed powers at the core vertices; it does not prove the theorem for the unchanged core. ## The quantitative circle-tree chapter A further chapter treats a different explicit description of the tangle construction: every vertex of an ordered tree carries an integer braid, and each child tangle is turned before it is stacked on the prescribed side of its parent braid. A terminal root gives the cylindrical closure. The strand pairing must give one knot. For vertex degree \(d_v\) and crossing power \(n_v\), the condition \[ \sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}\le2^{-25} \] gives the volume limit. It also gives a uniform profile as the meridian moves by order \(1/N\), with its first correction expressed by the preferred cusp shape. The [full statement](../../notes/actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) defines every framing factor and gives numerical sufficient bounds. Some short powers are allowed at sufficiently high-degree vertices; the earlier long-twist chapters retain their own construction class. The chapter illustrates an actual octahedral attachment and explains why it recovers the original exterior. Positive tetrahedra continue along the filling path until the primitive cone angle is \(2\pi\). This constructs the smooth knot complement whose volume appears in the quantum limit. Appendices E and F contain the full finite-sum, ordered-cut and geometric-completion proofs, including their face maps, peripheral words and uniform constants. The companion notes present the same calculations separately. ## The geometric longitude and the quantum recurrence The geometric-characteristic chapter identifies the longitude selected by the source with the preferred geometric longitude of the knot complement. It first constructs nonparabolic representations for trees of crossing circles, retaining the puncture eigenlines through each half twist. A rational-function argument then determines the remaining framing factor. The [strict-tree extension](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) allows product junctions without crossing circles, of arbitrary valence and adjacency. Insert a circle around a literal identity box at each such junction, then fill its meridian. This restores the original framed collar and its ordered based puncture loops. Eliminating the added angular variable gives the original product action, including at a possible half-edge fold. The argument therefore identifies the full marked representation germ of the original long-filled knot. Appendix H supplies the full microscopic expansion and its implication for a genuine all-level recurrence. Appendix I contains the circle-tree geometry, algebraic rigidity and Seifert-surface sign. Appendix J gives the strict-tree extension, the zero-crossing collar and the intrinsic transfer to covered net-twist and arbitrary-closure presentations. Together these results identify the selected complex geometric irreducible factor in the first nonzero classical symbol for every covered strict long-filling source, as well as the previously established circle-tree sources under the summed condition or the local bound \(2^{-120}\). The operator conclusion uses the full expansion and its shifted parameter neighborhoods; it does not follow just from the leading profile in a new numerical criterion. No assertion identifies the entire A-polynomial, the multiplicities of its factors or the entire recurrence ideal. ## How to read the proof The first part fixes the invariant normalization and derives the finite algebra of the tangle operations. A color is an integer label in that finite calculation. It is not an additional component of the final knot. The source formula retains values and first derivatives at repeated spectral points, which explains the use of Hermite interpolation. Newton polynomials make the allowed integer indices at a product explicit. These support conditions are kept before taking a continuum limit. The geometric part associates normalized state variables with angles of ideal pyramids and prisms. An ideal vertex lies at infinity in hyperbolic space. Strict angle inequalities produce genuine cells, and the ordered endpoint data determine their face identifications. A strictly concave angle functional has a unique geometric maximum. The proof then follows actual paths on the cusps to identify the meridian and longitude used for filling. The source estimates address a different issue: a signed sum can be much smaller than the sum of the absolute values of its terms. The exact reflection formula separates a central contribution from extra terms called aliases. The paper bounds all of those terms while preserving their finite supports. Concavity and supporting tangents reduce two important estimates to finite rational certificates. ![Supporting tangents used to control a single-piece attachment over its entire allowed state region.](../../manuscript/build/figures/attachment-tangents.png) Near the geometric maximum, a complex asymptotic formula gives an exponential action, a nonzero leading coefficient and a controlled error. The paper calls this a local packet. The estimates outside that neighborhood show why the packet really determines the invariant; locating a critical point by itself would not rule out a missing or canceled contribution. Finally, the filling transform is evaluated with all its Fourier modes and boundary terms. The marked meridian-longitude convention identifies the real part of its critical action with the volume after filling. This last normalization is what connects the finite invariant to the actual knot constructed at the beginning. The technical appendices supply the finite algebra, analytic interpolation estimates, certificate details and marked geometric calibration used in this chain. They are intended to make the proof readable without treating links to working notes as substitutes for arguments. ## Reproduce the finite certificates The quantitative chapter uses `python3 repro/run_research_checks.py curvature-fillings`. The [checks chapter](audits.md#checks-for-the-quantitative-volume-theorem) describes its three programs and their finite scope. From the repository root, run: ```sh python3 repro/verify.py --list python3 repro/verify.py --plan python3 repro/verify.py --output repro/results ``` The first two commands describe the checks. The third runs them serially, writes fresh results and compares them with the committed reference records. The [reproduction guide](../../repro/README.md) explains the software requirements and outputs; the [proof-input map](../../repro/PROOF_INPUTS.md) locates the written arguments behind each certificate. These checks use rational bounds with explicit remainders, not a numerical search for maxima. They verify finite arithmetic used in the proof. They do not mechanically verify the topology, the invariant normalization, or every analytic step of the manuscript. To build the paper and guide, use the commands in the [manuscript source guide](../../manuscript/README.md). The mathematical illustrations are supplied as editable TikZ sources as well as rendered assets. For the attachment diagram above, download the [vector PDF](../../manuscript/build/figures/attachment-tangents.pdf) or the [TikZ source](../../manuscript/figures/attachment-tangents.tex).

title: Volume equalities: the families and the hypotheses
text: # Volume equalities: the families and the hypotheses The results on this page compare a finite quantum invariant with the volume of the knot or link complement that the diagram actually constructs. For a knot $K$, the principal conclusion is $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). $$ Here $K_N$ is the reduced Kashaev invariant in the normalization fixed in the proof. The knot is held fixed while the positive integer level $N$ grows. The statements below include both even and odd levels unless a smaller scope is explicitly stated. The broadest construction below begins with a triangulated sphere and adds specified tangles to its planar diagram. Separate results give explicit twist and degree bounds for ordered tangle trees, as well as net-twist reductions preserving an existing knot. These hypotheses differ. Each section states the knot it constructs, the estimates it uses, and which parameters are held fixed. ## Decorating a planar diagram The [planar decoration theorem](../../notes/actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) starts from a more general diagram than a tree of tangle operations. Its input can be given entirely by finite combinatorial data: take a simple triangulation of the sphere with at least four vertices, and pair its triangles across selected edges so that each triangle belongs to exactly one pair. “Simple” means that there are no loops or repeated edges. The cyclic orders belong to the sphere embedding. Each paired pair of triangles specifies a crossing-circle tangle. Contracting the pair gives a four-ended box; the other edges specify the connections between boxes. Drawing the prescribed strands and placing an auxiliary circle around each pair constructs an actual link in the three-sphere. The proof gives a parity choice for the crossings that makes the main strands one knot. The theorem then adds finitely many terminal tangles on both sides of each original box. Each side receives an even number, and the added pieces have odd crossing parity. These insertions preserve the chosen endpoint pairing and create no internal closed component. They usually change the knot itself. **Conclusion.** For each such decorated diagram there is a finite threshold \(T\). Choose every original and added filling integer \(p_e\) independently with \(|p_e|>T\), retaining the chosen half twist \(\epsilon_e\), so that the signed number of crossings is \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\). The resulting knot is hyperbolic and satisfies the volume limit at the top of this page. Both signs and arbitrarily different magnitudes are allowed. The diagram, decoration, and all integers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. This covers arbitrarily large planar arrangements without a tree hypothesis. It does not cover the unchanged core knot, arbitrary short powers at the original boxes, or a diagram growing with \(N\). The threshold may depend on the decorated diagram. ### How the number of added tangles is chosen The proof first constructs the complete circle packing of the original sphere by maximizing a strictly concave angle function. Normalize the two circles beside the marked strand to parallel lines. Their curvatures are zero; every other circle has positive curvature. At one crossing circle, the two triangles have vertices \((x,b,y)\) and \((x,c,y)\). Here the letters denote the curvatures of the corresponding circles. The edge \(xy\) is the selected pairing edge, and \(b,c\) are its opposite vertices. Put \[ A=x+y>0,\qquad P=xy. \] Inserting a circle in the first triangular gap replaces \(b\), as seen from the retained crossing circle, by \[ b_1=b+A+2\sqrt{Ab+P}. \] The original circles remain in place. The new circle has curvature \(b_1\); the new matching edge joins it to the old circle \(b\). ![The old matched edge xy remains, while inserting w subdivides one triangle and creates the new matched edge bw.](../figures/balanced-terminal-fans.png) After \(j\) insertions on this side, \[ b_j=b+2j\sqrt{Ab+P}+j^2A. \] There is the same formula for \(c_k\) on the other side. Choose even nonnegative \(j,k\) so that \[ U=\frac{\sqrt{Ab+P}}A+j,\qquad V=\frac{\sqrt{Ac+P}}A+k,\qquad U,V\ge4,\quad |U-V|\le1. \] Such a choice always exists: even increments let the two numbers be brought within one, after which adding the same even increment makes both large enough. Repeating this finite procedure at every original crossing circle gives the required decoration. ### Why this proves an equality for the full invariant The exact finite evaluation is a coefficient of a product of local polynomials. All factors use the same face variables and the original marked coefficient. The proof divides each local polynomial into three explicit sums. One gives the geometric contribution. The two others must be bounded on the entire spectral interval, including its endpoints. Write \(F(x,b,y)\) for the normalized logarithmic weight of one triangle. At a crossing circle the condition needed for those two other sums is \[ F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y)>\log b,\qquad F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y)>\log c, \] with a condition omitted when its middle curvature is zero. Combining this result with the full quantum expansion proves that the selected complex geometric irreducible factor divides the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine all-level annihilator of the reduced invariant in these covered classes. The full and reduced normalizations have different gauge factors, which the proof keeps before removing common factors. The intrinsic conclusion also transfers to net-twist and arbitrary closure inputs that are carried by the stated marked ambient isotopies to a covered strict knot. The entire zero-framed family and preferred peripheral curves agree under that isotopy. The presentation-dependent edge factors are computed on the strict output; they are not asserted to match term by term in the input. No equality with the full A-polynomial, no factor multiplicity, and no identification of the entire recurrence ideal is claimed. Ordinary resonances and knots outside the covered classes remain separate questions.

title: How the full quantum invariant acquires the knot volume
text: # How the full quantum invariant acquires the knot volume This chapter follows the completed proof and then explains the local tools used in other presentations. The [methods chapter](methods.md) gives the definitions, elementary examples, and literature references for those tools. The [notation chapter](notation.md) records the conventions needed to compare their formulas. The main result concerns a particular, already defined knot invariant. For a knot \(K\) and an integer level \(N\), write \(K_N(K)\) for its reduced Kashaev invariant, normalized to be \(1\) on the unknot. The quantum parameter is \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\). A diagram computes \(K_N\) by multiplying crossing matrices, joining their indices along strands, and summing the remaining indices. Cups, caps and the marked cut specify how the strands close. In the technical notes, this entire prescribed expression is called the **source**. It includes its scalar factors and derivatives, not just the part that seems largest. The [strict Conway tree theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) proves \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K) \] for every fixed literal expression satisfying its finite compatibility test, once all independent signed twist weights are sufficiently long and the endpoint pairing gives a knot. A literal expression records the actual order of tangle products and quarter-turns; algebraically equal scalar formulas are not silently treated as isotopic diagrams. The tree and its integer weights stay fixed as \(N\) grows. This is a theorem for the stated class, not a claim that every arborescent knot has such a presentation. ## Why retaining the full expression matters A color is a representation label on a strand or an auxiliary crossing circle. At a root of unity, two spectral labels can have the same eigenvalue. The value at that eigenvalue then fails to determine the operator: its first derivative in the transverse spectral direction can also contribute. The notes call these derivative terms **normals**. Derivatives in the generic quantum parameter are another kind of normal, so the variable of differentiation must always be specified. Let \(\zeta\) denote the generic quantum parameter before specialization. For example, a factor \([2N]_\zeta\) vanishes when \(\zeta=q_N\) but can have a nonzero derivative there. Deleting it before differentiating changes the prescribed expression. The full invariant is a signed, generally complex sum. A large term or a large positive upper comparison does not prove that the sum has that size. Two requirements must be met together: the geometric contribution has a nonzero coefficient, and everything omitted from its neighborhood is uniformly smaller. A **packet** in this guide means a local asymptotic formula with its action, nonzero prefactor and controlled error. A **whole-source bound** means a bound on the entire original quantum sum, including all colors and derivative terms. These requirements have now been proved for the strict-tree class. The older local methods later in this chapter remain useful for other presentations. Their unresolved steps are not unresolved steps in the strict-tree theorem. ## The completed proof for strict trees The exact tangle recursion supplies the starting point. A physical leaf is a quarter-turned twist operator. Multiplication stacks two tangles in their recorded order, while a turn changes which two boundary strands are regarded as inputs. Expanding these operations in a fixed finite basis gives exact formulas and exact inequalities on the integer indices. After the forced closing index is removed, the remaining indices form a primitive integer lattice: there is no hidden multiplicity from using only a sublattice. This is what permits a local lattice sum to be compared with an integral without losing its normalization. At complete colors, the factorial weights have a real limiting action: the logarithm of a weight, divided by \(N\), has that limit. The action is a function of the scaled leaf and product indices, subject to the original compatibility equations. It must be maximized with those equations still imposed. Strictness ensures that the maximum occurs where the relevant cell angles are positive. The geometry chapter explains why the resulting cells reconstruct the actual augmented exterior, rather than merely a collection of tetrahedra of the correct total volume. The local analysis then permits the auxiliary colors to vary slightly in a complex neighborhood. The [general core theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) and the [quarter-index theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_quarter_index_color_packet.md) retain the exact recurrence, its boundary data and the original phases. They give a nonzero analytic contribution near the geometric critical point. The quarter-index case is needed because some strict diagrams have a limiting scaled leaf index exactly \(1/4\); it is an equal-modulus boundary for two transfer roots, not a collision of those roots. The proof controls their accumulated contributions instead of inferring dominance from their distinctness. The remaining difficulty is global: a pointwise estimate on each factor can be too large after the factors are joined. The solution uses two compatible estimates for parts of the tree. A product carrying an actual character operator is controlled by the [decorated-character theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md). A connected product region without such an operator is closed against an auxiliary positive comparison polynomial. The [probe theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) bounds that comparison at the region's actual geometric boundary action. The comparison polynomial is used only in the inequality; it does not replace a physical coupon in the invariant. The [spectral propagation theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_mixed_core_spectral_propagation.md) shows that these estimates survive the next turn and product. Here a spectral norm records both values and first derivatives at repeated spectral nodes. The proof keeps a neighborhood of the unique maximizing indices separate from its complement. In the neighborhood, the actual polynomial factors give angular decay and a local loss when a physical color is far from complete. Outside it, a fixed exponential gap absorbs the polynomial interpolation costs. Induction over the finite tree therefore controls the full expression at the correct action, without assigning the same cost to every turn. This yields two global facts. Every physical color tuple obeys the required upper bound, and any tuple with at least one color a fixed fraction away from complete has a strict exponential loss. The difference between a full leaf and its chosen local expression is an explicit complementary-color term, called an **alias**. Expanding these differences turns every unwanted term into an actual full quantum evaluation with at least one small color. The global color bound suppresses them. This is why the argument controls all aliases at once; it does not assume that individual absolute-value estimates preserve the cancellations. Finally, an exact finite Fourier identity inserts the prescribed integer twists into the original leaf frames. The local packet produces a nonzero saddle contribution. Estimates on the whole Fourier domain, including its boundary terms, make the remaining part exponentially smaller. The [marked filling theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) identifies the resulting action with the volume of the actual knot complement. Only auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled. The main knot cusp remains complete and unfilled. ## Subtree estimates with a uniform twist threshold For the ordered tree construction with at least one edge and an integer braid at every junction, the [directed subtree theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) uses an exact finite recursion with one attaching angle left free. Its outgoing polynomial always has degree at most \(N-1\), even for a large subtree. The proof establishes nonvanishing at angle zero, then divides by that exact value, retaining its phases and framing factors. The ratio has a real decay estimate and a complex estimate on a fixed rectangle. These bounds control the next finite crossing trace, including its Fourier endpoint terms. Its first contribution has coefficient one at both level parities, and the other contributions are strictly smaller. Different subtrees may use different decay constants. The last vertex needs no outgoing estimate because its value is the final scalar. This gives a finite numerical criterion and, in particular, the sufficient condition \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27}\quad\text{or}\quad d_v\ge2^{28} \] at each vertex independently. Here \(n_v\) is the signed crossing power and \(d_v\) the number of incident tree edges. The original strand pairing must form a knot. The theorem controls its actual invariant and identifies the limit with its complement volume. The tree and all powers are fixed before \(N\) grows. This numerical result complements the strict-tree long-filling proof; it does not narrow that proof to circle trees. ## The same limit written through a quantum \(A\)-operator A quantum \(A\)-operator is a finite difference operator in a meridian variable. It is more data than a classical algebraic curve, but an equation alone can still have several solutions. The actual solution is selected here by its original quantum-group definition and finitely many fixed small-color values. Write \(x=q_N^\alpha\) for the raw representation coordinate and \(M=-q_Nx\) for the marked meridian coordinate. If \(F_N(M)\) is the reduced ADO family in this coordinate, then \[ F_N(1)=K_N(K),\qquad F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N). \] The complete point is \(M=1\); \(C_j(q)\) is the ordinary reduced \(j\)-color period. These identities include the original framing and quotient-color conventions. The [finite cut-state proof](../../notes/finite_sum_annihilator.md) supplies a genuine level-independent annihilator \[ P(q,M,T)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_i(q,M)T^i,\qquad TM=qMT. \] Here \(d\) is the fixed operator order, the \(a_i\) are rational coefficient functions, and \((TF)(M)=F(qM)\). The operator is obtained from the finite quantum formula before evaluating the invariant. It is not defined by a ratio of already known values. The [finite-pointing theorem](../../notes/all_level_a_period.md) then expresses the exact scalar as \[ K_N(K)=\operatorname{CT}_{t=0} \bigl[r_N(q_N(1+t))\,c_0(q_N(1+t))\bigr]. \] Here \(c_0\) is a fixed vector of small-color Laurent polynomials, \(r_N\) is the ordered companion-matrix product prescribed by \(P\), and \(\operatorname{CT}\) means the constant term of the whole Laurent expansion. Singular intermediate steps are retained. Only a fixed number of derivatives of \(c_0\) is required, independent of \(N\). The [pointed quantum \(A\)-volume corollary](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) proves that this exact signed scalar has the knot-volume limit above. It also gives a positive ratio of coefficients of Gram determinants, equal to a sum of squared color periods, with the corresponding volume limit. The signed scalar is not replaced by a matrix norm or by a sum of absolute values. The full ADO normalization is retained as a rational factor whose whole value at \(M=1\) is \(i^{N+3}/N\). The [strict-tree geometric longitude theorem](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) identifies the selected curve with the preferred-longitude deformation for every covered strict long-filling presentation, including arbitrary product junctions without crossing circles. The full microscopic expansion then forces the selected geometric irreducible factor to divide the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine all-level reduced annihilator. The corresponding earlier circle-tree theorem retains its summed condition or its local bound \(2^{-120}\). These operator conclusions require estimates for the whole expansion on shifted parameter neighborhoods; the leading profile of a new numerical criterion alone is not a substitute. Full quantum-module or recurrence-ideal equality remains a separate problem. ## Other local tools, and their different scope The rest of this chapter explains methods developed for general augmented plat diagrams. A plat is a braid diagram closed by fixed cups and caps; its bridge width counts the chosen bridges. These results often hold at every fixed width, but some routes below still need a global estimate for unrestricted plats. This limitation concerns that route and class. It does not undo the complete proof just described. A few recurring names have a concrete role. A **channel** is an intermediate representation label in a change of basis. A **Casimir matrix** is the operator whose eigenspaces label those channels. A **\(q\)-Hahn polynomial** is a finite polynomial appearing in an actual matrix column; its root locations can control cancellation. A **resolvent** is \((zI-\Omega)^{-1}\) for such a matrix \(\Omega\). A **Ward identity** is an exact relation between shifted or differentiated terms of the original sum. These objects are used to keep track of the full contraction, not to introduce another knot invariant. Several notes also use the word **completed** for an operator that combines two colliding spectral channels with their value and derivative terms. It does not mean “a proof has been completed.” A **fold** is the midpoint where the paired channel labels meet. A complex **tube** is a fixed neighborhood of the real parameter region; an estimate on the integer samples alone is not an estimate throughout that tube. ## A finite function of the auxiliary colors For this subsection, fix one augmented plat diagram. It has \(b\) auxiliary crossing circles, each surrounding two strands in a specified part of the diagram. The auxiliary color \(n_i\), an integer between \(1\) and \(N\), chooses the representation on the \(i\)th circle. Complete color means \(n_i=N\). Its deficit is \(h_i=N-n_i\). The [complete-color formula](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) and [all-color formula](../../notes/actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md) compute the original marked scalar from the same crossing matrices, cups and caps for every fixed plat width. A specified function of noninteger colors is needed because a filling formula is a finite Fourier sum in the physical integer colors. To estimate that sum by stationary phase, one needs a specified analytic function near those samples. An arbitrary interpolation would change the saddle. The [entire color function](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md) constructs the needed finite function directly from the spectral decomposition of the complete-circle operator. Put \(M_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). The distinct spectral channels are numbered \(j=0,\ldots,M_N\), with eigenvalues \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\). Let \(L_{N,j}\) denote the actual component of the complete-circle operator at channel \(j\), including the derivative-derived term when the node is repeated. For a tuple \(\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_b)\), define \(A_N(\mathbf j)\) by inserting \(L_{N,j_i}\) at each auxiliary circle and carrying out the original matrix contraction. The fixed half twists, cups, caps, marked trace and external scalar all remain in this coefficient. Now let \(\chi=(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_b)\) be a complex vector and set \[ \begin{aligned} m_j&=N-2j-1,\\ C_N(\chi)&= \sum_{j_1=0}^{M_N}\cdots\sum_{j_b=0}^{M_N} A_N(j_1,\ldots,j_b) \prod_{i=1}^{b}\cos\!\bigl(\pi m_{j_i}\chi_i\bigr). \end{aligned} \] Every index and coefficient is therefore fixed by the original diagram. The function is entire because it is a finite sum of cosines. It is even in each variable. When \(N\) is odd, the final frequency is zero and its cosine is exactly \(1\); that endpoint is included. At physical high colors, substitute \(\chi_i=h_i/N\). The value of \(C_N\) is exactly the term obtained by keeping the complete-circle part of each color identity. This term is called the **core**. The same exact color identity also has a complementary small-color term, called an **alias**. Expanding the product gives \(C_N(h/N)\) plus one explicit term for every nonempty subset of alias choices. This is an identity of full operators, including their repeated-node derivatives. It does not say the aliases are small. At complete colors \(h_i=0\), they vanish, so \(C_N(0)\) is the full complete-color scalar. Finite Fourier orthogonality recovers every coefficient \(A_N(\mathbf j)\) from the values of \(C_N\) on the grid \(h_i/N\), \(0\le h_i<N\). Parseval's identity then controls a weighted sum of \(|A_N(\mathbf j)|^2\). It does not control cancellation in their signed sum. For unrestricted plats, this finite formula alone does not prove the required complex asymptotic or suppress the alias terms. For the strict Conway class, the later whole-sum argument described above supplies precisely those additional estimates. ## The finite polynomials select a local complex action After its forced zero is removed, every actual physical q-Hahn polynomial has simple negative real roots. The [proof](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) uses an exact sine recurrence, interlacing and sine coefficient operators; the numerical root checks only test the implementation. Consequently its logarithm, real on the positive axis, is holomorphic on the slit plane. Real factorial estimates first identify its strictly concave positive-axis variational limit. Uniform bounds from the negative roots and the identity theorem then continue the limit to a [uniquely selected holomorphic action](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md). On the physical Fourier arc, the corresponding continued saddle is nondegenerate. This proves the actual local exponential rate while retaining its cancellations. The [actual amplitude theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.md) now strengthens this to a nonzero prefactor and uniform relative error $O(N^{-1})$. Its proof uses the exact finite difference equation and a real normalization, retaining both original integer offsets. The scaled parameters are the actual values at level $N$, so no rate of convergence of those parameters is assumed. The [fixed-degree magnetic corridor](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md) places every magnetic zero outside the physical strip. The new [joint determinant theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md) goes further: the local polynomial is an explicitly normalized determinant $\det(zI+cD+K)$. Here $z,c$ are its scalar variables, $D$ is positive definite and the matrix $K$ is skew-Hermitian, $K^*=-K$. Its positive Hermitian part excludes zeros in a fixed joint domain, including at folded channels. The [joint amplitude theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) therefore permits the pair degree and magnetic coordinate to vary together complexly. Exact normalization removes sampling aliases; two original finite shift equations control both derivatives and fix a nonzero amplitude with relative error $O(N^{-1})$. The channel stays an integer. An explicit principal-square-root test identifies the selected local sheet on the central domain. The [full physical packet theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) now removes the central-domain restriction on fixed physical compacts. A second determinant uses two positive Hermitian matrices to put its zeros in an angular cone outside the physical sector. This supplies uniform inverse and logarithmic bounds. The source characteristic stays simple, so the same exact two-shift proof gives the selected action and nonzero amplitude throughout the full tube. The necessary finite-level boundary correction is retained. ![The joint domain in the real parts of the two physical wire coordinates, with its degree seam excluded.](../figures/joint-kernel-domain.png) The [small-channel normal theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md) retains the original generic source and bounds every fixed derivative by a polynomial times its root value. The [large-partner collision theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) expresses the actual paired first normal as a transverse derivative, with its full finite tail. That tail has extra poles, so the ordinary-column domain does not automatically serve the paired normal. The [near-fold complex theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) now gives subexponential relative cost on a fixed complex compact for $(l-j)\log N=o(N)$. It includes the actual large-channel tail. Fixed nonzero scaled channel shifts and a nonzero normal amplitude remain unresolved. On the physical integer grid, the [paired-normal bound](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md) is now proved for every complete double channel: $|w/C|\leq N^6/256+N^2/8$, with $O(N^4)$ cost when the scaled degree stays away from one. This includes the original large-channel contribution. The proof uses a positive imaginary part and the exact double-node reflection; integer samples alone do not extend the bound to a fixed complex neighborhood. The [physical generic-jet theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md) controls every fixed q derivative of all admissible physical columns and genuine divided pairs. It uses the actual forward and backward generic recurrences, retaining their distinct offdiagonal coefficients. This supplies higher physical jets without differentiating a root-only identity. It is separate from the complex-domain theorem and from a completed target tensor norm. The [common-framing criterion](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md) gives finite inequalities for one rank-one projector. The new [right-angled obstruction](../../notes/actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) rules out an all-central selected frame for the certified right-angled decomposition. Generic oriented-strip flags localize the weaker physical-support failures to any two prescribed distinct factors, at any bridge width, including the pair adjacent to the original mark. The [selected-factor localization](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) now puts every other ordinary factor on the selected full physical packet. For an unrestricted plat, this localization still does not identify a contributing integration contour or give a sharp bound on the completed contraction. Choosing the exceptional pair at one crossing-circle edge gives four external physical representation factors. The [matching-edge scalar](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.md) is then positive for every target channel, including high partners. The complete-circle [typed block identity](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) keeps the original cup, turn, circle measure and marked trace normal. The circle measure cancels its exponential row factor exactly. Only Taylor orders through two are needed after clearing the simple poles. The [completed-projector identity](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_completed_projector_block.md) now cancels the remaining target scalar normalization exactly. It combines colliding channels before specialization, retaining both their regular projector and nilpotent term. Only first derivatives of these completed operators and the complement remain; the scalar divided difference still includes the necessary second derivatives of the original weights. The resulting upper estimate is a positive scalar sum weighted by the native completed-projector and complementary-network costs. These costs are not assumed to be subexponential. This makes the remaining norm problem explicit without supplying a lower bound or changing the selected period. The [native-energy theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md) expresses the first of these costs through original columns and their exact bilinear measures. Every fixed derivative adds only a polynomial factor. The energy itself can grow exponentially: the degree-$t=m$ block of the simple midpoint projector at odd level $N=2m+1$ has rate $v_8/(2\pi)$. The full operator combines its physical degrees in one maximum or square sum; the wire constraints must remain shared when these operators are joined. This rules out dropping the energy as a normalization cost. The [full matching-graph identity](../../notes/general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md) is a complementary exact assembly tool: all folded sectors form one generic network with the original physical trace normal retained. It holds at both parities and uses the graph of the actual crossing-disk cut. No vanishing channel norm is inverted. ## The exceptional block is an actual operator period The [generic polynomial theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md) writes the completed block as $D_a^{-1}p_a(\Omega)$ before taking derivatives. Here $a$ is the retained channel index, $D_a$ is its explicit scalar normalization, $p_a$ is a finite polynomial and $\Omega$ is the actual target Casimir matrix. Its [zeros are all above two](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.md), so the finite polynomial selects a canonical logarithm and scalar action. The [general generating relation](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md) matches the actual four-parabolic character equation, including the inverse-turn sign and the source's additive scalar anchor. The spectral parameter of this polynomial is fixed by a specific word in the original meridians. Let \(B_{\mathrm{in}}\) be the determinant-one holonomy matrix of the incoming meridian, with its original basepath, and let \(B_{\mathrm{out}}\) be the corresponding transported outgoing meridian. Let \(c=\cot(\pi x)>0\) be the side ratio of the crossing-circle rectangle in its disk-framed normalization; \(x\) is the rectangle parameter. The inverse cup bend makes the relevant trace \[ z=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(B_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1}B_{\mathrm{out}}\right) =2-\frac{4}{c^2}. \] This is an ordered group word, not an independently chosen scalar target. The [marked-word theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_circle_rectangle_bound.md) proves \(0<c\le1\) when the rectangle occurs in the actual certified complete manifold, including both half-twist signs. Therefore \(c<1\) gives \(z<-2\), while \(c=1\) gives a genuine parabolic endpoint \(z=-2\). An abstract rectangle with \(c>1\) is algebraically possible, but it cannot realize that marked complete quotient. A polynomial of degree proportional to $N$ still cannot be replaced by its scalar value inside a contraction. The [exact period](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md) is $$p_a(\Omega)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma p_a(z)(zI-\Omega)^{-1}\,dz.$$ Its original Green entries retain both continuants and the full characteristic denominator. The [strict-support theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_cross_central_green_action.md) proves their selected leading action and bounds every fixed generic derivative when the two physical rows straddle the midpoint and $z$ lies in the stated common prefix domain, including fixed compact real intervals below $-2$. On the anti-diagonal they are exactly negative for real $z<-2$. The actual surrounding state is not thereby a positive functional or a continuant eigenstate. The [finite-propagation identity](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_finite_propagation.md) does give exact scalar action on a forward continuant in rows $u\leq t-a$, and on a backward continuant in rows $u\geq a$. These precise windows can leave a central gap. The environment and any complex magnetic continuation remain additional input. Separate [polynomial](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_endpoint_control.md) and [full-resolvent](../../notes/actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.md) bounds control the closing point $+2$ and its genuine normals on shrinking neighborhoods. They do not settle the possible geometric parabolic target $-2$, or the contour between the endpoint neighborhood and the candidate saddle. In this general-plat method, one must still estimate that actual contour integral and join it to the surrounding quantum sum without discarding its phases. ## Exact shifts transport finite quantum jets The [moving-period factorial](../../notes/actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md) is a specified meromorphic function that equals the original quantum factorial at every supported integer index. With $P=\pi i/\log\zeta$, it satisfies two exact equations: $$\widehat F_P(z+1)=(1-e^{2\pi i(z+1)/P})\widehat F_P(z),\qquad \widehat F_P(z+P)=(1-e^{2\pi i z})\widehat F_P(z).$$ At $P=N$, the second equation is also the cyclotomic product of the first $N$ shifts. Their multipliers satisfy the commuting-shift identity. The Gamma product fixes the actual section and its logarithmic marks; the shift equations alone are not a uniqueness theorem. Put $\Delta=N-P$ and $c(z)=1-e^{2\pi i z}$. The exact fixed-$N$ transport is $$\widehat F_P(z+N)=e^{\Delta\partial_z}\bigl(c(z)\widehat F_P(z)\bigr).$$ Fix a derivative order $J\ge0$. Modulo the $(J+1)$st power of the quantum deformation parameter, this exponential stops after $J$ derivatives. Away from $c=0$, conjugating by $c$ gives a unipotent operator whose difference from the identity has nilpotence index at most $J+1$. The connection has explicit poles at the integers. They account for genuine normal residues and cannot be removed by root specialization. The [specified exceptional lift](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) uses this same factorial and the original large white numerators to bound the full generic operator near the actual complex geometric frame. The [boundary theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md) computes what is added when its contour crosses the channel poles. These statements organize the exact source transport; this method still needs a proof that its geometric contribution survives in the unrestricted plat integral. The [tensor-source connection](../../notes/actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md) gives a rational gauge for the assembled summand itself. Put $g(z)=e^{2\pi iz}/(1-e^{2\pi iz})$. Its shift ratio is exactly the nonconstant cup multiplier. Products of $g$ and its inverse at the actual ordered cup and cap arguments give a specified gauge $G$. On a primitive free head lattice, the transport in direction $b$ is $$T_b=\chi(b)\,G\,e^{(N-P)D_b}\,G^{-1},$$ where $\chi$ is the retained parity character and $D_b$ is the directional derivative. These operators commute. On order-$J$ jets, every product of $J+1$ normalized differences from the identity vanishes. Constant head arguments require no gauge factor. The source remains undivided in its original period integral: $G$ can have zeros or poles on the physical lattice, whose boundary terms must still be computed. The [adjoint connection on the actual period](../../notes/actual_tensor_source_translated_cycle_normals.md) follows by finite-order integration by parts on that unchanged closed cycle. It acts on the original cotangent density multiplied by $G$, producing the required finite-part and double-pole terms. It is an exact relation between specified translated periods, with no claim that a translated head lies in the physical basis or that a geometric contour has been reached. The [complete local marked-density theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density.md) then assembles the selected factors with the original unrestricted mark. Their absolute normalization gives a nonzero fixed-channel density. At the complete geometric point, the channel Hessian is diagonal with entries $-4\pi i/\tau_i$, where $\tau_i$ are the actual primitive cusp shapes. After retaining the exact integer characters, the local sum over the original folded nodes is a nonzero Gaussian at both level parities. This establishes a local complete-source coefficient; the framing integral and its appearance in the original global cycle remain to be proved. The [braided change of cut](../../notes/actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.md) keeps this global question within the original source. Transporting a matrix-unit insertion by the recorded braid gives an exact second functional extracting the same marked scalar, with its genuine generic pivot and every derivative retained. The construction is independent of bridge width and permits different Morse levels. It does not eliminate the remaining two-cut array or evaluate the framing integral. Two further calculations specify that remaining integral. The [local source Ward theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md) proves that its framing density is $-c_D\,dr\wedge ds/[s(1+s)]$, with a nonzero framing-independent coefficient and the original mark retained. The [finite residual-current theorem](../../notes/actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md) supplies the corresponding source-defined off-diagonal bands and exact interval boundary terms. These are distinct results: transporting the actual finite chain to the geometric relative boundary, and evaluating its coefficient there, is still required. The [common charged head chart](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md) now constructs the Ward currents meromorphically before contraction, retaining the distinct band-support cycles. At the resonant boundary, [factorial estimates for growing head indices](../../notes/actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md), [root polynomial packets](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md), and the [genuine moving-parameter packet](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.md) give controlled pieces of the required matching calculation. Their scope is explicit: these pieces have not by themselves evaluated the unrestricted plat integral on its original contour. ## Exact recoupling exposes a local geometric scalar Four external objects can be paired in two ways. The actual change of basis is computed before root specialization, with its genuine pivotal turn. ![The two pairings of four external representation labels. The internal labels E and G are summed in the actual basis change.](../figures/four-port.png) The resulting finite Racah sum admits a positive, face-normalized scalar on the supported folded chamber. Its logarithmic rate is the volume of a specific hyperideal tetrahedron. This closes a local algebra-to-geometry step. It does not yet bound every entry of the completed physical transport in the required metric. A source normalization can have poles or zeros at the root, and complementary channels carry additional normal currents. The [scalar and normal theorem](../../notes/actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) states what is controlled and what remains. An [exact partner-reflection theorem](../../notes/actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md) now proves that all 64 complementary color choices have the same normalized root value. It uses the actual reciprocal source coefficients and residues of channel projectors on a regular invariant lattice. The same work gives an exact counterexample to equality of first normal derivatives. Root-value symmetry therefore helps organize the source without removing the normal-transport problem. The [all-partner first-normal theorem](../../notes/actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.md) now controls every supported reflected branch. A positive finite presentation of the complete generic source, combined with the exact Ward and Fourier identities, gives $|K'_B(q)|\leq C N^2(1+\log N)W_N^2$ for the branch-dependent generic tail $K_B$ and its positive normalized scalar $W_N$. It also gives a logarithmic relative bound for the coherent tail itself. The earlier two-current obstruction remains valid for those earlier relations alone; the new source presentation supplies the missing information. General higher normal orders and the completed physical transport metric remain open. ## Weighted Cauchy needs the right energy For a single complete physical column, write $C_j(t,u)$ for its entry at channel $j$, total degree $t$, and magnetic index $u=0,\ldots,t$. Let $\widehat f$ denote the finite Fourier transform specified by that column. The [exact Plancherel theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) now proves $$\frac{N}{j+1}|\widehat f(t/2)|^2\leq\sum_{u=0}^t|C_j(t,u)|^2\leq N|\widehat f(t/2)|^2.$$ The unused Fourier nodes vanish in the original polynomial, so the full discrete Fourier norm equals the actual physical norm. This works at both parities, including a half-integral midpoint. Combined with the exact bilinear measure, it gives the complete-channel energy profile and the full folded operator rate $5v_3/\pi$. Shared magnetic sums and phases remain when these operators are joined. The [shrinking-fold theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.md) extends that full real operator rate to every integer sequence $j/N\to1/2$. Fixed generic derivatives add only polynomial cost. This real norm statement permits a wider channel window than the separate complex-normal theorem; it supplies no complex confluent amplitude. There is also an exact [Fourier compiler for the complete-circle matching source](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md). Its matching magnetic indices are bounded integral Kirchhoff flows on the graph of physical cycles. The actual cups and caps make every cycle frequency even at both level parities, so its Fourier sums impose coupled congruences. The original mark supplies a one-unit charge. All source phases remain in this finite formula. Cauchy then gives a joint positive comparison of coherent cycle periods with the matching labels still shared. For a degree-$j$ polynomial $P(w)=\sum_k p_k w^k$ with the positive Fourier coefficients in question, the [coefficient-duality theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md) compares a coefficient with the best positive-radius bound. Their log-concavity gives $$p_k\leq\inf_{w>0}P(w)w^{-k}\leq(j+1)p_k.$$ The actual selected source action supplies the corresponding coefficient rate and an explicit positive minimizing radius on compact interior slope families. This is a two-sided local estimate. To use it globally, the actions must be joined on the compiler's flow and charge constraints, with its remaining phases retained. The [positive Fourier partition](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md) now supplies an explicit full-source comparison. Let $R$ be the number of matching circles, $C$ the number of restored physical cycles, and $A_{D,N}$ the original scalar for the fixed diagram $D$. The partition $Z_F(N)$, defined by the exact positive weights of that construction, satisfies $$|A_{D,N}|^2\leq N^{4R+2C-2}Z_F(N).$$ Every Kirchhoff equation, Fourier congruence and the original marked charge remains in $Z_F$. Its summands are products of positive coefficients and explicit sine-factorial weights. The equality before Cauchy retains all phases; this upper bound does not establish their survival. The [radial reconstruction obstruction](../../notes/actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) explains a remaining difficulty. At a strict positive radial saddle, all ordinary source factors would lie in the central selected domain. They therefore cannot all assemble into the complete geometric representation of the certified right-angled cut in one frame. This is a conditional geometric obstruction, with no asserted numerical rate gap. The exact phases and the exceptional matching-block route remain essential to investigate. A useful inequality has the form $$|K_N|^2\leq e^{o(N)}Z_N.$$ Weighted Cauchy can prove such an estimate once the inner product, original source cost, and dual cost are explicit. Choosing a positive form alone does not make those costs small. The repository contains exact counterexamples to proposed unmarked norms and to replacing a full magnetic tensor by its scalar rate. The whole-support boundary Gram theorem gives polynomial costs on each supported local cell. To obtain a theorem by this particular method, one must also control how those norms behave when cells are joined. Correlated seam labels must remain shared; maximizing local factors independently can change the answer. For the specified planar reflection doubles with three boundary representation labels, there is now a stronger [exact full-source identity](../../notes/actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.md): $$Z_N^{\mathrm{double}}=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal D_N}\frac{|Z_N^{\mathrm{half}}(\mathbf a)|^2}{\theta_N(\mathbf a)}\geq0.$$ Here $\mathcal D_N$ is the allowed set of boundary triples, and $\theta_N$ is the original positive boundary measure. Every interior color is already summed, with its phases retained, inside the half-packet. This includes the actual normals at both level parities. Since there are at most $N^3$ boundary triples, the doubled source differs from its largest squared weighted packet by at most that polynomial factor.
