Its asymptotic is therefore reduced to estimating the half-packets, whose internal cancellations have not disappeared. Positivity here allows zeros and is not a nonvanishing theorem for arbitrary plats. The retained Fourier phase now has an [exact integer quadratic form](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_centered_fourier_phase.md). The [holomorphic Legendre transport](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.md) restores that phase and the original winding characters in the selected ordinary action. Its [global chart](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_global_fourier_legendre_chart.md) is one-to-one on the full physical tube. These are action and coordinate theorems; they do not analytically continue individual finite Fourier coefficients or select the global source cycle. ## What the local estimates can and cannot conclude For sources with phases, a matching lower bound requires survival of the geometric contribution. A large positive comparison partition does not exclude cancellation in the original invariant. The [local energy geometry](../../notes/actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.md) makes this distinction explicit. The highest-weight block at the fold has the volume action of a variable ideal octahedron. Away from the fold, its actual measure forces a signed boundary term. Even at the real energy maximum, the marked complex phase need not be stationary. A global argument must use the original incidence and peripheral conditions to address those phases. The earlier positive-only Conway theorem used a different route, which is worth distinguishing from the current signed theorem. Exact support is an additive integer semigroup, which approximates a maximizing configuration along every sufficiently large level. Uniform factorial estimates prove the whole-source variational limit. The new geometric argument then proves that the reduced maximum is strict, matches the actual quadrilateral faces, and reconstructs the complete complement of every retained cylindrical factor. The new mixed-color proof supplies the additional filling estimates: exact leaf aliases lie in a square-zero radical, a strict seed-level gap survives arbitrary positive composition, and a finite complex lattice window has a nonzero Gaussian amplitude. This proves the long-full-twist source limit. The separate exact face-map and peripheral construction now identifies its rate with actual filled volume. The unchanged pure grammar still cannot produce knots by those fillings. Signed half twists change that source and its connectivity. The new [supporting-plane argument](../../notes/actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) bounds any number of propagated aliases by adding tangents to the same global action; the linear terms cancel under the actual wire constraints. A separately checked finite complex packet supplies the nonzero contribution. That earlier result applies to a fixed expression $C(FG)$ whose two children belong to its stated seed-generated grammar. Its marked geometry gives the corresponding filled knot and link equality. The strict-tree theorem at the start of this chapter removes that grammar restriction by the later character/probe induction, while retaining its explicit strictness and knot-pairing tests. The next boundary pieces now use the same original geometry: [literal prefix signs](../../notes/actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md), [generic complemented heads and the outgoing determinant](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md), and the [finite negative-clock boundary rate](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.md). The finite-current theorem also supplies an exact family of band weights that extracts the original root scalar after explicit bounded normalization. At the complete root this functional reduces to the existing coherent cut after a parameter change, so the residual framing freedom remains. This boundary-current route still lacks its unrestricted global internal-period comparison; the strict-tree theorem uses the different global argument explained above.

title: Methods and research approaches
text:
# Methods and research approaches The manuscript develops completed arguments under their stated hypotheses. This chapter also explains approaches whose general applications remain unresolved. Its purpose is to make the calculation behind each approach intelligible before sending the reader to a technical note. There are three different conclusions to distinguish. An **identity** rewrites the same finite quantity exactly. An **estimate** bounds its size, perhaps only from above. A **volume theorem** proves a limit for the original invariant and identifies the number in that limit with the volume of the specified knot complement. A useful identity or a sharp upper bound can be a completed result without being a volume theorem. Throughout, \(K\) is a fixed knot, \(N\ge2\) is the quantum level, and \(K_N(K)\) is the reduced Kashaev invariant; the unknot has value one. We use \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \zeta_N=q_N^2=e^{2\pi i/N}. \] Both roots occur in the literature. A formula written with \(q_N\) must not be compared with a formula written with \(\zeta_N\) without translating that convention. All diagrams and twist numbers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The [notation chapter](notation.md) gives the conventions used in the detailed calculations. The starting references are Kashaev's [definition of the invariant](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020) and [volume proposal](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9601025). The [Murakami–Murakami paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075) relates it to the colored Jones formulation. The finite invariant used here is specified directly; that relation is not a replacement for the source calculations. ## The estimate and the geometric identification Suppose an exact calculation splits the invariant into \[ K_N(K)=G_N+R_N. \] Here \(G_N\) is a specified contribution, including its original scalar factors, and \(R_N\) is everything else. Neither term is automatically a topological invariant on its own. A typical completed argument proves \[ G_N=a_N e^{NS},\qquad  rac{\log|a_N|}{N}\longrightarrow0,\qquad |R_N|\le e^{N(\operatorname{Re}S-\eta)+o(N)} \] for a fixed \(\eta>0\), with \(a_N
e0\) for sufficiently large \(N\). The complex number \(S\) is the critical value of the action in that calculation. Dividing by \(G_N\) shows that \(R_N/G_N	o0\), and hence \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =2\pi\operatorname{Re}S. \] There is still a geometric assertion to prove: \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] A formal critical point alone proves none of these three estimates. A positive comparison sum alone does not prove that \(a_N\) is nonzero. A representation of the knot group alone need not be the complete hyperbolic representation. ![The proof requires an exact decomposition, a nonzero geometric contribution, a bound on the remainder, and a geometric identification of the critical value.](../figures/methods-proof-map.svg) For the covered Conway constructions and decorated planar diagrams, the manuscript supplies all these steps. For an unchanged matched simple sphere with the stated Morse presentation and markings, the [geometric contribution theorem](../../notes/actual_morse_geometric_contribution.md) supplies the contribution and its actual filled volume; the general signed remainder estimate remains open. This is why that partial theorem is included without being advertised as a full volume theorem. ## Exact polynomials and shared face variables A **crossing circle** is an auxiliary component bounding a disk pierced by two strands. Removing twists and inserting these circles gives an augmented diagram. After cutting its finite tensor calculation along the projection regions, assign one commuting variable \(L_f\) to each face \(f\). The same face has the same variable at every incident crossing region. Put \(d=N-1\). For the complete-color source identities in this section take \(N\ge3\). A local operator \(p(\Omega)\), where \(\Omega\) is the specified pair Casimir matrix and \(p\) is a polynomial, gives a homogeneous polynomial \[ H_p(x,b,c,y) =\sum_{i+k+\ell+t=d}a_p(i,k,\ell,t)b^ix^ky^\ell c^t . \] The four variables label the four ordered faces adjoining that region. The coefficient \(a_p\) is the corresponding finite matrix coefficient after the stated change to face coordinates. A box carrying a linear map is sometimes called a *coupon* in tensor-diagram notation; here it means precisely this local operator. For the marked spherical construction with \(r\) crossing regions, there are \(r\) ordinary faces and two protected faces \(u,v\). Its shared polynomial is \[ S_N( oldsymbol\sigma) =\left[\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^dight] \left.\prod_{e=1}^{r}H_e( oldsymbol L;\sigma_e) ight|_{L_u=L_v=0}. \] The brackets mean coefficient extraction. The parameter \(\sigma_e\) is the spectral variable of crossing region \(e\). The two zero substitutions encode the original marked cut; they are not optional boundary conditions. The [finite source proof](../../notes/actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) and its [general Morse version](../../notes/research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) establish this identity with the scalar and endpoint conventions. For a simple illustration of why the variables must remain shared, \[ [z^2](a+bz)(c+dz)=bd. \] Replacing the two factors by separate maxima over their \(z\)-degrees would ignore the common target degree. In a knot diagram there are many such simultaneous constraints. The shared coefficient retains them before any asymptotic estimate. ![A local operator becomes a polynomial in its four adjacent faces. Multiplication and one common coefficient extraction retain the face-degree constraints. The general Morse proof also retains intervening cups and caps.](../figures/homogeneous-face-source.png) Repeated spectral roots require derivatives as well as values. If \(J=cI+U\) with \(U^2=0\), then \[ p(J)=p(c)I+p'(c)U. \] Thus knowing only \(p(c)\) does not determine the operator. This elementary example explains **Hermite data**: values and the derivatives prescribed by the multiplicities of the spectral roots. Derivatives in a spectral variable and derivatives in the generic quantum parameter are different data. Every use of a “normal term” in the notes must specify which derivative it means. The [finite filling estimate](../../notes/actual_uniform_filling_supremum_bound.md) bounds the next operation, inserting a fixed signed crossing power \(n\). For the original linear functional \(\mathcal L_N^n\) and a polynomial \(H\) of degree at most \(N-1\), \[ |\mathcal L_N^n H| \le (1+|n|/2)\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|H(\sigma)|. \] Its proof uses the exact values and derivatives at the spectral nodes. Applying it after the shared coefficient extraction adds no exponential cost at fixed twists. It does not estimate the supremum on its right. ## Positive sums, factorial asymptotics, and angle optimization The simplest variational argument applies to a positive sum. Suppose \(\mathcal X_N\) is a finite index set with \(|\mathcal X_N|\le N^c\), and the weights \(w_N(x)>0\) satisfy a uniform logarithmic estimate \[ \log w_N(x)=N F(x/N)+o(N). \] Here \(c\) is fixed and \(F\) is a continuous action on the limiting admissible set. The elementary inequalities \[ \max_x w_N(x)\le\sum_xw_N(x) \le|\mathcal X_N|\max_xw_N(x) \] give the exponential rate once admissible integer points approach a maximizer at every sufficiently large level. That last condition is an actual support question. A sequence of numerically favorable levels does not establish it. Quantum factorials lead to integrals of logarithms of sine functions. The basic example is \[  rac1N\log\prod_{j=1}^{\lfloor Ntfloor} 2\sin rac{\pi j}{N} \longrightarrow \int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi x)\,dx =- rac{\Lambda(\pi t)}{\pi}, \qquad 0<t<1, \] where \[ \Lambda(	heta)=-\int_0^	heta \log|2\sin s|\,ds \] is the Lobachevsky function. Near \(t=0,1\), the logarithmic singularities require endpoint estimates; uniformity there is not a consequence of a smooth Riemann-sum rule. This positive-sum argument is a discrete Laplace principle. It is distinct from both majorization and a Tauberian theorem, even though all three exploit positivity or convexity. The [positive Conway variational proof](../../notes/actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md) establishes the support and factorial estimates for its stated expressions. The [geometric realization](../../notes/actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) is a further argument. Positivity by itself neither constructs a knot complement nor proves invariance under changes of triangulation. A proposed positive tetrahedral model must also satisfy the appropriate local move identities with its full peripheral factors retained. An **angle structure** on an ideal triangulation assigns positive dihedral angles to its tetrahedra. In each tetrahedron the three angles at a vertex sum to \(\pi\); around each manifold edge the incident angles sum to \(2\pi\). Opposite tetrahedron edges have equal angles. These are linear conditions, so the allowed assignments form a relatively open convex polytope, when it is nonempty. For one positively oriented ideal tetrahedron with angle triple \((\alpha, eta,\gamma)\), its volume is \[ V(\alpha, eta,\gamma) =\Lambda(\alpha)+\Lambda( eta)+\Lambda(\gamma), \qquad \alpha+ eta+\gamma=\pi. \] The total volume is strictly concave on the positive angle domain. This is the concavity used in the Casson–Rivin variational approach; the volume is not described as a convex function to be minimized. Stationarity in all allowed directions supplies the remaining length and gluing conditions. The peripheral equations and the actual face identifications still have to be retained. The [marked positive gluing proof](../../notes/general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md) carries out these steps for its stated triangulation certificate. There are two logically different tasks here. One must find an interior critical point, and one must show that the cells and face pairings describe the intended manifold. Strict concavity proves uniqueness once those tasks have been met. It does not prove that every chosen triangulation has a positive solution. The [geometry chapter](geometry.md) explains the actual cells, cusp markings, and smooth fillings used in this project. For the precise standard criterion on an orientable manifold with torus boundary, see [Futer and Guéritaud, *From angled triangulations to hyperbolic structures*, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.0440). [Rivin's 1994 paper](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1994/139-3/p02) gives the earlier variational setting. The marked gluing proof linked above establishes the version used by this source rather than inferring it from the appearance of a dilogarithm. ## Weighted Cauchy and the cost of joining pieces Let \(\mathcal I_N\) be the original finite index set, and write a scalar evaluation as \(Z_N=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I_N}a_\alpha\). For any specified positive weights \(w_\alpha\), \[ |Z_N|^2 \le \left(\sum_\alpha w_\alphaight) \left(\sum_\alpha rac{|a_\alpha|^2}{w_\alpha}ight). \] This is Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the vectors \((\sqrt{w_\alpha})_\alpha\) and \((a_\alpha/\sqrt{w_\alpha})_\alpha\). A useful choice of weights must make both factors estimable for the original contraction. The matrix form says the same thing. If \(G\) is a positive definite Hermitian matrix, \(v\) is the source vector, and \(b\) is the row implementing the original closure, then \[ |bv|^2 \le (bG^{-1}b^*)(v^*Gv). \] The star denotes conjugate transpose. The first factor is the cost of the marked closure in the dual norm; the second is the source energy. Calling \(G\) a convenient inner product does not bound either cost. When two pieces share a boundary label \(j\), the contraction still has one common sum over \(j\). If its original measure is a positive number \(	heta_N(j)\), a useful exact form is \[ Z_{\mathrm{joined}} =\sum_j rac{Z_A(j)Z_B(j)}{	heta_N(j)}. \] Set \(F_A(j)=Z_A(j)/\sqrt{	heta_N(j)}\), and define \(F_B\) likewise. Cauchy bounds the square of the joined value by \((\sum_j|F_A(j)|^2)(\sum_j|F_B(j)|^2)\). It gives no lower bound on their overlap: the two vectors can be orthogonal. The [whole-support boundary estimate](../../notes/actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.md) and [exact joining identity](../../notes/actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) establish useful local inputs. For a reflected double, the two halves can be genuine complex conjugates in the specified pairing, giving a positive sum of squares. The [reflection-double theorem](../../notes/actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.md) proves precisely that identity. Its internal half-evaluations still contain their original phases. The general problem is to transport the estimates through the whole diagram and prove that the required contribution survives. ## What Fourier transformation preserves For a vector \(c=(c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1})\), define its unitary discrete Fourier transform by \[ \widehat c_k= rac1{\sqrt N} \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i jk/N}, \qquad 0\le k<N. \] The finite identity \[ \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi i k(j-\ell)/N} =N\,\mathbf1_{\{j=\ell\}} \] implies Parseval's identity \[ \sum_k|\widehat c_k|^2 =\sum_j|c_j|^2. \] Here \(\mathbf1\) is the indicator of the stated condition. This is an exact norm identity. It does not say that one Fourier coefficient equals the norm or that the phases of several contributions agree. For background on finite-group transforms and their normalization, see [Terras, *Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications*](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511626265). In the actual color transform, put \(c_0=K_N(K)\) and \(c_j=C_j(q_N)\) for \(1\le j<N\), where \(C_j\) is the original reduced, zero-framed ordinary-color evaluation. The [ordinary-color calculation](../../notes/ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md) identifies an energy \[ E_N=|K_N(K)|^2+R_N^{\mathrm{ord}}, \qquad 1\le R_N^{\mathrm{ord}}\le C N^B, \] with constants \(C,B\) depending on the fixed presentation. The superscript distinguishes this ordinary-color remainder from the earlier geometric remainder \(R_N\). The identification and polynomial bound are additional source statements; they are not part of abstract Parseval. If \(\log E_N/N	o\lambda>0\), then the Kashaev volume rate is \(\pi\lambda\). In particular \(C_1=1\), explaining the lower bound on \(R_N^{\mathrm{ord}}\). The ordinary-color bound uses the actual reduced root evaluation and its finite unitary realization, including the normalization cost. The face-source approach also uses finite cosine polynomials in auxiliary color parameters. Reflection of the allowed frequencies, the odd zero-frequency term, and the actual color-to-frequency map must be specified before invoking Fourier orthogonality. The [shared-cycle Fourier construction](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md) retains the flow equations, congruences, and original marked charge. Its [positive partition bound](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md) is an upper estimate. Discarding the remaining coefficient phases changes the quantity being estimated. ## Two different meanings of the Karamata suggestion **Majorization.** For real vectors \(u,v\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(u^\downarrow,v^\downarrow\) denote their coordinates in decreasing order. The relation \(u\prec v\) means \[ \sum_{i=1}^k u_i^\downarrow\le \sum_{i=1}^k v_i^\downarrow\quad(1\le k<m), \qquad \sum_i u_i=\sum_i v_i. \] For convex \(f\), it implies \(\sum_i f(u_i)\le\sum_i f(v_i)\). For concave \(f\), the inequality is reversed. This is the majorization form of Karamata's inequality. For matrices, exterior powers give analogous partial-sum inequalities for logarithms of singular values of a product. They control the largest available growth directions at each step. They do not force an evolving vector to stay on one chosen eigenvalue branch. The [regulator-majorization note](../../notes/regulator_majorization_and_source_energy.md) proves the relevant inequalities and gives a stronger sufficient criterion. One crucial input is a bistochastic positive transport that fixes the regulator observable: it preserves both identity and trace, as well as that specified observable. The criterion also retains its action factorization and endpoint costs. These properties have not been established for the general knot connection. The standard majorization definitions are developed in [Marshall, Olkin, and Arnold, *Inequalities: Theory of Majorization and Its Applications*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-68276-1). The matrix product result goes back to [Horn, *On the singular values of a product of completely continuous operators*](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.36.7.374). [Tao, Jeong, and Gowda](https://userpages.umbc.edu/~gowda/papers/trGOW20-02.pdf) discuss that matrix statement before developing its Jordan-algebra analogues. **Tauberian reasoning.** This is a different use of Karamata's name. For the positive energies \(E_N\) above, form \[ Z(s)=\sum_{N\ge2}E_Ne^{-sN}. \] The boundary of convergence gives \(\limsup_N N^{-1}\log E_N\). Under a separately proved power singularity \[ Z(\lambda+t)\sim C t^{-\alpha} \quad(t\downarrow0),\qquad C,\alpha>0, \] a positive-measure Tauberian argument gives a cumulative law \[ \sum_{2\le N\le x}e^{-\lambda N}E_N \sim  rac{C x^\alpha}{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}. \] Here \(\Gamma\) is the gamma function. The conclusion concerns a sum over levels, not each individual level. For example, the positive sequence \(E_N=e^{\lambda N}\) for even \(N\) and \(E_N=1\) for odd \(N\) has the corresponding cumulative exponential rate but no individual-level limit. This is an elementary sequence example, not a knot counterexample. The [Tauberian criterion](../../notes/actual_fourier_energy_tauberian_criterion.md) states a sufficient comparison between nearby levels and proves the implication. Neither that comparison nor the sharp Laplace singularity has been proved for the unrestricted knot source. The completed pretzel argument obtains its estimates directly and does not assume these missing Tauberian hypotheses. For the positive-measure statement, see [Michael Taylor, *Karamata's Tauberian Theorem*, §1](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2020/07/karamata.pdf). The linked local criterion gives a direct moment proof of the power-law case and explains the additional hypothesis needed at individual quantum levels. ## Complex critical points and the contribution of the original contour An oscillatory integral or finite sum can have several complex critical points. If its phase is \(F(z)\), a critical point solves \(
abla F(z)=0\). A local Gaussian calculation around a nondegenerate point involves the determinant of the Hessian matrix \(\partial^2F/\partial z_i\partial z_j\). The determinant's square root must follow the chosen contour and branch. The main issue is not just finding such a point. One must move the original contour to a neighborhood of it without losing boundary contributions, prove that the resulting coefficient is nonzero, and bound the complement. In the filling calculation, Fourier expansion produces integer indices \(\ell_e\), often called charges, in addition to the color variables. The original sum contains all those charges. A calculation for \(\ell_e=1\) alone does not establish the full asymptotic. The [whole geometric-period proof](../../notes/actual_morse_cross_filling_period.md) treats the large charges on the entire original intervals, retaining their endpoint currents. The remaining finite charges are compared on fixed complex neighborhoods. The phases, derivatives at repeated roots, and signs of independently chosen twists remain in the formula. For the covered full-invariant theorems, a further estimate controls the terms outside this geometric sector. The same distinction matters for slowly varying recurrences. Distinct instantaneous eigenvalues do not alone exclude exponentially significant transfer between branches. A small off-diagonal entry may be magnified after conjugation by exponential action weights. The [transport counterexamples and bounds](../../notes/actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md) explain the precise missing estimate. Thus neither diagonalizing each matrix separately nor naming a dominant classical branch is a substitute for controlling their ordered product. Local stationary-phase methods are treated in [Hörmander, *The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators I*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-61497-2). A related root-of-unity asymptotic problem is [Garoufalidis and Zagier's Nahm-sum analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07690). Its fixed-root radial limit and hypotheses differ from the growing-order roots and finite knot sums here; no identification of those objects is assumed. ## Quantum recurrences, the A-polynomial, and the selected solution The classical \(A\)-polynomial records peripheral eigenvalue pairs of representations of the knot group, after the chosen convention about reducible factors. Write \(M,L\in\mathbb C^	imes\) for the meridian and longitude eigenvalues. A branch of \[ A(M,L)=0 \] specifies a possible longitude as the meridian varies. It does not select the quantum invariant. The classical reference is [Cooper, Culler, Gillet, Long, and Shalen, *Plane curves associated to character varieties of 3-manifolds*](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~culler/papers/PlaneCurves/curves.pdf). The peripheral basis and the choice between eigenvalues and squared eigenvalues are part of the definition. A quantum recurrence acts on a specified sequence or function. For example, on a color sequence \(f_j\), one may set \[ (\widehat M f)_j=q^j f_j,\qquad (\widehat L f)_j=f_{j+1}, \qquad \widehat L\widehat M=q\,\widehat M\widehat L. \] This is an illustrative convention; squared meridian conventions replace \(q\) by \(q^2\). The operator, its coefficient ring, and its action must be stated together. A nonzero equation \(\widehat A f=0\) generally has several solutions. Finite initial data, normalization, and behavior at singular steps select the one representing the original invariant. This is the meaning of a **pointed recurrence** in the guide: the recurrence is accompanied by the data selecting its solution. The [pointed quantum A theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) retains those data, including derivatives at singular steps, for its covered family. Expressing an already proved limit through that recurrence is different from proving that an arbitrary quantization of the classical \(A\)-polynomial has the same limit. Prior recurrence results include [Garoufalidis and Lê on colored-Jones q-holonomicity](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309214) and [Brown, Dimofte, Garoufalidis, and Geer on the ADO family](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176). The latter's Theorem 4.4 retains an explicit framing and variable substitution. [Wilf and Zeilberger's multisum theory](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~zeilberg/mamarim/mamarimhtml/multiwz.html) provides the general creative-telescoping background. The local finite-source proof retains the actual boundary and root-normal data. These references do not supply a general identification of the classical geometric component. The proposed characteristic/deformation comparison is formulated in [Garoufalidis's 2004 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306230). The [geometric-characteristic theorem](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) proves a factor statement under its full asymptotic hypotheses: the selected geometric irreducible factor divides the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine all-level annihilator. It does not identify every factor, multiplicity, or the complete annihilator ideal. The [moving-meridian argument](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) supplies the actual state on its specified shrinking meridian neighborhood. The domain and derivative control are essential when substituting an asymptotic expansion into a recurrence. ## Torsors, logarithms, and the absolute volume A **torsor** for a group \(G\) is a nonempty space on which \(G\) acts freely and transitively: every two points differ by a unique group element, but there is no preferred origin. For example, the two square roots of a nonzero complex number form a torsor for \(\mu_2=\{1,-1\}\). Choices of logarithm differ by \(2\pi i\mathbb Z\). Horosphere decorations of a fixed positive cusped structure have one positive scale freedom per cusp. These examples are related bookkeeping problems, but they are not interchangeable torsors. The notes specify which group acts, what the points are, and which marked data choose a section. Passing to a cover can make a square root single-valued. It does not automatically choose the original quantum period or justify descent of its normalization. For torsors in algebraic families, one must also specify the base and the topology in which local sections exist; see [Stacks Project, §39.11](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0497). The elementary examples above have explicit fibers and actions. For an oriented ideal tetrahedron with shape \(z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0,1\}\), the signed volume is its Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm \[ D(z)=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z) +\arg(1-z)\log|z|, \] under its continuous single-valued interpretation. The dilogarithm initially satisfies \(\operatorname{Li}_2(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}z^n/n^2\) for \(|z|<1\), with analytic continuation elsewhere. A **regulator** here is the map taking the algebraic tetrahedral data, with their relations and markings, to the corresponding volume or complex period. The volume is positive for the positive orientation \(\operatorname{Im}z>0\). [Neumann's extended Bloch-group paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307092) explains how logarithmic lifts enter the complex regulator. The ordinary Bloch–Wigner volume and that lifted complex quantity must be distinguished. Algebraic gluing equations can make the selected shapes algebraic. That does not make their dilogarithm values algebraic numbers. Nor does algebraicity select an integration cycle for a quantum sum. To identify an action with volume, the proofs retain the actual shapes and based peripheral words, compare their differentials, and fix the additive constant at a known complete structure. For a filled auxiliary cusp, let \(U,V\) be the logarithms of the similarity multipliers of its primitive meridian and longitude. Equivalently, these are twice the selected eigenvalue logarithms, with the eigenvalues divided by their complete central signs before taking logarithms. In the convention used by the general Morse theorem, filling the primitive slope \(\mu+p\lambda\) imposes \[ U+pV=-2\pi i. \] The integer \(p\) is a fixed surgery coefficient. The specified logarithm is stronger data than the exponentiated equality \(e^{U+pV}=1\). Smooth metric completion, rather than the exponentiated equation alone, identifies the resulting hyperbolic manifold. The [regulator and completion proof](../../notes/general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) gives this argument in detail. The standard peripheral deformation and volume-potential framework is [Neumann and Zagier, *Volumes of hyperbolic three-manifolds*](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1016/0040-9383(85)90004-7/fulltext.pdf). The signs, primitive periods, and eigenvalue-versus-ratio convention in the displayed filling equation come from the local marked proof, not from an unrecorded change of that reference's coordinates. The [A-structure and torsor route](../library.html#torsors) retains this algebraic information and the selected period. Its general unresolved question is a source-preserving norm and survival theorem. An algebraic branch, a chosen logarithm, and a calibrated classical volume are substantial inputs, but they do not by themselves estimate the quantum invariant. ## Local recoupling, exceptional factors, and shared cores Changing the order in which representation factors are paired is called **recoupling**. Its matrix coefficients are quantum \(6j\), or Racah, coefficients. A \(q\)-Hahn polynomial is one of the finite orthogonal-polynomial expressions that appears after the specified index changes. The scalar formula must be used with its original row and column normalization; multiplying by a nonconstant factorial factor changes its exponential action. The [local Racah calculation](../../notes/actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) gives an exact kernel, and the [local volume theorem](../../notes/actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) identifies the action in its supported domain. A **hyperideal** vertex lies outside hyperbolic space in the projective model, with the incident edges crossing hyperbolic space; its polar plane supplies the truncation. These local tetrahedra are comparison cells. Their existence alone does not identify a glued knot complement. The local \(6j\)-volume relation is established literature: see [Costantino, *6j-symbols, hyperbolic structures and the Volume Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611399) and [Costantino and Murakami's non-integral representation model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4277). The [coverage comparison](../../notes/literature_hyperideal_racah_volume_coverage.md) records the root substitutions, supported angle ranges, and different regularizations. No novelty is claimed for the general local-volume mechanism. For the general right-angled source, a common choice of frame cannot put all local factors in the same strict selected domain. The [frame obstruction](../../notes/actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) and [localization theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) locate the exceptional pair and control the other factors under their stated hypotheses. Regrouping that pair gives an exact larger block. Its full operator norm and the remaining coherent contraction still have to be controlled. A favorable scalar coefficient is not a bound for that entire block. The cube calculations test a different issue: a network can contain a geometric region shared by several local pieces. The [four-rung cube result](../../notes/actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.md) sums specified channels and proves a volume rate for that partially projected source. Other cycle channels remain fixed. Removing those projections and handling all levels is a separate problem. The [shared-core geometry](../../notes/actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md) shows why simply adding local cell maxima can miss a genuine global volume term. ## Which approaches are retained, and where to read them The table covers the organized research routes. Each route includes its exact results, examples, and limitations; the [archive](../archive.html) also preserves earlier versions and unsuccessful constructions. Historical claims should be read with their corrections and dates, not promoted to current theorems. | Approach | What the argument does | Current place in the project | |---|---|---| | [Tangle trees and planar decoration](../library.html#equality) | Exact composition, strict estimates on shared variables, and a nonzero filling contribution. | Full volume theorems for the stated constructions and twist conditions. | | [Moving the main meridian](../library.html#moving-meridian) | Controls the actual reduced state on microscopic meridian neighborhoods and computes its correction. | Completed for the stated tree classes and domains; broader resonant continuation is separate. | | [Finite source and transport](../library.html#source) | Preserves matrix entries, spectral derivatives, endpoint terms, and shared coefficient constraints. | Exact identities and several bounds; an identity alone is not a volume theorem. | | [Angle optimization and geometry](../library.html#geometry) | Constructs cells, gluing, peripheral holonomy, and smooth ends. | Actual volume identification under the stated geometric hypotheses. | | [A-structures and torsors](../library.html#torsors) | Retains the selected solution, algebraic branch, logarithms, and regulator normalization. | Pointed and selected-factor theorems in covered families; general period estimates remain open. | | [Global maxima of the signed source](../library.html#sharp-source) | Keeps the common degree constraints while estimating possible competing regions. | Partial bounds and classifications; the unrestricted signed remainder comparison is open. | | [Fourier, Cauchy, and energy](../library.html#fourier) | Exact norm identities and weighted inequalities, with original boundary costs. | Completed local estimates and special-family arguments; no general lower bound follows from positivity. | | [Cube and shared-core calculations](../library.html#cube) | Tests joining formulas and the extra geometry carried by a non-tree core. | Proved projected statements; the full unprojected cube limit is not asserted. | | [Obstructions, transport, and alternative criteria](../library.html#frontier) | Records counterexamples to shortcuts, cross-level conditions, finite-cover questions, and remaining source estimates. | Research tools and precise open questions, rather than additional claimed knot families. | Finite covers also belong to the last two algebraic and transport routes. Hyperbolic volume multiplies by the degree of a finite covering map between complete hyperbolic manifolds. The original invariant has no automatic matching covering formula. The peripheral eigenvalue map and selected state would have to be transported and descended explicitly. A cover is therefore a possible construction tool, not an established reduction of the general conjecture. ## Literature and what is borrowed from it The following references identify the origin and established scope of the methods. The linked repository proofs state the actual versions used here. Historical attribution, an external theorem, a local proof, and a proposed extension are different kinds of evidence. The citations beside the methods identify the relevant statement and its role. For a first reading, the following sequence is useful: 1. **Invariant and volume question:** Kashaev's 1995 definition and 1997 volume paper, followed by Murakami–Murakami for the colored Jones relation. 2. **Geometric optimization:** Rivin's variational paper and Futer–Guéritaud for angle structures, allowed tangent directions, and the precise critical-point criterion. 3. **Norm estimates:** Terras for finite Fourier analysis; Marshall–Olkin–Arnold and Horn for majorization and product singular values. Weighted Cauchy and finite Parseval are proved explicitly above. 4. **Cross-level asymptotics:** Taylor's Tauberian notes. Compare the cumulative conclusion with the additional source-transport condition in the local criterion. 5. **Recurrences:** Wilf–Zeilberger for multisum elimination, then the colored-Jones and ADO papers for the objects and conventions concerned. Keep the classical A-curve and the proposed characteristic comparison separate. 6. **Regulators and peripheral geometry:** Neumann–Zagier for the local deformation potential, Neumann for logarithmic regulator data, and the explicit torsor definitions for any claimed group action. 7. **Local asymptotics versus a whole knot period:** Costantino's \(6j\)-volume result and the Nahm-sum comparison illustrate related problems with different normalizations and limiting regimes. The complete-source estimates and contour arguments remain the additional work in this project. The literature search is a coverage and attribution check. It does not turn an external paper into an unchecked proof input, or turn a local calculation into a theorem about an arbitrary knot. The manuscript states the actual hypotheses and supplies the arguments used for its conclusions.

title: Why the limiting action is the actual knot volume
text: # Why the limiting action is the actual knot volume ## The circle packing for a general planar core The [planar decoration theorem](../../notes/actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) constructs its geometry from a simple triangulation of the sphere. Remove one triangle and prescribe three mutually tangent boundary circles. Maximize the concave angle function subject to angle sum \(\pi\) in each triangle and \(2\pi\) at each interior vertex. The proof establishes strict feasibility by a finite counting argument, so the maximum has positive angles. Its multipliers give positive circle radii. Euclidean triangles with side lengths equal to sums of adjacent radii then develop into one embedded disk. Their angle sums remove interior holonomy, and the convex triangular boundary gives degree one. This proves that the circles have precisely the prescribed contacts. The white-circle planes and the circles through the three contact points of each triangle bound the required convex ideal right-angled polyhedron. A terminal insertion adds the circle in one triangular gap. All old circles remain fixed. Its three new supporting disks lie inside the old shaded supporting disk, so the attached octahedron respects every other face inequality. Repeating the insertion preserves convexity, even when the original sphere has separating triangles or the tangle connections have cycles. The two projection copies recover the actual augmented link, with the original crossing-disk face maps. The complete metric is the starting point for filling. The selected peripheral logarithms satisfy the actual primitive equation \(U_e+p_eV_e=-2\pi i\). The logarithmic cusp development has angular period \(2\pi\), so its metric completion is a smooth solid torus on that slope. The main meridian and longitude remain parabolic and the knot cusp is complete. Thus the final volume is that of the knot complement; it is generally smaller than the augmented volume. A formula involving dilogarithms is not yet a geometric volume formula. To obtain the volume on the right side of the theorem, the proof must construct the intended manifold, verify its metric, and retain the meridian and longitude used for each filling. This chapter explains those steps and the different roles of the local geometric results. For the [strict Conway tree theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md), all of these steps are proved. The full quantum estimates and the nonzero local contribution are proved as well. The result concerns the actual resulting knot complement, with its main cusp left unfilled. The more general plat constructions discussed later have their own hypotheses; a missing estimate in one of those routes is not a gap in the strict-tree theorem. ## Filling conditions checked at individual circles For the ordered tree with one crossing circle at every vertex, let \(d_v\) count the incident octahedral pieces in one projection half and let \(n_v\) be the signed crossing power. The [geometric criterion](../../notes/actual_all_circle_vertexwise_geometry.md) \[ \sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}\ge630 \] at each vertex constructs a positive deformation through the full filling path. The contraction bound is independent of the number of vertices. The original primitive filling curve has logarithmic period \(-2\pi i c\), for \(0\le c\le1\). At \(c=1\) it makes exactly one full turn, and the endpoint is the smooth metric on the original knot complement. The main knot cusp remains complete. The volume decreases along this path by the Schläfli formula. Its constant is fixed at the complete augmented exterior, which has two regular ideal octahedra per tree edge. This proves that the continued action is the actual hyperbolic volume. To obtain a quantum volume equality one also needs the finite-sum estimate; the [directed subtree theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) supplies it under its stronger finite numerical test. In particular, it suffices that every vertex independently satisfy \(|n_v|\ge2^{27}\) or \(d_v\ge2^{28}\), with the original knot pairing. This proves the actual complement-volume equality. The summed criterion remains a useful alternative. The geometric bound \(630\) alone is not a quantum estimate. ## The geometric objects and the required checks Start with the augmented diagram: each twist region has an auxiliary crossing circle around its two strands. Cutting along the projection sphere and the original crossing disks divides its exterior into pieces with labeled faces. The labels remember exactly how to glue the pieces back. They also remember which curves on each torus end are the original meridian and longitude. An **ideal vertex** lies at the boundary at infinity of hyperbolic space. A small horosphere about it cuts a Euclidean polygon from each adjacent cell. These polygons are the vertex links. In a complete link complement, the polygons around each end glue to a Euclidean torus. This torus is a cross-section of a **cusp**, the noncompact end of the manifold. Checking only that the dihedral angles sum to \(2\pi\) does not establish cusp completeness; the horospherical polygons must also match with the correct translations. An **angle structure** assigns positive dihedral angles to the proposed cells while satisfying their internal angle relations and the sum around every glued edge. Its volume is the sum of the cell volumes. The angles still retain the actual incidence equations: two copies of one manifold edge are not independent variables. At an interior maximum, variation in every allowed direction gives the shape-matching equations. The proof must then show that these equations produce the original face pairings and complete ends. A **marked** construction retains the chosen peripheral curves and their basepaths. This matters after filling. The equation that closes a meridian disk depends on a primitive pair of curves on the torus, not just on an unlabeled complex cusp shape. Replacing a primitive longitude by twice that curve would change the filling problem. ## The geometric proof for the explicit degree-and-twist bound The [quantitative theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) uses a particularly simple decomposition of the actual exterior. Each vertex of its ordered tree is a crossing circle, and each tree edge supplies one octahedron in each projection half. Inserting a terminal child attaches an octahedron along a shaded crossing-disk triangle. Reading the four strand joins shows that its other three shaded faces are exactly the new disk faces. The adjacent white projection faces join in their original order. ![One octahedron is attached along the shaded triangle of a projection half. Equal labels are identified with opposite boundary orientations. The two vertices O_v and O_w belong to the parent and child crossing circles; A, B, C and D are main-strand ends.](../figures/octahedral-page-attachment.svg) There are \(E\) octahedra in each half for a tree with \(E\) edges. The [ordered decomposition proof](../../notes/actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) retains the left and right insertion order, the actual rotations of child balls, and the single original half twist at each circle. These data determine the original manifold and its primitive cusp curves. The [angular formulas](../../notes/actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) subdivide the pair of octahedra into eight ideal tetrahedra. All shapes are \(i\) at the complete point and remain positively oriented for \(|\tau_v|<10^{-2}\). The numerical bound of the theorem puts the entire path of filling equations inside this chart. Along the path, the actual primitive slope has logarithmic period \(-2\pi i c\), with \(0\le c\le1\). Its angular period is therefore \(2\pi c\). The [completion argument](../../notes/actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) proves that each auxiliary end is a punctured metric tube with these periods. At \(c=1\), its core is smooth. Attaching these cores performs the original surgeries, while the main cusp remains complete. The boundary correction to the complex action cancels the filling term; the resulting real value is the volume of this knot complement. The constant is fixed by the complete augmented link, whose volume is \(2E\,v_8\), where \(v_8\) is the volume of a regular ideal octahedron. This argument allows the full meridian logarithm to accumulate one turn even when each angular variable is small. It is the step needed for the short powers permitted by the criterion. The [main-cusp continuation](../../notes/actual_all_circle_preferred_cusp.md) then compares the marked representations and follows the preferred longitude to the smooth endpoint. ## The strict-tree construction The [net-twist reduction](../../notes/actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) extends the use of this construction. It combines specified twist boxes by actual isotopies, retaining any half-turn of an intervening tangle. When its output is a strict presentation with sufficiently large combined twists, the geometric theorem below gives the output knot exterior its complete metric. The isotopy identifies that exterior with the input knot exterior, so the metric and its volume transfer directly. This comparison is made after the twists are inserted; it does not identify the auxiliary crossing-circle cusps of two different augmented presentations. A Conway expression is a recorded sequence of two operations on tangles: stack two boxes, or turn one box through a quarter-turn. Its leaves are the original twist regions. The finite strictness test in the theorem is a compatibility test for the positive angles of these operations. It is not a claim that any written tangle expression becomes hyperbolic when its displayed exponents are large. The geometric pieces follow these operations. Each leaf contributes an ideal quadrangular pyramid, and each retained product contributes an ideal triangular prism. Their volumes agree with the local terms of the complete quantum action. Each quadrilateral gluing face has four ordered ideal vertices. The order specifies which vertex is identified with which when two cells are attached; it is part of the geometry, not just a label for a boundary variable. The metrics of these faces are determined by derivatives of the action. When the full action is stationary under the shared-index constraints, those metrics agree across the actual ordered product faces. The [general strict-mask geometry theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) proves that these pieces assemble with the original cyclic orders, including turns and the different boundary edge types. An edge type records whether its face is supplied directly by a leaf crossing disk or by the surrounding projection region. The bookkeeping is needed to prevent a formally matching quadrilateral from being attached to the wrong side. The proof rules out the vertex identifications that would collapse a shaded triangle, checks the edge cycles, and constructs positive rectangular cusp links. The final identification with the diagram uses the [literal bowtie cut](../../notes/actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). A bowtie is the pair of triangular faces exposed by one crossing disk. Its four outer corners are joined by the actual main strands of the diagram. Reading those joins in their projection order determines every remaining face. Reversing the cut therefore recovers the original link exterior with its original auxiliary circles. Matching a count of vertices or a total volume would not suffice. The [marked deformation theorem for the full strict class](../../notes/actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) extends the complete construction to nearby complex auxiliary colors. Its face maps satisfy the original group relations, including their translational parts. Every main cusp remains parabolic. On an auxiliary cusp it supplies specified logarithms \(U_i,V_i\) of the peripheral multipliers. Here a logarithm includes its chosen branch, so it records a winding that a bare eigenvalue would forget. Write the actual twist weight as \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\), with \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) recording a retained half twist. The filling equation uses the primitive basis of this actual half-twisted link. For every fixed choice of sufficiently large independent signed \(p_i\), the nearby solution gives a smooth filling of the auxiliary cusp. The main knot cusp is never filled. The action, with its boundary correction, equals the volume of that resulting knot complement. The quantum theorem uses exactly this solution and normalization. The next sections give further details and explain the older constructions that supplied parts of this argument. ## The full geometric longitude for strict trees A cusp-shape calculation determines the tangent of a peripheral curve, but the [strict-tree longitude theorem](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) identifies the entire nearby curve for every covered strict long-filling construction. A meridian goes once around the knot. Its preferred longitude follows the knot once with zero linking number. Let \(M\) and \(L\) be their determinant-one holonomy eigenvalues on the same line. Write \(\mathcal E_T\) for the original physical quarter-turn edges, and let \(x_e(M)\) be their continued stationary indices. With \(X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}\), the formula is \[ L(M)=-M^{-w(D)-\sum_i n_i} \prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)}. \] Here \(w(D)\) is the oriented writhe and \(n_i\) are the original signed crossing powers. The filling path fixes the logarithms and selects the branch; algebraic elimination without that marking would retain other representations. The extension to a junction without a crossing circle uses a literal identity box \(R^0\). Add a crossing circle around its two straight strands and fill the new circle's meridian. This returns the original tangle. The proof fixes a product collar, a basepoint and access paths before taking any representation, so both based puncture loops are preserved in order. It then compares the full boundary tuples of matrices. Agreement of one scalar trace would not suffice. ![Meridian filling removes an added circle around a zero-crossing box while preserving the ordered based strand meridians.](../figures/zero-circle-junction.svg) At a bare product junction the new angular variable has a nondegenerate stationary point. Eliminating it returns the original product action and its Hessian. The full system remains regular when a physical edge has index one half; the proof does not assume that a folded quadratic equation has a simple root. The resulting representation factors through the original filled knot group and agrees with its marked geometric deformation. Combining this identification with the full filtered expansion gives the selected geometric factor of each genuine all-level annihilator for the covered strict long fillings. The original circle-tree operator theorem also applies under the earlier summed condition or the local bound \(2^{-120}\). No equality of the full A-polynomial or of recurrence ideals is asserted. Marked ambient isotopy carries the intrinsic curve and factor to the covered net-twist and arbitrary-closure inputs, even when their auxiliary augmented links differ. ## How the cells and the diagram are identified The [global Conway geometry theorem](../../notes/actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) supplies the face-pairing certificate for every cylindrical factor in its original positive seed-generated grammar. Here cylindrical closure joins each lower external strand to the corresponding upper strand; it differs from joining the two upper ends to each other and the two lower ends to each other. The later strict-mask theorem extends the geometric construction as described above. A leaf is an ideal quadrangular pyramid. A multiplication gate is a convex ideal triangular prism. Their volumes are exactly the source actions, and their ordered quadrilateral metrics are exponentials of the action derivatives. ![The source's leaf pyramid and multiplication prism. Blue faces are quadrilateral gluing faces with ordered vertices; the shaded leaf triangles retain the actual crossing-disk pairing.](../figures/conway-cells.png) Stationarity makes the shared quadrilateral gluing faces isometric under the literal stack maps. A boundary barrier proves that every unforced cell at the maximum is strict. The cells assemble into a convex ideal polyhedron; the actual cylindrical closure leaves only right-angled boundary edges. Reversing the projection and crossing-disk cuts reconstructs the original link. Four-step edge cycles give angle $2\pi$ with identity return, and matched rectangular horosphere links prove cusp completeness. Thus the two-copy volume is the volume of the actual complement. The [closed bowtie-cut proof](../../notes/actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) identifies every oriented white and shaded face from the literal original wires. It corrects an earlier overstatement about open cells: a quadrilateral gluing face alone is not half of the physical four-punctured tangle boundary. The closed reconstruction uses the entire labeled ribbon graph and reversible disk cut. It also gives each complete crossing-circle cusp its primitive shape $2i\cot(\pi x_i)$. The final product gate is forced flat and is removed from the geometric cell list using its exact unit source coefficient. This does not delete a quantum contribution or a link component. The [local cell proof](../../notes/actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md) also identifies source associativity with two triangulations of one actual ideal cube. A cap closure joins the two upper endpoints to one another and the two lower endpoints to one another. The [cap-sum reduction](../../notes/actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md) goes further: an actual two-punctured separating sphere splits every cap-closed product into componentwise connected sums. The quantum source factors and the angle polytope splits with it. This gives connected sums of theta links with strictly positive rate $4k v_8$, although the whole complement is not hyperbolic for $k\geq2$. ## Algebraic shapes and their volume regulator The [algebraic optimizer theorem](../../notes/positive_source_algebraic_volume_period.md) applies to every rational affine ideal-angle problem with positive rational weights. On the smallest face containing the maxima, flat atoms contribute zero. The remaining Hessian is definite after quotienting by the rational directions that leave all nonflat angles unchanged. Exponentiated stationarity then proves that the nonflat shapes are algebraic, including boundary and nonunique maxima. The Bloch group packages algebraic tetrahedron shapes together with the relations obtained by changing a triangulation. Its regulator evaluates those shape symbols by the oriented dilogarithm volume. The [Bloch regulator calculation](../../notes/actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.md) proves that the conjugate-antisymmetrized shape sum is a rational Bloch class with regulator equal to the source maximum. For the retained cylindrical factors, the new actual cell realization supplies its geometric interpretation. The class comparison takes place after passing to a common finite conjugation-stable number field containing the source shapes and all glued ideal vertex coordinates. The two copies have opposite mirror orientations, producing precisely the shape symbols $[z]-[\overline z]$ of the geometric fundamental chain; no identification with the geometric trace field is claimed. For a fixed positive Conway expression \(E\) in that earlier seed-generated grammar, let \(Z_{E,N}\) be its complete quantum sum. Its statement is $$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log Z_{E,N} =R_{F_E}(B_E),\qquad B_E=\sum_j([z_j]-[\overline{z_j}])\in B(F_E)_{\mathbb Q}.$$ Here \(z_j\) are the algebraic shapes, \(F_E=\mathbb Q(z_j,\overline{z_j})\) is the number field containing them and their conjugates, \(B(F_E)_{\mathbb Q}\) is the rational Bloch group, and \(R_{F_E}\) is its volume regulator at the specified complex embedding. For a retained cylindrical factor its value is now proved to be the actual complement volume. This regulator argument alone does not identify a generic main-meridian characteristic factor or prove arbitrary short-filling limits. The separate strict-tree longitude theorem above now identifies the selected factor for the covered long-filled knots. Actual all-level quantum A-operators exist by the finite cut-state proof, and the pointed operator-period theorem gives the same volume limit for those knots. Fixing an output index of an open tangle changes the maximization problem. The resulting function of the scaled output \(b\) is its boundary profile. The [boundary profile theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_boundary_volume_relation.md) also gives a full limit for every coefficient approaching any output $b\in[0,1]$. On $(0,1)$ its optimizer is unique and analytic, and its boundary conjugate is the actual quadrilateral modulus $\exp(-v'_E(b)/\pi)$. This is a geometric meaning for the source boundary relation; the variable is not yet the knot's peripheral holonomy. ## The deformed source has actual peripheral holonomy In the earlier positive grammar, the [marked deformation theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) constructs a representation of the actual link group for the auxiliary-color critical branch. Exact Möbius identities establish every white seam and shaded edge relation, including translations. All main cusps stay parabolic. Let \(\chi_i\) be the scaled auxiliary-color deficit, and let \(\phi(\chi)\) be the selected limiting action. For each auxiliary circle the primitive logarithms are $$U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i,\qquad V_i=-2\partial_i\phi(\chi).$$ The function \(G=2\pi i\phi\), called a primitive because its derivative is the displayed peripheral one-form, satisfies $dG=\tfrac12\sum_i V_i\,dU_i$, with its constant fixed by the complete fundamental-chain volume. Exponentiated source stationarity gives an algebraic marked peripheral branch; the selected branch is locally a Lagrangian graph: the exterior derivative of that peripheral one-form vanishes on it. This statement concerns the auxiliary peripheral coordinates, with the main cusps held parabolic. The displayed peripheral multipliers are squared SL eigenvalues, and no entire A-polynomial is inferred merely by elimination. At the original filling saddle, $U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i$ holds in the primitive disk marking. The actual nearby representation and the boundary-corrected regulator then identify the full quantum rate with the volume of the correctly filled complement. This applies to every retained robust factor and independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral fillings of any selected auxiliary circles. The component theorem keeps its link-only scope explicit. ## Half twists preserve the marked action through a shear The [odd-coupon deformation](../../notes/actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) changes the shaded face pairings and checks their edge words at general complex parameters. The original odd-link peripheral paths give $$U_i^\epsilon=U_i^0-\frac{\epsilon_i}{2}V_i^0,\qquad V_i^\epsilon=V_i^0,\qquad G_\epsilon=G_0-\sum_i\frac{\epsilon_i}{8}(V_i^0)^2.$$ These are also the exact derivatives and quadratic correction of the selected finite-source action. Write $M_i=e^{U_i}$ and $L_i=e^{V_i}$ for these auxiliary peripheral multipliers. On the marked double cover $\ell_i^2=L_i$, the half-longitude change becomes the integral monomial map $M_i^\epsilon=M_i^0\ell_i^{-\epsilon_i}$. The source selects the square root and its logarithm. The square root is part of the marked data. Changing it changes the logarithmic branch, so it cannot be discarded when comparing the source and the filling equation. This is the concrete peripheral data described as a torsor in the technical note. ![Left: a primitive filling slope on a schematic cusp torus. Right: local sheets of the peripheral square-root cover, with the selected branch and integral shear.](../figures/peripheral-torsor.png) The square is a fundamental domain, not a metric cusp shape. Its amber segments form the single primitive curve $\mu+2\lambda$ after opposite sides are identified. The two sheets on the right are a local picture of $\ell^2=L$; the cover is not asserted to split globally. The selected logarithm retains the primitive filling equation $U+pV=-2\pi i$. Smooth filling uses the primitive basis of the link with its retained half twists. Substituting a half-integer slope into the pure-link formula would double the primitive rotation angle when denominators are cleared. The actual odd-link construction avoids that error, keeps main cusps parabolic, and fixes the regulator at its complete volume. Together with the full changed-source estimates it yields the [general signed Conway knot and link theorem](../../notes/actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md). ## A second route: circle patterns for general augmented plats For a connected labeled right-angled augmented plat at any fixed bridge width, the [signed complete-source theorem](../../notes/general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) identifies the original source rate with the actual complete volume. The [fixed complex core theorem](../../notes/actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md) now gives a nonzero analytic asymptotic for its complete-image external-color term. This construction is independent of the strict-tree recursion; the statements below retain their own hypotheses. A circle pattern represents the labeled boundary faces by circles or lines at infinity, with the prescribed tangencies. The [marked circle-pattern theorem](../../notes/actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) reconstructs the two exceptional boundary faces as parallel lines and solves simultaneously for all finite circle centers and radii. The original positive face Hessian, followed by elementary rigidity of the center triangles, proves that this system has an invertible Jacobian. Its unique nearby solution has exactly the stationary radii of the source action, with one shared strip width and the selected boundary eigenlines retained. ![The actual marked lines retain their shared width and the selected eigenlines as matching tangencies deform.](../figures/marked-circle-strip.png) The [primitive collar theorem](../../notes/actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) computes the actual side pairing, selected eigenflag and half-twist shear, including a common marked-line limit. The [global geometric assembly](../../notes/actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) verifies the full original group presentation and identifies the core's limiting action with the marked geometric deformation. For complex meridian logs it retains the boundary correction $\tfrac12\sum_i\operatorname{Re}U_i\operatorname{Im}V_i$; for real external deficits this correction vanishes. For an unrestricted plat, these geometric and local core statements still need bounds on the remaining reflected-color terms before they imply a full filling theorem. Several separately certified plat families and the strict-tree class already have those bounds; see the [results](results.md) and [remaining scope](frontier.md). ![The same crossing-disk collar in two coordinates. On the left, the ordered contact points lie on the input and output circles. A Möbius coordinate sends the two selected eigenpoints to zero and infinity; on the right, the actual side pairing is a dilation. The auxiliary meridian follows its inverse.](../figures/deformed-circle-collar.png) An identity smoothing replaces a specified crossing-disk coupon by the identity and retains the remaining face identifications. For such a diagram, the [block capacity theorem](../../notes/actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) removes the need to assume an attained positive-radius minimum. Here capacity is the infimum of the positive weighted expression used for a coefficient bound. The theorem splits degenerate angle problems along two-edge cycles and constructs each simple block's actual polyhedron. The [block representation and volume theorem](../../notes/actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) then retains the original face pairings and realizes their volume sum as a regulator of the original group. Its deleted meridians lie in the kernel, so the [strict-kernel theorem](../../notes/general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) proves strict loss for every nonempty connected untwisted smoothing with finite capacity. Loop-infeasible cases already have an arbitrarily low capacity bound. The chain argument uses a controlled finite degeneration: cut corners have a common horospherical height and mutual distance $O(T^{-1})$. A uniform short-edge tetrahedron estimate makes the added volume vanish. Arbitrary ideal vertices merely approaching one another would not justify this step. The [near-maximal-volume corollary](../../notes/general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md) also gives uniform gaps from fixed marked peripheral trace conditions; applying those gaps to the remaining quantum color complement is still a source-estimate problem. ## A local tetrahedron is a genuine geometric result In the local theorem with four external representation labels, the exact half-shifted color coordinate is $$a_e=\frac{j_e+1/2}{N},\qquad \alpha_e=\pi-2\pi a_e.$$ The normalized scalar action is identified with the volume of the truncated hyperideal tetrahedron with these dihedral angles. The proof constructs the Gram matrix of the outward face normals in the Lorentz model of hyperbolic space, recovers edge lengths, checks the volume differential, and fixes the additive constant by an ideal calibration. Boundary values are continuous volume extensions. ![A truncated tetrahedron in a combinatorial projection. Blue triangles indicate polar truncation faces; the hyperbolic metric comes from the Gram matrix.](../figures/truncated-tetrahedron.png) This is stronger than observing that a factorial action resembles a dilogarithm. It is also local: a collection of such tetrahedra does not automatically form the knot complement. ## The global angle slice carries the topology An actual ideal triangulation specifies which faces are glued, which tetrahedron edges belong to each manifold edge, and which peripheral curves represent meridians and longitudes. Its angle constraints must retain this incidence. At a candidate maximum, stationarity must hold in every allowed angle direction. The corresponding shape and length equations must make adjacent cells agree. The resulting developing map must have the intended winding and end behavior. Complete cusps, or the specified filled peripheral equations, are part of the certificate. The [source-volume certificate](../../notes/source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md) keeps these requirements explicit. An algebraic critical point can be isolated and still belong to the wrong component or have the wrong peripheral marking. ## A general certificate through volume maximization For an actual marked ideal triangulation with torus vertex links, the [positive gluing criterion](../../notes/general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md) gives a direct proof of the Casson–Rivin equivalence: an interior critical point of the ideal-tetrahedron volume function is exactly a complete positive gluing. Strict concavity makes it the unique maximum, including over the closed angle polytope, and its value is the actual complement volume. The proof keeps the geometry explicit. Lagrange multipliers prescribe one truncated length for each global edge. These lengths determine compatible corner horospheres; the face maps then match them, giving complete flat cusp tori. Conversely, compatible horospheres make the geometric volume stationary under all allowed angle variations. There is a finite algebraic certificate using positive upper-half-plane phases and positive multiplier variables. The unique optimum has algebraic shapes. Neither its dilogarithm volume nor the original quantum period is asserted to be an algebraic number. Existence of an interior optimum on a proposed triangulation, and selection of its period by the quantum source, remain distinct questions. For fixed critical shapes, the positive multiplier solutions form a concrete torsor: one independent positive horosphere scale per cusp acts freely and transitively. This accounts for the decoration freedom in the algebraic certificate. It does not yet determine the quantum period, and extending the action to complex scalars requires retaining its sign kernels. For augmented plats, the [actual matching-graph construction](../../notes/general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md) is one way to supply this certificate: a positive labeled right-angled polyhedron gives the marked complete exterior and an explicit positive ideal triangulation. The general gluing criterion does not require that particular polyhedral decomposition or a bound on bridge width. ## The general endpoint action has the actual volume normalization The original augmented-plat coupon now has an [exact local critical-character map](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). It preserves the whole ordered meridian product, recovers the actual crossing-circle transport and retains both physical degree charts and signed half twists. On a correctly marked stationary branch, the original Fourier coupling gives $d(2\pi i\phi)=\tfrac12\sum_i V_i\,dU_i$ in its specified peripheral convention. A [generic-framing theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md) places the complete geometric representation in regular charts for every coupon simultaneously. It also solves the unrestricted integral degree-lifting problem. It does not put that candidate into a contributing physical support chamber or choose a contributing Poisson sector. The [endpoint regulator theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) fixes the absolute constant. The fully normalized q-Hahn action and the original crossing-circle diagram have the same rational wedge. Their Bloch–Wigner regulators agree at a real point and hence throughout the connected regular chart. The original diagram cycle has degree one on each cusp, so its regulator is the actual augmented-link volume. Writing $Y_D$ for the actual augmented-link exterior of the fixed diagram $D$, the full stationary-action identity gives $$2\pi\operatorname{Re}\phi(0)=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D).$$ This holds at a regular, correctly marked full geometric critical point; the fixed endpoint channel has purely imaginary logarithm and introduces no residual real contribution. The theorem fixes the geometric candidate's value. A quantum cycle coefficient, a nonzero amplitude and bounds for other contributions remain separate parts of the general conjecture. The same marked matrices now determine the [channel Hessian](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), without assuming a deformation theorem. If the endpoint transport is $I+b_iH_i$ with $H_i^2=0$, the actual primitive cusp shape is $\tau_i=(b_i-\epsilon_i/2)^{-1}$. Let $\xi_i$ be the scaled channel variables, $y$ the remaining magnetic variables, and $F$ the full local phase. After the two internal q-Hahn variables are eliminated on their marked critical sheets, $$\frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial\xi_i\partial\xi_j}=-\delta_{ij}\frac{4\pi i}{\tau_i},\qquad \frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial\xi_i\partial y}=0.$$ Since $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i>0$, this channel block has negative real part. Eliminating those channels gives the color Hessian $\pi i\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)$, with the factor of two in the transfer convention retained. The [marked multi-cusp rigidity theorem](../../notes/general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md) supplies a direct deformation proof from an actual positive ideal gluing certificate. Positive polarization makes the marked gluing Jacobian invertible; the developing-map inverse retains exact peripheral eigenflags, including infinitesimal data. The [actual critical-scheme theorem](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) then reconstructs the whole ordered representation from the stationary magnetic variables and conversely. The magnetic Hessian has exactly two null directions, both from framing. After taking a transverse slice, there is a nearby holomorphic geometric stationary branch, with the displayed peripheral differential and absolute volume anchor. This classical existence statement is general in plat width under the certificate. Selecting it from the original quantum sum is a separate analytic requirement, now met for the specifically proved families but not asserted for every plat. There is now an explicit [physical framing test](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md) for the domain of the joint kernel theorem. One rank-one projector records the common frame; traces of the original prefix words give finite strict inequalities for every input and output. The theorem distinguishes these inequalities from mere avoidance of algebraic chart poles. The [local sheet test](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) then checks which characteristic root the finite source selects. Neither test asserts that a common solution or a contributing global cycle always exists. The [right-angled framing obstruction](../../notes/actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) now rules out an all-central selected common frame for the certified right-angled plats. In the Lorentz model, the white face normals form a convex polyhedron whose facets correspond to the original shaded triangles. Under the oriented geometric strip conditions, the two flags determine a line through its interior. At each facet crossed by that line, a nonnegative relation among the three actual prefix diagonals violates strict physical support. Generic flags cross exactly two facets, so the obstruction involves exactly two local factors at every bridge width. Any two distinct facets can be prescribed, including the pair incident to the original marked physical edge. The [selected-factor corollary](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md), using the [full physical packet](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md), now proves that every other ordinary factor is physical and source-selected. The selected square root is continued from the original source; the old pointwise principal-root test is not assumed outside the central domain. The completed contraction and global quantum cycle remain unresolved. ![A schematic section of the white-normal convex polyhedron: the polarization line crosses two facets, locating the two strict physical-support failures.](../figures/two-exceptional-factors.png) For the complete-circle source, the pair at a crossing-circle matching edge now has an [exact rewrite with four external representation factors](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md). Its four outside objects are all physical, so the [positive scalar estimate](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.md) applies to every target channel, independently of bridge width. The original row measure cancels its exponential factorial gauge. In this unrestricted-plat method, the target tensor, the remaining network and the original integration contour still require control; geometric localization alone does not estimate them.
