The [finite selected-critical certificate](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) combines the positive gluing, common-frame and local-sheet tests, retaining the original logarithmic characters. When supplied, it identifies the geometric stationary germ with the source-selected local principal phase. At completeness the sheet tests also have an exact interpretation as oriented regions between the two actual disk circles. For other geometric realizations, existence of that simultaneous certificate remains open. For an unrestricted plat, this test alone does not show that the geometric point contributes to the original integration contour. The same deformation coordinates give a [geometric long-filling corollary](../../notes/general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) without a quantum input. Write $V_i(U)=U_i t_i(U)$ and set $e_i=1/p_i$ at filled cusps, $e_i=0$ at unfilled ones. The equations $V_i(U)+e_iU_i=-2\pi i e_i$ have an invertible Jacobian at completeness and a solution in one fixed polydisk. Their exact factorization bounds each $|U_i|$ by a constant times $|e_i|$. The existing geometric completion argument therefore applies to all independently long signed slopes. This proves the geometric threshold, while the volume-limit threshold still requires the quantum estimates. ## The local maximum can be the wrong global maximum The four face-support inequalities alone are insufficient. In the local hyperideal theorem, differentiating the normalized action with respect to a color gives the corresponding edge length. Increasing every color preserves those support inequalities and pushes the maximum to an octahedral boundary configuration. A manifold saddle therefore requires the actual global edge constraints or additional boundary contributions. This is a concrete obstruction to deriving the complement volume by multiplying separately maximized local estimates. There is now an exact [geometric interpretation of a native magnetic energy](../../notes/actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.md). At the folded color, the highest-weight degree block gives four positive ideal tetrahedra forming a convex ideal octahedron, whose maximum is $v_8$. The full boundary operator has the larger rate computed in the [Plancherel theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md). Away from the fold the normalized summands require a signed face term. These are local comparison geometries; placing their cells in the actual complement and matching the remaining phase equations still requires proof. The [positive radial Fourier obstruction](../../notes/actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) makes the phase issue concrete for the general certified right-angled source. Its retained cycle congruences close particular local momentum characters, including the cup signs and marked charge. They do not supply the real magnetic-coordinate matching equations carried by the discarded coefficient phases. An all-ordinary strict radial reconstruction would contradict the common-frame theorem above. This excludes that proposed geometric assembly, without asserting a strict gap between positive and coherent exponential rates. ## Shared cores explain the cube test For the certified augmented graph geometry, the actual volume has the form $$4b\,v_8+2\operatorname{Vol}(Q),$$ where \(Q\) is the supplied positive ideal right-angled central polyhedron and \(b\) counts the prescribed octahedral pieces in that construction. The exact cut, face, and cusp identifications are checked in its theorem. The core is shared by the graph; it is not a sum of independent vertex constants. The cube is a useful nontrivial example of this phenomenon. Its projected quantum calculations recover the shared core contribution. Extending those estimates to the full source is still a quantum problem, even after the geometric complement has been constructed.

title: What remains to be proved
text: # What remains to be proved ## The planar decoration result and the remaining general problem The [balanced decoration theorem](../../notes/actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) now gives a full invariant equality for a class without a tangle-tree hypothesis. Start with any simple triangulated sphere and a chosen perfect matching of its dual. The proof constructs its actual augmented link, circle packing, and a finite two-sided terminal decoration. Every original and added region can then receive independently sufficiently long signed twists. With the chosen knot parity, the resulting knot has the hyperbolic volume limit through all integer levels. This settles the full complementary-source estimate for those decorated diagrams: one shared complete packing satisfies the strict local inequalities, which give an exponential bound for the entire remainder. The geometric leading term is nonzero, and primitive completion identifies its action with the actual knot-complement volume. The proof includes general Morse diagrams, where cups and caps may occur between boxes. For the unchanged simple matched sphere, the [geometric contribution](../../notes/actual_morse_geometric_contribution.md) is now established directly from the original Morse source. Its [entire Fourier period](../../notes/actual_morse_cross_filling_period.md) is nonzero at sufficiently large levels of both parities, and its exponential rate is the volume of the original complement after independently sufficiently long fixed signed fillings. This statement concerns the central recurrence-path contribution, called CROSS in the finite formula; it is not a new invariant or a full-invariant volume theorem. The undecorated problem is the strict bound for the full source minus that geometric contribution. A simple white sphere alone does not yet supply this bound, and adding tangles generally changes the knot. Arbitrary short fillings, cores with loops or repeated white edges, and the general volume conjecture remain outside the planar result. This result is at the complete main meridian; extending its full meridian family and operator consequences is also separate work. ### What remains after the finite filling estimate The [uniform filling estimate](../../notes/actual_uniform_filling_supremum_bound.md) separates two parts of the calculation. After taking the common face coefficient, let \(S_N(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\) be the resulting spectral polynomial. Applying the original twist functionals gives \[ |Z_N(\boldsymbol n)| \le \prod_{e=1}^r(1+|n_e|/2)\, \|S_N\|_{[-2,2]^r}. \] The diagram and twist powers are fixed, so this factor adds no exponential growth as \(N\) increases. The proof retains derivatives at double spectral roots and the simple endpoint at odd levels. For a term containing a one-sided local factor, that coordinate costs at most \((N-1)/N\), independently of its twist power. The full complementary polynomial vanishes on the product of the spectral node sets. This yields a bound without first taking the absolute value of each local path. The missing estimate concerns the supremum of that shared complementary polynomial: it must lie strictly below the augmented geometric rate. Such a gap would make it negligible beside a separately established nonzero geometric term for sufficiently long fixed fillings. The full spectral polynomial is independent of the twists; bounding it at the augmented volume alone cannot prove the smaller filled volume. Thus the finite norm result simplifies the remaining estimate without adding a new knot family to the volume theorems. The volume limit is proved for fixed ordered cylindrical tangle compositions whose reduced net twists are sufficiently long and whose closed diagram is a knot, with elementary two-strand braid closures excluded. The [results chapter](results.md#arbitrarily-many-tangles-with-sufficiently-long-net-twists) defines the reduction and its size condition. For this class, the theorem concerns the full invariant and the volume of the actual knot complement. The remaining questions include short net twists outside the explicit criteria below, knot families outside these constructions, and identification of the full recurrence ideal beyond the selected geometric factor. The alternative plat methods below have their own open hypotheses. Those hypotheses are not missing steps in the proved Conway theorem. ## The boundary of the current Conway theorem The [net-twist theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) removes the requirement that the original written expression pass the strict type test. Its explicit isotopies bring integral twist boxes together, retaining the half-turns of intervening tangles. The resulting groups of twist numbers are fixed by the original expression. The output is either a strict template or an elementary braid closure. The large-twist hypothesis applies to the sums in those groups. The analytic inputs now include both the [complete-value strict-tree theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and the [moving-meridian theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) for every fixed strict tree. The topological reduction transfers the whole zero-framed meridian family to the same filled knot in its original presentation. It carries the meridian and preferred longitude as well, so the intrinsic volume and cusp expansion transfer with the invariant. The lower bounds on twist length still apply to the surviving sums. A small nonzero surviving twist remains outside this long-net-twist theorem; the quantitative circle-tree theorem below covers some such cases. Making the original written exponents large by inserting opposite twist pairs cannot remove it. Exact zero sums can be treated by a further topological reduction: the [closure extension](../../notes/actual_conway_arbitrary_closure_volume.md) permits cap closures and the resulting connected-sum factors. When the input is hyperbolic and every surviving strict weight is long, the input is isotopic to one covered strict knot. This strengthens the criterion for presentations; it adds no short-twist estimate. For this reduction theorem the threshold depends on the fixed construction. The separate circle-tree criterion below has a twist threshold independent of the tree, but still requires each diagram to be fixed before the quantum limit. Nor does the reduction classify all presentations of a given knot. There is also a precise operator question. A genuine all-level recurrence for the ADO invariant and finite initial data selecting its solution are already available. The [pointed quantum A-period theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) reconstructs the Kashaev invariant from that data, including the derivatives required at singular steps, and gives its volume limit for the covered knots. The [selected classical geometric factor](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) is now identified for every covered strict long-filling presentation, including its bare junctions, and for the circle-tree sources under the summed condition, the local bound \(2^{-120}\), or any [directed certificate](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_all_orders.md). Identifying the full quantum module carrying the marked logarithmic regulator remains a further problem. A scalar limit at the complete meridian does not by itself control the invariant as that meridian varies. ## What the actual meridian state requires The [nearby-zero theorem](../../notes/actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) makes the obstruction more precise. For the reduced ADO state in the marked meridian coordinate, the exact values are $$ F_N(1)=K_N(K),\qquad F_N(q_N)=1,\qquad q_N=e^{\pi i/N}. $$ The first value has positive exponential growth for the knots covered above. The second point is only order $1/N$ from the first. The crossing formulas give a Laurent degree bound of order $N$; factoring that polynomial then proves that actual zeros approach $M=1$ within distance $O(1/N)$. Consequently the unchanged state cannot have a holomorphic, nonvanishing branch asymptotic on a fixed neighborhood of completeness. The same ordinary-color values force a boundary factor in every polynomial annihilator. In the squared coordinate $Y=M^2$, write the shift as $\mathsf S Y=q^2Y\mathsf S$. The [peripheral normal-period theorem](../../notes/peripheral_normal_period.md) gives $$ P=B(Y-1). $$ Its formerly conditional positive-growth hypothesis is now satisfied for the covered knots. Removing the factor changes the state: $B$ annihilates $(Y-1)F_N$, which vanishes at completeness, and the original invariant is recovered from its normal derivative. Localizing the meridian to rational functions discards the corresponding boundary quotient. That quotient and the derivative data must be retained when interpreting the operator geometrically. An exact regularization is already available. Interpolate the ordinary colors by a polynomial $P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(Y)$ of degree at most $N-2$, and subtract it before dividing by $S_N(Y)=1+Y+\cdots+Y^{N-1}$. The resulting Laurent polynomial has the same complete exponential rate and satisfies an affine recurrence with a polynomially bounded source. Its shifted values involve derivatives of the original state, so the obstruction above does not apply to it automatically. For the figure-eight knot, the [meridian profile theorem](../../notes/actual_paired_factor_meridian_profile.md) now controls this regular remainder on the scale $Y=e^{z/N}$ for every fixed compact set of complex $z$. Its centered profile satisfies $\rho_N\to1$, including the ordinary-color resonances and every fixed derivative. The first correction is $$ N(\rho_N(z)-1)\longrightarrow\frac{\tau}{8\pi i}z^2, \qquad \tau=2\sqrt3\,i. $$ Here $\tau$ is the cusp shape computed from the preferred meridian and longitude. The proof obtains the coefficient directly from the finite sum; a separate matrix calculation fixes its geometric interpretation and sign. The figure-eight result includes all fixed complex \(z\)-disks, including the ordinary-color resonances, and identifies its correction with the preferred cusp shape. For every fixed strict Conway presentation with sufficiently long signed twists, a separate argument proves the actual reduced ADO profile on \(|s|\le R<1\), where \(M=q_N^s\). This disk stops before the first ordinary-color resonances. ## The filled moving-meridian theorem and its remaining limits The [filled-meridian theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) proves \[ \sup_{|s|\le R} \left|\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|F_N(q_N^s)| -\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)\right|\longrightarrow0, \qquad R<1, \] for every fixed strict Conway tree with independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists and the original knot and framing conditions. A bare junction is a product junction containing no crossing-circle operator. Its valence, adjacency to other bare junctions, and the size of its component impose no additional restriction. The [general component proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) controls the whole signed calculation. The earlier separated-junction, path and trivalent proofs remain valid special cases. The invariant is nonzero throughout the stated disk for sufficiently large $N$. If $A_N(s)$ is the exact crossing-and-framing scalar specified by the finite source, its normalized profile is \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)} =H_N(s)\bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr),\qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}. \] The lower bound comes from a nonzero term in the joint Fourier calculation. All Fourier indices are compared with the same filled critical action, so the fixed twist magnitudes need not be comparable. One presentation-dependent threshold works before choosing $R<1$; the starting quantum level may depend on the chosen twists and radius. The [longitude calculation](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) identifies the first correction with the preferred cusp shape $\tau_K$: \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =1+\frac{\pi i s^2\tau_K}{2N}+O(N^{-2}). \] The [exact scalar calculation](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) retains the integer framing term, and the geometric proof determines the preferred longitude after the auxiliary surgeries. Both the geometric identity and this asymptotic now cover the same strict-tree class. The [net-twist and closure corollary](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md#net-twists-and-other-conway-closures) transfers the intrinsic formulas to their reduced-knot presentations under the stated hypotheses on twist length and topology. It uses ambient isotopy of the zero-framed knot and its preferred peripheral curves; it does not identify different augmented links. The remaining limits are substantial. The disk shrinks like $1/N$ in the meridian coordinate and stops before $s=\pm1$, the first ordinary-color resonances. The general ordinary-color-subtracted state has not been continued through those resonances with the asserted profile. A bound for the whole complementary source is needed beyond the diagrams satisfying balance.](../figures/shared-entropy-frontier.png) ## The classified global upper problem The [global sharp majorant](../../notes/research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) controls every closed degree and real spectral parameter. Let $q$ record the normalized shared loads, let $H_\delta(q)$ be its local upper rate, and let $\mathcal P_D$ impose the original face demands. Then $$ \sup_{\boldsymbol\delta}|S_N(\boldsymbol\delta)|\le e^{N(M_D+o(1))},\qquad M_D=\max_{q\in\mathcal P_D,\;\boldsymbol\delta\in[0,1/2]^R} \sum_eH_{\delta_e}(q_e). $$ The source path decomposition names the central part the cross sector and the two one-sided parts the left and right sectors. In normalized degrees, cross means that both middle loads are at most $1/2$. A seam is their boundary; a non-cross load overloads one middle face. Exceptional cap corners meet both protected faces. [Boundary activation](../../notes/research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md) and [stationary classification](../../notes/research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) leave only complete cross factors, strict straddling one-sided factors and at most two marked caps at a maximizing configuration. The [seam theorem](../../notes/research_sharp_cross_degree_domination_and_seam_gap.md) proves $H_\delta\le h$ on all cross degrees. If $a_D$ is the smallest geometric middle deficit, its seam gap is $\pi a_D^2/2$. The entire seam-neighborhood filling period is exponentially negligible relative to the nonzero cross period for fixed sufficiently long fillings. Consequently, a competing non-cross maximum at or above the geometric rate $\Phi_D$ must be macroscopically overloaded. The [odd-cycle obstruction](../../notes/research_stationary_noncross_main_cycle_obstruction.md) prevents a common phase assignment there. It does not give a sufficient numerical loss by itself. The [flat-cap example](../../notes/research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) proves that a uniform local exponential angular gap is false. The unresolved question is an absolute bound at $\Phi_D$, not merely a positive relative loss from a larger envelope. See the [results discussion](results.md#a-global-source-upper-bound-and-the-classification-of-its-maxima) for the complete qualifications. ## Phase estimates, energy bounds and finite covers A regular source window restricts local starting and stopping rows away from singular endpoints. The [four-state transfer identity](../../notes/research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) keeps a before state, an active two-state block and an after state, including the direct diagonal path. The [positive active transfer](../../notes/research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) controls an outer phase mismatch. The [analytic switching theorem](../../notes/research_analytic_switching_suppression.md) controls a middle mismatch while retaining both boundary terms. The [regular-window theorem](../../notes/research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.md) supplies the strict endpoint losses needed to use that identity. ![The exact transfer, its boundary terms and the regular-window phase loss.](../figures/analytic-source-switching.png) The [mixed cycle criterion](../../notes/research_mixed_cross_window_cycle_packing.md) permits supported single-protected-face windows and entire cross coupons. Only nonzero incidences have phases. Fractionally packing incompatible cycles yields a shared loss $e^{-\kappa N}$. Its scope is summarized with the local extensions in [the results chapter](results.md#phase-cancellation-on-regular-source-windows). To prove a general invariant bound, the positive majorant rate minus $\kappa$ must still be below $\Phi_D$, and the decomposition must cover the whole source. A different route uses [one-sided relative energy](../../notes/actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.md). For a coefficient $a_N(q;\sigma)$ and its positive endpoint reference $p_N(q)$, weighted Cauchy bounds the exponential rate of $|a_N|^2/p_N$ by a triangle entropy. The folded-angle rearrangement is uniform through both parities and degree boundaries. The [protected-outer theorem](../../notes/actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md) identifies its sharp local value. The [shared-flow criterion](../../notes/general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md) combines this energy $g$ with endpoint entropy $h$ and another envelope $h_{\mathrm{env}}$, using $\min\{h_{\mathrm{env}},(h+g)/2\}$ on the same feasible flow. A strict maximum below $\Phi_D$ on the non-cross set implies the full filling theorem. The missing statement is the universal shared inequality; no new local asymptotic conjecture is needed for this criterion. ![A local energy estimate must still be combined with the shared face demands.](../figures/spectral-energy-rearrangement.png) The [finite-sector cover theorem](../../notes/general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md) is another sufficient condition. It allows finitely many genuine cross/left/right branches, each with one common weight per face and a strict bound below the geometric rate. It extends the [anchored criterion](../../notes/general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md). On a fixed seventeen-region marked source, the [separation theorem](../../notes/actual_shared_radius_certificate_separation.md) proves that every anchored choice fails by more than $0.025$, while forty refined branches pass with gap greater than $0.04$. This establishes a strict extension of certificate classes, not a classification of unmarked knots under all possible presentations. The [undivided-capacity result](../../notes/actual_complete_source_cauchy_capacity_gap.md) explains why a single optimized positive torus can lose exponential accuracy. The [fixed-triangle boundary gap](../../notes/actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md) settles certain endpoints, not all fractional mixtures. Universal existence of the finite-sector bounds remains open for the general plat route. ![A refined finite cover succeeds where a coarser certificate fails on the same source.](../figures/sector-certificate-separation.png) ## The external-color route and its exact cancellations The external-color method changes the colors of the crossing circles before filling. It must distinguish internal folded-label deficits from external color deficits. The [complete complex-core theorem](../../notes/actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md) gives a nonzero relative asymptotic on a fixed complex color neighborhood. Its finite action $S_N$ and Hessian remain in the formula. The [geometric deformation theorem](../../notes/actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) identifies the limiting action by $$ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S(\boldsymbol\chi) =\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_{\boldsymbol\chi}) +\frac12\sum_i\operatorname{Re}U_i\operatorname{Im}V_i, \qquad U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i. $$ For real small color parameters $\chi_i$, the boundary correction vanishes and the rate is the representation volume. Complex parameters require the correction. The [varying-action transfer](../../notes/general_long_filling_varying_action_transfer.md) permits the filling calculation to keep $S_N$ until its limit is taken. The [external reflection identity](../../notes/actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md) writes a color $N-h$ circle as a cosine-weighted complete term plus the literal color $h$ circle. In the window $h=z\sqrt N$, the complete term has a Gaussian limit fixed by the primitive cusp shape. At the opposite endpoint it has a full-size alias, canceled exactly by the small-color term. A bound for only the complete term would miss this cancellation. ![The cusp rectangles fix the peripheral normalization in the external-color Gaussian.](../figures/cusp-gaussian.png) The [source-divisor theorem](../../notes/general_long_filling_source_divisor.md) explains why nonzero leading amplitude at one point is not enough for every long slope tuple. A nonzero analytic germ allows an exceptional divisor; an amplitude that is a unit, or a specified coordinate monomial, gives the stronger uniform conclusion. The established complete core has a unit amplitude. The remaining source terms still need their own gap before that conclusion transfers to the invariant. The finite local equation is also known. The [fixed-fold Fourier period](../../notes/actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md) gives a four-component difference equation of bounded shift range with its actual finite polynomial solution and characteristic factors. [Exponential fold interpolation](../../notes/actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) controls the complex extension on the original grid. After face extraction, the equation couples neighboring coefficients; this particular local equation has not been reduced to a scalar knot equation by that elimination alone. The [coupled face system](../../notes/actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.md) preserves the shared coefficients and selected fold relation. At a marked double root, the [deformed circle-pattern theorem](../../notes/actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) recovers the geometric radii and eigenline germs from a nonsingular finite system. The [primitive collar calculation](../../notes/actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) then fixes the actual disk word and half-twist shear. Its one-side multiplier and the square from a double reflection must not be interchanged. ## Small-circle insertions and smoothing The [small-circle operator](../../notes/actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md) preserves the polynomial ring after all original paths are summed. Apparent negative powers cancel at the physical endpoints, and total degree excludes extra whole-level aliases. A color $h$ insertion costs at most $C^{h-1}$ in the stated weighted norm. The [simultaneous insertion theorem](../../notes/actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md) treats every untwisted subset with connected identity smoothing, even with cyclic dependencies or protected outgoing faces. It does not require a global elimination order; the [ordered construction](../../notes/actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions.md) is a special case. For disconnected smoothings, the subset contribution is exactly zero when $2\sum_{i\in J}(h_i-1)<N-1$. The demanded face degree exceeds the available degree. Deleted crossing circles carrying a half-twist are outside that untwisted statement. A geometric gap can be supplied by the [smoothing-capacity condition](../../notes/actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md) or the [fixed-radius criterion](../../notes/actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.md). A capacity is the optimized exponential bound from the positive angle/weight problem. The latter note includes a matched-graph example where its restricted test fails, but there is no proved adapter making it a counterexample for an original flat plat. The [capacity decomposition](../../notes/actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) handles unattained positive-radius infima. Loops are infeasible, separating two-edge cycles split the capacity additively, and nontrivial simple blocks carry actual right-angled polyhedra. Double-triangle blocks have zero contribution. This decomposition does not move the quantum mark or assert a finite quantum factorization. The [representation-volume strictness theorem](../../notes/general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) proves a strict gap when the reconstructed representation kills an essential meridian. The [block representation construction](../../notes/actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) extends the argument to degenerate blocks, keeping the original cuts and shaded pairings. It identifies the regulator with the sum of block volumes without claiming that the whole exterior splits geometrically into those blocks. These ingredients give the [untwisted color corridor](../../notes/general_untwisted_mixed_source_volume_corridor.md): for all sufficiently small normalized deficits on any fixed untwisted subset, the whole mixed source differs from its geometric core by an exponentially small relative error. Both parities are included. Its limit is the volume of the selected marked representation. A complete filled knot metric and a bound on the full complementary color region are further requirements. For signed replacements, the homogeneous source theorem gives a finite shared-radius certificate. Each unchanged circle contributes its two-triangle potential; each replaced signed circle contributes its four-angle potential, while an unsigned replacement has the sharper $\log\max(b,c)$ bound. Every nonempty reflected subset must have a common face-weight choice whose total rate, after subtracting the demanded face powers, is below the complete rate. These finitely many strict margins absorb the insertion costs on one color cube. Existence of the certificates is not automatic. The [single-circle signed theorem](../../notes/actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md) gives useful special cases and explicit curvature tests. ![The proved small-color corridors and the complementary color region still to be controlled in the general plat route.](../figures/external-color-corridor.png) The [positive Newton obstruction](../../notes/actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction.md) shows that a positive local kernel can have shared capacity above the complete geometric value. Its graph example is not asserted to come from the original flat-plat compiler. The [resummed small-circle kernel](../../notes/actual_resummed_small_circle_face_kernel.md) also has a unique-path coefficient exponentially larger than its crossing reference, even after Newton cancellations. These are obstructions to local norm shortcuts, not counterexamples to a bound after the full signed extraction. The [peripheral volume-gap theorem](../../notes/general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md) gives another geometric tool: keeping a fixed peripheral trace square away from the parabolic value forces a uniform volume loss. Applying it to the quantum source still requires a bound for the whole period, including its finite endpoints and signs. ## Direct twist transport and the classical operator question The [direct-power identity](../../notes/actual_direct_long_power_source.md) keeps a signed twist power inside its original box. Two kernels on the same pair compose by one coefficient extraction. This retains repeated-node derivative data and avoids introducing an external-color expansion. The [Casimir conic theorem](../../notes/actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md) describes the resulting local characteristic. With outer weights fixed, $A=x+y$ and $P=xy$, it reads $$ \sigma=2+\frac{(b+z+A)^2}{P-bz},\qquad b_{j+1}+\sigma b_j+b_{j-1}+2A=0. $$ On a regular generic fiber, the cover $\lambda^2+\sigma\lambda+1=0$ turns the transport into multiplication by $\lambda^n$ in a norm-one coordinate. At $\sigma=-2$ the transport is additive; at $\sigma=2$ the fiber is a nonreduced double line. The excluded divisors and choice of reference point matter. The word *torsor* in this route records that the multiplicative coordinate has no preferred origin until a reference is chosen. ![Generic multiplicative transport and its degenerate endpoint fibers, with the quantum Gaussian retained.](../figures/casimir-twist-transport.png) The [physical meridian theorem](../../notes/actual_crossing_torus_meridian_transport.md) identifies the local map with the actual crossing move $(A,B)\mapsto(A^{-1}BA,A)$, preserving $BA$, and gives the inverse for a negative crossing. With the cup, cap and mark phases included, every regular layered critical point produces a representation of the filled knot group. This forward construction does not prove that every root of a cleared equation lifts to the regular chart, classify escaping or singular points, or give a nonzero finite-sum coefficient for the geometric branch. Taking absolute values of all Hermite spectral terms gives an envelope at least as large as the drilled volume. It cannot prove the smaller filled-volume rate. The [spectral total-derivative identity](../../notes/actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md) therefore keeps the full polynomial numerator, both the ordinary and nilpotent terms at repeated nodes, all nonzero Fourier charges and endpoint currents. Its zero charge vanishes identically. The [Gaussian numerator formula](../../notes/actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md) is $$ (-1)^{N-1}V_N(-2\cosh w) =L_N+2\sum_{h=1}^{N-1}\cosh((N-h)w)L_h. $$ The $L_h$ are the physical-color coupons. This is a polynomial identity, not just an equality of sampled values. It gives a positive majorant near the negative endpoint, and a subexponential closing-cap cost near the other endpoint on a shrinking cap for fixed twists. The [even cross/one-sided reduction](../../notes/actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md) partitions the positive numerator into paths crossing the middle rows and paths staying on one side. The crossing part lies between $N H_M/2$ and $3N H_M/2$, coefficientwise, for the maximal complete-channel polynomial $H_M$. The remaining one-sided factors form a rooted forest under the stated diagram hypothesis. They need not vanish, and their half-sized blocks still have level $N$. The [global cross gap](../../notes/actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) and whole-period theorem control the cross contribution; a general bound for the macroscopic one-sided complement remains the issue beyond the sufficient criteria above. The earlier [matching-edge character relation](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md) and [continuant operator period](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md) remain exact inputs. The [retained alternating Newton equations](../../notes/actual_alternating_newton_peripheral_branch.md) match the primitive-collar trace relation after the specified elimination and rational change of variables. The [local action comparison](../../notes/actual_newton_complete_local_action.md) identifies the selected reciprocal logarithmic action with the complete-core action up to $\pi i$. Its continued critical point lies outside the terminating low-color range, so this germ identity does not select a contributing finite-sum cycle. These local comparisons do not themselves identify the classical geometric factor of the knot's quantum A-operator. That limitation coexists with the separately proved all-level operator and pointed-period theorem described at the start of this chapter. The [source and torsor library](../library.html) retains the different operator, regulator and relative-cycle approaches, including their counterexamples and corrections. ## How the alternatives fit together For strict Conway trees, the full source estimate and marked filling argument already prove the knot-volume limit. For general certified plats, the complete augmented source, positive endpoint, complex geometric packet and entire cross period are established. Balance, finite sector covers and shared-flow energy inequalities give sufficient conditions for the remaining source. Universal validity of those conditions is the outstanding issue in those routes. The pretzel, belt, signed Conway, Fourier, weighted-Cauchy, cube and other constructions remain in the [results chapter](results.md) and [research library](../library.html). Their narrower hypotheses should be kept when using them. In particular, a local norm obstruction, a projected cube calculation or an equality of classical actions is not a counterexample to the volume conjecture, and it is not by itself a proof of the full invariant limit.

title: Notation and conventions
text: # Notation and conventions The calculations in this guide pass through three kinds of object: a finite quantum expression, a function describing its large-level growth, and a geometric structure on a specified link complement. A symbol does not acquire a geometric meaning merely because it occurs in a critical-point equation. The proof must identify the relevant matrix, path, or gluing map. This chapter gives the conventions needed to read those identifications and to compare the different approaches in the [mechanism](mechanism.md) and [geometry](geometry.md) chapters. Letters are reused in the technical archive. In particular, a tangle turn, a crossing matrix, and a shift of a meridian variable are different operations. Local definitions take precedence when a note uses another convention. ## The invariant and the order of limits Fix the diagram, its ordered tangle construction, its integer twist powers, and any finite certificate used by a theorem. Then let the integer quantum level \(N\) tend to infinity. Statements for arbitrary finite trees or spheres allow arbitrarily large fixed diagrams; they do not allow the diagram to grow with \(N\). A universal sufficient twist bound and a uniform error estimate over all diagrams are different assertions. | Symbol | Meaning | | --- | --- | | \(N\ge2\) | Quantum level. Unless a theorem states otherwise, the limit includes both parities and composite levels. | | \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q_N=q_N^2\) | The chosen root and its square. In a fixed-level calculation, the subscripts are often omitted. | | \(d=N-1\) | Top index in the \(N\)-dimensional physical module. | | \(\zeta\) | A generic quantum parameter when a derivative is taken before root specialization. | | \([j]_\zeta=(\zeta^j-\zeta^{-j})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\) | Symmetric quantum integer. | | \(s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N)\), \(S_j=\prod_{a=1}^j s_a\), \(S_0=1\) | Root sine factors and their products. A normalizing factor \(S_j\) can have exponential size; it is not automatically absorbed into a polynomial error. | | \(K_N(K)\) | The reduced complete-color Kashaev invariant of the oriented, zero-framed knot \(K\), with unknot value one in the stated convention. | | \(n_i\) | The signed integer exponent of the physical checked crossing \(R\) in a fixed box. It is a twist count, not a level or a scaled color. | | \(\epsilon_i\in\{-1,0,1\}\), \(p_i\in\mathbb Z\) | Retained half twist and integral disk-filling parameter, with \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\). | | \(v_3,v_8\) | Volumes of a regular ideal tetrahedron and a regular ideal octahedron. | The volume statement uses the rate \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| \longrightarrow \operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] The absolute value is taken after the entire complex scalar has been evaluated. A large summand or a large sum of absolute values supplies no lower bound for that scalar. “Independently sufficiently long” means that a fixed presentation has a threshold and each surviving twist exceeds it in absolute value, with either sign and without a bound on ratios between twist lengths. In a net-twist reduction, the condition concerns the surviving signed sums, not each original summand. The [results chapter](results.md) states the separate long-filling, degree-and-twist, and decorated-planar hypotheses. ## Finite sums, colors and derivatives A **color** specifies a representation on a physical strand or auxiliary circle. An internal **channel** is a representation label introduced by a decomposition of tensor products. A **head index** specifies a basis vector inside a representation. These are different finite indices. The ordinary auxiliary color is \(j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and its highest weight is \(j-1\). Complete color means \(j=N\), with highest weight \(d\). Its external deficit is \(h=N-j\), and the corresponding scaled deficit is \(\chi=h/N\). Some older formulas use \(n\) for this color; their \(n\) must not be confused with a crossing power \(n_i\). An internal polynomial or head index \(r\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\) often gives a scaled variable \(x=r/N\). A different formula may use the half-shifted channel variable \[ a_j=\frac{j+1/2}{N},\qquad c_j=2\cos(2\pi a_j). \] For the folded spectral coordinate, set \[ \delta_j=\frac12-a_j,\qquad c_j=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_j). \] On the representative half of the spectrum, the continuous variable \(\delta\) near zero describes the internal endpoint near \(-2\); it is not the external color deficit \(\chi\). At odd levels the endpoint \(\delta=0\) is an actual simple node. At even levels the nearest representative has \(\delta=1/(2N)\). Those finite offsets are retained in the interpolation. The choice \(r/N\), \(r/(N-1)\), or \((r+1/2)/N\) must remain visible. They have the same interior leading limit in suitable regimes, but different exact endpoints and first corrections. For example, \(r_1+r_2\le d\) becomes \(x_1+x_2\le1-1/N\) when \(x_i=r_i/N\). Replacing it by a closed limiting inequality is an estimate, not an exact source identity. A **normal** is a derivative in a specified direction. At a repeated Casimir node \(c\), a polynomial operator can depend on both \(p(c)\) and \(p'(c)\); evaluating only \(p(c)\) loses its nilpotent part. This is the reason for Hermite data. A derivative in the generic parameter \(\zeta=q_Ne^t\), with \(N\) fixed, is another operation. A factor that vanishes at \(t=0\) can have a nonzero derivative there. Neither derivative is the next coefficient of an \(N\to\infty\) expansion. The [physical polynomial compiler](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) records the finite Casimir algebra and its repeated-root data. The [homogeneous face source](../../notes/actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) records how its polynomials become original matrix entries. Root-only identities must not be differentiated in a generic parameter without that additional source calculation. ## Source polynomials, sectors and the invariant The **source** is the full prescribed expression: physical matrices, their index ranges, cups, caps, the marked cut, and every scalar factor. A **coupon** is one specified operator inserted in a tangle box. A source polynomial is a way of storing the matrix entries of such an operator or the coefficients of a whole contraction. In the homogeneous face description, a box has ordered faces \((x,b,c,y)\): \(b,c\) are its middle faces and \(x,y\) its outer faces. Its polynomial \(H_e(x,b,c,y)\) has total degree \(d\). For a diagram with \(R\) boxes, the product has degree \(Rd\). With two protected faces \(u,v\), the original marked contraction is expressed by \[ \left[\prod_{f\ne u,v}L_f^d\right]\! \left.\prod_{e=1}^R H_e(L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e}) \right|_{L_u=L_v=0}. \] The brackets mean coefficient extraction, not substitution of face radii. There are \(R\) ordinary targets, each of degree \(d\), and two protected targets of degree zero. A shared face has one variable wherever it occurs. Giving separate occurrences unrelated values would change the problem. For physical coupons this coefficient formula gives the original scalar with its stated exterior normalization. If \(H_e\) is instead a spectral numerator depending on a variable \(\sigma_e\), the extracted result \(S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)\) is still a polynomial in those spectral variables. The original trace and filling functional remain to be applied. The [general Morse source theorem](../../notes/research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) keeps the turns, mark, primitive face grid, and both level parities in this description. Several decompositions of the source are used: | Term | Exact meaning | | --- | --- | | Complete-color source | The original contraction with every designated auxiliary color equal to \(N\). | | Color core | The term retaining the complete-circle part of each exact external-color identity. It can be an entire function of \(\chi\). | | Color alias | A complementary small-color term in that identity. Its exponential smallness is a theorem to be proved, not part of its definition. | | CROSS sector | The specified central-cut support in a local continuant/cofactor spectral numerator. | | LEFT or RIGHT sector | One of the complementary one-sided supports in that same numerator. | | All-CROSS contraction | The coefficient or period obtained by selecting CROSS at every box, while retaining the shared face targets and original trace. | | Full contraction | The sum over all the prescribed sector choices, with their signs and normal data. | The capitalized sector names are finite-support labels; CROSS does not mean a physical crossing matrix. A color core and an all-CROSS projection arise from different decompositions and must not be identified by their names. A nonzero all-CROSS period with the correct geometric rate does not by itself prove the full invariant's rate: the other sectors might contribute or cancel it. The [cofactor theorem](../../notes/actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) defines that projection, and the [balanced planar theorem](../../notes/actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) explains a sufficient comparison with the remaining sectors. ## Tangles and geometric variables A tangle box has four ordered endpoints. A product stacks compatible boxes in their specified order. A **physical quarter-turn** bends an incoming strand into an outgoing one and changes the input/output presentation. Its evaluation includes the original duality maps. The cylindrical closure joins lower endpoints to upper endpoints outside the box; the cap closure joins the two upper endpoints and the two lower endpoints respectively. These closures can have different topology. The knot test counts both components formed at final closure and any circles already closed inside a tangle. The guide usually writes \(R\) for a checked crossing operator, including the interchange of its two tensor factors, and \(T\) for a tangle turn. Some older notes call a turn \(R\). The shift called \(T\) in a quantum difference equation below is a third operation. A construction tree records products and turns; it is not a knot projection. A **circle-marked junction** contains a crossing-circle operator. A **bare junction** is a maximal consecutive group of products without one. Resolving a high-valence product into binary products introduces internal bookkeeping variables, not new physical quarter-turn edges. For a vertex \(v\), \(d_v\) is its graph degree, including the specified boundary attachments. It has no relation to the quantum top index \(d=N-1\). In strict-tree geometry, a physical turn edge has a normalized polynomial label \(x_e\). When exposed as the ordinary output of a rooted branch, that output angle is \(1-x_e\). The set \(\mathcal E_T\) in the longitude formulas consists of the original physical turn edges; hidden binary-resolution edges are excluded. The [strict-tree geometric theorem](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) explains this convention and the case \(x_e=1/2\). A geometric gluing face may be a quadrilateral with four ordered ideal vertices. “Ideal” means that its vertices lie on the sphere at infinity of hyperbolic space. The vertex order specifies the face identification. Some archive notes call such a boundary face a *port*; elsewhere that word refers to an external representation factor. It is necessary to check which meaning is intended. ## Circle packings, shapes and geometric actions In the face-source geometry, a positive real \(L_f\) is the **curvature**, or inverse radius, of a finite white circle. A protected value \(L_u=0\) denotes a straight line, not a circle of radius zero. Sending the marked tangency to infinity gives two parallel protected lines. The remaining circles lie in their common strip. Shared positive radii used in a Cauchy estimate are choices of weights; only a separately proved stationary identification makes them the geometric packing. A complex number \(z_\Delta\) attached to an ideal tetrahedron is its ordered cross-ratio shape. Its branch and orientation matter; a coordinate with positive imaginary part gives a positively oriented tetrahedron in the usual vertex convention. The same letter \(z\) can instead be a formal polynomial variable, a spectral variable, or the microscopic meridian coordinate below. These uses are unrelated. The real factorial rate uses \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad 0\le x\le1, \] with the integrable endpoint limits. The Lobachevsky function is \[ \Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log|2\sin u|\,du. \] Thus \(J(x)=-\Lambda(\pi x)/\pi\) on that real interval. Complex continuations require a specified logarithm and path; the absolute value in the real definition of \(\Lambda\) is not a holomorphic prescription. For a positive complete source, \(\Phi_D\) or \(F_0\) often denotes its maximal limiting action. Once the original geometry has been proved, its normalization is \[ 2\pi\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D), \] where \(Y_D\) is the complete **augmented** exterior. A filled critical action is generally complex. Its real part is converted to the filled volume only after the original primitive peripheral equations and the regulator boundary correction have been checked. A **boundary profile** maximizes an open tangle's action with one output index fixed. It retains that boundary constraint and its original joining terms. It is not an independent volume budget that can be added arbitrarily to a neighboring profile. ## Packets, gaps and finite actions A **packet** is a local asymptotic formula which includes the critical action, its nonzero amplitude, and a controlled remainder. A typical notation is \[ \mathcal I_N =N^\beta a_N e^{NS_N}(1+O(N^{-1})). \] Here \(\mathcal I_N\) is the specified integral or sum, \(\beta\) is its level exponent, \(a_N\) is the amplitude, and \(S_N\) is the finite-level critical value. A nonzero lower asymptotic needs control of \(a_N\) and all contributions outside the packet. Merely knowing \(S_N\to S\) does not permit replacing \(e^{NS_N}\) by \(e^{NS}\) with relative error tending to zero. A strict **exponential gap** at rate \(\Phi\) means an estimate such as \[ |\mathcal E_N|\le N^C e^{N(\Phi-\gamma)}, \qquad \gamma>0, \] uniformly on the parameter set stated in that theorem. A polynomial factor \(N^C\) does not change the rate. The constants and starting level may depend on the fixed diagram, fixed twists, compact domain, and derivative order. Uniformity through a complex neighborhood is stronger than a bound at physical integer samples. A Hessian records second derivatives of the relevant phase. The face Cauchy integral and the spectral filling integral use different Hessians and different determinant branches. “Primitive lattice” means the retained integer summation coordinates have no hidden finite-index multiplicity. “First charge” refers to the unit Fourier magnitudes in the exact filling transform; other charges and endpoint currents remain part of the original period until estimated. ## Augmented and filled complements; peripheral coordinates An **augmented exterior** \(Y_D\) is the complement of the main strands together with the auxiliary crossing circles. Filling an auxiliary cusp attaches a solid torus along the prescribed primitive slope and restores the twists. The resulting knot exterior is \(S^3\setminus K_{\boldsymbol p}\). Its volume generally differs from \(\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)\). The main knot cusp remains unfilled. On each auxiliary torus, \(\mu_i\) goes once around its crossing circle and \(\lambda_i\) is the recorded disk longitude. They form a primitive integral basis. Choose the specified matrix eigenline. Let \(m_i\) and \(\ell_i\) be the corresponding determinant-one eigenvalues divided by their values \(\pm1\) at completeness, so that both normalized eigenvalues equal \(1\) there. Continue their logarithms from that point and write \[ U_i=2\operatorname{Log}m_i,\qquad V_i=2\operatorname{Log}\ell_i . \] These are logarithms of **similarity multipliers**, equivalently twice the normalized eigenvalue logarithms. For example, if the chosen auxiliary longitude matrix in the Morse collar has eigenvalue \(J_i=-1\) at completeness, then \(\ell_i=-J_i\) and \(V_i=2\operatorname{Log}(-J_i)\). At the smooth unit-charge filling saddle the convention is \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i. \] The equation is an equality of the continued logarithms. Its exponential alone would allow a wrong winding, and at a parabolic longitude could permit a nontrivial filling holonomy. The [primitive collar calculation](../../notes/actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) fixes the paths; the [metric completion theorem](../../notes/general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) checks the actual log-link periods and the smooth solid torus. Two useful descriptions of the auxiliary deformation are \[ U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i \quad\text{in the external-color coordinate},\qquad V_i=-4\pi i\delta_i \quad\text{in the internal spectral coordinate}. \] They belong to the same selected branch only after the stationary equations and the marked geometric adapter identify them. In the angular circle-tree chart one instead writes \(V_i=2i\tau_i\). The angle \(\tau_i\) is therefore not a cusp shape. For the main cusp, normalize a horospherical Euclidean coordinate so that the positive meridian translates by \(1\). The preferred longitude follows the knot once with zero linking number; its translation is the **cusp shape** \(\tau_K\). If \(U_K=2\log M\) and \(V_K=2\log(-L)\) are centered at the complete lift, then \(dV_K/dU_K=\tau_K\) there. The sign \(-L\) centers the negative-unipotent preferred longitude lift \(L=-1\). Under surgery on the auxiliary circles, the image of the augmented main longitude need not remain preferred. If \(k_i=\operatorname{lk}(K,C_i)\) is the integer linking number with the \(i\)th crossing circle, the stated disk convention gives \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{fill}} =\lambda_{\mathrm{aug}}\, \mu_K^{\sum_i p_i k_i^2}. \] This shear changes the marked basis on the filled cusp. The [preferred-longitude proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) tracks it independently of the quantum asymptotic. ## The main-meridian quantum \(A\)-period The raw unrolled highest-weight coordinate is \(x=q_N^\alpha\). The marked meridian coordinate is \[ M=-q_Nx. \] Thus complete weight \(\alpha=d\) gives \(M=1\), and quotient color \(\alpha=j-1\) gives \(M=-q_N^j\). For the reduced, zero-framed ADO family \(F_N(M)\), \[ F_N(1)=K_N(K),\qquad F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N). \] The ordinary reduced \(j\)-color period is \(C_j(q)\). This notation is distinct from a color core also called \(C_N\) in some notes. The [pointing theorem](../../notes/kashaev_ado_pointing.md) fixes these equalities and the component convention. The microscopic variable is \(s\), defined by \[ M=q_N^s=e^{z/(2N)},\qquad z=2\pi i s. \] Bounded \(s\) describes an \(O(1/N)\) neighborhood of \(M=1\); it is not a fixed meridian neighborhood. The proved strict-tree profile uses \(|s|\le R<1\), before the first ordinary-color resonances at \(s=\pm1\). In particular \(F_N(q_N)=1\) even when \(F_N(1)\) has positive volume growth. The exact finite sine factor and scalar in that profile are \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\quad H_N(0)=1, \qquad A_N^{\mathrm{sc}}(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2}, \quad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_i n_i. \] Here \(w(D)\) is the oriented writhe. The superscript “sc” distinguishes this scalar from a finite critical action also often called \(A_N\). Its exponent uses the actual checked-crossing powers and framing convention. It is retained exactly even though it tends to one. The full modified-trace invariant is another normalization: \[ \mathcal N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M),\qquad d_N(M)=i^{N+3}\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}}. \] Evaluating the entire germ gives \(d_N(1)=i^{N+3}/N\) and \(d_N(q_N^s)/d_N(1)=H_N(s)^{-1}\). Thus its normalized profile cancels the reduced sine factor exactly. One must not set the numerator and denominator separately to zero. For the covered moving-meridian knots, the first correction in the zero-framed convention is \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =1+\frac{\pi i s^2\tau_K}{2N}+O(N^{-2}) =1+\frac{\tau_K z^2}{8\pi iN}+O(N^{-2}). \] The exact scalar contributes to this coefficient. The [scalar proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) and [geometric cusp proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) are separate arguments. Their combination is the [filled profile theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md), with its stated domain and fixed-presentation hypotheses. ## Difference operators, classical curves and selected solutions A quantum \(A\)-operator is a specified finite difference operator \[ P(q,M,T)=\sum_{j=0}^{r}a_j(q,M)T^j,\qquad (TF)(M)=F(qM),\qquad TM=qMT. \] Here \(r\) is the operator order, fixed independently of \(N\); it is not the top color index \(d\). The \(a_j\) are rational functions in the formal quantum and meridian variables. A **genuine all-level annihilator** comes from the original finite source before its values are evaluated. Choosing a new ratio of two values at each level is not such a construction. An equation \(PF=0\) does not select its solution by itself. The **pointed period** also retains a fixed vector \(c_0(q)\) of small-color Laurent polynomials and the prescribed companion transport row \(r_N(q)\). At a root pole its value is \[ K_N(K)=\operatorname{CT}_{t=0} \bigl[r_N(q_N(1+t))c_0(q_N(1+t))\bigr]. \] The constant term is taken after multiplying the entire Laurent germs. The parameter \(t\) here is a local evaluation variable, not the geometric deformation \(M=e^{\pi it}\) used in another note. The [pointed operator theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) explains the finite initial data and its volume statement. To form a classical symbol, first clear the specified rational denominators and remove the common power of \(q-1\), then take the first nonzero specialization and replace the commuting shift variable by \(L\). The **geometric \(A\)-curve** records the meridian and preferred-longitude eigenvalues of the selected geometric representations of the knot group. An arbitrary eliminated source equation can contain other components or points excluded from its original chart. In the geometric convention, \(M\) is the positive main meridian eigenvalue and \(L\) is the preferred-longitude eigenvalue on the same line. The source cut selects the \(M^{-1}\) line, so \(L\) is the inverse longitude eigenvalue there. At the complete filled knot, \(M=1\) and \(L=-1\). On the covered strict-tree germ, \[ L_{\mathrm{geom}}(M) =-M^{a(D)} \prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)}, \qquad X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}. \] The [full strict-tree longitude theorem](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) identifies these source variables and paths, including bare product junctions. This replaces the earlier circle-tree-only identification. Its operator corollary, and the [directed all-orders theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_all_orders.md), specify when the selected geometric irreducible factor divides the first nonzero classical symbol. Such divisibility does not identify every factor, its multiplicity, or the complete quantum recurrence ideal. ## What a torsor records A **torsor** is a space with a free and transitive action of a group, without a preferred origin. Choosing one point identifies it with that group, but a formula using the chosen coordinate must record the choice. Several different torsors occur in the archive. For auxiliary holonomy, a half-longitude eigenvalue satisfies \(\ell^2=e^V\), and the logarithm of \(\ell\) has integral-period ambiguity. The actual collar and complete anchor select the sheet and logarithm. A retained half twist changes \[ U^\epsilon=U^0-\frac{\epsilon}{2}V^0, \qquad V^\epsilon=V^0. \] On the selected double cover this is an integral monomial change of peripheral coordinates. It does not authorize a half-integer substitution into the pure-link filling formula. For a regular quantum difference module at a root of order \(m\), a chosen scalar frame can satisfy a cyclic norm equation \[ \prod_{j=0}^{m-1}\sigma^j(a)=v, \] where \(\sigma\) is the prescribed cyclic field automorphism and \(v\) a central eigenvalue. Replacing the frame by \(f\) changes \(a\) to \(a\,\sigma(f)/f\). This algebraic norm is not the absolute value of the knot invariant, nor an operator norm. The [intrinsic norm-torsor construction](../../notes/intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) states the additional hypotheses needed to compare its selected period with a regulator. A third local example is the [Casimir transport conic](../../notes/actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md): after choosing a spectral sheet and a reference point, crossing powers act multiplicatively on its regular fibers. The endpoint fibers degenerate, and the original excluded divisors and boundary targets remain part of the problem. An abstract norm torus or a local conic does not by itself identify a knot's geometric longitude or prove a nonzero source asymptotic. These distinctions explain why the guide keeps the operator, regulator, relative-cycle, and full-source methods separate. Each technical route states which object is constructed and which comparison is still required.

title: Checking the formulas and reproducing the calculations
text: # Checking the formulas and reproducing the calculations ## Uniform bounds for inserting twists With SymPy and NumPy installed, run: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py filling-supremum ~~~ The program checks the finite derivative interpolation formula in cyclotomic fields, the repeated and simple Chebyshev residues, and the reconstruction of positive and negative powers of the original crossing matrices. It also checks the lower-block numerator derivatives against the corresponding spectral projectors. The [proof](../../notes/actual_uniform_filling_supremum_bound.md) establishes the norm bounds for every level. The finite checks do not estimate a volume limit. ## The planar terminal decoration Run the finite checks with one command: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py balanced-terminal-fans ~~~ The script uses integer and rational arithmetic. It verifies the closed curvature recurrence and the rational lower bound in the analytic balance proof. It also constructs oriented stellar subdivisions, derives their new ordered quadrilaterals, checks the matching and even-level parity extension, and follows the endpoint pairings of even stacks of odd terminal tangles. These checks do not estimate a quantum limit or certify a numerical packing. The [written theorem](../../notes/actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) proves the packing, the exact full coefficient, the uniform estimates and the smooth primitive metric completion. The script checks the finite identities used by that argument. The repository contains written proofs, exact finite certificates, numerical checks and recorded outputs. They answer different questions. This chapter explains which calculations support which steps, and how to rerun them without treating a successful sample as a theorem. An exact symbolic calculation can establish an identity in formal variables. A rigorously bounded interval calculation can establish an inequality over an entire stated parameter domain. A finite counterexample can disprove a proposed identity. By contrast, checking many quantum levels or plotting a growth rate does not prove a uniform limit as \(N\to\infty\). The scope of each script must be read together with the mathematical argument that uses it. The current [strict Conway tree theorem](../../notes/actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) includes bounds for the full quantum sum, a nonzero selected contribution, the original normalization and the actual marked filling geometry. Its proof is not waiting for a theorem about all knots. The more specialized general-plat calculations catalogued below retain their own hypotheses and limitations. ## The directed degree and twist bound Run the new exact rational comparisons with one command: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py directed-tree-fillings ~~~ This uses only Python's standard library. It checks the inequalities in the [directed criterion](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md), including the uniform twist bound and the star whose center has power two. The comparisons use rational upper and lower bounds rather than decimal estimates. The written proof supplies the uniform kernel estimate, induction, noncancellation and identification with the actual hyperbolic volume. The program does not estimate a quantum limit. ## Inserting a circle at an unmarked junction With SymPy installed, run: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py strict-tree-geometry ~~~ The program checks local rational identities in the [strict-tree longitude proof](../../notes/actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md): the normalization of the white face maps, the primitive disk longitude, the two incident radius formulas, and the response at a possible half-angle fold. The based meridian paths, ordered boundary gluing and stationary elimination are proved in the text. They cannot be verified merely by equality of matrix traces. ## Reproducing the local tree argument This group requires Python and mpmath. Run it using one command: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py local-tree-fillings ~~~ The first two programs check 21 analytic and eight geometric constant comparisons by exact rational arithmetic. The third compares the polynomial subtree recursion with a separate spectral or first-derivative trace calculation in 48 finite cases, using 180 choices of root at 80-digit precision. The examples include both level parities, zero and signed powers, moving parameters, and constant channels with repeated spectral roots. All \(N\) edge indices are retained; removing the high indices changes every tested value. These checks verify the constants and finite identities used by the argument. The written proof supplies the induction for all finite trees, the contour bounds, noncancellation, and the metric completion. The scripts do not test the asymptotic conclusion by extrapolating finite levels. ## Checking the geometric longitude formulas With Python and SymPy installed, run the four exact-algebra programs through one command: ~~~sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py geometric-characteristic ~~~ The programs check the nonparabolic face maps and peripheral words, the four-puncture character matrices, the two eigenline choices in a half twist, and the differential and discriminant identities used by the rigidity argument. They compare rational functions symbolically, rather than sampling hyperbolic knots. The written proof establishes the ordered gluing, boundary pairing, constant field and regularity over every nonzero main meridian value. Those global arguments are not replaced by the script results. ## Checks for the quantitative volume theorem The [quantitative theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) has one reproduction command: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py curvature-fillings ``` Python, SymPy and mpmath are required. The group runs three programs. The first checks four edge-action identities symbolically and 990 complex Gaussian samples at 70-digit precision, at levels 160 through 256. The second verifies 46 rational identities for the actual octahedra, including the odd half-twist face returns, and seven bounds used in the positive angular chart. The third compares the literal tangle strand compiler with an octahedral attachment construction on 128 finite trees. It checks 448 left or right attachments, the resulting colored face cycles and signed disk pairings, and 28 symbolic peripheral and regulator identities. The saved outputs are the [analytic checks](../../experiments/all_circle_curvature_packet_results.json), [local geometric checks](../../experiments/two_octahedron_angular_edge_block_results.json) and [ordered attachment checks](../../experiments/ordered_octahedron_pages_results.json). Each records its finite scope. The arbitrary-tree induction, the metric completion and the uniform asymptotic estimates are written proofs; finite samples do not establish those conclusions. The [geometric chapter](geometry.md#the-geometric-proof-for-the-explicit-degree-and-twist-bound) explains how the proof identifies the original knot complement. ## Arbitrary multiplication regions The [general component theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) permits connected groups of product junctions of any fixed size and valence. Its new finite identities can be checked with one command: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py general-components ``` The program constructs each Newton polynomial over an exact cyclotomic number field. It compares its Laurent coefficients with the formula in the [Fourier reflection proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md), and independently divides products by the deformed polynomial relation. Subtracting the complete trace must cancel the first Fourier term. A further calculation verifies fusion in the full quotient algebra, including inputs whose values at repeated roots vanish but whose derivative contributions remain nonzero. The [recorded results](../../experiments/high_fourier_reflection_results.json) cover levels two through twelve, including both parities: 36 high-index polynomials, 721 trace differences and 33 fusion identities. These are exact finite algebra checks. The uniform Fourier loss, comparison of positive maxima and passage to the filled knot complement are proved in the three companion notes; the finite checks do not establish those analytical or geometric conclusions. ## Trivalent multiplication regions The [component theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_trivalent_component_bound.md) has one reproduction command: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py trivalent-components ``` The script constructs the Newton polynomials and performs division by the deformed polynomial relation in exact cyclotomic fields. It checks every cubic index triple through level ten, using symmetry to avoid repeated calculations. This includes internal indices above one half, zero and half endpoints, both parities, and the actual turn types. It also checks the elementary identities used in the simultaneous boundary comparison. The script uses Python and SymPy and has no numerical approximations. It checks the finite algebra; the proof supplies the concavity argument, the uniform gap, and the complex estimates needed for the [filled-knot theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_trivalent_filled_volume.md). ## The preferred cusp correction The exact crossing and framing calculation and the geometric longitude calculation can be reproduced together: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py meridian-cusp ``` The scalar program composes signed crossing words and compatible typed products from their local formulas, retaining negative powers and both orders of opposite colors. It also checks the shifted-grid phase algebra. The geometric program verifies the rational meridian frames, the product and turn coordinate maps, the two half-twist signs, and the longitude correction under surgery. Python and SymPy are sufficient. The [scalar proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) and [longitude proof](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) explain the global conclusions. The programs check their local identities; the identification of the preferred peripheral curves and the uniform large-level estimate are arguments in those proofs. ## Running a named group The [research-check runner](../../repro/run_research_checks.py) executes a selected group serially. The [group manifest](../../repro/research_check_groups.json) contains every command in its recorded order. Listing and previewing groups do not run a scientific calculation: python3 repro/run_research_checks.py --list python3 repro/run_research_checks.py general-plat --dry-run To run one group, omit the dry-run option. The runner saves a separate combined output log for every command and a JSON summary containing exit codes and durations. It continues after a failed check so the summary records the whole selected group, then returns a nonzero exit code if any command failed. It does not run unselected groups. The individual scientific scripts keep their existing behavior, including any result files they normally write. By default, logs go in a timestamped directory under the system temporary directory. To retain them in a chosen location, use: python3 repro/run_research_checks.py pointed-a --log-dir /path/to/check-logs The runner uses the Python interpreter that launched it. Select another interpreter with the `--python` option if the chosen group needs a different environment. The manifest replaces the former long command block; it preserves those commands rather than silently adding them to every build. ## The moving-meridian filling calculation The [moving-meridian theorem](../../notes/actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) has a focused reproduction group: python3 repro/run_research_checks.py moving-meridian-fillings It compares 380 finite evaluations at 80-digit precision. One calculation raises the full crossing polynomial to its signed integer power in the quotient algebra. The other uses the root-grid trace, including the derivative term at repeated roots. The cases include both level parities, negative crossing powers, and displaced complex meridians. A separate exact rational calculation checks 18 quadratic Fourier comparisons with signed twist numbers of different sizes. The [recorded output](../../experiments/main_meridian_direct_fillings_results.json) gives the precision and errors. These calculations test finite identities and normalization choices. The uniform contour estimates, the nonzero leading term and the identification with knot-complement volume are proved in the linked notes. The optional profile scan in the individual script is a numerical diagnostic, not a proof of the limit. ## Where to start for the current theorem The proof has three kinds of inputs. Exact source identities retain every color, repeated-node derivative and scalar factor. Analytical estimates control the large-\(N\) limit uniformly on the domains used by the proof. Geometric constructions identify the cells, face maps, cusp markings and filling slopes of the actual complement. A finite algebra script can check an identity used in any of these arguments, but it cannot replace the uniform estimate or the topological construction. The [two-leaf block inequality](../../notes/actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) and [single-leaf attachment inequality](../../notes/actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md) have finite rational certificates. They bound the competing alias expressions over their whole slope domains. Their verification uses exact interval arithmetic, explicit remainder bounds and finitely many vertices of fixed polytopes. Candidate points may help find a certificate; the verifier proves the displayed inequalities without trusting an optimizer. From the repository root, their principal verifiers are: python3 repro/run_research_checks.py conway-certificates The [unflagged-region probe estimate](../../notes/actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) applies those scalar inequalities to arbitrary coefficient arrays with the stated bounds. The [spectral propagation proof](../../notes/actual_conway_mixed_core_spectral_propagation.md) then carries the estimates through turns and products, at the actual geometric action. These are written analytical arguments. They do not infer their conclusions from a longer list of sampled levels. The [general marked geometry](../../notes/actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) follows the original diagram's face pairings and primitive cusp paths. Its completeness and smooth-filling arguments are also mathematical proofs rather than numerical manifold recognition. The theorem uses the original literal diagram for topology even when a different algebraic expression is useful for an estimate. ## Checks for the pointed quantum \(A\)-period The [operator-period corollary](../../notes/actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) combines the exact ADO annihilator and finite-pointing theorems with the already proved knot-volume limit. It does not estimate the invariant by replacing a signed companion-matrix product with its norm. Its constant-term formula is exactly the original scalar. The relevant scripts are: python3 repro/run_research_checks.py pointed-a The first checks the generic finite crossing lift, finite-boundary identities and the repairs used when an elimination relation vanishes after summation or root specialization. The second checks moving-\(q\) germs, including singular recurrence steps and their bounded derivative budgets. The third checks the coefficient ratio of the banded Gram determinants against the actual finite vector of color values. The general existence, uniqueness and asymptotic statements still rest on the corresponding proofs. The recorded outputs specify exactly which finite cases were run. ## Installing dependencies and reading a result file For the core symbolic and numerical scripts, install the recorded dependencies in a suitable Python environment: python3 -m pip install -r requirements-core.txt A result file's scope field explains what a successful check means. Some scripts verify exact algebra; others compare an exact expression with an asymptotic approximation at selected parameters. Optional geometry checks may require SnapPy, Regina, Sage or packages named by that script. There is no claim that every historical diagnostic is one application-wide passing test suite. The remainder is a topic-by-topic map of the earlier calculations. It retains their check counts and limitations so that a reader can reproduce an argument without confusing evidence for one formula with proof of a broader theorem. ## Coefficient regions in the general-plat method In this group of notes, a degree records how much of a face variable occurs in a polynomial coefficient. The labels CROSS, LEFT and RIGHT name regions of those degree inequalities; they are not new types of knot crossing. A protected variable is one fixed by the marked coefficient extraction. A seam is a boundary shared by two such degree regions.
