(3.1) All operations are polynomial remainders, multiplication matrices, determinants and number-field norms. Equivalently one can use successive resultants. Evaluation L_j->l_j sends H_N to Z_N, so Q_N(Z_N)=P_N(Z_N)=0. Thus (2.2) is a marked-root limit for explicitly A-generated integer polynomials P_N. The chosen root is essential. A field norm or the largest root over all independent sheet choices can combine other periods. No formula for such an unmarked choice is asserted. This construction is a classical polynomial period, with an existing algebraic norm definition; it is not a new definition of the literature quantum A-operator. ## 4. Cover transfer is exact before taking the limit For a peripheral monomial map m'=m^a l^b, l'=m^c l^d, k=ad-bc>0, use the same sampled marked points upstairs and transfer the integer increments by a'_j=a a_j+b b_j, b'_j=c a_j+d b_j. Then ordinary multiplication proves exactly product_j (l'_j)^(a'_j)(m'_j)^(-b'_j)=Z_N^k. (4.1) Thus this algebraic period has the correct degree law before any asymptotic argument. For a connected one-cusped manifold cover, k is the manifold degree. Laurent elimination gives the upstairs geometric A-factor as in [the cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md). Independent rounding upstairs changes the scaled log by o(1), so it gives the same limiting law. ## 5. A connected infinite class from the twist presentation Here is an independent algebraic connectedness argument, which avoids assuming an irreducibility theorem from the literature. Use the signed twist convention G_k=<a,b | a w^k=w^k b>, w=ab^(-1)a^(-1)b. Reading a full pair in the twist box conjugates by w; after k pairs the clasp closes by a w^k=w^k b. For k=1 the relation reduces to aba=bab. The hyperbolic twist members have k<=-1 or k>=2. The independently certified families in [the twist topology note](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md) have parameters p=-k-1 (even family) and p=k-2 (odd family), respectively. Their geometry is supplied by the explicit positive face/angle proof, rather than a cited character-variety irreducibility theorem. On the nonabelian meridian chart use A=[M 1;0 M^(-1)], B=[M 0;-u M^(-1)], s=M^2+M^(-2), W=AB^(-1)A^(-1)B, z=Tr(W)=u^2+(2-s)u+2. Direct multiplication gives A W-W B=(s-u-1)(A-B). Let S_(-1)=0,S_0=1,S_(j+1)=z S_j-S_(j-1), extended to all integer indices, and put S=S_(k-1),T=S_(k-2). Cayley--Hamilton gives the single relation (s-u-1)S-T=0. (5.1) Consecutive S,T have no common root. Also S(2)=k, T(2)=k-1. Set v=s-u-1; then z=2+u(1-v). On (5.1), S!=0 and v!=1: otherwise z=2 and S-T=1 would contradict (5.1). Hence every point of this chart is given by the rational parametrization v=T/S, u=(z-2)S/(S-T), s=z-1/[S(S-T)]. (5.2) The last equality uses S^2+T^2-z S T=1. This proves absolute irreducibility of the relevant (s,u) curve. The squared meridian m=M^2 gives the double cover m^2-s(z)m+1=0. (5.3) It is also absolutely irreducible. For k>0, D=S(S-T) has degree 2k-2, so (z-2)D-1 has odd degree 2k-1, is coprime to D, and has an odd-order zero. Thus s(z)^2-4 cannot be a square in C(z). For k=-h<0, take the largest real root z_0 of S_h, which lies in [0,2). At that point T=0, S^2=1, D=1, so s(z_0)=z_0-1 is strictly between -2 and 2. The real rational function s(z)^2-4 is negative there and positive for large real z, since s(z)~z. A real rational function that is a square in C(z) is either a real square or minus a real square: conjugating its square root gives the same root up to sign. Such a function cannot change sign on its real regular locus. This proves (5.3). Consequently this real irreducible marked eigenvalue curve contains both conjugate complete holonomies. The preferred squared longitude is a rational function on it, obtained from its peripheral word; its A-image is nonconstant and the map to that curve is finite on regular open sets. The complete volume values and boundary differential are (1.1). Therefore the polynomial limit theorem applies to every hyperbolic member of this twist family. The rational parametrization and connectedness are the additional algebraic checks here. The full hyperbolic geometry and preferred-peripheral certificates are the previously reconstructed ones; their conventions still have to be kept when writing a numerical A-polynomial. ## 6. A simpler cone product when a zero-volume endpoint is available This gives a useful direct numerical test, independent of the rounded two-endpoint construction. In ordinary SL_2 coordinates take the expanding longitude L(alpha), with M(alpha)=exp(i alpha/2), 0<=alpha<=Theta, along a geometric cone family ending at volume zero. Schlaefli gives Vol(X)=integral_0^Theta log|L(alpha)| d alpha. If M_E=exp(i Theta/2) is algebraic, choose q_N^N=M_E on that arc and L_j the continued A-root at M_j=q_N^j. Then lim_(N->infinity) (Theta/N) log|product_(j<N) L_j|=Vol(X). (6.1) The proof is the Riemann-sum theorem, including continuous or integrable logarithmic endpoint singularities. The geometric cone and zero-volume endpoint are hypotheses, not consequences of alternatingness. The earlier [cone-transfer note](quantum_a_volume.md) supplies this geometry and its quadratic A-factor for the figure-eight. Here the left side is the algebraic root product itself; no transfer-state dominance assumption is required. ## 7. Scope and coverage The classical regulator/volume framework is existing work. [Guilloux--Marche, 1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395) studies exact polynomials, their volume functions and Mahler measures. Its abstract was checked for coverage; its proofs are not premises for the arguments above. A bare Mahler measure is a different observable from the marked product here and can collect several volume contributions. [Hoste--Shanahan, math/0311051](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311051) provides adjacent coverage of twist-character recursions. The matrix, Chebyshev and irreducibility arguments above are independent of that proof. This is a proved classical marked polynomial-period limit, with an explicit broad connectedness criterion and the twist family application. Its finite sampling is not canonical. Constructing a preferred sequence from an existing quantum A-definition, and proving its volume limit, remains a further goal. Recovering Kashaev directly is its own subsequent objective, as distinguished from a relation with Jones. ## 8. Relation to the actual Kashaev torsor program The intended quantum route uses the A-structure attached to Kashaev itself to prove its volume growth. Its comparison with the previous repo is in [the primary status, Section 0](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md#0-comparison-with-the-previous-work-in-this-repo). The finite classical products above are not already that invariant. A direct small-level calibration is instructive: for the figure-eight at N=2 the cone product in Section 6 is 2+sqrt(3), whereas the original enhanced Kashaev crossing gives 5. The audit evaluates the latter directly from its W-symbol and pivotal closure, without a Jones evaluation. This only distinguishes this particular classical product from the finite invariant. It is not an obstruction to the invariant's own quantum A-torsor route. There is already a direct operator-period mechanism in [the all-level A-period note](all_level_a_period.md): a specified actual quantum annihilator and finitely many fixed initial periods recover Kashaev exactly by a companion product and whole-germ root evaluation. Its verification uses the original cut and quantum-group quotient modules. Jones need not be a definition or a proof input there. There is no need to reconstruct the invariant from the bare classical polynomial alone. The intrinsic route already starts with its actual annihilator and pointed source. Its geometric classical support and selected regulator norm are the missing conclusions. The classical product identity above supplies neither conclusion for that quantum object. A comparison to Jones is additional. [Audit](../experiments/audit_a_polynomial_volume_limits.py). [Results](../experiments/a_polynomial_volume_limits_results.json).

title: Exact boundary reduction of the original quantum-A energy
text: # Exact boundary reduction of the original quantum-A energy 28 October 2026. This implements the proposed boundary-to-interior strategy at the level of the original pointed operator. A regular interior with a weighted symbol gap can be eliminated with controlled cost. Its entire effect is an explicit positive operator on the retained boundary packets. This operator retains the original source, turning regions, endpoint resonance and selected observable. The reduction is proved below. A sharp estimate for its selected boundary response is not proved. In particular, uniqueness does not supply that estimate: a concrete two-endpoint example in Section 4 has an excellent interior gap and an exponentially small boundary eigenvalue. The complementary [interval propagation theorem](actual_pointed_a_interval_observability.md) gives a controlled whole-line Green extension and exponential inward decay from both retained endpoint packets, including shrinking symbol gaps. This note identifies the exact positive operator that determines those packets in the original global source. A subsequent [macroscopic actual-source estimate](actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md) does now bound the whole original value by a classical spectral integral, under its explicit actual-operator and classical-order hypotheses. Comparing that rate with volume remains open broadly. For the proposed stepwise energy mechanism, the [pointed metric calculation](actual_pointed_metric_transport_and_crossing_obstruction.md) shows precisely what source and endpoint costs must be retained and why tame full-space metrics can lose coherent phase cancellation. ## 1. Eliminate only an interior whose estimate has been proved Use the full bounded-jet system and weights in [the actual bulk energy theorem](actual_pointed_a_bulk_agmon_energy.md): L u=f, P=L* L, g=L* f, beta=f* f. (1) Here * means Hermitian transpose. The actual source consists of the fixed initial identity rows. Choose the remaining column set B to contain their colors, the complete color, and every turning, end or other exceptional packet. Write I for the regular interior columns. Thus g_I=0 exactly. No color or normal jet in B is removed. Suppose the full-output estimate on vectors supported in I gives mu ||v||^2 <= <v,P_II v>, ||P|| <= C, mu>0. (2) For example a fixed weighted symbol gap eta gives mu=eta^2/4 for large N by the proved localized Plancherel estimate. Several regular intervals are allowed: keep enough exceptional columns between them that the full banded operator does not couple their supports, or apply that same estimate to their union with its uniform gap. The operator in (2) retains ALL output rows meeting I. Set A=P_II, H=-A^(-1)P_IB, S=P_BB-P_BI A^(-1)P_IB, E v=(H v,v). (3) Then the exact original solution obeys u_I=H u_B, S u_B=g_B. (4) Moreover 0<=S<=P_BB, ||H||<=C/mu, ker P=E ker S. (5) Proof. Complete the square, for arbitrary v_I,v_B: <v,Pv>=<v_I-Hv_B,A(v_I-Hv_B)>+<v_B,Sv_B>. (6) This proves positivity, the Schur bound and the kernel assertion; the normal equations P u=g with g_I=0 prove (4). Conversely (4) implies the normal equations. Since the original system is consistent, their solutions also satisfy L u=f: their residual is perpendicular to the range of L while belonging to that range. Thus no spurious boundary solution has replaced the original source. For a weighted complete-color projection T_B, its value is T_B u_B. The original unweighted value is exp(-N phi(1)) times that value. For any full observable R u, its exact boundary observable is R_eff=R_I H+R_B, R u=R_eff u_B. (7) The fixed-jet pointing theorem gives ker P subset ker R for the selected constant-color observables (including their weighted versions). Consequently ker S subset ker R_eff. Higher-jet nonuniqueness is retained and does not change the observable. The estimates in (5) show that bulk elimination itself costs at most a power of N whenever mu^(-1) does. ## 2. The residual boundary period is positive and source-exact Let nu=dim ker S, equal to dim ker P and hence bounded by the original fixed jet budget. Define the two polynomials Q_B(lambda)=det(S+lambda I), D_B(lambda,z)=det[ S+lambda I+z R_eff* R_eff g_B; g_B* beta ]. (8) Then the SAME original selected energy is exactly ||R u||^2=[lambda^nu z]D_B/[lambda^nu]Q_B. (9) The denominator is positive; all coefficients of both polynomials are nonnegative real numbers. In particular (9) keeps the boundary source, rather than substituting a maximum eigenvalue or arbitrary boundary vector. Here is a direct proof. Since (1) is consistent, (4) gives beta=<u,Pu>=<u_B,S u_B>=g_B* S^+ g_B. (10) The matrix [S,g_B;g_B*,beta] is positive semidefinite: it is the Schur complement of A in the Gram matrix [P,g;g*,beta]. Factor it as Z* Z. Appending rows sqrt(lambda)[I,0] and sqrt(z)[R_eff,0] gives the matrix in (8). Expanding its determinant as squared minors proves coefficient nonnegativity. The same argument applies to Q_B. Decompose the boundary space orthogonally into ker S and its orthogonal complement. Both g_B and R_eff vanish on the kernel in the appropriate sense. Thus D_B has a factor lambda^nu. On the complement, S is positive definite and (10) makes its bordered Schur complement zero at z=0. Its derivative in z at lambda=0 is g_B* S^(-1) R_eff* R_eff S^(-1) g_B=||R_eff u_B||^2. Multiplication by det(S on (ker S)^perp) proves (9). This is a smaller exact period whenever I occupies most colors. With finitely many exceptional windows of width o(N), its matrix size is o(N), although its entries may retain exponentially small transport information. The latter qualification is essential. Auxiliary regulator weights need not themselves be algebraic; they are an estimating metric, not a new definition of the quantum invariant. Undoing the weight gives the original period exactly. ## 3. Regular interior coupling decays with distance Assume the block bandwidth of P is w and its norm is at most C>0. The proof of (2) gives mu<=C. In the original color distance, the interior Green blocks satisfy ||(A^(-1))_(jk)|| <= mu^(-1) exp[-mu |j-k|/(2 C w)]. (11) If w=0 the inverse is block diagonal instead. To prove (11), expand A^(-1)=(2C)^(-1) sum_(n>=0) (I-A/(2C))^n. The norm of the n-th power is at most (1-mu/(2C))^n. Its (j,k) block vanishes for n<ceil(|j-k|/w), even when I has gaps. Summing this tail and using 1-a<=exp(-a) gives (11). This is a direct banded-matrix proof, independent of diagonalizing the classical transfer. For widely separated boundary columns j,k, (3) therefore gives ||S_(jk)|| <= C' mu^(-1) exp[-c mu (|j-k|-2w)] when |j-k|>2w. (12) Only finitely many P neighbors of j and k occur in the product in (3). The analogous formula u_I=H u_B gives a sum of exponentially decaying contributions from the retained boundary data. If those data and the inverse gap are controlled, the regular interior carries their estimate with polynomial loss. It does not generate an additional volume exponent. The estimate is on the exact response, including all jets. ## 4. Why the residual boundary estimate is necessary Consider a simple, fully rigid sourced recurrence on j=0,...,n: y_0=b, y_(j+1)-2 y_j=0. (13) Its weighted gap with weight zero is |exp(i theta)-2|>=1. Its interior Gram matrix on I={1,...,n-1} has diagonal 5 and off-diagonal -2, so A>=I for every n. Keep B={0,n}. Eliminating I minimizes the energy |y_0|^2+sum_(j=0)^(n-1)|y_(j+1)-2y_j|^2 for prescribed endpoints. Since y_n-2^n y_0=sum_(j=0)^(n-1)2^(n-1-j) (y_(j+1)-2y_j), Cauchy--Schwarz, with equality attained by proportional residuals, gives D_n=sum_(j=0)^(n-1)4^j=(4^n-1)/3, <y_B,S y_B>=|y_0|^2+|y_n-2^n y_0|^2/D_n, S=[1+4^n/D_n, -2^n/D_n; -2^n/D_n, 1/D_n]. (14) The retained source is g_B=(b,0), beta=|b|^2. Solving S y_B=g_B gives y_0=b and y_n=2^n b, exactly as in (13). Yet ||S|| is bounded, det S=1/D_n, and its smallest eigenvalue is asymptotic to 3*4^(-n)/4. Thus a uniformly controlled bulk, a two-dimensional boundary space, and uniqueness still allow exponential source amplification. In (9) the selected period is exactly 4^n |b|^2. This example is a logical test of the propagation inference, not a knot counterexample. It explains why the actual boundary Schur operator and its selected source must be estimated rather than deleted. ## 5. The exact remaining geometric target For the actual complete-color observable, (9), together with undoing the weight, reduces the desired upper bound to a selected boundary response estimate. A sufficient condition is ||R_eff S^+ g_B|| <= exp[N Vol(S^3 minus K)/(2pi)+o(N)], (15) when R_eff includes undoing the weight. If R_eff selects only the weighted complete color, the right side is instead multiplied by exp(N phi(1)). This equivalence is explicit; it is not a proof of (15). One may also seek a source-compatible transport flag or an exact boundary factorization which proves (15) without bounding S^+ on irrelevant channels. The regulator must retain its source anchor: phi(0)=0 fixes the initial source scale, and a bound on absolute branch regulators alone controls their differences by at most 2 Vol. Neither (3) nor (9) removes that issue. The local physical-face fillings give possible information for the exceptional packets, but their identification with this complete boundary response still requires an exact source comparison. The independently proved ordinary-color bound concerns the CONSTANT color components j<N. It does not bound the normal jets in B. Those jets are necessary at singular recurrence steps, and (3)--(9) retain them. Replacing the complete boundary packet by its constant-color projection would therefore be an additional unproved inference. This is a constructive boundary-to-interior reduction, valid for the actual original operator wherever its stated bulk gap is verified. No broad sharp whole-source bound or geometric survival theorem is claimed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_a_boundary_schur_transport.py): four actual figure-eight source elimination identities, an exact rank-deficient rational fixture for the selected coefficient ratio, and four exact recurrence Schur complements. The actual scalar audit does not assert truncated-jet uniqueness; that input is the full pointed-system theorem used in the proof above.

title: Adaptive Fermat sampling preserves the entire original crossing source
text: # Adaptive Fermat sampling preserves the entire original crossing source 28 October 2026. The internal root-orbit source may be placed on its exact Fourier resonance without changing the original finite crossing operator. Its sampling point is allowed to depend on the input/output heads. The old degree-zero restriction is replaced by two explicit physical source walls. This is not an unsupported central base change or a modification of one homogeneous summand. The resulting source-flat family has a first-normal-jet reconstruction at resonance, with jet order independent of N. It fixes the whole finite state, including its currents. It does not prove a global geometric coefficient is nonzero. ## 1. Complete Laurent kernel and its only alias Put Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), d=N-1, retain the actual color x and scalar kappa, and use the COMPLETE positive crossing polynomial K(t)=B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0) R_N(z_6/z_0,x^(-1)z_6/t) B_N(x^(-1)z_7/z_6,x^(-2)z_7/t). (1) The physical crossing is its original finite input/output block, with kappa retained. This is the proved Gaussian-absorbed complete kernel; no original Gaussian was deleted from a separated sector. Expand the three factors with indices (i,j),(r,k),(h,l), respectively, each nonnegative pair having sum<N. One term has input demands a=j+r, b=i, output degrees c=r+k-h, e=h+l, t exponent p=i+j-k-l, c+e-a-b=-p. (2) In particular input powers are nonpositive, second-output degree is at most d, both output degrees are at most d, and -2d<=p<=d. For any nonzero sampling root t_0, (1/N)sum_(j=0)^d K(t_0 Q^j) =CT_t K+t_0^(-N)[t^(-N)]K. (3) There is exactly one possible alias. This identity is an equality of the COMPLETE finite Laurent kernel before any source split. ## 2. A source-flat adaptive family, including exact resonance Let A be an independent scalar source parameter. Choose the algebraic sampling root by t_0^(-N)=z_1^(-N)-A z_7^(-N). (4) The normalized symmetric root average is independent of which Nth root is chosen. Equations (3)--(4) show its two errors explicitly: z_1^(-N)[t^(-N)]K-A z_7^(-N)[t^(-N)]K. (5) The FIRST term demands incoming second index at least N, since K has no positive powers of z_1. The original finite INPUT space kills it. The SECOND term has negative second-output degree, since K has z_7 degree at most d. The original finite OUTPUT block kills it. Therefore the adaptive average has EXACTLY the original finite crossing operator, for EVERY A, not merely its closed trace. This is stronger than the earlier total-degree alias argument. The root t_0 has overall head degree one, so that argument alone would not apply. The two physical index walls in (5) are the replacement. No alias deletion is asserted for a separately continued full-Psi homogeneous/current sector. The symmetric average is linear in t_0^(-N). It consequently extends regularly across z_1^(-N)-A z_7^(-N)=0, even though the individual sample points then go to infinity. One first takes the COMPLETE symmetric average and the original finite block, not a value of a single divergent sample. In the all-homogeneous one-Psi field, the full-turn multiplier is (z_7/z_1)^N[1-(z_1/t_0)^N]=A. (6) Thus A=1 is precisely its exact Fourier resonance. It is reached inside an actual source-flat family, rather than by imposing A=1 inside the old co-source. The normalized finite-orbit/Fourier formula then has zero FINAL closure current and its explicitly known nonzero resonant coefficient. The pre-existing B/R currents must still be kept unless a further proved source map removes them. The stronger independent external-frame construction in [the balanced crossing theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) also balances all three B/R sources. That theorem is compatible with the present head-adaptive source map; it is not assumed in its proof. ## 3. Both signs and whole original words At complete color x=-q^(-1), the exact balanced relation is R_-=P overline(R_+)P, with the common scalar conjugated to kappa^(-1). Apply this relation to the COMPLETE polynomial source, with opposite root Q^(-1) and the formal two heads exchanged. Its adaptive negative sampling is t_(0,-)^(-N)=z_0^(-N)-A z_6^(-N). (7) The errors now demand first INPUT index at least N or have negative first OUTPUT degree. Both are removed by the SAME original physical finite blocks. This is an exact negative source representation, not a fixed-value balance of the old negative continuous Gaussian. Hence any number of crossings in ANY original signed braid or plat may be replaced simultaneously. Their finite matrices agree entrywise, and the original cups/caps, pivot, marked row, Cartan and zero-framing lines are unchanged. Arbitrary bridge count is allowed. There is also a raw no-healing formulation: the two complete modified kernels still have only nonnegative input demands and output upper bound d. A negative output cannot be healed at the next touching kernel, since that input has no such coefficient; an input demand at least N cannot be supplied by any preceding output. The original finite end sources kill surviving untouched invalid heads. This does not authorize arbitrary Laurent coupons that change that support. ## 4. The unsplit cyclic inhomogeneous equation The COMPLETE state has a concrete cyclic connection, not only the one-function homogeneous equation. Put u_0=t/z_1, v_0=x^(-1)t/z_0, a=x^(-1)z_7/z_6, c=z_6/z_0, w=x^(-1)z_6/t, B_0(t)=B_N(u_0,v_0), F(t)=B_N(a,a w)R_N(c,w), Y(t)=B_0(t)F(t)=K(t), D_0=1-u_0^N+v_0^N, H_pair=D_B R_N(c,w)+a D_R B_N(a,Qa w). The exact finite Newton/Rogers Ward equations imply POINTWISE Y(t)-b(t)Y(t/Q)=eta(t), b(t)=(z_7/z_1)(1-Q z_1/t), eta=B_0(t)H_pair(t)+(Qac/v_0)D_0 F(t/Q). (8) Indeed F(t)-ac F(t/Q)=H_pair(t), and v_0 B_0(t)=(u_0-Q)B_0(t/Q)+Q D_0. Multiplying these two identities proves (8) with every endpoint and source norm present. In particular the source eta is not declared zero on resonance. At t_j=t_0 Q^j, let Y_j=Y(t_j), eta_j=eta(t_j), and define (T_A v)_j=b(t_j)v_(j-1), j modulo N. Then T_A^N=A I by (6), and the actual state satisfies (I-T_A)Y=eta. (9) All these are finite algebraic functions on the specified sampling cover; no formal WKB expansion or choice of a new period is involved. ## 5. Resonant first-normal-source reconstruction On a regular local chart of the cover (4), let G_A=I+T_A+...+T_A^(N-1). The exact geometric-series identity gives G_A eta=(1-A)Y. (10) At A=1 the left side vanishes. Since the whole original state is regular on this chart, differentiating the ACTUAL source family gives Y|_(A=1)=-d_A(G_A eta)|_(A=1). (11) Thus the entire resonant finite state is fixed by the first normal jet of its explicit unsplit source, with jet order ONE independent of N. This is a source identity, not an instruction to divide by 1-A and separately evaluate a vanishing numerator. For an explicit homogeneous coefficient choose a holomorphic branch omega=A^(1/N) near one and the periodic cyclic gauge g_j(A), g_0=1, b(t_j)g_(j-1)=omega g_j. All b(t_j) are nonzero at resonance. Write tildeY_j=Y_j/g_j and tildeeta_j=eta_j/g_j. Averaging their equation yields mean(tildeeta)=(1-omega)mean(tildeY). Consequently its zero-clock homogeneous projection coefficient is mean(tildeY)|_(A=1) =-N*d_A mean(tildeeta)|_(A=1). (12) The normalized homogeneous vector g_j at resonance is the actual Fermat/cyclic full-Psi vector with the independently fixed Fourier normalizer. Equation (12) constructs its comparison coefficient from the original source, rather than assuming that coefficient exists or is nonzero. Its possible vanishing and its geometric overlap after exterior contraction still have to be checked. For a fixed word with m internal orbit variables, apply (10) to each complete tensor factor before the original finite contraction. The whole original period is thereby a mixed FIRST normal derivative in each of m independent source parameters at their Fermat values. The required jet order depends on the fixed word, not on N. These derivatives include the moving root and all source terms; differentiating only a homogeneous block would not be the same operation. ## 6. Scope The adaptive sampling and normal-source formulas are exact, source preserving and valid for all original signed finite words. They close an actual internal circle on its resonant algebraic multisection and give a prescribed normal-jet pointing there. Neither the one-dimensional homogeneous space nor its nonzero local Fourier vector by itself proves survival of the final geometric period. That remaining claim cannot be obtained by invoking divisor rigidity without the actual global source coefficient supplied by (12) and the exterior pairing.

title: The genuine adjacent observable algebra and its macroscopic source filtration
text:
# The genuine adjacent observable algebra and its macroscopic source filtration 29 October 2026. Two ACTUAL adjacent interval Casimirs already generate the full matrix algebra on the complete three-head source multiplicity. This narrows the older arbitrary-coupon quotient obstruction to a small physical moment-map algebra. Its proof is constructive and retains the original nilpotent normal source. The associated filtration is equally important: bounded-degree source tests see zero until an integer traversal of length N-1. A single original crossing has precisely that macroscopic observable degree. Thus full matrix generation does not disprove a filtered or microlocal geometric reduction, and low-degree source-null identities do not by themselves control its norm. ## 1. Original matrices, sources and charts Let N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, rho=q-q^(-1). On the COMPLETE original W=(V tensor V)_(degree d), use e_j=|j,d-j>. The actual interval Casimirs A=Omega12 and B=Omega23, in the left highest chart, are \[ A_{j,j}=q+q^{-1}-q(1-Q^j)^2-q^{-1}(1-Q^{j+1})^2, \qquad A_{j-1,j}=A_{j,j-1}=-(1-Q^j)^2, 	ag{1} \] \[ Be_j=c_je_j+b_je_{j-1},\qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad b_j=Q^j+Q^{-j}-2. 	ag{2} \] All off-diagonal coefficients in (1) are nonzero. Put c*=q+q^(-1). The original cup and ordinary cap are \[ p_j=Nx^{j-d},\qquad \ell_j=x^{-j}Q^{-j}/N=x^j/N. \] The complete anti-Pascal chart J satisfies the exact source identities \[ JB=AJ,\quad JAJ^{-1}=B^{\mathsf T},\quad Jp=Nx^{-d}e_d,\quad \ell J^{-1}=(x^d/N)e_0^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{3} \] These are the original coproduct and actual cap identities from [the complete source theorem](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), not a semisimple replacement. In particular all N multiplicities, both members of every colliding Casimir pair, and even levels remain. ## 2. A tame nilpotent source operator generates all channels The monic characteristic polynomial of A is \[ \mathcal P_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^d(z-c_j)=2T_N(z/2)+2. \] Its roots have multiplicity two, except the simple root -2 when N is odd. At N=2 it is z^2, so the following construction also applies. The irreducible Jacobi matrix A has cyclic endpoint vectors; hence its minimal polynomial is this full degree-N polynomial. Set Q0(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c*)^2. Define the explicit degree-d observable \[ \Xi_0(A)= rac{(A-c*)Q_0(A)}{Q_0(c*)}. \] Then \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Xi_0(A)=	heta p\ell,\qquad 	heta=(-1)^Nho^2
e0.} 	ag{4} \] Here is a proof not assuming a Jordan basis. At all other Casimir nodes the polynomial has the full required vanishing multiplicity. At c* it has value 0 and derivative 1. The eigenspace of an irreducible Jacobi matrix is one-dimensional, so its range is the original eigenline Cp and its row is the original eigenrow Cell. The coefficient is fixed by its (0,d) entry. Lower matrix powers cannot connect d to 0, and \[ (A^d)_{0,d}=\prod_{j=1}^d[-(1-Q^j)^2]=(-1)^dN^2. \] The elementary Chebyshev differential equation at the double zero gives Q0(c*)=N^2/(4-c*^2)=-N^2/rho^2. Since p0 ell_d=1, the coefficient in (4) is theta. This proves its normalization, including the exceptional N=2 case. In the original positive physical norm, \[ \|\Xi_0(A)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=N|ho|^2\leq4\pi^2/N. 	ag{5} \] Indeed ||p||^2=N^3 and ||ell||^2=1/N. This rank-one normal source is polynomially controlled; it is not an exponentially conditioned projector. It is nonzero even though it is square-zero, because ell p=0. For 0<=r,s<=d, \[ B^r\Xi_0(A)B^s=	heta(B^rp)(\ell B^s). 	ag{6} \] By (3), the columns B^r p are a basis: their J images are a nonzero constant times A^r e_d, which are triangular endpoint Krylov columns. The rows ell B^s are also a basis, since their products with J^(-1) are a nonzero constant times e0^T A^s. Therefore the N^2 operators in (6) are a basis of End(W). In particular \[  oxed{\displaystyle \mathbb C\langle A,Bangle =\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C).} 	ag{7} \] No arbitrary Borel-relative matrix coupon is needed for (7): A and B are the two actual adjacent interval observables. ## 3. Consequence for an exact positive or invariant quotient Suppose a linear quotient q0:W->H is compatible with these two observables: q0 A=A' q0 and q0 B=B' q0. Its kernel is invariant under (7), and is therefore either 0 or all of W. If it preserves the original source and its inserted observable values it cannot be the zero quotient, since \[ \ell B^d p=(-1)^dN^2
e0. 	ag{8} \] Thus it is injective. Equivalently, a positive semidefinite packet Gram whose nullspace is invariant under BOTH actual observables cannot remove a source channel: its nullspace is 0 or it kills the entire original source representation. A multiplicative quotient imposing a nonzero relation on this actual observable algebra is likewise impossible while retaining all source insertions. In particular setting the rank-one normal (4) to zero generates the whole matrix ideal by (6). This is a restriction on an EXACT observable-compatible quotient, not a no-go theorem for a nonmultiplicative Ward pushforward, a current-complex reduction, or a geometric comparison after taking semiclassical asymptotics. Nor does it preclude a faithful embedding of W into a larger positive angle space satisfying additional edge constraints. Such an embedding need not be a smaller quotient of this observable representation. The same statement applies to a reflected double IF both copies of the actual observable algebra are retained independently: (7) then gives the full matrix algebra on W tensor conjugate(W). It is not asserted for a construction that retains only synchronous diagonal braid action and no independent copy observables. ## 4. The exact source filtration: degree N-1 is essential Define \[ \mathcal F_m=\operatorname{span}\{p,Bp,\ldots,B^mp\}, \qquad0\leq m\leq d. \] The endpoint Jacobi calculation and (3) give EXACTLY \[ J\mathcal F_m=\operatorname{span}\{e_{d-m},\ldots,e_d\}, \quad\dim\mathcal F_m=m+1, \quad A\mathcal F_m\subset\mathcal F_m, \quad B\mathcal F_m\subset\mathcal F_{m+1}. 	ag{9} \] The A statement uses JAJ^(-1)=B^T, which is LOWER bidiagonal, and therefore preserves the displayed terminal coordinate subspace. Also \[ \ell|_{\mathcal F_{d-1}}=0,\qquad \ell B^m p=0\ (m<d),\qquad \ell B^d p=(-1)^dN^2. 	ag{10} \] More generally EVERY mixed word with fewer than d occurrences of B has zero original pairing ell w(A,B)p, independently of the number of A factors. In the J chart each B can lower the integer index by at most one, each A preserves or raises it, and the source travels from d to 0. Thus there is no cyclic shortcut. At the first detected degree the complete associated-graded source is explicit. For any nonnegative integers a0,...,ad, \[  oxed{\displaystyle \ell A^{a_0}B A^{a_1}B\cdots B A^{a_d}p =(-1)^dN^2\prod_{j=0}^d c_j^{a_j}.} 	ag{11} \] With exactly d lowering opportunities, every B must use its lowering Jacobi entry and every A its diagonal entry. This proves (11) as a unique finite path, with all original source constants cancelling as (Nx^(-d))(x^d/N)=1. In particular, for N>=3 and 1<=r<=d-1, \[ \ell B^{d-r}(A-c*)B^rp =(-1)^dN^2(c_r-c*)
e0. 	ag{12} \] The local cup relation (A-c*)p=0 therefore cannot be reimposed after an arbitrary legitimate exterior. Its first detectable exterior has macroscopic observable degree, not bounded degree. For the selected normal (4), the exact factorization (6) implies that an exterior on BOTH sides needs at least d B occurrences on each side before the original scalar can detect it. Its retained response is nevertheless explicitly local, rather than an unspecified lost normal direction. For ANY allowed exteriors U,V, \[ \ell U\Xi_0(A)Vp=	heta(\ell Up)(\ell Vp). 	ag{12a} \] This is the actual cup--cap rank-one surgery (4), with its known normalization; it does not define a metric from an unknown closed period. The individual factors still require their own estimates. With r such normals the exact correction is \(\ell U_0\Xi_0U_1\cdots\Xi_0U_rp =	heta^r\prod_{j=0}^r(\ell U_jp)\). All factors are in the SAME original cap/cup normalization; converting them to separately normalized knot periods retains their individual known external lines. No inequality between their volumes is implied. ## 5. A fixed braid already reaches the macroscopic degree This degree distinction is not permission to ignore it for fixed knot diagrams. The actual adjacent crossing is R23=kappa r_N(B), a polynomial of degree<N. Its coefficient at B^d has EXACT modulus N^(-2): \[  oxed{\displaystyle [B^d]R_{23}= rac{\kappa(-1)^d x^{-d}}{N^2}.} 	ag{13} \] To prove it directly from the original crossing, highest-chart extraction forces one finite transfer and gives (R23 p)_j=kappa p_j F_(d-j). Therefore \[ \ell R_{23}p=\kappa x^{-d} \sum_{k=0}^d Q^{k+1}F_k=\kappa x^{-d}. 	ag{14} \] The last sum telescopes, Q^(k+1)F_k=F_k-F_(k+1), with F_N=0. All lower polynomial degrees pair to zero by (10), proving (13). In particular the original crossing really has degree d, at every level, and its first detected source coefficient is polynomially large rather than exponentially suppressed. A fixed number of actual crossings can therefore expose the normal even though low-degree observable tests cannot. From (12a),(14), \[ \ell R_{23}\Xi_0(A)R_{23}p =	heta\kappa^2x^{-2d}=	heta x^{-d}
e0, 	ag{14a} \] of exact modulus |rho|^2. This is a polynomial-sized normal current between TWO original crossings. It must not be set to zero in an exact source identity, but it is compatible with a filtered construction that explicitly retains and estimates polynomial normal counterterms. These statements concern the specified complete source sector; no rank-one formula is asserted on an unrestricted larger multiplicity space without its actual charge projector. For any polynomial f of degree<d, (14) also gives the elementary operator-norm separation \[ \|R_{23}-f(B)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq1/N, 	ag{15} \] since the original source has dual product ||ell|| ||p||=N. This does not preclude a polynomial-error approximation at a specified order or an exponentially normalized upper comparison. It does show that fixed-degree truncation does not preserve even the first nonzero original source value automatically. The viable filtered alternative must therefore state how its fixed-degree Ward equations act on these degree-N crossing packets, including the retained normal source and the norm of the resulting counterterms. Low-degree tests against the bare cup are identically zero, so they cannot alone certify a nonzero geometric component or a polynomial-cost positive reduction. No sharp global energy estimate or obstruction to a properly controlled microlocal quotient follows from (7) alone. ## 6. Original braid algebra at prime levels For completeness there is an actual-word strengthening along every prime level. At an odd prime N, the nodal eigenvalues nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)] coincide only at the paired indices j+l=d. Indeed equality implies N divides (j-l)(j+l+1); for distinct indices primality forces j+l+1=N. At every double Casimir node r_N' is nonzero. Finite Hermite interpolation therefore recovers A as a polynomial in R12, and B as the same polynomial in R23. Hence \[ \mathbb C\langle R_{12},R_{23}angle=\operatorname{Mat}_N \quad	ext{for every prime }N. 	ag{16} \] N=2 has a single double node and nonzero derivative, so it also satisfies (16). For composite levels additional braid-phase coincidences can occur; (16) is not asserted there. The all-level observable statement (7) has no such restriction. The interpolation degrees and inverse norms in (16) are not claimed uniform or tame. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.py) reconstructs the original coproduct Casimir and physical highest intertwiner, checks the normal operator and full Krylov bases, all-level filtrations and source values, and the literal full-Cartan crossing coefficient. It does not infer a geometric norm from algebra dimension or from a finite numerical rank fit. The finite audit checks twelve literal coproduct/source modules at N=2,...,12,14, every rank-one observable generator and strict source flag, the retained normal between two actual crossings, and actual-braid recovery at the tested prime levels.

title: Exact adjacent-twist character coupling with its physical source
text: # Exact adjacent-twist character coupling with its physical source 28 October 2026. Adjacent original twist blocks have an exact coupled quantum-character algebra, not independent spectral phases. The identities below give a denominator-free braid recursion, fix the nearest-neighbor spectral phase ratios, and impose a **strict integer spectral window** on the original generic-meridian family. An actual cup port restricts the total Casimir without changing the marked co-source. These are reusable local identities at arbitrary width. They do not estimate the original whole-source q-Racah contour or prove a sharp volume upper bound or noncancellation. The exact phase coupling is a step beyond estimating separate repeated-crossing norms. ## 1. Physical trace coordinates Use the actual balanced generators K_i,F_i,Ecal_i=rho^2E_i on three physical heads, with q=exp(pi i/N), rho=q-q^(-1), delta=q+q^(-1). Let e_i=q Ecal_i and form the literal matrices L_(+,i)=[[K_i,e_i],[0,1]], L_(-,i)=[[1,0],[-K_iF_i,K_i]], G_i=L_(-,i)^(-1)L_(+,i). Keep the actual prefix-based meridians H_i from the shared quantum flags: H_1=G_1 and H_i=P_(i-1)^(-1)G_i P_(i-1), where P_(i-1)=L_(-,i-1)...L_(-,1). Define tr_q(T)=qT_11+q^(-1)T_22 and A=tr_q(H_2H_1)=Omega_12, B=tr_q(H_3H_2)=Omega_23, C=tr_q(H_3H_1), D=tr_q(H_3H_2H_1)=Omega_123. (1) The two displayed intermediate Casimirs are the actual coproduct Casimirs of the original physical heads. The prefix conjugation in B drops out of tr_q with its required q-ordering, not by ordinary trace cyclicity. Each head has central Casimir a_i; for common original meridian M, a_i=-(M+M^(-1)); at completeness a_i=-2. Set central coefficients alpha=a_1a_2+a_3D, beta=a_2a_3+a_1D, gamma=a_1a_3+a_2D. (2) The full original common Cartan cancels in conjugation statements, but remains on the actual crossing operators and their powers. ## 2. Exact quantum Fricke identities The following are finite polynomial identities, including N=2: q^(-1)AB-qBA=rho(delta C-gamma), q^(-1)BC-qCB=rho(delta A-alpha), q^(-1)CA-qAC=rho(delta B-beta), (3) [D,A]=[D,B]=[D,C]=0. They retain the coupled cubic q^(-1)ABC+q^(-2)A^2+q^2B^2+q^(-2)C^2 -q^(-1)A alpha-qB beta-q^(-1)C gamma =delta^2-a_1^2-a_2^2-a_3^2-D^2-a_1a_2a_3D. (4) No division by delta, rho, a clock determinant, or a nilpotent face is needed to state (3)--(4). Here is a reproducible algebraic proof, separate from finite-level numerical checks. Take independent quantum tori Z_i S_i=q^2S_i Z_i, and independent formal meridians M_i. Substitute K_i=-M_i q^(-1)Z_i^(-1), F_i=S_i(1-q^2 Z_i), Ecal_i=S_i^(-1)(M_i Z_i^(-1)-M_i^(-1)). (5) Their single-head Casimir is -(M_i+M_i^(-1)). Expand (1) using the two-by-two triangular inverse matrices, then put every product into the order S_1^u Z_1^v S_2^w Z_2^x S_3^y Z_3^z. Multiplication supplies only the scalar q^(2sum v_i u_i'). The accompanying certificate uses integer Laurent coefficients in q,M_1,M_2,M_3 and verifies that every coefficient of (3)--(4) is zero. A,B,C,D have respectively 14,14,62,34 Laurent terms before those identities are expanded. This is an exact generic-q polynomial certificate, not a sample at roots or an imported q-Racah theorem. It applies to the original finite nilpotent heads too. Indeed the single-head algebra with fixed Casimir has normal forms K^aF^b and K^aEcal^c; the mixed product FEcal is its fixed nonzero Laurent polynomial in K. The torus realization (5) is faithful on those normal forms: distinct F/Ecal degrees have distinct S powers, and the remaining nonzero Laurent factor cannot kill a Laurent polynomial in Z. Thus the certified identities hold in that central quantum-group quotient and then in its finite-head representations. This argument does not add the generic cyclic E endpoint to the original module. ## 3. Actual braid action and the retained twist phases The already directly verified original Hurwitz transport acts on H_1,H_2,H_3. Taking its ordered traces gives the exact identities, for equal colors (a_1=a_2=a_3=a, alpha=beta=gamma=a^2+aD), Ad(R_12):(A,B,C) -> (A,q alpha-qBA-q^2C,B), Ad(R_23):(A,B,C) -> (C,B,q alpha-qCB-q^2A). (6) The trace reductions in (6) are also included in the exact Laurent certificate, using H_i^(-1)=q^(-1)a_i I-q^(-2)H_i. Thus (6) does not infer a trace identity from a classical mnemonic. For distinct colors, the same proof retains the permuted a_i and the appropriate alpha, beta,gamma in (2); the present common-color formulas suffice for the original knot family. Literal inverse crossings give the inverse polynomial maps; no new scalar is supplied. Put B_t=R_12^t B R_12^(-t). The complete adjacent-block transport is B_(t+1)=-q B_t A-q^2 B_(t-1)+q alpha, B_0=B, B_(-1)=C. (7) This formula holds at every signed integer t and every N, with the whole physical boundary and original source unchanged. It retains the q-phase; replacing it by a real modulus recurrence is not valid. On the genuine generic-meridian family the first pair has distinct Casimir nodes and original eigenvalues c_j(Y)=q^(-1)YQ^(-j)+qY^(-1)Q^j, lambda_j(Y)=nu_jY^(-j), nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), 0<=j<N. (8) The normalized physical fusion/projector formulas in [the factorial-frame theorem](actual_twist_block_factorial_frame_bound.md) realize these operators with their actual normalizers. In particular the two homogeneous multipliers of (7) at A=c_j(Y) are -Q^(j+1)Y^(-1)=lambda_(j+1)/lambda_j, -Q^(-j)Y=lambda_(j-1)/lambda_j. (9) These are precisely the neighboring ratios of the original twist phases, not independently selected semiclassical characters. ## 4. A strict spectral window, rather than a cyclic replacement Let E_i(Y) denote the meromorphic actual pair-Casimir projectors, extended by the third head. For i!=j, project (7) between E_i and E_j. The central forcing disappears, and its scalar characteristic equation is (lambda_i/lambda_j)^2 +q c_j(Y)(lambda_i/lambda_j)+q^2=0. By (9), equality as a meromorphic function of Y forces the exponent of Y in lambda_i/lambda_j to be +1 or -1. Therefore E_i(Y) B E_j(Y)=0 unless i=j or i=j+1 or i=j-1 (10) as INTEGER indices in [0,N-1]. For N>=3 the apparent cyclic neighbor (0,N-1) is excluded. Casimir nodes alone are cyclic, but the original braiding eigenvalues (8) have a nontrivial endpoint norm character; discarding it would incorrectly allow that extra edge. The diagonal is fixed as well: (delta+c_j(Y)) E_j B E_j=E_j alpha E_j. (11) This follows from Ad(R_12)C=B and the diagonal part of (6). It is stated without dividing at a zero of the factor on the left. Equations (10)--(11) are the actual finite three-term spectral coupling underlying a q-Racah overlap. They remain identities of whole meromorphic germs at completeness; the colliding projectors cannot be independently evaluated or replaced by a semisimple root basis. For an adjacent sequence R_12^ell R_23^m, its exact kernel is obtained by composing the actual C_T E_i C_T^(-1) projector matrices with their lambda_i^ell and lambda_j^m factors, then applying the original co-source. Formula (10) supplies the coupling recurrence rather than treating those spectral labels as independent or modulo N. It does not yet evaluate the resulting multidimensional contour. ## 5. The original cup port gives the parabolic total character At completeness let p be the original cup on heads 1,2. Its actual Hopf identities E_tot p=F_tot p=0 and K_tot p=p imply that both two-head coproduct triangular matrices are identity on p. Consequently (D+2I)(p tensor v)=0 for EVERY third-head vector v. (12) Every actual word in R_12 and R_23 commutes with D, so (12) remains true on the entire transported cup-generated subspace. Spectator heads may be included. An original ordinary cap and full marked row can be left untouched: inserting D+2 into that original whole network gives zero by (12), with no change of co-source or division by a knot period. This is a forward source restriction, not an assertion that the unrestricted marked row is an invariant covector. One may NOT impose D=-2 on an arbitrary three-head port which has already interacted with outside heads. At such a port the full D in (2)--(7) must be retained and sewn to its actual exterior source. On a commutative principal chart, (4) at a_i=-2 becomes the usual four-punctured character cubic. On the actual cup slice D=-2 it is A^2+B^2+C^2+ABC-8(A+B+C)+28=0, (X+Y+Z)^2+XYZ=0, X=A-2,Y=B-2,Z=C-2. (13) This identifies the coupled trace support and its original parabolic source. It does not establish that the original spectral cycle has a nonzero intersection with its geometric place, or bound every complex boundary phase by knot volume. ## 6. Audit and remaining analytic problem python3 experiments/audit_actual_adjacent_twist_character.py The certificate checks nine generic Laurent identities with three independent formal meridians, including the cubic, centrality and both ordered Hurwitz trace reductions. Separate actual finite matrices test complete and generic M, four iterates of (7), and the original cup restriction with the FULL marked four-head plat closure. Both level parities and N=2 are included. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_adjacent_twist_character_results.json). What remains is an analytic/source theorem for the **joint** q-Racah overlap period: retain (8)--(11), its endpoint and meridian currents, and prove a contour bound or nonzero geometric coefficient after full closure. Character support and correct local phase ratios alone do not prove that estimate. No sharp-volume conclusion is claimed here. ## 7. A specific obstruction to leaving the spectral contour real At completeness the original spectral nodes are c_j(1)=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), and their real-angle limit lies in [-2,2]. On a regular physical classical chart, A is the actual trace of the product of its two based parabolic meridians, by (1). A nontrivial element in a discrete faithful hyperbolic manifold group cannot have real trace strictly between -2 and 2: such a matrix is elliptic, whereas the manifold's deck group acts freely and discretely on hyperbolic space. Thus a regular discrete-faithful pair-product trace cannot occur in the interior of this real spectral interval. A loxodromic pair product requires either a nonreal trace or a real trace outside that interval. Parabolic/central pair products belong to the turning values +/-2 and need their own retained boundary analysis. Consequently a proposed real-spectral-angle stationary proof cannot simply identify its real optimizer with a regular geometric pair whose product is loxodromic. The q-Racah spectral variable must undergo a complex deformation, or one must perform another actual polarization change with its source. This criterion is local and applies at any width; it is not a knot census or a disproof of a complex-contour route. Real eigenvalues of a nonnormal finite Casimir do not exclude complex principal characters in the original physical polarization. The claim concerns leaving THIS diagonal spectral contour real. This is why the coupled trace identities above still do not turn the local block bound into a sharp volume estimate: the actual complex spectral contour and its endpoint/normal source currents remain to be transported and bounded. They have not been selected by the algebraic cubic alone.

title: Zeros of the ADO meridian state approach the complete point
status: Nearby zeros, the required boundary factor and exact regularization
text:
# Zeros of the ADO meridian state approach the complete point 31 October 2026. For a knot whose Kashaev invariant has positive exponential growth, the reduced ADO meridian state takes exponentially different values at two points separated by order $1/N$. Its value at the complete point is the Kashaev invariant, whereas its value one quantum shift away is exactly $1$. The state is a Laurent polynomial whose degree grows at most linearly with $N$. Together these facts force actual zeros within order $1/N$ of the complete point. This note proves an explicit bound on that distance, retaining the marked meridian coordinate and the full modified-dimension factor. The obstruction to a uniform nonzero scalar asymptotic expression across the two points was already described in the [formal A-curve period discussion](formal_a_curve_period_torsor.md#the-actual-peripheral-normalization-includes-a-difference-constant) and the [regular-period construction](regularized_kashaev_period.md). The quantitative zero bound below makes that obstruction precise for the actual knot state. It does not identify a classical A-polynomial factor. The canonical regular remainder, defined by subtracting the ordinary-color polar data, remains a separate candidate for such a comparison. ## 1. The actual state and its two nearby values Fix a zero-framed knot $K$ for which the actual all-level volume limit is known. Write $K_N(K)$ for its reduced Kashaev invariant, with the unknot normalized to $1$, and assume \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|K_N(K)| =v= rac{V}{2\pi}>0. 	ag{1} \] For example, this applies to the fixed long-twist knots covered by the [strict Conway-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and the [ordered net-twist theorem](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md). In either application, the knot and its integer twist weights are fixed before $N$ tends to infinity. The argument below otherwise uses no restriction on the knot presentation. Let $F_N(M)$ be its reduced ADO state. It is the zero-framed cut-tangle scalar, equivalently the full modified-trace invariant divided by the modified dimension. The relation between the unrolled color parameter $\alpha$, its exponential $x$, and the marked meridian eigenvalue $M$ is \[ x=q_N^\alpha,\qquad M=-q_Nx. 	ag{2} \] Thus $\alpha=N-1$ gives $M=1$. The exact [ADO normalization](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) and [integer-color specialization](root_orbit_pointing.md) give \[ F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)\quad(1\le j\le N),\qquad F_N(1)=K_N(K),\qquad C_1(q)=1. 	ag{3} \] Here $C_j$ denotes the reduced $j$-dimensional ordinary quantum-group invariant of the same knot. In particular, its one-dimensional value is $1$. The [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) proves the exact identity \[ F_N(-M)=F_N(M) \qquad(N\ge2). 	ag{4} \] There is no even-level exception in (4). To recall why the normalization introduces no sign, choose a $b$-strand braid of writhe $w$ closing to $K$. Its closure has one component, so the braid permutation is a $b$-cycle and $w\equiv b-1\pmod2$. The integer $\kappa_D=w-b+1$ is therefore even. In the exact meridian-shift insertion, all crossing factors depend on $Y=M^2$. Their product over the $N$ shifts $Y\mapsto q_N^2Y$ is $1$: the numerator and denominator products cancel by $\prod_{r=0}^{N-1}(1-q_N^{2r}z)=1-z^N$. The remaining framing factor has cyclic product $q_N^{-N\kappa_D}=1$. After $N$ shifts, $M$ has become $-M$, proving (4). At a vanishing numerator or denominator this is the cancelled rational identity, not a quotient of separately evaluated zeros. Equations (3) and (4) now imply, exactly at every level, \[ F_N(q_N)=F_N(-q_N)=1. 	ag{5} \] For sufficiently large $N$, (1) also gives $K_N(K)
e0$. Consequently \[  rac{F_N(q_N)}{F_N(1)}= rac1{K_N(K)},\qquad \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N \log\left| rac{F_N(q_N)}{F_N(1)}ight|=-v. 	ag{6} \] The shift in (6) is the actual meridian shift $M\mapsto q_NM$. Writing $F_N(M)=f_N(Y)$ and $Q_N=q_N^2$, its squared-coordinate form is $Y\mapsto Q_NY$, with $f_N(Q_N)=1$. ## 2. A two-value estimate for Laurent polynomials The following elementary estimate explains why a degree bound matters. For a nonzero Laurent polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=m}^{n}a_jz^j$ with $a_ma_n
e0$, call $D=n-m$ its exponent spread. Multiplication by a Laurent monomial changes neither this spread nor the nonzero roots. **Two-value lemma.** Suppose $z_0,z_1
e0$ have equal modulus, $P(z_0)P(z_1)
e0$, and \[ A=\left| rac{P(z_0)}{P(z_1)}ight|>1,\qquad \delta=|z_1-z_0|. 	ag{7} \] Then $D>0$, and some nonzero root of $P$ lies at distance at most \[  rac{\delta}{1-A^{-1/D}} 	ag{8} \] from $z_0$. To prove this, factor the ordinary polynomial obtained by removing the lowest Laurent monomial: \[ z^{-m}P(z)=a_n\prod_{j=1}^{D}(z-\zeta_j). 	ag{9} \] Its constant coefficient is nonzero, so all $\zeta_j$ are nonzero. If $D=0$, the equal moduli of $z_0$ and $z_1$ would give $A=1$. For $D>0$, put $r=\min_j|z_0-\zeta_j|$. If $r\le\delta$, (8) already follows. Otherwise, the Laurent monomial has modulus ratio $1$, and the triangle inequality gives \[  egin{aligned} -\log A &=\sum_{j=1}^{D}\log  rac{|z_1-\zeta_j|}{|z_0-\zeta_j|}\ &\ge D\log\left(1- rac{\delta}{r}ight). \end{aligned} 	ag{10} \] Solving (10) for $r$ proves (8). The proof retains root multiplicities and requires no information about their angles or simplicity. A larger upper bound for $D$ may replace $D$ in (8), giving a weaker valid bound. ## 3. The finite crossing matrices give a linear degree bound Fix any braid presentation of $K$ with $b$ strands and $L$ crossings. Let $L_+$ and $L_-$ count the positive and negative crossings, so $L=L_++L_-$ and $w=L_+-L_-$. Put $d=N-1$. The [finite cut-state construction](finite_sum_annihilator.md) retains all indices in $\{0,\ldots,d\}$. The explicit [positive and negative crossing entries](relative_octahedral_period.md#exact-formulas-for-both-actual-crossings) make their color dependence particularly transparent. After stripping the common Cartan scalar, the positive entry with input indices $(a,b)$ and shift $k$ is an $x$-independent coefficient times \[ x^{-a-b-k}(Qx^2/Q^a;Q)_k, \qquad 0\le k\le\min(a,d-b),\qquad Q=q_N^2. 	ag{11} \] Here $(u;Q)_k=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-uQ^r)$. The negative entry is an $x$-independent coefficient times \[ x^{a+b-k}(Qx^2/Q^b;Q)_k, \qquad 0\le k\le\min(b,d-a). 	ag{12} \] These are the actual checked crossings; the two shift cutoffs are different and have both been retained. Expanding the finite products in (11) and (12) gives the respective exponent intervals \[  egin{aligned} [-a-b-k,-a-b+k]&\subset[-2d,0],\ [a+b-k,a+b+k]&\subset[0,2d]. \end{aligned} 	ag{13} \] For example, in the positive case $k\le d-b$ bounds $a+b+k$ by $2d$, while $k\le a$ bounds $-a-b+k$ by $0$. The negative case uses $k\le d-a$ and $k\le b$. The factorial denominators depend only on $q_N$, are nonzero for their actual indices below $N$, and introduce no color denominator. The common Cartan scalars cancel against the zero-framing twist correction. What remains of that correction is $x^{wd}$. Each of the $b-1$ pivotal traces contributes $x^{-d}$ times an $x$-independent factor. Thus the common remaining monomial is $x^{d(w-b+1)}$. Products and finite sums cannot enlarge the exponent interval. After including this monomial, the support of the actual reduced state lies in \[ [-d(L+b-1),\ d(L-b+1)]. 	ag{14} \] The substitution $x=-q_N^{-1}M$ only multiplies coefficients by nonzero constants. It leaves (14) unchanged. In particular the actual Laurent spread, after any cancellations, satisfies \[ D_N\le2L(N-1),\qquad D_N^Y\le L(N-1). 	ag{15} \] The second bound is for $f_N(Y)$: exact evenness (4) divides every actual exponent and its spread by two. These estimates hold at both parities and do not require a bound on the number of summands. For the knots in (1), $L>0$ and both spreads are positive for sufficiently large $N$, because a Laurent monomial cannot satisfy (6). ## 4. A quantitative zero bound at the complete point Let \[ r_N=\min\{|z-1|:z
e0,\ F_N(z)=0\},\qquad \delta_N=|q_N-1|=2\sin rac{\pi}{2N}. 	ag{16} \] For all sufficiently large $N$, the two-value lemma applied at $1$ and $q_N$ gives \[ r_N\le  rac{\delta_N}{1-|K_N(K)|^{-1/D_N}} \le rac{\delta_N} {1-|K_N(K)|^{-1/[2L(N-1)]}}. 	ag{17} \] In particular, \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty}Nr_N \le rac{\pi}{1-\exp(-V/(4\pi L))}. 	ag{18} \] The squared-meridian coordinate improves the constant. Apply the same lemma to $f_N$ at $1$ and $Q_N$. Its spread is at most $L(N-1)$, and $|Q_N-1|\sim2\pi/N$. Hence it has a zero $\zeta_N$ with \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty}N|\zeta_N-1| \le rac{2\pi}{1-\exp(-V/(2\pi L))}. 	ag{19} \] Choose the square root $z_N$ of $\zeta_N$ that tends to $1$. It is a zero of $F_N$, and $|z_N-1|=|\zeta_N-1|/|z_N+1|$, where $|z_N+1|	o2$. We obtain the stronger estimate \[  oxed{\displaystyle \limsup_{N	o\infty}Nr_N \le rac{\pi}{1-\exp(-V/(2\pi L))}.} 	ag{20} \] Every fixed braid presentation supplies a valid $L$. This is a bound on zeros of the actual reduced knot state, not an auxiliary polynomial chosen to have the same complete value. It does not give their number in the shrinking disk, their limiting directions, or a classical geometric interpretation of their factors. ## 5. Consequences for shift ratios and the full normalization There is no fixed complex neighborhood of $M=1$ on which all sufficiently large $F_N$ are nonvanishing. Moreover, (6) directly rules out a finite nonzero limit of $F_N(q_NM)/F_N(M)$ at $M=1$. These are distinct assertions: a zero of $F_N$ need not be a pole of that quotient, because a shifted numerator zero may cancel it. For example, a scalar WKB expression on a fixed neighborhood of $1$ would require a holomorphic action $S$ and nonvanishing amplitudes $a_N$ converging locally uniformly to a nonzero holomorphic function, with \[ F_N(M)=c_N e^{NS(M)}a_N(M),\qquad c_N
e0. 	ag{21} \] Such an expression would imply $F_N(q_N)/F_N(1)	o\exp(\pi iS'(1))
e0$, contradicting (6). It is also incompatible with (20). This does not exclude expressions on domains omitting the complete point, or with level-dependent divisors explicitly retained. A scalar normalization independent of $M$ changes neither the roots nor the ratio in (6). A fixed rational or algebraic gauge, on a branch that is holomorphic and nonzero near $(q,M)=(1,1)$, also cannot remove the roots and has ratio tending to $1$ between the two points. Gauges with moving poles or zeros require separate analysis. The actual full modified-trace state is an important example of the latter case. Its exact factor is \[ \mathcal N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M),\qquad d_N(M)=\eta_N rac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}},\qquad \eta_N=i^{N+3},\qquad d_N(1)=\eta_N/N. 	ag{22} \] At $M=q_N$ the denominator in (22) has derivative $-2Nq_N^{-1}$. Since $F_N(q_N)=1$, the full state has the uncancelled simple pole \[ \operatorname{Res}_{M=q_N}\mathcal N_N(M) = rac{\eta_N(1-q_N^2)}{2N}
e0 \qquad(N\ge2). 	ag{23} \] Its value at $M=1$ is nevertheless the regular whole-germ value $\eta_NK_N(K)/N$. Thus the full normalization does not supply a holomorphic nonzero scalar packet across these points either. For sufficiently large $N$, its shift quotient has a pole at $M=1$, consistent with the exact normalization gauge \[  rac{d_N(q_NM)}{d_N(M)} =-q_N^{-1} rac{q_N^2M^2-1}{M^2-1}. 	ag{24} \] ## 6. The canonical regular remainder is a different object The [regular-period construction](regularized_kashaev_period.md) subtracts prescribed polar data, rather than applying a nonzero scalar normalization. Let $P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}$ be the unique polynomial of degree at most $N-2$ taking the values $C_j(q_N)$ at $Q_N^j$ for $1\le j<N$. Define \[ S_N(Y)= rac{Y^N-1}{Y-1},\qquad R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}(Y) = rac{f_N(Y)-P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(Y)}{S_N(Y)}. 	ag{25} \] All roots of $S_N$ are simple ordinary-color points. The numerator vanishes there, so $R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is Laurent polynomial. In the full state this gives the exact separation \[ \mathcal N_N(M) =\eta_NM^{N-1}R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}(M^2) +\eta_NM^{N-1} rac{P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(M^2)}{S_N(M^2)}. 	ag{26} \] The second term contains all finite nonzero polar principal parts. The ordinary-color bound in the same construction gives $|P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(1)/N|=O_K(N^{b-1})$. Therefore \[ R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}(1) = rac{K_N(K)-P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(1)}{N},\qquad \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}(1)|=v. 	ag{27} \] Its first shifted value is not the ordinary anchor $1$. It is instead \[ R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}(Q_N) = rac{f_N'(Q_N)-(P_N^{\mathrm{ord}})'(Q_N)}{S_N'(Q_N)}. 	ag{28} \] Thus the two-value obstruction proved for $F_N$ does not automatically apply to $R_N^{\mathrm{reg}}$. Nor does (27) prove a neighborhood asymptotic or a shift-ratio limit for this remainder. A specified actual all-level annihilator gives the existing affine equation for the regular remainder, after its fixed rational gauge and denominator clearing. Its inhomogeneous term has fixed Laurent support and polynomially bounded coefficients. One possible next theorem would provide a locally uniform, nonzero shift-ratio limit for this actual regular state together with a locally uniform exponential lower bound. On a domain avoiding the fixed coefficient poles, such bounds would make the inhomogeneous term negligible after division by the state. The limiting ratio would then satisfy the homogeneous classical symbol. Its identification with the preferred geometric longitude would still require the marked geometric comparison. The complete scalar volume theorem and the [pointed quantum A-period and Gram formulas](actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) remain valid. What changes is the proposed neighborhood statement: the reduced state has the exponential one-step drop and nearby zeros proved above, and the full state has a nearby pole. The canonical regular remainder must be studied with its own affine equation and its ordinary-color subtraction intact. ## 7. The boundary factor of every polynomial annihilator The same ordinary-color bounds give an exact algebraic restriction on the recurrence. The squared-meridian version is the necessity theorem in [the peripheral normal-period note](peripheral_normal_period.md#2-a-nonzero-complete-column-forces-polynomial-growth). For the positive-volume knots in (1), its hypothesis is now established. Here is the corresponding statement without requiring an even operator. Let \[ P=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_i(q,M)T^i,\qquad TM=qMT,\qquad a_i\in\mathbb C[q^{\pm1},M^{\pm1}] 	ag{29} \] be any fixed genuine all-level annihilator of the reduced state, after clearing its rational denominators. Then \[ (q^{2i}M^2-1)\mid a_i(q,M)\quad(0\le i\le d),\qquad P=B(M^2-1) 	ag{30} \] for a polynomial quantum-torus operator $B$. This conclusion concerns all annihilators in the specified integral ring, not just a chosen minimal generator. Fix $i$ and evaluate the exact annihilation equation at $M=\pm q_N^{-i}$, with $N>d$. The $i$th term contains $F_N(\pm1)=K_N(K)$. Every other term is an ordinary-color value. If $k=j-i>0$, evenness and (3) give $F_N(\pm q_N^k)=C_k(q_N)$. If $k<0$, use $q_N^N=-1$ to obtain $F_N(\pm q_N^k)=C_{N+k}(q_N)$. All these indices lie between $1$ and $N-1$. The fixed-braid bound is uniform over that entire range: $|C_r(q_N)|\le(N/2)^{b-1}$. The fixed Laurent coefficients in (29) are bounded on these unit-circle trajectories. Hence the annihilation equation gives \[ |a_i(q_N,\pm q_N^{-i})|\,|K_N(K)|\le C_PN^{b-1}. 	ag{31} \] If the Laurent polynomial $a_i(q,\pm q^{-i})$ were nonzero, its finite vanishing order $
u$ at $q=1$ would give a lower bound $cN^{-
u}$ at $q_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$. Equation (31) would then bound $|K_N(K)|$ by a polynomial, contradicting (1). Thus both trajectory polynomials vanish identically. Their kernels are the relatively prime ideals generated by $M-q^{-i}$ and $M+q^{-i}$, proving the divisibility in (30). Finally, $T^i(M^2-1)=(q^{2i}M^2-1)T^i$, which proves the displayed order of multiplication. The finite exceptional levels of the annihilator do not affect this argument. For a polynomial annihilator in the squared-coordinate ring $Y=M^2$, with shift $\mathsf S Y=q^2Y\mathsf S$, the statement is $P_Y=B_Y(Y-1)$. An arbitrary unsquared operator need not itself have even coefficients. It splits as $P_0(q,Y,\mathsf S)+M P_1(q,Y,\mathsf S)$; evenness of the state makes the two parts separate annihilators, and the argument applies to each. Thus the squared polynomial annihilator ideal is contained in the left ideal generated by $Y-1$. Its cyclic module has the boundary quotient \[ \Delta=\mathcal R/\mathcal R(Y-1),\qquad \mathcal R=\mathbb C(q)[Y^{\pm1},\mathsf S^{\pm1}]. 	ag{32} \] The commutation rule above is understood in this ring. Localizing to $\mathbb C(q,Y)$ makes $Y-1$ invertible and kills this quotient. The boundary information must therefore be retained in a meridian lattice alongside the localized recurrence. This is a normalization factor of shift order zero; it is not the sought geometric factor involving the longitude variable. One must also keep the change of state when removing the factor: $B$ annihilates $(M^2-1)F_N(M)$, whose value at completeness is zero. The knot invariant is its normal derivative, \[ K_N(K)=\left. rac12 rac{d}{d\log M}  igl[(M^2-1)F_N(M) igr]ight|_{M=1}. 	ag{33} \] The peripheral normal-period note develops the corresponding affine lifting equation and states the additional rank condition under which its first normal derivative determines the period. Neither (30) nor the nearby-zero bound proves that rank condition or identifies the remaining classical characteristic factor with the geometric longitude. They specify boundary data that such a comparison must retain.

title: Positive angular coordinates for the octahedral edge blocks
status: Positive octahedral chart and full face maps
text: # Positive angular coordinates for the octahedral edge blocks 1 November 2026. Each edge in an ordered tree of crossing circles contributes two octahedra to the cut link exterior, one in each projection copy. This note gives their vertices and tetrahedron shapes as explicit functions of the two endpoint longitude parameters. The shapes remain positive on a fixed complex disk, independently of the size of the tree. The two-triangle disk boundaries depend only on their own circle parameter, which is what allows incident blocks with different other endpoints to be joined. The [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) identifies these cells and all their labels with the original link exterior. The [completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) then follows their actual logarithmic periods to the smooth filling. These are the geometric inputs to the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md), whose angular path is supplied by the [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md). ## 1. The actual two-leaf model Start with the literal two-leaf closure \(C(h_0T(h_1))\). At a pure leaf use the original coordinates below. Here \(T\) is the quarter-turn, \(C\) is the cylindrical closure, and \(h_j\) is the turned two-strand piece with its original crossing circle. \[ Q=(0,\infty,1,R),\qquad Z=\frac{1+E}{1+H},\qquad E=e^{2\pi ix},\quad H=e^{2\pi it}, \quad R=\frac{H(1+E)^2}{E(1+H)^2}. \tag{1} \] The parameter \(R\) in this display is the fourth normalized ideal vertex of the quadrilateral. The second projection copy has apex \(Z/E\), not a conjugation of the free parameters. The original turn and root closing maps are \[ T(z)=\frac{R_1-1}{z-1},\qquad C(z)=\frac{z-R}{z-1},\qquad R_1=1-R. \tag{2} \] These are the actual maps of [the original marked face maps](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), equations (11), (14), and the original closed projection cut. In particular both maps must be used when placing the second leaf. Applying only the turn would put the two complete apices at the same point. The complete two-leaf wire is \(x=1/4\). In each projection ball, the two ideal pyramids are joined along their ordered quadrilateral bases. Their six outer vertices form an octahedron. This is a literal local cut statement, not a deduction from its volume. ## 2. Solving in the two angular longitude variables Write \(\tau_0=\tau\), \(\tau_1=\upsilon\), and prescribe the actual disk longitude logarithms \[ V_j=2i\tau_j. \tag{3} \] The pure leaf relation gives \(v_j=-i\tau_j\), where \(v_j=\log[\sin\pi(x-t_j)/\sin\pi(x+t_j)]\). On the branch through completeness, put \[ y=\tan(\tau/2),\qquad z=\tan(\upsilon/2),\qquad k=(1+y^2+z^2)^{-1/2},\qquad k(0,0)=1. \tag{4} \] Then the exact solution of the two-leaf stationarity equations is \[ \begin{aligned} \tan(\pi x)&=k,\\ \tan(\pi t_0)&=iky,& \tan(\pi t_1)&=ikz,\\ E&=\frac{1+ik}{1-ik},& H_0&=\frac{1-ky}{1+ky},& H_1&=\frac{1-kz}{1+kz},\\ R&=\frac{1+z^2}{2+y^2+z^2},& R_1&=1-R,\\ Z_j&=\frac{1+E}{1+H_j}. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] Indeed the logarithmic ratio equation first gives \(\tan\pi t_j=ik\tan(\tau_j/2)\). Its ordered metric is \[ \kappa_j=\frac{k^2(1+\tan^2(\tau_j/2))} {1-k^2\tan^2(\tau_j/2)}. \tag{6} \] The wire equation is \(\kappa_0\kappa_1=1\). With \(a=y^2+z^2\), it factors as \((k^2+1)((1+a)k^2-1)=0\); the complete branch is (4). Thus \(\kappa_0=(1+y^2)/(1+z^2)\), which yields (5). No meridian-color approximation was used. The two octahedra have the same equator \(q=(0,\infty,1,R)\), and apices \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} & A & B\\ \hline +&Z_0&\displaystyle\frac{RZ_1}{Z_1-R_1}\\[2mm] -&Z_0/E&\displaystyle\frac{RZ_1}{Z_1-ER_1}. \end{array} \tag{7} \] For example, composing (2) gives \(C(T(Z_1))=RZ_1/(Z_1-R_1)\). Replacing the second-copy apex by \(Z_1/E\) gives the last entry. At zero the two rows are \[ (A_+,B_+)=((1+i)/2,(1-i)/2),\qquad (A_-,B_-)=((1-i)/2,(1+i)/2). \tag{8} \] The corresponding complete cells are the regular octahedra in their opposite labeled orientations. ## 3. Uniform positive tetrahedra on an explicit complex bidisk Subdivide the plus octahedron into the four tetrahedra with ordered vertices \((A_+,B_+,q_j,q_{j+1})\), \(j\bmod4\). Reverse the last two vertices in the minus copy. Use the cross ratio \[ [a,b,c,d]=\frac{(a-c)(b-d)}{(a-d)(b-c)}. \tag{9} \] All eight complete shapes are \(i\). This triangulates the actual two-pyramid union, with the internal diagonal joining its two apices. There is a uniform positive chart on \[ |\tau|,|\upsilon|\le 10^{-2}. \tag{10} \] Here are deliberately loose explicit bounds. The elementary sine and cosine series give \(|y|,|z|<0.005001\). Hence \(|y^2+z^2|<0.000051\), \(|k-1|<0.000026\), \(|E-i|<0.00006\), \(|H_j-1|<0.0102\), and \(|R-1/2|<0.000026\). Substitution in (5) gives \(|Z_j-(1+i)/2|<0.004\). In each denominator in the B column of (7), the complete modulus is \(1/2\), and its perturbation is less than \(0.0041\). The quotient estimate therefore bounds the motion of each finite vertex in (7) by \(0.02\); the remaining finite equatorial vertices are fixed or move by less than \(0.000026\). Every finite pair of distinct complete vertices occurring in (9) has separation at least \(1/2\). Each difference factor therefore changes by relative size less than \(0.08\). Comparing both the numerator and denominator products with one bounds the cross-ratio quotient change by \[ \frac{4(0.08)+2(0.08)^2}{(1-0.08)^2}<0.4. \tag{11} \] For a factor involving infinity there are fewer factors and the same bound suffices. Thus every ordered shape lies in \(|w-i|<0.4\), and in particular has positive imaginary part. All denominators and ideal vertices remain distinct. The internal diagonal has total angle \(2\pi\): its product relation telescopes exactly, and its integer angle branch is fixed by (8). This is positivity of the actual local geometric tetrahedra, not positivity of the original real \((x,t_j)\) angle chamber. For complex angular parameters the equatorial quadrilateral need not be planar. The triangular octahedral boundary and the positive tetrahedral subdivision are the retained geometric objects. ## 4. The two disk-side pants depend only on their longitude The local white matrices in a leaf frame are \[ \begin{aligned} W_0&=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&E\end{pmatrix},& W_1&=\begin{pmatrix}1&E-1\\0&E\end{pmatrix},\\ W_2&=\begin{pmatrix}E-R&R(1-E)\\E-1&1-ER\end{pmatrix},& W_3&=\begin{pmatrix}R&0\\1-E&ER\end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned} \tag{12} \] The relation \(Z^2-(1+E)Z+ER=0\) is retained. Put \[ Q=\frac{E-Z}{Z-1}=e^{-v}=e^{i\tau}. \tag{13} \] The incoming shaded triangle has cyclic vertices \((Z,\infty,1)\), and the outgoing one has \((Z,R,0)\). A disk cut doubles each of them across its adjacent white faces, producing the actual two-triangle pants boundary. In the plus chart, transport the opposite triangle through the appropriate \(W_j^{-1}\). If an oriented edge has endpoints \((a,b)\) and the third vertices on its two sides are \(c,d\), measure its complex ratio by (9). Direct substitution gives the following cyclic tables: \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{incoming edge}&(Z,\infty)&(\infty,1)&(1,Z)\\ \hline \text{ratio}&-Q^{-1}&-Q&-Q^{-1}\\[1mm] \text{outgoing edge}&(Z,R)&(R,0)&(0,Z)\\ \hline \text{ratio}&-Q&-Q^{-1}&-Q. \end{array} \tag{14} \] For example the first incoming ratio is \((1-Z)/(E-Z)=-Q^{-1}\). Across its base edge, the opposite apex is \(W_1^{-1}(Z/E)=Z-E+1\), giving \(-Q\). For the outgoing base, its opposite apex is \(W_3^{-1}(Z/E)=ER/(2E-Z)\), giving \(-Q^{-1}\). The remaining entries follow in the same way from (12). This table removes the other endpoint's angular parameter completely. It also retains the shear, not just the plane angle. The two main puncture products are one; the third puncture product is \(Q^{\pm2}\), with the actual disk longitude having multiplier \(Q^2=e^{2i\tau}\). The sign of the oriented pants boundary is the inverse convention already recorded by the original marked disk word. Consequently an outgoing disk-side boundary of one local block and an incoming boundary of another with the same \(\tau\) have inverse edge ratios under the original puncture matching. Normalize one triangle by its three ordered vertices. The other triangle's position is then fixed by (14), so the whole two-triangle transition matches. Their edge shears cancel and their interior-angle branches, continued from \(\pi\), sum to \(2\pi\). This is the local geometric seam calculation required for joining edge blocks. It does not assert an arbitrary reordering of the three punctures. ## 5. Local logarithmic increments and the edge action Let \(\psi(\tau,\upsilon)\) be the pure two-leaf action in the angular variables, retaining its complete constant. Its actual Legendre relation gives \[ \partial_\tau\psi=it_0 =-\frac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh} (\tan(\tau/2)\cos(\upsilon/2)), \tag{15} \] with the branch through zero; interchange the endpoints for the other derivative. To verify the last equality, use \(\operatorname{artanh}(ky)= \operatorname{arsinh}(y/\sqrt{1+z^2})\). The local pure meridional increment is therefore \[ -2\pi it_0=-2\pi\partial_\tau\psi. \tag{16} \] It is a small actual log-link increment in this fixed local chart. The [ordered disk-page proof](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md), Section 6, concatenates these local paths in their original order. The total pure meridian period is therefore the sum of (16). A single retained half twist of sign \(\epsilon_v\) adds \(-\epsilon_vV_v/2\), in the original primitive basis. Consequently \[ U_v=-2\pi\sum_{e\sim v}\partial_{\tau_v}\psi_e -i\epsilon_v\tau_v, \qquad V_v=2i\tau_v. \tag{17} \] The direct first-charge saddle with \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\) makes (17) exactly \(U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i\). The integer is fixed by concatenating the actual local increments and continuing the periods from the complete cusp, even when the total is no longer a small logarithm. Section 4 of the [completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) establishes that period statement without resetting a principal log. ## 6. Assembly in the original ordered exterior The [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) constructs the following finite assembly. Associate the two octahedra above to each physical edge of the circle tree. At a circle vertex, list its incident edges in the actual cyclic order and join the corresponding outgoing and incoming disk-side pants cyclically. Insert the prescribed retained half twist at its specified disk page. Table (14) supplies geometric seam matching for a common angular variable at that circle. The complete model has two octahedra per edge and \(D\) meridional sectors at a degree-\(D\) circle.
