The topological proof cuts each original circle neighborhood into ordered disk pages and uses terminal-vertex insertion to identify the two-leaf block at each physical quarter-turn, including its four marked main segments. The two-circle endpoint pairs are interlaced by the actual quarter-turn. The proof retains that matching and every left or right insertion in the original product order. It also proves that the primitive meridian crosses the pages once in their cyclic order, with only the single recorded half-twist shear. These facts justify the actual paths used in (17). At a distinguished odd seam one uses the original puncture-and-copy exchange, rather than an arbitrary permutation of the three pants punctures. The original matrices and their three full projective edge-return words are given in Section 3 of the [completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md). Table (14) transports that specified map between incident blocks with a common longitude parameter. Together, (10), (14), and the actual period equations provide the positive cells and link data used by that completion. The [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) keeps every angular parameter below \(0.00111\), within the radius \(0.01\) proved here. The complete conclusion and its precise class of diagrams are stated in the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md).

title: A quantitative quantum limit allowing short twists at large junctions
status: Quantitative finite-sum proof; geometric companions supplied
text: # A quantitative quantum limit allowing short twists at large junctions The number of branches incident to a crossing circle can supply part of the estimate previously obtained by taking its twist number large. This note proves the finite-sum limit under an explicit inequality in those two integers. The [volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) combines it with the ordered octahedral decomposition and positive filling path. The limiting action is therefore the volume of the original knot complement throughout the stated class, including the short coefficients permitted by the inequality. ## 1. Assertion and scope Consider an actual reduced Conway operation tree in which every product junction carries an original crossing-circle operator. Include ordinary terminal crossing circles as degree-one vertices. The resulting circle graph \(\mathcal T\) is a finite tree, with physical quarter-turn edges and no bare junctions. Keep the ordered branches, orientations, knot pattern, primitive cut and zero framing. For the literal construction defined in the [volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md), the strict angle condition follows inductively from the product intervals; it is not a further restriction on these trees. Let \(d_v\ge1\) be the graph degree of circle \(v\), and let \(n_v\in \mathbb Z\) be its actual fixed crossing power. The graph degree \(d_v\) is unrelated to the quantum degree \(N-1\). Put \[ \mathfrak S(\mathcal T,\mathbf n) =\sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}. \tag{1} \] The following conservative sufficient condition will be proved: \[ \mathfrak S\le2^{-25}. \tag{2} \] It implies a nonzero first joint Fourier charge and the actual reduced microscopic profile through both level parities, on every \(|s|\le R<1\). The exponential rate is the real part of the explicitly continued first-charge action. Conditions (1)–(2) are quantitative finite-action conditions, not an assumption that this saddle dominates. Short, even zero, crossing powers are permitted by this certificate. Section 11 explains how the companion geometric proofs identify the action with the actual knot volume under the same bound. The graph and all powers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The invariant in the conclusion is the reduced, zero-framed ADO polynomial \(F_N(M)\), normalized to one on the unknot. Its complete value is \(F_N(1)=K_N(K)\). Set \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\) and \(M=q_N^s\). The explicit elementary factors are \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin(\pi s)}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v. \] Here \(w(D)\) is the writhe of the fixed original diagram. The [scalar calculation](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) specifies the same framing convention, including all orientation types. The critical action in the limit is defined in Sections 4 and 7. ## 2. Dependencies and where the old proof used longness The dependencies are the current authoritative notes: * [the exact crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md), Sections 2–4 and 7: exact translated-grid trace, full crossing scalar, Fourier coefficients, normal limits and fixed-power polynomial bounds; * [the finite sum over internal edge indices](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md), Sections 2 and 4–8: primitive lattice, canonical \(G_N\), finite cotangent currents and the saddle insertion rule; * [the joint Fourier calculation](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md), Sections 3–5: real-spectator telescoping and the exact coefficient of charge one; * [bounds for the full polynomial traces](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Sections 1–4, with its cited full spectral-jet and Chebyshev folding bounds; * [the crossing and framing scalar](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md): the unchanged exact scalar identity for fixed integer powers. These are mathematical inputs, not numerical diagnostics. The [earlier source transfer theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) and [the pretzel filling calculation](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md) use reciprocal-slope implicit functions; the geometric source-regulator theorem uses a neighborhood of the complete framed representation. Longness enters the present published joint proof in four analytic places: existence and charge ordering of a nearby critical branch; a nonempty finite charge cutoff with a fixed tail loss; the angular connectors; and comparison of the total critical drop with fixed discarded-source losses. The geometric completion is a separate fifth use. This proof replaces the four analytic uses in the all-circle class. ## 3. A graph-independent discarded-source gap Use the fixed complete Newton basis \(e_k\), \(0\le k<N\), and write \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\quad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\quad G_0=g(1/4). \tag{3} \] The physical turn on a covariant edge retains equal indices and the actual factor \(\gamma_e(s)H_N(s)/W_k(s)\). This factor and its inverse are bounded on any fixed \(|s|\le R<1\), including all indices. Reference, pivot, framing and the single reduced-cut scalar are kept. At a circle vertex the actual typed tensor is the prescribed version of \[ \phi_\sigma\!\left(R_\sigma^{n_v} \prod_{e\sim v}e_{k_e}\right), \qquad \sigma=0,s,-s. \tag{4} \] The canonical polynomial of a fixed \(R_\sigma^{n_v}\) has polynomial complete spectral-jet norm. Low \(e_k\) have norm rate \(g(k/N)\); high \(e_k\) have polynomial norm, including their first normals. Finite-degree Chebyshev folding and exact top-coefficient extraction therefore give rate at most the sum of \(g\) over low incidences in (4). The polynomial exponent can depend on the fixed valence and power. This is the full carrier-normalized tensor, not a distinct-node trace. Opposite-color types retain their explicit outside scalar. Each physical edge has two incidences. The whole absolute rate is at most \(2\sum_{\text{low }e}g(k_e/N)\), and the positive complete action is \[ F_0=2|E(\mathcal T)|G_0. \tag{5} \] Retain the box \(k_e/N\in I=[1/5,3/10]\). Since \[ g'(1/4)=0,\qquad g''(x)=-4\pi/\sin2\pi x\le-4\pi,\qquad 2[G_0-g(x)]\ge4\pi(x-1/4)^2, \tag{6} \] one low edge outside \(I\) loses at least \(\pi/100\). A high edge loses \(2G_0\ge\pi/4\). Closed factorial bounds and polynomial state counting consequently give a grouped scalar error \[ N^{A_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}} e^{N(F_0-\eta_0)},\qquad \eta_0=\pi/200. \tag{7} \] This loss is independent of the tree size and the fixed powers; prefactors and starting levels are not uniform in those data. There are no bare-tensor replacement errors. No generic conversion from a small spectral norm to a low/high coefficient cone is used: the physical vertex trace (4) is bounded directly. ## 4. Exact edge action The retained packet factorizes over physical edges. Apart from its edge scalar, each factor is \[ K_N(t,u;s)=\sum_{k/N\in I}e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u) \frac{H_N(s)}{W_k(s)}. \tag{8} \] The canonical interpolation has phase \[ b(x,t)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi v+2\cos t)\,dv-2J(x),\qquad \psi(t,u)=\operatorname{stat}_x[b(x,t)+b(x,u)]. \tag{9} \] All branches are continued from \(x=1/4,t=u=0\). Writing \(c=\cos2\pi x\), the stationary equation gives exactly \[ c=\frac{1-\cos t\cos u}{2+\cos t+\cos u},\qquad \tan^2\pi x=\frac1{1+\tan^2(t/2)+\tan^2(u/2)}. \tag{10} \] Substitution \(z=\tan\pi v\) in \(b_t\) yields \[ \psi_t=-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{arsinh}(\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)). \tag{11} \] For \(Q=\sqrt{1-\sin^2(t/2)\sin^2(u/2)}\), \[ \psi_{tt}=-\frac{\cos(u/2)}{2\pi\cos(t/2)Q},\qquad \psi_{tu}=\frac{\sin(t/2)\sin(u/2)}{2\pi Q}. \tag{12} \] The Hessian determinant is exactly \(1/(4\pi^2)\). Thus \[ \Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)=\sum_{\{v,w\}\in E}\psi(\tau_v,\tau_w) =F_0-\tfrac12\sum_va_v\tau_v^2+\mathcal E(\boldsymbol\tau), \qquad a_v=d_v/(2\pi). \tag{13} \] In particular the diagonal curvature grows with graph degree. ## 5. An available complex packet and nonlinear bounds Take \(r=1/4\). Formula (10) gives \(|x(t,u)-1/4|<0.003\) on \(|t|,|u|\le r\): \(|\tan(t/2)|<0.128\), hence \(|c|\le2(0.128)^2/[2-2(0.128)^2]<0.017\), and \(x=1/4-\arcsin(c)/(2\pi)\). Here the radius is valid for the finite packet, not only its formal action. Put \(A=b(x,t)+b(x,u)\). On \(\Re x\in I\), \(|\Im x|\le1/50\), \(|t|,|u|\le1/4\), \[ A_{xx}=\sum_{\xi=t,u} \left[-\frac{2\pi\sin2\pi x}{\cos2\pi x+\cos\xi} -2\pi\cot\pi x\right], \qquad |A_{xx}|<44,\quad \Re A_{xx}<-12. \tag{14} \] For completeness, \(|\cos2\pi x|<0.338\), \(|\cos\xi-1|<0.032\), \(|\sin2\pi x|<1.009\). Also \(\Re\cot\pi x>0.72\), while the real part of the first fraction without \(2\pi\) exceeds \(0.328\): its conjugated numerator is at least \(0.95(0.655)-0.040(0.159)\) and its squared denominator is at most \(1.37^2\). These bounds imply (14). Use a finite cotangent contour of height \(h=1/500\) for the original integer sum. With \(X=\Re(x-x_*)\), \(Y=\Im(x-x_*)\), Taylor's formula gives \[ \Re[A(x)-A(x_*)]\le-6X^2+44|XY|+22Y^2. \tag{15} \] On a vertical endpoint side, \(|X|\ge0.047\), \(|Y|\le0.005\); the right side is below \(-0.002\). On a horizontal side its maximum in \(X\) is at most \((308/3)Y^2\le77/30000\), below the nonconstant cotangent-mode loss \(2\pi h=\pi/250\). The constant-mode integral translates to \(x_*\) with the same endpoint loss, and (14) gives a nondegenerate Gaussian on its real tangent. All canonical \(G_N\) arguments stay in regular bulk strips; no periodic normalization of the interpolation has been changed. Thus each exact edge sum has a nonzero analytic amplitude and the usual uniform \(O_R(N^{-1})\) relative expansion on this disk, with all midpoint offsets retained. Its leading factors and \(-A_{xx}(x_*)\) never vanish. Multiplication gives the whole packet expansion with phase (13), uniformly for the fixed tree. Useful explicit nonlinear constants follow from (12). Let \(\sigma=\sinh(r/2)\), \(k=\cosh(r/2)-1\), \(C=(1-\sigma^4)^{-1/2}\). The normalized diagonal error is at most \(2kC/(1-k)+C-1<1/50\), and the off-diagonal bound is \(\sigma^2C\); their sum is below \(1/25\). For example \(k<0.008\), \(\sigma<0.126\) prove these estimates. Set \(\delta=1/50\), \(\varepsilon=1/25\). Edgewise summation gives \[ \left|\mathcal E_v/\tau_v\right|\le\delta a_v,\qquad \sum_w|\mathcal E_{vw}|\le\varepsilon a_v,\qquad |\mathcal E(\boldsymbol\tau)| \le\tfrac\varepsilon2\sum_va_v|\tau_v|^2. \tag{16} \] The quotient extends at \(\tau_v=0\). For the first bound integrate the diagonal Hessian error with other coordinates fixed. The last bound uses \(2|zw|\le|z|^2+|w|^2\) on each edge, not a dimension-dependent maximum-norm estimate. ## 6. A uniform raw angular Gaussian For \(k/N\in I\) the exact product is \[ \frac{e_k(-2\cos t)}{e_k(-2)} =\prod_{j<k}\left(1- \frac{\sin^2(t/2)}{\cos^2((j+1/2)\pi/N)}\right). \tag{17} \] Put \(u=\sin^2(t/2)\) for real \(t\). The first \(\lfloor N/5\rfloor\) factors have absolute value at most \(1-\alpha_1u\), \(\alpha_1=2\sqrt5-4\); the remaining at most \(N/10+1\) factors are bounded by \(1+\alpha_2u\), \(\alpha_2=2\sqrt5/5\). These follow by checking the two linear pieces of \(|1-u/c|\) with \(c\ge\cos^2(\pi/5)\) and \(c\ge\cos^2(3\pi/10)\), respectively. Therefore \[ \left|\frac{e_k(-2\cos t)}{e_k(-2)}\right| \le e^2e^{-\alpha N\sin^2(t/2)},\qquad \alpha=\frac{9\sqrt5-20}{25}>\frac1{250}. \tag{18} \] For complex \(t+iy\), \(|y|\le1\), one factor's squared modulus is at most its real squared value plus \(18y^2\). Indeed its denominator \(c>1/3\), its real absolute value is below two, \(\cosh y-1\le y^2\), and \(|\sinh y|\le2|y|\). The real linear majorants above are at least \(1/2\); consequently the additional factor is at most \(e^{36y^2}\). Since \(k\le3N/10\), \[ |e_k(-2\cos(t+iy))| \le e^2e_k(-2) e^{N[-\alpha\sin^2(t/2)+11y^2]}. \tag{19} \] Use \(\sin^2(t/2)\ge t^2/\pi^2\) for \(|t|\le\pi\). Summing the positive edge references and retaining the bounded edge insertions yields \[ |B_N(\mathbf t+i\mathbf y,s)| \le N^A\exp N\left[ F_0-\frac1{400}\sum_va_vt_v^2+70\sum_va_vy_v^2\right]. \tag{20} \] We used \(2\alpha/\pi>1/400\), \(22\pi<70\). Endpoint translations \(O_R(N^{-1})\) affect only prefactors. ## 7. Critical branches without reciprocal-slope smallness Set \[ b_v=n_v/(2\pi),\quad D_v=a_v-ib_v,\quad t_0=1/16,\quad L_v=\lfloor t_0|D_v|\rfloor. \tag{21} \] Condition (2) implies \(|D_v|>32\) for all \(v\), so \(L_v\ge1\). For real continuous \(0\le\ell_v\le L_v\), the critical equation is \[ D_v\tau_v=-i\ell_v+\mathcal E_v(\boldsymbol\tau). \tag{22} \] The right-hand map after division by \(D_v\) is a contraction on the radius-\(1/4\) polydisk, with Lipschitz constant at most \(\varepsilon\). Its image has radius at most \(t_0+\delta/4<1/4\). Thus there is one analytic critical branch, also when some \(n_v=0\). Writing \(Q_v=\mathcal E_v/\tau_v\), the exact identity is \[ \tau_v=-i\ell_v/(D_v-Q_v). \tag{23} \] For positive \(\ell_v\), \(\Im\tau_v<0\). With \[ \gamma_+=\frac{1+\delta}{(1-\delta)^2}=\frac{2550}{2401}, \qquad \gamma_-=\frac{1-\delta}{(1+\delta)^2}=\frac{2450}{2601}, \tag{24} \] one obtains \[ \gamma_-\frac{\ell_va_v}{|D_v|^2} \le-\Im\tau_v\le \gamma_+\frac{\ell_va_v}{|D_v|^2}. \tag{25} \] For \(\Phi_\ell=\Psi+\tfrac i2\sum b_v\tau_v^2-i\sum\ell_v\tau_v\) and its stationary value \(\mathcal C(\ell)\), \(\partial_{\ell_v}\Re\mathcal C=\Im\tau_v\). Integration in the independent charges proves \[ \Re\mathcal C(\ell)\le\Re\mathcal C(\mathbf1) -\frac{\gamma_-}{2}\sum_v \frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2}(\ell_v^2-1),\quad\ell_v\ge1, \tag{26} \] \[ F_0-\beta\le\Re\mathcal C(\mathbf1)\le F_0,\qquad \beta=\frac{\gamma_+}{2}\sum_v\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2} =\pi\gamma_+\mathfrak S. \tag{27} \] Each positive-charge coordinate is nonzero and has modulus below \(t_0/(1-\delta)<\pi/2\), so the actual factor \(\prod\sin\tau_v\) is nonzero. On a real tangent the Hessian has real part at most \(-(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{diag}(a_v)\). The Gaussian determinant is nonzero. ## 8. Infinite tails and connectors Keep the exact full-normal charge coefficients \[ c_{\ell,N}(\sigma)= (-1)^{(N-1)(\ell-1)}U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi\sigma),\qquad c_{1,N}=1. \tag{28} \] Initially use formal parameter circles avoiding their removable sine denominators, as in the current joint-transform proof. Let \(A_0=1/400\) and choose \[ y_v=A_0t_0a_v/|D_v|. \tag{29} \] With spectators real or on physical translated grids, the exponent for this coordinate is bounded by \[ F_0-a_vt^2/400+|b_vty_v|-\ell y_v+70a_vy_v^2. \tag{30} \] After maximizing \(t\), the positive quadratic coefficient is \(70a_v+100b_v^2/a_v\le100|D_v|^2/a_v\). Since \(L_v+1>t_0|D_v|\), every omitted charge loses at least \[ \tfrac12A_0t_0^2a_v \ge1/(409600\pi). \tag{31} \] Further charges carry \(e^{-N(\ell-L_v-1)y_v}\). The coefficient bound \(\ell e^{2\pi R'(\ell-1)}\) is absorbed for large \(N\) at this fixed tree. Original endpoint loss is \(\pi^2a_v/400\). The chirp, finite-charge connector and imaginary Gaussian costs are bounded respectively by \(\pi A_0t_0a_v\), \(A_0t_0^2a_v\), and \(70A_0^2t_0^2a_v\), less than half that loss in total. The zero-mode current obeys the same estimate. Exact telescoping of physical functionals and finite real-integral approximants therefore gives the finite-charge formula with (31). No spectator uses another coordinate's complex filling contour. Next restrict real angles to \([-\rho,\rho]^m\), \(\rho=1/8\). The complement loses \(1/(51200\pi)\) by (20). Translate this box to the imaginary part of its critical point. On any connector write \(\tau_v=t_v-i v_v\), with \(0\le v_v\le-\Im\tau_{\ell,v}\). These points stay in the radius-\(1/4\) polydisk. From (16) and Young's inequality, \[ \Re\Phi_\ell(\mathbf t-i\mathbf v)\le F_0-\tfrac18\sum_va_vt_v^2+ \sum_v\left[\tfrac{1+\varepsilon}{2}a_v+ \frac{2b_v^2}{(3-4\varepsilon)a_v}\right]v_v^2 -\sum_v\ell_vv_v. \tag{32} \] The last two sums are at most \(-\tfrac14\sum_v\ell_vv_v\), because \[ \gamma_+\max\{(1+\varepsilon)/2,\;2/(3-4\varepsilon)\}<3/4. \tag{33} \] A connector face has some \(|t_v|=\rho\), and hence loss at least \(1/(1024\pi)\). This retains the negative Fourier contributions of all spectator coordinates instead of adding their imaginary growth costs independently. The translated real box has uniformly negative Hessian. Its translated horizontal integral has a relative Gaussian expansion at its own critical point. After the connectors are restored, the estimate for a nonminimal charge is its saddle term plus \(O(\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F_0-\eta)})\), with \(\eta\) as chosen below. A connector need not be below that nonminimal charge's much smaller critical action. It is below the first-charge action, which is all that is required: (26) and this additive error give strict first-charge dominance. Only the first charge is asserted to have a relative asymptotic for the original contour. ## 9. The actual analytic conclusion Allowing polynomial prefactors, all source, real-box and charge-tail errors above have loss at least \[ \eta=1/(819200\pi). \tag{34} \] The finite-sum contour errors have larger fixed edge losses from Section 5. Condition (2) gives \[ \beta\le\pi(2550/2401)2^{-25}<\eta/2. \tag{35} \] Thus all discarded errors lie below the same nonzero first-charge action. Only these fixed losses are compared with the total drop. The charge-dependent gaps (26) are compared directly with that filled action, not with the augmented reference. The first coefficient (28) is exactly one for both parities. The entire difference of physical traces and their finite-charge approximation is holomorphic through the collisions. The maximum principle gives the estimates on every \(|s|\le R<1\), including actual constant and moving types, without assuming separate removability of divided endpoint currents. The unchanged primitive count gives final power \(N^{3/2}\). All original crossing, mixed-reference, pivot and zero-framing factors are retained exactly. The resulting reduced invariant has \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)} =A_N(s)H_N(s)(1+O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-1})), \qquad \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|F_N(q_N^s)| \longrightarrow2\pi\Re\mathcal C(\mathbf1), \tag{36} \] uniformly on the disk, and is nonzero there for sufficiently large levels. The edge insertion rule also gives its cotangent correction at this same continued wire saddle. Section 11 supplies its geometric volume and cusp interpretation. ## 10. Explicit analytic nonvacuity For a star with center degree \(B\), arbitrary fixed center power \(n_0\), and leaf powers \(|n_j|\ge B\), \[ \mathfrak S=\frac{B}{B^2+n_0^2} +\sum_{j=1}^B\frac1{1+n_j^2}<2/B. \tag{37} \] Thus \(B\ge2^{26}\) suffices, even for short or zero \(n_0\). For two adjacent centers each of degree \(B+1\), with \(B\) leaves at each and every leaf power of magnitude at least \(B\), both center powers may be arbitrary fixed short integers: \(\mathfrak S<4/B\), so \(B\ge2^{27}\) suffices. The large constants reflect deliberately coarse global estimates. The general quantity (1) allows any number and arrangement of short high-degree circles within the sum budget. There is also an intrinsic interpretation at the original complete auxiliary cusps. The [marked peripheral calculation](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) gives \(U=\epsilon v-2\pi i t\), \(V=-2v\), with \(v=\log[\sin\pi(x-t)/\sin\pi(x+t)]\). At completeness, \(v_t=-2\pi c\), where \(c=\cot(\pi x)\). Consequently the primitive cusp shape is \[ \tau_{\mathrm{aux}}=\frac{dV}{dU} =\frac{2ic}{1-i\epsilon c}. \] The [complete tree geometry](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md), Section 5, gives \(c_v=1/d_v\) for the circle of degree \(d_v\). For the original filling slope \(\mu_v+p_v\lambda_v\), direct substitution now gives \[ \mathcal L_v^2 =\frac{|1+p_v\tau_{\mathrm{aux},v}|^2}{\Im\tau_{\mathrm{aux},v}} =\frac{1+n_v^2c_v^2}{2c_v} =\frac{d_v^2+n_v^2}{2d_v},\qquad \mathfrak S=\frac12\sum_v\mathcal L_v^{-2}. \tag{37a} \] Here \(\mathcal L_v\) is the length of the actual primitive filling slope divided by the square root of cusp area; the retained half-twist is included through \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\). Thus (2) is equivalently \(\sum_v\mathcal L_v^{-2}\le2^{-24}\) for this class. This is a translation of the analytic hypothesis using the proved cusp shape, not an imported geometric filling criterion. These examples retain the original knot/parity qualification. They are not claims of a new topological family or priority. Some star presentations overlap the existing long-pretzel and fixed-outer-power belt-stack results; zero boxes may admit the already known topological reduction. The graph-wide analytic criterion does not use those reductions. ## 11. Identification with the knot volume Small angular variables do not imply that the primitive meridian logarithms are small: a high-degree circle collects contributions from many edges. The geometric proof therefore follows the entire path of filling equations, with its logarithm branches retained. The [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) cuts the original augmented exterior into two octahedra per tree edge. Its literal strand matchings retain every face pairing, half twist and primitive peripheral path. The [angular construction](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) subdivides these octahedra into eight positive tetrahedra per edge on the chart \(|\tau_v|<10^{-2}\). Section 7 places the whole path \[ \Psi_{\tau_v}+\frac{i n_v\tau_v}{2\pi}=ic,\qquad 0\le c\le1, \] inside this chart. The [completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) computes the actual periods \[ U_v=-2\pi\Psi_{\tau_v}-i\epsilon_v\tau_v,\qquad V_v=2i\tau_v,\qquad U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi ic. \] It verifies that the primitive slope bounds a tube of cone angle \(2\pi c\). At \(c=1\) the tube is smooth, the auxiliary fillings are precisely the original surgeries, and the main knot cusp remains complete. The same proof fixes the additive volume constant at the complete augmented link and integrates the boundary-corrected action. It gives \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}\mathcal C(\mathbf1) =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \tag{38} \] Thus the analytic conclusion above is an actual uniform volume theorem under (2). The [preferred-cusp continuation](actual_all_circle_preferred_cusp.md) also identifies the first correction geometrically. This establishes the summed criterion, not arbitrary short fillings or a criterion for graphs with cycles. ## Reproducing the edge calculations The [elementary Newton estimates](all_circle_uniform_newton_bounds.md) give a second direct proof of the uniform discarded-state and complex-strip bounds. The exact edge equations and finite samples of that strip inequality can be checked with: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py curvature-fillings ``` The [script](../experiments/audit_all_circle_curvature_packet.py) verifies four symbolic identities and samples the printed complex inequality at both even and odd levels. Its [recorded output](../experiments/all_circle_curvature_packet_results.json) states that finite scope. The uniform inequalities, contour argument and asymptotic conclusion are proved above; the script does not establish geometric completion.

title: All orders of the meridian profile under the directed criterion
text: # All orders of the meridian profile under the directed criterion The directed degree-and-twist criterion gives more than a leading volume limit. For every fixed knot presentation satisfying that criterion, the actual meridian state has an asymptotic expansion to every finite order on the microscopic scale \(M=q_N^s\). Its coefficients have a precise polynomial degree bound. This bound allows an exact quantum recurrence to select the preferred geometric meridian–longitude curve of the original knot complement. The proof expands the actual normalized subtree integrals, retaining their full normal data and endpoint terms. It also works on the fixed translated parameter regions used by the recurrence. These are separate estimates from the previously established first-order profile. The extension has an operator consequence. For every knot satisfying the directed certificate, the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine fixed all-level reduced ADO annihilator contains the selected complex geometric meridian–longitude factor. The statement is about that factor, not the full A-polynomial, its multiplicity, or the entire operator ideal. ## 1. Fixed data and statement Fix one literal ordered all-circle tree with at least one edge, the original endpoint and orientation types, and its fixed signed powers \(n_v\). Its cylindrical closure is required to be one knot, with no component already closed inside a tangle. Fix a root and numbers \(0<c_v<2^{-16}\) at nonroot vertices satisfying equations (3), (8), and (9) of [the directed theorem](actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md). All this data is independent of the level. There is no new smallness condition on these data in this note. In particular the result covers the sufficient alternative \[ d_v\ge 2^{28}\quad\text{or}\quad |n_v|\ge2^{27} \quad\text{separately at every vertex}, \tag{1} \] and also the certificates allowed by the more general directed inequalities. The original knot and parity qualifications are unchanged. Both level parities are included. Use the actual zero-framed reduced state and its pointing: \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad M=-q_Nx=q_N^s,\qquad K_N=F_N(1),\qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}. \tag{2} \] Here \(x\) is the raw highest-weight parameter; internal wire variables will instead be denoted \(x_e\). Define the normalized full state \[ \mathcal Z_N(s)=\frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{K_NH_N(s)}. \tag{3} \] The directed theorem gives \(K_N\ne0\) for every sufficiently large level. The one factor \(H_N\) is exactly the conversion between the reduced and full trace, not a freely chosen regularization. **All-order statement.** Let \(K\) be any compact subset of the open upper half-plane. It can have any fixed real extent and can be a finite union of compact disks. For every finite \(L\), \[ \log\mathcal Z_N(s) =\sum_{r=1}^{L}N^{-r}p_r(s)+O_{K,L}(N^{-L-1}), \qquad \deg p_r\le r+1, \tag{4} \] uniformly on \(K\), with every prescribed finite number of derivatives on smaller compacts. The same polynomials occur on each original compact \(|s|\le R<1\). If a lower amplitude requires separating the two level parities, (4) is understood on each parity subsequence; its top diagonal is identical for both. The logarithm is the branch tending to zero, which is well defined for all sufficiently large levels on each such compact. The polynomials are selected by the original joint phase, including its first-charge mark. Put \[ \begin{aligned} J'(x)&=\log(2\sin\pi x),\qquad J(0)=0,\\ \mathcal K(x,t)&=2J(x)-J(x+t)-J(x-t),\\ \Phi_t(X)&=\Phi(X)+\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_T}\mathcal K(x_e,t) +\frac{\pi i\,a(D)}2t^2,\\ a(D)&=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v,\qquad S(t)=\Phi_t(X_*(t)). \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] The set \(\mathcal E_T\) is the set of original physical quarter-turn edges, \(X\) comprises their wire variables and the original circle angles, and \(X_*(t)\) is the critical point continued from the selected filled point at \(t=0\). The base phase is \[ \Phi(X)=\sum_{e=vw}\{b(x_e,\tau_v)+b(x_e,\tau_w)\} +\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_v n_v\tau_v^2-i\sum_v\tau_v, \tag{6} \] with the logarithms fixed by the original complete chart and first-charge continuation. The top coefficient of \(p_r\) is precisely the coefficient of \(t^{r+1}\) in \(S(t)-S(0)\). The last term in (6) must not be omitted. All constants and starting levels may depend on the fixed tree, signed powers, certificate, compact, derivative order and expansion order. This dependence does not change the finite directed certificate. No uniformity over an unbounded collection of diagrams is asserted. ## 2. The strict margins that the higher-order proof uses Retain the notation \(a_v,b_v,D_v,A_v,B_v,C_v,y_v,\beta_v,\eta_v\) of directed equations (4)–(7). Its proof supplies the following facts about the actual finite recurrence. The full edge kernel, including high indices, is \[ \mathscr K_N(t,u;s)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_k(s)}. \tag{7} \] It has exact trigonometric degree at most \(N-1\) in either angle. There is no discarded term in this definition. At a nonroot vertex the actual message is the full physical trace of the parent kernel times the child messages, with its original edge scalar. At the root the parent kernel is absent. This is directed (25)–(26), an ordering of a finite contraction, not a new topological rerooting. The conditional first-charge saddle is nondegenerate on the parent rectangle. The local exponent has second derivative with real part at most \(-(19/20)a_v\), and its complex second derivative has modulus at least \((19/20)|D_v|\). Its physical sine amplitude is nonzero. Relative to the conditional first charge, all original tail, endpoint, truncation and connector errors have a positive margin at least \(\eta_v-\beta_v>0\). Every retained charge \(\ell\ge2\) has the additional margin \[ \frac{190}{441}\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2}(\ell^2-1)>0. \tag{8} \] The first Fourier coefficient is exactly one, at both parities. The outgoing real-envelope regeneration has the strictly positive margin \((2^{-16}-c_v)\chi-\beta_v\) whenever an outgoing edge exists. There is no such requirement at the root. Here the complete basis is \(e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{j<k}(c_j-z)\), with \(S_k=\prod_{r=1}^{k}2\sin(\pi r/N)\), \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), and \(0\le k<N\). The paired factor is \(W_k(s)=\prod_{r=1}^{k}[1-\sin^2(\pi s/N)/\sin^2(\pi r/N)]\). These are the [physical fixed-basis coordinates](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md), including their repeated-node data. For the fixed finite tree, the minimum of any finite list of these positive margins and the one-edge wire-contour margins is positive. When necessary it may be reduced by a fixed factor, leaving room for the \(O(N^{-1})\) shifts of endpoints and for slightly nested compact contours. Polynomial factors in \(N\) do not use up that margin. The tail contains infinitely many Fourier charges, but its original estimate is a geometric series with ratio bounded by a constant times \(e^{-Ny_v}\); it does not require taking a minimum over infinitely many unrelated errors. The proof of these facts is in directed §§2–6, from its actual full kernel, its normalized real and strip bounds, and the exact translated-grid trace. In particular it does not assume a relative estimate at a very small nonminimal saddle. Each such charge is its local saddle contribution plus an additive error already below the first charge. That distinction remains in the higher-order argument. ## 3. The same margins on fixed translated charts Fix a compact \(K\subset\{\operatorname{Im}s>0\}\). The actual moving orientation types use \(s\) or \(-s\); the opposite-order constant type uses its original parameter zero and full normal functional. Only bounded prefactors change in passing from the original disk to these compacts. ### 3.1. The paired turn factors Euler's product gives the exact identity \[ W_k(s)=\prod_{\substack{1\le r\le k\\j\in\mathbb Z}} \left(1-\frac{s^2}{(r+jN)^2}\right), \qquad 0\le k<N. \tag{9} \] All integers in this product are distinct and nonzero. For bounded \(s\), the logarithms of the factors with sufficiently large integer modulus are bounded in absolute value by \(C_K/m^2\). The product over the finitely many remaining integers has a positive lower bound on \(K\cup(-K)\), since no integer lies there. Consequently every subset product in (9), and its inverse, is bounded uniformly in \(k,N\). Also \(H_N\) and its inverse are bounded there for all sufficiently large \(N\), since \(H_N\) tends uniformly to the nonzero function \(\sin(\pi s)/(\pi s)\). The proof of the directed rectangle bound uses these factors only through their absolute bounds. Its positivity argument is applied to the complete Newton factors at real angles before this bounded multiplier is inserted. Thus no positivity in \(s\) is required. The conditional constant remains the same \(\operatorname{Re}\psi(0,u)\), and the real/angular losses and the high-index complement loss are unchanged. ### 3.2. The actual fixed-power trace and its normal channels The canonical stripped fixed-power crossing polynomial has the exact interpolation of source-bound (D14): \[ r_{N,\sigma}^{[n]}(z)= -\frac1{N(U-U^{-1})} \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\lambda_j(\sigma)^n(t_j-t_j^{-1}) \frac{P_\sigma(z)}{z-c_j(\sigma)}, \quad U=e^{2\pi i\sigma}. \tag{10} \] Here \(t_j=q_N^{-2j-1+2\sigma}\), \(c_j(\sigma)=t_j+t_j^{-1}\), and \(P_\sigma(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi\sigma)\), where \(\mathcal T_N(t+t^{-1})=t^N+t^{-N}\). The quantity \(\lambda_j(\sigma)=(-1)^j q_N^{j(j+1)}(q_N^2)^{-\sigma j}\) is the stripped spectral value. The full physical representative is \(\kappa_\sigma^n r_{N,\sigma}^{[n]}\), where \(\kappa_\sigma=q_N^{(N-1+\sigma)^2/2}\). This common Cartan scalar is retained in the exact ledger, together with the prescribed mixed references. On \(K\cup(-K)\), \(|U-U^{-1}|\) has a positive lower bound. The nodes lie in an ellipse of height \(O_K(N^{-1})\), and the divided-difference estimates used in the original full-polynomial norm proof are polynomial in \(N\) there. The full eigenvalue and carrier scalars have bounded modulus for each fixed signed power, including negative powers. This proves the same polynomial norm bound used in outgoing-envelope regeneration, with its complete Hermite derivatives retained. For the constant channel \(\sigma=0\), use its original full trace, rather than evaluating an isolated singular summand of (10). Equivalently carry a small independent formal \(\sigma\) around zero, prove the estimate on a fixed parameter circle avoiding collisions, and apply the maximum principle to the **whole finite trace minus its first-charge expression**. All Fourier coefficients are entire in \(\sigma\), and the original physical trace has the proved removable normal value. Cauchy's formula also retains any fixed normal derivative required by the actual channel. The edge parameter \(s\) remains independent of this formal normal parameter during this argument. Nothing identifies a constant opposite-color channel with a moving same-color one. The full complete Hermite norm is the maximum of the values at the distinct complete Casimir nodes and the first derivatives at their double nodes. At odd levels the final node \(-2\) is simple and has no derivative coordinate. This norm, the canonical polynomial sup norm and the Chebyshev coefficient norm differ by polynomial factors in the fixed degree range. Chebyshev folding involves a fixed number of folds at a vertex, and \(\cos(2\pi\sigma)\) is bounded on the chosen parameter compacts. Thus directed (43) and the real-envelope patch remain valid. Their powers of \(N\) and constants can increase, but their exponential terms do not. ### 3.3. Grid translations, endpoint currents and tails Use the exact single-grid contour from the direct-crossing trace, not a periodic version of its chirp. A fixed \(\sigma\) shifts the grid and its endpoint rectangle by \(2\pi\sigma/N\). The latter displacement is \(O_K(N^{-1})\). At a translated vertical side the exact grid kernel is the same elementary expression \[ \frac{iN e^{-Nv}}{1+e^{-Nv}}. \tag{11} \] Thus the existing endpoint estimate applies there with at most a bounded exponential prefactor. The real interval and the retained local contours can be returned to the original ones with their connecting currents kept. Their locations are within \(O_K(N^{-1})\) of the original endpoint or fixed local connector and hence retain a fixed part of the original gap. For \(s\mapsto s+j\), reindex the central entries and explicitly retain the bounded number of wrapped entries near \(\pm\pi\). The chirp is not periodic; its wrapped values cannot be discarded by declaring the grids identical. Their exact factors are bounded on the fixed compact and the original endpoint action loss applies. The paired charges have coefficients \[ c_{\ell,N}(\sigma)=(-1)^{(N-1)(\ell-1)} U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi\sigma),\qquad c_{1,N}=1, \quad |c_{\ell,N}(\sigma)|\le \ell e^{2\pi|\operatorname{Im}\sigma|(\ell-1)}. \tag{12} \] For each vertex, the extra fixed exponential in \(\ell\) is absorbed in \(e^{-N\ell y_v}\) once \(N\) is large. The finite set of retained charges remains subject to (8). The endpoint and zero-mode currents are those of the original finite trace. All the bounds are conditional on the parent angle on its compact rectangle, not only at its eventual saddle. It follows by the exact same normalized subtree induction that the directed first-order theorem, its nonzero conditional first charge, its real/strip envelopes and all the fixed exponential errors hold on \(K\), with unchanged certificate. This statement follows from the finite source on \(K\). It is not analytic continuation of an asymptotic estimate proved elsewhere. ## 4. Arbitrary-order edge and conditional saddle expansions The canonical interpolation is \[ G_N(z)=\left(\frac{2\pi}{N}\right)^z\Gamma(z+1) \prod_{j\ge1} \frac{\Gamma(Nj+z+1)}{\Gamma(Nj-z)(Nj)^{2z+1}}. \tag{13} \] It satisfies, with the fixed normalization, \[ G_N(k)=S_k,\qquad G_N(z)G_N(N-1-z)=N,\qquad G_N(s)G_N(-s)=H_N(s)^{-1}. \tag{14} \] The midpoint \((N-1)/2\), rather than \(N/2\), remains in the exact Newton interpolation. In the bulk, every prescribed finite Stirling expansion gives \[ \log G_N(Nx)=NJ(x)+\tfrac12\log(2N\sin\pi x) +\sum_{j=1}^{L}N^{-j}b_j(x)+O(N^{-L-1}). \tag{15} \] This holds with any fixed number of derivatives on smaller complex bulk compacts. To justify summation in (13), take sufficiently many terms in the finite periodic-Bernoulli remainder for the Gamma factors. On a fixed bulk compact their arguments remain in a common right-half-plane sector. The remainder of the \(j\)-th product factor is bounded by \(C_LN^{-L-1}j^{-L-1}\), taking extra terms first when necessary for summability. The remaining finite number of factors is controlled in the same sector. Cauchy estimates give the derivatives. This proves every requested finite order; it assumes no convergence of the asymptotic series. The exact circle Newton interpolant is \[ \mathcal E_N(x,\tau)= \frac{G_N(d/2+u)G_N(d/2-u)} {G_N(d/2-Nx+u)G_N(d/2-Nx-u)G_N(Nx)^2}, \qquad d=N-1,\quad u=\frac{N\tau}{2\pi}. \tag{16} \] At \(x=k/N\), this equals \(e_k(-2\cos\tau)\). The exact edge multiplier is \[ \frac{H_N(s)}{W_k(s)} =\frac{G_N(k)^2}{G_N(k-s)G_N(k+s)}. \tag{17} \] The reflection and the factor \(H_N^{-1}\) in (14) fix the normalization in (17). Inverting that relation would insert an incorrect extra cut factor. On the directed local angle rectangle the edge critical wire remains in a fixed complex neighborhood of the real interval \((1/5,3/10)\), away from every factorial endpoint. Equations (15)–(17), the exact primitive wire contour and its endpoint currents therefore give an all-order version of directed (24): \[ \mathscr K_N(t,u;s)=N^{-3/2}e^{N\psi(t,u)}a_e(t,u) \left[1+\sum_{j=1}^{L}N^{-j}k_{e,j}(t,u,s) +O_{K,L}(N^{-L-1})\right]. \tag{18} \] The leading \(a_e\) is the original nonzero amplitude and is independent of \(s\). The coefficients and remainder are holomorphic in both angle variables and \(s\), with fixed derivative estimates on smaller compacts. The complementary wires, finite lattice currents and local-contour endpoints have the same fixed exponential losses as before; they are smaller than every requested relative power after comparison with the local saddle. For clarity, the all-order step in (18) can be carried out without citing a formal stationary-phase principle as an estimate. On the deformed local contour the real part of the exponent falls quadratically away from the selected saddle. Restrict to a fixed neighborhood, use the analytic Taylor series of the phase and amplitude to any desired finite order, put the centered variable equal to \(N^{-1/2}\) times a new variable, and integrate the resulting Gaussian moments. Split that neighborhood at a shrinking radius \(N^{-\epsilon}\), choosing sufficiently many Taylor terms for the requested order. Outside the shrinking neighborhood the quadratic bound is exponentially small; inside, the analytic Taylor remainder is dominated by an integrable Gaussian times its required power. Odd Gaussian moments vanish and the common half-power is already displayed in \(N^{-3/2}\). The same proof with the one-dimensional physical trace contour gives its \(N^{3/2}\) factor and all relative orders. All these estimates are uniform on the fixed parameter compacts, because the saddle, inverse Hessian and nonzero leading amplitude remain on compact sets. The integral of the absolute local Gaussian amplitude divided by the absolute value of its leading complex Gaussian integral is bounded uniformly on such compacts. The bound can depend on the fixed degree and signed twist. It is not asserted to be a universal constant across all trees. This is sufficient to integrate a uniform relative remainder without amplifying it by an exponential factor. ## 5. All-order normalized message induction We strengthen directed (28), keeping the same limiting phase and leading amplitude. For every requested \(L\), at every nonroot vertex, \[ \frac{M_{v,N}(u;s)}{M_{v,N}(0;s)} =e^{Nh_v(u)}\frac{\alpha_v(u)}{\alpha_v(0)} \left[1+\sum_{j=1}^{L}N^{-j}a_{v,j}(u,s) +O_{K,L}(N^{-L-1})\right]. \tag{19} \] The coefficients may and do have zero normalized value at \(u=0\). The remainder and any prescribed finite derivative are uniform on smaller parent compacts. The exact complex denominator is retained; it is not replaced by an absolute estimate or by a presumed asymptotic scalar. The leading amplitude is nonzero and independent of \(s\) after the exact outside physical scalars have been separated. For a terminal vertex, insert (18) into its exact full trace. The first charge has coefficient one by (12); its sine and Gaussian factors are nonzero. Expand that conditional first-charge integral to the requested order. The estimates in §2–3 bound the entire remainder of the trace below the first charge by a fixed exponential factor. Evaluating also at \(u=0\) and dividing the two expansions proves (19), and proves nonvanishing of the exact denominator for sufficiently large levels. Suppose (19) holds for the children of \(v\). Divide each exact child by its exact value at zero in the actual recurrence before making any approximation. The finite product of their expansions has every prescribed relative order. Its normalized leading amplitude has no zero, so the logarithm of this product, with the normalization fixed at zero, has an expansion of the same order. This is an ordinary finite algebraic operation on asymptotic series with a uniformly invertible leading term. In the conditional first-charge integral retain the limiting child phases in \(A_v^{\mathrm{loc}}\); place all higher logarithmic terms in the analytic amplitude. Equivalently one can perturb the conditional saddle by \(O(N^{-1})\), but no such perturbation is needed to estimate the remainder. The local absolute-to-leading Gaussian bound proved above shows that a uniform relative \(O(N^{-L-1})\) input error contributes a relative \(O(N^{-L-1})\) output error. Expand the new local amplitude and phase to a sufficiently high finite order and integrate. Division by the expansion at parent angle zero gives (19) at \(v\). Outside that conditional saddle, do not insert a truncated child expansion. Use the exact normalized real and strip estimates already proved on \(K\) in §3. They are precisely what controls the full charge tail, original endpoint currents and complementary contour portions. This prevents a local asymptotic remainder from being used as a global source bound. The finitely many nonminimal charges need only their existing bound below the first charge; expanding them to every order is unnecessary. All fixed derivatives are obtained on nested rectangles by Cauchy estimates, or by starting with sufficiently many orders and differentiating the local integral. Since the tree is fixed and every inequality has a strict margin, a finite nested system of slightly larger local compacts can be chosen. The real/strip bounds used for tails are those of the exact messages; they do not shrink with the order. Possible large constants in the coefficients only increase the level from which the estimate holds. They do not change any certificate inequality. At the root the same induction applies with no parent kernel and no outgoing envelope. Restore the exact child values at zero recursively. Their actions add at their selected conditional saddles, giving the original joint action (6); they are not separately replaced by subtree volumes. The scalar restoration is the original exact ledger \[ A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v, \tag{20} \] with the single reduced cut \(H_N\) left outside. Same-color chirps, opposite-order references, turn gammas, closing and writhe factors are each counted once, as in the exact-scalar theorem. All \(s\)-independent phases and powers of \(N\) cancel in the ratio (3). In particular there is no unspecified \(s\)-dependent oscillating subtree constant in (19). Every complete edge contributes \(N^{-3/2}\) and every trace contributes \(N^{3/2}\); the tree relation leaves the same total \(N^{3/2}\). The leading coefficient is nonzero. Thus the actual normalized whole source has an all-order expansion on the original disk and on \(K\). This proves existence and uniform remainder estimates; the next section identifies the polynomial degree filtration, which does not follow merely from existence. ## 6. Why the coefficients have the required degree filtration At a retained physical edge the only remaining microscopic dependence, apart from (20), is the exact factor (17). Put \(\delta=N^{-1}\) and introduce an auxiliary independent parameter \(t\). Applying (15) to (17), before substituting \(t=\delta s\), gives \[ \log\mathcal I_N(x,s) =\delta^{-1}\mathcal K(x,t)+B_0(x,t) +\sum_{j=1}^{L}\delta^jB_j(x,t)+O(\delta^{L+1}), \qquad t=\delta s. \tag{21} \] The \(B_j\) are holomorphic near \(t=0\), are even in \(t\), and vanish there. Terms in \(\log N\) cancel. An original offset \(x=\ell(X)+\delta c\), including the midpoint offsets from \(d=N-1\), contributes \(c\mathcal K_x\) to \(B_0\) and holomorphic further terms to the lower amplitudes; it does not change the leading phase in (5). To organize all orders, replace (17) in the **local first-charge integral** by its canonical interpolation with \(s=Nt\), for sufficiently small independent \(t\). All its factorial arguments then remain in the same complex bulk domain. This defines a local analytic family whose phase is exactly \(\Phi_t\) in (5). It is not an assertion about the physical source with \(s\) growing like \(N\): no global or tail estimate for that regime is used. Global errors have already been controlled for bounded physical \(s\). The auxiliary family organizes the local coefficients, and its restriction \(t=s/N\) reproduces the actual local source exactly. The full Hessian of \(\Phi\) is invertible. Indeed the wire Hessians in each edge contour are invertible. After eliminating them, each successive angular conditional Hessian is invertible by the bound in §2. The determinant identity for a block Schur complement therefore gives invertibility of the original joint Hessian. This also identifies the joint critical point and the phase independently of the order of finite contractions. The analytic implicit-function theorem gives \(X_*(t)\) for small \(t\), with all logarithms and first-charge marks retained. Expansion of this local analytic family to arbitrary finite order gives holomorphic coefficient germs \(C_j(t)\) such that \[ \log\mathcal Z_N(s)\sim N\{S(s/N)-S(0)\} +\sum_{j\ge0}N^{-j}\{C_j(s/N)-C_j(0)\}. \tag{22} \] One may perform the Gaussian expansions edge by edge and vertex by vertex, as in §5, or jointly. These are the same coefficients: at any finite order they are finite Gaussian moments of the same Taylor polynomial; iterated Gaussian integration and Schur complementation give the same moments. Absolute Gaussian domination justifies the uniform remainders in either computation. Thus (22) identifies the coefficients of the actual normalized induction, not those of an independently postulated effective phase. For each fixed truncation order, Taylor-expand the holomorphic functions in (22) in \(t\), then put \(t=s/N\). Terms from \(N(S-S(0))\) have degree \(r+1\) at order \(N^{-r}\); terms from all \(C_j-C_j(0)\) have degree at most \(r\). The even phase has \(S'(0)=0\), so no order-zero nonconstant term occurs. This proves (4) and its top-diagonal assertion, with uniform remainders on every fixed \(K\). Since every discarded term has a fixed exponential gap, its polynomial prefactor and any fixed derivative are smaller than the requested \(N^{-L-1}\) order. This argument also shows that the expansions on the disk and on all translated compacts have the same coefficients. They come from the same canonical local family and original scalar, not from continuing an asymptotic estimate across the resonances. Since \(\mathcal Z_N(s)\to1\) uniformly on each compact, its logarithm tending to zero is uniquely fixed for large \(N\). ## 7. The actual marked geometric germ for the new certificates The analytic extension does not replace the geometric part of the directed theorem. Its certificate gives \[ \sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}=2\pi|D_v|\ge2\pi\,2^{15}>630 \tag{23} \] at every vertex. The [vertexwise geometric theorem](actual_all_circle_vertexwise_geometry.md) supplies the positive ordered charge path with the original odd seams, primitive disk curves and the original main cusp unfilled. Back-substitution of the conditional first-charge roots places every angle in the common small-angular uniqueness polydisk; it is therefore the same path's endpoint, not merely a solution of exponentiated equations. This is directed §7, including its explicit backwards restoration. With \(Q_v=e^{i\tau_v}\), the primitive equations are \[ U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i,\qquad V_v=2\log Q_v, \qquad n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v. \tag{24} \] Along the continued charge path the constant on the right is \(-2\pi ic\). It is the linear term in (6). The positive endpoint has \(\operatorname{Im}\tau_v<0\), so \(Q_v^2\ne1\). A filling word commutes with this semisimple longitude; its eigenvalue ratio is one by (24), so it is projectively the identity. The representation therefore factors through the actual filled knot group on a neighborhood of the selected point. The [local rational reconstruction and longitude theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md) are algebraic statements on the full source branch; they do not require the old summed or maximum-based analytic inequality. The new directed case supplies exactly their required anchor: the actual positive filled holonomy at \(M=1\), the continued primitive logarithms, and the nondegenerate source critical point. The implicit branch of (5) consequently reconstructs a meridian-varying branch of representations of the filled group. Marked geometric rigidity identifies that branch with the geometric meridian germ of the actual knot. The negative longitude lift at its complete point is fixed by the once-bordered Seifert-frame calculation, not by a cusp tangent or a quantum normalization guess. For this branch the exact identity is \[ L_{\mathrm{geom}}(M) =-M^{a(D)}\prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)}, \qquad X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}, \tag{25} \] on the preferred longitude and the declared \(M\) eigenline, equivalently the inverse value on the source \(M^{-1}\) line. This is the geometric theorem's complete filled-germ statement; it does not require extending positive ideal tetrahedra through every algebraic value of \(M\). Differentiating a stationary value differentiates only the explicit parameter. The sine identity in (5), with its logarithm zero at \(t=0\), gives \[ e^{\mathcal K_t(x,t)}=\frac{M^2-X}{1-M^2X}, \qquad M=e^{\pi it}. \tag{26} \] Set \(h=\log q\), \(u=\log M\), and \[ \mathcal S(u)=\pi i\{S(u/(\pi i))-S(0)\}. \tag{27} \] Then (25)–(26) give \(-e^{\mathcal S'(u)}=L_{\mathrm{geom}}(e^u)\) as an identity of holomorphic germs, not just to second order. The original first-charge and filling mark select this germ among the solutions of the rational edge and vertex equations. ### The preferred-cusp first correction The analytic family in (5) is even in \(t\). Its selected critical point is therefore even, by uniqueness of the analytic implicit branch. The exact interpolated edge amplitude and scalar are even as well. Every stationary coefficient \(C_j(t)\) can consequently be chosen even. At order \(N^{-1}\), (22) has only \[ p_1(s)=\tfrac12 S''(0)s^2: \tag{27a} \] normalization eliminates a constant, the evenness eliminates the possible linear contribution \(C_0'(0)s\), and all other lower amplitudes begin at order \(N^{-2}\). Thus this coefficient is not identified merely by its highest polynomial degree. On the preferred geometric germ, the cusp shape is \(\tau_K=\left.\frac{d}{du}\log[-L_{\mathrm{geom}}(e^u)]\right|_{u=0}\). Equations (25)–(27) give \(S''(0)=\pi i\tau_K\). Restoring the exact original framing, already included in \(a(D)\), yields for every directed case \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{K_NH_N(s)} =1+\frac{\pi i\,\tau_K s^2}{2N} +O_K(N^{-2}). \tag{27b} \] This is uniform on each fixed compact used above and on each \(|s|\le R<1\), with the same geometric cusp shape of the original filled knot complement. In particular no additional unrecorded linear or constant scalar is left in the first correction. The exponential passage from the logarithm changes only order \(N^{-2}\) and higher. ## 8. Consequence for every genuine all-level annihilator Let \[ P(q,M,T)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,M)T^j, \qquad TM=qMT, \tag{28} \] be a specified nonzero fixed operator with coefficients in \(\mathbb C(q,M)\) which annihilates the actual whole reduced function \(F_N(M)\) at every sufficiently large level. Negative shifts can first be removed by multiplying by a power of \(T\). Clear fixed rational denominators and remove the common \(q-1\) valuation. Let \(P_0(M,L)\ne0\) be the resulting first classical symbol. This hypothesis is the genuine all-level source equation; an equation fitted to complete values or to finitely many jets is not enough. The existence of such fixed operators is proved by the [finite-sum annihilator theorem](finite_sum_annihilator.md), with its boundary terms retained. The full modified dimension is \[ d_N(M)=\eta_N\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}},\qquad d_N(1)=\eta_N/N,\qquad \eta_N=i^{N+3}. \tag{29} \] It satisfies \(d_N(q_N^s)/d_N(1)=H_N(s)^{-1}\). For \(f(M)=M-M^{-1}\), the exact reduced-to-full gauge is \[ \widetilde P=\sum_{j=0}^{d} a_j(q,M)(-1)^j\frac{f(M)}{f(q^jM)}T^j. \tag{30} \] Indeed \(H_N(s+j)/H_N(s)=(-1)^j f(M)/f(q_N^jM)\). After multiplying on the left by \(\prod_{j=1}^{d}f(q^jM)\), its first classical symbol is \[ f(M)^dP_0(M,-L). \tag{31} \] The meridian divisor and sign character remain in the calculation. Choose a small upper-half-plane disk \(D\) and apply (4) to the compact union of the required translates \(D,D+1,\ldots,D+d\), slightly enlarged for coefficient estimates. The exact root equation (30), after division by the nonzero \(\mathcal Z_N\), makes every coefficient of its asymptotic expansion vanish on \(D\). Clearing denominators as above makes these coefficient identities polynomial in \(s\); they therefore hold identically. Regrade the filtered series using \(u=hs\). The inequality \(\deg p_r\le r+1\) gives exactly \[ \log\mathcal Z\ \longleftrightarrow h^{-1}\mathcal S(u)+\sum_{j\ge0}h^j A_j(u), \tag{32} \] with no other negative power of \(h\). The finite difference under \(u\mapsto u+jh\) has no negative power; its constant coefficient is \(j\mathcal S'(u)\). Thus the formal shift ratio has constant term \(e^{j\mathcal S'(u)}\). The substitution \(\mathbb C[[h,u]]\to\mathbb C[s][[h]]\), \(u\mapsto hs\), is injective: distinct monomials \(h^au^b\) have distinct images \(h^{a+b}s^b\). Lifting the exact coefficient identity before substitution and taking its constant \(h\)-coefficient yields \[ f(e^u)^dP_0(e^u,-e^{\mathcal S'(u)})=0. \tag{33} \] The formal series ring is a domain and \(f(e^u)^d\) is nonzero, so it can be canceled in this proved identity. This does not discard a peripheral component from the original operator. Equations (25)–(27) identify the remaining germ as the actual geometric eigenvalue germ. Evaluation on that germ defines a nonzero prime in \(\mathbb C[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]\), since it contains \(P_0\). It contains no nonzero polynomial in \(M\) alone because the meridian varies on an open disk. Hence it has height one and is generated by one irreducible Laurent polynomial \(A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb C}\). Consequently \[ A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb C}(M,L)\mid P_0(M,L). \tag{34} \] For an operator over \(\mathbb Q(q,M)\), contract the same prime to \(\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]\). It is again a nonzero height-one prime, with an irreducible generator dividing \(P_0\) over \(\mathbb Q\). Its complex factorization contains the selected component and whatever conjugate components the rational field requires. This does not assert that the selected complex component is itself defined over \(\mathbb Q\). The evenness of the selected phase also gives the same reciprocal selected germ as in the existing filtered theorem. No new statement about multiplicities, equality with the full A-polynomial, or equality of operator ideals follows. There is no uniform nonvanishing claim across ordinary resonances and no physical fixed-\(M\ne1\) quantum asymptotic obtained by replacing bounded \(s\) by a quantity of order \(N\). ## 9. Proof dependencies and scope The [directed finite-source theorem](actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) supplies the following inputs: 1. Equations (N1)–(N4), (13), (25)–(26): actual basis, full Frobenius functional, complete metric, physical turn, and exact finite recurrence. These fix types, normals and the outside scalar. 2. Equations (14)–(24): full edge complement, conditional rectangle estimate, actual local wire contour and nonzero leading edge amplitude. Extending the compact changes only bounded \(H/W\) factors. 3. Equations (27)–(37): normalized conditional phase, its Hessian and Schur complement, first-charge drop and strict separation of retained charges. 4. Equations (38)–(43): actual full-input strip estimate, exact charge coefficient, tail/endpoint/current bounds, and outgoing-envelope regeneration. These estimates are applied to exact messages outside the local saddle at every asymptotic order. 5. Equations (44)–(46): backward restoration of the same joint critical point, common small-angular charge-path anchor and actual filled geometry. The [exact interpolation theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) and [regular-circle calculation](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), §10, fix (13)–(17), including all midpoint and reflection factors. The [direct-crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md), §§2–4, fixes the finite translated grids and their endpoint currents. The [full source bounds](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), (D9)–(D14), supply the full polynomial norm used in regeneration, including constant normal channels; the extension to compact nonreal parameters is checked in §3 above. The [exact scalar calculation](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) fixes (20) and the one reduced cut. The [filtered characteristic theorem](actual_main_meridian_filtered_characteristic.md) supplies the algebraic organization of the canonical insertion and the Ore gauge. Its analytic hypotheses for the directed certificate are proved here: §§3–5 give every finite asymptotic order on the required charts with a uniform remainder, and §6 identifies those actual coefficients with the joint two-parameter insertion. The published first-order profile alone is not used as a substitute for either step. Finally the [geometric-characteristic theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md), §§5–10, supplies the marked reconstructed branch and the preferred longitude, with §5's complete filled-point anchor checked in §7 above for the new certificate. The positive geometric path depends on (23), not on the older summed or maximum-based source criterion. Thus no old analytic class restriction is silently used to identify the new source branch. All work in this note is for the actual fixed finite tree. It does not give a multi-boundary replacement theorem for arbitrary short-power islands, nor an automatic result for a graph with cycles. Those would require their own conditional source estimates.

title: Volume limits from the degree and twist at each circle
status: Directed subtree criterion; uniform twist bound and independent degree alternative
text: # Volume limits from the degree and twist at each circle The [directed all-orders extension](actual_all_circle_directed_all_orders.md) proves the full expansion on the shifted microscopic meridian charts for every certificate below, identifies its preferred-cusp correction, and supplies the selected geometric-factor conclusion for genuine all-level annihilators. Start with a fixed finite ordered tree of two-strand integer braids, with at least one edge and one crossing circle at every vertex. Turn each child tangle through its specified quarter-turn before stacking it at the parent, and use the original cylindrical closure. The [literal construction and strand test](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md#the-knot-construction) retain the endpoint frames and require one closed main knot, with no component closed inside an intermediate tangle. Write \(d_v\) for the degree of vertex \(v\), and \(n_v\) for its signed number of half-twists. A sufficient condition for the volume limit is \[ \boxed{\qquad d_v\ge2^{28}\quad\text{or}\quad |n_v|\ge2^{27} \qquad\text{at every vertex}.\qquad} \] The alternative can be chosen separately at each vertex. High-degree vertices may retain any fixed signed powers, including zero and small nonzero powers. If the strand test gives a knot \(K\), its original complement is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] Both level parities are included. The tree, powers and degrees are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The constants are coarse sufficient bounds; they make no claim about the shortest possible twists. The more general criterion below assigns a real-decay bound to each subtree polynomial. Dividing by that polynomial's exact value at zero retains its complex scalar and isolates the contribution of the next trace. Different edges may use different bounds. The final vertex has no outgoing polynomial, so it need not pay the extra loss needed to send one to a parent. This distinction also gives a short-power star outside both the earlier summed and uniform local tests. Section 8 explains how to retain arbitrarily many prescribed short powers: add an even stack of sufficiently long terminal tangles at every vertex of a fixed ordered knot core. Their endpoint pairing preserves the knot condition, although the resulting knot type can change. The proof estimates the actual finite invariant throughout; it does not assume that a proposed global critical point dominates. ## 1. The directed criterion Put \[ a_0=\frac1{2\pi},\qquad k_0=2^{-16},\qquad R_0=\frac18,\qquad b_0=2^{-11},\qquad r_0=\frac1{16},\qquad t_0=2^{-14},\qquad \chi=1-\cos r_0. \tag{1} \] The parent-variable rectangle is \[ \mathcal R=\{u:|\Re u|\le R_0,\ |\Im u|\le b_0\}. \tag{2} \] Choose any vertex as root and direct all edges toward it. For every nonroot vertex choose a number \[ 0<c_v<k_0, \qquad \delta_v=\min\left\{\frac{b_0}2, \frac{c_v\chi}{4(1+c_v)}\right\}. \tag{3} \] These are parameters of the criterion. They can differ at every edge. They are not asymptotic quantities to be inferred from the invariant. Write \(q_v=1\) at a nonroot vertex and \(q_v=0\) at the root. If \(\mathrm{Ch}(v)\) is the set of children, define \[ \begin{aligned} a_v&=\frac{d_v}{2\pi},& b_v&=\frac{n_v}{2\pi},& D_v&=a_v-i b_v,\\ A_v&=\frac2{\pi^2} \left(q_vk_0+\frac12\sum_{w\in\mathrm{Ch}(v)}c_w\right),& B_v&=16q_v+|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|,& C_v&=B_v+\frac{b_v^2}{4A_v}. \end{aligned} \tag{4} \] There is at least one incidence at every vertex, so \(A_v,B_v\) are positive. Let \[ \delta_v^{\mathrm{in}} =\min\bigl(\{b_0\}\cup \{\delta_w:w\in\mathrm{Ch}(v)\}\bigr) \tag{5} \] and set \[ y_v=\min\left\{ \frac{\delta_v^{\mathrm{in}}}2, \frac{t_0|D_v|}{4C_v}, \frac{A_v\pi^2}{8(\pi|b_v|+t_0|D_v|)}, \sqrt{\frac{A_v\pi^2}{8B_v}} \right\}. \tag{6} \] Finally define two action quantities \[ \beta_v=\frac{210}{361}\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2}, \qquad \eta_v=\min\left\{ \frac12t_0|D_v|y_v, \frac12A_v\pi^2, A_vr_0^2, \frac18a_vr_0^2 \right\}. \tag{7} \] The criterion consists of the strict inequalities \[ \boxed{\quad t_0|D_v|\ge2,\qquad \beta_v<\frac{\eta_v}{2}\quad \text{at every vertex},\quad} \tag{8} \] and, only at nonroot vertices, \[ \boxed{\qquad \beta_v<(k_0-c_v)\chi.\qquad} \tag{9} \] It is a finite elementary test in the degrees, signed powers, root and positive numbers \(c_v\). It uses no value of an unknown quantum invariant and no assumed dominance of a global saddle. Its quantities are local: \(A_v\) and the available strip depend on the child budgets, while the exact child scalar will be divided out rather than estimated. Use the original reduced-state normalization \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(M=-q_Nx=q_N^s\), and \(F_N(1)=K_N\). The raw highest-weight parameter \(x\) here is distinct from a normalized wire coordinate. The [pointing theorem](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) fixes this ADO invariant and its zero framing. **Theorem.** If (3), (8), and (9) hold, the actual reduced state has \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1+O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-1}), \qquad |s|\le R<1, \tag{10} \] where \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_vn_v. \tag{11} \] Its complete values are nonzero for all sufficiently large levels and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \tag{12} \] Both level parities and the original normal channels are retained. The proof identifies the same original filled critical value as the marked geometric completion. It does not use a sum of independent subtree volumes. ## 2. An actual conditional kernel on a rectangle The fixed Newton polynomials are \[ \begin{gathered} d=N-1,\qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad S_k=\prod_{r=1}^k2\sin(\pi r/N),\\ e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{j<k}(c_j-z),\qquad 0\le k<N. \end{gathered} \tag{N1} \] Let \(\mathcal T_N(2\cos\theta)=2\cos(N\theta)\), and put \(P_\sigma(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi\sigma)\). The normalized polynomial trace is \[ \phi_\sigma(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_\sigma}F, \qquad \phi_\sigma(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}. \tag{N2} \] The remainder has degree less than \(N\). This is the full polynomial functional, including its derivative values when roots coalesce. The [typed turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) retains the paired factors \[ W_k(s)=\prod_{r=1}^k \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right). \tag{N3} \] After lowering the pairing (N2), a physical turn gives the equal-index weight \(\gamma_e(s)H_N(s)/W_k(s)\). The factor \(\gamma_e\) is the original scalar prescribed by that edge's orientation type. It stays in the exact scalar ledger. For the edge action write \[ \begin{gathered} J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\qquad G_0=g(1/4),\\ b(x,t)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos(2\pi v)+2\cos t)\,dv-2J(x),\\ \psi(t,u)=\operatorname{stat}_x[b(x,t)+b(x,u)], \qquad\psi(0,0)=2G_0. \end{gathered} \tag{N4} \] The logarithms and stationary branch are continued from \(x=1/4,t=u=0\). The finite factorial interpolation, the actual edge contour and this phase are proved in [the all-circle finite-sum theorem](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md). Its polynomial estimates use [the full Newton bounds](all_circle_uniform_newton_bounds.md). Use the exact full kernel \[ K_N(t,u;s)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_k(s)}. \tag{13} \] The definitions of \(e_k,W_k\) and the fixed anti-diagonal trace metric are unchanged. It is a polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in each of \(-2\cos t\) and \(-2\cos u\), hence has trigonometric degree at most \(N-1\) in either angle. The paired factors and their inverses are bounded for fixed \(|s|\le R<1\). Every inequality below permits a polynomial factor in N. The [full-kernel real estimate](actual_all_circle_local_message_volume.md#two-full-kernel-bounds) is \[ |K_N(t,u;s)|\le C_RN^{A_R} e^{N\{2G_0-k_0[(1-\cos t)+(1-\cos u)]\}}, \qquad t,u\in[-\pi,\pi]. \tag{14} \] The new estimate needed here is \[ |K_N(t+iy,u;s)|\le C_RN^{A_R} e^{N\{\Re\psi(0,u)-k_0(1-\cos t)+16y^2\}}, \quad u\in\mathcal R,\quad t\in[-\pi,\pi],\quad |y|\le b_0. \tag{15} \] Thus the parent compact is a long, thin rectangle, rather than the old disk of radius \(2^{-12}\). The constant term is the actual conditional phase \(\psi(0,u)\), not its upper bound \(2G_0+O(|u|^2)\). Here is a proof from the original finite kernel. Split the indices into \(I=[1/5,3/10]\) and its complement. The complementary full polynomial has the established single-edge loss \(\eta_K=\pi/200\), including high indices and their complete derivatives. Its ellipse bound is \[ C_RN^{A_R} e^{N\{2G_0-\eta_K+|y|+|\Im u|\}}. \tag{16} \] The exact edge phase has, on the radius 1/4 bidisk, \[ |\psi_{tt}+a_0|\le a_0/50, \quad |\psi_{uu}+a_0|\le a_0/50, \quad |\psi_{tu}|\le a_0/50, \quad \psi_t(0,u)=\psi_u(t,0)=0. \tag{17} \] In particular \(|\psi(0,u)-2G_0|\le |u|^2/10\). Hence (16) is smaller than (15): the sum \(b_0+b_0+(R_0^2+b_0^2)/10+2k_0\) is less than \(\eta_K/2\). All these constants are independent of the tree. For the retained indices write \(u=a+ib\). Their factors at \(a\) are positive. If \(r_j=\cos(2\pi(j+1/2)/N)\), then \(r_j>-1/3\) and \(r_j+\cos a>253/384\). Along \(|a|\le1/8,\ |b|\le2^{-11}\), the denominator \(r_j+\cos(a+ib)\) has modulus greater than \(3/5\), and \[ \left|\frac{d^2}{du^2}\log(r_j+\cos u)\right| =\left|\frac{-r_j\cos u-1}{(r_j+\cos u)^2}\right|<9. \tag{18} \] The first derivative at real a is real. Integrating vertically therefore gives the actual finite-product estimate \[ |e_k(-2\cos(a+ib))| \le e_k(-2\cos a)e^{5Nb^2},\qquad k/N\in I. \tag{19} \] At the other end retain the original product bound \[ |e_k(-2\cos(t+iy))| \le e^2e_k(-2)e^{N[-\alpha\sin^2(t/2)+11y^2]}, \qquad \alpha>1/250. \tag{20} \] The positive retained sum at \((0,a)\) is bounded by a polynomial times \(\exp(N\psi(0,a))\), uniformly for real \(|a|\le1/8\). This is the original one-edge positive Laplace estimate: its unique critical wire is \[ \tan^2(\pi x)=\frac1{1+\tan^2(a/2)}, \tag{21} \] which stays in the interior of \(I\). Its second derivative stays negative on this fixed real compact. Equations (19)–(20), and the second bound in (17), consequently give \[ |K_{N,I}(t+iy,u;s)|\le C_RN^{A_R} e^{N\{\Re\psi(0,u)-\alpha\sin^2(t/2)+11y^2+6b^2\}}. \tag{22} \] For \(|t|\ge1/8\), \[ 6b_0^2<\frac{\alpha}{2}\sin^2(1/16),\qquad 2k_0<\alpha/2. \tag{23} \] For example \(\sin(1/16)>1/(8\pi)\), \(\pi^2<10\) and \(\alpha>1/250\) already prove the first inequality. This proves (15) in this range. For \(|t|\le1/8\), the [canonical wire contour](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) gives the exact nonzero edge asymptotic on the 1/4 bidisk. Both \(u\) and \(t+iy\) lie strictly inside that disk. Integrating the first bound of (17) gives (15) there. The original lattice currents and (16) are exponentially smaller. In particular the full kernel, uniformly on this smaller rectangle product, retains \[ K_N(t,u;s)=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)} (1+O_R(N^{-1})), \tag{24} \] with the original nonzero holomorphic leading amplitude and midpoint normalization. The outside physical edge gamma is not included in \(a_e\). ## 3. The exact recursion may be rooted anywhere Lower the fixed Frobenius pairing at every vertex of the original closed source. Every physical turn then identifies equal Newton indices and retains its factor \(\gamma_e H_N/W_k\). The resulting finite scalar is a sum over the original edge indices of a product of the original vertex trace tensors. Choosing a root merely specifies the order of these finite contractions. It does not move a cut through a tangle, commute open operators or change a framing. Consequently the [exact recursions](actual_all_circle_local_message_volume.md#the-full-finite-kernel-and-exact-recursion) hold for any chosen root: \[ M_{v,N}(u)=\gamma_{e_v}(s)\, \mathcal D_{n_v,\sigma_v,N}^{(t)} \left[K_N(t,u;s)\prod_{w\in\mathrm{Ch}(v)}M_{w,N}(t)\right] \tag{25} \] at a nonroot vertex, and \[ Z_N=\mathcal D_{n_o,\sigma_o,N}^{(t)} \left[\prod_{w\in\mathrm{Ch}(o)}M_{w,N}(t)\right] \tag{26} \] at the root. The [original global closing, framing and reference factors](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md), and the original single reduced cut \(H_N\), remain outside (26). Edge gammas are counted once. The exact normal value \(\sigma_v=0\) and the moving values \(\pm s\) retain their actual orientation types. Each message is an even trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in \(u\), regardless of the subtree. There is no discarded-source error in (25)–(26). ## 4. The phase class and the variable envelopes The inductive analytic class is \[ h_v(0)=h'_v(0)=0,\qquad h_v(-u)=h_v(u),\qquad |h_v''(u)+a_0|\le a_0/20,\quad u\in\mathcal R. \tag{27} \] The leading normalized amplitude \(\alpha_v(u)/\alpha_v(0)\) is holomorphic and nonzero on a neighborhood of the required smaller compact. Exact subtree constants are retained: \[ \frac{M_{v,N}(u)}{M_{v,N}(0)} =\frac{\alpha_v(u)}{\alpha_v(0)}e^{Nh_v(u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad u\in\mathcal R. \tag{28} \] As usual a slightly smaller rectangle can be used for fixed derivative estimates; the strict margins permit an initially slightly larger one. The global assertions attached to \(c_v\) are \[ \left|\frac{M_{v,N}(t)}{M_{v,N}(0)}\right| \le CN^A e^{-Nc_v(1-\cos t)}, \quad t\in[-\pi,\pi], \tag{29} \] \[ \left|\frac{M_{v,N}(t+iy)}{M_{v,N}(0)}\right| \le CN^A e^{N[-(c_v/2)(1-\cos t)+y^2]}, \quad |y|\le\delta_v. \tag{30} \] The real sup norm, full canonical polynomial norm and complete derivative norm differ by polynomial factors at the required fixed multiples of N. No estimate drops the repeated-root normal data. For completeness, (30) follows from (28)–(29) and exact degree. The Poisson estimate for a Laurent polynomial of degree less than \(N\) is \[ |M_{v,N}(t+iy)/M_{v,N}(0)| \le CN^A e^{N[-c_v(1-\cos t)+(1+c_v)|y|]}. \tag{31} \] For \(|t|\ge r_0\) use (3). For \(|t|<r_0\) use the rectangle expansion and \[ \Re h_v(t+iy)\le -\frac{19a_0}{40}t^2+\frac{21a_0}{40}y^2. \tag{32} \] Both arguments give (30), without a conjectured quadratic estimate for an individual high Newton basis element. Assume the children satisfy (27)–(30). At a nonroot vertex set \[ A_v^{\mathrm{loc}}(t,u)=\psi(t,u)+\sum_wh_w(t), \quad C_{v,\ell}(u)=\operatorname{stat}_t \{A_v^{\mathrm{loc}}(t,u)+ib_vt^2/2-i\ell t\}. \tag{33} \] At the root omit \(\psi\) and \(u\). There are \(d_v\) incidences in \(t\). Hence \[ A_v^{\mathrm{loc}}(t,u)=\psi(0,u)-a_vt^2/2+E_v(t,u), \quad |E_{v,tt}|,\ |E_{v,t}/t|\le a_v/20. \tag{34} \] The root constant in this formula is zero. For \(0\le\ell\le L_v=\lfloor t_0|D_v|\rfloor\) the equation \(D_vt=-i\ell+E_{v,t}\) contracts in \(|t|\le b_0\). Indeed \(t_0+b_0/20<b_0\). The actual solutions lie in the smaller disk \(|t|\le t_0/(19/20)\), leaving room for the translated contours. The same elementary calculation as in the original proof gives \[ \frac{380}{441}\frac{\ell a_v}{|D_v|^2} \le-\Im t_{v,\ell}\le \frac{420}{361}\frac{\ell a_v}{|D_v|^2}, \tag{35} \] also for complex parent \(u\). No child phase is asserted to be real on the real axis. Its nonlinear derivative is \(t\) times a function bounded by \(a_v/20\), so the real part of the denominator remains positive. The normalized phase \(h_v=C_{v,1}(u)-C_{v,1}(0)\) satisfies \[ h'_v=\psi_u(t_{v,1},u),\qquad h''_v=\psi_{uu} -\frac{\psi_{ut}^2}{A_{v,tt}^{\mathrm{loc}}+ib_v}. \tag{36} \] Using (17) and \(|A_{v,tt}^{\mathrm{loc}}+ib_v|\ge(19/20)|D_v|\ge(19/20)a_0\) proves (27), since \(1/50+20/(19\cdot2500)<1/20\). This is uniform on the rectangle. Charge ordering and the current-vertex drop are \[ \Re C_{v,\ell}(u)\le\Re C_{v,1}(u) -\frac{190}{441}\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2}(\ell^2-1), \quad 0\le\Re\psi(0,u)-\Re C_{v,1}(u)\le\beta_v. \tag{37} \] At the root again replace \(\psi(0,u)\) by zero. ## 5. Actual trace tails with the directed budgets Divide every child by its exact nonzero value \(M_{w,N}(0)\). The induction uses those complex constants exactly; it never estimates them by their complete-source magnitudes. Equations (15) and (30) imply \[ |\text{normalized trace input}(t+iy,u)| \le CN^A e^{N[\Re\psi(0,u)-A_vt^2+B_vy^2]}, \quad |y|\le\delta_v^{\mathrm{in}}. \tag{38} \] The root constant is zero. The factor \(2/\pi^2\) in (4) is exactly the inequality \(1-\cos t\ge2t^2/\pi^2\) on the original interval. The [exact finite translated-grid trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md), with its endpoint currents, has charge coefficients \[ c_{\ell,N}(\sigma)=(-1)^{(N-1)(\ell-1)} U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi\sigma),\qquad c_{1,N}=1. \tag{39} \] For \(\ell>L_v\), moving the single-grid rectangle by \(y_v\) costs, after maximizing the chirp term in the real variable, at most \(C_v y_v^2\). Since \(\ell>L_v\) implies \(\ell>t_0|D_v|\), (6) gives a tail loss at least \[ t_0|D_v|y_v-C_vy_v^2\ge\frac12t_0|D_v|y_v. \tag{40} \] Successive charges have the additional factor \(\exp(-Ny_v)\). The exact fixed-compact growth of (39) is absorbed for all sufficiently large N. This starting level may depend on the fixed vertex.
