At an original endpoint \(\pm\pi\), the chirp and finite-charge connectors cost at most \[ (\pi|b_v|+t_0|D_v|)y_v+B_vy_v^2 \le A_v\pi^2/4. \tag{41} \] Thus their loss is at least \(A_v\pi^2/2\). This includes the original zero-mode current. Nothing is inferred by dropping the endpoint terms of the nonperiodic chirp. For a retained charge, restrict its real integral to \([-r_0,r_0]\). Its complement loses \(A_vr_0^2\) by (38). Translate the retained interval to \(\Im t_{v,\ell}\). Its endpoints remain in the analytic rectangle. The original local Young inequality, now on this larger real interval, is \[ \begin{aligned} \Re\{A_v^{\mathrm{loc}}(t-iz,u)+ib_v(t-iz)^2/2-i\ell(t-iz)\} &\le\Re\psi(0,u)-a_vt^2/8\\ &\quad+\left[\frac{21}{40}a_v+ \frac{2b_v^2}{(14/5)a_v}\right]z^2-\ell z. \end{aligned} \tag{42} \] For \(0\le z\le-\Im t_{v,\ell}\), the last line after its quadratic term is at most \(-\ell z/8\), since \((420/361)\max(21/40,5/7)=300/361<7/8\). Every such connector therefore loses at least \(a_vr_0^2/8\). The translated horizontal saddle has negative real quadratic part at most \(-(19/20)a_v\). The physical sine factor is nonzero at \(t_{v,\ell}\). Equations (40)–(42) prove an absolute conditional error bounded by \(CN^A\exp N[\Re\psi(0,u)-\eta_v]\). Nonminimal charges are their saddle terms plus this absolute error; no relative approximation is asserted at a much lower nonminimal action. Conditions (8) and (37) put the whole conditional error strictly below the first charge. Equation (39) gives its nonzero coefficient for both parities. This establishes (28) and nonvanishing of the exact \(M_{v,N}(0)\). For the child inputs, their exact analytic logarithms differ from the limiting phases by \(O(N^{-1})\), with fixed derivatives on the required smaller compact. The finite product of those corrections is retained in the amplitude, or moves the saddle by \(O(N^{-1})\). As the tree is fixed, it spends no new exponential budget. The leading amplitude is a product of nonzero edge, child and Gaussian factors. All N-dependent physical crossing and carrier phases remain in \(M_{v,N}(0)\); its normalized leading amplitude does not conceal such phases. The full physical trace and the first-charge approximation are holomorphic in the formal meridian variables. As in the original proof, first take parameter circles avoiding collisions and then apply the maximum principle to their whole difference. This covers every actual \(\sigma_v=0,\pm s\), including normal limits. No isolated divided current is declared removable without its companions. ## 6. Regenerating the outgoing real bound The [canonical polynomial bounds](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), equations (D9)–(D14), retain the full source. For real \(u\), (14), the polynomial real sup bounds of the normalized children, the actual fixed-power crossing polynomial, Chebyshev folding in the correct quotient, and the full top-coefficient functional give \[ |M_{v,N}(u)|\le CN^A \left|\prod_wM_{w,N}(0)\right| e^{N[2G_0-k_0(1-\cos u)]}. \tag{43} \] This retains repeated-root derivatives and all fixed normals. Dividing by the nonzero first-charge value at zero costs at most \(\beta_v\). For \(|u|\ge r_0\), (9) absorbs that cost and yields (29). For \(|u|<r_0\), (28) and (32) give the stronger estimate, since \(c_v<k_0\ll19a_0/20\). Equation (30) follows by Section 4. Thus the induction closes with the selected directed budgets, rather than a common decay constant. There is no outgoing real bound at the final root. Imposing (9) there would be an unnecessary restriction. Its only normalization comparison is the conditional trace estimate (8). ## 7. Original action, geometry, and scope Restore the exact subtree constants successively. Stationary elimination in (33) gives the original joint equations \[ \sum_{e\sim v}\psi_{e,\tau_v} +\frac{in_v\tau_v}{2\pi}=i. \tag{44} \] The constants telescope to the original critical value \[ \mathcal C(\mathbf1)=\operatorname{stat}_{\boldsymbol\tau} \left[\sum_e\psi_e+ \frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_vn_v\tau_v^2-i\sum_v\tau_v\right]. \tag{45} \] Back-substitute from the final root: its first-charge angle belongs to the rectangle, so each child's selected parent value does also, and the same statement continues down the finite tree. Every restored angle has modulus at most \(1/[(19/20)|D_v|]\). Thus the vector satisfying (44) lies inside the full simultaneous small-angular uniqueness polydisk, not just the conditional disks used during elimination. The existing contraction identifies it with the same branch as the marked positive charge path. Indeed (8) implies \[ \sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}=2\pi|D_v|\ge 2\pi\,2^{15}>630. \tag{46} \] The [vertexwise geometric theorem](actual_all_circle_vertexwise_geometry.md) applies with no sum condition. Its original ordered two-octahedron cut, odd seam, primitive periods and calibrated action identify \(2\pi\Re\mathcal C(\mathbf1)\) with the volume of the actual filled knot complement. This is a geometric input, not a deduction from the quantum saddle alone. There are \(|E|\) edge Gaussians \(N^{-3/2}\) and \(|V|\) trace Gaussians \(N^{3/2}\); \(|V|=|E|+1\) leaves the original \(N^{3/2}\) power with nonzero amplitude. The exact first Fourier coefficient is one. The retained edge insertion has leading value one, and the scalar ledger remains precisely (11). This proves (10)–(12), with the original peripheral and framing factors. The criterion allows different strip and real-decay budgets and a different choice of final vertex. It is not the assertion that arbitrary capped short-twist islands can be substituted as black-box messages. Such an island requires a multi-boundary version of the conditional normalization proved here for an actual edge. The pointwise source estimates on the older tiny disk alone do not supply that extension. ## 8. A uniform twist corollary, with no degree sampling The directed criterion has the following simple consequence: \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27}\quad\text{at every vertex} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{(10)--(12)}. \tag{47} \] This sufficient constant is independent of the number of vertices, their degrees and the choice of root. Here is a proof covering all degrees simultaneously. Choose \(c_v=k_0/2\) at every nonroot vertex and write \(\delta\) for their common value in (3). The elementary cosine estimate gives \[ \chi\ge\frac{r_0^2}{2}-\frac{r_0^4}{24} =2^{-9}\frac{3071}{3072}>2^{-10},\qquad \delta>2^{-30}. \tag{48} \] At any vertex, including the root, put \(\mathcal R_v=\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}\). Then \[ A_v\ge\frac{k_0d_v}{2\pi^2},\qquad B_v\le16d_v, \qquad C_v\le\frac{\mathcal R_v^2}{8k_0d_v}. \tag{49} \] For the last inequality use \(16\le1/(8k_0)\). Each of the four branches of the minimum in (6) consequently has the following lower bound, respectively: \[ \frac\delta2,\qquad \frac{t_0k_0d_v}{\pi\mathcal R_v},\qquad \frac{k_0d_v}{16\mathcal R_v},\qquad 2^{-12}. \tag{50} \] The second displayed quantity is smaller than the third and fourth. For the third bound, use \(\pi|b_v|+t_0|D_v|\le\mathcal R_v(1+t_0/\pi)/2\). Thus every branch of (7), not just its tail branch, is bounded below by \[ \eta_v\ge\min\left\{ \frac{t_0\mathcal R_v\delta}{8\pi}, \frac{t_0^2 k_0d_v}{4\pi^2}\right\}. \tag{51} \] Indeed the second entry here is smaller than each of the other three entries in (7), by their explicit values and \(t_0\ll r_0\). On the other hand \[ \beta_v=\frac{420\pi}{361}\frac{d_v}{\mathcal R_v^2} <\frac{4d_v}{\mathcal R_v^2}. \tag{52} \] For comparison with half the first entry of (51), it suffices that \(\mathcal R_v^2>64\pi/(t_0\delta)\), since \(d_v\le\mathcal R_v\). The right side is less than \(2^{52}\), using \(\pi<4\) and (48). For comparison with half the second entry it suffices that \(\mathcal R_v^2>32\pi^2/(t_0^2k_0)\), whose right side is less than \(2^{53}\), since \(\pi^2<10\). Both inequalities follow strictly from \(\mathcal R_v^2\ge n_v^2\ge2^{54}\). The charge-cut condition in (8) follows as well. For the outgoing patch, the sharper elementary estimate is \[ \beta_v\le\frac{210\pi}{361|n_v|} \le\frac{330}{361}\,2^{-26} <\frac{3071}{3072}\,2^{-26} \le\frac{k_0}2\chi. \tag{53} \] Here \(\pi<22/7\), \(d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le1/(2|n_v|)\), and the displayed rational comparison prove (9) for every degree. This completes the corollary without a numerical scan or a threshold depending on the tree. The same proof gives a mixed condition, chosen independently at each vertex: \[ \boxed{\qquad d_v\ge2^{28}\quad\text{or}\quad |n_v|\ge2^{27} \qquad\text{for every }v.\qquad} \tag{53a} \] Under the degree alternative, \(\mathcal R_v^2\ge d_v^2\ge2^{56}\) proves the same two tail comparisons, while \[ \beta_v\le\frac{420\pi}{361d_v} \le\frac{330}{361}\,2^{-26} <\frac{k_0}2\chi \tag{53b} \] is the same outgoing patch bound. Neither alternative needs to hold uniformly over all vertices. In particular, the high-degree vertices may retain any fixed signed powers, including zero and small nonzero powers. No sum over the number of such vertices occurs. Here is a precise extension construction illustrating that freedom. Start with any fixed ordered circle-tree core whose original endpoint pairing closes to a knot and has no internal closed component. Retain all its fixed signed powers. At every core vertex choose one of its actual product slots next to its crossing box and insert a consecutive stack of an even number \(B\ge2^{28}\) of new terminal pieces. Every new leaf has a fixed odd power satisfying \[ |n_{\mathrm{leaf}}|\ge2^{27}+1. \tag{53c} \] The physical quarter-turn of an odd two-strand braid has diagonal pairing \(X=\{02,13\}\); this pairing is invariant under the quarter-turn. An even ordered stack of these leaves has the through pairing \(I=\{03,12\}\) and creates no internal circle. Inserting it in the specified slot therefore preserves the original local endpoint pairing in that actual frame. This is a pairing calculation, not an isotopy removing the new tangles. At the original closing box the same insertion takes place inside its local ball. An added terminal leaf may then be chosen as the recursive root using the original closed-collar move with its induced frame reversal and factor order retained. Thus the resulting diagram is again a knot, while its knot type may change. Each old vertex now satisfies the degree alternative and each new leaf satisfies the twist alternative in (53a). The resulting actual knot complement is hyperbolic and satisfies (10)–(12). The number and arrangement of prescribed short-power vertices are arbitrary but fixed; the number \(B\) does not depend on their total count. ![An even stack of added odd terminal tangles preserves the core's endpoint pairing.](../book/figures/directed-tree-volume.svg) The upper drawing is a tree of tangle operations, not a knot projection. Only one added pair is drawn at each original vertex. The construction inserts \(B/2\) consecutive pairs in one specified product slot, retaining the original cyclic order; \(B\ge2^{28}\) is even. Each added leaf has odd \(|m|\ge2^{27}+1\), and every tree edge applies the physical quarter-turn \(T\). The lower drawing forgets crossings and shows the literal endpoint pairings: two diagonal pairings compose to the through pairing. It does not claim that the new braids can be removed by an isotopy. ## 9. A star beyond both previous quantitative tests Consider an ordered star rooted at its central vertex, of odd degree \(d=30{,}000{,}001\). Set its power to 2 and every terminal power to the fixed odd integer \(2^{60}+1\). Choose \(c_v=k_0/2\) on every leaf. The knot pairing can be checked in the original terminal-root syntax, even though the finite contraction is evaluated from the center. Label the boundary points lower left, lower right, upper right, upper left by \(0,1,2,3\). The even and odd braid pairings are respectively \[ I=\{03,12\},\qquad X=\{02,13\};\qquad T(I)=H=\{01,23\},\quad T(X)=X. \tag{54a} \] At a terminal root there are \(d-1\) other leaves. Their turned odd braids have pairing \(X\); their ordered product has pairing \(I\) because \(d-1\) is even. The central power \(2\) preserves it. Its actual quarter-turn has pairing \(H\), and stacking the root's odd braid against \(H\) still gives \(H\), with no internal closed arc. Cylindrical closure joins \(03\) and \(12\), so it closes \(H\) into one component. All intermediate products before that last stack are two through-strand braids. There is no hidden internal component. The criterion can be verified by rational enclosures without expanding this large tree. All leaves have the same data. The center has approximately \[ \beta_o=1.219\,10^{-7},\qquad \eta_o=2.713\,10^{-7},\qquad \frac{\beta_o}{\eta_o/2}<0.9. \tag{54} \] Every leaf has a much smaller ratio. The root does not satisfy the nonroot patch inequality for any \(c>0\), because \(\beta_o>k_0\chi\). Nevertheless its exact final trace satisfies (8). Thus that outgoing patch must not be charged to a root that sends no message. Moreover \[ \sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2} >\frac{30,000,001}{30,000,001^2+4}>2^{-25}, \tag{55} \] and its maximum is far above \(2^{-120}\). The example therefore lies beyond both published quantitative alternatives. Its size and all its powers are fixed; it is not an N-growing family. The constant sizes are coarse, and no optimality assertion is intended. Here are rational enclosures proving the inequalities rather than inferring them from those decimal values. Put \[ \pi_- =3,\quad \pi_+=22/7,\quad c=k_0/2,\quad \chi_-=r_0^2/2-r_0^4/24,\quad \delta_- =\frac{c\chi_-}{4(1+c)}. \tag{56} \] At the central vertex use the conservative height \(y_* =\delta_-/2\). It is at most each branch of (6). For example, with \[ D_- =\frac d{2\pi_+},\quad D_+=\frac{d+1}{2\pi_-},\quad A_- =\frac{dc}{\pi_+^2},\quad C_+=d+\frac{\pi_-^{-2}}{4A_-}, \tag{57} \] the three non-strip comparisons are \[ y_*<\frac{t_0D_-}{4C_+},\qquad y_*<\frac{dc}{8(1+t_0D_+)},\qquad y_*^2<\frac c8. \tag{58} \] The strip comparison follows from \(\delta\ge\delta_-\). Every quantity in (56)–(58) is rational. Direct cross-multiplication also gives \[ \frac{2[420\pi_+d/(361(d^2+4))]} {t_0D_-y_*/2}<\frac9{10}, \qquad 2\frac{420\pi_+d}{361(d^2+4)} <\min\left\{\frac{dc}{2},\ A_-r_0^2, \frac{D_-r_0^2}{8}\right\}. \tag{59} \] These compare the upper bound for twice the first-charge drop with all four lower bounds for \(\eta_o\). The charge cutoff is greater than two. For a leaf with \(n=2^{60}+1\), take \(y_*=t_0k_0/(2n)\). The same direct rational comparisons, using \(D_-=n/(2\pi_+)\), \(D_+=(n+1)/(2\pi_-)\), \(A_-=2k_0/\pi_+^2\), and \(C_+=16+[n/(2\pi_-)]^2/(4A_-)\), put this height below each branch of (6). They give a lower bound greater than \(2^{-49}\) for every entry of (7), while \(\beta_v<2^{-117}\). The outgoing patch follows from \(\beta_v<(k_0/2)\chi_-\). This proves the leaf inequalities. ## 10. Reproducing the finite arithmetic and pairings From the repository root run: python3 experiments/audit_actual_all_circle_directed_volume.py The [script](../experiments/audit_actual_all_circle_directed_volume.py) writes [its results](../experiments/actual_all_circle_directed_volume_results.json). An optional --output selects a different JSON file. It uses exact rational arithmetic for the constant inequalities, the all-degree corollaries and the star enclosures. It also constructs the literal four-endpoint pairings and checks the composition and closure identities used above. Those are finite checks, not numerical evidence for the asymptotic theorem. The proof of the full invariant estimates is the conditional kernel and trace induction in sections 2–7. The earlier [exact tree-message reproduction](../experiments/audit_all_circle_local_message_recursion.py) independently compares canonical quotient contractions with root-grid and complete first-normal traces; the present argument retains those same finite identities.

title: The geometric longitude of a tree of crossing circles
status: Geometric longitude and selected classical factor for circle trees
text:
# The geometric longitude of a tree of crossing circles The edge equations of a tree of crossing circles determine a representation of its link exterior. They determine the auxiliary meridians and longitudes directly. This note identifies the main preferred longitude: its eigenvalue is the product of the edge factors, with the monomial prescribed by the original zero framing. The construction retains the ordered tangles, crossing disks and their primitive peripheral curves. The half twist at a disk is inserted through its full two-generator boundary action. Merely exchanging three ideal vertices while retaining the old white-face maps would give a false gluing away from the parabolic main meridian. This is a geometric and algebraic identification. It does not extend a quantum asymptotic theorem to arbitrary short fillings. ## 1. The diagram and the longitude identity Take a finite tree with at least one edge. At each vertex \(v\), place one two-strand crossing-circle tangle, whose auxiliary circle bounds the specified twice-punctured disk. Retain a crossing \(R^{\epsilon_v}\), with \(\epsilon_v\in\{-1,0,1\}\). Every edge is an actual quarter-turn attachment between ordered stacks. The product order, rotations of the tangle balls, endpoint frames and cylindrical closing map are part of the diagram. There are no product junctions without their own crossing circle. Write \(\mathcal E\) for its set of edges. The [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) constructs two projection balls from this literal diagram. Each original edge contributes two octahedra. At each circle their disk-side pages are joined in the original cyclic order, with its retained half twist on one distinguished seam. Assume the main strands form one component, and orient that knot. Let \(\mu_K\) be its positive meridian and \(\lambda_{\mathrm{aug}}\) its preferred longitude in the augmented exterior. Use the main eigenvalue parameter \(M\). The source flag is the \(M^{-1}\) eigenline; the longitude coordinate below is its inverse eigenvalue, equivalently the eigenvalue on the \(M\) line. At auxiliary circle \(v\), the selected eigenvalue of the original primitive disk longitude is \(-Q_v\), so its projective similarity is \(Q_v^2\). Write \(U_v\) for the logarithm of its primitive meridian similarity at that auxiliary flag. For each edge \(e=vw\), introduce \(X_e\) and impose \[ (X_e+Q_v)(X_e+Q_v^{-1})(X_e+Q_w)(X_e+Q_w^{-1}) =(X_e-1)^2(1-X_eM^2)(1-X_e/M^2). 	ag{T1} \] Choose the branch through \(M=Q_v=1\), \(X_e=i\). Set \[ ho_{v,e}= rac{Q_v+X_e}{1+Q_vX_e},\qquad f_e= rac{M^2-X_e}{1-M^2X_e}. 	ag{T2} \] All rational identities are read on their regular open sets and then continued on the same irreducible source variety. Clearing a denominator does not add a new geometric branch. **Theorem.** Equations (T1) give a representation of the original augmented exterior near its marked complete structure. Its primitive auxiliary similarities are \[ \exp U_v=Q_v^{-\epsilon_v} \prod_{e
i v}ho_{v,e}. 	ag{T3} \] If \(w_\epsilon\) is the oriented writhe of the retained crossings and \(a_{\mathrm{aug}}=-w_\epsilon-\sum_v\epsilon_v\), then \[ L_{\mathrm{aug}}^2 =M^{2a_{\mathrm{aug}}}\prod_e f_e^2. 	ag{T4} \] Fill circle \(v\) on its original primitive slope \(\mu_v+p_v\lambda_v\), with \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\). The exponentiated filling equations are \[ \prod_{e
i v}ho_{v,e}=Q_v^{n_v}. 	ag{T5} \] Where \(Q_v^2
e1\) for every filled circle, these equations make each filling word projectively trivial, so the representation factors through the filled group. On that locus its preferred longitude satisfies \[ L_{\mathrm{fill}}^2=M^{2a(D)}\prod_e f_e^2,\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v. 	ag{T6} \] Here \(w(D)\) is the writhe of the original filled diagram. The squared formula is also an identity for the corresponding peripheral word on the augmented source variety. At \(Q_v=\pm1\), equation (T5) alone need not kill a nontrivial parabolic filling word, so that word identity does not by itself give a representation of the filled group. On a connected germ anchored at a complete hyperbolic filled knot point supplied by the existing marked completion theorem, the determinant-one sign is fixed: \[  oxed{\displaystyle L_{\mathrm{fill}} =-M^{a(D)}\prod_e rac{M^2-X_e}{1-M^2X_e}.} 	ag{T7} \] This is the geometric longitude of the original knot complement. It uses its preferred meridian and longitude; it is not a longitude of a different comparison diagram. The complete anchor and the primitive logarithmic filling marks are retained in section 5. The proof first establishes the squared identity, without a choice of global determinant-one lift, and then fixes the sign by a Seifert-surface frame calculation in section 10. The algebraic constant-field lemma also holds for finite simple graphs; the geometric theorem here is restricted to the literal ordered trees. ## 2. The local face maps We first construct the two-octahedron piece with its original white and shaded face labels. In this section \(E_0\) is a preliminary white-face coordinate, and \(X\) is the edge variable in (T1). Their distinction matters when \(M
e1\). ### 2.1. The parameters and the actual faces Write \(M\) for the main meridian eigenvalue parameter and set \(m=M^2\). The symbols \(Q\) and \(P\) are the chosen square roots of the two auxiliary longitude similarities. All parameters are near \((m,Q,P)=(1,1,1)\). We use \(E_0\) for a white-face coordinate, near \(i\). The effective-action wire coordinate will be denoted \(X\). The two projection copies have six ideal vertices \[  egin{array}{c|c|c} &	ext{equator}&	ext{circle apices}\ \hline +&(0,\infty,1,R)&(A,B)\ -&(0,\infty,1,S)&(a,b). \end{array} 	ag{N1} \] The four white identifications are the unique maps of the ordered triangles \[  egin{aligned} W_0:(A,0,\infty)&\longmapsto(a,0,\infty),& W_1:(B,\infty,1)&\longmapsto(b,\infty,1),\ W_2:(A,1,R)&\longmapsto(a,1,S),& W_3:(B,R,0)&\longmapsto(b,S,0). \end{aligned} 	ag{N2} \] These are the face labels of the original two-leaf cut. Changing the minus equator from \(R\) to \(S\) is necessary: retaining the old four white matrices would keep all four main meridians parabolic. Put \(L=E_0^{-1}\), and define \[  egin{gathered} S= rac{m^2R}{1+(m^2-1)R},\qquad \ell_1=L/m,\quad \ell_2=L/m^2,\quad \ell_3=Lm,\ c_2= rac{\ell_2(R-1)/(S-1)-1}{R-1},\qquad c_3= rac{\ell_3R/S-1}{R},\ W_0= egin{pmatrix}L&0\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad W_1= egin{pmatrix}\ell_1&1-\ell_1\0&1\end{pmatrix},\ W_2= egin{pmatrix}c_2+\ell_2&1-c_2-\ell_2\c_2&1-c_2\end{pmatrix}, \qquad W_3= egin{pmatrix}\ell_3&0\c_3&1\end{pmatrix}. \end{gathered} 	ag{N3} \] Thus \(W_2(z)=1+\ell_2(z-1)/(1+c_2(z-1))\). Every map sends its two equatorial vertices in (N2) correctly. If \(q=(0,\infty,1,R)\), the native main corner word \(W_{j-1}^{-1}W_j\) fixes \(q_j\) and has local derivative \[ (m^{-1},m,m^{-1},m)_j. 	ag{N4} \] At infinity the local coordinate is \(1/z\). To derive (N3), start with \(W_0(z)=Lz\). The derivatives at infinity, 1 and 0 give respectively \(\ell_1=L/m,\ell_2=L/m^2,\ell_3=Lm\). The remaining derivative at \(R\), on its branch through the complete chart, gives the displayed formula for \(S\). This supplies the actual peripheral condition, not just equal traces. ### 2.2. The auxiliary longitude equations and the local gluing locus Take \[ A= rac{mE_0+Q}{m+Q},\qquad B= rac{P(1-mE_0)}{P+m},\qquad a=A/E_0,\qquad b=1+ rac{B-1}{E_0m}=- rac{B}{E_0P}. 	ag{N5} \] There are two expressions for the equatorial coordinate: \[  egin{aligned} R_v&= rac{(mE_0+Q)(mE_0Q+1)} {E_0m(Q^2+1)+2E_0Qm^2+Q(1-m^2)},\ R_w&=- rac{P(mE_0-1)^2} {E_0m^2(P^2+1)+2E_0Pm+P(m^2-1)}. \end{aligned} 	ag{N6} \] The first is exactly \(W_2(A)=a\); the second is exactly \(W_3(B)=b\). Their common value is \(R\). For completeness, the longitude choices made here can be obtained before solving for the apices. The first longitude is \(W_2^{-1}W_0\). Its similarity in the coordinate with \(A\) at infinity is \(W_2'(A)/L\), and is prescribed as \(Q^2\). The chosen square-root branch is \(1+c_2(A-1)=-1/(mQ)\). At the other circle the longitude is \(W_1^{-1}W_3\), with similarity \(\ell_1/W_3'(B)=P^2\), and the chosen branch is \(1+c_3B=-mP\). Substitution gives (N5)--(N6). Both signs equal \(-1\) at completeness. Clearing the nonzero denominators of \(R_v-R_w\), and removing the factor \(E_0m^2\), gives \[  egin{aligned} G={}&E_0^2P^2Qm^2+E_0^2PQ^2m+2E_0^2PQm^2+2E_0^2PQm +E_0^2Pm+E_0^2Qm^2\ &+E_0P^2Q^2m+E_0P^2m-4E_0PQm+E_0Q^2m+E_0m\ &+P^2Q+PQ^2m+2PQm+2PQ+Pm+Q. \end{aligned} 	ag{N7} \] The local gluing equation is \(G=0\). At \(m=Q=P=1\), \(G=8(E_0^2+1)\), so \(G_{E_0}(i,1,1,1)=16i\). It follows that there is a unique holomorphic branch \(E_0\) near \(i\). Every denominator displayed above is nonzero on a sufficiently small neighborhood of this branch. The pure shaded maps in the two plus-copy circle frames are \[ S_v(A,R)=  egin{pmatrix}0&RA(1-A)\A-R&R-A^2\end{pmatrix},\qquad S_w(B,R)=  egin{pmatrix}B(B-1)&-RB(B-1)\B-R&R-B\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{N8} \] The first fixes \(A\) and sends \(\infty\) to \(0\) and \(1\) to \(R\). If \(a_j\in\mathbb Q(q,M)\), perform the denominator clearing over \(\mathbb Q\). Contract the same germ prime to \(\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]\). It is again nonzero, contains no polynomial in \(M\) alone, and has height one. If \(A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb Q}\) is its irreducible generator, then \[ A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb Q}\mid P_0 \quad	ext{over }\mathbb Q. 	ag{O18} \] Its complex factorization contains the selected geometric factor and any conjugate components forced by the rational coefficient field. A particular complex component need not itself be defined over \(\mathbb Q\). The conclusion applies to every specified genuine annihilator, including a minimal one if one is chosen. It does not identify the whole classical symbol with the full A-polynomial, compare entire operator ideals, or determine factor multiplicities. It also asserts no fixed-\(M
e1\) quantum asymptotic by substituting \(s\) of order \(N\), and no uniform nonvanishing through ordinary resonances. This proof treats ordered circle trees. The [strict-tree extension](actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) now handles product junctions without crossing circles by inserting a zero-crossing box and proving exact elimination after meridian filling. It therefore extends the geometric-factor conclusion to every strict presentation in the full-source theorem, and carries the intrinsic result through the covered net-twist and closure reductions. The additional volume cases in the directed criterion still require their own all-orders shifted-chart argument before they can be added to this operator statement.

title: Completing the crossing-circle fillings and calibrating their volume
status: Primitive smooth filling and calibrated knot volume
text: # Completing the crossing-circle fillings and calibrating their volume 1 November 2026. The octahedral cells of an ordered tree of crossing circles stay positive while their angular longitude parameters vary in a fixed small disk. This note proves that the parameter path selected by the analytic filling equations completes those cells to the actual filled link exterior. It follows the full logarithmic period of each primitive filling curve, so the completed meridian makes exactly one turn at the endpoint. It then identifies the absolute volume with the continued critical action. The [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) supplies the original topology and primitive curves. The [angular charts](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) supply the positive cells and their exact face maps. The [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) supplies the path under the explicit bound in (4). Together these establish the geometric part of the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md). Only the original crossing circles are filled; the main knot cusp remains complete and unfilled. ## 1. Exact topological and local inputs Fix a finite circle-only Conway tree with at least two circle vertices. Every edge is a physical quarter-turn and every vertex is an original crossing circle. Keep its actual ribbon orders, projection-copy labels, half twists and primitive disk curves. The [ordered cut theorem](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) supplies three marked facts. - The original projection and disk-page cuts give two octahedra per edge, with the six vertices and face maps of the literal two-leaf [angular chart](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md). Any transported corner permutations and projection-copy changes are retained. - At each original circle, outgoing and incoming pages are joined in their actual cyclic order. The retained half twist occurs at its distinguished original seam. The face maps keep their full three-point labels. - The disk longitude is the boundary loop with period \(V_v=2i\tau_v\). The original meridian concatenates the local meridional page paths, with the single half-longitude shear \(-\epsilon_vV_v/2\). These are the original primitive curves. Physical \(T^{-1}\), \(T\), and retained planar half-turns are not identified by source involutivity. Reversing a disk frame reverses both its paths and its peripheral coordinate. All formulas below use the fixed original disk basis. The local positive eight-tetrahedron chart is valid on \[ |\tau_v|,|\tau_w|\le10^{-2}. \tag{1} \] Its incoming pants edge ratios are \((-Q^{-1},-Q,-Q^{-1})\), and its outgoing ratios are their inverses, where \(Q=e^{i\tau_v}\). Thus the marked seam cancels the full complex shears, and its two interior-angle branches sum to \(2\pi\). This includes both projection copies. At zero these are the two regular octahedra in the actual two-leaf cut. ## 2. The analytic path and the actual peripheral formulas Let \(F_0\) be the complete positive action, normalized so that \(2\pi F_0\) is the volume of the original augmented exterior. There are two regular octahedra per tree edge at completeness. Let \[ \Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)=\sum_{\{v,w\}}\psi(\tau_v,\tau_w), \qquad \Psi(0)=F_0, \qquad \psi_{\tau_v}=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh} \bigl(\tan(\tau_v/2)\cos(\tau_w/2)\bigr). \tag{2} \] The local action is separately even, with its complete branch and constant. Fix the original signs \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,\pm1\}\), integral fillings \(p_v\), and powers \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\). The [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) supplies an analytic first-charge path \(\boldsymbol\tau(c)\), \(0\le c\le1\), with \[ \Psi_{\tau_v}+\frac{i n_v\tau_v}{2\pi}-ic=0,\qquad \boldsymbol\tau(0)=0,\qquad |\tau_v(c)|<10^{-2},\qquad \Im\tau_v(c)<0\quad(c>0). \tag{3} \] Write \(D_v\) for the circle-tree degree. The sufficient condition and pointwise bound are \[ \sum_v\frac{D_v}{D_v^2+n_v^2}\le2^{-25},\qquad |\tau_v(c)|\le \frac{2\pi c}{(1-1/50)\sqrt{D_v^2+n_v^2}}, \tag{4} \] The common bound is less than \(0.00111\), inside (1). The geometric proof only uses the explicit path properties (3). In a pure local block the small meridional increment is \(-2\pi\psi_{\tau_v}\). The ordered cut theorem consequently gives the original peripheral logarithms \[ U_v=-2\pi\Psi_{\tau_v}-i\epsilon_v\tau_v, \qquad V_v=2i\tau_v. \tag{5} \] Their exponentials are the actual holonomy multipliers. Section 4 proves that the chosen lifts are also the actual log-link periods. The stationary equation gives \[ U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi ic. \tag{6} \] The primitive basis is not reset when \(U_v\) approaches \(-2\pi i\). ## 3. Positive metric on the cut-and-glued exterior Realize every local block by its positive tetrahedra and perform the original identifications in Section 1. Within a block the rational face identities retain the full edge return map. At a page seam the inverse ratios give both zero shear and angle \(2\pi\), not only equality of multiplier moduli. Their branches are continued from the complete cells. At the distinguished odd seam use the original cross-copy maps, rather than the pure inverse-ratio identification. In the local leaf frame of the angular chart they are \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}R&-R\\1&ER-1-E\end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}R/E-1-1/E&R\\-1&R\end{pmatrix}. \tag{6a} \] They send respectively \((Z,\infty,1)\) to \((Z/E,R,0)\) and \((Z,R,0)\) to \((Z/E,\infty,1)\). Thus they specify all three ideal vertices and the actual exchange of projection copies. With the four original white maps \(W_j\), direct multiplication gives the full projective edge returns \[ W_0^{-1}BW_2^{-1}A=I,\qquad W_2^{-1}BW_0^{-1}A=I,\qquad W_1^{-1}BW_3^{-1}A=I. \tag{6b} \] These are identities under \(Z^2-(1+E)Z+ER=0\), not modulus comparisons. The incoming and outgoing marked pants structures depend only on their common \(Q=e^{i\tau_v}\), by the local edge-ratio calculation. Transport each to the same ordered three-vertex pants chart. Equations (6a)–(6b) then give the same odd seam between any two incident blocks, even when their far-end parameters differ. The allowed puncture exchange is exactly the one in (6a), not an arbitrary pants permutation. Every resulting edge has its complete angle branch \(2\pi\), by positivity and continuation from zero. The two physical signs retain their distinct primitive words and the single correction in (5). This gives a nonsingular local hyperbolic metric at every finite point of the original exterior. Face pairings are isometries, edge links have angle \(2\pi\) and identity return, and a finite subdivision vertex has a nonsingular spherical metric on its topological sphere link. Its complete local spherical development is the ordinary sphere. No global injectivity of the developing map is assumed. The actual horospherical triangles form a nonsingular similarity structure on each topological cusp torus. Main puncture holonomies are the nontrivial parabolics of the local pants and remain so in the fixed local charts. The actual primitive main meridian is one of these local words. Its commutant is the translation group at its flag. Hence each main torus has a complete Euclidean translation link. For \(c>0\), (3) and (5) give \[ \Re V_v=-2\Im\tau_v>0. \tag{7} \] The auxiliary peripheral group has a nonunit dilation and a second common fixed point \(q_v\). Its nonsingular similarity development misses \(q_v\). Indeed \((z-q_v)\partial_z\) is a globally invariant vector field; each possible zero has index \(+1\), whereas the total index on a torus is zero. On the simply connected link cover put \[ f_v=\log(\operatorname{dev}_v-q_v). \tag{8} \] Its real derivative is invertible. The metric \(|df_v|^2\) descends to a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the compact torus, and is complete. Geodesic path lifting makes \(f_v\) a covering of the Euclidean plane; since the plane is simply connected, it is a diffeomorphism. Its periods form an injective real rank-two lattice. ## 4. The periods throughout the charge path Let \(P_{\mu_v},P_{\lambda_v}\) be the actual periods of (8) on the retained primitive paths. Their exponentials are the actual peripheral multipliers, so \[ P_{\mu_v}-U_v,\quad P_{\lambda_v}-V_v \in2\pi i\mathbb Z. \tag{9} \] These differences are continuous for \(0<c\le1\). The link remains nonsingular, its development avoids the second fixed point, and the paths and flags are retained. Choose a logarithm at one basepoint and transport it continuously; rebasing adds a constant and does not change a period. The initial integers can be fixed directly from the complete charts. Choose a peripheral frame depending continuously on the selected flag and sending it to infinity. Write the longitude as \(z\mapsto a(c)z+b(c)\), with \(a(c)=e^{V_v(c)}\). At completeness \(a(0)=1\) and \(b(0)\ne0\), since the original primitive longitude is a nonzero translation in the complete torus. For \(c>0\), (7) makes \(a(c)\ne1\), and its second fixed point is \(q_v(c)=b(c)/(1-a(c))\). Thus \(|q_v(c)|\to\infty\). For this fixed finite tree, the developed fixed-generator paths remain in one bounded region and have bounded Euclidean lengths as \(c\downarrow0\). They use finitely many actual triangles and transition maps, all continuous in the complete charts. If their images lie in \(|z|\le B\) and their lengths are at most \(L\), their actual logarithmic increments obey \[ |P_\gamma(c)|\le\frac{L}{|q_v(c)|-B}\longrightarrow0. \tag{9a} \] Meanwhile (5) gives \(U_v,V_v\to0\). Each integer difference in (9) is therefore zero for sufficiently small \(c\), and hence on all of \((0,1]\). This fixes the winding without importing a small-neighborhood completion theorem or resetting principal logs at the endpoint. Equivalently, each page increment in (5) is small in its local two-leaf chart. Changes of a pants frame add logarithmic constants at the ends of a page path; those constants telescope around the circle. Its meridian accumulates the sum of the actual increments, even when high degree makes that sum close to \(-2\pi i\). The preceding continuity argument fixes the possible integer. The actual slope period is thus \(-2\pi ic\). Its complementary primitive curve is the original longitude: the determinant of \((\mu_v+p_v\lambda_v,\lambda_v)\) in the original basis is one. Its positive core translation length is \[ \ell_v=\Re V_v=-2\Im\tau_v. \tag{10} \] ## 5. Cone completion and the smooth endpoint The geometric end contains all sufficiently high vertical rays over its similarity triangles. Send its fixed points to zero and infinity, put \(r=y/|z|\), and use \[ R=\operatorname{arsinh}(1/r),\quad \theta=\Im f_v,\quad X=\Re f_v+\tfrac12\log(1+r^2). \tag{11} \] The metric is exactly \[ dR^2+\cosh^2R\,dX^2+\sinh^2R\,d\theta^2. \tag{12} \] Compactness of the actual similarity link shows that the end contains a whole punctured tube \(0<R<R_0\). Its primitive meridian period is \(-2\pi ic\), and its independent longitude has positive real part (10). Adding the axis produces a cone solid torus of angle \(2\pi c\), with the specified topological meridian. At \(c=1\) it is an ordinary smooth solid torus. Main cusps remain complete horoball quotients, and the remaining middle is compact. Thus the \(c=1\) metric is complete and has finite volume on the original filled topology. The complete universal local development covers simply connected hyperbolic space, so the resulting representation is the geometric holonomy. When the original component test gives one main component, the metric is on that original knot complement. Its main cusp is unfilled. The intermediate cone description makes no discreteness claim for \(0<c<1\). It records the positive metric and its actual link completion; smoothness is asserted at \(c=1\). ## 6. Absolute action and the primitive normalization The calibration can be derived on this explicit geometric block family. It does not require choosing an unmarked character component by comparison of its derivatives at one point. Put \(U_v^0=-2\pi\Psi_{\tau_v}\) and \[ G^0=2\pi i\left(\Psi-\sum_v\tau_v\Psi_{\tau_v}\right). \tag{13} \] Direct differentiation gives \[ dG^0=\tfrac12\sum_vV_v\,dU_v^0. \tag{14} \] The actual half twist changes \(U_v^0\) to \(U_v=U_v^0-\epsilon_vV_v/2\). Its marked primitive is therefore \[ G=G^0-\sum_v\frac{\epsilon_vV_v^2}{8} =2\pi i\left(\Psi-\sum_v\tau_v\Psi_{\tau_v}\right) +\sum_v\frac{\epsilon_v\tau_v^2}{2}. \tag{15} \] This is exactly the source Legendre transform with its complete constant. In particular \(\Im G(0)=2\pi F_0\). The original boundary fundamental-chain differential, applied to these actual positive blocks and their marked paths, gives \[ \operatorname{Vol}(\rho) =\Im G-\tfrac12\sum_v\Re U_v\Im V_v. \tag{16} \] The constant is fixed at the complete assembly. Every local shape stays in a simply connected positive neighborhood of \(i\), and Section 4 retains the actual period lifts. No volume period is reset. The positive tetrahedral volume sum also shows directly that the volume tends to \(2\pi F_0\) as \(c\downarrow0\). Define the stationary charge action \[ \mathcal C(c)=\operatorname*{stat}_{\boldsymbol\tau} \left[\Psi+\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_vn_v\tau_v^2 -ic\sum_v\tau_v\right]. \tag{17} \] At its critical point, set \(\Phi=G/(2\pi i)\). Substitution of (3) gives the exact cancellation \[ \Phi-\mathcal C(c)=-\frac{i}{2\pi}\sum_vp_v\tau_v^2, \qquad \tfrac12\Re U_v\Im V_v=p_v\Im(\tau_v^2). \tag{18} \] Consequently \[ \operatorname{Vol}_c =2\pi\Re\mathcal C(c). \tag{19} \] The primitive normalization has an independent differential check: \[ \frac{d}{dc}\,2\pi\Re\mathcal C(c) =2\pi\sum_v\Im\tau_v. \tag{20} \] The core is represented by the complementary primitive curve \(\lambda_v\), its length is (10), and its cone angle is \(2\pi c\). The finite-cell Schläfli differential \(-\tfrac12\sum_v\ell_v\,d(2\pi c)\) gives (20). This checks the factor and sign; (19) already follows from the marked regulator and the complete anchor, without cone rigidity. At \(c=1\), (19) identifies the actual analytic first-charge rate with the original smooth filled volume. The ordered topological theorem and the analytic criterion supply the topology and path (3) used in this proof. The finite-source dominance and its exact normalization are proved in the [analytic theorem](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md). ## 7. Scope of the completion The metric argument permits large global meridian logs while every edge block remains uniformly close to its regular geometry. It does not require a globally small framed-representation norm. The conclusion applies to the ordered all-circle trees of Section 1 under (4), or more generally whenever their actual analytic path satisfies (3). It does not assert that every bounded crossing power gives a hyperbolic filling. The degree-weighted bound permits some small powers because the resulting local angular changes remain small while the primitive meridian is assembled from many sectors. The [preferred-cusp continuation](actual_all_circle_preferred_cusp.md) also follows the actual main longitude through this family. Its marking is established by the original face words and surgery homology. The complete geometric and analytic conclusions are collected in the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md).

title: A volume theorem with a twist bound independent of the number of tangles
text: # A volume theorem with a twist bound independent of the number of tangles A knot in this theorem is built from a finite ordered tree of integer two-strand braids. Turn each child tangle through a quarter-turn before stacking it on its specified side of the parent braid. Close at a terminal vertex by the prescribed cylindrical closure. Each vertex, including each terminal vertex, has its own crossing circle in the augmented diagram. The [construction and strand test](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md#the-knot-construction) fix the endpoint orders and require that all the main strands form one knot, with no additional component closed inside a tangle. The number of vertices, their degrees, and the nesting depth may be arbitrary. We prove a sufficient condition at each vertex that does not depend on any of those global quantities. Write \(d_v\) for the number of incident tree edges and \(n_v\) for the signed number of half-twists in its braid. If \[ \max_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}\le2^{-120}, \] then the original knot complement is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] In particular, requiring every \(|n_v|\ge2^{119}\) suffices for every finite tree in this construction. This very coarse constant is a sufficient bound, not an estimate of the shortest twists for which the equality holds. The tree and all powers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The proof evaluates a subtree while leaving its attaching edge unevaluated. The result is a polynomial in the variable at the parent vertex. Dividing by its value at zero factors out the contribution already supplied by that subtree. When the next crossing trace is taken, its error can therefore be compared with the change at that one vertex. The proof below establishes the nonvanishing needed for this division and bounds the entire finite polynomial, including its high indices and repeated-root derivatives. The earlier [summed criterion](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) remains useful and has a much better numerical constant. The two criteria are alternatives. The local criterion removes a restriction on the total number of vertices; it does not subsume the earlier criterion for every individual diagram. ## 1. The theorem and its finite-source inputs Fix an ordered circle-only tree with at least one edge, its actual strand frames, retained signs, disk markings and integer powers \(n_v\). Its original closed main strands must form a knot. Let \(d_v\) be the graph degree. Define \[ \kappa=\max_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}. \tag{1} \] The sufficient local condition proved below is \[ \kappa\le 2^{-120}. \tag{2} \] The number of vertices is arbitrary but fixed before the quantum level tends to infinity. Constants in polynomial prefactors, error constants and starting levels may depend on that entire fixed tree. The numerical condition (2) does not. Under (2), the exact reduced zero-framed invariant has the same nonzero first-charge asymptotic and microscopic profile as in the published all-circle theorem: \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1+O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-1}),\qquad |s|\le R<1, \tag{3} \] \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|F_N(q_N^s)| \longrightarrow 2\pi\Re\mathcal C(\mathbf1). \tag{4} \] Here \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_vn_v. \tag{5} \] Every factor in (5) has its original normalization. Both parities, all sufficiently large composite levels, and all fixed signed powers satisfying (2) are included. The analytic conclusion (3)--(4) is proved here. For its volume interpretation use the already published ordered octahedral decomposition, angular charts and primitive completion. Their explicit positive-path hypotheses follow from the simultaneous contraction recorded in Section 7 below; they do not require the sum condition once such a path has been supplied. The same selected action therefore equals the volume of the original knot complement. This last implication uses the actual marked completion, not a source identity. The finite identities and estimates used below are: * [bounds for the full polynomial source](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Sections 1.1--1.4: complete Newton coordinates, full value/derivative norm, fixed crossing power and typed turn; * [the exact crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md), Sections 2--4: the exact translated-grid trace, Fourier coefficients, complete normal limits, and endpoint currents; * [the summed finite-sum estimate](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md), Sections 3--8: the single-edge index gap, canonical edge interpolation, explicit edge action and its derivative bounds; * [uniform Newton estimates](all_circle_uniform_newton_bounds.md): the original real and complex Newton estimates; * [the sum over internal edge indices](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md): the fixed Gamma interpolation and insertion rule. The estimates below use these exact identities on each finite subtree. No assumed dominance of a global saddle is an input. ## 2. The full finite kernel and exact recursion ![The parent variable remains free while the crossing trace evaluates the current vertex and its child subtree polynomials.](../book/figures/tree-boundary-message.png) Each triangle in the drawing represents a subtree, whose evaluation is a polynomial in the current angle \(t\). The edge to the parent is the only factor containing its angle \(u\). Put \(d=N-1\), \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), and \[ S_k=\prod_{r=1}^k2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{j<k}(c_j-z). \tag{6} \] The fixed pairing is \(\phi_\sigma(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}\). A physical turn, after lowering this pairing, identifies equal indices and retains \(\gamma_e(s)H_N(s)/W_k(s)\). Thus define \[ K_N(t,u;s)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_k(s)}. \tag{7} \] This is the full kernel, not the regular-window truncation. It is an even trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in each variable. The paired factors and their inverses are bounded uniformly in \(k,N\) on every fixed disk \(R<1\). Choose a terminal root. For a nonroot vertex \(v\), its message to the parent angle \(u\) is the exact polynomial \[ M_{v,N}(u)= \gamma_{e_v}(s)\, \mathcal D_{n_v,\sigma_v,N}^{(t)} \left[K_N(t,u;s)\prod_{w\text{ child of }v}M_{w,N}(t)\right]. \tag{8} \] The physical trace \(\mathcal D\) includes the full crossing scalar. The actual \(\sigma_v\) is \(s,-s\), or \(0\), according to the ordered pair. The reference monodromy factors remain outside in the same ledger as the published theorem. Formula (8) follows by expanding the original covariant contraction and doing finite sums in a different order. It does not commute physical tangles. At the root the final trace is \[ Z_N= \mathcal D_{n_0,\sigma_0,N}^{(t)} \left[\prod_{w\text{ child of }0}M_{w,N}(t)\right]. \tag{9} \] The original closing/framing factor, prescribed reference factors, and one reduced cut factor \(H_N(s)\) multiply (9). There is no discarded-source remainder in (8)--(9). Every original normal channel and every \(0\le k<N\) is still present. In particular \(M_{v,N}\) is always an even trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in its parent variable, regardless of the size of the subtree. This is seen directly from (7): the trace and all child operations act only in \(t\). ## 3. Two full-kernel bounds Use the following constants: \[ r=2^{-12},\quad c_K=2^{-16},\quad c=2^{-18}, \quad y_0=2^{-56},\quad \rho=2^{-14},\quad t_0=2^{-16}. \tag{10} \] All bounds allow polynomial factors in \(N\), depending on \(R\). Let \(G_0=g(1/4)\), and let \(\psi(t,u)\) be the published edge action, with \(\psi(0,0)=2G_0\). First, for real \(t,u\in[-\pi,\pi]\), \[ |K_N(t,u;s)| \le C_RN^{A_R} \exp N\{2G_0-c_K[(1-\cos t)+(1-\cos u)]\}. \tag{11} \] To prove this, split (7) into \(k/N\in I=[1/5,3/10]\) and its complement. On \(I\), the published product bound gives a factor \(\exp[-\alpha N\sin^2(t/2)]\) at each end, with \(\alpha>1/250\). The positive endpoint sum has rate \(2G_0\) and a polynomial prefactor. Outside \(I\), full Hermite interpolation gives a real sup bound with the single-edge loss \(\eta_K=\pi/200\), including high indices. Since \(4c_K<\eta_K\) and \(c_K<\alpha/2\), both pieces satisfy (11). Second, for complex \(|u|\le r\), real \(|t|\le\pi\), and \(|y|\le y_0\), \[ |K_N(t+iy,u;s)| \le C_RN^{A_R} \exp N\{\Re\psi(0,u)-c_K(1-\cos t)+16y^2\}. \tag{12} \] This conditional normalization is essential. Replacing \(\Re\psi(0,u)\) by \(2G_0+O(r^2)\) would introduce an unnecessary error larger than some of the later local tail losses. Here are the details. The complementary kernel, by the polynomial ellipse bound at each end, is at most \[ C_RN^{A_R} \exp N\{2G_0-\eta_K+|y|+|\Im u|\}. \tag{13} \] Since \(|\psi(0,u)-2G_0|\le r^2\), its fixed gap absorbs the entire claimed angular loss in (12), uniformly in \(t\). Indeed \(r+r^2+y_0+2c_K<\eta_K/2\). For the retained kernel and \(|t|\le1/8\), the published exact edge-sum saddle is uniform on \(|t+iy|,|u|\le1/4\). The exact formula for \(\psi_{tt}\) gives \[ |\psi_{tt}+1/(2\pi)|\le \frac1{50}\frac1{2\pi}. \tag{14} \] Separate evenness implies \(\psi_t(0,u)=0\). Integrating (14) on the segment from zero to \(t+iy\) proves a stronger version of the exponent in (12). Its polynomial amplitude and its exponentially small lattice currents are retained. For \(|t|\ge1/8\), use the explicit global bound \[ |e_k(-2\cos(t+iy))| \le e^2e_k(-2)e^{N[-\alpha\sin^2(t/2)+11y^2]}. \tag{15} \] The product at the other end satisfies \(|e_k(-2\cos u)|\le e_k(-2)e^{Nr^2}\) on \(I\): the normalized product factors have denominators \(\cos^2((j+1/2)\pi/N)\ge1/3\), and \(|\sin(u/2)|^2<r^2/3\). The additional change from \(2G_0\) to \(\Re\psi(0,u)\) costs at most another \(r^2\). Now \[ 2r^2<\frac{\alpha}{2}\sin^2(1/16),\qquad c_K<\alpha/4. \tag{16} \] These inequalities prove (12) on the remaining real angles. The first follows already from \(\alpha>1/250\), \(\sin(1/16)>1/(8\pi)\), and \(\pi^2<10\). No quadratic complex bound for an individual high basis element has been used in this argument. On the small bidisk \(|t|,|u|\le r\), the full kernel also has the same nonzero analytic saddle expansion as its retained part. The complementary estimate (13) has a fixed gap there. In particular, \[ K_N(t,u;s)=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u) e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O_R(N^{-1})), \tag{17} \] with the paired insertion included in the error and with the published exact midpoint normalization. The leading \(a_e\) is holomorphic and nonzero on a slightly larger disk. The outside \(\gamma_e(s)\) in (8) is not included in \(a_e\). ## 4. A closed class of boundary phases Write \(a_0=1/(2\pi)\). A boundary phase \(h(u)\) will satisfy \[ h(0)=h'(0)=0,\qquad h(-u)=h(u),\qquad |h''(u)+a_0|\le a_0/20,\quad |u|\le r. \tag{18} \] Assume the child phases have this property. At a nonroot vertex put \[ a_v=d_v/(2\pi),\quad b_v=n_v/(2\pi),\quad D_v=a_v-ib_v, \] \[ A_v(t,u)=\psi(t,u)+\sum_w h_w(t),\qquad C_{v,\ell}(u)=\operatorname{stat}_t \{A_v(t,u)+ib_vt^2/2-i\ell t\}. \tag{19} \] There are exactly \(d_v\) incidences in the \(t\) variable. Consequently \[ A_v(t,u)=\psi(0,u)-a_vt^2/2+E_v(t,u),\qquad |E_{v,tt}|\le a_v/20,\quad |E_{v,t}/t|\le a_v/20. \tag{20} \] The last quotient is removable at zero, by evenness in \(t\). For \(0\le\ell\le L_v=\lfloor t_0|D_v|\rfloor\), the equation \[ D_vt=-i\ell+E_{v,t}(t,u) \tag{21} \] is a contraction on \(|t|\le r\). Its Lipschitz constant is at most \(1/20\), and its image has radius \(t_0+r/20<r\). The solution has \[ |t_\ell|\le\frac{\ell}{(1-1/20)|D_v|},\qquad \frac{380}{441}\frac{\ell a_v}{|D_v|^2} \le-\Im t_\ell\le \frac{420}{361}\frac{\ell a_v}{|D_v|^2}. \tag{22} \] These inequalities hold also for complex \(u\). Indeed \(t_\ell=-i\ell/(D_v-Q_v)\), where \(|Q_v|\le a_v/20\); the real part of \(D_v-Q_v\) is positive. No reality assertion about a child phase is needed. The normalized outgoing phase is \[ h_v(u)=C_{v,1}(u)-C_{v,1}(0). \tag{23} \] Stationarity gives the exact derivative \[ h_v'(u)=\psi_u(t_1(u),u),\qquad h_v''(u)=\psi_{uu} -\frac{\psi_{ut}^2}{A_{v,tt}+ib_v}. \tag{24} \] The denominator has modulus at least \((19/20)|D_v|\). The explicit edge bounds on the radius \(1/4\) disk give \(|\psi_{uu}+a_0|\le a_0/50\) and \(|\psi_{ut}|\le a_0/50\). Since \(|D_v|\ge a_v\ge a_0\), the right side differs from \(-a_0\) by at most \[ a_0\left(\frac1{50}+\frac{20}{19\cdot2500}\right) <a_0/20. \tag{25} \] Thus (18) closes without a depth or vertex-count constant. The same calculation starts the recursion when there are no children. Charge ordering and the current vertex's action drop follow directly from \(\partial_\ell\Re C_{v,\ell}=\Im t_\ell\): \[ \Re C_{v,\ell}(u)\le\Re C_{v,1}(u) -\frac{190}{441}\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2}(\ell^2-1), \tag{26} \] \[ 0\le \Re\psi(0,u)-\Re C_{v,1}(u) \le\frac{210}{361}\frac{a_v}{|D_v|^2} =\frac{420\pi}{361}\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2}<4\kappa . \tag{27} \] There is no sum over descendants in (27). ## 5. The exact finite-message induction The inductive assertions are these, for all sufficiently large \(N\) depending on the fixed subtree, uniformly on each fixed main-parameter disk \(R<1\). 1. \(M_{v,N}(0)\ne0\), and on \(|u|\le r\), \[ \frac{M_{v,N}(u)}{M_{v,N}(0)} =\frac{\alpha_v(u)}{\alpha_v(0)} e^{Nh_v(u)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{28} \] The amplitude is holomorphic and nonzero; (18) holds. 2. For real \(|u|\le\pi\), \[ \left|\frac{M_{v,N}(u)}{M_{v,N}(0)}\right| \le C N^A e^{-Nc(1-\cos u)}. \tag{29} \] 3. For real \(|t|\le\pi\), \(|y|\le y_0\), \[ \left|\frac{M_{v,N}(t+iy)}{M_{v,N}(0)}\right| \le C N^A e^{N[-(c/2)(1-\cos t)+y^2]}. \tag{30} \] Only the phase bound and displayed exponential constants are uniform in the subtree. Amplitude bounds, polynomial powers and thresholds are allowed to depend on the fixed subtree. In (28) the normalization is the exact value \(M_{v,N}(0)\). It retains all \(N\)-dependent crossing, carrier and edge phases. More explicitly one may write \[ M_{v,N}(u)=\Omega_{v,N}(s,\boldsymbol\sigma)\, \alpha_v(u)e^{N\mathcal F_v(u)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{28a} \] Here \(\Omega_{v,N}\) is the original nonzero scalar ledger for that subtree, including the full \(q^{n_v(d^2/4-\sigma_v^2/2)}\) factors. It need not converge as \(N\) varies. The ratio in (28) cancels it exactly. The leading normalized amplitude \(\alpha_v(u)/\alpha_v(0)\) is independent of the microscopic parameters: the first charge coefficient is one and the paired edge insertion has leading value one. The next coefficients may depend on them. No oscillatory scalar has been hidden in a claimed \(N\)-independent amplitude. To obtain (30) from (28)--(29), use the exact degree bound following (9). For a Laurent polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(N-1\), the polynomial \(z^{N-1}f(z)\), and its reciprocal, give the elementary Poisson bound \[ |f(t+iy)|\le CN^A e^{N[-c(1-\cos t)+(1+c)|y|]} \tag{31} \] when its real bound is (29). It follows either by integrating the harmonic majorant \( -c(1-\cos t)\), or by the maximum principle on the disk. For \(|t|\ge r/2\), our \(y_0\) satisfies \[ (1+c)y_0<\frac c2(1-\cos(r/2)). \tag{32} \] For \(|t|<r/2\), use (28) and (18): \[ \Re h_v(t+iy)\le -\frac{19a_0}{40}t^2+\frac{21a_0}{40}y^2. \tag{33} \] Since \(|t+iy|<r\), these two estimates prove (30). The amplitude costs only a fixed polynomial factor. In applying the next trace, factor out the exact constants \(\prod_wM_{w,N}(0)\). Do not replace them by absolute complete-source bounds. On the local disk, the exact normalized child message has a holomorphic logarithm. More explicitly, (28) implies, on any fixed smaller disk, \[ \frac1N\log\frac{M_{w,N}(t)}{M_{w,N}(0)} =h_w(t)+\frac1N\log\frac{\alpha_w(t)}{\alpha_w(0)} +O(N^{-2}). \tag{34} \] The branches vanish at zero, and all fixed derivatives have the same orders by Cauchy. The thresholds in (34) may depend on the subtree. For a fixed vertex the sum of these corrections tends to zero. It therefore perturbs the local nondegenerate saddle by \(O(N^{-1})\), or equivalently is retained in its analytic amplitude. This is why inherited errors do not spend another exponential gap at every ancestor. ## 6. Conditional trace tails and connectors After extracting the exact child constants, (12) and (30) give the global bound for the actual input of the next trace: \[ |K_N(t+iy,u)\prod_w M_{w,N}(t+iy)/M_{w,N}(0)| \le CN^A e^{N[\Re\psi(0,u)-2^{-20}a_vt^2+128a_vy^2]}. \tag{35} \] Indeed \(1-\cos t\ge2t^2/\pi^2\), \(d_v=2\pi a_v\), and \(2\pi<8\). At a root with no outgoing edge, omit \(K_N\), replace \(\psi(0,u)\) by zero, and retain the same bound because there are \(d_v\) incoming messages. Set \[ A_0=2^{-41},\qquad y_v=A_0t_0a_v/|D_v|,\qquad L_v=\lfloor t_0|D_v|\rfloor. \tag{36} \] Condition (2) gives \(L_v\ge1\), and \(y_v\le2^{-57}<y_0\). The exact trace formula retains \[ c_{\ell,N}(\sigma)= (-1)^{(N-1)(\ell-1)}U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi\sigma), \qquad c_{1,N}=1. \tag{37} \] For a charge \(\ell>L_v\), the chirp and (35), maximized in \(t\), cost at most \[ \left(128a_v+\frac{b_v^2}{4\cdot2^{-20}a_v}\right)y_v^2 \le2^{18}\frac{|D_v|^2}{a_v}y_v^2. \tag{38} \] The negative Fourier term is at least \(t_0|D_v|y_v\). Since \(2^{18}A_0<1/2\), the omitted tail has loss at least \[ \frac12A_0t_0^2a_v=2^{-74}a_v>2^{-77} \tag{39} \] relative to \(\Re\psi(0,u)\). Each additional charge contributes \(e^{-N(\ell-L_v-1)y_v}\). For the fixed subtree, this dominates the exact coefficient growth \(\ell e^{2\pi R'(\ell-1)}\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). At the original real endpoints the Gaussian loss is \(2^{-20}\pi^2a_v\). The chirp and finite-charge connectors cost at most \(\pi A_0t_0a_v+A_0t_0^2a_v+128A_0^2t_0^2a_v\). Their sum is less than half the endpoint loss. The exact zero-mode current obeys that endpoint bound. Thus the original finite functional, including its endpoints and normals, is its finite charge sum plus a conditional error with loss (39). For each retained charge, restrict the real integral to \([-\rho,\rho]\). Its complement loses at least \(2^{-20}a_v\rho^2>2^{-51}\). Translate the interval to \(\Im t_\ell\); its endpoints remain in \(|t|<r\). With \(\delta=1/20\), the same elementary Young inequality as in the published calculation gives, along the connectors, \[ \Re\{A_v(t-iv,u)+ib_v(t-iv)^2/2-i\ell(t-iv)\} \le \Re\psi(0,u)-\frac18a_vt^2 +\left[\frac{1+\delta}{2}a_v+ \frac{2b_v^2}{(3-4\delta)a_v}\right]v^2-\ell v. \tag{40} \] For \(0\le v\le-\Im t_\ell\), the last two terms are at most \(-\ell v/8\), since \[ \frac{420}{361} \max\left\{\frac{21}{40},\frac{2}{14/5}\right\} =\frac{300}{361}<\frac78. \tag{41} \] Thus each connector has loss at least \(a_v\rho^2/8>2^{-34}\). The translated horizontal integral has a nondegenerate Gaussian with real quadratic part bounded above by \(-(19/20)a_v\). Its leading amplitude is nonzero: the edge amplitude, the child amplitudes and the actual \(\sin t_\ell\) are all nonzero. Combining these estimates, choose \[ \eta=2^{-80}. \tag{42} \] Every nonminimal charge is its saddle term plus an absolute conditional error \(CN^Ae^{N(\Re\psi(0,u)-\eta)}\). It need not have a relative expansion at its own much lower action. But (27) and (2) give \(4\kappa<\eta/2\). Consequently these errors are below the first conditional charge. Equation (26) orders all retained charges relative to that same charge. Its coefficient in (37) is exactly one, for both parities. This proves (28), with a nonzero leading amplitude. The argument initially takes the formal grid parameters on circles avoiding \(\sin2\pi\sigma=0\). The entire physical trace and its first-charge approximation are holomorphic through all collisions inside \(|\sigma|<1\). Apply the maximum principle to their whole difference on a slightly larger parameter disk. The leading orientation/crossing factors are explicit and nonzero; no divided endpoint current is declared separately removable. This extends the estimate, and the eventual nonvanishing, to every actual \(\sigma=0,\pm s\) and both complete parity sequences. Finally, prove (29) freshly from the exact trace rather than from its local approximation. This step can use polynomial norms directly, so colliding-grid derivatives cause no additional assumption. The real sup norm of each canonical child polynomial, divided by \(|M_{w,N}(0)|\), is polynomial by (29). For fixed real \(u\), (11) gives the real sup norm in \(t\) of the canonical kernel polynomial, retaining its factor \(\exp N[2G_0-c_K(1-\cos u)]\). Real sup and Chebyshev coefficient norms are polynomially equivalent at degree less than \(N\). The full crossing polynomial has polynomial norm. Multiply these polynomials, apply the exact Chebyshev folding bound in the correct \(P_{\sigma_v}\) quotient, and then its top-coefficient functional (D9)--(D11) in the published source bounds. All these are full polynomial identities and retain every normal channel. They give \[ |M_{v,N}(u)|\le CN^A\left|\prod_w M_{w,N}(0)\right| e^{N[2G_0-c_K(1-\cos u)]}. \tag{43} \] The nonzero value just proved at \(u=0\) has the exponent \(2G_0-\Delta_v\), with \(0\le\Delta_v<4\kappa\). For \(|u|\ge r/2\), \[ 4\kappa<(c_K-c)(1-\cos(r/2)); \tag{44} \] for \(|u|<r/2\), (28) and (33) give the stronger bound. Hence (29), and then (30), hold with the same constants for the outgoing message. This completes the induction. The proof is unchanged for a leaf, where the child product is empty. ## 7. Root assembly and the original filled action Apply the same local trace argument to (9). Its normalized input has \(d_0\) incoming messages and no outgoing edge, so the only change to (19)--(43) is to omit \(\psi(t,u)\) and its constant. The current-vertex drop, charge ordering, tails and connector estimates have the same constants. Recover the subtree constants recursively rather than summing their upper bounds. The child envelope identity (24) shows that the selected angles satisfy, at every original vertex, \[ \sum_{e\sim v}\psi_{e,\tau_v} +\frac{in_v\tau_v}{2\pi}=i. \tag{45} \] Their modulus is bounded by \(2\pi/[(19/20)\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}]\), which is much less than the geometric chart radius. Substituting the recursive critical values makes all child constants telescope. The root action is exactly \[ \mathcal C(\mathbf1)=\operatorname{stat}_{\boldsymbol\tau} \left[\sum_e\psi_e+ \frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_vn_v\tau_v^2-i\sum_v\tau_v\right]. \tag{46} \] It is the original filled action, not a sum of independently optimized cap actions. Its selected branch agrees with the unique small simultaneous solution, by the same weighted contraction used in (21). For the geometric path replace the right side of (45) by \(ic\), \(0\le c\le1\). The published explicit edge Hessian estimates give the simultaneous contraction on the radius \(1/4\) polydisk, with diagonal nonlinear bound \(a_v/50\) and row bound \(a_v/25\). Condition (2) implies \(\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}\ge\kappa^{-1/2}\). Consequently that solution has \[ |\tau_v(c)|\le \frac{2\pi c}{(1-1/50)\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}}<10^{-2}, \qquad \Im\tau_v(c)<0\quad(c>0). \tag{46a} \] The same factorization of the nonlinear derivative by \(\tau_v\) proves the sign, just as in (22). These are precisely the published primitive-completion hypotheses. All original disk periods, half twists and the calibrated action are therefore retained along the actual positive path. Each edge sum contributes \(N^{-3/2}\); each actual circle trace contributes \(N^2\) times one nondegenerate one-dimensional Gaussian, hence \(N^{3/2}\). Since a tree has one more vertex than edge, the final power is \(N^{3/2}\). All its leading amplitudes are nonzero. The exact first coefficient (37), rather than separate evenness alone, pairs the reflected Fourier modes. The edge insertion is still \(H_N/W_k\), with the original Gamma interpolation and physical offsets. Its leading value is one and its first correction is the same cotangent insertion as in the published theorem. The exact scalar ledger is unchanged by finite summation order. Thus the complete result is (3)--(5), and the same first correction can be obtained by the normalized insertion rule if desired. ## 8. Structural consequences and limitations This removes the sum over vertices from the sufficient analytic condition. For example \[ \frac{d}{d^2+n^2}\le\frac1{2|n|}\quad(n\ne0) \tag{47} \] shows that every \(|n_v|\ge2^{119}\) satisfies (2), regardless of the number or degrees of the vertices. The constant is very coarse; its purpose is a size-independent sufficient hypothesis. Zero or short powers are also allowed whenever their own degree makes (1) small. This is not the claim that the graph can grow with \(N\): every resulting diagram is fixed first. The proof is specific to the literal all-circle tree. It uses the exact degree-\(N-1\) boundary message and the one-edge kernel factorization. Arbitrary bare junctions, graphs with cycles, and rational slopes have not been included. The former summed criterion can remain a less restrictive sufficient test for individual diagrams; no comparison of optimal constants is claimed. The main analytic point is conditional normalization at the finite-polynomial level. Expanding child errors as absolute remainders at the augmented action, or using \(2G_0+O(r^2)\) instead of \(\psi(0,u)\) in (12), would not prove this theorem. The proof above keeps the exact child messages until the next local saddle and retains all source factors and normal channels.

title: An octahedral decomposition for ordered trees of crossing circles
status: Original ordered exterior and primitive cusp paths
text:
# An octahedral decomposition for ordered trees of crossing circles 1 November 2026. A crossing circle surrounds two strands of a link and bounds a disk punctured by them. Cutting along the projection regions and these disks opens the augmented link exterior into two balls. For the ordered tangle constructions considered here, each ball can be assembled from octahedra, with one octahedron for each edge of the tangle-operation tree. The proof identifies every boundary vertex and face, so it also identifies the original meridians and disk longitudes after the pieces are joined. The tangles have two strings and four ordered endpoints. Their operations are vertical stacking, quarter-turns in the projection plane, and the specified cylindrical closure. Every product junction in the reduced operation tree carries an original crossing circle; there are no junctions without a circle. The tree, the order of its branches, and all endpoint frames are retained throughout. Faces created by opening crossing disks are called shaded faces; the pieces of the projection regions are called white faces. This is the topological input for the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md). The [angular cell calculation](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) provides positive shapes for its octahedra, and the [completion theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) uses the path supplied by the [analytic filling criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md). The present proof concerns the augmented exterior before filling. ## 1. The actual ordered object and the statement At each vertex \(v\) of a finite tree put an original two-strand crossing-circle tangle \(P_v\). It retains the crossing \(R^{\epsilon_v}\), where \(\epsilon_v\in\{-1,0,1\}\), and its auxiliary component bounds the original twice-punctured disk. Every edge is an actual quarter-turn between two ordered product junctions. There are no product junctions without their own original circle. Terminal circles are included as vertices of degree one. The tree has at least one edge. Write \(T\) for the actual quarter-turn, \(C\) for the cylindrical closure, and \(R\) for one positive braid crossing in the original ordered terminal frame. The product order, the four endpoint frames, every rotation of a child ball, and every original disk orientation are part of the data. A representative recursive description has \[ W_v=P_v\prod_{w	ext{ child of }v}T(W_w). 	ag{1} \] The product here is in its specified order. At the closing sphere one may use the actual collar move to expose a root circle. A double turn then leaves its actual half-turn decoration on the affected subtree; it is not replaced by the scalar identity \(T^2=1\). The relevant moves are the literal closed-turn and cyclic collar isotopies in [the original ordered tangle moves](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md), equations (14)--(18). Their four collar sectors, and any reversal of the child order, are retained. Thus (1), with those transported frames, describes the original all-circle ordered operation tree. It does not introduce a commutativity move on open two-tangles. For clarity, the literal root adapter is \[ C\!\left(h_0T(E)ight) =C\!\left((TP_0)T(E)ight) \simeq C\!\left(P_0\,T^2(E)ight) =C\!\left(P_0\,	au(E)ight). 	ag{1a} \] Here \(	au\) is the actual half-turn of the ball. If \(E=L_1\cdots L_k\), then \(	au(E)=	au(L_k)\cdots	au(L_1)\), and \(	au(TW)=T	au(W)\). Thus the adapter reverses the displayed root order and transports every child frame; it does not suppress this rotation. The two-leaf case of (1a) is the base used below. More generally the original circle coupon can occur between two ordered lists of child factors in a nonroot junction. Keep that position: \[ W_v=\left(\prod_{w\in I_v^-}T(W_w)ight)P_v \left(\prod_{w\in I_v^+}T(W_w)ight). 	ag{1b} \] The lists record the cut at the parent edge in the original cyclic order. The left-insertion version of the calculation below handles this form without moving \(P_v\) through a child. Reassociation of a stack and transport of genuine turn-chain rotations put the literal circle-only tree in this form. At the root only the actual cyclic closed-collar move is used to choose its cutting position. Write \(E\) for the number of tree edges, \(V=E+1\) for the number of circles, and \(d_v\) for the number of edges incident to circle \(v\). The exterior admits the following labeled cut: * There is one pair of octahedral balls per original tree edge. * At a circle \(v\), its incident edge blocks are joined in the original cyclic order. There are \(d_v\) disk-side pages, and exactly one of their cyclic seams retains the original disk identification and its \(\epsilon_v\) crossing. All other page seams are the untwisted labeled identity seams supplied by the ordered insertion. * Cutting open those distinguished disk seams and the projection faces gives two balls. Each is a tree of \(E\) octahedra attached along \(E-1\) triangular faces. Its remaining boundary has exactly the two original shaded triangles of every crossing circle and the original white face cycles. Here an octahedron means the explicitly labeled topological cell. The [angular charts](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) give its positive shapes. The topological proof does not require the union of several cells to be convex. ## 2. How endpoint pairings determine the cut Use the closed-cut convention of [the projection and crossing-disk cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md), sections 2--4. For the turned elementary leaf \(h_v=T(P_v)\), label its four physical half-segments \[ (v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3) =(	ext{lower left},	ext{lower right}, 	ext{upper right},	ext{upper left}). 	ag{2} \] A quarter-turn cyclically shifts this tuple. A lower factor \(F\) followed by an upper factor \(G\) joins \(F_2\) to \(G_1\) and \(F_3\) to \(G_0\), leaving exposed \((F_0,F_1,G_2,G_3)\). Cylindrical closure joins positions 0 to 3 and 1 to 2. These are actual empty joining strips in the projection plane. One ideal vertex is assigned to each paired main segment and one vertex \(O_v\) to each original crossing-circle semicircle. The two shaded triangles of a leaf are \[ (O_v,v_1,v_2),\qquad (O_v,v_3,v_0), 	ag{3} \] where a half-segment in this display denotes the main-segment vertex containing it. Around \(O_v\) the cyclic order is \((v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3)\). At a main-segment vertex the two shaded corner sectors concatenate in the order of the actual planar joining strip. These sectors determine all white face cycles by the usual boundary walk. In particular the full oriented boundary ribbon graph follows from the literal matching; matching only face or component counts would not suffice. This endpoint construction records the reversible projection/disk cut. Drilling a boundary-parallel auxiliary semicircle and then opening its recorded half disk restores a ball. The disjoint leaf boxes permit this for all circles. White faces reglue by their actual projection labels. The two shaded faces reglue by the original disk map, including the retained half twist. The proof of that cut uses no quantum source identity. For the next local calculation it is useful to use an inverse turn: \[ P_v=T^{-1}(h_v),\qquad 	ext{its exposed tuple is }(v_3,v_0,v_1,v_2). 	ag{4} \] This is an exact physical identity by the definition of \(h_v\). It avoids using \(T^2=1\) on an arbitrary physical tangle. ## 3. One terminal insertion is exactly one octahedron Suppose the unturned \(P_v\) occurs at the beginning of its specified local stack. In the current full diagram, let \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) be the half-segments matched to \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) outside that box. Insert a new terminal child \(h_w\) immediately after \(P_v\). The literal product rule changes precisely the following two matches: \[  egin{array}{c|c} 	ext{before}&	ext{after}\ \hline v_1\! -\! x_1&v_1\! -\! w_1,\quad w_2\! -\! x_1\ v_2\! -\! x_2&v_2\! -\! w_0,\quad w_3\! -\! x_2. \end{array} 	ag{5} \] All other half-segment matches are unchanged. This remains true if \(x_1\) or \(x_2\) is in a nested factor or outside the local ball: the replacement only uses the two exposed output strips of \(P_v\). Name the old two vertices \(C=(v_1,x_1)\), \(B=(v_2,x_2)\), and name the new internal vertices \(D=(v_1,w_1)\), \(A=(v_2,w_0)\). The outside vertices \(C\) and \(B\) are now represented respectively by \((w_2,x_1)\) and \((w_3,x_2)\). Attach the octahedron with vertices \[ (O_v,O_w,A,B,C,D). 	ag{6} \] and equatorial cycle \((A,B,C,D)\). Its four shaded triangles are \[ (O_v,B,C),\quad (O_v,D,A),\quad (O_w,D,C),\quad (O_w,B,A). 	ag{7} \] Glue the first one to the old shaded face \((O_v,C,B)\). The two orientations are opposite, as required for joining oriented balls. The old face disappears. The second triangle in (7) is exactly the new \(v\) face in (3), and the last two are exactly the new \(w\) faces. The other shaded face of \(v\) is untouched. The four white triangles are the complementary octahedral faces. Along the three edges of the glued triangle, their unions with the old white pieces are precisely the new white regions. One can verify this directly: at each of \(B,C,O_v\) remove the two glued shaded sectors and concatenate the remaining sectors; their order is exactly the planar strip substitution (5). The new vertices \(A,D\) carry the new identity strips in that same order. Thus every remaining shaded sector and every cyclic vertex order agrees with the endpoint construction. Following these sectors around each white face therefore gives the same boundary cycle. Perform the same attachment in the other projection copy. This adds exactly one two-octahedron edge block and introduces one new original circle. It neither identifies two old circles nor inserts a circle at the attachment seam. The calculation also proves the inverse operation: remove a terminal edge block, restore the deleted triangular face, and undo (5). The original diagram loses that terminal child and otherwise retains its actual strand connections and order. There is also an explicit left-insertion version, needed for (1b). Inserting \(h_w\) immediately before \(P_v\) changes \[  egin{array}{c|c} v_3\! -\! x_3&v_3\! -\! w_3,\quad w_0\! -\! x_3\ v_0\! -\! x_0&v_0\! -\! w_2,\quad w_1\! -\! x_0. \end{array} 	ag{7a} \] This is the same octahedral attachment on the other shaded face \((O_v,v_3,v_0)\). The two formulas are direct applications of the same lower-output/upper-input stack rule. They retain the physical rotation of each tangle and all its endpoint labels. ## 4. Why this covers every ordered tree Start with one actual tree edge. The two-leaf matching gives exactly the octahedral boundary (7), in both projection copies. This is [the labeled two-circle block](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md), after the recorded endpoint-frame rotation. Its proof is a disk/projection cut, not an equality of two scalar sources. For a general tree, choose a terminal vertex as root and start with its unique incident edge. Expose that root by the actual closed-collar moves from section 1, retaining all transported frames and orders. The initial root then has no further children to insert; at the other endpoint the only existing edge is its parent edge. At each vertex add the children on the right of \(P_v\) in reverse final order, always immediately after \(P_v\). Add the children on its left in their final order, always immediately before \(P_v\). This is a construction of the specified word, not a permutation of an existing word: successive insertions produce exactly the two ordered lists in (1b), including the special case (1). A new child initially has only its own crossing-circle tangle; its children are subsequently inserted inside its own ball.
