Its actual quarter-turn carries the whole local insertion, including the two projection sides and all four endpoint labels. Any previously recorded half-turn or input/output reversal similarly carries the complete insertion and its order. It does not remove the frame decoration. Induction now gives exactly the original recursive word and its full boundary ribbon graph. Every step glues a ball along a triangular disk, so each projection copy stays a ball. There are \(E-1\) attachments after the initial octahedron. The shaded face count is \[ 4E-2(E-1)=2V. 	ag{8} \] The count is only a consistency check: the insertion proof has already identified each of these two faces with its particular original circle and each main-segment vertex with its literal pair. The equality of oriented ribbon graphs gives a label-preserving homeomorphism of the final boundary spheres. Extend it over the balls by a ball extension. All original white and disk-face pairing maps are matched, hence the quotient is the original link exterior. This is stronger than an identification of the unmarked manifold: the main arcs, individual auxiliary circles, disk sides, and their specified collar paths are preserved. The extra triangular interfaces provide the promised pages. In the whole exterior an upper interface triangle and its lower partner form a two-triangle, thrice-punctured sphere. The ends are the same original circle and its two physical main punctures. Its compactification is a twice-punctured spanning disk for that circle. These pages are obtained from the explicit cell subdivision and the preceding homeomorphism; we did not assume that a single original disk cut somehow creates all \(d_v\) pages. The insertion order places the pages consecutively in exactly the original cyclic order at that circle. There are \(d_v-1\) new seams there, plus the original distinguished disk seam. ## 5. Retained half twists and reversed disk frames First perform the projection construction with the disk cuts open. A retained crossing changes their regluing, not the half-segment compiler of the open cut. At each v keep its original distinguished seam throughout all insertions. Its original disk map is used once, after the untwisted page attachments. Thus no crossing is distributed among several edges, and no crossing is silently added at a new seam. For \(\epsilon_v=0\) the original pure disk map pairs the two sides within the same projection copy. For \(\epsilon_v=+1\) or \(-1\) use its actual odd pairings: the punctures exchange and the two projection copies are permuted as in the original A,B disk maps. The signs +1 and -1 have their distinct primitive meridian words even though their endpoint permutation has the same parity. The explicit collar permutation is also recorded in [the original half-twist collar](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md), section 3a. A full twist changes the peripheral marking and must not be discarded simply because its endpoint permutation is trivial. A physical rotation or reflection of a disk frame transports its puncture labels, its two pages, and its chosen meridian and longitude together. Apply the insertion table in that transported frame. In particular a reversal that exchanges the projection copies is applied to both halves of every incident block. There is no use of an arbitrary puncture permutation justified only by the rigidity of an abstract thrice-punctured sphere. These conventions cover the original signed and reversed diagrams. The local geometric block may be relabeled by these same actual rotations. Its shape formula is not used to determine the topology. ## 6. Exact primitive peripheral concatenation Fix one auxiliary circle \(v\) and orient its original disk-framed longitude \(\lambda_v\) and meridian \(\mu_v\) as in the original marked leaf theorem. After the page cut, a small cusp torus of \(v\) consists of \(d_v\) annular sectors, one from each incident edge block. Every page boundary on this torus is the same primitive disk-longitude class. A small meridian crosses these sectors once in their cyclic order. The insertion (5) subdivides one such transverse passage into two consecutive passages; it neither winds the meridian a second time nor changes its longitude class. This can also be read as a face-word statement. Each insertion replaces one original disk-face passage by two passages separated by the new triangular interface. In the final word all internal interface changes of coordinates occur in inverse consecutive pairs. After eliminating them, the retained word is the original disk meridian. Its ordered factors are one endpoint passage for each incident block, followed at the distinguished seam by the single original half-twist correction. This is a statement about the actual marked loop before evaluating its holonomy. Use the [local angular chart](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md), with common oriented longitude variable \(	au_v\) at all pages of this circle. Its incoming/outgoing edge-ratio tables give exactly the inverse seam maps with the just-established puncture matching. In one edge block its small pure meridional increment is \[ u_{v,e}=-2\pi\,\partial_{	au_v}\psi_e, \qquad V_v=2i	au_v. 	ag{9} \] This is the local primitive word, not an arbitrary logarithm of its multiplier. The longitude conjugates to the same element on all pages. Whenever it is loxodromic, its two fixed points are therefore carried to the same two marked points. In a coordinate with one at infinity and the other at \(q\), integrate \(d\log(z-q)\). The coordinate changes telescope in the concatenated path; the integral is the sum of the local increments (9). At the complete value it is the continuous limit of this equality. The original disk words fix the half-twist correction unambiguously. In the notation of the marked-leaf theorem, the pure meridian has multiplier \(ho\), and the two odd primitive words have multipliers \(ho Q\) and \(ho/Q\). Write \(
u\) for the local leaf response, so \(Q=e^{-
u}=e^{i	au_v}\) and \(
u=-i	au_v\). The physical \(R^{-1}\) tangle uses the first word and \(R\) uses the second. Thus the single retained crossing contributes \(\epsilon_v
u=-i\epsilon_v	au_v\), or equivalently \(-\epsilon_vV_v/2\). Consequently the actual continued primitive logs are \[ U_v=-2\pi\sum_{e\sim v}\partial_{	au_v}\psi_e -i\epsilon_v	au_v, \qquad V_v=2i	au_v. 	ag{10} \] The original proof of these primitive words is [the original marked face maps](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), sections 5--6, including its equations (15)--(18). The two-rectangle cusp lattice there certifies their primitivity. Our page insertion preserves those same paths; it does not choose a new rational meridian slope. In particular the integral in (10) is not reset to a principal logarithm after several pages. Each summand follows its local small branch, and the actual concatenated loop retains their full sum. This is precisely where a large total logarithm can occur while every individual block stays in its small positive chart. Along the continuous first-charge equations, with charge \(c\in[0,1]\), \[ \partial_{	au_v}\Psi + rac{i n_v}{2\pi}	au_v=ic, \qquad \Psi=\sum_e\psi_e, \qquad n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v, 	ag{11} \] (10) gives the exact original primitive filling word \[ U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i c. 	ag{12} \] At \(c=1\) this is one primitive turn. This calculation identifies the word and its continued logarithm. The [completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) verifies the positive-cell and nonsingular cusp-link conditions along the path and deduces the smooth complete filling. ## 7. From the cut to the geometric filling This proof applies to the actual ordered circle-only tree, with all its inherited frames and disk collars. It does not assert such a cut for an arbitrary scalar tensor network, for arbitrary branching of six independent boundary slots, or for a graph with cycles. It uses neither commutativity of pair-algebra polynomials nor equality of source actions. No auxiliary component is filled or deleted in the topological identification. The explicit terminal substitution (5), its ribbon-face realization (7), and the primitive path concatenation supply the ordered topological identification. The [local angular charts](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) give the positive cells and their full complex seam ratios. The [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) constructs the charge path, and the [geometric completion](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) proves that its endpoint is a smooth complete metric on the stated filled topology.

title: The preferred knot cusp along the angular filling path
status: Preferred longitude along the positive filling path
text: # The preferred knot cusp along the angular filling path 1 November 2026. A horospherical cross-section of the knot cusp is a Euclidean torus. Normalize the meridian's translation to one. The translation of the preferred longitude, which follows the knot once and has linking number zero with it, is its preferred cusp shape. The ordered page decomposition and its positive angular realization construct a representation of the original augmented exterior. This note identifies its preferred main-cusp translation. The argument does not use a quantum asymptotic to identify a representation or a cusp. The small-neighborhood argument below is used only to establish an identity of holomorphic germs. The identity then continues along the entire positive angular chart, even when the original auxiliary meridian logarithms are no longer small. The geometric inputs are the [ordered decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md), the [positive angular charts](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md), and their [actual filling completion](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md). The [analytic criterion](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) constructs the path used in the [quantitative volume theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md). The original marked inputs are the face-map theorem [the original marked face maps](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) and the full rational translation proof [the preferred-longitude translation proof](actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md). ## 1. Statement Fix an original ordered all-circle tree with at least one edge. Retain the original disk frames, half twists \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,1,-1\}\), and one main knot component. Let \(\mathcal E\) be its physical quarter-turn edges. Set \[ y_v=\tan(\tau_v/2),\qquad k_e=(1+y_v^2+y_w^2)^{-1/2},\qquad \tan(\pi x_e)=k_e,\qquad x_e(\mathbf0)=\frac14, \quad e=vw. \tag{1} \] All roots and inverse functions use their branches at zero. The local positive chart is \(|\tau_v|<10^{-2}\). The ordered page construction gives an actual marked representation there, with main meridian parabolic and primitive auxiliary longitude logarithm \(V_v=2i\tau_v\). Let \(L_{\mathrm{path}}\) be exactly the framed main path in Sections 2--6 of the preferred-cusp note. Let \(\lambda_K\) be the preferred longitude in the augmented exterior. Write \(w_\epsilon\) for the oriented writhe of its retained-half-twist diagram and \(\ell_v\) for the linking number of crossing circle \(v\) with the main knot. In the coordinate where the main meridian translates by one, their translations in the angular representation are \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{trn}(L_{\mathrm{path}}) &=2i\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\cot(\pi x_e)-\sum_v\epsilon_v,\\ \operatorname{trn}(\lambda_K) &=2i\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\cot(\pi x_e) -\sum_v\epsilon_v-w_\epsilon . \end{split} \tag{2} \] Here \(\operatorname{trn}\) denotes Euclidean translation, not matrix trace. The signs are those of the original positive checked crossing and the actual oriented writhe. For fixed integers \(p_v\), put \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\), and follow the positive charge path \[ U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i c,\qquad 0\le c\le1. \tag{3} \] Assume the path stays in the chart and has \(\operatorname{Im}\tau_v<0\) for \(c>0\), as supplied by the curvature-supported certificate. The completion theorem gives a smooth actual filled knot complement at \(c=1\). Its preferred cusp is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \tau_K=-w_{\mathbf n}-\sum_vn_v +2i\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\cot(\pi x_e(\boldsymbol\tau(1))).} \tag{4} \] Here \(w_{\mathbf n}\) is the oriented writhe of the diagram with the filled powers \(n_v\). Equivalently, the last sum is \(2i\sum_{vw\in\mathcal E}\sqrt{1+y_v^2+y_w^2}\), with the same branches. There is no smallness condition on the total \(U_v\) in this conclusion. ## 2. Why actual representations can be compared near zero There are two different geometric cell descriptions, so a source Hessian by itself does not identify their holonomies. We use the marked positive-gluing rigidity proved in [the marked multicusp gluing theorem](general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md), Sections 2--3 and 5. It is also used in Section 2 of [the original geometric deformation](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md). Here are the precise parts needed. The new complete triangulation consists of eight positive ideal tetrahedra per tree edge. Its face labels and peripheral paths are those of the original exterior, by the ordered page proof. The old complete construction gives that same marked exterior. Their complete holonomies are conjugate by an orientation-preserving marked isometry. This is the geometric uniqueness of the complete finite-volume metric. It can also be obtained from the existing maximal-volume conjugacy argument in [the geometric conjugacy theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md), Section 1: the page representation is an actual representation of the original group and its positive complete tetrahedra have volume \(2|\mathcal E|v_8=2\pi F_0\), the known complete volume. This use of rigidity is after the actual topological identification; an equality of cell volumes alone would not identify exteriors. For completeness, the positive-gluing uniqueness argument applies with an auxiliary longitude rather than a meridian prescribed at each auxiliary cusp. If there are \(t\) ideal tetrahedra and \(q\) cusps, select \(t-q\) independent edge equations and one primitive peripheral row at each cusp. The integral edge/peripheral identities identify the symplectic quotient of the edge row space with \(H_1(\partial M;\mathbb R)\). Thus these rows form a full-rank real Lagrangian matrix \((A\ B)\). Choose the main meridian row and all auxiliary longitude rows. They are independent and isotropic because they are one primitive nonzero class on each different torus. In the positive local orders write \[ u_j=\log z_j,\qquad v_j=\log(1-z_j^{-1}),\qquad D_j=\frac{dv_j}{du_j}=\frac1{z_j-1},\qquad \operatorname{Im}D_j<0. \tag{5} \] The Jacobian at fixed chosen peripheral logs is \(A+B\operatorname{diag}(D_j)\). If it killed a nonzero vector \(a\), then \((a,\operatorname{diag}(D_j)a)\) would lie in the complexification of a real Lagrangian subspace. Its symplectic pairing with its conjugate would vanish. The same pairing is, up to the fixed nonzero imaginary factor, \(\sum_j\operatorname{Im}D_j|a_j|^2<0\), a contradiction. The implicit-function theorem therefore gives one decorated shape germ for the main meridian log zero and the auxiliary logs \(V_v=2i\tau_v\). The cited multicusp theorem proves the rank and decorated-representation statements for exactly these mixed peripheral coordinates. Its polarization is the all-cusp form of the proof in [the polarized gluing argument](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md), Section 1. This is a statement about the entire nearby marked representation, not just a formal equality of its peripheral eigenvalues. To apply it to the old family, develop the vertices of the new ideal triangulation using the old representation and its recorded cusp flags. For a lifted ideal vertex \(gP_v\), use \(\rho(g)\xi_v\), where \(\xi_v\) is the selected peripheral fixed point. This is independent of the coset representative. Every complete tetrahedron has four distinct vertices, so the resulting cross ratios are holomorphic nearby and remain positive. They obey all the same edge and peripheral equations, with the same log branches by continuity. This puts the old representation into the new shape chart and justifies applying its uniqueness. No individual tetrahedron or subtree is separately conjugated. The old auxiliary longitude coordinates are valid near zero: the marked theorem gives a diagonal, nonzero derivative of \(V\) with respect to the original auxiliary colors. Thus the old family can indeed be parametrized by these same \(V_v=2i\tau_v\). The preceding uniqueness identifies its representation, with all original paths, with the new page representation on a neighborhood of zero. ## 3. Identification of the retained wire coordinates Equality of representation germs must also use the same variables in the cotangent expression. Here that identification follows from the exact classical Legendre calculation, not a comparison of volumes. In the original physical-edge variables the local angular action is \[ b(x,\theta) =\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi u+2\cos\theta)\,du-2J(x), \qquad J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du . \tag{6} \] For a circle vertex, the analytic elimination of its original hidden variables gives \[ \operatorname{stat}_{\theta_v}\left[ \sum_{e\sim v}b(x_e,\theta_v) +\frac{i\epsilon_v\theta_v^2}{4\pi} +i\chi_v\theta_v\right]. \tag{7} \] This is the original selected circle action, with its original physical-edge indices: the one-leaf identity is derived explicitly in [the regular crossing-circle action](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), Section 7, its circle-junction extension is in Section 9, and the joint-wire Legendre identity is (38)--(39) of [the joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md). The nondegenerate hidden Hessian makes these analytic eliminations unique near the original complete state. The identity retains the physical-edge variables before eliminating them. There are no bare junctions in the present tree. Set \(\theta_v=-\tau_v\), so that the original relation \(V_v=-2i\theta_v\) becomes the geometric convention \(V_v=2i\tau_v\). Separate evenness leaves \(b\) unchanged. Every retained edge \(vw\) therefore has the stationary equation \[ \partial_x\{b(x,\tau_v)+b(x,\tau_w)\}=0. \tag{8} \] Writing \(c_e=\cos2\pi x_e\), this is \[ (c_e+\cos\tau_v)(c_e+\cos\tau_w)=(1-c_e)^2. \tag{9} \] The branch through \(x_e=1/4\) gives \[ c_e=\frac{1-\cos\tau_v\cos\tau_w} {2+\cos\tau_v+\cos\tau_w}, \tag{10} \] which is exactly (1). The derivative of (8) at zero is nonzero. Thus these are the retained old physical-turn labels as analytic germs, not merely variables with the same complete values. The color itself also matches the primitive geometric meridian. Let \(\Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)\) be the sum of the stationary edge actions. The \(\theta\)-stationarity in (7) gives \[ \chi_v=-i\Psi_{\tau_v} +\frac{\epsilon_v\tau_v}{2\pi},\qquad -2\pi i\chi_v =-2\pi\Psi_{\tau_v}-i\epsilon_v\tau_v=U_v . \tag{11} \] The last expression is the actual page-by-page primitive word from the ordered decomposition. Near zero it has derivative \(d_v-i\epsilon_v\) in \(\tau_v\), where \(d_v\) is the circle's degree. This is nonzero. Equation (11) is not used as a substitute for the representation comparison in Section 2. ## 4. Holomorphic continuation of the actual main translation The old preferred-cusp proof establishes its rational identities before imposing any auxiliary filling equation. Its product potential, endpoint rebasing rule, actual quarter-turn maps, and pure and odd leaf words give \[ \operatorname{trn}(L_{\mathrm{path}}) =2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e)-\sum_v\epsilon_v . \tag{12} \] on the old nearby marked family. By Sections 2--3, (12) holds for the actual new page representation near zero. Both sides are holomorphic on the connected angular chart. For the right side this follows directly from (1). For the left side, keep the actual based main meridian and longitudinal words. The meridian is nonidentity parabolic throughout the chart: it is conjugate to one of the nontrivial local pants meridians. Locally send its marked fixed point to infinity and normalize its translation to one. The commuting longitudinal holonomy is then a translation as well. Its coefficient is holomorphic and independent of the remaining translation in this normalization. These local functions agree on overlaps, so they define one holomorphic translation ratio on the entire chart. Equivalently, choose the local trace-two unipotent lifts and write \(M=I+N\), \(L=I+\lambda N\). Since \(N\ne0\), the coefficient \(\lambda\) is a holomorphic function on any open set where a chosen entry of \(N\) is nonzero. The formulas agree on overlaps. This description uses no logarithm of the main longitude and therefore has no \(2\pi i\) or integer translation ambiguity. The identity theorem now extends (12) throughout that chart. A continuation along the positive charge path would suffice; no uniform neighborhood in the original summed meridian coordinates is required. The original endpoint-sign convention remains part of the word: when an arc is reversed, both its traversal and its unit-meridian orientation reverse. The affine multipliers \(-1\) at odd seams are not replaced by \(+1\). The homological computation of the fixed word is independent of the representation. It is exactly \[ [L_{\mathrm{path}}] =w_\epsilon[\mu_K]+\sum_v\ell_v[\mu_v],\qquad \lambda_K=L_{\mathrm{path}}\mu_K^{-w_\epsilon}. \tag{13} \] Hence the second identity in (2) continues with the first. ## 5. The preferred longitude after the actual fillings The original crossing circles are pairwise unlinked, and their primitive disk longitudes satisfy \([\lambda_v]=\ell_v[\mu_K]\). Filling the original slopes \(\mu_v+p_v\lambda_v\) gives \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{fill}} =\lambda_K\mu_K^{\sum_vp_v\ell_v^2}. \tag{14} \] This remains a fixed word on the main boundary throughout the cone path. At \(c=1\) it is precisely the preferred zero-linking longitude of the smooth filled knot exterior. At intermediate \(c\) its translation is simply the translation of that same boundary curve; no smooth filling at an intermediate nonintegral cone angle is asserted. The disk orientations give \(\ell_v^2=2(1+o_v)\) with \(o_v=1\) for parallel strands and \(o_v=-1\) for antiparallel strands, while \(w_\epsilon=\sum_vo_v\epsilon_v\) and \(w_{\mathbf n}=\sum_vo_vn_v\). Therefore \[ -\sum_v\epsilon_v-w_\epsilon+\sum_vp_v\ell_v^2 =-\sum_vn_v-w_{\mathbf n}. \tag{15} \] Adding the meridian translations in (14) to (2) proves (4). The new conclusion is a geometric identity on the positive angular continuation of this actual all-circle class. It does not extend the original real angle chamber, and it does not assert a formula on unrelated algebraic solutions. Its proof uses the exact marked representation, actual path words, local geometric uniqueness, and analytic continuation. The independent scalar calculation and the new source asymptotic may subsequently use (4), but neither was used to identify this cusp.

title: An explicit volume theorem for ordered trees of crossing circles
text: # An explicit volume theorem for ordered trees of crossing circles The number of twists at a region is not the only quantity that can make filling controllable. In the construction below, a crossing circle of large degree meets many geometric pieces. Its complete cusp makes even a small integer twist correspond to a long normalized filling slope. This gives a numerical sufficient condition for the volume conjecture in which some twist coefficients may be short or zero. The [local subtree theorem](actual_all_circle_local_message_volume.md) gives another sufficient condition for exactly this construction: \(\max_v d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le2^{-120}\). Its constant is smaller, but it has no sum over the vertices. In particular one universal twist threshold suffices for any finite tree. The summed criterion proved below remains a separate, often numerically better test. ## The knot construction A two-string tangle is drawn in a ball with four ordered boundary points: lower left, lower right, upper right, upper left. A product places one ball above another and joins their two adjacent endpoints by uncrossed arcs. The order of the factors is retained. The operation \(T\) rotates an entire ball through the specified quarter-turn in the diagram plane. Cylindrical closure joins lower left to upper left and lower right to upper right outside the final ball. Fix a finite tree \(\mathcal T\) with at least one edge, together with the cyclic order of the edges and the tangle frame at each vertex. There is one original crossing circle at every vertex, including the terminal vertices. There is no unmarked product junction. Each edge represents an actual quarter-turn of a child tangle, rather than a crossing of two drawn edges. Here is a precise recursive way to specify the diagrams. Choose a terminal vertex as root. At a nonroot vertex \(v\), put the integer braid \(R^{n_v}\) between the two ordered lists of its child tangles: \[ W_v=\left(\prod_{w\in I_v^-}T(W_w)\right)R^{n_v} \left(\prod_{w\in I_v^+}T(W_w)\right). \tag{1} \] The lists \(I_v^-\) and \(I_v^+\) specify the position of the crossing box in the original cyclic order. Empty lists are allowed. If \(w\) is the root's unique neighbor, close \(R^{n_0}T(W_w)\) cylindrically. This is an actual link diagram, not a tensor network considered only up to scalar identities. Other choices of cutting section are related by the physical closed-collar moves, with their induced rotations and reversals of factor order retained. The augmented diagram replaces each \(R^{n_v}\) by its crossing circle and a retained half twist \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,\pm1\}\), where \(n_v\equiv\epsilon_v\pmod2\). Filling that circle on its original disk-framed slope \(\mu_v+p_v\lambda_v\), with \[ n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v, \tag{2} \] restores exactly the indicated integer braid. Here \(\mu_v\) goes once around the auxiliary circle and \(\lambda_v\) follows its punctured disk. The main strands are not filled. We require that the closed main strands form one knot \(K\). This includes excluding a closed main component created inside an intermediate box. The test uses only the strand pairings and the parities of the \(n_v\); large magnitudes alone do not guarantee it. Write \(d_v\) for the degree of \(v\) in the circle tree and \(E=|E(\mathcal T)|\). This graph degree is unrelated to the quantum level \(N\). ## The quantitative theorem Let \(F_N(M)\) be the zero-framed reduced Akutsu--Deguchi--Ohtsuki (ADO) invariant of the actual knot, normalized to one on the unknot. Its marked meridian coordinate is \(M\), and at \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\) its complete value is the reduced Kashaev invariant \(K_N(K)=F_N(1)\). Moving the meridian on the scale considered here means setting \(M=q_N^s\), with \(s\) in a fixed complex disk. Define \[ \mathfrak S(\mathcal T,\mathbf n) =\sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2},\qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin(\pi s)}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\quad H_N(0)=1. \tag{3} \] Let \(w(D)\) be the oriented writhe of the actual filled diagram, using the same positive checked-crossing convention as \(R\). The exact framing and crossing factor is \[ A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v. \tag{4} \] The power uses the fixed logarithm \(\log q_N=\pi i/N\). All crossing and strand-turn factors are included in (4); it is not a chosen normalizing phase. **Theorem.** Fix the ordered tree, its diagram frames, and its signed integer powers before letting \(N\) tend to infinity. Suppose the main strands form a knot and \[ \mathfrak S(\mathcal T,\mathbf n)\le2^{-25}. \tag{5} \] Then the knot complement is hyperbolic, and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \tag{6} \] For every fixed \(R<1\), the stronger statements \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1+O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-1}), \qquad |s|\le R, \tag{7} \] and \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|F_N(q_N^s)| \longrightarrow\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K) \tag{8} \] hold uniformly on that disk. In particular these values are nonzero there for all sufficiently large levels. Both level parities and composite levels are included. The tree, its degrees, its twist numbers and the radius \(R\) do not grow with \(N\). The constant in (5) is conservative. It makes the condition explicit; no optimality is asserted. There is no additional strict-angle hypothesis for this literal class. Indeed an unturned elementary circle has attainable output interval \((1/2,1)\), and a turned subtree has interval \((0,1/2)\). The exact product interval shows that one upper-interval factor together with any number of lower-interval factors again has the full upper interval, in any fixed association. The turn changes it to the lower interval. At the terminal root the two complementary intervals give a strict closing pair. This inductive construction supplies the strict augmented geometry used by the finite-source proof. In the two-circle case the excluded two-odd pattern is not a knot; the knot test retains the necessary even, or pure, leaf. Two consequences make the range of (5) concrete. * For a tree with \(E\) edges, every tuple satisfying \( |n_v|\ge8192\sqrt E\) satisfies (5), because \(\sum_vd_v=2E\). * Start with any ordered tree on \(m\) vertices, with arbitrary fixed powers at those vertices. Attach \(B\) new terminal circles at each vertex and give each added circle a power of magnitude at least \(B\). The resulting sum is strictly less than \(2m/B\). Hence \(B\ge2^{26}m\) suffices, with the original powers still arbitrary, including zero. The knot/parity test remains necessary. An unmarked product junction can also be included by inserting the literal identity braid \(R^0\) at its prescribed position in the ordered stack. Add a crossing circle there in the augmented diagram and fill it with \(\epsilon=p=n=0\). The filled diagram is unchanged. The augmented exterior is different, and the added degree-\(d\) circle contributes \(1/d\) to (3). This gives a direct application to constructions with sufficiently large-degree unmarked junctions when the same total bound holds. It does not treat such junctions as free or assert that a low-degree unmarked junction satisfies (5). All these are finite constructions. Their potentially large size is fixed before the quantum limit. Related results use several invariant and root conventions; [the coverage discussion](general_untwisted_augmented_source_literature_coverage.md) records their precise scopes. ## Why the original exterior has the required geometric pieces Cut the augmented diagram along the projection sphere and the original crossing disks. The two resulting balls carry white projection faces and shaded disk triangles. At a leaf with half-segments \((v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3)\), the shaded triangles are \((O_v,v_1,v_2)\) and \((O_v,v_3,v_0)\), where \(O_v\) is the auxiliary-circle end. The literal strand matching fixes every cyclic vertex order and hence every white face boundary. Adding one terminal child supplies an explicit local cell attachment. Let \(h_v\) denote the quarter-turned crossing-circle tangle. Write its parent's unturned box as \(P_v=T^{-1}h_v\), so its exposed tuple is \((v_3,v_0,v_1,v_2)\). If the old downstream matches are \(v_1-x_1\) and \(v_2-x_2\), insertion of \(h_w\) immediately after \(P_v\) replaces them by \[ v_1-w_1,\quad v_2-w_0,\quad w_2-x_1,\quad w_3-x_2. \tag{9} \] Set \(C=(v_1,x_1)\), \(B=(v_2,x_2)\), \(D=(v_1,w_1)\), and \(A=(v_2,w_0)\). An octahedron with opposite vertices \(O_v,O_w\) and equator \(A,B,C,D\) has shaded faces \[ (O_v,B,C),\quad(O_v,D,A),\quad(O_w,D,C),\quad(O_w,B,A). \tag{10} \] Glue its first face to the old face \((O_v,C,B)\), with the opposite boundary orientation. The other three faces are precisely the new shaded faces prescribed by (9). The adjacent white sectors also concatenate in the literal strand order. Thus this is an attachment in the original cut, not a recognition based on equal volumes. ![Attaching one actual octahedron in a projection half. Equal vertex labels are identified, and the indicated boundary orientations are opposite. The triangle becomes internal; the other three shaded triangles retain the parent circle and introduce the new child circle. The same attachment is made in the other projection half. Only the glued faces are blue; the other disk faces are listed in (10). The cells come from the augmented knot diagram built by ordered two-string stacking and quarter-turns. The labels \(O_v,O_w\) belong to its actual auxiliary crossing circles.](../book/figures/octahedral-page-attachment.svg) The left-insertion version attaches along the other parent triangle. It allows the parent box to remain at its specified position among its children. Start from one tree edge and insert the remaining children in the appropriate left and right order, carrying each rotated child ball with its frame. Each projection half is a tree of \(E\) octahedra attached along \(E-1\) triangles. Its remaining shaded faces are exactly the original two per circle. The internal interfaces give the additional disk pages. At a circle of degree \(d_v\), the \(d_v\) incident blocks occur in the original cyclic order. One distinguished seam retains the original half twist; the other seams are the untwisted insertion maps. In particular the construction does not put one copy of the retained crossing on every incident edge. It also retains the actual half-turn produced when a turn is moved across the closing sphere. Restoring the labeled faces recovers the original augmented link and its primitive disk paths. The [ordered decomposition proof](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) gives the full half-segment and face-word calculation. ## Positive cells and primitive filling periods For an edge with endpoint angular variables \(t,u\), the finite quantum sum has the following analytic phase. Its derivatives determine the geometric logarithms below: \[ \begin{aligned} \psi(t,u)&=\operatorname*{stat}_{x}[b(x,t)+b(x,u)],\\ b(x,t)&=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi v+2\cos t)\,dv-2J(x),\\ J(x)&=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv. \end{aligned} \tag{11} \] Branches continue \(x=1/4,t=u=0\). In particular \[ \tan^2(\pi x)=\frac1{1+\tan^2(t/2)+\tan^2(u/2)},\qquad \psi_t=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh} (\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)). \tag{12} \] Let \(\Psi=\sum_{vw}\psi(\tau_v,\tau_w)\). The first Fourier term of the exact crossing traces has phase \[ \Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)+\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_v n_v\tau_v^2 -i\sum_v\tau_v. \tag{13} \] To locate its geometric branch, vary its last coefficient continuously from zero to one. For \(0\le c\le1\) solve \[ \Psi_{\tau_v}+\frac{i n_v}{2\pi}\tau_v=ic, \qquad\boldsymbol\tau(0)=0. \tag{14} \] The quantitative estimate (5) gives a unique branch with \[ |\tau_v(c)|\le \frac{2\pi c}{(1-1/50)\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}}<0.00111, \qquad\Im\tau_v(c)<0\quad(c>0). \tag{15} \] This is a bound on each local angular parameter. It is not a bound requiring the total primitive meridian logarithm to stay near zero. Each edge block admits eight positively oriented ideal tetrahedra whenever both angular parameters have modulus at most \(0.01\). Their complete shapes are \(i\), and their deformed shapes stay within distance \(0.4\) of \(i\). On a disk page put \(Q=e^{i\tau_v}\). The three complex ratios on its incoming edges are \((-Q^{-1},-Q,-Q^{-1})\); the outgoing ratios are their inverses. These ratios keep both angle and shear, and depend only on this circle's parameter. Consequently adjacent blocks fit even if their other endpoints have different parameters. At the distinguished odd seam the original cross-copy disk maps exchange the prescribed punctures. Their full matrix edge words are identities. Positivity and continuation fix every interior edge angle at \(2\pi\). The actual meridian crosses the consecutive disk-page sectors once. A pure edge contributes \(-2\pi\psi_{\tau_v}\); the single retained half twist contributes \(-i\epsilon_v\tau_v\). The original primitive logarithms are therefore \[ U_v=-2\pi\Psi_{\tau_v}-i\epsilon_v\tau_v,\qquad V_v=2i\tau_v, \qquad U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi ic. \tag{16} \] These are continued logarithms of actual paths. Their last identity cannot be obtained by reducing \(U_v\) to a principal logarithm. For completeness, the link of an auxiliary ideal vertex is a torus with a nonsingular similarity structure. Since \(\Re V_v>0\), its holonomy has a second fixed point \(q_v\) after the marked point has been sent to infinity. The developing image avoids \(q_v\): a zero of the invariant vector field \((z-q_v)\partial_z\) has positive index, whereas a torus has total index zero. Hence \(\log(z-q_v)\) develops a complete Euclidean torus. Near \(c=0\), \(q_v\) tends to infinity and the periods on the fixed original paths tend to zero. Their difference from (16) is a continuous integer multiple of \(2\pi i\), and is therefore zero along the whole path. The slope in (16) has cone angle \(2\pi c\). Its independent longitude has positive real period, so it bounds a punctured metric tube with a positive core length. At \(c=1\), attaching the core produces a smooth solid torus on precisely the original primitive slope. The main cusp stays a complete parabolic cusp. This constructs a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the original knot complement, including the short coefficients permitted by (5). The [local angular cells](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md) give the explicit vertex and face formulas, and the [geometric completion proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md) retains the original odd seams and logarithmic periods throughout this path. ## The action and the invariant have the same normalization The same actual cells fix the additive constant of the complex action. With \(V_v=2i\tau_v\), set \[ G=2\pi i\left(\Psi-\sum_v\tau_v\Psi_{\tau_v}\right) +\frac12\sum_v\epsilon_v\tau_v^2. \tag{17} \] Then \(dG=\frac12\sum_vV_v\,dU_v\). At zero, its imaginary part is the volume of the original complete augmented link. The marked boundary formula is \[ \operatorname{Vol}=\Im G-\frac12\sum_v\Re U_v\Im V_v. \tag{18} \] Let \(\mathcal C(c)\) be (13) with the last term multiplied by \(c\), evaluated at (14). Substitution of the original filling relation in (17)--(18) gives \[ \operatorname{Vol}_c=2\pi\Re\mathcal C(c). \tag{19} \] At \(c=1\), the right side is thus the volume of the knot complement just constructed. The finite invariant selects this action without an assumption about saddle dominance. The polynomial expansion of the finite invariant assigns an integer label \(0\le k<N\) to every internal edge. Its normalized label is \(x=k/N\); the high range is \(k>\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). The complete contribution of an edge is maximized at \(x=1/4\). Outside \([1/5,3/10]\), that edge loses a fixed exponential amount; a high index loses a fixed amount as well. The total discarded source has an absolute gap \(\pi/200\), independently of graph size, although its polynomial prefactor can depend on the fixed tree and powers. The exact finite angular sum has a Gaussian bound weighted by the vertex degrees. Its real decay constant can be taken as \(1/400\) and its imaginary growth constant as \(70\). Preconditioning (14) by \((d_v-i n_v)/(2\pi)\) gives a contraction with constant at most \(1/25\). The same estimates compare every retained nonzero Fourier charge with charge one, with a strict loss unless every charge has magnitude one. The exact crossing-trace identity has already paired the reflected positive and negative modes, and the resulting coefficient of the first charge is exactly one. Exact contour identities bound the omitted charge tails and their joining segments by an absolute exponential error. The possible drop of the first action is at most \(\pi(2550/2401)\mathfrak S\), which (5) places below half the available error gap. Thus the selected term is nonzero for both parities of \(N\). The physical closing trace contributes exactly \(H_N\), and all remaining crossing, changes of tensor order and zero-framing factors combine into the exact \(A_N\) in (4). The bounded insertion on each retained edge is \(1+O(N^{-1})\); the conditioned saddle evaluation therefore gives (7). The full constant and the scalar are retained when passing to (6)--(8). Neither the volume of a comparison diagram nor the complete augmented volume replaces the filled knot volume. The [quantitative finite-sum proof](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md) contains the uniform contraction, Fourier-tail and joining-contour estimates; the [elementary Newton bounds](all_circle_uniform_newton_bounds.md) give an independent derivation of the graph-independent decay constants. The [exact scalar proof](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) retains the physical strand orientations and framing in (4). ## A geometric form of the numerical condition At the complete auxiliary cusp the primitive shape is \(2i c_v/(1-i\epsilon_v c_v)\), where \(c_v=1/d_v\). The normalized length of a slope means its Euclidean length divided by the square root of the cusp area. For the actual primitive filling slope this gives \[ \mathcal L_v^2=\frac{d_v^2+n_v^2}{2d_v},\qquad \mathfrak S=\frac12\sum_v\mathcal L_v^{-2}. \tag{20} \] Thus (5) is equivalently \(\sum_v\mathcal L_v^{-2}\le2^{-24}\). This identity explains why high degree can compensate for a small crossing power. The proof above establishes the completion for these particular ordered exteriors; it does not import an unrelated normalized-length criterion or classify all short fillings. ## The preferred cusp and the first correction The remaining cusp belongs to the knot itself. Normalize its meridian translation to one. Its preferred longitude, which has linking number zero with the knot, then translates by a complex number \(\tau_K\), the preferred cusp shape. This geometric normalization is needed to interpret the first correction in the quantum profile. Let \(x_e^*\) be the branch in (12) evaluated at \(\boldsymbol\tau(1)\). The finite edge-insertion calculation retains one further term: \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N}\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^*) +O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}). \tag{21} \] The [finite insertion calculation](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md), Sections 5–6 and 8, gives an integrand independent of \(s\) multiplied by \(1-\pi s^2\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e)/N+O(N^{-2})\), uniformly with derivatives. At the nondegenerate joint saddle, the normalized expectation of this coefficient differs from its critical value by \(O(N^{-1})\). Its explicit factor \(1/N\) makes that an \(O(N^{-2})\) error. The common saddle corrections cancel in the ratio, and the other charges and contour terms are exponentially smaller by the quantitative estimate. This proves the remainder in (21) under the present summed criterion. The geometric translation calculation gives, on the same filled branch, \[ \tau_K=a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^*). \tag{22} \] This identification follows from the actual preferred longitude; it is not a definition of the cusp shape from (21). Let \(\lambda_{\mathrm{aug}}\) be the preferred main longitude in the augmented exterior and \(\mu_K\) its meridian. For the fixed filling integers retain the boundary word \(\lambda_{\mathrm{fill}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{aug}} \mu_K^{\sum_vp_v\ell_v^2}\), where \(\ell_v\) is the actual linking number with crossing circle \(v\). Before the endpoint this is simply a fixed curve on the unfilled main boundary. At \(c=1\), surgery homology identifies it with the preferred longitude of the smooth filled knot complement. Here is why its translation formula applies beyond the initial small-deformation neighborhood. The edge blocks form a positive ideal triangulation of the original augmented exterior. Near completeness, prescribing the main meridian logarithm and the primitive auxiliary longitude logarithms determines its marked shape germ uniquely. The [marked multicusp gluing theorem](general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md), Sections 2--3 and 5, proves precisely these mixed peripheral coordinates and the corresponding decorated representation statement. Its logarithmic gluing Jacobian has the form \(A+B\operatorname{diag}(1/(z_j-1))\). The edge and peripheral rows are Lagrangian, whereas positivity of the shapes gives \(\Im(1/(z_j-1))<0\); pairing a supposed kernel vector with its complex conjugate proves that the Jacobian is invertible. Developing this triangulation with the earlier marked representation and its actual cusp flags therefore identifies the two representation germs. The exact circle-variable elimination identifies their retained physical-edge labels by (12), before any edge is eliminated. The [preferred-longitude face-word calculation](actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) then supplies the translation \(a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e)\) for this fixed boundary word near completeness. Both sides continue holomorphically on the small angular chart: the main meridian remains a nonidentity parabolic, so the commuting longitude has a uniquely defined translation in its unit-meridian frame. This ratio has no logarithmic integer ambiguity. Their equality thus continues along the whole positive charge path. At the smooth endpoint the fixed word is the preferred longitude, giving (22). The same original surgery homology gives exactly the integer \(a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_vn_v\), with no unrecorded framing shear. The [preferred-cusp continuation proof](actual_all_circle_preferred_cusp.md) gives the representation comparison and peripheral calculation in full. Put \(z=2\pi i s\) and \[ \mathcal H_N(z)=\frac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}, \qquad\mathcal H_N(0)=1. \tag{23} \] Combining the exact factor (4), the expansion (21), and the geometric identity (22) gives \[ \frac{F_N(e^{z/(2N)})}{F_N(1)\mathcal H_N(z)} =1+\frac{\tau_K z^2}{8\pi iN} +O_{\mathcal T,\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}), \qquad |z|\le2\pi R<2\pi. \tag{24} \] All fixed derivatives have the corresponding limits on smaller disks. The shape in this formula belongs to the filled knot complement, not the complete augmented link. The exact scalar in (4) remains part of the statement; its quadratic expansion is the integer contribution to the preferred cusp in (24). ## The same limit from a pointed quantum A-operator Fix a genuine all-level quantum A-operator \(P\) annihilating the knot's reduced ADO family. Fix the finite initial vector \(c_0\) of ordinary-color polynomials selecting that family. The [pointed operator construction](actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md), Sections 2–3, forms the ordered recurrence row \(r_N(q)\) and proves the exact identity \[ \mathscr P_N(P,c_0) =\operatorname{CT}_{t=0} \bigl[r_N(q_N(1+t))c_0(q_N(1+t))\bigr]=K_N(K). \tag{25} \] Here \(\operatorname{CT}\) extracts the constant Laurent coefficient of the whole product. This retains the cancellations at singular recurrence steps and the required derivatives of the fixed initial data. It does not evaluate each singular factor separately. Applying (6) to this identity gives \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log|\mathscr P_N(P,c_0)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \tag{26} \] The condition is still (5), with the original knot and framing qualifications. Thus the new quantitative class also has an operator period on the left and its actual complement volume on the right. The finite initial data remain essential. Identifying the selected geometric factor of the classical symbol of \(P\) is a separate problem; no such identification is assumed in this corollary.

title: A vertexwise criterion for positive geometric fillings
text: # A vertexwise criterion for positive geometric fillings The global sum used to control the finite quantum source is not needed for geometric completion. For an ordered all-circle tree, the nonlinear charge equations admit a contraction whose norm is independent of the number of vertices. This gives a sufficient condition at each vertex, including vertices with zero or small crossing power and large degree. The conclusion below concerns the actual hyperbolic metric and its marked volume and cusp. It makes no new assertion about dominance in the finite quantum sum. ## 1. Statement Use the original ordered all-circle construction and its actual octahedral decomposition. There are at least two circle vertices. Every graph edge is an original physical quarter-turn, and each vertex carries an original crossing circle. Keep the original cyclic orders, disk frames, retained half twists \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,\pm1\}\), and primitive auxiliary curves \((\mu_v,\lambda_v)\). Fix the integers \(p_v\) and the physical powers \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\). Write \(d_v\ge1\) for the graph degree. Assume the original component test gives the required knot, when a knot-complement conclusion is desired. The following condition suffices for positive geometric completion: \[ \sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}\ \ge630 \qquad\text{for every vertex }v. \tag{1} \] There is a unique solution in the closed polydisk \(|\tau_v|\le10^{-2}\) of \[ \Psi_v(\boldsymbol\tau)+\frac{i n_v}{2\pi}\tau_v=ic, \qquad \Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)=\sum_{vw}\psi(\tau_v,\tau_w), \qquad 0\le c\le1. \tag{2} \] The solution continues holomorphically in \(c\) on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk, is zero at \(c=0\), and satisfies \[ \operatorname{Im}\tau_v(c)<0\quad(0<c\le1),\qquad |\tau_v(c)| \le\frac{2\pi c} {\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}-d_v/39000}. \tag{3} \] The denominator is positive. The original primitive periods obey \[ U_v=-2\pi\Psi_v-i\epsilon_v\tau_v,\qquad V_v=2i\tau_v,\qquad U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi ic. \tag{4} \] The cells consequently complete to cone solid tori of angle \(2\pi c\) for \(c>0\), and to smooth solid tori at \(c=1\). The main knot cusp remains unfilled and complete. In particular the endpoint is a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the actual filled knot complement. The constants in (1) are deliberately tied to the already established radius \(10^{-2}\) of the positive octahedral chart. The substantial difference from the earlier condition is that there is no sum over vertices. The number and relative sizes of the degrees and powers are unrestricted. The geometric inputs are the [ordered octahedral decomposition](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md), the [positive angular charts](actual_all_circle_angular_octahedra.md), and the [primitive filling completion](actual_all_circle_geometric_completion.md). Their conclusions about the actual ordered topology, positive tetrahedra, primitive periods, and completion are used below. No source comparison diagram is used. ## 2. Exact derivatives of the nonlinear error On the branches through zero define \[ F(t,u)=2\operatorname{arsinh}\! \left(\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)\right),\qquad E(t,u)=F(t,u)-t. \tag{5} \] The edge action satisfies \(-2\pi\psi_t=F\). Put \[ Q(t,u)=\sqrt{1-\sin^2(t/2)\sin^2(u/2)},\qquad Q(0,0)=1. \tag{6} \] Differentiation gives exactly \[ F_t=\frac{\cos(u/2)}{\cos(t/2)Q(t,u)},\qquad F_u=-\frac{\sin(t/2)\sin(u/2)}{Q(t,u)}. \tag{7} \] Indeed \(1+\tan^2(t/2)\cos^2(u/2)=Q^2/\cos^2(t/2)\); the square roots agree at zero and hence throughout the small connected chart. This fixes the branches in (7). For \(|t|,|u|\le10^{-2}\), let \[ a=\frac1{79000},\qquad b=\frac1{199},\qquad \omega=b^4,\qquad \delta=\frac1{39000}. \tag{8} \] The elementary series bounds with \(r=1/200\) give \[ |\sin(t/2)|\le\frac{r}{1-r^2/6}<b,\qquad |\cos(t/2)-1| \le\frac{r^2}{2(1-r^2/12)}<a, \tag{9} \] and the same for \(u\). Thus \(|Q|^{-1}\le(1-\omega)^{-1}\) and \(|Q-1|\le\omega\). To see the latter estimate, use \((Q-1)(Q+1)=-\sin^2(t/2)\sin^2(u/2)\); the branch has \(\operatorname{Re}Q>0\), so \(|Q+1|\ge1\). Equation (7) now yields \[ \begin{split} |E_t|&\le \frac{2a/(1-a)+\omega}{1-\omega}<\delta,\\ |E_u|&\le\frac{b^2}{1-\omega}<\delta. \end{split} \tag{10} \] Both final inequalities are rational comparisons. In particular, \(E(0,u)=0\), and \[ E(t,u)=tH(t,u),\qquad H(t,u)=\int_0^1 E_t(\lambda t,u)\,d\lambda,\qquad |H(t,u)|\le\delta. \tag{11} \] The function \(H\) is holomorphic also at \(t=0\). No division by a possibly vanishing unknown is needed to define it. ## 3. A contraction independent of the size of the tree Write \(L_v=\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}=|d_v-in_v|\). Multiplying (2) by \(-2\pi\) and using (5) gives \[ (d_v-in_v)\tau_v+ \sum_{w\sim v}E(\tau_v,\tau_w)=-2\pi ic. \tag{12} \] Define the fixed-point map \[ \mathcal T_{c,v}(\boldsymbol\tau)= -\frac{2\pi ic}{d_v-in_v} -\frac{\sum_{w\sim v}E(\tau_v,\tau_w)}{d_v-in_v}. \tag{13} \] On the closed polydisk of radius \(\rho=10^{-2}\), (11) and \(d_v/L_v\le1\) give, uniformly for complex \(|c|\le1\), \[ |\mathcal T_{c,v}| \le\frac{2\pi}{630}+\delta\rho<\rho. \tag{14} \] For example the last strict inequality already follows from \(\pi<22/7\). The total row derivative is at most \[ \frac{d_v\delta+d_v\delta}{L_v}\le2\delta<1. \tag{15} \] Hence (13) is a strict contraction in the ordinary maximum norm, with a constant independent of the graph size. It has exactly one fixed point in the polydisk. Iteration from zero converges uniformly in \(c\), so the fixed point is holomorphic for \(|c|<1\). The strict margin in (14) allows \(|c|\le1+\varepsilon\) for some positive \(\varepsilon\), proving the stated neighborhood assertion. The selected value at \(c=0\) is zero. The sign needed for geometric completion is not inferred from smallness. Equation (11) rewrites (12) as \[ A_v(\boldsymbol\tau)\tau_v=-2\pi ic,\qquad A_v=d_v-in_v+\sum_{w\sim v}H(\tau_v,\tau_w). \tag{16} \] For real \(c>0\), \[ \operatorname{Re}A_v\ge(1-\delta)d_v>0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau_v =-\frac{2\pi c\,\operatorname{Re}A_v}{|A_v|^2}<0. \tag{17} \] Moreover \(|A_v|\ge L_v-\delta d_v\), which proves (3). Every \(\tau_v\) is nonzero for \(c>0\). This argument allows arbitrary signs of \(n_v\), and \(n_v=0\). It makes no assumption that neighboring powers are comparable. The same sign proof works even when a large degree makes the total meridian logarithm in (4) close to \(-2\pi i\). ## 4. Actual metric and absolute volume The octahedral chart depends only on the parameters at the ends of one physical edge. Conditions (3) and (14) keep every such pair in its proved positive disk. The actual ordered disk seams match their full complex ratios, including the single prescribed odd seam. The original cut proof retains every primitive meridian and longitude. Thus the geometric completion theorem applies to the path just constructed, rather than to an unrelated solution of exponentiated gluing equations. In particular, the actual logarithmic periods start at zero as \(c\downarrow0\): in a fixed complete peripheral frame the second fixed point escapes to infinity, and the increments of \(\log(z-q_v)\) along the fixed generator paths tend to zero. Their differences from (4) are continuous integers times \(2\pi i\), and hence vanish along the whole path. The slope in (4) makes one full primitive turn at \(c=1\). This is the winding information that exponentiated filling equations alone would not supply. Let \[ \mathcal C(c)=\operatorname*{stat}_{\boldsymbol\tau} \left[\Psi+\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_vn_v\tau_v^2 -ic\sum_v\tau_v\right]. \tag{18} \] The same actual fundamental chain and primitive period calibration as in the completion theorem give \[ \operatorname{Vol}_c=2\pi\operatorname{Re}\mathcal C(c), \qquad \frac{d}{dc}\operatorname{Vol}_c =2\pi\sum_v\operatorname{Im}\tau_v(c). \tag{19} \] The complete anchor is the volume of two regular octahedra per tree edge. Every complementary primitive \(\lambda_v\) represents the core, of length \(\ell_v=-2\operatorname{Im}\tau_v\). The estimates above give the explicit bounds \[ \frac{4\pi c(1-\delta)d_v}{(L_v+\delta d_v)^2} \le\ell_v(c)\le \frac{4\pi c(1+\delta)d_v}{(L_v-\delta d_v)^2}. \tag{20} \] If \(S=\sum_vd_v/L_v^2\), integration yields \[ \frac{2\pi^2(1-\delta)}{(1+\delta)^2}S \le\operatorname{Vol}_0-\operatorname{Vol}_1\le \frac{2\pi^2(1+\delta)}{(1-\delta)^2}S. \tag{21} \] Here \(S\) is a useful bound on the volume change, not a hypothesis for existence or completion. When the main component is a knot, the independently geometric preferred-cusp continuation also applies. With the original oriented writhe \(w_{\mathbf n}\), it gives \[ \tau_K=-w_{\mathbf n}-\sum_vn_v+ 2i\sum_{vw} \sqrt{1+\tan^2(\tau_v(1)/2)+\tan^2(\tau_w(1)/2)}. \tag{22} \] Its proof uses the actual marked representation and preferred longitude. Equation (22) is not inferred from a quantum correction. ## 5. A finite criterion with different radii at different vertices One can keep the local graph data instead of using the common threshold (1). Choose radii \(0<r_v\le10^{-2}\). Set \[ s_v=\sinh(r_v/2),\qquad a_v=\cosh(r_v/2)-1,\qquad \omega_{vw}=s_v^2s_w^2. \tag{23} \] The same derivative calculation gives \[ \begin{split} \alpha_{vw} &=\frac{a_v+a_w}{(1-a_v)\sqrt{1-\omega_{vw}}} +\frac1{\sqrt{1-\omega_{vw}}}-1,\\ \beta_{vw} &=\frac{s_vs_w}{\sqrt{1-\omega_{vw}}}, \end{split} \tag{24} \] as bounds for \(|E_t|\) and \(|E_u|\) on the corresponding bidisk. Put \(h_v=\sum_{w\sim v}\alpha_{vw}\). The following finite inequalities suffice: \[ \begin{split} &2\pi+h_vr_v<L_vr_v,\qquad h_v<d_v,\\ &\max_v\left[ \frac{h_v}{L_v} +\sum_{w\sim v}\frac{\beta_{vw}r_w}{L_vr_v}\right]<1. \end{split} \tag{25} \] The first line makes (13) preserve the product of the vertex disks and gives the sign in (17). The second is a contraction bound in the weighted norm \(\max_v|\tau_v|/r_v\). The proof of Sections 3--4 applies unchanged, with \[ |\tau_v(c)|\le\frac{2\pi c}{L_v-h_v}. \tag{26} \] This is a finite numerical certificate in the integer degrees and powers and the chosen positive radii. All quantities can be bounded by rational Taylor enclosures; it does not assume the existence of a saddle or a geometric representation. More generally, the second line of (25) can be replaced by a positive-vector certificate for the derivative matrix with diagonal entries \(h_v/L_v\) and off-diagonal entries \(\beta_{vw}/L_v\). If a positive vector \(q\) and a number \(\kappa<1\) satisfy \(Mq\le\kappa q\), contraction holds in the \(q\)-weighted norm. The invariant polydisk is still supplied separately by the first line of (25). Thus choosing the contraction norm does not change the geometric parameter region. ## 6. What this extends, and what remains separate The global condition \(S\le2^{-25}\) implies (1), but the converse fails on arbitrarily large trees. For instance on paths with powers chosen from \(630,631\), every degree is at most two and (1) holds, whereas \(S\) grows linearly with the number of vertices. Choose the original parity pattern by the finite knot-component test when a knot is required. The vertexwise criterion also permits a zero power at any vertex of degree at least \(630\), together with other powers satisfying their own local inequalities. These examples concern the arithmetic hypotheses and the supplied actual diagram. They do not assert an unrestricted classification of small-slope fillings. The explicit positive radius is a sufficient chart, not the maximal positivity domain of the octahedra. The earlier quantum proof discards some parts of the source with a fixed absolute loss and then compares that loss with the total change of the critical action. The total change in (21) can grow with the size of a tree satisfying (1). Consequently this geometric theorem alone does not supply the earlier source dominance or a new volume-conjecture conclusion. The [local subtree argument](actual_all_circle_local_message_volume.md) provides such a quantum comparison under the stronger condition \(\max_v d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le2^{-120}\). The geometric condition \(L_v\ge630\) alone does not prove that quantum conclusion.

title: The normalization clock disk is not uniformly tame on the physical head
text: # The normalization clock disk is not uniformly tame on the physical head 29 October 2026. The selected original normalization scalar has a tame clock disk, but its ALL-INPUT physical operator does not. The distinction can be proved at the first normal jet, with the actual sources and full Cartan factor retained. This gives an explicit physical Ward current which a gluing theorem has to cancel coherently. The result does not assert exponential growth of a closed knot scalar, or failure of the source-specific shrinking-arc construction. It rules out promoting its selected scalar estimate to a uniform physical-head operator estimate. ## 1. The literal open-head normalization operator Let N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j|, and kappa=q^(d^2/2). Let R be the FULL original positive crossing on the physical pair degree-d block W, and set L=kappa^(-1)R. Keep the original cup and ordinary cap. The all-input cup slide exposes the operator \[ \mathcal C_N(t)=(\ell_{12}\otimes I_3) (I_1\otimes R^2)t^{J_2}(I_1\otimes p_{23}), \qquad J|a\rangle=a|a\rangle. \] Here R^2 acts on the degree-d subspace of the last physical pair; the full original physical crossings restrict to this block and the first head is its untouched spectator. This is the same actual local normalization slot as in [the mesoscopic-current theorem](actual_mesoscopic_clock_packet_currents.md#4-why-the-scalar-packet-does-not-already-solve-physical-gluing). The remaining physical input is arbitrary. Integer degree makes the operator diagonal, with EXACT entries \[ C_a(t)=x^{-a}Q^{-a}\sum_{n=0}^d(L^2)_{d-a,n}(xt)^n. \tag{1} \] Indeed the three factors are the cup coefficient N x^(n-d), the original crossing square kappa^2(L^2)_(d-a,n), and the cap x^(-a)Q^(-a)/N. The identity kappa^2=x^d gives (1). The apparent all-input source freedom is therefore fixed, not chosen by a favorable scalar period. At t=1 every entry is x^d=kappa^2. Write u(t)_j=(xt)^j and v(t)=L^2u(t). Because x^2=Q^(-1), \[ C_a(t)=x^a v_{d-a}(t),\qquad \max_a|C_a'(1)|=\|v'(1)\|_\infty. \tag{2} \] ## 2. The exact finite Ward register before the second crossing For 0<=i<=d define \[ D_i^+(s)=F_i^2\sum_{b=0}^i \frac{Q^{b^2}s^b}{F_{i-b}F_b^2}. \] Let D_i^-(s) denote the same polynomial with Q replaced by Q^(-1). All factorial indices are below N. Finite Durfee convolution gives D_i^+(1)=D_i^-(1)=1. Directly from the original crossing entries, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle (Lu(t))_i=x^i t^d D_i^-(1/t).} \tag{3} \] For clarity, the intermediate finite coefficient is \[ (Lu(t))_i=x^{-i}Q^{i(d-i)}t^{d-i}F_i^2 \sum_{k=0}^i\frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}t^k}{F_kF_{i-k}^2}. \] Replace k by i-b and use (Q^(-1);Q^(-1))_b=(-1)^b Q^(-b(b+1)/2)F_b to obtain (3). This is an all-port factorial identity, not an adjoint/unitarity claim. The finite polynomials obey \[ D_i^+(s)=(1+Q-2Q^i+Q^{2i-1}s)D_{i-1}^+(s) -Q(1-Q^{i-1})^2D_{i-2}^+(s). \tag{4} \] One elementary derivation uses formal series through degree d: U(z)=sum z^k/F_k has U(Qz)=(1-z)U(z), and W(z)=sum Q^(b^2)s^b z^b/F_b^2 satisfies W(z)-2W(Qz)+(1-sQz)W(Q^2z)=0. Compare coefficients of U(z)W(z). This proves (4) at the root without using any denominator F_N. Let P_i be the original Green register, \[ P_0=1,\qquad P_i=(1-Q^i)^2P_{i-1}+Q^i. \] Differentiating (4) at s=1 and factoring the resulting first difference gives the exact normal current \[ (D_i^+)'(1)-(D_{i-1}^+)'(1)=Q^iP_{i-1}. \tag{5} \] The base case is (D1^+)'(1)=Q. Equivalently, set w=Lu'(1); (3) gives w_i=x^i[d-(D_i^-)'(1)]. Therefore \[ \boxed{\displaystyle x^{-i}w_i-x^{-(i-1)}w_{i-1} =-Q^{-i}\overline{P_{i-1}},\quad1\leq i\leq d.} \tag{6} \] This is the retained physical normal current. It is not zero at a normalization leaf merely because its value at t=1 is a scalar. ## 3. The source endpoint forces a large interior current The all-parity original source endpoint has the independently derived quadratic-Gaussian asymptotic \[ P_d=N^{3/2}\exp\!\left[i\pi\left(\frac14-\frac N{12} +\frac1{4N}\right)\right]+O(\sqrt N). \tag{7} \] Its proof retains the complete pivotal derivative source, including the odd simple node: [the endpoint Gaussian theorem](actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian_asymptotic.md). In particular |P_d|>=c N^(3/2) for all sufficiently large N. No volume asymptotic or fitted saddle branch is assumed. The exact backward Green identity from [the terminal capacity proof](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md) is \[ P_t=F_t^2\left(\frac{P_d}{N^2} -\sum_{b=t+1}^d\frac{Q^b}{F_b^2}\right). \tag{8} \] Choose i nearest 5N/6, with 1<=i<=d, and t=i-1. For large N, s_t>N. The sine-factorial sequence increases up to its high peak and then decreases to s_d=N. Consequently s_b>=N for every b>t, so the tail in (8) has absolute value at most1/N. It follows from (7) that \[ |P_{i-1}|\geq c_1 N^{-1/2}s_{i-1}^2. \tag{9} \] Put J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi*u))du. Uniform sine-factorial asymptotics give \[ \log|P_{i-1}|\geq\frac{v_3}{\pi}N-O(\log N), \tag{10} \] since J has maximum v3/(2pi) at 5/6, where v3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. The lower bound is a coherent source result: the complex tail in (8) is estimated only AFTER the actual nonzero endpoint has been evaluated. ## 4. A quantitative all-input obstruction after the second crossing The literal original NEGATIVE crossing supplies \[ |(L^{-1})_{r,j}|= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{N^2}{s_r^2s_j^2s_{d-r-j}},&r+j\leq d,\\ 0,&r+j>d. \end{cases} \tag{11} \] No conjugate-transpose inverse is used. Define the exact row mass B_r=sum_j |(L^(-1))_(r,j)|. Since w=L^(-1)v'(1), (6) implies the FINITE inequality \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{a\geq i-1}|C_a'(1)| \geq\frac{|P_{i-1}|}{B_i+B_{i-1}}.} \tag{12} \] The color restriction follows from the two strict supports in (11), not from an imposed geometric color. It is enough to control the operator on its upper sixth of physical inputs. The global factorial minimum is log s_j>=-N v3/(2pi)-O(log N), and for r=i or i-1, log s_r^2=N v3/pi+O(log N). Hence (11) gives \[ \log(B_i+B_{i-1})\leq N\left(-\frac{v_3}{\pi}+\frac{3v_3}{2\pi}\right)+O(\log N) =\frac{v_3}{2\pi}N+O(\log N). \] Combining this with (10) proves a positive explicit exponent: \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\max_a|C_a'(1)| \geq\gamma:=\frac{v_3}{2\pi}>0.} \tag{13} \] The numerical value gamma is about0.16153. It is a rigorous LOWER bound, not the claimed exact jet exponent. Every C_a is a polynomial. Cauchy's derivative inequality now gives, for EVERY fixed c>0, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \liminf_N\frac1N\log \sup_{|t-1|\leq c/N}\|\mathcal C_N(t)\|_{\mathrm{op}} \geq\gamma>0.} \tag{14} \] The same assertion holds for any disk radius r_N<=1 with log(1/r_N)=o(N). It is therefore not repaired by choosing a smaller polynomial clock disk. This is a statement about the ALL-INPUT physical operator, not about the selected scalar row. This particular obstruction is independent of a choice of positive inner product on the SAME physical input/output head. The C_a(t) are the actual eigenvalues of the diagonal operator, so every such operator norm is at least max_a|C_a(t)|, even for N- and t-dependent metrics. A change between DIFFERENT input and output metrics has additional interfaces and is not covered by that observation. ## 5. The missing moment constraint is an actual normal Ward defect For a=d the original source packet is still C_d(t)=x^(-d)P_N(t), in the notation of the mesoscopic-current theorem. Its first derivative is x^(-d)Q conjugate(P_d-1), polynomial in N; the whole selected c/N disk is polynomially bounded by the original clock-disk proof. There is no contradiction with (13): the large normal response occupies other physical inputs. It can also be stated directly as a failure of the untwisted Hopf moment condition. The original single-head F acts by F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>. Therefore \[ [F,\mathcal C_N'(1)]|a\rangle =(1-Q^{a+1})(C_a'(1)-C_{a+1}'(1))|a+1\rangle. \tag{15} \] The terminal C_d' is polynomial, while (13) is exponential. Telescoping the physical differences and using |1-Q^(a+1)|>=4/N proves \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log\|[F,\mathcal C_N'(1)]\|_{\mathrm{op}} \geq\gamma. \tag{16} \] The same holds for Ecal, whose relevant coefficient magnitudes agree. Thus a polynomial-norm same-head correction cannot make this jet an intertwiner: its commutator would have to cancel (16). The required normal current is explicitly (5)--(6), not an unproved abstract error. The exact all-input tensor Ward identity identifies the omitted two-color insertion more directly. Put S=I tensor p and A_cap=ell tensor I, and let U=I tensor R_phys^2 act on the FULL physical pair space, not only its degree-d block. Define \[ \mathcal J_F(t)=A_{\mathrm{cap}}U K_1^{-1}F_2 t^{J_2}S,\qquad \mathcal J_E(t)=A_{\mathrm{cap}}U E_{{\mathrm{cal}},2}t^{J_2}K_3S. \] The actual coproduct and cup/cap intertwinings give \[ [F,\mathcal C_N(t)]=(1-t)\mathcal J_F(t),\qquad [E_{\mathrm{cal}},\mathcal C_N(t)]=(1-t^{-1})\mathcal J_E(t). \tag{17} \] Indeed only the middle-head term in the total coproduct fails to commute with t^(J2). In particular [F,C_N'(1)]=-J_F(1) and [Ecal,C_N'(1)]=J_E(1). The F insertion goes through pair degree d+1 and the E insertion through degree d-1. Replacing either by a shift of the recording register inside the degree-d scalar packet would omit that sector. Equations (16)--(17) prove that these ACTUAL physical normal-current operators have exponential norm; no polynomial operator correction may simply erase them. A full exterior may cancel it with neighboring clock/crossing currents or may retain a source projection excluding these inputs. Such a cancellation must be shown in its actual tensor slot, with the marked source unchanged. Replacing (1) by the selected value C_d(t), imposing a lowest-color projection on an internal head, or declaring the clock insertion a Hopf map omits the defect above. This proves the requested uniform physical operator extension FALSE. It leaves a source-compatible correlated/mesoscopic gluing theorem open. Tensoring a spectator identity does not change the lower bound; no claim about a general correlated whole-knot scalar or a one-dimensional unit-circle arc follows solely from the disk inequality (14). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_all_input_normalization_clock_obstruction.py) checks the original full R/cup/cap operator, the finite Ward recurrence, the exact derivative current, literal inverse row masses, and finite inequality (12). The endpoint Gaussian input has its separate all-level proof and original-source audit. The finite audit checks twelve literal all-input physical normalization operators at N=2,...,12,14, their exact root Ward jets and Hopf commutators; ten complete complex current/lower-bound families through N=96. Numerical jet rates are recorded only as diagnostics, not used to infer the positive lower exponent (13).

title: Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners
text: # Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners 29 October 2026. This proves a uniform polynomial relative bound for the ACTUAL first generic-q normal at every one of the 64 reflected branches of a supported folded sextuple. The new step is a positive finite presentation of the full generic source on face-supported branches, including branches whose seven-factorial formula has a live `[2N]` current. The already proved Fourier partner involution and exact first- normal Ward equation then cover the remaining branches. Every fixed generic normal order is controlled on the face-supported branches. The general 64-branch conclusion is FIRST ORDER ONLY. No completed physical recoupling norm or global volume equality follows merely from this local scalar theorem. ## 1. Statement and source convention Fix `N>=3`, `D=N-1`, `q=exp(pi i/N)`, and integer folded labels `j=(a,b,c,d,e,f)` in `[0,D/2]`, with all four face sums at least `D`. Use the SAME actual generic seven-factorial sum and normalization as in [the reciprocal source theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md): K_B(zeta)=[N]^2 S_B(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_B^2, k(B)=D_log(zeta) K_B(q). Here B records any subset of the six changes `j -> D-j`. The original actual source prefactors, peripheral factors and marking are not changed. The proved root-value identity gives `K_B(q)=W_N^2>0` for all branches. There is an absolute constant C such that max_B |k(B)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (1) The local analytic square root positive at q, and the first inverse jets of K and its square root, have corresponding relative bounds. Every implicit constant below is independent of the supported labels, level parity and compositeness. A set of high bits is called face-supported if it is contained in one of the four faces (a,b,e), (c,d,e), (a,d,f), (b,c,f). For every such branch, and every fixed r, the stronger conclusion is |D_log(zeta)^r K_B(q)| <= C_r N^(c_r) W_N^2, (2) with the analogous local square-root and inverse bounds. An opposite pair of high bits is not face-supported; that two-bit case is tail- free and is already covered by the positive-core theorem. ## 2. A root-unit presentation of the FULL generic source A tail-free branch already has all fixed-jet bounds. Consider a live face-supported branch, so all three opposite sums exceed `2D`. Choose an opposite pair with maximal label sum, and use tetrahedral relabeling to call it `(e,f)`, with f its high-bit edge and e its low-bit edge. This is possible: the largest opposite sum exceeds D, whereas an opposite pair with both bits low has sum at most D. A face contains at most one edge of each opposite pair. In this labeling, e<=D/2<=f, e+f>=max(a+c,b+d), min(a,b)<=D/2, min(c,d)<=D/2. (3) For the last assertion, the two remaining possible high edges are in the face containing f. Each of the two faces containing e therefore has at most one high external edge. The same assertion is immediate when there are fewer than three high bits. Set p=min(a+d,b+c), s=a+b+c+d, h=max(|a-b|,|c-d|), t0=s-2p, rA=a+b-h, rC=c+d-h, n=p-f, t=p+f-D. (4) The exact elementary identity p+h=max(a+c,b+d) (5) follows by expanding the difference of the maximum and minimum: its four possibilities are `a-b,b-a,c-d,d-c`. The true triangle conditions give `n>=0` and `h<=e`. Equations (3),(5) imply n<=e-h, h+e+n<=2e<=D, n<=t. (6) Furthermore 0<=n<=rA,rC<=D, 0<=t<=D, 0<=t0, t0+n<=D. (7) Indeed `rA,rC<=D` follows from (3), and `n<=e-h` together with `e<=a+b,c+d` proves their lower bounds. The upper bound on t follows from `p+f<=2D`, since both relevant face sums are at most `2D`. Finally `t0+n=max(a+d,b+c)-f` is a face deficit and belongs to `[0,D]`. All these are literal integer inequalities, including walls. Write `Q=zeta^2`, `alpha=zeta^(2h+1)`, `z=zeta^(2e+1)`. The already proved [actual generic source conversion](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md#6-exact-conversion-to-the-seven-factorial-sum-including-its-phase) is the exact identity S=S0 (V_n/C_n) G_n, G_n=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,Q^(-p-f-1),alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q^(t0+1),Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_k. (8) This is the actual finite generic series BEFORE specializing q. By (6),(7), every numerator and denominator factor of every term in (8) is a root unit. For the second upper parameter use `p+f+1=N+t`; its root exponents are those of `Q^-t`, and `k<=n<=t`. For the two spectral factors, their exponent ranges are h+e+1,...,h+e+k in [1,D], h-e,...,h-e+k-1 in [-D,-1]. (9) Thus there is no disappearing generic summand and no singular Pochhammer denominator in this presentation. ## 3. Every summand has positive root value Let `s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N)` and `c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N)`. Direct conversion of each finite Pochhammer in (8) to sine factors gives its kth root summand as A_k product_(i=0)^(k-1)(c_(h+i)-c_e), A_k= s_n/s_(n-k) * s_t/s_(t-k) * s_(rA-k)/s_rA * s_(rC-k)/s_rC * s_t0/[s_k s_(t0+k)] >0. (10) For clarity this is the same finite phase calculation as in the proved folded spectral formula; it only requires the inequalities (6),(7), not that every external label is folded. The residual monomial phase is `q^(Nk)` and the residual sign is `(-1)^k`, so both cancel. The spectral factorization uses (alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k = product_(i<k) alpha Q^i (c_(h+i)-c_e) at the root. Since `h+i<e<=D/2` whenever `i<k<=n`, every displayed cosine difference is strictly positive. The term at k=0 is one. Hence the ENTIRE true generic series has a positive common phase at q and a nonzero value `G_n(q)>0`. Each term in (8) is a product of a bounded number of finite unit Pochhammers of lengths O(N), with integer exponents O(N). On the uniform disk |log(zeta/q)| <= c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) every such term divided by its positive root value remains in a small sector about one. This is the elementary unit-factor harmonic estimate proved in the positive-core note: sum the logarithmic changes using `|sin(pi u/N)|>=2 dist(u,N Z)/N`. The bounded number of products, including negative exponents and exponents up to `2N`, only changes the absolute constant. Their positive sum obeys the same estimate. Cauchy inequalities therefore bound every fixed jet of G_n and its inverse relative to their root values. ## 4. Actual prefactor cancellation retains the generic normal It remains essential to check the prefactor in (8). Positivity of a substituted polynomial alone would not prove the source theorem. Choose `(a',b',c',d')=(a,b,c,d)` if `a+d<=b+c`, and `(b,a,d,c)` otherwise. The actual source formula gives R=(c+d-e, a+b-e, t0, a'-b'+e, d'-c'+e), S0=(-1)^s [s+1]!/product_(u in R)[u]!, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n], C_n=alpha^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^-rA;Q)_n(Q^-rC;Q)_n]. (12) Every entry of R is in `[0,D]`: these are face deficits, together with t0, bounded by (7). Because the branch is live, 2N<=s+1<3N, 0<=s+1-2N<n. (13) The second inequality follows from `max(a+d,b+c)+f<=2D`. Consequently `[s+1]!` contains exactly `[N]` and `[2N]`, while `(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n` contains exactly one zero factor, namely `1-zeta^(-4N)`. All other factors in (12) are root units by (6),(7). Cancel the common Pochhammers in V_n/C_n GENERICALLY. Then cancel the indicated zero factor using the exact identity [2N]/(1-zeta^(-4N))=zeta^(2N)/(zeta-zeta^-1). (14) If a superscript circle means omitting exactly the indicated factor, the result is the explicit analytic unit identity (-1)^D S/[N]=A(zeta) G_n(zeta), A(zeta)=(-1)^(D+s) zeta^(2N-2hn)/(zeta-zeta^-1) * [s+1]!^(omit N,2N)/product_(u in R)[u]! * (Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n^(omit -2N)]. (15) Every denominator in (15) is now a root unit. No term proportional to `[2N]` in the original seven-factorial sum has been dropped: (15) is an equality of the original generic germs, obtained from the exact finite source transformation and exact cancellation (14). The same unit-factor estimate applies to A and its inverse; the additional monomial has exponent O(N^2), and the extra quantum integer denominator is a root unit. Combining it with the positive G_n gives fixed relative jet bounds for the entire original regular source `(-1)^D S/[N]`. Its root value is the positive original core C, so A(q)>0 as well. The four regularized face factors are analytic units with the already proved uniform relative jet bounds. Therefore (2), its inverse version and its local square-root version follow on the SAME polynomial disk (11). ## 5. Cover all first normals using exact source relations The [first-normal Ward theorem](actual_partner_first_normal_ward_reduction.md) proves, for each opposite pair and every choice of the other bits, k(00)-k(01)-k(10)+k(11)=0. (16) Apply it independently to the three opposite pairs. Every branch is a signed sum of at most 27 branches having at most one high bit in each opposite pair. Thus it remains to handle high sets of size at most three, with no opposite pair. Sets of size zero, one or two are face-supported.
