A three-edge set with one edge of each opposite pair is either a face or the complement of a face, namely a three-edge star. Face sets satisfy (2). Consider a star set. If the branch is tail-free, use the positive-core theorem. If its maximal face sum is repeated, use the proved coherent Fourier bound. Otherwise use the exact controlled first-normal difference from the [Fourier source involution](actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.md#6-the-residual-is-an-exact-partner-involution): |k(B)-k(B*)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2, (17) where B* flips the three edges outside its unique largest face. The unique maximal face cannot be the all-low face complementary to the high star. Every other face shares one of its low edges and replaces its two remaining low edges by their high partners; its sum is at least that of the all-low face. Equality everywhere would also contradict uniqueness. Therefore the maximal face contains two high edges and one low edge. Its complementary flip turns the third high edge low and turns its other two low edges high. In terms of opposite pairs, B* has one pair in state `00` and two pairs in state `11`: a tetrahedral face contains exactly one edge from each opposite pair. Apply (16) to those two `11` pairs. This expresses k(B*) as a signed sum of at most nine branches with at most TWO high bits, all already controlled by (2). Equation (17) controls the star branch. Finally the initial 27-term interpolation proves (1) for every original partner, with constants independent of N, labels and parity. The estimates are on the actual full generic first normals. The proof has not replaced a normal by the root core, differentiated a root-value identity, or imposed the first-order Ward equation on higher orders. The original coherent tail itself now has a uniform bound on EVERY partner branch: |T_B(q)| <= C(1+log N) C_B(q). (18) For a tail-free branch T is zero. Otherwise write the exact germ as `K_B=U_B(C_B+[2N]T_B)^2`, where U_B is the product of the four regularized face factors. The logarithmic derivatives of U_B and the positive core C_B are `O(N^2(1+log N))`. Divide the first normal by `K_B(q)=U_B(q)C_B(q)^2` and use (1). This bounds `[2N]'(q) T_B(q)/C_B(q)` by the same order. Finally |[2N]'(q)|=2N/sin(pi/N)>=2N^2/pi, which proves (18). Thus the contribution of the actual retained tail to the first normal is controlled through an exact positive source presentation; no absolute estimate of its alternating summands was substituted. ## 6. Precise remaining scope This closes the local ALL-PARTNER FIRST-NORMAL scalar gap. Fixed higher normals are proved here for face-supported and tail-free branches. The exact first-normal Ward equation does not extend homogeneously to second order: its cluster trace contributes there. Thus arbitrary higher partner normals, the positive completed physical change-of-frame metric, shared global source constraints, and geometric overlap remain separate problems. Audit: [literal generic source transformation and support checks](../experiments/audit_actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound_results.json). The analytic bounds follow from the proof; the finite checks supplement the source and incidence identities.

title: One explicit divided-current kernel for every original plat source
text: # One explicit divided-current kernel for every original plat source 29 October 2026. The source-specific six-port kernel extends to EVERY fixed plat width. This supplies a concrete, proper original-source restriction before a coherent metric is chosen. It does not infer a sharp energy estimate from a small coefficient in an algebraic projector. ## 1. The actual regular divided currents Use the generic balanced original V_d, d=N-1, and the original coproducts from [the six-port normal-current proof](actual_six_port_divided_power_source_kernel.md). For an ordered block of 2r physical heads let H be its unrolled total weight. The regular first-normal operators are J_E=[Ecal_(2r)^N/(1-zeta^(2N))]_(zeta=q), J_F=[F_(2r)^N/(1-zeta^(2N))]_(zeta=q). (1) These are defined by generic division before specialization. Their ordered divided-coproduct formula is finite, with every nonzero local factorial index<N. They change H by +2N and -2N, respectively. Their normalization and all Cartan signs are those of the literal original matrices, not an abstract replacement representation. Consider the full physical K_total=1 sector Lcal=direct_sum_(k in Z) (V_N^tensor(2r))_(H=2Nk). (2) The source degree space is just its H=0 summand. Sector(2) is NOT being identified with the much smaller Hopf invariant space. ## 2. An ordinary sl2 action is an exact consequence of the normal Ward The generic divided commutation identity gives, at a vector of weight H, E^[N] F^[N]=sum_(t=0)^N [H choose t]_zeta F^[N-t]E^[N-t]. For H=2Nk, EVERY integer k, the root coefficients are [2Nk choose t]_q=0 (0<t<N), [2Nk choose N]_q=2k(-1)^N. (3) Here is a proof including negative k. In the finite product for the last Gaussian, the numerator contains [2Nk]; every other nonzero numerator factor specializes to [-j]=-[j], 1<=j<N. The zero ratio [2Nk]/[N] has derivative ratio -2k at q. Thus its value is (-1)^(N-1)(-2k)=2k(-1)^N. For t<N the numerator zero has no denominator zero. At k=0 the finite product is identically zero, consistent with(3). No semisimple or tilting theorem is used. The exact scalar connecting (1) with divided powers is alpha_N=N q^[-N(N-1)/2]/(1-Q)^N, alpha_N^2 rho^(2N)=N^2(-1)^(N-1), rho=q-q^-1. Consequently on(2) [J_E,J_F]=-N H. (4) Put e=J_E/N, f=-J_F/N, h=H/N. Equations(1),(4) give EXACTLY [e,f]=h, [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f. (5) This is a finite-dimensional ordinary sl2 action on a KNOWN physical sector, derived from the first normal of the actual quantum operators. It is not a statement that the physical braids are positive-unitary, and no Hermitian condition on e,f is assumed. ## 3. A finite explicit right inverse, with no complete-reducibility premise On the h=2 subspace define R=sum_(j>=0) (-1)^j f^(j+1)e^j/[(j+1)!(j+2)!]. (6) The sum is finite. Since |H|<=2r(N-1)<2rN, terms j>r-2 vanish. For r<2 this h=2 space is zero. On a vector v of weight2, (5) gives e f^(j+1)e^j v =f^(j+1)e^(j+1)v+(j+1)(j+2)f^j e^jv. Successive terms in eR cancel, and the first coefficient is 2/(1!2!)=1. Therefore e R=I on the ENTIRE weight2 space. (7) Thus J_E maps its weight0 space onto its weight2 space at every N and width. This argument proves the needed surjectivity directly; it does not import complete reducibility of a classical module. ## 4. The source is exactly that kernel at arbitrary width For an original 2k-head plat put r=k-1 and C=r d. The complete root invariant theorem identifies all invariants with W_r=(V_N^tensor(2r))_(degree C). Its literal coefficient extraction and original turns are those of [the complete source module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), section5. The target of J_E is the physical degree C-N space, call it L_r. If C-N<0 interpret it as zero. Let S_N^(2k) be the saturated specialization of GENERIC invariant tensors inside V_d(zeta)^tensor(2k), as in [the deformable-source construction](actual_six_port_deformable_source_and_recoupling.md). Every generic invariant is killed by the regular divided current. Extraction of its last two colors(0,d) gives ext(S_N^(2k)) subset ker(J_E:W_r->L_r). (8) The extraction proof is unchanged at arbitrary prefix width: fifth in the six-port argument is now head 2k-1. If that head has input c>0, its c ordinary lowerings leave E_prefix^(N-c) E_prefix^c=0 at the root; c=0 retains the full divided prefix operator. Last head color d forces zero lowering there. Thus no endpoint or derivative source is removed. It remains to compare exact dimensions. Write S(z)=1+z+...+z^d, a_j=[z^j] S(z)^(2r), a_j=0 outside its actual support. The full root space has dimension a_C and L_r has dimension a_(C-N). Over generic q, the invariant dimension in 2k heads is the weight-zero dimension minus the weight-two dimension: rank S_N^(2k)=[z^(kd)](1-z) S(z)^(2k). This follows either from the elementary generic highest-vector tensor decomposition, or by observing that each nontrivial even highest weight has one weight0 and one weight2 while the trivial module has only weight0. Using (1-z)S(z)^2=(1-z^N)S(z) and coefficient symmetry a_(C+j)=a_(C-j), its value telescopes to rank S_N^(2k)=a_C-a_(C-N). (9) Surjectivity(7) says the kernel on the right of(8) has exactly the SAME dimension. Saturation makes the specialization injective, so (8) is an equality: BOXED: ext(S_N^(2k))=ker(J_E:W_r->L_r). (10) In the full 2k-head root invariant space this is equivalently the kernel of its total J_E; adjoining total J_F changes nothing because all generic invariant lifts are killed by both. This is a VALUE source theorem: derivatives of the whole source still obey their differentiated inhomogeneous Ward equations, not a falsely homogeneous version of(10). ## 5. A completely explicit all-width source projector On W_r=weight0, (6)--(7) give the algebraic projection I-Re. In the original normal-current normalization its finite formula is P_source=I+sum_(m=1)^(r-1) J_F^m J_E^m/[N^(2m) m!(m+1)!]. (11) For r<=1 the sum is empty. Its range is exactly(10), and it is the identity there; P_source^2=P_source follows from eR=I. For six heads r=2 this reduces to I+J_F J_E/(2N^2), with the previously proved right inverse J_E J_F=-2N^2 I on L_r. All original regular generic braids, interval Casimirs and polynomial circle coupons preserve the source subspace. Therefore (11) may be inserted between their reduced gates on an original source orbit without changing any literal exterior co-source. It need not commute on the larger unrestricted root module, and a root-only Hopf coupon with no regular generic lift is not covered by this assertion. The operator(11) is generally oblique. Its polynomial coefficients in N do NOT make its norm polynomial: J_E and J_F themselves may have exponentially large entries in a specified frame. If a positive metric is needed, the orthogonal projector onto the SAME explicit kernel has norm one. In the physical W_r coordinates, the exact original boundary data satisfy ||w0||=N^[3(k-1)/2], ||lambda||=N^[-(k-1)/2], ||w0|| ||lambda||=N^(k-1). Orthogonal compression does not increase that boundary cost and retains the literal marked cap only after its proved whole-invariant reduction. This does not yet estimate the coherent word energy on(10). ## 6. Consequence for the first genuinely non-tree source block At six heads, the full root module has dimension(2N^3+N)/3, whereas the actual deformable source has dimension(N^3+N)/2. A generic 6j construction belongs on this latter saturated module. It must keep its complete confluence/normal coefficients, and must NOT be equated to the larger raw-root invariant space or to three free scalar circle registers. Formula(10) supplies its missing normal source equation explicitly; formula(11) provides an actual algebraic insertion enforcing that equation before positivity. The sharp analytic task remains the coherent Clebsch/Racah contraction on this constrained source, including its complex corridor and global complement. Neither dimension compression nor the ordinary sl2 relation is a sharp hyperbolic-volume estimate. No additional knot/link equality is claimed here merely from this source theorem.

title: Balanced anchors and the actual alternating-knot source
text: # Balanced anchors and the actual alternating-knot source 28 October 2026. In the exact charged source of an alternating one-component diagram, vanishing of every individual anchor defect forces all overcrossing clocks to be equal. This is a topological incidence statement, not a knot census. For the original figure-eight state the resulting diagonal clock sectors are ALL annihilated, at every level. More strongly, every nonzero clock sector has an anchor defect of size at least (N-1)/2. Thus individual sublinear-defect star estimates, or a positive balanced-anchor chamber alone, cannot cover this actual source. Further clustering/fusion may transport these defects; no statement that such a global method is impossible is made. ## 1. Alternation determines the defect equations Use the exact [charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) and [source closure contraction](actual_general_flow_fusion.md). Put d=N-1. In a strictly alternating diagram, each maximal overbridge is a single crossing. After contracting the original closure-adapter forest, its anchors are the physical oriented segments between successive OVER encounters. Each such segment contains exactly ONE UNDER encounter. Let crossing i be its first over encounter and j its next over encounter. If its under encounter has clock h_l, the three contributions to the anchor's incident linear-factor count are h_i from the first over-output block, d-h_j from the final over-input block, (d-h_l)+h_l=d from the spectator under encounter. A self-loop is counted twice, since it contributes a factor of that anchor at both ends. Phase rescalings from the retained pivots do not change these counts. Hence the EXACT incidence and defect are S_(i->j)=2d+h_i-h_j, delta_(i->j)=S_(i->j)-2d=h_i-h_j. (1) The successor relation on over encounters is one cycle for a one-component knot. Therefore all delta=0 iff all crossing clocks h_i=H. (2) For a link the same conclusion is componentwise. Formula (1) is valid independently of crossing signs. It uses physical over/under roles and survives the exact signed source gluing, rather than identifying successive braid positions with successive physical strand encounters. ## 2. The actual figure-eight cut forces its first clock to zero Take the original signed word [1,-2,1,-2], with clocks (h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3). We retain the original averaged pivotal scalar. The initial use of INTEGER degree conservation to write it as (1/N)Tr[(I tensor g tensor g)W] (3) is made before decomposing into clock sectors, as in the charged source theorem. No Schur lemma or marked-row substitution is applied to an individual h-sector afterward. For the support calculation choose fixed cyclic Fourier grids on head i with root x^(i-1), x=-exp(-pi*i/N). At a positive adjacent crossing these roots differ by x. The outgoing first propagated root is Q^(-1) times its fixed root; the other outgoing root is unchanged. Thus if (a,b;c,e) are its fixed-grid input/output colors, the actual overclock at the first +sigma_1 crossing is h_0=[b-c-1], (4) where brackets mean the representative in 0,...,d. The same-grid crossing is the exact finite Fourier transform of the original R, even where its old raw four-Psi presentation was singular. The closed polynomial port formulas extend there; their normalizer is a nonzero monomial. These clock dictionaries are unchanged by the propagated prefixes. If a positive under-input root has offset Q^v from its fixed position root, its under-output root has offset Q^(v-1), since it is x times the input root. The difference of the two label offsets therefore still gives b-c-1. For a negative understrand the offsets are Q^v and Q^(v+1), giving e-a-1. Thus resetting the grid labels does not silently replace the actual clock variables. Here is its elementary support dictionary. Put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-e], z=[e-b]. The two positive Pochhammers are nonzero exactly when u+v+t+z=d, h_0=u+v. (5) For example the first Pochhammer says u<=h_0 and then v=h_0-u; the second says z<=d-h_0 and then t=d-h_0-z. The negative table gives the same support equation, with its overclock u+z instead. Equivalently supported crossing colors have cyclic lifts b<=e_lift<=c_lift<=a_lift=b+[a-b]. (6) For clarity, the cut-support argument is recalled here. For fixed sentinels L,R define V(x)=[L-x_1]+sum_i[x_i-x_(i+1)]+[x_b-R]. The cyclic interval (6) makes V nonincreasing at every supported crossing: the two outside triangle inequalities have defects which are nonnegative multiples of N, and their middle intervals sum to [a-b]. The trace source (3) has input (A_1,[A_2+1],...) and output (A_1,A_2,...), because the actual pivot is a nonzero scalar times the cyclic shift. Choose L=A_1 and R=[A_b+1]. The endpoint difference of V is zero if A_2=A_1 and -N otherwise. Thus A_2=A_1 and V is constant along every supported source path. Translate colors by -A_1; this changes none of the support tests. The first head begins and ends at zero. The left triangle equality at position1 gives [0-c]=[0-a]+v. Its nonnegative increments must sum to zero, so v=0 at every position1 crossing and that head stays zero. Before the FIRST such crossing the second head stays one: its distance [0-x_2] is nondecreasing and begins at its maximum d. Thus at that first crossing a=0,b=1, so u=v=0. This proves pointwise, for EVERY cut color in the averaged source, nonzero fixed-clock source sector implies h_0=0. (7) This is the same support argument independently proved in [the original cyclic-cut theorem](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md), with its mapping (4)--(5) to the present clocks made explicit. It does not require intertwinement of separately split sectors. The center-independent homogeneous source theorem transports this support calculation back to its original regular frames. ## 3. A second support inequality in the actual reduced polynomial There is also a direct regular-Fermat test of the full reduced four-anchor polynomial. Up to a nonzero scalar, rescale its two anchors B,D by x^(-1), and call the four new variables A,B,C,D. Choose all four new variables to be Nth roots of one. This is permitted by the exact finite-flat source theorem, not a change of invariant or a pointwise replacement of the old raw kernel. The eight actual blocks have the following lengths and root starts: | tail -> head | length | start exponent p in (tail-Q^p head;Q)_L | | --- | --- | --- | | B -> C | d-h_0 | 0 | | C -> A | h_0 | 1 | | D -> A | d-h_1 | h_1+1 | | A -> B | h_1 | -h_1+h_2+1 | | C -> B | d-h_2 | h_0+h_2+2 | | B -> D | h_2 | -h_2-h_3-1 | | A -> D | d-h_3 | -h_1 | | D -> C | h_3 | 0 | This table includes all original closure pivot substitutions. It is a direct application of the actual graph metadata and full-block source contractions. No new graph or exterior coupon is introduced. Let a,b,c,e be the root-grid color indices of A,B,C,D. If a grid summand is nonzero, the D->A block forces r=[e-a] in [0,h_1]. The A->D block forces [a-e+h_1] in [d-h_3,d]. Since r<=h_1, the left representative is the ordinary integer h_1-r. Hence h_1-r>=d-h_3, h_1+h_3>=d. (8) The endpoint cases with an empty block give the same (possibly vacuous) inequalities. If (8) fails, EVERY point on this regular Fermat grid has polynomial value zero. Its exact source coefficient is therefore zero. Thus (8) is necessary for a nonzero h-sector, not merely an absolute-envelope or stationary-point condition. There is an independent pathwise check of (8), in the same cyclic coordinates as Section2. With first cut color zero, the source-cut support forces the four intermediate states to have the form initial (0,1,B+1), after first (0,D,B+1), after second (0,E,F), after third (0,0,F), final (0,0,B), all colors interpreted cyclically. The fourth negative crossing has current clock h_3=[B-1]. If B=0 it is d, proving (8). If B>0, its cyclic interval forces 1<=F<=B. At the second negative crossing h_1=u_2+z_2 with u_2=[B-D]>=0, z_2=[F-B-1]=N+F-B-1>=N-B. Thus h_1+h_3>=(N-B)+(B-1)=d. This argument uses only actual supported paths before summation. The grid offsets just checked show that h_1,h_3 here are the present propagated overclocks, not renamed old-corner variables. ## 4. Balanced diagonal sectors vanish, and defects must be macroscopic For this alternating one-component diagram, (2) makes every balanced clock sector (H,H,H,H). But (7) would force H=0, while (8) would require 2H>=d. As d>=1, these are incompatible. Therefore lambda(P_(H,H,H,H))=0, EVERY N>=2 and EVERY H in 0,...,d. (9) There is no asymptotic qualifier: the WHOLE fixed-H coefficient vanishes exactly in the actual original source. More generally, any nonzero sector has h_0=0 and max_i h_i>=d/2 by (8). Its cyclic clock range is therefore at least d/2. Along the physical four-overencounter cycle, total variation is at least twice the range. In fact the actual physical successor is (3,0,1,2), so the four defects are exactly (-h_3,h_1,h_2-h_1,h_3-h_2). Using (8) gives the stronger explicit bound sum_anchors |delta_i|>=d, max_anchors |delta_i|>=max(h_1,h_3)>=(N-1)/2. (10) Thus no sequence of nonzero figure-eight clock sectors can have all individual anchor defects o(N) in this representation. The positive balanced-anchor maximum principle and the retained sublinear local defect jets are consequently insufficient by themselves for its actual volume contribution. This does not rule out cluster reductions: full-kernel fusion can add opposite defects, and exact phase-aware fusions can change the remaining source variables. Equation (10) must be respected before such a further operation; it does not prove that a macroscopic defect core can never be reduced or analyzed geometrically. ## 5. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_alternating_balanced_source.py The audit verifies the sign-independent physical successor and incidence formula on actual alternating signed words after all original closures, the local cyclic-support dictionary directly against both original R matrices, the general reduced figure-eight block table, and exact zero of every diagonal sector at multiple levels. It separately checks the regular-grid support implications without replacing them by coefficient-modulus estimates.

title: The retained Newton sign and the actual local peripheral branch
status: Local critical scheme; marked peripheral comparison
text: # The retained Newton sign and the actual local peripheral branch 30 October 2026. The actual alternating low-color Newton sum has a localized critical scheme whose eliminated quadratic is exactly the polynomial closure of the original untwisted primitive-collar trace relation. Its selected complete germ is fixed by the already proved collar flags and meridian convention. For positive face variables, however, every real critical Newton index lies OUTSIDE the physical terminating range. The identity does not make that branch a contribution to the original finite sum. This is a local marked algebraic comparison, valid at an actual original port with positive outer and middle face variables. It is independent of bridge width. It does not cover a marked zero-face degeneration, a retained half twist at this port, the discrete endpoint analysis, or a global low-color representation/period. The nearby actual geometric family is already constructed separately; no new global gluing theorem is inferred from this scalar relation. ## 1. Keep the literal Newton coefficient and its sign The [exact Newton source formula](actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction.md), section0, gives T_h=sum_(r=0)^(h-1) (-1)^(h-1+r) b_(h,r) Bhat_r(-T), b_(h,r)=S_r^2 S_(h+r)/[S_(2r+1)S_(h-r-1)], S_j=product_(k=1)^j 2sin(pi k/N). Here 1<=h<=floor(N/2), and the coefficient of x^i y^j c^(m-i-j) in Bhat_r(-T)c^m is exactly [m r]_s [m+r-i-j r]_s [r i]_s [r j]_s. Write a_r for this four-binomial coefficient multiplied by the LITERAL signed b_(h,r). With s_j=2sin(pi j/N), direct factorial telescoping gives, when both terms are in the strict physical support, a_(r+1)/a_r = -s_(r+1)^2 s_(h+r+1) s_(h-r-1) s_(m+r-i-j+1) s_(m-r) ----------------------------------------------------------------. s_(2r+2)s_(2r+3)s_(r-i+1)s_(r-j+1) (0) In particular r+1<h. Its limit on each strict normalized compact is the NEGATIVE of the product on the left of (2). Thus (2) is the actual finite-ratio characteristic; it is not inferred by differentiating only a logarithmic asymptotic with an uncontrolled error. The three other shared-face characteristics follow by the same factorial telescoping in m,i,j. All finite offsets remain in these identities. The port and original q^(dp) character are those of that source identity. Its unwrapped physical support and its actual finite +1 shifts are retained; the calculation below concerns their limiting logarithmic critical equations, not an off-grid finite equality. Use the original Newton variables alpha=h/N, rho=r/N, mu=m/N, xi=i/N, eta=j/N. For 0<rho<alpha<1/2 and the strict nonzero Newton polytope, the genuine positive coefficient b_(h,r) has logarithmic rate B_alpha(rho)=2J(rho)+J(alpha+rho)-J(2rho)-J(alpha-rho), J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi z)) dz. The strict nonzero Newton polytope means rho<mu<1, 0<xi,eta<rho, xi+eta<mu, mu+rho-xi-eta<1. The coefficient's logarithmic rate is K=J(mu)+J(mu+rho-xi-eta)-J(mu-rho)-J(mu-xi-eta) -J(xi)-J(rho-xi)-J(eta)-J(rho-eta). Its shared-face critical action contains K+B_alpha+pi i rho+mu Log(b/c) +xi Log(x/b)+eta Log(y/b), with the fixed pi i alpha character and the rest of the original source still retained. Differentiating in mu,xi,eta gives the first three equations of section2; differentiating in rho gives (2). The finite +1 shifts affect this rate by o(1) on fixed strict compacts. They are not removed from the finite source. Differentiating gives exp(partial_rho B_alpha) =sin(pi(alpha+rho)) sin(pi(alpha-rho))/cos(pi rho)^2 =[sin(pi alpha)^2-sin(pi rho)^2]/cos(pi rho)^2. (1) The exact sign (-1)^(h-1+r) contributes pi i rho to the leading rho action. Its pi i alpha part must ALSO remain in the complete marked action; it is simply independent of rho. With K the actual four-tetrahedron Newton entropy, its retained rho critical equation is sin(pi(mu+rho-xi-eta)) sin(pi(mu-rho)) ------------------------------------------------- * sin(pi(rho-xi)) sin(pi(rho-eta)) [sin(pi alpha)^2-sin(pi rho)^2]/cos(pi rho)^2 = -1. (2) All logarithms use a specified continuation from the positive physical domain before adding the retained pi i character. There is no real interior solution in that domain, since every factor there is positive. This is precisely why its positive capacity maximum cannot be used as an actual saddle. Put Z=exp(2pi i mu), A=exp(2pi i xi), B=exp(2pi i eta), W=exp(2pi i rho), and kappa=4cos(pi alpha)^2. The two rational factors in (2) become (ZW-AB)(Z-W)/[Z(W-A)(W-B)], (W-exp(2pi i alpha))(W-exp(-2pi i alpha))/(W+1)^2. After multiplying their RECORDED denominators and bringing the -1 across, the constant and degree-four terms cancel. Divide only by the exponential unit W. The result is the quadratic (Z-A)(Z-B)(W+1)^2 +kappa (W-Z)(ZW-AB)=0. (3) This identity follows by expansion and contains no asymptotic approximation. The physical source fixes which component, logarithm and contour could be relevant; (3) does not choose them. The parameter kappa has the form of a meridian trace square under the established color marking, but this calculation alone does not identify the remaining variables with actual holonomy coordinates. Equation (3) is valid only off the denominators cleared from (2), including W=A,B,-1 and the original sine factors. At alpha=1/2 the second factor in (1) is identically 1 after cancellation. Then the uncleared equation reduces to W (Z-A)(Z-B)=0. Since W is an exponential unit, it has no generic finite solution. The double root W=-1 of (3) at kappa=0 is therefore extraneous, not an endpoint geometric saddle. Any treatment at that color must use the literal discrete endpoint/pole structure or an independently justified continuation. The coefficient's exact finite offsets and all other original phases remain essential. ## 2. The localized shared-face critical scheme Write the four positive face variables as x,b,c,y, retaining the source input b/output c convention from the Newton coefficient extraction. Let U=exp(2pi i alpha), kappa=(U+1)^2/U. Over the Laurent ring in U,Z,A,B,W and the four face variables, the UNSATURATED equations are b(Z-1)(ZW-AB)-c(Z-W)(Z-AB)=0, x(Z-AB)(W-A)-b(ZW-AB)(A-1)=0, y(Z-AB)(W-B)-b(ZW-AB)(B-1)=0, (Z-A)(Z-B)(W+1)^2+kappa(W-Z)(ZW-AB)=0. (4) The actual regular critical scheme is their localization by the following product of recorded nonzero factors. The saturation ideal defines its closure and has the same restriction on D_reg != 0: D_reg=xybc UZABW (Z-1)(Z-W)(Z-AB)(ZW-AB) (A-1)(B-1)(W-A)(W-B)(W-1)(W+1) (W-U)(W-U^-1). (5) These factors come from the strict sine-product arguments of the literal coefficient and its weight. Some cancel in particular formulas, but are not silently removed from the original regular chart. The choice of the continued logarithms is additional marked data, not encoded by this algebraic saturation alone. At endpoint arguments the unsaturated equations are merely a closure; they are not the actual critical scheme without a separate boundary analysis. The discriminant of the quadratic in W is exactly kappa {kappa(Z^2-AB)^2 -4(Z-A)(Z-B)(Z+1)(Z+AB)}. (6) At leading-coefficient or discriminant zeros it need not have two distinct finite branches. No branch or integration cycle follows from this discriminant. ## 3. Exact elimination using the three shared-face equations The first three equations admit the following direct reduction. Set t=b(ZW-AB)/(Z-AB), L=b+c+x+y, D=xy-bc, E=bc(x+y)+(b+c)xy, A0=x+y. On the regular chart (4) implies A=(xW+t)/(x+t), B=(yW+t)/(y+t), Z=(t-cW)/(t-c), Lt^2+(1+W)Dt-WE=0. (7) The denominators x+t,y+t,t-c are units on (5): if one vanishes, its corresponding unreduced equation forces W=1. For positive faces, LE+D^2=(b+x)(b+y)(c+x)(c+y)>0. Thus the simultaneous exceptional case E-Dt=Lt+D=0 cannot occur, and W=t(Lt+D)/(E-Dt). For this positive-face elimination chart and its nearby complex continuation, additionally localize at E-Dt and (c+x)(c+y). For the reverse reconstruction below also retain L and kappa as units. These are units on the positive locus; they are not consequences of (5) on every complex component. Retain the full pullback of (5) under these substitutions. In particular t, W, t-c and t-cW stay nonzero; Z=0 is not an allowed solution. The first Newton sine ratio has the exact expression exp(K_rho)=-1+W(c+x)(c+y)/[(t-c)(t-cW)]. Its correctly signed remaining equation is kappa(t-c)(t-cW) +(c+x)(c+y)[(W+1)^2-kappa W]=0. (8) After substituting W, the resultant is the unit (c+x)(c+y) times (Lt^2+E)^2-kappa t(t+x)(t+y)(E-Dt)=0. (9) This is another compact polynomial closure. It is used only with the same pulled-back exclusions, not as an unconditional off-grid identity. Eliminating t instead and putting zeta=(W+1)^2/W gives the factor (c+x)^2(c+y)^2 W^2 times (L^2+kappa D)zeta^2 -kappa(2L A0+kappa xy)zeta+kappa^2 A0^2=0. For kappa nonzero, z=zeta/kappa satisfies (L^2+kappa D)z^2-(2L A0+kappa xy)z+A0^2=0, (10) with discriminant kappa[4A0 E+kappa x^2y^2]. Extra roots on excluded divisors are not restored by the calculation. There is an explicit reverse reconstruction on the recorded open chart. If Q1,Q2 denote the left sides of (7)'s last equation and (8), then L Q2-kappa Q1 =(c+x)(c+y)[-kappa(1+W)t+L(W+1)^2-kappa A0 W]. Consequently t=L(W+1)/kappa-A0 W/(W+1) =W(Lz-A0)/(W+1). (10a) If P(z) denotes the left side of (10), direct substitution gives Q1=L W^2 P(z)/(W+1)^2 whenever (W+1)^2=kappa z W. Thus a root of (10), either W satisfying (W+1)^2=kappa z W, and (10a), followed by (7), reconstruct the original four equations whenever all recorded units remain nonzero. This proves equivalence on that open chart, not on its polynomial closure. The extra L unit is explicit; it cannot be inferred from (5) on an arbitrary complex component. ## 4. The real critical indices lie outside the terminating sum Assume x,b,c,y>0 and 0<alpha<1/2, so 0<kappa<4. The leading coefficient L^2+kappa D is positive, the middle coefficient has positive magnitude, and the discriminant in (10) is positive. Hence its two roots are real, distinct and positive. Let P be its left side. Exactly P(1)=(b+c)^2-kappa bc>0, 2(L^2+kappa D)-(2L A0+kappa xy) =2(b+c)^2+2A0(b+c)+kappa(xy-2bc)>0. The second inequality follows from kappa<=4, leaving 2(b-c)^2+2A0(b+c)+kappa xy>0. Thus the vertex lies below1; since P(1)>0, BOTH roots are strictly less than1. On a real unit-circle branch W=exp(2pi i rho), equation(10) reads z=cos(pi rho)^2/cos(pi alpha)^2 in (0,1). Its first-half real representative therefore has alpha<rho<1/2; the reflected representative lies in (1/2,1-alpha). Neither belongs to the ACTUAL terminating Newton range 0<r/N<h/N=alpha. This holds for every positive quartet, not only close to alpha=1/2. In fact these give ALL FOUR regular algebraic critical points over this positive base (before choosing logarithmic windings). For each of the two z roots, the two W roots are distinct, nonreal and on the unit circle. Also P(A0/L)=-kappa A0 E/L^2<0, so Lz-A0 is nonzero. Formula(10a) makes both t and t/W nonreal. It follows that x+t,y+t,t-c,t-cW and E-Dt are nonzero, as are A,B,Z from (7). Their differences A-1,B-1,W-A,W-B,Z-1,Z-W are nonzero multiples of W-1 or t(W-1). The first three equations then exclude Z-AB=0: that would force ZW-AB=0, contradicting Z(W-1)!=0. They also exclude ZW-AB=0. Finally W=exp(+/-2pi i alpha) is impossible because z<1. Every factor in (5) is therefore a unit. No extra positive-base branch is created by (10); all four are reconstructed by (10a). This does not choose the actual source logarithms or cycle. At alpha=1/2, (8) reduces on the saturated chart to the impossible condition (c+x)(c+y)=0. Thus the double W=-1 root of its polynomial closure is extraneous for positive faces, as already noted. At kappa=4 a root of (10) reaches1 only when b=c; the physical endpoint needs its own source treatment. This proves a selection exclusion, not exponential cancellation or an endpoint estimate. A deformation of the actual finite sum or cotangent chain must still account for its endpoints, crossed divisors and marks. No representation of the original group or peripheral branch is inferred from equations(4)--(10) alone. ## 5. The actual primitive-collar polynomial closure and selected germ Use the [actual primitive collar](actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md), sections1--3 and its marked-strip orientation in section5. Its original order is A_in=r_b r_x, B_in=r_y r_b, P=r_y r_x; its corner-preserving sidepairing carries the input b triangle to the output c triangle. This is not the doubled shaded-reflection word. Write u=sin(pi delta)^2, A0=x+y, Dg=A0^2-4xy u, Tb^2=b A0+xy+b^2u, Tc^2=c A0+xy+c^2u, Eb=A0+2bu+2sqrt(u)Tb, Ec=A0+2cu+2sqrt(u)Tc. The literal untwisted primitive collar has R0=Eb Ec/Dg on its selected flag. Write M for its selected auxiliary meridian EIGENVALUE, so the actual determinant-one meridian matrix has eigenvalues M,M^-1. Its marking is M=exp(-pi i alpha), R0=M^-2=exp(2pi i alpha), as in the [geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md), sections1--2. Therefore its trace square is kappa=R0+2+R0^-1. (11) Both square roots Tb,Tc are the positive ones at completeness, then continued on the actual marked germ. Eliminating them from (11) gives [kappa Dg-2Dg-2(A0+2bu)(A0+2cu)]^2 -64u^2 Tb^2 Tc^2 =Dg {16[(b+c)^2-kappa bc]u^2 -4(kappa-4)[2A0(b+c)+kappa xy]u +(kappa-4)^2 A0^2}. (12) Retain Dg != 0 and the actual selected square roots; squaring does not make the other sign combinations into the selected collar. For kappa != 4 and z != 1 put v=4u/(kappa-4), v=z/(1-z). After dividing (12) by (kappa-4)^2 and multiplying by (1-z)^2, its quadratic is EXACTLY (10). Equivalently u=(kappa-4)z/[4(1-z)] =-sin(pi alpha)^2 z/(1-z). (13) Thus the first three shared-face equations do identify the remaining Newton polynomial closure with the original untwisted peripheral trace relation, through the explicit rational change (13). This does not identify every critical point or its logarithmic lift with that representation: all earlier units, signs, and actual source support remain necessary. At kappa=4 equation(13) is interpreted by the selected germ limit, not by division at that divisor. The selection is visible already at the complete point. Set Tb0=sqrt(b A0+xy), Tc0=sqrt(c A0+xy). On the selected collar, v -> A0^2/(Tb0+Tc0)^2, z -> A0^2/[A0^2+(Tb0+Tc0)^2]. (14) This is the smaller z-root at kappa=4. The other squared branch uses (Tb0-Tc0)^2 instead; it is not the same selected flag continuation. For b=c it reaches z=1, where the displayed rational transformation is singular. For small real alpha the selected collar has delta = i alpha A0/(Tb0+Tc0)+O(alpha^2), with the stated M convention. Trace square alone would not fix this sign, distinguish a reciprocal collar, or retain the central SL lift. The selected choice is explicitly M_aux=R0^(-1/2) tending to1. Both low external color h and reflected high color N-h have the same limiting trace square; this does not identify their source periods or their selected contribution coefficients. In contrast the REAL Newton representative of either z-root has rho>alpha by the previous section. This gives an explicit separation between the algebraic peripheral branch and the physical terminating Newton support. There is one further marked selector: the two reciprocal W roots of the selected z do not have the same external momentum. Keeping the pi i alpha character, the stationary Newton action has derivative partial_alpha Psi=Log[sin(pi(alpha+rho))/sin(pi(alpha-rho))]+pi i, exp(partial_alpha Psi)=-sin(pi(alpha+rho))/sin(pi(alpha-rho)). (15) This also follows from the literal finite coefficient identity a_(h+1,r)/a_(h,r)=-s_(h+r+1)/s_(h-r), before taking its strict-compact limit. On the first-half branch alpha<rho<1/2 put delta=i beta, beta>0. Equation(13) implies EXACTLY sin(pi(rho+alpha))/sin(pi(rho-alpha))=exp(2pi beta). Indeed sinh(pi beta)=sin(pi alpha)cos(pi rho)/ sqrt[sin(pi(rho+alpha))sin(pi(rho-alpha))], and this equals the hyperbolic sine of half the logarithm of the displayed ratio. Hence (15) is exp(+2pi beta) for this W and exp(-2pi beta) for its reciprocal (rho replaced by1-rho). The already selected complete-core action has partial_alpha S=2pi i delta=-2pi beta. Therefore the RECIPROCAL W branch is the one whose exponentiated external momentum agrees with the actual primitive marking. The first-half W has the opposite external momentum. Both lie outside the terminating Newton range. This comparison is exact on the local selected germ and retains logarithmic winding ambiguities. It does not establish equality of the full Newton and core actions, an additive or monomial normalization, or their original contributing cycles. It provides no contribution coefficient or exponential estimate for the finite alternating sum. ## 6. Verification and remaining source question [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_alternating_newton_peripheral_branch.py) checks the exact cleared identities and discriminants, the original finite signed Newton coefficient ratios against their logarithmic limits, reconstruction of the uncleared shared-face equations, and the UNSQUARED selected collar R0 with its literal meridian orientation, and the finite external ratio selecting the reciprocal W momentum. The finite-coefficient checks retain all original offsets and compare (0) with an independently assembled literal signed factorial coefficient. The calculation isolates a concrete next requirement: continue the actual finite Newton/cotangent chain to the selected marked branch, retaining its terminating endpoints and every crossed divisor. Neither a root of the polynomial closure nor the absence of a real physical critical point proves exponential cancellation, nonvanishing, a regulator equality for the low-color period, or a global volume bound. The peripheral-branch identities do not supply full-action normalization, endpoint analysis, a contribution to the finite sum, or a global low-color volume bound.

title: Exact radial compactification and sublevel transport of strict-Hall source cores
text: # Exact radial compactification and sublevel transport of strict-Hall source cores 28 October 2026. For the original fixed-clock unit-factor source, every strict-Hall core admits an explicit radial retraction which never increases the modulus of its masterfunction. The retraction is piecewise monomial, has uniformly bounded logarithmic differential, and puts every sublevel cycle in a logarithmic box of radius O(log N). In addition, the complete logarithmic metric gives a global horizontal-lift proof that ordinary critical values are the ONLY nonzero finite bifurcation values of this product masterfunction. Consequently the original coefficient torus can actually be homotoped into every sublevel above all its regular critical moduli. This is not yet the polynomial-mass theorem: the horizontal flow in the bounded box need not have a proved uniform complexity or Jacobian bound. The clocks are fixed throughout. Their full coupled critical equations and the original volume bound do not follow from this result. ## 1. The actual source and its strict cores Let k>=2 and f(X)=gamma product_(e=1)^M(alpha_e X_(u_e)-beta_e X_(v_e)) / product_i X_i^(q_i), (1) where u_e!=v_e, |alpha_e|=|beta_e|=1, gamma!=0, q_i are integers, and sum_i q_i=M. All original scalar, pivot and feedback factors which have already been extracted remain in gamma or in the separate clock weight. Loops are evaluated as their exact scalar monomials before (1). For a nonempty proper anchor set I, let m_I count the factors internal to I, C_I its crossing factors, and e_I=q(I)-m_I. Assume 1<=e_I<=C_I-1 for EVERY such I. (2) The source cut theorem gives exactly these strict inequalities in each nontrivial residual SCC after tight cuts and forced factors are removed. They imply C_I>=2 and M>=2. They concern endpoint support, not the nonvanishing of the selected complex coefficient. The function (1) is invariant under common complex scaling. We work on the quotient torus T=(C*)^k/C*, using X_k=1 when a concrete coordinate system is needed. Its original source is the positive generator I=(2*pi*i)^(-(k-1)) integral_(|X_1|=...=|X_(k-1)|=1) f(X) dlog X_1 ... dlog X_(k-1). (3) The divisor f=0 is allowed in this coefficient cycle: the form in (3) is holomorphic there. It is removed only when discussing horizontal lifts over the nonzero base. ## 2. An exact OFF-critical cut derivative Put rho_i=log|X_i|, r_i=|X_i|, and delta_i=S_i-2q_i, where S_i counts the incident linear factors. At any point with f!=0, partial_(rho_i) log|f| =delta_i/2 + (1/2) sum_(e incident i) (r_i^2-r_j^2)/|alpha_e X_i-beta_e X_j|^2. (4) The sign in the numerator always uses i as the first endpoint, irrespective of the displayed orientation of the factor. This follows from Re[a/(a-b)]=(1+(|a|^2-|b|^2)/|a-b|^2)/2. Suppose every radius in I is at least exp(g) times every radius outside I, where g>0. Internal edge terms cancel after summing (4). Also (r_i^2-r_j^2)/|alpha_e X_i-beta_e X_j|^2 >=(r_i-r_j)/(r_i+r_j)>=tanh(g/2). Since delta(I)=C_I-2e_I, the exact high-cut direction V_I=sum_(i in I) X_i partial_(X_i) satisfies Re[(V_I f)/f] >=(C_I-2e_I+C_I tanh(g/2))/2. (5) In particular, for L=log M, (2) gives the uniform quantitative bound g>=L ==> Re[(V_I f)/f]>=1/(M+1). (6) Indeed tanh(L/2)=(M-1)/(M+1), so the right side of (5) is C_I M/(M+1)-e_I >=1-C_I/(M+1)>=1/(M+1). This is an identity and inequality away from the zero divisor, not an evaluation of the critical equations alone. ## 3. Explicit simultaneous gap clipping Order the logarithmic radii rho_(s1)<=...<=rho_(sk), and let g_j=rho_(s(j+1))-rho_(sj). Replace each g_j by min(g_j,L), preserving all arguments. Reconstruct the radii from these new adjacent gaps and then divide all coordinates by their kth coordinate to restore X_k=1. Call the resulting map C:T->T. The reconstruction is independent of the choices among equal radii, so C is continuous across order walls. A semialgebraic homotopy is obtained by interpolating the RADIUS RATIOS, not by using arbitrary real powers. For R_j=exp(g_j), set R_j(s)=(1-s)R_j+s min(R_j,M), 0<=s<=1. (7) Reconstruct as above to obtain C_s, with C_0=identity and C_1=C. Every changing gap stays at least L. Its derivative is nonpositive, and changing gap j is exactly translation in the high-cut direction I_j={s(j+1),...,sk}, modulo common scaling. Therefore (6) implies d/ds log|f(C_s X)|<=0, |f(C_s X)|<=|f(X)|. (8) At a zero of f, a zero factor has equal endpoint radii and equal phased arguments. Its endpoints remain at equal radii throughout (7), so that factor stays zero. Thus (8) extends across f=0 by continuity. Conversely no new zero factor is created: an originally positive radius gap remains positive because L>0, and arguments never change. The same homotopy therefore preserves the arrangement complement as well. Every output gap is at most L. Hence max_i log|C(X)_i|-min_i log|C(X)_i| <=(k-1)log M. (9) The map fixes this clipped region pointwise. It is thus a genuine strong deformation retraction of EVERY sublevel {|f|<=R} onto its intersection with the compact projective box (9). In the X_k=1 gauge, all log radii then have absolute value at most (k-1)log M. The endpoint map C is piecewise monomial in the positive radii. The pieces are indexed only by the k! orders and 2^(k-1) clipped-gap choices. On each piece, its logarithmic radial differential has integer entries bounded by 2; the argument map is the identity. Thus, in the standard Euclidean metric on (rho_1,...,rho_(k-1),theta_1,...,theta_(k-1)), its Lipschitz constant is at most 4k. The same bound holds throughout (7): the derivative of log R_j(s) with respect to log R_j lies in [0,1]. In particular, clipping increases Euclidean logarithmic (k-1)-mass by at most (4k)^(k-1). This statement uses the full real logarithmic metric; it does NOT claim such a comparison with only the absolute holomorphic wedge |dlog X_1 wedge ... wedge dlog X_(k-1)|, which can vanish on a real tangent plane before a nonholomorphic map is applied. Using auxiliary positive r_i with r_i^2=X_i conjugate(X_i), the maps C and C_s have semialgebraic graphs of degree bounded solely in k on each piece (the coefficient M is retained). Images of chains whose algebraic support degrees and multiplicities are polynomial in N therefore still have polynomial support complexity after clipping. No such complexity claim for the INTERIOR horizontal flow is inferred here. ## 4. Complete horizontal lifts: no hidden finite escape Give T its complete flat logarithmic metric. Let J be a compact subset of C* disjoint from all regular critical values of f. Write l_i=(X_i partial_(X_i) f)/f. Their sum is zero by homogeneity, so they define the logarithmic cotangent vector on the quotient. Outside the box (9), there is an adjacent gap greater than L. Equation (6) implies ||dlog f|| >=c_k/(M+1). (10) Here one may take c_k=1/(2sqrt(k)), a conservative quotient-coordinate constant. Inside the box, the set f^(-1)(J) is compact. A factor cannot approach zero there while f stays in J: the denominator is bounded away from zero, all other factors are bounded, and J stays away from zero. There is also no ordinary critical point there by the choice of J. Thus ||dlog f|| has a positive minimum on this compact set. For a piecewise C^1 base path w(t) in J, the standard logarithmic Hermitian dual gives the explicit horizontal vector field dZ/dt=(w'(t)/w(t)) conjugate(l(Z))/||l(Z)||^2, (11) in any orthonormal logarithmic quotient coordinates. Its defining identity is dlog f/dt=w'/w. Its norm is bounded on f^(-1)(J), by (10) outside and the compact positive minimum inside. Local uniqueness and completeness of the logarithmic metric therefore extend its flow for the whole finite path time. Indeed a bounded-speed finite-time path is Cauchy at a hypothetical endpoint; its limit remains in T, and f stays in J, so the ordinary local ODE existence theorem extends it. The same argument applies to every initial point, with smooth dependence on it and on the base path. Lifting a short base contraction and its reverse gives a local smooth trivialization over J. No finite nonzero bifurcation values occur outside the ordinary critical-value set. The outside bound (10) is uniform in N; the compact INSIDE minimum is only proved positive at each fixed N and has no polynomial lower bound here. ## 5. An actual homologous sublevel cycle for the original source There are finitely many regular critical VALUES. The critical locus is algebraic with finitely many irreducible components, and f is constant on each connected component of its regular critical locus. Put Mcrit=max_regular_critical |f|, using zero if that set is empty. Fix R>Mcrit. Over |w|>=R the horizontal lift (11) is complete on every finite closed radial base interval. Choose a smooth radial base homotopy which fixes |w|<=R and moves each point with |w|>R toward modulus R (or toward R+epsilon, followed by a limit). Lifting it wherever |f|>R and using identity elsewhere yields a deformation of T into {|f|<=R+epsilon}; the cutoff can be chosen so that it is the identity at the joining level. Only the compact range of |f| on the original coefficient torus is needed for its transported cycle, so there is no assertion of a uniform infinite-time lift. This produces a cycle Gamma_(R,epsilon) homologous in T to the original torus (3), with |f|<=R+epsilon. Compose it with the explicit clipping map C to put it in (9), preserving that sublevel and its homology class. The holomorphic coefficient form is closed on all of T, so its integral over the resulting cycle is exactly I, including its original scalar. This is a global existence theorem for the required sublevel homotopy, not a selection theorem for any individual critical point. It improves the earlier sufficient macrodeficit condition e_Z>B: strict Hall support alone gives the needed complete logarithmic lift for these PRODUCT masterfunctions. It does not assert that every critical stratum of an arbitrary compactification is regular; a topological horizontal lift on T is the exact conclusion needed here. ## 6. The quantitative step which this proof does NOT supply The endpoint clipping has fixed-dimensional semialgebraic complexity and bounded logarithmic mass distortion. The preceding interior horizontal flow need not be semialgebraic, and no uniform bound for its Jacobian or for the multiplicities of a replacement algebraic chain has been proved. Thus it is not yet valid to combine cycle existence with the earlier polynomial logarithmic-mass lemma and announce |I|<=poly(N) Mcrit. Effective triangulation of the sublevel SET alone would not prove that bound either: one must control a representative of the particular original integral homology class, including its coefficients. The present proof isolates that remaining mass/complexity issue inside an explicit compact logarithmic box, rather than leaving radius escape or asymptotic bifurcation as additional hypotheses. For the knot problem, every claim above still fixes the integer clocks. Their exact feedback, factorial weights and original finite source must remain when constructing the full phase cycle. Neither full critical Hurwitz support nor a general-knot exponential upper bound follows by taking absolute values over these fixed-clock cores. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_anchor_sublevel_radial_transport.py): actual source residual cores, exact off-critical cut derivatives, strict-Hall bounds, modulus-monotone simultaneous gap clipping, and horizontal right-inverse identities. The audit supplements the uniform proof; it does not estimate the unresolved interior flow mass.

title: Long twists in Conway tangles with an algebraic leaf certificate
text: # Long twists in Conway tangles with an algebraic leaf certificate 31 October 2026. This research theorem enlarges the previously proved three-or-more-leaf seed grammar to include two-leaf seeds. Its additional hypothesis is a finite inequality on the selected complete geometric solution. The conclusion concerns the original invariant and the **hyperbolic volume of the knot complement**. It is not a theorem for all arborescent knots. ## 1. The precise class and conclusion Let \(\mathcal R\) denote the literal quarter-turn of an ordered tangle, and let \(h=\mathcal R(L_N)\) be the original complete crossing-circle coupon. Use distinct leaves in each seed and form a fixed finite expression \[ A_s=h^s,\quad s\ge2,\qquad E::=A_s\mid\mathcal R(E)\mid E_1E_2. \tag{1} \] Stacking and turning retain the original strand order, cups, caps, disk framings and scalar normalization. Close \(FG\) by the original cylindrical closure \(C(FG)\), where both children belong to (1). The isolated closure \(C(A_2)\) is excluded. At the unique strict complete optimizer, let \(a_\ell\) be the original leaf coordinate, and put \(X_\ell=\cot(\pi a_\ell)>0\). Assume \[ X_\ell\ge\frac23 \quad\text{at every leaf}. \tag{2} \] Choose a fixed retained half-twist pattern \(\epsilon_\ell\in\{0,1,-1\}\) whose endpoint pairings give one main component without internal circles. At each auxiliary crossing circle insert the independently chosen disk-framed full twist \(R^{-2p_\ell}\). Thus, after all auxiliary circles have been filled, the actual leaf is \[ \mathcal R(R^{\epsilon_\ell-2p_\ell}). \tag{3} \] **Theorem.** For each fixed expression and such half-twist pattern there is a finite threshold \(T(E,\epsilon)\) such that, whenever the fixed signed integers \(p_\ell\) all satisfy \(|p_\ell|>T(E,\epsilon)\), the resulting knot \(K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\) is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N\bigl(K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr). \tag{4} \] Here \(K_N\) is the original marked one-cut invariant with its recorded enhancement. The reduced enhanced Kashaev normalization has an outer factor of unit modulus; the full modified one-cut normalization differs by the recorded factor of modulus \(1/N\). Neither changes (4). This is the comparison proved in the original [normalization theorem](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) and [crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md), not a new normalization chosen to force a volume limit. The diagram and slopes are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. Both parities and composite levels are included. Slopes may have different signs and unrelated magnitudes. There is no bound on the number of leaves, branching or turn depth, but the threshold is allowed to depend on the fixed expression. The knot cusp is never filled: the fillings in this construction remove only the auxiliary crossing-circle cusps. ## 2. Why the condition is finite and algebraic The geometry selects real \(B\) and positive \(X,Y\), with \(B=\cot(\pi b)\) and \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). For a two-leaf seed, \[ B=X-\frac1{2X},\qquad Y=\frac1{2X}. \tag{5} \] For a seed of width \(s\), the corresponding formulas are \(B_s=T_s(X)/U_{s-1}(X)\) and \(Y_s=1/U_{s-1}(X)\), on the branch with the original positive product denominators. Products use the original rational port rules; turns send \((B,X,Y)\) to \((-B,Y,X)\); the two root ports match as \((B,X,Y)\) and \((-B,X,Y)\). Thus (2) is checked on the selected complete gluing branch by the polynomial inequalities \[ X_\ell>0,\qquad 9X_\ell^2\ge4. \tag{6} \] The branch signs and nonzero denominators must be retained. Squaring equations and testing an arbitrary root of their elimination ideal is not the criterion. No quantum limit must be computed to test (6). More precisely, keep intermediate seed ports and all branch inequalities when clearing the positive denominators. These are equations and inequalities over \(\mathbb Q\), using rational tangent coordinates to record the strict angle branches if needed. The local equivalence with the critical-wire equations and their nonsingular Hessian makes the selected point isolated. An isolated point of a semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb Q\) has real-algebraic coordinates. Rational isolating boxes and the retained branch signs therefore turn (6) into an exact algebraic sign test. This does not require the entire complex solution variety to be zero-dimensional. The complete geometry proves, for every proper seed of width \(s\), \[ \cos\frac{\pi}{s+1}<X_\ell<1. \tag{7} \] Consequently every old proper seed with \(s\ge3\) passes (2) automatically. Only the new two-leaf seeds require a test; by (5) it is equivalently \(Y_2\le3/4\). The previously proved isolated closures \(C(A_s)\), \(s\ge4\), also retain their original theorem. There are actual passing expressions with the new seeds. For \(C(A_2\mathcal R(A_2))\), both seed ports are \((0,1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2)\), which are fixed by the turn and match at the root. Their leaves have \(a=\arctan(\sqrt2)/\pi\), all retained gates are strict, and \(X^2=1/2>4/9\). Strict concavity identifies this stationary solution with the complete optimizer. This is a genuine addition to the literal grammar; no topological novelty claim about its resulting knots is needed. ## 3. Source and geometric proof The new issue in admitting \(A_2\) is real: at even level its Newton support stops at \(N-2\), not \(N-1\). The proof does not restore that missing coefficient by changing the source. For any prescribed interior seed output \(b\), choose \[ b/2<a<\min(b,1/2). \tag{8} \] The two leaves and their product are then strict. This construction propagates through actual turns and products. At the closed root the only deleted gate has exact coefficient one and inputs summing to \(d=N-1\). Contract turns and solve that root relation integrally; all remaining wire coordinates form the original primitive lattice. Rounding a strict continuous state in these free coordinates gives admissible states at every sufficiently large level, including even levels. No relation \(2r=d\) is introduced. The original uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state count therefore give the complete variational limit. The boundary barrier and strict concavity give a unique interior optimizer and a negative definite reduced Hessian. The complete port inequality \(-Y<B<X\) starts already at (5), propagates under the same operations, and proves (7). Every complete leaf lies in \((1/4,1/2)\). The unchanged local ideal cells, ordered face maps, closed bowtie cut, edge words and cusp decorations construct the actual complete augmented link complement. The same local shaded pairings handle every retained half-twist pattern. These arguments are written in the [source extension](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md) and [geometric extension](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md). What is new analytically is the quantitative alias estimate. Define \[ \begin{split} J(x)&=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\\ g(a)&=J(2a)-4J(a),\qquad k(u)=-2J(u/2). \end{split} \tag{9} \] The [exact leaf certificate](actual_conway_algebraic_leaf_alias_certificate.md) proves, whenever \(1/4\le a\le\arctan(3/2)/\pi\), \[ k(u)\le g(a)+g'(a)(u-a)-\frac1{2500}, \qquad 0\le u\le1. \tag{10} \] The core envelope has the same supporting plane without this loss, and equality only at the complete leaf. Add the original product supporting planes. All linear terms cancel by the actual closed-wire stationarity equations. Hence every nonempty alias subset has a strict loss, uniformly over its full physical range. The all-core majorant has the same unique complete maximum, giving the remaining physical-color complement gap. All original normal terms, endpoint offsets and both level parities are retained. Inside a fixed strict complex neighborhood the old local coefficient interpolation applies, because its hypotheses are \(1/4<a<1/2\) and strict factorial arguments, not a seed-width condition. With \(H\) leaves the primitive wire lattice has dimension \(2H-3\). The leaf and gate powers together with its Gaussian sum give the same finite analytic packet \[ C_N^\epsilon(\chi) =N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(\chi)e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)} \bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr), \qquad a_\epsilon(0)\ne0. \tag{11} \] The original integer shifts and normalization remain in this formula. Restoring the original source also restores its explicitly stripped unit phase \(\eta_N=\exp[(i\pi(N-1)/4)\sum_\ell\epsilon_\ell]\). Its color Hessian is diagonal at completeness, with entries \(-2\pi X_\ell/(1-\epsilon_\ell iX_\ell)\), whose real parts are negative. Equations (10)--(11), together with the whole complement gap, verify the hypotheses of the existing [original-source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). It proves a nonzero full-sequence asymptotic for the original finite invariant, not only for a selected saddle contribution. For completeness, the action selected by that transfer is \[ S_{\epsilon,p}(\chi)=\Phi_\epsilon(\chi) +\frac{\pi i}{2}\sum_\ell\frac{(\chi_\ell-1)^2}{p_\ell}. \tag{12} \] The marked geometric extension retains \(U_\ell=-2\pi i\chi_\ell\), \(V_\ell=-2\partial_\ell\Phi_\epsilon\), and the absolutely calibrated primitive \(G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon\). At its selected small saddle, (12) imposes the original primitive filling equations \(U_\ell+p_\ell V_\ell=-2\pi i\). The complete-volume anchor and the original representation-volume differential give \[ 2\pi\Re S_{\epsilon,p}(\chi_*) =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr). \tag{13} \] The bounded marked branch completes to the intended smooth hyperbolic knot complement. Combining the full invariant asymptotic with (13) proves (4). ## 4. Arborescent scope and the remaining general problem Each all-filled leaf (3) is a rational tangle. Actual stacking and quarter-turns preserve Conway algebraicity, so their prescribed one-component closure is an arborescent knot. The old loop-free endpoint induction also extends: a two-leaf seed realizes the two types \(I,U\), turns permute types, and products retain at least two feasible choices while avoiding the circle-producing pair. Thus every expression has a constructible knot parity pattern. Full twists preserve that endpoint pattern. The strongest tangent version replaces (2) by \(a_\ell<a_{\mathrm{crit}}\) at every leaf, where \(a_{\mathrm{crit}}\) is the unique root in \((\arctan(3/2)/\pi,1/3)\) of \[ g(a)+(1-a)g'(a)=0. \tag{14} \] Condition (2) is the simpler algebraic sufficient test, with an explicit uniform margin. It is not automatic for every two-leaf tree. For example, the strict complete optimizer of \(C(A_2\mathcal R(A_4))\) has two leaves with \(X=1/\sqrt3\), or \(a=1/3\); their tangent at the genuine alias endpoint \(u=1\) has negative deficit. This disproves an automatic application of this supporting-plane argument. It does not disprove the full source gap or the volume conjecture for that expression. The next general problem is therefore concrete: control the original closed-source aliases when local tangent deficits are not individually positive, allowing compensation through the shared tangle constraints, or find a different estimate preserved under the actual contractions. The theorem above allows any finite number of suitably certified tangles and independently long twists; it does not remove the geometric certificate or cover every arborescent template. Nor does it construct a generic main-meridian quantum A-operator. The selected algebraic boundary branch, its logarithmic lifts and its calibrated period remain essential data beyond an elimination polynomial.

title: Knot complement volume under repeated single-tangle attachments
text: # Knot complement volume under repeated single-tangle attachments 31 October 2026. This research theorem enlarges the previously proved two-or-more-leaf composition class by permitting a single original leaf to be attached to either side of any completed child. The source estimate, ordered geometry and marked peripheral deformation are retained together. The conclusion is the hyperbolic volume of the resulting **knot complement**. Only the auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled; the knot cusp stays unfilled. ## 1. The class and quantifiers Let \(h=T(L_N)\) be the original turned complete crossing-circle coupon, \(T\) the literal ordered quarter-turn, and multiplication the original stack of four-port boxes. Distinct occurrences have independent leaves and auxiliary colors, with their original local disk framings and the original global one-cut mark retained. Define completed expressions by \[ E::=hh\mid T(E)\mid E_1E_2\mid hE\mid Eh. \tag{1} \] The closed class consists of the original cylindrical closures \(C(FG)\) with **both** \(F,G\) completed expressions in (1). Equivalently, any \(h^s\), \(s\ge2\), may be included among the initial blocks. Choose a fixed half-twist pattern \(\epsilon_\ell\in\{0,1,-1\}\) whose literal endpoint pairings give a knot without closed components inside the tangle tree. Such a pattern exists for every expression in this class by the constructive endpoint-pairing induction. At every auxiliary crossing circle insert an independently chosen, fixed disk-framed full twist \(R^{-2p_\ell}\). The resulting rational leaf is the actual tangle \(T(R^{\epsilon_\ell-2p_\ell})\). Write \(K_{E,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)\) for the resulting knot. **Theorem.** For each fixed finite expression and knot half-twist pattern there is a finite threshold \(P(E,\epsilon)\) such that, for all fixed signed integers \(p_\ell\) with \(|p_\ell|>P(E,\epsilon)\), the knot complement is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N\bigl(K_{E,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)\right). \tag{2} \] The number of tangles, nesting depth, and number of single-leaf attachments are arbitrary finite numbers. The signs and magnitudes of the \(p_\ell\) need not agree or be comparable. The expression and all twists are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity, through both parities and composite levels. No threshold uniform over all trees is claimed. Here \(K_N\) is the original marked invariant with the retained enhancement. The [normalization comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) and [original crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) retain an outer unit-modulus factor in the reduced enhanced Kashaev normalization, or the recorded single factor of modulus \(1/N\) in the full modified one-cut normalization. Both give (2). The previously proved isolated closures \(C(h^s)\), \(s\ge3\), are also available from the [two-or-more-leaf theorem](actual_arborescent_two_leaf_long_twist_volume.md). They are inherited cases, not an assertion that every root-leaf closure \(C(hE)\) belongs to (1). The isolated \(C(hh)\) remains excluded. ## 2. Strict geometry and the selected finite source The [source composition proof](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) establishes a strict reduced state at every interior output of every completed expression. At closure only the final forced gate is removed; its exact coefficient is one. Its inputs satisfy \(i+j=N-1\). The original entropy barrier and injective angle maps then give a unique strict complete optimizer with negative definite reduced Hessian. The [geometric composition proof](actual_conway_single_leaf_geometric_composition.md) retains the stationary port variables \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\qquad X^2+Y^2-B^2=1,\qquad -Y<B<X. \] Both completed root children have \(0<X,Y<1\), and these bounds propagate to all completed descendants. At a new leaf attachment, \[ B_p=X-\frac1{X+B},\qquad Y_p=\frac{Y}{X+B},\qquad X+B>0. \tag{3} \] The proper parent and child bounds imply \(1<2X(X+B)<4X^2\). The \(hh\) base gives the same lower bound from \(Y_p=1/(2X)<1\). Every physical leaf consequently satisfies \[ \frac12<X_\ell=\cot(\pi a_\ell)<1, \qquad \frac14<a_\ell<\frac{\arctan2}{\pi}. \tag{4} \] This is automatic for (1), not an extra test of individual knots. It supplies the strict high-index window required by the original [signed complex packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md). With \(H\) original leaves, the primitive wire lattice has dimension \(2H-3\). Turns impose \(r\mapsto N-1-r\), and one root variable is eliminated integrally; no constraint \(2r=N-1\) is introduced. Strict-state rounding works at every sufficiently large level. The \(H\) leaf factors and \(H-2\) retained gates have total prefactor \(N^{3-H}\); the lattice Gaussian gives \(N^{(2H-3)/2}\), leaving \(N^{3/2}\). Original integer offsets, Hermite directions and phases remain in the nonzero leading amplitude. The changed color Hessian has diagonal entries \[ -\frac{2\pi X_\ell}{1-\epsilon_\ell iX_\ell}, \tag{5} \] with negative real part. These facts concern the original finite source. The global alias bounds needed to pass to the full invariant are supplied next. ## 3. The estimate that makes a single attachment composable At an actual attachment, let \(\mu=f_E'(b)\) be the child slope and \(\lambda=f_{hE}'(c)\) the parent slope. Use the original leaf actions \(g,k\), gate action \(m\), and true support tetrahedron \[ D=\{(x,y,z):x,y\ge0,\ \max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}. \] The [single-leaf alias theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md) proves the two dual bounds \[ \begin{aligned} P(\mu,\lambda)&=\max_{D,\ x\le1/2} [g(x)+m(x,y,z)+\mu y-\lambda z],\\ Q(\mu,\lambda)&=\max_D [k(x)+m(x,y,z)+\mu y-\lambda z],\\ P(\mu,\lambda)-Q(\mu,\lambda)&\ge\frac1{2500} \quad\text{at every proper attachment.} \end{aligned} \tag{6} \] The child enters through its output tangent \(\mu y\); it is not replaced by a bare leaf. For \(1/2<X\le2/3\), the actual slopes lie in \([-2\log2,0]^2\). A finite rational certificate proves the stronger gap \(1/1000\) on that entire square: 55 dyadic rectangles, four slope corners, and the four exact vertices of \(D\) give 880 outward-rounded rational inequalities. A feasible pure state bounds \(P\) below; a global concave tangent bounds \(Q\) above. The [portable verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate.py) uses no numerical optimizer. For \(X\ge2/3\), the retained individual leaf certificate supplies the margin \(1/2500\). A separate monotone response argument and four-vertex endpoint certificate strengthen the bound on the actual small-\(X\) port set; they are not needed for (6). For every completed subtree the inductive estimate is its selected output tangent, with zero loss for its core and positive loss for any nonempty alias sector. The \(hh\) block supplies the base. Turns reverse the slope. Completed/completed products add the child tangents and the gate tangent; stationary equations cancel the internal linear terms. At \(hE\) the exact alias split is \[ A_h\star C_E+C_h\star A_E+A_h\star A_E. \tag{7} \] The three terms lose, respectively, the new margin (6), the inherited child margin, and their sum. The kernel \(\star\) retains all original colors, normal directions, and the constraint \(i+j\le N-1\). The same argument applies to \(Eh\). A turn is never replaced by a multiplicative rule. At the completed/completed root the two output tangents cancel on the original closing relation. The \(N-1\) shifts cost \(O(1)\) in the exponent. A fixed tree has only polynomially many wire states and finitely many alias sectors, so a strict whole-source alias gap follows. The all-core concave majorant has the same unique strict optimizer; compactness away from it and the original local far-color estimate give the physical-color complement gap. This supplies both global hypotheses of the [original-source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). ## 4. Why the right-hand side is the knot complement volume The geometry companion constructs the actual augmented-link complement \(Y_E^\epsilon\) from the original ideal pyramids, ordered multiplication prisms, bowtie cuts and signed shaded face pairings. A single leaf uses its original \(\pi/2\) CAP case; a completed input uses its completed CAP case. The completed/completed root retains the original closing maps. The cusp decorations and pointwise edge words give the complete metric, with absolute anchor \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon)=2\pi F_0. \tag{8} \] The original marked deformation retains the primitive auxiliary logs and absolute regulator \[ U_\ell=-2\pi i\chi_\ell,\qquad V_\ell=-2\partial_\ell\Phi_\epsilon,\qquad G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon. \tag{9} \] The changed half-twist correction is included. The full-source transfer gives a nonzero asymptotic with selected action \[ S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi) =\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)+\frac{\pi i}{2} \sum_\ell\frac{(\chi_\ell-1)^2}{p_\ell}. \tag{10} \] Its critical equations are exactly the primitive filling equations \(U_\ell+p_\ell V_\ell=-2\pi i\). The marked geometric completion and absolute regulator identity on this same branch give \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*) =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)\right). \tag{11} \] All auxiliary crossing circles have been filled to insert the chosen twists. The main component becomes the knot, and its cusp is unfilled. Thus (11) concerns its knot complement, whereas (8) concerns the starting augmented-link complement. The nonzero full-source asymptotic and (11) prove (2). ## 5. Scope and remaining work The new grammar permits repeated chains \(E_{n+1}=hT(E_n)\), starting from \(E_0=hh\), as well as arbitrary completed products and turns. This is a wider class of literal presentations than the previous seed grammar. Algebraic equalities between closed source scalars do not by themselves prove tangle isotopy or novelty of a knot class. No coverage theorem for every arborescent knot is asserted. Independently turned bare leaves and arbitrary root-leaf closures require further work. For example, \(C(hT(h^s))\) has a strict complete state but inner leaf coordinates exactly \(1/4\). The two transport eigenvalues there are distinct with equal modulus. The subsequent [quarter-index packet theorem](actual_conway_quarter_index_color_packet.md) extends the local selected packet through that boundary. It does not supply the whole-source alias and physical-color estimates for those closures. The completed-root restriction in (1) remains in force. The generic main-meridian quantum A-operator and coverage of all desired arborescent presentations remain open. The present theorem uses the original quantum source and its marked algebraic deformation, with the specified analytic and geometric dependencies.

title: Knot complement volume for arbitrary trees of two-or-more-leaf Conway seeds
text: # Knot complement volume for arbitrary trees of two-or-more-leaf Conway seeds 31 October 2026. This research theorem removes the geometric leaf test from the previous two-leaf extension. The argument contracts an entire two-leaf block before estimating its aliases. The resulting uniform bound applies automatically to every proper seed in the stated grammar. This is an theorem for an explicit arborescent class, not a theorem for every arborescent or hyperbolic knot. ## 1. The class and theorem Start with the original complete crossing-circle coupon \(h=\mathcal R(L_N)\), where \(\mathcal R\) is the actual ordered quarter-turn. Use distinct leaves and fixed finite expressions \[ A_s=h^s,\quad s\ge2,\qquad E::=A_s\mid\mathcal R(E)\mid E_1E_2. \tag{1} \] Use the original cylindrical closure \(C(FG)\), with both children generated by (1), or an isolated closure \(C(A_s)\) with \(s\ge3\). Choose a fixed leaf half-twist pattern \(\epsilon_\ell\in\{0,1,-1\}\) whose literal endpoint pairings give a knot after all auxiliary circles are filled. Such a loop-free pattern can be constructed for every expression. The isolated \(C(A_2)\) is excluded. Insert independently chosen fixed disk-framed full twists \(R^{-2p_\ell}\) at the auxiliary crossing circles. Thus the actual all-filled leaf is the rational tangle \[ \mathcal R(R^{\epsilon_\ell-2p_\ell}). \tag{2} \] **Theorem.** For each fixed expression and knot half-twist pattern there is a finite threshold \(T(E,\epsilon)\) such that, whenever all fixed signed integers satisfy \(|p_\ell|>T(E,\epsilon)\), the resulting knot \(K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\) is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N\bigl(K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr). \tag{3} \] Both level parities and composite levels are included. The number of leaves, branching and turn depth are arbitrary finite numbers. The expression and twists are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity; the theorem imposes neither common slope signs nor comparable slope magnitudes. It does not assert a threshold uniform over all trees. The invariant is the original marked one-cut invariant with its retained enhancement. The reduced enhanced Kashaev normalization has an outer factor of unit modulus, and the full modified one-cut normalization has the recorded single factor of modulus \(1/N\). These are the existing [normalization comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) and [crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). Neither normalization changes (3). Only auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled. The knot cusp remains unfilled, and the right side of (3) is the knot complement volume. Literal rational leaves, actual stacking, turns and the prescribed closure establish arborescent membership; no arithmetic identity of tangle fractions is substituted for those operations. ## 2. The estimate that removes the leaf condition The [complete two-leaf geometry](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md) already proves for every proper \(A_2\) seed \[ \frac12<X=\cot(\pi a)<1,\qquad \cot(\pi b)=X-\frac1{2X},\qquad F_2'(b)=2\log(2X^2). \tag{4} \] Previously a supporting plane at each leaf separately required \(X\ge2/3\). The [uniform block theorem](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) instead includes the original multiplication gate and proves \[ G_{AC}(z),\ G_{AA}(z) \le F_2(b)+F_2'(b)(z-b)-\frac1{100}, \qquad 0\le z\le1,\quad \frac12\le X\le1. \tag{5} \] The proof uses joint concavity and a finite exact rational certificate for the whole slope interval. Each supporting plane bounds the entire allowed polytope, and affine endpoint checks cover each slope interval. It keeps the true \(x+y\le1\) constraint. It does not sample unknown maximizers or extrapolate from selected knots. The [exact finite block transport](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md) groups two original leaves and their one gate without changing the source. Every Hermite term, physical color, phase and normalization remains present. The internal first derivatives vanish at completeness, so the block tangent in (5) has exactly the same derivative on its surrounding wire as the original action. In any sector containing an alias, use (5) on a contaminated two-leaf seed. Larger proper seeds retain their already automatic positive leaf bounds. Sum with the other complete seed and macro-product tangents. The original closed-tree stationarity cancels all free linear terms. The result has a strict gap below the complete source action. The actual \(d=N-1\) shifts cost only \(O(1)\) in the exponent; a fixed tree has polynomially many wire states and finitely many alias subsets. Thus the bound holds for the entire original alias contribution, uniformly in all physical colors. The all-core majorant agrees near the complete point with the strictly concave pure action and has that same unique global maximum. Outside a fixed strict neighborhood it has a compact gap. Inside, the original far-color core estimate supplies the strict loss when any physical color leaves the complete corridor. These facts give both whole-source hypotheses of the filling transfer. ## 3.
