Why the rate is the actual knot complement volume The [two-leaf source proof](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md) retains the exact primitive lattice and all offsets, including the missing even-level top coefficient of \(h^2\). Strict interior rounding supplies every sufficiently large level. Its complex packet has power \(N^{3/2}\) and nonzero leading amplitude, with the actual changed local action \(\Phi_\epsilon\) and explicitly retained unit phase. No new packet is chosen to fit the block estimate. Consequently the [original-source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) gives a nonzero asymptotic for the full invariant, with exponential action at the selected small saddle of \[ S_{\epsilon,p}(\chi)=\Phi_\epsilon(\chi) +\frac{\pi i}{2}\sum_\ell \frac{(\chi_\ell-1)^2}{p_\ell}. \tag{6} \] The geometric extension retains the actual signed augmented-link group, ordered face maps and primitive peripheral coordinates \[ U_\ell=-2\pi i\chi_\ell,\qquad V_\ell=-2\partial_\ell\Phi_\epsilon,\qquad G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon. \tag{7} \] Stationarity of (6) is exactly \(U_\ell+p_\ell V_\ell=-2\pi i\). The absolutely calibrated regulator and marked geometric completion on this same branch give \[ 2\pi\Re S_{\epsilon,p}(\chi_*) =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_{E,\epsilon}(p)\bigr). \tag{8} \] In particular the right side is neither merely the augmented-link volume nor the volume of an unrelated critical solution. Equations (5)--(8) and the nonzero full-source asymptotic prove (3). ## 4. The previously excluded three-leaf closure The [isolated three-leaf theorem](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md) also removes the old exclusion of \(C(A_3)\). Its complete state is \(a=\arctan(2)/\pi\), with pair output \(b=1-a\), \(X=1/2\), and \(F_0=2v_8/\pi\). The block lemma includes this endpoint. The exact full Newton algebra is commutative, so a sector with one or two aliases may pair those aliases first, leaving a core. The block slope equals that core's complete slope, \(-\log4\), and the original closing relation cancels their linear terms. For three aliases, each leaf has upper rate \(v_3/\pi\), and the one retained product has rate at most \(3v_3/\pi\). The elementary telescoping sine-series bound proves \[ F_0-\frac{6v_3}{\pi} =\frac2\pi(v_8-3v_3) >\frac{5747}{25344}>\frac1{100}. \tag{9} \] This supplies the whole-source gap for all seven alias sectors. The all-core maximum and far-color loss give the physical-color complement bound. Its existing primitive three-dimensional packet retains the essential \(N-1\) shift, nonzero amplitude and changed half-twist phases. The existing geometric closure has one completed child and one leaf, so its CAP seam has angle \(\pi/2\); that separate case is retained explicitly. Its actual complete volume, primitive paths and absolute regulator then give the same filling conclusion (3). The already proved isolated closures \(C(A_s)\), \(s\ge4\), continue to apply. Hence every isolated seed closure with \(s\ge3\) is included, while \(C(A_2)\) remains excluded. ## 5. Scope of the enlargement The former local-tangent failure \(C(A_2\mathcal R(A_4))\) is now covered, as are all other fixed expressions in (1) with the prescribed closure. There is no remaining algebraic leaf test to pass. The earlier [leaf-certified theorem](actual_arborescent_algebraic_leaf_long_twist_volume.md) remains valid as a sufficient special case and records the original limitation; the present theorem supersedes that limitation for this grammar. A coverage theorem for every arborescent presentation, or for arbitrary rational-tangle additions outside (1), has not been proved. The exact quantum boundary contraction and the signed estimate must survive those additional operations before claiming that scope. Likewise no generic main-meridian quantum A-operator is produced here. The theorem applies the stated packet and marked-completion results to this recursive class. Extension beyond that class remains a separate question.

title: The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape
text: # The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape 30 October 2026. The actual normalized augmented-plat phase has a nondegenerate channel block at every regular complete geometric point. After eliminating its two local q-Hahn variables on their recorded critical sheets, ALL channel/magnetic mixed second derivatives vanish at the complete channel endpoint. The diagonal entries are exactly H_(xi_i,xi_i)=-4pi i/tau_i, (0) where tau_i is the ACTUAL oriented primitive crossing-circle cusp shape, longitude translation divided by meridian translation. Hence each entry has strictly negative real part. This is a source theorem for every original augmented plat admitting the stated regular complete geometric chart, at any fixed width, with any retained half-twist pattern. The proof identifies the cusp shape directly from the actual meridian and longitude MATRICES. It does not infer that marking by matching a Hessian. It also does not assert that the remaining magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate after removing framing directions, or that a finite source cycle contributes a nonzero Gaussian amplitude. ## 1. A local critical reduction must keep its integer characters Use the fully normalized local phase Theta_epsilon and its rational critical map from [the actual character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Write y for the magnetic variables (tau,u,v), xi for the folded channel, and alpha,beta for the two internal q-Hahn variables. The high physical degree chart uses its proved affine adapter; its phase remains the same function of these LOW coordinates, not the same function with the physical pair product substituted for T. At a regular complete point J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1, both internal critical quadratics have simple roots. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem gives their chosen continuations alpha(y,xi), beta(y,xi) in a small logarithmic neighborhood. The exponentiated equations alone give Theta_alpha=2pi i n_alpha, Theta_beta=2pi i n_beta, with locally constant integers on these roots. Retain these characters and put Theta_tilde=Theta-2pi i(n_alpha alpha+n_beta beta). Then its two internal derivatives are EXACTLY zero. Define the root-reduced phase Theta_bar(y,xi) by substituting these roots into Theta_tilde. Envelope differentiation now gives exp(partial_xi Theta_bar)=R_epsilon =R0(-J)^epsilon. (1) Reducing an unadjusted phase whose internal derivatives are nonzero integer characters would add spurious alpha_xi and beta_xi terms. No choice of these local characters is, by itself, a proof that the corresponding Poisson sector contributes to the original finite sum. ## 2. Endpoint tangential derivatives vanish identically The actual source identities hold on the ENTIRE endpoint root chart: R0|_(J=-1)=1, C=I+bH, H=P+I, H^2=0, (dR0/dJ)|_(J=-1)=2b. (2) The derivative in (2) follows the implicit internal roots, holding the magnetic variables fixed. In particular it is not a derivative taken with their exponential coordinates Z,W incorrectly frozen. The scalar b is recovered from the actual ordered input/output meridians by b=Tr([H,A_in] A_out)/32. The endpoint regulator note's [rational chart](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), with Z=(a-1)/(a+1), W=(b0-1)/(b0+1), gives explicitly b=(2Ta b0-Ta-Tb0+a+b0-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b0-1)]. (3) Here b0 is a chart parameter, not the transport coefficient b. Formula (3) holds in both physical degree charts. The audit differentiates the original general-J rational expression for R0 using Z_J=-P_J/P_Z and W_J=-P_J/P_W, and checks (2) exactly over Q(T,a,b0). Because (-J)^epsilon=1 at J=-1, equation (1) implies partial_xi Theta_bar(y,1/2)=2pi i n_xi (4) for one LOCALLY CONSTANT integer n_xi on each connected marked endpoint chart. It does not automatically imply that this derivative is zero. Nevertheless differentiating (4) in ANY magnetic tangent direction gives partial_y partial_xi Theta_bar=0. (5) This is an identity along the whole endpoint chart, not a numerical vanishing at the geometric point alone. Finally dJ/dxi=-2pi i there, so (1),(2) give partial_xi^2 Theta_bar =-2pi i(2b-epsilon) =-4pi i(b-epsilon/2). (6) The high-degree adapter is independent of xi. Therefore (5),(6) remain valid in the actual high physical coordinates. ## 3. The primitive cusp translations fix the factor and sign The collar is the original threading word [2,1,1,2], followed by the retained main half twist R^epsilon. The [proved endpoint reconstruction](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), section 3, supplies its raw trace -2 auxiliary meridian C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-b)H]. (7) Thus the actual trace +2 meridian is mu=I+(epsilon/2-b)H. The actual disk-framed preferred longitude is P=BA, with no meridian power inserted. Since P=-I+H, its centered trace +2 representative is lambda_centered=-P=I-H. (8) Changing a matrix by its central minus sign changes no projective translation. Conjugate their common parabolic fixed point to infinity. The nonzero nilpotent H then has form [[0,h],[0,0]], h!=0. Equations (7),(8) say that the actual translations are translation(mu)=(epsilon/2-b)h, translation(lambda)=-h. Both primitive paths retain their original collar orientations. Therefore tau_geom=translation(lambda)/translation(mu) =1/(b-epsilon/2). (9) This proves the inverse cusp relation DIRECTLY at the complete point; no nearby deformation theorem or guessed cusp potential is used. With the positive orientation I(mu,lambda)=1, Im tau_geom>0. Substituting (9) into (6) proves (0), including Re(-4pi i/tau_geom) =-4pi Im(tau_geom)/|tau_geom|^2<0. (10) As a sign check, an actual rectangular crossing-circle cusp with c=cot(pi x)>0 has, in the SOURCE half-twist convention, tau_epsilon=2ic/(1-epsilon ic), b=1/(2ic), H_xixi=-2pi/c+2pi i epsilon. (11) Source epsilon=-1 is the geometric '+' collar of the matching-graph geometry note; the two notations should not be silently interchanged. The parameter x in (11) is a geometric rectangle parameter and is not being identified with a general Newton source coordinate. ## 4. The full original plat retains this diagonal block Sum the root-reduced phases of all original circle coupons, together with the original cup, cap, marking and exterior phases. Eliminate only the affine physical-wire degree equations, using coordinates independent of the channel variables. Denote the resulting local phase by F(y,xi_1,...,xi_r). The remaining y coordinates are the original magnetic degrees of freedom; no assertion about their Hessian or framing quotient is made. Cups/caps and the degree constraints introduce no additional channel dependence. At the full endpoint xi_i=1/2, equations (5),(6) give exactly F_(xi,y)=0, F_(xi_i,xi_j)=-delta_ij 4pi i/tau_i (12) at a regular complete geometric point. Off-diagonal channel terms vanish because each local reduced coupon contains only its own channel. The mixed block remains zero under the actual affine degree restriction. In particular the channel block is invertible with negative definite REAL PART in these actual channel coordinates, independently of any magnetic degeneracies. For clarity this statement concerns the marked phase. The integers in (4) remain locally constant, and the original normal equation becomes stationary only in the corresponding specified Poisson sector. Equation (12) does not choose that sector's coefficient in the finite source. ## 5. A local channel elimination, with the color normalization retained There is a limited but useful implicit-function consequence. Subtract the recorded constants 2pi i n_i xi_i from F, and add the actual positive cosine-branch color coupling -2pi i sum_i (xi_i-1/2) chi_i. (13) At chi=0 every point y of a sufficiently small endpoint chart has the channel stationary solution xi_i=1/2. By (12) and continuity, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem solves all CHANNEL equations uniquely for xi=xi(y,chi), near the geometric point. This eliminates only those variables. It does not solve the remaining y equations. At the complete geometric point, partial xi_i/partial chi_j=-delta_ij tau_i/2. (14) The resulting channel-eliminated phase f(y,chi) obeys f_(chi_i,chi_j)=delta_ij pi i tau_i, f_(chi,y)=0, (15) at chi=0. Replacing the cosine sign changes both first derivatives and leaves (15) unchanged. For the displayed positive cosine branch the physical similarity logs are U_i=-2pi i chi_i and V_i=4pi i(xi_i-1/2), so (14) also gives V_i/U_i=tau_i to first order, with the original inverse-meridian sign. The transfer convention writing f''=2pi i tau_packet therefore has tau_packet=tau_geom/2, as already required in the explicitly solved Conway sources. There is no additional factor of two in (0) or (15). What this removes is a genuine local obstruction: the folded channel normal is nondegenerate, its sign is controlled, its mixed second-order coupling to the magnetic coordinates vanishes, and its peripheral coefficient is correctly normalized. What remains includes the magnetic critical scheme and its genuine gauge directions, a selected complex magnetic branch, the physical support/Poisson cycle, boundary and alias estimates, and a nonzero amplitude. The physical channel endpoint is still an endpoint of the finite folded summation domain; this theorem does not turn it into an interior finite-state saddle. Audit: [exact cusp and channel calculation](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.py), [results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian_results.json). No magnetic quotient rigidity, physical cycle or global source estimate follows from the channel-only Hessian theorem.

title: The actual Casimir plat phase and its marked representation germ

text: # The actual Casimir plat phase and its marked representation germ 30 October 2026. On a regular chart at a complete geometric point, the constrained critical scheme of the original augmented-plat phase is isomorphic to the actual marked representation germ modulo one diagonal framing scale. This includes local Artin test rings, rather than only complex points or tangent dimensions. The proof reconstructs shared wire momenta from the event-incidence equations and supplies an inverse which is regular at the parabolic channel endpoint. The phase is the actual normalized Casimir/q-Hahn phase. This is not an application of the older braid-cut scheme claim with its different boundary state. Every original cup, ordinary cap, the unrestricted marked cap after its permitted whole-source degree restriction, and both physical degree adapters occur below. No quantum source quotient or asymptotic selection is asserted. ## 1. Objects and the precise local statement Fix a literal augmented plat, its retained half twists epsilon_v, and its actual outside wires. Its event graph has a vertex for each cup, cap or two-input/two-output circle coupon, and one directed edge for each physical wire between successive events. Identity segments are included in that wire. Let B be its oriented incidence matrix, with +1 at an incoming half-edge and -1 at an outgoing half-edge. The leading degree constraints are B x=b, b_cup=-1, b_cap=1, b_coupon=0. (1) Each connected component has equally many cups and caps, by counting its incoming and outgoing half-edges, so its entries of b sum to zero. The graph can have arbitrary cycles and width. We state the representation quotient for a CONNECTED event graph. The incidence construction below works componentwise without that assumption. A disconnected projection is a split diagram; contracting the connected local crossing-circle boxes does not change that connectivity. Thus the connected case includes an essential nonsplit augmented-plat diagram. Choose one of the actual low/high degree adapters at each coupon and a regular complete geometric point as in [the generic magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). Fix its affine logarithmic lift of (1), its simple internal q-Hahn roots, and all logarithmic characters. All displayed local-map denominators, prefix diagonals, main K+1, and the chosen total F charts are units. We work in the corresponding formal neighborhood over C. The internal roots are eliminated by the exact marked critical reduction in [the channel-Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), not by substituting roots into an unadjusted phase. For each auxiliary circle retain its longitude eigenvalue J_v near -1 and prescribe its physical meridian eigenvalue m_v near 1. The channel equation is the original one R_(epsilon_v)=m_v^(-2). (2) The complete fiber has m_v=1. Equivalently the positive cosine branch uses m_v=exp(-pi i chi_v) and adds 2 Log(m_v)(xi_v-1/2) to the phase, with J_v=exp(2pi i xi_v). Let Crit be the formal scheme given by magnetic criticality on ker B and (2), with the retained integer characters. Let Rep be the actual Morse/ crossing-disk representation germ with the same peripheral marking: main meridians have their exact unipotent eigenvalue +1, auxiliary meridians have selected eigenvalue m_v, and the raw ordered disk product has selected eigenvalue J_v. All the same regular chart conditions hold. The main flag means the kernel of mu-I, NOT an arbitrary invariant line of a trace-two Artin matrix. The auxiliary flag is the selected J_v eigenline of its noncentral disk product. Then there is an isomorphism of formal functors Crit = Rep / T_diag, (3) where T_diag acts by simultaneous projective diagonal conjugation. The quotient has a concrete local slice: set the momentum S on one chosen physical wire to 1. Every such S is a unit. No reductive-quotient existence theorem or reduction of a nonreduced ring is needed for (3). Sections 2--6 give mutually inverse constructions over every local Artin C-algebra with the specified residue point. ## 2. Incidence criticality reconstructs all wire momenta Use physical half-edge variables before imposing (1). At a low coupon take the following ambient extension of its root-reduced phase: s=x_in,1+x_in,2, u=x_out,1, v=x_in,1, f_v=Theta_bar(s,u,v,xi). The second output is recovered by degree conservation. Write D, Y_in, Y_out for the ACTUAL derivatives in the local character note. The four exponentiated half-edge derivatives of this extension are incoming: (D Y_in,D), outgoing: (Y_out,1). (4) For a high coupon use the actual affine function Theta_bar(2-s,u-s+1,v-s+1,xi). Formula (4) remains true with D_high=1/(D Y_out Y_in) and the physical high head coordinates. Thus there is no separate high-degree gauge assumption. Let p_(v,e) be the local derivative of the chosen ambient extension and c_e=exp(sum_(v incident e) p_(v,e)). Magnetic criticality means product_e c_e^(l_e)=1 for every l in ker_Z B. (5) The integer cycle lattice is the full kernel: an oriented graph incidence matrix is saturated. A direct construction is enough here. Choose a spanning tree and one vertex value t_v0=1. Solve along its edges c_e=t_tail(e)/t_head(e). (6) Every non-tree edge satisfies (6) precisely because its fundamental cycle satisfies (5). This constructs unit vertex values over ANY commutative test ring. They are unique up to one common unit per connected component; no extraction of roots is involved. Now define the momentum at each incident half-edge by S_(v,e)=t_v exp(B_(v,e) p_(v,e)). (7) Equation (6) says exactly that the two definitions of S on a wire agree. At a coupon (4),(7) give S_in=(t_v D Y_in,t_v D), S_out=(t_v/Y_out,t_v). (8) This is the original local kernel formula with g=t_v D. Conversely shared momenta satisfying that formula give (7), hence (6),(5). Choosing another ambient extension changes its derivatives by a local multiple of the degree row and merely changes t_v, leaving S unchanged. In additive logarithmic language, (5) is grad F=B^t lambda after keeping the fixed integral character, and t_v=exp(-lambda_v). On a formal Artin neighborhood the exponential is injective on nilpotents. Thus the exponentiated equations and the exactly marked critical equations have the same infinitesimal scheme, not just the same complex zero set. The spanning-tree construction also proves the asserted saturation and the absence of hidden finite scale choices. ## 3. The actual boundary maps have precisely the inverse-pair relation On their actual forced degree fibers, the leading cup, ordinary cap and marked cap phases are respectively pi i(x_1-1), pi i x_1, pi i x_2. (9) The marked restriction x_1+x_2=1 follows only after all other actual caps and degree-preserving coupons act; it is not a local replacement of an unrestricted mark in a degree-changing source. Apply (7) with B=-1 at a cup and B=+1 at a cap. The two momenta are (-t,t) for the cup and ordinary cap, and (t,-t) for the marked cap. All three therefore give X_1 X_2=1, S_1/S_2=-1. (10) For an actual physical head use K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^(-1)-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^(-1)]]. (11) It has determinant one and trace -2. Its exact -1 eigenline is spanned by (1,S). Since K+1 is a unit, this kernel line is unique over the Artin ring; no nilpotent invariant-flag freedom is silently added. Equation (10) is equivalent to the actual based pair product P=I. For the converse, K_total=1 gives X_2=X_1^(-1), while F_total=(1-X_1)(S_1+S_2)=0 forces S_1=-S_2 because 1-X_1 is a unit. These are identities over the test ring. The ordinary and marked phases differ on the degree fiber by pi i-2pi i x_1; this retained integral character has the same exponentiated relation (10), but must not be deleted from the action. ## 4. A regular parabolic inverse for each actual coupon The local critical map reconstructs actual ordered pair matrices from (X,S), preserves their ENTIRE product P, and fixes Tr P=J+J^(-1). Conversely, given regular incoming and outgoing heads with that product, their ratios S_in,1/S_in,2 and S_out,2/S_out,1 determine their internal q-Hahn roots by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. The Jacobi equation is the actual trace equation, so these roots satisfy the two internal critical equations. Total-F preservation gives the exact D and therefore (8); the regular high adapter gives the same conclusion in the other physical chamber. The chosen simple roots eliminate any additional local root choice in this formal neighborhood. At J=-1 one MUST NOT divide by J-J^(-1) in an Artin ring. Here is an explicit replacement for the local conjugator formula. Put Q=P-J^(-1)I, A=A_in, A'=A_out, c=Tr([Q,A](A'-A)) / Tr([Q,A](Q A-A' Q)), C=I+cQ. (12) At the complete point Q=H=P+I and A'=A+b[H,A]-4b^2H. The denominator in (12) is Tr([H,A]([H,A]-4bH))=32, (13) using Tr([H,A]^2)=32 and Tr([H,A]H)=0. It is a unit throughout the formal neighborhood. The original generic conjugator identity now extends in this regular expression and gives C A C^(-1)=A', [C,P]=0, det C=R0=1+c(J-J^(-1)). (14) For precision, these rational identities hold on the smooth localized internal-root chart before imposing the global critical equations; their specialization therefore holds on nonreduced Artin test rings as well. This is not cancellation by a nonunit in such a test ring. Specify the selected auxiliary eigenvalue m and let h_J=J^(-1)-1, which is a unit near J=-1. The actual physical auxiliary meridian is C_aux=m R0 h_J^(-epsilon) C^(-1)(P^(-1)-I)^epsilon. (15) It has selected J-flag eigenvalue exactly m and det C_aux=m^2 R0(-J)^epsilon=1 (16) by (2). All inverses in (12),(15) are units. At completeness (15) is I+(epsilon/2-b)(P+I), exactly the original primitive collar matrix. Its inverse followed by the retained Hurwitz half twist induces C on the main pair. Thus the auxiliary is the literal disk-framed meridian, not a centralizer chosen only from its eigenvalue ratio. Conversely an actual auxiliary meridian with that eigenvalue commutes with P. Its inverse, composed with the retained half twist, transports the pair. Normalize this projective conjugator to have eigenvalue one on the J^(-1) flag. This divides by a unit even at the endpoint, because the commutant of the noncentral P is the free span of I,P. The normalized matrix is (12), and its eigenratio gives (2). The normalization and the conjugator are unique: at the complete pair a matrix commuting with P=-I+H has form aI+bH; commuting also with A forces b=0 since [H,A] has a unit entry. The same unit linear minor proves this assertion in the whole formal neighborhood. ## 5. Assemble the actual marked representation, and invert it From a critical point, section 2 supplies shared physical heads (11). At every horizontal slice prefix-transport them by their actual lower triangular matrices. The local coupon preserves P, and each cup/cap has P=I, so prefixes outside the event remain unchanged. Physical wires therefore carry the same based meridian at both ends. At each circle, (15) satisfies exactly the original threading relation [2,1,1,2] and the retained main Hurwitz move. These are the literal van Kampen relations of the drilled box; inverse-pair caps close the outside plat. They construct a representation of the actual marked augmented link. For the reverse construction start with that representation and its recorded Morse basepaths. If H_1,...,H_m are the raw trace -2 main meridians at a slice, let P_i=H_i ... H_1, P_0=I and use Bminus(P)=[[1,0],[-P_21,P_11]], G_i=Bminus(P_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(P_(i-1))^(-1), K_i=(P_i)_11/(P_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (17) All denominators are units by the same regular chart. This is the explicit inverse of the actual prefix factorization. It remains valid over the Artin ring. The selected channel eigenvalue fixes the actual trace equation and its unique regular eigenline; the rational inverse from section 4 recovers the internal roots. The local maps then recover (8),(10), and section 2 gives magnetic criticality. No root is chosen by an order, norm, or independent semiclassical convention. Both constructions are inverse before quotienting, except for the one common scale in (6). Multiplying all momenta by t conjugates every matrix by diag(1,t) projectively: upper entries divide by t and lower entries multiply by t. The prefix construction respects that same conjugation. Setting one wire momentum to 1 removes exactly this freedom and proves (3) over all local Artin test rings. ## 6. Consequences and limits of the statement On the complete fiber m=1, (2) fixes J=-1 locally, scheme-theoretically. Indeed R_epsilon-1 vanishes identically on J=-1 and its J derivative there is 2b-epsilon=2/tau_geom, a unit at the actual complete cusp. The formal implicit-function theorem therefore gives J+1=0. This uses the primitive cusp normalization of the channel-Hessian theorem, not a semisimple endpoint quotient. At an irreducible geometric representation, changing the common projective frame supplies the PGL2 orbit; the diagonal scale above has already been quotiented. With the convention rho_g=g rho g^(-1), that scale acts on g by LEFT multiplication. Its two-dimensional local T_diag\PGL2 framing directions therefore remain in the critical scheme. Equation (3) identifies all its additional infinitesimal directions with actual marked representation deformations. This source equivalence alone does not exclude those additional deformations. The following corollary uses a separately checked geometric input. ## 7. With an actual positive certificate, the magnetic radical is exactly framing Assume additionally an ACTUAL marked positive complete ideal gluing certificate for this augmented exterior. The [multi-cusp marked rigidity theorem](general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md) identifies its decorated representation germ modulo PGL2 with a smooth germ whose coordinates are the primitive peripheral eigenvalue logs. It proves this identification on Artin rings, with the exact main eigenvalue conditions used above. Fix all main eigenvalues to +1 and fix the auxiliary eigenvalues m. The unframed germ is then a point. The complete geometric representation is irreducible, so its framed germ is a smooth PGL2 orbit. Equation (3) and its explicit one-scale slice therefore prove Crit at fixed m is smooth of dimension two. (18) This assertion holds formally over nearby auxiliary eigenvalue parameters as well. The dimension comes from the actual T_diag\PGL2 framing quotient, not from deleting two presumed redundant equations or counting variables and equations. At completeness write F for the root-reduced phase after its affine degree restriction, in free magnetic coordinates y and channels xi. The scheme Crit is the zero scheme of its EXACTLY marked derivatives. Consequently its Zariski tangent space is the kernel of Hess F, even before any reducedness assertion. Equation (18) now proves that this kernel is precisely the two-dimensional framing tangent space. The independently proved channel calculation gives Hess F = [[F_yy,0],[0,diag(-4pi i/tau_geom,i)]]. (19) The channel diagonal is invertible. Hence the two framing directions are purely magnetic, and ker F_yy = tangent(T_diag\PGL2), dim ker F_yy=2. (20) There are no further magnetic infinitesimal null directions on this regular positive geometric germ. A local slice transverse to these actual frame directions has a nondegenerate holomorphic quadratic form. This supplies a classical normal form; it is not a computation of an actual source density, a finite quantum gauge factor, or a Gaussian coefficient on the physical summation cycle. ### A nearby classical stationary branch and its absolute action There is now also a holomorphic CLASSICAL stationary branch. Choose a local slice transverse to the two framing directions and keep the geometric sheet's integer Poisson characters fixed. The marked geometric implicit-function theorem solves the representation uniquely on that slice for m_i=exp(-pi i chi_i) near 1. The inverse in (17), the regular internal-root maps, and the fixed local logarithms reconstruct all the actual principal-phase variables holomorphically. Equation (3) proves that these variables satisfy every exactly marked stationary equation. This proves existence; it is no longer an assumption about an unspecified classical critical branch. Its critical value phi(chi) is independent of the transverse framing slice. Along the connected local framing orbit all internal derivatives vanish, so the value of the same marked phase is constant. This statement does not reset any additive period or change an integer mark. The auxiliary-color normalization can be checked directly in the [exact entire core](actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md). Its full-algebra identity centers (-1)^h T_h into cos[pi(N-2j-1)chi]. On the positive cosine branch the order-N coupling is EXACTLY pi i(1-2xi)chi. The finite -1 contributes exp(-pi i chi) to the amplitude, not a new term in the principal phase. The actual main cups/caps, kappa^epsilon factors and original exterior line have no auxiliary chi dependence in this packet. Their known leading constant phases are retained. In particular there is no additional order-N exterior color character to discard or calibrate by the volume. Envelope differentiation and the proved literal peripheral marking give partial_i phi=pi i(1-2xi_i), U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=4pi i(xi_i-1/2), d(2pi i phi)=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. (21) Here U,V are the centered projective meridian and preferred-longitude logs. The negative cosine sign requires the simultaneous reciprocal eigenflag convention stated in the local character note; it gives the same primitive differential with those consistently marked logs. An independently changed exterior color character would change the corresponding linear action/log mark and is not covered by silently reusing (21). The [absolute endpoint regulator comparison](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) now applies to the complete point of this FULL stationary branch and fixes its value: 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D). (22) Finally (21) and dV_i=tau_geom,i dU_i at completeness, or equivalently the channel elimination calculation, give phi_(chi_i,chi_j)(0)=delta_ij pi i tau_geom,i. (23) Thus the general transfer's parameter is tau_packet=tau_geom/2. These are statements about the actual marked PRINCIPAL action on its geometric sheet. They do not prove continuation from the locally lattice-selected q-Hahn roots, a nonzero finite-source cycle coefficient, or a uniform quantum packet with this action. The branch is called geometric here, not source-selected. ## 8. Scope This is a formal classical equivalence. It neither quotients the finite quantum coupon algebra nor replaces its co-source. It does not locate the point in a physical support chamber, continue the source-selected local branches to it, choose its Poisson coefficient, compute a nonzero amplitude, or bound any competing source. The original marked action, peripheral factors and all finite-normal data remain unchanged. Audit: [incidence, boundary and regular centralizer certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.py). The critical-scheme identification retains the stated physical-branch, finite-source-cycle and amplitude limitations.

title: The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator
text: # The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator 30 October 2026. At the complete channel endpoint, the fully normalized q-Hahn coupon phase has the SAME Bloch–Wigner regulator as its original crossing-circle diagram, for every retained half twist. This is an absolute comparison: an exact rational wedge calculation gives a constant regulator difference, and a connected real chart proves that constant is zero. It is not an inference from matching peripheral derivatives. Consequently any regular, correctly marked geometric critical point of the assembled endpoint phase has critical rate equal to the volume of the actual augmented link. Existence of such a point on the source's required logarithmic sheet, a contributing cycle, and a nonzero controlled amplitude are separate questions. This note does not prove a source asymptotic. ## 1. The complete normalized endpoint symbol Use the original phase Theta_epsilon from [the local character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md), equation (1), with its inverse-measure factor H, both q-Hahn columns, and the retained half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i u), V=exp(2pi i v), Z=exp(2pi i alpha), W=exp(2pi i beta). At xi=1/2, J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1 and J0(1/2)=0. Adding H to the two column factorial actions cancels the terms J0(tau-1/2). The remaining factorial part is J0(u)+J0(tau-u)+J0(v)+J0(tau-v) -2[J0(alpha)+J0(1/2-alpha)+J0(beta)+J0(1/2-beta)] -J0(u-alpha)-J0(tau-u-1/2+alpha) -J0(v-beta)-J0(tau-v-1/2+beta). (1) The retained polynomial phase is pi i [(u+v)/2+(tau-1/2)(alpha+beta) +tau+3(epsilon-1)/4]. (2) On the original factorial branch, 2pi i J0(s)=-Li2(exp(2pi i s)) +pi^2(s^2-s)+Li2(1). (3) One verifies (3) by differentiation from 0<s<1 and the common value at s=0, then analytically continues with the recorded logarithmic marks. Thus the Bloch symbol of 2pi i Theta_epsilon is B_H=B(U,Z)+B(V,W), B(X,z)=-[X]-[T/X]+2[z]+2[-1/z]+[X/z]+[-Tz/X]. (4) The half-twist term in (2) contributes a REAL constant to 2pi i Theta, so it contributes no regulator. It does still change the actual auxiliary meridian needed to realize the same main-input/main-output relation. Neither that change nor the coefficient 2 in (4) may be discarded. ## 2. A rational chart for the endpoint critical correspondence Both actual internal q-Hahn equations at J=-1 are rationally parameterized by Z=(a-1)/(a+1), U=T(a-1)^2/(Ta^2+1), W=(b-1)/(b+1), V=T(b-1)^2/(Tb^2+1). (5) Indeed a=(1+Z)/(1-Z), and direct substitution gives the quadratic P(U,Z)=0 of the local character calculation; the same holds for V,W. Every regular endpoint root is represented by this chart away from the listed denominators. The chart has coordinates (T,a,b) in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of C^3. A common nonzero magnetic scale can be fixed at one: it simultaneously conjugates the head matrices and does not change any crossing symbol below. For clarity all reconstructions use the actual physical head matrices K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]]. (6) Put Y(X,z)=-(1-X)(Tz+X)/[(X-z)(T-X)], D=ZW(T-U)(T-V)/[(TZ+U)(TW+V)]. (7) In the low physical degree chart the input heads (X,S) are (V,Y(V,W)), (T/V,1), and the output heads are (U,1/[D Y(U,Z)]), (T/U,1/D). (8) Let A=G1, B=Lminus1^-1 G2 Lminus1, P=BA, H=P+I. Then H is nonzero nilpotent and the endpoint transport is C=I+cH, c=(2Tab-Ta-Tb+a+b-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b-1)]. (9) This follows either by multiplying the explicit matrices or by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32. In particular C A C^-1=A_out. The full ordered product P, including its Borel frame, is preserved. For the HIGH physical degree chart one must use the actual affine index adapter, rather than substitute the physical pair product into (4). Its input and output heads are respectively (V/T,Y(V,W)), (1/V,1), (U/T,D Y(V,W)), (1/U,D Y(U,Z)Y(V,W)). (10) The low variables in (4),(5),(7) remain unchanged. The exact finite high-block identification has no extra phase or scalar. Formula (6) with (10), followed by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32, gives exactly the same coefficient (9) in the high physical chart. The executable certificate checks it independently with the same original crossing rule below. ## 3. Reconstruct the actual auxiliary meridian and every crossing The positive Hurwitz half twist on a trace -2 pair is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I. At P=-I+H its projective normalization is I+H/2. Therefore the raw, trace -2 auxiliary meridian for the original coupon R^epsilon L_N is C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-c)H]. (11) This sign is its actual complete raw lift; the corresponding physical meridian has trace +2. The literal threading word [2,1,1,2] transports the main pair by C_aux^-1 and closes the auxiliary because it commutes with P. Composing its main half twist gives total conjugator I+cH. This uses the [proved original peripheral word](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), not an assigned auxiliary longitude. To recover the actual THIRD Gauss head from (11), let L=Lminus2 Lminus1 and set G3=L C_aux,raw L^-1. Its coordinates are K3=(G3)11, E3=(G3)12, F3=(G3)21/K3. (12) Now execute chronological adjacent crossings [2,1,1,2], and then the signed main crossing R^epsilon if epsilon is nonzero. All maps here are rational. For two input heads (k,e,f),(l,g,h), the original positive crossing, with d=1-eh, is (ld, [dg+e(dl-l^-1)]/k, kh/d), (k/d, e/(ld), l[df+h(d/k-k)]). (13) With physical clocks A0=-1/k, B0=-1/l its five-dilog symbol is [B0]+[1/d]+[1/A0]-[B0/d]-[1/(dA0)]. (14) The original negative crossing has c0=1-(B0/A0)gf and outputs (lc0, kg, f+h/k-f/(l^2c0)), (k/c0, le+g-k^2g/c0, f/l), (15) with symbol [A0]+[c0]+[1/B0]-[A0c0]-[c0/B0]. (16) Call the sum of these FOUR or FIVE actual symbols B_disk,epsilon. Direct rational substitution checks all nine final Gauss coordinates: the first two heads are exactly (8) or (10), and the auxiliary head is exactly (12) again. Thus this is the actual original closed circle, not an abstract centralizer with a missing closing/pivot convention. The closing pivot is a monomial; its complete leading contribution and the main marked cup/cap phases are included in (2) and the global source characters. They contribute no extra dilogarithm symbol. A monomial can still change an action value off stationarity; section 5 treats that point explicitly. ## 4. Exact wedge identity and absolute real normalization With delta[z]=z wedge (1-z), the following identity holds over the rational function field Q(T,a,b), for BOTH physical degree charts and all epsilon in {0,+1,-1}: delta(B_H-B_disk,epsilon)=0. (17) Here is a finite algebraic certificate for (17), including its procedure so no fitted regulator or floating point identity is involved. Use (5) in (4); construct B_disk by (6)--(16); factor every argument and its complement into irreducible polynomials over Q. For an argument z write v_z for its integer exponent vector, retaining positive rational prime factors as well as polynomial factors. Then expand sum_(coefficient n, argument z) n (v_z v_(1-z)^t-v_(1-z) v_z^t). (18) The matrices from (4) and (14),(16) are identical. Only the torsion sign -1 is removed in this rational exterior square; factors such as 2 are kept. The accompanying audit performs precisely (18), symbolically, and records every rational argument and the empty difference matrix. It also independently checks (9)--(13) and the complete auxiliary closure. Thus (17) is an identity of rational functions, not evidence from a finite sample of shapes. One compact form of the COMMON wedge, useful for checking the expansion without comparing two large symbol lists, is as follows. Put A_r=2Tr-T+1, B_r=Tr-r+2, F_r=Tr^2+1. Then BOTH sides expand to 2 T wedge (T+1) +sum_(r=a,b) [ A_r wedge T - A_r wedge F_r +2 A_r wedge (r-1) + B_r wedge F_r -2 B_r wedge (r-1) + F_r wedge r +2 r wedge (r-1) ]. (18a) There are exactly fifteen nonzero coefficients in this polynomial-factor basis. In particular the mixed factors involving both a and b from the actual four-crossing diagram cancel; this is a global identity for the whole coupon, not equality of independent crossing maxima. For any Bloch symbol B the differential of its Bloch–Wigner regulator factors through delta B: dD(z)=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z. Therefore (17) makes D(B_H-B_disk,epsilon) constant on its regular complex parameter chart. This chart is connected: it is obtained from C^3 by deleting finitely many proper polynomial hypersurfaces, and two generic points can be joined by complex lines avoiding their finitely many excluded intersection points. Every rational expression has real coefficients, so the chart contains a generic real point. At that point every argument is real and every Bloch–Wigner value is zero. Consequently D(B_H)=D(B_disk,epsilon). (19) This is the required ABSOLUTE regulator identity. Wedge equality alone would not prove it. Nor does (19) claim equality of integral Bloch classes, flattenings, or complex periods: rational wedge zero can retain information not measured by D. Changes of logarithmic sheet must continue to carry the original integer marks in the action. ## 5. Assemble the actual diagram and the critical action Apply (19) at every original twist-region coupon. The knot-only shortcut H2(M)=0 is NOT used: for a compact connected oriented link exterior H3(M)=0, so the exact sequence makes H3(M,partial M) -> H2(partial M) injective. The displayed degree-one cycle on EACH oriented cusp is precisely the boundary of the relative fundamental class, and hence fixes the relative class uniquely. Accidental developed crossing degeneracies can be avoided by adding their finitely many divisors to the generic frame exclusions, or handled by the continuous extension D(0)=D(1)=D(infinity)=0. Thus at the complete geometric representation sum_regions D(B_H)=Vol(actual augmented link). (20) One can use an actual positive gluing certificate to supply that geometric representation; (20) does not assume convexity of a particular source polytope or independently maximize individual regions. To pass from a Bloch symbol to the original action value, keep the full stationarity condition. In logarithmic variables z=rho+i theta the assembled action G=2pi i phi has the form G=sum n_j Li2(exp(a_j dot z+i pi nu_j)) +(1/2)z^t C z+i k dot z+c0, with real a_j,nu_j,C,k and Im c0=0, and C symmetric. For matching branches the exact identity is Im G-sum n_j D(exp(a_j dot z+i pi nu_j)) =rho dot Im(gradient G). (21) It follows by expanding Im Li2, the real quadratic, and the imaginary linear term; the full proof is in the repo's [wall regulator calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md), section 3. At a FULL stationary point on the recorded marked sheet the right side vanishes. If the channel is held at its endpoint rather than varied, its logarithm is log J=i pi modulo 2pi i and has rho_J=0, so its unsolved normal derivative contributes nothing to (21). Therefore, whenever the complete geometric character is realized by a regular correctly marked full critical point of this actual endpoint phase, 2pi Re phi(0)=Im G(0)=Vol(actual augmented link). (22) The original exterior framing factors of unit modulus add real constants to G and preserve (22). Equation (22) fixes the complete-volume ANCHOR needed alongside the proved primitive differential dG=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. title: An exact analytic function of the auxiliary colors
text: # An exact analytic function of the auxiliary colors Fix an augmented plat diagram: a braid closed by specified cups and caps, with an auxiliary crossing circle around each retained twist region. At quantum level \(N\), the color \(n_i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) labels the representation on the \(i\)th auxiliary circle. The complete color is \(N\), and its deficit is \(h_i=N-n_i\). This note constructs a particular entire function of the scaled deficits. It is a finite cosine sum whose coefficients are contractions of the original quantum operators. At physical high colors it gives exactly the complete-circle part of the invariant. The remaining terms are also specified by an exact identity. This construction is needed before complex stationary phase: an arbitrary interpolation of the integer color values would not preserve the quantum expression being estimated. The finite formula works for every fixed augmented plat and both parities of \(N\). It gives exact Fourier reconstruction and a positive squared-norm identity. Those identities alone do not prove cancellation bounds or a nonzero geometric contribution. Such additional estimates are now established for the [strict Conway class](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and other stated families; this note does not assert them for every plat. ## 1. Splitting one circle operator without losing derivatives Let \(\Omega\) be the original Casimir operator on the pair of physical strands. Write \(T_n,U_n\) for the Chebyshev polynomials of the first and second kinds, normalized by \(T_0=1\), \(T_1(t)=t\), \(U_0=1\), and \(U_1(t)=2t\). The color-\(n\) circle operator is \[ L_n=(-1)^{n-1}U_{n-1}(\Omega/2),\qquad L_0=0. \] At level \(N\), the full pair algebra satisfies \[ P_N(\Omega)=2T_N(\Omega/2)+2=0. \] This polynomial relation includes repeated spectral nodes. Working in its quotient retains the first derivatives at those nodes, which the source notes call first normals. Merely recording the distinct eigenvalues would discard that information. For every integer \(0\le h<N\), the exact circle identity is \[ L_{N-h}=(-1)^hT_h(\Omega/2)L_N+(-1)^NL_h. \tag{1} \] Indeed, the Chebyshev identity \(U_{N-h-1}=T_hU_{N-1}-T_NU_{h-1}\), together with \(T_N=-1\) in the full quotient, gives (1). The first summand is called the core term and the second the alias term. These are names for the two terms of an operator identity; neither name implies an asymptotic estimate. Put \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). The distinct spectral nodes are \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), for \(0\le j\le M\). Let \(L_{N,j}\) be the actual component of \(L_N\) at node \(c_j\), in every physical degree. The [complete compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) specifies these rank-one matrices and their derivative-derived coefficients. On the image of each component, multiplication by \(T_h(\Omega/2)\) acts by its value at \(c_j\): its derivative multiplies the complete-circle square-zero term and vanishes. Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} (-1)^hT_h(\Omega/2)L_N &=\sum_{j=0}^{M}\cos(\pi h m_j/N)L_{N,j},\\ m_j&=N-2j-1. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \] The centering in (2) uses that \(h\) is an integer. The frequencies \(m_j\) are distinct, nonnegative, and all have parity \(N-1\). At an odd level, \(m_M=0\), so the last cosine equals one. No division by a vanishing endpoint sine is involved. ## 2. Defining the whole finite function Fix the original augmented \(2k\)-plat skeleton and its \(b\) retained auxiliary circles. The number \(k\) records the plat width; \(b\) counts the color variables. At circle \(i\), retain the prescribed half twist \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}\), where \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\), followed by the circle operator \(L_{N-h_i}\). For a tuple \(\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_b)\), define \(A_N(\mathbf j)\) as follows: replace the \(i\)th circle operator by \(L_{N,j_i}\), retain \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}\), and perform the original marked contraction. Thus \(A_N\) includes the original cups, ordinary caps, unrestricted marked cap, pivotal factors and external scalar. It is a definite finite coefficient, not an unspecified boundary vector or normalization. For \(\chi=(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_b)\in\mathbb C^b\), set \[ C_N(\chi)= \sum_{j_1=0}^{M}\cdots\sum_{j_b=0}^{M} A_N(j_1,\ldots,j_b) \prod_{i=1}^{b}\cos(\pi m_{j_i}\chi_i). \tag{3} \] This is entire and even in each variable because the sum is finite. For a physical high-color tuple, \(0\le h_i\le M\), equation (2) shows that \(C_N(h/N)\) is exactly the contraction in which every circle uses its core term. At \(h=0\), every alias is \(L_0=0\), so \(C_N(0)\) is the full original complete-color scalar. Let \(Z_N(h)\) denote the full marked scalar at those physical colors. Expanding (1) at all circles gives \[ Z_N(h)=C_N(h/N) +\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,b\}} (-1)^{N|S|}Z_{N,S}(h). \tag{4} \] Here \(Z_{N,S}\) uses \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}L_{h_i}\) at every circle in \(S\), and the complete-image cosine factor of (2) at every other circle. The [all-color Hermite compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md) specifies each contraction, including the normal terms. Equation (4) retains all nonempty alias subsets; it does not say that they are smaller. For a physical low color \(n\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), the usual physical decomposition instead sets its core to zero and takes the full ordinary coupon as its alias. Formula (3) still has values at the corresponding grid points, but they belong to its finite Fourier extension. They are not a redefinition of the physical low-color core. This distinction becomes important when estimating the color complement. ## 3. Recovering the coefficients and their squared norm Define a frequency weight by \(w_j=1/2\) when \(m_j>0\), and \(w_j=1\) when \(m_j=0\). Direct summation gives the exact orthogonality relation \[ \frac1N\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} \cos(\pi h m_j/N)\cos(\pi h m_l/N)=w_j\delta_{jl}. \tag{5} \] To check it, expand the product into exponentials. The differences \(m_j-m_l\) are even integers of absolute value less than \(2N\). The sums \(m_j+m_l\) are also even; their only multiple of \(2N\) in this range is zero, occurring at the odd zero-frequency node. These observations give exactly the two weights above. No assumption that \(N\) is prime is used. Applying (5) in each variable recovers the original contraction coefficients: \[ A_N(\mathbf j)= \frac{1}{N^b\prod_{i=1}^{b}w_{j_i}} \sum_{h_1=0}^{N-1}\cdots\sum_{h_b=0}^{N-1} C_N(h/N)\prod_{i=1}^{b}\cos(\pi h_i m_{j_i}/N). \tag{6} \] The corresponding Parseval identity is \[ \frac1{N^b}\sum_{h_1=0}^{N-1}\cdots\sum_{h_b=0}^{N-1}|C_N(h/N)|^2 =\sum_{j_1=0}^{M}\cdots\sum_{j_b=0}^{M} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{b}w_{j_i}\right)|A_N(\mathbf j)|^2. \tag{7} \] For fixed \(b\), the transform costs only a power of \(N\). However, (7) measures squared magnitudes. It does not make the signed sum \(C_N(0)=\sum_{\mathbf j}A_N(\mathbf j)\) positive or prove that its geometric contribution is nonzero. ### The opposite endpoint and the limits of periodicity Let \(e_i\) be the \(i\)th coordinate vector. Since all frequencies have the same parity, the finite function obeys \[ \begin{aligned} C_N(\chi+e_i)&=(-1)^{N-1}C_N(\chi),\\ C_N(\chi_1,\ldots,-\chi_i,\ldots,\chi_b) &=C_N(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_i,\ldots,\chi_b). \end{aligned} \tag{8} \] Thus it is periodic at odd levels and antiperiodic at even levels. Values near the grid endpoint \(h_i=N\) reflect values near \(h_i=0\). There is a conditional consequence for a proposed global estimate of this extension. Suppose a fixed-neighborhood analytic asymptotic has complete rate \(F_0\) and an amplitude that is not identically zero near the origin. Choose arbitrarily small fixed positive real arguments where the amplitude is nonzero. Nearby grid values have rates arbitrarily close to \(F_0\), and (8) reflects them outside the near-zero neighborhood. Hence this Fourier extension cannot have a fixed exponential gap on the whole complementary cube. If the amplitude is nonzero at zero itself, the sample \(h=1\) already has the complete rate and reflects to \(h=N-1\). That particular moving-sample argument needs nonvanishing at zero, not merely a nonzero analytic function nearby. Periodicity by itself does not give this obstruction. In one variable, the exact reproducing kernel is \[ \sum_{j=0}^{M}w_j^{-1}\cos(\pi m_j\chi) =\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}e^{\pi i(N-1-2r)\chi} =\frac{\sin(N\pi\chi)}{\sin(\pi\chi)}. \tag{8a} \] At \(\chi=h/N\), for \(0\le h<N\), its value is \(N\delta_{h,0}\) at both parities. Multiplying by \(e^{NF_0}/N\) gives complete rate \(F_0\) and zero at every other sample. This example has no fixed-scale analytic neighborhood of the required asymptotic form. It explains why the additional hypothesis, and the physical distinction after (4), must be retained. Finally, the elementary inequality \(|\cos z|\le e^{|\operatorname{Im}z|}\) gives \[ |C_N(\chi)|\le e^{\pi(N-1)\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\chi_i|} \sum_{\mathbf j}|A_N(\mathbf j)|. \tag{9} \] This exact estimate has a linear cost in complex height. The quadratic height control needed for a filling saddle is a stronger analytical statement. ## 4. What this finite construction supplies Formula (3) specifies a regular continuation even at the odd zero-frequency endpoint. Within its stated cosine span it is uniquely determined by the grid values. It does not replace a generic-quantum-parameter germ of the whole pointed invariant. For a general fixed plat, using this function in a filling proof still requires a uniform asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood, a selected contribution on the original integration cycle, bounds for all physical alias terms and far colors, and the actual marked geometric regulator. The complete and mixed compilers expose those quantities but do not themselves estimate them. The twist threshold is attached to the fixed diagram; the frequency scale \(N\) remains the quantum level. The [finite check](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.py) tests the full-algebra split, the centered characters, the tensor Fourier identities and the reproducing-kernel example. Its recorded cases include 162 signed split identities, 204 centered characters and 27 tensor Fourier packets. The proofs above, rather than the number of cases, establish the general identities and their stated limitations.

text: # The actual marked framing density from Casimir-source Ward currents 30 October 2026. local source theorem. This concerns the leading LOCAL density of the actual complete-color augmented-plat source after transverse Gaussian elimination. It retains the original mark, all finite offsets and the actual magnetic top-form. The invariant ordered-flag form alone is not its density: the marked cut supplies a meromorphic factor. No coefficient of this local density in the original global period is asserted. ## 1. Exact white Ward identities on the specified complex-head source Write Q=zeta^2, d=N-1, m=d-a, B=Q^(-N), and use the actual LARGE polynomial H=H_m^B(U,V) of the [generic white-source theorem](actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md). With A0=Q^d=1/(BQ), it satisfies the two exact identities (1-U)H(U/Q,V)+U(1-V)H(U,V/Q) =(1-UV Q^(-m))H(U,V), (1) A0(U-A0)H(QU,V)+U(V-A0)H(U,QV) =(Q^m UV-A0^2)H(U,V). (2) They are polynomial identities in independent complex U,V and generic Q,B, before root specialization. Thus the actual raising and lowering intertwiner equations continue to the selected complex head chart; they are not inferred from agreement on a finite root grid. Here is an elementary finite proof. Put P_j(X)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(X-Q^r), N_b=V^b P_b(U)P_(m-b)(V), H=sum_(b=0)^m c_b N_b. Each N_b individually satisfies (1), by canceling the endpoint factors in P_j(X/Q). For (2), subtract its right side and apply the resulting operator L to one N_b. With M_b=V^b P_b(U)P_(m-1-b)(V), direct factor cancellation gives L N_b=-UV { Q^b(A0-Q^(m-b-1))(Q^(m-b)-1) M_b +A0(A0-Q^(b-1))(Q^b-1) M_(b-1) }. (3) The out-of-range endpoint terms have their displayed zero coefficient. The ACTUAL finite coefficients obey c_(b+1)/c_b =-B Q^(b+1)(1-Q^(m-b))(1-BQ^(m-b)) /[(1-Q^(b+1))(1-BQ^(b+1))]. (4) Substituting A0=1/(BQ) into (3) makes the coefficient of each M_b zero by (4). This proves (2) and its endpoints, with every generic coefficient retained. To check the source convention, the actual white is W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r. The original coproduct F equation is (1-Q^i)W(i-1,j;r-1) +zeta^(-d)Q^i(1-Q^j)W(i,j-1;r-1) =(1-Q^r)W(i,j;r), which is (1). The original Ecal equation gives (2) after multiplying by UV and its fixed monomial. No small/large root collision is used. The K equation is the literal affine degree constraint. The specified cups and inverse caps obey their exact unit-step Ward equations by the moving-factorial recurrence, with the highest weight fixed. For example p_L(x)/p_L(x-1) is -zeta^(L-2x)(1-Q^x)/(1-Q^(L-x+1)). (5) This makes the two terms in Delta(F)p_L cancel identically. Reversing the literal cap and using the same recurrence proves its dual equation. These identities are meromorphic; neither an endpoint pole nor its normal is deleted. The actual signed circle factors, fixed label weights and generic scalar adapters are independent of magnetic heads. ## 2. The actual half-index symbols, and their first transport This section uses the PHYSICAL semiclassical parameter h=Log Q=2pi i/N, not the distinct generic epsilon derivative at one fixed root. Set A=Q^(u+1/2), q=Log A, and for a fixed highest-weight-L head put M_L=zeta^(L+1). The row action of its original balanced generators is K=M_L/A, F=(1-A/zeta)T_-, Ecal=(M_L^(-1)-M_L zeta^(-1)/A)T_+, T_+ f(q)=f(q+h), T_- f(q)=f(q-h). (6) In the Weyl convention Op_W[a(q) exp(sp)]f(q)=a(q+sh/2)f(q+sh), their EXACT symbols are K=M_L/A, F=(1-A)exp(-p), Ecal=(M_L^(-1)-M_L/A)exp(p). (7) Thus there is no order-h subprincipal term in these symbols. At a complete physical head M_L=-1. Different-head products in the original coproduct have the same property. A right matrix action uses the transposed shift; direct substitution gives the same symbol with p reversed. This retains the input/output operator ordering. All half-index shifts and the exact parameters M_L=exp[h(L+1)/2] are kept in the action and amplitude. In particular L/(2N) and (L+1)/(2N) are not identified near the fold. At each finite N, change the already proved selected packet to the half-index variables exactly. Reexpanding it retains the order-one exponential from the shift of its action, as well as the amplitude and coordinate Jacobian. The fixed-derivative estimates for that packet justify this operation; one does not replace it by its limiting phase before making the change. The finite affine offsets and their characters are exactly those already retained in the [complete local marked-density theorem](actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density.md). The total K equation is an affine head constraint, so a trivalent tensor is initially supported on that constraint rather than an ordinary function of three unconstrained positions. Before the next calculation, take a primitive linear Fourier transform in one constrained head. Equivalently eliminate the same primitive affine equation with its full coarea half-density. The retained mixed position/momentum coordinates then give an ordinary local generating family. The Fourier normalization is kept as a base scalar and its Jacobian is kept in the density. This step does not apply an ordinary WKB formula to a delta-supported tensor or discard the K constraint. The first transport implication can be proved directly. Suppose P_h=sum_v a_v(q,h)T^v has Weyl symbol H(q,p)+O(h^2), and P_h[exp(S/h)(b+O(h))]=0 on a regular local Lagrangian chart. Expanding the actual shifted amplitude to first order gives, on H(q,S_q)=0, V dot partial_q b+(1/2)div_q(V)b=0, V=partial_p H(q,S_q). (8) Indeed each term contributes a_v exp(v dot S_q) v dot partial b; its remaining first correction is half the derivative of that same coefficient along v, including v^t S_qq v. Their sum is precisely half the displayed divergence. This is transport of the genuine Lagrangian half-density, rather than invariance of S alone. Primitive linear Fourier/constraint coordinates carry the same formula, by the ordinary Gaussian change of variables with its Jacobian retained. There is a useful normalization check. On the Hom correspondence P_out=P_in=P=[k,e;kf,*], the three principal constraint fields are X_K=(k/2)A_h, X_E=k A_f, X_F=A_e-(f/2)A_h, (9) where A_xi is actual simultaneous conjugation. In invariant group volume their divergences are 0,-e,f. Since X_E Log k=-e and X_F Log k=f, (8) gives k^(-1/2) times invariant half-density, not bare invariant half-density. Turning the input into an outgoing leg by the ACTUAL channel cup removes this adapter. For completeness, in the half-index coordinate u=(r+1/2)/N and lambda=(L+1)/N, the root cup is exp(pi i r) q0^(-r) G_N(r)G_N(L-r)/G_N(L). The uniform interior sine-factorial expansion makes each numerator G_N(Nu-1/2)=sqrt(N)exp[N J(u)](1+O(N^-1)). Therefore its variable amplitude is exp(-pi i u), namely sqrt(K) times a fixed-color scalar. The exact denominator G_N(L), also near the folded endpoint, stays in that scalar. This checks the required modular half-density factor without dropping an endpoint normalization. Equivalently the all-output vertex (W tensor I)p_(2a) is annihilated by its original total K-1,Ecal,F. On P_total=I, their fields are A_h/2,A_f,A_e, so its leading half-density is invariant. Ordinary caps have the dual property. This supplies a local check of the assembly below; it is not an assumption that every scalar kernel is a graph with nonzero mixed input/output Hessian. The latter would be false for the rank-one complete-circle kernel. ## 3. Actual scalar currents for an arbitrary fixed plat Keep the original Morse word, all complete-circle sectors, its cups, caps and the original exposed physical cut. Expand each sector as the literal W/pi network, or use its proved scalar-one exceptional packet with its restoring character. Equations (1)--(5) give its actual intertwiner identities in the independent complex heads. The retained cyclic turns and categorical duals use their original order. The exceptional numerator and its restored integer characters obey the same unit-step identities: an integer-affine exp(2pi i head) character is unchanged by every such shift. Compose the original Hopf-adjoint insertions through this network. There is an explicit finite scalar-current construction. Move each inserted K,Ecal,F through the next vertex using the displayed local identity; pair the two insertions on each contracted wire with its actual cup or cap. Keep every resulting multiplication coefficient. For a shifted factor c and an insertion j the reindexing is exactly j T^v c-(T^(-v)j)c =(T^v-I)[(T^(-v)j)c]. (10) Thus each unmatched internal term is a specified integral difference current, with its insertion shifted in the OPPOSITE direction. Use the original saturated affine head lattice to express these translations in a primitive free basis. The local degree equations ensure that the matched current has zero remaining constraint defect. No independent edge maximization or cyclic wrapping is involved. Ordinary pivotal contractions cancel the matched Hopf insertions. The only cut terms are the literal dual rows of the original mark, computed in the next section. This is the same finite Green-product construction as in the [ordered Gaussian-current calculation](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md), but here its local inputs are the independent-head Casimir identities (1),(2), not a braid mixed-Hessian model. The construction is an algorithm on the actual word and works at every fixed width and both level parities. It retains finite endpoint currents on an original finite domain. In the local regular meromorphic chart it is the corresponding interior current identity; no claim identifying that completion with the whole cyclotomic source is needed below. The principal vector of a local insertion is obtained by differentiating its ACTUAL symbol with respect to p: expansion of a shifted amplitude gives sum_v h_v exp(v dot p)v. Equations (7)--(9) therefore identify the local variations as the actual conjugation fields on its trivalent correspondence. Their propagation through the original shared heads agrees with the explicit incidence/momentum inverse of the [critical-scheme theorem](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md). On the regular complete geometric germ they are tangent to that exact critical scheme. The two cut-compensated combinations below are its two actual framing fields. This uses the source critical-scheme inverse, not merely constancy of the critical action. ## 4. The actual marked co-source, including its sign Use the original balanced cut e_ab=1/N. The one-cut array is diagonal term by term after the other actual caps, by total-degree conservation. For Phi(C)=Tr(eC), the exact dual Hopf rows are e_K=K^(-1)eK-e, e_E=K^(-1)e Ecal-Ecal K^(-1)e, e_F=eF-KF e K^(-1). (11) At complete color, with A=Q^a in the original integer-index convention, their diagonals are (e_K)_aa=0, (e_E)_aa=q0(1-Q)A/N, (e_F)_aa=(1-Q)A/N. (12) These follow by two neighboring matrix entries, with the actual zero end arrows retained. The original scalar summand already contains 1/N. title: The complete geometric disk character is a folded-channel endpoint
text: # The complete geometric disk character is a folded-channel endpoint 30 October 2026. There is a useful general restriction on the branch that the arbitrary-plat source must select. At every complete essential crossing-circle cusp, the ordered product of its two main puncture meridians has trace -2 in the common-trace lift. The classical symbol of the original pair Casimir is exactly this ordered trace. Hence the complete geometric character lies at the ENDPOINT of the folded real Casimir channels, not at a generic interior channel value. This is a geometric character and source-symbol statement. It does not prove that the quantum sum concentrates at that endpoint, that other channels have a gap, or that the complete geometric period has nonzero original coefficient. Those remain analytic tasks. ## 1. The actual crossing disk and its parabolic product Take an augmented plat with the labeled complete geometric certificate of [the matching-graph construction](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Choose one actual twice-punctured crossing disk. Let A and B be its two puncture meridians, transported to a common basepoint in their original order, and put P=BA. The disk's boundary is the peripheral longitude of the crossing circle, up to the recorded orientation and central lift. In particular the auxiliary meridian C commutes with P. Both peripheral generators have nontrivial parabolic complete holonomy: their translation periods generate the actual cusp lattice. The two main puncture flags are distinct. Indeed one cut half disk is the nondegenerate shaded ideal triangle (O,C1,C2), with its two main punctures at C1 and C2. Restoring its disk pairing retains these distinct developed flags for the two based meridians. Consequently A and B are nontrivial parabolics with distinct fixed points. Use the same trace lift for both meridians, as in the original common-color source; its complete head trace is -2. A central sign change of both heads does not change Tr(BA). A nontrivial parabolic C is conjugate in PSL2 to z -> z+1. A determinant-one matrix that commutes projectively with C commutes with its trace-two lift: the alternative sign would change the nonzero trace of that lift. A determinant-one matrix commuting with its trace-two lift has the form P=[[a,b],[0,a]], a^2=1. Thus Tr P is either 2 or -2. To choose the sign, conjugate the two distinct main flags to infinity and zero. Their common negative trace lifts then have the form A=-[[1,s],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[t,1]], s t !=0, Tr(BA)=2+s t. (1) Trace 2 would force st=0, contrary to the distinct nontrivial flags. Therefore Tr P=-2, s t=-4. (2) This argument uses the actual complete cusp and the nondegenerate disk triangle. An arbitrary pair of parabolics, or an unmarked solution of a polynomial relation, would not supply those inputs. Half twists transport the pair by its original Hurwitz map, which preserves the ordered product up to conjugacy. Thus (2) is unchanged by the retained signed half-twist pattern. ## 2. The original quantum character fixes the relevant trace coordinate The [actual adjacent-character identities](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) give, in the original ordered quantum flag algebra, Omega_(12)=tr_q(H_2 H_1). (3) Their principal q=1 symbol is the ordinary ordered trace Tr(BA). The heads are the actual prefix-based meridians, and the cap/Hurwitz presentation identifies their classical tuples with the marked plat representation scheme. Thus (2) imposes c=-2 on this geometric classical pair character. It is not a relabeling of a Newton output coordinate as a knot meridian. The complete-circle source compiler uses the original folded nodes c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), 0<=j<=floor((N-1)/2). Set delta_j=N-1-2j. Then exactly c_j=-2cos(pi delta_j/N), c_j+2=4sin^2(pi delta_j/(2N)). (4) For any sequence of these real nodes, c_j -> -2 if and only if j/N -> 1/2. If delta_j=o(N), the exact relation further gives c_j+2=(pi delta_j/N)^2[1+O((delta_j/N)^2)]. (5) At odd N the last node has delta_j=0 and is the simple endpoint. At even N the last folded node has delta_j=1 and belongs to the paired repeated-root sector. Their original source weights and normal terms therefore cannot be replaced by one parity-blind endpoint evaluation. Equations (3)--(5) locate the complete GEOMETRIC character within the compiler's classical channel coordinates. They do not assert that the other physical wire variables are at endpoints, nor that a stationary phase analysis of the complete coherent sum is finished. Complex contour sectors also require their actual source coefficients. ## 3. The marked peripheral cover resolves the trace ramification Continue the actual preferred crossing-circle longitude from completeness, with centered projective logarithm V. Keep its selected square root ell=exp(V/2), so L=ell^2 is the projective multiplier. In the common head lift the eigenvalues of P are -ell and -ell^-1, up to the recorded inversion of the preferred longitude. Consequently c=Tr P=-(ell+ell^-1)=-2cosh(V/2), c+2=-(ell-1)^2/ell=-V^2/4+O(V^4). (6) The square-root cover ell^2=L is etale on the peripheral torus. The subsequent trace map ell -> -(ell+ell^-1) is ramified at ell=1: it forgets the sign of V and its first-order deformation there. These are different maps. A marked longitude branch carries more first-order information than its trace equation at c=-2. For the real root nodes in (4), one compatible local logarithmic lift is V=2pi i delta_j/N; the reciprocal sheet changes its sign. This matches (6) exactly. It is a coordinate comparison, not an assertion that this logarithm is the quantum source's selected filling cycle. The conclusion for the general plat program is concrete: analyze the complete geometric endpoint on its marked peripheral cover, retaining both level parities and the original repeated-root source. A strict interior real saddle in the raw folded channel coordinate cannot represent (2). The required global source selection is still open. Audit: [trace, ramification and both-parity endpoint identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_geometric_channel_endpoint.py). The all-plat statement follows from the labeled disk/cusp argument and the already proved original quantum character identity, not from the finite-level examples in the audit. The endpoint result distinguishes the étale square-root cover from the ramified trace map. It gives no quantum concentration or gap.

title: The actual local source phase generates ordered character transport
text: # The actual local source phase generates ordered character transport 30 October 2026. The explicit augmented-plat phase has a direct algebraic map to the original ordered pair character. This note proves that map, including the full factorial normalization, its centralizer transport, and its regular parabolic limit on the longitude cover. It is a local critical-phase theorem, not a claimed full-source asymptotic or a new choice of quantum invariant. The remaining global issues are stated in section 6. In particular the local calculation does not assign the source action an absolute manifold regulator merely because its critical equations have the right character. Subsequent comparison: the [regular geometric chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md) supplies an unfolded complete geometric candidate, and the [endpoint regulator theorem](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) fixes its absolute volume anchor under full marked stationarity. Those additional results do not supply the physical cycle or global source estimate left open in this local note. ## 1. Retain the complete normalized coupon phase Use the low physical degree chamber of the [actual compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). Let tau be the scaled pair degree, u and v its output and input first magnetic indices, xi the folded Casimir index, and alpha,beta the two internal q-Hahn variables. All logarithms have the compiler's actual factorial marks. The complete coupon, with retained half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, has leading phase Theta_epsilon=H+Phi(tau,xi,u,alpha)+Phi(tau,xi,v,beta) +pi i[tau+(epsilon-1)(xi+xi^2)]. (1) Its already recorded external kappa^epsilon is not removed or replaced; its leading constant is a unit phase and has no derivative in these variables. The finite offsets and normal-derived coefficients remain those of the exact compiler. Equation (1) is their leading phase, not an equality of finite quantum germs. Write T=e^(2pi i tau), U=e^(2pi i u), V=e^(2pi i v), J=e^(2pi i xi), Z=e^(2pi i alpha), W=e^(2pi i beta). On a regular logarithmic chart the two internal equations are exactly P(U,Z)=0, P(V,W)=0, P(X,Y)=T(J-Y)^2(X-Y)+(Y-1)^2(TY-XJ). (2) Every formula below is localized only where its displayed denominators are nonzero. In particular these equations have not licensed deleting boundary strata. Their leading quadratic coefficients may be assumed nonzero for the symbolic certificate; the rational identities themselves hold wherever their displayed denominators are defined. ## 2. The actual Casimir equation, with its magnetic momentum Direct differentiation of Phi gives Y(X,Z)=e^(Phi_u)=(1-X)(TZ-XJ)/[J(X-Z)(T-X)]. (3) The principal symbol of the original symmetric Jacobi block is a(X)= (X-T)(1-X)/T, d(X)=2X(1+T-X)/T, Omega_cl=a(X)(y+y^-1)+d(X). These follow directly from the physical tridiagonal entries, with q->1 and q^(N-1)->-1. Equation (2) implies a(X)[Y(X,Z)+Y(X,Z)^-1]+d(X)=J+J^-1. (4) This is an exact rational identity modulo P. For example its difference from the right side equals -X(J-T)P(X,Z)/[JT(X-Z)(JX-TZ)]. Thus the critical phase yields the actual ordered pair trace, not just an independently chosen quadratic with the same number of roots. The inverse change is explicit: Z=XJ[y(T-X)+(1-X)]/[yJ(T-X)+T(1-X)]. (5) On its regular chart, the Jacobi equation (4) conversely implies (2). The local root is therefore selected by the actual magnetic momentum y; one does not choose a root by its numerical size. ## 3. Full normalization preserves the ordered product Differentiating ALL terms of (1), including H and pi i tau, gives D=e^(Theta_tau) =JZW(T-J)(T-U)(T-V)/[(TJ-1)(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ)]. (6) Omitting the inverse-measure factorials or their phase would change (6). Introduce an arbitrary nonzero common magnetic scale g. The actual incoming and outgoing raising-shift symbols are (S1_in,S2_in)=(g Y(V,W),g), (S1_out,S2_out)=(g/[D Y(U,Z)],g/D). (7) The signs in (7) follow from a kernel: right multiplication by a raising shift differentiates its input positively, and left multiplication differentiates its output negatively. For a physical head define its original classical flag matrices by K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, Lplus=[[K,E],[0,1]], Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=Lminus^-1 Lplus=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]]. Their product is P=B A=[[T^-1,E_tot],[F_tot/T,F_tot E_tot+T]], F_tot=F1+K1^-1 F2, E_tot=E1 K2+E2. (9) Equations (2),(3),(6),(7) give F_tot,out=F_tot,in, K_tot,out=K_tot,in=T^-1, Tr P_in=Tr P_out=J+J^-1. (10) For F_tot nonzero, (9) then gives E_tot,out=E_tot,in as well. The identity continues wherever the full rational expressions are defined; the present proof uses the stated regular F_tot chart. For reproducibility set g=1 and write f=(1-V)Y(V,W)+T-V. The first equality in (10) is the following explicit certificate: [(1-U)/Y(U,Z)+T-U]-D f = VZ(J-T)(T-U)P(V,W) /[(V-W)(JT-1)(JU-TZ)(JV-TW)].
