It exchanges the total F and E and inverts total K. Therefore the whole high ordered product is preserved as well. There is no independent high frame gauge or differentiation of a root-only identity involved. The high coupon has the SAME channel derivative (12), and the four centralizer identities (14) are also checked symbolically in these physical high coordinates. Thus the local principal map covers BOTH original degree chambers, while retaining their separate integer lifts. ## 4. The channel derivative is a centralizer eigenratio Let R0=e^(partial_xi Theta_0). Direct differentiation yields R0=ZW(J-1)^4(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ) /[JUV(J-Z)^2(J-W)^2(T-J)(TJ-1)]. (12) For J!=+/-1 define the matrix C=I+(R0-1)/(J-J^-1) (P-J^-1 I). (13) Its eigenvalues on the P-eigenlines J and J^-1 are R0 and 1, respectively, so det C=R0 and C commutes with P. Moreover A_out=C A_in C^-1, B_out=C B_in C^-1. (14) These are exact rational identities on (2). An entirely polynomial certificate is obtained by putting Ctilde=(J-R0/J)I+(R0-1)P. Clear only its displayed denominators in Ctilde A_in-A_out Ctilde. Every one of the four resulting entries has zero remainder modulo the two explicit quadratics P(U,Z),P(V,W). The accompanying executable certificate performs this calculation over Q(T,U,V,J), not at sampled roots or numerical shapes. Equations (8),(9) supply all matrices used. The second identity of (14) follows from the first and preservation of P. Thus R0 is the eigenratio of a genuine ordered-pair conjugator. It is not merely a scalar Casimir value. To compare with determinant-one peripheral lifts one must retain the selected square root of R0. For the retained half twist, the FULL derivative is e^(partial_xi Theta_epsilon)=R0(-J)^epsilon. (15) The physical conjugator in (14) is independent of epsilon at fixed magnetic/channel variables. Equation (15) removes the explicit half twist from its peripheral marking. Indeed positive original Hurwitz transport is (A,B)->(A^-1 B A,A); with P=BA it is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I, whose eigenratio is -J^-1. Therefore internal stationarity in the pure spectral phase, R0(-J)^epsilon=1, gives exactly that recorded signed Hurwitz factor. It would be incorrect to call R0 itself the unchanged auxiliary meridian for every epsilon. For the entire core's cosine branch exp[+pi i N(1-2xi)chi], the additional xi derivative is -2pi i chi. Hence its channel equation is R0(-J)^epsilon=e^(2pi i chi). (16) The opposite Fourier branch inverts the right side. The external color deficit chi is distinct from the internal channel xi. The primitive collar is fixed by the original threading word, not by centralization alone. Apply the positive Hurwitz rule chronologically at [2,1,1,2] to the three meridians (A,B,C_aux), and put K=P^-1 C_aux P. The exact three outputs are (K^-1 A K, K^-1 B K, K). Closing the auxiliary sets K=C_aux. Thus the pure physical transport is conjugation by C_aux^-1. The actual zero-self-linking disk longitude is P=BA, with no meridian factor, as proved in the [literal mixed-loop marking](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), sections 4--5. Its argument uses the two underpasses and the absence of an auxiliary self-crossing; it is independent of plat width. On the chosen P eigenflag J=-ell, the primitive auxiliary meridian has eigenvalue M_aux. Hence the pure transport eigenratio is M_aux^-2. The retained main half twist adds the already computed factor (-J)^(-epsilon) to the physical transport and adds no auxiliary longitude detour. Consequently the exact marked relation is R0(-J)^epsilon=M_aux^-2=e^(-U_aux), M_aux=-q^(N-h) -> e^(-pi i chi), U_aux=-2pi i chi. (16a) This calibrates (16) and the primitive collar in the original source convention. Opposite eigenflag choices are retained by the Fourier sign, rather than replacing the projective multiplier by an unmarked square root. ## 5. The endpoint retains additive transport, rather than losing it At the geometric endpoint J=-1, both quadratics (2) have simple roots on any chart where their discriminants are nonzero. Equation (12) obeys R0=1 (17) identically modulo those two endpoint quadratics. Thus complete internal channel stationarity is automatic EXPONENTIALLY; a Poisson/logarithmic sheet is still to be recorded. It does not force C to be identity. Continue the two chosen roots analytically with J. The quotient in (13) has a removable singularity and C=I+b(P+I), b=(1/2) dR0/dJ at J=-1. (18) The derivative in (18) is along the chosen roots of (2), not a derivative with Z,W incorrectly frozen. The matrix H=P+I is nonzero and H^2=0 at an essential complete crossing disk. For common-trace parabolic A,B, Tr(H A)=4. Consequently the same coefficient is recoverable without any limit by b=Tr([H,A_in] A_out)/32. (19) To verify (19), C A C^-1=A+b[H,A]-4b^2 H, while Tr([H,A]^2)=32 and Tr([H,A]H)=0. The positive-certificate disk has distinct puncture flags, so this is its regular additive centralizer, not the central matrix P=-I. On the selected longitude cover set J=-ell=-exp(V_long/2). Then d_(V_long) log R0 at completeness=-b, log[R0(-J)^epsilon]=log R0+epsilon V_long/2. The peripheral differential on a selected stationary branch There is a useful conditional consequence for the FULL assembled core phase, rather than just one local coupon. Envelope differentiation gives partial_i phi=sigma_i pi i(1-2xi_i). (23) On the marked longitude branch centered at xi_i=1/2 put V_i=sigma_i 2 Log(-J_i) =sigma_i 4pi i(xi_i-1/2), U_i=-2pi i chi_i. text: # The complete source has a nonzero local marked density and folded Gaussian 30 October 2026. In a low physical degree t, the EXACT fixed-channel coefficient of the circle is C_(N,a)^epsilon(t;u,v) =kappa^epsilon x^(-t) nu_a^(epsilon-1) h_(t,a) f_a(t,u) f_a(t,v), h_(t,a)=k_a s_t^2/[s_(t-a)s_(t+a-d)], nu_a=(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. (1) Use the literal translated high block when needed. Equation (1) is the [complete root compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md), including the full first-normal circle coefficient; it is not a value-only spectral projector. In particular the original scalar and its endpoint values are h0_a=k_a N s_(2a)/s_a^2, h0_M=N (N odd), h0_M=2N/sin(pi/N) (N even). (2) The latter formula follows from s_(N-2)=N/[2sin(pi/N)] and s_(N/2-1)^2=N/2. The vanishing paired retraction pi_a W_a=0 does NOT make (1) zero. The original nilpotent circle is h0_a W_a pi_a, whose displayed scalar already contains that circle's normal. In a 2k-head plat, keep all k original bottom cups, k-1 ordinary top caps, and the unrestricted original marked top row. Degree conservation forces the last pair to have degree d only AFTER the other caps act. Their product then has scale N^k N^(-(k-1)) N^-2=N^-1, (3) and an explicitly retained nonzero monomial in x. Thus the marked ROOT compiler is a finite sum of products of (1) and this monomial. It contains no further local q derivative. This direct use of the original mark is essential: nonzero E_a at one block would not by itself evaluate F_Delta'(0)/nu_N, the alternative whole-network ordinary-trace normal. That identity is proved only after the complete original closure. We do not differentiate one factor, assign a normal to each vertex, or move the bare mark. ## 2. The full normalization gives N^-1 per circle at the fold Put tau=t/N, alpha=a/N, eta=tau+alpha-1, zeta=tau-alpha. First work on a fixed ordinary physical compact, with alpha in a fixed real interval ending at 1/2. The finite source keeps its actual alpha. The original sine-factorial continuation G_N, on its marked strip, gives hhat_(t,a)=k_a G_N(N tau)^2/ [G_N(N zeta) G_N(N eta+1)]. (4) This is (1) on its supported physical grid. The endpoint +1 comes from d=N-1. The elementary uniform expansion G_N(Nw)=sqrt(2N sin(pi w)) exp[N J(w)](1+O(N^-1)) and the exact sine recurrence at N eta+1 give hhat_(t,a)=k_a b_h(tau,alpha) exp[N H(tau,alpha)] (1+O(N^-1)), H=2J(tau)-J(zeta)-J(eta), b_h=sin(pi tau)/[2sin(pi eta) sqrt(sin(pi zeta)sin(pi eta))]. (5) All sine factors here are units on the compact; their branches are the actual continued ones. In particular b_h remains nonzero and smooth at alpha=1/2. The large even value in (2) has canceled against the actual CD/column normalization. It is not an extra N in the coupon density. The [full ordinary packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) satisfies fhat_a=N^-1/2 B_alpha exp(N Phi_alpha)(1+O(N^-1)), where B_alpha is nowhere zero, uniformly through alpha=1/2. Hence (1) has the actual relative packet C_(N,a)^epsilon =kappa^epsilon k_a N^-1 b_epsilon exp[N Theta_epsilon^lit](1+O(N^-1)), Theta_epsilon^lit=H+Phi_alpha(tau,u/N)+Phi_alpha(tau,v/N) +pi i[-tau+(epsilon-1)(alpha+alpha^2)], b_epsilon=b_h B_alpha(tau,u/N) B_alpha(tau,v/N) exp[pi i(tau+(epsilon-1)alpha)]. (6) The exact kappa and retained outside framing line remain outside this formula. The -tau in (6) uses literal x^-t=q^-dt; the alternative +tau differs by the recorded degree character exp(-2pi i t). No character is discarded when comparing (6) to the marked stationary action. Every factor of b_epsilon is nonzero. Errors and fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller compacts, with smooth dependence on real alpha. The exceptional circle has the SAME assertion. Indeed its correctly restored [entire coefficient](actual_matching_edge_deficient_packet_regulator.md) is exactly C_a(t;r,s)=k_a beta_a^2 V_a(d-t) q^[d(r+s-t)] R_a(q^(t-2r);c_t) R_a(q^(t-2s);c_t). Its scalar-one reflection sends (t,r,s) to (N-t-2,r+N-t-1,s+N-t-1). At negative determinant arguments the reflected values lie in the ordinary physical packet (6). The [joint deficient theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.md) then supplies a nowhere-zero relative packet for each ratio R_a(z)/R_a(z_*), uniformly for the actual real alpha through the fold. The remaining ratio is the EXACT nonzero monomial q^[d(r+s-r_*-s_*)]. Multiplying these ratios propagates (6)'s absolute N^-1 scale and nonzero amplitude to the actual exceptional geometric compact. Different bounded marked logarithmic lifts retain their exact monomials; no root of a squared character is chosen afresh. This argument includes both beta factors, the residual sine product, the finite reflection offset -2, and the original fold weight k_a. There is no assertion that the individually large beta factors have a smooth nonzero endpoint asymptotic before that cancellation. The [literal generic lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) has the additional root character exp(-2pi i v); restoring the actual physical turn cancels it, giving precisely C_a above. Thus it does not introduce an additional zero or unknown scalar in the restored density. ## 3. A nonzero fixed-channel marked density Use the proved actual geometric frame, slightly deformed if needed to make the exceptional degree nonreal. All ordinary factors are on their selected physical sheets, and the exceptional pair is in the joint deficient corridor on its reflected selected sheet. These conditions are strict and hold on a common neighborhood. The internal q-Hahn roots have already been summed by their actual finite relative packets. Choose the original free magnetic coordinates y after the affine wire constraints. Retain every finite d=N-1 offset and every original cup, cap, degree and Poisson character. For a fixed vector of actual channels alpha=(a_1/N,...,a_R/N) near (1/2,...,1/2), the continued marked ROOT summand therefore has D_N(y,alpha)=U_N N^(-R-1) product_i k_(a_i) b_N(y,alpha) exp[N F(y,alpha)](1+O(N^-1)). (7) Here U_N is only the explicitly recorded head-independent unit phase. The original external line, if any, is kept separately. The functions b_N are holomorphic in y, smooth in the real alpha, nowhere zero, and bounded above and away from zero with fixed derivatives on smaller compacts. They include the nonzero order-one exponentials from the finite affine offsets. Such offsets may be kept literally instead; expanding them changes only b_N and its relative O(N^-1) error. The proof is multiplication of the FIXED number R of packets (6), their exceptional continuation, and the exact marked factor (3). This proves nonzero local density for the complete fixed-channel source, not merely nonzero separate polynomial values. It uses a direct root marked compiler, rather than an unjustified inference about the derivative of an ordinary closed density. The specified meromorphic extension agrees with the original source on its supported grid; its local use does not move any support-dependent residue cycle. ## 4. The actual endpoint lattice has a nonzero local folded Gaussian Fix a point y0 of the complete geometric framing orbit in this chart. Use the FULL marked channel stationarity: the channel derivatives of the unadjusted phase are 2pi i n_i with fixed integers n_i. Subtract these exact characters. This changes no actual channel summand because exp(2pi i n_i a_i)=1. In these marked conventions, F_alpha(y0,1/2)=0, F_(alpha_i,alpha_j)(y0,1/2)=delta_ij H_i, H_i=-4pi i/tau_i, Re H_i<0, (8) where tau_i are the actual oriented primitive cusp shapes. Half twists are included: H_i=-2pi/c_i+2pi i epsilon_i in the rectangular convention. The [channel Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md) also proves F_(alpha,y)=0 at the endpoint. Negative real part alone would not substitute for the first equality in (8). The selected branch here is fixed as a neighborhood germ by the full ordinary anchor and the scalar-one deficient reflection, not merely by matching endpoint magnetic momenta. Thus its channel derivatives are the derivatives of the same actual marked principal phase. Explicitly, F=F_raw-2pi i sum_i n_i alpha_i is unchanged in the exponential at every actual grid point; at alpha=1/2 its exponential includes the known unit exp(-pi i N sum_i n_i). Alternatively use the centered F_c=F_raw-2pi i sum_i n_i(alpha_i-1/2), and place that compensating unit in U_N. These conventions give the same (9); the unit is not erased. Let 0<delta<1/6, and sum (7) only over the actual folded labels with 0<N/2-a_i<=N^(1/2+delta). This is a sum of SPECIFIED local continued density values at y0, not the original magnetic period. It has sum_local D_N(y0,a/N) =U_N N^(-R/2-1) b_N(y0,1/2) exp[N F(y0,1/2)] *(2pi)^(R/2)/product_i sqrt(-H_i) *(1+O(N^-1/2)). (9) Each square root is selected by continuation from H_i<0 real; Re H_i<0 makes it nonzero. This coefficient is nonzero at both parities. Here is an elementary lattice proof retaining the endpoint weights. For odd N, the numbers w=N/2-a are 1/2,3/2,5/2,...; their weights are 1 at w=1/2 and 2 thereafter. For even N they are 1,2,3,..., all with weight 2. In either case, for Re H<0, N^-1/2 sum_w k_a exp[H w^2/(2N)] =2 integral_0^infinity exp(H z^2/2) dz+O(N^-1/2) =sqrt(2pi)/sqrt(-H)+O(N^-1/2). (10) The half-step shift and the one exceptional odd weight affect only the O(N^-1/2) error. A direct interval Riemann estimate, using the integrable derivative of the Gaussian, proves this uniformly on compact subsets of Re H<0. The omitted tail is exponentially small in N^(2delta). Taylor's formula gives the quadratic diagonal in (8); the error in N F is O(|w|^3/N^2). On the stated window it tends uniformly to zero. Its Gaussian-weighted absolute sum, and the corresponding variation of b_N, are O(N^-1/2) relative to N^(R/2). This proves (9), including complex H_i; no positivity of the complex terms is assumed. The actual half-twist phase has an independent exact lattice check. Set s=d-2a, s_min=0 at odd N and 1 at even N, and a_max=M. Then nu_a/nu_(a_max) =exp[pi i(s^2-s_min^2)/(4N)]. (11) Indeed the integer character in (-1)^a cancels the linear term in a(a+1) along this parity-restricted lattice. Thus a retained signed half twist contributes its specified quadratic phase, with no alternating nearest-channel factor. Formula (9) does not require an exact even extension of the finite density across the folded endpoint; its one-sided Riemann proof uses the actual two parity lattices directly. No finite noninteger-channel interpolation has been used. Only the proved uniform packet at ACTUAL discrete a_i, its smooth coefficient functions, and the original channel spacing enter. The window has s_i=d-2a_i=O(N^(1/2+delta)), so it is also inside the already proved s_i log N=o(N) generic-normal upper-bound window. That latter bound is not needed to obtain the root local coefficient (9). ## 5. What the magnetic quotient Hessian does and does not add At the certified geometric point the [actual critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), section 7, identifies the magnetic Hessian radical with exactly the two-dimensional T_diag\PGL2 framing tangent space. On a holomorphic slice transverse to this orbit the magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate. Together with (7) and a nonsingular coordinate Jacobian, this gives a nonzero transverse Gaussian density PER UNIT local framing volume: its coefficient divides the nonzero numerator by the chosen square root of the transverse Hessian determinant. A small local descending Morse cycle for those transverse variables has that nonzero coefficient. This does not integrate the framing orbit or assign its measure to the finite source. Nor does a local Morse cycle establish its coefficient in the original physical cycle. In particular every real forbidden integer degree slice of the exceptional source has zero original period, despite the nonzero continued density away from its real lattice. The degree/cotangent transport and its residue terms cannot be omitted. Thus the unresolved question is not an unspecified zero of a local complete-circle amplitude: fixed-channel density (7) and the marked local folded sum (9) are nonzero. The remaining global work includes the actual degree/magnetic cycle and framing integral, its boundary terms and competing contributions, and any mixed-color extension. No nonzero individual genuine q-normal density is claimed or required by this direct root marked-density theorem. Focused audit: [source normalizations and actual folded lattices](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density.py), [saved results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density_results.json). It checks 49 original h0 endpoint values, 674 exact fold half-twist ratios, five literal unrestricted marked plat contractions, eighteen signed full-coupon relative packets at both parities, and eighteen complex-Gaussian parity calibrations. The source comparisons use the literal terminating columns independently of their determinant formulas. The Gaussian calibrations test the elementary lattice lemma, not a global source period. Uniformity and the exceptional continuation follow from the proofs above and their already audited source dependencies. The conclusion is a nonzero complete local density. It does not supply a global period, framing integral, mixed-color packet, or an individual nonzero generic-normal amplitude. The magnetic transverse statement is per unit local framing volume. No original cycle coefficient or mixed-color theorem is inferred.

title: An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats
text: # An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats 30 October 2026. Every fixed 2k-head plat made from the original complete crossing-circle coupons R^epsilon L_N, epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, has an explicit finite factorial sum with its entire original phase. There is no restriction on k>=2 or on the graph formed by its twist regions. The physical q-Hahn sums simplify: their internal quadratic phases cancel exactly, leaving a single linear Fourier phase. The resulting internal critical equation is a quadratic polynomial. This is a source-exact complete-color statement. It supplies an explicit global phase and finite algebraic candidate equations. It does not select their geometric branch, prove a global contour/gap, or supply a mixed-color filling corridor. Thus it is an advance toward a theorem for arbitrary fixed sufficiently twisted plats, not that volume theorem itself. A proposed twist threshold T(D) depends on the fixed skeleton D; it is distinct from quantum level N. ## 1. The phase of the actual physical Casimir column Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^-1, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2sin(pi r/N). For 0<=b<=a<=d write the POSITIVE sine binomial beta(a,b)=s_a/(s_b s_(a-b)). Let t<=d be an actual low physical pair degree, j a Casimir index, and 0<=u<=t. The actual canonical eigenvector of the physical pair Casimir has first entry one and components f_u(c_j), with c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). Its already proved finite q-Hahn formula is f_u(c_j)=x^(t-j)/[t choose j]_Q sum_a (-1)^a x^[-(t-j-u+2a)] Q^[a(a-1)/2+a(t-j-u+a)] [j choose a]_Q [u choose a]_Q [t-u choose j-a]_Q, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (1) All factorial indices are below N. In particular (1) describes the original physical column, not an arbitrarily normalized eigenbasis. The elementary marked identity [v choose w]_Q=q^[w(v-w)] beta(v,w) turns (1) into the simpler exact formula f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a (-1)^a q^[a(t+j+1)] E(t,j,u,a), E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j)>0. (2) Indeed the complete exponent of q inside (1) is -u+2a+a(a-1)+2a(t-j-u+a) +a(j-a)+a(u-a)+(j-a)(t-u-j+a)-j(t-j) =a(t+j+1)-(j+1)u. (3) The a^2 terms cancel. No factorial envelope or asymptotic estimate is used in this cancellation. On every channel that survives the COMPLETE circle, d-j<=t and j<=floor(d/2). Put delta=t+j-d. Since (-1)^a=q^(-Na), (2) is f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a q^(delta a) E(t,j,u,a), 0<=delta<=floor(d/2). (4) Thus the summation variable carries a positive-coefficient polynomial at one specified Fourier argument q^delta. Its entire phase is retained; positivity of its coefficients does not imply positivity or a lower bound for that value. ## 2. Complete signed coupons in every original degree Take an arbitrary physical pair degree S in 0,...,2d. Set t=min(S,2d-S), shift=max(0,S-d). Use physical basis |shift+u,S-shift-u>, 0<=u<=t. The high block is literally the low block under this index translation, for both the Casimir and original signed crossing. For every j with j<d-j<=t the full reflected-circle resolution has positive coefficient h_(t,j)=2s_t^2/[s_(t-j)s_(t+j-d)]. If N is odd and j=d/2<=t, use the same formula WITHOUT the factor 2. No other channel contributes. Let nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. Then the EXACT all-input kernel of B_epsilon=R^epsilon L_N is B_epsilon[u,v]=kappa^epsilon x^(-t) sum_j h_(t,j) nu_j^(epsilon-1) f_u(c_j) f_v(c_j). (5) This is bilinear in the two physical columns, not Hermitian. To prove it, start with the actual positive reflected tensor H=L_N P=sum_j h v_j v_j^*. Its normalized last component is (v_j)_t=x^t nu_j, and literal reversal gives P conjugate(v_j)=conjugate(x^t nu_j) v_j. Hence L_N=H P has coefficient h x^-t nu_j^-1 times v_j v_j^T. On this actual complete-circle image, R acts by kappa nu_j. At a double root its normal correction annihilates L_N: the latter is its derivative times the square-zero Jordan operator. At the odd simple root the value calculation is immediate. This proves (5) for both signs, all parities and all physical degree blocks. Thus the normal directions responsible for L_N have been evaluated exactly BEFORE the rank-one image is used. Formula (5) is not an initial semisimple quotient, and it does not identify an arbitrary generic-q germ with its root values. Substitution of (4) makes each (j,a,b) contribution to (5) the positive factorial weight h_(t,j) E(t,j,u,a) E(t,j,v,b) times kappa^epsilon (-1)^[t+(epsilon-1)j+u+v] q^[t+(epsilon-1)j(j+1)-(j+1)(u+v)+delta(a+b)]. (6) Equation (6) is the complete physical coupon phase. In particular the two internal summation variables have no individual square term. ## 3. Compile any fixed augmented 2k-plat Fix the positions and order of the twist regions in a literal 2k-head plat. Augment every chosen region by its original auxiliary circle and retain its prescribed parity epsilon. Use the original bottom cups, ordinary top caps and ONE unrestricted marked top cap: p_ab=N x^-b delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. (7) The original exterior line chi_N, including framing, stays explicit. All crossing-circle coupons and any remaining original crossings preserve integer degree. Only after the k-1 ordinary top caps have acted does total degree kd force the marked pair degree to d. This is the permitted whole-source restriction; m is not replaced locally in a separated degree-changing sector. Expand every augmented coupon by (5), or further by (6). Sum every actual physical wire index, channel j and internal q-Hahn index. Unchanged identity wires identify their labels. The resulting finite sum is EXACTLY chi_N times the original marked plat contraction. There is no inverse Clebsch matrix, recoupling determinant, fitted boundary vector, or division by a knot value in this construction. The powers in (7) multiply to N^-1; all other powers, phases and factorials are those in (5)--(6). Each kappa^epsilon is retained as its explicit external unit phase, not reset to one. For a fixed skeleton this is a finite union of rational affine state polytopes. The low/high choices t=S or t=2d-S give finitely many chambers. Every surviving channel and internal summation range is an explicit linear inequality, such as d-j<=t, 2j<=d, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). All lattice offsets from d=N-1 and both parity endpoint weights are kept in the exact formulas. The number of states is bounded by a power of N depending on the fixed diagram. Augmentation removes the large full-twist powers from the number of blocks; those fixed filling parameters are not extra copies of a quantum-level dependent packet. This also computes the physical coefficient tensor entering the [marked multiport Chebyshev packet](actual_marked_multiport_chebyshev_source_packet.md). That packet's correct C,...,C,H conjugation and final half-bandwidth fold may be applied afterward. Neither its polynomial DCT cost nor this exact compiler proves a sharp coherent energy bound. ## 4. An explicit global action and a local quadratic critical equation Let J(z)=integral_0^z Log(2sin(pi w))dw with the marks continued from positive factorial arguments. Put B(v,w)=J(v)-J(w)-J(v-w). For scaled labels (tau,xi,upsilon,alpha)=(t,j,u,a)/N the real factorial action of E is Ecal=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). (8) Its exact leading complex phase after (4) is Ecal+pi i[upsilon-xi*upsilon +(tau+xi-1)alpha]. (9) The finite +1 terms and d=N-1 differences give specified order-one amplitude/phase corrections; they are recovered from (4), not discarded. For a whole coupon add two copies of (8), the h action 2J(tau)-J(tau-xi)-J(tau+xi-1), (10) and the exact polynomial phase read from (6). Include the source characters from (7). Summing these functions over the original network gives its explicit global candidate phase. Uniform factorial errors are O_D(log N) even at endpoints; this alone bounds the absolute term envelope, not the coherent sum from below. There is a particularly simple algebraic equation for an INTERNAL q-Hahn stationary variable. The derivative of (8) exponentiates to sin(pi(xi-alpha))^2 sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / [sin(pi alpha)^2 sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))]. (11) The phase in (9) supplies exp(pi i(tau+xi-1)). Set T=exp(2pi i tau), Jc=exp(2pi i xi), U=exp(2pi i upsilon), Z=exp(2pi i alpha). With the original logarithmic marks and away from the displayed pole divisors, exp(partial_alpha Phi)=1 is exactly T(Jc-Z)^2(U-Z)+(Z-1)^2(TZ-U Jc)=0. (12) Its cubic terms cancel. The remaining quadratic coefficients are A=T(2Jc+U-2)-U Jc, B=T(1-Jc^2-2Jc U)+2U Jc, C=U Jc(T Jc-1), A Z^2+B Z+C=0. (13) The degree is at most two on special parameter loci; no division by A is made. Such degenerations and the specified pole divisors must remain in any branch analysis. The complete global stationarity equations likewise become explicit rational Laurent equations after exponentiating the original wire variables and clearing ONLY specified nonzero denominators. Thus finite algebraic candidate-branch and Jacobian tests are available at arbitrary fixed bridge width. Pole exclusions, logarithmic marks, boundary sectors and the original finite cycle remain part of the problem. A solution of (12) has not thereby been identified with a geometric tetrahedron or an A-polynomial branch. ## 5. Why the real positive saddle criterion does not automatically apply This exact phase also locates an obstruction. At a real strict complete-image channel, 0<tau+xi-1<1/2. The factorial logarithmic derivative (11) is positive real, while the derivative phase has argument strictly between 0 and pi/2. Consequently an interior real alpha cannot solve the stationary equation even after subtracting an integer Poisson frequency. Equivalently, the representation before (4) has imaginary derivative between 2pi and 5pi/2; its retained integer mark removes 2pi and leaves exactly the phase in (9). On the boundary delta=0 the finite q-Hahn sum in (4) IS positive, but this is one channel boundary, not a theorem that the whole augmented source concentrates there. The odd simple channel and even endpoint pairs must also remain in any endpoint analysis. Thus the real-concave version of the [analytic sewing criterion](actual_six_port_analytic_sewing_criterion.md) cannot be applied to this raw expanded phase by ignoring its Fourier factor. One needs a source-preserving complex deformation, a selected local resummation, or another exact period representation, followed by a global boundary/gap and nonzero-period argument. The quadratic (12) makes the local candidate branches explicit; it does not choose their original-cycle coefficients. The mixed ordinary-circle colors required by long Dehn filling need a separate extension as well. Audit: [physical Casimir columns, full signed coupons and marked plats](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.py). The fresh audit passes N=2,...,10: 99 original degree blocks, 704 canonical-column entries, all three signed complete coupon identities in every block, and eight literal marked plat contractions at k=2,3,4. Its matrices are built independently from the original coproduct and signed crossings, not from the q-Hahn formula being checked. The symbolic phase cancellation and quadratic degree are also checked exactly. These are source-identity checks, not numerical evidence for an unproved all-plat volume limit. The finite compiler does not supply a mixed-color packet or select a geometric cycle.

title: A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing
status: Finite framing tests; right-angled obstruction follows
text: # A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. This note reduces the simultaneous framing question for the actual complete augmented-plat character to a strict semialgebraic feasibility problem in one rank-one projector. It also treats the smaller central domain used by the joint accretive determinant. The criterion keeps every original prefix word and both actual degree adapters. There is no assertion that this feasibility problem always has a solution. The positive gluing certificate and the regular critical-scheme theorem do not by themselves prove that assertion. In particular, a nonempty real-open set of perfectly regular frames fails physical support at any one essential crossing disk. The obstruction below explains why merely avoiding algebraic divisors cannot settle the issue. ## 1. The common frame is a rank-one projector Fix the actual marked geometric representation and its finite original Morse word. For its prefix matrices Q use the same trace -2 main lifts as in the [regular magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). A simultaneous projective frame g, modulo LEFT diagonal changes, is equivalently Pi=g^(-1) E_11 g, Pi^2=Pi, tr Pi=1, det Pi=0. (1) Indeed the two eigenspaces of Pi have distinct eigenvalues 1 and 0, so every such projector is obtained this way; its stabilizer is precisely the projective diagonal torus. This is the same two-dimensional complex framing quotient as in the [actual critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md). Every needed prefix diagonal is the LINEAR function a_Q=tr(Q Pi)=(g Q g^(-1))_11. (2) At an input of a crossing-circle coupon put Q_0=W, Q_1=A W, Q_2=P W, P=B A, a_i=tr(Q_i Pi). For the output, replace A by the actual outgoing first meridian A'; Q_0 and Q_2 are unchanged. The original two physical wire phases are X_1=-a_0/a_1, X_2=-a_1/a_2, T=X_1 X_2=a_0/a_2. (3) We always impose the other finitely many regular-chart nonvanishings from the cited chart theorem. No independent local change of frame is permitted in (2). ## 2. Exact strict-support criterion For a nonzero X off the positive real axis choose its wire logarithm by x=Log_(0,2pi)(X)/(2pi i), 0<Re x<1. (4) Write s=x_1+x_2. The actual low adapter is tau=s, u=x_1; the high adapter is tau=2-s, u=1-x_2. At the complete channel the strict local physical domain is 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re u<Re tau. (5) For three nonzero prefix diagonals, (4)--(5) hold if and only if Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, 0 is not in the real convex hull of {a_0,a_1,a_2}. (6) Here the low or high adapter is determined, rather than freely chosen. The second condition is equivalent to the existence of one open half-plane through the origin containing all three numbers. Proof. Rotate a_0 to the positive axis. Under the convex-hull condition the three arguments have lifts arg a_0=0, arg a_2=delta in (-pi,pi), arg a_1=beta, max(0,beta,delta)-min(0,beta,delta)<pi. The first condition in (6) says delta is neither 0 nor an endpoint. The canonical physical arguments are consequently 2pi Re x_1=pi-beta, 2pi Re x_2=pi+beta-delta. (7) Their sum is 2pi-delta. Thus delta>0 gives the low adapter, delta<0 gives the high adapter, and Re tau=1-|delta|/(2pi) in (1/2,1). Both inequalities for u follow from 0<Re x_i<1: in the low case tau-u=x_2, and in the high case tau-u=1-x_1. Conversely (5) puts the sum of the two wire arguments strictly between pi and 3pi and away from 2pi. The inverse formulas (7) put the three prefix arguments in an interval of width less than pi. This proves (6). The input and output have the same a_0,a_2. Their prescribed adapter therefore agrees. Their canonical sums agree in real part by (7) and in imaginary part by X_1 X_2=T. Thus degree conservation holds as an EXACT complex equality, not only after exponentiation. At a cup or cap the first and last prefix words agree. The corresponding condition is simply that a_1/a_0 is not a nonpositive real number; all diagonals are nonzero. Then X_2=X_1^(-1) and their canonical logarithms sum exactly to 1. Applying these tests at every event makes the chosen wire logarithms solve the original affine incidence equations Bx=b without any additional integer adjustment. Ordinary and marked cap characters are still the distinct characters recorded in the source. ## 3. The central joint domain has an even simpler test The central domain adds |2 Re u-Re tau|<1/2 (8) to (5). This is the leading open domain Re c>0, Re z>0 for c=-cos(pi tau), z=exp[pi i(tau-2u)]. The exact finite c has tau+1/N in place of tau; any compact subset of (5),(8) satisfies its corresponding inequality for large N. For BOTH actual adapters, tau-2u=x_2-x_1. (9) Consequently the central condition is adapter-independent. In physical wire real parts it is the diamond |Re x_1-1/2|+|Re x_2-1/2|<1/2, Re(x_1+x_2) != 1. (10) An exact test using only the prefix diagonals is Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, |a_2| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_0)) +|a_0| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_2)) > 0. (11) Proof. In the argument lifts above, (8) is |2 beta-delta|<pi. This says precisely that a_1 lies in the open half-plane centered at the bisector of the MINOR angular interval from a_0 to a_2. The vector a_0/|a_0|+a_2/|a_2| points along that bisector. Taking the scalar product with a_1 gives (11). Conversely the resulting interval delta/2-pi/2<beta<delta/2+pi/2, with |delta|<pi, puts all three arguments in an interval of width less than pi. Thus (11) itself implies (6), as well as (8). This extra inequality is substantial: same-side disk flags, or merely being in the larger physical strip (5), does not imply (11). ## 4. A finite semialgebraic feasibility problem Equations (1),(2),(6) give a finite strict semialgebraic test for a simultaneous physical magnetic frame. One can encode the convex-hull test with one complex separator n_f per input/output triple: |n_f|^2=1, Re(n_f a_(f,i))>0 for i=0,1,2. For the central domain there are no separator choices. Introduce positive real r_(f,0),r_(f,2) with r_(f,i)^2=|a_(f,i)|^2 and require r_(f,2) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,0))) +r_(f,0) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,2))) > 0. (12) Also require the square of Im(a_(f,0) conjugate(a_(f,2))) to be positive, impose the cup/cap tests, and retain every regular-chart nonvanishing. All coefficients are algebraic when the actual marked representation is algebraic. Only one projector Pi is shared by the whole diagram. This formulation is suitable for an exact feasibility or infeasibility certificate; it is not a collection of independent local frame choices. A strict feasible frame persists under sufficiently small changes of the marked representation. The strict inequalities give a common positive margin on the finite set of triples, and all denominators remain nonzero. In particular it would persist for sufficiently long fillings once obtained at completeness. This persistence does not obtain the initial frame. Nor does (12) make the pair totals real: their imaginary parts come from the moduli of the prefix ratios. A theorem continuing only u at fixed real t,j cannot be applied to these generally complex totals. Even a joint domain requires comparing its selected internal roots with the actual geometric roots, and subsequently controlling the contributing global finite-source cycle. ### A finite family sharing one disk product is always feasible There is a constructive positive result: all input/output triples from any fixed finite family of transports sharing the SAME product P and prefix W can be made central simultaneously. This does not couple different disk products or different prefixes. Normalize A,P as in (13), put H=P+I, and write its transported splits as A_b=(I+bH)A(I-bH), with b in the given finite complex set. This includes every complete centralizer transport and any retained finite half-twist shifts. For a>0 put h=sqrt(2a+1) and take the projector L_a=[[1+a/2+i h/2, (a-1)/4+i h/2], [-a-1, -a/2-i h/2]]. (12a) Direct multiplication gives L_a^2=L_a, tr L_a=1, tr(P L_a)=1, tr(A L_a)=a, tr([H,A] L_a)=-4i h, tr(A_b L_a)=a-4i b sqrt(2a+1)-8b^2. (12b) For the finite b-set the last expression is a+O(sqrt(a)), uniformly as a tends to positive infinity. It therefore has positive real part for every b once a is large enough. The central scalar inequality in (11), with endpoints 1,1, is then strictly positive for every triple. Only its T=1 seam remains. These finitely many scalar inequalities hold on an open neighborhood of L_a in the complex projector surface. The nonconstant function tr(P L) cannot be real on any such open neighborhood. A sufficiently small perturbation therefore removes the seam, and gives all the strict central tests. For an arbitrary shared prefix W, recover the actual common projector by Pi=W^(-1)L/tr(W^(-1)L). (12c) It is rank-one of trace one, and its actual prefix diagonals are one common nonzero scalar times tr(L),tr(A_b L),tr(P L). Thus the central inequalities are unchanged. The additional trace in (12c) does not vanish identically on the projector surface: otherwise ell(W^(-1)v)=0 for every ell(v)=1, forcing W^(-1)=0. Hence its zero set cannot contain the feasible open neighborhood. The perturbation can simultaneously avoid this trace, the seam, and the finitely many proper regular-chart divisors. This proves the assertion for W as well, rather than assuming the W=I projector survives unchanged. The construction is a precise favorable near-coincident-frame mechanism at ONE auxiliary flag. It proves that each coupon's incoming and outgoing central inequalities are locally compatible. It leaves the genuinely simultaneous problem (12), with the actual different products and prefixes of the full plat, unresolved. ## 5. A geometric necessary condition and an open obstruction There is a useful uniform restriction on possible solutions. At one essential complete disk normalize its distinct puncture flags so that A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A=[[1,1],[-4,-3]]. (13) This normalization follows directly from Tr A=Tr B=Tr P=-2. The circle through the three parabolic flags is then the real circle. Write Pi=v ell with ell(v)=1, put w=ker ell, and put z=Wv. These are projective points; z is the right framing point transported by the ACTUAL prefix W. If (6) holds, then z and w lie in the same open side of this circle. (14) In particular replacing z by v in this test would be incorrect. Here is a direct proof. For real r=(r_0,r_1,r_2) set M(r)=r_0 I+r_1 A+r_2 P. The matrices in this pencil are real-linearly independent and det M=2(r_0^2+r_1^2+r_2^2)-(r_0+r_1+r_2)^2. (15) Suppose z,w are in opposite open half-planes. The condition M(r)z=w is two homogeneous real linear equations in three r's, so it has a nonzero solution. M(r) cannot annihilate a nonreal z: its real and imaginary vector parts are linearly independent, which would force M=0. The real Möbius transformation identity Im M(z)=det(M) Im(z)/|M_21 z+M_22|^2 therefore gives det M<0. Normalize the sign so that sum r_i>0. Equation (15) forces every r_i>0: if, for example, r_0<=0, then det M=(r_1-r_2)^2+r_0^2-2r_0(r_1+r_2)>=0, because r_1+r_2>0. This is a contradiction. Now 0=ell(M(r)Wv)=r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+r_2 a_2. This is a strictly positive convex relation after division by sum r_i, contradicting (6). If z is nonreal and w is on the real circle, the same argument gives det M=0 and r_i>=0, still a nontrivial convex relation. If z is on the real circle, solve instead M(r)z=0, again two real equations in three unknowns. The same det=0 argument gives r_i>=0 and the same relation for every w. The point at infinity is handled in homogeneous coordinates, or by a real change of disk coordinates. Thus a good triple must satisfy (14). This is a necessary condition, not a converse. The opposite-side choice is a nonempty REAL-OPEN condition on the common framing quotient. It also allows v and w to be distinct, as required for a projector. The common regular-frame locus is a complex Zariski open dense subset by the cited chart theorem. It intersects this real-open bad set: a nonzero holomorphic polynomial cannot vanish on a real-open subset of this complex manifold. Hence EVERY such complete character has common regular frames that fail physical support already at this disk. This conclusion holds independently of whether the representation has a positive gluing certificate. For a small exact illustration use W=I, v=(i,1), ell=(1,i)/(2i), so w=-i. Equations (13) give (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1+i/2,-1-5i/2), (1/2)a_0+(5/12)a_1+(1/12)a_2=0. (16) The endpoint discriminant numerator is a_0 a_1+a_1 a_2+a_0 a_2=1/4, and the leading-coefficient numerator a_0+a_2+4a_1=-4-i/2; both are nonzero. Thus this support failure is not just the local root-discriminant failure. Formula (16) is only a local illustration; the preceding open-density argument deals with all the other regular divisors of the actual finite diagram. Near-coincident framing points do not evade (14). In the limit w=v, each condition concerns v and Wv on its own developed disk circle. The different prefixes W are fixed words of the representation, not small perturbations of the identity. No simultaneous same-side or central-domain conclusion follows just by taking w close to v. ## 6. What an ordinary fixed-total fiber estimate does and does not say At fixed real discrete t,j, the proved magnetic corridor can be multiplied over a fixed finite number of ORDINARY q-Hahn column factors. Pull their magnetic u variables back by affine wire maps preserving every such total. On a compact subset of the common corridors, the relative errors multiply to 1+O(1/N), the leading actions add, and the nonzero amplitudes multiply. An already evaluated normal-derived coefficient depending only on these fixed t,j may remain an EXACT scalar outside this product. This elementary product statement estimates neither generic q/normal derivatives of the columns nor the rank-two derivative terms of mixed source kernels. It supplies no bound for fiber summation and does not release t,j. It therefore does not establish an asymptotic for an arbitrary full original-source summand containing those normal terms. Audit: [exact projector, determinant, convexity and adapter checks](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.py). The audit includes numerical argument comparisons only as regressions of the explicit equivalences; it is not an existence search or a proof of a favorable simultaneous frame for arbitrary augmented plats. The expanded audit includes 100 exact central-feasibility checks for the constructive lemma. No global existence or cycle claim follows.

title: A global selected frame with one real deficient degree
status: Uniform real deficient frame and exact branch calibration
text: # A global selected frame with one real deficient degree 30 October 2026. For every chosen matching edge of an actual certified right-angled augmented plat, there is a common algebraic frame whose two support failures occur precisely at that edge. Their normalized total is the REAL number sigma=1/6, while their magnetic rows are genuinely complex. Every other ordinary factor remains strictly physical and source-selected. This is a classical framing and branch-calibration theorem. A fixed integer deficient degree corresponds to an identically zero physical slice of the finite polynomial operator. The construction does not turn that slice into a nonzero quantum period. ## 1. Use the actual cusp and prefix normalization Fix the labeled matching-polyhedron certificate and one crossing-circle edge. In its actual disk coordinate eta, the two outward shaded disks are the half-planes below y=0 and above y=H, where H=1/c>=1. The inequality is the proved actual rectangle bound, including retained half twists. The two incident white planes are the vertical lines x=0 and x=1, with reflections -conjugate(eta) and 2-conjugate(eta). The actual incoming pair and its transport are A=[[-1,0],[-2,-1]], P=[[-1,-2],[0,-1]], C: eta -> eta+iH, A_o=C A C^-1. (1) These are precisely the conjugated original matrices and primitive collar, not an independent choice of a rectangle or meridian. All other shaded outward disks are bounded Euclidean disks in this chart. Their supporting planes do not contain the chosen ideal cusp; their outward sides cannot contain that cusp, which lies in the closed polyhedron. There are only finitely many such disks. Choose any 0<d<H and a midpoint r with d/2<r<H-d/2. For a large positive real X choose the TWO GLOBAL shaded-exterior flags w=X+i(r-d/2), w0=1-X+i(r+d/2). (2) They are between the two horizontal lines and, for sufficiently large X, outside every other bounded shaded disk. Thus w,w0 are in K. Recover the global image flag v=r_(F0)(w0) using the ACTUAL exterior white reflection F0. Together with kernel w this determines the common rank-one frame, provided v!=w. At the chosen left prefix white face F, reflection is -conjugation. The literal prefix identity gives local image z=r_F(w0)=X-1+i(r+d/2), z-w=-1+id. (3) This retains W_prefix v; it does not replace it by v. The equality v=w is avoidable: if F0 is one of the two incident vertical faces, its reflected image differs from w by +/-1+id; otherwise its bounded circle reflection sends w0 near infinity to a finite point as X grows, while w tends to infinity. ## 2. The deficient degree is exactly real and prescribed Normalize the local projector by its prefix trace. Direct traces in (1) give a0=1, a2=Tr(P Pi)=-1-2/(z-w)=(1+id)/(1-id), a1=Tr(A Pi)=-1+2zw/(z-w), a1_out=-1+2(z-iH)(w-iH)/(z-w). (4) Put sigma=atan(d)/pi in (0,1/2). Then a2=exp(2pi i sigma). Both middle diagonals in (4) have the same leading term 2X^2/(-1+id). Its argument is pi+pi sigma, strictly between pi and pi+2pi sigma. For all sufficiently large X, zero is therefore strictly inside BOTH actual input/output prefix triangles. These are exactly the strict failed-triangle tests, with no boundary limit taken in the final frame. Their canonical physical wire sums are 2-sigma, so the original high adapter gives the EXACT normalized complex degree sigma, with zero imaginary part. Write its two normalized magnetic rows as r_in, r_out. The actual high coordinates are U_in=-a2/a1, U_out=-a2/a1_out. Equations (4) imply Re r_in, Re r_out -> sigma/2, Im r_in, Im r_out =log(X)/pi+O(1), Re(r_out-r_in)=H/(pi X)+O(X^-2)>0. (5) The errors are uniform when the midpoint r stays in a compact subinterval of (d/2,H-d/2). Hence both rows are strictly inside the real degree interval and are nonreal; their difference avoids the target-total seam for sufficiently large X. Because H>=1, the UNIVERSAL choice d=1/sqrt(3) is allowed. It gives sigma=1/6, Re r_in,Re r_out ->1/12. (6) The construction can instead use any fixed d in (0,H). In particular it gives an open range of real deficient degrees when needed. ## 3. Exactly these two factors fail; all source seams can be avoided The global polarization kernel line for w,w0 lies through the interior of the white-normal polyhedron. The two strict relations in (4) put its exits in the interiors of the two designated triangular facets. A line has only two exits from a convex polyhedron. Thus no other facet has zero in its prefix triangle. Once the finite real seams are excluded, every other ordinary factor is strictly physical; its K flags then select its actual source sheet by the full-domain selected-factor theorem. Here is explicit seam control at FIXED d. It avoids an unjustified genericity argument on this restricted framing family. Up to one common scalar, the actual white prefix diagonals are the outward unit-circle polarizations. For a bounded white circle of center a+ib and radius R>0, remove only its positive factor 1/R and write L=-X^2+X+a^2-a+(r-b)^2-d^2/4-R^2 +i[(r-b)(1-2X)+(a-1/2)d]. (7) The two oriented vertical white forms are 1-id and 1+id. Formula (7) follows directly from `(w-a-ib)(conjugate(w0)-a+ib)-R^2`. For distinct bounded circles, Im(L1 conjugate(L2)) is a nonzero polynomial in X,r. Its X^3 coefficient detects distinct heights b. If the heights agree, its X^2 coefficient detects distinct horizontal centers a because d!=0. If both centers agree, the radius difference multiplies the nonzero imaginary part of L. A bounded-circle/vertical pair has a nonzero X^2 coefficient proportional to d, and the two vertical forms have imaginary product +/-2d. Thus every ratio of distinct white prefix diagonals can simultaneously be made nonreal by choosing (X,r) off finitely many proper real polynomial zero sets. This also supplies the ordinary cup/cap seam tests. The remaining specific regular-chart exclusions can be checked without claiming that an arbitrary divisor misses this family. Every bounded-circle form has the SAME-sign leading coefficient -1/R times X^2. Thus all required positive linear combinations, including a0+a2+4a1 and adjacent sums, have nonzero leading term. If only the two vertical forms occur in a sum, their sum is 2. For the discriminant a0a1+a1a2+a0a2, at least two bounded faces give a nonzero positive X^4 coefficient. The only case with one bounded face is the chosen pair of vertical faces; its leading coefficient is that bounded form times their sum 2, again nonzero. All prefix diagonals themselves are nonzero for large X. Finally each head or disk product is a noncentral trace-minus-two parabolic in its actual Borel frame. Its diagonal is nonreal by the ratio tests, and so is not -1. Determinant one then forces both offdiagonal entries to be nonzero. This checks the required main K+1 and total E/F charts. Together with the preceding leading coefficient and discriminant tests, these are the finite exclusions listed in the regular geometric phase-chart theorem. The actual simple internal roots and their rational inverses are therefore regular as well. All constraints hold on a nonempty open set of large X and allowed r. For an algebraic geometric certificate, take d=1/sqrt(3) and choose algebraic X,r outside the finite excluded polynomial sets. This gives an algebraic common frame. No rationality of the logarithms is claimed. ## 4. Exact magnetic branch data in this frame The following identities specify the geometric branch against which an actual second-chamber source continuation must be compared. They do not assume that such a continuation has already been proved. Put C0=cos(pi sigma)=1/sqrt(1+d^2) and L=2X-1. The two normalized determinant coordinates z_j=exp(pi i sigma)/U_j are exactly z_in =C0[(L^2+1+d^2-4r^2)/2+2irL], z_out=C0[(L^2+1+d^2-4(r-H)^2)/2+2i(r-H)L]. (8) Thus z_in lies in the UPPER half-plane, and z_out in the LOWER half-plane, for every X>1/2 and the stated midpoint interval. The actual original HIGH internal-root formulas give Z_in=-1/[L+2i(r+d/2)], Z_out=1/[L+2i(r-H-d/2)]. (9) The output uses its ACTUAL disk normalization C^-1, so its kernel coordinate is w-iH. Omitting that shift would give an incorrect output root even though the leading real sign agrees. For W(z)=1-2C0 z, equations (8) give perfect squares W(z_in)=-C0^2(L+2ir)^2, W(z_out)=-C0^2(L+2i(r-H))^2. (10) Take sqrt W positive at negative real z and continue through the upper or lower half-plane, respectively. Its values are -iC0(L+2ir) at the input and +iC0(L+2i(r-H)) at the output. Substitution of (9) in the original magnetic momentum formula Y=(1-U)(TZ+U)/[-(U-Z)(T-U)], T=exp(2pi i sigma), yields exactly Y_geo(z)=(z-i sqrt W(z))^2/[1-2C0 z+z^2]. (11) For example, at the input put A=L+2ir. Both sides reduce to `[(A-1)^2+d^2]/[(A+1)^2+d^2]`. At the output the same formula with A=L+2i(r-H) is inverted. In particular Y_in=1-2/X+O(X^-2) and Y_out=1+2/X+O(X^-2). Equation (11) is the branch obtained by REFLECTING the high-degree positive-center characteristic to negative z: z_high=-z changes its plus-square-root formula to the minus sign in (11). If an actual finite source continuation is anchored by that reflection, (8)--(11) identify its upper/lower continued characteristics with the actual geometric ones. They do not select a finite source by an arbitrary algebraic root or infer its relative amplitude. ## 5. The source-zero wall and global period remain This common frame supplies real sigma and complex rows for a local source analysis. It does not authorize replacing a generally complex degree by discrete samples in a theorem that has not controlled that continuation. In particular, at a fixed INTEGER deficient t the retargeted separation h=d-t exceeds the folded polynomial degree a. The entire physical fixed-h slice of p_a(J) is identically zero, including every genuine generic-q jet. Deforming magnetic rows alone does not create a nonzero original source in that slice. The geometry is therefore a useful actual branch and normalization test for the required continuation, not a contributing-cycle theorem. The [entire finite root continuation](actual_matching_edge_entire_operator_kernel.md) is established separately and retains the physical support zeros. Its selected asymptotic through this wall, its genuine generic normals, and the global marked period still require separate proofs. Focused audit: [circle regularity and actual marked branch identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_real_deficient_frame.py). It checks fourteen exact local identities, eighteen actual disk frames and thirty-six geometric characteristic comparisons. The global convex cut and avoidance arguments are the proofs in sections 1--3, not claims inferred from sampled polyhedra. The real deficient-frame construction does not supply a finite second-chamber packet or a nonzero global period.

title: A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character
text: # A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character 30 October 2026. A complete geometric augmented-plat representation can be put simultaneously into the regular magnetic charts of the actual local critical-character map. This is a finite generic-framing theorem, not an assumption that the geometric flags are already in a convenient chart. At the leading exponentiated level its original Morse degree constraints also have an integral logarithmic lift. The statement constructs a regular candidate for the UNFOLDED principal equations. It does not prove that its logarithms lie in a nonempty physical support chamber, choose its Poisson sector in the original finite cycle, establish a nondegenerate reduced critical branch, or supply a quantum asymptotic. Those distinctions matter at the folded channel endpoint. ## 1. The actual prefix factorization Fix the finite ordered Morse word of the augmented plat and its actual complete geometric representation. Use common trace -2 lifts of the main meridians. At each circle box its two puncture flags are distinct and their ordered product P is noncentral parabolic with trace -2, as in the [geometric endpoint theorem](actual_augmented_plat_geometric_channel_endpoint.md). The same statements hold after its retained Hurwitz half twists. These hypotheses do not require a right-angled cell decomposition. In any actual complete geometric augmented exterior, the disk boundary is a nontrivial peripheral longitude of its auxiliary cusp. If its two main puncture parabolics had the same fixed point, their nontrivial parabolic product would have that point too. This would identify a main cusp lift with an auxiliary cusp lift. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint sufficiently small horoballs; two horoballs with the same ideal center intersect. This is impossible for different components. The elementary common-trace calculation then forces Tr P=-2. At any horizontal cut let H_1,...,H_m be its ordered based meridians and Q_i=H_i ... H_1, Q_0=I. For a determinant-one matrix Q with Q_11!=0 put Bminus(Q)=[[1,0],[-Q_21,Q_11]], Bplus(Q)=[[Q_11,Q_12],[0,1]]. Then Q=Bminus(Q)^-1 Bplus(Q). Consequently the original physical head at slot i is G_i=Bminus(Q_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(Q_(i-1))^-1, K_i=(Q_i)_11/(Q_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (1) For K_i!=0,-1 these are finite nonzero magnetic coordinates. The determinant-one and trace -2 equations give exactly the original head matrix (8) of the [local critical map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Thus (1) does not introduce an independent flag realization. Change the ONE common frame by g in SL2(C), so every word Q changes to gQg^-1. There are finitely many heads and boxes. The following sections show that each excluded condition is a proper algebraic subset of this same frame group. Their finite union cannot cover it. ## 2. Every required endpoint chart divisor is avoidable A nonzero 2-by-2 matrix R has a nonzero (gRg^-1)_11 for some g. Indeed otherwise every vector/covector pair v,l with l(v)=1 would have l(Rv)=0, forcing R=0. Thus a forbidden diagonal of any NONZERO fixed word combination is a proper condition. This handles all prefix diagonals. It also handles K_i=-1, since Q_i+Q_(i-1)=(H_i+I)Q_(i-1) is nonzero for a nontrivial trace -2 parabolic. At a local input pair put R=Q_(i-1), A=H_i, B=H_(i+1), P=BA and Q_0=R,Q_1=AR,Q_2=PR. Write a_r=(gQ_r g^-1)_11. Its low physical coordinates obey U=-a_0/a_1, T=a_0/a_2. (2) The exclusions T=+/-1 and U=T are diagonal conditions for (I-/+P)R and (I+B)AR. These matrices are nonzero. The endpoint q-Hahn quadratic leading coefficient is U(T+1)-4T. Its vanishing, away from the nonzero a_r, is exactly a_0+a_2+4a_1=0. The corresponding fixed matrix is (I+P+4A)R. It is nonzero because Tr(I+P+4A)=-8. The discriminant is proportional to T+1-U. Here its vanishing is the quadratic expression a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=0. (3) To prove this is PROPER for every prefix R, conjugate just for this nonvanishing proof to the canonical pair A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], R=[[a,b],[c,d]], ad-bc=1. The normalization follows from the two distinct flags and Tr(BA)=-2. For the test frames g_r=[[1,r],[0,1]], direct multiplication gives a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=-( -a+c r-c )^2. (4) This polynomial is not identically zero, since the first column (a,c) of R is not zero. Therefore (3) is avoidable by a generic common frame. A different test frame can prove propriety for each box; the final choice avoids ALL of their finitely many bad loci. Both total F and total E may also be required nonzero. In the local Borel frame E_tot=P_12/a_0, so its zero is proper because P is noncentral. For F_tot the numerator, up to nonzero diagonal factors, is det(Rv,PRv), where v=g^-1 e_1. This quadratic in v is not identically zero for a noncentral P. Thus this exclusion is proper too. These conditions exclude every pole in the endpoint local formulas. For example P(U,Z) at J=-1 cannot have Z=0,1,-1,U or TZ+U=0: substitution gives a nonzero product of T,U,T+1,U-1,U-T. Its leading coefficient is nonzero and its discriminant is nonzero, so both roots are finite and simple. The actual magnetic momentum selects its root by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. For the HIGH chamber use T_low=T_phys^-1 and U_low=U_phys/T_phys. The discriminant divisor transforms by T_low+1-U_low=(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys, and the leading coefficient by U_low(T_low+1)-4T_low =[U_phys(T_phys+1)-4T_phys]/T_phys^2. All other excluded head and total-coefficient divisors are the same ones above, with F and E exchanged. Thus the single generic frame works for either actual degree adapter at every box. If the marked geometric representation is algebraic, the good frame may be chosen algebraic (in fact rational after fixing its matrix coordinates). To see this use a rational big-cell parametrization of SL2 and clear the finitely many nonzero denominators. A nonzero polynomial over a number field cannot vanish on all rational tuples, by the elementary one-variable root count and induction. Equations (1) and the local inverse then give algebraic magnetic and internal phases. This does not make their logarithms algebraic. ## 3. The unconstrained integral degree lift The leading Morse degree equations are sum_out-sum_in=0 at a coupon, sum_out=1 at a cup, and sum_in=1 at a cap. Regard every physical wire as an oriented edge between successive events. Their coefficient matrix is the oriented incidence matrix of this finite graph: each wire occurs once positively and once negatively. Choose any logarithms of the magnetic X_e. Since the exponentiated degree equations hold, each defect from the desired affine equation is an integer. On each connected component the sum of these defects is zero. The wire terms cancel, and that component has equally many cups and caps, by counting incoming and outgoing half-edges. Every integral vertex vector of total zero is the incidence image of an integral edge vector: choose a spanning tree, remove its leaves one by one, and put the leaf defect on its unique remaining edge. The last defect is zero by the total-sum condition. Adding these integer corrections to the wire logarithms solves all affine degree equations exactly. This does NOT enforce 0<=Re u_e<=1, select the finite low/high support chambers, or erase a recorded phase. The original ordinary and marked cap characters differ by an integral Poisson character and must still be kept. The result is an unrestricted logarithmic lift, not a claim about the support of the physical finite sum. ## 4. Consequence and precise remaining gap In the good common frame reconstruct the local roots from the actual geometric momenta. Both q-Hahn internal equations hold. The local map preserves the whole ordered product and recovers the actual inverse auxiliary transport; at completeness its channel equation is R_epsilon=1. Shared wires carry the SAME X,S, and original cups/caps give the inverse-meridian relation P=I. Thus the local derivatives match on the tangent lattice of the Morse degree constraints, and their exponentials are one. Section 3 supplies an affine degree lift. This is a regular geometric solution of the UNFOLDED exponentiated principal equations, with the original marked representation. It is a genuine candidate input to the regulator comparison. The result does not identify a physical support chamber with a nonempty selected cycle, or show that the required logarithmic/Poisson sector contributes. It makes no claim of a reduced nondegenerate Hessian, nearby holomorphic critical family, nonzero source amplitude, or volume asymptotic. The frame construction is not an argument that one may change the original quantum source by choosing a favorable co-source. It is a coordinate choice on its classical marked character, retaining the original cup/cap equations. The dimension of its framing orbit after the phase-coordinate reductions is not asserted here. ## 5. The remaining bridge to the source-selected local branch The [actual q-Hahn logarithm theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) now selects the local internal branch for REAL strict physical parameters, including the folded endpoint. At that endpoint, if 1/2<tau<1, 0<u<tau, w=exp[pi i(tau-1/2)], its selected logarithmic root satisfies max(0,u-tau+1/2)<Re alpha<min(u,1/2), Im alpha>0. Consequently Z=exp(2pi i alpha) lies in the upper half of the unit disk. The strict inequality tau>1/2 matters: at w=1 the selected alpha is real instead. The implicit function theorem also gives joint complex parameter germs near these regular physical points. These are source-selected local data, not yet a global continuation to the geometric candidate constructed above. The exact endpoint quadratic is [U(T+1)-4T] Z^2+2U(T-1) Z+U(T+1)=0, discriminant=16TU(T+1-U). A small loop about U=T+1 at a generic fixed T exchanges its two roots. Thus unspecified algebraic or holomorphic continuation can change the branch. What is still needed is a common admissible continuation domain, or an explicitly controlled path, which carries the ACTUAL selected local kernels and their original logarithmic marks from a nonempty physical support chamber to the geometric point at every coupon simultaneously. Generic avoidance of the discriminant and the integral affine lift in section 3 do not supply that statement. Even after such a branch comparison, the remaining whole-source cycle and noncancellation estimate would be separate work. Long fillings perturb the auxiliary color parameters chi by O(1/p) near the complete source, with p the filling slope. They do not by themselves resolve this base magnetic branch-selection problem. The source-divisor extension permits a finite-order zero of an already constructed analytic amplitude; it does not construct the missing selected branch or prove that its amplitude germ is nonzero. Audit: [exact generic-chart identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.py).

text: # Selected physical factors outside one exact matching-edge block 30 October 2026. This note assembles two separate inputs: the actual source's full physical packet and the proved right-angled geometric localization. It does not identify a contributing global finite cycle. ## 1. Inputs and statement Fix an actual augmented plat of arbitrary fixed width, with its retained half twists, literal Morse word, original exposed physical mark, and a positive convex ideal right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate as in [the actual matching geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). The actual source is the full marked matching-graph source; its folded labels, partner normals and generic lifts are not replaced by a root-only semisimple network. Choose any one crossing-circle matching edge e. Use the following two established inputs, with their distinct scopes: * The [prescribed-pair geometric theorem](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) supplies a common regular frame with strip flags in the common shaded exterior K. Its only two strict physical-support failures are the two shaded facets at the ends of e. All other ordinary input/output factors have their actual canonical low or high physical coordinates. * The [full physical complex packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) concerns the original finite q-Hahn column. Its limiting domain is P={ (tau,nu) in C^2 : 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }. (1) On each compact of P, for sufficiently large N and actual integer folded channels j with j/N near 1/2, it gives the selected ordinary packet with nonzero amplitude. Its selected characteristic extends from the previously proved central domain. No complex continuation of the finite index j is inferred from this statement. Then the common frame can be chosen so that EVERY ordinary factor outside the two ends of e belongs to the source-selected branch on P. The two exceptions comprise ONE original matching-edge operator, whose four exterior objects all have highest weight d=N-1. That operator has the exact generic recoupling and retained first-normal formula of [the marked four-port block](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md). The original physical mark remains where it was. The finite collection of good factors lies in a common compact subset of P. Consequently their ordinary finite-column packets can be multiplied there, with the product of their nonzero amplitudes and relative error 1+O(1/N). This is a local product statement at the framed geometric germ, not an estimate of the complementary tensor contraction, its summation, or the completed marked source. ## 2. The selected flag branches continue throughout P Here is the additional proof needed beyond the old central-domain statement. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i nu), zeta=T^(1/2)/U, W=1-(T+1)/U, V=W+zeta^2, (2) where T^(1/2)=exp(pi i tau) retains its marked argument. The full packet proves W and V nonzero on P at the endpoint channel xi=1/2. Its square root of W is the analytic continuation from the positive real center. It need not be the pointwise principal square root outside the central domain. Since P is convex and W is nonzero, that continued square root is single valued. Normalize the actual incoming puncture matrices as A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P_disk=B A. The exact original head formulas in the [selected local certificate](actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) give, for image flag z and kernel flag w, U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), Y_in=-w/(z+1), Y_out=Y_in^(-1). (3) First use the low adapter U_phys=U,T_phys=T. Directly solving (3), with delta=U/(1-U), gives the two pairs Delta=U(T+1-U)/T=-U^2 W/T, w=(-1 +/- sqrt(Delta))/(2(1-U)), z=w+delta. (4) The marked exponential arguments in (1) imply U!=1 and U!=T. Equation (2) gives Delta!=0. Thus (4) defines two distinct global analytic pairs of finite flags on P. Their actual normalized prefix triple is (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1/U,1/T). (5) The strict physical criterion applies to this triple throughout (1): the canonical physical wire coordinates are nu and tau-nu. The proved real determinant-pencil argument therefore puts z,w on the same OPEN side of the real disk circle. Neither flag can reach that circle along either analytic branch. In particular no unrecorded passage through infinity changes its side; infinity itself belongs to the forbidden circle. For the actual high adapter one instead has T_phys=1/T, U_phys=U/T. Its physical wires are 1+nu-tau and 1-nu. Both are in the canonical strip, and the total has the required high degree. Crucially, U_phys(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys=Delta. (6) The same discriminant gives the two analytic flag pairs, now using 1-U/T in the denominator. This denominator is nonzero. Their physical triple (1,-T/U,T) is, up to a common nonzero factor and exchange of the outer terms, the triple (5). Hence the same open-side conclusion holds. The full tube P is connected. At any central base point, the original source calibration already proves selected input means both flags below the incoming real circle, and selected output means both flags above its own real circle, in BOTH adapters. The source characteristic has no collision on P, and the flag branches have no collision or circle crossing. Continuing that calibration proves throughout P selected input iff Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output iff Im z>0 and Im w>0. (7) Each line uses that factor's own actual disk normalization. This proof continues the selected root, not the old pointwise test Re sqrt(W)>0. ## 3. From actual strips to all good factors At a complete coupon, the primitive collar gives C=I+b(P_disk+I), with Im b<0 and b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp. In eta(s)=1/(2s+1), eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. Consequently (7) is equivalent, at any STRICTLY PHYSICAL input/output pair, to the same two actual strip tests as before: 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (8) The exact based-prefix dictionary of the right-angled localization identifies these with its common shaded-exterior flags. Choose its prescribed failed facets to be the two ends of e. Every other factor then has strict physical support AND the required oriented strip side. Equations (7),(8), proved on the larger tube, make each of those factors source-selected. This is the extra conclusion that the earlier central-domain theorem could not provide. There are finitely many factors, so their strict margins have a common positive lower bound after fixing this frame. Small neighborhoods of their actual low/high coordinates have compact closure in P. Apply the full packet on those neighborhoods, uniformly for its allowed actual integer channels, and multiply a fixed finite number of estimates. For an algebraic geometric certificate the frame may be chosen algebraic, as in the prescribed-pair theorem. This does not turn the selected logarithmic action into a root-only polynomial evaluation: its original logarithmic characters and finite-source normalization remain specified. ## 4. Exact exceptional block and limits of the conclusion Both exceptional factors are kept together on e. The marked block theorem bends its actual operator K_a by the original physical cups, recouples through EVERY target g=0,...,d, and writes its whole-source first normal as Taylor coefficients of order at most two after clearing the possible simple poles. It retains the original circle weight and half-twist phase. The native row weight and physical cup scale introduce no exponential loss. Its explicit target and complement costs J_g,J_C are still part of that theorem's bound; they are not removed by the present geometric localization. The full packet also supplies the actual small-channel fixed generic jet bounds and the near-fold partner-normal upper bound on these SAME complex compacts. In its notation, for fixed r and s=l-j, |D^r C_j/C_j| <= C_r N^(8r), |w_(j,l)/C_j| <= C N^8(C N^16)^s, s<=eta N. (9) Here D=q d/dq, and the derivatives in the numerator are generic-q derivatives evaluated at the root; the denominator is the ordinary root column. Constants depend on the chosen compact, and every channel is still an actual integer. For a fixed number of good factors, the additional partner-normal loss is exp(O(sum s_i log N)). It is subexponential when each s_i log N=o(N). A fixed nonzero scaled separation is not covered by that inference. These are upper bounds, not a nonzero confluent amplitude. The separate all-physical lattice jet theorem is not by itself a theorem for complex geometric totals. No global cycle, lower bound, nonzero completed saddle coefficient, or sharp estimate of the complementary contraction has been proved here. Nor have we made the entire factorization physical: its two necessary support defects remain, now in one exact block. The useful reduction is that all other ORDINARY factors have an actual selected physical packet, at arbitrary fixed plat width, while the exceptional block has an exact source-preserving expression with its boundary costs displayed. Focused audit: [exact new low/high flag identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.py). It checks both adapters and all four flag branches: eight original-head identities, twelve actual prefix traces, three discriminant identities and four sheet-involution identities. These are new exact algebraic checks only; the outside-central finite-source comparisons belong to the separate full-physical packet audit. The square root is continued from the prescribed matching-edge pair, rather than chosen pointwise as a principal root. The local product theorem does not control the complementary contraction. The proof uses the prescribed-pair identity and the full physical packet; a numerical fixture alone cannot select the global frame or branch.
