text: # A finite certificate for the selected geometric principal phase **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. For any fixed augmented plat, of arbitrary width, this note gives explicit tests which identify the geometric stationary branch with the source-selected LOCAL q-Hahn principal action. It also expresses the endpoint sheet test as a condition on the two common framing flags. No intersection with the original finite summation cycle is inferred. The certificate has not been shown to exist for every positive geometric augmented plat. Its point is to replace an unspecified local branch-identification assumption by finite tests on the actual marked representation, with all input/output signs retained. ## 1. Data and the selected-critical certificate Fix the actual augmented-plat Morse word, retained half twists, and primitive peripheral marks. Supply: 1. An actual marked positive complete gluing certificate, as in [the geometric certificate theorem](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md). It gives the geometric representation, not an unrelated component of the character equations. 2. ONE rank-one projector Pi satisfying all the regular-chart, central-support and cup/cap tests of [the physical framing criterion](actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md). These include the original affine degree equations with the canonical wire logarithms and the actual low/high adapters. 3. The actual magnetic multiplier at each ordinary column factor. At an input it is Y_geo=S_1/S_2; at an output it is Y_geo=S_2/S_1. The momenta S are reconstructed from the original prefix matrices, not chosen separately to make a test pass. 4. The selected-root test in section 2 at every input and output, and the original logarithmic/Poisson characters of the full marked phase. The latter are retained as part of the certificate, rather than erased after exponentiation. These conditions imply the following LOCAL conclusion. The actual geometric critical germ is a germ of the source-selected principal phase. Modulo its two framing directions its magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate. Its fully marked critical action phi has d(2pi i phi)=1/2 sum V_i dU_i, 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D), phi_(chi_i chi_j)(0)=pi i tau_i delta_(ij), (1) with U_i=-2pi i chi_i and the original primitive cusp shapes tau_i. Its ordinary q-Hahn column amplitude factors are nonzero. The conclusion concerns the actual marked phase and its ordinary column factors. It is NOT a full-source amplitude theorem, a bound for generic normal currents, a continuation of the finite discrete channel, or a claim that the original cycle contributes at this germ. ## 2. The local sheet test is algebraic on the marked cover Use the actual low coordinates tau,nu of each column, after applying the high adapter when required. Put xi=1/2, zeta=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], c=-cos(pi tau), W=1+2c zeta, V=1+2c zeta+zeta^2. (2) Here W is a scalar, not a prefix matrix. In the central domain Re c>0, Re zeta>0. Both W/zeta and V/zeta have positive real part; hence W and V avoid the nonpositive real axis. In particular the principal square root of W has strictly positive real part. The [joint original-kernel theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md), section 7, gives the source-selected multiplier Y_sel=(zeta+i sqrt(W))^2/V. (3) For the actual geometric multiplier define r_geo=[V Y_geo-zeta^2+W]/(2i zeta). (4) The actual Casimir characteristic equation says r_geo^2=W. Therefore Y_geo=Y_sel if and only if Re r_geo>0. (5) This is an equality test for the selected root, not just a test that both values solve the characteristic polynomial. The source theorem fixes the square root by its actual center phase and finite-source continuation. All expressions in (2)--(5) are algebraic after retaining the marked square root of T=exp(2pi i tau). Its argument is pi Re tau in (pi/2,pi), which fixes the square-root sign; zeta=T^(1/2)/U with U=exp(2pi i nu). Thus for an algebraic marked representation and projector the endpoint root test is a finite real-algebraic test. The logarithmic characters of the action remain additional marked data, not a consequence of squaring (4). ## 3. Exact flag formulas, including the output sign and high adapter Normalize one actual incoming pair to A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A, H=P+I. Write Pi=v ell, ell(v)=1. In these disk coordinates let w be the kernel flag of ell and let z be the image flag W_prefix v. This use of the actual prefix is essential. Normalize the local rank-one matrix W_prefix Pi by its trace; it has image z and kernel w. In affine coordinates a representative of the local common frame is g=[[1,-w],[1,-z]]. Direct substitution into the original head and prefix formulas gives U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), S_1/S_2=-w/(z+1). (6) The source internal root in a low column is obtained from the actual inverse, at J=-1, Z=-U[y(T-U)+(1-U)]/[-y(T-U)+T(1-U)]. (7) For the input use y=S_1/S_2; for the output use its RECIPROCAL. Equations (6),(7) give Z_in,low=(2w+1)/(2w-1), Z_out,low=(2z+1)/(2z+3). (8) For the high adapter one must first replace T_low=T_phys^(-1), U_low=U_phys/T_phys. Keeping the same actual input/output momentum convention in (7) then gives Z_in,high=-(2z+1)/(2z+3), Z_out,high=-(2w+1)/(2w-1). (9) These are rational identities, not deductions from a root-only symmetry. They retain the output sign of a kernel and the actual high-degree translation. ## 4. The endpoint selected sheets are oriented disk sides For any strict central triple, its two local framing flags z,w are on the SAME open side of the real disk circle, by section 5 of the physical framing criterion. The two roots of the local characteristic give the two opposite choices of that side. One can see the latter directly from (6). Fix U_phys,T_phys and put d=U_phys/(1-U_phys)=z-w. The equation for w is quadratic; its roots have sum -(d+1). Consequently its two flag pairs are related by (z,w) -> (-w-1,-z-1). (10) They therefore lie on opposite sides of the real circle. There is no collision or boundary crossing in the central domain. For example T+1-U cannot vanish there: arg T is in (pi,2pi), arg(1+T) is strictly between arg T and 2pi, while the strict physical U argument lies between 0 and arg T. The other regular root denominators are excluded by the regular-chart assumptions. The simple characteristic and the connected central domain preserve the two sheet labels. At a strict physical real point, the actual selected internal root Z is in the upper half of the unit disk, as proved by the original q-Hahn selection theorem. Equation (8) then gives w below the real circle for an input, and z above it for an output. Equation (9) gives the SAME respective side choices in the high adapter. Together with the same-side necessity, continuation through the central domain therefore proves the equivalent tests selected input <=> Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output <=> Im z>0 and Im w>0, (11) where each line uses that factor's OWN actual disk normalization. The inequalities in (11), rather than an upper-half-disk assertion for Z at arbitrary complex parameters, are what continue globally. They agree with (5); either supplies the same endpoint sheet test. ## 5. A global strip-intersection question remains For one actual complete coupon its transport is C=I+bH. The primitive mark fixes b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp, so Im b<0 for the positive geometric orientation. In the incoming disk coordinate set eta(s)=1/(2s+1). Direct substitution gives eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. The incoming condition in (11) becomes Im eta>0; the outgoing condition, in the disk frame C^(-1), becomes Im(eta+2b)<0. Thus, CONDITIONAL ON the strict central inequalities, both input and output are selected exactly when 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (12) This is the actual oriented region between the two developed disk circles. Positivity of the primitive cusp orientation gives its positive height. It does not prove that all such regions meet. Let Omega_f denote this region in the one global flag sphere, using the actual input disk normalization at coupon f. Formula (12) gives the necessary separated global conditions w in intersection_f Omega_f, v in intersection_f W_f^(-1) Omega_f. (13) Once the coupled central tests also hold, (13) is sufficient for ALL endpoint local sheet tests. This is a finite geometric version of the certificate. It identifies the precise role of the actual prefix pullbacks; independent local flags do not establish (13). No general identification of these intersections with exteriors of polyhedral face disks is asserted here. Such an identification would need the actual based words and both disk copies, as well as the coupled central inequalities. The common-product feasibility lemma in the preceding framing note concerns support only; it does not by itself supply these selected input/output sheets. ## 6. Proof of the certificate and precise persistence The sheet test identifies each actual geometric magnetic multiplier with the selected local multiplier. The regular inverse (7) then identifies its internal root with the source-selected root, including the high adapter. The original full coupon phase, its factorial measure, external phases and marked cap characters are retained. Fixing the stipulated logarithmic/Poisson characters gives the actual marked principal phase, rather than merely its exponentiated equations. The [critical-scheme inverse](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) now identifies this germ with the actual marked geometric representation germ modulo the diagonal scale. The positive multi-cusp gluing rigidity theorem makes its only magnetic null directions the two framing directions. A transverse framing slice therefore has nondegenerate magnetic Hessian. The same theorem's classical action corollary, using the primitive collar differential and the absolute endpoint regulator, gives exactly (1). No new period normalization is introduced by the test. The joint column theorem gives, for actual integer channels with real xi_N=j/N near 1/2, the nonzero ordinary amplitude fhat=N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(1/N)). A fixed finite product of such ordinary factors has the product estimate on a compact common domain. This supplies nonzero ordinary column amplitude germs at the certified branch; it supplies neither generic normal-factor estimates nor a full-source saddle coefficient. All strict central inequalities and (5) persist under small marked peripheral deformation. The unramified geometric germ and transverse critical slice then continue the certified CLASSICAL selected branch. The selected coefficient functions also continue holomorphically in xi near 1/2. This applies to sufficiently long geometric fillings, with their original primitive marks. It does not continue the finite discrete index j to a complex value or justify a channel contour. The remaining global tasks are substantive: produce the certificate for a broad geometric class, control all required normal currents, and prove that the original finite cycle has the required contribution and global exponential bound. This note resolves none of those tasks merely by having a stationary point with the correct volume. Audit: [exact original-head, adapter and strip identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.py). The certificate distinguishes classical continuation from a finite-channel or whole-source asymptotic. Its general existence and the existence of a contributing cycle are not established here.

title: The crossing-circle cusp lattice, including its half-twist marking
text: # The crossing-circle cusp lattice, including its half-twist marking 29 October 2026. The explicit face-labeled antiprism geometry gives the crossing-circle cusp shape without an additional factor two. Put \(c=\cos(\pi/s)\). In the positive diagonal half-twist marking, \[ \boxed{\qquad \tau_{\mathrm{std},+} =\frac{2ic}{1+ic} =\frac{2c^2+2ic}{1+c^2}.\qquad} \tag{1} \] The opposite half twist has \(\tau_{\mathrm{std},-}=2ic/(1-ic)\), whose real part is negative and whose imaginary part is the same. At \(s=3\), these are \(\pm2/5+4i/5\). The untwisted marked shape is \(2ic\). These statements concern the crossing-circle cusps, not the main component cusp. The words “positive diagonal” specify the peripheral marking below. The metric face pairing alone does not distinguish the two half twists: they differ by a full twist. Consequently (1) is not, by itself, a proof that an independently defined quantum logarithm is the preferred longitude, or a proof of its sign convention. It gives an explicit two-path calibration for making that comparison. ## 1. Compute one actual horospherical rectangle Use the explicit \(\mathcal P_s\) in [the geometric-volume proof](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md). Set \(\alpha=\pi/s\), \(t=\tan(\pi/4-\alpha/2)\), and \(\rho=t^{-1/2}\). Before doubling the antiprism its ideal vertices in the complex boundary are \[ Z_k=\rho e^{2ik\alpha},\qquad U_k^+=\rho^{-1}e^{(2k+1)i\alpha}. \] Reflection across the base circle \(|z|=\rho\) gives the other half of the doubled polyhedron: \(U_k^-=\rho^3e^{(2k+1)i\alpha}\). The four neighbors of \(Z_0=\rho\) are \(U_{-1}^{\pm},U_0^{\pm}\). Send \(Z_0\) to infinity by the holomorphic Mobius map \(m(z)=1/(z-\rho)\). Their images form a Euclidean rectangle. For an explicit calculation put \(A=\rho^2=(1+\sin\alpha)/\cos\alpha\). The lower left and lower right corners are \[ m(U_0^+)=-\frac{\rho A}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)} -i\frac{\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)}, \] \[ m(U_0^-)=\frac{1}{\rho\sin\alpha(1+A^2)} -i\frac{\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)}. \] The other two are their complex conjugates. Hence the width and height are \[ W=\frac1{\rho\sin\alpha},\qquad H=\frac{2\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)},\qquad \boxed{H/W=\frac{2A}{1+A^2}=\cos\alpha=c.} \tag{2} \] Since all incident faces are vertical planes after this Mobius map, their intersections with any horosphere about infinity give exactly this rectangle, up to its common Euclidean scale. Its vertical sides are the shaded \(T_0^+,T_0^-\) faces. Its horizontal sides are the white \(Q_0,Q_{-1}\) faces. Normalize by \(W\) and translate to the rectangle \([0,1]\times[0,c]\). There are exactly TWO such rectangles at this cusp, one from each projection polyhedron. There are not four cusp rectangles merely because the whole three-manifold contains four antiprisms: doubling across a base merges the two half rectangles into the one just computed. ## 2. Develop the exact face pairings Keep rectangle 0 at \(x+iy\), \(0\leq x\leq1\), \(0\leq y\leq c\). White gluing by the original vertex labels develops rectangle 1 as \[ x+iy\longmapsto x+i(2c-y). \tag{3} \] It lies in \([0,1]\times[c,2c]\). The two white identifications therefore give the vertical period \(2ic\). For no half twist, shaded gluing is within each copy and matches the same outer labels. It identifies its left and right sides at the same local \(y\), giving period 1. Thus the untwisted lattice is \[ \mathcal L_0=\langle1,2ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z}. \tag{4} \] For a half twist, the original face pairing switches copies AND exchanges the two outer labels. In local rectangle coordinates it sends \((0,y)_0\mapsto(1,c-y)_1\). In the development (3) its translation is \(1+ic\). The other shaded pair gives \(1-ic\). Consequently the half-twisted lattice is \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal L_{\mathrm h} =\langle1+ic,1-ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z} =\langle2,1+ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z}.\quad} \tag{5} \] Its area is \(2c\), the sum of the two original rectangle areas. ## 3. Identify the meridian and preferred longitude paths The shaded faces are the two sides of the original twice-punctured crossing disk. The cusp boundary of that disk runs ALONG their vertical sides and passes through the two white identifications. It has translation \[ \lambda=2ic. \tag{6} \] This is the disk-framed longitude: pushing the crossing circle off inside its spanning disk has zero linking with the circle itself. Punctures by the other component do not change that self-linking calculation. The loop traverses each of the two shaded sides once; using \(4ic\) would traverse this longitude twice. A positively transverse local meridian crosses the disk seam once. In the untwisted marking it has translation 1. In the positive diagonal half-twist marking it follows the corner path \((0,0)_0\mapsto(1,c)_1\) in local labels and has \[ \mu_+=1+ic. \tag{7} \] The opposite half-twist marking uses \(\mu_-=1-ic=\mu_+-\lambda\). Both \((\mu_+,\lambda)\) and \((\mu_-,\lambda)\) are primitive bases of (5): their oriented parallelogram area is \(2c\). Equations (6)--(7) prove (1). In particular choosing a half of \(\lambda\) would not define a curve in (5), and doubling \(\lambda\) would not give a peripheral basis. The explicit integer-shear calibration is \[ \mu_++p\lambda=1+i(2p+1)c,\qquad \mu_-+p\lambda=1+i(2p-1)c. \tag{8} \] Thus a claimed filling equation must record which of these two base meridians corresponds to its retained physical half twist. The original source \(R^{-(2p+1)}\) has a specified braid convention and a specified kernel integer \(p\). To match it to (8), it is enough to identify the \(p=0\) corner path and the direction of the \(p\mapsto p+1\) full twist; one cannot infer that information from the unmarked ideal triangle isometry alone. Replacing \(R^{-1}\) by \(R\) changes the half-twist marking by one longitude even though the complete metric volume is unchanged. ## 4. Comparison with the complete mixed-phase Hessian If the original mixed-phase coordinates have \(z=2\log M\), \(\partial G/\partial z=\log L\), and \(\partial^2G/\partial z_i^2=\tau_s\), then the geometric cusp shape they predict is \(\tau_{\mathrm{std}}=2\tau_s\), since \(d\log L/d\log M=2\,d\log L/dz\). For the stated formal value \[ \tau_s=e^{iu_*}\cos u_*,\qquad \tan u_*=\sec\alpha, \] one gets \[ 2\tau_s=\frac{2ic}{1+ic}, \] which is exactly the positive-diagonal shape (1). This independent geometric calculation excludes the proposed extra factor two. It does not supply the missing quantum-to-peripheral coordinate identification or select the half-twist sign by itself. There is a concrete source sign to check in making that identification. For the literal auxiliary color \(j=N-h\), put \(H=Q^h\). The centered auxiliary meridian \(M_{\mathrm{aux}}=-q^j\) has \(2\operatorname{Log} M_{\mathrm{aux}}=-\operatorname{Log} H\). Thus if a phase calculation uses \(z=\operatorname{Log} H\) and \(G_z=\operatorname{Log} L_H\), its ratio with this auxiliary meridian is \(-2G_{zz}\), not \(+2G_{zz}\). The positive sign in the preceding comparison requires, for example, the dual longitude \(L_{\mathrm{geom}}=L_H^{-1}\). This is a coordinate/peripheral sign that must be proved; it cannot be hidden in the rectangle count. For coverage only, the statement of Theorem 1.1 in [Purcell--Reid--Stewart](https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/papers/GeometryAugLinksSfces.pdf) records that crossing-circle cusps have two rectangles, that the longitude uses two shaded sides, and that a half-twist meridian is a diagonal. No proof from that source is used above. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_pretzel_crossing_circle_cusp.py) checks the literal vertex images, labeled face translations, primitive areas and both half-twist/filling markings at 28 widths.

title: The geometric volume of the literal augmented pretzel source
text: # The geometric volume of the literal augmented pretzel source 29 October 2026. The link underlying the original \(s\)-box source \(B_i=R^{-1}L_N\), for odd \(s\geq3\), is a half-twist partner of the untwisted fully augmented pretzel link. It has \(s+1\) components, not one. Both complements have the volume \[ \boxed{\displaystyle V_s=8s\left[ \Lambda\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2s}\right) +\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4-\frac\pi{2s}\right)\right].} \tag{1} \] Here is an explicit face-labeled geometric construction and a direct volume calculation. No quantum invariant is changed. In particular, volume invariance of the half-twist partners does NOT permit deleting the retained half twists from their original quantum source. ## 1. A right-angled ideal antiprism constructed explicitly Put \(\alpha=\pi/s\), \(h=\tan(\alpha/2)\), and \(r=\sqrt{1-h^2}\). In the ideal boundary of the Klein ball take \[ A_k=(r\cos(2k\alpha),r\sin(2k\alpha),h), \quad B_k=(r\cos((2k+1)\alpha),r\sin((2k+1)\alpha),-h). \] Their convex hull is the \(s\)-antiprism \(\mathcal A_s\): two \(s\)-gonal faces and the \(2s\) staggered side triangles. For example the side face \((A_0,A_1,B_0)\), in coordinates rotated by \(\alpha\), has supporting plane \[ X+bZ=c,\qquad b=\frac{r(1-\cos\alpha)}{2h},\quad c=\frac{r(1+\cos\alpha)}2. \] Its spacelike Lorentz normal is \((c,\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha,b)\). The top face normal is \((h,0,0,1)\). Their Lorentz product is \(b-hc=0\), exactly because \(h^2=(1-\cos\alpha)/(1+\cos\alpha)\). The adjacent lower side face has normal \((c,1,0,-b)\); its product with the upper normal is \(\cos\alpha-b^2-c^2=0\). Rotations and the top/bottom symmetry give every other edge. Thus ALL dihedral angles are \(\pi/2\). All vertices are distinct and ideal, all the face planes are supporting, and their normals are spacelike. This constructs the metric directly. ## 2. The actual projection polyhedra are DOUBLES of antiprisms Double \(\mathcal A_s\) across one of its \(s\)-gonal faces. The adjacent triangle pairs become coplanar and merge to quadrilaterals. The resulting ideal right-angled polyhedron \(\mathcal P_s\) has vertices \[ Z_k,\ U_k^+,\ U_k^-,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z/s, \] and the following face cycles: \[ W_+=(U_{s-1}^+,\ldots,U_0^+),\quad W_-=(U_0^-,\ldots,U_{s-1}^-), \] \[ Q_k=(Z_k,U_k^+,Z_{k+1},U_k^-), \quad T_k^+=(Z_k,U_{k-1}^+,U_k^+),\quad T_k^-=(Z_k,U_k^-,U_{k-1}^-). \tag{2} \] The white faces are \(W_\pm,Q_k\), the shaded faces are \(T_k^\pm\). There are \(3s\) ideal vertices, \(6s\) edges, \(s\) white quads, two white \(s\)-gons and \(2s\) shaded triangles. Every edge separates a white and a shaded face. This is exactly the topological projection-plane cut of the untwisted pretzel port graph in [the original source theorem](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md). The \(k\)-th crossing disk meets the adjacent planar arcs labeled \(U_{k-1},U_k\); flattening its two sides gives the bowtie \(T_k^+,T_k^-\) with common ideal crossing-circle vertex \(Z_k\). Between consecutive disks, the planar arc gives the quad \(Q_k\). The two remaining planar regions follow the cycles \(W_+,W_-\). Thus cutting the two complementary balls along the crossing disks gives TWO copies \(\mathcal P_s^{(0)},\mathcal P_s^{(1)}\), with the displayed face identifications. This is a labeled cellulation of the literal link complement, not just a match of its cusp count. In the untwisted graph, white faces glue across the two copies by their labels, while each \(T_k^+\) glues to \(T_k^-\) WITHIN its own copy, fixing \(Z_k\) and matching each outer index to itself. Restoring a half twist changes that shaded gluing to \[ T_k^+\subset\mathcal P_s^{(\epsilon)} \longleftrightarrow T_k^-\subset\mathcal P_s^{(1-\epsilon)}, \quad Z_k\mapsto Z_k,\quad U_{k-1}^+\mapsto U_k^-,\quad U_k^+\mapsto U_{k-1}^- . \tag{3} \] The CROSS-COPY change in (3) is necessary: swapping the two outer labels inside the same oriented copy would give the wrong boundary orientation. Equation (3) is the actual exchange of the two punctures of the crossing disk. It realizes the retained odd half twist of \(R^{-1}L_N\); its sign affects the peripheral marking, not this metric volume. The ordinary circle is not filled or removed. Every edge cycle has FOUR right angles under either choice, including mixed choices at different disks. Symmetric small horospheres can be chosen at the two vertex orbits \(Z\) and \(U\). The white isometries preserve them. The two outer vertices of each shaded triangle have equal decorations by its reflection symmetry, so BOTH the untwisted and half-twisted shaded identifications preserve them. Thus the cusp rectangles glue without dilation to compact flat tori. This verifies completeness as well as the \(2\pi\) edge equations. The untwisted link has \(s\) planar main components and \(s\) crossing circles. With every half twist restored, following the main strands advances their labels by two modulo \(s\); for odd \(s\) these form one main component. The literal quantum base therefore has \(s+1\) cusps. It is an AUGMENTED LINK base, not the filled pretzel knot. We have constructed the same complete finite-volume metric from two copies of \(\mathcal P_s\), hence FOUR copies of \(\mathcal A_s\), for all these half-twist partners. No hyperbolic Dehn filling is used in this equality. ## 3. Direct volume of one antiprism Send the north ideal point to \(\infty\) in upper half-space by stereographic coordinates. For \(t=\tan(\pi/4-\alpha/2)\) and \(\rho=t^{-1/2}\), the vertices are \[ a_k=\rho e^{2ik\alpha},\qquad b_k=\rho^{-1}e^{(2k+1)i\alpha}. \] Cone the oriented boundary faces to \(\infty\), triangulating the two base polygons in matching fans. This is the ordinary signed pyramid volume identity, obtainable first with a finite cone point and then by taking its ideal limit. The two base-cone volumes cancel: the similarity \(z\mapsto\rho^{-2}e^{i\alpha}z\) takes one fan to the other, fixes \(\infty\), and their boundary orientations are opposite. No assertion that all these outside cones form a disjoint triangulation is needed. Each side pair gives the two oriented ideal tetrahedron shapes \[ z_+=\tfrac12+\tfrac i2 t,\qquad z_-=\tfrac12-\frac i{2t}, \] with net volume \(D(z_+)-D(z_-)\). Put \(\beta_\pm=\pi/4\pm\alpha/2\). Their Euclidean triangle angles give \[ D(z_+)=2\Lambda(\beta_-)-\Lambda(2\beta_-) =2\Lambda(\beta_+), \] \[ -D(z_-)=2\Lambda(\beta_+)-\Lambda(2\beta_+) =2\Lambda(\beta_-). \] The last equalities follow by differentiating the elementary Lobachevsky duplication identity and fixing its value at zero. Summing over the \(s\) side pairs proves \[ \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal A_s) =2s[\Lambda(\beta_+)+\Lambda(\beta_-)], \] and multiplying by four proves (1). At \(s=3\), the explicitly constructed antiprism is a regular ideal octahedron, so \(V_3=4v_8\), not \(2v_8\). ## 4. Coverage and exact quantum scope For coverage only, Kellerhals's [abstract, introduction and Theorem C](https://homeweb.unifr.ch/kellerha/pub/Kellerhals-FAL.pdf) identify the untwisted pretzel FAL with the \(2s\)-chain-link family, state the four-antiprism decomposition, and state the same volume formula. The derivation above is independent of that paper's proof. The [Meyer--Millichap--Trapp abstract](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2020/26-8.html) also records the study of fully augmented pretzel link complements. No literature volume-conjecture proof is being used. Equation (1) is the genuine geometric right side for the unfilled source \(B_i=R^{-1}L_N\). It does not prove its quantum asymptotics, nonzero geometric coefficient, or the analogous assertion for its fixed-slope fillings. All retained half-twist phases, the original marked cut and the full peripheral line remain in the source theorem; they have not been replaced by the untwisted invariant. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.py) checks the normals/supporting planes, all labeled face pairings and edge cycles, cusp links and original half-twist component counts, and the independent ideal-tetrahedron volume calculation.

title: A finite algebraic dominant-root certificate for the actual backward cubic
text: # A finite algebraic dominant-root certificate for the actual backward cubic 29 October 2026. This is an exact spectral input for the next original Newton source packet in [the endpoint theorem](actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.md). It proves a strict dominant-mode gap on every closed subinterval of 0<=u<pi/2 for its actual backward principal cubic. It does not infer the original source projection from two scalar endpoint sizes, nor claim a whole-word asymptotic without the exact backward source/current. ## 1. The cubic and the assertion Put Z=exp(-2iu) and f_Z(lambda)=lambda^3+(5Z-3)lambda^2 +(3-7Z+3Z^2)(1-Z)lambda-(1-Z)^5. (1) There is a continuous root mu(u), beginning at mu(0)=-2, which is the UNIQUE root of largest modulus for 0<=u<pi/2. It is nonzero and simple there. Consequently for every fixed u_0<pi/2 there are constants min_(0<=u<=u0)|mu(u)|>0, max_(0<=u<=u0,max other roots lambda)|lambda/mu(u)|<1. (2) The small roots may collide at u=0, but the isolated dominant line remains regular there. At u=pi/2 the largest moduli do tie; no strict gap at that endpoint is asserted. The discriminant is exactly disc f_Z=-Z^6(Z-1)^2(27Z^2-54Z+23). (3) The two zeros of its last factor are positive real numbers different from1. Thus all three roots are distinct on 0<u<=pi/2. Distinctness alone would not prove(2): the FORWARD cubic of this same source has an interior dominant-modulus switch. We instead exclude dominant ties by the finite real-algebraic calculation below. ## 2. An exact test for a pair of equal moduli For p(lambda)=lambda^3+a lambda^2+b lambda+c, c!=0, form the cubic T(t)=[a^3 c(t+2)-a^2 b^2-a b c(t^2+5t+4) +b^3(t+2)+c^2(t+1)^3]/c^2. (4) Its three roots, counted with multiplicity, are lambda_i/lambda_j+lambda_j/lambda_i, i<j. Indeed a direct resultant identity is Res_lambda(p(lambda),w^3 p(lambda/w)) =c^3(w-1)^3 w^3 T(w+w^-1). (5) Two nonzero distinct roots have equal modulus only if their root of T is REAL in[-2,2]. Conversely a real t in[-2,2] gives a unit-modulus ratio, by solving w+w^-1=t. This is an exact test, including an opposite root pair t=-2. Specialize(4) to a=5Z-3, b=(3-7Z+3Z^2)(1-Z), c=-(1-Z)^5. On the open lower unit semicircle put v=Z+Z^-1=2cos(2u), so -2<v<2. Write R=R_2/2 and R_2=2(v-2)^4 t^3 +(-3v^4+39v^3-166v^2+292v-184)t^2 +(15v^4-72v^3+141v^2-181v+134)t -7v^4+62v^3-87v^2-132v+220, I=(9v^3-57v^2+120v-84)t^2 +(-9v^3+120v^2-373v+339)t +9v^3-66v^2+235v-288. Exact expansion gives (T_Z+T_(Z^-1))/2=R/(v-2)^4, (T_Z-T_(Z^-1))/(Z-Z^-1)=I/(v-2)^4. (6) For real t, an equal-modulus pair must therefore satisfy R=I=0. Their resultant and linear subresultant are Res_t(R,I)=(v-2)^4 P(v), S_1=(v-2)^4[A(v)t+C(v)], (7) where P=19683v^13-275562v^12+1388745v^11-1804275v^10 -10052343v^9+44382411v^8-41161510v^7-136024030v^6 +409871548v^5-286814789v^4-449999851v^3 +1045577541v^2-804786993v+230409954, A=486v^6-3807v^5+8973v^4+4038v^3 -51728v^2+82608v-43461, C=-243v^6+3240v^5-12492v^4+6666v^3 +61295v^2-138366v+89982. The audit verifies the displayed polynomial identities by exact symbolic arithmetic. No fitted spectral curve or floating-point root count is used. ## 3. Only one interior parameter can have an equal-modulus pair Exact Sturm counts show P has precisely TWO roots in(-2,2), one in each of the rational intervals J_-=[-1761026772/10^9,-1761026771/10^9], J_+=[ 1314531712/10^9, 1314531713/10^9]. (8) Horner evaluation with rational interval arithmetic proves A!=0 on both intervals. On J_-, 1<-C/A<2; on J_+, 4<-C/A<5. The latter root cannot give an equal-modulus pair because t must belong to[-2,2]. All possible interior ties are therefore at the single root v_* in J_-. Approximate values, used ONLY as labels, are v_*=-1.761026771989515..., t_*=1.479926424410411..., u_eq/pi=.421400986116556... . ## 4. That possible tie involves only the two smaller roots For v in J_-, the corresponding lower-unit-circle Z lies in the exact rectangle Re Z in J_-/2, -474021285/10^9 < Im Z < -474021281/10^9. (9) The imaginary bounds follow by squaring their positive absolute values against 1-v^2/4. Use the following rational centers and radius r=1/1000: z_1=(1168965+2383072 i)/10^6, z_2=(2467958+ 977085 i)/10^6, z_3=(3765644- 990050 i)/10^6. (10) For every Z in(9), exact rectangular arithmetic gives, for each center, |f_Z(z_j)|<1/50000, |f'_Z(z_j)|>1, |3z_j+(5Z-3)|<20. On |lambda-z_j|=r the Taylor remainder is consequently bounded by 1/50000+20r^2+r^3 < r < |f'_Z(z_j)|r. Rouche's theorem isolates exactly one root in each disk. The disks are pairwise disjoint, so they exhaust all three roots. Their centers satisfy the exact rational inequalities |z_1|,|z_2|<3-r, |z_3|>3+r. Thus the first two roots have modulus<3 and the third modulus>3. In particular a tie at v_* cannot be a tie for the largest modulus. At u=0 the isolated root -2 is strictly larger than the two zero roots. By(3) it continues without an eigenvalue collision. Dominance could be lost only at an equal-modulus pair, and sections2--4 have excluded every possible dominant tie in the open half-circle. This proves(1)--(2). ## 5. What the actual source still has to supply This certificate is a usable piece of a source-selection proof rather than a replacement for it. For the literal backward recurrence, retain its three-component initial vector and all inhomogeneous currents. On a prefix where its exact evolution is the homogeneous companion of(1) plus a uniform smooth O(1/N) matrix error, suppose its actual initial vector is a nonzero polynomial-scale multiple of the dominant vector plus a relative error epsilon_N=o(1). This allows the actual O(N^(-1/2)) initial error, not only O(1/N). Then(2) proves dominant transport on every strict half-prefix by the following direct iteration. Choose a smooth dominant/complement frame, divide each step by mu, and obtain a scalar block1+O(1/N) coupled by O(1/N) to a uniformly stable two-dimensional block B(u). For any fixed strict prefix its powers are uniformly exponentially bounded: the two-by-two Cayley--Hamilton formula bounds them by C(m+1)r^m for some r<1, including coincident fast eigenvalues. Hence H(u)=sum_(m>=0) (B(u)^m)^* B(u)^m converges with bounded first derivative, I<=H<=C I, and H-B^*HB=I. Thus the B norm contracts by at most sqrt(1-1/C)<1. The moving-frame/moving-H error per step is O(1/N). Write a_i,b_i for the scalar and complementary components after dividing out the accumulated mu factors. For a fixed sigma<1, a direct induction in these block equations gives ||b_i||/|a_i| <= C[sigma^i epsilon_N+1/N], a_i/a_(i-1)=1+O(1/N). The induction starts because a_0 is nonzero and epsilon_N tends to0; the stable block absorbs its O(1/N) errors for all sufficiently large N. Every scalar ratio is then nonzero, and its product is bounded above and below by fixed positive constants. The total scalar coupling from the initial transient is at most C epsilon_N/N, since sum sigma^i is bounded. Summed logarithms have O(1) error relative to the dominant primitive. The double FAST root at0 causes no problem: only the dominant projection must be smooth, and its complementary block is uniformly stable there. The hypotheses in that last paragraph concern the ACTUAL vector source. Two scalar endpoint magnitudes do not establish them. The exact Q^2 delta_(i,1) forcing and the second reset D_2=0 of the forward Ward equation cannot be deleted when deriving this backward vector. In particular an interior inhomogeneous current must either be retained as an additional state with its own estimate, or bounded directly; the spectral result(2) does not make it harmless. Regularity of the cubic or nonzero Gaussian endpoint values alone is not being called a whole-source theorem. Audit: [exact ratio identities, Sturm intervals and three rational root disks](../experiments/audit_actual_backward_cubic_dominant_source_certificate.py). It uses exact rational arithmetic throughout, with no sampled eigenvalue plot or numerical integral in its proof.

title: A regular balanced full-Psi Fourier kernel for the original crossing source
text: # A regular balanced full-Psi Fourier kernel for the original crossing source 28 October 2026. At the complete original color, independent finite Fourier frames turn the entire two-Newton/one-Rogers crossing into a regular, explicitly normalized full-Psi Fourier kernel. All three finite source norms vanish on this frame's Fermat multisection. The resulting operator is EXACTLY the original physical crossing. The proof first bounds every possible alias error to degree +N, then eliminates it with one exact original E-coproduct Ward identity. Consequently all original words, currents, caps and sources are retained. This is stronger than setting a central scalar to one inside the old co-source. The external frames and internal Fermat sampling are part of one specified finite source map. Every intermediate frame change, original cup/cap, pivot and scalar line remains. The theorem does not prove a nonzero global geometric intersection or scalar volume limit. ## 1. Original kernel and the finite frames Use q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), s=x^N, so s^2=1. Retain the original common Cartan scalar kappa. The exact [complete positive layer](actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.md) is the original physical finite block of kappa CT_t K(t), K=B_N(t/z1,x^(-1)t/z0) R_N(z6/z0,x^(-1)z6/t) B_N(x^(-1)z7/z6,x^(-2)z7/t). (1) The complete positive Gaussian cell has ALREADY been contracted in (1); this is its exact finite coefficient identity, not a pointwise discard of a continuous Gaussian. The finite polynomials are B_N(u,v)=sum_(j=0)^d product_(k=0)^(j-1)(u-Q^k v), R_N(u,v)=sum_(i+j<N) F_(i+j)/(F_i F_j) u^i v^j. For nonzero r define the normalized finite frame F(r)_(k,a)=N^(-1/2) (r Q^k)^a, F(r)^(-1)_(a,k)=N^(-1/2) (r Q^k)^(-a). (2) Choose nonzero central values A,B with B!=s A, and fixed roots r0^N=A, r1^N=B, r6=x r1, r7=x r0, t0^(-N)=r1^(-N)-r7^(-N). (3) The last quantity is nonzero. For each external pair of input/output Fourier labels evaluate z_i=r_i Q^(label_i), and set t_j=t0 Q^j. Define the TWO-HEAD Fourier matrix M_(k,l;i,j)=kappa/N^3 sum_(m=0)^d K(t0 Q^m), (4) at these four external grid points. Define its decoded physical operator by Rhat_+=(F(r6)^(-1) tensor F(r7)^(-1)) M (F(r0) tensor F(r1)). (5) The factor N^(-3) in (4) is exact: N^(-2) is the two-head Fourier kernel normalization and N^(-1) is internal root averaging. **Exact-operator theorem.** Rhat_+=R_+, including its original Cartan line. Section 2 first proves that their difference can only have degree +N in the original finite index basis. Section 5 then proves that this difference is zero, using the actual E current. ## 2. The exact degree/carry proof Expand the three factors of (1) with indices (i,j),(r,k),(h,l), respectively, each nonnegative pair having sum<N. A term has external input/output exponents a=j+r, b=i, c=r+k-h, e=h+l, t-power p=i+j-k-l, c+e-a-b=-p. (6) Consequently a in[0,2d], b,e in[0,d], c in[-d,d], p in[-2d,d]. Internal root averaging keeps precisely p=0 and p=-N. Its latter term is t0^(-N)[t^(-N)]K. For p=-N, the same inequalities show that a<N and c>=0: a>=N would force output total>=2N, while c<0 would force output total<d. Neither is possible. Thus these terms already have valid original head indices and change degree by N. External inverse Fourier extraction folds a,c modulo N. On p=0, an input a>=N folds to a-N and adds degree N; an output c<0 folds to c+N and also adds degree N. These two cases cannot coincide: the former has original input total>=N, the latter original output total<d. All remaining p=0 terms are exactly the original physical finite block of (1). This proves the theorem. All root radius factors are retained in the folding; they are nonzero scalars and do not alter the degree calculation. On b physical heads the ideal of strictly positive changes N,2N,... has b-th power zero. Every original signed crossing preserves degree. Thus a word in these completed blocks differs from its original word only by that source-null ideal. The full original pointed partial trace kills it entrywise, and the pointed plat source kills it by its actual ordinary-cap constraints. The marked row alone is not assumed fixed-degree: cups have total k d, ordinary caps require (k-1)d, and an error would force the last pair to degree d+N>2d. This is the same proved [integer-degree source mechanism](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md). ## 3. ALL three original source norms vanish on this actual grid Write T=t0^N, and at a grid point put u=t/z1, v=x^(-1)t/z0, f=x^(-1)z7/z6, r=z6/z0, w=x^(-1)z6/t. Their central powers are independent of all the finite labels: u^N=T/B, v^N=s T/A, r^N=s B/A, w^N=B/T, f^N=s A/B, (fw)^N=s A/T. Equation (3) implies exactly 1-u^N+v^N=0, 1-r^N-w^N=0, 1-f^N+(fw)^N=0. (7) All factors are regular on the stated torus: r^N and w^N are nonzero and different from one; the same holds for the central arguments of the Newton full-Psi factors, 1/u and v/u (and 1/f and w). The bare v^N itself need not avoid one. Hence each original finite polynomial equals its FULL source-normalized homogeneous term on this multisection: B_N(u,v)=S_B(u,v), R_N(r,w)=T_R(r,w), B_N(f,fw)=S_B(f,fw). (8) These are consequences of the independently proved finite source identities and their exact Fermat normalizers, including the opposite-root Rogers current. No current is thrown away before the complete sampling map (1)--(5). The regular restrictions in (3) ensure that the currents in those identities are regular; at a collision their combined finite expression must instead be continued, as usual. ## 4. Explicit normalized full-Psi Fourier evaluation Use the exact notations and constants of [the complete Fourier source, Sections 5--6 and 11](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md). Let a,b,c,d0 be the retained logarithms of z0,z1,z6,z7, respectively, X=Log x and tau0=Log t0. Put beta=b-a-X, f_log=d0-c-X, rho=c-a, z=h+b-tau0, lambda=d0-b+2pi*i. The original affine 2pi*i mark is retained. Define C_boundary=(N^2/phi_N) exp[N(f_log-b)](1-exp(Nrho)) *Psi_+(beta)Psi_+(h-f_log)/Psi_+(rho) *exp{[beta*b-(c-X)(f_log+rho)]/h}, H_bal=i sqrt(N) phi_N zeta_0 (1-exp(-Nlambda)) exp[(N+z/h)lambda]. (9) Then EVERY entry of (4) is exactly M=kappa/N^3 C_boundary *(1-exp[N(c-X-tau0)]) exp(lambda*tau0/h) *H_bal*F_ref(lambda). (10) F_ref is the independently normalized full-Phi Fourier function F_ref(lambda)=zeta_0/(i sqrt(N)) *exp[i sqrt(N)lambda c_b-iNlambda^2/(4pi)] *Psi_+(lambda+2pi*i+h). (11) Thus (10) has FOUR variable full-Psi factors and its explicitly known Gaussian and central norm factors. It is an evaluation of the continued Fourier function with its stated logarithmic marks; an unrecorded move to a convergent real contour is not asserted. For the proof, exact shared-face sewing first gives Psi_-(sigma-h)Psi_+(sigma)=1-exp(Nsigma). After separation the only internal full function is Psi_+(z-hj). Its orbit is sum_j Psi_+(z-hj)exp(lambda*j) =Psi_+(z)B_(Q^(-1))(exp lambda, exp(lambda+z-h)). Here the second Newton balance is automatic: exp(Nlambda)(1-exp(Nz))=1. (12) The fully normalized resonant identity of Section 11 therefore has zero closure current and equals H_bal F_ref. Substitution gives (10). Every prefactor and variable full-Psi value in (10) is finite and nonzero on the regular chart. Alternatively the finite balanced Newton Fourier recurrence proves directly that the final orbit sum is nonzero. Hence every entry of this actual FOUR-LEG Fourier kernel is nonzero. ### A root-independent four-function kernel and its controlled density All internal-root dependence in (10) cancels. In the same retained external logarithms set G=d0-a-X, R_c=exp(Nrho)=s B/A, E=N f_log+(N+1)lambda/2 +[G(b-c+X)+lambda^2/2]/h. Then (10) is the particularly simple exact expression M=kappa zeta_0^2/N *R_c(1-R_c)^2 exp(E) *Psi_+(beta)Psi_+(h-f_log) Psi_+(lambda+2pi*i+h)/Psi_+(rho). (14) To verify it, the powers in (10)--(11) multiply to kappa zeta_0^2/N. Balance gives 1-exp(Nrho)=1-R_c, 1-exp(Nsigma)=R_c, and 1-exp(-Nlambda)=1-R_c. In the exponent use z+tau0=h+b, i sqrt(N)c_b=-(N+1)/2, and beta+lambda=G+2pi*i. The term (2pi*i b)/h=N b cancels the -N b from the boundary prefactor. The remaining exponent is exactly E. No affine mark is removed. For central A,B in a fixed compact subset of A B(B-s A)!=0, with fixed bounded root logarithms, the entire density outside the FOUR full-Psi functions has sharp polynomial size: c_K/N <= |kappa zeta_0^2 R_c(1-R_c)^2 exp(E)/N| <=C_K/N, (15) uniformly for EVERY choice of the four finite labels and every N. Indeed each external logarithm has real part O_K(1/N) and imaginary part O_K(1). X is purely imaginary. Products in E/h therefore have bounded real parts, as do N f_log and (N+1)lambda/2. Also |kappa|=|zeta_0|=1 and R_c,1-R_c are uniformly bounded above and below. This proves (15). Thus the reference kernel has an explicit nonzero original-source local density, with no hidden exponential gauge or periodic normalizer. Its dilogarithmic action is in its four full functions and recorded Gaussian. This is a local normalization theorem; sewing and applying the original global source can still cancel. ### A genuine positive octahedral chart of this ACTUAL kernel The four classical shapes in (14), with their signed orientations, are u=-z1/z0, v=-z6/z7, w=z7/z1, and -(uvw), where the last minus denotes its coefficient in the Bloch sum, not multiplication of its shape by -1. Thus the signed regulator is D(u)+D(v)+D(w)-D(uvw). On the unit-angle chart let 0<theta1,theta2,theta3<pi, pi<theta1+theta2+theta3<2pi, theta4=2pi-theta1-theta2-theta3. Then u=exp(i theta1), v=exp(i theta2), w=exp(i theta3), and the negative fourth tetrahedron has positive quad shape 1/(uvw)=exp(i theta4). These are four positive ideal tetrahedra around an octahedral diagonal, with total angle 2pi. On every compact subset of this chart, the independently proved [full-Psi strip estimate](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md#a-uniform-geometric-phase-on-the-whole-selected-strip) and (15) give the actual kernel a nonzero analytic leading density. Recorded whole-turn shifts contribute their exact nonzero central factors; they are bounded on the stated central compacta. Its leading logarithmic modulus obeys the uniform two-sided estimate log|M|=N V(theta)/(2pi)-log N+O_K(1), (15a) with V equal to the volume of those four positive tetrahedra and theta the sampled angles in that compact chamber. The O(1/N) root-modulus and half-step changes alter the logarithm by O_K(1). This is a statement about the literal original finite Fourier kernel, not a newly chosen packet. The volume is strictly concave on this convex angle chamber. Indeed for L(theta)=D(exp(i theta)), L''(theta)=-cot(theta/2)/2, and Hess V=-diag(cot(theta_i/2))/2 +cot((theta1+theta2+theta3)/2) 11^t/2. Both terms are negative definite or negative semidefinite here, with the first strictly negative. Its unique maximum is theta1=theta2=theta3=theta4=pi/2, the regular octahedron. The existence of this local chart does not place the complete global geometric critical point on its sewn original source. ## 5. An exact original E-current eliminates every possible alias The degree +N allowance in Section 2 can be removed. Retain the original complete scaled head current and coproduct Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, Ecal|0>=0, K|a>=x Q^(-a)|a>, E_total=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2. (16) The actual R_+ commutes with E_total. In the finite Fourier frame, put (Tf)(z)=f(Qz). Then EXACTLY, for every nonzero frame radius, Ecal=z^(-1)(T^(-1)-I), K=x T^(-1). There is no missing wrap: the coefficient of the input constant in the first expression is zero, and all other powers lower without crossing the finite top. Use z0,z1,z6,z7 for the four grid values, and let M denote (14). Its exact one-step full-Psi identities give the ratios R1=M(z6/Q,z7/Q)/M =-z6/z0 *(1-z7/z1)/(1-z6/(Qz0)), R2=M(z6,z7/Q)/M =q z6/z7 *(1-z7/z1)/(1-Qx z6/z7), M(z0 Q,z1 Q)/M=R1, R4=M(z0,z1 Q)/M =q z1/z0 *(1-z7/z1)/(1-z1/(xz0)). (17) All untouched arguments in each ratio are held fixed. Their denominators are nonzero on the regular central chart. Here q=-1/x and Q=x^(-2). Substituting (17) proves the rational identity x/z6*(R1-R2)+(R2-1)/z7 =x/z0*(Q^(-1)R1-R4)+(Q^(-1)R4-1)/z1. (18) This is precisely the matrix relation E_total,out M=M E_total,in. The factors Q^(-1) on the right come from transposing the finite input difference: z_j^(-1) at its shifted row becomes Q^(-1)z_input^(-1). Thus (18) is the original quantum-group current, not merely its commuting symbol. Decoding the four finite frames proves [Rhat_+,E_total]=0. For completeness, (17) can be checked without an operator claim. Under logarithmic shifts (delta a,delta b,delta c,delta d0) =h(Ai,Bi,Ci,Di), put dl=Di-Bi, dG=Di-Ai, dJ=Bi-Ci. The Gaussian in (14) has ratio x^(-dl) exp[dG(b-c+X)+dJ(d0-a-X)+dl lambda] *Q^(dG*dJ+dl^2/2). Apply Psi(z+h)=Psi(z)/(1-exp z) and its inverse to the four full functions. For the four shifts in (17) the displayed ratios result directly. Equation (18) is then an elementary rational identity; cross-multiplication uses only Qx^2=1. Finally E_total is INJECTIVE on each physical total-degree subspace t>=N. Its inputs have first index a=t-d,...,d, all positive. The first output (t-d-1,d) sees only the leftmost input, with nonzero coefficient (Q^(-(t-d))-1)K_d. Remove it and continue: the bidiagonal matrix forces every remaining input coefficient to vanish. Let Delta=Rhat_+-R_+. It has degree +N by Section 2 and commutes with E_total. On input degree zero, E_total Delta=0; injectivity at degree N implies Delta=0 there. Induct on input degree j: Delta E_total=0 follows from the preceding degree, hence E_total Delta=0, and injectivity at j+N implies Delta=0. At j>=N-1 the target degree exceeds 2d and Delta already vanishes. This proves Rhat_+=R_+ for EVERY level, including N=2, composite and even levels. ## 6. Signed words, adapters, source, and scope The negative block is obtained by the exact complete-color antiunitary mirror R_-=P overline(R_+)P, with its original Cartan factor and all frames/marks transported. Applying the same mirror to (5) gives the EXACT original negative operator. This does not balance the raw negative continuous Gaussian at a fixed value of its integration variable; that shortcut would be false. The literal inverse of (5) is consequently the original negative crossing as well. Independent frames at consecutive gates must be joined by their EXACT finite change of frame. On one shared head it is F(r')F(r)^(-1)_(j,k) =(1/N)sum_(a=0)^d (r'/r)^a Q^((j-k)a) =[1-C]/[N(1-(r'/r)Q^(j-k))], C=(r'/r)^N, (13) with its removable finite-sum values. If the central values and their fixed logarithmic marks stay in a compact nonzero set, r=exp(Log A/N), these frames and their inverses have uniformly bounded norms. The same holds for (13). All original cups/caps, pivots and scalar lines are transformed by those same frames. Their polynomial norms at the complete color remain polynomial. No matching of independent central values is required. In fact forcing direct same-grid closure on a one-component braid drives this local regular chart to t0=infinity; the adapters in (13) are what avoid that artificial restriction. Their off-diagonal tails are generally O(1/N), not exponentially small, and are part of the retained global gluing and co-source. After inserting these adapters, decoding the whole finite network recovers the EXACT original physical word, by Section 5. This retains arbitrary inserted original currents and coupons when they are transformed by the same finite frames. The global construction and its source are recorded in [the regular balanced word theorem](regular_balanced_fermat_word_source.md). This theorem resolves the local circle/current normalization by an actual finite polarization. It supplies a nonzero local Fourier kernel with the original closed scalar retained. Global selected geometric survival, source-angle bounds, and dominance still require control of the sewn finite Fourier sum and the retained adapters. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.py) checks independent original crossing matrices, exact finite-index folding, both signs, full original word/cap sources, the central balances, and the full-Psi/Fourier scalar at independent complex grid points.

title: Octahedral belt stacks and their marked outer collars
text: # Octahedral belt stacks and their marked outer collars 29 October 2026. There is an infinite family of actual augmented link diagrams, with unbounded numbers of complete crossing circles, whose original Kashaev volume limits follow from the complete-circle source packet. The balanced case has a direct positive nodal-energy proof; the general case uses its coherent complex Gaussian. The operation is CYCLIC stacking along one actual twice-punctured crossing disk. It is not branching scalar Frobenius multiplication. The source, the cut collars, and their complete metric are specified below. The later coherent boundary-packet theorem removes the balance restriction and allows every FIXED integer outer crossing power. Section 3a gives the literal collar certificate for this extension; section 4a links its original-source asymptotic. The filename retains the earlier balanced checkpoint, which remains the elementary positive special case. ## 1. The two typed pieces, before evaluating any invariant Let C be the literal auxiliary tangle [2,1,1,2] with its third top/bottom endpoints joined on the right. Its two physical input and two physical output ports stay open. It evaluates to L_N, with the original ordinary pivot and no extra trace denominator. Let X_+ and X_- be the original single checked crossings. Use the genuine quarter-turn F, with the duality adapters of [the physical turn theorem](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md). The positive piece D_+ is the two-strand tangle D_+ = F(X_+ C) X_- . (1) It is obtained by opening the OUTER auxiliary circle of the verified [two-octahedron source](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md). Its other auxiliary circle remains closed. Its two disk-side boundary collars are the two standard twice-punctured disks used to stack two-strand tangles. Define D_- as the mirror of D_+, followed by the 180-degree rotation reversing its input/output direction. This is a definition of an actual diagram, not a polynomial selected from an invariant. The rotation carries its two physical punctures and the belt-boundary collar along with it. The mirror of C is the negative crossing word [-2,-1,-1,-2], not a convention that silently keeps all four crossings positive. There is a direct unoriented/typed identification with the same crossing circle: draw its disk horizontally in D^2 times I around the two vertical physical strands. Reflection in the vertical plane containing those strands fixes the disk and its boundary AS SETS, and reverses the auxiliary boundary orientation. There is no curl or self-framing change. The reversed auxiliary is its genuine dual. For the complete balanced color its actual self-duality matrix is U_(a,b)=x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), U=p/N, U unitary. Use the original dual cup/cap to identify that reversed closed leg; the two inverse U adapters and their original scalar normalizations cancel on the CLOSED auxiliary. Its pivotal factor is transported by this duality, not replaced by hand while leaving the crossings unchanged. No main-head conjugation remains. Hence the actual closed negative word has the same all-input operator L_N. This is the round crossing-disk reflection with its typed duality, not an inference solely from the real polynomial L_N. The focused audit also closes the negative universal-R word with the literal original pivot and checks its full matrix at five levels. Here is the all-port source reading. Write z=F(R^-1 L_N), so z#=F(R L_N). The operator/source of the two pieces is EXACTLY f_+ = z# R^-1, f_- = R z. (2) For f_+ this is the literal word (1), read in the source's product order. For f_-, reflection sends R to R^-1, L_N to L_N, and F to the same real unscaled turn. It first gives z R. Input/output reversal is the genuine 180-degree rotation: it REVERSES the stacking order and acts on each Hopf box by F^2. The full physical turn theorem proves F^2 h=h on the complete pair algebra, so it gives Rz. This argument retains all cups, caps, Cartan phases and Casimir normal coefficients. It does not derive the reflected port reading by first commuting two scalar polynomials. The full original matrix audit separately checks the rotations and (2). For any fixed word epsilon=(epsilon_1,...,epsilon_n), epsilon_i in {+,-}, stack these ACTUAL pieces in that order, retain ONE outer auxiliary circle C around their two physical strands, and take the original denominator/marked closure. Call this link L_epsilon. There is one inner circle per piece and one outer belt. Removing the circles leaves a stack of two-strand full twists: D_+ becomes X_-^2 and D_- becomes X_+^2. Its permutation is the identity. Consequently L_epsilon has n+3 components: two main components, n inner circles and one outer belt. No component identification is being inferred from an invariant value. ## 2. The literal disk cut and the geometric pieces Use the labeled cut certificate of the two-octahedron base. Its two regular octahedra P_+,P_- have opposite labeled orientations and opposite vertex pairs {X0,X1}, {Y+,Y-}, {Z+,Z-}. The OUTER disk has shaded triangles A=(X0,Y+,Z+), B=(X0,Y-,Z-). The other disk has C=(X1,Y+,Z-) and D=(X1,Y-,Z+). The original white identity face gluings join A+ to A- along all THREE edges. They similarly join B+ to B-. Thus S_A=A+ union A-, S_B=B+ union B- (3) are the two actual thrice-punctured sphere boundaries after cutting the outer disk. The original outer A-to-B shaded pairings are the only face identifications removed by this cut. The inner C-to-D pairings remain. The resulting piece is connected and contains exactly two complete regular octahedra. These pants are TOTALLY GEODESIC, not just intrinsically ideal triangulated surfaces. Every shaded face meets an adjacent white face at pi/2. Reflection in that white face therefore continues the shaded plane to itself. Across each of the three edges in (3) the two shaded triangles develop into a single plane. The metric on (3) is the complete ideal two-triangle pants metric. This is the geometric reading of the actual collar opening used in (1): a twice-punctured crossing disk has three ideal boundary ends, namely its outer belt and its two physical punctures. Its two sides are S_A,S_B with these same three labeled ends. Restoring the collars is the inverse of the base's proved disk cut. Therefore stacking the open diagram pieces joins an output copy of these pants to the input copy of the next piece. After the last piece, the single remaining outer circle closes this stack in a cycle. No additional complete circle is inserted at an intermediate seam. The reflected/reversed piece has the same geometric certificate. On its cut octahedra, reflection exchanges P_+ and P_-. The input/ output reversal exchanges Y+ with Y- and Z+ with Z-, fixing X0,X1. This interchanges A and B, C and D, and the corresponding white faces. This is exactly the collar reversal in the diagram definition of D_-. It is an octahedral symmetry on the vertex labels, and preserves the three actual boundary-end labels after transporting them with the piece. Thus its geometric boundaries are precisely those used by the source reading (2). ## 3. Complete hyperbolic metric after an arbitrary fixed stack Glue these geometric pieces by the actual cyclic collar maps. A three-puncture bijection is an isometry of the ideal two-triangle pants. In the present labeled construction it can be checked directly: the corresponding map of a shaded triangle extends to an octahedral symmetry. In normalized hyperboloid coordinates the ideal vertices are (1,+/-e1),(1,+/-e2),(1,+/-e3). The symmetry sends these light vectors EXACTLY, not merely their rays. Therefore it preserves the canonical horospheres and the two-triangle cusp sections. The same holds for the reflected/reversed collar maps above. Each seam joins two geodesic boundary half-neighborhoods by an isometry, giving an ordinary smooth hyperbolic neighborhood. In the regular-cell certificate each boundary edge has angle pi on its side, so the joined angle is exactly 2pi. There is no edge cone angle or undetermined axis dilation. Matched canonical horospheres give Euclidean torus cusp sections of the actual diagram; shrinking them gives disjoint sections. There are finitely many cells and the remaining truncated core is compact. Thus every end contains a full horoball cusp and the glued finite-volume metric is complete. This proves, for every fixed word epsilon of length n>=1, that the ACTUAL complement of L_epsilon is hyperbolic and Vol(S^3 minus L_epsilon)=2n v8. (4) The topology is obtained by reversing the literal disk/collar cuts, not by recognizing a census triangulation or matching a numerical volume. For all plus signs this is also the explicit cyclic cover obtained by taking n copies of the cut base and shifting the two outer A-to-B face pairings by one sheet. The metric proof does not need to identify mixed words with that particular peripheral cover. ### 3a. Any fixed integer outer crossing power Let L_(epsilon,a) be the same literal stack, but insert X^a in the OUTER disk collar between the retained C and the first piece. Here a is any fixed signed integer. Its placement is part of the actual diagram, and its source is phi(L_N R^a product_i f_(epsilon_i)). The belt component is RETAINED; none of its cusps is filled. A single X exchanges the two physical punctures of the standard twice-punctured disk. After passing to its complete ideal pants, this is the isometry that fixes the belt end, exchanges the two physical ends, and EXCHANGES its two ideal triangles. This last exchange is necessary: permuting two vertices in one fixed triangle alone would give the wrong oriented collar map. In the canonical labels of section 2, put the extra power at the last cyclic seam. Its exact face maps are | Parity of a | Source to target | Vertex map | | --- | --- | --- | | even | A_last^+ to B_first^-, A_last^- to B_first^+ | X0 fixed, Y+ to Y-, Z+ to Z- | | odd | A_last^+ to B_first^+, A_last^- to B_first^- | X0 fixed, Y+ to Z-, Z+ to Y- | This is obtained by tracing the two punctures through the actual single collar crossing. It is also the usual two-puncture half rotation of the disk. Its square is a full collar twist: as an ideal pants map it is isotopic to the identity, while the rotations at its ends record a change of the BELT PERIPHERAL MARKING. Thus adding two crossings changes that marking without changing the unmarked complete face quotient. Negative a has the same parity description with its opposite recorded twist. No preferred meridian is silently kept fixed while deleting R^a from the quantum source. Every displayed triangle map still extends to an octahedral symmetry preserving the normalized light vectors. In the explicit eight-tet subdivision, a last odd seam toggles the target cell P_+ versus P_- while exchanging Y and Z. These two changes cancel in local coordinates: its gluing permutation remains 0132. All tetrahedra keep their positive shape i, all edge products are one and all edge angles are 2pi. The same canonical cusp sections therefore match, without dilation, at either parity. The two main components of the untwisted stack merge exactly when a is odd: after the circles are removed, the physical two-strand permutation is that of X^(2(n_- - n_+)+a). Here n_+ and n_- count plus and minus pieces. Each of the n inner circles and the single outer belt remains distinct. Consequently components L_(epsilon,a) = n+3 for even a, n+2 for odd a. (4a) The exact cusp links of the modified cell quotient have precisely these counts. They are connected orientable flat tori; for an odd collar the former Y and Z main links become one. The compact-core and matched horoball argument of section 3 applies unchanged. We have proved the ACTUAL geometric statement Vol(S^3 minus L_(epsilon,a))=2n v8 for every fixed n>=1, epsilon and a in Z. (4b) This is a complete augmented exterior with its marked collar, not a Dehn-filled exterior or a volume-continuity assertion. ## 4. Balanced words give the full original volume limit Suppose n=2k and the word has exactly k plus and k minus pieces. By (2), the actual fixed-root source is Phi_epsilon,N = phi(L_N product_i f_(epsilon_i)). (5) The complete two-head Hopf commutant is the FULL algebra C[Omega], including its repeated-root normal directions. Consequently all the f_i commute there, and R^k R^-k cancels in the entire product: product_i f_(epsilon_i)=(z# z)^k. In an adjacent +- pair this is also the direct cancellation of the literal factors X_- X_+; the general reordered formula is a proved all-input source identity, not a claim that every different ordering is isotopic. The retained-belt theorem now gives Phi_epsilon,N=N sum_c m_c |z_N(c)|^(2k)>0, lim_N (2pi/N) log Phi_epsilon,N=4k v8. (6) All N, both parities and all composite levels are included. The [complete-source normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) retains only its original unit framing/component phases (or the single recorded 1/N in the one-cut modified convention); it adds no modified dimension per circle. Combining (4),(6), the literal original reduced Kashaev evaluation satisfies lim_N (2pi/N) log |<L_epsilon>_N| =Vol(S^3 minus L_epsilon)=4k v8. (7) This proves a growing complete augmented LINK family. It does not prove arbitrary long fillings of these new bases, fixed knots, or arbitrary-bridge volume limits. The quantum gluing graph here is a cycle along ONE retained belt; a branched tree requires its actual six-port tensor and cannot be substituted into (5). ### 4a. Coherent source extension to every sign word and outer collar For n_+ plus and n_- minus pieces put n=n_+ + n_->0 and e=n_- - n_+. The full commutant/source calculation, with the actual typed pieces (2), is phi(L_N R^a product_i f_(epsilon_i)) =phi(L_N R^(e+a) (z#)^n_+ z^n_-). (8) There is no absolute value inside this unbalanced channel sum. The [coherent original belt-stack asymptotic](actual_coherent_octahedral_belt_stack_asymptotic.md) proves its nonzero all-N asymptotic from the actual complex complete-circle boundary packet. It retains the full crossing phase, endpoint multiplicities, ordinary pivots and marked source. Its complex Gaussian has coefficient n-i(e+a), whose real part n is positive, so it never vanishes for these fixed integers. In particular lim_N (2pi/N)log|phi(L_N R^(e+a)(z#)^n_+ z^n_-)|=2n v8. (9) Applying the SAME explicit original reduced normalization as above and the geometric collar certificate (4b) gives lim_N (2pi/N)log|<L_(epsilon,a)>_N| =Vol(S^3 minus L_(epsilon,a)) =2n v8. (10) The word, its length n and the signed outer integer a are fixed before N tends to infinity. Both parities and composite levels are included. The balanced positive source in (6) is a special case; the general theorem needs the coherent complex Gaussian and does not follow by taking magnitudes of individual channel terms. Arbitrary fillings of these new bases and genuinely branched multi-belt source graphs remain outside the statement. Coverage only: the abstract of Roland van der Veen's [Proof of the volume conjecture for Whitehead chains](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611181) already states a volume-conjecture theorem for an infinite link family extending the Whitehead link and Borromean rings. The present literal belt stacks may lie in that family; no new literature-family claim is made without an exact clasp/port dictionary. Neither that paper's proof nor its asymptotic formula is an input above. The reusable result established here is the full original-source DCT energy bridge and its specified physical belt seam. The odd outer collar simultaneously exchanges the pants triangles and the physical punctures, giving permutation 0132. Its canonical horospheres, component counts and marked collar use the complete source’s specified kappa square root. The word is fixed and nonempty, and the signed outer twist a is fixed before N tends to infinity. The finite source/cell audit checks both collar parities, all signs and outer powers. Software recognition and finite profiles are supplementary, not premises for the topology or asymptotic theorem. Fillings, branched six-port gluing and literature novelty are not concluded here. Audit: [literal balanced sources and exact cyclic face certificate](../experiments/audit_actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.py). The optional literal-diagram/software comparison is supplemental; the proof is the reversible cut, matched pants collars, and exact regular-cell metric above. Reproducible local commands (no dependency installation): python3 experiments/audit_actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.py .venv/bin/python experiments/audit_actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.py --software-only The first uses NumPy for full original source matrices. The second uses the existing geometry environment, requires no NumPy, and adds only its separately labeled literal-diagram diagnostics.

title: Balanced terminal decorations and volume limits beyond tangle-operation trees
text: # Balanced terminal decorations and volume limits beyond tangle-operation trees A crossing circle surrounds two strands and bounds their twice-punctured disk. A terminal decoration inserts another such two-strand piece in an actual product collar on one side of an original crossing disk. The original diagram may have arbitrary cycles; it is not required to be built from a tree of two-strand products. The starting condition is combinatorial: the actual connected augmented diagram has a simple triangulated white sphere, with its recorded crossing-disk matching and cyclic orders. The proof constructs its positive right-angled geometry, then adds the terminal pieces so that one shared complete circle packing controls every sector of the original quantum source. All data are fixed before the level tends to infinity. ## 1. The theorem and its quantifiers Let \(D\) be a fixed connected augmented link diagram with the following data. * Its white triangulation is a simple triangulated sphere, with the original perfect matching of dual triangles and four distinct white vertices at each matched quadrilateral. * Its simple white sphere has at least four vertices; the positive geometric certificate is constructed below, not imposed separately. * A strand edge, meaning a nonmatching side in the white triangulation and called MAIN in the source formulas, is marked. The associated two protected white curvatures are zero in the actual marked complete packing. * The cyclic order, original half-twist frame and disk-framed meridian/longitude at every crossing circle are fixed. * A parity vector for the original boxes makes their filled main strands a knot, with no internally closed extra component. There is a finite literal terminal decoration \(\widehat D\) of this diagram with even numbers of new terminal pieces on both sides of each original box such that: 1. The original endpoint pairing and knot condition are preserved when each new terminal power is odd. 2. The refined white sphere is simple, has its actual positive cut certificate, and its one marked complete packing satisfies the strict complete-radius balance inequalities at every old and new crossing circle. 3. There is a threshold \(T(\widehat D)\) such that, for every fixed integer filling vector \(p\) with all \(|p_e|\ge T(\widehat D)\), independently in sign and size, and the recorded retained half twists \(\epsilon_e\in\{-1,0,1\}\), the actual powers \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\) produce a hyperbolic knot \(K_p\) and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K_p)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_p). \tag{T1} \] Here \(K_N\) is the original zero-framed reduced complete-color invariant at \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), with its recorded enhanced component convention.
