Local holomorphic regularization and preservation of its side currents remain valid. Nor is gamma an excess over the figure-eight volume rate: it is the single regular-tetrahedron rate. A sharp whole-knot bound still requires control after the exterior pairing, or a contour argument separating that saddle from the collision collar. No positive geometric intersection or knot-volume asymptotic is proved here. Reproducible finite/source and saddle checks: [audit script](../experiments/audit_actual_beta_collision_normal_jet.py).

title: The original beta current is a geometric extension, not a degenerate sector
text: # The original beta current is a geometric extension, not a degenerate sector 28 October 2026. The retained current has an exact triangular connection. Its power-series symbol is rational, but its logarithmic continuation can carry the SAME nondegenerate geometric full-Psi block as the residue. Thus a current in a full knot expansion cannot be declared geometrically degenerate from its local leading symbol alone. The complete original source is the invariant section of a rank-two extension. All identities below use the original polynomial B_N and the exact source cycle in [the beta-source theorem](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md), with the [proved normalizer](actual_trivalent_beta_normalizer.md). They do not introduce a different positive invariant or inserted coupon. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy_results.json) check the commuting source-preserving matrices, seven normal-jet orders, nine actual full-Psi deck laws, eighteen Ward laws and six differential identities. The all-level proofs below do not infer their claims from those finite checks. ## 1. The exact extended state Put h=2*pi*i/N, Q=exp h, u=exp l, v=exp(l+c). Initially take -pi<Im l<0, 0<Im c<pi. The original state and source are B_N(u,v)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) product_(j<a)(u-Q^jv), U=u^N, V=v^N, A=U-V, D=1-A, S_N(l,c)=(N/phi_N) exp(Nl-cl/h) Psi_+(c)Psi_+(h-l), B_N=S_N+D I_N. (1) I_N is the UPWARD Barnes line of the cited theorem, including its actual source residues. It is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on compact subsets of this initial positive boundary chamber, including the matched D=0 locus. Formula (1) defines its actual continuation elsewhere with the transported logarithmic marks. Apparent divisions by D below are always removable in this initial matched chamber; they must not be inverted separately on every continued branch. ## 2. Exact inhomogeneous Ward system The two original finite recurrences and exact Psi steps give S_N(l,c)=(u-v) S_N(l,c+h), I_N(l,c)=(u-v) I_N(l,c+h)+1, (2) v S_N(l+h,c)=(u-1) S_N(l,c), v I_N(l+h,c)=(u-1) I_N(l,c)+1. (3) The equations are literal on a common convergence chamber, and hold under continuation with its residue currents. They do not permit shifting a bare Barnes line across poles without those currents. Combining them, the u-only root shift is v S_N(Qu,v)=(u-1)(Qu-v)S_N(u,v), v I_N(Qu,v)=(u-1)(Qu-v)I_N(u,v)+Qu. (4) The +1 and +Qu are fixed original endpoint sources, not unspecified knot periods. The central D is invariant under each root shift. There is also an exact differential connection. Write p(Z)=d_Z Log Psi_+(Z), a meromorphic function explicitly given in the original full-Psi source note. Put q_c=-l/h+p(c), q_l=N-c/h-p(h-l). Then d_c S_N=q_c S_N, d_l S_N=q_l S_N. Differentiating the original invariant (1) gives the safe cross-multiplied form D d_c I_N+NV I_N=d_c B_N-q_c S_N, D d_l I_N-NA I_N=d_l B_N-q_l S_N. (5) No localization at a vanishing D is needed. Off that divisor, let J_N=B_N/D. The entire connection is equivalently d(I_N-J_N)=d Log(S_N/D) * (I_N-J_N). (6) Thus the inhomogeneous source is explicit and rational in the marked root coordinates u,v (not only their central powers U,V); its homogeneous line is precisely the original geometric full-Psi line. The connection is flat, since d_l q_c=d_c q_l=-1/h. This calculation does not classify its nonperturbative sectors from a formal asymptotic series. ## 3. Both boundary deck generators and their commutator Let T=2*pi*i. Under a v-only logarithmic deck turn c->c+T, the full-Psi monodromy and the Gaussian in (1) give exactly S_v=S/A, I_v=I-S/A. (7) For the simultaneous u,v deck turn l->l+T, c fixed, they give S_s=(U-1)S/V, I_s=I+S/V. (8) Therefore a u-only turn l->l+T,c->c-T gives S_u=A(U-1)S/V, I_u=I+U S/V. (9) These are meromorphic connection formulas with the full central factors retained. They are first established away from their displayed divisors, then interpreted by the matched total source. For example A=0 can make the individual continued terms singular although the polynomial B_N remains regular. For the column (S,I)^t, the v and simultaneous matrices are M_v=[[1/A,0],[-1/A,1]], M_s=[[(U-1)/V,0],[1/V,1]], M_u=[[A(U-1)/V,0],[U/V,1]]. (10) They obey M_v M_s=M_s M_v and M_u=M_s M_v^(-1). Thus both boundary deck generators commute, with their actual extension cocycle; there is no untracked central commutator. Direct multiplication shows [1,D]M_v=[1,D]M_s=[1,D]M_u=[1,D]. (11) The literal original source B_N=S+D I is their invariant section. On the balanced locus A=1, all three diagonals are one and their nonidentity parts square to zero. This is a genuine unipotent rank-two extension, not a claim of nilpotence of the full knot transport group. Generically the same extension also has nontrivial multiplicative norm characters; those characters cannot be discarded. More generally an arbitrary v deck of order m and simultaneous deck of order n have the exact solved transport mu=A^(-m)[(U-1)/V]^n, S' =mu S, I'=I+[(1-mu)/D]S. (12) Since mu=1 on D=0, the quotient is regular there and tends to -m+n/V. For the normal-jet ring modulo D^(p+1), write M=Id+L. Then L^k=(mu-1)^(k-1)L and therefore L^(p+2)=0. Every fixed normal jet has finite unipotent transport, with the full all-winding answer already given by (12). For an individual v deck the index p+2 is attained. This statement concerns the proved local deck connection, not every change of charts in a knot triangulation. Away from D=0 the gauge (S,I)->(S,B=S+D I) diagonalizes these matrices. Its determinant is D. Thus this splitting is invalid on the balanced source divisor itself; it cannot be used to discard the nontrivial unipotent extension or its normal derivatives. The geometric line span(S) is preserved, but the decomposition into an invariant original source and a current is not preserved as two independent scalar sectors. This is the precise failure of a proposed global proof that excludes every current term before its continuation. ## 4. A regular growing geometric sector inside a continued current Consider a compact original gap family with |u|<|v| and Lambda(u,v)>max(0,log|u|,log|v|), where Lambda is the exact residue rate in the normalizer theorem. Such genuine positive bipyramid families exist near |v|=1 and lower u with |u|<1. The principal current is O(1), whereas S grows with its specified full-Psi geometric phase. On this chamber 1/A=-v^(-N)[1+O((|u|/|v|)^N)]. Equation (7) therefore gives I_v=I+v^(-N)S[1+O((|u|/|v|)^N)]. (13) Since Lambda-log|v|>0, the continued current has a nonzero growing geometric sector. Its added phase differs from S only by the integer logarithmic mark -2*pi*i Log v. Their exponentiated canonical relations are the SAME and the geometric shapes remain regular. This conclusion uses an exact current connection and a checked rate gap; it is not inferred merely from a nonzero local density. An especially transparent fixed-center example is u=-i,v=1 along N=4m+1. Then A=-1-i stays nonzero and the principal I is bounded, while the current after the v deck has exponential rate lim_(m->infinity) (2*pi/N)log|I_v(-i,1)|=2D(i)>0. (14) The underlying positive bipyramid has p=q=2+i, H=1-2i and two outputs i,i. All five signed shapes are strictly nondegenerate. The source and all physical centers are unchanged by the logarithmic turn; B_N is exactly invariant by (11). This is a local original-source countercheck to automatic geometric degeneracy of retained currents. It is NOT a counterexample to a global knot volume statement, nor a claim that a particular full knot cycle must perform this deck turn. ## 5. Exponentially small geometry is also present in the current extension There is a second exact description in the open contraction chamber |u|+|v|<1. Its infinite Newton series H_N(u,v)=sum_(a>=0) product_(j<a)(u-Q^jv) converges absolutely and normally. The integer relation P_(a+N)=A P_a shows H_N=B_N/(1-A)=B_N/D, I_N=H_N-S_N/D. (15) No tail or boundary source has been omitted. The single-valued analytic series H_N stays fixed; the full-Psi block produces precisely the current deck jumps (7)--(9). For u=-4i/5,v=1/100 from the positive-bipyramid example in the beta-source theorem, the exact residue rate is strictly negative: Lambda=[ImLi_2(i/80)+ImLi_2(4i/5)]/(2*pi) +(1/4)log(1/125)<0. The imaginary dilogarithms are each less than their positive imaginary arguments; this bounds their sum by 65/80, while the logarithm is strictly negative by a fixed larger margin. Thus the full current contains the explicitly specified exponentially small term -S_N/D in (15). Its rational power-series symbol cannot determine this sector or its deck continuation. The source identity, rather than a chosen formal series, is needed for exterior composition. This is a specified exact source decomposition, not a claim that H_N itself has no further exponentially small components or that a unique transseries convention has been proved for it. ### The principal normalization symbol to every power On every compact subset of the initial positive boundary chamber, the actual current has an asymptotic expansion to every fixed order I_N(u,v)=sum_(k=0)^K h^k R_k(u,v)+O_K(h^(K+1)), R_0=1/(1-u+v), R_k=(u-v)/(1-u+v) sum_(j=1)^k (v*d_v)^j R_(k-j)/j!. (15a) All coefficients are rational, with poles ONLY on 1-u+v=0 and pole order at most 2k+1. The first correction is the one already independently derived in the beta theorem. Equation (15a) follows formally from the exact inhomogeneous Ward equation (2); the actual uniform remainder requires the contour estimate as well. Here are details supplying that estimate to every fixed order. The full-Psi logarithm has a complete fixed-order expansion on compact subsets of its selected strip. In a left-half-plane anchor this is proved directly: its noncentral logarithmic Fourier coefficient is -exp(nZ)/[n(1-Q^n)], N not dividing n. For n below a fixed small multiple of N, expand 1/(exp(hn)-1) to the required Bernoulli order. The remainder is bounded by a fixed power of |hn|, whose sum against exp(n Re Z) is convergent. The remaining modes and the explicit central logarithmic terms are exponentially small. To continue to an arbitrary compact selected-strip set, use the EXACT finite derivative formula sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)g_Z(ell/N) in equation (7b) of the full-Psi source note. Its g_Z is holomorphic on a common neighborhood of [0,1]. Euler--Maclaurin to any fixed order has a uniform remainder there; integrate it from the already normalized anchor. Cauchy estimates give the same derivative bounds. This proves the needed full-Psi expansion with its actual normalization, not a formal periodic replacement. In the Barnes integral, cut |Im a| at C log N, choosing C sufficiently large for the requested order. The already proved strict exponential tails make the omitted part smaller than that order. On the retained part the expansion of the ratio at c and c+ha has polynomial coefficients in a and a uniformly bounded remainder times a fixed power of 1+|a|. Taylor's formula and the exponential contour majorant then permit termwise integration with an O(h^(K+1)) remainder. Each coefficient is an ordinary Barnes moment of (u-v)^a, hence a rational derivative of 1/(1-u+v). Uniqueness of the recursion identifies it with (15a). Differentiation in u,v is uniform on smaller compact sets by holomorphy. There is a precise formal bubble geometry: on 1-u+v=0 the two shape arguments are x=v/u=1-y, y=1/u, and D(x)+D(y)=0. (15b) This justifies calling the FORMAL rational current a normalization or bubble channel in this chart. It does not classify the exact current: (7)--(15) display its additional geometric continuation and exponentially small sectors. In particular a formal pole calculation cannot replace the rank-two source connection. ## 6. What this settles for the next global step The normalization-current symbol and exact Ward equations are now available for whole-word composition. A global proof may use the invariant rank-two extension and its matched currents, or prove that its particular physical cycle avoids specified deck transfers. It cannot prove the needed gap by declaring every current sector a degenerate representation: (13)--(14) would contradict that assertion. The remaining geometric question is about the ACTUAL joint original cycle, its permitted branch transport, and the exterior stationary equations. None of the local identities above supplies a global geometric quotient or forces its coefficient to be nonzero. ## 7. Why killing the current is not a source-preserving deck quotient There is a concrete algebraic obstruction, stronger than observing a continued current with a large rate. Work over a ring R of single-valued meromorphic boundary functions on a regular marked chart, with A and D units. The logarithmic deck transformations fix R. Use the ACTUAL source presentation with generators S,I and its pointing B=S+D I. This is meromorphic deck descent data, not a claim that its variable coefficient matrices are constant monodromy matrices of a complex local system. Put J=D I. Equation (7) gives T_v(S)=S/A, T_v(J)=J-(D/A)S. (16) Let pi be an R-linear quotient whose kernel is stable under this actual deck transport. If pi kills the current J, it also kills T_v(J)-J. Since D/A is a unit, it follows that pi(S)=0, pi(B)=0. (17) Thus a nonzero invariant geometric quotient cannot be constructed by simply quotienting out this current. This uses the original polynomial pointing and its exact full-Psi deck law; no arbitrary replacement period or unknown knot scalar is introduced. Without inverting D, the same calculation forces D pi(S)=0. Hence a D-torsion-free quotient still kills S and B. A quotient supported on the balanced divisor, its derived normal source, or a comparison which is not deck-equivariant is a different object. The normal jets of Section 3 must not be discarded to identify those alternatives. The quotient here is taken over the REMAINING boundary variables before their period pushforward. A final exterior integral is not R-linear in a variable which it integrates. Hence (17) does not say that a particular integrated current can never vanish while a geometric integral survives. It excludes setting the current KERNEL to zero in a pointwise, deck-compatible comparison; nonlocal cycle cancellation after the exterior integration is a separate question. There is no assertion here that every local v turn is an allowed independent deck transformation after all boundary variables have been coupled. That is checked by the actual monomial boundary map. The following coupled version makes the required check explicit. ## 8. Disjoint original sink fibers and their coupled descent presentation In the original reduced atomic graph, an eligible beta sink has three incident atoms, all pointing into it before factorial reflection: one reciprocal factorial, one positive Euler transfer, and one positive factorial. Its finite coefficient contraction is exactly B_N from (1). Two such sinks cannot share an atom: an oriented incidence column has only one positive entry. Since neither sink is an original boundary cap vertex, no cup/cap factor has been removed by this observation. Consequently a family of s eligible sinks can be contracted simultaneously at the finite-coefficient level. The local result is the product of their B_N kernels with the SAME remaining original boundary functional. The sums are finite, so no contour interchange or independent-sector convergence is assumed for that identity. Its expansion into S_i+D_i I_i is pointwise exact on their common marked boundary chart. The exact u=Q^2U,v=QV tags and reflected NQ^d source factors are those of the beta-source theorem; each stays in its specified kernel or exterior density, according to that representation. None is reset. Eligibility matters: an original U/u/F sink is not the U/v/F beta kernel. BEFORE exact Gaussian absorption, the strict nine-atom crossing has the proved star {0,1,3} for either sign and additionally {2,4,6} for a negative crossing. The final raw star {5,7,8} contains a u transfer. For a positive crossing, however, the original finite Gaussian and its adjacent reciprocal diagonal combine EXACTLY by d_a/F_a=p_a*x^(-2a). Slot 5 is thereby a V diagonal, and {5,7,8} becomes a second genuine beta star, disjoint from {0,1,3}. This is an identity of the COMPLETE original finite Gaussian operator, not a pointwise removal at fixed continuous Gaussian variable. Thus each sign has two simultaneous eligible beta stars after this exact preprocessing, with the remaining adapters retained. Their literal whole-word monomials and Gaussian grouping belong to the original crossing assembly; they cannot be guessed from only the local shape relations. For each selected beta sink form its rank-two presented descent module M_i with the matrices of Section 3. Pull these modules back by the ACTUAL boundary monomials in the remaining head/Gaussian variables, and tensor them: M_presented=tensor_(i=1)^s M_i, b=tensor_(i=1)^s(S_i+D_i I_i). (18) This has a rank-2^s presentation. Its evaluation into actual functions may have further relations after boundary coupling; faithfulness is not inferred. Its pointing evaluates to the original product of finite B_N kernels. It has not been defined from the final knot value. The first guaranteed sink gives a literal check on this pullback. Label the single-crossing boundary/head coordinates as in the original nine-atom graph, with the sink z_2 and its neighbors z_0,z_1,z_4. Its reciprocal leg, positive Euler leg and positive factorial give the finite coefficient product (z_2/z_1)^i/F_i, p_j(x^(-1)z_2/z_0)^j, F_a(z_4/z_2)^a. The z_2 constant coefficient forces a=i+j and is exactly B_N(u_0,v_0), u_0=z_4/z_1, v_0=x^(-1)z_4/z_0. (18a) Thus a local z_0 logarithmic turn has a=0,b=-1 in the notation below, and its beta character is A_0=u_0^N-v_0^N, generically different from one. The nontrivial individual characters in (20) therefore occur in an ACTUAL crossing boundary map. In a whole word that head can also enter other sinks or source factors; all their pulled-back transformations must be composed. Equation (18a) does not assert that the local v turn is independent of those changes. For a particular head logarithmic turn, let the actual boundary map shift Log u_i by 2pi*i*a_i and Log v_i by 2pi*i*b_i. In (12) this means n=a_i and m=b_i-a_i. Thus each beta factor has its explicit character mu_i and current coefficient from that formula. Tensor the corresponding matrices. They preserve (18), and their geometric/current sectors mix by these specified coefficients. Untouched full-Psi factors, Gaussian and peripheral/source lines must carry their OWN descent factors as well; no conclusion about the full graph character follows from the beta factors alone. One useful falsification criterion applies directly to this coupled presentation. Localize where every D_i and mu_i is a unit, and put J_i=D_i I_i. Suppose a deck-stable quotient kills EVERY tensor sector containing at least one J_i. Under an allowed head turn, S_i -> mu_i S_i, J_i -> J_i+(1-mu_i)S_i. (19) Apply the turn to the sector with precisely its ith factor J_i and all other factors S_j. Modulo the killed sectors its image is (1-mu_i) product_(j!=i)mu_j * product_j S_j. (20) If any such 1-mu_i is a unit, the quotient kills the entire geometric product and therefore the original pointing b. It is not enough that the PRODUCT of the mu_i equals one: individual current sectors still mix into that product by (20). If all relevant characters are one, or one restricts to their fixed-character divisors, this obstruction alone decides nothing; the retained normal jets and exterior source still have to be computed. Equations (18)--(20) specify a source-preserving composition object and a check against an invalid quotient. They do not make the individual sector integrals single-valued on the original head torus. On overlapping logarithmic charts the FULL tensor descent data, and the matched source seams, are compulsory. Nor does the nonzero meromorphic product of local residues imply that its FINAL exterior period is nonzero. That remaining pairing is precisely what a global geometric coefficient theorem must control.

title: Polynomial-cost sublevel cycles for arbitrarily wide blockwise source cores
text: # Polynomial-cost sublevel cycles for arbitrarily wide blockwise source cores 28 October 2026. There is a constructive higher-anchor case of the missing mass theorem. Articulation points split the original coefficient, master, and torus by an explicit unimodular monomial change of variables. If every remaining biconnected block is either a two-anchor block or a balanced unit-factor block, the resulting product cycle has polynomial logarithmic mass. No semialgebraic triangulation or bound on an integer boundary-matrix inverse is assumed. The anchor count is arbitrary but fixed. This does not cover an unbalanced biconnected block with three or more anchors, does not sum the original clocks, and proves no new knot volume theorem. ## 1. Same original source and the exact articulation split Use the strict-Hall master and source of [the radial transport theorem](actual_anchor_sublevel_radial_transport.md): f=P/product_v X_v^(q_v), P=gamma product_e(alpha_e X_(u_e)-beta_e X_(v_e)), |alpha_e|=|beta_e|=1, sum_v q_v=M. Original extracted scalars remain in gamma. Parallel factors are retained with their multiplicities; their underlying simple graph determines the articulation points. Zero loops and forced cuts have already been treated by the exact source identities, not removed by an absolute estimate. Suppose v is an articulation point, and C_1,...,C_s are the components after deleting v. Put V_a=C_a union {v}, let P_a contain exactly the factors on V_a, and let M_a=degree P_a. Assign the component charges q_u^(a)=q_u, u in C_a, q_v^(a)=M_a-sum_(u in C_a)q_u. (1) Their sums are M_a, and sum_a q_v^(a)=q_v. These are FORCED charges: homogeneity makes every coefficient in the exterior C_a require exactly the displayed remaining power of X_v. Thus [product_v X_v^(q_v)]P =gamma product_a [product_(u in V_a)X_u^(q_u^(a))]P_a, (2) where gamma is allocated once, or equivalently kept outside every scalar-free factor on the right. There is no summation over articulation charges and no unknown source normalization. The same factorization holds before integration. Choose X_v=1 as the common gauge, and use Y_(a,u)=X_u/X_v for u in C_a. Then T=(C*)^V/C* ~= product_a ((C*)^(V_a)/C*), f=gamma product_a f_a. (3) This is a unimodular monomial isomorphism, so the logarithmic top form and the original torus generator are the product forms and generators, with the common orientation fixed accordingly. Iterating at further articulations gives the biconnected-block factorization. Each factor belongs to exactly one block. Strict Hall is preserved by (1). For a set I not containing v, its internal factors, crossing count and deficit are exactly the original ones. For a local set containing v use its nonempty complement J in C_a and the identity e_I=C_J-e_J. Hence every proper local cut remains strict. In particular q_v^(a)=C_(C_a)-e_(C_a) is a positive integer. ## 2. The regular critical values also split exactly In the independent coordinates (3), dlog f=direct_sum_a dlog f_a. A nonzero point is therefore critical exactly when EACH component is critical. Its value is gamma times the product of their values. Whenever the component regular critical sets are nonempty, Mcrit(f)=|gamma| product_a Mcrit(f_a). (4) All blocks used below have a nonempty regular critical set. This is immediate for balanced blocks by their positive unit-torus maximum. For a two-anchor strict-Hall block, its Laurent map has poles at both ends; its derivative numerator has degree m, and removing a root of multiplicity h from that numerator removes only h-1 copies. Thus at least one derivative zero remains off its zero divisor. The identity (4) does not declare these FIXED-clock critical points to be full knot/Hurwitz critical points. It only gives the exact critical modulus appearing in the present coefficient estimate. ## 3. Balanced blocks require no deformation or integer-chain estimate For a block B with incidence counts S_u and charges q_u, suppose S_u=2q_u for every vertex u of B. (5) On its unit torus every radial derivative of log|f_B| vanishes: this is the exact off-critical identity with equal endpoint radii and delta=0. The nonzero maximum on that compact torus also has all angular derivatives zero. It is consequently a regular complex critical point. Conversely the cut maximum principle forces every regular critical point of a connected balanced block to have equal radii. Therefore Mcrit(f_B)=max_(unit torus)|f_B|. (6) The original unit torus itself lies in the Mcrit sublevel and has normalized logarithmic top-form mass one. There is no positivity or noncancellation inference about its integral: it can vanish. ## 4. Two-anchor blocks have the already proved explicit cycle A two-anchor block with m factors and strict charge 1<=q<=m-1 becomes f_B(z)=gamma_B z^(-q) product_(j=1)^m(z-u_j), |u_j|=1. For every R_B>Mcrit(f_B), the boundary of the component of {|f_B|>R_B} containing the zero pole is a smooth oriented circle. It represents the original generator, lies on |f_B|=R_B, and its normalized logarithmic length tends, as R_B decreases to Mcrit, to at most A_B=4m^2 log(m+1). (7) This is the proved [two-anchor minimax estimate](actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.md). The circle is a selected component of a degree-2m real algebraic lemniscate. Its original pole component, not a favorable saddle, selects it. Repeated or arbitrarily clustered unit roots are permitted. ## 5. Actual polynomial-mass product cycle and its coefficient bound Assume EVERY biconnected block is either two-anchor or satisfies (5). For each balanced block retain its unit torus; for each two-anchor block use the circle above. Their product, followed by the inverse monomial isomorphism (3), is homologous to the original source torus. Its absolute logarithmic top-form mass is exactly the product of the block masses, because the monomial logarithmic determinant is +/-1. For any R>Mcrit(f), choose the finitely many R_B sufficiently close to their Mcrit values that the product supremum is less than R. The constructed product cycle then lies in {|f|<=R}. Its limiting normalized mass is at most the product of the A_B over two-anchor blocks. Hence |I| <=Mcrit(f) product_(two-anchor blocks B) 4m_B^2 log(m_B+1). (8) For fixed original diagram width and block count, m_B=O(N), so the cost is polynomial in N. This bound includes |gamma| through (4). It is not rescaled by the coefficient I or by a guessed regulator period. The cycles also have bounded-complexity algebraic supports. They are products of real algebraic lemniscates and unit tori; the monomial change has degree bounded by the fixed anchor count. Their support degree is polynomial in N. Their logarithmic radius range is O(log N), by the explicit modulus-nonincreasing radial clipping if necessary. On the product cycle the real logarithmic mass is the product of the block lengths/torus masses; the fixed monomial change and clipping multiply it by at most a constant depending on the anchor count. Thus the construction itself supplies the chain complexity which cannot be inferred from a triangulation of a general sublevel set. ## 6. Exact remaining scope This is an arbitrary-width source transport theorem, with a structural condition on its blocks. Exact articulation factorization reduces the general mass problem to UNBALANCED BICONNECTED unit-factor cores with at least three anchors. The statement does not prove that the full original clock source decomposes into the permitted block family. Actual macro-defect sectors can contain the excluded cores. In particular, taking absolute values over clocks after (8) is not a sharp knot upper bound. The critical actions in (4) are conditional, and all factorial weights, feedback phases and original normalization still enter the full source. The missing full-clock support/critical comparison remains in addition to the unbalanced-core mass problem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_blockwise_sublevel_source_transport.py): exact articulation charge and coefficient factorization, strict-Hall preservation, actual source residual cores and wider mixed balanced/tree examples, plus critical splitting and the quantitative coefficient bound.

title: Actual braid transport has a flat Borel-relative algebra and a divided cap period
text: # Actual braid transport has a flat Borel-relative algebra and a divided cap period Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual diagonal quantum Borel action has an explicit free fusion basis. Actual crossing words become matrices over a finite flat algebra, including at the original nilpotent source. The pivotal highest-input cap is an explicit Frobenius functional with its marked density. It is a divided central-F trace on a cyclic chart; bare semisimple reduction loses a nonzero actual period. This supplies an actual word AND source comparison, rather than only an auxiliary source-frame classification. Its target is not identified with a geometric gluing algebra or the A-polynomial. The central-F parameter below is not identified with the meridian or Q-normal. ## 1. The actual Borel algebra and its flat central extension Fix the actual root Q=exp(2 pi i/N), N at least two. On each regular holonomy splitting module retain K_i=x_i diag(Q^(-j)) and the actual F_i with F_i^N=phi_i. We can use the original balanced head frame: its nonwrapping arrow j to j+1 is 1-Q^(j+1), and its wrapping arrow is phi_i/N. This is exactly the factorial gauge of the regular module, not an altered representation. Put \[ H=(K_1\cdots K_b)/(x_1\cdots x_b),\qquad f=\Delta^{b-1}F=\sum_{i=1}^bK_1^{-1}\cdots K_{i-1}^{-1}F_i. \] Actual quantum-group multiplication and the root binomial identity give \[ H^N=1,\qquad Hf=Q^{-1}fH,\qquad f^N=\Phi:=\sum_{i=1}^b(x_1\cdots x_{i-1})^{-N}\phi_i. \tag{1} \] For example for two terms A=F_1,B=K_1 inverse F_2 one has BA=QAB, so all intermediate coefficients of (A+B)^N vanish. Iteration proves (1). Every complete center and meridian factor is retained in Phi. Define the algebra A_Phi by these three relations, with idempotents \[ e_j=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}Q^{ja}H^a,\quad z_{a,j}=f^a e_j,\quad 0\leq a,j<N. \] It has the EXPLICIT free basis z_(a,j). Multiplication is \[ z_{a,j}z_{c,k} =\begin{cases} \Phi^{\lfloor(a+c)/N\rfloor} z_{a+c\bmod N,k},& k=j-c\pmod N,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{2} \] This formula is associative (it records the shift of the idempotent and total integer f exponent) and realizes all defining relations, so it also proves the basis assertion without a dimension guess. Thus this is a flat rank-N-squared algebra over the WHOLE Phi base. At Phi=0 its ideal (f) is nonzero, nilpotent and two-sided, with quotient the N diagonal characters. It is the truncated quantum Borel algebra, also known as a Taft algebra. It is not Mat_N there. For Phi nonzero the cyclic module f e_j=e_(j+1) for j<N-1 and f e_(N-1)=Phi e_0, with H e_j=Q^(-j)e_j, gives Mat_N. The idempotents and nonzero cyclic arrows exhibit every matrix unit. After retaining a root rho^N=Phi, the normalized shift f/rho has Nth power one and gives a cyclic companion frame. This is a generic cyclic chart, not an extension of its bare matrix algebra through the nilpotent source. ## 2. Explicit free fusion for any number of actual strands For b=2 let u=e_0 tensor ones, and define \[ \mathcal F:A_\Phi\longrightarrow V_1\otimes V_2, \quad z_{a,j}\longmapsto f^a(e_0\otimes e_j). \tag{3} \] This is A_Phi-linear, because e_j u=e_0 tensor e_j. It is an isomorphism, including on Phi=0. Indeed the unique term with first output index a is F_1^a(e_0) tensor e_j, with coefficient (Q;Q)_a. Every other term has first index strictly smaller than a. No first-leg wrap occurs in fewer than N applications. In order of first index, (3) is block triangular with diagonal (Q;Q)_a times I_N. These are original nonzero factorial units. The determinant is their product, independent of phi_1,phi_2. For b greater than two, let t=(t_3,...,t_b) index the remaining physical heads and set u_t=e_0 tensor ones tensor e_t. Then \[ A_\Phi\otimes R^{N^{b-2}}\longrightarrow V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_b, \quad a\otimes t\longmapsto a u_{t} \tag{4} \] is again an isomorphism. The projector e_j selects the unique second index j-sum(t_i) modulo N; all-first-leg f terms give the same triangular diagonal (Q;Q)_a. Hence the actual tensor module is a FREE left A_Phi module of rank N^(b-2). This is a non-naive fusion basis built from the actual coproduct; no proposed product of two repaired head shifts has been substituted for it. The inverse is regular in all phi_i because that determinant is a fixed unit. Every actual matrix, source vector, cap and current has an exact conjugate under (4). There is no discarded endpoint, choice of replacement co-source or asymptotic remainder here. ## 3. Actual local R and arbitrary words act on this relative algebra The actual checked R intertwines the diagonal coproduct. On the same-color nilpotent section it commutes with H and f. Therefore (4) takes each actual local crossing and inverse into \[ \operatorname{End}_{A_\Phi}(A_\Phi^{N^{b-2}}) \cong \operatorname{Mat}_{N^{b-2}}(A_\Phi^{op}). \tag{5} \] For two strands it is right multiplication by a unique unit a_R, computed from R u using (3). It is NOT an unspecified scalar: the literal actual R matrix, including its half-Cartan and scalar line, fixes a_R. Composition and every signed braid relation follow by conjugating the actual word through the same basis change. The same construction applies to the full actual holonomy Hom line on its admissible splitting covers in [the regular holonomy theorem](regular_holonomy_braiding.md). The checked map preserves the diagonal coproduct, the product of the marked K roots and Phi in (1). Source and target versions of (4) give A_Phi-linear maps. Retain the actual Hom line and all closing root phases; no new global scalar frame is supplied here. The semicyclic case is the explicit polynomial intertwiner in [the carry-braiding theorem](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md), including its transported centers and corrected wrap factor. Thus (5) is actual root-parameter word transport across central Phi=0, not an assertion of topological invariance of a new period. The original selected word and its original source are transported together. On the nilpotent section their value is exactly the original invariant with every external normalization retained. ## 4. A regular Frobenius functional is a divided cyclic trace Define on the WHOLE flat algebra \[ \tau_{top}(z_{a,j})=\delta_{a,N-1}. \] Its left-dual basis is explicitly \[ d_{a,j}=f^{N-1-a}e_{j+a\bmod N},\qquad \tau_{top}(d_{a,j}z_{c,k})=\delta_{a,c}\delta_{j,k}. \tag{6} \] No Phi enters this Gram matrix: a matching product has exponent N-1 and never crosses a full f cycle. Thus this is a nondegenerate Frobenius functional on every fiber, including the nilpotent one. For any actual co-source Lambda on this relative algebra the marked density is the explicit finite element \[ C_\Lambda=\sum_{a,j}\Lambda(z_{a,j})d_{a,j},\qquad \Lambda(a)=\tau_{top}(C_\Lambda a). \tag{7} \] For several strands apply (7) to each relative matrix entry. Their coefficients are the literal pulled-back pivotal/cut rows from (4). This gives a concrete relative period for an arbitrary actual braid, not a replacement regular trace. For clarity the arbitrary-braid source formula is explicit. Let s,t index the tail labels of (4), and let a_(t,s) in A_Phi be the actual relative word matrix: its action is a tensor s to sum_t a a_(t,s) tensor t. For a closed input tuple (c,s), with c the second physical input, put k=c+sum_i s_i modulo N. Define the actual finite rows \[ L_{(c,s),t}(z) =(\mathrm{ones}^t\otimes e_c^t\otimes e_s^t) \mathcal F(z\otimes t), \] \[ \Lambda_{t,s}(z) =\sum_{c=0}^{N-1}\left(g_2(c)\prod_{i=3}^b g_i(s_i)\right) L_{(c,s),t}(e_k z). \] The g_i are the original pivotal entries with their actual colors. The original period, with its assigned external line gamma_beta, is EXACTLY \[ P_\beta=\gamma_\beta\sum_{t,s}\Lambda_{t,s}(a_{t,s}) =\gamma_\beta\sum_{t,s}\tau_{top}(C_{t,s}a_{t,s}), \tag{7a} \] where C_(t,s) is given by (7). This uses the original INPUT e_0 on the first strand, the SUM over its output, and every other original pivotal closure. Indeed e_k u_s is the literal input e_0 tensor e_c tensor e_s. Applying the A_Phi-linear word then gives this formula entry by entry. All closing identifications and the root of total K remain on their original cover. On the cyclic chart (7a) is the sum of Tr_N(f C_(t,s) a_(t,s))/Phi by (8), with its regular divided extension at Phi=0. No unspecified cap functional is introduced. In the N-dimensional cyclic splitting of Section 1, a stronger WHOLE polynomial identity is \[ \operatorname{Tr}_N(fa)=\Phi\,\tau_{top}(a). \tag{8} \] It suffices to check the basis: only a=f^(N-1)e_j contributes, when f a=Phi e_j. Consequently tau_top is exactly the retained DIVIDED central-F normal trace Tr(fa)/Phi, regular at Phi=0. Bare ordinary trace kills the nilpotent ideal and loses this value. The Frobenius functional is twisted rather than cyclic: its Nakayama transport is H to QH, f to f. It becomes conjugation by f only on Phi nonzero. No categorical modified-trace axioms are claimed solely from (6)-(8). ## 5. The actual two-leg cap density is explicit On the actual nilpotent same-color section put F_a=(Q;Q)_a, x=K on e_0 and g_j=(xQ^(-j))^(1-N). For a right multiplication operator R_a on A_0, the original highest-input pivotal cut is \[ \Lambda_{cap}(a)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}g_j L_j(e_j a),\quad L_j(z)=(\mathrm{ones}^t\otimes e_j^t)\mathcal F(z). \tag{9} \] All zero-framing, full d_N(M) and common crossing lines remain their original external factors. There is no extra 1/N here. For the basis z_(a,k), the finite binomial expansion of the ACTUAL coproduct gives \[ \Lambda_{cap}(f^a e_k)= \begin{cases} x^{1-N-a}Q^{-(k+a)}F_{k+a}/F_k,& k+a<N,\\ 0,&k+a\geq N. \end{cases} \tag{10} \] For the first case e_j f^a e_k requires j=k+a, and closing the second output at j forces all a lowering steps onto that leg. In the second case the required wrap is zero. This proves (10) with the original pivotal weights rather than an abstract trace. The density in (7) factors explicitly as C_cap=L R with \[ L=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{x^j}{F_j}f^j e_{N-1},\qquad R=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x^{1-N-k}Q^{-k}F_k f^{N-1-k}e_k. \] The multiplication rule (2) gives \[ R L=\gamma e_{N-1},\quad C_{cap}^2=\gamma C_{cap},\qquad \gamma=N x^{2-2N}Q\ne0. \tag{11} \] Thus the cap is a marked primitive projective density, with its full source character gamma retained. Formula (11) is asserted on Phi=0 here: modulo the nilpotent ideal C_cap/gamma is the primitive idempotent e_(N-1), so it is primitive. A generic cyclic cap must keep its actual wrap coefficients. Neither cyclicity of tau_top nor erasure of gamma is used to convert it into a preferred modified trace. ## 6. An actual period detects the nilpotent relative source At N=2, q=i, eta=exp(pi i/4), x=i, direct use of the actual positive balanced R gives \[ a_R=\eta I+\frac{\eta^{-1}}2 f e_0. \] Here (f e_0)^2=0 and the second term lies in the nilpotent radical. The original cap (9)-(10) satisfies \[ \Lambda_{cap}(I)=0,\qquad \Lambda_{cap}(f e_0)=2. \tag{12} \] Thus Lambda_cap(a_R)=eta inverse, the actual nonzero one-crossing cut before its retained external lines. Its entire value comes from the radical term; semisimple reduction gives zero. More generally Lambda_cap(a_R^m)=m eta^(m-2) in this example. The full framing and modified-dimension lines multiply these exact values and have not been reset. This is an actual source obstruction to factoring the word period through the semisimple quotient, not the previously noted failure of a naive tensor product of repaired shift pairs. The regular module's ordinary trace also kills the radical, whereas the actual divided cap functional does not. ## 7. Quantum normal and geometric comparison remain distinct The flat A_Phi transport is at a fixed original root Q. It does not by itself extend through a moving Q^N normal. For example, at N=2 the original finite matrices have \[ f_{tot}^2=(1+Q)F_1K_1^{-1}F_2,\qquad \left[\frac{f_{tot}^2}{1-Q^2}\right]_{Q=-1} =\tfrac12F_1K_1^{-1}F_2\ne0. \tag{13} \] On the actual highest product source at x=i its all-ones output value is -2i. A claimed whole Q-normal Taft model setting f^N=0 would erase this real actual current. Its divided-power/endpoint extension must be kept. The central Phi normal, the meridian norm and the Q-normal are not equated by their notation. The construction provides an actual non-naive word/source transport and an explicit divided-trace period candidate before jets in the central parameters. It still does not identify that period with the marked geometric Bloch regulator, prove survival of its geometric block under the final finite source, or control its hyperbolic-volume norm. The smooth companion frame alone does not supply those additional identifications. There is a further essential distinction. Phi in this note is the Frobenius-center value of a coproduct power at a FIXED root Q_N. It is not a coordinate on the q-to-one geometric critical variety. At the actual M=1 augmentation all root central meridians are I. The direct Wirtinger induction in [the closed-braid center calculation](closed_braid_period_line.md), Section 4, proves that its completed knot-representation germ is entirely abelian. Consequently deforming this center/source family locally at that closed augmentation cannot produce the hyperbolic flat connection. The generic semicyclic comparison remains on its reducible character locus. The full holonomy line and this fusion basis can be considered at other admissible center points, but that does not continue the specified augmentation frame or identify its selected period on another component. Any regulator comparison must leave this local germ by an independently proved global center or q-to-one critical source transform. The exact socle/divided-trace formula by itself does neither. In particular its nonzero nilpotent source class must not be renamed the geometric period or its coefficient. [Exact actual fusion, R, cap and normal checks](../experiments/audit_actual_borel_regular_fusion.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_borel_regular_fusion_results.json).

title: A literal Borel Ward contraction for the actual finite cut
text: # A literal Borel Ward contraction for the actual finite cut Research construction, 27 October 2026. This derives an explicit split Ward complex and its cut functional from the actual root matrices. It identifies exactly what unknot normalization fixes. It does not yet map the partially summed geometric Gaussian block into that complex or prove a selected global geometric contribution. ## 1. The two actual matrices already determine the scalar Ward kernel Fix N>=2, Q primitive of order N, x=-M/q!=0. In the original balanced basis w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a, 0<=a<N, the actual generators are K_aa=k_a=x Q^(-a), F_(a+1,a)=f_a=1-Q^(a+1), 0<=a<N-1, with all other F entries zero. Distinct k_a and nonzero f_a are units at every M!=0, including the complete value M=1. No E coefficient is inverted, so no color-reducibility wall is removed. For C in End(V) put delta(C)=([K,C],[F,C]), p(C)=Tr(C)/N, i(c)=c I. (1.1) Define two explicit maps on a pair (X,Z) of matrices. Let H_K(X) have zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries H_K(X)_(a,b)=X_(a,b)/(k_a-k_b), a!=b. Put d_r=Z_(r+1,r)/f_r and define the diagonal matrix H_F(Z)_aa=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-2)(N-1-r)d_r -sum_(r<a)d_r. (1.2) Then, for every matrix C, C=i p(C)+H_K([K,C])+H_F([F,C]). (1.3) For the off-diagonal entries this is immediate. On the diagonal, [F,C]_(r+1,r)/f_r=C_rr-C_(r+1,r+1); cumulative summation gives the diagonal minus its average, proving (1.3). In particular ker delta=k I. Define the actual Ward complex to be W^0=End(V) --delta--> W^1=im(delta). The map h(X,Z)=H_K(X)+H_F(Z) satisfies h delta=I-i p, delta h=I on W^1, p h=0, h delta i=0. (1.4) Thus it is an explicit strong contraction onto k I in degree zero. There is no claim that the unrestricted codomain End(V)^2 has vanishing higher cokernel; W^1 is the actual image subspace. These are matrix identities, independent of any irreducibility, semisimplicity, Haar integration, or modified-trace existence theorem. ## 2. The original marked cut is cohomologous to the normalized scalar row In this same balanced basis the prescribed source and co-source are psi=(1,...,1)^t and phi=(1/N)(1,...,1). Hence e=psi phi, e_(a,b)=1/N, Phi(C)=Tr(e C). The original pivot is g=K^(1-N), and its marked defect is D=g^(-1)e; thus the actual expression is Phi(C)=Tr(g D C). Neither the pivot nor the full external modified-dimension line d_N(M) is dropped. There is an explicit matrix B_cut, with zero diagonal, such that (B_cut)_(a,b)=1/[N(k_a-k_b)], a!=b, [K,B_cut]=e-I/N. (2.1) Consequently, for every C, Phi(C)-p(C)=-Tr(B_cut[K,C]). (2.2) Thus the degree-one row b(X,Z)=-Tr(B_cut X) is an exact cochain homotopy Phi-p=b delta on the Ward complex. In particular the original rank-one cut and the scalar normalized trace agree exactly on Ward-closed matrices. Their common value on I is one. This is the literal unknot normalization, rather than a comparison of two quantities that only have the same norm. The pivot's ordinary trace is still zero; (2.2) does not replace the marked defect D by an ordinary pivotal closure. At the root D^2=0, gD=e and DgD=D, as in [the actual relative source](relative_framing_source_transgression.md). The equality of cut rows is an equality on the Ward complex, with the defect retained. ## 3. The actual closed tangle is Ward closed The prescribed R matrices intertwine the actual coproduct, and the cups and pivotal caps are the explicit Hopf maps already checked in [the duality calculation](relative_pivotal_duality.md). Composing these identities around the closed strands shows that the original (1,1)-tangle endomorphism C commutes with K and F. It therefore lies in ker delta and equals p(C)I by (1.3). This proves the finite scalar/cut conclusion directly from the actual matrices. It also gives an exact target for any proposed framing reduction: a map of actual partial-source complexes into W, with the cut row (2.2) and its homotopy transported, would reduce that framing problem to its scalar Ward class. The global intertwining identity alone does not construct such a map for a partially summed array. A remaining external internal index is not an open-tangle matrix index. Moving F through the unsummed network generally produces currents in those remaining flow coordinates. Their exact finite boundary, canonical carries and normal source must be retained to identify its complex with W. ## 4. Actual coproduct symbols and the two cut-framing currents There is a direct principal-symbol comparison, using the already proved actual moment-map identity. On the tensor product put K_tot=Delta^(b-1)K, Ecal_tot=rho^2 Delta^(b-1)E, F_tot=Delta^(b-1)F, rho=q-q^(-1). In balanced wave coordinates A=Q^a and S f(A)=f(QA), their local input matrices have symbols K=x/A, e=(1-x^2/A)p/x, f=(1-A)/p. The actual finite Ecal is the truncated matrix, including its rank-one endpoint subtraction; only its interior symbol is used in this display. The actual coproducts are Delta K=K tensor K, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Writing the classical prefix product as P=[a b;c d], its exact Gauss factorization gives symbol(K_tot)=a, symbol(Ecal_tot)=b, symbol(F_tot)=c/a. (4.1) Indeed the upper triangular products multiply their off-diagonal entries by E_1K_2+E_2, while the lower triangular product gives F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2. Taking B_-^(-1)B_+ gives P with precisely the three entries in (4.1). For simultaneous conjugation A xi and the actual symplectic form, [the uniform moment-map calculation](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) proves iota_(A xi) Omega=(2u da+v dc+w db)/a, xi=u h+v e_sl+w f_sl, where h=diag(1,-1), e_sl=E_12, f_sl=E_21. With the convention iota_(X_H)Omega=dH, equation (4.1) therefore yields X_logK=A(h/2), X_F=A(e_sl-(c/(2a))h), X_Ecal=A(a f_sl). (4.2) The cut stabilizer is ker ell, ell(h,e_sl,f_sl)=(2,1,-1). Thus K,F alone describe a different Borel. Its actual cut basis h+2f_sl, e_sl+f_sl is instead obtained from A(h+2f_sl)=(2/a)(X_K+X_Ecal), A(e_sl+f_sl)=X_F+(c/a^2)X_K+(1/a)X_Ecal. (4.3) These relations also give literal quantum Ward identities with a specified operator order. For any full tensor endomorphism J commuting with the actual coproduct generators, both W_1(J)=2 K_tot^(-1)([K_tot,J]+[Ecal_tot,J]), W_2(J)=[F_tot,J]+F_tot K_tot^(-1)[K_tot,J] +K_tot^(-1)[Ecal_tot,J] (4.4) vanish exactly. Their first commutator symbols divided by H=Log Q give the two vector fields in (4.3). No quantum Log K is needed. The coefficients in (4.4) multiply on the left; interchanging their order introduces genuine additional quantum terms. Equations (4.3)--(4.4) identify the principal cut-framing currents, but are not by themselves a quantum representation of the cut Borel Lie algebra. The Hopf-adjoint presentation below removes their variable-coefficient ambiguity at the finite matrix level. ### The Hopf adjoint gives constant conjugation fields For h in the actual quantum group define its actual action on matrices by ad_h(C)=sum rho(h_1) C rho(S h_2). The displayed coproduct and antipode formulas give, exactly, (ad_K-I)(C)=[K,C]K^(-1), ad_Ecal(C)=[Ecal,C]K^(-1), ad_F(C)=[F,C]+K^(-1)[K,C]F. (4.5) In the tensor formulas K,Ecal,F are their actual total coproducts. The first commutator symbols divided by H are therefore (ad_K-I)/H -> A(h/2), ad_Ecal/H -> A f_sl, ad_F/H -> A e_sl. (4.6) For F, the extra term contributes (c/a)X_logK, canceling the h component in (4.2). Thus 2(ad_K-I)+2ad_Ecal, ad_F+ad_Ecal (4.7) are literal quantum Ward operators with principal fields A(h+2f_sl), A(e_sl+f_sl). They use the actual truncated E, including its endpoint, and no logarithm of K. The conventional opposite sign of fundamental conjugation vector-field brackets agrees with the Ecal-to-f_sl and F-to-e_sl correspondence. No exact two-generator Lie or coideal presentation is being inferred solely from these first symbols. The K,F Hopf Ward rows and the rows in (1.1) are related by an invertible exact row operation: X_H=X K^(-1), Z_H=Z+K^(-1)X F, X=X_H K, Z=Z_H-K^(-1)X_H K F. (4.8) Hence (1.4) transfers to the Hopf Ward complex by substituting the second line of (4.8) into h. Its cut homotopy is Phi-p=-Tr(K B_cut (ad_K-I)(C)), (4.9) with B_cut from (2.1). This is an actual cochain row transformation. ### Pivotal partial trace is an exact Hopf-adjoint chain map For two actual modules V,W let ptr_W(C)=Tr_W((I tensor g_W)C), g_W=K_W^(1-N). Then for every matrix C, not only for invariant intertwiners, ptr_W(ad_h C)=ad_h(ptr_W C). (4.10) One exact proof identifies End(V tensor W) with V tensor W tensor W* tensor V* and contracts W tensor W* by the actual right pivotal cap w tensor phi |-> phi(g_W w). This cap is a Hopf map by the checked antipode identities. The resulting contraction is literally the displayed weighted partial trace. There is also a generator check with no categorical premise. For K, cyclicity of the W trace and commutation of g_W with K_W give the assertion. For Ecal, expand [Ecal_V K_W+Ecal_W,C] * (K_V K_W)^(-1). The V terms give the right side, and the two W terms cancel because K_W^(-1)g_W is central. For F, expand the third formula of (4.5) for F_tot=F_V+K_V^(-1)F_W. Again the V terms give the right side; the W terms cancel by K_W F_W g_W K_W^(-1)=g_W F_W, which follows from the same centrality. The generator identities extend by composition to every h. Iterating gives every original pivotal closed-strand contraction. Thus the degree-zero map ptr and its rowwise degree-one map give an exact map from the full finite tensor Hopf-Ward complex (using its actual image as degree one) to the cut Hopf-Ward complex. The scalar contraction and the actual cut homotopy are now attached to that finite diagram. This does not yet identify scalar partial Gaussian elimination with that operator-valued diagram. It must transport the E endpoint, the diagonal K poles, cumulative F carries, and the chosen normal source. A remaining flow index is not automatically an open matrix index. That is the remaining algebraic comparison, rather than a consequence of Schur scalarity or (4.10). ## 5. Uniform size and regularity of the actual contraction For the prescribed unit-circle root, |Q^(-a)-Q^(-b)|>=4/N for a!=b, |1-Q^(r+1)|>=4/N. These follow from sin(pi/N)>=2/N. With the maximum entry norm, ||H_K(X)|| <= N ||X||/(4|x|), ||H_F(Z)|| <= N(N-1)||Z||/4. (4.1) The coefficients in (1.2) each have modulus at most one, giving the second bound. Hence the actual Ward contraction is regular at M=1 and has polynomial bounds in N on compact meridian sets away from zero. This estimate does not involve d_N(M); that separate marked line keeps all its original divisors and jets. Polynomial control of a projection does not imply that its value on a given nonzero vector has a nonzero exponential rate. Its kernel contains many nonzero matrices. The bound is useful only after the actual source class has been shown to survive the map. ## 6. What this does and does not settle about the geometric block The partially summed actual family has a nonzero transverse formal geometric block and an actual bulk operator with geometric support, as proved in [the partial support construction](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). The remaining two-index framing functional has not thereby been identified with the contraction (1.4), nor with the sourced centralizer transgression. That identification requires explicit Ward currents from the local R coproduct identities after partial elimination, and a map retaining the chosen source and normal row. If a nonzero formal geometric class were proved to map into ker delta as a nonzero endomorphism, then its cut would be nonzero algebraically: ker delta=k I and Phi(I)=1. This is a precise reduction of the needed normalization problem, not a proof of that embedding or its nonzero scalar coefficient. Ward identities plus unknot normalization alone cannot prove that coefficient is nonzero for every knot: arbitrary scalar families C_K=c_K I satisfy both commutator equations, with c_unknot=1 and c_K=0 allowed elsewhere. The missing source map must supply more information than the universal commutant calculation. No global cycle, Stokes, or volume inference is made here. The [cyclic Ward completion](cyclic_ward_norm_adapter.md) also computes the missing raising edge, its full Frobenius determinant character, and a literal quantum-factorial affine source equation. This retains the complete d_N(M) adapter. It is a further exact source datum for the missing Gaussian/adjoint comparison, rather than a replacement for that comparison. ## 7. Subsequent currents and an exact divided-normal realization of the cut The [literal local R currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md) now give the unsummed E and F Ward divergence formulas with the full missing-edge source and inserted moments. Their ordinary closed wall source cancels exactly, so a locally nonzero wall entry cannot by itself certify the global geometric contribution. On the genuine complete integral-color lift there is a different specified normal operator: the [true divided Hopf adjoint](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md) J_ad=[(ad_Ecal)^N/(1-Q^N)]_root. For the literal missing edge W=E_(N-1,0), direct calculation gives J_ad(W)=-N sum_(a=0)^(N-2) E_(a,a+1), Phi(J_ad(W))=-(N-1). Therefore the normalized row Phi_div(C)=-Phi(J_ad(C W))/(N-1) has Phi_div(I)=1 and obeys the exact all-matrices homotopy Phi_div-Phi=(Phi_div-Phi)h delta. It returns the original invariant on every actual closed tangle. Generic pivotal naturality before division also gives an explicit full-network realization, with the ordered insertion T(W_cut tensor I) retained. This supplies an actual divided-normal cut, rather than a conjectural scalar normalization. The [complete-color theorem](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md) keeps its q-normal distinct from the fixed-root meridian normal, and retains the pivot and framing derivatives. Its one-sided fusion correction is a finite exponential with nilpotence bounded by tensor length. The opposite divided Ward actions contain an SL_2 block, so a nilpotent whole gauge group is not asserted. The Gaussian/source comparison and selected volume norm remain the additional theorem. The [subsequent complete-color residual theorem](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md) now computes the dual cut rows explicitly and transports their currents through the actual nondegenerate transverse Gaussian. Their two compensated framing fields have precisely the source covariance of Omega_cut, and their formal ideal is the flat line of that actual Gaussian amplitude. This supplies an all-order interior formal ideal, while preserving the distinction from the whole finite relative-source complex. The [finite-cut source audit](finite_cut_euler_source_obstruction.md) shows explicitly why such local formal closure alone cannot prove nonzero selected source survival. [Exact matrix audit](../experiments/audit_actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.py). [Results](../experiments/actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction_results.json).

title: Uniformly bounded physical quantum meridians through every actual braid
text: # Uniformly bounded physical quantum meridians through every actual braid 28 October 2026. The particular Heisenberg meridian matrices of the original quantum crossing are uniformly bounded in N along any fixed signed braid word, despite the possible exponential condition number of its crossing matrices. The reason is the EXACT quantum Hurwitz law: their conjugates are fixed Nielsen words in the initial meridians, whose inverses have a bounded polynomial formula. Their entries and adjoints asymptotically commute in operator norm. Consequently every positive Gram moment limit has compact, honest SL2 free-group/braid-graph support, including Gauss-chart boundaries. This does NOT impose the original knot closure on such a positive state or identify singular atomic shape phases with that support. Those are explicit remaining requirements for a sharp upper bound. ## 1. The original complete-head observables form a bounded star family Use the actual balanced factorial basis, N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^(-1), rho=q-q^(-1). Put K=x Z^(-1), e=q rho^2 E, f=F, Z w_a=Q^a w_a. These are the original finite quantum-group matrices. Explicitly f w_a=(1-Q^(a+1))w_(a+1), a<d, f w_d=0, e w_(a+1)=(x^(-1)-xQ^(-a))w_a, a<d. In the actual flat positive head metric, ||K||=||K^(-1)||=1, ||e||,||f||<=2, K^*=K^(-1), e^*=x f, f^*=x e. (1) The last identities follow entrywise using xQ=x^(-1). They do not assert unitarity of the original braiding or positivity of its pivotal closing, both of which have separate exact obstructions. The scaled relations are Ke=QeK, Kf=Q^(-1)fK, [e,f]=(Q-1)(K-K^(-1)), fe=c-QK-K^(-1), c=x^(-1)+Qx. (2) Thus commutators among e,f,K,K^(-1) and ALL their adjoints have norm O(|Q-1|)=O(1/N). Different heads commute exactly. There is no inverse rho or factorial in these estimates. ## 2. Bounded matrices and polynomial inverses On an auxiliary two-dimensional space define the actual L matrices L_+=[[K,e],[0,I]], L_-=[[I,0],[-Kf,K]], L_-^(-1)=[[I,0],[f,K^(-1)]], G=L_-^(-1)L_+=[[K,e],[fK,fe+K^(-1)]]. (3) All L matrices and their inverses have norm at most 3: each is a unitary block diagonal plus an off-diagonal block of norm at most 2. Consequently ||G||,||G^(-1)||<=9. The exact quantum identity already proved from the original entries is G^2-cG+QI=0, G^(-1)=Q^(-1)(cI-G). (4) It supplies an alternative polynomial inverse, without choosing a Gauss face denominator or inverting a nilpotent root shift. For b heads set P_(j-1)=L_(-,j-1)...L_(-,1) and H_j=P_(j-1)^(-1)G_j P_(j-1), 1<=j<=b. (5) These are the actual based meridians (the physical SL2 lift is -H_j). Before any braid action, ||H_j||,||H_j^(-1)||<=9^j<=C_b, C_b=9^b. (6) All entries are fixed-degree polynomials in the head observables (1), with coefficients bounded uniformly in N. Their inverse entries also have this property by (4). ## 3. Exact all-word Heisenberg transport and its uniform bound Let B_i be the original checked crossing on heads i,i+1, with its full common Cartan scalar either included or retained in the unchanged external line. The direct finite proof in [the shared quantum flags](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md) gives the exact two-head identities. They extend to (5) as Ad_(B_i) H_i=H_(i+1), Ad_(B_i) H_(i+1)=H_(i+1)H_iH_(i+1)^(-1), Ad_(B_i) H_j=H_j for j!=i,i+1. (7) Indeed the earlier prefix commutes with B_i. For later heads the two adjacent L_- factors in the prefix have their product preserved by the same original Hopf intertwining; thus the later prefix is unchanged. The inverse crossing gives Ad_(B_i^(-1)) H_i=H_i^(-1)H_(i+1)H_i, Ad_(B_i^(-1)) H_(i+1)=H_i. (8) No inverse of B is estimated by its operator norm. Repeatedly substituting (7)-(8) expresses, for EVERY actual signed prefix W of length m, W H_j W^(-1)=w_(W,j)(H_1,...,H_b), (9) where w is the explicit free-group Nielsen word. Its unreduced length is at most 3^m; free cancellation can only improve it. Therefore, uniformly for all levels N, ||W H_j W^(-1)||, ||(W H_j W^(-1))^(-1)|| <=C_b^(3^m). (10) The bound is intentionally coarse and may be large in the fixed diagram. Its point is independence of N. All full Cartan/framing/ peripheral scalars remain those of W; its scalar line cancels only in this genuine conjugation identity. Each entry on the right of (9), and its adjoint, is a fixed-degree bounded polynomial in (1). Leibniz expansion of a commutator and (2) now prove, for ANY two such entries at ANY two prefixes, ||[A_N,B_N]||, ||[A_N,B_N^*]||<=C_(b,W)/N. (11) Thus the full finite family of transported physical meridian observables is uniformly bounded and asymptotically commuting as a star family. A general Heisenberg conjugate of an arbitrary coupon does not enjoy (10); the exact Nielsen relation is essential here. ## 4. What every positive Gram limit actually supports Take ANY positive trace-class Gamma_N of trace one on the initial b-head Hilbert space. This could be a normalized Gram of a specified annotated network if that construction is available; no positive pivotal closing is being assumed. For the fixed family above every polynomial moment is uniformly bounded, so a subsequence has all moments convergent. Equation (11) lets these limits be regarded as a functional on the COMMUTATIVE polynomial star algebra of the limiting entries. It is positive because for every polynomial p, lim Tr(Gamma_N p_N^*p_N)>=0. It has a compact representation. To see the needed boundedness directly, use real and imaginary coordinate operators. Each has norm at most a fixed C. Thus in its polynomial GNS inner product, multiplication by each real coordinate is a commuting selfadjoint operator of norm at most C: positivity of C^2-X_N^2 passes to the limit. Their joint spectrum is compact and represents the moments by a positive measure. This uses the actual operator bounds, not normalized expectations of a nonpositive source. At any character of that commutative algebra let k,e,f denote a head's values. Equations (1)-(2) imply |k|=1, f=-conjugate(e), ef+k+k^(-1)=-2. The commuting matrix g from (3) therefore has determinant one and trace -2. Its based versions h_j in (5) are genuine SL2 matrices, including the central value -I. All their inverses remain regular. The exact identities (7)-(9) show that the time-indexed character matrices are precisely the honest free-group Hurwitz braid graph. This statement persists when a local Gauss coordinate or flag cross-ratio chart degenerates. It does not require a bounded inverse of that chart's denominator. For example, if a SPECIFIED positive annotated state additionally obeyed the actual closed-meridian matching equations in mean square, its limiting measure would be supported on honest knot representations. For a polynomial matrix constraint F, the statement follows from Tr(Gamma_N F_N^*F_N)->0 and positivity. Establishing that property for the original relative closing is a remaining theorem, not a consequence of (10) or an assertion of this note. ## 5. Why final cut vectorization does not supply those constraints The actual assembled knot cut is C_K=f_(K,N)I. When it is nonzero, its normalized vectorized Gram is EXACTLY |vec C_K><vec C_K|/||C_K||_HS^2 =|vec I><vec I|/N. (12) It is the same cut state for every knot. The scalar norm stores the unknown period; the normalized state by itself contains no interior meridian or atomic-shape data. Such data must be added as a specified bounded observable/source lift, rather than inferred from (12). Retaining all internal coupon moments is possible algebraically, but the original closing is not a positive multiplicative compression: its canonical nilpotent Pi satisfies ptr_g(Pi)=I and Pi^2=0, while ptr_g(I)=0. The [actual positivity obstruction](actual_quantum_source_positivity_obstruction.md) therefore remains relevant. The polynomial norm of that extension helps retain it; it does not automatically make its positive Gram impose all original closure equations. Finally, honest physical braid-graph support alone does not identify the JOINT atom-shape limit at singular face denominators. A boundary comparison must retain those shapes and their regulator, not merely bounded physical matrices. The saturated critical compactification theorem already bounds the regulator on the genuine critical joint closure; this note does not prove that every source boundary belongs to that closure. The unconditional advance is (9)-(11): the specific physical Heisenberg meridians need no uncontrolled braid-condition-number estimate. No sharp whole-period upper bound is asserted here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_bounded_quantum_meridians.py): literal original signed prefixes, all based quantum matrices, exact Nielsen substitution, polynomial inverses and direct complex star/ commutator bounds. It retains both crossing signs and original Cartan factors in the matrix comparisons.

title: The actual braid transport has a semisimple sector
text: # The actual braid transport has a semisimple sector Research note, 26 October 2026. The finite-by-Heisenberg result for ideal shape ordering does not extend to the full actual braid-source transport. At every level the latter has a connected subgroup with an SL_2 quotient. We prove this from the prescribed crossing, using a nonzero exact pivotal moment and an ordinary-trace identity with definite sign. Finite-index restriction cannot remove that sector. This suggests a relative approach: retain the semisimple central/spectral algebra and study its normalization or period extension. We give an explicit rank-four algebra for the two unipotent generators, and show how the already computed actual two-channel source splits on a quadratic spectral cover. Neither construction identifies its spectral coordinate with the geometric A-curve or proves the volume conjecture. ## 1. Fix the actual crossing and its phase Let N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and use exactly the actual color V=V_(x_0), x_0=q^(N-1)=-q^(-1). Write B for the checked crossing with the common Cartan scalar removed, as in the original ADO cut. Its zero-framing scalar is theta=x_0^(1-N), theta^(2N)=1. Replacing B_i by theta^(-1)B_i gives the same zero-framed word evaluation and is still a braid representation. Thus the pure braid powers below are the actual normalized ones: U_1=B_12^(2N)=I+X, U_2=B_23^(2N)=I+Y, J=B^(2N)-I, X=J tensor I, Y=I tensor J. (1.1) For the full universal crossing the common scalar and twist cancel in this same normalization. No peripheral or modified dimension factor is changed. The [independently proved Casimir interpolation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#3-the-actual-crossing-has-a-unique-confluent-polynomial) has double nodes c_k=q^h+q^(-h), h=2k+1<N, with r_N(c_k)=nu_k=(-1)^k q^(k(k+1)), r_N'(c_k)/nu_k=-(N-h)/[2(q^h-q^(-h))]. The one possible simple node has the same root-of-unity property nu_k^(2N)=1. Since B=r_N(Omega), (1.1) obeys J^2=0, X^2=Y^2=0. (1.2) The claim follows by evaluating the value and derivative of (r_N^(2N)-1)^2 at every double node; both are zero. The same polynomial vanishes at the simple node. This is a statement about the actual matrices, not a formal leading symbol or a spectral projector substituted for a crossing. ## 2. An exact nonzero pivotal moment Keep the original K and pivot g=K^(1-N)=(-1)^(N-1)K. The already proved closing functional on the Casimir algebra is ptr_K f(Omega) =[-sum_(h odd, 0<h<N) (c_h f(c_h)+(q^h-q^(-h))^2 f'(c_h)) + simple-node contribution] I. For f=r_N^(2N)-1 its node values are zero and its double-node derivatives are -N(N-h)/(q^h-q^(-h)). Therefore, exactly, ptr_K J=Phi_N I, Phi_N=N sum_(h odd, 0<h<N)(N-h)(q^h-q^(-h)) =-2N^2/rho !=0. (2.1) For the last equality multiply the sum by rho and use rho(q^h-q^(-h)) =(q^(h+1)+q^(-h-1))-(q^(h-1)+q^(-h+1)). The weighted sum telescopes; q^N=-1 and the Q-geometric sum give -2N, for either parity of N. Thus no exceptional level or unverified noncancellation hypothesis enters (2.1). With the actual pivot the corresponding scalar is L_N=(-1)^(N-1) Phi_N. Sequentially closing strands 3 and 2 in XY gives t_reduced,W(XY)=L_N^2, mathfrak_t_W(XY)=d_N(1)L_N^2 !=0, d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N. (2.2) These are the actual cut and its full modified normalization. This test uses the pure-braid source operators; the braid powers depend on N. It is not the fixed-knot volume limit. ## 3. A negative ordinary trace forces a semisimple quotient For a pair matrix use the total integer degree a+b. The actual B and J preserve that degree, so the ordinary partial traces A=Tr_1 J, C=Tr_2 J are diagonal. We claim C=-conjugate(A). Here is a direct proof retaining the original Cartan order. Write B=P D Theta, where P is the swap and D_(a,b)=x_0^(-a-b)q^(2ab). In this color E_j=[j]_q^2 is real and F is the real unit shift. Complex conjugation of the finite Euler coefficients gives Theta^(-1), while conjugation gives D^(-1) on D. The finite inverse identity is the ordinary Euler convolution on its nilpotent argument. Hence conjugate(B)=D^(-1) P B^(-1) P D, conjugate(J)=-D^(-1) P J P D. (3.1) The second equation uses J^2=0. On diagonal entries the D factors cancel. Summing the diagonals gives C=-conjugate(A). Consequently on W=V^(tensor 3), Tr_W(XY)=Tr(A C)=-sum_a |A_aa|^2 <0. (3.2) The strict inequality has a proof, not a numerical assumption: Tr(A K)=Tr[J(I tensor K)]=N Phi_N !=0. Indeed (2.1) computes this trace by closing the other factor. As |K_aa|=1, it also gives the quantitative bound -Tr_W(XY) >= N |Phi_N|^2=4N^5/|rho|^2. (3.3) Now XY has a nonzero eigenvalue lambda. Choose v with XYv=lambda v and put w=Yv. Then Xv=0, Xw=lambda v, Yv=w, Yw=0. The vectors v,w are independent. Their plane is invariant under U_1,U_2, with matrices U_1|=[1 lambda;0 1], U_2|=[1 0;1 1]. (3.4) Their cyclic powers are Zariski dense in the respective one-parameter upper and lower unipotent groups, since the characteristic is zero. Those two groups generate SL_2: elementary upper/lower row operations give its open Gaussian cell and its remaining matrices. Thus the closure of the subgroup generated by U_1,U_2 has an SL_2 quotient on this plane and lies in the identity component of the full braid image closure. In particular that identity component is not solvable, and is not nilpotent. Every finite-index subgroup of the original braid group contains positive powers of both pure braids. The same plane argument applies with their two nonzero parameters rescaled. Thus no such restriction removes this connected semisimple sector, at any N>=2. The invariant plane here is selected from an eigenvalue of XY; it is not asserted to be the two-cup corner. That corner is not generally preserved by the full braid powers. Nor does this theorem compute the difference-Galois group of the minimal quantum A-operator or identify its selected geometric branch. It tests the full retained braid transport, which is stronger data than a normalization line. ## 4. The two-square-zero algebra has an explicit spectral center There is nevertheless a useful reduction. In the universal algebra on X,Y with X^2=Y^2=0, put c=XY+YX. It commutes with both generators. Every alternating word reduces to a C[c]-linear combination of 1,X,Y,XY; for example (XY)^k=c^(k-1)XY and XYX=cX. These four elements are independent, as the following model over C[c] shows: X=[0 1;0 0], Y=[0 0;c 0], XY=[c 0;0 0]. Its commutator equations also show that the center is exactly C[c]. After c is inverted the algebra is Mat_2(C[c,c^(-1)]), with matrix units e_11=XY/c, e_22=YX/c, e_12=X, e_21=Y/c. (4.1) Thus on a simple nonzero spectral component the comparison problem reduces to a line. Replacing a source module by only its scalar center still loses its multiplicity, lattice and period functional; those remain specified data. At c=0 the flat abstract fiber is the four-dimensional exterior algebra X^2=Y^2=0, YX=-XY. Its augmentation ideal has cube zero, and [1+sX,1+tY]=1+2stXY is central. This is the two-step nilpotent fiber. The ambient two-by-two matrix specialization of the displayed model is not faithful there; using it alone would lose the flat source directions. A finite field extension cannot send a nonzero spectral value c to this zero fiber. For the actual X,Y of (1.1), (3.2) proves that nonzero spectral components occur. The spectral center is for this pair of pure powers. It is not claimed to commute with the original B_12,B_23, or to give their entire knot-period decomposition. ## 5. The actual cap source detects its matrix sector There is also a completely calibrated source test. Use the actual adjacent cups and caps from [the source normal form](adjacent_source_normal_form.md#1-adjacent-cups-and-caps-give-opposite-source-matrix-units). Their operators Pi_1,Pi_2 have square zero and obey Pi_1 Pi_2 Pi_1=Pi_1, Pi_2 Pi_1 Pi_2=Pi_2. Their common corner is two copies of V. On it they are E_12,E_21, with the actual full modified trace d_N(1) times the ordinary two-by-two trace. Let A_s=I+s Pi_1, B_t=I+t Pi_2, C_(s,t)=A_s B_t A_s^(-1) B_t^(-1). On the corner det C=1 and Tr C=2+s^2t^2, and it is the identity on the complementary source. Therefore, exactly, mathfrak_t_W(C_(s,t)^m-I) =d_N(1)[T_m(2+s^2t^2)-2], (5.1) T_0=2, T_1=z, T_(m+1)=zT_m-T_(m-1). This follows from the actual rectangular trace calibration, not from choosing a new scalar trace. For s=t=1 the trace argument is 3, so the right side detects the semisimple matrix dynamics. These localized source units need not be braid words; (3.4) supplies the separate genuine-braid theorem. Growth in m in (5.1) concerns word length at a fixed N, not growth of a fixed knot as the level changes. ## 6. A cover can split the spectral algebra instead of killing it The original meridian source already has the appropriate quadratic deformation. Its two numerators satisfy t_1^2=delta t_1, t_2^2=delta t_2, z=t_1t_2+t_2t_1-delta(t_1+t_2) central. On the actual charged two-copy block, delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), A_N=(-1)^N rho(M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^N+M^(-N)), z=A_N^2-delta^2. (6.1) All functions are the previously calibrated actual ones. In particular the peripheral denominator is retained. More generally pass to the quadratic cover A^2=z+delta^2. Where A and z are units, the identities e_11=(t_1t_2-delta t_1)/z, e_22=(t_2t_1-delta t_2)/z, e_12=(t_1-delta e_11)/A, e_21=(t_2-delta e_22)/A (6.2) are matrix units, directly splitting this rank-four algebra. The actual mark is A=A_N, and at completeness A_N=(-1)^N rho^2 is nonzero. Thus the meridian source is on the matrix-algebra locus at each fixed level, rather than at its nilpotent fiber. Once these source generators and the charged simple module are matched, their simultaneous comparison is a scalar line. This is a useful finite-cover reduction of a torsor problem. It preserves the semisimple algebra, its integral source and its trace, while making the remaining comparison rank one. It does not prove that the same central functions and cut are realized on the geometric triangulation or A-curve. This statement concerns the integral numerators t_i. It does not supply a common finite lattice for both unscaled projectors t_i/delta; their double-pole trace obstruction from the adjacent-source note remains in force. ## 7. Consequence for the Regge and cover strategy The [finite Regge/ordering result](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) and its Heisenberg period kernel remain valid. The present theorem rules out extending that nilpotence claim to the whole actual braid-source group. A finite cover can still choose roots, split a spectral algebra and make scalar comparison possible, as (6.2) shows. The target must keep the semisimple source and seek a controlled period extension or marked quotient over it. Such a relative viewpoint has existing coverage in [Hain's relative Malcev theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9607019). Also, the stated homological model of [De Renzi--Martel, 2212.10940](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10940) uses Heisenberg coefficients for quantum mapping-class-group representations. A nilpotent coefficient group does not assert that the represented mapping class or braid image is nilpotent. [Karvounis, 1909.11162](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11162) already treats projective quantum-sl2 braid representations and nontrivial central action. Only their stated coverage was consulted; none of their proofs is used above. We have not identified the SL_2 plane of (3.4) with hyperbolic holonomy, built the requisite relative completion of the selected quantum A-period, or proved its regulator norm. The original conjecture remains unproved. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_semisimple_transport.py) checks the genuine pure powers, the conjugation and pivotal identities, full original source closings, and the spectral matrix-unit and commutator formulas. [Results](../experiments/actual_semisimple_transport_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_actual_semisimple_transport.py

title: The actual braided residual-framing current
status: Actual finite framing current and source-preserving boundary weights
text: # The actual braided residual-framing current 30 October 2026. After a legitimate coherent functional fixes the first cut, the actual Hopf adjoint gives an exact current in the second cut.
