Its coefficients are two routed OFF-DIAGONAL bands of the original tensor. They are not reconstructed from the diagonal two-cut array. The identity holds at arbitrary width, with actual finite endpoints and every genuine quantum jet. This is a finite-source integration-by-parts identity. Its closed flux is zero; no nonzero relative framing residue or selected global cycle coefficient is inferred from that fact. ## 1. The source, coherent first cut, and actual generic generators Use the [braided source adapter](actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.md). Fix d=N-1 and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). At the two actual Morse cuts let V=V_d^tensor b, W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and let A:W->V and B:V->W be the original covariant maps. Original cups, caps and all scalar/peripheral factors remain in A,B. The partial closure P_V uses the actual generic pivot g=(-1)^d K on the closed heads. Let U be the recorded braid carrying the chosen W head to its first position. Thus in the parallel convention U=R_1...R_j, with R_j acting first. Define the WHOLE band operator C_(p,q)=P_V[A U^-1(E_pq tensor I)U B], J_(a,l)=(C_(l,l))_(a,a). (1) Indices outside 0,...,d are zero ACTUAL matrix entries. No Fourier wrap or continued endpoint is substituted for that zero. By actual integer degree conservation C_(l,l) is diagonal, although the nearby band operators in (1) need not be. Closing the identity cut gives sum_l C_(l,l)=z(epsilon)I. For t distinct from 0,1 put beta_a(t)=binom(d,a)t^a(1-t)^(d-a), e_t=beta(t) 1^T, Tr e_t=sum_a beta_a=1. (2) This is the existing coherent boundary functional with w=1 and z_coh=t/(1-t). It is source-preserving on the WHOLE exposed scalar: Tr(e_t zI)=z, exactly, including the fixed d=N-1. It is not an additional normalized state on the second identity edge. All formulas below also hold for any specified quantum-independent vector beta of sum one; (2) is the legitimate coherent localization used here. Write the actual generic generator entries as k_a=zeta^(d-2a), f_a=1-Q^(a+1), 0<=a<d, e_a=zeta^(-N)(1-Q^(N-a)), 1<=a<=d, Q=zeta^2. (3) Their missing endpoint arrows are ZERO. In particular f_d=e_0=0 as matrices, even though the untruncated expressions in (3) need not vanish there at generic zeta. The Hopf adjoints are ad_K C=K C K^-1, ad_E C=[E,C]K^-1, ad_F C=[F,C]+K^-1[K,C]F. The residual combination is D_c=ad_F-ad_E-2(ad_K-I). (4) Its proved principal framing field is partial_r in the actual F(r,s) chart, with the first cut clock A_cut=(1+s)^-1 fixed; see [the actual Ward fields](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). Multiplication by s gives s partial_r. We do not identify a finite translation with this infinitesimal field merely from its symbol. ## 2. A source-defined flux using the two neighboring bands For 0<=a<d define L_a=f_a beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1), L_-1=L_d=0. (5) Define the actual band pairing and its second-head flux by T_t(p,q)=Tr(e_t C_(p,q)), M_l=f_l T_t(l+1,l) +(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1)) T_t(l,l+1), 0<=l<d, M_-1=M_d=0. (6) Every C_(p,q) contains the full U and U^-1 and all original contractions. In particular (6) is not a choice of interpolation for J. The source identity is M_l-M_(l-1) =sum_(a=0)^d (L_a-L_(a-1)) J_(a,l) =sum_(a=0)^(d-1) L_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a+1,l)], 0<=l<=d. (7) Here is a direct proof. Generic pivotal partial closure is an exact Hopf-adjoint map, and A,B,U intertwine the actual coproduct. Therefore applying D_c to C_(l,l) is the same as replacing its inserted E_ll by the corresponding adjoint in W. Since E_ll commutes with K, the spectator terms cancel, and the inserted matrix is exactly f_l E_(l+1,l)+(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1))E_(l,l+1) -f_(l-1)E_(l,l-1)-(e_l/k_l)E_(l-1,l), (8) tensored with the spectator identity and conjugated by U. Its pairing is the left side of (7), with all four bands and their actual order. On the first cut the dual rows are, literally, e_(t,K)=K^-1 e_t K-e_t, e_(t,E)=K^-1 e_t E-E K^-1 e_t, e_(t,F)=e_t F-K F e_t K^-1. The K row has zero diagonal. Direct multiplication gives (e_(t,F)-e_(t,E)-2e_(t,K))_(a,a) =f_a beta_a-f_(a-1) beta_(a-1) -(e_a/k_a) beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1) =L_a-L_(a-1). (9) Only these diagonals pair with C_(l,l). This proves the first equality in (7); finite summation by parts gives the second. The proof applies to rectangular A,B and arbitrary fixed width. It uses the actual routed bands, not a scalar Ward operator assigned to an unrelated residual index. For clarity, the generic interior coefficient in (5) is e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)=zeta[Q^(a+1-N)-1]. At the root (5) becomes L_a=(1-Q^(a+1))[beta_a-q0 beta_(a+1)]. This shorter root formula must NOT be differentiated as the generic current: the omitted term is zeta Q^(a+1)(Q^-N-1) beta_(a+1), whose first derivative at zero is -2N q0 Q^(a+1) beta_(a+1). Equation (5) retains it and all higher genuine derivatives. ## 3. Finite-head integration by parts, with the interval ends Let R_l denote either expression on the right of (7), and let h_l be any specified finite-head weight. On EVERY actual subinterval 0<=L<=R<=d, sum_(l=L)^R h_l R_l =h_R M_R-h_L M_(L-1) +sum_(l=L)^(R-1)(h_l-h_(l+1)) M_l. (10) In particular a window's two current ends are retained. On the whole head interval the actual endpoint arrows make M_-1=M_d=0. For h=1 this says sum_l R_l=0. It also follows from sum_l J_(a,l)=z and sum_a(L_a-L_(a-1))=0. Neither proof says that the current has zero period on an arbitrarily selected relative subchain, or that one of its two ends contributes nontrivially. The identity is generic before any specialization. It may be differentiated to any fixed quantum order, with the derivatives of the actual U, inverse route, generator entries, pivots, coupons and any moving h retained. The same holds for a specified finite sum of channel assignments with its original coefficients. The original closed normalization remains F=D_N z and z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, with D_N=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. No extra derivative per band or per vertex is introduced by (7). ### The complete Fourier endpoint of the same actual channel At completeness let S be the cyclic physical-head shift and X_j its original Fourier projectors, (X_j)_(r,s)=Q^[j(s-r)]/N, eta_j=Q^j, j mod N. For the ROUTED first-slot channel C(X)=P_V[A U^-1(X tensor I)U B], the [complete Fourier source theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies: A U^-1 and U B are still actual covariant maps. Thus C(X_j)=z X_j. Its proof uses the actual root adjoint equations and C(I)=zI and also applies to the rectangular maps above. Since 1^T X_j=delta_(j,0)1^T, the legitimate first coherent functional still gives Tr(e_t C(X_j))=z delta_(j,0), exactly for every t. The actual cyclic generator formulas give D_c X_j=(eta_j-q0 eta_j^-1+2)X_j +(q0^-1 eta_j^-1-2)X_(j+1)-Q^-1 eta_j X_(j-1). (10a) Consequently this SAME sourced residual current has the exact three-node Fourier endpoint distribution Tr[e_t C(D_c X_j)] =z[(3-q0)delta_(j,0)+(q0-2)delta_(j,N-1) -delta_(j,1)]. (10b) Overlapping labels are added when N=2. The total of (10b) is zero. It is a statement about the original complete root source, not its generic normal, and no off-root cyclic endpoint is added. It locates the current at the complete resonance rather than at regular-node principal samples. Its coefficient remains the UNKNOWN whole scalar z; homogeneous Ward equations alone cannot determine it or show that the selected geometric component survives there. ## 4. The specified moving-period realization and its boundary chain There is a source-preserving residue realization of the coefficients in (6), not a new interpolation of those finite values. Expand their original generic tensors, including the routed crossings, in the specified finite white/cup/cap presentation. For U and U^-1 this is the FULL generic spectral expansion of each original crossing, with both small and large partner channels and their actual spectral denominators. It is not the restricted regular complete-circle sector sum. Use the actual large white polynomials and moving-period factorial with P=pi i/Log zeta. Keep every fixed generic spectral scalar and every integral character; clear a known intermediate scalar pole before taking the required higher jet. This is the source class of the [actual tensor connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). For each admissible assignment and each off-diagonal band retain its own primitive affine head lattice and original finite support. The band source has a fixed integral charge offset. At every allowed integer point its moving-period coefficient is the actual generic matrix entry. Its small product-cotangent torus therefore gives that same entry. Summing those tori reproduces T_t(p,q), and the displayed combinations reproduce M_l and (7), with no omitted normal. An original constant forbidden stratum remains zero rather than being assigned a 0/0 continuation. The first head may be left as the exact finite coherent sum (2). There is no need to invent a meromorphic interpolation of beta_a. For the remaining free coordinates x of an individual band let S(epsilon,x) be its specified meromorphic summand, Gamma its actual ordered residue cycle, and c(x)=product_j pi cot(pi x_j). For an integral translation v and an analytic retained weight w, change of variables gives the EXACT chain identity integral_Gamma c w (S_v-I)S =integral_Gamma c (S_-v w-w)S +integral_(Gamma+v-Gamma) c (S_-v w)S. (11) All periods use (2pi i)^(-n_free). The only fact used about c is its integer periodicity. When the last cycle difference is filled by an allowed annular chain, its value is the sum of the actual crossed source residues, with their orientations. All other crossed divisors, and any remaining relative ends, stay in that formula. At a coincident source/cotangent pole one must use the full finite part and complement derivative, as in the [actual degree-wall theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md). It is not enough to multiply a cup's simple residue by an assigned geometric scalar. Equation (7) is proved AFTER the original finite internal period contraction. The subsequent [common-band theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md) supplies its meromorphic interior Ward assembly on one primitive free-head lattice, with the actual charged insertions and full routed source. Its different original support cycles are still retained. Equation (10) keeps the exact finite-head ends of this contracted current, and (11) transports EACH specified band summand with those cycle differences. These formulas do not replace Gamma+v by Gamma merely because the source has a moving-P quasiperiod. The latter has its nontrivial rational gauge, characters and divisors even at finite normal order. ## 5. The literal source between Fourier nodes The actual routed channel has more information than its cyclic samples. Its genuine integral source preserves UNWRAPPED integer charge: if an inserted matrix is supported on row minus column equal to n, its output has that same charge. This follows before root specialization from the original crossings, cups, caps and typed degree equations. The fixed weight differences of rectangular A and B cancel. A bare root K-eigenvalue, which would identify n and n+N, is not used here. Put T_n=sum_(r-s=n)E_rs, with -d<=n<=d. Then X_j=N^-1 sum_n eta_j^(-n)T_n. Separating the DISTINCT output matrix diagonals in C(X_j)=zX_j proves C(T_n)=zT_n, -d<=n<=d, X(p)_(r,s)=p^(r-s)/N, C(X(p))=zX(p), p in C*. (12) In fact the j=0 identity suffices. X(p) is a specified finite rank-one matrix, not an interpolation assigned to contracted source values. Every physical position and every unwrapped band remains. Pairing with the same first coherent functional (2) gives exactly Tr[e_t C(X(p))]=z b_N(t,p), b_N(t,p)=(1-p^N)/[N(1-p)] (1-t+t/p)^(N-1). (13) The factor at p=1 is its removable value one. This formula follows by separately summing p^r and beta_s p^(-s), so it keeps the actual coherent degree d=N-1 and the original p=eta^-1 orientation. Whenever b_N(t,p)!=0, dividing THIS specified functional by b_N returns exactly the original root scalar z. This licenses that finite band-momentum boundary family; it does not license a general second diagonal functional or simultaneous evaluation of two heads. There is an exact whole-source absorption of this insertion. Let H=C(I)=P_V[AB]=zI, with the original pivots and all other source factors. Equation (12) gives Tr[e_t C(X(p))]/b_N(t,p)=Tr[e_eff H], e_eff=e_t X(p)/b_N(t,p), (e_eff)_(a,c)=beta_a(t)p^(-c)/(1-t+t/p)^d. (13a) Thus the right side is evaluated on the original white-cut network, without the extra U and U^-1 insertions. This is an identity AFTER the whole root contraction, not a local rule for moving X(p) through one crossing or moving a bare mark. No pivot has been added or removed. Moreover e_eff is exactly the existing normalized coherent kernel with z_coh=t/(1-t) and w=p^-1. Put D_p=diag(p^a). Directly, D_p^-1 e_eff D_p=e_(t_eff), t_eff=t/[p(1-t)+t]. (13b) The [original common diagonal gauge](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md) preserves t_eff and removes this common momentum p. Its one-cut physical map forgets the residual centralizer coordinate. Therefore the absorption supplies no additional pin of that coordinate: the two apparent parameters are one coherent position and the already present common diagonal gauge. The canceled formula for e_eff may extend across a Fourier zero of b_N, but this is not a generic-q removal of that zero or a contour transport statement. The source therefore has an exact boundary-scale test. In the first-slot chart r=1/(1-p)-b0 s, retain c0=b0 s and set p_N=1-1/(N rho+c0). For rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, and t,c0 in fixed compacts, direct expansion of the FINITE factor in (13) gives b_N(t,p_N)=rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t/rho)+O(N^-1). (14) The error is uniform and absolute, including its limiting zeros. On a compact avoiding those zeros it is relative, and b_N and its inverse have bounded size for large N. At the exact Fourier nodes p=Q^-j, j!=0, (13) instead vanishes exactly. Their limiting positions rho=1/(2pi i j) are precisely the zeros in (14). At rho=infinity the displayed limiting factor tends to one. No pointwise substitution of p into the whole internal source is used to prove these facts. In the absorbed one-cut expression, t_eff=t+t(1-t)/(N rho)+O(N^-2). Thus this scaling gives a small coherent-position tilt, not an independent centralizer condition. All of (12)--(14) is ROOT-ONLY. For the original moving-q channel write Delta(epsilon,p)=C_epsilon(X(p))-z(epsilon)X(p). Although Delta(0,p)=0, its genuine first quantum derivative need not vanish. The focused original-matrix checks below exhibit nonzero derivatives, including after the coherent pairing. They retain the actual route, endpoint arrows and generic pivot. Thus differentiating (13) would discard a source term. If a quantum-dependent p is used, the additional p derivative of Delta(0,p) is zero; it does not remove the genuine defect. All required normals still use the original generic channel and the source currents (5)--(11). More explicitly, for the SAME actual generic A,B,U and pivot, the identity retaining every quantum correction is Tr[e_t C_epsilon(X(p))]/b_N =Tr[e_eff H_epsilon]+Tr[e_t Delta(epsilon,p)]/b_N. (14a) Every genuine jet differentiates the full right side. The second term cannot be discarded by the root absorption (13a). Equation (14) is a matching condition for any proposed contracted hard-edge calculation. Its coefficient is the UNKNOWN whole z. Local nonzero white packets do not determine how their transverse periods and charged support cycles reproduce that coefficient. ## 6. What covariance fixes in the genuine normal There is an exact freedom at every N. Write tau_e(X)=Tr(g_e X), D_e=tau_e(I), with the original generic pivot, and put B_e(X)=D_e X-tau_e(X)I. (15) Cyclicity of trace gives tau_e(ad_E X)=tau_e(ad_F X)=0 and tau_e(ad_K X)=tau_e(X) for the actual adjoints above; I is invariant. Thus B_e is a regular covariant channel, made from the straight channel and pivotal evaluation and coevaluation. It has B_e(I)=0. At the root tau_0(T_n)=0 for every unwrapped band, including T_0=I since D_0=0. Adding c(e)B_e therefore preserves C_e(I)=z(e)I and every root identity (12), for any holomorphic c. Nevertheless the constant diagonal of X(p) gives EXACTLY B_e(X(p))=D_e[X(p)-I/N], B'_0(X(p))=nu_N[X(p)-I/N], Tr[e_t B'_0(X(p))]=nu_N[b_N(t,p)-1/N]. (16) Except at the displayed zeros, this changes the retained coherent normal without changing z. This is freedom in the linear span of actual covariant tensor channels; it does not assert that every such linear combination is a single connected augmented plat. For the original routed channel, charge conservation also implies that Delta(e,p) has zero diagonal at every e: its charge-zero input is I/N and C_e(I)=z(e)I. A diagonal first functional consequently kills this defect, but also kills every nonzero off-node band. That is a zero constraint, not a determination of a boundary coefficient. The freedom is visible in an exact family of connected source words. At N=2 retain q as the generic quantum parameter, eta=q^(1/2) with eta_0=exp(pi i/4), and the original positive crossing and pivot R=eta Rhat, Rhat=[[1,0,0,0],[0,0,q^-1,0], [0,q^-1,1-q^-2,0],[0,0,0,1]], g=diag(-q,-q^-1), D=-q-q^-1. (17) These are the d=1 specialization of the original highest-weight R and pivotal closure. For any odd k>=3 choose A=R^(k-1), B=U=R. The actual routed channel is C_k(X)=ptr_g[R^(k-2)(X tensor I)R^2], C_k=eta^k Chat_k, z_k=eta^k zhat_k. Set lambda=-q^-2, u_j=sum_(r<j)lambda^r and v_j=1-u_j. The middle block of Rhat has roots 1,lambda, so its kth power is u_k times that block plus v_k I. The two literal pivotal terms of Chat_k(E10) are -q u_(k-1) and -q^-3. It follows that zhat_k=-q-q^-1 v_k, psihat_k=Chat_k(E10)_(1,0)-zhat_k =(q^-1-q^-5)u_(k-2), Chat_k(X)=(zhat_k+psihat_k)X-psihat_k tau_q(X)I/D. (18) For the last formula, the actual generic adjoint module End(V_1) splits as C I plus ker tau_q; the latter is generated by E10 and its E-adjoint ladder and has dimension three. Equivalently (18) follows by multiplying the displayed middle-block powers. Its apparently singular quotient denotes the regular literal source. Since tau_q(X(p))=D/2, the actual defect is exactly eta^k psihat_k[X(p)-I/2]. At q=i, zhat_k=-ki, psihat_k=0, partial_e psihat_k=-4i(k-2), [partial_e Delta_k(E10)]_(1,0)/z_k(0)=4(k-2)/k. (19) Here Delta_k(E10) means C_k(E10)-z_k E10. The Cartan factor eta_0^k is restored in both numerator and denominator; its derivative multiplies psihat_k(i)=0. Any retained nonzero regular exterior framing scalar has the same cancellation in this ratio. The ratios are 4/3 for k=3 and 12/5 for k=5. In particular C_5-(5/3)eta_0^2 C_3 has root scalar zero but nonzero extreme-band normal (-16i/3)eta_0^5. Both individual words are original connected odd two-braid closures with the same cut, pivot and route. For t=2/3,p=2, b_2=1 and the paired defect is HALF the extreme-band coefficient, giving ratios 2/3 and 6/5 instead. Covariance does identify the extra datum. For ANY regular covariant N=2 channel with C(I)=zI and the root identities (12), the same generic adjoint decomposition gives (18) with a scalar psi vanishing at the root. Since D'_0=-2i and g_0[0,0]=-i, C_0(E00)-z_0 E00=-psi'_0 I/2, Delta'_0(X(p))=psi'_0[X(p)-I/2]. (20) Thus this normal is determined by an additional ROOT open-diagonal source period, not by the whole-source scalar z. More generally the defect is independent of the regular covariant lift when the FULL root channel is fixed. Suppose C_e and Ctilde_e use the SAME actual generator family and fixed highest weights, are regular covariant, preserve unwrapped charge, and C_0=Ctilde_0 as maps on End(V_d). The quotient L_e=(C_e-Ctilde_e)/e is then regular, covariant and scalar on I. The proof in Sections 3--4 of the [universal root theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies to this quotient: it uses only linearity, root adjoint covariance and L(I)=zI. Our actual root generators are precisely its M=1 generators, with BOTH missing endpoint arrows zero. Its K row, highest-input E recurrence and physical F induction therefore give L_0(X_j)=(z'_0-ztilde'_0)X_j; its Fourier-row basis gives the full matrix identity. No realization of L_e as one closed word is needed. Unwrapped charge separates the T_n as in (12), so Delta'_0(p)=Deltatilde'_0(p). (21) This requires equality of the whole open root map, not merely its scalar closure, nor equality of individual small/large root columns. Equations (15)--(21) rule out determining it from covariance and root absorption alone. They neither refute the hyperbolic conjecture nor show that the additional period cannot be controlled on the selected geometry. ## 7. The remaining equation at the framing diagonal The new ingredient relative to the old formal Ward ideal is the source-defined M_l in (6), including the off-diagonal routed bands and its finite endpoint chain. Its principal D_c field is the residual centralizer direction. A stationary pushforward would have to send THIS current and THIS chain, with the coherent first head and original complement, to the residual framing current. In particular neither the finite values J_(a,l) nor the nonzero local stationary density determine the residue at the framing diagonal. No continuous second-head current has been defined by interpolating (7). To obtain the desired framing coefficient one must identify the pushforward of the prescribed band periods (6) and the endpoint/divisor chain (10),(11) with that diagonal current, and compute its actual relative coefficient. A global cycle or nonzero endpoint intersection is not proved here. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_residual_framing_current.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_residual_framing_current_results.json) check 19 actual braid/complete-circle sources, including rectangular one-to-three-head birth/death cuts: 326 original routed band value/first jet coefficients, 134 flux coefficients, 334 weighted interval/jet identities, and 48 nonzero retained generic-normal corrections. Separate original-matrix checks verify 1177 full Fourier-projector channel entries and 67 three-node complete current values. The off-node extension checks 2087 unwrapped Toeplitz entries, 801 literal rank-one source entries and 57 coherent pairings. It retains 588 nonzero genuine first-normal entries and 54 nonzero coherent normal defects. Twelve boundary-scale checks include a limiting Fourier zero. The whole-source absorption has 114 actual root/first-jet checks and 801 effective coherent-gauge entries; 139 symbolic kernel identities, 139 gauge identities, six trace normalizations and the first position tilt are checked independently. The genuine-normal extension additionally checks the literal N=2 crossing and pivot jets, the factorized arbitrary-k channel identity, and the full generic channels, restored normal ratios and open-diagonal adapter for five odd braid powers. These finite checks accompany the all-k block-power proof (18), rather than replacing it. Symbolic checks verify the universal integer-shift chain rule and its resonant cotangent finite part. They do not audit an off-grid Ward identity or a stationary framing pushforward. Finite currents, off-grid Ward identities and a geometric period are distinct levels of the argument. The off-node result concerns the finite rank-one source, unwrapped charge and root boundary profile. It does not determine z, differentiate its root factor, or select a transverse period. The absorption identities (13a),(13b),(14a) reduce the whole source to the existing one-cut coherent family; they do not independently localize the residual framing direction. Freedom in the normal tensor span is distinct from freedom among two actual connected words. Independence of a lift is not determination by a scalar root coordinate, and no geometric-period obstruction follows.

title: A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights
status: Exact braided change of cut with genuine pivotal derivatives
text: # A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights 30 October 2026. finite-source theorem. The literal second identity cut cannot be replaced by another normalized boundary state, or even by an untransported pivotal marginal. There is an exact repair: retain the actual braid carrying the selected wire to the exposed position. Its conjugated matrix-unit insertion gives a second co-source for the SAME whole marked scalar. The original pivot, all exchange bands, and all genuine quantum derivatives remain explicit. This is a global finite-source identity. It does not prove that this co-source has a nonzero coefficient on the selected geometric framing fiber, or replace the two-cut tensor by simultaneous point evaluation. ## 1. The genuine generic source and its original first cut Fix N, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). Use the original ordinary highest-weight-d module and the ACTUAL generic physical cup. Its pivotal matrix is g(epsilon)=(-1)^d K(epsilon), g_a(epsilon)=(-1)^d zeta^(d-2a), D_N(epsilon)=Tr g=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. (1) At the root this is the original K^(1-N), on every physical index. Away from the root the latter frozen power is a different germ. In particular the derivative in (1) is (d-2a)g_a, not (1-N)(d-2a)g_a. All assertions below use (1). Take an actual parallel physical level with b ordered heads and write the cut word as A B, with matrices composing right to left. Cups and caps elsewhere are their original maps. On the complete source use the regular Hopf lifts of its root complete-circle sectors, or the proved exactly equivalent literal polynomial presentation WITH all its moving scalar adapters. A bare root-value substitution is not a generic lift. Let G=g tensor ... tensor g, P(C)=Tr_(heads 2,...,b)[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)C]. The exposed endomorphism is H=P(A B)=z(epsilon)I. This follows from the actual generic Hopf covariance and the distinct K weights and nonzero interior F arrows. Its root marked value is z(0), while the ordinary closed source is F=Tr(G A B)=D_N z, z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, nu_N=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1). (2) This is the same original exposed mark and trace normal as in the [full source theorem](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). The retained exterior normalization and peripheral factors multiply both sides; they are not changed here. The formulas also apply at an actual Morse level after transporting its oriented objects with their literal duality maps. A braid route between different ordered boundary objects then includes those maps. The following displayed parallel-head formulas specify the simplest case; one must not replace a typed route by an unclocked permutation. ## 2. What the literal second identity cut does not satisfy Insert E_bb on a chosen intermediate wire and keep the original first cut open. With the second index renamed j to avoid confusion with the number of heads, set J_(a,j)=[P(A E_jj^(slot) B)]_(a,a). (3) Summing the actual identity edge gives sum_j J_(a,j)=z, (1/N)sum_(a,j)J_(a,j)=z. (4) It follows that the first head can be fixed at ANY actual physical a0, giving z=sum_j J_(a0,j), with no new scalar. But the column sums need not be constant, and multiplying the first index by g_a does not fix that defect. The old exposed marked row is not a Hopf cap on an arbitrary partially summed tensor. For a concrete exact example, use the original three-positive-crossing two-strand word at N=3, cut after its first crossing and select its second wire. In the audit's cyclotomic field F_1009, with every original pivotal factor retained and the common exterior scalar omitted on both sides, its row sums are (227,227,227), while its column sums are (758,555,377). With g=(374,1,634), its pivotal column sums are (903,221,894). Thus neither proposed second marginal is a source identity. These examples only distinguish the formulas; the correct identity is proved next at every generic parameter and every level. ## 3. The actual braided projector and its two exact marginals Number the selected wire by j=0,...,b-1. Let R_i be the actual generic crossing between slots i-1 and i. Choose the recorded route U=R_1 R_2 ... R_j, U^-1=R_j^-1 ... R_2^-1 R_1^-1. (5) Thus R_j acts first and the selected wire moves left one position at a time. A different specified signed braid route is allowed with its literal inverse; the route is data. Every crossing and its full scalar is retained. Put X_l=U^-1(E_ll tensor I)U, J^U_(a,l)=[P(A X_l B)]_(a,a). (6) The X_l are actual mutually orthogonal idempotents with sum I. They are GENERALLY NOT local matrix units on the selected wire. Their full exchange and prefix bands are indispensable. The universal identities are J^U 1=z 1, g^T J^U=z g^T. (7) For the first, sum X_l=I and use H=zI. For the second define C_new=U B A U^-1. It is an actual Hopf intertwiner, so P(C_new)=z_new I. Every factor commutes with the total pivot G. Cyclicity of the FULL ordinary trace therefore gives D_N z_new=Tr(G U B A U^-1)=Tr(G B A)=D_N z. Cancel the nonzero generic function D_N before root specialization. Both open endomorphisms are regular, so z_new=z through epsilon=0. For each l, the same trace calculation now gives sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) =Tr(G A X_l B) =Tr[G U B A U^-1(E_ll tensor I)] =g_l z. (8) This proves (7) with the actual order of U and its inverse. It uses the whole closed trace, not movement of a bare root mark. Since g_l is always a unit, it supplies the exact second co-source z=g_l^-1 sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) (9) at any physical l. The original first-cut source remains z=(1/N)sum_(a,l)J^U_(a,l). The formula is valid for arbitrary fixed complete-channel assignments and their finite sum, with their original signs and scalar weights. Differentiating it retains the actual U, U^-1, g and coupon derivatives; no unproved generic normal is suppressed. The two cuts need not have the same Morse width. More generally let V=V_d^tensor b and W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and use the actual rectangular covariant maps A:W->V and B:V->W. The selected route U and X_l act on W; use P_V in (6). Covariance gives G_V A=A G_W and G_W B=B G_V. The entire trace step is then Tr_V(G_V A X_l B)=Tr_W(G_W B A X_l). The ordinary partial closures P_V(A B) and P_W(U B A U^-1) are scalar on the same exposed simple object. Cancelling the SAME generic D_N proves (7)-(9) unchanged. This includes actual intervening births and deaths, with their original cups, caps and typed duality transport; it introduces no new pivot on the second identity edge. At the root g^T1=D_N(0)=0. Thus (9) is an essentially canceling pivotal co-source, not another positive normalized row. Equations (7) do not determine the individual entries of J^U: perturbations Z satisfying Z1=0 and g^T Z=0 remain. This kernel has dimension (N-1)^2: it is precisely Hom(C^N/span(1),ker(g^T)). It cannot be removed by two independent point evaluations. ## 4. Root characters and the change of cut-density line There are two distinct continuations to complex magnetic indices. The finite generic matrix pivot in (1) is defined on physical integer a. The specified actual CUP continuation instead gives, by its literal ratio p_d(a,d-a)/p_d(d-a,a), ghat(epsilon;a)=(-1)^d exp(2pi i a) zeta^(d-2a). (10) It agrees with (1) at every physical integer a and every epsilon. At the root, for complex a, it is exactly the marked literal power q0^[(1-N)(d-2a)]. Consequently ghat(0;a)/ghat(0;l) =exp[2pi i(a-l)] A_l/A_a, A_a=exp(2pi i a/N), A_l=exp(2pi i l/N). (11) A_l is the clock of the new FIRST head after the recorded braid U; it is not automatically the clock of the old bare selected wire. The integer-linear character is one on the physical grid, but not on a continued complex magnetic chart. Nor may the root power in (11) be differentiated as if it were the generic cup germ (10). This distinction is independent of the matrix identity (8). The actual geometric cut forms have the corresponding algebraic line transition: writing the conjugation-invariant form on the ordered-flag surface as Omega=-Tr(Pi dPi wedge dPi), their fixed-cut forms are Omega_cut,i=-A_i Omega. Their ratio is A_l/A_a. Thus the algebraic factor in (11) is exactly the expected change of cut-density line, WITH its source character still present. This does not identify the whole continued tensor, its integration cycle, or its boundary residues merely from equality of that ratio. ## 5. Remaining fiber and source problem The braided correction (6) is a concrete finite source operation; it neither normalizes away the kernel in (7) nor supplies an asymptotic bound for that kernel. Its added routes are actual matrices and may carry substantial magnetic growth before contraction. A geometric framing reduction must still transport this entire co-source, including the exchange bands, into the residual centralizer fiber and its original relative ends. The nonzero unit g_l^-1 in (9) is an exact normalization of the whole scalar, not a proof that a particular local geometric block survives this functional. Existing two-cut current identities retain the relevant band and endpoint data; no replacement by a trace-one state on the second identity edge is made. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter_results.json) check 16 original braid/complete-circle sources at parallel widths two and three, 476 actual adapted entry value/first-jet coefficients, and 116 weighted column value/first-jet coefficients. They also retain the failed literal second marginals, check the original generic crossing intertwiners and their inverses, and verify the whole-source trace normal. These finite checks supplement the generic proof; they do not test a geometric fiber integral. These identities do not assert that the selected geometric fiber survives contraction with the retained co-source.

title: Exact charged bridge phase and a further original-source selection rule
text: # Exact charged bridge phase and a further original-source selection rule 28 October 2026. After exact signed overbridge elimination, all quadratic interior-clock phases telescope. The COMPLETE bridge is one charge-d cyclic beta product with explicit linear weights. This gives its full marked complex action. Positive absolute entropy does not automatically make that action stationary. An actual post-elimination 5_2 source fiber has nonzero phase flux at its unique conditional absolute maximum. More constructively, its remaining finite Fourier sum vanishes EXACTLY on that entire high-entropy clock region. The vanishing is a new complementary charge constraint, not a discarded small term or a counterexample to the volume conjecture. ## 1. Exact normalization and complete phase telescoping Use the original signed bridge theorem and its full normalizers in [the source-preserving unwinding note](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md). Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^(-1). A bridge has m encounters, signs sigma_j, monotone clocks h_1>=...>=h_m, and original port parameters a_j,b_j with a_j b_j=Q^2 x. Let u_j be the spectator output, z6 for a positive encounter and z7 for a negative one. The signed table gives EXACTLY c_j=kappa^(sigma_j)/N *a_j^(-h_j) q^(-h_j^2+(1+sigma_j)h_j). (1) For a positive encounter u_j=Q^(-h_j)/(x a_j); for a negative one u_j=Qx/a_j. Substituting either in the proved original c_j gives (1), including every sign and half-step. Combining all c_j, link monomials and Gaussian phases, the complete non-Pochhammer/non-binomial prefactor is kappa^w/N *Zin^(-h_1) *product_(j<m) a_j^(-(h_j-h_(j+1))) *a_m^(-h_m) *(-1)^(sum_(j=2)^m h_j) *q^(-h_1^2+h_1+sum_j sigma_j h_j), w=sum_j sigma_j. (2) All interior quadratic clocks have cancelled, not been dropped by taking absolute values. Define NONNEGATIVE integer charges n_0=d-h_1, n_j=h_j-h_(j+1) (1<=j<m), n_m=h_m, sum_(r=0)^m n_r=d, w_r=sum_(j=1)^r sigma_j. Put t_0=1, t_r=(-1)^r q^(2+w_r)/(Zin a_r), 1<=r<=m, z_0=b_1/Zin, z_r=a_r b_(r+1)Q^(-1)=x^(-1)a_r/a_(r+1), 1<=r<m, z_m=a_m Zout. Then the ENTIRE original conditioned bridge coefficient is B_gamma=kappa^w product_(r=0)^m [(z_r;Q)_(n_r)/F_(n_r) *t_r^(n_r)], F_n=(Q;Q)_n. (3) This identity includes every original N factor. To prove it, the telescoping q-binomial product is F_(h_1)/[F_(h_m)product F_(h_j-h_(j+1))]. Reflect F_(h_1)F_(d-h_1)=N(-1)^(h_1)q^(h_1(h_1+1)). Its N cancels the 1/N in (2), its quadratic cancels -h_1^2, and its sign combines into (-1)^(sum_j h_j). Finally sum_j h_j=sum_(r>=1)r n_r and sum_j sigma_j h_j=sum_(r>=1)w_r n_r. This proves (3). The exact parameters obey z_(r-1)t_(r-1)=Q^(epsilon_r)t_r, epsilon_r=(1-sigma_r)/2, z_m t_m=Tend=(-1)^m q^(2+w) Zout/Zin. (4) These are source identities, not an imposed balancing condition. ## 2. The full leading COMPLEX bridge action Write T_r=n_r/N, U_r=exp(2pi*i*T_r). The exact charge is sum T_r=1-1/N; its leading equation is sum T_r=1. On a fixed nondegenerate logarithmic cell the marked complex action is W_gamma=sum_r [Li_2(z_r)-Li_2(z_r U_r) -Li_2(1)+Li_2(U_r) +Log U_r Log t_r]. (5) The full coefficient has exp[N W_gamma/(2pi*i)] times its specified subexponential density, with kappa^w still EXACTLY outside. If one expands the original complete kappa as well, its leading action is the known real constant -pi^2 w. It changes no stationarity equation. The q^(2+w_r) factors in (3) remain in the exact source and its finite-level phase; they affect (5) at subleading order for fixed word length. Branches in (5) mean the continuation of each actual finite Pochhammer arc. Equivalently define its leading logarithm by integrating Log(1-z exp(2pi*i*t)) along that arc; do not give the endpoint dilogarithms unrelated principal branches. The factorial starting at 1 has its usual integrable endpoint. The full differential, before imposing actual spectator-flow dependencies, is dW=sum_r { Log[t_r(1-z_r U_r)/(1-U_r)] dLog U_r +Log[(1-z_r U_r)/(1-z_r)] dLog z_r +Log U_r dLog t_r }. (6) Thus the Gaussian/monomial source has not disappeared from the action. It is now the explicit Log U Log t coupling. If the bridge parameters a_r are independent while its charges vary, constrained charge criticality requires t_r(1-z_r U_r)/(1-U_r)=Lambda, U_r=(Lambda-t_r)/(Lambda-z_r t_r). At leading order (4) gives z_r t_r=t_(r+1). Hence product U_r=(Lambda-1)/(Lambda-Tend). The charge equation product U_r=1 therefore requires Tend=1 for a finite regular interior critical point. Generic endpoint data do not satisfy it. This is a conditional phase-flux test, not a global knot critical equation: the actual anchored flow makes some a_r depend on other charges and supplies the extra terms in (6). There is an exact finite counterpart. If the a_r really are held independent during summation over all charges, write U_z(v)=sum_(n=0)^d (z;Q)_n v^n/F_n. Then sum_(sum n=d) B_gamma =kappa^w [v^d] U_Tend(v) product_(sigma_r=-1)(1-t_r v)^(-1). (7) Proof: modulo v^N the finite quantum binomial theorem is U_z(v)=P(zv)/P(v), with the original finite Euler P. Using P(Qv)=P(v)/(1-v), equations (4) telescope the product. This independent-parameter sum must not be applied to a whole knot while ignoring the actual spectator-flow dependencies. ## 3. Real angular entropy and phase, with every sheet retained On the original fixed-central grids, |z_r| and |t_r| differ from one by O(1/N). Write their leading arguments as z_r=exp(2pi*i*alpha_r), t_r=exp(2pi*i*tau_r). Let J(s)=-D(exp(2pi*i*s))/(2pi), periodic, and let chi(s)=({s}^2-{s})/2. The leading logarithmic modulus per N and phase per N are E_gamma=sum_r [J(alpha_r+T_r)-J(alpha_r)-J(T_r)], Theta_gamma/pi=sum_r [chi(alpha_r+T_r)-chi(alpha_r)-chi(T_r)+2T_r tau_r]. (8) The phase includes the c_j monomials and original Gaussian phases through tau_r. The omitted kappa phase is label-independent and specified above. Equation (8) is a piecewise quadratic real phase on every actual support cell, not a positive weight. At the usual nonzero radial grid regularization the errors are O(log N) in log magnitude; on endpoint-free cells the neighbor phase derivatives converge with O(1/N) error. On a positive arc 0<alpha_r<alpha_r+T_r<1, (8) reduces to Theta_gamma=pi sum_r T_r(alpha_r+2tau_r). Choosing the actual lifted relation alpha_r=tau_(r+1)-tau_r there gives Theta_gamma=pi sum_r T_r(tau_r+tau_(r+1)). Its internal phase derivative is pi(T_(r-1)+T_r), strictly positive when the adjacent charges are positive. A real absolute optimizer is therefore not automatically a complex stationary point. The corresponding absolute entropy is the sum of twice the ideal tetrahedron volumes with angles pi*T_r, pi*alpha_r, pi*(1-alpha_r-T_r). These form a genuine positive concave angle chart, but the retained phase remains. ## 4. A new complementary-charge rule for an actual remaining wire Consider an actual under-output followed by a reduced overbridge-input on the SAME ordinary wire. Suppose its full dependence is g(Z)=Z^(r-H)(aZ;Q)_(d-r)(b/Z;Q)_(d-H), ab=Q, 0<=r,H<=d. (9) Then the exact remaining constant term is CT g=(-1)^(d-r) a^(H-r) *Q^[(d-r)(d-r-1)/2-H(d-H)] *[r choose d-H]_Q. (10) In particular it is ZERO unless r+H>=d. No geometric norm is divided out in (10). This is a new source-support selection in addition to overbridge monotonicity. Here is an elementary proof, without assuming a q-Chu theorem. Put t=aZ, L=d-r, K=d-H. Reflect the second product: (Q/t;Q)_K=(-1)^K Q^(K(K+1)/2)t^(-K) (tQ^(H+1);Q)_K. Thus CT g is a^(H-r)(-1)^K Q^(K(K+1)/2) times [t^L](t;Q)_L(tQ^(H+1);Q)_K. If r+H<d, the product is (1-t^N) times a polynomial of degree<L, so this coefficient vanishes. If r+H>=d it is (1-t^N)/(tQ^L;Q)_(H-L+1). Finite q-Pascal gives its t^L coefficient Q^(L^2)[H choose L]_Q. Root factorial reflection turns the result into (10); the parity factor is exactly Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), also at even N. For r+H<=d-1 the stronger root-circle identity is g(Z)=(-1)^(d-H)a^(-(d-H))Q^((d-H)(d-H+1)/2) *Z^(r-d)(1-(aZ)^N) *(Q^(H+1)aZ;Q)_(d-1-r-H). (11) On the original grid the norm 1-(aZ)^N is a fixed nonzero scalar. Its remaining Fourier powers lie from r-d through -H-1, entirely negative and strictly above -N. Thus the original N-point SUM, not merely a formal constant term, is exactly zero in this region. ## 5. Whole original post-reduction sanity check: 5_2 Use the independently identified original word [1,1,1,2,-1,2] and its actual averaged cut and two pivots in the [post-bridge source audit](../experiments/audit_bridge_reduced_absolute_envelope.py). Its overpaths are [0],[1],[2,3],[4],[5]; wire 8 has already been eliminated in the genuine two-crossing bridge. Keep the audit's rational labels, but change label6/N from 9/10 to 89/100. Then the underclock of crossing1 is r/N=1/100, while the first reduced overbridge clock is H/N=59/100 and the second is 35/100. The nontrivial bridge inequality is strict. The remaining wire5 occurs only in the under-output of crossing1 and the input of that reduced bridge. Their actual parameters satisfy ab=Q: a=Q^(r+1)/z3 and b=z6/x, while z6=x z3 Q^(-r). Every other crossing, reduced bridge factor and original boundary coupon is independent of wire5. Thus (9)--(11) apply to the ENTIRE remaining source, with its full scalar. The label5/N=1/10 lies at the unique conditional global absolute maximum in this fiber. Indeed its one remaining Pochhammer has asymptotic length 1-r/N-H/N=2/5; the two endpoints are conjugate there. Yet its phase flux under label5 -> label5+1 tends to pi(1+r/N-H/N)=21pi/50 !=0 modulo 2pi. (12) The complete reduced entropy at this supported source point is 2.546436873747266..., much larger than the geometric knot-volume rate. This does not refute the volume conjecture: (11) shows its conditional source sum is EXACTLY ZERO. The large real envelope is removed by a further source constraint, not by a norm estimate. For a direct phase calculation on this cell, the whole source's leading phase obeys (1/pi) partial_(label5/N) Theta =xi3-2xi6+xi7+1=21/50. The original cap/pivot factor is nonzero and independent of wire5; common kappa/framing phases are retained and cancel from this neighbor ratio. The audit compares the whole actual finite-source ratio with (9), not a newly chosen co-source or a pre-elimination summand. The lesson is constructive. Exact bridge reduction gives a positive entropy chart, but no automatic real saddle. One must also perform or control the remaining anchor contractions. Equation (10) proves one actual new complementary-charge selection; its condition ab=Q is typed and must be checked before applying it elsewhere. No claim that all remaining seams have this form is made. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_bridge_charge_phase.py) checks the exact charged identity, its optional independent-parameter height sum, the complementary seam for every clock, and the whole original post-bridge phase/source fiber.

title: Actual cap residues at the Pachner norm wall
text:
# Actual cap residues at the Pachner norm wall 28 October 2026. The actual source and co-source give an explicit residue functional at the simultaneous norm wall of [the last-move calculation](oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.md). For a full holomorphic product it retains its original matrix corner. For split meromorphic terms it retains a finite list of source jets, with bounds uniform in the level. The cap is not a projector onto geometric edge winding one. The results below use exactly the source frames and residue constants of [the cap-wall theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md). They do not replace an invariant or assign an arbitrary source to the geometric triangulation. The original geometric exterior still needs its typed comparison with these local matrix coordinates. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.py) checks 148 direct finite-product identities in cyclotomic fields, the generic first and second central jets, and the uniform-bound constants. Its [saved results](../experiments/actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge_results.json) separate central-meromorphic, fixed-cover-pole, and global-source scope. For the original word, its Ward corner is used only after the full intertwining contraction has been assembled. These residue formulas do not authorize applying that Ward replacement separately to a cyclic/sewing sector whose full original marked row is different. ## 1. Coincident residues reproduce the original corners Fix $N\ge2$, $d=N-1$, $Q=e^{2\pi i/N}$ and put $$ \varepsilon=a^N,\quad \delta=(1-\varepsilon)^{1/N},\quad u_0=\delta,\quad u_d=Q\delta, $$ with the branches equal to $1$ at $\varepsilon=0$. For $s,t\in\{0,d\}$ use the original Fermat frames $$ P_n^{s}(a)=  rac{a^n}{\prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-u_sQ^j)},\qquad L_m^{t}(a)= a^{-m}\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-u_tQ^j). 	ag{1} $$ Their original residue constants are $$ \alpha_0= eta_0=1,\qquad \alpha_d=1-Q,\qquad eta_d=N. $$ Write $\sigma_0=	au_0=0$, $\sigma_d=1$, $	au_d=d$, and $D_{ts}=\sigma_s+	au_t$. For any matrix $O(a)$ holomorphic at zero, $$  oxed{\quad  rac1{\alpha_s eta_t} \operatorname{Res}_{a=0} a^{D_{ts}-1} L^t(a)O(a)P^s(a)\,da =\langle e_t,O(0)e_sangle. \quad} 	ag{2} $$ Indeed $P^d_d=(1-Q)a^{-1}+O(a^{N-1})$, while $P^d_n=O(a^n)$ for $n<d$. Also $L^d_d=Na^{-d}+O(a)$ and $L^d_m=O(a^{-m})$ for $m<d$. At the zero corner $P^0_0=L^0_0=1$, whereas $P^0_n=O(a^n)$ and $L^0_m=O(a^{N-m})$ for $m,n>0$. Thus exactly $(m,n)=(t,s)$ has the maximal required pole; every other term has at least one additional power of $a$. Multiplication by a holomorphic $O(a)$ cannot create another residue. For $s=t=d$, (2) is specifically $$  rac1{N(1-Q)} \operatorname{Res}a^{N-1}L^d(a)O(a)P^d(a)\,da =O_{dd}(0). 	ag{3} $$ This equals the actual independent input/output cap residues. It is an equality of residue functionals on the stated class, not a pullback of two differential forms to their diagonal. For individually singular factors the order of regularization must therefore still be proved; it cannot be inferred by substituting the same parameter into two residue formulas. Taking $O=I$ in (3) gives exactly one. The marked wall has its original unit augmentation. ## 2. Exact source jets for meromorphic split terms Suppose now $O=O(\varepsilon)$ is meromorphic, with pole order at most a fixed integer $p$: $$ O(\varepsilon)=\sum_{r=-p}^{\infty}O_r\varepsilon^r. $$ Let $m(n)=n+t-s mod N$, valued in $0,\ldots,d$. The residue functional in (2) is exactly $$ \mathcal R_{ts}(O) =\operatorname{CT}_{\varepsilon=0} \sum_{n=0}^{d}H^{ts}_n(\varepsilon) O_{m(n),n}(\varepsilon). 	ag{4} $$ All factors in this formula are retained. Direct telescoping in (1) gives the following kernels: | Input $s$ | Output $t$ | Kernel | |---|---|---| | $0$ | $0$ | $H_0=1$; for $n>0$, $H_n=(1-\delta)/(1-Q^n\delta)$ | | $d$ | $d$ | $H_n=\varepsilon(1-Q\delta)/[N(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1}\delta)]$ | | $d$ | $0$ | $H_d=(1-Q\delta)/(1-Q)$; for $n<d$, $H_n=(1-\delta)(1-Q\delta)/[(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1}\delta)]$ | | $0$ | $d$ | $H_0=\varepsilon/[N(1-\delta)]$; for $n>0$, $H_n=\varepsilon/[N(1-Q^n\delta)]$ | The quotients at $\varepsilon=0$ are their removable values. Every kernel is holomorphic there and $H^{ts}_n(0)=1$ exactly when $n=s$, and is zero otherwise. If $H^{ts}_n=\sum_{r\ge0}H^{ts}_{r,n}\varepsilon^r$, then $$  oxed{\quad \mathcal R_{ts}(O)= \sum_{r=0}^{p}\sum_{n=0}^{d} H^{ts}_{r,n}(O_{-r})_{m(n),n}. \quad} 	ag{5} $$ Thus a full regularized product uses only its original corner. Its singular summands can also use $H_1,H_2,\ldots,H_p$. Those terms disappear only when their corresponding pole coefficients cancel in the complete product or source current. For the marked $d	o d$ corner, write $K=H^{dd}$. At $n
e d$, $$ K_{1,n}= rac1{N(1-Q^{n+1})},\qquad K_{2,n}= rac{Q-Q^{n+1}} {N^2(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1})^2}. 	ag{6} $$ At $n=d$, $$ K_{0,d}=1,\quad K_{1,d}= rac{Q}{N(1-Q)}- rac{N-1}{2N},\quad K_{2,d}=- rac{N^2-1}{12N^2}. 	ag{7} $$ The second-order coefficient includes the cubic expansion of $\delta$ before the removable denominator is divided. ## 3. Uniform bounds: no exponential source-jet cost Take $ho=1/16$. On $|\varepsilon|\leho$, $$ |\delta-1|\le rac{2|\varepsilon|}{N}. $$ For a nontrivial root $Q^r$, put $\ell=\operatorname{dist}(r,N\mathbb Z)\ge1$. The elementary sine bound gives $|1-Q^r|\ge4\ell/N$, and hence $$ |1-Q^r\delta|\ge rac{3\ell}{N},\qquad \left| rac{1-Q\delta}{1-Q}ight|<2. 	ag{8} $$ All nonexceptional entries of the table are therefore bounded by $(4/3)|\varepsilon|/\ell$. The two removable quotients use $$ A(\varepsilon)= rac{\varepsilon}{N(1-\delta)} = rac{1+\delta+\cdots+\delta^{N-1}}N, \qquad |A|\le1+ho. $$ In particular $$ K_d=A+ rac{\varepsilon Q}{N(1-Q)},\qquad |K_d|\le1+ho+ho/4<2. $$ The remaining wrap value $(1-Q\delta)/(1-Q)$ is also bounded by two. Consequently, for **all four actual cap channels**, all $N\ge2$, and all indices, $$ \sup_{|\varepsilon|\le1/16}|H^{ts}_n(\varepsilon)|\le2, \qquad |H^{ts}_{r,n}|\le2\cdot16^r. 	ag{9} $$ For example, in the original flat Euclidean matrix basis, $$  oxed{\quad |\mathcal R_{ts}(O)| \le2N\sum_{r=0}^{p}16^r\|O_{-r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}. \quad} 	ag{10} $$ The factor $N$ can be replaced by a trace-norm bound on each selected cyclic diagonal. Independent source variables tensor: for a fixed word and fixed pole orders their combined extraction has polynomial cost in $N$. This is a bound relative to the actual Laurent coefficient norms. It does not turn exponentially large input currents into small ones without their exact cancellation. Nor is the norm asserted unchanged under an exponentially conditioned fusion frame. The [actual sewing theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md) retains at most second-order poles per Euler variable. When such an actual matrix term is expressed in the stated central local coordinate, (5)--(10) give its exact cap correction and a bound for the finite source-jet pushforward. They do not authorize dropping the sewing poles or their finite-part prescription. ### Fixed pole order on the Fermat cover, without central descent There is a complementary statement for an actual matrix that is meromorphic in $a$ itself. Put $$ \widehat P_s=a^{\sigma_s}P^s/\alpha_s,\qquad \widehat L_t=a^{	au_t}L^t/ eta_t,\qquad J_{ts}(a)=\widehat P_s(a)\widehat L_t(a). $$ These are the regular original cap frames. The uniform cap-wall estimate gives an absolute $C$ such that their Euclidean norms are at most $C$ on $|a|\le1/(16N)$. Consequently the rank-one kernel has trace norm at most $C^2$ there. If $O(a)=\sum_{\ell=-p}^{\infty}A_\ell a^\ell$, then exactly $$ \mathcal R_{ts}(O)= \sum_{r=0}^{p}\operatorname{tr}(A_{-r}J_{ts,r}), \qquad \|J_{ts,r}\|_1\le C^2(16N)^r. 	ag{10a} $$ This follows from the original formula $\operatorname{Res}\widehat L_tO\widehat P_s\,da/a$ and Cauchy's coefficient estimate in trace norm. Thus $$ |\mathcal R_{ts}(O)| \le C^2\sum_{r=0}^{p}(16N)^r\|A_{-r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}. 	ag{10b} $$ For $0<r<N$ the actual endpoint jets are especially explicit. Writing $F_r=(Q;Q)_r$ and $F_r^-=(Q^{-1};Q^{-1})_r$: $$  egin{array}{c|c|c} &r=0&0<r<N\ \hline [a^r]\widehat P_0&e_0&e_r/F_r\ [a^r]\widehat P_d&e_d&e_{r-1}/F_r\ [a^r]\widehat L_0&e_0^t&e_{N-r}^t/F_r^-\ [a^r]\widehat L_d&e_d^t&e_{d-r}^t/F_r^- \end{array} 	ag{10c} $$ The first central correction to $\delta$ has degree $N$, which proves this table directly from (1). These are genuine source and co-source derivatives, with all original normalizations. A fixed pole order on the cover and a fixed pole order in the central variable are different hypotheses: a central pole of order $p$ has cover order $Np$. Estimate (10) is strong precisely because it uses central descent and exact cyclic-diagonal telescoping. Estimate (10b) applies without descent only when the cover pole order is bounded. Neither is a uniform assertion for arbitrary separated Puiseux factors with growing pole order. ## 4. Monodromy selects the physical cap charge Under $a\mapsto Qa$, $\delta$ is fixed and $$ P^s(Qa)=ZP^s(a),\qquad L^t(Qa)=L^t(a)Z^{-1},\qquad Ze_n=Q^ne_n. $$ The total residue weight is $Q^{D_{ts}}$. Deck averaging keeps precisely matrix entries with $$ m-n\equiv t-s\pmod N. $$ The zero jet of (4) further selects the actual corner $(t,s)$. For $d	o0$ and $0	o d$ this is the WRAPPED entry of the corresponding cyclic diagonal, with coefficient one. Thus actual cap residues require, rather than delete, a retained cyclic boundary charge. In particular the compatible root monodromy $(Q,Q^{-1},Q)$ of the last Pachner wall cannot by itself be read as a projector onto geometric edge winding one. It gives a finite root/deck charge. The geometric integer lift has not been identified with the original integer-degree/carry data. ## 5. The literal primitive cap retains the generic local wall There is also a direct local nonvanishing statement. Express the primitive normalized pentagon in a common clock/shift basis $$ X=\mu Z,\quad Y=\eta S,\quad ZS=QSZ, \quad \mu(0)=Q,\quad \eta^N=x_0, $$ and take the actual $d$ input and output cap corners in that basis. At a generic exceptional direction, $x_0
otin\{0,1\}$ and $y_0=1-x_0$. The regular two-atom side is $$ O_0=D(Y;b)\,D(bX;h),\quad b^N=y_0,\quad h^N=x_0. $$ The second factor is diagonal with every entry nonzero. Write the first as $\sum_{n=0}^{d}c_nS^n$. Its exact cyclic difference equation gives $$ (Q^n-b)c_n=\eta Q^{n-1}c_{n-1}, 	ag{11} $$ with indices cyclic. Since $\eta
e0$ and $b^N=1-x_0
e1$, every coefficient is nonzero: one zero would propagate around the entire cycle and make the invertible matrix zero. Therefore $$  oxed{\quad (O_0)_{dd}=c_0\,D(bX;h)_{dd}
e0.\quad} 	ag{12} $$ Formula (3) says that the actual paired cap retains this local wall. It is not killed by operator regularity, by a norm-root zero, or by deck averaging. This does **not** identify this primitive cap placement with the exterior of the specific oversized $5_2$ face. The actual crossing's atom order and commutator orientation must be matched; an equation between central sums alone does not establish that embedding. No global excessive-face coefficient is computed here. The result is the explicit original-cap local charge and the finite uniformly bounded extraction map that an eventual typed exterior comparison must preserve.

title: Four-channel actual cap pushforward with signed deck characters
text: # Four-channel actual cap pushforward with signed deck characters 28 October 2026. This extends the exact central-meromorphic [actual cap extraction](actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.md) to bounded SIGNED Puiseux characters. The source, co-source, residue weights and 0/d corner indices are the original ones. Fixed negative characters cost a power of N. Arbitrary bulk characters are not covered by this polynomial bound. ## 1. A single exact formula for every actual endpoint channel Put d=N-1, epsilon=a^N, delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), delta(0)=1. Use the original Fermat sources P^s and L^t, s,t in {0,d}, and alpha_0=beta_0=1, alpha_d=1-Q, beta_d=N. Set sigma=1_(s=d), D=sigma+t, R=(1-Q delta)/(1-Q), E_j=product_(h=0)^(j-1)(1-delta Q^h), E_(j+N)=epsilon E_j. The last identity extends E_j to ALL signed integers j as a meromorphic germ. It retains, rather than resets, the full central norm. Let O(a)=a^ell O_ell(epsilon), ell any integer. The exact cap functional [alpha_s beta_t]^-1 Res_(a=0) a^(D-1) L^t(a) O(a) P^s(a) da is the central constant coefficient of sum_(n=0)^d H_n^(ts,ell)(epsilon) [O_ell(epsilon)]_(m(n),n), m(n)=(n+t-s+ell) modulo N, where h=n+sigma and H_n^(ts,ell)=B_t R^sigma E_(h+ell)/E_(h+1), B_0=1-delta, B_d=epsilon/N. (1) Here the representative m(n) is always in 0,...,d. The epsilon powers in (1) include the corresponding integer carry exactly. To prove (1), express every source product in the common E frame: denominator(P^0_n)=E_(n+1)/(1-delta), denominator(P^d_n)=E_(n+2)/[(1-delta)(1-Qdelta)], numerator(L^0_m)=E_m, numerator(L^d_m)=E_(m+1)/(1-delta). The prefactor in the residue contributes a^(D+ell+n-m). Since D+ell+n-m is a multiple of N, this is precisely its integer power of epsilon. Apply E_(j+N)=epsilon E_j. All long products cancel, leaving exactly (1). This proves the operator indices, normalization and deck charge simultaneously. At ell=0 it is the four-channel table in the earlier theorem. No assumption that an arbitrary singular matrix descends to epsilon has been made: its chosen character a^ell is part of the input. Summing the actual character decomposition preserves the original matrix operator. A character may not be deleted because its central norm later has a numerical specialization. ## 2. Bounded signed characters have polynomial source cost For ell>=1 the quotient in (1) is the SHORT numerator product E_(h+ell)/E_(h+1) =product_(j=h+1)^(h+ell-1)(1-delta Q^j). (2) For ell=-k, k>=1, it is the SHORT reciprocal product E_(h-k)/E_(h+1) =1/product_(j=h-k)^h(1-delta Q^j). (3) Take rho=1/16 and N>k. In (3) the interval contains at most one exceptional factor 1-delta. If it occurs, B_0 cancels it exactly, while B_d cancels it by epsilon/[N(1-delta)]=(1+delta+...+delta^(N-1))/N. Thus the kernel is holomorphic at epsilon=0. All other factors have absolute value at least 3/N on |epsilon|<=rho; also |R|<2. For (3), cancel the exceptional factor when present; otherwise use that same B_t estimate. This proves (4), not merely a coefficient estimate at one root value. For an actual central Laurent matrix with fixed pole order p, O_ell(epsilon)=sum_(r=-p)^infinity A_r epsilon^r, Cauchy's estimate and (4) give the exact finite pushforward cap(O)=sum_(r=0)^p sum_n [epsilon^r]H_n (A_(-r))_(m(n),n), |cap(O)| <=N C_ell(N) sum_(r=0)^p16^r||A_(-r)||_op, (5) where C_ell(N) is the corresponding bound in (4). Thus fixed signed characters and fixed central pole orders have polynomial cost. For ell=-k the asymptotic requirement N>k is explicit; smaller levels use the same exact formula (1), after retaining its additional integer epsilon carry. Fixed finitely many small levels do not alter the volume-rate assertion. This is not a bound for unrestricted ell=ell(N). The bulk-sector example derived in the all-sector analysis has exponential source cost despite fixed central pole order. Its actual support must be checked in a singular Pachner operator before applying (5). ## 3. Arbitrary meromorphic operators on the cap cover There is also a separate statement that needs no central descent. Define the original normalized source frames p_hat_s=a^sigma P^s/alpha_s, l_hat_t=a^t L^t/beta_t. They are holomorphic with respective values e_s,e_t^t at zero, and have uniformly bounded Euclidean norms on |a|<=1/(16N), by the explicit cap-frame estimate. If O(a)=sum_(j=-p)^infinity A_j a^j is any actual matrix Laurent germ with fixed COVER pole order p, the exact cap residue is CT_a l_hat_t(a) O(a) p_hat_s(a). The rank-one source kernel has trace norm bounded by an absolute constant C on that circle. Cauchy on its coefficients proves |cap(O)| <= C sum_(j=0)^p(16N)^j||A_(-j)||_op. (6) Thus every such actual cover-meromorphic operator has a polynomial finite-jet extraction, even if it is not invariant under a->Qa. Fixed central pole order and fixed cover pole order are different: an epsilon pole of order p has cover order Np. Formula (6) must not be substituted for (5) while hiding that growth. For 0<=r<N, the four normalized cover jets are explicitly | Endpoint | r=0 | 1<=r<N | |---|---|---| | input0 | e_0 | e_r/F_r | | inputd | e_d | e_(r-1)/F_r | | output0 | e_0^t | e_(N-r)^t/F_r^- | | outputd | e_d^t | e_(d-r)^t/F_r^- | Here F_r^-=(Q^-1;Q^-1)_r. These follow by canceling the unique vanishing factor and using full factorial reflection; they include the wrapped channels. They independently fix the indices in (1). ## 4. Actual-network scope The source functionals in (1), (5) and (6) are the actual normalized 0/d corners used simultaneously by the original pair-fused plat. The original Cartan, framing, turn and peripheral lines multiply the same expressions. Independent source variables tensor with the displayed constants. For a fixed word and bounded pole orders and signed-character support, the total extraction cost is a fixed power of N relative to the original Laurent-coefficient norms. These are the specified relative-head coordinate norms. No equality with the physical tensor metric across a nonunitary fusion is asserted, and an exponentially large coefficient matrix remains exponentially large in these bounds. An equality of complete actual typed meromorphic operators on the same marked cover remains an equality after this finite extraction. This supplies the regularized residue rule for a typed Pachner identity when its actual exterior maps and common cover have been specified. It does not supply that exterior comparison merely from a classical five-term identity, nor equate the character label with a geometric edge winding. Singular factors must first be composed with their actual maps, or all their finite source jets and integer carries must be retained term by term in a common Laurent expansion. [Exact original-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_signed_deck_pushforward.py). ## 5. Sharp scope: a bulk character has exponential cap extraction The bounded-character hypothesis above cannot be removed from the original SINGLE-HEAD d-to-d cap functional. For N>=7 set L=ceil(N/6), U=floor(5N/6), n=L-2, r=U-n, m=U, O(a)=a^r epsilon^-1 |m><n|. All indices lie in the original head range and 1<=r<N. (8) On every fixed circle |epsilon|=rho in (0,1), however, ||O(a)||_op=rho^(r/N-1)<=rho^-1, uniformly in N. Its central pole order is exactly one; the deck character r grows proportionally to N. title: Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy
text: # Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy 29 October 2026. An arbitrary binary tree of the original ordinary-cap reassociation packets contracts exactly. Its internal factorials telescope, its actual phases remain explicit, and its full squared kernel is ONE positive angle-simplex weight. After its known row normalization the complete boundary packet is a coisometry; overlaps between any two such normalized cap trees are contractive. This holds at arbitrary fixed width, including all endpoint indices and arbitrary adjoining tensors. This is a constructive boundary contraction theorem. It does not say that a knot's interior operator preserves these source packets, that complete-channel Racah matrices are contractive, or that the remaining marked cap is an ordinary cap. No new whole-knot volume estimate follows from this theorem alone. ## 1. The literal node and its source type Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and the physical gauge B_a=N^(1/4)/sqrt(s_a). Let A=(C'_23)^(-1)C'_12, with the original finite Euler maps. The [proved original pivotal-cap identity](actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) uses ellhat=sqrt(N)ell, where ell is the LITERAL original ordinary cap including its pivot. Its gauged map Khat=(ellhat_12 tensor I)A is Khat_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) q^[a(n-N-1)] sqrt(w_d(a,c,d-n)), w_d(i,j,k)=1/(s_i s_j s_k). (1) The b=d selection is the result of the COMPLETE pivotal q-Pascal sum, not a discarded input channel. In the ungauged physical coordinates and with the literal ell the same node is Kraw_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) N^(-1) p(a) F_n/(F_a F_c), p(a)=(-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2]. (2) The original Cartan/framing/peripheral lines on any exterior are unchanged. Equation (2) uses x=-q^-1; the full unreduced meridian factors in the local theorem must instead be retained off completeness. ## 2. A source-exact complete tree, with every phase retained Choose any planar binary tree T with l>=1 ordered leaves. Its original physical input has 2l-1 heads: l active leaves, and one separator head between each two successive leaves. At an internal node, first contract its left and right subtrees, then apply the three-head node (1) to their two outputs and the original separator between them. Each separator is used once. These are ordinary compositions of the specified actual maps. Every nonzero input has ALL l-1 separator indices d. If the active indices are a_1,...,a_l, its root index is n=sum_i a_i<=d. Conversely every such input is allowed: all intermediate subtree sums are at most n. There is exactly one intermediate root index at every node. Therefore no unperformed internal summation or cyclic alias remains. For an internal vertex v write n_v for its subtree sum and n_L(v) for its left-subtree sum. The complete normalized-cap, quarter-gauged kernel is Khat_T(n;a_1,...,a_l; separators) =delta_(separators,d)delta_(n=sum a_i<=d) N^(-(l-1)/2) sqrt(s_n/product_i s_(a_i)) q^(Theta_T), Theta_T=sum_(v internal) n_L(v)(n_v-N-1). (3) Proof. Replace each square root in (1) by N^(-1/2)sqrt(s_(n_v)/(s_(n_L)s_(n_R))), using s_j s_(d-j)=N. Every internal s cancels between its output and its parent's input. The phases multiply to exactly the displayed sum. They have NOT been replaced by one, nor asserted to cancel on a cycle. There is an independent exact polynomial form for the LITERAL original cap tree before physical gauging: Kraw_T=N^(-(l-1)) F_n/(product_i F_(a_i)) product_(v internal) p(n_L(v)). (4) This follows by the same cancellation using (2), and specifies every original root phase. In particular it is not a norm-only construction. The literal gauged cap tree equals N^(-(l-1)/2)Khat_T: each use of ellhat in (3) restores its stated ell=ellhat/sqrt(N) factor. All input and output B gauges are explicit, and their internal inverse factors cancel under composition. No separator-state norm is silently substituted for its actual physical coordinate. ## 3. Exact positive simplex incidence and all-width energy By reflection, the squared surviving entry (3) is |Khat_T|^2=N^(2-l)/[s_(d-n) product_i s_(a_i)]. (5) Thus its true nonnegative integer charges are (a_0,a_1,...,a_l), a_0=d-n, sum_(i=0)^l a_i=d. (6) This is a bijection, not a relaxation: every composition in (6) is one allowed input/root combination of the complete tree. The internal subtree charges are its specified partial sums. All zero angles and zero-length slots are retained by s_0=1. Let E_(l,n)=N^(-(l-1))s_n sum_(a_1+...+a_l=n) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). Different root rows have disjoint input-degree support, hence EXACTLY Khat_T Khat_T^*=diag(E_(l,0),...,E_(l,d)), ||Khat_T||_op^2=max_n E_(l,n), ||Khat_T||_HS^2=N^(2-l) Z_(l+1,N), Z_(m,N)=sum_(a_0+...+a_(m-1)=d) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). (7) These quantities are independent of the binary tree. Equations (3)--(7) are an exact controlled contraction for the entire ordinary-cap tree, not independent Cauchy bounds at its nodes. For fixed l>=2 put Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt. The uniform factorial estimate at ALL 0<=a<N gives log||Khat_T||_op^2=log||Khat_T||_HS^2+O(log N) =N (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1))/pi+O_l(log N). (8) Here the first equality follows directly from the N rows in (7). To prove the second, the continuum objective on (6) is sum_i Lambda(pi a_i/N). On the simplex of nonnegative angles summing to pi its unique maximum, for m=l+1>=3, is m Lambda(pi/m). For completeness its Hessian on the interior is -diag(cot theta_i). If all angles are below pi/2 it is negative on sum-zero vectors. If one angle exceeds pi/2, put S=sum of the other angles<pi/2. Weighted Cauchy and sum tan(theta_i)<tan S=-tan(theta_big) show the same strict negativity on the sum-zero tangent. Equality at pi/2 follows directly from the positive remaining cotangents. Thus the function is strictly concave; symmetry fixes its maximum at equal angles. Continuity includes the boundary. Rounding an equal composition to the integer sum d gives the lower bound at every sufficiently large level; there are only polynomially many compositions and all factorial errors are O_l(log N), giving the upper bound. No lattice progression is needed. For l=1 the map is identity, E_(1,n)=1, and its energy exponent is zero. There is a stronger UNIFORM root-conditioned formula. For every 0<=n<=d, including both endpoints, put t=n/N. Then log E_(l,n)=(N/pi)Phi_l(t)+O_l(log N), Phi_l(t)=l Lambda(pi*t/l)-Lambda(pi*t). (9) The constant is independent of n. For fixed sum of the l leaf angles, at most pi, the concavity argument just given places their maximum at equal values. The case l=2 at total pi may have additional maximizers, without affecting this value. For the lower estimate, distribute the integer n among l parts differing by at most one. Each angle changes by O_l(1/N), whose Lambda error is O_l(log N/N) uniformly even at zero or pi. There are at most (N+1)^(l-1) compositions. Applying the uniform factorial estimate to every term in E_(l,n), and to s_n, therefore proves BOTH sides of (9), with the stated uniform error. For l>=2 and 0<t<1 the explicit boundary action satisfies Phi_l'(t)=pi log[sin(pi*t)/sin(pi*t/l)], Phi_l''(t)=pi^2[cot(pi*t)-(1/l)cot(pi*t/l)]<0. (9a) Indeed x cot x is strictly decreasing on (0,pi), since its derivative has numerator sin(x)cos(x)-x<0. Its unique maximum is t=l/(l+1). Using Lambda(pi-theta)=-Lambda(theta), the maximum is exactly (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1)), giving (8). Formula (9) also includes a prescribed root tending to t=1, with rate l Lambda(pi/l)/pi. For l=1, E_(1,n)=1 and Phi_1=0 identically. ## 4. Exact coherent packet overlaps are contractive Every E_(l,n) is positive and known without a knot value. Define R_T=diag(E_(l,n)^(-1/2)) Khat_T. Then R_T R_T^*=I_N. Consequently P_T=R_T^*R_T is a specified orthogonal projection on the full physical input space, including its literal separator-d selection. For ANY two planar binary trees on the same ordered heads, R_T R_U^* is diagonal and ||R_T R_U^*||<=1. (10) The diagonal entry is the ACTUAL mixed phase sum of the two root rows, divided by E_(l,n); Cauchy proves its modulus at most one. This retains the off-diagonal leaf copies inside P_T and the full phases Theta_T. An arbitrary finite sequence of these packet overlaps is contractive. No artificial dephasing, ordinary positive pivotal trace or favorable choice of unknown source has been introduced. For a specified remaining row z on the root, its complete original boundary-functional norm remains exactly ||z Khat_T||^2=sum_n |z_n|^2 E_(l,n). (11) One may not drop these root weights, replace a marked row by an ordinary cap, or normalize z using an unknown period. For literal caps multiply the energies by N^(-(l-1)) as stated after (4). ## 5. What this gives for global gluing This proves a genuine positive angle incidence for a complete tree source: (6), including all its internal actual partial sums. It is a single angle simplex. It is NOT yet the edge/peripheral incidence of a knot ideal triangulation. The identity applies to arbitrary fixed width and to any polynomial or matrix exterior because it is an actual boundary-operator identity. The complete-channel Racah transition on an interior port has additional channels beyond these ordinary-cap packets. It is not the compression R_T R_U^*. Nor is an arbitrary interior R word proved to preserve P_T. The full marked packet in the local theorem must also remain. Thus (10) is a constructive boundary-tree overlap estimate; using it as a unitary or complete projection on an arbitrary knot interior would be an extra unproved step. The original full-source goal still needs the corresponding complete-channel or source-specific interior control. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.py): original coproduct-derived reassociation with the literal ordinary cap, all middle-index cancellations, exact complete tree q-factorial/phase formula, angle-simplex bijection, row energies, and coherent overlaps. The finite audit checks five levels of literal original cap/reassociation matrices and complete tree phases, and twenty all-tree-shape families checking metric kernels, positive simplex incidence, full mixed overlaps and retained arbitrary root co-sources. Python compilation passes.

title: The original operator period has a controlled closing region at two
text: # The original operator period has a controlled closing region at two 30 October 2026. A whole right half-disk at the spectral endpoint has vanishing exponential cost as its radius tends to zero. The bound is uniform over EVERY physical degree and every original matrix entry, including the Jordan blocks. Fixed genuine generic-q and spectral derivatives of the resolvent have the same vanishing-rate property. Combined with the separately proved canceled Sears bound for the actual scalar polynomial, it controls the full original integrand and its fixed generic normals throughout that region. The same estimates extend to a fixed angular slit cone on both sides of that half-disk, avoiding the spectral poles on the left real ray. The statement is an upper estimate. It does not select a contributing contour or give a nonzero saddle contribution. The scalar normal input to the final assembly is proved in its linked companion theorem. ## 1. Uniform finite statement Use the original physical matrix J_t, q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, N>=3, and 0<=t<=d. Define f(r)=sqrt(r) log(2+1/r), r>0, and f(0)=0, H_N(r)=C N^3 exp[C N f(r)+C(log N)^2]. (1) There is an absolute C such that for every 0<=r<=1/4, ||(zI-J_t(q))^-1||op<=H_N(r), Re z>=2, |z-2|<=r. (2) The same holds for the actual high-degree blocks, by their exact generic adapter. For fixed nonnegative integers j,k, with R_t(h,z)=(zI-J_t(q exp(h)))^-1, one also has on this region ||partial_h^j partial_z^k R_t(0,z)||op <=C_(j,k) N^j max(1,H_N(r))^(j+k+1). (3) These are genuine generic derivatives of the original matrix, with its distinct moving upper and lower entries. In particular lim_(r down 0) limsup_(N->infinity) N^-1 log sup_(t,z) ||partial_h^j partial_z^k R_t(0,z)||op <=0. (4) Here z ranges over the half-disk in (2). Replacing a zero norm by max(1,norm) gives the equivalent nonnegative-rate formulation. More generally fix 0<gamma_0<pi/2. All these statements hold, with constants depending on gamma_0, throughout K_(r,gamma_0)={2} union {z=2+rho exp(i phi): 0<rho<=r, |phi|<=pi-gamma_0}. (4a) This includes parts of the disk to the LEFT of two, but excludes a fixed angular neighborhood of the left real ray containing the poles. ## 2. Every prefix has a small positive determinant rate Put theta=pi/N. The exact ground-state congruence in the [endpoint theorem](actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.md) gives, for any leading prefix of size 1<=m<=t, |det(J_[m]-zI)|=|det(L_m+(z-lambda_0)V_m)|, lambda_0=2cos(theta), |(V_m)_(r,r)|=1. (5) L_m is the real Dirichlet path matrix with conductances a_r=4sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta), 0<=r<t, (L_m)_(r,r)=a_(r-1)+a_r, a_(-1)=0, (L_m)_(r,r+1)=-a_r. (6) The final term a_(m-1) is retained as a Dirichlet boundary spring. The principal minors are positive, so expansion in the diagonal perturbation, term by term in absolute value, yields |det(L_m+(z-lambda_0)V_m)| <=det L_m det(I+s L_m^-1), s=|z-lambda_0|, det L_m=product_(r=0)^(m-1) a_r. (7) The following estimate holds uniformly in ALL t,m,N and 0<=s<=2: log det(I+s L_m^-1) <=C N f(s)+C(log N)^2. (8) Here is a direct path proof, including the two small-conductance endpoints. Let h_r=min(r+1,t-r). Since t<=N-1, both integers r+1 and t-r, and their distances from N, are at least h_r. The elementary sine lower bound therefore gives a_r>=16 h_r^2/N^2. (9) The exact inverse-trace formula for L_t then gives Tr L_t^-1=sum_(r=0)^(t-1)(r+1)/a_r<=C N^3. (10) In particular its smallest eigenvalue is at least c N^-3. Partition the rows of L_t into consecutive dyadic blocks from the left and right endpoints towards the middle. There are O(log N) blocks, with a bounded number of each dyadic length, apart from at most two shorter remainder blocks. On a block of length ell, every internal conductance is at least c ell^2/N^2 by (9). Remove the springs between blocks and the final Dirichlet spring. The resulting block-diagonal Neumann operator is smaller than L_t as a quadratic form. A constant-conductance Neumann path of length ell has eigenvalues 4 a sin^2(pi k/(2ell)), 0<=k<ell. Consequently each such block contributes at most 1+C min(ell,N sqrt(lambda)) eigenvalues at most lambda. Summing the dyadic lengths gives the counting estimate n_t(lambda)<=C log N +C N sqrt(lambda) log(2+1/lambda). (11) For clarity, with x=N sqrt(lambda), the sum of lengths below x is O(x), while the larger blocks contribute O(x[1+log(N/x)]). If x<1, their contribution is O(x log N), which is bounded by the second term in (11). For large lambda the trivial bound n_t<=N is stronger. Prefix interlacing gives n_m(lambda)<=n_t(lambda) and the same lower eigenvalue bound as in (10). For positive eigenvalues mu, integrate the identity log(1+s/mu)=integral_mu^infinity s/[lambda(lambda+s)] d lambda. The C log N term of (11), starting at cN^-3, costs O((log N)^2). The other term has integral at most C N f(s): set lambda=s y and use the integrability of y^-1/2(1+y)^-1 and the same function times |log y|. This proves (8), with s=0 immediate. No inverse bound for a long complex Casimir prefix was assumed. Only the real positive path L_m enters this comparison. ## 3. Exact cancellation controls all original Green entries For u<=v the original continuant identity expresses R_(u,v) as the leading prefix determinant of size u, the trailing determinant of size t-v, and the product of original upper entries between them, divided by the full characteristic polynomial. At the root the trailing prefix is the reflected conjugate of a leading prefix; the magnitudes a_r in (6) obey a_(t-1-r)=a_r.
