Those bounds remain open outside the already proved face- supported and tail-free branches. Audit: [exact cyclotomic source calculation](../experiments/audit_actual_cluster_projector_positive_metric_obstruction.py) and [recorded certificate](../experiments/actual_cluster_projector_positive_metric_obstruction_results.json). This excludes the stated common orthogonal metric shortcut, not a general volume conjecture.

title: A polynomial-cost critical-value upper bound for two-anchor source cores
text: # A polynomial-cost critical-value upper bound for two-anchor source cores 28 October 2026. A genuine minimax deformation is available for any two-anchor residual core of the actual unit-factor source. Its original coefficient is bounded by its largest regular critical modulus times an explicit polynomial in its degree. No positivity, accessible highest saddle, nonzero thimble coefficient, or lower bound on critical values is assumed. This is an upper bound only. It does NOT prove the knot upper bound. These anchor critical points are conditional on the remaining integer clocks; they are not automatically FULL critical points of the knot's coupled phase. The sharp regulator theorem cannot be applied to them without that step. ## 1. Statement with its original coefficient normalization After extracting the actual scalar and any monomial factors, a two-anchor core with strict Hall support has the form f(z)=gamma z^(-q) product_(j=1)^m (z-u_j), |u_j|=1, gamma!=0, 1<=q<=m-1, I=CT_z f(z)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral f(z) dz/z. (1) Here m and q can depend on N. Repeated roots and arbitrarily close unit roots are allowed. All extracted source scalars remain in gamma. This is exactly the homogeneous two-anchor coefficient after removing its common scale. Put p=m-q and M=max_(f'(z)=0, z!=0, f(z)!=0)|f(z)|, with M=0 if the regular critical set is empty. Then |I| <=4 m^2 log(m+1) M. (2) In particular m=O(N) gives only polynomial transport cost. If a separate argument bounds EVERY such full-source critical modulus by exp(N V+o(N)), (2) would give the same exponential upper bound. It is not inferred here that these conditional critical values have V=Vol(knot)/(2*pi). ## 2. The critical-value contour exists without selecting its saddle Fix R>M. The Laurent polynomial f is a proper finite map from C* to C: its only poles on the sphere are 0 of order q and infinity of order p. There is no finite asymptotic value at either pole. Over {|w|>R}, f has no critical point. Every component of its preimage is therefore an unramified finite cover of an annulus. Such a component is an annulus with one end over infinity. It contains exactly one of the two pole ends. Thus there is one component around 0 and one around infinity, of degrees q and p. The finite boundary Gamma_R of the component around 0 is a smooth closed level curve |f|=R. It winds once around 0, and so represents the original positive generator in (1). This proves |I| <= R/(2*pi) integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z|. (3) The assertion is not that the source reaches every critical point. The contour uses a level above all critical values; an inaccessible highest point is entirely compatible with (3). For completeness the annular-cover statement can be read locally and topologically. A connected finite cover of the punctured disk at infinity corresponds to a finite-index subgroup of Z, hence is again a punctured disk. Filling its puncture adds one pole. It cannot contain both poles or a third component without a pole. Its regular level boundary is an embedded circle. No transport norm has yet been assumed; it is estimated next. ## 3. A uniform logarithmic length estimate The level equation is a real algebraic curve of degree 2m: |gamma|^2 product_j |z-u_j|^2-R^2 |z|^(2q)=0. Every radial ray meets it at most 2m times: along a fixed ray it is a nonzero real polynomial of degree 2m in the radius. Every circle meets it at most 2m times: the restriction is a nonzero trigonometric polynomial of degree m. It cannot vanish identically on a circle, since its highest harmonic has the nonzero product of the leading and constant coefficients of product(z-u_j). The elementary one-dimensional coarea/total-variation count therefore gives, writing r_min,r_max for the extreme radii of Gamma_R, integral |dArg z| <=4*pi*m, integral |d log|z|| <=2m log(r_max/r_min). Since |dz/z|<=|dArg z|+|d log|z||, integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z| <=4*pi*m+2m log(r_max/r_min). (4) These are bounds on a single component by the number of intersections of the whole level curve. Tangencies affect a set of measure zero and do not invalidate the total-variation estimate. ## 4. Unit roots prevent an exponential transport constant Put A_+(R)=max(0,log(R/|gamma|)+m log2). For |z|>=2, |f(z)|>=|gamma| 2^(-m)|z|^p, and for |z|<=1/2, |f(z)|>=|gamma| 2^(-m)|z|^(-q). Hence on the level curve log(r_max/r_min) <=2log2+A_+(R)(1/p+1/q). (5) This does NOT require a lower bound on M/|gamma|. If that ratio is extremely small, the positive-part expression clips to zero once its logarithm is below -m log2. Root clustering causes no hidden log(1/M) transport factor. The exact two-anchor critical-flow equation bounds every regular critical radius between 1/m and m; it is the two-vertex case of [the cut maximum principle](charged_critical_flow_and_chambers.md). It also follows directly by comparing the real parts of sum_j z/(z-u_j)=q inside and outside the unit circle. Thus, for M>0, M/|gamma| <=(m+1)^(2m). Take R down to M in (3)--(5), without deforming through the critical level. Since 1/p+1/q<=2, |I|/M <=2m+(m/pi)[2log2+2(2m log(m+1)+m log2)] <=4m^2 log(m+1). This proves (2). If M=0, use any R>0 and let R decrease to zero in the same estimates; the bounded positive-part expression gives I=0. The proof is uniform in the unit-root positions and their multiplicities, with no assumption of a fixed saddle Hessian. ## 5. The precise higher-dimensional issue The one-variable proof uses a proper map C*->C. A Laurent polynomial on a torus of dimension at least two is generally NOT a proper map to C, even when every ordinary critical radius is bounded. Nonzero finite asymptotic values and critical values on boundary restrictions must be included before repeating the annular fibration argument. In the original source these are not removed merely by saying the torus generates its absolute homology. The [exact cut/flag jets](charged_source_cut_jets.md) retain coordinate boundary currents and bound their small-deficit normal cost. They do not bound the remaining core periods or force a constrained boundary stationary point into the saturated genuine critical variety. The [critical regulator compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md) controls limits of FULL genuine critical points, not arbitrary such restricted boundary points. Those distinctions are essential for extending (2) to the complete clock-coupled knot period. Thus (2) supplies an actual polynomial-cost minimax estimate for a source class to which it applies. The missing general upper-bound theorem is still to prove that the FULL phase, with all its retained relative boundary strata, has no larger relevant stratified critical value. No new knot or broad knot class is proved here. ## 6. A rigorous logarithmic-mass estimate for a prospective global chain There is one higher-dimensional quantitative step which can be proved without assuming a controlled gradient flow. Let an oriented real r-cycle Gamma in (C*)^r be a finite sum of semialgebraic pieces Gamma_a with integer multiplicities c_a. Suppose each piece is contained in a real algebraic support whose complexification has dimension r and degree D_a. Suppose also |log|z_i||<=B on the chain. Then integral_Gamma |dlog z_1 wedge ... wedge dlog z_r| <=4^r (B+pi)^r sum_a |c_a|D_a. (8) Lower-dimensional strata have zero r-dimensional integral. Supports can be split into their regular pieces without changing their total degree bound. Singular pieces of full real dimension r require their own r-dimensional support; an arbitrary algebraic superset of larger dimension does not satisfy the hypothesis. Proof. Write dlog z_i=d rho_i+i d theta_i. The absolute r-form is bounded by the sum of the 2^r real wedge forms obtained by selecting rho_i or theta_i at every coordinate. For each corresponding projection, the area formula integrates its absolute Jacobian by counting fibers. A fixed rho_i imposes the quadratic equation Re(z_i)^2+Im(z_i)^2=exp(2rho_i); a fixed theta_i imposes one real linear equation, with an extra ray inequality. At a regular fiber point these equations cut the complexified r-dimensional support in an isolated point. Bezout's inequality bounds their number by 2^r D_a. This remains a bound on the isolated points even if an unrelated positive-dimensional complex intersection is present; the singular/projection-critical locus has image measure zero. If s radial coordinates were selected, the projection box has volume at most (2B)^s(2pi)^(r-s). Sum these bounds over all coordinate choices and over the chain pieces. The result is 2^r sum_a|c_a|D_a * (2B+2pi)^r, which is (8). Angular seams are omitted sets of measure zero and the absolute-Jacobian count includes all windings. Consequently an ACTUAL homologous sublevel representative with polynomial sum|c_a|D_a and polynomial logarithmic radius range would have polynomial log-form mass. Bounding its exponential integrand would then give the desired upper estimate without a hidden exponential transport constant. This is a proved mass lemma, not a claim that an effective semialgebraic triangulation constructs that representative. Construction with the original relative source, and control of its full stratified critical values, remain separate. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.py): exact source normalizations, complete regular critical sets for root families including repeated roots, the critical radius and level-radius bounds, the explicit polynomial prefactor, and the inaccessible-highest example as a check that an upper estimate does not assert selection.

title: The original filling kernel is an exact centered Gaussian with a normal source
text: # The original filling kernel is an exact centered Gaussian with a normal source 29 October 2026. The full original twist, including every projective Casimir jet, is an exact centered Gaussian in the pair eigenlogarithm. Its finite Fourier coefficients have an exact Poisson/Fresnel formula with a retained INTEGER LINEAR charge weight. No coprimality or parity restriction is needed. The representation gives actual nonzero local Gaussian charge channels near real complete color for fixed |p|>=2. It does not prove that their exterior pairing survives in a filled knot. ## 1. Full-Hermite Gaussian, not a value-only Gauss sum Use the original N,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N),Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and hbar=2pi i/N. The node eigenlogs are UNWRAPPED: x_k=pi i(2k+1)/N, w_k=exp(x_k), 0<=k<N. For an integer P, the actual twist2P data in the [complete Fourier-Hermite theorem](actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md) are h_k=nu_k^(2P), d_k=-P(d-2k)h_k. They satisfy EXACTLY \[ \boxed{h_k=\kappa^{-P} \exp\{P(x_k-\pi i)^2/\hbar\},\qquad d_k=\left.\partial_x\left[\kappa^{-P} e^{P(x-\pi i)^2/\hbar}\right]\right|_{x=x_k}.} \tag{1} \] Indeed the derivative multiplier is P(2k+1-N), and expanding the square gives precisely Q^(P k(k+1)). Its difference is a full integer turn, not an omitted even-level sign. The centered square is invariant under x->2pi i-x, so it has the compatible paired values, opposite derivatives, and zero derivative at the odd simple node x=pi i. Every original normal jet is present. There is also a source-independent matrix form avoiding any sum over auxiliary colors. The function K(z)=arccosh(-z/2)^2 has the branch analytic on C minus[2,infinity), with its removable continuation at z=-2. On the nodes, K(c_k)=(x_k-pi i)^2. The actual finite Casimir has all its eigenvalues below2. Full holomorphic/Hermite functional calculus therefore gives \[ \boxed{R^{2P}=\kappa^P\exp\{P K(\Omega)/\hbar\}.} \tag{2} \] This equality uses BOTH (1) conditions and the FULL polynomial P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2. It is not an assertion that R is Euclidean unitary; its nilpotent exponential is retained. For the filled odd box the exact formula is \[ \mathscr R(R^{-(2p+1)}) =\kappa^{-p}\mathscr R\{R^{-1} e^{-pK(\Omega)/\hbar}\}. \tag{3} \] The actual turn map mathscrR is linear, not multiplicative. Formula (3) does not move the exponential through a turn as a new local operator or discard a source-normal direction. ## 2. A coherent all-color finite Gaussian kernel The exact marked transforms are H_n=N^(-1)sum_k h_k w_k^(-n), D_n=N^(-1)sum_k d_k w_k^(-n), a_n=[D_n+(N-n)H_n]/N, 0<=n<N. (4) At n=0, D_0=0 so (4) includes a_0=H_0. These a are the actual first-kind Chebyshev coefficients, not freely chosen Fourier values. For an arbitrary original mixed-circle exterior A_j, where A_j multiplies L_(j+1), put eta_n=(-1)^n(A_n-A_(n-2)), A_negative=0. Then the FULL filling/source identity is \[ \kappa^{2P}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\beta_j A_j =\frac{\kappa^{2P}}{N^2} \sum_{n,k=0}^{N-1}h_kw_k^{-n} [N-n-P(d-2k)]\,\eta_n. \tag{5} \] It holds for scalar, Hilbert-valued or operator-valued exteriors in their original order. Taking a difference on the exterior retains the two finite color endpoints; no periodic substitute for that finite difference is made. For completeness the normal transform can be recovered coherently from the value transform alone, with its compulsory full finite Hilbert kernel: \[ D_n=-iP\sum_{m\ne n}\frac{H_m}{\sin(\pi(m-n)/N)}. \tag{6} \] Derive this by the elementary DFT of k: its nonzero-frequency coefficients are -1/(1-Q^(-l)), and its mean is d/2. That mean cancels the -PdH_n term exactly. The matrix in (6) is Hermitian and has norm |P|d. This does NOT allow one to discard D when H_n vanishes at a particular color: it mixes all retained colors. All gcd/parity behavior is already exact in (4). For P!=0 put g=gcd(|P|,N), L=N/g. The value H_n is zero unless g divides n. After that reduction it has modulus L^(-1/2) for odd L. For even L it is zero unless (P-n)/g congruent to (P/g)L/2 modulo2, and otherwise has modulus sqrt(2/L). These statements follow by grouping the quadratic sum into g cosets and expanding its squared modulus; the latter leaves only the shifts0, and L/2 if L is even. They include L=1 by its trivial sum. Their PHASES remain the actual finite Gaussian sum in (4); none is divided out as a nonzero normalizer. For P=0, H_n=delta_(n,0),D_n=0, exactly. In particular arithmetic zeros of the value Gauss sum do not determine support of the full-Hermite filling kernel. ## 3. Exact finite-window Poisson representation and endpoint current Set t_k=(k+1/2)/N. For P real integer define the entire finite coefficient interpolation \[ a(n)=\frac{\kappa^{-P}}N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} [2P(t_k-\tfrac12)+1-n/N] e^{2\pi i PN(t_k-1/2)^2-2\pi i n t_k}. \tag{7} \] It is exactly (4) on the physical n=0,...,N-1. It is a specified interpolation of the FILLING COEFFICIENT, not a new assertion about an arbitrary nonintegral ordinary-color exterior. Define \[ I_{P,N}(b)=\int_0^1 e^{2\pi i PN(t-1/2)^2-2\pi i bt}\,dt, \quad J_{P,N}(n)=\frac{e^{\pi i PN/2}(1-e^{-2\pi i n})}{2\pi i N}. \] The all-N, all-parity exact formula is \[ \boxed{a(n)=\kappa^{-P} \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}^{\mathrm{symmetric}}(-1)^\ell \{(\ell+1)I_{P,N}(n+N\ell)-J_{P,N}(n)\}.} \tag{8} \] The SUM IS PAIRED symmetrically in ell. Each paired tail is O(ell^(-2)) on compact n sets for fixed N,P; the series is then locally uniformly convergent. The endpoint current J is essential off the integer lattice. No unsupported absolute summation of its constant pieces is intended. Here is a direct proof. Apply midpoint Fourier sampling to the periodic extension of the smooth finite-window integrand in (7). Its Fourier coefficient at frequency N ell acquires (-1)^ell. The periodic extension may jump at its endpoints, but its Fourier series converges to each interior t_k. Its paired Fourier aliases converge as stated, by two integrations by parts; their leading odd1/ell terms cancel. In that coefficient put b=n+N ell. The amplitude equals [2P(t-1/2)-b/N]+(ell+1). The first bracket is the phase derivative divided by 2pi i N. Its integrated endpoint is EXACTLY -J_(P,N)(n). This proves (8) and specifies the original side current rather than assuming it vanishes under a later complex-color deformation. For physical INTEGER n, J=0 and (8) simplifies to \[ a_n=\kappa^{-P}\sum_\ell^{\mathrm{symmetric}} (-1)^\ell(\ell+1)I_{P,N}(n+N\ell). \tag{9} \] Thus the integer linear charge weight is exactly the retained NORMAL data in (4), not an optional phase-space amplitude. In particular ell=-1 is killed on the original integer color grid. Off that grid its term is -J and may NOT be dropped. The zero charge is therefore not deleted from a deformed source by fiat. When P!=0, each integral in (8) is explicitly a finite Fresnel difference. With b arbitrary complex, \[ I_{P,N}(b)=e^{-\pi i b-\pi i b^2/(2PN)} \int_{-1/2-b/(2PN)}^{1/2-b/(2PN)}e^{2\pi i PN v^2}\,dv. \tag{10} \] The integration segment is the translated original interval, and the integrand is entire. For P=0 use its elementary Fourier integral instead. Thus no division by a Gauss sum or a coprimality assumption has entered any formula. ## 4. Exact odd-filling operator and its classical charge equation Put B_j=mathscrR(R^(-1)L_(j+1)), and eta_n^B=(-1)^n(B_n-B_(n-2)), B_negative=0. Substituting P=-p into (5),(9) gives an ALL-INPUT identity for the filled box: \[ \boxed{\mathscr R(R^{-(2p+1)}) =\kappa^{-p}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\eta_n^B \sum_\ell^{\mathrm{symmetric}}(-1)^\ell(\ell+1) I_{-p,N}(n+N\ell).} \tag{11} \] All exteriors and original modified/peripheral factors are kept when this is inserted in a diagram. Multiple boxes can be replaced simultaneously before their original marked closure, by ordinary linearity. Formula (11) is the coherent surgery kernel, rather than an absolute sum over independently normalized circle invariants. To state its local symbol precisely, let a=n/N, b/N=a+ell, y=2pi i(t-1/2), mu=2pi i(a-1), and c=ell+1. Stationarity of the Gaussian integral in (9) gives \[ 2P y-\mu=2\pi i c. \tag{12} \] For the actual negative odd filling, P=-p, this is mu+2p y=-2pi i c. It is the canonical FULL-TWIST charge relation with the half twist already in B_j. The exact physical auxiliary color is j=n+1, whose squared-meridian log near completeness is mu_phys=2pi i((n+1)/N-1)=mu+hbar. Thus the finite equation has the corresponding retained Weyl shift, and (12) is its leading classical form. Identifying y with a chosen topological longitude also requires the actual peripheral chart, not an inference from a classical A-polynomial alone. For the actual low mixed pretzel core the sign can be checked directly. Put H=Q^h for auxiliary color j=N-h. Its literal coefficient has the identity a_(h,v)x^v/N^2=q^(h^2)F_(2v)/[F_v^2F_(v-h)F_(v+h)]. Thus its phase replaces 4Li2(X) by 2Li2(X)+Li2(X/H)+Li2(XH), and includes +(Log H)^2/2. Differentiation at a regular internal saddle gives dG/dLogH=LogH+Log(1-X/H)-Log(1-HX) =Log[(H-X)/(1-HX)]=Log L_H, with its continued integer mark. Here mu_phys=-LogH, rather than LogH. In the circle kernel the factor (-1)^(j-1) cancels the Gaussian linear action -pi i mu_phys, leaving (LogH-2pi i c)^2/(4p) up to real constants for P=-p. Its combined stationary equation is therefore LogH+2p LogL_H=2pi i c. This is a calculation from the original factorial and normal-source phases. It still does not assert the actual exterior contour selects that stationary point. ## 5. Exact first-order transport of the FULL filling coefficient There is an additional useful source Ward identity for a(n). Shifting the original periodic chirp index k->k+1 gives, on integer n, \[ H_{n-2P}=Q^{n-P}H_n, \quad D_{n-2P}=Q^{n-P}(D_n-2P H_n+2Pq^{-n}). \] The boundary term 2P is the retained jump of the original LINEAR normal weight at k=N-1. Substitution in (4) cancels the homogeneous H terms and proves \[ \boxed{a(n-2P)=Q^{n-P}a(n)+\frac{2P}{N}q^{n-2P}, \quad n\in\mathbb Z.} \tag{12a} \] Outside 0<=n<N this uses the specified finite interpolation (7), not an extension of missing Chebyshev coefficients by zero. For complex n the EXACT retained current is \[ a(n-2P)-Q^{n-P}a(n)-\frac{2P}{N}q^{n-2P} =\frac{(e^{-2\pi i n}-1)q^{n-2P}}{N^2} [N-n+P(N+1)]. \tag{12b} \] Thus the physical coefficient recurrence is affine, not an illicit homogeneous theta recurrence after complex-color deformation. For P!=0, define g_n=q^(n^2/(2P))a_n, with the original log q. Equation (12a) says g_(n-2P)-g_n=(2P/N)q^(n^2/(2P)-n). Every physical coefficient packet is therefore a sum of at most 2|P| homogeneous quadratic chirps and explicit INCOMPLETE finite quadratic sums. For instance along n_j=n_0+2Pj in the actual window, j>=0, \[ a_{n_j}=q^{-n_j^2/(2P)} \left[q^{n_0^2/(2P)}a_{n_0} -\frac{2P}{N}\sum_{t=1}^j q^{n_t^2/(2P)-n_t}\right]. \tag{12c} \] The anchors are explicit finite Gaussian data (4), bounded by 1+|P|. No anchor is a knot period. Equation (12c), or the exact Fresnel representation (8), supplies the endpoint function with its actual source rather than approximating D by a Gaussian value. Polynomially small errors in this endpoint function cannot simply be discarded against an exponentially smaller filled rate. ## 6. The actual circle difference cancels its current and folds EXACTLY The current J in (8) is periodic in n with period1. It therefore cancels TERMWISE in the original circle-basis difference. Define the canonical ENTIRE extension b_ext(j)=exp(pi i(j-1))[a(j-1)-a(j+1)], K_P(h)=b_ext(N-h). The physical circle coefficient for color j is beta_(j-1). For 1<=j<N it equals b_ext(j); for the last color, \[ \beta_{N-1}=\tfrac12 b_{\mathrm{ext}}(N). \tag{12d} \] The half is compulsory: the original aliases give a(N)=0 and a(N+1)=-a(N-1), while the missing actual coefficient a_(N+1) was extended by ZERO in the finite circle-basis conversion. There is an exact ENTIRE Weyl symmetry, not only an equality on the color lattice: \[ \boxed{K_P(h)=K_P(-h),\qquad h\in\mathbb C.} \tag{12e} \] To prove it without discarding a current, put y_k=x_k-pi i and use the finite Gaussian expression (7). Directly \[ K_P(h)=\frac{2(-1)^{N-1}}{N^2}\sum_k h_k e^{hy_k} [(h+2Py_k/\hbar)\sinh y_k+\cosh y_k]. \tag{12f} \] The k,d-k pair has y mapped to -y and h_k unchanged. Its sum is even in h. The odd simple y=0 term is even as well. Equivalently, the exact alias identities H(-n)=e^(2pi in)H(n), D(-n)=-e^(2pi in)D(n), together with antiperiodicity at n+N, give (12e), including its necessary exp(pi i(j-1)) factor. For ANY even core exterior C_h=C_(-h), scalar or operator-valued, and any integer H with 0<=H<N, the literal physical-color sum therefore obeys \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}C_h =\frac12\sum_{h=-H}^H K_P(h)C_h.} \tag{12g} \] This keeps the physical half weight at h=0. In the actual pretzel core, C_h is even on the physical grid by its finite Chebyshev relation. Its symmetric finite-factorial continuation keeps the pair F_(v-h)F_(v+h) and q^(h^2), and is even as well; a new one-sided exp(pi i h) continuation must not be substituted for it. Thus the fold applies before the original marked closure and with arbitrary spectator boxes. It iterates over several color ports. The remaining high bands/aliases and any cutoff at +/-H remain their actual source terms; (12g) makes no global tail assertion. The current-inclusive Poisson formula becomes especially simple for this folded kernel. With c=ell+1 and b=Nc-h, \[ K_P(h)=\kappa^{-P}e^{\pi i(N-h-1)} \sum_\ell^{\mathrm{symmetric}}(-1)^\ell c [I_{P,N}(b-1)-I_{P,N}(b+1)]. \tag{12h} \] There is NO omitted J in this equation: J(j-1)=J(j+1) cancels exactly for all complex j. The charge c=0 is thus truly absent from the full circle kernel, even off lattice. This stronger conclusion holds after the actual circle difference, not for an individual a(n) in section3. Reflection (h,c)->(-h,-c) preserves each paired contribution in (12h). Indeed I(-b)=e^(2pi ib)I(b) by t->1-t; its factor e^(-2pi ih) cancels the reflected prefactor and the two odd signs cancel. Thus +/-charge folding keeps the EXACT endpoint Fresnel functions too. The h=0 endpoint is removed by a genuine whole-source identity, not by comparing two formal saddle heights. ## 7. An actual nonzero LOCAL Gaussian charge, and the remaining gate Fix |P|>=2 and 0<=h/N<=delta<1/2, with physical n=N-1-h. For each c=+1 or -1, the stationary point of the labeled integral with ell=c-1 stays strictly inside [0,1], uniformly for large N. The exact Fresnel integral therefore has \[ I_{P,N}(n+N\ell)= \frac{e^{i\,\operatorname{sgn}(P)\pi/4}}{\sqrt{2|P|N}} e^{-\pi i(n+N\ell)-\pi i(n+N\ell)^2/(2PN)} +O_{P,\delta}(N^{-1}). \tag{13} \] This follows by the elementary full real Gaussian integral and one integration by parts on its two nonstationary omitted tails. It is uniform and NONZERO for sufficiently large N. The original normal charge factor c is nonzero on both channels. No unknown cycle coefficient occurs INSIDE this labeled real Gaussian integral. For P=0 or |P|=1, the exact formulas remain valid; uniform endpoint asymptotics are not substituted for (13). For the circle difference itself the corresponding leading charge term is, with b=Nc-h and ell=c-1, \[ \frac{2i\kappa^{-P}e^{i\operatorname{sgn}(P)\pi/4}} {\sqrt{2|P|N}} (-1)^{(N+1)\ell}c\sin\frac{\pi b}{PN} \exp\{-\pi i(b^2+1)/(2PN)\}. \tag{13a} \] This follows by subtracting the two actual Gaussians at b-1,b+1. Its c=+/-1 amplitudes are nonzero in a fixed sufficiently small real complete-color corridor for |P|>=2. Under (h,c)->(-h,-c), the sine and c both reverse and all remaining factors agree. Thus the two geometric-charge halves ADD at h=0; the apparent half-line endpoint is not an independent positive-height error. One must still retain exact endpoint corrections until their exterior pairing is estimated to the needed exponential accuracy. This is a local source-channel result, not yet nonzero filled-knot pairing. The complete sum in (11) retains all charges; arithmetic Gauss cancellations can and do occur. A complex geometric color deformation must retain the full current-inclusive kernel before using the proved difference cancellation, all exterior/source data, and its endpoint transport. Neither (13) nor the formal relation (12) proves survival after that original exterior contraction. The subsequent [exact source Fourier estimate](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md) retains those endpoint currents and proves a uniform high-charge gap. Combined with the original analytic mixed source it now yields [nonzero survival of the entire truncated cusp-color sum](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md) for independently large fixed signed fillings. That theorem still retains the complementary physical color region as an open whole-source gate; it does not infer its absence from the local Gaussian above. ## 8. The wrapped normal current is an explicit original source The endpoint function also has a finite operator Ward identity. It identifies its forcing term without discarding it. Let f_P be the degree-<N Casimir polynomial for r_N^(2P), so that R^(2P)=kappa^(2P)f_P(Omega). Define a LINEAR map on Casimir polynomials by \[ (\mathcal T f)(w+w^{-1}) =f(Qw+Q^{-1}w^{-1})+f(Q^{-1}w+Qw^{-1}). \tag{14} \] The symmetric Laurent expression is a polynomial: its constant Chebyshev coefficient is doubled and its nth coefficient is multiplied by Q^n+Q^(-n). Products on the following left side are evaluated in the FULL Casimir algebra, with reduction modulo P_N where necessary. Write rho=q-q^(-1). Then, for every integer P and every N>=2, \[ \boxed{\mathcal T f_P(\Omega) -Q^P\,2T_{2P}(\Omega/2)f_P(\Omega) =\frac{2PN}{\rho}\,\Xi_0(\Omega) =2PN(-1)^N\rho\,p\ell.} \tag{15} \] Here T_(-n)=T_n and Xi_0 has value zero at every node, derivative one at c_0=q+q^(-1), and derivative zero at the other double nodes. The literal original cup and ordinary cap p,ell have precisely the normalizations used throughout this note. To prove (15), put G(x)=kappa^(-P)exp(P(x-pi i)^2/hbar). Its exact shifts satisfy G(x+/-hbar)=Q^P exp(+/-2Px)G(x). The interpolating Laurent polynomial g(x)=f_P(e^x+e^(-x)) has the same value and x derivative as G at every original node x_k. Consequently both sides of (15) have zero node values. All their normal derivatives agree except when a shift crosses the original logarithmic window. At x_0 the derivative defect is +2PN, and at x_d it is -2PN; the shifted endpoint value is one in both cases. Dividing by dc/dx=rho and -rho, respectively, gives the SAME Casimir derivative 2PN/rho at the paired node c_0. At the odd simple node no extra normal condition is imposed. Full Hermite uniqueness proves the first equality, including even and composite levels. For the second equality use the [normalized original source observable](actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.md), Xi_0=(-1)^N rho^2 p ell on the degree-d block. This identity extends to the entire physical pair: both sides are Hopf intertwiners, and the degree-d block generates the whole pair by the actual E/F maps, as proved in the [full pair commutant theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). There is no unrecorded projector onto that block. Most usefully, the exact endpoint forcing becomes a scalar when placed in its ACTUAL odd-box turn. Indeed R^(-1)p=kappa^(-1)p and the genuine unscaled turn obeys mathscrR(p ell)=I. Therefore \[ \boxed{\mathscr R\!\left[ R^{-1}\{\mathcal T f_P-Q^P 2T_{2P}(\Omega/2)f_P\}\right] =2PN(-1)^N\rho\,\kappa^{-1}I.} \tag{16} \] Its scalar modulus is at most 4pi|P|, uniformly in N. This is an all-input original-source reduction, not just a formal critical value statement. It can be inserted with arbitrary spectators in this typed slot. In a composed source the displayed current removes that box and leaves its explicitly known scalar factor. Equations (15)--(16) do not bound the inverse Ward transport, nor identify a general Fresnel endpoint remainder with this one term. The map mathcalT is the specified linear Casimir q-shift, not a physical gate that may be relocated through other boxes. A global filled-knot estimate must still control the resulting actual source and any iteration of this identity. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.py) tests original full physical signed twists and odd filled boxes, all-node Gaussian values AND derivatives, finite Hilbert normal data, gcd/parity selection, the current-inclusive Poisson/Fresnel identity, the uniform nonzero labeled charge asymptotic, and the full physical endpoint Ward (15) with its scalar turned source (16).

title: Coherent complete-belt stacks with arbitrary signs and outer twists
text: # Coherent complete-belt stacks with arbitrary signs and outer twists 29 October 2026. The complete-circle boundary packet removes the balance restriction from the original quantum source of the literal octahedral belt stacks. No ordering, parity or residue subsequence is selected. A fixed extra signed crossing power is retained exactly; its literal geometric collar certificate is linked separately below. ## 1. The exact original source and its nodal crossing phase Use the genuine full checked crossing R, the complete ordinary auxiliary-circle operator L_N and the unscaled physical turn of [the original stack construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md). Write z=z_N, z^sharp for its literal reflected polynomial, and f_+=z^sharp R^(-1), f_-=Rz, n=p+q>0, e=q-p, Phi_(p,q,a;N)=phi(L_N R^a product_i f_(epsilon_i)), where the fixed word epsilon has p plus and q minus pieces, and a is any fixed signed integer. The whole pair commutant is the FULL Hermite algebra, so the exact all-port identity is Phi_(p,q,a;N)=phi(L_N R^(e+a)(z^sharp)^p z^q) =N sum_(j=0)^(N-1) R(c_j)^(e+a) conjugate(z(c_j))^p z(c_j)^q. (1) The second equality is the proved original complete-belt sewing functional; the repeated Casimir normal source has not been replaced before closure. Its derivative pairing gives precisely the displayed N-weighted nodal sum. The all-port equality in the first line includes the normal directions and is stronger than the final nodal formula. Put d=N-1, q_root=exp(pi i/N), kappa=exp(pi i d^2/(2N)) and theta_j=(2j+1-N)pi/N, c_j=-2cos(theta_j). The literal crossing has R(c_j)=kappa(-1)^j q_root^[j(j+1)]. Consequently, at EVERY node and both parities, R(c_j)=kappa^(1/2) exp[iN theta_j^2/(4pi)], kappa^(1/2) HERE MEANS exp[pi i d^2/(4N)]. (2) There is no principal-square-root convention. The two exponent formulas differ by -2pi i j, exactly. Since the two indices of a double node give the same eigenvalue, (2) is compatible with all multiplicities in (1). In particular |R(c_j)|=1. ## 2. The nonzero all-parity coherent Gaussian The [source-exact boundary packet](actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.md) gives, uniformly for small real theta, z(-2cos theta)=exp(-i pi d/4) a(i theta) exp[Nj(i theta)] [1+O(1/N)], j(i theta)=j_0-theta^2/(4pi)+O(theta^4), a(0)=2^(-9/4) exp(i pi/8), j_0=v8/pi. (3) Both a(i theta) and j(i theta) are even analytic; j(i theta) is real. Every fixed neighborhood of theta=0 has an exponential gap on its complement for the literal polynomial. The twist in (2) has unit modulus, so it preserves that entire-source gap. Combining (1)--(3), the local exponent is EXACTLY, to quadratic order, nN j_0 - N[n-i(e+a)]theta^2/(4pi). Its real quadratic part is positive because n>0, even for arbitrarily large FIXED signed a. The nodal grid has step2pi/N and shift0 for odd N, shift1/2 for even N. Its complex Gaussian sum is sum_j exp[-N(n-i(e+a))theta_j^2/(4pi)] =sqrt(N)/sqrt(n-i(e+a)) [1+O(exp(-cN))]. Here and below sqrt has positive real part. This follows directly by Fourier transforming the Gaussian: all nonzero frequencies are bounded by exp[-pi N Re(1/(n-i(e+a)))], at either lattice shift. The two tails outside the fixed local window are exponentially small as well. Taylor expansion of the even analytic amplitude and quartic exponent has relative error O(1/N); dominated Gaussian integration makes that estimate uniform on the actual lattice. The resulting FULL original source is Phi_(p,q,a;N) =N^(3/2) 2^(-9n/4) kappa^(a/2) exp[-ie pi/8+ie pi/(4N)] /sqrt(n-i(e+a)) * exp[nN j_0] [1+O(1/N)]. (4) The fixed constant in the error can depend on p,q,a. There is no claim uniform in a growing with N. To check the phase explicitly, the constant factors BEFORE simplification are kappa^((e+a)/2) exp[-ie pi d/4] exp[ie pi/8]. Since d^2/N-d=-d/N, these equal precisely those in (4). This retains the original crossing scalar kappa, not only its modulus. No source phase, normal or winding coefficient is dropped. The leading factor in (4) is nonzero at EVERY sufficiently large level, without a prime-level, parity or congruence restriction. In particular lim_N (2pi/N) log|Phi_(p,q,a;N)|=2n v8. (5) For p=q=k and a=0, (4) reduces to the earlier retained-belt constant N^(3/2)2^[-(9k+1)/2]/sqrt(k), providing a normalization check. The excluded n=0 case has no positive localized packet and is not covered by this theorem. ## 3. Actual links and the precise geometric scope For a=0 the literal octahedral stack proof already constructs the ACTUAL complement for every fixed sign word of length n>=1. Its complete regular-cell metric has volume2n v8, without a balance hypothesis. Its original source is exactly (1). The original reduced single-cut Kashaev normalization differs only by the recorded unit phases (and the stated single1/N in the modified convention), so (5) proves the full original volume limit for EVERY such sign word. Thus unbalanced stacks, including a single positive or negative piece, are now included. This is an actual link-family extension, not a new claim about arbitrary bridge graphs or independently filled crossing circles. Its possible containment in previously known Whitehead-chain families retains the earlier coverage caveat. For a!=0, (1)--(5) retain the literal original outer R^a insertion with all of its source scalars. The [outer-collar puncture permutation/isometry certificate](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md#3a-any-fixed-integer-outer-crossing-power) identifies its ACTUAL complement with the same complete regular-cell gluing, of volume2n v8. Its component count is n+3 for even a and n+2 for odd a. Thus the original volume equality holds for every fixed sign word and every fixed integer outer twist a. The topological assertion comes from that literal collar certificate, not from the quantum rate. Audit: [full original sign-word/outer-twist sources, high-precision nodal phase checks and coherent Gaussian calibrations](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_octahedral_belt_stack_asymptotic.py). the finite checks cover seven full physical levels,210 all-sign word operators and490 complete original outer-twist closures;860 100-digit all-parity nodal phase checks; six growing-N families of complete coherent Gaussian calibrations. The phase identities themselves are proved algebraically above; the phase checks and profiles supplement the analytic proof and are not its noncancellation premise. Independent analytical check: the global critical-path auditor re-derived (2), the exact imbalance/Cartan phase in (4), and the complex Gaussian at both lattice shifts. The pointwise source error is controlled after summation by its absolute real Gaussian, with fixed factor depending on n,e,a. Thus no parity cancellation or unestimated residue current is being assumed away.

title: A finite Fourier identity for coherent Racah normal tails
text: # A finite Fourier identity for coherent Racah normal tails **Later result, 29 October 2026:** the [all-partner first-normal theorem](actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.md) now bounds every actual coherent tail, including the symmetric component left undetermined by the involution below. It uses a positive presentation of the full generic source in addition to these Fourier identities. Higher general normal orders remain open. 29 October 2026. This is an own finite algebraic identity for the actual retained `[2N]` current. It gives a uniform logarithmic relative bound when the largest face sum occurs at least twice, including genuinely nonempty high-partner tails. For arbitrary partner labels the identity retains a second alternating sum. No general bound on that residual, higher normal jets, or completed physical transport is asserted. ## 1. The actual tail and its positive core Use the symmetric quantum-factorial convention and the exact generic sum of [the supported normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md). Put `D=N-1`, `theta=pi/N`, `q=exp(i theta)`, `Q=q^2`, and s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2 sin(u theta), s_0=1. For any partner of a supported folded sextuple let `F_i` be its four face sums and `Q_k` its three opposite sums. Assume the tail is live: `min Q_k>2D`. Define a_i=2D-F_i, b_k=Q_k-2D, c_k=D-b_k=3D-Q_k. The exact face-deficit inequalities give 0<=a_i<=c_k<=D-1 for EVERY i,k, sum_k c_k-sum_i a_i=D. (1) Indeed `c_k-a_i=D-(Q_k-F_i)>=0`; the equality follows from `sum F_i=sum Q_k`. Order the four `a_i` as A=a_1<=B=a_2<=a_3<=a_4. The true positive core, indexed by `z=2D-v`, is C=sum_(v=0)^A C_v, C_v=(1/N) product_k s_(c_k-v) /[s_v product_i s_(a_i-v)] >0. (2) This is the same `C(q)` appearing in the ACTUAL generic identity (-1)^D S/[N]=C(zeta)+[2N] T(zeta). (3) The true root current is T(q)=-2 sin(theta) N^2 sum_(k=0)^(D-c_max-1) (-1)^k s_k / [product_i s_(a_i+1+k) product_j s_(D-c_j-1-k)]. (4) All displayed factorial arguments are between zero and `D`. No invalid factorial has been assigned a value or silently removed. ## 2. Exact coherent Fourier reduction Write H_r=sum_(u=1)^r cot(u theta), H_0=0, J_v=H_v+sum_k H_(c_k-v)-sum_i H_(a_i-v). Then the following identity is exact at every level, of either parity: T(q)=-sin(theta) sum_(v=0)^A C_v J_v +(2 sin(theta)/N) sum_(v=A+1)^B (-1)^(A+v) E_v, (5) where E_v=s_(v-A-1) product_k s_(c_k-v) /[s_v product_(i=2)^4 s_(a_i-v)] >0. (6) An empty last sum is zero. In particular it is absent when `A=B`, equivalently when the largest face sum occurs at least twice. The second sum is essential. For `N=5` and partner labels `(a,b,c,d,e,f)=(2,2,3,3,2,2)`, one has the ordered arrays `a_i=(0,1,1,2)`, `c_k=(2,3,3)`. The first sum in (5) is zero, whereas the retained residual gives `T(q)=-1`. Dropping it would incorrectly assert zero current. ## 3. Own finite algebraic proof This proof only uses polynomial division, finite sums of roots of unity, and the elementary sine-factorial reflection `s_r s_(D-r)=N`. Let R(x)=product_k product_(u=1)^(c_k)(1-Q^u x) / product_i product_(u=1)^(a_i)(1-Q^u x), f(x)=x R(x)/(1-x), K=sum_k c_k(c_k+1)/2-sum_i a_i(a_i+1)/2, beta=(2 sin(theta)/N) i^(N-2) q^(-K). In (4) put `j=k+1` and use the sine-factorial reflection on its three descending denominators. Converting every remaining sine by `2 sin(u theta)=i q^(-u)(1-Q^u)` gives exactly T(q)=beta sum_(j=1)^(D-c_max) f(Q^j). (7) The phase is important: the alternating sign and the degree difference in (1) leave `q^(2j)=Q^j`, the numerator `x` in `f`. After cancellation, `f` has SIMPLE poles precisely at r_v=Q^(-v), 0<=v<=A. For `1<=u<=A` the numerator has three factors `1-Q^u x` and the denominator has four. Above `A` there are no poles because every `c_k` is at least every `a_i`. Its polynomial part has degree at most `D=N-1`: the numerator degree minus denominator degree is `D`. Let B_v=[(1-x/r_v) f(x)]_(x=r_v), L_v(x)=(1-x/r_v) f(x). Ordinary partial fractions give a polynomial `P` of degree at most `N-1` with f(x)=P(x)+sum_v B_v/(1-x/r_v). Since `f(0)=0`, one has `P(0)=-sum_v B_v`. Sum this identity over all `N`th roots except its pole set. For a nonconstant monomial of degree less than `N` the full root sum is zero, and sum_(x^N=1,x!=r_v) 1/(1-x/r_v)=(N-1)/2. The finite regular parts at the other omitted roots cancel the corresponding partial-fraction corrections. Thus sum_(x^N=1,x not a pole) f(x) =sum_(v=0)^A [r_v L_v'(r_v)-(N+1)B_v/2]. (8) For example, the finite regular part of `f` at `r_v` is `-r_v L_v'(r_v)`. This also checks the constant `(N+1)/2` in (8). Direct conversion of the unit factors gives, for EVERY `v`, B_v=i^(-D) q^K N C_v, r_v L_v'(r_v)/B_v=(N+1)/2-(i/2)J_v. (9) Here is an explicit verification rather than an assumed residue sign. For `v>=1`, set `(Q;Q)_r=product_(u=1)^r(1-Q^u)`. Cancelling the three numerator and four denominator zero factors gives B_v=(-1)^v Q^[v(v-1)/2] product_k (Q;Q)_(c_k-v) /[(Q;Q)_v product_i (Q;Q)_(a_i-v)]. Converting these factorials to sines leaves the phase `i^(-D) q^(K-vN)(-1)^v=i^(-D)q^K`, proving the first part of (9). For `v=0` it is immediate from `R(1)`. The logarithmic derivative of a unit factor is -Q^w/(1-Q^w)=1/2-(i/2)cot(w theta). After removing the pole, the signed number of unit factors is `N-1`, and the leading factor `x` contributes one. The real part is therefore `(N+1)/2`. The negative indices `1-v,...,-1` and the factor `1-x` contribute `H_v`, while the remaining positive indices contribute the other seven sums in `J_v`. This proves the second part of (9). Since `beta B_v=-2i sin(theta) C_v`, (8) contributes exactly the first term of (5). It remains to compare (8)'s root set with (7)'s ACTUAL finite range. For roots `x=Q^(-v)` outside the range in (7), cancellation shows: * `0<=v<=A`: these are precisely the omitted poles; * `A<v<=B`: the regular value can be nonzero; * `B<v<=c_max`: the regular value is zero. The last assertion follows by counting factors: above `B`, at most two denominator factors remain while at least three numerator factors remain up to `a_4`; beyond `a_4`, no denominator factors remain, and at least one numerator factor remains up to `c_max`. For the middle range the exact unit-factor conversion gives beta f(Q^(-v))=(2 sin(theta)/N)(-1)^(A+v+1) E_v. (10) One can verify (10) before conversion using f(Q^(-v))=(-1)^(A+1) Q^[vA-A(A+1)/2] (Q;Q)_(v-A-1) product_k (Q;Q)_(c_k-v) /[(Q;Q)_v product_(i=2)^4 (Q;Q)_(a_i-v)]. Subtracting these extra regular nodes from (8) proves (5), including its residual sign. This is a finite proof for all arrays satisfying (1), not an inference from finitely many knots or levels. ## 4. A proved nonempty-tail first-normal bound Suppose `A=B`. Since `H_r=H_(D-r)` and positive cotangents obey `cot(u theta)<=1/(u theta)` for `u<N/2`, 0<=H_r<=(N/pi)(1+log N), 0<=r<=D. Equations (2),(5) therefore give the uniform coherent bound |T(q)| <= 8(1+log N) C(q). (11) Unlike an estimate of the absolute summands in (4), this uses the actual cancellations. The factor 8 is deliberately nonsharp. Together with the existing positive-core jet estimate and the exact normal derivative dot G(q)=dot C(q)+4N/(q-q^-1) T(q), G=(-1)^D S/[N], dot=D_(log zeta), it proves, with an absolute constant `C_*`, |dot G(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) C(q). (12) Indeed the sharper form before `sin(theta)<=pi/N` is applied in (11) cancels the denominator in `4N/(q-q^-1)` directly. The analytic face factors have the same unit-factor logarithmic bound. Hence for this entire repeated-maximal-face class, the ACTUAL normalized squared scalar and its local positive square root satisfy K(q)=W_N^2, |dot K(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N^2, H(q)=W_N, |dot H(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N. (13) Their first inverse jets have the corresponding reciprocal bounds. This conclusion includes live `[2N]` currents; it does not extend to higher generic normal orders merely by differentiating (5), which is an identity on the fixed cyclotomic fiber. ## 5. The former all-high diagnostic is now a theorem Take `N=3m+1` and all six high spins equal to `2m`. Then `a_i=0`, `c_k=m`, `A=B=0`, and `C=s_m^3/N`. Equation (5) proves EXACTLY T(q)/C(q)=-3 sin(theta) sum_(u=1)^m cot(u theta). (14) More generally, every live partner array with all four faces equal `2D` has `a_i=0`; (14) becomes T(q)/C(q)=-sin(theta) sum_k sum_(u=1)^(c_k) cot(u theta). Thus the finite Fourier proof is not confined to the equilateral sequence. The former numerical observations remain archived as their historical record; (14) now follows from the own uniform identity. ## 6. The residual is an exact partner involution For a unique minimum `A<B`, define new arrays a*=(A,D-c_1+A,D-c_2+A,D-c_3+A), c*=(D-a_2+A,D-a_3+A,D-a_4+A). (15) They again satisfy (1), have the SAME unique minimum `A`, and applying (15) twice returns the original arrays up to permutation. Substitute `v=A+1+k` in the residual in (5), and apply `s_r s_(D-r)=N` to its three numerator factorials. The three factors of `N` cancel its prefactor exactly. The result is the ACTUAL tail formula (4) for `(a*,c*)`, with no extra factor or sign. Therefore T(a,c)-T(a*,c*)=-sin(theta) sum_(v=0)^A C_v J_v. (16) Moreover the same factorial reflection proves C*_v=C_(A-v), C*=C, J*_v=-J_(A-v). (17) The last equality also follows directly from `H_(D-r)=H_r`. Thus the difference in (16) is logarithmically bounded relative to `C`, whereas this involution alone leaves the average of the two currents undetermined. Repeated application is not a contraction. For the actual tetrahedral labels, this is an actual PARTNER move, not just a transformation of abstract factorial arrays. If the unique largest face is `F_1=a+b+e`, retain those three edges and replace its complementary edges by (c,d,f) -> (D-c,D-d,D-f). (18) The unchanged face sum is `F_1`; the other new face sums are the three numbers `2D-Q_k+F_1`, and the new opposite sums are `2D+F_1-F_i` for `i!=1`. These are exactly (15). They again have the same unique largest face, because the original tail is live. The other choices follow by tetrahedral relabeling. In particular (16) controls a difference of the full ACTUAL first normals, not merely a difference of bare root tails. Both core germs have polynomial logarithmic derivatives, their root cores agree by (17), and the four face factors also have polynomial logarithmic derivatives. Differentiating (3) for each branch therefore gives |dot K_B(q)-dot K_(B*)(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (19) No equality of the two generic normal germs is asserted. Combining these controlled three-edge differences with other exact source relations is a possible next step; (16) by itself does not fix the common first-normal component. ## 7. What the general residual still requires For a unique largest face, the last sum in (5) is still alternating. No polynomial relative bound on its absolute envelope has been proved here. Positivity of the residues does not authorize replacing this residual by its absolute sum. The exact formula exposes the partner involution and proves the repeated-maximal-face class, but it does not close the general first-normal transport problem. The transformed summation interval need not be shorter than the original one. The identity holds for abstract arrays (1) as well as actual partner branches. Applying it to a source retains all original generic normalization, peripheral factors and marked exterior data through the already proved coefficient theorem. It does not alone supply a positive completed recoupling metric or identify a global complement. Audit: [exact finite-field Fourier and tail checks](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues_results.json). The algebraic argument proves the Fourier residue identity uniformly. The finite balanced-array and all-high checks are supplementary.

title: A coherent bridge has a pointed metric potential and a coercive source-fixed optimization
text: # A coherent bridge has a pointed metric potential and a coercive source-fixed optimization 29 October 2026. The six-head bridge and the COMPLETE terminal packet can be composed before an operator norm is taken. Eliminating the bridge is exactly a POINTED diagonal potential on the terminal INPUT; the terminal Green/Newton interference remains intact. Its best all-input constant in the actual pair-degree bias family is a coercive log-convex finite-dimensional optimization. Minimizers stay in a fixed compact interval uniformly in N. They obey an exact physical charge-balance equation, with no exponential cost at the original paired sources. This gives a quantitative local metric step with arbitrary spectator inputs. It does not bound the preceding biased word or prove that such steps telescope across overlapping bridges. No sharp knot-volume bound or new geometric-edge identification is asserted. ## 1. The SAME original maps and physical metric Keep the original root N>=2,d=N-1,Q=q^2,x=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a| and all kappa/source factors. Let W_2=(V^tensor4)_(degree2d), W_1=(V^tensor2)_(degree d). Use the physical source-fixing coordinate gauge G_a=s_a/sqrt(N) on each input/output head. It fixes original cups and ordinary caps pointwise, since G_aG_(d-a)=1. The whole marked closure is kept by the complete invariant-source theorem. Write L for the gauged POSITIVE bridge map L=(ell_12 tensor I_34) R_23:W_2->W_1 from [the exact open bridge theorem](actual_terminal_bridge_operator_reduction.md). For input |a,b,c,e> it forces k=d-a-c, u=b-k=d-e, a+c+k=d, 0<=k<=d-u. (1) Its full coefficient includes the original phase; in this gauge its magnitude is N/(s_a^2 s_c^2 s_k). All through-head feedback is the actual strict shift and unitary clock, not a scalar substitution. Let T:W_1->C^N be the original complete terminal packet. It has [the closed all-input kernel](actual_terminal_packet_closed_kernel.md), including its partial factorial Green register P_t. On W_1 the physical product gauge is one. Thus that literal T matrix is unchanged. The full six-head terminal bridge is K=TL, with every spectator port retained. Its row sum is the original source row by the cap/Hopf identity, not by a new boundary functional. Define the genuine pair-degree bias on W_2 by A_delta|a,b,c,e>=exp[delta(a+b-d)]|a,b,c,e>, L_delta=L A_delta^(-1), delta real. (2) It is obtained by the SAME coordinate factor exp(delta(j-d/2)) on heads1,2. It fixes every original paired cup/cap. Equation (1) gives a+b-d=u-c, so its exact coefficient change is exp[delta(c-u)]. In particular the original initial vector w_0=p_12 tensor p_34 obeys A_delta w_0=w_0. No knot value or unknown solution defines this bias. ## 2. Exact coherent composition reduces to a pointed potential Rows of L_delta have disjoint spectator e=d-u. Consequently its COMPLETE row Gram is exactly L_delta L_delta^*=diag(E_delta(u)), E_delta(u)=N^2 sum_(k=0)^(d-u) sum_(a+c=d-k) exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2). (3) All its original phases were retained before taking this Gram. The complete composition therefore satisfies the operator identity (T L_delta)(T L_delta)^* =T diag(E_delta(u)) T^*=:M_N(delta). (4) It is not necessary to replace E_delta by its largest row. In particular (4) keeps its THROUGH-COLOR dependence and all the Green/Newton/R interference inside the terminal T. Here u is a PHYSICAL degree-basis index of W_1, not a Casimir node. The terminal Gram T^*T still mixes distinct Casimir nodes; (4) does not return to the disproved nodewise Cauchy budget. Define the exact constant C_N(delta)=lambda_max(M_N(delta))>0. (5) It is the SMALLEST all-input constant in the typed inequality ||T L w||^2 <=C_N(delta)||A_delta w||^2, EVERY w in W_2. (6) This follows from T L=(T L_delta)A_delta and the largest singular value. It remains true with an arbitrary Hilbert spectator tensor, including matrix-valued exterior columns; no spectator coefficients have been commuted. Optimality is an actual singular-value statement on the COMPLETE module, not an independently estimated path sum. Equivalently the conditional bridge cost is exact: if v is a specified output of L_delta, its minimum input norm squared is sum_u |v_u|^2/E_delta(u), since L_delta has full row rank. Thus (4) is the actual pointed input metric for the terminal packet. For clarity, the known ordered factorization of T is T=N^(-1) D_out U^(2) D_in P(J) Rev (kappa^(-1)R). Substituting it in (4) leaves the middle operator R diag(E_delta) R^* between Rev and the two Green factors. It does NOT allow P(J), Rev, R and E_delta to be reordered. The terminal singularity P_1=0 at N=6 causes no difficulty: T need not be invertible anywhere in (4)--(6). For the unchanged scalar source, the exact terminal row factorization also yields |chi_N sum_n (T L w)_n|^2 <=|chi_N|^2 N C_N(delta)||A_delta w||^2. (7) The N is the known number of coherent packets. The full positive completion by exp(-N^2)I from the terminal Gram theorem still has polynomial dual cost; no boundary source is normalized by a period. The full positive completion can be kept throughout. Put H_epsilon=(TL)^*(TL)+epsilon I on the COMPLETE W_2, and consider its exact norm after the same input bias. Its optimal constant C_(N,epsilon)(delta) satisfies C_N(delta)<=C_(N,epsilon)(delta) <=C_N(delta)+epsilon exp(2|delta|d). (7a) This follows by conjugating H_epsilon with A_delta^-1 and using the exact input charge range[-d,d]. For epsilon=exp(-N^2), the difference is superexponentially small on every bounded bias set. No channel in ker(TL) is removed. Log convexity and the coercive bounds below apply to this completed norm too: apply the same column exponential-sum proof to the fixed stacked matrix (TL,sqrt(epsilon)I)A_delta^-1. The tiny regularizer is therefore compatible with the complete positive inner product, not an assumed inverse of T or L. ## 3. The local metric optimization is genuinely coercive Let t_u=T e_u be a COMPLETE terminal input column. Equations (3)--(4) give the positive matrix exponential sum M_N(delta)=sum_(u,k,a+c=d-k) N^2 exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2) t_u t_u^*. (8) For any fixed unit output vector z with T^*z!=0, z^*M_N(delta)z is a positive sum of exponentials in delta. Its logarithm is convex by the elementary log-sum-exp Hessian. Vectors in the common nullspace give zero and are ignored in the Ritz supremum. Since log C_N is that supremum, delta -> log C_N(delta) is convex. (9) There are ACTUAL opposite extreme charges, not just a formal convex hull assumption. The bridge states (a,c,k,u)=(0,d,0,0) and (d,0,0,d) each have squared coefficient N^-2 before the bias. The closed terminal entries give |T_(0,0)|=1/N, |T_(0,d)|=1. Their rank-one positive contributions imply, for ALL real delta, C_N(delta)>=N^-4 exp(2delta*d), C_N(delta)>=N^-2 exp(-2delta*d). (10) Thus log C_N tends to infinity at BOTH ends and attains a finite global minimum. Neither uniqueness nor positivity of every terminal eigenvalue is required. Moreover all minimizers are uniformly bounded as N varies. The uniform sine-factorial estimate bounds s_a and s_a^-1 by N^C exp(CN), with constants independent of a. The explicit closed T entry consists of a bounded number of such ratios, a sum of at most N terms, and |P_t|<=(4^(t+1)-1)/3. Therefore ||T||<=N^C exp(C_T N). The independently proved pointed bridge profile gives max_u E_0(u)<=N^C exp(Nv_8/pi). Hence log C_N(0)<=C_0N+C_1log N. (11) At a minimizer delta_N, C_N(delta_N)<=C_N(0). Combining (10) with (11), and d=N-1>=N/2, proves |delta_N|<=C_2 (12) with an explicit finite constant obtainable from those factorial bounds, independent of N. Thus the optimal local typed metric does not require a bias growing with N or an unknown solution. Its exponential coordinate conditioning is the controlled physical degree weight in (2); original paired boundary norms remain fixed. ## 4. Its optimality equation is an exact physical charge balance If the largest eigenvalue in (5) is simple at a minimizing delta, let z be its unit eigenvector. Differentiating the finite matrix sum (8) gives EXACTLY sum_(u,k,a+c=d-k) (c-u) N^2 exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2) |z^*t_u|^2=0. (13) For a multiple largest eigenvalue, the same equation holds with |z^*t_u|^2 replaced by Tr(rho t_ut_u^*), for a positive trace-one rho supported on that largest eigenspace. To see this, the left and right derivatives of the largest eigenvalue are the minimum and maximum quadratic forms of M_N' on the top eigenspace. At a minimum they enclose zero; a convex mixture gives rho. All weights in (13) are nonnegative and sum to C_N(delta) after dropping (c-u). Thus the maximizing output-energy ensemble has zero mean ACTUAL pair-degree charge, a+b-d=u-c. The true bridge angle sum a+c+k=d and cutoff k<=d-u are retained simultaneously. This is a concrete local metric-duality constraint, not an assertion of a complete hyperbolic gluing equation or a peripheral parameter. It concerns the all-input norm optimizer, not automatically the selected original-source distribution. The exact negative-bridge analogue uses the dual physical gauge G^-1, complementary angles and the corresponding E_-(u) profile. The same matrix-potential construction applies. Changing between the two physical gauges retains the actual G^2 interface; it is not a free contraction in this optimization. ## 5. Why it does not yet telescope through an arbitrary prefix For an original preceding braid B and its original source w_0, (6) is the genuine pointed bound ||T L B w_0||^2 <=C_N(delta)||A_delta B w_0||^2, A_delta B w_0=(A_delta B A_delta^(-1))w_0. (14) The conjugated prefix and all its original coefficients remain. A_delta commutes with generators contained in input pair12 or34, but not with the overlapping bridge R_23. Its matrix entries gain the exact pair-degree difference of their physical input/output. Thus one cannot optimize (5) and then keep the untransformed preceding word. This is the retained interface to be controlled in a sequence of bridge eliminations. The new result is an exact, coercive ALL-input step relative to the fixed terminal Gram, preserving all spectator operators and known sources. It improves on a free octahedral maximum by retaining the pointed potential and a physical degree-balance condition. It does not prove a global telescoping potential, a knot-volume upper bound, or geometric survival. No additional presentation counterexample is needed or claimed by this local optimization theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_terminal_bridge_metric.py): eleven levels N=2,...,12. The code constructs L directly from the original R and cap, T from its independently verified closed kernel, and tests (4) on all open columns, arbitrary two-column spectator states, exact paired-source invariance, both coercive bounds, log convexity and the minimizing charge equation. Finite numerical optimization supplements the all-level convex/coercivity proof.

title: When the compact physical star locus can contain hyperbolic geometry
text: # When the compact physical star locus can contain hyperbolic geometry 28 October 2026. The compact Gram intersection is not automatically a real-form locus of zero-volume representations. It CAN contain a discrete-faithful representation: an explicit algebraic figure-eight example is given below. There is also an all-width feasibility criterion, including a necessary common-circle condition on the chosen bridge eigenflags. Thus real compact accessibility depends on the actual bridge marking; it cannot be assumed for a broad knot class. The original cap has an exact nonzero coefficient on every matched product packet, with no asymptotic normalization ambiguity. That computes the cap half of a weighted geometric overlap. It leaves the original braid transition amplitude, and possible cancellation in the full overlap, unproved. ## 1. The compact cap locus is an explicit bridge-generator real form Use the original complete source and the bounded physical meridians of [the cup/cap Gram theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md). A compact head character has |k|=1, e=-conjugate(f), k+k^(-1)+ef=-2, G=[[k,e],[fk,k^(-1)+fe]]. (1) An ordinary adjacent cap relation is H_2 H_1=I. By the triangular factorization, it says L_(-,2)L_(-,1)=L_(+,2)L_(+,1). One is lower triangular with top-left one; the other is upper triangular with bottom-right one. Consequently BOTH are I. All earlier paired L_- prefixes therefore reset after each cap. The chosen top bridge generators are precisely G_1,G_3,..., with their partners inverse. Conversely for ANY G with data (1), the partner k_2=k^(-1), e_2=-k^(-1)e, f_2=-k f (2) also satisfies the compact star conditions, and its two L products are I. Thus the compact top-cap locus is exactly the product of these explicit bridge-generator sets, with based partners inverse. This also includes G=-I, but a discrete-faithful meridian is noncentral. Let a representation of a fixed k-bridge plat be given, and let mu_r be its CHOSEN oriented top bridge meridians, with trace two. It lies, up to simultaneous conjugation, in the compact physical intersection IF AND ONLY IF there exists one g in PGL2(C) such that, for EVERY r, G_r=-g mu_r g^(-1)=[[a_r,b_r],[c_r,-2-a_r]], |a_r|=1, c_r=-a_r conjugate(b_r). (3) Necessity is (1) and the prefix reset. For sufficiency put k=a_r, e=b_r,f=c_r/a_r, construct all partners by (2), and use the given plat representation relations. They are exactly the bottom Nielsen cap constraints. The same common conjugation, not independently chosen frames at the bridges, is essential. Formula (3) is a finite real-algebraic feasibility test at ANY width. ## 2. Equivalent common Hermitian-matrix criterion There is a useful coordinate-free version of (3). It is equivalent to the existence of Hermitian matrices B,J such that B>0, signature(J)=(1,1), J B^(-1) J=B, mu_r^* J mu_r-J =-(1/2)(mu_r-I)^* B(mu_r-I), every r. (4) These are actual matrix conditions on the specified meridians. They do not require an arbitrary choice of a geometric action normalization. Proof in the compact frame. Put J_0=diag(1,-1), B=I. If G is (1), write N=G+I. A noncentral N has null image/kernel line (1,t), |t|=1, and takes the form N=a [[1,-t^(-1)],[t,-1]], a=1+k, |a-1|=1. (5) Direct multiplication gives N^*J_0 N=0 and N^*J_0+J_0N=N^*N/2. Hence G^*J_0G-J_0=-N^*N/2, which is (4), since mu=-G. Conversely for a noncentral trace-minus-two G satisfying that equation, apply it to a nonzero v in ker(G+I). It forces v^*J_0v=0. Thus v=(1,t), |t|=1. In (5), the same equation forces |a|^2=2 Re a, equivalent to |a-1|=1. This recovers (1). The central case is G=-I and is included directly. Under a common conjugation g set B=g^*g and J=g^*J_0g. These satisfy (4). Conversely J B^(-1)J=B makes B^(-1/2)J B^(-1/2) a Hermitian involution of signature (1,1). A unitary diagonalization therefore produces g with precisely those B,J, reducing back to the compact frame. This proves equivalence. ## 3. A genuine all-width obstruction: bridge flags must be concyclic Every noncentral compact G has its unique eigenflag (1,t) in (5), with |t|=1. Consequently ALL chosen bridge eigenflags of a compact representation must lie on ONE generalized round circle before conjugation. For four distinct flags every cross-ratio must therefore be real. Equivalently they must be null for one indefinite Hermitian form J. This is a necessary condition at arbitrary bridge number; it is not claimed sufficient without the amplitude conditions (4). Thus a discrete-faithful representation whose chosen bridge flags have a nonreal four-point cross-ratio is absent from that particular compact physical star intersection. It could still contribute to the original scalar through a complex analytic saddle. Ordinary real Gram moment support would miss that exponential mechanism. The criterion concerns the ACTUAL chosen bridge generators. A change of bridge presentation can change the set of flags. It is not a claim that a given knot has no other compactly accessible presentation. ## 4. Complete two-bridge criterion: an explicit cardioid For two noncommuting noncentral trace-two parabolics put tau=Tr(mu_1 mu_2)-2 !=0, phi=Arg tau in (-pi,pi]. Then (3) holds IF AND ONLY IF phi!=pi, 0<|tau|<=16 cos^2(phi/2). (6) In particular a nonzero negative real tau is excluded. To prove this, write the two compact matrices using (5), with a_j=1+k_j and unit flags t_j. Their trace invariant is exactly tau=a_1 a_2(2-t_1/t_2-t_2/t_1) =4 a_1 a_2 sin^2(delta/2), a_j=2cos(alpha_j)exp(i alpha_j), -pi/2<alpha_j<pi/2, alpha_1+alpha_2=phi. Since cos(alpha_1)cos(alpha_2)<=cos^2(phi/2), this proves necessity. Conversely choose k_1=k_2=exp(i phi), a_1=a_2=1+exp(i phi), and t_1=1,t_2=exp(i delta), where sin^2(delta/2)=|tau|/[16cos^2(phi/2)]. These give the prescribed invariant. Two irreducible trace-two parabolics are determined up to simultaneous conjugation by tau: use their distinct fixed eigenvectors as a basis, obtaining [[1,s],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[t,1]], then diagonally normalize s=1; the remaining parameter is st=tau. This proves sufficiency for the original pair, not only for some abstract representation. ## 5. Exact discrete-faithful prototype inside the compact intersection Use the independently checked figure-eight Riley pair A=[[1,1],[0,1]], B=[[1,0],[u,1]], u^2-u+1=0, u=exp(i*pi/3), from [the marked holonomy proof](marked_braid_holonomy.md). Set a=1+u, z=(5+i sqrt(11))/6, z+z^(-1)=5/3, G_1=[[u,-a],[a,-2-u]], G_2=[[u,-a/z],[a z,-2-u]]. (7) Both matrices satisfy (1), and Tr(G_1G_2)-2=u. There is an explicit conjugation, not just matching dimensions: F=[[a(z-1),1],[a(z-1),z]], F A F^(-1)=-G_1, F B F^(-1)=-G_2. (8) Its determinant is nonzero. The identity for B uses a^2=3u and 3(z-1)^2+z=0. Thus this is the SAME discrete-faithful representation, at the recorded geometric embedding. All algebraic identities hold at BOTH Riley embeddings. Conjugating u,z and every displayed matrix gives the conjugate discrete-faithful place, including the positive-volume convention used in the earlier regulator calibration. Compact accessibility is therefore not confined to the opposite volume orientation. With top meridians (G_1,G_1^(-1),G_2,G_2^(-1)), the actual Nielsen word for the four-plat [2,-1,2,2] satisfies BOTH bottom inverse-pair relations exactly. Symbolically their common Riley factor is u^2-u+1. After the top pair substitutions the remaining free-group relator is a cyclic permutation of the usual figure-eight relation a b^(-1) a^(-1) b a=b a b^(-1) a^(-1) b, so this is the same two-bridge presentation. Consequently the complete compact star intersection can contain a discrete-faithful point. It is not uniformly a trivial, unitary-group or zero-volume representation locus. This is a prototype diagnostic of the GENERAL criterion, not a new figure-eight asymptotic proof or a broad accessibility claim. ### The same prototype has NO wholly real compact source-to-source transport There is an exact limitation even in this accessible case. The top compact point above does NOT imply that the actual incoming cup point pulled through W is also compact. In fact no simultaneous frame makes both endpoints compact for this discrete-faithful plat. The other bottom bridge generator of [2,-1,2,2], in the canonical A,B frame, is C=A^(-1) B A^(-1) B^(-1) A =[[2,u],[u-1,0]]. The three distinct fixed flags of A,B,C are 0,infinity,u-1 in the column-ratio coordinate. Their unique generalized circle has, up to a nonzero real scalar, Hermitian form J_0=[[0,2-u],[1+u,0]], det J_0=-3. Direct exact multiplication gives A^*J_0A-J_0=diag(0,3), B^*J_0B-J_0=diag(3,0), C^*J_0C-J_0=0. (8a) Any common compact frame for A,B,C would, by Section 3, have this same null circle. But (4) forces a NONZERO negative rank-one defect for every noncentral bridge meridian and every B>0. The last identity in (8a) contradicts it for C, regardless of the scale/sign of J_0. Thus the bottom Nielsen cap equations in the weak Gram intersection are weaker than demanding that its transported input variables obey the same physical star real form. This is allowed because the original W is nonunitary: Ad_W does not preserve adjoints. The geometric source-to-source transition here must be treated by complex analytic propagation, not by a positive real canonical map between the two compact cup loci in this fixed physical polarization. New frame adapters could change that question, but would have to retain their source and exponential normalization. This explicitly locates a mechanism by which weak Gram support can fail to see the exponential geometry, even when its necessary intersection contains that representation. ## 6. The original cap packet weight is nonzero EXACTLY The cap half of an admissible real compact overlap can also be computed without a formal Gaussian approximation. The original normalized cup has coefficients phat_(i,j)=x^(-j)delta_(i+j,d)/sqrt(N). For ANY unit vector v in C^N define its actual reflected dual by (J_x bar v)_j=x^(-j) conjugate(v_(d-j)). It is a unit vector and direct summation gives <v tensor J_x bar v, phat>=N^(-1/2). (9) For k cups choose arbitrary unit v_r and put z_0=tensor_r(v_r tensor J_x bar v_r), z=G_top^* z_0, phihat=G_top^* uhat. With ALL original pivot phases retained, <z,phihat>=N^(-k/2). (10) In particular cup-compatible localized product packets have a known nonzero cap coefficient, uniformly in their centers and N. This is the actual positive cap state fixed in the source theorem; it is not a new favorable cap or a division by the knot period. There is an exact whole-source decomposition. Choose ANY orthonormal basis {v_(r,a)} on the first head of each pair and form the matched packets z_a above. They are orthonormal and phihat=N^(-k/2) sum_a z_a, P_N=chi_N N^(k/2-1) sum_a <z_a,W uhat>. (11) Thus every cap coefficient in this complete decomposition is the same positive polynomial factor. A single chosen packet may be included by extending its v_r to an orthonormal basis. The individual projector-weighted term is exactly chi_N N^(k/2-1)<z,W uhat>. For (7) this includes localized packets at the geometric compact point. On each odd head take a Gaussian of width sqrt(N), center N/3-1/2, and phase exp(-i Arg(t_r)j), with t_1=1,t_2=z; normalize on j=0,...,d and use the exact reflected dual above on its partner. The K,e,f mean-square errors relative to (7) and (2) are O(1/N): the clock varies by O(N^(-1/2)) across the packet, the shift error is O(N^(-1/2)), and the endpoint tails are exponentially small. Applying the specified G_top^* changes the shift phase only by Q, so the same leading geometric point is retained. Its cap coefficient is STILL exactly (10), rather than merely a formal Gaussian unit. At the conjugate Riley place the same construction has center 2N/3-1/2 and the conjugated t_r; the source root and pivots remain the original ones. Equation (11) does NOT say that its braid transition amplitudes have the same phase or that the geometric one is nonzero. Those amplitudes still contain the original whole W and can cancel in their sum. The bounded Nielsen constraints control their classical support, not their action-normalized coefficients. No exponential overlap estimate has been proved here. In particular one may not infer that a geometric point satisfying (3) has positive mass in the actual ket Gram limit. The exact criterion (3)-(6) and cap amplitude (9)-(11) locate the next missing quantity: the original braid transition to a geometric matched packet, with its actual analytic cycle, and its cancellation against the other transitions. Weak real Gram support alone cannot supply it; when (3) fails it cannot see that geometric point at all. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_compact_geometric_bridge_criterion.py): exact algebraic compact figure-eight data and literal four-plat Nielsen equations, common Hermitian identity, the two-bridge cardioid construction, and exact original cup/pivot packet coefficients.

title: What the original compact trace does not localize
text: # What the original compact trace does not localize 28 October 2026. Independent lower-bound audit. The exact compact coherent source is a genuine normalized matrix trace. That fact does not make the original crossing a pullback along a map of the compact source, and it does not make its total-normalized selected functional a rational trace on the geometric critical field. The two failures below concern the specified original operators and source, rather than arbitrary replacement periods. They exclude an exact finite-graph Lefschetz shortcut. They do not exclude a semiclassical Fourier-integral or derived-correspondence construction with its own source transport theorem. ## 1. Every original crossing level has a full-rank coherent endpoint Use the balanced factorial basis of the [compact source](compact_coherent_source_period.md), d=N-1, Q=exp(2 pi i/N), x=-exp(-pi i/N), F_k=(Q;Q)_k, F_0=1. Let B be the original checked positive crossing, with its common nonzero Cartan scalar retained externally. In these actual balanced coordinates its coefficient for |a,b> -> |b+k,a-k> is (-1)^k x^(-a-b-k) Q^[ab+(a-b)k-k(k+1)/2] {b+k choose k}_Q (Q x^2 Q^(-a);Q)_k. (1) This is the original coefficient followed by its literal two head factorial changes, as independently specified by `MixedEntries.direct` in the [whole-source audit](../experiments/audit_figure_eight_whole_source.py). No cup or co-source is replaced here. Because Q x^2=1 and Q^(-d)=Q, (1) gives B |d,0> = sum_(k=0)^d c_k |k,d-k>, c_k=(-1)^k x^(-d-k) Q^[d k-k(k+1)/2] F_k. (2) Every c_k is nonzero. Thus the two-head coefficient matrix is anti-diagonal with nonzero determinant: its Schmidt rank is exactly N. There is an equally useful transpose statement: B^t |d,0> = sum_(k=0)^d t_k |k,d-k>, t_k=x^(-d-k) Q^(-k) F_d/F_(d-k). (3) For (3), apply (1) to input (k,d-k) and transfer k, and use (Q^(-k);Q)_k=(-1)^k Q^[-k(k+1)/2] F_k. All t_k are again nonzero. These formulas are valid at every N>=2; neither a numerical asymptotic nor a particular knot is involved. The independent original E/Cartan evaluator also checks both formulas exactly over the existing prime-field realizations for N=2,...,13. ## 2. No exact single-graph pullback, even on a dense rational chart The coherent evaluation embedding for one head is the degree-d Veronese curve P^1 -> P(H^0(P^1,O(d))^*). For two heads its image lies in the rank-one locus for the tensor product of the two head spaces. The endpoint |d,0> is such an evaluation tensor; the binomial normalizations do not alter that endpoint or tensor rank. A weighted composition operator on sections along a rational map f:(P^1)^2 -->> (P^1)^2 has the following necessary property wherever it is defined: T^t ev_p = h(p) ev_(f(p)). (4) It therefore maps coherent evaluation tensors to rank-one tensors on a dense open set. Every two-by-two minor expressing rank at most one is a polynomial in the evaluation coordinates. If it vanishes on that dense open set it vanishes everywhere. If T is invertible its image never vanishes, so indeterminacy at a special endpoint cannot evade this test. Equation (3) contradicts (4). Consequently the actual B is not a weighted pullback on this compact source, even along a rational map defined only generically. Constant changes of frame on individual heads preserve tensor rank, so separate head frame changes do not repair the obstruction. More generally, suppose T is a sum of r weighted graph pullbacks on a common dense open set. Then T^t ev_p is a sum of r rank-one tensors, so it has matrix rank at most r there. The rank-at-most-r locus is closed, hence that bound holds at the endpoint as well. Equation (3) forces r >= N. (5) Thus an exact graph-pullback expansion of bounded branch number cannot be the sought fixed finite geometric Lefschetz model. A genuine quantized canonical correspondence is a different object: it need not act by pointwise composition on holomorphic sections. None of (2)--(5) rules out such an object or its eventual stationary localization. ## 3. The original selected leading source need not descend as a field trace There is a second, independent obstruction to applying [irreducible critical trace nonvanishing](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) without constructing its actual comparison map. Use the exact original positive figure-eight state, with its literal monomial insertions: mu_N(f)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) |(Q;Q)_n|^2 f(Q^n), mu_N(1)=K_(4_1,N)>0. (6) This is the same source as in the [actual quotient obstruction](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md). Its continuous rate is H(s)=2 integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi t)) dt. The logarithmic endpoint singularities are integrable. Comparing the monotone endpoint pieces and ordinary interior Riemann sums gives log |(Q;Q)_n|^2=N H(n/N)+O(log N) uniformly in n. The unique global maximum of H on [0,1] is s=5/6. Indeed H'=2 log(2 sin pi s) has zeros 1/6 and 5/6, with the former a minimum; H(0)=H(1)=0 and H(5/6)>0. Thus for any fixed neighborhood U of 5/6 the normalized mass outside U is exponentially small. For every fixed Laurent polynomial f, positivity and continuity give mu_N(f)/mu_N(1) -> f(z_*), z_*=exp(-pi i/3). (7) In particular the actual leading normalized first moment is z_*. On the critical algebra K=Q[Z]/(Z^2-Z+1) this selected limiting functional is one complex embedding. It is not a Q-valued field trace: its value on Z is nonrational. After extension to C the algebra splits as C x C and the functional in (7) has weights (1,0), up to the order of its two embeddings. Its moment matrix has rank one. This is compatible with the exact finite source and with every nonzero weight in (6). The trace-duality theorem itself remains correct. Its hypothesis is an F-valued functional on an irreducible finite extension over F. The total-normalized selected functional in (7) does not have that rational descent. Taking F=C instead splits the critical algebra and removes irreducibility. Finite normalized matrix trace faithfulness does not supply the missing descent.
