This does NOT disprove rational descent of a separately action-normalized, multi-sector critical module. Division by the dominant total period automatically suppresses any lower-action sector, even if that sector has a nonzero rationally descended coefficient before this division. Thus (7) excludes identifying this particular limiting functional with a rational field trace; it does not show that the conjugate sector's own coefficient vanishes or that a suitable per-sector construction is impossible. Equation (7) is a diagnostic of the already specified original source, not a definition of a new source by dividing an unknown invariant. In particular it is not an adapter proposed for a general knot. ## 4. Consequence for the lower-bound strategy The exact compact trace supplies the original cycle and a faithful finite matrix pairing. It supplies neither the graph hypothesis of ordinary holomorphic Lefschetz localization nor rational descent of the total-normalized leading functional. Both shortcuts have concrete failures above. The separately action-normalized microlocal comparison is not decided by these tests. An action-normalized microlocal correspondence could still solve the problem, but it must construct the geometric summand and prove that the original source has nonzero image there. Rewriting its conclusion as a positive rank in a critical field does not bypass that step. No new broad-class exponential lower bound is proved by this audit.

title: Complementary root arcs preserve the source, but change its relative cycle
text: # Complementary root arcs preserve the source, but change its relative cycle 28 October 2026. A long actual root arc can be replaced exactly by the inverse complementary arc on a regular Fermat fiber. The central norm is compulsory. For a homogeneous original source, the resulting complementary period has an explicitly determined central divisor. Its scalar numerator is the SAME original selected coefficient. There is also an exact global cycle check: after any nonempty set of these complements, its bare ordinary product-torus integral, enclosing all the Fermat roots, is ZERO. The original nonzero source is carried by additional short-arc relative residue cycles. Thus center freedom does not justify substituting a bare convex torus for the original selected cycle. A construction retaining those relative cycles remains possible; it is not supplied by the complement identity. ## 1. Exact complementation with its original source normalizer Use the actual charged polynomial source with d=N-1, I_N(h)=lambda_C(P_h), K_N=chi_N/N sum_h W_h I_N(h), deg P_h=k d, lambda_C=[X_1^d ... X_k^d] mod(X_i^N-C_i). All W_h, pivots and chi_N remain. The equality between lambda_C and the specified Fermat residue, and its center independence at this degree, were proved in the [actual source theorem](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md). Let a genuine two-anchor block be B_L(X_i,X_j;a)=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(X_i-Q^r a X_j). For every 0<=L<=N, set D=B_(N-L)(X_i,X_j;aQ^L), F_i=X_i^N-C_i, K_ij=C_i-a^N C_j. Then the ordinary polynomial identity is B_L D=X_i^N-a^N X_j^N=K_ij+F_i-a^N F_j. (1) If K_ij!=0, D has no zero on the Fermat fiber and is a UNIT in its finite algebra. Its inverse is exactly B_L/K_ij. Thus replacing B_L by K_ij/D is a source-exact identity. There is no numerical normalization chosen by the value of a knot invariant. A nonunit tail coefficient alpha contributes its retained factor alpha^L; loops have already been evaluated as scalar monomials instead. Choose any fixed collection S of block slots, with r=|S|>=1, and write P_h=E_h product_(e in S)B_e. Define the rational representative R_h=E_h product_(e in S)D_e^(-1), K_S=product_(e in S)K_e. On the regular central domain where all K_e!=0, lambda_C(R_h)=I_N(h)/K_S. (2) The left means the SAME selected sum of local grid residues, not an unspecified contour integral of the rational representative. Equation (2) follows from (1) in the finite algebra and the original center independence of lambda_C(P_h). It fixes its central divisor exactly; its remaining scalar is the original period I_N(h). Knowing that divisor does not establish that this scalar is nonzero. For the actual bridge blocks a is a diagram-dependent power of x times an integer power of Q: the h-dependence enters only the latter. Consequently a^N=(x^N)^integer is a signed diagram datum, independent of the clocks. For a fixed choice of potential block slots, even when a length is zero, the same K_S can be retained through the full clock sum. The normalized complementary whole period is then exactly K_N/K_S. Choosing only the long blocks separately in each sector is also legitimate, but its norm product must remain inside that sum. ## 2. The bare source torus of the complemented form is exactly zero Define the rational k-form Omega_comp=K_S R_h(X) dX_1...dX_k/product_i F_i. (3) Take any ordinary product torus T with each radius larger than |C_i|^(1/N), and assume that no D_e vanishes anywhere on T. Such radii always exist: for unit arc coefficients any unequal endpoint radii avoid that edge's roots. The normalization of integrals is (2*pi*i)^(-k). Then EXACTLY integral_T Omega_comp=0. (4) Proof. Complementing one block changes its homogeneous X-degree from L to -(N-L), a decrease of N. Thus deg R_h=k(N-1)-rN. Dilate all radii of T by the same positive factor t>=1. No F_i pole is crossed, since all its roots were inside the original coordinate circle. The D_e are homogeneous, so their zero set cannot cross this common dilation either. Holomorphic top-form Stokes therefore makes the integral constant in t. On the dilated torus the k-form has size O(t^(-rN)): the numerator, dX and the Fermat denominators contribute respectively t^(k(N-1)-rN),t^k and t^(-kN). Its integral tends to zero. This proves (4), without an asymptotic exchange in N. For comparison, the original polynomial form Omega_poly=P_h dX/product_i F_i integrates on this same torus to lambda_C(P_h)=I_N(h). Thus the chosen sum of small grid-residue tori is not homologous to T in the complement of the NEW short-arc divisors unless that source value happens to vanish. Every nonzero original source requires an additional relative residue cycle in this presentation. The statement includes complementing a zero-length block: in the finite algebra 1=K_ij/(X_i^N-a^N X_j^N). This exact unit insertion still creates new off-fiber poles and a zero bare-torus integral. One cannot infer a selected geometric cycle merely from the poles of a chosen rational representative. ## 3. The missing source currents are explicit For one complemented block let P_h=E B_L and write F_other=product_(ell notin {i,j})F_ell. Equation (1) gives the EXACT identity of meromorphic forms Omega_poly-Omega_comp = E/D *[1/(F_j F_other)-a^N/(F_i F_other)] dX. (5) Each term has lost one Fermat denominator. It has zero local product residue at every original grid point because D is regular there. That explains why (1) preserves lambda_C. It does NOT make these currents zero on an enlarged torus: the short-arc divisors can supply the missing pole. Combining (4)--(5) gives I_N(h)=integral_T E/D *[1/(F_j F_other)-a^N/(F_i F_other)]dX. (6) Thus these explicitly retained currents carry the ENTIRE selected source on that torus. They cannot be declared subleading from the complement identity or from central regularity. With several complements, expanding each K_e+F_i-a^N F_j gives the corresponding finite collection of mixed source currents; dependent intersections must remain jointly regulated if they are converted to contour residues. ### A literal unit source cell The actual full closure/reproducing block is B_d(X,Y;Qt)=sum_(j=0)^d X^(d-j)(tY)^j. With the permitted exterior Y^d its original selected coefficient is EXACTLY one. Its complement is D=X-tY and K=C_X-t^N C_Y. On every product torus enclosing both Fermat root grids and avoiding X=tY, its complemented bare integral is zero by (4), while the two currents in (5) have sum one. This is the original reproducing source normalization, not an auxiliary quantum invariant. Both unpivoted t=1 and actual pivotal t=Q^(-1) cases retain these values. ## 4. A constructive finite forest residue formula The additional relative cycles have an exact algebraic decomposition. Choose ANY nonempty forest of actual two-anchor block slots and orient each edge from a child i to its parent p(i). Reverse a block when necessary using its exact identity B_L(X,Y;a)=(-a)^L Q^[L(L-1)/2] B_L(Y,X;a^(-1)Q^(1-L)). Every such scalar and the original gamma,W_h,chi_N remain. Write the oriented selected blocks as B_(L_i)(X_i,X_p;a_i), and put m_i=N-L_i, S_i=B_(m_i)(X_i,X_p;a_i Q^(L_i)), H_i=F_i S_i for a nonroot, H_r=F_r for a forest root, R=(product_i K_i) E. Here P_h=E product_i B_(L_i) includes the actual orientation scalars. Assume generic nonzero centers so ALL path norms C_i-(product_(edges on i->ancestor) a_e^N) C_ancestor are nonzero. This is stronger than merely checking each adjacent K_i. For the actual unit-root phases, a_e^N=+1 or -1, so pairwise distinct centers up to sign suffice. The result extends rationally wherever the corresponding joint residue is defined, but colliding residues must not be split independently. The triangular monic system H=0 has simple zeros. At a nonroot choose either F_i=0, or a short root X_i=a_i Q^(L_i+r_i)X_p, 0<=r_i<m_i. (7) Every component of chosen short edges has one root satisfying its original Fermat equation. This lists ALL zeros of H, not only an assumed geometric branch. With standard Grothendieck orientation, sum_(all H zeros) R(X)/det(partial H/partial X)=0. (8) Here is a direct proof of the zero. H_i is monic in its child variable, of degree N+m_i; a root equation has degree N. Their coefficients depend only on parents. Consecutive monic division in child-to-parent order gives a basis with child exponent <N+m_i and root exponent <N. Every reduction preserves or decreases TOTAL degree: the highest part is homogeneous and the central term decreases degree by N. The global sum of residues equals the coefficient of the top basis monomial. This follows inductively from the elementary one-variable identity that, for monic h, sum_(h(x)=0)A(x)/h'(x) is the highest coefficient of the remainder of A modulo h. The required top degree is sum_i(deg_(X_i)H_i-1)=k(N-1)+sum_nonroot m_i, whereas deg R=k(N-1)-sum_nonroot L_i. Their difference is exactly N times the number of forest edges, which is positive. The top coefficient therefore vanishes, proving (8). Equivalently the leading homogeneous system has no projective zero: start with each root and propagate zero to its children. There is no omitted residue at infinity. For the EMPTY choice of short edges every F_i vanishes. At those points R/product S_i=P_h, so their sum of residues is EXACTLY I_N(h). Consequently I_N(h)=-sum_(nonempty selected-short subsets) sum_(their explicit zeros) R/J_H. (9) All relative cycle coefficients in this complete decomposition are fixed, with no unknown knot scalar. For fixed diagram size its number of points is polynomial in N: it is at most product_roots N product_nonroots(N+m_i). This is a finite canonical residue presentation once the actual forest and orientations have been specified, not a positivity assertion about its terms. The triangular Jacobian is completely explicit. Its factor at i is N X_i^d S_i(X) if F_i=0, (X_i^N-C_i) partial_(X_i)S_i if S_i=0, and at an original forest root it is N X_r^d. At the short root (7), partial_(X_i)S_i =(a_i Q^(L_i)X_p)^(m_i-1) *(-1)^r_i Q^[r_i(m_i-1)-r_i(r_i+1)/2] *F_(r_i) F_(m_i-1-r_i), F_j=(Q;Q)_j. (10) This is obtained by splitting the other roots at r_i. Every factor is nonzero under the stated genericity; its possible exponential size is retained. For an entirely selected SPANNING tree, X_i=beta_i X_r. Homogeneity of E cancels all powers of X_r against (10) and the root Jacobian. The N identical root labels cancel its 1/N exactly, leaving an explicit sum of products of the factorials in (10), the evaluated remaining actual blocks E(beta), and the retained central path norms. This is an exact full-source channel, but it is generally only ONE part of (9). The mixed subsets must not be discarded. More generally, grouping a selected component into one root gives source charge d+sum_selected_internal(d-L_i), which can exceed N-1. Its remaining regular-Fermat root sum has genuine winding sectors. It cannot be called the ordinary top coefficient, or simplified by dropping cyclic aliases, before the stated component sums or a further source identity have been performed. ## 5. An arbitrary-block contraction, with its changed source charge The one-edge case also has a direct ordinary-coefficient formulation. Put m=N-L, b_r=aQ^(L+r), and w_r=1/product_(s!=r)(b_r-b_s), 0<=r<m. For ANY polynomial exterior E and all other original charges equal to d, there is the exact source identity [X_i^d X_j^d X_other^d] B_L E =sum_(r<m) w_r [X_j^(2d-L) X_other^d] E(X_i=b_r X_j). (11) Its ordinary parent charge is 2d-L=d+m-1, and must be retained. The root sum is essential; its individual regular-Fermat channels need not have the same ordinary coefficient. Proof. The Lagrange sums sum_r w_r b_r^p vanish for p<m-1 and equal h_(p-m+1)(b) for p>=m-1. Their generating function is sum_(k>=0)h_k(b)t^k =product_(s=0)^(L-1)(1-aQ^s t)/(1-a^N t^N). Only p<=2d-L can contribute to the coefficient on the right, hence k<=d. In that range h_k is exactly the kth coefficient of the displayed numerator, including its zero range L<k<N. These are precisely the coefficients of B_L needed on the left. This proves (11), without choosing an unknown normalization or a geometric cycle. For subsequent charges larger than d, the same short-root formula cannot simply be iterated: the next complete homogeneous index may reach N, where the denominator above produces aliases. For example N=3,L=2,E=X_i^3, with tail charge 2 and parent charge 3, gives zero on the original side but a nonzero short-root evaluation. The full forest formula (9) retains the necessary mixed channels; further charge/jet reductions require an additional explicit source identity. ## 6. Consequence for a geometric cycle construction Complementation itself is fully authorized by the existing actual source and preserves every normalization. It can replace long arcs by shorter inverse factors and may provide useful geometric charts. But its selected relative cycle has to be transported as well. Equations (4)--(6) show precisely why a bare torus replacement loses the original source, even with arbitrary regular Fermat centers. Large N-dependent centers need extra care: K_e can itself carry an exponential action. It is retained in (1)--(6), and fixed-center tame Fourier-frame estimates do not extend automatically to it. Conversely on fixed compact central domains these factors may be tame, but the relative currents still need not vanish. A successful Rivin comparison would therefore have to map the FULL grid/short-arc relative cycle, or the explicit currents (5), to a source-compatible convex chain and compute its geometric coefficient. Its starting value is not determined by the known central divisor (2). No broad volume upper or lower bound follows from the present complement identity alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complementary_source_transport.py): actual charged polynomials after closure contraction, ALL triangular forest zeros and mixed short subsets, original scalar/orientation/path norms, factorial Jacobians and the spanning-tree root cancellation, a whole original signed pivotal scalar, and the original unit closure cell's zero bare integral versus nonzero source currents.

title: Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor
text: # Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor 29 October 2026. At the original boundary-parabolic complete color, the marked raw augmented-link period differs from its reduced zero-framed quantum/Kashaev evaluation only by a unit phase. The full one-cut ADO modified evaluation has the additional EXACT factor i^(N+3)/N. This is not an assertion about a generic meridian germ's size. It follows by retaining and then specializing that whole normalization germ and all actual turns. ## 1. Which scalar is raw, reduced, or modified Fix N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d and kappa=q^(d^2/2). The raw source here is the one in the [literal augmented pretzel diagram](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md): every full physical crossing has its original common Cartan, the crossing circles are the exact auxiliary pivotal traces L_N, and the main component has k genuine cups, k-1 ordinary caps and ONE original marked cap. Their balanced entries are p_ab=Nx^(-b)delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. The [direct turn/source calculation](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) proves that these are precisely the original left/right duality and the selected cut projector. Specifically, with g=K^(1-N), e=psi phi, psi_a=1,phi_a=1/N and D=g^(-1)e, \[ \operatorname{Tr}(gDC)=\operatorname{Tr}(eC),\qquad m p=1. \tag{1} \] Each cup contributes its actual N, each ordinary cap 1/N, and the single marked cap 1/N^2. Their net scalar is EXACTLY 1/N, the original cut average. There is no other cut normalization waiting outside this raw tensor contraction. Balanced factorial changes cancel by exact basis covariance on every internal wire; their potentially exponential condition numbers are never estimated as an external scalar. At completeness the original twist is \[ \theta_d=q^{(d^2+2(1-N)d)/2}=q^{-d^2/2}=\kappa^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Therefore any recorded change from the actual diagram's framing to the chosen component framings is a product of integer powers of theta_d, and has modulus one. For a braid normalization using total writhe w it is theta_d^(-w)=kappa^w. If individual component self-framings are prescribed instead, their difference from this convention is a linking/framing character, again a unit phase. Mutual crossings are not silently called self-writhe; only the modulus statement is independent of that convention. Let A_raw be the actual tensor scalar and F_red the reduced zero-framed evaluation with the same chosen marked component. With its explicitly recorded framing character zeta_(N,L), \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)=\zeta_{N,L}A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L), \qquad |\zeta_{N,L}|=1. \tag{3} \] This applies to the original auxiliary-circle diagram before or after its exact finite L_N contraction. Each closed auxiliary circle uses an ORDINARY pivotal trace already in L_N, with no added1/N, no division by its zero quantum dimension, and no extra modified dimension attached to it. Modifying every component independently would define a different normalization from the original one-cut source. ## 2. The modified dimension is specialized as a WHOLE germ At fixed root q, use the original meridian M=-q q^alpha=e^u, so alpha=d+u/Log q. The given modified dimension is \[ d_N(\alpha)=-q^{N(1-N)/2} \frac{q^{\alpha+1}-q^{-\alpha-1}} {q^{N\alpha}-q^{-N\alpha}}. \] Substitution, retaining both numerator and denominator, gives the ENTIRE specified local meridian function \[ d_N(e^u)=i^{N+3}\frac{\sinh u}{\sinh(Nu)},\qquad \boxed{d_N(1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N.} \tag{4} \] This is a removable value, not a cancellation of two separately evaluated zeros. The full one-cut modified invariant, by its original definition, is d_N(M) times the reduced selected tangle scalar. Consequently \[ \mathcal N_N(L;M=1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N F_{\mathrm{red}}(L), \qquad |\mathcal N_N|=\frac1N|A_{\mathrm{raw}}|. \tag{5} \] There is ONE such factor, on the marked component. The other components were closed by the ordinary trace in section 1. No claim about q-transverse derivatives is made: (4) is the actual meridian germ at a fixed root, not a substitution of a generic-q ordinary pivot for the full modified source. Equations (3)--(5) prove, in the respective two normalizations, |chi_red|=1, |chi_full|=N^(-1), (1/N)log|chi_red|=(1/N)log|chi_full|+log(N)/N=0. In particular the previously unspecified common external chi_N has zero exponential rate at THIS complete pointing. It need not have polynomial size on an arbitrary moving peripheral germ. ## 3. The enhanced Kashaev comparison extends to a link The original comparison note states its conclusion for knots. The local matrix identities used there also suffice for the present multicomponent source; no quotient-color argument is needed. Here is the missing connectivity check. Let a b-strand braid be colored by the full original V_N and close every head but the chosen first one with the actual pivot. The resulting cut matrix C commutes with E,F,K. This follows by partial trace of the explicit Hopf coproduct identities. For the K-pivot convention, tracing [A,E_prefix K_last+E_last] ordinarily over the last head yields commutation with E_prefix. For F, use K conservation and cyclicity to obtain Tr_last K_last[A,K_prefix^(-1)F_last]=0. Multiplying the original pivot by its complete scalar sign leaves this intertwining assertion intact. Repeating the argument closes all other heads, regardless of how many link components their permutation has. On the remaining V_N, K has N distinct weights and all internal F coefficients are nonzero. Thus C is a SCALAR matrix, at all even and composite N as well. Connectivity of the closed link was not used. The selected Tr(eC) is that scalar. The exact original Fourier/diagonal comparison in [the crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) therefore works unchanged on this link cut. The large factorial similarities on traced factors cancel by cyclicity; the one on the open factor cancels because C is scalar. The local equality gamma alpha_q=alpha_K cancels all writhe factors. This compares the enhanced Kashaev period with the ordinary quantum-group enhancement with unknot value1, without any exponential gauge. To fix the dual/primal convention explicitly, the crossing note uses the dual pivot K^(-1). The original matrix B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-N)) v_(d-j) in [the complete pointing comparison, section 2](kashaev_ado_pointing.md#2-exact-specialization-to-the-original-kashaev-period) intertwines that dual module with the primal one, conjugates its pivot to K, and satisfies R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Those are direct generator and finite-crossing identities. The same full cut scalarity cancels this open-factor conjugation as well. Thus the primal K in the next display and the dual K^(-1) in the enhanced crossing comparison refer to identical scalar evaluations, with no additional normalization character. There is one useful sign when the latter is instead expressed with the ADO pivot/twist. At completeness g_ADO=(-1)^d K, theta_ADO=(-1)^d alpha_q. For a b-strand closure of total writhe w, the trace and framing ratios multiply to (-1)^(d(b-1-w)). If that closure has c components, its permutation gives w congruent to b-c modulo2. Hence \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{ADO}}(L) =(-1)^{d(c-1)}\langle L\rangle_{N} \tag{6} \] in those two explicitly specified enhanced-framing conventions. Other recorded choices of individual zero framings add only their already described unit twist character. In particular \[ \boxed{|\langle L\rangle_N|=|F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)| =|A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L)|.} \tag{7} \] For the odd-pretzel complete augmented diagram there is one main component and s genuine auxiliary circles, so c=s+1. The sign in (6) is (-1)^(ds); it is immaterial to the exponential rate but is not asserted to be one. The local full Cartan and the exact half-twist phases remain IN A_raw and in its proved leading constant. They are not counted a second time in chi. ## 4. What this closes, and its precise limit For the original one-cut enhanced Kashaev link evaluation, the full raw-period asymptotic has EXACTLY the same absolute value and exponential rate. For the full modified ADO evaluation it has the factor1/N and the phase in (4); its leading N-power must be adjusted accordingly. This closes the external normalization gate at the complete augmented source. It does not identify its action with a manifold volume without the geometric face-gluing calibration, and it proves no Dehn-filling or fixed-knot statement. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.py) compares original enhanced Kashaev matrices, ordinary quantum matrices, and the actual ADO pivot/twist through full cuts of both knots AND multicomponent links. It checks scalarity, the component-dependent sign, and the entire modified-dimension germ. It does not replace a link by a knot on the basis of an invariant.

title: Complete actual Casimir packets and their recoupling measure
text: # Complete actual Casimir packets and their recoupling measure 29 October 2026. Every physical integer-degree block has an explicit complete Casimir frame, including all confluent derivative columns. Its inverse is determined by a closed bilinear Christoffel--Darboux measure. That measure has explicit sine-factorial profiles; at degree N-1 all its double-node weights are polynomial. No tame eigenframe is inferred from tame spectral jets. The adjacent complete-channel change has an explicit all-entry product formula before restriction to a total-three-head multiplicity module. Its entries admit finite angle-factorial envelopes, with every inverse normalizer accounted for. The original cup and both cap rows are kept. The remaining marked-source norm and coherent overlap action are not asserted to have the sharp volume bound. ## 1. Literal Jacobi blocks and the high-degree mirror Put `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `x=q^d=-q^-1`. Use the original balanced F,Ecal,K and tensor Casimir Omega as in [the source Hermite theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md). For total degree `0<=T<=d`, write physical states `|u,T-u>`, `0<=u<=T`, and set `v=T-u`. The block J_T of Omega is COMPLEX SYMMETRIC tridiagonal. Its offdiagonal from u to u+1 is A_u=Q^(-v)(1-Q^v)(1-Q^(u+1)), 0<=u<T. (1) Its diagonal is D_u=(Q^(-u)-1)xQ^(-v)(1-Q^u) +(Q^(-v)-1)x^(-1)Q^u(1-Q^v) +q x^2Q^(-T)+q^(-1)x^(-2)Q^T. (2) Both formulas are direct application of F_tot E_tot and the actual Cartan. Every A_u is nonzero. The product is especially simple: B_T=product_(u=0)^(T-1) A_u=(-1)^T s_T^2, s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|. (3) For `T>d`, put `K=2d-T`, `a0=T-d`. Its block is the SAME J_K after translating the physical first index by a0. One proof uses the actual root Chevalley matrix `W|a>=(-1)^a|d-a>`: `W F W^-1=Ecal`, `W Ecal W^-1=F`, `W K W^-1=K^-1`. Chevalley followed by tensor flip commutes with Omega, and its coefficient is constant on a fixed integer degree. Thus the high blocks introduce no additional frame cost or missing channels. The same comparison follows from direct entries (1)--(2). ## 2. Explicit polynomial columns and generic-q confluence Define continuants p_0(z)=1, p_1(z)=z-D_0, p_(u+1)(z)=(z-D_u)p_u(z)-A_(u-1)^2 p_(u-1)(z). For `0<=u<=T` put f_u(z)=p_u(z)/(A_0...A_(u-1)), f_0=1. (4) The characteristic polynomial is P_T(z)=p_(T+1)(z)=product_(j=0)^T(z-c_j), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). (5) There are only simple or double nodes; a collision is exactly `j+l=d`. The self-paired node j=d/2, when integral, is simple. At a simple node take the column f(c_j); at a double node take BOTH f(c_j), f'(c_j). (6) The last-row recurrence gives `(J_T-z)f(z)=-P_T(z)e_T/B_T`. Hence (6) is the exact Jordan chain `(J_T-c)f'=f` at a double node. These are normalized ACTUAL Clebsch columns and their generic-q divided differences, not an arbitrarily supplied Jordan basis. To see this, vary q to zeta near q with ordinary highest weight d. Its highest vector at degree j has coefficients b_0=1 and b_a=(-1)^a x^(-a) Q^[a(j-1)-a(a-1)/2] (Q^(N-j);Q)_a/(Q^(N-a);Q)_a, (7) where in (7) `Q=zeta^2`, `x=zeta^d`. The E equation directly gives its successive ratio. Its divided descendant `F_tot^(T-j)h_j/(Q;Q)_(T-j)` has eigenvalue `zeta^(2N-1-2j)+zeta^(-2N+1+2j)`. Its first physical component is `x^(-(T-j))[T choose j]_Q`, nonzero near the root because `T<N`. Thus normalizing that component to one gives the unique first-row recurrence solution f(zeta,lambda_j(zeta)). This proves (5) by generic distinctness and dimension T+1. For colliding j,l the divided difference of these two normalized columns converges to f'(c); the common zeta derivative cancels. The eigenvalue gap has logarithmic derivative `2N` times `q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1)`, up to its order sign, and is nonzero. All denominators in (7) and in these low-degree descendants have factorial indices at most d. Exact generic-q duality is retained; no fixed-q meridian splitting is imposed on an exact dual cap. ## 3. The complete inverse, including every derivative normalizer Let V_T have the columns (6), grouped by distinct nodes. Different nodes and their chains are orthogonal for the BILINEAR pairing `u^T v`, because J_T is symmetric. This is not a Hermitian positivity assertion. Define `nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1))`. At a simple node c_j, the bilinear block is the nonzero scalar sigma_j=x^T nu_j P_T'(c_j)/B_T. (8) At a double node c=c_j=c_l, put `Q_j(z)=P_T(z)/(z-c)^2` and let r'_j be the derivative of the original normalized crossing polynomial at c. Its exact block is K_j=[[0,sigma_j],[sigma_j,sigma_j eta_j]], sigma_j=x^T nu_j Q_j(c)/B_T, eta_j=r'_j/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). (9) In particular `sigma_j` never vanishes. The full frame and inverse are V_T^T V_T=K_T=directsum K_j, V_T^(-1)=K_T^(-1)V_T^T, K_j^(-1)=sigma_j^(-1)[[-eta_j,1],[1,0]] (10) for a double block; a simple block has inverse `sigma_j^-1`. This proves completeness and gives the ENTIRE inverse, without a condition-number guess or loss of a Jordan channel. Proof of the normalizers. Christoffel--Darboux for the continuants is sum_(u=0)^T f_u(z)f_u(w) =[P_T(z)p_T(w)-p_T(z)P_T(w)]/[(z-w)B_T^2]. Its simple-node specialization gives `P_T'(c)p_T(c)/B_T^2`. At a double node it gives `Q_j(c)p_T(c)/B_T^2` for f^T f', and `[Q_j(c)p_T'(c)+Q_j'(c)p_T(c)]/B_T^2` for f'^T f'. The first physical row of the original checked R in degree T has only the last column, with coefficient `kappa x^-T`. Therefore f_T(c_j)=x^T nu_j, f_T'(c_j)=x^T r'_j at a double node. Since `p_T=B_T f_T`, these formulas prove (8)--(9), including all phases. The actual full Cartan kappa cancels in this argument; it remains on R itself. ## 4. Exact sine-factorial measures, all parities and all degrees Write `a_j=|1-Q^(2j+1)|`. For a simple UNPAIRED j (`j<d-T`), |sigma_j|=s_(T-j)s_(T+j+1)/(s_T^2 a_j). (11) For a double pair `j<l=d-j<=T`, |sigma_j|=N s_(T-j)s_(T+j-d)/(s_T^2 a_j^2). (12) For the simple SELF-paired node `j=d/2<=T` at odd N, |sigma_j|=N s_(T-j)^2/s_T^2. (13) Every index lies in `0,...,d`. To prove these, factor each nonzero node difference into |c_j-c_k|=|1-Q^(j-k)| |1-Q^(j+k+1)|. The first product gives `s_j s_(T-j)`, deleting the partner factor when present. The second is the circular interval j+1,...,j+T+1: delete its self factor, and its unique root-zero partner if present. Root complementation `s_d=N` gives exactly (11)--(13). No separate factorwise N^O(N) bound is used. At T=d this simplifies to |sigma_j|=1/|1-Q^(2j+1)|^2 for EVERY double node, |sigma_(d/2)|=1 at the simple odd-level node. (14) Thus the full degree-d channel MEASURE is polynomial; this does not say the Clebsch frame or its Hermitian inverse is tame. For all double blocks, nonzero node gaps are at least `16/N^2` and the independently derived actual jets obey `|r'_j/nu_j|<=N^2/8`. Consequently `|eta_j|<=C N^3`. The inverse block in (10) has no additional exponential factor beyond its explicit `1/|sigma_j|`. ## 5. Explicit q-Hahn sums and a quantitative angle profile For `T<=d`, set `r=T-j` and `I={max(0,u-r),...,min(j,u)}`. At the actual root the value column is f_u(c_j)=x^r/[T choose j]_Q * sum_(a in I) (-1)^a x^[-(r-u+2a)] Q^[a(a-1)/2+a(r-u+a)] [j choose a]_Q [u choose a]_Q [T-u choose j-a]_Q. (15) This follows by expanding the actual highest vector (7) at the root, then applying the divided coproduct descendant. All three binomial factors retain their true root phases. In particular it is a closed finite Clebsch/q-Hahn sum, with no unknown knot period. Let beta denote the positive sine-binomial magnitude and put E_(T,j,u)=sum_(a in I) beta_(j,a)beta_(u,a) beta_(T-u,j-a)/beta_(T,j). (16) Then `|f_u(c_j)|<=E_(T,j,u)`. For a double pair j,l, |f_u'(c_j)|<=C N^2(1+log N) [E_(T,j,u)+E_(T,l,u)]. (17) For (17), differentiate the ACTUAL generic-q sums before their confluence. Each factorial has index below N and `|D_logzeta log F_a|<=N^2(1+log N)` at the root. There are a bounded number of factorial ratios and quadratic monomials in every summand and its endpoint normalizer. The eigenvalue-gap derivative has modulus at least eight. Thus differentiation costs only the displayed polynomial times the SAME positive factorial profiles. No exponential frame factor is put into the error term. Every beta in (16) is `N w_d(k,L-k,d-L)`, with exact sum d. Equivalently E is `N^2` times a finite sum of THREE such positive cell weights divided by the known boundary weight `w_d(j,T-j,d-T)`. Their charges and the range I are literal integer Clebsch incidence; the denominator is a compulsory boundary metric. Equations (10)--(13),(16)--(17) give a quantitative profile for the entire frame AND inverse, including every Jordan derivative. They are bounds, not assertions that the q-Hahn phases can be deleted at the sharp exponent or that these cells already form geometric edges. For high physical T extend the notation by `E_(T,j,u)=E_(2d-T,j,u-(T-d))`, and use the corresponding low-block measure sigma; inadmissible physical indices have value zero. ## 6. Complete adjacent-channel kernel at arbitrary width Lift the block frames to the full physical pair, preserving total T. Before restricting the THREE-head total Casimir, its complete pair coordinate change has the following exact entry. For input pair degree T, channel gamma (value or derivative type), and third physical index c, choose an output first physical index u. Put b=T-u, T'=b+c. If the physical indices are admissible, the output pair channel delta has coefficient Rcal_((u,T',delta);(T,gamma,c)) =V_T[u,gamma] (V_T'^(-1))[delta,b]. (18) Otherwise it is zero. Here high blocks use the unitary index translation from Section1. Equation (18) is simply the two ACTUAL pair frames sewn at the shared physical index; no complete channel or derivative row has been suppressed. Its entries are products of the finite q-Hahn columns and explicit inverse rows (10). For a double channel use `Ebar=E_j+E_l`, and for a simple channel use E_j. Equations (10),(16)--(17) give, uniformly in all admissible ports, an all-channel estimate of the form |Rcal|<=C N^5(1+log N)^2 Ebar_(T,gamma,u) Ebar_(T',delta,b)/|sigma_delta|. (19) All exponential factors on the right are the stated sine-factorial angle profiles. Restricting (18) to a fixed total-three-head Casimir or a source-generated Hom space is the subsequent genuine Racah contraction; it cannot be assumed from (18) alone. This distinction avoids a spurious tensor-multiplicity assertion at the root. The original signed pair crossing in these frames is exactly kappa times blocks `nu_j` at simple nodes and `[[nu_j,r'_j],[0,nu_j]]` at double nodes; its literal inverse retains the inverse derivative. Thus twist phases remain coherent when (18) is used in an arbitrary original braid. This is an all-exterior operator/source coordinate change, not a replacement invariant. The original pivot, framing, modified-dimension germ and peripheral line are transported unchanged. None is divided by the spectral measure sigma or selected afterward from the knot value. ## 7. The original source and the remaining estimate At degree d the c_* block may be replaced, by its explicit two-by-two adapter, with the uniformly conditioned p,t source frame of [the source Hermite theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md). If g_0=x^-d, its columns in the canonical f,f' coordinates are p=N g_0 f(c_*), t=-(mu_N/gamma_N)p+(g_0/gamma_N)f'(c_*). (20) This retains the original cup, ordinary cap and marked row. Ordinary caps vanish on other Casimir blocks and select the corresponding source derivative row; the cup lies in the source value channel. The marked row does NOT vanish on arbitrary other channels. Its complete coefficients are the explicit sums `m V_T`; in an assembled original plat integer degree forces the final marked pair to degree d, as before. No sectorwise marked-corner substitution is made here. For example a positive spectral packet metric can be specified by giving each canonical simple/double block the positive scalar `|sigma_j|` times identity, with the source block (20) handled in its actual p,t frame. This defines a full positive Gram by pullback through the COMPLETE frame. Its original marked dual norm and its adjacent overlap energies are explicit via (10),(15),(18), but no polynomial or sharp-volume bound for them is asserted. The new result supplies the actual all-channel frame, inverse measure and factorial/angle envelopes needed to ask that question. The remaining sharp step is a coherent estimate of (18) after its actual source-generated restrictions and closure, rather than separate absolute maximization of (16) or of twist eigenvalues. The subsequent [source-generated complete module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) and [positive-source Gram calculation](actual_complete_channel_positive_gram.md) do give polynomial BOTH boundary norms after the actual J recoupling. However its fixed canonical positive-channel energy is [nonsharp already for the original figure-eight](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md). This does not invalidate the frames or measures above; a sharp norm estimate must retain a more selective coherent packet, such as the [source-exact terminal construction](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md), and control its general propagation. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.py): original generator-built blocks, all nodes and derivative columns, full inverse/bilinear measures and phases, finite Clebsch sums, high-degree mirror and original signed crossings/source adapters.

title: Positive complete-channel Grams with the original source
text: # Positive complete-channel Grams with the original source 29 October 2026. The complete source-generated N-dimensional module has an explicit positive Gram, independent of the braid word and its unknown value. All Casimir value AND derivative channels are retained. The original incoming cup and outgoing cap have polynomial norms in this metric. Their exact weighted norms below provide an honest Cauchy inequality for the original reduced scalar. This independently checks the full source formulas in [the complete multiplicity theorem](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md#4a-a-complete-positive-hermite-metric-with-both-original-sources-polynomial). It also identifies the natural positive CD-weighted metric, distinct from the simpler unweighted channel metric. They are polynomially equivalent, so neither changes the exponential target. The unresolved step is an upper estimate on the COHERENT channel energy, not a missing boundary normalization. ## 1. Physical, right and channel coordinates Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d. Let w be the physical degree-d two-head vector representing the COMPLETE actual three-head Hopf intertwiner I_w. The original source module has actual recoupling J, original pair cup p, and ordinary cap ell, with EXACT identities Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, ell J^(-1)=(x^d/N)e_0^T. (1) The module contains every intermediate Casimir Jordan channel. An original signed word W acts on it as W_mult. Its genuine reduced open-strand scalar, with its assigned external line chi_N, is K_N=chi_N ell W_mult p. (2) Equation (2) is the already proved whole-source opening of the marked cut: the exterior is the original Hopf braid, its remaining V map is scalar, and the actual cut functional has value one on I_V. It is NOT a local substitution of an ordinary cap for the unrestricted marked row in an arbitrary exterior. The full marked operator is retained when an exterior is not a Hopf intertwiner. Let V=V_d be the canonical COMPLETE Casimir/Hermite frame from [the all-channel theorem](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md). The three coordinate systems are physical w, right y=Jw, channels z=V^(-1)y. Put F=V^(-1)J. For ANY explicitly assigned positive channel matrix D, G_D=F^* D F, u=Fp, b=ell F^(-1)=ell J^(-1)V, W_ch=F W_mult F^(-1). (3) G_D is positive definite of full rank N. It depends on the specified actual module and D, not on W or K_N. Exactly K_N=chi_N b W_ch u, ||p||_(G_D)^2=u^*D u, ||ell||_(G_D^(-1))^2=b D^(-1)b^*. (4) The two choices considered here are D=I and the positive CD measure `D_CD=directsum |sigma_j| I_(multiplicity j)`. The bilinear CD matrix itself is not being called positive. The complete original Cartan, framing, modified dimension and peripheral line remain in W and chi_N, exactly as assigned before the change of coordinates. ## 2. Exact cancellation in the complete source At a double node c=c_j let `Q_j(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2`, `P_N=T_N+2`, and let nu_j be the original crossing eigenvalue. The canonical frame has endpoints (f_d(c),f_d'(c))=x^d(nu_j,r_N'(c)), K_j=sigma_j[[0,1],[1,eta_j]], eta_j=r_N'(c)/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). Applying its EXACT inverse to (1) gives u_double=(-N nu_j sigma_j^(-1) Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), N nu_j sigma_j^(-1)), b_double=(x^d/N,0). (5) The potentially large crossing derivative cancels in the first component. It has not been dropped: its cancellation uses the full value/derivative inverse, not an independent semisimple evaluation. At a simple node `u=N nu_j/sigma_j`, `b=x^d/N`. There is an exact elementary simplification. The Chebyshev polynomial defined by its recurrence obeys (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. It follows either by differentiating `T_N(2cos t)=2cos Nt`, or by induction in that recurrence. At every double root, Q_j(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c)=c/(4-c^2), sigma_j=(-1)^d x^d nu_j/(4-c^2). (6) Thus (5) is simply u_double=N(-1)^d x^(-d)(-c,4-c^2), b_double=(x^d/N,0). (7) At the odd-level simple node c=-2, sigma=x^d nu, u=Nx^(-d), b=x^d/N. (8) All phases, parity and N factors are fixed. Neither original source has an exponential hidden normalization in these FULL coordinates. ## 3. Unweighted channel metric: the simpler Cauchy prefactor For D=I, let S_N=||u||_2^2 and T_N=||b||_2^2. Then exactly T_N=ceil(N/2)/N^2, S_N=N^2[sum_double(c_j^2+(4-c_j^2)^2)+1_(N odd)]. (9) The notation T_N here denotes a source norm, not the Chebyshev polynomial of Section2. Explicitly, S_N=N^2(4N-1), N odd, S_N=4N^3, N even and N>=6, S_4=192, S_2=64. These are the source formulas proved in the multiplicity note. They also follow directly by summing second and fourth powers of `2cos((2j+1)pi/N)` and pairing the repeated nodes. In particular S_N T_N<=4N^2, EVERY N>=2. (10) With the explicitly known unit source `u_0=u/sqrt(S_N)` define `E_I(W)=||W_ch u_0||_2^2`. Genuine Cauchy--Schwarz gives |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 S_N T_N E_I(W) <=4|chi_N|^2 N^2 E_I(W). (11) There is no contraction to K_N in the definition of this Gram: F is the whole N-channel frame, u_0 has the explicit components (7)--(8), and W_ch is the full original matrix word with every mixed channel, phase and derivative retained. A useful balanced scalar normalization is G_bal=F^*F/N, E_bal(W)=||W_mult p||_(G_bal)^2 =||W_ch u||_2^2/N. (11a) Then the EXACT original outgoing dual norm is `||ell||_(G_bal^(-1))^2=ceil(N/2)/N<=1`, while the incoming norm squared is `S_N/N=O(N^2)`. In particular |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 [ceil(N/2)/N] E_bal(W). (11b) This version needs no additional polynomial Cauchy loss: it uses the original unnormalized incoming cup. It is the same positive Gram up to its specified scalar, not a different source. ## 4. Positive CD measure: exact weighted source norms For D=D_CD, each double block has weight `(4-c_j^2)^(-1)`; the odd simple block has weight one. Let A_N=u^*D_CD u, B_N=b D_CD^(-1)b^*. Equations (7)--(8) give the exact finite formulas A_N=N^2[sum_double((4-c_j^2)+c_j^2/(4-c_j^2)) +1_(N odd)], B_N=N^(-2)[sum_double(4-c_j^2)+1_(N odd)]. (12) In closed form, A_N=N^4/4+N^3/2, B_N=1/N, N even>=4, A_N=N^2(N^2+3N+8)/6, B_N=(N+1)/N^2, N odd, A_2=16, B_2=1. (13) For a direct proof put theta_j=(2j+1)pi/N, so `4-c_j^2=4sin^2 theta_j`. The sum of reciprocal sine squares over odd indices is `N^2/4` at even N and `(N^2-1)/6` at odd N before the factor 1/4. These follow by subtracting even from all root reciprocal-square sums, or pairing the odd and even indices when N is odd. Also `c^2/(4-c^2)=4/(4-c^2)-1`. The first sine-square sum is a finite geometric sum; N=2 is its stated resonance. This proves (13) at composite and even levels without a modular half inverse. In particular `A_N B_N<=2N^3` for every N>=2. With `u_CD=u/sqrt(A_N)` and `E_CD(W)=||W_ch u_CD||_(D_CD)^2`, |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 A_N B_N E_CD(W) <=2|chi_N|^2 N^3 E_CD(W). (14) This is a different natural positive metric from D=I; its source normalizers must not be mixed with (9). Both metrics retain the same complete channel source and original scalar. For the similarly balanced metric `F^*D_CD F/N`, the original outgoing dual norm squared is `N B_N<=2`; its incoming norm squared is `A_N/N=O(N^3)`. Its corresponding unnormalized-cup energy obeys the same bound as (11b), with coefficient `N B_N`. ## 5. One remaining coherent-energy assertion The two channel metrics are polynomially equivalent: I/4<=D_CD<=max(1,N^2/16) I. (15) The corresponding normalized-source energies E_I,E_CD therefore have the same exponential rate, whenever that rate or limsup is considered. No exponential conditioning is hidden by changing between these two explicitly related channel measures. The physical maps V and J themselves need not have polynomial norms. The right-frame generators are the FULL Hermite block matrix `D_braid=kappa r_N(Jordan(A))` and its complete conjugate `C D_braid C^(-1)`, where `C=V^(-1)JV`. Derivative rows remain. A single repeated-generator power costs polynomially, but C can carry exponential energy and phase cancellation. For this fixed positive Gram, the sufficient energy statement would be limsup_N (pi/N)log E_I(W)<=Vol(K), (16) or the stronger specified positive-geometric-partition comparison `E_I(W)<=exp(o(N)) Z_geo,N`. Equation (11) would then give the sharp original upper bound. It is not implied by positivity, the unit spectral values, a Krein conservation law, or polynomial boundary norms. Equivalently one may use E_bal of (11a): it differs from E_I by the explicit polynomial initial factor S_N/N. The subsequent [exact original energy calculation](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md) shows that (16) is FALSE for this fixed candidate Gram already on the true figure-eight word `[2,-1,2,2]`. The odd-level simple channel has the exact coefficient proved in [the finite quadratic transform](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md), forcing `liminf_odd (pi/N)log E_bal>=v_8>Vol(4_1)`. The source/Cauchy theorems above remain exact; this particular positive norm retains more exponential energy than the final period. Both D=I and the polynomially equivalent CD metric have this problem. A [specified terminal packet Gram](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md) provides a different source-preserving metric on the SAME complete module and recovers the sharp figure-eight energy. Its kernel is positively completed, not discarded. A general sharp prefix bound for that terminal construction is still unproved. This theorem solves the complete boundary-norm problem on the actual three-head Hom module (hence the original four-plat source), not the global coherent q-Racah growth problem. At larger bridge width the actual complete multiplicity reduction is known, but a compatible complete-channel positive metric still has to be constructed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_channel_positive_gram.py): original coproduct-built complete source module and endpoint identities, full Hermite inverse and parity, both positive metrics/source norms, and original signed open-strand periods with the prescribed source.

title: The complete original circle has a complex packet through the quarter transition
text: # The complete original circle has a complex packet through the quarter transition 29 October 2026. The actual complete-circle polynomial z_N has a uniform nonzero asymptotic on a FIXED complex neighborhood of c=-2. The source is continued coherently through the quarter-index modulus crossing, using an exponentially accurate analytic diagonalization, a genuine high-index source anchor, and an explicit negative cumulative action for the unwanted channel. No phase-sector assumption is made. This is a fixed-root spectral/color-coordinate theorem. Its parameter below is NOT declared to be a peripheral meridian or an independently changed auxiliary-circle color. Such a source identification requires its own exact transform. All physical Casimir normal derivatives remain in the same original polynomial. ## 1. Statement and original finite source Keep N,d,q,Q,kappa,M,F_r,s_r and the exact A_r,D_r,U_r of [the coherent inner source](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md). Set u=pi r/N, nu_r=(-1)^r q^[r(r+1)] and define the EXACT chirp-normalized source on its physical grid by W_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)e^(i pi d/4)U_r/nu_r. The original Newton coefficient is EXACTLY b_(N,r)=e^(-i pi d/4) [s_(2r)/s_r^6] W_(N,r), z_N(c)=N^2 sum_(r=0)^M b_(N,r) product_(a<r)(c_a-c). (1) This follows by inserting D_r and the original factorial phases; no absolute value replaces the inner sum. The established source formula on strict high-index compact sets is W_(N,r)=w_0(u)[1+O(1/N)], w_0(u)=e^(iu/2)sqrt(sin u), u>pi/4. (2) There is eta_0>0 such that UNIFORMLY for |eta|<=eta_0, z_N(-2cosh eta)=e^(-i pi d/4)a(eta)exp[N j(eta)] [1+O(1/N)], (3) u_*(eta)=atan(cosh(eta/2)), T=2cosh eta, a(eta)=e^[i u_*(eta)/2]/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)], j(eta)=Psi(u_*(eta),eta), Psi(u,eta)=[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi +(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2u)Log(T+2cos v)dv. All branches are continued from real u=pi/4, eta=0; Lambda denotes its holomorphic local continuation in the displayed regular arguments. The amplitude is nonzero. Both a and j are even holomorphic functions of eta, so (3) is equivalently a holomorphic statement on a fixed disk in c=-2cosh eta about -2. It includes all fixed-order normal derivatives on a smaller disk by Cauchy's estimate. ## 2. The exact direction of transport and a source barrier The original backward Ward for U gives W_r=a_N(u)W_(r+1)+b_N(u)W_(r+2), (4) a_N=Q^(-1)(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1)/(1-QY)^2, b_N=-Q^(-1)(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y) /[(1-QY)^2(1-Q^2Y)], Y=e^(2iu). Thus X_r=(W_r,W_(r+1))^T propagates from HIGH r to LOW r: X_r=T_N(u_r)X_(r+1), T_N=[[a_N,b_N],[1,0]]. Its principal eigenvalues in this direction are lambda_slow=1, lambda_fast=-cot(u)^2. (5) They are distinct and nonzero near pi/4, including at the modulus crossing. That fact alone is insufficient for a selected-source claim. Use the [proved analytic diagonalization lemma](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md) on a fixed complex neighborhood of pi/4, with the shift direction in (4). The same proof with the reversed shift supplies bounded V_N=V_0+O(1/N), nonzero diagonal d_s,d_f and R_N=O(exp(-sigma N)) such that EXACTLY V_N(u)^(-1)T_N(u)V_N(u+pi/N)=diag(d_s,d_f)+R_N. (6) The hypotheses here are explicit rational functions, not an unknown solution bound. On |Re u-pi/4|,|Im u|<=pi/32 the sine and cosine are bounded away from zero. The supplied eigenframe has columns (1,1)^T,(-cot^2u,1)^T; it and its inverse are bounded. One may use conservative bounds K=20, nonzero-root/gap bounds1/4 and eventual diagonal bound M=20, after rescaling x=u/pi and taking stadium radius 1/256. The rational coefficients have T_N-T_0=O(1/N) there, directly from Q-1=O(1/N) and their nonzero denominators. Hence the lemma gives a COMPUTABLE fixed sigma>0. Constants may be coarse; no optimal conversion exponent is needed. Choose a fixed sufficiently small delta>0, h=delta/4, and a high anchor grid point u_b=pi/4+2delta+O(1/N). Require delta<pi/4096 and 16delta^2/pi<sigma/4. Propagate(6) over [pi/4-h,u_b]. The cumulative REAL logarithmic action of the fast channel relative to the slow one is A_f(u)=pi^(-1)integral_u^(u_b)2log cot v dv. (7) This is the sign appropriate to HIGH-to-LOW transport, not its inverse. On this interval the total diagonal action width is at most 16delta^2/pi+O(1/N). For every target |u-pi/4|<=h the action in(7) is at most -gamma_0 for a fixed gamma_0>0. For example -8<=d(2log cot v)/dv<=-4 on the small window; the negative contribution from pi/4 to pi/4+2delta exceeds the possible positive contribution from pi/4-h to pi/4 by a fixed multiple of delta^2. At the high anchor, the ACTUAL source vector from(2) is w_0(u_b)(1,1)^T+O(1/N). Its slow component in V_N is bounded away from zero, and its fast component is O(1/N). Both entries are literal finite original U sums. In the interaction picture, all off-diagonal terms in(6) are bounded by exp[-N(sigma-width)]. Their product is I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-width)]). Equations(2),(7) therefore give, on the whole target grid, the selected slow solution with error O(exp(-gamma N)), for some fixed gamma>0. The other actual source component and every conversion term have been estimated, not deleted. There is no assumed adiabatic survival across a long crossing interval. ## 3. A holomorphic interpolant of the SAME selected grid packet The slow diagonal has d_s=1+O(1/N), holomorphically. Apply optimally truncated Euler--Maclaurin to the sum of Log d_s from u to u_b and multiply by the first component of V_N and its EXACT source coefficient at u_b. Construct it first on a fixed smaller complex tube containing the ENTIRE interval [pi/4-h,u_b], and then restrict to a still smaller tube around |u-pi/4|<=h. This defines a zero-free holomorphic function W_hat_N(u); its high-anchor value is part of the same interpolant, not an independent continuation constant. The usual analytic remainder is explicit: Cauchy bounds on a tube of radius a give a remainder bounded by C N[K/(pi aN)]^(2K); choose K=floor(cN). Thus, after shrinking the tube once, W_(N,r)=W_hat_N(pi r/N)+O(exp(-gamma' N)) (8) on its physical grid. This construction uses known coefficient functions and the finite source anchor; its normalization is not defined using the unknown closed circle value. The same EM formula at u and u+pi/N gives its diagonal shift relation with an exponential holomorphic residual. Together with(6) this makes W_hat_N satisfy(4) with an exponential residual throughout the tube. It and its derivatives are uniformly bounded: Log d_s=O(1/N), its sum is O(1), and the slow eigenvector component stays near1. Its leading amplitude is explicit, not a new connection constant. Expanding(4), using a_0+b_0=1, gives W_hat_N'/W_hat_N =-2i [partial_Q(a_N+b_N)]_(Q=1)/(a_0+2b_0)+O(1/N) =iY/(Y-1)+O(1/N). The denominator is -4Y/(1-Y)^2, so is nonzero. The high source anchor(2) fixes the solution of this first-order transport on the whole anchor-to-target tube. Integration on the fixed complex tube proves W_hat_N(u)=e^(iu/2)sqrt(sin u)[1+O(1/N)] (9) UNIFORMLY and holomorphically on the smaller tube, now through BOTH sides of pi/4. The exponential grid residual in(8) is separate from the inverse-N leading-amplitude error in(9). ## 4. Coherent outer sum, retained residuals and the full complex saddle At eta=0 the old ALL-index envelope of the exact source is J_1(u)+E(u), where J_1'=4log cot u/pi and E'=-2log cot u/pi below pi/4, E=0 above it. Hence its unique maximum is j_0=v_8/pi at pi/4. Every index outside the fixed window in(8) has a strict exponential gap. This includes all lower indices; they have not been set to zero. The same gap holds uniformly for sufficiently small complex eta. One can bound the Newton factor on its fixed enclosing Bernstein ellipse. Its continuum logarithm converges uniformly to the eta=0 logarithm as the ellipse shrinks: the only endpoint singularity is the integrable log(2+2cos v). Thus first choose the r-window/gap, then the fixed eta disk. The polynomial all-index prefactors do not affect the gap. On the retained window use(8), with the actual half-shift Newton product and sine factorials. These have zero-free holomorphic interpolants with exponentially small RELATIVE grid residuals. For the sine factorial, separate log(sin v/v), keep Gamma(k+1) exactly, and apply the same optimal EM bound to the regular factor. For the Newton product apply midpoint EM to Log(T+2cos v); its leading prefactor is ONE. All arguments here lie in regular compact strips. The discarded indices and ALL grid interpolation residuals are bounded absolutely by poly(N)exp[N(j_0-g)] for some fixed g>0, uniformly on a sufficiently small complex eta disk. This is not a claim inferred from pointwise O(1/N) continuation. The exact interpolant is used before its leading approximation, just as in the previous mixed-color source. For the retained finite r-sum choose half-grid vertical endpoints. Its exact cotangent rectangle has vertical |cot(Nu)|<=1. Their source phases have a fixed endpoint gap. At fixed height d_0 the horizontal cotangent errors are O(exp(-2Nd_0)), while the complete phase increases by at most C d_0^2 at eta=0. Choose d_0 small, then shrink the complex eta disk again. All four residual currents are strictly below the nearby saddle. The two constant cotangent parts give the same analytic integral with density N/pi; no integer residue or endpoint term has been discarded. The exponent is Psi in(3). At eta=0 its unique saddle is pi/4, with Psi_uu=-8/pi. Its analytic continuation is u_*(eta), and stays in the fixed interpolation tube. Ordinary analytic Gaussian expansion, with its fixed nonzero source density from(9), gives(3). Inserting the explicit sine-factorial prefactor gives exactly the stated a(eta). The external exp(-i pi d/4) and the unchanged Cartan normalization are already in(1), at both parities. Alternatively, this analytic leading coefficient is fixed uniquely by its agreement with the already proved real eta>0 formula on the nonempty overlap where the saddle lies strictly above pi/4. This identifies its continuation through eta=0 without an extra endpoint or parity factor. ## 5. Nodal concentration, original normals, and a retained-belt corollary The new packet has j(0)=j_0, j''(0)=1/(2pi), a(0)=2^(-9/4)e^(i pi/8). For real theta near0 this yields the whole original nodal packet z_N(-2cos theta)=e^(-i pi d/4)a(i theta) exp[Nj(i theta)][1+O(1/N)], j(i theta)=j_0-theta^2/(4pi)+O(theta^4). (10) There is also an exponential nodal gap outside every fixed theta neighborhood. For a root c_a in[-2,2], the factor at a unit w obeys |c_a-w-w^(-1)|<=|c_a-Rw-(Rw)^(-1)| for R>1. Apply the established same-angle circle envelope and let fixed R decrease toward1. Its continuum arc-convolution profile is continuous, has a unique maximum at(theta,u)=(0,pi/4), and has strictly smaller endpoint values. Compactness proves the gap. This uses the coherent U envelope, not a sector claim. For precision, the convolution is over the symmetric arc[-2u,2u] of g_1(t)=log|1-e^(it)|, centered at pi+theta. For0<u<pi/2, g_1 is strictly increasing with circular distance from0, so this arc integral has its unique maximum at theta=0. At u=0 or pi/2 it is constant in theta, but the resulting all-index actions are strictly less than j_0. Moreover ||g_R-g_1||_(L^1(S^1))->0, which bounds the difference of ALL these arc integrals uniformly in both u and theta. Thus the limiting argument uses a uniform integral bound, not pointwise logarithmic convergence at a root. Equation(3) is holomorphic in c, so the original first-normal source is retained by differentiating it on a smaller disk. For example z_N'(-2)/z_N(-2)=-N/(4pi)+O(1). Nothing is replaced by a value-only semisimple trace. The [exact complete-belt source](actual_complete_circle_nodal_energy_and_belt_sewing.md) therefore has, for every fixed integer k>=1, the nonzero ALL-parity asymptotic phi(L_N(z_N^sharp z_N)^k) =N^(3/2) 2^[-(9k+1)/2]/sqrt(k) exp(2kNj_0)[1+O(1/N)]. (11) Indeed its exact source is N sum_(a=0)^(N-1)|z_N(c_a)|^(2k). The nodal angles around -2 have step2pi/N, with shift0 for oddN and1/2 for evenN. The Gaussian in(10) gives the same leading sum at both shifts; all other nodes have the proved exponential gap. The derivative source producing this exact belt trace remains literal. This establishes a genuine complete-circle boundary packet and a whole original retained-belt amplitude. An independently changed ordinary auxiliary color, a filling transform, or a branched six-port sewing must still be identified with this packet by an exact source map. They are not inferred merely from the spectral parameter eta. Audit: [literal finite circle coefficients, quantum recurrence/chirp and boundary Gaussian](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.py), the finite checks cover eleven literal all-parity full sources and first normals, exact symbolic chirped recurrence/transport, and six growing-N complex-packet/normal/retained-belt calibrations. The analytic proof, not those finite calibrations, establishes the fixed neighborhood and the exponential current bounds. The theorem concerns the stated spectral packet and complete retained-belt source. The physical color and filling identification is separate.

title: A sharp complete-circle nodal energy from the original source
text: # A sharp complete-circle nodal energy from the original source 29 October 2026. The actual complete-circle packet has the sharp physical-node exponent \(v_8/\pi\). This follows from an exact discrete Chebyshev identity and the already proved NONZERO finite-source asymptotic on each fixed Bernstein ellipse. It needs no assertion about the phases of all Newton or monomial coefficients. Consequently a retained complete belt gives a positive original source, with an exact rate for every fixed reflected power. This is an all-channel source theorem. Its interpretation as a family of geometric belted sums requires a separate literal disk-gluing certificate; it is not inferred from the rate. ## 1. The unchanged packet and the actual complete belt Use \(N\geq2,d=N-1,q=e^{\pi i/N},Q=q^2\), and \[ M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor,\qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad 0\leq a<N. \] These are the actual pair-Casimir nodes. Write \(m_c=2\) at each double node and \(m_{-2}=1\) at the odd simple node, so \(\sum_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}m_c=N\). Let \[ z_N=\mathscr R(R^{-1}L_N),\qquad z_N^\sharp=\mathscr R(RL_N),\qquad j_0=v_8/\pi. \tag{1} \] Here \(R\) is the FULL original checked crossing, \(L_N\) its literal ordinary auxiliary-circle trace, and \(\mathscr R\) the genuine unscaled turn. The sharp sign is coefficient conjugation in the real Casimir variable, realized by the stated actual reflected diagram. The [complete polynomial proof](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) gives \(\deg z_N=M\), at every parity, including every Casimir normal. The [full-circle sewing theorem](general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md#7-complete-circle-connectors-a-coherent-channel-sum-not-independent-blocks) proves on the FULL root algebra \[ \phi(L_Nfg)=N\sum_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}m_c f(c)g(c). \tag{2} \] The positive weights in (2) come from the retained derivatives of \(L_N\) at its double zeros. Thus (2) does not discard the original nonsemisimple normal source. In particular the complete belt has not been replaced by a value-only trace with different normalization. ## 2. Exact discrete Chebyshev sampling, with both endpoint parities Let \(T_k(\cos\theta)=\cos(k\theta)\). For \(0\leq k,l\leq M\), \[ \frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}T_k(c_a/2)T_l(c_a/2) =\begin{cases}1,&k=l=0,\\1/2,&k=l>0,\\0,&k\ne l.\end{cases} \tag{3} \] Indeed \(\sum_a e^{in(2a+1)\pi/N}=0\) for \(0<|n|<N\), and \(k+l\leq2M<N\). Product-to-sum proves (3). Replacing the sum over \(a\) by the distinct-node sum with weights \(m_c\) is EXACT. The odd endpoint \(-2\) has weight one; there is no duplicated simple node or omitted even middle node. For any complex polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(M\), write \[ f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^M a_kT_k(z/2),\qquad b(f)=\max_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}|f(c)|. \] Equation (3) gives \[ a_0=\frac1N\sum_cm_cf(c),\qquad a_k=\frac2N\sum_cm_cf(c)T_k(c/2)\quad(k>0). \] Hence \(|a_0|\leq b(f), |a_k|\leq2b(f)\). For fixed \(\eta>0\), \[ \boxed{\quad |f(-2\cosh\eta)|\leq(2M+1)e^{M\eta}b(f) \leq N e^{M\eta}b(f). \quad} \tag{4} \] This uses \(T_k(-\cosh\eta)=(-1)^k\cosh(k\eta)\), not an extrapolation of numerical root values. It is stable at all levels. ## 3. Sharp maximum on the actual physical nodes The [proved finite-source circle theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), equations (9),(13)--(15), supplies for EVERY fixed \(\eta>0\) \[ z_N(-2\cosh\eta) =e^{-i\pi d/4}a(\eta)e^{Nj(\eta)}(1+o(1)), \qquad a(\eta)\ne0, \tag{5} \] \[ \limsup_N\frac1N\log\max_{|w|=e^\eta} |z_N(w+w^{-1})|\leq j(\eta),\qquad \lim_{\eta\downarrow0}j(\eta)=j_0. \tag{6} \] These are estimates for the literal finite polynomial, not a formal critical value or an unspecified contour. In particular (5) has a proved nonzero source amplitude. The limiting value in (6) follows from the displayed Lobachevsky formula there: \(j(0)=8\Lambda(\pi/4)/\pi=v_8/\pi\). Put \(b_N=b(z_N)\). The segment \([-2,2]\) lies inside every fixed Bernstein ellipse \(z=w+w^{-1},|w|=e^\eta\). The maximum principle and (6) give \[ \limsup_N N^{-1}\log b_N\leq j(\eta). \] Conversely (4),(5), and \(M/N\to1/2\) give \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log b_N\geq j(\eta)-\eta/2. \] Let \(\eta\downarrow0\) AFTER these limsup/liminf inequalities. No estimate uniform in a shrinking ellipse is required. We obtain \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log \max_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}|z_N(c)|=\frac{v_8}{\pi}.} \tag{7} \] This does not assert that the maximizing node is always \(-2\), or that \(z_N(-2)\) has a nonzero limiting prefactor. In particular it does not require a special odd-level simple-node argument. ### A reusable bandlimited cyclotomic source criterion The same proof applies to ANY sequence of actual two-port source polynomials \(f_N\) of degree at most \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). Suppose that for each fixed \(0<\eta<\eta_0\) an actual finite-source estimate proves \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log|f_N(-2\cosh\eta)|\geq j(\eta), \qquad \limsup_N N^{-1}\log\max_{|w|=e^\eta}|f_N(w+w^{-1})| \leq j(\eta), \tag{7a} \] where \(j(\eta)\to j(0)\in\mathbb R\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\). Then the exact DCT and the maximum principle give \[ \lim_N N^{-1}\log\max_c|f_N(c)|=j(0),\qquad \lim_N N^{-1}\log\phi(L_N f_N^\sharp f_N)=2j(0). \tag{7b} \] For the second assertion use (2), with \(N\max_c|f_N(c)|^2\leq\phi(L_N f_N^\sharp f_N) \leq N^2\max_c|f_N(c)|^2\). Thus (7a) is a concrete sufficient source/Fourier criterion for this complete-belt energy. It requires an actual selected-source lower estimate, not only a classical algebraic curve or a formal principal symbol. The verified packet \(z_N\) supplies (7a) by its finite-source central Gaussian, with no new assumption. The degree/nonaliasing hypothesis is essential. There are only \(M+1\) distinct physical nodes. Their product polynomial \(G_N(z)=\prod_c(z-c)\), of degree \(M+1\), is nonzero in the FULL Casimir algebra but vanishes at every physical node. Consequently its retained-belt energy is zero. At even \(N=2L\), explicitly \(G_N(z)=2T_L(z/2)\), so it has the nonzero radial exponential rate \(\eta/2\) while its sampled maximum vanishes identically. Its normal directions have not vanished in the full algebra; it is the exact complete-belt functional that pairs them to zero. Neither an arbitrary degree-near-\(N\) packet nor a saturated classical curve can be substituted into this bandlimited theorem. ## 4. Exact positive energies for arbitrary fixed reflected powers For any FIXED integer \(k\geq1\), define the literal complete-belt source \[ \mathcal B_{k,N} =\phi\!\left(L_N(z_N^\sharp z_N)^k\right) =N\sum_cm_c|z_N(c)|^{2k}>0. \tag{8} \] Strict positivity at every \(N\) follows already from the exact nonzero degree-\(M\) polynomial: it cannot vanish at all \(M+1\) distinct physical nodes. No asymptotic lower estimate is needed for this finite-level assertion. All the ports before the final closure remain those of the original two-strand tangle. Equation (8) consists of \(2k\) actual turned circle boxes in series, with ONE retained auxiliary complete circle around their two physical strands, and the original marked closure. It is not a metric defined from its final scalar. At every fixed \(N\) \[ N b_N^{2k}\leq\mathcal B_{k,N}\leq N^2 b_N^{2k}. \] Consequently \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_N N^{-1}\log\mathcal B_{k,N}=2k\frac{v_8}{\pi}, \qquad \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\mathcal B_{k,N}=4k v_8.} \tag{9} \] More generally let \(F_N=R^{e_N}z_N^a(z_N^\sharp)^b\), where \(a,b\geq0\) are fixed, \(a+b>0\), and \(e_N\) is ANY integer. The physical nodal values of \(R\) have modulus one, including even/composite levels. Therefore, EXACTLY, \[ \phi(L_NF_N^\sharp F_N) =N\sum_cm_c|z_N(c)|^{2(a+b)}, \tag{10} \] and its exponent is \(2(a+b)j_0\), independently of the twist. This is a source-preserving statement at this particular retained complete-belt seam. It is not a claim that arbitrary filled exterior volumes ignore twists: the complete belt cusp is still present. For the cut box \[ f_N=z_N^\sharp R^{-1} \] of the verified two-octahedron base, \(f_N^\sharp f_N=z_N^\sharp z_N\) in the FULL actual algebra, so (8) is also its genuine reflected complete-belt sewing. Its quantum cut differs from the Newton reflection cut used to prove that original base's rate. The one-cut reduced normalization and its recorded component/frame characters are those of the [complete-point comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md). They have modulus one, or the stated single \(N^{-1}\) in the one-cut modified convention. They do not alter (9). No extra modified dimension is assigned to each auxiliary circle. ## 5. The remaining geometric gluing condition The [two-octahedron cut certificate](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md) supplies a concrete base and its actual twice-punctured crossing disks. The [literal stack and outer-collar theorem](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) now matches (8) with these actual geodesic pants gluings and proves its balanced complete-link volume equality. It also gives the metric for arbitrary fixed sign words and fixed integer outer collars; the nonzero asymptotic in that broader case uses the separate [coherent source Gaussian](actual_coherent_octahedral_belt_stack_asymptotic.md), not the positive-energy argument alone. General tangle or branched graph sewings do not inherit this particular collar certificate. In particular (8) must NOT be reinterpreted as a tree of scalar Frobenius vertices. Such a tree inserts \(L_N^{|E|}\) and vanishes at every even level when \(|E|\geq2\), as the exact earlier source calculation shows. A branched physical vertex has six open legs and its original saturated source kernel; (7) does not replace that kernel or prove its geometric energy bound. A general graph/filling volume conjecture remains open here. Audit: [full physical belt sources and exact discrete sampling](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_nodal_energy_and_belt_sewing.py). The exact nodal sewing is restricted to the stated seam. It does not establish a geometric or arbitrary-six-port extension.

title: The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial
text: # The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial 30 October 2026. The complete ROOT circle, with its original weight and literal W/pi cup normalization, has an exact homogeneous polynomial factorization in its four face diagonals. For EVERY original folded channel that polynomial has nonnegative coefficients. Its local zeros enforce the original unwrapped channel support on a modular physical-head grid. Both level parities are included. This is local source algebra. The global face-grid measure, marked coefficient, stationary angle balance and original relative period are separate statements. ## 1. Exact local variables, lifts and scalar Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and keep an actual integer 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Write m=d-a, s=d-2a and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), k_a=1 if s=0, otherwise k_a=2. Let x,b,c,y be the outer, incoming-middle, outgoing-middle and final face diagonals, respectively. Choose their logarithms and use the literal centered physical heads S=d/2+N(Log x-Log b)/(2pi i), R=d/2+N(Log x-Log c)/(2pi i), sigma=d+N(Log x-Log y)/(2pi i). (1) The other physical heads are sigma-S and sigma-R. The auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, with its actual complement 2a-r. Thus Q^S=-q^-1 x/b, Q^(sigma-S)=-q^-1 b/y, Q^R=-q^-1 x/c, Q^(sigma-R)=-q^-1 c/y. The physical half-index and the auxiliary finite color are not confused. Define, using the original Hermitian matrices H_-,H_+, D_a(x,z,y)=det[z I+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y). (2) The empty determinants and products are one. Then the full coefficient of the specified regular root complete-circle source is EXACTLY h0_a W_a pi_a =k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y) D_a(x,c,y) Ptilde_s(x,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (3) This is the fixed-root Hopf lift from the [original source envelope](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md), not a newly chosen off-grid continuation of a canceled exceptional kernel. A retained half twist multiplies (3) by its original fixed scalar omega_a^epsilon. Every power in (3) uses the logarithms in (1). If one adds literal N-lifts to R,S,sigma, the multiplier is (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)]. The degree lift n_sigma cancels. It is identically one at odd N; at even N it must be retained or canceled by a proved global source-character calculation. Formula (3) makes no independent wrapping of an out-of-basis head. ## 2. Proof from the literal large white and cups At the root the actual white and dual are W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m q^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^1(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m, pi_a(r;i,j)=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)]. Here gamma_a=q^(2-a^2)/N^2 is FIXED, h0_a=k_a N beta_a, pV(z)=N q^(-d^2+dz), and no paired norm pi_a W_a is inverted. The exact Chevalley factor is W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=q^[s(a-r)]W_a(i,j;r). Let T=Q^sigma and P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j). The exact root reflection of the SPECIFIED factorial section gives p_(2a)(d+a-sigma) =F_s q^[2m(d+a)] T^-a/P_s(T). (4) Indeed p_(d-s)(z)=F_s exp(pi i z)q^[(s-1)z] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(z+j)); substitute z=d+a-sigma and retain exp(pi i z)=q^(Nz) literally. This proves (4) before canceling its possible poles. The root identities H_m=H_a P_s and H_a(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=q^(a^2) beta_a, are source-exact finite polynomial identities. For comparison with the previously normalized entire circle C_a, substitution in the preceding literal W/pi expression gives the same head factor q^[d(R+S-2sigma)]/P_s(T) as in C_a. Its remaining scalar ratio is one: use F_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2] S_j, S_(d-j)=N/S_j. The ratio reduces to q^[-2N(-2N+a+3)]=1. This proves h0_a W_a pi_a=C_a as the specified meromorphic root functions, not just at physical nodes. It does not identify their moving-q germs with a different generic lift. Now use the exact original normalized coefficient C_a=k_a V_a(d-sigma) q^[d(R+S-sigma)-2a^2] H_a(U_o,V_o)H_a(U_i,V_i)/T^a, V_a(h)=product_(j=a+1)^m 2sin(pi(h+j)/N). On the logarithms (1), direct factorization gives V_a(d-sigma)=Ptilde_s(x,y)/(xy)^(s/2), H_a(-q^-1 x/z,-q^-1 z/y)=(-q^-1)^a K_a y^-a D_a(x,z,y), q^[d(R+S-sigma)]=(xy/(bc))^(d/2). (5) For the first identity, the scalar in the sine product is i^s q^[-sum_(j=a+1)^m j]=i^s q^(-sN/2)=1. The remaining powers of xy cancel because d=2a+s, and K_a^2 q^(-2a^2)=beta_a^2. This proves (3) with its exact scalar. The same formulas show that additional N-lifts contribute (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)+(s-d)n_sigma]=(-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)], since s-d=-2a. ## 3. Coefficient positivity and homogeneity D_a is homogeneous of degree a in x,z,y and has NONNEGATIVE REAL coefficients. This follows directly from the actual positive matrices, without assuming their entries are real. Factor H_-=B_-B_-* and H_+=B_+B_+*, and apply Cauchy--Binet to the rectangular matrix [sqrt(z) I, sqrt(x/2) B_-, sqrt(y/2) B_+]. Its determinant expansion is a sum of squared absolute minors times the indicated monomials, hence has the claimed coefficients. Since all three source matrices I,H_-,H_+ are positive definite, every homogeneous monomial of degree a in the three variables in fact has positive coefficient: subtract a sufficiently small positive multiple of I from each matrix, then select the three identity parts in the same Cauchy--Binet expansion. This is a coefficient statement for each fixed N,a; no uniform lower coefficient bound is claimed. More strongly, the retained forced product has the exact positive expansion for EVERY original folded label: Ptilde_s(x,y)=sum_(j=0)^s [S_s/(S_j S_(s-j))] x^(s-j)y^j. (7) To prove it, multiply its finite linear factors, or induct on their number, to obtain the coefficient (-1)^j Q^[(a+1)j+j(j-1)/2] [s choose j]_Q. The exact finite Gaussian coefficient is [s choose j]_Q=q^[j(s-j)] S_s/(S_j S_(s-j)). The remaining q exponent is j[2a+2+j-1+s-j]=j(2a+1+s)=jN. Its factor q^(jN)=(-1)^j cancels the displayed sign. This proves (7), whose coefficients are strictly positive because s<N. It also retains both maximal-fold parities: Ptilde=1 at odd simple fold and Ptilde=x+y at even maximal fold. No quarter-channel restriction is needed. The numerator in (3) is consequently a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2a+s=d with nonnegative coefficients in the four face variables. The monomial denominator and all finite logarithmic carries are still part of the source. Evaluating some face variables at complex values does not preserve positivity of the resulting specialized coefficients. ## 4. Local modular support retains one forced zero Take physical heads i,j in {0,...,d}, sigma=i+j. In the original white the unwrapped auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, so its actual allowed range is 0<=r<=2a, equivalently m<=sigma<=d+a. (6) At U=Q^i,V=Q^j, every Newton summand of H_a has factors forcing k<=i and a-k<=j. Therefore H_a(Q^i,Q^j)=0 if sigma<a. Exact root complementation sends the pair to (d-j,d-i), proving the same vanishing if sigma>2d-a. The complete circle retains ONE factor P_s(Q^sigma) after (4) cancels one of the two factors from its large numerators. Hence: * If sigma<m, either sigma<a and the small numerator vanishes, or a<=sigma<m and the retained P_s vanishes. * If sigma>d+a, either sigma>2d-a and the complementary small numerator vanishes, or sigma-N belongs to [a,m-1] and P_s vanishes. These are zeros of the canceled entire root coefficient, not an assignment of a value to an unexplained 0 times infinity. Thus a modular auxiliary residue outside its original support is killed locally even though its individual continued channel cup may have a pole. If both physical pairs of a circle survive and their totals agree modulo N, both totals lie in the SAME interval (6), containing only 2a+1<=N integers. They therefore agree exactly. The auxiliary row is then the original unwrapped row. The complementary physical cup also adds no modular states: i+j congruent to d modulo N with 0<=i,j<=d forces i+j=d, since d-N<0 and d+N>2d. This local check supplies the missing support input for a possible global face-grid transformation.
