Hence e_d is cyclic for A. Since Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, p is cyclic for B on ALL N multiplicities. This establishes complete source generation by the actual character/Ward algebra. It is distinct from claiming cyclicity under one braid alone: at composite levels distinct Casimir nodes can have the same R eigenvalue, and no reduction based only on those eigenvalues is authorized. ## 4. Exact original boundary source and a tame Hermite recoupling The same finite q-binomial identities in (8) give Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, J e_0=p/N, ell J^(-1)=(x^d/N)e_0^T. (12) For example row0 of J is x^(-d)(1,x,...,x^d), whereas ell_j=x^j/N. Thus the cap identity is literal, including its pivot. For EVERY word W in the two original signed crossings, (ell_12 tensor I) W (p_12 tensor I) =[ell W_mult p] I_V, ell W_mult p=e_0^T [J W_mult J^(-1)] e_d. (13) The first equality follows from the actual Hopf intertwiner and Schur calculation on the explicitly simple V: commuting with H makes a matrix diagonal and commuting with F makes it scalar. All actual common Cartan and external framing factors remain. Any originally prescribed cut functional with value1 on I gives that same scalar; arbitrary inserted nonintertwining exteriors must instead retain their literal transported functional. The original degree-d marked row m and ordinary row ell are coordinate duals to p,t on their source Hermite plane. Their full physical use is distinct: for arbitrary w the unrestricted marked contraction is the matrix M(w)_(beta,a)=sum_(u,v) x^v/N^2 [I_w|a>]_(u,v,beta). (14) This matrix, not just m restricted to W, is retained if the actual exterior asks for a marked row on that pair. No scalar replacement of (14) is asserted for arbitrary exteriors. There are useful quantitative bounds BEFORE any ambient recoupling estimate. Let g_r=F_12^r|0,0>/F_r; every one of its r+1 nonzero components is the unit phase x^(-second color). The original Hermite t obeys (A-c_*)t=theta p, theta=(-1)^N rho^2. Since F_12 is injective in degree d-1, this gives exactly E_12^c t=theta N q^(c-1)F_(c-1)/(1-Q^d) g_(d-c), 1<=c<=d. (15) The subsequent E coefficients are q(1-Q^j), giving the product in (15). The distinct last colors in H_L(t) are orthogonal. Using the finite root reciprocal-square identity therefore gives <H_L(p),H_L(t)>=0, ||H_L(p)||^2=N^3, ||H_L(t)||^2=||t||^2+N^3|rho|^2(N^2-1)/24, N^3/4<=||H_L(t)||^2<=pi^2 N^3/3. (16) Thus the two embedded highest SOURCE columns have condition at most2 at EVERY N. This concerns those source columns, not all N multiplicities or arbitrary descendants of t. The full recoupled source frame is also explicit: (Jt)_j=Nx^(-d)(-q)^j(1-Q)/(1-Q^(j+1)), 0<=j<d, (Jt)_d=t_0. (17) Indeed (B^T-c_*)Jt=theta Nx^(-d)e_d; its first coordinate is fixed by ell t=1 and (12). The recurrence in the remaining coordinates has ratio -q(1-Q^j)/(1-Q^(j+1)), proving (17). Its last coordinate follows from the last row of J. Writing alpha=Nx^(-d), remove the e_d component of Jt. The remaining vector z is orthogonal to Jp and satisfies exactly N^2<=||z||^2=N^2|rho|^2(N^2-1)/12<=pi^2 N^2/3. The removed scalar is t_0/alpha=(-1)^N rho Hbar, where Hbar=N^(-1)sum_u sum_(j<=u)(1-Q^j)^(-1). Its absolute value is at most pi(1+log N). Hence [Jp,Jt] has condition at most (pi/sqrt(3))[1+pi(1+log N)]^2. This is a proved tame recoupling of the original two-dimensional source packet into the complete multiplicity module, not an ambient q-Racah bound. For arbitrary complete multiplicities there are specified coherent positive Grams, without a choice depending on the unknown braid: G_high=sum_c (E_12^c)^* E_12^c/|F_c|^2, G_full=sum_a (F_123^a H_L)^*(F_123^a H_L)/|F_a|^2. (18) These give EXACTLY ||H_L(w)||^2 and ||I_w||_HS^2. The right chart Grams satisfy G_left=J^*G_right J. Formula (18) retains all mixed copies; it does not claim polynomial conditioning of the complete Gram or that both braids are contractions in it. The explicit q-Pascal entries (8) can carry angle energy. ## 4a. A COMPLETE positive Hermite metric with both original sources polynomial There is a useful non-diagonal Cauchy metric on ALL N channels, not just the source plane. Use the [complete physical degree-d Hermite frame](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md) V for A: at a double node c=c_j=c_(d-j) take f(c),f'(c), normalized by f_0(z)=1; at a simple node take f(c). Its entire inverse is the bilinear Christoffel--Darboux inverse, not a Hermitian orthogonality assumption. Write nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. For a double node let Q_j(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2. Its exact block is V^T V=K, K_j=sigma_j [[0,1],[1,eta_j]], eta_j=r_N'(c)/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), V^(-1)=K^(-1)V^T, f_d(c)=x^d nu_j, f_d'(c)=x^d r_N'(c). (18a) The single-node formula is V^T V=sigma_j on that block. At degree d the exact normalizers satisfy |sigma_j|=1/|1-Q^(2j+1)|^2 at a double node, |sigma_j|=1 at the possible simple node. (18b) These follow by the Jacobi continuant CD identity: its endpoint residue is Q_j(c) f_d(c)/product offdiag, while its next derivative adds f_d'(c) and Q_j'(c). Thus the inverse and every normalizer in (18a) are fixed by the original Jacobi matrix; no selected knot value or favorable metric is used. The TRUE complete source-multiplicity Racah matrix is C=V^(-1) J V. (18c) This is already restricted to the N-dimensional actual Hom space. It is not the larger physical adjacent-frame product before total-character restriction. In RIGHT channel coordinates z=V^(-1)Jw the complete positive inner product is ||w||_ch^2=||V^(-1)Jw||_2^2. (18d) It is full rank, includes every Hermite derivative channel, and depends only on N and the specified original module. The exact positive Hermitian matrix is G_N=J^*(V^(-1))^*V^(-1)J. Thus ||p||_(G_N)=||u||_2 and the exact dual norm of ell is ||a||_2; the bilinear CD matrix K is not itself being called positive. The exact generators are D=kappa r_N(Jordan(A)) and C D C^(-1), with their literal inverses. The first consists of the known unit-value and polynomial first-jet blocks; the second retains the FULL coherent Racah transport. Both original sources in this metric are polynomial. Put u=V^(-1)Jp and a=ell J^(-1)V. From the exact endpoint source (12) and CD inverse (18a), their entries at each double node are (u_value,u_derivative) =(-N nu_j sigma_j^(-1) Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), N nu_j sigma_j^(-1)), (a_value,a_derivative)=(x^d/N,0). (18e) At a simple node they are u=N nu_j/sigma_j and a=x^d/N. In particular the original full Cartan phase is retained in the generator matrices; the source scalar cancellation is exactly (12). For clarity, the potentially large crossing derivative cancels in u_value: applying sigma^-1[[-eta,1],[1,0]] to the endpoint vector x^d(nu_j,r_N') leaves -x^d nu_j sigma^-1 Q_j'/Q_j in the first entry. This is an exact SOURCE cancellation; replacing Hermite columns by independent spectral values would miss it. There is an exact simplification, stronger than a polynomial gap estimate. P_N=T_N+2 satisfies the Chebyshev equation (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. At a double node, this equation and its derivative give Q_j(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c)=c/(4-c^2). The original offdiagonal product of A is (-1)^d N^2, so CD gives sigma_j=(-1)^d x^d nu_j/(4-c^2). Hence the exact complete source (18e) is simply (u_value,u_derivative)=N(-1)^d x^(-d)(-c,4-c^2), (a_value,a_derivative)=(x^d/N,0), (18f) at every double node. At the simple node, present only at odd N, sigma=x^d nu and u=Nx^(-d), a=x^d/N. All constants and phases in these formulas are retained. Thus the source norms are explicit. Put n_distinct=ceil(N/2). Then ||a||_2^2=n_distinct/N^2, ||u||_2^2=N^2[sum_double(c^2+(4-c^2)^2) +1_(N odd)]. The first n_distinct formula here uses the ACTUAL number of distinct nodes: n_distinct=N/2 at even N and (N+1)/2 at odd N. The sum is elementary: ||u||_2^2=N^2(4N-1), N odd, ||u||_2^2=4N^3, N even, N>=6, ||u||_2^2=192 at N=4, 64 at N=2. Indeed the full list c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N) has sums sum c_j^2=2N and sum c_j^4=6N except the resonant levels2,4. Pairing j with d-j and treating the simple c=-2 separately gives the displayed formula. Direct substitution proves both exceptional levels. In particular the UNIFORM source product is ||u||_2 ||a||_2<=2N, for EVERY N>=2. (18g) Thus the COMPLETE positive Gram (18d) has polynomial BOTH original boundary norms, exactly as required for an honest Cauchy--Schwarz estimate. For every original three-head word, |chi_N ell W_mult p| <=|chi_N| ||a||_2 ||W_ch u||_2 <=2|chi_N| N ||W_ch||_op. (18h) One need not replace the source energy by a full operator norm: with E_N(W)=||W_ch u||_2^2 the stronger pointed bound is |chi_N ell W_mult p|^2 <=|chi_N|^2 n_distinct/N^2 E_N(W). (18i) Here E_N is a specified positive doubled energy built from the actual coherent matrices D,C, the complete initial vector (18f), and every mixed channel. It is not a sum of independently squared paths or a new chosen boundary state. This is a complete source-preserving positive-metric statement, not a metric pulled back from the unknown word. The subsequent [exact full-source test](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md) proves that its coherent energy is NONSHARP already for the actual figure-eight, despite (18g). A single D has polynomial norm, but coherent transport through C creates the displayed excessive channel. The [terminal packet Gram](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md) constructs a different positive metric on this same complete module with the sharp benchmark rate; general-prefix energy remains unproved. No individual absolute q-Hahn path or diagonal clock majorant is substituted for W_ch. ## 4b. A local cap-Ward quotient does not propagate through an adjacent crossing There is a minimal original-source test for quotienting currents before taking a positive norm. Set D=A-c_*I on the complete W above. Since ell D=0, the ordinary-cap row descends to the LINEAR quotient Q_cap=W/im D. This is a state/current quotient, not a quotient of the full observable algebra. Nevertheless it cannot be propagated unchanged through even one adjacent original R_23. The exact source-Hermite relation (15) gives p=D(t/theta), theta=(-1)^N rho^2!=0, [p]=0 in Q_cap. The primitive has polynomial norm O(N^(7/2)), by the proved tame source frame and |rho|>=4/N. Thus no large-current asymptotic is needed for this test. On the other hand the literal original crossing gives (R_23 p)_j=kappa p_j F_(d-j), ell R_23 p=kappa x^(-d) sum_(r=0)^d Q^(r+1)F_r =kappa x^(-d)!=0. (18j) The sum telescopes by Q^(r+1)F_r=F_r-F_(r+1), F_N=0. Therefore R_23(im D) is not contained in im D, so there is no induced map R_23:Q_cap->Q_cap. A local quotient would send the original cup to zero before this crossing and lose the exact unit source (18j). Equivalently the missing overlap current is explicitly nonzero: ell [R_23,A](t/theta)=kappa x^(-d). All kappas and boundary normalizations are the original ones, and (13) identifies this pairing with the original whole marked source. This argument uses one actual source and crossing; it does not rely on the separate full-observable-algebra no-quotient theorem. A GLOBAL equation/source quotient can still retain the transported current and its boundary term. Positive Schur/minimum-energy reduction is legitimate after those complete compatible variables have been assembled. The local calculation above supplies no geometric bound on that global quotient energy. In particular, a polynomial boundary Riesz norm or a polynomial primitive for one Ward current does not prove a sharp energy estimate across arbitrary overlapping crossings. ## 5. All odd-head Hom spaces and every even-plat source The same endpoint argument works at arbitrary fixed width. Put b=2r+1 and D=r d. Let W_r=(V^tensor(2r))_(integer degree D), H_r(w)=sum_(c=0)^d (-xQ)^c E_(2r)^c w/F_c tensor |c>, I_w|a>=F_b^a H_r(w)/F_a. (19) Then restriction to last color0 proves an exact bijection W_r=Hom_Hopf,H(V,V^tensor(2r+1)), dim W_r=[z^(rd)](1+z+...+z^d)^(2r). (20) The E recurrence and E_prefix^N=0 prove both directions exactly as in (4). The highest H and K are d,x, and the complete F string gives the whole V map. For fixed r>=1 this dimension is O_r(N^(2r-1)); r=0 means the one-dimensional scalar Hom. No internal channel between successive braid gates is projected. Now take an original 2k-head plat, r=k-1, b=2k-1. Define Phi_w=(I_w tensor I)p =N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d) F_b^a H_r(w)/F_a tensor |d-a>. (21) These are EXACTLY all invariant tensors in V^tensor(2k). For a direct inverse expand an invariant tensor by its last head. Its last-color-d component is highest on the first b heads. The F equation then determines every other component by psi_(d-a-1)=x F_b psi_(d-a)/(1-Q^(a+1)). This is precisely (21), and the last endpoint holds by F_b^N=0. Its inverse on w is the coefficient of last TWO colors(0,d) multiplied by x^d/N. The E equation supplies the same highest constraint; there is no unperformed normal/source condition. Both signed original braids preserve these COMPLETE invariant tensors. Therefore every original plat word has an exact reduced operator B_word on W_r, computed by (21), the actual physical word, and that specified coefficient extraction. In particular this is a strict all-word representation, not the upper corner of a nonmultiplicative truncation. Most importantly the FULL original top source is retained. Set w_0=p^tensor(k-1), lambda=ell^tensor(k-1) on W_r. Then Phi_(w0)=p^tensor k, and EXACTLY (ell^tensor(k-1) tensor m) Phi_w=lambda(w), original plat scalar=chi_N lambda B_word w_0. (22) To prove it, compose I_w with the first k-1 ORDINARY caps. This is a Hopf map V->V and hence scalar. Its highest matrix entry is lambda(w), because those caps require prefix degree D and therefore select c=0 in (19). Composing this scalar map with the LAST literal marked cap on the original cup gives m p=1. This is a whole invariant-tensor identity. It does not replace m by an ordinary cap on arbitrary physical sectors. The reduced source norms in the stated orthonormal W_r basis are ||w_0||=N^[3(k-1)/2], ||lambda||=N^[-(k-1)/2], ||w_0|| ||lambda||=N^(k-1). (23) Thus no exponential boundary cost is hidden in this complete all-width reduction. At k=2 these are precisely the source p and ordinary row ell in (12)--(13). The actual common external chi_N is unchanged and is not asserted to have polynomial size. ## 6. Every induced generator has an explicit actual Casimir Write the even prefix in (19) as A_prefix tensor B_head, with 2k-3 and one physical head respectively. On its degree D slice put H_boundary=q x K_B+q^(-1)x^(-1)K_B^(-1) -x E_A F_B K_B, O_prefix=F_prefix E_prefix+qK_prefix +q^(-1)K_prefix^(-1). (24) The ordering F_B K_B is part of the formula. The full induced positive braid generators on W_r are physical R_i restricted to W_r, i<=2k-3, kappa r_N(H_boundary), i=2k-2, kappa r_N(O_prefix), i=2k-1. (25) Their negatives are the literal inverses. For k=1 the prefix is trivial and only the final value r_N(q+q^(-1)) occurs. Here is an extraction proof, rather than an assumed spectral matching. For the penultimate pair only last colors0,1 in (19) contribute to its output color0. The c=0 part gives xF_B E_B plus the Cartan terms in (24). The c=1 part is -x F_B(E_A K_B+E_B). The F_BE_B terms cancel, leaving exactly H_boundary, with no omitted endpoint term. Polynomial functional calculus then gives the middle formula (25). For the last pair, its coproduct Casimir can be moved through the invariant tensor (21) to the complementary even prefix. This keeps the same Casimir because the actual antipode fixes it: S(FEcal)=Ecal F, and Ecal F=FEcal+rho(K-K^(-1)) cancels the shifted Cartan terms. This is the literal cup duality (3), so no transpose framing factor or new norm character is inserted. It proves the last formula (25); specializing the same polynomial gives the full R, including all Jordan derivatives. Physical generators inside the prefix commute with its total E/F and give the first formula. These formulas implement the entire original scalar in a coherent source-generated module of polynomial dimension at fixed width. They do NOT establish a sharp bound for products of the two noncommuting boundary Casimir polynomials. The remaining task is their complete-channel/coherent angle-energy estimate, with the source (22), rather than any phase-free path majorant. ## 7. Verification and scope The finite audit uses the actual signed crossing matrices and their $E,F$ actions. Its scope is the specified word algebra, not an arbitrary coupon algebra; finite checks do not replace the all-level proof. This is different from the auxiliary classical Clebsch memory in [the degree-elevation dilation](clebsch_memory_dilation_and_actual_r_excursions.md). Here we use complete ACTUAL Hopf Hom spaces and invariant tensors, not a chosen upper subchannel with discarded R excursions. It is also stronger than retaining only the c_0 Jordan source plane: all intermediate channels (8)--(11),(24)--(25) are present. Their nontrivial norms and the geometric global estimate remain open.

title: A sharp capacity for two coherently composed original bridge packets
text: # A sharp capacity for two coherently composed original bridge packets 29 October 2026. The terminal packet with its adjacent inverse and the open signed bridge can be estimated TOGETHER, with their common physical color retained. Their exact operator norm has a strictly smaller exponent than the product of their separate sharp norms. The resulting constant is the unique maximum of an explicit strictly concave angle function. This is a sharp all-input norm theorem for an actual four-crossing terminal block, and gives a quantitative bound for the full original source with arbitrary prefixes and arbitrary plat width. Its constant is a block capacity, not asserted to be the volume of the closed knot. The requested sharp knot-volume estimate remains open. ## 1. The actual coherent block and its exact row Gram Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j|. Let R be the FULL original checked crossing on the pair degree-d multiplicity W_1. Put P_0=1, P_t=(1-Q^t)^2 P_(t-1)+Q^t, H=T R^(-1)=N^(-1) diag(x^n) R diag(P_(d-u)). (1) Here T is the complete original terminal packet, with all cap and Cartan factors retained. The exact formula, endpoint cancellation, and uniform bounds are proved in [the original Green estimate](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md): |P_t|<=N+4s_t^2, P_t=1/(2-Q^t)+O(1/N) uniformly when t/N is in a compact subset of (1/6,1/2). (2) Let L:W_2->W_1 be the POSITIVE open bridge (ell_12 tensor I_34)R_23, in the source-fixing physical coordinate gauge g_j=s_j/sqrt(N). This gauge fixes every original paired cup and ordinary cap. The whole marked closure is retained through the complete invariant-source theorem. Its exact row Gram is LL^*=diag(E_N(u)), E_N(u)=N^2 sum_(k<=d-u) s_k^(-2) sum_(a+c=d-k) s_a^(-4)s_c^(-4). (3) Thus the COMPLETE coherent block C=HL satisfies CC^*=H diag(E_N) H^*. (4) No exterior coefficient or Green factor is commuted in (4). Both sides can be tensored with an arbitrary Hilbert spectator space. The actual source row is 1^T C. Its Cauchy cost is at most N, also for the positive completion C^*C+exp(-N^2)I. The [pointed row theorem](actual_terminal_bridge_operator_reduction.md) gives, uniformly in u including the endpoints, log E_N(u)=(N/pi)h(u/N)+O(log N), h(t)=v_8, 0<=t<=1/2, h(t)=8 Lambda(pi*t/2)-2 Lambda(pi*t), 1/2<=t<=1, (5) where Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin s)ds and v_8=8Lambda(pi/4). The transfer restriction k<=d-u is part of (3); taking independent free maxima would lose it. ## 2. The sharp answer On 0<=alpha,beta<=pi/2, with gamma=pi-alpha-beta, define F(alpha,beta)=4Lambda(alpha)+6Lambda(beta)+2Lambda(gamma) +8Lambda((pi-beta)/2). (6) Let C_* be its maximum. It is attained at a UNIQUE point with 0<alpha_*<pi/2, pi/6<beta_*<pi/2, sin(gamma_*)=2sin(alpha_*)^2, sin(gamma_*)cos(beta_*/2)^2=sin(beta_*)^3. (7) The sharp all-level operator estimate is log ||H L||_op^2=(N/pi) C_*+O(log N). (8) In particular v_8+3v_3<C_*<2v_8, C_*=6.930886593131580854..., alpha_*/pi=0.243487774973153603..., beta_*/pi =0.347871118966627868... . (9) Here v_3=3Lambda(pi/3). The decimal values only describe the analytically specified unique maximum; the proof does not infer the rate or its strict gaps from numerical fitting. ## 3. The Green remainder has a strictly smaller exponent The actual crossing support is i+u>=d. With h_0=i+u-d, |R_(i,u)|=s_i^2 s_u^2/(N^2 s_(h_0)). (10) By (2), pointwise on this support, |H_(i,u)|<=|R_(i,u)|+4N|R_(i,u)|/s_u^2. (11) Multiply each column by sqrt(E_N(u)). The operator norm is bounded by the Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and (11) bounds that norm by the sum of the two Hilbert--Schmidt norms of the displayed nonnegative entry majorants. This is used only AFTER the actual coherent P_t endpoint cancellation which proves (2). Write J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi*s))ds=-Lambda(pi*t)/pi. For the second majorant the squared exponential profile is at most h(u/N)+pi[4J(i/N)-2J((i+u-d)/N)]<=v_8+3v_3. (12) Indeed max J=v_3/(2pi) and min J=-v_3/(2pi). Polynomial N factors and the uniform factorial errors cost O(log N). This argument includes all physical endpoints and every parity. The first majorant has squared profile h(u/N)+pi[4J(i/N)+4J(u/N)-2J((i+u-d)/N)]. (13) If u/N<=1/2 then J(u/N)<=0, so (12) bounds (13) too. For u/N>=1/2 put alpha=pi(1-i/N), beta=pi(1-u/N). Replacing the exact offset d=N-1 by N changes the action by O(log N/N), uniformly, using the modulus |Lambda(a)-Lambda(b)|<=C|a-b|(1+|log|a-b||). This includes the thin support strip where the limiting gamma would otherwise be between -pi/N and zero; adjust the angles by O(1/N) into the closed simplex before applying the formula. The limiting expression (13) is precisely (6), with beta<=pi/2. An alpha>pi/2 cannot maximize it: then 0<gamma<pi/2 and swapping alpha and gamma raises 4Lambda(alpha)+2Lambda(gamma) by 2[Lambda(gamma)-Lambda(alpha)]>0. Hence its maximum is C_*. Finally C_*>v_8+3v_3. Evaluate (6) at alpha=pi/4,beta=pi/3. Its excess over v_8+3v_3 is -4Lambda(pi/4)+5Lambda(pi/3)+2Lambda(5pi/12)>0. Strict concavity of Lambda on (0,pi/2), with Lambda(pi/2)=0, gives Lambda(5pi/12)>Lambda(pi/3)/2 and Lambda(pi/3)>2Lambda(pi/4)/3. Combining them proves the displayed strict inequality. Thus the remainder in (12) cannot control the sharp exponential rate, and the upper half of (8) follows. ## 4. Strict concavity, the unique optimizer, and the lower bound Inside the rectangle 0<alpha,beta<pi/2 put a=cot(alpha)>0, b=cot(beta)>0, g=cot(gamma)=(1-ab)/(a+b). The negative Hessian of (6) is [[4a+2g, 2g], [2g, 6b+2g+2tan(beta/2)]]. (14) Its first principal minor is positive. If g>=0 this is immediate; if g<0, then g>-ab/(a+b)>-a, so 4a+2g>2a. Before its last positive diagonal term, the determinant is 24ab+8ag+12bg=8+16ab+4bg>0. For g>=0 the first expression is positive. For g<0, bg=(1-ab)b/(a+b)>=1-ab, so the second is at least12+12ab. The extra term in (14) increases the determinant. Thus F is STRICTLY concave throughout this convex rectangle. The alpha derivative tends to +infinity at alpha=0, and at alpha=pi/2 it is 2log(cos(beta)/2)<0. The beta derivative at beta=pi/2 is 2log(cos(alpha)/2)<0. At beta=pi/6 it is 2log(2sin(gamma))+4log(2cos(pi/12))>0, since gamma ranges from pi/3 to5pi/6. Concavity then excludes every beta<=pi/6 from the maximum. These statements give the unique interior optimizer and the range in (7). Setting the two first derivatives to zero gives exactly its trigonometric equations. The upper gap C_*<2v_8 is also strict without decimals. The separate crossing squared profile has maximum v_8 only at alpha=beta=pi/4. The row profile h has maximum v_8 only for u/N<=1/2, i.e. beta>=pi/2. They cannot attain both maxima together. Continuity on the compact angle domain therefore gives a strict gap for their sum. For the lower bound in (8), take integers i,u nearest N(1-alpha_*/pi), N(1-beta_*/pi), with the exact support retained. The Green index t=d-u satisfies t/N->beta_*/pi in (1/6,1/2), so (2) gives a nonzero limiting P_t. Equations (5),(10) then imply log(|H_(i,u)|^2 E_N(u))=(N/pi)C_*+O(log N). Equation (4) has norm at least this single squared entry of H diag(sqrt E). Conversely its Hilbert--Schmidt bound costs at most N^2 terms. This completes (8), including odd, even and composite levels and all original normalization factors. ## 5. A full-source consequence at arbitrary plat width For a six-head plat the actual terminal block has action order [2,-3,4,4]. First R23 couples the first ordinary cap to the remaining pair, then the inverse R34 is retained, and finally R45^2 meets the terminal cap. The exact cap identities give C=HL on W_2. Thus for ANY preceding original braid B, |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 N ||HL||^2 ||B w_0||_g^2. (15) The input metric g is the specified source-fixing physical factorial metric. Its original paired source w0=p tensor p has polynomial norm. The preceding operator is transported in that metric; its cost has not been dropped from (15). The same terminal block can be placed at the last five odd heads of a 2k-head plat for ANY k>=3, with action order [2k-4,-(2k-3),2k-2,2k-2]. All earlier ordinary caps commute with this terminal block and can be contracted exactly. Their product norm is polynomial. This leaves the same complete W_2 input and the SAME HL estimate. The preceding braid may use every head, including the last marked partner: its complete invariant-tensor inverse is (x^d/N) times extraction of the last two colors (0,d), not an unjustified odd-head cut replacement. The gauges of those two colors multiply to one. For reference each original physical signed crossing in the common gauge g_j=s_j/sqrt(N) has Hilbert--Schmidt norm exp[Nv_8/(2pi)+O(log N)]. (16) Its nonzero modulus is s_(b+k)^2/(s_b^2 s_k) for the positive sign, and s_(a+k)^2/(s_a^2 s_k) for the negative sign. With three nonnegative complementary variables the limiting action is 2Lambda(alpha)+2Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma); its maximum is v_8/2, at alpha=beta=pi/4,gamma=pi/2. The strict physical support admits nearest lattice points, and its O(N^3) entries cost only log N. Consequently an arbitrary fixed m-crossing prefix in this all-width family satisfies the actual bound |K_N|<=|chi_N| N^C exp{N[m v_8+C_*]/(2pi)}. (17) The exponent C depends only on the fixed word and width. This saves more than two crossing capacities compared with separately charging the FOUR terminal crossings; it also improves the two separate packet capacities 2v_8. It is a bound for the whole original source, with chi_N retained. It is not a claim that m v_8+C_* equals or is at most the hyperbolic volume. Further coherent global constraints and geometric survival remain to be proved. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_composed_bridge_capacity.py) checks the actual finite operator product, its exact row Gram, the unique angle optimizer and growing-level capacity bounds. The finite audit compares marked sources, signed crossing compositions, optimizer equations and norm sandwiches. The finite support strip is included explicitly in Section 3.

title: The original source has an exact cyclic-dilogarithm and ordinary-Gaussian period
text: # The original source has an exact cyclic-dilogarithm and ordinary-Gaussian period 28 October 2026. The remaining finite marked Gaussian in [the exact cyclic/Hardy network](actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.md) can also be removed. The original knot period is an exact integral of the literature cyclic dilogarithm and its inverse, ordinary Cauchy kernels, and ordinary continuous Gaussian weights. There are no finite Dirichlet, finite Euler, or finite Gaussian scalar kernels in this presentation. The cycle is a specified **fibered torus over real Gaussian variables**, with Gaussian-dominated absolute convergence. It is not a fixed product of circles interchanged formally with an unbounded Gaussian integral. All original source, peripheral, Cartan and framing factors are retained. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_continuous_gaussian_network.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_continuous_gaussian_network_results.json) check 660 exact both-sign phase identities, eight whole original pivotal word matrices with joint Gaussian moments and no finite Gaussian kernel, ten real-Gaussian quadratures, and the fibered radius bounds. ## 1. The exact Gaussian moment, with both signs fixed Put $h=2\pi i/N$, $Q=e^h$. For the original equal-color Gaussian, $$ d_a=(-1)^a x^{-2a}\exp\{h(a^2-a)/2\}. $$ For $s\in\{+1,-1\}$ set $$ c_s=-x^{-2s}e^{-sh/2},\qquad \alpha_s=\sqrt{\pi}(1+is),\qquad \alpha_s^2=2\pi is. \tag{1} $$ Then exactly $$ \boxed{\quad d_a^s= \sqrt{\frac{N}{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-N\xi^2/2} (c_se^{\alpha_s\xi})^a\,d\xi. \quad} \tag{2} $$ Indeed the centered Gaussian of variance $1/N$ has complex moment $\exp(\alpha_s^2a^2/(2N))=\exp(sh a^2/2)$. Multiplication by $c_s^a$ gives the original linear phase and meridian powers. For $s=-1$, the sign is still $(-1)^a$, as required by the inverse Gaussian. For a typed unequal-color crossing replace $x^{-2s}$ by $(xy)^{-s}$ in (1). Nothing else changes. No common Cartan factor is incorporated into this replacement. For every polynomial $f$, (2) gives an exact operator identity $$ \mathsf D_sf(z)= \sqrt{\frac{N}{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-N\xi^2/2} f(c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}z)\,d\xi. \tag{3} $$ Each integrand is a dilation, so it preserves polynomial degree. Before every original Gaussian its active head lies below $N$. Thus (3) equals the original finite marked Gaussian on every actual input. This is an equality of whole operators on those inputs, not an assumed selected Gaussian branch. The active scalar Cauchy kernel for the dilation is $$ \frac1{1-c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}z/w}. \tag{4} $$ All spectator heads retain their ordinary Hardy kernels. There is one independent $\xi$ for each original Gaussian factor, hence one for each signed crossing in the specified strict presentation. ## 2. A common fibered cycle Retain the norm-one literature functions $$ \mathcal V_N(t)=(1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)} \prod_{\ell=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^\ell t)^{-\ell/N}, \qquad \mathcal U_N(t)=\mathcal V_N(t)^{-1}, \tag{5} $$ on their branches equal to one at zero. All non-Gaussian kernels and reflected monomials are exactly those in the previous theorem. Choose $\rho=1/16$. On a fixed color chart choose $0<\lambda\le1$ with $\lambda\le|x_j|$ and choose $$ C_c\ge\max(1,\sup|x_j|^2,\sup|x_j|^{-2}). $$ The same bound covers the typed products $(x_jx_{j+1})^{\pm1}$. Insert a Hardy identity-reset layer before every elementary factor. Given preceding output radii $R_j$, first put $r_j=\rho R_j/2$. Before a transfer decrease its numerator radius, if needed, so $r_{\mathrm{num}}/r_{\mathrm{den}} \le\rho\lambda/2$. For the factor's output radii use $$ s_j=\rho r_j/2 $$ except at a positive factorial, where $s_i=2r_i/\rho$, and at a Gaussian, where use $$ \boxed{\quad s_i=\frac{\rho}{2C_c}e^{-2|\xi|}r_i. \quad} \tag{6} $$ Since $\operatorname{Re}\alpha_s=\sqrt\pi<2$, $$ |c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}|\,s_i/r_i \le\frac\rho2e^{\sqrt\pi\,\xi-2|\xi|} \le\rho/2. \tag{7} $$ Thus every cyclic atom argument and every Cauchy-kernel argument has modulus at most $\rho/2$. At a positive factorial the reflected argument has modulus $|Qw_i/z_i|=\rho/2$; its full scalar kernel is still $N(z_i/w_i)^{N-1}\mathcal V_N(Qw_i/z_i)$. These inequalities hold simultaneously for every $\boldsymbol\xi\in\mathbb R^m$. The number of layers is fixed by the word. There is no inequality closing terminal radii back to initial radii, because the fused source is monomial. The construction uses no $N$-dependent radius constant on the fixed color chart. For each $\boldsymbol\xi$, take the product of the positively oriented circles of these radii and its uniquely anchored lift through (5). Denote it by $\Gamma(\boldsymbol\xi)$. The full integration chain is the union of these tori over the oriented base $\mathbb R^m$. The radii are continuous and piecewise smooth because of the minima and absolute values. Their strata glue without additional internal boundary. When the logarithmic torus volume form is wedged with all $d\xi_j$, its $d\log r(\boldsymbol\xi)$ terms vanish. Equivalently one integrates the fibers with their usual $dz/(2\pi iz)$ measure. There is **no extra radius Jacobian**. ## 3. Absolute convergence on the full fibered chain The following bounds are uniform in $N$ and in the real Gaussian variables; constants depend on the fixed word and color chart. First, all radii can be chosen at most one. A positive factorial's increase after its reset never exceeds its preceding radius. If $L$ is the number of elementary factors, put $$ c_{\mathrm{reset}}=\min(\rho/2,\rho^2\lambda/4),\qquad c_* =c_{\mathrm{reset}}\rho/(2C_c)>0. $$ An induction gives, at every layer, $$ -\log r_j\le C_{\mathrm{word}} +2\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}|\xi_\ell|. \tag{8} $$ One may take $C_{\mathrm{word}}$ to be a fixed multiple of $L|\log c_*|$. Minima in the radius construction only replace one radius by a fixed constant times another; they do not introduce products of previously accumulated logarithms. Second, the exact logarithm of (5) gives on $|t|\le\rho$ $$ |\log\mathcal V_N(t)|,\ |\log\mathcal U_N(t)| \le-\frac N4\log(1-\rho). \tag{9} $$ Here $|Q^r-1|\ge4/N$ for every nontrivial root, and the resonant logarithmic coefficients cancel exactly. All Hardy and Gaussian-dilation kernels are bounded by $(1-\rho)^{-1}$. Every reflected factorial contributes its original factor $N$ and a monomial whose radius ratio is fixed at $2/\rho$. Every source exponent has magnitude at most $N-1$. Consequently the absolute scalar density, apart from the unchanged external line $\chi_{\beta,N}$ and the normalized Gaussian measure, is bounded by $$ C N^B \exp\left\{C_0N+C_1N\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell|\right\}. \tag{10} $$ Thus the full pullback is dominated by $$ C N^B \exp\left\{C_0N+C_1N\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell| -\frac N2\sum_\ell\xi_\ell^2\right\}. \tag{11} $$ This is integrable for every $N$. With the normalized Gaussian measures its integral is at most $C'N^B e^{C_2N}$. We make no additional growth assertion about the retained external $\chi_{\beta,N}$. These estimates prove Fubini and the disappearance of Gaussian boundary terms at real infinity. ## 4. Exact original-source identity, with no finite scalar kernels Let $\mathcal H_{\ell,N}(\boldsymbol\xi)$ be the kernels of the cyclic/Hardy network with each finite Gaussian replaced by (4). Let $m$ be their Gaussian count. The original full fused-plat period is exactly $$ \begin{split} P_{\beta,N} ={}&\chi_{\beta,N}N^{1-k} \left(\frac N{2\pi}\right)^{m/2} \int_{\mathbb R^m} e^{-N\|\boldsymbol\xi\|^2/2}\\ &\quad\cdot \int_{\Gamma(\boldsymbol\xi)} (z^0)^{a_{\mathrm{in}}}(z^L)^{-a_{\mathrm{out}}} \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} \mathcal H_{\ell,N}(\boldsymbol\xi) \prod_{\ell,j}\frac{dz_j^\ell}{2\pi iz_j^\ell} \,d\boldsymbol\xi . \end{split} \tag{12} $$ Every source exponent, factor $N$, monomial, norm root, half-character and original external scalar is retained. No finite $\Gamma_{\pm,N}$, finite Euler polynomial, or finite Dirichlet numerator occurs in its scalar integrand. For a fixed $\boldsymbol\xi$, the torus contraction is the original completed polynomial word with its Gaussian factors replaced by independent dilations. Each head is still polynomial and all previous support/barrier arguments remain valid. The contraction is a finite sum of products of the dilation moments. Integration of each independent variable gives (2), in its original operator order, and therefore the exact original word. Estimate (11) also justifies this as an equality of absolutely convergent multiple integrals, rather than only an iterated polynomial calculation. The full original Ward corner is fixed BEFORE expanding the Gaussian factors. A fixed-$\boldsymbol\xi$ word need not be a Hopf intertwiner. We do not reapply the Ward corner reduction to such an individual word or replace its transported co-source by a newly chosen cap. Linearity of the already proved full-source functional is what is used in (12). Any specified root-specialized quantum A-annihilator of the original meridian function therefore annihilates (12) as well. No identification of a classical symbol or selected geometric component is inferred. ## 5. Uniform leading symbols on the INITIAL cycle There is now a direct uniform phase comparison for the actual scalar functions on this cycle, without a finite Taylor-remainder sector. For every fixed $\rho<1$, $$ \begin{split} \mathcal V_N(t) &=(1-t)^{1/2} \exp\{\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h\} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})),\\ \mathcal U_N(t) &=(1-t)^{-1/2} \exp\{-\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h\} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})). \end{split} \tag{13} $$ The normalized errors are analytic and admit the same bound with any fixed number of derivatives on smaller disks. All logarithms are the anchored branches. For a direct proof split the logarithmic series $\log\mathcal V_N(t)=\sum_{N\nmid m}t^m/[m(Q^m-1)]$ at $m=N/2$. On the lower range, $$ \frac1{e^{hm}-1}=\frac1{hm}-\frac12+O(|h|m). $$ For example the remainder bound on $|hm|\le\pi$ follows from the elementary sine/cotangent formula, with its removable value at zero. Summation gives $O_\rho(1/N)$. The upper range is exponentially small in $N$, using $|Q^m-1|^{-1}\le N/4$. The omitted resonant coefficients are exponentially small too. Thus $$ \log\mathcal V_N(t) =\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h+\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-t) +O_\rho(N^{-1}), $$ and Cauchy estimates give the derivative version. The exact Gaussian weight in (12) is $e^{-N\xi^2/2}$. On the original color charts, the remaining $q$ phases shift the small cyclic arguments by $e^{\beta h}$ for fixed half-integer or integer $\beta$. Their change is an explicit nonzero amplitude: $$ \mathcal V_N(e^{\beta h}t) =(1-t)^{1/2-\beta}e^{\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})), \tag{14} $$ with the inverse formula for $\mathcal U_N$. The dilation Cauchy kernel has the same type of uniform nonzero density correction, since its argument stays below $\rho$. Thus (12) has actual dilogarithm/Gaussian leading symbols and a specified nonzero leading density on its INITIAL fibered cycle. This is a pointwise integrand comparison. It does not imply a relative asymptotic for a cancelling total period, geometric dominance, or a nonzero intersection with a Rivin critical cycle. ## 6. The remaining global theorem The finite scalar endpoints have been replaced by global anchored functions and a specified convergent cycle, with exact equality to the original invariant. Their boundary information has not been discarded: it is carried by that cycle, the norm-root branches, the original affine charges and the Cauchy pole data. To prove a broad volume theorem one must still transport this cycle to the geometric ideal-angle chain, retaining norm-divisor residues, compatible root frames, Cauchy-pole contributions and the original pointed source. The oversized weak alias example shows why an unmarked choice of every nonnegative angle locus would be incorrect. No global transport or volume limit is claimed here.

title: Continuous real-spectral positivity of each exact tail continuant
text: # Continuous real-spectral positivity of each exact tail continuant exact lemma, 31 October 2026. This strengthens the local tail estimate used in the [global CROSS theorem](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md). It gives no positivity statement for the full spectral numerator or for the signed prefix factors. Write $\theta=\pi/N$, $s_j=2\sin(j\theta)$, and $$ \alpha_{j-1}(\delta)=4\cos^2\!\left((j-\tfrac12)\theta\right)-4\sin^2(\pi\delta). $$ For a fixed original start $i$ in the lower range $0\leq i\leq j\leq\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, normalize the [exact tail continuant](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) by $$ Q_j=\frac{K_{i,j}}{\prod_{r=i+1}^{j}s_r^2}. $$ Then $Q_i=1$, $Q_{i+1}=x+y$, and the exact recurrence for $j\geq i+2$ is $$ Q_j=(x+y)Q_{j-1}+\beta_jxyQ_{j-2}, \qquad \beta_j=\frac{\alpha_{j-1}}{s_js_{j-1}}.\tag{1} $$ In the actual lower range the denominator is positive. The recurrence starts at its second step, so it never divides by $s_0$. Direct product-to-sum gives the row-independent identity $$ s_js_{j-1}+\alpha_{j-1} =4\cos^2(\pi\delta)-4\sin^2(\theta/2).\tag{2} $$ Consequently $1+\beta_j\geq0$ for every row whenever $$ |\delta|\leq\frac12-\frac1{2N}. $$ Set $D_j=Q_j-xQ_{j-1}$. The exact induction is $$ D_j=y\left[D_{j-1}+(1+\beta_j)xQ_{j-2}\right].\tag{3} $$ Its initial value is $D_{i+1}=y$. Thus $Q_j$ and $D_j$ have nonnegative coefficients in $x,y$ on the entire indicated real-spectral interval, including its endpoint. The proof also allows $x=0$ or $y=0$. It uses no sign condition on $\beta_j$ itself. For arbitrary complex outer faces, this proves $$ |K_{i,j}(x,y;\delta)|\leq K_{i,j}(|x|,|y|;\delta).\tag{4} $$ The original start sum is therefore bounded at arbitrary face phases by the same absolute-prefix sum used in the global CROSS upper-action proof. No cancellation is discarded inside the tail recurrence. For a polynomial in $\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)$ of degree at most $CN$, this interval corresponds to $[-2,2\cos(\pi/N)]$. The affine Chebyshev variable of $\sigma=2$ relative to this interval is $1+O(N^{-2})$. The real Bernstein inequality therefore extends a uniform supremum bound to $[-2,2]$ with factor $\exp[O(C)]$, since $$ \operatorname{arcosh}(1+O(N^{-2}))=O(N^{-1}).\tag{5} $$ This is an absolute polynomial-norm extension, not a coefficientwise extension of positivity beyond the last physical spectral node. The [global LEFT weighted envelope](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) applies this distinction to the actual one-sided source. ## Validation and scope The row identity uses the original starting rows and avoids the zero sine denominator. It proves neither a shared one-sided capacity bound nor positivity of the full numerator.

title: Coupled crossing gauges: an exact optimizer and a twist-block improvement
text: # Coupled crossing gauges: an exact optimizer and a twist-block improvement 28 October 2026. The original endpoint-preserving gauge program can be implemented as a finite convex optimization, with its full original paired source retained. For a broad explicit alternating-sign class, flat gauges are its **exact finite-N global minimizers** at the single-crossing Hilbert--Schmidt partition. Even replacing HS norms by operator norms cannot improve its exponential crossing envelope. Thus this particular optimization does not produce the Rivin volume. There is a constructive improvement after coherent block contraction: an entire repeated-crossing twist block has a uniform exponential norm bound independent of its length. It improves the crossing bound for every repeated-generator block of length at least five in the specified original braid word, at arbitrary width. No conversion of an arbitrary unoriented diagram twist region is assumed. This is not the sharp knot-volume bound or a lower bound. ## 1. The implemented original program and its entropy dual Use the source-preserving gauge program in [the weighted Fourier energy theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md#3-a-computable-positive-energy-upper-bound-hierarchy). The width is 2k; every original cap/cup pair is adjacent. On every physical wire edge e choose arbitrary real logs s_e(a), 0<=a<N. At each endpoint the only restrictions are s_(odd,a)+s_(even,d-a)=0, d=N-1. (1) These make the endpoint gauges fix the original paired cups, ordinary caps, and the marked cap after its legitimate whole-degree restriction. All scalar, pivotal and framing lines stay as before. An internal wire has a single gauge on its entire segment between incident gates. For a crossing v let i=(a,b), o=(c,e). Put Phi_N(s)=(1/2)sum_v log sum_(i,o) |R_v(o,i)|^2 exp(2s_out(o)-2s_in(i)). (2) The sums use the original physical crossing support, not a cyclic completion. Positive entries are exactly R_+(a+b-e,e;a,b) =kappa x^(-b-e)Q^(eb) F_(a+b-e)F_a/[F_(a-e)F_bF_e], (3) with 0<=e<=a<N and a+b-e<N. The negative moduli are obtained by swapping both input and output heads, from the proved actual antiunitary identity. The common kappa is a retained unit phase. Thus no knot scalar is input to the objective. The resulting rigorous bound is |P_N| <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) exp(inf_s Phi_N(s)). (4) The implementable objective (2) is convex log-sum-exp. The new script eliminates (1) with a signed union-find and supplies its analytic gradient to L-BFGS. It keeps separate intermediate wire gauges and the independent top and bottom source gauges; it does not optimize each crossing in isolation. There is a useful dual characterization. At every crossing choose a probability p_v on its actual nonzero entries. Require identical one-head marginals at the two ends of every internal wire and require reflected odd/even marginals at each paired boundary. Such probabilities annihilate every gauge linear term in (2). The elementary entropy identity log sum_i exp(l_i)=max_p [sum_i p_i l_i-sum_i p_i log p_i] therefore gives the lower certificate inf_s Phi_N(s) >= (1/2)sum_v [sum p_v log|R_v|^2-sum p_v log p_v]. (5) If the maximizing constrained probabilities are strictly positive, Lagrange multipliers give p_v proportional to the exponentials in (2), and equality holds. Indeed the entropy has infinite inward derivative at a zero coordinate whenever a strictly positive feasible point exists, so its maximum is interior. Its derivative annihilates the constraint tangent space, hence is a linear combination of the constraint rows, which gives precisely those multipliers. This is a finite-dimensional entropy/flow duality with actual R weights. It does not identify those flows with geometric angle structures. The subsequent [joint projector-profile bound](actual_twist_block_projector_barrier.md) sharpens the block constant below to 4v_3+2v_8 while retaining the same original source, frame and meridian-circle proof. The valid coarser estimates here are unchanged. ## 2. Exact optimum for alternating signs by generator position Suppose the word has the sign pattern sign(sigma_i)=epsilon*(-1)^(i+1), epsilon=+1 or -1, (6) at every occurrence of generator i. Its index sequence is arbitrary, as are its length and even width. The theorem applies whenever its plat closure is the desired one-component knot; no knot-specific calculation enters. It is not a claim that every alternating knot presentation automatically has (6). **Exact optimizer theorem.** For every N>=2, inf_s Phi_N(s)=m log||R_+||_HS. (7) Thus the fully coupled single-crossing HS gauge program is already minimized by s=0, including all endpoint gauges allowed in (1). Proof. Normalize the squared moduli of the positive crossing: p_+(o,i)=|R_+(o,i)|^2/||R_+||_HS^2. The literal matrix (3) is symmetric: R_+(o,i)=R_+(i,o). It follows that its input and output first-head marginals coincide, as do its second-head marginals. Let them be p_H and p_L. Root factorial reflection gives a second exact modulus symmetry, |R_+(c,e;a,b)| =|R_+(d-e,d-c;d-b,d-a)|. (8) Indeed the new transfer difference is still a-e=c-b, and |F_j||F_(d-j)|=N cancels all reflected numerator/denominator factors in (3). Consequently p_H(a)=p_L(d-a). For the negative crossing the two head marginals are interchanged. Under (6), any given odd physical head therefore has the same marginal at ALL its incident crossings, and every even head has the reflected marginal. Which of the two is called H depends only on epsilon. Assign these same marginals to untouched wire segments too. All internal wire constraints and all boundary reflection constraints in Section 1 are satisfied. The strictly positive probabilities p_v=|R_v|^2/||R_v||_HS^2 are thus feasible in (5). Their entropy value is exactly sum_v log||R_v||_HS=m log||R_+||_HS. The same value is attained by s=0 in (2), proving (7). Equivalently, the entire projected gradient at s=0 vanishes, not merely the gradients of individually balanced crossings. Convexity then certifies the global minimum without any numerical convergence assumption. This is why some randomly initialized large-N numerical optimizations converge slowly in gauge-null directions; the exact stationary certificate avoids confusing that with a smaller optimum. ## 3. Even operator-norm gauges retain the crossing exponent Let a_N+b_N=d with a_N/N ->3/4 and b_N/N ->1/4. When epsilon=+1, put the fixed indices (a_N,b_N,a_N,b_N,...) on the physical heads; reverse them for epsilon=-1. At a positive crossing this gives the diagonal entry R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N). At a negative crossing it gives the head-swapped diagonal entry with the same modulus. This is a single physical index path through the WHOLE network, and its paired endpoint charges are exactly d. Every gauge in (1) is one on each of these endpoint states. Along the path the interior gauge ratios telescope. Bounding each local operator norm by this one entry therefore gives, for ANY N-dependent choices of positive diagonal wire gauges, product_v ||G_out,v R_v G_in,v^(-1)||_op >= |R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N)|^m. (9) This is a lower bound on the norm-based upper-bound program, not on the actual scalar period; other state paths can cancel that scalar. The uniform factorial estimate shows log|R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N)| =N[2J(3/4)-J(1/2)-2J(1/4)]+O(log N) =N v_8/(2pi)+O(log N). Flat gauges have that same operator-norm exponent by the original crossing theorem. Hence the best single-crossing operator program, as well as (7), has the exact exponential rate inf_gauge sum_v log||R_v,gauge|| =m N v_8/(2pi)+O_word(log N). (10) This decides the proposed finest local scaling route for the class (6), at arbitrary width. It cannot by itself lower the crossing envelope to the smaller hyperbolic knot volume. A genuinely coherent block contraction is necessary. ## 4. A uniform twist-block improvement from the actual Casimir Such contraction does yield a quantitative general improvement. Let B be either original complete crossing on two physical heads, with its original unit Cartan/framing factors retained. For every integer ell and every N>=2, ||B^ell||_op <=32 N^2(1+|ell|) c_*^N, ||B^ell||_HS <=32 N^3(1+|ell|) c_*^N, c_*=7+5sqrt(2). (11) The exponential constant is independent of twist length. No spectral condition number or unproved semisimplicity is hidden in (11). Here is a direct norm proof from the already independently derived [actual Casimir crossing polynomial](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#3-the-actual-crossing-has-a-unique-confluent-polynomial). Use Ecal=rho^2 E and the actual complete physical matrices. They obey ||F||,||Ecal||<=2, K unitary, F Ecal+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=-2I. On the tensor product put Omega=F_tot Ecal_tot+qK_1K_2+q^(-1)K_1^(-1)K_2^(-1), F_tot=F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2, Ecal_tot=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2. Expanding and using the single-head Casimir identity gives Omega=-2(K_2+K_1^(-1)) -(q+q^(-1))K_1^(-1)K_2 +F_1 Ecal_2+K_1^(-1)Ecal_1 F_2K_2, so ||Omega||<=14 in the original flat balanced metric. Let P_N(z)=T_N(z)+2, T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1). The proved actual polynomial identity is B=lambda_0 r_N(Omega), |lambda_0|=1, with P_N(Omega)=0. Its roots c=2cos(pi h/N), h odd, 1<=h<N are double. When N is odd there is additionally the simple root -2. At every double root r_N(c)=nu, |nu|=1 and |r_N'(c)|=(N-h)/(4 sin(pi h/N))<=N^2/8. (12) The simple root value has modulus one. These spectral jets, including their derivatives, follow from the defining finite R by confluent generic-q highest-weight interpolation; no diagonalizability at the root is used. For an explicit bounded Hermite basis set Q_c(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2, A_c=Q_c(c)=N^2/(4sin^2(pi h/N)), alpha_c=Q_c'(c)/A_c=c/(4-c^2), e_c(z)=Q_c(z)[1-alpha_c(z-c)]/A_c, j_c(z)=(z-c)Q_c(z)/A_c. These polynomials have respectively the jets (1,0) and (0,1) at c, and zero jets at all other roots. At a possible simple root -2 use e_-(z)=P_N(z)/[(z+2)P_N'(-2)], with |P_N'(-2)|=N^2. Consequently the exact polynomial representing B^ell/lambda_0^ell is f_ell(z)=sum_double [nu^ell e_c(z) +ell nu^(ell-1)r_N'(c) j_c(z)] +sum_simple nu^ell e_-(z). (13) This formula works for negative ell too: r_N is a unit modulo P_N. For completeness the constants can be controlled explicitly. Integrate around |z|=R=14+1/N. The resolvent norm is at most N by its Neumann series. Put r(R)=(R+sqrt(R^2+4))/2. The Chebyshev recurrence gives |T_N(z)|<=2r(R)^N, and |P_N(z)|<=5 c_*^N, |z-c|>=12, A_c>=N^2/4, |alpha_c|<=N^2/8. The first inequality uses N[log r(14+1/N)-log r(14)]<=1/sqrt(200). It follows on that circle that |e_c(z)|<c_*^N/3, |j_c(z)|<=5c_*^N/(3N^2), |e_-(z)|<=5c_*^N/(12N^2). Together with (12), the at most N interpolation conditions bound |f_ell(z)| by N(1+|ell|)c_*^N. Cauchy's matrix functional calculus therefore gives ||f_ell(Omega)||<=R N^2(1+|ell|)c_*^N, which is stronger than the operator inequality (11). The HS inequality costs at most sqrt(N^2)=N. Thus no exponentially conditioned eigenbasis has entered the proof. ## 5. Whole-word consequence at arbitrary width Partition any fixed original knot word into maximal repeated-generator twist blocks of lengths ell_t, leaving other crossings as blocks of length one. Perform these actual matrix contractions first, preserving the original source and all common phases. Combining (11) with the ordinary crossing bound gives the unconditional whole-source estimate limsup_N (2pi/N)log|P_N| <=sum_t min(|ell_t|v_8, 2pi log(7+5sqrt(2))). (14) The factors 32N^3(1+|ell_t|), spectator dimensions and all complete source normalizations contribute only O_word(log N). The same holds for the reduced original Kashaev scalar. This applies to arbitrary width and sign patterns, not just the twist-knot family. There is also a direct finite-N source justification which includes ODD braid width and does not require passing to an even plat. For a b-strand knot cut use its original complete pivot g, which is unitary, and retain the unit-modulus zero-framing line in W. The exact actual cut is C=Tr_env[W(I tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))]=K_N I. Every partial trace of a unitary-weighted operator has norm at most the environment dimension times its operator norm. Thus, with every normalization still original, |K_N| <= N^(b-1)||W||_op <= N^(b-1) product_t min( ||B_sign(t)||_op^|ell_t|, 32N^2(1+|ell_t|)(7+5sqrt(2))^N). (14a) At completeness the full ADO modified dimension is its known root phase divided by N, so it does not change the exponential bound. This proof uses the actual original pivotal cut, not a new positive closing trace. It supplies the source estimate for (14) at every braid width. Since 2pi log(7+5sqrt(2)) < 5 v_8, every repeated-generator block of length at least five gives a strict improvement over its separate-crossing bound. The displayed numerical comparison can be verified by elementary convergent series for sqrt(2), log and Catalan's constant; it is not used for (11) or (14). The constant is deliberately coarse, so (14) is not asserted to equal or be bounded by Vol(S^3-K). It establishes a real quantitative gain from coherent block contraction in the specified braid word after the finest gauge program has been shown ineffective on the alternating-sign class. ## 6. Reproduction and numerical scope python3 experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.py python3 experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.py --full The script uses exact finite factorial moduli in logarithmic form; the only floating operations in the objective are ordinary positive log-sum-exp and its gradient. It checks the transpose/reflection marginals through N=32 and optimizes complete coupled wire gauges at width four and six. In the class (6), the independently verified zero gradient is the global certificate, so starting at that point does not rely on slow optimization in null directions. Nonalternating examples are diagnostics; finite-iteration results there are feasible upper bounds and are not claimed exact optima. The block tests independently construct the bounded physical Omega, check its actual polynomial crossing identity, and evaluate positive and negative twist powers through N=10. The all-N bound is the analytic Hermite/resolvent proof above, not extrapolation from those powers. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy_results.json).

title: The exact alias-tangent threshold and a rational port certificate
text: # The exact alias-tangent threshold and a rational port certificate 31 October 2026. **analytic and original-source certificate.** The exact algebraic port condition below gives a uniform mixed-source gap; it is a sufficient condition on the actual complete optimizer, not an automatic property of every two-leaf expression. This enlarges the sufficient leaf interval in the existing whole mixed-source Conway argument. It does not assert that every expression using h^2 has the required strict geometry, finite lattice packet, or passing leaf labels. Those source and geometric hypotheses are supplied separately by the [two-leaf source interface](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md) and [actual geometric interface](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md). The actual functions are those of the [full original mixed-source theorem](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md): \[ \begin{gathered} J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\\ g(a)=J(2a)-4J(a),\quad 0\le a\le\tfrac12,\qquad k(u)=-2J(u/2),\quad 0\le u\le1. \end{gathered} \] The coefficient bounds for the full original core and alias, including Hermite/normal data and both parities, are retained from that source theorem. Nothing below replaces them by a semisimple or nodal estimate. ## 1. Exact minimization of the leaf tangent deficit For 1/4<=a<1/2, put s(a)=g'(a)=2log cot(pi a) and \[ I(a)=\min_{0\le u\le1}\left[g(a)+s(a)(u-a)-k(u)\right].\tag{1} \] The exact derivatives are \[ \begin{gathered} g''(a)=-\frac{4\pi}{\sin(2\pi a)}<0,\qquad k'(u)=-\log(2\sin(\pi u/2)),\\ k''(u)=-\frac\pi2\cot(\pi u/2)<0\quad(0<u<1). \end{gathered}\tag{2} \] Let a0=atan(sqrt(2))/pi. For a in [1/4,a0], the unique maximizer of k(u)-s(a)u is \[ u(a)=\frac2\pi\arcsin\frac{\tan^2(\pi a)}2.\tag{3} \] with u in [1/3,1]. At a=a0 it is the endpoint 1. On the strict interior the envelope derivative is \[ I'(a)=g''(a)(u(a)-a)<0. \] The continuous extension has the same monotonicity at both endpoints. The already proved exact lower bound is \[ I(a)\ge I(a_0)\ge c_0,\qquad c_0=\frac{2\operatorname{Catalan}}\pi-\frac34\log2 >\frac{161}{3960}>0.\tag{4} \] For a>=a0, s(a)<=-log2. Since k' decreases to -log2, the function s(a)u-k(u) is decreasing on [0,1], strictly except possibly at its right endpoint. Thus its minimum is EXACTLY at u=1. Since k(1)=0, \[ I(a)=H(a):=g(a)+(1-a)g'(a),\qquad a_0\le a<\tfrac12.\tag{5} \] In particular H'(a)=(1-a)g''(a)<0. No sampling of the alias range or unknown optimizer is involved in (5). ## 2. The exact threshold exists and lies below one third Introduce the real inverse-tangent integral \[ \operatorname{Ti}_2(x)=\int_0^x\frac{\arctan t}{t}\,dt,\qquad x\ge0. \] If x=cot(pi a), integration from g(1/2)=0 gives \[ \begin{aligned} g(a)&=-\frac2\pi\int_0^x\frac{\log t}{1+t^2}\,dt\\ &=\frac2\pi\left[\operatorname{Ti}_2(x)-\arctan(x)\log x\right]. \end{aligned} \] Since 1-a=1/2+atan(x)/pi, this yields the exact simplification \[ H(a)=\frac2\pi\operatorname{Ti}_2(x)+\log x,\qquad x=\cot(\pi a).\tag{6} \] At a0, H is strictly positive by (4). At a=1/3, x=1/sqrt(3), and atan(t)<t gives Ti2(x)<x. Using pi>3 and log3>1, \[ H(\tfrac13)<\frac{2}{3\sqrt3}-\frac12<0.\tag{7} \] For the elementary log inequality, exp(1)<3 follows directly by bounding its factorial series. The last inequality in (7) follows from 16<27. Strict decrease and continuity therefore prove a UNIQUE \[ a_{\mathrm{crit}}\in(a_0,\tfrac13),\qquad H(a_{\mathrm{crit}})=0.\tag{8} \] For the whole interval 1/4<=a<1/2, the exact supporting-plane condition I(a)>0 holds if and only if a<a_crit. At equality it has zero margin; above it, the genuine alias endpoint u=1 lies above the tangent. That is a failure of this sufficient tangent method, not a lower bound for an actual mixed source or a volume obstruction. No decimal approximation defines or proves (8). ## 3. A sharper reusable algebraic certificate: cot(pi a)>=2/3 Set \[ a_* =\frac1\pi\arctan\frac32. \] It lies strictly above a0 because 3/2>sqrt(2). At x=2/3 the alternating series for Ti2 is valid, with decreasing terms. Four terms give \[ \operatorname{Ti}_2(\tfrac23) >\frac23-\frac{(2/3)^3}{9}+\frac{(2/3)^5}{25}-\frac{(2/3)^7}{49} =\frac{1708762}{2679075}.\tag{9} \] The positive series log((1+y)/(1-y))=2sum_(n>=0)y^(2n+1)/(2n+1) at y=1/5, bounding all remaining denominators by 7, gives \[ \begin{aligned} \log\frac32 &\le2\left[\frac15+\frac{1}{3\cdot5^3}+\frac{1}{5\cdot5^5} +\frac{1}{7\cdot5^7(1-1/25)}\right]\\ &=\frac{177391}{437500}. \end{aligned}\tag{10} \] Since pi<22/7, equations (6),(9),(10) imply the exact rational margin \[ H(a_*)>\frac7{11}\frac{1708762}{2679075}-\frac{177391}{437500} =\frac{57269}{136687500}>\frac1{2500}.\tag{11} \] Every inequality here is analytic or rational arithmetic; no asymptotic computation or numerical sign test is used. Combining (4), strict decrease in (5), and (11) proves \[ \begin{gathered} k(u)\le g(a)+g'(a)(u-a)-\frac1{2500},\\ 0\le u\le1,\qquad \frac14\le a\le a_*. \end{gathered}\tag{12} \] It also sharpens the exact bracket to \[ \frac1\pi\arctan\frac32<a_{\mathrm{crit}}<\frac13. \] The certificate (12) is algebraic in the positive actual port variable: \[ X=\cot(\pi a)\ge\frac23 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 9X^2\ge4.\tag{13} \] The positivity of X and the retained a>=1/4 hypothesis matter in the equivalence and source application. No claim is made that the true transcendental threshold itself is an algebraic port condition. For comparison, the simpler bound X>=7/10 also follows without the Ti2 series. For a0<=a<=atan(10/7)/pi, concavity gives g(a)>=g(a0)+g'(a)(a-a0). Hence \[ \begin{aligned} H(a)&\ge c_0+(1-a_0)[g'(a)+\log2]\\ &>\frac{161}{3960}-\log\frac{50}{49} >\frac{161}{3960}-\frac1{49}=\frac{3929}{194040}>0. \end{aligned} \] The cutoff (13) admits the larger interval and will suffice below. ## 4. Exact conditional mixed-source transfer Consider a FIXED actual Conway source made from the original leaves T(R^epsilon L_j), actual Newton products and literal turns, with the original final cylindrical closure. Suppose its complete pure source has a unique strict optimizer, every unforced gate is strict, and every actual complete leaf label satisfies \[ \frac14<a_\ell<a_{\mathrm{crit}}.\tag{14} \] Retain all finite source, strict lattice, nonzero complete packet and geometric assumptions required by the existing assembly. The present statement supplies the mixed-source inequality; it does not reprove those other assumptions for a new grammar. For a finite set of leaves define c=min_l I(a_l)>0. The original all-color core has uniform upper rate \[ \widetilde g(u)=g(\max(u,\tfrac14)),\qquad 0\le u\le\tfrac12. \] This function is concave: it is constant up to 1/4, its right derivative there is zero, and it is strictly concave thereafter. Thus, for every leaf in (14), \[ \widetilde g(u)\le g(a_\ell)+g'(a_\ell)(u-a_\ell).\tag{15} \] with equality only at u=a_l. Its pure-core counterpart obeys the same upper bound. For an alias, (1) gives on its ENTIRE physical range \[ k(u)\le g(a_\ell)+g'(a_\ell)(u-a_\ell)-I(a_\ell), \qquad0\le u\le1.\tag{16} \] The exact original multiplication action remains concave on max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1. Add its supporting planes at the SAME complete state to (15),(16). All linear terms cancel under the original affine turn and closure equations by complete-source stationarity. For any nonempty alias subset S the resulting rate is at most \[ F_0-\sum_{\ell\in S}I(a_\ell)\le F_0-c.\tag{17} \] This argument uses neither a vanishing product of aliases after turns nor covariance of a projected coupon. It keeps the full original Hermite/normal terms in the known source bounds. At finite level the actual wire affine right sides are 1-1/N. Fixed tangent slopes therefore cost only O(1) in the exponent, while endpoint-uniform factorial and transport errors are o(N). The fixed circuit has polynomially many wire states and finitely many alias subsets. Reducing c if necessary gives the whole mixed-source radical gap uniformly over all physical auxiliary colors, both parities and composite levels. The physical-color complement argument also transfers. The concave all-core majorant is bounded above by the sum of the same supporting planes. Equality forces every leaf to equal its original a_l by (15) and every retained strict gate to equal its original state. It therefore has the same unique maximum. Compactness gives a gap outside a fixed complete-state neighborhood. Inside that neighborhood, choose beta<1/2 larger than every leaf label; the existing uniform far-color core loss applies with unchanged terminal source and recurrence branches. Combining it with (17) gives the existing complete-color corridor gap. If every leaf obeys the algebraic condition (13), one can take the uniform tangent margin 1/2500 in this argument. Under merely (14) the positive margin depends on the fixed actual optimizer, as permitted by the original fixed-expression quantifiers. This is a CLOSED-source argument. It does not assert an open, coefficientwise error comparison for an h^2 seed at every prescribed output, and does not fill a missing finite top coefficient by changing the exact source lattice. ## 5. Interface with h^2 and other actual seeds The existing complete port formulas for A_s=h^s are \[ X=\cot(\pi a),\qquad B_s=\frac{T_s(X)}{U_{s-1}(X)},\qquad Y_s=\frac1{U_{s-1}(X)}. \] Whenever the independently checked closed strict geometry gives the proper-seed inequalities, s>=3 already forces X>1/sqrt(2)>2/3. Thus all old admissible seeds retain the new certificate automatically. For a proper h^2 seed the known port relation is Y_2=1/(2X). The new test becomes X>=2/3, equivalently Y_2<=3/4, in addition to the actual strict source/geometric hypotheses. The weaker proper h^2 inequality X>1/2 by itself does NOT imply (13) or (14). Thus a fixed mixed grammar with h^2 seeds can inherit the old mixed-source proof by checking the algebraic inequality (13) at its actual selected complete gluing branch, provided its other source, packet and geometric interfaces have been proved independently. This does not cover all h^2 expressions. When those separately proved packet and actual marked-geometry hypotheses hold, the [original-source long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) applies with all its original scalar, Cartan, phase and peripheral normalizations. Fix the expression and its retained half-twist signs, then fix independently sufficiently long signed integral full-twist fillings. The threshold may depend on this fixed datum. If the chosen main-component parity gives a knot and ALL auxiliary circles are filled, the conclusion is the actual **knot complement volume**: \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] The limit retains both parities and composite levels. With some auxiliary circles unfilled, the corresponding conclusion concerns the actual remaining cusped link complement. This conditional transfer does not assert that every two-leaf expression passes (13) or (14), and does not replace the original signed knot by a different diagonal or pure partner. ## Dependencies - [Whole original mixed-source gap](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) - [Full Newton transport and normal terms](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md) - [Uniform all-color core envelope](actual_pretzel_global_core_spectral_gap.md) - [Actual seed port formulas](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md) No numerical asymptotic audit is used as proof. Native MathML and AST dependency checks validate the document rather than its conclusions.

title: Long-twist volume equality for every strict Conway composition tree
status: Every fixed strict literal Conway tree
text: # Long-twist volume equality for every strict Conway composition tree 31 October 2026. A knot can be built by stacking and turning two-strand tangles, then joining their outside endpoints. This note proves the volume conjecture for every fixed construction of this kind that satisfies the strictness test below, once each of its signed twist counts is sufficiently large. The test is finite and depends on the specified construction. It does not assert that every arborescent knot has such a presentation. The proof has two parts that must be kept together. The finite quantum source is estimated without discarding the cancellations between its terms. Its selected asymptotic is then identified with the hyperbolic geometry of the same marked tangle construction. Rearranging a source for an estimate is not used as a substitute for an isotopy of tangles. ## 1. The tangle construction and the theorem A two-strand tangle is placed in a box with four ordered boundary endpoints. Let \(R^n\) be the standard two-strand braid with \(n\) signed half-twists. Positive and negative integers give the two crossing directions. The operation \(T\) turns a box through a quarter-turn, with the fixed endpoint convention of the source construction. Multiplication \(FG\) stacks two boxes in order, and \(C\) is the prescribed cylindrical closure of the four remaining endpoints. Fix a finite expression \[ \tau=C(FG) \tag{1} \] built from these operations and \(H\ge2\) separately labeled basic pieces. Each piece occurs once and has its own integer weight. After the auxiliary fillings, the \(i\)th piece is the rational tangle \[ h_i(n_i)=T(R^{n_i}). \tag{2} \] The number of pieces is denoted by \(H\); the type label \(H\) introduced below is a separate use of that letter. Write \(K_\tau(\mathbf n)\) for the diagram obtained from this literal construction. Its endpoint order, local disk framings and cylindrical closure are fixed. The invariant also keeps the one-cut mark used to define the reduced evaluation: one component is cut at the specified place before the enhanced scalar is taken. ### The finite strictness test The source calculation associates a normalized output state to every open subexpression. There are three possible intervals of strict output states. Type \(L\) has interval \((0,1/2)\), type \(H\) has interval \((1/2,1)\), and type \(A\) has interval \((0,1)\). These are state variables in the finite-sum and angle calculation, not twist counts. Start with type \(L\) on each basic piece. A turn exchanges \(L\) and \(H\) and preserves \(A\). At a product use \[ LL,LA,AA\longmapsto A,\qquad HL,HA\longmapsto H,\qquad HH\longmapsto\varnothing. \tag{3} \] where either order of the two input types is allowed. The symbol \(\varnothing\) means that there is no strict state. At the final closure in (1), the root pair must be \(AA,AL,AH\) or \(LH\), again in either order. Call a presentation passing these checks **strict**. For example, a stack of two basic pieces has type \(A\), so the closure of two such stacks passes the test. The isolated closure of two basic pieces has root pair \(LL\) and fails. Failure is a limitation of this theorem for that presentation, not a counterexample to the volume conjecture. The [source compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) proves that this recursive test is equivalent to a strict state in the reduced wire polytope: the set of normalized internal indices satisfying all product and closure constraints. Thus strictness is checked on the finite construction; it is not an assumption that an unspecified critical point behaves well. **Theorem.** For every fixed strict presentation \(\tau\), there is a finite number \(B(\tau)\) with the following property. Choose a fixed tuple of integers \(\mathbf n\) with \(|n_i|>B(\tau)\) for every piece. If following the endpoints of the literal diagram gives one component and no internal closed component, then \(K_\tau(\mathbf n)\) is a hyperbolic knot and \[ \boxed{\quad \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log|K_N(K_\tau(\mathbf n))| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_\tau(\mathbf n)). \quad} \tag{4} \] Here \(K_N\) is the reduced enhanced Kashaev evaluation in the normalization of the source construction. The limit runs through all positive integer levels, including even, odd and composite levels. The signs and relative magnitudes of the integers are unrestricted. The presentation and all twist integers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity, and the threshold may depend on the entire presentation. The [constructive pairing theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), §7, supplies knot-producing parity choices for every strict presentation. It does not say that every parity choice gives a knot. One can equivalently fix a knot-producing pattern \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\), write \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\), and require the independently signed integers \(|p_i|\) to be sufficiently large. Taking the maximum over the finitely many parity choices gives the stated \(B(\tau)\). These knots are Conway algebraic, or arborescent, because the pieces (2), their ordered products and their turns are actual Conway tangle operations. The theorem concerns the stated class of presentations and long weights. It does not classify all arborescent knots or all their possible presentations. ## 2. The finite source and its geometric exponential rate Before filling, each twist region is represented by an auxiliary crossing circle and an integer color. A color is a representation label in the invariant, not another component of the final knot. The local operator, also called a coupon, is \[ P_i=R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i},\qquad h_i=T(P_i),\qquad 1\le j_i\le N. \tag{5} \] Here \(L_{j_i}\) is the crossing-circle operator of color \(j_i\), and \(R^{\epsilon_i}\) retains the prescribed half-twist. Applying the tangle operations to these operators and then closing gives the scalar \(Z_N^\epsilon(\mathbf j)\), called the source of (1). The local spectral algebra can have repeated roots. A polynomial operator at a double root is determined by both its value and its first derivative there. These derivative coefficients are the first normal terms. They are retained in \(Z_N^\epsilon\), together with every color, unit framing phase and peripheral mark. Keeping only values at the spectral nodes would change the source. The positive complete-color calculation has exponential rate \[ F_0=\max_{y\in P_\tau} \left\{\sum_{i=1}^H g(a_i(y)) +\sum_{v=1}^{H-2}m(x_v(y),y_v(y),z_v(y))\right\}, \tag{6} \] with local functions \[ \begin{aligned} J(t)&=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\\ g(a)&=J(2a)-4J(a),\\ m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). \end{aligned} \tag{7} \] The function \(J\) is the integrated log-sine function. The leaf term \(g\) and product term \(m\) arise from the exact sine-factorial coefficients. The variables \(a_i\) are normalized leaf indices, while \(x_v,y_v,z_v\) are the two inputs and output at a product. The polytope \(P_\tau\) retains their common wire constraints, so adjacent products cannot optimize their shared index independently. The symbol \(y\) in the maximum denotes the full vector of independent state variables. At the closing product, the coefficient is exactly one. That factor is removed from the action, while its complementary-index relation is kept. Every remaining product satisfies \(\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\). The compiler produces a primitive integer lattice of dimension \(2H-3\): after choosing free coordinates, there is no further hidden congruence restricting the admissible grid. Strictness gives the interior geometric maximum in the knot cases of the theorem. The [general core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) and [marked geometric theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) identify \(2\pi F_0\) with the volume of the complete augmented exterior. They also give a nearby geometric deformation and a nonzero local asymptotic. A local asymptotic alone does not bound the rest of a signed sum. The global estimate needed here is \[ \begin{aligned} \sup_{\mathbf j}|Z_N^\epsilon(\mathbf j)| &\le \exp N(F_0+o(1)),\\ \max_i(N-j_i)\ge\delta N \quad&\Longrightarrow\quad |Z_N^\epsilon(\mathbf j)| \le \exp N(F_0-\gamma_\delta) \end{aligned} \tag{8} \] for each fixed \(0<\delta<1\), with \(\gamma_\delta>0\). The first line bounds every physical color tuple. The second gives a strict loss whenever at least one color stays a fixed positive fraction away from the complete color \(N\). Sections 3–5 prove this estimate for the whole strict class. ## 3. Decomposing the source and keeping its boundary constants The [reduced-hub normal form](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) rewrites the full colored contraction as a finite tree of product junctions. A *hub* is one such junction after adjacent products without a turn between them have been combined. An internal edge between hubs carries \(T\). An ordinary external leaf carries \(h_i\); a *flagged* leaf carries its turn \(Th_i=P_i\). The flag records this algebraic position of the turn, not an additional feature added to the knot. In this form strictness is equivalent to at most one flagged leaf per hub. The equality is an identity of colored tensors, including their first normal terms. It does not assert an isotopy relative to the tangle boundary. For \(H\ge3\), a tree with no flagged hub reduces to the previously proved class whose final two boxes are both constructed from two-piece stacks by turns, products and single-piece attachments, or to the isolated three-leaf closure. For \(H=2\), the strict two-leaf knot case is covered by the [weighted-tree theorem](actual_conway_weighted_tree_long_twist_volume.md). It therefore suffices to consider \(H\ge3\) with at least one flag and choose a flagged leaf \(P_0\) as the root of the contraction. A flagged descendant sends the subtree operator \[ D_i[E]=T(P_iE),\qquad E=\prod_j Q_j, \tag{9} \] to the next junction. The factors \(Q_j\) are the attached subtrees and have type \(L\) or \(A\). The output \(D_i[E]\) has type \(L\); an ordinary physical leaf is the case \(E=1\). We call these subtree operators boundary modules because they carry the data that must be passed to the rest of the contraction. Now group every maximal connected set of unflagged hubs into one component. Its outgoing operator is \[ Q=T(A(F_1,\ldots,F_s)),\qquad s\ge2, \tag{10} \] where \(A\) ends in an unturned product and the boundary inputs \(F_i\) all have type \(L\). Within the component there are only the completed products and turns of the earlier construction. Equations (9) and (10) alternate along a finite tree. Each step depends only on smaller subtrees, which is why the induction below terminates. To keep track of exponential constants, let \(f_Q(b)\) be the optimized positive action of a subtree \(Q\) when its output is fixed at \(b\). This is its boundary profile. Define \[ \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le b\le1/2}\{g(b)+f_Q(b)\},\qquad G_0=g(1/4)=\frac{2\,\mathrm{Catalan}}{\pi}. \tag{11} \] where Catalan denotes Catalan's constant. The maximization in \(\Omega_Q\) closes that profile against one leaf action. It supplies the boundary rate to be used for the whole subtree, rather than a freely chosen norm budget. The [rigid-profile theorem](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) proves \[ f_{D_i[E]}(b)=g(b)+c_i,\qquad c_i=\sum_j\Omega_{Q_j},\qquad \Omega_{D_i[E]}=c_i+2G_0. \tag{12} \] for the module (9). In particular, it fixes the additive constant \(c_i\) from its attached subtrees.
