Let V_F^0 be the SAME sum of leaf and multiplication tetrahedral volumes, restricted to this face. Equivalently these are the polytope and volume function for R F with its final turn wire deleted. Thus the proved full-sequence limit is lim_N (2pi/N)log D_N(F)=2 max_(P_F^0) V_F^0. (4) For the cap-closed product FG, the final product has output z=0. The exact constraints max(x,y)<=z<=x+y force x=y=0. Its product weight is exactly one at every level, and its continuous product action is m(0,0,0)=0. More explicitly, the three product angle triples are all (0,0,1), so the entire final gate is flat. Deleting the forced wires therefore gives the literal affine identity P_(FG)^0 = P_F^0 x P_G^0, V_(FG)^0 = V_F^0 + V_G^0. (5) These equalities hold on the whole CLOSED polytopes, not just near a saddle. They include boundary maxima and every shared wire inside each factor. Consequently max V_(FG)^0 = max V_F^0 + max V_G^0. (6) At the exact integer level the state sets have the same Cartesian product and the weights multiply. Thus (5) is stronger than deriving additivity after taking a limit: both its quantum and angle versions come from the same forced zero-coordinate conservation law. The stationarity equations for nonflat atoms split into the two independent systems as well. Any claim of a single nondegenerate geometric critical point for the unreduced whole expression must first remove this forced-flat gate and respect the topological decomposition (2). Uniqueness or algebraicity of the two reduced optima does not erase the connected-sum sphere. ## 4. A general boundary reduction procedure Retain a closure flag C or D alongside the actual expression tree. At a turn, switch the flag and retain the child's diagram and mark. At a product with flag D, split into the two children, each with flag D, and record the sphere and its upper/lower cap labels from section 2. At a product with flag C, stop at that factor. Leaves are retained. This terminates since each step removes at least one expression vertex. It yields simultaneously: * an exact product of original source scalars; * an exhibited componentwise connected-sum decomposition of the unmarked closed diagram, with transported marked data recorded; * a Cartesian product decomposition of its reduced angle polytopes, and an additive decomposition of their volume functions. No assertion of primeness is attached to the factors at which this procedure stops. A four-punctured Conway seam inside such a factor still needs its actual incidence and completeness proof. This is an exact boundary reduction, not a complete JSJ algorithm. ## 5. Positive exponential growth can come from several hyperbolic pieces Let A=h^3 be the robust seed and set, for k>=1, E_k=R((R A)^k). The whole original scalar satisfies, at EVERY N>=3, C_N(E_k)=C_N(A)^k. (7) This follows from (1) and R^2=1 on the actual algebra. In this particular family there is no ambiguity about the connected-sum component: A has U main pairing and two internal main circles; R A has through pairing and the same two internal circles. In its cap closure the upper and lower caps therefore lie on ONE main component. Every interface sphere in section 2 joins those components. Rotating the closed factor back identifies it with the actual theta closure C(A), including the transported point on that component. The [theta-link geometry](actual_marked_theta_link_and_angle_geometry.md) already proves that this factor is the literal untwisted six-component augmented theta link, has four regular ideal octahedra, and satisfies the original-source limit 4v8. Consequently E_k is an actual componentwise connected sum of k such theta links and has number of components = 5k+1, lim_N (2pi/N)log C_N(E_k)=4k v8. (8) For k>=2 its complement is not a complete finite-volume hyperbolic manifold. Here is a group proof which avoids inferring topology from the scalar. The explicit sum sphere gives, by cutting collars and van Kampen, an amalgam of the two summand groups over the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by the glued component's meridian mu. Each theta summand is already proved complete hyperbolic, so its cusp group injects as Z^2. Choose a longitude lambda_1 and lambda_2 in the two adjacent summands. Each commutes with mu, and neither lies in <mu>. The amalgam normal-form argument says that their commutator lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_1^-1 lambda_2^-1 is nontrivial: its four letters alternate between the factors and none lies in the amalgamated cyclic subgroup. Their images remain nontrivial after further sums by the same normal form. In a torsion-free orientation-preserving hyperbolic manifold group, the centralizer of a nontrivial parabolic is abelian. To see this directly, conjugate that parabolic to z->z+1. A commuting Mobius map must fix infinity, hence has form z->az+b; commutation forces a=1. All such translations commute. Here mu would be the meridian of an actual cusp and hence a nontrivial parabolic, contradicting the two noncommuting longitudes in its centralizer. This proves the stated nonhyperbolicity. Equation (8) is therefore equality with the SUM of the volumes of the exhibited hyperbolic summands, not the volume of a nonexistent complete hyperbolic structure on the whole complement. No general simplicial-volume or JSJ-identification theorem is needed or claimed for this statement. It supplies a necessary scope check for any proposed universal Conway volume theorem, while preserving the exact whole-source and variational information. ## 6. What remains after the reduction This result supplies a general topology-compatible reduction rather than a new primitive hyperbolic equality. It strengthens the earlier pure cap-run example: the obstruction persists with arbitrary positive rates and with genuine complete hyperbolic factors, so a nonzero variational maximum is not a hyperbolicity certificate. For each retained cylindrical factor, the outstanding task remains the actual global face/edge/peripheral dictionary for its nonflat angle functional. The two-punctured sum spheres above can be removed before that task. An internal four-punctured seam cannot be removed by the same argument. Audit: [exact full-source, support, and component checks](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction_results.json). The finite calculations supplement the uniform algebraic identity, explicit sphere construction, and variational Cartesian-product proof; they are not numerical manifold recognition or a proof for unreduced primitive factors. The cap-sum decomposition identifies connected sums. It does not identify an unreduced diagram with a primitive hyperbolic complement.

title: A uniform complex packet for the actual positive Conway core
text: # A uniform complex packet for the actual positive Conway core 29 October 2026. A fixed rectangular window about the unique strict complete optimizer gives an EXACT separately-even holomorphic packet for the original positive auxiliary-color core. Its complex asymptotic has a nonzero analytic amplitude at every level parity. The proof keeps the finite lattice window, its endpoint currents and all nonzero cotangent modes. It is not an inference from a real-grid asymptotic. This note concerns the core packet and its comparison with the WHOLE positive core on real physical colors. Signed alias estimates and a geometric peripheral interpretation are additional inputs; they are not supplied by the complex Laplace argument itself. ## 1. The actual lattice and a fixed strict window Fix one retained cylindrical robust Conway factor. Expand its seed blocks into h leaves and products, and let H be its number of leaves. The expanded expression tree has H-1 products. Delete only the final forced-flat product, whose exact multiplication coefficient is one, and impose its exact input relation i+j=D, where D=N-1. The remaining H leaves and H-2 products have a unique strict complete optimizer by the existing boundary-barrier theorem. Every leaf index lies strictly between zero and D/2, and every retained product's four strict inequalities hold there. There are exactly d=2H-3 (1) free integer wire coordinates. Indeed the H leaf outputs and H-1 product outputs give 2H-1 variables before the final closure. Turn outputs are eliminated one at a time by r_out=D-r_in. Fixing the root output and its final input-sum relation removes two variables. The last relation involves variables of disjoint child subtrees with coefficients +1 or -1, so one can solve it integrally. There is no parity-dependent lattice index or omitted congruence class. Choose the remaining physical wire indices k_1,...,k_d as coordinates and put x=k/N. Every other physical wire has the exact form r_w=N ell_w(x)+delta_w, (2) where ell_w is integral affine and delta_w is a fixed integer. The constants delta_w retain every occurrence of D=N-1. They are not silently replaced by zero. Let x_0 be the strict complete optimizer in these coordinates. Choose a sufficiently small closed rectangular box B centered at x_0, entirely inside the strict source domain. Let chi_l=h_l/N be the auxiliary-color deficit of leaf l. At physical colors h_l>=0, its exact positive core coefficient is A_(N,r_l)(h_l)=N^2 s_(2r_l) /[s_(r_l)^2 s_(r_l-h_l)s_(r_l+h_l)]. (3) On a small fixed complex chi polydisk, replace every sine factorial in the SAME leaf and product weight by the [canonical marked interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) G_N. Define the packet Z_N^win(chi)=sum_(k in Z^d, k/N in B) I_N(k/N,chi), (4) where I_N is the product of the H interpolated factors (3) and the H-2 actual interpolated Newton multiplication coefficients. After shrinking B and the chi polydisk, every scaled factorial argument has real part in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,1), on a fixed complex thickening of B. Thus I_N is holomorphic and nonzero there. For large N, EVERY lattice point in (4) is an actual admissible core state at every physical color in the chosen real chi window. No support indicator changes inside this box. Formula (4) is finite and separately even in every chi_l, by the two factors r_l+-h_l in (3). ## 2. Exact normalization of the interpolated summand Write every factorial argument as N alpha_nu(x,chi)+c_nu, with integer c_nu, and let sigma_nu be its signed multiplicity. The canonical uniform expansion gives G_N(N alpha+c) =sqrt(2N sin(pi alpha)) exp[N J(alpha)] (2sin(pi alpha))^c [1+O(N^-1)], J(alpha)=integral_0^alpha Log(2sin(pi u))du. (5) Its marks are continued from positive real arguments. The remainder and its fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller complex compact sets. Equation (5) follows directly from the canonical expansion at alpha+c/N; its shift factor is ESSENTIAL when c is nonzero. Define f(x,chi)=sum_nu sigma_nu J(alpha_nu(x,chi)), b(x,chi)=2^(3-3H) product_nu sin(pi alpha_nu)^(sigma_nu/2) (2sin(pi alpha_nu))^(sigma_nu c_nu). (6) All square roots and powers are continued from the positive real complete window. A leaf has one numerator and four denominator factorials, with its extra N^2. A retained product has two numerator and five denominator factorials. Consequently sum_nu sigma_nu=-3H-3(H-2)=6-6H, I_N(x,chi)=N^(3-H) b(x,chi) exp[Nf(x,chi)] [1+O(N^-1)]. (7) The leading amplitude b is nonzero and positive on the real complete window. It contains all D=N-1 offset factors from (2); there is no unknown periodic normalization. At chi=0, f is exactly the complete source action V_E/pi in the selected free wire coordinates. For general chi it is the sum of the actual product actions and g_chi(x_l)=J(2x_l)-2J(x_l) -J(x_l-chi_l)-J(x_l+chi_l) (8) over the leaves. Here x_l=ell_l(x) is its limiting leaf coordinate. ## 3. A finite-window complex lattice Laplace lemma The following elementary argument applies to (7), and more generally to a fixed-dimensional analytic summand N^a b_N exp(N f), provided: * f is holomorphic on a fixed complex thickening of B and a parameter polydisk, real on the real slice at zero; * at zero it has its unique strict nondegenerate maximum x_0 in B, with negative definite real Hessian; * b_N=b+O(N^-1) uniformly holomorphically, with b(x_0,0)>0; * the source sum uses the entire rectangular integer lattice window. Shrink the box if necessary so the real Hessian stays uniformly negative definite throughout it. The implicit-function theorem gives one holomorphic critical point x_*(chi) near x_0. Put phi(chi)=f(x_*(chi),chi), A(chi)=-f_xx(x_*(chi),chi). Then uniformly on a fixed smaller complex parameter polydisk, sum_(k/N in B) N^a b_N(k/N,chi) exp[Nf(k/N,chi)] =N^(a+d/2) (2pi)^(d/2) b(x_*(chi),chi)/sqrt(det A(chi)) exp[Nphi(chi)] [1+O(N^-1)]. (9) The determinant square root is positive at zero. Here is a proof that explicitly controls the discrete nonzero modes. For each coordinate enclose its retained integer interval by a rectangle whose vertical sides are halfway between consecutive lattice points, and whose horizontal sides have fixed imaginary heights +-eta. The endpoints differ from B's endpoints by O(1/N). The product residue formula with kernels pi N cot(pi N z_j) is EXACTLY the original finite sum. On a vertical half-grid side |cot(pi N z_j)|<=1. On a horizontal side, cot(pi N(x+i eta))=-i+O(exp(-2pi N eta)), cot(pi N(x-i eta))= i+O(exp(-2pi N eta)). (10) At parameter zero the real part of f changes by O(d eta^2) under these imaginary shifts, because its first derivatives are real. The same bound holds with a small additional parameter error after shrinking the parameter disk. The real boundary of B has a fixed strict gap below f(x_0,0). Choose eta first, small enough that O(d eta^2)<pi eta and small enough to retain half the boundary gap. Then choose the fixed parameter disk sufficiently small to retain both inequalities, relative to Re phi(chi). Every contour piece with a vertical side is exponentially below the critical value. Every nonconstant cotangent-error term in the product expansion has at least the factor exp(-2pi N eta); the possible phase increase is smaller than exp(pi N eta). Polynomial prefactors cannot remove these strict exponential gaps. The 2^d constant horizontal kernel terms have coefficient N^d/2^d and the same orientation. Deforming their horizontal boxes to the real box only adds vertical connectors with the already established boundary gap. Thus the exact sum equals N^d times the ordinary analytic integral over B, up to a uniform exponentially smaller error. Replacing the real half-grid rectangle B_N by B changes only O(1/N)-wide boundary strips, which have the same strict exponential gap. This is the finite-window counterpart of suppressing all nonzero Poisson modes; no infinite-lattice replacement was made. Finally deform that integral to x_*(chi)+(B-x_0). This translation remains inside the same holomorphic tube. Its endpoint connectors have the boundary gap. On the translated box, Re(f(x_*+u,chi)-phi(chi))<=-c|u|^2 uniformly for real u, since A(chi) remains close to a positive definite real matrix. Taylor expansion and Gaussian integration give the stated determinant. The nominal N^-1/2 corrections are odd in u and integrate to zero on the symmetric Gaussian domain; truncation errors are exponentially small. The remaining relative error is O(N^-1), including the uniform b_N-b error. This proves (9) for the exact finite packet, not merely for real parameter values or a selected subsequence. ## 4. The Conway packet and its color Hessian Apply (9) with a=3-H and d=2H-3. There is a fixed complex chi polydisk on which Z_N^win(chi)=N^(3/2) a_E(chi) exp[Nphi_E(chi)] [1+O(N^-1)], (11) a_E(chi)=(2pi)^((2H-3)/2) b(x_*(chi),chi)/sqrt(det A(chi)). (12) The amplitude is nonzero and a_E(0)>0. This is the raw source normalization in the stated free integer coordinates. Any separately recorded enhancement or framing phase must still multiply it; (11) does not remove such a factor from an invariant. All statements hold on the whole sequence of sufficiently large N, including both parities. The upper leaf cutoff floor((N-1)/2) lies outside the fixed strict window. Half-grid endpoint choices affect only exponentially small boundary terms, and (2) has no parity- dependent lattice density. The canonical factorial normalization has fixed the actual square roots and the offset factors in (6). The phase and amplitude are separately even in each chi_l. Indeed f and the summand have this symmetry, and uniqueness of the local critical branch gives the same symmetry for x_*. At completeness, phi_E(0)=max V_E/pi, partial_(chi_l) phi_E(0)=0, partial_(chi_l)partial_(chi_m) phi_E(0) =-2pi cot(pi x_(l,*)) delta_lm. (13) To verify the last formula, f_(x chi_l)(x,0)=0 IDENTICALLY in x, because each leaf factor is even in its own parameter. Hence the usual critical-point Schur-complement correction vanishes here. The direct second derivative of (8) is -2pi cot(pi x_l). Every x_(l,*) is in (0,1/2), so this Hessian is strictly negative. Uniformity on a complex disk also supplies every fixed color parameter derivative by Cauchy estimates on a smaller disk. ## 5. Comparison with the positive core, and the remaining interfaces For physical real deficits in a sufficiently small fixed window, the positive core outside B is exponentially smaller than the complete source at chi=0. Indeed each exact deformed core coefficient is at most its complete counterpart, the product coefficients are positive, and the complete action has a strict compact support gap outside B. The polynomial number of states and the uniform global factorial estimates preserve that gap. Therefore |Z_N^core(h)-Z_N^win(h/N)| <=poly(N) exp[N(phi_E(0)-gamma)] (14) with gamma>0. Shrink the real color window so phi_E(h/N) stays above phi_E(0)-gamma/2. Equations (11),(14) then give exponential relative accuracy for the WHOLE positive core. A separate uniform estimate for the signed alias sectors can be combined with (14); the present proof does not assume such sectors are absent. Nor does the complex window argument identify chi with a geometric meridian or establish the Dehn-filling contour. It supplies the exact even analytic core packet, its nonzero marked amplitude, its all-parity normalization and its uniform complex saddle expansion, which those later steps require. ## 6. An explicit three-leaf calibration, including the integer shift For the retained seed C(h^3), use the three original leaf indices i,j,k as free coordinates. The surviving gate output is EXACTLY t=D-k. Thus its limiting output is z=1-x_3, but its interpolated factorials have the additional shift -1 in t. The limiting phase is F(x_1,x_2,x_3)=sum_l g(x_l)+m(x_1,x_2,1-x_3). Its unique maximum occurs at all three x_l=a=atan(2)/pi. Directly, sin(pi a)=2/sqrt(5), sin(2pi a)=4/5, sin(pi(3a-1))=2/(5sqrt(5)), g'(a)=m_z(a,a,1-a)=-log4, m_x(a,a,1-a)=m_y(a,a,1-a)=log4. These give stationarity in the actual three free coordinates. The negative Hessian and its positive determinant square root are A=(25pi/4)(I_3+1 1^T), sqrt(det A)=125pi^(3/2)/4. (15) Each unshifted leaf amplitude in (5) is sqrt(10)/8; the unshifted gate amplitude is 5sqrt(10)/16. The actual output t=N(1-x_3)-1 adds the factor exp(-m_z)=4. Equivalently its seven factorial shifts are 0,-1,0,0,-1,-1,+1 in the displayed numerator/denominator order of the exact Newton coefficient mu_(N;i,j,t)=s_(i+j)s_t /[s_i s_j s_(t-i)s_(t-j)s_(i+j-t)]. Thus b(a,a,a,0)=(sqrt(10)/8)^3 (5sqrt(10)/16) 4=125/512, a_(h^3)(0)=(2pi)^(3/2)b/sqrt(det A)=sqrt(2)/64. (16) Omitting D=N-1's shift would give a leading amplitude four times too small. This makes the shift convention in (2),(5) testable. The phase is F_0=3g(a)+m(a,a,1-a)=2v_8/pi, using the already proved [whole three-leaf seed evaluation](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md). Hence the theorem above and the positive-core comparison give Z_(h^3,N)=(sqrt(2)/64)N^(3/2)exp(2Nv_8/pi)(1+O(N^-1)). (17) The audit derives the gradient, Hessian, determinant and amplitude from the individual signed factorial arguments using exact rational and radical arithmetic. It also evaluates the original positive sum sum_(0<=i,j,k<=M; i+j+k>=D) a_(N,i)a_(N,j)a_(N,k) mu_(N;i,j,D-k). For N=5,8,20,40,80 its ratios to the leading term of (17) are 1.44279, 1.26530, 1.10276, 1.05067 and 1.02515. Additional levels 21,41,81 check the odd sequence. These finite values are diagnostics of the independently proved normalization, not an extrapolation argument for (17) or the complex-window theorem. Audit: [exact calibration and finite positive sums](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_complex_window_laplace_results.json). The complex-window argument retains the primitive lattice count, integer offsets and finite contour errors. It requires the separate source-algebra and alias results. The [whole-source assembly](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) combines this packet with separately proved alias and marked geometric results.

title: Controlling a turn preceded by an actual character operator
text: # Controlling a turn preceded by an actual character operator A polynomial operator in a knot calculation is determined at a repeated spectral node by both its value and its first derivative. This note uses a norm retaining both pieces of data. It proves that a specific physical operation preserves useful bounds in that norm: multiply by the actual circle character and retained half twist, then apply the physical turn. The result has three parts. The operation adds a precisely determined exponential cost, concentrates the canonical output polynomial near the spectral point \(-2\), and gives a strict loss when any original circle color is a fixed fraction away from complete. Products preserve the same kind of estimate. Consequently one can iterate these operations through the recursive class defined in Section 4. The [reduced-hub source adapter](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) identifies that class with trees in which every multiplication hub has a distinguished original character. A turn without such a character is a different operation. Its sharp norm cost is computed in Section 5, but this cost cannot simply be added to a previously fixed geometric action. The later [positive-probe theorem](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) supplies the additional estimate used for those regions in the full strict-tree proof. The finite inputs are the [original positive Newton turn and pairing](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md), the [full-Hermite localization estimates](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), and the [exact root-character Fourier theorem](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md). The [rigid-spine geometry](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) separately identifies the complete action for the fully flagged class. ## 1. A norm that retains the full spectral data Fix the level \(N\), set \(d=N-1\) and \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), and use the following polynomial and basis. Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind; the physical turn is the separate map \(T\) in (1). \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad c_k=2\cos((2k+1)\pi/N),\qquad \widehat B_r(z)=\frac{\prod_{a<r}(c_a-z)}{s_r^2}, \qquad s_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin(\pi a/N),\quad s_0=1. \] The algebra is \(\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\). The roots of \(P_N\) are the actual Casimir nodes: they are double except for the simple node \(-2\) at odd levels. The basis elements \(\widehat B_r\) have indices \(0\le r\le d\). The marked closure functional \(\phi\) and the physical turn obey \[ T\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{d-r},\qquad \phi(\widehat B_r\widehat B_t)=\mathbf1_{r+t=d}. \tag{1} \] At a double node \(c\), reduction modulo \((z-c)^2\) retains \(F(c)+F'(c)(z-c)\). For example, the local class \(z-c\) has zero value and nonzero derivative, so nodal values alone would not detect it. The following faithful norm measures exactly the retained Hermite data: \[ \|F\|_{\mathcal J} =\max\{\max_{\text{double }c}(|F(c)|+|F'(c)|), |F(-2)|\text{ if }N\text{ is odd}\}. \tag{2} \] The derivative rule \((FG)'=F'G+FG'\) shows that this norm is submultiplicative. Let \(R\) be the original crossing operator, and let \(L_j(z)=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2)\) be the color-\(j\) circle character, where \(U_{j-1}\) is the second-kind Chebyshev polynomial. The physical color satisfies \(1\le j\le N\), and \(\epsilon\in\{0,\pm1\}\) records the retained half twist. The residue formula and the actual crossing data give \[ |\phi(F)|\le3N\|F\|_{\mathcal J},\qquad \|R^\epsilon L_j\|_{\mathcal J}\le CN^3 \quad(1\le j\le N,\ \epsilon=0,\pm1). \tag{3} \] The second inequality is for the actual crossing, not a semisimple replacement: its node values have modulus one, \[ \frac{R'(c_k)}{R(c_k)} =-\frac{N-1-2k}{4i\sin((2k+1)\pi/N)} \] at every double node, and this has size \(O(N^2)\). The original circle is \(L_j(z)=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2)\); it has \(|L_j|\le N\), \(|L_j'|\le CN^3\) on \([-2,2]\). The odd simple node has no derivative obligation. The input \(E_N\) may already be a product of subtree operators. It may have degree greater than \(N-1\) before reduction. The operation studied here, called a decorated character turn, is \[ D_{N,j}^{\epsilon}[E_N] =T(R^\epsilon L_jE_N)\pmod {P_N}. \tag{4} \] Its canonical degree-\(<N\) representative has coefficients \[ D_{N,j}^{\epsilon}[E_N]=\sum_{r=0}^{d}d_r\widehat B_r,\qquad d_r=\phi(\widehat B_rR^\epsilon L_jE_N). \tag{5} \] Indeed (1) extracts the coefficient \(d-r\) before applying \(T\). Formula (5) is useful because it bounds an output coefficient by the full marked pairing before reconstruction. It retains all original confluent terms and all original colors. In particular it is not a covariance assertion for a projected coupon. Define the rate function and its maximal value by \[ J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\quad g(u)=J(2u)-4J(u),\quad G_0=g(1/4)=2\,\mathrm{Catalan}/\pi. \] Here Catalan denotes \(\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}(-1)^m/(2m+1)^2\). The proved Newton estimates, with absolute powers independent of all physical colors, are \[ \begin{array}{ll} \|\widehat B_r\|_{\mathcal J} \le CN^5\widehat B_r(-2),& \log\widehat B_r(-2)=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N),\quad 0\le r\le M,\\[2mm] \|\widehat B_r\|_{\mathcal J}\le N^2/16,&M<r<N, \end{array} \tag{6} \] Both endpoints and both parities are included. These are §§2–3 of the [full-Hermite localization theorem](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md). Combining (3), (5), and (6) proves the full-coefficient estimate \[ |d_r|\le CN^C\|E_N\|_{\mathcal J} \begin{cases} \widehat B_r(-2),&r\le M,\\ 1,&r>M. \end{cases} \tag{7} \] There is no sum over input coefficients and no loss depending on the degree of the unreduced representative \(E_N\). In particular \(E_N=1\) gives, for the whole physical leaf \(h_j^\epsilon=T(R^\epsilon L_j)\), \[ |[\widehat B_r]h_j^\epsilon| \le \begin{cases} \exp\{Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)\},&r\le M,\\ CN^C,&r>M. \end{cases} \tag{8} \] This does not assert the same bound for the separate coherent core. The two original bands can cancel in a low coefficient. Consequently the plateau bound on the isolated signed core is not contradicted. ## 2. Reconstructing the output and locating its angular maximum The real number \(F\) in the next hypothesis is an exponential upper rate for the input family. It is not another polynomial. Suppose, uniformly in that specified family, \[ \|E_N\|_{\mathcal J}\le \exp N(F+e_N),\qquad e_N\longrightarrow0. \tag{9} \] Then \[ \|D_{N,j}^{\epsilon}[E_N]\|_{\mathcal J} \le \exp N(F+2G_0+\widetilde e_N), \qquad \widetilde e_N\longrightarrow0. \tag{10} \] This follows by reconstructing from (7) and using (6): the low sum is at most a polynomial times \(\|E_N\|_{\mathcal J}\sum_{r\le M}\widehat B_r(-2)^2\); the high sum has only a polynomial cost. Since \(g\) has its unique maximum \(G_0\) at \(1/4\), (10) follows uniformly. A fixed loss in the input exponent \(F\) is preserved exactly in (10). More strongly, (9) alone implies that the output polynomial has a fixed angular Gaussian envelope. There are \(c,C,y_0>0\), independent of the input family and physical character color, such that \[ |D_{N,j}^{\epsilon}[E_N](2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le \exp N\{F+2G_0-c(\vartheta-\pi)^2+Cy^2+\widetilde e_N\}, \quad 0\le\vartheta\le2\pi,\ |y|\le y_0. \tag{11} \] The variables \(\vartheta\) and \(y\) describe the complex spectral ellipse \(z=2\cos(\vartheta+iy)\). Its real midpoint \(\vartheta=\pi,y=0\) is \(z=-2\). Inequality (11) gives quadratic decay away from that angle and a quadratic cost for moving a small distance off the real axis. Here and below the polynomial in (11) is the unique representative of degree less than \(N\). There is no claim that arbitrary unreduced representatives satisfy it. For completeness, the low Newton strip rate is \[ b(u,\vartheta,y) =\int_0^u\log|2\cos(2\pi v)-2\cos(\vartheta+iy)|\,dv-2J(u). \tag{12} \] Uniform upper Riemann sums hold on the closed range \(0\le u\le1/2\): truncate the logarithm below, pass to uniform Riemann sums, then remove the truncation using uniform integrability of the two circular logarithms. This retains moving and coalescing numerator zeros. The sine factorial error is uniformly \(O(\log N)\). At \(y=0\), strict circular rearrangement gives \[ b(u,\vartheta,0)\le b(u,\pi,0)=g(u), \tag{13} \] strict for \(0<u<1/2\) and \(\vartheta\ne\pi\bmod2\pi\). Hence \(g(u)+b(u,\vartheta,0)\) has the unique maximum \(2G_0\) at \((u,\vartheta)=(1/4,\pi)\). Near that point, with \(w=\vartheta-\pi+iy\), its analytic Newton action is \[ B(u,w)=-J\!\left(\frac12-u+\frac{w}{2\pi}\right) -J\!\left(\frac12-u-\frac{w}{2\pi}\right)-2J(u), \qquad B_{ww}(u,0)=-\frac{\tan\pi u}{2\pi}. \tag{14} \] Thus the maximum has a strict index and angular quadratic loss and a quadratic height cost. The complementary compact set has a uniform strict real gap, which survives small fixed complex heights. Equation (7), not a separate core envelope, now gives the low part of (11). For the high part (7) gives full-jet norm at most \(\operatorname{poly}(N)\|E_N\|_{\mathcal J}\). The already proved full Hermite interpolation estimate gives, for a canonical polynomial, \[ |F(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le CN^Ce^{N|y|}\|F\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{15} \] Choose \(y_0\) small compared with \(2G_0\) and reduce \(c\) so \(c\pi^2< G_0\). The high part then fits beneath (11) with a fixed loss. This proves the whole output envelope. No spectral gap for the input \(E_N\) was required in this step. ## 3. A color away from complete causes a strict loss A uniform norm bound alone gives Section 2. To gain a loss from the newly inserted color, the Fourier argument also needs an angular estimate for the actual input polynomial. Suppose that an actual representative of the input, possibly an unreduced product, obeys \[ |E_N(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le \exp N\{F-c_E(\vartheta-\pi)^2+C_Ey^2+e_N\}, \quad |y|\le y_E, \tag{16} \] with \(c_E\ge0\). The empty product \(E_N=1\), \(F=0\), is allowed. Every fixed number of angular derivatives required by the Fourier argument follows by Cauchy's estimate on disks of radius \(1/N\) in a smaller fixed strip. The exponent changes by \(O(1)\) there; the polynomial-in-\(2\cos\vartheta\) reflection and periodicity handle the endpoint disks. Thus these derivatives cost only powers of \(N\), uniformly in the physical colors. For a fixed syntax every unreduced representative used here has degree \(O(N)\); no arbitrary continuation of a finite physical-color array is being differentiated. Choose once a compact interval \(I\subset(0,1/2)\) about \(1/4\). Uniformly for \(r/N\in I\), the exact low Newton polynomial itself has the sharper envelope \[ |\widehat B_r(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le \exp N\{g(r/N)-c_I(\vartheta-\pi)^2+C_Iy^2+e_N'\}, \qquad c_I>0,\quad e_N'\to0. \tag{17} \] The proof is (12)–(14), now with \(u\) in a fixed compact interval: strict rearrangement gives the angular complement gap uniformly, and \(B_{ww}\) is uniformly negative near \(\pi\). Therefore \(\widehat B_rE_N\) satisfies the whole-child hypothesis of the [exact root-character Fourier theorem](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md), uniformly over \(r/N\in I\), with rate \(F+g(r/N)\). That exact theorem retains the actual \(R^\epsilon\) values and normals, the missing Fourier winding \(m=-1\), and both endpoint currents. For every fixed \(\delta>0\), it gives some \(\gamma_\delta>0\) such that \[ N-j\ge\delta N,\quad r/N\in I \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |d_r|\le \exp N\{F+g(r/N)-\gamma_\delta\}. \tag{18} \] This use is not an appeal to analyticity of arbitrary physical colors. Only the actual integer \(j\) occurs in the exact Fourier identity. Outside \(I\), the low reconstruction cost \(2g(r/N)\) has a fixed gap below \(2G_0\). The high reconstruction has the fixed \(2G_0\) gap already seen in §2. Equations (6)–(7),(18) imply \[ \sup_{N-j\ge\delta N} \|D_{N,j}^{\epsilon}[E_N]\|_{\mathcal J} \le \exp N(F+2G_0-\eta_\delta) \tag{19} \] for all sufficiently large \(N\). Every original sign, parity, composite level and physical input color is covered. The constants depend on the fixed input strip bounds and \(\delta\), not on those colors or on \(N\). In particular (18) with \(E_N=1\) proves a uniform strict whole-leaf coefficient loss at every macroscopic physical deficit, on each compact regular index interval. This is stronger than only bounding the full leaf's norm. ## 4. Iterating products and decorated turns The first example is one physical leaf: take \(E=1\) and obtain \(T(R^\epsilon L_j)\). A second example is the product of two such leaves, followed by another decorated turn. In each case the original character remains immediately before its recorded turn. Formally, start with the empty product \(1\), form finite products, and apply any number of operations \[ E\longmapsto D_j^\epsilon[E]=T(R^\epsilon L_jE). \tag{20} \] Every operation uses a distinct original physical circle color and retained half twist. No coupon is moved through a turn. Assign the integer count \(n(1)=0\), make it additive under products, and put \(n(D[E])=n(E)+1\). Every resulting coupon \(E\) with \(n(E)>0\) has: 1. the uniform full-jet upper rate \(2n(E)G_0\); 2. an angular Gaussian envelope of the form (16) at that same rate, with a strictly positive angular constant; 3. for each fixed \(\delta>0\), a strict full-jet loss whenever any one of its original physical colors satisfies \(N-j_i\ge\delta N\). The proof is finite induction. Products use the exact norm product rule and multiply the actual polynomial envelopes. A decorated turn uses (10)–(11). A deficit in the newly inserted character uses (19). A deficit in a descendant gives a strict input norm loss, which (10) preserves. Fixed finite products and sums have only polynomial or fixed multiplicative costs and are absorbed by reducing the positive margin. The case \(E=1\) needed for a first leaf was explicitly included. For any nonempty such \(E\), close the source by one further original character: \[ Z_N(\mathbf j)=\phi(R^{\epsilon_0}L_{j_0}E_N). \tag{21} \] Equations (3), (16), and the same root-character theorem prove \[ \sup_{\mathrm{physical}\ \mathbf j}|Z_N(\mathbf j)| \le \exp N\{2n(E)G_0+o(1)\}, \tag{22} \] and for each fixed \(\delta>0\), \[ \max_i(N-j_i)\ge\delta N \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |Z_N(\mathbf j)|\le \exp N\{2n(E)G_0-\gamma_\delta\}. \tag{23} \] If a descendant is far, use its norm loss and (3). If only the closing character is far, use the exact Fourier theorem on the full input envelope (16). In particular the root is not estimated by a separate positive alias function. ## 5. Exact complete normalization and limitations The [positive complete-character kernel](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) checks the rate, not just the upper bound. For pure complete characters the exact transform is \[ [\widehat B_r]D_N^0[E] =N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\widehat B_r(c_k)E(c_k). \tag{24} \] For \(r>M\) this vanishes. If all input nodal values are nonnegative, the surviving coefficients and every output nodal value are nonnegative. The empty input is positive, and products preserve this property. At the smallest distinct node \(c_M\), retain just the physical grid term \(k=M\) and \(r_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\): \[ D_N^0[E](c_M)\ge N\,\widehat B_{r_N}(c_M)^2E(c_M). \tag{25} \] The original sine products give \(N^{-1}\log\widehat B_{r_N}(c_M)\to G_0\) at both parities. At even levels the node shift from \(-2\) is \(O(N^{-2})\); the selected quarter-index factors stay away from zero, so its logarithmic cost is \(O(N^{-1})\). At odd levels \(c_M=-2\). Induction through the fixed tree and the exact complete closure \(\phi(L_NE)=N\sum_kE(c_k)\) gives \[ Z_N(N,\ldots,N)>0,\qquad \lim_N N^{-1}\log Z_N(N,\ldots,N)=2n(E)G_0. \tag{26} \] Equation (26) concerns this pure complete specialization. Thus the reference in (22)–(23) is the actual pure complete source rate. The separate [strict-source adapter](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) and [geometric action calculation](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) identify this recursive tree with the fully flagged hub presentation. Its rate is therefore the complete geometric action of that presentation, not an independently chosen norm budget. The same estimates also determine the sharp exponential cost of the bare turn in this norm: \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log\|T\|_{\mathcal J\to\mathcal J}=2G_0. \tag{27} \] For the upper bound set \(j=1,\epsilon=0\) in (7), so that \(L_1=1\) and \(D_{N,1}^0[E]=T(E)\). Its finite reconstruction bound is an operator estimate uniform over all inputs, and (6) gives rate at most \(2G_0\). For the lower bound use \(T(L_N)=h_N^0\): the input has polynomial norm, while the complete positive source estimate gives \(N^{-1}\log\|h_N^0\|_{\mathcal J}\to2G_0\). Thus (27) includes all original normal directions. It does not assign that cost to the geometric action of an arbitrary existing diagram. The limitation of this particular induction is now explicit. It preserves a specified character multiplication immediately before each turn. An arbitrary internal turn with no such physical character is not charged to an existing original leaf by (20). Adding an artificial \(L_j\), treating the turn as multiplicative, or assigning the resulting extra \(2G_0\) to the old geometric action would change the problem. Thus this lemma alone does not give the required geometric bound for a region without a character. The positive-probe and mixed-core propagation theorems treat that region separately; they are not consequences of pretending that (20) includes a bare turn. The original alias identity converts (23) into a total nonempty-alias gap after a finite complementary-color expansion, with its exact scalar signs and source adapter retained. The local core packet and marked filling theorem are additional inputs. The [strict-tree assembly](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) combines these results with the separate estimate for regions without characters. This note proves the spectral closure lemma used there, rather than a filling theorem from the norm bound alone.

title: Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links
text: # Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links 29 October 2026. The robust positive Conway grammar cannot produce knots by filling all its auxiliary circles with the existing integral FULL-TWIST kernel. If a compiled expression contains S occurrences of its seed A=h^3, every such filled diagram has at least 2S+1 main components. In particular the smallest seed still has at least three. This is a literal connectivity obstruction, independent of any asymptotic estimate or geometric deformation. It does not contradict the complete retained-circle volume theorem. It prevents presenting a future filling theorem for this unchanged class as a knot theorem. ## 1. The two internal circles in every seed The original unrotated complete circle L_N threads two through main arcs, with identity endpoint pairing. The genuine quarter-turn h=Rturn L_N has the planar U pairing: its two bottom main ports are joined to one another, as are its two top main ports. Stacking two U boxes creates one closed internal main component between the upper cap of the lower box and the lower cup of the upper box. It leaves U pairing on the four external ports. Therefore A=h^3 has exactly TWO closed internal main components and U external pairing. This is an actual tangle calculation, not a decomposition into quantum channels. A quarter-turn rotates a tangle and preserves all its already closed components. Stacking two tangles also preserves every closed component in each: identity wires are attached only to their exposed ports, so they cannot connect an existing closed component to another one. A stack can create additional closed components, but cannot destroy those present before it. Induction on E ::= A | Rturn E | E E consequently gives internal main components of E >= 2S(E), where S(A)=1, S(Rturn E)=S(E), and S(EF)=S(E)+S(F). Closing the four exposed ports adds at least one further main component. Hence every actual closed expression has c_main(E) >= 2S(E)+1. (1) Both cylindrical and cap closures satisfy this lower bound. All 3S(E) auxiliary components are counted separately. ## 2. The exact filling kernel preserves that connectivity The original auxiliary-color filling identity replaces a retained complete circle by the literal full twist R^(-2p), with p an integer, and its separately recorded scalar. A full twist has the IDENTITY permutation of its two main endpoints for every sign and magnitude of p, including p=0. Thus the replacement has the same main pairing as the original unrotated L_N. After the same physical quarter-turn, each replaced leaf has the same U pairing as h. All subsequent identity stacks, rotations and closures therefore have exactly the SAME main-component connectivity as the unfilled expression. In particular every one of the seed's two internal main circles persists after these fillings. If I is any subset of the auxiliary circles, the filled link has c_total(E,I)=c_main(E)+3S(E)-|I|, c_total(E,I) >= 5S(E)+1-|I|. (2) Filling every auxiliary component gives c_total=c_main>=2S+1>1. The threshold "sufficiently long" does not change this conclusion. Neither a sign choice nor arbitrarily large full-twist powers can change an even braid permutation into an odd one. ## 3. What a knot extension actually requires To reach knots one must change the original source topology, for example by retaining an ODD half-twist coupon at selected auxiliary ports before performing the full-twist fillings, or by using another seed whose exposed main connections can join these components. Such a change has its own exact quantum source. The present positive Newton coefficients and whole-source theorem cannot silently be reused after changing those coupons. The existing odd-pretzel knot construction does retain the required odd half twists, which is why its connectivity differs from the pure h grammar here. Volume invariance of an unmarked complete half-twist partner does not identify its finite quantum source or prove its long-filled asymptotic. The general complete Conway construction and any verified full-twist extension of it therefore provide a broad LINK theorem. A broad KNOT theorem remains a separate critical-path task. Audit: [literal pairings and full-twist permutation checks](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction_results.json). The proof of (1)--(2) is the all-expression component-preservation induction, not an extrapolation from the finite samples. Every seed has two permanent internal main circles. Turns and stacks preserve them, and full-twist filling has the identity endpoint permutation. Thus the resulting link-only scope is a topological fact, independent of source asymptotics.

title: A general quarter bound and the full core estimate for strict Conway trees
status: General strict-knot core theorem; aliases separate
text: # A general quarter bound and the full core estimate for strict Conway trees 31 October 2026. research proof. The assertions concern every fixed literal strict cylindrical tree, not only the completed grammar of the published manuscript. The alias part of the original invariant remains separate. No change to that manuscript's theorem is made here. ## 1. Exact scope and inputs Let the original closed expression be \(C(FG)\), where each of \(F,G\) is any finite expression in the physical leaf \(h\), the actual turn \(T\), and ordered product. Delete only its forced final gate, whose coefficient is one; retain the exact relation \(r_F+r_G=N-1\). Assume the reduced positive wire polytope has a strict state. Thus all original leaf labels are in \((0,1/2)\), and every retained gate has \(\max(x,y)<z<x+y<1\). Write \(H\ge2\) for the number of leaves. The exact compiler, boundary barrier and angle-map proof in [the exact source compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), §§1–3, apply to this arbitrary strict syntax. They give a primitive lattice of dimension \(K=2H-3\), a compact reduced polytope \(P\), and a unique strict complete maximizer \(y_*\). All wire labels are affine in the primitive variables; their finite versions include the original fixed integer offsets from \(d=N-1\). Set \[ A(y)=\sum_{i=1}^{H}g(a_i(y))+\sum_{v=1}^{H-2}m(x_v(y),y_v(y),z_v(y)), \qquad F_0=A(y_*), \] where \(g(a)=J(2a)-4J(a)\) and \(J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt\). Each original leaf has a fixed physical sign \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\). At every physical color its exact core/alias split is performed in the original full Hermite–Newton algebra, before any products or turns. Let \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{core}}_N(\mathbf h)\) be the literal scalar with every leaf replaced by its core. This is a summand of the actual source, not a new definition of the knot invariant. A core is zero if its color deficit exceeds the original low-core range. The additional exact inputs are the port types and product equations of [the strict-mask geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md), the high and quarter finite-source packet theorems, and the uniform all-color coefficient bounds proved in [the uniform all-color proof](../manuscript/sections/B2-global-core-envelope.tex). In particular the global core bound is \(\exp N(\widetilde g+o(1))\) with uniform \(o(1)\), not a global polynomial-prefactor estimate. ## 2. Every complete closed-tree leaf is at or above one quarter For an optimized open port put \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\quad \kappa=e^{-f'(b)},\quad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\quad Y^2=\kappa X^2,\quad X,Y>0. \] Then \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). The exact strict types are \[ L:(B,X,Y)=(B,B,1),\quad H:(B,X,Y)=(-Y,1,Y),\quad A:-Y<B<X. \] A turn exchanges \(X,Y\) and negates \(B\). A product has a common child \(X\), \(S=B_1+B_2>0\), and \[ B_o=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{S},\qquad Y_o=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{S}. \] At the cylindrical root the two \(B\)'s are opposite and their ordered metrics agree, so their \(X,Y\) agree. In type \(AA\), \(|B|<\min(X,Y)\), whence the quadratic identity gives \(X,Y<1\). In \(AL\), the \(L\) port has \(Y=1\), and the \(A\) inequality \(-1<-X\) gives \(X<1\). In \(AH\), the \(H\) port has \(X=1\), and the \(A\) inequality \(Y<1\) gives the other bound. In \(LH\) the explicit forms force \(X=Y=1\). These exhaust all strict root pairs. For the downward product step set \(c=1-X^2\). The identity \[ (B_1^2+c)(B_2^2+c)-(B_1B_2-c)^2=c(B_1+B_2)^2 \] gives \(Y_o^2-B_o^2=1-X^2\), hence \(X_o=X\). Every child type has \(B_i\le X\); positivity of \(S\) gives \(B_i>-B_j\ge-X\). Consequently \(Y_i^2=1+B_i^2-X^2\le1\). Starting with the root bounds, products and turns therefore give \(X,Y\le1\) at every port. At an original leaf, \(X=\cot\pi a\), so \[ \boxed{\quad 1/4\le a_i(y_*)<1/2.\quad} \tag{1} \] Equality is allowed. It is a regular angle state, even though the two source recurrence roots there have equal modulus. The [quarter packet theorem](actual_conway_quarter_index_color_packet.md) treats that boundary using the actual finite source anchor. ## 3. Gate curvature controls every primitive direction Let \(V(a,b,c)=-\pi[J(a)+J(b)+J(c)]\), \(a+b+c=1\), be the ideal tetrahedron volume. Its Hessian is strictly negative on nonzero tangent vectors of the positive angle simplex. For a strict gate set \(p=z-x\), \(q=z-y\), \(r=x+y-z\), \(w=1-x-y\). The exact identity is \[ \pi m(x,y,z)=V(y,x,w)+V(p,q,2r+w)+V(p+q,r,r+w). \tag{2} \] All three triples are positive and sum to one. If a tangent has zero quadratic form in the first atom, then \(\delta x=\delta y=0\). Zero quadratic form in the second then forces \(\delta z=0\). The third atom has nonpositive Hessian and cannot undo this conclusion. Thus **each strict gate has a negative-definite Hessian in its three wire variables**, including when one input is above one half. For \(H\ge3\), the collection of all retained gate-label maps is injective on the primitive tangent space. To see this, contract the unary turn chains, retaining their affine complements. Every leaf or product output in a nontrivial root subtree occurs at a retained gate. Its variation is therefore zero if all gate variations are zero. The only possible uncovered wire is a root subtree consisting of one leaf and turns; the other subtree is nontrivial, and the root complementary relation sets that leaf variation to zero as well. Both subtrees can be single leaves only when \(H=2\). It follows that the sum of the retained gate Hessians is negative definite on the full primitive space whenever \(H\ge3\). This uses the actual wire graph and its unit closing relation; it does not add a spurious root gate or assume leaf curvature where it has disappeared. ## 4. The all-core majorant has the same unique geometric maximum Put \[ \widetilde g(a)=g(\max(a,1/4)),\qquad \bar g_{\epsilon}(a)= \begin{cases}g(a),&\epsilon=0,\\ \widetilde g(a),&\epsilon=\pm1, \end{cases} \] and define on the original closed polytope \[ \bar A_\epsilon(y)=\sum_i\bar g_{\epsilon_i}(a_i(y))+ \sum_v m(x_v(y),y_v(y),z_v(y)). \tag{3} \] Both leaf functions are concave. The plateau extension is continuously differentiable at \(1/4\), because \(g'(a)=2\log\cot\pi a\) vanishes there. By (1), every leaf has the same value and first derivative at \(y_*\) in (3) as in the complete action. Therefore \(\bar A_\epsilon(y_*)=F_0\) and \(d\bar A_\epsilon(y_*)=0\). Concavity gives \(\bar A_\epsilon\le F_0\) on all of \(P\). For \(H\ge3\), the gate curvature from §3 gives a strictly quadratic local loss. Indeed, in a small compact strict neighborhood the sum of gate terms lies below its tangent by \(c\|y-y_*\|^2\), \(c>0\), and every leaf term lies below its tangent by concavity. The tangent linear terms cancel by stationarity. Thus \[ \bar A_\epsilon(y)\le F_0-c\|y-y_*\|^2 \tag{4} \] there, without differentiating the plateau twice. A second global maximum would give a constant segment to \(y_*\), contradicting (4). Compactness therefore gives a strictly positive gap outside any fixed neighborhood of \(y_*\). For \(H=2\), at least one pure leaf gives the same strictness: after the turns and the strict root relation both original leaf coordinates are one common \(a\), and the majorant is either \(2g(a)\) or \(g(a)+\widetilde g(a)\), uniquely maximized at \(a=1/4\). If both leaves are odd, the majorant is \(2\widetilde g(a)\) and is flat for \(a\le1/4\). This case is excluded from this core theorem. It has two main components: both odd leaves have endpoint pairing \(X\), turns preserve \(X\), and \(X X=I\) closes to two components. Thus every strict two-leaf **knot** pattern has a pure leaf and is included. ## 5. Uniform estimates for the literal complete core sum Fix a small rectangular primitive window \(B\) around \(y_*\), with closure in the strict polytope. In exact finite coordinates its wires are \(r_w=NL_w(k/N)+\delta_w\), with the original integer offsets. Choose \(0<\beta<1/2\) larger than every leaf label on this window. For every physical core color, the global coefficient estimate is \[ |c^{\epsilon}_{N,h,r}|\le \exp N\{\bar g_\epsilon(r/N)+e_N\},\qquad e_N\longrightarrow0, \tag{5} \] uniformly in \(h,r\). The pure case follows from its exact factorial formula and the positive color deficit. The signed case is the collision-safe frozen-block bound, including its terminal source and singular lower endpoint. Gate factorial errors are uniformly \(O(\log N)\). Fixed affine offsets change continuum rates uniformly by \(o(1)\), even at feasible endpoints, by uniform continuity of \(J\) on its closed interval. There are polynomially many states for the fixed tree. Apply the strict compact gap in §4 to (5), then absorb the finitely many \(e_N\)'s and uniform offset errors into half that gap. The contribution of **all core states outside \(B\)** is therefore \[ O\!\left(N^C e^{N(F_0-\gamma)}\right), \tag{6} \] uniformly over the whole physical color cube. This bound concerns an absolute sum of those states; no cancellation or discarded channel is needed to obtain it. For the endpoint comparison, first divide every exact finite wire by \(d=N-1\); its full array then lies in \(P\) exactly. Its \(r/N\) coordinates differ by \(O(1/N)\), and uniform continuity compares the rates at two admissible arrays. No \(J\) is evaluated beyond its closed domain. Shrinking or enlarging the fixed window by \(O(1/N)\) preserves the same positive outside gap. Inside \(B\), the signed recurrence's strict far-color estimate applies for \(r\le\beta N\), including \(r/N=1/4\). Its proof uses a strict spectral interval above \(\max(\beta,1/4)\), which every backward path crosses. Hence if one physical deficit is at least \(\delta N\), for fixed \(\delta>0\), its rate loses a uniform positive amount relative to \(\widetilde g\). For a pure leaf the exact loss is \[ \Delta(a,t)=J(a-t)+J(a+t)-2J(a)>0 \quad(0<t\le a<1/2), \] or the core coefficient is zero when \(h>r\). Compactness of the window and the fixed lower bound on \(t\) give the pure uniform loss too. Together with (6) this proves \[ \max_{\exists i:\,h_i>\delta N} |\mathcal A^{\mathrm{core}}_N(\mathbf h)| \le N^C e^{N(F_0-\gamma_\delta)}. \tag{7} \] Colors outside the core's original support contribute zero, not an uncontrolled analytic continuation. ## 6. The exact local packet and the remaining alias obligation On \(B\), continue only the paired color factorials of the exact finite core coefficients. This gives the finite even holomorphic window \(\mathcal C_N(\boldsymbol\chi)\), after removal of the known unit phase \(\eta_N=\exp(i\pi(N-1)\sum_i\epsilon_i/4)\). By (1), each leaf lies in a high-index neighborhood or in the proved quarter neighborhood. Use the corresponding exponentially accurate **actual-source** index interpolant. Their errors, summed over polynomially many window states, are \(\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F_0+C\|\chi\|^2-c_0)}\), so shrinking the fixed color polydisk makes them negligible before any complex saddle. The interpolated phase is the sum of the selected \(f_{\epsilon_i}\) and the unchanged gate actions. Its complete wire Hessian is invertible. The original finite cotangent rectangles and Gaussian calculation apply in the same primitive coordinates, retaining all offsets and boundary currents. There are \(H\) leaf factors of order \(N^{1/2}\), \(H-2\) gate factors of order \(N^{-3/2}\), and \(K=2H-3\) Gaussian variables. Consequently \[ \mathcal C_N(\chi)=N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(\chi)e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)} (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_\epsilon(0)\ne0. \tag{8} \] All square roots, offsets and chirps are inherited from the source. At completeness the signed/pure amplitude ratio is \(\prod_{\epsilon_i\ne0}\sqrt{\sin\pi a_i}\,e^{-i\epsilon_i\pi a_i/2}\), which is nonzero also at a quarter leaf. Separate evenness gives \[ \partial_i\partial_j\Phi_\epsilon(0)= -\frac{2\pi c_i}{1-\epsilon_i i c_i}\delta_{ij},\qquad c_i=\cot\pi a_i>0. \tag{9} \] In particular its real part is strictly negative, giving a fixed joint complex Gaussian envelope for the exact finite window. Estimates (6)–(8) give the original all-core source comparison in the small physical color corridor and its far-color complement, at both parities and all sufficiently large levels. The actual source is \(\mathcal A_N=\mathcal A_N^{\mathrm{core}}+\mathcal A_N^{\mathrm{alias}}\), where the second term is the sum of all nonempty alias sectors with their original signs. Thus for every strict knot pattern the missing global source input has been reduced to \[ \sup_{\text{all physical colors}} |\mathcal A_N^{\mathrm{alias}}(\mathbf h)| \le N^C e^{N(F_0-\gamma)} \tag{10} \] for some fixed \(\gamma>0\), or to an equally sufficient estimate after the exact filling pairing. A separate bound for every sector is sufficient but not logically necessary. Pointwise positive alias envelopes can fail to prove (10); their failure is not a lower bound on the actual alias. Once (10) is proved for a class, the [general marked-mask construction](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) identifies \(U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i\), \(V_i=-2\partial_i\Phi_\epsilon\), and the original primitive filling action with the actual knot complement volume. The proved entire Fourier–Hermite filling transfer then gives the full original-invariant volume limit for independently long fixed signed twists. This is a reduction of the remaining conjectural step, not an assertion that (10) holds for every strict tree. ## scope This argument concerns the literal all-core source for strict knot patterns. A gap for every nonempty alias sector is a separate requirement. For the root-star family, the [full-jet localization](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md) and [root-character Fourier contraction](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md) supply the additional alias estimate. Arbitrary turned children still require that separate global argument. The published completed-root manuscript is unchanged by these companion research notes.

title: Actual marked deformation and smooth filling for every strict Conway mask tree
text: # Actual marked deformation and smooth filling for every strict Conway mask tree 31 October 2026. geometric and local-source theorem. This extends the [general strict-mask complete geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) to the original pure/odd face pairings, primitive peripheral paths and absolute filled-volume calibration. Every complete leaf is at or above the quarter index, so the proved high and quarter packet constructions cover the entire fixed tree. The [general core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) controls the all-core sector for every strict knot pattern. A global nonempty-alias estimate remains separate. No enlarged full-invariant limit is inferred from geometry or the local packet alone. ## 1. Scope and complete port data Take a fixed literal expression \(C(FG)\) in leaves \(h\), ordered products and actual turns \(T\). Delete only its forced final product, whose coefficient is one, retaining its original complementary-wire relation. Assume the reduced positive wire polytope has a strict state: \[ 0<a_i<\frac12,\qquad \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1 \tag{1} \] for every leaf and retained gate. The positive action has a unique strict optimizer with negative-definite reduced wire Hessian. The complete geometry theorem constructs its actual two-ball right-angled augmented link exterior. It retains every original shaded triangle, ideal vertex and oriented ribbon path; no two corners of one leaf become transitively identified, and every edge cycle has four distinct occurrences. The [exact compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) assigns each open expression a strict type \(L=(0,1/2)\), \(H=(1/2,1)\), \(A=(0,1)\), or empty. The nonempty product rules, including reversed orders, are \[ LL,LA,AA\longmapsto A,\qquad HL,HA\longmapsto H; \qquad HH\longmapsto\varnothing. \tag{2} \] Turns exchange \(L,H\) and preserve \(A\). The strict cylindrical root pairs are \(AA,AL,AH,LH\), in either order. For an optimized port of output \(b\), set \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\quad \kappa=e^{-f_E'(b)},\quad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\quad Y^2=\kappa X^2,\quad X,Y>0. \] Then \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\), and the exact port types are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} L&(B,X,Y)=(B,B,1),\quad B>0\\ H&(B,X,Y)=(-Y,1,Y),\quad Y>0\\ A&-Y<B<X. \end{array} \tag{3} \] A turn maps \((B,X,Y)\) to \((-B,Y,X)\). At a strict product the children have common \(X\); with \(S=B_1+B_2>0\), \[ B_o=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{S},\qquad Y_o=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{S}. \tag{4} \] Number the port edges cyclically. FREE edges are \(0,2\). Let \(\eta_j=1\) precisely when the adjacent nonport face is SHADED. Its dihedral angles divided by \(\pi\) are \[ \theta_j=\begin{cases} b-\eta_j/2,&j=0,2,\\ 1-b-\eta_j/2,&j=1,3. \end{cases} \tag{5} \] An \(L\) mask is supported only on CAP edges, an \(H\) mask only on FREE edges, and an \(A\) mask vanishes. The leaf mask is \((0,1,0,1)\). A turn rotates it; a product has mask \((\eta^F_0,0,\eta^G_2,0)\). Its shared child FREE edge has angle \(1-(\eta^F_2+\eta^G_0)/2\), and those two bits cannot both be one at a strict product. Root complementary types likewise forbid two shaded bits on a closing seam. These are individual edge statements; the asymmetric \(H\) pattern must not be replaced by a pair-symmetric one. ## 2. A general quarter-index theorem **Proposition.** At the complete optimizer of every strict closed tree, every port has \(X,Y\le1\). Consequently \[ \boxed{\frac14\le a_i<\frac12\quad\text{for every original leaf}.} \tag{6} \] At the root, complementarity gives opposite \(B\)'s and equal ordered metrics, hence common \(X,Y\). In type \(AA\), \(|B|<\min(X,Y)\), so \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\) gives \(X,Y<1\). In \(AL\), the \(L\) port has \(X=B,Y=1\); the other port has \(B_A=-X>-1\), hence \(X<1\). In \(AH\), the \(H\) port has \(X=1\), while the \(A\) inequality gives \(Y<1\). In \(LH\), the explicit forms force \(X=Y=1\). For the downward step put \(c=1-X^2\). The identity \[ (B_1^2+c)(B_2^2+c)-(B_1B_2-c)^2=c(B_1+B_2)^2 \] gives \(Y_o^2-B_o^2=1-X^2\), so positivity implies \(X_o=X\). Every child type has \(B_i\le X\), and \(S>0\) gives \(B_i>-B_j\ge-X\). Thus \[ Y_i^2=1+B_i^2-X^2\le1. \] Products propagate the bounds to both children, and turns swap them. At a leaf \(X=\cot(\pi a)>0\), proving (6). Equality is genuine. For \(C(hT(h^s))\), the unturned \(h^s\) port is \((1/s,1,1/s)\), its turn is \((-1/s,1/s,1)\), and the root leaf port is \((1/s,1/s,1)\). The seed leaves have \(a=1/4\), the root leaf has \(a=\arctan(s)/\pi\), and all retained gates are strict. At a quarter leaf the source recurrence roots are \(+i,-i\): this is an equal-modulus boundary, not an eigenvalue collision. No strict quarter inequality is asserted for the enlarged syntax. ## 3. The selected source action and regular deformed charts Keep each physical sign \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) in its original leaf frame. On the continued complete branch define \[ \begin{aligned} J(s)&=\int_0^s\operatorname{Log}(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\\ g(x,t)&=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t),\\ v&=g_t=\operatorname{Log}\frac{\sin\pi(x-t)}{\sin\pi(x+t)},\\ \chi&=t-\frac{\epsilon v}{2\pi i},\qquad f_\epsilon(x,\chi)=g(x,t)-\frac{\epsilon v^2}{4\pi i}. \end{aligned} \tag{7} \] The implicit derivative at completeness is \(1-\epsilon i\cot(\pi x)\ne0\). Thus (7) is a unique holomorphic germ, even in \(\chi\), and exactly \[ df_\epsilon=g_x\,dx+v\,d\chi. \tag{8} \] The [high-index source identity](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md), §2, and the [quarter packet theorem](actual_conway_quarter_index_color_packet.md) identify this same branch with the actual continued finite source, including its original chirp. Proposition (6) covers every leaf of a fixed strict tree. No continuation into arbitrary low complete indices is being assumed. For precision, the negative-source action and (7) have the same branch of the algebraic equation \[ K^2(1+E)^2+K[(H+H^{-1})E^2+2]+(1-E)^2=0, \quad E=e^{2\pi ix},\ H=e^{2\pi i\chi},\ K=e^{-f_x}, \tag{9} \] selected by \(K=\tan^2(\pi x)\) at \(H=1\). The constant is fixed at \(x=1/2\) for fixed small \(\chi\): then \(v=0\), \(t=\chi\), and \(g(1/2,t)=0\) by \(J(1/2+t)=-J(1/2-t)\). The selected source integral \(\int_x^{1/2}\operatorname{Log}\mu(u,\chi)\,du\) tends to zero with regular \(\mu(1/2,\chi)=1\). The hidden \(t\) does not tend to zero. Schwarz reflection gives the positive sign. In the original reduced free wires \(y\), set \[ \mathcal A_\epsilon(y,\chi)= \sum_i f_{\epsilon_i}(a_i(y),\chi_i)+\sum_{\text{retained gates}}m. \tag{10} \] At zero color this is the complete positive action. Its invertible wire Hessian gives a unique holomorphic critical branch \(y_*(\chi)\); write \(\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)=\mathcal A_\epsilon(y_*(\chi),\chi)\). By (8), wire stationarity is exactly the original ordered metric matching, evaluated at the hidden pure colors. Turns and the root complementary relation are unchanged. All finitely many complete flags and three-point charts are nondegenerate, so remain regular on one small polydisk. The second-copy charts are holomorphic: invert the prism angle phases, without conjugating free source variables. Normalize a leaf port to \((0,\infty,1,R)\), put \(T=e^{2\pi it}\), and select \[ Z=\frac{1+E}{1+T},\qquad R=\frac{T(1+E)^2}{E(1+T)^2},\qquad Z^2-(1+E)Z+ER=0. \tag{11} \] The projection apices are \(Z,Z/E\). This is the original reflected-minus convention, including when deformed white pieces are not planar. ## 4. Actual and virtual white maps for every mask Use the universal matrices \[ \begin{aligned} W_0&=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&E\end{pmatrix},& W_1&=\begin{pmatrix}1&E-1\\0&E\end{pmatrix},\\ W_2&=\begin{pmatrix}E-R&R(1-E)\\E-1&1-ER\end{pmatrix},& W_3&=\begin{pmatrix}R&0\\1-E&ER\end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned} \tag{12} \] Each fixes the endpoints of its port edge. The strengthened invariant is: - If \(\eta_j=0\), \(W_j\) is the actual transition on the adjacent WHITE piece to the other projection copy. - If \(\eta_j=1\), \(W_j\) is a virtual WHITE completion map, not a map assigned to the actual SHADED face. It prescribes the transition that must lie across the surviving shaded edge after gluing. - Every already internal shaded edge has its actual adjacent WHITE map equal to this completion map in the original leaf frame. WHITE pieces already joined carry the same entire Möbius map, including translation. At a leaf, \(W_0,W_2\) are actual WHITE maps, sending \(Z\) to \(Z/E\) by (11). The matrices \(W_1,W_3\) are virtual completions at its shaded CAP bases. No fictitious white face is inserted. In the original world charts, the [generic prism identities](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md), §3, are \[ \begin{aligned} W_{F,1}=W_{G,1}=W_{o,1}&=B_{\mathrm{top}},\\ W_{F,3}=W_{G,3}=W_{o,3}&=B_{\mathrm{bottom}},\\ W_{F,2}&=W_{G,0},\\ W_{o,0}=W_{F,0},\qquad W_{o,2}&=W_{G,2}. \end{aligned} \tag{13} \] Here the two \(B\)'s are actual WHITE prism triangle maps. These are rational identities in independent prism phases, valid also above a half-index wire label. They use the original ordered maps \[ F:C\mapsto(v_0,v_1,P,\infty),\qquad G:C\mapsto(\infty,P,v_2,v_3). \] They are not modulus-only identities or reflected substitutions. There are exactly three seam checks. 1. At a child CAP seam the prism side is WHITE. A zero bit identifies two actual white maps across a flat seam by (13). A nonzero bit preserves the shaded triangle and supplies its actual completion from the prism map. 2. At the shared FREE edge the bits are \((0,0),(1,0)\), or \((0,1)\). In the first case actual WHITE pieces merge by \(W_{F,2}=W_{G,0}\). In the other two, the unmasked child's actual map supplies the masked child's completion. The edge stays right angled. The forbidden \((1,1)\) case would be a strict \(HH\) product. 3. The remaining output FREE maps inherit their status through the last line of (13); the two output CAP maps are actual prism WHITE maps. This is precisely the mask \((\eta^F_0,0,\eta^G_2,0)\). The turn and closing identities are \[ \begin{aligned} T_Q(z)&=\frac{R-1}{z-1},& T_QW_{j+1}(E,R)&=W_j(E^{-1},1-R)T_Q,\\ C_Q(z)&=\frac{z-R}{z-1},& C_QW_j(E^{-1},R)&=W_{2-j}(E,R)C_Q. \end{aligned} \tag{14} \] A turn rotates the mask and transports actual/virtual status unchanged. At the root, the complementary-type rule excludes two shaded bits on a paired edge. Zero/zero pairs merge actual WHITE pieces; one/zero pairs supply the required completion from the actual white side. No port remains, so every original shaded base now has its required actual adjacent WHITE map. This proves the invariant without a pair-symmetric \(H\) pattern, without restricting internal wire labels below \(1/2\), and without using a virtual map as a premature face pairing. It includes turned bare leaves and all strict root-leaf closures. Every triangular piece in one original WHITE face has one entire common transition, even if its deformed image is not planar. The original abstract face-paired balls, rather than deformed embeddedness, determine the representation. ## 5. Original shaded words and the actual group In each original leaf frame retain \[ S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-ER\\1&-1-E\end{pmatrix},\quad A=\begin{pmatrix}R&-R\\1&ER-1-E\end{pmatrix},\quad B=\begin{pmatrix}R/E-1-1/E&R\\-1&R\end{pmatrix}. \tag{15} \] The pure map \(S\) pairs within one copy. The odd maps \(A,B\) pair \((Z,\infty,1)\) with \((Z/E,R,0)\), and \((Z,R,0)\) with \((Z/E,\infty,1)\). At completeness these are the original half-disk rotations. Every half-twist pattern therefore has the same complete metric: the four edge occurrences remain distinct, changing the copy permutation does not collapse original corners, and the canonical length-one shaded decorations are preserved. With \(\bar S\) denoting \(E\mapsto E^{-1}\), the pure relations are \[ W_0S=\bar S W_0,\qquad W_2S=\bar S W_2,\qquad W_3S=\bar S W_1. \tag{16} \] The odd relations are \[ W_0^{-1}BW_2^{-1}A=I,\qquad W_2^{-1}BW_0^{-1}A=I,\qquad W_1^{-1}BW_3^{-1}A=I. \tag{17} \] These hold for independent nearby \(E,R\), pointwise, including translations and dilations. Section 4 makes every \(W\) in the base words an actual final white transition for arbitrary masks. The [original closed cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) supplies two actual topological balls. Their dual two-skeleton has face transitions as generators and original edge words as relations. The WHITE seams and all shaded relations have been verified. Hence these maps define an actual holomorphic framed representation \(\rho_\chi\) of the original signed augmented-link group near its oriented complete holonomy. Products and turns conjugate the original leaf data into world coordinates; they neither replace a physical leaf by a scalar coupon nor change its integral disk curves. At a main corner the two final original WHITE sectors have maps \(W_{j-1},W_j\), one possibly supplied as a completion. The actual small main meridian is \(W_{j-1}^{-1}W_j\), or its inverse. Their derivatives at the common corner are equal: \(E^{-1}\) at \(C_0,C_2\), \(E\) at \(C_1,C_3\), in finite local coordinates. Its multiplier is identically one. It stays nonidentity near completeness and is therefore parabolic. Its peripheral commutant consists of translations. All main cusp groups remain parabolic, whatever their number of components. ## 6. Primitive auxiliary curves and the absolute action The auxiliary collar remains in its original leaf box. Its two shaded triangles and apex are untouched by port attachments. The original primitive disk curves therefore persist through turns and closures; world-coordinate transport conjugates their whole words. Put \[ \rho=\frac{Z}{1+E-Z},\qquad Q=\frac{E-Z}{Z-1}. \] The disk longitude is \(W_2^{-1}W_0\), with flag-at-infinity multiplier \(Q^2\). The pure meridian \(S^{-1}\) has multiplier \(\rho\). The odd primitive meridians \(A^{-1}W_0\), \(W_0^{-1}B\) have multipliers \(\rho Q\), \(\rho/Q\). Their complete translations are \(-2\) and \(2E\); the longitude translates by \(-2(E+1)\). The two-rectangle lattice proves primitivity. The [original threading calculation](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md), §§4–5, fixes the sign: the typed loop \([2,1,1,2]\) followed by \(R^{-1}\) has actual auxiliary matrix \(I-(P+I)/(1+E)\), \(\operatorname{Tr}P=-2\), preferred projective longitude \(-P\), and translation ratio \(1+E\). Thus the physical \(R^{-1}\) coupon uses the first odd path and \(R\) the second. This is local to the original leaf frame; a port turn does not rename its physical sign. Using (11), \(\rho=e^{-2\pi it}\), \(Q=e^{-v}\). The actual centered similarity logs are \[ U_i=-2\pi it_i-\frac{\epsilon_iV_i}{2}=-2\pi i\chi_i, \qquad V_i=-2v_i=-2\partial_i\Phi_\epsilon. \tag{18} \] They are squared-eigenvalue logs; the original lift and pivot characters are retained in the finite source. The half-longitude shear compares actual primitive bases, not an integral half-longitude curve or an ordinary rational filling of the pure partner. With \(G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon\), on the same connected marked family, \[ dG=\frac12\sum_iV_i\,dU_i,\qquad G_\epsilon-G_{\mathrm{pure}}=-\sum_i\frac{\epsilon_iV_i^2}{8}, \qquad \Im G(0)=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon)=2\pi\Phi_\epsilon(0). \tag{19} \] The comparison uses the hidden pure colors and stationary wires. The original ideal-chain Bloch differential cancels internal faces and keeps each primitive torus's \(-2\) eigenlog wedge. Thus \[ d\operatorname{Vol}(\rho)=\frac12\sum_i (\Re V_i\,d\Im U_i-\Re U_i\,d\Im V_i). \] The complete degree-one anchor fixes the constant, giving \[ \operatorname{Vol}(\rho_\chi)=\Im G(\chi) -\frac12\sum_i\Re U_i\Im V_i. \tag{20} \] This is the actual original fundamental class, not an unrelated Bloch cycle with the same differential. Known real Cartan constants remain recorded. The complete imaginary normalization is geometric. ## 7. Smooth actual fillings and knot pairing Evenness makes all mixed wire/color first derivatives vanish at zero. There is no wire Schur correction to the color Hessian. With \(c_i=\cot(\pi a_i)>0\), \[ \partial_i\partial_j\Phi_\epsilon(0) =-\frac{2\pi c_i}{1-\epsilon_i i c_i}\delta_{ij} =2\pi i\tau_i\delta_{ij},\qquad \tau_i=\frac{ic_i}{1-\epsilon_i i c_i},\quad \Im\tau_i>0. \tag{21} \] Choose any auxiliary subset to fill and set \(\chi_i=0\) elsewhere. Separate evenness gives \(V_i=0\) at the unfilled auxiliary cusps, so they remain parabolic. For independently signed integers \(p_i\), the actual primitive equations are \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i. \tag{22} \] Writing \(r_i=1/p_i\), their Jacobian in \(\chi\) at \(r=0\) is \(-4\pi i\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)\), invertible by (21). The implicit-function theorem supplies the selected solution in one fixed reciprocal-slope polydisk, without slope-comparability conditions. Apply the [proved framed completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md), also proved in [Appendix D](../manuscript/sections/D-marked-cell-calibration.tex), §4. Its hypotheses are now all supplied: an actual nearby representation, actual fixed flags, primitive small logs and parabolic unfilled cusps. Its core/cusp development proves the actual log-link periods before multiplying by the slopes, and completes each punctured tube by one angular turn. The result is a smooth complete finite-volume metric on the original disk-filled topology. The physical power is \(R^{\epsilon_i-2p_i}\), once; a knot cusp is never filled. At the saddle, (20) becomes \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon(\mathbf p)) =2\pi\Re\left[ \Phi_\epsilon(\chi_*)+\frac{\pi i}{2} \sum_{i\,\mathrm{filled}}\frac{(\chi_i-1)^2}{p_i}\right]. \tag{23} \] This geometric theorem is unconditional for each fixed strict syntax and sign pattern. If all auxiliaries are filled and the literal main pairing has one component, it is the volume of the resulting **knot complement**. No isotopy to a completed-root expression is asserted. Such a one-component choice exists. For cyclic terminals write \(I=(03)(12)\), \(U=(01)(23)\), \(X=(02)(13)\). A leaf offers \(\{U,X\}\); turn exchanges \(I,U\) and fixes \(X\). The product table is | Lower / upper | \(I\) | \(U\) | \(X\) | |---|---|---|---| | \(I\) | \(I\) | \(U\) | \(X\) | | \(U\) | \(U\) | \(U\) plus an internal loop | \(U\) | | \(X\) | \(X\) | \(U\) | \(I\) | Only \(U\cdot U\) is forbidden. For sets \(A=\{I,U\}\), \(B=\{I,X\}\), \(C=\{U,X\}\), the allowed output sets of \(AA,AB,AC,BB,BC,CC\) are respectively \(A,\{I,U,X\},C,B,\{I,U,X\},A\), also in reversed order. Thus every node retains at least two loop-free choices. At the root one of \(U,X\) closes to one main component. Full twists preserve that endpoint permutation. This is a finite pairing proof, not an invariant limit argument. ## 8. The exact local packet and the remaining source obligation The [general core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) gives the complete analytic details; we record why they apply to this actual masked deformation. With \(H\) leaves, there are \(H\) leaf indices and \(H-2\) retained gate-output indices before the final unit relation. Eliminating that relation leaves the primitive lattice \(\mathbb Z^K\), \(K=2H-3\), including a bare or turned root leaf. Turns are the literal integer map \(r\mapsto d-r\), \(d=N-1\). In primitive coordinates each exact wire is \(r_w=NL_w(k/N)+\delta_w\), with its original fixed integer offset. Choose a small fixed rectangular window \(B\) around the strict complete optimizer. Every gate is strict there. By (6), shrink it inside either a high-index or the proved quarter neighborhood for each leaf. Let \(\ell_N^\epsilon\) be its exact finite continued-color core coefficient, after extracting only the known constant unit chirp. The exact window is \[ \mathcal C_N(\chi)=\sum_{k/N\in B} \prod_i\ell_N^{\epsilon_i}(r_i,\chi_i) \prod_g\mu_N(r_{g1},r_{g2},r_{g3}). \tag{24} \] Its support is fixed before complex colors, and it is finite, separately even and holomorphic on a fixed small color polydisk. The gates are the exact seven-factorial Newton coefficients; every physical small-color entry retains the original normal directions. Use the specified high or quarter holomorphic index interpolant at each leaf and the canonical factorial interpolant at each gate. Before any oscillatory sum, the total grid residual is bounded by \[ \operatorname{poly}(N)\exp N(F_0+C\|\chi\|^2-c),\qquad c>0. \] There are polynomially many states, and the even color perturbation is uniformly quadratic. Shrink the fixed color disk to put this residual strictly below the nearby critical action. The interpolated summand has phase (10), leading power \(N^{3-H}\), and nonzero holomorphic density. Indeed each of the \(H\) leaves contributes \(N^{1/2}\), and each of \(H-2\) gates contributes \(N^{-3/2}\). Its density includes exactly \[ \exp\left[ \sum_i\delta_i\partial_x f_{\epsilon_i} +\sum_g\nabla m\cdot\delta_g\right], \] using the changed signed action at nonzero color. Apply the finite half-grid cotangent rectangles in the primitive coordinates. The strict local maximum gives a gap on side faces. On horizontal contours of small height \(a\), nonconstant kernel terms lose \(e^{-2\pi aN}\), while the analytic phase costs at most \(e^{N(Ca^2+C\|\chi\|^2)}\). Choose height first and color disk second. The constant term supplies \(N^K\) times the finite integral. Shift to the nearby critical contour and apply its nondegenerate Gaussian, which supplies \(N^{-K/2}\). All contours stay in the common fixed interpolation domains; all joining pieces are retained and exponentially smaller.
