Since \(3-H+K/2=3/2\), adding the grid residual back only now gives \[ \mathcal C_N(\chi)=N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(\chi)e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)} (1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_\epsilon(0)\ne0. \tag{25} \] The extracted \(\eta_N\) multiplies both sides in the original source. The density, original offset exponential and determinant branch are nonzero at completeness. Both parities have the same primitive density. Evenness gives the Hessian (21) without a wire Schur correction and the usual fixed complex Gaussian envelope for this exact finite window. For completeness, the all-core gap for \(H\ge3\) follows from gate curvature even when leaf curvature is lost on a plateau. Put \(p=z-x,q=z-y,r=x+y-z,w=1-x-y\). The exact three-atom identity is \[ \pi m=V(y,x,w)+V(p,q,1-p-q)+V(p+q,r,r+w). \tag{26} \] Each positive tetrahedral angle Hessian is negative definite on its simplex. The first atom pins \(\delta x,\delta y\); the second then pins \(\delta z\). The third is concave. Hence each strict gate is negative definite in its three wires. Their combined label map has zero kernel on the primitive tangent space: every leaf/output wire meets a retained gate, except possibly one root leaf pinned by the complementary root relation. Thus their total Hessian is negative definite for \(H\ge3\). Use \(g\) for pure leaves and \(\widetilde g(a)=g(\max(a,1/4))\) for signed cores. These are concave and have the same complete values and first derivatives as \(g\), by (6). The complete stationary point is therefore the global maximum of the core majorant. Gate curvature makes it a strict local maximum; a second global maximum would force a constant segment into that neighborhood. Compactness gives the global state gap. The uniform closed coefficient upper estimate absorbs its \(o(N)\) error; the compact window has every leaf below some \(\beta<1/2\), so the collision-safe recurrence also gives the strict far-color loss. The [core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) retains the original finite targets and endpoint normalization in these estimates. For \(H=2\), one pure leaf supplies the strict \(g+\widetilde g\) or \(2g\) maximum. Both odd leaves instead give the flat majorant \(2\widetilde g\) on \([0,1/4]\), although the actual complete action \(2g\) has unique quarter maximum. This is an exception to this core argument for that **link**, not a knot pattern: turns fix both odd pairings \(X\), and \(X\cdot X=I\) closes to two main components. It is not a counterexample to a sharper full-source estimate. For every strict knot pattern, the remaining global input is therefore a bound on the sum of nonempty alias sectors, with their original signs, or an equally sufficient bound after the exact filling pairing. The [whole-source transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) then identifies (23) with the original invariant's full-sequence rate, retaining the original currents, charges, parity and nonzero coefficient. No general alias bound follows from port rigidity, the masked geometry, or the all-core result. No theorem for all arborescent knots is claimed.

title: Actual complete geometry for all strict Conway source trees
text: # Actual complete geometry for all strict Conway source trees 31 October 2026. complete-geometry theorem. This note extends the original ideal-cell construction to every literal \(h/T/\mathrm{product}\) expression with a strict reduced cylindrical state. Four individual edge masks replace the insufficient pair-symmetric port pattern. The proof retains the actual colored boundary, terminal identifications, reversible link cut and cusp cycles. The conclusion concerns the complete augmented-link complement and its original positive source. It is not a signed-source or long-filling theorem for the enlarged syntax. ## 1. Statement and the strengthened induction invariant Let \(F,G\) be arbitrary finite expressions in the original leaf \(h\), literal ordered turn \(T\), and ordered product. Require the original reduced wire polytope of \(C(FG)\), after deleting only its forced final gate, to have a strict state: all leaf labels belong to \((0,1/2)\), and every retained product obeys \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. \tag{1} \] The [exact strict-output compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), §2, assigns each open expression one of the types \[ L=(0,1/2),\qquad H=(1/2,1),\qquad A=(0,1),\qquad\varnothing. \] Here \(h\) has type \(L\); \(T\) exchanges \(L,H\) and fixes \(A\); the product table is \[ LL,LA,AA\longmapsto A,\qquad HL,HA\longmapsto H,\qquad HH\longmapsto\varnothing, \tag{2} \] with reversed input orders included. An empty type remains empty. Every stated interval is actually attained. Thus the strict cylindrical root pairs are \(AA,AL,AH,LH\), in either order; \(LL\) and \(HH\) fail. The two children need not belong to the earlier completed grammar. **Theorem.** The unique complete positive optimizer builds an actual convex ideal right-angled polyhedron with the original colored bowtie ribbon boundary. Its two projection copies, with the original labeled face pairings, give the actual complete finite-volume augmented-link complement. All auxiliary components are retained, and the volume is twice the sum of the retained source-cell volumes. The open-cell induction keeps more than its angles: 1. An actual three-dimensional convex ideal polyhedron has a supported, nondegenerate quadrilateral output \(Q=(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)\). 2. Each original leaf retains its two distinct shaded ideal triangles. Its apex and four corners remain distinct; those two triangles meet only at their original apex. 3. Every nonport edge is right angled and separates WHITE from SHADED. Each port edge has one adjacent nonport face, recorded individually. 4. Each port corner is an active original terminal singleton. A consumed terminal pair and an auxiliary apex never occur on a later port. 5. Each active corner carries one original shaded sector; an internal main vertex carries the two sectors of its paired terminals in their original ribbon order. These statements, including vertex identifications and cyclic orders, are proved below. ## 2. Exact type data, stationary cells and individual edge masks The strict-state construction and original nonvertex-flat boundary barrier apply on each actual open type interval. The retained angle maps recover all wires, so the optimizer is unique and strict with negative definite reduced Hessian. Its profile \(f_E(b)\) is analytic there. The [original derivative identities](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) give the entire ordered-face isometry condition \[ \kappa_{\mathrm{child}}\kappa_{\mathrm{prism\ input}}=1. \] They are used on the actual source-selected branch. For clarity, the exact port and profile information extends to all nonempty types. Put \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\qquad \kappa=e^{-f_E'(b)},\qquad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\qquad Y^2=\kappa X^2, \qquad X,Y>0. \] Then \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\), a turn sends \((B,X,Y)\) to \((-B,Y,X)\), and strict stationary products have common \(X\) with \[ B_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{B_FB_G+X^2-1}{B_F+B_G}, \qquad Y_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{Y_FY_G}{B_F+B_G}, \qquad B_F+B_G>0. \tag{3} \] Induction proves \[ \begin{array}{c|c} L&(B,X,Y)=(B,B,1),\quad B>0\\ H&(B,X,Y)=(-Y,1,Y),\quad Y>0\\ A&-Y<B<X. \end{array} \tag{4} \] The leaf and turn cases are immediate. The \(LL,LA,AA\) cases are the same exact port preservation calculations as in the [single-leaf geometry theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_geometric_composition.md), §2. In an \(HA\) product common \(X=1\), and the \(A\) input has \(B_A>0\), \(Y_A=B_A\). Writing the \(H\) input as \((-u,1,u)\), strict support gives \(B_A-u>0\), and (3) yields \[ B_{\mathrm{out}}=-\frac{uB_A}{B_A-u} =-Y_{\mathrm{out}}. \] For \(HL\), the \(L\) input at \(X=1\) is \((1,1,1)\), giving the same calculation. This proves every case of (4). Since the leaf derivative is \(g'(b)=2\log\cot(\pi b)\), (4) also gives absolute constants \(c_E\) with \[ f_E(b)=g(b)+c_E\quad(E:L),\qquad f_E(b)=g(1-b)+c_E\quad(E:H). \tag{5} \] These are optimized classical profile identities on the whole connected strict interval, extending continuously to its feasible endpoints. They are not finite quantum scalar factorizations or tangle isotopies. No such factorization is used here. The geometric pattern requires finer data than (4). Number the output edges \(j=0,1,2,3\) cyclically; edges \(0,2\) are FREE. Let \(\eta_j=1\) when the adjacent nonport face is SHADED and \(\eta_j=0\) when it is WHITE. The actual dihedral angles, divided by \(\pi\), are \[ \theta_j= \begin{cases} b-\eta_j/2,&j=0,2,\\ 1-b-\eta_j/2,&j=1,3. \end{cases} \tag{6} \] The mask supports satisfy \[ L:\ \eta_0=\eta_2=0,\qquad H:\ \eta_1=\eta_3=0,\qquad A:\ \eta_j=0\ \text{for all }j. \tag{7} \] Only these support inclusions are asserted: an \(L\) or \(H\) mask can have one nonzero bit or none. The bare leaf is the explicit ideal pyramid, with mask \((0,1,0,1)\). Its four other edges are right, and its shaded triangles are \((O,C_1,C_2)\) and \((O,C_3,C_0)\). Each output corner carries one shaded sector. A literal turn rotates the port and mask once and changes \(b\) to \(1-b\). It changes no face or vertex identification. It exchanges the \(L/H\) support conditions and preserves the \(A\) condition. At a product use the [original ordered prism maps](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md): \[ \begin{aligned} F:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)&\longmapsto(v_0,v_1,P,\infty),\\ G:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)&\longmapsto(\infty,P,v_2,v_3). \end{aligned} \tag{8} \] The prism triangles are WHITE. Write \(p=z-x\), \(q=z-y\), \(w=1-x-y\). All cells are strictly three-dimensional. The output mask is exactly \[ \eta^{\mathrm{out}} =(\eta^F_0,\,0,\,\eta^G_2,\,0). \tag{9} \] A child CAP seam has angle \(1-\eta_j/2\). A zero bit gives flat WHITE/WHITE merging; a nonzero bit gives a right SHADED/WHITE edge. The shared input edge \(P\infty\) has total angle \[ w+\left(x-\frac{\eta^F_2}{2}\right) +\left(y-\frac{\eta^G_0}{2}\right) =1-\frac{\eta^F_2+\eta^G_0}{2}. \tag{10} \] Both bits could be one only for \(HH\), which has no strict state. Thus this edge is also flat WHITE/WHITE or right SHADED/WHITE. The output FREE angles are \(p+x-\eta^F_0/2\) and \(q+y-\eta^G_2/2\); the CAP angles remain \(1-z\). These are (6) and (9). The type table verifies (7) in every case. This refinement is necessary. A basic \(H\) lower child and an \(L\) or \(A\) upper child produce FREE angles \(z-1/2\) and \(z\). They are unequal; a pair-symmetric \(H\) angle pattern would be false. All port angles in (6) lie strictly between zero and one on their actual type intervals. The first attachment is locally convex before the second: its two FREE seam angles are \(z-\eta^F_0/2\) and \(1-y-\eta^F_2/2\). A nonzero first bit forces \(x>1/2\), hence \(z>1/2\); a nonzero second bit forces \(x>1/2\), hence \(y<1/2\). These angles are positive and at most one. The CAP seams have already been checked. Equation (10) completes the second-attachment check. ## 3. Convexity, ideal coincidences and all port corners Position two convex ideal cells on opposite sides of their matching supported face. In hyperbolic space their intersection is exactly that face. The finite union is closed, connected and locally convex at every finite boundary point by the preceding angles. Any two finite points have a shortest path in the union: a length-bounded minimizing sequence stays in a compact ambient ball, and constant-speed compactness gives a limit. Local convexity makes it an ambient geodesic locally, hence the unique whole geodesic segment. The union is convex. This is the [original supported-face proof](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), applied to the refined angles. The output remains a genuine supported quadrilateral. Its four edge angles are strictly positive and nonflat, so no other boundary piece extends its supporting face through an output edge. This also excludes accidental ideal coincidences, which an argument inside hyperbolic space alone would miss. Cells on opposite supporting sides can have common ideal points only on the ideal circle of the support plane. A cell has no ideal vertex on that circle other than its matching quadrilateral's corners: an additional vertex would enlarge the supporting face past a quadrilateral edge, contradicting its strict supporting angle. The ideal closure of the quadrilateral itself has only its four ideal vertices. Therefore only the prescribed face-corner identifications occur. This applies to the first attachment and to the second; its remaining input face stays supported and nondegenerate. Every shaded triangle remains an entire unchanged face. It is never an attaching port. Its seams are always right, never flat, by the CAP rule and (9)–(10). Only WHITE pieces merge. No shaded edge is deleted, subdivided or merged into another shaded face. No leaf apex is ever on an attaching port, so it stays a separate ideal vertex with its four original right edges and two shaded sectors. The output-corner patterns are explicit. At \(C_j\), the adjacent bits \(\eta_{j-1},\eta_j\) have sum at most one by (7). The two port-edge angles sum to \(1-(\eta_{j-1}+\eta_j)/2\); every other angle is right. The Euclidean ideal-link angle sum gives \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \eta_{j-1}+\eta_j&\text{valence}&\text{cyclic faces}\\ 0&4&\mathrm{PORT,WHITE,SHADED,WHITE}\\ 1&3&\mathrm{PORT,WHITE,SHADED} \ \text{in the recorded cyclic order}. \end{array} \tag{11} \] Each exposed corner has one original shaded sector. Under (8), an output corner inherits one child terminal; only the two internal interface corners combine terminals. A turn rotates their sectors. This proves the full corner invariant, including the asymmetric cases. ## 4. Exact terminal accounting: no transitive corner collapse Give each leaf the four original symbols \((i,0),(i,1),(i,2),(i,3)\). An open expression has exactly four active singleton symbols in its ordered port. All other terminals are partitioned into disjoint two-element pairs. A paired symbol is permanently consumed: its vertex is internal and never appears on a later attaching or output port. Apices \(O_i\) are separate symbols and never enter this matching. This holds for a leaf. A turn permutes the active singletons. For a product of disjoint child trees, (8) consumes exactly \[ F_2\sim G_1,\qquad F_3\sim G_0, \] and leaves \(F_0,F_1,G_2,G_3\) active. It never acts on a previously consumed pair. Each new pair contains terminals from different child leaf sets. Thus there are no chains of pair equalities and no classes with more than two terminals. The six prism vertices implement exactly these identifications; their fresh names create no additional relation among old internal vertices. Section 3 excludes extra geometric identifications. For \(C(FG)\), either retain these two root interface pairs and close the remaining four singletons, or delete the forced root prism and use the entire original closing map \[ F:C_j\longmapsto G:C_{3-j}. \tag{12} \] This forms all four pairs between the distinct root-child leaf sets. Both descriptions give the same matching. Every original terminal is used once in one pair; no pair contains two terminals of one leaf. Consequently every leaf has four distinct main corner vertices after closure. Its two original shaded triangles are nondegenerate, distinct, and meet only at their original apex. This rules out transitive identification, rather than merely checking each individual gluing. ## 5. The closed sphere and the exact oriented ribbon cut Root stationarity at complementary labels \(b,1-b\) gives equal ordered quadrilateral metrics, so (12) is the actual closing isometry. Paired FREE or CAP angles sum to one minus half their two mask bits. Two nonzero bits would require \(HH\) on a FREE edge or \(LL\) on a CAP edge. Neither root pair is strict. All closing seams are therefore flat WHITE/WHITE or right SHADED/WHITE. The supported-face argument makes the union an actual convex ideal polyhedron \(P\). Its boundary is a sphere, every surviving edge is right, and every such edge belongs to an original shaded triangle. All other seams merge only white pieces. There is no duplicate shaded edge or white bigon: distinct shaded faces cannot share an edge because each such edge has a WHITE side. White faces are actual maximal convex ideal polygons, with no zero-width or two-edge region. To identify the original link, use the [independent literal-wire compiler](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). At leaf \(i\), put shaded triangles \((O_i,C_{i1},C_{i2})\), \((O_i,C_{i3},C_{i0})\) in the original oriented chart. At each terminal record the outgoing-next and incoming-previous shaded neighbors. Product (8) concatenates the two recorded sectors at each consumed terminal pair; turn rotates the ports; closure (12) makes the original cylindrical pairs. These are precisely the metric cell maps and cyclic orders. The refined masks change which seams remain right edges, without changing terminal pairings or orientations. Every shaded edge survives and every remaining seam is WHITE/WHITE flat. The resulting metric boundary is exactly the original bowtie ribbon graph. All white facial cycles are its complementary oriented facial walks. One global orientation is retained throughout. The projection cut is reversible for arbitrary literal syntax here. Each auxiliary circle remains in its original disjoint leaf box with its recorded twice-punctured disk. In either projection ball, drilling its boundary-parallel semicircle and cutting along the same half disk cancel one handle in that collar. The collars are disjoint. This leaves a ball with the original ideal main-segment vertices and disk triangles. Its oriented boundary is the ribbon cellulation just proved. Match the labeled sphere cellulations and extend over the two balls. Restoring the original white projection pairings and shaded disk pairings recovers the actual augmented-link exterior. The construction has degree one and retains every component. It does not interpret an auxiliary open quadrilateral port as a physical four-punctured boundary. ## 6. Nondegenerate cusp rectangles and four-step edge cycles Every ideal vertex of \(P\) has only right incident edges. Its sufficiently small horosphere section is a finite convex Euclidean polygon with all angles \(\pi/2\); the angle sum forces four sides. It is a nondegenerate rectangle. Its supporting faces are distinct and \(P\) has three-dimensional interior; coincident opposite supporting lines would put \(P\) into a plane. Every side length is positive. Colors alternate WHITE and SHADED. Take two oppositely oriented projection copies. A white pairing matches identically labeled faces across copies. The shaded pair for leaf \(i\) is glued within each copy by the original rule fixing \(O_i\), mapping \(C_{i1}\) to \(C_{i0}\), and \(C_{i2}\) to \(C_{i3}\). These ideal-triangle maps are isometries. For an edge \(e\) of one shaded triangle, its partner \(e'\) belongs to the other shaded triangle of the same leaf. They are distinct: those triangles share only the apex, not an edge. The complete edge cycle has the four occurrences \[ e^{(0)},\quad e'^{(0)},\quad e'^{(1)},\quad e^{(1)} \tag{13} \] up to cyclic order. There is no shorter self-gluing return. The shaded maps are inverse labeled triangle maps, and white maps are the identity between labeled copies. The cycle returns pointwise on its edge, with total angle \(2\pi\) and no residual longitudinal translation. At each ideal vertex, scale its horosphere so the two equal positive SHADED side lengths are one. Each shaded triangle now has its canonical three corner segments of length one. All shaded maps preserve these horospheres; white pairings join identical decorations. Shrink them uniformly to disjoint cusp neighborhoods. Their rectangles glue without dilation into compact nonsingular Euclidean surfaces, identified by the actual link cut as the original cusp tori. The truncated core is compact. Thus the assembled metric is complete and has finite volume. Each leaf apex retains its exact local rectangle. The original [primitive crossing-circle paths](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md), §6, therefore remain the actual complete meridian and disk-framed longitude, with ratio \(2i\cot(\pi a_i)\). This complete marking alone does not establish a deformed signed-source representation. ## 7. Volume, connected-sum scope and the quantum limitation Each local cell is attached on the opposite supported side of its face. The cell adjacency graph is a tree and every cell has positive volume. With \(\mathcal A_E\) the original dimensionless sum of leaf and retained gate actions, \[ \operatorname{Vol}(P)=\pi\max\mathcal A_E,\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^0)=2\pi\max\mathcal A_E. \tag{14} \] The original positive finite source \(Z^0_{E,N}\) has the same rate. Uniform factorial upper bounds and polynomial state counting give the upper bound; primitive every-level rounding of the strict optimizer gives a positive lower term at both parities. Thus \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log Z^0_{E,N} =\operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^0). \tag{15} \] All original normal directions and finite source support remain present. This does not discard the [cap-connected-sum obstruction](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md). A cap product \(D(FG)=C(T(FG))\) forces its final product output to zero, both inputs to zero, and that gate to be flat. Such a diagram has not been exhibited as a strict root \(C(F'G')\) of the present kind. The boundary cap reduction retains its two-punctured sum sphere and gives the sum of piece volumes. Here the additional information is the explicit complete metric. A nontrivial sum of already complete cusp pieces would give two noncommuting longitudes centralizing their common meridian, contrary to the abelian parabolic centralizer in this metric. Hyperbolicity has not been inferred merely from positivity of a source rate. Likewise the rigid \(L/H\) constants in (5) are not interpreted as finite scalar factors or automatic connected-sum factors. The theorem above is for the original untwisted complete source. No extension to arbitrary retained half-twist patterns is claimed by this note. Their local pairing construction is a separate input. Nor is a signed packet, global alias bound, or long-filling volume theorem inferred for the whole enlarged syntax. Strict \(L/H\) expressions can contain quarter-index leaves; the analytic treatment of those leaves and the required global source estimates are separate from this complete geometry. ## Inputs The proof uses the [strict-type and rounding theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), the [original stationary ports](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md), the [actual ideal prism metrics and ordered maps](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md), the [supported-face and complete-cusp construction](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), and the [independent original bowtie cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). Sections 2–6 audit the additional type, mask, ideal-coincidence and cellulation obligations rather than assuming the older completed-only scope.

title: Complete half-twist partners and a general knot-connectivity construction
status: Complete partners and constructive knot patterns
text: # Complete half-twist partners and a general knot-connectivity construction 29 October 2026. Every fixed half-twist pattern on the leaves of a retained robust Conway factor has an actual complete hyperbolic augmented-link complement, with the SAME volume as its pure partner. This follows from explicit changed face pairings of the already proved polyhedron, including their pointwise edge words and complete cusp links. No unmarked half-twist invariance theorem is imported. Moreover EVERY robust expression has a constructible half-twist pattern whose main strands form ONE component, before or after any integral full-twist fillings. Thus the grammar has genuine arbitrarily branching knot candidates. The required odd-source mixed-color estimates and marked DEFORMED geometry remain separate from the complete theorem here. ## 1. The actual local cut after one half twist Use the original closed bowtie cut and its labels S0=(O,C1,C2), S1=(O,C3,C0). Superscripts + and - distinguish the two projection balls. Without a half twist the shaded gluing stays within each ball, fixing O and matching C1 to C0, C2 to C3. The white faces pair the two balls by their original projection labels. To insert a literal half twist, cut at that leaf's original twice- punctured crossing disk and rotate one side through +pi or -pi around its normal. In coordinates on the disk this is (y,z)->(-y,-z), with the projection line z=0 and the two punctures at y=+a,-a. It exchanges the punctures AND the upper and lower half disks. Consequently the new shaded pairings are S0+ -> S1-: O+->O-, C1+->C3-, C2+->C0-, S1+ -> S0-: O+->O-, C3+->C1-, C0+->C2-. (1) The reverse pairings are their inverses. The white maps are unchanged. These are maps across copies; making the same puncture swap within one copy would give the wrong boundary orientation. This is a literal reversible local cut of the original odd leaf T(R^epsilon L_N), epsilon=+1 or -1. Quarter-turning its one-crossing main tangle gives the opposite pairing (0,2),(1,3), exactly as (1). All original turns and identity strips outside this disk remain in place. The closed bowtie proof therefore identifies the resulting face quotient with the actual half-twist partner exterior. The two signs have the same boundary half-rotation and hence the same unmarked face pairing. Their collar paths differ by a full twist, which changes the primitive crossing-circle meridian by one disk longitude. Complete volume does not depend on this marking, but a future filling equation must keep the chosen sign and collar path. ## 2. Exact odd edge holonomy Keep the complete stationary polyhedron of the pure source. At this leaf set E=exp(2pi i x), 0<x<1/2, and normalize its ordered port to Q=(0,infinity,1,R), R=(1+E)^2/(4E), O+=(1+E)/2, O-=(1+E)/(2E). The four actual white/completion maps are the matrices W0,...,W3 in [the marked pure-deformation proof](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md), equation (8). At the COMPLETE point the cross-half map in the first line of (1) is T=[[R,-R],[1,ER-1-E]]. (2) It sends infinity to R, 1 to 0 and O+ to O-. The second map is T'=bar(T)^(-1), where bar(E)=E^-1 and bar(R)=R. Direct multiplication gives all three pointwise odd edge words: W0^(-1) T' W2^(-1) T = identity, W2^(-1) T' W0^(-1) T = identity, W1^(-1) T' W3^(-1) T = identity. (3) The first two are the two pairs of bowtie sides incident to O; the third is the CAP-base pair. The reverse edge words are their inverses. Each word visits four distinct copies of an edge. Each corner still has dihedral angle pi/2, so its total is 2pi. Equation (3) additionally rules out translation or dilation along that edge; the angle count alone would not suffice. Every edge belongs to one leaf bowtie. An arbitrary mixture of even and odd leaves therefore uses the already checked pure edge word or one of (3), independently at that leaf. All white/white auxiliary seams remain the original pointwise identities. This proves every edge relation for an arbitrary fixed pattern, not just one isolated half-twist example. ## 3. Complete cusps and unchanged actual volume Use the complete right-angled polyhedron's canonical horosphere decoration: at each ideal vertex scale its rectangular link so that both opposite shaded sides have length one. They have equal length because they are opposite sides of a rectangle. The same decoration is placed in the other copy. Every ideal shaded triangle then has the same length-one horocycle at each of its three corners. Both the original shaded maps and the changed cross-half maps (1) preserve these horocycles, including their corner permutation. White maps preserve the copied rectangular links. Hence the new cusp links are finite Euclidean rectangle gluings without a dilation defect. Their corner angles sum to 2pi by the four-edge cycles. The literal link-exterior topology makes each connected link a torus. They give complete flat cusp tori and complete horoball ends after a uniform shrink. All finite points are smooth by (3). Thus the quotient of the two original polyhedra is the complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL half-twist partner. Its oriented volume is exactly twice the unchanged polyhedron volume: Vol(S^3 minus L_E^epsilon) =2 Vol(P_E)=2pi phi_E(0). (4) Combined with the independently proved whole complete odd-source asymptotic in [the original Newton transport theorem](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md), this identifies its full-sequence exponential rate with the actual half-twist partner volume, for every fixed ±/0 pattern. This is a COMPLETE statement. The mixed pure-cell construction with opposite apex flags cannot be reused unchanged in (1): the odd cross-half equations and the correct meridian marking must be solved for the odd source's own deformed action. ## 4. The two primitive half-twist markings The complete crossing-circle cusp can also be computed directly. In its original local upper-half-space coordinate, (C0,C1,C2,C3)=(1,E,-1,-E), O=infinity. The lower and upper white maps to the reflected copy are B0(z)=-z/E+(E+1)/E, B2(z)=-z/E-(E+1)/E. The two cross-half shaded maps in (1) are T0(z)=-z/E+(E-1)/E, T1(z)=-z/E-(E-1)/E. (5) The disk-framed longitude still crosses the bottom white face and returns through the top, giving lambda=B2^(-1)B0=-2(E+1). The two signed meridian collar paths give translations mu_+=-2, mu_-=2E, mu_+-mu_-=lambda. (6) For example the elementary shaded/white paths B0^(-1)T0 and B0^(-1)T1 translate by 2 and 2E; reversing the first gives mu_+. Which collar is called + is the geometric positive-diagonal convention. Identifying it with the chosen quantum R or R^-1 requires retaining that braid convention; it is not inferred from the unmarked metric. Put c=cot(pi x)>0. Relative to the pure meridian mu_0=E-1, mu_+=mu_0+lambda/2, mu_-=mu_0-lambda/2, tau_+=lambda/mu_+=2ic/(1+ic)=1+E, tau_-=lambda/mu_-=2ic/(1-ic)=-1-E^-1. (7) These relations compare Euclidean translation vectors; lambda/2 alone need not be a loop of either cusp lattice. Each pair (mu_+,lambda) or (mu_-,lambda) has area 4 sin(2pi x), exactly the total area of the two original rectangles, so each is a primitive peripheral basis. This checks the complete marking rather than merely the isometry type of an unmarked cusp. ## 5. Literal main connectivity Ignore auxiliary circles only for counting the main components. For the four ports (bottom-left,bottom-right,top-right,top-left) write I=(0,3)(1,2), U=(0,1)(2,3), X=(0,2)(1,3). A pure leaf has pairing U. An odd leaf has pairing X by (1). A turn swaps I and U and fixes X. The literal stack table is | lower / upper | I | U | X | |---|---|---|---| | I | I | U | X | | U | U | U plus one internal circle | U | | X | X | U | I | This is obtained just by following the original two identity wires. The ONLY operation creating a new internal main circle is U times U. Once an internal component exists later operations cannot remove it. The cylindrical closure of I has two components; those of U and X have exactly one. At a robust seed h^3 choose either: * all three leaves odd: its pairing is X, with no internal circle; * exactly one leaf pure and the other two odd: its pairing is U, with no internal circle. Thus the seed can realize the set C={U,X} without loops. A turn permutes the three pairing types. To see that arbitrary branching never destroys the needed choices, put A={I,U}, B={I,X}, C={U,X}, D={I,U,X}. When the forbidden loop-creating choice U times U is excluded, the products of the three two-element sets are | lower / upper | A | B | C | |---|---|---|---| | A | A | D | C | | B | D | B | D | | C | C | D | A | In particular at least two feasible pairing types survive every product. The statement remains true if a child already offers D. Induction proves that EVERY robust expression offers at least two types with no internal main circles. At least one is U or X. Choose that root type and backtrack the finite choices in the table: its cylindrical closure has one main component. This is a linear-time constructive parity prescription for arbitrary fixed branching and turn depth. One may choose either sign on every odd leaf; only parity affects connectivity. Subsequent full twists have even endpoint permutation and preserve it. Therefore after filling ALL auxiliary circles by any integral full-twist parameters, the resulting diagram is a KNOT in S^3. With some auxiliary circles retained it has one main component and those auxiliary components. The complete augmented partner is hyperbolic by sections 1--3. The odd mixed source estimates and the correctly marked deformed branch are separate inputs. They are now supplied in the [long-filled knot and link assembly](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) for C(FG) with robust children. That mixed-color filling theorem continues to exclude C(A), although the complete theorem here covers it. Audit: [exact odd edge words, cusp paths and constructive knot patterns](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry_results.json). The finite audit checks all three generic odd edge words, both primitive diagonal markings and their two-rectangle areas, all nine products of pairing sets, 69 literal expression witnesses and 483 signed full-twist checks. Complete geometry alone is not used to claim a filled quantum theorem.

title: Long fillings of the isolated three-leaf Conway source
text:
# Long fillings of the isolated three-leaf Conway source 31 October 2026. original-source theorem. The isolated closure $C(A_3)=C(hhh)$ has a whole-source alias gap and a physical-color complement gap for every fixed pure or signed half-twist pattern. Its existing finite complex packet and marked geometry therefore give the original long-filling volume limit at both level parities. The new input is the [uniform two-leaf block lemma](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md), including its endpoint $X=1/2$, together with the elementary three-alias bound below. All original colors, Hermite normal directions, phases, marks and circle factors are retained. More precisely, let $\epsilon_l\in\{0,+1,-1\}$ at the three original leaves, and let $Y^\epsilon$ be the actual augmented exterior. Fill any chosen auxiliary subset $I$ by independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral full twists $R^{-2p_i}$. The literal power at a filled leaf is $\epsilon_i-2p_i$; an unfilled cusp is kept complete, not represented by $p_i=0$. Then $$ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_{C(A_3),N}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf p)ight| =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(Y^\epsilon(\mathbf p)ight). 	ag{1} $$ The signs, filling subset and slopes are fixed before $N$ tends to infinity. The threshold depends on the fixed source, sign pattern and filling subset; all independently chosen $|p_i|$ beyond it are allowed. The slopes need not have the same sign or comparable magnitudes. Both parity subsequences and composite levels are included. After all auxiliary fillings, a loop-free one-main-component parity pattern gives a knot, and the right side of (1) is its hyperbolic **knot complement volume**. Partial fillings retain the actual remaining cusps. The normalization is the original marked one-cut scalar: its external enhancement has unit modulus for the reduced enhanced Kashaev invariant, and modulus $1/N$, once, for the full modified one-cut normalization. These are the unchanged [original normalization conventions](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) and [crossing comparison](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). ## 1. Exact regrouping in the original source Each physical changed leaf is $X_l=T(R^{\epsilon_l}L_{j_l})$, with its original turn, pivot, Cartan phase and independent color $1\le j_l\le N$. It belongs to the full pair-Casimir algebra $H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)$. Its exact core/alias split $X_l=C_l+A_l$ also consists of elements of that algebra. Consequently $\phi(X_1X_2X_3)=\phi((X_iX_j)X_k)$ for every permutation $(i,j,k)$. This is associativity and commutativity of the actual physical commutant, with the original marked Frobenius functional. The complete turned coupons are formed first; no factor is moved across a quarter-turn. It is an algebraic identity for the original scalar, not an assertion that arbitrary permutations of physical tangles are relative-boundary isotopies. There is an explicit verification using the [original positive Newton product](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md). Put $d=N-1$, $M=\lfloor d/2floor$, and $s_r=\prod_{t=1}^r2\sin(\pi t/N)$, with $s_0=1$. Its factorial reflection $s_rs_{d-r}=N$, the positive product kernel, and $\phi(\widehat B_u\widehat B_v)=\mathbf 1_{u+v=d}$ give $$  egin{aligned} \mathcal T_N&=\{(i,j,k)\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^3: i+j,\ i+k,\ j+k\le d,\quad i+j+k\ge d\},\ \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j\widehat B_k) &=  egin{cases} \displaystyle  rac{s_{i+j}s_{i+k}s_{j+k}} {N\,s_i s_j s_k s_{i+j+k-d}}, &(i,j,k)\in\mathcal T_N,\[6pt] 0,&(i,j,k)
otin\mathcal T_N. \end{cases} \end{aligned}	ag{2} $$ Indeed, start with $\mu_{i,j,d-k}$ and apply factorial reflection to its three complementary indices. Every factorial index in (2) lies between $0$ and $d$. The identity is symmetric and includes all repeated-node normal data; its zero cases follow from full polynomial divisibility, not just nodal values. The factor $1/N$ is the derived kernel scalar, not an additional circle or mark normalization. Thus, for each chosen alias subset, one may select the useful grouping while bounding the same original signed sector. At most three free original leaf indices remain; the internal pair output is exactly $d$ minus the third leaf index. The final gate coefficient is one. Independent colors and either half-twist sign cause no exception. The [full Newton transport](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md) and [finite block source proof](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md) supply the literal core/alias arrays, including odd alias indices above $M$ and all Hermite directions. For clarity, write the retained continuum profiles as $$  egin{aligned} J(t)&=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du,\ g(t)&=J(2t)-4J(t),\ \widetilde g(t)&=g(\max\{t,1/4\}),\quad 0\le t\le1/2,\ k(t)&=-2J(t/2),\quad 0\le t\le1,\ m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). \end{aligned}	ag{3} $$ These are upper rates for the actual finite core, alias and product coefficients, respectively, with their original uniform errors. The product domain remains $\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1$. ## 2. One or two aliases: the endpoint of the uniform block lemma The isolated complete optimum has all three leaf coordinates $$  egin{aligned} a&= rac{\arctan2}{\pi},\qquad X=\cot(\pi a)= rac12,\qquad b=1-a,\ \lambda&=F_2'(b)=g'(a)=-\log4,\ F_0&=3g(a)+m(a,a,1-a)= rac{2v_8}{\pi}, \end{aligned}	ag{4} $$ where $F_2(b)=2g(a)+m(a,a,b)$ is the optimized pure pair action at this output. These are the exact [three-leaf complete-source formulas](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md), §6. The internal pair gate is strict, even though this pair is not a proper macro-seed with $X>1/2$. The uniform block lemma includes $X=1/2$ and supplies a margin greater than $1/100$ throughout the output interval. For one alias, group it with a core, leaving the other core. For two aliases, group them together, leaving the unique core. Equation (2) justifies either grouping with the original colors and signs. If $z$ is the pair output and $u$ is the remaining core output, their upper rates satisfy $$  egin{aligned} G_{\mathrm{AC}}(z),\ G_{\mathrm{AA}}(z) &\le F_2(b)+\lambda(z-b)- rac1{100},\ \widetilde g(u)&\le g(a)+g'(a)(u-a). \end{aligned}	ag{5} $$ The second inequality is the complete core tangent, valid because $a>1/4$. The exact root relation is $z+u=d/N$. Since $a+b=1$ and $g'(a)=\lambda$, the summed per-state action is at most $$ F_0- rac1{100}+\lambda\left( rac dN-1ight) =F_0- rac1{100}+ rac{\log4}{N}. 	ag{6} $$ The affine discrepancy is therefore bounded in the exponent. There are only polynomially many states, and the original local errors are uniformly $o(N)$. Each such signed sector has upper rate at most $F_0-1/100$, uniformly over its physical colors. No individual alias tangent at $a$ is required. ## 3. Three aliases: an elementary absolute margin Let $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$ be the regular ideal tetrahedron volume, where $\Lambda$ is the Lobachevsky function, and let $v_8=4G$, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. The maximum of $k$ on $[0,1]$ is $v_3/\pi$. Its normalization follows, for example, from $$ J(2t)=2J(t)-2J(1/2-t),\qquad 3J(1/3)=2J(1/6),\qquad k(1/3)=-3J(1/3)= rac{v_3}{\pi}. 	ag{7} $$ The retained product action is the sum of three ideal-tetrahedron volumes divided by $\pi$. Explicitly, with $p=z-x$, $q=z-y$, $r=x+y-z$ and $w=1-x-y$, the angle triples are $(y,x,w)$, $(p,q,2r+w)$ and $(p+q,r,r+w)$. Each is nonnegative with sum one on the true product domain, including its boundaries and an allowed input above half. Each triangle entropy is at most $v_3/\pi$, so $m\le3v_3/\pi$. The final gate is flat and contributes no action. Every three-alias sector therefore has upper rate at most $6v_3/\pi$. The strict comparison needs no decimal volume estimate. The sine series gives $$ v_3= rac{3\sqrt3}{4}\sum_{n\ge0} \left( rac1{(3n+1)^2}- rac1{(3n+2)^2}ight) < rac{39\sqrt3}{64}< rac{273}{256}. 	ag{8} $$ The $n=0$ term is $3/4$. For $n\ge1$, replacing the second denominator $3n+2$ by $3n+4$ strictly increases the differences, and the resulting tail telescopes to $1/16$. The last inequality uses $\sqrt3<7/4$. The first two alternating Catalan terms give $v_8>32/9$. Thus $$ F_0- rac{6v_3}{\pi} = rac2\pi(v_8-3v_3) > rac2\pi rac{821}{2304} > rac{5747}{25344} > rac1{100}, 	ag{9} $$ using $\pi<22/7$. This is a coarse exact bound, not a claim that the alias upper profiles attain it. There are seven nonempty alias subsets. Summing their bounds and absorbing the polynomial factors and uniform $o(N)$ errors gives, at both parities and for all sufficiently large $N$, $$ \sup_{1\le j_1,j_2,j_3\le N} \left|Z_N^\epsilon(\mathbf j)-Z_N^{\epsilon,\mathrm{core}}(\mathbf j)ight| \le \exp\!\left[N\left(F_0- rac1{200}ight)ight]. 	ag{10} $$ The estimate may also be maximized over the finitely many sign patterns. Pure-alias nilpotent vanishings can improve some sectors, but are not assumed for arbitrary mixed patterns. ## 4. Whole physical-color complement and the finite complex packet On the all-core support the limiting majorant is $$ \overline F(x_1,x_2,x_3) =\sum_{l=1}^3\widetilde g(x_l)+m(x_1,x_2,1-x_3), \qquad 0\le x_l\le rac12,\quad x_1+x_2+x_3\ge1. 	ag{11} $$ It is concave and agrees with the pure action near the strict complete optimum $(a,a,a)$, since $a>1/4$. Its Hessian there is negative definite. If another point also maximized it, the intervening segment would contradict this local strictness. Thus this is its unique global maximum, and the complement of any small fixed complete-state window has a compact gap. Continuity carries the gap to the exact finite supports. Inside that window, every leaf lies below a fixed $ eta<1/2$. The existing actual core recurrence gives a strict local rate loss when its physical color lies outside a fixed small complete corridor. The high-index proof requires the strict quarter condition $a>1/4$, not the proper-seed upper bound on $a$. Pure leaves satisfy the corresponding factorial estimate; a zero core causes no difficulty. Combining the inside and outside regions with (10) proves, for every fixed sufficiently small $\delta>0$, some $\gamma_\delta>0$ such that $$ \max_{\substack{1\le j_l\le N\ N-j_l\ge\delta N	ext{ for some }l}} |Z_N^\epsilon(\mathbf j)| \le\exp[N(F_0-\gamma_\delta)] 	ag{12} $$ for all sufficiently large $N$, at both parities. The minimal-seed lattice and pure packet are explicitly calibrated in [the finite complex-window theorem](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md), §6. The three original leaf indices $i,j,k$ are free primitive integer coordinates, and the retained gate output is $t=d-k=N(1-x_3)-1$. Every factorial argument at $(a,a,1-a)$ is strict. Rounding this three-dimensional lattice works at every sufficiently large level without a parity constraint. Its complete negative Hessian and pure amplitude are $$ A= rac{25\pi}{4}(I_3+\mathbf1\mathbf1^\mathsf T), \qquad \sqrt{\det A}= rac{125\pi^{3/2}}4,\qquad a_{\mathrm{pure}}(0)= rac{\sqrt2}{64}. 	ag{13} $$ The output shift by $-1$ contributes the essential factor $\exp(-m_z)=4$ at completeness. The calibrated pure packet has power $N^{3/2}$ and phase $F_0$. No unspecified lattice density or periodic prefactor is introduced. For changed leaves, each local high-index theorem in [the actual mixed complex packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md), §§1–6, applies on a fixed compact neighborhood of $a\in(1/4,1/2)$. Its finite source formula, chirp and exponentially accurate relative interpolation do not depend on seed width or require two completed root children. Here $H=3$, there is one retained gate, and the interpolated summand has power $N^{3-H}=1$. The primitive Gaussian sum supplies $N^{3/2}$. With these free leaf coordinates, all leaf offsets are zero: the sole leading affine offset is $\exp[-m_z(x_1,x_2,1-x_3)]$, evaluated at the changed critical point. It equals $4$ only at completeness. If different shifted leaf coordinates are used, the general offset formula in the packet theorem, (23), uses the changed leaf derivatives $f_{\epsilon_l}$. No pure colored offset is reused away from completeness. The changed complete multiplier and the retained external phase are $$  egin{aligned} a_\epsilon(0) &= rac{\sqrt2}{64} \prod_{\epsilon_l
e0}\sqrt{\sin(\pi a)} \exp(-i\epsilon_l\pi a/2)
e0,\ \eta_N&=\exp\!\left[ rac{i\pi d}{4}\sum_{l=1}^3\epsilon_light]. \end{aligned}	ag{14} $$ The phase $\eta_N$ remains outside the normalized packet. Its separately even color action has Hessian $$ \partial_{\chi_l}\partial_{\chi_m}\Phi_\epsilon(0) =- rac{\pi}{1-\epsilon_l i/2}\,\delta_{lm}, 	ag{15} $$ whose real part is negative definite. All original $N^2$ circle factors, Hermite normal data and exact $N-1$ offsets remain unchanged. The finite window contour proof therefore gives the same normalized complex packet, with nonzero leading amplitude and relative $O(N^{-1})$ error. Equations (10) and (12) supply the previously missing comparison with the whole physical mixed source, including aliases and color endpoints. ## 5. Marked geometry and the filling conclusion Use the existing [complete geometry of isolated $C(A_3)$](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), §§2, 6–7. Its proof explicitly glues the completed $hh$ child to the last leaf with the corresponding $\pi/2$ CAP sums; it does not assume that both root children are completed cells. The literal closed projection cut, right-angled polyhedron and full cusp checks already cover this case. Its doubled complete volume is $4v_8$. The [half-twist partners](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md) use the same original leaf disk maps and retain this complete volume at every fixed sign pattern. The selected mixed action is regular at all three strict high leaf indices, and its wire Hessian (13) is invertible. The original rational white, prism, turn and closing maps and signed shaded words therefore assemble its nearby representation through the [marked peripheral deformation](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md), §§4–6. Its primitive coordinates remain $$ U_l=-2\pi i\chi_l,\qquad V_l=-2\,\partial_{\chi_l}\Phi_\epsilon. 	ag{16} $$ No pure rational-filling substitution is made. The complete geometric anchor fixes the absolute regulator, and every main cusp remains parabolic. The selected action, original finite packet, nonzero amplitude and both whole-source gaps now supply every hypothesis of the [original-source long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). With the original primitive slope convention, the critical equation is $U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i$. The same action and normalization identify the limit with the actual hyperbolic exterior volume, proving (1). After all auxiliary fillings, each leaf is the literal rational tangle $T(R^{\epsilon_l-2p_l})$. Their original products and cylindrical closure give a Conway algebraic link; the [one-main-component parity criterion](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) selects knots. All auxiliary components have then been removed by filling, while the knot cusp remains complete. No rational-fraction arithmetic is being substituted for tangle isotopy. This extension makes no assertion about isolated $C(A_2)$, arbitrary algebraic tangles, or diagrams varying without bound as $N$ grows. ## scope and validation scope The proof uses the retained original coefficient, packet and marked-geometry theorems at the strict isolated state and the exact rational certificate for the uniform block lemma. No new numerical test or asymptotic inference from finite samples is used here. Native equation rendering and relative source links are checked separately. Existing theorem, checkpoint, status and public files are unchanged.

title: Long-full-twist volume equality for every retained robust Conway factor
text: # Long-full-twist volume equality for every retained robust Conway factor 29 October 2026. The complete quantum hypotheses of the general long-filling transfer theorem now hold for EVERY retained cylindrical robust Conway factor. This gives a full original-source limit after independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral full twists, with a nonzero leading coefficient and both level parities retained. Its rate is the ACTUAL hyperbolic volume of the correctly marked filled link complement. The [marked deformation theorem](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) constructs the required representation and fixes its absolute regulator. These pure robust sources remain LINKS after the indicated fillings; they do not give a new knot family. ## 1. Exact scope and source normalization Let C(E) be C(A), A=h^3, or C(FG) with F,G robust expressions generated by A, the actual quarter-turn and actual product. Fix the entire compiled diagram, its retained auxiliary circles and original mark. Choose a subset I of the auxiliary circles. At each i in I substitute the original full twist R^(-2p_i) through its exact Fourier--Hermite auxiliary-color kernel. Unfilled colors stay at their complete value; they are not assigned p_i=0. Let K_(E,N)(p) denote this actual scalar with its separately recorded original enhancement/framing factor chi_N, where log|chi_N|=o(N) and chi_N is nonzero. The result applies first to the literal raw one-cut source and then to any stated normalization with this property. No new normalization depending on the unknown completed invariant is introduced. The principal analytic inputs are now proved: * The [mixed-leaf identity](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md) retains the full repeated-root algebra, positive core and signed square-zero radical. * The [uniform whole-source gap](actual_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) bounds every propagated alias and the ENTIRE complementary physical color cube after arbitrary finite turns and branching. * The [finite complex packet](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md) has a uniform, separately-even, nonzero asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood, with its actual integer lattice and D=N-1 offsets. These facts supply hypotheses (2)--(5) of the [general original-source transfer theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). Its already proved exact contour and charge argument therefore applies. No source assumption is inferred merely from geometric existence. ## 2. The actual packet and its selected action Use chi_i=(N-j_i)/N for each chosen auxiliary color. Let y denote the free wire coordinates of the reduced strict source problem. Define f_E(y,chi)=sum_leaves g_(chi_l)(x_l(y)) +sum_retained_products m(x,y,z), g_chi(x)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-chi)-J(x+chi), J(x)=integral_0^x Log(2sin(pi t))dt, (1) where chi_l=0 for unfilled circles, the source marks are continued from the positive complete chamber, and all true product/turn relations remain in the affine wire maps. There is a unique holomorphic critical branch y_*(chi) near the strict complete optimizer. Put phi(chi)=f_E(y_*(chi),chi). (2) The exact finite packet has asymptotic N^(3/2) a_E(chi) exp[N phi(chi)](1+O(N^-1)), with a_E nonzero and a_E(0)>0, uniformly in a fixed complex polydisk. Both phi and a_E are separately even. If x_(i,*) is the complete maximizing leaf label, then phi(0)=max V_E/pi, phi''(0)=-2pi diag(cot(pi x_(i,*))). (3) Thus the transfer theorem's parameters are tau_packet,i=i cot(pi x_(i,*)), with positive imaginary part. They are HALF the actual complete geometric cusp ratios tau_geom,i=2i cot(pi x_(i,*)); this factor is required by the recorded full-twist/peripheral convention. ## 3. The unconditional original-source limit For independently sufficiently large fixed signed integers p_i, let chi_*(p) be the unique small solution of partial_i phi(chi)+(pi i/p_i)(chi_i-1)=0 for i in I. (4) Existence and uniqueness follow by the implicit-function theorem in the small independent parameters 1/p_i. Define S_p(chi)=phi(chi)+(pi i/2)sum_(i in I)(chi_i-1)^2/p_i. (5) Then the FULL original invariant has a nonzero asymptotic of the form K_(E,N)(p)=chi_N kappa^(-sum_i p_i) N^(3/2) D_E(p) exp[N S_p(chi_*(p))](1+O_p(N^-1)), D_E(p)!=0, (6) with the explicit retained unit Cartan/framing factors of the transfer theorem. In the pure positive mixed-circle chart its packet phase eta_N is one. In particular lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_(E,N)(p)| =2pi Re S_p(chi_*(p)). (7) To check (4)--(5) directly against the transfer conventions, its Fourier critical equations are partial_i phi(chi)+2pi i z_i=0, chi_i-2p_i z_i=1. Thus z_i=(chi_i-1)/(2p_i); substituting into phi(chi)+2pi i chi.z-2pi i sum(p_i z_i^2+z_i) gives exactly (5). The nonzero prefactor and the addition of the minimal signed charge sectors are those proved in the transfer theorem, not an inference from a positive real maximum before filling. All ordinary auxiliary colors, projective normals, paired endpoints and nonminimal Fourier charges are accounted for by that theorem and the whole-source gap. There is no prime-level, odd-level, equal-slope or same-sign restriction. The number of circles and every slope are fixed before N tends to infinity. ## 4. The actual filled hyperbolic volume At zero inverse slope the source anchor is 2pi phi(0)=2max V_E=Vol(S^3 minus L_E), (8) by the complete geometry and its [corrected closed projection cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). The source rate in (7) tends to this actual complete volume as all |p_i| tend to infinity. For example its quadratic decrease is 2pi Re S_p(chi_*) =2pi phi(0)-sum_i pi^2/[2p_i^2 cot(pi x_(i,*))] +O(||p^(-1)||^3). (9) This follows by inserting chi_*,i=-i/[2p_i cot(pi x_(i,*))]+O(||p^(-1)||^2) in (5). Its geometric interpretation uses the full marked construction below, not merely agreement with the complete cusp Hessian. The [marked deformation proof](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) now supplies an actual bounded framed representation near the complete one, with the original peripheral marking and full action differential. Here U,V are logarithms of projective similarity multipliers, equivalently squared SL(2,C) peripheral eigenvalues: G=2pi i phi+recorded real constant, U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi. (10) All white and shaded edge words are pointwise identities, every main cusp stays parabolic, and the auxiliary paths are the primitive disk meridian and longitude. With the complete regulator anchor, (4) gives U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i exactly. Unfilled auxiliary cusps also remain parabolic. The existing general geometric completion theorem therefore applies, and the absolute regulator identity proves lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_(E,N)(p)|=Vol(S^3 minus L_E(p)). (11) This uses the actual group representation and every peripheral mark; it does not infer geometry just from matching open-port cross ratios. ## 5. These fillings do not produce knots If E contains S robust seeds, it already contains at least 2S internal main circles. Closing its exposed strands adds at least one more. Full twists have even endpoint permutation and preserve these components. The [literal component theorem](actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.md) therefore gives at least 2S+1 main components after filling every auxiliary circle. Consequently (11) is a broad actual LINK volume equality, with arbitrary fixed branching and turn depth. A new knot theorem needs different source connectivity, such as suitable retained odd half-twist coupons, with its own phase and source estimates. The filled-volume identification does not remove that requirement. The subsequent marked deformation supplies the geometric interface used in the final theorem. The marked representation, primitive unit filling equation, and absolute regulator establish (11). They are the geometric inputs needed in addition to the quantum argument (1)–(7). The later [signed half-twist extension](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) changes the original leaf connectivity and proves its separately selected source and peripheral geometry. For C(FG) with robust children it gives long-filled knot and link families at arbitrary fixed diagram branching and turn depth. The pure component obstruction in section 5 remains unchanged.
