text: # The actual marked deformation of every retained Conway factor 29 October 2026. This constructs an actual framed representation of the original closed link exterior for the mixed-circle critical source. All face-pairing relations hold as PSL(2,C) identities, including the white seams and the full four-step shaded-edge holonomies. The primitive crossing-circle logarithms are U_i=-2pi i t_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi(t). Thus the existing source filling saddle is the actual marked filling equation. The conclusion concerns the broad robust LINK class. Even full-twist fillings of these pure sources do not produce knots. The proof uses the [actual closed bowtie cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). An open metric quadrilateral is an auxiliary chart, not an asserted physical four-punctured boundary. No representation is inferred merely from matching quadrilateral metrics. ## 1. The analytic branch to be represented Fix a retained cylindrical factor C(A), A=h^3, or C(FG), where F,G belong to the robust turn/product grammar. Delete its final forced-flat product and retain the exact relation between the two final wire labels. For its free wire coordinates y and independent auxiliary parameters t_i write the original mixed-core action f(y,t)=sum_i g(x_i(y),t_i)+sum_products m(x,y,z), g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t), J(a)=integral_0^a Log(2sin(pi u))du. (1) The logarithms are continued from the strict complete positive chamber. The complete wire Hessian is negative definite. Hence there is one holomorphic critical branch y_*(t) near zero, and phi(t)=f(y_*(t),t). (2) Uniqueness and the separate evenness of (1) imply that every wire label and phi are separately even in all t_i. For small real t, all cell angles used below remain strict. Stationarity still says that ordered quadrilateral metrics match under the original stack corner maps. ## 2. The mixed leaf and its two actual flags Put E=exp(2pi i x), H=exp(2pi i t). A mixed leaf is the ideal pyramid with apex infinity and cyclic base C0=1, C1=E/H, C2=-1/H, C3=-E. (3) The consecutive half-arc lengths of its unit-circle base are (x-t, 1/2-x, x+t, 1/2-x). Triangulating the base gives volume pi g(x,t). Indeed the intermediate diagonal angles cancel, and J(2x)-2J(x)=-2J(1/2-x). Its ordered base cross ratio is kappa=sin(pi(x-t))sin(pi(x+t))/cos(pi x)^2 =exp(-partial_x g). (4) Normalize its ordered base to (0,infinity,1,R), where R=1/(1+kappa)=cos(pi x)^2/cos(pi t)^2 =H(1+E)^2/[E(1+H)^2]. (5) In this chart the plus-t apex is zeta_+=(1+E)/(1+H). The minus-t leaf has the SAME ordered base metric and its normalized apex is zeta_-=H zeta_+. These are the two roots of zeta^2-(1+E)zeta+ER=0. (6) For the second projection ball use the reflected MINUS-t cell, not the reflection of the plus-t cell. Its apex is zeta_+/E. Its main segment vertices remain the same real ordered base vertices. In the actual bowtie cut the shaded map takes (O,C1,C2) to (O,C0,C3). In the normalized chart its projective matrix is S=[[0,-ER],[1,-1-E]]. (7) It fixes both roots in (6). This follows by substitution, rather than by naming an unmarked eigenvalue of the Newton boundary relation. ## 3. Four universal boundary transport matrices For an ordered auxiliary port Q=(0,infinity,1,R) of wire label b, put E=exp(2pi i b). The following matrices send a plus chart to its reflected minus chart: W0=[[1,0],[0,E]], W1=[[1,E-1],[0,E]], W2=[[E-R,R(1-E)],[E-1,1-ER]], W3=[[R,0],[1-E,ER]]. (8) Wj fixes the two endpoints of port edge j,j+1. All equalities between matrices below are projective. The FREE edges are 01 and 23; CAP edges are 12 and 30. For the mixed leaf, W0 and W2 are its ACTUAL white triangle maps: they fix the relevant two main vertices and send zeta_+ to zeta_+/E. For W2 the last assertion follows from (6). The matrices W1,W3 are completion-plane maps: at a leaf they describe the white pieces attached on the other side of its shaded CAP edges, not extra leaf white faces. One useful geometric description of (8) is that Wj followed by complex conjugation is reflection in a plane through the corresponding port edge. Its angle with the port plane is pi b on FREE edges and pi(1-b) on CAP edges, with the side fixed by the ordered chart. These are virtual planes for the mixed leaf; its actual white planes need not be their fixed planes. Equation (8), rather than an assumption of planarity of the deformed white polygons, is the transport data. ### The product identities Use the literal prism coordinates and child maps from [the local-cell proof](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md): lower Q=(v0,v1,P,infinity), upper Q=(infinity,P,v2,v3), output Q=(v0,v1,v2,v3). (9) The white prism triangles are T_top=(P,v1,v2) and T_bottom=(infinity,v0,v3). Call their actual maps to their reflected copies B_top,B_bottom. Transport each set of matrices (8) to the common prism coordinate. Then direct substitution gives ALL the needed identities: W_lower,1=W_upper,1=W_output,1=B_top, W_lower,3=W_upper,3=W_output,3=B_bottom, W_lower,2=W_upper,0, W_output,0=W_lower,0, W_output,2=W_upper,2. (10) Here the three E parameters are exp(2pi i x), exp(2pi i y), exp(2pi i z), and each R is the actual ordered-port value. These identities can also be checked by the plane description: the CAP/input angles complement each other; the common two-input FREE seam has angle w+x+y=1; the two output FREE angles are p+x=z and q+y=z. The maps are equal on entire planes, including their translations, since their ordered edge endpoints and reflection planes agree. No mere equality of absolute cross ratios is used. For a wholly algebraic check of (10), put A=exp(2pi i p), B=exp(2pi i r), C=exp(2pi i q). The prism coordinates are v0=1, v1=A, v2=AB, v3=ABC, P=1+A-A[AB(1+C)-1-A]/[A^2 B^2 C-A], (11) and the three E parameters are BC, AB, ABC. Conjugation replaces A,B,C by their reciprocals. If T sends an ordered port to (0,infinity,1,R), its world-coordinate matrix is bar(T)^(-1) Wj T. Inserting (11) gives (10) by cancellation of rational functions. The accompanying audit checks these identities symbolically with independent indeterminates A,B,C. ### Turns and final cylindrical closure A turn replaces E by E^-1, R by 1-R. The coordinate change is T(z)=(R-1)/(z-1), and exact substitution in (8) gives T W_(j+1)(E,R)=W_j(E^-1,1-R) T. (12) For the final ordered gluing j->3-j the two wire labels add to one and their kappas are equal. The normalized coordinate change is C(z)=(z-R)/(z-1), and C W_j(E^-1,R)=W_(2-j)(E,R) C. (13) Thus every original turn and the actual cylindrical closing map retain the complete transport matrices, not only their port metrics. ## 4. All original white face maps exist Build both halves using the prescribed metric quad maps. For real t, the plus and minus source wire values are equal. Every prism is therefore the same before reflection, and all corresponding main vertices have the same normalized port coordinates. Only auxiliary apices select the opposite roots (6). Induct on the actual expression. At a leaf its two white triangle maps are W0,W2. At a product the CAP pieces already white in a nonleaf child match the attached prism maps by (10). If the child is a leaf, its CAP face is shaded and the prism supplies precisely its completion map W1 or W3. The two-input FREE seam matches by the middle identity in (10). The remaining boundary pieces have exactly the output maps in (8). Equations (12),(13) perform every turn and final closure. Consequently any two triangular pieces belonging to the SAME original white face have EXACTLY the same Mobius map. This statement continues through all the white/white seams, including those whose deformed pieces are no longer coplanar. Their two-step edge holonomy is the identity. The original closed bowtie ribbon graph fixes which pieces belong to each white face; no open-port topology is being assumed. ## 5. Shaded edge relations and actual representations Write bar(S) for (7) with E replaced by E^-1; R is unchanged. Direct matrix multiplication gives W0 S=bar(S) W0, W2 S=bar(S) W2, W3 S=bar(S) W1. (14) The first two equations are the two pairs of bowtie sides incident to O. The last equation is its CAP-base pair. They are precisely the four-step edge words: shaded in the first half, white to the second, inverse shaded there, and inverse white back. Every such word is POINTWISE the identity in PSL(2,C), including any possible dilation or translation along its ideal edge. The [closed cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) supplies two actual topological balls and the labeled white/shaded gluings. Choose one of the face transitions to join their frames. The remaining face transitions generate the fundamental group; its edge relations are exactly the two-step white seams and four-step bowtie words just proved. Equivalently subdivide the balls and their faces and use the standard dual two-skeleton presentation, whose two-cells are these edge words. Thus these matrices define an ACTUAL representation of the original link group. This argument does not need the deformed half-ball image to remain an embedded convex polyhedron. At t=0 the construction is the proved complete geometric holonomy. The finitely many face matrices and cusp flags vary analytically and stay in a bounded framed neighborhood of it. Extend to complex t by holomorphic continuation: the second half means the Schwarz-reflected minus branch, with conjugated coordinate coefficients, rather than antiholomorphic dependence on t. Every identity above is holomorphic and holds for small real independent t, hence on a complex polydisk. ## 6. All main cusps remain parabolic At a main corner Cj the two original white sectors give its small meridian: cross one white face and return through the other. In its local port frame the resulting map is W_(j-1)^(-1) Wj, or its inverse according to the orientation. Both factors fix Cj. Their derivatives there are equal: at C0,C2 they are E^-1, and at C1,C3 they are E, using the finite local coordinate at infinity. Thus the multiplier of this actual meridian is one, IDENTICALLY in the deformation. The meridian is nonidentity at the complete point and remains so after shrinking the neighborhood. It is therefore parabolic. The actual longitude commutes with it, so it too is a translation in the common flag frame and has multiplier one. This proves parabolicity of the entire main peripheral groups, not only a trace equation at one flag. ## 7. Primitive auxiliary holonomies and their source derivatives Use the same primitive paths as at completeness in the closed-cut note. The crossing-circle meridian is the inverse shaded map. In the original leaf coordinate (3) it sends C3 to C2, C0 to C1 and fixes infinity: mu(z)=H^-1 z+(E-1)/H. Hence its small centered similarity log is exactly U=-Log H=-2pi i t. (15) The disk-framed longitude crosses the bottom white face and returns through the top. In the normalized chart it is W2^-1 W0, fixing zeta_+. Its multiplier in the flag-at-infinity coordinate is exp(V)=[(zeta_+-E)/(zeta_+-1)]^2 =[(1-EH)/(E-H)]^2 =[sin(pi(x+t))/sin(pi(x-t))]^2. (16) One can check the first equality directly: a Mobius map fixing a finite flag has flag-at-infinity multiplier reciprocal to its ordinary derivative there. Use (6) when differentiating W2^-1 W0. Continue the logarithm from V=0, obtaining V=2Log[sin(pi(x+t))/sin(pi(x-t))] =-2 partial_t g(x,t). (17) The paths are the primitive meridian and disk-framed longitude already calibrated by the two-rectangle complete cusp; no doubled longitude or unrecorded change of slope is inserted. Their continuations cannot change integral marking in a small connected neighborhood. Internal criticality and the envelope rule now give for every circle U_i=-2pi i t_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi(t). (18) An unfilled auxiliary color has t_i=0. Separate evenness makes V_i=0 there as well, so it remains a complete parabolic cusp. In particular dV_i/dU_i at zero =2i cot(pi x_(i,*)), in agreement with the primitive complete lattice, while the packet parameter in phi_ii=2pi i tau_packet,i is half this ratio. ## 8. Algebraic marked peripheral equations This construction also supplies finite algebraic equations for the ACTUAL peripheral branch. Exponentiate every internal stationarity equation, retaining all port variables and excluding the strict denominators. The product cross ratios are rational functions of their angle phases, and (4) is rational in E,H. Include M_i=H_i^-1, L_i=[(1-E_i H_i)/(E_i-H_i)]^2. (19) Here M_i=exp(U_i), L_i=exp(V_i) are the centered PROJECTIVE similarity multipliers. An SL(2) eigenvalue convention takes their square roots on the local marked branch, retaining its original central signs. No SL(2) spin is silently identified with one in (19). Here M_i,L_i are the PSL(2,C) similarity multipliers, equivalently the squared SL(2,C) peripheral eigenvalues. An SL lift and its spin would need to be retained before changing to unsquared variables. All equations are over Q after choosing the finitely many phase variables clearing the rational wire coefficients. Select the branch through the complete positive solution and retain its actual marking. The nondegenerate internal Hessian gives the analytic branch already used above. Thus (19) is a marked gluing presentation of an actual peripheral representation branch. Elimination may introduce extra components or factors; no irreducibility or equality with an entire classical A-polynomial is asserted merely by eliminating variables. More precisely, near the selected complete point the exponentiated stationarity Jacobian in the internal wire phases is nonsingular: on its continued logarithmic sheet it is the invertible wire Hessian times invertible phase-coordinate factors. Hence this algebraic solution branch is locally etale over the auxiliary H coordinates. Its marked peripheral image is the analytic graph L=L(M) given by (19). Equation (20) below implies sum_i dU_i wedge dV_i=0, so this actual H-dimensional peripheral germ is Lagrangian. The source action is its calibrated local primitive, not a period attached to an unidentified algebraic curve. ## 9. Absolute regulator and actual long-filled volumes Put G=2pi i phi, with any explicitly recorded real action constant retained. Equation (18) gives the full differential dG=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i. (20) At zero the actual oriented fundamental-chain volume is Im G(0)=2pi phi(0)=Vol(S^3 minus L_E), by the complete cell theorem and the closed bowtie cut. This anchors the SAME oriented representation family, not a possibly unrelated Bloch cycle of equal regulator. For completeness, the marked fundamental-chain differential is dVol(rho)=(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i]. It follows by differentiating each ideal tetrahedron's Bloch--Wigner volume; internal face/edge terms cancel, and a primitive meridian and longitude on a boundary torus have the signed intersection pairing. With eigenlogs U/2,V/2 the boundary pairing is -2, giving precisely the factor 1/2 displayed here. Distinct tori have zero cross pairing. This is the diagram-independent marked-chain calculation proved in [the general regulator theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md), section 6. Applying (20) and the complete anchor yields the ABSOLUTE identity on the connected small branch Vol(rho_t)=Im G(t)-(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (21) Now choose any subset of auxiliary circles and sufficiently long fixed signed integral full twists p_i. The actual original-source filling saddle is phi_i(t)+(pi i/p_i)(t_i-1)=0. By (18) this is exactly U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i, in the primitive disk marking. Unfilled main and auxiliary cusps stay parabolic. The actual nearby framed representation therefore satisfies every hypothesis of the general geometric completion theorem. It gives a smooth complete hyperbolic metric on the correctly marked filled link exterior. Using Re U_i=-p_i Re V_i at the saddle in (21) gives Vol(L_E(p))=2pi Re[phi(t)+(pi i/2) sum_i(t_i-1)^2/p_i]. (22) The already proved [whole original-source transfer](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) has exactly the right side of (22) as its full-sequence exponential rate. Hence it is the ACTUAL filled hyperbolic volume for every fixed retained robust factor and all independently sufficiently long signed integral fillings of any chosen subset. Its original normalization, normal terms, level parities and nonzero prefactor are those of that source theorem; geometry does not replace them with another state. This is a general branching LINK theorem. The [component obstruction](actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.md) still gives at least 2S+1 main components for S robust seeds after all even full-twist fillings. A knot extension needs different connectivity and its separately checked quantum source, such as retained odd twists. Audit: [exact peripheral and transport matrices](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation_results.json). The finite audit checks all nine generic prism identities over Q(A,B,C), all four turn identities, all four cylindrical closure identities, the three pointwise shaded-edge identities, and every main/auxiliary peripheral matrix check. No sampled phase values are used in this audit. In the original leaf coordinate, the two white slopes compose to the complete longitude translation -2(E+1), with multiplier (16).

title: Spectral and physical-color propagation through mixed Conway cores
status: Canonical Gaussian and all-color loss through mixed components
text: # Spectral and physical-color propagation through mixed Conway cores 31 October 2026. source theorem. This proves the sharp canonical spectral envelope and hereditary physical-color gap for an unflagged component, at its actual closed-probe action. Together with the proved decorated-character estimate, it gives a mutual induction through fixed mixed flagged/unflagged reduced source trees. All original full Hermite coordinates and finite targets are retained. No filled-volume statement or change of marked geometry is inferred here. The finite inputs are the [full-Hermite Newton and interpolation bounds](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), the [exact root-character Fourier theorem](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md), and the [decorated-character coefficient duality](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md). The separately proved [positive coefficient-cone theorem](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) supplies the original-action upper bound and strict high-sector gap. The [reduced-hub adapter](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) and [rigid-profile calculation](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) supply the actual component typing and additive classical constants. The [intrinsic component-probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md) identifies the same pressure and the proper effective-leaf parameter ranges. ## 1. Exact finite norms and the regular-index extension Let \(d=N-1\), \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), and use the original complete algebra, normalized Newton polynomials \(B_r=\widehat B_r\), marked functional \(\phi\), and turn \(T\). Write \(J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt\) and \(g(u)=J(2u)-4J(u)\). The norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal J}\) records all nodal values and first normals, with only the value at the odd simple node. Thus \[ T B_r=B_{d-r},\qquad \phi(B_rB_s)=\mathbf1_{r+s=d},\qquad D_j^\epsilon[E]=T(R^\epsilon L_jE),\qquad [B_r]D_j^\epsilon[E]=\phi(B_rR^\epsilon L_jE). \tag{1} \] Write \(w_{N,r}=B_r(-2)\) for \(r\le M\), and \(w_{N,r}=1\) for \(r>M\). All these weights are strictly positive. The existing finite estimates are uniform at both parities and all colors: \[ \|B_r\|_{\mathcal J}\le N^Cw_{N,r},\qquad \log w_{N,r}=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)\ (r\le M),\qquad |[B_r]D_j^\epsilon[E]|\le N^C\|E\|_{\mathcal J}w_{N,r}. \tag{2} \] Here the last \(w_{N,r}\) is only the coefficient envelope: it is not a spectral weight on the unreduced input. The canonical degree-\(<N\) representative \(H\) obeys \[ |H(2\cos(\theta+iy))|\le N^C e^{N|y|}\|H\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{3} \] The regular-index far-color estimate of the decorated-character theorem holds on every fixed compact interval \(I\subset(0,1/2)\), including intervals away from \(1/4\). Precisely, suppose an actual representative \(E_N\) has \[ |E_N(2\cos(\theta+iy))| \le \exp N\{c-c_E(\theta-\pi)^2+C_Ey^2+e_N\}, \quad 0\le\theta\le2\pi,\ |y|\le y_E, \quad c_E\ge0,\quad e_N\to0. \tag{4} \] The empty input \(1\) is allowed. For any fixed \(I\) and \(\delta>0\), there is \(\eta>0\) such that, uniformly in physical colors and \(\epsilon\in\{0,\pm1\}\), \[ r/N\in I,\quad N-j\ge\delta N \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |[B_r]D_j^\epsilon[E_N]| \le \exp N\{c+g(r/N)-\eta\}. \tag{5} \] Proof. The original low Newton polynomial has logarithmic strip action \[ b(u,\theta,y)=\int_0^u \log|2\cos(2\pi v)-2\cos(\theta+iy)|\,dv-2J(u). \tag{6} \] For \(u\in I\), circular rearrangement gives \(b(u,\theta,0)<g(u)\) away from \(\theta=\pi\), uniformly on a closed angular complement. Near \(\pi\), with \(z=\theta-\pi+iy\), its holomorphic action is \[ \mathcal B(u,z)=-J(1/2-u+z/(2\pi))-J(1/2-u-z/(2\pi))-2J(u), \qquad \mathcal B_{zz}(u,0)=-\tan(\pi u)/(2\pi)<0. \tag{7} \] The compact interval stays away from both index endpoints. The uniform logarithmic-product upper estimate therefore gives constants \(c_I>0\), \(C_I,y_I>0\) and \(e'_N\to0\) such that \[ |B_r(2\cos(\theta+iy))| \le w_{N,r}\exp N\{-c_I(\theta-\pi)^2+C_Iy^2+e'_N\}. \tag{8} \] This uses truncated-log Riemann upper bounds, so moving numerator zeros are retained. Multiplying (8) by (4) supplies the exact root-character Fourier theorem with input \(B_rE_N\) and reference \(c+g(r/N)\). Its missing folded winding, both joining currents, and the physical R normal are unchanged. That theorem proves (5). Fixed derivatives required there follow by Cauchy on radius \(1/N\) in a smaller fixed strip, with polynomial cost. For a fixed source the actual product representatives have degree \(O(N)\); no continuation of an arbitrary physical-color array is used. A preexisting norm loss in \(E_N\) is even simpler: (2) propagates it uniformly at every output index, both low and high. ## 2. The proved coefficient-cone input Let \(A\) be one fixed original unflagged component, with effective type-\(L\) inputs \(F_i\), and set \(Q=T(A)\). The inputs retain their actual Newton coefficient arrays, which may depend on arbitrarily many original physical colors. Assume their uniform envelopes are \[ |[B_r]F_i|\le \exp N(c_i+e_N) \begin{cases}w_{N,r},&r\le M,\\1,&r>M.\end{cases} \tag{9} \] The original Newton multiplication constants are nonnegative; a turn is exact index reversal. Taking coefficientwise absolute values therefore supplies a positive state majorant without deleting any finite state or normal. For the canonical output \(Q=\sum_rq_rB_r\), use the exact nonnegative probe \[ W_N=\sum_{r\le M}w_{N,r}B_r+\sum_{r>M}B_r, \qquad \sum_rw_{N,r}|q_r|\le\phi(W_N A^{\mathrm{abs}}). \tag{10} \] Here \(A^{\mathrm{abs}}\) means the positive circuit with absolute input arrays; it is not the absolute value of the output polynomial at a point. Equality holds with the nonnegative majorant output coefficients. In particular the original output reversal \(d-r\) is retained in the probe extraction. The [independently proved cone theorem](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) gives the following input. Set \[ \Omega=\sum_i c_i+\Phi_{C(hA)}, \tag{11} \] Here \(\Phi\) is the original complete action with unit type-\(L\) profiles \(g\); thus \(\Omega\) is the intrinsic action \(\Omega_Q\). In (10): * the sum of every sector with a high input index OR a high probe index is at most \(\exp N(\Omega-\gamma)\), for some \(\gamma>0\); * the all-low sector has the original positive action as a uniform closed upper envelope on its compact finite state polytope; * that upper-envelope action has one strict interior maximizer, of value \(\Omega\), whose probe index \(\beta\) and all effective input indices \(\alpha_i\) belong to \((0,1/2)\). Every fixed closed complement of that maximizer has a strict gap. The fixed finite number of sectors and polynomial number of original states are included in the uniform \(o(N)\) estimates. The effective modules need no independent physical alias identity: the cone proof uses (9), the exact positive gate and the earlier scalar supporting-plane certificates. It proves all these statements without assuming a signed mixed-tree source bound. In particular the upper-envelope action may have a strict maximizer even when the given input arrays vanish identically. ## 3. Canonical Gaussian localization at the actual pressure Using the theorem in §2, uniformly over all original physical colors, \[ \|Q_N\|_{\mathcal J}\le\exp N(\Omega+o(1)), \tag{12} \] and its canonical representative satisfies \[ |Q_N(2\cos(\theta+iy))| \le\exp N\{\Omega-c(\theta-\pi)^2+Cy^2+o(1)\} \quad (|y|\le y_0) \tag{13} \] with fixed \(c,C,y_0>0\). This is the sharp canonical spectral envelope at \(\Omega_Q\). It does not add the uniform bare-turn cost \(2G_0\). Proof. Equation (12) is (2) and (10). Choose a fixed compact interval \(I\) about \(\beta\) strictly inside \((0,1/2)\). Decompose the actual state expansion of the canonical output as \(Q=Q_{\mathrm{good}}+Q_{\mathrm{bad}}\), where \(Q_{\mathrm{good}}\) contains only all-low states with \(r/N\in I\). The cone theorem and strict compactness bound the weighted coefficient mass of \(Q_{\mathrm{bad}}\) by \(\exp N(\Omega-\gamma_1)\). Hence its full-jet norm has that same gap. It is itself a canonical polynomial, including its high-index part, so (3) gives \[ |Q_{\mathrm{bad}}(2\cos(\theta+iy))| \le\exp N\{\Omega-\gamma_1+|y|+o(1)\}. \tag{14} \] For the good part apply (8) to every output \(B_r\). The original positive probe already contains exactly its factor \(w_{N,r}\), so summing costs no additional exponential weight: \[ |Q_{\mathrm{good}}(2\cos(\theta+iy))| \le\exp N\{\Omega-c_I(\theta-\pi)^2+C_Iy^2+o(1)\}. \tag{15} \] Choose \(y_0<\gamma_1/4\) and \(c\le c_I\) with \(c\pi^2<\gamma_1/4\). Then (14) fits below (13) with a fixed residual gap; (15) proves the remaining part. Only canonical output polynomials enter (3), while input products may remain unreduced. Thus no representative-dependent ellipse estimate has been applied to an arbitrary quotient element. ## 4. Physical-color deficits of effective L modules Suppose an original physical color \(j\) lies in input module \(i\). It suffices that for every fixed compact interval \(I_i\) about its actual clean index \(\alpha_i\), and every fixed \(\delta>0\), the module has a local coefficient loss \[ N-j\ge\delta N,\quad r/N\in I_i \ \Longrightarrow\ |[B_r]F_i|\le \exp N\{c_i+g(r/N)-\eta_{i,\delta}\}, \qquad \eta_{i,\delta}>0. \tag{16} \] The unconditional envelope (9) remains in force at other indices. Then the actual unflagged output has a full-jet deficit \[ N-j\ge\delta N \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|Q_N\|_{\mathcal J}\le\exp N(\Omega-\eta'_{i,\delta}), \qquad \eta'_{i,\delta}>0. \tag{17} \] Indeed contaminated sectors already have a fixed cone gap. In the clean sector outside the \(\alpha_i\) window, the unique original maximizer gives another fixed gap. Inside that window, replacing just the one input coefficient envelope by (16) lowers every positive state weight by its fixed exponential factor. Equations (2),(10) finish the proof. No bound on the variance of an arbitrary spectator, no pointwise sign control, and no independent alias provenance for the effective module is used. There are finitely many original colors in a fixed component, so their positive margins can be minimized. For a genuine decorated module \(F_i=D_j^\epsilon[E]\), (9) follows from (2). Its own character satisfies (16) by the regular-index theorem (5). A physical-color deficit in \(E\) giving a full-jet loss yields (16), indeed a uniform all-index loss, directly by (2). Thus descendant losses pass through a complete unflagged component at its actual intrinsic action. The local index \(\alpha_i\) can be above \(1/4\); no quarter-only estimate is used. ## 5. Mutual induction through the actual reduced source The [finite reduced-hub decomposition](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) expresses each fixed mixed strict source, rooted at a flagged character, as alternating decorated type-\(L\) modules and unflagged components of the kind covered by §2. The entirely unflagged case already has the completed source estimates. Start with the empty input \(1\). At a decorated module, multiply the actual child canonical representatives; their full-jet rates add, their angular Gaussian envelopes multiply, and a child deficit supplies a norm loss. Equations (2),(5) give its low/high coefficient envelopes and all regular-index physical-color losses. At an unflagged component, (12),(13),(17) give the output full-jet rate, fresh Gaussian localization, and every descendant deficit. Iterate over the fixed finite source. The classical rigid-spine identity identifies its decorated constant with the sum of its satellites' actual \(\Omega\), so this induction never inserts an artificial character or rate budget. For a closing original character, the existing exact Fourier theorem now supplies its own far-color loss and the norm bounds supply all other color losses. The complementary-color expansion can then restore the original all-core packet, as in the assembly. Those final source and marked-filling adapters are not re-proved here. The analytic induction uses the separately proved coefficient-cone theorem and the original reduced-hub typing; it does not assume a prior full mixed-tree source theorem. This note does not promote a new global volume statement. All sources, physical signs, levels and finite targets remain original. The input and output constants may depend on the fixed finite component, and no claim is uniform over trees whose size grows with \(N\). ## scope and preservation The mutual induction uses exact normal-preserving probe weights and the canonical good/bad decomposition. It does not assume the signed mixed-source bound that it proves. An arbitrary input can vanish. The propagation argument does not give a lower coefficient rate.

title: Volume equality after combining the net twists of an ordered Conway tree
status: Ordered tangle reduction and sufficiently long net twists
text: # Volume equality after combining the net twists of an ordered Conway tree 31 October 2026. A written tangle construction may contain several twist boxes whose signed counts add to a much smaller number. Large individual counts therefore do not give a meaningful geometric condition until these combinations have been identified. This note gives an explicit normalization by isotopies of the ordered tangles. Its surviving weights are sums over disjoint sets of the original boxes. The new argument is topological. Once the resulting strict presentation has sufficiently long net twists, the [volume theorem for strict Conway trees](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) supplies the analytic limit. That theorem's estimates are an input here, not re-proved below. Every comparison of knot complements is made after filling the twist regions; no tangle isotopy is inferred from a scalar identity of quantum sources. ## 1. The construction and the conclusion A box contains a two-strand tangle with four specified endpoints. In the diagram plane, label them (0,1,2,3), starting at the lower left and proceeding through the lower right, upper right and upper left. Let $R^n$ be the standard integral two-strand braid with $n$ signed half-twists. Let $T$ be the specified quarter-turn of the box in its diagram plane. A basic piece is \[ h_i(n_i)=T(R^{n_i}). \tag{1} \] Each occurrence has its own label $i$, and each label occurs once. Products stack boxes in the stated order. Such compositions may close an additional circle inside a box; every such circle is retained. The cylindrical closure $C$ connects the two bottom endpoints to the corresponding top endpoints by the prescribed empty outside arcs. We first consider a fixed finite expression \[ \mathcal E=C(FG). \tag{2} \] Turns, ordered products and the pieces (1) are the only operations in $F,G$. There are $m\ge2$ original labels. No condition on the signs, sizes or nonvanishing of the integers is needed for the topological normalization. The distinction between a *formal piece* and its evaluated tangle is useful. A formal piece has a nonempty set $B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ attached to it and integer weight \[ W_B=\sum_{i\in B}n_i. \tag{3} \] It remains a named piece even if a particular assignment makes $W_B=0$. Keeping this record is a bookkeeping choice, not a claim that a zero-twist rational tangle is geometrically nondegenerate. Fix the original parity vector \[ e=(e_1,\ldots,e_m),\qquad n_i\equiv e_i\pmod2. \tag{4} \] **Ordered normalization theorem.** The ordered expression (2) determines a partition into nonempty disjoint sets \[ \{1,\ldots,m\}=B_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup B_s. \tag{5} \] For each parity vector (4), a deterministic finite procedure gives exactly one of the following two outputs. The partition (5) is the same for every parity vector; only the recorded orders of subexpressions can depend on the parities. * A fixed strict literal Conway presentation $\sigma_e=C(F_eG_e)$, with $s\ge2$ formal pieces of weights $W_{B_1},\ldots,W_{B_s}$. * The integral braid closure $C(R^{n_1+\cdots+n_m})$. For every integer assignment satisfying (4), the input filled link is ambient isotopic in the oriented $S^3$ to the indicated output link. The statement includes assignments with zero original weights, zero intermediate sums, or zero final sums. Every box order and every rotation introduced by the isotopy is recorded in the output. No reflection of $S^3$, arbitrary mutation, or permutation of unrelated tangle factors is used. Here *strict* is a property of the literal formal presentation. Give $h$ type $L$; a turn exchanges $L,H$ and fixes $A$. Products obey \[ LL,LA,AA\longmapsto A,\qquad HL,HA\longmapsto H, \qquad HH\longmapsto\varnothing, \tag{6} \] with either order allowed in each listed pair. The permitted closing pairs are $AA,AL,AH,LH$, in either order. In the angle calculation underlying the strict theorem, these three types correspond to output intervals $L:(0,1/2)$, $H:(1/2,1)$ and $A:(0,1)$. Here the table is used as an explicit finite test on the written construction. The strictness test makes no assertion about the complete geometry of a particular short or zero numerical filling. Geometry is supplied by the separate long-twist theorem when its numerical hypotheses hold. Let $K_N$ be the reduced enhanced Kashaev invariant with the normalization of [the strict-tree volume theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md). **Net-weight volume theorem.** For every fixed input (2) there is a finite $B(\mathcal E)$ with this property. Apply the ordered normalization at the parity vector of a fixed integer assignment. Suppose its output is strict, the filled diagram has exactly one link component, counting any circles already closed inside its subexpressions, and \[ |W_{B_j}|>B(\mathcal E)\quad(1\le j\le s). \tag{7} \] Then the input knot is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K_{\mathcal E}(\mathbf n))| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathcal E}(\mathbf n)). \tag{8} \] The expression and the entire integer assignment are fixed before $N$ tends to infinity. The limit includes both parities and composite levels. The bound is independent of the signs and relative magnitudes of the final sums. It does not require any lower bound on the original individual weights. If the input is already assumed to be a hyperbolic knot, the elementary output is impossible. Thus, for such an input, (7) is the only additional size condition in this theorem. Appendix A explains separately what can be done when final sums vanish; they are not silently removed in the theorem just stated. ## 2. Actual rotations and the twist-sliding isotopy Use spatial coordinates $(x,y,z)$, with $z$ the stack axis and $y$ perpendicular to the diagram plane. Three proper rotations of a box will occur: \[ \begin{aligned} \rho(x,y,z)&=(-x,-y,z),\\ \kappa(x,y,z)&=(x,-y,-z),\\ \tau(x,y,z)&=(-x,y,-z). \end{aligned} \tag{9} \] Their permutations of the four endpoints are, respectively, $(01)(23),(03)(12),(02)(13)$. The last rotation is the physical planar half-turn $T^2$. Direct composition of the spatial rotations gives \[ \begin{aligned} \rho(FG)&=\rho(F)\rho(G),& \kappa(FG)&=\kappa(G)\kappa(F),& \tau(FG)&=\tau(G)\tau(F),\\ \rho(TF)&=T\kappa(F),& \kappa(TF)&=T\rho(F),& \tau(TF)&=T\tau(F). \end{aligned} \tag{10} \] The standard integral braid $R^n$ is fixed by each of these half-turns. This can be seen in its usual symmetric spatial drawing. The reversal of a coordinate in the projected drawing is accompanied by reversal of depth, so the integer crossing sign is retained. Consequently every $h_i(n_i)$ is fixed as well. Pushing a rotation through an expression using (10) therefore changes specified product orders but leaves every leaf weight unchanged. It neither duplicates a leaf nor introduces a minus sign in (3). The twist-sliding move is \[ R^a F\simeq \rho^a(F)R^a. \tag{11} \] relative to the four outside endpoints. Here and below $\simeq$ denotes an actual unframed ambient isotopy, carrying any marked point and any ribbons that have been recorded. For completeness, put $F$ in a smaller round cylinder inside its box, leaving two empty strand collars above and below. In cylindrical coordinates $(r,\phi,z)$, choose cutoffs $\eta(r),\xi(z)$ equal to one on the smaller cylinder and zero near the outside boundary. The maps \[ (r,\phi,z)\longmapsto (r,\phi+t\pi\eta(r)\xi(z),z),\qquad 0\le t\le1, \tag{12} \] are homeomorphisms, and form an isotopy fixed on the outside boundary. At $t=1$, the inner tangle has undergone $\rho$. The two end collars have acquired inverse half-twist braids. Choosing the sign of the angle to agree with $R$, and applying the same construction to $\rho(F)$, proves (11) for $a=1$. The reverse isotopy proves $a=-1$, and iteration gives all integers. In particular (11) is valid at $a=0$. Internal closed components move with the inner cylinder and do not affect the argument. Adjacent integral boxes satisfy \[ R^aR^b\simeq R^{a+b}. \tag{13} \] Opposite crossings cancel by Reidemeister II; equal signs concatenate. Equations (11) and (13) allow integral boxes separated by arbitrary ordered factors to be collected at one end of their common stack. The factors that they cross acquire the displayed $\rho$ rotations. This is not the assertion that arbitrary two-tangles commute. All sliding decorations depend only on the parities of the moved powers. Since a moved power is always a sum of a specified set of original weights, its parity is determined by (4). ![The two local moves used in the normalization. Sliding a twist past a tangle retains the indicated rotation of that tangle; adjacent integral boxes combine by adding their signed weights. The outside endpoints and ordered attachments are retained.](../book/figures/net-twist-reduction.png) ## 3. The closing sphere and moving a turn through it The actual convention for $C(FG)$ joins \[ F_2\!\leftrightarrow G_1,\quad F_3\!\leftrightarrow G_0, \quad F_0\!\leftrightarrow G_3,\quad F_1\!\leftrightarrow G_2. \tag{14} \] The first two pairs are the stack interface and the last two are the cylindrical closing arcs. They are the empty planar arcs of the original construction, not a four-punctured-sphere gluing specified only by its point permutation. Straighten this collar while retaining its four planar sectors. In round coordinates on the two tangle balls the resulting sphere gluing is \[ h(x,y,z)=(x,y,-z),\qquad h(i)=3-i. \tag{15} \] This reflection is orientation reversing on the boundary sphere. It is different from the proper rotation $\kappa$, even though they have the same permutation of the four displayed endpoints. If $T_t$ is rotation in the diagram plane through the appropriate angle $t\pi/2$, then \[ hT_th^{-1}=T_t^{-1}. \tag{16} \] Apply $T_t$ to one ball and $T_t^{-1}$ to the other. Equation (16) says that the maps agree on their identified boundaries. They extend over the balls and give an ambient isotopy of the glued $S^3$, starting at the identity. At $t=1$, this proves \[ C((TF)G)\simeq C(F(TG)),\qquad C((TF)(TG))\simeq C(F\tau(G)). \tag{17} \] The actual half-turn in the second identity must be retained and expanded by (10). This argument would fail for a gluing collar with an additional boundary Dehn twist; (14) and its empty arcs are essential. We also use the cyclic move \[ C(FG)\simeq C(GF). \tag{18} \] Place the two stack intervals successively in the standard unknotted solid torus $D^2\times S^1$ and move the choice of cutting section past the first interval. Translation in the circle direction gives the required isotopy, carrying the marked point with it. It extends to the standard ambient $S^3$. This cyclic move does not permute factors in an open stack. Ordinary reassociation of a stack only changes the heights of its boxes and is also relative-boundary isotopy. ## 4. A terminating symbolic normalization The procedure never tests whether a weight is numerically zero. Every operation is performed on the formal labeled boxes. First shorten all chains of turns. Replace $T^2$ by the actual $\tau$, push $\tau$ through the remaining subtree by (10), and resolve it on the standard leaves. Flatten consecutive ordered products by associativity. At this stage the expression has maximal ordered stacks of at least two factors; their factors have one of the forms \[ h(B),\qquad Th(B)=R^{W_B},\qquad T(P), \tag{19} \] where $P$ is another maximal stack. A displayed integral box in (19) is called a *direct integral factor*. This is only a description of its position in the ordered stack. Choose a deepest maximal stack that has at least two direct integral factors. Collect all of them at its right end by (11), retaining the rotations of every intervening factor. Fuse them using (13). The resulting integral factor is named $Th(B)$, where $B$ is the union of their disjoint label sets. Its weight is the sum (3). Convert all $\rho,\kappa,\tau$ decorations back to ordered expressions with (10), shorten new turn chains and flatten new adjacent products. Repeat. A rotated direct integral factor remains direct integral. A rotated ordinary leaf remains an ordinary leaf. A rotated turned stack remains a turned stack, with perhaps reversed order inside it. Thus the procedure never hides an integral factor by pretending that a rotated arbitrary tangle is unchanged. Every fusion reduces the number of formal weighted leaves by at least one. It does so even when the new sum evaluates to zero: the new box remains a single recorded box. Between fusions, shortening turns removes unary vertices and flattening removes product vertices; propagating a rotation creates neither new leaves nor new turns. Thus this procedure terminates. When no further fusion is possible, each maximal stack has at most one direct integral factor. An induction from its deepest children proves: * Every factor other than a direct integral factor has type $L$ or $A$. * A maximal stack with no direct integral factor has type $A$. * A maximal stack with one direct integral factor has type $H$. Indeed the factors $T(P)$ have type $A$ when $P$ has type $A$, and type $L$ when $P$ has type $H$. Multiplying $L/A$ factors gives $A$; inserting the one $H$ factor gives $H$. Any ordered binary resolution of such a stack respects (6), since it cannot create a product of two $H$ factors. The lower bound of two factors in a maximal stack is used here. If all factors of a maximal stack have fused into one, that remaining factor is an integral box. Suppressing the now unary product vertex therefore cannot leave a lone arbitrary turned stack. This observation will also control the closing root. ## 5. The final root and the fixed output template Starting from (2), the root remains a product unless all of its factors fuse into one integral box. In the latter case the answer is the elementary closure, and the procedure stops. Otherwise let $k\ge2$ be the number of factors in the normalized maximal root stack. There is at most one direct integral factor. If $k\ge3$, the closing pair is strict. With no integral factor, expose one $L/A$ factor against the product of the remaining $k-1$ factors, which has type $A$. With one integral factor, use the cyclic move (18) to expose it against the product of the other factors. The closing pair is then $HA$. All orders inside the two factors remain the recorded ones. For $k=2$, every pair is permitted except $LL$. A type-$L$ factor is literally $T(U)$, where $U$ is either one integral box or a stack with exactly one direct integral factor. This includes the ordinary leaf $h(B)=T(R^{W_B})$. Therefore the remaining failure has the form \[ C((TU)(TV))\simeq C(U\tau(V)). \tag{20} \] Flattening the right-hand side exposes exactly two direct integral factors, one from each displayed part. Their other factors are of type $L$ or $A$. Collect and fuse the two integral factors using (11)–(13), with the precise rotations retained. This reduces the number of formal weighted leaves. Normalize again. The argument uses no nonzero-weight hypothesis. If the fused sum is zero, its named box $R^0=Th(0)$ remains in the stack. If there are other factors, it still occupies the one direct-integral position for the formal type test. If there are no other factors, the output is the elementary $C(R^0)$. We do not remove this box, expose a cap, or infer a nondegenerate geometric filling from it. Every return from (20) makes a fusion, so the entire root procedure terminates after at most $m-1$ fusions. When it stops, it has either a strict closing pair or the single integral closure. Every operation preserves or unions the disjoint label sets. They therefore give the partition (5); in the single-box case their union is all original labels. Fix a deterministic choice whenever several deepest stacks are available, for example the first in the current ordered traversal. The only numerical information used by the procedure is the parity in a rotation $\rho^{W_B}$. All these parities are fixed by (4). It follows inductively that the visited ordered trees, the unions of label sets, and the final expression are identical for every integer assignment in that parity class. Numerical zero tests, which would have invalidated this inference, have deliberately been omitted. ### Reading the net-weight groups without choosing parities The partition can be found before any integers or parities are assigned. The following finite graph is a record of the tangle operations, not a new knot projection or an identification of quantum tensors. Remove the final closing product in $C(FG)$ and join the output ends of $F$ and $G$. Represent each remaining product by a trivalent vertex. Put a bit on each edge equal to the number of quarter-turns on that edge modulo two. For this bookkeeping, the basic piece $h_i=T(R^{n_i})$ includes one turn on its leaf edge, and the end of that edge is the labeled integral box $R^{n_i}$. Contract every internal edge whose bit is zero. For $m\ge3$, this produces a tree of product junctions of valence at least three, with bit one on every internal edge. A leaf with bit zero is a direct integral leaf at its junction; a leaf with bit one is an ordinary turned leaf. At each junction $v$, put all its direct integral labels in a single block $I_v$, if this set is nonempty. Each ordinary leaf is a singleton block. These sets give (5). Replacing each nonempty $I_v$ by one integral leaf can lower a junction's valence. A newly two-valent junction necessarily has one fused integral leaf and one other incidence. If that incidence is an internal turn edge, suppress the junction and send its integral leaf through that turn: the neighboring junction receives an ordinary leaf. Its valence is unchanged, and it receives no new direct integral label. Thus no second round of unions is needed. There are two small endings. A two-valent junction whose other incidence is an ordinary leaf is the strict mixed two-leaf closure. A one-valent junction consists of a sole integral leaf and is the entire connected tree, giving the elementary closure. If two newly two-valent junctions are connected by a turn edge, suppressing either gives the same mixed two-leaf closure. For an input with just two leaves, let $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ be their turn bits relative to their integral boxes. Equal bits give the one block $\{1,2\}$; unequal bits give two singleton blocks and the strict mixed closure. Here is why this graph describes the actual normalization rather than only a source identity. The rotations (10) reverse some orders but preserve every edge's turn parity and every leaf label. Associativity joins product vertices across a zero-bit edge. Moving a turn through the closing sphere preserves the total bit on that unrooted edge. In the failed $LL$ root (20), the two displayed turns have total bit zero; the product regions on its two sides already belong to the same contracted junction. Their exposed integral factors therefore belong to one prescribed block. The physical slides can gather these factors in their ordered stack, with all rotations retained. One can also expose any chosen junction at the closing sphere: use associativity and cyclicity along the path to it, moving each encountered turn across the sphere by (17). This moves existing sibling tangles in their recorded order; it does not permute arbitrary satellites. Gather one junction's full block before proceeding to the next. A two-valent suppression is then precisely the closed-turn move carrying its integral box into an ordinary leaf at its neighbor. These are the actual isotopies already proved above. Consequently the graph's blocks are fixed independently of the original integer parities. The parities only choose the rotations of the surviving ordered subexpressions. The earlier termination proof still applies to this prescribed schedule. This proves the ordered normalization theorem. It is stronger than a normalization restricted by the nonvanishing of every intermediate subset sum. ## 6. Peripheral curves, marked evaluation and framing The isotopies above are orientation preserving on $S^3$. They carry the link itself, all its components, and any chosen marked point. In a knot case the output consequently has exactly the same component as the input. An endpoint calculation can test this, but it must retain both the pairing of the four exposed endpoints and the number of circles already closed inside each box. At a product, trace the joined strands, add each new closed circle to that count, and retain the new exposed pairing. A turn only permutes the exposed endpoints. At closure, add the cycles formed by the closing arcs. The total, not merely the exposed closing cycle, must be one. This test is fixed throughout a parity class. In particular, a knot output has no internal closed component in any proper subtree. Such a circle has no endpoint through which a later operation could connect it to the rest. The remaining arcs still have the four external endpoints and form at least one more component when the entire diagram is closed. An internal circle would therefore contradict the one-component hypothesis. This verifies the internal-component condition in the strict-template theorem. Restrict an isotopy to the complement of a small transported tubular neighborhood of the knot. This gives an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of exteriors. A meridian is transported because it bounds a disk meeting the core once. After orienting the knot and carrying that orientation, its preferred longitude is also transported: it is the primitive longitude of linking number zero. In particular, an unrecorded extra meridional power is not inserted into the preferred longitude by the normalization. The auxiliary crossing circles used to prove the long-filling theorem for the output are a separate matter. Several filled input twist boxes can become one output box. We do not assert that their unfilled augmented links are homeomorphic, identify their individual cusp meridians, or replace several independent circle colors by one color before filling. The comparison is between the already filled knots. The output strict template supplies its own actual auxiliary circles, primitive fillings and marked geometric calibration. There is also no need to equate two raw blackboard-framed tensor contractions. An ambient isotopy transports any ribbon, but the transported ribbon may differ by integral self-twists from the standard ribbon chosen when drawing the output. The invariant $K_N$ in (8) is the reduced knot invariant with its prescribed framing normalization, so isotopic unframed knots have the same $K_N$. The chosen point remains on the unique knot component; the reduced one-cut invariant does not depend on where that component is cut. Even when raw framed evaluations are used as intermediate expressions, the difference cannot affect the rate. At complete color $d=N-1$, the actual twist scalar is \[ \theta_d=q^{-d^2/2},\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N}, \qquad |\theta_d|=1. \tag{21} \] A change of integral ribbon framing is an integer power of this scalar, by the original normalization theorem. That integer may depend on the fixed diagram and fixed weights; its modulus is nevertheless one at every $N$. The separate modified-dimension convention, if used, has its original factor $\eta_N/N$, where $\eta_N=i^{N+3}$; the same convention must be used on both sides, and it is not created or removed by this normalization. Thus the finite topological invariant, or the absolute value of its specified raw normalization, is preserved. No derivative or confluent coefficient of an unfilled colored source has been discarded to reach this conclusion. Those source data are simply not the object being identified here. In particular, if $\sigma_e$ is the strict output and $\mathbf W=(W_{B_1},\ldots,W_{B_s})$, the normalized knot invariants satisfy the exact identity \[ K_N(K_{\mathcal E}(\mathbf n)) =K_N(K_{\sigma_e}(\mathbf W)),\qquad N\ge2. \tag{21a} \] This follows for the based reduced evaluation as well: cutting the unique knot component gives an intertwiner of the complete color. Its distinct weight spaces and the nonzero adjacent raising and lowering maps force that intertwiner to be scalar. Transporting the cut therefore introduces no new normalization. This argument is not permission to move a mark to a different component of a link. For hyperbolic outputs, transport the complete hyperbolic metric along the exterior homeomorphism. This produces a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the input exterior of exactly the same volume. Consequently the geometric identification in (8) is with the input knot complement, not with a comparison diagram's unrelated augmented volume. ## 7. The threshold and the elementary alternative For each original parity vector $e$, the procedure gives a single structural output. If it is strict, let $B_e$ be the threshold of that strict literal presentation from [the strict-tree volume theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md). There are at most $2^m$ such outputs. Taking the maximum of their finite thresholds, and increasing it to at least $2$, gives a finite $B(\mathcal E)$. If there are no strict outputs, take $B(\mathcal E)=2$; the non-elementary part of the theorem is then empty. For a fixed assignment with strict output and (7), that theorem constructs the smooth complete metric on the output knot exterior and proves its all-level invariant limit. Section 6 identifies both the knot invariant and that metric volume with the input. This proves (8). The output knot condition follows from the assumed one-component input, rather than from an assumed equality of source scalars. In the original filling convention, write \[ n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i,\qquad W_B=\epsilon_B-2p_B,\qquad p_B=\sum_{i\in B}p_i+ \frac{\epsilon_B-\sum_{i\in B}\epsilon_i}{2}, \tag{22} \] where $\epsilon_B\in\{0,1\}$ has the parity of the sum. The last correction is an integer fixed by the chosen parities. Thus the theorem concerns independently long *net* filling slopes, with a fixed parity offset. It is not a condition that all original $p_i$ be independently large. Within a final block, equal signs prevent cancellation; arbitrary independent signs do not. The integral output is the usual $(2,s)$ torus braid closure. It is a knot only when $s$ is odd. For $s=\pm1$ it is an unknot. For odd $|s|\ge3$, its torus decomposition gives the group \[ \langle a,b\mid a^2=b^{|s|}\rangle. \tag{23} \] The common element is central and has nonzero image in the abelianization, so it is not the identity. A finite-volume hyperbolic knot group has trivial center: a central element commutes with the rank-two peripheral parabolic group, hence is a parabolic translation fixing that cusp point; centrality would then force the whole group to fix that point, which is incompatible with a finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold. The cyclic unknot group is also not such a group. Thus an elementary output cannot be a hyperbolic knot. No quantum asymptotic for torus knots is needed to exclude it from the hyperbolic corollary. Finally, a condition on all written weights cannot replace (7). Inside any integral box, \[ R^a\simeq R^{a+2k}R^{-2k}. \tag{24} \] Both written magnitudes can be made arbitrarily large while their net is the fixed $a$, with the same original knot. This holds even when that knot is hyperbolic. It explains the net-weight hypothesis without providing a counterexample to any volume-conjecture equality. ## 8. A worked reduction, including a cancelling pair Write $h_j=T(R^{n_j})$. Consider the actual ordered diagram \[ K=C\!\left( R^{n_1}R^{n_2}h_3\, T(R^{n_4}R^{n_5}h_6) \right). \tag{25} \] It is an expression in the original pieces because $R^{n_i}=Th_i$. Each of its two displayed stacks contains a pair of direct integral boxes. Set \[ a=n_1+n_2,\qquad b=n_4+n_5. \tag{26} \] Adjacent braid cancellation alone gives \[ K\simeq C\!\left(R^a h_3 T(R^b h_6)\right). \tag{27} \] The four net blocks are $\{1,2\},\{3\},\{4,5\},\{6\}$. To check strictness, $R^b h_6$ has type $HL$, hence type $H$; its turn has type $L$. The product $h_3T(R^b h_6)$ has type $A$, and the outer pair is $HA$. Thus, if the actual closure is a knot, a fixed lower bound on $|a|,|b|,|n_3|,|n_6|$ gives the volume equality for this input diagram. The cancellation issue is visible without numerical examples. Taking $n_1=M+a$ and $n_2=-M$ makes both written twist counts arbitrarily large while leaving $a$ fixed. The theorem tests $a$, not the two written magnitudes. If $a=0$, formula (27) still holds, with its identity box retained. Removing that identity is an optional further reduction. The physical closing-sphere move and cyclicity give \[ \begin{aligned} C\!\left(h_3T(R^b h_6)\right) &\simeq C\!\left(R^{n_3}\tau(R^b h_6)\right)\\ &=C\!\left(R^{n_3}h_6R^b\right) \simeq C\!\left(R^{n_3+b}h_6\right). \end{aligned} \tag{28} \] The middle equality uses the actual reversal $\tau(R^b h_6)=h_6R^b$; it does not erase a half-turn on an arbitrary box. The final step moves the last integral box around the cylindrical closure and fuses adjacent braids. The surviving groups are now $\{3,4,5\}$ and $\{6\}$, with the zero block $\{1,2\}$ removed. If these two new weights are long and the closure is a knot, the strict two-leaf theorem applies. This is a further theorem on that zero wall, not a replacement for the fixed four-block normalization valid for all assignments. ## 9. The pointed quantum \(A\)-period gives the same limit The net-weight theorem also applies to the exact reconstruction from a recurrence operator. Fix a knot covered by (7), with all integer weights fixed, and write $V=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)$. The [pointed quantum \(A\)-period theorem](actual_conway_pointed_quantum_a_volume.md) supplies the following algebraic input for this same knot. Choose once and for all a genuine nonzero annihilator $P(q,M,\mathsf S)$ of its reduced ADO family, with $\mathsf S M=qM\mathsf S$. Here $\mathsf S$ is the recurrence shift, not the tangle quarter-turn. The marked meridian is $M=-qx$, where $x$ is the raw exponential color; the complete color at $q_N=e^{\pi i/N}$ has $M=1$. Fix the initial vector $c_0(q)$ from the finite window of ordinary color polynomials prescribed by the pointing theorem. These polynomials select the knot's solution of the recurrence. Let $r_N(q)$ be the corresponding companion-matrix row that propagates this initial vector to color $N$. For all sufficiently large levels, in particular beyond the fixed initial window, the pointed period is \[ \mathscr P_N(P,c_0) =\operatorname{CT}_{t=0} \bigl[r_N(q_N(1+t))c_0(q_N(1+t))\bigr] =K_N(K). \tag{29} \] The constant term is taken after multiplying the full Laurent germs, so poles of individual companion steps can cancel. The required number of derivatives of the fixed initial polynomials is bounded by the fixed operator, independently of $N$. These are exact reconstruction statements, not estimates derived from a companion-matrix norm. Combining (29) with (8) gives \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log|\mathscr P_N(P,c_0)|=V. \tag{30} \] There is a positive formulation as well. The pointed theorem constructs a positive determinant ratio $\mathscr G_N(P,j_0)$ from the Gram matrix of the finite recurrence system with its initial conditions. Its exact value is $\sum_{j=j_0}^{N}|C_j(q_N)|^2$, where $C_j$ is the ordinary reduced color-$j$ invariant of this knot. The terms with $j<N$ have a polynomial total bound for a fixed braid presentation, whereas the complete term is $|K_N(K)|^2$. Hence \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\pi}{N}\log\mathscr G_N(P,j_0)=V. \tag{31} \] For the full one-cut modified evaluation, keep the actual peripheral factor \[ d_N(M)=i^{N+3}\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}},\qquad d_N(1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}{N},\qquad \mathcal N_N(K;1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}{N}\mathscr P_N(P,c_0). \tag{32} \] The value at $M=1$ is the removable value of the whole function. It does not assign a new modified dimension to each fused twist box and does not change the exponential limit. An annihilator computed from the normalized presentation can differ from one computed from the input presentation. With each operator's own fixed initial data, (29) reconstructs the same knot invariant. Equality of these selected scalar periods does not assert equality of the operators, recurrence ideals, companion matrices or unpointed modules. Identifying a selected classical \(A\)-polynomial factor is also a separate problem. ## Appendix A. Optional reduction on a final zero-sum wall The main theorem keeps every box symbolically, including evaluated zero boxes. It therefore remains a valid isotopy statement on a wall $W_B=0$, but the longness condition (7) fails there. One must not apply the strict long-filling theorem to a zero net weight. There is a separate, explicit topological reduction available on such a wall. Set $D(E)=C(TE)$; this is the cap closure of $E$, joining its upper endpoints to each other and its lower endpoints to each other. A zero ordinary piece is $h(0)=T(R^0)$, the cup-cap tangle, not the through-identity tangle. A chosen leaf of any cylindrical product closure can be exposed as $C(h_iQ)$. To prove this, follow its path to the root. Associativity and (18) move each sibling into the other factor. When the path crosses a turn, use the first identity in (17) to transfer that turn to the other factor. Each step shortens the path to the chosen leaf, retains every sibling exactly once, and records every resulting order. If the chosen leaf is zero, this gives \[ C(h(0)Q)\simeq D(Q). \tag{33} \] There is no deletion of an extra closed component in (33). Its two arcs are precisely the two caps in $D(Q)$. A lone zero leaf is handled directly by the elementary closures below. At a cap-closed root the rules are \[ D(TF)=C(\tau F),\qquad D(FG)=D(F)\mathbin{\#}D(G). \tag{34} \] The second formula is a componentwise connected sum with specified components: the component containing the upper cap of $F$ is joined to the component containing the lower cap of $G$. An empty horizontal collar between the two boxes gives a sphere meeting the link exactly in its two interface arcs. Cutting along that sphere and capping the punctures gives exactly the two displayed cap closures. Thus (34) is a topological splitting along a two-punctured sphere; it is not a Conway mutation along a four-punctured sphere. Component labels and the mark must be retained. Run the symbolic normalization separately on each resulting cylindrical product factor. If a final weight is zero, apply (33) again. The elementary endings are \[ \begin{array}{ll} C(R^s)=\text{the }(2,s)\text{ braid closure},&D(R^s)=\text{an unknot},\\ C(h(s))=D(R^s),&D(h(s))=C(R^s). \end{array} \tag{35} \] The unknot assertion uses the end cap to remove the successive curls in the unframed diagram; their ribbon twists, if retained, are recorded separately. At $s=0$, $C(R^0)$ is the two-component unlink, not a discarded unit. This specialized procedure terminates. Fusion and numerical-zero removal each decrease the total number of live weighted leaves. Between these events, (34), turn shortening and stack flattening remove vertices from the finite expression forest. The context operation for (33) moves existing turns and siblings but does not copy them. The result is a finite tree of componentwise connected sums of strict factors with nonzero final weights, elementary braid closures and unknots. Surviving and deleted label blocks partition the original labels. Unlike the main symbolic output, the specialized decomposition can change when additional subset sums vanish. Its structure is fixed by the original parities and the zero/nonzero pattern of the finitely many subset sums. It remains a finite normalization, not a prime or JSJ decomposition. The source identity for a cap closure is not needed to prove this decomposition, and no invariant multiplicativity or volume additivity is being inferred merely from the notation in (34). A direct useful corollary requires no further classification: if this displayed decomposition has one strict knot factor whose net weights exceed its threshold, and all other factors are unknots, the input is isotopic to that strict factor and (8) follows. This corollary covers some final zero-sum walls. A general assertion about the quantum rate of several nontrivial factors, or about short remaining weights, is outside the result proved here. ## Appendix B. General root turns and cap closures For a more general input $C(E)$ that was not initially written as a product closure, or for an input $D(E)$, first process its outermost operations. A top turn changes $C(TF)$ to $D(F)$, while $D(TF)$ is the first formula in (34), retaining the physical half-turn. A cap-closed product splits by the second formula in (34). A cylindrical product is treated by Sections 4–5. A single integral or rational box is treated by (35). This preliminary root reduction is structural and does not test numerical weights. Its two-punctured spheres may already produce several factors even when no sum vanishes. In contrast, for the original input (2), the symbolic procedure never creates a cap closure: the root can become unary only by fusing all its direct integral factors into one integral box. That is why the main theorem has exactly one output for each parity rather than an unrecorded connected-sum collection. The same explicit one-strict-factor-and-unknots corollary applies to a general root. Without that condition, the decomposition itself is the topological conclusion. No claim of hyperbolicity is made for a connected sum of nontrivial factors. The later [arbitrary-closure theorem](actual_conway_arbitrary_closure_volume.md) proves that this condition follows from hyperbolicity of the input, provided every surviving strict factor has sufficiently long weights. It takes a finite maximum of thresholds over parity and subset-sum zero patterns, and uses the meridian centralizer to exclude two nontrivial factors. It also gives an explicit topological criterion for hyperbolicity under that longness hypothesis. The fixed-partition theorem above is unchanged. ## Inputs and scope The local geometric moves are given in full in Sections 2–3. Their original endpoint convention is the one in [the ordered stack and closing construction](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md), §2. The component labels in the cap splitting are those of [the cap-closure splitting theorem](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md), §2. The [reduced-junction source construction](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) has compatible graph bookkeeping. Its commutative Frobenius identities are not premises of this topological proof. The asymptotic input is the theorem for every strict literal presentation in [the strict-tree volume theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md). Its original marked representation and smooth completion are supplied by [the marked deformation and filling theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md); the present argument transports their already filled knot complement, rather than rebuilding the unfilled cusp dictionary after fusion. The unit framing statement is equation (2) of [the complete-color normalization theorem](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md). The result is therefore a genuine extension from strict presentations to presentations that *normalize* to a strict template with long net weights. It does not assert a threshold on unreduced individual twists, identify the distinct augmented exteriors before filling, equate independent circle colors, or prove the short-twist conjecture for all arborescent knots. Those distinctions are part of the theorem, not omissions from its normalization algorithm. The [literature comparison](positive_conway_literature_coverage.md#7-ordered-compositions-with-long-net-twists) records related primary statements and their knot, invariant and level restrictions. It is a coverage check; no external proof is used in the reduction above.

title: The actual signed color packet through the quarter-index boundary
text:
# The actual signed color packet through the quarter-index boundary 31 October 2026. local source theorem. This extends the LOCAL original mixed-color coefficient theorem across $x=1/4$. The selected branch has a source-fixed nonzero amplitude on a fixed joint complex neighborhood, with an exponentially small relative error on the physical Newton grid. Both transport channels and every conversion error are retained in the proof. No global alias estimate, full filled-volume theorem, or arbitrary-syntax geometric theorem is inferred here. The exact inputs are the [selected mixed-inner source](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md), §§1–6; the [analytic diagonalization lemma](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md), §§1–3; the [complete-color crossing proof](actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.md), §§2–3; and the [signed Conway packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md), §§1–5. The last complete-color crossing proof is used as a template, not as a mixed-color identification: the literal mixed finite sum and its recurrence are printed below. ## 1. Literal source, parameters, and result Put $d=N-1$, $M=\lfloor d/2floor$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, $Q=q^2$, $\kappa=q^{d^2/2}$, $F_j=(Q;Q)_j$, and $t=h/N$. For a physical integer $r>|\operatorname{Re}h|$ define the specified continuation of the original finite source by \[  egin{aligned} A_{h,r}&=\sum_{v=r}^{M}  rac{Q^{-vr}F_{2v}}{F_v\widehat F_N(v-h)\widehat F_N(v+h)F_{v-r}},\ D_{h,r}&= rac{Q^{-r^2}F_{2r}} {F_r\widehat F_N(r-h)\widehat F_N(r+h)},& U_{h,r}&= rac{A_{h,r}}{D_{h,r}}. \end{aligned}	ag{1} \] Here $\widehat F_N$ is exactly the [marked factorial completion](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) of the original source, not an independently selected solution. At physical integer $h\ge0$ with $h\le r$, (1) is the actual low-core coefficient normalization. For r in a fixed neighborhood of N/4, all shifted factorial arguments remain in regular compact substrips after choosing a small fixed complex t disk. In particular (1) is holomorphic and even in t. Its terminal source is $U_{h,M}=1$. Write $\varepsilon=1/N$, $x=r/N$, $Y=e^{2\pi i x}$, $H=e^{2\pi i t}$, and \[ \operatorname{den}(x)=(1-QY/H)(1-QYH). \] The exact recurrence, including the terminal wall, is \[  egin{aligned} U_r&=p(x,t,\varepsilon)U_{r+1}+q_c(x,t,\varepsilon)U_{r+2},\ p&=- rac{Q^{-2}Y^{-1}[(H+H^{-1})Q^3Y^2+Q+1]} {\operatorname{den}(x)},\ q_c&=- rac{Q^{-4}Y^{-2}(1-Q^2Y)(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y)} {\operatorname{den}(x)\operatorname{den}(x+\varepsilon)},\ q_c((M-1)/N,t,1/N)&=0,& U_{M-1}&=p((M-1)/N,t,1/N). \end{aligned}	ag{2} \] The wall zero is literal at both parities and for every complex t in this corridor. No $D_{h,M+1}$ is divided out. The exact Ward telescoping proof of (2) continues to this factorial completion because its lower endpoint is $v=r$. Thus the parameter extension in this note is attached to the original source itself. Set $p_0=p(x,t,0)$ and $q_0=q_c(x,t,0)$. Let $\mu_s,\mu_f$ be the two analytic roots of $\mu^2-p_0\mu-q_0=0$, labeled at $t=0$ by \[ \mu_s(x,0)=-Y^{-1},\qquad \mu_f(x,0)=Y^{-1}\cot^2(\pi x).	ag{3} \] The selected logarithm is continued from $\operatorname{Log}\mu_s(1/2,t)=0$. Define \[  egin{aligned} S(x,t)&=\int_x^{1/2}\operatorname{Log}\mu_s(u,t)\,du,\ 
u&= rac{p_1+q_1/\mu_s-q_0(\partial_x\mu_s)/\mu_s^2} {1+q_0/\mu_s^2},\ C(x,t)&=\sqrt{\mu_s(x,t)}\exp\!\left[ \int_x^{1/2} rac{
u(u,t)}{\mu_s(u,t)}\,duight]. \end{aligned}	ag{4} \] $p_1,q_1$ are the $\varepsilon$ derivatives of the exact rational functions (2) at zero. All marks in (4) continue the established high-index ones. **Local quarter theorem.** There exist fixed $h_0,t_0,a_0,c>0$ and, for every sufficiently large N of either parity, a zero-free holomorphic function $I_N(x,t)$ on \[ |\operatorname{Re}x-1/4|<h_0,\qquad |\operatorname{Im}x|<a_0,\qquad |t|<t_0, \] such that, uniformly for physical $r/N$ in the smaller real interval and all complex $|t|<t_0$, \[  egin{aligned} U_{Nt,r}&=I_N(r/N,t)[1+O(e^{-cN})],\ I_N(x,t)&=C(x,t)e^{NS(x,t)}[1+O(N^{-1})]. \end{aligned}	ag{5} \] The second estimate is uniform holomorphically on a fixed smaller joint domain. The constants and domains are independent of N. The first is a relative source-grid assertion and the second a complex asymptotic of the explicit interpolant; they are different estimates. ## 2. Uniform analytic diagonalization before choosing the crossing width Set $X_r=(U_r,U_{r+1})^{\mathsf T}$ and $T_N= egin{pmatrix}p&q_c\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. The exact direction is $X_r=T_N(x_r,t)X_{r+1}$, from high index to low index. First choose a fixed regular complex neighborhood of $x_0=1/4$ and a fixed sufficiently small t disk. At $(x_0,0)$, the roots in (3) are $i,-i$. On the closure of a small enough neighborhood they remain distinct, nonzero and bounded, with a bounded analytic eigenframe $V_0$ whose columns are $(\mu_s,1)^{\mathsf T}$ and $(\mu_f,1)^{\mathsf T}$. All denominators in (2) are bounded away from zero. The exact rational $T_N$ equals $T_0+O(1/N)$ uniformly there, including all t in the chosen disk. Apply the proved analytic diagonalization lemma with reversed shift direction. Its matrix commutator construction is holomorphic in the additional parameter t and uses only uniform coefficient, inverse-frame, nonzero-root and eigenvalue-gap bounds. It supplies a COMPUTABLE fixed $\sigma>0$, bounded holomorphic $V_N,V_N^{-1}$, and diagonal $D_N$ such that \[  egin{aligned} V_N(x,t)^{-1}T_N(x,t)V_N(x+\varepsilon,t)&=D_N(x,t)+R_N(x,t),\ V_N&=V_0+O(\varepsilon),\ D_N&=\operatorname{diag}(\mu_s,\mu_f)+O(\varepsilon),\ \|R_N\|&\le C e^{-\sigma N}. \end{aligned}	ag{6} \] Each diagonal entry is nonzero. Its first component in the selected column is also nonzero. These assertions hold on a fixed smaller complex neighborhood. All bounds are uniform in the small t disk. The diagonalization is performed BEFORE shortening the crossing window; $\sigma$ therefore does not shrink with that subsequently chosen window. The lemma's construction can be taken even in t: its initial rational coefficients, labeled roots, and every commutator correction are even. No ratio of physical source values, and no putative already-selected solution, is used to construct $V_N$ or $D_N$. ## 3. A negative cumulative competitor action survives complex colors Choose $\delta>0$ small and set $h=\delta/4$. Here this width $h$ is distinct from the color index in (1). Let the high anchor be the actual integer $b_N=\lceil N(x_0+2\delta)ceil$ and $x_b=b_N/N$. We work with targets $|x-x_0|\le h$. The entire interval $[x_0-h,x_b]$ lies in the regular domain. At $t=0$, the relative log modulus is \[ f(x)=\log|\mu_f/\mu_s|=2\log\cot(\pi x),\qquad f(x_0)=0,\qquad f'(x)=- rac{4\pi}{\sin(2\pi x)}.	ag{7} \] Shorten $\delta$ so $-8\pi\le f'\le-4\pi$. If $x\le x_0$, the possible positive contribution from $x$ to $x_0$ is at most $4\pi h^2$, whereas the negative contribution from $x_0$ to $x_0+2\delta$ is at most $-8\pi\delta^2$. If $x\ge x_0$, integrate directly from $x$ to $x_0+2\delta$. Consequently, uniformly in the whole target interval, \[ \int_x^{x_b}\log\left| rac{\mu_f(u,0)}{\mu_s(u,0)}ight|du \le-7\pi\delta^2+O(N^{-1}).	ag{8} \] All partial relative actions along the anchor-to-target interval have absolute value at most $C_0\delta^2+O(N^{-1})$, for a fixed explicit coefficient bound $C_0$; for example $C_0=40\pi$ suffices here. On the fixed regular domain an analytic logarithm of $\mu_f/\mu_s$ exists. Its even parameter dependence gives \[ \left|\operatorname{Log}(\mu_f/\mu_s)(x,t) -\operatorname{Log}(\mu_f/\mu_s)(x,0)ight| \le C_1|t|^2.	ag{9} \] This is a complex-parameter estimate; taking real parts controls actual moduli for every complex $t$. Choose $\delta$ first with $C_0\delta^2<\sigma/8$. Then choose $t_0$ smaller so $3C_1\delta t_0^2<\pi\delta^2$. Equations (8)–(9), ordinary uniform Riemann estimates, and $D_N=\mu+O(1/N)$ give \[  egin{aligned} |G_f(r)/G_s(r)|&\le C e^{-6\pi\delta^2N},\ \max_{\mathrm{partial}}\left|\log|G_f/G_s|ight| &\le N\sigma/4+O(1). \end{aligned}	ag{10} \] for target r and along the full propagation interval, respectively. Here $G_i(r)=\prod_{j=r}^{b_N-1}d_i(x_j,t)$ and $G_i(b_N)=1$. The two statements have different domains: the strict negative bound is for targets near quarter; the width bound covers ALL partial products. The $O(1)$ rounding and diagonal-correction costs are uniform. Thus the fast branch may locally exceed the selected branch below quarter, but its ACCUMULATED action from the actual high anchor is still strictly smaller on this sufficiently short target interval. This is the extra information not supplied by eigenvalue separation. ## 4. Exact source anchor, both channels, and all conversion errors At $x_b$, the established high-index theorem applies uniformly for all complex $|t|<t_0$, since $x_b$ is a fixed positive distance above quarter. It gives the actual source vector and the ratio to its next coordinate. In the frame (6), write \[ V_N(x_b,t)^{-1}X_{b_N} = egin{pmatrix}a_{s,N}(t)\a_{f,N}(t)\end{pmatrix}. \] Its exact entries are defined by the original finite sums (1).
