The high theorem and $V_N=V_0+O(1/N)$ imply \[  egin{aligned} a_{s,N}(t)&= rac{C(x_b,t)}{\mu_s(x_b,t)} e^{NS(x_b,t)}[1+O(N^{-1})],\ |a_{f,N}/a_{s,N}|&\le C/N. \end{aligned}	ag{11} \] In particular $a_{s,N}$ is holomorphic and zero-free after shrinking the fixed disk, uniformly for large N. Neither coefficient is set to zero. The uniform relative form in (11), not a bound at $t=0$ alone, is used. For completeness the exact interaction calculation is as follows. Write $Y_r=V_N(x_r,t)^{-1}X_r$ and $G_r=\operatorname{diag}(G_s(r),G_f(r))$. Then \[ G_r^{-1}Y_r=(I+E_r)G_{r+1}^{-1}Y_{r+1},\qquad E_r=G_r^{-1}R_N(x_r,t)G_{r+1}. \] By the partial width bound (10), \[ \|E_r\|\le C e^{-3\sigma N/4},\qquad \prod_r(I+E_r)=I+O(Ne^{-3\sigma N/4}).	ag{12} \] The $1/d_i$ factors are uniformly bounded. Factoring $a_{s,N}$ and using (10)–(12) in the first component gives, on the target grid, \[ U_r=a_{s,N}(t)[V_N(x_r,t)]_{1,s}G_s(r) [1+O(e^{-c_1N})].	ag{13} \] The direct fast source component is bounded by $N^{-1}$ times its strict negative relative action; its converted contributions are bounded by (12) with the full calibrated action width. Formula (13) therefore does not discard a Stokes multiplier, reset any action, or suppose that an $O(1/N)$ local error remains small under an uncontrolled long product. ## 5. Exponentially accurate interpolation of the selected product Let $l_N(x,t)=\operatorname{Log}d_s(x,t)$ on the fixed regular tube, with the mark continuing $\operatorname{Log}\mu_s$. The functions $l_N$ and all their Cauchy derivative bounds are uniform in $N,t$ on a slightly smaller fixed tube. For physical $r\le b_N$ let $E_N^s(x,t)$ be the optimally truncated analytic Euler–Maclaurin expression for \[ \sum_{j=r}^{b_N-1}l_N(j/N,t): \] \[  egin{aligned} E_N^s(x,t)&=N\int_x^{x_b}l_N(u,t)\,du + rac{l_N(x,t)-l_N(x_b,t)}2\ &\quad+\sum_{k=1}^{K} rac{B_{2k}}{(2k)!}N^{1-2k} \left[\partial_x^{2k-1}l_N(x_b,t)-\partial_x^{2k-1}l_N(x,t)ight]. \end{aligned}	ag{14} \] Choose $K=\lfloor c_2Nfloor$ with a sufficiently small fixed $c_2>0$. On the fixed tube, Cauchy gives $|l_N^{(k)}|\le Bk!a^{-k}$. The usual analytic remainder bound $CN[K/(\pi aN)]^{2K}$ is therefore exponentially small, uniformly for the physical grid and complex t. This gives \[ I_N(x,t)=a_{s,N}(t)[V_N(x,t)]_{1,s}e^{E_N^s(x,t)}.	ag{15} \] All three factors are holomorphic and zero-free on the fixed smaller domain. The anchor is an explicitly known finite source coefficient, not an unknown closed invariant. Equations (13)–(15) prove the first assertion of (5). There is no need to interpolate or estimate a moving support cutoff: r and the anchor remain physical integers and the factorial continuation in t was already fixed in (1). ## 6. The leading action and amplitude are the original selected ones The selected vector from (6), propagated only with $d_s$, satisfies the original scalar recurrence up to an exponentially small holomorphic relative defect. One can see this from both rows of the exact matrix identity (6), since its first component and $d_s$ are nonzero. Its scalar one-step ratio is \[ v_{s,N}(x,t)=d_s(x,t)  rac{[V_N(x,t)]_{1,s}}{[V_N(x+\varepsilon,t)]_{1,s}}. \] It satisfies $v_{s,N}=\mu_s+O(\varepsilon)$, with corresponding derivative bounds, and its Riccati residual is exponentially small. Expanding that residual to first order yields \[ v_{s,N}=\mu_s+\varepsilon
u+O(\varepsilon^2).	ag{16} \] with EXACTLY $
u$ from (4). The denominator $1+q_0/\mu_s^2=1-\mu_f/\mu_s$ is bounded away from zero, even at quarter; there it equals two at $t=0$. To justify the expansion without a formal series assumption, Cauchy bounds give derivatives of $v_{s,N}-\mu_s$ of order $O(\varepsilon)$; substituting $v_{s,N}=\mu_s+O(\varepsilon)$ in the exact Riccati defect then solves its first-order coefficient with $O(\varepsilon^2)$ remainder by this nonzero denominator. The eigenvector ratios telescope. Euler–Maclaurin applied to (16) therefore gives the selected first component between x and $x_b$ as \[ \sqrt{ rac{\mu_s(x,t)}{\mu_s(x_b,t)}} \exp\!\left[N\int_x^{x_b}\operatorname{Log}\mu_s(u,t)\,du +\int_x^{x_b} rac{
u(u,t)}{\mu_s(u,t)}\,duight] [1+O(N^{-1})].	ag{17} \] This is a holomorphic estimate, not an extrapolation from its real grid values. Explicitly, writing $v_1=[V_N]_{1,s}=\mu_s+O(\varepsilon)$, Cauchy also gives $v_1'=\mu_s'+O(\varepsilon)$, and (16) implies \[ d_s=\mu_s+\varepsilon(
u+\partial_x\mu_s)+O(\varepsilon^2). \] Insert this expansion directly into (14). The additional integral of $\mu_s'/\mu_s$ is $\operatorname{Log}\mu_s(x_b)-\operatorname{Log}\mu_s(x)$; together with the half-endpoint term and $v_1(x)/v_1(x_b)$, it gives the square root in (17). The remaining Bernoulli terms and integrated $O(\varepsilon^2)$ error are uniformly $O(1/N)$ on the smaller complex tube. Thus no uniqueness principle on a finite grid is being used to obtain complex uniformity. At the anchor, $a_{s,N}[V_N]_{1,s}$ equals $C(x_b,t)e^{NS(x_b,t)}[1+O(N^{-1})]$ by (11). Multiplying (17) proves the second assertion of (5), with the original C and S in (4), uniformly holomorphically on a smaller fixed tube. The endpoint normalization at $1/2$ and BOTH parity marks came from the high-source theorem; no new connection or endpoint constant appears at quarter. At $t=0$ this recovers, on both sides of quarter, \[ S(x,0)=i\pi(1/2-x)^2,\qquad C(x,0)=\sqrt{\sin(\pi x)}e^{-3\pi i(1/2-x)/2}.	ag{18} \] The exponential grid residual and the inverse-N leading expansion remain separate throughout this proof. ## 7. Original signed Conway coefficients and the local wire packet Keep the exact finite coefficients $d_N^\epsilon(r,t)$, the removed phase $e^{-i\epsilon\pi d/4}$, and the continuous chirp of [signed Conway packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md), §§1–3. For the negative sign, replace only its high-source interpolation $e^{E_N}$ by $I_N$ in (15). Here $\epsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}$ is the physical half-twist sign, distinct from the step size $\varepsilon=1/N$: \[  egin{aligned} A_N^{\mathrm{hol}}(x,t)&=  rac{N^2G_N(2Nx)}{G_N(Nx)^2G_N(N(x-t))G_N(N(x+t))},\ P_N(x)&= rac{\kappa^{-1}e^{i\pi d/4}} {e^{-i\pi Nx+i\pi Nx(Nx+1)/N}},\ I_N^-(x,t)&=A_N^{\mathrm{hol}}(x,t)P_N(x)I_N(x,t). \end{aligned}	ag{19} \] These are the SAME canonical factorial and chirp marks. Their exact source identity uses $q^{h^2}D_{h,r}/D_{0,r}=G_N(r)^2/[G_N(r-h)G_N(r+h)]$; hence no quadratic color factor is lost. At physical r, (19) agrees with the normalized literal negative core coefficient up to the relative exponential residual in (5). For the positive sign use its Schwarz reflection in x,t; for the pure sign use $A_N^{\mathrm{hol}}$ itself. All are even holomorphic in t. The leading formulas are unchanged: \[  egin{aligned} I_N^\epsilon(x,t)&=N^{1/2}b_\epsilon(x,t) e^{Nf_\epsilon(x,t)}[1+O(N^{-1})],\ f_0(x,t)&=g(x,t),\ f_-(x,t)&=g(x,t)+S(x,t)-S(x,0),\ f_+(x,t)&=\overline{f_-(\overline x,\overline t)}. \end{aligned}	ag{20} \] where $g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t)$. The old explicit $b_\epsilon$ are nonzero and analytically extend through $x=1/4$. In particular \[  egin{aligned}  rac{b_\epsilon(x,0)}{b_0(x,0)} &=\sqrt{\sin(\pi x)}e^{-i\epsilon\pi x/2}, &&\epsilon\in\{-1,1\},\ \partial_t^2 f_\epsilon(x,0) &=- rac{2\pi\cot(\pi x)}{1-\epsilon i\cot(\pi x)}, &&\epsilon\in\{0,-1,1\}. \end{aligned}	ag{21} \] The implicit shear identity for $f_\epsilon$ continues across quarter by the identity theorem on the common connected neighborhood. Its derivative $1-\epsilon i\cot(\pi x)$ remains nonzero there. This is identification of the already selected source action, not an inference from its Hessian. Consequently the existing finite tensor-cotangent/local Gaussian proof extends to any FIXED strict wire window whose leaf coordinates lie in the union of this quarter neighborhood and the previously proved high intervals, provided its original pure wire Hessian is negative definite and its primitive lattice and support are retained. Bound the exponential coefficient residuals absolutely before the complex wire saddle, then shrink the fixed color polydisk so they remain below the selected action. The exact finite window still has $N^{3/2}$ amplitude, all original affine offsets, the external $\eta_N$ phase and the diagonal color Hessian (21). The shifted critical wire stays in the fixed interpolation tubes. This conditional LOCAL consequence applies to the strict quarter leaves of the test family $C(hT(h^s))$ once its already identified strict lattice window is supplied. It is not by itself a whole-source or filling claim. ## 8. Scope, parameter order, and remaining obligations The order of constants is essential: fix the rational analytic recurrence domain and its uniform diagonalization barrier; choose a much shorter anchor-to-target interval; retain its negative cumulative relative action; then choose a small complex-color disk. Choose the EM tube and truncation on fixed domains. Finally let N tend to infinity through both parities. All target and color radii are fixed positive numbers, not shrinking with N. Neither root separation nor an $O(1/N)$ local transport approximation would prove (5). Equations (8)–(13) explicitly control the actual other source channel and exponentially small mode conversions with their accumulated actions. The extension only crosses a short regular modulus boundary; it does not continue the selected branch arbitrarily far below quarter. No omitted low-core indices, alias sectors, physical-color complements, root-leaf geometry or global boundary currents have been set to zero. Global source gaps and the actual marked peripheral geometry remain the separate hypotheses of the long-filling transfer theorem. This note gives a local analytical input that was previously unavailable, with its exact source normalization preserved. ## scope and preservation The quarter-index packet is local. It does not supply a global source gap or a new filling-volume theorem.

title: Reduced Frobenius hubs, strict support, and a positive complete-character kernel
text:
# Reduced Frobenius hubs, strict support, and a positive complete-character kernel 31 October 2026. source theorem. The calculations use the full repeated-root algebra, with all independent physical leaf colors and first normal coefficients. They give a sharp strictness criterion and an exact recursive source interface. No tangle isotopy is inferred from an algebraic rerooting. The flag-free case reduces to source estimates already proved for the completed grammar and isolated three-leaf closure. The case with one flagged leaf at every hub is covered by the companion [decorated-character spectral theorem](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md). Mixed flagged and unflagged hubs require a further analytic operation, specified below. The later [positive probe bound](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) and [spectral propagation theorem](actual_conway_mixed_core_spectral_propagation.md) provide it, completing the [strict-tree volume theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md). This note proves the finite algebra and support statements used in that argument. ## 1. Source conventions and the exact local tensor Let \(d=N-1\), \(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\), and \(e_r=\widehat B_r\), \(0\le r\le d\). Use the physical turn \(T\), marked functional \(\phi\), and independent leaves \[ h_i=T(p_i),\qquad p_i=R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i},\qquad 1\le j_i\le N,\quad \epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}. \] No two colors or signs are identified. The proved source rules are \[  egin{gathered} Te_r=e_{d-r},\qquad \phi(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d},\ e_i e_j=\sum_{r=\max(i,j)}^{i+j}\mu_{i,j,r}e_r,\qquad \mu_{i,j,r}=  rac{s_{i+j}s_r}{s_i s_j s_{r-i}s_{r-j}s_{i+j-r}}>0 \quad(i+j\le d),\ e_i e_j=0\quad(i+j>d),\qquad s_r=\prod_{t=1}^r2\sin rac{\pi t}{N},\quad s_0=1. \end{gathered}	ag{1} \] These are the [exact source compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), §1, and the underlying [positive Newton multiplication theorem](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md). Their proof is polynomial with multiplicities, so first normal coefficients are retained. The symmetric trivalent tensor \(C(i,j,k)=\phi(e_i e_j e_k)\) is the exact factorial tensor in the [isolated three-leaf source](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md), §1. Its support is \[ i+j,\ i+k,\ j+k\le d,\qquad i+j+k\ge d. 	ag{2} \] Every supported entry is positive. In scaled strict coordinates its domain is pairwise sums less than one and total sum greater than one. Thus a product gate with inputs \(x,y\) and output \(z\) is this tensor with legs \(x,y,1-z\): \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. 	ag{3} \] This identifies strict support without relying on an equality between signed scalar sums. Write \(\mathbf J_{ij}=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}\), so \(\mathbf J^{-1}=\mathbf J\). Internal propagation with no turn is \(\mathbf J\); an inserted turn gives \(\mathbf JT=I\). A leaf with edge parity \(\sigma\) supplies \(T^\sigma h_i\). These conventions follow by raising the output index of \(C\) with \(\mathbf J\) in (1). ## 2. An exact product-hub support lemma For \(n\) fixed basis inputs \(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_n}\), the product is zero unless \[ i_p+i_q\le d\qquad(p
e q). 	ag{4} \] If (4) holds, its positive support is exactly \[ \left[\max_p i_p,\ \min\!\left(d,\sum_p i_pight)ight]\cap\mathbb Z. 	ag{5} \] For \(n=1\) this is its singleton support. Necessity of (4) follows by associating a violating pair first. For sufficiency, use any binary parenthesization. Each child has the interval (5) inductively. The two lower endpoints have sum at most \(d\), by (4); the exact interval compiler therefore gives (5) for the parent. Every coefficient asserted positive has a positive summand. This proves the result for every grouping, not merely after choosing a favorable grouping. Consequently the \(k\)-valent tensor \(C_k(\mathbf i)=\phi(\prod_p e_{i_p})\) has positive support exactly \[ \sum_p i_p\ge d,\qquad i_p+i_q\le d\quad(p
e q). 	ag{6} \] For \(k=2\) this is \(i_1+i_2=d\); for \(k\ge3\) it is a nontrivial positive tensor. Its value is defined by (1), including all scalar factors, not by a new normalization. There is a corresponding strict statement with fixed external labels \(0<x_p<1\). A product of \(n\ge2\) inputs admits strict intermediate gates with prescribed output \(z\) precisely when \[ x_p+x_q<1\quad(p
e q),\qquad \max_p x_p<z<\min\!\left(1,\sum_p x_pight). 	ag{7} \] This holds for every binary parenthesization. Necessity follows by following any two leaves to their first common gate: its two input labels are at least those leaf labels and have sum less than one. The output is strictly larger than each input and strictly smaller than their sum, which also gives the remaining inequalities. For constructive sufficiency, for a child set \(S\) put \[ L_S=\max_{p\in S}x_p,\qquad U_S=\min\!\left(1,\sum_{p\in S}x_pight). \] A nonsingleton child can take every value in \((L_S,U_S)\); a singleton takes its fixed value. At a parent with target \(z\), restrict both child values below \(z\). Their available sum has lower endpoint \(L_1+L_2<1\) and upper endpoint \(\min(U_1,z)+\min(U_2,z)>z\). Both child sets are nonempty because \(z>L_i\). Thus choose a sum strictly between \(z\) and one. If both children are singletons, their single sum already lies there. This gives the strict parent gate and then strict children by induction. A closed \(k\)-hub, \(k\ge3\), in any resolution into trivalent product tensors, admits strict internal wires precisely when \[ \sum_p x_p>1,\qquad x_p+x_q<1\quad(p
e q). 	ag{8} \] Split at any root pairing. The two child intervals from (7), with singleton exceptions, contain values summing to one: their lower endpoint sum is less than one, and their upper endpoint sum is greater than one. This proves sufficiency. Necessity follows from the same gate inequalities and the final complementary relation. For \(k=2\) the root pairing is the equality \(x_1+x_2=1\), with no retained gate; that exception remains separate. In particular, collapsing or resolving an internal edge with no turn preserves strict feasibility at the same external labels. This is the strict-support justification that an appeal to associativity alone would not supply. ## 3. The reduced unrooted source and its sharp strictness criterion Start with a literal cylindrical expression \(C(FG)\) with \(H\ge3\) original leaves. Contract unary turn chains modulo \(T^2=I\) and suppress the degree-two closing vertex. At each multiplication use the tensor and metric conventions of §1. This gives an unrooted trivalent tree with independently labelled physical leaves and turn parities on its edges. Collapse every internal edge of parity zero. Adjacent symmetric tensors contract through \(\mathbf J\) to \(C_k\), by Frobenius associativity. The resulting tree has product hubs of valence at least three, all hub-to-hub edges of parity one, and a flag \(\sigma_i\) on each leaf edge: \[ \sigma_i=0:\ h_i=T(p_i),\qquad \sigma_i=1:\ Th_i=p_i. 	ag{9} \] The reduced tree is unique up to isomorphism with the original leaf labels retained: it is obtained by contracting the components of the zero-parity internal edges. This uniqueness is only for the named algebraic moves, not a classification modulo every identity of \(\mathcal H_N\) or every tangle isotopy. **Strict-hub theorem.** The closed expression has a strict reduced state if and only if each reduced hub is incident to at most one flagged leaf. Necessity follows from (8). Two flagged original leaves have leg labels \(1-a_i>1/2\) and \(1-a_j>1/2\), violating their pair inequality. The hub resolution lemma makes this argument independent of the initial parenthesization. For sufficiency, first suppose there is a hub-to-hub edge and root there. Looking toward a parent edge, each hub has at least two other incident branches. A leaf branch has type \(L=(0,1/2)\) if unflagged and \(H=(1/2,1)\) if flagged. Inductively, a child hub has product output of type \(H\) if it contains one flagged leaf, and \(A=(0,1)\) otherwise: incoming hub branches have types \(T(H)=L\) or \(T(A)=A\), and cannot supply an \(H\) input. At most one \(H\) input is allowed, and the exact strict table gives precisely these \(H/A\) outputs. Across the root \(T\) edge the possible closed pairs are \[ A/A,\qquad A/L,\qquad H/A,\qquad H/L, 	ag{10} \] all strict. These are the original full type intervals, not selected pointwise labels. For a single hub, no flag means a product of \(H\ge3\) leaves of type \(L\); exposing one leaf gives the strict pair \(L/A\). With one flag expose that leaf, giving \(H/A\). This proves sufficiency. The local resolution lemma transports the resulting strict state back to the original syntax. With two original leaves there is no hub; the only datum is the edge turn parity. The strict case has parity one and closed pair \(L/H\). This two-leaf case is separate from the \(H\ge3\) packet and from knot-component claims. ## 4. Exact recursive interface and the extent of grammar reduction Choose a flagged leaf at a root hub when one is present. For any other hub \(v\), let \(Q_v\) be its outgoing coupon after the edge \(T\) toward its parent. Its exact recursion is \[ Q_v=  egin{cases} T\!\left(p_{i(v)}\prod_w Q_w\prod_l h_light), &	ext{if \(v\) has a flagged leaf \(i(v)\)},\ T\!\left(\prod_w Q_w\prod_l h_light), &	ext{if \(v\) has no flagged leaf}. \end{cases} 	ag{11} \] Products contain all other incident branches, with original labels. They have at least one factor in the first case and at least two in the second. The final scalar at the chosen flagged root is \[ Z_N=\phi\!\left(p_0\prod_w Q_w\prod_l h_light). 	ag{12} \] These are exact identities for arbitrary independent colors and half signs, including all normal directions. The child messages have type \(L\) in the first case of (11) and \(A\) in the second. These two operators, rather than arbitrary matrices or a semisimple quotient, are the compositional spectral interface. The recursive notation may initially give a closing character with only one decorated child. This is not an extra \(H\ge3\) boundary case. Writing \(D_i[E]=T(p_iE)\), self-adjointness gives exactly \[ \phi(p_0D_1[E])=\phi((Tp_0)p_1E)=\phi(h_0p_1E). 	ag{13} \] If \(E=1\), there are exactly two physical leaves and no hub. If \(E\) is a nonempty product of recursive child coupons, the right side is rooted at character \(p_1\), with ordinary satellite \(h_0\) and all factors of \(E\). There are at least two root satellite factors and hence valence at least three. Every physical color and half sign is retained. The turn moves across the exposed pairing, not through a product. If there are no flagged leaves, root at any internal edge, or split a single hub into two groups of at least two leaves. Both open sides belong to \[ E\ ::=\ hh\ \mid\ T(E)\ \mid\ EE\ \mid\ hE\ \mid\ Eh. 	ag{14} \] Thus \(H\ge4\) reduces as a full source to the [completed/completed-root grammar](actual_arborescent_single_leaf_long_twist_volume.md); \(H=3\) is the [isolated \(C(hhh)\) case](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md). All independent colors remain. The root cut exists because each side of an internal edge contains at least two leaves. This is a source reduction, not a topological move. A single hub with one flag is the proved root star: \[ \phi\!\left(p_0\prod_i h_iight) =\phi\!\left(h_0T\!\left(\prod_i h_iight)ight). 	ag{15} \] If there is precisely one flagged hub but further hubs, it is \(C(h_0T(E))\) with a completed child \(E\). Multiple flagged hubs are governed by (11). In general they do not disappear by the named Frobenius rerooting, associativity, commutativity and \(T^2\) moves: those moves preserve the reduced flagged tree. This is an obstruction to that restricted simplification procedure, not to additional source identities or to the desired asymptotic theorem. For example, the two-hub source \[ \phi\!\left((Th_1)h_2\,T((Th_3)h_4)ight) 	ag{16} \] is strict and has one flagged and one unflagged leaf at each hub. Under the named moves it is neither a flag-free completed-root tree nor a single-hub root star. This is a structural witness, not a numerical knot experiment. The [cap identity](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md) \[ D(FG)=D(F)D(G),\qquad D=\phi T, \] still holds with its separate marked topological interpretation. It applies when a \(D\)-product is exposed. It is not a rule for factoring the \(C\)-contractions (11)–(16); no cap factor has been inserted here. ## 5. A positive complete-character kernel and the fully flagged action At pure complete colors \(p_i=L_N\), define \(K_N(E)=T(L_NE)\). Coefficient reversal and the exact complete trace identity give, for every full Hermite element \(E\), \[ [e_r]K_N(E)=\phi(e_rL_NE) =N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_r(c_k)E(c_k),\qquad c_k=2\cos rac{(2k+1)\pi}{N}. 	ag{17} \] The trace identity retains the repeated-node multiplicities. It is not a substitution of a different closure: in \(\phi(L_NF)\) the two original normal contributions cancel exactly. See the [root-character contraction](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md), §2, and its [prior squared-kernel identity](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md). For \(r>M=\lfloor d/2floor\), \(e_r\) vanishes at all nodes. Thus \(K_N(E)\) has degree at most \(M\) and is determined by the finite kernel \[ K_N(E)(c_l)=N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left[\sum_{r=0}^{M}e_r(c_l)e_r(c_k)ight]E(c_k). 	ag{18} \] On the distinct nodes \(c_0,\ldots,c_M\), every \(e_r(c_k)\) is nonnegative and is zero for \(k<r\). Let \(n_k\) be its multiplicity in the full grid: two except at the odd simple node, where it is one. Put \(B_{kr}=e_r(c_k)\) and \(\mathbf D=\operatorname{diag}(n_k)\). The matrix in (18) is \(NBB^{\mathsf t}\mathbf D\). It is entrywise nonnegative, self-adjoint and positive definite for the inner product weighted by \(\mathbf D\), because \(B\) is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Its symmetric conjugate is the positive Gram matrix \[ N\mathbf D^{1/2}BB^{\mathsf t}\mathbf D^{1/2}. 	ag{19} \] This kernel is not a contraction with polynomial norm. Its exact exponential size is the useful feature. Let \(c_*=c_M\) and \[ G_0=g(1/4),\qquad g(u)=J(2u)-4J(u),\qquad J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt. \] The [uniform Newton estimate](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), §3, is \(\log e_r(-2)=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)\), with \(\max g=G_0\). Consequently \[ \max_l|K_N(E)(c_l)| \le \exp\{N(2G_0+o(1))\}\max_k|E(c_k)|. 	ag{20} \] For a nonnegative nodal \(E\), keeping \(k=M\) and \(r=\lfloor N/4floor\) gives \[ K_N(E)(c_*)\ge \exp\{N(2G_0-o(1))\}E(c_*). 	ag{21} \] At odd levels \(c_*=-2\). At even levels \(c_*+2=O(N^{-2})\); all quarter-index factors stay away from zero, so this changes their logarithm by \(O(N^{-1})\). The shifts and nodal multiplicities are therefore harmless at both parities. The tree and its number of factors are fixed before the limit. Suppose every reduced hub has exactly one flagged leaf. Root at one of them. Every nonroot flagged hub is \(K_N\) of a product of its child messages; every unflagged original leaf is \(h_N=K_N(1)\). All these messages are nonnegative on the nodal grid by (18). Inductively, (20)–(21) show that their maximum nodal rate and their \(c_*\) rate agree and add \(2G_0\) for each \(K_N\) operation. The final scalar is \(N\sum_kE_{\mathrm{root}}(c_k)\), with no further exponential cost. There is one \(K_N\) operation for every physical leaf except the flagged root. Hence the positive complete scalar has the exact all-level rate \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log Z_N(N,\ldots,N) =2G_0(H-1). 	ag{22} \] This supplies both a lower and an upper bound for the original complete source. Its equality with the original strict classical action uses the existing positive coefficient and strict lattice theorem; no oversized norm has been renamed a geometric action. The [rigid-spine geometry](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) independently derives the same value from the rigid \(L\) profiles. At noncomplete colors or with half twists, (11)–(12) remain exact, but positivity of (17)–(21) is not asserted. The companion [decorated-character theorem](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md) proves a full-source spectral class closed under \[ E\longmapsto T(R^\epsilon L_jE), 	ag{23} \] and finite products, at exactly this complete rate. Together with the source adapter above, this covers the case in which every hub is flagged. An unflagged hub requires \(E\mapsto T(E)\), the second case of (11); it is not an instance of (23) with an existing physical character. Mixed flagged/unflagged trees therefore require more than that closure statement. The later positive probe and spectral propagation theorems cited in the introduction supply the additional estimates. ## 6. Scope The finite support lemma, reduced-hub criterion, recursive source identities and positive complete-character kernel follow from the recorded exact source. No finite audit or numerical scan is used. The classification concerns the specified full-source contraction and its strict support, not all tangle isotopies or knot types. Transferring a source estimate to a literal knot-volume theorem additionally uses its original local packet, whole filling transfer and [marked geometric interface](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md).

title: Rigid spines and the geometry of fully flagged Conway trees
status: Rigid profiles and actual weighted-tree calibration
text: # Rigid spines and the geometry of fully flagged Conway trees 1 November 2026. structural and complete-geometry theorem. This note uses the [strict-output compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), the [general complete-mask geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) and the [original marked filling calibration](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md). Its source normal form retains every independent original color and normal coordinate. A rigid classical profile is not a scalar quantum coupon, a source-neutral operation or a tangle isotopy. The [reduced-hub source theorem](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) gives the exact finite algebraic interface. The separate [decorated-character estimate](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md) supplies its signed analytic closure; no such estimate is deduced here from the geometry alone. ## 1. The exact rigid-spine decomposition The strict types are \[ L=(0,1/2),\qquad H=(1/2,1),\qquad A=(0,1), \] with \(LL,LA,AA\to A\), \(HL,HA\to H\), and \(HH\) empty; orders can be reversed. Turns exchange \(L,H\) and preserve \(A\). Consequently: - A product with output \(H\) has exactly one \(H\) child. Its other child has type \(L\) or \(A\). - No product has output \(L\). - Starting at any \(L/H\) root, follow its turn child, or the unique \(H\) child at a product. This reaches exactly one original leaf \(h_*\). Call this path the *rigid spine* and its off-path subtrees \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\) its satellites. Every satellite has type \(L\) or \(A\). Each product on the spine has type \(H\), so turns between successive product vertices have even parity. The original full pair-algebra turn satisfies \(T^2=I\). Thus the actual full coupons obey \[ \begin{aligned} E_H&=(Th_*)\prod_{j=1}^m Q_j,\\ E_L&=T\!\left[(Th_*)\prod_{j=1}^m Q_j\right]. \end{aligned} \tag{1} \] Here \(E_H,E_L\) name expressions of the indicated types; the equality retains their values and first normals at all repeated source roots. Every physical leaf can independently be \(h_i=T(R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i})\). The product order can be kept as inherited; associativity and commutativity are identities in the original pair algebra. The unreduced framed expression remains the topology. In particular, (1) does not remove a pair of physical turns from that topology. Nor does it make \(E_H\) a scalar multiple of \(Th_*\), or \(E_L\) a scalar multiple of \(h_*\). An exact \(N=3\) check gives \[ h=10-z,\qquad Th=z^2-1,\qquad h\,Th=10z^2-2z-8. \] In the full algebra \(\mathbb C[z]/((z-1)^2(z+2))\), the ratio on the paired-node normal at \(z=1\) is \(9\), whereas the ratio at the simple node \(z=-2\) is \(12\). ## 2. Every satellite has an intrinsic \(X=1\) state Write \(f_Q(b)\) for the original positive optimized profile. Set \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\qquad \kappa=e^{-f_Q'(b)},\qquad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\qquad Y^2=\kappa X^2. \] Then \(X,Y>0\) and \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). The proved port types are \[ L:(B,B,1),\qquad H:(-Y,1,Y),\qquad A:-Y<B<X. \] At a strict product the children have common \(X\), and \[ B_o=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{B_1+B_2},\qquad Y_o=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{B_1+B_2},\qquad B_1+B_2>0. \tag{2} \] Every \(H\) product therefore has common \(X=1\). Its satellite is evaluated at an output \(\beta_Q\) satisfying \[ B_Q=Y_Q=b_Q>0,\qquad X_Q=1,\qquad f_Q'(\beta_Q)+g'(\beta_Q)=0,\qquad g'(\beta)=2\log\cot(\pi\beta). \tag{3} \] This state depends only on \(Q\), not on the \(H\) output or the other satellites. Indeed, the strict closed positive source \(C(hT(Q))\) maximizes \(g(\beta)+f_Q(\beta)\) on \(0\le\beta\le1/2\). The original root/compiler and entropy-barrier theorem gives a unique strict optimizer, since \(Q\) has type \(L\) or \(A\). Its equation is (3). Alternatively, on the positive-\(B\) part of either type, strict concavity makes \(\kappa\) increasing while \(1+B^2\) decreases. Thus \(X_Q\) decreases strictly there. The strict closure supplies existence of the unique \(X=1\) state. For \(Q:L\), one has \(\beta_Q=1/4\) and \(b_Q=1\). For \(Q:A\), the strict inequality \(B_Q<X_Q\) gives \[ \frac14<\beta_Q<\frac12,\qquad 0<b_Q<1. \tag{4} \] Define the absolute closed satellite action \[ \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le\beta\le1/2} \bigl[g(\beta)+f_Q(\beta)\bigr] =g(\beta_Q)+f_Q(\beta_Q). \tag{5} \] This is the complete action of the literal source \(C(hT(Q))\), with its own additional bare leaf. The complete-mask theorem identifies \(2\pi\Omega_Q\) with that augmented exterior's volume. This identifies a scalar constant; it neither decomposes the original exterior topologically nor factors its signed source into satellite sources. ## 3. Harmonic parameter addition and absolute profile constants At one \(H\) product, write the input, satellite and output as \((-u,1,u)\), \((b,1,b)\) and \((-v,1,v)\). Equation (2) gives \[ v=\frac{ub}{b-u},\qquad 0<u<b,\qquad \frac1u=\frac1v+\frac1b. \tag{6} \] Let \(u_0\) be the cotangent of the distinguished physical leaf, and let \(v\) be the final \(H\) port's \(Y\)-coordinate, equivalently the final \(L\) port's \(X\)-coordinate. Iteration gives \[ \frac1{u_0}=\frac1v+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac1{b_{Q_j}}. \tag{7} \] The response map is represented on \(u\) by \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1/b&1\end{pmatrix}. \] It translates \(1/u\) by \(-1/b\), so successive response maps commute and their translation parameters add. This is a stationary port parameter calculation. Without an original-word computation it is not a physical peripheral-holonomy identification. Its positive action increment below also prevents volume neutrality. For any \(v,b>0\), (6) gives \(0<u<b\), the original unsquared strict \(H\)-product branch. The profile theorem identifies it with the unique original optimizer, rather than a new squared-equation branch. At a strict closed complete configuration the proved bounds \(X,Y\le1\) give \(v\le1\). Since \(b_Q\le1\), a spine with \(m\) satellites obeys \[ \cot(\pi a_*)=u_0\le\frac1{m+1},\qquad a_*\ge\frac{\arctan(m+1)}{\pi}. \tag{8} \] The inequality is strict if \(v<1\) or any satellite has type \(A\). Long rigid spines therefore force their distinguished physical leaf toward index \(1/2\). Every leaf still satisfies \(a\ge1/4\). The absolute constants also add exactly. Suppose an input has \(f_H(x)=g(1-x)+c_H\). Its output has the derivative of \(g(1-z)\). To determine the additive constant, take \(z\to1\) along its connected \(H\) branch. Then \(v=-\cot(\pi z)\to+\infty\), \(u\to b_Q\), and \(x\to1-\beta_Q\). The original gate reaches \(x+\beta_Q=z=1\). Its continuous action is zero: all three volume atoms in \(\pi m\) degenerate, equivalently its final gate coefficient is one. Hence \[ c_{\mathrm{out}} =c_H+f_Q(\beta_Q)+g(\beta_Q) =c_H+\Omega_Q. \tag{9} \] There is no arbitrary integration constant. Turns preserve it and \(c_h=0\), so both cases in (1) have \[ c_E=\sum_{j=1}^m\Omega_{Q_j}. \tag{10} \] For \(Q:L\), \(f_Q=g+c_Q\) gives \(\Omega_Q=2G_0+c_Q\), where \(G_0=g(1/4)=2G/\pi\) and \(G\) is Catalan's constant. For \(Q:A\), \(\Omega_Q\) remains the complete root-leaf action (5); this is not a finite scalar coupon replacement. ## 4. The \(A\)-core skeleton and the remaining source boundary After maximal rigid \(L\) subtrees are treated as typed leaves, an \(A\) subtree has the completed grammar \[ A::=LL\mid T(A)\mid AA\mid LA\mid AL. \tag{11} \] This is a combinatorial and classical decomposition. Each effective \(L\) profile is \(g\) plus its fixed constant, so the usual completed optimization applies and adds those constants. The original signed coupons remain the full turned products (1). Replacing a physical alias inside a module by an alias of its effective profile requires a separate full-source estimate. There is an exact boundary separation. If an \(L\) module is an input of a retained product in a closed configuration, its \(X\) is at least \(1/2\). For an \(H\) neighbor, common \(X=1\). Otherwise let the other port be \((B,X,Y)\). The \(L\) port is \((X,X,1)\), and \(Y_{\mathrm{out}}\le1\) gives \[ 1+B^2-X^2\le(B+X)^2,\qquad 1\le2X(B+X)\le4X^2. \] The last inequality is strict for an \(A\) neighbor, giving \(X>1/2\). An effective \(L\) boundary below \(1/2\) can therefore occur only at the final complementary root. Its distinguished physical leaf may nevertheless have cotangent below \(1/2\), by (7). This separates the completed \(A\)-core parameter range from the rigid module regime. It does not remove amplitudes, currents or independent colors. ## 5. Fully flagged hubs: complete action and physical leaf ports Assume a finite reduced Frobenius tree whose internal vertices, called hubs, have valence \(d_v\ge3\). Internal edges carry \(T\); ordinary external leaves carry \(h_i\); exactly one external leaf at each hub is flagged \(Th_i\). The graph is a tree. The [reduced-hub theorem](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) provides its exact source interface, rather than an isotopy assertion. Root at a hub and expose its flagged leaf as \(h_0\) in \(C(h_0T(\prod Q))\). Every nonroot hub has the module \[ L_v=T\!\left[(Th_v)\prod_{\text{satellites }Q}Q\right], \tag{12} \] where a satellite is an ordinary \(h_i\) or another \(L\) module. A nonroot hub has \(d_v-2\) satellites; the root has \(d_{\mathrm{root}}-1\). All modules are type \(L\), so this literal tree is strict. The existing mask theorem applies to its actual topology. Every root satellite has \(b_Q=1\). Its full closure gives \(\cot(\pi a_{\mathrm{root}})=1/(d_{\mathrm{root}}-1)\). Every child \(L\) module then has incoming \(X=1\), so (7) gives \[ \cot(\pi a_v)=\frac1{d_v-1} \quad\text{for every flagged physical leaf}. \tag{13} \] Every unflagged physical leaf has cotangent \(1\), hence index \(1/4\). These are original physical leaf labels, although a flagged leaf becomes unturned in the Frobenius scalar. All retained gate labels are the strict unsquared values from (2) and (6). By (9), a nonroot hub contributes \(2G_0(d_v-2)\) in addition to its descendants' constants, and the root contributes \(2G_0(d_{\mathrm{root}}-1)\). If \(H\) is the number of physical leaves, the tree identity gives \[ \sum_v(d_v-2)=H-2,\qquad F_0=2G_0(H-1),\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(Y)=2\pi F_0=2v_{\mathrm{oct}}(H-1), \quad v_{\mathrm{oct}}=4G. \tag{14} \] This is the actual complete volume of the stated literal realization. It does not assert that its source cells individually are regular octahedra or supply a new topological octahedron decomposition. Knot patterns come from the original pairing compiler. At each physical leaf there are choices \(U,X\); turn exchanges \(I,U\) and fixes \(X\). Only \(U\cdot U\) creates an internal circle. The [proved two-choice induction](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), §7, supplies a loop-free root pairing with one component. Thus knot patterns exist, but any fixed sign pattern must still pass that actual pairing check. Full twists preserve it. The original primitive slopes and knot-complement calibration are those of the marked-mask theorem. ## 6. Literal integer-weighted Conway-tree dictionary Choose a finite ordered rooted tree with \(H\ge2\) weighted vertices. Give each vertex its own integer crossing weight \(n_v\). For each nonroot vertex define the actual turned tangle recursively by \[ L_v=T\!\left(R^{n_v}\prod_{w\ \mathrm{child\ of}\ v}L_w\right). \tag{15} \] An empty product gives the terminal \(L_v=T(R^{n_v})\). Equivalently \(L_v=T(W_v)\), with \(W_v=R^{n_v}\prod_w T(W_w)\). Thus the formula includes branching and unary continued-fraction chains, in their inherited ordered frames. The root closure is prescribed literally as \[ C\!\left(T(R^{n_0})\,\ T\!\left(\prod_{w\ \mathrm{child\ of}\ 0}L_w\right)\right). \tag{16} \] No assertion that (16) is a different conventional numerator closure is needed. For the augmented source restore \[ P_v=R^{\epsilon_v}L_{j_v},\qquad h_v=T(P_v),\qquad L_v=T\!\left(P_v\prod_wL_w\right),\qquad n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v. \tag{17} \] Here \(p_v\in\mathbb Z\) is the original filling slope coefficient; \(P_v\) is the original coupon. Each weighted vertex supplies exactly one original physical circle/color. Consequently \(H\) in (14) is also the number of weighted vertices. With at least two root children, every nonterminal nonroot vertex is a flagged hub of valence \(2+\#\{\text{children}\}\); the root hub has valence \(1+\#\{\text{children}\}\). Terminal weighted vertices are unflagged leaves. Hence (12) is exactly the canonical source expression of this weighted tree. A nonroot vertex may have one child; it still has valence three. The one-child root is also allowed, but its degree-two source must be handled explicitly. If its unique child is terminal, the source is \(\phi(P_0T(P_1))\), the strict two-leaf \(LH\) case. If that child has descendants, write \(E=\prod_wL_w\); then \[ \phi\!\left(P_0\,T(P_1E)\right) =\phi\!\left((TP_0)\,P_1E\right). \tag{18} \] This is exact self-adjointness of the original turn for the full Frobenius pairing. The right side has a flagged root \(P_1\), an ordinary leaf \(TP_0\), and the original descendants. It proves the source reduction and action count, not an isotopy re-rooting. The literal left-side presentation is itself strict by the \(LH\) root rule, and retains its own original mask geometry and peripheral words. Its pure complete source rate, hence its complete geometric action, agrees by (18). In the two-leaf case the direct profile is \(2g(a)\), with maximum \(2G_0\), so (14) holds there too. Fixed sign patterns still require the original loop-free one-component test; the two-odd two-leaf pattern is not a knot. ![A literal weighted Conway syntax tree. Nodes carry integer crossing weights; each edge carries the indicated turn. This is a syntax diagram, not a knot projection.](../book/figures/weighted-conway-tree.svg) [Reproducible TikZ source](../book/figures/weighted-conway-tree.tex), [PDF](../book/figures/weighted-conway-tree.pdf), and [PNG](../book/figures/weighted-conway-tree.png). After every auxiliary component is filled, (17) gives the actual crossing powers once. A one-component main pairing yields a **knot complement**; its knot cusp is unfilled. The finite choices \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,\pm1\}\) allow a common diagram threshold on independently large \(|n_v|\) whenever the separate analytic filling theorem supplies thresholds on \(|p_v|\). This dictionary alone is not that invariant-limit theorem. ## 7. Coverage and the separate signed estimate The [older belt construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) restricts its gluing graph to a cycle along one retained belt and explicitly requires a separate tensor argument for branched multi-belt graphs. The [root-star coverage audit](actual_conway_root_star_prior_source_coverage.md) establishes exact source overlap of one-hub examples with nonzero inner half twists. Neither result alone proves a branched-hub estimate. Formula (14) calibrates the complete action of the present source tree. It makes no claim of a new unmarked knot family or a literature-wide coverage classification. In particular, arbitrary Conway diagrams need not have a fully flagged reduced hub tree. The quantum induction retains the actual unturned \(R^\epsilon L_j\) immediately before each turn, all independent colors and every normal direction. The separate [decorated-character closure](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md) proves estimates for this operator. They do not follow from the harmonic response (7), the constant identity (10), or the complete value (14). An unflagged hub requires a different operator, with no original character at that vertex; adding a new circle would change the source. ## scope The reduced-hub tensor identity and positive complete kernel give the same all-parity action as (14). The weighted-tree dictionary separates the one-child root source identity from topology; no topological rerooting is asserted.

title: Exact root-character contraction and a correlated spectral localization lemma
status: Exact contraction and root-star source theorem
text: # Exact root-character contraction and a correlated spectral localization lemma 31 October 2026. original-source theorem. The exact root-character contraction retains the full repeated-root algebra and all first normal directions. A correlated spectral estimate proves the whole-source alias and physical-color gaps for every fixed root star $C(hT(h^s))$, $s\ge2$, with independent colors and arbitrary retained half-twist signs. This is a source theorem, separate from the marked geometric and whole-period steps needed for a filled-knot conclusion. No corresponding spectral estimate for an arbitrary turned child is assumed. The missing winding in the exact Fourier identity was already proved in [the outer squared-kernel theorem](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md), §§1–4. The residue calculation and periodic endpoint repair below provide an alternative proof and retain the same normal-coordinate cancellation. [The prior-source comparison](actual_conway_root_star_prior_source_coverage.md) also records the exact all-inner-odd belt-source overlap; no novelty or topological classification is asserted. ## 1. Source normalization and exact rerooting Put $d=N-1$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, $\kappa=q^{d^2/2}$, and $P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2$. The physical pair algebra is $\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)$. The actual marked closure and normalized Newton basis obey $$ \begin{aligned} \phi(f)&=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f\bmod P_N),\\ \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)&=\mathbf1_{i+j=d},\\ T\widehat B_i&=\widehat B_{d-i}. \end{aligned} $$ These are the original source identities in [the exact source compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), §1, and [the finite invariant normalization](../manuscript/sections/02-finite-source.tex). In particular T is a linear involution, not an algebra automorphism. Coefficient reversal gives, for all $F,G\in\mathcal H_N$, $$ \phi((TF)G)=\phi(F(TG)),\qquad \phi((TF)(TG))=\phi(FG).\tag{1} $$ The actual circle is $L_j=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2)$, $1\le j\le N$. A retained half twist is the original $R^\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon\in\{0,+1,-1\}$. Consequently the literal root-leaf contraction is $$ \phi\bigl(T(R^\varepsilon L_j)T(E)\bigr) =\phi(R^\varepsilon L_jE).\tag{2} $$ All child colors, all half twists in E, the root color j, the marked closure and the normal coefficients remain unchanged. Equation (2) is a scalar source identity. No tangle isotopy or new framing follows from it. ## 2. A finite Fourier formula retaining every winding and normal Let F(z) be ANY polynomial representative, not necessarily reduced modulo $P_N$. Write its finite symmetric Laurent expansion as $$ F(w+w^{-1})=\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z}a_rw^r, \qquad a_{-r}=a_r. $$ Then, for $0\le h\le d$, $$ \phi(L_{N-h}F)=(-1)^hN^2 \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^m(m+1)a_{h+mN}.\tag{3} $$ The sum is finite. In particular its $m=-1$ term is IDENTICALLY ZERO. If $\deg F\le d$, only $m=0$ can contribute, and the answer is $(-1)^hN^2a_h$. The general formula allows one to leave a whole child product unreduced; the other terms are not optional error terms. Proof. The coefficient-at-infinity form of the closure is $(-1)^dN^2$ times the coefficient of $z^{-1}$ in $F(z)/P_N(z)$. For $z=w+w^{-1}$, use $$ \begin{aligned} P_N(w+w^{-1})&=w^{-N}(w^N+1)^2,\\ U_{N-h-1}\!\left(\frac{w+w^{-1}}2\right) &=\frac{w^{N-h}-w^{-(N-h)}}{w-w^{-1}},\\ dz&=(1-w^{-2})\,dw. \end{aligned} $$ After including the sign of $L_{N-h}$, the desired coefficient is $(-1)^hN^2$ times the coefficient of $w^{-1}$ in $$ F(w+w^{-1})\frac{w^{2N-h-1}-w^{h-1}}{(w^N+1)^2}. $$ Expansion at infinity gives $$ \sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m(m+1) \bigl[a_{h+mN}-a_{2N-h+mN}\bigr]. $$ Use $a_{-r}=a_r$ and set $m=-n$ in the second half to obtain (3). This residue computation automatically reduces modulo the FULL $P_N$; there is no semisimple quotient. There is an equivalent finite Hermite sampling formula. Put $$ \theta_\ell=\frac{(2\ell+1)\pi}{N},\qquad w_\ell=e^{i\theta_\ell},\qquad c_\ell=w_\ell+w_\ell^{-1}, \qquad0\le\ell<N. $$ Then $$ \phi(L_{N-h}F)=(-1)^h\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}w_\ell^{-h} \left[(N-h)F(c_\ell)+(w_\ell-w_\ell^{-1})F'(c_\ell)\right].\tag{4} $$ Indeed discrete Fourier orthogonality yields $N^{-1}\sum_\ell w_\ell^{-h}A(w_\ell)=\sum_m(-1)^m a_{h+mN}$, while applying $w\,d/dw$ to A gives the same sum weighted by $h+mN$. Their combination $(1-h/N)A+N^{-1}wA'$ gives precisely $m+1$. Formula (4) counts each double node twice and the odd simple node once. At the latter $\theta=\pi$, the factor multiplying F' vanishes. At $h=0$ it gives the familiar exact $\phi(L_NF)=N\sum_\ell F(c_\ell)$: the derivative terms cancel in conjugate pairs. ## 3. Replace the root crossing by its exact analytic Hermite chirp Choose the literal branch $$ \rho_{\varepsilon,N}(\theta)=\kappa^\varepsilon \exp\!\left[i\varepsilon\left(\frac\pi2-\frac\pi{4N} -\frac{N\pi}4\right)\right] \exp\!\left[\frac{i\varepsilon N(\theta-\pi)^2}{4\pi}\right].\tag{5} $$ At every $\theta_\ell$, this equals the original $R^\varepsilon(c_\ell)$, since $R(c_k)=\kappa(-1)^kq^{k(k+1)}$. On $0<\theta<\pi$ its logarithmic angular derivative is $i\varepsilon N(\theta-\pi)/(2\pi)$. The original normal formula $$ \frac{R'(c_k)}{R(c_k)} =-\frac{d-2k}{2(q^{2k+1}-q^{-2k-1})}. $$ multiplied by $dc/d\theta=-2\sin\theta$ gives exactly that derivative. Reflection $\theta\mapsto2\pi-\theta$ gives the second occurrence of every double node. The odd simple node has no normal obligation. Thus, for $$ \mathcal E_N(\theta)=E_N(2\cos\theta),\qquad F_N(\theta)=\rho_{\varepsilon,N}(\theta)\mathcal E_N(\theta). $$ (2) is EXACTLY $$ Z_{N,h}=(-1)^h\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}e^{-ih\theta_\ell} \left[(N-h)F_N(\theta_\ell)-iF_N'(\theta_\ell)\right].\tag{6} $$ No off-grid polynomial estimate for R has been used. In particular the linear exponential cost of bounding its canonical polynomial off the real interval is absent. ## 4. A whole-child spectral hypothesis and its consequences Here is a concrete analytic sufficient condition on the ENTIRE child, not a bound imposed separately on the root alias. Suppose fixed $F_*,c,C,\eta_0>0$ and $A_N>0$ satisfy $\log A_N=o(N)$, uniformly over any allowed child-color family, and $$ |\mathcal E_N(\theta+iy)| \le A_N\exp\!\left(N\left[F_*-c(\theta-\pi)^2+Cy^2\right]\right), \qquad0\le\theta\le2\pi,\quad |y|\le\eta_0.\tag{7} $$ Here $A_N$ is a scalar subexponential prefactor. The hypothesis is invariant under any scalar phase in the child. All constants are independent of its physical colors. Then the original root contraction obeys $$ \max_{0\le h\le d}|Z_{N,h}| \le\exp\!\left(N[F_*+o(1)]\right).\tag{8} $$ and for every fixed $\delta>0$ there is $\gamma_\delta>0$ such that $$ \delta N\le h\le d \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |Z_{N,h}|\le e^{N(F_*-\gamma_\delta)}.\tag{9} $$ for all sufficiently large N, at BOTH parities and every root half sign. The o(1) and threshold are uniform over the stated child family. A uniform loss in $F_*$ in (7) propagates to (8). The elementary upper (8) follows directly from (6), using Cauchy's estimate on a radius 1/N disk for $\mathcal E_N$ and the explicit chirp derivative. The resulting cost is polynomial in N; periodicity of $\mathcal E_N$ handles the endpoint disks. The 1/N shifts cost only a bounded exponential factor. The proof of (9), including the joining currents, occupies Section 5. Its essential feature is the exact missing $m=-1$ term. If the circle color $j=N-h$ is small, the nearest folded Fourier mode would otherwise be -j. That mode has zero weight. Therefore (9) applies to ALL $j\le(1-\delta)N$, not merely to a folded half-color range. ## 5. Proof of the far-color estimate, with both endpoint currents Write $u=\theta-\pi$. The chirp has modulus $e^{-\varepsilon Nuy/(2\pi)}$. Completing the elementary real square in (7) gives constants $c_1,C_1>0$ such that $$ |F_N(\theta+iy)| \le A_N\exp\!\left(N[F_*-c_1u^2+C_1y^2]\right).\tag{10} $$ Shrink $\eta_0$ once. In fixed disks about $\theta=0$ and $\theta=2\pi$ the same function and any fixed finite number of its derivatives are bounded by $\operatorname{poly}(N)A_Ne^{N(F_*-\gamma_0)}$ with $\gamma_0>0$. One may prove this either by Cauchy on a still smaller fixed disk or by differentiating the explicit chirp and applying Cauchy to the child. These endpoint disks are far from $\theta=\pi$; their fixed positive angular loss exceeds all sufficiently small height costs. The statement includes complex endpoints, not just their real values. The function $F_N$ has equal endpoint values and is symmetric under $F_N(2\pi-\theta)=F_N(\theta)$. Its first derivative jump is $$ F_N'(2\pi)-F_N'(0)=i\varepsilon N F_N(0). $$ Set $\psi(\theta)=\theta(2\pi-\theta)$, $$ b_N=-\frac{i\varepsilon N F_N(0)}{4\pi},\qquad G_N(\theta)=F_N(\theta)-b_N\psi(\theta).\tag{11} $$ Then $G_N,G_N',G_N''$ have matching endpoint values: the first two by construction, the last by the reflection symmetry. Its periodic extension is $C^2$ and piecewise analytic. It has Fourier coefficients $$ g_{N,k}=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} G_N(\theta)e^{-ik\theta}\,d\theta. $$ with $g_{N,k}=O_N((1+|k|)^{-4})$. This follows by four integrations by parts, retaining the finite third-derivative jump. Consequently the series for G and G' converge absolutely, and substituting them into (6) is legitimate: $$ Z_{N,h}(G)=(-1)^hN^2 \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^m(m+1)g_{N,h+mN}.\tag{12} $$ The correction $b_N\psi$ has nodal functional bounded by $\operatorname{poly}(N)A_Ne^{N(F_*-\gamma_0)}$. It is not discarded; it will be added back at the end. For $k>0$ shift the coefficient contour to $\operatorname{Im}\theta=-\eta$; for $k<0$ shift to $+\eta$, where $0<\eta\le\eta_0$ is fixed. Both vertical joining sides must remain. Their difference has the form $$ D_N(y)=G_N(2\pi-iy)-G_N(-iy),\qquad k>0. $$ or its upper-half counterpart. By (11), $D_N(0)=D_N'(0)=D_N''(0)=0$. Its first three y derivatives on the fixed joining interval have the endpoint-gap bound above. Three integrations by parts in $\int_0^\eta e^{-|k|y}D_N(y)\,dy$ yield the explicit upper bound $$ \operatorname{poly}(N)A_Ne^{N(F_*-\gamma_0)} \left[e^{-|k|\eta}\bigl(|k|^{-1}+|k|^{-2}+|k|^{-3}\bigr) +|k|^{-4}\right]. $$ The lower-limit terms vanish because the three stated endpoint jets match. The upper-limit terms are precisely the retained joining-current terms. The shifted horizontal edge is bounded using (10), and the subtracted quadratic has the smaller endpoint exponent. Thus, after adjusting a polynomial factor independent of k, $$ |g_{N,k}|\le\operatorname{poly}(N)A_N \left[e^{N(F_*+C_1\eta^2)-|k|\eta} +\frac{e^{N(F_*-\gamma_0)}}{(1+|k|)^4}\right], \qquad k\ne0.\tag{13} $$ For $h\ge\delta N$ and $0\le h\le d$, every NONZERO-weight frequency $h+mN$ in (12) has absolute value at least $\delta N$. This uses $m=-1$ having zero weight. The exponentially decaying terms sum to at most a fixed multiple of $e^{-\delta N\eta}$; the inverse-fourth-power terms are absolutely summable after multiplication by $|m+1|$. Choose fixed eta small enough that $C_1\eta^2<\delta\eta/2$. Equations (12),(13) and the correction bound give (9), reducing the positive margin to absorb $\log A_N=o(N)$ and polynomial factors. All choices precede $N\to\infty$. No contour height is allowed to grow with N, and no endpoint current is omitted. ## 6. Actual all-s root-star source theorem and its remaining boundary The required input is [the full-jet star localization theorem](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), §§1–8. For every fixed $s\ge2$, take the literal expression $$ \begin{aligned} Z_N(j_0,\ldots,j_s) &=\phi\!\left(h_{j_0}^{\varepsilon_0} T\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\varepsilon_i}\right)\right),\\ h_j^\varepsilon&=T(R^\varepsilon L_j). \end{aligned} $$ Every leaf is independent. Every $1\le j_i\le N$ and $\varepsilon_i\in\{0,+1,-1\}$ is allowed. This is a whole original source, not an equal-color restriction. Put $G_0=g(1/4)=2\operatorname{Catalan}/\pi$ and $F_*=2sG_0$. Here $M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor$, $s_r=\prod_{v=1}^r2\sin(\pi v/N)$, $s_0=1$, $J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv$, and $g(u)=J(2u)-4J(u)$. The cited input proves (7) for the WHOLE physical child product, uniformly in all those colors and signs. Its source-exact proof uses: $$ \widehat B_r(-w-w^{-1}) =\sum_{\ell=0}^{2r} \frac{s_{2r}}{s_r^2s_\ell s_{2r-\ell}}\,w^{r-\ell}, \qquad0\le r\le M.\tag{14} $$ with strictly positive Laurent coefficients; polynomially conditioned full Hermite interpolation; a polynomial bound on the first normals of ALL high Newton coordinates; and the actual core/alias coefficients. The unique joint core-envelope maximum is $(r/N,\theta)=(1/4,\pi)$. Logarithmic Taylor expansion gives the negative angular quadratic there; a strict arc-rearrangement inequality and uniform moving-zero logarithm bounds control its complement. The whole high alias has a strict rate loss even after its full normal data are included. This proves (7) on a fixed complex strip, not merely on real nodes. Moreover, in the full-jet norm used in that proof, every child alias has rate at most $2G_0-\Delta$, where $\Delta=G_0-v_3/\pi>0$, every whole child has rate at most $2G_0$, and a child with $N-j_i\ge\delta N$ has a uniform strict loss. The unturned physical root $R^\varepsilon L_j$ has polynomial jet norm. Those facts give strict losses for all sectors containing a child alias, and for every physical-color complement in a child, uniformly in the ROOT color and sign. The remaining sector in this proof is the root alias with all children unrestricted. Its exact form is, up to the original sign, $$ \phi\!\left(R^{\varepsilon_0}L_h \prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\varepsilon_i}\right), \qquad1\le h\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor. $$ In (9) the complementary index is $N-h\ge N/2$. Hence that ENTIRE contraction has a fixed strict loss below $F_*$. No absolute value has been inserted inside its root Fourier sum. The missing $m=-1$ term is decisive, because it removes the potentially small mode -h. To spell out the sector bookkeeping, write each full child as core plus alias and let $E_{\mathrm{core}}$ be the product of its core factors. Then $$ \begin{aligned} Z_{\mathrm{full}}-Z_{\mathrm{all\text{-}core}} &=\phi\!\left(\mathrm{root}_{\mathrm{alias}}T(E_{\mathrm{full}})\right)\\ &\quad+\phi\!\left(\mathrm{root}_{\mathrm{core}} T(E_{\mathrm{full}}-E_{\mathrm{core}})\right). \end{aligned} $$ The first summand has the root-character loss just proved. The second has at least one child alias. By (1), its root factor becomes $T(\mathrm{root}_{\mathrm{core}})$, the difference of the two physical unturned circle coupons used by the exact core/alias identity; its jet cost is still polynomial. Expanding finitely many child factors therefore gives a fixed $\gamma_{\mathrm{alias}}>0$ with $$ |Z_{\mathrm{full}}-Z_{\mathrm{all\text{-}core}}| \le e^{N(F_*-\gamma_{\mathrm{alias}})}.\tag{15} $$ uniformly over every physical color tuple and half-twist pattern, for all sufficiently large N. For the same reason, (9) plus the child-color jet loss gives, for every fixed $\delta>0$, $$ \max_i(N-j_i)\ge\delta N \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |Z_{\mathrm{full}}|\le e^{N(F_*-\gamma_\delta)}.\tag{16} $$ The preliminary complete bound is $|Z_{\mathrm{full}}|\le e^{N(F_*+o(1))}$. All statements include both parities and composite levels. The reference is exactly the original complete action. At all pure complete colors, $$ \begin{aligned} Z_N(N,\ldots,N)&=\phi(L_Nh_N^s) =N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_N(c_k)^s>0,\\ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_N(N,\ldots,N)&=2sG_0. \end{aligned}\tag{17} $$ The last assertion follows from the actual positive Newton expansion: $\log\widehat B_r(-2)=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)$, so the maximizing index is quarter. For odd N the node -2 is present. For even N use the closest node and $r=\lfloor N/4\rfloor$; all its relevant factors stay away from zero, and the $O(N^{-2})$ node shift changes that single term by only $O(N^{-1})$ in logarithm. This is a genuine every-level lower bound, not an upper-only normalization. There are $H=s+1\ge3$ literal leaves. The complete star has inner leaf labels 1/4 and root label $\arctan(s)/\pi$. At each inner prefix the exact port is $(B,X,Y)=(1/r,1,1/r)$, so every retained gate is strict. The original wire lattice still has $K=2H-3$ coordinates. The [general all-core and quarter-packet argument](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) uses the strict gate Hessians and the high/quarter source theorems; it provides the unique complete all-core maximum, its state complement gap, and the original nonzero local $N^{3/2}$ packet with all offsets and phases. Equations (15),(16) restore that packet to the WHOLE physical star source. The stronger local spectral packet in the independent child proof is consistent with this original wire packet but is not needed to replace it. This is a source theorem. Applying a whole-filling theorem additionally requires the original marked geometric deformation and full Fourier-period interfaces, with their fixed-slope and knot-component hypotheses. No tangle isotopy or new filling normalization is claimed in this derivation. For arbitrary completed E with internal turns, (1)--(6) remain exact, and (7)--(13) remain a valid sufficient implication. This note DOES NOT claim that such E satisfies (7) at its original geometric exponent. The high Newton part of a general turned child is not determined by its node values; silently replacing it by a semisimple quotient would lose precisely the normal contribution in (4). That broader spectral localization is the remaining general task. ## 7. The envelope obstruction The following elementary calculation explains why a separate positive root-alias envelope does not suffice. For C(h T(h^s)), a=$\arctan(s)/\pi$ and $X=1/s$. If $s\ge8$, the elementary Ti_2/atan inequalities give $\pi g(a)<37/48$, while $k(a)\ge\operatorname{Catalan}/\pi>8/(9\pi)$. Hence $$ k(a)-g(a)>\frac{17}{144\pi}>\frac{119}{3168}. $$ The last inequality uses $\pi<22/7$. This is only failure of a proposed positive upper bound to certify a gap, not a lower bound on the signed alias or a counterexample to a volume limit. The correlated Fourier contraction above avoids applying that separate root envelope.

title: Full-Hermite localization for an actual Conway root star
text: # Full-Hermite localization for an actual Conway root star 31 October 2026. This proves an absolute whole-source upper bound and strict child-alias/child-color gaps for the literal scalar \[ Z_N(j_0,\ldots,j_s)= \phi\!\left(h_{j_0}^{\varepsilon_0} \mathsf T\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\varepsilon_i}\right)\right). \] Here \(h_j^\varepsilon=\mathsf T(R^\varepsilon L_j)\), \(\varepsilon_i\in\{0,1,-1\}\), and \(s\ge1\) is fixed. It preserves every repeated Casimir root and its first normal. It does NOT prove the remaining root-only far-color gap, a full filling asymptotic, or a norm estimate preserving the optimized action of an arbitrary turned child. The inputs are the [exact color source algebra](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md), the [full Newton half-twist transport](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md), and the [uniform coherent-core recurrence bound](actual_pretzel_global_core_spectral_gap.md). The [root-character Fourier contraction](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md) uses the angular estimate below to control root aliases and root-only far colors. The [general all-core packet theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) supplies the complementary original wire-window statement. Neither companion is needed to infer the estimates proved here. ## 1. The actual full-jet norm and the marked scalar Put \(d=N-1\) and \(\theta=\pi/N\). \[ \begin{gathered} P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad c_k=2\cos((2k+1)\theta),\quad0\le k<N,\\ B_r(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(c_a-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/s_r^2,\qquad s_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin(a\theta). \end{gathered} \] The original algebra is \(\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\). Each distinct interior node is double; at odd \(N\) there is also the simple node \(-2\). On this full algebra define \[ \|F\|_{\mathcal J}= \max\left\{\max_{\text{double }c}(|F(c)|+|F'(c)|), \ |F(-2)|\ \text{if }N\text{ is odd}\right\}. \tag{1} \] The derivative at the odd simple node is not a quotient invariant and is deliberately absent. This is a genuine norm, and the ordinary product rule proves exactly \[ \|FG\|_{\mathcal J}\le\|F\|_{\mathcal J}\|G\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{2} \] The original marked functional is \(\phi(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}F\). Equivalently it is the sum of the finite residues of \((-1)^dN^2F/P_N\). At a double node \(c=2\cos t\), \[ \frac{P_N''(c)}2=\frac{N^2}{4\sin^2t},\qquad \frac{P_N'''(c)}6=\frac{N^2\cos t}{8\sin^4t}. \] These follow by differentiating \((4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0\). Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \phi(F)&=(-1)^d\sum_{\text{double }c} [(4-c^2)F'(c)-cF(c)]+\mathbf1_{N\text{ odd}}F(-2),\\ |\phi(F)|&\le3N\|F\|_{\mathcal J}. \end{aligned}\tag{3} \] In particular the norm does not replace \(\phi\) by its semisimple trace. The unturned physical root coupon has only polynomial cost: \[ \|R^\varepsilon L_j\|_{\mathcal J}\le CN^3,\qquad 1\le j\le N,\quad\varepsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}. \tag{4} \] Indeed \(|L_j(z)|=|U_{j-1}(z/2)|\le j\) on \([-2,2]\); Markov's inequality gives \(|L_j'|\le j(j-1)^2/2\) there. The original Hermite crossing has unit-modulus node values and \[ \frac{R'(c_k)}{R(c_k)} =-\frac{d-2k}{4i\sin((2k+1)\theta)}. \] at the double nodes, of modulus at most \(N^2/8\). The inverse has the negative logarithmic derivative and the same modulus. The original Cartan scalar is a unit phase. By the full Frobenius turn identity, with no tangle isotopy asserted, \[ Z_N=\phi(R^{\varepsilon_0}L_{j_0}E_N),\qquad E_N=\prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\varepsilon_i}. \tag{5} \] Combining (2)--(5) gives the general algebraic criterion \[ |Z_N|\le CN^4\|E_N\|_{\mathcal J}.\tag{6} \] Thus any actual child estimate in this norm passes through every physical root color and both half-twist signs at polynomial cost. The question is the size of the CHILD norm, not the root character. ## 2. High Newton coordinates have only polynomial normal size Let \(\lceil N/2\rceil\le r\le d\) and \(\ell=N-r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). Reflection \(c_{d-a}=c_a\) gives the exact polynomial identity \[ B_r(z)B_\ell(z)=(-1)^NP_N(z).\tag{7} \] \(\widehat B_r\) vanishes at all the actual nodes. Its derivative at a double node \(c_k\), indexed uniquely by \(0\le k<\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), is also zero unless \(k<\ell\). When \(k<\ell\) both factors in (7) have a simple zero. Since \[ |B_\ell'(c_k)| =\frac{s_{\ell+k}s_{\ell-1-k}}{2\sin((2k+1)\theta)}, \qquad s_rs_{\ell-1}=N. \] the quadratic term of (7) gives \[ |\widehat B_r'(c_k)| =\frac{s_{\ell-1}^2} {2\sin((2k+1)\theta)s_{\ell+k}s_{\ell-1-k}}. \tag{8} \] This includes \(\ell=1\) and both endpoint parities. To bound it, put \[ D_k=\frac{s_{\ell+k}s_{\ell-1-k}}{s_{\ell-1}^2}. \] One has \(D_0=2\sin(\ell\theta)\), while \[ \frac{D_{k+1}}{D_k} =\frac{\sin((\ell+k+1)\theta)}{\sin((\ell-1-k)\theta)} \ge1. \] The two positive angles sum to \(2\ell\theta\le\pi\), and the first is the larger. Thus \[ \|\widehat B_r\|_{\mathcal J} \le\max_{0\le k<\ell} \frac1{4\sin((2k+1)\theta)\sin(\ell\theta)} \le\frac{N^2}{16}. \tag{9} \] All high-coordinate first normals are retained in this estimate. At odd \(N\) the simple-node value is zero, as required by (1). The exact constant is not needed later; polynomial growth is. ## 3. Low-degree interpolation costs only a polynomial Let \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). For every polynomial \(F\) of degree at most \(M\), \[ \|F\|_{\mathcal J}\le CN^5\max_{\text{distinct }c}|F(c)|. \tag{10} \] Here is an elementary interpolation proof covering both parities. At even \(N=2m\) the distinct nodes are the zeros of \(Q_N(z)=2T_m(z/2)\). At odd \(N=2m+1\) they are the zeros of \[ Q_N(z)=(z+2)\bigl[U_m(z/2)-U_{m-1}(z/2)\bigr]. \] The number of nodes is \(M+1\). In the even case \(\|Q_N\|_{[-2,2]}\le2\) and \(|Q_N'(c)|\ge m\). In the odd case \(\|Q_N\|_{[-2,2]}\le4N\). At an interior node \(c=2\cos t\), the identity \[ U_m(\cos t)-U_{m-1}(\cos t)=\frac{\cos(Nt/2)}{\cos(t/2)}. \] gives \(|Q_N'(c)|=N/[2\sin(t/2)]\ge N/2\); at \(-2\) its magnitude is \(N\). Markov's inequality bounds \(\|Q_N'\|\) by \(CN^3\) in both cases. The real mean-value theorem therefore bounds each Lagrange cardinal \(Q_N(z)/[(z-c)Q_N'(c)]\) by \(CN^2\) on \([-2,2]\). Summing at most \(N\) cardinals gives \(\|F\|_{[-2,2]}\le CN^3\max_c|F(c)|\). A final Markov inequality gives (10), including all the double-node derivatives. For \(r\le M\), index the distinct nodes by \(0\le k\le M\). The actual nodal values \(\widehat B_r(c_k)\) are nonnegative: they vanish if \(k<r\) and every factor is positive otherwise. Moreover \[ \max_c\widehat B_r(c)\le\widehat B_r(-2). \] Thus for any coefficients \(a_r\), \[ \left\|\sum_{r=0}^M a_r\widehat B_r\right\|_{\mathcal J} \le CN^5\sum_{r=0}^M|a_r|\widehat B_r(-2). \tag{11} \] The positive expression on the right is only an upper bound. No positivity of a signed source polynomial on an interval is assumed. Uniform sine-factorial summation, including the integrable endpoint at \(r/N=1/2\), yields \[ \begin{gathered} \log\widehat B_r(-2)=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N),\qquad0\le r\le M,\\ g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\qquad J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt. \end{gathered}\tag{12} \] Indeed the logarithmic rate is \(2\int_0^x\log\cot(\pi t)\,dt\). It vanishes at \(x=0\) and has the same derivative as \(g\). The midpoint cosine product and ordinary sine factorials each have uniform \(O(\log N)\) errors on this closed range. ## 4. Actual leaf core and alias bounds in the full-jet norm Let \[ \begin{gathered} G_0=g(1/4)=\frac{2\,\mathrm{Catalan}}{\pi},\qquad K_0=\max_{0\le u\le1}k(u)=\frac{v_3}{\pi},\\ k(u)=-2J(u/2),\qquad\Delta=G_0-K_0>0. \end{gathered}\tag{13} \] The maximum of \(k\) is at \(u=1/3\); the duplication identity for \(J\) gives its value \(v_3/\pi\). Positivity of \(\Delta\) is elementary. For instance \(\mathrm{Catalan}>8/9\) and \[ v_3=\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\sum_{n\ge0} \left[(3n+1)^{-2}-(3n+2)^{-2}\right]<\frac{301}{256}. \] follow by keeping the first term, bounding the remaining positive series by \(1/16+\int_1^\infty(3x+1)^{-2}\,dx=7/48\), and using \(\sqrt3<7/4\). Hence \(\Delta>1387/(2304\pi)>0\). Write the exact physical leaf as \(C_j^\varepsilon+A_j^\varepsilon\). The proved coherent core coefficients have the UNIFORM exponential upper rate \(\widetilde g(u)=g(\max(u,1/4))\); pure coefficients satisfy the stronger \(g\). Equations (10)--(12) give \[ \max_{j,\varepsilon}\|C_j^\varepsilon\|_{\mathcal J} \le\exp\{N(2G_0+o(1))\}. \tag{14} \] The \(o(1)\) is uniform over the original physical colors and indices. Its proof is the actual complete-diagonal recurrence with its terminal source, not an assumed coefficientwise contraction under a half twist. The key maximization is \[ \max_{0\le u\le1/2}\{\widetilde g(u)+g(u)\}=2G_0. \] and this maximum is unique at \(u=1/4\). Thus the Newton evaluation weight removes the flat plateau of \(\widetilde g\) which obstructs the bare coefficient argument at quarter leaves. For an alias, split its actual polynomial into indices \(\le M\) and \(>M\). The low part is bounded by (11), the high part by (9). The full triangular transport theorem gives coefficient rate at most \(k(u)\) on ALL \(0\le u\le1\), with only a polynomial prefactor. Therefore \[ \max_{j,\varepsilon}\|A_j^\varepsilon\|_{\mathcal J} \le\exp\{N(G_0+K_0+o(1))\} =\exp\{N(2G_0-\Delta+o(1))\}. \tag{15} \] For the low part use \(g\le G_0\) and \(k\le K_0\). For the high part \(\max_{u\ge1/2}k(u)=k(1/2)=G_0/2\), which is smaller still. This is not an alias value-only bound: (9) is precisely the estimate of the normals invisible at all nodes. There is also a strict child-color gap. For every fixed \(\delta>0\) there is \(\gamma_\delta>0\) such that \[ \max_{\substack{N-j\ge\delta N\\\varepsilon}} \|h_j^\varepsilon\|_{\mathcal J} \le\exp\{N(2G_0-\gamma_\delta+o(1))\}. \tag{16} \] If \(j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), the core is absent and (15) applies. Otherwise \(h=N-j\le M\). Fix \(\beta\in(1/4,1/2)\). For \(r\le\beta N\), the exact global far-color recurrence subtracts a positive constant from \(\widetilde g\) uniformly when \(h\ge\delta N\). For \(r>\beta N\), \(g+\widetilde g=2g\) has a fixed gap below \(2G_0\). Equations (10)--(12) prove the claimed bound for the signed cores; for the pure core the original ratio \(J(x-t)+J(x+t)-2J(x)\) supplies the same strict loss near quarter. Adding the alias bound proves (16). ## 5. The original product star and its exact exponential reference For each fixed \(s\), (2), (6), and (14)--(16) imply \[ \sup_{\text{physical }j_i,\varepsilon_i} |Z_N(j_0,\ldots,j_s)|\le\exp\{N(2sG_0+o(1))\}. \tag{17} \] with both parities and every original normal term retained. Every nonempty CHILD alias sector has rate at most \(2sG_0-\Delta\), and whenever at least one CHILD color satisfies \(N-j_i\ge\delta N\), the whole source has a uniform strict gap below \(2sG_0\). The root color \(j_0\) and sign \(\varepsilon_0\) are unrestricted in these statements. The reference \(2sG_0\) is exactly the actual pure complete action, rather than a convenient larger norm. At all complete pure colors, \[ Z_N(N,\ldots,N)=\phi(L_Nh_N^s) =N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_N(c_k)^s>0. \tag{18} \] The complete \(h_N\) has positive Newton coefficients \(a_{N,r}=N^2s_{2r}/s_r^4\) of rate \(g(r/N)\). From (12), its maximum nodal value has upper rate \(2G_0\). Conversely choose \(r=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) and the smallest node \(c_M\). For odd \(N\) this is \(-2\). For even \(N\), \(c_M+2=O(N^{-2})\); on the chosen \(r\) range every \(c_a+2\) is bounded away from zero, so replacing \(-2\) by \(c_M\) changes the logarithm of this single positive term by \(O(N^{-1})\). That term has rate \(2G_0\). Thus \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\max_kh_N(c_k)=2G_0,\qquad \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_N(N,\ldots,N)=2sG_0. \tag{19} \] In particular (17) does not pay a spurious root-leaf alias action. For the critical family \(\mathsf C(h\,\mathsf T(h^s))\), its geometric value, when that geometry is invoked, is the same original complete action (19). No topological re-rooting or identification with a different source has been used. ## 6. Boundary of the full-jet estimate The estimates prove a useful root-independent contraction criterion: if an arbitrary actual child \(E_N\) has a full-jet rate at most \(F_E\), then all the literal root-color contractions (5) have rate at most \(F_E\), with the same strict losses whenever present in the child norm. They do not prove that \(F_E\) equals the optimized closed action for every child. In particular the turn is not polynomially bounded in this fixed norm: \(L_N\) has polynomial jets but \(\mathsf T L_N=h_N\) has rate \(2G_0\). An arbitrary turned child's internal action cannot be preserved by simply declaring this Hilbert or trace norm invariant. For the product star, the ONLY color case not given a strict loss by (16) is one in which all children remain in the complete corridor but the root color is macroscopic. Formula (4) estimates that root character in absolute value and cannot produce its oscillatory loss. The exact Fourier/Hermite contraction is still required for that case; it is supplied by the [independently proved root-character theorem](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md). In particular this note alone does not restore the full filling period at its action below the complete value, and asserts no new long-twist volume equality. ## 7. A global angular Gaussian envelope for the whole child polynomial The norm estimate has a useful stronger form on a fixed complex angular strip. Write \(\vartheta\) for its angular coordinate, distinct from \(\theta=\pi/N\). There are constants \(c,C,y_0>0\) and a uniform \(e_N\to0\) such that every physical leaf, at all colors and signs, obeys \[ |h_j^\varepsilon(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le\exp\{N[2G_0-c(\vartheta-\pi)^2+Cy^2+e_N]\}, \quad0\le\vartheta\le2\pi,\quad |y|\le y_0. \tag{20} \] In particular the positive-axis endpoints have a fixed exponential gap. The same estimate, with a polynomial multiplier and slightly smaller \(c\) and \(y_0\), holds for any fixed number of angular derivatives. Consequently \(E_N\), a product of \(s\) such actual leaves, has the same type of estimate with complete rate \(2sG_0\). Constants may depend on the fixed \(s\), not on any physical colors. Here are the two required arguments, including the normal coordinates. First, full Hermite interpolation is polynomially conditioned: \[ \|\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}F\|_{[-2,2]} \le CN^C\|F\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{21} \] To see this, first replace \(F\) by its representative of degree below \(N\). Interpolate the values by a polynomial \(I\) of degree at most \(M\), using the distinct-node polynomial \(Q_N\) in section 3. Its norm and derivative norm have polynomial bounds by the proof of (10). The difference \(F-I\) is divisible by \(Q_N\). Write \(F-I=Q_NG\). At each double node \(G(c)=(F'(c)-I'(c))/Q_N'(c)\). For even \(N\) there are \(m\) such nodes and \(\deg G\le m-1\), so the same Chebyshev interpolation applies. For odd \(N\) there are \(m\) double nodes and \(\deg G\le m-1\); interpolate at the roots of \(K_m(z)=U_m(z/2)-U_{m-1}(z/2)\). One has \(\|K_m\|\le N\) and \(|K_m'(c)|=N/[8\sin(t/2)\cos^2(t/2)]\ge N/8\). The same mean-value/Markov cardinal argument is polynomial. Multiplying by \(Q_N\) proves (21). Expanding that representative of degree below \(N\) in Chebyshev polynomials, each coefficient has modulus at most twice its interval supremum. Thus (21) also gives the explicit strip consequence \[ |F(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le CN^Ce^{N|y|}\|F\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{22} \] Apply this to the alias and use (15). For \(y_0<\Delta/4\) its entire complex-strip rate is at most \(2G_0-3\Delta/4\). This includes precisely the high-index normals which nodal evaluation alone would miss. For a core, all Newton indices are at most \(M\). Its termwise upper action is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal A(u,\vartheta,y)&=\widetilde g(u)+b(u,\vartheta,y),\\ b(u,\vartheta,y)&=\int_0^u \log|2\cos(2\pi v)-2\cos(\vartheta+iy)|\,dv-2J(u). \end{aligned}\tag{23} \] The corresponding finite products have this UNIFORM limsup majorant on the compact set \(0\le u\le1/2,\ 0\le\vartheta\le2\pi,\ |y|\le y_0\). For completeness, truncate each logarithm below by \(\log\epsilon\). The truncated factors are continuous, so their midpoint Riemann sums converge uniformly. The untruncated sum is bounded above by that sum. The two circular-distance factors in \(2\cos(2\pi v)-2\cos(\vartheta+iy)\) have uniformly integrable negative logarithmic tails. Their integral truncation error tends uniformly to zero, including coalescing zeros and moving integration endpoints. The endpoint factorial errors are \(O(\log N)\). Taking N first and then \(\epsilon\) down to zero proves the required uniform upper bound. At \(y=0\), the circular-arc rearrangement gives \[ b(u,\vartheta,0)\le b(u,\pi,0)=g(u). \tag{24} \] strictly when \(0<u<1/2\) and \(\vartheta\ne\pi\bmod2\pi\). Indeed the numerator integral is \(1/(2\pi)\) times the integral of \(\log|1-e^{it}|\) on the arc of length \(4\pi u\) centered at \(\vartheta\). That even circular function is strictly increasing in distance from zero on \((0,\pi)\); the arc integral is uniquely largest when centered at \(\pi\), unless the arc is empty or the entire circle. It follows from (24) and section 4 that \(\mathcal A\) has the unique maximum \(2G_0\) at \((u,\vartheta)=(1/4,\pi)\). Near that point none of the numerator factors vanishes. Put \(w=\vartheta-\pi+iy\). The holomorphic action there is \[ \begin{gathered} B(u,w)=-J\!\left(\frac12-u+\frac{w}{2\pi}\right) -J\!\left(\frac12-u-\frac{w}{2\pi}\right)-2J(u),\\ B(u,0)=g(u),\qquad B_{ww}(u,0)=-\frac{\tan(\pi u)}{2\pi}. \end{gathered}\tag{25} \] The real part of \(B\) equals \(b\). Its even Taylor expansion in \(w\), together with the quadratic strict maximum of \(\widetilde g+g\) at \(1/4\), gives constants \(c_1,c_2,C>0\) such that \[ \mathcal A(u,\vartheta,y) \le2G_0-c_1(u-1/4)^2-c_2(\vartheta-\pi)^2+Cy^2. \] on a fixed neighborhood. The one-sided second derivatives of \(\widetilde g\) at \(1/4\) are sufficient: the added \(g\) has strictly negative second derivative on BOTH sides.
