On the complementary compact set at \(y=0\), (24) gives a fixed strict gap. Continuity of the integral in (23) preserves half that gap for a sufficiently small fixed \(y_0\). Reducing \(c_2\), if necessary, puts this whole complement under the right side of (20). Sum the at most \(N\) core terms and absorb the uniform recurrence error. The aliases from (22) also fit the same estimate after reducing \(c\). This proves (20) for the actual whole polynomial. To obtain derivatives apply Cauchy's estimate on angular disks of radius \(1/N\) inside a smaller strip. The exponent in (20) changes by only \(O(1)\), so each fixed derivative costs a power of \(N\). No arbitrary off-grid continuation of the physical color is used. ## 8. A joint spectral/color packet at the negative endpoint The [quarter-index source theorem](actual_conway_quarter_index_color_packet.md) gives a nonzero local analytic packet compatible with (20), including all original phases. The canonical factorial continuation is the one in the [exact interpolation theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). Choose a fixed small index window \(I\) about \(x_0=1/4\). The selected normalized local coefficient \(\ell_N^\varepsilon\) has an exponentially accurate holomorphic interpolant \[ I_N^\varepsilon(x,t) =N^{1/2}b_\varepsilon(x,t)e^{Nf_\varepsilon(x,t)} [1+O(N^{-1})]. \] Here \(t\) is the actual scaled child deficit, the window is fixed before \(N\), and the original unnormalized coefficient is \(e^{i\varepsilon\pi d/4}\ell_N^\varepsilon\). The approximate equality on the physical index grid is relative exponential, as proved by the source theorem; we do not use the displayed \(O(N^{-1})\) in place of that fact. For integer \(r=Nx\), the exact Newton polynomial at \(z=-2\cos w\) has the canonical interpolation \[ \mathcal B_N(x,w)= \frac{\prod_{\pm}G_N(N/2-1/2\pm Nw/(2\pi))} {G_N(Nx)^2\prod_{\pm}G_N(N/2-Nx-1/2\pm Nw/(2\pi))}. \tag{26} \] This follows directly by multiplying \(4\cos(\pi(a+1/2)/N+w/2)\cos(\pi(a+1/2)/N-w/2)\). All Gamma arguments are in fixed regular strips near the chosen index window. The canonical factorial expansion gives \[ \mathcal B_N(x,w) =\frac{e^{NB(x,w)}}{2N\sin(\pi x)}[1+O(N^{-1})]. \tag{27} \] uniformly holomorphically. The half-integer shifts in (26) cancel the four numerator/denominator sine prefactors; omitting them would give a wrong amplitude. Define the exact finite analytic window \[ W_N^\varepsilon(t,w)= \sum_{r/N\in I}\ell_N^\varepsilon(r,t)\widehat B_r(-2\cos w). \] The factorial source continuation is taken only on this regular window; there is no proposed continuation of a moving low-index cutoff. Let \[ F_\varepsilon(x,t,w)=f_\varepsilon(x,t)+B(x,w). \] At \((x,t,w)=(1/4,0,0)\), its data are \[ \begin{gathered} F=2G_0,\qquad F_x=0,\qquad F_{xx}=-8\pi,\\ F_{tt}=-\frac{2\pi}{1-\varepsilon i},\qquad F_{ww}=-\frac1{2\pi},\qquad F_{xt}=F_{xw}=F_{tw}=0. \end{gathered}\tag{28} \] Thus a unique nearby critical \(x_\varepsilon(t,w)\) is holomorphic and even separately in \(t,w\). The same finite cotangent-rectangle proof used for the original wire packet, now in one index, applies to this fixed window: exponential grid error first, then the nonconstant cotangent modes and endpoint connectors, then the translated complex Gaussian. It gives \[ \begin{aligned} W_N^\varepsilon(t,w)&= a_\varepsilon(t,w)e^{N\Phi_\varepsilon(t,w)}[1+O(N^{-1})],\\ \Phi_\varepsilon(t,w)&=F_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon(t,w),t,w),\\ a_\varepsilon(t,w)&= \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{-F_{\varepsilon,xx}(x_\varepsilon(t,w),t,w)}} \frac{b_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon(t,w),t)} {2\sin(\pi x_\varepsilon(t,w))}\ne0. \end{aligned}\tag{29} \] The power of \(N\) is zero: the coefficient contributes \(N^{1/2}\), the Newton factor \(N^{-1}\), the primitive one-index sum \(N\), and the Gaussian \(N^{-1/2}\). Square roots continue their positive complete Gaussian marks. In particular \[ a_0(0,0)=\frac14,\qquad a_\varepsilon(0,0)=\frac14\,2^{-1/4}e^{-i\varepsilon\pi/8}, \quad\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}. \tag{30} \] These are amplitudes for \(W\), before restoring \(e^{i\varepsilon\pi d/4}\). For physical \(|h|\le\delta N\), the actual whole leaf satisfies \[ h_{N-h}^\varepsilon(-2\cos w)= e^{i\varepsilon\pi d/4}W_N^\varepsilon(h/N,w) +O\!\left(e^{N(2G_0-\gamma)}\right). \tag{31} \] uniformly for \(w\) in a fixed small complex disk. To prove this, use the unique index maximum in section 7 to bound the omitted core indices, and use (15),(22) for the alias. Shrink the \(t,w\) domains so these fixed residual levels stay below \(\operatorname{Re}\Phi_\varepsilon\). This proves (31) without analytically extending the full alias in color. For the product of \(s\) physical children, multiply (29)--(31), retaining the product of the original unit phases. Its joint spectral/color packet has phase \(\sum_i\Phi_{\varepsilon_i}(t_i,w)\) and nonzero amplitude \(\prod_i a_{\varepsilon_i}\). At complete colors its \(w\)-Hessian is \(-s/(2\pi)\). The exact unturned root chirp discussed in the separate Fourier contraction calculation adds \(i\varepsilon_0w^2/(4\pi)\), giving \[ -\frac{s-i\varepsilon_0}{2\pi}. \tag{32} \] Consequently a subsequent local Fourier stationary calculation has the root color Hessian \(-2\pi/(s-i\varepsilon_0)\), agreeing with the literal complete root port cotangent \(1/s\). Equation (32) is a compatibility check and local input; the global root-character Fourier identity and its endpoint currents remain the separate contraction proof. The theorem localizes the stated root-star source. It does not assert a general turned-child bound or a filled-volume theorem.

title: Root-star compositions and the knot complement volume
status: Root-star family; independently long fixed twists
text: # Root-star compositions and the knot complement volume 31 October 2026. assembly. This note concerns the literal composition \(C(h_0T(h_1\cdots h_s))\), with \(s\ge2\). The analytic argument treats the correlated root character together with its child. It does not replace the original signed source by a positive alias envelope. The theorem records all physical pure/odd patterns in this literal presentation. Its all-odd source overlaps an existing belt-stack theorem; no new knot isotopy classification is asserted. The published completed-root manuscript is unchanged. ## 1. Statement and original normalization Each \(h_i=T(R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i})\) is an original turned circle coupon, with its own color \(1\le j_i\le N\), physical half-twist sign \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\), and disk framing. Products and \(T\) are the actual ordered tangle operations. Retain the original cylindrical closure and one-cut mark. Fix a half-twist pattern whose literal terminal pairings have one main component and no internal closed component. Such patterns exist by the endpoint-pairing construction in the [general marked geometry theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), §7. At leaf \(i\), insert a fixed signed full twist \(R^{-2p_i}\). Filling that circle replaces the leaf by the rational tangle \(T(R^{\epsilon_i-2p_i})\). Write \(K_{s,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)\) for the resulting knot in this retained presentation. **Theorem.** For every fixed \(s\ge2\) and knot half-twist pattern there is \(P(s,\epsilon)<\infty\) such that, for all fixed signed integers \(|p_i|>P(s,\epsilon)\), the knot complement is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N(K_{s,\epsilon}(\mathbf p))\right| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{s,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)). \tag{1} \] The level runs through both parities and all composite levels. The \(s+1\) slopes are independently chosen, with no restriction on their relative signs or magnitudes. They and the expression are fixed before the limit; the threshold is allowed to depend on that expression and half-twist pattern. Here \(K_N\) is the original reduced enhanced invariant. The [normalization comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) keeps its outer framing character of modulus one. In the full modified one-cut convention there is instead the recorded single nonzero factor of modulus \(1/N\). Either convention gives (1). This factor is applied once to the whole original diagram, not once per auxiliary register. ## 2. The complete action and the all-core packet Set \[ J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad g(a)=J(2a)-4J(a),\qquad G_0=g(1/4). \] The complete port of a prefix of \(r\) children is \((B,X,Y)=(1/r,1,1/r)\). Thus the inner leaves have label \(1/4\), the outer root leaf has label \(\arctan(s)/\pi\), and every retained product gate is strict. There are \(H=s+1\) leaves, \(H-2\) retained gates, and \(2H-3\) primitive free wires. Only the final forced gate is removed, retaining its exact \(N-1\) complement relation. The [full-jet child proof](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md) and [root contraction proof](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md) give, with \(h_N=h_N^0=T(L_N)\), the every-level positive complete reference \[ \phi(L_Nh_N^s)=N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} h_N(c_k)^s>0,\qquad F_0=\lim_N N^{-1}\log\phi(L_Nh_N^s)=2sG_0. \tag{2} \] Here \(c_k=2\cos((2k+1)\pi/N)\); the sum counts repeated nodes with their grid multiplicities. This is the action of the original complete source. Its equality to the geometric action also follows from the strict wire variational formula and the actual complete geometry; it is not a freely chosen comparison rate. The [general core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) applies since \(H\ge3\). It gives a separately even finite holomorphic window \(\mathcal C_N(\chi)\), retaining the original offsets, \[ \mathcal C_N(\chi)=N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(\chi) e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_\epsilon(0)\ne0,\quad \Phi_\epsilon(0)=F_0. \tag{3} \] Its approximation to the all-core source is exponentially accurate in a fixed small physical color corridor after the explicit unit phase \(\eta_N=\exp(i\pi(N-1)\sum_i\epsilon_i/4)\) is restored. The all-core complement has a strict gap over the whole physical color cube. The high-index and quarter-index packets supply (3) on a fixed complex neighborhood, including their exponential index-interpolation errors. The diagonal color Hessian is \[ \Phi_{ij}(0)=-\frac{2\pi c_i}{1-\epsilon_i i c_i}\delta_{ij}, \qquad c_0=1/s,\quad c_i=1\ (1\le i\le s). \tag{4} \] Its real part is negative definite. Consequently (3) has the fixed complex Gaussian envelope needed for the full filling transfer. ## 3. Restoring the whole physical source Write the literal scalar using exact rerooting: \[ Z_N=\phi\bigl(T(R^{\epsilon_0}L_{j_0})T(E_N)\bigr) =\phi(R^{\epsilon_0}L_{j_0}E_N),\qquad E_N=\prod_{i=1}^sT(R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i}). \tag{5} \] This is a scalar equality in the original repeated-root algebra. It retains all normal coefficients and does not assert a tangle isotopy. The child proof bounds a physical leaf in the full value-and-normal norm at rate \(2G_0\), with a uniform strict loss for an alias or a macroscopic color deficit. The norm is submultiplicative. The unturned root functional has only polynomial norm, uniformly in its physical color. Hence any child alias or far color loses a fixed amount below \(F_0=2sG_0\) after the actual root contraction. For the remaining root terms, the child product has a fixed angular strip bound at exactly \(F_0\), with quadratic localization about \(\theta=\pi\). The root contraction theorem keeps the actual half-twist chirp in both values and normals. Its Fourier formula has weights \((-1)^m(m+1)\) at frequencies \(h+mN\); the potentially dangerous \(m=-1\) frequency has weight zero. The endpoint repair and both vertical joining currents have a separate strict gap. This proves a uniform root far-color estimate. The complementary color in a root alias is macroscopic, so the same estimate controls the whole correlated root alias without a separate positive root envelope. For completeness, the exact telescoping split is \[ Z_N-Z_N^{\mathrm{core}} =\phi\bigl(A_0T(E_N)\bigr) +\phi\bigl(C_0T(E_N-E_N^{\mathrm{core}})\bigr), \tag{6} \] where \(C_0,A_0\) are the original turned root core and alias. The first term has the correlated root gap. In the second, \(TC_0\) is the difference of the two physical root coupons, so still defines a polynomially bounded functional on the child's full-jet norm. There is no norm estimate for an arbitrary turn hidden in this step. Thus for some \(\gamma>0\), uniformly in all physical colors, \[ |Z_N-Z_N^{\mathrm{core}}|\le N^C e^{N(F_0-\gamma)}. \tag{7} \] Together with the core theorem, this supplies both the full physical color-complement gap and the exponentially accurate comparison with (3). All hypotheses of the [original-source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) are now verified for this literal source. ## 4. Filling and the actual hyperbolic volume The exact circle-basis identity substitutes each \(R^{-2p_i}\) in the original diagram. Its full Fourier–Hermite coefficients have total variation at most \(2N(1+|p_i|)\). Hence the global errors in (7) remain exponentially small after filling with any fixed slope tuple. The transfer theorem retains the nonzero charges, all endpoint currents and the nonzero leading amplitude. For independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes its selected action can be written \[ S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi)=\Phi_\epsilon(\chi) +\frac{\pi i}{2}\sum_{i=0}^s\frac{(\chi_i-1)^2}{p_i}, \qquad dS_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*)=0. \tag{8} \] Indeed its Fourier variables obey \(\partial_i\Phi+2\pi iz_i=0\) and \(\chi_i-2p_iz_i-1=0\); eliminating \(z_i\) gives (8). The resulting asymptotic has a nonzero coefficient and exponent \(N S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*)\), up to the recorded unit phases and polynomial normalization. Its logarithmic rate is therefore \(2\pi\Re S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*)\). The [general marked-mask theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) applies to this strict tree and these exact physical signs. It constructs the actual signed augmented-link group representation, with primitive auxiliary logarithms \[ U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i,\qquad V_i=-2\partial_i\Phi_\epsilon, \qquad G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon. \tag{9} \] The original fundamental-chain regulator is calibrated at the complete metric, and its volume is \(\Im G-\tfrac12\sum_i\Re U_i\Im V_i\). Equations (8) are precisely \(U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\), with primitive angle \(2\pi\). The proved framed metric completion yields a smooth complete metric on the actual disk-filled topology for all slopes in one fixed reciprocal polydisk. Its volume is exactly \[ 2\pi\Re S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*) =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{s,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)). \tag{10} \] Take a common threshold for the analytic and geometric neighborhoods. Only the auxiliary crossing circles are filled; the main knot cusp remains unfilled. Equations (7)–(10) prove (1). ## 5. What this adds and what remains open The root-star expression has a bare root leaf and is outside the literal completed-root grammar of the published manuscript. This is a statement about that grammar, not a claim that its knot types were previously unknown or cannot admit another covered presentation. The [prior-source coverage comparison](actual_conway_root_star_prior_source_coverage.md) records two concrete overlaps. The missing Fourier mode already appears in the [outer squared-kernel theorem](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md). When every inner sign is nonzero, the entire mixed-color scalar (5) is the earlier octahedral-belt scalar with outer power \(a=\epsilon_0+n_+-n_-\). Its full source estimate was already available. The present child argument also allows inner \(\epsilon_i=0\), outside that recorded two-type belt alphabet. A source identity alone supplies no isotopy or correspondence of peripheral curves. The marked-mask proof in §4 establishes the geometry of the actual current presentation independently. The ordinary pretzel source has no outer \(L_j\) and is not the same literal source. For arbitrary strict closed trees, the core estimate and actual marked filling calibration are now available. The remaining source requirement is a nonempty-alias bound at the complete geometric rate, or an equally sufficient bound after exact filling. The present Fourier theorem gives such a bound when the turned child is a product of physical leaves. It does not prove the necessary spectral localization for an arbitrary child with internal turns. Presentation coverage and a generic main-meridian quantum A-operator theorem remain separate open tasks.

title: Root-star sources: exact overlap with prior belt and pretzel results
text: # Root-star sources: exact overlap with prior belt and pretzel results 31 October 2026. This is a source and coverage audit, not a new asymptotic theorem or a classification of tangle isotopy types. It compares the literal mixed-color source of \(C(h_0T(h_1\cdots h_s))\) with the earlier notes, including all first Casimir normals and the original marked closure. ## 1. The mixed-color identity and the belt alphabet Work in the full physical pair algebra \(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\), with its original turn \(T\), crossing \(R\), ordinary circle \(L_j\), and marked functional \(\phi\). Put \[ h_j^\epsilon=T(R^\epsilon L_j),\qquad Z_N(\mathbf j)=\phi\!\left(h_{j_0}^{\epsilon_0} T\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\epsilon_i}\right)\right) =\phi\!\left(L_{j_0}R^{\epsilon_0} \prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\epsilon_i}\right). \tag{1} \] The last equality is the Frobenius turn identity, proved with the full Newton basis in [the root-character contraction](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md), §1. Every color \(1\le j_i\le N\) remains independent. The [literal octahedral belt construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md), §1 and §4a, reads its two typed pieces as \(f_+=T(RL_N)R^{-1}\) and \(f_-=RT(R^{-1}L_N)\). The [mixed-circle packet](actual_belt_stack_auxiliary_color_inner_packet.md), §§1 and 6, retains the same physical reflection and turn with every ordinary color. Thus their mixed versions are exactly \[ f_+(j)=h_j^{+1}R^{-1},\qquad f_-(j)=Rh_j^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Here the superscript \(-1\) on \(h_j^{-1}\) denotes the negative half-twist sign, not a multiplicative inverse. If all inner signs are nonzero, let \(n_+\) and \(n_-\) count them and choose the fixed outer crossing power \(a=\epsilon_0+n_+-n_-\). Commutativity within the full pair algebra gives \[ \begin{aligned} \phi\!\left(L_{j_0}R^a\prod_{i=1}^s f_{\epsilon_i}(j_i)\right) &=\phi\!\left(L_{j_0}R^{a-n_++n_-} \prod_{i=1}^s h_{j_i}^{\epsilon_i}\right)\\ &=Z_N(\mathbf j). \end{aligned}\tag{3} \] This is equality of the entire mixed-color scalar, not only its complete value or its leading action. The physical turn/reflection formulas establish (2) before commutativity is used; no normal directions or Cartan factors are discarded. The [long-filled belt theorem](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) already supplies the whole-source packet and all-color estimates for every fixed two-type word and every fixed integer \(a\), at both parities and composite levels. It also proves independently long signed fillings of any auxiliary subset for its literal belt diagram. Consequently the all-inner- \(\pm1\) scalar in (1) overlaps that prior analytic theorem. A pure root \(\epsilon_0=0\) is included by the choice of \(a\). An inner pure leaf \(\epsilon_i=0\) is outside the recorded two-type alphabet; its inclusion in the current source estimate should be stated separately. Equation (3) alone proves neither isotopy of the two diagrams nor a correspondence of their peripheral curves. The current root-star geometry and filling calibration use the [marked-mask construction](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) for the literal current presentation. No new topological family or priority claim follows from this comparison. ## 2. The missing Fourier mode was already proved The [outer squared-kernel theorem](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md), §§1–4, already retains values and first normals and gives \[ \phi(L_{N-h}F)=N^2\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} (1-\ell)(-1)^{(N-1)\ell}\widehat F_{\ell N-h}, \tag{4} \] where its angular coordinate is \(z=-2\cos\theta\). The potentially small winding \(\ell=1\) has coefficient zero. Its finite double-pole contour keeps all four boundary pieces and proves a whole-color gap from a Gaussian angular packet and a strict complementary-node gap. The present coordinate \(z=2\cos\vartheta\) differs by a shift of \(\pi\). Writing \(F(2\cos\vartheta)=\sum a_re^{ir\vartheta}\), symmetry and \(m=-\ell\) turn (4) into \[ \phi(L_{N-h}F)=(-1)^hN^2\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z} (-1)^m(m+1)a_{h+mN}. \tag{5} \] Thus the missing \(m=-1\) mode is the same cancellation. The current residue derivation, calibrated chirp and periodic endpoint repair give an alternative proof and an application to the stated child estimate; they do not establish a previously absent Fourier identity. ## 3. Distinct nearby source families The [pretzel source reduction](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), §1, identifies the ordinary mixed odd-pretzel scalar with a product of rotated boxes, hence with \(\phi(\prod_i h_{j_i}^{-1})\) in these conventions. It has no outer \(L_{j_0}\). Its [long-filling theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) and [width extension](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) concern that different marked source. The root-star argument therefore does not, merely by (3), remove the recorded pretzel width restriction. The [balanced alternating-source note](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) instead treats anchor defects in the charged source of an alternating diagram, with an exact figure-eight obstruction. It is not a Conway root-star or belt-source theorem. ## Audit scope The comparison above reads the cited finite-source identities and their stated theorem scopes. It does not reprove their asymptotic or geometric dependencies, claim a new tangle equivalence, or assert coverage of every algebraic link. Mathematical rendering and relative-link checks are preservation checks; no numerical asymptotic experiment is used.

title: A single-leaf alias gap that composes with an arbitrary completed child
text: # A single-leaf alias gap that composes with an arbitrary completed child 31 October 2026. source-envelope theorem. The proof retains the actual seven-factorial multiplication gate and the completed child's output tangent. It uses no child coefficient lower asymptotic or replacement coupon. The [finite source and lattice adapter](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) and [geometric proper-port theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_geometric_composition.md) are separate inputs. The applicable closed class has two completed root children and proper completed ports $0<X,Y<1$. Root-leaf closures that reach the quarter-index equal-modulus dominance boundary remain separate. ## 1. Exact parameter domain at a single-leaf attachment Attach the original leaf $h$ to a completed child $E$ by the original product. The selected common $X$ is the cotangent of the leaf coordinate $a$. Write the child port as $(B,X,Y)$, its output as $(B_p,X,Y_p)$, and the corresponding output angles as $b,c$. Original product stationarity gives \[ \begin{aligned} a&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}X}{\pi},& b&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}B}{\pi},& c&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}B_p}{\pi},\\ Y^2&=1+B^2-X^2,&S&=X+B>0,\\ B_p&=X-\frac1S,&Y_p&=\frac YS,\\ \mu&=P_E'(b)=2\log(X/Y),& \lambda&=P_{\mathrm{parent}}'(c)=2\log(X/Y_p). \end{aligned}\tag{1} \] Here $\operatorname{arccot}$ takes values in $(0,\pi)$. Assume both child and parent are proper: $0<X<1$ and $0<Y,Y_p<1$. Then $Y<1$ gives $|B|<X$, while $Y_p<1$ is equivalent to \[ B>L(X):=\frac1{2X}-X. \] Since $B<X$, this forces $X>1/2$. Every newly attached leaf in this class therefore remains in the strict source interval \[ \frac14<a<\frac{\arctan(2)}\pi.\tag{2} \] The only region not covered by the earlier individual-leaf certificate is $1/2<X<2/3$. On its closed enlargement $1/2\le X\le2/3$, \[ 0<L(X)\le B\le X,\qquad \frac1{2X}\le Y\le1. \] The exact reflection $B'=1/(X+B)-X$ maps $[L(X),X]$ onto itself, interchanges its endpoints, and satisfies $Y_p^2=1+(B')^2-X^2$. Consequently, setting $p=e^\mu$ and $q=e^\lambda$, \[ p,q\in[X^2,4X^4]\subset[1/4,1],\qquad \mu,\lambda\in[-2\log2,0].\tag{3} \] This compact slope domain follows from actual proper ports; it is not an extra assumption on the source. ## 2. A universal dual inequality with a linear child Retain the [original complete, core and alias actions](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md): \[ \begin{aligned} J(t)&=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du,& g(t)&=J(2t)-4J(t),\\ \widetilde g(t)&=g(\max(t,1/4)),&k(t)&=-2J(t/2),\\ m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z),\\ D&=\{x,y\ge0:\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}. \end{aligned} \] Define \[ \begin{aligned} P(\mu,\lambda) &=\max_{D,\,x\le1/2} [g(x)+m(x,y,z)+\mu y-\lambda z],\\ Q(\mu,\lambda) &=\max_D[k(x)+m(x,y,z)+\mu y-\lambda z]. \end{aligned}\tag{4} \] Only the new leaf has the core restriction $x\le1/2$ in $P$. The completed child coordinate $y$ retains its full interval $[0,1]$: it is bounded by its own tangent, not identified with another bare leaf. There is an exact calibration on the whole square (3). Set \[ \begin{aligned} X&=\sqrt{p+q+pq}-\sqrt{pq},&S&=\sqrt{q/p},\\ B&=S-X,&B_p&=X-1/S,\\ a&=\operatorname{arccot}(X)/\pi,& b&=\operatorname{arccot}(B)/\pi,& c&=\operatorname{arccot}(B_p)/\pi. \end{aligned}\tag{5} \] Here $1/2\le X<1$. Indeed $X\ge1/2$ is equivalent to $p+q-\sqrt{pq}\ge1/4$, which follows from $(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2+\sqrt{pq}\ge1/4$. And $X<1$ follows from $(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2<1$. Also $Y^2=1+B^2-X^2=X^2/p>0$. The point $(a,b,c)$ is strictly in $D$: $X+B=S>0$, $X-B_p=1/S>0$, $B-B_p=Y^2/S>0$, and the remaining sine numerator is $X^2>0$. The actual derivatives are \[ m_x(a,b,c)=-2\log X,\qquad m_y(a,b,c)=-\mu,\qquad m_z(a,b,c)=\lambda.\tag{6} \] Since $g'(a)=2\log X$, global concavity proves \[ P(\mu,\lambda)=g(a)+m(a,b,c)+\mu b-\lambda c.\tag{7} \] **Square certificate.** On the full square in (3), \[ Q(\mu,\lambda)\le P(\mu,\lambda)-\frac1{1000}. \tag{8} \] The [exact verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate.py) and [rational data](../experiments/conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate.json) partition the entire square into 55 dyadic rectangles. On each rectangle, a fixed feasible rational pure point gives a lower bound for $P$. A fixed rational tangent to the concave function $k+m$ gives a global upper bound for the alias action. The four exact vertices of $D$ are \[ (0,0,0),\quad(1,0,1),\quad(0,1,1),\quad(1/2,1/2,1/2). \] Together with the four slope corners, these give 16 inequalities per rectangle, or 880 in total. Affinity covers every rectangle and the entire product polytope. Recursive subdivision proves coverage without gaps. The [result record](../experiments/conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate_results.json) has minimum certified lower bound \[ \frac{55437191760019874892517972684020763373}{10^{40}} >\frac1{1000}. \] The verifier uses the same rational engine as the two-leaf certificate. Its outward arithmetic and sine, logarithm, Machin and integrated Euler-product remainders are explicit there. No optimizer is called, and candidate-state accuracy is not a premise. ## 3. The actual new-leaf inequality and inherited gap Let $C=P_E(b)$ be the child's selected complete value. Suppose its core and aggregate alias arrays satisfy, uniformly in all physical colors and all output indices $r$, \[ \begin{aligned} |C_{E,r}|&\le\exp\!\left(N[C+\mu(r/N-b)+e_N]\right),\\ |A_{E,r}|&\le\exp\!\left(N[C+\mu(r/N-b)-\gamma_E+e_N]\right),\\ e_N&\longrightarrow0,\qquad\gamma_E>0. \end{aligned}\tag{9} \] This is an output-tangent upper bound. It does not say that the same weights minimize a separate constrained problem at every $r$. For an alias at the new leaf, adding the child tangent gives its constant $C-\mu b$ plus $k(x)+m+\mu y$. Equations (7)–(8) prove \[ \begin{aligned} k(x)+m(x,y,z)+C+\mu(y-b) &\le P_{\mathrm{parent}}(c)+\lambda(z-c)-\frac1{1000},\\ P_{\mathrm{parent}}(c)&=g(a)+C+m(a,b,c), \qquad 1/2<X\le2/3. \end{aligned}\tag{10} \] This is the original parent action and slope, with its actual boundary coordinate. For $X\ge2/3$, the [earlier exact algebraic leaf certificate](actual_conway_algebraic_leaf_alias_certificate.md) gives \[ k(x)\le g(a)+g'(a)(x-a)-\frac1{2500}. \] The original gate and child tangents cancel the $x,y$ terms by (6). Thus the same block inequality holds for every proper attachment with uniform margin \[ \delta_{\mathrm{leaf}}=\frac1{2500}.\tag{11} \] For a new core leaf, $\widetilde g$ is bounded by its complete tangent because $a>1/4$. The same calculation gives the parent tangent with zero loss. The exact finite parent split is \[ \begin{aligned} C_{\mathrm{parent}}&=C_h\star C_E,\\ A_{\mathrm{parent}}&=A_h\star C_E+C_h\star A_E+A_h\star A_E. \end{aligned}\tag{12} \] Here $\star$ is the original Newton kernel, including $i+j\le d=N-1$ and all normal directions. The three terms lose, respectively, $\delta_{\mathrm{leaf}}$, $\gamma_E$, and their sum. Polynomially many kernel indices and the uniform $O(\log N)$ factorial errors can be absorbed into a new error tending to zero. Hence (9) propagates with \[ \gamma_{\mathrm{parent}} =\min(\gamma_E,\delta_{\mathrm{leaf}})>0.\tag{13} \] The order $Eh$ gives the same statement by the exact commutative product; no coupon is moved through a turn. Turns and completed/completed products preserve the tangent hypotheses. The actual turn reverses $r$ to $d-r$, changes the slope from $\mu$ to $-\mu$, and has finite affine error $-\mu/N$. A product of two completed children uses their two tangent bounds and the actual gate tangent; internal derivatives cancel, and a contaminated sector retains at least its smaller child margin. This proves a finite-tree induction, including $hT(E)$ when $T(E)$ is a proper completed child. The closing demand and all turns still use $d/N=1-1/N$, so their total finite error is $O(1)$ in the exponent for a fixed tree. The two-leaf block lemma supplies the $A_2$ base. Larger original seeds may use their earlier leaf proof or the proved composition where proper. Every nonempty alias sector in a proper completed/completed closure therefore has a positive global gap. The all-core concave majorant and actual far-color recurrence give the physical-color complement. The strict-state, high-leaf and primitive-lattice hypotheses are checked in the linked source and geometry companions; they are not inferred from this upper bound. ## 4. A stronger response bound on actual proper ports The square certificate does not depend on this section. The following separate argument shows that, for $1/2\le X\le2/3$, the dual gap is at least its value at $\mu=\lambda=-\log4$. A four-vertex certificate then gives the stronger margin $3/50$ on this smaller parameter set. Fix $p,q>0$ and optimize $m+\mu y-\lambda z$ over $y,z$ at a fixed $0<x<1$. Each fiber has strict points. Every saturated gate constraint has a nonvertex-flat original tetrahedron, so motion toward a strict point has positive infinite inward derivative; the linear terms remain finite. The gate maximum is strict. Its Hessian in $y,z$ is negative definite: the first angle triple controls $y$, and with $y$ fixed the second controls $z$. The fiber maximum is unique and analytic in $x$, and its partial Legendre profile is concave. Write \[ U=\cot(\pi x),\quad V=\cot(\pi y),\quad W=\cot(\pi z),\qquad A=U-W>0,\quad r=q/p,\quad c_0=\frac{q(p+q+1)}p. \] Using the original signs $m_y=-\mu$, $m_z=\lambda$, \[ U+V=rA,\qquad V=rA-U,\qquad c_0A^2-2qUA-(1+U^2)=0,\qquad E=c_0A-qU>0. \tag{14} \] The positive quadratic root is the unique strict physical fiber. Implicit differentiation gives exactly \[ \frac{dW}{dU}=\frac{(1+q)V}{E},\qquad \frac{dV}{dU}=\frac{(q/p)(1+p)W}{E}.\tag{15} \] At the pure state of an actual port with $X\le2/3$, one has $V=B>0$ and $W=B_p<0$. Increasing $x$ lowers $U$, so (15) strictly increases $V$ and decreases $W$. Those signs are preserved through continuation toward $x=1$. The optimized child angle $y$ therefore decreases and output angle $z$ increases. At the pure $a$, the alias action $k(x)$ plus this partial Legendre profile has derivative $k'(a)-g'(a)>0$. This strict inequality holds on $[1/4,1/2)$, as proved in the [monotone two-leaf response theorem](actual_conway_two_leaf_monotone_alias_response.md). Concavity forces its maximizing $x_*$ to exceed $a$. The possible endpoint $x_*=1$ has uniquely $y_*=0,z_*=1$ and satisfies the same strict comparisons. Strict concavity of $k$ makes the complete alias maximizer unique; Danskin differentiation remains valid at that endpoint. For $\Delta=P-Q$, \[ \partial_\mu\Delta=b-y_*>0,\qquad \partial_\lambda\Delta=z_*-c>0, \quad a\ge1/4,\ V>0,\ W<0. \tag{16} \] A parameter path stays in this regime. At an actual port with $X\le2/3$, $p,q\ge1/4$. If $p\ge q$, first run $(t,t)$ from $t=1/4$ to $q$, then $(p',q)$ from $p'=q$ to $p$. On the diagonal, $X=\sqrt{t^2+2t}-t$ increases, $V=1-X>0$, and $W=X-1<0$. On the second piece $X_p>0$, because $p'(1+q)>q^2$. Thus $X$ stays between $1/2$ and its actual terminal value, at most $2/3$. There $S=\sqrt{q/p'}\le1$ implies $W=X-1/S<0$; and $V=S-X$ decreases to its positive final value, so remains positive. Both logarithmic slopes increase along this path. If $p\le q$, use \[ m(x,y,z)=m(x,1-z,1-y). \] This exact gate involution swaps $\mu,\lambda$ and adds the same constant to both dual values. It preserves $\Delta$ and supplies the symmetric path. Equation (16) proves \[ \Delta(\mu,\lambda)\ge\Delta(-\log4,-\log4). \tag{17} \] The limiting $X=1/2$ endpoint is included. No alias branch was selected by squaring a stationary equation. The [endpoint verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_single_leaf_endpoint_certificate.py) uses the same rational engine, with pure point $(352416,352416,647584)/10^6$ and alias tangent point $(570352,246081,753919)/10^6$. At $\mu=\lambda=-2\log2$ it checks all four vertices of $D$. The [exact result](../experiments/conway_single_leaf_endpoint_certificate_results.json) has minimum lower bound \[ \frac{613089614904949907163494204377649845509}{10^{40}} >\frac3{50}. \tag{18} \] The feasible pure point bounds $P$ below, and the global $k+m$ tangent bounds $Q$ above. Optimizer accuracy is not a premise. Together with (17), this proves the stronger actual-port margin stated here. ## 5. Scope and the root-leaf frontier This is an upper-envelope induction at a selected proper completed-port configuration of the original source. The source and geometry companions supply such configurations for their stated grammar. No claim is made that every algebraic tangle has the required strict states or local packet. In particular $C(hT(A_s))$ is a different boundary regime. Its seed has $X=1$, $B=Y=1/s$, so every inner leaf label equals $1/4$, whereas the outer leaf has cotangent $1/s$. Its pure retained cells can remain strict. The inherited signed source packet meets an equal-modulus dominance boundary there, not an eigenvalue collision or a forced-flat geometric cell. Equations (11)–(13) do not remove that separate packet obligation. ## scope and exact verification The square certificate is the primary proof of the uniform compositional margin. The response argument and endpoint certificate independently strengthen it on the actual proper-port subdomain. Neither proof relies on numerical sampling or a coefficient lower asymptotic.

title: Complete and marked Conway geometry with single-leaf attachments
text: # Complete and marked Conway geometry with single-leaf attachments 31 October 2026. geometric extension and source-interface audit. Keep the original crossing-circle leaf \(h\), literal turn \(T\), identity stacks, source marking and fixed disk framings. Define **completed** expressions by \[ E::=hh\mid T(E)\mid E_1E_2\mid hE\mid Eh. \tag{1} \] Every occurrence has its own leaves. The closed class here is \(C(FG)\), where both root children are completed expressions in (1). Turns act on completed expressions; independently turned bare leaves are not additional atoms of this grammar. This class has strict complete states, a unique complete optimizer and the actual complete augmented-link metric. Every physical complete leaf satisfies \(1/2<\cot(\pi a)<1\). The original local complex packet, primitive marked deformation and actual filled-volume action remain valid. The [source composition theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) and [single-leaf alias comparison](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md) supply the separate global source estimates. Geometry alone is not used to infer an alias gap. The root-leaf closures discussed in §6 remain outside the high-index packet conclusion. ## 1. Strict feasibility and the only deleted flat gate Each completed expression has a strict pure wire state at every prescribed output \(b\in(0,1)\). For \(hh\), choose equal leaves \[ \frac b2<a<\min\left(b,\frac12\right). \] At \(E_1E_2\), choose both child outputs in this same interval. At \(hE\) or \(Eh\), use this \(a\) for the bare leaf and for the completed child output, then use the child's strict state. At \(T(E)\), prescribe child output \(1-b\). This is an induction using the original product inequalities \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. \] At \(C(FG)\), delete only the final forced gate. Its exact finite coefficient is one and its inputs sum to \(d=N-1\). Choose limiting root-child outputs \(1/2,1/2\); both completed children have the strict states just constructed. Every retained leaf and product is therefore strict. The [original complete boundary barrier](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), §2, applies. An endpoint wire descends to a leaf endpoint or a product atom \((0,a,1-a)\); every other retained product boundary also exposes such an atom. Moving toward the strict state has positive infinite derivative there and no negative infinite derivative elsewhere. There are no additional forced-flat or maximizing-flat retained cells in this grammar. The original angle maps recover all independent leaf and product wires. Consequently the complete reduced Hessian is negative definite and the strict maximizer is unique. Proper output profiles are analytic on \((0,1)\). This is a sufficient combinatorial criterion for nondegeneracy, with the grammar in (1) retained. The excluded \(C(hh)=C(A_2)\) has two leaves whose forced sum is one, so both equal \(1/2\) and no strict retained state exists. Initial turns of an entire closed expression retain the existing [original \(C/D\) cap-sum reduction](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md); they are not silently included in the completed-root statement. ## 2. The strict completed-port invariant survives \(hE\) and \(Eh\) At a stationary proper output \(b\), set \[ B=\cot(\pi b),\qquad \kappa=e^{-f_E'(b)},\qquad X=\sqrt{\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa}},\qquad Y=\sqrt{\kappa}\,X. \] Then \(X,Y>0\) and \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). An actual bare leaf has \[ B=X=\cot(\pi a)>0,\qquad Y=1. \tag{2} \] The [original stationary product formulas](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) use a common \(X\): \[ B_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{B_1+B_2}, \qquad Y_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{B_1+B_2}, \qquad B_1+B_2>0. \tag{3} \] Every completed expression in (1) obeys \[ -Y<B<X. \tag{4} \] The \(hh\) base is \(B=X-1/(2X)\), \(Y=1/(2X)\). A turn sends \((B,X,Y)\) to \((-B,Y,X)\), preserving (4), and the completed/completed product is the original exact preservation proof. For the new \(hE\) product, write \(B\) for the completed child's first coordinate. Formula (3) becomes \[ B_{\mathrm{parent}}=X-\frac1{X+B},\qquad Y_{\mathrm{parent}}=\frac{Y}{X+B},\qquad X+B>0. \tag{5} \] If \(X\ge1\), (4) and the hyperboloid identity give \(B>0\) and \(B>\sqrt{X^2-1}\). Thus \(B_{\mathrm{parent}}>0\) and \(B_{\mathrm{parent}}<X\); its lower inequality is automatic. If \(0<X<1\), put \(\alpha=\arccos X\) and \(h_0=\sin\alpha\). The bare leaf has angle \(\alpha\) in the exact cotangent chart: \[ (B_h,Y_h)=(h_0\cot\alpha,h_0\csc\alpha)=(X,1). \] The completed child has \[ (B,Y)=(h_0\cot\beta,h_0\csc\beta),\qquad \beta>\alpha. \] The positive denominator in (5) selects \(\alpha+\beta<\pi\). The parent angle is \(\alpha+\beta\), so its upper inequality is strict, and \[ B_{\mathrm{parent}}+Y_{\mathrm{parent}} =h_0\cot\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}>0. \] This proves (4). The \(Eh\) order gives the same inequalities by the exact symmetry of (3), without changing its physical frame. ## 3. Closed propagation and the stronger leaf bound At the completed root, the two completed ports are \((B,X,Y)\) and \((-B,X,Y)\). Applying (4) to both gives \(|B|<\min(X,Y)\). The hyperboloid identity then implies \[ 0<X<1,\qquad 0<Y<1 \tag{6} \] for both root children. These bounds propagate to every completed descendant in (1). Turns exchange \(X\) and \(Y\). At a retained product the common \(X\) already lies below one. Write each child in the angle chart of §2. A completed child has angle strictly greater than \(\alpha\); a bare leaf has angle exactly \(\alpha\). The positive denominator selects a total angle below \(\pi\). Parent \(Y<1\) gives \[ \alpha<\theta_1+\theta_2<\pi-\alpha. \] Every child angle is at least \(\alpha\), so a completed child's angle lies strictly between \(\alpha\) and \(\pi-\alpha\). Hence its \(Y<1\), and its \(X\) is the common \(X<1\). A bare leaf keeps \(Y=1\); that equality is not propagated as a strict completed-port bound. Every physical leaf occurs either in an \(hh\) base or at a single \(hE/Eh\) attachment. At the base, \(Y_{\mathrm{parent}}=1/(2X)<1\) gives \(X>1/2\). For a single attachment, (5), the completed child hyperboloid and \(Y_{\mathrm{parent}}<1\) imply \[ 1+B^2-X^2<(X+B)^2,\qquad 1<2X(X+B)<4X^2, \tag{7} \] where the last strict inequality is \(B<X\). Again \(X>1/2\). The inherited \(X<1\) holds in both cases. Thus every actual complete leaf satisfies \[ \frac12<X_\ell=\cot(\pi a_\ell)<1,\qquad \frac14<a_\ell<\frac{\arctan2}{\pi}<\frac12. \tag{8} \] This conclusion uses the completed-root grammar. It does not assert the stronger individual-leaf cutoff \(X\ge2/3\), which is a separate source certificate. For later source bounds, an attachment with \(X\le2/3\) has \[ \begin{aligned} \frac1{2X}-X&<B<X,\\ \mu=f_{\mathrm{child}}'(b_{\mathrm{child}}) &=\log\frac{X^2}{1+B^2-X^2},\\ \lambda=f_{\mathrm{parent}}'(b_{\mathrm{parent}}) &=\mu+2\log(X+B). \end{aligned} \tag{9} \] On \(1/2<X\le2/3\), both slopes belong to \((-2\log2,0)\). For either the child or parent, \(Y<1\) gives \(2\log(X/Y)>2\log X>-2\log2\). Its hyperboloid identity gives \(Y^2=1+B_{\mathrm{port}}^2-X^2\ge1-X^2>X^2\), since \(X^2<1/2\); therefore \(2\log(X/Y)<0\). These are the geometric parameter bounds used by the separate alias comparison. ## 4. Actual complete metric and topology Each new \(hE/Eh\) product is an attachment already used inside the original \(h^s\) seeds: one genuine leaf pyramid, one completed child cell and the original ideal multiplication prism. The strict variables of §1 give the same positive tetrahedra and ordered input-face metrics. Use the original [ordered prism maps](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md) \[ \begin{aligned} F:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)&\longmapsto(v_0,v_1,P,\infty),\\ G:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)&\longmapsto(\infty,P,v_2,v_3). \end{aligned} \] The leaf-side CAP sums are \(\pi/2\) where the corresponding completed child sum would be \(\pi\); every other seam angle is the same original strict angle or flat \(\pi\) sum. These are exactly the one-leaf attachment cases of the [complete cell construction](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), §4. Supported-face gluing is convex, creates no accidental vertex identifications off the common face, and yields the completed output corner pattern PORT, WHITE, SHADED, WHITE. All expressions in (1) are therefore actual convex ideal completed cells. Turns apply only to those cells, so their original ordered rotation and color pattern apply. The root has two completed children. Its original \(j\mapsto3-j\) closing map matches both FREE and CAP pairs with angle sum \(\pi\); the resulting closed polyhedron is right angled. The [literal crossing-disk bowtie cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) uses the original leaves, stacks and turns, without a lower bound on the size of a child subtree. Its segment pairings and white facial cycles agree with the metric prism maps. It gives the actual closed augmented-link exterior with degree one. Canonical rectangular cusp decorations and the four-step pointwise edge words prove complete finite volume. Retained signed half twists replace only the original shaded pairings within their leaf disks by the [checked cross-copy pairings](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md). Both complete cusp decorations and all pointwise pure/odd edge words remain valid. For every fixed half-twist pattern, \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon) =\operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^0)=2\pi F_0. \tag{10} \] This identifies the actual augmented-link geometry with its original marking. The constructive knot parity survives the new operations. A leaf has the two choices \(\{U,X\}\), and the \(hh\) base has \(\{I,U\}\). The original loop-free product table sends every pair of two-element feasible sets to a set with at least two elements, after excluding its sole circle-producing pair \(U\) times \(U\). This applies to \(hE/Eh\) and to \(EE\), and a turn permutes the three types. Each completed expression consequently has at least two loop-free choices. The root can be chosen \(U\) or \(X\), whose cylindrical closures have one main component. Either half-twist sign realizes an odd leaf; integral full twists preserve the selected endpoint pairing. ## 5. Primitive lattice, selected packet and marked deformation With \(H\) physical leaves, the original full binary source tree has \(H-1\) products. Removing the forced final gate leaves \(H-2\). Contract all turns integrally by \(r_{\mathrm{out}}=d-r_{\mathrm{in}}\) and solve the single root input relation for a variable in one of its disjoint child trees. The remaining original wire lattice is primitive \(\mathbb Z^{2H-3}\). No relation \(2r=d\) is introduced. The strict state gives a parity-independent integer window and every-level rounding for all sufficiently large \(N\), as detailed in the [finite source composition proof](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md). By (8), every leaf lies in a fixed compact high-index interval \((1/4,1/2)\), and every retained factorial argument is strict. The exact pure/signed local coefficient formulas, continuous chirp, selected transport root and exponential interpolation error in the [original signed packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md) therefore apply on a fixed complex tube. They do not require both inputs of every retained product to be completed. The \(H\) leaf factors and \(H-2\) gates have total prefactor \(N^{3-H}\). The primitive \((2H-3)\)-dimensional lattice Gaussian contributes \(N^{(2H-3)/2}\), giving \(N^{3/2}\). All original integer offsets are retained with the changed local derivatives \(f_\epsilon\) and the unchanged gate derivatives. The external phase remains \[ \eta_N=\exp\left(\frac{i\pi(N-1)}4\sum_\ell\epsilon_\ell\right). \] At completeness the normalized amplitude is the positive pure one times \[ \prod_{\epsilon_\ell\ne0} \sqrt{\sin(\pi a_\ell)} \exp\left(-\frac{i\epsilon_\ell\pi a_\ell}{2}\right), \] and is nonzero. The color Hessian entries are \[ -\frac{2\pi X_\ell}{1-\epsilon_\ell iX_\ell}, \tag{11} \] with strictly negative real part. The original finite tensor-cotangent rectangle proof retains every boundary connector and nonconstant kernel mode. It supplies the same exact finite complex packet locally, with the original lattice and normalization. For the geometric interpretation, the selected local shear \[ \chi=t-\frac{\epsilon g_t}{2\pi i},\qquad f_\epsilon=g-\frac{\epsilon g_t^2}{4\pi i} \] is regular because every leaf is strictly high in (8). The nine [original rational prism identities](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) also cover \(hE/Eh\): a leaf input is already a permitted prism input. The turn and completed/completed closing identities remain unchanged. They give one actual white-face map and the same pure/odd shaded edge words on the original bowtie quotient. The resulting signed augmented-link representation has its original parabolic main cusps, primitive auxiliary logs \[ U_\ell=-2\pi i\chi_\ell,\qquad V_\ell=-2\partial_\ell\Phi_\epsilon, \] and the absolute primitive \(G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon\), including the correction \(-\epsilon_\ell V_\ell^2/8\). Its complete anchor is (10). The original regulator identity and geometric completion give \[ \begin{aligned} U_\ell+p_\ell V_\ell&=-2\pi i,\\ \operatorname{Vol}\bigl(Y_E^\epsilon(p)\bigr) &=2\pi\operatorname{Re}\left[ \Phi_\epsilon(\chi_*)+ \frac{\pi i}{2}\sum_{\ell\ \mathrm{filled}} \frac{(\chi_\ell-1)^2}{p_\ell}\right]. \end{aligned} \tag{12} \] The physical powers are \(\epsilon_\ell-2p_\ell\). After all auxiliary fillings and a loop-free one-main-component parity choice, (12) is the actual knot complement volume. The knot cusp remains unfilled. The whole mixed-source alias and complement estimates are separate inputs to the full invariant limit. The existing all-core majorant and far-color local estimate apply by (8); the [single-leaf alias theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md) and its finite source companion supply the new block comparison. The local geometric and packet conclusions above do not substitute for those estimates. ## 6. The root-leaf frontier is genuine The theorem above requires two completed root children. For the different closure \(C(hT(A_s))\), \(s\ge2\), the exact state is \[ \begin{aligned} A_s:&\quad X=1,\quad B=Y=1/s,\\ T(A_s):&\quad(B,X,Y)=(-1/s,1/s,1),\\ h:&\quad(B,X,Y)=(1/s,1/s,1). \end{aligned} \tag{13} \] The inner seed leaves all equal \(1/4\); the root leaf equals \(\arctan(s)/\pi\), with cotangent \(1/s\). Every retained seed gate is strict. Its successive output labels are \(b_j=\arctan(j)/\pi\), and \[ b_{j-1}<b_j<b_{j-1}+\frac14<1. \] The complete source therefore has a genuine strict optimizer. The original one-leaf/completed-child closing case has CAP sum \(\pi/2\), rather than \(\pi\), and the remaining convex cut/cusp proof gives the actual complete finite-volume metric. A flat-cell argument does not rule out this configuration as nonhyperbolic. The same local complete half-twist pairing proof applies. The limitation on reusing the signed high-index packet is its inner leaves at exactly \(1/4\). In the complete local source recurrence, the selected transport root and its competitor have equal modulus there, while their algebraic values remain distinct. For example, the original characteristic equation at \(x=1/4,t=0\) has roots \(\mu=\pm i\). This is a dominance boundary, not an eigenvalue collision. The old uniform high-index interpolation and decaying-competitor proof does not extend across it without additional source analysis. For \(s\ge3\), the root leaf even has cotangent below \(1/2\). These facts do not contradict (8): in (13), the root completed port has \(Y=1\), and its top turn exposes an internal completed \(X=1\). The strict root bounds (6) are unavailable. The still broader syntax \(C(hT(h))\) has the exact complete scalar \(\sum_r a_{N,r}^2\) and leaves at \(1/4\). This is a source-level warning against deducing a strict high-quarter packet from strict feasibility alone. Its separate complete geometric realization is not needed for the completed-root theorem. ## Dependencies The geometric inputs are the [ordered ideal prism](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md), [complete cell and cap construction](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), [stationary port identities](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md), and [literal bowtie cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). The [two-leaf geometry audit](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md) records the retained base and original primitive conventions. The local analytic inputs are the [signed complex packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md) and [actual marked deformation](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md). The separate new source and alias companions are linked above. This note concerns the stated completed-root construction. It does not assert a theorem for arbitrary turned-leaf expressions or all arborescent links.

title: Exact source composition with single-leaf Conway attachments
text: # Exact source composition with single-leaf Conway attachments 31 October 2026. original-source theorem. For the completed grammar $E::=hh\mid T(E)\mid EE\mid hE\mid Eh$ and cylindrical closures $C(FG)$ with **both root children completed**, the exact source has a strict complete optimizer, a primitive wire lattice, the retained finite complex packet, and whole-source alias and physical-color gaps at both parities. No additional individual-leaf condition is required. All physical colors, original support constraints, Hermite normal data, phases and normalization are retained. The proof below includes the exact finite support compiler and the single-leaf alias induction. Its analytic companion is the [single-leaf alias composition theorem](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md); the [geometric companion](actual_conway_single_leaf_geometric_composition.md) retains the actual metric and primitive marked interfaces. The [assembled long-filling theorem](actual_arborescent_single_leaf_long_twist_volume.md) states their consequence for the original invariant. Root-leaf closures with a quarter-index turning point remain a separate regime. These are literal four-port ribbon sources, not formal rational fractions or replacement coupons. ## 1. The literal compiler and an exact all-level support recursion Let h be the original turned complete-circle coupon, T the actual physical quarter-turn, and FG the original stack. Every copy is an independent box; its colors, signs, auxiliary circle and original mark are retained. For any finite expression in h,T,product the source is evaluated in the FULL algebra $H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)$, $d=N-1$ and $M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor$. Write $\widehat B_r$ for the actual normalized Newton basis and $s_r=\prod_{t=1}^r2\sin(\pi t/N)$, with $s_0=1$. The exact rules are $$ \begin{aligned} T\widehat B_r&=\widehat B_{d-r},\\ \widehat B_i\widehat B_j &=\sum_{r=\max(i,j)}^{i+j}\mu_{i,j,r}\widehat B_r,\\ \mu_{i,j,r}&=\frac{s_{i+j}s_r} {s_i s_j s_{r-i}s_{r-j}s_{i+j-r}}>0,\qquad i+j\le d. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ and the product is zero if i+j>=N. This is polynomial divisibility with multiplicities: repeated-root normals are not removed. The complete h has strictly positive coefficients exactly on [0,M]. For every positive pure compiled box, its nonempty finite Newton support is an INTEGER INTERVAL. If I_F=[l_F,u_F], the exact support compiler is $$ \begin{aligned} I_h&=[0,M],& I_{TF}&=[d-u_F,d-l_F],\\ I_{FG}&=\begin{cases} \varnothing,&l_F+l_G>d,\\ [\max(l_F,l_G),\min(d,u_F+u_G)],&l_F+l_G\le d. \end{cases} \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ An empty support propagates through both operations. Every index displayed in (2) has strictly positive coefficient. To verify the product assertion, let max(l_F,l_G)<=r<=min(d,u_F+u_G). Choose i,j in their original intervals with i,j<=r and i+j=max(r,l_F+l_G). Such integers exist because min(u_F,r)+min(u_G,r)>=r, while both upper bounds exceed their respective lower bounds. The chosen sum is<=d and r lies in [max(i,j),i+j], so (1) supplies a positive contribution. The reverse inclusion is immediate. This proves (2) at every level, without a full-support hypothesis or parity approximation. The actual closing scalar C_N(F)=phi(F) selects coordinate d; the cap scalar D_N(F)=phi(TF) selects coordinate zero. Hence exact closed support is read directly from (2), or for a cylindrical final product from $$ C_N(FG)=\sum_{r=0}^d f_r g_{d-r}.\tag{3} $$ All factors here have the existing physical normalization. For changed leaves T(R^epsilon L_j), use the same finite contraction (1),(3) with their actual signed core/alias arrays. Positivity and the interval conclusion are claimed only for the complete pure source; the compiler itself is valid without positivity. ## 2. An exact strict-state classification, separate from finite support A strictly realized open output b means all underlying leaf labels lie in (0,1/2), and every product satisfies $$ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1.\tag{4} $$ Turns impose y=1-x. For arbitrary finite h/T/product syntax, the set of strictly realized outputs is one of FOUR possibilities: $$ L=(0,1/2),\qquad H=(1/2,1),\qquad A=(0,1),\qquad \varnothing. \tag{5} $$ Here h has type L; T exchanges L,H, fixes A, and preserves emptiness. The product table is symmetric: $$ \begin{aligned} LL&\longmapsto A,& LA&\longmapsto A,& AA&\longmapsto A,\\ HL&\longmapsto H,& HA&\longmapsto H,& HH&\longmapsto\varnothing. \end{aligned}\tag{6} $$ If either child has empty strict-state set, so does its parent. This table is exhaustive, not a necessary-only filter. For LL at any b in (0,1), choose both inputs a with b/2<a<min(b,1/2). For LA, choose a sufficiently small L input c and A input b-c/2. The AA case follows by using two inputs in L. For HL or HA, necessarily b>1/2; choose the H input b-c/2 and the other input c>0 sufficiently small. HH violates x+y<1. These constructions also prove every asserted interval is attained. For a cylindrical final product C(FG), delete only its forced last gate. A strict reduced state exists exactly when $$ S_F\cap(1-S_G)\ne\varnothing.\tag{7} $$ where S is the strict output set. Thus LL and HH fail, while LA, HA, AA, and LH pass. Neither this classification nor an empty strict-state type asserts that the finite quantum source vanishes. For example T(h)T(h) has zero source at even levels, but at odd levels a nonzero boundary-only product supported at d; this follows directly from (2). The completed grammar used here is $$ E\ ::=\ hh\ \mid\ T(E)\ \mid\ EE\ \mid\ hE\ \mid\ Eh. \tag{8} $$ It may equivalently include any h^s, s>=2, as initial blocks. Every E in (8) has type A and admits a strict state at EVERY output b in (0,1). Consequently every fixed C(FG), F,G in (8), has a strict reduced state: choose both closing outputs1/2. A cylindrical closure with one bare leaf and one E also has strict states, but has a distinct packet issue in §5. ## 3. Primitive lattice, unique strict optimizer, and complete source No old all-output finite-support statement is imported. Contract every turn chain by its exact relation r->d-r. At a cylindrical final product, eliminate one root input using i+j=d and delete that gate, whose coefficient is exactly one. The root subtrees are disjoint. Hence no equation2r=d is created. The remaining unturned wire outputs are free integer coordinates; all other indices are integer affine functions with coefficients+1 or-1. If there are H original h leaves, there are H-1 binary products. Removing the last one leaves H-2 independent product outputs, H leaf outputs, and one closing relation. Thus the free dimension is $$ K=2H-3.\tag{9} $$ Round d times a strict reduced state in these primitive coordinates and restore eliminated indices exactly. Errors stay bounded for a fixed tree, whereas each strict inequality has a fixed macroscopic slack. All original leaf and gate support constraints hold for every sufficiently large N, at BOTH parities. In particular all leaf indices lie strictly below M; the even A2 missing top coordinate is irrelevant to this interior argument. For an arbitrary expression, a prescribed open output must have r_N/d->b in its ACTUAL strict-output interval S_E. For the completed grammar (8), S_E=(0,1), so every interior b is allowed. Fix that output first and round the remaining coordinates in a strict state at r_N/d. The original leaf/gate factorial bounds are uniform on the closed support and have O(log N) errors for a fixed tree. The usual leaf atoms (x,1/2-x,1/2), twice, and three gate atoms are unchanged. Any nonforced boundary maximum has a nonvertex-flat atom, possibly reached by descending through endpoint wires and turns. The segment to the constructed strict state has positive infinite entropy derivative there; no other atom has negative infinite derivative. Thus the reduced maximum is strict. The retained angle maps recover all free wires, so strict tetrahedral concavity gives a negative definite reduced Hessian and a unique optimizer. This is the original barrier/injectivity proof with the new strict-state construction. Polynomially many states give the upper limit. Primitive rounding of the strict maximizer gives a genuine positive single-state lower limit at every sufficiently large N. The original complete source therefore has its full positive exponential rate, and fixed-output profiles are analytic: $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_N^0=\max\mathcal A, \qquad f_E(b)=\max_{\text{output }b}\mathcal A_E.\tag{10} $$ This theorem is about the original positive source, not yet its mixed whole-source replacement or a new topological volume identification. ## 4. Normal forms and actual topological operations There are three distinct levels of simplification. (a) Literal stack associativity merely changes the heights and parentheses of fixed ordered boxes and is a boundary-preserving tangle isotopy. It retains every coupon, turn and frame. Flatten consecutive product vertices into an ORDERED list; do not move any factor through an intervening turn. This gives a useful actual compiler normal form with alternating product blocks and turned subexpressions. (b) In the full source algebra multiplication is commutative and T^2=1. One may therefore additionally reorder a product block or cancel adjacent turn operators when computing the scalar, with all mark conventions still recorded. These source equalities do NOT prove relative-boundary tangle isotopies for arbitrary boxes. In particular T is not multiplicative, and there is no valid rule T(FG)=(TF)(TG). The exact Frobenius identity phi((TF)G)=phi(F(TG)) follows by coefficient reversal, but it too must not be promoted to an unproved physical tangle move. For the open positive expression grammar, flattening product blocks, using source-only commutative reordering, and removing adjacent algebraic turns gives a syntactic criterion for the OLD A_s>=2 grammar: every leaf belongs to an unturned product block, and in each maximal product block the number of direct bare h factors is either zero or at least two; each turned child must recursively satisfy the same condition. In particular a lone h or T(h) is not an old completed expression. The new grammar (8) additionally permits one bare h beside a completed factor. Thus h T(hh), and chains built by E_(n+1)=h T(E_n) starting at hh, are new presentations under this restricted normalization. This is NOT a proof of a new knot isotopy class or of inequivalence under all possible source identities. Some closed instances regroup into old grammar: for example C((h T(A2))A2)=C(A3 T(A2)) as a source scalar. Keep the actual ordered diagram when drawing any geometric claim. (c) The [existing boundary cap reduction](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md) has a separate topology proof. With a closing flag C or D, a turn switches the flag; a D-product splits into its two D-children because $$ D_N(FG)=D_N(F)D_N(G).\tag{11} $$ The physical empty collar exhibits the corresponding TWO-punctured sphere and componentwise connected sum, with the upper/lower cap components and mark transported. A C-product is retained, not factored. This gives an exact source and topological boundary reduction for arbitrary boxes, but is not a JSJ decomposition or an isotopy reducing every new tree to old robust ones. The entire rational angle polytope also splits at a D-product. ## 5. The precise high-index and packet interface The original stationary port variables are B=cot(pi b), X^2+Y^2-B^2=1, X,Y>0. A leaf has (B,X,Y)=(X,X,1). Every completed E in (8) satisfies -Y<B<X at each interior optimized output. The $A_2$ base and ordinary completed product/turn steps are proved in the [existing port theorem](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) and the [two-leaf base extension](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md). For a single leaf attachment to a completed child, stationarity gives common X and, writing B for the child cotangent, $$ \begin{aligned} B_{\mathrm{parent}}&=X-\frac1{X+B},\\ Y_{\mathrm{parent}}&=\frac{Y_{\mathrm{child}}}{X+B},\\ Y_{\mathrm{child}}&=\sqrt{1+B^2-X^2},\qquad X+B>0. \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ This preserves -Y_parent<B_parent<X. If X>=1 this is immediate from B>0 and X^2-1>=0. If X<1, put h0=sqrt(1-X^2), alpha0=arccos X. The leaf has angle alpha0 in B=h0 cot(alpha); the completed child has beta>alpha0, and X+B>0 says alpha0+beta<pi. Their sum gives the strict parent inequality. At completed/completed closure C(FG), the original matching of ports gives X,Y<1 at both root children. At any product with X<1, every child angle is at least alpha0, with equality only for a leaf; a completed child's angle is strictly greater. The bound Y_parent<1 means alpha+beta<pi-alpha0, so each completed child also has Y<1. Turns exchange X,Y. Hence all completed ports in the closed grammar have X,Y<1, and every leaf has X<1, i.e. its Newton coordinate is strictly greater than1/4. For a direct single attachment, Y_parent<1 and B<X sharpen this to $$ \frac12<X<1,\qquad \frac1{2X}-X<B<X.\tag{13} $$ Indeed Y_child<X+B squares to1<2X(X+B), and B<X then forces X>1/2. The same lower X bound for the leaves in an A2 base follows from its Y=1/(2X)<1. Thus every leaf of a fixed completed/completed tree has a positive margin inside (1/4,atan(2)/pi). No uniform margin over all trees is asserted. This supplies the exact LOCAL changed-source packet assumptions: fixed strict high-index window, the original relative exponential interpolation, primitive dimension (9), and all original affine shifts. Each leaf contributes N^(1/2), each of H-2 retained gates N^(-3/2), giving summand N^(3-H). Its Gaussian lattice factor N^(K/2) produces N^(3/2). The changed leaf and gate derivatives in the original integer-offset amplitude remain mandatory. At completeness the multiplier is nonzero, and the separately even color Hessian retains diagonal entries $$ -\frac{2\pi X_l}{1-\epsilon_l iX_l}.\tag{14} $$ with negative real part. These are local finite packet facts; the full mixed source still needs §6. Root-leaf closures require an explicit exclusion from this automatic interface. At C(hE), the completed root may have Y=1, and a turn can pass that equality to X=1 deeper inside. In the exact example C(h T(A_s)), A_s at X=1 has B_s=Y_s=1/s. The turn gives (-1/s,1/s,1), which matches the closing leaf with X=1/s. Thus all s inner leaf indices are EXACTLY1/4, while the remaining leaf is arccot(1/s)/pi. Strict complete states exist, but the inherited strict-quarter packet cannot simply be quoted. The even simpler C(h T(h)) has exact scalar sum_r a_r^2 and a unique complete leaf coordinate1/4. These are source/packet limitations, not asserted topology or hyperbolicity obstructions. The [isolated $C(A_3)$ theorem](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md) is separately proved and does not justify every root-leaf closure. ## 6. Exact reduction of the mixed gap to one new local dual inequality Fix the actual closed complete optimizer of C(FG) in (8). For each completed subtree E let b_E be its optimized output and lambda_E=f'_E(b_E). The useful inductive statement is, uniformly in every physical color and finite output r and for EACH specified alias subset S_E, $$ \left|[\widehat B_r]E_{S_E}\right| \le\exp\!\left\{N\left[f_E(b_E) +\lambda_E\left(\frac rN-b_E\right)-\delta_{S_E}\right]+o(N)\right\}. \tag{15} $$ where delta_empty=0 and delta_nonempty>0. No coefficient lower bound or sharpness of this envelope is asserted. A2 supplies this statement through the uniform block lemma. At a turn, exact coordinate reversal retains it with lambda sign reversed and an O(1) affine exponent cost. At a product of completed subtrees, their tangents and the concavity of the actual gate m give the parent's tangent by stationary cancellation; child gaps add. Every state retains the original i+j<=d constraint. The only new step is hE. At its actual common-X state let $$ \begin{aligned} a&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}X}{\pi},\qquad y=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}B}{\pi},\\ z&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}(X-1/(X+B))}{\pi},\\ \lambda_c&=2\log(X/Y_{\mathrm{child}}),\\ \lambda_p&=\lambda_c+2\log(X+B). \end{aligned}\tag{16} $$ All arccot values lie in(0,1) after division by pi. The parameter region is exactly (13). The local inequality needed for this induction, proved in §7, is the strictly positive margin $$ \begin{aligned} \Delta(X,B)&=g(a)+\lambda_cy+m(a,y,z)-\lambda_pz\\ &\quad-\max_D\{k(u)+\lambda_cv+m(u,v,w)-\lambda_pw\}>0,\\ D&=\{(u,v,w):u,v\ge0,\ \max(u,v)\le w\le u+v\le1\}. \end{aligned}\tag{17} $$ The actual alias index u is NOT restricted below1/2. The child output v also retains its whole original interval. The finite kernel and all normal directions have already been accounted for in (1). If the new leaf is core, replace k(u) by gtilde(u), u<=1/2. Concavity and stationarity give equality of that maximum with the pure reference in (17). Thus a contaminated child transfers its existing gap. If the new leaf is alias, (17) supplies a gap whether the child is clean or already contaminated; in the latter case the child gap adds. This proves (15) inductively once (17) is proved at the finitely many actual attachment states. The fixed tree needs only positive margins there, not a universal lower bound throughout the open parameter region. Finally the two root tangents cancel on the literal i+j=d. The N versus d shift gives only a fixed O(1) exponent. Summing polynomially many original states and finitely many sectors produces a whole-source alias gap. The all-core concave majorant has its unique strict maximum at the actual pure optimizer; compact outside-window and actual local far-color losses then give the whole physical-color complement gap. This is the same finite source-to-packet interface as the block proof, with (17) as its ONLY new analytic alias obligation. Section7 supplies it. The actual geometric and marked filling interfaces remain separately sourced; the finite contraction alone is not a new topological volume proof. ## 7. The exact square certificate discharges the remaining inequality Write mu=lambda_c and lambda=lambda_p. Define the two exact variational quantities on the original product tetrahedron D from (17): $$ \begin{aligned} P(\mu,\lambda)&=\max_{D,\,u\le1/2} \{g(u)+m(u,v,w)+\mu v-\lambda w\},\\ Q(\mu,\lambda)&=\max_D \{k(u)+m(u,v,w)+\mu v-\lambda w\}. \end{aligned}\tag{18} $$ The pure objective is concave. At the actual point(a,y,z), its three derivatives vanish by the original stationary equations, so its maximum is exactly the pure reference in (17). The same is true with gtilde in place of g: near a>1/4 they agree, and both resulting objectives are concave. Hence P-Q=Delta(X,B) for the actual slopes. For 1/2<X<=2/3 and L=1/(2X)-X<B<X, the two slopes belong to [-2log2,0]. To check this directly, B is positive and $$ \frac1{4X^2}<Y_{\mathrm{child}}^2<1,\qquad \log(X^2)<\mu<\log(4X^4)\le\log(64/81)<0.\tag{19} $$ For lambda(B)=log[X^2(X+B)^2/(1+B^2-X^2)], its derivative has the sign of 1-X^2-XB, which is positive throughout this region since 1-X^2-XB>1-2X^2>=1/9. At B=L and B=X its limits are log(X^2) and log(4X^4), respectively. These are both in[-log4,0]. Thus the following certificate applies to every actual low-X attachment. The [exact attachment verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate.py) imports the unchanged outward rational arithmetic and analytic enclosures from the [two-leaf verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_two_leaf_block_alias_certificate.py). Its [fixed rational data](../experiments/conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate.json) is a recursively subdivided quadtree of 55 closed dyadic rectangles covering $(\mu,\lambda)/\log2\in[-2,0]^2$. Each leaf has a rational pure point p with p_1<1/2 and a rational strict alias point q, both in D. No optimizer is used by verification. For H=k+m, concavity gives its global affine upper tangent at q. For each of the four rectangle corners and each of the FOUR original vertices $$ (0,0,0),\quad(1,0,1),\quad(0,1,1),\quad(1/2,1/2,1/2). $$ the verifier checks the lower bound $$ \begin{aligned} &g(p_1)+m(p)-[H(q)+\nabla H(q)\mathbin{\cdot}(w-q)]\\ &\qquad+\mu(p_2-w_2)-\lambda(p_3-w_3)>\frac1{1000}. \end{aligned}\tag{20} $$ This is880 exact inequalities. Affinity in each slope and in w extends (20) throughout the entire rectangle times D. The pure point provides a lower bound for P, while the tangent provides an upper bound for Q. Recursive four-way subdivision proves full square coverage without gaps; no sampling or approximate coverage enters the argument. All interval arithmetic uses outward integer rounding at denominator 10^40. The Machin arctangent, sine Taylor, atanh-log and integrated Euler-sine expansions have exact rational remainders. The imported arithmetic and analytic-function syntax trees are identical to those in the block certificate. The [recorded result](../experiments/conway_single_leaf_attachment_certificate_results.json) gives the least certified rational lower bound: $$ \frac{55437191760019874892517972684020763373}{10^{40}} >\frac1{1000}.\tag{21} $$ Thus P-Q>1/1000 on the full square, and in particular Delta>1/1000 at every actual attachment with X<=2/3. For $X\ge2/3$, the [existing exact full-leaf tangent certificate](actual_conway_algebraic_leaf_alias_certificate.md) gives $$ k(u)\le g(a)+g'(a)(u-a)-\frac1{2500},\qquad 0\le u\le1. \tag{22} $$ The tangent of the concave gate m and the identities g'(a)+m_u=0, mu+m_v=0, m_w=lambda then cancel all three variables. Consequently Delta>1/2500 also throughout this remaining actual region. Neither part discards alias indices above half. The induction (15) is now proved for every fixed completed tree (8). Every contaminated A2 starts with its known block gap; every newly aliased single attachment has (20) or (22); an existing child gap passes unchanged or adds. Turns and all exact closing offsets cost only O(1) in the exponent. Since the tree is fixed, summing its actual finite sectors gives a positive whole-source alias margin. Compactness and the actual far-color estimates then give the entire physical-color complement gap as described in §6. These are source bounds for all original colors and both parity sequences. Together with §5 they supply the unchanged finite complex packet and whole-source hypotheses for the separately verified geometric/filling interfaces. No additional individual leaf certificate is required. ## 8. Inputs The original [physical source/compiler](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md) and [positive full-Newton multiplication](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md) supply the exact finite operations. The [two-leaf source proof](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md), §§1–2, supplies the predecessor strict-state and rounding arguments. The [complete geometric proof](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), §§3–6, and the port inputs linked above retain the original leaf and prism data. The local changed source is the [actual mixed complex packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md). The induction starts with the [uniform two-leaf alias lemma](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) and its [finite block source adapter](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md). The exact finite support and strict-state tables are proved for arbitrary $h/T$/product syntax. The all-output, strict-quarter and local-packet extension, and the automatic mixed gaps proved here, are restricted to (8) with completed/completed $C(FG)$ closure. The normal-form discussion distinguishes actual stack isotopy, algebraic scalar identities, and the separately proved cap connected-sum moves. It does not assert coverage of all algebraic tangles or knots, or exhibit a new isotopy class. The root-leaf quarter examples prevent extending the inherited packet from strict feasibility alone. The rational certificate uses rigorous function enclosures; no continuum inequality is inferred from sampled or floating-point tests.

title: Every complete robust Conway leaf lies strictly above one quarter
text: # Every complete robust Conway leaf lies strictly above one quarter 29 October 2026. For every retained cylindrical robust factor, the unique complete source optimizer satisfies x_l>1/4 at EVERY h leaf. This follows from the actual g,m stationarity equations and a preserved port inequality. No circle-packing estimate is assumed. The result is about the existing positive complete source; replacement by a different quantum coupon still requires its own local and global source estimates. ## 1. Positive port variables from the actual source derivatives For a proper robust expression E at output b in (0,1), let f_E(b)=v_E(b)/pi be its strictly optimized source action. Put B=cot(pi b), kappa=exp(-f'_E(b)), X=sqrt((1+B^2)/(1+kappa)), Y=sqrt(kappa) X. (1) Thus X,Y are positive and X^2+Y^2-B^2=1. The already proved strict maximum theorem makes these derivatives legitimate at every proper macro-port of the complete optimizer. A literal turn sends (B,X,Y) -> (-B,Y,X). (2) At a product F G with strict input/output x,y,z, write U=cot(pi x), V=cot(pi y), Z=cot(pi z), and D=(U+V)Z-UV+1>0. The strict inequality x+y<1 gives U+V>0. Directly differentiating the SAME seven-factorial action m gives kappa_F=exp(m_x)=(U+V)(U-Z)/D, kappa_G=exp(m_y)=(U+V)(V-Z)/D, kappa_out=exp(-m_z)=(U-Z)(V-Z)/D. (3) Here the first two signs use f'_F=-m_x and f'_G=-m_y at the inner maximum. Since 1+kappa_F=(1+U^2)/D, 1+kappa_G=(1+V^2)/D, 1+kappa_out=(1+Z^2)/D, all THREE ports have the same X=sqrt(D), and Z=(UV+X^2-1)/(U+V), Y_out=Y_F Y_G/(U+V). (4) The positive square root in the last identity is fixed by U+V>0. These are exact algebraic consequences of stationarity, not new gluing assumptions. ## 2. A strict inequality preserved by the entire robust grammar Every proper robust port satisfies -Y < B < X. (5) First check A=h^3. At a leaf the actual action has g'(a)=2log cot(pi a). Therefore its coordinates are B=X=cot(pi a)>0, Y=1. The common-X identity (3) makes the three stationary seed leaf coordinates equal. Composing twice using (4) gives B_2=(2X^2-1)/(2X), Y_2=1/(2X), B_A=X(4X^2-3)/(4X^2-1), Y_A=1/(4X^2-1). (6) The second product has B_2+X>0, so X>1/2. Consequently X-B_A=2X/(4X^2-1)>0, B_A+Y_A=(2X-1)(X+1)/(2X+1)>0, which proves (5) for every interior seed output. Equation (2) preserves (5), because its two inequalities exchange. It remains to check a product of two ports satisfying (5). If the common X>=1, the identities Y_F^2=1+U^2-X^2 and U>-Y_F force U>0; similarly V>0. Also U<X, V<X and U>sqrt(X^2-1), V>sqrt(X^2-1). Hence 0<X-U<1 and 0<X-V<1 (also at X=1). Equation (4) gives Z>0 and Z-X=((X-U)(X-V)-1)/(U+V)<0. Thus -Y_out<Z<X. If 0<X<1, put h=sqrt(1-X^2), and write uniquely U=h cot alpha, Y_F=h csc alpha, V=h cot beta, Y_G=h csc beta, 0<alpha,beta<pi. With alpha_0=arccos X, the upper inequalities U<X,V<X say alpha,beta>alpha_0. The actual U+V>0 says alpha+beta<pi. Equation (4) is now exactly Z=h cot(alpha+beta), Y_out=h csc(alpha+beta).
