(7) Thus Z<X since alpha+beta>alpha_0, while Z>-Y_out follows from cot t+csc t=cot(t/2)>0 for 0<t<pi. This proves preservation of (5), and hence proves it for all robust expressions. ## 3. Closure and downward propagation For a retained factor C(FG), its two proper children F,G are robust. After deleting the final forced-flat gate, their outputs are b,1-b. Stationarity of f_F(b)+f_G(1-b) gives equal derivatives and therefore equal kappa. Their port data are consequently (B,X,Y) and (-B,X,Y). Applying (5) to both gives |B|<min(X,Y). Since X^2+Y^2-B^2=1, this implies 0<X<1, 0<Y<1 (8) at both root child ports. These two strict bounds propagate down the ROBUST macro-tree. They are preserved by a turn. At a product, X is common, hence already below one. Use (7). Its parent Y_out<1 means alpha_0<alpha+beta<pi-alpha_0. Each robust child already has alpha,beta>alpha_0 by (5), so each also lies below pi-alpha_0. Therefore sin alpha,sin beta>h, which gives Y_F,Y_G<1. Thus (8) holds at every robust seed port. STOP this propagation at A: its individual leaf ports have Y=1, so (8) is not asserted for those ports. Instead use (6): all three seed leaves share the seed's X. Since this X is strictly below one, cot(pi x_l)=X<1, hence x_l>1/4. (9) The remaining retained factor C(A) is equally explicit. Its two closing children are h^2 and h; their cotangents are opposite. The same root matching again makes X common. Thus B_2=-X in (6), forcing X=1/2 and x_l=atan(2)/pi>1/4 for all three leaves. This proves (9) for every retained cylindrical robust factor. For each FIXED expression there is a positive minimum margin above 1/4 because it has finitely many leaves. No uniform margin across all expressions is claimed or needed here. The theorem locates the whole positive-source optimizer in the strict local regime required by the proposed odd-half-twist packet. It does not itself identify that packet with the pure source or prove survival of its summed complex amplitude. No uniform margin over all expressions or odd-coupon source theorem follows from this leaf-parameter bound.

title: A whole-source gap from exact two-leaf Conway block transport
text: # A whole-source gap from exact two-leaf Conway block transport 31 October 2026. original-source theorem. For every fixed closed $C(FG)$ built from seeds $A_s=h^s$, $s\ge2$, actual turns and products, the full mixed source has a uniform alias gap and a physical-color complement gap at both parities. No individual-leaf certificate is required. The proof combines the exact finite contraction below with the [uniform two-leaf block lemma](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md), whose exact rational certificate supplies a margin greater than $1/100$. All Hermite normal directions, physical colors, phases and original targets are retained. Isolated $C(A_2)$ remains excluded. ## 1. Original algebra and exact alias provenance Put d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), kappa=q^(d^2/2), and use the full physical algebra H_N=C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2). Its normalized Newton basis is Bhat_r, 0<=r<=d, with sine factorial s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N). The genuine turn T and marked cylindrical functional obey $$ T\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{d-r},\qquad \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)=\begin{cases}1&i+j=d,\\0&i+j\ne d.\end{cases}\tag{1} $$ The EXACT full-algebra product is $$ \begin{aligned} \widehat B_i\widehat B_j&=\sum_{r=\max(i,j)}^{i+j}\mu_{i,j,r}\widehat B_r,\\ \mu_{i,j,r}&=\frac{s_{i+j}s_r}{s_i s_j s_{r-i}s_{r-j}s_{i+j-r}}>0, \qquad i+j\le d. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ and is zero for i+j>=N. The latter is polynomial divisibility with node multiplicities, so it does not discard Hermite normals. Formula(2) applies to arbitrary i,j, including an input above M; no new product rule is used for aliases. For each actual auxiliary color 1<=j<=N, let the pure leaf have the exact split h_j=C_j+A_j. For j=N-h, 0<=h<=M, $$ C_j=\sum_{v=h}^{M}\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^2s_{v-h}s_{v+h}}\widehat B_v, \qquad A_j=(-1)^N h_h,\qquad h_0=0.\tag{3} $$ For j<=floor(N/2), C_j=0 and A_j=h_j. In particular A_N=0. In every case A_j lies in span{Bhat_v:v>=ceil(N/2)}, with each coefficient bounded byN/2 in modulus. More precisely, for 1<=h<=floor(N/2), $$ h_h=\sum_{t=0}^{h-1}(-1)^{h-1+t}b_{h,t}\widehat B_{d-t},\qquad b_{h,t}=\frac{s_t^2s_{h+t}}{s_{2t+1}s_{h-t-1}}>0.\tag{4} $$ These identities include every original auxiliary pivot, with no extra1/j or1/N factor. They are the actual complete-circle source identities, not spectral values with a guessed normal completion. For epsilon=+-1 define the original half-twist transport $$ \begin{aligned} T_\epsilon(f)&=T\bigl(R^\epsilon T(f)\bigr),\\ T_\epsilon(\widehat B_v)&=\kappa^\epsilon(-1)^v \sum_{r=0}^{v}q^{\epsilon v(r+1)}\binom vr_q\widehat B_r,\\ \binom vr_q&=\frac{s_v}{s_r s_{v-r}}. \end{aligned}\tag{5} $$ For epsilon=0 use the identity. Set C_j^epsilon=T_epsilon(C_j) and A_j^epsilon=T_epsilon(A_j). Thus the changed physical leaf is EXACTLY C_j^epsilon+A_j^epsilon=T(R^epsilon L_j), in the entire algebra. The core has support r<=M at every sign; an odd alias may have any0<=r<=d. The color-specific alias formula is the finite sum of (4) and (5), with all their signs and q phases retained. A useful exact warning is visible already at h=1: h_1=Bhat_d and [d choose r]_q=1. Consequently T_epsilon(h_1) has a nonzero modulus-one coefficient at EVERY r (apart from its unit kappa factor). Its square has a nonzero constant coefficient, namely the square of that constant. More generally the product for either pair of odd signs has a nonzero constant. A pure alias h_1 times an odd alias has its nonzero r=d coefficient. Only the two-pure-alias product vanishes by the genuine nilradical square. Thus an arbitrary signed A2 block cannot discard its double-alias sector. ## 2. Exact block kernel and supports For arrays u_i,v_j in the same full Newton basis define $$ \begin{aligned} (u\star v)_r&=\sum_{(i,j)\in D_N(r)}\mu_{i,j,r}u_i v_j,\\ D_N(r)&=\{0\le i,j\le d:i+j\le d,\ \max(i,j)\le r\le i+j\}. \end{aligned}\tag{6} $$ For an A2 seed with actual independent physical colors and signs, its exact four sectors are CC,AC,CA,AA under this kernel. Every seed coefficient is the sum of those sectors; no nilradical quotient or covariance of a projected coupon is being invoked. A CC sector restricts i,j<=M. An AC sector restricts only its core index<=M; a pure alias further restricts its own index>=ceil(N/2). An AA sector must still satisfy i+j<=d. In particular TWO inputs above half cannot survive together, but ONE such input is allowed. The same kernel applies at every higher product, independent of whether its inputs already contain aliases or have been turned. A macro-turn reverses its COMPLETE coefficient array: u_r becomes u_(d-r), with no extra phase. At the root C(FG), equation(1) contracts precisely the pairs i+j=d. These rules propagate every original sector and target through any finite tree. They never introduce one variable per repeated occurrence of a wire. Grouping the two leaves and their one gate as (6) is just associating finite sums, not a change of tangle or a replacement source. Higher products and turns remain the original physical operations. The inside gate appears exactly once, the two circle factors remain exactly once each, and the single global marked closure is unchanged. ## 3. Uniform closed-domain envelopes, including inputs above half Use the original local upper rates $$ \begin{aligned} \widetilde g(x)&=g(\max(x,1/4)),\quad0\le x\le1/2,\\ k(x)&=-2J(x/2),\quad0\le x\le1,\\ J(x)&=\int_0^x\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x). \end{aligned}\tag{7} $$ Uniformly over all physical colors, signs, finite indices and both level parities, core coefficients have rate<=gtilde and aliases have rate<=k, with a single error e_N->0. A pure core is bounded by g<=gtilde; a pure alias has polynomial coefficients and rate0<=k. These are the actual transport bounds, not termwise estimates on an incorrectly truncated physical sum. The uniform positive Newton product rate is $$ \begin{aligned} m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z),\\ D&=\{x,y\ge0:\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ It stays continuous and concave on ALL of D, including x>1/2 or y>1/2. To check this from the original atoms, put p=z-x,q=z-y,r=x+y-z,w=1-x-y. Then the three normalized angle triples are $$ (y,x,w),\qquad(p,q,2r+w),\qquad(p+q,r,r+w). $$ All entries are nonnegative and each triple sums to1 on D; their volume sum is pi m. No half-coordinate assumption occurs in this derivation. The exact factorial formula gives log mu=N m(i/N,j/N,r/N)+O(log N) uniformly on its finite support. An input sum above d is ZERO, not an analytic continuation of (8). For z in[0,1], define the closed seed envelopes $$ \begin{aligned} G_{CC}(z)&=\max_{D,\,x,y\le1/2}[\widetilde g(x)+\widetilde g(y)+m(x,y,z)],\\ G_{AC}(z)&=\max_{D,\,y\le1/2}[k(x)+\widetilde g(y)+m(x,y,z)],\\ G_{AA}(z)&=\max_D[k(x)+k(y)+m(x,y,z)]. \end{aligned}\tag{9} $$ where each maximization retains D. G_CA=G_AC by exact symmetry. These are upper envelopes, not claimed coefficient rates or lower asymptotics. Their values are finite, continuous and concave: the fibers are compact, admit continuous feasible perturbations, and the joint actions are concave. Uniformly for every actual output r and all physical colors, $$ \left|[\widehat B_r](\mathrm{sector})\right| \le\exp\!\left[N\bigl(G_{\mathrm{sector}}(r/N)+o(1)\bigr)\right].\tag{10} $$ Indeed (6) has at mostN^2 summands, each satisfies the same compact-domain bound, and the input restrictions in(9) contain its true support. Missing boundary states, zero coefficients and exact cancellations can only improve the upper bound. The O(logN) product error and uniform leaf error remain o(N) after this finite multiplication. One may retain the physical complementary-color parameter chi=h/N to use k_chi(x)=J(x+chi)-J(x)-J(chi) for x<=1-2chi and k(x) otherwise, from the exact old transport formula. This improves(9) without changing(6). Nothing here requires maximizing colors independently before the physical filling sum. ## 4. The uniform block inequality at the actual complete state At an actual complete A2 seed let both leaf coordinates be a and its output be b. Its strict profile is F2(b)=2g(a)+m(a,a,b). With X=cot(pi a), $$ \cot(\pi b)=X-\frac1{2X},\qquad Y=\frac1{2X},\qquad F_2'(b)=-\log\bigl[(Y/X)^2\bigr]=2\log(2X^2)=:s(X).\tag{11} $$ For a proper seed in the closed $s\ge2$ grammar, $1/2<X<1$. The [uniform block lemma](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) proves the following inequalities on the larger closed range $1/2\le X\le1$: $$ \begin{aligned} G_{AC}(z)&\le F_2(b)+s(X)(z-b)-\frac1{100},\\ G_{AA}(z)&\le F_2(b)+s(X)(z-b)-\frac1{100},\qquad0\le z\le1. \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ One does not require that every alias leaf separately lie below its complete tangent. Nor may one delete x+y<=1 when checking(12): that would bound a different, larger problem. The corresponding CC inequality with zero loss already follows from the original joint concavity and seed stationarity. At(a,a,b), a>1/4, so gtilde agrees locally with g; the x,y derivatives of g(x)+g(y)+m vanish. Its joint supporting plane therefore has ONLY the output slope s(X). This proves G_CC(z)<=F2(b)+s(X)(z-b), with equality attained atz=b. Strictness of the original state identifies its equality set locally, as needed below. The companion proof encloses every transcendental quantity by rational intervals and checks global supporting planes on sixteen exact intervals of $s(X)/\log2\in[-2,2]$. Its smallest certified dual margin exceeds $1/25$; the conservative $1/100$ in (12) is therefore uniform. The certificate retains all vertices of the actual AC and AA product polytopes. It uses feasible pure states for a lower bound and globally concave alias tangents for an upper bound. Finite diagnostics are not used as proof, and (10) alone would not imply (12). ## 5. The whole closed-tree source gap Consider a fixed closed C(FG) in the s>=2 grammar. Expand the source by the original choice of core or alias at EACH leaf. In every A2 seed group its two choices and its internal gate by(6). Leave larger seeds expanded into leaves and gates; all their complete leaves have the old automatic interval 1/4<a<atan(sqrt2)/pi and therefore retain a positive leaf tangent margin. By the uniform block lemma, (12) holds at EVERY actual A2 seed of this fixed complete optimizer. Its margin $1/100$ and the old positive margins at the other leaves have a positive common lower bound $\gamma$. For an expanded sector containing at least one alias, use a positive-loss bound(12) on any contaminated A2 seed, or the old leaf bound on its alias in a larger seed. Use the zero-loss CC block bound on unaffected A2 seeds and the original complete tangents elsewhere. All these tangents are taken at the SAME original global complete optimum. The internal derivatives of an eliminated A2 seed vanish; its output coefficient is exactly(11). Thus replacing that subaction by its profile tangent preserves every derivative at the uncontracted original boundary wire. Sum the remaining actual gate tangents and retain every turn relation and the final root input relation. Original stationarity cancels ALL free linear terms. The result for this alias sector is at most F0-gamma. At finite N use r/N, not a silently shifted lattice. Product inequalities remain inD; turn and closing equations have right side d/N=1-1/N. Every fixed tangent has finite slope, so the affine cancellation error isO(1/N), henceO(1) in the exponent. For fixed H there are only polynomially many remaining wire states and finitely many sectors. The finite coefficient bounds in(10) therefore imply, after decreasing gamma, $$ \sup_{\text{all physical colors}}|Z_N-Z_N^{\mathrm{core}}| \le\exp\!\left[N(F_0-\gamma/2)\right].\tag{13} $$ for all sufficiently large N, at both parities. Every original normal term, physical color, unit Cartan phase and actual mark remains in this bound. There is no coefficientwise statement about an arbitrary external source; this is the stated closed original tree at its own complete stationarity. The remaining physical-color complement proof is inherited without requiring an open block lower bound. Before block contraction, the all-core majorant is the concave sum of gtilde and the same gates on the full original polytope. It agrees locally with the strict pure action, so the complete optimum is its unique global maximum. Outside a fixed strict full-wire window it has a compact gap. Inside, every leaf lies below a fixed beta<1/2; if some original color is outside the small complete corridor, the existing strict actual core recurrence estimate loses a positive amount at that leaf. These two regions give a uniform whole-core complement gap. Add(13) to get the entire physical-source complement gap. The exact complex packet, primitive lattice and marked geometric interfaces are unchanged. More explicitly, for each sufficiently small fixed $\delta>0$ there is $\gamma_\delta>0$ such that $$ \sup_{\exists\,l:\,N-j_l\ge\delta N}|Z_N(j_1,\ldots,j_H)| \le\exp\!\left[N(F_0-\gamma_\delta)\right] \tag{14} $$ for all sufficiently large $N$. The expression and its half-twist signs are fixed before this limit; all physical colors are included. Because (12) holds on the FULL proper-seed range, no individual-leaf algebraic cutoff remains in (13)–(14). These are the missing whole-source inputs for the existing exact packet and original long-filling transfer. After all auxiliary fillings and a loop-free parity choice, that transfer's geometric conclusion concerns the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement. The separate primitive slope, nonzero normalization and fixed sufficiently long filling hypotheses remain those of the original transfer theorem. This does not identify every arborescent template with the stated grammar. ## Inputs Exact identities(1)–(6): [original positive Newton multiplication](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md) §§1–2; [exact pure-color core and alias](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md) §§1–4,6; [full half-twist transport](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md) §§1–2. Uniform envelopes and concavity: [original mixed-source supporting-plane argument](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) §§3–5 and [original variational action](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md) §§1–2,4. Strict complete state, ports and unchanged packet: [two-leaf source and packet interface](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md) and [two-leaf complete and marked geometry](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md). No private diagnostic is an input.

title: Exact monotone alias response of a two-leaf Conway block
text: # Exact monotone alias response of a two-leaf Conway block 31 October 2026. analytical and original-source statement. The one- and two-alias conjugate gaps of an actual two-leaf seed increase with its complete output slope throughout the proper-port range. The proof retains the original multiplication constraints and the core plateau. It also gives a restriction on where a leafwise failing seed can occur in the selected complete geometry. The independently proved [uniform block certificate](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) supplies positive gaps on the entire interval, including its lower endpoint. That proof does not depend on the monotonicity derived here. Conversely, the present response proof does not use that certificate until its final consequence. There is no circular dependency. Use the original functions \[ \begin{aligned} J(t)&=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi v))\,dv,\\ g(a)&=J(2a)-4J(a),\\ \overline g(a)&=g(\max(a,1/4)),\qquad 0\le a\le1/2,\\ k(a)&=-2J(a/2),\qquad 0\le a\le1,\\ m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). \end{aligned} \] The product domain is \(D=\{x,y\ge0:\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}\). These are the [original core/alias envelopes](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) and seven-factorial multiplication action. They are upper bounds for the actual full Newton source, including its normal directions; they are not replacement coupons or asserted coefficient lower rates. ## 1. A failing seed must face a turn or the deleted closing product At a proper \(A_2\) seed, let \(X=\cos\alpha\), where \(0<\alpha<\pi/3\). Its selected port is \[ B=X-\frac1{2X}=\sin\alpha\cot(2\alpha), \qquad Y=\frac1{2X}=\sin\alpha\csc(2\alpha). \] Suppose this seed enters a retained macro product without an intervening odd turn. The other proper child has the same \(X\) and angle \(\beta>\alpha\). The proper parent has \(Y_{\mathrm{parent}}<1\), so its product angle satisfies \[ 2\alpha+\beta<\pi-\alpha. \] Hence \(4\alpha<\pi\), or \(X>1/\sqrt2\). Such an \(A_2\) already passes the old leaf interval. An even number of intervening turns has the same effect on these exact port variables; this is not an isotopy assertion about the physical tangle. More generally, an unturned completed top product at \(X\le1/\sqrt2\) has two input angles greater than \(\alpha\). Its output angle exceeds \(2\alpha\ge\pi/2\), so its \(B\) is negative. This includes an unturned seed \(A_s\), \(s\ge2\), expanded into products. A seed failing the algebraic leaf cutoff, \(X<2/3\), has \[ B<-\frac1{12},\qquad Y>\frac34. \] It cannot directly enter a retained macro product without an odd turn. If the unturned \(A_2\) itself is a closed root child, its reflected sibling has positive \(B\) and the same \(X<2/3\). That sibling must have an odd top turn after consecutive turns are reduced in the port formulas. These statements follow from the [actual two-leaf geometry](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md) and its strict proper-port inequalities. Alone, they do not prove an alias entropy gap. ## 2. Fixed-output alias blocks are strictly interior For \(0<b<1\), define \[ \begin{aligned} H_{AC}(b) &=\max_{\substack{(x,y,b)\in D\\y\le1/2}} \{k(x)+\overline g(y)+m(x,y,b)\},\\ H_{AA}(b) &=\max_{(x,y,b)\in D} \{k(x)+k(y)+m(x,y,b)\}. \end{aligned} \tag{1} \] The \(AC\) order is immaterial by the exact symmetry of \(m\). Both profiles are continuous and concave on the closed interval \([0,1]\). At every interior output, their maximizing inputs and all product inequalities are strict. Here is the boundary justification. Each fixed-output domain has a strict point: take \(x=y\) between \(b/2\) and \(\min(b,1/2)\). Put \(p=b-x\), \(q=b-y\), \(r=x+y-b\), \(w=1-x-y\). The original decomposition of \(\pi m\) has angle triples \[ (y,x,w),\qquad(p,q,2r+w),\qquad(p+q,r,r+w). \] Every saturated product inequality gives a nonvertex-flat atom when \(0<b<1\). For example, \(w=0\) gives \((x,1-x,0)\); \(r=0\) gives \((b,0,1-b)\); \(p=0<q\) gives \((0,q,1-q)\); and \(p=q=0\) gives \((0,b,1-b)\). At \(y=0\), one has \(x=b\) and the first triple is \((b,0,1-b)\), up to ordering; the \(x=0\) case is identical. A segment toward a strict point consequently has positive infinite product derivative. The concave leaf terms have no negative infinite inward derivative: \(k\) has a positive infinite inward derivative at \(0\) and a finite one at \(1\); \(\overline g\) is a plateau at \(0\) and has positive infinite inward derivative at \(1/2\). Thus no boundary maximum is possible. This uses the [original tetrahedral barrier](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), not an alias lower asymptotic. At a strict point the first product tetrahedron has coordinates \((x,y,1-x-y)\). Its strict concavity controls every fixed-output input direction. The maximizing pair is therefore unique. The profiles are \(C^1\) by uniqueness and the envelope theorem; the plateau seam of \(\overline g\) at \(1/4\) is itself \(C^1\). Fixing \(b\) and a feasible interior \(x\) likewise gives a unique strictly interior maximizing core input \(y(x)\) in the \(AC\) problem, throughout the interval between the pure input and its alias maximizer used below. The same one-variable barriers exclude the gate endpoints, and the leaf barrier excludes \(y=1/2\). The stationary equations are legitimate on both sides of the plateau seam. ## 3. Exact output response, including the core plateau Let \(X_0\in[1/2,1]\) and use the pure \(A_2\) stationary state \[ \begin{aligned} a&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}X_0}{\pi},& Z_0&=X_0-\frac1{2X_0},\\ b&=\frac{\operatorname{arccot}Z_0}{\pi},& \lambda&=F_{A_2}'(b)=2\log(2X_0^2). \end{aligned} \tag{2} \] Here \(\operatorname{arccot}\) takes values in \((0,\pi)\). The complete input lies in \([1/4,\arctan(2)/\pi]\), and the output is strictly inside \((0,1)\), including both displayed endpoints. Concavity and the unchanged first derivatives at \(a\ge1/4\) show that this pure state is also the unique maximum of the all-core \(\overline g\) block at output \(b\), and of its \(\lambda\)-weighted full block. For every \(a\in[1/4,1/2)\), \[ k'(a)-g'(a)>0. \tag{3} \] At \(1/4\), \(k'=-\log\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}>0=g'\). On that interval, \[ (k'-g')' =\frac{4\pi}{\sin(2\pi a)} -\frac{\pi}{2}\cot\frac{\pi a}{2} \ge4\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}(1+\sqrt2)>0. \] For \(AC\), fix the output \(b\) from (2), optimize the core input \(y\), and view the resulting action as a concave function of \(x\). At \(x=a\), the maximizing core input is \(y=a\). The \(x\) derivative is (3), so its actual maximizing alias input satisfies \(x_{AC}>a\). Write \[ U=\cot(\pi x),\quad V=\cot(\pi y),\quad Z=\cot(\pi b),\quad D_0=(U+V)Z-UV+1>0. \] The [actual product derivative identities](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) are \[ e^{m_y}=\frac{(U+V)(V-Z)}{D_0}, \qquad e^{-m_z}=\frac{(U-Z)(V-Z)}{D_0}. \tag{4} \] On the branch \(y>1/4\), core stationarity \(g'(y)+m_y=0\) gives \(D_0=V^2\), hence \[ \begin{aligned} U&=\frac1{V-Z}-V,& \frac{dU}{dV}&=-\frac1{(V-Z)^2}-1<0,\\ m_z&=\log\frac{V^2}{1+Z^2-V^2}. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] The last expression is strictly increasing in \(V>0\) on its physical positive-denominator branch. Since \(U\) decreases as \(x\) increases, the output slope increases with \(x\) along this optimized core response. On the plateau \(0<y<1/4\), core stationarity is \(m_y=0\). It gives \(D_0=(1+V^2)/2\), and, with \(w=V-Z>0\), \[ \begin{aligned} U&=Z+\frac{1+Z^2-w^2}{2w},& \frac{dU}{dV}&=-\frac{1+Z^2}{2w^2}-\frac12<0,\\ m_z&=\log\frac{1+V^2}{1+2Z^2-V^2}. \end{aligned} \tag{6} \] Again the output slope increases strictly with \(V\), hence with \(x\). At \(y=1/4\), \(V=1\), both expressions for \(U\) and both output slopes agree. The unique response cannot jump at this seam. Starting at \(x=y=a\) and ending at \(x_{AC}>a\) therefore proves \[ H_{AC}'(b)>\lambda. \tag{7} \] For \(AA\), exchange symmetry and uniqueness force the fixed-output maximizing inputs to satisfy \(x=y\). At \(x=y=a\), the derivative along that diagonal is twice (3), so the maximizing input \(x_{AA}=y_{AA}\) is greater than \(a\). Along a symmetric input, put \(U=\cot(\pi x)\) and \(D_0=2UZ-U^2+1\). Then \[ m_z=\log D_0-2\log(U-Z),\qquad \frac{d m_z}{dU} =-\frac{2(1+Z^2)}{D_0(U-Z)}<0. \tag{8} \] The output slope again increases with \(x\), proving \[ H_{AA}'(b)>\lambda. \tag{9} \] This proof keeps the plateau branch and does not select an alias solution by a squared stationarity equation. For reference, the generic alias-port equations are also algebraic after setting \(t=\sin(\pi x/2)\). Its \(\kappa=e^{-k'(x)}=2t\), so \[ U=\frac{1-2t^2}{2t\sqrt{1-t^2}},\qquad X=\frac1{2t\sqrt{(1-t^2)(1+2t)}},\qquad Y=X\sqrt{2t}. \] With an interior core partner on the \(g\) branch, that partner's cotangent is \(X\). At output tangent \(\lambda\), write \(r=e^{\lambda/2}\). The product equations become \[ r=\frac{U+X}{\sqrt{2t}},\qquad B_{\mathrm{out}}=X-\frac1{r\sqrt{2t}}. \tag{10} \] The plateau has the different core relation (6). Formula (10) does not license discarding that branch or a finite-support boundary. ## 4. The conjugate gap increases on the entire proper-port range For \(\lambda\in[-\log4,\log4]\), use \(a,b=b(\lambda)\) from (2) and define \[ \begin{aligned} P(\lambda)&=2g(a)+m(a,a,b)-\lambda b,\\ A_J(\lambda)&=\max_{0\le z\le1} \{H_J(z)-\lambda z\},\\ \Delta_J(\lambda)&=P(\lambda)-A_J(\lambda), \qquad J\in\{AC,AA\}. \end{aligned} \tag{11} \] By (7), (9) and concavity, every maximizing output of \(A_J(\lambda)\) is strictly greater than \(b(\lambda)\). This permits boundary maximizers; it does not assume a strictly interior conjugate maximizer. The convex conjugates \(A_J\) are Lipschitz. The pure function \(P\) is smooth, with derivative \(-b(\lambda)\). At almost every \(\lambda\), \[ \Delta_J'(\lambda)=z_J(\lambda)-b(\lambda)>0. \tag{12} \] The argmax graph over the closed \(\lambda\) interval is compact and contains no point with \(z\le b(\lambda)\). Its separation from \(z=b(\lambda)\) therefore has a positive minimum. Both gaps are strictly increasing, with a uniform positive lower derivative bound on this fixed interval. In particular, \[ \Delta_J(\lambda)\ge\Delta_J(-\log4). \tag{13} \] This is an exact all-proper-port reduction. The independent uniform block certificate proves \(\Delta_{AC}(-\log4),\Delta_{AA}(-\log4)>1/100\); in fact its rational supporting planes prove the entire interval directly. Hence (13) supplies an additional structural explanation, without being needed to validate those finite inequalities. The [exact finite block transport](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md) then retains every original input-sum cutoff, target, turn and closed-source normalization when summing the block gaps. The local envelopes remain upper bounds rather than asserted signed coefficient limits. The full quantum and filled-volume conclusion still uses the separately proved packet and primitive geometric interfaces.

title: Two-leaf seeds in the actual complete Conway geometry
text: # Two-leaf seeds in the actual complete Conway geometry 31 October 2026. geometric extension and dependency audit. Keep the original retained crossing-circle leaf \(h\), its literal turns and identity stacks. Allow seeds \(A_s=h^s\) for every fixed \(s\ge2\) and the grammar \[ E::=A_s\mid T(E)\mid EE. \] Consider the actual cylindrical closure \(C(FG)\), where both \(F\) and \(G\) are expressions in this grammar. Isolated \(C(A_2)\) is excluded. The strict complete source optimizer builds the actual complete finite-volume right-angled two-ball link metric. Every fixed retained half-twist partner has the same complete volume. The marked deformed representation and its actual filled-volume action also extend. The old restriction \(s\ge3\) is unnecessary for these geometric statements. This note does not assert a universal mixed-color or alias gap. The [two-leaf source theorem](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_source.md) treats the finite source, rounding and packet separately; the [algebraic leaf certificate](actual_conway_algebraic_leaf_alias_certificate.md) supplies an additional sufficient alias condition. A full quantum limit requires those analytic hypotheses. ## 1. The exact new strict base For every prescribed seed output \(b\in(0,1)\), choose \[ \frac b2<a<\min\left(b,\frac12\right). \] Take both leaves of \(A_2=hh\) equal to \(a\). The single retained product \((a,a)\mapsto b\) has \[ p=q=b-a>0,\qquad r=2a-b>0,\qquad w=1-2a>0. \tag{1} \] Both leaf atoms and all three product atoms are strict. This is an existence state of the original wire polytope; it imposes no equal-label restriction on the finite source sum. The [old seed extension](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md), from \(A_{s-1}\) to \(A_s\), now starts at \(s=2\). Choose a last leaf \(0<c<\min(b/2,1-b,1/4)\), set \(t=b-c/2\), use a strict \(A_{s-1}\) state at \(t\), and attach \((t,c)\mapsto b\). At a macro product choose both child outputs in \((b/2,\min(b,1/2))\); at a turn use the child output \(1-b\). Every proper expression therefore has a strict state at every \(b\in(0,1)\). For \(C(FG)\), delete only the forced final gate, whose two input loads sum to \(1\), and choose both child outputs to be \(1/2\). This gives a strict reduced state. The [complete boundary barrier](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), §2, now applies without change. Every proper endpoint wire propagates to a leaf endpoint or a product with a nonvertex-flat atom \((0,a,1-a)\). Any saturated retained product inequality similarly exposes such an atom. Its positive infinite directional derivative toward the strict state cannot be canceled by any other atom, whose derivative is finite or positive infinite. Every maximizing leaf and retained prism is consequently strict. The retained tetrahedron angle maps recover all leaf and product wires; turns recover their wires, and the deleted final gate adds no free direction. Strict concavity gives a unique maximizer and a negative definite reduced Hessian. Fixed proper-output profiles are real analytic on \((0,1)\). None of this argument uses a third leaf once (1) is supplied. ## 2. Exact \(A_2\) ports and the unchanged macro inequalities Use the original port variables \(B=\cot(\pi b)\), \(X,Y>0\), with \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). A leaf of complete label \(a\) has \(B=X=\cot(\pi a)>0\) and \(Y=1\). The actual stationary product laws are \[ B_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{B_1+B_2}, \qquad Y_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{B_1+B_2}, \qquad B_1+B_2>0. \tag{2} \] At the unique optimized \(A_2\) state, the two leaves have the same \(X\), directly by the stationary input equations. Therefore \[ B=X-\frac1{2X},\qquad Y=\frac1{2X},\qquad X>0, \qquad B+Y=X>0,\qquad X-B=\frac1{2X}>0. \tag{3} \] In particular \(-Y<B<X\). Moreover \(B(X)\) is strictly increasing from \(-\infty\) to \(+\infty\), so for every \(b\in(0,1)\) its selected solution is the unique positive \[ X=\frac{B+\sqrt{B^2+2}}2. \tag{4} \] This agrees with strictness; no branch is inferred from a squared equation alone. For all \(s\ge2\), the original Chebyshev recurrence gives \(B_s=T_s(X)/U_{s-1}(X)\), \(Y_s=1/U_{s-1}(X)\), and the same strict inequality \(-Y_s<B_s<X\). Its proof can start at (3). Equivalently, when \(X=\cos\alpha<1\), put \(h_0=\sin\alpha\) and use \(B_s=h_0\cot(s\alpha)\), \(Y_s=h_0\csc(s\alpha)\), with the positive denominators selecting \(0<s\alpha<\pi\). The hyperbolic \(X>1\) branch and the \(X=1\) limit have the same inequalities. The [macro preservation proof](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) uses only this inequality. The literal turn \((B,X,Y)\mapsto(-B,Y,X)\) preserves it. At a product with \(X<1\), put \(h_0=\sqrt{1-X^2}\), \(\alpha=\arccos X\), and write the child ports as \((B_i,Y_i)=(h_0\cot u_i,h_0\csc u_i)\). Their inequalities give \(u_i>\alpha\); the positive denominator in (2) gives \(u_1+u_2<\pi\). The output has angle \(u_1+u_2\), hence again \(-Y_{\mathrm{out}}<B_{\mathrm{out}}<X\). For \(X\ge1\), the same inequality places each child \(B_i\) between \(\sqrt{X^2-1}\) and \(X\). Thus \(0<X-B_i<1\), and \[ B_{\mathrm{out}}-X =\frac{(X-B_1)(X-B_2)-1}{B_1+B_2}<0. \] The output \(B\) is positive, supplying its lower inequality. All steps include the \(A_2\) base without a new hypothesis. At the closed root, the actual ordered port matching gives \((B,X,Y)\) and \((-B,X,Y)\). Applying \(-Y<B<X\) to both yields \(|B|<\min(X,Y)\). The hyperboloid identity implies \(X<1\), \(Y<1\). These bounds propagate down each macro product: its common \(X<1\) stays fixed; writing its child angles \(u,v\) as above, \(Y_{\mathrm{out}}<1\) gives \(u+v<\pi-\alpha\). Since \(u,v>\alpha\), each child has \(\alpha<u,v<\pi-\alpha\), hence \(Y_{\mathrm{child}}<1\). Turns exchange \(X,Y\). Stop at a seed, not at its individual leaves, whose \(Y\) is \(1\). For a proper seed \(A_s\), \(Y_s<1\) implies \(\sin(s\alpha)>\sin\alpha\), consequently \((s+1)\alpha<\pi\). Thus \[ \cos\frac{\pi}{s+1}<X<1,\qquad \frac14<a< \frac1\pi\arctan\!\left(\sec\frac{\pi}{s+1}\right) \le\frac{\arctan2}{\pi}. \tag{5} \] For \(A_2\), this is precisely \(1/2<X<1\) and \(1/4<a<\arctan(2)/\pi\). The upper endpoint differs materially from the old \(\arctan(\sqrt2)/\pi\) mixed-source bound. ## 3. The complete geometric inputs The existing geometric proof can now be read with \(A_2\) as its base, without changing a local cell, ordered face map or cut. - The leaf pyramid requires only \(0<a<1/2\). Its two shaded triangles, right apex edges and ordered base quadrilateral are unchanged. - The [ideal multiplication prism](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md) requires exactly \(p,q,r,w>0\). Its three ideal tetrahedra, face metrics and dihedral-angle formulas use only these strict variables. There is no seed-width parameter in the local theorem. - The ordered stack maps remain \(F:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)\mapsto(v_0,v_1,P,\infty)\) and \(G:(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)\mapsto(\infty,P,v_2,v_3)\). Stationarity matches the full ordered quadrilateral metrics. A turn rotates this actual frame. - Convex attachment uses the same angle sums \(\pi/2\) or \(\pi\) on input CAP edges and strict output angles \(\pi b,\pi(1-b)\). The first \(A_2\) product already has the completed port pattern PORT, WHITE, SHADED, WHITE. Products and turns preserve it. Supported-face gluing prevents accidental vertex identifications outside the common face; the cell adjacency is a tree. - Both root children in \(C(FG)\) are completed cells, including \(A_2\) and turned \(A_2\). The actual closed map \(C_j\mapsto C_{3-j}\) preserves the ordered metric and FREE/CAP pairs. Both opposite angle pairs sum to \(\pi\), so the common face disappears as a flat white seam. The result is the same convex ideal right-angled polyhedron, with every nonflat edge in an original leaf bowtie. - The [literal projection-ball cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) uses only the original leaf boxes, segment pairings, turns and stacks. Its ribbon induction gives exactly the shaded triangles, white facial walks and cyclic orders of the metric construction. It does not count at least three leaves in an open seed. The existing caveat remains: an auxiliary open quadrilateral port is not itself half of a physical four-punctured tangle boundary. - Every finite edge has the same pointwise four-step return and four right angles. Canonical rectangular cusp links give equal opposite shaded sides. Scaling them to length \(1\) makes every shaded-triangle and copied-white gluing preserve horospheres. The reversible cut identifies their compact links with cusp tori. Completeness and finite volume follow. If \(V_E\) is the original source-selected sum of leaf and prism volumes, the actual pure augmented exterior \(Y_E\) therefore satisfies \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E)=2\max V_E. \tag{6} \] This identifies the geometric variational value. The finite quantum source requires its separate positivity and rounding argument. The algebraic shape and rational Bloch-chain comparison also uses only these local pyramids and prisms, their five-term relations, the common algebraic coordinate field, and this degree-one closed fundamental chain. It introduces no further \(s\ge3\) hypothesis. ## 4. Complete retained half-twist partners The [complete half-twist partner](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md) changes the original shaded-disk pairings across the two projection copies. Its three exact edge words are identities for \(E=e^{2\pi i a}\) throughout \(0<a<1/2\). They do not require \(a\le\arctan(\sqrt2)/\pi\) or a seed of length \(3\). Every edge belongs to one original leaf bowtie, so arbitrary fixed signs select one of the already checked pure or odd edge words. The canonical triangle decorations are preserved by the changed vertex bijections. Hence every fixed sign pattern \(\epsilon\) has an actual complete finite-volume metric with \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon) =\operatorname{Vol}(Y_E)=2\max V_E. \tag{7} \] The primitive meridian and longitude paths and their rectangle-area checks are local and remain nonsingular for \(0<a<1/2\). This is a complete geometric statement. The old whole mixed-color supporting-plane estimate need not hold throughout (5); a complete metric alone does not identify the independently long filled quantum asymptotic. ## 5. The two exclusions and the source interface Isolated \(C(A_2)=C(hh)\) has forced last inputs \(x+y=1\), with both leaves at most \(1/2\). Thus \(x=y=1/2\). Both leaf cells and the last gate are flat, so there is no strict reduced assignment. It is excluded here. Its flat source alone does not establish a topological nonhyperbolicity statement. There is also a genuine finite-level change. For even \(N=2m\), the leaf Newton support ends at \(M=m-1\). The \(A_2\) coefficient at the top degree \(d=2m-1\) is absent, because a product has output at most \(2M=d-1\). The old assertion that every robust seed has every coefficient positive for every \(N\ge3\) cannot be quoted with \(A_2\) substituted. For odd \(N\), \(2M=d\). These endpoint facts do not obstruct a fixed strict interior optimizer, but the source theorem must round on the actual support. That audit is separate from (6)–(7). The complete geometric argument has no remaining use of \(s\ge3\). That restriction did supply the old mixed alias interval. Every expression, turn, sign pattern and diagram is fixed; this note claims no uniform estimate over unbounded trees. ## 6. The deformed representation and primitive filling action The marked geometric interfaces also extend. Retain all original free wires \(y\), delete only the forced-flat final gate, and use the original pure mixed-core action \[ \begin{aligned} f_0(y,t)&=\sum_i g(x_i(y),t_i)+\sum_{\mathrm{products}}m,\\ g(x,t)&=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t),\\ J(a)&=\int_0^a\operatorname{Log}(2\sin(\pi u))\,du. \end{aligned} \tag{8} \] The logarithmic sheets continue from the strict complete chamber. Section 1 supplies the same invertible complete wire Hessian. Thus the free-wire equations have one holomorphic critical branch near independent \(t=0\), with separately even critical action \(\phi_0(t)\). Every complete leaf in (5) lies in the original strict high branch \(1/4<x<1/2\). For a retained half-twist \(\epsilon\in\{0,+1,-1\}\), the original [selected-source shear](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md) is \[ \begin{aligned} v&=g_t(x,t),& \chi&=t-\frac{\epsilon v}{2\pi i},\\ f_\epsilon(x,\chi)&=g(x,t)-\frac{\epsilon v^2}{4\pi i},& df_\epsilon&=g_x\,dx+v\,d\chi. \end{aligned} \tag{9} \] At \(t=0\), the change of variables has derivative \(1-\epsilon i\cot(\pi x)\), nonzero for every \(0<x<1/2\). The source-branch verification uses \(x>1/4\) to select its simple root and fixes the additive constant by continuation to \(x=1/2\). It has no upper cutoff \(\arctan(\sqrt2)/\pi\). Consequently (5) supplies every local branch assumption, including for \(A_2\). This does not establish a global alias bound. For explicit geometric data, set \(E=e^{2\pi i x}\), \(T=e^{2\pi i t}\), and \[ Z=\frac{1+E}{1+T},\qquad R=\frac{T(1+E)^2}{E(1+T)^2},\qquad Z^2-(1+E)Z+ER=0. \tag{10} \] Use the original ordered port \((0,\infty,1,R)\), first-ball flag \(Z\), and second-ball flag \(Z/E\). The same four white/completion matrices \(W_0,\ldots,W_3\) from the [pure marked theorem](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) apply. Its nine prism identities and turn/closure identities are rational identities in independent local angle phases; they contain no seed width. They propagate one Möbius map on each original white face through every \(A_2\) product. Nonplanar deformed white pieces are not assumed to be reflection planes. At pure leaves keep the original within-copy shaded map \(S\). At odd leaves retain the original cross-copy maps \(A,B\). Their three pointwise edge words \[ W_0^{-1}BW_2^{-1}A,\qquad W_2^{-1}BW_0^{-1}A,\qquad W_1^{-1}BW_3^{-1}A \] are identities for independent \(E,R\), not only at completeness. The same closed bowtie quotient gives the actual group presentation. These matrices therefore define a representation of the actual signed augmented-link exterior in a bounded framed neighborhood of its complete holonomy. Matching a port cross ratio alone is not being used to infer a group or physical tangle boundary. The main meridian still crosses its two original white sectors, whose \(W\) maps have the same derivative at the corner. It is parabolic and remains nonidentity near the complete anchor; its whole peripheral commutant remains parabolic. At an auxiliary flag, the original disk longitude has multiplier \(Q^2\), where \[ \rho=\frac{Z}{1+E-Z},\qquad Q=\frac{E-Z}{Z-1}. \] The pure meridian multiplier is \(\rho\); the two primitive signed collar paths have multipliers \(\rho Q\) and \(\rho/Q\). Their complete translations and two-rectangle area give the same original primitive marking. The physical \(R^\epsilon\) sign is fixed by the original local threading calibration. The [signed marked theorem](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) therefore gives, with the same small logarithms, \[ U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i,\qquad V_i=-2\partial_i\phi_\epsilon(\chi),\qquad U_i=U_i^{\mathrm{pure}}-\frac{\epsilon_i V_i}{2}. \tag{11} \] This half-longitude shear compares the actual signed cusp lattices; it does not assert that half a longitude is primitive in either one. The physical filled crossing power is exactly \(\epsilon_i-2p_i\). The selected primitive \(G_\epsilon=2\pi i\phi_\epsilon\) retains its local quadratic correction \(-\epsilon_iV_i^2/8\), with \(dG=\tfrac12\sum_i V_i\,dU_i\). Its complete value is the actual signed volume (7), on the same oriented family. The original fundamental-chain differential gives the absolute identity \[ \operatorname{Vol}(\rho_\chi) =\operatorname{Im}G_\epsilon -\frac12\sum_i\operatorname{Re}U_i\,\operatorname{Im}V_i. \tag{12} \] There is no added integration constant, framing character or unrelated representation component. For any fixed filled auxiliary subset and independently sufficiently long fixed signed integers \(p_i\), the selected-action saddle \[ \partial_i\phi_\epsilon+ \frac{\pi i}{p_i}(\chi_i-1)=0 \] is exactly \(U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\). The complete auxiliary Hessian is nonsingular: \(\cot(\pi x_i)>0\) and \(1-\epsilon_i i\cot(\pi x_i)\ne0\). Thus the small saddle exists for all sufficiently small independent \(1/p_i\). Unfilled cusps remain parabolic by separate evenness. The [marked geometric completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) identifies this bounded framed branch with the smooth complete holonomy of the actual signed filled topology. At that saddle, (12) becomes \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_E^\epsilon(p)) =2\pi\operatorname{Re}\!\left[ \phi_\epsilon(\chi_*)+ \frac{\pi i}{2}\sum_{i\ \mathrm{filled}} \frac{(\chi_i-1)^2}{p_i} \right]. \tag{13} \] When every auxiliary circle is filled and the fixed parity pattern has one main component, this is the actual knot complement volume. Partial fillings retain the corresponding augmented-link cusps. In hidden pure variables the equation has \(p_i-\epsilon_i/2\); replacing it by ordinary rational filling of the pure partner would change the primitive angle and marking. No such replacement is made here. The geometric input to the [original whole-period theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) therefore extends throughout the stated \(s\ge2\), \(C(FG)\) grammar. A full invariant equality follows only when its actual finite packet, rounding and whole-source complement estimates are also supplied. A separately proved condition such as \(\cot(\pi x_i)\ge2/3\) at every complete leaf can supply the new alias estimate; it is not automatic from (5). ## Dependencies The proof extends the local cells, ordered maps and primitive markings of the linked original notes. In particular, the [signed long-filling theorem](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) keeps geometry, the finite complex packet, and the whole-source gap as distinct inputs. No previous theorem file is changed. The geometric extension is uniform on its stated domain. The invariant limit additionally requires the separate source estimates; it does not follow from geometry alone.

title: Two-leaf Conway seeds: complete source, geometry, and the mixed-source hypothesis
text: # Two-leaf Conway seeds: complete source, geometry, and the mixed-source hypothesis 31 October 2026. Complete-source extension and conditional mixed-source interface. The seed restriction can be reduced to two leaves for the COMPLETE source and its literal geometry on C(FG), with both children built from such seeds. The previous all-level, all-output strict-support assertion cannot be retained. A geometry-certified mixed-source statement follows under the explicit tangent condition below; that condition is not automatic in the enlarged grammar. This note verifies the exact source and packet inputs for the existing long-filling transfer under that certificate; it does not claim that every two-leaf diagram passes it. ## 1. Exact grammar and the finite support issue Use the unchanged physical leaf h=T(L_N), actual quarter-turn T, original identity-wire stack, and marked cylindrical closure C. Allow finite expressions E ::= A_s | T(E) | EE with s>=2, where A_s contains s distinct h coupons. Fix a closed C(FG) with F,G from this grammar. All trees are fixed before N. Put d=N-1 and M=floor(d/2). The original complete leaf has strictly positive Newton coefficients at every 0<=r<=M. Exact positive multiplication shows $$ \operatorname{supp}(A_2)=\{0,\ldots,2M\}. $$ For a chosen k<=2M distribute k=i+j with i,j<=M and choose the upper product output k; its coefficient is positive. No product output exceeds i+j. At odd N, 2M=d. At even N, 2M=d-1, so the top coordinate is genuinely missing. Actual turns may move this missing coordinate to the bottom. In particular, the old proof by all-output support induction is unavailable. The original complete-source identities, scalar normalization and nonnegative Newton coefficients themselves remain exact. They do not require a robust seed: see [original physical Conway source](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md) §§1,3–4. ## 2. Strict classical states replace full finite support At prescribed seed output b in (0,1), choose equal leaves $$ \frac b2<a<\min\!\left(b,\frac12\right). $$ Then the only gate of A_2 satisfies max(a,a)<b<2a<1 and each leaf is strictly between 0 and 1/2. For A_s with s>2, the induction already given in [arbitrary-width seed proof](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md) §1 applies. At a macro-product choose both child outputs in (b/2,min(b,1/2)); at a turn use 1-b. This constructs a strict state for every open expression at every interior output. For C(FG), delete ONLY its forced last gate, whose exact finite coefficient is one and whose inputs obey i+j=d. Choose continuous child outputs 1/2,1/2. Every remaining leaf and product inequality is strict. The boundary-barrier argument of [original complete geometry](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) §2 now applies without change: a proper endpoint wire descends to a nonvertex-flat atom, and every other gate equality exhibits one directly. A segment to this strict state gives +infinity directional derivative at that atom, never a negative infinite contribution elsewhere. The reduced maximum is interior and unique. The retained tetrahedral angle maps recover all free wires, so its Hessian is negative definite. Fixed interior-output profiles are real analytic. Here is an every-level lattice proof that does NOT use full seed support. Contract every chain of turns: a wire then equals a chosen unturned integer coordinate or d minus it. Delete the forced final gate and express one root child coordinate as d minus the other. The two children have disjoint trees; these operations introduce no equation such as 2r=d. All remaining unturned outputs are free integer coordinates. Round d times each coordinate of any strict reduced real state to a nearest integer, then restore all eliminated coordinates by those exact affine formulas. Each coordinate error is bounded independently of d. Every nonforced inequality has fixed positive slack; therefore every rounded state is valid for all sufficiently large d, at both parities. In particular each leaf lies below M, even when 2M=d-1. The finite state count is polynomial in N. The original uniform leaf/gate factorial estimate is N times the same continuous action plus O(log N), including d versus N offsets. Applying it to the rounded unique maximum gives the lower limit; summing the uniform upper bound gives the upper limit. Thus $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_{E,N}^{0}=\max_{P_E}A_E. $$ for the whole original pure complete scalar, along all sufficiently large levels. It is strictly positive at those levels. For an open output sequence r_N/d->b in (0,1), use the analytic strict profile at b_N=r_N/d and round only its other coordinates. The same argument proves its coefficient limit. No finite-N full-support claim, or N=2 claim, is needed. The isolated C(A_2) really lies outside this theorem. Its two leaves must sum to d. At even N that is impossible because 2M=d-1, so the actual scalar is zero. At odd N only both leaf labels M occur; the continuum state is (1/2,1/2), all retained leaf volumes are zero. It has no strict complete metric of the type used here. Isolated C(A_s),s>=3, has the existing separate strict complete argument; this does not extend the mixed-color theorem for C(A_3). ## 3. Literal complete geometry and complete signed coupons The companion [two-leaf seed geometry proof](actual_conway_two_leaf_seed_geometry.md) checks the complete and deformed geometric interfaces in detail. For an optimized A_2 let X=cot(pi a)>0. Its port is exactly $$ \begin{aligned} B_2&=X-\frac1{2X},\qquad Y_2=\frac1{2X},\\ B_2+Y_2&=X>0,\qquad X-B_2=\frac1{2X}>0. \end{aligned} $$ Hence -Y<B<X holds for this seed at every interior output. The macro-product and turn preservation proof in [strict-quarter port theorem](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) §§2–3 uses precisely this inequality. At a closed C(FG), the reflected root ports give X,Y<1; those two inequalities propagate to every macro-seed port. At an A_2 seed, Y=1/(2X)<1 therefore yields $$ \frac12<X<1,\qquad \frac14<a<\frac{\arctan2}{\pi}. $$ For s>=3 the old sharper width-dependent bound remains valid. The geometric proof in [original complete geometry](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) §§3–7 uses strict leaf/prism angles, exact ordered input maps, and the completed child FREE/CAP pattern. A_2 already is a completed product; both closed root children are completed. Thus its original convex gluing, right-angled closed polyhedron, reversible bowtie cut and canonical cusp decoration apply. The assembled complete hyperbolic metric is on the actual augmented complement, with volume 2pi max A_E. This is not an identification from a formal tangle fraction or from matching just a port modulus. All leaf coordinates remain in a compact subinterval of (1/4,1/2) for each fixed expression. Consequently the actual high-index complete odd-coupon asymptotic and its concave plateau bound apply. Replacing g by g_tilde only at the chosen odd leaves gives a concave majorant agreeing with the pure action near its strict maximum; this maximum is still the unique global one. The original primitive central lattice has 2H-3 free wires: H leaf outputs, H-2 retained product outputs, and one root input relation. The strict lattice construction above preserves that primitive lattice and every d=N-1 shift. Thus the complete signed amplitude argument of [original half-twist Newton transport](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md) §4 is inherited, including its nonzero local amplitudes and original phase. The changed shaded gluings and complete cusp/edge checks of [literal half-twist partner geometry](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md) §§1–3 are local to these same literal leaf disks. This establishes the COMPLETE signed source/volume interface; it does not by itself supply a mixed-color gap. The connectivity induction also survives: A_2 realizes {I,U} without internal loops (both odd, or one pure and one odd). The existing turn/set-product table therefore gives the same constructive one-main-component parity choice. ## 4. Exact additional hypothesis for the whole mixed-color estimate Retain the original functions $$ \begin{aligned} J(t)&=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du,\\ g(a)&=J(2a)-4J(a),\qquad k(u)=-2J(u/2),\\ I(a)&=\min_{0\le u\le1}\bigl[g(a)+g'(a)(u-a)-k(u)\bigr]. \end{aligned} $$ A sufficient condition on the ACTUAL complete optimizer is $$ I(a_l)>0\qquad\text{for every leaf }l.\tag{H} $$ This condition is finite, geometric and uses the original optimized leaf labels. Since the expression is fixed, its minimum is a positive constant. Under (H), every step of [whole mixed-source gap](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) §§4–5 applies on the unchanged expanded alias support: core tangents, gate tangents and affine-wire cancellation give a loss for every nonempty alias subset; the all-core concave majorant and local physical-color loss give the entire complement gap. Both parity offsets and the polynomial state count are unchanged. This proves the same two WHOLE mixed-source inequalities there, conditional on (H), without requiring all finite Newton outputs to occur. It is not yet a new assertion of the final filling theorem. For a0=atan(sqrt2)/pi, the earlier theorem proves I>0 on [1/4,a0]. For a>=a0, g'(a)<=-log2 and k'(u)>=-log2, so k(u)-g'(a)u is maximized at u=1. Hence $$ I(a)=g(a)+(1-a)g'(a),\qquad I'(a)=(1-a)g''(a)<0.\tag{A} $$ In particular the universal A_2 upper bound atan2/pi is insufficient. The separately proved algebraic sufficient cutoff is X=cot(pi a)>=2/3: its tangent margin is greater than 1/2500. Its exact proof and conditional source transfer are in [algebraic leaf alias certificate](actual_conway_algebraic_leaf_alias_certificate.md). Thus this condition on every actual A_2 seed, with the old automatic condition at all larger proper seeds, suffices for (H). ## 5. A strict A_2 tree where the inherited tangent fails Consider the literal permitted tree $$ E=C\bigl(A_2T(A_4)\bigr). $$ where A_4 may itself be the product of two A_2 seeds. The following strict stationary data are exact, not a numerical scan. At the first A_2 take leaf cotangent X=1/sqrt3, so its common leaf label is a=1/3. Its port is $$ (B,X,Y)=\left(-\frac1{2\sqrt3},\frac1{\sqrt3},\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right). $$ At A_4 take leaf cotangent X=sqrt3/2=cos(pi/6). Formula B_j=T_j(X)/U_(j-1)(X) gives B_2=1/(2sqrt3), B_3=0, B_4=-1/(2sqrt3), and Y_4=1/sqrt3. Its turn therefore has the port $$ \left(\frac1{2\sqrt3},\frac1{\sqrt3},\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right). $$ These are exactly the reflected matching root ports. Every seed gate is strict: its common-X product rule has positive denominators, the A_4 outputs have the listed cotangents, and the leaf-to-output inequalities are strict. For an elementary check, its common leaf a satisfies 1/4<a<1/3; the first output b_2 lies between a and 2a, the second equals1/2 and lies between b_2 and b_2+a, and the third b_4=1-b_2 lies between1/2 and1/2+a. The A_2 gate also has a<b_4<2a. Thus this is a strict stationary state and, by the uniqueness proved above, the actual complete optimizer. At the first seed leaf a=1/3, g'(a)=-log3 and the alias endpoint u=1 gives $$ g(1/3)+g'(1/3)(1-1/3)-k(1) =g(1/3)-\frac23\log3<0. $$ Indeed g(1/3)<=g(1/4)=2Catalan/pi<2/3 and log3>1. Therefore (H) fails for this actual enlarged-grammar optimizer. This is only a failure of the leafwise supporting-plane proof: it does NOT exhibit a whole-source alias maximum, realize the local envelope sharply, or disprove a mixed-source/filling gap. Other ports and shared constraints may compensate the local deficit. ## 6. Exact changed-source packet and marked-geometry interfaces The following verifies the inherited hypotheses rather than using the name of the grammar. Write H for the number of actual leaves and K=2H-3 for the primitive wire dimension. Before closure there are H leaf outputs and H-1 product outputs; eliminate each turn by r_out=d-r_in, fix the root output, and solve its input-sum equation integrally for a variable from one of its disjoint child trees. This removes two variables, with coefficient +1 or -1. There is no even-level index-two lattice. The remaining coordinates k lie in Z^K and every physical wire is r_w=N ell_w(k/N)+delta_w, with ell_w integral affine and the original fixed integer shifts delta_w. Equal optimized seed labels impose no equation on this lattice. Choose a small fixed rectangular wire box around the strict optimizer. All leaves lie in one compact subinterval of (1/4,1/2), all retained gate factorial arguments lie in (0,1), and these properties persist on a fixed complex tube. For sufficiently small physical color deficits h_l<=delta N, EVERY integer state in that box is admissible for every sufficiently large N of either parity. In particular r_l+h_l<=M and r_l-h_l>=0. No seed boundary output is used to define or complete this window. The EXACT local coefficients remain those of [exact changed-source complex packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md) (1)–(3): $$ \begin{aligned} A_N(v,t)&=\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^2G_N(v-Nt)G_N(v+Nt)},\\ d_N^0(r,t)&=A_N(r,t),\\ d_N^\epsilon(r,t)&=\kappa^\epsilon\sum_{v=r}^{M} (-1)^v q^{\epsilon v(r+1)}\binom vr_q A_N(v,t),\qquad\epsilon=\pm1,\\ \ell_N^\epsilon(r,t)&=e^{-i\epsilon\pi d/4}d_N^\epsilon(r,t). \end{aligned} $$ Here $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, $\kappa=q^{d^2/2}$, and $s_j$ is the original sine factorial. The Gaussian coefficient is $\binom vr_q=s_v/(s_rs_{v-r})$. Thus each circle still contributes its original N^2 coefficient factor, not an extra normalized loop. All Hermite/normal directions, Cartan phases, physical signs and the unit eta_N=exp[(i pi d/4)sum epsilon_l] are unchanged. The packet is the finite sum of products of these H coefficients and the H-2 original retained Newton gate coefficients on that rectangle. The exponentially accurate high-index interpolation in that note §3 is a LOCAL coefficient theorem on any such compact high-index interval. Its exact chirp, selected recurrence solution and relative exp(-sigma N) grid error do not involve the seed width or require other output coefficients to be nonzero. The canonical factorial marks likewise depend only on the actual strict factorial arguments. Each leaf contributes N^(1/2); each retained gate contributes N^(-3/2). Hence the interpolated summand has power N^(H/2-3(H-2)/2)=N^(3-H). Its original offset amplitude is $$ b_E=\left(\prod_l b_{\epsilon_l}\right)\left(\prod_g b_{\mu,g}\right) \exp\!\left[\sum_l\delta_l\partial_x f_{\epsilon_l} +\sum_g\nabla m(w_g)\mathbin{\cdot}\delta_{w_g}\right]. $$ Here $b_{\epsilon_l}$ and $b_{\mu,g}$ are the original local leaf and gate amplitudes from the exact changed-source packet. The CHANGED local actions $f_\epsilon$, not the pure colored ones, occur in the offset factor. The full wire Hessian is negative definite at completeness. Analytic implicit function theory therefore gives one nearby holomorphic critical point. The finite tensor-cotangent proof retains all rectangle boundary currents and all nonzero modes; its assumptions are this strict window, the local joint interpolant, and its fixed exponential grid error. They have just been verified. The same argument yields $$ \begin{aligned} C_N^\epsilon(t)&=N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(t)e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(t)} \bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr),\\ a_\epsilon(t)&=\frac{(2\pi)^{K/2}b_E(y_*(t),t)} {\sqrt{\det[-F_{\epsilon,yy}(y_*(t),t)]}}. \end{aligned} $$ Indeed 3-H+K/2=3/2. At zero the amplitude is the positive pure one times product_(epsilon_l!=0) sqrt(sin(pi a_l))exp(-i epsilon_l pi a_l/2), so it is nonzero. The local action shear and separate evenness are unchanged; writing c_l=cot(pi a_l)>0, the color Hessian is exactly $$ \partial_{t_l}\partial_{t_m}\Phi_\epsilon(0) =-\frac{2\pi c_l}{1-\epsilon_l i c_l}\,\delta_{lm}. $$ Its real part is strictly negative. This establishes the exact finite complex corridor packet at both parities, including its normalization, nonzero amplitude and original shifts. No all-boundary finite support was used in any step. Under (H), section4 supplies the entire physical-color gap and all-alias gap. The concave core majorant gives the outside-wire-window gap. Combining these with the exact packet gives the original mixed source versus packet error exp[N(F0-gamma)] on a fixed small physical corridor, uniformly at both parities. Thus the two quantum hypotheses of [original-source long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) §1 are satisfied, including mu=3/2 and the displayed eta_N, for every fixed passing A_2-based expression. Finally, the marked geometry uses no missing finite-support assertion: [marked odd peripheral deformation](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) §§3–6 uses the strict complete geometric anchor, the same local selected action, rational ordered white/prism/turn maps, and exact local shaded/peripheral words. These inputs are identical at every cell of the enlarged tree. Its complete polygons are nondegenerate by §3 here, and the same wire Hessian supplies the nearby branch. The primitive paths therefore remain U_l=-2pi i t_l, V_l=-2 partial_l Phi, and the same actual odd-link full-twist equation U_l+p_l V_l=-2pi i applies. The absolute regulator is anchored at the actual complete volume proved above. No rational filling of a different pure partner is substituted. Accordingly this interface audit supplies all inputs for the existing long-filling transfer on the subclass satisfying (H), in particular the finite algebraic condition $X\ge2/3$ at each $A_2$ seed. Any resulting enlarged filling statement must retain the original quantifiers: one fixed literal diagram and sign pattern, any chosen auxiliary subset, independent integral slopes sufficiently long for that fixed datum, then all N tending to infinity. It must not assert that every A_2 diagram passes the extra condition. The explicit example in §5 shows why such an assertion would be unsupported. ## Inputs Existing workspace inputs are [original physical Conway source](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md), [whole-source variational limit](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md), [original complete geometry](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), [arbitrary-width seed proof](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md), [strict-quarter port theorem](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md), [original half-twist Newton transport](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md), [whole mixed-source gap](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md), and [literal half-twist partner geometry](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md). The new steps are the A_2 strict seed, explicit every-level interior rounding, source-interface audit, and exact C(A_2 T(A_4)) tangent failure. The mixed-source transfer also requires $\min_l I(a_l)>0$.

title: A positive comparison for a Conway region without a character operator
status: Sharp positive probe at the intrinsic component action
text: # A positive comparison for a Conway region without a character operator A tangle subtree is represented by a polynomial operator. To continue the quantum estimate through a turn, one must control both its values and its first derivatives at the repeated spectral nodes. A general norm bound for the turn has an exponential cost that need not equal the geometric contribution of that particular subtree. This note obtains the sharper, geometry-dependent estimate for a connected region of multiplication operations with no distinguished character operator inside it. The reduced composition graph calls such a region **unflagged**. Its boundary inputs are actual polynomial operators supplied by adjacent subtrees. They may have complex coefficients and independent physical colors. The proof takes absolute values of their coefficient arrays and closes that positive comparison against a specified polynomial \(W_N\), called the probe. This is a device for an inequality: no additional crossing circle is inserted into the knot. The theorem proves the norm bound, a strict loss for specified high-index contributions, and a way to transfer a loss from one boundary coefficient to the whole region. The [spectral propagation theorem](actual_conway_mixed_core_spectral_propagation.md) uses these conclusions to control angular decay. Their role in the complete volume argument is stated in the [strict-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md); no independent filling argument is attempted here. ## 1. The algebra, the probe and the input bounds Fix the level \(N\), put \(d=N-1\), and let \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). We work in the original pair algebra \[ \mathbb C[z]/(P_N(z)),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, \] where \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial. Its Newton basis is \[ e_r(z)=\widehat B_r(z)=\frac{\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(c_a-z)}{s_r^2},\qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\qquad s_r=\prod_{a=1}^{r}2\sin(\pi a/N),\quad s_0=1. \] The physical turn reverses this basis: \(Te_r=e_{d-r}\). The marked closure functional \(\phi\) satisfies \(\phi(e_re_t)=\mathbf1_{r+t=d}\). These are the exact multiplication, turn and pairing conventions of the [reduced-hub source theorem](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md). The norm \(\|F\|_{\mathcal J}\) is the maximum of \(|F(c)|+|F'(c)|\) over double nodes, together with \(|F(-2)|\) at the odd simple node when present. It is a norm on the full quotient. For example, a local component proportional to \(z-c\) vanishes at the double node but still has a nonzero derivative there. A value-only norm would miss it. The first derivatives are the first Hermite normals retained by the invariant. The logarithmic profiles used below are \[ \begin{gathered} J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\\ \widetilde g(x)=g(\max(x,1/4))\quad(0\le x\le1/2),\\ k(x)=-2J(x/2)\quad(0\le x\le1). \end{gathered} \] We also write \(G_0=g(1/4)\), the maximum of \(g\) on its low-index interval. The probe assigns the large low-index basis elements their endpoint weights and assigns weight one to the remaining indices: \[ w_{N,r}= \begin{cases} e_r(-2),&0\le r\le M,\\ 1,&M<r\le d, \end{cases} \qquad W_N=\sum_{r=0}^{d}w_{N,r}e_r. \tag{1} \] All weights are positive. This choice is dictated by the size of the basis elements, not by a positivity assumption on the physical operator. The full value-and-derivative norm satisfies \[ \|e_r\|_{\mathcal J}\le CN^Cw_{N,r}, \tag{2} \] uniformly at both parities, by the [low-degree interpolation and high-normal estimates](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), §§2–3. Moreover, \[ \log w_{N,r}=Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)\qquad(0\le r\le M) \tag{3} \] uniformly on the closed low range. The high weight has zero logarithmic rate. The comparison coupon \(W_N\) is never inserted into the invariant. Let \(A\) be the expression obtained by taking one maximal connected unflagged region and viewing its attachment to the rest of the tree as the output. Its boundary has \(n\ge2\) inputs, each supplied by a type-\(L\) module. The type means that its strict complete-positive output labels range between zero and one half, with the corresponding boundary profile; it does not say that the full signed polynomial has only low coefficients. Internal edges carry the turn \(T\), and each multiplication vertex has at least three incident branches, counting its output. The reduced-hub theorem places \(A\) in the following recursive rule \[ E\ ::=\ LL\ \mid\ T(E)\ \mid\ EE\ \mid\ LE\ \mid\ EL. \tag{4} \] For example, the smallest component is the product \(A=LL\) of two boundary modules, and its turned output is \(Q=T(LL)\). Larger components may contain turns and further products, exactly as in (4). Every boundary occurrence refers to a distinct original module. Write its actual coefficient array as \[ F_{i,N}=\sum_{r=0}^{d}f_{i,N,r}e_r,\qquad 1\le i\le n. \] The constants \(c_i\) measure the exponential contributions already accumulated inside those modules. They are not circle curvatures. Assume they are fixed real numbers, with one error \(e_N\to0\), uniform over the specified physical input parameters, such that \[ |f_{i,N,r}|\le \begin{cases} \exp\{N[c_i+g(r/N)+e_N]\},&r\le M,\\ \exp\{N[c_i+e_N]\},&r>M. \end{cases} \tag{5} \] These are coefficients of the whole module after its actual operations. The split at \(M\) is a low/high coordinate split. It is not identified with that module's physical core/alias decomposition. Let \(A_N=A(F_{1,N},\ldots,F_{n,N})\) and \(Q_N=T(A_N)\). Let \(A^0\) denote the same expression with each atomic input replaced by the pure complete physical \(h_N=T(L_N)\). Set \[ \Phi_A=\text{complete action of }C(hA^0),\qquad \Omega=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i+\Phi_A. \tag{6} \] The reference \(C(hA^0)\) is flag-free (its effective leaves are ordinary complete leaves, with no separate character attached to a multiplication hub), has \(n+1\ge3\) effective leaves, and has a strict reduced state. For \(n=2\) it is \(C(hhh)\); for \(n\ge3\) its source reduces to the earlier rule requiring composite factors on both sides of the closing product by the exact flag-free adapter. Using this reference does not modify \(A_N\). ## 2. Why closing against the probe bounds the norm Replace every input coefficient by its modulus and compile \(A_N^{\mathrm{abs}}\) from these nonnegative arrays using the same products and turns. The positive Newton product and exact index reversal imply coefficientwise \[ |[e_r]A_N|\le [e_r]A_N^{\mathrm{abs}}. \tag{7} \] The comparison uses the positive multiplication table and the exact reversal of coefficient indices. It does not treat the turn as a multiplicative map or estimate its norm separately. The full pairing extracts each output coefficient: \[ [e_r]T(A_N)=\phi(e_rA_N). \] All basis products and the marked coefficient functional have nonnegative coefficients in this calculation. Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \|T(A_N)\|_{\mathcal J} &\le CN^C\sum_{r=0}^{d}w_{N,r}|\phi(e_rA_N)|\\ &\le CN^C\phi(W_NA_N^{\mathrm{abs}}). \end{aligned}\tag{8} \] Every first normal is retained, including high Newton coordinates invisible at all nodes. The last scalar is nonnegative and its finite source has only polynomially many index states, because the component is fixed. The same estimate holds sectorwise. Split each input into \(r\le M\) and \(r>M\) arrays, and split \(W_N\) likewise. For each specified input band assignment and probe band, the positive closed contraction bounds the corresponding output contribution. In particular the high output part of \(T(A_N)\) is bounded using the high probe \(W_N^{\mathrm{hi}}\). ## 3. Transferring the scalar inequalities to these arrays Use the profiles defined in Section 1. On these domains \(g\le\widetilde g\) and \(k\ge0\). The input bounds (5) and probe (3) satisfy the earlier leaf upper hypotheses, with the constants \(c_i\) added in every sector: \[ \begin{array}{ll} \text{low coordinates:}&\text{rate}\le g\le\widetilde g,\quad r/N\le1/2,\\ \text{high coordinates:}&\text{rate}\le0\le k. \end{array} \tag{9} \] The high coordinate range is a subset of the unrestricted range allowed by the earlier alias inequalities. No physical alias identity or complementary-color relation is needed for this comparison. The precise input from those proofs is a scalar variational inequality. For a fixed closed flag-free expression, put \(\widetilde g\) at each chosen low leaf, \(k\) at each chosen high leaf, and the actual concave gate action \[ \begin{aligned} m(x,y,z)={}&J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z) \end{aligned} \] on its original domain \[ D=\{x,y\ge0:\max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}. \] For every nonempty chosen high subset, the supremum of the action is strictly below the pure complete action. The proof uses only the displayed profiles and domains: - In an \(A_2\) seed, the uniform block inequalities bound the \(AC\) and \(AA\) envelopes by its complete profile tangent minus \(1/100\). Here these two labels mean that one or both leaves use the competing profile \(k\), while the other uses \(\widetilde g\); they do not refer to the component operator \(A_N\). They allow the alias coordinate over its whole interval and thus also cover the present high band. - At a single attachment, the exact square certificate and the remaining leaf tangent bound \(k+m\) against the child's profile tangent with a strict loss. A child loss passes through the pure \(\widetilde g+m\) step. - Turns reverse the output index and tangent sign. Products add the concave gate tangent. At the closed root all free linear terms cancel. - The isolated three-leaf case uses its separate endpoint \(A_2\) regrouping and three-alias bound. It covers \(n=2\) here with the same pair-sum and total-sum constraints. These statements are proved in the [block source argument](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md), §§3–5; [uniform two-leaf inequality](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md); [single-leaf source induction](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), §§6–7, and its [analytic companion](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md); and the [isolated three-leaf proof](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md), §§1–3. Their supporting-plane inequalities do not require the leaf arrays to attain their upper profiles or to arise from a particular physical color. The finite sums are bounded after taking coefficient magnitudes. They therefore give the same upper bounds for arbitrary arrays satisfying (5). The gap is not inferred by comparing two actual source values. If \(C(W_NA_N^{\mathrm{abs}})\) was not initially parenthesized in the earlier closed-composite rule, apply the exact flag-free rerooting to each fixed band assignment. Every external array and its band remain intact. All intermediate kernels remain positive. The complete pure action is unchanged by the same exact source identity and its proved coefficient asymptotics. The isolated case with three effective leaves is handled separately as above. Finite support still requires \(i+j\le d\); larger input sums are zero. Turn and closing relations retain \(d/N=1-1/N\). Uniform factorial rates have \(O(\log N)\) errors on the whole closed support. The supporting-plane proof costs only \(O(1)\) under those affine shifts; compact continuity and uniform closed rates give the same limiting bound. The single uniform \(e_N\), the fixed number of input arrays, and the polynomial number of states are absorbed by reducing a fixed positive gap. ## 4. The resulting bound and the contributions with high indices Under the input hypothesis (5), there is \(\gamma_A>0\), depending on the fixed component but not its physical input parameters, such that \[ \phi(W_NA_N^{\mathrm{abs}}) \le \exp\{N[\Omega+o(1)]\}, \tag{10} \] and every sector with at least one high input or a high probe satisfies \[ \text{positive sector}\le \exp\{N(\Omega-\gamma_A)\} \tag{11} \] for all sufficiently large \(N\). Section 3 proves the nonempty high cases; the all-low sector uses the original pure complete maximum. Consequently \[ \|Q_N\|_{\mathcal J}\le\exp\{N[\Omega+o(1)]\}, \tag{12} \] and, for a possibly smaller \(\gamma_A'>0\), \[ \|(Q_N)^{\mathrm{hi}}\|_{\mathcal J} \le\exp\{N(\Omega-\gamma_A')\}. \tag{13} \] Every contribution containing a high input satisfies the same strict bound. The superscript in (13) denotes the actual output Newton coordinates \(r>M\), including their normals. This is sharp as an action budget, not a lower statement for every arbitrary input array. For reference arrays \(e^{Nc_i}h_N\), the low probe is coefficientwise comparable to \(h_N\) within powers of \(N\). Both positive coefficient families have the uniform closed rate \(g\) with \(O(\log N)\) error, so \[ N^{-C}h_N\le W_N^{\mathrm{lo}}\le N^Ch_N \] coefficientwise. Positivity gives the same exponential rate \(\Phi_A\) for the reference low-probe contraction. The high sectors already have a strict loss. Thus \(\Omega\) is the pure reference action, rather than the generic bare-turn cost \(2G_0\) added to an existing action. ## 5. Which indices can attain the upper rate The preceding estimate removes every term with a high input or a high output index. To use the remaining terms in a larger tree, we also need to know where their indices can be concentrated. Let \(y\) denote the original primitive variables of \(C(hA^0)\), including the scaled probe index \(u=r/N\) and the \(n\) effective input indices \(a_i\). The all-low comparison has the uniform closed upper action \[ \sum_i c_i+g(u)+\sum_i g(a_i) +\sum_{\text{retained gates}}m. \tag{14} \] This upper envelope is the genuine pure complete action of that reference expression. Arbitrary input arrays need not attain it and may even vanish. The strict-state/compiler theorem gives a unique strict optimizer \(y_*\). Its probe index \(\beta\) and effective input indices \(a_i^*\) lie in \((1/4,1/2)\); in the isolated three-leaf case they are \(\arctan(2)/\pi\). The strict gate and angle Hessian gives local strict curvature. Hence for each fixed neighborhood \(U\) of \(y_*\), there is \(\gamma_U>0\) such that \[ \text{all-low positive sum outside }U \le\exp\{N(\Omega-\gamma_U)\}. \tag{15} \] The effective parameter range is checked in the [intrinsic probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), §§1–3. Estimate (15) is uniform under (5), since only upper profiles are used. It is stated in the original resolution and coordinates of this component, even if another rooting was used in §3 for the high-sector bound. No transformed state index is identified with an original physical color. Only a compact regular low-index window around \(\beta\) can therefore attain \(\Omega\); the effective input indices lie in compact regular windows around their own \(a_i^*\). This gives an explicit coefficient loss-transfer statement.
