Suppose one fixed compact interval \(I_i\) contains \(a_i^*\) in its interior, and for a specified physical parameter subfamily, \[ |f_{i,N,r}| \le\exp\{N[c_i+g(r/N)-\delta+e_N]\} \quad\text{when }r/N\in I_i,\qquad \delta>0. \tag{16} \] Choose \(U\) so its \(i\)-th input coordinate lies in \(I_i\). The clean sum inside \(U\) loses \(\delta\), its outside loses \(\gamma_U\), and every high sector loses \(\gamma_A\). By (8), after reducing the smallest margin, \[ \|Q_N\|_{\mathcal J}\le\exp\{N(\Omega-\eta)\}, \qquad \eta>0, \tag{17} \] uniformly over that subfamily for all sufficiently large \(N\). Only coefficient upper bounds enter this proof. It does not infer a physical-color gap from positivity of the signed source or convergence of derivatives. The regular windows and the same finite comparison are also inputs to canonical spectral localization. That analytic step is separate from the finite norm and loss-transfer estimates proved here. ## 6. Why this exponent is the required geometric one A boundary profile gives the optimized complete action of an open subtree as a function of its scaled output label \(b\). Suppose each boundary module has the rigid positive profile \(f_i(b)=g(b)+c_i\). Independence of its internal optimization at a fixed boundary label gives \[ f_A(b)=f_{A^0}(b)+\sum_i c_i,\qquad f_Q(b)=f_A(1-b),\qquad Q=T(A). \] The intrinsic pressure means the maximum obtained by pairing that output profile with one complete leaf. In the geometric boundary coordinates this is the specialization \(X=1\), and it is \[ \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le b\le1/2}[g(b)+f_Q(b)] =\sum_i c_i+\Phi_A=\Omega. \tag{18} \] This is the pressure entering a rigid spine when \(Q\) is a satellite. The probe in (8) estimates that boundary pressure; it has not added a physical crossing circle. The absolute constants and pressure identification use the [intrinsic probe adapter](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), §4, the [rigid-profile geometry](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md), and [complete-mask geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md). Every maximal unflagged component of a strict reduced tree has only type-\(L\) modules or ordinary leaves on its boundary: adjacent flagged hubs send type-\(L\) messages, and the remaining original leaf flags are zero. Its parent-facing root has at least two other branches, so \(n\ge2\). This is the component scope needed for alternating flagged and unflagged reduction. The result does not turn the comparison bands into physical aliases, assume positivity of actual signed modules, or prove a local packet. No source equality is promoted to tangle isotopy. The argument uses the exact earlier rational block certificates without changing their domains. No numerical asymptotic fit enters the norm or loss-transfer proof. The separate geometric adapter supplies the effective parameter range and the equality of pressures used above.

title: Intrinsic probe geometry for unflagged Conway components
status: Exact component action, proper ports and universal pressure gap
text: # Intrinsic probe geometry for unflagged Conway components 31 October 2026. geometric and classical-action theorem. It supplies the exact parameter range and absolute pressure used by the separate [full-normal coefficient-cone bound](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md). The classical probe does not insert a physical circle into the invariant. No signed coefficient estimate follows from the geometry alone. The inputs are the original [strict-mask complete geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md), the [marked quarter-bound theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), the [rigid-spine action identity](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md), and the [exact reduced-hub source](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md). The appendix proves a separate universal pressure gap for an unturned product hub, with an explicit constant greater than \(1/10\). ## 1. The component and its effective leaves Root a strict reduced Frobenius hub tree at a flagged original leaf. A maximal connected component of unflagged hubs has a unique parent edge. Orient that edge toward its parent. Its outgoing source is \[ Q=T(A), \] where \(A=FG\) is an unturned product with at least two branches. Inside the component there are only products and turns of \(A\)-type subtrees. Each boundary satellite from a flagged descendant is an \(L\)-type module; each ordinary original leaf is also \(L\). The exact positive profile of such a boundary module is \(f_{L_i}=g+c_i\), with its absolute constant fixed by the [rigid-spine theorem](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md). Replacing that profile by an effective bare \(g\)-leaf changes the whole component action only by the sum of those constants: \[ f_A(z)=f_{A^{\mathrm{skel}}}(z)+\sum_i c_i. \tag{1} \] The skeleton is a completed expression in effective \(L\) leaves: \(LL,T(A),AA,LA,AL\). No quantum coupon is replaced by \(h\). Define the intrinsic probe \[ \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le a\le1/2} \bigl[g(a)+f_Q(a)\bigr] =\max_{0\le a\le1/2} \bigl[g(a)+f_A(1-a)\bigr]. \tag{2} \] This is the positive action of the strict literal closure \(C(hA)\), with a bare probe leaf. The root is \(L/A\), so the established [strict-state/barrier theorem](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) gives a unique strict optimizer. The probe equation says \(X_Q=1\); since \(Q=T(A)\), equivalently \(Y_A=1\). In the port of the unturned \(A\), root complementarity gives \[ (B_A,X_A,Y_A)=(-x,x,1),\qquad 0<x<1. \tag{3} \] The strict upper bound follows from the \(A\) inequality \(B_A>-Y_A\). The probe leaf has cotangent \(x\). The parent flagged spine evaluates precisely this same intrinsic state: its \(H\)-product has common \(X_Q=1\). Thus (2) is the actual component state selected by the original complete source, not a freely imposed boundary value. ## 2. Every effective leaf is in the closed proper range At the last product \(A=FG\), the strict source equations and the input type inequalities imply \[ Y_A^2=(B_F-B_A)(B_G-B_A)\le(X_A-B_A)^2. \] At (3), this is \(1\le4x^2\), hence \[ \frac12\le x<1. \tag{4} \] Thus even the artificial closing probe leaf has the required range. All descendant \(A\) ports are strictly proper. At the root product, common \(X=x<1\); if a child has type \(A\), its cotangent obeys \(B_i<X\), while positivity of \(B_i+B_j\) and \(B_j\le X\) gives \(B_i>-X\). Consequently \[ Y_i^2=1+B_i^2-X^2<1,\qquad X_i=X<1. \] A turn swaps these two strict bounds. The same argument propagates through every product. The root \(A\) alone may have \(Y_A=1\). For any effective \(L\) input of a retained product, its port is \((X,X,1)\). If the other input is \((B,X,Y)\), the output bound \(Y_o\le1\) gives \[ 1+B^2-X^2\le(B+X)^2,\qquad 1\le2X(B+X)\le4X^2. \tag{5} \] Hence every effective leaf has \(X\ge1/2\). With an \(A\) neighbor the last inequality is strict. If the two children are \(L,L\) and the parent is a proper descendant, \(Y_o<1\) makes the first inequality strict. The inherited \(X<1\) gives the upper bound. Equality \(X=1/2\) can therefore occur only when the root \(A\) itself has two effective \(L\) children. This is exactly the isolated effective three-leaf closure \(C(hhh)\); all three effective leaves then have \(X=1/2\). Otherwise every effective leaf, including the probe, has \[ \frac12<X<1. \tag{6} \] These claims concern effective component leaves. Physical leaves inside their decorated satellites may be at quarter index or have smaller cotangents, as the rigid-spine law already describes. ## 3. Relation to the already certified local parameter domains The [two-leaf block certificate](actual_conway_uniform_two_leaf_block_alias_gap.md) covers \(1/2\le X\le1\), including its exact lower endpoint. The [single-leaf attachment comparison](actual_conway_single_leaf_alias_composition.md) covers proper child ports and the closed slope square used for the bad range \(1/2\le X\le2/3\); the older single-leaf bound covers \(X\ge2/3\). The only new possible parent boundary is the root \(A\) with \(Y_A=1\). For a root single attachment \(A=LF\), write \(X=x\). Equations (3),(5) give the other child's cotangent and height exactly: \[ B_F=\frac1{2x}-x,\qquad Y_F=\frac1{2x}. \] In the bad range \(1/2\le x\le2/3\), the child and parent slopes are \[ \mu=f_F'=2\log(2x^2),\qquad \lambda=f_A'=2\log x. \tag{7} \] Both belong to the original closed square \([-2\log2,0]^2\). The child is proper; equality \(x=1/2\) cannot occur for an \(A\) child, but its limiting value is already in the certificate. For a root \(LL\) block the endpoint \(x=1/2\) is in the original two-leaf block interval. There is also an exact source regrouping of the positive probe. Because \(A=FG\) is unturned, \(C(h(FG))\) can be regrouped in the full Frobenius scalar. If either \(F\) or \(G\) is type \(A\), group \(h\) with the other branch, leaving two completed root children. If both are effective \(L\) leaves, it is the [isolated effective three-leaf closure](actual_conway_isolated_three_leaf_long_twist_volume.md). This is an algebraic source regrouping and a parameter check, not a topology or arbitrary colored-module replacement theorem. Thus there is no missing geometric parameter range at this probe. Whether a proposed signed coefficient adapter actually has these effective \(g+c_i\) source envelopes remains a separate obligation. ## 4. Absolute constants and the original root action Equation (1) gives the exact identity \[ \Omega_Q =F_{\mathrm{probe}}(A^{\mathrm{skel}})+\sum_i c_i. \tag{8} \] No scalar constant is normalized away. Each \(c_i\) is itself the sum of its satellite pressures from the rigid-spine theorem. For completeness, close the whole original reduced tree at a flagged leaf \(h_0\), with satellites \(Q_j\) of type \(L\) or \(A\). Its original Frobenius scalar is \(\phi((Th_0)\prod_jQ_j)\), equivalently \(C(h_0T(\prod_jQ_j))\). The associated \(H\)-profile has \[ f_H(z)=g(1-z)+\sum_j\Omega_{Q_j}. \] At the original coefficient-one closing endpoint \(z=1\), \(g(0)=0\). Continuity of the original optimized action therefore yields \[ F_0=\sum_j\Omega_{Q_j}. \tag{9} \] Alternatively the same equality follows directly by using the original complementary root relation in the positive profile convolution. Substituting (8) and the exact rigid constants recursively into (9) is a finite accounting identity on the original tree. It retains exactly the original complete action. The bare probe appearing in \(F_{\mathrm{probe}}\) is an intrinsic classical dual used to determine a constant; it is not an extra physical auxiliary color, and it does not add an uncharged \(2G_0\) to the quantum source. ## 5. Scope of the probe Equations (1)–(9) concern the original positive profiles and their complete selected states. The effective leaves carry their exact additive constants. Their signed coupons and independent physical colors are retained by the separate coefficient-cone theorem. The old block and attachment certificates therefore have no missing geometric parameter range at this probe. Whether a proposed coefficient comparison belongs to the required cone is a source obligation; the profile identity does not prove it. The complete action accounting does not add an artificial \(2G_0\), a crossing circle or a filling slope. ## Appendix. A universal dual-pressure gap for an unturned product ### A.1. The exact product hypothesis Let \(A=FG\) be an actual unturned product, with both children of strict type \(L\) or \(A\). Either child may have its own internal turns. The product has strict output interval \((0,1)\). Let \(f_A(z)\) be its original positive optimized action, extended continuously to the closed output interval. The established [strict-state/barrier theorem](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) gives a unique strict optimizer and an analytic strictly concave profile on \((0,1)\). At that optimizer put \[ B=\cot(\pi z),\qquad B_i=\cot(\pi x_i),\qquad \kappa_A=e^{-f_A'(z)},\qquad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa_A},\qquad Y^2=\kappa_A X^2. \tag{A1} \] The source equations give a common positive \(X\) for both inputs and the output: \[ X^2+Y^2-B^2=1,\qquad B(B_1+B_2)=B_1B_2+X^2-1,\qquad B_1+B_2>0. \tag{A2} \] Strict gate support \(z>x_i\) and the exact child type inequalities give \[ B<B_i\le X. \tag{A3} \] Equality \(B_i=X\) holds for a child of type \(L\); it is strict for a child of type \(A\). This hypothesis is automatically the local one at an unflagged reduced product hub: its incoming branches have type \(L\) or \(A\). A larger product can be associated at its last binary gate. All constants internal to rigid children remain in the profiles. Define the two intrinsic probe pressures \[ \Omega_A=\max_{0\le a\le1/2}\bigl[f_A(a)+g(a)\bigr], \qquad \Omega_{TA}=\max_{0\le a\le1/2}\bigl[f_A(1-a)+g(a)\bigr], \tag{A4} \] where \[ g(a)=J(2a)-4J(a),\quad J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\quad G_0=g(1/4)=\frac{2G}{\pi} \tag{A5} \] and \(G\) is Catalan's constant. The associated strict closed roots supply interior maximizers. The first probe has \(X_A=1\); the second has \(Y_A=1\), since the turn exchanges \(X,Y\). Closed endpoints are included in (A4) only to make compactness explicit. ### A.2. Derivative domination by the two-leaf product Rearranging (A2) gives the exact identity \[ Y^2=(B_1-B)(B_2-B)\le(X-B)^2. \tag{A6} \] All factors are positive by (A3), so there is no sign or squared-branch ambiguity. Using \(Y^2=1+B^2-X^2\), (A6) becomes \[ 1\le2X(X-B),\qquad X\ge X_2(B):=\frac{B+\sqrt{B^2+2}}2. \tag{A7} \] If either child has type \(A\), the inequalities are strict. For the actual two-leaf product \(hh\), both inputs have \((B_i,X,Y_i)=(X,X,1)\), so \[ B=X_2-\frac1{2X_2},\qquad Y_2=\frac1{2X_2},\qquad f_{hh}'(z)=\log(4X_2^4)=2\log(2X_2^2). \tag{A8} \] For any fixed \(B\), the function \[ x\longmapsto\log\frac{x^2}{1+B^2-x^2} \] is strictly increasing on \(0<x<\sqrt{1+B^2}\). Equations (A1) and (A7) therefore give the whole-output inequality \[ f_A'(z)\ge f_{hh}'(z), \qquad 0<z<1. \tag{A9} \] It is strict everywhere if either child has type \(A\). If both children are \(L\), their profiles are \(g\) plus constants, and equality in (A9) is exact, with those constants added to \(f_{hh}\). At \(z=1/2\), \(B=0\) and \(X_2=1/\sqrt2\), so \(f_A'(1/2)\ge0\). Strict concavity of \(f_A\) implies \[ \max_{0\le z\le1/2}f_A(z)=f_A(1/2). \tag{A10} \] The continuous endpoint values do not add a new maximizer above this value. ### A.3. An explicit uniform gap greater than \(1/10\) Use the fixed upper-half probe \(z=7/12\), so its root leaf has \(a=1-z=5/12\). On \(1/2\le z\le7/12\), \[ B\ge\cot(7\pi/12)=\sqrt3-2>-\frac1{2\sqrt3}. \] The final inequality is exactly \(7>4\sqrt3\), proved by \(49>48\). Since \(X_2(B)\) is increasing and \[ \frac1{\sqrt3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=-\frac1{2\sqrt3}, \] one has \(X_2(B)>1/\sqrt3\). Thus (A8)–(A9) imply \[ f_A(7/12)-f_A(1/2) \ge -\frac16\log(3/2). \tag{A11} \] The original leaf \(g\) is concave on \([0,1/2]\), with \(g(1/2)=0\). Its chord from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\) yields \[ g(5/12)\ge G_0/3. \tag{A12} \] Evaluating (A4) at \(a=5/12\) and using (A10)–(A12) proves \[ \boxed{\quad \Omega_{TA}-\max_{0\le z\le1/2}f_A(z) \ge \frac{G_0}{3}-\frac16\log(3/2) >\frac1{10}. \quad} \tag{A13} \] The last inequality is elementary and requires no numerical evaluation. The alternating Catalan series gives \(G>1-1/9=8/9\); the classical bound \(\pi<22/7\) therefore gives \(G_0>56/99\). Also \(\log(3/2)<1/2\). Hence the middle expression in (A13) is strictly larger than \[ \frac{56}{297}-\frac1{12}=\frac{125}{1188}>\frac1{10}. \] This constant is independent of the product syntax, its size and all additive rigid-profile constants. No compact family or lower bound on its intrinsic satellite curvature is required. ### A.4. Reflection and pressure comparison The exact two-leaf root satisfies \[ X_2(B)X_2(-B)=\frac12. \] Equation (A8) consequently gives \(f_{hh}'(1-z)=-f_{hh}'(z)\). The difference \(f_{hh}(z)-f_{hh}(1-z)\) has zero derivative and vanishes at \(1/2\); therefore \(f_{hh}\) is symmetric under \(z\mapsto1-z\). Integrating (A9) from \(1-z\) to \(z\) proves \[ f_A(z)\ge f_A(1-z)\quad (1/2\le z\le1),\qquad \Omega_{TA}\ge\Omega_A. \tag{A14} \] For \(1/2<z<1\), the first inequality is strict if either child is type \(A\). The maximizing probe for \(\Omega_A\) is strictly in \((0,1/2)\), so the pressure inequality is then strict too. With two \(L\) children, both profiles differ from the symmetric \(hh\) profile only by a constant, so \(\Omega_{TA}=\Omega_A\). The unturned product condition is essential to the proof. Applying an outer turn reverses the output derivative, and does not preserve (A9) or the claimed orientation of (A14). This note makes no corresponding claim for an arbitrary type-\(A\) expression with a top turn. ### A.5. Exact scope for the pending signed estimate The result proves the requested classical inequality for the high Newton-index part of a candidate unflagged-turn estimate, if that part has already been bounded by the original lower-half profile. It does not itself establish that quantum coefficient bound or replace the original signed coefficient by its positive profile. The separate [coefficient-cone theorem](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md) supplies its own exact finite adapter. The low Newton part uses a separate source-exact alias or spectral estimate; it is not inferred from this pressure inequality. Likewise (A14) does not allow the exponential norm of an arbitrary turn to be charged to a new physical leaf. There is no new source-circle insertion, isotopy, geometric volume replacement, or full mixed-hub theorem here. ## scope This is an analytical proof, with no numerical test or inferred topological re-rooting. The signed coefficient bound, local packet, primitive filling calibration and eventual invariant limit remain separately named inputs.

title: A uniform mixed-color source gap for arbitrary robust Conway expressions
text: # A uniform mixed-color source gap for arbitrary robust Conway expressions 29 October 2026. The positive complete-circle Conway source controls its ENTIRE original auxiliary-color packet. The signed radical contributions are uniformly exponentially smaller than the complete source, even after arbitrary finite branching and turns. For every retained cylindrical factor there is also a strict gap outside any fixed small complete-color corridor. These are whole-source estimates, not bounds on selected colors. The complex corridor packet and the marked geometric peripheral interpretation remain separate statements. No Newton output is declared to be a meridian. ## 1. Exact source and conclusions Use the original pure leaf h_j=Rturn(L_j), with actual auxiliary color 1<=j<=N. Put D=N-1, M=floor(D/2). The [mixed-leaf theorem](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md) gives h_j=C_j+R_j, C_(N-h)=sum_(v=h)^M N^2 s_(2v)/(s_v^2 s_(v-h)s_(v+h)) Bhat_v for 0<=h<=M, C_j=0 for j<=floor(N/2). (1) Every C_j has nonnegative Newton coefficients bounded coefficientwise by h_N. Every R_j lies in the square-zero nilradical J_N=span{Bhat_v:v>=ceil(N/2)}, J_N^2=0, (2) and each coefficient has absolute value at most N/2. These are identities in the full repeated-root algebra, including its original normal data. Let E be any fixed robust expression generated by A=h_N^3, actual turn, and product. Give every individual circle leaf an independent ordinary color j_l. Let A_(E,N)(j) be its original marked cylindrical scalar, C_(E,N)(j) the same circuit with each leaf replaced by C_j, and Z_(E,N)=A_(E,N)(N,...,N)>0. **Uniform radical-gap theorem.** There are gamma>0 and N_0 such that for all N>=N_0 and ALL physical auxiliary-color choices, |A_(E,N)(j)-C_(E,N)(j)|<=exp(-gamma N) Z_(E,N), 0<=C_(E,N)(j)<=Z_(E,N). (3) The analogous coefficientwise estimate holds for the OPEN operator at every output. It is preserved under further positive Conway composition, not only by the final closure. For a retained cylindrical factor C(A), or C(FG) with F,G robust, write F0=max A_E, where A_E=V_E/pi is the complete source action after removing only the forced flat final product gate. For every sufficiently small fixed delta>0 there is gamma_delta>0 such that, for large N, max_(some N-j_l>delta N) |A_(E,N)(j)| <=exp[N(F0-gamma_delta)]. (4) Both parities and composite levels are included. The expression and delta are fixed before N tends to infinity. The gaps are proved below; no numerical profile is used to infer their existence. ## 2. The two-leaf profile has its free maximum at output 1/2 Set J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi u))du, g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x), 0<=x<=1/2, m(x,y,z)=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y) -J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). The product domain is max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1. The proved ideal-atom decompositions make g and m concave on their closed domains, with a negative definite Hessian on their effective interior variables. Define F2(t)=max [g(x)+g(y)+m(x,y,t)], 0<=t<=1, (5) with x,y<=1/2 and the product constraints retained. It is finite, continuous and concave on [0,1]. For 0<t<1 a strict feasible point is x=y in (t/2,min(t,1/2)). The nonvertex-flat inward barrier and negative Hessian give a unique strict optimizer and a strictly concave analytic profile on (0,1). Its free maximum occurs at t=1/2, x=y=a=(1/pi)atan(sqrt(2)). (6) Indeed, in the strict domain, exp(m_x)=sin(pi(x+y))sin(pi(z-x)) /[sin(pi x)sin(pi(x+y-z))], exp(m_z)=sin(pi z)sin(pi(x+y-z)) /[sin(pi(z-x))sin(pi(z-y))], g'(x)=2log cot(pi x). At (6), cos^2(pi a)=1/3, exp(m_x)=exp(m_y)=2, g'(a)=-log 2, and exp(m_z)=1. Thus all three derivatives vanish. Concavity and strictness prove the unique global maximum and hence F2'(t)>0 for 0<t<1/2. (7) ## 3. A radical leaf cannot maximize a three-leaf seed Let F3(b) be the complete h_N^3 coefficient profile, normalized as log(coefficient)/N. Exact positive associativity and its variational limit give F3(b)=max [F2(t)+g(y)+m(t,y,b)], (8) with 0<=y<=1/2. Every b in (0,1) has a unique strict optimizer. At b=1 the final gate is forced flat, but the three leaves and preceding gate are strict at the unique maximum. These are purely variational facts from the [boundary profile proof](actual_conway_boundary_volume_relation.md) and its cylindrical endpoint argument; no complement identification is needed here. An alias leaf has output y>=1/2 and polynomially bounded coefficient. Its relaxed envelope inside the three-leaf seed is G(b)=max [F2(t)+m(t,y,b)], y>=1/2, max(t,y)<=b<=t+y<=1, 1/2<=b<=1. (9) F3 and G are continuous on this closed interval. For G, convex combination of feasible states proves concavity; compactness gives upper semicontinuity and endpoint interpolation gives the opposite inequality. **Key claim: every maximum in (9) has y=1/2.** Take 1/2<b<1 and suppose a maximum had y>1/2. There is a strict feasible point with y>1/2: choose y in (1/2,b) and then t in (b-y,min(b,1-y)). Joining to it excludes every flat prism boundary by the nonvertex-flat inward volume barrier. At t=0, y=b and the atom (b,0,1-b) supplies the same barrier. F2 has no negative infinite inward derivative. Therefore the supposed maximum has a strict prism, 0<t<1-y<1/2, and stationarity gives m_y=0, F2'(t)+m_t=0. (10) The first equation yields exp(m_t)=sin(pi y)sin(pi(b-t)) /[sin(pi t)sin(pi(b-y))]>1. (11) The numerator minus the denominator is exactly sin(pi b)sin(pi(y-t))>0. Equations (7),(11) contradict the second equation in (10). This proves the claim for 1/2<b<1. At b=1/2 the constraint y<=b forces y=1/2. At b=1 the constraints force t+y=1, the last product action vanishes, and (7) makes F2(t) maximal at t=1/2, again giving y=1/2. Since g(1/2)=0, (9) is thus the restriction of the complete problem (8) to the boundary leaf y=1/2. The strictness and uniqueness in (8), including b=1, imply F3(b)>G(b) for every b in [1/2,1]. Consequently gamma_*=min_(1/2<=b<=1) [F3(b)-G(b)]>0. (12) This uses continuity and compactness, not finitely sampled outputs. ## 4. Uniform exact seed comparison Expand the original three-leaf seed: h_(j1)h_(j2)h_(j3) =C_(j1)C_(j2)C_(j3) +sum_(i=1)^3 R_(ji) product_(k!=i) C_(jk). (13) Terms with two aliases vanish EXACTLY by (2), including their normals. Commutativity of the actual pair algebra puts the remaining alias last inside this seed. No operator is moved through a turn or another box. By positivity the coefficientwise absolute value of each summand in (13) is bounded by the corresponding coefficient of (N/2) [sum_(v=ceil(N/2))^D Bhat_v] h_N^2. (14) It is zero at outputs r<ceil(N/2). For any sequence of remaining outputs r/D->b, endpoint-uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state counts give limsup_N (1/N)log coefficient_r(14)<=G(b). (15) To verify (15), select a largest summand and pass to convergent scaled indices. Their limits satisfy the closed constraints in (9), and the two complete leaves give (5). The alias has zero exponential cost. Replacing scale N by D changes the exponent by O(log N), also at sine zeros. This argument includes b=1/2 and b=1. For the complete seed coefficient a_(N,r), the exact-output boundary limit says, along EVERY such output sequence, (1/N)log a_(N,r)->F3(b). (16) This is the proved prescribed-output theorem, not an assumption that rounded real optimizers have the correct output. Compactness and (12),(15),(16) now imply, uniformly over all outputs and all colors, |mixed_seed_r-core_seed_r| <=exp(-gamma_* N/2) a_(N,r) (17) for sufficiently large N. Otherwise a sequence of failures would have a convergent output subsequence contradicting the strict gap (12). The factor three in (13) and polynomial factors are absorbed by halving the gap. Outputs below ceil(N/2) have identically zero error. ## 5. Arbitrary turns and branching preserve the gap Let S be the fixed number of seed occurrences. The actual turn permutes Newton coefficients; multiplication has nonnegative structure constants; the marked closure extracts one coefficient. Thus absolute coefficientwise inequalities propagate through every operation. Each seed is its nonnegative core plus an error bounded by epsilon_N times the complete seed, with epsilon_N=exp(-gamma_*N/2). Each core is itself bounded by the complete seed. Expanding multilinearly in seed errors, without moving a turn, bounds the error at every open output by [(1+epsilon_N)^S-1] times the complete coefficient. (18) This proves the open version of (3), and then its marked closure. Turns do not preserve the nilradical; the entire propagated radical was bounded, not removed by passing to a semisimple quotient. ## 6. The whole physical color complement has a strict gap For a retained cylindrical factor the reduced complete angle problem has a unique strict maximum x_*. Every leaf lies in (0,1/2), and every unforced prism is strict. The complete variational theorem gives log Z_(E,N)=NF0+o(N). If some j<=floor(N/2), the core circuit is zero and (3) proves (4). Otherwise put chi_l=(N-j_l)/N. For a leaf with output x>=chi, its core action is g_chi(x)=g(x)-Delta(x,chi), Delta(x,chi)=J(x-chi)+J(x+chi)-2J(x)>=0. (19) For 0<x<1/2 and 0<chi<=x, this loss is strictly positive. Differentiate in chi<x: partial_chi Delta =log[sin(pi(x+chi))/sin(pi(x-chi))]>0, and use continuity at chi=x. The loss may vanish at x=1/2, so the strict COMPLETE optimizer is essential. Take the compact joint domain of feasible complete states and parameters 0<=chi_l<=x_l with at least one chi_l>=delta. Its deformed action is at most F0. Equality would require x=x_* and every loss zero, impossible at the selected interior leaf with chi_l>=delta. Hence the maximum on this joint domain is F0-c_delta for some c_delta>0. Uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state counts bound the entire positive core outside the corridor by exp[N(F0-c_delta/2)] for large N. Combining this with (3) proves (4). All physical auxiliary colors, signed radical terms and original normal directions are covered. ## 7. Remaining steps toward a filled-knot equality These estimates apply to an arbitrarily branched fixed robust Conway source. The [general original-source filling theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) additionally requires the specified finite holomorphic corridor packet with a uniform nonzero complex saddle asymptotic, and an actual marked peripheral representation whose regulator is its action. Neither is inferred just from the gap or from naming a boundary curve an A-polynomial. Audit: [finite source expansion and analytic identities](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.py). Its checks supplement the analytic proof, not an extrapolation of exponential rates from finitely many levels. This source-gap result does not supply a complex packet or peripheral representation. The separate interfaces are now supplied by the [uniform complex packet](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md) and [actual marked deformation](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md). Together they give the [full long-filling hyperbolic volume equality](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) for the retained robust link class.

title: A uniform alias gap for an entire two-leaf Conway block
text: # A uniform alias gap for an entire two-leaf Conway block 31 October 2026. This proof treats two leaves and their original multiplication gate together. It holds on the entire proper-seed range and removes the earlier individual-leaf condition \(X\ge2/3\). Its finite certificate uses exact rational inequalities with proved transcendental remainder bounds, not numerical sampling. ## 1. The original functions and the uniform statement Retain the original complete, core and alias profiles \[ \begin{gathered} J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\\ \widetilde g(x)=g(\max(x,1/4)),\quad 0\le x\le1/2, \qquad k(x)=-2J(x/2),\quad 0\le x\le1. \end{gathered} \tag{1} \] The actual Newton product action and its whole domain are \[ \begin{split} m(x,y,z)&=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y)\\ &\quad-J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z),\\ D&=\{x,y\ge0:\ \max(x,y)\le z\le x+y\le1\}. \end{split} \tag{2} \] All these actions are continuous and concave on their stated domains. The tetrahedral decomposition of \(m\) proves this even when one input exceeds \(1/2\). An alias is not assigned the support of a pure leaf. At a complete optimized seed \(A_2\), set \[ \begin{gathered} X=\cot(\pi a),\qquad \cot(\pi b)=X-\frac1{2X},\\ F_2(b)=2g(a)+m(a,a,b),\qquad \lambda=F_2'(b)=2\log(2X^2). \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] For \(1/2\le X\le1\) this state is strict, \(a\ge1/4\), and \(-2\log2\le\lambda\le2\log2\). Define the dual upper envelopes \[ \begin{split} Q_{AC}(\lambda) &=\max_{D,\ y\le1/2} [k(x)+\widetilde g(y)+m(x,y,z)-\lambda z],\\ Q_{AA}(\lambda) &=\max_D[k(x)+k(y)+m(x,y,z)-\lambda z]. \end{split} \tag{4} \] **Uniform block lemma.** For every \(X\in[1/2,1]\), \[ Q_{AC}(\lambda),\ Q_{AA}(\lambda) \le F_2(b)-\lambda b-\frac1{100}. \tag{5} \] Equivalently, the corresponding output envelopes satisfy \[ G_{AC}(z),\ G_{AA}(z) \le F_2(b)+\lambda(z-b)-\frac1{100},\qquad 0\le z\le1. \tag{6} \] These are upper envelopes for the actual coefficients. No assertion is made that a physical color or a signed coefficient attains them. The coefficient bounds include the original normal terms, both level parities and every retained half-twist sign, as checked in the [exact block source proof](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md). ## 2. Reduction to finitely many global supporting inequalities Let \(P(\lambda)\) be the maximum of \(g(x)+g(y)+m(x,y,z)-\lambda z\) over \(D\) with both inputs at most \(1/2\). At (3), both input derivatives vanish and the output derivative is \(\lambda\). Concavity proves \[ P(\lambda)=F_2(b)-\lambda b. \tag{7} \] Explicitly, the original product derivatives at (3) are \(m_x=m_y=-2\log X\) and \(m_z=2\log(2X^2)\), while \(g'(a)=2\log X\). Thus the three derivatives of the pure dual action vanish, including at the endpoints of the stated range. Any strict rational pure state \(p=(a_p,a_p,b_p)\) gives the lower bound \[ P(\lambda)\ge A(p)-\lambda b_p, \qquad A(p)=2g(a_p)+m(p). \tag{8} \] For either alias action \(H=k+\widetilde g+m\) or \(H=k+k+m\), choose a rational strict state \(v\); for \(AC\), choose its core coordinate above \(1/4\). The global tangent bound is \[ H(w)\le H(v)+\nabla H(v)\cdot(w-v). \tag{9} \] The full polytopes have exactly these vertices: \[ \begin{split} V_{AC}={}&\{(0,0,0),(1,0,1),(1/2,1/2,1/2), (0,1/2,1/2),(1/2,1/2,1)\},\\ V_{AA}={}&\{(0,0,0),(1,0,1),(0,1,1),(1/2,1/2,1/2)\}. \end{split} \tag{10} \] To check completeness, use nonnegative coordinates \(p=z-x,q=z-y,r=x+y-z,w=1-x-y\), which obey \(p+q+2r+w=1\). Thus \(D\) is a tetrahedron. Cutting it by \(y\le1/2\) removes one vertex and adds the two displayed edge intersections. A linear function attains its global maximum at a listed vertex. Partition \(\lambda/\log2\) into sixteen intervals \[ [-2+j/4,-2+(j+1)/4],\qquad j=0,\ldots,15. \tag{11} \] The [rational certificate table](../experiments/conway_two_leaf_block_alias_certificate.json) specifies one pure state and one state for each alias action on each interval, all with denominator \(10^6\). For every vertex \(w\) and both endpoints \(t\) of its interval, the [exact verifier](../experiments/verify_conway_two_leaf_block_alias_certificate.py) checks \[ A(p)-t\log2\,b_p-H(v)-\nabla H(v)\cdot(w-v) +t\log2\,w_z>\frac1{100}. \tag{12} \] For each fixed vertex this expression is affine in \(t\), so its endpoint checks cover the entire interval. Its dependence on \(w\) is affine, so the vertex checks cover the entire polytope. Equations (8)--(12) prove (5) for every real slope in the range. No assumption about the location or uniqueness of an alias maximizer is used; core plateau and boundary maximizers are included automatically. There are 32 block comparisons and 288 endpoint/vertex inequalities. Their smallest certified lower bound is \[ \frac{210002102902309638093785766005979344329} {5000000000000000000000000000000000000000} >\frac1{25}>\frac1{100}. \tag{13} \] The [result record](../experiments/conway_two_leaf_block_alias_certificate_results.json) contains every rational lower bound. A candidate optimizer was useful for finding the rational table; optimization is absent from verification and is not a premise of the proof. ## 3. Rational enclosures for every transcendental expression The verifier performs outward-rounded interval arithmetic with integer endpoints at denominator \(10^{40}\). It uses no floating-point trigonometric functions or special-function library. The gradients are \[ \begin{split} g'(y)&=2\log\cot(\pi y),\qquad k'(x)=-\log(2\sin(\pi x/2)),\\ m_x&=\log\frac{\sin\pi(x+y)\sin\pi(z-x)} {\sin\pi x\sin\pi(x+y-z)},\\ m_y&=\log\frac{\sin\pi(x+y)\sin\pi(z-y)} {\sin\pi y\sin\pi(x+y-z)},\\ m_z&=\log\frac{\sin\pi z\sin\pi(x+y-z)} {\sin\pi(z-x)\sin\pi(z-y)}. \end{split} \tag{14} \] All arguments are strictly positive at the rational states. For the core derivative, cosine is evaluated as \(\sin\pi(1/2-y)\). Machin's identity \(\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)\), with 40 alternating terms and the next-term bound, encloses \(\pi\). Reduce sine arguments to \((0,\pi/2]\), then use its Taylor polynomial through degree 41 and the degree-43 remainder bound. Positive logarithm arguments are rescaled by recorded powers of two. For \(z=(x-1)/(x+1)\), the 80-term expansion \[ \log x=2\sum_{j=0}^{79}\frac{z^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R, \qquad 0\le R\le\frac{2z^{161}}{161(1-z^2)} \tag{15} \] is used on the explicitly checked interval \(0\le z<1/2\). The same series at \(z=1/3\) encloses \(\log2\). For the actions use \(J(0)=J(1/2)=J(1)=0\) and \(J(1-t)=-J(t)\). Euler's sine product, followed by integration, gives for \(0<t<1/2\) \[ J(t)=t\log(2\pi t)-t -\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\zeta(2n)t^{2n+1}}{n(2n+1)}. \tag{16} \] The expansion follows from \(\log(1-t^2/k^2)\); the remaining integrated terms have one sign and are summable. The logarithmic term is integrable at zero. Use \(\zeta(2)=\pi^2/6\), and for \(2\le n\le20\) the rational integral-comparison bounds \[ \sum_{k=1}^{64}k^{-2n}\le\zeta(2n) \le\sum_{k=1}^{64}k^{-2n}+\frac{64^{1-2n}}{2n-1}. \tag{17} \] Since \(\zeta(2n)<2\), the omitted part of (16) has absolute value at most \[ \frac{2t^{43}}{21\cdot43(1-t^2)}. \tag{18} \] All inequalities in (12) therefore have proved rational enclosures. Outward interval error can only weaken the certified gap. The verifier checks feasibility, branch inequalities and contiguous slope coverage as well as the final comparisons. ## 4. Consequence for the whole original source The exact block source proof contracts only the two original leaves and their one positive Newton multiplication gate. It retains \(i+j\le N-1\), all phases and the full Hermite data. Internal first derivatives vanish at the complete seed; its output derivative is exactly (3). Using (6) therefore preserves every surrounding wire derivative when the original stationary supporting planes are summed. Every proper two-leaf seed in the retained \(C(FG)\), \(s\ge2\) grammar has \(1/2<X<1\). Thus (5) applies automatically. Larger proper seeds retain their old positive leaf margins. Every nonempty alias sector loses a positive amount after summing the actual seed and macro-product bounds. The \(d=N-1\) shifts cost only \(O(1)\) in the exponent, and fixed trees have polynomially many wire states. The all-core concave majorant and original far-color core estimate then give the complete physical-color complement gap. The previously primitive lattice, complex packet and marked geometry for this entire grammar are unchanged. Consequently the original filling transfer gives the hyperbolic knot complement volume after all auxiliary fillings and a loop-free knot parity choice, without the individual-leaf cutoff. Isolated \(C(A_2)\) is still excluded. The old local-tangent example \(C(A_2\mathcal R(A_4))\) is now covered: its negative individual deficit is compensated by the original multiplication gate. The grammar still is not asserted to represent every arborescent template. ## Verification and scope The exact verification is reproducible with the standard Python library: ```sh python experiments/verify_conway_two_leaf_block_alias_certificate.py ``` The separate [geometric response argument](actual_conway_two_leaf_monotone_alias_response.md) explains why the worst conjugate gap occurs at the lower endpoint, but is not needed for this proof: the finite certificate covers the whole interval directly.

title: Independently long integer twists on weighted Conway trees
status: All fixed weighted trees in the literal closure
text: # Independently long integer twists on weighted Conway trees 31 October 2026. The class is specified by literal ordered tangle operations. Every finite rooted ordered tree with at least two vertices gives such a presentation; its branching, valence and depth are unrestricted. A fixed knot-producing parity pattern and sufficiently large independent integer weights give the original invariant's hyperbolic knot complement volume limit. General arborescent coverage and mixed flagged/unflagged source trees remain separate. ## 1. The weighted tangle presentation and theorem Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite rooted ordered tree with \(H\ge2\) vertices, numbered with root \(0\). There is one integer twist box at each vertex. Write \(T\) for the original ordered quarter-turn and \(R^n\) for the original integral two-strand twist tangle. For each nonroot vertex define recursively \[ Q_v(\mathbf n)=T\!\left(R^{n_v}\prod_{w\text{ child of }v} Q_w(\mathbf n)\right), \tag{1} \] where the product keeps the given child order and an empty product is one. At the root retain the literal cylindrical closure \[ K_{\mathcal T}(\mathbf n) =C\!\left(T(R^{n_0})\, T\!\left(\prod_{w\text{ child of }0}Q_w(\mathbf n)\right)\right). \tag{2} \] ![A weighted Conway composition tree with branching and a unary chain; this specifies syntax, not a knot projection.](../book/figures/weighted-conway-tree.png) The marked one-cut convention, terminal order and disk framings are part of (1)–(2). These are Conway tangle operations on integral rational pieces, so a one-component result is an arborescent knot. No conventional plumbing or numerator-closure isotopy is required by this definition. **Weighted-tree theorem.** For every fixed \(\mathcal T\) there is a finite \(B(\mathcal T)\) such that, for every fixed tuple of integers \(\mathbf n\) with \(|n_v|>B(\mathcal T)\), if the literal pairing in (1)–(2) has one component and no internal closed component, its complement is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N(K_{\mathcal T}(\mathbf n))\right| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathcal T}(\mathbf n)). \tag{3} \] The original reduced enhanced Kashaev evaluation is denoted by \(K_N\). Both parities and all composite levels occur in the limit. The signs and magnitudes of the weights are independent; no ratio bound is imposed. The tree and all integer weights are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The threshold is allowed to depend on the whole tree. Every tree in this statement has knot-producing parity choices. This is the constructive terminal-pairing conclusion of the [general marked-mask geometry theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), applied to the literal expression below. It does not say that every parity choice makes a knot. Full twists preserve the pairing. Equivalently, first fix \(\epsilon_v\in\{0,\pm1\}\) giving a knot and write \(n_v=\epsilon_v-2p_v\). There is \(P(\mathcal T,\epsilon)\) such that (3) holds for all independently fixed signed integers \(|p_v|>P(\mathcal T,\epsilon)\). Taking a maximum over the finitely many knot-producing parity patterns, and increasing the integer threshold, gives the displayed formulation in terms of \(|n_v|\). ## 2. The exact colored source and its strict geometry Before filling, vertex \(v\) carries the original auxiliary character \(P_v=R^{\epsilon_v}L_{j_v}\), with independent \(1\le j_v\le N\). Set \[ h_v=T(P_v),\qquad D_v[E]=T(P_vE),\qquad Q_v=D_v\!\left[\prod_wQ_w\right],\qquad E_0=\prod_{w\text{ child of }0}Q_w. \tag{4} \] The original scalar is exactly \[ Z_N(\mathbf j)=\phi(h_0T(E_0))=\phi(P_0E_0). \tag{5} \] The equality is the full Frobenius turn identity. No normal direction, physical color, framing character or additional dimension factor is removed. In the literal h/T/product language a nonterminal \(Q_v\) is \(T[(T h_v)\prod_wQ_w]\); a terminal \(Q_v\) is \(h_v\). Each \(Q_v\) has strict type L. Inductively, a nonempty product of its children has type L or A, so its product with \(T h_v\), of type H, has type H and its final turn has type L. At the root, \(E_0\) is L or A, and \(h_0T(E_0)\) has a strict complementary root pair. Thus the [strict-source compiler](actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md) and [marked-mask theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) apply without an additional geometric test for this class. Put \(G_0=g(1/4)=2\mathrm{Catalan}/\pi\), with \(g(a)=J(2a)-4J(a)\) and \(J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt\). The [exact complete-character kernel](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md), or independently the [rigid-spine action formula](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md), gives \[ F_0=\lim_N\frac1N\log Z_N^0(N,\ldots,N)=2G_0(H-1), \qquad \operatorname{Vol}(Y_{\mathcal T}^{\epsilon})=2v_{\mathrm{oct}}(H-1), \quad v_{\mathrm{oct}}=4\mathrm{Catalan}. \tag{6} \] Here \(Z_N^0\) has all signs zero, and \(Y_{\mathcal T}^{\epsilon}\) is the actual complete augmented exterior with the retained signs. Equation (6) is an absolute calibration, not a norm budget chosen for convenience. Its rightmost volume belongs to the unfilled augmented link; the knot volume in (3) is the distinct filled critical value in §5. ## 3. A global estimate closed under arbitrary branching Use the faithful full-Hermite norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal J}\), recording values and first derivatives at every double Casimir node and the value at the odd simple node. The [decorated-character theorem](actual_conway_decorated_character_spectral_closure.md) proves, for the actual turn and all physical signs and colors, \[ \|D_j^\epsilon[E]\|_{\mathcal J} \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{2NG_0}\|E\|_{\mathcal J}. \tag{7} \] The input norm also yields a Gaussian angular envelope for the canonical output, localized at \(z=-2\). Multiplication preserves both the norm bound and the envelope. The [exact root-character Fourier theorem](actual_conway_root_character_fourier_contraction.md) gives a strict loss whenever the newly inserted character has a macroscopic color deficit. A deficit in a descendant already gives a norm loss, which (7) preserves. There are exactly \(H-1\) decorated turns below the closing character. The latter has polynomial norm in the original closure. Hence the induction gives, for every fixed \(\delta>0\), some \(\gamma_\delta>0\) and all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \max_{\substack{1\le j_v\le N\ \text{for all }v\\ \max_v(N-j_v)\ge\delta N}} |Z_N(\mathbf j)| \le e^{N(F_0-\gamma_\delta)}. \tag{8} \] It also gives a uniform whole-cube upper rate \(F_0+o(1)\). The complete positive kernel supplies a matching lower rate in (6). Thus no oversized bound has been substituted for the complete action. The Fourier input to this induction retains the normal terms. Their weights cancel the folded frequency that would otherwise destroy (8) near the smallest physical colors. The estimate concerns the original whole source, before any asymptotic replacement or filling sum. ## 4. A general complementary-color principle for all alias sectors This step is independent of the shape of \(\mathcal T\). Let any fixed multilinear original source have \(H\) physical leaves \(h_j^\epsilon\). For \(j>N/2\), its [exact original split](actual_conway_two_leaf_block_source_gap.md), §1, is \[ h_j^\epsilon=C_j^\epsilon+A_j^\epsilon, \qquad A_j^\epsilon=(-1)^N h_{N-j}^\epsilon, \qquad h_0^\epsilon=0. \tag{9} \] For \(j\le N/2\), the core is zero. These are identities in the full repeated-root algebra; the physical half-twist transport is linear and preserves (9). Assume that the whole source has a strict gap whenever any color is at most \(N/2\), uniformly over all other physical colors. If all \(j_v>N/2\), multilinearity gives \[ Z_N^{\mathrm{core}}(\mathbf j) =\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,H-1\}} (-1)^{|S|}(-1)^{N|S|}Z_N(\mathbf j^{,S}), \qquad j_v^{,S}=\begin{cases}N-j_v,&v\in S,\\j_v,&v\notin S. \end{cases} \tag{10} \] Every nonempty subset inserts at least one small color. A zero color makes that whole term zero. There are only \(2^H-1\) such terms, with \(H\) fixed. If some original \(j_v\le N/2\), the all-core source is zero and the assumed gap applies directly to \(Z_N\). Consequently \[ \sup_{\text{physical }\mathbf j} |Z_N(\mathbf j)-Z_N^{\mathrm{core}}(\mathbf j)| \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F_0-\gamma)} \tag{11} \] for some \(\gamma>0\). This controls the total nonempty-alias contribution without estimating its separately expanded signed coefficients. Applying (8) with \(\delta=1/2\) proves (11) for every weighted tree. The [general core theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) now supplies an exact finite, separately even holomorphic window \(\mathcal C_N\) with \[ \mathcal C_N(\chi)=N^{3/2}a_\epsilon(\chi) e^{N\Phi_\epsilon(\chi)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad a_\epsilon(0)\ne0,\quad \Phi_\epsilon(0)=F_0, \tag{12} \] For physical deficits \(h_v=N-j_v\) in a fixed small corridor, \[ |Z_N(\mathbf N-\mathbf h)-\eta_N\mathcal C_N(\mathbf h/N)| \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F_0-\gamma)},\qquad \eta_N=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\pi(N-1)}4\sum_v\epsilon_v\right). \tag{12a} \] The packet expansion holds on a fixed complex neighborhood, retaining every original integer offset, unit phase and interpolation error. Every complete leaf is at least quarter index. For \(H\ge3\) the gate Hessians supply full primitive rank; for the two-leaf knot case, a pure leaf supplies the needed curvature. Both-odd two-leaf patterns have two main components and are not among the knots in (3). The diagonal color Hessian has entries \[ \partial_v\partial_w\Phi_\epsilon(0) =-\frac{2\pi c_v}{1-\epsilon_vi c_v}\delta_{vw}, \qquad c_v=\cot(\pi a_v)>0. \tag{13} \] Its real part is negative definite. Equations (8), (11) and (12) verify all global and local hypotheses of the original-source filling transfer. ## 5. The selected filled action is the actual knot complement volume For the integral filling slopes \(p_v\), so the physical power is \(R^{\epsilon_v-2p_v}\). The full Fourier–Hermite circle-basis identity substitutes those powers exactly into the original diagram. Its coefficient mass is at most \(2N(1+|p_v|)\) per port. Thus (8) and (11) remain exponentially negligible after filling for each fixed slope tuple. The [entire filling theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) retains all endpoint currents and nonzero charges and proves a nonzero asymptotic with selected exponent \[ S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*)= \Phi_\epsilon(\chi_*)+\frac{\pi i}{2} \sum_v\frac{(\chi_{*,v}-1)^2}{p_v}, \qquad dS_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*)=0. \tag{14} \] Its leading amplitude is nonzero for all independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes. This controls the whole invariant, not merely one formal stationary term. For the same literal strict tree, the [general marked-mask theorem](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) gives an actual nearby representation of the original augmented-link group, with primitive logs and absolutely calibrated regulator \[ U_v=-2\pi i\chi_v,\qquad V_v=-2\partial_v\Phi_\epsilon, \qquad G=2\pi i\Phi_\epsilon, \quad \operatorname{Vol}(\rho_\chi)=\Im G-\frac12\sum_v\Re U_v\Im V_v. \tag{15} \] The stationary equations in (14) are exactly \(U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i\). The framed metric-completion theorem then gives a smooth complete finite-volume metric on the actual disk-filled manifold, with primitive angular turn \(2\pi\). All auxiliary crossing circles are filled; the main knot cusp remains unfilled. On that solution, \[ 2\pi\Re S_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}(\chi_*) =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathcal T}(\mathbf n)). \tag{16} \] One fixed reciprocal-slope neighborhood works for the finitely many ports. Taking a common analytic and geometric threshold proves (3). The [original normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) changes the retained scalar by a unit framing character, or by the recorded single polynomial one-cut factor in the modified convention; neither changes the logarithmic limit. ## 6. More general presentations and the remaining boundary The same conclusion holds for any fixed original strict h/T/product expression whose reduced Frobenius hub tree has exactly one flagged original leaf at every hub, and whose actual endpoint pairing gives a knot. The [reduced-hub theorem](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) is an exact identity for all independent physical colors and first normals. It transfers (8) to the original expression. Principle (9)–(11) then restores that expression's own core packet, and its own marked geometry proves (16). No tangle isotopy or peripheral identification between rearranged expressions is needed. For arbitrary strict syntax the exact reduced-hub criterion is at most one flagged leaf per hub. The no-flag case reduces to the already proved completed grammar; the present argument treats the all-hubs-flagged case. Mixtures still contain genuine turns without an adjacent original physical character. The full-Hermite turn norm has exponential rate \(2G_0\); charging that cost to an invented leaf would exceed the known geometric action. A sharp estimate for such mixed trees remains open. The weighted-tree theorem permits arbitrary finite branching and unary continued-fraction chains, but uses the displayed literal closure. It is not a classification of all arborescent knot presentations, a uniform threshold over growing trees, or a generic main-meridian quantum A-polynomial theorem. Those broader parts of the active goal remain open. ## Coverage and scope The [repository comparison](actual_conway_root_star_prior_source_coverage.md) identifies the earlier outer-kernel cancellation and the one-hub all-odd overlap with the belt source. The [belt construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) explicitly leaves branched multi-belt graphs outside its source argument. The new ingredient here is closure under nested \(T(R^\epsilon L_jE)\) with distinct original characters, together with the complementary-color principle. For literature coverage, [van der Veen's Whitehead-chain paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611181) states a volume-conjecture theorem for an infinite family of links. It is a relevant comparator; no equivalence of its knot types with all presentations (1)–(2), or novelty classification, is proved here. Its proof is not an input to this argument.

title: Correlated neighboring bands of the original boundary source
status: Correlated adjacent-band errors and the normalized finite-clock quotient
text: # Correlated neighboring bands of the original boundary source 30 October 2026. The exact ratio of two neighboring charged source products is rational in their actual clocks. On the original six-type resonant boundary chart, their root packet errors are correlated strongly enough to divide by the odd-source normalization of size N^-1. The resulting model is an explicit FINITE quotient. Its classical limit, a transverse Gaussian reduction, and its coefficient in the original period are not evaluated here. ## 1. One original product and one integral band path Use the labeled right-angled matching polyhedron, actual cut and original white-prefix dictionary of the [common chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). There is one main component. Let N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Fix the actual folded labels a_i, m_i=d-a_i and deficits s_i=d-2a_i. The number of original tensors is fixed. Initially one can require sum s_i<=S0, independently of N; the proof below is uniform also for 0<=s_i<=eta N, with a sufficiently small fixed eta. After the two ACTUAL cuts, use the primitive common head chart of the [charged-current theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md). The component charge conditions must hold. Fix its free coordinates and the two input heads at the common boundary assignment. Its three bands are restrictions of the SINGLE affine family h(delta)=h_N+delta v, (1) where v is the recorded integral charge path. Its entries are bounded independently of N. All original vertex equations, reversed dual heads and cup complements hold for complex delta. In particular delta=+1 and -1 are not independent head assignments or independently selected asymptotic branches. Their original physical supports remain different. Let S_N(delta) be the actual charged ROOT product s_delta of the common-band theorem: original whites, literal pi duals, the remaining cups/caps, turns and fixed root channel weights, before any internal head sum or exposed coherent functional. The ordinary scalar cap at the exposed cut has been REMOVED. Its replacement is the literal off-diagonal coherent row after the two bands are assembled. Keeping that old diagonal cap would annihilate a nonzero charged band. For all remaining local tensors we use the specified continuation in the [original source envelope](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md). This is not its closed charge-zero product S_F. In particular its charge-zero complementary mark/cap formula Xi_N is NOT used for delta=+/-1. The coherent binomial row is applied after this statement; its input head is fixed along (1), so its common factor can also be retained on both sides of the pointwise ratio. The hypothesis is on this actual source presentation: each numerator must be one of the original six types 200,002,220,022,202,222. Unspecified routed R or U factors can introduce 000 or 020. Their inclusion is NOT justified by the theorem, even if their contracted root channel has the same scalar. No off-grid equality between such presentations is assumed. Take r_frame=N rho, rho in a positive real compact, and the first-cut angle in a fixed sufficiently small positive compact of the common chart. For some c>0 independent of N, (1) extends to |delta|<cN: each clock is multiplied by exp(2pi i v_e delta/N), a small bounded complex perturbation. The scaled escaping clocks remain in compact subsets of C*, the finite negative clocks stay in a small neighborhood of the negative ray, and 202 totals stay near their positive ray. The 200/002 Bessel factors stay uniformly away from zero. Shrink c once for the finite network. The exact head lifts and all half-index offsets are kept; this extension does not assert finite-a stationarity. ## 2. Rational source quotients before asymptotics The actual large white is W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m q^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^1(U,V)/F_m, i+j=m+r, U=Q^i, V=Q^j, F_m=(Q;Q)_m. For ANY integral u,v its exact meromorphic quotient is W_a(i+u,j+v;r+u+v)/W_a(i,j;r) =q^(-dv) H_m^1(Q^u U,Q^v V)/H_m^1(U,V). (2) The same identity holds before specialization with q replaced by zeta and the actual H_m^(Q^-N). Thus (2) is not obtained by differentiating a root collision. It retains the internal Casimir label m. For the specified cup, L<N fixed, p_L(x)=exp(pi i x) q^[x(L-x-1)] Fhat_N(x)Fhat_N(L-x)/F_L, the factorial recurrence gives, for u>0, p_L(x+u)/p_L(x) =(-1)^u q^[u(L-2x-1)-u^2] product_(j=1)^u(1-Q^(x+j)) /product_(j=0)^(u-1)(1-Q^(L-x-j)). (3) Negative shifts are the reciprocal formula at the shifted base head. Caps use the literal complementary argument and inverse. Physical cup scales are constant in x. Formula (3) also holds for the specified generic moving-period factorial, before taking the root. For estimates at the ROOT, an exact simplification is essential. Write L=d-s and use the PROVED root reflection with the moving-factorial section specialized only now. It gives the meromorphic identity p_(d-s)(x)=C_(N,s) exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)), C_(N,s)=N(-1)^s Q^[s(s+1)/2]/F_(d-s). (4) Explicitly, the reflection is Fhat_N(x)Fhat_N(d-x)=N q^[x(x-d)]. Apply the unit recurrence s times to its second factor. The removed product is product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(-x-j)); factoring each negative power gives exactly (4). Also C_(N,s)=F_s by the finite root factorial identity. In particular p_d(x)=exp(pi i x)q^-x, and p_(d-s)(x+1)/p_(d-s)(x) =-q^(s-1)(1-QU)/(1-Q^(s+1)U), U=Q^x. (5) The exp(pi i x) in (4) is literal. It is not set to one off the integer lattice. The physical scale N q^-d^2 and every other source character remain. Equation (4) cancels the quadratic factorial gauges BEFORE estimating derivatives; estimates for their separate absolute logs, which can be of size N log N, are unnecessary. For clarity, the literal dual is still pi_a(r;i,j)=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)], (6) with FIXED root gamma_a and the actual reversal. Equations (2),(3) applied to (6), together with the recorded turn and peripheral characters, prove that S_N(+1)/S_N(-1) is an explicit rational function of the base clocks. No norm pi_a W_a is inverted. Apparent denominators are kept, or canceled as meromorphic factors; the boundary chart below avoids them. This proves the rational identity BEFORE any asymptotic replacement or normalization by the odd source. ## 3. The finite model and a bounded neighboring quotient Here are explicit choices of numerator model B_(m,N)(U,V). All finite clocks in the formulas co-vary along (1). Put a=d-m, s=m-a, P_s(T)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r), K_a=[2a choose a]_Q, M(U,V)=I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+, M0(U)=I-(qU/2)H_-. Below S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), S_0=1, is the sine factorial; it is distinct from the channel deficit s. The matrices are the actual positive Hermitian source matrices from the [complementary packet](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md). The following are finite expressions, including their source phases: * 200: E_m(U,V) J_0(2sqrt(K)), where E_m=(-1)^m Q^{m(m+1)/2}(UV)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q^r/U), K=sin^2(pi m/N)(V-1)/(pi^2(U/N^2)V). The Bessel series specifies this expression without a square-root ambiguity. * 002: product_(r<m)(V-Q^r) J_0(2sqrt(K0)), where K0=N^2 V sin^2(pi m/N)(1-U)/pi^2. * 220: V^a K_a det M0(U) P_s(UV). The actual large-partner product is retained exactly. * 022: (UV/A0)^m times the 220 model at (A0/V,A0/U), A0=Q^d. This is the literal generic reciprocity restricted to the root. * 202: A_a(UV)P_s(UV), where A_a(T)=(-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2] sum_(k=0)^a [S_a/(S_k S_(a-k))]^2(QT)^k. * 222: V^a K_a det M(U,V) P_s(UV). This model is the EXACT root numerator; no determinant is frozen at its limiting clocks. The first two and the relative 202 estimate are proved in the [root hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). The 220 comparison is proved in the complementary packet; multiplying both sides by the SAME P_s changes no relative error. The 022 model uses its exact reciprocity. The 222 zero exclusion and its uniform finite-clock neighborhoods are proved by [positive determinant domination](actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.md). Replace each numerator of S_N(delta) by its displayed model, and keep EVERY other factor exactly. Call the resulting nonzero product B_N(delta). Uniformly on |delta|<cN, S_N(delta)=B_N(delta)(1+R_N(delta)), |R_N(delta)|<=C/N, (7) where R_N is holomorphic. This follows by the finite product of the uniform holomorphic root estimates on the indicated complex compact domains, not by extending estimates known only on a real ray. The first two limiting Bessel factors are nonzero on the common chart; continuity gives the required smaller complex neighborhoods. For 202 and 222, P_s has roots on the unit arc near -1 when eta is small, whereas the total lies near a positive compact. For the mixed outer-degree types its total tends to zero or infinity, and the reciprocity above retains the corresponding nonzero partner factors. We also need the two-sided bound |B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)|+|B_N(-1)/B_N(+1)|<=C. (8) Here is a direct proof, with no assumption on an absolute logarithm of B_N. Write D=partial_delta; each varying clock Z obeys D Z=(2pi i n/N)Z for a fixed bounded integer n. For (4), all factors Q^(x+j), 1<=j<=s, either remain uniformly separated from 1 in a compact negative-clock neighborhood, or tend uniformly to zero or infinity. Thus D log p_(d-s)(x) =v_x[pi i+(s-1)pi i/N] +(2pi i v_x/N) sum_(j=1)^s Q^(x+j)/(1-Q^(x+j)) is O(1+s/N). Physical cups have s=0. This also controls inverse cups and the reversed arguments in (6). The actual common-chart factorial-domain proof ensures these assertions for the auxiliary heads, including 202/202 and both maximal-fold parities. No escaping Gamma factor remains to estimate after the EXACT identity (4). Each original white/turn/peripheral character has a linear head exponent with coefficient O(N) in a power of q or Q (and the retained bounded integer character in (4)); therefore its logarithmic delta derivative is O(1). No arbitrary added character with an unbounded logarithmic delta derivative is covered by (8). Fixed root weights, factorials, gamma and K_a have derivative zero. In the 200/002 models the degree-m monomials and endpoint products have bounded logarithmic derivative: each finite linear factor has logarithmic derivative O(1/N), while m=O(N). The Bessel factor has derivative O(1/N), since its argument varies by O(1/N) and it stays away from zero on a fixed complex compact. For 220, H_- is positive. Its eigenvalue product proves |U partial_U log det M0(U)|<=C a on the negative-clock neighborhood. For 202 the negative real roots of its positive-coefficient polynomial give |T partial_T log A_a(T)|<=C a near the positive ray. Each partner factor gives an additional O(1/N) delta derivative, uniformly under the separation just stated. The 022 expression has the same bounds after its literal reciprocal substitutions and exact monomial. Finally, for 222 fix the nearby negative raw clocks as a reference. For M_ref=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+, alpha,beta>0, conjugation by M_ref^-1/2 puts both positive summands below I. A small complex clock neighborhood leaves the normalized inverse bounded and bounds M_ref^-1/2 (D M) M_ref^-1/2 by C/N. Hence |tr(M^-1 D M)|<=C a/N. This controls the exact finite determinant uniformly at the fold. Combining the finitely many factors yields |D log B_N|<=C on |delta|<=2, with its continuous local logarithm. Integration between -1 and +1 proves (8). ## 4. Correlation survives the small odd-source denominator Apply Cauchy's formula to the SAME R_N in (7) on the delta disk. For |delta|<=2 it gives |D R_N|<=C/N^2. Therefore S_N(+1)/S_N(-1) =[B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)](1+O(N^-2)). (9) The improved error is a correlation statement. Two unrelated relative O(N^-1) estimates would not prove it. All source and model quotients are nonzero here for sufficiently large N. Let t range in a fixed real compact subset of (0,1), and retain the EXACT normalization of the [source-preserving odd insertion](actual_source_preserving_odd_framing_period.md), kappa_N(t)=1-q-t^d+q(1-t)^d. Its proved lower bound is |kappa_N|>=1/N. Equations (8),(9) give [S_N(+1)-q S_N(-1)]/[kappa_N S_N(-1)] =[B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)-q]/kappa_N + O(N^-1). (10) In particular this theorem retains the exact q, rather than replacing it by one before a cancellation of order N^-1. The entire finite model quotient, every cup character, internal channel label, clock correction and half-index offset remains on the right of (10). The constants are uniform for bounded total deficit, both parities, and also in a sufficiently small fixed near-fold label neighborhood 0<=s_i<=eta N. Thus they apply to the shrinking window sum_i s_i log N=o(N). This is a ROOT ratio result and does not expand the previously proved generic-normal window. No assertion is made that the right side of (10) has a nonzero limit, or even stays bounded. In particular replacing its finite label dependence by the complete parabolic stationary value would require an additional argument. Formula (10) supplies an explicit model with an absolute O(N^-1) error relative to S_N(-1), even when its leading finite quotient has not been evaluated. ## 5. What contraction would additionally require This is a theorem about the original uncontracted products on a common affine band path. Their coherent first-cut weight, the original internal head measure and the two original support cycles have not been removed. A ratio of sums or periods is not the sum or period of the pointwise ratio in (9). Uniform pointwise relative errors alone do not control the relative error of a complex integral with cancellation. A Gaussian-reduced version would need one common holomorphic transverse reduction, its full coarea/Hessian factor, controlled common cycles and ends, and a nonzero model pushforward with a uniform relative remainder. If such a reduction itself supplies (7) on a cN disk and (8), the same Cauchy proof gives (9),(10) for that reduced family. This implication is conditional; those analytic and cycle hypotheses are not proved by the present uncontracted calculation. Nor is a routed source with uncontrolled 000/020 factors covered by removing its routing only after contraction. Focused audit: [original shifts and correlated local packets](../experiments/audit_actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio_results.json). It checks 649 actual white neighboring quotients and 649 literal dual neighbors through the first genuine quantum jet, 68 generic cup shifts, 58 root reflection-reduced cups and two symbolic source exponents. At 160 digits it compares 48 original finite Newton sums with the six model formulas, then checks 384 packet values, 96 paired W-pi source quotients and their normalized odd errors, 192 complex head-neighborhood values and 48 exact escaping-cup logarithmic derivatives. Both level parities and fixed neighboring folded labels are retained. The local signed fixtures cover all six types, including an explicitly supplemental 202/202 face pair; they are not a numerical global-network proof. The theorem concerns an uncontracted source in the specified controlled presentation. It supplies no Gaussian reduction or period coefficient. The charged product has its exposed scalar cap removed, and the charge-zero Xi_N formula is omitted. No contracted, arbitrarily routed, or model-limit conclusion follows.

title: What all-face collars do not supply: source homology and a gluing criterion
text: # What all-face collars do not supply: source homology and a gluing criterion 28 October 2026. The physical-face collars and quantitative regular gradient estimate are compatible local analytic ingredients. They do not alone prove a low-action deformation of the original scalar. There is an exact source-homology obstruction to applying that argument as one ordinary contour homotopy of its undecomposed holomorphic summand. The obstruction occurs for the SAME hyperbolic knot after ordinary signed Markov stabilizations; it is not a hypothetical phase counterexample. Source-specific current cancellation, exact normalization pruning or a pointed-operator reduction can evade it. Thus this does not rule out all contour or boundary-to-interior methods. A sufficient quantitative gluing criterion is given below; its source-compatibility premise is not yet proved for the full cotangent atlas. ## 1. A precise individual-evaluation homology lemma Let F_N be holomorphic on the swept region Omega_N in C^r. Let Gamma_0 be the original product residue contour around the finite integer box in the independent original source coordinates. For every valid state p in that box, the ordinary product Cauchy kernel gives F_N(p)=(2pi*i)^(-r) integral_(Gamma_0) F_N(z) dz_1...dz_r/product_j(z_j-p_j). (1) Suppose a closed deformed current Gamma_N, including all its retained components and multiplicities, is homologous to Gamma_0 in Omega_N minus UNION_(j,n) {z_j=n}, (2) where the removed set includes ALL coordinate integer divisors met by the original source. In particular every form in (1) stays holomorphic on the deformation complement. Equation (1) holds with Gamma_N too, independently of whether it was originally obtained using a cotangent kernel. Define its individual Cauchy mass M_(p,N)=(2pi)^(-r) integral_(Gamma_N) |dz_1 wedge ... wedge dz_r|/product_j|z_j-p_j|. Then EXACTLY |F_N(p)| <= M_(p,N) sup_(Gamma_N)|F_N|. (3) Consequently, if log M_(p,N)=o(N), a deformation in this homology class cannot place the undecomposed density below the exponential rate of that original individual state. Subexponential geometric mass plus subexponential inverse distance to these Cauchy kernels is a sufficient hypothesis on M. An arbitrary deformation with uncontrolled near-divisor mass is not covered. This is a statement about ordinary homology preserving ALL individual evaluation tests. It deliberately excludes source-specific crossings of canceled divisors, dropping exact zero pairings only for the selected source, current recombination, and distinct transports of meromorphic phase sectors whose compensating poles must be paired. Such operations can change these extra tests while preserving the original period. They are possible escapes, not contradictions to (3). ## 2. An actual same-knot family with arbitrarily high individual states Use the original complete physical head, with Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), d=N-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, g_b=theta Q^(-b), theta=x^(1-N), kappa=exp(pi*i*(N-1)^2/(2N)). For a positive crossing, a DIAGONAL original matrix element has a=b+k and exact value r_+(a,b;k)=kappa x^(-2b)Q^(b^2) F_a^2/[F_k F_b^2]. (4) The original negative crossing on the reversed pair has the conjugate value, including conjugate kappa. For N divisible by four take A=3N/4, B=N/4, k=N/2. The actual endpoint-uniform factorial estimate, or its elementary interior Euler--Maclaurin proof, gives |r_+(A,B;k)|=|r_-(B,A;k)| =(2N)^(-1/2) exp[N v_8/(2pi)](1+O(1/N)). (5) Indeed I(3/4)=-I(1/4)=Catalan/(2pi), I(1/2)=0 and v_8=4 Catalan. The factorial square-root prefactors give precisely (2N)^(-1/2). Both actual half-root and full Cartan phases are retained in (4); they have modulus one. Start from ANY fixed one-component braid diagram of ANY hyperbolic knot K. Its closed state with every head A and every original transfer zero is valid. Every original crossing then has modulus one, at either sign, and all original pivots also have modulus one. Append signed Markov stabilizations, starting with a positive one and then alternating signs. The new last head values are B,A,B,A,..., and every appended transfer is k=N/2. Each new crossing is diagonal: (A,B) is unchanged by the positive crossing and (B,A) is unchanged by the negative crossing. Thus this is an EXACT valid closed original state at every stage, with no mod-N routing or reset. With s such stabilizations, its absolute value is (2N)^(-s/2) exp[s N v_8/(2pi)](1+O_s(1/N)), (6) up to the retained label-independent external line, which has no exponential modulus at the original complete normalization. The single original averaged-cut factor 1/N also changes only a power of N. No additional average is attached to each new head. ### Independent check of the whole original Markov normalization The exact original partial trace of the new head is Tr_new[(I tensor g)R_+]=kappa theta I, Tr_new[(I tensor g)R_-]=kappa^(-1)theta^(-1)I. (7) Here is a direct proof without assuming an external invariance theorem. For the positive case its a-th cut diagonal, divided by kappa theta, is F_a^2 sum_(b=0)^a Q^(b^2)/(F_(a-b)F_b^2)=1. (8) The rational identity follows by decomposing a partition with largest part at most a by its Durfee square of side b: the square contributes Q^(b^2), the part to its right is a b by (a-b) rectangle, with generating polynomial {a choose b}_Q, and the part below has largest part at most b, contributing 1/F_b. This is a bijection, so 1/F_a=sum_b Q^(b^2){a choose b}_Q/F_b as a formal power series and hence as a rational identity. All root denominators satisfy b<=a<N. There is no first-partial-trace off-diagonal by exact degree support. For the negative trace put A'=d-a and replace b by d-r. Exact factorial reflection at Q^(-1) and the SAME identity (8) give, before its final Cartan simplification, the scalar kappa^(-1)theta x^(2a) Q^[-a^2+1+A'(A'+1)]. Since x^2=Q^(-1), A'+a=N-1 and theta^2 Q=1, this is exactly the second value in (7), with no parity exception. Both are unit scalars. The original zero-framing line cancels precisely these actual Markov factors. Partial tracing the new head in a whole word uses its original pivot and NO factor 1/N; the sole original average in (2) of the cardinal source stays unchanged. Thus every stabilized diagram has the SAME original knot invariant and the same volume, while (6)'s individual-state rate is arbitrarily large as the fixed number s increases. This independently checks every new pivot and normalization relevant to the example. ## 3. Consequence for the proposed global dynamics For the cardinal completion, F_N is holomorphic on the stated joint box and equals the exact original summand at every valid integer state. Therefore (1)--(6) apply to that ACTUAL source. Choosing s with s v_8>Vol(K) rules out an undecomposed low-|F_N| cycle with subexponential Cauchy mass in the homology class (2), at the desired knot-volume level. All proper physical faces of that diagram still have the proved outward action coefficient, and its genuine regular critical values still have the representation-volume bound. This pinpoints a compatibility which those local results alone do not establish. One must use the selected source, not silently prove an equally strong estimate for every individual-state evaluation. The already proved exact Markov pruning DOES evade this example; it contracts a complete source cell before absolute estimation. It is part of the remedy, rather than a contradiction to the theorem. Additional source-specific relations can likewise evade the extra evaluation tests. The example does not prove that a pruned diagram still has the same obstruction, nor that all sector/current contour methods fail. ## 4. A sufficient quantitative gluing criterion and its power count The following criterion isolates what a valid boundary-to-interior construction would have to add. It is local-current data rather than an assumption that the unknown whole period already has a low-action representative. Suppose the finite physical-face atlas is supplied with SOURCE-specific chain homotopies on the complete marked sector/current complex, with all these properties: * Their boundary formulas include all overlap curtains, valid cotangent residue currents, and paired artificial pole currents. The formulas glue on overlaps and preserve the selected original period. They need not preserve the additional tests (1). * A common marked height H is used. A face operation, including its outgoing current pieces, lowers H by at least g_N=c N^(-alpha)log N, up to a smaller overshoot O(N^(-beta)log N), beta>alpha. No unmatched side current is left at arbitrary height. Already low-height terminal pieces are allowed. * After the leading height is accounted for, each operation has a bounded number of pieces and log mass cost at most C log^C N+C N^(1-beta)log^C N. The exact collar Gamma bounds can provide this type of local estimate; their leading negative action must not be counted again as a positive amplitude loss. * Regular gradient segments preserve the same source class and have cumulative log mass at most N^(B epsilon)log^C N, with B epsilon<1. All ends either enter another covered patch or the target sublevel. If the initial relevant height range is O(log^C N), these properties give the desired exp(o(N)) total transport cost. In fact the number of face operations is at most J_N=O(N^alpha log^C N), because each spends at least a fixed fraction of g_N in height. Their combined log mass is consequently bounded by O(N^alpha log^C N+N^(1+alpha-beta)log^C N)=o(N), (9) provided alpha<1 and beta>alpha. Fixed branching adds only O(J_N). The regular-flow cost is also o(N). A transported chain ending in H<=Vol(K)/(2pi)+eta then gives the upper bound by triangle inequality; letting eta decrease gives the sharp limsup. This proves the criterion. The not-yet-verified part for the actual global cotangent atlas is precisely the first two source-compatible gluing properties, including valid interior residue currents and overlap heights. Finite face count, endpoint action drop and a regular flow bound do not imply them. In particular source-universal chart identities alone preserve the individual tests behind (3); state-specific normalization/Ward or pointed-A information must enter where that barrier is exceeded. ## 5. Independent audit of the source-specific A-boundary alternative The [A-boundary Schur theorem](actual_a_boundary_schur_transport.md) uses the initial weighted identity-row source: $g_I=0$ exactly when those colors are retained in $B$. Completing the square gives $H=-P_{II}^{-1}P_{IB}$ and the positive Schur operator $S$, with $\ker P=E\ker S$. Consistency fixes $\beta=g_B^*S^+g_B$; the border normalization is not independently chosen. I checked the positive bordered Gram and the selected coefficient formula [lambda^nu z]D/[lambda^nu]Q, including the retained kernel: g_B and the selected observable vanish on it, so the kernel factors off as lambda^nu and the z derivative is the exact squared selected boundary response.
