The banded Neumann-series inverse decay and the rigid two-endpoint recurrence example also check, including lambda_min(S)~3*4^(-n)/4. No source or weight correction was needed. The fresh audit passed four actual pointed-source eliminations, the exact one-dimensional retained-kernel fixture and four rational rigid boundary recurrences. This construction can escape (3): it estimates the ACTUAL selected source response, not every holomorphic state evaluation. Its remaining boundary energy estimate is not supplied by uniqueness or the good interior gap. [Independent original-source normalization audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cotangent_homology_stabilization.py) checks (4)--(8), both crossing signs and every new pivotal trace.

title: Exact coupled cap sources and their regular meridian boundary relation
text: # Exact coupled cap sources and their regular meridian boundary relation 28 October 2026. Every terminal pair source can be peeled by exact coefficients before taking a critical-point limit. The resulting source is a coupled geometric polynomial, including at the original marked cap. An exact interval identity retains its complete numerator and gives a regular complex Lagrangian on which the actual framed meridians are inverse. This supplies the classical cap equation missing from treating the two terminal monomials as independent saddle variables. The retained interval endpoints are disjoint from every regular noncentral geometric critical branch for a one-component knot. It does not compute the intersection of the original interval/torus cycle with a hyperbolic thimble. In particular, a generic geometric clock is complex, while the initial interval parameter is real. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_coupled_caps_interval_source_results.json) check the literal duality matrices, all fused boundary coefficients, whole original four-head words, interval identities on their logarithmic charts, and the actual framed meridian product. ## 1. Physical pair sources, with their original normalization Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, y=x^(-1)Q^(-1), K_i=x_i B_i^(-1). Use the existing balanced factorial basis and the actual oriented dual in [the pivotal-duality proof](relative_pivotal_duality.md). On the physical basis vector indexed by (a,b), the cup and ordinary right cap are cup_x(a,b)=N x^(a-d) delta_(a+b,d), cap_x(a,b)=N^(-1) y^a delta_(a+b,d). (1) The original averaged marked right cap, before any Ward-corner replacement, is mark_x(a,b)=x^b/N^2, 0<=a,b<N. (2) Here is a direct normalization check. In the original unbalanced basis, J_x e_b=c_b e_(d-b)^*, c_b=(-x)^b Q^(b(b+1)/2), and the pivot is g_a=x^(-d)Q^(-a). The balanced reflection identity is F_b F_(d-b)=N(-1)^b Q^(b(b+1)/2). Thus the balanced cup is F_a F_b/c_b on a+b=d; the ordinary cap is c_b g_a/(F_a F_b). These give (1). Writing D_F=diag(F_a), the actual averaged defect is D_F^(-1)g^(-1)e D_F, e_(a,b)=1/N. Its cap row is (D_F^(-1)g^(-1)e D_F)^t g J_x before balancing, which gives (2) at EVERY pair (a,b), not just on the invariant fiber. For a k-pair plat, the cup degree is k d. Each ordinary cap forces degree d on its pair. The actual word and every Gaussian dilation sector preserve total integer degree. Consequently, after the k-1 ordinary caps, (2) is paired only with the marked fiber a+b=d. On that fiber it is mark_x(a,d-a)=x^(d-a)/N^2. (3) This restriction uses degree, not a Ward identity applied separately to a Gaussian sector. Finite head support and all external scalar lines are retained. If one first uses the already assembled Ward corner, reversing that corner after decomposing into Gaussian sectors is not justified; start from (2) instead. Let K_N(r)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) r^a. With the coefficient-source convention that a row at (a,b) contributes z_1^(-a)z_2^(-b), the exact coupled kernels are Cup_x(z_1,z_2)=N x^(-d) z_2^d K_N(x z_1/z_2), Cap_x(z_1,z_2)=N^(-1) z_2^(-d) K_N(Q^(-1)z_2/(x z_1)), Mark_x(z_1,z_2)=x^d N^(-2) z_2^(-d) K_N(z_2/(x z_1)). (4) The last line is precisely (2) on its forced degree fiber. Its normalization is different from the ordinary cap. The phase Q^(-1) in the ordinary cap is retained. ## 2. Exact terminal-factor peeling These kernels can also be recovered by peeling the terminal factors in [the all-Hardy residue graph](actual_hardy_forest_residue_reduction.md). For the actual inverse fusion C_x^(-1)=F_2 F_1^(-1) V_- F_2^(-1), the ordinary fused row is N^(-1)<0,d|. The terminal F_2 extracts F_d=N, while the first-head reciprocal factorial at output 0 extracts 1. The remaining exact coefficient is [b^d] U_N(b/z_2) V_N(b/(x z_1)) =z_2^(-d) (t;Q)_d/N =z_2^(-d) K_N(Q^(-1)t)/N, t=z_2/(x z_1). (5) Only the first N jets of U_N,V_N occur. The first equality is the finite q-binomial theorem; the second follows from (t;Q)_d=(1-t^N)/(1-Q^(-1)t). Both numerator and denominator are retained, with the ratio extended as its polynomial. For completeness, the fused original marked row m_x=mark_x C_x on the same degree fiber has m_x(r,d-r)=x^(d-r)(-1)^r Q^(-r(r+1)/2) F_r^2/N^2. (6) Indeed the explicit fusion coefficient gives sum_(a=0)^r F_(d-a)/F_(r-a)=N, by the finite q-binomial theorem and the reflection identity. This yields (6). Peeling its adjacent complete inverse fusion gives m_x C_x^(-1)=mark_x, not a new selected row. There is no division by the knot value and no requirement that it be nonzero. Equations (4)--(6) eliminate all terminal monomial/factorial caps and their redundant fusion-frame variables by exact coefficients. They do not discard a terminal source endpoint: that information is in K_N. ## 3. Replace K_N by its exact interval source On a chosen logarithmic chart write L=Log r and put A(r)=Log r/(r-1), K_N(r)=N A(r) integral_0^1 exp(N s Log r) ds. (7) This is an exact elementary integral, since its right side is (r^N-1)/(r-1). On the sheet L=0 at r=1, A extends analytically with A(1)=1 and is nonzero nearby. The two interval endpoints remain present; (7) does not replace their difference by one exponential. On a different logarithmic sheet at r=1 the individual factors in (7) have a compensating pole and zero. The combined function is still the polynomial K_N, but the factors must not be continued separately through that point. On any compact logarithmic chart avoiding those points, the interval integrand is bounded and ordinary Fubini applies. A full angular circuit is treated as a lifted cut chart with its matched ends. Substituting (7) into (4) gives the exact boundary kernels Cup_x=N^2 x^(-d) z_2^d A(r_cup) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r_cup)ds, Cap_x=z_2^(-d) A(r_cap) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r_cap)ds, Mark_x=x^d/N z_2^(-d) A(t) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log t)ds, r_cup=x z_1/z_2, r_cap=Q^(-1)t, t=z_2/(x z_1). (8) In particular the original marked normalization is x^d/N after introducing its one interval, not 1. These formulas can be inserted in the original whole physical word. They are exact scalar source identities, including with its continuous Gaussian variables. Concretely, if W_beta is the original physical word on 2k heads, its original selected scalar is the pairing of W_beta with k copies of (1) as input, k-1 ordinary cap rows, and the one row (2), times the unchanged external scalar line chi_beta,N. Equations (3)--(8) replace only those sources. Each of the 2k turns contributes one interval coordinate, independently of N. The boundary fusion frames can all be removed; the unshortened all-Hardy graph now has 6m+2k complex coordinates for m crossings, together with its m real Gaussian coordinates and the 2k interval coordinates. This count is before any further coefficient or residue simplification. The source numerator is encoded by the retained ends of these intervals, not deleted. For a source-compatible initial cycle one may ensure that every boundary ratio has modulus different from 1. Initial cup radii can be chosen freely. At a terminal touched head the last active factorial is positive: its output radius can be enlarged arbitrarily while keeping its reflected cyclic argument small. If it is the first head of its last crossing, the only subsequent transfer lowers that head and increasing this radius also makes the transfer argument smaller. The second-head terminal factorial has no subsequent transfer. Thus the final radius of each touched head can be enlarged independently; for each terminal pair choose a sufficiently large common scale giving |t|=1/2. An untouched head has its free source radius. This preserves the previous small-atom chamber and gives fixed positive separation of the boundary ratios from 1. The logarithmic radius bounds remain C(1+sum|xi|), so the original Gaussian domination still applies. Initial cup ratios can be perturbed off 1 if an untouched pair fixes their reciprocal ratio. ## 4. The regular complex boundary relation Let h=2*pi*i/N and define a clock by B=exp(p), where p is the logarithmic semiclassical momentum. In (8), stationarity in the interval interior requires Log t=0 at leading order (or Log r_cup=0 for the cup). The resulting paired relation is z_2=x z_1, B_1=exp(2*pi*i*s), B_2=B_1^(-1). (9) The cup and covector orientations give opposite source momenta and the same physical constraint. For the ordinary cap Log r_cap=Log t-h; its extra factor exp(-2*pi*i*s) is nonzero and is kept in the amplitude. At the exact position t=1 its already-integrated kernel has K_N(Q^(-1))=0, and the ordinary cap--cup bubble remains exactly zero. The nonzero density asserted below is the JOINT (head,s) density before integrating s, not a claim that this integrated kernel is nonzero at t=1. The original marked bubble is instead one. Both normalizations are checked by the audit. Integrating out s can produce cancellation and must not be mistaken for a proof of selected noncancellation. The exact degree d=N-1 gives the affine constraint D+1=N, and the leading clock lifts in (9) have p_1+p_2=2*pi*i. It is not a zero-charge constraint produced by forgetting the half-step. At finite N the source monomial has p_1+p_2=h d and hence B_1 B_2=Q^d=Q^(-1); together with the actual dual color xy=Q^(-1) this gives K_tot=1 exactly. The principal constraints (9) are its Q-to-1 limit. No exact finite clock identity B_1 B_2=1 is asserted. For fixed x the set (9), with z_1 nonzero and B_1 nonzero and different from 1, is nonempty, regular, and Lagrangian: dlog B_2=-dlog B_1 and dlog z_2=dlog z_1 cancel the two symplectic terms. The factor A has value 1 on its selected local sheet at the stationary relation. Interval orientation is +1. Thus the local source density there is nonzero, with its original scalar and Gaussian determinant still retained. This statement is about a boundary relation and local density, not a computed geometric-thimble multiplicity. ## 5. These are the actual inverse peripheral meridians Use the commuting principal symbols of the actual balanced generators: K_i=x_i/B_i, f_i=(1-B_i)z_i, e_i=z_i^(-1)(x_i^(-1)-x_i/B_i), x_1=x, x_2=x^(-1). On (9), direct substitution gives K_tot=K_1 K_2=1, f_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2=0, e_tot=e_1 K_2+e_2=0. (10) At completeness x=-1, (9) reads z_2=-z_1. These are exactly the classical equations of the actual dual pair, not equations of a newly assigned boundary invariant. To check the based meridians, retain the actual Gauss convention L_(+,i)=[[K_i,e_i],[0,1]], L_(-,i)=[[1,0],[-K_i f_i,K_i]], G_i=L_(-,i)^(-1)L_(+,i), H_1=G_1, H_2=L_(-,1)^(-1)G_2 L_(-,1). Then the exact classical matrix multiplication is H_2 H_1=(L_(-,2)L_(-,1))^(-1)(L_(+,2)L_(+,1))=I. (11) The last equality follows from (10): both triangular products are I. Raw G_2 G_1 is generally NOT the correct based product. These H_i are the same framed meridians whose exact quantum Hurwitz transport was proved in [the actual shared-flag note](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md). Thus the boundary branch in (9) is compatible with an actual knot representation's oriented cup/meridian relation. Conversely, H_2 H_1=I makes the upper triangular product L_(+,2)L_(+,1) equal the lower triangular product L_(-,2)L_(-,1). Their diagonal and off-diagonal entries force exactly (10). On the regular locus B_1 different from 1, K_tot=1 gives B_2=B_1^(-1), and f_tot=(1-B_1)(z_1-z_2/x)=0 gives z_2=x z_1. Thus (9) is precisely the regular physical cap locus, not only a sufficient special family. At x=-1, this chart covers the Zariski-open part of the nontrivial trace -2 parabolic class with G_(11) different from 0,-1. Explicitly B=-1/G_(11), z=(-G_(11)-1)/G_(12). The determinant and trace equations force G_(12)G_(21)=-(G_(11)+1)^2, so z is nonzero there. For finitely many nontrivial parabolic meridians, a simultaneous generic SL(2,C) conjugation avoids all these finitely many proper closed conditions: each is proper on a parabolic conjugacy class, and SL(2,C) is irreducible. Hence a supplied geometric knot representation with inverse meridians at its paired turns has a simultaneous regular boundary chart. At each turn the second physical factor is recovered by (10)--(11), giving B_2=B_1^(-1), z_2=-z_1. In a list of adjacent paired turns the preceding paired triangular products are I by (10), so the first meridian of the next pair is in the same based frame; a separate independent frame per cap is not being assumed. This is a classical simultaneous framing statement. It does not supply a quantum cycle map implementing that conjugation. This does not assert that every INTERNAL factorization chart of the word is regular in that frame. Further five-term/relative-chart transport may still be needed there. For example, substituting the regular physical cap into the inverse fusion chart gives K=V, A=UK=1 and J=V/K=1. This intrinsic terminal auxiliary degeneration is why adjacent boundary factors were peeled by coefficients rather than declared regular independent saddles. There is also an exact agreement with the literal five-flag source mark. Put R=x z_1/z_2 and X=x z_2/z_1, as in the [marked full-Phi flag calculation](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md). At the complete root x^2=Q^(-1), so X=Q^(-1)/R. The source branch R=1 therefore has precisely the mark X=Q^(-1). In the original finite typed source, the independently proved equality is X cup=Q^(-1)cup. This marking match does not impose X^N=1 on the unwrapped scalar coordinate; the latter remains a variable until an actual source/cycle map supplies that specialization. ## 6. Complex cap clocks have an exact endpoint-fixed source deformation Initially s is the real interval [0,1]. Its interior clocks lie on the unit circle. A generic geometric B is any nonzero complex value; its logarithm gives a complex s modulo integers. No claim is needed that a single frame puts every B on the unit circle. There is instead an exact source-preserving deformation. For fixed Log r, the function exp(Ns Log r) is ENTIRE in s. Consequently, for any compact piecewise smooth path gamma from 0 to 1, integral_gamma exp(Ns Log r) ds =integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r) ds. (12) This follows from its entire primitive, also at Log r=0. Given a regular geometric clock B, choose any s_g=Log B/(2*pi*i) and an endpoint-fixed path through s_g. Equation (12) proves exact equality of the original source pointwise in every other variable. It holds for all caps simultaneously by taking the product paths. The endpoints are unchanged; there are no residues or omitted source corrections in this s-only deformation. One may prescribe a nonzero local tangent at s_g as well. If useful, a single generic classical frame can also avoid the positive real ray for all the finitely many B. Each B is a nonconstant holomorphic function of that frame; its positive-ray inverse image has empty interior by the open mapping theorem. On this additional dense open real-analytic choice, use 0<Arg B<2*pi, giving 0<Re s_g<1. This is not required for (12), but places the desired complex point directly above the interior of the initial interval strip. On a fixed compact path family, |s| is bounded. The additional absolute factor is at most exp(CN|Log r|); the initial radius estimates make this at most exp(C'N(1+sum|xi|)). Thus the original Gaussian majorant still justifies the joint path deformation and Fubini. The marked logarithmic charts in r, including their matched angular ends, remain as in Section 3; entireness in s is not a license to discard those data. Therefore the theorem removes the spurious separate-terminal-monomial critical equations and supplies a regular actual meridian boundary Lagrangian with nonzero density. The boundary interval paths can be deformed through its desired complex clocks exactly. This does not yet prove that the bulk head-variable cycle reaches the same geometric branch with nonzero whole-cycle intersection, or that its endpoint/alias contributions have smaller exponential rate. ## 7. A regular interval endpoint cannot carry a noncentral knot representation At either retained interval endpoint s=0 or 1, the principal source clocks are B_1=B_2=1. Stationarity in s is not imposed at an endpoint, so this does NOT require z_2=x z_1. Nevertheless, at x=-1 the actual classical generators have e_i=f_i=0, K_i=-1 for every finite nonzero z_i. Hence each physical G_i=-I, and the framed H_i is also -I. Suppose a complete stationary solution is in regular charts where the actual Hurwitz laws and paired boundary equations define a representation of a ONE-component knot group. All its oriented meridians are conjugate, up to inversion. If one is -I, every meridian is -I; since meridians generate the knot group, the induced PSL(2,C) representation is trivial. Thus no noncentral geometric representation occurs at a regular source interval endpoint. In particular, choose a regular geometric critical point and small coordinate neighborhoods of its finitely many interval coordinates s_g. Each s_g is different from 0 and 1, since its meridian is not central. The neighborhoods can be chosen with positive separation from both endpoints. Every endpoint stratum has empty intersection with this neighborhood of the geometric critical branch. Thus the localized geometric stationary germ, including its Gaussian block, has no contribution from a cap interval endpoint. This removes an endpoint cancellation of THAT local block; it does not compute the original whole-cycle coefficient of that block. This is a source-support exclusion on the regular representation locus. It is not an estimate for endpoint periods on singular norm divisors, escaping flags, or extra integer phase aliases. Those are precisely the cases where a regular representation argument alone supplies no bound. ## 8. Uniform regular-geometric exclusion of physical cutoff walls The same argument applies to fixed signed endpoint-clock projectors in the actual five-term/flag moves, including the explicit E_0(Z) in [the marked full-Phi flag calculation](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md). The clock here must be a PHYSICAL actual head clock, or an explicitly tracked exact Hurwitz conjugate of one; arbitrary fusion-relative clocks are not covered. For Z^N=1 define its original spectral projector E_j(Z)=N^(-1)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Q^(-jr)Z^r. Exactly, (Z-Q^j)E_j=0. Let j range over a fixed finite set of signed integers as N grows, so the top index d is j=-1. Their principal characteristic wall is B=1. At complete color the corresponding actual physical meridian is G=-I, as proved above. A regular actual Hurwitz solution for a one-component knot on ANY such wall therefore has trivial induced PSL(2,C) representation. This gives a uniform LOCAL statement near a compact regular geometric critical branch. There are only finitely many tracked clocks, and their B values differ from 1. Choose delta>0 such that |B-1|>=delta throughout a sufficiently small compact neighborhood. For all large N, |B-Q^j|>=delta/2 for every one of the finitely many signed j. More explicitly, suppose a wall component admits a regular formal WKB expansion exp(S/h)(a_0+h a_1+...), h=2*pi*i/N. A physical clock acts with leading multiplier B=exp(partial_(log z) S). Its annihilating relation (Z-exp(jh))f=0 first gives (B-1)a_0=0. Since B-1 is invertible on this neighborhood, a_0=0. At each subsequent order the lower coefficients already vanish, leaving (B-1)a_r=0; hence EVERY a_r=0. Exact Hurwitz conjugation transports both the annihilating equation and this regular symbol argument. A bounded fixed number of clock shifts only changes the finite signed set of j. Thus physical endpoint-projector corrections have zero regular formal geometric block in these charts. They cannot cancel a nonzero localized geometric Gaussian block there. This is neither an analytic bound on the full root-level correction nor a proof that such a Gaussian block is selected by the original whole cycle. Two limitations are essential. First, a bulk index j_N/N tending to a nonzero angle has principal B=exp(2*pi*i*lim j_N/N), not 1, and is not excluded. Second, relative fusion clocks A=J=1 can occur on a REGULAR physical cap, as the explicit inverse-fusion calculation in Section 5 shows. A projector in such a relative clock must not be called a physical meridian cutoff without its actual clock map. No finite Ore localization is being performed. Inverting all the shifted factors 1-Q^r Z at fixed N would invert their product 1-Z^N=0 and destroy the whole finite module. Formal regular-geometric exclusion at bounded signed shifts does not authorize this globally invalid operation, or deleting any original finite source/projector. ## 9. Finite physical-projector stationary strata have action zero There is also a critical-VALUE statement, including the missing normal equation of an endpoint projector. It applies to a network of actual canonical crossing relations, the original inverse-meridian turns, and finitely many explicitly tracked PHYSICAL signed-endpoint projectors. Require finite nonzero physical position coordinates. At every crossing the shape tuple must be regular, or a genuine joint limit of its regular actual rational graph; an arbitrary cleared auxiliary chart is not sufficient. Stationarity is imposed in all remaining phase directions. The following argument does not assume stationarity in a projector's fixed clock normal. First, a general finite unit-wall calculation extends the action identity. Write the full leading phase, with all original logarithmic marks retained, in the form W(Z)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(exp(a_j.Z+i phi_j)) +Z^t C Z/2+i kappa.Z+c, where C is real symmetric, a_j,phi_j,kappa are real and Im c=0. Restrict it to a stratum of linear logarithmic constraints A Z=i theta_0, A and theta_0 real. (15) Thus A Re Z=0. Dilog terms identically equal to Li_2(1) on the stratum are real constants, with their consistent integer marks, and are omitted from its derivative. If this restricted finite phase is stationary, the gradient of its remaining expression is conormal to (15). Its contraction with Re Z consequently vanishes. The off-critical defect identity from [the actual regulator calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) therefore gives EXACTLY Im W=sum_j epsilon_j D(exp(a_j.Z+i phi_j)). (16) This also covers dependent linear unit-wall constraints, after using a basis of their conormal space. It avoids assigning a finite value to a singular normal derivative: remove the constant Li_2(1) terms before differentiating on the stratum. Equivalently their possible normal limits are bounded by rho log|rho|, which tends to zero. All Gaussian/cap variables and pure-imaginary integer logarithmic terms remain in this calculation. An unrelated constrained maximum of the real part of W does not satisfy this stationarity hypothesis. Next the original physical projector kernel is, in the actual position frames, (F_out E_j F_in^(-1))(zout,zin) =N^(-1)(zout/zin)^j. (17) For a bounded signed index choose its representative j_N in [0,d]. Its leading clock lift h j_N, h=2pi*i/N, is either 0 or 2pi*i; the latter integer logarithmic phase in (17) is retained. In either case its characteristic correspondence is B_in=B_out=1, positions zin,zout arbitrary. (18) Thus a projector can allow a position/flag jump. It does NOT permit a physical MERIDIAN jump: at B=1 the original finite-chart formulas give K=-1,e=f=0 and G=-I, independently of that position. Based conjugation preserves -I. All the other crossing, wire and turn relations therefore glue physical meridian matrices through this projector just as through an ordinary wire. They define a representation of the SAME one-component knot group, even though the auxiliary position need not be periodic at that wire. One meridian is -I by (18); every knot meridian is conjugate to it, up to inversion. Hence ALL meridians are -I. In these finite charts every physical clock equals one. The original direct five-symbol crossing regulator is consequently zero at EACH crossing: its arguments are A=B=C_plus=C_minus=1. The nine-symbol value has the same limit whenever the specified joint actual graph limit exists. Cups, caps, Gaussians and the retained projector marks add no Bloch terms. Equation (16) proves Im W=0 (19) for every such stationary physical-projector stratum. This extends the local geometric exclusion of Section 8 to a value bound for finite physical-wall stationary blocks, despite their omitted clock-normal equations. It is not an analytic bound on the sum or mass of those blocks. Auxiliary fusion clocks, escaping positions, arbitrary cleared-graph branches and bulk indices j_N/N not tending to 0 or 1 remain excluded. Nor does (19) apply to an unidentified TRANSFER-index endpoint: its zero-transfer Cartan-flip branch need not force any physical meridian to be central. Those boundaries require their own exact source grouping.

title: The full numerator after localization: exact cross cofactors and the packet interface

text: # The full numerator after localization: exact cross cofactors and the packet interface The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . Sections 1--3 are finite identities of the original polynomial source. Sections 4--6 distinguish a concrete remaining asymptotic theorem from those identities. No frozen file is modified and no filling-cycle or relative packet theorem is asserted. The source normalization is that of actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md; the full resolvent numerator, not a complete-image interpolation, is used throughout. ## 1. Actual polynomial block and cleared lower cofactors Put d=N-1, m=floor(N/2), theta=pi/N, sigma=-2-u, and P_N(u)=(-1)^d H_(V_N(-2-u)), a_j=2+2cos((2j+1)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta), A=x+y, P=xy. The original triangular matrix 2+Omega+u has diagonal a_j+u and negative lowering entries -s_j^2 A and -s_j s_(j-1)P. All physical endpoint zeros remain in these entries. A numerator path j to i has middle monomial b^i c^(d-j), its positive step product, and the product of a_r+u over exactly its UNUSED rows. This is a polynomial identity also at every zero of a_r+u. Take the lower block with rows 0,...,m-1. Initially off its poles let A_-(u)=product_(r=0)^(m-1)(a_r+u), K_-=(2+Omega+u)_-^(-1), D(b)=A_- sum_(i=0)^(m-1) b^i (K_-)_(i,m-1), E(b)=A_- sum_(i=0)^(m-2) b^i (K_-)_(i,m-2). (1) These are CLEARED cofactors, hence polynomials, with degrees m-1 and m-2 in (x,b,y). Set E=0 for m=1. Define polynomials R_j(b) without any denominators by R_0=1, absent negative indices zero, and R_j(b)=b^j product_(r<j)(a_r+u) +s_j^2 A R_(j-1)(b) +s_j s_(j-1)(a_(j-1)+u)P R_(j-2)(b). (2) The source path recursion, splitting at its first step from j, gives D(b)=R_(m-1)(b), E(b)=(a_(m-1)+u)R_(m-2)(b). (3) For odd N also use R_m, with the same original s_m and a_(m-1). Neither (2) nor (3) is a lower-level quantum source; the level stays N. There is also an exact determinant realization. In the block on rows 0,...,j, replace the LAST row of 2+Omega+u by (1,b,...,b^j). Its determinant is R_j(b), by the row-replacement formula det(A)(w A^-1)_j. This remains polynomial at singular A and does not assert that the row-replaced matrix is positive or Hermitian. ## 2. Exact central-cross factorization at both parities For EVEN N=2m the CROSS support is i<=m-1,j>=m. Its polynomial is P_cross(u)=s_m^2 A D(b)D(c) +s_m s_(m-1)P [D(b)E(c)+E(b)D(c)]. (4) Proof: every decreasing path crosses the central cut exactly once, by m->m-1, m+1->m-1, or m->m-2. These are precisely the three terms. Row reflection r->d-r identifies the upper and lower diagonal products and exchanges the corresponding one- and two-step weights. The full diagonal product is A_-^2, which cancels the two cleared cofactor denominators. This proves (4) off a finite set; polynomial continuation proves it everywhere, including u=-a_(m-1). For ODD N=2m+1 the CROSS support is i<=m,j>=m. Put G(b)=A_- b^m+s_m^2 A D(b)+s_m s_(m-1)P E(b)=R_m(b). Then exactly P_cross(u)=G(b)G(c)+u s_m s_(m+1)P D(b)D(c). (5) Visited-central paths split at row m, giving the first product. A cross path skipping m has the unique two-step jump m+1->m-1; its UNUSED central row supplies u, giving the second term. Here s_(m+1) =s_m. The original full diagonal product is u A_-^2, but (5) has no division by u and no discarded derivative term. In particular its u derivative retains both differentiated visited-central paths and the central-skipping term. Thus (4)--(5) include the actual semisimple information; they are not identities only at the complete nodes. Products of (4) or (5), followed by the ONE original shared target coefficient and protected targets zero, give the exact all-CROSS shared numerator. Distinct ports keep their distinct spectral u_e. There is no new N factor, local mark, or independent face summation. ## 3. Exact complete-node anchor and what it does not imply At a paired physical node c_a, the full-Hermite identity gives L_(N,a)=(-1)^d (2/N)V_N(c_a). At the odd simple endpoint c_*=-2 it instead gives L_(N,*)=V_N(-2)/N. The original homogeneous complete-circle theorem writes H_(L_(N,a))=N k_a B_(N,a), B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), k_a=2 paired, k_*=1 simple. Consequently, UNIFORMLY over both multiplicity types, (-1)^d H_(V_N(c_a))=N^2 B_(N,a). (6) The right side has b,c degrees at most a<=floor(d/2), hence lies entirely in the CROSS support. Thus (4)--(5) agree with the FULL numerator at EVERY folded spectral node. On the fold cover sigma(delta)=-2cos(2pi delta), u(delta)=-4sin^2(pi delta), delta_a=(d-2a)/(2N), (7) equation (6) supplies the exact original anchor for comparison with actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md. It does NOT justify differentiating that interpolation to get V'. There are fewer distinct spectral nodes than the degree of V, and the semisimple interpolation ambiguity is real. Nor does (4) imply that its three summands have a common nonvanishing complex phase. The new identity makes the remaining object explicit; it does not settle its Stokes structure or a relative amplitude. ## 4. A concrete continuum candidate, not a claimed packet For a fixed starting row i, its cleared interval continuant obeys K_(i,j)=s_j^2 A K_(i,j-1) +s_j s_(j-1)(a_(j-1)+u)P K_(i,j-2). With s(t)=2sin(pi t), a(t)=4cos^2(pi t), its positive constant-block root at real u>=0 is Lambda(t;u)=[s(t)^2 A +sqrt(s(t)^4 A^2+4s(t)^2(a(t)+u)P)]/2. (8) At the upper fold t=1/2 its discriminant is nonzero whenever A>0. Thus clearing the half cofactor removes the artificial a_j^-1 singularity there. It does not remove the lower endpoint t=0. The corresponding candidate action for D(b), normalized at u=0, is F_u(x,b,y)=max_(0<=mu<=1/2) [mu log b+int_0^mu log(a(t)+u)dt +int_mu^(1/2)log Lambda(t;u)dt]. (9) For b>0, its interior saddle solves b(a(mu)+u)=Lambda(mu;u), hence sin^2(pi mu)=b^2(1+u/4)/[(b+x)(b+y)]. (10) Under (7), this is the already recorded deformed middle-angle equation. At u=0, the proved half-block weighted theorem normalizes (9) to the actual triangle F(x,b,y), with no arbitrary constant. For b=0 the initial row is forced to i=0. If also xy=0 the recurrence is an exact monomer product; otherwise the lower-endpoint transfer eigenvalues approach equal modulus and must be treated explicitly. Equations (8)--(10) are an explicit candidate and algebraic saddle calculation. This handoff does NOT claim uniform complex asymptotics or a nonzero relative prefactor from this calculation. In particular, the proved positive logarithmic rate is weaker than such a packet. ## 5. The precise relative theorem needed by the original period The spectral-polydisk-complement theorem gives, for the original shared numerator S_N and its exact all-CROSS part C_N, S_N-C_N=O(exp[N(Phi-gamma/2)]) (11) on a sufficiently small FIXED spectral polydisk, at both parities. It also gives exact spectral-jet bounds on radius N^-2. These are absolute estimates, not a nonzero approximation for C_N. A useful next theorem must give C_N on the ACTUAL delta cover near the saddles used by the original spectral cycle, after the original shared face coefficient extraction. It may be a single branch only where that is proved, or a finite branch sum with its actual sector coefficients. Schematically one needs C_N(delta)=sum_tau N^(beta_tau) A_(tau,N)(delta) exp[N S_(tau,N)(delta)] + controlled relative/absolute remainder, (12) uniformly on specified complex sectors or saddle neighborhoods, with nonzero amplitudes for the selected contributions and enough holomorphic margins to differentiate. Finite-N actions must retain the actual parity anchor and all original scalar characters. The theorem must include the original face torus: a local pointwise cofactor formula alone does not license Gaussian reduction of the shared coefficient. The old complete-source face Hessian and torus gap provide a plausible starting point at delta=0, but their transfer to (4)--(5) still requires relative control, including every protected zero pattern. A fixed complex disk free of zeros or Stokes curves is NOT imposed here; a sectorial finite-branch theorem sufficient on the contributing saddle neighborhoods would suffice. Once such a packet has real rate at least Phi-gamma/4 on those neighborhoods, (11) is exponentially smaller there. Uniform holomorphic errors then legitimately control the V' semisimple term by Cauchy. This would use an estimate of the ACTUAL cofactors, not differentiation of complete node samples. ## 6. Why shrinking endpoint disks do not by themselves suffice For a fixed integer crossing power n the exact full-Hermite Gaussian is R^n=q^(n d^2/4) exp[n N K(Omega)/(4pi i)], K(sigma(delta))=-(2pi delta)^2. The retained scalar q^(n d^2/4) remains outside the local phase. In the exact midpoint Fourier formula of actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md, put phi=pi-2pi delta. The charge ell contributes, apart from its recorded constant sign, exp[N(pi i n delta^2+2pi i ell delta)]. (13) More explicitly, let I_(D,n) denote the original marked contraction with the actual coupon R^(n_e) at each port. Any separately recorded exterior framing scalar stays outside this formula. The existing single-coupon total-derivative identity, followed by the exact shared coefficient extraction, gives the following WHOLE-source formula: I_(D,n)=q^[(d^2/4)sum_e n_e] (-i)^R sum_(ell in (Z\{0})^R) [product_e ell_e] (-1)^[(N+1)sum_e ell_e] int_[-1/2,1/2]^R [product_e sin(2pi delta_e)] S_N(-2cos(2pi delta_1),...,-2cos(2pi delta_R)) exp{N sum_e[pi i n_e delta_e^2 +2pi i ell_e delta_e]} ddelta. (13a) Indeed the one-coupon prefactor -iN^2/2 times the Fourier measure 1/(2pi) times B_f=2sin(phi)fV/N^2 is -i/(2pi). Substitution phi=pi-2pi delta supplies 2pi, while the midpoint sign (-1)^ell and exp(-pi i N ell) combine to the displayed sign. Thus all N^2 factors cancel in the period prefactor, not in S_N itself. For each fixed N the sum is absolutely convergent by the proved C^1 periodic endpoint regularity and Fourier O(|j|^-3) bound. Its constants need not be uniform in N. Because S_N and the Gaussian are even in EACH delta_e, reversing a single ell_e reverses its integral and also the prefactor ell_e. Thus the terms are equal under independent charge sign reversal; one may equivalently sum over positive ell_e with prefactor (-2i)^R. This is an exact parity identity, not proof that only ell_e=1 survives. Endpoint currents remain encoded by the actual finite interval and its periodic regularity; integration by parts cannot silently erase them. Formula (13a) uses the original FULL V at every port. The ell=0 integral of the total derivative is EXACTLY zero. For a bounded surviving nonzero charge, the local critical equation is partial_delta S(delta)+2pi i n delta+2pi i ell=0. (14) Its candidate near-parabolic solution is delta=O(1/n), with the diagram's coupled derivatives included. For independently large FIXED twists, this displacement is fixed as N grows. The required packet is therefore near a nonzero fixed delta*, not just on the N^-2 spectral disk (delta=O(1/N)) controlled by endpoint jets. Even a proved (12) would leave the source-preserving cycle comparison, the nonzero charges and their possible cancellations, and the global complement to check. The +2 Gaussian closing cap is already proved in actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md and is not a new missing endpoint estimate. Its bulk sign warning still applies: a whole spectral ellipse has a Gaussian-growing side. Largeness of n does not by itself justify dropping it. The existing strict physical prefix and cross-central Green actions are selected integrand rates; they neither identify (4)--(5) on complex face sectors nor prove (12). Likewise actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md has a different strict physical/complex-magnetic chart and an integer channel, so an explicit adapter would be needed before importing its relative bound. ## 7. A proved central-strip relative bound and the endpoint amplitude anchor This section is stronger than a bare endpoint jet majorant but still has a SHRINKING spectral domain. It does not prove (12) at fixed delta*. Fix 0<eta<1/4 and N>=1/eta. Restrict a local numerator to endpoints i<=N(1/2-eta), j>=N(1/2+eta), and denote it P_eta(u). A fixed integer rounding of these inequalities does not matter. The following is COEFFICIENTWISE in all four faces: [u^k]P_eta(u) <= binom(N,k) C_eta^k P_eta(0), (15) C_eta=max{1/[4sin^2(pi eta/2)], 1/[4cos(pi eta)cos(2pi eta)]}. Here and below a zero coefficient on the right also forces zero on the left. In particular this is not an estimate only after choosing positive face radii. Proof. Expand each one-step factor x+y into its two labeled terms. A coefficient of u^k consists of an actual path and a k-element set S of unused rows, at which the factor a_r+u contributes u rather than a_r. For a selected row outside the open central strip N(1/2-eta)<r<N(1/2+eta), leave the path unchanged and restore a_r. Its weight ratio is 1/a_r<=1/[4sin^2(pi eta/2)]. A selected central row lies strictly between both endpoints. If unused it MUST be skipped by the step r+1->r-1. Replace that dimer by r+1->r->r-1, assigning x to the first step and y to the second. This preserves the exact outer exponents and both middle exponents. The old dimer with its selected unused factor removed has weight s_(r+1)s_r xy; the repaired two steps have weight s_(r+1)^2s_r^2 xy. Their ratio is 1/[s_r s_(r+1)], bounded by the second quantity in C_eta. Selected skipped rows cannot be adjacent, so all these repairs are compatible. Given S and the repaired labeled path, collapsing exactly those two-step runs recovers the original path. Thus the map is injective for each S, with weight ratio at most C_eta^k. There are at most binom(N,k) choices of S. At odd N a surviving term from a path skipping m necessarily selects m in S: otherwise its unselected a_m factor is zero. Repair then visits m, exactly as required for P_eta(0). All other repaired paths also have nonzero zero-spectral weights. This proves (15) at BOTH parities without dividing by the zero row. Summing (15), for complex u with |u|<=r, |P_eta(u)-P_eta(0)|_coef <=[(1+C_eta r)^N-1] P_eta(0). (16) Now choose eta from the unique geometric maximizer, so every actual geometric middle load is <=1/2-4eta. Let Z_N(u)=(-1)^(dR) S_N(-2-u_1,...,-2-u_R) be the actual shared numerator, and Z_eta its restriction to these central-strip endpoints at every port. The complement lies in a closed incidence set separated from q_geom: for all sufficiently large N some middle load is >=1/2-2eta. The same uniform full-h entropy and support-preserving spectral comparison used for the one-sided gap therefore give a number gamma_eta>0 and one fixed spectral polydisk such that |Z_N(u)-Z_eta(u)|<=exp[N(Phi-gamma_eta)]. (17) Shrinking the fixed polydisk absorbs its spectral majorant cost. At u=0, Z_N(0)>0 and log Z_N(0)/N -> Phi: for even N this is the proved full endpoint theorem; for odd N it is the exact simple-fold complete coefficient. Positivity gives Z_eta(0)<=Z_N(0). Applying (16) before the original shared coefficient extraction consequently proves, uniformly in this polydisk, |Z_N(u)/Z_N(0)-1| <= product_e(1+C_eta |u_e|)^N-1+O(e^(-cN)). (18) Choose fixed c0>0 so exp(R C_eta c0)-1<1/2. The full numerator is then nonzero on |u_e|<=c0/N for all sufficiently large N, and is uniformly 1+O(N max|u_e|)+O(e^(-cN)) relative to its actual endpoint value when max|u_e|=o(1/N). Cauchy on c0/N also gives, for every multiindex alpha and sufficiently large N, |partial_sigma^alpha S_N(-2,...,-2)| <=2 alpha! (N/c0)^|alpha| |S_N(-2,...,-2)|. (19) These are spectral derivatives only. The constant c0 is attached to the fixed original diagram; no growing-width uniformity is claimed. There is a useful EXACT-SOURCE amplitude anchor. For even N the maximal complete node has delta_min=1/(2N) and u_min=-4sin^2(pi/(2N))=O(N^-2). Apply (18) at that node in every port and use the exact node identity (6). If B_top=[original ordinary targets] product_e B_(N,M), with the original two protected targets zero, then (-1)^(dR) S_N(-2,...,-2) =N^(2R) B_top [1+O(N^-1)] (N even), (20) S_N(-2,...,-2)=N^(2R) B_top (N odd). (21) The odd formula is the exact simple-node identity, not an asymptotic consequence of (18). Formula (20) controls the actual even semisimple endpoint amplitude against the known complete-fold anchor. It still does not extend a relative packet to the fixed O(1/n) delta saddle: the zero-free disk just proved has delta size O(N^-1/2). ## 8. Exact cofactor interpolation and a global all-CROSS spectral bound Write J=floor((N-1)/2) at even levels and J=m at odd levels. Thus J=m-1 for N=2m and J=m for N=2m+1. Every R_j, 0<=j<=J, has spectral degree at most j. The J+1 distinct physical nodes are u_a=-a_a=-2-2cos((2a+1)pi/N), 0<=a<=J. The following coefficientwise fact supplies the needed nodal control: 0<=R_j(b;u_a)<=R_j(b;0), for all j,a<=J. (22) If j<=a, every diagonal a_r-a_a actually used by (2) is nonnegative and no larger than a_r; (22) follows directly by induction. If j>a, the inhomogeneous term of (2) vanishes after row a, giving exactly R_j(u_a)=K_(a,j)(u_a) R_a(u_a). (23) Normalize q_r=K_(a,a+r)/product_(v=a+1)^(a+r)s_v^2. The exact trigonometric identity a_(j-1)-a_a=-s_(j+a)s_(j-a-1), s_j s_(j-1)-s_(j+a)s_(j-a-1)=s_a s_(a+1) gives q_0=1,q_1=x+y and q_r=(x+y)q_(r-1)-gamma_r xy q_(r-2), gamma_r=1-s_a s_(a+1)/[s_j s_(j-1)] in [0,1], j=a+r<=J. (24) In particular q_r>=0 COEFFICIENTWISE: induct on q_r-xq_(r-1) =y[q_(r-1)-xq_(r-2)]+(1-gamma_r)xyq_(r-2)>=0. Also q_r<=(x+y)^r, by (24) and induction. At u=0 the same interval continuant contains its all-monomer term plus only nonnegative terms. Hence K_(a,j)(u_a)<=K_(a,j)(0). Together with the j=a case of (22), the product in (23) is bounded by K_(a,j)(0)R_a(0), a literal subset of the zero-spectral paths contributing R_j(0) (those whose start is at most a and which visit a). This proves (22). The nodal K factors were not assumed positive without proof. Even N has the m shifted Chebyshev-root nodes. Odd N has m+1 reflected Chebyshev-Radau nodes, including u=0. Since deg_u R_j<=J, ordinary Lagrange interpolation is EXACT. Its Lebesgue function on [-4,0] is bounded by C log(N+1). One elementary proof uses the full N-point odd-angle cosine grid, pairing reflected nodes. For even N the cosine degree is at most m-1 and the Dirichlet kernel has degree m-1; for odd N it has degree m. Discrete cosine inversion is exact on these spaces. The sum of absolute normalized kernel values is O(log N), by |D_k(t)|<=min(2k+1,1/|sin(t/2)|) and the harmonic sum over equally spaced points. Pairing cannot increase that bound. No interpolation is being applied directly to full V. Apply interpolation separately to each FACE coefficient in (22): |R_j(u)|_coef<=C log(N+1) R_j(0), -4<=u<=0. (25) On the delta cover, the ordinary polynomial Bernstein-Walsh bound in z=-1-u/2=-cos(2pi delta) then gives |R_j(u(delta))|_coef <=C log(N+1) exp[2pi j |Im delta|] R_j(0). (26) For completeness, this bound follows by writing z=(w+w^-1)/2: the exterior maximum principle for w^(-j)p((w+w^-1)/2) bounds it by sup_[-1,1]|p|, with |w|=exp(2pi|Im delta|). Apply this scalar argument to each coefficient polynomial of actual degree at most j. Return to the exact central formulas (4)--(5). On any fixed strip |Im delta|<=T, the factors |u| and |a_(m-1)+u| are bounded by a constant depending only on T. The other cofactor products compare COEFFICIENTWISE to the zero-spectral central kernel. Indeed at even N, D_b(0)>=s_(m-1)^2 (x+y) R_(m-2)(b;0), (x+y)^2>=2xy, so either xy D_b(0)R_(m-2)(c;0) term is bounded by a constant times (x+y)D_b(0)D_c(0). The constants are uniform for N>=4. The latter is itself a summand of P_cross(0). At odd N, G_b(0)>=s_m^2(x+y)D_b(0), G_b(0)G_c(0)>=2s_m^4 xy D_b(0)D_c(0). Thus (26) yields the all-level coefficientwise bound |P_cross(u(delta))|_coef <=C_T log^2(N+1) exp[2pi d |Im delta|] P_cross(0). (27) It respects each actual original face exponent, so taking products and the ONE original marked shared coefficient gives |S_(N,cross)(sigma(delta))| <=[C_T log^2(N+1)]^R exp[2pi d sum_e |Im delta_e|] Z_(N,cross)(0). (28) In particular the all-CROSS numerator has global REAL-spectral upper rate Phi throughout the complete real interval [-2,2]. This is stronger than a small endpoint-disk bound, but is not an angular gap on the face torus and not yet a FULL-numerator bound on that interval. It retains the actual shared targets and no independent choice of face radii. For clarity, the remaining one-sided issue has an exact formulation. At even N, P_left(u) is A_-(u) times the lower-block adjugate generating polynomial (with its actual c^m factor), and A_-(u)=2(-1)^m T_m((-2-u)/2) is bounded by 2 on the real interval. The adjugate entries have degree at most m-1 and thus the same exact interpolation. At a node a an entry i,j is zero unless i<=a<=j; its surviving expression has factors K_(i,a)K_(a,j), nonnegative, but also product_(r>j)(a_r-a_a), with sign (-1)^(m-1-j). Separate absolute prefix/suffix ratios against u=0 can be exponentially large. A uniform comparison of their COMBINED nodal coefficients has not been proved here. The global bound (28) must not be extended to the full one-sided remainder by silently dropping these factors. In fact such a POLYNOMIAL COEFFICIENTWISE extension to the full real interval is false. Take N=4k, m=N/2=2k, and j=k-1. The LEFT monomial x^j c^(d-j), with b=y=0, has exactly one path, using j one-steps. Its full-numerator coefficient is A_-(u) [product_(r=1)^j s_r^2] product_(r=j+1)^(m-1)(a_r+u). (29) At u=-4, equivalently sigma=+2, |A_-(-4)|=A_-(0)=2. Its absolute ratio to the positive endpoint coefficient at u=0 is therefore product_(r=k)^(2k-1) tan^2((r+1/2)pi/N). (30) The logarithmic rate of (30) is 2 integral_(1/4)^(1/2) log tan(pi t)dt =2 Catalan/pi>0. (31) The endpoint logarithm is integrable; deleting a fixed small terminal interval and using the elementary sine-product bound there proves the midpoint Riemann limit, with no numerical extrapolation. Thus the combined one-sided adjugate coefficients really can exceed their u=0 values exponentially, even after restoring A_-(u). The issue is not merely a weakness of separate prefix/suffix estimates. It also occurs at a FIXED STRICT INTERIOR spectral point, not just at the already controlled closing cap. Take sigma=sqrt(3), u=-2-sqrt(3), and N divisible by24. Then m=N/2 is divisible by12, so A_-(u)=2T_m(cos(pi/6))=2. The same coefficient ratio is product_(r=N/4)^(N/2-1) [sqrt(3)-c_r]/[2+c_r] >=(sqrt(3)/2)^(N/12) (1+sqrt(3))^(N/6) =(3+2sqrt(3))^(N/12). (32) Indeed c_r<=0 throughout the product and c_r<=-1 on its last N/6 indices. This exact positive exponential lower bound requires no asymptotic extrapolation or endpoint limit. This is a LOCAL COEFFICIENT obstruction. It is not a counterexample to a shared-source spectral bound or to the original +2 physical resolvent cap. The marked coefficient may enforce additional global cancellations and incidence constraints. It shows precisely why the all-CROSS coefficientwise theorem cannot be substituted for a full real-spectral numerator theorem on the original period. ## Finite validation ../experiments/audit_actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.py compares the factorization with the original full-numerator unused-row path polynomial, already independently validated against physical coproduct matrices in the public Gaussian-resolvent audit. At N=3,...,12 it checks 85 spectral values, 10395 polynomial coefficients, all 10 last-lower- diagonal zero cases, and 40 full complete-node/CROSS identities. Results: ../experiments/actual_cross_cofactor_factorization_results.json. The same helper additionally checks 8326 central-strip derivative coefficient inequalities on 8786 original paths at N=8,...,15, 70 digits, using eta=1/8 and the displayed uniform C_eta. This is a finite check of the exact repair statement, not the proof of its all-level bound. The proofs of (17)--(21) also use the separately endpoint volume, uniform coefficient, and unique-max theorems. It additionally checks 7324 nodal lower-cofactor coefficient bounds (22) at N=3,...,18, retaining all starting rows and both parities. The factorization comparisons are exact finite-field tests. No new independent physical matrix audit, fixed-complex relative packet (12), or finite-cycle survival is advertised here. [Focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.py) · [Recorded output](../experiments/actual_cross_cofactor_factorization_results.json). These finite checks supplement the written proof and retain the scope recorded in their output.

title: A global angular gap for the actual cleared cross cofactors
status: Global local-angle bound on a thin spectral strip
text: # A global angular gap for the actual cleared cross cofactors The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . All matrices, paths and spectral nodes are at the original level N. This is a local cofactor estimate on a thin spectral cover strip, not a Gaussian-cycle or whole-source theorem. ## 1. Statement and exact source inputs Put d=N-1, J=floor(d/2), theta=pi/N, a_r=4cos^2((r+1/2)theta), s_r=2sin(r theta), A=x+y, P=xy, p_r=s_r^2 A, q_r(u)=s_r s_(r-1)(a_(r-1)+u)P. For j=J-k, with 0<=k<=k0 fixed, let R_j(b,u) be the actual cleared cofactor with recurrence R_j=b^j product_(r<j)(a_r+u)+p_j R_(j-1)+q_j(u)R_(j-2). (1) This includes D,E's R factor, and odd G. A zero face remains zero. Assume the positive entries of (x,b,y) range in a fixed positive compact, A>0, and at least TWO entries are positive. Let epsilon>0. If the circular phases of the positive face entries have diameter at least epsilon, then there exist gamma>0,C,K and a FIXED strip height tau>0 such that, uniformly for |Im delta|<=tau and all real Re delta, |R_j(x exp(i theta_x),b exp(i theta_b),y exp(i theta_y); -4sin^2(pi delta))| <=C N^K exp(-gamma N) R_j(x,b,y;0). (2) The statement includes b=0 and either single protected outer face. For b=0,xy=0 there is only one positive variable and the cofactor is an exact monomial; there is no relative-angle condition to assert. The case x=y=0 is excluded by the actual marked matching-edge dictionary. The exact node adapter, proved independently from the original matrices, is, for 0<=a<=j, R_j(b,-a_a)=K_(a,j)(-a_a) S_(2a)D_a(x,b,y), (3) R_a(b,-a_a)=S_(2a)D_a(x,b,y). Here K_(a,a)=1, K_(a,a-1)=0, and K follows p_v,q_v above. Also 0<=R_a(b,-a_a)<=R_a(b,0), 0<=K_(a,j)(-a_a)<=K_mono(a,j):=product_(v=a+1)^j p_v. (4) These are COEFFICIENTWISE statements. For completeness the latter normalizes K by product s_v^2, giving Q_r=A Q_(r-1)-gamma_r xy Q_(r-2), gamma_r=1-s_a s_(a+1)/(s_(a+r)s_(a+r-1)) in [0,1]. Induction on Q_r-xQ_(r-1)=y[Q_(r-1)-xQ_(r-2)] +(1-gamma_r)xyQ_(r-2) proves Q_r>=0, then Q_r<=A^r. Thus no absolute value of a sign-changing tail is assumed positive. The nodal positivity proof is in the cross-cofactor handoff §8. ## 2. A strict gap at all far nodes Choose a fixed small delta0>0, for example delta0<1/8. Call a node far if a/N<=1/2-delta0. This definition only separates nodes for this proof. It does not alter the physical folded label or its half-index. We prove, whenever at least two faces are positive, R_j(b,-a_a)<=C exp(-gamma_far N)R_j(b,0) (5) uniformly over ALL these far nodes. This estimate needs no angular separation. Polynomial factors are harmless and can be absorbed by slightly reducing gamma_far. First suppose xy>0; b may be zero. The fixed interval I=[1/2-delta0/2, 1/2-delta0/4] lies AFTER every far row a and BEFORE j for all sufficiently large N. On it every ratio q_v(0)/(p_v p_(v-1)) =(a_(v-1)xy)/(s_v s_(v-1)(x+y)^2) is bounded below by a positive compact-set constant. Choose cN disjoint pairs of adjacent steps in this interval. Starting with the all-monomer path from j to a, either retain each selected pair or replace it by its original dimer. The choices are independent and all paths are physical. Their sum therefore gives K_(a,j)(0)>=exp(c' N)K_mono(a,j). (6) On the other hand, K_(a,j)(0)R_a(b,0) is precisely the subset of paths in R_j(b,0) whose starting row is at most a and which visit a. There is no multiplicity in splitting a path at that row. Combining (4),(6) proves (5). All selected rows stay in a fixed strict bulk interval, so neither a near-zero initial row nor the actual folded endpoint affects the constants. Now suppose xy=0 and b>0. Write A for the sole positive outer face. The recurrence is first order and its actual zero-spectral starting terms are W_i=b^i product_(r<i)a_r product_(v=i+1)^j [s_v^2 A], R_j(b,0)=sum_(i=0)^j W_i. For a far node, all starts i>a vanish exactly, and for i<=a the ratio to W_i is product_(r<i)(1-a_a/a_r). Uniformly for sufficiently large N, a_a>=c_delta0>0 and a_r<=4. Hence starts i>=eta N have ratio at most (1-c_delta0/4)^(eta N). The remaining short starts have an independent exact gap. Choose fixed eta>0 small enough that, on the given positive compact, W_(i+1)/W_i=b a_i/(s_(i+1)^2 A)>=1+c for all 0<=i<=2eta N and all sufficiently large N. Such eta exists from the displayed original sine/cosine entries. Each i<=eta N is then exponentially smaller than W_floor(2eta N), by at least eta N consecutive ratios. Summing at most N terms gives sum_(i<=eta N) W_i<=CN exp(-c'eta N)R_j(b,0). Combining the two ranges proves (5), including x=0 and y=0. The only remaining case b=0,xy=0 is the excluded one-variable angular case. ## 3. The near nodes have the original determinant angular gap For a/N>=1/2-delta0, a>=a0N for a fixed a0>0. Apply the EXACT PSD contraction of actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md §2 to D_a=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+]. Its finite pair-trace lower bounds hold for every a0N<=a<=floor(d/2), not only a deficit o(N): this is the explicit scope and bulk-square proof in actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md §§1--4. When x,b,y are all positive, the b--x and b--y pair traces are at least cN. If the positive-phase diameter is at least epsilon, one of these two phase differences is at least epsilon/2. When one outer face is zero, its single remaining pair has the same bound (220/022). When b=0 and x,y>0, the original 202 variance/pair trace is at least cN. Consequently in every applicable zero pattern, |D_a(x exp(i theta_x),b exp(i theta_b),y exp(i theta_y))| <=exp(-gamma_ang N)D_a(x,b,y). (7) This is a determinant modulus inequality on the ENTIRE phase torus, not a local complex-log estimate. The positive polynomial K in (3) has modulus at most its positive-radius value. Equations (3),(4),(7) therefore prove the same exponential nodal bound relative to R_j(0). For far nodes, (5) and the positive coefficient statement (4) already prove the bound at arbitrary phases. Thus ALL nodes a=0,...,j satisfy |R_j(faces with phases;-a_a)| <=C exp(-gamma0 N)R_j(positive faces;0). (8) ## 4. Exact interpolation, including the omitted last nodes The actual spectral degree of R_j is at most j. The full physical node family a=0,...,J is the even Chebyshev-root or odd Chebyshev-Radau family after the affine change z=-1-u/2. Its exact interpolation Lebesgue norm on [-4,0] is O(log(N+1)); this follows from discrete cosine inversion on the original N-point odd-angle grid and the bound |D_J(t)|<=min(2J+1,1/|sin(t/2)|). This is the same exact interpolation used in the cofactor handoff, not interpolation of full V. If j=J, apply it directly to (8). If j<J, DO NOT use an unavailable D_a adapter at a>j. Instead put p(u)=R_j(faces with phases;u), Q(u)=p(u) product_(a=j+1)^J (u+a_a). The degree of Q is at most J. At the retained nodes its absolute value is bounded by 4^k times the right side of (8); at the omitted nodes it is EXACTLY zero. Full-grid interpolation gives ||Q||_[-4,0]<=C_k log(N+1) exp(-gamma0 N)R_j(0). (9) Division by these k fixed-in-number factors costs only a polynomial in N, even though their roots cluster at the endpoint. Here is an elementary bound with no spacing assumption. A polynomial p of degree j and interval supremum M has derivative supremum at most C(j+1)^3 M: expand in Chebyshev polynomials, whose coefficients have magnitude at most2M, and use ||T_l'||<=l^2. Around a point attaining M, a one-sided interval of length c/(j+1)^3 has |p|>=M/2. Remove small neighborhoods of the k roots occupying less than half that interval. At a remaining point every factor has magnitude at least c_k/(j+1)^3. Hence ||p||_[-4,0]<=C_k(j+1)^(3k)||Q||_[-4,0]. (10) This also holds for complex p, by the same cosine coefficient bound. Thus every required literal terminal cofactor satisfies an exponential angular gap on the WHOLE real spectral interval, with a polynomial prefactor. No last row or parity node has been silently replaced. Finally the elementary polynomial Bernstein bound on [-4,0] gives |p(-4sin^2(pi delta))| <=exp(2pi j |Im delta|)||p||_[-4,0]. (11) Indeed z=-1-u/2=-cos(2pi delta)=(w+w^-1)/2 with |w|=exp(2pi|Im delta|); apply the exterior maximum principle to the polynomial of degree j after this substitution. Since j<=N/2, choosing pi tau<gamma0/2 makes (9)--(11) imply (2), with a possibly reduced gamma. The estimate is uniform for the full real fold interval and its periodic copies, not only near delta=0. ## 5. Scope This proof uses exact original node identities, finite positive paths, actual PSD angular bounds and finite polynomial interpolation. No complex starting-row contour or generic off-node PSD representation is required. Every physical starting row and the protected-middle i=0 contribution remains. The one-variable monomials are explicitly exempt because their sole phase is a common homogeneous phase. The local factors can serve a whole shared-face angular argument only after checking the actual connected phase graph, keeping every other factor under a uniform spectral bound, and retaining the original marked coefficient and finite central prefactors. The local theorem alone is not a full shared coefficient asymptotic or a selected Gaussian period. ## Scope This is a local cofactor input, with no independent whole-source or Gaussian-cycle assertion.
