text: # Actual cleared cross cofactors: interior starting-row packet The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . This concerns the original finite homogeneous cofactor, not an arbitrary interpolation of its complete-channel samples. The middle face b is positive. The separate protected-middle proof treats b=0. Exactly one protected outer face x=0 or y=0 is included below; both outer faces zero are excluded. ## 1. The finite determinant and the exact physical-node adapter Use the original level N, theta=pi/N, h=1/N, and put alpha_j(u)=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta)+u, s_j=2sin(j theta), A=x+y, P=xy, p_j=s_j^2 A, q_j=s_j s_(j-1)alpha_(j-1)(u)P. Let $A_{[0,j]}(u)$ be the original upper two-diagonal matrix with diagonal alpha_r, entries -p_r at (r-1,r), and -s_r s_(r-1)P at (r-2,r). The absent physical entries are zero. The actual cleared cofactor is \[ R_j(b,u)=\det A_{[0,j]}(u)\,(1,b,\ldots,b^j)\, A_{[0,j]}(u)^{-1}e_j. \tag{1} \] Equivalently, replace the LAST ROW of A_[0..j] by (1,b,...,b^j) and take its determinant. Row replacement proves (1) off the poles; the determinant proves its polynomial extension across every alpha_r=0. Thus it is not necessary to assume an invertible physical block. The exact path formula is R_j= sum_(i=0)^j b^i [prod_(r<i)alpha_r] K_(i,j), (2) K_(i,i)=1, K_(i,i-1)=0, K_(i,v)=p_v K_(i,v-1)+q_v K_(i,v-2). Consequently R_0=1 and R_j=b^j prod_(r<j)alpha_r+p_j R_(j-1)+q_j R_(j-2). (3) There is a precise link to the previous positive q-Hahn determinant, but only at its actual spectral node. Write a_r=alpha_r(0), and fix 0<=a<=floor((N-1)/2). At u=-a_a, alpha_a=0, so for j>=a, R_j(b,-a_a)=K_(a,j)(-a_a) R_a(b,-a_a), R_a(b,-a_a)=S_(2a) D_a(x,b,y). (4) For the second identity use the original full-numerator value at that node: the all-CROSS formula equals N^2 times the literal complete-circle polynomial, including its beta and forced factors. The first identity makes its b and c dependence R_a(b)R_a(c). Comparing the monic b^a,c^a coefficients with the original D_a(b)D_a(c) gives (4), since prod_(r<a)(a_r-a_a) =prod_(r<a)4sin((a+r+1)theta)sin((a-r)theta)=S_(2a). The scalar outer factor is a nonzero polynomial (already nonzero at x>0,y=0), so cancellation takes place in the polynomial domain. The odd simple node is included. The case a=0 is the empty product1. Equation (4) does NOT identify generic-u R_j with a moving-dimensional q-Hahn determinant. Formula (1) is its actual off-node continuation. ## 2. Statement of the relative complex packet Fix a compact positive real set with b>0, A>0 and x,y>=0. A zero outer face stays exactly zero; other faces vary in a small fixed complex logarithmic neighborhood. Let the terminal row n=n_N satisfy n/N=1/2+O(1/N), n<=floor(N/2), as for R_(m-2), R_(m-1) and the odd R_m. The constants in the O term are bounded. For all sufficiently large N there are holomorphic phases phi_N(t;u,x,b,y) and holomorphic units a_N(t;u,x,y), on a fixed complex neighborhood of the interior real starting saddle, such that R_n(b,u)=sqrt(2pi N) a_N(t_N) exp[N phi_N(t_N)]/sqrt(-partial_t^2 phi_N(t_N)) *[1+O(N^-1)]. (5) Here t_N is the unique nearby zero of partial_t phi_N, and the square root is continued from its positive real value at u=0. All finite prefix products and the actual terminal n remain in phi_N; no source scalar is discarded. The estimate is uniform on a sufficiently small FIXED complex u disk and the indicated face neighborhood, with fixed parameter derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. In particular R_n is a unit there for all sufficiently large N. The phases converge with fixed derivatives to phi(t;u)=t Log b+integral_0^t Log alpha(v,u)dv +integral_t^(1/2) Log lambda(v,u)dv, alpha(v,u)=4cos^2(pi v)+u, lambda(v,u)=2sin(pi v)[sin(pi v)A +sqrt(sin^2(pi v)(x-y)^2+(4+u)P)]. (6) The square root and logarithms are continued from positive real values where their respective integrals occur. Only alpha on [0,t] is logged; it is uniformly nonzero there. Zeros of alpha near the UPPER terminal do not enter that logarithm or cause a zero of lambda. The limiting saddle is the analytic continuation of sin^2(pi t_b(u))=(1+u/4)b^2/[(b+x)(b+y)], t_b(0) in (0,1/2). (7) For x=0 this is (1+u/4)b/(b+y), and similarly for y=0. At u=0 the critical value in (6) is the original absolute triangle potential F(x,b,y). The finite terminal shift is retained in phi_N, not replaced by1/2 in the prefactor or finite action. ## 3. Uniform analytic dominant tail, including zero upper diagonals Choose fixed 0<ell<t_b(0)<r<1/2 uniformly over the real compact, with the saddle separated from ell,r. On a larger real interval containing [ell,1/2], the transfer recurrence for K has p(t)=4sin^2(pi t)A, q(t,h)=4sin(pi t)sin(pi(t-h)) [4cos^2(pi(t-h/2))+u]P. At h=u=0 the two characteristic roots are lambda and lambda_-, with lambda a unit and |lambda_-/lambda|<=kappa<1. This remains true in a fixed small complex t/face/u neighborhood and for small h. It includes the terminal alpha=0 cases: only the smaller root may vanish. If P=0, q=0 and the recurrence is first order, with the same unit dominant root. An exponentially accurate analytic ratio can be constructed directly. Start from the analytic positive characteristic root of z^2-pz-q=0, and iterate r_(l+1)(t)=p(t)+q(t,h)/r_l(t-h). (8) Use nested rectangles whose left real margin advances by h at each step; keep one extra shifted rectangle for the final residual. On a uniform O(h) neighborhood of the starting root, (8) preserves that neighborhood and has pointwise derivative modulus at most kappa'<1. Translation of the analytic seed costs O(h). After L=floor(cN) steps, where c is smaller than the available left margin, r_N is analytic, a unit, and r_N(t)-p(t)-q(t,h)/r_N(t-h)=O(exp(-c_1 N)), r_N(t)=lambda(t,u)+O(h). (9) The contraction estimate is between successive nested rectangles, not an assumed contraction on a fixed domain invariant under translation. Cauchy estimates on the retained common neighborhood give all fixed derivative bounds. The construction never divides by lambda_-. For integer i/N in [ell,r], divide the actual K_(i,j) by Y_j=prod_(v=i+1)^j r_N(vh), with Y_i=1. In the exact zero-residual recurrence, consecutive differences of K/Y multiply by -k_N(jh), k_N(t)=q(t,h)/[r_N(t)r_N(t-h)], |k_N|<=kappa'. The initial values are K_(i,i)=1,K_(i,i-1)=0. Hence the dominant initial projection is the analytic truncated sum a_N(t)=sum_(l=0)^(L') (-1)^l prod_(v=1)^l k_N(t+vh), (10) with L'=floor(c_2 N) smaller than every remaining terminal distance. The omitted tail is exponential. Its leading value is 1/(1+k_0(t)), a positive unit, and a_N differs from it by O(h). The residual (9) adds O(N exp(-c_1 N)) to the normalized solution: the difference recurrence and a geometric-series bound control the solution uniformly, then a discrete Gronwall factor is1+o(1). Thus uniformly in all these actual integer starts and complex parameters, K_(i,n)=a_N(ih) prod_(v=i+1)^n r_N(vh) [1+O(exp(-c_3 N))]. (11) ## 4. Exponentially accurate analytic starting-row interpolation On [0,r] and its fixed complex neighborhood, alpha(t+h/2,u) is an analytic unit. The midpoint prefix product prod_(v<i)alpha_v can therefore be interpolated by an optimally truncated Euler--Maclaurin primitive, anchored at0. The tail product in (11) has the same construction applied to Log r_N, anchored at the ACTUAL t=n/N. Uniform holomorphy gives C^k k! derivative bounds. Choosing the number of Bernoulli terms proportional to N gives an O(exp(-c_4 N)) remainder on smaller fixed neighborhoods, as in the proved analytic discrete primitive lemma for the original fold factors. Explicitly, on a retained analytic strip of width d_0, the order-2K Euler--Maclaurin remainder for a log SUM is bounded by C h^(2K-1) (2K)!/(2pi d_0)^(2K) <= C h^(-1) [C_0 K h]^(2K). The same estimate holds for the midpoint rule, whose periodic Bernoulli functions have the same factorial bound. It follows from the integral remainder and |f^(2K)|<=C (2K)! d_0^(-2K); the strip and C are uniform for both Log alpha and the constructed Log r_N. Choose K=floor(c_0/h) with C_0 c_0<1. The polynomial h^(-1) is absorbed by shrinking the positive exponential constant. Thus the LOG-product error, and hence its relative product error, is O(exp(-c_4 N)), uniformly in the actual integer endpoints. The finite truncated primitive itself is holomorphic on the smaller strip used below. Keep these finite primitives, rather than only their leading integrals. With the exact b^i factor and (10), they define w_N(t)=a_N(t) exp[N phi_N(t)] such that EACH actual summand of (2), for i/N in [ell,r], equals w_N(i/N)[1+O(exp(-c_5 N))]. The phase converges with fixed derivatives to (6). All primitive anchors, their endpoint half terms and finite terminal shifts stay in phi_N. This proves the normalization claim in (5), without inferring a continuum phase solely from node interpolation. All starts OUTSIDE [ell,r], including i=0, remain in the argument. At positive faces and u=0 the uniform interval theorem gives their exact weighted rate. The limiting phase is strictly maximized at t_b(0), since its derivative is Log[b/L(t;x,y)] and L is strictly increasing from0 to infinity. Choose ell,r so those tails have a fixed gap c_6>0, uniformly over the real compact. For small complex u, apply the original unused-row product bound to each term in (2). The product of all nonzero lower-row ratios is at most exp[N theta(|u|)+O(log N)], theta(v)=arcosh(1+v/2). This also covers odd terminal n=m: the cofactor excludes alpha_m=0. The original missing steps and all other starting rows are retained. A small logarithmic face perturbation costs exp(C rho N), since each term has the same finite homogeneous degree n. Taking the fixed u and face neighborhoods small enough makes their total cost less than c_6 N/4. The entire omitted starting-row sum is therefore exponentially below the continued saddle, not merely small at a real parameter. ## 5. The actual discrete saddle and its contour At u=0, partial_t^2 phi(t)<0 uniformly on [ell,r]. On a sufficiently small fixed complex parameter neighborhood, the IFT gives a holomorphic t_N with partial_t phi_N(t_N)=0, t_N=t_b(u)+O(1/N), and Re[-partial_t^2 phi_N] bounded below by a positive constant near the continued horizontal saddle contour. The finite-grid replacement is justified, including its vertical edges. Let ell_N,r_N^end be the half-grid boundaries around the integer starts in [ell,r]. For a fixed small height eta, the exact residue formula is sum_i w_N(i/N) =N/(2i) integral_(rectangle) cot(pi N z) w_N(z) dz. (12) On the upper/lower sides cot(pi N z)=-/+ i+O(exp(-2pi eta N)). On the vertical half-grid sides its modulus is at most1. The real endpoint gap persists along those sides for small eta and small complex parameters. On the horizontal sides the phase costs at most C eta^2 at the real reference, plus C rho from the parameter perturbation. Choose eta first so 2pi eta>C eta^2, then rho small enough for the cotangent error and vertical currents to have a uniform exponential gap relative to exp[N phi_N(t_N)]. Cauchy's theorem now compares (12) with N times the ordinary integral along [ell_N,r_N^end]; the retained vertical connector terms have the same gap. No endpoint current has been declared identically zero. The exponentially small interpolation error from section4 also stays exponentially small AFTER summation: its possible absolute-sum loss is O(rho N), and the parameter neighborhood was chosen smaller than its fixed exponential accuracy. Deform the ordinary interval to the horizontal segment through t_N, retaining both endpoint connectors. Uniform strict concavity along that segment gives the Gaussian formula (5), with relative O(N^-1) and the continued positive square root. Analyticity and Cauchy margins give the claimed fixed parameter derivatives of that relative error. ## 6. What this packet does and does not supply The proof treats b>0 and every actual starting row; i=0 is exponentially subdominant in this chart. It includes x=0 or y=0, where q=0, (8) is exact, and a_N=1. It does NOT discard i=0 when b itself is the protected zero: that different chart is the separate protected-middle theorem. Under u=-4sin^2(pi delta), the packet is holomorphic in delta on a fixed small cover neighborhood. In particular it covers selected fixed delta=O(1/n_twist) sectors once the signed twists are sufficiently long for this fixed diagram. This is a finite cofactor asymptotic, not a choice of a contributing charge or cycle in the full Gaussian period. The exact central cross formulas must still be assembled with their literal alpha prefactors, both parities and original shared coefficient extraction. Their leading central factors are nonzero near u=0, but the whole phase-sensitive period requires its own selection argument. Once the separate b=0 packet and the exact central factors are included, there is a direct calibration of the local LEADING action. At every physical fold node, the all-cross polynomial is exactly N^2 B_(N,a). These nodes become dense in a fixed small real delta interval. Uniform convergence of the present normalized logarithm and the already proved complete fold interpolation therefore gives psi_b(u(delta))+psi_c(u(delta)) =F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y)-V(delta;x,b,c,y), where psi_b=phi(t_b(u);u). The real node values are positive, fixing the logarithmic branch and absolute constant. Both sides are holomorphic, so the identity extends to the same small complex cover neighborhood, with shared-face derivatives. This identifies a leading local action; it does not identify the finite cofactor with the old interpolant or prove a global face-torus gap or selected Gaussian contribution. ## Focused finite validation Private helper ../experiments/audit_actual_cross_cofactor_interior_packet.py compares the row-replaced determinant directly with the cleared recurrence and compares its physical-node values with the independently built original positive q-Hahn matrices. At 85 digits, N=3,...,18, real/complex faces and each one-protected-outer specialization, it passes1056 row determinants, 352 matrix node adapters,352 exact sine scalars and960 tail factorizations; maximum relative error is below2e-85. These checks validate the finite adapter. The relative complex asymptotic is the analytical proof above, not a conclusion inferred from finite node or rate samples. ## Scope This is an interior cofactor packet. It does not establish a whole-face torus bound or a contributing Gaussian cycle. [Focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cross_cofactor_interior_packet.py) · [Recorded output](../experiments/actual_cross_cofactor_interior_packet_results.json). These finite checks supplement the written proof and retain the scope recorded in their output.

title: Actual all-CROSS cofactors and the complete-fold interpolant
text: # Actual all-CROSS cofactors and the complete-fold interpolant The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . This is a quantitative analytic consequence of the actual cofactor packets. It does not infer a generic-q derivative or select a Gaussian cycle. All face zeros remain the original protected zeros. ## 1. Exact objects and the theorem Let P_(N,cross)(u;l) be the original local all-CROSS numerator, with the sign (-1)^d already included, and let mathcal B_N(delta;l) be the EXACTLY anchored interpolation in actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md. Thus u(delta)=-4sin^2(pi delta), delta_a=(N-1-2a)/(2N), P_(N,cross)(u(delta_a);l)=N^2 B_(N,a)(l), (1) B_(N,a)/mathcal B_N(delta_a)=1+O(exp(-cN)). (2) Both P_(N,cross)(u(delta)) and mathcal B_N(delta) are even in delta. Equation (1) is the original paired/simple-node identity with its actual N^2 factor. Equation (2) keeps the original B_(N,M) anchor, half-index, forced factor, beta factors and complex face neighborhood. Fix a compact positive geometric face set in any one of its actual protected-zero patterns. The ordinary-middle and protected-middle cofactor packets imply that, after decreasing a FIXED disk and FIXED complex face neighborhood, there is kappa>0 such that P_(N,cross)(u(delta);l) =N^2 mathcal B_N(delta;l)[1+O(exp(-kappa N))] (3) uniformly for |delta|<=a and l in that neighborhood, for both parities and all sufficiently large N. All fixed delta and face derivatives of the relative error obey the same statement on smaller neighborhoods. The positive number a is independent of N. It may depend on the fixed diagram/face compact and the previously proved analytic accuracy. This theorem concerns the ACTUAL finite cofactor, not a freely chosen interpolation of its nodal values. The proof uses its independent complex packet to control its off-node growth. No uniqueness assertion is made for arbitrary analytic functions having the same physical node values. ## 2. The whole central factor is an analytic unit Write A=x+y, P=xy, m=floor(N/2), D_b=R_(m-1)(b,u), E_b=(a_(m-1)+u)R_(m-2)(b,u), and G_b=R_m(b,u) at odd levels. Put S=sqrt(A^2+uP), Lambda_*=2(A+S), (4) with S=A at u=0. The actual cofactor packets, including their finite terminal rows, imply uniformly on a fixed complex neighborhood R_n/R_(n-1) -> Lambda_*, for the terminal rows used here. For b>0 this follows from the same starting-row saddle with one more terminal recurrence step; the inhomogeneous terminal source is exponentially smaller because its start is separated from the strict interior saddle. For b=0 it is the explicit protected-middle packet. When P=0 it follows from the exact first-order terminal recurrence. No division by a vanishing smaller transfer eigenvalue is used. The exact even factorization gives P_cross/(D_b D_c) =s_m^2 A+s_m s_(m-1)P(E_b/D_b+E_c/D_c) ->4A+8uP/Lambda_*=4S. (5) The exact odd factorization gives P_cross/(G_b G_c) =1+u s_m s_(m+1)P D_b D_c/(G_b G_c) ->1+4uP/Lambda_*^2=2S/(A+S). (6) Both limits are holomorphic units near u=0, also at one-outer-zero specializations. Equations (5),(6) retain the actual finite coefficients; they are used here only to establish a uniform nonvanishing factor and its subexponential logarithmic size. Thus the full local P_cross has a holomorphic logarithm on a fixed small disk and complex face polydisc. Its normalized logarithm converges there, uniformly on smaller closures, to the sum of the two actual cofactor actions. ## 3. Subexponential ratio growth, with no fitted normalization The same uniform normalized-log convergence holds for mathcal B_N from its original B_(N,M) anchor and the explicit analytic fold interpolation. At positive real faces and sufficiently small real delta, every cofactor packet above is on its positive branch; hence all logarithms can be chosen real there. The dense physical nodes (1),(2) force the two limiting normalized logarithms to agree on that real delta interval. The identity theorem extends the equality in delta and then in each complex face variable. Equivalently one may use the independently proved absolute cofactor/complete-action identity; it fixes the same constant and is not needed as an extra interpolation assumption. Consequently, on one fixed outer circle |delta|=R and a smaller fixed closed face neighborhood, sup |P_cross/(N^2 mathcal B_N)| <= exp(o(N)), sup |P_cross/(N^2 mathcal B_N)-1| <= exp(o(N)), (7) where o(N)/N tends to zero uniformly. The exact N^2 contributes only 2log N to a logarithm. No uncontrolled face-dependent exponential normalization is introduced. A polynomial bound would suffice but is not necessary; the uniform subexponential estimate (7) is enough. ## 4. Finite Cauchy--Lagrange rigidity, including both parity grids Set f_N(delta)=P_cross/(N^2 mathcal B_N)-1. On a fixed real interval |delta|<=a, take EVERY physical node and its reflection. At odd N this is the grid j/N (including0); at even N it is (j+1/2)/N. Thus the chosen nodes t_0<...<t_(M-1) have spacing exactly1/N, lie in [-a,a], and M=2aN+O(1), |f_N(t_j)|<=C exp(-cN). (8) Evenness supplies the negative nodes without a new continuation or phase convention. Choose 0<a<R/8 within the original physical matching window, and evaluate |z|<=a. The exact interpolation formula is f_N(z)=sum_j f_N(t_j) ell_j(z) +(1/(2pi i)) integral_(|zeta|=R) f_N(zeta)/(zeta-z) product_j[(z-t_j)/(zeta-t_j)] dzeta. (9) There are no other poles since mathcal B_N is a unit on the outer disk. The contour remainder is at most C exp(o(N)) [2a/(R-a)]^M. (10) Its exponent is strictly negative, uniformly in the fixed complex face parameters. To bound the noisy-node polynomial, use the exact spacing: product_(k!=j)|t_j-t_k| =N^(-(M-1)) j! (M-1-j)!, sum_j |ell_j(z)| <= (4aN)^(M-1)/(M-1)! <= exp([2a log(3e)+o(1)]N). (11) The harmless 3e accommodates the bounded endpoint rounding. Choose a still smaller so 2a log(3e)<c/2. Equations (8),(11) then give an exponentially small polynomial part. Equations (10),(11) prove (3), with some fixed kappa>0. Analytic Cauchy estimates on nested disks and face neighborhoods give all fixed derivative versions. Since both sides are even, they also define the same exponentially accurate relative comparison in the spectral coordinate u near0, on a smaller fixed disk. ## 5. Consequences and remaining estimates The old complete-fold interpolation now describes the actual all-CROSS local numerator, including its spectral derivatives, with exponential precision. This is stronger than matching only the principal phase or only the original node values. The semisimple nodal ambiguity is resolved HERE by the independent actual cofactor growth theorem and (9), not by formally differentiating an arbitrary root identity. For finitely many original ports the local relative comparisons multiply on the common positive-face complex chart, with the same kind of exponential error. The original shared target and physical half-powers, cups, mark and finite phase scalars must still be retained. In particular (3) by itself does not identify an entire shared face-torus coefficient: its angular complement needs an actual uniform estimate. Nor does it prove the selected full Gaussian contour, the surviving charge sum, or a genuine-q first-normal theorem. No external-color alias is discarded. The interpolation argument uses exact Cauchy and Lagrange formulas. Finite samples do not establish its uniform error bound.

text: # The full-V cofactor branch and the original marked peripheral action The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . The exact central-cofactor formulas are in [actual cross cofactor factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md). This note identifies their indicated principal branch, including its absolute normalization and the actual primitive logs. It does NOT prove that a particular global quantum cycle selects it or that every complex cofactor has a single-branch relative asymptotic. Use spectral w=-sigma-2 (the cofactor note calls it u); the original protected white faces are still named u,v and remain zero. At every port put A=x+y>0 and P=xy. The principal diagonal and cleared tail root are a(t)=4cos^2(pi t), s(t)=2sin(pi t), Lambda(t;w)=[s(t)^2 A+sqrt(s(t)^4 A^2 +4s(t)^2(a(t)+w)P)]/2. (1) For positive x,b,y select the root positive at w=0. Set w=-4sin^2(pi delta), sigma=-2cos(2pi delta), s=sin(pi delta), c=cos(pi delta), T_b=sqrt[bA+xy+b^2 s^2], D=A^2-4xy s^2, E_b=A+2b s^2+2s T_b. (2) All square roots/logs are the ones at delta=0. The finite physical node is delta_a=(N-1-2a)/(2N), not an unrecorded unshifted row a/N. The finite cofactors keep that half-index and all parity scalars. ## 1. Exact equality of the two normalized analytic actions Define F_w by the stationary value F_w=mu Log b+integral_0^mu Log(a(t)+w)dt +integral_mu^(1/2)Log Lambda(t;w)dt, (3) where mu is the continuation of the complete interior solution. It obeys b(a(mu)+w)=Lambda(mu;w), sin^2(pi mu)=c^2 b^2/[(b+x)(b+y)], mu=(1/pi)atan(b c/T_b). (4) These identities follow by substitution into the quadratic for Lambda; no asymptotic differentiation is involved. For small positive real delta, mu<1/2-delta, so the first logarithm in (3) is positive along its path. For positive x,y, Lambda(t)/t is nonzero and analytic at t=0. Separating its log t singularity therefore defines a holomorphic germ of (3) near delta=0, including b=0 by its limiting stationary value. Ordinary positive b may vary down to zero on a fixed bounded interval after shrinking this germ. Formula (3) is a stationary analytic value for complex parameters, not a complex maximum operation. For precision at b=0, write Lambda=t L with L(0) a unit and mu=b m with m(0) a unit. In mu Log b minus integral_0^mu Log t, the only potential logarithmic singularity is mu Log(b/mu); it is holomorphic. Thus this is an analytic extension, not just a continuous rate limit. Let Q_b(delta) be the original determinant-plus-beta-plus-HALF-forced- product triangle action of the coupled complete source. Its proved literal definition, putting nu=1/2-delta, is Q_b=I(2nu)-2I(nu)+integral_0^nu Log lambda_b(t)dt +(1/4)integral_nu^(1-nu) Log[x^2+y^2-2xy cos(2pi t)]dt, I(v)=integral_0^v Log(2sin(pi t))dt, lambda_b(t)=[A+2b cos^2(pi t) +2cos(pi t)sqrt(b^2cos^2(pi t)+bA+xy)]/[4cos^2(pi t)]. This is the actual beta, determinant and forced-product rate from [actual positive face channel rate](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md), not a chosen antiderivative. Cancellation of their spectral derivatives gives its normalization and differential Q_b(0)=F(x,b,y), partial_delta Q_b=-Log(E_b/sqrt D), partial_Log(b) Q_b=(1/pi)atan(b c/T_b). (5) Then the exact action-germ identity is F_w=Q_b(delta). (6) Here is a complete constant check. The envelope rule in (3) gives partial_Log(b) F_w=mu, so F_w-Q_b is independent of b. Also partial_delta mu=-b s/T_b, partial_Log(b) Log(E_b/sqrt D)=b s/T_b. (7) The second identity follows directly from partial_b E_b=s E_b/T_b. It remains to fix the b-independent term, not assume it zero. At b=0, put lambda=2sqrt(xy)/A in(0,1]. With theta=pi t, differentiating the integral in (3) gives partial_delta F_w|_(b=0) =-lambda^2 s c integral_0^(pi/2) dtheta/[W(theta)(sin theta+W(theta))], W(theta)=sqrt[(1-lambda^2)sin^2 theta+lambda^2 c^2]. Rationalize the denominator and put z=cos theta. The result is -s c integral_0^1 {1/sqrt(1-z^2) -1/sqrt(1-lambda^2 s^2-(1-lambda^2)z^2)} dz/(z^2-s^2). (8) The apparent pole at z=s is removable: the two square roots there are both c. For an elementary evaluation, each integral of 1/[(z^2-s^2)sqrt(B-Cz^2)] has antiderivative [1/(2s c)] log |(c z/sqrt(B-Cz^2)-s) /(c z/sqrt(B-Cz^2)+s)|, because B-C s^2=c^2 in BOTH terms of (8). Subtract these antiderivatives before evaluating: their logarithmic singularities at z=s cancel, with no jump. They both vanish at z=0. At z=1 the first tends to zero and the second is -artanh(lambda s)/(s c). Hence partial_delta F_w|_(b=0)=-artanh(lambda s) =-Log[(A+2s sqrt(xy))/sqrt(A^2-4xy s^2)]. (9) This calculation uses small real delta>0, where every real branch is specified; holomorphic continuation then gives the identity of germs. It agrees EXACTLY with (5) at b=0. Equations (7),(9) give the full partial_delta identity for every b>=0. Finally (3) at delta=0 is the already calibrated complete triangle action: integral_0^(1/2)log a=0, and the actual lower-block product contributes no exponential constant. Thus F_w-Q_b vanishes at delta=0 and has zero delta derivative, proving (6) with no additive face-dependent or spectral constant. ## 2. All allowed marked zeros, including the lost local strip flag If exactly one of x,y vanishes, Lambda=s(t)^2 A is the EXACT monomer root. Differentiating (3) gives partial_delta F_w=-2 artanh[(s/c)tan(pi mu)] =-2 artanh(b s/T_b) =-Log(E_b/A), (10) since D=A^2. This proves the same normalization directly on the one-line triangle, without dividing by xy. It also follows by a dominated limit of (8); the integrable bounds C+2|log t| are uniform as xy decreases to0. If b=0 and xy=0, (3) is exactly F_w=(1/2)Log A, (11) independent of w, just as the original cofactor is the monomer product A^n product_(j=1)^n s_j^2. For b=0 and xy>0, (9) is its nonconstant spectral force. These include every allowed triangle of the original marked dictionary. Both outer faces cannot be the two protected MAIN faces on a matching edge; thus A>0 remains part of that dictionary. At a two-line triangle (11) alone does NOT recover its selected flags. For example at b=y=0 its actual strip height still obeys H=2c^2/x: the finite x-circle is tangent to the marked b-line and intersects the marked y-line in the recorded orientation. The existing [actual marked deformed circle pattern](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) retains this common line geometry and its selected eigenlines. We use THAT global boundary adapter, not the double root or constant action to invent a flag. The protected-middle relative packet proved separately in [actual cross cofactor protected packet](actual_cross_cofactor_protected_packet.md) has finite-N product prod_j[s_j lambda_(j,+)] and a nonzero bounded amplitude. Its logarithmic limit is exactly (3) at b=0, since s(t)lambda_+(t)=Lambda(t;w). Thus (6),(9) identify an analytically PRESENT branch for those actual cleared cofactors, including the exact monomer case. For a summed ordinary middle b>0 and for the original shared coefficient, the corresponding relative packet is a separate requirement. ## 3. The original physical conic and all momenta By (4), the physical input momentum p=exp(-2pi i mu) satisfies exactly \[ \sigma=2+\frac{(p-1)^2}{p}\frac{(b+x)(b+y)}{b^2}=-2-w. \tag{12} \] This is the original crossing Casimir, with the physical inverse of the coefficient momentum as fixed in [actual crossing torus meridian transport](actual_crossing_torus_meridian_transport.md). It is not a new trace convention. The reciprocal output momentum is selected by the CROSS action Q_b+Q_c. More precisely retain the full physical adapter H/(bc)^(d/2). For its principal phase Theta=Q_b+Q_c-(Log b+Log c)/2, the original head change of variables gives ALL derivatives p_in=exp(-i theta_b), p_out=exp(+i theta_c), g_out/g_in=exp[i(theta_y,in+theta_y,out)]. (13) The three angles in each triangle are those of the deformed center triangle. Identity (6), together with the already proved full face gradients of Q, supplies the outer derivative in (13), not only (12). The regular ordered-character calculation in [actual whole source coupled face difference system](actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.md), §4, therefore applies without changing a physical half power: the ENTIRE ordered product P=BA is preserved and the same primitive centralizer transports both punctures. Its selected spectral line is J=-exp(-2pi i delta), lambda=-J. (14) At the protected zeros use the common marked line pattern and its literal reflection products; no singular old Gauss denominator is canceled there. The actual original input b/output c collar has, on that J-line, R0=E_b E_c/D, C=I+(R0-1)/(J-J^(-1)) (P-J^(-1)I). (15) The quotient is the already proved removable divided difference on the selected marked germ. Its delta=0 limit is the nontrivial parabolic collar, not I. The corner order and three contacts are those proved in [actual deformed circle primitive collar](actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md); in particular C is a primitive shaded pairing, not the square of two shaded reflections. These equations identify the regular original crossing/A-torsor branch. They do not identify every branch of the full cofactor characteristic or claim a scalar eliminated A-polynomial. ## 4. Global marked geometry and the correct polarization For a fixed original certified D, form the stationary face action A_epsilon(delta)=crit_(ordinary faces) {sum_i [Q_bi(delta_i)+Q_ci(delta_i)] -sum_(ordinary f)Log l_f +pi i sum_i epsilon_i delta_i^2}. (16) The two original marked faces remain zero. The existing face Hessian, marked circle reconstruction and source IFT give its selected local analytic branch and one common circle family. By (6) it is exactly the candidate full-V CROSS branch with the retained half-twist character. This is an equality of principal action germs, conditional on that branch when discussing a relative asymptotic of the full numerator. The existing actual group assembly supplies its representation with primitive logs U_i=-Log R0_i-epsilon_i Log(-J_i), V_i=2Log(-J_i)=-4pi i delta_i, partial_delta_i A_epsilon=U_i. (17) The derivative uses face stationarity; it does not differentiate an unproved asymptotic. At zero its diagonal Jacobian is partial_delta_j U_i=-2(C_i-pi i epsilon_i)delta_ij, C_i=pi[T_bi(0)+T_ci(0)]/(x_i+y_i)>0. (18) Thus these are actual local coordinates on the same marked geometric germ as the complete Fourier core. This is a LONGITUDE-polarized primitive. Put G_lon=2pi i A_epsilon. Then dG_lon=-(1/2)sum_i U_i dV_i. (19) The core instead has chi_i=-U_i/(2pi i) and S_core(chi)=A_epsilon(delta)+2pi i sum_i chi_i delta_i. Consequently G_mer=2pi i S_core=G_lon+(1/2)sum_i U_i V_i, dG_mer=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i. (20) The complete source fixes 2pi Re A_epsilon(0)=Vol(Y_D). Applying the proved core regulator identity through this exact Legendre relation therefore gives the ABSOLUTELY normalized longitude action 2pi Re A_epsilon(delta) =Vol(rho_delta)-(1/2)sum_i Im U_i Re V_i. (21) No local open-word re-framing invariance is used. Equation (21) retains the complex boundary term; for real delta its V are purely imaginary and that term vanishes. All known spectral-independent framing and finite parity scalars remain outside the normalized principal action. ## 5. Original Gaussian charges and primitive filling logs For an actual fixed crossing exponent n_i=epsilon_i-2p_i, the full Hermite Gaussian contributes pi i n_i delta_i^2 and a surviving Fourier charge ell_i contributes 2pi i ell_i delta_i, with their original constant scalar signs retained. Its principal phase is therefore A_epsilon(delta)-2pi i sum_i p_i delta_i^2 +2pi i sum_i ell_i delta_i. Stationarity gives EXACTLY U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i ell_i. (22) For the original unit charge ell_i=1 this is the already calibrated primitive smooth filling equation. Reciprocal delta/J branches reverse the corresponding logs and charges; kappa or the trace alone cannot choose them. The charge0 contribution is identically zero in the original spectral total-derivative formula and must not be resurrected as a complete-point saddle. text: # A fixed angular gap for the actual protected-middle cofactor The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . The middle face is the original protected zero b=0. The proof uses the literal level-N recurrence and preserves all its endpoint coefficients. It is independent of the relative cofactor packet and does not assert a whole shared-face torus gap. Write theta=pi/N and s_j=2sin(j theta), a_j=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta), A=x+y, P=xy, p_j=s_j^2 A, q_j(w)=s_j s_(j-1)(a_(j-1)+w)P. The original cleared cofactor is R_0=1, R_(-1)=0, R_j(w)=p_j R_(j-1)(w)+q_j(w)R_(j-2)(w). (1) The spectral coordinate is w=-sigma-2. In particular no inverse of a near-fold diagonal is introduced. All factors at the actual terminal rows m-2,m-1,m, m=floor(N/2), remain in (1). ## 1. Exact coefficientwise spectral control For N>=3 and 0<=n<=floor(N/2), as polynomials in x,y,w, 0 <= R_n(w) <= (1+w)^n R_n(0). (2) Inequality means comparison of every coefficient. Therefore, for positive real x,y and arbitrary complex w, |R_n(x,y;w)| <= R_n(x,y;|w|) <= (1+|w|)^n R_n(x,y;0). (3) To prove (2), put d_j=s_j s_(j-1)xy. Positivity of the recurrence at w=0 gives, for j>=2, R_j(0)>=(p_j p_(j-1)+q_j(0))R_(j-2)(0). The polynomial p_j p_(j-1)+q_j(0)-d_j has coefficients (s_j s_(j-1))^2 at x^2 and y^2, s_j s_(j-1)[2s_j s_(j-1)+a_(j-1)-1] at xy. Its bracket satisfies the EXACT level-N identity 2s_j s_(j-1)+a_(j-1)-1 =4cos(theta)+1-2cos((2j-1)theta) >=1. (4) Here N>=3 and all the used s_j are nonnegative. Hence R_j(0)>=d_j R_(j-2)(0), coefficientwise. The induction from j=0,1 is R_j(w) <= (1+w)^(j-1) [p_j R_(j-1)(0)+(q_j(0)+w d_j)R_(j-2)(0)] <= (1+w)^j R_j(0). The first inequality uses (1+w)^(j-2)<=(1+w)^(j-1), coefficientwise also in w. This proves (2), including every zero outer specialization. ## 2. Three-step angular contraction Fix x0,y0>0, put A0=x0+y0, P0=x0y0, and let x=x0 exp(i alpha), y=y0 exp(i beta). If the circular distance of alpha-beta from0 is at least epsilon, with 0<epsilon<=pi, then |x+y|<=r A0, r=sqrt[1-4P0/A0^2 sin^2(epsilon/2)]<1. (5) Set v=|w|. Taking absolute values in (1) is bounded by the positive recurrence with first coefficient r p_j, second coefficient q_j(v), where now p_j=s_j^2 A0 and q_j(v)=s_j s_(j-1)(a_(j-1)+v)P0. Let T_j=[[p_j,q_j(v)],[1,0]], T_j^r=[[r p_j,q_j(v)],[1,0]]. On the bulk interval N/8<=j<=3N/8 and 0<=v<=1, p_j >=4sin^2(pi/8)A0, q_j(v) <=4(4+v)P0 <=5A0^2. Write beta0=16sin^4(pi/8)/[16sin^4(pi/8)+5], eta=(1-r)beta0>0. (6) For any three consecutive indices contained in that interval, T_j^r T_(j-1)^r T_(j-2)^r <=(1-eta) T_j T_(j-1) T_(j-2) (7) entrywise. Indeed their top-left entry is a sum of terms with at least one p, so contracts by at least r. Their bottom-right entry is p_(j-1)q_(j-2), also contracting by r. The remaining entries are (p_j p_(j-1)+q_j)q_(j-2), p_(j-1)p_(j-2)+q_(j-1). In each, the fraction carried by its two-p term is at least beta0. That part contracts by r^2. Since 1-r^2>=1-r and beta0<=1, all four entries obey (7). This proves a uniform positive amount of one-step mass; it does not assert that every individual path has a linear number of one-steps. If N>=64 and 3N/8<=n<=floor(N/2), the integer interval from ceil(N/8) to floor(3N/8) contains at least N/16 disjoint triples. All remaining matrices satisfy T_j^r<=T_j. Multiplication of nonnegative matrices and the exact initial vector (1,0)^T gives |R_n(x,y;w)| <= (1-eta)^(N/16) R_n(x0,y0;v). (8) No division by a transfer entry or by R_(-1) has occurred. ## 3. A fixed complex spectral neighborhood Combine (3),(8), using n<=N/2. For |w|<=eta/16, one obtains |R_n(x0 exp(i alpha),y0 exp(i beta);w)| <=exp(-eta N/32) R_n(x0,y0;0). (9) At w=0 the stronger exponent eta N/16 follows. Constants are uniform when (x0,y0) lies in a fixed positive compact set and epsilon is fixed. The actual terminal indices m-2,m-1 and m satisfy the interval condition for all sufficiently large N. Both parities are included. If exactly one outer face is zero, (1) is instead the exact monomer R_n=(x+y)^n product_(j=1)^n s_j^2, independent of w. Its modulus is unchanged by its sole phase, so there is no relative-angular condition or gap to claim in that case. If both outers vanish, R_n=0 for n>0; this is excluded by the original marked MAIN-versus-MATCHING dictionary on the geometric chart. The bound is on the actual cofactor, at the original protected target. A whole shared-face angular gap still requires the graph argument showing that every nontrivial face phase is detected by an appropriate ordinary-middle or protected-middle factor. text: # A relative packet for the cleared cofactor at a protected middle face The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . This concerns the actual fixed-root lower cofactor with b=0. It is not a whole-source saddle, filling-cycle or genuine-q theorem. All products below stay at level N. ## 1. Exact recurrence and statement Let x,y range in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of ANY fixed positive pair, let u range in a sufficiently small complex disk about 0, and put A=x+y, P=xy. Write h=1/N, s_j=2sin(pi*j/N), a_j=4cos^2(pi*(j+1/2)/N). The original cleared cofactor recurrence at b=0 is R_0=1, R_(-1)=0, R_j=s_j^2 A R_(j-1)+s_j s_(j-1)(a_(j-1)+u)P R_(j-2). Set L_j=R_j/(product_(r=1)^j s_r). Then EXACTLY L_j=s_j A L_(j-1)+(a_(j-1)+u)P L_(j-2), (L_0,L_(-1))=(1,0). (1) The normalization causes no loss at j=1: its second term multiplies L_(-1)=0. Fix 0<t_0<1/2 and take t_0 N<=n<=N/2. Define T_h(t)=[[2sin(pi*t) A, P(4cos^2(pi*(t-h/2))+u)],[1,0]], lambda_+(t), lambda_-(t)=its two eigenvalues, g(t)=lambda_+(t)-lambda_-(t). The square-root branch has g>0 at real x,y>0,u=0. Write lambda_(j,+) for lambda_+(j/N), and similarly for minus and g. The matrix at t=0 is only a reference eigenbasis; it does not change the initial vector. For all sufficiently large N these branches are holomorphic and C_j=(lambda_(j-1,+)-lambda_(j,-))/g_j =1+O(h), A_(N,n)=lambda_(n,+)/g_0 product_(j=1)^n C_j, E_(N,n)=product_(j=1)^n [s_j lambda_(j,+)]. Then uniformly on the stated FIXED complex neighborhood, R_n(0;x,y;u)=A_(N,n) E_(N,n) [1+O(N^-1)]. (2) The explicit amplitude A_(N,n) is holomorphic, uniformly bounded and bounded away from zero. The same relative error has fixed parameter derivative bounds on every smaller neighborhood, by Cauchy. The finite-N product E retains all endpoint factors and parity dependence; no scalar normalization is discarded. ## 2. The eigenvalues have an algebraic gap even at the lower endpoint For positive real x,y, u=0 and h=0, the discriminant is 4sin^2(pi*t)A^2+16cos^2(pi*t)P>0, 0<=t<=1/2. Its minimum and lambda_+ are positive on this compact interval. They remain uniformly separated from zero for sufficiently small complex parameter perturbations and small real h>=0. In particular |g|>=c and |lambda_+|>=c. All derivatives needed below are uniformly bounded on a small extension of this interval. lambda_- may vanish; no inverse of lambda_- is used. Put r(t)=lambda_-(t)/lambda_+(t). At t=0, r(0)=-1 EXACTLY, also for complex parameters. Since lambda_++lambda_-=2sin(pi*t)A, r'(0)=2pi A/lambda_+(0). Its real part is uniformly positive near the positive real parameters. Therefore |r(t)|<=exp(-c t) for 0<=t<=epsilon with uniform c>0, after shrinking the parameter neighborhood. On [epsilon,1/2], the real unperturbed |r| is strictly less than1; compactness extends a bound |r(t)|<=exp(-c t) there as well. These estimates are uniform in sufficiently small h. Equality of the eigenvalue MODULI at t=0 therefore does not imply coalescence: |1-r| stays uniformly positive. ## 3. A one-step normal form, including the initial negative branch Use E(t)=[[lambda_+(t),lambda_-(t)],[1,1]]. For the state vector v_j=(L_j,L_(j-1))^T, set w_j=E(jh)^(-1)v_j. The exact update is w_j=diag(lambda_(j,+),lambda_(j,-)) B_j w_(j-1), B_j=E(jh)^(-1)E((j-1)h). Here (B_j)_(++)=C_j. Divide out product lambda_(j,+) C_j, so the normalized update has the form M_j=diag(1,d_j)+F_j, d_j=r(jh)(B_j)_(--)/C_j, F_j diagonal entries 0, offdiagonal entries O(h). These matrices are samples of smooth functions of t, with F'(t)=O(h), |1-d(t)|>=c, and |d_j|<=exp(Ch-c*j*h). Choose the offdiagonal near-identity correction X_j by (X_j)_12=-(F_j)_12/(1-d_j), (X_j)_21= (F_j)_21/(1-d_j), diag X_j=0. Then X_j=O(h), X_j-X_(j-1)=O(h^2). Direct multiplication gives (I+X_j)^(-1) M_j (I+X_(j-1)) =diag(1,d_j)+O(h^2). (3) Only 1-d_j is divided out. This remains valid when d_j=0 and when r(0)=-1. The diagonal product norms are at most exp(Cnh), and the same holds for the corrected matrices, since each step has norm at most exp(Ch)+O(h^2). Telescoping their n-fold products in operator norm gives an O(nh^2)=O(h) error from the diagonal product. Meanwhile |product_(j=1)^n d_j|<=exp(Cnh-c h n(n+1)/2)=O(exp(-c' N)) for t_0 N<=n<=N/2. Thus the initial negative branch is retained and then proved exponentially suppressed; it is not discarded by fiat. The initial eigenvector coordinates are exactly (1/g_0,-1/g_0). The near-identity corrections change them by O(h). Inverting the final basis yields L_n=[product lambda_(j,+) C_j] lambda_(n,+)/g_0 [1+O(h)], uniformly, since lambda_(n,+)/g_0 is bounded away from zero. This is (2). The amplitude product is bounded and nonzero because every C_j=1+O(h) and n=O(N). Uniform holomorphy proves the asserted Cauchy bounds. ## 4. Scope and exact degenerate outer faces If b=0 and exactly one of x,y vanishes, the original recurrence is instead the EXACT monomer product R_n=(x+y)^n product_(j=1)^n s_j^2, independent of u. No limiting inverse of xy is used. If both outer faces vanish and n>0, the same original recurrence is zero; this is not part of the positive geometric triangle chart. For x,y>0 the terminal ratios following from (2), uniformly on a smaller neighborhood, are R_n/R_(n-1)=s_n lambda_(n,+) [1+O(N^-1)] when n is m or m-1, m=floor(N/2). The limiting ratio is Lambda_*=2[A+sqrt(A^2+uP)]. Consequently E(b)/D(b) tends to u/Lambda_* at this protected middle, with absolute O(N^-1) error. The case u=0 retains its actual small finite-N factor a_(m-1); the displayed limit does not replace that factor in any exact source identity. No claim is made here for an independently summed positive starting row b>0, the original shared face torus, or the original Gaussian filling period. Those require additional arguments. title: Original crossing layers: a punctured Casimir norm torus and its parabolic limit
status: Exact local characteristic and norm-torus transport
text: # Original crossing layers: a punctured Casimir norm torus and its parabolic limit 30 October 2026. This is derived from the ACTUAL homogeneous root crossing kernel and its coefficient composition. It solves the local classical transport for every integer power. It does not prove a selected finite-cycle contribution, a kernel norm bound, a knot A-polynomial identification or a filled-volume limit. Throughout N>=3,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N), hbar=2pi i/N. Fix the original outer face variables x,y and put A=x+y,P=xy,f(z)=(z+x)(z+y). The letters P and sigma below are not new quantum parameters. The generic algebra is over characteristic zero with xyA nonzero; all source divisors explicitly recorded below remain excluded. ## 1. The exact original kernels and their composition The [frozen homogeneous theorem](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) gives the original coupon polynomial H_F(x,b,c,y), homogeneous of degree d. For literal polynomials F,G in the SAME pair Casimir, including their full repeated-node data, H_FG(x,b,c,y)=[z^d] H_F(x,b,z,y) H_G(x,z,c,y). (1) Indeed H_G is the matrix of G on input monomials c^j, and H_F is the matrix of F on their output powers z^j. The coefficient condition t_left+i_right=d is exactly matrix multiplication. There is no extra N or mark factor in (1). If F,G are at different original ports, (1) does NOT assert that they commute or share one Casimir. For epsilon=+/-1 the full original crossing is R^epsilon=lambda0^epsilon r_N^epsilon(Omega), lambda0=q^(d^2/2), with the original square-root lift. The normalized homogeneous coefficient at x^k b^i y^l c^t, i+k+l+t=d, is exactly (-1)^(k+l+1) q^[epsilon(kl-(i+1)(t+1))] N/(S_i S_k S_l S_t). (2) No Hermite derivative has been replaced by nodal values. Formula(1) therefore gives R^n with its EXACT lambda0^n for every integer n, including negative n. All original cups, caps, physical endpoint zeros and marked face targets remain those of the homogeneous theorem. Write normalized simplex variables I,K,L,T with sum1 in the leading limit. The principal phase of (2), INCLUDING lambda0, is E_simplex + I Log b+K Log x+L Log y+T Log c +pi i(K+L)+epsilon pi i(KL-IT)+epsilon pi i/2. (3) Here E_simplex=(Lambda(pi I)+Lambda(pi K)+Lambda(pi L) +Lambda(pi T))/pi on its recorded continuation. The finite source is still (2), with i+k+l+t=N-1; its order-one phases and finite offsets are not discarded by using (3) for a principal characteristic. ## 2. Both signs and the actual input/output convention At a regular critical point of (3) put E_I=exp(2pi i epsilon I), and similarly E_K,E_L,E_T. Taking the three constrained differences of derivatives gives E_I^-1=1-b v, E_K=1+x v, E_L=1+y v, E_T^-1=1-c v. For either sign, exp(pi i epsilon)=-1 and the actual linear sign in (3) is exp(pi i)=-1. Thus the same equations hold; no epsilon-dependent integer character has been silently changed. Product E_I E_K E_L E_T=1 implies v[(x+y+b+c)+(xy-bc)v]=0. The v=0 branch has all sine factors zero and is excluded from the regular critical chart. Consequently, with D=P-bc and L0=A+b+c, E_I=D/f(b), E_T=D/f(c), E_K=-(x+b)(x+c)/D, E_L=-(y+b)(y+c)/D. (4) The recorded regular open set is xybc D f(b)f(c)L0 !=0. (5) In particular every E_j-1 remains nonzero. These are exponentiated critical equations, not a claim selecting logarithms or an integration chain. The linear signs and lambda0 are still present in (2),(3). The homogeneous kernel has LEFT output b, RIGHT input c. The actual coefficient target in (1) is degree d, hence the principal gluing law is T_left+I_right=1, NOT zero. Use the momentum r=exp(2pi i I) at the left face; the matching right momentum is r'=exp(-2pi i T). Then the coefficient/pullback advance from left to right is F_+(b,r)=(c,r'), c=[P-r f(b)]/b, r'=f(c)/(P-bc), F_-(b,r)=(c,r'), c=[P-f(b)/r]/b, r'=(P-bc)/f(c). (6) Direct substitution proves F_-=F_+^-1. Thus inverse crossings have opposite canonical transport. If the kernel is viewed instead as a map FROM its input phase point TO its output, the displayed advance is reversed. This is an orientation convention, not a new inverse crossing. The exact R R^-1 coefficient contraction is H_1. For equal signs in two successive layers, (4) and the target give (P-bz)(P-zc)=f(z)^2. (7) For opposite signs they give b=c on the regular chart, as required by (6). A cancelled pair can have a nonisolated middle critical variable; the finite identity is (1), not a claim about a Gaussian saddle of that identity kernel. ## 3. The invariant is the principal original Casimir The original face operator T has principal symbol T(b,r)=-(r+r^-1)+(2-r-r^-1)(A/b+P/b^2). Since the actual Casimir is Omega=-T, its symbol is sigma=2+[(r-1)^2/r] f(b)/b^2. Insert r=(P-bz)/f(b) (or its reciprocal for the inverse sign): sigma=2+(b+z+A)^2/(P-bz). (8) This is the actual conserved pair Casimir, not a chosen first integral of an unrelated recurrence. On (7), putting d1=P-bz,d2=P-zc and f=f(z), the relation d1d2=f^2 gives (b+z+A)^2/d1=(f-d1)^2/(z^2d1) =(d1+d2-2f)/z^2 =(z+c+A)^2/d2. Hence sigma is preserved, and (7) becomes EXACTLY c=-sigma z-b-2A. (9) Conversely (8),(9) imply (7) wherever the recorded units hold. Thus the full local layer sequence obeys b_(j+1)+sigma b_j+b_(j-1)+2A=0. Here and in (10), (b,z) denotes the POSITIVE companion chart on the common phase space: z=[P-r f(b)]/b. A negative crossing acts by the inverse of this map, rather than silently reusing its actual negative-layer right neighbor as that positive companion coordinate. All integer powers are powers of the one affine matrix M_sigma=[[0,1,0],[-1,-sigma,-2A],[0,0,1]], (b_j,b_(j+1),1)^t=M_sigma^j(b_0,b_1,1)^t. (10) Its determinant is1, so this includes negative powers. It is one formula for arbitrary fixed signed twist lengths, not a recurrence established by checking finitely many powers. ## 4. Explicit norm-one coordinate and the source punctures The fixed-Casimir conic is b^2+z^2+sigma bz+2A(b+z)+A^2-(sigma-2)P=0. (11) Assume sigma^2!=4 and C0=(sigma-2)[P-A^2/(sigma+2)] !=0. Put u=b+2A/(sigma+2), v=z+2A/(sigma+2), lambda^2+sigma lambda+1=0. Then (u-lambda v)(u-lambda^-1 v)=C0. (12) The involution is lambda<->lambda^-1. The conic is a torsor for the norm-one group of this quadratic spectral algebra, and the actual map (9) multiplies the first factor by lambda and the second by lambda^-1. In particular it is diagonal after this spectral cover. There is even an explicit norm trivialization: w=((lambda+1)/(lambda-1))*(x+lambda y), Norm(w)=C0, a=(u-lambda v)/w, Norm(a)=1, a ->lambda a. (13) To verify the norm, use Norm((lambda+1)/(lambda-1))=-(sigma-2)/(sigma+2) and Norm(x+lambda y)=x^2-sigma xy+y^2. Both factors are units under the stated generic hypotheses. The inverse crossing gives a->lambda^-1 a in the same phase-space convention (6). Thus arbitrary signed powers are explicit multiplication by lambda^n. The reference point a=1 is b=-x,z=-y. It lies on EVERY conic, but is an EXCLUDED SOURCE POINT: P-bz=0, f(b)=f(z)=0. Thus (13) is an algebraic norm trivialization; it does not make the actual source regular at its reference point. On the spectral cover, u=[lambda bar(w)/a-lambda^-1 w a]/(lambda-lambda^-1), v=[bar(w)/a-w a]/(lambda-lambda^-1). The regular SOURCE STATIONARY chart is the complement of (5) after this substitution. These are divisors of that classical critical chart, not new poles of the finite homogeneous polynomial H_R. In particular the possibly coincident basepoints b,z=(-x,-y),(-y,-x) have norm coordinates 1 and (y+lambda x)/(x+lambda y). Their adjacent lambda and lambda^-1 translates give the f(b) and f(z) zeros. The b=0,z=0 divisors are retained too. A word analyzed in this regular critical chart must retain the preimages of these divisors under ALL its intermediate powers. Transport of the completed algebraic conic is not permission to move the original source contour through them. ## 5. Exact Darboux factor and existing quantum Gaussian For this coordinate calculation always use the POSITIVE companion z=[P-r f(b)]/b as a rational coordinate on the common phase space, regardless of the sign of the next actual crossing. Then, for fixed x,y, the actual cotangent two-form is omega=dLog r wedge dLog b=db wedge dz/(P-bz). Let F be the left side of (11) and eta=u-lambda v. Then d sigma=(F_b db+F_z dz)/(P-bz), lambda F_b+F_z=(lambda-lambda^-1)eta, d sigma=-(lambda-lambda^-1)dLog lambda. These imply, with NO factor2 or sign ambiguity, omega=dLog lambda wedge dLog eta =dLog lambda wedge dLog a. (14) The scalar w depends only on lambda at fixed x,y and thus contributes zero to the wedge. With the explicit convention i_X omega=-dH, H=(Log lambda)^2/2 generates the displayed pullback advance a->lambda a. This agrees with (6); the opposite input-to-output interpretation reverses that map. This recovers an explicit classical coordinate for the EXISTING full-Hermite Gaussian functional calculus, rather than replacing it. The [existing Gaussian theorem](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md), section1, proves R^(2P)=q^(P d^2/2) exp[P K(Omega)/hbar], where K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2 is analytic off[2,infinity) with its removable value at sigma=-2. The same node and derivative check gives for every integer n R^n=q^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega)/(2hbar)]. (15) Indeed at c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), with x_j=pi i(2j+1)/N, K(c_j)=(x_j-pi i)^2, and the actual normalized crossing value is nu_j=exp[pi i(j^2-dj)/N]. This uses (-1)^j=exp(-pi i j), the unwrapped sign required by the original derivative. The derivative of the exponential at the node is the literal multiplier -n(d-2j)/[2(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))]; paired nodes retain this derivative, and the odd simple node needs no quotient0/0. Values and derivatives therefore agree in the full Casimir quotient. Negative n are allowed because all crossing eigenvalues are units. On the classical spectral cover K=(Log lambda)^2, so (14),(15) give the same Hamiltonian, with the recorded scalar factors unchanged. The finite ratio nu_(j+1)/nu_j=-q^(2j+2) has principal limit lambda=-exp(2pi i j/N), a root of lambda^2+sigma lambda+1=0. Its extra finite q shift is not dropped from (15) or from the kernels. Neither the unit-modulus node values nor the torus action bounds the full quantum operator or its shared-face coefficient. ## 6. The two endpoint fibers are different At sigma=-2, with A!=0, the original conic is the reduced parabola (b-z)^2+2A(b+z)+A^2+4P=0. Put t=b-z. Then the actual affine map gives t->t+2A, and b=-[(t-A)^2+4P]/(4A), z=-[(t+A)^2+4P]/(4A). The affine matrix M_-2 satisfies (M_-2-I)^3=0, and its square is nonzero when A!=0. Thus M_-2^n=I+n(M_-2-I)+n(n-1)(M_-2-I)^2/2 (16) for EVERY integer n. This is concrete nilpotent/unipotent classical transport at the parabolic Casimir, with quadratic face dependence. It does not imply polynomial growth of an original quantum period. At sigma=+2 the SCHEME (11) is the nonreduced double line (b+z+A)^2=0. Its reduced line has z=-b-A and the map is the involution (b,z)->(z,b). The full affine matrix retains its Jordan data: (M_2+I)^2(M_2-I)=0. Explicitly, if e=b+z+A with e^2=0, then M_2^2(b,z)=(b-2e,z+2e). Thus the reduction loses a real normal transport even though it is an involution on ordinary points. Do not call this fiber the same additive torsor as sigma=-2, and do not replace the double-line scheme by its reduction when retaining normal data. The regular one-layer critical chart excludes the reduced line because L0=0. This is a degeneration of the closure. For sigma^2!=4 but C0=0, (12) is a pair of lines rather than a norm-one torsor. Formula(10) still gives exact algebraic transport. The generic torus theorem does not assert that this reducible fiber is nonsingular. ## 7. Existing repository scope and the remaining source question The repository already has exact full-Hermite Gaussian powers in [the Gaussian source note](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md) and its Fourier-Hermite source dependencies. It also has [the uniform group-relator note](uniform_twist_relator_source.md), sections1--2: a quadratic norm group for the TWIST-KNOT GROUP RELATOR w^k, explicitly not the original quantum crossing-source torsor. The [intrinsic quantum-A norm-torsor](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) construction is a different cyclic quantum-A norm group. None of those statements is being reproved or relabeled as this local theorem. A focused search of the current notes found no displayed source-face conic (11) or the coefficient-layer recurrence (9). The additional interface here is the explicit original R-layer critical relation, its preserved ACTUAL pair Casimir, signed inverse conventions, norm coordinate, source punctures, and two distinct parabolic endpoint schemes. It holds at a local port independently of bridge width. Whole networks still require their original shared face targets, exterior phases and mark. No eliminated knot variety, period contribution, or volume estimate follows just from this algebraic linearization. No literature novelty claim is made. Coverage only: [Goldman, The complex-symplectic geometry of SL(2,C)-characters over surfaces](https://math.umd.edu/~wmg/csymp.pdf), PDF dated2 September2003, Proposition2.6.1 and sections2.6.1--2.6.2, already relates Dehn twists to Hamiltonian trace flows and distinguishes generic multiplicative from noncentral parabolic additive orbits. The [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304307v2) is version2, 3 October2003. Those statements are coverage context, not inputs to this proof. The present conic has not thereby been identified with that surface character variety; multiplicative/additive twist dynamics is not being claimed as new in itself. ## 8. Verification scope The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_crossing_casimir_torus.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_crossing_casimir_torus_results.json), checks 14 symbolic identities, 450 signed-integer torus steps, 866 inverse-chart checks, 20 excluded reference points and 180 parabolic or reduced-endpoint steps. It independently compares 28 original integer crossing powers, including identity cases, on 3,024 physical entries and 966 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros. Twelve mixed inverse compositions, 70 exact Gaussian node VALUES and 14 adjacent spectral ratios retain all displayed scalar phases. The full-Hermite Gaussian DERIVATIVE assertion is the analytical node-and-derivative proof in section5 and its existing source theorem; these 70 value checks are not advertised as an independent numerical derivative audit. The crossing-Casimir torsor does not determine a quantum norm, a selected finite-cycle contribution or a long-filled volume estimate.

title: Original crossing-circle sources and the complete twist-filling packet
text: # Original crossing-circle sources and the complete twist-filling packet 29 October 2026. A crossing-circle source can be calculated from the original mixed universal crossings and pivotal trace. Its complete-color operator is generally noninvertible and is nilpotent at even levels. Therefore a fixed N-colored augmented-link scalar is not, by itself, an all-port filling state for the original knot. The constructive replacement is the COMPLETE auxiliary-color packet. Its N loop operators form a polynomial basis including all confluent Casimir jets. The explicit Fourier--Hermite kernel then reconstructs each original full-twist block at polynomial coefficient cost. This gives an exact arbitrary-width source formula over mixed-color augmented diagrams, with the original marked cut unchanged. It does not prove a nonzero geometric coefficient at a fully augmented base, or transport such a coefficient through long fillings. Those require the selected mixed-color base period, not just its operator basis or a positive geometric reference chain. ## 1. The literal encircling operator Put N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^-1. The two physical targets are the original complete V_d heads. Their Casimir is Omega=F12 Ecal12+q K12+q^-1 K12^-1, Ecal=rho^2 E. For 1<=j<=N let A_j be the ordinary j-dimensional highest-weight auxiliary module, with H weights j-1-2a, 0<=a<j. Use the literal mixed universal R, including q^(H tensor H/2), and close the auxiliary strand with g_j=K_j^(1-N). There is NO new 1/j or 1/N in this auxiliary trace. The main modified/marked source stays where it was. Define L_j on the two physical targets by the actual block-braiding monodromy. With the auxiliary strand initially in position3 this is the typed braid [2,1,1,2], followed by the original pivotal trace of strand3. Intermediate crossings use their actual changing strand dimensions. Write T_n(z)=2cos(n theta) and U_n(z/2)=sin((n+1)theta)/sin(theta) when z=2cos(theta). These are polynomial conventions: T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1), U_0=1,U_1=z,U_(n+1)=zU_n-U_(n-1). Then the exact all-input circle identity is L_j=(-1)^(j-1) U_(j-1)(Omega/2). (1) The notation U_n(Omega/2) means the displayed recurrence U_1=Omega. In particular L_1=I and L_2=-Omega. ### Independent proof, including the root specialization First work at generic q with ordinary finite highest-weight modules and the standard pivotal trace K_j. Block braiding is obtained by the actual coproduct identities of the finite universal R, proved coefficientwise in the [ordinary-color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md). The resulting closed loop is a Hopf intertwiner: its cups/caps use the standard pivot and every mixed crossing is the actual intertwiner. No division by a quantum dimension enters this statement. On a target highest vector of H weight n, choose the block-braiding order in which the first nilpotent factor acts by target E. It annihilates that vector. In the return crossing any positive target F power cannot contribute to its highest coefficient. Thus only the two full Cartan factors contribute to that coefficient, giving Tr_(A_j)(K_j q^(n H_j)) =sum_(a=0)^(j-1) q^[(n+1)(j-1-2a)] =U_(j-1)((q^(n+1)+q^(-n-1))/2). (2) For a generic pair V_d tensor V_d the explicit highest vectors have weights n=2d,2d-2,...,0. Their descendants have total dimension N^2 and distinct Casimir values. Therefore (2) proves the FULL matrix identity U_(j-1)(Omega/2), not merely its eigenvalues at a root. All mixed R denominators are [h]!, h<=j-1<=N-1, and target factorial frame denominators have indices at most d. They are nonzero at q_N. The matrix identity consequently specializes regularly, including the actual nilpotent/Jordan coefficients at colliding Casimirs. At the root the ACTUAL auxiliary pivot satisfies K_j^(1-N)=(-1)^(j-1)K_j, since every H_j weight has parity j-1. This proves (1) with the literal original pivot and full Cartan normalization. This root specialization is not a claim about generic-q derivatives of the ADO pivotal source, for which K^(1-N) must remain literal. ## 2. The full pair relation and the complete-color circle On the two original complete targets, P_N(Omega)=0, P_N(z)=T_N(z)+2. (3) To check (3) without semisimplification, multiply the N quantum-shifted factors of FEcal=Omega-qK-q^-1K^-1. Their product is F^N Ecal^N=0. The elementary root product evaluates it as T_N(Omega)+K^N+K^-N. For two complete heads K12^N=1, giving (3). The degree-d physical block is the actual irreducible tridiagonal Jacobi matrix with nonzero adjacent entries. Its first coordinate is cyclic, so its minimal polynomial has degree N and is exactly P_N. Equation (1) at j=N is equivalently L_N=(-1)^d T_N'(Omega)/N. (4) It annihilates the highest pair vector |0,0>, and the ACTUAL cup p: L_N|0,0>=0, L_N p=0. (5) For the first identity use its Casimir c_0=q+q^-1 and U_d(c_0/2)=0. The same value holds on p. Alternatively its literal highest trace is q^(d^2)sum_(a=0)^d Q^a=0, retaining the Cartan and pivot. For even N, T_N+2=T_(N/2)^2. Hence (3)--(4) give L_N^2=0. (6) The operator is nonzero on the degree-d block: P_N there has actual double Jordan nodes and (4) has a nonzero first derivative at each. For odd N there is a single simple node -2; all other nodes are double. There is an exact projector P_St onto that simple total Steinberg channel, with L_N^2=N^2 P_St, L_N^3=N L_N^2. (7) The nilpotent part on the double channels is retained in (7). These are full matrix statements, not an odd-level semisimple replacement for the source. The original tame Hermite source plane makes the missing normal information especially concrete. In [its actual normalization](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md), (Omega-c_0)t=theta p, theta=(-1)^N rho^2, mp=1, mt=0, ell p=0, ell t=1. At c_0 the derivative in (4) is (-1)^d N/[2sin^2(pi/N)]. Therefore L_N t=2N p. (8) Its coefficient is polynomial, but (8) is a nonzero NORMAL source. An ordinary positive scalar replacing L_N would lose this datum. In particular no all-input local operator S_p can satisfy R12^(2p)=S_p L_N, because the left side is invertible on |0,0> and the right side vanishes there. A scalar at fixed complete crossing-circle color therefore cannot be inverted into every original filling port. This does not say that a complete augmented-link scalar is zero, or that its geometric saddle cannot survive; the original modified source can detect nilpotent channels after the surrounding tangle. ## 3. The complete crossing-circle filling packet The N polynomials L_1,...,L_N have successive degrees0,...,d and nonzero leading coefficients. They are a basis of C[z]/(P_N). The original complete crossing has the already proved ALL-INPUT form R12=kappa r_N(Omega), r_N(c_k)=nu_k=(-1)^k q^[k(k+1)], c_k=q^(2k+1)+q^(-2k-1), r_N'(c_k)/nu_k=-(d-2k)/[2(q^(2k+1)-q^(-2k-1))] (9) at each double node. At the odd simple node only its value is required. The paired node k'=d-k has the same nu, so (9) is well-defined as a Hermite specification. All original first-normal coefficients are part of this formula. For every integer p the [explicit Fourier--Hermite filling kernel](actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md) constructs coefficients a_(p,j) such that R12^(2p)=kappa^(2p) sum_(j=1)^N a_(p,j) L_j, (10) sum_j |a_(p,j)| <= 2N(1+|p|). (11) The kernel interpolates the full Hermite data of r_N^(2p) modulo P_N; it is not an interpolation of repeated eigenvalues without their derivatives. Equation (1) identifies every term of that polynomial kernel with a literal mixed-color crossing circle. Consequently (10) is an original tensor/source identity, not an assumed surgery formula or a semisimple Kirby-color substitution. ## 4. Arbitrary-width original-source filling identity Take any original marked braid/plat diagram with a fixed collection of disjoint, specified two-strand full-twist boxes. Write their powers as R_i^(2p_i), keeping all other signed crossings, turns, pivots and the original marked cut literally. An odd twist box may retain its one original half twist and apply (10) only to the even remainder. At a dual-oriented port transport the actual whole identity by its given rigid duality; no independent auxiliary cut is introduced. Remove the full twists and insert a crossing circle in each box. For colors j_i, let A_N(j_1,...,j_s) be that mixed-color diagram's literal contraction: physical heads still have complete color N, each new circle uses its ordinary auxiliary module and pivot from Section1, and the main modified/marked source is unchanged. Then K_N=chi_N product_i kappa^(2p_i) sum_(j_1,...,j_s) product_i a_(p_i,j_i) A_N(j_1,...,j_s). (12) The displayed chi_N is the original filled-diagram peripheral and framing line. It has not been replaced by a guessed normalization of the augmented diagram. If a separately normalized augmented-link invariant is used, its precise ratio to this literal A_N must first be calculated. No new 1/N or 1/j average is attached to the circles. Proof: tensor (10) with all spectators, substitute it at each box, expand finitely, and apply the unchanged original functional. Each auxiliary trace in (1) is exactly the local box operator. This proves (12) at arbitrary braid width, for either sign of p_i and at every N, with all Casimir normal coefficients retained. For fixed s the coefficient l1 norm is at most product_i 2N(1+|p_i|). (13) It is polynomial for fixed filling slopes, even if they are chosen large; more generally it is exp(o(N)) when sum_i log(1+|p_i|)=o(N). This is a quantified original-source filling map. Taking absolute values in (12) only gives an augmented-family envelope, not the smaller volume of the filled knot. The oscillatory kernel and selected filling saddle still matter. The auxiliary j<N terms in (12) are genuine ordinary modules with their literal traces. One must NOT identify them with closed N-dimensional ADO components at ordinary meridian points merely by the one-component quotient lemma: that lemma does not apply to separate closed crossing-circle components. The finite all-input identity (1) is the comparison used here. ## 5. Consequence for a fully augmented geometric-survival strategy The actual algebraic filling port and its normal data are now explicit. It is possible to pose the survival problem for a fully augmented diagram with arbitrarily many twist regions, using its full original mixed-color packet and (12). This is broader input than a single twist family and does not replace the knot invariant by an AK state. What is NOT proved is that this mixed-color base has a positive original relative cycle with nonzero geometric coefficient, uniformly in the cusp-color corridor required by long filling. The positive constrained-lens reference chart does not establish that source identification. Nor does a fixed-color augmented scalar plus (11) supply it, because (5)--(8) exhibit its lost normal information. Even given such a base, its geometric coefficient must be transported through the actual oscillatory filling kernel, including its boundary and confluent channels. No Stokes constancy or noncancellation theorem is inferred just from the polynomial coefficient cost (13). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.py) constructs mixed universal R matrices with their full half-Cartan, the typed four-crossing loop, original pivotal traces, complete pair Casimirs and actual positive/negative twist matrices. It compares all input columns, nilpotent parities and original source normals.

title: Every actual root braid period has a source-equivalent Euler/Gaussian completion
text: # Every actual root braid period has a source-equivalent Euler/Gaussian completion 27 October 2026. The original checked crossing admits an explicit Euler/Gaussian completion whose error raises the TOTAL INTEGER head degree by N. On b strands all positive multiples-of-N errors form a source-null ideal with bth power zero. Consequently every SIGNED braid word in the completed generators and their literal inverses has exactly the original full one-cut pivotal matrix. This holds at every root and as the whole original meridian family. The bounded nilpotence concerns the error between two realizations, not the full braid action. The completed crossings need not obey the braid relation as matrices. They obey it modulo the proved source-null ideal, and their original closed scalar is exactly the original knot invariant. No quantum factorial model is substituted on asymptotic grounds and no numerical peripheral factor is chosen afterward. The construction uses the existing original root R-matrices and [actual Borel fusion](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md). It removes a specific finite-support wall for CLOSED braid periods. It does not yet prove their hyperbolic growth, nor preserve arbitrary inserted currents or moving-q normal jets. ## 1. The original positive crossing coefficient in the relative algebra Fix Q=q^2 of exact order N>=2 and write F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The nilpotent balanced heads have F e_a=(1-Q^(a+1))e_(a+1), K e_a=xQ^-a e_a. Let A_0=<H,f | H^N=1,Hf=Q^-1fH,f^N=0> with its usual right idempotents e_k. For two equal colors, the actual triangular fusion is C(f^a e_k)=f_total^a(e_0 tensor e_k). Its physical kernel is C_(u,v;a,k)=x^(u-a) F_a F_v/[F_(a-u)F_k] if 0<=u<=a, v=k+a-u<N; otherwise zero. (1) Retain the original common Cartan scalar kappa=R_(00,00). It can equally be recorded in its prescribed external Hom/normalization line; it is not reset in this calculation. The positive crossing R commutes with the actual diagonal Borel action, so C^-1 R C is RIGHT multiplication by a unique element a_R. That coefficient is exactly a_R=kappa sum_(a,k>=0,a+k<N) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2) x^(-a-2k) f^a e_k/F_a. (2) Here all a,k lie in 0,...,N-1. Formula (2) is an all-level coefficient identity for the actual R, not its semiclassical symbol. To prove it, apply the word to the algebra unit. Its physical seed is e_0 tensor ones, and the literal original crossing has R(e_0 tensor e_j)=kappa x^-j e_j tensor e_0. For total degree n<N, invert the upper-triangular block (1) on this vector. If its relative coefficients are h_a on f^a e_(n-a), put d_a=F_a h_a/[x^a F_(n-a)]. The equations are sum_(a=u)^n d_a/F_(a-u)=delta_(u,n) x^(-2n). Their reversed sequence is the inverse Euler series: d_a equals x^(-2n) times (-1)^(n-a)Q^((n-a)(n-a-1)/2)/F_(n-a). Undoing the change gives precisely (2), with k=n-a. There is no component of degree n>=N because the physical vector above has none and fusion preserves the total unwrapped degree a+k. ## 2. The completion is a genuine Euler times a marked Gaussian Define U_x(f)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)x^-a f^a/F_a, D_x(H)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)x^(-2k)e_k, a_tilde=kappa U_x(f)D_x(H), R_tilde=C R_(a_tilde) C^-1. (3) The Euler factor has constant term one and nilpotent argument. Every Gaussian entry is nonzero. Thus (3) is an invertible actual finite matrix, with no support projector or division by an unknown period. Its negative crossing is its LITERAL inverse, R_tilde^-1=C R_(kappa^-1 D_x^-1 U_x^-1) C^-1. Right multiplication reverses composition, so the order of these factors is intentional. In (2), a_R is precisely the NONWRAPPED part of (3); the missing terms are f^a e_k with a+k>=N. This formula also has a local unequal-color version. For a checked crossing from colors (x_1,x_2) to (x_2,x_1), use input fusion C_in and output fusion C_out. Then its relative coefficient is a_R=kappa sum_(a+k<N) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)x_1^-a(x_1x_2)^-k f^a e_k/F_a, and its completion is obtained by dropping a+k<N, namely kappa U_(x_1)(f)D_(x_1x_2)(H). The same triangular inversion applies, replacing its top right side by (x_1x_2)^-n. The equal-color case already covers every ordinary knot braid. At the complete color x=-q^-1, the right Euler argument in (3) is x^-1 f=Qz for z=xf. Thus this is exactly u_N(Qz), the Euler orientation appearing in the correctly transported primitive source sector of [the whole-word gauge theorem](whole_word_primitive_source_gauge.md). That observation identifies the actual local factor, without equating the full invariant with a single Fourier sector. The finite Gaussian is marked, not a periodically extended scalar Gaussian: its unwrapped entries obey d_(k+N)=-x^(-2N)d_k. For example its exact coefficient-algebra conjugation contains D_x f D_x^-1=-x^-2 fH^-1 +Q^-1 x^-2(1+x^(2N))f e_(N-1). (4) The second term is the original wrap correction. A numerical factor such as its complete value two has not been silently erased. Below we prove which closed-source operations kill its positive weight; outside that algebra (4) must retain the entire factor. ## 3. Every wrapped error raises physical integer degree by N Let D_b=sum_i J_i be the ordinary INTEGER head degree, J_i e_a=a e_a. Fusion preserves this degree: (1) has u+v=a+k as an equality of integers, not modulo N. Consider right multiplication by a wrapped path f^a e_k, a+k>=N. On a basis input f^c e_j it is nonzero only when j=k+a modulo N and c+a<N. Its output is f^(c+a)e_k. Therefore output degree-input degree =(c+a+k)-(c+j)=N. (5) No additional wrap can occur because 0<=a,k<N. Conjugating by C or by the two color versions of C preserves (5). In particular Delta=R_tilde-R raises total integer degree exactly N. The original R and R^-1 preserve integer degree exactly. Locally the two-head degree range is 0,...,2N-2, so Delta R^-1 Delta=0, R_tilde^-1=R^-1-R^-1 Delta R^-1. (6) Thus the negative completion also differs from the original inverse only by an operator of degree +N. The explicit inverse in (6) agrees with the inverse of the Euler/Gaussian factors in (3). ## 4. A level-uniform nilpotent error ideal for every braid index On b heads let F_b be the algebra of operators having only degree changes 0,N,2N,..., and let n_b be the subspace with only strictly positive such changes. It is a two-sided ideal of F_b. Since all physical degrees lie between zero and b(N-1), n_b^b=0. (7) More precisely its power floor(b(N-1)/N)+1 vanishes. The degree-zero projection pi_0 is an algebra homomorphism, with kernel n_b. It splits by embedding the degree-preserving operators themselves. On unit groups its kernel is 1+n_b; every fiber over a prescribed degree-zero unit is a torsor under that unipotent group. Inversion is the finite series in n_b, and [1+n_b^r,1+n_b^s] lies in 1+n_b^(r+s). Hence its nilpotence class is at most b-1, independently of N. This is a bounded error transport, not a nilpotence assertion for the whole actual braid group or its degree-zero semisimple sector. Embed (3) and (6) at every crossing of an arbitrary SIGNED braid word beta. Each completed factor belongs to F_b and has original degree-zero part. Consequently W_tilde(beta)-W(beta) belongs to n_b, (8) pi_0(W_tilde(beta))=W(beta). This includes arbitrarily long words; the nilpotence bound in (7) depends on braid index, not crossing number or level. The completed generators satisfy every actual braid relation MODULO n_b. They need not satisfy the braid relation as matrices: the exact audit finds nonzero positive-weight braid defects. No unrestricted new braided tensor functor is claimed. ## 5. The original full first-cut matrix kills the ideal Use the actual pivotal closure on all heads except the first, with the original diagonal pivots g_i=K_i^(1-N).
