At odd N retain the single c_*=-2 node with its value projector P_*. The ACTUAL normalized crossing data are r_N(c_a)=nu_a=(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], gamma_a=r_N'(c_a)/r_N(c_a) =-(N-h)/[2(q^h-q^(-h))]. (5) Thus r_N^n has data nu_a^n and n gamma_a nu_a^n for every integer n; negative powers are legitimate because the values are units. These are full Hermite data, not an eigenvalue-only interpolation. For a polynomial H let |H|_coef replace each coefficient by its absolute value. Define the positive polynomial E_n=sum_a (|H_(P_a)|_coef+|n gamma_a| |H_(Q_a)|_coef) +[odd N: |H_(P_*)|_coef]. (6) For n!=0, |H_(R^n)|_coef<=E_n. The unit lambda0^n does not affect this inequality. The complete coupon is L_N=(-1)^(N-1)U_(N-1)(Omega/2). Its paired values vanish, while |L_N'(c_a)|=N/[2sin^2(pi h/N)], |L_N'(c_a)|/|gamma_a| =2N/[(N-h)sin(pi h/N)] <= N^2. (7) Indeed sin(pi h/N)>=2min(h,N-h)/N. If h<=N/2 the ratio is at most N^2/[h(N-h)]<=N^2; if h>=N/2 it is at most N^2/(N-h)^2<=N^2. At the odd simple node L_N(-2)=N. The triangle inequality, |n|>=1, and the independently proved nonnegative coefficients of H_(L_N) give the EXACT coefficientwise comparison H_(L_N) <= N^2 E_n. (8) This comparison is local, but its consequence retains the full shared source constraint. On any certified original connected fixed flat plat with R boxes and nonzero integers n_e, multiply (8) and extract the original marked target: [target] prod_e E_(n_e) >=N^(-2R) [target] prod_e H_(L_N). (9) The common original prefactor is polynomial in N and every crossing scalar has modulus1. The right side has the augmented complete-volume rate, by the [complete augmented-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) with zero half twists. Every positive-radius Cauchy bound for the left side is at least that coefficient, so optimizing the radii cannot remove this obstruction. In particular this specific phase-blind Hermite strategy cannot yield any upper exponential rate strictly below the augmented volume, even for arbitrarily large fixed powers. When a hyperbolic nontrivial filling with smaller volume is under consideration, the [representation-volume strictness theorem](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) identifies the needed strict geometric decrease. Inequality (9) shows why a successful direct spectral proof must retain cancellation beyond (6). It does not contradict a phase-preserving bound, the volume conjecture, or a source estimate using different structure. The case n=0 is excluded: its nilpotent derivative weight vanishes. ## 3. The exact Gaussian retains the missing phases The existing [Gaussian filling theorem](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md), section1, proves even powers using full Hermite functional calculus. The same value-and-derivative argument gives every integer n: hbar=2pi i/N, K(z)=arccosh(-z/2)^2, R^n=q^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega)/(2hbar)]. (10) K is analytic on C minus[2,infinity), with its removable value at -2. The fractional q power uses the literal original Log q. At a paired node set phi=pi(2a+1)/N and s=d-2a. Then K(c_a)=-pi^2s^2/N^2, q^[(d^2+s^2)/4]=lambda0(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], K'(c_a)=-pi s/[Nsin(phi)], [n/(2hbar)]K'(c_a)=-ns/[4i sin(phi)]=n gamma_a. Thus (10) matches every derivative as well as every value. The odd simple node needs only its value. The unwrapped sign in the value formula is (-1)^a=exp(-pi i a); resetting it to the opposite analytic character would change the derivative. Full Hermite uniqueness proves (10), including n<0. This is not a generic-q identity or a unitary diagonalization. The cut at2, the nodes approaching it, all source punctures and the noncommuting neighboring Casimirs remain relevant to a global estimate. ## Validation and remaining scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_direct_long_power_source.py) compares homogeneous compositions with independently built original R matrices, including wrong-unwrapped totals and both signs. It also constructs the canonical Hermite basis and checks the coefficientwise comparison and Gaussian value/derivative data at both parities. [Results](../experiments/actual_direct_long_power_source_results.json) record the finite checks; they do not serve as a proof of an asymptotic. The finite audit checks the original powers, physical entries, wrong-total zeros, Hermite data, Gaussian values and derivatives. The phase-blind envelope does not imply a phase-preserving global rate or a selected-cycle contribution.

title: Actual divided Ward closure keeps a whole Green cap current
text: # Actual divided Ward closure keeps a whole Green cap current Research proof, 27 October 2026. Actual pivotal closure gives a global current map for every finite weighted braid word and every integral divided generator. The map retains the actual coupling moments, the marked cut row, and the whole ordinary/frozen pivot adapter. Its endpoint is an explicit inserted current, rather than an inference from scalarity of the unweighted knot matrix. This does not identify the resulting finite current with the two internal geometric Gaussian currents. In particular the [memory-Borel wall](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md) is not declared to be a quantum-group coproduct generator. The high-color statements also do not identify its whole normal jets with those of the original low color; only the previously proved root scalar comparison may be used for that purpose. ## 1. The actual divided coproduct and adjoint Use the generic integral Weyl family and the conventions Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, K E K^(-1)=Q E, K F K^(-1)=Q^(-1) F, S(E)=-E K^(-1), S(F)=-K F, Q=q^2. Put E^(a)=E^a/[a]_q! and F^(a)=F^a/[a]_q!. Their matrices are integral Gaussian matrices on every actual integral color. They are retained before root specialization. Direct expansion of the two q-commuting summands gives Delta E^(n)=sum_(k=0)^n q^(k(n-k)) E^(n-k) tensor E^(k) K^(n-k), Delta F^(n)=sum_(k=0)^n q^(-k(n-k)) K^(-k) F^(n-k) tensor F^(k). (1.1) For example AB=Q BA for A=E tensor K, B=1 tensor E. The coefficient of B^k A^(n-k) is the ordinary Q-Gaussian; dividing by [n]_q! changes it to q^(k(n-k)). This proves (1.1) without a root-level division. Iteration retains every multiindex of total size n, including mixed ordinary/divided terms. The adjoint on matrices is A_h(C)=sum h_1 C S(h_2). In particular A_(E^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(-k(n-1)) E^(n-k) C E^(k) K^(-n), A_(F^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(k(n-1)) F^(n-k) K^(-k) C K^k F^(k). (1.2) The antipode factors in (1.2) follow by multiplying S(E)=-E K^(-1) and S(F)=-KF. At n=N the terms 1<=k<N are essential. Replacing (1.2) by a plain commutator with the individual divided matrix loses them, even when that individual matrix vanishes on a small color. Write D_h=A_h-epsilon(h)I. All matrices in (1.1)--(1.2) and their actual normal coefficients are regular on the integral color lattice. Full Cartan, framing and peripheral scalar factors remain part of every operator below. ## 2. An explicit integral current for every actual crossing Write either signed actual checked crossing, with its literal unwrapped transfer, as R_t(w)=sum_(k>=0) w^k R_(t,k), R_t(1)=R_t. The sum is finite. The color list is switched after the crossing; rho_in and rho_out denote its actual iterated coproduct matrices. For any integral h define Xi_(h,t,k)=rho_out(h) R_(t,k)-R_(t,k) rho_in(h), J_(h,t)(w)=sum_(k>=1) (1+w+...+w^(k-1)) Xi_(h,t,k). Actual R intertwining says sum_k Xi_(h,t,k)=0. Therefore rho_out(h)R_t(w)-R_t(w)rho_in(h) =(w-1)J_(h,t)(w). (2.1) This is an explicit polynomial division by w-1. It neither divides by [N]_q! nor chooses a root primitive. Hence it applies directly to h=E^(N),F^(N) with (1.1), to both crossing signs, and to every whole normal jet. Every transfer endpoint is present. For h=E,F it is the generating transform of the literal [crossing-transfer currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md). The same construction applies to a cut or component-position weight w^J: its value at w=1 is the identity intertwiner. For a link retain one such initial-position weight per component. Let W(w)=R_m(w_m)...R_1(w_1), including any position weights as additional factors. All actual tensor spectators are included in rho_t(h). The elementary telescoping identity gives Xi_h(W)=sum_t (w_t-1) W_>t J_(h,t)(w_t) W_<t. (2.2) To pass to the true Hopf adjoint use the exact identity D_h(W)=sum_(h) Xi_(h_1)(W) rho_0(S h_2). Thus (2.2) gives specified whole matrix currents B_(h,t) with D_h(W)=sum_t (w_t-1) B_(h,t)(w), B_(h,t)=sum_(h) W_>t J_(h_1,t)(w_t) W_<t rho_0(S h_2). (2.3) All coproduct and antipode factors occur in their displayed order. Equation (2.3) is a global finite-word current identity. It uses actual matrices, rather than assigning a coproduct to the memory Cartan or to a projected highest-spin corner. ## 3. The ordinary pivotal cap and its marked source row For an actual closed tensor factor let P_o(C)=Tr_W[(I tensor K_W)C]. This is an exact intertwiner of the Hopf adjoints on ALL matrices: P_o D_h=D_h P_o. (3.1) For E the two internal terms cancel because K_W^(-1)K_W=I; for F they cancel because K_W F_W K_W^(-1)=Q^(-1)F_W. K is immediate by cyclicity. The identities extend to products; alternatively (1.1)--(1.2) give a direct integral check for every divided generator. Apply the generic identity first and then specialize its regular matrices. This is the actual divided-cap argument of [the marked-edge note](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md), now applied to the coupled currents (2.3). Let Phi_A(C)=Tr(A C) be the original cut row, allowing its whole q-dependent source, pivot and normalization. Its exact dual row is D_h^vee(A)=sum_(h) rho(S h_2) A rho(h_1) -epsilon(h)A. Cyclicity, not invariance of A, gives Phi_A(D_h C)=Tr[D_h^vee(A) C]. (3.2) Consequently pivotal closure of (2.3) is the source-sensitive map Tr[D_h^vee(A) P_o W] =sum_t(w_t-1) Phi_A(P_o B_(h,t)). (3.3) The original coherent cut, uniform interval cut and normalized trace are distinct A's in (3.2)--(3.3). They may not be substituted for each other on the wall. In particular their values on the normalized Frobenius wall E_(N,0) remain respectively 2^(-N), 1/(N+1), and zero. ## 4. Actual Green moments leave a finite difference of the moment Put E_t=w_t partial_(w_t) and let p be any actual index-moment polynomial. Define its forward finite difference by Delta_t p(x)=p(x+e_t)-p(x). Apply p(E) to (3.3) and only then put every w=1. The exact product rule p(E)(w_t f)=w_t p(E+e_t)f proves Tr[D_h^vee(A) P_o p(E)W]_(w=1) =sum_t Phi_A[P_o (Delta_t p)(E) B_(h,t)]_(w=1). (4.1) Thus a constant moment has zero current endpoint. A nonconstant Green moment has the SPECIFIED lower-moment current on the right; unweighted Schur scalarity does not make it zero. The identity applies to every ordered binomial moment in the [full finite Green certificate](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md). It retains shifted supports because it was proved for the whole coupled finite word before evaluating the couplings. Equations (2.3), (3.2) and (4.1) give a literal current/source map for arbitrary braids. Their coefficientwise normal derivatives are full Leibniz convolutions, including derivatives of A, the generators, every R, and the pivotal cap. The [strict relative word transport](relative_word_green_transport.md) carries these same whole identities and their marked endpoints to its relative/Fock/Mellin/Rees diagram. It cannot turn the right side of (4.1) into zero by omitting the endpoint row. ## 5. The frozen pivot has an exact whole moment-clock adapter On an actual integral color of highest weight m and number J, K=q^m Q^(-J), Z=Q^N, chi=q^(Nm), g_f=K^(1-N)=chi^(-1) K Z^J. Hence its WHOLE pivotal cap is P_f=chi^(-1) P_o M_(Z^J), (5.1) where M means left multiplication on the CLOSED factor. This is the literal position clock already included among the actual Green/Jackson observables. It is not replaced by its root value. For several closed factors use the product of their marked chi's and clocks. The scalar chi and the external modified dimension are retained exactly. For a general diagonal g commuting K, direct expansion gives (P_g A_E-A_E P_g)(C) =Tr_W([K_W^(-1)g,E_W] C) K_V^(-1), (P_g A_F-A_F P_g)(C) =K_V^(-1)Tr_W[(gF_W-K_W F_W g K_W^(-1))C]. (5.2) For g=g_f and delta=1-Q^N, the two cap rows are exactly [K^(-1)g_f,E]=(delta/(1-delta)) E K^(-N), g_f F-K F g_f K^(-1)=-delta Q^(-1) Fg_f. (5.3) They vanish at the root, but their first normal rows generally do not. Formula (5.1) supplies the analogous ALL-divided answer without division by delta: R_h:=P_f A_h-A_h P_f =chi^(-1)P_o[M_(Z^J),A_h]. (5.4) At the root Z=1, R_(h,0)=0 for every actual divided h. If a subscript 1 denotes the delta coefficient, then R_(h,1)=-chi_0^(-1) P_(o,0)[M_J,A_(h,0)]. (5.5) No derivatives of A_h have disappeared by assumption: their commutators with M_(Z^J)|_0=I vanish identically. The root map P_f,0=chi_0^(-1)P_o,0 has its full sign chi_0 retained. Higher normal terms of (5.4) retain the binomial moments of Z^J=(1-delta)^J and the generator/cap derivatives. There is an exact ordered identity explaining why dividing a small-generator cap row by the cyclotomic zero does NOT give a nonzero root divided-cap defect. Write A=A_E on the full tensor, a=A_E on the cut, R=P_f A-aP_f, and c_N=[N]_q!. Then sum_(j=0)^(N-1) a^(N-1-j) R A^j =P_f A^N-a^N P_f =c_N chi^(-1)P_o[M_(Z^J),A_(E^(N))]. (5.6) The last side is divisible by delta*c_N, hence by delta^2. All N ordered terms on the left must be combined BEFORE dividing by c_N or delta. The same identity holds for F. Thus the root frozen cap really commutes with the genuine divided adjoint, whereas its first normal defect is precisely (5.5). For the frozen cap replace (3.3) by the exact identity Tr[D_h^vee(A) P_f W] =sum_t(w_t-1)Phi_A(P_f B_(h,t))-Phi_A(R_h W). (5.7) Its Green version replaces the last term by -Phi_A[R_h p(E)W]|_(w=1), in addition to the explicit Delta_t p currents in (4.1). This is the surviving cap/source term when the ordinary and frozen pivotal routes are compared. ## 6. A genuine divided Cartan row contracts the cut wall explicitly On high color r=N use the constant beta frame and the ACTUAL word H_Fr(q)=tau [E^(N)(q),F^(N)(q)], tau=(-1)^(Nr-1). Its root individual-color matrix is h_cl tensor I_head. Its coproduct is tau[Delta E^(N),Delta F^(N)], with every mixed term of (1.1), rather than a primitive sum assigned to the memory clock. Let P_w select the extreme Fr block (N,0), keeping ALL head entries. When a cut functional is written after P_w, that selected block is embedded back in its original matrix corner before evaluation. There is an exact WHOLE contraction, not only a root formula. Both divided matrices preserve the residue strings j=aN+s, so H_Fr(q) is diagonal for every q. Write its actual diagonal entries as H_(a,s)(q), and set Lambda_(s,t)(q)=H_(N,s)(q)-H_(0,t)(q). These are specified rational functions obtained by two products of the actual integral Gaussian arrows. All have root value -2N, so each is a regular UNIT in the whole local coefficient ring at q_N. For every cut matrix C, P_w C=Lambda^(-1) entrywise* P_w[H_Fr(q),C]. (6.0) No unknown comparison section or normal jet is used to define this inverse. It preserves the actual source row by replacing it with the explicitly rescaled row Phi_w^sharp(X)=Phi_A(embed_w[ Lambda^(-1) entrywise* P_w X]). Thus Phi_A(embed_w P_w C)=Phi_w^sharp([H_Fr(q),C]) as a WHOLE rational identity, including the original q-dependent source and its full peripheral scalar. At the root it becomes P_w[H_Fr,0,C]=-2N P_w C. (6.1) Thus for any chosen cut source row the explicit root cochain row -Phi_A P_w/(2N) contracts its wall component through the ACTUAL Cartan commutator. This does not replace the memory-Borel complex: it uses the additional actual divided quantum-group word H_Fr. In particular it does not assert that this row is already one of the two partially contracted geometric framing currents. There is a completely specified all-braid pivotal map for (6.1). For ANY Hopf element h and any full matrix C, (3.1) and the antipode identity give [rho_cut(h),P_o C] =sum_(h) P_o(D_(h_1) C) rho_cut(h_2). (6.2) Indeed sum D_(h_1)(C)rho(h_2)=[rho(h),C]. Apply (2.3) to each h_1 in (6.2). With Phi_w^sharp, this transports the WHOLE wall row of the closed weighted word through actual pivotal closure. For h=H_Fr its root version is the explicit sum of -(w_t-1)/(2N) * Phi_A P_w[ sum_(h) P_o B_(h_1,t) rho_cut(h_2)]. (6.3) All coproduct/mixed terms and their source factors are retained. For a moment insertion replace w_t-1 by the Delta_t p rule of (4.1). For the frozen cap replace each P_oD term by D P_f=P_fD-R, using (5.4); the resulting cap term in (6.3) has the SAME explicit R row, not a new unspecified source. The normal Cartan corrections cannot be suppressed. Write H_Fr(q)=sum_i delta^i H_i and C(q)=sum_j delta^j C_j. The exact coefficient identity is P_w C_j=-1/(2N) P_w( [H_Fr(q),C(q)]_j-sum_(i=1)^j[H_i,C_(j-i)]). (6.4) In particular the first normal contains the explicit term [H_1,C_0]. Derivatives of the chosen source are applied afterward by their full convolution. Formula (6.4) is the expansion of the WHOLE unit inverse (6.0), not a substitute for it. This is a source-sensitive cut-chain contraction for every actual closed word. If its original Green current is not homogeneous or is not uninserted, (6.3)--(6.4) specify its remaining endpoint instead of setting it to zero. ## 7. Bare wall trace and a nonzero actual closed return At the root the actual high-color pivot is independent of the Frobenius block. Therefore closing a BARE Fr wall w=E_(N,0) gives Tr_Fr(w)=0. Returning insertions change this statement: Tr_Fr(e^N w)=Tr_Fr(w e^N)=N!. Both factors are actual integral divided-source matrices. Such a dressed trace may not be replaced by the trace of its wall factor. Likewise the original open-cut row sees Phi_+(w)=2^(-N), even though the ordinary trace kills it. The [incidence/source calculation](degree_elevation_wall_residual_and_source_moments.md) and [actual crossing example](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md) already fix these distinct rows and an actual local current that reaches the wall. The mixed adjoint in (1.2), the weighted word current in (2.3), and the cap clock in (5.1) specify which factors must accompany it through a real closure. There is also a nonzero PIVOTALLY CLOSED actual R coefficient, uniformly for every N. Take r=N, m=N(N+1)-1, k=N^2, and use the positive UNCHECKED universal R on two actual high colors. Insert on the closed first leg the literal coupon B=E_(N,0)^Fr tensor P_(head,0). Consider the open matrix entry from index 0 to k. The closed trace has exactly one contributing matrix entry: R takes the closed index k to 0 with transfer k, and B returns it to k. Writing eta_N=q_N^(1/2) with its marked phase, its first nonzero normal coefficient is [delta^N] (ptr_K[(B tensor I)R])_(k,0) =q_N^(m-2k) N^N N! eta_N^(m(m-2k)) != 0. (7.1) All lower coefficients of this entry vanish. To prove it, use the LITERAL transfer coefficient q^(k(k-1)/2) rho^k[k]_q! {m choose k}_q q^(m(m-2k)/2). Its factorial part is (-1)^k q^(-k)(Q;Q)_k. For k=N^2 the prefactor at the root is one. The N zero factors give N!delta^N, and each of the N nonzero root blocks gives product_(a=1)^(N-1)(1-Q_N^a)=N. Finally {m choose k}_(q_N)=1: the ordinary Q-Gaussian cancels EXACTLY to the regular unit product_(a=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^(N^2+a))/(1-Q^a), whose root value is one, and the symmetric conversion factor is q_N^(-N^2(N-1))=1. Multiplication by the CLOSED pivot at index k gives (7.1). The frozen cap multiplies this leading coefficient by its retained chi_0^(-1), so it is also nonzero. Thus a bare wall has zero closed trace, but an actual universal crossing can provide its return and yield a nonzero closed normal source. This is a sourced R coefficient, not an assertion that an uninserted knot has a nonzero wall. It also records why a fixed normal-order test with order<N cannot see this particular return. For the unweighted generic ordinary ribbon tangle, the complete long matrix is scalar and its projected wall is zero. The stronger usable statement here is the all-word formula (4.1): after a Green insertion its exact defect is a finite difference of THAT moment, with the source row still present. For the frozen ADO route add the explicit whole cap clock (5.7). These are finite formulas to check on a proposed geometric source map, not grounds for dropping the Green endpoints. Bare wall trace, full uninserted scalarity, and a Green/current endpoint are three different operations. The [independent cut-charge/tail audit](global_green_cut_tails_and_wall_transport_residual.md) records an additional exact restriction: an original charge-zero array and scalar Green moments have a diagonal cut kernel termwise. Homogeneous actual Hopf currents retain their integer charge, including divided mixed terms and normal jets. A cut tail outside the finite color range is retained by its endpoint row rather than folded into the head. These facts exclude a direct unmatched extreme wall in their stated charge range; they do not remove a returning wall or the current/source terms in (4.1) and (5.7). The remaining geometric comparison must transport these specified rows and currents through the actual partial Gaussian contraction. Neither a memory-Borel contraction nor scalarity of the completed unweighted word supplies that map. Exact audits: [script](../experiments/audit_actual_divided_ward_closure.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_divided_ward_closure_results.json). The cap, ordered-divided cancellation, actual Cartan unit and closed-return proofs have a separate [independent audit](global_green_cut_tails_and_wall_transport_residual.md).

title: Coherent doubled reassociation and one-power angle transfer weights
text: # Coherent doubled reassociation and one-power angle transfer weights 29 October 2026. An actual reassociation packet has an exact doubled Gram with FOUR one-power affine-angle weights on its diagonal. The shared-head positive trace has a literal Fourier/Kraus summation and an unwrapped physical edge constraint. Its off-diagonal terms retain the two-copy phases; they are not replaced by a product of magnitudes. An operator Cauchy inequality then gives an explicit positive path majorant for ANY fixed signed plat, with its original source and cap supports retained. This is an actual bound, not a new invariant. The raw path majorant has an [actual-source oversized closed-route obstruction](actual_closed_pascal_route_energy.md), so it cannot itself supply the sharp knot-volume bound. The physical shared-head equation alone is not the ideal edge-angle identification. The [ordinary-cap coherent collapse](actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) is a source-specific way to improve it before any such dephasing. ## 1. Literal finite Euler transfers and the source-fixed metric Keep N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1 and s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|. On an actual physical pair define V_12=x^-1 S_1^- F_2, S^-|a>=|a-1>, S^-|0>=0, F|b>=(1-Q^(b+1))|b+1>, F|d>=0. The original normalized Borel transfer and its literal inverse are C'_12=p_N(V_12), (C'_12)^-1=sum_(r=0)^d (-1)^r Q^[r(r-1)/2]V_12^r/F_r, p_N(t)=sum_(r=0)^d t^r/F_r, F_r=(Q;Q)_r. (1) These are finite nilpotent matrices, not source-free cyclic completions. Their exact coefficients are C'_12|a,b>=sum_r x^-r [b+r choose r]_Q |a-r,b+r>, (C'_12)^-1|a,b> =sum_r (-1)^r Q^[r(r-1)/2]x^-r [b+r choose r]_Q |a-r,b+r>, (2) 0<=r<=min(a,d-b). The formula follows by applying V_12^r; its F product is F_(b+r)/F_b. The inverse in(1) follows from the finite Euler identity modulo V_12^N=0. All endpoint terms and its actual inverse phases are retained. Use the physical metric and its coordinate gauge h_a=sqrt(N)/s_a=L_a^-1/2, B=diag(sqrt(h_a))=L^-1/4. (3) This is a PHYSICAL head metric, not the length-register D_l frame. Since h_a h_(d-a)=1, the gauge B on paired heads fixes the actual cups and ordinary caps pointwise; its marked source use retains the already proved whole-operator degree restriction. Pivots are diagonal and commute with B. The full original source is therefore transported as in the physical weighted-Fourier theorem. No ordinary positive pivotal trace is presumed. Write hats for conjugation by the appropriate tensor power of B. Set beta(L,r)=s_L/(s_r s_(L-r)). Directly from(2),(3), |C'hat_12[(a-r,b+r),(a,b)]|^2 =beta(a,r)beta(b+r,r) =N^2 w_d(r,a-r,d-a)w_d(r,b,d-b-r), (4) w_d(i,j,k)=1/(s_i s_j s_k), i+j+k=d. The inverse has exactly the same diagonal energy weights. This includes r=0 and all allowed endpoints, with s_0=1. Each w appears ONCE in the doubled diagonal weight. The original coefficients were not replaced by positive weights before being squared. ## 2. The actual three-head packet and its complete doubled Gram Let A=(C'_23)^-1 C'_12. (5) Given input i=(a,b,c), its allowed outputs are o=(a-r,b+r-s,c+s), 0<=r<=min(a,d-b), 0<=s<=min(b+r,d-c). (6) The intermediate state (a-r,b+r,c) is UNIQUE. Consequently A[o,i]=(-1)^s Q^[s(s-1)/2]x^[-(r+s)] [b+r choose r]_Q [c+s choose s]_Q. (7) This is the whole actual packet, including the inverse's finite current/wall data. It is not the homogeneous part of a separate beta expansion. Its exact integer support has not been relaxed. In the metric(3), write Ahat[o,i]=q^[r(b-d)+s(c+s)] sqrt(W(i;r,s)), W=N^4 product_(j=1)^4 w_d(t_j), (8) where t_1=(r,a-r,d-a), t_2=(r,b,d-b-r), t_3=(s,b+r-s,d-b-r), t_4=(s,c,d-c-s). The phase in(8) uses the exact identity [L choose r]_Q=q^[r(L-r)]beta(L,r) and x=q^d. No half integer modular inverse is used. It is valid at both parities. Its positive gauge changes no phase. For an arbitrary boundary matrix D, including a matrix-valued exterior, the complete doubled contraction is (Ahat^* D Ahat)_(i,j) =sum_(o,o') conjugate(Ahat[o,i]) D_(o,o') Ahat[o',j]. (9) Thus mixed copies have their actual phase DIFFERENCE and a square root of the two diagonal W weights. Formula(9) does not set i=j or o=o' before the exterior has specified that contraction. If a different exact factorial presentation uses an explicit Theta current, substituting its FULL identity into(9) gives the same Gram, including all cross terms with that current. One must not add a second independent current to(7), nor keep only its homogeneous summand. The separate tame-current metric L^(1/2) is not silently identified with the quarter gauge(3). ## 3. What a shared-head Fourier/Plancherel sum really does For a positive input density rho define the actual positive map E(rho)=Tr_(middle output)[Ahat rho Ahat^*]. (10) For each physical middle color M=0,...,d, let K_M be the matrix obtained from Ahat by fixing its middle output to M and retaining its two outer output ports. Then EXACTLY E(rho)=sum_(M=0)^d K_M rho K_M^*. (11) Its term between copies (i,r,s) and (j,r',s') carries M=b+r-s=b'+r'-s'. (12) This is an UNWRAPPED equality, not a permitted extra alias. It has either exact Fourier expression delta_(M,M')=(1/N)sum_(ell=0)^d Q^[ell(M-M')] =(1/(2N))sum_(ell=0)^(2N-1)q^[ell(M-M')]. (13) Both are alias-free here because M,M' lie in0,...,d. Applying the unitary Fourier matrix to the Kraus list merely replaces K_M by its Fourier combinations and leaves(11) unchanged. This is a genuine coherent shared-head sum. It leaves the mixed outer/input copies of(9) and their phases. It does not assert that a coherent INTERNAL wire in the original scalar can simply be traced or phase-averaged: if its actual exterior couples M and M', that matrix stays in(9). Nor does(12) identify a triangulation's positive edge sum2d. Such a geometric incidence requires the separate oriented/source map. The measure in(11) is a positive Hilbert trace in the doubled energy, not the ordinary pivotal trace at complete color. All original pivots and cut rows remain in the external observable. ## 4. A quantitative diagonal-observable inequality Let D=diag(d_o) with d_o>=0. Every output o of A has at most N^2 possible inputs i: its fixed total degree determines b once a,c are chosen. Rowwise Cauchy--Schwarz in(9) therefore proves the operator inequality Ahat^* D Ahat <=N^2 diag(T_A^t d), (T_A)_(o,i)=|Ahat[o,i]|^2. (14) In particular its explicit column energy is E_i=N^4 sum_(r,s satisfying6) product_j w_d(t_j), Ahat^* Ahat <=N^2 diag(E_i). (15) This is an actual all-input estimate AFTER the two finite Euler operators and their current data have been combined into A. The same proof for one C' or its inverse uses at most N inputs per output and the two once-power weights(4): C'hat^* D C'hat <=N diag(T_(C')^t d). (16) Tensoring spectator identities changes none of these counts. Equation(14) is an inequality, not a claim that the off-diagonal Gram terms vanish. It explicitly pays a polynomial factor when they are estimated. Other coherent packet Grams can improve it. ## 5. A full original signed-plat consequence The actual Pascal/fusion alphabet proves, without any source-null remainder, R_+=kappa C'_12 D_2 C'_21 (C'_12)^-1, R_-=kappa^-1 C'_12 (C'_21)^-1 D_2^-1 (C'_12)^-1, (17) where D_2 is the original diagonal Gaussian, of unit modulus at complete color, and kappa is the original Cartan scalar. This follows also by C=C'diag(F_a) in the actual Borel factorization; conjugating its opposite transfer by diag(F_a) gives C'_21. All factors are the strict physical matrices in(1), including the top/bottom walls. There is no independent cyclic or ghost source discarded in(17). Let the original 2k-head plat have m signed crossings, and write its literal source as P_N=chi_N N^(k-1)<phi,W u>, ||phi||=||u||=1, with the actual normalized cups u and the actual pivoted cap phi. The quarter gauge fixes these paired source vectors. Let P_cap be the diagonal projector onto degree d on EACH final cap pair. The unit vector phi lies in its range, so |phi><phi| <=P_cap. (18) This retains the actual cap support; it does not replace the original invariant by an ordinary positive trace. Expand each crossing by(17), combine any desired exact packets BEFORE estimating, and apply(14) or(16) backwards to(18). Gaussian phases act trivially on diagonal observables. If the uncombined alphabet contains L=3m C' factors, define the explicit positive physical-path sum Z_path=sum_(i_0,...,i_L) |u_(i_0)|^2 1_cap(i_L) product_(j=1)^L |C'hat_j[i_j,i_(j-1)]|^2. (19) Here |u_i|^2=N^-k on the original input cup-complement states and zero elsewhere. Every physical index lies in0,...,d and every transfer has its exact unwrapped support. Then |P_N|^2 <=|chi_N|^2 N^(2k-2+3m) Z_path. (20) This is a uniform bound for arbitrary fixed braid/bridge width. It keeps the whole original external line. Each factor in(19) is exactly N^2 times TWO one-power affine-angle weights, by(4). Grouping adjacent reassociations replaces two steps by(8),(14) with their four one-power weights and the corresponding N^2 row count. Other exact contractions can be performed first too. The resulting positive path space has honest source boundary conditions and physical conservation laws. This note does not claim that these are the ideal triangulation's complete edge constraints, or that its maximum angle volume is Vol(S^3-K). Those are the remaining geometric-energy requirements. In particular(20) by itself is not the sharp volume theorem. More strongly, the [checkerboard closed-route theorem](actual_closed_pascal_route_energy.md) exhibits, on the authorized original averaged trace source at N=3r+1, a positive path of squared weight N^(4m)w_d(r,r,r)^(4m) in every length-m signed word. Its rate 4m v_3/pi can increase under word normalizations while the knot period is unchanged. Some such routes cancel even within a local R entry: this is a path-majorant obstruction, not a nonzero complete clock-sector assertion. Coherent source grouping must precede a sharp estimate. The pivotal-cap identity linked above gives one such exact grouping and its one-angle energy. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_doubled_reassociation_angle_transfer.py): the literal finite inverse, exact four-weight phases, doubled Kraus/Fourier sum, operator inequalities, and complete original signed-plat source bounds. The finite audit checks four exact mixed-copy/Fourier packet families and four complete original signed-plat source inequalities, with literal Cartan scalar and pivots retained. The all-level statements follow from the displayed finite operator identities and Cauchy inequalities.

title: Subexponential factorial charts at the original head endpoints
text: # Subexponential factorial charts at the original head endpoints 28 October 2026. A factorial change of head basis can be exponentially conditioned on the whole physical color space. On either sublinear endpoint band its condition number is subexponential, uniformly at every level. This makes the natural blowup coordinates of a noncentral endpoint meridian accessible at no additional exponential rate. The change preserves the full original tensor source. It does not turn a truncated head identity into an equality of its two conjugate positions. That normal matching source is calculated explicitly below. In particular this is a quantitative chart estimate, not the sharp whole-knot bound or geometric survival theorem. ## 1. Uniform condition number, including all normal coefficients Put Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), d=N-1, F_a=product_(j=1)^a(1-Q^j), and D=diag(F_0,...,F_d) in the original orthonormal balanced head basis. For 0<=R<=floor(d/2), let P_R project onto {0,...,R} union {d-R,...,d}. Define H_N(0)=1 and H_N(R)=(e*N/R)^R for R>=1. Then max_(a in P_R) |F_a| <= N H_N(R), max_(a in P_R) |F_a|^(-1) <= H_N(R), cond(D restricted to P_R) <= N H_N(R)^2. (1) Proof. For 1<=a<=R<N/2 the elementary sine inequalities give (4/N)^a a! <= |F_a| <= 2^a. Using a!>=(a/e)^a and the increase of r*log(e*N/r) for r<N, both |F_a| and its reciprocal are at most H_N(R). The a=0 case is one. The exact reflection formula, with its phase retained, is F_a F_(d-a)=N (-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2). Thus the upper band has |F_(d-a)|<=N H_N(R) and reciprocal at most H_N(R)/N. These prove (1), without evaluating a factorial at its forbidden zero F_N. If R=R_N=o(N), log cond <= log N+2R log(e*N/R)=o(N). (2) This estimate controls the ENTIRE band vector and every linear functional on it, not just the value at its endpoint or a fixed number of derivatives. It does not bound a fiber that has already summed over unrestricted bulk labels. There is also an everywhere invertible, globally tame finite matrix D_R=D P_R+(I-P_R), ||D_R|| ||D_R^(-1)||<=N H_N(R)^2. (3) For a fixed tensor network, independent copies of (3) at any fixed number of physical wires still have exp(o(N)) combined condition number. Nothing is assumed about the size of the knot invariant. ## 2. Exact source-preserving changes and the retained endpoint arrows For adjacent tensors A and B on a shared physical head, insert B A=(B D_R)(D_R^(-1) A). (4) All other heads are spectators. The original pivots commute with D_R because both are diagonal; an exposed cup, cap or marked row is transformed by the same explicit inverse pair rather than reset. Consequently any fixed collection of such changes preserves the original scalar exactly, for arbitrary crossing signs and braid width. The factors in the norm comparison are bounded by (3). Let S be the physical unilateral raising matrix, S|a>=|a+1> for a<d and S|d>=0. The balanced raising operator is exactly Fcal=D S D^(-1), Fcal|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1> (a<d). (5) With the cyclic unitary shift X|d>=|0>, the formula instead is Fcal=D X D^(-1)-(1/N)|0><d|. (6) The rank-one term is mandatory: F_d=N, and the original raising operator is nilpotent. Replacing (5) by a cyclic Weyl generator without (6) changes the source. A coefficient 1/N alone is not a reason to discard its contraction with an unrestricted exterior. For the tame truncated gauge D_R, (5) holds on arrows with BOTH ends in its endpoint band. Globally the exact conjugated raising matrix has coefficient (1-Q^(a+1)) g_a/g_(a+1), g_a=F_a on P_R and g_a=1 otherwise, (7) and is zero at the top. Thus the two possible band-interface arrows remain explicitly in (7); the middle arrows are unchanged. Their norm is at most 2 cond(D_R), hence subexponential. No band interface or cyclic endpoint is silently deleted. ## 3. The classical endpoint chart is genuinely noncentral At complete color use the actual commuting head symbols K=-B^(-1), f=(1-B)z, e=(B^(-1)-1)/z. The actual Gauss meridian is G=[[K,e],[f*K,f*e+K^(-1)]], det G=1, Tr G=-2. On B!=1 the change from z to f is canonical: dlog B wedge dlog f=dlog B wedge dlog z. (8) Its generating derivative is log(1-B), precisely the factorial shift in (5). In the chart (B,f), e=(1-B)^2/(B f). (9) This chart is regular at B=1 when f!=0, and there G=[[-1,0],[-f,-1]]. (10) Thus z=f/(1-B) escaping to infinity can describe a FINITE, NONCENTRAL meridian. An argument that substitutes B=1 while keeping z bounded misses (10). The complementary chart (B,e) has f=(1-B)^2/(B e); at B=1 and e!=0 it gives the upper noncentral unipotent. Its symplectic orientation is recorded by dlog B wedge dlog e=-dlog B wedge dlog z, or by using B^(-1) as its momentum. The two charts cover all noncentral trace -2 matrices with G_11=-1; the central matrix is the remaining point. This is a regular chart of the actual meridian surface. It is not an assertion that a restricted face stationary point glues its two neighboring meridians. The quantum estimate (1) makes the factorial part of this chart affordable on the physical collar; it does not prove a full contour comparison through that collar. ## 4. What the exact normal source still requires Across a shared head, the two copies of the factorial basis change cancel coefficient by coefficient. In particular they do not alter the low-band projector P_low=sum_(a=0)^R |a><a|. In the unitary finite Fourier basis its exact kernel is (1/N) sum_(a=0)^R Q^(a(j-i)). (11) Keeping the unwrapped complex position ratio t in the same finite polynomial gives (1/N) K_R(t), K_R(t)=sum_(a=0)^R t^a =(1-t^(R+1))/(1-t). (12) Both numerator and denominator in (12) are retained, with value R+1 at t=1. On |t|<=C, |K_R(t)|<= (R+1) max(1,C)^R=exp(o(N)) (13) when R=o(N) and C is fixed. But for every fixed |t|<1 and R->infinity, K_R(t)->1/(1-t), which is nonzero when t!=1. Hence a tame endpoint source does NOT impose equality of its two positions. The estimate also controls every fixed logarithmic derivative of this EXACT source. If |Log t|<=C and s is a fixed nonnegative integer, |(t*d/dt)^s [(1/N)K_R(t)]| <= N^(-1)(R+1)^(s+1) exp(CR). (13a) This follows term by term from the finite sum, including s=0 and R=0. Thus fixed normal jets of a low-band seam have the same subexponential cost for R=o(N), without using an asymptotic delta function or dividing by 1-t. It does not remove the upper-band factor t^(d-R), whose modulus can have an N-order rate off the unit circle. Splitting (12) into 1/(1-t)-t^(R+1)/(1-t) creates two apparent matching poles at t=1. Their residues cancel exactly. On a bounded logarithmic ratio chamber and R=o(N), BOTH terms have zero N-order rate away from the pole; one cannot discard the second as having a strictly lower exponential rate. The upper band has its additional factor t^(d-R), which must also be retained. In chart (9), the original shared-head equation is f_left=f_right, because the common B is the same and z_left=z_right before taking its limit. Evaluating only at B=1 or replacing its normal source by (13)'s numerical bound does not supply that equation. The full head contraction retains it; an isolated endpoint packet has (12) instead. This pinpoints the remaining need for a coupled contour or exact cancellation across the head bands, rather than claiming that a tame chart alone proves the volume estimate. [Independent finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_endpoint_head_factorial_chart.py) checks the norm bound, the cyclic correction, actual signed full-word gauge invariance, and the Fourier source with its canceled matching residues. These checks supplement the uniform arguments above. The normal-matching limitation in Section 4 is essential. No whole-source or geometric critical-value bound follows merely from (13a). ## 5. Nilpotent reconstruction retains a genuine source current Let 1<=s<N, P=I-S^s(S*)^s=P_low(s-1), and let T_s(C)=S^s C(S*)^s on the original finite orthonormal head. Direct multiplication, before any source evaluation, gives (I-T_s)C=P C+S^s[(S*)^s,C]. (14) The inverse I+T_s+T_s^2+... is finite and has norm at most ceil(N/s), since S is a contraction. Thus it controls the ENTIRE right side of (14), including its commutator current. At the actual marked knot cut C=K_N I this commutator vanishes, but reconstruction then only repartitions the same unknown scalar K_N among its head bands. At an internal open wire with the original modified mark retained elsewhere, its environment need not be scalar, so deleting the current in (14) is not justified by the marked-cut identity. There is a concrete obstruction to extending the polynomial norm claim merely by inserting degree-preserving original crossings. On TWO actual heads put S_1=S tensor I, let R be the original COMPLETE positive checked crossing including kappa, and define T_R(A)=R S_1^s A(S_1*)^s R^(-1). (15) This superoperator is nilpotent: it raises the total degree of both the row and column of A by s. Its nilpotence order is at most ceil((2d+1)/s). Nevertheless its Green inverse is exponentially conditioned, for every s=s_N=o(N). Here is an exact matrix certificate. Set k=floor(N/2), j=floor(N/4) and a=k+j. For all sufficiently large N, s<=j and a<=d. The original crossing has the DIAGONAL coefficient r=R_((a,j),(a,j)) =kappa x^(-2j) Q^(j^2) F_a^2/(F_k F_j^2). (16) It is diagonal because transfer k=a-j sends input (a,j) to (j+k,a-k)=(a,j); this uses the checked-crossing order. The exact complete-color inverse relation R^(-1)=Flip conjugate(R) Flip gives R^(-1)_((j,a),(j,a))=conjugate(r), with every scalar kept. Take the unit Hilbert--Schmidt matrix A=|a-s,j><j-s,a|. Then the ((a,j),(j,a)) entry of T_R(A) is EXACTLY |r|^2. The row and column total degrees of T_R^ell(A) are both a+j-s+ell*s. Thus no other ell contributes to that entry, and different powers are Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal. Consequently ||(I-T_R)^(-1)||_(HS->HS)>=|r|^2 =exp[(v_8/pi)N+O(log N)], (17) where v_8 is the regular ideal octahedron volume. The last equality uses the uniform factorial estimate and the exact bulk maximizer proved in [the weighted crossing audit](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md): log|r|/N -> -4J(1/4)=v_8/(2pi). In particular this failure is not an arbitrary nilpotent-matrix example or an omitted half-Cartan factor; it occurs for the literal original R and its inverse. Statement (17) rules out a polynomial OPERATOR transport estimate from positive grading and nilpotence alone. It does not prove an exponential lower bound for the original scalar pairing of this Green kernel. Such a pairing can cancel large intermediate matrix entries, so Hopf-Ward control of the full current in (14) remains the constructive question. No internal-current cancellation or whole-knot volume conclusion is asserted here.

title: The actual pivotal cap is a two-sided Euler coefficient functional
text: # The actual pivotal cap is a two-sided Euler coefficient functional Research proof, 27 October 2026. This is an exact root-level statement about the original two-leg source after the actual Borel fusion, valid at every level. Its coefficient functional has a rational kernel with two adjacent quantum poles. The full central-F extension has explicit affine and wrapping corrections. None of these variables is identified with the physical Fourier momentum or the geometric A-curve. The starting fusion, actual cap and all external normalization lines are those in [the actual Borel-relative period](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md). In particular, no new invariant, cap normalization or preferred solution is introduced below. A scalar normalization multiplying the original word multiplies both sides of every period identity below. ## 1. Algebra and the original cap Let Q have exact order N, with N at least two, over a characteristic-zero coefficient field. Put F_j=(Q;Q)_j and F_0=1; F_(N-1)=N. Retain the actual common highest K-eigenvalue x, assumed invertible. The actual coproduct algebra is \[ A_\Phi=\langle H,f\mid H^N=1,\quad Hf=Q^{-1}fH, \quad f^N=\Phi\rangle. \] Here f is the actual TOTAL lowering operator, not an individual meridian clock. For two legs with actual F_i^N=phi_i, \[ \Phi=\phi_1+x^{-N}\phi_2. \tag{1} \] The idempotents e_j have H-eigenvalue Q^(-j). The free basis is f^a e_j, with 0<=a,j<N, and e_j f=f e_(j-1), cyclically. Let \[ \tau(f^a e_j)=\delta_{a,N-1},\qquad \rho_0(b)=[f^{N-1}e_0]b. \tag{2} \] The functional tau is Frobenius, but is not an ordinary cyclic trace. It does satisfy tau(h(f)b)=tau(b h(f)) for every polynomial h(f), because its Nakayama map fixes f. Also \[ \tau(e_{N-1}b)=\rho_0(b). \tag{3} \] To verify (3), left multiplication by e_(N-1) selects f^a e_j only when j+a=N-1 modulo N; tau then selects a=N-1 and hence j=0. Under the actual triangular fusion, the original highest-input, all-ones-output pivotal cap has the following exact values: \[ \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(f^a e_k)= x^{1-N-a}Q^{-b}\frac{F_b}{F_k} \begin{cases} 1,&k+a<N,\\ \phi_2,&k+a\geq N, \end{cases} \qquad b=k+a\pmod N. \tag{4} \] Indeed the source projector requires output weight b. Returning the second output to its original pivotal closure forces all a lowering steps onto that leg. Its nonwrapping coefficient is F_b/F_k; a second-leg wrap supplies phi_2. The factors x^(1-N-a)Q^(-b) are the original pivotal weight and K_1 inverse factors. This is the same literal cap as before fusion. The first-leg central parameter enters the relative algebra through (1), not through a replacement for this second-leg wrap. ## 2. Exact two-sided Euler form on the nilpotent fiber Write z=xf and define the finite polynomials \[ u(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{z^j}{F_j},\qquad v(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \frac{(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}z^j}{F_j},\qquad v_2(z)=v(Q^2z), \quad \gamma=Nx^{2-2N}Q. \tag{5} \] On phi_1=phi_2=0, the original cap is exactly \[ \boxed{\quad \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(a)=\gamma\rho_0\big(v_2(z)\,a\,u(z)\big). \quad} \tag{6} \] The shift Q^2 is necessary. Replacing v_2 by v is false in general; level two conceals the error since Q^2=1 there. Here is a direct all-level proof. The cap density from the actual fusion factors as L R, where \[ L=u(z)e_{N-1},\qquad R=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x^{1-N-k}Q^{-k}F_k f^{N-1-k}e_k. \] The elementary product identity \[ F_{N-1-j}=N\frac{(-1)^jQ^{j(j+1)/2}}{F_j} \] gives R=gamma e_(N-1)v_2(z), coefficient by coefficient. Thus the exact density is C=gamma u(z)e_(N-1)v_2(z). Moving u through tau, which is permitted for polynomials in f, and then using (3) proves (6). This derivation uses the actual cap density, rather than prescribing a desirable co-source afterward. The finite Euler equations on this nilpotent fiber are \[ u(Qz)=(1-z)u(z),\qquad v(z)u(z)=1. \] For degrees below N the first follows by subtracting consecutive coefficients; its remaining degree-N term vanishes because z^N=0. The second follows either by the finite q-binomial formula or by the same recurrence and constant term one. Consequently \[ v_2(z)u(z)=\frac1{(1-z)(1-Qz)}=:J_Q(z), \tag{7} \] and (6) has the equivalent exact form \[ \boxed{\quad \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(a)=\gamma\rho_0 \left[J_Q(z)\,u(z)^{-1}a\,u(z)\right].\quad} \tag{8} \] All inverses in (7)-(8) exist in the truncated algebra: their arguments have constant term one and z is nilpotent. Formula (8) is a coefficient identity with a rational kernel; it does not introduce a convergent contour integral or an asymptotic cycle. In particular J_Q must be applied AFTER the indicated actual-word Euler conjugation. Inserting it as an extra weight in the old unconjugated word would change the period. For any actual two-leg word W that commutes with the diagonal Borel action, its fused action is right multiplication by the unique element a_W. The original period, with its original external line gamma_W, is therefore exactly \[ P_W=\gamma_W\gamma\rho_0 \left[J_Q(z)u(z)^{-1}a_Wu(z)\right]. \tag{9} \] This applies to words, their signed inverses and their exact compositions. It is not limited to a chosen critical branch. There is a relevant left/right distinction. Physical total F acts by LEFT multiplication on this free fused module, whereas a_W is its RIGHT-multiplication coefficient. Thus the conjugation a_W -> u^(-1)a_W u in (8) is in the right coefficient algebra. It is not conjugation of the physical word by u(physical total F): the latter commutes with a Borel-linear word and would do nothing. For more than two legs the actual free relative module has matrix-valued word coefficients and its original entry-dependent cap rows; those rows must be retained. No assertion that all of them equal this single two-leg cap is being made. ## 3. The whole central-F extension retains its wrap correction Equations (5) still define polynomials on the full flat A_Phi family. Define \[ C_E=\gamma u(z)e_{N-1}v_2(z),\qquad \Lambda_E(a)=\tau(C_Ea)=\gamma\rho_0(v_2(z)a u(z)), \] and the explicit element \[ W=\sum_{a=1}^{N-1}\sum_{b=0}^{a-1} x^{1-N-a}Q^{-b}\frac{F_b}{F_{N+b-a}} f^{N-1-a}e_b. \tag{10} \] Then the exact original whole cap is \[ \boxed{\quad C_{\mathrm{act}}=C_E-x^N\phi_1 W,\qquad \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(a)=\Lambda_E(a)-x^N\phi_1\tau(Wa). \quad} \tag{11} \] This correction is essential even when Phi=0: opposite nonzero leg centers can have zero total center. To prove (11), evaluate the Euler density on f^a e_k. The idempotent in u e_(N-1)v_2 forces the coefficient of u to have index k and that of v_2 to have index N-1-b, where b=k+a mod N. If k+a<N, their total f degree, including a, is N-1. The value is the first case of (4). If k+a>=N, that degree is 2N-1 and one factor Phi occurs. The resulting value is \[ \Lambda_E(f^a e_k)=x^{1-N-a}Q^{-b}\frac{F_b}{F_k} \begin{cases}1,&k+a<N,\\ x^N\Phi,&k+a\geq N.\end{cases} \tag{12} \] The Frobenius dual-basis formula makes tau(W f^a e_k) zero in the first case and x^(1-N-a)Q^(-b)F_b/F_k in the second. Now use x^N Phi=x^N phi_1+phi_2. Equations (4), (11) follow on every basis element, hence on the whole flat family. The Euler density itself has a useful exact central scalar: \[ e_{N-1}v_2(z)u(z)e_{N-1}=d\,e_{N-1},\qquad d=1+\frac{N-3}{2N}x^N\Phi,\qquad C_E^2=\gamma d C_E. \tag{13} \] Only total degrees zero and N contribute in this corner. The degree-N coefficient of v_2(z)u(z) is \[ -\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\frac{Q^{2j}}{1-Q^j} =\frac{N-3}{2N}. \] For the last equality use sum 1/(1-Q^j)=(N-1)/2, sum Q^j=-1 and t^2/(1-t)=1/(1-t)-1-t. This proves (13), including composite N. If phi_1=0, C_act=C_E and the same quadratic relation holds for the actual cap. In general its explicit W correction cannot be discarded. In particular d is not the multiplicative Euler norm 1-x^N Phi. ## 4. Exact dressed source Ward equation and its affine completion Let sigma fix H,x and send f to Qf. This is an algebra automorphism, with sigma=Ad(H inverse). Put \[ t=1-z,\qquad t_2=1-Q^2z,\qquad c=x^N\Phi/N. \] Direct comparison of consecutive coefficients in (5), including the last degree, gives the WHOLE polynomial equations \[ \boxed{\quad \sigma u=t u+c,\qquad t_2\sigma v_2=v_2-c.\quad} \tag{14} \] The last coefficients are respectively +z^N/N and -z^N/N. They are not zero away from the nilpotent source. On the open chart 1-x^N Phi invertible, t_2 is invertible since its cyclic product is 1-x^N Phi. For any a put \[ V=t_2^{-1}\sigma(a),\qquad T(a)=Vt,\qquad \delta(a)=T(a)-Q^{-1}a. \tag{15} \] Then the exact actual co-source equation is \[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(\delta(a)) &=\gamma c\rho_0\big(Vtu+cV-v_2V\big) -x^N\phi_1\tau(W\delta(a)). \end{aligned}} \tag{16} \] For a proof, put b=v_2 a u. Equation (14) gives, with the noncommutative order retained, \[ v_2T(a)u-\sigma(b)=c\big(Vtu+cV-v_2V\big). \] Since rho_0(sigma b)=Q^(N-1)rho_0(b)=Q^(-1)rho_0(b), applying gamma rho_0 and then (11) proves (16). On the actual nilpotent source phi_1=phi_2=0, both right-hand terms vanish. Thus this is the exact dressed Ward identity \[ \Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(T(a)-Q^{-1}a)=0. \tag{17} \] It is a statement about the original cap, not just a homogeneous formal solution. At nonzero centers (16) specifies the affine defect and the source's first-leg wrap term. Treating (17) as homogeneous on that whole family would erase actual source data. ## 5. The source connection in x is also explicit At phi_1=phi_2=0 define \[ A=\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\frac{x^{r-1}f^r}{1-Q^r},\qquad A_2=\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\frac{Q^{2r}x^{r-1}f^r}{1-Q^r}. \] The finite Euler equation gives u^(-1)partial_x u=A and partial_x v_2=-A_2 v_2. For example, take the nilpotent logarithm in u(Qz)=(1-z)u(z): in degree r<N its coefficient is 1/[r(1-Q^r)], which proves these formulas by differentiation. Differentiating (6) therefore gives exactly \[ \partial_x\Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(a) =\frac{2-2N}{x}\Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(a) +\Lambda_{\mathrm{act}}(\partial_xa+aA-A_2a). \tag{18} \] The scalar gamma character has been retained. In particular (18) agrees with the x^(1-N-a) dependence of every original basis cap value in (4). This is an x-connection at the fixed root, not an identification with the moving-q normal direction. ## 6. What this does and does not resolve on the critical path This result supplies an exact actual-word/source transform with a rational coefficient kernel. It removes the need to guess an unsourced double-pole weight for the two-leg Borel cap. It also locates all central-F affine and wrapping defects before taking jets. These are useful prerequisites for a selected-period map. The equality z=xf is an operator in the TOTAL lowering algebra. It has not been identified with the physical second-meridian Fourier variable p, nor with a coordinate on the geometric critical variety. Similarity between J_Q and a geometric density with a double pole is not such an identification. The actual word is Euler-conjugated in (8), and the central correction in (11) is not optional. The fixed-root central-F family also does not contain the moving-q divided-power normal automatically. Thus the next required bridge is an actual source-compatible symbol/period transform from the dressed word and cap in (8) (or its full relative matrix source) to the geometric meridian/A-period object. That map must carry actual source currents to zero and send the original selected class to a proved nonzero geometric class. This note constructs no such map, and proves neither its subexponential coefficient nor the global volume norm. Gates C, D and E remain open. ## 7. Exact checks The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_euler_cap_boundary.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_euler_cap_boundary_results.json) were rerun successfully at N=2,...,7. The checks use the literal original physical cap after triangular fusion, not a cap defined by the answer (6). They cover 139 nilpotent basis Cauchy/connection identities and 139 explicit rational-kernel coefficient identities, 556 whole cap basis values across four central specializations per level, 24 whole Euler/wrap cases, 500 affine co-source Ward identities on their invertible charts, and 24 literal signed-word period tests. The proofs above are all-level; these exact finite-field tests are independent convention and coefficient checks, not a substitute for those proofs.

title: The original braid period has an exact finite Euler/Gaussian Cauchy network
text: # The original braid period has an exact finite Euler/Gaussian Cauchy network Subsequent exact simplification, 28 October: the [Hardy support theorem](actual_hardy_cauchy_network.md) proves that, in this COMPLETE ordered factorization, every internal upper-projector branch is killed by an existing factorial barrier. The [cyclic-function completion](actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.md) then replaces the finite Euler kernels by the anchored literature cyclic functions without changing the original whole source. The endpoint warnings below remain valid for the separate finite scalar kernels and arbitrary inserted coupons; they are not an obstruction to those proved complete-word replacements. The new representation still requires its selected geometric-cycle theorem. 28 October 2026. The all-word Euler completion gives a strict factorization of the original crossing into scalar Euler transfer operators, factorial diagonals and a marked Gaussian diagonal. The factorial kernels themselves are Euler polynomials. Consequently the entire original period is an explicit Laurent-polynomial Cauchy integral with a number of variables depending on the fixed braid, not on N. Its original cap and peripheral line are retained. This is useful for the proposed global contour route: it gives an actual finite-polynomial integrand, not a different state integral or an assumed sum over critical points. The finite-head projectors have endpoint branches with their own exponential scale. The construction does not prove that the geometric saddle is selected. The existence of an exact finite-variable source period and coherent composition was already proved in [the compact coherent calculus](compact_coherent_source_period.md). The additional content here is the explicit factorization of its actual crossing kernels into scalar u_N/v_N, Gaussian and finite projection atoms, with their precise arguments and original source. This exposes the functions whose GLOBAL asymptotics a contour proof must control; it is not a new abstract kernel-composition theorem. ## 1. Strict factorization after taking the zero-weight part Use q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q and F_a=(Q;Q)_a. Let u_N(t)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)t^a/F_a, v_N(t)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)(-1)^aQ^(a(a-1)/2)t^a/F_a. On one head let S^+ and S^- be the truncated unit raising and lowering shifts. Define on two heads X_-=S_1^- S_2^+, X_+=S_1^+ S_2^-, U_-=u_N(x^-1 X_-), V_-=v_N(x^-1 X_-), U_+=u_N(x^-1 X_+), V_+=v_N(x^-1 X_+). Both transfer arguments have Nth power zero, so V_- and V_+ are the exact inverses of U_- and U_+. Let F_i be the diagonal whose entry on head i is F_a, and let D e_(a,k)=d_k e_(a,k), d_k=(-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)x^(-2k). Then the ACTUAL fusion and positive/negative crossings obey C=F_2 U_- F_1 F_2^-1, C^-1=F_2 F_1^-1 V_- F_2^-1, R_+=kappa C D U_+ C^-1, R_-=kappa^-1 C V_+ D^-1 C^-1. (1) Here kappa is the original common Cartan scalar, kept unchanged. The formula for C follows entrywise: X_-^h sends (a,k) to (a-h,k+h), giving exactly x^-h F_a F_(k+h)/[F_h F_k], the proved actual fusion coefficient. For R_+, start from the [source-equivalent completion](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md), whose right Euler uses S_1^+ times CYCLIC lowering on head two. Its physical positive-N-weight part is precisely the part where that cyclic shift wraps. Replacing it by S_2^- takes the degree-zero part. Since C and D preserve integer degree, the resulting matrix is the actual R, not only an equivalent scalar period. This gives the third formula in (1); ordinary matrix inversion gives the fourth. Thus each crossing is an ordered product of ten elementary factors. All factors in (1) now preserve total unwrapped degree. This strict factorization still has finite-head projections; those projections are encoded explicitly below, not silently removed. ## 2. Scalar Laurent-polynomial kernels Identify a head vector with a polynomial in z of degree<N. For Laurent inputs define Pi_N to retain exponents 0,...,N-1 and put K_N(t)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)t^a=(1-t^N)/(1-t). The apparent pole is removable: K_N is a polynomial. For b heads the exact projection formula is (Pi_N f)(z)=CT_w product_i K_N(z_i/w_i) f(w). Consequently the transfer factors in (1) have the kernels K_(U_-,N)(z,w)=product_i K_N(z_i/w_i) u_N(x^-1 w_2/w_1), K_(U_+,N)(z,w)=product_i K_N(z_i/w_i) u_N(x^-1 w_1/w_2), (2) with v_N replacing u_N for the inverses. These formulas are exact on finite-head inputs: Pi_N of a monomial transfer is precisely the corresponding product of truncated shifts. In a full kernel composition every preceding output already lies in that head. The diagonal factor on a head has kernel sum_a c_a(z/w)^a. In particular its nontrivial scalar factors are F^-1: u_N(z/w), F: N(z/w)^(N-1) v_N(Qw/z), D^s: Gamma_(s,N)(z/w), s=+1,-1, Gamma_(s,N)(t)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)d_a^s t^a. (3) Every other spectator head contributes K_N(z_i/w_i). The factorial identity in (3) follows from F_a=N Q^(-a-1)[t^(N-1-a)]v_N(t), sum_(a=0)^(N-1)F_a t^a=N t^(N-1)v_N(Q/t). It retains its full factor N and monomial t^(N-1). All kernels in (2)-(3) are finite Laurent polynomials. Their only coordinate singularities are zero/infinity; the notation with 1-t in K_N does not create an additional pole in the complete kernel. ## 3. The full original source and a fixed-dimensional integral Let beta have b heads and m signed crossings, and expand (1) in its original order. There are L=10m elementary factors A_l. Let K_l(z^l,z^(l-1)) be their scalar kernels in (2)-(3), extended by spectator K_N factors to b variables. Keep the original pivots g_a=(xQ^-a)^(1-N). At the actual root their head kernel is G_N(t)=sum_a g_a t^a=x^(1-N)K_N(Q^-1 t). For the original normalized-average first-cut source, its scalar kernel is EXACTLY S_N(z^0,z^L)=(1/N)K_N(z_1^0)K_N((z_1^L)^-1) product_(i=2)^b G_N(z_i^0/z_i^L). (4) For the proved fixed-first-input/all-ones-output source at index zero, simply replace its first factor by K_N((z_1^L)^-1). These are the specified original source matrices, not a preferred new contour or solution. The known root scalar-closure identity equates their uninserted original periods. If chi_(beta,N)(M) is the original external modified-dimension, framing and common-Cartan line, then P_(beta,N)(M)=chi_(beta,N)(M) CT_(z^0,...,z^L) S_N(z^0,z^L) product_(l=1)^L K_l(z^l,z^(l-1)). (5) In (5), the factors kappa^sign from (1) are included once in chi, if they were not already retained in the local kernels. They are the original factors. One may leave (3)'s factors N inside their kernels rather than collect them; no numerical multiplier is fixed after specialization. The proof is elementary coefficient contraction: each CT at an internal head identifies its outgoing and incoming finite index. The source kernel (4) performs exactly the original first-cut pairing and all original pivotal closures. Thus (5) is the literal actual tensor contraction written in scalar variables. Equivalently every CT in (5) is an integral dz/(2pi*i*z) over ANY nonzero circle. There are b(10m+1) variables, independent of N. Since the full integrand is a finite Laurent polynomial, all these radii can be varied freely without crossing a noncoordinate pole. The equality holds for the whole root meridian family. It is not an assertion about moving-q normal jets. There are only m Gaussian kernels Gamma. Expanding those alone gives a sum over m indices k_j in 0,...,N-1, with explicit weights product_j d_(k_j)^(sign_j), whose remaining coefficient integral contains only u_N,v_N, finite projection kernels and source monomials. This is the requested fixed-number-of-indices Euler/Gaussian realization of the original scalar. ## 4. The endpoint branches that a global deformation must retain Formula (5) makes contour deformation possible, but does not remove the finite-head endpoint actions. For fixed t with |t|!=1, (1/N)log|K_N(t)| -> max(0,log|t|), (6) uniformly on compact sets away from the unit circle. This follows directly from (1-t^N)/(1-t). Thus discarding its numerator is an exponentially wrong replacement in the |t|>1 chamber. If the kernel network has nu projection factors, expand their numerators simultaneously: product_e K_N(t_e) =sum_(epsilon in {0,1}^nu) (-1)^|epsilon| product_e t_e^(N epsilon_e)/(1-t_e). (7) There are at most 2^nu branches, where nu<=bL+b+1 is independent of level. In each radius chamber avoiding t_e=1, (7) is an exact identity on the SAME torus. Its branch actions retain the linear terms 2pi*i sum epsilon_e Log(t_e)/h, h=2pi*i/N. Individual branches have artificial poles that cancel in their marked sum; deforming them across those poles separately requires the corresponding residue correction. In particular, `K_N(z/w) dw/w=[1-(z/w)^N]dw/(w-z)` is regular at the proposed reproducing face `w=z`. For any other factor regular there, the two split residues are `+f(z)` and `-f(z)`. Thus a reduction keeping only the first reproducing residue loses the accompanying tail chain. This is visible to the original source even in degree zero: with the literal transfer arguments `X_-=S_1^- S_2^+`, `X_+=S_1^+ S_2^-`, `X_-X_+=(I-E_top) tensor (I-E_bottom)`. The averaged original two-head pivotal cut evaluates this as `-(N-1)g_0/N`, whereas ordinary multiplication of the reciprocal Laurent arguments gives `I`, whose pivotal cut is zero. These walls are not in the proved positive-N-weight source-null ideal. Quantitative interior conditions under which the tails really are exponentially small are given in [the analytic bulk projection theorem](analytic_bulk_projection_and_euler_endpoint.md). This counts ONLY the projection-numerator choices. It does not count or control every semiclassical branch of u_N,v_N or the Gaussian polynomials Gamma. Their own finite truncations and Stokes transitions also have to be analyzed. In particular the proved small-disk Euler expansions cannot be continued uniformly to arbitrary geometric radii merely because the finite polynomials are entire in their arguments. These endpoint choices are not new knot states or independently normalizable periods. They are components of one prescribed source. Around a closed chain made only of projection ratios, the product of their moduli is one, so they cannot ALL lie in the decaying |t_e|<1 chamber. Other diagonal factors in an actual network can change that feasibility problem; no universal infeasibility assertion for every connected knot is made here. Likewise the monomials in (3) and the marked Gaussian factors must remain in the global phase. Strict concavity of a bulk volume functional alone does not bound the full upper envelope (6)-(7) or prove cancellation cannot occur between its branches. The concrete next problem is therefore well defined: choose a torus through the complete geometric point, prove uniform actual atom asymptotics there INCLUDING the marked endpoint branches, and establish the global real-part gap and nonzero derived source. The present note supplies that exact integrand and its finite branch bookkeeping, not those three analytic/geometric assertions. ## 5. The single general comparison still to prove For clarity, a sufficient general comparison proposition for THIS literal network is the following. It is an OPEN target, not a consequence claimed here. For the proposed broad class of positive geometric ideal triangulations, construct a source-preserving reduction of (5) and a contour deformation of its original marked cycle to a relative Rivin-angle chain such that: 1. Every auxiliary integration, cap, projection-numerator branch and peripheral normal row is carried by an exact identity or by a contour deformation with its matched residue terms. 2. The resulting chain projects to the positive angle domain with oriented local degree plus or minus one at its complete Rivin optimizer. The full derived source coefficient at that point is nonzero, with its normalization bounded above and below by powers of N. 3. The actual finite atoms have a UNIFORM comparison on that chain to the calibrated marked action. Its unique maximal real exponent is Vol(X)/(2pi) at the complete point; all other stationary or escaping boundary pieces have a strict exponential gap or a proved smaller contribution. After redundant source variables are eliminated, a nondegenerate Gaussian contraction (or the corresponding sourced clean-critical calculus), with its local remainder controlled RELATIVE to the full nonzero leading source coefficient, and the global gap would then give log|P_(beta,N)|=N Vol(X)/(2pi)+o(N), with the original polynomial peripheral factors still attached. The leading source coefficient may vary with N; the stated upper and lower polynomial bounds do not assert a fixed power or a convergent prefactor. A formula N^alpha(c+o(1)) would require an additional coherent density expansion. The logarithmic statement already proves the original volume limit. It is not enough to match one local saddle of one atom or show that the positive angle optimizer exists. The currently unproved assertion is the whole marked chain/source comparison above, particularly its degree-one/nonzero-source property and uniform control of all atom endpoint sectors. Rivin strict concavity controls the optimizer ON an already supplied angle chain; it does not determine the homology or intersection degree of the original cycle (4). Formula (5) now makes that cycle and every required function explicit for the comparison. ## 6. Exact checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network_results.json) check (1) against the original positive and negative crossing, the actual fusion matrix, transfer projection kernels, factorial reflection kernels and full original word/source contractions. These are exact finite-field convention checks; (1)-(7) are direct all-level identities. No lower bound for the hyperbolic volume exponent is claimed.

title: The actual Euler meridian half-step has a controlled norm and a nonzero endpoint
text: # The actual Euler meridian half-step has a controlled norm and a nonzero endpoint 27 October 2026. The right Euler frame in the original all-strand cap has an explicit adapter under M -> qM. Its operator and inverse have at most polynomial norm in the specified flat relative metric. Its canonical endpoint evaluation is EXACTLY 2/[N(1-q)], and its affine cyclic transport retains the central factors 1+Z and 1-Z. This is a sourced local calculation, not a new knot invariant or a proof of selected geometric survival. It controls the Euler part of the meridian frame change. It does not bound the fusion change in the original physical metric or the full word/source contraction. ## 1. The actual adapter and all its coefficients Use q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2, and the right coefficient algebra of [the all-strand original source](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md). Put z=xf with z^N=0, x=-M/q, and u_N(z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) z^k/(Q;Q)_k. Keep the same abstract coefficient-module frame when changing M. The actual meridian step M -> qM sends x to qx and hence z to qz. Define the two inverse, finite polynomial adapters B_N(z)=u_N(qz)u_N(z)^-1, A_N(z)=B_N(z)^-1=u_N(z)u_N(qz)^-1 (1) in that nilpotent algebra. The actual word basis uses u_N^-1, so the direction of the basis change can use A_N rather than B_N; both bounds below are stated. This is not a substitution into a classical momentum coordinate. Their unique degree-<N representatives are A_N(z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) a_k z^k, a_k=(q;Q)_k/(Q;Q)_k, B_N(z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) b_k z^k, b_k=q^k(q^-1;Q)_k/(Q;Q)_k. (2) One can prove (2) without an infinite-product specialization. The nilpotent Euler equation u_N(Qz)=(1-z)u_N(z) gives (1-z)B_N(Qz)=(1-qz)B_N(z) modulo z^N. Its constant coefficient is one; comparing every higher degree below N gives exactly the b_k recurrence in (2). Taking the inverse gives the analogous a_k recurrence. All its denominators 1-Q^k, 0<k<N, are actual nonzero root units. ## 2. The unreduced polynomial Ward equations retain the source For their CANONICAL degree-<N representatives, before discarding degree N, the exact polynomial identities are (1-z)B_N(Qz)-(1-qz)B_N(z)=-(2/N) z^N, (1-qz)A_N(Qz)-(1-z)A_N(z)=+(2/N) z^N. (3) All coefficients below degree N cancel by (2). For the first top coefficient use the FULL root products product_(r=0)^(N-1)(1-q^-1 Q^r)=2, (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N, b_(N-1)=2q^(N-1)/[N(1-q^-3)]. Thus (q-Q^-1)b_(N-1)=2q^N/N=-2/N. The second top coefficient is (1-q^-1)a_(N-1)=2/N. These prove (3), including composite levels. The factor two comes from q^N=-1 and has not been absorbed into a normalization. Evaluate the FIRST identity at the polynomial argument z=1. Its shifted term is multiplied by zero, so one obtains B_N(1)=2/[N(1-q)] =1/N+(i/N)cot(pi/(2N)). (4) At z=q^-1 the same identity gives B_N(q)=2/[N(1-q^-1)]=conjugate(B_N(1)). (5) In particular B_N(1) is nonzero at every level and tends to 2i/pi. Equation (4) is an exact evaluation of the specified polynomial, not a claim that z=1 defines a character of z^N=0. The source term in (3) is necessary for that evaluation. ## 3. The affine norm torsor has both central divisors Keep the same polynomials but now place z in the cyclic algebra z^N=Z, with Z a central parameter. Away from 1-Z=0 the first identity in (3) becomes the exact AFFINE difference equation sigma(B_N)=L(z)B_N-2Z/[N(1-z)], sigma(z)=Qz, L(z)=(1-qz)/(1-z). (6) The cyclic norm of its homogeneous multiplier is exactly product_(j=0)^(N-1)L(Q^j z)=(1+Z)/(1-Z). (7) It follows directly from product(1-Q^j z)=1-Z and q^N=-1. This specifies the local homogeneous norm curve and its retained affine source. At Z=0 the homogeneous cyclic norm is one and the affine term vanishes; the marked degree-<N section has B_N(0)=1. At the norm divisor Z=1, (3), rather than two separately undefined quotients in (6), gives the regular endpoint value (4). Deleting either 1+Z or the source 2Z/N changes this comparison. This is the actual Euler adapter's local norm/source extension. It is not identified with the knot's geometric A-curve. Replacing z^N=0 by Z here defines a specified polynomial cyclic extension of this adapter; it does not assert a full moving-q or full-word holonomy extension. ## 4. Uniform coefficient and operator bounds Write t=pi/N. For k>=1, the exact phases and positive magnitudes in (2) are a_k=exp(-ikt/2) alpha_k, b_k=-exp(-ikt/2) beta_k, alpha_k=product_(r=1)^k sin((r-1/2)t)/sin(rt), beta_k=alpha_k sin(t/2)/sin((k-1/2)t). (8) There are all-level bounds alpha_k <= 2/sqrt(min(k+1,N-k)), beta_k <= pi/[min(k,N-k)]^(3/2). (9) Here is an elementary proof. For k<=N/2 write alpha_k=w_k product_(r=1)^k sinc((r-1/2)t)/sinc(rt), w_k=product_(r=1)^k (r-1/2)/r. The function log(sinc v) decreases on (0,pi/2]. The logarithm of the displayed product sums its decreases over disjoint half intervals, so is between zero and log(pi/2). Induction gives 1/sqrt(4k+1) <= w_k <= 1/sqrt(k+1). For the other half use the exact reflection identity alpha_(N-1-l)=1/[N alpha_l sin((l+1/2)t)], which follows by splitting the full odd-root product. The inequality sin v>=2v/pi for v<=pi/2 gives the first bound in (9). Finally sin(t/2)<=pi/(2N) and sin((k-1/2)t)>=2 min(k-1/2,N-k+1/2)/N give the second bound. These estimates include both tails. Summation yields, with deliberately generous explicit constants, sum_(k=0)^(N-1)|a_k| <= 8 sqrt(N), sum_(k=0)^(N-1)|b_k| <= 1+6pi. (10) For example sum_(m>=1)m^(-3/2)<=3 suffices for the second. Consequently for EVERY contraction Z_0 with Z_0^N=0, ||B_N(Z_0)|| <= 1+6pi, ||B_N(Z_0)^-1||=||A_N(Z_0)|| <= 8 sqrt(N). (11) The flat right-regular basis f^a e_j makes R_f a truncated unit-coefficient shift, so ||xR_f||<=1 on |M|=1. Thus (11) applies to the actual relative right-Euler adapter in that SPECIFIED metric. A physical fusion basis can be ill conditioned; (11) is not a bound in every metric and is not a bound for the whole knot operator. ## 5. The omitted endpoint carry stays nonzero In the nilpotent algebra (1) implies B_N(qz)B_N(z)=1-z modulo z^N. As an ordinary polynomial its exact form is B_N(qz)B_N(z)-(1-z)=z^N R_N(z), degree R_N<=N-2. (12) Using (4)-(5), its endpoint carry is exactly R_N(1)=4/[N^2 |1-q|^2] =1/[N^2 sin^2(pi/(2N))] -> 4/pi^2. (13) Thus the high-degree carry does NOT vanish at the source endpoint. Replacing the canonical finite adapter there by the ordinary square-root relation B(qz)B(z)=1-z would change the period, even though that relation holds in the nilpotent algebra. Evaluating before the prescribed reduction is not an algebra homomorphism. In particular A_N(1) and B_N(1) need not be reciprocal. ## 6. Critical-path meaning and checks This result supplies an actual meridian source adapter with a proved subexponential condition bound, a nonzero exact endpoint and a specified affine norm torsor. It retains precisely the central norm and highest-degree terms that a premature evaluation would erase. It is not a proof that the knot-dependent endpoint sum S_N has any lower bound or nonzero geometric image. Fusion, word transport, the peripheral line and all source sectors must still be compared to the marked geometric A-period. The original volume conjecture remains unproved. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_euler_meridian_half_step.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_euler_meridian_half_step_results.json) pass 23 exact finite-field levels N=2,...,24. They check the actual Euler quotients, inverses, both UNREDUCED source equations, exact endpoints, nonzero polynomial carry and both cyclic norm factors. Nine complex diagnostics through N=4096 check the separately proved coefficient bounds.

title: Even paired black, ordinary-white and original marked contractions
text: # Even paired black, ordinary-white and original marked contractions 29 October 2026. The actual EVEN central two-vertex source has an exact positive marked contraction, despite the zero self-pairing of every paired image. The calculation uses the true ordinary metric and a regular generic lift of the full nilpotent coupon. It does not replace the paired channel by a projector, move the mark onto an ordinary quotient, or identify white with the Hermitian adjoint of black. For N=2m>=4 put j=m-1, d=N-1, theta=pi/N. Write the already proved actual black scalar as A_N=q^[1-m(m-1)] S_N, S_N=sum_(k=1)^(m-1) sin(k theta)cos(k theta) beta(m,k)^4>0. Then the original marked two-vertex source, with all three circles in this paired central sector, is EXACTLY Z_even=8 N^3 S_N^2/cos(theta) =(1/2)exp(2N v8/pi)[1+O(1/N)]. (1) The N=2 central sector is zero. Other joint channels and their coherent sum are not evaluated here. For comparison, the [odd simple central contraction](actual_central_black_white_marked_contraction.md) is N^3 S_N^2 with its different odd quartic S_N. ## 1. Actual paired image and its genuine pivotal dual Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_r=(Q;Q)_r. Let W:Q_j->V_N tensor V_N be the full actual Clebsch map in the [even normal source packet](actual_trivalent_even_central_normal_packet.md). Q_j has dimension 2j+1=N-1 and its genuine ordinary metric is G_rr=sin((r+1)theta)/sin(theta), 0<=r<=2j, pi=G^(-1) W^dagger P, pi W=0, L_c=h0 W pi, h0=2N/sin(theta). (2) L_c is the COMPLETE c=-2cos(theta) sector of the original circle. Its first normal has already been applied in (2). It is nonzero and nilpotent; it is not the spectral projector of that paired cluster. The original physical self-duality is p_(a,b)=N x^(-b)delta_(a+b,d), ell_(a,b)=x^a/N delta_(a+b,d), ell=p^(-1). On Q_j choose the ordinary self-duality with highest coefficient one: pQ_(r,2j-r)=(-q^(2j))^r Q^[-r(r+1)/2] F_r F_(2j-r)/F_(2j), ellQ=pQ^(-1). (3) For a map W its genuine right dual is D(W)=pQ^T W^T(ell^T tensor ell^T)P. It is a bilinear pivotal dual. The actual all-input equality is D(W)=gamma pi, gamma=q^[3m^2-2m+1]/N^2. (4) Both maps preserve the actual INTEGER H grading. In that homogeneous Hom space a map onto the simple Q_j has, after duality, a highest vector in the uniquely determined pair kernel of degree m.
