Its highest equation is a first-order recurrence with all its interior coefficients nonzero. Thus this homogeneous Hom space is one-dimensional. Periodic K aliases in other integer degrees are not asserted to be absent from an unrelated ungraded Hom problem. To fix the scalar without a normalization convention, take input colors a,b with a+b=m. The actual lowest endpoint is W_(2j)(j+a,d-a)=q^j h_a, h_a=q^(ma) beta(m,a). Since pQ_(2j,0)=q^(-2j), the left side of (4) is q^(-j)x^m h_a/N^2; the right row before gamma is conjugate(h_b). The ratio h_a/conjugate(h_b)=q^(m^2) gives (4). The dual in the opposite direction satisfies D(pi)=gamma^(-1)W. Indeed direct matrix multiplication gives D^2(W)=(K_V^(-1) tensor K_V^(-1)) W K_Q=W. The signs from the two physical factors square to one. No use is made of the false equality pi W=I. Let J=p_16 p_23 p_45 be the original nested black cup source. Define U=pi^tensor3 J, Lambda=ell^S W^tensor3. The original nested matching is unchanged by right-dual reversal, so exactly as an index identity, Lambda=gamma^3 D_Q(U). (5) The true black tensor is U=s Theta, s=N^3 A_N/G_jj=N^3 A_N sin(theta), (6) where Theta is the actual invariant in Q_j^tensor3 normalized to one at magnetic colors (2j,j,0). This is the independent ordinary 3j of the even source theorem, not a tensor defined by dividing U by a selected entry. ## 2. A generic finite theta evaluation, proved by Vandermonde Temporarily take a generic parameter zeta, write Q=zeta^2 and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. In the ordinary highest-weight 2j object, with the cup (3), the highest vector for the same ordinary object inside its square has entries h_a=(-1)^a Q^[-a(a+1)/2] F_(j+a) F_(2j-a)/(F_j F_(2j)), 0<=a<=j. (7) This follows directly from h_(a+1)/h_a=-Q^(-a-1)(1-Q^(j+a+1))/(1-Q^(2j-a)). Let WQ_r=F_pair^r h/F_r. Its entire lowest slice is WQ_(2j)(j+a,2j-a)=h_a. (8) For a finite proof, both sides obey the same first-order lowest F equation. At a=j the actual divided coproduct gives sum_(s=0)^j (Q^-j,Q^(j+1);Q)_s/F_s^2 =(Q^-j;Q)_j/F_j=(-1)^j Q^[-j(j+1)/2]. This is the second finite Chu identity (obtained by base inversion from the elementary finite proof in [the quadratic source transform, section2](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md)). It equals h_j, proving (8) with scalar one. Schur's first-order highest recurrence makes D(WQ)WQ a scalar eta_j times the identity. Evaluate it on the highest vector using (3),(8): eta_j=(-1)^j Q^[-j(j-1)/2] sum_(a=0)^j Q^[-(j+1)a] [j+a choose a]_Q [2j-a choose j-a]_Q =(-1)^j Q^[-j(3j+1)/2] [3j+1 choose j]_Q. (9) The last equality is elementary Vandermonde: the summation is the coefficient of u^j in 1/[(uQ^(-j-1);Q)_(j+1)(u;Q)_(j+1)] =1/(uQ^(-j-1);Q)_(2j+2). Expand each reciprocal finite product by its elementary coefficient formula. This proves (9) as a finite rational identity, without a published theta or 6j evaluation. Set Theta0=(WQ tensor I)pQ. Its stated anchor is a_j=(Theta0)_(2j,j,0)=(-1)^j zeta^[-j(j+3)]. (10) The actual cap/cup index contractions give K_Q T=eta_j I for the cut theta, where T_st=sum_(a,b)Theta0_(a,b,s)D(Theta0)_(a,b,t). Equivalently this follows from the invariant E equations, which give K_Q T scalar, and the same highest coefficient used in (9). Consequently the normalized invariant Theta=Theta0/a_j obeys D(Theta)Theta=eta_j [2j+1]_zeta/a_j^2. (11) At the even root this expression, and the entire effective cut, are ZERO: [3j+1 choose j]_Q has a simple factor 1-Q^N, while F_j and F_(2j+1) are units. This is why the odd retraction argument cannot be reused. ## 3. Retain the physical mark by a regular normal trace quotient Lift the physical V_N, the ordinary Q_j and their cups to the same generic parameter zeta near q. An explicit regular lift of W starts at physical degree t=d-j=m with highest coefficients h_a(zeta)=(-1)^a zeta^(-da) Q^[a(t-1)-a(a-1)/2] (Q^(j+1);Q)_a F_(d-a)/F_d, and uses the actual divided-F descendants through r=2j. Its highest recurrence proves covariance, and factorial reflection gives exactly the root h_a in section1. All defining factorial denominators have index <=d<N, including F_d in this highest lift. They are units. Define the regular lift pi(zeta)=gamma^(-1) D(W(zeta)), using the FIXED root gamma from (4). It specializes to the genuine pi in (2). Thus h0 W(zeta)pi(zeta) is a regular Hopf coupon whose root value is the exact full-normal circle sector L_c. This is a chosen regular lift for a FIXED-ROOT identity. It is not a claim that the original moving-q circle or pivot has this entire generic normal germ. The lifted U is s(zeta)Theta(zeta), with s holomorphic and its root value given by (6). The generic ordinary closed physical diagram with coupons W pi is therefore, by (5),(11), F(zeta)=gamma^3 s(zeta)^2 eta_j(zeta)[2j+1]_zeta/a_j(zeta)^2. (12) Cut the original marked physical arc before closing it. Its open map is a scalar t(zeta)I on the physical highest-weight d module. All its entries are regular, so t is holomorphic at q. The physical cup has p0=N zeta^(-d^2), and direct cup/cap multiplication gives ell p^T=(-1)^d K_V, F(zeta)=(-1)^d [N]_zeta t(zeta). (13) At the root this is exactly the original pivot K^(1-N), since K^N=(-1)^d I. The unrestricted original marked row satisfies m p=1, so its fixed-root closure is t(q). The mark has remained on the physical V_N strand throughout. No paired projector or arbitrary modified-trace axiom is introduced. The zero in (11) is simple. Since N=2m, j=m-1 and 3j+1=N+j-1, factor that zero explicitly in (9), giving lim_(zeta->q) eta_j [2j+1]_zeta/[N]_zeta =(-1)^j q^[-3j(j+1)+d] N/[(1-Q^j)F_(2j)]. (14) Indeed F_(3j+1)/(1-Q^N) specializes to N F_(j-1). Equation (14) retains the normal responsible for the original marked scalar; it is not obtained by setting the ordinary zero to a positive value. From (12)--(14), the marked scalar for three W pi coupons is t(q)=(-1)^(m+1) q^(-2) sin(theta)^2 tan(theta) A_N^2. (15) Substitute gamma from (4), s from (6), a_j from (10), and use F_(2j)=N/(1-Q^-1), (1-Q^-1)/(1-Q^j)=i tan(theta). These identities give every phase in (15). Multiplying by h0^3, then using A_N=q^[1-m(m-1)]S_N and q^N=-1, cancels the remaining phase and proves (1). Each fixed edge twist R^e L_c contributes its literal unit omega_j^e, where omega_j=kappa(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. The complete expression therefore acquires omega_j^(e1+e2+e3). Any external original line factor chi_N stays outside this raw formula. ## 4. An explicit checkable marked co-source identity Use the unscaled W-coordinate white tensor Vm of the [literal branching vertex](actual_trivalent_complete_circle_vertex_kernel.md), and the independently normalized Theta in (6). The same result is equivalently the full coherent magnetic sum sum_(r1,r2,r3) Theta_(r1,r2,r3) conjugate(Vm_(r1,r2,r3)) =N^4 sin(theta)^2/cos(theta) conjugate(A_N). (16) The ordinary white covector is nonzero and equals (5), but its closed pairing with U is zero. Formula (16) evaluates the original marked normal co-source instead. It does not assert equality of the marked white tensor with an adjoint black tensor on arbitrary exteriors, and gives no full magnetic norm estimate. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_even_central_black_white_marked_contraction.py) checks the generic finite theta evaluation separately from exact root source/duality data and literal full physical marked closures. The analytic argument above proves every even level N>=4, including composite levels. The N=2 zero is retained separately.

title: An explicit root-channel adapter for the first-normal defect
status: Exact root-channel normal adapter and finite Plancherel bound
text: # An explicit root-channel adapter for the first-normal defect 30 October 2026. The genuine first quantum defect of the original off-node boundary functional is an explicit function of TWO root-channel insertions. The adapter has polynomial norm O(N^2) on the actual boundary scale. It retains the full open root channel, not just its scalar closure z. This is a finite-source identity at every N>=2 and arbitrary fixed Morse width. It gives neither a bound for the root-channel norm nor the coefficient of a geometric relative period. ## 1. The actual family and its divided descendants Fix N>=2, d=N-1, q=q0 exp(epsilon), q0=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. The highest weight d and the physical indices remain FIXED. Use F e_a=(1-Q^(a+1))e_(a+1), 0<=a<d, F e_d=0, K e_a=q^d Q^(-a)e_a, ad_F X=FX-K^-1 X K F, ad_K X=KXK^-1. (1) Let C_e be a holomorphic family of linear maps on End(V_d), commuting with these ACTUAL generic adjoints, and suppose C_e(I)=z(e)I. (2) The original routed channel C_e(X)=P_V[A U^-1(X tensor I)U B] satisfies these hypotheses with the original generic pivot g=(-1)^d K, actual endpoints and all peripheral factors; the [braided source/current theorem](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md) includes rectangular cuts and arbitrary fixed width. No bare root mark is made covariant, and no routed U band is omitted here. Only K and F covariance is needed in the proof below. For 0<=s<=d put h_s(q)=(-1)^s Q^[s(s+1)/2] {d choose s}_Q, {d choose s}_Q=product_(j=1)^s (1-Q^(N-j))/(1-Q^j). For -d<=n<=d let s0=max(-n,0), and define the n-th-band matrix V_n(q)_(s+n,s)=h_s(q)/h_s0(q) whenever 0<=s,s+n<=d; all other entries are zero. (3) All h_s(q0)=1, by 1-Q0^(N-j)=-Q0^(-j)(1-Q0^j). Thus (3) is holomorphic near the root and V_n(q0)=T_n, the literal unwrapped band sum sum_(r-s=n) E_rs. In particular V_-d=E_0d and V_0=diag(h_0,...,h_d). Here is the entire descendant calculation. The successive ratio is h_(s+1)/h_s=-Q^(s+1)(1-Q^(d-s))/(1-Q^(s+1)). On a band with entries h_s, the coefficient of ad_F is (1-Q^(s+n+1))h_s-Q^n(1-Q^(s+1))h_(s+1) =(1-Q^(N+n))h_s. (4) At either physical end the missing term is zero. Substitution of the same ratio verifies (4) at the newly appearing left endpoint; at the right endpoint h_(d+1)=0 is used only as that finite zero, not as a new cyclic arrow. After normalizing (3), for -d<=n<d, ad_F V_n=c_n(q)V_(n+1), c_n=1-Q^n if n<0, c_n=1-Q^(N+n) if n>=0. (5) In particular c_0=1-Q^N vanishes at the root. It is canceled GENERICALLY, before taking root values. Equivalently, with F_k=product_(j=1)^k(1-Q^j), (ad_F)^(d+n) E_0d =F_(d+n) sum_s (h_s/h_d) E_(s+n,s). (6) For d+n>=N, (6) cancels the common factor in F_(d+n); it never divides a specialized zero matrix by a root zero. This explains the positive-band descendants without replacing the physical endpoint. Generic ad_K has distinct eigenvalues on the different integer bands. Its extreme band is one dimensional, so C_e(E_0d)=lambda(e)E_0d, with lambda holomorphic. Covariance and the nonzero generic factors (5) imply C_e(V_n)=lambda(e)V_n, -d<=n<=d. (7) Analytic continuation gives (7) at the root too. Since V_0(q0)=I, lambda(0)=z(0). Thus this proof also gives C_0(T_n)=z_0 T_n directly from regular generic K/F covariance, without an off-root cyclic shift or an assumed interpolation. ## 2. Two literal root insertions give the first-normal defect Write C_1=partial_epsilon C_e|0, z_1=z'(0), and mathcal A=C_0-z_0 Id_End. Define the explicit root diagonal H_0=0, H_s=2N sum_(j=1)^s 1/(1-Q0^j), H=diag(H_0,...,H_d). (8) This is the genuine derivative h'_s(q0). Indeed differentiating the product for h_s gives s(s+1)+sum_j[2N/(1-Q0^j)-2j], leaving exactly (8). In particular it keeps the derivative of Q^N; the root simplification h_s(q0)=1 is not differentiated instead. The derivative J_n=V'_n has entries H_s-H_s0 on its band. Differentiating (7), and subtracting the derivative of (2) at n=0, gives the EXACT identities eta I=mathcal A(H), eta=lambda'(0)-z_1, (C_1-z_1 Id_End)T_n =eta T_n-mathcal A(J_n). (9) There is no unspecified scalar normal in eta: it equals any diagonal entry of mathcal A(H), or Tr(mathcal A(H))/N. For ANY unwrapped Toeplitz matrix X=sum_n x_n T_n, let J(X)=sum_n x_n J_n. Since J(X)=XH-sum_n x_n H_max(-n,0) T_n and mathcal A annihilates every T_n, (9) simplifies to (C_1-z_1 Id_End)X=eta X-mathcal A(XH). (10) In particular for X(p)_(r,s)=p^(r-s)/N, p!=0, the genuine defect Delta_e(p)=C_e(X(p))-z(e)X(p) has Delta'_0(p)=eta X(p)-mathcal A(X(p)H), eta I=C_0(H)-z_0 H. (11) Thus only the original ROOT insertions H and X(p)H are required, in the SAME routed channel with its original closure. If p depends on epsilon, the extra derivative is zero because the root defect vanishes identically in p. No derivative of a root-only simplification of an individual coupon has been used. For the original coherent row e_t of trace one and its exact b_N(t,p)=Tr[e_t X(p)], the retained scalar defect is therefore Tr[e_t Delta'_0(p)] =eta b_N(t,p)-Tr[e_t C_0(X(p)H)] +z_0 Tr[e_t X(p)H]. (12) If b_N!=0 this may be divided by that SAME b_N. Equation (12) does not evaluate either new root period from z. In particular it does not introduce a second trace-one localization or remove U. There is a useful exact check against the free pivotal channel B_e(X)=D_e X-tau_e(X)I, tau_e(X)=Tr(g_e X), D_e=tau_e(I). Swapping the sums in (8) gives sum_s Q0^(-s)H_s=-2N/(1-Q0^-1), tau_0(H)=-nu_N, nu_N=D'_0. Equations (11) then give eta=nu_N and Delta'_0(p)=nu_N[X(p)-I/N], retaining the physical trace-normal sign. The actual N=2 odd-braid family in the current theorem shows that these additional open data cannot generally be replaced by z. ## 3. The exact Plancherel bound Center H by its scalar mean: tildeH_s=H_s-N^-1 sum_r H_r. Both (9) and (10) are unchanged, since mathcal A(I)=mathcal A(X)=0. Set R_N^2=N^-1 sum_s |tildeH_s|^2. This variance has a finite exact Fourier formula. With hat f_k=sum_s f_s Q0^(-ks), define the cyclic difference b_s=H_s-H_(s-1 mod N). Then b_0=-N(N-1) and b_s=2N/(1-Q0^s) for s>0. Pairing s with N-s gives sum_(s>0)(1-Q0^s)^-1=(N-1)/2. The successive differences of sum_(s>0)Q0^(-ks)/(1-Q0^s) are -1 for 1<=k<N, hence hat b_k=-2Nk, hat H_k=-2Nk/(1-Q0^-k), 1<=k<N, R_N^2=4 sum_(k=1)^(N-1) k^2/|1-Q0^k|^2. (13) These are the unnormalized Fourier transform and its Parseval factor 1/N^2; no extra N is suppressed. Also sum_(k=1)^(N-1) csc^2(pi k/N)=(N^2-1)/3. For an elementary proof, logarithmically differentiate P(x)=(x^N-1)/(x-1)=product_(k>0)(x-Q0^k) twice at x=1, using P(1)=N, P'(1)=N(N-1)/2 and P''(1)=N(N-1)(N-2)/3. Subtract the two resulting sums to get sum |1-Q0^k|^-2=(N^2-1)/12. Therefore R_N^2<=N^2(N^2-1)/3, R_N<=N^2/sqrt(3). (14) Use Hilbert--Schmidt norm on matrices and its induced norm on channels. If |log|p||<=A/N, then ||X(p)||_HS<=exp(A), ||X(p)tildeH||_HS<=exp(A)R_N, |eta|<=R_N ||mathcal A||_(HS->HS). The second inequality follows entry by entry from |p^(r-s)|<=exp(A); the third follows from eta I=mathcal A(tildeH). Consequently ||Delta'_0(p)||_HS <=2exp(A)R_N ||mathcal A||_(HS->HS) <=4exp(A)N^2/sqrt(3) ||C_0||_(HS->HS). (15) For the last inequality, C_0(I)=z_0 I gives |z_0|<=||C_0||. The actual scale p_N=1-1/(N rho+c0), with rho in a fixed compact of C* and c0 bounded, satisfies this hypothesis uniformly for large N. Scalar pairing retains its actual factor ||e_t||_HS, and division by b_N retains |b_N|^-1; neither is silently declared polynomial. Most importantly, (15) is NOT a bound by |z_0|. The full channel norm can contain large independent open-source contributions. ## 4. A canonical square-zero part of the root channel Every such root channel preserves E_N=span{I,H}, and in the ordered basis I,H its matrix is [[z_0,eta],[0,z_0]]. (16) For composition of two admissible channel families, z(CD)=z(C)z(D), eta(CD)=z(C)eta(D)+eta(C)z(D). (17) Thus z+eta e, e^2=0, is an exact dual-number character of this channel algebra. Where z!=0, eta/z is additive under composition. This is literal finite linear algebra. Arbitrary braid coupons are not thereby factored into these End(V_d) channels, and (17) implies no global growth, transport or triangulation theorem. The first-normal defect is therefore explicitly determined by the FULL root channel, while (11)--(12) identify which additional root insertions must be retained. The original finite support cycles, their moving-period boundary terms and their relative geometric coefficient remain outside this adapter. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_explicit_root_channel_normal_adapter.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_explicit_root_channel_normal_adapter_results.json) pass 133 exact generic ladder entries and 54 raw divided-descendant identities. Nineteen original braid, complete-circle and rectangular sources give 2087 all-band first-normal defect comparisons, 2087 normalized-descendant jet entries, 801 off-node adapter entries, 57 coherent-period identities and 57 genuine moving-p checks. Twelve actual channel compositions check (17). Exact finite-field tests give 496 Fourier modes, 31 Parseval identities and 62 pivotal free-channel normal checks. Twenty boundary norm checks at 90 digits have maximum relative Parseval error below 4.2e-90. These tests retain the actual generic pivots; they do not infer the root-channel norm from z. The estimate concerns the first-normal defect, not C_1 or z_1 separately. It retains the full-root-channel norm and the stated period scope.

title: An exponentially tame completion of the original source
text: # An exponentially tame completion of the original source 28 October 2026. The known positive-integer-carry completion has a source-preserving deformation which makes its ENTIRE overflow part arbitrarily small exponentially, in the original balanced flat norm. This is a quantitative result for every fixed signed braid or marked plat, before taking absolute estimates. It removes one specified family of source-zero completion branches; nilpotence alone had not provided such an estimate. The genuine degree-zero original word is unchanged. Its geometric critical support, singular cycle boundaries and scalar exponential estimate remain to be controlled. This theorem does not make those remaining contributions small, and it is not a volume bound. ## 1. Keep the original crossing and its carry extension Put d=N-1, Q=exp(2 pi i/N), x=-exp(-pi i/N). Let R_plus and R_minus=R_plus^(-1) be the original complete balanced crossings, including their common Cartan scalar. The independently proved [Euler completion](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md) has R_tilde_plus=R_plus+Delta_plus, R_tilde_minus=R_minus+Delta_minus, Delta_minus=-R_minus Delta_plus R_minus. (1) Each Delta has total INTEGER degree change exactly +N, whereas the original crossings preserve that degree. The literal completed crossings are mutual inverses. On b heads the positive-carry ideal has bth power zero. For an arbitrary scalar z define R_(sigma,z)=R_sigma+z Delta_sigma. (2) The two signs in (2) remain literal inverses: locally Delta_plus R_minus Delta_plus=0. For z=r^N, (2) is exactly R_(sigma,z)=r^D R_tilde_sigma r^(-D), (3) where D is local total integer head degree. This is an algebraic identity, not an estimate in an ill-conditioned changed metric. In particular the original degree-zero R_sigma in (2) is untouched. For ANY signed word beta on b heads, W_z(beta)=W(beta)+sum_(l=1)^(b-1) z^l W_l, W_l has degree +lN. (4) Thus the number of carry orders is bounded by braid width, not N or word length. Its entire original pivotal first-cut matrix equals that of W for EVERY z. Closing the other heads requires a first input/output difference strictly between -N and N, which excludes every positive carry. All original full dimension, peripheral, framing and Cartan factors multiply the same matrices and remain. The identity (4) also holds as the original root meridian family; the quantitative norms below are stated at complete color. The same exact source identity holds for the original marked plat. For 2k heads, the cups have total input degree kd. The k-1 ordinary caps fix degree (k-1)d and the FULL marked pair accepts degree from 0 to 2d. Hence the allowed total degree difference lies in [-d,d], again excluding +lN. No cap or marked row is replaced here. ## 2. The factorized quantum atom is retained In the relative algebra H^N=1, Hf=Q^(-1)fH, f^N=0, let e_j be its original right idempotents and write f_z=f[1-(1-z)e_d]. (5) Its right multiplication is the old nilpotent shift except that its wrapped step has weight z. The two-head fusion C preserves integer degree. The original right-coefficient calculation gives R_(+,z)=C right[kappa U_x(f_z) D_x(H)] C^(-1), U_x(t)=sum_(a=0)^d x^(-a)t^a/F_a, D_x(H)=sum_(k=0)^d (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)x^(-2k)e_k. (6) Indeed the coefficient of f^a e_k in U_x(f_z)D_x is its old completed coefficient multiplied by 1 if a+k<N and by z otherwise. There is at most one wrap. This proves (6), including the literal inverse with the original reversed factor order. No positive model or postulated tetrahedral weight is introduced. Since f_z^N=0, any anchored analytic cyclic-dilog completion with the same first N Euler coefficients acts identically on f_z. The literature norm-one functions and every norm factor can therefore be retained exactly as in the existing cyclic network theorem. The boundary idempotent in (5) is NOT discarded: damping is a controlled regularization of its carry, not a claim that the wall or its full inserted Ward complex has vanished. For 0<=z<=1, right multiplication by f_z is a weighted partial permutation of norm at most one in the original relative monomial basis. D_x and its inverse have norm one at complete color. ## 3. Uniform original-metric exponential bounds Here are bounds with an explicit constant and no unspecified factorial conditioning. For 0<=a<N, |F_a|<=2^N, 1/|F_a|<=(N/2)^a/a!, sum_(a=0)^d 1/|F_a|<=exp(N/2). (7) To prove the middle inequality, sort any a distinct nonzero root factors |1-Q^j|. The kth smallest is at least 2k/N: its distance from a multiple of N occurs at most twice, and 2sin(pi s)>=4s for 0<=s<=1/2. Their product is at least (2/N)^a a!. This applies to the actual initial root products. For completeness, fix a total degree T in the actual fusion (1) of the completion proof. Its block, with indices u<=a, factors as C_(u,a)=l_u M_(u,a) r_a, l_u=x^u F_(T-u), M_(u,a)=1/F_(a-u), r_a=x^(-a) F_a/F_(T-a). (8) All indices lie in [0,d]. The triangular Toeplitz M is a finite Euler function of a unit-norm shift. Its inverse has the same coefficient magnitudes, by the finite Euler convolution. Equation (7) therefore gives ||C||<=exp[(1+2log2)N], ||C^(-1)||<=exp[(3/2+log2)N]. (9) For example the three inverse factors in (8) have norms at most 2^N exp(N/2), exp(N/2), exp(N/2). These are bounds in the original balanced physical and relative monomial metrics. They do not claim that C is isometric. The Euler factor and its inverse in (6) each have norm at most exp(N/2). Put A=3+3log2. Equations (6)--(9) imply ||R_tilde_sigma||<=exp(AN), ||R_sigma||<=exp(AN), ||Delta_sigma||<=2exp(AN). (10) For the middle bound the original R is the block-diagonal degree-zero part of its completion, an orthogonal degree pinching of norm at most one. The same argument applies to the literal negative inverse. The original complete kappa has modulus one and is included throughout. ## 4. Entire overflow is arbitrarily small before an absolute bound Let the fixed signed word have m crossings, and choose z_N=exp(-tau N), tau>=0. Tensoring with untouched heads changes none of the local norms. The ordinary product telescoping identity and (10) give ||W_(z_N)-W|| <=2m 3^(m-1) exp[(mA-tau)N]. (11) For any prescribed L>0 choose tau>=mA+L. The entire carry error then has norm at most 2m3^(m-1)exp(-LN), while its original closed source is EXACTLY zero by (4). This holds for both signs in the same original flat metric, without changing that source to a conjugated or exponentially conditioned boundary vector. The trace norm of the original reduced first-cut functional is at most N^(b-1), since every closed pivot is unitary. Original finite cups/caps likewise have polynomial norms at complete color. Thus (11) also bounds their absolute carry contributions by a polynomial times exp(-LN), with the external source line chi_N retained explicitly. This does not require taking absolute values of the individually enormous unregularized carry paths. The finite factor-path absolute envelope can also be controlled, without relying on cancellation inside C or its inverse. For an N^2-by-N^2 matrix T, its entrywise absolute matrix obeys ||abs(T)||<=||T||_HS<=N||T||. Right Euler monomial shifts are partial permutations, so their entrywise absolute sum still has norm at most exp(N/2). The Gaussian absolute matrix is the identity. Consequently the nonnegative matrices summing all unwrapped or wrapped local C/Euler/Gaussian/C^(-1) paths each have norm at most L_N=N^2 exp(AN). Each wrapped path in (5)--(6) has exactly one factor z. In a word, the sum of absolute weights of paths with at least one wrap is therefore bounded in operator norm by m 2^(m-1) N^(2m) exp[(mA-tau)N]. (12) The positive-carry degree restriction actually forbids those paths from the plain original closed source term by term. Estimate (12) also applies before that contraction, or after polynomially bounded inserted coupons, when the simple closed-source degree exclusion is unavailable. Thus the quantitative claim is not an inference from source cancellation or an exchange of an infinite scalar expansion. It concerns the specified finite factor expansion; an arbitrary later scalar-contour rewriting must retain its own source identity. There is also a controlled extension to the earlier coupon caveat. Insert finitely many specified matrices whose original norms are polynomial in N, including fixed products of normalized E,F,K Ward coupons. Their completed-minus-original sourced products obey the same telescoping estimate with those polynomial factors. The equality is generally NOT exact for degree-lowering coupons; the known N=2 example becomes z_N times its original nonzero carry value. It is now smaller than any desired exponential rate by increasing tau. No moving-q normal identity is inferred. In particular let Q_in,Q_out be any of the specified physical Hopf/Ward matrices, of polynomial norm, satisfying the exact actual identity R_sigma Q_in=Q_out R_sigma. The deformed factor has ||R_(sigma,z_N) Q_in-Q_out R_(sigma,z_N)|| <=2 exp[(A-tau)N] (||Q_in||+||Q_out||). (13) Thus the damping can preserve the entire fixed finite collection of original Ward identities to an arbitrarily negative exponential order, even when their individual degree-lowering coupons detect the undamped carry. This is a norm statement on the original source complex. It does not identify stationary branches of an uncontrolled scalar factorization merely from those equations. ## 5. Exact scope for a global critical upper bound This is a source-preserving analytic completion with a verified absolute norm estimate for its entire source-zero overflow. Its matrix kernels are finite Laurent polynomials of degree O(N) on each local input/output pair, and (4) is polynomial in z of degree at most b-1. It can be inserted into the existing fixed-variable Euler/cyclic-dilog scalar networks; it introduces no hidden N-rank co-source or unknown scalar normalization. It does NOT prove that every stationary point of an arbitrary scalar factorization is physical, or that a raw scalar cycle can be replaced by its geometric contour. The idempotent (5), genuine degree-zero kernel, clock feedback and source/cycle boundaries remain. Excluding their nonphysical limiting stationary strata, or showing their aggregate cancellation, is the remaining task. In particular (11) is not an exponential estimate for W itself or for its original knot scalar. It removes the additional positive-N carry branches of this specified completion from that problem, with an arbitrarily strong bound rather than a formal source-null assertion alone. ## 6. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_exponentially_tame_carry_completion.py The audit verifies (5)--(6), degree-gauge covariance, literal signed inverses, and complete original one-cut/marked-plat sources for several nontrivial signed words. It independently tests the fusion factorization (8), the inverse Euler Toeplitz blocks, and the claimed original-metric inequalities on complex matrices. The all-level proof is (7)--(11), not a finite inference.

title: Complete-circle pruning through an exposed six-head source
text: # Complete-circle pruning through an exposed six-head source 29 October 2026. The actual saturated six-head source kills an unsaturated triple at an EXPOSED marked white vertex, before the unrestricted mark acts. The same argument kills unsaturated boundary triples in the typed three-port graph substitution. This is a whole source cancellation with all complete-circle normals retained. No bare mark is moved through a nested cap. ## 1. The actual support theorem being used Let O be the local ring of analytic functions at zeta=q=exp(pi i/N) and K its fraction field. For the generic balanced highest-weight-d physical module V_d(zeta), d=N-1, put Lambda_6=Inv_K(V_d(zeta)^tensor6) intersect V_d(O)^tensor6, S_N=Lambda_6/(zeta-q)Lambda_6. This is the ACTUAL saturated original-source specialization, not the span of one cup seed and not the whole enlarged root invariant space. The [proved six-port source support](actual_six_port_three_circle_support.md) states that on S_N the product of the three disjoint complete-circle sectors obeys (L_a tensor L_b tensor L_c) S_N=0 whenever a+b+c<d. (1) Each L_j is the full root sector of L_N, including its nilpotent first normal on a paired cluster. The source theorem proves (1) by clearing the absent generic joint corner. No root semisimplification or deletion of a derivative projector is involved. ## 2. A literal six-head ordinary removal Take the ordered NC/Morse graph and exposed white vertex v of the [corrected first-normal theorem](actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md). Its three edge slots are in increasing order. Omit ALL THREE cap arcs of that white vertex. All other white cap arcs are ordinary. Because the outer arc of v is exposed, these remaining caps can be removed in their actual innermost Morse order without closing or passing over any of the six retained physical heads. The last six heads are exactly the three ordered consecutive pairs at v. Also temporarily omit the three pair coupons incident to v. Define Y(zeta) to be the remaining physical six-head column, with the original cup source and every other edge coupon present in its chosen regular generic Hopf lift. Every cup, cap removal and internal edge map is a regular generic Hopf map. Thus Y(zeta) in Lambda_6, Y(q) in S_N. (2) The generic lifts may be analytic full-cluster Casimir polynomials, or the explicitly regular h0 W(zeta)pi(zeta) lifts with the correct root value. They must not be singular individual generic projectors. Membership (2) uses only their regularity and covariance. Actual integer H=0 is preserved by the source, coupons and cap removals. The omitted three coupons touch NONE of the other removed cap heads. They can therefore be applied LAST to the retained six heads as an exact index contraction. This is a commutation of maps on disjoint indices, not a braid or a tensor flip. For their original exponents, the observed physical column is Y_obs=(R^(e1)L_a tensor R^(e2)L_b tensor R^(e3)L_c)Y(q). (3) The R powers preserve each paired source and are invertible, so (1) gives Y_obs=0 when a+b+c<d. Only AFTER this equality are the three remaining arcs closed by two ordinary caps and the original full m. Consequently their marked source is zero, without invoking any local invariant property of m or replacing it by an ordinary covector. The conclusion holds for every internal channel assignment, with all its phases and normals. It proves that an exposed marked-white unsaturated term in the first-normal formula cancels COHERENTLY: [product_(other vertices)s_v(0)] s_mark'(0) Xi_Gamma(0)=0. (4) If another source factor is zero the same conclusion already follows directly or by the multiple-zero rule. A local s_mark' can be nonzero; (4) is a whole-source compatibility relation, not its local deletion. Together with the existing black and ordinary-white zero statements, the complete exposed NC graph source can be summed using ONLY labels with J_v>=d at EVERY vertex, including the marked one. ## 3. The unsupported three-port seam is zero before its exterior For the typed graph substitution in [the three-port sewing theorem](actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md), B has an outer white block on slots (0,k,E_B-1). Omit its three caps and its three incident pair coupons. This is exactly the ordinary removal above, giving a physical Y_B(q) in S_N. In the new graph its three boundary coupons occur ONCE each on the merged edges; all other maps lie in B or in A's exterior. Their product annihilates Y_B(q) when the shared triple has sum <d. Hence the entire B source column is zero before pairing with ANY exterior supplied by A. Thus the unsupported triangular seam term is zero as an actual source, not a zero divided by a marked theta scalar. The exact whole raw gluing rule is Z_new=sum_(a+b+c>=d) Z_A(a,b,c) Z_B(a,b,c)/Z_theta(a,b,c). (5) The complete coherent interior sums are taken inside each Z_A,Z_B; the three shared boundary labels are summed once and stay correlated. Z_theta is the proved strictly positive all-channel marked expression. There is no omitted unsaturated correction in THIS typed complete- circle operation. An ordinary open coefficient may have nonzero higher normals there, but the original fixed first-normal source is zero by (1)--(3). ## 4. What is not annihilated An unsupported open S_N cell can carry a nonzero marked functional. Equation (1) kills its TOP COMPLETE-CIRCLE observation, not the cell or its lower moments. The correlated boundary torsor is unchanged. Nor does this argument apply to a bare mark at a nested cap: omitting that vertex can leave enclosing cap annuli across the retained heads, so the same untransported six-head array need not satisfy (2). The assumption of COMPLETE circle color is essential. Replacing L_N by a different ordinary auxiliary color gives different spectral values and normals; its product is not the top product in (1). No auxiliary-color corridor or filling-current pruning is asserted. The [focused sewing audit](../experiments/audit_actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.py) constructs the actual physical Y before boundary circles, checks its ordinary six-head Ward equations and extracted divided-power kernel, then verifies its full observed zero on an unsaturated boundary. The all-N proof is the regular-source membership and the already proved all-N source support (1), not extrapolation from those levels. The source theorem retains the nested-cap countercurrent and requires the stated cap-removal order, saturated-lattice membership, regular lifts and disjoint coupon commutation. It is not a norm estimate or a general graph-volume claim.

title: External circle reflection and its primitive cusp normalization
status: Exact reflection; mesoscopic Fourier and primitive cusp
text: # External circle reflection and its primitive cusp normalization 30 October 2026. The original color N-h circle splits exactly into a cosine-weighted COMPLETE circle and a literal small-color circle. This gives a precise interface to the positive face coefficient without discarding any root Casimir normal. The rectangle calculation independently identifies the primitive cusp shape associated with the folded Gaussian. Neither calculation proves the missing general complex external-color packet or its global gap. The exact cosine core was already identified in the [entire core-color compiler](actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md). The new interface here is its positive face-coefficient realization, its retained small-color and normal terms, and the independent primitive rectangle normalization. ## 1. The actual full-matrix polynomial identity Put N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N). To distinguish the two Chebyshev normalizations, write C_m(z)=2T_m(z/2), P_m(z)=U_m(z/2), C_0=2, C_1=z; P_0=1, P_1=z. The [literal mixed-circle theorem](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) proves, on the two original complete physical targets, L_n=(-1)^(n-1)P_(n-1)(Omega), 1<=n<=N, C_N(Omega)=-2I. (1) The auxiliary module has dimension n and its actual pivot K_n^(1-N). There is no additional 1/n trace factor. Equation (1) includes every double-node Jordan coefficient and the odd simple Steinberg node. Define L_0=0. For 1<=h<N the elementary sine subtraction formula proves the POLYNOMIAL identity P_(N-h-1)(z)=T_h(z/2)P_(N-1)(z) -T_N(z/2)P_(h-1)(z). Substitution of (1), with its signs, gives L_(N-h)=(-1)^h T_h(Omega/2)L_N+(-1)^N L_h. (2) The same equation holds at h=0 using T_0=1 and L_0=0. The value T_N(Omega/2)=-I is supplied by the actual full pair relation, not by checking only its repeated eigenvalues. For the INTERNAL complete-circle label 0<=a<=floor(d/2), put s_a=d-2a, c_a=q^(2a+1)+q^(-2a-1), L_(N,a)=h0_a W_a pi_a. These are the actual complete sectors, including the nilpotent ones. At a double node L_N(c_a)=0, so multiplying by T_h retains exactly T_h(c_a/2)L_N'(c_a); its apparent T_h' term is multiplied by zero. At the odd simple node the ordinary value is retained. Therefore (-1)^h T_h(Omega/2)L_N =sum_a cos(pi h s_a/N) L_(N,a). (3) Here (-1)^h cos(pi h(2a+1)/N)=cos(pi h s_a/N) follows from 2a+1=N-s_a and the INTEGER external deficit h. In particular no auxiliary color is being identified with an internal channel. ## 2. An exact subset expansion of the original mixed source At R specified original circle ports substitute (2), tensor with all spectators, and keep each R_i^epsilon_i, physical cup/cap, unrestricted original mark and exterior framing line. Multilinearity gives a sum over subsets J of the ports. At i in J retain the literal small-color operator L_(h_i); at i outside J retain the weighted complete sum (3). The subset scalar is (-1)^(N|J|). A port with h_i=0 cannot occur in a nonzero such subset term. The term J=empty is EXACTLY F_N(h)=chi_(D,N) N^R sum_a product_i[k_ai beta_ai^2 omega_ai^epsilon_i cos(pi h_i s_ai/N)] C_(N,a), (4) where C_(N,a) is the [original positive face coefficient](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md), beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, k_a=1 at s_a=0 and2 otherwise, and omega_a=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)]. The physical-source notation and finite scalar of that theorem are unchanged. Equation (4) applies to its connected original plat scope, independently of the additional geometric certificate used for asymptotics. Consequently F_N(Nx) is an entire, separately even finite cosine polynomial in the EXTERNAL variables x_i. Its frequencies are the INTERNAL integer deficits s_ai. This is a specified exact finite function, not an interpolation inferred from sampled asymptotics. The nonempty-J terms are not known errors. They contain ordinary simple channels killed by L_N and the full value/normal blocks of the [mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), equations(7),(8). They must remain until a bound on their ACTUAL contractions is proved. There is a necessary far-end cancellation even for one port. Since s_a=d modulo2, the polynomial in (4) satisfies F_N(N-h)=(-1)^(N-1)F_N(h). (5) Thus the complete cosine term alone has an opposite-end alias with the full complete rate. It cannot provide the entire external-color gap. Outside the physical high-color range, F_N is the displayed algebraic subset term, not a redefinition of the older compiler's physical low-color core, which was set to zero. Extending the algebraic convention to h=N, the two terms in (2) cancel exactly to L_0=0. This does not wrap a physical auxiliary color; it records the endpoint cancellation that an estimate of the combined original source must respect. ## 3. The genuine first normal has explicit additional terms Keep d fixed and let zeta=q exp(epsilon). Define the signed STANDARD-pivot polynomial family Ltilde_j(epsilon)=(-1)^(j-1)P_(j-1)(Omega(epsilon)), Delta_N(epsilon)=C_N(Omega(epsilon))+2I. The polynomial identity before specialization is Ltilde_(N-h)=(-1)^h T_h Ltilde_N+(-1)^N Ltilde_h +(-1)^(N+1)Delta_N Ltilde_h/2. (6) All T_h here have the actual moving Casimir argument. Delta_N(0)=0 but Delta_N'(0) is generally nonzero. Its first-normal contribution cannot be deleted by differentiating the root relation (1). In fact that defect itself has an exact complete-sector resolution: Delta_N'(0)=sum_a (-1)^N N s_a [q^(2a+1)-q^(-2a-1)] L_(N,a). (7) To prove this without a differentiated root identity, use the actual generic eigenvalues from the mixed compiler. At a double pair a,d-a, put w=q^(2a+1), A=2N-1-2a, B=2a+1. The eigenvalues are zeta^A+zeta^-A and zeta^B+zeta^-B. Their difference is -2N(w-w^-1)epsilon+O(epsilon^2). The corresponding Delta values are -N^2 A^2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^4) and -N^2 B^2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^4). Their divided difference is therefore [2N^2 s_a/(w-w^-1)] epsilon+O(epsilon^2). The exact linear interpolation on this generic two-dimensional spectral block now gives Delta_N'(0) as that coefficient times its root Casimir nilpotent. Dividing by the original L_N'(c_a)=(-1)^d 2N/(4-c_a^2) proves (7). Unpaired simple blocks have zero first derivative; the odd self-node has s_a=0 and also contributes zero. This proves (7) on every physical degree block. There is a SECOND distinction: the original moving auxiliary pivot is K_j^(1-N), not its fixed-root replacement (-1)^(j-1)K_j. Let H_j have weights j-1-2r and let M_j(epsilon) be the literal typed monodromy [2,1,1,2]. Exactly, K_j^(1-N)=(-1)^(j-1)K_j exp(-N epsilon H_j). Thus, with the actual standard trace identity kept before the limit, (Llit_j)'(0)=(Ltilde_j)'(0)-N B_j, B_j=(-1)^(j-1)Tr_aux[K_j(q)H_j M_j(q)]. (8) Set B_0=0 along with the algebraic convention L_0=0. Combining (6),(8) gives the literal first-normal reflection: retain the derivatives of (-1)^h T_h L_N and (-1)^N L_h, then add (-1)^(N+1)Delta_N'(0)L_h/2 +N[(-1)^h T_h B_N+(-1)^N B_h-B_(N-h)]. (9) The derivative of T_h(Omega(epsilon)/2) is included. Every spectator, source cup, mark and exposed trace normalization still has its own derivative when the identity is contracted. No whole-source generic normal is replaced by a root value. Equations(2),(3) already retain the spectral normals f'(c); these are distinct from epsilon derivatives. ## 4. The actual tangent-circle rectangle fixes the factor two At one original crossing disk let x,y be the outer white-circle curvatures and b,c its two middle curvatures. They are the SAME shared face variables (circle curvatures) used by the coefficient theorem, with zero for either of the two marked white lines. Put A=x+y, T_b=sqrt(bA+xy), T_c=sqrt(cA+xy), C=pi(T_b+T_c)/A. (10) The certified rectangle is nondegenerate, so A>0 and T_b+T_c>0. For positive x,y,b,c put the outer tangency at z=0 and their centers at1/x and -1/y. Under the conformal inversion w=1/z their circles become the white lines Re w=x/2 and Re w=-y/2. For a middle circle of curvature b above that tangency, its original center is (x-y)/(bA)+i 2T_b/(bA), radius1/b. This follows by squaring its two external tangency equations. Its center norm squared minus radius squared is4/(bA); inversion therefore gives center (x-y)/4-i T_b/2 and radius A/4. The middle c circle on the other side gives center (x-y)/4+i T_c/2. The orthogonal shaded planes are the horizontal lines through these centers. Hence the actual crossing-circle rectangle has white-line width W=A/2, shaded-line height H=(T_b+T_c)/2. (11) The zero-curvature cases follow by the same formulas and continuous line limits. No auxiliary color or finite off-critical frame has been substituted for this complete circle packing. The [original two-rectangle cusp marking](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), section6, has even meridian spanning height H and disk longitude spanning TWO widths. In its positive orientation, tau_geom,0=2i W/H=2i A/(T_b+T_c)=2pi i/C. (12) The area of this primitive basis is2WH, the area of the two actual rectangles. This accounts for the factor2; one rectangle width alone would give the wrong longitude. For the SOURCE half twist R^epsilon, the already typed collar calibration in the [channel Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), section3, gives tau_geom,epsilon=tau_geom,0/(1-epsilon tau_geom,0/2) =2pi i/(C-pi i epsilon). (13) Source epsilon=-1 is the geometric '+' collar. This is the marked diagonal meridian in the half-twisted cusp lattice, not a claim that half of the longitude is an integral loop in the original lattice. ## 5. The exact empty-subset term has a mesoscopic complex Gaussian law Assume the fixed connected labeled right-angled certificate of the [signed complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Let A_N^epsilon=F_N(0) be the original complete signed source. Let l_N be its all-maximal positive coefficient radius, and retain Z_i,N=C_i(l_N)-pi i epsilon_i with Re Z_i,N>=c>0. For every fixed compact complex polydisc K, F_N(sqrt(N) z)/A_N^epsilon =exp[-pi^2 sum_i z_i^2/Z_i,N] [1+o(1)] (14) uniformly for z in K. All fixed z derivatives converge uniformly on smaller compact polydiscs to the derivatives of the displayed Gaussian. This is an absolute derivative statement, not a relative estimate at zeros of a differentiated Gaussian. Here is a direct proof retaining both finite lattices. Write a_i=M-t_i, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M in {0,1}. The signed theorem gives the actual relative sector weights uniformly for max t_i<=N^(1/2+delta), 0<delta<1/6, as exp[-sum_i Z_i,N t_i(t_i+s0)/N] [1+o(1)]. The extra factor is cos(pi z_i(2t_i+s0)/sqrt(N)). At odd levels k_M=1 and all other multiplicities are2; at even levels all are2. Thus u=t+s0/2 gives the full integer or half-integer Gaussian, with the retained factor exp(Z_i,N s0^2/(4N)). Uniform Riemann summation on either lattice gives sqrt(N) integral_R exp(-Z x^2)cos(2pi z x) dx =sqrt(pi N) Z^(-1/2) exp(-pi^2 z^2/Z). The square root has positive real part. The integral follows first for real positive Z and then by holomorphy on Re Z>0. Its convergence is uniform on the stated compact sets of Z and complex z. The original source tails remain controlled. The cosine product costs at most C exp(C sum_i t_i/sqrt(N)), so the central absolute majorant is exp(-c|t|^2/N+C|t|/sqrt(N)). The uniform relative sector error therefore contributes o(N^(R/2)). Beyond the mesoscopic window and below the fixed macroscopic cutoff, the proved common-radius bound is a fixed polynomial times that same Gaussian majorant, and its tail tends to zero. Beyond the macroscopic cutoff the original rate gap exp(-cN+o(N)) loses at most exp(C sqrt(N)), and remains a gap. Thus these sums concern the full finite F_N, not just a chosen window. Divide by the nonzero signed complete asymptotic. Its common exterior phase and omega_M factors cancel literally. The Gaussian is bounded away from zero on K. Finally Cauchy's formula on a slightly larger compact polydisc proves the derivative assertion. Equation (14) concerns the EXACT empty-subset term. It does not bound any nonempty-J small-color diagram, identify it with the whole mixed source, or give a fixed complex neighborhood of h/N. ## 6. The primitive Hessian matching and remaining external problem The [signed complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) has folded weight exp[-Z t(t+s0)/N], where Z=C-pi i epsilon, s0=d-2floor(d/2), and s=s0+2t. The cosine in (3) is therefore in exactly the normalization whose Gaussian transform has the candidate quadratic external action phi(x_ext)=Phi-pi^2 x_ext^2/Z+O(x_ext^4). (15) Equation (14) proves this Gaussian normalization on its mesoscopic scale; it does NOT assert a general fixed-neighborhood external asymptotic or an analytic action phi. If the required packet is proved, its retained similarity coordinates U=-2pi i x_ext and V=-2phi' give V/U=tau_geom,epsilon to first order by (13). In particular phi''(0)=pi i tau_geom,epsilon. The transfer template which writes phi''=2pi i tau_packet uses tau_packet=tau_geom,epsilon/2=pi i/Z. (16) This agrees with the existing marked channel elimination and keeps the primitive cusp shape separate from the packet's Hessian convention. A real sqrt(N) folded-window estimate does not imply a relative packet on a fixed COMPLEX external neighborhood: the relevant complex internal displacement is then of order N. The general nonempty-J small-color contractions, the combined far-color and alias gap, and the actual nonlinear marked regulator comparison remain necessary inputs to [general long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md), equations(2)--(5). None is claimed here. The external h_i and the internal s_i,a_i remain different variables throughout. ## 7. A strict bound for the all-small untwisted subset One subset admits an immediate literal bound. Assume EVERY circle is replaced by L_(h_i), h_i>=1, and every retained epsilon_i is zero. Write B_N^small(h) for this original marked contraction. In the original balanced complete physical basis, F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=(Q^(-u)-1)|u-1>, K|u>=q^d Q^(-u)|u>. Thus ||F||,||Ecal||<=2 and ||K||=||K^-1||=1. The original coproducts F12=F tensor I+K^-1 tensor F and Ecal12=Ecal tensor K+I tensor Ecal have norms at most4. Hence ||Omega||<=18. Its exact Chebyshev recurrence gives by induction ||L_h||<=19^(h-1), retaining its actual full matrix. The k bottom cups have norms N^(3/2), the k-1 ordinary caps have norms N^(-1/2), and the unrestricted marked cap has norm N^-1: their respective supported entries have moduli N,1/N,1/N^2, with N,N,N^2 entries. The exterior framing factor is a unit. The literal matrix contraction therefore satisfies |B_N^small(h)|<=N^(k-1/2) 19^[sum_i(h_i-1)]. (17) If any h_i=0 this algebraic subset term is zero. Equation(17) is subexponential for h_i=O(sqrt(N)). For a fixed certified positive-volume exterior, it also gives a strict gap below F0=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi) throughout 1<=h_i<=delta N whenever delta R log19<F0. This covers only J=all ports and epsilon_i=0. A proper subset still contains its actual complete coupons; a signed port still contains R^epsilon. Neither may be deleted from the norm estimate. No general proper-subset gap, signed small-color bound, or mixed packet follows from (17), and no generic-q normal is inferred from this root estimate. ## 8. Verification and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp_results.json), checks 78 formal polynomial identities, 54 full root matrix reflections, 204 actual complete-sector weights, 54 genuine polynomial first jets, and nine full Casimir-relation normal defects. Six exact inversion identities and nine primitive/packet Hessian identities check the geometric normalization. An additional 216 complex Gaussian comparisons retain both finite fold lattices and their first two derivatives; they are checks of the Gaussian step, not substitutes for the source-tail proof of (14). title: The original factorial interpolant is exactly a full-Psi quotient
text: # The original factorial interpolant is exactly a full-Psi quotient 28 October 2026. The normalized factorial interpolation used for the original finite sums is the SAME full Faddeev function already used in the relative moment source. There is no residual period-one multiplier. This supplies a literal five-full-Psi formula for every original physical crossing coefficient, including its support zeros and complete scalar. This is a normalization comparison inside the existing double-sine/Barnes framework. It is not a new quantum invariant or a selected-cycle theorem. ## 1. Exact identity and elimination of the periodic ambiguity Let N>=2, h=2pi*i/N, d=N-1 and use the exactly normalized functions Fhat_N and G_N of [the factorial theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). Let Psi be the original positive full function and phi_N=Psi(h)=sqrt(N)exp{i pi[1/4-(N+1/N)/12]}. Then as meromorphic functions of z, Fhat_N(z)=phi_N/Psi(h(z+1)). (1) Here is an independent proof fixing the possible period-one ambiguity. Both sides are nonzero and holomorphic on -1<Re z<N. For Fhat this was proved from its convergent Gamma product. For Psi use the proved identification Psi(Z)=Phi_(1/sqrt(N))(sqrt(N)Z/(2pi)-c_b). The zero-free strip |Im argument|<Im c_b becomes precisely 0<Im Z<2pi(1+1/N), or -1<Re z<N. These strip and conjugation facts are proved from the defining integral in [the full-Phi audit](faddeev_pentagon_audit.md), not assumed from a published pentagon. The two first-shift equations imply that H(z)=Fhat_N(z)Psi(h(z+1))/phi_N is one-periodic on their overlap. It extends to an entire, nowhere-zero one-periodic function by translations of this strip. Fix an entire logarithm L of H. On a central vertical strip of width one, both signs of log|H| have the bound |Re L(z)|<=C_N(1+|Im z|^2 log(2+|Im z|)). (2) For clarity this is a rough FIXED-N growth estimate, not a semiclassical estimate. The finite Barnes-G expression for Fhat proves it directly. All its Gamma/Barnes arguments have positive real parts in this strip. The convergent digamma series gives psi(w)=O(log(2+|w|)) there; integrating the proved derivative d_w log BarnesG(1+w) =w psi(1+w)-w-1/2+(log(2pi))/2 along a vertical line bounds its logarithm by O(t^2 log(2+|t|)). The same estimates bound both numerator and denominator in the finite Barnes product. The full-Phi left/right asymptotics on a fixed horizontal strip bound the Psi part, including its reciprocal, by a quadratic logarithm. This proves (2). Periodicity extends it to the whole plane. An entire harmonic function with growth O(R^2 log R) has zero derivatives of every order at least three: its circle Fourier coefficients of order ell are O(R^(2-ell)log R), tending to zero for ell>=3. Apply this to Re L, or the harmonic Cauchy formula. Thus L is a polynomial of degree at most two. Periodicity of H forces L(z+1)-L(z) to be a constant 2pi*i*m, m integer, so the quadratic coefficient is zero. Since H(0)=1, H(z)=exp(2pi*i*m z). (3) Finally take Re z=d/2. The real Gamma product and exact reflection G_N(z)G_N(d-z)=N give |G_N(z)|=sqrt(N). The modulus of the explicit Gaussian factor in Fhat is ONE on this line, hence |Fhat|=sqrt(N). The argument h(z+1) has Im equal to pi(1+1/N); its Faddeev argument is real. The proved conjugation identity therefore gives |Psi|=1. As |phi_N|=sqrt(N), we have |H|=1 on this entire vertical line. Equation (3) now forces m=0. This proves (1), including its phase. ## 2. Exact five-function original crossing coefficient For the positive physical crossing with input (a,b), total transfer k, and output (b+k,a-k), the original coefficient is r_plus(a,b,k)=kappa x^(-a-b+k)Q^(b(a-k)) F_(b+k)F_a/[F_k F_b F_(a-k)]. Apply (1) to the normalized interpolation in the transfer variable z. Its FULL function factor, with all fixed factors also expressed in Psi, is exactly Fhat(b+z)F_a/[Fhat(z)F_b Fhat(a-z)] =phi_N^(-1) Psi(h(b+1))Psi(h(z+1))Psi(h(a-z+1)) /[Psi(h(a+1))Psi(h(b+z+1))]. (4) The original Cartan monomial and kappa remain unchanged. Formula (4) is a literal equality, not an equality up to a central factor. Its negative version is the actual balanced antiunitary mirror, with the opposite full function and conjugate marked constants. At every physical integer z in [0,d], forbidden transfers z>a or b+z>=N are EXACT zeros of this expression. They are the actual pole/zero cancellations of the completed function. The half-integer rectangle of [the endpoint-packet theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md) therefore represents the original finite transfer sum directly with these five functions, preserving all corners and source data. The five classical arguments are B, A/V, V, A and T/V, where A=Q^a, B=Q^b, V=Q^(a-z), T=AB. Their signed sum is exactly the original direct crossing symbol -[A]-[T/V]+[V]+[B]+[A/V]. Thus no extra auxiliary nine-to-five calibration is needed in THIS physical coefficient chart. This does not remove the true transfer boundary current (the low normal packet has the nonzero source in equation (12) of the endpoint theorem), provide an infinite-height quadrature estimate, or establish a global cycle with a sharp bound. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.py): independent Barnes-G versus completed full-Psi evaluations, original allowed/forbidden transfer values and exact normal/source identities.

# Exact homogeneous insertion for a far-charge coupon, and why it is not an identity insertion , 31 October 2026. This accompanies the [whole-domain large-charge theorem](actual_whole_domain_large_charge_tail.md). It supplies an exact source coefficient bound, not a shared volume or capacity theorem. ## 1. The full face-grid transform gives a coefficient bound For ANY actual fixed-root Casimir coupon $F=f(\Omega)$, with the complete Hermite data retained, its homogeneous kernel has degree $d=N-1$: $$ H_F(x,b,c,y)=\sum_{a+i+t+s=d}h_{a,i,t,s}\,x^ab^ic^ty^s. $$ Set $c=1$ and sample the THREE independent original clock cosets $$ b=Q^p,\qquad x=-qQ^r,\qquad y=-q^{-1}Q^s,\qquad0\leq p,r,s<N. $$ The actual input clocks $U=-q^{-1}x/b$ and $V=-q^{-1}b/y$ are respectively $Q^{r-p},Q^{p-s}$, and the output relation $c=Q^{-p}b$ is literal. Write canonical physical heads $u=[r-p]_N$, $v=[p-s]_N$, $R=r$, $S=[-s]_N$, and retain the TRUE integer displacement $\Delta=R-u$. The [original local matrix/grid identity](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) therefore says $$ H_F(-qQ^r,Q^p,1,-q^{-1}Q^s)=Nq^{d\Delta}F_{R,S;u,v}.	ag{1} $$ Although $\Delta$ is congruent to $p$ modulo $N$, their phase ratio is $(-1)^{d(\Delta-p)/N}$, which cannot be dropped at even levels. For example $N=4$, $p=3$, $r=0$, $s=1$ has $u=1$, $v=2$, $R=0$, $S=3$ and $\Delta=-1$, a valid nonzero transition with the opposite carry sign. If canonical representatives violate unwrapped total conservation, the right side is zero, exactly as is the left side by the original physical endpoint factors. No nonphysical wrap is inserted. All coset and $q$ factors in (1) have modulus one, at both parities. Every exponent of $H_F(x,b,1,y)$ is between $0$ and $d<N$. Its coefficients are thus recovered WITHOUT aliases by the three-dimensional inverse DFT on this grid, with the fixed coset phases removed. Consequently $$ |h_{a,i,t,s}|\leq N\max_{\mathrm{physical\ entries}}|F_{\mathrm{entry}}| \leq N\|F\|_{\mathrm{op}}.	ag{2} $$ The remaining exponent $t=d-a-i-s$ is fixed by homogeneity. In particular this is not an estimate that loses an exponential basis conversion. It uses the SAME original balanced physical tensor basis as the endpoint and Fourier-tail theorems. Let $h_d(x,b,c,y)=\sum_{a+i+t+s=d}x^ab^ic^ty^s$ denote the complete homogeneous polynomial with all coefficients $1$. Then $$ |H_F|_{\mathrm{coef}}\preceq N\|F\|h_d.	ag{3} $$ An entire spectral function of $\Omega$ still reduces to its unique finite Hermite polynomial, so (1)-(3) apply to the absolutely summed far-charge coupon $T_{N,n;M}$ as well. Combined with the tail theorem, for $M=\lceil|n|/2+1+Dceil$, $$ |H_T|_{\mathrm{coef}}\preceq e^{N\varepsilon(D)+o(N)}h_d.	ag{4} $$ with the horizontal tail already made decreasing. The $o(N)$ is uniform in $N$ for each fixed $n,D$. No arbitrary face radius has replaced an original marked coefficient. ## 2. The precise partial-source coefficient family Insert $T_i$ on a nonempty subset $S$ and keep the exact original $R_j^{n_j}$ on its complement. Multilinearity gives the finite identity $$ Z=\sum_{\substack{\kappa_i\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^4,\ |\kappa_i|=d\i\in S}} \left[\prod_{i\in S}h_{T_i}(\kappa_i)ight] \left[L^{\,\mathbf d-\sum_{i\in S}\kappa_i}ight] \prod_{j
otin S}H_{R_j^{n_j}}.	ag{5} $$ Here $\mathbf d$ is the original target vector, and each $\kappa_i$ is extended by zero to the other original faces. Terms with any negative target, including a positive allocation to either protected zero face, are zero. There are at most $O(N^{3|S|})$ terms. Thus (4) bounds this source by a polynomial number of the ACTUAL shifted-target coefficients in (5), with an arbitrarily small extra rate $\sum_i\varepsilon(D_i)$. Those shifted coefficients, with their original signed phases, are the remaining source-specific problem. The fixed-radius growth of $h_d$ is $\log\max(x,b,c,y)$, because its number of monomials is polynomial in $N$. It is not $\log\max(b,c)$, the rate of $H_1$. In particular (4) is NOT an identity-insertion or smoothing theorem. ## 3. Full Fejer entropy is not everywhere nonnegative A proposed shortcut would replace a port by $h_d$, note its entropy $0$, and appeal to nonnegativity of the removed full Fejer entropy $h$. That nonnegativity is false for an ACTUAL coefficient. At even $N=2m$ let $a_r=4\cos^2((r+1/2)\pi/N)$, $s_j=2\sin(j\pi/N)$, and $P=(-1)^d H_{V_N(-2)}$. The monomial $x^jc^{d-j}$, with $b=y=0$ and $0\leq j<m$, comes from the unique all-one-step path from $j$ to $0$. Since $\prod_{r=0}^d a_r=4$, its exact coefficient is $$ [x^jc^{d-j}]P= rac{4\prod_{r=1}^j s_r^2}{\prod_{r=0}^j a_r}.	ag{6} $$ Take $j/N	o
u\in(0,1/2)$. The integrable endpoint Riemann sums give $$ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log igl([x^jc^{d-j}]P igr) =2\int_0^
u\log	an(\pi t)\,dt=E(0,

u=1/4$ and returns to $0$ only at $1/2$. At $
u=1/4$ its value is $-2G/\pi$, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. This is the established CLOSED half-block coefficient entropy and the actual one-sided branch of $h$; there is no omitted source scalar. Replacing (6) by coefficient $1$ of $h_d$ increases this local entropy. The endpoint maximum's uniqueness therefore does not by itself imply a strict gap after an $h_d$ insertion. This is a local obstruction to THAT comparison, not a global source counterexample. ## 4. The far-charge endpoint functional is not scalar identity There is also a direct phase-preserving fixed-$N$ check. Keep $N,n$ fixed, $n
e0$, and let $\ell$ tend to positive infinity. For the exact whole- interval $B_{N,n}$ in the tail note, $$  egin{aligned} B(1/2)&=B(-1/2)=0,\qquad B'(1/2)=B'(-1/2),\ B''(1/2)-B''(-1/2)&=-8\pi^2inN e^{\pi inN/4}V_N(2). \end{aligned}	ag{8} $$ The source is odd in $\delta$, so its third derivatives also agree at the two endpoints. Five integrations by parts, keeping all endpoint terms, yield $$  egin{aligned} J_{N,n,\ell}&=(-1)^{N\ell}e^{\pi inN/4} rac{nV_N(2)}{\pi N^2\ell^3} +O_{N,n}(\ell^{-5}),\ F_{N,n,\ell}&=q^{nd^2/4}e^{\pi inN/4} \left[- rac{in(-1)^\ell V_N(2)}{\pi N^2\ell^2}ight]+O_{N,n}(\ell^{-4}). \end{aligned}	ag{9} $$ Using the exact sign-charge equality and the elementary alternating tail sum, this also gives $$ T_{N,n;M}=q^{nd^2/4}e^{\pi inN/4} \left[- rac{in(-1)^{M+1}V_N(2)}{\pi N^2M^2}ight]+O_{N,n}(M^{-3}).	ag{10} $$ These limits are ONLY $\ell$ or $M	o\infty$ at fixed $N$; they are not interchanges with the level limit in (4). They identify the actual endpoint coupon: $V_N(2)=4(2-\Omega)^{-1}$, rather than $I$. For example the one-step $xc^{d-1}$ coefficient is a nonzero negative step weight times a product of positive factors $2-c_r$. Thus $H_{V_N(2)}$ has nonzero outer powers, and (10) gives the same nonzero outer coefficient for every sufficiently large $M$ at fixed $N,n$. Therefore literal coefficientwise domination by a multiple of $H_1$, whose outer powers vanish, cannot hold for every far coupon. The correct possible next step is a source-specific bound for these near-+2 coupons and shifted targets, not replacement by identity. ## Validation and scope The finite carry check uses the actual original Casimir entry; it is not a new large-level estimate. The fixed-level large-charge limits in (9)–(10) are never interchanged with the level limit. title: Exact Gaussian stabilization preserves the unresolved geometric source
text: # Exact Gaussian stabilization preserves the unresolved geometric source 28 October 2026. The finite Fourier kernel in the actual clock-feedback theorem has a nonzero coefficient with normalization exactly one. Its Jacobian and transverse determinant can be computed without assumptions about a geometric saddle. But it is an exact stabilization of the SAME coupled action and the SAME original source. It does not supply the missing geometric intersection number. This answers a specific possible shortcut: Fourier-Gaussian ellipticity does not turn the already known geometric normal block into a selected global geometric contribution. No claim about the impossibility of a different global contour construction is made. ## 1. The finite feedback extension splits exactly Use the primitive variables and actual diagram matrix T of [the feedback theorem](actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md), not independent physical spectator parameters. There are m crossings. On a coefficient R^nu Y^h the normalized finite Fourier realization is N^(-m) sum_(eta,lambda in (Z/N)^m) Q^[-lambda dot eta+lambda dot h+nu^T T eta]. (1) The clock h is the actual over-monotone clock; nu is the integer primitive Laurent exponent. Every original closure, pivot, dimension, framing and Cartan factor remains in its coefficient and its specified charged source. Equation (1) is only the exact feedback kernel. Make the finite change of variables eta=h+u, lambda=T^T nu+v, (2) with all entries interpreted modulo N in this finite sum. For EVERY integer nu,h and EVERY diagram T, this is a bijection, and its exponent is exactly -lambda eta+lambda h+nu^T T eta =nu^T T h-v dot u mod N. (3) Thus (1) is Q^(nu^T T h) * N^(-m) sum_(u,v)Q^(-v dot u) =Q^(nu^T T h). (4) For each fixed u the v sum is N^m if u=0 and zero otherwise. The extra Gaussian therefore has coefficient ONE, at every N, with no determinant character, unknown periodic unit or knot normalization. This statement survives the original source pairing, including the contracted closure jets. Indeed the change (2) does not change nu or h, and (4) holds coefficientwise before any anchor substitution, charged coefficient, clock sum or external scalar. Hence those operations commute with eliminating this normalized Gaussian. No source division is used. It is important that the shifts in (2) depend on the coefficient momenta nu,h. They describe a canonical Fourier stabilization, not a single substitution of the physical spectator coordinates. They cannot be used to replace the coupled action by the zero-feedback action. ## 2. Exact Jacobian and Hessian comparison The same fact has a precise local stationary interpretation. Let x be any regular local phase coordinates, with scaled momenta nu(x),h(x). Write alpha=2*pi*i and let S_0(x) be the independent coefficient action. The extended action is S_ext(x,eta,lambda)=S_0(x) +alpha[lambda(h(x)-eta)+nu(x)^T T eta]. (5) Use the local change eta=h(x)+u, lambda=T^T nu(x)+v. (6) Its full Jacobian, including x, is block triangular with identity on the diagonal, so its determinant is EXACTLY one. There is the exact identity of functions, not just of quadratic terms, S_ext=S_act(x)-alpha v dot u, S_act=S_0+alpha nu(x)^T T h(x). (7) Consequently the critical scheme is the product of that of S_act with u=v=0, including multiplicities and local Artin rings. At a critical point the Hessian is congruent to Hess(S_act) direct_sum [[0,-alpha I],[-alpha I,0]]. (8) Thus nullity Hess(S_ext)=nullity Hess(S_act), det Hess(S_ext)=(-1)^m alpha^(2m)det Hess(S_act) (9) when the determinants are defined in the full coordinates. The same formula applies to nondegenerate transverse slices in a Morse--Bott germ, with the original radical retained. The normalized Fourier half-density has the exact coefficient (4), so this auxiliary block changes no selected transverse amplitude or residual source density. Equations (5)-(9) are used only when a regular coefficient phase is available. They do not assert uniform asymptotics across a finite window, an endpoint, or a singular Fourier chart. Equation (4) itself has none of those restrictions. ## 3. The complete geometric fixed set is not isolated by this operation There is a concrete obstruction to applying an isolated-fixed-point Bethe/Lefschetz formula after merely adding this feedback kernel. For the actual marked knot critical scheme, simultaneous conjugation by B_1=Stab_(PGL_2)(1) preserves the chosen inverse cut flag and all closed braid equations. This group has dimension two. At the complete discrete-faithful representation its projective centralizer is trivial, so its orbit is a smooth two-dimensional family of distinct marked critical points. This is exactly the framing torsor in [the actual geometric normal theorem](actual_geometric_normal_period.md), whose Hessian has that two-dimensional radical. In particular, for the regular marked Hurwitz return map Phi, its infinitesimal conjugation vectors obey D Phi(v)=v. Therefore det(I-D Phi)=0 before a stated framing reduction. Adding (1) does not repair that determinant: (7) preserves the critical germ and (8) preserves its radical. One may choose a transverse framing section and obtain the already proved nonzero normal Gaussian block. Its two-form must still be paired with the specified original relative source. Taking an arbitrary section or assigning its relative period the value one would add a source selection, rather than derive it from (4). The new closure contractions in [general flow fusion](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) do retain the original source exactly. Their full length-d block is the reproducing kernel of the finite source algebra: contraction through an arbitrary exterior implements substitution modulo the original nilpotent walls. It is an identity on the transmitted finite state space, with pivots retained. It supplies no additional framing section or condition on the geometric relative period. At a regular phase realization it removes identity-wire coordinates, not the conjugation orbit above. ## 4. Exact consequence for the critical path There is no unknown Gaussian normalization left in this part of the comparison. If a source-preserving regular phase comparison with the geometric chart is constructed, its feedback stabilization contributes one and leaves its geometric coefficient unchanged. This is useful normalization control. But the full source coefficient which would have to be shown nonzero is still the original one. Neither invertibility of G_T, its unit coefficient norm, the perfect socle pairing, nor the nonzero transverse determinant computes that coefficient. The precise unproved step is the image of the original relative class in the action-normalized geometric summand after the remaining framing/charge contraction. The Gaussian (1) does not weaken that step, since (4) eliminates it without changing that class. This result therefore rules out the proposed inference from a nonzero Fourier-Gaussian fiber to whole-source geometric survival. It is not a volume-conjecture proof, a new sharp scalar bound, or an assertion that a global positive contour cannot exist. ## 5. Reproducible audit [audit_actual_feedback_geometric_selection.py](../experiments/audit_actual_feedback_geometric_selection.py) checks (3)-(4) with actual diagram T rows, both crossing signs and arbitrary primitive exponent signs; compares the stabilized complete source with original pivotal signed matrices; and verifies the full Jacobian, stationary Hessian congruence, determinant and lifted framing radical on an explicit nonlinear regular phase germ. The finite identities and general proofs above are not inferred from the tests.

title: Simultaneous terminal reduction of the actual Fejer entropy source
text: # Simultaneous terminal reduction of the actual Fejer entropy source , 31 October 2026. The labeled right-angled certificate and the original protected MAIN edge are used. This does not license an arbitrary one-port relabel, which fails in the recorded width-three counterexample. No diagonal or other free endpoint is removed here. Use the finite pattern set A_D and limiting polytopes P_s of [the original shared entropy theorem](actual_fejer_shared_entropy_variational.md). Let s belong to A_D, and let q in P_s include the individual cross triangular allocations. Let J be the set of ALL its one-sided ports whose terminal parameter is nu=1/2. Replace every port in J by cross simultaneously, leaving all other types unchanged; call the new pattern s'. Then s' belongs to A_D. Moreover the SAME limiting global degree vector q belongs to P_s', and its local entropies can be preserved. Thus a maximizer for W_D can be chosen with no terminal one-sided ports. This statement does not assert that one may change only some of J while leaving the other terminal labels intact. ## 1. A strict all-cross middle margin from the actual geometry The existing certified complete circle packing supplies an all-cross angle flow q_geom on the same original incidence graph. Every port has total load1, every ordinary face has total1, and both original protected faces have total0. All its middle loads are STRICTLY less than1/2. To see this, the middle load is a single triangle center angle divided by2pi. A finite positive middle can have angle pi only if BOTH outer curvatures vanish. The two protected vertices form a MAIN edge, while the two outers of a source triangle form its MATCHING edge, so they cannot be those two vertices. A protected middle has load0. Since the original graph is fixed and finite, there is eta>0 such that EVERY middle incidence of q_geom is at most1/2-eta. This is an actual certified shared flow, not independently selected local radii or an assumed positive-class realization. ## 2. Strict margins and exact finite integral support At every port now marked cross in s', each middle incidence of q is at most1/2. This holds for the old cross ports and for the newly relabeled ones: their overloaded load is1/2, while their other middle load is mu<=nu=1/2. Every one-sided port left in s' has nu<1/2, so its overloaded load is strictly greater than1/2. If such ports remain, put delta=min_(remaining one-sided e)(q_over(e)-1/2)>0. Choose 0<epsilon<min(1/2,delta/2), ignoring the delta condition if no one-sided port remains, and set q_epsilon=(1-epsilon)q+epsilon q_geom. This convex combination preserves ALL original port supplies, face targets, incidence repetitions and protected zeros. Every new cross middle is at most1/2-epsilon eta. Every remaining overloaded middle is at least1/2+delta/2, since each individual incidence lies in[0,1] and its change under the combination is at most epsilon. Let gamma>0 be the smaller of these two margins (or only epsilon eta if there are no remaining one-sided ports). For N=2m,d=2m-1 multiply q_epsilon by d. This is a real bipartite flow with EXACT port supplies d, ordinary-face targets d and protected targets0. Integral cycle rounding, inside the floor/ceiling interval of every entry, gives an integer flow with the same exact balances and entrywise error at most1. No new auxiliary target is introduced. If d gamma>=2, its middle entries satisfy the original finite bounds: cross: d(1/2-gamma)+1<=m-1, one-sided: d(1/2+gamma)-1>=m. All other entries remain nonnegative and have sum d at each port; protected entries remain exactly zero. Consequently every port is in its actual original local support, including the forced outer unit at cross ports. This proves finite feasibility for EVERY even N with N-1>=2/gamma, hence s' belongs to A_D. The strict perturbation is used only to prove membership in A_D. It does not replace the desired limiting point q by q_epsilon. Once membership is known, the already proved source lattice-approximation lemma applies to q itself in P_s'. ## 3. Preserve the actual entropy and reduce the maximizing type For a left port with nu=1/2, the actual load and entropy are q=(xi,mu,1/2,1/2-mu-xi), E=C(xi,mu,1/2-mu-xi). Use this vector as the input cross triangle and the degenerate output triangle(0,1/2,0). Their cross load is exactly q and their entropy sum is exactly E, since C(0,1/2,0)=0. For a right port interchange the two triangles. Retain every existing cross allocation unchanged. Thus all shared limiting targets and the total entropy are preserved. If J is nonempty, the number of one-sided labels strictly decreases. In particular choose a maximizer for the compact W_D problem with the fewest one-sided labels among all maximizing representations. The preceding construction shows it has no terminal nu=1/2 one-sided port. If every one-sided port was terminal, the resulting pattern is all-cross and its value is bounded by the already proved complete geometric value Phi_D. The reduction leaves diagonal mu=nu, free lower endpoints, other outer-degree boundaries and ordinary-multiplier degenerations open. It also does not imply any individual finite term survives a Gaussian filling contour. ## Scope The terminal calculation concerns the finite source and entropy functional only; it gives no new quantum asymptotic estimate.

title: The even Fejér source: complete crossing paths and a forest remainder
status: Exact complete cross comparison and one-sided forest support
text: # The even Fejér source: complete crossing paths and a forest remainder Status update, 31 October 2026: the [full endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) now controls the entire positive source, and the [unique-maximizer theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) gives a strict exponential gap for the one-sided remainder under the same labeled certificate. The exact decomposition and the warnings about inferring bounds from forest topology alone remain valid. , 31 October 2026. This is an exact coefficient reduction at every even level N>=4 for the original connected fixed flat plat. No estimate of the remaining forest contribution is asserted. The shared original marked targets are unchanged. The geometric rate corollary assumes the same labeled right-angled certificate as the complete-source theorem. Let N=2m>=4,d=N-1, c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), s_j=2sin(jpi/N). In the actual face monomial basis, Omega z^j=c_j z^j-s_j^2(x+y)z^(j-1)-s_js_(j-1)xy z^(j-2). Use the [original homogeneous compiler](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md). Let chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2 and V_N(z)=chi_N(z)(z-Omega)^(-1), its polynomial resolvent numerator. Let P=-H_(V_N(-2)) be the positive Fejer homogeneous polynomial. The exact fixed-root resolvent convention is that of the [spectral derivative theorem](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md). Every path goes from its input j to its output i using steps1 or2; its middle exponents are b^i c^(d-j). A k-step path contributes its positive edge product times product_(unvisited r)(2+c_r), with the usual binomial expansion of its one-step factors (x+y). Split P=P_cross+P_left+P_right by cross: i<=m-1 and j>=m; left: j<=m-1; right: i>=m. These three classes partition the actual path set. Equivalently the cross part consists of monomials whose b and c exponents are both<=m-1. The two other classes have respectively c exponent>=m or b exponent>=m. Thus the decomposition is also by disjoint monomial supports, without any cancellation or selection of a new physical state. The three polynomials are parts of the original homogeneous coupon; they are not asserted separately to be covariant Casimir coupons or physical-head projections. The identity between the original source and the coefficient of their SUM is the frozen compiler identity. ## 1. Exact coefficientwise comparison for the entire cross part Put c_*=-2cos(pi/N), delta=2+c_*=4sin^2(pi/(2N)). The two minimum diagonal entries are c_(m-1)=c_m=c_*. At spectral value c_* the polynomial numerator has a nonzero path exactly when it visits BOTH indices m-1,m: otherwise its unused-factor product contains a zero. Call the resulting positive polynomial B=|H_(V_N(c_*))|_coef.
