For a path visiting both central indices, its coefficient at -2 divided by its coefficient in B is a subproduct of (2+c_r)/(c_r-c_*), r notin{m-1,m}. Every ratio is>=1, and the product of ALL such ratios is exactly C_N=[4/delta^2]/[chi''(c_*)/2] =4(4-delta)/(delta N^2)<2. (1) Here chi(-2)=4 and chi''(c_*)/2=N^2/[delta(4-delta)]. The bound delta N^2>=8 follows from the chord bound for sin on[0,pi/4]. Consequently B<=P_both<=C_N B coefficientwise. Every cross path that misses one of the central indices has exactly one crossing two-step: either m->m-2 or m+1->m-1. Split that step into two consecutive one-steps. This produces a path visiting both central indices, with the SAME input/output and total face degree. Its other edges and unused factors are unchanged; only the missed central factor delta is removed. If the original two-step starts at j0, its edge is s_(j0)s_(j0-1)xy and the repaired pair is s_(j0)^2s_(j0-1)^2(x+y)^2. Since xy<= (x+y)^2/2 coefficientwise, original path <= delta/[2s_(j0)s_(j0-1)] * repaired path =delta/[8cos(pi/N)] * repaired path. (2) A repaired path has at most TWO original preimages (merging either of those two pairs). Hence B <= P_cross <= C_N[1+delta/(4cos(pi/N))] B <3B. (3) The last bound uses N>=4, delta<=2-sqrt2 and cos(pi/N)>=sqrt2/2. All statements are coefficientwise, so they remain true at zero protected faces and after every original shared coefficient extraction. Let H_M be the actual maximal complete-channel contribution to H_(L_N), including N k_M beta_M^2 D_M(x,b,y)D_M(x,c,y)Ptilde_1(x,y), M=m-1. The exact paired derivative formula gives H_M=2B/N. Thus (N/2)H_M <= P_cross <= (3N/2)H_M. (4) Here beta and D are the literal factors of the [complete-circle polynomial theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md). This includes the forced factor x+y and the actual multiplicity k_M=2. It is a comparison within the original source coefficient, not after choosing independent local radii. For a diagram with the stated geometric certificate, the all-cross term of the entire marked Fejer source has exactly the [known complete-volume exponential rate](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md), with only fixed-diagram polynomial factors between its two bounds. At odd N the full positive endpoint numerator is already N times the simple maximal complete coupon, so its whole coefficient has that rate directly. The forest remainder treated here is specific to even levels. ## 2. Exact shared degree restriction on the remainder Expand the whole positive product by choosing cross,left,right at each original port. A noncross port puts at least m units into exactly one of its two middle faces: c for left, b for right. Draw its middle-graph edge pointing to that overloaded face. Each ordinary face has target d=2m-1, so it cannot receive TWO such arrows. Each protected face has target0, so it receives none. The original flat-plat middle graph has the [frozen gap description](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md): each odd gap is a path of distinct bounded faces; each internal even gap is a cycle based at the SAME exterior face u, with its other faces unique to that gap. Therefore every selected-edge cycle contains u. An orientation with indegree<=1 at each vertex and indegree(u)=0 cannot exist on such a cycle: its equal numbers of edges and vertices would force indegree1 everywhere. This includes the length-two multicycles. Thus every nonzero remainder term is a ROOTED FOREST of noncross middle edges. Each component has exactly one indegree-zero root; any protected face in that component must be that root. Geometry independently checked this use of the frozen gap lemma. No free re-marking, smoothing order, or graph-to-plat adapter is used. This is the precise remaining positive source problem: bound the shared marked coefficient for these one-sided forest components, with the cross coupons on their complement. The cross comparison(4) does not estimate their weights. Local positive-radius estimates can be too large and are not substituted for this shared problem. ## 3. Exact half-size factorization, without an asymptotic conclusion For a left path all visited rows are in0,...,m-1, so every upper-half diagonal factor is unused. Their product is exactly2, since the two halves have equal products and chi(-2)=4. Moreover c^(d-j)=c^m c^(m-1-j). Consequently P_left=2c^m times the degree-(m-1) positive polynomial resolvent numerator of the literal lower m-row triangular block, at spectral value -2. The analogous upper block gives P_right with the factor b^m. All original sine coefficients are still evaluated at level N, not at level m. Replacing them by a level-m source would be a new, unproved step. The factorization explains the overloaded-face condition but does not yet identify an entropy or an actual smoothed representation for the forest. In particular the already proved L_1 smoothing gap cannot be applied merely because the selected middle graph is a forest. ## Validation and remaining scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.py) checks the complete positive path sum, the central coefficient comparison, the repair and half-block identities, and actual original gap charts. [Results](../experiments/actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction_results.json) include nonzero marked-target support terms with noncross ports: the forest contribution does not vanish merely by this graph argument. The source interface of the path representation is separately audited against the original coproduct matrices; these new checks do not relabel that earlier test as a new independent physical-matrix construction. The positive path partition is not a covariant complete-colored image or a half-colored tensor. The scalar identity does not justify an $L^1$ smoothing argument for the half-block forest.

title: Diagonal Fejer ports reduce to a true identity smoothing
status: Literal identity forests and smoothed incidence constraints
text: # Diagonal Fejer ports reduce to a true identity smoothing 31 October 2026. diagonal and identity-forest reduction. This keeps the original protected targets and all remaining cross/left/right data. It does not factor arbitrary Green ports across matching/matching digon cuts. ## 1. Polynomial cost and the fixed-label distinction At N=2m,d=N-1 the FULL diagonal part of the positive endpoint numerator is exactly P_diag(b,c)=sum_(i=0)^d (4/a_i)b^i c^(d-i), a_i=4cos^2(pi(i+1/2)/N). Thus coefficientwise H_1<=P_diag<=C N^2 H_1, H_1=sum_(i=0)^d b^i c^(d-i). (1) Here C is absolute. The root at the half-integer sample closest to N/2 gives min a_i=4sin^2(pi/(2N)), so (1) is immediate. A fixed LEFT or RIGHT diagonal label includes only its corresponding half of the i range. For such a label retain ONLY the upper bound by C N^2 H_1. Equality of exponential rates with the full identity kernel is asserted only after summing BOTH actual diagonal types. At fixed diagram size the product cost remains polynomial. At the limiting entropy level a diagonal port has exactly q=(0,mu,1-mu,0), E=0, or its actual reflection. Enlarging its two possible half ranges to all identity loads sigma_b,sigma_c>=0, sigma_b+sigma_c=1 is therefore valid for an upper-bound reduction, without any phase or entropy cost. No remaining one-sided port is changed. ## 2. Feasibility forces the diagonal middle graph to be a forest Take any selected set D of diagonal ports in a feasible limiting source flow. Its middle b-c edges lie in the original gap graph. The only possible cycles are the entire internal even-gap cycles, each containing the protected exterior vertex u. If a component has n vertices and at least n edges, its identity edge loads already sum to at least n. Its vertices have total target at most n-1, since it contains u; all remaining local loads are nonnegative. This is impossible. Hence the diagonal middle graph is a forest, and its literal identity smoothing is connected. A tree cannot contain two protected vertices either: its n-1 edge loads would exceed the at most n-2 available targets. Thus each tree has at most ONE protected vertex directly from the load count. For a tree with n vertices the sum of its internal edge loads is n-1. The total remaining load is therefore1 when all its vertices are ordinary, and0 when it contains a protected vertex. Collapse that actual tree to one face of the same ordinary/protected type. Push all remaining local incidences to their resulting face label. Every remaining port retains its own local exponent vector and E. Conversely, for any nonnegative remaining loads with the collapsed face target, the lift of the identity loads is UNIQUE. Root a tree at its protected vertex if present, otherwise anywhere. At an edge parent->child let L be the total remaining load in the child subtree. Then assign sigma_child=1-L, sigma_parent=L. (2) Since a subtree load lies in[0,1] (or is zero in a protected tree), these are valid identity loads. Summing the subtree balances proves (2), and subtracting them proves every original face equation. No local E or entropy changes in this transport. The same is an EXACT finite coefficient identity. For an arbitrary remaining polynomial with nonnegative exponents, a surviving monomial has total degree d on each ordinary merged tree and0 on a protected tree. At an internal edge its endpoint identity degrees are j_child=d-L_degree(subtree), j_parent=L_degree(subtree). Both lie in[0,d]. Each H_1 coefficient is one, so there is no counting multiplicity. Consequently extracting the original target after inserting all H_1 factors equals extracting the ordinary d targets of the polynomial obtained by IDENTIFYING the face variables in each tree. This is the actual source-preserving identity smoothing, not a formal zero-radius substitution. Combined with (1), it bounds any fixed diagonal sector by the true smoothed remaining positive source with polynomial cost. ## 3. Two useful exclusions after deleting ALL diagonal ports Suppose D contains every diagonal port of the particular limiting flow. The resulting white triangular cellulation has NO loop edge. To prove this, choose the mark-free side of a proposed loop at a. If it contains v interior white vertices, Euler counting gives 2v-1 shaded triangles inside. The dual bridge must be MATCHING: the odd number of dual vertices and one matching incidence per vertex force its single crossing edge to be matching. There are v-1 whole retained ports inside and one inside triangle of that bridge port. Its middle is inside; both outer incidences are at a. The v ordinary interior targets sum to v. The whole ports supply at most v-1 there, so the bridge middle must carry the FULL unit, and every other incidence of that port must be zero. It is therefore a diagonal endpoint, contrary to its retention. Likewise no remaining MATCHING edge joins the two protected merged faces. Both outer loads of that port would be zero. For a one-sided port this forces nu-mu=0, hence diagonal; for a cross port the two middle loads would have to be1/2 each, but its actual finite cross support needs one outer unit. At the limiting functional this is the same full-diagonal load (1/2,1/2), with zero entropy. It can be included in D ONLY for the LIMITING entropy/load reduction: its zero entropy and identity load are the same. This does NOT apply the finite comparison (1) to that cross sector, which still needs its one outer unit. The separate [full-kernel entropy theorem](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) supplies the source RATE comparison for these limiting endpoints. The finite inequality in section1 is still not applied to a cross sector. The combinatorial no-protected-matching conclusion therefore concerns the enlarged LIMITING identity reduction when those cross endpoints are included. The remaining cellulation may have parallel edges and degree-two faces. Those are not excluded by this count and must not be replaced by a simple graph without retaining the actual topology. ## 4. What decomposes and what still does not A MAIN/MAIN two-edge cut leaves complete ports on each side. On its mark-free side, the number of internal ordinary targets equals the number of contained ports. Total-degree conservation then forces ALL incidences on its two boundary faces to have zero load. Thus this cut has the same zero-boundary separation as the complete-source angle proof; absolute local entropy constants are unchanged. A MATCHING/MATCHING cut is different. Two retained Green ports can cross it. Let ell>=0 be the total load that the v-1 whole inside ports send to the two boundary faces. The exact balance is q_inside,1+q_inside,2=1+ell. A cross middle is at most1/2, so in the old complete proof this forced ell=0 and both inside middles to equal1/2. General Green ports may have asymmetric middle loads and may also have ell>0. Therefore the old independent block capacity factorization does NOT extend by the same argument. This is an explicit remaining coupling, not a scalar normalization issue or a reason to alter the original support. A possible way around it is a DIRECT signed developing disk on the loopless triangular cellulation with parallel edges. Its vertex links are still topological circles/intervals, so the signed center holonomy argument should not require simpliciality. Repeated edges then develop to the same circle contact, which the global oriented chain permits. This still requires proving the correct treatment of structurally forced zero degrees and any escaping ordinary multipliers. The original representation must be restored by actual identity meridians at the deleted ports. If their outer product becomes nonparabolic, its recorded flag and the proved zero-volume filling cap must be used; an artificial x/y tangency must NOT be inserted. The exact reductions above do not yet show that the reduced mixed-E maximum is attained on the regular signed-development stratum, nor bound the remaining coupled matching cuts. No general diagonal-boundary volume inequality is asserted. The full-kernel companion gives the rate-level CROSS-seam reduction. No independent Green-block factorization across matching cuts is asserted.

title: Fejér entropy signs and the remaining homogeneous-tail comparison
status: Entropy signs and restricted insertion gap
text:
# Fejér entropy signs and the remaining homogeneous-tail comparison 31 October 2026. This checks the actual [closed local coefficient entropy](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) and [full-kernel entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md). It disproves nonnegativity of the full local entropy, proves strict positivity at every port of the original simple-white geometric flow, and gives a scoped shared-capacity reduction. No estimate for a complementary source with arbitrary signed crossing powers follows. ## 1. An exact source coefficient disproves nonnegativity Use the original even level $N=2m$, $d=N-1$, $M=m-1$, with $$ s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad a_r=4\cos^2\!\left( rac{\pi(r+1/2)}Night). $$ For a left path from $j$ to $i=0$, the coefficient of $x^j c^{d-j}$ has no $y$ and therefore has no dimer. There is exactly one path, using all single-$x$ steps. The original half-block identity gives exactly $$ [x^j c^{d-j}]P_N= rac4{a_0}\prod_{r=1}^j rac{s_r^2}{a_r}, \qquad 0\leq j\leq M.	ag{1} $$ No other half or cross part has these degrees when $j<M$. The source scalar $4/a_0$ is retained and has zero exponential rate. For $j/N	o
u\in(0,1/2)$, the elementary log-sine/cosine Riemann limit, with its integrable lower endpoint, gives $$ h(
u,0,1-
u,0)=E(0,
u,
u) =2\int_0^
u\log	an(\pi t)\,dt<0.	ag{2} $$ The integral is strictly negative for every $0<
u<1/2$: its derivative changes sign only at $1/4$ and its total value at $1/2$ is zero by $t\mapsto1/2-t$. In particular, for $N=4k$ and $j=k$, $$ h(1/4,0,3/4,0)=- rac{2G}{\pi},\qquad G=-\int_0^{\pi/4}\log	an u\,du>0.	ag{3} $$ Here $G$ is Catalan's constant. This is the entropy of an actual coefficient of the full positive numerator, not a factorwise estimate or a missing exponential normalization. Continuity of $h$ also supplies strictly negative points in the interior of the four-face simplex. Thus restricting away from zero faces cannot repair the assertion $h\geq0$. There is an exact global floor. The closed coefficient formula gives $$ E(\mu,
u,\xi)\geq2\int_\mu^
u\log	an(\pi t)\,dt \geq- rac{2G}{\pi}. $$ The last minimum takes the whole negative interval $[0,1/4]$ and no positive part. The cross entropy is nonnegative by Section 2. Therefore $$ \min_{	ext{simplex}}h=- rac{2G}{\pi}.	ag{4} $$ ## 2. The geometric port entropy is strictly positive For a triangle of loads $\alpha_x+\alpha_b+\alpha_y=1/2$, write $$ C_{\mathrm{tri}}( oldsymbol\alpha)=\sum_j f(\alpha_j),\qquad f(t)= rac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}{\pi}. $$ Direct differentiation gives $f'(t)=\log\cot(\pi t)$, while $f(0)=f(1/2)=0$ and $f(1/2-t)=f(t)$. Hence $f(t)>0$ for $0<t<1/2$. Thus $C_{\mathrm{tri}}\geq0$, with equality only at a triangle vertex. In particular every cross port has $h\geq0$, including all seams. Now use the actual simple white triangulation, with the two adjacent protected faces $u,v$ joined by the marked MAIN edge. A matching port has triangles $(x,b,y)$ and $(x,c,y)$, with distinct middle vertices $b,c$ and common MATCHING edge $xy$. The geometric ordinary curvatures are strictly positive; the two protected curvatures are zero. In the actual angle formula a corner load is positive exactly when its curvature is positive, except that the one remaining positive corner in a two-line triangle carries the whole $1/2$. The two triangles cannot both have zero entropy. If $x,y$ are ordinary, both triangles have at least two positive corners. If exactly one of $x,y$ is protected, at most one of the distinct $b,c$ can be the other protected vertex, so the other triangle has at least two positive corners. Both $x,y$ cannot be protected, because their edge is MATCHING while $uv$ is the marked MAIN edge. These exhaust the cases. Therefore the geometric split has a strictly positive sum of its two triangle entropies at every port $e$. The definition of $h$ as the maximum over cross splits yields $$ h(\mathbf q_{\mathrm{geom},e})>0\qquad	ext{for every }e.	ag{5} $$ This is pointwise for each fixed certified diagram. No diagram-uniform positive lower bound is asserted. Simplicity and the actual MAIN/MATCHING label are used; the conclusion is not silently extended to a repeated-incidence multigraph. ## 3. Exact mixed rate and a strict partial comparison Let $J$ be any nonempty set of ports. Replace their positive full kernels by $$ h_d(x,b,c,y)=\sum_{\substack{a+i+t+s=d\a,i,t,s\geq0}}x^a b^i c^t y^s, $$ whose every coefficient is one. This polynomial has the full degree-$d$ simplex support and local coefficient entropy zero. It is only the absolute homogeneous bound supplied by the [far-tail Fourier adapter](actual_far_charge_homogeneous_insertion.md); it is not identified with the identity coupon $H_1$ or any original covariant coupon. Keep $F_N$ at all other ports, with its original parity-appropriate positive definition, all original ordinary targets $d$, and both protected targets zero. The same unrestricted degree-$d$ bipartite-flow rounding and uniform local entropy theorem prove that this positive mixed coefficient has rate $$ \Psi_J=\max_{\mathbf q\in\mathcal P_D}H_J(\mathbf q),\qquad H_J(\mathbf q)=\sum_{e
otin J}h(\mathbf q_e).	ag{6} $$ Here $\mathcal P_D$ is the original marked flow polytope. The number of arrays is polynomial in $N$; floor/ceiling cycle rounding respects the actual balances and incurs only $O(1/N)$ in local loads. Full supports eliminate a fixed-pattern feasibility issue. This argument is valid at both parities using the established common local $h$. The [endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) and [unique geometric maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) give $$ H(\mathbf q)=\sum_e h(\mathbf q_e)\leq\Phi_D,\qquad H(\mathbf q)=\Phi_D\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mathbf q=\mathbf q_{\mathrm{geom}}. $$ Define the compact restricted set $$ \mathcal K_J^+=\{\mathbf q\in\mathcal P_D:h(\mathbf q_e)\geq0	ext{ for every }e\in J\}. $$ There is a strict gap on this set: $$ \max_{\mathbf q\in\mathcal K_J^+}H_J(\mathbf q)<\Phi_D.	ag{7} $$ Indeed $H_J\leq H\leq\Phi_D$ there. Equality at a maximizer would force $H=\Phi_D$ and every removed entropy zero. Uniqueness would then give $\mathbf q=\mathbf q_{\mathrm{geom}}$, contradicting (5) and $J
e\varnothing$. Compactness and continuity turn this pointwise exclusion into a positive fixed-diagram gap. Consequently, if the full comparison $\Psi_J<\Phi_D$ fails, every maximizing flow reaching or exceeding $\Phi_D$ has at least one inserted port with $h(\mathbf q_e)<0$. Such a port is strictly one-sided: one middle exceeds $1/2$, its interval has positive length, and it is neither a pure-middle diagonal nor a cross seam. These overloaded edges obey the same original rooted-forest constraint, because each ordinary face has total demand $1$, each protected face demand $0$, and every original middle-gap cycle contains the protected exterior. Subsets of those edges remain forests. This is a general reduction of the remaining $h_d$ majorant problem to negative-entropy one-sided forest branches. It is not a bound for those branches. The tempting deduction from unique geometric maximality alone is invalid, since replacing a negative $h$ by zero increases the local objective. Formula (4) gives only the crude unconditional estimate $$ \Psi_J\leq\Phi_D+|J| rac{2G}{\pi}, $$ which is not the desired strict gap. The exact far Fourier tails retain covariance and alternating spectral data that the $h_d$ majorant discards. Neither (6) nor (7) is a bound for a complementary source with arbitrary remaining signed $R$ powers; that stronger source problem still requires its own estimate. ## Validation and scope The local negative-entropy obstruction does not disprove a general shared-source bound, and the positive mixed comparison remains restricted to the explicitly stated subset of its original flow polytope.

title: Continuous full-kernel entropy and exact identity reduction of maxima
status: Full-simplex entropy and exact identity reduction
text: # Continuous full-kernel entropy and exact identity reduction of maxima Completion: the [general endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) assembles this local result into the actual augmented-volume equality. Its [unique geometric maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) gives concentration; the original filling conjecture remains open. 31 October 2026. full-kernel entropy and identity-reduction theorem. This uses the [proved uniform closed local coefficient limits](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md). It does not assume that an infeasible fixed half-label pattern becomes feasible. It sums the full positive local kernel before forgetting its type. ## 1. The full local coefficient entropy is continuous For q=(X,B,C,Y)>=0, X+B+C+Y=1, define h(q) as follows. If C>=1/2, put h=E(B,1-C,X). If B>=1/2, put h=E(C,1-B,X). If B,C<=1/2, put h(q)=max_s { Ctri(s,B,1/2-B-s) +Ctri(X-s,C,1/2-C-X+s) }, (1) where max(0,X+C-1/2)<=s<=min(X,1/2-B), and Ctri(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi) is the proved triangle entropy. The conventions agree on every overlap. At C=1/2 the second triangle is pure-middle, of entropy zero, and (1) is Ctri(X,B,Y), which is EXACTLY E(B,1/2,X). The B=1/2 boundary is reflected. At B=C=1/2 all entropies are zero. The interval in (1) has continuous endpoints, so compact maximization and continuity of Ctri prove h is continuous on the whole simplex. The closed half-block theorem proves the same for its two one-sided pieces. In particular h(0,B,1-B,0)=0 for every 0<=B<=1. (2) Let p_N(n) be the coefficient of the FULL positive polynomial P in a nonnegative local exponent vector n of total degree d=N-1. Every such coefficient is positive. The exact supports partition all these vectors into cross (both middle<=m-1), left (c>=m), and right (b>=m). The uniform half-block limits, positive cross convolution and B_cross<=P_cross<=3B_cross give sup_(n>=0, sum n=d) |N^-1 log p_N(n)-h(n/d)| ->0. (3) For the cross convolution the allowed outer-split interval has integer endpoints. Every limiting split has an O(1/N) integer approximation; there are O(N) summands. Uniform continuity of Ctri therefore makes its log-sum rate uniformly the maximum (1), including the terminal faces. The finite forced outer unit is retained in this argument. The changes from i/N,j/N to n/d are O(1/N) in the closed parameters, so continuity justifies that normalization. This is NOT a bound on an individual cross term by H1 at zero outer degree. ## 2. A shared variational theorem without fixed half labels Take any fixed finite incidence graph of these homogeneous degree-d polynomials, allowing repeated global labels among a port's four separate incidences. Give every ordinary face target d and each protected face target zero. Let P be the nonnegative real flow polytope with port supplies1, ordinary face demands1 and protected demands0. If its total supplies/demands disagree, or the polytope is empty, the coefficient is zero. Otherwise lim_(even N) N^-1 log [original target] product_e P_e =max_(q in P) sum_e h(q_e). (4) The upper bound follows by (3) and the polynomial number of arrays. For the lower bound, take a maximizing q and multiply by d. This gives EXACT integer node balances with real edge values. Fractional-cycle rounding inside each floor/ceiling interval gives an integral flow, with error at most one per incidence. The local polynomial contains EVERY degree-d monomial, so this rounded array is an actual positive term, regardless of which half label it receives at that level. Continuity of h and (3) give its desired rate. Repeated incidences remain parallel arcs in the rounding graph. Thus (4) agrees with the previously proved W_D on the original diagram, since both are limits of the SAME source. It does not deny the original eventual-feasibility test for FIXED patterns; it avoids assigning a fixed pattern at the seams, where h has the same continuous value. The formulation also applies to actual identity-smoothed incidence maps even when they are not simplicial right-angled certificates. No arbitrary graph-to-original-plat adapter is asserted. The same argument permits some local H1 factors. At such an identity port remove its two outer incidence arcs; the remaining middle loads sum to one and its coefficient entropy is identically zero. All its allowed coefficients are one, and fractional-cycle rounding respects this reduced incidence graph. Thus the corresponding mixed flow maximum is the ACTUAL mixed positive coefficient rate as well. ## 3. A maximum with pure-middle ports is an exact lower-port problem Let q attain (4), and let D be ANY collection of its pure-middle ports, including ordinary one-sided diagonals and a pure-middle cross endpoint (0,1/2,1/2,0). Replace those full local P factors by H1. The SAME q is feasible in the mixed identity flow polytope and has the same entropy by (2). Therefore the mixed maximum is at least W_D. Conversely, coefficientwise H1<=P_diag<=P, so its actual mixed coefficient rate is at most W_D. Hence W_D = rate of the actual mixed source with H1 on D. (5) This equality is about the FULL summed local kernel and its rate. It makes no false finite comparison between a cross boundary monomial and H1. In particular it repairs the pure-middle cross seam only after (3)--(4), without relabeling an infeasible fixed source pattern. Feasibility forces the diagonal middle graph to be a forest: every possible original even-gap cycle contains the protected exterior, and its unit edge supplies exceed that component's ordinary demands. A tree cannot contain two protected vertices either. The [exact subtree coefficient identity](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md) therefore identifies the mixed H1 coefficient with the true connected identity smoothing, with all face targets and no multiplicity. Thus (5) is a genuine reduction to fewer remaining positive P ports. What it does NOT yet prove is that the resulting non-simple smoothed incidence graph has a regular entropy maximizer or that its W is bounded by the original complete volume. Matching/matching cuts can still carry asymmetric Green loads; their complete-source block factorization is not assumed. The remaining geometry must retain the actual smoothing and, when restoring deleted cusps, its literal identity meridians. The rate-level identity reduction does not give a volume bound for every nonsimple smoothed source or a quantum filling asymptotic.

title: The actual Fejér half block: uniform coefficient entropy
text: # The actual Fejér half block: uniform coefficient entropy , 31 October 2026. This gives the exact level-N half-block recurrence, its weighted rate, and the uniform exponential rate of EVERY coefficient, including the boundary degrees. It also fixes the complete-triangle normalization and disproves one proposed endpoint-convexity shortcut. These are local source theorems; no shared forest bound, representation, or filling-cycle conclusion is asserted. All limits below run through every even N tending to infinity. ## 1. The original finite polynomial and its exact recurrence Let N=2m>=4, d=N-1, M=m-1, theta=pi/N, and c_j=2cos((2j+1)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta), a_j=2+c_j=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta), product_(j=0)^M a_j=2. Use the [original homogeneous source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) and its [positive cross/half decomposition](actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md). Thus P=-H_(V_N(-2)), where V_N is the actual polynomial resolvent numerator, and P_left contains exactly the physical paths j to i with 0<=i<=j<=M. Their middle monomial is b^i c^(d-j). These pieces are not separately asserted to be covariant coupons. For an interval i+1,...,j let K_(i,j) be its positive tiling continuant. A monomer at r has weight s_r^2(x+y); a dimer ending at r has weight s_r s_(r-1) a_(r-1)xy. The latter includes the UNUSED intermediate diagonal. Set K_(i,i)=1 and Q_(i,j)=K_(i,j)/product_(r=i+1)^j a_r. The actual path expansion is exactly P_left=2 sum_(i<=j) b^i c^(d-j) product_(r<i)a_r product_(r>j)^M a_r K_(i,j) =4 sum_(i<=j) b^i c^(d-j) Q_(i,j)/a_i, (1) Q_(i,i)=1, Q_(i,i+1)=alpha_(i+1), Q_(i,j)=alpha_j Q_(i,j-1)+beta_j Q_(i,j-2), alpha_j=(s_j^2/a_j)(x+y), beta_j=(s_j s_(j-1)/a_j)xy. (2) All absent negative-index terms are zero. The original level remains N, not m. Define the strictly positive coefficients A_N(i,j,k)=[x^k y^(j-i-k)]Q_(i,j), 0<=k<=j-i. The corresponding coefficient of P_left is (4/a_i)A_N. The multiplier 4/a_i is between a positive constant and CN^2, uniformly in every row. Right paths are obtained by the literal row reflection j -> d-j and b <-> c, with the same x,y polynomial. ## 2. Uniform weighted rate, retaining both physical endpoints Fix positive x,y, uniformly on compact positive sets. The limiting Perron root at t=j/N is L(t;x,y)=[(x+y)sin^2(pi t)+sin(pi t) sqrt((x+y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4xy cos^2(pi t))] /[2cos^2(pi t)], L^2-(x+y)tan^2(pi t)L-xy tan^2(pi t)=0, L>0. (3) It increases strictly from zero to infinity. Uniformly over ALL rows, sup_(0<=i<=j<=M) |N^-1 log Q_(i,j)(x,y) -integral_(i/N)^(j/N) log L(t;x,y)dt| ->0. (4) Here is a proof with no endpoint gap. Fix eta>0. On eta N<=j<=(1/2-eta)N the coefficients of (2) stay in a compact positive set, converge uniformly to their limits, and vary by O_eta(1/N) per step. For a constant recurrence q_l=alpha q_(l-1)+beta q_(l-2), q_0=1,q_1=alpha, one has q_l=(lambda_+^(l+1)-lambda_-^(l+1))/(lambda_+-lambda_-), lambda_-<0<lambda_+, |lambda_-|/lambda_+<=r_eta<1. Hence c_eta lambda_+^l<=q_l<=C_eta lambda_+^l, and the corresponding transfer-matrix powers obey the same upper exponential bound. Partition an arbitrary interior interval into blocks of length floor(sqrt N), with shorter end blocks. Positivity compares each block with its minimum and maximum constant coefficients. Retaining only tilings which do not cross a block boundary gives the lower bound; transfer matrices give the upper bound. The logarithmic block overhead is O_eta(sqrt N+1), and the accumulated variation cost is O_eta(sqrt N). Thus (4) holds uniformly for all interior intervals, including short ones. The omitted endpoint intervals cost at most C eta N log(2/eta)+C log N (5) in absolute logarithmic size. For the upper bound use transfer norm at most product_j(1+alpha_j+beta_j). Near zero these coefficients are bounded; near M the denominator a_j is comparable to ((M-j+1/2)/N)^2, giving the sum of logarithms C eta N+2 sum_(r<=eta N)log(N/r). For the lower bound concatenate only monomers on the omitted sites. Near zero alpha_j>=c(j/N)^2, and near M it is bounded below by a positive constant; their negative logarithms satisfy (5). These arguments also apply to intervals entirely inside an endpoint portion. Finally log L=log t+O(1) near zero and log L=-2log(1/2-t)+O(1) near one half, so the omitted limiting integrals are O(eta log(2/eta)). Let N tend to infinity and then eta to zero. This proves (4), locally uniformly in the positive weights. Write F(x,b,y) for the ABSOLUTELY normalized source triangle potential in [the original action theorem](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md), section6. Equation (1), (4), and polynomially many summands imply lim N^-1 log P_left =max_(0<=mu<=nu<=1/2) [mu log b+(1-nu)log c+integral_mu^nu log L(t)dt]. (6) For fixed mu the expression is convex in nu, so its maximum is at nu=mu or nu=1/2. The latter is (log c)/2+H(x,b,y), where H=max_(0<=mu<=1/2) [mu log b+integral_mu^(1/2)log L(t)dt]. The unique maximizer obeys L(mu)=b, or tan(pi mu)=b/sqrt(b(x+y)+xy). Its envelope derivative with respect to log b is mu, exactly the source triangle middle angle divided by 2pi. Both H-(log b)/2 and F-(log b)/2 tend to zero as b tends to infinity: for H use the logarithmic endpoint tail, and for F use its original positive logdet integral and integrable cos^(-2) endpoint bound. Therefore H=F with NO missing additive constant. Also F>=(log b)/2, from the actual determinant's b^M term. Consequently lim N^-1 log P_left =max(log c,F(x,b,y)+(log c)/2), lim N^-1 log P_right=max(log b,F(x,c,y)+(log b)/2), lim N^-1 log P=max(F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y),log b,log c). (7) The last formula uses the exact cross comparison. All weights in (7) are positive and fixed before N. It is NOT a coefficientwise bound by a complete coupon plus an identity coupon, and it licenses no exchange of infimum over shared radii with a maximum over local branches. ## 3. Actual coefficients in strict interiors Put D={0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu}, g(t,l)=log L(t;exp(l),1) =l/2+log tan(pi t)+asinh(tan(pi t)cosh(l/2)), Phi(mu,nu,l)=integral_mu^nu g(t,l)dt, E(mu,nu,xi)=inf_(l real)[Phi(mu,nu,l)-xi l]. (8) First consider compact subsets of 0<mu<nu<1/2, 0<xi<nu-mu. Normalize Q_(i,j) by product_(v=i+1)^j a'_v, where a'_v=s_v^2/a_v. The resulting monic degree-r polynomial, r=j-i, satisfies p_0=1, p_1=x+y, p_r=(x+y)p_(r-1)+gamma_r xy p_(r-2), gamma_r=a_(i+r-1)/(s_(i+r)s_(i+r-1))>0. (9) Substituting x/y=-z^2 and dividing by z^r gives the Jacobi recurrence q_r(t)=t q_(r-1)(t)-gamma_r q_(r-2)(t), t=z^-1-z. Its symmetric tridiagonal matrix has positive off-diagonal entries, so its roots are real and simple. The map z>0 ->z^-1-z is bijective onto the real line. Thus p_r(x,1) has exactly r negative real roots. The compact-interval bounds on gamma give a uniform Jacobi norm bound, placing all these roots in a compact negative interval away from zero and infinity. The polynomial is reciprocal as well. After a bounded tilt x=exp(l), y=1, its coefficient distribution is therefore a sum of r independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities uniformly away from zero and one. For k/r in a compact subset of (0,1), the unique exact-mean tilt stays bounded. Its probability at that mean is comparable to r^(-1/2): Fourier inversion has a Gaussian expansion on |theta|<=r^(-2/5), variance comparable to r, and modulus bounded by exp[-c r sin^2(theta/2)] elsewhere. Bounded third moments give the relative Gaussian error o(1). The logarithm of this probability is therefore O(log N). The weighted theorem (4) and this exact coefficient identity give N^-1 log A_N(i,j,k) -> E(mu,nu,xi) (10) for every sequence i/N->mu,j/N->nu,k/N->xi in a strict interior, locally uniformly there. To justify convergence of the exact tilts, the normalized log polynomials are convex and converge locally uniformly to differentiable strictly convex Phi. The two secant inequalities imply convergence of their first derivatives on compact intervals; the unique limiting tilt satisfies Phi_l=xi. The same root/variance bounds imply Phi_ll>0. No derivative of an unsupported weighted asymptotic has been taken. ## 4. The closed-domain theorem The function E is continuous on ALL of D, and sup_(0<=i<=j<=M,0<=k<=j-i) |N^-1 log A_N(i,j,k)-E(i/N,j/N,k/N)| ->0. (11) This also holds for the actual half-block coefficient (4/a_i)A_N, since its additional logarithm is uniformly O(log N). For continuity set q=nu-mu, B=2 integral_mu^nu log tan(pi t)dt, and delta_r(t)=asinh(tan(pi t)cosh(r/2))-r/2-log tan(pi t), r>=0. This is positive, decreases to zero, and is dominated by the integrable delta_0: it is -log t+O(1) at zero and tends to log2 at one half. Its full-interval integral tends to zero as r tends to infinity. Exactly, with a=min(xi,q-xi), E=B+inf_(r>=0)[a r+integral_mu^nu delta_r(t)dt]. (12) Hence B<=E<=B+integral_mu^nu delta_0, which proves E->0 uniformly as q->0. As a->0 choose a large fixed r first; (12) gives E-B->0 uniformly. Where a>=a0>0 the minimizer is restricted to a common compact r interval, so continuity follows by compact minimization. In particular E(mu,nu,0)=E(mu,nu,nu-mu)=B. For the uniform upper bound, every finite real l gives N^-1 log A_N<=N^-1 log Q_(i,j)(exp(l),1)-(k/N)l. At each point of D select a finite l within epsilon of its infimum, even when the infimum is reached only at infinity. Continuity gives a neighborhood where the same l works within 2epsilon. A finite cover of D and (4) for this finite set of tilts give the uniform upper bound. For the lower bound consider any sequence tending to a point with 0<xi<q. Trim to i'=max(i,ceil(eta N)), j'=min(j,floor((1/2-eta)N)), and set r'=j'-i', r=j-i, k'=floor(k r'/r). For small fixed eta, r'>0 and 0<=k-k'<=r-r'. Retain an arbitrary interior tiling and specified x- and y-monomers on the omitted sites. This is an actual subset of the original tilings, with no crossing dimer, and gives A_N(i,j,k)>=A_N(i',j',k') product_(omitted v)a'_v. (13) The omitted logarithmic cost is at most (5). Apply (10) to the strict retained interval, let N tend to infinity, and then eta to zero. Continuity gives the required lower rate. If xi=0 or q, including sequences whose integer k is not exactly extreme, the all-monomer term gives A_N>=binom(r,k) product a'_v>=product a'_v. Uniform log-sine/cosine Riemann estimates, including the upper half-step, give N^-1 log product_(v=i+1)^j a'_v =B(i/N,j/N)+O(log N/N). (14) This also handles q=0. Compactness turns these sequential lower bounds into the uniform statement (11). It is an exponential-rate theorem, not a relative amplitude or derivative asymptotic. ## 5. Exact endpoint normalization and a finite entropy formula Let R_M(b) be the original lower-block path numerator starting at M, with every ending b^i retained. Replace each unused spectral factor a_r, r<M, by a_r^*=c_r-c_*, where c_*=-2cos(pi/N), to obtain D_b=R_M^*(b). These definitions keep every original sine coefficient. The exact path comparisons give D_b<=R_M<=sqrt(C_N)D_b, C_N=4(4-delta)/(delta N^2)<2, delta=2-2cos(pi/N), [b^i x^k y^(M-i-k)]R_M=(2/a_i)A_N(i,M,k), B_cross=4(x+y)D_bD_c, B_cross<=P_cross<3B_cross. (15) For completeness, the comparison factor is the product over the lower unused rows of a_r/a_r^*, bounded by sqrt(C_N). Splitting the paired root path at its compulsory central one-step gives the last exact factorization. The recorded complete-channel identity implies D_b=C_front D_M(x,b,y), where D_M is the original determinant and C_front=product_(r<M)a_r^*=N/[2sin(pi/N)]. Thus this normalization differs from that determinant by only a polynomial scalar, not an unknown exponential constant. It follows uniformly on the ENTIRE triangle simplex that its actual coefficient entropy is C(alpha_x,alpha_b,alpha_y)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x), alpha_x+alpha_b+alpha_y=1/2, alpha_j>=0, C(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi), V(theta)=2sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin w|dw. (16) The finite third degree is M-i-k, not N/2-i-k. Its bounded offset disappears only after (11) and uniform continuity. To prove the absolute last equality, for strict positive alpha choose x=tan(pi alpha_x), b=tan(pi alpha_b), y=tan(pi alpha_y). Their pairwise product sum is one. The unique maximizer in (6) with nu=1/2 is alpha_b, and the original triangle derivatives of F are exactly alpha_x,alpha_b,alpha_y. Differentiating this already proved smooth formula shows that log(x/y) is the correct minimizing tilt. Therefore E=F-sum alpha_j log L_j. The absolute source identity 2pi F=sum theta_j log L_j+V(theta) proves (16); continuity includes every boundary face. At a cross port the two triangular allocations and the ONE forced x-or-y unit in (15) must remain explicit before shared coefficient extraction. There is also a finite formula for the general E. For mu<nu put q=nu-mu, Dangle=2pi(xi-q/2), a=cos(pi mu), b0=cos(pi nu), kappa=sin Dangle/sqrt(a^2+b0^2-2a b0 cos Dangle), alpha_x(t)=1/4-t/2+asin(kappa cos(pi t))/(2pi), alpha_b(t)=t, alpha_y(t)=1/2-t-alpha_x(t). (17) Use the real principal arcsine. The domain |Dangle|<=pi q implies |kappa|<=1: the difference between the squared denominator and sin^2 Dangle is (cos Dangle-a b0)^2-(1-a^2)(1-b0^2)>=0. For strict outer degrees kappa=tanh(l/2) for the unique tilt, because direct integration gives alpha_x(t)=partial_l Phi(t,1/2,l) and Dangle=asin(kappa a)-asin(kappa b0). The right side is strictly increasing with the required range; this fixes the original branch after squaring. At xi=0,q take kappa=-1,+1. Subtracting the two correct endpoint Legendre identities gives E(mu,nu,xi)=C(alpha(mu))-C(alpha(nu)). (18) Set E=0 when mu=nu. This is a finite Lobachevsky evaluation on the whole closed domain. Its corresponding left degree vector is alpha(mu) on (x,b,y), minus alpha(nu) on (x,c,y), plus e_c. The output triangle can be written with generalized angles (-theta_x,2pi-theta_c,-theta_y); the Lobachevsky reflection identities give its negative V. This is a signed-angle identity, not a developing map, an independent geometric volume bound, or a cycle-selection rule. ## 6. The fixed-outer-degree endpoint convexity claim is false At l=0 one has g_l=1/2 and g_ll=sin(pi t)/4. At the balanced xi=(nu-mu)/2, the tilt is therefore zero. Hold mu and xi FIXED while varying nu. The exact Legendre Schur complement is E_(nu,nu)=pi cos(pi nu)/[sin(pi nu)(1-sin(pi nu))] -pi/[cos(pi mu)-cos(pi nu)]. (19) Indeed Phi_(nu,l)=1/2 and Phi_(l,l)=[cos(pi mu)-cos(pi nu)]/(4pi). At nu=1/4 the first term is pi/(1-1/sqrt2); for every 0<mu<1/4 the second term is larger. In particular mu=1/8,nu=1/4,xi=1/16 is a strict regular negative-curvature point. Choose a sufficiently small fixed rational epsilon>0. For all large even N use rounded i=N/8,k=N/16,j0=N/4 and jplus/minus=N(1/4+/-epsilon). The uniform coefficient theorem and (19) give, for the ACTUAL coefficients mathcal A_N(j)=(4/a_i)A_N(i,j,k), log mathcal A_N(j0) -[log mathcal A_N(jminus)+log mathcal A_N(jplus)]/2 >=c_epsilon N>0. (20) Thus coefficient log-convexity in this exact direction fails exponentially. The common source factor 4/a_i is retained. This does not disprove a shared forest bound: an exchange that changes other face degrees could behave differently. Holding the proportion xi/(nu-mu) fixed is a DIFFERENT direction and is not addressed by (19). Fixed-positive-radius endpoint convexity in (6) cannot be used after fixing xi without this Schur correction. ## 7. Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_fejer_half_block_entropy_results.json) retain independent original numerator comparisons, positive paths, and the absolute triangle anchor. Finite closed-boundary rate and coefficient-curvature profiles are diagnostics for the displayed proofs, not substitutes for uniform estimates. The exact source interface is also covered by the frozen numerator and cross-half audits linked above. The author run passes at 75 digits: 329 left and 329 right original numerator coefficients, 96 direct positive paths, 5 independent triangle anchors, 11 recurrence identities and 11 Jacobi/log-root identities, 52 actual negative roots, 12 closed-entropy integral reconstructions, and 64 extreme coefficient checks. It records 25 weighted-rate and 88 closed-coefficient profiles, and four increasing-level failures of the proposed coefficient log-convexity. The largest anchor or entropy reconstruction error is below 7e-76. These finite checks do not prove the uniform limits; those are proved above. No shared entropy maximum is evaluated here; in particular no local max/min exchange, general forest-volume inequality, or signed long-filled knot asymptotic is claimed.

title: Actual representation and signed volume from hybrid tight-cut pieces
status: Original group and relative volume from hybrid pieces
text: # Actual representation and signed volume from hybrid tight-cut pieces 31 October 2026. conditional representation and relative-volume theorem. The [hybrid tight-cut theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) supplies the finite-flow input. This note proves the geometric and original-source topology step for its exact output, without an independent Green-block capacity factorization. It concerns the positive endpoint source, not the original phase-sensitive filled-knot period. ## 1. Precisely the decomposition data required Start with the actual connected identity smoothing of the original certified flat plat. Its full positive-kernel maximum is the same W_D by the [full-kernel identity reduction, §3](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) and its [literal forest contraction](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md). At a chosen maximum, remove every pure-middle port by that reduction and represent terminal one-sided seams as CROSS at the same full-kernel entropy value. Use the following output of the hybrid tight-cut construction: * The remaining loopless white triangular cellulation is cut along actual digon disks into a finite tree of triangular spheres. * Each child is marked at the two adjacent vertices of its cut boundary; the root retains the original protected pair. Boundary loads on each mark-free side are zero, so the exact entropy is the SUM of the piece entropies, with the original triangle constants and multiplicities. * No GREEN (strict one-sided) port is cut. Every port crossing a matching cut is CROSS. Its entropy is the additive C(alpha)+C(beta), and its two original triangles are retained separately on their actual sides. No new physical auxiliary circle is inferred from closing a piece. * A strict relative hybrid witness on each piece, with the existing strict Green row margins, excludes every ordinary zero corner by the proved epsilon-log entropy gains. Finite row-space multipliers then give positive finite ordinary curvatures, protected curvatures zero, and the actual local tangent-circle angles. Each ordinary signed star has total0 or2pi; only the two forced marked lines degenerate. These are explicit inputs here. The [hybrid flow proof, §§4–5](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) and the [corner expansions and multiplier argument, §§2–4](actual_fejer_nondiagonal_maximizer_regularity.md) supply their finite support and regularity content. In particular an arbitrary digon decomposition with GREEN ports cut in half would NOT satisfy them. ## 2. Each piece has one actual signed circle development Apply the [cooriented developing-disk argument, §2](actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md) to each piece, with the following explicit multigraph and boundary adaptations. Its new protected edge need not be MAIN. If it is MAIN, the two adjacent triangles have protected middles, so they cannot be negative. If the edge was a MATCHING cut, its two incident triangles are the retained CROSS halves and are again positive. Their new protected outer loads are zero, so each is the fixed two-line triangle (0,0,pi). Thus in both cases the two marked triangles supply the genuine common strip. At a matching cut, formally pair the two boundary CROSS half-triangles along the new matching edge. This retains the cubic perfect-matching incidence needed for parity; it creates NO physical coupon. A GREEN matching edge between the new protected vertices would have both outer loads zero, hence be a pure-middle port already removed. Every other parallel marked edge gives an allowed MAIN/MAIN or CROSS MATCHING/MATCHING cut. Exhaustive splitting therefore makes the remaining marked line/line edge unique. Remove one positive marked triangle. The remaining abstract complex is a triangulated disk. A finite/finite edge fixes an orientation-preserving Euclidean gluing by its two distinct ordered centers; a line/finite edge fixes it by its COORIENTED line and center. The unique line/line edge is on the boundary and is never used for an underdetermined gluing. Around each interior finite vertex the holonomy fixes its center and rotates by its signed star angle, either zero or 2pi, so it is the identity. These vertex loops generate the dual disk's cycles. Boundary fans propagate the SAME two cooriented lines. The final finite circle touches both inward sides, forcing its radius to be half their shared distance and closing the omitted triangle. This argument uses disk topology and nondegenerate edge data, not simplicity of the remaining finite-edge graph. Double-triangle pieces have zero entropy and zero volume and are represented by two lines and one tangent circle. Every piece therefore gives its ONE family of oriented white planes, with each adjacent pair distinct and tangent. Its developed image may fold. Its signed two-ball chain volume is exactly the sum of sigma V for its original triangles, by the [signed cyclic-polygon and contact-triangle identities, §§1–2](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md). ## 3. Glue the pieces, retaining every original port pairing Root the actual cut tree. A child's marked ordered tangent pair is mapped to its already assigned parent pair by an orientation-preserving Mobius map. Explicitly send their common contacts to infinity; both ordered pairs become opposite cooriented parallel planes. Positive scale and translation match their width and position. The remaining horizontal translation is free. Each interior white label belongs to one piece; shared boundary label occurrences form connected subtrees. Recursion therefore gives ONE reflection for every actual smoothed white face. No independent reflection is chosen at different occurrences of a face. The free translations can be chosen generically to avoid accidental coincidences of distinct nonadjacent white circles. This is not an embedding requirement; all adjacent tangent pairs already remain nondegenerate. The original main prefixes telescope and cups/caps give their literal inverse pairs, exactly as before the cuts. For a GREEN port both triangles lie in the same piece, so its actual source collar C is already supplied by the [literal signed Green formula, §3](actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md) and is conjugated by that piece's ONE gluing map. For an original CROSS port whose two triangles lie in different pieces, its outer white pair x,y is common. Let P=r_y r_x=-I+H. It is noncentral parabolic. Each ordered triangle gives an actual raw first meridian A with trace-2 and with Tr((P+I)A)=4. After H=[[0,h],[0,0]], h!=0, this says A_21=4/h. Trace and determinant determine the other entries from A_11. The centralizer I+tH acts simply transitively on these pairs. Hence there is a UNIQUE actual C mapping its recorded input first meridian to its recorded output first meridian; it maps the second as well because the whole ordered product P is common. Equivalently C sends ALL THREE original contact flags: O=x/y is fixed, C1=x/b goes to C0=x/c, and C2=b/y goes to C3=c/y. It is precisely the original untwisted shaded pairing within the first ball. The second ball uses r_u C r_u with ONE global r_u, and the inverse is used on the reverse pairing. This does NOT pair the two artificial halves used to close a child piece into a new physical coupon. The original port may continue to connect different pieces after the geometric cut. Its raw auxiliary meridian is -C^-1, with the original physical lift C^-1. The actual four-crossing threading word returns it and transports both ordered main ports. Thus every original smoothed Morse relation holds. The two halves' independent local radii are not asserted to form a regular source-gradient chart at that boundary port; the boundary representation is constructed by its ACTUAL three-point relation and its globally computed entropy, not by selecting an unproved finite-sum or local re-framing branch. All actual main meridians are noncentral parabolic. At any retained auxiliary cusp, C^-1 and its actual preferred longitude P are in the same parabolic translation centralizer. This remains true if C=I, because P remains noncentral. Thus the entire peripheral subgroup preserves the contact and its canonical horosphere. ## 4. The original relative fundamental chain has the summed volume Use the TWO original cut balls of the actual smoothed projection and their literal proper digon-cut disks. Under the common reflection assignment the two ends of each disk are the SAME tangent-pair contact. Their canonical pair horosphere is common. The [finite incidence and short-edge construction, §4](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) places all disk replacements at height T with bounded horizontal coordinates, preserving the actual shaded/white pairings. Added tetrahedra have an edge of length O(1/T), so |Vol tetra|<=2pi ell cosh^2 ell makes their total volume vanish. Cut-disk collapse has relative degree one in the abstract domain. It leaves every original shaded triangle uncut and retains its actual C map even when its partner lies in a different block. These are geometric chain operations, not source factorizations. Each resulting abstract piece is developed by its assigned signed circle family. Cone its white/shaded faces to its own marked boundary contact; the signed cyclic fan identity gives its first-ball volume (1/2)sum sigma V, including winding-zero white polygons. The ONE global reflection r_u develops the second original ball, reversing target and abstract orientations together, so its contribution is the same. Mobius alignment of a piece preserves this geometric volume; no open Gauss regulator is reset or declared invariant. The collapsed disks add zero, and all original boundary faces pair. Therefore Vol(rho_sm)=sum_pieces sum_(triangles in piece) sigma V =2pi sum_pieces (actual entropy). (1) There is no missing constant: the input entropy splitting uses the already proved C=V/(2pi) and E=C_input-C_output. Artificial closing triangles are the forced two-line V=0 configurations. The original mark and target degrees were retained in the identity and tight-cut steps; no new quantum mark or 1/N normalization is introduced. ## 5. Return to the original drilled group Restore each actual deleted UNTWISTED port. Its middle faces were identified, so its ordered input and output pairs agree. Assign the original auxiliary meridian to identity. The literal threading word is then the identity. Its original outer product may be axial (loxodromic or elliptic), parabolic or central, because the removed matching edge imposed no remaining tangency. Choose its recorded peripheral flag and use the [proved zero-volume axis/parabolic filling-cap construction, §4](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md). No artificial outer contact is inserted. This gives a representation rho of the original drilled group, factoring through the actual meridional identity smoothing, with Vol(rho)=Vol(rho_sm)=2pi W_D (2) IF the exact hybrid decomposition/regularity hypotheses in section1 have been established for that maximum. The [representation-volume bound and strict-kernel theorem, §§1–3](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) then give W_D<=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). If at least one original meridian was killed, the already proved strict-kernel bound is strict; comparison with the known all-cross lower bound would exclude such a maximizing identity-deletion case. This assembly does not itself prove the hybrid tight-cut classification or the exclusion of every further free KKT stratum. It records exactly what geometry follows from those finite-flow outputs, and preserves all original group, peripheral and chain data needed for the comparison. ## Scope Root, coherent and cluster the complete conditional proof: the matching-mark CROSS boundary rows, cooriented piece development, original three-contact collar maps across pieces, one global reflected copy, actual digon-disk chain collapse and restored identity meridians. The axial restoration explicitly includes elliptic as well as loxodromic outer products. The formal boundary matching preserves combinatorial incidence only; no finite source coupon is inserted there. This proof retains one original relative fundamental chain and the actual source flags. It does not use the false local assertion that resetting a Gauss reference preserves an open crossing-word regulator; the [global chain note](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md) explains the replacement. [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_hybrid_piece_representation.py) checks 270 signed cyclic fans, four repeated-contact fans, four angle sums, 24 actual circle/line tangencies, eight contact-triangle volumes and two oriented two-ball strip chains. Its [recorded results](../experiments/actual_fejer_hybrid_piece_representation_results.json) use 80-digit arithmetic; root the code and cluster and replayed it. These finite geometric identities supplement the analytic proof; they do not prove general source pairings, relative degree or the cut-disk collapse. The conditional geometric conclusion does not by itself supply an asymptotic for the original phase-sensitive long-filled knot source.

title: Hybrid Fejer flow: all proper tight sets come from permitted digon cuts
status: Exact hybrid Hall cuts, forced zeros and feasible perturbations
text: # Hybrid Fejer flow: all proper tight sets come from permitted digon cuts 31 October 2026. This is a finite incidence theorem for the ACTUAL loopless white triangular cellulation obtained after source-preserving identity smoothing. The [closed local entropy](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) and [original shared source](actual_fejer_shared_entropy_variational.md) provide its local functions and literal incidence conventions. It does not replace a matching/matching Green cut by two independent entropy maxima. ## 1. Literal hybrid network Let T be a loopless triangular cellulation of the sphere, with R+2 white vertices and 2R triangular cells. Multiple edges remain distinct. The dual cubic graph has its original perfect matching: each port is the pair of triangles adjacent to its matching white edge. Keep two distinct protected white vertices u,v joined by an actual edge. Every other white vertex has target1; both protected targets are0. Some ports are tagged CROSS, others GREEN. A CROSS port retains its TWO triangle nodes, each of supply1/2, incident to that triangle's ordinary vertices. A GREEN port has ONE node of supply1 and its FOUR original incidences x,b,c,y: shared outer triangle corners x,y are aggregated once. Distinct incidences among these four remain parallel arcs if their global face labels coincide. This is the hybrid limiting flow used to perturb a fixed cross/strict-one-sided entropy point. The full supply is R, equal to the ordinary targets. For a set S of ordinary vertices let C_0(S) be the total supply of the complete triangle network touching S, and C_H(S) that of the hybrid network. Directly from the original pair of half-supplies, C_H(S)=C_0(S)+(1/2)g(S), (1) where g(S) counts the GREEN ports for which EXACTLY ONE of the two triangles touches S. In particular merging a pair never lowers a Hall capacity. The finite flow criterion is C_H(S)>=|S| for every S. ## 2. Complete Hall inequality and the equality case Take a nonempty proper S among the R ordinary vertices, and put U=V(T)\S, n=|U|. The induced embedded graph G=T[U] is loopless and contains the retained protected edge uv. Let p be the number of original triangular cells wholly supported on U. Each is still an actual face of G; a triangular face of G enclosing removed vertices does NOT count in p. Every other original triangle touches S, so C_0(S)=(2R-p)/2, C_0(S)=|S| iff p=2n-4. (2) Here is a face count which also handles disconnected induced graphs and isolated vertices. Move one point of S to infinity. Every original triangle supported on U is bounded in this planar drawing. For a connected component G_i with n_i>=2 vertices, write f_i for its bounded faces, e_i for its edges and p_i for its bounded original triangles. All face boundary walks have length at least2. Euler and edge counting give e_i=n_i+f_i-1, 2e_i>=3p_i+2(f_i-p_i)+2, p_i<=2n_i-4. (3) The final2 is the outer boundary walk. An isolated vertex contributes no triangle. If there are c>=1 nontrivial components and a isolated vertices, summing gives p<=2(n-a)-4c<=2n-4. (4) Thus the complete and hybrid Hall inequalities hold. For S empty or all ordinary vertices they are the trivial zero or total balance; every triangle has an ordinary corner because it has three distinct vertices and only u,v are protected. If S is proper and tight, p=2n-4. Equations (3)--(4) force a=0,c=1: G is connected. Every face not one of the p original triangles has boundary walk EXACTLY two edges, including the outer face. Since proper S implies n>=3, such a two-edge face cannot be one bridge traversed twice: its next boundary step would continue around the nontrivial remainder at one of its endpoints. Equivalently a bridge bounding a complete two-step face walk would make the entire connected graph a single edge. Consequently these faces are genuine digons bounded by two DISTINCT parallel original edges. Every removed S vertex belongs to the interior of one of these digon faces. Conversely each such non-original face contains removed vertices; the original cellulation is triangular. Therefore S is precisely the union of the interior vertex sets of these pairwise interior-disjoint actual digon disks. Each disk is mark-free in its interior. This classification uses the induced graph at S, not an assumed preselected digon decomposition tree. ## 3. Hybrid tightness merges only neighboring holes with the same endpoints Suppose C_H(S)=|S|. Then (1) and (4) force both C_0(S)=|S| and g(S)=0. Consider the digon disks from section2. Across an edge on one such disk's boundary, the inside triangle touches S. If this edge is MATCHING and its port is GREEN, the other triangle must touch S too, or that port would contribute to g(S). That other triangle belongs to a second digon disk on the other side of the SAME boundary edge. The two digons therefore have the same ordered pair of boundary vertices. Merge them across that green edge. Their union is again a digon disk bounded by the two remaining parallel edges. For clarity, all these mergers can be done at once. The adjacency graph of the S-digon disks across green matching boundary edges has degree at most2. Every connected component has a fixed endpoint pair. It cannot be a cycle for a proper S: a full cyclic family of parallel edge sectors fills the sphere except those two vertices, so the connected induced graph G would have only those vertices, contrary to n>=3. Its components are paths; each merges to one actual digon. This also proves that an intervening matching edge is removed only from the description of the separating boundary, not from the source or from its Green pair. After merging, every surviving matching boundary edge belongs to a CROSS port. A MAIN boundary edge never splits a paired triangle node. The two boundary edges of each resulting digon have the same type: the disk contains 2v triangular cells for v interior vertices, and the parity count of their one matching incidence per dual vertex forces an even number of matching edges to cross its two-edge boundary. Thus the permitted cuts are exactly MAIN / MAIN; or MATCHING / MATCHING with BOTH ports CROSS. (5) Each resulting disk is individually hybrid-tight. Its 2v triangles exhaust the demand v of its interior vertices; no green node crosses its boundary. The original tight set is a union of their interiors. In particular a general GREEN matching/matching cut has NOT been declared tight, split, or assigned additive entropy. The full set S of ordinary vertices is only the redundant total balance. Its possible U={u,v} one-edge or full-cycle exception does not force any additional ordinary incidence to vanish. ## 4. Forced zeros and a positive relative-interior witness For any feasible hybrid flow, a tight S forces every node touching S to send its entire supply into S. Thus each of its arcs to an ordinary vertex outside S is zero. Conversely an ordinary incidence arc is forced zero ONLY this way. One direct proof avoids a nondegeneracy assumption on the balance matrix. To force a small positive amount epsilon on an arc n->f, reduce that row supply and the target at f by epsilon. For any vertex set S containing f, both capacity and demand decrease equally. For S not containing f but touched by n, only capacity decreases. Such a constraint obstructs every positive epsilon exactly when S was tight. The finitely many other inequalities have positive slack, so a sufficiently small epsilon preserves them. The ordinary Hall criterion then supplies the remaining flow. Hence every non-forced ordinary arc is positive in some feasible flow. Averaging finitely many such flows gives one witness positive on ALL non-forced ordinary arcs and zero on the forced ones. Redundant face balances cause no difficulty. Equations (2)--(5) show that all forced zeros have the precise source-permitted digon origin above. Inside a MAIN/MAIN tight disk, whole ports remain inside and all incidences at its boundary white faces are zero. At a permitted MATCHING/MATCHING cut, its two inside CROSS triangles each have their two boundary corners zero and their interior middle corner1/2. These are constant, zero-entropy triangles. Only CROSS pairs are cut, so their additive C+C data may be retained/repaired across the boundary; no difference E=C_input-C_output is separated into independent pieces. The original outside and inside middle degrees are not reset by this network statement. Geometry and actual face-pairing assembly remain separate obligations. These cuts may be iterated as an exact HYBRID flow decomposition. Close the two sides by identifying their two boundary edges. The inside has new protected pair a,b and the outside retains its old pair. A MAIN cut leaves whole port nodes on their original sides. At a permitted matching cut, retain each of the four original CROSS triangle nodes on its own side and pair the two nodes on a closed side only as the formal C+C description. This creates no new physical coupon. The inside boundary loads are zero by tightness, while every outside boundary demand is unchanged. Thus the original hybrid feasible polytope is exactly the Cartesian product of those two piece polytopes, and its entropy is their sum: every GREEN E factor stays whole and every cut factor was additive C+C. The closure remains loopless, both marked vertices are adjacent, and every proper cut strictly reduces the number of triangles on each side. Iteration terminates. On each resulting piece there is no proper tight set, so section4 gives positivity on every ordinary allowed arc; the marked zero-dimensional triangle rows retain their fixed values. ## 5. Consequence for the boundary-regularity argument At a full-kernel maximum, tag terminal seams CROSS and keep the remaining strict non-diagonal half ports GREEN. The full continuous-h theorem permits this limiting description without claiming eventual feasibility of a newly fixed finite label pattern. The cross variables are their actual two triangle allocations. A small mixture with the relative-interior witness of section4 remains cross-admissible; each green point stays in its own strict half chamber because its original interval length and upper-endpoint margin are positive. The proved corner expansions then give a nonnegative epsilon log(1/epsilon) coefficient at every factor. Any zero ordinary degree or cross-triangle corner that is NOT structurally forced by (5) is activated and yields a strict positive gain. Thus such a maximum has no free zeros beyond those tight digon cuts. This assertion keeps diagonal ports excluded; their negative epsilon log(1/epsilon) term is not an allowed remainder. To turn this into a volume bound one must use the actual permitted cut pieces and their inherited marked flags when constructing finite positive multipliers and the global relative chain. The present proof is the complete finite support/witness classification, not an assertion that independent Green capacities factor across arbitrary digons. ## Scope The induced-face Euler argument includes disconnected induced graphs, digon faces and the proper-subset exception. The iterative cut uses variational C+C bookkeeping; it is not a finite-coupon replacement. Geometry additionally target-read the final iterative paragraph and confirmed its Cartesian flow product, unchanged outside targets, formal matching parity and termination. This record is scoped to the finite hybrid theorem and its regularity perturbation. This finite combinatorial proof has no separate numerical audit. It does not itself identify a group representation or a relative fundamental class, and it does not infer a phase-sensitive original filling asymptotic. The geometric piece assembly and whole-source comparison require their separate proofs.

title: Marked-line development for a regular signed Green configuration
status: Marked signed-circle development with retained boundary hypotheses
text: # Marked-line development for a regular signed Green configuration Completion: the [hybrid-piece theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_piece_representation.md) and [general endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) now handle the additional maximizing boundary strata. The failed local re-framing claim below remains withdrawn; the proof uses the original sewn relative fundamental chain. 31 October 2026. conditional stationary-stratum lemma. This extends the real local Green regulator to the FORCED two marked zero curvatures. It does not remove additional free row/outer endpoint strata or prove that a maximum of the compact entropy problem satisfies the hypotheses below. ## 1. Exact hypotheses from the original source Let C be the actual simplicial white triangulation of the certified connected flat plat, with the two original protected vertices u,v joined by their MAIN edge. Give every other vertex f a finite positive curvature l_f and set l_u=l_v=0. There are no additional zero or infinite radii. At each source triangle use the usual tangent-circle angle vector theta_j=2 atan(l_j/sqrt(l_0 l_1+l_1 l_2+l_2 l_0)). (1) A one-line triangle has angle zero at that line and strictly positive angles summing pi at its finite vertices. A two-line triangle uvf has angles (0,0,pi). Assign each triangle a sign sigma=+1 or -1. At cross ports both signs are positive. At a left Green port the input triangle (x,b,y) is positive and output (x,c,y) is negative; a right port reverses these roles. The negative triangle's middle is the overloaded face. Assume the actual shared degree equations hold. Every ordinary vertex has demand1 and protected vertices have demand0. The [exact signed-angle formula for E](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) gives, at every finite vertex f, sum_(triangles at f) sigma theta_(triangle,f) =2pi(1-o_f), (2) where o_f is the number of its overloaded-middle incidences. Original finite feasibility gives o_f in {0,1}; protected faces have o_f=0. No independent angle optimization has replaced the source constraints. The two uv triangles necessarily have POSITIVE sign. Indeed uv is a MAIN edge, so in either triangle one of u,v is its middle. A negative triangle would overload that protected middle, which is impossible. These two triangles have no other degeneracy than their two line faces. At a constrained source stationary point, equations (1) hold with ONE shared vector of finite positive multipliers whenever all remaining row/outer equations are strict. Forced cases l_b=0, l_x=0 or l_y=0 are retained as the corresponding one-step/endpoint limits; no derivative in a protected zero variable is imposed. This clause is a hypothesis on the stationary stratum, not a claim about every maximizer. ## 2. A cooriented developing disk closes the SAME marked strip Remove the open uvf_R triangle from the sphere. The remaining complex is a triangulated closed disk, whose boundary vertices are u,v,f_R. Start with the other uv triangle uvf_L. Realize u,v as the outward halfplanes Y<=0 and Y>=H and f_L as a circle of radius r_fL=1/l_fL tangent to both, with H=2r_fL. Fix its horizontal center at zero. This uses one common Euclidean normalization, not separate normalizations at different ports. Every all-finite triangle of prescribed positive radii is a rigid configuration of three EXTERNALLY tangent circles. Choose the orientation of its center triangle to be its prescribed sigma relative to the actual cyclic source order. A one-line triangle is likewise rigid: its two finite centers are on the inward side of that COORIENTED line, at normal distances r_f,r_g, and their horizontal separation is 2sqrt(r_f r_g). The two choices of its sign reverse that horizontal displacement. Glue these rigid configurations along their actual shared edges. Along a finite/finite edge two distinct ordered centers determine the unique orientation-preserving Euclidean motion. Along a line/finite edge the cooriented line and finite center determine that motion. The only line/line edge uv is on the boundary of the disk, so it is never used as an underdetermined interior gluing. Thus every dual path develops the same radius data by actual Euclidean motions. Here is the complete holonomy check. A dual cycle surrounding an interior finite vertex fixes its developed center. Its rotation is the signed sum of the center angles in its star, which is 2pi or zero by (2). It is therefore the identity Euclidean motion, including its translation part. This remains true at f_L: its uv corner contributes the recorded pi and the two cooriented line normals are opposite. Cycles of the dual disk are generated by these interior finite-vertex stars. The vertices u,v are BOUNDARY vertices, so no unproved translation loop around an infinite vertex remains. Development is path-independent. The incident triangles of each boundary vertex u or v form a connected fan. They therefore propagate the SAME cooriented line, not an independent parallel translate at each occurrence. The final boundary circle f_R is one circle tangent on the inward side to both already fixed lines. Its center consequently has Y=r_fR and H-Y=r_fR. Hence r_fR=H/2. This closes the omitted positive uv triangle and proves the shared-strip condition. The result is a globally assigned family of oriented white circles and the original two opposite lines. Adjacent circles are externally tangent. Nonadjacent circles may overlap, and the developed triangular surface may fold or have winding zero at overloaded vertices. Embeddedness, convexity and local degree one are NOT used or asserted. ## 3. Explicit boundary reflection and source-collar adapters Write an anti-Mobius reflection by a determinant -1 matrix J; products of reflections use J_2 conjugate(J_1). For x,y>0, normalize the outer circles to center0/radius1/x and center (x+y)/(xy)/radius1/y. Put A=x+y, T_z=sqrt(z A+xy), and use J_x=[[0,1/x],[x,0]], J_y=[[A/x,-(2x+y)/x^2],[y,-A/x]], J_z^eta=[[z/x+(y-x)/A+2i eta T_z/A,-z/x^2-2/x], [z,-z/x-(y-x)/A+2i eta T_z/A]]. (3) For z>0 this is the circle tangent to both outer circles on the eta side. At z=0 the SAME matrix is a line reflection; all entries stay finite and its determinant stays -1. Thus a protected middle parent requires no division by its vanished clock or a newly chosen flag. When x=0,y>0 choose instead the actual lower line and tangent y circle: J_x=-iI, J_y=[[i,0],[y,i]], J_z^eta=[[-2eta sqrt(z/y)+i,-4/y], [z,2eta sqrt(z/y)+i]]. (4) The finite z circle has center -2eta/sqrt(zy)+i/z and radius1/z. At z=0, (4) is the second line reflection [[i,-4/y],[0,i]], namely Y=2/y. In particular the double-zero corner x=b=0 retains the ACTUAL two-line strip and its selected contact, while T_b=0 is never divided out. For y=0,x>0 the explicitly ordered version is J_x=[[i,0],[x,i]], J_y=-iI, J_z^eta=[[2eta sqrt(z/x)+i,-4/x], [z,-2eta sqrt(z/x)+i]]. (4b) It follows by reversing the outer pair in (4) AND changing eta to -eta; P is inverted and H changes sign, so the displayed source coefficient in (5) remains exactly the same. This is the recorded ordering adapter, not a free independent reversal of a source port. In either chart put P=J_y conjugate(J_x), A_z=J_z conjugate(J_x), B_z=J_y conjugate(J_z), so B_z A_z=P. These are the original ordered raw meridians, all of trace -2. Direct multiplication gives H=P+I, H^2=0, H!=0, C=I+i(eta_c T_c-eta_b T_b)H/[2(x+y)], C A_b C^-1=A_c, C B_b C^-1=B_c. (5) For (4), T_z=sqrt(zy), so (5) holds verbatim with x=0. These are the SAME source signs and entire-pair transport as the full physical half-power derivative calculation. They are not selected from trace alone. The actual threading word [2,1,1,2] takes raw auxiliary -C^-1, closes it and transports both physical ports. The original cup/cap/mark and all original prefix orders remain those of the source. IMPORTANT CORRECTION FROM THE original-WORD TEST: the local regulator is NOT invariant under an arbitrary common Mobius conjugation followed by resetting the Gauss reference flag. The four-crossing heads return correctly, but the open-port Bloch sum changes. For example, the regular quartet (x,b,c,y)=(2,3,5,7), cross signs (+,-), in the explicitly tested new frame has word regulator 5.61311634644, whereas V_b+V_c is 9.50477551507. At forced marked boundaries the discrepancy persists. The new frame in this test is the common conjugation D=[[1,0.37+0.21i], [0.17-0.13i,1+(0.37+0.21i)(0.17-0.13i)]]. All original returned heads still agree to 75-digit accuracy. The earlier proposed generic-frame continuity proof is WITHDRAWN. Thus (3)--(5) prove the actual line/circle GROUP adapter. They do not yet prove the source regulator identity in a freshly chosen Gauss frame. One must transport the original reference decoration, or compare the FULL sewn fundamental chain so that open-port boundary coboundaries are included.
