text: # Complete figure-eight clock sectors and diagonal Gram metrics 29 October 2026. The exact factorial length frame has a polynomial original clock co-source. Nevertheless one fully anchor-contracted clock sector of the original figure-eight knot has twice the desired volume rate. Consequently every positive DIAGONAL clock metric has an exponentially excessive Cauchy budget on this actual source. This concerns a COMPLETE clock sector, after its anchor sums and original closure contractions. It is not an expanded crossing state or an arbitrary inserted coupon. It does not disprove Cauchy--Schwarz, the volume conjecture, or a coherent non-diagonal special inner product. ## 1. The original source and its exact reduced table Use `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `x=-q^-1`, `F_a=(Q;Q)_a`, `s_a=|F_a|`. The actual word is `[1,-2,1,-2]`. Its clocks are the original overclocks `(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3)`. The [whole charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) and [actual closure contractions](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) give K_N=sum_h K_(N;h), K_(N;h)=(chi_N/N) zeta_(N;h) C_(N;h), |zeta|=1. (1) `chi_N` is the unchanged original external dimension/framing line; at completeness its modulus and inverse have polynomial size. Every common Cartan, pivot and source factor stays in (1). `zeta` consists only of the explicitly retained powers of `x,Q`, the crossing Cartan phases and the closure-rescaling monomials. No unknown knot scalar has been divided out. The full source support gives `h_0=0`, before any separate-sector Schur argument. In the rescaled anchors of [the actual alternating-source table](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md#3-a-second-support-inequality-in-the-actual-reduced-polynomial), write `B_L(U,V;Q^p)=product_(r<L)(U-Q^(p+r)V)`. Then C_(N;h)=[A^d B^d C^d D^d] product of these EIGHT blocks: | tail -> head | length | p | | --- | --- | --- | | B -> C | d-h_0 | 0 | | C -> A | h_0 | 1 | | D -> A | d-h_1 | h_1+1 | | A -> B | h_1 | -h_1+h_2+1 | | C -> B | d-h_2 | h_0+h_2+2 | | B -> D | h_2 | -h_2-h_3-1 | | A -> D | d-h_3 | -h_1 | | D -> C | h_3 | 0 | This table includes the original pivotal closure substitutions. For auditability, `zeta` in (1) is obtained without any scalar choice by: the `charged_data` weight; the `normalized_graph` tail monomials; the `contract_edge` closure factors; and the substitutions of anchors `B,D` by `x^-1 B,x^-1 D`. Each factor is an original root of unity. Those exact operations are implemented in the audit linked below. The normalized blocks b_L=B_L/D_L, D_L=s_L^(1/2)/N^(1/4) have `D_(d-h_i)D_(h_i)=1` at each crossing. Thus the product of all EIGHT table normalizers is exactly one. The coefficient `C_(N;h)` is also the completely contracted normalized-b clock STATE in this closure-contracted presentation. The co-source remains polynomial, as in [the exact clock-source theorem](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md). ## 2. A uniform family with no internal cancellation Let N=3k+1, d=3k, h=(0,2k,k,2k), k>=1, beta_(L,r)=|[L choose r]_Q|=s_L/(s_r s_(L-r)), S_k=sum_(r=0)^k beta_(2k,r) beta_(2k,k-r)>0. (2) Then the COMPLETE table coefficient is exactly C_(N;(0,2k,k,2k))=N q^(3k^2-2k) S_k/F_k. (3) In particular the original sector modulus is |K_(N;(0,2k,k,2k))|=|chi_N| S_k/s_k. (4) Here is a direct coefficient proof. The full `B_d(B,C;1)` contracts `B=Q^-1 C`. Its `C -> B` loop is `C^(2k)N/F_k`. Reversing the `D -> A` interval and concatenating it with the `A -> D` interval produces `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)` with reversal factor xi_1=(-Q^(2k+1))^k Q^[k(k-1)/2]. The replacement in `B -> D` contributes `Q^-k`. For the two remaining C/D intervals use B_k(C,D;Q^(-3k)) B_(2k)(D,C;1) =xi_J (C^N-D^N)/(C-Q^(-2k)D), xi_J=(-1)^(2k)Q^[(2k)(2k-1)/2]. (5) For `0<=r<=k` its coefficient of `C^(k-r)D^(2k+r)` is `xi_J Q^[-2k(2k+r)]`. The remaining A/D extraction is therefore the `D^k` coefficient of `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)^2`, times the displayed common root factors. Indeed the second interval has effective start `Q^(k-2k-2k)=Q^(-3k)=Q`. The coefficient of `A^(2k-r)D^r` in `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)` is (-q^(2k+1))^r beta_(2k,r). Consequently every summand of its `D^k` coefficient has the SAME phase. Combining this phase, (5), `xi_1` and `Q^-k` gives precisely `q^(3k^2-2k)`, proving (3). All finite sums, including the loop factor, have been evaluated; no uncontracted anchor is left. ## 3. Its exact exponential rate Put `Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin u)du` and `v_3=3 Lambda(pi/3)`. The successive ratios of `beta_(2k,r)` are beta_(2k,r+1)/beta_(2k,r) =sin((2k-r)pi/N)/sin((r+1)pi/N), which decrease with `r` because `(2k+1)pi/N<pi`. Hence the symmetric summands in `S_k` are maximal at the integer(s) nearest `k/2`. The sum lies between that maximum and `(k+1)` times it. The uniform factorial estimate, including its endpoints, is log s_a=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi*a/N)+O(log N). It follows directly that lim_(k->infinity) (1/N)log(S_k/s_k) =[3Lambda(pi/3)+2Lambda(pi/6)]/pi =2v_3/pi=Vol(4_1)/pi. (6) The elementary Lobachevsky duplication identity gives `2Lambda(pi/6)=3Lambda(pi/3)=v_3`. The identification `Vol(4_1)=2v_3` uses its two regular ideal tetrahedra, rather than an asymptotic volume formula for the invariant. Thus the actual complete sector has lim (2pi/N)log|K_(N;h)|=2 Vol(4_1). (7) This is larger than the desired full-knot rate `Vol(4_1)`. The full original figure-eight scalar does have that latter rate by its separately proved positive finite sum. There must therefore be cancellation between COMPLETE clock sectors in this exact frame. ## 4. What this forces on a special inner product For the flat clock energy `G_N=sum_h |K_(N;h)|^2`, (7) gives liminf_(N=1 mod3) (pi/N)log G_N >=2 Vol(4_1). (8) The same exponent holds for the normalized-b state energy, because the original co-source coefficient in (1) has only polynomial norm. This rules out identifying that flat energy, up to subexponential factors, with a positive geometric angle partition of rate `Vol/pi`. More generally let `K=sum_h a_h f_h`. For EVERY positive diagonal metric `G=diag(g_h)` the exact Cauchy budget is B(G)=(sum_h g_h|f_h|^2)(sum_h |a_h|^2/g_h) >=(sum_h |a_h f_h|)^2. (9) The infimum over all positive `g_h` is the right side, obtained by `g_h` proportional to `|a_h|/|f_h|`; zero entries follow by limits. In particular (7) makes ALL diagonal-clock Cauchy budgets too large for the desired geometric upper exponent, even when the metric depends arbitrarily on `N` and on the entire diagram. For a general positive definite, possibly non-diagonal `G`, the Riesz vector of the linear co-source `sum_h a_h f_h` is `conj(a)`. Consequently its budget is B(G)=(f^*Gf)(a^T G^(-1)conj(a)) >=||f||^2 ||a||^2/kappa(G). (10) In the original singleton source `||a||` has polynomial upper and lower bounds, while this fixture gives `||f||^2>=exp[2N Vol(4_1)/pi-o(N)]`. Therefore a sharp budget `B(G)<=exp[N Vol(4_1)/pi+o(N)]` requires log kappa(G)>=N Vol(4_1)/pi-o(N) (11) along this subsequence. Exponential conditioning is allowed: the factorial metrics already exhibit it. Equation (11) is not a nonexistence theorem. It says that a successful coherent Gram has to retain genuine phase cancellation; a diagonal reweighting cannot replace it. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_figure_eight_clock_gram.py): the literal original reduced table and its exact root-field coefficient, the common-phase formula (3), positive-sum maximum bounds and the large-level rate. The proof above is uniform in all `k`.

title: The fixed complete Hermite energy overshoots the original figure-eight rate
text: # The fixed complete Hermite energy overshoots the original figure-eight rate 29 October 2026. The complete positive channel metric constructed in [the actual source multiplicity module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) has polynomial BOTH original boundary norms. Its full coherent energy nevertheless exceeds the sharp knot-volume rate already for the literal original figure-eight word. This is proved by one EXACT complete channel, not by a dephased path, an unconstrained clock sector, or a numerical fit. For every odd N=2m+1>=3, the simple Casimir channel c=-2 has the exact amplitude z_simple=N Q^[m(m+1)] F_m B_m, B_m=sum_(r=0)^m |[m choose r]_Q|^2 >0. (1) All original Cartan phases and cap/cup normalizations are included. Consequently the normalized fixed-Gram energy satisfies E_N >=N^2 B_m^2, log(N^2 B_m^2)=N v_8/pi+O(log N), (2) where v_8=4 Catalan is the regular ideal octahedron volume. Since v_8>Vol(S^3 minus 4_1), this fixed Gram CANNOT supply a sharp figure-eight energy upper bound. It remains a valid Cauchy metric. The obstruction concerns this explicitly specified complete energy, not every coherent metric or a source-specific regrouping. ## 1. The complete metric and the original word Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, and kappa=q^(d^2/2). On the complete N-dimensional three-head Hom space W use the physical basis |a,d-a>. Let R be the original positive pair crossing on degree d, including kappa, and let J be the exact symmetric anti-Pascal recoupling from [the complete module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md). The original pair source is p_a=Nx^(a-d), ell_a=x^a/N. The full signed generators are R_12=R and R_23=J^-1 R J. Let V be the COMPLETE degree-d canonical Hermite frame of the actual pair Casimir A, with f_0(c)=1, and define S=V^-1 J, G_N=S^*S/N. The metric is full rank and depends only on the original module and N. Its normalized ordinary-cap dual norm is <=1 and its initial cup energy is O(N^2), as proved in the complete source theorem. The TRUE figure-eight four-plat has chronological word [2,-1,2,2], W=R_23^2 R_12^-1 R_23. (3) It is NOT the original three-braid trace word with a newly attached cup. The [whole-source proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) identifies (3), its literal turns and its oriented framing. At completeness it gives EXACTLY ell Wp=K_N(4_1)=sum_(a=0)^d |F_a|^2. (4) In particular no unknown knot scalar is used to define G_N. The complete coherent output and normalized energy tested here are z=SWp, E_N=||z||_2^2/N. (5) The external line chi_N, if retained as a separate convention, is put inside the transported state and multiplies (5) by |chi_N|^2. In the reduced, zero-framing normalization (4) the scalar is the displayed positive original period. We never replace the full Cartan by its modulus inside the finite algebra below. ## 2. A positive full-channel covector, derived from the actual Casimir Assume N=2m+1. The pair Casimir has the SIMPLE channel c_m=q^(2m+1)+q^(-2m-1)=-2. It has no derivative column. Let f=f(-2) be its canonical eigenvector f_0=1. The exact identities from the source module are J=J^T, J A J^-1=B^T, B e_j=c_j e_j+b_j e_(j-1), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), b_j=Q^j+Q^-j-2. (6) For completeness symmetry of J follows directly from its formula: J_ij/J_ji reduces to1 using F_jF_(d-j)=N(-1)^j Q^[j(j+1)/2] and x^2Q=1. Set y=Jf. Since (B^T+2)y=0, its coordinates below m are zero. For j=m+r, r>=1, its recurrence has the real positive ratio y_(m+r)/y_(m+r-1)=b_(m+r)/b_r =|1-Q^(m+1-r)|^2/|1-Q^r|^2. The last row of J is e_0^T, so y_d=f_0=1. Thus EXACTLY y_i=0 for i<m, y_(m+r)=|[m choose r]_Q|^2, 0<=r<=m. (7) This is an eigenvector calculation on the COMPLETE original module. It retains the coherent q-Hahn sums within f and J. No path phases have been deleted. The root phases cancel only in the proved recurrence (7). ## 3. The original finite source reduces the selected channel to one sum The first actual crossing on the cup has the exact highest-chart coefficient (R_23 p)_a=kappa p_a F_(d-a). (8) Indeed the cup has third physical color0, and extracting output third color0 uses the literal ground-output coefficient R_(b,0;b,0)=kappa F_b. This does not change the rest of the source. Set v=R^-1(R_23 p). In RIGHT physical coordinates the remaining two R_23 factors are R^2. At the simple channel its CD inverse row is f^T/sigma, with sigma=x^d nu_m, nu_m=(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)], kappa^2=x^d. Consequently the full simple-channel coordinate is z_simple=(kappa^2 nu_m^2/sigma)y^T v=nu_m y^T v. (9) All kappa factors have been accounted for, rather than dropped. Here is a source-exact finite evaluation of y^T v. Substitution of the original negative crossing into (8), followed only by root complementation of factorials, gives for every 0<=i<=d v_i=x^(i-d)(-1)^i Q^[i(i+1)/2-d] F_(d-i)/F_i *sum_(b=i)^d Q^b F_b^3/F_(b-i). (10) This is the full negative matrix applied to (8), not one route. Put zeta_m=(-1)^m x^-m Q^[m(m+1)/2+1]. Using (7), each term in the selected contraction becomes exactly y_(m+r)v_(m+r) =zeta_m Q^(r^2)/F_r^2 *sum_(b=m+r)^(2m) Q^b F_b^3/F_(b-m-r). Swap b=m+t and r. The elementary finite Durfee-square identity sum_(r=0)^t Q^(r^2)/(F_r^2 F_(t-r))=1/F_t^2 (11) therefore gives y^T v=zeta_m Q^m F_m^3 U_m, U_m=sum_(t=0)^m Q^t (a;Q)_t^3/F_t^2, a=Q^-m=Q^(m+1). (12) One direct proof of (11) works first with a formal variable Q. The generating function for partitions with largest part at most t is1/F_t. Decomposing them by Durfee square r gives sum_r Q^(r^2)[t choose r]_Q/F_r: the right rectangle contributes the Gaussian polynomial and the lower partition contributes1/F_r. Substitution of the factorial expression gives (11). This rational identity extends to the present root because all its factorial indices are<N. No convergence argument at a unit root is used. ## 4. An elementary terminating transform makes the WHOLE projection positive The finite identity needed in (12) is U_m=(-1)^m Q^[-m(3m+1)/2] B_m, B_m=sum_(k=0)^m Q^[-k(m-k)] [m choose k]_Q^2. (13) The last summands are precisely the positive magnitudes in (1). Here is a derivation, independently reproduced in the [finite transform proof](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md). Expand the THIRD (a;Q)_t by the finite q-binomial theorem and put t=k+j,n=m-k. Its inner sum is the terminating Chu identity sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j^2 Q^j/ [F_j(Q^(k+1);Q)_j] =Q^(-n^2)(a;Q)_n F_k/F_m. (14) For a direct finite proof, the general identity with one numerator replaced by b and the denominator by c is sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j(b;Q)_j Q^j/[F_j(c;Q)_j] =b^n(c/b;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. After multiplication by (c;Q)_n it is the Newton expansion of product_(i=0)^(n-1)(b-cQ^i) in the basis (b;Q)_j. The recursion b(b;Q)_j=Q^-j[(b;Q)_j-(b;Q)_(j+1)] and Gaussian Pascal give its coefficients by induction. Taking b=Q^-n,c=Q^(k+1), and Q^(m+1)=a proves (14). Inserting (14), use (a;Q)_k=(-1)^k Q^[-mk+k(k-1)/2] F_m/F_(m-k). The total sign is(-1)^m. Its exponent is -m(3m+1)/2-k(m-k). The remaining factorial ratio is [m choose k]_Q^2. This proves (13) with no uncomputed scalar. Combining (12),(13), its remaining phase is Q^[-2m^2+m+1]=Q^[(1-m)(2m+1)]=1. Hence y^T v=F_m^3 B_m. Finally F_m^2=N nu_m, and (9) yields z_simple=nu_m F_m^3 B_m=N nu_m^2 F_m B_m, which is exactly (1). This proves the witness for EVERY odd level, including composite levels, using only nonzero factorials of index<N. ## 5. Rigorous exponential excess of the normalized complete energy Let J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi*s))ds and Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin u)du. The uniform root factorial estimate gives, simultaneously for every 0<=r<=m, log |[m choose r]_Q| =N[J(m/N)-J(r/N)-J((m-r)/N)]+O(log N). At m/N->1/2 the unique maximum is r/N->1/4. The derivative is log[sin(pi*(m/N-t))/sin(pi*t)], so its unique zero is t=m/(2N), with the expected sign on either side. Rounding to the nearest integer changes the objective by O(log N/N). There are only m+1 positive summands. Therefore log B_m=(4N/pi)Lambda(pi/4)+O(log N) =(2N/pi) Catalan+O(log N). (15) Here Catalan=2Lambda(pi/4); J(1/2)=0. Since |F_m|^2=N, the selected coordinate of (5) alone proves E_N>=|z_simple|^2/N=N^2 B_m^2, liminf_(N odd) log E_N/N>=8Lambda(pi/4)/pi=v_8/pi. (16) The original scalar (4) instead has squared rate Vol(S^3 minus 4_1)/pi=6Lambda(pi/3)/pi. Strict concavity of Lambda on(0,pi/3), with Lambda(0)=0, gives Lambda(pi/4)>(3/4)Lambda(pi/3). Thus v_8=8Lambda(pi/4)>6Lambda(pi/3)=Vol(S^3 minus 4_1). The excess is strict, without relying on numerical knot recognition or a fitted limit. In particular no polynomial factor can repair a sharp-volume upper bound for THIS E_N. We do not assert that the full energy limit equals v_8/pi. The proved lower witness is enough to decide the question. Other complete channels can only increase this positive energy. The ordinary-cap scalar still sums their VALUE coordinates COHERENTLY and gives (4). Thus the excess is not a counterexample to the invariant's volume limit or to Cauchy--Schwarz; it locates cancellation/energy discarded by this fixed metric. A non-diagonal source/word regrouping can change that energy and is not excluded. The same witness also applies to the complete diagonal CD-weighted channel metric with block weight |sigma_j|: its simple c=-2 weight is EXACTLY1. More generally any replacement channel metric bounded below by exp(-o(N)) times the identity retains the exponential excess. This does not exclude a coherent non-diagonal terminal/source Gram with a small eigenvalue on the offending full packet. Such a Gram requires an additional actual contraction or source argument; the polynomial boundary norms alone do not supply it. ### No positive metric separated by Casimir node has a sharp Cauchy budget There is a stronger conclusion that does not require a lower bound on the metric. Work in the full channel coordinates z=SWp and keep the actual cap row a=ell S^(-1). At the SIMPLE odd-level node c=-2, a_s=x^d/N, z_s=N Q^[m(m+1)]F_m B_m. Let D_N be ANY positive Hermitian metric block diagonal by distinct Casimir nodes. Its two-by-two Hermite blocks may be arbitrary positive matrices; their weights may depend exponentially on N or on the word. The isolated simple block is some number g_s>0. Positivity gives a D_N^(-1) a^*>=|a_s|^2/g_s, z^*D_N z>=g_s|z_s|^2. Consequently its ENTIRE Cauchy budget, not merely its state energy, satisfies (a D_N^(-1) a^*)(z^*D_N z) >=|a_s z_s|^2=N B_m^2. (17) By (15) this has exponential rate v_8/pi, strictly above the squared original invariant's rate. Thus arbitrary reweighting of separate Casimir nodes cannot fix the estimate by trading source cost against state energy. The sharp metric must mix distinct nodes, or use an actual coherent packet contraction that does so. The [terminal positive Gram](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md) provides precisely such a contraction on the same full module for the benchmark, with all original source factors retained. ## 6. Stable whole-source audit [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.py) retains the literal full original R and inverse, all half-Cartan kappas, the complete cup and cap, and the actual chronological word (3). Exact finite-field checks verify the selected FULL channel, not an isolated path. High-precision complex checks use the original q-binomial pair matrix, its exact antiunitary negative, and the closed CD inverse blocks. There is NO ill-conditioned dense numerical inverse. The exact scalar is compared to (4) at every tested level. The saved audit reports eight exact odd-root source witnesses, ten growing-level high-precision complete energies through N=129, and precision-refinement comparisons including the highest tested level. These are supplementary to Sections2--5, which prove the all-odd-level witness and strict exponential excess. The independent finite-transform artifact checks its elementary identities separately from the asymptotic.

title: Actual ordinary-color q-jets: one-volume growth and a macroscopic tame source
text: # Actual ordinary-color q-jets: one-volume growth and a macroscopic tame source 28 October 2026. The ordinary-color VALUES are polynomial at q_N, but their q-normal derivatives need not be. For the actual figure-eight state, the first derivative at color N-1 has the sharp volume exponent, with an explicit positive formula and leading constant. Nevertheless EVERY fixed-order q-jet, uniformly over all ordinary colors, has at most that ONE-volume exponent, not two volumes. A separate positive-plat argument gives a genuinely broad source filtration: every fixed q-jet is polynomial for colors k(j-1)+1<=N in a fixed k-bridge presentation. This includes the entire figure-eight half-orbit and its midpoint. It permits restarting the actual fixed-budget pointed recurrence at a macroscopic color, with polynomial data and no input from the complete value. ## 1. The actual whole-source cyclotomic polynomial Use the independently proved ordinary-color identity C_j(q)=sum_(k=0)^(j-1) T_(j,k)(q), T_(j,k)=product_(r=1)^k (q^(2j)+q^(-2j)-q^(2r)-q^(-2r)). (1) Its reduced unknot normalization, crossing Cartan phases and zero framing are the original ones. At roots (1) is the actual Newton state of the pointed Green theorem; for fixed j the generic Laurent identity follows from the independently identified ordinary quotient at infinitely many levels. Thus (1) is not fitted to K_N. Put q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q=q_N^2, F_k=(Q;Q)_k and J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi t))dt, gamma=max J=J(5/6), Delta=2gamma=Vol(4_1)/(2pi). All q-derivatives below keep the integer color j FIXED. They are not meridian derivatives or derivatives along a changing root level. ## 2. A sharp exact first jet at the top ordinary color Write D_q=q d/dq. For every N>=3, (D_q C_(N-1))(q_N) =-2N(Q-Q^-1) sum_(k=1)^(N-2) |F_(k-1) F_(k+1)|/|F_2|. (2) Every summand is POSITIVE real before the displayed common phase. Indeed all nonconstant T_(N-1,k) contain the root-zero factor r=1. Its derivative is -2N(Q-Q^-1). Every remaining factor is Q+Q^-1-Q^r-Q^-r =4sin(pi(r+1)/N)sin(pi(r-1)/N)>0, 2<=r<=N-2. Multiplication gives precisely the factorial quotient in (2), with the k=1 empty product equal to one. This is a derivative of the COMPLETE original ordinary state, rather than an individual large summand. Its value C_(N-1)(q_N)=1 does not control this jet. The exact leading asymptotic, through ALL integer levels, is (D_q C_(N-1))(q_N) =-i N^(7/2)/(pi 3^(1/4)) exp(N Delta)(1+o(1)). (3) Proof. Uniformly on compact 0<s<1 the elementary factorial estimate is |F_k|=sqrt(2Nsin(pi k/N)) exp(NJ(k/N))(1+O(1/N)), and its all-index version has logarithmic error O(log N). Also |F_2|=8pi^2/N^2 (1+O(N^-2)). Thus the summand in (2), at s=k/N, is [N^3 sin(pi s)/(4pi^2)] exp(2NJ(s))(1+O(1/N)). The exponent has its unique global maximum at s=5/6 and second derivative -2pi sqrt(3). Endpoint-uniform estimates discard its complement exponentially. Rescale k=5N/6+sqrt(N)xi. The lattice Gaussian sum has integral 3^-1/4, with arbitrary fractional part of 5N/6. Since sin(5pi/6)=1/2, its sum is N^(7/2)/(8pi^2 3^(1/4)) exp(NDelta)(1+o(1)). Finally -2N(Q-Q^-1)=-8pi i(1+O(N^-2)). This proves (3). At N=2 the only ordinary color is trivial and the first jet is zero. ## 3. Uniform ONE-volume upper bound for every fixed q-jet For every fixed nonnegative integer r there are constants A,C_r independent of N and j such that |[t^r] C_j(q_N(1+t))| <=C_r N^(A+4r) exp(NDelta), 1<=j<N. (4) The same assertion holds for logarithmic derivatives D_q^r, with a different fixed C_r. It controls the ENTIRE fixed-order ordinary jet vector, up to polynomial dimension factors. In particular fixed jets do not accumulate a two-volume rate in this example. Here is a direct all-color proof, including activated root zeros. For each factor in (1), at q_N, f_(j,r)=-4sin(pi(j+r)/N)sin(pi(j-r)/N). For r<j<N it is zero only when j+r=N, and there is at most ONE such factor in a product. Every nonzero factor has magnitude at least 16/N^2. Every fixed-order derivative of a factor is bounded by C_r N^r. Repeated Leibniz differentiation therefore costs at most C_r N^(4r) times the product of all NONZERO root factors: there are at most N^r choices of differentiated factors, at most r removed nonzero factors, and derivative powers cost N^r. An undifferentiated zero simply makes that term zero. It remains to bound these root products, not to assume them tame. If k<min(j,N-j), their exact magnitude is |T_(j,k)(q_N)| =|F_(j+k)|/[|1-Q^j| |F_(j-k-1)|]. (5) Its logarithm is at most N(max J-min J)+O(log N)=NDelta+O(log N). If j>N/2 and k>=m=N-j, the zero at r=m is removed; the remaining absolute product is EXACTLY |F_(k+m) F_(k-m)|/[|1-Q^m| |1-Q^(2m)|]. (6) All factorial indices are in 0,...,N-1 and 2m<N. Since each J is at most gamma and the two denominators are bounded below by 4/N, (6) has the same exponential upper bound. Equations (5)--(6), the all-index factorial estimate and the additional sum over k prove (4). This proof does not rely on cancellations or an ordinary-jet bound which is being inferred from the desired volume theorem. ## 4. A broad polynomial window, including the midpoint The independent positive-plat/source proof in [the macroscopic normal-jet window](ordinary_color_macroscopic_normal_jet_window.md) gives, for ANY fixed knot with a k-bridge plat and every fixed r, |[t^r]C_j(q_N(1+t))|<=C_(K,k,r) N^(c_(K,k,r)) whenever k(j-1)+1<=N. (7) The inclusive endpoint is important. Its elementary inputs are: * The actual endpoint-zero TL path space for the 2k(j-1)-strand cable has maximum height k(j-1). On the one-sided arc theta in [pi/(2N),pi/N), all required sine weights are positive. * Actual colored cups have squared norm [j]^k, and the reduced original closure divides by exactly [j], giving the generic-arc bound |C_j(exp(i theta))|<=[j]_theta^(k-1). * The actual zero-framed finite cut is Laurent in q^(1/2) of degree O_K(j^2). Clearing its denominator after a tangent-half-angle substitution makes an ordinary polynomial on an interval of length comparable to 1/N; the clearing factor varies by O_K(1). Elementary Chebyshev coefficient/derivative bounds give polynomial fixed derivatives, including at the one-sided endpoint. The proof takes the invariant polynomial to the endpoint, rather than differentiating a singular path basis or a zero quantum dimension. For k>=2 the relevant ordinary [j] is nonzero. For the figure-eight, k=2. Thus every fixed q-jet is polynomial uniformly through j=floor((N+1)/2). In particular the midpoint has NO positive exponential jet rate. No matching positive lower rate is claimed there: a particular derivative may vanish. On the other hand (3) proves sharp one-volume growth near the far endpoint. The polynomial source filtration therefore separates actual tame half-orbit data from exponentially large far normal response. ## 5. Restart the ACTUAL pointed system without using C_N Assume k>=2; the one-bridge unknot is already identically one. Let an actual all-level annihilator have order d and pole budget B as in the pointed Gram theorem. Define J_N=1+floor((N-1)/k), j0=J_N-d+1. For large N, j0 is beyond the fixed exceptional starting colors. Prescribe the actual B-jets of C_(j0),...,C_(j0+d-1), all inside the polynomial window (7), and impose the SAME all-level recurrence through color N. This produces an exact tail pointed system with polynomial source supported in its initial d blocks. The original valuation proof still makes its constant values unique: the sum of leading-coefficient zero orders over this TAIL is no larger than the original uniform budget B. Subtraction of any two solutions with zero prescribed initial jets therefore leaves every constant coefficient zero. Nothing in that induction requires a starting color fixed independently of N; the bounded source was the missing quantitative input, now supplied by (7). After the same jet scaling the tail bulk symbol and all normal resonance data are unchanged. Its starting coordinate tends to 1/k, rather than zero. This is an actual source-preserving improvement, not a definition using an unknown target value. A tail Green/transfer estimate still needs its singular-step and spectral control. In particular a general sharp Vol conclusion does not follow merely from this restart, nor from the figure-eight calculation (3)--(4). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_figure_eight_ordinary_normal_jets.py): actual cyclotomic Taylor jets, all-color product identities, the positive endpoint formula and leading constant, and midpoint/tail growth diagnostics. Finite checks supplement the all-level proofs.

title: The actual regular figure-eight connection and regulator-fixed channels
text: # The actual regular figure-eight connection and regulator-fixed channels 28 October 2026. This tests the majorization criterion on the ACTUAL regular affine figure-eight quantum-A packet, rather than on the already excluded positive pivotal trace of the original crossing. The natural instantaneous modal connection is not a scalar multiple of a unitary. Its polar unitary is bistochastic but does not fix the geometric regulator observable. The same failure occurs inside the macroscopic source tail at Y=-i, not only at Y=i. This is a local statement in a specified classical eigenframe. A superadiabatic change of frame can remove the first-order off-diagonal terms; no impossibility of a different global source-retaining connection is asserted. ## 1. A pure amplitude map cannot be silently made bistochastic Let C be an invertible square matrix. Suppose a completely positive trace-preserving map Phi has, for every pure input psi, a pure output on the line C psi. Then C^*C is a scalar matrix, and Phi is the corresponding unitary channel. This includes a claimed equality with C psi psi^* C^* up to one common scalar, as well as the normalized pure-output prescription. Proof. Write Phi(X)=sum_a K_a X K_a^*. Positivity and the rank-one output imply K_a psi is on the line C psi for every psi and a. Thus C^(-1)K_a preserves EVERY vector line. Applying it to basis vectors and their pairwise sums gives C^(-1)K_a=c_a I. Trace preservation yields (sum|c_a|^2)C^*C=I. Since C is square, its scalar normalization is unitary; unitality follows as well. Agreement on ONE selected pure state is much weaker and does not imply this conclusion. Introducing a dephasing, a Kraus completion, or a state-dependent postselection normalization changes the original coherent map unless the extra source contributions are retained. ## 2. Exact original connection and its normalized eigenframe Use the exact coefficients and original source of [the actual regulator-weighted transfer](actual_regulator_weighted_a_transfer.md): w_(j+1)=T_Q(Y)w_j+f_Q(Y), Q=exp(i tau), tau=2pi/N, T_Q=[-c0/c+, -c-/c+; 1,0], f_Q=(D/c+,0)^t. No affine source is set to zero in this note. In a classical modal frame S(Y) its exact update is z_(j+1)=K_N(Y)z_j+g_N(Y), K_N=S(QY)^(-1)T_Q(Y)S(Y), g_N=S(QY)^(-1)f_Q(Y). (1) On a hyperbolic interval put P=Y^2+Y^-2-Y-Y^-1-2, lambda+lambda^-1=P, V=[lambda,lambda^-1;1,1], Lambda=diag(lambda,lambda^-1). Choose the real negative expanding root lambda<-1 and normalize EACH eigenvector column in the Euclidean norm: S=V diag(n1,n2), n1=(lambda^2+1)^(-1/2), n2=-lambda n1. This is a fixed, tame modal energy convention. Its columns need not be mutually orthogonal in the original companion coordinates. Factor the known one-step diagonal propagation on the LEFT and call C_N=Lambda^(-1)K_N its instantaneous connection. This is a factorization of (1); the source g_N stays in (1) and, if the output is divided by Lambda, must be divided by Lambda there as well. Put s=sqrt(3). At Y=i, P=-4 and lambda=-2-s. The exact quantum subprincipal term AND moving-frame derivative give C_N=I+tau E+O(tau^2), E=[ -5/12 (s-1)/6; -(s+1)/6 -5/12 ]. (2) Here is a direct derivation from the previously checked connection. In the unnormalized frame V, K_N=Lambda+hB+O(h^2), h=i tau, with B12=i(s-1)/6 and B21=-i(s+1)/6. The full first-order matrix Lambda^(-1)iB is [ (s-1)/6 (3s-5)/6; -(3s+5)/6 -(s+1)/6 ]. Column normalization conjugates it by diag(1,2+s), and subtracts diag(d_theta log n1,d_theta log n2). At Y=i, d_theta log n1=1/4+s/6, d_theta log n2=1/4-s/6, since d_theta P=2. This proves every entry of (2). Omitting the moving normalization would give different diagonal terms. ## 3. The polar test fails for the diagonal regulator observable Equation (2) gives C_N^*C_N=I+tau[ -5/6 -1/3; -1/3 -5/6 ]+O(tau^2). (3) The off-diagonal term is nonzero, so no common scalar normalization makes this pure amplitude map unitary for all sufficiently large N. The lemma in Section 1 excludes a bistochastic channel agreeing on all pure inputs with this specified connection. Its polar decomposition C_N=U_N H_N does have a unitary part: U_N=I+tau(s/6)[0,1;-1,0]+O(tau^2), H_N=I+tau[-5/12,-1/6;-1/6,-5/12]+O(tau^2). (4) For a nonconstant diagonal calibrated regulator R=diag(r1,r2), (U_N^* R U_N-R)_12 =tau(s/6)(r1-r2)+O(tau^2). (5) Thus the natural polar unitary is bistochastic but NOT regulator-fixed. Dropping H_N is not the actual amplitude evolution. Its off-diagonal positive part also fails to commute with R. Both errors are polynomial, whereas the exponential action gauge requires the stronger control in the majorization theorem. This rotation cannot be removed by a positive diagonal rescaling of the same classical eigenlines. Such a rescaling with ratio t>0 changes the off-diagonal generator entries to a t and -b/t, where a=(s-1)/6,b=(s+1)/6. The polar skew entry has modulus (a t+b/t)/2>=sqrt(ab)=1/(3sqrt(2))>0. Diagonal phase marks change its phase but cannot make it vanish. This statement is about the specified instantaneous eigenlines, not arbitrary nondiagonal frame corrections. Conjugation gives the actual SOURCE-TAIL point Y=-i, x=3/4: C_N(-i)=I-tau E+O(tau^2), (U_N(-i)^* R U_N(-i)-R)_12 =-tau(s/6)(r1-r2)+O(tau^2). (6) The geometric/conjugate figure-eight regulators are different there. From the midpoint zero anchor they agree at x=2/3, while on 2/3<x<1 one eigenvalue has |lambda|>1 and its reciprocal has modulus less than one. Their regulator derivatives have opposite nonzero signs, so the gap at x=3/4 is nonzero. Hence (6) is a test on the relevant restarted half orbit as well. The affine source is present in BOTH modes. At either Y=i or -i, f_0=(2,0)^t and S^(-1)f_0=(-sqrt(lambda^2+1)/s, sqrt(lambda^2+1)/((-lambda)s))^t. (7) Both entries are nonzero. Neither the polar part nor a regulator projection may be substituted into (1) without its transformed source and the corresponding energy cross term. ## 4. An actual conserved flux, and its limitation The exact rational functions -c0/c+, -c-/c+ and D/c+ are REAL when |Q|=|Y|=1: conjugation Q->Q^-1,Y->Y^-1 fixes each one. This follows by direct factor cancellation, not just at the classical limit. On a regular arc where det T_Q>0 put J=[0,i;-i,0]. For every real 2 by 2 matrix T, T^* J T=(det T)J. (8) Thus T_Q/sqrt(det T_Q) preserves this Hermitian indefinite Wronskian form EXACTLY. Similarly C_N is real with positive determinant, so its polar U_N is a real rotation and fixes J exactly. This gives an actual fixed Hermitian observable, but it is not the diagonal geometric regulator: its eigenvectors are the circular superpositions of the two real modal lines. The form has eigenvalues +1,-1 and provides no positive norm bound. Moreover the actual ordinary figure-eight values and source are real on the root orbit, so their J flux is identically zero; the affine cross current vanishes on such real vectors too. Large real solutions can have zero flux. This conserved observable cannot replace the required positive regulator energy. It also does not establish an identity on the tiny COMPLEX-q source circle. ## 5. The source-specific route remains possible The explicit failure above does not exclude an exact global flag after a nontrivial source-retaining change of coordinates. Already locally an O(h) nondiagonal correction can kill the O(h) mixing: if K=Lambda+hB, choose X_ik=-B_ik/(lambda_i-lambda_k), i!=k, and use V_new=V(I+hX). The transformed off-diagonal starts at O(h^2); the affine source transforms by the same inverse frame. The previously proved analytic iteration improves this locally to an exponentially small remainder, with an explicit action barrier. The actual [pointed Newton--Green factorization](pointed_newton_green_barrier.md) also supplies a stronger global source estimate for this prototype, without proving this local bistochastic description. These tests neither rule out nor construct a different source-selected global flag. What does not follow from the Ward identities or the eigenvalue curve alone is the proposed bistochastic, regulator-fixed description in the instantaneous classical frame: (2)--(7) are exact obstructions to that literal claim. A global coherent/normal source reduction, its nodal connection matrices, and their exponential costs still need a separate proof for a broad class. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_regulator_channel_test.py) verifies the exact constants, rational reality, both actual orbit points, polar and regulator defects, retained source components, and the Wronskian alternative.

title: A complete positive Fourier--Hermite filling Gram and an actual source discriminant
text: # A complete positive Fourier--Hermite filling Gram and an actual source discriminant 29 October 2026. The full crossing-circle kernel gives an explicit positive, full-rank coherent Gram, independent of the unknown period. Its filling-source dual norm is exactly 1+ell^2(N^2-1)/(12N^2). It retains every confluent Casimir jet. The same construction has a precise limitation: its energy is polynomially equivalent to the whole mixed-color packet energy, so it does not automatically see the smaller filled volume. ## 1. Complete data and the positive metric Use the original kernel and conventions of [the Fourier--Hermite theorem](actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md). For an integer crossing power ell let h_k=nu_k^ell, d_k=-ell(d-2k)h_k/2, w_k=q^(2k+1), d=N-1. Put \[ H_n=N^{-1}\sum_kh_kw_k^{-n},\qquad D_n=N^{-1}\sum_kd_kw_k^{-n}. \] Their exact marked aliases are H_(N-n)=-H_n, D_(N-n)=D_n, D0=0. For n<N/2 write m=N-n and r=n/N. Define N orthonormal compatible-data coordinates \[ y_0=H_0,\qquad (y_{n,H},y_{n,D})=(\sqrt2H_n,\sqrt2D_n/N), \] with the additional y_mid=D_(N/2)/N when N is even. At that index H_(N/2)=0. Odd N has no middle coordinate; its simple Casimir node has only a value, with logarithmic derivative zero automatically. Let a be the first-kind Chebyshev coefficient vector. The exact alias inverse a=K y is \[ a_0=y_0,\qquad \begin{pmatrix}a_n\\a_m\end{pmatrix} =\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1-r&1\\-r&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}y_{n,H}\\y_{n,D}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a_{N/2}=y_{\mathrm{mid}}. \tag{1} \] Define the real difference matrix S by \(\beta_j=(-1)^j(a_j-a_{j+2})\), with a_N=a_(N+1)=0, and set B=S K. The original all-input filling identity is \[ R^{\ell}=\kappa^{\ell}\sum_{j=0}^d\beta_jL_{j+1}, \qquad\beta=B y. \tag{2} \] Every L_(j+1) is the literal ordinary auxiliary-circle operator, with its full Cartan and pivot and no added color average, by [the original circle-source proof](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). For a complete mixed-color exterior packet A=(A0,...,Ad)^T put z=B^T A and \[ \boxed{\quad E_N(A)=\|z\|^2=A^\dagger G_N A, \qquad G_N=\overline B B^{\mathsf T}>0.\quad} \tag{3} \] B is real in these coordinates, but the conjugation in (3) makes the complex Riesz convention explicit. There is a particularly simple direct formula. Set eta_n=(-1)^n(A_n-A_(n-2)), A_negative=0. Then z0=eta0, and for n<m, \[ z_{n,H}=((1-r)\eta_n-r\eta_m)/\sqrt2,\qquad z_{n,D}=(\eta_n+\eta_m)/\sqrt2, \] with z_mid=eta_mid when present. Thus the energy keeps explicit cross-color interference, not just separate squared color values. Marked Fourier Parseval gives the EXACT source cost \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \|y_\ell\|^2=\frac1N\sum_k(|h_k|^2+|d_k/N|^2) =1+\frac{\ell^2(N^2-1)}{12N^2}=:c_{N,\ell}.} \tag{4} \] Here sum_k(d-2k)^2=N(N^2-1)/3. Since B is invertible, this is also the exact dual norm beta^T G_N^(-1) conjugate(beta), not just an upper bound. For the original scalar, with its actual external line chi retained, \[ |\chi\kappa^{\ell}\beta^{\mathsf T}A|^2 \leq|\chi|^2c_{N,\ell}E_N(A). \tag{5} \] The pairing is y^T z; its Hilbert Riesz vector is conjugate(y). No unknown closed invariant defines the metric. Equations (3)--(5) also apply to Hilbert-valued packets. For arbitrary operator-valued exteriors A_j, preserving their original order, they give the all-input positive inequality \[ (\sum_j\beta_jA_j)^\dagger(\sum_j\beta_jA_j) \preceq c_{N,\ell}\sum_r Z_r^\dagger Z_r. \tag{6} \] All original Casimir jets are retained. This is a genuine positive filling port, not an inverse of the possibly nilpotent complete-color circle alone. ## 2. Polynomial conditioning and simultaneous fillings Each two-by-two block in (1) has norm at most sqrt(3/2) and inverse norm at most sqrt6. Also ||S||<=2 and ||S^(-1)||<=N, by finite summation along each parity chain. Therefore \[ \boxed{\displaystyle (6N^2)^{-1}\|A\|^2\leq E_N(A)\leq6\|A\|^2, \qquad\operatorname{cond}(G_N)\leq36N^2.} \tag{7} \] For s specified twist boxes use the tensor product transform B^T on the s color registers, AFTER retaining their entire original mixed-color exterior. The dual cost is exactly product_i c_(N,ell_i), and the Gram is positive full rank with polynomial conditioning for fixed s. Physical boxes may overlap in time; the original operator order in each packet entry is not changed. This does not assume independent physical contractions. For full twists ell_i=2p_i, the cost is at most product_i(1+p_i^2/3), independent of N. It is subexponential whenever sum_i log(1+|p_i|)=o(N). All source, framing, and peripheral factors remain the exact ones outside the filling identity (2). ## 3. A complete actual source discriminant Use the original four-plat multiplicities, cup p, cap ell and full crossings R1,R2 from the source theorems. Define ONE fixed base packet \[ A_j=\ell R_2^2L_{j+1}(\Omega_{12})R_1R_2p,\quad0\leq j<N. \] The raw filled period with slope p is F_p=ell R2^2 R1^(2p+1) R2 p=kappa^(2p) beta_(2p)^T A. The original normalization/cup slide and whole figure-eight source give the EXACT values \[ F_0=A_0=x^d=\kappa^2,\qquad F_{-1}=Z_N:=\sum_{a=0}^d|(Q;Q)_a|^2. \tag{8} \] No augmented geometric saddle is assumed. The second value is the literal original [figure-eight whole-source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md); the first is the actual [all-input normalization tangle](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md). Apply (5) with ell=-2. Since c_(N,-2)<=4/3, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle E_N(A)\geq\frac34 Z_N^2.} \tag{9} \] At p=0 the exact dual cost is 1 and the filled raw scalar has modulus one, yet the SAME coherent positive energy has positive exponential rate. This is a fully contracted original packet, not an expanded absolute-value path or a guessed augmented invariant. It also quantifies the requirement on a different color metric H. The bound ||B||^2<=6 and (4) give ||beta_(-2)||^2<=8. Hence ||A||^2>=Z_N^2/8. The p=0 source is beta0=e0, so its Cauchy budget under ANY positive H satisfies \[ (A^\dagger H A)(e_0^\dagger H^{-1}e_0) \geq Z_N^2/[8\operatorname{cond}(H)]. \tag{10} \] A zero-exponent sharp budget for this normalization therefore requires exponential metric anisotropy, or actual coherent pruning before the energy is formed. Polynomial-conditioned changes of the complete Fourier--Hermite norm cannot supply it. Exponential anisotropy is allowed; (10) is a necessary quantitative condition, not a no-go theorem for all coherent metrics. ## 4. The same defect persists in a hyperbolic final knot There is a source-exact all-width insertion, not merely a scalar coincidence. Let M_j be the physical one-input/one-output tangle whose complete source entry is A_j. Each crossing, original turn, and auxiliary pivotal loop is a Hopf map. Thus M_j commutes with K and F on the original complete V_N. Its K eigenvalues are distinct, so it is diagonal; every interior F coefficient is nonzero, so all diagonal entries agree. Consequently M_j=A_j I at EVERY N. The p=0 tangle is topologically the straight unframed strand. Here is the local move proof, separately from its scalar evaluation: slide the free strand past the neighboring cup (the oriented cup-slide Reidemeister-II isotopy), leaving the two crossings directly above that cup. Each is a removable Reidemeister-I kink on the same arc. The remaining cup/cap cancels by the snake isotopy. No closed component remains. In the actual framed tensor calculation the two kinks have the retained unit factor kappa^2, as (8) verifies on every input; the prescribed zero-framing line is kept when this tangle is inserted into a diagram. Insert it into a strand of any original knot J. The raw mixed-color packet is multiplied by its original cut scalar, and after retaining the original external line its energy is |K_N(J)|^2 E_N(A), up to the displayed unit framing phase. All such phases remain in the exact scalar identity and do not change this norm. The unframed p=0 filled knot is still J. By (9), \[ E_N^{\mathrm{inserted}}(J)\geq\frac34|K_N(J)|^2 Z_N^2. \tag{11} \] For the independently proved benchmark J=4_1, K_N(J)=Z_N, so this Gram has energy at least 3Z_N^4/4 while the final knot has squared scalar Z_N^2. Its energy exponent is at least DOUBLE the correct figure-eight squared-volume exponent. This counterexample uses a redundant normalization augmentation and the p=0 filling. It does NOT exclude a properly reduced fully augmented diagram or a long-filling subclass. It proves that exact filling, complete jets, and a polynomial dual source cost do not by themselves imply the filled-volume energy bound. Normalization pruning or a source/slope-dependent geometric norm remains substantive. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_filling_fourier_hermite_gram.py) checks the full marked aliases and positive Gram, exact source dual costs, all-input operator inequality, original mixed-color scalar tangles, and the two actual source fillings (8). No geometric energy bound is inferred from interpolation or from coefficient mass. The finite audit checks seven complete positive Grams with49 signed dual-source costs; five literal all-input mixed-circle packets N=2,...,6; six complete original two-filling energy discriminants.

title: A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints
text: # A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints 29 October 2026. The full finite filling kernel, including its linear normal weight, has exponentially small endpoint-frequency strips when paired with an analytic source having a strict complete-color maximum. This is an estimate on a truncated original color corridor. It does not bound colors outside that corridor or prove survival of the remaining filled saddle. No Fresnel endpoint remainder is replaced by a polynomial error. ## 1. An exact finite Fourier lemma with its source hypotheses Let H=floor(delta N), d_N=(H+1/2)/N. Suppose a physical packet c_h, -H<=h<=H, has a holomorphic interpolation f_N(z), for |Re z|<=2delta and |Im z|<=sigma_0, satisfying \[ \|f_N(x+iy)\|\le C N^B \exp\{N(F-a x^2+C_0 y^2)\},\qquad a>0, \tag{1} \] \[ \|c_h-f_N(h/N)\|\le C N^B e^{N(F-\gamma)},\qquad\gamma>0. \tag{2} \] These are hypotheses on the specified source, not on arbitrary holomorphic test functions. Scalar or finite-dimensional vector/operator packets with the displayed norm bounds are allowed. All constants are independent of N. For any fixed phi_0>0 and fixed nonnegative integer r, there are g>0 and C',B' such that \[ \boxed{\left\|\sum_{h=-H}^Hh^r c_h e^{i\phi h}\right\| \le C'N^{B'}e^{N(F-g)},\quad \operatorname{dist}(\phi,2\pi\mathbb Z)\ge\phi_0.} \tag{3} \] The distance is at most pi; the assertion is empty if phi_0>pi. In particular no number-theoretic restriction on N is involved. Here is an exact contour proof retaining the finite endpoints. Reduce phi modulo2pi into [phi_0,2pi-phi_0], which changes no physical value. For a fixed small sigma>0 use the rectangle in the UNWRAPPED variable z whose vertical sides have Re z=+/-(H+1/2) and whose horizontal sides have Im z=+/-sigma N. Then \[ \sum_{h=-H}^H h^r f_N(h/N)e^{i\phi h} =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint z^r f_N(z/N)e^{i\phi z} (\pi\cot\pi z-i\pi)\,dz. \tag{4} \] Every enclosed integer has residue one. The subtracted entire term -i pi changes no residue and is essential for simultaneous upper and lower decay. Indeed pi cot(pi z)-i pi=2pi i/(exp(2pi i z)-1). On the upper horizontal side its product with exp(i phi z) is at most 4pi exp(-phi sigma N); on the lower side it is at most 4pi exp(-(2pi-phi)sigma N), for all sufficiently large N. On either vertical half-integer line the sharper exact bound is |exp(i phi z)(pi cot(pi z)-i pi)| <=2pi exp[-phi_0 |Im z|]<=2pi. Choose sigma<=sigma_0 so that C_0 sigma^2<=min(a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2). For large N, d_N>=delta/2. The horizontal exponent in (4) is at most F-phi_0 sigma/2, and the vertical exponent is at most F-a delta^2/8. Its contour length and z^r cost only powers of N. Equation (2) contributes at most C N^(B+r+1)exp[N(F-gamma)] on the physical grid. Thus one may take g=min(gamma,a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2)>0. (5) This proof neither discards a vertical current nor assumes that a universal residue rewrite lowers the maximum of arbitrary source values. Its input is precisely the state-specific analytic bound (1). ## 2. Apply the lemma BEFORE any Gaussian approximation to the filling Use the original q,Q,kappa and the exact full-jet kernel from [the coherent filling theorem](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md). For t_k=(k+1/2)/N and y_k=2pi i(t_k-1/2), write \[ K_P(h)=\frac{2(-1)^{N-1}}{N^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_k e^{hy_k} \left[(h+2Py_k/\hbar)\sinh y_k+\cosh y_k\right]. \tag{6} \] Here |h_k|=1 for every integer P and real physical data. The original normal derivative has not been dropped: 2Py_k/hbar is its unwrapped linear weight, and the h term comes from the same exact circle difference. Every factor outside exp(hy_k) is at most polynomial in N for fixed P, uniformly over k. Here beta and K_P are the coefficients of the NORMALIZED power f_P=r_N^(2P), exactly as in the filling theorem. The actual box R^(-1)R^(2P) multiplies every color pairing below by the known unit phase kappa^(2P). In particular the actual prefactor corresponding to kappa^(-P) in (10)--(11) is kappa^P. This original phase is kept; it does not change any norm estimate. Let K_P^end retain any subset of the original k values with |t_k-1/2|>=eta_0>0. For a physical EVEN core c_h=c_(-h), the original half-color convention gives the exact truncated pairing sum_(h=0)^H beta_(N-h-1)c_h =(1/2)sum_(h=-H)^H K_P(h)c_h. (7) In (6), phi_k=2pi(t_k-1/2) belongs to [-pi,pi], and dist(phi_k,2pi Z)>=2pi eta_0 on the retained endpoint strips. Apply (3) for r=0,1 and sum the N original k values. It follows that \[ \boxed{\left\|\frac12\sum_{h=-H}^H K_P^{\mathrm{end}}(h)c_h\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g)}.} \tag{8} \] This is a bound on the EXACT finite endpoint part, with both parities, all gcd cases and the normal source retained. There is no infinite charge tail to estimate, and no O(1/N) Fresnel error against an exponential target. The bounded current of section8 in the coherent filling note is consistent with (8), but (8) does not assume that every endpoint remainder equals that one Ward forcing. ## 3. The actual mixed-source input and its precise remaining scope The EXACT finite packet in [the analytic original-source theorem](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md) provides (1)--(2) for a mixed pretzel period at fixed odd s>=5, on a sufficiently small complete-color corridor. Here the other physical cusp colors may be fixed in a sufficiently small corridor. To specify the interpolation, retain a fixed regular high Newton-index window in each box, use its canonical paired factorial continuation Fhat(v-h)Fhat(v+h) and q^(h^2), and apply the UNCHANGED Hermite functional Phi_2. The lower index windows and the full nonempty alias sets are their proved exponentially smaller physical source errors. Its separate exact-interpolation bridge must be retained; a pointwise relative O(1/N) approximation on the color lattice alone does NOT imply (2) with an exponentially small Fourier error. This construction is even in the continued color, rather than an arbitrary exp(pi i h) extension. The resulting nonzero analytic leading phase, composed with chi=pi z, is even in the color variable z=h/N. Its real second derivative at zero is strictly negative, uniformly for the other sufficiently small physical colors. Taylor's formula and the elementary inequality 2|xy|<=epsilon x^2+y^2/epsilon give Re Phi(x+iy)<=Re Phi(0)-a x^2+C_0 y^2. The analytic amplitude is uniformly bounded by a polynomial in N. The exact high-window finite-source interpolation error and the alias bound supply (2), after shrinking the corridor so that its height stays within gamma/2 of the complete height. Thus (8) removes a genuine class of endpoints of this original mixed-source corridor. Aliases need not be even and are estimated before folding. Directly from the original finite H,D data, |a_n|<=1+|P| for 0<=n<N and |beta_j|<=2(1+|P|). Their entire corridor pairing therefore costs only another factor 2N(1+|P|) times the proved alias error. The exact normal forcing and the vertical color sides in (4) are both retained. This does not estimate physical colors h>H. It does not discard the central k strip, establish a nonzero filled critical pairing, or identify its action with a preferred topological longitude. A fixed-large-filling proof still requires those three steps, including the peripheral sign convention. The present source-conditioned estimate is not an all-input operator norm bound for a free exterior. ## 4. The combined source is a total derivative, with exact paired charges There is a useful exact representation for the remaining coherent packet, avoiding the separate interpolation of any a_n. For ANY physical even core in (7), set \[ \mathcal F_N(z)=\sum_{h=-H}^Hc_h e^{2\pi i h z},\qquad U_N(z)=e^{2\pi iPNz^2}\sinh(2\pi i z)\mathcal F_N(z), \qquad z_k=(k+1/2)/N-1/2. \tag{9} \] The literal entire-normal filling kernel (6) gives EXACTLY \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =\frac{(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P}}{2\pi iN^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}U_N'(z_k).} \tag{10} \] Indeed differentiating U multiplies its sinh term by 2pi i(2PNz+h) and differentiating sinh supplies 2pi i cosh. These are precisely BOTH linear normal contributions in (6). This holds with operator-valued c_h in their unchanged exterior order. In particular U_N(1/2)=U_N(-1/2)=0, and U_N'(1/2)=U_N'(-1/2) =-2pi i exp(pi iPN/2)sum_h(-1)^h c_h. The periodic extension of U_N' is continuous, with piecewise smooth derivative. Its Fourier series is absolutely convergent (two integrations by parts bound its nonzero coefficients by a constant times frequency^(-2)). Exact midpoint Fourier selection and one integration by parts therefore prove \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P} \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}} (-1)^{m(N-1)}m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2} e^{2\pi iN(Pz^2-mz)}\sinh(2\pi i z) \mathcal F_N(z)\,dz.} \tag{11} \] The series is absolutely convergent for each N. Its constants can depend on the actual source; no uniform asymptotic tail estimate is silently inferred. The zero charge vanishes EXACTLY from the two original endpoint zeros of U_N, not by discarding a Fresnel current. Because the core is even, mathcalF_N is even and U_N is odd. The integrals at -m and m are opposites, so their weighted contributions in (11) are equal. Thus the +/-m channels ADD exactly, at every parity and level, before any saddle approximation. For the source obeying (1)--(2), mathcalF_N and its fixed derivatives are exponentially small on any fixed real strip eta_0<=|z|<=1/2, by (3). Equations (10)--(11) therefore provide a source-faithful central phase problem with exact normal charge m. The finite-k endpoint bound (8) is already quantitative. Passing between a restricted central integral and (11) must still retain the new side currents at its artificial cutoff; absolute convergence at fixed N alone is not a uniform exponential bound on all charges. The uniform infinite-tail bound is proved separately below; a central-saddle conclusion is not inferred from fixed-N convergence. ## 5. A uniform exponential high-charge tail, with its paired current Under (1)--(2), the large-|m| part of (11) is exponentially smaller than exp(NF). This is a UNIFORM estimate; absolute convergence at each fixed N alone would not suffice. For fixed integer P there are M_P>0 and finite B_P,C_P, independent of N, such that \[ \boxed{\sum_{|m|>M_P} \left\|m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}U_N(z)e^{-2\pi imNz}\,dz\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g_*)}.} \tag{12} \] The positive gap g_* and the contour width below depend ONLY on the source hypotheses, not on P. This matters for independently large fillings with no comparability between their lengths. First, (3), for a small real neighborhood of +/-1/2 in z, extends to a FIXED small complex strip. In its exact rectangle proof, an extra Im z=v in the Fourier variable costs at most exp(2pi delta |v|N) on the physical source support. The same argument applies to fixed derivatives of mathcalF_N, by taking r larger in (3). Thus for some fixed sigma_1,g_1>0, ||mathcalF_N^(j)(+/-1/2+iv)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F-g_1)], |v|<=sigma_1, j=0,1,2. Fix a smaller sigma>0 using ONLY this source strip. On either endpoint line, at height -v, the chirp costs at most exp(2pi|P|Nv), and its first two derivatives cost powers of N and P. Keep that v-dependent cost; do not bound it by exp(2pi|P|sigma N) and then shrink sigma as the filling length grows. For m>0 shift its Fourier integral DOWN by sigma. On the lower horizontal side the elementary physical-grid estimate ||mathcalF_N(x-i sigma)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F+2pi delta sigma)] gives an upper bound poly(N)exp{N[F-2pi sigma(m-|P|-delta)]}. (13) Crucially the two vertical currents must be paired. Their common Fourier endpoint phase is (-1)^(mN), and their difference is V_N(v)=U_N(1/2-iv)-U_N(-1/2-iv), 0<=v<=sigma. The original integer Fourier polynomial mathcalF_N is periodic. Together with the sinh zeros this gives V_N(0)=V_N'(0)=0 exactly, as already checked before (11). The source derivative bound on the two vertical strips, with the chirp cost explicitly retained, gives ||V_N(v)||<=poly(N,P)v^2 exp[N(F-g_1)+2pi|P|Nv]. Consequently the paired vertical contribution obeys \[ \left\|m\int_0^\sigma e^{-2\pi mNv}V_N(v)\,dv\right\| \le\frac{\operatorname{poly}(N,P)m}{(m-|P|)^3N^3} e^{N(F-g_1)},\quad m>|P|. \tag{14} \] For m>M_P>=2|P|+2delta+2 this is at most a fixed multiple of poly(N,P)m^(-2)N^(-3)exp[N(F-g_1)], which is summable. The horizontal bounds (13) have an exponentially convergent geometric sum with gap at least 2pi sigma, independent of P. Take g_*=min(g_1,2pi sigma)>0. The upper shift for negative m is identical; for an even core it also follows from the exact +/-m identity. This proves (12). Neither individual vertical current is set to zero. Here is the precise multiport justification. Leave all remaining z_j variables REAL until their tails have been removed. On the entire source U=exp(2pi iN sum P_i z_i^2) product_i sinh(2pi i z_i) mathcalF_N(z), define the commuting COLOR-register functionals D_i U=(2pi iN^2)^(-1)sum_k partial_i U(z_(i,k)), I_(i,m)U=(-1)^(m(N-1))m integral_[-1/2,1/2] U dz_i, D_i^lo=sum_(0<|m|<=M_i) I_(i,m), D_i^tail=D_i-D_i^lo. Midpoint Poisson and the matched endpoint values prove D_i=sum_m I_(i,m) exactly. These operations act linearly on scalar color registers; they do NOT commute or reorder physical Hopf boxes or matrix-valued exterior coefficients. Exact telescoping gives \[ \prod_iD_i-\prod_iD_i^{\mathrm{lo}} =\sum_i\left(\prod_{j<i}D_j^{\mathrm{lo}}\right) D_i^{\mathrm{tail}}\left(\prod_{j>i}D_j\right). \tag{14a} \] For fixed M_j, the real-integral functional D_j^lo has supremum norm at most sum_(0<|m|<=M_j)|m|=M_j(M_j+1). The original D_j uses N samples and one derivative. Its mixed derivatives on U cost powers of N and P_j: all remaining chirps have modulus ONE at real z_j, while differentiating them supplies only P_j N. Differentiating mathcalF_N supplies integer powers of h_j, bounded by powers of N. The endpoint Fourier bound and (14) are uniform in these remaining real spectators AND in every mixed derivative just described. To see this directly, sum the other physical h_j in absolute value using the original source bound exp[N(F_0-a sum x_j^2+C sum y_j^2)]. Their sums and fixed powers of h_j cost only powers of N; no positive exponential is introduced. The contour shift and paired vertical current occur ONLY in the tail coordinate i. Thus each term of (14a) is bounded by poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-g_*)], with g_* fixed by the source and independent of the largest slope. There is no uncontrolled infinite charge sum in a spectator coordinate. Later central saddle-contour motions are made only AFTER (14a) has removed the tails. Equations (8),(11),(12) leave a FINITE set of nonzero coherent central charges for every fixed collection of integer fillings. Their source Fourier saddle is made explicit next. Comparing the remaining charge actions and bounding colors outside the chosen corridor are separate tasks. ## 6. A nonzero central Fourier packet from the EXACT analytic source This step uses the stronger, proved input from the exact color packet: on a fixed complex polydisk, with r color ports, C_N(pi x)=N^(3/2)e^(-i s pi d/4) A(pi x) exp[N phi(x)](1+O(1/N)), phi(x)=Phi_s(pi x), phi(0)=F_0, phi''(0)=2pi i tau_s I, tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, Im tau_s>0. (15) The exact function C_N, not just this leading expression, has the complex Gaussian bound (1) in all continued coordinates. The case needed for filling all boxes is r=s. Define the ENTIRE finite packet mathcalF_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(pi h/N) exp(2pi i h dot z). (16) It is exactly even in every z_i. For a fixed sufficiently small complex z-polydisk, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem defines grad phi(xi(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi(z))+2pi i xi(z) dot z. Then, UNIFORMLY on a smaller fixed complex polydisk, \[ \boxed{\mathcal F_N(z)=N^{(r+3)/2}e^{-i s\pi d/4} B(z)e^{N\Psi(z)}(1+O(1/N)),\quad B(z)=\frac{(2\pi)^{r/2}A(\pi\xi(z))} {\sqrt{\det[-\phi''(\xi(z))]}}.} \tag{17} \] The Gaussian square root is fixed at zero by the positive real part of -phi''(0). In particular B(0)=A(0)(-i tau_s)^(-r/2) !=0, xi(z)=-z/tau_s+O(||z||^3), Psi(z)=F_0-i pi sum_i z_i^2/tau_s+O(||z||^4). (18) Both Psi and B are even in each z_i and B is nonzero on a smaller polydisk. All phases in (15) remain in (17). Here is the finite-source proof of (17). Apply exact half-integer cotangent rectangles in the h coordinates to (16). The two constant cotangent parts give the ordinary integral with density N^r. The nonconstant parts cost exp(-2pi sigma N) on its horizontal sides; the extra factor exp(2pi iN x dot z), the quadratic complex-source growth and the small complex z displacement cost strictly less after choosing sigma first and then the z-polydisk. The vertical h sides keep their strict endpoint gap from (1). This proves mathcalF_N(z)=N^r integral_[-d_N,d_N]^r C_N(pi x)exp(2pi iN x dot z)dx +poly(N)exp[N(F_0-g)], g>0. (19) Slightly changing the half-integer endpoints of the integral is exponentially harmless, and all corresponding side currents are in the displayed error. This is a statement about the EXACT holomorphic source; a pointwise real-grid O(1/N) error would not imply (19). Deform the ordinary integral locally to the parallel real contour through xi(z). Its end connectors retain their strict gap for small z. The real part of phi'' remains negative definite, uniformly near zero. The elementary multivariate Gaussian integral and the uniform analytic amplitude in (15) therefore give (17); its exponentially small cotangent remainder stays below the saddle after shrinking the z-polydisk. This also proves the required uniformity BEFORE any later z-contour motion. No original-cycle coefficient has been assigned. For completeness, apply (11) successively in all r filled ports. The actual R powers restore their phases as explained above. The exact corridor source is \[ (-1)^{r(N-1)}\kappa^{\sum_iP_i} \sum_{m_i\ne0}(-1)^{(N-1)\sum_i m_i}\prod_i m_i \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^r} e^{2\pi iN\sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i)} \prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_i)\mathcal F_N(z)\,dz. \tag{20} \] All original normal charges and the full original source are kept. Every coordinate reflection (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i) preserves its term, so the 2^r all-unit charges have exactly equal contributions, including the even-level signs. There is no charge with m_i=0. The large-charge remainder is controlled by (12) before any Gaussian approximation; the real endpoint-frequency strips are controlled by (8). Equations (17),(20) therefore give an actual nonzero analytic source amplitude for the remaining finite central phase problem Psi(z)+2pi i sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i). (21) The comparison of its finite charges, its legitimate local saddle contours, and the physical color complement are not replaced by formal stationarity. In particular (20) alone is not a theorem for an entire filled knot. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.py) checks the exact finite-k normal-weighted decomposition, its retained half-color source and endpoint split, the contour equality (4), and the quantitative estimates on explicitly controlled analytic packets, and the combined-source total derivative and exact paired-charge Fourier selection in (10)--(11). The actual mixed-source hypotheses are proved in the linked source notes; finite tests alone do not establish them.

title: Quantitative loss on a fixed boundary face of the complete angle flow
text: # Quantitative loss on a fixed boundary face of the complete angle flow 31 October 2026. analytical lemma. This concerns the original complete triangle capacity and its actual shared face equations. It does not turn the weighted LEFT envelope into a coefficientwise comparison. ## 1. Strong concavity with the source normalization For every actual triangle corner use the normalized load \(a=\theta/(2\pi)\in[0,1/2]\), with each triangle row summing to \(1/2\). Protected-face corners are zero, and every ordinary face has total load one. Let \(\mathcal P\) be this compact feasible polytope, retaining all actual corner incidences. Its complete source entropy is \[ E(a)=\sum_{t,f}f(a_{tf}),\qquad f(s)=\frac{\Lambda(\pi s)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi s)}{\pi}. \] This is the normalization in the [triangle Legendre identity](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md). For \(0<s<1/2\), direct differentiation gives \[ f''(s)=-\frac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi s)}\leq-2\pi. \] Consequently \(f(s)+\pi s^2\) is concave, including both endpoints by continuity. Summing this fact proves, for \(a,b\in\mathcal P\) and \(0\leq t\leq1\), \[ E((1-t)a+tb)\geq(1-t)E(a)+tE(b) +\pi t(1-t)\lVert a-b\rVert_2^2. \tag{1} \] Let \(a^*\) maximize \(E\) on \(\mathcal P\), and set \(\Phi=E(a^*)\). In the actual geometric case, \(\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\). Since the left side of (1), with \(a=a^*\), is at most \(\Phi\), dividing by \(t>0\) and letting \(t\downarrow0\) gives \[ \boxed{\quad E(b)\leq\Phi-\pi\lVert b-a^*\rVert_2^2.\quad} \tag{2} \] No derivative at a forced zero or at a singleton row is used. In particular the maximizing assignment is unique even on a proper supported face. ## 2. Fixing selected triangles to their corner vertices Choose a set \(J\) of distinct original triangles and an allowed ordinary corner \(c(t)\) in each. Impose the additional constraints \[ a_t=v_t:=\tfrac12 e_{c(t)},\qquad t\in J. \] Write \(\mathcal P_J\) for the resulting face of \(\mathcal P\). If it is nonempty, (2) proves the explicit bound \[ \max_{\mathcal P_J}E \leq\Phi-\pi\sum_{t\in J}\lVert v_t-a_t^*\rVert_2^2. \tag{3} \] If it is empty, its entropy maximum is \(-\infty\). The loss in (3) is strict as soon as one chosen row was not already that singleton row at the complete solution. Distinct rows make the displayed squared losses additive; their shared face constraints remain in force. There is an exact shared-radius dual formulation. Write \(h_f=\log l_f\) for ordinary faces and retain protected zeros by deleting their allowed corners. With the same half-degree triangle function \(Q\), put \[ B_J(h)=\sum_{t\notin J}Q((e^{h_f})_{f\in t}) +\tfrac12\sum_{t\in J}h_{c(t)}-\sum_f h_f. \tag{4} \] Then \[ \inf_{h\in\mathbb R^{F_{\mathrm{ord}}}} B_J(h) =\max_{\mathcal P_J}E. \tag{5} \] Here the right side has value \(-\infty\) when infeasible; positive minimizing radii need not exist. To verify (5), take the product of all remaining compact triangle simplexes and the selected singleton rows, let \(A\) be its original face-incidence map, and define \(H(d)=\max_{Aa=d}E(a)\). Its hypograph is closed and convex, because the domain is compact and \(E\) is continuous and concave. Weak duality follows directly from the local Legendre formula. Strict separation of \((\mathbf1,H(\mathbf1)+\varepsilon)\) from that hypograph gives an affine majorant of height at most \(H(\mathbf1)+\varepsilon\) at \(\mathbf1\). The separating coefficient of the vertical coordinate is positive: it is nonnegative by downward closure, and if it were zero the feasible point with the same face coordinate would contradict strict separation. Normalizing that coefficient to one produces (4). Let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). When \(\mathbf1\) is outside the compact incidence image, separation in face coordinates and scaling the separator sends (4) to \(-\infty\). ## 3. What this resolves in the one-sided envelope For a LEFT port \((x,b,c,y)\), its term \[ Q(x,b,y)+\tfrac12\log c \] is exactly (4)'s local expression when the original \((x,c,y)\) triangle is fixed to its \(c\)-corner vertex. At the actual complete packing with \(c>0\) and \(x+y>0\), this triangle has at least two positive weights, so its maximizing row is not that vertex. Thus (3) gives a strict, explicit capacity loss for any fixed nonempty collection of these triangle restrictions, with the original common face constraints. The reflected statement applies to RIGHT ports. This proves a statement about the specified comparison capacities. It does not bound the full LEFT polynomial by that one comparison: the [proved weighted envelope](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) also has the branch \(\log c\). A pointwise maximum of the two branches does not permit each branch to choose its own Cauchy radii before the original coefficient is extracted. An additional finite comparison, or a bound for their convex mixtures with the same face constraints, is still necessary for a general full-invariant theorem. ## Validation The proof is analytic: scalar differentiation, strong concavity on the closed simplex, and finite convex separation. No finite-width experiment is used to infer (2), (3), or (5). No comparison with the complete one-sided envelope is supplied.

title: Exact unit-mass transport for phase-flat charged block cores
text: # Exact unit-mass transport for phase-flat charged block cores 28 October 2026. An additional constructive case of the fixed-clock mass problem covers UNBALANCED biconnected cores with any fixed number of anchors. The hypothesis is the flatness of their actual positive-binomial block connection, not balance of their individual binary-factor incidences. It is checked from the original block metadata. No finite source is changed. The conclusion is stronger than existence of a semialgebraic replacement: one constant-radius source torus has normalized logarithmic mass ONE. There is also an explicit polynomial lower bound relative to its positive capacity. This is a fixed-clock theorem. Flatness is not automatic on surviving knot sources, and this note supplies no general full-clock volume estimate. ## 1. Original blocks and a precise phase test Let Q=exp(2pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N), and take the actual residual block source P(X)=gamma product_e product_(r=0)^(L_e-1) (alpha_e X_(u_e)-Q^r beta_e X_(v_e)), f(X)=P(X)/product_i X_i^(a_i), 1<=L_e<=N-1, |alpha_e|=|beta_e|=1, sum_i a_i=sum_e L_e=M. All extracted original normalizers and clock factors remain outside or in gamma as previously specified. Loops and tight cuts are treated by their exact source rules before taking this residual connected core. Assume its strict Hall inequalities: for every nonempty proper vertex set I, 0<a(I)-m_I<C_I. (1) The block coefficient identity from [the actual phase calculation](anchor_phase_cycles_and_exact_fusion.md) is product_r(alpha X_u-Q^r beta X_v) =alpha^L sum_(j=0)^L c_(L,j) w_e^j X_u^(L-j)X_v^j, c_(L,j)=|[L choose j]_Q|>0, w_e=-(beta_e/alpha_e)q^(L_e-1). (2) Assume there are unit phases eta_i such that w_e=eta_v/eta_u on every edge. Equivalently every oriented block-cycle holonomy is one. This is a finite spanning-tree test, including every parallel edge and original closure block. For actual root phases it is exact integer arithmetic modulo 2N, rather than a numerical small-phase test. Substitution X_i=eta_i^(-1)Y_i transforms the ENTIRE polynomial to P(eta^(-1)Y)=Gamma P_+(Y), P_+(Y)=product_e sum_j c_(L_e,j)Y_u^(L_e-j)Y_v^j, Gamma=gamma product_e alpha_e^(L_e)eta_u^(-L_e). Consequently the original coefficient has the exact pointing [X^a]P=Gamma product_i eta_i^(a_i) [Y^a]P_+. (3) The factors in (3) are known source factors; they are not chosen from the unknown period. Their modulus is |gamma|. ## 2. An actual regular critical point and a unit-mass sublevel torus Set G(rho)=log P_+(exp rho)-sum_i a_i rho_i. For each block use its normalized positive weights proportional to c_(L,j) exp((L-j)rho_u+j rho_v). Differentiation gives Hess G=sum_e Var_e(j)(e_v-e_u)(e_v-e_u)^t. (4) Every variance is strictly positive. Connectivity therefore makes G strictly convex modulo the common scale. It is coercive on that quotient. To see this without a capacity theorem, order the rho_i and write their successive gaps as g_j, with high vertex sets I_j. Choosing the larger endpoint of every block gives an endpoint monomial of coefficient at least one, and hence G(rho)>=sum_j [C_(I_j)-(a(I_j)-m_(I_j))]g_j >=max rho-min rho. (5) The last inequality uses the integral strict Hall condition (1). Adding the constant log|gamma| would restore the outside scalar. Thus a unique minimizer rho_* exists modulo scale. Its positive value Cap=|gamma| exp G(rho_*) is an ACTUAL regular complex critical modulus of f at X_i=eta_i^(-1)exp(rho_*,i). Holomorphic differentiation agrees with the real logarithmic derivative there, and every block is nonzero because its transformed coefficients and arguments are positive. The existing radial cut theorem in addition bounds its radius ratios by (M-1)^(k-1). On the shifted source torus X_i=eta_i^(-1)exp(rho_*,i+i theta_i), the triangle inequality in (2) gives |f(X)|<=Cap. This torus is homologous to the original coefficient torus in (C*)^k/C*, by ordinary finite changes of radii and angles; its normalized absolute logarithmic top-form mass is exactly one. Therefore |[X^a]P|<=Cap<=Mcrit(f). (6) This bypasses the unknown complexity of interior gradient transport for this entire class, including its unbalanced biconnected members. It does not assert that Cap is the largest of all complex critical moduli. ## 3. A source-exact polynomial lower bound Let B be the number of nonempty blocks. At rho_*, choose independent integer random variables J_e with probabilities p_e(j)=c_(L_e,j)exp((L_e-j)rho_u+j rho_v)/Z_e. The mean endpoint assignment is a, by criticality. Expanding P_+ gives the EXACT identity |[X^a]P|/Cap=Prob(endpoint degrees equal a). (7) The sequences p_e are log-concave. Indeed their successive ratios, apart from a positive tilt, are sin(pi(L-j)/N)/sin(pi(j+1)/N). These decrease because the sum of the two relevant cotangents is sin(pi(L+1)/N) divided by positive sine factors. For L=N-1 the ratios are constant, so the same conclusion holds. Extend log p_e affinely between integers, obtaining a concave function phi_e. If mu_e=E J_e, Jensen and the entropy bound give phi_e(mu_e)>=sum_j p_e(j)log p_e(j)>=-log(L_e+1). (8) There is an integral endpoint flow j_e with the SAME required degrees and with sum_e phi_e(j_e)>=sum_e phi_e(mu_e). Here is an elementary rounding proof. Confine each coordinate to [floor mu_e,ceil mu_e]; every phi_e is affine on this box. The nonintegral edges of a feasible flow have no degree-one vertex, since the required incidence imbalance is integral. They therefore contain an undirected cycle. Move in both directions along that cycle until an edge becomes integral. The current flow is a convex combination of the two endpoints, so at least one endpoint does not decrease the affine objective. Repeat; an integral feasible flow is reached after at most B steps. This is the usual network-flow rounding proved here with its source degrees retained. The probability of that ONE integral flow, using (8), is at least product_e(L_e+1)^(-1). Equation (7) now proves Cap/product_e(L_e+1) <= |[X^a]P| <= Cap. (9) For a fixed original diagram B is bounded independently of N, so the lower factor is polynomial in N. This is actual selected-coefficient noncancellation in a fixed sector, not a conclusion from a nonzero ambient module or a guessed local saddle. ## 4. What must still be checked for a whole knot The phase test must hold for the ACTUAL surviving block graph, after every proposed exact fusion, with all original closure and clock factors. The existing nonzero 6_3 family has a macroscopic curved bulk cycle, so the test is not automatic for alternating diagrams or arbitrary widths. No arbitrary-width hyperbolic-knot class satisfying it in every sector has been established here. An original full clock sum may also cancel between the known phases in (3) and its retained W_h. There is a finite way to certify UNIFORM anchor flatness, if a diagram class supplies the needed identities. For the original metadata each block gain is q^(b_e N+c_e+sum_j a_ej h_j), with integer coefficients. On a stratum where the nonempty blocks and chosen source fusions are fixed, spanning-tree propagation makes each cycle exponent an affine integer function of (N,h). Uniform flatness is exactly its vanishing modulo 2N on that stratum's integer clock lattice. Check its values on one lattice point and on generators of the difference lattice. The constants and linear coefficients are explicit, so this avoids an all-level numerical extrapolation. The unit-block-preserving source fusions used here only multiply or divide unit gains and impose affine charge/length equalities; their finite anchor-decreasing order gives finitely many such strata for a fixed diagram. This is a certification procedure, not a proof that the test succeeds on any new knot class. Including the clocks as extra coefficient variables would require an exact nonnegative-coefficient, phase-flat presentation of their FULL feedback and factorial weights. The anchor Ward equations alone do not provide this: their critical points are not critical in h. Equations (6)--(9) therefore cannot be assigned the knot regulator bound without that missing joint comparison, and no nonflat sectors are discarded. For the general nonflat mass problem, semialgebraic complexity of one sublevel set still does not control the particular transported source class. Effective local trivializations over a polynomial number of base intervals cannot simply be composed while retaining polynomial degree or multiplicity. This note avoids that issue only by constructing the constant-radius torus above. A bare quotient by the critical ideal is not an alternative finite-source argument. Already for f=z+z^(-1), its critical derivative z-z^(-1) has CT[z(z-z^(-1))]=-1. Thus the original coefficient functional does not annihilate the critical ideal.
