The [subsequent one-index source theorem](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) and [its independent audit](one_index_fourier_source_independent_audit.md) use actual ROOT scalarity of the fully reclosed cut to fix ANY first input a while retaining the original sum over its outputs. Thus the selected scalar is sum_j Jtilde_(a,j), with no remaining outside 1/N and with its internal Fourier 1/N unchanged. A fixed good root-of-unity phase sequence retains a nonzero geometric normal block. Section 8 of the partial support theorem gives the corresponding nonzero operator on each finite residue class. The unresolved global pushforward can therefore be formulated as ONE exterior Fourier-label sum. Whole q-normal source defects remain explicit; root scalarity is not extended off root. The [rank-one prefix calculation](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) now simplifies the fixed-A rational inverse to an explicit Möbius map of projective lines and computes its single intrinsic density pole. The [actual cancellation theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) provides an important scope test: an actual port current with zero final source still has a nonzero block of the same geometric action on this chart. Consequently this local block and its partial A-factor do not, by themselves, prove selected survival.

title: Exact physical port polynomials and global conditional angular profiles
text: # Exact physical port polynomials and global conditional angular profiles 28 October 2026. The original four-full-Psi crossing has exact finite-band Laurent-polynomial interpolants in each port, while the other three ports stay on their specified correlated grids. These are the actual finite Fourier interpolants, with their entire source normalization fixed by a known local kernel entry. Their apparent full-Psi poles cancel after the exact fixed-grid period factors and integer aliases are retained. This proves a nonzero analytic symbol for a single actual finite Fourier adapter on a compact positive crossing chart. It also gives the unique GLOBAL angular modulus maximum on the whole conditional port circle. It does not justify moving several unrelated ports simultaneously or suppressing a whole knot's boundary sectors. ## 1. Actual kernel, grids, and the two integer chamber labels Use the EXACT original operator and source of [the balanced Fourier theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md). Write q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, h=2pi*i/N, d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), X=pi*i-h/2. The marked grids have z0=r0 Q^i, z1=r1 Q^j, z6=x r1 Q^k6, z7=x r0 Q^l, r0^N=A, r1^N=B, A B(B-x^N A)!=0. Retain a,b,c,d0 for their logarithms and define k=the representative of l-i modulo N in {1,...,N}, m=the representative of k6-j modulo N in {1-N,...,0}. Choose the corresponding matched logarithmic lifts so that d0-a-X=k h and c-b-X=m h. The whole-turn characters are one at the original balanced grids, so this does not change M or discard its compensating central factors. The positive octahedral chamber has 1<=k<=N-1, 2-N<=m<=0. (1) Indeed its positive angle sums are, up to the recorded half-step, theta1+theta3=2pi*k/N and theta2+theta3=2pi*(N+m-1)/N. These are both between zero and 2pi. The EXACT polynomial statements hold for all those cyclic representatives, including k=N and m=1-N. Only the positive-chart estimates need the strict ranges in (1). Let M be the actual normalized Fourier matrix entry, including its original kappa and every fixed central factor. It is explicitly the four-full-Psi expression (14) of the linked theorem; every grid entry is nonzero on its regular torus. ## 2. The exact original finite-band interpolants Write (v;Q)_L=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(1-Q^r v). For a single variable Z and all other ports fixed on the original grids, define the following Laurent polynomials: P0(Z)=Z^m (z1/(xZ);Q)_(N+m-1), P1(Z)=(Q^(k+1)x z0/Z;Q)_(N-k), P6(Z)=Z^(N-k)(Q^(1-k)Z/z0;Q)_(k-1), P7(Z)=(Q^m Z/(x z6);Q)_(-m). (2) P0 and P7 use m in {1-N,...,0}; P1 and P6 use k in {1,...,N}. They have the exact physical spectra | Port | Powers | Physical frequency indices | | --- | --- | --- | | input z0 | negative | -m,...,N-1 | | input z1 | negative | 0,...,N-k | | output z6 | positive | N-k,...,N-1 | | output z7 | positive | 0,...,-m | Every coefficient inside the stated interval is nonzero. Each interval is contained in the original head band 0,...,N-1. Choose any fixed grid value Z_* for the port under consideration. Then its exact original Fourier interpolation is g_port(Z)=M(Z_*) P_port(Z)/P_port(Z_*). (3) This preserves the full original scalar. M(Z_*) is a known explicit local four-full-Psi value, not an unknown knot period. P_port(Z_*) is nonzero since its root central argument is not one. No new normalization is introduced by (3). Equation (3) agrees with M at EVERY old grid point. Since its physical frequency interval lies in 0,...,N-1, finite Fourier uniqueness makes it the actual original finite-band interpolation. It therefore holds for every complex nonzero Z, with no omitted residues or approximate projection. At the two cyclic endpoint cases the table is literal: k=N gives P1=1 and P6 of degree N-1; m=1-N gives the input monomial P0=Z^(1-N) and P7 of degree N-1. There is no degree-N norm polynomial substituted for a constant grid row. ## 3. Full-function proof, including every period and alias factor In the exact kernel use beta=b-a-X, f=d0-c-X, rho=c-a, lambda=d0-b+2pi*i, G=d0-a-X, J=b-c+X. Its full-function part is Psi(beta)Psi(h-f)Psi(lambda+2pi*i+h)/Psi(rho). First use the EXACT whole-turn identity Psi(lambda+2pi*i+h) =Psi(h+d0-b)/(1-exp[N(d0-b)])^2. (4) On the old grids exp[N(d0-b)]=x^N A/B, and R=exp(Nrho)=x^N B/A. Thus the central density R(1-R)^2 in kernel (14), divided by (1-1/R)^2 from (4), is exactly R^3. For interpolation, these are the fixed old-grid constants. They are retained in the normalizer in (3). This qualification matters: substituting a moving Z into the RAW four-Psi expression changes those Nth powers. That meromorphic continuation is generally NOT the finite Fourier interpolation. For example (4) creates moving double poles at (z7/Z)^N=1; they are absent from the polynomial (3). No contour is moved across such artificial poles by the present theorem. For input z0, rho-beta=c-b+X=(N+m-1)h. Hence Psi(beta)/Psi(rho)=(exp beta;Q)_(N+m-1). The exact Gaussian in kernel (14) has a-dependent power exp(m a). This gives P0 after the fixed central factors are retained. For input z1, beta+(d0-b)=G=kh. Full inversion gives Psi(beta)Psi((k+1)h-beta) =zeta exp[pi*i*(sqrt(N)beta/(2pi)-c_b)^2] *(Q^(k+1)exp(-beta);Q)_(N-k). Combining its Gaussian with the original kernel Gaussian leaves exp(-N beta), times a factor independent of b. On the old grid exp(-N beta) is a known fixed central scalar. Retaining that scalar gives precisely P1. This is the integer alias +N b; it is compensated by its known old-grid value. For output z6, h-f=rho+(1-k)h, so Psi(h-f)/Psi(rho)=(Q^(1-k)exp rho;Q)_(k-1). The original Gaussian power is exp[-(N+k)c]. Its fixed-grid alias exp(-2N c) is retained as a central scalar, leaving exp[(N-k)c] and giving P6. For output z7 put t=h-f. Then t+(h+d0-b)=(N+m+1)h. The same full inversion gives a polynomial of length -m, with argument Q^m z7/(xz6). Its Gaussian combines with the original one to give exp(3N d0), independent of the remaining polynomial. This is again a known old-grid central scalar and gives P7. All displayed Gaussian cancellations are exact, including the affine logarithmic marks and half-step in X. Thus the integer aliases +N b,+2N c,-3N d0 are NOT discarded phases: their known central values are in (3). Nonzero coefficients in (2) follow from the finite q-binomial theorem, since all factorial indices in its lengths are less than N. There is also a genuine TWO-port result. With b,c fixed on their original grids, the physical interpolant factors exactly: M_interp(Z0,Z7)=M(z0_*,z7_*) *P0(Z0)P7(Z7)/[P0(z0_*)P7(z7_*)]. (3a) With a,d0 fixed, the analogous formula uses P1(Z1)P6(Z6). To prove this, kernel (14) on the original grids separates into an a-only factor times a d0-only factor when b,c are fixed: its Gaussian has no a*d0 term, and its full functions and central factors split. The other pair splits likewise. Every two-by-two conditional minor is zero. Tensor-product finite Fourier uniqueness then proves (3a) for BOTH free complex variables, with the complete original scalar. This is a paired polynomial identity, not the assertion that the raw four-Psi formula is the same off-grid function. ### The pair scalar is explicit and tame The reference value in (3a) can be eliminated altogether. Use the [uniform signed role table](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md) and write the paired kernel as c_sigma Pout Pin, with the physical over/under clock h in 0,...,d used there. Then c_(+,over)=kappa/N *(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z6^h, c_(+,under)=kappa/N *(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z0^(-h), c_(-,over)=kappa^(-1)/N *(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z7^h, c_(-,under)=kappa^(-1)/N *(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z1^(-h). (3b) These retain the ENTIRE original crossing scalar and phase. Their magnitudes lie between c_K/N and C_K/N on fixed nonzero central compacta, uniformly in every spectator label and h. Their explicit Gaussian and monomial phases can still carry a leading oscillatory action; tameness is not positivity. Here is an independent all-level proof directly from original coefficients. For the positive over-pair extract over-input physical frequency h and over-output frequency zero. Since the chosen Pin starts with Z^(-h) and Pout with 1, this coefficient is exactly c. The original sparse crossing gives c=kappa/N^2 z6^h F_h sum_(t=0)^(d-h) [h+t choose t]_Q Q^(-ht). Root complementation turns its summand into (-1)^t Q^(t(t+1)/2)[d-h choose t]_Q. The finite q-binomial theorem makes that sum F_(d-h). Finally F_h F_(d-h)=N(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2). This proves the first line. For the positive under-pair extract input frequency zero and output frequency h; the same original coefficient sum appears, multiplied by z0^(-h). The exact negative mirror conjugates kappa and Q and swaps ports, proving the other lines. Reversing a Q^(-1) product only reorders its factors and introduces no further scalar. All steps hold for even and composite levels as well. This improves merely specifying the scalar by a known local value: no hidden exponential magnitude is left in the pair normalization. It also fixes the normalization of every source-preserving bridge contraction in the linked theorem. ## 4. Actual adapter action and a nonzero analytic symbol For an outgoing positive-band port the exact finite adapter F(r')F(r)^(-1) acts on the sampled polynomial by g(r Q^j) -> g(r' Q^j). (5) For an incoming port the inverse/contravariant adapter has the same evaluation statement with the matching direction and the negative powers in (2). This is finite Fourier interpolation, not a formal pseudodifferential assertion. Take r'/r=exp(delta/N) with delta in a fixed compact set. On a compact positive octahedral chart every factor in the corresponding Pochhammer arc stays uniformly away from zero. The arc connects two nonreal positive-orientation endpoints without crossing 1. Its length is at most N. Thus log[g(Z exp(delta/N))/g(Z)] =delta p_port(Z)+O_K(1/N), p_port=(1/N) Z partial_Z log P_port. (6) The estimate is uniform, with derivatives: the second logarithmic derivative of each factor is bounded, so the sum of N such derivatives is O_K(N). Equation (6) follows by Taylor expansion through a displacement delta/N. Ordinary Riemann sums on the zero-free arc give p_port's explicit classical limit with another O_K(1/N) error. The resulting adapter symbol is exp(delta p_port), nonzero and bounded above and below on compact data. The sign convention in (6) is the Laurent power of the kernel: physical incoming momentum is -p_port, whereas physical outgoing momentum is +p_port. The REAL parts of its physical incoming/outgoing momenta, after the just-proved fixed aliases, are p_in,0=1-(theta2+theta3)/(4pi), p_in,1=1/2-(theta1+theta3)/(4pi), p_out,0=1-(theta1+theta3)/(4pi), p_out,1=1/2-(theta2+theta3)/(4pi). (7) Every one belongs to (0,1), uniformly away from its ends on every compact positive chamber. At the regular octahedron they are (3/4,1/4;3/4,1/4). This agrees with the original finite-head indices, not an independently selected wave packet. Equivalently, the exact global linear alias of the original action is 2pi*i(b+2c-3d0), with inverse scalar compensation by exp[-N(b+2c-3d0)]. On the original grids this scalar is known and bounded for fixed central data. Its derivative puts all four momenta in the physical band without changing any actual matrix value or original source. ## 5. Unique GLOBAL fixed-port angular maxima Assume additionally |A|!=|B|, as in the fixed regular choice A=2,B=3i. Along each original port circle all Pochhammer roots are radially separated by a constant times 1/N. Uniformly on the ENTIRE conditional angular circle, sum_(j=0)^(L-1) log|1-e^((gamma+i phi)/N) e^(i theta)Q^j| =N integral_0^(L/N) log|1-e^(i(theta+2pi t))|dt +O_K(log N). (8) Here gamma ranges in a compact set bounded away from zero, L<=N, and phi is bounded. To prove (8), regularize the periodic logarithmic singularity at radial distance |gamma|/N. Its total variation is O_K(log N), giving that Riemann-sum error; its integrated change from the boundary logarithm is O_K(log N/N). This also proves the endpoint uniformity. Known monomial and source constants do not depend on theta. Let L(theta)=D(exp(i theta)). On a fixed positive crossing chart the four angles sum to 2pi. A conditional port varies only one of the following two FULL-circle profiles, up to constant and reversal of its angular coordinate: H_delta(theta)=L(theta)-L(theta+delta), J_delta(theta)=L(theta)+L(delta-theta), 0<delta<2pi. (9) For input z0 and output z6 use H with the sum of the two other relevant positive angles; for input z1 and output z7 use J with the fixed sum of their two varying positive angles. By (8) these are the true leading logarithmic modulus profiles of the original finite polynomials on the whole circle. Explicitly, (2pi/N)log|g_port| equals its H_delta or J_delta profile, plus an angularly constant normalization and O_K(log N/N). The profile itself is not divided by 2pi. All quantum whole-turn factors are already in the fixed source normalization from Section 3. The maxima in (9) are UNIQUE and GLOBAL: max H_delta=2L(pi-delta/2), theta_*=pi-delta/2, max J_delta=2L(delta/2), theta_*=delta/2. (10) For H, differentiation gives H'=log|sin((theta+delta)/2)/sin(theta/2)|. Its only stationary points are theta_* and theta_*+pi. The former is the strict global maximum; the latter is the strict minimum. At shape-1 points the derivative is logarithmically infinite with the same monotone direction on both sides, so no extra endpoint maximum is concealed. For J the same computation gives its maximum theta_* and minimum theta_*+pi. The curvatures at the maxima are -tan(delta/4) and -cot(delta/4), respectively. At these maxima the two varying positively oriented tetrahedron angles are equal. If the other pair was positive, the maximum lies in the positive chamber. Every other sheet or endpoint on this conditional circle is strictly lower. On compact delta ranges, excluding a fixed neighborhood of theta_* gives a UNIFORM gap. This is a conditional statement. The other ports are held fixed. Its maximum is not automatically the complete global geometric point after sewing the original knot. ## 6. Composition scope and the remaining global source issue The exact formulas may collapse ONE adapter, or the paired adapters of (3a), while the untouched opposite ports remain on their correlated original grids. Nothing here permits applying the other pair's formula after arbitrary movements of the first pair. In particular a general geometric complex deformation can destroy its integer relation. The exact [deck-character calculation](balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md) makes the obstruction explicit. If the first pair moves so that D!=sA, then the other input port has mu_b-1=(sD-A)/(A-sB), generically nonzero. The physical FOUR-variable Laurent polynomial remains single-valued; the raw four-Psi continuation does not. Known fixed-grid constants and integer alias multipliers alone cannot turn that raw continuation into a simultaneous equality. An asymptotic comparison in a complex neighborhood may still be possible, but it needs the additional seam terms or their actual bounds, beyond the one-pair theorem. Known phase oscillation is not removed by the modulus maxima. On the positive real-angle chamber the mixed input-output Hessian of the retained leading REAL action is partial_(theta_out) partial_(theta_in) Re W =-(1/2) I_2. Head-only or input/output-only gauges do not remove it. The exact one-port adapter result (5)--(7) controls its local Fourier action; it does not make the entire sewn original scalar a positive Laplace integral. Global cycle selection, compatible elimination order, and the retained cap/boundary source still need a proof. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fourier_port_polynomials.py) checks (2)--(3) against independently evaluated original crossing matrices and their Fourier transforms, every allowed k/m frequency support and scalar normalization, and the analytic adapter and profile estimates.

title: An actual zero-source Fourier current retains a geometric formal block
text: # An actual zero-source Fourier current retains a geometric formal block Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The last Fourier-label source has an explicit, uniformly tame cyclic current complex. A literal Cartan port current of the original knot tensor lies in its zero-source subspace, retains the actual highest-input one-sided support, and on the proved regular geometric chart has a NONZERO formal block with the SAME regulator action. Thus nonzero geometric partial support, root scalarity, the pointed boundary line and one-sided support do not by themselves prove survival in the selected sum. This is an actual current/source obstruction, not a replacement state or a proposed positive model. The geometric formal assertion below uses the regular good-A chart; it does not assert that chart extends to the highest-input boundary A=1. ## 1. A literal whole Cartan current has zero selected source Let T_(c,d;a,b) be the original two-cut tensor, with every original cap, pivot, scalar and peripheral line retained. Put B=diag(Q^b) on the SECOND physical wire and define W(T)=[(I tensor B)T(I tensor B^-1)-T]/(Q-1). (1) Its literal band coefficient is W(T)_(c,b+q;a,b)=[q]_Q T_(c,b+q;a,b), [q]_Q=(Q^q-1)/(Q-1). (2) For every integer q this is a Laurent polynomial in Q, including negative q; it has a regular Q=1 continuation. Formula (1) is a specified actual position/Cartan PORT current. It makes no assumption about an untwisted total Hopf action on a reshaped tensor. Partial trace on the second identity wire is invariant under this conjugation. Therefore the ENTIRE reclosed first-wire matrix obeys ptr_second W(T)=0 (3) as a WHOLE finite-matrix identity, including all q-normal derivatives. No root scalarity is used in (3). The first input/output source, highest vector, Whittaker row and external dimension line remain exactly the originals. The multiplier (2) changes no index or support. If T is charge zero and the first input is a, its band interval is [a-(N-1),a]. At the highest input a=0 it remains the original nonpositive interval. In particular the actual endpoint defects 1-Q^N and M-M^-1 of [the highest boundary](actual_highest_whittaker_boundary_and_moving_walls.md) have not been discarded or replaced by cyclic off-root formulas. ## 2. The exact root Fourier current complex Let J_j be the RAW Fourier partial array with fixed first input, including its inverse-Fourier 1/N. Its selected source is Sigma J, where Sigma J=sum_j J_j, with NO outside 1/N. At Q=Q_N the actual Fourier transform sends (1) to J_W,j=(J_(j+1)-J_j)/(Q_N-1), (4) with cyclic j modulo N. This follows from (2) and Q_N^(Nq)=1, or by the actual cyclic companion matrix at the root. Thus Sigma J_W=0, in agreement with the stronger whole identity (3). Put D=(S-I)/(Q_N-1), S J_j=J_(j+1), and P J=(Sigma J/N)1. Over the root coefficient field, ker D=constant vectors, im D=ker Sigma. (5) There is an explicit centered inverse h on the zero-source space. For f put g=f-Pf and (h f)_j=(Q_N-1){sum_(k<j)g_k -(1/N)sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)sum_(k<ell)g_k}. Direct telescoping, including the cyclic last endpoint, proves D h=h D=I-P, h P=0, Sigma h=0. (6) This is a strict finite cyclic source/current contraction, with section i(c)=c1/N. It is not an assertion that the actual port clock remains a cyclic shift off root. At whole Q its Vandermonde companion has the previously proved last-row carry, and (3), not an uncorrected cyclic formula, is the normal-source identity. This image statement also lifts to literal highest-input port tensors, rather than only abstract sequences. For any g with Sigma g=0 put f_(-b)=sum_j g_j Q_N^(jb), 1<=b<N, and take R_(b,0;0,b)=f_(-b)/[-b]_(Q_N), with every other entry zero. All arrows are in the original head, the tensor is charge zero, its highest band support is one-sided, and its reclosed matrix is zero. The highest Fourier family of W(R) is EXACTLY g. Every divided coefficient here is a nonzero head unit. Thus every zero-source highest Fourier array has an explicit actual-port Cartan primitive. In the flat root metrics, Parseval and |[-b]_(Q_N)|>=1 give the tame bound ||R||_HS<=sqrt(N)||g||_2. This concerns the linear actual port/ current category; it does not assert that arbitrary R is a new uninserted knot word. In the flat complex root metric the cyclic Fourier basis is unitary. For nonzero mode k the inverse h has multiplier (Q_N-1)/(Q_N^k-1), whose modulus is at most one. Hence EXACTLY ||h||_2<=1, ||J||_2^2=|Sigma J|^2/N+||(I-P)J||_2^2, |Sigma J|=sqrt(N) dist(J,im D). (7) Thus the selected norm measures distance from actual zero-source currents, rather than the size of the partial array. There is no positive lower bound for that distance from ||J|| alone. These are norms of this specified finite source complex, not estimates for the full knot word or a uniform q-normal neighborhood. For a literal ACTUAL example, the two-cut unknot is the flip tensor. At first input zero it has F_0(eta_F)=sum_(b=0)^(N-1) eta_F^-b, J_j=delta_(j,0), J_W,j=[delta_(j+1,0)-delta_(j,0)]/(Q_N-1). The last array is nonzero, one-sided before Fourier transformation, and its selected source is zero at every N>1. Its source and actual moving endpoint operators are precisely the originals. ## 3. The same actual current has nonzero geometric normal support Now use the proved good first-position phase, not the unproved highest-boundary extension. The actual proper root lift and its nondegenerate Fourier Gaussian give Z(v,H)=C(H) exp(S_geo/H)[A_0(v)+H A_1(v)+...], eta=exp(v), p_e=eta^-1. Here S_geo is independent of v; all original base, peripheral, half-density and Fourier phase marks stay in C and the chosen line. Multiplication of the actual open coefficient by (2) is EXACTLY the external shift identity Z_W(v,H)=[Z(v+H,H)-Z(v,H)]/(exp(H)-1). (8) Equation (8) uses the specified proper root lift of the partial family; it does not equate that lift's q-normal jets with the whole-Vandermonde family. It follows coefficientwise, rather than by a growing-band analytic limit. Hence Z_W=C(H) exp(S_geo/H)[partial_v A_0+O(H)]. (9) The leading derivative is NOT identically zero. Indeed the uniform actual Gaussian/holonomy density and its Fourier Jacobian show at fixed good A that A_0(v)=c(M,A) partial_v r(eta), (10) up to the retained fixed ordered Fourier phase. Here is the needed frame-independence justification, rather than a free normalization: the [actual uniform density theorem](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) gives Omega_beta^2=(-T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2. Its determinant ratio T_beta is invariant under simultaneous representation framing; the frame-change determinants in its two chain maps cancel and det Ad(g)=1. On the marked half-density cover the square of Omega_beta/Omega_cut is therefore frame-constant. Differentiating that square in characteristic zero makes the marked ratio itself frame-constant. The exact Fourier Jacobian then gives (10), with a nonzero c depending only on M,A and the retained base mark. At completeness r(eta) is the nonconstant rational inverse of the actual birational (A,p_e) chart. If partial_v A_0 vanished, eta partial_eta r would be a constant d. Then dr=d deta/eta. A derivative of a rational function has zero logarithmic residue at eta=0, so d=0, forcing r constant. This contradicts that birational chart. Thus partial_v A_0 is nonzero on a dense regular open. The result persists on the marked meridian deformation germ. Equations (3) and (9) prove the advertised obstruction: an ACTUAL zero-source port-current family has a nonzero formal geometric block with the same marked action as the knot. For its certificate use a common LEFT multiple, rather than assuming this insertion has unit principal amplitude: its multiplier vanishes at t=0 and contains H^-1. Let D(eta) be the already constructed meridian certificate for the original partial array and its SAME formal block, with eta the physical Fourier character Q^j. Then D(Q eta) annihilates the externally shifted array J(Q eta) and formal block Z(Q eta). The meridian shift fixes Q,eta. A nonzero common left multiple of D(eta) and D(Q eta), over the indicated localized Ore field, consequently annihilates their difference divided by Q-1, BOTH for actual root arrays and for the exact formal difference (8). Clear its denominators and remove its common q-1 power. Its leading symbol has the geometric factor because (9) is a nonzero formal block with the same longitude action. This avoids applying the unit-amplitude coefficient theorem directly to a vanishing insertion. The [original certificate theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) supplies D and its formal identity. The selected scalar of this current family is nevertheless identically zero, whose minimal scalar annihilator is one. This is an explicit mechanism by which geometric partial support is lost in the final source pushforward. This does NOT say the uninserted knot's selected geometric contribution is zero, nor establish an actual exponential norm for the current arrays. It says that taking a nonzero local WKB line alone is not a faithful map on the actual source quotient. Any global comparison must carry the current/relative class and its marked cycle, not merely its action or leading local solution. ## 4. Compatibility with the first-cut highest moment decomposition There is a complementary exact first-port description in [the rank-one moment/orbit theorem](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). With A_j[c,a]=T^V_(c,j;a,j), it proves J_whit,j=P_N/N+beta_K(D_K A_j), beta_K(X)=sum_(c=1)^(N-1) X_(c,0)/(Q_N^-c-1). The equality is entrywise: D_K multiplies that entry by Q_N^-c-1. The highest moment row c=0 forces q=0 in the uninserted conserving tensor and is constant in j at the root. Its exact beta norm is sqrt((N^2-1)/12). This decomposition retains the original orbit row and its Ward sector; it does not compute the unknown scalar P_N or move the regular good-A geometric block to A=1. Together with (5)--(9), it identifies the extra requirement sharply: the selected scalar class must be determined in the cyclic/current quotient, including boundary and normal data. Scalar root closure, pointing, algebraicity of the geometric optimizer and a nonzero partial A-factor do not supply that determination by themselves. The [flat cyclic source-frame theorem](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md) is consistent with this: it fixes the aligned whole clock/source frame before jets, but the scalar of the supplied closed word is separate. Here its actual cyclic-source kernel and a nonzero geometric formal current in that kernel are both explicit. [Exact current/source and cyclic-complex audit](../experiments/audit_zero_source_fourier_current.py) and [saved results](../experiments/zero_source_fourier_current_results.json). The checks pass seven root levels with all 8,771 port units, 119 highest-input conserving units, 35 cyclic homotopy basis vectors, eight checks of the proved norm bound, and the exact whole-Q two-cut unknot. The latter detects the nonzero off-root carry missed by treating the root cyclic difference as a whole companion formula. [The intrinsic Mobius-pole calculation](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) makes r(eta) and its pole explicit. Its root norm factor 1-lambda^N explains why sampling the rational principal density is not automatically a uniform source comparison. In particular the actual figure-eight principal pole meets the sampling grid at N divisible by six, while its finite arrays remain regular.

title: An exact bridge-number certificate for odd-prime-divisible plat boxes
status: Exact minimal bridge number from original plat Fox colors
text: # An exact bridge-number certificate for odd-prime-divisible plat boxes elementary certificate, 31 October 2026. This result is independent of the source asymptotics and circle-packing balance condition. It identifies exact-bridge congruence subfamilies when the prescribed plat parity gives a knot. Geometric balance must be established separately. ## 1. Fox colors and the signed crossing map Fix an odd prime $p$ and work over $\mathbb F_p$. A Fox coloring assigns a field element to each diagram arc between undercrossings. At a crossing, if $a$ is the overstrand color and $b,c$ are the two understrand colors, the condition is $$ b+c=2a.\tag{1} $$ All colorings, including the $p$ constant colorings of a knot, are counted. The rule is unoriented and unchanged on reversing a strand orientation. Follow a braid in its actual geometric slot order. Choose the positive crossing convention in which an incoming ordered pair $(a,b)$ becomes $(2a-b,a)$. Its matrix and inverse are $$ \begin{aligned} T&=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}=I+A, &A&=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^2=0,\\ T^{-1}&=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=I-A. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ The opposite naming convention interchanges $T$ and $T^{-1}$ and has the same consequence. For every signed integer $e$, $$ T^e=I+eA.\tag{3} $$ This follows by the binomial formula for $e\geq0$ and the exact inverse $I-A$ for negative $e$. Thus $p\mid e$ implies $T^e=I$ over $\mathbb F_p$. At a crossing on slot $j$, embed this two-by-two block in the identity on the other slots; the same identity holds there. This is an identity on the ordered color register, not on strand labels. The underlying endpoint permutation remains the transposition of the two slots when $e$ is odd. In particular, $T^p=I$ for odd $p$ does not make the tangle an identity tangle or a permutation identity. ## 2. Coloring invariance, including constant colorings The local rules give bijections of coloring sets under all three Reidemeister moves, keeping exterior colors fixed. For type I, (1) forces the new short arc to have the old arc's color, so the extension is unique. For type II, write $s_a(b)=2a-b$. The strand passing under the other twice undergoes $s_a$ twice, and $s_a^2=I$; its intermediate color is uniquely determined. For type III, the exact identity $$ s_a\circ s_b=s_{s_a(b)}\circ s_a.\tag{4} $$ follows by evaluating both sides on $c$: both give $2a-2b+c$. This is the crossing-rule relation for the two three-crossing arrangements, and every intermediate color is uniquely determined from the exterior data. It proves the local bijection, with all orientation versions covered because (1) is unoriented and $s_a$ is its own inverse. Thus the number $\operatorname{Col}_p(K)$ is invariant under diagram moves for the same unframed knot. The bijections preserve constant colorings, so counting all colors introduces no diagram-dependent convention. The usual Reidemeister characterization of diagrams of the same knot is the underlying diagram-equivalence fact used here. ## 3. Exact count for the supplied standard plat Consider a standard $2k$-plat whose genuine crossings all lie in specified adjacent-strand boxes $\sigma_{j_i+1}^{e_i}$. Here the physical slots are numbered from $0$, so slot $j$ is the conventional generator $\sigma_{j+1}$. Use the standard adjacent cup and cap pairs $$ (0,1),(2,3),\ldots,(2k-2,2k-1) $$ in the same geometric slot order. Assume every $e_i$ is divisible by $p$. There are no extra uncontrolled crossings outside these boxes; any such crossings would have to be included in the color propagation separately. At one end each cup forces its two colors equal. The initial register is exactly $$ (a_0,a_0,a_1,a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1},a_{k-1}), \qquad(a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1})\in\mathbb F_p^k.\tag{5} $$ Every full box acts as the identity by (3), even though its physical endpoint permutation can be nontrivial. The opposite register is again (5), so all standard cap constraints hold automatically. These are topological arc constraints; the quantum marked-cap matrix does not modify the underlying diagram or its Fox coloring rule. Propagation through the actual braid is invertible and uniquely fixes every intermediate arc color. Conversely, every coloring restricts to one register (5). Hence the count is exactly $$ \operatorname{Col}_p(\text{plat})=p^k.\tag{6} $$ No strand permutation is dropped: the register uses geometric slot positions at each horizontal section. One must not propagate colors by the bare permutation after already applying the crossing matrices. The link component count is separate. If $\tau$ maps lower slot labels to upper labels, pull the upper adjacent matching back by $\tau$. The union of the lower matching $M$ and $\tau^{-1}M\tau$ is a two-colored $2$-regular multigraph on the $2k$ lower endpoints. Its cycles are precisely the plat components. Thus the prescribed parity yields a knot exactly when this graph is connected. Only $e_i$ modulo $2$ enters $\tau$. ## 4. Any knot with bridge number $b$ has at most $p^b$ colorings Take a diagram with $b$ overpassing bridges. Its overpasses have no undercrossings and carry $b$ individual colors. Every underpass starts at an endpoint of an overpass. Starting with that known endpoint color, follow the underpass: at each crossing the overpass color $a$ is already known, and (1) updates the traveling color by $c\mapsto2a-c$. All underpass arc colors are therefore determined by the $b$ chosen overpass colors. At their opposite endpoints the remaining matching conditions may impose restrictions, but never create an additional choice. Restriction to the overpasses is injective, so $$ \operatorname{Col}_p(K)\leq p^b.\tag{7} $$ This also covers the one-bridge unknot with no crossings. A geometric $b$-bridge presentation has its usual diagram with $b$ overpasses, so (7) applies to the minimal bridge number. Conversely, the supplied $2k$-plat is a $k$-bridge presentation: keep its braid monotone and use its $k$ caps as the only maxima. Its knot therefore has bridge number at most $k$. If the component test in Section 3 gives a knot $K$, invariance, (6), and (7) imply $$ p^k=\operatorname{Col}_p(K)\leq p^{\operatorname{br}(K)}, \qquad\operatorname{br}(K)\geq k, \qquad\boxed{\operatorname{br}(K)=k}.\tag{8} $$ The conclusion is minimal bridge number, not only a supplied plat width. ## 5. Compatibility with the actual signed filling parameters In the original source convention the full box exponent is $$ e_i=n_i=\epsilon_i-2P_i, $$ where $\epsilon_i$ is the fixed half-twist parity and $P_i$ is the signed integer full-twist parameter. Since $p$ is odd, $2$ is invertible modulo $p$. The condition $p\mid n_i$ is precisely $$ P_i\equiv\epsilon_i/2\pmod p.\tag{9} $$ It does not change $n_i\bmod2$ or the prescribed component permutation. Each congruence class contains arbitrarily large positive and negative $P_i$, independently at every box. It is therefore compatible with any fixed parity pattern already proved to give a knot and any independently sufficiently long signed-twist threshold. The prime $p=3$ already suffices. For example, the [simple-white family's component-parity construction](general_simple_white_plat_class.md), Section 3, can be combined with (9): the first $O$ layer has odd exponents and the other boxes even; its width-two example uses the stated first-slot odd exponent. The [balanced reduced-layer family](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes the separate geometry for $k\geq4$. In its congruence subfamilies, this coloring argument certifies minimal bridge number exactly $k$. The analytic volume theorem itself has no extra congruence restriction. ## Validation and scope The Fox certificate does not imply circle-packing balance.

title: Actual Frobenius endpoint periods and the normal current correction
text: # Actual Frobenius endpoint periods and the normal current correction Research proof and independent audit, 27 October 2026. The actual paired Frobenius source has an explicit Serre-dual relative interval with the required geometric endpoints. Its original whole quantum source gives a rational relative-period deformation of this interval. The normal connection required by that deformation is computable; it is already different from a naive divided-Borel generator at first order. Endpoint norm growth is also explicit. This is a source-level relative-period map. It does not identify the full braid network's residual Gaussian currents with it. ## 1. The canonical interval is an actual finite unipotent source Use the actual Sym^N source and dual from [the marked Borel construction](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md). Write \[ \psi_\alpha=\alpha^N\sum_{k=0}^N v_k,\qquad \lambda_m(v_k)=\alpha^{-N}\binom Nk \left(\frac{1+m}{2}\right)^{N-k} \left(\frac{1-m}{2}\right)^k . \tag{1} \] The source pairing is one. These formulas include the missing finite-u chart point m=-1 (u=infinity); no inverse flag coefficient is introduced there. Take D=0 in the framing map, so \[ s=C\alpha^2,\quad r=(1+m)/2,\quad A=(1+s)^{-1},\quad \tau=r/s=\frac{1+m}{2C\alpha^2}. \] The geometric marked interval tau=0 to 1 has the EXACT endpoints \[ m_0=-1,\qquad m_1=-1+2C\alpha^2. \tag{2} \] Put L=C alpha^2 and n=h+f-e, where e,f,h are the original root divided Frobenius matrices. Direct calculation in the actual module gives \[ n\psi_\alpha=0,\quad n^{N+1}=0,\quad \partial_m\lambda_m=\tfrac12\lambda_m n, \quad\lambda_\tau=\lambda_0\exp(\tau L n). \tag{3} \] Equivalently, \[ \lambda_\tau(v_k)=\alpha^{-N}\binom Nk (L\tau)^{N-k}(1-L\tau)^k . \tag{4} \] Thus the interval co-source is a specified finite expression, \[ \mathcal I=\int_0^1\lambda_\tau\,d\tau =\lambda_0\sum_{j=0}^N\frac{(Ln)^j}{(j+1)!}, \qquad \mathcal I Ln=\lambda_1-\lambda_0. \tag{5} \] No inverse of n is used. Every original matrix insertion B satisfies \[ \mathcal I[Ln,B]\psi_\alpha =(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)B\psi_\alpha. \tag{6} \] This retains both endpoints and their alpha-dependent displacement. Since Omega_cut=d tau wedge dlog A, integrating its source kernel along this marked interval gives precisely the co-source (5) times dlog A, with that orientation. An arbitrary translation tau_0(A) moves both endpoint rows; it does not erase them. At L=1, the beta integral in (4) gives \[ \mathcal I(v_k)=\frac{\alpha^{-N}}{N+1}. \tag{7} \] For alpha=C=1 this is the original uniform Frobenius co-source. Thus exponential endpoint norms do not imply an exponential scalar period: the full integrated row, including cancellations, matters. ## 2. Serre residue preserves the same actual endpoint rows Use the exact convention \[ v_k\longmapsto\binom Nk z^k\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,O(N)), \quad c_\lambda(z)=\sum_{k=0}^N \frac{\lambda(v_k)}{\binom Nk}z^{-k-1}. \] The second expression is a Cech representative for H^1(O(-N-2)); its pairing is Res_(z=0) c_lambda f dz. These conventions and all actual normal operators are developed in [the global Frobenius Cech source](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). For the interval (4) the representative is explicitly \[ c_\tau(z)=\alpha^{-N}\sum_{k=0}^N (L\tau)^{N-k}(1-L\tau)^k z^{-k-1}. \tag{8} \] It is polynomial in tau, has the fixed allowed Cech exponents, and retains both endpoints in (2). Residue, interval integration, and the finite matrix action commute exactly. Hence (5)--(6) hold as Serre-dual cohomology identities, not only scalar coincidences. The residue pairing alone supplies no identification of n with the network's full actual Hopf-adjoint current. ## 3. An original whole-source rational period retains ALL normal jets Fix a residue string s of the original high integral color. Let F_s(q), E_s(q) be its actual divided matrices, with the original root sign included in E_s, so their root values are f,e. Write \[ B_k(q)=[\exp F_s(q)v_0]_k,\qquad A_k(q)=[v_0^*\exp E_s(q)]_k . \] The exponentials are finite because these matrices are strictly triangular. Their root values are B_k=1 and A_k=binom(N,k). Define original whole source and homogeneous dual \[ \begin{split} \psi(q)&=\alpha^N\sum_k B_k(q)v_k,\\ \widetilde\lambda(q,m)(v_k) &=\alpha^{-N}A_k(q) ((1+m)/2)^{N-k}((1-m)/2)^k,\\ U_s(q,m)&=\widetilde\lambda(q,m)\psi(q),\qquad \lambda(q,m)=\widetilde\lambda(q,m)/U_s(q,m). \tag{9} \end{split} \] These are the actual divided-source germs, expressed homogeneously; the normalization is their ACTUAL pairing. No root binomial weight is differentiated in place of that pairing. In particular \[ U_s(q_N,m)=1 \tag{10} \] for every finite m, including both endpoints. Consequently the whole interval co-source \[ \mathcal I_s(q)=\int_0^1 \lambda(q,-1+2L\tau)\,d\tau \tag{11} \] is a rational relative-period integral on the tau line with the zeros of U_s deleted and endpoints 0,1 retained. For fixed N it is analytic near q_N on a small neighborhood where the compact path has no U_s zero. Equivalently it exists coefficientwise in the completed actual quantum normal ring. Every coefficient of the inverse of U_s is polynomial in m because its constant coefficient is one; normal expansion and the compact interval integral commute. The same applies to its Serre representative (8), replacing lambda by (9), and to every original whole matrix insertion B(q). For each finite normal truncation this is an explicit algebraic calculation followed by a relative rational period. It imposes no uniform-in-N neighborhood, metric bound, or geometric-saddle claim. It is generally a period, rather than a rational function of q: integrating a rational row with moving poles can produce logarithms. There is also an exact source-pair current connection. Put \[ P_0=\psi_0\lambda_0(\tau),\quad P_q=\psi(q)\lambda(q,\tau), \quad G=\psi(q)\lambda_0+(I-P_q)(I-P_0). \] Its root is I, so it is an invertible rational germ; directly G psi_0=psi(q) and lambda(q)G=lambda_0. Define \[ K_q=G(Ln)G^{-1}-(\partial_\tau G)G^{-1}. \tag{12} \] Since psi(q) is tau-independent, the exact identities are \[ K_q\psi(q)=0,\quad\partial_\tau\lambda(q)=\lambda(q)K_q, \] and for every insertion, including tau-dependent ones, \[ \partial_\tau[\lambda(q)B(q,\tau)\psi(q)] =\lambda(q)([K_q,B]+\partial_\tau B)\psi(q). \tag{13} \] Integration gives the ACTUAL endpoint rows with all normal coefficients retained. Formula (12) constructs a source connection; it does not assert that the network's Hopf current equals K_q. That comparison requires an actual intertwining calculation. ## 4. A literal actual first-normal defect forbids the naive lift The distinction in the last sentence is already necessary at N=3, r=3, residue string s=1 of the original high color 12. Use epsilon=log(q/q_3), q_3=exp(pi i/3), and include the actual root sign tau=(-1)^(Nr-1)=+1 in e(q). Direct integral Gaussian coefficient differentiation gives \[ e(q)=e+\gamma\epsilon e+O(\epsilon^2),\quad f(q)=f+\gamma\epsilon f+O(\epsilon^2),\qquad \gamma=1-2q_3=-i\sqrt3. \tag{14} \] For example the first divided coefficient is, including its constant beta sign, [4]_q/[1]_q; the sign does not affect its logarithmic derivative, which at q_3 is 3(q_3+q_3^{-1})/(q_3-q_3^{-1})=gamma. The remaining entries give the same gamma, as the exact audit checks independently using integral Gaussian polynomials. The naive whole divided generator \[ n(q)=[e(q),f(q)]+f(q)-e(q) \] therefore satisfies \[ n(q)\exp(f(q))v_0 =-2\gamma\epsilon f\psi_0+O(\epsilon^2)\ne0. \tag{15} \] Indeed psi_1=gamma f psi_0, n_1=gamma(2h+f-e), [n,f]=-2f-h, and n psi_0=0. This proves (15) without numerical approximation. The endpoint current (12) kills the actual whole source; hence it differs from L n(q) already in this first normal. The extreme residue strings s=0 and s=N-1 have vanishing first derivative here, so testing only them misses the defect. This is a source/connection defect, not a claim about failure of the actual quantum-group relations. ## 5. A sharp endpoint metric obstruction and its limitation The actual root Frobenius coherent metric in this divided basis is g_k=binom(N,k). Then \[ \|\psi_\alpha\|^2=|\alpha|^{2N}2^N,\qquad \|\lambda_m\|_*^2=|\alpha|^{-2N} ((1+|m|^2)/2)^N. \] Thus the normalized rank-one source coupon satisfies EXACTLY \[ \|\psi_\alpha\lambda_m\| =(1+|m|^2)^{N/2}. \tag{16} \] Any translated geometric interval of length one at fixed s has endpoint displacement m_1-m_0=2s. The triangle inequality gives max(|m_0|,|m_1|)>=|s|, hence \[ \max_{j=0,1}\|\psi_\alpha\lambda_{m_j}\| \ge(1+|s|^2)^{N/2}. \tag{17} \] At the regular anchor s=-2,A=-1 this is at least 5^(N/2), for EVERY translation of the marked interval. The unshifted endpoints are m=-1,-5, giving 2^(N/2) and 26^(N/2). This rules out an automatic tame UNITARY endpoint comparison in the specified actual Frobenius coherent metric. It does not rule out the integrated period or cancellations: (7) is an exact counterexample to that inference. A transported metric, a contour comparison, or retained character compensation needs its own proof. Neither Serre duality nor a root Borel isomorphism supplies that proof by itself. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint.py) checks the finite unipotent/interval identities, Serre residues, the actual integral Gaussian first-normal defect, and the metric formulas. No volume asymptotic is assumed.

title: The finest crossing bound is unchanged by arbitrary matrix wire gauges
text: # The finest crossing bound is unchanged by arbitrary matrix wire gauges 29 October 2026. Allowing off-diagonal matrices on individual physical wires does not improve the existing alternating-sign crossing bound. This extends the earlier diagonal optimizer theorem to every positive definite one-wire matrix, with the original paired source fixed. The proof uses the full one-head density matrices, not only their diagonal entries. It does NOT exclude entangled metrics on several wires, coherent clock packets, or norms formed after block contraction. ## 1. Exact source-preserving matrix gauges Use the original balanced crossing matrices and paired plat source of [the weighted energy theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md). At the bottom a cup pair is, up to its retained scalar, vec(U), where U is an anti-diagonal unitary matrix. At the top the ordinary or marked co-source similarly has an anti-diagonal unitary coefficient matrix; the ordinary pair includes its actual pivot. The marked pair is used only after the already proved whole-degree reduction. No source is changed on a separately dephased state. On each physical wire segment choose an arbitrary positive matrix P_e=exp(H_e), H_e Hermitian. At a bottom pair require P_o U P_e^T=U, H_e=-U^T H_o^T bar(U). (1) The second identity is equivalent to the first, by the unique Hermitian matrix logarithm. At a top pair apply the same formula to the conjugate of its actual cap matrix. These relations fix the actual input vector and output covector. In particular their diagonal entries obey (H_e)_(b,b)=-(H_o)_(d-b,d-b), d=N-1, (2) regardless of the off-diagonal entries or the retained root phases. Bottom and top gauges can be chosen independently subject to their own source relations. Untouched wires keep the same matrix at both ends. For a gate v define C_v=(P_out,1 tensor P_out,2) R_v (P_in,1 tensor P_in,2)^(-1), F(P)=sum_v log ||C_v||_HS. (3) All interior gauges cancel in the full original product. Equations (1) retain its endpoint source, so the standard whole-source bound using (3) remains valid, with the same external polynomial factors. ## 2. The full one-head densities are diagonal Every literal R_v preserves total INTEGER head degree. Therefore R_v R_v^* and R_v^*R_v commute with the sum of the two degree operators. Taking either partial trace shows that EACH one-head reduced density commutes with the simple one-head degree operator. It is consequently diagonal. This is an exact matrix statement, including the complete-color endpoint and its nilpotent source. Normalize these reduced matrices by ||R_v||_HS^2. For R_+, symmetry R_+^T=R_+ makes its input and output first-head densities equal, and likewise for its second head. Denote their diagonal probabilities by p_H and p_L. The literal factorial reflection gives p_H(a)=p_L(d-a). (4) For R_- the two one-head densities are exchanged. These are the same exact coefficient identities proved in [the diagonal gauge theorem](actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.md), now supplemented by the off-diagonal vanishing above. The common Cartan/framing scalar is a unit phase and remains external. ## 3. Convexity along every Hermitian gauge ray proves the optimizer Assume the actual signed word has sign(sigma_i)=epsilon*(-1)^(i+1), epsilon=+1 or -1, (5) at each occurrence of generator i. Its index sequence, number of crossings and even width are otherwise arbitrary. When its plat is a one-component knot, all original source identifications above apply. For ANY collection H satisfying (1), set P_e(t)=exp(t H_e). The endpoint relations hold at every real t. Vectorizing a gate gives vec(C_v(t))=exp(t K_v) vec(R_v), K_v=H_out,1+H_out,2-H_in,1^T-H_in,2^T, (6) where each term acts on its own tensor leg. Thus K_v is Hermitian. By its finite spectral decomposition, log ||C_v(t)||_HS =one_half log sum_j w_j exp(2t lambda_j), w_j>=0. (7) Its second derivative is twice the variance of lambda_j under the displayed normalized weights, hence nonnegative. No assumption that different H_e commute is used: the four operators in (6) act on separate legs. F(P(t)) is therefore convex in t. At t=0 its derivative is the sum, over every outgoing wire, of Tr(H_e rho_out,e), minus the corresponding incoming terms. Under (5), every odd physical wire has the same normalized one-head density at all its incident gates, and every even wire has its reflected density. All interior terms cancel. At a paired boundary the remaining terms cancel by (2),(4). Off-diagonal H entries contribute zero because the full densities are diagonal. Therefore dF(P(t))/dt at t=0 =0. (8) Convexity on the ray from identity to any prescribed P proves the EXACT finite-level theorem inf_{all positive matrix wire gauges preserving source} F(P) =m log ||R_+||_HS, (9) where m is the number of crossings. Flat gauges attain the right side. This is a proof for all admissible matrices, not numerical optimization over a chosen finite set of off-diagonal perturbations. The same conclusion holds if invertible complex one-wire gauges are allowed. Write each as U_e P_e by polar decomposition. At every gate the outer unitary factors do not change its HS norm. The positive parts preserve the unitary paired source too: if A U B^T=U, then B=U^T A^(-T)bar(U), whose positive polar factor is U^T P_A^(-T)bar(U). The analogous cap formula follows from A^T L B=L with its unitary L. Thus (9) applies to their positive parts. ## 4. Operator norms and the actual scope Each crossing acts on N^2 dimensions, so ||C_v||_HS/N <= ||C_v||_op <= ||C_v||_HS. Consequently the optimum product of operator norms differs from the HS optimum by at most a power N^m. The already proved crossing factorial asymptotic gives, for all these matrix wire gauges, inf sum_v log ||C_v||_op =m N v_8/(2pi)+O_word(log N). (10) This is a limitation of the finest local norm estimate, not a lower bound on the knot invariant. It leaves all cross-gate interference outside the norm, which is precisely what the desired coherent Gram must recover. The normalized-star identities and the new Pascal packet metric act on coupled boundary/coefficient data; they are not excluded by (9). Neither a general tensor-product wire metric nor a diagonal clock metric can by itself supply the sharp geometric bound for the alternating-sign class (5). The original source and degree hypotheses are explicit. This theorem does not apply an ordinary positive pivotal trace at color N, nor does it assert that every alternating knot presentation has pattern (5). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_matrix_wire_gauge.py): literal positive/negative crossing reduced densities, original cup/cap matrix gauges, zero derivatives and finite off-diagonal gauge rays at several widths. The proof of the all-matrix optimizer is (6)-(9).

title: Exact pole pushforward with the original scalar cut-wall current retained
text: # Exact pole pushforward with the original scalar cut-wall current retained 28 October 2026. The absolutely convergent [full-Psi flow cycle](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md) can be pushed to a bare full-function head period PLUS an explicit scalar current on the negative-ray atomic cut walls. The current is an oriented tubular boundary of a specified radius homotopy; all wall intersections are retained with a common regularization. It is not an unknown matrix normalization or an asserted zero correction. This supplies an allowed exact cycle deformation and locates its additional chains. It still does not prove geometric survival or a sharp global bound on those chains. A cycle passing through a regular critical point does not determine its Lefschetz intersection number. For 0<|A|<R off the negative real ray, M_(epsilon,R)[1/(1-A/t)] =Psi_epsilon(Log_principal A). (1) This is an ordinary cut-disk Cauchy formula, not a formal coefficient expansion on its radial piece. For epsilon=+1 integrate Psi(Log t)dt/(t-A) around the disk cut on the negative axis, with an inner circle of radius delta. Its inner-circle integral tends to zero since Psi tends to 1 and A is fixed nonzero. On the two cut lips, Psi_lower=(1-t^N)Psi_upper. Their difference gives exactly the negative-ray term in M. Equation (1) cannot be applied to the original flow cycle with fixed head variables without moving that cycle: its head radii depend on the moment radii. More generally it may be chosen to have ANY prescribed finite head radii at a fixed Gaussian tuple xi_g: use that prescribed vector in a compact xi neighborhood, the small-argument construction outside it, and a log-convex smooth interpolation. Enlarge the finitely many R_j to cover the compact modified neighborhood. All bounds in (3) remain uniform in xi. The flow proof extends verbatim from R_j=1 to any fixed finite R_j: replace -log|t_j| in its bound by its positive part; on 1<=|t_j|<=R_j all extra radial powers are bounded by R_j^N. Thus the original source still has an absolute Gaussian majorant with explicit exp(C_word N) constants. No discarded exterior-radius estimate is being substituted for the exact ray chain. At the target, integrate each full moment chain first. Equation (1) gives the bare product of Psi_epsilon(Log_principal A_j), with exactly the original monomials, Gaussian and coupled K_N sources. This target period is well-defined as an ordinary angular cut period. Its moment form is locally absolutely integrable even where a radial pole meets the head torus: integrate its real radial distance first to obtain at most a logarithm of the angular distance to Arg A_j=pi. Products of finitely many such logarithms are integrable. Indeed Holder's inequality reduces this to finite powers of one logarithm of a nonzero torus character, whose Haar integral is finite. Each radial variable is separate even if some atomic angular characters coincide. Condition (3) prevents circle-pole intersections. The head source contributes at most exp(CN(1+sum|xi|)) times a fixed power of N. All A_j stay in a bounded disk, where the selected principal-log full function is bounded at each N, including its continuous limit at zero. Therefore the target period is jointly absolutely convergent with its Gaussian variables as well. ## 3. The exact global homotopy and its correction current Let lambda_0(t,xi) be the reduced flow-dual radii, and use the single angle-INDEPENDENT homotopy on the FULL head-angle torus lambda_s=(1-s)lambda_0+s lambda_*, 0<=s<=1. (4) There is no restriction to an isolated angular box whose side prisms would be omitted. The form is the original scalar full-function form, first with the exact K_N cap kernels integrated as polynomials. Source interval versions can be reinserted using their exact relative derivative on logarithmic seams. On every moment circle, both endpoints of (4) have |A_j|<R_j. Log-convex interpolation preserves this, so no D_j is crossed on circle pieces. On a moment ray t_j=-r_j, a crossing of D_j requires A_j=t_j<0. (5) These are the only extra pole loci in the head-radius homotopy. All head angular boundaries are paired globally. If one instead partitions into angular chambers, their side prisms MUST be included; they cancel pairwise off (5), with the remaining pole tubes retained. For complete precision, truncate every radial variable at a common delta>0, truncate the Gaussian box, and remove a common small tubular neighborhood of the union of (2) from the homotopy (4). Apply Stokes to its complement. Retain the ENTIRE induced tubular boundary, including all its matched intersections/corners; do not replace it by independent unsupported simple residues. Denote its integral, with the complement's boundary orientation, by W_(delta,epsilon). The matched full-Psi logarithmic lips are exactly those in M, so their outer endpoints cancel using the original monodromy. On a fixed radial end face the full form has dt_j=0. Gaussian end faces vanish in the limit by its majorant. One obtains P_original=P_bare+W, W=lim_(delta->0,epsilon->0) W_(delta,epsilon), (6) with the SAME common regularization for all tube pieces. The sign is fixed by the complement's boundary orientation. The resulting correction in (6) is exactly W=-epsilon/(2*pi*i) integral_0^a Psi_epsilon(log r+i epsilon pi) (-r)^N F(-r) dr/r. (7) Taking F(u)=u^(-b), 0<=b<N, gives precisely the original coefficient identity v_b=C_b-J_b. Thus this pushforward does not silently discard the low Cauchy moments of t^N Log t. Actual wall geometry, and what remains on the critical path A simple wall retains the explicit charge A_j^N. Its leading action is W_0+2*pi*i Log A_j. Regular transverse iterations give integer sums of these marks. The exponentiated actual canonical/Hurwitz equations and the original caps are unchanged. The atom argument on the cut is flat; it need not be a physical degenerate meridian clock. Normalization ray cells can still carry the full geometric rate and must be grouped exactly. (8) The shifted logarithm is in the selected epsilon strip. Otherwise the principal logarithm already is in that strip. On compact angular cells away from the real rays, the uniform full-Psi symbol therefore applies to an EXACT finite integer-mark expansion. This does not assert that arbitrary Stokes branches in other domains are exhausted; positive-ray interfaces and all cut/corner chains remain part of the source. Apply the exact scalar source identity first: its remaining Gaussian integrand is a finite sum of entire exponential moments, with Gaussian decay on horizontal lines. The adapted flow radii satisfy the same bound with bounded imaginary parts, so this is an allowed full scalar cycle deformation, not an assumption that a fixed-circle Gaussian interchange is valid. Consequently a regular target head/Gaussian/cap chart can be specified through a given finite geometric point. The exact price is the current W in (6), not an unspecified comparison factor. title: Exact full-Psi deck characters and central gluing
text: # Exact full-Psi deck characters and central gluing 28 October 2026. The full functions in the original source and its new beta residue factors have an exact algebraic deck character. Products and integral monomial gluing carry this character without an unknown central normalizer. Its triviality equations are the marked exponential gluing equations in Frobenius coordinates. This constructs central data of the actual specified full-function components. It does not assert that the original invariant is only one such component, or that its complete relative source lies on the character-one locus. The [actual beta deck extension](actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy.md) shows why those additional assertions would be false without source and cycle control. ## 1. A full-function identity on the logarithmic cover Put h=2*pi*i/N, N>=2. Use precisely the two original functions Psi_epsilon, epsilon=+1,-1, with Psi_epsilon(L+epsilon*2*pi*i) =Psi_epsilon(L)/(1-exp(NL)). (1) For every integer m, meromorphic continuation gives Psi_epsilon(L+2*pi*i*m)/Psi_epsilon(L) =(1-exp(NL))^(-epsilon*m). (2) This includes negative shifts and all divisor multiplicities. An identity across a zero or pole is understood after cross-multiplication; no vanishing norm factor is separately inverted on the source. Let Z=(Z_1,...,Z_d) be marked logarithmic coordinates. Take integer row vectors a_j, a symmetric integer matrix C, constants ell_j and a specified linear term b_N. The constants may include actual colors and exact h or h/2 shifts. Consider the SPECIFIED component F_N(Z)=P_N(exp Z) exp[(Z^t C Z/2+b_N^t Z)/h] product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(a_j.Z+ell_j), (3) where P_N is single-valued meromorphic in exp Z. It can contain the original integer powers, factorial constants and boundary polynomials; it is not assumed small. Write X_k=exp(NZ_k), Xi_j=exp(N ell_j), A_j=Xi_j product_k X_k^(a_jk), gamma_k=exp(N b_N,k+pi*i*N C_kk). Direct substitution in (2)--(3) gives EXACTLY F_N(Z+2*pi*i e_k)/F_N(Z)=chi_k(X), chi_k=gamma_k product_l X_l^(C_kl) product_j(1-A_j)^(-epsilon_j a_jk). (4) All half-step phases are present in Xi_j and gamma_k. In particular an h/2 shift contributes -1 to Xi_j and cannot be dropped before taking the Nth-power norm. The factor pi*i*N C_kk is also necessary. For example the bare Gaussian exp(-eta^2/(2h)) has character (-1)^N exp(-N eta), (5) not exp(-N eta). Such signs can cancel an actual half-step elsewhere in a complete kernel, but may not be removed from individual factors. For any winding n in Z^d, F_N(Z+2*pi*i*n)/F_N(Z) =exp[N n^t C Z+pi*i*N n^t C n+N b_N^t n] product_j(1-A_j)^(-epsilon_j a_j.n) =product_k chi_k^n_k. (6) The last equality uses n^t C n-sum_k n_k C_kk in 2Z. Thus the complete deck action is an algebraic character on the central torus, not only an infinitesimal semiclassical relation. Formula (6) fixes the integer Gaussian cocycle as well as its first generators. If a later elimination produces rational C or rational linear coordinates, (4) must be used on the corresponding integral cover or before that elimination. Clearing a common denominator and restricting to its integral deck sublattice is sufficient. This does not identify different logarithmic sheets of the original source. ## 2. The character-one equations are marked Frobenius gluing On a selected central logarithmic chart Y=Log X define W_cent,N(Y)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(Xi_j exp(a_j.Y)) +Y^t C Y/2+sum_k Log(gamma_k)Y_k. (7) The logarithms of gamma keep their specified marks from (4). Differentiation gives exp(partial_(Y_k) W_cent,N)=chi_k(X). (8) Consequently chi_k=1 is precisely the EXPONENTIAL marked gluing equation for this component. Its logarithmic lifts differ by the recorded multiples of 2*pi*i. This is an exact central identity at every N, before making a saddle approximation. The central variables X=exp(NZ) and the ordinary semiclassical shape variables exp Z are different. Equation (8) is not a convergence theorem between their evaluations, and does not put the selected source on chi=1. It specifies the Frobenius copy of the same monomial/dilogarithmic equations, with its actual norm and Gaussian marks retained. ## 3. The actual beta residue verifies the complete formula For the proved original trivalent section, put l=Log u, k=Log v. Its exact form is S_N=(N/phi_N)u^N exp[(l^2-kl)/h] Psi_+(k-l) Psi_+(h-l). (9) Here C=[[2,-1],[-1,0]], both atom signs are positive, and their rows are (-1,1),(-1,0). The exact h shift has central value one. The factor u^N is single-valued and stays in P_N; it has a genuine exponential rate but no deck character. Let U=u^N,V=v^N,A=U-V. Formula (4) becomes chi_u=A(U-1)/V, chi_v=1/A. (10) These are the independently derived exact beta deck multipliers. They are also the exponential derivatives of the classical marked phase after substituting the central variables. At chi_u=chi_v=1, the finite nonzero torus condition is simply A=1. The factor u^N is INVISIBLE in (10); its correct value was established by the separate original-source rigidity proof. Thus even this exact character calculation alone would not normalize the period. The untouched full-Psi atoms in the original scalar crossing obey (2) individually. The original continuous Gaussian of sign s is exp[-s eta_s^2/(2h)] with eta_s=sqrt(2*pi*i*s)xi; its character is (-1)^N exp(-sN eta_s). Equation (5) displays the positive case. In these respective coordinates the dilation atom rows remain integral. The new beta residue has precisely (9), including its rational prefactors after exact Q-tag shifts. Therefore all these actual components are covered by the SAME character rule before their original external integration. No alternative knot state is introduced. ## 4. Integral head gluing carries the characters exactly Suppose local component i has logarithmic arguments Z_i=L_i T+c_i, where L_i is an integer matrix describing its actual head and boundary monomials. Include all untouched atom, Gaussian and source factors. If T_k makes one full turn, factor i makes the integer winding L_i e_k. Therefore the geometric product has chi_total,k=chi_external,k product_i product_a chi_(i,a)^(L_i[a,k]). (11) This follows from exact meromorphic identities, so it does not require pairwise independence of monomial arguments, a nonsingular B block, or a saddle determinant. Equivalently substitute Z_i in (3): C_total=sum_i L_i^t C_i L_i and the atom incidence rows pull back by L_i. The linear terms include C_i c_i as well as the original b_i. Formula (4) for this substituted function is identical to (11), including the parity constants in (6). For the literal eligible crossing star u=z_4/z_1, v=x^(-1) z_4/z_0, its three head characters are z_4 turn: chi_u chi_v=(U-1)/V, z_1 turn: chi_u^(-1)=V/[A(U-1)], z_0 turn: chi_v^(-1)=A. (12) Their product is one, as required by invariance under simultaneous scaling of its three heads. They are generally not individually one. The central color x^N remains inside V; it is not specialized to a clock value merely because the finite head has dimension N. For a finite collection of pairwise disjoint eligible sink stars, the sink source has the tensor product presentation of the beta rank-two extensions, with its original exterior pairing. Formula (11) computes the character of the full selected component. The finite sink pointing product_i B_i, which also contains the current sectors, is invariant in its boundary monomials. Untouched full functions still have their own characters and matched relative cycles. Invariance of the sink pointing does NOT imply that its all-residue sector, or that sector times untouched fields, has character one. ## 5. What the central equations establish and what they do not On any stated actual phase graph, (8) and (11) provide the exact central norm equations whose classical gluing description has already been checked. An A-polynomial elimination must keep the same regular graph, peripheral marks and saturation divisors. Arbitrary denominator-cleared components are not restored by calling these equations Frobenius gluing. The theorem does not identify an eliminated curve with the selected minimal quantum A-operator or prove that its geometric branch contributes to the original scalar. The current extension and original relative integration class remain indispensable. In particular, the exact current can gain a nondegenerate geometric residue under a deck turn. Killing every current is not a source-preserving quotient even when a product character is one. The constructive output is explicit: the entire residue product's deck character and its character-one variety are known from the actual monomial incidence and Gaussian data. The missing global step concerns the selected marked relative class on that variety, not an unspecified central multiplier for each local beta section. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_psi_frobenius_deck_gluing.py) checks direct complete-function turns with both orientations, mixed integer Gaussian matrices, arbitrary integer windings, half-step and odd-Gaussian signs, the actual beta characters, and the literal three-head pullback. Finite checks supplement the exact identities (2)--(6), not a source-selection assertion. Cap factors are used as their complete finite polynomials or with their matched relative interval seams. No scalar character is assigned to an isolated fractional interval-density summand.

title: An absolute scalar full-Psi cycle for the original whole source
text: # An absolute scalar full-Psi cycle for the original whole source 28 October 2026. The [rational audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.py) and [certificates](../experiments/actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle_results.json) check 189 individual all-N atom capacities before and 189 after the Hardy-forest contraction, and 25 whole-network primal/dual radius solutions, with rational checks of every constraint and exact objective equality after recovery. These audit the general flow proof below; they are not a knot-family proof by examples. ## 1. The actual scalar kernels to which the theorem applies Subsequent exact simplification: [the cut-wall pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md) removes the remaining moment resolvents in favor of a bare full-Psi head period PLUS its explicit aggregate scalar cut-wall current. Insert scalar Hardy identities before/after elementary gates, in the same harmless initial chamber as before. All head variables are z_v. Each scalar atomic kernel is a positive/negative Euler coefficient generating kernel with a monomial argument. All can be expressed using v_(epsilon,N), with epsilon=+1 or -1: v_N(A)=v_(+,N)(A), u_N(A)=v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)A), F^(-1) diagonal: v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)z/w), F diagonal: N(z/w)^d v_(+,N)(Qw/z), d=N-1. (1) Thus a moment atom has argument A_j=kappa_j z^(v_j), where v_j has one +1 and one -1. The reflected factorial also has its original prefactor N(z/w)^d. The Q shifts are exact. Gaussian dilation kernels are ordinary Hardy kernels with coefficient g_s(x,y,xi)=-(xy)^(-s)exp(-s h/2) exp(sqrt(pi)(1+i s)xi), h=2*pi*i/N, s=+1 or -1. (2) They carry the exact Gaussian weight sqrt(N/(2*pi))exp(-Nxi^2/2). Every other spectator/reset is 1/(1-z_out/z_in). The physical cup/ordinary cap/original marked cap are exactly (4) of the coupled-cap note, including their distinct powers of N and color. The full marked row is restricted to D=d only by whole integer degree, as proved there; no Ward identity is reapplied to a summand. ## 2. Full-function moment chains, with no finite resolvent Let Psi_epsilon be precisely the full rational Faddeev function fixed in [the full-function source theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). For R>0 define the scalar functional M_(epsilon,R)[f]= (1/(2*pi)) integral_(-pi)^pi Psi_epsilon(log R+i epsilon theta) f(R exp(i epsilon theta)) dtheta -epsilon/(2*pi*i) integral_0^R Psi_epsilon(log r+i epsilon pi)(-r)^N f(-r) dr/r. The untruncated geometric kernel has no numerator 1-(A_j/t_j)^N and no matrix source. ## 3. Coefficient-independent continuous support Expand every ordinary Hardy kernel in nonnegative powers. Absolute convergence, including every original coupled cap Under (8) every geometric kernel has modulus at most (1-exp(-eta))^(-1).
