This proves the required Fubini; it is stronger than declaring a finite matrix-coefficient sum first. The exact interval sources of the coupled-cap theorem may be included as well. Choose principal Log r on its cut plane. Uniformly there, with its removable value at 1, |Log r/(r-1)| <=C(1+|log|r||) exp(-max(0,log|r|)). (14) Near 1 this follows from removability; for |r|>=2 or <=1/2 it is immediate, and the remaining compact annulus is bounded. On ANY fixed compact cap path with 0<=Re s<=1, |exp(Ns Log r)|<=exp(N max(0,log|r|)+C_path N). The one power lost in (14) changes N back to d=N-1. Hence the interval source obeys (13), up to a fixed product of logarithmic factors bounded by powers of 1+sum tau+sum|xi| using (12). Radial integrals of those logarithms still converge. Thus the real intervals and the compact complex cap paths inside the vertical strip have the SAME absolute convergence theorem. The generic simultaneous classical framing in the cap note puts all desired s_g in that strip. Source logarithmic cuts are matched exactly, rather than discarded. If L changes to L+2*pi*i, the difference of the two interval densities N L exp(NsL)/(exp L-1) is d_s { [exp(Ns(L+2*pi*i))-exp(NsL)]/(exp L-1) }. The primitive vanishes at both s=0 and s=1. Thus the seam is an exact relative interval derivative with fixed ends; it produces no extra period. This is the explicit scalar cut gluing needed when using the principal source chart in (14). ## 6. Exact equality with the original selected scalar If the interval presentation is used, first evaluate those intervals to recover their exact cap polynomials; the joint absolute bound permits this order. Then integrate the head circles in the convergent chamber. Expansion of their rational geometric kernels is absolutely convergent. By Section 3, only indices 0<=r_j<N survive the original source, so this head integral is a FINITE Laurent polynomial in the moment t_j^(-1). Apply (4) separately at every atom. Equations (1) recover the original finite Euler/factorial coefficients exactly, with all Q shifts and N factors. The joint Gaussian moments give the exact original Gaussian diagonal. All original Cartan, pivot, framing, modified-trace and peripheral lines remain attached once. Consequently, for every fixed signed physical word and its original selected plat source, P_(beta,N)=chi_(beta,N)(N/(2*pi))^(m/2) integral_R^m exp(-N||xi||^2/2) (tensor_j M_(epsilon_j,1)) [ integral_head_tori R_(beta,N)(z,t,xi) prod_v dz_v/(2*pi*i z_v) ] dxi. (15) Here R is the explicitly specified product of ordinary scalar Hardy kernels, original reflected monomials and the coupled sources, or their exact interval forms. Its number of variables is determined by the word and bridge count, independently of N. Equation (15) is a single tensor-product scalar RELATIVE cycle. Writing it as circle/ray pieces is optional bookkeeping, not a selection of a new invariant. In particular no exponentially large unspecified matrix source is hidden in (15). All possible exponential factors are explicit: full Psi functions, Gaussian weights, original monomial/interval phases, and the retained radial powers (-r)^N. Their cancellations are still part of the original problem. ## 7. What the pole pushforward does and does not prove The new atomic rational poles are t_j=A_j(z). Each is primitive and has scalar normal form dt_j/(t_j-A_j). With its induced orientation its residue is +1; their normals are independent because every t_j occurs in its own pole equation. The ordinary head Hardy poles have the already proved forest normal degree +1. At a regular local chart where these residue operations are allowed, the ALL-CIRCLE atomic residue branch has density the product of the full functions Psi_epsilon(Log A_j), with exactly the original reflected monomials, Gaussian and coupled caps. The complete relative source also has its retained ray-weighted pole and cut currents. Its full residue is not being identified with this single bare-function product. Using the uniform full-Psi symbol on its selected strip, its leading action is therefore the SAME signed sum of Li_2 and monomial/Gaussian terms computed in the Hardy-forest note. The exact Gaussian canonical graph and the actual fusion graphs give the actual framed Hurwitz holonomy. The cap equations are precisely the inverse-meridian locus proved in the coupled-cap note. This is a statement about the regular all-pole critical scheme, not existence of a global geometric cycle. The full functions are regular across the apparent interior cyclotomic roots on their selected strip; a positive geometric argument may have ANY modulus. Local residue/chart deformations may use that regularity while retaining every negative-ray and source-cut face in (3). Enlarging an outer radius is an exact moment-chain deformation, but its extra ray segment must be kept; for R>1 it need not be small. The known ordered support theorem can push the HEAD Hardy forest on every radially truncated cycle r_j>=delta>0, with all source-null negative currents retained first. Section 8 below proves the stronger fact that the reduced whole-source flow polytope is unchanged. Thus the reduced full-source cycle itself has the same absolute radial bound, without needing a new divergent-piece prescription. This does not permit deleting atomic ray/cut currents or independently assigning a period to a divergent separated negative-current component. Bare substitution remains false. For example the ordinary full-turn moment at a<N differs from the original v_a by its nonzero radial source E_a(R). Its small-radius leading term is E_a(R)=epsilon R^(N-a)/(2*pi*i*(N-a))+O_N(R^(N-a+1)|log R|). The logarithmic term t^N Log t has nonzero low Cauchy moments. It is not an integer high-degree tail annihilated by a head barrier. The explicit relative cycle (3), plus the flow-controlled radii, is the proved correction to that substitution. A further global pole pushforward must transport this whole relative class. Normal degree one of the all-pole graph does not determine its geometric-thimble coefficient and does not prove noncancellation of the original period. ## 8. The full-Psi cycle remains absolute after Hardy-forest contraction Contract all head-Hardy edges at their pole equations, including the Gaussian edges with their full g factors. Their graph is the forest already proved in the Hardy-reduction note. In a component, write z_v=c_v z_root, where c_v is its nonzero product of Gaussian dilation factors. Every remaining moment argument is still a primitive ratio of two DIFFERENT retained head segments. A transfer connects different heads; an active factorial connects the two segments it separates. Thus no atomic argument becomes a constant self-loop. There is an exact equality of CONTINUOUS route polytopes: reduced atom/cap flows <--> original atom/cap/head-Hardy flows. (16) Here the reduced constraints only require atom orders nonnegative and cup/cap orders in [0,d]; omitted head currents are not assumed nonnegative. To prove (16), first reconstruct the omitted currents as SIGNED real numbers. On each forest component, the contracted balance equation is exactly the compatibility condition for a unique solution of its tree incidence equations; solve from the leaves. These numbers are precisely the signed head indices in the ordered physical word. Suppose a reconstructed index first becomes negative. A diagonal preserves the index, and Gaussian dilation does too, so a lowering transfer must create it. There are only the following possibilities. * In C^(-1) it is the first head, whose following reciprocal first-head factorial forces the index to be nonnegative. * In the central transfer it is the second head, which the incoming reciprocal second-head factorial of C forces nonnegative before another transfer touches it. * In the final transfer of C it is the first head. At the next touching crossing it is either the second head, killed immediately by the incoming reciprocal factorial, or the first head, lowered before that crossing's reciprocal first-head factorial. An untouched negative head is incompatible with the final finite cap. These are inequality statements for real indices. They do not use integrality, coefficient cancellation, or a finite matrix norm. The initial cup and final cap indices are in [0,d]. Hence no reconstructed negative current is possible. All omitted head currents are nonnegative and (16) follows. The upper barriers of Section 3 then give atom order at most d and all head currents at most k d. The g factors introduce only explicit costs. If delta_v=log|c_v|, the reduced atomic coefficient log is ell_e+v_e.delta, the source monomial has its additional fixed term gamma.delta, and a cap edge has the same substitution. After reconstructing a flow, these costs sum to the original Gaussian/color costs by the tree balance equations. Their bound is still C_word N(1+sum|xi|). Apply exactly the duality of Section 4 to this reduced incidence matrix, now with ONLY atomic geometric kernels. Equations (11)--(14) hold unchanged. The graph has b+6m complex head coordinates, its original m continuous Gaussian variables and its original coupled sources. It has NO head-Hardy/reset kernels. The pure full-Psi moment cycle on this reduced graph is jointly absolutely convergent. For exact equality, perform the original forest annulus argument at every common radial cutoff delta>0. The initial and reduced whole-source cycles both satisfy the absolute bound above, so take delta to zero in those cycles. No separate convergence of an individually source-null annulus component is required or asserted. The audit contracts the literal time-layered head forest, drops ALL of its nonnegativity constraints, maximizes each reduced atom order, and reconstructs the unique omitted tree currents exactly.
