title: Exact fusion relates the right Euler operator to physical clocks
text: # Exact fusion relates the right Euler operator to physical clocks Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual two-leg fusion kernel gives an exact polynomial operator relation between the RIGHT lowering coefficient and physical/relative clocks. All nilpotent endpoints are retained. This provides a concrete coordinate relation for the Euler cap rather than guessing that its argument is a physical Fourier momentum. It does not yet supply a geometric period map or a selected geometric sector. ## 1. The actual finite kernel Use the [actual Borel fusion](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) on two nilpotent heads. Their highest K eigenvalues x,y are invertible. Set F_j=(Q;Q)_j, with Q of exact order N. Relative basis vectors are f^a e_j, where f is the TOTAL physical lowering operator acting on the LEFT. Their images under the actual fusion C are f^a(e_0 tensor e_j). In the physical basis (u,v), the kernel is exactly \[ C_{u,v;a,j}= \begin{cases} x^{u-a}\displaystyle\frac{F_aF_v}{F_{a-u}F_j}, &0\leq u\leq a,\quad v=j+a-u<N,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{1} \] To prove (1), write f=A_0+B_0 with A_0=F_1 and B_0=K_1 inverse F_2. Then B_0 A_0=Q A_0 B_0. In the q-binomial expansion of f^a, the term with u first-leg lowering steps has coefficient F_a/[F_u F_(a-u)]. Acting on the source gives F_u from the first leg, x^(u-a) from the K_1 inverses, and F_v/F_j from the second leg. Terms exceeding the second nilpotent head vanish. This gives (1) with no asymptotic step. In the ordering by a on the relative side and u on the physical side, C is upper block triangular. Its diagonal blocks are F_a times the identity. They are units, so C is invertible. The kernel depends on x, but not on y. Let D_a and D_j be the relative diagonal clocks Q^a and Q^j. Let U,V be the physical diagonal clocks Q^u and Q^v. Equation (1) immediately gives \[ C D_aD_j=UV C. \tag{2} \] ## 2. Right lowering and its exact clock equation Right multiplication R_f in the coefficient algebra is \[ R_f(f^a e_j)= \begin{cases}f^{a+1}e_{j-1\bmod N},&a<N-1,\\0,&a=N-1. \end{cases} \tag{3} \] This is different from physical total lowering, which is LEFT multiplication in the fused module. Define the transported operators \[ A=C D_a C^{-1},\qquad J=C D_j C^{-1},\qquad f_R=C R_f C^{-1}. \] Then the following are exact finite matrix identities: \[ \boxed{\quad x(1-U^{-1}A)f_R=(1-QA)(1-J),\qquad AJ=UV. \quad} \tag{4} \] They are not assertions merely about interior matrix entries. Before conjugating, the first identity reads \[ x C R_f-xQ U^{-1}C R_fD_a=C(1-QD_a)(1-D_j). \tag{5} \] For j>0 and a<N-1, use (1) at consecutive relative labels: \[ \frac{C_{u,v;a+1,j-1}}{C_{u,v;a,j}} =x^{-1}\frac{(1-Q^{a+1})(1-Q^j)}{1-Q^{a+1-u}}. \tag{6} \] The polynomial equation obtained by clearing the denominator in (6) is valid even when that denominator is zero. At the new support u=a+1, the left coefficient vanishes and the old kernel entry is zero. At any other excluded row both sides vanish. For j=0, R_f sends the second label to N-1. Its new kernel support is ONLY u=a+1,v=N-1. The left coefficient 1-Q^(a+1-u) is then zero, and the right side is zero because 1-Q^j=0. This is an actual wrapped endpoint, not a discarded row. For a=N-1 the left side is zero by (3), while the right side has factor 1-Q^N=0. These observations establish (5) on every matrix entry. Finally R_f D_a=Q^(-1)D_a R_f, so conjugating (5) gives the ordered equation in (4). Also, exactly, \[ [A,J]=0,\qquad A f_R=Q f_R A,\qquad J f_R=Q^{-1}f_R J. \tag{7} \] These follow directly from the relative basis, including its cyclic j endpoint, at the root Q^N=1. ## 3. The apparent denominator is nilpotent at the actual root It would be incorrect to divide the first equation in (4) by 1-U inverse A as an actual finite operator. In fact \[ (1-U^{-1}A)^N=0. \tag{8} \] Indeed C is upper block triangular with scalar diagonal blocks F_a. Conjugating D_a by C yields an upper block triangular A with diagonal blocks Q^u. Therefore U inverse A is upper block triangular with every diagonal block equal to one. Its difference from one is strictly upper block triangular, which proves (8). Thus (4) is an exact polynomial transport identity through this endpoint, not a rational inverse formula for f_R. It retains a singular clock divisor that a prospective period transform must handle. No scalar normalization removes (8). ## 4. A useful prospective principal relation, with its scope The [actual cap](actual_euler_cap_cauchy_boundary.md) uses the Euler argument x f in the RIGHT coefficient algebra. On a commutative principal-symbol chart associated with (4), that argument would satisfy \[ z(1-A/U)=(1-A)(1-J),\qquad AJ=UV. \tag{9} \] Where 1-A/U is invertible this can be written \[ z=\frac{(1-A)(1-J)}{1-A/U}. \tag{10} \] Equations (9)-(10) specify the algebraic symbol relation forced by the exact kernel. They do not prove that a particular semiclassical symbol chart exists for the full selected word, that it is symplectic, that z equals a geometric Fourier momentum, or that its divisor is traversed by the original source class. In particular (10) is NOT the finite root matrix equation, because of (8). This still makes a concrete step beyond the former unspecified right-Euler/physical-clock relation: the actual finite kernel and all its endpoint terms are now explicit. A geometric comparison must use this relation and the original cap, rather than silently replacing the cap argument by another momentum. ## 5. Truncated generic-Q kernel exposes a top-degree defect For a Q not satisfying Q^N=1, retain the SAME finite formula (1), provided F_1,...,F_(N-1) are units, and the SAME nilpotent shift (3). These are well-defined matrices, without claiming they form the actual generic-q word module. Let Pi_top project to a=N-1. The exact finite-kernel identity is now \[ \begin{aligned} x C R_f-xQ U^{-1}C R_fD_a &=C(1-QD_a)(1-D_j)\\ &\quad -(1-Q^N)C(1-D_j)\Pi_{\mathrm{top}}. \tag{11} \end{aligned} \] The same entry proof applies away from a=N-1, including j=0. At a=N-1 the left side vanishes by truncation. The correction in (11) subtracts exactly the nonzero right side there. Consequently the root identity has a visible normal endpoint term before root specialization. Dividing (11) by 1-Q^N and discarding its last term would change the kernel calculation. This is only a statement about this explicit finite kernel; it does not provide a moving-q extension of actual braid intertwining, fusion of divided powers, or the original whole q-normal source. Those further comparisons remain necessary. ## 6. Exact checks The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_fusion_right_euler_clock_results.json) pass at N=2,...,9 with unequal x=3,y=7. At each actual root they compare (1) to the literal coproduct fusion matrix and check (2), (4), (7), (8). Eight additional generic-Q kernel cases check the full nonzero endpoint correction (11). The all-level entry proofs above establish the theorem; these exact checks verify its conventions and endpoints.

title: A selected actual gauge period evaluates fixed observables at the algebraic point 2
text: # A selected actual gauge period evaluates fixed observables at the algebraic point 2 27 October 2026. An actual source period now gives a direct local instance of the proposed quantum-period-to-algebraic-point mechanism. For the canonical primitive gauge g_N, its top-coefficient period, normalized by its EXPLICIT Gauss period, converges on every fixed polynomial observable to evaluation at z=2. Its universal moment recursion and finite cyclic source are exact. This is a proved selection statement for this local gauge period, rather than only the construction of a formal critical branch. The observable degree must be independent of N. The transformed full knot word does not satisfy that restriction automatically. This does not identify the knot's quantum A-module or prove a new knot-volume limit. It supplies one fully sourced local comparison which a whole-word construction may try to extend. ## 1. The actual period and its known normalization Let Q=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2, and let g_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)c_r z^r be the CANONICAL nilpotent polynomial of the primitive source gauge v_N(z)v_N(Qz), as in [the actual gauge theorem](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md). For a polynomial P define the actual linear period I_N(P)=[z^(N-1)] P(z)g_N(z), c_N=I_N(1)=c_(N-1). (1) The [exact resonant calculation](actual_primitive_gauge_resonant_endpoint.md) proves, including all endpoint terms, c_N=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(-1)^rQ^(r(r-1)/2) =omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N), omega_N=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)/4-pi*i/(4N)]. (2) Thus c_N is nonzero for all sufficiently large N and its modulus is polynomially bounded above and below. Normalizing by c_N uses this evaluated universal Gauss period. It does NOT divide by the unknown knot invariant or choose its exponential normalization. This is a sourced period of the same actual coefficient algebra. For example it is realized by the original two-leg Euler cap with its explicit insertion b=J_Q(z)^-1 P(z)g_N(z), apart from the already specified cap scalar and the conversion f=z/x. No new invariant is defined by (1). ## 2. An exact period Ward identity and a two-generator module The UNREDUCED polynomial identity is (1-z)(1-Qz)g_N(Qz)-g_N(z) =-(2/N)z^N+c_N z^(N+1). (3) Multiplying by any polynomial P and extracting degree N-1 kills the right side. Rescaling the coefficient variable therefore gives the exact source identity I_N[Q^-1 P(Q^-1z)(1-Q^-1z)(1-z)-P(z)]=0. (4) Put i_m=I_N(z^m), using the UNWRAPPED nonnegative degree m. Then (4) is the N-independent recursion i_(m+2)=(1+Q)i_(m+1)+(Q^(m+2)-Q)i_m, i_0=c_N, i_1=(1+Q)c_N-2Q/N. (5) The second initial value follows from the degree-N relation in (3). Degrees m>=N give i_m=0, consistently with (5); no cyclic identification of that degree has been made. Define universal integer polynomials H_m(Q),R_m(Q) by H_0=1, H_1=1+Q, R_0=0, R_1=-2Q, F_(m+2)=(1+Q)F_(m+1)+(Q^(m+2)-Q)F_m (6) for either F=H or F=R. Induction in the exact recurrence gives I_N(z^m)=H_m(Q)c_N+R_m(Q)/N (7) for EVERY m>=0. Thus every fixed polynomial period is an explicit linear combination of TWO known source periods, c_N and 1/N. The coefficients in (6) are independent of level. This is stronger than a purely formal large-N moment calculation. An independent coefficient proof can be useful. For 0<=m<N, the root factorial reflection gives c_(N-1-m)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1-m) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2)(Q^(r+1);Q)_m. Expanding its finite product and using t_r Q^(sr)=(-1)^s Q^(-s(s-1)/2)t_(r+s) gives H_m(Q)=sum_(s=0)^m Q^s {m choose s}_Q, |I_N(z^m)-H_m(Q)c_N|<=m 2^m/N. (8) For the last estimate compare each shifted Gauss interval with the full interval: at most m terms are missing, all of modulus one. The Gaussian binomial has nonnegative integer polynomial coefficients with total binomial(m,s), so its modulus on |Q|=1 is at most that number. Equations (5)-(8) agree exactly. ## 3. The selected leading symbol is evaluation at 2 At Q=1 the universal coefficients obey H_m(1)=2^m, R_0(1)=0, R_m(1)=-2^m for m>=1. (9) For a FIXED polynomial P, with coefficients independent of N, (7)-(9) and Q_N=1+O(1/N) therefore imply I_N(P)=P(2)c_N+[P(0)-P(2)]/N+O_P(N^(-3/2)), (10) I_N(P)/I_N(1)=P(2)+O_P(N^(-1/2)). (11) The constants may depend on that fixed polynomial. In particular P(2)!=0 proves nonvanishing for all sufficiently large N. If P(2)=0 and P(0)!=0, the boundary period 1/N is instead leading. If both vanish, (10) only gives the indicated smaller-order bound; it is not a nonvanishing claim. The classical limit of the actual Ward relation (4) is ((1-z)^2-1)P(z)=z(z-2)P(z). Its two algebraic support points are 0 and 2. The ACTUAL Gauss normalization and moments select the point 2. Consequently the map in (11) is asymptotically multiplicative on every fixed polynomial window: both P and PR are evaluated at 2. No regular map from the nilpotent finite algebra to that point is asserted. This is a genuinely nonlocal period selection: the coefficient degree increases with N. Directly specializing the finite nilpotent generator to the scalar 2 would be invalid. The period calculation supplies the comparison instead. The exact rational endpoint observable (1-z)^-1, interpreted by its Taylor expansion at zero before coefficient extraction, also fits this picture in this particular case: I_N((1-z)^-1)=g_N(1)=2/N-c_N. Its leading value is -1=1/(1-2). This assertion follows from the separately proved exact endpoint identity, not from extending (11) to every rational function without a new estimate. ## 4. The leading period also intertwines ordered gauge meridian steps Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. For any FIXED integer r use the actual primitive gauge increment D_r(z)=g_N(q^r z)/g_N(z) in z^N=0. (12) All quotients are units in that algebra, with canonical normal forms. Positive r gives the ordered product of the actual M->qM gauge increments; negative r uses their genuine inverses. The [whole-word gauge theorem](whole_word_primitive_source_gauge.md) proves the r=1 increment before any endpoint evaluation. Exactly, I_N(P D_r)=q^(r(N-1)) I_N(P(q^-r z)). (13) Indeed D_r g_N=g_N(q^r z) modulo z^N; multiplying by a polynomial P and extracting degree N-1 gives (13) by rescaling the variable. The source phase q^(r(N-1))=(-1)^r q^-r is retained. It cannot be replaced by one before evaluation. Combining (11) with (13) gives the sourced meridian relation I_N(P D_r)/c_N -> (-1)^r P(2). (14) This extends to every fixed finite Ore observable Ahat=sum_r P_r(q,z) T^r, Tz=qzT, T(g_N)(z)=g_N(qz), where the r range and polynomial degrees in z are independent of N, and the coefficient functions are regular at q=1. Define its actual period by I_N[(Ahat g_N)/g_N]. Then I_N[(Ahat g_N)/g_N]/c_N -> sum_r (-1)^r P_r(1,2). (15) The limit is a character of the commutative symbol algebra at (z,T)=(2,-1). Products of any two such fixed observables stay in the same class, and the Ore coefficient shifts q^r z tend to z, so the leading evaluation is multiplicative as well. This is an actual local period/connection comparison, not only moment evaluation. The meridian steps here are the GAUGE PART of the knot's transport. Fusion, actual word coefficients and the full peripheral line remain separate data. The gauge wave equation itself has the fixed operator [(1-z)(1-Qz)T^2-1]g_N=0 modulo z^N, whose unreduced source is (3). Its classical symbol is (1-z)^2 T^2-1; the selected character (2,-1) lies on it. It is not the knot's quantum A-polynomial. ## 5. The moment recursion has a retained cyclic source For reference set X_m=Q^m and let E raise m. Then EX=QXE, and (5) is the actual local source recursion P_cap=E^2-(1+Q)E+Q(1-QX). (16) Its ordinary commutative symbol is (E-1)^2-X. At X=1 the two roots are 0 and 2; the selected branch in (11) is the unit root 2. This is a recursion of the universal cap-gauge moments. The index m is observable degree, NOT the knot's meridian color, and P_cap is not identified with its quantum A-polynomial. Folding i_0,...,i_(N-1) into a cyclic array changes (16). The exact cyclic residual is (P_cap i)_m=c_N delta_(m,N-2) -(2Q/N)delta_(m,N-1). (17) For m<N-2 use (5). At m=N-2 the wrapped i_N contributes c_N in place of zero. At m=N-1 the wrapped i_(N+1) and i_N give i_1-(1+Q)i_0=-2Q/N. This proves (17), also at N=2. The finite cyclic source cannot be erased by calling (12) an unpointed homogeneous spectral equation. The Gauss period and its smaller boundary term are its specified source data. ## 6. Its root norm curve is exactly its classical curve, with the source retained The moment recursion in (16) has companion matrix C(X)=[[0,1],[-Q(1-QX),1+Q]], V_(m+1)=C(Q^m X)V_m. Let H_N(X)=C(Q^(N-1)X)...C(X) be its forward cyclic monodromy. Its characteristic polynomial is EXACTLY det(v-H_N)=(v-1)^2-U, U=X^N, (18) at every level. This is the same polynomial as the classical symbol of (16), after identifying its central variables with the classical variables. No conjectural norm-curve equality is used to obtain it. Here is a direct proof. The determinant is the full product det H_N=product_(j=0)^(N-1)Q(1-Q^(j+1)X) =1-X^N. The trace is invariant under X->QX by cyclic conjugacy wherever C(X) is invertible, hence as a polynomial identity. In a closed walk contributing to the trace, each occurrence of the X-dependent lower-left edge must be paired with an upper-right edge. Thus the trace has degree at most floor(N/2)<N. A Q-invariant polynomial of that degree is constant. At X=0 the companion has eigenvalues 1,Q, so its Nth power has trace 2. This gives (18), including composite levels and all determinant zeros. The selected finite source still matters. At X=1 its nonzero initial vector is V_0=(c_N,(1+Q)c_N-2Q/N)^t. The exact unwrapped moments give V_N=(i_N,i_(N+1))=0, so H_N(1)V_0=0. (19) It is in the central v=0 kernel, while the leading fixed-degree period in (11) selects the classical point z=2. The two facts refer to different selections: finite cyclic monodromy of the sourced state and the leading local observable period. They cannot be identified merely because the two defining curves in (18) agree. The singular orbit and the source in (17) must be retained. In particular the generic invertible norm-torsor description alone does not extend through this v=0 fiber. This is an explicit, fully evaluated local example of both norm-curve compatibility AND its limitations for selected periods. It is not an assertion of either compatibility or a particular central character for the knot's own quantum A-module. ## 7. The selected action and prefactor have a marked dilogarithm calibration The exact Gauss proof identifies the period, its phase and its nonzero prefactor. There is a compatible classical critical-action calibration. For coefficient extraction I_N(1) the relevant action in the logarithmic coordinate x=Log z is S(z)=2Li_2(z)-2pi*i Log z. Continue from the unit disk to 2 through the upper half-plane. Then Log(1-2)=-pi*i, and the elementary dilogarithm reflection identity gives Li_2(2+i0)=pi^2/4+pi*i log 2, S(2)=pi^2/2, D_z S(2)=0, D_z^2 S(2)=-4. (20) Here D_z=z partial_z. The phase exp[S(2)/h], h=2pi*i/N, is exactly exp[-pi*i*N/4], the leading phase of c_N in (2). The measure also matters: [z^(N-1)] is the Cauchy measure dz/z^N, so choosing the above action leaves amplitude z dx, with value 2 at the saddle. A quadratic Fresnel calculation with that amplitude and Hessian -4 gives exp[-pi*i*N/4] exp[-pi*i/4]/sqrt(N), again the actual leading Gauss prefactor. Omitting the amplitude z would lose a factor two. This is an independently matched action/density calibration. The Gauss argument proves selection and the asymptotic directly; no unproved deformation of an analytic dilogarithm contour beyond the established small-disk chart is used as its proof. At this real shape 2 the Bloch--Wigner value is zero: its Li_2 imaginary part cancels Log|2| Arg(1-2). Thus this local source comparison has zero volume rate and does not introduce a knot's hyperbolic volume by interpreting a gauge-chart value as that volume. ## 8. Scope for the general torsor program This proves the requested kind of algebraic leading-period mechanism in a real local part of the original source: a quantum Ward module, a selected period, an algebraic critical point and a nonvanishing criterion P(2)!=0, with known polynomially sized normalization and all cyclic source terms retained. It does not prove that the FULL transformed word, whose degree and number of entries grow with N, has such a fixed presentation. It does not intertwine the knot's meridian insertion with this degree recursion. It does not identify the point 2 with a geometric knot holonomy or assign it a positive hyperbolic volume. The leading hyperbolic action and global sector cancellation remain the original open problem. Nor may (11) be naively extended to Laurent observables: the formal coefficient of z^-1 g_N at degree N-1 is zero, rather than (1/2)c_N. Rational localization needs a sourced period construction; it is not inversion of a nilpotent finite matrix. Even rational expressions regular at 2 need their actual source lattice. For example (3) gives EXACTLY I_N(J_Q)=Q^-1 c_N, I_N((1-z)^-2)=c_N+(1-Q)g_N(Q). The second identity follows by differentiating (3) at z=1 and using I_N((1-z)^-2)=N g_N(1)-g_N'(1). These rational functions have the same classical expression (1-z)^-2 but different quantum pole arrangements. The displayed additional endpoint term is not controlled by the fixed-polynomial theorem. Its vanishing or size cannot be assumed from pointwise convergence of the two rational expressions away from their poles. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_gauge_critical_evaluation.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_gauge_critical_evaluation_results.json) check the exact moment, two-period and cyclic-source equations at finite-field roots. High-precision fixed-degree samples diagnose the proved algebraic evaluation limit.

title: The actual Gauss-wall co-source and its relative cut-current map
text: # The actual Gauss-wall co-source and its relative cut-current map Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual coherent kernel determines both anchored Gauss-wall co-sources explicitly. Their difference is the original selected trace class, not zero. The two corresponding finite cut-current maps have a shared binomial wall row and two literal endpoint corrections. They glue exactly on every actual zero-extended Green array. This constructs an actual finite relative current map for the cut direction. It also identifies a definite nonzero boundary class which two Weyl charts cannot erase. It does not identify the internal Gaussian images of the remaining currents with these finite co-sources, or select a geometric global contribution. ## 1. The literal coherent kernel has two anchored wall primitives Let N>=2, n=N-1, and use the actual compact source with T=v a, Omega_0=dv wedge da=-dT wedge dlog v, f_C(v,T)=sum_(i,j=0)^n C_ij binom(n,j) v^(i-j)T^j(1-T)^(n-j). (1) This is the actual matrix symbol, written on v!=0. It includes the full weighted-word and Green-current matrices before any scalar projection. The normalized compact period is Tr(C)/N. On the resolved framing threefold retain nu_cut=-(d eta/eta) wedge Omega_0/(1-eta v), D_cut={1-eta v=0}, E={eta=0}. On the Gauss wall, eta=1/v, so D_cut=C^*_v times A^1_T, Res_(D_cut)(f_C nu_cut)=-f_C(v,T)dT wedge dlog v. (2) Here f_C nu_cut is the explicit source-kernel lift of the known principal framing form. It is not silently identified with an internal Gaussian current. Define the two actual anchored primitives on D_cut by zeta_C^+=-sum_(i,j) C_ij binom(n,j)v^(i-j) [integral_0^T t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt]dlog v, zeta_C^-=+sum_(i,j) C_ij binom(n,j)v^(i-j) [integral_T^1 t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt]dlog v. (3) Polynomial antiderivation proves `d zeta_C^+=d zeta_C^-=(2)`. The lower primitive is marked to vanish at T=0 and the upper one at T=1. Their difference is exactly zeta_C^--zeta_C^+ =(1/N)sum_(i,j) C_ij v^(i-j)dlog v. (4) Indeed `binom(n,j) integral_0^1 t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt=1/N`. Every off-diagonal term in (4) is exact on C^*, with primitive `C_ij v^(i-j)/[N(i-j)]`. Therefore its full boundary class is [zeta_C^--zeta_C^+] =(Tr(C)/N)[dlog v] in H^1(D_cut). (5) This is a concrete Cech obstruction to choosing a common anchored primitive. For the actual closed knot cut C=F_N(Y)I, it is exactly `F_N(Y)dlog v`. This is nonzero as a whole meridian family at every level, since the original ordinary-color anchor gives F_N(Q_N)=1. A particular complete value K_N can still vanish. Two Weyl charts alone cannot turn (5) into zero while retaining the actual selected source class. ## 2. The wall co-sources are exact positive finite matrix rows On the intersection loop of the actual radial normal homotopy, T=1/2 and v=exp(i phi), integration of (3) gives integral_C zeta_C^+=-c lambda_N^+(C), integral_C zeta_C^-=+c lambda_N^-(C), c=2pi*i. (6) The two functionals are literal diagonal matrix rows lambda_N^+(C)=sum_(j=0)^n w_(N,j) C_jj, w_(N,j)=binom(n,j)integral_0^(1/2)t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt =[1/(N 2^N)]sum_(r=j+1)^N binom(N,r), lambda_N^-(C)=Tr(C)/N-lambda_N^+(C). (7) The finite binomial identity in (7) follows by differentiating the indicated binomial tail in its upper limit; its value at zero fixes the integration constant. Thus no unknown knot period is used to define these co-sources. All weights are positive and lambda_N^+(I)=lambda_N^-(I)=1/2, w_(N,n-j)=1/N-w_(N,j). (8) Let W_M be the actual root Weyl operator, with its retained diagonal coefficients and index reversal. Conjugation reverses the diagonal entries, so exactly lambda_N^+(W_M C W_M^(-1))=lambda_N^-(C). (9) This functional identity holds generically and extends on the paired fractional source lattices at a resonance. It does not assert that W_M acts on every coherent coordinate by a classical Mobius transformation. Off-diagonal angular weights in (6) have been integrated explicitly. Every full-head Gamma/frame comparison in the current source theorems is diagonal. Its conjugation commutes with both weight matrices in (7), so both co-sources are invariant under it on all matrices. The bounded Gamma source comparison transports the wall charge; it cannot discard it. For the actual closed knot they return F_N(Y)/2 each, including the original full external phase and modified dimension if it is restored. ## 3. A literal cut difference has a shared degree-elevated wall row Let J_j be any finite zero-extended actual cut-current array, and take the literal shift `(S J)_j=J_(j+1)`. Define the degree-elevated wall co-source B_N(J)=[1/(N2^N)]sum_(j=0)^N binom(N,j)J_j. (10) The j=N value is retained. It lies outside the original head and can occur in the shifted currents even though the original state is supported in 0,...,n. Extend the head rows (7) by zero outside that interval. Direct summation by parts gives lambda_(N,head)^+((S-1)J)= B_N(J)-J_0/N, lambda_(N,head)^-((S-1)J)=-B_N(J)+J_N/N. (11) For example the backward difference of the positive head weights is the binomial row, except for the additional -1/N at j=0. This proves (11) including all shifted endpoints. Equivalently use the explicit finite relative extensions lambda_(N,rel)^+(J) =lambda_(N,head)^+(J)+(1/N)sum_(j<0)J_j, lambda_(N,rel)^-(J) =lambda_(N,head)^-(J)+(1/N)sum_(j>=N)J_j. (12) The sums are finite on the actual Green arrays. They agree with (7) on every original head-supported state and satisfy lambda_(N,rel)^+((S-1)J)=+B_N(J), lambda_(N,rel)^-((S-1)J)=-B_N(J), lambda_(N,rel)^++lambda_(N,rel)^- =(1/N)sum_(all j). (13) Thus the two chart currents glue exactly through the SAME wall row. Their endpoint counterterms are specified by (11), not assigned by a generic relative-cohomology existence theorem. The source degree in (10) has a precise meaning. On a source space of dimension N+1 with the ordinary coherent degree N, B_N(J)=(1/N)sigma_(diag(J_0,...,J_N))(T=1/2). (14) This is an ordinary coherent source-current realization, not an assertion that the knot representation has changed color. In particular an N-dimensional head row alone cannot replace the j=N endpoint in (10). ## 4. The exact least-moment Green certificate maps to this relative complex The original arrays of [the full Green certificate](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md) already contain their prescribed 1/N. Write them as I_raw and J_(i,raw). Before using the matrix-normalized rows (7), define explicitly I_mat=N I_raw, J_(i,mat)=N J_(i,raw). (14a) The same pointwise Green identity holds for these rescaled arrays, since every external coefficient and shift commutes with N. Summing the noncut indices gives exactly the actual cut diagonal C_jj from I_mat, and J_cut below always means the corresponding J_mat sum. Thus the actual selected scalar is `(1/N)sum_j I_mat,j=sum_j I_raw,j`. This rescaling does not change the state; it aligns its original normalized array with its coherent matrix coefficient. Apply (11)--(13) coefficientwise to I_mat and J_mat. The weights depend only on the cut index. They commute with every other flow translation, with coupling derivatives in those other variables, and with its external meridian Ore operators. Cut-index moment factors remain inside J itself. Thus the cut divergence maps to the explicit wall row (10), while all other unsummed flow divergences remain literal currents. In particular first sum only the actual finite transverse indices, leaving the cut j and the other framing index k. Denote the resulting matrix-normalized arrays by calI and calJ_1,calJ_2. The exact least-moment certificate becomes the specified two-current identity (-1)^h A_alpha lambda_(N,rel)^+(calI) = B_N(calJ_1)+(S_k-1)lambda_(N,rel)^+(calJ_2), (-1)^h A_alpha lambda_(N,rel)^-(calI) =-B_N(calJ_1)+(S_k-1)lambda_(N,rel)^-(calJ_2). (14b) Thus one framing divergence has been converted into a concrete degree-elevated wall row with its endpoints retained. This is a finite source/current pushforward, not a replacement of the finite transverse sum by the internal formal Gaussian. The second divergence in (14b) has not been assigned an unjustified Weyl action. After summing the noncut finite indices, write J_cut for the resulting matrix-normalized cut current. Since the original unweighted closed cut is scalar, each hemisphere evaluates the original state to F_N/2. The actual scalar annihilator therefore implies B_N(J_cut)=0, (15) with its full shifted endpoint convention. This is an exact finite source constraint, not an inference from a locally nonzero or zero Gaussian coefficient. The two charts' signed wall sources cancel in (13) even before using (15). Equivalently one may keep raw arrays throughout and use the rows N lambda_N^+, N lambda_N^- and N B_N. In that convention the endpoint counterterms are exactly J_(cut,raw,0) and J_(cut,raw,N), since `J_mat/N=J_raw`. The coefficient N in this equivalence is essential and is not suppressed. For the second external framing index one still has a literal finite zero-extended sum and its endpoint currents. It is not an extra independent cut color. The actual Weyl identity (9) does not automatically act on that transfer index. An auxiliary second Bernstein source can encode its finite sum, but calling its reflection the actual quantum Weyl action would require a new network/current map. Neither (9) nor (15) supplies that identification after transverse Gaussian contraction. ## 5. The shared wall row has a macroscopic entropy phase Its coefficient at j/N=T in an interior real interval obeys (1/N)Log[binom(N,j)/2^N] =-Tlog T-(1-T)log(1-T)-log2+O(log N/N). (16) The elementary integral bounds for log(N!) give this uniformly on compact subintervals of (0,1). This real phase has a unique maximum at T=1/2 and second derivative -1/[T(1-T)]. Thus the row (10) is not an arbitrary order-one amplitude in a formal Gaussian comparison: it can localize and lift one framing direction. Its total positive weight is 1/N, but that alone does not bound a cancellation-prone Green current or an unknown selected knot sum. On the physical logarithmic section, T=1/2 has A_cut=-1, a regular complete framing. At the wall D_cut itself, however, A_cut=(1-eta v)^(-1) is infinite. The radial normal homotopy shares the base latitude T=1/2 while moving between those different normal points. The binomial row alone does not identify them without the relative normal-chain data. It does not prove that the remaining internal geometric critical point lies on the selected global source cycle, or that all other critical and escaping pieces are absent. ## 6. What is still unmatched The two source charts, their complete relative endpoint map, the degree-elevated wall row, and the nonzero Cech class (5) are now explicit for every actual finite source and Green current. They retain all marked Weyl/Gamma factors and can be computed before any partial trace or meridian specialization. The missing comparison is specific: the internal Gaussian pushforward of the actual currents must carry the rows `J_0/N`, `J_N/N`, and B_N(J), including their entropy phase, to the corresponding geometric endpoint and wall functionals. The second framing direction additionally needs an actual pre-collapse source map. Declaring those currents exact or identifying two abstract Borel actions does not compute it. In particular the known principal residue equality does not identify the lifted f_C nu_cut with every higher Gaussian current. The present construction does not claim that further map, nonzero selected geometric microstalk, a full scalar geometric-factor theorem, or a volume limit. ## 7. Exact audit [audit_actual_gauss_wall_cut_current.py](../experiments/audit_actual_gauss_wall_cut_current.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_gauss_wall_cut_current_results.json) verify the incomplete-beta/binomial coefficients, Weyl complement and half normalizations, both head endpoint terms, and the complete zero-extended relative Green maps over Q for N=2 through 16. The current values are independent symbols, including both endpoint tails. All matrix-unit wall primitives and their Cech difference are checked at sizes 2 through 6. An additional entropy-phase grid checks the scale in (16). The proof is uniform in N and in the actual matrix coefficients; these checks are not knot examples and assume no selected asymptotic or quantum-to-Gaussian current identification.

title: The original Gaussian resolvent has a positive numerator and a controlled closing cap
status: Exact full numerator; controlled root Gaussian closing cap
text: # The original Gaussian resolvent has a positive numerator and a controlled closing cap 31 October 2026. The exact original numerator has a positive path expansion and a Fejer all-color formula, while the Gaussian resolvent has a subexponential closing cap at +2. No global contour selection, source asymptotic or generic-q continuation of the Gaussian is asserted. ## 1. Inputs already proved in the repository [actual matching edge continuant operator period](actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md) gives the actual generic tridiagonal blocks, both continuants, all Jordan poles and the true physical high-total adapter. [actual casimir off spectrum prefix action](actual_casimir_off_spectrum_prefix_action.md) and [actual matching edge cross central green action](actual_matching_edge_cross_central_green_action.md) give selected logarithmic actions only on strict physical prefix/row compacts. They do not cover arbitrary complex magnetic heads, midpoint prefixes or a global contracted exterior. The latter theorem is explicitly an integrand theorem. [actual casimir endpoint resolvent bound](actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.md) bounds EVERY original block by CN^17 at +2 and on |sigma-2|<=cN^-18, including genuine resolvent normals. The stronger [actual casimir closing region bound](actual_casimir_closing_region_bound.md) gives, for fixed gamma>0, throughout the angular cone sigma=2+r exp(i phi), |phi|<=pi-gamma, ||(sigma-Omega)^-1|| <= CN^3 exp[CN f(r)+C log^2 N], f(r)=sqrt(r) log(2+1/r). It includes every physical degree and all fixed genuine RESOLVENT jets. Thus the +2 joining region was already controlled; it must not be reported as an unresolved endpoint estimate. The new exact all-integer Gaussian uses the full Hermite data: R^n=q^(n d^2/4) f_n(Omega), f_n(sigma)=exp[n N K(sigma)/(4pi i)], K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2, chi_N(sigma)=2T_N(sigma/2)+2, V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega)^-1. K is analytic on C minus [2,infinity), removable at -2. This equality is at the original root; it does not identify an arbitrary off-root R germ. The homogeneous source applies coefficient extraction to the ordered product of these local functions, retaining all original targets and the unit q^(n d^2/4). No additional N or marked scalar is introduced by this functional calculus. ## 2. A direct Gaussian consequence for the entire closing cap On either side of the K slit near +2, K(sigma)=-pi^2+O(sqrt(|sigma-2|)), |f_n(sigma)|<=exp[C |n| N sqrt(|sigma-2|)]. The estimate is uniform on either slit side, including its boundary values. Therefore the old whole-cone resolvent bound gives ||f_n(sigma)(sigma-Omega)^-1|| <=CN^3 exp[CN(f(r)+|n|sqrt(r))+C log^2 N]. (1) For every FIXED integer n this has vanishing exponential rate as r->0. It also holds with fixed genuine q derivatives on the resolvent ALONE, using the old resolvent product rule. Those are not advertised as genuine derivatives of R^n. There is an actual joining path in the Gaussian slit. Run inward on the two rays sigma=2-r exp(+/-i gamma), down to radius rho_N=min(cN^-18,r_N/2) when the outer radius is r_N, and join them by the short LEFT arc of that circle. The rays are covered by (1). The left arc is in the old polynomial endpoint disk and lies to the RIGHT of the largest spectral node, whose distance from 2 is comparable to N^-2. It never crosses the K cut. On that arc |f_n|=exp[O(|n|N sqrt(rho_N))] and the full resolvent is polynomial. The cap therefore has rate at most C[f(r)+|n|sqrt(r)], and any r_N->0 yields exp[o(N)] for fixed n. This establishes only the closing portion of a contour, with no estimate for its surrounding source contraction. ## 3. Exact positivity of the FULL homogeneous resolvent numerator Use distinct names B,C for the two middle face weights. In the proved source polynomial representation, Omega=-T acts on z^j, 0<=j<N, by Omega z^j=c_j z^j-b_j(x+y)z^(j-1)-e_j xy z^(j-2), c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), b_j=4sin^2(j pi/N), e_j=4sin(j pi/N)sin((j-1)pi/N). Here b_0=e_0=e_1=0 and all allowed lowering weights are nonnegative. These are the original endpoint factors, not cyclic replacements. Expand the resolvent by ALL finite downward paths from j to i, using steps one or two. A path with k steps visits k+1 distinct row indices. Multiplication by chi_N removes precisely those k+1 factors, with their multiplicities even when eigenvalues coincide. Its numerator is (-1)^k (positive step weight) product_(unvisited r)(sigma-c_r). At sigma=-2-u, u>=0, the product has sign (-1)^(d-k). Consequently P_N(u;x,B,C,y):=(-1)^d H_(V_N(-2-u))(x,B,C,y) is a polynomial with NONNEGATIVE coefficients in all FIVE variables u,x,B,C,y. Its face degree remains d. The same original homogeneous adapter is used, including C^(d-j) for the initial degree j. For every complex sigma, |H_(V_N(sigma))|_coef <= P_N(|sigma+2|;x,B,C,y). (2) The inequality is termwise in face coefficients, since |sigma-c_r|<=|sigma+2|+2+c_r. It controls the entire polynomial numerator, including its independent semisimple data; no interpolation from only the complete-channel values was used. Cauchy on a fixed spectral disk also controls spectral derivatives by the same positive regularization with an enlarged radius. The spectral total-derivative identity supplied independently by cluster is compatible with this statement. Its paired data involve BOTH V(c) and V'(c); the latter cannot be recovered by differentiating a root-only complete-channel simplification. There is an exact Fejer normalization of the endpoint coupon. With T=-Omega, define F_N(X)=(T_N(X)-1)/(X-1), using the polynomial quotient. Then (-1)^d V_N(-2)=F_N(T/2) =N+2 sum_(j=1)^(N-1)(N-j) T_j(T/2) =L_N+2 sum_(h=1)^(N-1)L_h. (2a) The first equality follows by dividing chi_N(sigma)-chi_N(-2) by sigma+2 and using T_N(-X)=(-1)^N T_N(X). The other two follow from the finite cosine telescope. This is a coherent identity in the actual Casimir quotient, not positivity of the separate L_h coupons. It makes the extra semisimple endpoint data completely explicit. No existing Fejer-named note was found in the repository search. More generally the divided Chebyshev identity gives EXACTLY (-1)^d V_N(-2cosh w) =L_N+2 sum_(h=1)^(N-1) cosh((N-h)w)L_h. (2b) For example, subtract 2T_N(t/2) from 2T_N(s/2), divide by s-t, and expand in U_(h-1)(t/2); then set s=-2cosh w and t=Omega=-T. This is a polynomial identity in s,t, so it includes coincident nodes and all Hermite derivatives. The homogeneous coupon map and the whole original marked contraction preserve it linearly. For a set E of spectral ports, the contracted product of these signed numerators is consequently the exact finite sum over 1<=h_e<=N of the original external-color source, with weights 1 at h_e=N and 2cosh((N-h_e)w_e) at h_e<N. Every retained crossing on a complementary port remains in its actual order. There is no free interpolation or new mark. At a V-only selected port the coupon is literally L_h, with no newly inserted half crossing. If an original R^epsilon is retained separately at that same port, it multiplies BOTH sides of (2b) in its original order. Thus the shared numerator-capacity problem is concretely an exponential generating transform of ALL original colors. The existing small-deficit corridor controls only h_e close to N; neither (2b) nor path positivity supplies the missing phase-sensitive far-color bound. ## 4. Parity and an explicit limitation of a numerator norm argument For odd N, -2 is a simple node and V_N(-2)=N^2 P_simple=N L_(N,simple). For even N=2m, the exact scalar polynomial identity is -V_N(-2)=(2-Omega) U_(m-1)(Omega/2)^2. (3) Indeed chi_N(sigma)-4=(sigma^2-4)U_(m-1)(sigma/2)^2 and V_N(-2)=(chi_N(Omega)-chi_N(-2))/(Omega+2), interpreted as its polynomial quotient. Formula (3) retains semisimple contributions. The unrestricted positive-weight norm in (2) does NOT always have the complete folded rate. The B^d coefficient is a length-zero path, hence [B^d]P_N(u)=|chi_N(-2-u)|/(2+u+c_d). (4) At even N and u=0 this tends to one. Thus at x=y=C=1, B=exp(8), liminf N^-1 log P_N(0)>=8. In contrast, positivity and degree a of the original folded determinant give F(1,B,1)+F(1,1,1) <= (1/2)log B+2F(1,1,1) <=4+pi<8. The last elementary bound uses F(1,1,1)=3[Lambda(pi/6)+Lambda(pi/3)]/pi<=pi/2, obtained by the absolute Fourier bound |Lambda(theta)|<=pi^2/12. This is a strictly positive quartet, not a zero-face pathology. At odd N, the coefficient (4) vanishes exactly at u=0. But for any fixed k>0 and u_N=N^-k its exponential rate is zero: writing eta_N=arccosh(1+u_N/2), its numerator is 4sinh^2(N eta_N/2), while eta_N~sqrt(u_N). Therefore the same lower rate 8 reappears under polynomially small regularization. The relevant limits do not commute. No coefficientwise domination by bare P_N(0) is asserted. This is only a LOCAL arbitrary-positive-radius norm limitation. It is not a counterexample to the original shared marked coefficient, nor to a rate statement on a specially certified packing radius. The large diagonal term has a source-specific face degree and can be constrained by the remaining original graph. The phase-blind Hermite obstruction in [actual direct long power source](actual_direct_long_power_source.md) is a separate, graph-wide result. ## 5. The Gaussian does not automatically damp a whole enclosing contour On the spectral cover put sigma=-2cosh w, w=s+it, s>0, |t|<pi. Then K=squared w, |f_n|=exp[n N s t/(2pi)], chi_N(-2cosh w)=2[(-1)^N cosh(Nw)+1]. On a fixed compact with s>0, N^-1 log |f_n/chi_N| -> n s t/(2pi)-s. (5) Thus one side is damped and the other grows. On the growing side, a fixed spectral ellipse with |t|>2pi/|n| gives positive scalar quotient rate, increasing with |n|. The exact matrix numerator can change that rate, but the mere largeness of a fixed twist cannot justify a global decrease. A complete ellipse also meets the K cut near +2; deleting that point and using the proved cap does not change this bulk sign issue. In the half-plane Re w>0 the exact denominator has the convergent expansion epsilon=(-1)^N, 1/chi_N=epsilon exp(-Nw)/(1+epsilon exp(-Nw))^2 =sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1) epsilon^m m exp(-mNw). (6) The individual Gaussian-charge phase is n w^2/(4pi i)-m w, before adding the actual V numerator phase and all face coefficient actions. Its stationary point without that numerator is w=2pi i m/n. There is no justification for discarding every m except the smallest. This agrees with the independently derived nonzero midpoint charges in the exact full-Hermite Fourier formula. ## 6. A precise remaining input A sufficient next theorem would control the original marked, shared-face resolvent numerator after sewing, uniformly on a specified spectral cycle and on the needed complex face torus. It must include the full V (or V and V'), not just positive complete samples, and prove: 1. a local analytic relative packet at the selected near-parabolic stationary point, including its original coefficient contour; 2. a strict global real-action bound for the complement of that packet on a homologous product cycle, preserving every spectral pole and the endpoint/Fourier currents; 3. control of every surviving nonzero charge in (6), or its equivalent unsplit resolvent period, with the actual neighboring Casimirs kept in their original order. The torsor theorem solves the classical local transport and normalizes the Gaussian Hamiltonian. The existing Green estimates supply selected integrand phases on strict physical charts, and (1) completes the +2 cap for this root Gaussian. Neither supplies the missing global source-specific amplitude, cycle comparison or complementary gap. The exact positive path theorem (2) is a concrete input, but (4) explains why replacing its shared coefficient by an unrestricted local norm would not complete the argument. ## Validation and scope The [focused original-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap_results.json) record 77 symbolic identities, 3,100 independently built original coproduct/physical-grid entries (including 1,000 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros), and 4,039 nonnegative path/complex majorant checks. They do not numerically establish any asymptotic or contour claim. The joining radius must remain inside both the endpoint disk and an arbitrarily shrinking outer cap. The remaining bulk/shared-source requirements in Section 6 are not proved.

title: General source-preserving fusion of the original charged network
text: # General source-preserving fusion of the original charged network 28 October 2026. Two exact operations apply to the WHOLE original charged source at arbitrary valency and arbitrary braid width: 1. A full length-N-1 block is the source reproducing kernel. It can be contracted through ANY polynomial exterior, not merely through one complementary Pochhammer. 2. A balanced trivalent charged star is exactly a triangle of three root intervals, with an explicit nonzero q-binomial scalar. The first operation contracts every original closure adapter of a nontrivial knot at the SOURCE level, retaining the actual pivots. The second is a genuine higher-valency fusion. Its proof is a root-orbit divisibility argument and degree rigidity, not a borrowed analytic pentagon or an assumed positive source. These operations do not yet reduce every original network or prove its selected geometric coefficient. A degree obstruction below explains why arbitrary charge stars cannot simply be declared balanced. ## 1. The source in which the operations are exact Use N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N). The [whole charged bridge theorem](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) has already proved, with ALL original scalar lines retained, K_N=chi_N/N sum_h W_h lambda(P_h), lambda(P)=[X_1^d ... X_k^d]P, deg P_h=k d. (1) All h are the actual over-monotone clocks. The canonical [source theorem](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md) permits the SAME lambda to be evaluated in A_0=K[X_1,...,X_k]/(X_1^N,...,X_k^N). (2) This is an exact equality of the original selected period. It is not a rule setting every separate regular-grid factor to zero. The perfect multiplication pairing is lambda(X^a X^b)=delta_(a+b,d). In particular arbitrary polynomial exteriors are admissible in the algebraic identities below. No original coupon or scalar is removed. ## 2. Full blocks reproduce arbitrary exteriors Write B_L(X,Y;a)=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(X-Q^r aY). Root complementation gives B_d(X,Y;a)=sum_(j=0)^d X^(d-j)(aQ^(-1)Y)^j. (3) For ANY polynomial F(X,Y,U), with U denoting all other anchors, [X^d] B_d(X,Y;a)F(X,Y,U) =F(aQ^(-1)Y,Y,U) mod (Y^N,U_i^N). (4) There is no valency or individual-degree restriction on F. Indeed the left side is sum_(j<N)(aQ^(-1)Y)^j [X^j]F. Every missing term of the substitution has a factor Y^N and vanishes in (2). Pairing with the remaining original source proves (4) for the whole scalar. A tail coefficient alpha contributes its actual factor alpha^d. The reverse contraction, which may retain a preferred anchor, is [Y^d] B_d(X,Y;a)F(X,Y,U) =(aQ^(-1))^d F(X,(aQ^(-1))^(-1)X,U) mod (X^N,U_i^N). (5) All displayed monomial factors in (4)--(5) remain. If the two anchors already coincide, then B_d(X,X;a)=X^d G_N(aQ^(-1)), G_N(t)=sum_(j=0)^d t^j. Thus its source contraction is G_N(aQ^(-1)) times evaluation of the remaining polynomial at X=0, NOT a variable identification. For an actual root phase t=q^m, G_N(t)=N if m=0 mod 2N, 0 if m even, not0 mod2N, 2/(1-q^m) if m odd. (6) Every nonzero value has modulus between 1 and N. Its fixed-order logarithmic derivatives are bounded by N^(p+1), directly from the finite sum. This is a general tame fusion of a saturated source cycle, including its resonant value; no central norm is silently inverted at resonance. ### All original closure adapters can be contracted The closure numerator in the actual source is C(Z,Y)=sum_(j=0)^d Z^(d-j)(tY)^j=B_d(Z,Y;Qt), t=1 on the unpivoted cut, t=Q^(-1) on a pivotal head. Therefore its SOURCE relation is Z=tY, with the exact factors of (4) or (5). The original pivot scalar x^(1-N) also remains. This is the nilpotent-source contraction (4), not the forbidden pointwise matching of distinct regular Fermat grids or a bare Cauchy pole substitution. In the anchored graph the closure edges have in-degree and out-degree at most one. A closure-only cycle would follow a physical component through only UNDER encounters and closures, without any overbridge event. A one-component knot with at least one crossing has no such component: each of its self-crossings has an over encounter on the same component. Thus its closure edges form a forest. Contracting them by (4)--(5) removes ALL b boundary-adapter anchors, leaving exactly B anchors, one per open overbridge event (or their canonically identified representatives). This proves an exact globally sewn original source at the jet fiber. It retains chi_N/N and every pivot phase. It does not claim the raw four-Psi continuation has become periodic away from its sampling grid. For links with a closure-only component, the remaining cycle is instead evaluated by (6) and its accompanying zero-anchor substitution. ## 3. Balanced star--triangle identity Let k_1,k_2,k_3>=0, k_1+k_2+k_3=d, and L_i=d-k_i. For arbitrary nonzero a_i, the exact polynomial identity is [Z^d] product_(i=1)^3 B_(L_i)(X_i,Z;a_i) =C a_1^(k_2)a_2^(k_3)a_3^(k_1) *B_(k_3)(X_1,X_2;Q^(k_2+1)a_1/a_2) *B_(k_1)(X_2,X_3;Q^(k_3+1)a_2/a_3) *B_(k_2)(X_3,X_1;Q^(k_1+1)a_3/a_1), (7) C=(-1)^(k_1+k_3) Q^[k_1(k_1-1)/2+k_3(k_3-1)/2-k_2] *[d-k_2 choose k_3]_Q. (8) All lengths and factorials are at most d; the scalar is NONZERO. It must be retained. In particular its modulus need not be tame when all k_i are proportional to N. No half-volume or unknown period factor is absorbed into C. The balance condition is exactly L_1+L_2+L_3=2d. The three new lengths are k_i=d-L_i. The identity remains valid when some are zero, and after substituting coinciding outer variables. ### Proof by root covering and degree First set every a_i=1. The left side F has total outer degree d. For a cyclic pair (i,j) and the remaining index l, specialize X_i=Q^p X_j, p=k_j+1,...,k_j+k_l. The Z-root arcs of the two corresponding blocks are {Q^(p-r)X_j:0<=r<L_i}, {Q^(-s)X_j:0<=s<L_j}. Their union contains a FULL orbit of N roots. Equivalently their missing intervals, of lengths k_i+1 and k_j+1, are disjoint at precisely the displayed k_l positions. Hence the complete product of all three blocks is divisible, as a polynomial in Z, by X_j^N-Z^N. Its residual Z-degree is 2d-N=N-2=d-1. The coefficient of Z^d is therefore zero: the first term cannot reach degree d and the Z^N term already exceeds it. Thus F is divisible by all three displayed families of linear outer factors on the right of (7). Their total degree is k_1+k_2+k_3=d, exactly deg F, so their quotient is a scalar. The coefficient X_1^(L_1)X_2^(k_1) at X_3=0 fixes that scalar. It is (-1)^d Q^[k_3(k_3-1)/2+L_3(L_3-1)/2] [L_2 choose k_3]_Q on the left, and (-1)^(k_2) Q^[k_2(k_1+1)+k_2(k_2-1)/2] in the proposed product. Their ratio simplifies to (8). Finally rescale X_i by a_i and extract the factors a_i^(L_i). The remaining scalar powers are a_1^(k_2)a_2^(k_3)a_3^(k_1), which proves the full formula (7). Because (7) is an ordinary polynomial identity, it can be inserted inside ANY original exterior source pairing. The removed central anchor carries exactly its original charge d; every other anchor keeps its original charge. No scalar knot value is used to choose the normalization. Reversing any incident block is permitted with its exact monomial coefficient, so all strand orientations are covered. ### Connection and reverse move For a block of length L, its positive sine-binomial connection is w=-a q^(L-1). If the three star edges are oriented outer-to-center, then the new triangle edges obey exactly w_(i->j,new)=w_i/w_j. (9) Indeed the extra exponent is k_1+k_2+k_3+1=N and q^N=-1. Thus the new triangle is flat and has the same boundary path phases as the old star. Other nonflat cycles of the complete graph are not erased or declared positive. Conversely (7), divided by its explicit NONZERO scalar, inserts a charged anchor into a matching flat triangle. This is an exact source-preserving inverse move, including zero-length degeneracies. More explicitly, orient the triangle cyclically with lengths (k_3,k_1,k_2), sum d, and normalized root parameters (lambda_12,lambda_23,lambda_31). Its connection is flat precisely when lambda_12 lambda_23 lambda_31=Q^2. (10) Choose a_1=1, a_2=Q^(k_2+1)/lambda_12, and a_3=Q^(k_3+1)a_2/lambda_23. Equation (10) supplies the remaining edge. Thus the inverse has no unsolved normalizer or extension-field choice. A common nonzero rescaling of all a_i is simply the scale of the introduced anchor and is canceled by the retained scalar. This has a genuinely nonzero, nondegenerate typed application inside the original source, rather than only in an auxiliary graph. For the figure-eight word [1,-2,1,-2], its actual clocks h=(0,a,b,a+b), a>0, b>0, a+b<d, give the three bulk blocks of lengths (a,b,d-a-b) and holonomy one. The inverse move therefore has all three positive triangle lengths. At N=4, a=b=1, the complete original clock-sector coefficient is exactly 4(q^2-1), hence nonzero. The audit inserts the (2,2,2) star, retains its original exterior and inverse scalar, and checks the same coefficient. This example checks applicability of the general source identity; it is not a proof of nonvanishing for all clocks in the displayed family or a knot-volume asymptotic. ## 4. What simple source splitting can and cannot balance The full kernel (3) is also the canonical coproduct kernel of the source pairing. It permits splitting an anchor into two charged anchors joined by a full length-d edge, with an arbitrary partition of the old incident polynomial factors. This is exact by (4). Let the old incident lengths sum to S. Replace its neighborhood by r charged anchors and a TREE of r-1 such reproducing edges, without changing its external factors. The total incident length, counted at all new vertices, is S+2d(r-1). If every new vertex were a balanced star, that sum would be 2dr. Necessarily S=2d. Arc subdivision does not change S. Thus an unbalanced anchor cannot be converted to nothing but balanced stars merely by inserting source identity kernels and partitioning its old factors. A two-factor piece with lengths summing to d does give a balanced star after such a split, but its third edge is full length d and the triangle move has a zero-length edge. This alone is not a nondegenerate geometric triangulation. The local defect S-2d is additive under full-edge contraction and is unchanged at outer vertices by the balanced star--triangle move. Defects can be transported or combined; they cannot be silently discarded. Additional exact channel sums or a genuinely deficient-star identity would be needed for a universal reduction. ## 5. Scope of the general advance The full-kernel contraction performs the original boundary gluing at arbitrary valency. The balanced star--triangle move is an exact higher-valency rule inside the actual charge algebra, with its normalizer fixed and its root-orbit proof given above. Both commute with arbitrary exterior original source pairing and allow repeated application wherever their algebraic hypotheses hold. They do not prove that every charged knot graph admits an all-balanced trivalent resolution. Nor do they turn a general remaining cycle sum into positive weights or prove its geometric contribution survives. In particular no quantum determinant or general volume theorem is inferred from the existence of these local rules alone. For coverage only, root-of-unity Fermat and restricted star--triangle identities have substantial precedent, including [Faddeev--Kashaev, *Quantum Dilogarithm*](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9310070). No claim to the first such identity is intended. The independently proved implementation here is the ordinary polynomial identity with its exact scalar and the actual selected socle-source contraction; no proof or analytic contour from that literature is imported. ## 6. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_general_flow_fusion.py The audit checks the arbitrary-polynomial reproducing law, all balanced length triples and generic coefficients at several roots, connection transport, and contraction of every actual original closure adapter inside the whole charged source before comparison with the original signed physical word scalar.

title: A generic all-port single Racah kernel with actual Clebsch normalization
text: # A generic all-port single Racah kernel with actual Clebsch normalization 29 October 2026. This proves a SINGLE terminating balanced 4phi3 formula for every entry of the genuine inverse four-port recoupling matrix. All external nonnegative INTEGER highest weights are allowed, including half-integral spins and their actual cyclic-turn sign. The normalizer comes from a true boundary entry and a leading coefficient, not a quoted 6j evaluation or polynomial norm formula. The independent source is the actual two-sum/all-entry construction in [the ordinary four-port theorem](actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.md). All high channels and generic normal tails are retained. Root sign coherence, positive recoupling and sharp graph energy are not inferred. ## 1. Highest-weight notation and actual bases Use generic zeta, Q=zeta^2 and F_n=(Q;Q)_n. On the ordinary module V_A of INTEGER highest weight A>=0 use the original balanced generators and canonical cup: P_A(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(A-u-1)] F_u F_(A-u)/F_A, p_A(u,A-u)=P_A(u), ell_A=p_A^(-1), F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=zeta^(-A-1)(1-Q^(A+1-u))|u-1>, K|u>=zeta^A Q^(-u). Take external highest weights A,B,C,D with even total. The allowed intermediate highest weights are E=max(|A-B|,|C-D|),...,min(A+B,C+D), step2, G=max(|B-C|,|D-A|),...,min(B+C,D+A), step2. (1) Assume these equal-cardinality ranges nonempty. Every W_AB^E has its first highest component one. Put m=(A+B-E)/2. Its actual highest coefficients are h_AB^E(s)=(-1)^s zeta^[s(A-2B+2m-s-1)] F_(B-m+s)F_(A-s)/(F_(B-m)F_A), (2) and W_AB^E[r]=Delta(F)^r h/F_r, with the canceled physical coproduct entries proved in the independent source theorem. Define FULL invariant columns in the SAME external A,B,C,D order: S_E=(W_AB^E tensor W_CD^E)p_E, T_G(u,v,w,z)=(-1)^A zeta^(A-2u) [(W_BC^G tensor W_DA^G)p_G](v,w,z,u). (3) The factor (-1)^A K_A is the ACTUAL last-to-first pivotal turn: ell_A^T p_A=(-1)^A K_A^(-1). It reduces to the older K_A for integer spins but its sign matters when A is odd. Scaled physical cups have reciprocal evaluations and retain this same snake. We prove S_E=sum_G L_(G,E)T_G on EVERY external color. These are inverse coefficients, not the specialized six-head source column. ## 2. Explicit product normalizers from actual boundary entries Set H=(A+B+C-D)/2, L=min(A,H), Gmax=min(A+D,B+C), n=(Gmax-G)/2, U=(C+E-D)/2, V=(D-C+E)/2, m=(A+B-E)/2, chi_E=(-1)^U zeta^[U(E-U-1)-CV] F_U F_D/(F_((C+D-E)/2) F_E). (4) The unique outer-color contribution in the true S column gives S_E(i,H-i,0,D)=chi_E W_AB^E[U](i,H-i). (5) Its LAST physical Clebsch entry X_E has a product evaluation: if L=H: X_E=F_H h_AB^E(m)/(F_m F_U); otherwise L=A, put k=E-U: X_E=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+2Am-m^2-m+k(E-B)] F_(m+k)/(F_m F_k). (6) The first is the unique coproduct term with second color zero. For the second the proved lowest endpoint is W_AB^E[E](A,B-m)=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+2Am-m^2-m]. Apply Ecal^(E-U). To finish with first color A every lowering must act on the second object. Its coefficient divided by the target coefficient zeta^[-(E-U)(E+1)]F_(E-U) gives (6). Thus no magnetic sum is hidden in X_E. For G put i0=(A+G-D)/2, m_bc=(B+C-G)/2, m_da=(D+A-G)/2. The first nonzero T-chart entry is b_G=(-1)^A zeta^(A-2i0) h_BC^G(m_bc) *(-1)^m_da zeta^[-AD+2D m_da-m_da(m_da+1)]. (7) Indeed T_G(i,H-i,0,D)=0 for i>i0, and its value at i0 is (7). It retains the canonical cup, the W_DA lowest endpoint and the odd-A cyclic sign. Every b_G is a nonzero generic product. Define also J_n=zeta^[-n(B+1)] F_L F_(B-H+L) /[F_(L-n)F_(B-H+L-n)], J_0=1. (8) This is the product of n lower off-diagonals of the ACTUAL first pair Casimir on physical prefix degree H: Omega_AB(i,i-1)=zeta^(-B-1) (1-Q^i)(1-Q^(B-H+i)). (9) All factorial indices in (4),(6),(7),(8) are nonnegative on their physical ranges. The formulas are source entries, not fitted gauges. ## 3. The single terminating balanced Racah formula If A+D<=B+C choose differences C-D,B-A; otherwise choose D-C,A-B. Their maximum is E_min=max(|A-B|,|C-D|). Call the larger s1=E_min and the other s2. Define alpha=zeta^(1+s1), beta=zeta^(1+s2), gamma=zeta^(-1-C-D), delta=zeta^(-1-A-B), P=alpha beta gamma delta=Q^(-Gmax), z_E=zeta^(E+1), K=zeta^(Gmax+1). (10) At equality this gives the same unordered parameter set. The first parameter alpha is fixed to specify the polynomial normalization. Put C_n=alpha^n(PQ^(n-1);Q)_n /(alpha beta,alpha gamma,alpha delta;Q)_n, G_n(E)=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,PQ^(n-1),alpha z_E,alpha/z_E;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,alpha beta,alpha gamma,alpha delta;Q)_k. (11) Listed Pochhammers are multiplied. This is ONE finite sum, possibly terminated earlier by another numerator. All generic denominators are units in the physical length: alpha beta has positive exponent of Q, while alpha gamma and alpha delta first reach zero AFTER n. The leading coefficient C_n is nonzero generic. Then the exact all-entry source coefficient is L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n C_n) *G_n(E), S_E=sum_(G in (1)) L_(G,E)T_G. (12) No 6j formula, norm or orthogonality measure is an input. ## 4. The uniquely fixed actual Jacobi operator The actual fourth-leg bend identifies an invariant column with a highest-weight-D three-object column. Its third-color-zero chart w(i)=Psi(i,H-i,0,D), max(0,H-B)<=i<=L, is injective by the original highest equation and ordinary F descendants. The actual middle Casimir Bmid in that chart is the upper-bidiagonal matrix (Bmid)_ii=zeta^(D-A+1)Q^i+zeta^(-D+A-1)Q^(-i), (Bmid)_(i-1,i)=-zeta^(B+C-A-1)Q^(i-H) *(1-Q^(A+1-i))(1-Q^(H-i+1)). (13) This is the independently derived physical color0/color1 extraction. Let Amid=Omega_AB. The S_E and T_G have respective eigenvalues lambda_E=zeta^(E+1)+zeta^(-E-1), lambda_G. Put lambda(W)=zeta^(W+1)+zeta^(-W-1), Delta=zeta+zeta^(-1), rho=zeta-zeta^(-1), and central values a0=lambda(A)lambda(B)+lambda(C)lambda(D), b0=lambda(B)lambda(C)+lambda(A)lambda(D), c0=lambda(A)lambda(C)+lambda(B)lambda(D). The original generic cleared Fricke identities force Bmid to be three-diagonal in the S basis. Write its action as Bmid S_E=p_E S_(E+2)+d_E S_E+m_E S_(E-2). The first relation gives d_E=(Delta b0-c0 lambda_E)/(Delta^2-lambda_E^2). (14) The E=0 exception means A=B,C=D and is fixed by the ACTUAL cup projection rather than cancellation of 0/0. With S1=sum_(i=0)^A Q^-i and S2=sum_(i=0)^A Q^(-2i), (13) gives ell_A p_A=(-1)^A zeta^A S1, ell_A Bmid p_A=(-1)^A{ zeta^(C+1)(1+Q^(A+1))S1 +[zeta^(2A-C-1)-zeta^(C+1)Q^(A+1)]S2}. The finite ratio S2/S1=(1+Q^(-A-1))/(1+Q^-1) gives d_0=lambda(A)lambda(C)/Delta, the value of (14) after imposing A=B,C=D and canceling. A=0 is immediate in one dimension. The diagonal of the second Fricke relation fixes the products P_E=p_E m_(E+2), with P_(E_min-2)=0, by [2lambda_E-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(E+2)]P_E +[2lambda_E-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(E-2)]P_(E-2) =rho^2[Delta a0-c0 d_E-Delta^2 lambda_E +lambda_E d_E^2]. (15) The forward coefficient is nonzero generic. There is a known ACTUAL LEFT eigenrow fixing the remaining gauge. At G=Gmax one has i0=L, so this physical eigenrow is simply the last chart coordinate. Hence ell_0(E)=L_(Gmax,E)=chi_E X_E/b_(Gmax)!=0. (16) This is a genuine source row, not a prescribed spectral weight. Set u_E=p_E ell_0(E+2)/ell_0(E) and v_E=m_E ell_0(E-2)/ell_0(E). Their sum is lambda_Gmax-d_E, and their successive products are still P_E. Starting from v_Emin=0, the sum and (15) determine them uniquely whenever the proposed interior u is nonzero. The exact result is u_E=K U(z_E), v_E=K U(z_E^-1), U(z)=product_(t=alpha,beta,gamma,delta)(1-tz) /[(1-z^2)(1-Qz^2)], d_E=K+K^-1-K[U(z_E)+U(z_E^-1)]. (17) To prove this uniformly, use independent formal variables zeta,Q^a,Q^b,Q^c,Q^d,Q^e, with A=2a,...,E=2e. For the first branch K=zeta Q^(a+d), both (14),(17) and the product recurrence (15) have IDENTICALLY ZERO cleared rational numerators. The attached audit supplies these two exact six-variable symbolic certificates. The second branch follows by a<->b,c<->d, which preserves a0,b0,c0. Parameter permutation preserves U. After canceled endpoint factors are evaluated, U(z_E) is nonzero on every interior channel and vanishes at the upper endpoint; U(z_E^-1) vanishes at the lower endpoint. The uniqueness therefore proves (17) for the ACTUAL operator, with no unfixed sign. ## 5. Leading coefficients supply the true source normalization Let ell_G(i0)=1 be the physical LEFT eigenrow of (13), zero below i0 and satisfying the elementary one-step equation above i0. The independent two-sum source identity is L_(G,E)=ell_G(w_E)/b_G, w_E(i)=S_E(i,H-i,0,D). (18) Divide by (16). Equation (17) gives the actual finite problem U(z_E)[g(E+2)-g(E)]+U(z_E^-1)[g(E-2)-g(E)] =(Q^-n-1)(1-PQ^(n-1))g(E). (19) Indeed lambda_G=lambda_Gmax+K(Q^-n-1)(1-PQ^(n-1)). This is the exact affine eigenvalue conversion, not a replacement of the physical Casimir. Our OWN [finite symmetric polynomial calculation](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) proves that G_n solves (19), with leading coefficient C_n in lambda_E=z_E+z_E^-1. Its degree is n and its generic leading coefficient is nonzero. The finite grid has distinct Casimir nodes, and its forward coefficient is nonzero until the last slot, so the actual source row is proportional to G_n. Its multiplier still needs determining. For that multiplier, the physical Amid is irreducible tridiagonal. Starting from its last row yields w_E(i)/w_E(L)=a polynomial in lambda_E of degree L-i with leading coefficient 1/product_(t=i+1)^L Amid(t,t-1). (20) Formula (9) evaluates its denominator. In (18) only i>=i0=L-n occurs and ell_G(i0)=1. Thus L_(G,E)/ell_0(E) has degree n and leading coefficient b_(Gmax)/(b_G J_n). (21) Since n is less than the number of channel nodes, this polynomial leading coefficient fixes the proportionality even on the finite grid. Comparing (21) with C_n proves EXACTLY (12), on every color. ## 6. Exact conversion to the seven-factorial sum, including its phase Put [r]!=zeta^[-r(r-1)/2]F_r/(1-Q)^r and s=(A+B+C+D)/2. The tetrahedral incidence is the FOUR faces and THREE opposite sums t=( (A+B+E)/2, (C+D+E)/2, (B+C+G)/2, (D+A+G)/2 ), u=( s, (A+C+E+G)/2, (B+D+E+G)/2 ). Define the literal seven-factorial finite sum S=sum_(z=max t)^(min u) (-1)^z [z+1]! /(product_i[z-t_i]! product_j[u_j-z]!). (22) All its true factorial indices are nonnegative. Choose the effective quadruple (A',B',C',D')=(A,B,C,D) when A+D<=B+C, and (B,A,D,C) otherwise. This latter permutation leaves (22) exactly unchanged: it exchanges its last two faces and its last two opposite sums. Set t0=s-Gmax, R1=(C+D-E)/2, R2=(A+B-E)/2, R3=(A'-B'+E)/2, R4=(D'-C'+E)/2, S0=(-1)^s [s+1]!/([R1]![R2]![t0]![R3]![R4]!), Mstar=(Gmax+G)/2+1, V_n=zeta^n (Q^-Mstar;Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n]. (23) Every factor in S0 and V_n is nonzero generic. The EXACT source normalization of the seven-factorial convention is S=S0 (V_n/C_n)G_n(E), L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) *S. (24) This includes all signs and powers of zeta. In particular the coefficient is not merely equated to a positive square or to an unnormalized named 6j symbol. Here is an own finite proof of (24). Write a=A'/2,b=B'/2,c=C'/2, d=D'/2, e=E/2, f=G/2. Then fmax=a+d, n=fmax-f and t0=b+c-a-d. At f=fmax the z range in (22) is the SINGLE z=s, which is precisely S0. For general n write z=s-k. Dividing by S0 gives the finite falling-product identity S/S0=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k [R1]_k^down [R2]_k^down [R3]_(n-k)^down [R4]_(n-k)^down /([s+1]_k^down [t0+1]_(n-k)^up [k]![n-k]!). (25) The products have their evident consecutive quantum integers. If a formal term lies outside the true range of (22), one falling product contains [0], and that term is EXACTLY zero. No nonzero factorial is assigned to a negative index. For generic formal z_E, factor the k=0 term of (25). Its residual balanced series is 4phi3(Q^-n,Q^-R1,Q^-R2,Q^(-t0-n); Q^(-s-1),Q^(R3-n+1),Q^(R4-n+1);Q,Q). (26) Apply the OWN finite Sears identity, retaining Q^-R1 and taking d_S=Q^(-s-1), e_S=Q^(R3-n+1). The resulting series is exactly the same finite symmetric eigenpolynomial as (11), but with FIRST parameter gamma=zeta^(-1-C-D). In particular its numerator pair is Q^-R1 and Q^(-c-d-e-1), and its denominator parameters are Q^-D', Q^(-(s-B')), Q^(-s-1). After multiplying the k=0 term and canceling the two E-dependent Sears denominator products, its scalar is D_n=(-1)^n zeta^[n(B'-A'+n+1)] (Q^(s-B'-n+1),Q^-D';Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n]. (27) These cancellations are performed as rational identities in formal z_E BEFORE specializing a channel. Thus the identity still holds when a k=0 factorial representation would have a negative index: the falling-product polynomial (25) has no such division. The OWN symmetric-polynomial proof makes the normalized degree-n eigenpolynomial independent of its first parameter. Its leading coefficient when gamma is first is C_n^gamma=gamma^n(PQ^(n-1);Q)_n /(gamma alpha,gamma beta,gamma delta;Q)_n. Reverse the finite product (Q^(s-B'-n+1);Q)_n in (27). The factors Q^-D' and Q^(-(s-B')) cancel those of C_n^gamma. All signs cancel, the remaining zeta monomial is zeta^n, and D_n C_n^gamma=V_n. (28) Consequently D_n times the gamma-first polynomial equals (V_n/C_n)G_n(E), proving (24). This is a finite product/Sears proof; no generic factorial interpolation or quoted tetrahedral theorem is required. The rational identity for formal z_E specializes to every physical E using (25). ## 7. Exact source relation to a face-normalized scalar metric The actual prefactor in (24) SEPARATES the two intermediate labels: a_E^src=chi_E X_E/S0(E), b_G^src=1/(b_G J_n V_n), L_(G,E)=b_G^src a_E^src S. (29) Thus source columns rescaled as S_E/a_E^src and b_G^src T_G have coefficient EXACTLY the seven-factorial sum (22). No phase has been omitted in this row/column gauge. For an admissible highest-weight triple define its usual finite factorial expression, without assuming any 6j interpretation, D(U,V,W)=[(U+V-W)/2]![(U+W-V)/2]![(V+W-U)/2]! /[((U+V+W)/2)+1]!, D_E=D(A,B,E)D(C,D,E), D_G=D(B,C,G)D(D,A,G). The coefficient sqrt(D_E D_G)S is therefore an explicit diagonal gauge of the actual source: use sqrt(D_E)S_E/a_E^src and b_G^src T_G/sqrt(D_G) as its two generic bases. Square-root branches can be fixed positive at real 0<zeta<1, where every factorial is positive. The squared identity is branch-independent. For ANY separately fixed level N it says exactly [N]^2 D_E D_G L_(G,E)^2/(a_E^src b_G^src)^2 =[N]^2 D_E D_G S^2. (30) In particular (30) identifies the source with this convention of the normalized scalar metric BEFORE a root normal is taken. If the four face sums are in the saturated low-fold chamber, the familiar root-zero factors in (30) are the actual generic ones. High partners and [2N] tails remain in the same equality. Principal-root positivity of the scalar convention must keep its spin phase. For INTEGER spins (all six highest weights even), the supported theorem gives the positive once-power factorial square. For admissible half-integral spins the branch-free generic identity (30) still holds, but the positive sine-factorial square differs by the sign (-1)^(A+B+C+D+E+G). This is the parity of the four face zero-removal signs. No positive-square assertion for arbitrary half-spin data is silently included in (30). These are diagonal gauges of a SCALAR recoupling matrix. They may have zeros or poles at the root; paired confluence and original boundary costs still require their own estimates. They neither make the physical root operator positive nor identify this scalar metric with the full marked magnetic/tensor energy. Also a_E^src depends on its four external objects; it has not been asserted to be a single universal per-edge metric throughout a graph. ## 8. Generic normals and scope The theorem and (24) are rational BEFORE root specialization. High intermediate channels, high partners and every normal of the original maps remain present. Individual source factors may have zeros or poles at a root, and extra terminations can have derivative tails. The GENERIC finite sum and original source maps must be combined before taking a fixed marked normal. In particular second-orbit zeros such as [2N] in (22) are retained in (24); they cannot be deleted when comparing first normals. There is a useful explicit finite normal budget. If the EXTERNAL highest weights A,B,C,D are all <N, while intermediate E,G retain their ENTIRE ranges (1), then every denominator of G_n in (11) is a root unit. Indeed alpha beta=Q^(t0+1), and the last exponent t0+n is one of the ordinary physical coupling deficits, hence <N. The other two exponents start at -m_cd or -m_ab for the minimal E, with n<=m_cd,m_ab<N; their products end before exponent zero. The factor F_n is a unit too. The numerator of C_n has at most one simple root zero: its negative exponents have magnitude <2N and length <N. The actual chi_E has at most one pole, from F_E on a high channel E>=N, whereas X_E, b_G and J_n are physical products with indices <N. Consequently pole_order L_(G,E)<=2. (31) The full invariant T_G has at most one pole from its canonical p_G, so each term L_(G,E)T_G has pole order at most THREE. To check this complete physical identity through its first normal, retain Taylor orders zero through FOUR after multiplying by the cube of a local root parameter. This is a uniform finite normal budget, not a bound on coefficient magnitudes. For unfolded high EXTERNAL partners with highest weights >=N use the generic formula itself and retain its explicit zero factors; (31) is not asserted for that different range. The identity supplies finite actual all-port coefficients for graph contractions and meromorphic jets. It does not make a recoupling positive, unitary, polynomially conditioned or sharply controlled under cycle sewing. Audit: [uniform certificates and independent literal source tensors](../experiments/audit_actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.py). The finite audit checks two universal Fricke/AW identities, 381 generic all-port external families and 1125 single-sum source entries, including half-integral spins with the true (-1)^A cyclic sign. Eight root zero-order families check all 40,820 channel entries, including 14,332 retained high-channel entries, with the certified inverse pole bound two and full-term first-normal budget four. Finite tests supplement the displayed uniform proof; they are not a polynomial-fitting argument. The single-Racah identity does not imply an energy bound or positivity at every root.

text: # An exact generic boundary gauge for the original marked source 30 October 2026. A symmetric analytic basis change removes the nonmonomial part of every ordinary cup and preserves the entire original marked source, including its retained trace normal. Its transformed white coefficients are given below in terms of the original generic q-Hahn numerator. This is a finite tensor identity on the actual modules, including the paired nilpotent sectors. It is not a complex magnetic continuation theorem. ## 1. A root-normalized symmetric basis Fix N>=3, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), zeta=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=zeta^2, and F_n=(Q;Q)_n. For any actual module V_L with 0<=L<N set b_L(r;zeta)=zeta^[r(L-r)] F_r F_(L-r)/F_L, b_L^0(r)=b_L(r;q0)=s_r s_(L-r)/s_L, s_n=product_(k=1)^n 2sin(pi k/N), g_L(r;zeta)=[b_L(r;zeta)/b_L^0(r)]^(1/2), G_L=diag(g_L(0),...,g_L(L)). (1) The square root is the analytic one equal to 1 at epsilon=0. Every factorial index is below N, so all these functions are units on a neighborhood of the actual root. In particular G_L(q0)=I, g_L(r)=g_L(L-r), b_d^0(r)=1. (2) The last identity is s_r s_(d-r)=s_d=N. In the actual ordinary cup normalization, including its ordering, p_L(r,L-r)=(-1)^r zeta^(-r) b_L(r;zeta). The physical cup is pV=N zeta^(-d^2) p_d. Replace each module basis by its columns G_L and transform both covariant and contravariant tensor indices. Thus p'_L=G_L^(-1) p_L G_L^(-T), ell'_L=G_L^T ell_L G_L, ell_L=p_L^(-1). Then, EXACTLY before root specialization, p'_L(r,L-r)=(-1)^r zeta^(-r) b_L^0(r), pV'(r,d-r)=N zeta^(-d^2-r)(-1)^r. (3) The generic factorial factors have moved to the adjacent tensors; they have not been deleted from the source. The gauge has polynomial cost on physical indices. Indeed |1-q0^(2k)|>=c min(k,N-k)/N and direct logarithmic differentiation of (1) gives O(N^2 log N), uniformly in L,r. The same product estimate on a sufficiently small disk proves |g_L(r;zeta)|+|g_L(r;zeta)^(-1)|<=C for |epsilon|<=c/[N^2(1+log N)]. (4) Consequently every fixed epsilon derivative of g_L or its inverse is bounded by C_m[N^2(1+log N)]^m. These are estimates at the actual integer module indices only. ## 2. The actual white map, dual, and cyclic order Let W_a:V_(2a)->V_d tensor V_d be the original regular generic Clebsch map, 0<=a<=floor(d/2), with the normalization in [the full matching-graph source](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). Keep its exact dual pi_a=gamma_a^(-1) p_(2a)^T W_a^T (ellV^T tensor ellV^T) P, gamma_a=q0^(2-a^2)/N^2. (5) Here gamma_a is the fixed root scalar in that regular lift; P reverses the two physical heads. Put G_pair=G_d tensor G_d and W'_a=G_pair^(-1) W_a G_(2a), pi'_a=G_(2a)^(-1) pi_a G_pair, K'_a=W'_a pi'_a=G_pair^(-1)(W_a pi_a)G_pair. (6) Substitution of (3) into (5), using P G_pair=G_pair P, proves the SAME categorical dual formula with every tensor primed. This verifies compatibility with the actual bent edges, rather than replacing the white vertex by a Hermitian adjoint.
