All generic intertwining identities remain true after conjugating the module matrices by G_L. No division by pi_a W_a occurs. In particular its root is still zero on a paired sector and the identity on the odd simple sector. The nilpotent source has not been replaced by a semisimple quotient. The exact generic reversal J_L|r>=zeta^[-(L+1)r]|L-r> commutes with G_L by (2). Therefore the original Chevalley/high- degree adapter also holds for the primed white maps. Likewise the actual four-physical-head cyclic turn, with its coefficient (-1)^d zeta^(d-2u), commutes with the product of four G_d factors: the diagonal coefficient commutes and the cyclic permutation permutes identical factors. No unproved cyclic-module adapter is being applied to the original nilpotent module. ## 3. The actual LARGE-channel numerator The generic source distinction is essential here. W_a takes values in the channel of highest weight 2a, so its generic Casimir eigenvalue is zeta^(2a+1)+zeta^(-2a-1). In the original compiler indexing its channel is m=d-a, not a. These two generic eigenvalues coincide at the root but have different derivatives. Use the actual generic polynomial from the [collision/source theorem](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md): H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m (-1)^k B^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q (BQ^(m-k+1);Q)_k/(BQ;Q)_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) product_(j<m-k)(V-Q^j), B=Q^(-N). For 0<=r<=2a put m=d-a, sigma=m+r and i+j=sigma, with 0<=i,j<=d. Then the original white coefficient is EXACTLY W_a(i,sigma-i;r) =(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^B(Q^i,Q^(sigma-i))/F_m, (7) and its transformed coefficient is W'_a(i,sigma-i;r) =g_(2a)(r)/[g_d(i)g_d(sigma-i)] * right_side_of_(7). (8) For the low half r<=a, the original endpoint and normalized LARGE column are W_a(0,sigma;r)=zeta^(-dr) F_sigma/(F_m F_r), C_m(zeta;sigma,i)=zeta^(di) H_m^B(U,V)/D_m(Q^sigma), D_m(T)=product_(k=0)^(m-1)(T-Q^k), D_m(Q^sigma)=(-1)^m zeta^[m(m-1)]F_sigma/F_r. The actual finite Clebsch sum divided by its endpoint is C_m; cancellation gives (7). For ALL r one can verify (7) term by term, without extending that nonexistent physical endpoint into high degrees. In the original Clebsch sum use highest index b and set k=j-m+b. Its denominator is F_b F_(m-b) F_k F_(r-k), with r-k=i-b. Its complete q exponent simplifies to -dr+di-2db+2bj+b(b-1), exactly the converted finite-H summand. The factorial numerator is F_(a+b)F_(d-b)/(F_a F_d) on both sides. Terms outside their finite support vanish by their Newton products, so the same identity holds in the high half r>a. All denominators in H_m and F_m are root units because m<N. Thus (7) is regular BEFORE taking its generic normal and specifies the full original white tensor, without a root-only high adapter. There is a decisive check already at a=0. The original coefficient is W_0(i,d-i;0)=(-1)^i zeta^(-i)b_d(i;zeta), W'_0(i,d-i;0)=(-1)^i zeta^(-i), whereas the SMALL normalized compiler column is C_0=zeta^(di). Their root values agree, but their generic derivatives do not. Thus substituting the small-channel generic R_a into W_a merely because the root columns collide would be incorrect. The precise possible bridge to the small numerator is the exact collision identity, with B temporarily independent of Q: H_m^B-H_a^B product_(k=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^k) =(1-B^2 Q^N) T_(a,m)^B(U,V), m+a=d. (9a) It holds in the localized generic coefficient ring by the finite terminating identity proved in the collision note. Along the ACTUAL source B=Q^(-N), the derivative of 1-B^2 Q^N at q0 is 2N. Thus the transverse term in (9a) contributes to the original first normal. A bound or packet for the small R_a alone does not control that term. Equation (8), not a differentiated root simplification, is the transformed source requiring continuation. ## 4. Exact cancellation on the whole marked source Apply (1)--(6) at every physical and channel occurrence of the original typed matching graph. Every contracted wire has one G_L and one G_L^(-1); cups and caps transform as in (3). Consequently the ordinary closed scalar satisfies F'_Delta(epsilon)=F_Delta(epsilon) (9b) as an analytic identity, for any fixed original diagram and every fixed choice of its folded channel labels. This also holds after the finite label sum and retained signed half-twist factors. No coupon is commuted through another coupon. It is the exact coordinate invariance of this specified finite tensor contraction. Keep the SAME exposed original physical head. Its open endomorphism transforms by G_d^(-1) H G_d. For the original Hopf-covariant contraction H=z_Delta I, so its scalar is unchanged. The physical ordinary dimension remains D_N(epsilon)=(-1)^d[N]_(q0 exp(epsilon)), nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^(-1)). (10) This can also be checked directly from (3): the ratio of the two ordered complementary cup entries is still (-1)^d zeta^(d-2r). Since G_d(q0)=I, the original unrestricted marked row on that exposed arc is unchanged at the root, including its exact normalization m pV(q0)=1. Thus the source's genuine trace-normal extraction is preserved: Z_Delta=F_Delta'(0)/nu_N=F'_Delta{}'(0)/nu_N. (11) If one represents the mark off root as a row, it must transform covariantly too; retaining an untransformed generic row while changing its cup is not (9b). The proof of (11) uses the original ordinary closure and its first normal, so it requires no invented off-root mark and no movement of the bare root mark. For the complete-circle decomposition this applies to the regular Hopf lift in the full-source theorem. As there, that lift is not asserted to be the original complete circle's entire moving-q germ. The root scalar and its normalized ordinary trace derivative are independent of that choice. For an actual specified generic coupon (for example the original exceptional polynomial operator), basis covariance (9b) applies to that very coupon and all its generic jets. It does not replace its moving-q germ by the complete-circle lift. ## 5. What finite gauge cancellation does not prove The physical estimates (4) do NOT imply estimates at complex magnetic coordinates. There is an exact elementary obstruction to such an inference. Given any proposed holomorphic interpolation g(epsilon,u) of a physical gauge, replace it by g(epsilon,u) exp[epsilon exp(N^2) sin^2(pi u)]. (12) For every integer u this changes neither its value nor ANY of its epsilon derivatives. For integer L it preserves the symmetry u<->L-u. Yet its first generic derivative at a fixed noninteger u can be arbitrarily large. Even fixing all finite physical jets and the reversal symmetry does not determine the needed off-grid gauge. One may cancel specified factors algebraically in an exact whole- source continuation BEFORE estimating them. Alternatively one may prove bounds for an explicitly chosen continuation of the factors in (8). Neither operation follows from the physical cancellation (9b). In particular the existing joint deficient-degree theorem controls the actual R numerators, while the remaining boundary factors, the full generic operator lift in that chart, and the global degree period still require their own exact constructions. ## 6. What can nevertheless be bounded in the deficient corridor The exact numerator in (7) gives a useful positive statement without inventing a continuation of G_L. Define the unprimed white continuation by the RIGHT SIDE of (7), with m=d-a fixed, sigma=N Sigma complex, r=sigma-m, and a specified magnetic lift i of size O(N). It is a literal finite generic source expression, agreeing with every physical white entry as just proved. Denote it by mathscr W_a(zeta;sigma,i). It is not defined by interpolation of physical samples. Fix a compact K in the joint deficient corridor of the [actual joint numerator theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.md), using z=q0^(sigma-2i) and its marked logarithmic lift. Put s=m-a=d-2a. There are eta,c,C>0, depending on K, such that for 1<=s<=eta N, every fixed k>=0, and all sufficiently large N, |partial_epsilon^k H_m^B(Q^i,Q^(sigma-i))|_0 <=C_k N^(10k) (C N^20)^s |H_a^1(U0,V0)|, (13) |partial_epsilon^k mathscr W_a|_0 <=C_k N^(10k) (C N^20)^s |mathscr W_a(q0)|. (14) The root quantities on the right are nonzero on K. The simple odd midpoint s=0 is covered directly by the small-numerator theorem. Thus the relative generic cost is subexponential in every window s log N=o(N), and polynomial for bounded s. This is an upper bound, not a nonzero leading normal amplitude. It concerns the specified unprimed white continuation; no bound for the unspecified complex gauge in (8) is asserted. Here is a proof retaining all large-channel factors. The exact generic normalization is H_n^B(Q^i,Q^(sigma-i))=zeta^(n sigma) K_n R_n(zeta;sigma,z). The joint deficient theorem supplies the actual small determinant M_a(epsilon), a bounded inverse, and a bounded determinant ratio on |epsilon|<=rho=c N^(-10). Its last diagonal cofactor is R_(a-1), so R_(a-1)/R_a is bounded on this disk too. The exact all-degree generic recurrence and its source justification are recorded in [the near-fold partner theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md). On the circle |epsilon|=rho its only spectral denominators satisfy |Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-j)|>=c rho, j=1,2, n<=m, with the j=2 equation used only when defined. At the unique folded resonance the factor is 1-Q^(-N); its modulus is comparable to N rho, and the other factor is comparable to N^(-1). All other required gaps are at least cN^(-2). The finite rational coefficient formulas therefore give |alpha_n|<=C/rho, |beta_n|<=C/rho^2. Propagating the ACTUAL recurrence exactly s steps gives |R_m/R_a|<=(C N^20)^s. (15) The accompanying exact scalar quotient is K_m/K_a=product_(j=2a+1)^(2m)(1-B^2 Q^j) /[product_(j=a+1)^m(1-B^2 Q^j) product_(j=a+1)^m(1-BQ^j)]. (16) Its denominator indices stay uniformly near N/2, so their root values are units with a fixed lower bound; its 2s numerator factors are bounded above. Consequently |K_m/K_a|<=C^s. Also |zeta^(s sigma)|<=C_K^s, since the scaled marked parameters remain in a fixed compact. These estimates and the small-numerator bound prove (13) on the circle. The original finite H_m is holomorphic inside it: all denominator Pochhammer indices are below N. Thus Cauchy's estimate applies to H_m, not to its singular monic R_m. At the root the collision identity (9a) gives H_m^1=P_s(T0)H_a^1, P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j), c_K^s<=|P_s(T0)|<=C_K^s. (17) The last bounds hold because the deficient total Sigma is separated from the near-fold interval [a/N,m/N]. In particular no D_a(T0) is divided out, even when Sigma N is a deficient integer. Finally the monomial and F_m^(-1) in (7) have bounded relative variation on the same disk, by the fixed marked-lift bound and the root-unit factorial estimate in section 1. This proves (14). One can retain the actual transverse numerator as well. With the original compiler eigenvalues lambda_n=zeta^(2N-1-2n)+zeta^(-2N+1+2n), lambda_m-lambda_a=-(zeta^s-zeta^(-s)) (zeta^N-zeta^(-N)), the function mathscr T_a=[H_m^B-P_s(T)H_a^B]/(lambda_m-lambda_a) (18) is holomorphic through epsilon=0 by (9a). On the same circle the denominator has modulus at least c s rho. Applying the preceding estimates and then Cauchy's formula gives |partial_epsilon^k mathscr T_a|_0 <=(C_k/s) N^[10(k+1)](C N^20)^s |H_a^1|. (19) This is the original divided numerator with the actual gap sign. It does not divide by D_m(T), so it has none of the spurious deficient-degree column poles. It does not assert that the full exceptional operator's unspecialized boundary factors have already been continued or bounded. Nor can these nonreal local estimates turn an identically zero forbidden physical degree slice into a nonzero global period. Focused audit: [original cups, large white numerators, whole marked plats, and deficient generic circles](../experiments/audit_actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source_results.json). The exact checks passed 282 cup four-jets, 1,028 original LARGE white/numerator four-jets including high physical degrees, 14 actual categorical duals, and 24 marked trace-normal equalities on six full original plats. They retain 45 explicit small/large generic mismatches. The actual divided-numerator checks passed 147 physical four-jets, including 98 nonzero transverse normals, and 40 deficient integer-total collision identities. At 150 digits, eight complex root collisions, 32 genuine large-source circle identities and 32 starting cofactors passed; the maximum literal-source relative error was below 3.1e-136. These finite checks verify the source and normalizations; the uniform estimates are the analytic arguments above. Physical samples do not imply complex gauge bounds. A generic large partner is not replaced by its small root value, and no full exceptional-operator or global-period asymptotic follows. The full meromorphic operator lift is a separate result.

title: A generic all-partner factorial formula for the actual six-head source
text: # A generic all-partner factorial formula for the actual six-head source 29 October 2026. This derives the local nested-cup coefficient and its ordinary closed trace at GENERIC zeta, for every physical pair channel 0<=j<=d=N-1, including the high partner d-j. The construction uses the actual Clebsch maps, genuine ordered ribbon duals, and physical cups. No root factorial reflection, conjugation, or quoted quantum 6j formula is used. Combining the factors gives a finite double-sum expression with an explicit root pole on each paired axis. Every actual marked joint-cluster moment is consequently an explicitly bounded-order Taylor coefficient, of order at most four. This supplies the previously missing generic input for the [actual boundary moments](actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). The finite double source sum below is now reduced to an exactly normalized SINGLE generic Racah sum in [the actual source-column identity](actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md), including all high partners and normal tails. It does not prove that their ratios, the boundary Gram, or recoupling maps have polynomial or subexponential conditioning. ## 1. Generic modules and literal duality Fix N>=2, d=N-1. In this note Q=zeta^2 is GENERIC, and F_k=(Q;Q)_k, F_0=1. The highest-weight L module, in its divided-F basis |u>, has F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=zeta^(-L-1)(1-Q^(L+1-u))|u-1>, K|u>=zeta^L Q^(-u)|u>. Use Delta(F)=F tensor I+K^(-1) tensor F and Delta(Ecal)=Ecal tensor K+I tensor Ecal. The canonical cup is P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)] F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). (1) Its first coefficient is one. The physical cup is pV=cV p_d, cV=N zeta^(-d^2), exactly the regular lift of the original cup. All generic formulas below are rational identities, so their stated continuations do not assume denominators remain nonzero at the root. For every j=0,...,d set l=d-j and define h_j(u)=(-1)^u zeta^(-du) Q^[u(l-1)-u(u-1)/2] F_(j+u)F_(d-u)/(F_j F_d), 0<=u<=l, W_j|r>=Delta(F)^r h_j/F_r, 0<=r<=2j. (2) The highest E equation gives (2) directly. The E,F commutator gives every interior covariance equation. The last F equation follows either from the endpoint below or from the full-column-rank physical E matrix above degree d. Thus W_j is the ACTUAL generic intertwiner from the ordinary highest-weight 2j module, without restricting j to the root low fold. Here is a useful formula with ONLY physical factorial denominators. For 0<=A,B<=d and A+B=l+r, W_j[r](A,B)=F_A F_B sum_u h_j(u) zeta^(-dt) Q^(ut) /[F_u F_(l-u) F_t F_(r-t)], t=B-l+u, max(0,l-B)<=u<=min(l,A), 0<=t<=r. (3) Outside these ranges the entry is zero. Indeed, write Delta(F)=A0+B0 with A0 B0=Q^(-1)B0 A0, expand with the finite Gaussian binomial, and cancel F_r. The two physical moves have lengths t and r-t; therefore ALL four denominator indices in (3) are <=d, even when r>=N. Formula (3) proves the entire W_j matrix is holomorphic at zeta=q=exp(pi i/N), including the high partner channels. Let P exchange the two physical legs. The actual right ribbon dual is DW_j=p_(2j)^T W_j^T(ellV^T tensor ellV^T)P, DW_j[r;u,v]=P_(2j)(2j-r) W_j[2j-r](d-v,d-u)/[pV(d-v)pV(d-u)]. (4) There is no Hermitian conjugation in (4). The swaps and inverse cup coefficients are fixed by the actual nested arcs. ## 2. Own endpoint and projector normalization The generic lowest endpoint is EXACTLY W_j[2j](j+u,d-u)=zeta^[j(d-2j)]h_j(u). (5) Proof. The lowest F equation and the highest E equation have the same coefficient ratio, so it suffices to take u=0 in (3). The remaining finite sum is sum_s (-1)^s Q^[s(s-1)/2] F_(d-s)/[F_s F_(l-s)F_(j-s)]=Q^(lj). For an own finite verification, rewrite it as F_d/(F_l F_j) times 2phi1(Q^-j,Q^-l;Q^-d;Q,1). The finite identity sum_(s=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_s(b;Q)_s (cQ^n/b)^s/[F_s(c;Q)_s]=(c/b;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n follows from the already [finite-binomial proof](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md), section2, by replacing Q,b,c with Q^(-1),b^(-1),c^(-1) and clearing the displayed finite powers. Substitution n=j,b=Q^-l,c=Q^-d gives the endpoint constant in (5). This is a finite summation proof, not an assumed recoupling formula. The exact generic norm is DW_j W_j=n_j I, n_j=(-1)^(d+j)cV^(-2) zeta^[j(j+1)-d(2j+1)] F_(d+j+1)/[F_(d-j)F_(2j+1)]. (6) To prove its scalarity directly, DW_j W_j commutes with the generic ordinary K,F: its distinct K weights force diagonality, and nonzero interior F arrows force equal entries. Take its first entry, apply (5), and insert the cups (1). The only sum remaining is sum_(u=0)^l Q^[-(j+1)u] [j+u choose j]_Q[d-u choose j]_Q =Q^[-(j+1)l][d+j+1 choose l]_Q. After multiplication by Q^((j+1)l), this is the coefficient of z^l in 1/[(z;Q)_(j+1)(zQ^(j+1);Q)_(j+1)]. Expanding the reciprocal finite products by their inductive coefficient formula proves it. All remaining factors give (6). Consequently e_j=W_j DW_j/n_j, j=0,...,d (7) are the genuine generic pair projectors and sum to the physical identity. Indeed they are intertwiners with distinct ordinary highest weights; (6) gives their own nonzero retractions, and their dimensions sum_j(2j+1)=N^2. Their pair Casimir eigenvalues are c_j(zeta)=zeta^(2j+1)+zeta^(-2j-1). ## 3. Finite factorial source corner and full closed trace Take ANY ordinary triangle a,b,c in 0,...,d. Put J=a+b+c, r=b+c-a, r1=a+b-c, r2=a+c-b. The original six-head source is pV_16 pV_23 pV_45. Apply DW_a,DW_b, DW_c on consecutive physical pairs and extract ordinary output (2a,r,0). Define the following completely explicit analytic sum: B_abc=sum_(k=0)^(d-max(a,c)) h_a(d-a-k) h_c(d-c-k) *W_b[r1](d-c-k,a+k) /[P_d(d-a-k)P_d(k)P_d(d-c-k)]. (8) Each W entry in (8) is the physical finite sum (3). Hence (8) is a finite DOUBLE quantum-factorial sum, with at most N^2 terms; every denominator factorial index is <N. In particular B_abc is holomorphic on a fixed neighborhood of each chosen root, including when a,b,c are high partners. The literal source corner is sDW_abc=cV^(-3) zeta^[c(d-2c)-2c] P_(2b)(r1) B_abc. (9) To check (9), the three source cup constraints reduce the contributing physical indices to (u1,u2,u3,u4,u5,u6) =(d-k,a+k,d-a-k,c+k,d-c-k,k). In (4), the first W is its highest column, the third is its lowest column (5), and the middle is W_b[r1]. Three of the six physical inverse cups cancel the three actual source cups. The remaining three give precisely (8). This derivation retains every original port and source coefficient. Let Theta_abc be the genuine ordinary invariant with corner Theta_abc(2a,r,0)=1. The generic ordered pairing already derived by finite Vandermonde in the [marked two-vertex note](actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md), section2, is valid WITHOUT a low-fold restriction: Xi_abc=D(Theta_cba)Theta_abc =(-1)^r1 zeta^[2c-r1(r-1)] F_(2b)F_r2 F_(J+1) /[(1-Q)F_r F_(2a)F_r1 F_(2c)]. (10) The original ordinary closure with projectors e_a,e_b,e_c is therefore T_abc=sDW_abc sDW_cba Xi_abc/(n_a n_b n_c). The reversed labels in its second factor are necessary: white is the genuine ordered dual, not a same-order adjoint. Outside ordinary triangle support T_abc=0 identically. Combining ALL cups and norms yields the simpler exact formula T_abc=(-1)^d zeta^E/(1-Q) *F_r F_r1 F_r2 F_(J+1) *product_(j=a,b,c) [F_(d-j)(1-Q^(2j+1))/F_(N+j)] *B_abc B_cba, E=d(3a+2b+3c+3)-4a^2-4c^2+2ac-2J. (11) This is an actual generic source trace, not a tetrahedron assigned by name. For a direct normalization check, multiply the two ordinary cup factors in (9) by (10): their surviving factorials are F_r F_r1 F_r2 F_(J+1)/[(1-Q)F_(2a)F_(2b)F_(2c)]. Division by (6) replaces F_(2j+1)/F_(2j) by 1-Q^(2j+1). All physical scales cV cancel. The total sign is (-1)^d, since r1+J is even, and the remaining zeta exponent is E. Formula (11) keeps the ordinary quantum dimension and every high-partner term. ## 4. A nonsingular coefficient formula for every marked cluster moment Now specialize near the principal root q=exp(pi i/N), using the NORMAL COORDINATE Z=1-zeta^(2N), zeta=q(1-Z)^(1/(2N)), zeta(0)=q. (12) This specifies the analytic germ; it is not a free physical-color parameter. For each folded label l_i<=floor(d/2), take branches J_i={l_i,d-l_i} if 2l_i<d, J_i={l_i} if 2l_i=d. Let r0 be the number of paired axes. It is fixed for all <=8 branch triples. Each denominator F_(N+j) in (11) contains exactly one factor Z. On an odd simple axis, 1-Q^(2j+1)=Z cancels it. Therefore G_abc(Z):=Z^r0 T_abc(zeta(Z)) (13) is EXPLICITLY holomorphic, by replacing each F_(N+j) by F_(N+j)/Z and each odd simple numerator 1-Q^(2j+1) by 1. No cancellation of large singular matrices is needed to evaluate this formula. Use the literal root polynomial L_N(z)=(-1)^d U_d(z/2). A legitimate generic lift of the actual root eta on an axis is L_N(Omega(zeta)) times its analytic full cluster projector. At a paired branch j, L_N(c_j(zeta(Z)))=Z ell_j(Z), ell_j(Z)=(-1)^d zeta^[-d(2j+1)] *[sum_(v=0)^(2j) (1-Z)^v] /[1-zeta^(4j+2)]. (14) The denominator in (14) is a root unit on every paired axis. This is the finite character identity, not an omission of a Hermite jet. For I a subset of the paired axes, define H_I(Z)=sum_(a,b,c)in(J_1,J_2,J_3) G_abc(Z) product_(i in I) ell_(j_i)(Z), k_I=r0+1-|I|, 1<=k_I<=4. (15) Then the ACTUAL original marked boundary moment is EXACTLY m_I=(-1)^d(q-q^(-1)) [Z^k_I] H_I(Z). (16) In particular the top-circle moment needs one normal; the empty moment can require four. All lower moments, high fold partners and their cancellations are retained. This formula applies outside the regular saturation region too; no unsupported cell has been deleted. Proof of the coherent cancellations. At the root, distinct Casimir nodes coalesce only in the pairs j,d-j. The finite-dimensional Riesz projector for such a whole cluster is analytic and equals e_j+e_(d-j) generically; at a simple node it is e_j. This can equally be written by finite polynomial Chinese remainders. Thus the original closed physical lift with selected circles is the REGULAR function F_I(Z)=Z^(|I|-r0)H_I(Z). Keep the original globally exposed marked outer cap (16); the other caps are ordinary. Cutting it and bending with the SAME physical cup gives a generic Hopf endomorphism of V_N. Its distinct generic K weights and nonzero F arrows force a scalar z_I(zeta)I. The open maps are regular because the FULL cluster projectors and all actual physical maps are regular. Its ordinary trace is F_I(Z)=D_N(zeta) z_I(zeta), D_N=(-1)^d[N]_zeta =(-1)^(d+1) zeta^(-N) Z/(zeta-zeta^(-1)). Hence H_I is divisible by Z^k_I, exactly. The original unrestricted marked row applied to the original cup is one, so m_I=z_I(q). Taking the coefficient gives (16), since q^(-N)=-1. It agrees with the t-normal formula F_I'(0)/nu_N for zeta=q exp(t), but removes all apparent negative Laurent orders before computing that normal. This is a regular Hopf lift of the prescribed ROOT moment. It does not identify a formal continuation of a root scalar with the actual moving-q circle or colored-source family. Lift independence follows from the exposed physical scalar cut and its identical root maps. A bare marked row at an arbitrary nested white cap is not substituted for this cut; see the corrected hypothesis in the [first-normal source theorem](actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md). ## 5. Bounded jets and the remaining analytic gate Equations (3),(8),(11)--(16) give a finite algorithm with no matrix minor inversion. There are <=8 branches, each B has <=N^2 terms, and every needed jet order is <=4, independently of N. The generic qdim has not been canceled before the actual marked quotient, nor have the first normals of paired circles been replaced by values. The formulas also admit explicit factorial ENVELOPES for their fixed jets. Divide every root-zero factor out first. On |Z|<=c/N^2, each remaining quantum factor with index<=3N changes by relative O(1/N), uniformly, because its nonzero root magnitude is >=2sin(pi/N), while the change of its exponent is O(|Z|). The product of O(N) factors is therefore bounded by a constant times its root product. Powers zeta^E, |E|=O(N^2), have the same property. Cauchy's coefficient bound multiplies this envelope by at most C_k N^(2k) at fixed order k. The finite character in (14) costs an additional polynomial factor. Applying this termwise to the explicit finite sums gives genuine bounded-normal factorial upper bounds, with only polynomial jet cost. This does NOT prove that m_I/m_top or the boundary square-root unit has polynomial growth. The absolute factorial envelope can exceed the coherent top moment, and (16) retains cancellations between different high/low branches and different summands. A quantitative comparison for that EXACT coefficient remains necessary for a tame source-aware Gram or general graph sewing theorem. Audit: [generic full physical and root-normal comparisons](../experiments/audit_actual_generic_six_head_tetrahedral_source.py). The audit checks 11 generic finite-field families, all j=0,...,d, 784 literal source corners, and 134 full physical ordinary closures. It also checks 14 actual root joint-cluster families through N=7, all marked moments on each cluster, including unsupported triples, and exact cancellation of every pole and ordinary trace constant. These finite checks supplement the derivations and do not establish conditioning or a new graph volume limit. The finite source and normal formulas do not constitute a conditioning theorem.

title: The actual generic six-head source as a typed recoupling column
text: # The actual generic six-head source as a typed recoupling column 29 October 2026. This identifies the full generic source coefficient `B_abc` with a precisely normalized Clebsch recoupling coefficient. The proof uses the original nested physical cups and ordered ribbon duals, including the pivotal clock at the bend. It applies to every ordinary triangle `0<=a,b,c<=d=N-1`, including the high root partners. It is a rational generic identity; root zeros and poles are not discarded. The finite source sum is defined in [the generic six-head note](actual_generic_six_head_tetrahedral_source.md), §3. The unequal Clebsch conventions and complete four-port identities are those of [the four-port kernel](actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.md), §§1–4. No quantum 6j formula, orthogonality assertion, or asymptotic estimate is an input here. ## 1. The two genuinely typed Hom bases Put `Q=zeta^2`, `F_r=(Q;Q)_r`, and `V=V_d`. The ordinary object `Q_j` has highest weight `2j`. Every Clebsch map `W_AB^C` below has its first highest-vector component equal to one. Set cV=N zeta^(-d^2), pV=cV p_d, P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)] F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). For fixed `a,b`, a basis of `Hom(Q_b,V tensor V tensor Q_a)` is L_c=(W_c tensor I_Qa) W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb, |a-b|<=c<=min(a+b,d). (1) Here `W_c:Q_c -> V tensor V` is the physical equal-pair map. A right basis instead first couples `V tensor Q_a` to an ordinary channel of highest weight `D`. We use its particular channel `D=d`: T=(I_V tensor W_(V,Qa)^V) W_b, T=sum_c H_c L_c. (2) All expressions have the displayed physical order `V,V,Q_a`. In particular `H_c` is a RIGHT-to-LEFT coefficient, rather than the inverse four-port coefficient. Generic highest-weight decomposition proves the bases complete; equivalently the explicit unequal Clebsch norms in the four-port note give their retractions before specialization. Write r=b+c-a, r1=a+b-c, r2=a+c-b. The exact source-to-recoupling identity is H_c=(-1)^(d+c) zeta^E F_r1 F_r2 F_(d-a) F_(d-c) F_(2c+1) /[F_a F_d F_(d+c+1)] * B_abc, E=-2a^2-5c^2+2ac+2bc+ad+3dc-c+d. (3) This is an equality of generic rational functions, not an equality deduced from root nodal values. The following index proof fixes every clock and scalar in (3). ## 2. Bend the original three-cup source Let J=pV_16 pV_23 pV_45, U=(DW_a tensor DW_b tensor DW_c)J. The actual generic source formula gives `U=sDW_abc Theta_abc`, where `Theta_abc(2a,r,0)=1` and sDW_abc=cV^-3 zeta^[c(d-2c)-2c] P_(2b)(r1) B_abc. (4) Move the first ordinary leg to the last by the ACTUAL inverse cyclic turn, and bend the now first `Q_b` leg into an input. The resulting map `M:Q_b -> Q_c tensor Q_a` has literal entries M_(gamma,alpha;t)=sum_beta ell_(2b)(t,beta) K_(2a)(alpha)^-1 U_(alpha,beta,gamma). (5) The `K_(2a)^-1` is essential: for an even highest weight `2a`, the inverse cyclic cup/cap turn is `K_(2a)^-1`, not a permutation. Taking the input highest color `t=0` and output `(gamma,alpha)=(0,r2)` gives M=sDW_abc kTheta W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb, kTheta=(-1)^r1 zeta^[2c+r1(2a+1-r1)] F_(2b)F_r2/(F_r F_(2a)). (6) Indeed `ell_(2b)(0,2b)=zeta^(2b)` and `K_(2a)(r2)^-1=zeta^(2c-2b)`. The remaining canonical invariant coefficient is the direct highest equation Theta_abc(r2,2b,0)=(-1)^r1 zeta^[r1(2a+1-r1)] F_(2b)F_r2/(F_r F_(2a)). There is no division by a root-zero invariant norm in this step. ## 3. The same bend, keeping all physical ports open Define an actual map from one physical object into `V tensor Q_a` by Wtilde_a(i6,alpha;i2) =(-1)^d K_d(i2) K_(2a)(alpha)^-1 sum_i1 DW_a(alpha;i1,i2) pV(i1,i6). (7) This is a rigid bend of `DW_a`, so it is a generic Hopf map. Directly from the highest entry `(i6,alpha;i2)=(0,a;0)` one obtains Wtilde_a=theta_a W_(V,Qa)^V, theta_a=cV^-1 zeta^[a(2a-d)] F_a F_d/(F_(2a)F_(d-a)). (8) For completeness the entry before the remaining physical cup cancels is DW_a(a;d,0)=cV^-2 zeta^[a(2a-d)] F_a F_d/(F_(2a)F_(d-a)). It follows by taking the unique term of the physical divided-coproduct formula for `W_a[a](d,0)`. In (7), the signs and the highest physical clock cancel against `pV(d,0)`, leaving exactly `cV` times that entry. Now substitute the THREE literal cups of `J` and the ordered formula for `DW_b` into (5). The cups `pV_23,pV_45` force `i3=d-i2`, `i5=d-i4`. Their only surviving ratio is pV(i4)/pV(d-i4)=(-1)^d K_d(i4). The ordinary input bend contributes `P_(2b)(t)/P_(2b)(2b-t)=K_(2b)(t)`. Physical weight conservation in `W_b[t](i5,i2)` gives K_(2b)(t)=K_d(i5)K_d(i2), K_d(i4)=K_d(i5)^-1. Thus the two physical clocks at `i4,i5` cancel, with precisely the remaining factors in (7). This proves the all-input map identity M=(DW_c tensor I_Qa)(I_V tensor Wtilde_a) W_b =theta_a (DW_c tensor I_Qa) T. (9) Equation(9) preserves arbitrary allowed exterior tensors and all input colors of `Q_b`. It is stronger than comparing a single source corner. Apply `DW_c` to (2). The generic equal-pair norm is DW_c W_c=n_c I, n_c=(-1)^(d+c)cV^-2 zeta^[c(c+1)-d(2c+1)] F_(d+c+1)/(F_(d-c)F_(2c+1)). (10) Different generic channels are killed. Comparing (6),(9) gives H_c=sDW_abc kTheta/(theta_a n_c). (11) Insert (4),(6),(8),(10) and use P_(2b)(r1) kTheta =zeta^[2c(r1+1)] F_r1 F_r2/F_(2a). The powers of `cV`, all three ordinary cups, and `F_(2a)` cancel. The remaining exponent and factorials are exactly (3). ## 4. Actual Casimir consequence and limits The RIGHT map `T` factors through the ordinary physical object `V_d` on positions 2,3. Hence Omega_23 T=(zeta^N+zeta^-N) T. (12) Consequently the vector of actual coefficients `H_c` from (3) solves the genuine left-channel Casimir eigenproblem, including its endpoint conditions. This supplies a literal source normalization for comparison with a finite Askey–Wilson/Sears polynomial. Identifying that polynomial requires matching the actual channel recurrence and gauge; its identity is not assumed in this note. All equations above are generic identities. They may be continued as meromorphic identities to the root, with paired columns and their normal derivatives retained together. Individual factors in (3) or (11) can vanish or have poles; the regular original physical source `B_abc` is still the finite analytic sum in the six-head note. Nothing here bounds recoupling conditioning, turns the ordered dual into a Hermitian adjoint, or proves a primitive-graph positive asymptotic. ## 5. Verification The matching audit constructs the physical `W_j,DW_j` independently, checks (7),(8) on every input color, and verifies (3) by projecting the full map (2) for every admissible triangle at generic finite-field levels. A separate literal six-head contraction verifies (5),(9), including the pivotal clock, before reducing to a scalar. These finite checks supplement the displayed generic index proof.

title: The actual generic trivalent source is the normalized single Racah sum
text: # The actual generic trivalent source is the normalized single Racah sum 29 October 2026. This proves the previously missing GENERIC finite identity, with the normalization determined by the original nested cups and genuine ordered duals. It includes both low channels and their high fold partners before root specialization. The proof uses an actual mixed-highest Casimir matrix, two universal rational certificates, the literal coefficient COLUMN obtained by bending, and our own finite polynomial/Sears calculation. No quoted quantum 6j evaluation is a premise. This is a finite identity and preserves the normal tails. A tame boundary-conditioning or general graph asymptotic estimate is not claimed solely from this formula. ## 1. Statement with the actual source normalization Let N>=2, d=N-1, zeta generic, Q=zeta^2, F_n=(Q;Q)_n, and [n]! = zeta^[-n(n-1)/2] F_n/(1-Q)^n. For every ordinary triangle 0<=a,b,c<=d put J=a+b+c and r=b+c-a, r1=a+b-c, r2=a+c-b. Let B_abc be the ACTUAL analytic factorial source sum defined in (8) of [the generic six-head theorem](actual_generic_six_head_tetrahedral_source.md). It is not defined through the formula to be proved here. Then B_abc=(-1)^J zeta^D [a]![b]![c]!/[J+1]! *S_abc, D=a^2-b^2+c^2-ab-ac+bc-cd, (1) where the SINGLE terminating sum is S_abc=sum_z (-1)^z [z+1]! /([z-J]! product_(j=a,b,c)[z-d-j]! [d+a+b-z]![d+a+c-z]![d+b+c-z]!), max(J,d+a,d+b,d+c)<=z <=min(d+a+b,d+a+c,d+b+c). (2) Every factorial index in its true range is nonnegative. Equations (1),(2) are generic rational identities, so all root-zero factors and all generic normals must be retained when specializing them. ## 2. An actual finite highest-source space First take a>=b, put h=a-b, and let C={h,h+1,...,min(a+b,d)}, D0=d+h, V=ker(Ecal_12^(2a+1)) in (V_d tensor V_d)_(degree D0). The generic physical Clebsch columns from the six-head theorem give a basis v_c=W_c[a+c-b], c in C. Indeed the generic physical pair decomposes into its distinct Casimir eigenspaces with highest weights 2c; in degree D0, precisely these descendants are killed by Ecal_12^(2a+1). Their highest lift to Hom(Q_b,V_d tensor V_d tensor Q_a) is H(w)=sum_(u=0)^(2a) alpha_u Ecal_12^u w tensor |u>, alpha_u=(-1)^u zeta^[u(4a+1)]Q^[-u(u-1)/2] F_(2a-u)/F_(2a). The direct E equation proves this formula, and extracting the third color zero is its inverse. Thus no full ambient space is silently identified with the actual highest source. Let A=Omega_12 and B be Omega_23 transported to this highest chart. In physical prefix coordinates |s,D0-s>, h<=s<=d, direct extraction of third colors zero and one gives B_ss=zeta^(-d+2b+1)Q^s+zeta^(d-2b-1)Q^(-s), B_(s-1,s)=-zeta^(2a-1)Q^(s-D0) (1-Q^(d+1-s))(1-Q^(D0-s+1)). (3) All other entries vanish. The diagonal FE contribution from third color zero cancels the corresponding term from third color one. This is the actual right-pair Casimir, whose physical V_d-channel eigenvalue is H0=zeta^N+zeta^(-N). The first physical component of each v_c has a closed finite Chu evaluation: phi_c=v_c(h,d) =zeta^[-dc+2(d-c)h] F_(d-h)/[F_(d-c)F_(c-h)]. (4) For clarity, (4) is obtained directly from the physical coproduct sum for W_c[c+h](h,d). After extracting zeta^(-dc)F_h/F_c, the remaining sum is sum_u(-1)^u Q^[u(u-1)/2] F_(d-u)/[F_u F_(d-c-u)F_(h-u)]. The finite second Chu identity, already proved by finite binomial expansion in the six-head note, evaluates it to Q^((d-c)h)F_c F_(d-h)/[F_(d-c)F_h F_(c-h)]. Thus (4) is not an assumed endpoint value. Put f_c=v_c/phi_c; every f_c has first physical component one. ## 3. A universal, uniquely determined three-diagonal matrix Write lambda_c=zeta^(2c+1)+zeta^(-2c-1), delta=zeta+zeta^(-1), rho=zeta-zeta^(-1), and alpha=H0^2+lambda_a lambda_b, beta=gamma=H0(lambda_a+lambda_b). The independently proved, generic [quantum Fricke identities](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) apply to the actual adjacent Casimirs in this highest-source module. Eliminating their third generator gives A^2B-(Q+Q^-1)ABA+BA^2+rho^2 delta^2 B =rho^2(delta beta-gamma A), B^2A-(Q+Q^-1)BAB+AB^2+rho^2 delta^2 A =rho^2(delta alpha-gamma B). (5) These are universal cleared Hopf-algebra equalities, not a recurrence deduced from a guessed Racah sum. In the A-eigenbasis f_c, the first identity forces B to be tridiagonal: its off-diagonal coefficient can be nonzero only when the two indices differ by one. Its diagonal is b_c=H0(lambda_a+lambda_b)/(delta+lambda_c). (6) For c>0 this follows by canceling the nonzero generic factor delta-lambda_c. The channel c=0 occurs only when h=0 and a=b; there that factor is identically zero and requires a separate ACTUAL source calculation. Here f_0=p_d is the canonical physical cup. Its genuine retraction is the canonical cap ell_d, up to the same scalar on numerator and denominator, so b_0=(ell_d B p_d)/(ell_d p_d). Put S1=sum_(s=0)^d Q^(-s), S2=sum_(s=0)^d Q^(-2s). Using (3) and P_d(s)/P_d(d-s)=(-1)^d zeta^d Q^(-s), the diagonal and upper off-diagonal terms give EXACTLY ell_d p_d=(-1)^d zeta^d S1, ell_d B p_d=(-1)^d{ zeta^(2a+1)(1+Q^N)S1 +[zeta^(2d-2a-1)-zeta^(2a+1)Q^N]S2}. The finite geometric ratio S2/S1=(1+Q^(-N))/(1+Q^(-1)) reduces this to b_0=H0 lambda_a/delta=beta/(2delta), exactly (6). This supplies the exceptional endpoint without continuing in an integer channel. Write B f_c=p_c f_(c+1)+b_c f_c+m_c f_(c-1). Here m_h=0 and p_maxC=0. The two remaining coefficients are kappa0=zeta^N Q^b, p_c=-kappa0^-1 Q^(c-h) (1-Q^(c+h+1))(1-Q^(a+b-c))(1-Q^(d-c)) /[(1-Q^(2c+1))(1+Q^(c+1))], m_c=-kappa0^-1 Q^c (1-Q^(c-h))(1-Q^(N+c))(1-Q^(a+b+c+1)) /[(1+Q^c)(1-Q^(2c+1))]. (7) Here is a uniform proof of (7), rather than interpolation of matrix data. Since f_c has first physical component one, (3) and the first row of the physical A give a prescribed row-sum p_c+b_c+m_c=S_c. To state this and its certificate without long monomial powers, use INDEPENDENT formal variables q,t,H,V,Y and set Q=q^2, t=zeta^N, H=Q^h, V=Q^b, Y=Q^c, lambda(Y)=qY+q^(-1)Y^(-1), A00=q/t^2(1-H)(1-t^2/H) +qH/t^2(1-t^2/Q)(1-Q)+q/H+H/q, B00=QHV/t+t/(QHV), S(Y)=B00-(tV/q)(lambda(Y)-A00). (8) The coefficient of the first off-diagonal in B divided by that in A is exactly -tV/q; hence (8) is the first-row equation for EVERY c. Substituting (6),(7) in p+b+m-S gives the IDENTICALLY ZERO rational function of q,t,H,V,Y. The diagonal of the second identity in (5) fixes products P_c=p_c m_(c+1) by the first-order recursion [2lambda_c-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(c+1)]P_c +[2lambda_c-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(c-1)]P_(c-1) =rho^2[delta alpha-gamma b_c-delta^2 lambda_c +lambda_c b_c^2]. (9) Its forward coefficient is nonzero generic, and P_(h-1)=0. Substitution of (7) in (9) is a SECOND identically zero rational function in those five independent variables. The accompanying symbolic certificate clears each denominator and verifies zero. These two identities determine the actual coefficients uniquely: at h, m_h=0 and the row-sum gives p_h; then (9) fixes P_h, so m_(h+1)=P_h/p_h, and the next row-sum fixes p_(h+1). Continue. All interior proposed p_c are nonzero generic; their only physical endpoint zeros are c=a+b or c=d. Thus induction proves (7) at every channel, including the endpoint, without an undetermined sign. If b=0 the space has one dimension and the statement is immediate. ## 4. The source is a coefficient COLUMN, with literal bend normalization Use the actual generic maps T=(I_V tensor W_(V,Qa)^V)W_b, L_c=(W_c tensor I_Qa)W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb. The right map T has Omega_23 eigenvalue H0 on ALL input colors, since its positions23 factor through the actual V_d. Its left-basis expansion is T=sum_c R_Hom(c) L_c, R_Hom(c)=J_c B_abc, J_c=(-1)^(d+c) zeta^ER F_r1 F_r2 F_(d-a)F_(d-c)F_(2c+1) /[F_a F_d F_(d+c+1)], ER=-2a^2-5c^2+2ac+2bc+ad+3dc-c+d. (10) The full source-independent map proof, using only cups and Clebsch maps, is in [the literal generic tetrahedral bend](actual_generic_tetrahedral_source_as_recoupling.md). In brief, bend the b output of (DW_a tensor DW_b tensor DW_c)(p16 p23 p45). The resulting map is simultaneously a known multiple of W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb and (DW_c tensor I)(I tensor Wtilde_a)W_b. The latter bent Wtilde_a is its actual first-entry-one mixed Clebsch map times its explicitly computed cup scalar. Composing DW_c W_c=n_c then proves (10). It is a map identity before scalar extraction, not a scalar fit. The third-color-zero coefficient of L_c is nu_c v_c, where nu_c=(-1)^r2 zeta^[r2(2c-4a+r2-1)] F_(2a)F_r/(F_r1 F_(2c)). Thus in the f_c basis the RIGHT coordinate column of T is y_c=J_c nu_c phi_c B_abc. (11) This is not the inverse coefficient obtained by applying a left eigenrow to v_c. Confusing them changes the transpose and invalidates the recurrence. Define a nonzero generic gauge by K_c=(-1)^(d+b+c) zeta^P F_a F_(N+a)F_(2b)F_(d-a+b) /[F_(J+1)F_(a-b)F_r F_b F_(d-a)F_r1F_(d-c)], P=2a^2-b^2+3c^2-2ac+2bc-d(a+b+2c+1)+b+c, g_c=B_abc/K_c, sigma_c=J_c nu_c phi_c K_c. (12) All factorial indices here are nonnegative on C. From the explicit products, its successive ratio is sigma_(c+1)/sigma_c =-Q^(c-h)(1-Q^(c+h+1))(1-Q^(2c+3)) *(1-Q^(a+b-c))(1-Q^(d-c)) /[(1-Q^(2c+1))(1-Q^(N+c+1)) *(1-Q^(J+2))(1-Q^(c-h+1))]. (13) Successive ratios are used only when both indices belong to C; outside C the corresponding term is its actual endpoint zero. There is an exact source endpoint: at c=h the source Euler formula has r=0 and directly gives B_abh=K_h. Hence g_h=1. No unknown endpoint residue or source coefficient is supplied as an assumption. ## 5. The exact finite eigenproblem is our own AW polynomial operator Put X=Q^N. For c in C define u_c=(1-Q^(h+c+1))(1-Q^(c+1)) *(1-Q^(c-a-b))(1-X^-1Q^(c+1)) /[(1-Q^(2c+1))(1-Q^(2c+2))], v_c=(1-Q^(h-c))(1-Q^(-c)) *(1-Q^(-a-b-c-1))(1-X^-1Q^(-c)) /[(1-Q^(-2c-1))(1-Q^(-2c))], Lambda_b=(Q^-b-1)(1-X^-1Q^-b). (14) At c=0 the second formula has its removable value after canceling (1-Q^(-c))/(1-Q^(-2c))=1/(1+Q^(-c)). Direct rational substitution of (7),(13) gives b_c=H0-kappa0(Lambda_b+u_c+v_c), p_c=kappa0 v_(c+1) sigma_(c+1)/sigma_c, m_c=kappa0 u_(c-1) sigma_(c-1)/sigma_c. (15) These are also checked identically over the five-variable rational field. Since y is the coefficient COLUMN, its Casimir equation is H0 y_c=p_(c-1)y_(c-1)+b_c y_c+m_(c+1)y_(c+1). Equations (11),(15) therefore give the exact source recurrence u_c(g_(c+1)-g_c)+v_c(g_(c-1)-g_c) =Lambda_b g_c. (16) Equivalently the gauged physical matrix is H0 I+kappa0(L_AW-Lambda_b I), with L_AW the difference operator on the left of (16). Its physical Casimir eigenvalue is H0, NOT lambda_b. The latter is the affine difference-operator eigenvalue only. Our independently proved [finite symmetric polynomial operator](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) applies with base Q and parameters A0=zeta Q^(a-b), B0=zeta, C0=zeta^(-1)Q^(-a-b), D0=zeta/X, z_c=zeta Q^c, degree n=b. Its forward/backward coefficients are exactly (14). Thus the finite polynomial calculation in that note proves that G_c=4phi3(Q^-b,X^-1Q^-b,Q^(a-b-c),Q^(a-b+c+1); Q^(a-b+1),Q^-2b,X^-1Q^(a-b+1);Q,Q) (17) satisfies (16). The sum has length b; no denominator reaches zero in its generic physical range, since d>=a>=b. At c=h one numerator is one, so G_h=1. Also v_h=0, u_maxC=0, and every interior u_c is nonzero generic. Consequently the scalar three-term recurrence with its ACTUAL endpoint g_h=1 determines all its values uniquely. It follows that B_abc=K_c G_c, for a>=b, c in C. (18) This is the decisive source-selection step. It is a finite exact recurrence argument; no semiclassical branch or noncancellation assumption is made. ## 6. Own Sears conversion gives the single sum First suppose a=max(a,b,c) and d>=b+c. Write z=d+a+k in (2). The factorial ratios give the balanced finite long series H=4phi3(Q^-r,Q^(N+a+1),Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(N-b-c),Q^(a-b+1),Q^(a-c+1);Q,Q). Its prefactor is the k=0 term of (1). Apply our OWN finite Sears identity, taking termination length b, retained parameter Q^-r, d_S=Q^(a-b+1), e_S=Q^(a-c+1). Extending the sum to length b is legitimate since Q^-r already kills all k>r. It gives H=(Q^(b+1),X^-1Q^(a-b+1);Q)_b /(Q^(a-c+1),X^-1Q^(c+1);Q)_b *G_c. Here the k=0 prefactor of (1) is explicitly R0=(-1)^(d+b+c) zeta^D [a]![N+a]! /([J+1]![d-b-c]![a-b]![a-c]![r]!). Reverse the two negative-start Pochhammers in the Sears factor. That factor becomes Q^[b(h-c)] F_(2b)F_(d-h)F_(a-c)F_(d-b-c) /[F_b F_(d-a)F_r1 F_(d-c)]. All four latter factorials cancel those in R0 as displayed in (12). For the phase, converting R0 to F factorials gives exponent D-T(a)-T(N+a)+T(J+1)+T(d-b-c)+T(h)+T(a-c)+T(r), where T(n)=n(n-1)/2. Adding 2b(h-c) gives exactly P in (12). Thus their product is K_c with its full sign and phase, not merely its square. Equation (18) proves (1) in this region. To remove the temporary size restriction, fix ordinary a=max(a,b,c). The independently proved [generic source polynomial reduction](generic_trivalent_bilinear_racah_port.md), section3a, normalizes the ACTUAL B to R_SRC(X), degree at most r, after the explicit factor (XQ^-a)_(2a+1). The proposed single sum normalizes to the explicit R_TGT(X) of that same degree. Their normalizations and constants were derived by finite products there. For every real 0<zeta<1, the preceding argument proves equality at ALL X=Q^(d+1), d>=b+c. These are infinitely many distinct points. Thus the two finite polynomials agree identically. Their rational coefficients in Q then agree generically as well. Substitute X=Q^(d+1) for ANY physical d>=a. If a term would have d-b-c+k<0, its finite product (XQ^(-b-c+k);Q)_(J+1) contains 1-Q^0 and is EXACTLY zero. This restores precisely the correct lower limit z>=J. Therefore the same identity covers d<b+c and every high-partner range. No nonzero factorial is assigned to a negative index. Finally remove the ordering restriction by genuine cyclic duality. For the canonical physical cup, P_d(d-u)/P_d(u)=(-1)^d zeta^(-d+2u). Cycling the three consecutive physical PAIRS in p16 p23 p45 gives exactly the inverse K on the moved pair. Intertwining transports it to the moved ordinary object. Hence U_bca(r_b,r_c,r_a)=K_a^(-1)(r_a)U_abc(r_a,r_b,r_c). The ordinary Theta coefficient needed to extract the new canonical corner is computed by its finite two-term E recursion, first along third color zero to second color 2b, then keeping that second color maximal. It is Theta_abc(0,2b,r2) =zeta^Et F_(2b)F_r2/(F_r1F_(2c)), Et=-2(a^2-ab-a+bc-c^2). Substituting the ACTUAL source-corner prefactors (9) of the generic six-head theorem cancels every factorial and sign, leaving B_bca=zeta^[D(b,c,a)-D(a,b,c)]B_abc. (19) Every triple can be cyclically rotated so its largest label is first. The factorial prefactor and the finite sum in (1),(2) are symmetric. Thus (19) proves (1) for ALL ordered ordinary triangles. ## 7. Root normals, scope and audit There is also a useful EXACT closed-trace corollary. With the original ordinary closure T_abc from (11) of the generic six-head theorem, T_abc=(-1)^d product_(j=a,b,c)[2j+1] *[r]![r1]![r2]!/[J+1]! *product_(j=a,b,c)([j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!) *S_abc^2. (20) This is a square of the generic scalar, not a Hermitian absolute square. It keeps the genuine ordinary dimensions. To verify all normalization factors directly, insert (1) for B_abc and B_cba in that source trace and replace F_n by zeta^[n(n-1)/2](1-Q)^n[n]!. The powers of 1-Q cancel. Writing T(n)=n(n-1)/2, the remaining exponent is the identically zero polynomial E+D(a,b,c)+D(c,b,a)+T(r)+T(r1)+T(r2)+T(J+1) +sum_(j=a,b,c)[T(d-j)-T(N+j)+2j]=0, where E is the actual trace exponent in the six-head theorem. This also proves (20) without importing a tetrahedral trace normalization. Equations (1),(2) now give a single factorial sum for each generic branch in the full <=8-branch marked cluster formula. This identity holds before specialization, so it retains the derivative tails that are lost by imposing Q^N=1 first. For low-fold principal-root labels, one can extract the known single [N] factor and recover the proved positive root partition. High partners and terms crossing N retain their actual zero orders; they must be combined as prescribed by the generic cluster formula before a marked normal is taken. The proof has NOT yet established a polynomial bound for every lower marked moment divided by the positive top moment. Such a bound requires estimates for the explicit factorial sums and their bounded normals; it does not follow merely from (1). Audit: [universal symbolic recurrence and literal source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.py). The two Fricke/boundary rational certificates and the transpose/AW gauge certificates have identically zero cleared numerators in five independent parameters. The supplementary original-matrix audit passes eleven generic families, 489 all-vector Jacobi recurrences, full highest-source column/endpoint checks, and cyclic source covariance. These are exact checks supporting the uniform proof, not an inference from numerical polynomial fitting. The generic scalar identity does not imply conditioning or asymptotic estimates.

title: The actual coefficient model has a nonzero geometric normal period
text: # The actual coefficient model has a nonzero geometric normal period Research note, 26 October 2026. This derives the first transport amplitude from the original crossing coefficients and proves a uniform Morse--Bott statement at the complete hyperbolic representation. After transverse formal contraction, the resulting actual-coefficient normal connection is formally gauge equivalent to the marked geometric one. This is a comparison of local normal stationary blocks. It is not a construction of the selected global finite-state cycle, an identification of its quantum-A annihilator ideal, or a volume-conjecture proof. ## 1. The actual state and its independent flow variables Keep the original reduced state F_N(M), q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q_N^2, x=-M/q_N and Y=M^2. Use exactly the factorial boundary frame of [the marked critical-correspondence proof](marked_braid_holonomy.md). Its cut vector is constant and its covector is the normalized average. The reduced period is still F_N(M); the factor 1/N is retained. Take a b-strand knot braid with m crossings, read in the actual operator-action order. Start with integer positions a_0,...,a_(b-1) and one transfer k_t for each crossing. The position update is (a,b) -> (b+k,a-k) for a positive crossing, (a,b) -> (b-k,a+k) for a negative crossing. Closing strands 1,...,b-1 gives b-1 independent integral equations. Their matrix on the initial positions is a cofactor of P-I for the braid permutation P. Because the closure is a knot, P is one cycle; this cofactor has determinant +1 or -1. Thus all positions except a_0 are solved integrally in terms of a_0 and all m transfers. The total-index conservation gives the remaining closure as well. There are exactly d=m+1 (1.1) independent phase variables, on an integral flow lattice with no unrecorded determinant. This counts variables of the actual cut sum, not a substituted geometric state. ## 2. The principal amplitudes retain the color half-step Write H=Log Q, A=Q^a, B=Q^b, C=Q^k. The balanced positive crossing has exact variable product P_Q(QB)P_Q(QC)P_Q(Y/A) /[P_Q(QBC)P_Q(YC/A)P_Q(Q)], (2.1) with the already proved Gaussian factor. The negative product replaces B by A and Y/A by Y/B, with its different Gaussian. The cancellation Qx^2=Y is important in (2.1): the last two variable arguments are not Q-shifted arguments. For the existing compact product, Log P_Q(z)=Li_2(z)/H+(1/2)Log(1-z)+O(H), Log P_Q(Qz)=Li_2(z)/H-(1/2)Log(1-z)+O(H). Every higher variable coefficient is rational in z. Also Log x=Log M+pi*i-H/2 on the specified sheet. Its contribution to the Gaussian amplitude is sqrt(AB) positively and sqrt(C/(AB)) negatively. Therefore the squared variable principal amplitudes of the actual coefficients are a_(+,0)^2=AB (1-BC)(1-Y/A) /[(1-B)(1-C)(1-YC/A)], a_(-,0)^2=C/(AB) (1-AC)(1-Y/B) /[(1-A)(1-C)(1-YC/B)]. (2.2) All five shape arguments are nonzero and different from one on the established geometric chart, so these are units there. Their square-root covers and original phases are retained. This includes the exact local transport. For example the three positive internal shift ratios are R_a=BC/x * (1-Y/(QA))/(1-YC/(QA)), R_b=A/(Cx) * (1-QBC)/(1-QB), R_k=-A/(QBCx) * (1-QBC)(1-YC/A)/(1-QC). (2.3) The negative ratios are R_a=x/B * (1-QAC)/(1-QA), R_b=x/A * (1-Y/(QB))/(1-YC/(QB)), R_k=1/x * (1-QAC)(1-YC/B)/(1-QC). (2.4) They follow by cancelling finite factors; no asymptotic knot identity is used. If S is the actual local leading action, each equation verifies [H]Log R_i=(1/2)S_(ii)+partial_i Log a_0. (2.5) For the actual meridian half-step M->exp(H/2)M, its ratios are R_M^+=(ABC)^(-1/2)(1-YC/A)/(1-Y/A), R_M^-=(AB/C)^(1/2)(1-YC/B)/(1-Y/B). (2.6) They have zero first H correction and satisfy S_(uu)/8+partial_u Log a_0/2=0. The half-step and its original square-root character are therefore checked independently. The closed pivot and zero-framing factors contribute principal amplitude M^(b-1-w)/product_(j=1)^(b-1) A_j, where w is the writhe and A_j are initial closed positions. Their leading phases and base-only constants remain the ones in the [actual action calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). Thus the complete variable amplitude is nonzero on the chart. Neither the fixed P_Q(Q)^(-m) nor the boundary normalization 1/N has been evaluated separately at a root or discarded. ## 3. The geometric critical scheme is smooth with two framing directions The actual crossing calculation gives an isomorphism of open critical schemes with framed augmented knot representations, with its inverse meridian eigenflag fixed to the cut flag 1. Its formulas and inverses have unit denominators on the chosen chart, so this includes Artin rings, not just complex points. The framing group is B_1=Stab_(PGL_2)(1), of dimension two. The geometric representation is irreducible and its projective centralizer is trivial; the framing torsor is explicitly split by three developed flags, as already constructed in that note. Here is why the unframed geometric germ is smooth with meridian as coordinate, without importing a deformation-rigidity proof. Use the positive triangulation and invertible marked gluing Jacobian in [the geometric rigidity note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md). The development construction identifies its germ with the augmented representation quotient. This identification also works over Artin rings: three distinct vertex flags give the unique face transformation; their differences stay units. The product around an edge fixes its two distinct endpoints and has multiplier the edge shape product, hence is identity when that product is one. The dual two-skeleton therefore constructs a flat representation. Conversely a representation and peripheral flag give the developed cross-ratios. Normalizing one ordered triple makes these two constructions inverse. The fixed SL2 lift is retained on its etale sign cover. The marked gluing germ is etale over the meridian. Consequently the actual framed critical germ at fixed M is a smooth open part of its two-dimensional B_1 torsor. The actual inverse cut flag can be compared by (U,V)->(-U,-V); both peripheral signs are changed together, preserving the regulator differential. It follows that the Hessian of the flattened actual phase has kernel=T(B_1), rank=d-2=m-1. (3.1) Indeed the local gradient ideal is the logarithm of the exponentiated critical equations. Its Jacobian is the Hessian, and smoothness of this very critical scheme gives rank d-2. This is a Morse--Bott assertion for the actual coefficient phase. Alternatingness is not required; the positive geometric input is the already audited one for hyperbolic knot exteriors. ## 4. A nonzero transverse formal block of the actual coefficients Choose two actual position/transfer coordinates chi whose differential on the framing torsor is invertible. Their level set is an algebraic transverse slice. Restriction of the symmetric Hessian to the remaining d-2 coordinate directions is nondegenerate, because those directions complement its radical. Let this restriction be H_perp. Formal Gaussian contraction on the slice now yields a nonzero normal block, with variable leading term A_(perp,0)=a_(beta,0)/sqrt(det(-H_perp)), (4.1) up to the retained coordinate half-density. The numerator is a unit by Section 2 and the denominator is a unit by (3.1). Subtract the full constant and quadratic phase before Wick contraction; all remaining vertices have degree at least three. At each formal H order there are finitely many contractions. All coefficients are algebraic functions of the critical representation and framing, regular at the complete chart. Before selecting a framing section, the result is a formal two-form density on B_1. If r,s are coordinates on that torsor, then its squared leading coefficient is a_(beta,0)^2 det(partial chi/partial(r,s))^2 /det(-H_perp). (4.2) This formula changes correctly under a different transverse coordinate choice. It does not perform the remaining framing period. Replacing that period by evaluation at an arbitrary framing section would change the selected global construction. ## 5. Formal normal difference transport agrees with the geometric line Let K be a common algebraic function field for the geometric gluing branch and its rational framing section, adjoining the recorded half-density roots. The actual normal block has form Z_act^perp=C_beta(H) exp(S_act/H) A_act(M)(1+sum_(j>=1)H^j A_j(M)). (5.1) C_beta(H) denotes its recorded base-only normalization line, including the fixed product and cut-average constants and powers of H. If a constant Li_2(1) is moved from the phase into this line, that move is recorded on both sides. No value of an individual compact factor at a root is assigned. All variable amplitudes in (5.1) belong to K, and A_act is a unit on the complete chart. The positive triangulation's dual local formal period in the geometric rigidity note has the same property. Its leading action satisfies the same preferred-longitude differential as S_act, and both complete imaginary values equal Vol(M). Their leading difference is therefore an M-constant real phase, retained in the comparison line. Use epsilon=H=2h, h=Log q, throughout. After retaining those base-only lines, the ratio of the two normal amplitudes is an explicitly recursively computable g(M,h) in K[[h]]^times. (5.2) It is their quotient of formal Gaussian series. The leading term is the ratio of the algebraic unit amplitudes; every higher coefficient follows by finite division in K. Thus, for their actual meridian-step ratios with sigma(M)=exp(h)M, a_act^perp=a_geo * sigma(g)/g. (5.3) Equivalently their formal period connections differ by h dLog g, with all leading longitude and lift characters matched. This proves a formal normal-connection comparison to all orders. It is not merely a comparison of leading dilogarithmic symbols. The full ADO factor d_N(M), including its root-central difference constant, remains the original one. It is not absorbed into the coefficientwise formal unit (5.2). Its local nodal density comparison is the separate exact result of the preceding note. ## 6. What this does and does not select The normal block comes from the actual coefficient model and has nonzero principal amplitude. The remaining framing density and its boundary source have not been paired with the actual finite cut cycle. Equation (5.3) consequently does not identify the quantum-A module of the selected finite sum, its root monodromy eigenline, or its complete value with this normal block. In particular no conclusion about a geometric factor of the minimal summed operator follows just from the nonzero normal block: taking the remaining relative period can kill a class. The whole selected root source and its lattice still have to be transported, including all polar intersections and caps. Nor are the formal series assumed to converge or to control their selected value along h=pi*i/N. The volume-norm theorem is still required for the original F_N(1). There is a concrete check against a tempting simplification. The raw normal framing density is not automatically a constant Haar form. At the figure-eight algebraic critical point over F_97 with Riley root 36, frames (r,s)=(2,3),(3,2) give squared two-form coefficients 92 and 77. Multiplication by s^2 gives 52 and 17, and multiplication by s^4 gives 80 and 68. Thus neither dr ds/s nor dr ds/s^2 is the raw coefficient density up to a frame-independent multiplier. A global framing comparison needs its specified quantum adapters and boundary source, not an assumed group-volume factor. There is also an exact characteristic-zero calculation on the full framing chart. Put t=(1-sqrt(-3))/2 and tau_cusp=2-4t. The squared coefficient of dr ds in the same normal two-form is f_perp(r,s)^2=-tau_cusp/[6 s^2(s+1)^2]. (6.1) The [full two-variable audit](../experiments/audit_full_framing_density.py) retains both framing derivatives and checks the two Hessian null vectors in Q(sqrt(-3))(s,r). Exact polynomial arithmetic proves independence of r on this figure-eight chart. [Results](../experiments/full_framing_density_results.json). The [regular meridian centralizer](regular_meridian_centralizer.md) now explains the additional (s+1) divisor. Its invariant two-form adapted to the actual cut coordinate is Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(s+1)], so (6.1) says exactly Omega_perp^2=(-tau_cusp/6)Omega_cut^2. Contracting the latter with its centralizer vector s partial_r gives dlog A_cut, A_cut=1/(1+s). This identifies the geometric quotient form; it does not yet prove that the original finite source and its selected cut implement this contraction. Neither the formula for every knot nor that period comparison is assumed. The subsequent [actual cut-residue/density calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) now derives the logarithmic cut co-source directly from the original finite average. Both original crossing amplitudes have a mixed-Hessian/momentum-coboundary factorization; the momentum factors cancel on every critical closure and leave the original pivot. The corrected ambient phase volume is invariant under the regular-meridian centralizer. A linearized fixed-point complex supplies an invariant torsion under a stated rigidity hypothesis. Identifying that determinant line with this normal Gaussian density and transporting the selected internal source remain work. ## 7. Precisely where the ideal triangulation theorem enters The positive triangulation theorem supplies more than a numerical expression for volume. Its geometric shapes produce the marked Bloch representative beta_T, with D(beta_T)=Vol(M); Section 3 uses positivity to prove an invertible marked gluing Jacobian. Development then transports this rigidity to the actual critical scheme. Sections 4--5 consequently construct a nonzero transverse formal block from the original crossing coefficients and compare its connection with the geometric regulator line. These implications use the ideal triangulation theorem at the geometric realization and rigidity step. They do not assert that the theorem supplies a quantum source, a selected relative period, or a quantum comparison along arbitrary changes of triangulation. In particular, the algebraically split framing torsor does not fix a pairing of (4.2) with the original cut cycle. Selecting an ordinary algebraic frame and selecting a horizontal pointed relative period are different operations. This gives a precise route for the next theorem. Transport the actual relative source, its integral lattice, and its full cut through a tetrahedral presentation to the positive triangulation. Retain the marked meridian, longitude lift, and peripheral factors throughout. The selected resulting relative class must pair nontrivially with the normal block above. The required comparison concerns this class and its period, rather than just the critical equations or the existence of an unpointed module isomorphism. Control of that selected period's regulator norm across levels is additional to the local formal comparison. ## 8. An exact obstruction for a proposed source comparison When the two proposed source objects admit specified equal-rank affine presentations over the same difference field (F,sigma), write them as sigma(v)=C_K v+c_K, sigma(w)=C_T w+c_T. (8.1) This is a conditional comparison criterion; neither the existence of a global geometric inhomogeneous factor for every knot nor a selected triangulation source is assumed to have been proved. A change w=Gv+t with G invertible intertwines (8.1) exactly when sigma(G) C_K=C_T G, (sigma-C_T)t=c_T-sigma(G)c_K. (8.2) The first equation compares the homogeneous connections. Once it is solved, the remaining obstruction is the explicit additive class [c_T-sigma(G)c_K] in F^d/(sigma-C_T)F^d. (8.3) Indeed, with H_aug=[G t;0 1] and U_i=[C_i c_i;0 1], the identity sigma(H_aug)U_K=U_T H_aug is exactly the two equations (8.2). Thus this obstruction concerns the horizontal affine extension, not the existence of points on its underlying affine space. The geometric gluing germ does not determine (8.3). For an elementary demonstration take F=C(q,M), sigma(M)=qM and C=1. The sources c=0 and c=1 have the same homogeneous connection, but are inequivalent: sigma(t)-t=1 has no rational solution. Expand any t in C(q)((M)); the constant Laurent coefficient of sigma(t)-t is zero, whereas that of 1 is one. This proves the claim without a growth argument. It does not model a hyperbolic knot; it isolates the additional datum any comparison must retain. Even a solution of (8.2) over a completed field is only a formal extension comparison. To identify actual selected periods one must also transport the source-one section p, the meridian lattice Lambda, and the augmented cut functional lambda: p_T=H_aug p_K, Lambda_T=H_aug Lambda_K, lambda_T H_aug=lambda_K. (8.4) Whenever these identities hold in the actual whole-germ period realization, they give lambda_T(p_T)=lambda_K(p_K), including at a marked specialization where the common lattice makes the period regular. Equation (5.3) solves only the homogeneous formal normal comparison; it does not establish (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual relative source. Finite-cover descent alone cannot fill this gap, as the trace argument in the [affine-source note](affine_quantum_a_period.md) shows. This is the explicit source-compatible comparison for which the positive ideal triangulation supplies the geometric target. ### When the source comparison also determines the period There is a useful conditional reduction at a root. Work over a coefficient field E with sigma of finite order n; for the actual M coordinate and q_N this can be n=2N. Suppose both specified source extensions in (8.1) have nonresonant cyclic monodromy, det(I-H_K)det(I-H_T)!=0. Their rational horizontal source-one sections are unique, by the cyclic descent proof in [the affine-source note](affine_quantum_a_period.md): v_K=(I-H_K)^(-1)s_K, v_T=(I-H_T)^(-1)s_T. Iterating the actual affine comparison (8.2) around the orbit gives G H_K=H_T G, s_T=G s_K+(I-H_T)t. Substitution therefore proves exactly v_T=G v_K+t. Thus an independent choice of rational horizontal section is unnecessary under these hypotheses. When the specified selected sections belong to this rational solution space and the cut and lattice are also transported, their scalar periods agree, including a common regular complete specialization. Nonresonance may fail at the complete point: the equality is first an equality of rational whole germs, then is evaluated on the specified common lattice. This is not a proof of those hypotheses for the actual geometric source. In a resonant block homogeneous rational sections remain, and the original pointing must still be supplied. Nor does a separately chosen root-level affine gauge control the comparison across levels: a nonresonant extension always has a rootwise rational splitting. A fixed generic comparison, or another proved uniform realization with its normalization, is still required. The triangulation theorem supplies the geometric chart on which to seek that comparison; it does not construct the gauge or prove the selected period's regulator norm. The subsequent [common period-space construction](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) now records this geometric action line together with the actual Frobenius and Tate marks over one logarithmic Heisenberg connection. Its phase and norm identities are exact. A source-cohomology retraction shows why that enlargement alone cannot split an existing generic source. It does not prove (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual knot period or control the selected realization of the formal amplitude (5.2). The subsequent [actual cut-wall source calculation](cut_wall_and_cyclic_source.md) now identifies a local part of this comparison. The normalized actual cut has consecutive wall factors p,sigma(p); its regularized dual presentation and the geometric cyclic lattice have the same point source. An explicit regular formal unit calibrates the geometric collision to the actual wall, including its residue. The full ADO common frame is retained. This is a comparison of local presentations over S, not a solution of (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual global source and selected knot section. ## 9. Exact checks and coverage [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normal_stationary_period.py) verifies all six exact internal first-transport identities and both meridian half-step identities symbolically from (2.3)--(2.6). Twenty-four independent geometric charts use both algebraic Riley roots over F_97,F_193,F_601 and four different regular frames per root. The Hessian is constructed from the actual phase, while its null vectors are differentiated from independent representation matrices. Each five-variable Hessian has rank three and precisely the two framing null directions. Every selected transverse determinant and actual principal amplitude is nonzero. The meridian deformation tangent satisfies the mixed Hessian equation, and the reduced second derivative is twice the independently computed marked longitude derivative. These are validations of the uniform scheme and Gaussian arguments, not volume experiments. The additional univariate function-field certificate proves (6.1) and checks both framing null vectors before the stated restriction. [Results](../experiments/actual_normal_stationary_period_results.json). Critical-point existence and optimistic-limit potentials have the coverage already recorded in the marked-braid note. Formal stationary phase and formal difference connections likewise have existing coverage in the earlier comparison notes. No published proof is assumed here and no novelty claim is made. The result added here is the particular normal-block comparison in the original coefficient conventions, with the actual subprincipal color, pivot and half-step factors retained. The subsequent [uniform density theorem](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) now gives the intrinsic variable principal coefficient for arbitrary knot braids: its parity-normalized square is -T_beta Omega_cut^2/2. The Gaussian kernel and self-dual cokernel are explicitly matched to the endpoint cut complex. Thus the determinant identification is no longer limited to the two prototype knots. Its base-only quantum normalization and selected global period remain unproved. Reproduce the finite and symbolic first-transport diagnostics with: python3 experiments/audit_actual_normal_stationary_period.py

title: The whole original source as an exactly charged bridge-flow coefficient
text: # The whole original source as an exactly charged bridge-flow coefficient 28 October 2026. After the exact simultaneous overbridge reduction, ALL remaining understrand anchor sums can also be performed exactly. The result is a finite charged coefficient, with one charge N-1 at every anchor. There are no extra cyclic alias sectors in this whole coefficient. This follows from nonnegative polynomial degree and global homogeneity, with the original closed-braid source retained. This is a larger closed algebra than the isolated complementary Pochhammer class. Its coefficients remain coupled and oscillatory. It does not prove a positive state, geometric selection or scalar noncancellation. ## 1. Use the original scalar source before splitting Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), s=x^N. Let W be ANY original complete signed braid word on b heads, in the balanced factorial basis. Every actual crossing preserves total INTEGER head degree. The original closed-head pivots are diagonal, g_a=(x/s)Q^(-a). Therefore the original one-cut partial trace is diagonal on its remaining head. The original averaged marked row, with every entry 1/N, has exactly the same scalar pairing as I/N on this already assembled diagonal matrix. Hence the actual scalar is K_N=chi_N/N *Tr[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g) W]. (1) The external original dimension/framing line chi_N remains. This uses integer-degree conservation BEFORE any Fourier or bridge decomposition. It is not a sectorwise replacement of the marked row, a claim about arbitrary inserted currents, or an extra pivotal trace. Put W in the exact regular propagated frames. This removes every interior Fourier adapter. At closure head i retain its exact adapter, including the pivot when i>1. If Z is its final-grid input and Y its initial-grid output, the kernel is E_i(Y,Z)=eta_i/N *Z^(-d) C_i(Z,Y), C_i(Z,Y)=sum_(a=0)^d Z^(d-a)(t_i Y)^a, (eta_1,t_1)=(1,1), (eta_i,t_i)=(x/s,Q^(-1)), i>1. (2) This is the finite Fourier sum, including its removable values. Its numerator is a homogeneous d-form. Equivalently C_i(Z,Y)=product_(r=1)^d (Z-Q^r t_i Y). (3) Every nontrivial boundary adapter stays in (2). Matching incompatible central grids or replacing it by an identity is unnecessary. ## 2. Each reduced overbridge is a homogeneous d-form Use the exact [signed overbridge theorem](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md). An overbridge e has m encounters in physical strand order, signs sigma_j, clocks d>=h_1>=...>=h_m>=0, and spectator UNDER outputs u_j. Its conditional crossing parameters can be written a_j=alpha_j/u_j, b_j=beta_j u_j, alpha_j=Q^(-h_j)/x, beta_j=Q^(h_j+1), sigma_j=+1, alpha_j=Qx, beta_j=Q, sigma_j=-1. In either case alpha_j beta_j=Q^2x. Write Delta_j=h_j-h_(j+1), and f_sigma(h)=(-1)^h Q^(sigma*h(h+1)/2). Define the explicit factor Gamma_e=kappa^(sum_j sigma_j) *product_j f_(sigma_j)(h_j) *product_(j<m) [(-alpha_j)^(h_(j+1)) Q^(h_(j+1)(h_(j+1)-1)/2)] *F_(h_1)/[F_(h_m) product_(j<m)F_(Delta_j)], F_r=(Q;Q)_r. (4) Every factorial index in (4) is at most d. All crossing normalizers are now explicit. In particular the powers N from the internal strand sums and the factors 1/N at crossings leave precisely 1/N for this ENTIRE bridge. Let Zin and Zout be its overstrand endpoint variables. Directly clearing the denominators in the exact bridge formula gives B_e=Gamma_e/N *Zin^(-d) P_e(Zin,Zout,u_1,...,u_m), (5) P_e= product_(0<=r<d-h_1)(Zin-Q^r beta_1 u_1) *product_(j<m) product_(0<=r<Delta_j) (u_j-Q^(r-1)alpha_j beta_(j+1)u_(j+1)) *product_(0<=r<h_m)(u_m-Q^r alpha_m Zout). (6) The three collections have lengths d-h_1, sum Delta_j, h_m. Their total is EXACTLY d. Thus P_e is a homogeneous degree-d polynomial with no negative powers, even when spectator variables later coincide or particular coefficients vanish. Equation (5) has only ONE denominator, at the overbridge input. For example each link denominator u_j^(Delta_j) is canceled by the corresponding spectator powers of the closed crossing scalar and link monomial. The last spectator power clears the last output Pochhammer; the input endpoint becomes Zin^(-d). This is an exact polynomial identity, not a modulus estimate. ## 3. Understrand clocks and a global bijection At a signed crossing the overclock from the actual port table is label_under,out=label_under,in-sigma*h (mod N), z_under,out=x^sigma z_under,in Q^(-sigma*h). (7) The label equation holds for both signs, with the table's physical over/under conventions. The root equation also uses the actual propagated roots, not an independently imposed meridian value. Regard every compressed overbridge and every retained closure adapter (2) as an event with one physical input and one output. Cut the oriented strand at these events. Between successive events the remaining encounters are exclusively UNDER encounters. Untouched head identities have already been suppressed. If there are B overbridge events, there are k=B+b events and exactly k intervening directed segments. The closure adapter events break any directed cycle of under encounters, even on a link component which is always under in the open braid. Assign one anchor variable X_a to the first grid port on each such segment. Starting there, (7) gives EVERY port on the segment as z_v=zeta_v(h) X_a, zeta_v=x^(sum_previous sigma) Q^(-sum_previous sigma*h). (8) For fixed clocks the map from the segment anchor label to its port labels is a cyclic translation. Conversely a collection of the old segment labels determines each h by (7) and its initial anchor label. Thus the change from all remaining port labels to the crossing clocks h and k anchor labels is a BIJECTION, of counting Jacobian one. No congruence sectors are thrown away. Every anchor segment ends at the input of exactly one event. Thus, after (8), it acquires exactly ONE denominator X_a^d, from (2) or (5). The phase zeta_event,input^(-d) is retained in the event factor. All event output and spectator variables in their numerators are also substituted by (8). No selected-overbridge variable reappears. Write P_h(X) for the product of these k substituted event numerator polynomials, and W_h=product_overbridges Gamma_e *product_closure eta_i *product_events zeta_event,input^(-d). (9) The root substitutions in each event polynomial preserve degree, so P_h has nonnegative exponents and TOTAL degree k d. Its coefficients and W_h are fully explicit functions of Q,x,kappa,h; they do not depend on an unknown knot period or on the initial Fermat centers. The latter only specify the anchor sampling grids. ## 4.
