Exact disappearance of EVERY cyclic anchor alias The complete source (1), after the bijection and simultaneous overbridge reduction, is K_N=chi_N/N *N^(-k) sum_(h over-monotone) W_h sum_(X_a^N=C_a, all a) [product_a X_a^(-d)] P_h(X). (10) Each C_a is the actual fixed nonzero central value at its segment anchor. It need not be one. Every event contributes its exact 1/N; there are k events. Expand a monomial X^e in P_h. Root sampling can keep it only if e_a-d=N l_a, for integers l_a, all a. But e_a>=0 and d=N-1 imply l_a>=0. Global homogeneity gives sum_a N l_a=sum_a e_a-kd=0. Therefore ALL l_a are zero. The argument includes arbitrarily large single-variable degrees: there is no omitted high-degree positive alias, because it would require a negative alias elsewhere, which the lower bound -d excludes. Consequently, termwise in h, sum_(X_a^N=C_a) [product X_a^(-d)]P_h(X) =N^k [X_1^d ... X_k^d]P_h(X). (11) There are no powers of the C_a on the right. This proves exact frame-center independence of the WHOLE anchored coefficient at each clock assignment, without deleting a separate current sector. Substituting into (10) gives the final original-source identity K_N=chi_N/N *sum_(h over-monotone) W_h [X_1^d ... X_k^d]P_h(X). (12) All k finite anchor sums have been evaluated. Their N^k cancels the N^(-k) event normalizations EXACTLY. The remaining 1/N is the original averaged first-cut source in (1), not a guessed normalization. ## 5. The resulting charged flow algebra and its scope Every event polynomial is a product of d explicit linear differences of anchors; closure uses (3). Expanding these factors chooses an endpoint anchor for each factor. The coefficient in (12) keeps exactly d choices at EACH anchor. Thus it is a finite nonnegative integer-charge flow problem, with a complex unit-phase weight on each choice. The overbridge clock domain is the independent product of monotone simplexes, equivalently the compositions (d-h_1,Delta_1,...,Delta_(m-1),h_m), all >=0, sum=d. The polynomial coefficient algebra is closed under further anchor elimination: taking one degree-d coefficient preserves nonnegative polynomial exponents and lowers total degree by d. It does not preserve the isolated two-Pochhammer factorization. It is in this larger EXACT charged algebra that the understrand elimination closes; no tuned Vandermonde identity or discarded boundary term is required. ### Exact anchor-cycle transport and charged source currents For every FIXED h the period in (12) is the specified Laurent polynomial form (1/(2*pi*i)^k) integral P_h(X) product_a dX_a/X_a^(d+1). (13) It has no finite noncoordinate poles. Consequently the product circle radii can be changed to ANY finite positive radii, with the original coefficient and source unchanged. This is a literal torus homotopy in (C*)^k; it does not use the raw off-grid four-Psi continuation. Its linear-form zeros are zeros, not residue divisors. No discarded Phi seam, Cauchy collision or unretained cyclic carry is needed for this anchor-radius transport. Escape to zero/infinity is not part of the assertion. The exact charged Ward current at each anchor is [X^d](X_a partial_(X_a)-d)P_h=0. (14) More generally the integral of X_a partial_(X_a)[F P_h product_b X_b^(-d)] against product_b dX_b/X_b is zero, for a Laurent-polynomial test F. After multiplying by the FULL W_h and summing h it is still zero. This is a current of the proved charged representation, not a claim that arbitrary new matrix coupons preserve its previous root-grid support theorem. If none of the linear forms L_r vanishes, the finite-N stationary anchor equations of (13) in logarithmic coordinates are explicitly sum_r c_(r,a) X_a/L_r(X)=d, all a, L_r(X)=sum_a c_(r,a)X_a. (15) Thus the stationary current is a rational charge-balance equation. Each form contributes total one, so the sum of (15) is the known identity kd=kd. One common scale is redundant. Exactly, without an asymptotic argument, [X_1^d...X_k^d]P_h(X) =[Y_1^d...Y_(k-1)^d]P_h(Y_1,...,Y_(k-1),1). (16) This follows from total degree kd. It removes the common C* scale from the actual source period. Neither (15) nor (16) by itself identifies its stationary scheme with the knot A-curve; the remaining clock equations and their actual source selection must also be proved. ### The exact grouped graph connection Let q=exp(pi*i/N). A block of length 0<=L<=d has the form product_(r=0)^(L-1)(alpha X_i-Q^r beta X_j). Its coefficient with j-charge a is alpha^L S_(L,a) w^a X_i^(L-a)X_j^a, w=-(beta/alpha)q^(L-1), S_(L,a)=product_(r=1)^L sin(pi*r/N) /[product_(r=1)^a sin(pi*r/N) product_(r=1)^(L-a) sin(pi*r/N)] >0. (17) This follows from [L choose a]_Q=q^(a(L-a))S_(L,a), together with the q-binomial expansion. Thus the phase is LINEAR in the block charge after a fixed block phase is removed; it is not a quadratic approximation. For the actual blocks in (6), after the undertransport (8), the connection phases are exactly input: w=q^(sigma_1*h_1) zeta_(u_1)/zeta_(Zin), link j: w=q^(sigma_(j+1)*h_(j+1)-sigma_j*h_j) zeta_(u_(j+1))/zeta_(u_j), output: w=q^(-sigma_m*h_m) zeta_(Zout)/zeta_(u_m), closure: w=t_i zeta_(Zout)/zeta_(Zin). (18) For closure the first argument in its length-d block starts at Q, as in (3), which makes its residual phase exactly the actual pivot t_i=1 or Q^(-1). No extra half-turn is hidden in (18). Within one bridge, (18) telescopes using the local potentials q^(sigma_j*h_j)zeta_(u_j) and the unshifted endpoint potentials. That fact alone is not global flatness: distinct spectator ports u_j can belong to the SAME under-anchor segment and have different local potentials. A gauge test must use the actual grouped graph and differences of FEASIBLE charge flows, including its capacities, rather than an unsupported abstract cycle. The audit exposes this graph through graph_blocks(H,S,h). Its metadata records every block's anchor endpoints, length, event type, and exact integer q-exponents for alpha,beta,w, modulo 2N. It also records the baseline outgoing degree at each anchor. If a block chooses head charge a_e in [0,L_e], the exact charge equations are sum_(head=i) a_e-sum_(tail=i) a_e =d-sum_(tail=i)L_e. (19) These metadata reproduce the whole polynomial coefficient, with (17) and all fixed block phases retained. They do not assert that the connection has trivial holonomy on the feasible-flow lattice. Equation (12) is stronger than retaining a generic higher hypergeometric remainder at every underbridge. It supplies the complete source charge at all anchors and removes all cyclic carry ambiguity from those sums. It does not make the remaining h/flow sum positive. The phases in (4), (8), and the linear forms remain; they can produce cancellation. Identifying a global geometric critical branch and its selected coefficient is still required. No broad scalar volume limit follows solely from (12). For literature COVERAGE only, quantum-determinant presentations of the Kashaev invariant were already reported by [Huynh--Le, *On the Colored Jones Polynomial and the Kashaev invariant*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503296). The abstract also proposes comparing that determinant with a determinant expression for hyperbolic volume. No determinant formula or analytic proof from that paper is used here, and no novelty claim for coefficient/determinant reformulations in general is intended. The independent statement proved above is the exact original-source clock bijection, event charge and absence of cyclic anchor aliases. The proof is for the original complete braid word and its stated scalar source. An inserted degree-changing coupon need not permit (1) and would need its own charged source form. The theorem does not discard such a coupon or claim the same charge automatically. ## 6. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.py The audit verifies the signed undertransport and event/segment bijection, pointwise homogeneous bridge forms with all original normalizations, the alias-free root-grid coefficient identity, and the full formula (12) against original signed physical word matrices and their actual averaged pivotal scalar, including its external framing/dimension line.

text: # Global real-spectral gap of the actual all-CROSS source , 31 October 2026. This estimates the original CROSS path sectors on the entire real spectral interval. The local bound is a weighted VALUE bound, not a coefficientwise strict inequality. The original face Cauchy period and its previously proved angular gap are retained when sewing. No moving one-sided sector is included. ## 1. Original cofactors and a uniform slow-transfer upper bound Put $h=1/N$, $s_j=2\sin(\pi jh)$, $$ \alpha_r(\delta)=4\cos^2\!\left(\pi(r+\tfrac12)h\right)-4\sin^2(\pi\delta), \qquad A=x+y>0,\quad P=xy\geq0. $$ where every nonzero face weight lies in a fixed positive compact and protected zeros stay EXACTLY zero. The terminal indices $n$ below satisfy $n=N/2+O(1)$ and $n\leq N/2$, with a fixed bound on the $O(1)$. The [literal cofactor](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) has its exact start decomposition $$ \begin{aligned} R_n(b,\delta)&=\sum_{i=0}^n b^i\left(\prod_{r=0}^{i-1}\alpha_r(\delta)\right)K_{i,n},\\ K_{i,i}&=1,\qquad K_{i,i-1}=0,\\ K_{i,j}&=s_j^2A K_{i,j-1}+s_js_{j-1}\alpha_{j-1}(\delta)P K_{i,j-2}. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ This is the original cleared cofactor, without a changed starting row. For $b=0$ only $i=0$ occurs. Negative $\alpha$ factors are not replaced in the tail recurrence by their absolute values. Set $L_{i,j}=K_{i,j}/\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r$. Its exact transfer matrix is $$ T_h(t,\delta)=\begin{pmatrix} 2A\sin(\pi t)&4P\left[\cos^2\!\left(\pi(t-h/2)\right)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)\right]\\ 1&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad t=jh.\tag{2} $$ For real $0\leq\delta\leq1/2$ its limiting spectral radius is $$ \begin{aligned} \rho(t,\delta)&=A\sin(\pi t)+\sqrt{4P\cos^2(\pi\delta)+(x-y)^2\sin^2(\pi t)},\\ \Lambda(t,\delta)&=2\sin(\pi t)\rho(t,\delta). \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ Indeed the discriminant simplifies to $4[4P\cos^2(\pi\delta)+(x-y)^2\sin^2(\pi t)]\geq0$. The eigenvalues are real and the positive root has magnitude at least that of the other root. In particular $$ ct\leq\rho(t,\delta)\leq C,\qquad ct^2\leq\Lambda(t,\delta)\leq C, \qquad0<t\leq\tfrac12.\tag{4} $$ uniformly in $\delta$, including $x=y$ and $\delta=1/2$. There the limiting matrix can be defective; no eigenbasis is inverted. For every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly in all $i,n$, real $\delta\in[0,1/2]$, and all large $N$, $$ |K_{i,n}|\leq\exp\!\left\{N\int_{i/N}^{1/2}\log\Lambda(t,\delta)\,dt+\varepsilon N\right\}.\tag{5} $$ The same bound, with another $\varepsilon N$ allowance, holds for all face weights in a sufficiently small FIXED complex neighborhood of their reference values, with protected zeros still zero, and $\delta$ in a sufficiently thin FIXED complex strip around the real interval. The reference $\Lambda$ on the right is evaluated at the real weights and $\operatorname{Re}\delta$. All choices depend on $\varepsilon$ and the positive compact, not on the starting row or $N$. Here are details sufficient to include the degeneracy in this claim. First restrict $t$ to $[\eta,1/2]$. The spectral radius is bounded below there. For EVERY real reference matrix $T=T_0(t,\delta)$, Cayley--Hamilton gives $$ \|T^k\|\leq C_\eta(k+1)\rho(t,\delta)^k,\qquad k\geq1.\tag{6} $$ For distinct eigenvalues use the power divided difference, a sum of $k$ terms each bounded by $\rho^{k-1}$; the same polynomial identity includes repeated eigenvalues by its derivative limit. Uniformly bounded $\|T\|$ and $\rho\geq c_\eta$ supply the displayed constant. This is valid even on the entire coalescing line $x=y$, $\delta=1/2$. Choose a FIXED block length $k$ so $\log[2C_\eta(k+1)]/k$ is small. On each block, the exact product differs from the reference constant product by $O_k(h)$, uniformly in the row and $\delta$. The same finite product estimate applies after a sufficiently small fixed perturbation of the face weights and $\delta$. Decrease that perturbation until its error is at most $C_\eta(k+1)\rho^k$. Multiplying the block estimates and using the uniform continuity of $\log\rho$ on $[\eta,1/2]$ gives the integral of $\log\rho$ plus the prescribed small per-row error. The finitely many incomplete blocks cost $o(N)$. Thus no modulus gap, eigenvector condition number, or n-dependent perturbation disk is used. On $t<\eta$ use the bounded transfer entries directly, at cost $C^{\eta N}$. The missing logarithmic integral is bounded in absolute value by $C\eta\log(2/\eta)$, uniformly, by (4). The additional exact factors $s_j$ have the same elementary endpoint bound. First choose $\eta$ small, then $k$ large, then the fixed complex perturbation small, and finally $N$ large. This proves (5). Replacing $n/N$ by $1/2$ costs $o(N)$, since $n$ differs from $N/2$ by only $O(1)$ and $\Lambda$ is bounded away from zero at $1/2$. ## 2. Uniform prefix sums and the exact maximization For real $\delta$ the prefix logarithm obeys the uniform upper Riemann bound $$ \sum_{r<i}\log|\alpha_r(\delta)| \leq N\int_0^{i/N}\log|4\cos(\pi(t+\delta))\cos(\pi(t-\delta))|\,dt+o(N).\tag{7} $$ A zero sampled factor makes that summand zero, so it causes no upper bound problem. To justify uniformity even near the endpoints, truncate the logarithm from below. The truncated function is jointly continuous on the compact $(t,\delta)$ rectangle. Its integrals converge uniformly to the untruncated integrals: the two shifted cosine logarithms have uniformly integrable singularities. Equivalently the level sets of $|4\cos(\pi(t+\delta))\cos(\pi(t-\delta))|$ below $r$ have length $O(\sqrt r)$; integrating their distribution gives the uniform truncation error. The same argument with $\log(|\alpha|+r)$ proves an arbitrarily small additional integral error for a sufficiently small fixed COMPLEX spectral perturbation. No lower bound on the distance to a physical node is assumed. If $b>0$ is perturbed in a small fixed complex face neighborhood, $\lvert b_{\mathrm{complex}}\rvert^i/b^i\leq e^{O(\theta N)}$ for $i\leq N$, with $\theta$ the relative neighborhood size. This is absorbed in the same $\varepsilon N$ allowance. A protected $b=0$ stays exactly zero and has only start $0$. Combining (1), (5), (7), and at most $N+1$ starts gives the uniform weighted upper rate $$ \begin{aligned} \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\lvert R_n(b,\delta)\rvert &\leq\max_{0\leq\mu\leq1/2}F_{\mathrm{abs}}(\mu,\delta),\\ F_{\mathrm{abs}}(\mu,\delta)&=\mu\log b+\int_0^\mu\log|a(t)+u|\,dt +\int_\mu^{1/2}\log\Lambda(t,\delta)\,dt,\\ a(t)&=4\cos^2(\pi t),\qquad u=-4\sin^2(\pi\delta). \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ For $b=0$ the right side means its sole allowed start $\mu=0$. The proof above yields an explicit UNIFORM $\varepsilon N$ version of (8), also in the fixed small face/spectral neighborhoods described after (5). No rate of convergence stronger than that is needed for a strict gap. For $b>0$ put $c=\cos(\pi\delta)$, $z=\sin^2(\pi\mu)$, $w=c^2/z$ and $D_0=(x-y)^2$. At a regular interior point, $$ \partial_\mu F_{\mathrm{abs}}=\log\frac{b\lvert a(\mu)+u\rvert}{\Lambda(\mu,\delta)}, \qquad\frac{b\lvert a+u\rvert}{\Lambda}= \frac{2b\lvert w-1\rvert}{A+\sqrt{D_0+4Pw}}.\tag{9} $$ When $0\leq\delta<1/2$, the sign-change point is $t_c=1/2-\delta$. Before $t_c$, $w$ decreases from infinity to $1$ and the ratio in (9) strictly decreases from infinity to $0$. For $w>1$ its derivative has positive numerator $$ A+\frac{D_0+2Pw+2P}{\sqrt{D_0+4Pw}}, $$ with the $P=0$ case interpreted directly. Thus there is one maximum, at $$ \sin^2(\pi\mu_*)=\frac{c^2b^2}{(b+x)(b+y)},\qquad0<\mu_*<t_c.\tag{10} $$ After $t_c$, $w$ decreases from $1$ and the numerator $1-w$ increases while the denominator decreases. The ratio is strictly increasing whenever this interval is nonempty. Therefore every post-$t_c$ critical point is a MINIMUM, and that part has its maximum at an endpoint. The complete prefix integral is zero: $$ \int_0^{1/2}\log|4\cos(\pi(t+\delta))\cos(\pi(t-\delta))|\,dt=0.\tag{11} $$ This follows by shifting the two intervals and using the reflection and period of $\log|2\cos|$; it also holds at $\delta=0,1/2$ by integrability. Consequently $F_{\mathrm{abs}}(1/2,\delta)=\tfrac12\log b$. The pre-$t_c$ maximum is exactly the original triangle action $Q_b(\delta)$, with its complete normalization. Thus $$ \max_\mu F_{\mathrm{abs}}(\mu,\delta)=\max\left\{Q_b(\delta),\tfrac12\log b\right\}.\tag{12} $$ For $b=0$ it is $Q_0(\delta)$, without the second branch. At $\delta=1/2$, the ratio (9) is the constant $b/\max(x,y)$, so the same statement follows by its endpoint values. In particular $Q_b(1/2)=\tfrac12\log\max(x,y)$, understood as the continuous limit. For clarity, the action identification in (12) uses the proved [cofactor/marked-action identity](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md) near $\delta=0$. The real integral at $\mu_*$ has positive prefix factors and positive $\Lambda$, and is real analytic on $0\leq\delta<1/2$. Its defining formulas have no zero or branch crossing there. The identity therefore continues on this connected real interval. Its endpoint value follows either from (3) at $\delta=1/2$ or from uniform integrability in (8). The cases $P=0$ and $b=0$ use the exact first-order/sole-start formulas and the same limit. ## 3. Strict local spectral decrease, with the monomial exception The actual $Q$ action has the exact real derivative $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{dQ_b}{d\delta}&=-\log\frac{E_b}{\sqrt D},\\ E_b&=A+2b\sin^2(\pi\delta) +2\sin(\pi\delta)\sqrt{bA+P+b^2\sin^2(\pi\delta)},\\ D&=A^2-4P\sin^2(\pi\delta). \end{aligned}\tag{13} $$ For $0<\delta<1/2$ this derivative is strictly negative whenever $b>0$ or $P>0$. The possible logarithmic singularity at $\delta=1/2$, $x=y$ is integrable. Also the interior maximum at $\delta=0$ proves $Q_b(0)>\tfrac12\log b$ when $b>0$ and $A>0$. Therefore, for each $\eta>0$, $$ \max\left\{Q_b(\delta),\tfrac12\log b\right\} \leq Q_b(0)-\gamma_\eta,\qquad\eta\leq\delta\leq\tfrac12.\tag{14} $$ with $\gamma_\eta>0$ on each fixed positive compact of the nonzero weights, provided $b>0$ or $P>0$. For $b=0$ omit the second branch. The sole exception $b=0$, $P=0$ is the literal one-variable monomial; its cofactor is independent of $\delta$, and no false gap is claimed. Every actual port has $A=x+y>0$: its outer pair is MATCHING, whereas the two protected faces share the original MAIN edge. It has at least one nonmonomial triangle. Indeed, if one outer face vanishes, there remains only one other protected zero, so at least one middle is positive. If both outers are positive, $P>0$ in both triangles. Thus each port's product of two cofactors has a strict gap in (14) when its spectral $\delta$ stays away from $0$. The exact even/odd central cofactor formulas contain two or three products, each with BOTH triangle cofactors and terminal indices $N/2+O(1)$. All central coefficients have bounded degree and bounded size on the fixed face/spectral compact. Therefore (8)-(14) imply $$ |P_{N,\mathrm{cross}}(\delta;\text{positive faces})| \leq\exp\!\left\{N\left[Q_b(0)+Q_c(0)-\gamma_\eta+o(1)\right]\right\}, \qquad\eta\leq|\delta|\leq\tfrac12.\tag{15} $$ Uniform $\varepsilon$ versions hold on a small fixed complex neighborhood of the reference faces and a fixed thin complex $\delta$ strip. This follows from the proof of (5),(7), not from coefficientwise domination by the value at positive faces. For all $\delta$ the same estimate without $-\gamma_\eta$ holds. In particular every other port has a controlled endpoint rate while one separated port supplies a strict loss. ## 4. Sewing the original marked Cauchy period Fix the actual positive complete ordinary radii, with both protected variables zero. Their endpoint weighted exponent after the original degree-$d$ targets is $\Phi_D$. Take the exact all-CROSS marked coefficient $C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$, with its original simultaneous-rotation quotient or, equivalently, the full original Cauchy torus. Outside a fixed neighborhood of the common ordinary-face phase, the already proved [global cofactor angular theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) supplies a strict exponential gap, uniformly for ALL real spectral deltas. Its proof retains all terminal cofactors and every central summand; it also holds in a sufficiently thin fixed complex spectral strip. Inside a sufficiently small fixed common-phase neighborhood, use (15) and its proved small complex FACE extension. If $\max_i|\operatorname{Re}\delta_i|\geq\eta$, at least one port supplies $\gamma_\eta$, while all the other ports cost only their endpoint rates and arbitrarily small chosen errors. Since the graph is fixed, choose those errors so their sum is less than half that loss. The common face phase cancels exactly by total degree and original targets. No independent face radii are optimized. It follows that for each fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $\tau,\gamma>0$, $N_0$ such that $$ |C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)|\leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}.\tag{16} $$ for $N\geq N_0$, all $\operatorname{Re}\delta_i\in[-1/2,1/2]$ with $\max_i|\operatorname{Re}\delta_i|\geq\eta$, and $|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq\tau$. To include boundary neighborhoods cleanly, first prove the real decrease for $\eta/2$ and then shrink $\tau$. Every fixed derivative has the same strict rate on a smaller strip by Cauchy's estimate. Both level parities are included. This is an actual GLOBAL spectral gap of the all-CROSS shared source, away from the geometric point on the centered fold cover. It is not a coefficientwise strict inequality and it is not a global FULL-V theorem. Genuine moving one-sided paths can violate the corresponding full coefficient bound, as the previously recorded $\sigma=\sqrt3$ example shows. Any use of (16) in the original Fourier period must still retain whole-domain charge summation and its endpoint currents. The [whole all-CROSS period theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) performs that transfer and obtains the filled-volume asymptotic for this sector. It does not identify the all-CROSS sector with the full invariant. ## Scope and focused finite checks The equality in (12) concerns the absolute envelope. Equation (8) is a limsup bound for the actual cofactor; cancellation can make its rate smaller. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_global_cross_spectral_gap_results.json) check four symbolic identities, 120 original recurrence/start-sum identities, 26,880 rescaled tail entries and 240 finite characteristic identities at 65 digits, across both parities and all stated zero patterns. Author replay maximum relative identity error was 1.26e-64. Its 120 finite weighted-rate comparisons are explicitly diagnostics. They do not substitute for the uniform proof or numerically verify the original shared coefficient gap.

title: A global spectral bound for an actual diagonal source sector
text: # A global spectral bound for an actual diagonal source sector analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This concerns the original homogeneous face polynomial and its original shared marked coefficient. The triangular-basis diagonal sector is not identified with the identity operator. A coefficientwise inequality reduces its absolute bound to an actual identity-inserted positive source. ## 1. The exact diagonal polynomial and a uniform real bound Let $N\geq3$, $d=N-1$, and $$ \chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2, \qquad c_j=2\cos\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{N},\quad 0\leq j<N. $$ In the original triangular face representation, $\Omega$ has diagonal $c_j$ and lowers the face degree by one or two. The zero-step part of its actual resolvent numerator is $$ \begin{aligned} V_N(\sigma)&=\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega)^{-1},\\ D_N(\sigma;b,c)&=\sum_{j=0}^{d}d_j(\sigma)b^jc^{d-j}, &d_j(\sigma)&=\frac{\chi_N(\sigma)}{\sigma-c_j}. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Every quotient is a polynomial, including all repeated and simple spectral nodes. This is exactly the part of $H_{V_N}$ with zero outer exponents. The middle names $b,c$ and their original orientation are unchanged. It is a restriction of the homogeneous coefficient polynomial, not an assertion that the physical kernel has been diagonalized or made into an identity. For every real $\sigma\in[-2,2]$, $$ |d_j(\sigma)|\leq N^2.\tag{2} $$ Indeed, $\chi_N(c_j)=0$ and the real mean-value integral gives $$ d_j(\sigma)=\int_0^1\chi_N'\bigl(c_j+t(\sigma-c_j)\bigr)\,dt. $$ For $z=2\cos\theta$, $$ \chi_N'(z)=N U_{N-1}(\cos\theta),\qquad U_{N-1}(\cos\theta)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}e^{i(N-1-2r)\theta}. $$ Its modulus is at most $N$, including the endpoint limits. Thus the removable values are handled automatically, and $$ |D_N(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}}\leq N^2 H_1(b,c), \qquad H_1(b,c)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}b^jc^{d-j}.\tag{3} $$ This is an upper bound, not an equality or a phase-preserving replacement of $d_j$ by $1$. The weight in (1) depends on both $j$ and $\sigma$. Since $d_j$ has degree $d$, there is also a uniform complex-cover bound: $$ \bigl|d_j(-2\cos(2\pi\delta))\bigr| \leq N^2 e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}.\tag{4} $$ For completeness, if a polynomial $p$ of degree $d$ is bounded by $M$ on $[-1,1]$, then $w^{-d}p((w+w^{-1})/2)$ is holomorphic outside the unit disk and at infinity, with boundary modulus at most $M$. The exterior maximum principle gives $|p((w+w^{-1})/2)|\leq M|w|^d$. Apply this with $p(z)=d_j(-2z)$ and $|w|=e^{2\pi|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$. No division by distance to a spectral node occurs. ## 2. The positive identity-inserted reference at both parities For the original fixed certified diagram $D$, let $F_N$ denote its actual positive Fejér reference coupon: $$ F_N= \begin{cases} (-1)^dV_N(-2),&N\text{ even},\\ V_N(-2)-N^{-2}V_N'(-2),&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases} $$ Fix a nonempty set $I$ of ports carrying the literal identity coupon. Let $Z_{I,N}$ be the original shared marked coefficient with $H_1$ at $I$ and $H_{F_N}$ elsewhere. Every original ordinary target is $d$; the two original protected targets are zero. The [strict identity-insertion theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md), Section 6, gives at even levels a compact full-flow maximum $W_I<\Phi_D$, where $\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$, or a zero source when the flow is infeasible. Its proof uses an actual representation of the original drilled group killing an essential deleted auxiliary meridian, together with the canonical general-peripheral volume bound. It does not bound independent pieces with unrelated marks. The same rate applies at odd levels. This does not differentiate an even identity: the odd regularized coefficient theorem gives the same uniform local full-simplex entropy $h$ for $H_{F_N}$, while $H_1$ has exact coefficient $1$ on its middle edge and zero elsewhere. Removing the two outer arcs at identity ports leaves the same integral bipartite-flow rounding with literal degree $d$. Compact Laplace therefore gives, at both parities, $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_{I,N}=W_I<\Phi_D.\tag{5} $$ If the flow is infeasible, every finite coefficient is zero. This includes an identity edge joining the two protected roots: it cannot supply positive degree $d$ to either zero target. No protected radius is replaced by a positive surrogate. ## 3. Two strict-gap consequences for the actual spectral sectors First take one port $i$ in the pure-middle diagonal sector (1), with arbitrary $\sigma_i\in[-2,2]$. Allow every other port to retain its full numerator, provided $|\sigma_j+2|\leq r$. The [original unused-row majorant](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md), Section 3, gives $$ |H_{V_N(\sigma_j)}|_{\mathrm{coef}}\leq M_N(r)H_{F_N}, \qquad M_N(r)\leq\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N\theta(r)}, \qquad\theta(r)=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+r/2).\tag{6} $$ At odd levels the factor $\max(1,N^2r)$ in $M_N$ is essential. Bare $H_{V_N(-2)}$ is not an odd majorant. Taking absolute coefficients before multiplying and extracting the one original marked target proves the finite inequality $$ |Z_{\mathrm{diag}\ i;\,\mathrm{full\ elsewhere}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \leq N^2M_N(r)^{R-1}Z_{\{i\},N}.\tag{7} $$ Choose fixed $r>0$ so $(R-1)\theta(r)$ is smaller than half the positive gap $\Phi_D-W_{\{i\}}$. Equation (5) gives $\gamma>0$ and $N_0$ such that, uniformly in this region and at both parities, $$ |Z_{\mathrm{diag}\ i;\,\mathrm{full\ elsewhere}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)},\qquad N\geq N_0.\tag{8} $$ If the identity reference is zero, the sector is identically zero. Constants depend on the original fixed diagram. No independently framed norm or unproved physical smoothing has been used. Second, if all other ports are restricted to their actual CROSS sectors, those ports may range over the entire real spectral interval. The [exact cofactor interpolation theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), Section 8, gives $$ |P_{N,\mathrm{cross}}(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}} \leq C\log^2(N+1)P_{N,\mathrm{cross}}(-2) \leq C\log^2(N+1)H_{F_N},\qquad \sigma\in[-2,2].\tag{9} $$ Combining (3) and (9) with the same marked extraction gives (8) uniformly over the full real spectral cube. The proof applies to any fixed nonempty collection $I$ of diagonal ports, using $Z_{I,N}$, with CROSS elsewhere. This is an inequality for every original coefficient; it neither identifies the restricted quantum sector with a smoothed representation nor asserts absence of cancellation. Both conclusions persist on a sufficiently small fixed complex strip in each globally varying $\delta$ coordinate. Equation (4) and the strip version of (9) add at most $2\pi N\sum_j|\operatorname{Im}\delta_j|$ to the exponent. Shrink the strip so this and the cost in (6) fit within the strict gap in (5). Polynomial factors contribute $o(N)$. ## 4. The entire original Fourier period of the diagonal/CROSS sector Use the global case of Section 3: a fixed nonempty set $I$ is pure diagonal and every other port is CROSS. For a disjoint path partition, remove the odd central zero-step monomial from CROSS and assign it to the diagonal class. This is only a coefficient projection onto positive outer degree, so (9) remains an upper bound. The exact sectors are then disjoint at both parities. Let $Z_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ be this shared sector polynomial. It has degree at most $d$ in each spectral variable. The preceding proof supplies fixed $\tau,\gamma>0$ such that $$ \left|Z_N\bigl(-2\cos(2\pi\delta_1),\ldots,-2\cos(2\pi\delta_R)\bigr)\right| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\tag{10} $$ for all large $N$, uniformly when $|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq\tau$ and for all real parts. Real periodicity follows from the polynomial cosines. Shrink $\tau$ once for Cauchy estimates; it is independent of the crossing powers. Insert this sector into the exact original Fourier formula, retaining its scalar, charge factors, sine factors and parity. Write $$ \begin{aligned} B_N(\boldsymbol\delta) &=\left(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right) Z_N(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)) e^{\pi iN\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2},\\ J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} &=\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R}B_N(\boldsymbol\delta) e^{2\pi iN\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i}\,d\boldsymbol\delta. \end{aligned} $$ Every $n_i$ is a fixed integer, with independent signs allowed. At either endpoint of coordinate $i$, $$ B_N|_{\delta_i=\pm1/2}=0, \qquad \partial_iB_N|_{\delta_i=1/2} =\partial_iB_N|_{\delta_i=-1/2}.\tag{11} $$ The sine vanishes, its derivative is $-2\pi$ at both endpoints, the source sees $\sigma_i=2$ at both, and the Gaussian is $e^{\pi iNn_i/4}$ at both. Only the sine-derivative term survives. These identities persist after derivatives in other coordinates. The Fourier endpoint factor is the same $(-1)^{N\ell_i}$ at both ends. Three integrations by parts therefore give $$ \begin{aligned} J_i=(2\pi iN\ell_i)^{-3}\bigg\{& \left[\partial_i^2 B_N e^{2\pi iN\ell_i\delta_i}\right]_{-1/2}^{1/2}\\ &-\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\partial_i^3 B_N e^{2\pi iN\ell_i\delta_i}\,d\delta_i\bigg\}. \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ The first two endpoint terms vanish by (11); the second-derivative endpoint difference in (12) is retained. Repeat in every coordinate. The boundary operations commute with the other derivatives and preserve their endpoint identities. There are at most $3^R$ terms, each with at most three derivatives per coordinate and evaluations or integrals over intervals of length one. Cauchy applied to the source alone in (10) bounds all such fixed-order derivatives by $C_\tau e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}$. On the real cube the Gaussian has modulus one, and its $k$th derivative in coordinate $i$ is bounded by $C_k(1+N|n_i|)^k$. Thus $$ |J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}| \leq C_{D,\tau,R}\left(\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3\right) e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3}.\tag{13} $$ The derivative cost $N^{3R}$ has canceled the integration-by-parts denominator. No Gaussian growth on the complex strip is used. The entire sector stays on the original whole real cube. The original charge weights have modulus $\prod_i|\ell_i|$; the parity and original framing scalar have modulus one. Since $\sum_{\ell\ne0}|\ell|^{-2}=\pi^2/3$, the complete charge sum is absolutely bounded by $$ |I_{N,\mathbf n;\,\mathrm{diag}\ I,\,\mathrm{CROSS\ elsewhere}}| \leq C_D\left(\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3\right)e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}.\tag{14} $$ This includes all charges and the actual second-derivative currents. It is not a sharp-cube localization or separately divergent inside/outside charge sum. Multilinearity of the finite source and fixed-level absolute Fourier convergence justify taking this polynomial sector; (13) additionally proves its uniform summability. There are finitely many diagonal/CROSS sectors for fixed $D$, so the same conclusion with a smaller gap holds for their union. For sufficiently long fixed independent signed twists, the proved local unit-charge filling rate exceeds $\Phi_D-\gamma/2$. Equation (14) is exponentially smaller than that nonzero local contribution. Constants may grow polynomially with the fixed powers; no joint growing-power/level asymptotic is claimed. The first case of Section 3, where other full ports are controlled only near $-2$, does not automatically have this whole-period conclusion. Equation (14) explicitly uses the global CROSS bound at every other port. ## 5. Remaining scope and verification The result is compatible with failure of a global coefficientwise endpoint bound for the full numerator. That failure already occurs at $\sigma=\sqrt3$ for a genuinely one-sided path with positive outer exponent, not for (1). Such a remote moving port is not covered by (9) or a small spectral neighborhood in (6). The [short-moving extension](actual_global_short_moving_spectral_sector_gap.md) treats a separate small outer-degree corridor; it does not exhaust macroscopic one-sided paths. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap_results.json) retain the exact finite source. The finite audit checks zero-step and divided-Chebyshev formulas, removable node values, parity sectors and marked sector polynomials. Its four nonzero fixtures include whole-interval three-integration-by-parts identities with nonzero second-derivative endpoint currents. These checks supplement the entropy and infinite-charge proofs.

title: The global LEFT weighted spectral envelope
status: Global weighted LEFT/RIGHT bound at all face phases
text:
# The global LEFT weighted spectral envelope theorem, 31 October 2026. This bounds the actual triangular-face LEFT sector at fixed positive face moduli. It is not a coefficientwise inequality or an optimized shared-capacity theorem. All original unused prefix and suffix rows are retained. ## 1. The original finite sector and its continuum upper envelope Put $A=x+y>0$, $P=xy\geq0$, $d=N-1$, $m=\lfloor N/2floor$, and $$ \alpha_r(\delta)=4\cos^2\!\left( rac{\pi(r+1/2)}Night)-4\sin^2(\pi\delta), \qquad s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N). $$ The LEFT sector has $0\leq i\leq j\leq m-1$. Up to its recorded overall sign, its [exact start/end summand](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) is $$ A_{\mathrm{rest}}(\delta)b^ic^{d-j} \left(\prod_{r<i}\alpha_right) \left(\prod_{j<r<m}\alpha_right)K_{i,j},	ag{1} $$ where $K_{i,i}=1$ and $$ K_{i,j}=s_j^2AK_{i,j-1}+s_js_{j-1}\alpha_{j-1}PK_{i,j-2}. $$ The omitted-half product $A_{\mathrm{rest}}$ is retained. For even $N$ it is $2T_m(\sigma/2)$, up to a sign, and has real-interval modulus at most $2$. For odd $N=2m+1$ it is $(\sigma+2)P_m(\sigma)$, up to a sign, with $$ P_m(2\cos	heta)= rac{\cos((m+1/2)	heta)}{\cos(	heta/2)}. $$ The quotient is a finite alternating cosine sum, bounded by $N$ on the real interval. Thus $|A_{\mathrm{rest}}|\leq4N$ at odd levels, including its removable endpoint. These exact factors have zero exponential upper rate. The uniform transfer estimate in the [global CROSS proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) applies to $K_{i,j}$ with any interval endpoints, by the same fixed-block matrix power argument. Together with uniform upper Riemann bounds for both unused prefix and suffix, it gives the upper action $$ F_L(\mu,
u,\delta) =\mu\log b+(1-
u)\log c+\int_\mu^
u\log L_\delta(t)\,dt, \qquad0\leq\mu\leq
u\leq rac12,	ag{2} $$ where $$  egin{aligned} \alpha(t)&=4 igl(\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta) igr),\ \Lambda(t)&=2\sin(\pi t) \left[A\sin(\pi t)+\sqrt{(x-y)^2\sin^2(\pi t)+4P\cos^2(\pi\delta)}ight],\ L_\delta(t)&= rac{\Lambda(t)}{|\alpha(t)|}. \end{aligned} $$ This rewriting uses $\int_0^{1/2}\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt=0$ only after bounding the actual two outside products. It makes no finite division by $\alpha$ and includes sampled spectral zeros. Logarithmic singularities are uniformly integrable. The $O(1/N)$ endpoint shifts and at most $N^2$ start/end pairs cost $o(N)$, uniformly in endpoints and real $\delta$. If $b=0$, only $\mu=0$ is allowed. If $c=0$, the finite LEFT polynomial vanishes identically because its $c$ exponent is at least $\lfloor N/2floor>0$. The sharp envelope identity is $$ \sup_{\substack{\delta\in[0,1/2]\0\leq\mu\leq
u\leq1/2}}F_L(\mu,
u,\delta) =\max\left\{\log c,Q_b(0)+ rac12\log cight\},	ag{3} $$ for $c>0$ and $b\geq0$. Here $Q_b$ is the same absolutely normalized [original triangle action](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). Equality in (3) concerns the continuum upper envelope; it does not claim that every oscillatory finite polynomial realizes that rate. ## 2. Exact endpoint optimization First suppose $b>0$ and $0<\delta<1/2$. Set $$ z=\sin^2(\pi\delta),\qquad k=\cos(\pi\delta),\qquad D=A^2-4Pz>0,\qquad t_c= rac12-\delta. $$ $L_\delta$ increases from $0$ to infinity before $t_c$ and decreases from infinity to $$ L_{\mathrm{end}}= rac{A+\sqrt D}{2z} $$ after $t_c$. The endpoint derivatives in (2) are $$ \partial_\mu F_L=\log b-\log L_\delta(\mu),\qquad \partial_
u F_L=\log L_\delta(
u)-\log c.	ag{4} $$ Before $t_c$, the $\mu$ dependence has its unique maximum at $\mu_b$, defined by $$ \sin^2(\pi\mu_b)= rac{k^2b^2}{(b+x)(b+y)}.	ag{5} $$ A stationary $
u$ before $t_c$ is a minimum; a stationary $\mu$ after $t_c$ is a minimum. Thus the only candidates beyond the diagonal $\mu=
u$ have $\mu=\mu_b$ and either $
u=1/2$ or a post-sign-change stationary $
u_c$. The boundary $\mu=0$ is included by $b	o0$; for positive $b$, the initial positive derivative rules it out unless $\mu=
u=0$. These observations also cover the boundaries of the ordered endpoint triangle. The diagonal contributes at most $\max\{\log c,(\log b+\log c)/2\}$. The terminal endpoint $
u=1/2$ gives $$ Q_b(\delta)+ rac12\log c.	ag{6} $$ The proved derivative $Q_b'=-\log(E_b/\sqrt D)$, with $$ E_b=A+2bz+2\sqrt z\sqrt{bA+P+b^2z}, $$ is nonpositive, strictly negative unless $b=P=0$. Hence (6) never exceeds $Q_b(0)+	frac12\log c$. Also $Q_b(0)\geq	frac12\log b$, so the two quantities in (3) already cover every diagonal candidate. A post-sign-change maximum exists only when $c\geq L_{\mathrm{end}}$. If $c>\max(x,y)$, this is precisely $\delta\geq\delta_c$, where $$ \sin^2(\pi\delta_c)= rac Ac- rac P{c^2},\qquad \sin^2(\pi
u_c)= rac{k^2c^2}{(c-x)(c-y)}.	ag{7} $$ At $\delta=\delta_c$, $
u_c=1/2$; for $\delta>\delta_c$, $t_c<
u_c<1/2$. If $c\leq\max(x,y)$, there is no such interior branch. ## 3. The straddling branch has only spectral minima Define the post-sign-change stationary action $$ J_c(\delta)=
u_c\log c+\int_0^{
u_c}\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt +\int_{
u_c}^{1/2}\log\Lambda(t)\,dt. $$ Then the straddling value is exactly $$ S_L(\delta)=Q_b(\delta)+\log c-J_c(\delta).	ag{8} $$ There is no new additive action constant: (8) follows by subtracting the integrals and using the same complete prefix integral zero as in (2). Put $$ T_c^-=\sqrt{c^2z-cA+P},\qquad H_c=2cz-A+2\sqrt z\,T_c^-. $$ On the strict branch $c>L_{\mathrm{end}}$, the exact derivative is $$ J_c'(\delta)=-\log rac{H_c}{\sqrt D}.	ag{9} $$ A direct normalization proof avoids guessing a complex sheet. The envelope rule gives $\partial_{\log c}J_c=
u_c$. Differentiating (7) gives $\partial_\delta
u_c=-c\sin(\pi\delta)/T_c^-$. Direct algebra gives $\partial_{\log c}\log H_c=c\sin(\pi\delta)/T_c^-$. Thus the difference between the two sides of (9) is independent of $c$ for each fixed $\delta$. As $c$ decreases to $L_{\mathrm{end}}$, $
u_c$ tends to $1/2$. At that endpoint the complete prefix integral has derivative zero, so $J_c'$ tends to zero. The vanishing tail is regular because $\alpha(1/2)=-4z
e0$. Simultaneously $T_c^-$ tends to zero and $H_c$ tends to $\sqrt D$. This fixes the difference to zero and proves (9). Moving interior logarithmic zeros are handled by uniform-integrability and principal-value differentiation of the explicit log-cosine primitive; no finite sampled quotient is used. Consequently $$ S_L'(\delta)=\log rac{H_c}{E_b}.	ag{10} $$ The two positive numbers are larger roots with the same product $D$: $$  egin{aligned} E_b&=C_b+\sqrt{C_b^2-D},& C_b&=A+2bz,\ H_c&=C_c+\sqrt{C_c^2-D},& C_c&=2cz-A. \end{aligned} $$ Both $C_b,C_c\geq\sqrt D$ on this branch, and the larger-root function is strictly increasing in $C$. Hence $$ \operatorname{sign}S_L' =\operatorname{sign}(C_c-C_b) =\operatorname{sign}[(c-b)z-A].	ag{11} $$ Since $z$ increases with $\delta$, this sign can only pass from negative to positive. An interior spectral stationary point is therefore a minimum. At the branch entry the value is (6). As $\delta	o1/2$, both $\mu_b$ and $
u_c$ tend to zero, and uniform integrability gives $S_L	o\log c$. The straddling branch is thus bounded by the right side of (3). The diagonal and terminal candidates were already bounded in Section 2. At $\delta=0$, their known maximization attains (3), proving the envelope identity. The proof extends to $b=0$ by its sole-start limit and to $xy=0$ by the exact first-order recurrence and displayed formulas; $A$ stays positive. The possibly singular endpoint $D=0$ occurs only at $\delta=1/2$, $x=y$, and is handled by the same continuous endpoint value. The original protected faces are never replaced by positive radii. ## 4. All face phases and the final spectral cap The [exact continuous-real positivity lemma](actual_continuous_real_tail_coefficient_positivity.md) supplies a finite strengthening. Normalize $$ Q_r= rac{K_{i,i+r}}{\prod_{v=i+1}^{i+r}s_v^2}. $$ Then $$ Q_r=(x+y)Q_{r-1}+ eta_jxyQ_{r-2},\qquad  eta_j= rac{\alpha_{j-1}}{s_js_{j-1}},\quad j=i+r. $$ This recurrence is used only for $r\geq2$, hence $j\geq i+2$; $Q_1=x+y$ is handled separately, so no denominator $s_0$ is introduced. The identity $$ \alpha_{j-1}+s_js_{j-1} =4\cos^2(\pi\delta)-4\sin^2\!\left( rac\pi{2N}ight)	ag{12} $$ is independent of $j$. Thus $ eta_j\geq-1$ for $|\delta|\leq1/2-1/(2N)$, equivalently $\sigma\in[-2,2\cos(\pi/N)]$. Induction using $$ Q_r-xQ_{r-1} =y[Q_{r-1}-xQ_{r-2}]+(1+ eta_j)xyQ_{r-2} $$ proves coefficientwise nonnegativity on this entire interval. The initial values are $Q_0=1$, $Q_1=x+y$. Arbitrary phases of $x,y$ therefore have modulus bounded by the same $K$ at their positive moduli. In (1), taking absolute values of $b,c$ and of the retained scalar prefix and suffix factors reduces all face phases to the same envelope (2). No one-sided angular gap or absolute-value replacement inside the signed recurrence is used. The remaining real spectral cap $[2\cos(\pi/N),2]$ has width $O(N^{-2})$. For a polynomial $p$ of degree at most $d$ bounded by $M$ on $[-2,b_N]$, $b_N=2\cos(\pi/N)$, the exterior-circle maximum principle gives $$ |p(2)|\leq M\exp\!\left[d\,\operatorname{arcosh} rac{6-b_N}{b_N+2}ight] \leq CM. $$ The same bound holds throughout the cap; its exponent is $O(1)$ uniformly in $N\geq3$. Apply it to the actual LEFT polynomial at each fixed face-phase tuple. Thus (3) bounds the global real-spectral weighted absolute value at arbitrary face phases. The RIGHT version follows by reversing the original row and middle orientation. Applying the same polynomial argument on the full real interval extends the bound to a fixed complex $\delta$ strip, at additional cost $e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$, uniformly in those face phases. This is still not coefficientwise domination: the known $\sigma=\sqrt3$ individual-coefficient counterexample is compatible with summing at fixed moduli. Nor may the actual shared coefficient be replaced by an unproved infimum of sums of local maxima. At fixed moduli the weighted full upper rate is bounded by $$ \max\{Q_b(0)+Q_c(0),\log b,\log c\}, $$ because $Q_b(0)\geq	frac12\log b$, $Q_c(0)\geq	frac12\log c$, and a geometric mean never exceeds the larger endpoint. Zero-middle terms are interpreted by the exact vanishing statements above. A [strict complete-radius balance condition](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) permits a shared-source application; no general capacity equality follows here. ## Validation and scope The recurrence is used only from its second step. This is a weighted local theorem, not a coefficientwise comparison or a shared capacity equality.

title: A global spectral gap for short-moving source sectors
text: # A global spectral gap for short-moving source sectors analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This retains the actual full numerator, original two protected targets and entire Fourier period. It extends the diagonal/CROSS sector lemma to a fixed small outer-degree corridor. It does not bound remote one-sided paths of arbitrary macroscopic displacement. Here "moving" refers to the original triangular face path degree; it is not an identification with physical input/output head displacement. ## 1. Exact path divided differences, including repeated nodes Write $d=N-1$, $\chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2$ and $c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)$. In the original triangular face path expansion, a path from $j$ to $i$ has $k$ one- or two-row steps, displacement $$ D=j-i,\qquad k\leq D\leq2k, $$ and $k+1$ distinct visited row indices $v_0,\ldots,v_k$. Its scalar factor is $$ \prod_{r\ \mathrm{not\ visited}}(\sigma-c_r) =\chi_N[c_{v_0},\ldots,c_{v_k},\sigma].\tag{1} $$ The right side is the divided difference of order $k+1$. Repeated spectral values among the $c_{v_l}$ mean the exact Hermite divided difference. The identity remains polynomial at all removable nodes: $\chi_N$ vanishes with at least the required multiplicity at the listed nodes, so Newton's divided-remainder identity proves (1). It also follows by polynomial division, with no inverse spectral gap. For real $\sigma\in[-2,2]$, the iterated fundamental theorem of calculus on the divided-difference simplex bounds (1) by $$ \frac{\sup_{[-2,2]}|\chi_N^{(r)}|}{r!} =\frac{2N}{N+r}\binom{N+r}{2r},\qquad r=k+1.\tag{2} $$ Here is an elementary proof of the derivative value used in (2). Each derivative of $T_N$ has nonnegative Chebyshev coefficients, since $T_j'=jU_{j-1}$ and $U_{j-1}$ is a nonnegative sum of cosine characters. Therefore its absolute maximum on $[-1,1]$ occurs at $1$. Differentiating $(1-z^2)T_N''-zT_N'+N^2T_N=0$ at $z=1$ gives $$ T_N^{(r)}(1)=\frac{N^2\prod_{a=1}^{r-1}(N^2-a^2)}{(2r-1)!!}. $$ The scaling $\chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2$ and division by $r!$ give (2). The divided-difference simplex has volume $1/r!$, including the limit of coincident nodes, so the same bound applies there. The remaining original step weights have absolute value at most $4$. A one-step move contributes a multiple of $x+y$; a two-step move a multiple of $xy$. There are at most $2^D$ compositions of $D$ into steps $1,2$, and each path's chosen outer coefficient is at most $4^k2^k\leq8^D$. The total coefficient of any monomial $x^ab^ic^{d-j}y^{D-a}$ is therefore bounded by $$ 2\cdot16^D\left[\frac{e(N+D+1)}{2D+2}\right]^{2D+2}.\tag{3} $$ Indeed $\binom{N+r}{2r}\leq[e(N+r)/(2r)]^{2r}$, and this last expression is increasing for $1\leq r\leq N$: its logarithmic derivative is $2\log((N+r)/(2r))+2r/(N+r)>0$. This applies with $r\leq D+1\leq N$. No cancellation among different paths is required for the upper bound. For $0<\eta<1$, let $L_{N,\eta}$ be the exact coefficient projection of $H_{V_N}$ onto outer degree $a_x+a_y\leq\lfloor\eta d\rfloor$, and put $$ T_{N,\eta} =\sum_{\substack{|\mathbf a|=d\\a_x+a_y\leq\lfloor\eta d\rfloor}} x^{a_x}b^{a_b}c^{a_c}y^{a_y}. $$ All coefficients of $T$ are $1$. Equations (1)--(3) prove uniformly over the whole real interval $$ \begin{aligned} |L_{N,\eta}(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}}&\leq K_{N,\eta}T_{N,\eta},\\ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log K_{N,\eta}&\leq\omega(\eta),\\ \omega(\eta)&=\eta\log16+2\eta\log\frac{e(1+\eta)}{2\eta} \longrightarrow0. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ One can take $K$ to be the right side of (3) at $D=\lfloor\eta d\rfloor$. Every coefficient polynomial has spectral degree at most $d$. Thus the exterior-circle maximum-principle argument of the diagonal lemma extends (4) to $\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)$, multiplying its right side by $e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$. Both parities, the central odd row and all repeated spectral nodes are included in these polynomial identities. ## 2. Shared target continuity, rather than an identity reset Fix the actual certified diagram $D$ and a nonempty set $I$ of ports. At $I$ take the projection $L_{N,\eta}$; elsewhere take the exact CROSS projection. Keep the original ordinary targets $d$ and protected targets $0$. The global CROSS coefficient bound from the [cofactor interpolation lemma](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) is $$ |P_{\mathrm{cross}}(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}} \leq C\log^2(N+1)H_{F_N}, $$ on the real interval, where $F_N$ is the actual even positive endpoint or odd regularized Fejer reference. Its strip version has the same degree-$d$ exponential factor as (4). Hence the absolute original sector is bounded by $K_{N,\eta}^{|I|}[C\log^2(N+1)]^{R-|I|}$ times $$ [\text{original targets}]\, \prod_{i\in I}T_{N,\eta;i}\prod_{j\notin I}H_{F_N;j}.\tag{5} $$ The comparison does not change the positive outer degrees into zero. They remain in (5) with the exact shared incidences and protected targets. In particular, it does not apply the old identity theorem to a finite shifted target or to a physically different coupon. Let $\mathcal P_I(\eta)$ be the compact continuous flow polytope on the original port-to-face incidence graph: each port supplies $1$, each ordinary face demands $1$, each protected face demands $0$, and at a port in $I$ the total outer load is at most $\eta$. Let $$ W_I(\eta)=\max_{\mathbf q\in\mathcal P_I(\eta)} \sum_{j\notin I}h(\mathbf q_j).\tag{6} $$ with value minus infinity for an empty polytope. Here $h$ is precisely the [continuous full-simplex local entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) of $H_{F_N}$, the same at both parities. Selected ports have entropy zero because $T$ has coefficient $1$. The uniform local coefficient theorem, and the polynomial number of degree-$d$ monomial assignments for fixed $D$, give the upper bound $$ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\bigl(\text{coefficient in (5)}\bigr) \leq W_I(\eta).\tag{7} $$ Only an upper bound is needed: no boundary rounding or eventual fixed-label feasibility is asserted here. Normalize the integer exponents by $d$, retaining the exact face balances; replacing $d/N$ by $1$ is uniform because $h$ is continuous on its compact simplex. At $\eta=0$ this is exactly the identity-inserted compact flow problem, so $W_I(0)<\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$ by the [proved strict identity theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) for the original drilled group. Moreover $$ W_I(\eta)\longrightarrow W_I(0)\qquad\text{as }\eta\downarrow0.\tag{8} $$ To see this, take a convergent subsequence of maximizers in the nested compact polytopes. Its limit lies in $\mathcal P_I(0)$; continuity of the entropy gives the upper inequality, and inclusion gives the reverse inequality. If $\mathcal P_I(0)$ is empty, compactness instead implies $\mathcal P_I(\eta)$ is empty for every sufficiently small $\eta$. Combining (4),(7),(8), choose a fixed $\eta_D>0$ so $$ W_I(\eta_D)+|I|\omega(\eta_D)<\Phi_D-2\gamma_D.\tag{9} $$ There are finitely many nonempty $I$, so $\eta_D$ and $\gamma_D$ can be chosen for all of them at once, ignoring identically zero cases. Shrinking a fixed complex $\boldsymbol\delta$ strip absorbs $2\pi\sum_j|\operatorname{Im}\delta_j|$. For all sufficiently large $N$, at both parities the sector satisfies $$ \left|Z_{I,\eta_D;\mathrm{cross}}(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta))\right| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_D)}.\tag{10} $$ uniformly on that strip. Constants depend on the original fixed diagram, independently of the eventual fixed signed crossing powers. ## 3. Whole original period and precise remaining scope The sector in (10) is still a polynomial of spectral degree at most $d$ in every coordinate. The three-integration-by-parts argument of [the global diagonal/CROSS sector theorem](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md), §4, therefore applies verbatim to its entire original Fourier period. In particular, sine factors give $B(\pm1/2)=0$ and matching first derivatives; the second-derivative endpoint current is retained. Cauchy differentiates the source on its fixed strip, while the Gaussian is differentiated only on the real cube. Summing all nonzero integer charges with the actual charge weights gives $$ \left|I_{N,\mathbf n;\,\mathrm{short}\ I,\,\mathrm{cross\ elsewhere}}\right| \leq C_D\prod_j(1+|n_j|)^3e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_D)}.\tag{11} $$ Thus a fixed small outer-degree corridor, including genuinely moving near-diagonal paths, is exponentially negligible relative to the [proved local unit-charge contribution](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) for independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists. No sharp local cube splits an infinite charge sum. If disjoint sectors are required, project overlapping classes further; coefficient projections preserve every upper bound. This does not control a macroscopic one-sided path whose outer load stays outside this small corridor. In particular the known $\sigma=\sqrt3$ counterexample with outer load tending to $1/4$ is compatible with (11). Nor does the statement bound a partial-far-charge source with an uncontrolled original $R^n$ coupon at another port. Those remain separate global phase-sensitive questions.

title: A source-exact full half-clock dilation of the physical head
text: # A source-exact full half-clock dilation of the physical head 28 October 2026. At complete color the original N-dimensional head is an invariant orthogonal window in an explicit 2N-clock representation. The weighted cyclic shifts have zeros at both window boundaries. The unrolled H, full half-Cartan, genuine dual, N-normalized turns, original pivot and selected cut all lift exactly. For a one-component knot, the selected cut forces the physical window around the entire component, so the full extended contraction is the original scalar. This supplies a legitimate unitary 2N Fourier ambient space. It does not supply the global triangulation edge character required by the [positive-angle majorant](positive_angle_majorant_and_integer_winding.md). The new ambient clock dilates the old window; its conserved physical charge is already present in the original unrolled degree equations. ## 1. Exact complete-color generators Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d=-q^-1, and c=q-q^-1. Use the original balanced basis w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a. The original head is H w_a=(d-2a)w_a, K w_a=x Q^-a w_a, F w_a=(1-Q^(a+1))w_(a+1), E w_a=(Q^-a-1)/c^2 w_(a-1), 0<=a<N, (1) with the nonexistent endpoints set to zero. Indeed the original unbalanced E coefficient is [a]_q[N-a]_q=[a]_q^2 and [a]_q^2/(1-Q^a)=(Q^-a-1)/c^2. No factorial metric change is being made in this note: (1) is the already used balanced presentation. On W=C^(2N), with orthonormal basis u_J, define T u_J=q^J u_J, X u_J=u_(J+1 mod2N), F_W=X(1-Q T^2), E_W=X^-1(T^-2-1)/c^2, K_W=x T^-2, H_W u_J=(d-2J)u_J. (2) Here TX=qXT; Q is still q^2 of order N. The zeros of F_W occur at J=d,2N-1 and those of E_W at J=0,N. Hence W=W_0 direct_sum W_1, W_0=span(u_0,...,u_d), W_1=span(u_N,...,u_(2N-1)) (3) is an orthogonal decomposition into invariant unrolled modules. Under u_(N epsilon+a) <-> w_a, E,F,K are the original matrices, and H is shifted by -2N epsilon. In particular W=V_d direct_sum V_(d-2N), E_W^N=F_W^N=0. (4) The first-window inclusion i and p=i^* are isometric and satisfy p i=I. Any prescribed original head metric can instead be copied orthogonally to both summands; the inclusion remains isometric. Unitary ordinary DFT statements below use the balanced flat metric. The unrolled quantum relations follow on each summand from (1). For example [H,E]=2E and [H,F]=-2F hold at the cyclic wraps because the corresponding weights are ZERO, not because H was made cyclic. Replacing H by a residue class would lose this justification. ## 2. The full Cartan and the genuine dual Use the original finite universal crossing, in its original order, Rcheck=Flip q^(H tensor H/2) sum_(n=0)^d q^[n(n-1)/2] c^n/[n]_q! E^n tensor F^n. (5) Formula (5), and its actual inverse, are well defined on W. Every denominator has n<N and is nonzero. Since each summand in (3) is invariant, a crossing transports its two summand labels with the physical strands. On the selected W_0 tensor W_0 its restriction is EXACTLY the original Rcheck, including the common Cartan scalar kappa=q^(d^2/2). No kappa was stripped or replaced by a 2N scalar. The full Cartan is not the bare cyclic phase Q^(ab). On the original window it is q^[(d-2a)(d-2b)/2] =kappa q^[-d(a+b)] Q^(ab). (6) On W_epsilon tensor W_eta its ratio to the original Cartan is (-1)^[d(epsilon+eta)]. This is a unit phase; it follows by expanding the two unrolled H shifts before taking q powers. The restriction statement itself does not require dropping this phase elsewhere. Use the GENUINE dual W^*, with the original antipode and pivotal duality. It is V_d^* direct_sum V_(d-2N)^*. In the copied original dual basis u_(N epsilon+a)^vee its H weights are H_Wvee=d+2N epsilon-2a. (7) In particular, its second dual summand is not assigned the naive weight d-2(N+a). Those two expressions differ by 4N, which is invisible to q^H but not to unrolled H as an operator. The true dual is what justifies the cups, caps and half-Cartan identities. Write the original pivotal matrix as g_a=x^(1-N) Q^-a. The root parameter is still N: the pivot on W is K_W^(1-N), not K_W^(1-2N). Copy this exact matrix to both summands. In the original unrolled convention the twist at highest weight alpha is q^[(alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2]; its values at d and d-2N agree, since their ratio is q^(2N^2)=1. Thus the original zero-framing correction also lifts with its exact scalar. The original left turns, in the original factorial boundary frame, lift as coev_L^W=sum_(epsilon=0,1) sum_(a=0)^d N x^-a u_(N epsilon+d-a) tensor u_(N epsilon+a)^vee, ev_L^W(u_(N epsilon+a)^vee tensor u_(N eta+b)) =delta_(epsilon,eta) x^a/N delta_(a+b,d). (8) The right turns have the SAME original pivot factors; for example coev_R^W=sum_(epsilon,a) N x^-a g_(d-a)^-1 u_(N epsilon+a)^vee tensor u_(N epsilon+d-a). (9) These are the direct-sum genuine turns, not new normalization choices. They use N and 1/N, not 2N and 1/(2N). Restricting every leg to the first summand gives the literal original turns. The ordinary cap is still not declared to be the Hermitian adjoint of the cup; this dilation does not change the pivotal trace's positivity. ## 3. Exact original one-component source Let P_0=i p be the first-window projector. If the original closed-braid source is the normalized averaged cut, retain it literally as (1/N) Tr_(W cut)(P_0 C_W), (10) with every original closed pivot and zero-framing factor retained. If the original source is a specified cut matrix entry, retain that entry in W_0 instead. These choices agree for the uninserted scalar knot endomorphism; they are NOT interchanged for arbitrary inserted exteriors. In a plat retain its actual marked coupon g E_00 and its prescribed pivotal side, extended in W_0. No replacement by I_W/(2N) is made. **Source theorem.** Replace every physical head by W, every dual by W^*, and use (5),(8),(9) and their actual inverse/right versions. For ANY one-component knot presentation, its original selected scalar is unchanged. Proof. Expand the extended contraction by summand labels epsilon. Each crossing transports the two labels with their physical strands; each cup or cap matches the label on its two incident physical legs. Thus the label is constant along each physical link component. The original selected cut forces label0 on its component. Since there is only one component, every nonzero term lies in W_0 on every physical leg. Each local restriction is exactly the original coupon, including Cartan, pivot, boundary and framing constants. Therefore the entire sum equals the original scalar, not merely its modulus or its leading exponent. This proof also retains literal original insertions which preserve or are lifted inside the selected summand, provided their original cut functional is kept unchanged. It does not apply a scalar-knot trace conversion after inserting new coupons. For a multi-component link, each component must carry its specified selected projector if this same statement is wanted. Leaving another component unselected permits its other summand and is a different source. Likewise arbitrary new offdiagonal summand-changing coupons are outside the theorem. The construction is an exact COMPLETE-COLOR lift. At generic color the direct sum V_alpha direct_sum V_(alpha-2N) still gives an exact isometric module lift, but the simple E polynomial in (2) no longer gives its boundary values: endpoint projectors are then required. No unproved whole-meridian polynomial-weight extension is inferred from the complete-color q-number zeros. The original full modified dimension remains an external normalization line throughout. ## 4. What full-clock information actually follows On W and its genuine dual the copied half-clock is T u_J=q^J u_J. Although their unrolled H lifts differ, both satisfy T=q^(d/2) q^(-H/2). (11) The dual second-summand difference4N contributes q^(2N epsilon)=1. Unrolled total-H conservation therefore gives the EXACT identity [Rcheck,T tensor T]=0. (12) On every full turn, J+Jvee=2N epsilon+d, so (T tensor Tvee)coev=q^d coev. (13) The corresponding cap has the same affine charge. Consequently a full q-character average is legitimate at these PHYSICAL vertices. The charge in (12) is not only modulo N: on the original window, the conserved unwrapped total lies in[0,2d], whose width is <2N, so its modulo2N equation is equivalent to exact integer equality. However, (12)--(13) already hold on the original N-window. They are its existing integer flow and inverse-meridian pairing laws, now realized in a full-clock ambient space. The quantum factorial still has base Q=q^2 and length N; the nilpotency order in (4) is still N. Nothing has changed it to a 2N-dimensional cyclic dilogarithm. There is an explicit limitation for the OLD unweighted N-cyclic shift used in cyclic-atom factorizations. Its exact blockwise lift is not X. Put P_wall=|d><d|+|2N-1><2N-1|, S_hat=X(I-P_wall)+X^(1-N)P_wall. (14a) Then S_hat is the direct sum of the two original N-cyclic shifts, so S_hat^N=I. Directly on every basis vector, T^2 S_hat=Q S_hat T^2, T S_hat-q S_hat T=-2q X^(1-N)P_wall T. (14b) The right side is a nonzero rank-two wall current, of norm2 in the flat metric. The two weights in (2) kill their respective endpoint terms, which is why the complete original R lifts cleanly. An old cyclic-atom factorization, however, must use S_hat and retain (14b) if its old Q-Weyl relation is refined to a q relation. Replacing its unweighted S_N by X without this correction changes its physical restriction. Thus the dilation does not automatically upgrade the old cyclic shape algebra to a free full-q Weyl algebra. The small rank alone supplies no bound after arbitrary factorial conjugations. Let F_(2N) be the unitary 2N discrete Fourier transform. The physical window becomes the rank-N projector (F_(2N) P_0 F_(2N)^*)_(rs) =(1/(2N)) sum_(a=0)^d q^[a(r-s)]. (14) Its diagonal is1/2. For r!=s its entry is zero if r-s is even and 1/[N(1-q^(r-s))] if r-s is odd. Thus the selected Fourier source is not an independent uniform full-clock source: it retains this exact projector, or its propagated equivalent under the full contraction. Plancherel preserves it rather than deleting it. To apply the positive affine-angle theorem one must STILL construct the actual source map to tetrahedral nonnegative angles with sum d, identify the geometric edge-incidence rows, and prove the full edge character Ek=2d modulo2N with subexponential comparison norm. Physical head conservation (12) is not that global geometric edge equation. Joint noncommuting quantum shapes are not automatically positive angle labels either. This dilation resolves the cyclic-wrap issue for the physical head; it does not close those geometric/source gates. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_half_clock_source_dilation.py): literal generators and unrolled relations, full Cartan/crossings, genuine dual turns, physical affine charge, Fourier projector and selected original one-component braid sources. Finite checks are supplementary to the direct-sum and component-label proof above.

title: A finite half-color quadratic transform for the original source
text: # A finite half-color quadratic transform for the original source 29 October 2026. This proves the exact simple-channel coefficient of the original figure-eight four-plat in the complete Casimir frame. The finite proof uses one terminating q-Chu identity, proved below by finite binomial expansion. It retains all root phases, common Cartan factors and the actual original cup/cap opening. The resulting coefficient is a positive sine-binomial square sum times its known phase. It tests the pointed energy of the complete channel Gram, not the value of the invariant after its final cap. ## 1. A reusable odd-root quadratic transform Let `N=2m+1>=3`, let Q have exact order N, put `F_r=(Q;Q)_r` and `a=Q^(-m)=Q^(m+1)`. All factorials below have index at most 2m and are nonzero. Define S_m=sum_(k=0)^m Q^[-k(m-k)] [m choose k]_Q^2. Then EXACTLY sum_(t=0)^m Q^t (a;Q)_t^3/F_t^2 =(-1)^m Q^[-m(3m+1)/2] S_m. (1) This is a finite 3-parameter-to-2-parameter quadratic source transform. It is valid at composite odd levels as well as prime ones, with no square-root choice or root-zero denominator. Proof. Expand the THIRD Pochhammer by the finite binomial theorem, put `t=k+j`, `n=m-k`, and retain the other two factors. The left side becomes sum_(k=0)^m (-a)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2+k](a;Q)_k^2/F_k^2 *sum_(j=0)^n Q^j (aQ^k;Q)_j^2 /[F_j(Q^(k+1);Q)_j]. Apply terminating q-Chu to the inner sum with terminating length n, `b=Q^-n=aQ^k`, `c=Q^(k+1)`. It is Q^(-n^2)(Q^(m+1);Q)_n/(Q^(k+1);Q)_n =Q^(-n^2)(a;Q)_n F_k/F_m. (2) Here the ODD ROOT relation `Q^(m+1)=a` is essential. Substitute (a;Q)_r=(-1)^r Q^[-mr+r(r-1)/2]F_m/F_(m-r). Each k-th term is now `(-1)^m Q^[-m(3m+1)/2-k(m-k)] [m choose k]_Q^2`. This proves (1), including every sign and exponent. ## 2. Elementary finite q-Chu and Durfee identities The finite identity used in (2), whenever its denominators are units, is sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j(b;Q)_j Q^j /[F_j(c;Q)_j] =b^n(c/b;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (3) No published summation proof is a premise. Here is a direct finite proof. First the binomial theorem gives sum_(s=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_s Q^s/F_s *(cQ^s;Q)_(n-s) =(-c)^n Q^[n(n-1)/2]. (4) To check (4), expand the last Pochhammer. Its c^r coefficient contains `(Q^(1-(n-r));Q)_(n-r)`, zero unless r=n. Only that last coefficient survives, giving the right side. Multiply (3) by `(c;Q)_n`, expand `(b;Q)_j`, and extract b^r. Set `j=r+s` and apply (4) with length n-r and parameter cQ^r. The result is (-c)^(n-r) Q^[(n-r)(n-r-1)/2][n choose r]_Q, the b^r coefficient of `b^n(c/b;Q)_n`. Thus (3) is a rational identity before specialization and holds at the stated roots. Its useful finite Durfee consequence is sum_(r=0)^t Q^(r^2)/(F_r^2 F_(t-r))=1/F_t^2. (5) Indeed take n=t, b=Q^-t, c=0 in (3), multiply by Q^(t^2), and reverse its summation index. This proves (5) by the same finite algebra, without an infinite-product interpretation. ## 3. The actual complete-channel coefficient Now use the principal `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=2m`, `x=q^d=Q^m`, `nu_m=(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)]`. Let R_1,R_2 be the two original generators on the complete source multiplicity module, including their common Cartan kappa. The TRUE four-plat action order is `[2,-1,2,2]`, hence W=R_2^2 R_1^(-1) R_2. Let V be the complete physical Casimir/Hermite frame, J the actual anti-Pascal recoupling, and p the original cup. Define the COMPLETE right-channel output z=V^(-1)J Wp. At odd N the node c=-2 is simple, with normalized eigenvector `f_0=1`, crossing value nu_m and bilinear norm `sigma=x^d nu_m`. Its exact coefficient is z_simple=N Q^[m(m+1)] F_m S_m. (6) At the principal root `S_m=sum_(r=0)^m |[m choose r]_Q|^2>0`. Thus (6) is not an expanded path or a guessed saddle surviving selection; it is the ENTIRE actual channel after all its sums. ## 4. Source reduction to the quadratic transform The actual J is symmetric: its anti-Pascal formula and `F_jF_(d-j)=N(-1)^jQ^[j(j+1)/2]` give `J_(i,j)=J_(j,i)`. Put `y=Jf`, `h=R_2p`, `v=R_1^(-1)h`. The lower bidiagonal equation for y, with endpoint `y_d=f_0=1`, gives exactly y_i=0 for i<m, y_(m+r)=Q^[-r(m-r)][m choose r]_Q^2. (7) The successive ratio is the square of `|1-Q^(m-r)|/|1-Q^(r+1)|`; its complex factorial form in (7) keeps the phase identity at arbitrary primitive Q. The FIRST original R_2 on the cup highest lift has a forced final third-head color zero. In the literal positive crossing the transfer must equal that second input color. Its coefficient simplifies to `kappa F_(d-i)`, using `x^2=Q^-1`. Therefore h_i=kappa p_i F_(d-i), p_i=Nx^(i-d). (8) The literal original inverse crossing then gives v_i=x^(i-d)(-1)^i Q^[i(i+1)/2-d] F_(d-i)/F_i *sum_(b=i)^d Q^b F_b^3/F_(b-i). (9) For example (9) follows directly by the finite inverse-R transfer sum and the SAME reflection identity; the common kappa in (8) cancels the prescribed inverse kappa. No external normalization has been changed. Multiply (9) by (7), put `i=m+r`, and interchange `b=m+t` and r. Using (5) gives y^T v=C sum_(t=0)^m Q^(m+t) F_(m+t)^3/F_t^2, C=(-1)^m x^(-m) Q^[m(m+1)/2+1]. (10) This intermediate reduction is a finite identity with the original source; in particular no extension beyond the true finite ranges has been made. Since `F_(m+t)=F_m(a;Q)_t`, (1) evaluates (10): y^T v=Q^[-2m^2+m+1]F_m^3 S_m =F_m^3S_m=N nu_m F_m S_m. (11) The remaining exponent is `(1-m)(2m+1)`, a full root period. The last equality is the full reflection identity `F_m^2=N nu_m`. Finally the simple inverse channel row is `f^T/sigma`. Moving the two terminal R_2 factors through J and selecting that simple channel gives z_simple=(kappa^2 nu_m^2/sigma)y^T v =nu_m y^T v. Here `kappa^2=x^d` for the actual odd-level full Cartan. Substituting (11) proves (6), with all source and common-line phases retained. ## 5. Scope for the proposed positive energy For the balanced complete-channel Gram `G=(V^(-1)J)^*(V^(-1)J)/N`, the original pointed energy is `E_N=N^(-1)||z||_2^2`. Equation (6) implies EXACTLY E_N>=N^2 S_m^2, (12) because `|F_m|^2=N`. The asymptotic consequence is developed in the companion energy audit; it concerns THIS particular positive Gram. It does not contradict its exact Cauchy inequality, and it does not rule out a different source-preserving coherent terminal Gram that contracts more of the actual tensor before squaring. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.py): the finite q-Chu/quadratic transform and the literal full original four-plat simple-channel coefficient, at odd composite and prime levels, with all common Cartan and source constants.

title: Exact Hardy replacement of the internal finite-head projectors
text: # Exact Hardy replacement of the internal finite-head projectors 28 October 2026. The original scalar Euler/Gaussian network admits an exact simplification: **every internal finite Dirichlet kernel can be replaced by an ordinary Hardy Cauchy kernel**, provided its existing finite factorial and Gaussian kernels are retained. This holds for every signed braid word and its full original source. With the proved fused plat source, the boundary is monomial as well. Thus the Dirichlet numerator branches are unnecessary in this presentation of the complete word. This does not remove the actual finite Euler/Gaussian endpoint sectors. Their support is essential to the proof. Nor does the theorem identify a new geometric edge's three indices with a charged degree. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_hardy_cauchy_network.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_hardy_cauchy_network_results.json) check the full original signed crossing matrices and original whole-word pivotal cuts while allowing nonzero intermediate indices beyond the head. ## 1. The actual operators, extended without an upper head projection Let $\mathcal P=\mathbb C[z]$, and let $H_N$ be its subspace of degree below $N$. On $\mathcal P$ use the unilateral shifts $$ J_+z^a=z^{a+1},\qquad J_-z^a=\begin{cases}z^{a-1}&a>0,\\0&a=0.\end{cases} $$ They have no upper cutoff. Define the original finite polynomials $$ u_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}\frac{t^h}{F_h},\qquad v_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} \frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}t^h}{F_h}, \qquad F_h=(Q;Q)_h. $$ On a pair put $$ U_-^\infty=u_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+),\quad V_-^\infty=v_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+), $$ and define $U_+^\infty,V_+^\infty$ by reversing the two shifts. Only the lower polynomial wall is imposed. Extend each existing finite diagonal kernel by zero outside its original active-head support: $$ \begin{split} \mathsf Fz^a&=F_az^a,\quad \mathsf F^{-}z^a=F_a^{-1}z^a &&(0\le a<N),\\ \mathsf Fz^a&=\mathsf F^{-}z^a=0 &&(a\ge N). \end{split} \tag{1} $$ The superscript minus here is the zero-extended finite inverse diagonal, not an inverse on $\mathcal P$. Likewise retain $\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{-}$ with their original nonzero entries for $0\le a<N$ and zero entries above the head. Spectator heads are identities on all nonnegative indices. No new cutoff has been added to (1): these are exactly the finite scalar kernels already present in the [literal network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md). ## 2. The support lemma removes the internal upper projections Let $P$ project onto $H_N\otimes H_N$ and put $$ C^\infty=\mathsf F_2U_-^\infty\mathsf F_1\mathsf F_2^{-}, \qquad \overline C^\infty= \mathsf F_2\mathsf F_1^{-}V_-^\infty\mathsf F_2^{-}. \tag{2} $$ These are the original strict fusion and inverse-fusion words. Their support has the following exact properties: $$ C^\infty=PC^\infty P,\qquad \overline C^\infty=P\overline C^\infty,\qquad C^\infty|_{H_N^2}=C,\qquad \overline C^\infty|_{H_N^2}=C^{-1}. \tag{3} $$ For the first operator the two right diagonal factors kill inputs outside the head. Its transfer only lowers the first index, so that index stays in the head; the left $\mathsf F_2$ kills every second-index overflow. For the second operator the two left diagonals enforce its output support. On a head input, an overflow generated by $V_-^\infty$ is precisely the second-index overflow killed by $\mathsf F_2$. These are the same coefficient sums as the finite fusion and its finite inverse. Keep the original Cartan scalar $\kappa$, and define $$ \begin{split} R_+^\infty&=\kappa C^\infty \mathsf D U_+^\infty\overline C^\infty,\\ R_-^\infty&=\kappa^{-1}C^\infty V_+^\infty\mathsf D^{-}\overline C^\infty. \end{split} \tag{4} $$ Then for the actual inclusion $i:H_N^2\to\mathcal P^2$, $$ \boxed{\qquad R_\pm^\infty i=iR_\pm.\qquad} \tag{5} $$ Indeed $\overline C^\infty i=iC^{-1}$. The transfer $U_+^\infty$ or $V_+^\infty$ can overflow only its first index. Before the next transfer, $C^\infty$ applies its input support $P$, which kills that overflow. Its surviving part is exactly the truncated $U_+$ or $V_+$ in the original strict factorization. The two extensions in (4) need not be inverses on the whole polynomial space. Their restrictions to the original head are the prescribed signed inverse crossings. That is sufficient for an arbitrary signed word. The proof is unchanged for unequal colors in the actual [typed strict formula](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md): $C_x^{-1}$ on input, $C_y$ on output, the original $D_{x,y}$, and the stated $x^{-1}$ or $y^{-1}$ Euler argument. Their coefficients change; the support argument does not. All unrolled common Cartan and external normalization lines multiply the same two realizations. ### Every nonempty upper-tail branch vanishes in the complete crossing One may replace ANY subset of the original internal finite projections by Hardy projections, not merely all of them at once. To see this, follow the three transfer stages in (4), in traversal order. 1. The inverse-fusion $V_-^\infty$ can overflow only head two. The following $\mathsf F_2$ kills that overflow before the central transfer. 2. The central $U_+^\infty$ or $V_+^\infty$ can overflow only head one. The input $\mathsf F_1$ of the final fusion kills it before the final $U_-^\infty$ transfer. 3. The final $U_-^\infty$ can overflow only head two, which the last $\mathsf F_2$ kills. The remaining factors between these barriers are diagonal; they cannot return an overflow to the head. Spectator heads remain in their original finite heads. Earlier killing by any additional finite projection therefore removes only paths that the barrier would already kill. On Laurent inputs the exact decomposition is $$ \Pi_N=\Pi_+-\Pi_{\ge N},\qquad \Pi_{\ge N}(z,w)=\frac{(z/w)^N}{1-z/w}. \tag{5a} $$ In the nested Hardy chamber, expand the original finite projection factors using (5a). **Every term containing at least one upper-tail factor has zero full-crossing action on the original head.** The same assertion holds for boundary fusion factors and for every original full word by (6). This is an ordered barrier identity. It is not an assertion that an arbitrary endpoint coupon or Ward current is zero. Inserting a new operator between a transfer and its barrier can invalidate it. ## 3. Whole-word and source identity For $b$ heads write $i_b:H_N^{\otimes b}\to\mathcal P^{\otimes b}$. Embedding the two-head operators of (4) at every letter gives for EVERY signed braid word $$ \boxed{\quad W^\infty(\beta)i_b=i_bW(\beta).\quad} \tag{6} $$ This follows by induction from (5); no intermediate finite-head projector is used. Every original input/output entry, pivotal partial trace, marked source, peripheral function and external framing line is consequently preserved.
