The same inclusion intertwines any original finite-head coupon inserted BETWEEN complete crossings, provided its extension restricts to that coupon on the head. This includes the original Hopf currents, so the full Ward identities and their original source pairings are preserved. It does not assert the same statement for an arbitrary coupon inserted between the elementary factors of one crossing. The original closed-braid boundary still has its prescribed finite pivotal sum. Alternatively use the already proved full fused $2k$-plat formula $$ P_{\beta,N}=\chi_{\beta,N}N^{1-k} \langle e_{\mathrm{out}},B_\beta e_{\mathrm{in}}\rangle. \tag{7} $$ Here every input pair is $(d,0)$; every ordinary output pair is $(0,d)$; the marked output pair is $(d,0)$. Expand $B_\beta$ into its actual pair fusions, signed crossings and retained original scalar lines. Apply (3)--(6). The result is exactly (7) on the polynomial space, with monomial input and coefficient-extraction output. The Ward corner in (7) is the theorem for the FULL assembled intertwining word. It is not applied separately to a Hardy, cyclic, or sewing summand. ## 4. The scalar integral has no finite Dirichlet numerators Let $$ K_+(t)=\frac1{1-t},\qquad |t|<1. $$ This is the Hardy reproducing kernel for nonnegative powers. For example the transfer kernel on two heads is now $$ \prod_j K_+(z_j/w_j)\, u_N(x^{-1}w_2/w_1), \tag{8} $$ with $v_N$ and the reversed argument for the other transfers. The diagonal kernels are exactly the existing finite ones: $$ \mathsf F^{-}:u_N(z/w),\qquad \mathsf F:N(z/w)^{N-1}v_N(Qw/z),\qquad \mathsf D^{\pm}:\Gamma_{\pm,N}(z/w). \tag{9} $$ Their spectators contribute $K_+$ instead of $K_N$. Thus **all internal factors $(1-t^N)/(1-t)$ are replaced by $1/(1-t)$**, without approximating or discarding a period. The proof is the complete ordered support identity above, not replacement of one split reproducing residue in isolation. For monomial boundary data $e_a,e_c$ and a word with $L$ elementary factors, its entry is $$ \operatorname{CT}_{z^0,\ldots,z^L} (z^0)^a(z^L)^{-c} \prod_{\ell=1}^{L}K^\infty_\ell(z^\ell,z^{\ell-1}). \tag{10} $$ Choose nested positive radii $|z^\ell_j|<|z^{\ell-1}_j|$. Every Hardy series converges there; every other factor is a finite Laurent polynomial. The CT is consequently a literal rational Cauchy integral. There are a fixed number of variables for a fixed plat, independent of $N$. No cycle made solely of Hardy inequalities is being imposed: the boundary in (10) is monomial. The initial/final finite indices and every scalar in (7) remain the original ones. ## 5. Exact gain and the remaining geometric charge This eliminates a specific exponential branch family from the original scalar Cauchy presentation: the finite Dirichlet numerators and their artificial split poles. Nonzero intermediate overflow routes are allowed and then killed by the support of the original diagonal kernels. The earlier source-visible coupon $X_-X_+$ has no intervening finite diagonal barrier: an upper excursion can return before it is tested. Its nonzero endpoint correction is therefore consistent with this theorem. Likewise the cyclic-sewing and Fermat-cap walls are different relative terms and have not been deleted here. It does not eliminate the finite endpoints of $u_N,v_N$ or $\Gamma_{\pm,N}$. The diagonal support in (1) is essential; replacing those kernels by unrelated nonfinite symbols is outside the theorem. The Hardy poles in (8) are also genuine reproducing poles; contour transport must retain their actual residues. All elementary transfers preserve total INTEGER degree. Hence (10) retains the original total plat degree $k(N-1)$, and after ordinary caps the remaining pair has the exact affine charge $D+1=N$ from [the charged cap theorem](actual_degree_carry_and_cap_winding_obstruction.md). The theorem does not impose that pair charge at every intermediate slice: crossings between pairs move degree between them. What is still missing is the source-preserving identification of a geometric Pachner edge's three angle clocks with that augmented charged class. The Hardy replacement supplies a simpler exact whole-word integral on which to seek it; it does not prove $h_1+h_2+h_3=N$ for an unassigned geometric edge or select the hyperbolic critical cycle.

title: Exact Hardy-forest residue reduction of the original selected cycle
text: # Exact Hardy-forest residue reduction of the original selected cycle 28 October 2026. All Hardy/reset variables in [the continuous-Gaussian cyclic period](actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) admit a simultaneous ordinary-residue reduction. The surviving cycle is specified explicitly. Every other annulus component is retained first and then proved zero against the original source by a one-way negative-index barrier. The normal residue coefficient is exactly $+1$. This is the coefficient of the Hardy pole graph, **not** a computed intersection number with a hyperbolic thimble. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_hardy_forest_residue.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_hardy_forest_residue_results.json) check eight original whole-word pivotal matrices with no intermediate Hardy/head projection, 360 signed head columns, 812 negative-current subsets, nonzero surviving negative outputs before the original source, the pole-forest Jacobian, and reduced radius chambers. ## 1. Hardy poles form a forest Keep the fully telescoped physical braid word, with its boundary pair fusions and original monomial input/output. Every Hardy factor connects consecutive variables of ONE head in word time: $$ K_e=\frac1{1-g_e z_{\mathrm{out}}/z_{\mathrm{in}}}. $$ Here $g_e=1$, except at an actual Gaussian dilation where $g_e=c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}$. Transfer multiplication does not identify different heads. An active factorial kernel breaks the path; its input and output variables remain independent. The monomial source adds no closing Hardy edge. Thus the Hardy pole graph is a forest of head-time segments. Choose one terminal variable per segment and set $$ u_e=\frac{z_{\mathrm{in}}}{g_ez_{\mathrm{out}}}. \tag{1} $$ The logarithmic incidence matrix is triangular/unimodular. Using path normals followed by the terminal coordinate gives determinant one with the induced orientation. The base-only $d\log g_e$ terms vanish when wedged with all Gaussian $d\xi$ variables. Consequently $$ K_e\,\frac{du_e}{2\pi i u_e} =\frac{du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)}. \tag{2} $$ Every normal pole is now independent, with residue $+1$. No scalar $g_e$, determinant root, meridian factor, or Gaussian Jacobian is removed. Such factors remain in the substituted source and cyclic arguments. ## 2. A reduced cycle before taking the residues The pole graph sets $u_e=1$: $$ z_{\mathrm{in}}=g_ez_{\mathrm{out}}. \tag{3} $$ After imposing it, retain one complex variable per head-time segment and every real Gaussian variable. Equivalently, one may retain the initial coordinate of each head and a new coordinate after each active factorial. Moving the retained coordinate within a segment multiplies it by a known nonzero product of $g_e$; its logarithmic Jacobian is one. There are $b+6m$ complex coordinates for the displayed strict $m$-crossing physical word on $b$ heads. The two boundary pair-fusion frames of a $2k$-plat add $6k$, giving $6m+8k$ in the unshortened presentation. Further exact simplifications may reduce this count. All counts are independent of $N$. ### Explicit radii without resets Take $\rho_0=1/64$ and $0<\lambda\le1$ below all active color moduli. The following construction works for every fixed Gaussian tuple and every signed word. For one crossing, let its input head radii be $R_1,R_2$, and put $G=|c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}|$. The inverse-fusion part is realized by $$ \begin{split} b&=\min(\rho_0R_2/2,\ \rho_0\lambda R_1/2),\\ a&=\rho_0R_1/2,\\ c&=\max(2b/\rho_0,\ 2aG_*/(\rho_0\lambda)), \end{split} \tag{4} $$ where $G_*=1$ for the positive crossing and $G_*=\max(1,G)$ for the negative crossing. The first reciprocal factorial updates head two to $b$. Its following $V_-$ transfer has argument modulus at most $\rho_0/2$. The reciprocal factorial on head one updates it to $a$, and the positive factorial on head two updates it to $c$. Positively, the central transfer uses radii $a,c$, then the Gaussian graph changes head two to $c/G$. Negatively, that Gaussian graph comes first and the central transfer uses $a,c/G$. Formula (4) makes its argument small in either order. For the final fusion choose $$ e=\min(\rho_0(c/G)/2,\ \rho_0\lambda a/2),\quad f=2a/\rho_0,\quad q=2e/\rho_0. \tag{5} $$ Its reciprocal second-head diagonal updates to $e$, its positive first-head factorial to $f$, its $U_-$ multiplier leaves these coordinates unchanged, and its final factorial updates head two to $q$. Every cyclic argument has modulus below $\rho_0$. Spectator coordinates are simply identified, rather than being constrained by an extra radius inequality. For a boundary fusion use its three diagonal updates and the same preparation of its one transfer; no Gaussian compensation is needed. The inverse boundary fusion is handled in the same way. The full complex Gaussian relation in (3), including its phase, is imposed; (4)--(5) give its radii. All logarithms of the chosen radii satisfy $$ |\log r_j|\le C_{\mathrm{word}} \left(1+\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell|\right). \tag{6} $$ Indeed each update is a minimum/maximum of one preceding logarithm plus a fixed constant and, at most, a term $\pm\log G$. There is no multiplicative recursion of logarithms. This gives a specified reduced fibered torus cycle, not separate incompatible local circles. ## 3. An exact simultaneous annulus decomposition Let $H$ be the number of Hardy edges. Starting from the reduced radii above, choose $$ \eta=\frac{\log2}{4(H+1)}. $$ In the normal coordinates (1), allow $e^{-\eta}\le|u_e|\le e^\eta$ independently. Each unreduced head coordinate is a retained coordinate times a product of path normals and Gaussian factors. Each cyclic argument therefore changes in modulus by at most $e^{2H\eta}<\sqrt2$. Since its reduced value is below $1/64$, it remains below $1/16$ throughout this complete polyannulus. In particular NO cyclic norm divisor is crossed. Every cyclic root has its original anchored lift. Only the explicit independent poles $u_e=1$ occur in these annuli. The outer torus $|u_e|=e^\eta$ has every Hardy argument strictly below one. It can be reached from the original reset-cycle chamber without crossing a pole or norm divisor: all radius constraints are affine strict inequalities in logarithmic radii, so interpolate linearly. Both cycles have cyclic arguments below $1/16$ and Hardy arguments below one. Estimate (6) and the Gaussian majorant hold uniformly in this homotopy. Now apply the ordinary annulus identity in each independent $u_e$: $$ \int_{|u_e|=e^\eta}\frac{F\,du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)} =F|_{u_e=1} +\int_{|u_e|=e^{-\eta}} \frac{F\,du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)}. \tag{7} $$ The other variables are retained. Iteration gives a finite sum of $2^H$ relative components: the full pole graph and all possible nonempty sets of inner circuits. Nothing is shrunk to zero or infinity. Any information inside an inner circuit, including possible distant branch divisors, is still represented by that circuit. The assertion below is that its original source pairing is zero, not that it is zero in unpointed twisted homology. On each inner circle, $$ K_e=-\sum_{a<0}(g_ez_{\mathrm{out}}/z_{\mathrm{in}})^a. \tag{8} $$ It is precisely the negative-Laurent current at that head-time edge. Residue edges implement ordinary coordinate identification/dilation. All these series converge absolutely in their stated chambers. Every branch cycle has the same type of joint bound $$ C N^B\exp\{C_0N+C_1N\sum|\xi_\ell| -N\|\boldsymbol\xi\|^2/2\}. $$ For the absolute coefficient expansion, bound cyclic coefficients on a slightly larger disk still below one; the resulting absolute series has the same exponential-in-$N$ bound. Hardy series have a fixed geometric ratio $e^{-\eta}$. Thus Fubini/Tonelli and coefficient routing are justified, including the noncompact Gaussian base and the radius homotopy. ## 4. Every nonempty inner-current component is source-null Use signed integer head indices; do NOT impose a Hardy projection. The exact scalar kernels have these elementary support properties: - a reciprocal factorial has only nonnegative diagonal coefficients, so it kills a negative active index; - a positive factorial has only diagonal indices at most $d=N-1$; its negative Laurent coefficients are retained and may be nonzero; - a transfer has order $h\ge0$ and changes indices by $(a,b)\mapsto(a-h,b+h)$ or $(a+h,b-h)$; - a Gaussian dilation preserves every signed index. Consider the actual fully ordered crossing $C\,D\,U_+\,C^{-1}$ or $C\,V_+\,D^{-1}C^{-1}$. 1. In $C^{-1}$, a new negative first index is lowered further before the reciprocal first-head factorial kills it. A negative second input is killed immediately by its first reciprocal second-head diagonal. 2. A negative second index created by the central transfer survives any dilation, then is killed by $C$'s first reciprocal second-head diagonal. 3. The last $U_-$ in $C$ can emit a negative FIRST head. Its other head is nonnegative and at most $d$ after the last positive factorial. At the next crossing touching the negative head, that head is killed in $C^{-1}$: immediately if it is second, or after further lowering if it is first. An untouched negative head cannot heal. Diagonal negative Laurent coefficients never change an index and therefore cannot repair it. This proof uses no cancellation of coefficients and is independent of colors or Gaussian values. The original cup input is nonnegative. A boundary fusion applied to $(d,0)$ produces no negative survivor, since its last positive factorial requires $h\le d$. The terminal inverse-fusion frames kill any negative head. Alternatively, an original finite nonnegative output coefficient or pivotal cut kills any untouched negative output. Thus there is NO supported route from any nonempty negative-current component in (7) to the original output source. Its exact pairing is zero. Arbitrary Laurent-healing coupons inserted inside the word are outside this statement; original finite coupons may be extended by zero outside their heads. This is a route-support proof on the actual kernels, not reconstruction and evaluation of an entire prefix polynomial. Infinite cyclic tails are handled by the convergence argument in Section 3. Combining (7)--(8), the original selected period equals the **pure all-pole graph integral with coefficient exactly $+1$**. All other circuits have been retained and explicitly proved source-null. ## 5. Explicit reduced scalar phase and cycle coordinates After the residues: - each transfer is multiplication by its cyclic function in the two current head coordinates; - every spectator/reset coordinate is identified; - an active factorial retains a new complex coordinate and its cyclic convolution kernel; - a Gaussian identifies its input/output by $w=g_s(\xi)z$, and its ordinary Gaussian variable remains integrated on $\mathbb R$. There are no rational Hardy poles left. The surviving cycle is exactly the fibered product of circles in (4)--(5), with the anchored cyclic roots, not an arbitrary positive-angle chain. Here is the variable-dependent leading phase of one positive crossing explicitly. Let its input coordinates be $z_1,z_2$, its six successive active factorial output coordinates be $u_1,\ldots,u_6$, and put $g=-(xy)^{-1}e^{\sqrt{\pi}(1+i)\xi}$. The output coordinates are $u_5,u_6$. With limiting marked colors $x,y$ and phase convention $\exp(W/h)$, $$ \begin{split} W_+={}&-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/z_2) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/(xz_1)) -\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/z_1) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/u_3)\\ &-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/(xu_3)) -\operatorname{Li}_2(gu_4/u_3) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/u_5) -\operatorname{Li}_2(u_4/(yu_5)) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_4/u_6)\\ &+2\pi i\left[ \log(u_3/u_1)+\log(u_5/u_2)+\log(u_6/u_4) \right]-\pi i\xi^2 . \tag{9} \end{split} $$ For a negative crossing use $g=-(xy)e^{\sqrt{\pi}(1-i)\xi}$ and replace its central term $-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/(xu_3))$ by $+\operatorname{Li}_2(gu_2/(yu_3))$. All other terms follow the same strict order. The full word phase is the sum of these local phases and boundary-fusion phases, together with $2\pi i$ times the original initial-minus-terminal source logarithms. The original external $\chi_{\beta,N}$ is retained separately. Exact $q$ half-steps and the difference between $N$ and $N-1$ contribute the specified nonzero amplitude; they are not discarded normalization. All logarithmic marks in (9) come from the original reflected factorial monomials and source. Norm roots retain the continuation from the small-argument cycle. ## 6. Actual classical coordinates, rather than unnamed auxiliaries Let $p$ be the momentum conjugate to $\log z$, so $B=e^p$ is the physical clock $Q^a$. The reduced elementary phase relations give: $$ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{kernel}&\text{canonical input/output relation}\\ \hline \mathcal U(z/w)& B_{\mathrm{out}}=B_{\mathrm{in}}=B,\quad z=w(1-B)\\ N(z/w)^d\mathcal V(Qw/z)& B_{\mathrm{out}}=B_{\mathrm{in}}=B,\quad z=w/(1-B)\\ \text{Gaussian}& B_{\mathrm{out}}=B_{\mathrm{in}}=B,\quad w=c_sB^s z \end{array} \tag{10} $$ The positive-factorial momentum lift includes its retained $2\pi i$. The transfer multipliers change the momenta by the derivatives of their dilogarithms. For example a $U_-$ multiplier with $t=x^{-1}z_2/z_1$ sends $$ B_1\mapsto B_1/(1-t),\qquad B_2\mapsto B_2(1-t), $$ and leaves the two position coordinates unchanged. The Gaussian relation follows from $\partial_\xi W=-2\pi i\xi+\alpha_s p=0$ and $\alpha_s^2=2\pi is$. This identifies concrete parts of the known actual fusion chart. For a full $C_x$ put $A=B_1,J=B_2$ and $$ K=1-\frac{z_2}{xz_1}(1-A)(1-J). $$ Composition of the elementary relations gives $$ \begin{split} U&=A/K,\qquad V=JK,\\ z'_1&=z_1/(1-A),\qquad z'_2=z_2(1-J)/(1-JK). \tag{11} \end{split} $$ With $$ p_A=z_1^{-1},\quad p_J=z_2^{-1},\quad p_U=(z'_1)^{-1},\quad p_V=(z'_2)^{-1}, $$ equation (11) is EXACTLY the previously proved [actual rational fusion graph](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md), including its inverse. Thus the remaining coordinates are actual cotangent/head variables. There is also a literal shared-flag dictionary on the unwrapped Laurent realization: $$ Z_i=B_i,\quad S_i=z_i,\quad X=xz_2/z_1,\quad Z=B_1,\quad XZ=QZX. \tag{12} $$ At the complete color, $$ (Q-B_1^{-1})X=q\,\mathcal E_1z_2. $$ This is the actual tetrahedral factor in [the middle five-point wall calculation](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). However $X^N=x^Nz_2^N/z_1^N$ is still a variable central multiplication; no typed $X^N=1$ has been imposed by renaming variables. At $M=1$ the classical generators are $F=(1-B)z$, $\mathcal E=z^{-1}(B^{-1}-1)$ and $K=-B^{-1}$. Up to its specified scalar lift, the actual shared meridian matrix is the usual unipotent Gauss chart with $A=B$ and flag coordinate $z^{-1}$. This gives an explicit comparison with known classical flag variables, not a conclusion that the reduced cycle is already a positive Rivin-angle cycle. ## 7. What remains unproved The selected auxiliary Hardy cycle has now been pushed forward exactly, with its normal degree $+1$, all inner currents accounted for, and an explicit reduced phase and cycle. The unreduced Hardy normal directions are no longer being treated as ordinary geometric stationary variables. The reduced cycle is still the small-argument anchored cycle above. Its transport through cyclic norm divisors and the actual five-term flag atlas to a regular hyperbolic chart has not been proved. Neither the normal residue degree nor the existence of a geometric critical representation computes its geometric intersection number. In particular no volume conjecture or hyperbolic noncancellation is claimed here.

title: The actual highest-input / Whittaker-output boundary retains two walls
The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm
text: # The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm 27 October 2026. The explicit cyclic source gauge in [the actual Fourier twisted-trace theorem](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md) has a rigorously computable exponential scale, even in the flat right-regular metric. This is an ACTUAL gauge from the original source construction, not an arbitrary central rescaling of a state. It proves why solving its norm-one transport equation does not by itself give a subexponential comparison to a geometric period. The result also identifies a concrete dilogarithm action of this source gauge on a regular chart. It does not identify that chart with the marked geometric A-component or its Bloch regulator. ## 1. The specified actual gauge Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, h=2pi*i/N and z^N=0. The primitive k=1 source sector has the unique scalar-polynomial gauge with constant term one g_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz) =[u_N(z)u_N(Qz)]^-1, (1) u_N(z)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) z^a/(Q;Q)_a, v_N=u_N^-1 in the nilpotent algebra. It solves g_N(Qz)/g_N(z)=1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)], eliminating the corresponding inner twist of the source automorphism. The constant-term and transport equation make it unique: a quotient of two gauges would be Q-invariant, hence constant in degree<N. The full matrix comparison can have other choices; no uniqueness claim for all matrix gauges is made. The CANONICAL polynomial representative of (1), of degree<N, is exactly the Taylor polynomial through degree N-1 of exp(L_N(z)), where L_N(z)=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) (1+Q^a) z^a/[a(Q^a-1)] =-i sum_(a=1)^(N-1) cot(pi*a/N) z^a/a. (2) Indeed the logarithm of v_N in the nilpotent algebra is sum z^a/[a(Q^a-1)]. Adding its shifted logarithm gives (2). This establishes the relation to the ACTUAL finite gauge before using analytic estimates. It is not an unproved resummation of quantum jets. ## 2. Uniform asymptotics of the actual polynomial on a fixed disk For |z|<=1/4 one has, uniformly as N grows, g_N(z)=exp[(2/h) Li_2(z)+O(1/N)]. (3) The same statement with the opposite sign holds for the canonical degree-<N representative of g_N^-1. In particular these finite polynomials have no zero on that disk for all sufficiently large N. Here is a proof that retains the truncation error. First, on every fixed disk |z|<=rho<1, L_N(z)=(2/h)Li_2(z)+O(1/N). (4) For a<=N/2 use the uniform elementary estimate cot(t)=1/t+O(t) on 0<t<=pi/2. Dividing its error by a gives O(1/N) per coefficient, whose sum against rho^a remains O(1/N). For a>N/2, the inequality |cot(pi*a/N)| <= N/[2 min(a,N-a)] gives a tail O(rho^(N/2) log N), and the omitted tail of Li_2 is smaller. This proves (4) with both root endpoints accounted for. Put G_N=exp(L_N) as an ordinary analytic function. On |z|=1/2, the coarser |cot(pi*a/N)|<=N/2 gives |L_N(z)| <= (N/2)log 2, |G_N(z)| <= exp[(N/2)log 2]. Cauchy's coefficient bound and the degree-N Taylor tail therefore give, throughout |z|<=1/4, |G_N(z)-g_N(z)| <= 2 exp[-(N/2)log 2]. (5) Meanwhile (4) gives |G_N(z)| >= exp[-N Li_2(1/4)/pi-O(1/N)]. For example Li_2(1/4)<=13/48, so Li_2(1/4)/pi is strictly smaller than log(2)/2. Thus (5) is exponentially small RELATIVE to G_N on the entire disk. Combining it with (4) proves (3) for the actual canonical polynomial. Replacing L_N by -L_N proves the inverse statement by the identical estimate. The Taylor-tail estimate is essential. Nilpotent equality alone would not justify evaluating its analytic exponential away from zero, as the nonzero endpoint carry in [the meridian half-step theorem](actual_euler_meridian_half_step.md) explicitly demonstrates. ## 3. A positive exponential lower bound for this comparison gauge Take w=i/4 and set c=Im Li_2(i/4)/pi > 0. The alternating power series proves Im Li_2(i/4) >= 1/4-(1/4)^3/9=143/576. Equation (3) gives the precise scalar-gauge rate log|g_N(i/4)|=c N+O(1/N). (6) To pass from this polynomial value to an ACTUAL finite operator, use the flat right-regular basis f^a e_j. The operator R_f is a truncated shift with unit coefficients. For |x|=1, its argument xR_f has norm one, and the powers applied to a degree-zero basis vector are orthogonal. If g_N(z)=sum c_a z^a, this gives ||g_N(xR_f)|| >= (sum |c_a|^2)^(1/2) >= sqrt(15/16)|g_N(i/4)|. (7) The second inequality is just Cauchy--Schwarz for evaluation at |w|=1/4. Multiplication by x^a changes no coefficient norm. Thus this specified comparison gauge has exponential operator growth, with liminf N^-1 log||g_N(xR_f)||>=c. Applying the inverse version of (3) at -i/4 proves the same lower bound for its inverse. Its condition number therefore has liminf logarithmic rate at least 2c. All these operators are unipotent: their diagonal entries and determinants are one. The source transport is cyclic and obeys its exact norm-one equation. Those algebraic facts coexist with the exponential norm in (7). This result concerns the flat coefficient metric. A nonunitary physical fusion change requires its own metric comparison. ## 4. Implication for the intended torsor proof The primitive source transport is explicitly SOLVED at each level, and its gauge action is the specified dilogarithm in (3). Its comparison is not tempered. A proof may carry this action into the marked regulator rather than try to discard the gauge as a normalization. Which combination of actions and source sectors is selected by the original knot word remains to be proved. This establishes neither a counterexample to the volume conjecture nor an exponential estimate for the knot invariant. The number c above is a gauge-chart value, not a knot's hyperbolic volume. It does not rule out a different whole comparison with controlled norm. It does rule out inferring such control for this actual primitive gauge solely from Hilbert 90, finite cyclicity, unipotence or determinant one. The rigorous uniform normal-form estimate (3) is the new local period/action comparison here. The nonzero selected geometric image and global sector/cancellation estimates remain open. Subsequent direct source calculations now distinguish that operator norm from selected local periods. The [canonical resonant endpoint](actual_primitive_gauge_resonant_endpoint.md) is an explicit Gauss period of size N^-1/2. The [normalized top-coefficient period](actual_gauge_period_selects_algebraic_point.md) selects the algebraic point 2 on fixed polynomial observables and intertwines fixed ordered gauge meridian steps. Thus this specified source has an evaluated local leading period, not just an exponential operator estimate. Its full knot-word coupling and selected hyperbolic action remain unproved. [The high-precision diagnostic](../experiments/audit_actual_hilbert90_gauge_action.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_hilbert90_gauge_action_results.json) compare the literal finite v_N(z)v_N(Qz) polynomial with exp(L_N) and its dilogarithm action. The theorem rests on the uniform proof above; numerical rate samples are not used as a proof.
