text: # Homogeneous face kernels for the original Casimir coupons 30 October 2026. This stays within the original fixed flat-plat presentation. No arbitrary matched graph-to-plat adapter is being assumed. ## 1. One homogeneous local polynomial Let N>=3,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N),Q=q^2, and let Omega be the actual balanced pair Casimir. At a box retain the literal face order (x,b,c,y): input middle b, output middle c. If F=f(-T), where T is the [source-normalized small-circle face operator](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md), write for 0<=j<N F z^j=sum_(a,beta>=0; a+beta<=j) M_f(j;a,beta) x^a y^beta z^(j-a-beta). Define a HOMOGENEOUS polynomial in the four original faces by H_f(x,b,c,y)=sum_(j=0)^d sum_(a,beta) M_f(j;a,beta) x^a b^(j-a-beta)c^(d-j)y^beta. (1) All exponents are nonnegative and its total degree is d. This uses the whole polynomial f(Omega), with all repeated-node data; it is not a spectral-value interpolation. The operator T preserves polynomials and degree and commutes with z^N, so the N input monomials determine the exact local cyclic shift operator. Examples, with all scalar conventions explicit: H_1=sum_(j=0)^d b^j c^(d-j). H_(L_h)=T_h^(b) H_1, H_(L_h R^epsilon)=lambda0^epsilon T_h^(b) H_(r_N^epsilon), lambda0=q^(d^2/2), epsilon=+/-1. (2) Here T_h=P_(h-1)(T), and the superscript means that T acts on the variable b with outer variables x,y. The original square-root lift in lambda0 is retained. This is root algebra, not a genuine-q germ. The normalized crossing polynomial r_N and its inverse have the literal Hermite data in the signed one-port theorem. Write M=floor(d/2); the quantities k_a, beta_a, D_a and Ptilde_s below are the exact factors of the [positive-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md). The complete circle has the exact identity H_(L_N)=N sum_(a=0)^M k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)Ptilde_(d-2a)(x,y). (3) It follows either by applying the already proved original complete spectral identity to (1), or by the finite Newton formula. With a retained half twist, insert the actual omega_a^epsilon in (3). For each fixed complete channel, its H is N times that literal local positive polynomial, including k_a beta_a^2 and its phase. ## 2. Exact local physical face-grid identity Keep ALL formal Casimir step words and group them by p modulo N only after inserting the source phase q^(d p). Write the resulting normalized q-difference operator F g(z)=sum_(p mod N) A_p(x/z,y/z) g(Q^-p z). Its inverse finite Fourier transform is exact: A_p(X,Y)=N^-1 sum_(j=0)^d P_j(X,Y) Q^(p j), P_j=sum M_f(j;a,beta)X^aY^beta. (4) On the actual face grid, c=Q^-p b. Consequently c^-d H_f(x,b,c,y)=sum_j P_j(x/b,y/b)(b/c)^j =N A_p(x/b,y/b). (5) For the physical input heads u,v and output heads r,s, the literal clocks are U=-q^-1 x/b,V=-q^-1 b/y, and p=r-u. The original matrix element is therefore f(Omega)_(r,s;u,v) =N^-1 q^(-d p)c^-d H_f(x,b,c,y) (6) when the output clocks are represented by c. This includes zero when the modular output has the wrong UNWRAPPED total: every Casimir word has the true vanishing physical endpoint coefficient, so an illegal wrap has zero coefficient before it can become a physical path. The finite R/R^-1 are the actual polynomials in this same Casimir, with the specified lambda0 and Hermite derivative. Equation(6) is not an extension obtained by discarding a physical endpoint. ## 3. Original mark, integer lifts and even-level carries Use the actual connected flat plat with R boxes and R+2 white faces. Retain the original cups and every ordinary cap except its ONE original unrestricted marked cap. There are R ordinary face targets and two protected faces u,v. All coupons f(Omega) preserve the literal integer sum of the two main-head indices. Thus after the other caps the two indices at the marked cap necessarily sum to d, exactly as in the original marked face-coefficient proof. Its ratio to the ordinary cap is still the actual N^-1 (L_v/L_u)^d, not a new trace functional. For a nonzero physical state, the centered main heads define an integer conserved flow on the actual planar four-valent Morse graph, including the cups and caps. The elementary planar face-potential argument gives integer lifted potentials, unique up to a common constant, with the literal half-index offsets. Equivalently, the main heads have i=d/2+n_left-n_right+(t_left-t_right)/2. Here t=0 for odd N and t is the original gap parity for even N. Adjacent main regions have opposite t at even N; the two middle faces of a box have the same t. In particular the ACTUAL physical p=r-u equals n_b-n_c, not just its residue modulo N. Use these lifted logarithms in the intermediate half powers. Then q^(-d p)(bc)^(d/2)=c^d, (7) f(Omega)_(r,s;u,v)=N^-1 H_f(x,b,c,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (7a) The second identity follows DIRECTLY from (6),(7); it does not use a complete-box factorization as a black box. Here is the entire remaining turn calculation. It is the literal matrix calculation in the [original marked face-coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md), sections 2--3. For a physical complementary pair with first head i and second j=d-i, cup(i,j)=N q^(-d^2+di), cap(i,j)=N^-1 q^(di), mark(i,j)=N^-2 q^(dj). The centered first head on a cup/cap has outside region o and inside region z, so q^(di)=q^(d^2/2)(L_o/L_z)^(d/2). Thus each cup constant is N q^(-d^2/2), each ordinary cap constant is N^-1 q^(d^2/2), and their k pairs cancel EXACTLY. The mark-to-ordinary-cap ratio is N^-1 q^(-d^2)Q^(dj)=N^-1(L_v/L_u)^d, with the original SECOND head j. This uses the whole-source complementary constraint already proved above, rather than restricting the original mark in advance. Let T_f count +1 for each outside cup/cap corner and -1 for each inside corner. The turn product is therefore N^-1 (L_v/L_u)^d product_f L_f^[(d/2)T_f]. Let M_f count the input/output middle incidences at ALL original boxes, independently of which f(Omega) is inserted. The flat-plat sweep gives M_f-T_f=2 at every bounded face and M_u-T_u=-2 at the exterior. Every bounded gap segment has two middle-or-inside-turn ends; the exterior has 2(k-1) middle ends and 2k outside turns. This argument uses only the original projection, not a smoothed graph. Multiplying (7a) over the R boxes now gives the literal total summand N^(-R-1) product_e H_(f_e) *(L_v/L_u)^d product_f L_f^[(d/2)(T_f-M_f)] =N^(-R-1) product_e H_(f_e) /product_ordinary L_f^d. (7b) All half powers have disappeared and every face exponent in the final expression is integral. Changing any lifted n_f by N leaves it unchanged. This is why both parities have the same final formula; local lift signs have not been reset independently. The original cup, cap, mark and index formulas have all been displayed, and none depends on using a complete coupon at a box. Conversely each original finite face-grid point specifies canonical physical main heads. If an unwrapped conservation equation fails, its actual matrix element (6) vanishes. If all are nonzero, the conserved flow gives the lifted potentials just used, so the equality applies. The original positive complete-channel support zeros are included when such coupons are retained. Thus this is an equality of the actual finite source sums, not an unconstrained off-grid continuation. ## 4. Whole-source polynomial coefficient, with no smoothing hypothesis The original finite face grid has N^(R+1) points, after fixing the exterior potential. The original marked scalar is N^-1. Each of the R local inverse Fourier transforms contributed exactly N^-1. Therefore the actual source is the normalized face-grid average of product_(boxes e) H_(f_e)(L_x,L_b,L_c,L_y) /product_(ordinary faces) L_f^d. (8) Equivalently it is Z_N=[product_(ordinary faces) L_f^d] product_e H_(f_e)(L_x,L_b,L_c,L_y), with both protected exponents equal0. (9) The primitive grid normalization is exactly accounted for: there is NO extra N^R in (9), because H_f itself includes the N in (3). If r boxes remain complete and the others are general, extracting their N factors gives N^r times the original remaining spectral scalars. All external Cartan and framing factors stay exactly where specified. To prove that the grid average is exactly (9), the numerator is a polynomial with nonnegative exponents (not necessarily positive coefficients), homogeneous of degree dR. The grid selects exponents d mod N at all R ordinary faces and0 mod N at the protected face v. Since d=N-1, the former have minimal nonnegative representative d. The total degree forces them ALL to equal d, and the protected exponents to equal zero. The exterior face exponent then also equals zero. In the even coset, the resulting phase is one since every exponent equals its target. This excludes ALL aliases on the original grid. It does not use a merge forest, an elimination order, or the connectedness of any identity-smoothed projection. In particular (9) applies to disconnected small-port subsets and to sets with outer-variable dependency cycles. The fixed original projection remains connected, which is the stated flat-plat hypothesis. ## 5. Exact signed magnitude and all-subset local norm certificate For the geometric rate and corridor statements below, assume the original flat plat has the same actual labeled nondegenerate right-angled certificate as the complete-source volume theorem. The finite algebra in sections 1--4 needs only the stated connected original flat-plat source. Put S_0=1 and S_j=product_(v=1)^j 2sin(pi v/N). For i+k+l+t=d, the normalized positive crossing polynomial has exact coefficient on b^i x^k y^l c^t (-1)^(k+l+1) q^[kl-(i+1)(t+1)] N/(S_i S_k S_l S_t). (10) For the inverse, invert q in the displayed phase; all sine factors remain positive. The original lambda0^epsilon multiplies this whole polynomial. Formula(10) follows from the finite q-multinomial kernel: j=d-t, and S_j S_t=S_d=N. In particular its weighted coefficient norm is EXACTLY the positive homogeneous polynomial A_N(b,x,y,c)=sum_(i+k+l+t=d) N b^i x^k y^l c^t/(S_i S_k S_l S_t). (11) Uniform sine-product estimates give N^-1 log A_N -> G(b,x,y,c), the four-angle potential of the [signed one-port theorem](actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md). This follows directly from a single degree-d simplex, not from a maximum over operator blocks. At fixed positive radii, (2) therefore implies ||H_(L_h R^epsilon)|| <=C_b^(h-1) A_N, ||H_(L_h)|| <=N C_b^(h-1) max(b,c)^d, (12) C_b=3+4(x+y)/b+4xy/b^2. The second inequality retains the exact leading rate of H_1, I(b,c)=log max(b,c), max(b,c)^d <= ||H_1|| <=N max(b,c)^d. In particular I<=G, since the b and c corners occur in (11). This keeps the actual cancellations within each local f before taking absolute values. Multiplying (12) and taking the SINGLE coefficient (9) gives the independent-old-face bound without any dependency-order issue. The strongest direct finite certificate is allowed to use different SHARED old-face radii for different subsets. For a nonempty reflected subset S, choose ONE positive radius l_f for each original face, and set C_S(l)=sum_(e notin S) [F(l_x,l_b,l_y)+F(l_x,l_c,l_y)] +sum_(e in S, epsilon_e!=0) G(l_b,l_x,l_y,l_c) +sum_(e in S, epsilon_e=0) I(l_b,l_c) -sum_(ordinary f) log l_f. (13a) Here F is the actual fold triangle rate, including its beta scalar, from the [all-channel rate theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) and its [absolute endpoint normalization](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md). All local factors use the SAME l_f wherever that face occurs. The complete half-twist phases have modulus one and remain in the exact source before applying this bound. The sufficient test is for every nonempty S subset E, there exists l^(S)>0 with C_S(l^(S)) < Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (13b) No uniformity over a changing graph or infinitely many subsets is needed: the original graph and E are fixed. An infimum certificate strictly below Phi_D suffices, because then some finite positive radii realize a smaller strict margin. This formulation retains I for unsigned deleted ports; replacing I by G is a weaker optional bound. The I-only capacity is the same smoothed positive-source capacity underlying the already proved untwisted corridor. No universal existence of mixed signed/unsigned certificates is asserted. Here is a direct justification of that I-only identification. Use the literal merge-forest/exterior-cycle classification in the [simultaneous source theorem](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md), including its disconnected case, and the finite angle-entropy duality of the [smoothed-source capacity theorem](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md). The dual of I(b,c)=max(log b,log c) assigns nonnegative loads sigma_b,sigma_c with sum one to the edge endpoints, with zero entropy. A connected merge tree has total remaining triangle load one if its root is ordinary, and zero if its root is protected. Given a feasible merged angle flow, its lift to the original vertices is unique: at an edge oriented parent-to-child, let L be the remaining triangle load in the entire child subtree, and set sigma_child=1-L, sigma_parent=L. All these loads are in [0,1], since the subtree load is nonnegative and at most the whole component load. Subtracting neighboring subtree balances verifies every original face target; the root balance follows from the component total. Conversely, summing an original feasible flow over each component gives the merged flow. The edge entropy is zero, so both maximized entropies, hence both capacities, agree, whether or not a finite radius minimizer exists. If smoothing disconnects the projection, the exterior component has beta>=1 actual cycles and would require remaining triangle load -beta: its number of original ordinary targets minus its number of deleted edges. Nonnegative angle loads make this impossible; the dual capacity is -infinity. No analogous identification is made for a signed G edge. One simpler sufficient test uses the original marked packing for all S. At those radii put g_e=F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y)-G(b,x,y,c). (13) If g_e>0 for every port in E, then (13b) follows, because I<=G. Every original ordinary target remains d, so this is the literal original target subtraction and it also covers disconnected replacements. Readjusting the shared radii in (13b) can certify a subset even when its original-packing local g_e is nonpositive. For a boundary quartet with some marked face variables zero, this criterion is understood by the LITERAL polynomial and its continuous rate. In (11), zero variables require the corresponding exponents to vanish. The entropy maximum is over that simplex face; G is continuous on every nonzero nonnegative quartet. The same is true of the actual triangle potential F. Hence if (13) is strictly positive there, one may set the marked zeros to sufficiently small FIXED positive radii before applying (12). The C_b constants can grow, but are then fixed; delta is chosen afterwards. No positivity of every boundary g_e is assumed. The local criterion is sufficient, not universal. ## 6. Whole mixed-source corridor under finite shared-radius certificates Let E be any set of varied original circle ports, with their actual epsilon_i in {0,+1,-1}. Suppose the finite shared-radius test (13b) holds. In particular it holds under the simpler local test (13), with the literal marked-zero convention above. No assumption on the identity smoothing of E or of its subsets is needed. All external colors outside E remain N, with arbitrary original complete half twists retained. There are constants delta,gamma>0 and K such that the original mixed source A_N and its EXACT empty-subset complete-image core F_N^E obey |A_N(N-h_E,N_else)-F_N^E(h)| <=N^K exp[N(Phi_D-gamma)] (14) for every sufficiently large N of both parities and every PHYSICAL integer 0<=h_i<=delta N. Indeed the exact reflection expands over finitely many nonempty subsets. A term selecting a zero deficit vanishes because L_0=0; apply (12) only to the positive deficits in the remaining terms. Equations(9),(12) bound each original subset at its chosen shared old-face radii l^(S). The strict margins in (13b) have a positive minimum over the finitely many subsets. If using marked-zero data, first fix positive regularizations preserving those margins. Choose delta afterwards so that all the finite small-color costs C_b^(h_i-1) consume less than half the smallest margin. No N-dependent optimization of radii is used. The uniform all-channel upper estimate handles all remaining complete labels, and their number and measures are polynomial. The original reflection signs and half-twist phases are retained before this bound. Shrink delta further inside the [zero-free complex-core packet](actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md). Its uniform lower rate is at least Phi_D-gamma/2 there. Thus A_N(N-h_E,N_else)/F_N^E(h)=1+O(exp(-cN)) (15) uniformly on that integer corridor. For h_N/N -> chi real in this cube, the [actual marked geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) then gives lim (2pi/N)log|A_N(N-h_(N,E),N_else)| =Vol(rho_chi). (16) The regulator boundary correction vanishes because the selected peripheral U_i=-2pi i chi_i have zero real part. Finite-N critical actions are kept in the core's relative asymptotic; only their proved uniform limit is used here. This is a SUFFICIENT shared-radius corridor. The local-G test is only one way to satisfy it. Some actual boundary quartets fail (13); no universal certificate or positivity, far-color bound, genuine-q normal identity, or filling transfer follows. ## 7. A certified actual local instance and validation The criterion is not merely an open locus of unrelated curvature data. The already used actual width-three flat plat with box word [1,3,0,2,4,1,3], protected faces 0,8, has an exact marked strip packing with finite curvatures (25,9,16,4,1,9,1). At its zero-based port 3 the actual quartet (x,b,c,y) is (4,9,1,1), with distinct unmarked middle faces. Here G=log9 by the dominant-side case, and F(4,9,1)+F(4,1,1)-log9 > 0.45. (17) The audit gives rational centers/radii, verifies every white contact/noncontact and shaded supporting-circle inequality on the original face chart, and certifies (17) by a finite Lobachevsky series with its explicit analytic tail. This supplies an actual one-port instance of (13b), not a claim that all actual diagrams satisfy (13). For the stronger simultaneous theorem, (13b) must be verified for every nonempty subset of the chosen E. Focused audit: [original local matrices, full sources and certificate](../experiments/audit_actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source_results.json). The local checks retain arbitrary polynomial coupons, both crossing signs with lambda0, wrong unwrapped totals, and complete-channel phases. The whole checks use original cups/caps/unrestricted mark, compare coefficient extraction with full physical contractions, and independently average the original even/odd face grids on selected fixtures. They include all-deleted and disconnected substitutions. These finite checks support the exact proof; they do not numerically prove universal shared-radius certificates or a volume limit. The source audit compares complete and signed polynomial coefficients, retained crossing phases, physical entries, whole sources and face-grid points, including illegal-total zeros. It also checks exact white and shaded support. The geometric gap is certified by a 256-bit outward-rounded Arb evaluation of a 100-term Lobachevsky series, with total tail below 0.01910 and lower bound above 0.46643723013, stronger than (17). The conclusion retains the sufficient-certificate, physical-root and fixed-presentation scope.

title: An interior five-point wall cannot be relocated by bare cut cyclicity
text: # An interior five-point wall cannot be relocated by bare cut cyclicity Research note, 28 October 2026. This tests a possible simplification of the retained wall in [the literal middle five-point calculation](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). At the marked endpoint that wall contributes a known polynomial scalar. The same assertion is **false for an untransported interior wall**. An original one-crossing cup and an original figure-eight network give explicit incompatible relocation factors. The result concerns the original actual source, not a hypothetical state model. It does not exclude a Ward-completed relocation with additional currents and its full relative co-source. It proves which additional data cannot be discarded. ## 1. Fix the original wall and source conventions Take N>=2, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), complete color x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, d=N-1, k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1). Use actual balanced heads K=xZ^(-1), e=q rho^2 E, f=F, and cyclic marks S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), W=E_d(Z_1)X. Equivalently, W=x mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor S_2. (1) The original cup and full averaged marked cap are p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. (2) Let B be the original positive checked crossing, with its unchanged common scalar Cartan line kappa external. Thus the full crossing is kappa B and Bp=p. All framing and peripheral factors below multiply the same expressions; none is reset to a new numerical value. The endpoint identities, already proved in the preceding note, are Xp=Q^(-1)p, mWp=Q^(-1)/N. For any actual knot cut C_N=K_N I, a defect on that marked endpoint therefore gives mW(C_N tensor I)p=Q^(-1)K_N/N, m(1-W)(C_N tensor I)p=(1-Q^(-1)/N)K_N. (3) The second multiplier has modulus between 1/2 and 3/2, so this endpoint correction preserves every normalized volume exponent, without a volume conjecture premise. Equations (3) alone do not relocate an interior two-head coupon. ## 2. The exact naturality/current condition fails The coupon (1) acts on two physical heads. Cutting its two ends does not leave a one-strand knot endomorphism. Moreover it is not a Hopf intertwiner. For the actual total lowering current F_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2, direct multiplication gives [K_1K_2,W]=0, [F_tot,W]=(Q^(-1)-1)mu^(-1) |d><0| tensor S_2^2 !=0. (4) Indeed f_1W=Wf_1=0. The two remaining products are mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor Q^(-1)f_2S_2 and mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor S_2f_2; their difference is (4). The defect is nonzero at every N>=2 and every nonzero mu. Thus weight zero is insufficient for naturality. If a single-head coupon D is an actual Hopf intertwiner, then commuting with the distinct K eigenvalues and all nonzero consecutive F arrows forces D=cI. Such a coupon can be relocated along that strand with the original normalizations. For a multi-head coupon, block naturality requires its actual tensor-object intertwining equations, and its closing functional is not automatically a scalar one-strand cut. Coupon (1) does not even pass (4). More generally, moving an inserted coupon through a typed crossing R must retain the exact discrepancy Delta_R=R D_in-D_out R. (5) An admissible relative Ward comparison may remove (5) only after exhibiting its actual typed current homotopy and checking its pairing with the full marked co-source. Vanishing of an unmarked scalar or a cyclic matrix trace does not provide that check. The existing [Ward co-source homotopy](ward_cyclic_wall_contraction_and_marked_augmentation.md) makes the issue explicit: if mu-ell=nu F on the relevant fiber, then with an inserted W the omitted term is nu F(AWBp). For original intertwining exteriors and Fp=0, this contains the term nu A[F,W]Bp. Equation (4) supplies the literal current that must be transported here. ## 3. Two ordinary partial traces lose the actual source Retain the original pivot g=x^(1-N)Z^(-1). Both ordinary pivotal partial traces vanish: Tr_2[(1 tensor g)W]=0, Tr_1[(g tensor 1)W]=0. (6) This follows directly from (1): both |d><0| and the cyclic shift S_2 have zero diagonal. Nevertheless mWp=Q^(-1)/N is nonzero. Consequently an ordinary partial trace or an argument dividing by the ordinary quantum dimension cannot give the original marked evaluation. Indeed Tr(g)=0 at the same color. The original modified/relative source is essential, rather than an optional normalization of (6). Modified-trace cyclicity is a statement about its specified categorical morphisms. Extending it to all arbitrary linear coupons while retaining this marked functional would be false, as the next calculation shows. ## 4. An all-level one-crossing identity Define the actual finite Euler value U_Euler,N(1)=sum_(j=0)^d 1/F_j, F_j=(Q;Q)_j. This is the Euler polynomial of the original crossing, not the differently named meridian norm adapter u_N in other notes. Then exactly m W Bp=Q^(-1)/N, m B Wp=Q^(-1)U_Euler,N(1). (7) To prove the second identity note Wp=NQ^(-1)|d,0>. The original crossing coefficient from (d,0) to (h,d-h) is r(d,0,h)=N x^(-d-h)Q^(-h)/F_(d-h). Multiplication by m contributes x^(d-h)/N^2. Since x^(-2)=Q, the product with NQ^(-1) simplifies to Q^(-1)/F_(d-h). Summing h proves (7). The first identity uses the original Bp=p. Thus no published modified-trace proof or unknown scalar is involved. At N=2, Q=-1, x=i, these marked values are mWBp=-1/2, mBWp=-3/2. (8) The full original crossing changes these to -kappa/2 and -3kappa/2, with identical exterior factors. They are still unequal. This is an actual one-crossing source counterexample to bare cyclic relocation. ## 5. A scalar multiplier cannot repair all exteriors Use the actual three-braid figure-eight word T=B_1 B_2^(-1)B_1 B_2^(-1). Keep the global typed wrap marks (1,k,1), rather than resetting them independently at each insertion. Close heads 2 and 3 with the original pivots. The marked first cut uses the full functional N^(-1)sum_(a,b)C_(a,b) in the balanced basis, exactly as in the original Gauss source. For the uninserted scalar cut this is the original invariant. After inserting a nonintertwining coupon it is kept fixed and is not replaced by a highest entry. At N=2 the uninserted cut is 5I. Insert W on heads 1,2 at each of the five displayed word gaps, from left to right. Their original marked values are (-5/2,-3/2,-5/2,5/2,5/2). (9) These are exact complex-root values. The word has writhe zero, so the common scalar crossing factors cancel in the same way in all five expressions. Its original full peripheral normalization is also the same throughout. The gap-0 to gap-1 relocation is through the same local positive crossing as in (8). In (8) its ratio is 3; in (9) its ratio is 3/5. Consequently there is no scalar c_N(M), depending only on that local crossing, the root and peripheral color, that repairs this untransported wall move in every original exterior. A phase or a factor such as 1+M^n cannot fix this environment dependence. A larger current/source state must be retained. ## 6. Consequence for the remaining proof The marked endpoint wall in (3) is controlled by a known nonzero scalar and costs no exponential uncertainty. That result survives. What fails is moving an arbitrary interior wall to that endpoint while keeping its bare formula and then applying (3). A possible valid route is to transport W together with its current (4) and the original co-source homotopy, including all residues and normals. The discrepancy (5) then has a precisely stated relative pairing to check. Neither ordinary trace cyclicity nor a local scalar adjustment supplies that transport. The computations here do not prove that the required completed currents cannot cancel across a full five-point move. They show that such cancellation is a genuine missing theorem. No sharp upper or lower bound relative to a selected geometric period follows from these relocation tests. In particular the exact endpoint polynomial factor does not select a geometric saddle of the interior period. ## 7. Independent exact audit Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_interior_wall_cut_relocation.py The audit uses original E/Cartan crossing coefficients and the original pivots. It checks twelve complete/wrap families for (4), (6), (7), and twelve original figure-eight gap families through N=7 over exact prime fields. A separate exact SymPy calculation at Q=-1,x=i proves (8)--(9), including the uninserted cut 5I. Highest-entry diagnostics are recorded separately and are never used to replace the full marked source after insertion.

title: An original-source zero-side patch across an isolated shape-one divisor
text: # An original-source zero-side patch across an isolated shape-one divisor 28 October 2026. A single transverse A=1 exit of a DIRECT full-Psi factor is locally removable. The actual function is holomorphic on the entire shrinking patch, including all its accumulating zeros. After crossing to its zero side, its outgoing current is the exact sum of TWO regular selected-strip currents. The whole norm factor 1-A^N, its logarithmic mark and every original side current are retained. For a fixed finite patch this costs exp(o(N)). With a normal collar chosen smaller than the background regularity scale, both outgoing phase sectors are downhill. This does not bound the global number of visits, sum an arbitrary set of simultaneous signed collisions, or estimate the remaining original side currents by knot volume. ## 1. Precise local source hypotheses Let u=Log A be a genuine complex normal coordinate to A=1 in the INTEGRATION variables, with u=0 on the divisor. In the actual monomial phase charts this is a fixed real integral linear combination of the log coordinates; complete it by fixed linear coordinates y. The coordinate change has N-independent condition number. A purely external meridian specialization is not an available normal contour direction. The argument A includes every original Q/q/color tag of that full-Psi factor. If its classical signed monomial differs by an O(1/N) logarithmic shift, keep that shift in u exactly. It moves the collision center by O(1/N), which is inside the collar since alpha<1; the uniform estimates are unchanged. In particular its N-th power need not be one for a half-root tag. The exact factor 1-exp(Nu) below retains that character and is not replaced by the untagged 1-A_classical^N. This applies to an actual source chart before singular elimination: use the [atomic-window whole-source resolution](atomic_window_total_source_resolution.md) and keep its finite-window interval sources and original coupled caps. The finite window is an entire polynomial in its argument; its exact interval prefactor Log r/(r-1) has its removable value at r=1. Near a lone atomic t=1, these sources therefore introduce no new normal pole. Their N-dependent exponential monomials stay in G, with interval variables and endpoints fixed by the local normal translation. The remaining rational/head exclusions must still be checked on the chart. This does not assume an eliminated current with an apparent inverse norm is holomorphic term by term. Suppose the original scalar differential form on this chart is omega_N=Psi_epsilon(u) exp(G(u,y)/h) a_N(u,y) du wedge dy, h=2pi i/N, epsilon=+1 or -1, (1) where a_N and the FULL original relative co-source are holomorphic in the normal tube being used. All other actual full-Psi factors, fixed Gaussian/interval phases and N-dependent monomial factors are retained in G and a_N. Their own shape and quantum-pole exclusions remain valid. The unexpanded original ray currents and boundaries remain part of the same relative chain. No bare reciprocal full function or unpaired norm denominator is assumed holomorphic by definition. For the quantitative estimates, assume the other regular factors obey the slowly expanding window bounds with L=N^epsilon_0. In the fixed normal coordinate these imply |partial_u G|<=C_0+C_1 epsilon_0 log N (2) when their logarithmic marks stay bounded. For downhill alone it is enough to impose this bound on |Re partial_u G|: arbitrary retained integer wall marks have purely imaginary normal derivative and do not affect that bound. The rational/half-density amplitude is bounded by a fixed power of N, or more generally by exp(o(N)), on this tube. The tube is ISOLATING: no other dilogarithm shape-one divisor, source pole, cap singularity or quantum pole is crossed. These are substantive local hypotheses. In particular the lemma cannot be applied separately to two current summands whose apparent norm poles only cancel in their sum. One must first use their actual holomorphic aggregate. Set delta=N^(-alpha), with 0<alpha<1. The patch below lies in |Re u|<=delta, -3delta<=epsilon Im u<=delta. By isolation, all other factors remain regular throughout this patch. N is sufficiently large that Ndelta>=2pi and a fixed multiple of delta is small. ## 2. Uniform full-function bound on the ENTIRE collision collar Use the exact quantum shift, with its original logarithmic lift, Psi_epsilon(u+epsilon h_0) =Psi_epsilon(u)/(1-exp u), h_0=2pi i/N. (3) Choose a FIXED integer m=O(Ndelta) large enough that every u in the patch has delta<=epsilon Im(u+epsilon m h_0)<=Cdelta. Iteration gives the literal function identity Psi_epsilon(u) =Psi_epsilon(u+epsilon m h_0) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-exp(u+epsilon j h_0)). (4) The shifted factor is holomorphic and nonzero in its selected strip. Every product factor is entire; its size is at most Cdelta on the patch. Equation (4) proves that Psi itself is holomorphic there and retains the simple zeros u=-epsilon j h_0; no pole or residue is created by crossing them. The argument uses the actual full function, not the norm-one cyclic atom. At the shifted point the shrinking-strip estimate applies. The local dilogarithm expansion Li_2(exp w)=pi^2/6+O(w(1+|Log w|)) gives sup_patch |Psi_epsilon(u)| <=exp[C Ndelta(1+|log delta|)+O(log N)] =exp(o(N)). (5) The constant pi^2/6 contributes unit modulus in the prescribed h_0 phase. This upper bound is uniform through every zero; no lower bound for Psi or its logarithm across those zeros is claimed. The variation of the other leading phase across this normal patch is O(delta log N) by (2). Thus relative to the same tangential base phase at u=0, the entire local integrand changes its exponential scale only by exp(O(Ndelta log N)+o(N)). Fixed-dimensional translations and their sweeps have at most polynomial mass cost. ## 3. Exact outgoing selected-strip sectors Translate the normal variable by H_t(u,y)=(u-2i epsilon delta t,y), 0<=t<=1. (6) For incoming |u|<=delta the output u'=u-2i epsilon delta satisfies -3delta<=epsilon Im u'<=-delta. The exact FULL-turn identity is Psi_epsilon(u') =(1-exp(Nu')) Psi_epsilon(u'+epsilon 2pi i). (7) The shifted factor now lies in its original selected strip with margin at least delta. Hence the outgoing differential form is exactly the sum omega_out,0 = Psi_epsilon(u'+epsilon 2pi i) exp(G(u',y)/h_0) a_N(u',y) du' wedge dy, omega_out,1 = -exp(Nu') omega_out,0. (8) Their leading actions are W_0=epsilon Li_2(exp u')+G(u',y), W_1=W_0+2pi i u'. (9) The dilogarithm and logarithm in W_0 are on the shifted selected strip, not reset to an unrelated principal value. The factor 1-exp(Nu') has NOT been divided out or replaced by a number. It records the entire outgoing zero lattice and the original integer norm/ray mark. There are exactly two currents here, independent of N, with coefficients +1,-1. ## 4. Genuine downhill transport on nested collars The singular leading action is epsilon Li_2(exp u). Along a vertical normal translation its derivative satisfies, on any continued local sheet away from u=0, d/ds Im W(u-i epsilon s,y) =-epsilon Re(partial_u W) =log|1-exp u|-epsilon Re(partial_u G). (10) This real derivative is independent of the logarithm branch. It is locally integrable through u=0 itself. Since |u|<=Cdelta on the patch, (2) gives d/ds Im W <=-(alpha-C_1 epsilon_0)log N+C. (11) Choose C_1 epsilon_0<alpha<1. (12) For large N this is uniformly negative. Thus the normal patch is genuinely downhill, not merely of subexponential amplitude cost. The background exponent epsilon_0 may first be chosen small enough to permit (12). If the SAME exponent is used for both collars and the arbitrary background bound is only O(log N), strict downhill does not follow automatically; the upper bound (5) still does. For incoming points in the selected side, continue its classical action along (6) without silently changing sheets. On Re u'<0 it agrees with W_0 at the outgoing point and W_1 has smaller imaginary part. On Re u'>0 it agrees with W_1 and W_0 has smaller imaginary part. This is the usual local Li_2 monodromy difference 2pi i u'; both continuations agree at u'=0. The statement holds for either epsilon by conjugate reflection. Therefore max(Im W_0,Im W_1) <= Im W_in-c delta log N (13) on a complete translation of length 2delta, under (12), for some fixed c>0. Retained integer logarithmic marks only add a constant 2pi m Re u along each vertical path, so the same downhill conclusion holds with those marks included. The two-sector split does not introduce an uncontrolled leading action. ## 5. The original chain identity, INCLUDING side currents Let Gamma be any fixed finite-dimensional original chain portion in the isolating tube, with its original source and logarithmic marks. Let S=H_*([0,1] times Gamma) and S_side=H_*([0,1] times partial Gamma), with the product orientation. Since partial S=Gamma_out-Gamma-S_side, holomorphy of the FULL differential form in (1) proves exactly integral_Gamma omega_N =integral_(Gamma_out,0) omega_out,0 +integral_(Gamma_out,1) omega_out,1 -integral_(S_side) omega_N. (14) No additional residue is produced at u=0 or at the lower neighboring cyclotomic zeros. The original radial/logarithmic boundaries are carried by the same homotopy or left outside its support; they are not deleted by (14). If the chart has to be split along a logarithmic seam, the two original seam currents are matched using the exact identity (7), rather than assuming the classical Li_2 branch is single valued. The whole norm factor in (7) is retained. The side current in (14) is compulsory. It vanishes for a closed chain piece, cancels on a common face of two pieces using the SAME homotopy, or remains as an explicit original relative boundary term. Normal side faces with |Re u|=delta already lie outside the shape-one divisor and are regular. Boundaries from other coordinates remain their original exit currents; this theorem does not estimate them by knot volume. All finite patch sweeps have exp(o(N)) local cost relative to the retained tangential phase, by (5), (2) and their bounded translation Jacobians. This removes the isolated shape-one divisor as a local analytic barrier and returns its outgoing contribution to REGULAR full-Psi charts with explicit integer sectors. It does not prove a global bound on the number of patches, revisits or accumulated branching. ## 6. Several independent divisors, and the limitation For a fixed number p of INDEPENDENT normal coordinates u_j, direct factors product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(u_j), an isolating polydisc and background satisfying the corresponding bounds, the translations in (6) commute. Their exact outgoing factor is product_j (1-exp(Nu_j')) product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(u_j'+epsilon_j 2pi i). Thus a fixed simultaneous patch has 2^p regular outgoing sectors, with every integer mark retained, and the same exp(o(N)) bound. Under nested collars satisfying (12) in each direction, the actions are downhill coordinate by coordinate. Product-chain side currents are retained by the same Stokes formula. This is a fixed finite independent-normal statement, not a cancellation theorem. Dependent signed normals can prevent a common zero-side translation; oppositely cooriented copies of the same divisor are the simplest example. Balanced collisions, simultaneous source poles, nontransverse normal maps, and arbitrary collision circuits are excluded. No automatic cancellation or sharp whole-knot estimate is inferred there. ## 7. Reproduction and scope of the checks python3 experiments/audit_actual_isolated_shape_one_patch.py The exact finite-product checks are made at Re u<0 so their logs are on the original convergent anchored branches; no floating branch unwrapping is assumed. They compare both signs of (4),(7), retaining the norm factor, through N=256 and both level parities. Separate phase calculations test both outgoing sectors with adverse polynomial background derivatives. The finite audit checks 36 exact normal-chart transitions and 48 signed two-sector downhill checks. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_isolated_shape_one_patch_results.json). The theorem and its uniform estimates follow from the analytic proof above. The checks do not establish a global patch-count bound, a simultaneous dependent-collision theorem or a geometric lower bound.

title: The original clock source under the factorial LENGTH gauge
text: # The original clock source under the factorial LENGTH gauge 29 October 2026. The full original clock co-source has polynomial Riesz norm in the proposed factorial length frame, provided every crossing is first kept as a singleton over-event. Each crossing then supplies a complementary pair of lengths. This is an exact source embedding for arbitrary signed braid width, including the original cut, pivots, clock feedback and external scalar. After an overbridge has been unwound, its factorial Gamma is no longer a harmless phase. In the same length frame its exact norm is a positive angle-simplex partition. The two descriptions are consistent: unwinding has moved a genuine weight from the tensor network into the clock co-source. It must be retained there or assigned back to a specified bulk tensor. This note concerns the LENGTH registers, not a replacement metric on physical heads. It does not establish a positive geometric state or a sharp knot bound. ## 1. The actual singleton presentation Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=-q^-1 and F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, L_a=s_a^2/N, A_a=L_a^(1/8), D_a=A_a^2=s_a^(1/2)/N^(1/4). (1) The exact reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives D_a D_(d-a)=1, D_d=N^(1/4). (2) For a binary block B_l(X,Y;a)=product_(r<l)(X-Q^r aY), use the proposed normalization b_l=B_l/D_l. Its coefficients, phases and spectator dependence are otherwise unchanged. All original LENGTH SLOTS are retained, including l=0: D_0=N^-1/4 and b_0=N^1/4. A raw empty factor B_0=1 can be omitted, but after normalization its scalar must then be recorded. The complementary products below include those zero-length slots. In [the original charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), one may choose EVERY crossing as a singleton over-event: no identity requires compressing a maximal overbridge. For a word with m crossings on b heads there are then m+b anchor events. At crossing j its two binary blocks have lengths (d-h_j,h_j), 0<=h_j<=d. (3) All m clocks are independent. Their feedback into spectator ports is the same exact signed integer map as in the global source theorem; it is not suppressed or untwisted. The m crossing Gamma factors are now just kappa^(sigma_j)(-1)^h_j Q^[sigma_j h_j(h_j+1)/2], of modulus one. Every other factor in W_h is a power of x,Q or an original pivotal phase. Thus |W_h|=1. The original complete dimension/framing line is denoted chi_N and remains outside. Every closure block has length d. Therefore the whole block normalizer is EXACTLY, and independently of every clock, product_edges D_(length)=N^(b/4). (4) There is no factorial action hidden in (4): each pair in (3) cancels by (2). If f_h is the ACTUAL normalized b-network coefficient, the exact scalar is K_N=(chi_N/N) N^(b/4) sum_(h in{0,...,d}^m) W_h f_h. (5) The original cut factor1/N has not been absorbed into an invented boundary normalization. The f_h can be exponentially large and oscillatory. Equation(5) makes no assumption about their size. ## 2. Exact source norm and a real full-source Cauchy inequality Give the clock space C^({0,...,d}^m) its standard orthonormal basis. The Riesz norm of the co-source in (5) is EXACTLY ||ell_N||=|chi_N| N^(b/4+m/2-1). (6) Indeed there are N^m entries, all of the same modulus. This gives the genuine original-source inequality |K_N|^2 <= |chi_N|^2 N^(b/2+m-2) sum_h |f_h|^2. (7) For fixed word and the known complete scalar line, the source factor is polynomial. This is an exact Cauchy--Schwarz theorem, not a proposed positive pivotal trace or a favorable cut. Equivalently, the length-register inclusion |h_1,...,h_m> -> tensor_j |d-h_j,h_j> tensor |d>^(tensor b) (8) is isometric before the diagonal D frame. Applying D on every length leg leaves every clock pair fixed and multiplies the closure legs by N^(b/4), exactly as in (4). Arbitrary diagonal unit-phase clock/flow feedback commutes with this length frame; its actual phases remain in the network. It supplies no additional Riesz cost at the boundary. No relation between a length leg and a physical head index is presumed. There is a slightly cleaner equivalent source. Contract the b original closure blocks by the exact source reproducing law BEFORE taking a norm. Each normalized full block contributes the retained scalar D_d^-1=N^-1/4, canceling (4). The remaining clocks are still independent and the new weights W'_h have modulus one. For a one-component presentation with at least one crossing, the closure edges form the proved forest, so no unexplained full-loop factor is introduced. The resulting literal co-source has K_N=(chi_N/N) sum_h W'_h f'_h, ||ell'_N||=|chi_N|N^(m/2-1). (9) The original pivots survive as their exact root phases in f'_h and W'_h. Equations(6),(9) use their own typed bulk families; one must not keep (6)'s family while deleting its closure scalar. These polynomial SOURCE norms do not estimate the positive energy sum|f_h|^2. In particular they do not identify that energy with the geometric angle partition. A large energy is compatible with an exact Cauchy inequality. Global angle support, edge characters and coherent normalized-block gluing are additional requirements. ## 3. The exact cost after overbridge unwinding An m_e-encounter bridge has r=m_e+1 composition lengths n_0=d-h_1, n_j=h_j-h_(j+1), n_(r-1)=h_(m_e), n_i>=0, sum_i n_i=d. (10) The original Gamma in the bridge theorem satisfies EXACTLY |Gamma_e|=s_(h_1)/(s_(h_m) product_j s_(h_j-h_(j+1))) =N/product_(i=0)^(r-1) s_(n_i). (11) No normalization is chosen by dividing by the knot value. Under the SAME b=B/D convention its transformed co-source coefficient has modulus |Gamma_e product_i D_(n_i)| =N^(1-r/4) product_i s_(n_i)^(-1/2). (12) Thus its exact squared Riesz norm, on the orthonormal composition basis, is N^(2-r/2) Z_(r,N), Z_(r,N)=sum_(n_i>=0,sum n_i=d) product_i s_(n_i)^(-1). (13) For a collection of compressed bridges, after the closure forest has been contracted, independence of their monotone clock domains gives the WHOLE original co-source norm ||ell_comp||^2=|chi_N|^2/N^2 product_e [N^(2-r_e/2) Z_(r_e,N)]. (14) The feedback phases can couple the bulk coefficients but do not change this norm: their moduli are one. Keeping a normalized coefficient family and declaring its Gamma source unit would change the original source. For r=2, reflection gives Z_(2,N)=1 EXACTLY. Consequently (13) is N, agreeing with the singleton source norm in (9). For r>=3, the source weight really can have exponential scale. If Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin u)du, then log Z_(r,N)=N r Lambda(pi/r)/pi+O_r(log N). (15) In particular r=3 is the positive tetrahedral angle energy of rate v_3/pi. This is useful geometric weight, not an unrecorded error or a claim of geometric knot gluing. Proof of(15). The uniform factorial estimate gives log s_a=N J(a/N)+O(logN), with J(t)=-Lambda(pi*t)/pi, including a=0,d. There are polynomially many compositions and changing their total d/N to1 changes the maximum by O(logN/N), using the integrable logarithmic endpoint modulus of continuity. It remains to maximize sum_i Lambda(pi*x_i), x_i>=0,sum x_i=1. For r>=3 a maximum cannot lie on the boundary: adding a small positive coordinate increases the sum by a positive -delta log delta term, except at a pure vertex; there, distributing delta equally among two zero coordinates gives a positive delta log2 term. At an interior maximum no coordinate can be at least1/2: each of the other coordinates is strictly smaller than its complement, so shifting mass to one of them increases the function by the derivative -pi log(2sin(pi*x)). On the remaining region all coordinates are below1/2, where this function is strictly concave. Its unique maximum is therefore the uniform point x_i=1/r. Rounding that point to a composition of d gives the matching lower bound with O(logN) loss. This proves(15). An isometric complementary-pair encoding cannot erase the Riesz norm(13): isometries preserve it. It may instead KEEP the positive simplex weight as a bulk/source tensor. That is exactly the weight(12), and its global geometric incidence must still be proved. The polynomial singleton source and the weighted compressed source are two exact organizations of the SAME state. ## 4. What this settles for the proposed special inner product The original clock source is not an uncontrolled exponential boundary factor in the uncompressed length frame: (6)--(9) give its exact polynomial norm at arbitrary width. The original clocks, phases, closure and full external line are explicit. This does not mean that a contracted normalized b-network scalar has polynomial norm, nor that its anchor coefficient functional has polynomial dual norm in every proposed polynomial metric. For example, with the half-factorial metric ||X^a||^2=s_a, a valence-v anchor's exact dual norm squared is sum_(sum a_i=d, a_i<=l_i) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). Complementary valence2 is tame; higher valency carries another positive simplex weight when its capacity constraints allow it. Those gluing weights must be retained in a global Cauchy/angle calculation. These are typed source and dual norms. They do not replace every trivalent tensor by a positive sum-d vertex with complementary pairings on every edge: a closed such network would require both Vd=Ed and 3V=2E, which are incompatible for d>0,V>0. In the actual binary blocks the two flow powers sum to the BLOCK LENGTH l, not d; the remaining length registers and oriented dual source charges are essential. A geometric edge-incidence theorem cannot be inferred by forgetting those types. No geometric coefficient or lower bound follows from this source norm alone. The useful next question is whether the COMPLETE normalized state energy, with these exact source and gluing weights, has the desired geometric edge support and volume bound. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_length_gauge_clock_source.py): uncompressed original signed source identities, complementary normalization, complete bridge Gamma and Riesz partition formulas.

title: Exact length-normalized stars and their doubled Gram
text: # Exact length-normalized stars and their doubled Gram 29 October 2026. The original charged star admits an exact factorial length normalization which removes its exponential scalar. Its doubled boundary Gram changes by exactly `1/N`. Contiguous parallel fusion then supplies the square root of the positive affine-angle weight. These are source-preserving tensor identities, with all phases retained. The length frame has a polynomial original clock co-source, as proved in [the independent source calculation](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md). This does not estimate the norm of the completely contracted clock state. Indeed [a complete figure-eight sector](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md) shows why a diagonal norm on those clocks is insufficient for the sharp volume comparison. ## 1. The typed length frame Set `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, and F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, L_a=s_a^2/N, A_a=L_a^(1/8), D_a=A_a^2=s_a^(1/2)/N^(1/4). Root complementation gives, exactly, s_a s_(d-a)=N, A_a A_(d-a)=1, D_a D_(d-a)=1. (1) For an actual root interval put B_l(X,Y;a)=product_(r=0)^(l-1)(X-Q^r aY), b_l(X,Y;a)=B_l(X,Y;a)/D_l. (2) The index `l` is an interval LENGTH. Equation (2) is not permission to apply a physical-head diagonal gauge to a fusion-relative index. For a fixed charged graph it is a scalar normalization of each actual polynomial block, so its effect on the full source is unambiguous. In particular `D_0=N^(-1/4)` and `b_0=N^(1/4)`: zero-length slots are retained, or their exact scalar is explicitly compensated. An empty unnormalized block may be omitted; its normalized version is not one. If `P_G` is a graph polynomial, let `D(G)=product_edges D_l`. Then P_G=D(G) P_(b,G). (3) Every original graph prefactor is multiplied by `D(G)` when the blocks are changed to `b`. For varying lengths this is a diagonal change of frame on explicit length registers. Interior inverse changes cancel; the actual source and all its length constraints must be transported. For singleton over-events every crossing has lengths `(d-h,h)`, so its factor in (3) is one. The original closure blocks contribute only `D_d=N^(1/4)` each; their exact source contractions cancel these factors in the closure-contracted presentation. Thus the original singleton clock co-source is polynomial, including its original feedback, pivots, framing and peripheral line. No knot value is used to choose this frame. ## 2. The normalized balanced star, including its full phase Take nonnegative `k_1+k_2+k_3=d`, put `l_i=d-k_i`, and assume `|a_i|=1`. The [proved actual star identity](actual_general_flow_fusion.md#3-balanced-star--triangle-identity) has outer triangle B_(k_3)(X_1,X_2;Q^(k_2+1)a_1/a_2) B_(k_1)(X_2,X_3;Q^(k_3+1)a_2/a_3) B_(k_2)(X_3,X_1;Q^(k_1+1)a_3/a_1). Define `T(k)=k(k-1)/2` and w(k)=1/(s_(k_1)s_(k_2)s_(k_3)), u(k,a)=(-1)^(k_1+k_3) *Q^[T(k_1)+T(k_3)-k_2]*q^(k_1 k_3) *a_1^(k_2)a_2^(k_3)a_3^(k_1). (4) Here `|u|=1`. The sine-binomial identity [l choose r]_Q=q^[r(l-r)] s_l/(s_r s_(l-r)) and (1) give the original star scalar `N w(k) u(k,a)`. Changing all six interval blocks according to (2) therefore gives [Z^d] product_i b_(d-k_i)(X_i,Z;a_i) =N^(-1/2) u(k,a) product_triangle b_k. (5) Indeed the normalizer ratio is product_i D_(k_i)/D_(d-k_i) =product_i D_(k_i)^2 =1/[N^(3/2)w(k)]. (6) This proves (5) at every level, including zero lengths and coincident outer variables. It is a polynomial identity, valid inside ANY polynomial exterior paired by the original socle coefficient. There is no change of selected period and no positive-trace assumption. More generally the normalization `B_l/A_l^theta` changes the scalar to N^(1-3theta/4) w(k)^(1-theta/2) u(k,a). (7) Thus `theta=1` gives `N^(1/4) sqrt(w) u`, while the frame (2), `theta=2`, makes the star scalar polynomial and independent of the angles in modulus. Formula (7) explains precisely where the full binomial is moved; it has not been discarded. Let `v_old,v_new` be the boundary coefficient vectors of (5) in ANY common positive Hermitian boundary metric `H`. Then <v_old,H v_old>=N^(-1)<v_new,H v_new>. (8) The stronger rank-one Gram equality follows as well. The same `H` must be used on the typed outer boundary on both sides; replacing it by unrelated positive metrics would require their actual adapters. ## 3. Parallel fusion produces the positive angle weight For `L+M<=d` the ordered intervals concatenate exactly: B_L(X,Y;a) B_M(X,Y;aQ^L)=B_(L+M)(X,Y;a). In the same frame (2), b_L(a)b_M(aQ^L) =N^(1/4) sqrt(|[L+M choose L]_Q|) b_(L+M)(a) =N^(3/4) sqrt(w_N(L,M,d-L-M)) b_(L+M)(a), (9) where `w_N(a,b,c)=1/(s_a s_b s_c)` and `a+b+c=d`. The local identity `|[a+b choose a]_Q|=N w_N(a,b,c)` is exact. All interval roots and reversal phases remain in their stated places. In particular (9) is a genuine square-root positive-angle amplitude, not an identification of an unnormalized star with its square root. For a full block, `b_d=N^(-1/4)B_d`. Its arbitrary-exterior reproducing contraction therefore has polynomial cost `N^(-1/4)` times the original unit monomial. A saturated full-block loop retains its exact finite geometric sum; short loops are not declared tame. A fixed valid reduction program made from (5), (9), full-block contractions and explicit interval reversals has scalar equal to a power of `N`, a retained unit phase, and the product of the square-root angle weights from its parallel fusions. A tame terminal pairing and a proved geometric incidence certificate would turn such a program into a sharp comparison. Existence of that program and certificate for all original clock graphs, or for a broad knot class, is not proved here. ## 4. A compatible anchor metric and its compulsory dual weight One useful coefficient metric on a single anchor is ||X^a||^2=m_a=s_a/sqrt(N). (10) The coefficient of `X^(L-r)Y^r` in `b_L(X,Y;a)`, for `|a|=1`, has squared norm in the tensor product of (10) N^(-1/2) |[L choose r]_Q| =sqrt(N) w_N(r,L-r,d-L). (11) This follows by multiplying its squared coefficient by `m_r m_(L-r)`; no phase is changed. Its sum over `r` is therefore an actual positive affine-angle partition up to a power of `N`. The trivalent anchor co-source `lambda_d(X^aY^bZ^c)=delta_(a+b+c,d)` has squared dual coefficient weight 1/(m_a m_b m_c)=N^(3/2)w_N(a,b,c), a+b+c=d. (12) Equations (11)--(12) must both be retained. Merely using (11) and declaring the anchor contraction a unit functional loses its dual angle weight. The metric `m_a=s_a` instead changes only the displayed powers of `N`. It does not remove the exponential weight. These exact local Gram identities provide a concrete special inner product for the user's Cauchy proposal. The remaining requirement is a coherent GLOBAL estimate of the normalized network energy with its actual dual contractions. The complete clock-sector example linked above rules out obtaining that estimate from a diagonal clock norm alone; it does not rule out a non-diagonal Gram retaining cancellation. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_length_normalized_star_gram.py): full normalized polynomial stars and phases, parallel fusion, and both coefficient/dual angle-weight identities.

title: Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing
text: # Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing 28 October 2026. This gives a local marked-action upper bound for a holomorphic recurrence at a modulus crossing where its eigenvalues are DISTINCT and nonzero. The proof constructs an exponentially accurate diagonal form by elementary matrix identities and Cauchy estimates. It needs no exact solution, source overlap, formal WKB summation theorem or pointwise dominance assumption. The sufficient condition compares a COMPUTABLE analytic remainder barrier with the width of the marked classical actions. It always holds on a sufficiently short regular crossing window. Extending it over a whole knot orbit still requires a global action-barrier comparison; mere single-valued calibration of an action does not prove that. Actual real ramification and singular leading coefficients are outside this local theorem. ## 1. Explicit analytic data Write epsilon=1/N and x_(j+1)=x_j+epsilon on a fixed real interval I. Let U_R denote its complex stadium of radius R. Suppose T_N and T_0 are holomorphic on U_(2R), uniformly bounded, and ||T_N-T_0||_(U_(2R))<=C_0 epsilon. (1) Assume T_0 has a supplied holomorphic eigenbasis V_0 there: V_0^(-1)T_0V_0=D_0=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_d), ||V_0||,||V_0^(-1)||<=K, |lambda_i|>=m>0, |lambda_i-lambda_k|>=delta>0. (2) These are bounds on specified coefficient functions. For a classical companion, V_0 has columns (1,lambda_i,...,lambda_i^(d-1))^t, so all data are directly checkable on its normalized spectral branches. An actual recurrence as in [the whole-source spectral theorem](actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md) satisfies (1) on any such regular fixed domain, uniformly on its small complex-q source circle. An unverified classical polynomial alone does not supply that actual quantum premise. After the exact change by V_0, put B_N(z)=V_0(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_0(z). Cauchy's estimate gives B_N=D_0+O(epsilon) on U_R. Initially set D=diag B_N, R_N=B_N-D. The diagonal gap is at least 3delta/4 for large N and ||R_N||<=C epsilon. All constants below are uniform. ## 2. Exponentially accurate diagonalization, with its proof There are explicitly bounded constants sigma>0,C and holomorphic V_N,D_N,R_N on U_(R/2), with D_N diagonal, such that EXACTLY V_N(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_N(z)=D_N(z)+R_N(z), ||V_N-V_0||+||V_N^(-1)-V_0^(-1)||<=C epsilon, ||D_N-D_0||<=C epsilon, ||R_N||<=C exp(-sigma N). (3) The shifted identity is asserted where both z and z+epsilon belong to that neighborhood; this includes every real step across I. The one-dimensional case has no off-diagonal part and is immediate. Here is a constructive proof with quantitative constants. Maintain ||D||<=M and diagonal gap g=delta/2; take M larger than twice the initial diagonal bound. If R is off diagonal with norm eta, solve [D,X]=-R, diag X=0, X_(ik)=-R_(ik)/(D_(ii)-D_(kk)), ||X||<=a eta, a=d/g. On a stadium narrowed by Delta>=2epsilon, Cauchy gives ||X(z+epsilon)-X(z)||<=2a eta epsilon/Delta. With X^+=X(z+epsilon), (I+X^+)^(-1)(D+R)(I+X)=D+F, F=(I+X^+)^(-1)[(X-X^+)D+R X]. (4) This is an exact identity. If a eta<=1/2, its new off-diagonal norm is bounded by eta_new <=[8Ma epsilon/Delta+4a eta] eta. (5) Its diagonal change is O(eta^2). To see the latter without losing a derivative, (X-X^+)D is off diagonal. Its contribution to diag F therefore requires the extra factor (I+X^+)^(-1)-I=O(eta). The other term RX already has size O(eta^2). Choose a fixed c<=min(R/8,R/(128Ma)), p=floor(cN), Delta=R/(2p). For sufficiently large N the starting eta is at most 1/(32a). Equation (5) then decreases eta at least by a factor 1/2 at EVERY step. The accumulated diagonal change is O(sum eta^2)=O(epsilon^2), so the stated bound M and gap g persist. The p domain losses total R/2 and Delta>=4epsilon, so all exact shifts are legitimate. The basis is the product of I+X at each step. Since sum ||X||<=2a eta_0=O(epsilon), it and its inverse are I+O(epsilon). The final off-diagonal is O(epsilon*2^(-p)). For example one may use sigma=(c log 2)/2. (6) All bounds are derived from (1)--(2), not an unknown solution. They are conservative, not optimal conversion exponents. The same construction is holomorphic in additional parameters wherever those uniform premises hold, including the actual tiny complex-q circle. ## 3. A checkable action-width criterion Normalize the real marked actions at the left endpoint a of I: A_i(x)=integral_a^x log|lambda_i(t)| dt, W=max_(x in I)[max_i A_i(x)-min_i A_i(x)]. (7) Suppose W<sigma. Then the EXACT product P_N of T_N across I satisfies limsup (1/N)log||P_N||<=max_i A_i(b), (8) where b is its right endpoint. Every specified input and output with subexponential norms has the same upper bound. This is a product bound, not merely a prediction from formal critical points. Proof. Let d_(i,j) be the diagonal entries of the actual D_N(x_j), and put G_0=I, G_(j+1)=D_N(x_j)G_j, all diagonal. Uniformly in j, log |(G_j)_(ii)|=N A_i(x_j)+O(1), (9) by (3), nonvanishing in (2), and the ordinary uniform Riemann estimate. The remaining EXACT recurrence after G_j has factors I+E_j, E_j=G_(j+1)^(-1)R_N(x_j)G_j. Equations (3), (7), and (9) give ||E_j||<=C exp[-N(sigma-W)]. There are O(N) steps, so their product is I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)]). Consequently P_N=V_N(b) G_n [I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)])] V_N(a)^(-1). This proves (8) and gives an exponentially small relative matrix remainder after the explicitly marked diagonal propagation. The exponential anisotropy of G_j is RETAINED and estimated by W; it is not asserted to be a tame positive full-space metric. In fact the same proof pins down the WHOLE singular-value vector. Let A_(1)(b)>=...>=A_(d)(b) be the sorted endpoint actions. Under the stated barrier, bounded invertible endpoint frames and the I+o(1) middle factor give, for every k, log sigma_k(P_N)=N A_(k)(b)+O(1). (9a) Use the elementary singular-value inequalities for multiplication by a bounded invertible matrix on both sides of the diagonal G_n. Thus all partial sums satisfy the corresponding asymptotic log-majorization, and every fixed continuous convex function of the normalized log singular values has the endpoint-action limit. This conditional pinching is stronger than a convexity estimate. It does not make the barrier follow from Karamata, and does not prove a nonzero overlap for the selected scalar source. For finite N there is a more flexible certificate: construct (3) and the diagonal G_j, compute bounds e_j>=||G_(j+1)^(-1)R_NG_j||, and use ||P_N||<=||V_N(b)|| ||V_N(a)^(-1)|| max_i |(G_n)_(ii)| product_j(1+e_j). (10) Proving sum_j e_j=o(N) suffices. These quantities use only the explicitly constructed local diagonalizers and scalar diagonal products, not the unknown exact vector solution or its final scalar. ## 4. A distinct-root modulus crossing is locally harmless For two branches suppose |lambda_1(x_*)|=|lambda_2(x_*)|, while the eigenvalues themselves stay separated as in (2). On I=[x_*-ell,x_*+ell], let |d/dx log|lambda_1/lambda_2||<=L. Then |A_1(x)-A_2(x)|<=L ell^2 throughout I. Thus L ell^2<sigma is a sufficient condition for (8), even if the larger modulus switches at x_*. The bound applies also to distinct REAL roots of opposite sign. No positive real weights are introduced. The analytic data may be fixed on a neighborhood of x_* first; sigma is then independent of the shortened ell. Hence a sufficiently short crossing window always meets this condition. For more than two regular branches use W<=2ell max_(i,k) sup_I|log|lambda_i/lambda_k||. All quantities are checkable from a specified classical curve and actual analytic recurrence. For a simple root of F(x,L), partial_x Log lambda=-F_x/(lambda F_L), which bounds L. A calibrated Bloch/peripheral action may supply the A_i, but (7) still requires the explicit quantitative width comparison. This does not contradict the [Gaussian conversion example](analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md). On its whole interval the conversion has positive gain even though the complete branch actions vanish. Its global width cannot satisfy the sufficient barrier comparison. On a sufficiently short regular window the theorem gives precisely the local estimate (8). An exponentially small local conversion can still grow after a long external propagation; it cannot be discarded in later gluing. ### A verified action-coordinate radius can replace the Euclidean one The proof also works in a supplied univalent holomorphic coordinate w=zeta(z). Assume the transformed matrices and basis obey (1)--(2) on an action-plane neighborhood of radius R_w, and the EXACT shifted coordinate map f_epsilon(w)=zeta(zeta^(-1)(w)+epsilon) is holomorphic there with |f_epsilon(w)-w|<=V epsilon. In (4) set X^+=X(f_epsilon(w)). Cauchy's estimate changes (5) only by replacing epsilon/Delta with V epsilon/Delta. Hence one may use c<=min(R_w/(8V),R_w/(128MaV)), sigma=c log2/2. (11) The actual sampled recurrence and the real actions (7) are unchanged; no continuum substitution for a discrete step is made. This follows from a verified analytic coordinate and shift map, not a formal replacement of the independent variable. At a distinct-root crossing, an appropriately marked zeta(z)=integral Log(lambda_i/lambda_k) dz has nonzero derivative unless that MARKED logarithm vanishes. It is therefore a valid local coordinate on a sufficiently small domain. Its analytic inverse may be bounded by excluding its actual action-plane critical values and singularities. This gives a CHECKABLE action-domain version of the remainder barrier. It does not identify the optimal barrier with the nearest calibrated collision action, or show that a zero regulator jump implies the global width inequality. Those stronger connection statements are still unproved. ## 5. What finite gluing additionally requires On overlapping regular domains with the SAME marked V_0 and the same iteration (4), two truncation depths give compatible frames: their ratio is I+O(exp[-min(sigma_1,sigma_2)N]) on a smaller overlap. Indeed their factors are literally the same up to the smaller depth; every additional X is already exponentially small there. An action-coordinate refinement controlling that connection, rather than the conservative Euclidean sigma, remains necessary for the proposed general endpoint theorem. Thus the proved local result is (3)--(8), including regular modulus crossings and an explicit analytic barrier.
