For the equal-color object with parameter \(s\), the actual checked crossing has scalar and stripped eigenvalues \[ \kappa_s=q^{(d+s)^2/2},\qquad \lambda_r=(-1)^r q^{r(r+1)}q^{-2sr}, \qquad 0\le r<N. \tag{4} \] These are the physical crossing and its retained Cartan scalar. Define \[ a_s=\frac d2+s,\qquad \tau_r(s)=\frac{2\pi}{N}(a_s-r),\qquad z_r=-2\cos\tau_r(s). \tag{5} \] Then \(e^{iN\tau_r}=\eta e^{2\pi is}\), and the \(z_r\) are the roots of \(P_s\), with multiplicity at collisions. For the prescribed logarithmic lift, \[ r^2+(N+1-2s)r=(r-a_s)^2-a_s^2+2Nr. \tag{6} \] The last summand contributes \(e^{2\pi ir}=1\). Therefore \[ \lambda_r=q^{-a_s^2} \exp\!\left(\frac{iN\tau_r(s)^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{7} \] Multiplication by the physical scalar in (4) gives the exact formula \[ \boxed{\displaystyle (\kappa_s\lambda_r)^\epsilon =C_{N,\epsilon}(s) \exp\!\left(\frac{i\epsilon N\tau_r(s)^2}{4\pi}\right), \quad C_{N,\epsilon}(s)=q^{\epsilon(d^2/4-s^2/2)},} \tag{8} \] for \(\epsilon=0,\pm1\). In particular, no factor of modulus \(e^{cN}\) has been suppressed. The complete factor \(q^{\epsilon d^2/4}\) has modulus one, and \(C_{N,\epsilon}(s)\) and its inverse are uniformly bounded on every fixed \(s\)-disk. The crossing operator is denoted by \(R_s\) below; the unsubscripted real number \(R\) is the radius of the parameter disk. The opposite equal-color orientation uses \(-s\); (8)'s scalar is even in \(s\). The two mixed reference orders use the full complete crossing polynomial \(r_0\), with the already specified bounded monodromy scalar on reversal. They are addressed by the constant-relation version at the end. ## 2. A paired-grid integral with no meridian denominator Fix \(0\le R<1/2\) and \(y>0\). Let \(\mathcal R_y\) be the positively oriented rectangle with real sides at \(-\pi,\pi\) and imaginary sides at \(-y,y\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), both grids \(\tau_r(s)\), \(\tau_r(-s)\), \(0\le r<N\), lie inside it uniformly on \(|s|\le R\). Their real endpoints stay strictly between \(-\pi\) and \(\pi\), since \[ |\operatorname{Re}\tau_r(\pm s)| \le\pi-\frac{\pi(1-2R)}{N}. \tag{9} \] Their imaginary parts are at most \(2\pi R/N<y\). Let \(E_{N,s}\) be any raw polynomial, and put \[ B_{N,s,j}(\tau) =\sin(j\tau) \exp\!\left(\frac{i\epsilon N\tau^2}{4\pi}\right) E_{N,s}(-2\cos\tau). \tag{10} \] This function is odd in \(\tau\), even when its coefficients and \(s\) are complex. The exact contour identity is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \phi_s(R_s^\epsilon L_jE_{N,s}) =-\frac{N^2 C_{N,\epsilon}(s)}{2\pi i} \int_{\partial\mathcal R_y} B_{N,s,j}(\tau)\, \frac{e^{iN\tau}} {(e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{2\pi is}) (e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{-2\pi is})}\,d\tau .} \tag{11} \] Here \(R_s^\epsilon\) means the actual full crossing polynomial, including the scalar of (4), raised to the indicated fixed power and interpreted in the original quotient. The product with \(E\) need not be reduced before using (11). We prove the identity initially at generic \(s\). For \(u=e^{i\tau}\), the derivative at a root is \[ P_s'(-u-u^{-1}) =\frac{2iN\sin2\pi s}{u-u^{-1}} =\frac{N\sin2\pi s}{\sin\tau}. \tag{12} \] Lagrange interpolation, (3), and (8) thus give \[ \phi_s(R_s^\epsilon L_jE) =\frac{\eta N C_{N,\epsilon}(s)}{\sin2\pi s} \sum_{r=0}^{N-1}B_{N,s,j}(\tau_r(s)). \tag{13} \] Introduce logarithmic-derivative kernels \[ K_{\pm s}(\tau)= \frac{iN e^{iN\tau}}{e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{\pm2\pi is}}. \tag{14} \] Each has residue one at its grid. Since \(\tau_{d-r}(-s)=-\tau_r(s)\), oddness of \(B\) implies \[ \sum_r B(\tau_r(s)) =\frac1{4\pi i} \int_{\partial\mathcal R_y}B(\tau) (K_s(\tau)-K_{-s}(\tau))\,d\tau. \tag{15} \] The difference is exactly \[ K_s-K_{-s} =-2\eta N\sin2\pi s\, \frac{e^{iN\tau}} {(e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{2\pi is}) (e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{-2\pi is})}. \tag{16} \] Substitution in (13) proves (11), including its sign and its power \(N^2\). There is no division by \(\sin2\pi s\) left in (11). No pole lies on its contour boundary for \(|s|\le R\), once \(N\) is sufficiently large as in (9). Thus its right side is holomorphic through \(s=0\). The actual crossing polynomial has its established removable complete collision, including the full first normal coefficients. Analytic continuation proves (11) at completeness as well. It does not replace the full Hermite trace by values at a repeated root. ## 3. Uniform estimates for the contour kernel Write \[ \mathcal K_{N,s}(\tau)= \frac{e^{iN\tau}} {(e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{2\pi is}) (e^{iN\tau}-\eta e^{-2\pi is})}. \tag{17} \] On either horizontal side, with \(\tau=t\pm iy\), the two root constants have moduli in \([e^{-2\pi R},e^{2\pi R}]\), while \(|e^{iN\tau}|=e^{\mp Ny}\). For sufficiently large \(N\), \[ |\mathcal K_{N,s}(t\pm iy)|\le C_R e^{-Ny}. \tag{18} \] On a vertical side \(\tau=\pm\pi+iv\), the exponential is \(e^{iN\tau}=-\eta e^{-Nv}\). Put \(t=e^{-Nv}>0\). For \(|\arg(e^{\pm2\pi is})|\le2\pi R<\pi\), \[ |t+e^{\pm2\pi is}| \ge \cos(\pi R)\bigl(t+|e^{\pm2\pi is}|\bigr) \ge c_R(t+1). \tag{19} \] It follows that \[ |\mathcal K_{N,s}(\pm\pi+iv)| \le C_R\frac{t}{(1+t)^2} \le C_Re^{-N|v|}. \tag{20} \] This bound includes \(v=0\); no unproved separation of individual roots is required there. The hypothesis \(R<1/2\) is used both in (9) and (19). ## 4. A strict far-color loss Assume the raw remaining source has the fresh Gaussian bound \[ |E_{N,s}(-2\cos(t+iv))| \le N^K \exp N\{F-c t^2+C v^2+\epsilon_N\}, \quad |t|\le\pi,\ |v|\le y_0,\ |s|\le R, \tag{21} \] where \(c>0\), \(C\ge0\), \(\epsilon_N\to0\), and all constants are uniform over the other physical auxiliary colors. A product of a fixed number of canonical outputs with their respective fresh Gaussians satisfies (21) at the sum of their assigned actions; no prior quotient reduction is needed. The root crossing's Gaussian phase obeys \[ \left|\exp\!\left(\frac{i\epsilon N(t+iv)^2}{4\pi}\right)\right| =\exp\!\left(-\frac{\epsilon Ntv}{2\pi}\right) \le\exp\!\left(\frac{N|t v|}{2\pi}\right), \tag{22} \] and \(|\sin(j(t+iv))|\le e^{j|v|}\). Fix \(0<\delta<1\) and suppose \[ 1\le j\le(1-\delta)N. \tag{23} \] On the horizontal sides of the rectangle, (18), (21), and (22) give exponent at most \[ F+\epsilon_N-c t^2+ \frac{|t|y}{2\pi}+Cy^2-\delta y. \tag{24} \] Completing the square yields \[ -ct^2+\frac{|t|y}{2\pi}\le\frac{y^2}{16\pi^2c}. \tag{25} \] Set \(C_*=C+(16\pi^2c)^{-1}\), and choose a fixed positive \[ y\le y_0,\qquad C_*y^2\le\frac{\delta y}{2}. \tag{26} \] The horizontal exponent is then at most \(F-\delta y/2+\epsilon_N\). On the vertical sides \(t=\pm\pi\), (20)--(23) give exponent at most \[ F-c\pi^2+C v^2+\frac{|v|}{2} -\delta|v|+\epsilon_N \le F-c\pi^2+Cy^2+\frac y2+\epsilon_N. \tag{27} \] Shrink \(y\) further so that \[ Cy^2+\frac y2\le\frac{c\pi^2}{2}. \tag{28} \] This is compatible with (26), since \(y\) is free to be any sufficiently small fixed number. The vertical exponent is then at most \(F-c\pi^2/2+\epsilon_N\). The contour has bounded length. Its prefactor in (11), the source prefactor in (21), and the bounded scalar in (8) have only polynomial cost. Thus there is \(\gamma>0\), depending on the fixed source parameters, \(R\), and \(\delta\), such that \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \sup_{\substack{|s|\le R\\1\le j\le(1-\delta)N}} |\phi_s(R_s^\epsilon L_jE_{N,s})| \le\exp N(F-\gamma), \qquad \epsilon=0,\pm1,} \tag{29} \] for every sufficiently large \(N\), at both parities. The same proof applies to the opposite-color root relation \(P_0\): use \(\sigma=0\) in the kernel and the complete crossing chirp, retaining the bounded mixed-order monodromy scalar. The actual typed turn ratios used to expose the root are bounded as well. The single primitive main-cut factor \(H_N(s)\) does not change the loss on the disk under consideration. ## 5. Exposing each original circle ### 5.1. The source information used Fix a strict literal Conway source whose reduced tree has no adjacent bare hubs. A flagged hub has exactly one original flagged leaf; a bare hub has none. The construction, all its ordered maps, its \(m\) labeled original circles, and its retained half-twist pattern \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) are fixed. Let \(F_0\) be its original complete action. Here \(L\) denotes a branch with a rigid boundary profile \(g+c\), and \(A\) denotes a completed product branch with its own optimized boundary profile. These are branch types, distinct from the ordinary character \(L_j\). The profiles and their intrinsic pressures are normalized by \[ g(a)=\int_0^{2a}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt -4\int_0^a\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad G_0=g(1/4),\qquad \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le a\le1/2}\{g(a)+f_Q(a)\}. \tag{R0} \] The function \(f_Q(a)\) is the exponential rate of the original positive coefficient at fixed output label \(a\), after optimizing that branch's internal labels. If \(f_B\) is this function for the unturned product of \(B\) ordinary leaves, write \(\widehat\omega_B=\max_{0\le a\le1/2}\{g(a)+f_B(1-a)\}\). Every additive constant \(c\) retains the internal action of its branch. We use the following two proved source bounds, including their fresh Gaussian conclusions: - an ordinary or decorated outgoing \(L\)-module has its original spectral pressure \(\Omega_L=2G_0+c_L\) and a fresh Gaussian at that pressure; - an outgoing bare-hub \(A\)-module with \(B\ge2\) incoming \(L\)-cones has original pressure \(\Omega_Q=\widehat\omega_B+\sum c_b\) and a fresh Gaussian there. These are Sections 1 and 3 of the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md). In the second statement the Gaussian follows from the original clean low-coordinate profile and the strictly smaller spectral remainder, not merely from a norm estimate. The resulting assertion is: for every fixed \(0\le R<1/2\) and \(0<\delta<1\), there is \(\gamma>0\) such that \[ \sup_{\substack{|s|\le R,\ 1\le j_i\le N\\ \text{some }j_i\le(1-\delta)N}} |\mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(q^s)| \le \exp N(F_0-\gamma) \tag{R1} \] for every sufficiently large \(N\), at both parities. The scalar is the actual reduced auxiliary-colored source, with the prescribed main cut and framing. The argument does not sum auxiliary filling colors. The contour estimate is proved in Sections 1–4 above. The [original intrinsic-pressure identities](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md) and [source recursion](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) fix its absolute action. No additional geometric comparison is assumed. ### 5.2. The actual closing adjunction In fixed canonical Newton coordinates, the pairing for either actual quotient is \[ \langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f_n g_{N-1-n}. \tag{R2} \] Every prescribed typed turn is \[ \begin{gathered} H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_n(s)=\prod_{r=1}^n \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right),\\ T_\gamma=\frac{\gamma_N(s)}{H_N(s)} \mathbf J\operatorname{diag}(W_n(s)), \qquad \mathbf J_{ij}=\mathbf1_{i+j=N-1}. \end{gathered} \tag{R3} \] The removable value \(H_N(0)\) is one, and the prescribed turn scalar \(\gamma_N(s)\) is \(1\) or \(q^{\pm s^2/2}\), according to its actual domain and codomain. Consequently \[ \langle T_{\gamma_1}f,g\rangle =\frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2} \langle f,T_{\gamma_2}g\rangle. \tag{R4} \] Both sides are \(\gamma_1H_N^{-1}\sum W_nf_ng_n\). The scalar ratio records the two actual object types. Coherent carriers cancel in the composed pairing; the primitive top moment is the same for either orientation. This is an identity of the original full typed tensor contraction, including the first normal coordinates. Changing the direction of a finite tree's recursive evaluation uses (R4), associativity within compatible objects, and the exact consecutive-turn identities. It multiplies the scalar only by the recorded bounded phase \(\chi_{i,N}(s)\), which is a fixed product of powers of \(q^{s^2/2}\). The original root crossing and circle pivot stay in their coupons. There is no assertion of an isotopy or of a scalar factorization of an effective branch. ### 5.3. The three possible positions Choose an original circle \(i\), and orient all subtree evaluations toward its incident hub. Each child subtree remains in the separated-bare-hub class. The same induction supplies its original intrinsic pressure and fresh Gaussian. #### A flagged leaf If \(i\) is the marked leaf of a flagged hub, expose its original coupon \(p_i=R_s^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i}\). Let \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\) be the other incident outgoing modules, each of type \(L\) or \(A\). The normalized closing scalar is \[ Z_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(s) =\chi_{i,N}(s)\, \phi_\sigma\!\left(R_s^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i} E_i\right), \qquad E_i=\prod_{a=1}^k Q_a, \tag{R5} \] where the product defining \(E_i\) is retained as a raw polynomial. Each factor is canonical and has its fresh Gaussian at \(\Omega_{Q_a}\). Their product therefore has a fresh Gaussian at \(\sum_a\Omega_{Q_a}=F_0\), by the original flagged-root action identity. #### An ordinary leaf at a flagged junction Now \(h_i=T_{\gamma_1}(p_i)\) is ordinary at its hub. That hub has a different marked original coupon \(p_v\), and its remaining branches are \(Q_a\) of type \(L\) or \(A\). Before the closing adjunction the scalar is the pairing of \(T_{\gamma_1}p_i\) with \(p_v\prod_aQ_a\). Transfer the closing turn by (R4). The remaining canonical polynomial is \[ E_i=T_{\gamma_2}\!\left(p_v\prod_aQ_a\right). \tag{R6} \] This is exactly a decorated \(L\)-module, so it has a fresh Gaussian at \[ \Omega_{E_i}=2G_0+\sum_a\Omega_{Q_a}. \tag{R7} \] This rate is the original \(F_0\): using \(v\) as the earlier flagged root gives the same sum, with the selected ordinary leaf contributing its intrinsic pressure \(2G_0\). The scalar again has the form (R5), with its actual phase ratio included in \(\chi_{i,N}\). #### An ordinary leaf at a bare junction The selected leaf \(h_i=T_{\gamma_1}p_i\) occupies one incidence of the bare hub. Every other child branch is type \(L\), because adjacent bare hubs are forbidden. There are \(B=d_v-1\ge2\) such branches. Transferring the selected leaf's turn gives \[ E_i=T_{\gamma_2}\!\left(\prod_{a=1}^B L_a\right). \tag{R8} \] This is exactly the whole bare-hub output. It has a fresh Gaussian at \[ \Omega_{E_i}=\widehat\omega_B+\sum_ac_a. \tag{R9} \] The closure with the selected existing ordinary leaf is precisely its defining intrinsic probe, so (R9) equals the original \(F_0\). That leaf was already in the source; it has not been added as a new crossing circle. Equation (R5) again holds with the prescribed typed adjunction scalar. These alternatives exhaust every original leaf when a hub exists. In the strict two-leaf case, exposing either original coupon leaves the other decorated leaf, with Gaussian budget \(2G_0=F_0\), and the same closing adjunction supplies (R5). ### 5.4. The color gap and the main cut For each fixed \(i\), the polynomial \(E_i\) in (R5), (R6), or (R8) is independent of \(j_i\). Its Gaussian constants and error are uniform over the other original physical colors. It is either one canonical outgoing polynomial or a product of a fixed number of canonical outgoing polynomials. Its degree is therefore \(O(N)\), though the half-twist contour estimate needs only its polynomial analyticity and Gaussian bound. In every case its bound has the form \[ |E_i(-2\cos(t+iv))| \le N^{K_i} \exp N\{F_0-c_i t^2+C_i v^2+o(1)\}, \quad |t|\le\pi,\quad |v|\le y_i, \tag{R10} \] with \(c_i>0\). The contour estimate (29) applied to (R5) gives a strict loss \(\gamma_i>0\) whenever \(j_i\le(1-\delta)N\). It covers both signs \(\epsilon_i=\pm1\) and the pure case \(\epsilon_i=0\), and also the constant opposite-color relation with its known monodromy scalar. The original reduced cut is \[ \mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(q^s) =H_N(s)\,Z_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(s). \tag{R11} \] There is still only one such boundary factor. It and every \(\chi_{i,N}\) are bounded on the fixed disk and do not change the strict rate. The finite number of original leaves permits \(\gamma\) in (R1) to be chosen smaller than every \(\gamma_i\), while absorbing all uniform \(o(1)\) errors and polynomial factors. This proves (R1). Under the original strict marked geometry, \(2\pi F_0=\operatorname{Vol}(Y^\epsilon)\). This identifies the action appearing in (R1); it is not a comparison with a newly assembled probe link. ### 5.5. Scope The estimate is for the auxiliary-colored source before the filling transform, and its reference rate is the augmented complete action. It does not prove the filled knot's lower volume rate or the convergence of the normalized regular main-meridian profile. The radius is fixed below \(1/2\), as required by the chosen unwrapped crossing-root contour. Adjacent bare hubs remain outside this source induction. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md), Sections 6–8, supplies the same norm and angular interfaces for arbitrary adjacent bare junctions. The earlier [component extension](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md) remains a special case. The separate [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) proves the uniform filled-knot volume limit on \(|s|\le R<1\) by a joint crossing-power calculation. The smaller radius here belongs to this auxiliary-color estimate and is not the radius of that filled theorem. ## 6. Finite reproduction The [reproduction script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_auxiliary_color_gap.py) constructs the actual canonical crossing from its physical eigenvalues at generic parameters and from its full complete Newton polynomial at \(s=0\). It constructs the inverse crossing in the quotient, keeps the circle pivot, performs ordinary polynomial multiplication and division, and compares the resulting top-coefficient trace with the rectangle integral (11). The [recorded results](../experiments/main_meridian_auxiliary_color_gap_results.json) contain 24 contour comparisons at levels 2 and 3, with all three half-twist choices, the complete parameter and a complex parameter, and deficient and complete auxiliary colors. At 60-digit working precision the largest scaled discrepancy is less than \(3.2\times10^{-43}\). The complete parameter uses the full Hermite specialization. These finite checks test the exact identities and their normalization. The uniform color loss follows from the contour bounds and the source Gaussian proved above.

title: Adjacent product junctions in the main-meridian source bound
text: # Adjacent product junctions in the main-meridian source bound This special-case argument is retained in full. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) and [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) now permit every fixed strict bare component, without an additional valence or path condition. 1 November 2026. The [main-meridian source bound](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) allows a product junction with no crossing-circle operator only when the neighboring product junctions carry such operators. This note gives a sufficient condition that permits several junctions without an operator to be adjacent. The condition counts the branches attached to each connected group of these junctions. More attached branches provide a quantitative margin that controls the error introduced by the next turn. The comparison uses the positive complete-color calculation for the same tangle construction. Every boundary variable remains constrained by its original product and closing equations. In particular, the proof retains the additive constants in the boundary profiles; independently optimized pieces are not assigned a common boundary value after the fact. The result applies to a fixed finite tree. It includes a bound on the summed contribution of high Newton indices, which is needed when the crossing-circle operators are replaced by fixed crossing powers. That bound remains a comparison with the augmented action. A theorem for the smaller filled-knot exponent requires the additional contour and stationary-phase analysis of the filled source. ## 1. The tree and the sufficient condition Start with a strict ordered Conway construction in the sense of the [general strict-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md), Sections 1–3. Its leaves represent the prescribed rational pieces. Before auxiliary filling, the corresponding local operators are \[ p_i=R_s^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i},\qquad h_i=T_s(p_i), \qquad \epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\},\quad 1\le j_i\le N. \tag{1} \] Here \(R_s\) is the physical crossing operator, \(L_{j_i}\) is the ordinary operator associated with crossing circle \(i\), and \(T_s\) is the physical quarter-turn. The parameter \(s\) changes the main meridian to \(M=q^s\), where \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\). Each operation uses its specified orientation and polynomial coordinates. Group consecutive products that have no intervening turn into a single product junction. The resulting [reduced source tree](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md) has a quarter-turn on every edge joining two junctions. A junction is **bare** if it contains no unturned operator \(p_i\). It is **flagged** if it contains one. Strictness permits at most one such operator at a junction. An ordinary external leaf remains a turned operator \(h_i\). Junctions have valence at least three; the two-leaf construction is a separate case already included in the source-bound theorem. Let \(\mathcal U\) be a maximal connected component of bare junctions. If \(D_v\) is the full valence of a vertex \(v\), define \[ b_v=D_v-\deg_{\mathcal U}(v). \tag{2} \] Thus \(b_v\) counts the incidences that leave this component at \(v\): ordinary external leaves and edges to flagged junctions. It does not count the edges joining bare vertices inside \(\mathcal U\). The constants in the criterion come from the sine-factorial action \[ J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad g(u)=J(2u)-4J(u),\qquad G_0=g(1/4)=\frac{2G}{\pi}, \tag{3} \] where \(G=\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r/(2r+1)^2\) is Catalan's constant. For \(k\ge4\), put \[ \varepsilon_k=(k+1)\left[ J\left(\frac14+\frac1{k+1}\right) +J\left(\frac14-\frac1{k+1}\right)-2J(1/4)\right]. \tag{4} \] **Component criterion.** Each maximal bare component must satisfy one of the following alternatives: - It consists of one junction, of arbitrary fixed valence at least three. - Every \(b_v\ge5\), and \[ \eta_{\mathcal U}:=2G_0- \max_{\mathcal P\text{ a simple path in }\mathcal U} \sum_{v\in\mathcal P}\varepsilon_{b_v-1}>0. \tag{5} \] Paths consisting of one vertex are included. Condition (5) is independent of the choice of root used to evaluate the tree. A simpler sufficient condition, proved below, is \[ b_v\ge\max(8,4m)\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal U, \qquad m=|\mathcal U|. \tag{6} \] The first alternative needs neither (5) nor (6): it is the existing whole-junction theorem. Under this criterion, the source bound extends to the whole construction, uniformly over its original auxiliary colors and on every fixed disk \(|s|\le R<1\). More precisely, the proof preserves each branch's original positive low-index profile and a remainder with a strictly smaller spectral rate. After closing, the total contribution of states with a high retained edge index has a strict exponential loss. Section 7 states the resulting source and volume consequences, and distinguishes them from the separate requirements for a filled invariant. ## 2. Polynomial coordinates, norms, and boundary profiles Write \(d=N-1\) and \(m_N=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). The fixed complete Newton basis is \[ S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin\frac{\pi a}{N},\qquad c_a=2\cos\frac{(2a+1)\pi}{N},\qquad e_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(c_a-z),\quad 0\le r<N. \tag{7} \] Empty products are one. An index is low when \(r\le m_N\), and high otherwise. These are coefficient ranges used in the proof, not a change to the physical colors. The same-color polynomial relation is \(P_s(z)=\mathsf T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s)\), where \(\mathsf T_N(u+u^{-1})=u^N+u^{-N}\). Opposite-color objects use \(P_0\). A canonical polynomial has degree less than \(N\). Its norm is \[ \|F\|_{\mathrm J}= \max\left\{|F(c_a)|:0\le a\le m_N; |F'(c_a)|:c_a\text{ is a double root of }P_0\right\}. \tag{8} \] The derivative entries retain the first normal information at repeated roots. At odd levels the final node \(-2\) is simple and has no derivative entry. Full Hermite interpolation makes (8) polynomially equivalent to the canonical sup norm on \([-2,2]\). It is therefore a norm on the complete polynomial, not merely on its values at distinct nodes. For the relation appropriate to the input, define \[ \phi_\sigma(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_\sigma}F, \qquad \sigma=s\text{ or }0. \tag{9} \] The fixed metric is exactly \(\phi_\sigma(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}\). The [physical turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) gives \[ T_s=\frac{\gamma_N(s)}{H_N(s)}\mathcal R\operatorname{diag}(W_r(s)), \qquad \mathcal R e_r=e_{d-r}, \] \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_r(s)=\prod_{a=1}^r \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi a/N)}\right). \tag{10} \] The actual orientation determines the scalar \(\gamma_N(s)\in\{1,q^{s^2/2},q^{-s^2/2}\}\). Formula (10) is used in that orientation, with its prescribed carrier. The factors, their inverses, and \(H_N\) are uniformly bounded on each \(|s|\le R<1\). Three estimates from the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Sections 1.1–1.4, will be used repeatedly. Quotient multiplication of a fixed number of canonical polynomials has polynomial norm cost; the trace (9) has polynomial cost; and \[ \|e_r\|_{\mathrm J}\le N^C \begin{cases} \exp\{Ng(r/N)+O(\log N)\},&r\le m_N,\\ 1,&r>m_N. \end{cases} \tag{11} \] The constants may depend on the fixed construction and parameter disk, but not on the level or physical colors. These statements keep the full quotient multiplication, including terms that vanish at completeness and reappear when \(s\ne0\). A branch has a **boundary profile** \(f_Q(u)\): fix its normalized output at \(u\), and maximize its positive complete source action over the remaining variables. Every additive constant accumulated inside the branch is part of this profile. Its intrinsic spectral pressure is \[ \Omega_Q=\max_{0\le u\le1/2}\{f_Q(u)+g(u)\}. \tag{12} \] This pressure is the exponential rate obtained by coupling the branch to the positive Newton norm comparison. The additional test factor in that comparison is not a physical crossing circle. The [rigid-profile theorem](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md), Sections 2–3, identifies a class of branches, called type \(L\), whose profiles have the form \(g+c\). Ordinary leaves and branches emerging from a flagged junction have this type. Their pressure is \(c+2G_0\). A turned product emerging from a bare junction has type \(A\); its profile is kept as a function of its output and is not replaced by \(g+c\). Positive reference polynomials realize these same profiles. For an L branch choose \[ Q_N^0=e^{Nc}h_N,\qquad h_N=\sum_{r\le m_N}\frac{N^2S_{2r}}{S_r^4}e_r. \tag{13} \] For a bare output use the complete product and reversal, \[ Q_{v,N}^0=T_0\prod_i^{*_0}Q_{i,N}^0. \tag{14} \] Their Newton coefficients are nonnegative. The positive source variational principle gives the original boundary profile at every strict interior output, with the usual lattice approximation providing the lower rate. These are comparison polynomials; they need not equal the finite physical branch. This distinction also avoids comparing to a physical endpoint coefficient that can vanish at one parity. ## 3. The local error estimate Maintain an exact decomposition of an actual branch into a low part and an error, \[ Q_{N,s}=C_{N,s}+E_{N,s},\qquad [e_r]C_{N,s}=0\quad(r>m_N), \] \[ |[e_r]C_{N,s}|\le e^{No(1)}[e_r]Q_N^0\quad(r\le m_N), \qquad \|E_{N,s}\|_{\mathrm J} \le e^{N(\Omega_Q-\gamma_Q+o(1))},\quad\gamma_Q>0. \tag{15} \] All errors are uniform on the fixed disk and physical-color cube. Because the tree is fixed, a finite number of polynomial factors is included in the displayed \(o(1)\). The physical coefficient extractor for a turn preceded by a circle operator is \[ [e_r]T_s(R_s^\epsilon L_jE) =\frac{\gamma_N(s)W_{d-r}(s)}{H_N(s)} \phi_\sigma(e_rR_s^\epsilon L_jE). \tag{16} \] The polynomial norm bounds for \(R_s^\epsilon L_j\), quotient multiplication, and (11) give the full coefficient bounds \[ |[e_r]T_s(R_s^\epsilon L_jE)| \le e^{N(c+o(1))} \begin{cases}e^{Ng(r/N)},&r\le m_N,\\1,&r>m_N, \end{cases} \quad\text{if }\|E\|_{\mathrm J}\le e^{N(c+o(1))}. \tag{17} \] Thus an L branch starts (15) with \(\gamma_L=2G_0\): its high part has rate at most \(c\), while its pressure is \(c+2G_0\). A spectral deficit in the input of (16) decreases the scalar constant in both lines of (17) by exactly that deficit. This last fact will be important when errors pass from one bare component to another. Now consider a bare junction with children \(Q_i\). Let \(A=\prod_iQ_i\) be its unturned product and \(Q_v=T(A)\). The two relevant pressures are \[ \Omega_A=\max_{u\le1/2}\{f_A(u)+g(u)\},\qquad \Omega_v=\max_{u\le1/2}\{f_A(1-u)+g(u)\}. \tag{18} \] At odd levels \(-2\) is an actual complete node. High Newton factors vanish there and low factors are positive. The exact identity \(A_N^0(-2)=\prod_iQ_{i,N}^0(-2)\), followed by the positive Laplace principle, gives \[ \Omega_A=\sum_i\Omega_i, \qquad \Delta_v:=\Omega_v-\sum_i\Omega_i. \tag{19} \] The equality is between parity-independent classical actions. It does not imply additivity at an arbitrary cut of a closed diagram. The derivative inequality in the [probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), Appendix A.2–A.4, gives \(\Delta_v\ge0\). It is strict if the last product has an A child, or if there are at least three inputs. The two-L-input product has \(\Delta_v=0\). Define the outgoing low part by \[ C_v=\Pi_{\mathrm{lo}}T_s\prod_i^{*_\sigma}C_i, \qquad E_v=Q_v-C_v. \tag{20} \] The all-parity low-array comparison in the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 2.5, preserves its positive reference majorant (14). There are two remaining kinds of contribution. The high output of the all-low product has spectral rate at most \(\sum_i\Omega_i\), because extraction against a high \(e_r\) costs only a power of \(N\). If a nonempty set of inputs is replaced by errors, quotient multiplication gives raw rate at most \(\sum_i\Omega_i-\sum_{i\in S}\gamma_i\). High output still costs only a power of \(N\). For low output, extraction and reconstruction use two low Newton factors, and cost at most \(2G_0\), since \(\max g=G_0\). Therefore, with \(\gamma_*\) the smallest child gap, \[ \|E_v\|_{\mathrm J}\le \exp N\left\{\Omega_v- \min\bigl(\Delta_v,\Delta_v+\gamma_*-2G_0\bigr)+o(1)\right\}. \tag{21} \] This proves the conditional propagation estimate, including the possible cost of the next turn. A positive child gap alone would not suffice. ## 4. A coupled pressure bound from rigid boundary branches Suppose the bare junction has at least \(k\ge4\) L children with profiles \(g+c_1,\ldots,g+c_k\). The other children may have any fixed strict L or A profiles. Then \[ \Delta_v\ge2G_0-\varepsilon_k. \tag{22} \] The proof supplies one admissible contribution to the full coupled positive sum. It keeps the other children's intrinsic constants and boundary constraints. The pressure \(\Omega_v\) is the rate of \[ \phi_0\left(h_N\prod_iQ_{i,N}^0\right). \tag{23} \] Work along odd levels to prove this inequality of classical actions. Choose the Newton index nearest \(N/4\) in each of the \(k\) indicated L references and in the existing comparison factor \(h_N\). There are \(k+1\) such factors. In every other child choose a low index nearest an intrinsic maximizing index \(\beta_i\in(0,1/2)\). The strict probe theorem supplies this interior index and the positive coefficient lower rate there. All selected indices are low and their pair sums are less than \(N\) for large levels. The \(k+1\ge5\) quarter indices alone have total greater than \(N\), so the tuple is inside the original positive closing support. No inconsistent boundary assignment has been introduced. For a low Newton factor, its Laurent expansion at \(z=-u-u^{-1}\) has coefficients \[ e_n(-u-u^{-1})=\sum_{r=-n}^{n}a_r^{(n)}u^r, \qquad a_r^{(n)}=\frac{S_{2n}}{S_n^2S_{n+r}S_{n-r}}. \tag{24} \] They are nonnegative, symmetric, and unimodal. Their uniform exponential rate is \[ \frac1N\log a_r^{(n)} =b_{n/N}(r/N)+O(\log N/N), \] \[ b_u(t)=J(2u)-2J(u)-J(u+t)-J(u-t),\qquad b_u(0)=g(u). \tag{25} \] Let \(a_r\) denote the convolution for the selected product, containing a fixed total of \(B\) factors. The exact odd Fourier trace and the interval-tail estimate of the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Sections 2.1 and 2.3, imply \[ \phi_0\left(\prod e_{n_i}\right) \ge N^2(a_{N-1}-a_{N+1}) \ge N^{2-B}a_{N-1}. \tag{26} \] This is a finite positive coefficient inequality; it does not approximate the difference by a derivative. In \(a_{N-1}\), distribute the exponent \(N-1\) equally, up to integer rounding, among the \(k+1\) quarter-index factors. Give exponent zero to every other factor. The assignment is allowed because \(1/(k+1)<1/4\). Combining (25) with the chosen reference coefficients yields \[ \Omega_v\ge \sum_{i=1}^k c_i+\sum_{i\ \mathrm{other}}\Omega_i +(k+1)\left[G_0+b_{1/4}\left(\frac1{k+1}\right)\right]. \tag{27} \] Subtracting \(\sum_i\Omega_i=\sum_{i=1}^k(c_i+2G_0)+\sum_{\mathrm{other}}\Omega_i\) gives exactly (22). This lower bound uses a single feasible contribution to (23). In particular, it does not assume that separately optimized cap values can be added at a shared boundary. The size of the loss is explicit. Since \(J''(u)=\pi\cot(\pi u)\), \[ \frac{J''(1/4+t)+J''(1/4-t)}2=\pi\sec(2\pi t). \tag{28} \] Integrate this identity against the symmetric triangular kernel for the central second difference. It gives \[ 0<\varepsilon_k\le \frac{\pi\sec(2\pi/(k+1))}{k+1},\qquad \varepsilon_k=\frac{\pi}{k+1}+O((k+1)^{-3}). \tag{29} \] In particular, \[ \varepsilon_{b-1}\le\frac{\pi\sqrt2}{b} \quad(b\ge8). \tag{30} \] ## 5. Propagation along every path in a component Decrease each maintained gap to at most \(2G_0\), if necessary. Combining (21) and (22) gives \[ \min\bigl(\Delta_v,\Delta_v+\gamma_*-2G_0\bigr) \ge\gamma_*-\varepsilon_k. \tag{31} \] Thus enough rigid inputs allow an adjacent bare junction to pass on the original low profile while losing at most \(\varepsilon_k\) of its error gap. Orient a maximal bare component toward any one of its boundary incidences. Every nonroot vertex receives all its boundary incidences as L children. At the component root at most one of these incidences is used as the parent. Hence every vertex has at least \(b_v-1\) L children, irrespective of the chosen root. Apply (31) with that number of selected children; any additional boundary child is left among the other inputs in (27). Boundary L modules begin with gap \(2G_0\). Induction toward the component root gives an outgoing gap at least \[ 2G_0- \max_{\mathcal P\text{ a directed descendant path from }v} \sum_{w\in\mathcal P}\varepsilon_{b_w-1}. \tag{32} \] Every directed path is a simple path of \(\mathcal U\), so (5) makes this positive for every root direction. The component is fixed and finite; its polynomial costs remain \(e^{No(1)}\). Condition (6) is an elementary sufficient test. If \(m=|\mathcal U|\), then (30), \(\pi<22/7\), and \(\sqrt2<10/7\) give \[ \sum_{v\in\mathcal U}\varepsilon_{b_v-1} <\frac{220m}{49\max(8,4m)}\le\frac{55}{49}. \tag{33} \] The alternating series for Catalan's constant gives \(G>8/9\), so \[ 2G_0=\frac{4G}{\pi}>\frac{112}{99}>\frac{55}{49}, \qquad \frac{112}{99}-\frac{55}{49}=\frac{43}{4851}>0. \tag{34} \] This proves the criterion with a definite margin. The path test can be substantially weaker than this convenient valence bound. For a singleton component, the [whole-junction theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Sections 3.3–3.4, supplies its positive high-input and high-output gaps. Its two-input exception is covered by the exact cubic support argument there. Thus a singleton requires no boundary-count restriction beyond its original valence and strictness. ## 6. Grouped high-index errors and fixed crossing powers The preceding norm estimate must be refined to distinguish inherited errors from newly created high indices. This distinction prevents an error from being charged another \(2G_0\) every time it crosses a flagged junction. For an outgoing L module of constant \(c_v\), use an exact decomposition \[ L_v=L_v^{\mathrm{low}}+I_v+H_v. \tag{35} \] The first term retains only low indices on every retained edge of its subtree, including its outgoing edge. The inherited error \(I_v\) satisfies the full coefficient bounds (17) with \(c_v\) replaced by \(c_v-\eta_v\), for some \(\eta_v>0\). The term \(H_v\) has high outgoing support and coefficient rate at most \(c_v\); by (11), its spectral rate is \(c_v=\Omega_v-2G_0\). At an ordinary leaf there is no inherited error: use its exact low and high projections. At a flagged junction, expand the input product using the corresponding decompositions. A term with a child error has a strictly smaller spectral rate, because quotient multiplication has polynomial cost. Formula (16) converts that spectral loss into a full coefficient loss in both ranges of (17). These terms form \(I_v\). Apply the same formula to the all-low input term and split its output into low and high ranges, giving \(L_v^{\mathrm{low}}\) and \(H_v\). This supplies (35) without treating a spectral estimate as a coefficient estimate without proof. Now evaluate an entire bare component. Its estimate is multilinear in its boundary arrays and applies to arbitrary arrays obeying (17). Its original pressure is affine in their scalar constants: \[ \Omega_{\mathcal U}(c_1,\ldots,c_b) =\Omega_{\mathcal U}(0,\ldots,0)+\sum_{i=1}^b c_i. \tag{36} \] This follows from the positive reference recursion: multiplying one boundary array by \(e^{Nc_i}\) adds precisely \(c_i\) to every constrained source action. If one input is an inherited error with constant \(c_i-\eta_i\), the whole component estimate therefore loses \(\eta_i\). It is not necessary to subtract \(2G_0\) again. For the remaining boundary terms, the low parts have the original profile majorants and the high parts begin with gap \(2G_0\). The path proof gives \[ Q_{\mathcal U}=Q_{\mathcal U}^{\mathrm{low}}+E_{\mathcal U}, \qquad \|E_{\mathcal U}\|_{\mathrm J} \le e^{N(\Omega_{\mathcal U}-\eta_{\mathcal U}'+o(1))}, \qquad\eta_{\mathcal U}'>0. \tag{37} \] Here the low term keeps every boundary, internal, and outgoing retained edge low. A newly generated gap may be chosen below (5), or below the singleton gap. Previously inherited losses enter through (36). At the next flagged junction, (16) changes (37) back into the coefficient form required in (35). Since there are finitely many components, a positive minimum remains after all polynomial factors are absorbed. At the closing root, the coupon and trace have polynomial norm cost. If no flagged junction exists, expose an existing ordinary leaf and use the exact Frobenius adjunction for its turn. The component is then evaluated toward that boundary incidence, which (5) already permits. No new comparison leaf or geometric constant is inserted. The two-leaf case remains the separate source-bound case. It follows that the exact scalar satisfies \[ Z_{N,s}=Z_{N,s}^{\mathrm{all\ low}} +O\bigl(e^{N(F_0-\eta)}\bigr), \qquad \eta>0, \tag{38} \] where \(F_0\) is the original augmented complete action. The error is the summed contribution of states with at least one high retained edge. It is not the sum of absolute values of every internal crossing path or every separate return term. The same argument applies if a circle coupon is replaced by a fixed composable power \(R_s^{n_i}\), for example \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\). The [fixed-power bound](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 1.3, gives polynomial canonical norm for every such power on \(|s|\le R<1\), retaining its Cartan factor and orientation. Therefore (16)–(17) remain valid with that coupon. Equations (35)–(38) then use the same augmented comparison profiles and the same positive structural margins. Polynomial exponents and the level from which the bounds hold may depend on the fixed integers \(n_i\); the exponential gaps do not require their sizes to be comparable. For these filled coupons, \(F_0\) in (38) is still the action of the original augmented comparison. The argument has not identified the filled critical action, proved a nonzero filled contribution, or compared this gap with the complete-to-filled volume change. Those are additional steps in a filled-source theorem. ## 7. The source bound, geometric constants, and remaining scope For the unfilled physical source (1), a flagged branch has \[ f_L(u)=g(u)+c,\qquad c=\sum_i\Omega_i, \qquad\Omega_L=c+2G_0. \tag{39} \] A bare branch retains \(f_Q(u)=f_A(1-u)\) and (18). These are the original profile identities, including their absolute constants, from the [rigid-spine geometry](actual_conway_rigid_spine_and_flagged_tree_geometry.md) and [probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md). At a flagged root, \(F_0=\sum_i\Omega_i\). In the absence of a flagged root, the existing-leaf adjunction gives the original intrinsic probe action. These are coupled source identities, not a volume decomposition into independent pieces. The exact main-cut normalization supplies one factor \(H_N(s)\), together with the recorded framing and type scalars. Their bounds on each fixed \(R<1\) do not change the exponential rate. Consequently \[ \sup_{|s|\le R,\,1\le j_i\le N} |\mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(q^s)| \le e^{N(F_0+o(1))}. \tag{40} \] Under the original knot, absence-of-internal-component, and marked-geometry hypotheses, the complete-color value at \(s=0\) has the nonzero asymptotic stated in the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 4.6, (T32). The whole source equals its selected core there because the complementary color is zero. This supplies the lower rate in the supremum, so \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\sup_{|s|\le R,\,1\le j_i\le N} |\mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(q^s)| =2\pi F_0=\operatorname{Vol}(Y^\epsilon). \tag{41} \] The complement \(Y^\epsilon\) is the augmented complement, with the crossing circles unfilled. Both parities are included. For two leaves the same pure-leaf qualification as in that complete source theorem is retained. The original profile also gives a fresh angular Gaussian for each outgoing A branch. Its low reference has a unique strict interior maximizer \(\beta\) of \(f_Q(u)+g(u)\). Near \((\beta,\pi)\), the low Newton angular action has a strict quadratic maximum; away from it the positive profile has a fixed gap. The remainder in (15) has a spectral gap, which absorbs the polynomial Hermite interpolation cost and its \(e^{N|y|}\) strip growth after the strip is narrowed. Thus \[ |Q_{N,s}(2\cos(\vartheta+iy))| \le\exp N\{\Omega_Q-c(\vartheta-\pi)^2+Cy^2+o(1)\} \tag{42} \] for suitable fixed positive constants. This is the reconstruction argument of the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 3.5, using the retained profile. It is not a claim that an arbitrary turn preserves a Gaussian. Because (5) works for every root direction, one can expose any original auxiliary circle and use the exact three cases in the [auxiliary-color gap theorem](actual_main_meridian_auxiliary_color_gap.md). When the circle is an ordinary leaf at a bare component, the outgoing object is now the entire component controlled above. Its action and Gaussian are still the original ones. The same root contour therefore yields a strict auxiliary-color deficit on every fixed \(|s|\le R<1/2\). The path condition is sufficient, not a classification of all adjacent bare components. The tree, colors' roles, framing, and every fixed crossing power are fixed before the level tends to infinity. Neither (38) nor (41) alone gives a filled-knot theorem or a limiting main-meridian profile at a displaced parameter. Those conclusions require a conditioned local contraction and, for fillings, the actual parameter-dependent crossing-power contour with its endpoint currents. ## 8. Finite reproduction The accompanying [direct-crossing reproduction script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_direct_fillings.py) compares powers of the full polynomial crossing, reduced modulo the physical relation, with the generic root-grid trace and the analytic complete first-normal trace. It includes negative powers and parameter values on both sides of the half-integer collision. A separate rational calculation checks the quadratic joint-charge comparison for unequal signed slopes. These finite checks do not prove the component pressure inequality or an asymptotic source theorem. With Python and `mpmath` installed, run from the repository root: ```bash python3 experiments/audit_main_meridian_direct_fillings.py ``` The default output is [the reproduction record](../experiments/main_meridian_direct_fillings_results.json). Use `--output` to choose another location. The optional `--profile-diagnostic` flag repeats the archived local profile scan; it is numerical evidence and is kept separate from the finite identities and exact rational checks.

title: Positive boundary pressures for Conway product trees
status: Positive boundary pressures and deletion of turns in Conway product trees
text:
# Positive boundary pressures for Conway product trees A Conway tangle is built by stacking ordered two-string tangles and applying quarter-turns. Group consecutive products that have no turn between them into a single product junction. A connected region with no crossing-circle operator is then a tree of product junctions; its internal edges are the physical quarter-turns. This note studies the positive action obtained from the complete Newton contraction of such a region. The underlying ordered constructions and their strict angle domains are defined in the [strict-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md). The results compare entire coupled boundary pressures. Deleting a turn and fusing its two product junctions cannot increase the complete positive maximum. Several prescribed high boundary labels can also be moved simultaneously to one half without decreasing the pressure which bounds them. An exact half-label identity then reassembles whole junctions with several high incidences. These comparisons are used by the [general component estimate](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) and the [Fourier reflection bound](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md). The comparison trees need not define the same link as the starting diagram. Their positive maxima are bounded by the starting action. The marked representation, filling curves and final knot-complement volume remain those of the starting construction. ## 1. Complete actions, boundary variables and product junctions Put \[  egin{aligned} J(u)&=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad 0\le u\le1,\ g(a)&=J(2a)-4J(a),\qquad 0\le a\le	frac{1}{2},\ m(x,y,b)&=J(x+y)+J(b)-J(x)-J(y)\ &\quad-J(b-x)-J(b-y)-J(x+y-b). \end{aligned} 	ag{1} \] The closed domain of a retained multiplication gate is \[ \max(x,y)\le b\le x+y\le1. 	ag{2} \] Its strict domain has all three inequalities strict. A rigid ordinary boundary branch has profile \(g(a)+c\); its fixed constant \(c\) includes any action already accumulated inside that branch. We keep all such constants throughout. A **covariant label** at a junction means the label inserted into its complete trace tensor. If that incidence is used as the ordinary output of a rooted product, the output is its complement. Thus a cubic junction has the symmetric action \[  egin{split} t(x,y,z)&=m(x,y,1-z)\ &=J(x+y)+J(x+z)+J(y+z)-J(x)-J(y)-J(z) -J(x+y+z-1). \end{split} 	ag{3} \] The symmetry follows from \(J(1-u)=-J(u)\). A physical quarter-turn edge identifies equal covariant labels at its two ends. An unturned edge inside a binary product resolution identifies complementary covariant labels. In ordinary rooted coordinates the latter simply passes a child output into the parent input. Consider a fixed finite connected tree \(\mathcal G\) of actual product junctions, each of full valence \(D_v\ge3\), counting its boundary attachments. All internal edges of \(\mathcal G\) are physical quarter-turns. At every external incidence place an ordinary profile \(g+c_j\), except when a boundary label is explicitly fixed. Choose one original ordered binary resolution of each junction and retain all its hidden variables. The complete action is the sum of its gate actions and boundary profiles, on the resulting compact angle polytope. Its maximum, when all ordinary boundaries are free, is denoted by \(F(\mathcal G)\). For a whole junction with prescribed covariant labels \(a_1,\ldots,a_D\), strict support is exactly \[ a_i>0,\qquad a_i+a_j<1\quad(i
e j), \qquad \sum_i a_i>1. 	ag{4} \] The closed support uses nonstrict inequalities. The junction action \(V_D(a_1,\ldots,a_D)\) is the maximum of the complete positive gate sum in its fixed resolution. It is continuous on that support. The next section proves the resolution statement needed here. ## 2. Strict resolutions and uniqueness of the positive maximum ### 2.1. A prescribed association has the same strict output interval For positive input labels \(a_1,\ldots,a_k\), the exact product interval is \[ a_i+a_j<1\quad(i
e j),\qquad \max_i a_i<b<\min\left(1,\sum_i a_iight). 	ag{5} \] These conditions are necessary and sufficient for strict intermediate gates at output \(b\), in every prescribed binary association. They are the fixed-label form of the [ordered product lemma](actual_conway_reduced_hub_source_normal_form.md), Section 2. Here is its constructive proof. For a child set \(S\), put \(L_S=\max_{i\in S}a_i\) and \(U_S=\min(1,\sum_{i\in S}a_i)\). A composite child has available outputs \((L_S,U_S)\), by induction; a singleton has its fixed label. At a parent with target \(b\), restrict both child values below \(b\). Their lower sum is less than one by the pair condition, and their upper sum exceeds \(b\) by the total condition. Choose their sum in \((b,1)\). If both are singletons, their fixed sum is already in that interval. The two inputs are less than \(b\), so the parent gate is strict. Repeat down the fixed binary tree. Conversely, each gate output exceeds both inputs and is less than their sum. The gate at which any two original inputs first meet also forces their pair sum below one. These observations prove the necessity in (5). Exposing the last incidence of a whole junction makes its ordinary output \(b=1-a_D\); (5) then becomes precisely (4). The closed statement follows either from the same finite interval rules or by taking limits. No hidden covariant edge is treated as a physical equal-label edge in this argument. Assigning \(3/8\) to all physical edges and ordinary boundaries satisfies (4) at every unmarked hub. It gives a strict witness after the hidden unturned labels are constructed by (5). If at most one boundary at each hub is fixed at half, assign \(3/8\) to all other physical labels. A marked hub then has largest pair sum \(7/8\) and total at least \(5/4\); an unmarked hub has largest pair sum \(3/4\) and total at least \(9/8\). The same construction gives a strict witness. These margins persist when all fixed half labels are changed slightly and independently. ### 2.2. The maximum is strict, with a negative definite Hessian The relevant curvature and boundary facts can be seen directly from the ideal-tetrahedron atoms. For a positive angle triple with sum one, write \[ \mathcal V(a,b,c)=-\pi[J(a)+J(b)+J(c)]. 	ag{6} \] Its Hessian is negative definite on the two-dimensional angle plane. Indeed in coordinates \((a,b)\), minus that Hessian has positive diagonal entries proportional to \(\cot\pi a+\cot\pi c\) and \(\cot\pi b+\cot\pi c\), and positive determinant because \(\cot\pi a\cot\pi b+\cot\pi b\cot\pi c+ \cot\pi c\cot\pi a=1\). For a strict gate put \(p=b-x\), \(q=b-y\), \(r=x+y-b\), and \(w=1-x-y\). Then the exact three-atom identity is \[ \pi m(x,y,b)=\mathcal V(y,x,w) +\mathcal V(p,q,2r+w) +\mathcal V(p+q,r,r+w). 	ag{7} \] All three triples are positive. Zero quadratic form in the first atom forces \(dx=dy=0\); the second then forces \(db=0\). The third contributes a nonpositive quadratic form. Thus every strict gate has a negative definite Hessian in all three labels, including labels above half. Also \(g'(a)=2\log\cot\pi a\), so \(g''(a)<0\) for \(0<a<1/2\). At a nonvertex-flat atom \((0,a,1-a)\), \(0<a<1\), a segment into the positive simplex has volume derivative \(+\infty\). This follows from \(J(tu)=tu\log t+O(t)\). At a vertex-flat atom the \(t\log t\) terms cancel; positive atoms have finite derivatives. No negative infinite term can cancel the barrier. Root the resolved tree at any retained output, or at a prescribed half boundary if one is present. Output zero forces both product inputs to zero. Output one either has two interior children summing to one, giving a nonvertex-flat atom, or lets this endpoint descent continue through a child. A physical turn exchanges zero and one; an artificial unturned edge preserves the ordinary endpoint. The descent follows child edges in a finite tree. It cannot end at an interior prescribed output or a fixed half terminal. It reaches an ordinary leaf endpoint, where the inward derivative of \(g\) is infinite, or an interior pair summing to one. Thus no maximizing state can have an endpoint wire. With all wires interior, any remaining equality in (2) supplies a nonvertex-flat atom in (7). The maximum is strict. Every free coordinate appears in a retained gate or in an ordinary leaf term. Summing their Hessians therefore gives a negative definite quadratic form on the actual independent wire variables. This proves uniqueness. The same argument includes varying prescribed boundary labels, since each appears at a gate. The implicit-function theorem and the negative Schur complement then give an analytic, strictly concave optimized boundary pressure near a strict constrained state. Compactness makes this branch the constrained global maximum in a small boundary neighborhood. Rooted unturned subtrees used below have strict ordinary output interval \((0,1)\). To check the induction, a rigid leaf has interval \((0,1/2)\), a turn preserves the full interval of a composite subtree, and a product of two leaf or composite inputs can realize every \(0<b<1\) by choosing inputs less than \(b\), with sum between \(b\) and one. Formula (5) then resolves all further products. The boundary argument above applies with that output fixed. These facts supply the strict analytic profiles used next. ## 3. Response equations and the reflection of one output Let \(f(b)\) be a strict optimized ordinary-output profile. Define \[ B=\cot\pi b,\qquad \kappa=e^{-f'(b)},\qquad X^2= rac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\qquad Y^2=\kappa X^2. 	ag{8} \] Thus \(X,Y>0\) and \(X^2+Y^2-B^2=1\). A rigid leaf has \((B,X,Y)=(B,B,1)\). We call a composite response proper when \(-Y<B<X\). At a stationary product wire, differentiation of (1) and the sine difference identities give a common positive \(X\) for both inputs and the output, with \[ B_o= rac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{B_1+B_2},\qquad Y_o= rac{Y_1Y_2}{B_1+B_2},\qquad B_1+B_2>0. 	ag{9} \] For example the input derivative is \(m_x=J'(x+y)-J'(x)+J'(b-x)-J'(x+y-b)\); stationarity says \(\kappa_x=e^{m_x}\). Substitution in (8) gives (9) and its output derivative. These are the same response equations as in the [intrinsic probe calculation](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), Appendix A. Inputs with \(-Y_i<B_i\le X\) produce a proper product output. For \(X\ge1\), the quadratic relation and the lower bound force \(B_i>0\), and \[ B_o-X= rac{(X-B_1)(X-B_2)-1}{B_1+B_2}<0. 	ag{10} \] For a rigid input one factor is zero; otherwise it is less than \(X-\sqrt{X^2-1}\le1\). Also \(B_o>0>-Y_o\). For \(X<1\), put \(h=\sqrt{1-X^2}\) and write \(B_i=h\cot\alpha_i\), \(Y_i=h\csc\alpha_i\). Then \(\alpha_i\ge\arccos X\) and the positive denominator in (9) gives \(\alpha_1+\alpha_2<\pi\). The output has that sum as its angle, so it is proper. An artificial unturned edge passes this response directly. A physical turn sends it to \((-B,Y,X)\), which is again proper. In the present bare trees a turned child is always composite; no turn of a rigid leaf is inserted into this induction. At the last binary gate of an unturned product, strict support gives \(B<B_i\le X\). Rearranging (9) yields \[ Y^2=(B_1-B)(B_2-B)\le(X-B)^2, \qquad X\ge X_2(B):= rac{B+\sqrt{B^2+2}}2. 	ag{11} \] The unsquared factors are positive. Since \(x\mapsto\log[x^2/(1+B^2-x^2)]\) is strictly increasing, \[ f'(b)\ge f_2'(b)=2\log(2X_2(B)^2), 	ag{12} \] where \(f_2\) is the genuine two-rigid-leaf product profile without the additive constants. If either input at the last gate is proper, all these derivative inequalities are strict. The identity \(X_2(B)X_2(-B)=1/2\) gives \(f_2'(1-b)=-f_2'(b)\), and hence \(f_2(b)=f_2(1-b)\). Integrating (12) proves \[ f(b)\ge f(1-b),\qquad 1/2\le b\le1. 	ag{13} \] For a rooted bare tree this inequality is strict above half unless the whole rooted side is one trivalent hub with two rigid external leaves. Indeed a higher-valence root has a composite child in its last binary gate, and a branch through another hub is a proper turned composite child. The exceptional profile is exactly \(f_2+c\). In the nonexceptional case \(f'(b)+f'(1-b)>0\), so the strict reflection difference persists at \(b=1\) by continuity. At half, (12) gives \(f'(1/2)\ge0\), strictly in the same nonexceptional case. ## 4. Complete physical edge labels are at most half Cut a physical edge of \(\mathcal G\) and root each side there. Each side is an unturned product with at least two inputs of the kind just considered: rigid leaves or physical turns of composite products. Denote the two complete profiles by \(f_A,f_B\). If \(z\) is the equal covariant label on the physical edge, its two ordinary outputs are both \(1-z\). The exact cut pressure is \[ f_A(1-z)+f_B(1-z). 	ag{14} \] For \(z>1/2\), both derivatives \(f_A'(1-z),f_B'(1-z)\) are positive by (12); (14) therefore decreases strictly. At half its derivative is strictly negative unless both rooted sides are the exceptional two-leaf product. Thus the complete maximizing label satisfies \[ 0<z_e\le1/2 \quad	ext{on every physical internal edge}. 	ag{15} \] Equality is possible exactly when the entire component is two trivalent hubs, each with two rigid external leaves. In that case (14) is \(2f_2(1-z)+c\), whose unique maximum is at half. Apply this cut argument to each edge of the same original optimizer. It does not replace neighboring subtrees by independently capped maxima. In every other fixed tree, all physical internal labels and all ordinary leaf labels have a compact window inside \((0,1/2)\). Hidden unturned-resolution labels retain their strict bulk window inside \((0,1)\) and need not be below half. The exceptional two-hub internal label can be continued through half within that bulk window. ## 5. Exact ordered fusion and deletion of any set of turns Set \(d=N-1\), \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), \(S_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N)\), and \[ e_r(v)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-v),\qquad P_0(v)=\mathcal T_N(v)+2, \quad \mathcal T_N(u+u^{-1})=u^N+u^{-N}. 	ag{16} \] The complete functional is \(\phi_0(F)=(-1)^dN^2[v^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_0}F\). Its full Frobenius metric and turn are \[ \phi_0(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d},\qquad T_0(e_i)=e_{d-i}. 	ag{17} \] The repeated-node first normals are part of this algebra. Since \(e_{d-i}\) is the dual basis to \(e_i\), \[ \sum_{i=0}^d\phi_0(Ae_i)\phi_0(e_{d-i}B)=\phi_0(AB). 	ag{18} \] To prove (18), expand \(A=\sum_i\phi_0(Ae_i)e_{d-i}\) and apply \(\phi_0(\,\cdot\,B)\). This is a full algebra identity, not only an equality of values at distinct eigenvalues. Reflecting exactly one endpoint of an equal-index physical connection changes it into the complementary pairing (18). That pairing fuses two complete product junctions. The induced order is read along the boundary of a small ribbon neighborhood of the two vertex disks and their joining band. With a root outside the band, the child's ordered product is substituted in its original position in the parent's product. No attached branches are permuted. The order after several fusions is the boundary order of the same contracted ribbon neighborhood, independently of the sequence of edge contractions. If valences \(D_1,D_2\ge3\) fuse, the resulting valence is \(D_1+D_2-2\ge4\). A connected fused set \(K\) has valence \(2+\sum_{v\in K}(D_v-2)\). It is again a product tree of the same class; contraction creates no cycle or duplicate branch. Its strict witness and unique maximum follow from Section 2. For one cut, use the actual two rooted profiles from Section 4. The complete pressures before and after removing the physical turn are exactly \[  egin{split} F_T&=\max_{0\le b\le1}[f_A(b)+f_B(b)],\ F_I&=\max_{0\le b\le1}[f_A(b)+f_B(1-b)]. \end{split} 	ag{19} \] For \(b\ge1/2\), (13) bounds the second summand by the matched summand at \(b\). For \(b\le1/2\), apply (13) to \(A\) and use the matched summand at \(1-b\). Therefore \(F_I\le F_T\). If one side is \(f_2+c\), symmetry gives equality of maxima. If neither side is symmetric, the comparison is strict away from half, while at half the matched summand has positive derivative and is not maximal. Compactness then gives \(F_I<F_T\). For any subset \(S\) of physical internal edges, let \(\mathcal G/S\) be the ordered tree obtained by removing those turns and fusing their unturned connections. Apply (19) successively to the actual profiles of each current fused tree. Its rigid boundary profiles and constants have not changed. This proves \[ F(\mathcal G/S)\le F(\mathcal G). 	ag{20} \] No matching hypothesis on \(S\) is needed for this pressure inequality. Restricted complementary-index sums may be enlarged to the complete positive sum in (18), so (20) also bounds their rates. The proof does not hold a multi-boundary pressure fixed while changing its other couplings. ![A trace-difference upper bound reflects one endpoint; the complementary complete pairing then fuses by an exact algebra identity.](../book/figures/main-meridian-reflected-turn-fusion.svg) The five exterior branches in the fused example are retained in their induced order. The first arrow is an upper bound and includes enlarging a restricted positive index sum; the second arrow is (18). Deleting a turn compares pressures. It does not identify the two knot complements. ## 6. Several prescribed high boundaries can be clamped together Now fix \(r\ge1\) marked covariant boundary labels \(\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)\), with at most one marked incidence at each actual whole hub. A mark has no leaf action. All other boundaries retain their ordinary profiles \(g+c_j\). Let \(\Psi(\mathbf z)\) be the maximum of this same full resolved action. At \(\mathbf z_0=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\), Section 2 gives a unique strict optimizer and an analytic pressure with negative definite Hessian. With no marks, no boundary comparison is needed. The partial derivatives at the all-half point satisfy \[ \partial_{z_i}\Psi(\mathbf z_0)\le0. 	ag{21} \] To prove this without differentiating a nonexistent terminal profile, root the same resolved tree at mark \(i\). Its ordinary output is half. For any other fixed half terminal, use the positive response \(\kappa=e^{m_x}\) supplied by its incident strict gate. Its cotangent is \(B=0\), so \(-Y<B<X\) automatically. This assigns a response, not a new action or an artificial physical leaf. Equations (9)–(10) now propagate proper responses through both unturned and turned edges, exactly as before. At the final binary product strict support makes both inputs less than half, so \(B_1,B_2>0\). Its output has \(B=0\), and \[ Y^2=1-X^2=B_1B_2\le X^2, \qquad \partial_{z_i}\Psi =-\log(X^2/Y^2)\le0. 	ag{22} \] Changing the root does not change the pressure: the same cubic action (3) is symmetric, physical edges still identify equal labels, and hidden unturned edges still identify complements. Thus (22) proves every component of (21) for the same constrained problem. The pressure is jointly concave, since convex combinations of full feasible states are feasible and the action is concave. For every feasible \(\mathbf z\ge\mathbf z_0\), its supporting plane gives \[ \Psi(\mathbf z)\le\Psi(\mathbf z_0). 	ag{23} \] This includes closed endpoints. Explicitly, with \(\mathbf v=\mathbf z-\mathbf z_0\ge0\), concavity gives \[ \Psi(\mathbf z)-\Psi(\mathbf z_0) \le rac{\Psi(\mathbf z_0+t\mathbf v)-\Psi(\mathbf z_0)}t. 	ag{24} \] For small \(t>0\), the right side lies on the analytic strict branch. Its limit is nonpositive by (21). If \(\mathbf v
e0\), the negative definite Hessian makes it strictly negative for small enough \(t\), unless it was already negative at first order. Thus (23) is strict away from the all-half boundary. This is a simultaneous comparison. It asserts neither monotonicity of one coordinate with other marks held above half nor a simultaneous reflection inequality \(\Psi(\mathbf z)\le\Psi(1-\mathbf z)\). The turn-deletion theorem supplies the separate coupled reflection comparison needed for (20). ## 7. The half-label cardinal identity For odd \(N=2m+1\), the complete relation has double nodes \(c_0,\ldots,c_{m-1}\) and the simple node \(c_m=-2\). The polynomial \(e_m^2\) vanishes with both first jets at every double node. Also \(S_m^2=N\), and \[ e_m(-2)=1, \qquad \phi_0(e_m^2)=1. 	ag{25} \] For example \(P_0=(v+2)\prod_{j<m}(c_j-v)^2\); \(P_0'(-2)=N^2\) gives the positive numerator value \(N\) in the first identity. The second follows directly from the top coefficient of the degree-\(d\) polynomial \(e_m^2\). Thus this square is the full Hermite projector onto the simple node: \[ e_m^2 F\equiv F(-2)e_m^2\pmod{P_0},\qquad \phi_0(e_m^2F)=F(-2). 	ag{26} \] There is no missing derivative contribution at a double node. For \(k\ge2\) and low remaining indices, \[ \phi_0\left(e_m^k\prod_j e_{n_j}ight) =\prod_j e_{n_j}(-2). 	ag{27} \] Uniform closed sine-factorial estimates give \(N^{-1}\log e_n(-2)=g(n/d)+O(\log N/N)\) on the low range. The positive ordered resolution identifies the complete tensor rate with \(V_D\). Its primitive half-label face can be approximated at odd levels while preserving all the prescribed equalities. Taking rates in (27), followed by continuity, proves \[  oxed{\quad V_D(\underbrace{	frac12,\ldots,	frac12}_{k\ge2}, x_1,\ldots,x_{D-k}) =\sum_{j=1}^{D-k}g(x_j), \qquad 0\le x_j\le	frac12. \quad} 	ag{28} \] The real complete action is independent of level parity. Odd levels calibrate (28); the proof does not assert that an even-level simple node projector exists. Zero low labels and further half labels are included because the closed action is continuous and \(g(0)=g(1/2)=0\). ## 8. Reassembling whole junctions with several high incidences This final comparison is useful when an absolute tensor bound has the following local action: each low incidence contributes \(g(x)\), and each high incidence contributes zero. For the moving Newton tensor this follows from the high basis polynomial's polynomial full spectral-jet norm, the low norm rate \(g\), and finite-degree Chebyshev folding. The [source bounds](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 3.4, retain those full norms and show that trace extraction costs only a polynomial factor. No same-index moving/complete comparison is assumed. Choose a nonempty set of pairwise nonadjacent whole junctions, each with at least two high incidences. Bound them by the local action just described. All other junctions must already have their complete positive tensors or a justified positive majorant at the same labels. In particular an uncontrolled moving junction with exactly one high incidence cannot be left in these old regions. Actual equal-color moving junctions are nonadjacent across physical turns, but constant junctions need not alternate with them globally. Remove the selected junctions. A retained complete hub has at most one strictly high incidence, since its complete pairwise support forbids two indices whose sum exceeds \(d\). At every high interface to a removed junction mark its adjoining old-region boundary. Mark an original external high input as well, retaining its constant \(c_j\) and its zero variable cone action. Thus each retained hub has at most one mark. At each low arm from a removed junction, place the single profile \(g(x)\) from its local upper bound on the adjoining old region. The nonadjacency and the tree condition make this assignment unique. Keep each ordinary external \(g+c_j\) unchanged. Optimize these whole old regions and apply (23) jointly to their high marks. Regions without marks are simply optimized with their ordinary profiles. Reinsert each removed junction with every high incidence set to half and with the newly optimized low-arm values. Formula (28) supplies exactly the sum of the \(g\) profiles already charged on its low arms. Remove those auxiliary boundary profiles when reinserting the junction: the same action now comes from that junction itself. They are consumed once, rather than added again. For an external low arm, its original \(g(x)+c_j\) remains and the junction supplies the additional \(g(x)\) already present in its upper bound. For an external high arm, the variable action was zero and the replacement leaf has \(g(1/2)=0\). If the entire graph is one selected junction, this external-arm accounting applies directly. Zero arms and limiting half labels are covered by (28). The result is a feasible state of the same complete tree with action at least the upper action being compared. At least one reinserted junction has a pair sum equal to one. The finite union of these closed pair-equality faces misses the original strict optimizer. Compactness therefore supplies a positive gap \[ \mathcal A_{\mathrm{comparison}} \le F(\mathcal G)-\delta, \qquad \delta>0. 	ag{29} \] At finite levels normalize these real comparison labels by \(d=N-1\). The closed support conditions are then exact; switching between \(n/d\) and \(n/N\) costs only \(O(\log N)\) in the logarithmic factorial estimates. Polynomially many states and polynomial tensor factors preserve the strict exponential gap, at both level parities. The geometric loss can be chosen before a fixed microscopic parameter radius. ## 9. Combining reflection, fusion and the geometric target For clarity, the graph facts used when (20) and (29) are combined are exact. A selected one-high moving difference has one high physical edge and all other incidences low. Its neighbor is a constant old vertex, whose nonzero complete tensor has at most one high incidence. Thus the selected internal edges form a matching. Reflecting one endpoint and fusing along each such edge leaves only low exterior incidences on every fused hub. It creates no additional high mark when the several-high junctions of Section 8 are removed. Those junctions are never fused and remain pairwise nonadjacent. The inherited orders, remaining physical turns and all boundary constants are unchanged. If a one-high difference instead uses an original external high index, reflection creates a low index \(r=d-h\). Its actual cone action was \(c_j\); the complete comparison leaf has \(g(r/d)+c_j\). The surplus \(g(r/d)\ge0\) is a retained loss, not a new physical action. At a strict ordinary-leaf optimizer it is positive; its endpoint cases are controlled by the compact complement of that optimizer. The Fourier companion proves the local bounds and the additional strict loss when an internal deletion has equal pressure. All of these constructions end with a pressure at most the complete positive action \(F_0\) of the starting strict tree. The original complete geometry identifies \(2\pi F_0\) with its augmented volume. The subsequent wire packet, joint filling saddle, primitive equations and scalar ledger continue to use the starting tree, including every physical edge; the comparison fusions are not inserted into that packet. In the [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) the actual equation remains \(U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\), with physical power \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\). Only auxiliary circle cusps are filled. The volume on the right is the knot complement of that original filled diagram, whose main cusp remains unfilled.

title: A filled crossing as an exact polynomial trace
status: Exact crossing-power traces at a moving meridian
text:
# A filled crossing as an exact polynomial trace The operator obtained by filling one crossing circle is an actual fixed power of the crossing. It can therefore be studied without first expanding that power in the moving auxiliary-color basis. The result below is local: it applies to a fixed product of regular low Newton factors at one crossing-circle junction. It supplies a nonzero leading term, an exponentially accurate analytic interpolation in the incident wire variables, and its exact dependence on the microscopic main meridian. Section 6 identifies its action with the marked long-filling action. The last section explains how the local estimate enters the [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) and why the [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md) is needed when different twist powers are independently long. The polynomial coordinates and the typed crossing are fixed by the [Newton compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) and the [turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md). The canonical sine-factorial interpolation used below is also derived in the [regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), Section 10. All crossing powers are fixed before the level tends to infinity. ## 1. The finite operator and the statement Put \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad d=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\qquad P_s(z)=T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s), 	ag{1} \] where \(T_N(2\cos t)=2\cos Nt\) is monic. The fixed complete Newton basis is \[ e_k(z)= rac{\prod_{a=0}^{k-1}(c_a-z)}{S_k^2},\qquad c_a=2\cos rac{(2a+1)\pi}{N},\quad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k2\sin rac{\pi a}{N}. 	ag{2} \] We use the original Frobenius functional \[ \phi_s(f)=\eta N^2[z^{N-1}](f mod P_s). 	ag{3} \] The crossing \(R_s\) includes its physical Cartan scalar. At a generic root, write \[ 	au_r(s)= rac{2\pi}{N}\left( rac d2+s-right),\quad z_r(s)=-2\cos	au_r(s),\quad 0\le r<N. 	ag{4} \] Its exact full eigenvalue is \[ R_s(z_r(s)) =q^{d^2/4-s^2/2} \exp\left( rac{iN	au_r(s)^2}{4\pi}ight). 	ag{5} \] In particular, for any fixed integer \(n\), \[ C_{N,n}(s)=q^{n(d^2/4-s^2/2)},\qquad R_s^n(z_r(s))= C_{N,n}(s)\exp\left( rac{inN	au_r(s)^2}{4\pi}ight). 	ag{6} \] All root collisions in \(|s|<1\) are interpreted by the actual holomorphic crossing polynomial and its full normal coefficients. The [Newton compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) and [physical crossing bounds](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 1.3, make \(R_s\), its inverse, and every fixed power holomorphic on this disk. The first nonremovable same-color interpolation resonance is at \(s=\pm1\), outside the present statement. Fix an integer \(B\ge1\), a compact interval \(I=[\delta,1/2-\delta]\subset(0,1/2)\), and \(0\le R<1\). For integer indices \(k_a/N\in I\), let \[ E_{N,\mathbf k}(z)=\prod_{a=1}^B e_{k_a}(z),\qquad V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)=\phi_s(R_s^nE_{N,\mathbf k}). 	ag{7} \] There is \(n_0=n_0(I,B)\) such that, for each fixed integer \(|n|\ge n_0\), the complete tensor \(V_{N,0}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)\) is nonzero for all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly over these indices. Moreover, there is \(\kappa>0\), depending on the fixed data including \(n\) and \(R\), for which \[  oxed{\displaystyle  rac{V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)} {V_{N,0}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)} =q^{-ns^2/2} igl(1+O(e^{-\kappa N}) igr), \qquad |s|\le R<1.} 	ag{8} \] Both parities are included. The integer \(n\) is fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The statement does not concern a growing filling coefficient \(n=n(N)\). The proof gives an analytic interpolation in the complex variables \(x_a=k_a/N\). Its main-meridian ratio is exactly \(q^{-ns^2/2}\). Thus (8) is more than a comparison on a real lattice, but it is still a local junction result. ## 2. An exact contour with the actual crossing power For this section set \[ B_N(	au)=\sin	au\,E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2\cos	au) e^{inN	au^2/(4\pi)}. 	ag{9} \] This is an entire odd function. Lagrange interpolation at the generic roots gives \[ V_{N,s}^{(n)} = rac{\eta N C_{N,n}(s)}{\sin(2\pi s)} \sum_{r=0}^{N-1}B_N(	au_r(s)). 	ag{10} \] Indeed \(P_s'(z_r)=N\sin(2\pi s)/\sin	au_r\), and (3) gives the remaining \(\eta N\). The formula initially excludes the zeros of its displayed sine; analytic continuation later restores the full normal trace. Choose \(R'\) with \(R<R'<1\) and \(R'
e1/2\). We first estimate (10) only on the parameter circle \(|s|=R'\). On this circle \(|\sin(2\pi s)|\) is bounded below by a positive constant. Put \[ \Delta_s= rac{2\pi s}{N},\qquad K_s(	au)= rac{iN e^{iN	au}} {e^{iN	au}-\eta e^{2\pi is}}. 	ag{11} \] Let \(\mathcal R_y+\Delta_s\) be the positively oriented rectangle with vertices \(\pm\pi\pm iy+\Delta_s\). It contains exactly the \(N\) points (4), for fixed \(y>0\) and sufficiently large \(N\). Each pole of \(K_s\) has residue one, so \[ \sum_r B_N(	au_r(s)) = rac1{2\pi i}\int_{\partial(\mathcal R_y+\Delta_s)} B_N(	au)K_s(	au)\,d	au. 	ag{12} \] The translation matters when \(|\operatorname{Re}s|\ge1/2\). It keeps the vertical sides halfway between their neighboring grid poles. At \(	au=\pm\pi+iv+\Delta_s\), one has exactly \[ e^{iN	au}=-\eta e^{2\pi is}e^{-Nv}, \qquad K_s(	au)= rac{iN e^{-Nv}}{1+e^{-Nv}}. 	ag{13} \] There is consequently no vertical pole-separation assumption on the argument of \(s\). On the upper horizontal side the convergent geometric expansion is \[ K_s(	au)=-iN\sum_{\ell\ge1} \eta^\ell e^{-2\pi i\ell s}e^{i\ell N	au}, 	ag{14} \] and on the lower side it is \[ K_s(	au)=iN\left(1+\sum_{\ell\ge1} \eta^\ell e^{2\pi i\ell s}e^{-i\ell N	au}ight). 	ag{15} \] The terms are entire functions of \(	au\). Their horizontal integration paths can therefore be moved to the fixed sides \([-\pi,\pi]\pm iy\); the short endpoint connectors stay within \(O_R(1/N)\) of the old vertical sides. No deformation of the meromorphic kernel through a moving pole is being asserted here. Define the fixed lower-side integrals \[ I_{\ell,N}^{(n)}(y) =\int_{-\pi-iy}^{\pi-iy} \sin	au\,E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2\cos	au) e^{inN	au^2/(4\pi)-i\ell N	au}\,d	au. 	ag{16} \] The upper side, with its boundary orientation, contributes the same \(I_\ell\) after \(	au\mapsto-	au\), because \(B_N\) is odd. The difference of the two coefficients in (14)--(15) is \(2i\sin(2\pi\ell s)\). The zero mode in (15) has zero integral on the real segment by oddness; moving its lower path to that segment produces only endpoint currents. Thus \[ V_{N,s}^{(n)} =- rac{N^2C_{N,n}(s)}{\pi i} \sum_{\ell\ge1} \eta^{\ell-1} U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi s)\,I_{\ell,N}^{(n)}(y) +\mathcal E_{N,s}(y). 	ag{17} \] Here \(U_{\ell-1}(\cos z)=\sin(\ell z)/\sin z\), and \(\mathcal E_{N,s}\) contains the original two vertical sides, the endpoint connectors, and the zero-mode endpoint currents. Formula (17) is first justified on \(|s|=R'\), where (10) has a bounded denominator. It is an exact convergent contour decomposition there, not a Poisson expansion of a nonperiodic real chirp.
