For clarity, the sign and normalization in (17) can also be checked on \(|s|<1/2\) with the paired kernel \[  rac{e^{iN	au}} {(e^{iN	au}-\eta e^{2\pi is}) (e^{iN	au}-\eta e^{-2\pi is})}. 	ag{18} \] Its two horizontal expansions have coefficients \(\eta^{\ell-1}U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi s)\), and its prefactor is \(-N^2C_{N,n}/(2\pi i)\). The two sides give the factor two in (17). This check does not impose the smaller radius on the translated-contour proof. ## 3. The finite Newton action and the first saddle Normalize the Newton product at its positive maximum: \[ A_N(	au)= rac1N \log rac{E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2\cos	au)} {E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2)}. 	ag{19} \] There is a fixed neighborhood of zero on which the logarithm is analytic, even, and real on the real axis, uniformly for all allowed indices. The product formula (2) gives \[ A_N(0)=0,\qquad A_N''(0)=-a_N,\qquad a_N= rac1{2N}\sum_{a=1}^B\sum_{r=0}^{k_a-1} \sec^2 rac{(r+1/2)\pi}{N}. 	ag{20} \] In particular, \(a_-\le a_N\le a_+\) for fixed positive constants. Midpoint integration gives \[ a_N= rac1{2\pi}\sum_{a=1}^B	an(\pi x_a)+O(N^{-2}), \qquad x_a=k_a/N. 	ag{21} \] All derivatives of \(A_N\) on a smaller fixed complex disk are uniformly bounded. Its local expansion is \[ A_N(	au)=- rac{a_N	au^2}{2}+O(	au^4). 	ag{22} \] We also use the established global Newton strip bound: for each fixed small real \(ho>0\), there are \(c_ho,y_ho>0\) such that \[ |E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2\cos(t+iv))| \le N^C E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2) e^{-c_ho N+C Nv^2}, \quad ho\le|t|\le\pi+O_R(N^{-1}),\ |v|\le y_ho+O_R(N^{-1}). 	ag{23} \] It follows directly from the positive low-Newton Laurent profile and its strict angular maximum. Its use here is for the raw product, not for a high-degree canonical reduction. For the first Fourier term put \[ \Phi_{1,N}(	au) =A_N(	au)+ rac{in	au^2}{4\pi}-i	au. 	ag{24} \] Its critical equation can be written \[ 	au= rac{2\pi}{n} + rac{2\pi i}{n}A_N'(	au). 	ag{25} \] The analytic implicit function theorem at \(1/n=0,	au=0\), with the uniform bounds above, gives a unique critical point in the chosen neighborhood for \(|n|\) sufficiently large. Uniformly in the index window, \[ 	au_{*,N} = rac{2\pi}{n} - rac{4\pi^2ia_N}{n^2}+O(|n|^{-3}), 	ag{26} \] \[ \Phi_{1,N}(	au_{*,N}) =- rac{i\pi}{n} - rac{2\pi^2a_N}{n^2}+O(|n|^{-3}). 	ag{27} \] These formulas are valid for both signs of \(n\). In particular \(\operatorname{Im}	au_{*,N}<0\), and \(\sin	au_{*,N}
e0\). Move (16), for \(\ell=1\), to the horizontal line through this critical point. The endpoint currents satisfy (23). On a fixed small interval around \(\operatorname{Re}	au_*\), the real part of the second derivative remains negative, and outside that interval the local quadratic bound or (23) gives a strict loss. The ordinary analytic Gaussian expansion therefore gives \[ I_{1,N}^{(n)} =E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2)e^{N\Phi_{1,N}(	au_{*,N})} \sin	au_{*,N} \sqrt{ rac{2\pi}{-N\Phi_{1,N}''(	au_{*,N})}}  igl(1+O_n(N^{-1}) igr). 	ag{28} \] The square root has the branch determined by the oriented horizontal contour; equivalently its denominator has positive real part at zero chirp and is continued along the actual quadratic phase. This leading coefficient is nonzero. The constants may depend on the fixed \(n\), but are uniform over the wire window. ## 4. One height controls every higher Fourier term Choose a smaller fixed local radius so that \[ \operatorname{Re}A_N(t-iy) \le- rac{3a_N}{8}t^2+C y^2 	ag{29} \] there. This follows from (22), the positive lower bound for \(a_N\), and the fact that the first change in the real part under an imaginary displacement is quadratic in \(y\). Set \[ y= rac{8\pi^2a_N}{n^2}. 	ag{30} \] For large fixed \(|n|\), this height lies in the local strip. On its lower side the real exponent of the \(\ell\)-th term is bounded by \[ - rac{3a_N}{8}t^2 + rac{|n|\,|t|y}{2\pi} -\ell y+C y^2. 	ag{31} \] Maximizing the first two terms over \(t\) gives \[  rac{n^2y^2}{6\pi^2a_N}. 	ag{32} \] For \(\ell=2\), substitution of (30) into (31)--(32) gives \[ - rac{16\pi^2a_N}{3n^2}+O(n^{-4}). 	ag{33} \] By increasing \(n_0\), this is at most \(-	frac92\pi^2a_N/n^2\), whereas (27) has real part at least \(-	frac52\pi^2a_N/n^2\). Every \(\ell>2\) has the additional loss \(-(\ell-2)y\). On the complementary angular interval, the chirp has modulus at most \(\exp(N|n||t|y/(2\pi))\), whose exponent is \(O(N/|n|)\). Thus (23) still gives a fixed strict angular loss for all sufficiently large \(|n|\). The same argument controls the vertical sides and the endpoint connectors in Section 2. Their imaginary heights are at most \(y+O_R(N^{-1})\); the chirp cost is \(O(N/|n|)\), while their Newton loss is a fixed multiple of \(N\). The factors \(K_s\) on the translated vertical sides are only \(O(N)\) by (13). The infinite sum is also controlled. On the parameter circle, \[ |U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi s)| \le \ell e^{2\pi R'(\ell-1)}. 	ag{34} \] The additional \(\exp(-N(\ell-2)y)\) makes the sum of all \(\ell\ge2\) a convergent geometric tail for large \(N\). The connector estimates can be summed in the same way, since their heights differ from \(y\) by only \(O_R(N^{-1})\). We have proved, uniformly on \(|s|=R'\), \[ V_{N,s}^{(n)} =- rac{N^2 C_{N,n}(s)}{\pi i}\,I_{1,N}^{(n)} +O\!\left( |I_{1,N}^{(n)}|\,N^2 e^{-\kappa N}ight) 	ag{35} \] for some positive \(\kappa\), after shrinking it to absorb polynomial factors. Now define the *whole* difference between the left side of (35) and its displayed first-term approximation. Both are holomorphic for \(|s|<1\), including \(s=0,\pm1/2\). The maximum principle transfers the boundary estimate to \(|s|\le R\). This argument does not claim that the separately divided endpoint errors in (10) are individually removable. Evaluating (35) at \(s=0\), using (28), and dividing proves (8). Uniform holomorphy on a slightly larger disk gives the corresponding estimates for every fixed \(s\)-derivative on the smaller disk. ## 5. A specified analytic wire interpolation The preceding proof controls actual integer indices. To move wire contours, use the canonical sine-factorial function \[ G_N(z)=\left( rac{2\pi}{N}ight)^z\Gamma(z+1) \prod_{m\ge1}  rac{\Gamma(Nm+z+1)} {\Gamma(Nm-z)(Nm)^{2z+1}}. 	ag{36} \] On \(-1<\operatorname{Re}z<N\), it is holomorphic and nonzero, with the fixed positive-base logarithms, \(G_N(k)=S_k\), and \[  rac{G_N(z+1)}{G_N(z)} =2\sin rac{\pi(z+1)}{N}. 	ag{37} \] Its uniform complex bulk expansion is established in [exact factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) and is used below. Put \(u=N	au/(2\pi)\) and \[ \mathcal E_N(x,	au)=  rac{G_N(d/2+u)G_N(d/2-u)} {G_N(d/2-Nx+u)G_N(d/2-Nx-u)G_N(Nx)^2}. 	ag{38} \] For every physical \(x=k/N\), the shift equation (37) gives exactly \(\mathcal E_N(k/N,	au)=e_k(-2\cos	au)\). For \(x\) in a fixed small complex neighborhood of \(I\) and \(	au\) in a sufficiently small fixed disk, all arguments of (38) stay in regular bulk strips. Choose a fixed small \(a>0\) containing all the first saddles for \(|n|\ge n_0\), and define \[ \mathfrak V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf x) =- rac{N^2C_{N,n}(s)}{\pi i} \int_{-a}^{a}\sin	au\, \prod_{j=1}^B\mathcal E_N(x_j,	au) e^{inN	au^2/(4\pi)-iN	au}\,d	au. 	ag{39} \] This is jointly holomorphic in the complex wire variables and in \(s\). After shrinking the wire neighborhood, the saddle stays inside the contour endpoints and its amplitude remains nonzero. The argument of Sections 3--4, with the omitted angular tails included among the endpoint errors, gives on every physical grid point \[ V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k) =\mathfrak V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k/N)  igl(1+O(e^{-\kappa N}) igr). 	ag{40} \] The comparison is exponential before any subsequent wire cancellation. The interpolant itself has the exact ratio \[  oxed{\displaystyle  rac{\mathfrak V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf x)} {\mathfrak V_{N,0}^{(n)}(\mathbf x)} =q^{-ns^2/2}.} 	ag{41} \] Thus there is no unspecified meridian-dependent local amplitude. For later action comparison, the limiting Newton action is \[ b(x,	au)= \int_0^x \log rac{\cos(\pi v+	au/2)\cos(\pi v-	au/2)} {\sin^2(\pi v)}\,dv, 	ag{42} \] with the real branch at \(	au=0\) continued inside the fixed disk. Its second derivative there is \(-	an(\pi x)/(2\pi)\). For the junction, write \(b(\mathbf x,	au)=\sum_jb(x_j,	au)\). The action selected by (39) is exactly \[ \mathcal T_n(\mathbf x) =\operatorname{stat}_{	au} \left[b(\mathbf x,	au) + rac{in	au^2}{4\pi}-i	auight], 	ag{43} \] on the branch near \(	au=2\pi/n\). The unit factor \(q^{nd^2/4}\) in (39) remains outside this action; it is not silently reset. ## 6. Equality with the original marked filling action Let the original local crossing sign be \(\epsilon\in\{0,\pm1\}\), and let \(p\) be its integer auxiliary filling coefficient, so that the literal remaining crossing is \(R^n\), with \[ n=\epsilon-2p. 	ag{44} \] The [regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), Sections 6–7, identifies the selected local action of the colored source packet as \[ f_\epsilon(\mathbf x,t) =\operatorname{stat}_{	au} \left[b(\mathbf x,	au) + rac{i\epsilon	au^2}{4\pi}+it	auight]. 	ag{45} \] This identity uses the actual auxiliary deficit and the old shear branch, not a new polarization convention. In the auxiliary Fourier transform, add \(2\pi i t z\). Stationarity in \(t\) imposes \(	au=-2\pi z\). Since \(b\) is even in \(	au\), the resulting action is \[ \Psi(\mathbf x,z)=b(\mathbf x,2\pi z)+i\pi\epsilon z^2. 	ag{46} \] The original filling functional subtracts \(2\pi i(pz^2+z)\). Substitution of (44) and \(	au=2\pi z\) gives \[ \Psi(\mathbf x,z)-2\pi i(pz^2+z) =b(\mathbf x,	au)+ rac{in	au^2}{4\pi}-i	au. 	ag{47} \] This is precisely the direct first-Fourier-term action in (43), including its charge, its sign, and the primitive filling coefficient. The other wire variables can be included before taking stationarity in (45)--(47). Hence the selected joint critical point of the direct model is the old selected long-filling critical point, on its original marked branch. Under the hypotheses of the [strict-tree filling theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and its [marked geometry](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), the geometric calibration identifies the real part of the resulting *whole* critical action with \(\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)/(2\pi)\), where only the auxiliary circles are filled and the knot cusp remains complete. This action identity does not require any new moving auxiliary-filling coefficient formula. The topological normalization is also unchanged: the actual filled local operator is \(R_s^{\epsilon-2p}\), not an asymptotic replacement. The physical Cartan factors \(C_{N,n}(s)\), all six typed edge factors, and the original ribbon/closing scalar \(\zeta_N(s)\) must still be multiplied exactly. In particular, a final profile must retain \(\zeta_N(s)/\zeta_N(0)\). No claim that this ratio tends to one is needed for logarithmic volume equality. ## 7. Global majorants and the whole-source interface There is a useful global local majorant. For all low incident indices, including their endpoints, (10), evaluated on \(|s|=R'
e1/2\), gives \[ |V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)| \le C_{n,R',B}N^2 E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2). 	ag{48} \] Indeed the shifted root heights are \(O(1/N)\), the full fixed-power chirp is bounded on them, and the positive Laurent coefficients bound the raw product by a constant times its value at \(-2\). At completeness, \[ \phi_0(L_NE_{N,\mathbf k}) \ge N(\pi/4)^B E_{N,\mathbf k}(-2) 	ag{49} \] at both parities, with the sharper odd constant one. The actual trace is holomorphic on \(|s|<1\), so the maximum principle proves the all-low comparison \[ |V_{N,s}^{(n)}(\mathbf k)| \le C_{n,R,B}N\,\phi_0(L_NE_{N,\mathbf k}), \qquad |s|\le R<1. 	ag{50} \] This comparison is with the old complete positive circle tensor, not with a filled signed tensor. For a fixed tree in the [source-bound class](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), or its [component extension](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md), the grouped high-error induction uses a polynomial spectral bound for a fixed crossing power at a decorated junction. That bound is available for \(R_s^n\). Together with (50), the original strict positive action therefore controls high labels and the complement of the selected low window at a rate \(F_0-\eta\). The loss \(\eta>0\) is a fixed structural loss; constants depending on the fixed integers \(n_v\) affect polynomial prefactors, not this rate. Long fillings make the actual filled critical action arbitrarily close to \(F_0\), so it can be arranged above \(F_0-\eta/2\). The remaining local comparison has a precise form. Replace the moving bare tensors by their complete tensors using the exponential regular-window alias estimate, and replace every filled circle tensor by (39). The only residual meridian dependence, besides the exact scalars (41), is the internal-edge factor \[ \gamma_N(s) rac{H_N(s)}{W_{k}(s)}. 	ag{51} \] Its canonical analytic wire continuation is \[ \gamma_N(s)  rac{G_N(Nx)^2}{G_N(Nx-s)G_N(Nx+s)} =1+O_R(N^{-1}) 	ag{52} \] uniformly on a fixed complex regular wire neighborhood. Thus it is a holomorphic amplitude perturbation, with no change to the selected action. A whole filled profile now requires transporting this analytic amplitude through the original finite primitive wire window and its selected complex saddle, with its endpoint currents. A pointwise \(O(N^{-1})\) comparison on the real grid is insufficient: the filled exponent is smaller than the complete positive exponent. The required comparison is instead an insertion-compatible complex-window saddle statement for the unchanged complete bare tensors and (52), while retaining the circle integrals jointly. The [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) constructs that finite window, and the [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md) keeps all circle charges until they have been compared at the same joint critical point. Selecting (39) separately at each circle before that comparison would not justify independently unequal long powers. The action match (47), the nonzero local amplitudes, and the exponentially accurate physical-grid comparison supply its local inputs. The original strict-source packet supplies the marked branch and the undeformed nonzero critical point. The compatibility of the actual finite wire contour and its holomorphic amplitude insertions must be stated explicitly before deducing a whole filled lower bound. With the finite-window and joint-charge interfaces supplied by those companion proofs, the main cut contributes exactly one \(H_N(s)\), the framing ratio remains explicit, and the nonzero critical action is the knot-complement volume by Section 6. The [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) states that conclusion with its source and knot hypotheses. A norm upper bound alone would not supply the required nonzero saddle.

title: Framing and the exact scalar in the main-meridian profile
status: Exact framing and crossing scalar in the meridian profile
text: # Framing and the exact scalar in the main-meridian profile 1 November 2026. Moving the main meridian changes the physical crossing matrices, the maps that bend strands, and the scalar used to correct the diagram to zero framing. These changes must be kept together. A factor that is harmless for the exponential volume rate can still contribute to the first correction of order \(1/N\). This note computes the scalar retained in [the filled main-meridian profile](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md). The answer is a single quadratic phase. Its exponent is determined by the actual crossing powers and the oriented writhe of the diagram. The proof uses the physical duality maps and crossing normalization; the preferred cusp shape is identified by a separate geometric calculation. ## 1. Statement and convention Fix an oriented Conway knot diagram \(D\), built from ordered products, physical quarter-turns and two-strand crossing boxes. The order of its endpoints and its original reduced cut are retained. A product stacks compatible two-strand operators; a quarter-turn bends one incoming strand into an outgoing strand and one outgoing strand into an incoming strand. The crossing boxes contain the integral words \(R^{n_i}\). Here \(n_i\) is the signed exponent of the actual checked crossing: the crossing matrix followed by the interchange of its two tensor factors. For example, if another diagram convention calls a pretzel integer \(a_i\) but inserts \(R^{-a_i}\), then \(n_i=-a_i\) in the formulas below. Let \(w(D)\) be the oriented writhe, the sum of the oriented crossing signs in the one-component diagram. It is the linking number of the knot with its blackboard parallel. Planar joining arcs and quarter-turns add no crossings or curls. Any additional framing curl must be included in both the physical word and its writhe. Put \[ N\ge2,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad d=N-1,\qquad \alpha=d+s,\qquad M=-q\,q^\alpha=q^s. \tag{1} \] The reduced ADO invariant \(F_N(M)\) is the scalar of the actual cut \((1,1)\)-tangle, corrected to zero framing and normalized so that the unknot has value one. It is the full modified-trace invariant divided by its modified dimension. The coordinate \(M\) in (1) is the marked meridian; \(s=0\) is its complete value \(M=1\). This is the normalization fixed by [the ADO comparison](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). The \(N\)-dimensional highest-weight module with weight \(d+s\) is denoted by \(V_+\), and its actual dual, with weight \(d-s\), by \(V_-\). Their highest-root coordinates are \(x=-q^{-1}q^s\) and \(y=-q^{-1}q^{-s}\). The two opposite-color ordered objects are \[ A=V_+\otimes V_-,\qquad B=V_-\otimes V_+. \tag{2} \] A change of order from \(A\) to \(B\) is represented by an actual invertible intertwiner. To express all such maps as polynomials in a Casimir operator, the [Newton compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md), Section 4, fixes the following reference maps: \[ G_A=I,\qquad G_B=\check R_{+,-}r_0(\Omega_A)^{-1}, \qquad C_{D,C}=G_DG_C^{-1}. \tag{3} \] Here \(\Omega_A\) is the total quantum Casimir acting on \(A\). Every intertwiner of this type is a polynomial in the Casimir after its reference map is removed. The polynomial \(r_0\) is the full complete crossing, including its Cartan scalar. Its values are nonzero at every spectral root, so it is invertible in the finite Casimir algebra. This algebra also retains the first derivatives at repeated roots; these data are not replaced by values alone. Formula (3) uses the full polynomial inverse in that algebra. The remaining factors that depend on a wire index are \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad H_N(0)=1, \qquad W_k(s)=\prod_{r=1}^k \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right), \quad 0\le k<N. \tag{3a} \] The factor \(H_N\) comes from the actual reduced cut. The ratios \(H_N/W_k\) occur on physical turn edges. They are kept separately because their dependence on the internal label \(k\) contributes to the first asymptotic correction. Let \(A_N(s)\) be the product of the remaining normalized scalar factors: the zero-framing scalar, the six-type turn scalars, the equal-color crossing phases, and the reference factors of opposite-color crossing words. Every factor is divided by its value at \(s=0\). The single reduced-cut factor \(H_N\) and the index-dependent edge ratios \(H_N/W_k\) are excluded. Then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle A_N(s)=q^{\,a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_i n_i.} \tag{4} \] This is an exact identity for the scalar just defined. An asymptotic statement about the whole invariant requires the separate estimates of its finite sum. The identity shows that \(A_N\) has no surviving term linear in \(s\) and no additional meridian-dependent cup or cut factor. For the standard positive checked braid convention, let \(o_i=+1\) when the two oriented strands in the original crossing disk are parallel and \(o_i=-1\) when they are antiparallel. These signs refer to the actual knot orientation, before any artificial reinterpretation of a dual strand as an upward vector-space factor. Reversing one tangent reverses the oriented crossing sign; reversing both preserves it. Hence \[ w(D)=\sum_i o_i n_i,\qquad \boxed{\displaystyle a(D)=-2\sum_{i:\,o_i=+1}n_i.} \tag{5} \] Formula (4) retains the actual writhe and the actual \(R\)-exponents. Formula (5) is its form in the standard positive-braid convention. The integer \(a(D)\) is even and depends on this diagrammatic decomposition; it is not, by itself, a knot invariant. Every power of \(q\) means the exponential with \(\log q=\pi i/N\) fixed by the unrolled source. The scalar identity holds for every oriented Conway knot diagram to which the typed compiler applies. The moving-meridian asymptotic in Section 6 additionally requires a strict presentation and independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists. The exact scalar calculation itself requires neither a large-level limit nor the analytical estimates used to prove that profile. ## 2. Closing, the mark, and the absence of another monomial The actual unrolled twist is \[ \theta_\alpha=q^{(\alpha^2+2(1-N)\alpha)/2}. \tag{6} \] At \(\alpha=d+s\), its exponent completes the square: \[ \theta_{d+s}=q^{(s^2-d^2)/2},\qquad \frac{\theta_{d+s}^{-w}}{\theta_d^{-w}} =q^{-ws^2/2}. \tag{7} \] The same formula holds for the dual color \(d-s\). Thus the actual zero-framing correction is already a purely quadratic scalar. The linear term in the common crossing Cartan factor must not be separately retained after this substitution and after the exact shifted-grid calculation below. The closing calculation uses the actual evaluation maps. In [the pivotal duality calculation](relative_pivotal_duality.md), Section 2, the Cartan generator acts by \(Kv_a=xQ^{-a}v_a\). If \(\varphi_a\) is the dual basis, the selected module duality is \[ J_xw_a=c_a(x)\varphi_{d-a},\qquad c_a(x)=(-x)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}. \tag{8a} \] Its double dual is exactly \[ (J_x^{-1})^t J_y=K^{1-N}=g,\qquad y=x^{-1}Q^{-1}. \tag{8} \] Here the superscript \(t\) is matrix transpose. Indeed the \(a\)-th diagonal entry on the left of (8) is \(c_a(y)/c_{d-a}(x)=x^{1-N}Q^{a(N-1)}\), the corresponding entry of \(g\). This includes both parities of \(N\). The left and right evaluation/coevaluation maps obey the four snake identities: bending a strand out and back returns the identity. Their powers of \(x\), including those of order \(N\), are already part of the physical turns. They do not leave an additional scalar outside those maps. The original cut projector also fixes its normalization exactly. In the balanced basis it is \(e=\psi\varphi\), where \(\psi_a=1\), \(\varphi_a=1/N\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}e=1\). With the marked defect \(\mathcal{D}=g^{-1}e\), \[ \operatorname{Tr}(g\mathcal{D}C)=\operatorname{Tr}(eC). \tag{9} \] For the actual cut operator \(C=cI\), this is \(c\). Moving the mark transports the whole defect, so (9) computes the same scalar. The [explicit cap and marked-cut formulas](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), Sections 1–2, give \(N^kN^{-(k-1)}N^{-2}=N^{-1}\) for a presentation with \(k\) cups, \(k-1\) ordinary caps and one marked cap. This count is independent of the color; all remaining color monomials stay in the evaluation maps. There is an equivalent direct two-string closure calculation. The normalized functional \(\phi_\sigma\) on the finite Casimir algebra is \[ \phi_\sigma(f)=s_0[z^d]f,\qquad s_0=(-1)^dN^2. \tag{9a} \] The polynomial is first reduced to degree less than \(N\) in the actual algebra. Here \(\sigma=s\) or \(-s\) for equal colors and \(\sigma=0\) for opposite colors. The symbol \([z^d]\) means the coefficient of \(z^d\). Thus \(\phi_\sigma\) keeps the whole polynomial, including its repeated-root coefficients. The actual partial pivotal moments are \[ \operatorname{ptr}_{g_2}\Omega^r=0\quad(r<d),\qquad \operatorname{ptr}_{g_2}\Omega^d=s_xI,\qquad \frac{s_x}{s_0} =\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}=:H_N(s). \tag{10} \] Both left and right closings, and either choice of the surviving dual color, have the same ratio. If \(f_D\) is the polynomial of the whole unframed physical operator after the actual closing turn has been retained, then \[ F_{D,\mathrm{raw}}(q^s)=H_N(s)\phi_\sigma(f_D). \tag{11} \] This is [the compiler's primitive closing formula](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md), Section 5, equations (21)–(23), applied before the zero-framing correction. The polynomial \(f_D\) contains every physical crossing and physical turn. An alternative cap closure first performs its actual closing turn and then uses (11). Consequently, if all crossing powers and turn scalars are assigned to their local entries, the remaining closing scalar of the filled theorem has the exact complete-value ratio \[ \frac{\zeta_{\mathrm{closing},N}(s)} {\zeta_{\mathrm{closing},N}(0)} =q^{-w(D)s^2/2}. \tag{12} \] Constants depending only on \(N\), such as a fixed Fourier or complete balancing convention, cancel from this ratio. An explicitly relocated reference factor must of course be returned to its local entry before using (12). No such relocation changes the total in (4). The rationality proof in [the ADO normalization](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), Section 1, uses a different intermediate normalization: it strips the common factor \(q^{\alpha^2/2}\) from each crossing of a same-color braid. In that convention the combined Cartan and framing ratio is \[ q^{w(ds+s^2/2)}q^{-ws^2/2}=q^{wds}. \tag{12a} \] Thus a linear term appears in that intermediate gauge. The filled compiler uses the full physical crossings, whose Cartan factors are already included in (24); its remaining closing factor is (12), not (12a). Multiplying a full-crossing computation by the stripped convention's monomial would count the Cartan normalization twice. The fact that an intermediate formula contains a linear term therefore supplies no additional factor for the ledger here. ## 3. The four mixed generators, including negative odd words The full monodromy identity from [the turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md), Section 3, equations (41)–(42), is \[ \check R_{-,+}\check R_{+,-} =q^{-s^2}r_0(\Omega_A)^2. \tag{13} \] Its proof separates the channels by a generic perturbation of the sum of the highest weights and then continues the full polynomial identity. Thus (13) retains derivatives at repeated roots; a nodal-only statement would not suffice. Removing the coherent carrier (3) gives: | Starting order | Physical generator | Extracted polynomial | | --- | --- | --- | | \(A\) | \(\check R_{+,-}\) | \(r_0\) | | \(B\) | \(\check R_{-,+}\) | \(q^{-s^2}r_0\) | | \(A\) | \(\check R_{-,+}^{-1}\) | \(q^{s^2}r_0^{-1}\) | | \(B\) | \(\check R_{+,-}^{-1}\) | \(r_0^{-1}\) | Every crossing swaps the order, regardless of its sign. For a word of length \(L\), signs \(\delta_j\in\{1,-1\}\), and net exponent \(n=\sum_j\delta_j\), the exponent of \(q^{s^2}\) starting at \(A\) is \[ \frac{L-n}{2}-\left\lfloor\frac L2\right\rfloor =-\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor. \tag{14} \] Starting at \(B\) replaces the floor of \(L/2\) by its ceiling, giving \(-\lceil n/2\rceil\). Therefore \[ f_{n,A}=q^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor s^2}r_0^n,\qquad f_{n,B}=q^{-\lceil n/2\rceil s^2}r_0^n. \tag{15} \] These formulas apply to negative integers and to alternating positive and negative odd blocks. For example \(n=-1\) starting at \(A\) has factor \(q^{s^2}\), whereas starting at \(B\) it has factor one. Replacing a negative odd reference by the coherent carrier is done once; adding its conversion again to (15) would be a double count. We denote the scalar multiplying \(r_0^n\) in (15) by \(\rho_N^{(n)}(s)\), with the starting order retained. Its complete value is one. This is the opposite-color factor used in the global product below. For later use, write \(\delta(n)\in\{0,1\}\) for the parity of \(n\), using Euclidean division even when \(n<0\). In units of \(s^2/2\), (15) has scalar exponent \[ -2\lfloor n/2\rfloor=-n+\delta(n),\qquad -2\lceil n/2\rceil=-n-\delta(n). \tag{16} \] The two parity terms will cancel against the turns. This is why treating every mixed word as a scalar \(q^{-ns^2/2}\) before retaining the reference maps would be incorrect locally, even though that scalar is the final global result. ## 4. A boundary grading makes all turn phases telescope Assign an integer \(\chi\) to the six actual spaces of polynomial morphisms: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{space}&\chi\\ \hline \operatorname{End}(V_+\otimes V_+),\ \operatorname{End}(V_-\otimes V_-)&0\\ \operatorname{End}(A),\ \operatorname{End}(B)&0\\ \operatorname{Hom}(A,B)&1\\ \operatorname{Hom}(B,A)&-1 . \end{array} \tag{17} \] This is an integer assigned to an ordered boundary type, not a scalar extracted from an unknown invariant. On the opposite-color category it is \(h(\text{target})-h(\text{source})\), with \(h(A)=0,h(B)=1\). Consequently \(\chi(YX)=\chi(Y)+\chi(X)\) for every compatible product. The six forward physical turns have the following scalar exponents. An entry \(a\) means multiplication by \(q^{as^2/2}\), in addition to the paired sine-product operator. | Input space | Output space | \(a\) | | --- | --- | ---: | | \(\operatorname{End}(V_+\otimes V_+)\) | \(\operatorname{Hom}(B,A)\) | \(-1\) | | \(\operatorname{Hom}(B,A)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(V_-\otimes V_-)\) | \(1\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(V_-\otimes V_-)\) | \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\) | \(1\) | | \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(V_+\otimes V_+)\) | \(-1\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(A)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(B)\) | \(0\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(B)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(A)\) | \(0\) | These are the actual maps of [the six-type turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md), Section 3. In each row the exponent is \(\chi_{\mathrm{out}}-\chi_{\mathrm{in}}\). Thus its scalar is \[ \gamma_{\mathscr T}(s) =q^{(\chi_{\mathrm{out}}-\chi_{\mathrm{in}})s^2/2}. \tag{18} \] Indeed the four successive types have \(\chi\)-values \(0,-1,0,1,0\), so their exponents are \(-1,+1,+1,-1\); the opposite-color endomorphism turns have exponent zero. The remaining operator is \(H_N^{-1}\mathcal R\operatorname{diag}W\), where \(\operatorname{diag}W\) multiplies Newton coefficient \(k\) by \(W_k\) and \(\mathcal R\) reverses the \(N\) coefficients, sending index \(k\) to \(d-k\). It is separate from this scalar. An equivalent algebraic proof removes all turn phases at once. In a space of type \(\chi\), replace a coordinate polynomial \(f\) by \[ \widetilde f=q^{-\chi s^2/2}f. \tag{19} \] Compatible products remain ordinary multiplication because \(\chi\) adds. Every turn loses precisely its scalar (18). The final true endomorphism has \(\chi=0\), so the root scalar is unchanged. This is only a proof of scalar cancellation; it is not a change to the actual definition of the invariant. At an opposite-color word \(R^n\), its input-output type has \(\chi=\delta(n)\) if it starts at \(A\), and \(\chi=-\delta(n)\) if it starts at \(B\). Equations (16) and (19) therefore leave the scalar \[ q^{-ns^2/2}. \tag{20} \] In the original coordinates the same statement is \[ \sum_{\text{actual turns}}(\chi_{\mathrm{out}}-\chi_{\mathrm{in}}) =-\sum_{\text{crossing leaves}}\chi_i, \tag{21} \] since products add \(\chi\) and the closing endomorphism has \(\chi=0\). Thus every floor/ceiling parity term cancels, for either starting order and any signs of the powers. The argument is performed on the expression with its actual ordered input and output spaces. To rewrite it as a contraction with all indices incoming, pair each output with the compatible reverse morphism space. The reference maps around each resulting vertex compose to the identity. Reassociating this finite contraction retains every original edge tensor and its scalar. If an edge is described using a different forward turn, the known ratio of the two turn scalars is kept. No interchange of physical tangles is used. ## 5. Equal-color crossings and the global result At an equal-color vertex with \(\sigma=s\) or \(-s\), the full crossing eigenvalue has common Cartan scalar \[ \kappa_\sigma=q^{(d+\sigma)^2/2}. \tag{22} \] Writing its actual grid as \[ \tau_j=\frac{2\pi}{N}\left(\frac d2+\sigma-j\right) \tag{23} \] gives the exact quadratic-exponential identity, including the finite sign \((-1)^j\), \[ \kappa_\sigma(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)-2\sigma j} =q^{d^2/4-\sigma^2/2} \exp\left(\frac{iN\tau_j^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{24} \] For an integer crossing power \(n\), all factors are raised with their actual integer powers. Hence the complete-value ratio of its explicit chirp scalar is exactly \(q^{-n\sigma^2/2}=q^{-ns^2/2}\). This is the factor used in the regular-circle and direct-crossing trace theorems. In particular the apparent linear term \(d\sigma\) in (22) has not been omitted: it is absorbed by the actual translated grid (23), as the equality (24) shows. Equal-color crossing leaves have \(\chi=0\). Combining (20), (21) and (24), the product of all edge and crossing/reference factors in the filled profile is therefore \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \left(\prod_e\gamma_e(s)\right) \left(\prod_{i\text{ equal}}q^{-n_i\sigma_i^2/2}\right) \left(\prod_{i\text{ opposite}}\rho_i^{(n_i)}(s)\right) =q^{-(\sum_i n_i)s^2/2}.} \tag{25} \] Multiplication by the remaining zero-framing ratio (12) proves (4). This proof includes the original root closing turn. It also includes any pure leaf as the case \(n_i=0\). There is a useful filling form of the answer. Let \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) be the retained half twist at auxiliary crossing circle \(i\), and let \(p_i\in\mathbb Z\) be its integer filling coefficient in the original primitive slope \(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\). The resulting crossing power is \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\). Even twists do not change the oriented pairing, so the signs \(o_i\) are unchanged. If \(w_\epsilon=\sum_i o_i\epsilon_i\) is the writhe of the retained half-twist diagram, then \[ \begin{aligned} a(D) &= -w_\epsilon-\sum_i\epsilon_i +2\sum_i(o_i+1)p_i\\ &= -w_\epsilon-\sum_i\epsilon_i +4\sum_{i:\,o_i=+1}p_i. \end{aligned} \tag{26} \] In particular pure parallel fillings contribute \(4p_i\), whereas antiparallel fillings contribute zero to this integer. The same quantities occur in the independent geometric surgery bookkeeping through the squared linking number of a crossing circle, but that interpretation is not used in the proof. ## 6. The moving profile and the preferred cusp The scalar identity above requires no strict geometric saddle or long-twist assumption. To apply it to an asymptotic, impose the hypotheses of [the filled main-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md), Section 1. The [general filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) uses this exact scalar for every fixed strict Conway knot presentation with independently sufficiently long signed twists. Its analytic proof now permits arbitrary bare components. The scalar identity itself follows from the finite crossing and duality calculation above. For this class there is one presentation-dependent threshold \(B\) such that the theorem holds for all fixed signed crossing powers \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\) with \(|n_i|\ge B\). The signs and magnitudes are independent; no ratio between the magnitudes is bounded. They are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The threshold is independent of the subsequent fixed disk \(0\le R<1\). Both even and odd levels are included. Substitution of (4) into that theorem's second-order insertion formula gives \[ \frac{F_N(q^s)}{F_N(1)} =H_N(s)q^{a(D)s^2/2} \left(1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}) +O(N^{-2})\right). \tag{27} \] All estimates are uniform on a fixed disk \(|s|\le R<1\). The integers \(n_i\), the orientation pattern and the presentation are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The edge sum is the same filled complex saddle sum as in that theorem. The exact bound \( |\log A_N(s)|\le \pi|a(D)|R^2/(2N) \), using the specified exponential, shows that the scalar tends to one uniformly. Moreover, \(H_N(s)=\sin(\pi s)/(\pi s)+O_R(N^{-2})\). Consequently the reduced invariant has the limit \[ \frac{F_N(q^s)}{F_N(1)} \longrightarrow\frac{\sin\pi s}{\pi s} \tag{28} \] locally uniformly before the first ordinary resonance. The quotient at \(s=0\) is assigned its removable value one. For clarity, the full modified-trace invariant is \[ \mathcal N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M),\qquad d_N(M)=i^{N+3}\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}}, \qquad \frac{d_N(q^s)}{d_N(1)}=\frac1{H_N(s)}. \tag{28a} \] The whole germ gives \(d_N(1)=i^{N+3}/N\). Thus its normalized profile tends to one. These profile limits use the proved filled packet, not scalar bookkeeping alone. No continuation of these uniform estimates across \(s=\pm1\) is asserted. More precisely, without dividing out the scalar, \[ \frac{F_N(q^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =1+\frac{s^2}{N} \left(\frac{i\pi a(D)}2 -\pi\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}})\right) +O(N^{-2}). \tag{29} \] Thus omitting \(A_N\) can change the first correction even though it changes neither the leading disk profile nor the logarithmic volume. Set \(z=2\pi i s\), so that the marked meridian is \(M=e^{z/(2N)}\) and its squared coordinate is \(M^2=e^{z/N}\). Equation (29) becomes \[ 1+\frac{z^2}{8\pi iN} \left(a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}})\right) +O(N^{-2}). \tag{30} \] The independent calculation of [the preferred main cusp](actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) identifies \[ \tau_{\mathrm{main}} =a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}). \tag{31} \] Here the meridian translates by one and the longitude is the primitive preferred longitude, with linking number zero after the auxiliary fillings. That calculation follows the original face maps and the homology of the filled auxiliary slopes. It does not infer the longitude from (30). Combining the two results gives the geometric form of the first correction: \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{F_N(q^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =\frac{\mathcal N_N(q^s)}{\mathcal N_N(1)} =1+\frac{\tau_{\mathrm{main}}\,z^2}{8\pi iN} +O_{D,\mathbf{n},R}(N^{-2}).} \tag{32} \] The equality between the two ratios is exact; their common asymptotic is uniform on the fixed disk. The filled theorem already identifies the uniform logarithmic rate there with the actual volume of the resulting knot complement. Only the auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled; the main knot cusp stays unfilled. ## 7. Scope of the calculation The exact scalar calculation uses the ribbon twist, actual duality and marked cut, six-type turns, mixed monodromy and the full shifted-grid crossing identity. The latter is derived in detail in [the regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), Sections 1–3, and [the direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md). The argument is finite-level algebra and applies at both parities. Changing coherent reference maps can redistribute scalar phases among edges and odd vertices. Compatible composition and the actual closing cut preserve their total. Changing the framing changes the recorded twist factor. Changing the reduced cut normalization changes the invariant, so that change must be stated separately. The complete-value volume theorem has broader coverage. In particular [the strict-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) establishes the long-twist volume equality at \(M=1\) without the additional product-junction restriction used by the moving theorem. The profile and first correction in Section 6 are asserted only for the moving theorem's stated class. Exact knowledge of a framing factor does not supply the remaining estimates for other trees. The geometric comparison in (31) uses the preferred peripheral curves of the same knot. It does not identify a classical geometric factor of a quantum annihilator, nor does it give a profile on a fixed nonshrinking disk in \(M\). The microscopic coordinate and the exclusion of ordinary resonances remain part of the statement. ## 8. Reproducing the finite identities The [exact scalar script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_exact_scalar.py) starts from the two mixed positive crossings, obtains the inverse crossings, and composes signed words with their actual starting and ending orders. It also derives the integer grading from the six turn phases, checks compatible products and turns on finite expression trees, and compares the shifted-grid exponents as rational polynomials. Its [recorded results](../experiments/main_meridian_exact_scalar_results.json) list the inputs and the scope of the checks. To run the scalar checks together with the geometric matrix identities, use the repository runner: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py meridian-cusp ``` The scalar script uses Python's standard library; the geometric script also requires SymPy. These computations check local algebra. The physical tensor formulas, the longitude's topology, and the uniform asymptotic estimates are supplied by the proofs, rather than by a finite list of examples.

title: The meridian profile and volume for Conway knots with long twists
status: Uniform meridian profile and the volume of the filled knot complement
text: # The meridian profile and volume for Conway knots with long twists 1 November 2026. This proof concerns the actual reduced ADO invariant of a filled knot, with its zero framing and its prescribed meridian coordinate. The meridian moves by an amount of order \(1/N\), while the quantum parameter remains at the exact \(2N\)-th root of unity. For every fixed strict Conway presentation described below, the invariant has a nonzero asymptotic on every fixed microscopic disk before the first ordinary-color resonance. Its logarithmic growth is the volume of the resulting knot complement. The proof keeps the whole finite quantum sum. It obtains a nonzero leading term by treating the Fourier variables for all filled circles together. The geometric input is the original strict augmented geometry, its marked deformation and its smooth long fillings. The resulting volume is the volume of the knot complement after the auxiliary crossing circles have been filled; the knot cusp itself remains unfilled. ## 1. The presentations and the theorem Start with one fixed literal closed Conway construction in ordered products, physical quarter-turns and the original crossing-circle leaves. Its endpoint orders, knot pattern and local disk framings are fixed. Assume its positive wire domain has a strict state: original leaf parameters lie in \((0,1/2)\), and each retained multiplication gate satisfies \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. \tag{1} \] Only the forced final flat gate is deleted, with its exact complementary-index relation retained. The original geometric construction then gives a complete augmented exterior with a unique strict positive source optimizer. We retain the original knot/component qualifications; in particular the strict two-leaf knot case includes a pure leaf, rather than the two-odd-leaf link pattern. Group consecutive multiplications with no intervening turn into a product junction. Each edge of the resulting tree carries a physical quarter-turn. A junction containing an original crossing-circle operator is called a circle junction; a junction containing none is called bare. The theorem allows every finite connected group of bare junctions, with arbitrary valences at least three. There is no additional condition on their adjacency, number of attached branches, or path lengths. The [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) proves the estimate that permits this scope. For a fixed component, let \(\Omega_{\mathcal U}\) be its positive complete action after closing its output with the norm comparison. Replacing its moving multiplication tensors by complete tensors leaves a remainder \(E_{\mathcal U,N}\) satisfying \[ \|E_{\mathcal U,N}\|_{\mathcal J} \le \exp\{N(\Omega_{\mathcal U}-\eta_{\mathcal U}+o(1))\}, \qquad \eta_{\mathcal U}>0. \tag{2} \] Here \(\mathcal J\) measures both values and first derivatives at the complete polynomial roots. The estimate retains the deformed edge factors and boundary arrays. It is a conclusion of the component proof, not an extra hypothesis on the presentation. The positive action uses \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x). \tag{3} \] The proof of (2) compares whole finite contractions. Reflecting one index in an error term can remove a turn in a positive comparison tree, whose pressure is no larger than the original pressure. These comparison trees do not replace the original diagram in the invariant or the geometric volume calculation. At circle \(i\), retain the original parity representative \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) and fill that auxiliary cusp with the integer disk-filling coefficient \(p_i\). The remaining physical crossing power is exactly \[ n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i. \tag{4} \] Thus all allowed \(n_i\) have their prescribed parity. The resulting knot is denoted by \(K_{\mathbf n}\). Every auxiliary circle is filled in this statement; the main knot cusp stays unfilled. There is a single constant \(B\), depending on the fixed strict presentation and its original knot/parity conventions, such that the following holds whenever all the fixed signed integers \(n_i\) satisfy \(|n_i|\ge B\). Their signs are independent, and no ratio between their absolute values is bounded. They and the presentation are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The constant \(B\) is independent of the subsequently chosen radius \(0\le R<1\). Put \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\). Let \(F_N(M)\) be the actual zero-framed reduced ADO invariant of \(K_{\mathbf n}\), in the marked coordinate \(M\), with unknot value one. Section 2 fixes this normalization. The exact scalar from the original finite compiler is \[ A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_i n_i, \] where \(w(D)\) is the oriented writhe of the filled diagram, and each \(n_i\) uses the original checked-braid convention. Then, uniformly for \(|s|\le R<1\), through both even and odd levels, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)} =A_N(s)H_N(s)\bigl(1+O_{\mathbf n,R}(N^{-1})\bigr), \qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\quad H_N(0)=1.} \tag{5} \] The denominator \(F_N(1)\) is nonzero for every sufficiently large level. The right side is also uniformly nonzero on the stated disk for large \(N\). Moreover, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \sup_{|s|\le R} \left|\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|F_N(q_N^s)| -\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathbf n})\right| \longrightarrow0.} \tag{6} \] The starting level and the error constants may depend on the fixed integers \(\mathbf n\) and on \(R\). The threshold \(B\) does not. There is a precise first correction after the exact scalar factors are divided out. If \(x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}\) is the generally complex normalized label of physical edge \(e\) at the selected filled joint saddle, then \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)} {F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}) +O_{\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}). \tag{7} \] The sum is over the physical turn edges, not the artificial edges introduced when resolving a bare product into binary gates. It is evaluated at the filled saddle, not at the complete augmented optimizer. The [preferred-longitude calculation](actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) identifies the full first correction geometrically. In the meridian-longitude basis of the knot complement, let \(\tau_K\) be the translation of the preferred longitude when the meridian translates by one. Then \[ \tau_K=a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}). \tag{7a} \] Combining (7a) with the exact scalar above gives \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =1+\frac{\pi i s^2\tau_K}{2N} +O_{\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}).} \tag{7b} \] This is also the normalized profile of the full modified-trace invariant, by (12). The geometric identity (7a) and the asymptotic (7b) now apply to the same strict-tree class under the stated long-twist hypotheses. Neither statement identifies a classical \(A\)-polynomial factor. ## 2. The actual invariant and its scalar factors Set \(d=N-1\). The actual color module has highest weight \(\alpha=d+s\), with highest-root coordinate \(x=q_N^\alpha\). The marked meridian is \[ M=-q_Nx=q_N^s. \tag{8} \] In particular \(s=0\) is the complete marked value \(M=1\), not \(M=-1\). Use the original finite quantum-group crossing, pivotal matrix \(K^{1-N}\), and ribbon twist \[ \theta_\alpha =q_N^{(\alpha^2+2(1-N)\alpha)/2}. \tag{9} \] The reduced \((1,1)\)-tangle scalar, corrected to zero framing, is \(F_N(M)\). It is equivalently the full modified-trace ADO invariant divided by its modified dimension. It is not obtained by dividing an already reduced cut scalar a second time. The exact source comparison in [the exact ADO normalization](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) gives \[ F_N(1)=K_N(K_{\mathbf n}), \tag{10} \] where \(K_N\) is the original reduced enhanced Kashaev invariant. The quotient and its framing equality are valid for knots at both parities. The full modified-trace invariant, denoted here by \(\mathcal N_N(M)\), is \[ \mathcal N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M),\qquad d_N(M)=\eta_N\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}}, \quad \eta_N=i^{N+3}. \tag{11} \] Whole-germ evaluation gives \[ d_N(1)=\frac{\eta_N}{N},\qquad \frac{d_N(q_N^s)}{d_N(1)}=\frac1{H_N(s)}. \tag{12} \] Thus the single factor \(H_N\) in the reduced profile (5) is canceled, exactly, in the profile of the full modified-trace invariant. Both normalizations have the same logarithmic volume on the disk. No numerator or denominator of (11) is separately set to zero. Here is the ledger defining \(A_N\). Fix the actual six-type compiler and its original reference carriers once. In lower-index convention an edge has the exact propagator \[ (T_e\mathbf J)_{ab} =\mathbf1_{a=b}\,\gamma_{e,N}(s) \frac{H_N(s)}{W_a(s)},\qquad W_a(s)=\prod_{r=1}^a \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right), \quad \mathbf J_{ab}=\mathbf1_{a+b=d}. \tag{13} \] The factor \(\gamma_{e,N}\) is the specified typed scalar, a power of \(q_N^{s^2/2}\) or one. It is not included again in a vertex or in the closing factor. At an equal-color circle vertex the actual grid parameter is \(\sigma_i(s)=s\) or \(-s\). The full crossing-power scalar is \[ C_{N,n_i}(\sigma)=q_N^{n_i(d^2/4-\sigma^2/2)},\qquad \frac{C_{N,n_i}(\sigma_i(s))}{C_{N,n_i}(0)} =q_N^{-n_i\sigma_i(s)^2/2}. \tag{14} \] At an opposite-color vertex the Casimir relation is constant and the grid parameter is zero. Denote its exact fixed-power reference factor, divided by its value at \(s=0\), by \(\rho_{i,N}^{(n_i)}(s)\). This is computed by the prescribed crossing word and reference map. The derivation below gives its exact floor or ceiling exponent, according to the starting order of the two strands, including negative powers. A change from an original negative-odd reference is made once, before this factor is entered in the ledger. Let \(\zeta_N(s)\) contain only the remaining original closing, pivotal and zero-framing scalar. All local edge and crossing/reference factors just described are excluded from it. This scalar is fixed by the finite source compiler before any asymptotic is taken; it is not defined by dividing the answer by a proposed profile. A root reference factor placed outside the vertex ledger must be assigned explicitly to \(\zeta_N\), and then omitted from \(\rho\). With normalized \(\gamma_{e,N}(0)=\rho_{i,N}^{(n_i)}(0)=1\), set \[ \boxed{\displaystyle A_N(s)=\frac{\zeta_N(s)}{\zeta_N(0)} \prod_e\gamma_{e,N}(s) \prod_{i\text{ equal}}q_N^{-n_i\sigma_i(s)^2/2} \prod_{i\text{ opposite}}\rho_{i,N}^{(n_i)}(s).} \tag{15} \] If a convention does not normalize an individual reference to one at completeness, its complete-value ratio is used in (15). No factor is then counted twice. The packet and joint-transform notes abbreviate the closing and opposite-reference product by \(\widehat\zeta_N=\zeta_N\prod_{i\text{ opposite}}\rho_{i,N}^{(n_i)}\), and reserve \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}\) for \(\prod_e\gamma_{e,N}\). Formula (15) writes the same factors separately. Using \(\widehat\zeta_N\) therefore removes the separate \(\rho\)-product from that formula; it does not add another copy. For example, a zero-framing correction of writhe \(w\) has the exact ratio \(q_N^{-ws^2/2}\), since \(\theta_{d+s}=q_N^{(s^2-d^2)/2}\). This is one part of the ledger, not a reason to discard any other prescribed closing factor. The finite ledger consists of known nonzero elementary phases and monomials, with only polynomial level factors in the absolute complete normalization. In particular \[ \log|\zeta_N(0)|=o(N),\qquad \sup_{|s|\le R} \left|\log\left|\frac{\zeta_N(s)}{\zeta_N(0)}\right|\right| =o(N). \tag{16} \] These bounds follow from the original scalar formulas. The [exact scalar calculation](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) simplifies their complete product: \[ A_N(s)=q_N^{[-w(D)-\sum_i n_i]s^2/2}. \tag{16f} \] It proves the cancellation of all intermediate turn factors and the remaining closing factor separately. Thus \(A_N(s)\to1\) uniformly on each fixed microscopic disk. Keeping its first term is necessary for (7b): it supplies the integer part of the preferred cusp shape. ### Why mixed-order products have no missing crossing factor The reference maps used to encode a tangle must be distinguished from physical crossings. Write \(A=V_x\otimes V_y\), \(B=V_y\otimes V_x\), where \(x=-q_N^{-1}q_N^s\) and \(y=-q_N^{-1}q_N^{-s}\). These are the two possible orders of opposite colors. Both use the constant Casimir relation. Let \(r_0\) be the full complete checked-crossing polynomial, including its Cartan scalar and its first-normal coefficients at repeated roots. It is an invertible polynomial element of that relation. The [actual Newton compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md), §4 (16b)–(18), chooses \[ G_A=I,\qquad G_B=\check R_{x,y}r_0(\Omega_A)^{-1},\qquad C_{D,C}=G_DG_C^{-1}. \tag{16a} \] Thus a morphism from object \(C\) to object \(D\) has coordinates \(C_{D,C}f(\Omega_C)\). The Casimir is natural under these intertwiners. For compatible \(X:C\to D\), \(Y:D\to E\), one has exactly \[ \bigl(C_{E,D}g(\Omega_D)\bigr) \bigl(C_{D,C}f(\Omega_C)\bigr) =C_{E,C}(gf)(\Omega_C). \tag{16b} \] This is why serial composition is polynomial multiplication. The inverse map in (16a) is the true coherent inverse, not a positive reverse crossing. The [physical turn calculation](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md), §3 (41)–(42), proves the full monodromy identity \[ \check R_{y,x}\check R_{x,y} =q_N^{-s^2}r_0(\Omega_A)^2,\qquad G':=\check R_{y,x}r_0(\Omega_B)^{-1} =q_N^{-s^2}G_B^{-1}. \tag{16c} \] The proof retains the coefficients at repeated roots: perturb the sum of the two highest weights to separate the channels, compare the physical monodromy there, and continue the polynomial identity using the nondegenerate moment pairing. Thus (16c) is not only an equality at distinct eigenvalues. After the coherent reference map is removed, the four signed mixed crossings have the following polynomials. | Starting order | Physical crossing | Target order | Polynomial | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \(A\) | \(\check R_{x,y}\) | \(B\) | \(r_0\) | | \(B\) | \(\check R_{y,x}\) | \(A\) | \(q_N^{-s^2}r_0\) | | \(A\) | \(\check R_{y,x}^{-1}\) | \(B\) | \(q_N^{s^2}r_0^{-1}\) | | \(B\) | \(\check R_{x,y}^{-1}\) | \(A\) | \(r_0^{-1}\) | In particular two positive crossings retain the polynomial \(q_N^{-s^2}r_0^2\). That polynomial is not a carrier that can be canceled. Conversely, no extra \(r_0^2\) should be inserted after multiplying the two displayed polynomials. For an arbitrary signed word, every crossing swaps the order, irrespective of its sign. If its signs are \(\delta_j\in\{1,-1\}\) and its net exponent is \(n=\sum_j\delta_j\), summing the scalar exponents in the table gives \[ f_{\mathrm{word},A}=q_N^{-\lfloor n/2\rfloor s^2}r_0^n, \qquad f_{\mathrm{word},B}=q_N^{-\lceil n/2\rceil s^2}r_0^n. \tag{16d} \] For example, for a word of length \(L\) starting at \(A\), the exponent of \(q_N^{s^2}\) is \((L-n)/2-\lfloor L/2\rfloor=-\lfloor n/2\rfloor\). Starting at \(B\) replaces the floor of \(L/2\) by its ceiling. This also proves (16d) for negative \(n\), and for alternating positive and negative odd blocks. The extra scalar when two odd blocks meet is precisely the carry in the floor of their sum. These are the explicit values of \(\rho^{(n)}\) for the stated reference orders. The original turn table already includes the scalar correction between \(G'\) and \(G_B^{-1}\); it must not be applied a second time. A product junction is lowered using its compatible reverse morphism. Its carrier product then closes to the identity. For instance, \[ C_{A,C}h(\Omega_C)\, C_{C,B}g(\Omega_B)\, C_{B,A}f(\Omega_A)=(hgf)(\Omega_A). \tag{16e} \] Its normalized pivotal trace is therefore \(\phi_\sigma(hgf)\), with the actual common cut scalar retained separately. The same cancellation holds at every valence. Crossing polynomials such as \(r_0^n\) remain inside this trace. This construction is applied to the original typed expression first. Each turn is reconstructed as an actual morphism, curried by the prescribed dualities, and expressed again using (16a). After lowering all vertices, changing the evaluation root only reassociates the same finite tensor contraction, retaining each original edge tensor \(T_e\mathbf J\) and its scalar \(\gamma_e\). It does not create a new untyped physical word. If a reversed edge is described using another forward turn type, the already known ratio of its two typed scalars is kept. Finally, the actual cylindrical closing cut leaves an endomorphism of its ordered two-strand object; an alternative cap closure retains its physical closing turn first. Its carrier is \(C_{A,A}=I\), so the compiler's partial pivotal trace gives exactly the single factor \(H_N\). This verifies the product and closing conventions used in (15), including their repeated-root data. It asserts no isotopy exchanging arbitrary tangles. ## 3. From the whole finite source to one grouped wire packet The same fixed complete Newton basis is used at the moving main meridian: \[ e_k(z)=\frac{\prod_{a=0}^{k-1}(c_a-z)}{S_k^2}, \quad c_a=2\cos\frac{(2a+1)\pi}{N}, \quad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k2\sin\frac{\pi a}{N}, \quad 0\le k\le d. \tag{17} \] Its first-normal coefficients at repeated Casimir roots are part of the algebra. They are not discarded when the main color moves. The exact metric remains \(\phi_s(e_a e_b)=\mathbf1_{a+b=d}\); a physical turn consequently gives the equal-label edge (13). The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md), Sections 3–7, separates an outgoing branch into a contraction of complete tensors and a remainder with a strict loss in its full spectral norm. The complete contraction keeps the actual deformed edge factors, low boundary arrays and every internal index in the complete support. A decorated turn converts an incoming spectral error into the required low/high coefficient bounds. The component comparison then carries that loss through all internal turns by homogeneity in the boundary constants. It does not impose a new loss budget at each junction. The new local ingredient is the [reflected Fourier estimate](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md). In the difference between a moving and a complete trace, the first Fourier term cancels. With one high index, the remaining terms are bounded by a complete tensor with that index reflected. Exact fusion turns this into a positive comparison tree. With several high indices, the [half-boundary comparison](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md) supplies a complete boundary state instead. A strict Fourier or boundary loss controls every nonempty correction pattern. These estimates also apply when the circle operator is the actual fixed power \(R_s^{n_i}\). Every fixed power and its inverse have polynomial spectral norm on \(|s|\le R<1\), with constants depending on the fixed power. For a low product \(E=\prod e_{k_a}\), its raw shifted-grid trace satisfies \[ |\phi_\sigma(R_\sigma^{n_i}E)| \le C_{\mathbf n,R}N\,\phi_0(L_NE). \tag{18} \] The comparison uses the complete pure circle tensor on the right, not an absolute filled state sum. It follows from positivity of the Laurent coefficients of the low basis factors, the actual shifted root grid and the bounded full chirp on its \(O(N^{-1})\) height. The exact complete node sum gives \[ \phi_0(L_NE)\ge N(\pi/4)^{\deg_{\mathrm{factors}}E}E(-2). \tag{19} \] The odd-level constant can be replaced by one. The even constant comes from the actual nearest-node ratio and is uniform up to the low endpoints. Holomorphic continuation of the whole trace includes its removable collisions. Let \(F_0\) be the maximum of the original complete positive action, so \(2\pi F_0=\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\) for the augmented exterior with crossing circles unfilled. The general component theorem controls the grouped corrections, high boundary contributions and the complement of the strict original window with a fixed loss below \(F_0\). The [complete-edge theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md) puts every physical internal label of a bare component strictly below half, except when the entire component consists of two trivalent junctions with two rigid branches at each. Its one internal label is exactly half. Every circle-incident label is in a compact subinterval of \((0,1/2)\). Hidden unturned indices used to resolve products retain their full strict intervals. At a nonexceptional bare junction, the regular low trace theorem gives \[ \phi_\sigma\left(\prod e_{k_a}\right) =\phi_0\left(\prod e_{k_a}\right) (1+O_R(e^{-\kappa N})). \tag{20} \] The incident labels are compactly inside the low range and their sum is greater than one. In the exceptional two-junction component, both tensors are cubic. On their old support the degree of \(e_i e_j e_k\) is less than \(2N-1\); division by \(P_0+\Delta_\sigma\) therefore leaves its top trace coefficient unchanged. Their moving and complete traces agree exactly, including indices crossing half in the retained neighborhood. The general component comparison includes the local replacements (20). Together with (18) and localization of the positive binary-resolution variables, it gives one fixed source error \[ O\!\left(N^C e^{N(F_0-\eta_0)}\right), \qquad \eta_0>0. \tag{21} \] The loss is geometric or comes from a closed coefficient-rate inequality. It is independent of the sizes of the fixed \(n_i\) and of the compact radius \(R<1\); prefactors and the starting level may depend on them. The summed high-state estimate is grouped through actual modules. It is not an absolute bound on every individual return term of a resolved quotient product. After these exact reductions, introduce one angular variable \(\tau_i\) at every original circle. Before its crossing trace is applied, the finite packet is \[ B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s)= \sum_{\mathbf k/N\in\mathcal W} \prod_{g\text{ bare}}\mu_{N,g}(\mathbf k) \prod_{i\text{ circle}}\prod_{e\sim i} e_{k_e}(-2\cos\tau_i) \prod_e\gamma_{e,N}(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_{k_e}(s)}. \tag{22} \] The source fixes every index and every \(d=N-1\) offset. The box \(\mathcal W\) is an actual primitive integer box. There are no chirps or sine trace factors in \(B_N\). It is exactly even in each angle. ## 4. The finite packet, rather than a real-grid approximation The [grouped wire-packet theorem](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) constructs (22) directly. A complete bare vertex of valence \(D\) has \(D-2\) nontrivial positive multiplication coefficients and \(D-3\) hidden integers; its last output is \(d\) minus the closing incident index. Along with the physical edge labels, these give \[ K=E+\sum_{\mathrm{bare}\ v}(D_v-3) \tag{23} \] independent integers, with no parity-dependent lattice density. This is not the uncontracted count \(2H-3\), since the circle vertices have already been collapsed. The canonical Gamma-product interpolation of the sine factorials is used in every original bare coefficient and every Newton evaluation. It is zero-free in the needed bulk strips, has the exact shift \(G_N(z+1)/G_N(z)=2\sin(\pi(z+1)/N)\), and retains every finite integer offset. In particular \[ \frac{H_N(s)}{W_{Nx}(s)} \quad\text{has the specified continuation}\quad \frac{G_N(Nx)^2}{G_N(Nx-s)G_N(Nx+s)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N}\cot(\pi x)+O_R(N^{-2}). \tag{24} \] The notation on the left means the physical ratio at integer \(Nx\), with the right side its chosen analytic continuation. At zero angles, eliminating the hidden positive circle variables from the original constrained action gives exactly the action in (22). The remaining bare gate Hessians and the circle functions \(g\) make its primitive wire Hessian negative definite. This proves a unique strict grouped optimizer at the same original value \(F_0\). It is not a sum of independently maximized boundary budgets. The exact finite-lattice residue formula with cotangent kernels moves the primitive wire sum to its holomorphic saddle. Its half-grid vertical boundaries, nonzero cotangent modes and all endpoint connectors have fixed source losses. Thus, on one fixed complex angular polydisk, \[ B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s) =N^\nu\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}(s) a(\boldsymbol\tau)e^{N\Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)} (1+O_R(N^{-1})), \quad \nu=\frac32(1-H),\quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}=\prod_e\gamma_{e,N}. \tag{25} \] Here \(a\) is nonzero, the relative error is uniformly holomorphic, and both \(a\) and \(\Psi\) are separately even. At the complete saddle, \[ \Psi(0)=F_0,\qquad \Psi''(0)=-\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_H), \qquad a_i=\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{e\sim i}\tan(\pi x_e^*)>0. \tag{26} \] The mixed wire-angle derivatives vanish at zero by exact evenness, so eliminating the wires produces no off-diagonal Hessian correction there. The same exact finite packet has a raw-product bound on a strip around the entire real angular cube: \[ |B_N(\mathbf t+i\mathbf y,s)| \le N^C \exp N\{F_0-c\|\mathbf t\|^2+C'\|\mathbf y\|^2\}. \tag{27} \] It includes \(O(N^{-1})\) endpoint translations and fixed derivatives on smaller strips. Near zero this follows from the regular analytic Newton product; away from zero, strict circular rearrangement gives a fixed angular loss that absorbs the uniform logarithmic Riemann-sum error. It does not assert that an arbitrary quotient product or turn preserves a Gaussian. This real-spectator bound is what permits one circle contour to be treated while all others stay on their original grids or real integration paths. ## 5. All Fourier charges are compared at one joint saddle The [direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md) retains the actual operator and its contour. For an equal-color vertex its exact eigenvalue at \[ \tau_r(\sigma)=\frac{2\pi}{N}(d/2+\sigma-r) \tag{28} \] is \(C_{N,n}(\sigma)e^{inN\tau_r(\sigma)^2/(4\pi)}\). The root trace is continued as a whole through its collisions. A translated rectangle keeps the vertical sides halfway between the original grid poles. Pairing its positive and negative Fourier terms gives coefficients \[ \eta^{\ell-1}U_{\ell-1}(\cos2\pi\sigma), \qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad \ell\ge1. \tag{29} \] The first coefficient is exactly one. The sine in the trace makes the zero Fourier integral odd; its endpoint currents are retained and estimated, rather than dropped. Opposite-color vertices use \(\sigma=0\), with their separate reference factors still present. Choose one sufficiently small number \(t_0>0\). At circle \(i\), retain charges \(1\le\ell_i\le L_i=\lfloor t_0|n_i|\rfloor\) and use horizontal height \(y_i=A_0t_0/|n_i|\), with \(A_0\) sufficiently small. The global bound (27) makes every omitted charge lose a fixed amount, not merely \(O(n_i^{-2})\), from \(F_0\). On a translated vertical side the exact kernel is only \(O(N)\); its chirp cost is \(O(Nt_0)\), absorbed by the fixed angular endpoint loss. Remove these tails by the exact telescoping product of the coordinate trace functionals. While a tail is removed at circle \(i\), all spectators remain on real integrals or on their physical \(O(N^{-1})\)-translated grids. Their fixed-power chirps have bounded modulus there. Consequently no estimate introduces a positive exponential cost involving a different, much larger slope. The divided formulas are initially estimated on parameter circles avoiding the displayed sine denominator; the maximum principle is then applied to the whole holomorphic difference, restoring all collision values and every compact disk \(R<1\). The [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md) now compares every remaining charge on the same branch. After the finite reduction, a charge vector has joint action \[ \mathcal T_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\tau) =\Psi(\boldsymbol\tau) +\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_i n_i\tau_i^2 -i\sum_i\ell_i\tau_i. \tag{30} \] Set \(\varepsilon_i=1/n_i\) and \(t_i=\ell_i/n_i\). Its selected critical equation is \[ \tau_i=2\pi t_i+ 2\pi i\varepsilon_i\Psi_i(\boldsymbol\tau). \tag{31} \] The implicit-function theorem gives one branch on a fixed polydisk in \((\mathbf t,\boldsymbol\varepsilon)\), with no relation between the different \(\varepsilon_i\). At this branch complete the square. The critical action is a purely imaginary term \(-i\pi\sum t_i^2/\varepsilon_i\) plus an analytic function \(\mathcal W(\mathbf t,\boldsymbol\varepsilon)\), even in each \(t_i\). At \(\boldsymbol\varepsilon=0\), it is \(\Psi(2\pi\mathbf t)\). Hence (26), on a smaller fixed polydisk, implies \[ \Re\mathcal T_{\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\tau_{\boldsymbol\ell}) \le\Re\mathcal T_{\mathbf1}(\boldsymbol\tau_{\mathbf1}) -\sum_i\frac{\pi^2a_i}{n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1). \tag{32} \] This compares each charge with the same joint filled action. It does not compare a tiny local alias loss with the total complete-to-filled volume drop. Separate evenness also writes \(\Psi_i=\tau_iQ_i(\boldsymbol\tau^2)\), with \(\Re Q_i<0\) near zero. Therefore \[ \tau_{\boldsymbol\ell,i} =\frac{2\pi t_i} {1-2\pi i\varepsilon_iQ_i(\boldsymbol\tau_{\boldsymbol\ell}^2)}, \qquad \Im\tau_{\boldsymbol\ell,i}<0,\qquad |\Im\tau_{\boldsymbol\ell,i}| \le C|t_i|/|n_i|. \tag{33} \] These componentwise heights control the endpoint connectors even for independently unequal signed slopes. Every \(\tau_{\boldsymbol\ell,i}\) is nonzero, so the trace amplitude \(\prod_i\sin\tau_i\) is nonzero at the saddle. The real part of the angular Hessian on its translated real tangent plane remains negative definite; the chirp contributes only a purely imaginary Hessian. The finite wire packet is holomorphic on the contour before this translation, so its uniform error in (25) can be integrated with the Gaussian estimate. The resulting first-charge amplitude is nonzero. Every other retained charge is exponentially smaller by (32). The fixed errors from (21), the high-charge tails and the real angular complement are absorbed by taking all \(|n_i|\) sufficiently large: the real first-charge action tends to \(F_0\) uniformly as \(\max_i|1/n_i|\to0\). This proves directly, at completeness, an asymptotic of the form \[ F_N(1) =\zeta_N(0) \left(\prod_i q_N^{n_i d^2/4}\right) N^{3/2}D_{\mathbf n}\, e^{N\mathcal T_{\mathbf1}(\boldsymbol\tau_{\mathbf1})} (1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})), \qquad D_{\mathbf n}\ne0, \tag{34} \] with any fixed complete reference constants retained in the chosen closing ledger. The \(N^{3/2}\) power is the grouped count \(\nu+3H/2\). Formula (34), rather than an earlier quantum volume theorem, supplies eventual nonvanishing and the lower exponential bound at both parities. The choices of windows, \(t_0\), structural gaps and geometric reciprocal-slope neighborhood depend only on the fixed source. They determine one lower bound \(B\) for every \(|n_i|\). The radius \(R\) changes only the bounded trace coefficients, prefactors and starting level. Thus \(B\) is independent of \(R<1\). A geometric bound stated originally in \(|p_i|\) is included by increasing \(B\), since \(|p_i|\ge(|n_i|-1)/2\). ## 6. The full action is the original marked filling action It remains to identify the action in (34), including its linear term and its primitive marking. Let \(\mathbf y\) be the grouped wire variables, \(M_{\mathrm{bare}}(\mathbf y)\) the sum of their complete bare-gate actions, and \[ b_i(\mathbf y,\tau_i) =\sum_{e\sim i}b(x_e(\mathbf y),\tau_i) \tag{35} \] the even Newton angular action at circle \(i\). Before eliminating wires, the original selected auxiliary-color source has local action \[ \mathfrak f_{\epsilon_i}(\mathbf y,\chi_i) =\operatorname{stat}_{\tau_i} \left[ b_i(\mathbf y,\tau_i) +\frac{i\epsilon_i\tau_i^2}{4\pi} +i\chi_i\tau_i\right]. \tag{36} \] The identity is the [actual regular circle-source branch](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), with its original chirp and shear. It is not a quadratic approximation. The auxiliary Fourier transform adds \(2\pi i\chi_i z_i\), so stationarity in \(\chi_i\) imposes \(\tau_i=-2\pi z_i\). Evenness of \(b_i\) gives \[ b_i(\mathbf y,2\pi z_i)+i\pi\epsilon_i z_i^2. \tag{37} \] The original filling term is \(-2\pi i(p_i z_i^2+z_i)\). Substituting (4) and now writing \(\tau_i=2\pi z_i\), the entire expression is exactly \[ b_i(\mathbf y,\tau_i) +\frac{in_i\tau_i^2}{4\pi}-i\tau_i. \tag{38} \] Adding the unchanged bare actions and imposing the common wire stationarity gives (30) with charge \(\mathbf1\). Holomorphic uniqueness near the complete state shows that the two elimination orders select the same branch and the same additive constant. For clarity, the peripheral variables here belong to the auxiliary crossing circles, not to the microscopic main meridian \(M\). In the original marked convention, \[ U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i,\qquad V_i=-2\,\partial_{\chi_i}\Phi_\epsilon. \tag{39} \] The Fourier stationarity gives \(V_i=4\pi iz_i\), and filling stationarity gives \(\chi_i-2p_i z_i=1\). Therefore \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i. \tag{40} \] The sign and primitive coefficient in (40) are retained. They ensure a single \(2\pi\) angular turn in the completed solid-torus collar. The geometric input is [the marked strict-tree geometry](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), §6 (18)–(20) and §7 (22)–(23), with the smooth-completion argument in [the source regulator and metric completion](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). Its absolute regulator and actual cusp marking give \[ 2\pi\,\Re\mathcal T_{\mathbf1} (\boldsymbol\tau_{\mathbf1}) =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathbf n}). \tag{41} \] Only the auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled. The main knot cusp remains complete and unfilled. This is an identification with the actual hyperbolic metric on the knot exterior, not just with a formal representation or a relative volume. No quantum lower bound is used in this geometric step. ## 7. The profile, its correction, and the uniform logarithmic limit The first charge coefficient in (29) is one for every parameter and every level parity. Consequently its only main-meridian dependence outside the wire insertion consists of the exact crossing/reference phases in (14)–(15). All other charges and all fixed currents are exponentially smaller, uniformly on each \(|s|\le R<1\), after the single choice of \(B\). The wire packet contains the product of (24). Its exact normalized finite-contour insertion has the expansion \[ \frac{B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s)} {\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}(s)B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,0)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e(\boldsymbol\tau)) +O_R(N^{-2}) \tag{42} \] on a fixed complex angular neighborhood. This statement comes from the canonical Gamma interpolation and the same finite lattice contour; it is not extrapolated from grid values. Apply the analytic Gaussian insertion rule once more at the joint first-charge saddle. For a holomorphic function \(c\), its normalized Gaussian expectation is \(c\) at the saddle plus \(O(N^{-1})\): the linear term is odd, and the first surviving corrections cost \(N^{-1}\). Applied to the coefficient already multiplied by \(N^{-1}\) in (42), this gives an \(O(N^{-2})\) remainder. The common first-order saddle correction in numerator and denominator cancels. This proves (7), with all scalars in \(A_N\) and the single cut factor \(H_N\) retained exactly. Its weaker form is (5). For fixed \(R<1\), \(H_N\) and its inverse are uniformly bounded, and \[ H_N(s)\longrightarrow\frac{\sin\pi s}{\pi s} \tag{43} \] uniformly on the disk, including the value one at zero. The limit has no zero there. The same is true of the elementary nonzero factors after their known phases are retained, with subexponential bounds as in (16). Equation (34) and the geometric equality (41) give the logarithmic rate at \(s=0\); (5) transfers it uniformly to the entire fixed disk, proving (6). Uniform holomorphy on a slightly larger compact disk also gives the corresponding fixed-derivative estimates for the normalized profiles. The variable \(z=2\pi i s\) converts (7)'s residual term to \[ \frac{z^2}{4\pi N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}). \tag{44} \] The exact scalar contributes \(a(D)z^2/(8\pi iN)\). The [geometric longitude theorem](actual_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.md) identifies its sum with (44) as \(\tau_Kz^2/(8\pi iN)\), proving (7b). The two calculations are independent: the quantum calculation fixes the scalar, and the geometric calculation follows the actual longitude through the face pairings and disk fillings. The reduced ratio consequently tends to \(\sin(\pi s)/(\pi s)\) without an additional scalar normalization. The normalized full modified-trace invariant tends to one. ## 8. What this theorem does and does not extend The [complete-value volume theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and the present moving-meridian theorem apply to the same fixed strict literal Conway trees, with their knot and long-filling hypotheses. The present result additionally gives a uniform complex profile, nonvanishing and the preferred-cusp correction. The earlier singleton, path and trivalent arguments remain valid special cases of the general component comparison. The disk restriction is essential. The present proof treats \(|s|\le R<1\); it does not cross the first ordinary-color resonances \(s=\pm1\), where the reduced ordinary-color anchor and the full modified dimension have different behavior. The removable same-color Casimir collisions within this disk are included by the full physical source. A zero-free microscopic disk is also not a fixed open disk in the \(M\)-plane. There is no remaining bare-component valence or path restriction. The filling integers must still be fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity and sufficiently long in the stated strict presentation. The theorem does not extend the ordinary-color-subtracted remainder through its resonance divisors, or identify a selected classical main-meridian \(A\)-factor. Those are separate problems. ## 9. The proof route The [exact ADO normalization](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) fixes the invariant, the coordinate \(M=-qx\), and the modified dimension. The [oriented source compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) and [physical quarter-turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) give its polynomial coordinates, compatible reference maps, full normal coefficients and original closing trace. The global estimate uses [source growth near the complete main meridian](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) for the physical leaf and decorated-turn inputs, and the [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) for every connected group of bare junctions.
