Its [Fourier lemma](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md) and [positive-pressure lemmas](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md) control the complete correction patterns without discarding their internal correlations. The [regular bare trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_bare_trace.md) then applies on the original strict low windows, with exact cubic equality in the two-junction exception. The local circle operators and their marked analytic continuation are established in the [regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md). The [direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md) keeps the actual filled crossing power, rather than substituting a complete-color expansion. The [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) supplies the exact finite lattice and its complex contour. The [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md) retains all Fourier charges until their common saddle has been compared; it supplies the nonzero lower bound used here. The [general core action](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md) and [strict-mask complete geometry](actual_conway_general_strict_mask_geometry.md) provide the original strict optimizer and augmented metric. The [marked geometric deformation](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), §§6–7, and [metric-completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) identify the selected long-filling action with the volume of the actual knot complement. The earlier quantum volume limit is not used as an analytic lower-bound input in this route. ## 10. Net twists and other Conway closures The same intrinsic conclusions hold for the presentations admitted by the [ordered net-twist reduction](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) and the [arbitrary-closure reduction](actual_conway_arbitrary_closure_volume.md). These reductions use actual ambient isotopies of the tangles, including the recorded endpoint orders and rotations. A net twist is the signed sum attached to one surviving block of the original twist boxes; large opposite signs in that block can cancel. For a fixed ordered cylindrical input, apply its deterministic reduction. If the output is a strict knot presentation and every surviving net twist is sufficiently long, the uniform volume limit (6), nonvanishing, and intrinsic cusp expansion (7b) hold for the input knot. For an input with either the cylindrical or cap closure, zero net weights may also be removed by the prescribed topological reduction. If the input is hyperbolic and every surviving strict factor has sufficiently long net twists, the reduction theorem shows that exactly one strict knot factor remains and all other factors are unknots. The input is ambient isotopic to that strict knot. Here is why this transfers the whole meridian family. Orient the strict knot by the transported orientation of the input, and use zero framing on both. The reduced ADO invariant is the same Laurent family \(F_N(M)\) under this ambient isotopy, not merely the same value at \(M=1\). Any ribbon twist introduced in a diagram calculation is canceled by the full twist scalar at color \(d+s\). The meridian and the preferred zero-linking longitude are transported as well. The complete hyperbolic volume and the preferred cusp shape therefore agree. Applying (6) and (7b) to the strict representative proves those same formulas for the input. There are finitely many reduced outputs for a fixed input expression, including its parity and zero-weight branches. Take the maximum of their strict-presentation thresholds and of the hyperbolicity thresholds used in the topological reduction. This gives one net-twist threshold independent of the later radius \(R<1\). All net weights and their zero relations stay fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The presentation-dependent scalar \(a(D)\) and the individual physical-edge cotangents may be computed on the strict representative. No equality between the raw scalar ledgers, auxiliary circle sources, or augmented complements of two different presentations is needed. The transferred statements use the zero-framed invariant and the intrinsic preferred-cusp formula (7b).

text: # A classical characteristic selected by the microscopic meridian state The reduced ADO invariant is a function of a marked meridian eigenvalue \(M\). Its exact quantum recurrence compares the values at \(M,qM,q^2M,\ldots\). We prove that, for the knot classes specified below, the complete asymptotic expansion on the scale \(M=q_N^s\) selects one analytic curve in the classical symbol of every such recurrence. The curve is determined by the actual finite invariant and its original normalization. The selected curve passes through \((M,L)=(1,-1)\), has the preferred cusp shape as its logarithmic tangent, and is invariant under \((M,L)\mapsto(M^{-1},L^{-1})\). We also give a rational formula for its longitude coordinate in the original internal variables. The [circle-tree longitude theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md) and its [extension through unmarked product junctions](actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) identify this entire germ with the geometric meridian–longitude germ for all the full-source classes listed below. Together with this note, they give the selected geometric factor of every genuine classical symbol. The marked isotopies in the net-twist and closure reductions transfer the intrinsic conclusion to the corresponding original knots. Fix a knot admitting one of the following presentations, with its original endpoint orders, orientations and peripheral markings: * a strict ordered Conway presentation with independently long fixed filling powers, under the hypotheses of the [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md); * an ordered all-circle tree satisfying the [summed degree-and-twist criterion](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md), \(\sum_v d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le2^{-25}\); * an ordered all-circle tree satisfying the [local degree-and-twist criterion](actual_all_circle_local_message_volume.md), \(\max_v d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le2^{-120}\). In the last two cases \(d_v\) is the number of edges incident to vertex \(v\), and \(n_v\) is its signed integer crossing power. In particular \(L_{\mathrm{eff}}(1)=-1\). The inserted phase is even in \(t\), so uniqueness of the critical point gives \(X_*(t)=X_*(-t)\). Consequently the derivatives of the \(E_e\) contribute nothing to the first derivative of (31) at \(M=1\). With \(u=\log M\), \[ \left.\frac{d}{du} \log\frac{e^{2u}-E_e(u)}{1-e^{2u}E_e(u)} \right|_{u=0} =2\frac{1+E_e(0)}{1-E_e(0)} =2i\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}). \tag{32} \] Equation (32) recovers \(a(D)+2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}})=\tau_K\), and also checks the orientation of the candidate longitude. Every higher derivative is specified by the coupled modified equations and (31); none is supplied by this first-derivative check. ### 7.2. Explicit equations for an all-circle tree For the all-circle construction, there are no bare product vertices to resolve, so the modified critical equations have a particularly short finite form. Let \(e=vw\) be an original tree edge, with wire \(x_e\), and let \(\tau_v\) be the angular variable of the crossing trace at vertex \(v\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} b(x,\tau) &=\int_0^x\log(2\cos(2\pi r)+2\cos\tau)\,dr-2J(x),\\ E_e&=e^{2\pi i x_e},\qquad Q_v=e^{i\tau_v}. \end{aligned} \tag{33} \] The logarithm is initially the real one for \(0<x<1/2\), \(\tau=0\), and is continued on the selected regular chart. This is exactly the circle-incidence action from the [grouped packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md), (23)--(24), and the [all-circle edge calculation](actual_all_circle_curvature_filling_limit.md), Section 4. Up to a fixed additive constant independent of \(t\), the first-charge phase before stationary elimination is \[ \Phi_t(\mathbf x,\boldsymbol\tau)= \sum_{e=vw}\bigl[b(x_e,\tau_v)+b(x_e,\tau_w)+K(x_e,t)\bigr] +\sum_v\left(\frac{i n_v\tau_v^2}{4\pi}-i\tau_v\right) +\frac{\pi i\,a(D)}2t^2. \tag{34} \] The linear term \(-i\tau_v\) is the retained first Fourier charge. It must remain when selecting the logarithmic branch, although it will disappear from the exponentiated equations. Differentiating (33) first in \(x\) gives \[ \exp b_x =\frac{2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos\tau}{4\sin^2(\pi x)} =-\frac{(E+Q)(E+Q^{-1})}{(E-1)^2}. \tag{35} \] For the angular derivative, the change of variable \(y=\tan(\pi r)\) gives \[ b_\tau=-\frac1\pi \operatorname{artanh}\!\left(\tan(\tau/2)\tan(\pi x)\right), \qquad \exp(-2\pi b_\tau)=\frac{Q+E}{1+QE}. \tag{36} \] The branch of \(\operatorname{artanh}\) is zero at \(\tau=0\). To verify the second identity without a sign choice, substitute \(\tan(\tau/2)=-i(Q-1)/(Q+1)\) and \(\tan(\pi x)=-i(E-1)/(E+1)\) into \(\exp(2\operatorname{artanh}z)=(1+z)/(1-z)\). The wire equation is \(b_x(x_e,\tau_v)+b_x(x_e,\tau_w)+K_x(x_e,t)=0\). The two minus signs in (35) cancel. Using (30) therefore gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(E_e+Q_v)(E_e+Q_v^{-1}) (E_e+Q_w)(E_e+Q_w^{-1})\\ &\quad=(E_e-1)^2(1-E_eM^2)(1-E_e/M^2). \end{aligned} \tag{37} \] The edge equation is linear in the trace of its internal variable. Put \[ Z_e=E_e+E_e^{-1},\qquad B_v=Q_v+Q_v^{-1},\qquad D_M=M^2+M^{-2}. \tag{37a} \] Dividing (37) by \(E_e^2\) gives \[ (Z_e+B_v)(Z_e+B_w)=(Z_e-2)(Z_e-D_M). \] The quadratic terms cancel, leaving \[ Z_e=\frac{2D_M-B_vB_w}{B_v+B_w+D_M+2}. \tag{37b} \] The denominator is eight at the complete point and remains nonzero on the selected small-filling chart. The equation \(E_e^2-Z_eE_e+1=0\), with its chosen branch through \(E_e=i\) at completeness, recovers the original edge variable. This determines the internal variable by a quadratic equation with its original branch retained. The angular equation, with its first-charge mark, is \[ \sum_{e\ni v}b_\tau(x_e,\tau_v) +\frac{i n_v\tau_v}{2\pi}-i=0. \tag{38} \] Multiplication by \(-2\pi\) and exponentiation give \[ \prod_{e\ni v}\frac{Q_v+E_e}{1+Q_vE_e}=Q_v^{n_v}. \tag{39} \] In obtaining (39), the additive term \(-2\pi i\) has exponent one. Equation (38), rather than (39) alone, retains which Fourier charge was used. Equations (37), (39), and the longitude expression (31) are a finite rational system with parameter \(M\). Work on the original chart where their denominators are units, or equivalently clear denominators and saturate by those factors before taking the selected germ. The nondegenerate critical point and the continued logarithms choose one analytic solution through the original filled point. Exponentiation has other branches and cannot replace that choice. Eliminating the \(E_e,Q_v\) on this chosen germ gives the same \(L_{\mathrm{eff}}\) as (26), not a separately normalized polynomial curve. The [geometric longitude theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md) constructs those nonparabolic blocks, glues their ordered boundary representations, and proves that (31) is the preferred longitude. Its algebraic rigidity argument rules out a residual meridian factor beyond the stated framing monomial. The first-charge logarithms still select the filled geometric branch among the algebraic solutions. ### 7.3. Scope of the geometric identification The [marked Conway deformation](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), Section 3, has a leaf function \[ g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t), \qquad K(x,t)=g(x,t)-g(x,0). \tag{40} \] That equality of scalar functions does not identify their peripheral uses. In the existing leaf construction \(t\) is the hidden auxiliary-circle parameter. Section 5 of that note proves that every actual main meridian remains parabolic identically: the two adjacent white maps have the same derivative at their common corner. The [primitive collar calculation](actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) likewise identifies an auxiliary meridian and disk longitude. The preferred-cusp theorem computes a translation in their parabolic main peripheral commutant. None of these statements gives a main meridian with eigenvalue \(e^{\pi it}\) simply by substituting this \(t\) into its existing cells. The original marked braid source supplies a different nonparabolic construction. The [critical-correspondence theorem](marked_braid_holonomy.md), Sections 4--6, identifies its regular exponential critical scheme with framed knot representations with actual meridian eigenvalue \(M\). The [longitude-insertion theorem](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md), Sections 1--4, identifies its preferred longitude, full meridian gauge, and logarithmic action differential. The [actual geometric normal-period theorem](actual_geometric_normal_period.md), Sections 3--5, constructs the local geometric formal block of that braid scheme. Those results do not yet identify the grouped modified equations (30) with that particular critical block. The [strict-tree longitude theorem](actual_strict_tree_geometric_characteristic.md) now supplies the missing comparison at unmarked product junctions. It inserts a zero-crossing box with an auxiliary circle, proves the exact stationary elimination including its constant, and checks the full based boundary maps after meridian filling. Thus the whole geometric representation is recovered, including a possible half-angle fold. It does not infer the preferred longitude from agreement of the cusp tangent alone. The argument also does not claim a physical asymptotic formula for fixed \(M\ne1\), or for \(s\) growing with \(N\). The variable \(t\) in Section 4 is an auxiliary analytic parameter used to organize all fixed-\(s\) coefficients. The ordinary-color divisors remain in (2), (18)–(20). The translated charts in Section 2 stay away from those divisors; no uniform nonvanishing state across ordinary-color resonances has been asserted. For every full-source class listed at the start, the selected curve is therefore the geometric eigenvalue germ, and its irreducible Laurent factor divides the first nonzero classical symbol. The [directed all-orders theorem](actual_all_circle_directed_all_orders.md) now proves the needed expansion on shifted charts for every certificate of the [directed degree-and-twist theorem](actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md). Its additional cases therefore have the same selected geometric-factor conclusion. No equality with the full A-polynomial or with an entire annihilator ideal is claimed.

title: A finite matrix test for the microscopic main-meridian profile
status: Conditional uniform meridian profile and volume criterion
text: # A finite matrix test for the microscopic main-meridian profile The main meridian is the small loop linking the knot once. Write its eigenvalue as $M$, and let $f_N(Y)$, with $Y=M^2$, be the reduced ADO knot invariant at level $N$. The value $f_N(1)$ is the complete-color scalar. A volume theorem for that scalar does not by itself control $f_N$ when the meridian moves: zeros can approach $M=1$ at distance of order $1/N$. This note gives a conditional way to control the smaller deformation $Y=e^{z/N}$, with $z$ in a fixed complex disk. Its input is a specified difference operator obtained from the actual finite cut formula, together with the first variation of that same formula in the quantum parameter. Retaining this variation matters: the operator at the root of unity alone loses the central direction in which the meridian profile varies. The algebraic reduction proved below has a bounded size. The number of free central coordinates is at most the fixed shift order of the operator, and the actual cut formula bounds their Laurent degrees independently of $N$. The first variation therefore gives a linear system with a bounded number of rows and columns. A uniform lower bound for its smallest singular value, together with an explicit condition on the reconstruction frame, implies boundedness of the normalized regular meridian profile. An alternative criterion uses a regular-singular differential equation and finitely many resonance tests. Under either criterion, the regular remainder and the reduced invariant have the same leading logarithmic growth as $f_N(1)$ on a smaller fixed $z$-disk. For a knot covered by the complete-color volume theorem, this growth is the volume of that same knot complement. The matrix and regular-singular estimates are hypotheses: this note does not prove them for every knot in the covered class, and it does not assume that the normalized profile converges to one. ## 1. The specified state and the additional operator input Fix a knot, its zero-framed finite cut, and its actual reduced even ADO state. Write \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q_N=q_N^2,\qquad Y=M^2,\qquad U=Y^N, \qquad K_N=f_N(1). \tag{1} \] Assume the scalar result for this knot gives $N^{-1}\log|K_N|\to v>0$. All normalizations below are therefore defined for sufficiently large levels. The [ordinary-color pointing and its polynomial bound](regularized_kashaev_period.md) give \[ f_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)\quad(1\le j<N),\qquad |C_j(q_N)|\le D_N,\qquad ND_N/|K_N|\longrightarrow0. \tag{2} \] The [actual crossing support](relative_octahedral_period.md) and its [Laurent-degree bound](actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) give an interval of integer carries $k_-\le k\le k_+$, independent of level, such that \[ f_N(Y)=\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}Y^t f_{t,N}(U),\qquad f_{t,N}(U)=\sum_{k=k_-}^{k_+}c_{k,t,N}U^k. \tag{3} \] The interval can be enlarged to cover finitely many small levels. Its existence follows term by term from the actual Laurent support bound, and does not estimate the signed coefficients $c_{k,t,N}$. Retain a specified whole finite-cut preoperator \[ \mathcal A(q,Z,Y,S)=\sum_k a_k(q,Z,Y)S^k, \qquad (S_q F)(Y)=F(q^2Y), \tag{4} \] and its supplied finite lift $G_N(q,Y)$, with \[ \mathcal A(q,q^N,Y,S_q)G_N(q,Y)=0, \qquad G_N(q_N,Y)=f_N(Y). \tag{5} \] Work over $\mathbb C(q)$; no descent of an arbitrarily chosen minimal operator to $\mathbb C(q^2)$ is assumed. The [squared-meridian finite-sum construction](even_meridian_norm_descent.md), using the [finite-sum annihilator argument](finite_sum_annihilator.md), supplies one whole lift and preoperator over $Q=q^2$. For that choice, (4) is obtained by substituting $Q=q^2$ and replacing its central variable $Q^N$ by $Z^2$. Thus (5) is available constructively from the finite source. The formulas below also allow a specified whole preoperator over the larger field. Clear fixed denominators and make a fixed Laurent shift normalization before using (4). Suppose all $Y$ exponents in its coefficients lie in $[-D,D]$, with $D$ independent of $N$. Terms that vanish at $Z=-1$ are retained. The nonzero root specialization \[ P_N=\mathcal A(q_N,-1,Y,S_{Q_N}) \tag{6} \] has a fixed shift width $w$, and both endpoint coefficients are nonzero rational functions of $Y$, outside finitely many levels. We may shift its first nonzero index to zero. The whole preoperator can have larger order than this root specialization. These are supplied-operator data, not coefficients reconstructed from unknown values of $f_N$. The first-normal coefficient $\partial_Z\mathcal A$ is additional to the root operator: replacing $\mathcal A$ by $\mathcal A+(Z+1)B$ leaves (6) unchanged but changes the first-normal rule. A fixed pointing of (6) alone does not specify that rule. Such a replacement need not annihilate the same actual finite lift. ## 2. The exact residue-coordinate normal equation Use the actual first-order deformation \[ q=q_N\left(1+\frac{\epsilon}{2N}\right),\qquad q^2=Q_N\left(1+\frac{\epsilon}{N}\right),\qquad Z=q^N=-\left(1+\frac\epsilon2\right),\qquad \epsilon^2=0. \tag{7} \] The sign of the $Z$ derivative in this coordinate is consequently negative. If (4) came from a $Q^N$ variable, the chain rule for $Z^2$ gives its usual positive derivative instead. Every rational function of $Y$ has a unique expression in the basis $1,Y,\ldots,Y^{N-1}$ over $\mathbb C(U)$. For a residue coordinate $h_t(U)$, the $k$th shift has the exact expansion \[ S_q^k\bigl(Y^t h_t(U)\bigr) =Q_N^{kt}Y^t\left[h_t(U)+ \epsilon k\left(\frac tN h_t(U)+U h_t'(U)\right)\right]. \tag{8} \] Let $L_N(U)$ be the $N\times N$ matrix of (6) in this basis. Let $C_N(U)$ be the matrix of $\sum_k k a_k(q_N,-1,Y)S_{Q_N}^k$. Finally set \[ J_N(U)= \operatorname{Mat}\!\left( \sum_k\left[\frac{q_N}{2N}\partial_q a_k -\frac12\partial_Z a_k\right]_{q_N,-1} S_{Q_N}^k\right) +C_N(U)\operatorname{diag}_{0\le t<N}(t/N). \tag{9} \] At the actual root, the microscopic shift $Y=e^{z/N}\mapsto Q_NY$ is exactly $z\mapsto z+2\pi i$. It is not a small translation in $z$. The differential term in (8) comes from varying the supplied quantum parameter through (7), not from an invalid small-step Taylor expansion of the root shift. All shifts in the first term are retained, including those whose root coefficients vanish. Write the first-order lift of (3) as the coordinate vector $\mathbf f_N+\epsilon\mathbf g_N$. Expanding (5), using (8), proves \[ L_N\mathbf f_N=0,\qquad L_N\mathbf g_N+C_N U\mathbf f_N'+J_N\mathbf f_N=0. \tag{10} \] This is a direct residue-basis form of the [source-corrected first quantum-normal equation](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md). Its relation to the general kernel-to-cokernel construction is explained in [the first quantum-normal connection](first_quantum_normal_connection.md). The derivative of the whole coefficients in (9), the moving-shift clock $t/N$, and the derivative of the central variable are all essential. For $N>D$, every entry of $L_N,C_N,J_N$ is a Laurent polynomial in $U$ with exponents in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Indeed a term $Y^lS^k$ sends column $t$ to the residue of $t+l$, with the single carry $\lfloor(t+l)/N\rfloor$. The entries of $J_N$ have the same carries; differentiating coefficients or multiplying by $t/N$ does not change them. No estimate for a determinant or its inverse follows merely from this entrywise fact. ## 3. Fixed rank and bounded central degree Let $r_N=\dim_{\mathbb C(U)}\ker L_N$. Then \[ 1\le r_N\le w. \tag{11} \] For the upper bound choose a generic complex value of $U$, a root $Y$ of $Y^N=U$, and evaluate a rational solution at its $N$ orbit points. The root equation is an order-$w$ cyclic recurrence. Its leading coefficient is nonzero at every orbit point for generic $U$, so its first $w$ values determine the remaining values successively. The residue-to-orbit evaluation matrix is invertible. The generic nullity of $L_N$ is therefore at most $w$. Nonzero $f_N$ gives the lower bound. There is also a uniform degree bound for the large minors of this matrix. Let $I,J$ be row and column sets of size $N-r$, where $r\le w$. Expand a determinant term, and within each matrix entry choose one of its actual $Y$ shifts $l_t$. Its exponent of $U$ is \[ \frac{\sum_{t\in J}t-\sum_{s\in I}s+ \sum_{t\in J}l_t}{N}. \tag{12} \] The first difference equals the difference of the omitted index sums, so its absolute value is at most $r(N-1)$. The last sum has absolute value at most $D(N-r)$. Consequently every such minor has Laurent support in $[-E,E]$, where one uniform choice is \[ E=D+w. \tag{13} \] This bound survives cancellation and holds for all replacement minors used by Cramer's rule. It is not the much larger bound obtained by multiplying arbitrary entry degrees: the actual carry identity (12) is the reason the degree stays bounded. Choose a nonzero maximal minor $\Delta_N$ of size $N-r_N$ with the smallest vanishing order at $U=1$ among all nonzero maximal minors. Reorder the selected rows and columns to write \[ L_N=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ \mathsf C&\mathsf D\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det A=\Delta_N. \tag{14} \] The generic right and left kernel frames are \[ V_N=\begin{pmatrix}-A^{-1}B\\ I_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad W_N=\begin{pmatrix}-\mathsf C A^{-1}&I_r\end{pmatrix}. \tag{15} \] Their entries are signed ratios of maximal minors, or constants. Every numerator therefore vanishes at least to the order of $\Delta_N$ at $1$. Cancelling that common power produces frames holomorphic at $U=1$, with common denominator $\widehat\Delta_N$ nonzero there. Numerators and denominator still have Laurent support in $[-E,E]$. The lower identity block in $V_N$ and right identity block in $W_N$ show that these are frames of the saturated generic kernel and its dual cokernel near $1$; this does not identify them with a possibly larger special-fiber kernel. There is an additional, genuinely quantitative condition needed for reconstruction: **Uniform frame condition.** After a common nonzero scalar normalization, the Laurent coefficients of $\widehat\Delta_N$ and of all the cancelled Cramer numerators in (15) are bounded, and $|\widehat\Delta_N(1)|$ is bounded below by a positive constant. Since their degree is bounded, this gives a fixed disk $|U-1|<R_0$, $R_0<1/2$, on which the entries of $V_N,W_N$ and every fixed derivative are uniformly bounded. The estimate is entrywise; an $r\times N$ matrix with bounded entries need not have an operator norm bounded independently of $N$. Such a norm estimate is not used below. The frame condition is an explicit test on operator minors, not an assertion about the unknown selected solution. It is not automatic from nonzero minors at each level. ## 4. The unknown central coordinates have bounded Laurent degree Let $T_N\subset\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ be the $r_N$ free column indices in (15), and set \[ \mathbf a_N(U)=\frac N{K_N}\bigl(f_{t,N}(U)\bigr)_{t\in T_N}. \qquad \frac N{K_N}\mathbf f_N(U)=V_N(U)\mathbf a_N(U). \tag{16} \] The indices $T_N$ may change with $N$. Every coordinate in the first formula remains an original residue coordinate from (3). Hence every coordinate of $\mathbf a_N$ has support in the same fixed carry interval $[k_-,k_+]$. No rational change of coordinates has been applied to these unknowns. It is the reconstruction matrix $V_N$, not the free coordinate vector, that is rational in $U$. The complete and ordinary values determine the initial vector quantitatively. The inverse finite Fourier transform gives, for every $0\le t<N$, \[ f_{t,N}(1)=\frac1N\left[K_N+ \sum_{j=1}^{N-1}C_j(q_N)Q_N^{-jt}\right]. \tag{17} \] Thus all coordinates of $\mathbf a_N(1)$ equal $1+o(1)$, uniformly even when their selected indices move with $N$. More precisely their errors have modulus at most $(N-1)D_N/|K_N|$. This is not an additional bound assumed on unknown normal jets. Multiply the second equation in (10) by $W_N$ and substitute (16). The unknown first lift disappears because $W_NL_N=0$. The exact result is \[ B_N(U)U\mathbf a_N'(U)+E_N(U)\mathbf a_N(U)=0, \tag{18} \] \[ B_N=W_N C_N V_N,\qquad E_N=W_N\bigl(C_N U V_N'+J_N V_N\bigr). \tag{19} \] Every coefficient here is constructed from (4), its first coefficient derivatives, root substitution, and minors. Neither $f_N$ nor its unknown first lift is needed to assemble (18). The state is used only to prove that its actual free coordinates solve it and to provide the already known data (17). Let $\Delta$ denote the cancelled common denominator from Section 3. The entries of $B_N$ have denominator $\Delta^2$ and numerator support in $[-(2E+1),2E+1]$. The entries of $E_N$ have denominator $\Delta^3$ and numerator support in $[-(3E+1),3E+1]$. The latter assertion includes the derivative $UV_N'$: differentiating a Laurent numerator does not enlarge its support. Therefore multiplying (18) by $\Delta^3$ gives \[ \mathcal B_N(U)U\mathbf a_N'(U)+ \mathcal E_N(U)\mathbf a_N(U)=0, \tag{20} \] where both matrix Laurent bands lie in $[-L,L]$, with the fixed bound $L=3E+1$. Sums over $N$ entries can change their coefficients and conditioning, but do not change this degree bound. ## 5. A bounded matrix criterion using only fixed-degree identities Put $d_c=k_+-k_-$ and write $\mathbf a_N(U)=U^{k_-}\mathbf b_N(U)$, where $\deg\mathbf b_N\le d_c$. Equation (20) becomes \[ \mathcal B_N U\mathbf b_N'+ (k_-\mathcal B_N+\mathcal E_N)\mathbf b_N=0, \qquad \mathbf b_N(1)=\mathbf a_N(1). \tag{21} \] Multiply the first equation by $U^L$ and equate coefficients. Together with evaluation at $1$, this is a linear system \[ H_N\mathbf x_N=(0,\mathbf a_N(1)), \tag{22} \] where $\mathbf x_N$ is the vector of the $r_N(d_c+1)$ polynomial coefficients of $\mathbf b_N$. There are at most $r_N(d_c+2L+1)+r_N$ rows. Both dimensions are bounded independently of $N$. Redundant zero rows may be removed, and the homogeneous equation rows may be rescaled or combined by specified invertible row operations; their right side is zero. Such choices must be recorded when discussing conditioning. **Finite matrix criterion.** Suppose the uniform frame condition holds and there is a choice of the just described operator-only row normalizations for which \[ \sigma_{\min}(H_N)\ge\delta>0 \tag{23} \] at all sufficiently large levels. Then the actual microscopic regular profiles are locally uniformly bounded near zero, with every fixed derivative bounded on smaller disks. Indeed (17), (22), and (23) bound the coefficient vector $\mathbf x_N$ uniformly. The dimensions are bounded, so all choices of the usual finite-dimensional norms are uniformly equivalent. The fixed degree and fixed negative monomial in (21) bound $\mathbf a_N$ on $|U-1|<R_0$. Equation (16) and the uniform frame condition then give the exact scalar bound \[ g_N(z):=\frac{f_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N} =\frac1N\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}e^{tz/N} \bigl[V_N(e^z)\mathbf a_N(e^z)\bigr]_t=O(1) \tag{24} \] on a fixed small $z$-disk. The factor $1/N$ cancels the number of residues; $|e^{tz/N}|\le e^{|z|}$ and $r_N\le w$. For the [canonical ordinary interpolant and regular remainder](regularized_kashaev_period.md), denoted by $P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}$ and $R_N$, the [exact centered identity](scaled_meridian_regular_profile.md) is \[ g_N(z)=H_N^{\mathrm{res}}(z)\rho_N(z)+\pi_N(z), \quad H_N^{\mathrm{res}}(z)=\frac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}, \quad \rho_N(z)=e^{(N-1)z/(2N)}\frac{NR_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N}. \tag{25} \] Here $\pi_N=P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(e^{z/N})/K_N\to0$ with all fixed derivatives by (2). On a sufficiently small disk, $H_N^{\mathrm{res}}$ is uniformly nonzero. Thus (24) bounds $\rho_N$. Cauchy's inequality proves the derivative bounds. If a larger domain is controlled, the [boundary-circle division argument](scaled_meridian_regular_profile.md) applies across its resonance points; no larger domain is inferred from the local test. A directly usable sufficient version of (23) is coefficientwise convergence of the normalized bounded matrices $H_N$ to a matrix $H_\infty$ with full column rank. One may use finitely many rank/chart subsequences, with the same uniform lower bound. This test concerns coefficients of a fixed-size algebraic system assembled from the actual source-normal operator. It does not assume convergence, boundedness, or a proposed value of the unknown profile. At any one level, full column rank only gives algebraic uniqueness on the fixed carry range; its smallest singular value may still tend to zero. The distinction is precisely the remaining conditioning issue. The input degree bound alone does not imply (23). ## 6. A regular-singular alternative with finitely many resonance tests There is another sufficient criterion when $B_N$ in (18) is generically invertible. Put $w_0=U-1$ and form the exact rational matrix \[ A_N(w_0)=-\frac{w_0}{U}B_N(U)^{-1}E_N(U),\qquad U=1+w_0. \tag{26} \] The equation is $w_0\mathbf a_N'=A_N(w_0)\mathbf a_N$. Its rational degrees are bounded. For example the numerator and denominator of $B_N^{-1}E_N$ can be taken with Laurent half-width at most $(2r_N+1)E+r_N$, using the adjugate and the bounds following (19). Multiplication by $w_0/U$ changes this by at most two. This statement does not assert bounded coefficients or separation of the zeros of those denominators from $1$. Assume the frame condition, and assume (26) is holomorphic on one fixed disk $|w_0|<R$, with $\|A_N\|\le C$ there. This is a concrete uniform Fuchsian test: after the indicated factor $w_0$ there is no pole, and the remaining fixed-degree denominators have a uniform zero-free disk. It can be established by cancelled coefficient bounds and a positive lower bound for their denominator values at zero. It is a test on the first-normal matrices, not an estimate of the unknown selected state. Write $A_N(w_0)=\sum_{j\ge0}A_{j,N}w_0^j$. Choose an integer $J>2C$, and suppose \[ \sup_N\|(nI-A_{0,N})^{-1}\|<\infty \qquad (1\le n\le J). \tag{27} \] For $n>J$, the Neumann series gives a uniform bound $2/n$ for the inverse. Hence a constant $C_1$ gives $\|(nI-A_{0,N})^{-1}\|\le C_1/(n+1)$ for every positive integer $n$. The actual free coordinates are holomorphic at $U=1$. Their Taylor coefficients satisfy exactly \[ (nI-A_{0,N})\mathbf a_{n,N} =\sum_{j=1}^n A_{j,N}\mathbf a_{n-j,N},\qquad n\ge1. \tag{28} \] Their constant coefficients are uniformly bounded by (17); the equation at order zero is automatically satisfied. On a slightly smaller fixed disk, Cauchy's estimate gives $\|A_{j,N}\|\le C_2 R_1^{-j}$. For $0<r<R_1$, multiply the norm of (28) by $r^n$, sum finite partial sums, and discard the helpful factor $1/(n+1)\le1$. If $t=r/R_1$ is small enough that $C_1C_2t/(1-t)<1/2$, the convolution term is absorbed. This proves \[ \sum_{n\ge0}\|\mathbf a_{n,N}\|r^n \le 2\sup_N\|\mathbf a_N(1)\|. \tag{29} \] Equation (24) again proves local boundedness of $\rho_N$. If some positive integer residues are resonant or approach resonance, the same argument works after separately bounding the finitely many actual coefficients $\mathbf a_{n,N}$ for $0\le n\le J$. No extra jet bound is needed in the nonresonant case (27). The resonant version is a finite additional pointing requirement, not a claim that ordinary values already control those jets. An especially simple operator-side test is $A_{0,N}\to A_0$ with no positive integer eigenvalue, together with the stated uniform Fuchsian bounds. Only finitely many inverses need checking because the residue norm is bounded. If the symbol $B_N$ is singular, this argument cannot be obtained by writing a formal inverse; the bounded matrix test in Section 5 remains meaningful without that inverse. The [factorial atom and repeated-root diagnostic](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md) illustrate the role of the source and resonance. For the actual factorial atom $(Y;Q)_N$, the supplied preoperator is $S-(1-Z_2Y)/(1-Y)$, with $Z_2=Q^N$. The residue calculation gives $U a'+U(1-U)^{-1}a=0$, whose root section is $a=1-U$. In (26) its residue is the positive integer $1$: its value at $U=1$ is zero and does not fix the first derivative. The resonance qualification is therefore necessary even for this elementary finite-source atom. For the previously recorded diagnostic $(S-1)(S-Z_2)$, the root operator is $(S-1)^2$ and both projected first-normal matrices vanish on its central solution line. The finite matrix in (22) then contains only the initial-value condition and cannot determine several allowed carries. These are checks of the supplied normal rule, not additional knot examples. ## 7. A conditional local meridian volume consequence Either criterion proves more than an abstract normal-family statement when combined with the complete scalar theorem. The original subtraction gives \[ \rho_N(0)=\frac{K_N-P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(1)}{K_N}=1+o(1). \tag{30} \] Suppose one of Sections 5–6 bounds $|\rho_N|$ by $C$ on $|z|<R$. Cauchy's inequality bounds its first derivative by $2C/R$ on $|z|\le R/2$. For all sufficiently large $N$, (30) differs from $1$ by at most $1/4$. Choose a fixed $r>0$ with $r\le R/2$ and $2Cr/R\le1/4$. Then \[ \frac12\le|\rho_N(z)|\le C\qquad (|z|\le r). \tag{31} \] Shrink $r$ further if necessary so that the same disk has a fixed lower bound for $|H_N^{\mathrm{res}}|$. Since $\pi_N\to0$, (25) gives fixed positive lower and upper bounds for $|g_N|$ there as well. Consequently, if the complete scalar satisfies \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V, \tag{32} \] then uniformly for $|z|\le r$, \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\bigl|R_N(e^{z/N})\bigr|\longrightarrow V, \qquad \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\bigl|f_N(e^{z/N})\bigr|\longrightarrow V. \tag{33} \] For the first limit, use the exact factorization $R_N(e^{z/N})=K_N N^{-1}e^{-(N-1)z/(2N)}\rho_N(z)$. Its logarithm differs from $\log|K_N|$ by $-\log N+O(1)$ uniformly on the disk. For the second, $f_N(e^{z/N})=K_Ng_N(z)$ and the difference is $O(1)$. This proves both limits, including their uniformity, without assuming that $\rho_N$ converges to $1$ or even has a unique subsequential limit. For a knot covered by the [strict-tree theorem](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) or its [net-twist formulation](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md), the complete scalar theorem identifies $V$ with the volume of that same knot complement. The two conclusions in (33) then retain that geometric right side. They remain conditional on the explicit finite matrix or Fuchsian estimates above. The disk is fixed in $z$, hence has meridian radius $O(1/N)$; this does not contradict the [nearby-zero theorem](actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) or give a zero-free neighborhood of fixed radius in $M$. No extension to all microscopic disks or identification of a selected classical factor is inferred. ## 8. The remaining conditioning problem The actual finite source already supplies (1)–(5), the fixed carry interval, and the ordinary initial estimate (17) for a knot with the proved positive scalar rate. The whole preoperator is obtained from its finite summation rules, not from a fit to invariant values. From that supplied preoperator, Sections 2–4 prove the exact normal matrix equation and the bounded central degrees without a profile hypothesis. Sections 5–6 prove two quantitative sufficient criteria, and Section 7 gives their conditional local meridian volume consequence. What is not supplied by the scalar theorem is the uniform frame condition, a lower singular-value bound for (22), or the alternative Fuchsian and residue estimates. Those are operator/lattice conditioning statements. They can now be phrased using bounded central degrees and a fixed number of free coefficients; their validity for a broad knot class remains open. The matrix test avoids an unspecified infinite family of normal-derivative estimates, but does not prove its own lower bound. The separate [quarter-turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) establishes a polynomial spectral estimate for each physical tangle turn on a small fixed meridian-displacement disk, relative to the complete turn of the same polynomial. This is a bound for a local tensor operation. It does not give a lower bound for the minors defining the reconstruction frame or for the smallest singular value in (22), and it does not establish the Fuchsian criterion. The conditioning hypotheses of this note are therefore unchanged. The [whole-source growth theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) goes further for strict trees with separated bare product junctions: it proves an exact supremum-volume limit, at both parities, for the unsummed auxiliary-colored source on \(|s|\le R<1\). Its uniform upper bound uses the augmented volume, and its lower witness is the complete point. That statement does not supply uniform conditioning of this finite system, local boundedness of the normalized filled-knot remainder, or the pointwise conclusion in Section 7. Thus these operator hypotheses remain genuine additional conditions. The use of $f_N$ rather than the affine remainder does not discard the latter's source. The identity $f_N=S_NR_N+P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}$ is retained throughout, the ordinary values determine (17), and (25) uses the same actual subtraction and full-state centering monomial. If one writes a root equation directly for $R_N$, conjugation by $S_N$ produces the inhomogeneous term from $P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}$; it cannot be set to zero. Likewise, any boundary factor already present in the specified whole preoperator remains inside $L_N$ and its full generic kernel. No rank-one quotient is silently taken. Finally, the [central comparison](central_source_freedom_in_regular_profiles.md) $\widetilde f_N=h_N(Y^N)f_N$ preserves the root equation, ordinary values, affine root source and Mellin quantum jets. It does not generally satisfy (10) for this same whole preoperator. Conversely, even a uniqueness result for (18) at each level would not imply the uniform estimates in Sections 5–6. The new test separates these two issues explicitly. It proves no identification of a classical geometric factor, no fixed meridian neighborhood free of zeros, and no particular limit such as $\rho_N\to1$. The [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) obtains a uniform volume limit and an explicit profile by a direct finite-sum argument for strict trees satisfying its component condition. It retains all original scalar factors and proves a nonzero first Fourier contribution. That theorem does not prove the conditioning hypotheses of the finite matrix system here, or the corresponding statements for the ordinary-color-subtracted remainder through its resonances. ## 9. Relation to established difference-equation constructions Additional differential data at a root of unity have an established role in difference equations. Hardouin's *Iterative q-Difference Galois Theory*, Section 3.2, descends iterative data to a fixed subspace and gives a connection there; this is related to the need to retain more than the root shift alone. Di Vizio and Hardouin study the cyclic iterate and root specializations in their treatment of generic Galois groups. These results do not provide the uniform frame or conditioning bounds assumed here. [Hardouin's primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.4826), [Di Vizio–Hardouin's author text](https://divizio.perso.math.cnrs.fr/PREPRINTS/qGKGENERIC-gros/qGKgeneric.pdf). Central variables also compress degree bounds in the reduced-norm computation of Bostan, Caruso and Schost, Section 3. Their setting is positive-characteristic differential and shift operators. The present carry calculation is given explicitly in (12), and the source-normal and quantitative estimates are proved here with their stated hypotheses; no identification with that different setting is required. [Bostan–Caruso–Schost's primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.5341).

title: Main-meridian estimates for arbitrary Conway product regions
status: Main-meridian estimates for arbitrary Conway product regions
text: # Main-meridian estimates for arbitrary Conway product regions 1 November 2026. A fixed Conway construction joins two-string tangles by ordered products and physical quarter-turns. Consecutive products with no turn between them form one product junction. A junction is bare when it carries no original crossing-circle operator. This note treats an arbitrary finite connected region of such junctions: their number and their valences are unrestricted, and both are fixed before the level tends to infinity. The main meridian moves by an amount of order \(1/N\). That deformation changes the polynomial relation in some orientation types, so a whole-junction trace can acquire terms absent at completeness. A comparison with the complete trace at the same indices is false in general. The proof instead separates the trace difference according to its high indices. With one high index, an exact Fourier bound reflects that index and an exact Frobenius pairing fuses two junctions in a positive comparison tree. With several high indices, a half-label projector supplies a boundary comparison. In each case the full neighboring branches remain coupled, and the comparison pressure is bounded by the pressure of the original construction. The clean part uses complete bare tensors with the **original deformed edge factors, boundary arrays and typed carriers retained**. It is not the invariant evaluated at the complete meridian. The grouped remainder has a strict exponential loss. Sections 1–7 prove this source statement and its passage through the actual circle operators. Sections 8–10 verify the original wire-packet and filling interfaces. Together with those established proofs, the result removes the bare-component restriction from the [filled meridian-profile and volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md). All its strictness, knot, framing, fixed-parity and sufficiently-long fixed-twist hypotheses remain. The fused trees occur only in upper estimates. No isotopy or equality of knot complements is inferred from the fusion identity, and the final volume and preferred cusp always belong to the original filled knot. ## 1. Fixed source, boundary arrays, and the theorem Let \(\mathcal G\) be a fixed finite tree of actual bare product junctions. Every junction has full valence at least three and every edge between junctions carries an original physical quarter-turn. A higher-valence junction is kept whole in its moving trace. Only its complete positive comparison may be resolved by the original ordered binary products. Set \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), and \[ c_j=2\cos\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{N},\quad S_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin\frac{\pi j}{N},\quad e_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z). \tag{1} \] Indices \(r\le m\) are low; the others are high. The actual orientation type uses either \(P_0=\mathcal T_N+2\) or \[ P_s=\mathcal T_N+2\cos(2\pi s),\quad \Delta_s=2\cos(2\pi s)-2,\quad \phi_s(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F. \tag{2} \] Both repeated-node values and first normal coordinates remain in this quotient. Equal-color moving junctions are an independent set along physical turn edges. Constant junctions may be adjacent; strict alternation is neither assumed nor needed. For every external branch, assume its entire canonical coefficient array satisfies \[ |f_{i,N,r}(s)|\le e^{N(c_i+\epsilon_N)} \begin{cases}e^{Ng(r/d)},&r\le m,\\1,&r>m,\end{cases} \qquad \epsilon_N\longrightarrow0, \tag{3} \] uniformly in its stated physical colors and on each fixed \(|s|\le R<1\). Here \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt, \qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\quad 0\le x\le\tfrac12. \tag{4} \] The constants \(c_i\) are the original accumulated branch actions, not independently assigned cap volumes. All finite \(r/N\)-to-\(r/d\) changes have uniform cost \(O(\log N)\) in the exponent, including endpoints. The profile labels describe open branches of the positive complete calculation. A rigid branch, called type \(L\), has output interval \((0,1/2)\) and optimized action \(g(b)+c\). A composite branch of type \(A\) has strict output interval \((0,1)\); it may contain products and turns. The symbol \(C\) denotes the prescribed cylindrical closing trace. In \(C(hA^0)\), the expression \(A^0\) is the positive reference defined below and \(h\) is the pure rigid comparison leaf with profile \(g\). It implements the output norm estimate; it is not an added physical crossing circle. Expose the component as an unturned product expression \(A\), and put \(Q=T_s(A)\). Let \(A^0\) be the complete positive reference with the same tree and pure rigid boundary profiles. The intrinsic probe action is \[ \Omega_Q=\Phi_{C(hA^0)}+\sum_i c_i. \tag{5} \] The original strict probe geometry identifies this with the pressure of that same branch. Assume the reference has its original strict state; this is automatic for the unturned component with L/A inputs used in the strict reduced-tree induction. For a canonical polynomial \(F\) of degree less than \(N\), \(\|F\|_{\mathcal J}\) is the maximum of the values \(|F(c_j)|\) at distinct complete nodes and the derivative magnitudes \(|F'(c_j)|\) at double nodes. At odd levels \(-2\) is simple and contributes only its value. This norm retains all first Hermite normal coordinates: a polynomial can vanish at every node while its derivative at a double node remains nonzero. **Component theorem.** There is a fixed \(\eta>0\) such that \[ \|Q_{N,s}\|_{\mathcal J} \le e^{N(\Omega_Q+o(1))}. \tag{6} \] There is also an exact decomposition into a clean complete-tensor contraction and a grouped remainder: \[ Q_{N,s}=Q^{\mathrm{clean}}_{N,s}+E_{N,s}, \qquad \|E_{N,s}\|_{\mathcal J} \le e^{N(\Omega_Q-\eta+o(1))}. \tag{7} \] In \(Q^{\mathrm{clean}}\), all bare tensors use \(\phi_0\), all external component inputs and the output are low, and every original complete-supported internal index is retained. The physical paired edge factors and actual low boundary arrays remain in this contraction. Its coefficientwise absolute value is bounded by a subexponential multiple of the same complete positive reference, with the constants in (5). High original boundary inputs and a high output have the strict loss in (7). The assertions hold through both parities and on every fixed \(R<1\). The fixed geometric and regular-window losses can be chosen before \(R\); polynomial prefactors and the eventual level threshold may depend on \(R\). An inherited loss in one full boundary array subtracts that loss from every estimate by homogeneity. No internal high index is automatically discarded from the clean complete contraction. ## 2. Three exact local inputs Write \(V_s(\mathbf n)=\phi_s(\prod e_{n_i})\) and \(\delta V_s=V_s-V_0\). Fixed valence is understood in all polynomial prefactors. First, for an all-low tuple, \[ |V_s(\mathbf n)|+|\delta V_s(\mathbf n)| \le N^{C_R}V_0(\mathbf n). \tag{8} \] The first bound is the same-level all-parity whole-trace theorem in [source bounds and typed coefficient extractors](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 2; the second follows by the triangle inequality. It keeps all signed Fourier aliases together. On a compact regular all-low window with strictly positive whole-junction support slack, \[ |\delta V_s(\mathbf n)| \le N^{C_R}e^{-\kappa N}V_0(\mathbf n). \tag{9} \] This is the regular bare trace theorem, [regular bare-trace estimate](actual_main_meridian_regular_bare_trace.md): the first Fourier alias is independent of \(s\), and the remaining aliases have a strict rate loss. The window requires each incident normalized label in a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\) and the sum of the labels strictly greater than one. A cubic tuple with at most one high index instead has \(\delta V_s=0\) exactly by degree, so no low-window assertion is needed for its half-label exception. Second, if precisely one index is high, say \(h>m\), and \(F\) is the product of the low factors, set \(r=d-h\). Then \[ |\delta\phi_s(e_hF)| \le N^{C_R}|\Delta_s|\,\phi_0(e_rF). \tag{10} \] This is a comparison with a *reflected* complete tensor. It is not a comparison with \(\phi_0(e_hF)\), which can be exponentially smaller. The exact proof is [high-index Fourier reflection](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md), Sections 1–4. Briefly, the high polynomial has two signed Fourier tails and polynomial Laurent norm. Alias one cancels in \(\delta\phi\), so only frequencies at least \(2N-1-h=N+r\) remain. The endpoint coefficient of \(e_r\), the interval-tail lemma and the all-low theorem recover the positive complete trace on the right at the original level, including even parity. When all low factors lie in a fixed compact interval inside \((0,1/2)\) and \(r/N\) is bounded below, the strict convolution-concavity comparison at frequencies \(N+r\) and \(N-1-r\) strengthens (10) to \[ |\delta\phi_s(e_hF)| \le N^{C_R}|\Delta_s|e^{-\kappa N}\phi_0(e_rF). \tag{11} \] The estimate includes \(r/N\) near half. If its right side vanishes, (10) already gives exact zero. The exponent \(\kappa\) is fixed before \(R\). Third, for any tuple, the full spectral-jet estimates and finite-degree Chebyshev folding give \[ |V_s(\mathbf n)| \le N^{C_R}\exp\left\{N\sum_{i:n_i\le m}g(n_i/d)\right\}. \tag{12} \] Every high basis polynomial has polynomial full-jet norm; each low one has rate at most \(g\). Quotient multiplication of a fixed number of factors and the trace have polynomial cost. This does not discard high first normals. With at least two high indices, \(V_0=0\) by its pairwise support, so (12) also bounds \(\delta V_s\). For an old whole junction with at least two half incidences, \[ V_D^{\mathrm{action}}(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,x_3,\ldots,x_D) =\sum_{i=3}^Dg(x_i), \quad 0\le x_i\le\tfrac12. \tag{13} \] Additional half incidences cost zero. The exact calibration at odd \(N=2m+1\) is \(\phi_0(e_m^2F)=F(-2)\), \(e_m(-2)=1\): the square kills both jets at all double nodes and is the normalized simple-node projector. The parity-independent closed old action gives (13), including zero arms. The complete derivation and the arbitrary-valence simultaneous reassembly are in [component pressure comparison](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md). ## 3. Expand differences and retain the sector graph Expand every moving tensor by the exact identity \[ V_s=V_0+\delta V_s. \tag{14} \] There are finitely many choices because the original tree is fixed. Then partition its finite label sum into low/high bands. At a selected difference tensor there are three possibilities: no high incidence, one high incidence, or at least two high incidences. Apply (8), (10), or (12), respectively. Unselected tensors and constant-quotient tensors retain their exact complete positive values. A term outside any such complete support is zero. A selected one-high difference with an internal high incidence meets a constant old vertex. Its moving endpoint has no other high incidence; its old endpoint has at most one high incidence by the complete pairwise support. Therefore the selected internal high edges form a matching. Reflecting the moving endpoint changes their equal-index contraction into the complementary metric contraction. Precisely, \[ \sum_{i=0}^d\phi_0(Ae_i)\phi_0(e_{d-i}B)=\phi_0(AB). \tag{15} \] This is the exact full Frobenius identity; the dual basis is \(e_{d-i}\). It fuses the two adjacent complete product junctions after the selected turn is deleted. The other low incidences remain correlated inside the resulting whole tensor. No low arm is replaced by an independent \(g\) profile in this step. Call the set of these edges \(S\), and the contracted old tree \(\mathcal G/S\). Its induced ribbon orders are obtained by substituting the child product into its original position. The valence of a fused pair is \(D_1+D_2-2\ge4\). Because \(S\) is a matching, every fused hub has only low exterior incidences in the original sector. The restored complementary index in (15) can be kept as a hidden unturned wire in a prescribed resolution; summing it gives exactly the fused positive tensor. Discarding its band restrictions only enlarges that positive comparison. ![A trace difference is bounded by a reflected complete pairing, which fuses into one product junction.](../book/figures/main-meridian-reflected-turn-fusion.svg) The drawing records a tree of operations, not a knot diagram. Reflecting one endpoint changes equal covariant labels into complementary labels. The positive sum then fuses the two junctions in their induced order, retaining the other branches. The physical source and its peripheral marking are unchanged; the fused tree is used only to bound its pressure. The pressure of this full comparison tree satisfies \[ F(\mathcal G/S)\le F(\mathcal G). \tag{16} \] The proof is [component pressure comparison](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md). For one deleted edge the two rooted profiles are actual unturned products with L/A inputs. They obey \(f_X(b)\ge f_X(1-b)\) for \(b\ge1/2\), by derivative domination over the symmetric two-leaf profile. Hence \[ \max_b[f_A(b)+f_B(1-b)]\le\max_b[f_A(b)+f_B(b)]. \tag{17} \] The fused tree remains in this old pressure class, so the comparison iterates using its current coupled profiles. The constants never change. Equality can occur, notably when a cut side is the two-leaf product. Thus (16) alone is not a strict error estimate. If a selected one-high difference instead meets an original external coefficient array, there is no edge to fuse. Change its summation variable from \(h\) to \(r=d-h\). Its coefficient has rate \(c_i\), whereas the low reference coefficient has rate \(g(r/d)+c_i\). This introduces the nonnegative surplus \[ g(r/d). \tag{18} \] Keep that surplus for the strict estimate; it is not an altered physical coefficient or a new circle. ## 4. Sectors with several-high tensors or unreflected high boundaries The selected several-high moving vertices are never fused. They remain pairwise nonadjacent. A fusion in (15) does not create a new high exterior incidence: its endpoints had only the selected high edge. Removing the several-high vertices therefore leaves old regions with at most one high marked incidence at each retained old hub. Their other incidences retain their complete correlations. At a low arm of a removed several-high vertex, charge its \(g(x)\) from (12) to the adjoining old region as an ordinary free boundary profile. At a high arm mark the adjoining old boundary. Original unreflected high external inputs, including a high output probe, have rate \(c_i\), not \(g(x)+c_i\) at \(x>1/2\); mark those boundaries too. Each old hub still has at most one mark. All original constants are retained exactly once. The arbitrary-valence old simultaneous-half theorem applies jointly to every marked region. It changes all its high marked labels to half without decreasing its upper comparison pressure. Reinsert each removed vertex by (13), using the low-arm values chosen by the neighboring region optimizers. Its old cardinal action consumes each previously assigned \(g\) once. External low arms keep their own boundary \(g+c_i\) in addition to the cardinal contribution; external high arms become half with \(g(1/2)=0\). Zero arms and all other closed endpoints follow by continuity. This constructs a feasible state of the same contracted complete tree. At least one pair at a reinserted vertex is saturated, or an original high boundary has become a half leaf. Either is a closed boundary face disjoint from its unique strict maximum. The compact action polytope consequently gives a fixed strict loss below \(F(\mathcal G/S)\), and hence below the original pressure by (16). If there are no several-high vertices but an original external/probe high remains unreflected, apply the existing complete arbitrary-component high-input/probe theorem to the fused old tree. The same old-half argument marks its high external incidences and yields its strict boundary loss. This step precedes all regular-saddle reasoning. A high original array is never treated as a low pure leaf without its separate comparison. The finite number of band patterns and possible sets \(S\) permits a common positive loss. Uniform closed factorial errors and all polynomial factors are absorbed into its half, for sufficiently large levels. These arguments also cover sectors with both one-high differences and several-high tensors; the matching property is what preserves the old-region mark hypothesis after fusion. ## 5. Remaining correction sectors near a contracted strict maximum It remains to treat a nonempty difference sector with no several-high tensor and no unreflected original high boundary. After the comparisons above it is bounded by a complete positive contraction of \(\mathcal G/S\), retaining all restored unturned wires and any reflected external label. The reference maximum is unique and strict. Outside any fixed neighborhood of it, the positive resolved action has a fixed compact gap. It remains to examine that neighborhood, where a mere polynomial comparison would not suffice if (16) is an equality. If an external one-high difference is present, its reflected label at the strict reference maximum is in \((0,1/2)\). Since \(g\) is positive there, the surplus (18) has a fixed positive lower bound in a small neighborhood. It gives the required exponential loss. Boundary limits of that label are outside the strict maximizing neighborhood and were already covered by compact separation. Suppose next that an internal one-high difference is present. Then \(S\ne\varnothing\), and the fused tree has a hub of valence at least four. The old complete physical-edge theorem says every remaining physical internal label is strictly below half: its only equality exception is the entire two-trivalent-hub tree, which is impossible here. Ordinary boundary labels are also strictly between zero and half. These statements concern physical edges; hidden unturned wires are not required to be low. At the selected reflected vertex, every factor other than the reflected one is an exterior incidence of its fused pair. The matching property ensures none of these is another restored unturned edge. Its labels therefore lie in a fixed compact interval inside \((0,1/2)\). Write \(x_r=r/d\) for the normalized restored reflected wire. It is strictly positive at the resolved strict maximum. If that maximum has \(x_r>1/2\), the sector restriction \(r\le m\), equivalently \(x_r\le m/d\), is separated from it and the sector has a compact gap. Otherwise, in its allowed portion of a small neighborhood, \(x_r\) stays bounded below and all the other factors are in the regular low interval. Estimate (11) supplies a fixed exponential loss. It is valid also when the limiting \(x_r\) equals half. Finally suppose there is no selected one-high difference, internal or external. Then \(S\) is empty, and every selected difference has all incidences low. The comparison is the original old tree. At its strict optimizer all physical labels are strictly low except for the two-trivalent-hub exception. In the nonexceptional case, each selected junction has regular low incident labels and strict whole-hub total slack; (9) supplies a loss. In the exceptional case every bare tensor is cubic, and the selected all-low difference is identically zero by the degree bound. More generally a nonzero all-low difference must occur at a noncubic junction, which itself excludes that exception. These alternatives exhaust the nonempty difference sectors. At least one strict analytic factor suffices; other selected differences may keep their polynomial old majorants. The uniform finite-angle and radius constants are harmless because the tree is fixed. We obtain \[ \sum_{\text{nonempty difference sectors}} |Z_{N,\mathrm{sector}}(s)| \le e^{N(F(\mathcal G)-\eta+o(1))}. \tag{19} \] This is an absolute bound after the stated whole-tensor regroupings. It is not a bound on each signed coefficient of a high polynomial or on the absolute sum of an unregrouped crossing-state expansion. ## 6. Norm extraction, clean reference, and inherited errors The output probe is made explicit by the exact typed turn formula. In the appropriate constant or moving trace, \[ [e_r]Q=\frac{\gamma_N(s)W_{d-r}(s)}{H_N(s)}\, \phi_\sigma(e_rA), \qquad \|Q\|_{\mathcal J} \le C_RN^C\sum_{r=0}^d w_{N,r}|\phi_\sigma(e_rA)|, \tag{20} \] where \(w_{N,r}=e_r(-2)\) at low indices and \(w_{N,r}=1\) at high indices. The low weight has the same closed rate \(g\) as an ordinary boundary, and the high one has rate zero. Also \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_r(s)=\prod_{j=1}^r\left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)} {\sin^2(\pi j/N)}\right), \qquad \gamma_N\in\{1,q^{s^2/2},q^{-s^2/2}\}. \tag{21} \] The paired factors and their inverses are uniformly bounded on fixed \(R<1\). Apply Sections 3–5 to this probe-closed tree. Its original action is exactly (5), not the pressure of a newly inserted physical crossing circle. The high-probe case is the high-boundary case of Section 4. Summing (20) costs only a polynomial factor and proves (6)–(7). For the empty difference sector with all external indices low, coefficientwise comparison with the original positive reference follows directly from (3), the positive old product law, and bounded paired factors on the finitely many physical edges. The exact pure complete coefficients have the same closed rate \(g\), with a uniform polynomial ratio. The clean contraction therefore preserves the original full positive low-output profile; it is not reset to \(g+c\) after a bare component. All original complete internal indices remain in this term. If one full input array improves by \(e^{-N\gamma}\), every multilinear contraction, trace comparison, and positive majorant above improves by that same factor. The constants in every reference profile shift by \(-\gamma\); the stationary labels, deletion comparison, compact gaps, and cardinal identities do not change. There is no extra charge of \(2G_0\) at an internal turn. This proves inherited-error propagation for the whole coefficient array and hence for its converted spectral norm. An input known only to have a small \(\mathcal J\)-norm is not declared to satisfy (3) by generic coefficient recovery. In the actual reduced-tree induction it first passes through the intervening circle-marked or decorated extractor, including its physical coupon and turn. Equations (D23)–(D24) of [source bounds and typed coefficient extractors](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) give the low-\(g\)/high-zero cone at precisely that interface and propagate the inherited loss. The low trace probe costs \(g\); the high probe has polynomial norm. This conversion is performed once there. No new conversion is needed inside a whole bare component, whose inherited boundary arrays already satisfy the full cone (3). It is not inferred from a pointwise boundary profile or an independent cap budget. ## 7. Fresh Gaussian localization and the global source induction The clean low output retains the old probe profile \[ f_A(1-u)+g(u)+\sum_i c_i. \tag{22} \] Its intrinsic maximizer is strictly inside \((0,1/2)\). The original complete probe has a unique strict state and an off-window gap. On a compact interval around that output, the exact low Newton spectral factor has a negative angular quadratic term. Summing the low clean coefficients gives the same fresh Gaussian at its actual \(\Omega_Q\). The grouped error in (7), and every clean output away from the interval, has a fixed rate gap. Canonical Hermite interpolation and the finite-degree Bernstein bound absorb these terms on a sufficiently small complex angular strip. This is precisely the coefficient/profile-to-Gaussian argument in [spectral propagation theorem](actual_conway_mixed_core_spectral_propagation.md), Sections 1–4, with the component cone and high gap now supplied without a valence restriction. The mutual global induction therefore has the same two genuine interfaces. A circle-marked junction uses the physical decorated-character or fixed-crossing cone, whose input is the actual neighboring spectral budget. A bare component uses the theorem above and retains its original low profile plus a grouped small remainder. The intrinsic rigid/probe geometry accounts for all constants and gives the original root action. No independent cap action is substituted for a shared boundary. For fixed crossing powers \(R_s^{n_i}\), their physical polynomial norms have polynomial size on fixed \(R<1\); this supplies the same augmented-budget cone, with constants depending on the fixed powers. It does not yet identify the smaller filled exponent. Original auxiliary colors and fixed half-twist choices instead use the existing full-color cone uniformly. Descendant full-array losses propagate as in Section 6. Exposing any original circle by the exact typed adjunction then supplies the same raw spectral Gaussian at the original root pressure. The auxiliary-color contour argument consequently has its original scope \(R<1/2\), without a component-size restriction. The source upper bound itself has scope \(R<1\). The root with no unturned circle operator uses an existing ordinary leaf and the original typed self-adjoint pairing; it introduces no extra \(2G_0\). The two-leaf case remains the previously treated case with its original knot/pure-leaf qualification. The present component proof does not alter it. ## 8. The original complete wire window and complex angular parameters For an arbitrary old bare tree with rigid boundary profiles, the strict optimizer has all physical internal labels below half except for the entire two-trivalent-hub component, whose one internal label is half. This follows by cutting an edge: the pressure is \(f_A(1-z)+f_B(1-z)\), and each actual unturned product satisfies \(f_X'\ge f_2'\), strictly unless it is the isolated two-leaf product. Thus its derivative is negative above half and at half except in that one case. This is [component pressure comparison](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md). Consequently every nonexceptional whole bare vertex is in the regular all-low trace window at the original complete state. Its moving trace can be replaced by its complete trace with exponential relative error (9). The exceptional vertices are cubic and have exact moving/complete equality on the entire strict old window, since their raw degree is less than \(2N-1\). Hidden unturned-resolution labels can exceed half and remain in the original bulk domain. The original ordered positive resolutions supply exactly the previous primitive lattice and all \(d=N-1\) offsets. No turn is deleted from this local physical packet. Deleted/fused trees were only upper comparisons for error sectors. The actual clean packet uses the original tree, original physical edges and original peripheral marks. The canonical Gamma interpolation for \(H_N/W_r\) is regular on every compact \(0<x<1\), including half. Gate factorial arguments are bulk by strict old support. Circle angular factors require compact low incident labels; those follow from the original rigid/probe geometry. The strict Hessian, midpoint offsets, finite cotangent currents and positive elimination used in [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) are unchanged. The relative conditioning uses the positive complete wire majorant and the nonzero complete signed packet at the same \(N^{3/2}\) scale, not an unregrouped crossing-state total variation. The grouped errors in Sections 3–6 are estimated in the full physical fixed-power contraction before any circle contour is moved, exactly as in Section 4, equations (18)–(20), of the current grouped-packet proof. They remain an additive scalar error; no analytic angular continuation of an individually discarded sector is required. For the retained finite packet, every circle-incident index lies in its regular low interval. Its exact factors \(e_n(-2\cos\tau)\), canonical Gamma interpolation, and the original angular Gaussian give the same real-spectator and small-complex-strip estimates as Section 7 of that proof. Every circle has an incident edge, so each angular variable retains a strict Gaussian loss. The finite-current and endpoint estimates apply to this clean packet. The structural source gap, the wire box and the packet strip are fixed-tree choices independent of the filling powers. The compact meridian disk changes polynomial constants, not the complete action or the strict geometric/Fourier losses. ## 9. What is needed to pass to the filled invariant The new component estimate supplies the missing global source error bound. To obtain the filled nonzero asymptotic one must still use all of the established interfaces, in their original order: 1. The regular physical circle trace and its canonical Gamma wire interpolant retain the exact type, Cartan scalar, ordinary-circle normalization and the chosen entire continuation. They are the proofs in [regular physical circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md) and [direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md). 2. The finite original wire packet, its strict complex saddle, and its real-spectator angular Gaussian use the unchanged local window described in Section 8. All hidden unturned variables and physical-edge insertions remain in that packet. 3. The joint filling transform retains every charge. Its tail truncation has a fixed loss with real spectators, and its componentwise charge comparison treats independently long signed powers without comparing their ratios. A minimum local alias error is not compared with the total filled action drop. 4. The original marked geometry supplies the smooth fillings, the primitive peripheral equation and the absolute filled action. All pressure comparisons in this note end at the original augmented action; no fused comparison diagram contributes a substituted volume. These hypotheses are exactly those proved in [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) and [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md). Their proofs depend on the component class through the global grouped errors and the regular original window. Sections 6–8 supply those two inputs for every fixed strict bare component. The joint first-charge nonzero coefficient, reflected-sign sum and primitive Hessian are unchanged. Choose a structural error margin from the finitely many sectors above, together with the unchanged regular packet margin. The original long-filling implicit theorem makes the total action drop smaller than this margin when every fixed signed power is sufficiently long. The joint charge proof then handles arbitrarily unbalanced such powers. As before, the resulting slope threshold is fixed before \(N\) and before the disk radius \(R<1\). The subsequent maximum-principle extension changes starting levels and error constants, not that threshold. ## 10. Exact normalization and the resulting scope With the interfaces in Section 9, the formulas of [filled meridian-profile and volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md), equations (5)–(7b), retain their exact meaning for every fixed strict literal Conway tree, without the former singleton/trivalent/path alternative for bare components. In particular the reduced zero-framed scalar has marked meridian \(M=q_N^s\), and the exact factors remain \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad A_N(s)=q_N^{a(D)s^2/2},\qquad a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_i n_i. \tag{23} \] The reduced profile is \(A_NH_N(1+O(N^{-1}))\) on fixed \(R<1\), while the full modified dimension cancels exactly the one factor \(H_N\). The absolute exponent is the volume of the original filled knot complement. The first correction uses the original filled labels and the preferred cusp \[ \tau_K=a(D)+2i\sum_{e\ \mathrm{physical}} \cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}). \tag{24} \] No fused edge is removed from this sum; fusion appeared only in upper comparisons. The scalar ledger and the geometric preferred-longitude proof already apply to the full original strict class. This conclusion retains every other theorem hypothesis: a fixed literal ordered presentation and its strict positive domain; the original one-component/knot and framing conventions; the prescribed parity pattern and signed long powers fixed before the level; the two-leaf pure-leaf qualification; and the original marked filling completion. It does not classify arbitrary link diagrams or remove the need for a strict normalized presentation. A separate topological normalization theorem, if invoked, must still transport the full marked invariant rather than only its complete scalar. The [local pointwise counterexample](actual_main_meridian_same_index_obstruction.md) is fully compatible with this result. A one-high moving tensor can be exponentially larger than its same-index complete value. The proof bounds its difference by a reflected complete tensor, preserves its correlations by exact fusion, compares the whole fused pressure with the original one, and supplies the missing strict loss at an equality saddle through the Fourier tail. No step restores the disproved pointwise inequality.

title: The finite wire sum before the crossing traces
status: The finite wire sum near its complex critical point
text: # The finite wire sum before the crossing traces The polynomial contraction for a Conway construction sums over integer Newton indices on its internal edges. At a junction carrying a crossing circle, a polynomial trace remains to be evaluated. This note first sums the internal indices while keeping one angular variable for each such trace. The resulting finite function is called the wire packet. Near its geometric critical point, it has a uniform complex asymptotic with a nonzero leading coefficient. An exact representation of the finite lattice sum controls the boundary terms when the integration contours move. The crossing-circle traces are applied only after this common finite sum has been constructed. This order matters when filling coefficients are independently long: a local Fourier error cannot be compared with a product of independently filled exponents. The theorem below constructs the packet and evaluates its meridian-dependent insertion. The [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md) then compares the Fourier frequencies of the entire contraction. ## 1. Source, class, and the assertion Fix a [strict ordered Conway source](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md), with the stated knot and absence-of-internal-component hypotheses whenever a knot volume is mentioned. Use its reduced tree of ordered product junctions and physical quarter-turn edges. A **circle vertex** contains one original operator belonging to a crossing circle; an ordinary original leaf is a circle vertex of valence one. A **bare vertex** is a product junction containing no such operator. Thus this tree has \(H\ge2\) circle vertices, \(J\ge0\) bare vertices, and \(E=H+J-1\) edges. Every bare vertex has valence at least three. We retain the original orders, orientation types, closing mark and framing. The global source-to-window statement applies to every finite bare component. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) supplies a complete-tensor contraction and a grouped remainder satisfying \[ \|E_{\mathcal U,N}\|_{\mathcal J} \le e^{N(\Omega_{\mathcal U}-\eta_{\mathcal U}+o(1))}, \qquad \eta_{\mathcal U}>0. \tag{1} \] Here \(\Omega_{\mathcal U}\) is the maximum of the complete positive action after closing the component output by the norm comparison, with all incoming branch constants retained. The norm \(\mathcal J\) takes the maximum of the canonical polynomial's values at the complete roots and its first derivatives at the double roots; the odd simple root contributes only a value. These are the output pressure and full value-and-derivative norm defined in Section 1 of the component theorem. The action functions used below are \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\quad(0\le x\le1),\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x)\quad(0\le x\le\tfrac12). \] The complete-tensor contraction retains every internal complete-supported index and the actual deformed edge factors. The losses are fixed before the meridian disk radius and the fixed crossing powers. The other inputs are the physical cones in the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), the [regular bare trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_bare_trace.md), the [regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md), and the all-low fixed-power comparison in the [direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md), Section 7. Grouped errors are controlled in the original filled scalar before contour deformation; only the retained finite packet is analytically continued in the angular variables. Put \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad d=N-1,\quad m_N=\lfloor d/2\rfloor, \qquad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k2\sin(\pi a/N), \qquad e_k(z)=\frac{\prod_{a=0}^{k-1}(c_a-z)}{S_k^2}, \quad c_a=2\cos\frac{(2a+1)\pi}{N}. \tag{2} \] The main meridian is \(M=q^s\), with \(0\le R<1\) fixed and \(|s|\le R\). The fixed complete basis (2) is used also in the moving quotient. The exact metric is \(\phi_s(e_a e_b)=\mathbf1_{a+b=d}\).
