In lower-index convention the physical edge is \[ (T_e\mathbf J)_{ab}=\mathbf1_{a=b} \gamma_{e,N}(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_a(s)}, \qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}, \quad W_a(s)=\prod_{r=1}^a \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right). \tag{3} \] The prescribed six-type compiler determines the scalar \(\gamma_{e,N}\), a retained power of \(q^{s^2/2}\), or one. In particular the two labels on a physical turn edge are equal. Formula (3) must not be replaced by the weighted reversal on an upper coefficient vector. For all indices, \(H_N/W_a\) and its inverse are uniformly bounded on \(|s|\le R<1\). Choose one fixed ordered binary resolution of each complete bare tensor. Section 2 specifies its exact primitive coordinates and their offsets. Let \(\mathcal W\) be a sufficiently small rectangular box about their complete maximizing value. Define the finite polynomial \[ B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s)= \sum_{\mathbf k/N\in\mathcal W} \left(\prod_{g\text{ bare gate}}\mu_{N,g}(\mathbf k)\right) \left(\prod_{v\text{ circle}}\prod_{e\sim v} e_{n_e(\mathbf k)}(-2\cos\tau_v)\right) \left(\prod_{e}\gamma_{e,N}(s) \frac{H_N(s)}{W_{n_e(\mathbf k)}(s)}\right). \tag{4} \] Every affine index in (4) is the exact integer index, including all occurrences of \(d=N-1\). No crossing chirp and no factor \(\sin\tau_v\) is in (4). These belong to the subsequent trace functional. The packet is exactly separately even and \(2\pi\)-periodic in the angular variables. There are a real analytic action \(\Psi\), a nonzero analytic amplitude \(a\), a fixed complex angular polydisk, and a fixed small strip around the entire real angular cube, with the following properties. Write \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}(s)=\prod_e\gamma_{e,N}(s)\). Then on the local polydisk \[ B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s) =N^{3(1-H)/2}\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}(s) a(\boldsymbol\tau)e^{N\Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)} (1+O_R(N^{-1})). \tag{5} \] The error is uniformly holomorphic on a slightly larger polydisk. Both \(\Psi\) and \(a\) are separately even. If \(x_e^*\) is the complete normalized edge label, then \[ \Psi(0)=F_0, \qquad \Psi_{\tau_v\tau_w}(0) =-\mathbf1_{v=w}\frac1{2\pi} \sum_{e\sim v}\tan(\pi x_e^*). \tag{6} \] All diagonal curvatures in (6) are positive. Here \(F_0\) is the original complete positive source action, so the existing marked geometry identifies \(2\pi F_0\) with the volume of the original augmented complement. For constants \(A,c,C,y_0>0\), the exact finite packet also obeys \[ |B_N(\mathbf t+i\mathbf y,s)| \le N^A\exp N\{F_0-c\|\mathbf t\|^2+C\|\mathbf y\|^2\}, \quad |t_v|\le\pi,\quad |y_v|\le y_0,\quad |s|\le R. \tag{7} \] The same estimate, up to a constant factor, holds at endpoint translates of size \(O_R(N^{-1})\). Every fixed angular or main-parameter derivative satisfies the corresponding estimate with an additional power of \(N\) on a smaller strip. There is a more precise normalized insertion formula. Let \(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau)\) be the wire saddle below, and \(x_e(\boldsymbol\tau)\) its limiting edge labels. Uniformly on a smaller fixed complex polydisk, \[ \frac{B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s)} {\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}(s)B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,0)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e(\boldsymbol\tau))+O_R(N^{-2}). \tag{8} \] No first-order meridian-dependent amplitude is hidden in (8). ## 2. The exact bare resolution and primitive lattice At a bare vertex of valence \(D\ge3\), order its incident labels \(n_1,\ldots,n_D\) according to the chosen original multiplication association. Associativity permits a sequential notation for the same positive resolution; it does not assert a tangle isotopy. The original nonnegative multiplication coefficient is \[ \mu_{ij}^{r}= \frac{S_{i+j}S_r} {S_iS_jS_{r-i}S_{r-j}S_{i+j-r}}, \quad i+j\le d,\quad\max(i,j)\le r\le i+j, \tag{9} \] and is zero outside this support. Set \(r_1=n_1\) and \(r_{D-1}=d-n_D\). The exact complete trace is \[ \phi_0\left(\prod_{a=1}^D e_{n_a}\right) =\sum_{r_2,\ldots,r_{D-2}} \prod_{a=2}^{D-1}\mu_{r_{a-1},n_a}^{r_a}. \tag{10} \] The final multiplication by \(e_{n_D}\), followed by the trace, has coefficient one after the exact condition \(r_{D-1}+n_D=d\) is imposed. It contributes no additional free variable or nontrivial gate. Thus (10) has \(D-3\) hidden integer variables and \(D-2\) nontrivial gates. All signs and factors in (9) are the complete source factors, not an asymptotic surrogate. Use the edge indices together with the hidden variables in (10) as coordinates. They are independent integer coordinates before inequalities are imposed. There are \[ K=E+\sum_{v\text{ bare}}(D_v-3), \qquad G=\sum_{v\text{ bare}}(D_v-2) \tag{11} \] free coordinates and nontrivial bare gates, respectively. Every remaining index has the form \(N\ell(\mathbf y)+\delta\), where \(\mathbf y=\mathbf k/N\), \(\ell\) is integral affine and \(\delta\) is a fixed integer. In particular \(d-n_D=N(1-y_D)-1\). The full coordinate lattice is \(\mathbb Z^K\); there is no parity-dependent sublattice or determinant factor. The tree has no further closing equation after the covariant edge variables and the local complements in (10) are imposed. This count is different from \(2H-3\), the count before circle vertices are contracted. Indeed a pure circle tensor at valence \(D\) can be positively expanded using the complete leaf \(h_N=T_0L_N\) and \(D-1\) multiplication outputs. Those \(D-1\) variables have already been eliminated in (4). Restoring all of them recovers exactly \(2H-3\). Let \(D_c=\sum_{v\text{ circle}}D_v\) and \(D_b=\sum_{v\text{ bare}}D_v\). Since \(D_c+D_b=2E\), the number \(G\) and the lattice dimension satisfy \[ G=D_b-2J, \qquad K=E+D_b-3J, \qquad -D_c-\frac32G+\frac12K=\frac32(1-H). \tag{12} \] This is the power of \(N\) in (5). Each basis evaluation has power \(N^{-1}\), each nontrivial bare gate \(N^{-3/2}\), and the primitive wire Gaussian contributes \(N^{K/2}\). Subsequent circle integrations, each with \(N^2\) trace factor and \(N^{-1/2}\) Gaussian factor, recover \(N^{3/2}\) for the whole source. This last bookkeeping does not itself prove any filled asymptotic. ## 3. Original action and the strict grouped optimizer The [complete-edge theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md) determines the regularity needed here. Circle-incident labels are strictly in \((0,1/2)\). Physical edges inside a bare component are also strictly below half, except when that component consists of two trivalent junctions with two rigid boundary branches at each. Its one internal label equals half. This follows by cutting an edge and comparing its two unturned profiles; it does not require a lower bound on the number of branches at a junction. All internal indices remain in the finite sum. In the exceptional two-junction case the edge is allowed to cross half within a compact subset of \((0,1)\). Its two cubic traces agree exactly with their complete traces on the strict old support. Hidden unturned product indices retain their original strict bulk ranges in every component. At a bare vertex, summing its strict binary inequalities gives \[ \sum_{e\sim v}x_e^*-1 =\sum_{g\text{ at }v}(x_g+y_g-z_g)>0. \tag{13} \] A sufficiently small retained-edge neighborhood therefore has all labels in \([\delta,1-\delta]\), all circle-incident labels in \([\delta,1/2-\delta]\), and every bare incident sum at least \(1+\delta\), for some \(\delta>0\). Every nonexceptional component also has its physical internal labels in a compact low interval. Here is why the grouped wire action has exactly the original maximum, rather than an independently optimized upper budget. At completeness, for a product \(E=\prod_{a=1}^D e_{n_a}\) of low basis elements, \[ \phi_0(L_NE)=N\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}E(c_r), \qquad N(\pi/4)^D E(-2)\le\phi_0(L_NE)\le N^2E(-2). \tag{14} \] At odd levels the lower constant is one. At even levels, for the node closest to \(-2\), \[ \frac{e_n(-2\cos(\pi/N))}{e_n(-2)} =\prod_{a=0}^{n-1} \frac{\cos(a\pi/N)\cos((a+1)\pi/N)} {\cos^2((a+1/2)\pi/N)} \ge\frac N2\tan\frac{\pi}{2N}\ge\frac\pi4. \tag{15} \] The product decreases over the low range and its endpoint is the displayed value. Every summand in the node sum is nonnegative. Equations (14)–(15) retain both parities and the simple odd endpoint. The complete leaf has positive coefficients \([e_r]h_N=N^2S_{2r}/S_r^4\) for \(r\le m_N\) and zero otherwise. Indeed \([e_r]h_N=\phi_0(L_Ne_r)\); the complete node sum is \(N^2\) times the zero Laurent coefficient of \(e_r(-u-u^{-1})\), because its Laurent degree is \(r<N\), and that coefficient is \(S_{2r}/S_r^4\) in the low range. High \(e_r\) vanish at every complete node. Expanding the product \(E\) using (9), the identity \(L_N=T_0h_N\) makes the circle trace (14) an exact positive sum of these leaf coefficients and complete gates. Thus the original positive source can be expanded first at all circle vertices and then at bare vertices, without a signed cancellation or a changed source. The rate of (14), uniformly on a regular incident-index neighborhood, is \(\sum_{a=1}^D g(x_a)\). Its positive finite expansion has the original compact constrained action; uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state counting imply that its conditional maximum is precisely that sum. At the projected original strict state its hidden maximizer is strict. The leaf and gate Hessians make the hidden Hessian negative definite there, so the maximizing hidden variables continue analytically for nearby incident variables. Therefore eliminating those variables gives the actual analytic phase \(\sum g(x_a)\), including its derivatives, not merely a numerical equality at one point. For each strict gate write \[ m(x,y,z)=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y) -J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). \tag{16} \] The grouped phase at zero angles is consequently \[ A(\mathbf y,0)=\sum_{g\text{ bare}}m(x_g,y_g,z_g) +\sum_{v\text{ circle}}\sum_{e\sim v}g(x_e). \tag{17} \] It has the original maximum \(F_0\) and the projected original strict maximizer \(\mathbf y^*\). The exact positive expansion above also shows that its compact complement has a strict original-source gap. More directly, \(g''<0\) on \((0,1/2)\), and the retained gate action \(m\) has a negative definite three-variable Hessian in its strict domain. These facts are proved from the original volume atoms in the [general core packet theorem](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md), Sections 1 and 3–5. Every circle-incident edge variable is covered by a \(g\) term; every remaining edge and every hidden bare variable is an argument of a retained \(m\). Hence the combined Hessian in the primitive coordinates is negative definite. Global concavity then gives uniqueness of the grouped maximum. Choose the rectangular box \(\mathcal W\) about \(\mathbf y^*\) so its closure is entirely strict. All affine factorial arguments in every bare gate lie in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1)\), circle-incident edges are regular low, bare–bare edges stay in the interior of \((0,1)\), and (13) holds throughout the box. For all sufficiently large \(N\), every point of the entire integer box is an actual supported state; no indicator changes there. ## 4. What is replaced before the packet is used The source-to-window reduction is an absolute error statement at the augmented exponent \(F_0\). It is not a relative error assertion at a filled critical action. First, the [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) gives a fixed loss for every nonempty multiplication correction and every high component-boundary contribution. Its clean term uses complete tensors and retains all internal indices in their complete support. The estimate applies to the actual fixed crossing \(R_s^n\) in place of \(R_s^\epsilon L_j\): a fixed power and its inverse have polynomial spectral norm on \(|s|\le R<1\), and the actual decorated extractor produces the required low/high coefficient cone. Inherited full-cone losses pass through the component by homogeneity in its boundary constants. The finite minimum of the structural gaps is positive. Prefactors may depend on the fixed powers; these exponential losses do not. For the remaining contraction, the component boundary indices are low and every bare tensor is complete. Its positive resolution gives a coefficientwise majorant with the original boundary profiles; a spectral norm is not substituted for that comparison. At a circle vertex and for any low product \(E\), the actual fixed-power trace has the same-level bound \[ |\phi_\sigma(R_\sigma^nE)| \le C_{n,R,D}N\,\phi_0(L_NE), \qquad |\sigma|\le R<1. \tag{18} \] One direct proof uses the exact shifted root sum for generic \(\sigma\), on a larger parameter circle where \(\sin2\pi\sigma\) is bounded away from zero. Each shifted root has angular imaginary height \(O(N^{-1})\). Positivity of the Laurent coefficients of \(E(-u-u^{-1})\) bounds its value by \(C E(-2)\); the fixed-power full chirp has bounded modulus on this grid. The root sum is at most \(C N^2E(-2)\). Divide by the lower bound (14), then apply the maximum principle to the whole holomorphic trace to include the collisions \(\sigma=0,\pm1/2\). This proves (18) with the full normal data. Constant opposite-color types have the same bound with their prescribed scalar retained. Complete bare tensors have the positive expansion (10). Together with (18), the clean component comparison bounds the remaining contraction by a polynomial times the original pure positive reference. An edge assignment outside the neighborhood in (13) misses its unique optimizer and has a fixed action loss. This proves the off-edge-window estimate before any circle contour is moved. Inside that neighborhood, a trivalent bare trace is exactly unchanged. Indeed the old pair support gives \(i+j+k\le3d/2<2N-1\). In division by \(P_0\), the quotient has degree at most \(N-2\); the constant change \(P_0\mapsto P_0+\Delta_\sigma\) cannot change the remainder's coefficient of degree \(N-1\). Thus \(\phi_\sigma(e_i e_j e_k)=\phi_0(e_i e_j e_k)\), including the full internal label range. At every nonexceptional vertex, the local replacement used by the component theorem has the regular estimate \[ \phi_\sigma\left(\prod_{e\sim v}e_{n_e}\right) =\phi_0\left(\prod_{e\sim v}e_{n_e}\right) (1+O_R(e^{-\kappa_vN})), \tag{19} \] uniformly over the physical indices, both parities and \(|\sigma|\le R\). It uses precisely the compact low-index and incident-sum hypotheses in (13). For valence at most four the identity is exact. For higher valence it follows from strict Fourier-tail separation in the [regular bare trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_bare_trace.md). These finitely many local replacements are already included in the grouped component error. Equivalently, multiplying them out with (18) and the positive reference bounds their total by \(N^A e^{N(F_0-\kappa)}\). No independent relative errors of oscillatory filled tensors are multiplied. After this replacement, resolve every complete bare tensor by (10). The positive reference now bounds the sum of any subset of these resolved states. Its strict optimizer projects to \(\mathbf y^*\), and removing the grouped primitive box \(\mathcal W\) has a fixed loss. This is the hidden-variable part of the off-window argument, not a claim that an unresolved scalar upper bound controls every uncontracted path. Consequently the exact original source, after its recorded outer framing and cut factors have been kept, differs from applying the actual circle trace functionals to (4) by \[ O\!\left(N^A e^{N(F_0-\eta_0)}\right), \qquad \eta_0>0. \tag{20} \] The number \(\eta_0\) can be chosen below the finite minimum of the component losses, the original compact-complement losses, and the regular bare losses. These are geometric or closed coefficient-rate losses. Thus one fixed positive choice works for every compact main disk \(R<1\), with constants and the starting level depending on \(R\); the finite Fourier multipliers, fixed-power polynomial bounds and bounded edge factors affect only those constants. It is also independent of how large the fixed crossing powers subsequently are. This statement does not compare (20) with a filled exponent; that requires the joint saddle. ## 5. Canonical analytic interpolation and the finite summand Use the canonical marked sine-factorial interpolation \[ G_N(z)=\left(\frac{2\pi}{N}\right)^z\Gamma(z+1) \prod_{a\ge1} \frac{\Gamma(Na+z+1)}{\Gamma(Na-z)(Na)^{2z+1}}. \tag{21} \] It is zero-free on \(-1<\Re z<N\), equals \(S_k\) at integer \(k\), and satisfies \(G_N(z+1)/G_N(z)=2\sin(\pi(z+1)/N)\). The positive real marks and their analytic continuations are those in [exact factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md); no arbitrary continuation of grid values is used. On fixed bulk complex compact sets, \[ G_N(N\alpha+c)=\sqrt{2N\sin\pi\alpha}\, e^{NJ(\alpha)}(2\sin\pi\alpha)^c (1+O(N^{-1})), \tag{22} \] with uniform fixed derivatives and further uniform inverse-power expansions. The fixed integer \(c\) must be kept. Replace the factorials in (9) by (21), with their exact affine arguments. For the circle-incidence factors, put \(u=N\tau/(2\pi)\) and use \[ \mathcal E_N(x,\tau)= \frac{G_N(d/2+u)G_N(d/2-u)} {G_N(d/2-Nx+u)G_N(d/2-Nx-u)G_N(Nx)^2}. \tag{23} \] The shift equation proves \(\mathcal E_N(n/N,\tau)=e_n(-2\cos\tau)\) exactly. On a fixed complex neighborhood of the regular wire box and a fixed small angular polydisk, every argument is in a regular bulk strip. Formula (22), including the \(-1/2\) midpoint offsets, gives \[ \mathcal E_N(x,\tau) =\frac{e^{Nb(x,\tau)}}{2N\sin\pi x}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad b(x,\tau)=\int_0^x \log\{2\cos(2\pi u)+2\cos\tau\}\,du-2J(x). \tag{24} \] The logarithm is continued from its positive value at real \(x\in(0,1/2)\), \(\tau=0\). In particular \(b(x,0)=g(x)\). If an exact index is \(N\ell(\mathbf y)+\delta\), substitute \(x=\ell+\delta/N\) in (23). Its leading amplitude then includes \(e^{\delta b_x(\ell,\tau)}\). The proof retains these factors by the exact interpolation rather than renormalizing them away. The exact edge continuation is \[ \mathcal I_N(x,s) =\frac{G_N(Nx)^2}{G_N(Nx-s)G_N(Nx+s)}. \tag{25} \] Indeed \(G_N(s)G_N(-s)=1/H_N(s)\), and the shift equation gives \(\mathcal I_N(n/N,s)=H_N(s)/W_n(s)\). Uniformly on the fixed complex regular wire tube and \(|s|\le R<1\), \[ \mathcal I_N(x,s) =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N}\cot(\pi x)+O_R(N^{-2}). \tag{26} \] To verify the sign, put \(L_N(z)=\log G_N(z)\). Then \(L_N''(Nx)=\pi\cot(\pi x)/N+O(N^{-2})\), and \[ 2L_N(Nx)-L_N(Nx-s)-L_N(Nx+s) =-s^2L_N''(Nx)+O(N^{-3}). \] All fixed derivatives have the same uniform bounds on smaller tubes. Let \(\mathcal A(\mathbf y,\boldsymbol\tau)\) be the sum of the gate actions (16) and the circle-incidence actions \(b(x_e,\tau_v)\). Combining (22)–(26), the exact interpolated summand of (4), divided by \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}\), is \[ N^a\,\beta_N(\mathbf y,\boldsymbol\tau) e^{N\mathcal A(\mathbf y,\boldsymbol\tau)} \prod_e\mathcal I_N(n_e/N,s), \qquad a=-D_c-\frac32G, \tag{27} \] where \(\beta_N=\beta+O(N^{-1})\) is uniformly holomorphic and \(\beta\) is nonzero, positive at real zero angles. It contains every \(d\)-offset and every square-root mark. The phase is independent of \(s\) and is separately even in the angular variables. ## 6. The finite lattice contour and its endpoint currents The exact finite lattice sum, rather than a formal integral, is treated as follows. At zero angles its phase has the strict nondegenerate maximum \(\mathbf y^*\) in the primitive box. The implicit-function theorem gives a unique holomorphic wire saddle \(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau)\) on a fixed complex angular polydisk. Put \[ \Psi(\boldsymbol\tau)=\mathcal A(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau),\boldsymbol\tau), \qquad Q(\boldsymbol\tau)=-\mathcal A_{yy}(y_*,\boldsymbol\tau). \tag{28} \] The matrix \(Q\) is positive definite at zero. Choose its determinant square root by the original positive real Gaussian. For each primitive coordinate enclose precisely its retained finite integer interval by a rectangle whose vertical sides are half-grid lines and whose horizontal sides have imaginary heights \(\pm h\). The product residue formula with kernels \(\pi N\cot(\pi Nz)\) is exactly the sum (4). The endpoints differ from the chosen real box by \(O(N^{-1})\). On a vertical half-grid side the cotangent has modulus at most one; on horizontal sides, \[ \cot(\pi N(x+ih))=-i+O(e^{-2\pi Nh}), \qquad \cot(\pi N(x-ih))= i+O(e^{-2\pi Nh}). \tag{29} \] At zero angular parameter the phase gains at most \(O(h^2)\) under these imaginary translations. The real boundary has a fixed strict loss. Choose \(h\) first so this gain is smaller than both half the boundary loss and \(\pi h\), and then shrink the fixed angular polydisk. Every contour with a vertical coordinate is exponentially below \(\Re\Psi\); every nonconstant cotangent mode has the factor \(e^{-2\pi Nh}\) and loses an exponential after allowing the phase gain. Uniformly bounded edge insertions and their derivatives do not change these losses. The constant horizontal terms add to \(N^K\) times the ordinary integral over the real box. Their connectors and the \(O(N^{-1})\)-wide changes of endpoints have the same boundary loss. Deform this integral to \(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau)+(\mathcal W-\mathbf y^*)\). This stays inside the fixed tube, its connecting faces have a fixed loss, and its real translated tangent plane has a uniformly negative real quadratic part. Gaussian expansion now gives \[ a(\boldsymbol\tau)= \frac{(2\pi)^{K/2}\beta(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau),\boldsymbol\tau)} {\sqrt{\det Q(\boldsymbol\tau)}}. \tag{30} \] It is nonzero near zero. Odd Gaussian corrections integrate to zero; the first relative remainder is \(O(N^{-1})\), holomorphic on a fixed neighborhood. Equation (12) gives the power in (5). This is the same finite-contour argument as the [finite complex-window Laplace theorem](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md), Section 3, applied to the actual grouped lattice rather than reusing its ungrouped dimension. Every factor in (27) is separately even in each angle. Uniqueness gives the same symmetry to \(y_*,\Psi,a\). Also \(\mathcal A_{y\tau_v}(\mathbf y,0)=0\) identically in the wire variables. Direct differentiation of (24) gives \[ b_{\tau\tau}(x,0)=-\frac{\tan\pi x}{2\pi}. \tag{31} \] Thus the usual Schur-complement correction to the angular Hessian vanishes at zero, proving (6). This is an exact consequence of the even source, not an assumed diagonal approximation. The same contour proves the insertion rule used in (8). For any fixed holomorphic function \(c(\mathbf y,\boldsymbol\tau)\), the normalized finite sum with this extra factor is \(c(y_*(\boldsymbol\tau),\boldsymbol\tau)+O(N^{-1})\), uniformly holomorphically. To see the error order, expand \(c\) about the saddle: its linear Gaussian term is odd, while the quadratic term and the linear term paired with the cubic phase correction cost \(N^{-1}\). The exponentially small finite-grid currents remain negligible. Expand the product of (26), apply this insertion rule to \(-\pi s^2\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e)\), and bound its \(O(N^{-2})\) remainder on the deformed Gaussian contour. Dividing by the nonzero saddle expansion at \(s=0\) proves (8). No unknown common coefficient of order \(N^{-1}\) is needed, because it cancels in the ratio. ## 7. Global angular bounds and real spectators Fix a compact regular interval \(I\subset(0,1/2)\). For a physical \(n/N\in I\), there are \(c,C,y_0>0\) such that \[ |e_n(-2\cos(t+iv))| \le N^A e^{Ng(n/N)}e^{-Nct^2+NCv^2}, \qquad |t|\le\pi,\quad |v|\le y_0. \tag{32} \] Here is a proof that separates the regular center from moving numerator zeros. On a fixed small disk about \(t=0\), every numerator factor is nonzero. The exact finite product is even, and its logarithmic second derivative at zero is \[ -\frac12\sum_{a=0}^{n-1} \sec^2\frac{\pi(a+1/2)}N =-\frac{N}{2\pi}\tan(\pi n/N)+O(N^{-1}). \tag{33} \] All fixed higher derivatives of the logarithm are \(O_I(N)\). Together with \(e_n(-2)=e^{Ng(n/N)}[2N\sin(\pi n/N)]^{-1}(1+O(N^{-1}))\), this gives (32) near the center by an even analytic Taylor estimate. On the compact real complement, the limiting numerator logarithmic integral is strictly smaller than its value at zero. In fact it is the integral of \(\log|1-e^{iu}|\) over a circular arc of fixed length \(4\pi x\); for \(0<x<1/2\) this is uniquely largest when the arc is centered opposite its singularity. This is exactly the circular rearrangement argument in the [root-star localization theorem](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), Section 7. Uniform truncated logarithmic Riemann sums provide the closed upper bound even when numerator zeros move or coalesce. The negative logarithmic tails of the two circle-distance factors are uniformly integrable; denominator factorial errors are \(O(\log N)\). Thus the compact complement has a fixed exponential loss, uniformly in \(x\in I\). Continuity of this logarithmic integral preserves half the loss on a sufficiently small complex strip. The uniform \(o(1)\) in the finite upper estimate is absorbed in another quarter of that loss for all sufficiently large \(N\). Reducing \(c\) so \(c\pi^2\) is smaller than the remaining loss proves (32) on the complement. This absorption is why a polynomial prefactor is legitimate in (32), although a global complete-core recurrence bound at arbitrary indices only has a uniform \(e^{No(1)}\) prefactor. No uniform polynomial core bound at collisions has been assumed. In (4) every circle-incident edge index stays in one such compact interval. Apply (32) at every circle incidence. All bare coefficients in (4) are nonnegative, and the edge ratios are uniformly bounded. The zero-angle positive sum has rate \(F_0\) with a polynomial bound, either by (5) at zero or directly by the regular factorial expansion and fixed-dimensional Laplace estimate. Summing yields (7), with a strictly positive angular loss for every circle since every circle has an incident edge. The actual polynomial in each angle is periodic. Therefore replacing a real endpoint \(\pm\pi\) by \(\pm\pi+O(N^{-1})\) changes the relevant squared distance to the nearest multiple of \(2\pi\) by only \(O(N^{-1})\). This costs a bounded factor in (7). Complex translations of height \(O(N^{-1})\) are also permitted. Consequently endpoint currents with real spectator variables, or spectators on their physical translated grids, retain a fixed angular loss. No spectator is required to lie on a slope-dependent complex contour for this assertion. Cauchy's estimate on disks of radius \(1/N\), and on a slightly larger main-parameter disk, supplies the stated derivative bounds. ## 8. Applying the crossing traces Let \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma,N}[f]=\phi_\sigma(R_\sigma^n f^\sharp)\), where \(f(\tau)=f^\sharp(-2\cos\tau)\). With its full crossing scalar, \[ R_\sigma^n(z_r(\sigma)) =C_{N,n}(\sigma)e^{inN\tau_r(\sigma)^2/(4\pi)}, \quad C_{N,n}(\sigma)=q^{n(d^2/4-\sigma^2/2)}, \quad\tau_r(\sigma)=\frac{2\pi}{N}(d/2+\sigma-r). \tag{34} \] The actual orientation type selects \(\sigma_v=s,-s\), or \(0\), and supplies its recorded reference scalar \(\rho_{v,N}(s)\). Keep the original closing/framing scalar \(\zeta_N(s)\) separate, and define \[ \widehat\zeta_N(s)=\zeta_N(s)\prod_v\rho_{v,N}(s). \tag{34a} \] The per-type factors are specified in the [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md); the [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md), (4a), uses the same combined-factor convention. The edge product remains exactly \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{edge},N}\). The exact polynomial functionals in distinct angular variables commute as evaluations of a fixed tensor contraction. This is not a statement that physical tangles commute. The source-to-packet conclusion has the form \[ \mathcal F_N(q^s) =\widehat\zeta_N(s)H_N(s) \left(\prod_{v=1}^H\mathcal D_{n_v,\sigma_v(s),N}^{(v)}\right) B_N(\boldsymbol\tau,s) +O\!\left(N^Ae^{N(F_0-\eta_0)}\right), \tag{35} \] with the harmless outer elementary factors understood in the displayed normalization. Equation (34a) records the closing/framing and reference factors explicitly; there is exactly one primitive main-cut factor \(H_N\). The edge scalars in (4) are not counted again in \(\widehat\zeta_N\). Formula (35) includes the high-state, off-window and moving-bare replacement errors described in Section 4. It asserts neither that the error is relative to a filled scalar nor that a first local Fourier charge may be selected independently at every circle. The packet is precisely suitable for the joint transfer: exact separate evenness, a nonzero complex wire saddle, diagonal negative angular Hessian, a fixed angular corridor, and real-spectator endpoint bounds. The [joint filling transform](actual_main_meridian_joint_filling_transform.md), Sections 3–5, proves the charge comparison and controls the nonperiodic endpoint currents. It uses (4)–(8) as inputs; it is not used to prove them. The resulting invariant statement appears in the [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md). The present proof uses the original positive source action and its strict geometric optimizer, but does not import an old filled-invariant volume asymptotic. A subsequent joint first-charge calculation can supply its own nonzero filled amplitude; identifying that action geometrically is a separate marked-action statement. If that later transfer selects a nondegenerate joint first-charge saddle, the analytic insertion proof above can be applied once more to the combined wire-and-angle contour. After retaining the exact product of edge, crossing, reference and framing scalars outside, the residual edge multiplier is \[ 1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N} \sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}) +O_R(N^{-2}). \tag{36} \] Here \(x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}\) denotes the generally complex wire value at that **filled** joint saddle. It must not be replaced by the complete value \(x_e^*\). This is a conditional Gaussian insertion corollary, not a cusp identification. The common first saddle coefficient cancels in the ratio; exponentially smaller charges and endpoint currents must first be controlled by the separate joint argument. No conclusion about a growing slope, a fixed neighborhood in the meridian coordinate, or an arbitrary main-meridian ordinary-color subtraction follows from the packet theorem.

title: A reflected trace bound for one high Newton index
status: A reflected trace bound for one high Newton index
text: # A reflected trace bound for one high Newton index The finite tangle algebra is written in a Newton polynomial basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_{N-1}\). In this note an index is **high** when it exceeds \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). This is an internal basis index, not an auxiliary crossing-circle color. Its distinction from a low index matters because the high polynomial has signed Fourier coefficients and vanishes at the complete spectral nodes, while its derivatives at repeated roots need not vanish. When one high basis polynomial is multiplied by several low ones, moving the main meridian can make the trace exponentially larger than its complete value. The useful comparison concerns the difference of the two traces. Its first Fourier alias cancels exactly. The remaining difference is bounded by a positive complete trace in which the high index \(h\) is replaced by \(N-1-h\). In a regular low-index window there is a further strict exponential loss. The proof below retains both level parities, all Fourier aliases, and the coefficient trace at repeated roots. Section 5 explains how the reflected index is used in a whole ordered tree through the [component-pressure comparison](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md). The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) combines this bound with the other index sectors. The comparison does not identify the two diagrams produced by deleting a turn, and it does not assert a bound by the same-index complete trace. ## 1. Exact Fourier coefficients of a high Newton polynomial Fix an integer \(N\ge2\), and put \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad d=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor d/2\rfloor, \quad S_j=\prod_{v=1}^j2\sin(\pi v/N),\quad S_0=1, \qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N). \tag{1} \] The fixed polynomial and the coefficient trace are \[ e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{v=0}^{j-1}(c_v-z),\qquad P_s(z)=\mathsf T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s),\qquad \phi_s(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F. \tag{2} \] Here \(\mathsf T_N(u+u^{-1})=u^N+u^{-N}\). The remainder is a polynomial of degree less than \(N\); it retains both the value and first normal at a repeated root. Write \(\eta=(-1)^{N+1}\). Suppose \(m<h\le d\), and set \(a=N-h\) and \(v=2h-N\ge0\). The Fourier expansion has a central gap: \[ e_h(-u-u^{-1})=\sum_{k=-h}^{h}A_k u^k, \qquad A_k=0\quad (|k|<a). \tag{3} \] For the two remaining tails its coefficients are exactly \[ \boxed{\quad A_k=(-1)^{h-|k|} \frac{S_{2h-N}}{S_h^2S_{|k|-a}S_{h-|k|}}, \qquad a\le |k|\le h. \quad} \tag{4} \] Every factorial in (4) has index between zero and \(N-1\). In particular (4) includes the even-level endpoint \(h=N/2\): then \(v=0\), and the only coefficients are \(A_h=A_{-h}=S_h^{-2}\). To prove this directly, factor the numerator as a string of consecutive odd powers: \[ e_h(-u-u^{-1})= \frac{u^{-h}}{S_h^2} \prod_{j=0}^{h-1}(1+q^{2j+1}u)(1+q^{-2j-1}u). \tag{5} \] The \(2h\) factors have exponents \(-2h+1,-2h+3,\ldots,2h-1\). Removing one complete cycle of \(N\) factors leaves the exact identity \[ \prod_{j=0}^{h-1}(1+q^{2j+1}u)(1+q^{-2j-1}u) =(1-\eta u^N)\prod_{j=0}^{v-1}(1-q^{2j-v+1}u). \tag{6} \] The last product is one when \(v=0\). Its finite binomial expansion is \[ \prod_{j=0}^{v-1}(1-q^{2j-v+1}u) =\sum_{l=0}^v(-1)^l\frac{S_v}{S_lS_{v-l}}u^l. \tag{7} \] This follows by the two-term coefficient recurrence for a finite geometric product; no root-of-unity factorial is divided by a zero factor. Multiplication by \(1-\eta u^N\) gives the negative-frequency interval \([-h,-a]\) and the positive-frequency interval \([a,h]\). In the latter interval \(k=a+l\), and \(-\eta(-1)^l=(-1)^{h-k}\). Symmetry under \(u\mapsto u^{-1}\) gives the other interval. This proves (3)–(4), including their signs. There is a useful interpretation of its closed coefficient rate. Define \[ J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi y)\,dy, \quad g(t)=J(2t)-4J(t), \quad b_t(w)=J(2t)-2J(t)-J(t+w)-J(t-w). \tag{8} \] For \(\alpha=(N-h)/N\) and \(w=k/N>0\), the uniform sine-factorial estimate gives \[ \frac1N\log|A_k| =H_\alpha(w)+O(\log N/N), \quad H_\alpha(w)=-J(2\alpha)+2J(\alpha) -J(w-\alpha)+J(w+\alpha). \tag{9} \] The error is uniform on the closed coefficient support. Reflection \(J(1-t)=-J(t)\) and duplication \(J(2t)=2J(t)-2J(1/2-t)\) yield \[ H_\alpha(w)=b_{1/2-\alpha}(w-1/2)-g(1/2-\alpha). \tag{10} \] Thus the absolute coefficient rates are those of a low finite packet centered at frequency \(1/2\), normalized to have maximum rate zero. The signs in (4) still alternate. Formula (10) is not a positive expansion of the actual high polynomial. For later use, the full coefficient norm has a polynomial bound \[ \sum_{k=-h}^h|A_k|\le C N^C, \qquad m<h<N. \tag{11} \] One proof applies the uniform factorial estimate in (9): strict concavity of \(b_t\) gives \(b_t(w)\le b_t(0)=g(t)\), also by continuity at the endpoints. There are at most \(2N\) coefficients. Alternatively, the established high Newton spectral-jet bound and complete Hermite interpolation give a polynomial sup norm on \([-2,2]\); each Fourier coefficient is bounded by that sup norm. Both arguments concern the actual fixed polynomial, including its normals. ## 2. The first alias cancels in the trace difference Let \(F=\prod_{j=1}^B e_{n_j}\), where \(B\) is fixed and \(0\le n_j\le m\). Write \[ F(-u-u^{-1})=\sum_{k=-D}^D f_k u^k, \qquad D=\sum_j n_j. \tag{12} \] These coefficients are nonnegative, symmetric and unimodal. Indeed each low factor has coefficients \[ [u^{k-n}]e_n(-u-u^{-1}) =\frac{S_{2n}}{S_n^2S_kS_{2n-k}}, \qquad 0\le k\le2n<N; \tag{13} \] the successive ratio proves unimodality. Decomposing each factor as a nonnegative sum of centered interval indicators shows that convolution preserves it. We set \(f_k=0\) outside the support. For any polynomial \(G\), if \(G(-u-u^{-1})=\sum g_k u^k\), the exact finite Fourier trace is \[ \phi_s(G)=N^2\sum_{l\ge1}\eta^{l+1} (g_{lN-1}-g_{lN+1})U_{l-1}(\cos2\pi s). \tag{14} \] Only finitely many terms occur. This identity is a polynomial quotient identity and therefore includes the collision values of \(s\). It follows either from the generic simple-root residue sum followed by polynomial continuation, or from the exact monic Chebyshev reduction. At \(s=0\), \(U_{l-1}(1)=l\). Apply (14) to \(G=e_hF\). Since \(U_0=1\), its first alias cancels exactly in \(\phi_s(G)-\phi_0(G)\). Every remaining Fourier coefficient is evaluated at an absolute frequency at least \(2N-1\). Equations (11)–(12) and unimodality give \[ |g_{lN\pm1}|\le C N^C f_{lN-1-h} \le C N^C f_{2N-1-h},\qquad l\ge2. \tag{15} \] The number of aliases is bounded in terms of \(B\). Moreover \(U_{l-1}(\cos2\pi s)-l\) is divisible by \(\Delta_s=2\cos2\pi s-2\), with a quotient bounded on any fixed disk. Therefore, for every fixed \(R<\infty\), \[ \sup_{|s|\le R}\frac{|(\phi_s-\phi_0)(e_hF)|}{|\Delta_s|} \le C_{B,R}N^{C_B} f_{2N-1-h}. \tag{16} \] At zeros of \(\Delta_s\), the quotient is understood as its polynomial continuation. No estimate in this section assumes a sign for the high coefficients or an absence of higher aliases. ## 3. Recovering a positive complete comparison at both parities Set \(r=d-h\), so \(0\le r\le m\), and put \(C=e_rF\). Its Laurent coefficients \(c_k\) are nonnegative, symmetric and unimodal. The positive endpoint coefficient of the extra low factor is \([u^r]e_r=S_r^{-2}\); hence \[ c_{N-1}\ge S_r^{-2}f_{N-1-r} \ge N^{-1}f_{N+r} =N^{-1}f_{2N-1-h}. \tag{17} \] Here \(S_r^2\le N\): the successive sine factors first decrease the partial products and then increase them up to the midpoint product, whose square is \(N\) at odd levels and \(N/2\) at even levels. The two frequencies in (17) satisfy \(N-1-r\ge0\) and \(N-1-r\le N+r\). The interval-tail lemma gives \[ c_{N-1}\le(2m+1)^{B+1}(c_{N-1}-c_{N+1}). \tag{18} \] For clarity, that lemma states that a convolution of \(B+1\) nonnegative symmetric unimodal sequences supported on \([-m,m]\) satisfies \(c_k\le(2m+1)^{B+1}(c_k-c_{k+2})\) for \(k\ge m\). After the interval-indicator decomposition, a nonzero integer convolution strictly decreases in its upper tail, so its positive two-step difference is at least one while its value is at most the product of the interval lengths. This includes zero radii and support endpoints. At even levels the complete trace itself has alternating alias signs, so (18) cannot simply be summed into it. A fixed-dimensional interpolation recovers the first difference instead. Put \[ d_l=c_{lN-1}-c_{lN+1},\qquad Q_N(X)=\sum_{l=1}^{B+1}\eta^{l+1}d_lU_{l-1}(X). \tag{19} \] Absent aliases are assigned coefficient zero. Formula (14) gives \(Q_N(\cos2\pi s)=N^{-2}\phi_s(C)\). Choose once and for all \(B+1\) distinct real parameters in \([0,1/8)\). Their cosine values are distinct, so evaluation in the basis \(U_0,\ldots,U_B\) is an invertible matrix depending only on \(B\). In particular \[ d_1\le C_BN^{-2}\max_j|\phi_{s_j}(C)| \le C_BN^{C_B}\phi_0(C). \tag{20} \] The last step is the established all-low whole-trace comparison, valid at both parities for every tuple of low indices. That theorem is proved in Section 2 of [the source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) by the finite Fourier identity, adjacent odd level, interval-tail comparison and original positive slack-path map. Only its all-low case is used here. The number of interpolation values is fixed independently of \(N\); no unknown state or growing inverse matrix enters (20). Combining (16)–(20) proves the finite reflected-index bound \[ \boxed{\quad |(\phi_s-\phi_0)(e_hF)| \le C_{B,R}N^{C_B}|\Delta_s|\, \phi_0(e_{d-h}F), \quad h>m,\quad n_j\le m,\quad |s|\le R. \quad} \tag{21} \] Both traces on the right are at the original level. A zero right side forces the left side to vanish. For \(B=0\) this also follows immediately by degree. The trace estimate allows any fixed finite \(R\); an application to physical turns retains its separate pre-resonance restriction \(R<1\) and its bounded typed factors. The full moving trace consequently has the positive majorant \[ |\phi_s(e_hF)|\le \phi_0(e_hF) +C_{B,R}N^{C_B}|\Delta_s|\phi_0(e_{d-h}F). \tag{22} \] The first complete tensor is nonnegative and is zero outside its old support. Equation (22) does not assert polynomial domination by that first term. The [nine-factor counterexample](actual_main_meridian_same_index_obstruction.md) shows why the second term must be allowed to be exponentially larger than the first. ## 4. Strict loss on a regular low-factor window The reflected estimate can be sharpened where \(r/N\) stays positive and every \(n_j/N\) stays in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1/2)\). This uses the two different frequencies in (17), rather than replacing both by the coarser tail bound. Fix \(\delta>0\), and suppose \[ \delta\le n_j/N\le1/2-\delta\quad(1\le j\le B), \qquad r/N\ge\delta. \tag{23} \] For \(u\) in that low interval, the individual coefficient action from (13) is \(b_u(t)\) in (8), and \[ b_u''(t)=-\frac{\pi\sin(2\pi u)} {\sin\pi(u+t)\sin\pi(u-t)} \le-\lambda_\delta<0, \qquad |t|<u. \tag{24} \] For example \(\lambda_\delta=\pi\min_{u\in[\delta,1/2-\delta]}\sin2\pi u\) works. The convolution rate \[ B_{\mathbf u}(t)=\max\left\{\sum_{j=1}^B b_{u_j}(v_j): |v_j|\le u_j,\ \sum_jv_j=t\right\} \tag{25} \] is even and strongly concave with modulus \(\lambda_\delta/B\). To prove the modulus directly, use strong concavity for each summand and \(\sum_j(v_j-w_j)^2\ge B^{-1}(\sum_jv_j-\sum_jw_j)^2\), then maximize. Thus, for \(0\le t_1\le t_2\) in its support, \[ B_{\mathbf u}(t_2)-B_{\mathbf u}(t_1) \le-\frac{\lambda_\delta}{2B}(t_2^2-t_1^2). \tag{26} \] This includes support endpoints by continuity. Uniform factorial estimates and the fixed number of convolution variables give \(\log f_k=N B_{\mathbf u}(k/N)+O_B(\log N)\) whenever \(f_k>0\). The lower bound follows by rounding a constrained maximizing tuple to integer indices with the same integer sum; each index changes by \(O_B(1)\), and the endpoint logarithmic modulus of \(J\) costs only \(O_B(\log N)\). The upper bound is the same factorial estimate summed over at most \(N^{B-1}\) tuples. Take \(t_1=(N-1-r)/N\) and \(t_2=(N+r)/N\). If \(f_{N+r}=0\), (16) is zero and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise both frequencies lie in the support, and (26) gives \[ f_{N+r}\le C N^C \exp\left\{-\frac{2\lambda_\delta r}{B}+O(1)\right\} f_{N-1-r}. \tag{27} \] Use the first inequality of (17), then (18)–(20). For some \(\kappa_{B,\delta}>0\), and all sufficiently large levels, \[ \boxed{\quad |(\phi_s-\phi_0)(e_hF)| \le C_{B,R,\delta}N^C|\Delta_s|e^{-\kappa_{B,\delta}N} \phi_0(e_{d-h}F). \quad} \tag{28} \] The loss can be fixed before \(R\); only the prefactor and eventual threshold depend on the disk. This is a relative loss against the reflected complete tensor, not against the same-index complete tensor. ## 5. Several reflected interfaces and the strict old window The finite estimates above now have a precise whole-tree interface. The required positive-pressure comparison is proved separately in [the component-pressure theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md). It applies to an original ordered tree of whole bare junctions, all of valence at least three, whose internal edges are physical quarter-turns and whose external profiles are the original rigid functions \(g+c_j\). The constants are retained. Write \(F(\mathcal G)\) for its complete positive maximum. ### 5.1. Reflection removes a turn in the positive comparison The exact complete metric and turn are \(\phi_0(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}\) and \(T_0(e_i)=e_{d-i}\). Consequently \[ \sum_{i=0}^d\phi_0(Ae_i)\phi_0(e_{d-i}B)=\phi_0(AB). \tag{29} \] Reflecting exactly one endpoint of an equal-label physical-turn edge therefore changes it into the complementary pairing (29). Removing that turn and fusing the two ordered old products is an exact positive tensor operation, with the induced boundary order. It is not an assertion that the physical links before and after deletion are isotopic. The pressure comparison retains the neighboring profiles. At a cut physical edge they are unturned product profiles \(f_A,f_B\), and the original and deleted pressures are \[ F_T=\max_b\{f_A(b)+f_B(b)\},\qquad F_I=\max_b\{f_A(b)+f_B(1-b)\}. \tag{30} \] The product-response theorem gives \(f_X'\ge f_2'\), and \(f_2\) is symmetric. Hence \(f_X(b)\ge f_X(1-b)\) for \(b\ge1/2\). Applying this to the smaller of the two arguments in the deleted summand gives \(F_I\le F_T\). After fusion the new hub still has valence at least three, and its original ordered positive resolution has a unique strict maximizing state. The same argument can therefore be applied successively to the *current* fused tree. For any finite set \(S\) of deleted edges, \[ F(\mathcal G/S)\le F(\mathcal G). \tag{31} \] This does not hold the old multi-boundary responses fixed while changing their couplings. Each stage uses the actual profiles of that fused tree. The cited geometric proof establishes the induced cyclic order, exact fusion and strictness hypotheses. For moving-source applications, expand each one-high tensor as its complete tensor plus its difference. Replace a selected difference by (21). Actual typing makes moving equal-color vertices nonadjacent. A selected internal high edge meets a constant old tensor, whose complete support permits at most one high incidence. Thus the selected internal edges form a matching. Each selected moving endpoint has all other indices low, and its old neighbor also has all other indices low. Every fused hub therefore has an all-low exterior in that band sector. The other physical edges are retained. After positive fusion, summing all complementary hidden labels gives the old tensor of \(\mathcal G/S\). The original band restrictions can be kept in its positive resolution or discarded for an upper bound. They do not change its lattice spacing: reflection is the exact integer substitution \(h\mapsto d-h\). ### 5.2. The strict fused optimizer supplies the Fourier window First note an elementary degree restriction that needs no old-support assumption. A cubic tensor with one high index and two low indices has degree at most \(d+2m\le2N-2\). Its trace difference vanishes, because the first possible changing alias has degree \(2N-1\). Therefore every nonzero selected one-high difference has valence at least four. It need not have valence at least five: off the complete support a valence-four difference can be nonzero. Fix a nonempty set of selected internal differences, and keep the complementary labels of the deleted edges as hidden variables in a fixed old positive resolution of \(\mathcal G/S\). Let \(w_S\) be its unique strict complete optimizer. An internal fusion of a valence-at-least-four selected vertex with a valence-at-least-three neighbor creates valence at least five. In particular the fused tree cannot be the exceptional tree consisting of two trivalent hubs, each carrying two rigid external leaves. The old physical-edge half theorem now puts every remaining physical internal label of \(w_S\) strictly inside \((0,1/2)\); the external rigid labels also lie strictly in that interval. Hidden unturned labels remain in their original strict interval \((0,1)\). For a selected difference, each of its other incidences is a remaining physical edge or an original rigid leaf: the matching has removed only its unique high edge. Thus all the low factors entering that difference lie in a fixed compact low-index window near \(w_S\). Let \(r\) be the hidden complementary index of that selected edge, and let \(x_r\) be its normalized value at \(w_S\). Strictness gives \(x_r>0\). If \(x_r>1/2\), the closed limiting sector \(r/N\le1/2\) excludes \(w_S\), and the whole sector has a compact old-action gap. Otherwise \(r/N\) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant in a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(w_S\). The value \(x_r=1/2\) is allowed: (23) requires a positive lower bound on \(r/N\), not separation of that particular probe from half. All *other* factors are strictly below half. Hence the precise hypotheses of (28) hold near every fused optimizer that can contribute to the reflected sector. The finite restriction \(r\le m\) can only reduce this sum. This argument uses the unconstrained strict optimizer of the same fused old action, followed by restriction to the band sector. It does not assume that an arbitrary band-constrained optimizer is strict. Values \(r\) near zero are in the compact complement of this optimizer, rather than being inserted into a false uniform interior Fourier estimate. ### 5.3. Combining the local Fourier loss and compact separation Use the coarse inequality (21) on all selected differences. Resolve every resulting complete tensor positively. This gives a polynomial multiple of the original positive state sum of \(\mathcal G/S\), with its exact rigid boundary profiles and constants. Its closed factorial errors and the number of states are subexponential uniformly up to support faces. Outside a fixed neighborhood of \(w_S\), uniqueness and strictness give a rate at most \(F(\mathcal G/S)-\eta_S\), with \(\eta_S>0\). Inside that neighborhood, apply (28) at one selected difference and use (21) at the others. The resulting bound has a further fixed loss \(\kappa_S>0\). If the band sector excludes \(w_S\), only the first case is needed. Thus the sum of this selected correction sector has rate \[ F(\mathcal G/S)-\min(\eta_S,\kappa_S)+o(1) \le F(\mathcal G)-\min(\eta_S,\kappa_S)+o(1), \tag{32} \] with the irrelevant minimum omitted when only the compact-complement case occurs. One may shrink either positive constant to absorb polynomial factors. The structural loss is fixed before the parameter disk; \(R\) affects constants and the eventual level threshold. There are only finitely many selected sets for a fixed component. No division by a complete tensor is used when that tensor vanishes. Equation (21) already forces the corresponding exact difference to be zero. Similarly, the argument never assigns a relative asymptotic to an old-support boundary tensor. It uses its positive closed upper envelope and the compact separation of the *whole* old action. ### 5.4. A reflected original external index If the unique high incidence is an original external leaf, there is no internal turn to delete. Its actual high coefficient cone contributes the rate \(c_j\). After reflection to \(r=d-h\), the old comparison leaf contributes \(g(r/N)+c_j\). Thus the missing quantity \[ g(r/N)\ge0 \tag{33} \] is a loss, and must be retained rather than silently supplied to the original source. At the strict old optimizer the reflected leaf is inside \((0,1/2)\), where this loss is strictly positive. Away from a neighborhood of that optimizer, old compact separation applies. This handles the two endpoints without pretending that \(g\) is uniformly positive on the closed interval. If internal corrections are present as well, first perform their fusions and retain (33) in that same positive tree. If there are only external corrections, the nonzero selected vertex already has valence at least four by the cubic degree argument, so the exceptional two-trivalent geometry cannot arise. One external loss or one internal Fourier loss is enough; the other differences may retain their coarse reflected bounds. The boundary constants and all unchanged input profiles are counted once. ### 5.5. What this interface supplies Equations (29)–(33), with the separately proved old fusion theorem, close the strict-window requirement for a finite family of one-high trace differences. Several reflected incidences are not treated as independent caps: their positive contraction is the same fused tree, and the sequential pressure theorem controls that tree as a whole. The [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) organizes the other sectors, including vertices with several high incidences, external high coefficient cones and inherited errors. Its half-cardinal comparison is compatible with the matching: every fused exterior is low, so it creates no additional high mark, and the remaining several-high moving vertices stay nonadjacent. That component proof retains the actual typed edge factors and the required output-norm interfaces. The [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) then uses the original finite wire packet and marked filling action; its geometric conclusion is not inferred from the reflected trace bound alone. ## 6. Proof inputs, finite checks and scope The finite Fourier trace, complete positive multiplication and all-low comparison are proved in [Source growth near the complete main meridian](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 2. Its Section 1.4 and the [full-jet localization theorem](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md) give the high Newton and polynomial Hermite bounds. The neighboring derivative comparison is proved in [the unflagged probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), Appendix A. The [component-pressure theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md) supplies the ordered fusion, simultaneous pressure comparison and complete physical-edge half bound used in Section 5. The finite identities have a standalone reproduction through the research-check runner: ```bash python3 repro/run_research_checks.py general-components ``` The high-Fourier check constructs the Newton polynomials directly over exact cyclotomic number fields, performs an independent monic quotient division with a formal parameter \(\Delta\), and compares the result with the Fourier formula. It also checks the full Frobenius fusion identity with an input that vanishes at repeated-node values but has nonzero first-normal trace. The recorded levels include both parities. These finite algebra checks test the identities and their signs; the uniform inequalities, strict exponential loss and pressure comparison are established by the arguments above. No topological move or invariant equality follows merely by replacing an index in (21). The replacement is an upper comparison for an exact trace difference in the fixed basis. Actual mixed carriers, scalar framings and paired edge weights remain those of the original typed contraction. Their boundedness on fixed pre-resonance disks can be used separately; they have not been absorbed into a new trace definition.

title: Computing oriented tangles as the main meridian varies
status: Exact oriented tangle calculation and primitive closing trace
text:
# Computing oriented tangles as the main meridian varies 1 November 2026. A two-strand tangle is a piece of a knot diagram inside a box, with four ordered boundary points. Its quantum operator can be encoded by a polynomial in the two-strand Casimir. Turning or joining boxes then becomes a finite calculation on polynomial coefficients. The main meridian parameter is the eigenvalue assigned to a small loop around the knot itself; it is distinct from any auxiliary crossing-circle color. There are two distinct operations in a main-meridian deformation: changing the polynomial coordinates of a coupon, and changing the multiplication and turn tensors of the physical source. A bound for the first operation does not by itself control the second: [products that vanish at completeness can acquire nonzero coefficients](actual_main_meridian_newton_multiplication.md). This note proves the polynomial basis bound, constructs an exact formal compiler for a fixed oriented Conway tree, and retains the actual primitive closing trace. The separate [quarter-turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) now computes all six physical turn types in fixed polynomial coordinates and bounds them relative to the complete turn. The closing normalization still supplies only one factor \(H_N\); it does not force the remaining regular contraction to tend to one. ## 1. The moving Newton basis and its exact dual Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad M=q^s,\quad Y=M^2,\quad p=Q^{-1}. \] Write \[ \sigma_r=\prod_{v=1}^r2\sin(\pi v/N),\qquad \sigma_0=1. \] Thus \(\sigma_d=N\) and \(\sigma_r\sigma_{d-r}=N\). For \(a
e0\), set \[ c_j(a)=ap^j+a^{-1}p^{-j},\qquad B_r(a;z)=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j(a)-z),\qquad e_r(a;z)= rac{B_r(a;z)}{\sigma_r^2}. 	ag{1} \] The same-color moving nodes use \(a_s=q^{-1}Y\); the complete nodes use \(a_0=q^{-1}\). For clarity put \(e_r^s=e_r(a_s)\). Let \(\mathcal T_0=2,\mathcal T_1=z,\mathcal T_{r+1}=z\mathcal T_r-\mathcal T_{r-1}\). The two relevant algebras are \[ \mathcal A_s=\mathbb C[z]/P_s(z),\qquad P_s(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+Y^N+Y^{-N}, 	ag{2} \] for equal colors, and the constant algebra \(\mathcal A_0\) for opposite colors. Section 4 derives the physical duality that distinguishes these two algebras. The Casimir and pivotal moment identities used there are the exact identities of [the intrinsic cut calculation](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md). The elementary identity \[ c_{d-j}(a_s)=c_j(a_{-s}) 	ag{3} \] gives an exact dual basis, even though the forward basis is no longer self-dual. Define \[ \phi_s(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f mod P_s). \] Then \[  oxed{\quad \phi_s(e_i^s e_j^{-s})=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}.\quad} 	ag{4} \] For \(i+j<d\) this is degree. For \(i+j=d\), compare leading coefficients and use \(\sigma_i\sigma_j=N\). For \(i+j\ge N\), the first \(i\) nodes in forward order together with the first \(j\) nodes in reverse order contain all \(N\) indexed nodes. Their product is divisible by \(P_s\), with multiplicities retained. This proves (4) at collisions as well. In particular, if \(f=\sum_{r=0}^d f_r e_r^s\), then \[ f_r=\phi_s(f e_{d-r}^{-s}),\qquad \phi_s(f)=f_d. 	ag{5} \] This is an exact finite coefficient extractor. It is not a positivity assertion for the deformed multiplication. ## 2. An elementary finite connection formula For an indeterminate \(z\), define \[ \Psi_n(a;z)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-ap^jz+a^2p^{2j}). \] For generic \(p,a,b\), the following finite identity holds. It is the standard connection relation for the Askey–Wilson factorial basis, recorded in Ismail and Stanton, [*Expansions in the Askey–Wilson Polynomials*, equation (2.4), PDF page 7](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~stant001/PAPERS/AF-Ismail-Stanton.pdf#page=7). Indeed, with \(z=v+v^{-1}\), one has \(\Psi_n(a;z)=(av,a/v;p)_n\); clearing the finite factorial denominators in their formula gives (6). We give the elementary induction because it also justifies specialization at roots of unity. No physical turn or quotient-algebra assertion is imported from that connection relation. \[ \Psi_n(a;z)= \sum_{k=0}^n {n rack k}_p(a/b)^k (abp^k;p)_{n-k}(a/b;p)_{n-k}\Psi_k(b;z), 	ag{6} \] where \((v;p)_r=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(1-vp^j)\) and \({n rack k}_p=(p;p)_n/((p;p)_k(p;p)_{n-k})\). Here is a direct induction. Multiplying the \(k\)-th basis polynomial by the new factor gives \[ (1-ap^nz+a^2p^{2n})\Psi_k(b;z) =(a/b)p^{n-k}\Psi_{k+1}(b;z) +(1-(a/b)p^{n-k})(1-abp^{n+k})\Psi_k(b;z). 	ag{7} \] Thus the proposed coefficients in (6) must satisfy the recurrence given by (7). For \(1\le k\le n\), write \(m=n+1-k\), substitute the displayed factorial products, and cancel their common factors. The remaining identity is \[ p^m(1-p^k)(1-abp^{k-1}) +(1-p^m)(1-abp^{n+k}) =(1-p^{n+1})(1-abp^n). 	ag{8} \] The constant terms agree because \(m+k=n+1\); the coefficients of \(ab\) agree after factoring out \(p^n\). The endpoint cases follow from their single surviving term. The case \(n=0\) starts the induction. Clearing the denominators proves the polynomial identity wherever the resulting finite expressions are defined. In particular it applies at the present root for \(n<N\). Since \[ B_n(a;z)=a^{-n}p^{-n(n-1)/2}\Psi_n(a;z), \] equation (6) gives the normalized connection \[ e_n(a;z)=\sum_{k=0}^n C_{nk}(a,b)e_k(b;z), 	ag{9} \] with \[  oxed{\quad C_{nk}(a,b)=  rac{\sigma_k^2}{\sigma_n^2} a^{k-n}p^{[k(k-1)-n(n-1)]/2} {n rack k}_p (abp^k;p)_{n-k}(a/b;p)_{n-k}. \quad} 	ag{10} \] Every diagonal entry is one. Interchanging \(a,b\) gives the inverse change of coordinates, because both are bases of the same space of polynomials of degree less than \(N\). ## 3. Uniform polynomial bounds, including all endpoint indices **Proposition.** For every fixed \(R<\infty\), the connection from \(e_r^s\) to \(e_r^0\) and its inverse have coefficient \(\ell^2\)-operator norms at most \[ C_R N^{A_R}\qquad (|s|\le R), 	ag{11} \] for constants independent of \(N\) and its parity. The assertion includes \(k=0\), \(n-k=1\), and all indices \(0\le k\le n<N\). It also holds for every fixed derivative in \(s\), with possibly different constants. To prove it, first let \(m=n-k\ge1\). At \(|p|=1\), \[ \left|{n rack k}_pight| = rac{\sigma_n}{\sigma_k\sigma_m}. \] For \(a=a_s\), \(b=a_0\), equation (10) therefore becomes \[ |C_{nk}(a_s,a_0)| =|a_s|^{-m}  rac{|(Yp^{k+1};p)_m|}{\prod_{r=k+1}^n|1-p^r|}  rac{|(Y;p)_m|}{\prod_{r=1}^m|1-p^r|}. 	ag{12} \] There is no missing factorial factor in this cancellation. Let \(d_r=\min(r,N-r)\), \(1\le r<N\). Then \[ |1-p^r|=2\sin(\pi r/N)\ge rac{4d_r}{N}. 	ag{13} \] For \(|w|\le R+1\), \[ |e^{2\pi iw/N}-1| \le rac{2\pi(R+1)e^{\pi(R+1)}}N. 	ag{14} \] Comparing \(1-Yp^r\) with \(1-p^r\), and \(1-Yp^{r-1}\) with \(1-p^r\), bounds each ratio in (12) by \[ 1+ rac{K_R}{d_r}, \qquad K_R= rac{\pi(R+1)e^{\pi(R+1)}}2. 	ag{15} \] This uses \(w=s\) in the first product and \(w=s+1\) in the second. Consequently each product is at most \[ \prod_{r=1}^{N-1}\left(1+ rac{K_R}{d_r}ight) \le \exp\left(K_R\sum_{r=1}^{N-1} rac1{d_r}ight) \le C_RN^{2K_R}. 	ag{16} \] Also \(|a_s|^{-m}\le e^{2\pi R}\). Thus every entry has a uniform polynomial bound. When \(m=0\), the entry is exactly one and no denominator of index zero is used. For the inverse, take \(a=a_0,b=a_s\). The product \(ab\) is unchanged, and \(a/b=Y^{-1}\). The two products are bounded in exactly the same manner, now with shifts \(s\) and \(1-s\); the prefactor has modulus one. This proves the same entry bound for the inverse. A matrix of size \(N\) with entries bounded by \(B\) has \(\ell^2\)-operator norm at most \(NB\), proving (11). Each entry is entire in \(s\); Cauchy's estimate on the larger disk \(|s|\le R+1\) gives the derivative assertion. The estimate is deliberately not optimized. Its role is to prove that changing the normalized Newton coordinates on a bounded microscopic disk has no exponential cost. In particular the ordinary resonance at \(s=1\) is not a singularity of this polynomial basis change. The actual realization of the polynomial algebra by tensor operators can nevertheless lose rank there, and a physical coupon's canonical polynomial coefficients can have poles. ## 4. An exact finite compiler with all orientation types Choose an orientation of the actual knot. A strand directed with the chosen vertical coordinate carries \(V_+=V_{-q^{-1}M}\); a reversed strand carries its dual \(V_-=V_{-q^{-1}M^{-1}}\). The possible ordered two-strand objects are \[ ++,\quad --,\quad +-,\quad -+. \] An oriented two-string tangle preserves the total sign of these objects. Thus there are six relevant intertwiner spaces: the four endomorphism spaces and the two maps between \(+-\) and \(-+\). An intertwiner is a linear map commuting with the quantum-group action on these two-strand objects. We will show that each of these six spaces has rank \(N\) over the fixed-level formal ring \(\mathbb C[[u]]\), where \(M=e^u\), near completeness. Here are the duality conventions. Write \(ho=q-q^{-1}\), and use the nilpotent module basis \[ Kv_a=xQ^{-a}v_a,\qquad Fv_a=v_{a+1},\qquad Ev_a=[a] rac{xq^{1-a}-x^{-1}q^{a-1}}{ho}v_{a-1}, \qquad [a]= rac{q^a-q^{-a}}{ho}. 	ag{16c} \] Outside-basis arrows are omitted. The coproduct and antipode are \[  egin{aligned} \Delta E&=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,& S(E)&=-EK^{-1},\ \Delta F&=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F,& S(F)&=-KF,\ \Delta K&=K\otimes K,& S(K)&=K^{-1}. \end{aligned} 	ag{16d} \] These are the conventions of [the intrinsic cut and meridian atlas](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md). If \(\varphi_a\) is dual to \(v_a\) and \(y=x^{-1}Q^{-1}\), the actual duality is \[ J_x:V_y\longrightarrow V_x^*,\qquad J_xw_a=c_a(x)\varphi_{d-a},\qquad c_a(x)=(-x)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}. 	ag{16e} \] For example, the dual action is \(F\varphi_a=-xQ^{-a}\varphi_{a-1}\), so equivariance under \(F\) is precisely \(c_{a+1}=-xQ^{a+1}c_a\). Equivariance under \(K\) uses \(Q^d=Q^{-1}\). Under \(E\), it follows from \(e_a(y)=e_{N-a}(x)\), where \(e_a(x)\) denotes the coefficient of \(E\) in (16c). Thus \(J_x\) is an invertible module map for every \(x
e0\), including ordinary-color resonances. For \(x=-q^{-1}M\), its dual root is exactly \(-q^{-1}M^{-1}\). For general roots \(x_1,x_2\), the physical Casimir is \[ \Omega=ho^2F_{\mathrm{tot}}E_{\mathrm{tot}} +qK_{\mathrm{tot}}+q^{-1}K_{\mathrm{tot}}^{-1}. \] The intrinsic cut calculation gives \[  egin{gathered} \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\left(z-qx_1x_2Q^{-j} -q^{-1}(x_1x_2)^{-1}Q^jight) =\mathcal T_N(z)+(x_1x_2)^N+(x_1x_2)^{-N},\ P_{x_1,x_2}(\Omega)=0,\qquad \operatorname{ptr}_{g_2}\Omega^r=0\quad(0\le r<d),\qquad \operatorname{ptr}_{g_2}\Omega^d=s_{x_1}I,\qquad g_2=K_2^{1-N}. \end{gathered} 	ag{16f} \] For either root \(x_1=-q^{-1}M^{\pm1}\), \[ s_{x_1}=(-1)^dN rac{\sinh(Nu)}{\sinh u},\qquad s_{x_1}(0)=(-1)^dN^2. 	ag{16g} \] The partial trace means that the second strand is closed with its pivotal operator \(g_2\), while the first remains open. Its scalar is a unit in the formal ring at \(u=0\). These exact matrix identities hold at colliding eigenvalues as well. For any object \((\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\), its full formal centralizer is the rank-\(N\) Casimir order \[ \mathbb C[[u]][z] ig/ \left(\mathcal T_N(z)+M^{N(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)} +M^{-N(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)}ight). 	ag{16a} \] Here is a proof of the full formal centralizer. At \(u=0\), all four objects specialize to the complete tensor square. Its centralizer has dimension \(N\), by [the physical pair-commutant theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). The kernel dimension of the intertwining equations over the fraction field cannot exceed this special-fiber dimension. On the other hand, (16f) makes \(1,\Omega,\ldots,\Omega^d\) independent: multiply any putative relation of degree \(r<N\) by \(\Omega^{d-r}\) and take the partial trace. Its leading coefficient must vanish. The same moment calculation proves that these powers span the integral formal order. Their pairing matrix has determinant \[ \det\left(\operatorname{ptr}_{g_2}\Omega^{i+j}ight)_{0\le i,j<N} =(-1)^{N(N-1)/2}s_{x_1}^{\,N}. 	ag{16h} \] Reversing its columns gives a triangular matrix with diagonal \(s_{x_1}\). An integral intertwiner is a fraction-field linear combination of the powers; pairing with every power and using this unit determinant forces its coefficients into \(\mathbb C[[u]]\). This proves (16a), including its lattice. It does not assert a uniformly bounded inverse on a color disk as \(N\) varies. For \(++\) and \(--\), (16a) is the moving order (2), using respectively \(e_r^s\) and \(e_r^{-s}\). For \(+-\) and \(-+\), it is the constant opposite-color order. Choose one reference object in each sign class. In the zero-sign class choose reference \(+-\), and normalize its carrier as follows. Let \(r_0\) be the full original complete checked-crossing polynomial in \(\mathcal A_0\), including its common Cartan scalar and its first coefficients at repeated roots. It is a unit in this algebra, because all of its nodal values are nonzero. Let \(r_0^{-1}\) denote its fixed polynomial inverse modulo \(P_0\), and put \[ G_{-+}(M)= \check R_{+,-}(M)\,r_0^{-1}(\Omega_{+,-}(M)): V_+\otimes V_-\longrightarrow V_-\otimes V_+, \qquad G_{+-}=I. 	ag{16b} \] The universal identity \(P_0(\Omega_{+,-})=0\) makes the polynomial factor and its inverse regular at every nonzero color, including the ordinary resonances. The physical mixed braiding is invertible there too. In the complete physical identifications used by the original turn theorem, \(\check R_{+,-}(1)=r_0(\Omega_{+,-}(1))\). Consequently \(G_{-+}(1)=I\), with no omitted scalar. Set \(C_{B,A}=G_BG_A^{-1}\). For the other classes the carrier is the identity. Every intertwiner from object \(A\) to object \(B\) then has a unique form \[ C_{B,A}f(\Omega_A),\qquad \deg f<N. 	ag{17} \] All original Cartan and framing scalars remain in the physical maps or their polynomial coefficients. These coherent carrier choices make serial composition literal polynomial multiplication: \[ (C_{C,B}g(\Omega_B))(C_{B,A}f(\Omega_A)) =C_{C,A}(gf)(\Omega_A). 	ag{18} \] Indeed the Casimir is natural under intertwiners, and the carriers multiply to \(C_{C,A}\). This is a coordinate identity, not a tangle isotopy or a new crossing inserted in the diagram. A quarter-turn is the actual evaluation/coevaluation currying, with its ordered duality maps. For example, in the original nilpotent basis, \[ \mathcal T_x(A)^{\,jb}_{ak} = rac{c_a(x)}{c_b(x)}A^{\,d-a,j}_{k,d-b}, \qquad c_a(x)=(-x)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}. 	ag{19} \] To derive (19), insert \(\sum_l v_l\otimes\varphi_l\), apply \(A\) to the middle two strands, and evaluate the first two. Before using \(J_x\), the resulting map sends \[ \varphi_i\otimes v_k\longmapsto \sum_{j,l}A^{ij}_{kl}\,v_j\otimes\varphi_l. \] Applying (16e) to the two dual factors gives (19). Its domain is \(V_y\otimes V_x\), and its target is \(V_x\otimes V_y\); it is not an endomorphism of the same-color tensor square. Every matrix entry is regular for \(x
e0\). On a fixed microscopic disk \(|s|\le R\), the entry rearrangement and \(|c_a/c_b|=|M|^{a-b}\) even give \[ e^{-\pi R}\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le\|\mathcal T_x(A)\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le e^{\pi R}\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}. 	ag{19d} \] Here \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\) is the Euclidean norm of all matrix entries. This physical matrix estimate is not a Newton coefficient or spectral estimate. Left bends retain their actual inverse pivotal maps. After the turn, remove the chosen output carrier and recover the unique polynomial by the actual partial pivotal trace. Equivalently, if \(G\) is the resulting endomorphism and \(e_r^\sigma\) is its selected Newton basis, its coefficient is \[ f_r= rac{s_0}{s_x} \left(\operatorname{ptr}_{g_{\mathrm{second}}} \left(G\,e_{d-r}^{-\sigma}(\Omega)ight)ight)_{\mathrm{scalar}}, \qquad s_0=(-1)^dN^2. 	ag{20} \] For an opposite-color object, \(\sigma=0\). For a left closing convention, use the already proved left partial trace and its actual inverse pivot; it has the same scalar factor. Formula (20) is just the exact duality (4) and the intrinsic two-color moment identity. It keeps all repeated-node derivatives. Equations (17)--(20), together with the actual leaf crossings and their inverse powers, give a finite recursive compiler for every fixed oriented Conway expression. At each node its original object type is recorded. Its multiplication tensors can be extracted using (4); its turn tensors are the physical currying tensors expressed by (20). This is an equality of the original tensor contractions over the formal ring, not a proposed substitute source. It remains an exact meromorphic coefficient presentation wherever these coordinates continue; the physical tensor contraction itself is regular at ordinary-color resonances. The identification with the original complete turn also requires its physical basis calibration. Set \(ho=q-q^{-1}\), \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\), and at \(M=1\) use \[ |aangle=\delta_a v_a,\qquad \delta_a= rac{ho^a}{F_a}. 	ag{19a} \] The rescaled generators \(E_{\mathrm{bal}}=ho E_{\mathrm{std}}\), \(F_{\mathrm{bal}}=ho F_{\mathrm{std}}\) then have the original balanced entries \[ E_{\mathrm{bal}}|aangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1angle,\qquad F_{\mathrm{bal}}|aangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1angle. 	ag{19b} \] The diagonal change of basis leaves \(K\) and the pivotal operator unchanged. Since \(x=-q^{-1}\), one has \(c_a(x)=q^{a^2}\). The finite product \(F_d=N\) gives \[ F_aF_{d-a}=N(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2},\qquad \delta_a\delta_{d-a}c_a(x)= rac{ho^d}{N}x^a. 	ag{19c} \] For the product identity, divide \(F_d\) by \(F_{d-a}\) and replace each factor \(1-Q^{N-r}\) by \(-Q^{-r}(1-Q^r)\). Thus the balanced duality coefficients have ratio \(x^{a-b}\); their common scalar cancels in currying. Formula (19) in these coordinates is the transpose of the original turn in equation (2) of [the complete Newton turn theorem](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md): its \((jb;ak)\) entry is \(x^{a-b}A_{(d-a,j);(k,d-b)}\). The output of that original turn is a polynomial in the balanced Casimir, which is complex symmetric on every degree block. Taking its transpose therefore makes no change. At \(M=1\), every carrier is the identity, every Newton basis is the complete one, and this calculation identifies the retained physical dualities with the original unscaled turn. Consequently the compiler specializes to the proved complete multiplication table, coordinate reversal \(e_r\mapsto e_{d-r}\), and original closing functional. This checks its actual complete source fiber, not only its abstract algebra. The identity \(G_{-+}(1)=I\) does not by itself bound this carrier uniformly on a microscopic color disk. The only color-dependent denominator in the trace-dual recovery (20) is \(s_x\). The factors \(\sigma_r\) are nonzero constants at each fixed level; the pivot, Casimir matrices, physical duality maps and actual mixed braiding and inverse are holomorphic for nonzero \(M\) on the retained logarithmic cover. The common Cartan scalar is included; after factoring it out, the remaining entries are Laurent expressions in \(M\). An iterative evaluation therefore has a coarse pole-order bound depending only on the fixed tree: one power of \(s_x^{-1}\) for each physical leaf whose coordinates are extracted and each internal turn. When the leaves are the original \(h=T(R^n)\), evaluate each such leaf from its physical matrix and extract once; this count is at most the number of all displayed turns, including those leaf turns. A bare \(R^n\) leaf need not have a regular polynomial representative, so a bound solely by internal turns would be false. There is a stronger final cancellation statement. Apply (20) directly to the entire physical tangle, after removing its single chosen carrier. Every resulting coordinate has the form \[ f_r(M)= rac{s_0}{s_x(M)}\,b_r(M), 	ag{20a} \] with \(b_r\) holomorphic at every nonzero ordinary-color point. Those zeros of \(s_x\) are simple. Thus every final Newton coordinate has at most a simple ordinary-color pole, irrespective of the apparent higher pole orders in the recursive calculation. The same holds for every fixed subtree. This is an exact cancellation identity, with no quantitative bound on \(b_r\) relative to the selected closing scalar. The polynomial basis estimate (11) applies to the changes between the Newton frames occurring here. A separate physical calculation now evaluates the turn tensor (20): in fixed complete polynomial coordinates it is coefficient reversal multiplied by the paired sine product \(W_n(s)/H_N(s)\) and a specified scalar \(1\) or \(q^{\pm s^2/2}\). The [quarter-turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) bounds these factors and their inverses uniformly for \(|s|\le R<1\). On \(|s|\le1/16\), it also compares the full spectral-jet norm with the complete turn of the same polynomial, with factors at most \(CN^7\). This local comparison does not estimate crossing coordinates through a resonance. The later [source-growth theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) controls the signed contraction for strict trees whose bare product junctions are not adjacent, on each fixed disk \(0\le R<1\). ## 5. The primitive closing trace leaves one boundary factor Orient and cut one of the actual cylindrical closing arcs of the knot. The whole remaining two-string tangle is an endomorphism of the ordered object determined by those two arcs; the cylindrical closing matching gives the same input and output object. If the presentation uses the other cap closure, retain the actual closing turn before taking this cut. The selected side of the pivot and the zero-framing correction are retained. Let \(f_{K,M}\) be the polynomial of this entire physical operator, with its framing scalar included. The exact two-color pivotal moment formula gives \[ F_N(M)=s_x[z^d]f_{K,M} = rac{s_x}{s_0}\,\phi_s(f_{K,M}). 	ag{21} \] Here \(F_N(M)\) is the zero-framed reduced cut invariant, normalized so that the reduced unknot has value one. Its complete value is \(K_N=F_N(1)\). The coefficient polynomial \(f_{K,M}\) and the scalar function \(F_N(M)\) are different objects: the former encodes the remaining two-strand operator, while the latter is obtained after closing one strand. The [intrinsic cut normalization](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) fixes this distinction and the pivotal scalar. The same \(s_x\) occurs for either strand orientation: \[ s_x=(-1)^dN\, rac{\sinh(Nu)}{\sinh u}, \qquad s_x(1)=s_0. 	ag{22} \] For an opposite-color root, use the constant \(P_0\) in \(\phi_s\). In its Newton coordinates, \(\phi_s(f_{K,M})\) is exactly the last coordinate, by (5). On the microscopic scale \(M=e^{z/(2N)}\), this yields the exact formal/meromorphic identity \[  oxed{\quad  rac{F_N(e^{z/(2N)})}{K_N} =H_N(z)\,A_{K,N}(z),\qquad H_N(z)= rac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}, \quad} 	ag{23} \] where \(K_N=F_N(1)
e0\) and \[ A_{K,N}(z)= rac{\phi_s(f_{K,e^{z/(2N)}})}{K_N}, \qquad s= rac{z}{2\pi i},\qquad A_{K,N}(0)=1. \] This is the primitive reduced cut, not the ordinary zero-dimensional pivotal trace. With the prescribed full modified dimension \[ d_N(M)=i^{N+3} rac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}}, \] one has \(d_N(M)s_x=Nq^{N(1-N)/2}\); multiplying (21) by \(d_N\) makes the full trace constant. There is a corresponding Euler-characteristic bookkeeping rule for the computation tree. Lower every operation's output with the actual pairing \((s_x/s_0)\phi_s\). Each lowered vertex contributes the common scalar \(s_x/s_0\), and each internal contraction uses its inverse. A connected tree has one more such vertex, counting its terminal closing functional, than internal edges. Exactly one scalar survives, giving (23). This counts the tensor computation, not the Euler characteristic of a hyperbolic manifold. The leaf coefficients and turn tensors still carry their genuine color dependence. The factorization is not holomorphic across every resonance. For example, at \(s=1\), [ordinary-color pointing](actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) gives \(F_N(q)=C_1=1\), while \[  rac{s_x}{s_0}= rac{\sin(\pi s)}{N\sin(\pi s/N)} \] has a simple zero. Consequently the normalized coefficient contraction in (23) has a pole at \(z=2\pi i\). In the \(s\)-coordinate its residue is \[ - rac{N\sin(\pi/N)}{\pi K_N}. 	ag{24} \] It may be exponentially small, but it is not zero. Thus no uniform holomorphic compiler bound on a disk containing that resonance follows just by factoring out \(H_N\). ## 6. What support and normalization do not prove For opposite colors, the fixed abstract multiplication retains the complete Newton support. For equal colors, a formerly forbidden product need not vanish.
