One exact way to see the change is to keep the complete basis as a vector-space basis and write \[ P_s=P_0+\Delta_s,\qquad \Delta_s=Y^N+Y^{-N}-2=2\cos(2\pi s)-2. \] If \(i+j\ge N\), then the complete-basis product has a polynomial factorization \(e_i^0e_j^0=P_0h_{ij}\), with \(\deg h_{ij}\le N-2\). Therefore in the moving algebra \[ e_i^0e_j^0\equiv-\Delta_s h_{ij}\pmod{P_s}. 	ag{25} \] For fixed microscopic \(s\), \(\Delta_s\) is of order one, not of order \(N^{-1}\). A polynomially controlled basis change does not suppress this new term. The exact turn comparison retains the distinction between equal-color and opposite-color objects; its fixed polynomial coordinates do not identify their multiplication algebras. The additional products in (25) therefore remain in the physical calculation. At first order there is a useful distinction: \(\Delta'_0=0\), so the multiplication of fixed degree-\(<N\) polynomials has zero first derivative at completeness. The moving Newton coefficients can nevertheless have nonzero first derivatives. The [multiplication note](actual_main_meridian_newton_multiplication.md) computes the exact connection derivative and shows that these first derivatives are precisely its basis-change contribution; they do not by themselves give a coordinate-independent first-order obstruction. Finally write the even reduced state as \(F_N(M)=f_N(Y)\), with \(Y=M^2\). Let \(P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}\) be the unique polynomial of degree at most \(N-2\) matching \(f_N\) at the \(N-1\) nontrivial \(N\)-th roots of unity. Define \[ S_N(Y)=1+Y+\cdots+Y^{N-1},\qquad R_N(Y)= rac{f_N(Y)-P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(Y)}{S_N(Y)},\qquad ho_N(z)=e^{(N-1)z/(2N)}  rac{N R_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N}. \] The numerator vanishes at every zero of \(S_N\), so this quotient has no pole there. The exponential factor retains the centered normalization of the full state. The [canonical ordinary-color subtraction](regularized_kashaev_period.md) gives the exact decomposition \[  rac{F_N(e^{z/(2N)})}{K_N} =H_N(z)ho_N(z)+\pi_N(z),\qquad \pi_N(z)= rac{P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(e^{z/N})}{K_N}. 	ag{26} \] Thus the coefficient contraction of (23) is precisely \[ A_{K,N}=ho_N+ rac{\pi_N}{H_N}. 	ag{27} \] This identifies the pole in (24) and the required subtraction in the same primitive trace normalization. For knots with positive complete exponential rate, \(\pi_N\) is exponentially small on compact sets, but its quotient by \(H_N\) still has the actual finite poles. After subtracting it, a bounded signed contraction gives normality of \(ho_N\) and subsequential limits \[ g(z)=H(z)a(z),\qquad H(z)=2\sinh(z/2)/z,\qquad a(0)=1. \] Boundedness and the boundary normalization do not force \(a=1\). Even reciprocal central multipliers with value one and vanishing first derivative at \(U=1\) can change this limiting function while preserving all root orbit values and the marked ramified normal fibre. They are not new actual knot sources; they show why the weaker data cannot imply the missing estimate or identification. The result is an exact whole-tangle compiler with a polynomially controlled Newton basis deformation and the retained boundary factor. Its application to [separated bare product junctions](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) now gives an exact supremum-volume limit for the auxiliary-colored source on \(M=q^s\), \(|s|\le R<1\), at both parities. A bare junction has no distinguished original crossing-circle operator; the condition is that no two such junctions are adjacent. The comparison includes the channels opened in (25) after summing them inside the actual junction. The geometric constant is the volume with the auxiliary circles unfilled, and the lower witness is the complete value. The [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) now removes that separation condition: it controls every fixed connected group of bare junctions, with arbitrary valences. The [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) proves a normalized profile and a uniform knot-volume limit for the full strict-tree class with independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists, using additional complex-contour and geometric arguments. Continuation of the ordinary-color-subtracted state through its resonances remains a further question. Polynomial spectral stability of an arbitrary turn does not itself preserve a localized jet profile. ## 7. Reproducing the finite identities From the repository root, with SymPy, mpmath and Matplotlib installed, run ~~~sh python3 experiments/audit_main_meridian_newton_algebra.py ~~~ The [script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_newton_algebra.py) compares independently expanded rational polynomials for the multiplication and connection identities, and reduces mixed-duality products in exact cyclotomic fields. It also records high-precision evaluations of the opened-sector factorization. The [output record](../experiments/main_meridian_newton_algebra_results.json) separates exact identities from asymptotic diagnostics. The uniform estimates are proved above and in [the multiplication theorem](actual_main_meridian_newton_multiplication.md), rather than inferred from these finite checks.

title: Newton products when the main meridian changes
status: Exact products, basis derivative and uniform interior estimates
text:
# Newton products when the main meridian changes 1 November 2026. Joining two tangle boxes requires multiplying their Casimir polynomials. At the complete color, many of the resulting coefficients vanish exactly. Varying the main knot meridian can make them nonzero, even on the microscopic scale used in the meridian profile. This note establishes an exact multiplication rule in the actual equal-color Casimir polynomial algebra. The [oriented compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) supplies the physical turns and closing trace separately. The multiplication rule alone gives no bound for a knot invariant. ## 1. Definitions and the exact formula Fix \(N\ge2\), set \(	heta=\pi/N\), \(q=e^{i	heta}\), \(ho=q-q^{-1}\), and write \[ [a]= rac{\sin(a	heta)}{\sin	heta},\qquad [r]!=\prod_{u=1}^r[u],\qquad S_r=\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(u	heta),\quad S_0=1. 	ag{1} \] The argument \(a\) in a bracket may be complex. Factorials are used only at integers in \(0,\ldots,N-1\), so their denominators below never vanish. The symbol \(S_r\) is the \(s_r\) of the original Newton normalization; a capital letter distinguishes it from the meridian displacement \(s\). Let \(Y=q^{2s}\), and use the nodes and monic Chebyshev polynomial \[  egin{aligned} c_j(s)&=q^{2j+1}Y^{-1}+Yq^{-2j-1} =2\cos((2j+1-2s)	heta),\ \mathcal T_N(v+v^{-1})&=v^N+v^{-N},\ P_s(\omega)&=\mathcal T_N(\omega)+Y^N+Y^{-N}. \end{aligned} 	ag{2} \] These are the equal-color nodes of [the actual meridian Casimir source](meridian_casimir_source.md), §1. The Newton polynomials are \[ B_r(s,\omega)=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j(s)-\omega),\qquad e_r(s,\omega)= rac{B_r(s,\omega)}{S_r^2}, \quad 0\le r<N. 	ag{3} \] The polynomials \(e_r\) form a basis at every complex \(s\), including repeated nodes. Their degrees and nonzero leading coefficients give this statement without any eigenvalue separation. The product of all node factors gives \[ B_N=(-1)^N P_s. 	ag{4} \] Thus the following formulas hold in \(\mathbb C[\omega]/(P_s)\), for all complex \(s\), with every repeated-root direction retained: \[ B_iB_j=\sum_{k=\max(i,j)}^{\min(i+j,N-1)} A_{ijk}(s)B_k, 	ag{5} \] where \[  oxed{\; A_{ijk}(s)= (-ho^2)^{i+j-k}  rac{[i]![j]!} {[k-i]![k-j]![i+j-k]!} \prod_{r=k+1}^{i+j}[r-2s]. \;} 	ag{6} \] In normalized coordinates, \[ e_ie_j=\sum_{k=\max(i,j)}^{\min(i+j,N-1)} \mu_{ijk}(s)e_k, 	ag{7} \] with \[  oxed{\; \mu_{ijk}(s)=  rac{S_k^2} {S_iS_jS_{k-i}S_{k-j}S_{i+j-k}} \prod_{r=k+1}^{i+j}2\sin((r-2s)	heta). \;} 	ag{8} \] Every product with no factors is one. In particular, no factorial at \(i+j\ge N\) is introduced or canceled. The associated change of factorial basis is classical: see Ismail and Stanton, [*Expansions in the Askey–Wilson Polynomials*, equation (2.4), PDF page 7](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~stant001/PAPERS/AF-Ismail-Stanton.pdf#page=7). The companion note gives that connection formula and its root-of-unity proof. Here the required statement is multiplication in the specified quotient, with the normalization in (3) and all factors crossing the index \(N\) retained. ![The normalized product indices at completeness and after a generic meridian displacement.](../book/figures/moving-newton-products.svg) The horizontal coordinate is \(x=i/N\), and the vertical coordinate is \(y=j/N\). At completeness, \(e_ie_j\) vanishes when \(i+j\ge N\). Under a generic displacement \(s\), coefficients in that region can be nonzero; their finite output indices still satisfy \(\max(i,j)\le k\le\min(i+j,N-1)\). The line \(x+y=1\) is the exact finite threshold \(i+j=N\). The diagram describes coefficient support, not growth of a contracted knot invariant. ## 2. Proof by the Newton recurrence The elementary node difference is \[ c_i(s)-c_k(s) =4\sin((k-i)	heta)\sin((k+i+1-2s)	heta) =(-ho^2)[k-i][k+i+1-2s]. 	ag{9} \] Since \((c_i-\omega)B_k=B_{k+1}+(c_i-c_k)B_k\), multiplication by the next factor of \(B_i\) requires \[ A_{i+1,j,k} =A_{i,j,k-1} +(-ho^2)[k-i][k+i+1-2s]A_{i,j,k}. 	ag{10} \] The term \(B_N\) is zero in the quotient. Thus (10) is also the exact recurrence at the top retained index \(k=N-1\); there is no wrap-around contribution. The required scalar identity is \[ [i+1][i+j+1-2s] =[k-j][k-2s] +[k+i+1-2s][i+j+1-k]. 	ag{11} \] For a direct verification, multiply by \(\sin^2	heta\). In the difference of the first two sine products, the difference angles are both \((2s-j)	heta\). The product-to-sum formula leaves \[  rac{\cos((2k-j-2s)	heta) -\cos((2i+j+2-2s)	heta)}2, \] which is the final sine product in (11). Substitution of (6) in (10), followed by factorial cancellation and (11), proves the recurrence at the interior indices. One may do the cancellation first for generic \(s\), then clear the shifted factors. Both resulting sides are entire trigonometric polynomials in \(s\), so the identity holds at their zeros as well. Equivalently, multiply the recurrence by the common nonzero integer factorial denominator before using (11). At the lower and upper support endpoints, the vanished \([k-i]\) factor and the empty product give the recurrence directly. The initial condition \(B_0B_j=B_j\) is exact. Induction through \(0\le i<N\) proves (5)–(6). Finally, \[ S_r=(2\sin	heta)^r[r]!,\qquad -ho^2=(2\sin	heta)^2 \] convert \(A_{ijk}S_k^2/(S_i^2S_j^2)\) into (8), with all powers of \(2\sin	heta\) canceled. This verifies the proposed normalization and sign. For instance, \(B_1^2=B_2+(c_0-c_1)B_1\) gives \[ \mu_{111}(s)= rac{\sin((2-2s)	heta)}{\sin	heta}. 	ag{12} \] This checks the shift \(2s\), rather than \(s\), and the sign in (8). At \(s=0\), if \(i+j<N\), (8) reduces to \[ \mu_{ijk}(0)=  rac{S_{i+j}S_k} {S_iS_jS_{k-i}S_{k-j}S_{i+j-k}}, 	ag{13} \] the existing positive complete-source multiplication coefficient. If \(i+j\ge N\), the retained product in (8) contains its zero at \(r=N\), so every coefficient is zero. This agrees with the complete-color divisibility \(B_iB_j=0 mod P_0\). For generic \(s\), these same terms no longer vanish. ## 3. An exact factorization for the opened sector Assume \(i+j\ge N\), and put \[ h=i+j-N,\qquad 
u_{ijk}=  rac{S_kS_h} {S_iS_jS_{k-i}S_{k-j}S_{i+j-k}}. 	ag{14} \] All these numbers are positive. For \(0\le n<N\), define the entire shifted sine product \[ \mathcal A_{N,n}(a) =\prod_{r=1}^{n}  rac{\sin(\pi(r+a)/N)}{\sin(\pi r/N)}. 	ag{15} \] Reflecting the factors below \(N\), retaining the factor at \(N\), and changing the signs above \(N\) gives the exact identity \[  egin{aligned} \prod_{r=k+1}^{N+h}2\sin rac{\pi(r-2s)}N ={}&(-1)^h rac{NS_h}{S_k}\, 2\sin rac{2\pi s}{N}\ &	imes\mathcal A_{N,N-k-1}(2s) \mathcal A_{N,h}(-2s). \end{aligned} 	ag{16} \] Here \(S_{N-k-1}=N/S_k\) uses the complete sine product. The factor at \(r=N\) is \(+2\sin(2\pi s/N)\), not its negative. Hence \[ \mu_{ijk}(s)= (-1)^h\,2N\sin rac{2\pi s}{N}\, 
u_{ijk}\, \mathcal A_{N,N-k-1}(2s)\mathcal A_{N,h}(-2s). 	ag{17} \] This is an identity of entire functions, including \(s=0\). The first derivative has a particularly simple exact form, requiring no bulk assumption: \[  oxed{\; \partial_s\mu_{ijk}(0)=4\pi(-1)^h
u_{ijk}. \;} 	ag{18} \] Both shifted products equal one at zero, and the derivative of \(2N\sin(2\pi s/N)\) there is \(4\pi\). Thus every admissible opened coefficient has a nonzero first derivative at completeness. These are derivatives of the coefficient array in the moving Newton basis; no assertion about the contraction of those derivatives in a knot source follows. ### The first derivative depends on the chosen basis The nonzero derivative in (18) is not an intrinsic first-order change of the quotient multiplication. To see this, identify all the degree-\(<N\) polynomial vector spaces by keeping the complete basis \(e_r(0,\omega)\) fixed. Put \[ \Delta_s=Y^N+Y^{-N}-2=2\cos(2\pi s)-2. 	ag{18a} \] For any two degree-\(<N\) polynomials, divide their product once: \[ fg=P_0Q+R,\qquad \deg R<N,\qquad \deg Q\le N-2. \] Reduction modulo \(P_s=P_0+\Delta_s\) gives the exact fixed-coordinate product \[ \mathsf M_s(f,g)=R-\Delta_sQ. 	ag{18b} \] There is no further reduction, because \(Q\) already has degree less than \(N\). In particular, \(\mathsf M'_0=0\). The connection matrix in [the oriented compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) describes the moving coordinates: \[ e_n(s)=\sum_{k=0}^n C_{nk}(s)e_k(0). \] For \(m=n-k>0\), its derivative is exactly \[ C'_{nk}(0)=  rac{(-1)^{m+1}\pi}{N\sin(\pi m/N)},\qquad C'_{nn}(0)=0. 	ag{18c} \] Indeed the connection coefficient contains exactly one vanishing factor \(1-Y\). Differentiate it and cancel the remaining root factorials. The result before the last simplification is \[ (-1)^{m+1} rac{2\pi i}{N}  rac{q^{-m}}{1-q^{-2m}}, \] which equals (18c). Thus the derivative matrix is triangular and constant along each diagonal. Since \(\sin(\pi m/N)\ge2\min(m,N-m)/N\), both its absolute row sums and its absolute column sums are \(O(\log N)\). Its coefficient \(\ell^2\)-operator norm is therefore \(O(\log N)\). Let \(D\) be the linear operator defined by \(D e_n(0)=\sum_k C'_{nk}(0)e_k(0)\), and let \(\widetilde{\mathsf M}_s\) be multiplication written with moving coefficient labels. Differentiating the change of coordinates gives \[ \widetilde{\mathsf M}'_0(f,g) =\mathsf M_0(Df,g)+\mathsf M_0(f,Dg)-D\mathsf M_0(f,g). 	ag{18d} \] This accounts for (18) as a basis-change effect. At nonzero fixed \(s\), (18b) still contains the genuine order-one factor \(\Delta_s\). The first-order coordinate observation neither removes those sectors for general \(s\) nor bounds their signed contraction. There is a further precise statement for the generator \(\omega\). In the fixed complete basis, let \(A_s\) be its multiplication matrix and let \(\mathbf e_r\) denote the \(r\)-th coefficient vector. At \(s=0\), \[ (A_0)_{rr}=c_r(0),\qquad (A_0)_{r+1,r}=-4\sin^2(\pi(r+1)/N). \] All other entries vanish. Since \(B_N(0)=(-1)^NP_0\equiv(-1)^{N+1}\Delta_s\pmod{P_s}\) and \(S_d=N\), only the last column changes: \[ A_s=A_0+ rac{(-1)^N\Delta_s}{N^2} \mathbf e_0\mathbf e_d^{\,T}. 	ag{18e} \] Thus \(\|A_s-A_0\|_{\ell^2	o\ell^2}=|\Delta_s|/N^2=O_R(N^{-2})\) on every bounded \(s\)-disk. This bound concerns the abstract coefficient norm of the single multiplication generator. It does not bound \(f(A_s)\) for a level-dependent polynomial or any physical turn. For completeness, writing \(E=\mathbf e_0\mathbf e_d^{\,T}\) gives \(E^2=0\) and \(EA_0^mE=0\) for \(m<d\), because \(A_0\) is lower bidiagonal. Starting at \(\mathbf e_0\), each return through \(E\) requires at least \(N\) steps. Hence powers of total degree below \(2N\), applied to the constant vector, contain at most one return, as also follows from the division in (18b). This last statement is about polynomial evaluation on the constant vector, not all entries of a matrix power. ## 4. A uniform shifted-product estimate through its zeros For fixed \(R<\infty\) and \(0<\delta<1/2\), uniformly for \(\delta N\le n\le(1-\delta)N\) and \(|a|\le R\), \[ \mathcal A_{N,n}(a) = rac{(N\sin(\pi n/N)/\pi)^a}{\Gamma(1+a)} V_{N,n}(a), \qquad V_{N,n}=1+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}), 	ag{19} \] where \(V_{N,n}\) is a nonvanishing holomorphic unit on a neighborhood of that disk. Real positive bases in complex powers use their real logarithms. The estimate and its inverse hold with every fixed \(a\)-derivative on smaller disks. To establish the zero-preserving version of (19), let \[ g(t)= rac{\sin(\pi t)}{\pi t},\qquad g(0)=1. \] Use its analytic logarithm near the compact interval \([0,1-\delta]\), extended slightly to the left. Factor the product exactly as \[ \mathcal A_{N,n}(a)=  rac{\Gamma(n+a+1)}{\Gamma(n+1)\Gamma(1+a)} \prod_{r=1}^{n} rac{g((r+a)/N)}{g(r/N)}. 	ag{20} \] The factor multiplying \(1/\Gamma(1+a)\) is nonzero and holomorphic on every fixed \(a\)-disk once \(N\) is large. In particular it defines the unit without dividing by a zero of the sine product. Taylor expansion of \(\log g\), followed by a uniform Riemann-sum estimate, gives \[ \sum_{r=1}^n [\log g((r+a)/N)-\log g(r/N)] =a\log g(n/N)+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}). 	ag{21} \] The uniform Gamma-ratio estimate is \(\Gamma(n+a+1)/\Gamma(n+1)=n^a(1+O_R(n^{-1}))\). Since \(n\ge\delta N\), (19) follows. The exact expression (20), rather than a quotient of two vanishing functions, proves that the error factor is a unit at negative integer \(a\) as well. Cauchy's formula on a larger disk supplies the derivative statements. ## 5. The explicit resonance factor in the opened bulk Assume that \(h\), \(k\), and \(N-k\) stay a fixed positive fraction of \(N\). The admissible index constraints then also keep \(h\) below \(N\) by a fixed positive fraction. Apply (19) to the two factors in (17), and use \[  rac1{\Gamma(1+2s)\Gamma(1-2s)} = rac{\sin(2\pi s)}{2\pi s}. \] This gives the exact factorization \[  oxed{\; \mu_{ijk}(s)= (-1)^h\,2\sin(2\pi s)\,
u_{ijk} \left[  rac{\sin(\pi(k+1)/N)}{\sin(\pi h/N)} ight]^{2s}W_{N,ijk}(s), \;} 	ag{22} \] where, on every fixed complex \(s\)-disk, \[  egin{aligned} W_{N,ijk}(s) &= rac{N\sin(2\pi s/N)}{2\pi s}\, V_{N,N-k-1}(2s)V_{N,h}(-2s),\ W_{N,ijk}(s)&=1+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}),\qquad W_{N,ijk}(0)=1. \end{aligned} 	ag{23} \] The apparent quotient in (23) has its usual value one at zero. It and both \(V\)'s are holomorphic units on the fixed disk for large \(N\). Equations (22)–(23) therefore include every fixed half-integer resonance; no division by \(\sin(2\pi s)\) was used to define \(W\). In particular, throughout this bulk range the only zeros of the coefficient on a fixed disk are the simple zeros of \(\sin(2\pi s)\), once \(N\) is sufficiently large. The quotient by that entire sine factor has a nonzero holomorphic continuation. A lower exponential estimate for \(\mu\) itself cannot hold uniformly through those zeros. Let \[ J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du,\qquad x=i/N,\quad y=j/N,\quad \xi=k/N. 	ag{24} \] The uniform complete factorial estimate \(\log S_r=NJ(r/N)+O(\log N)\), \(0\le r<N\), now gives \[  egin{aligned}  rac1N\log
u_{ijk} ={}&J(\xi)+J(x+y-1)-J(x)-J(y)\ &-J(\xi-x)-J(\xi-y)-J(x+y-\xi) +O(\log N/N). \end{aligned} 	ag{25} \] All arguments of \(J\) in (25) lie in \([0,1]\). At permitted equality faces the same closed factorial estimate applies. Formula (22) shows that (25) is the absolute exponential rate of \(\mu_{ijk}(s)\) for each fixed \(s
otin	frac12\mathbb Z\), and is the rate of its sine-divided continuation uniformly on every fixed \(s\)-disk. It also gives a uniform upper rate for \(\mu\), including at its zeros. The sign \((-1)^h\) in (22) is indispensable. Thus these newly opened sectors do not extend the old positive multiplication cone. ## 6. The old bulk sectors acquire a nonconstant bounded multiplier For the old sector \(i+j<N\), suppose \[ \delta N\le k\le i+j\le(1-\delta)N. \] The exact quotient obtained from (8) and (13) is a product of nonzero factors on every fixed \(s\)-disk for large \(N\). Taking the logarithm near \(s=0\) gives \[  egin{aligned} \log rac{\mu_{ijk}(s)}{\mu_{ijk}(0)} &=- rac{2\pi s}{N}\sum_{r=k+1}^{i+j} \cot(\pi r/N)+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1})\ &=-2s\log rac{\sin(\pi(i+j)/N)}{\sin(\pi k/N)} +O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}). \end{aligned} 	ag{26} \] Therefore \[  oxed{\; \mu_{ijk}(s)=\mu_{ijk}(0) \left[  rac{\sin(\pi(i+j)/N)}{\sin(\pi k/N)} ight]^{-2s} (1+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1})). \;} 	ag{27} \] The final error is again a holomorphic unit, uniform with every fixed derivative. The leading multiplier is generally not one. Thus even within the old support, a microscopic meridian displacement is not automatically a coefficientwise \(1+O(N^{-1})\) perturbation of this normalized gate. Its exponential rate is unchanged, but its order-one normal dependence must be contracted with the rest of the source. ## 7. Scope for a tangle compiler Equations (5)–(8) are exact algebraic multiplication identities in the moving equal-color Casimir algebra. Their proof is valid at both level parities, all composite levels, and all complex meridian displacements. They use no approximation of repeated nodes by simple nodes. The old complete-color support condition \(i+j<N\) is special. Equation (18) shows nonzero first derivatives in the moving basis, while (18b)–(18d) explain why these are not a coordinate-independent first-order obstruction. For nonzero microscopic displacements, the existing strict wire polytope and its old absolute majorant cannot simply be assumed to describe the varied source without additional terms. Conversely the existence of these terms is not a lower bound on a full knot invariant; cancellations and the actual closure remain essential. Equations (22) and (27) identify their normal multipliers and exponential rates in the stated bulk ranges. They do not supply endpoint-uniform analytic bounds for every new gate state. The [oriented compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) gives the exact turns between equal-color and opposite-color sectors and the primitive cut normalization. The [quarter-turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) now bounds every actual turn relative to complete reversal: uniformly in diagonal weighted Newton norms on \(|s|\le R<1\), and with polynomial factors in the full spectral-jet norm on \(|s|\le1/16\). Its fixed polynomial frame does not remove the additional multiplication sectors. A later [whole-source comparison](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md) sums these signed terms before taking absolute values and proves the augmented supremum-volume limit for strict trees with no adjacent bare product junctions. It is uniform over the auxiliary colors and \(|s|\le R<1\), at both parities. This does not bound each opened coefficient by an old positive coefficient. Adjacent bare junctions and the moving filled-knot profile remain beyond that theorem. ## 8. Reproducing the formulas and diagram From the repository root, with SymPy, mpmath and Matplotlib installed, run ~~~sh python3 experiments/audit_main_meridian_newton_algebra.py ~~~ The [script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_newton_algebra.py) directly expands the two sides of the generic multiplication formula over the rational numbers, checks the finite connection formula independently, and checks the dual basis in exact cyclotomic fields. Its [result file](../experiments/main_meridian_newton_algebra_results.json) also contains high-precision bulk-factor diagnostics, distinguished from exact polynomial identities. The same command draws the support diagram in [PDF](../book/figures/moving-newton-products.pdf), [SVG](../book/figures/moving-newton-products.svg), and [PNG](../book/figures/moving-newton-products.png). Finite diagnostics illustrate the proved estimates; they do not prove uniform convergence.

title: The preferred knot-cusp shape from a Conway construction
status: Preferred knot-cusp shape from the original face maps and surgeries
text: # The preferred knot-cusp shape from a Conway construction 1 November 2026. A cusp of a hyperbolic knot complement has a Euclidean torus cross-section. Its meridian goes once around the knot. Its preferred longitude follows the knot once and has linking number zero with it. Normalize the meridian's Euclidean translation to one; the longitude then translates by a complex number \(\tau_{\mathrm{main}}\), the **preferred cusp shape**. This note computes that number from the actual face maps of a Conway construction. The constructions considered here begin with two-string tangles in a ball, with four ordered endpoints. They are joined by vertical stacking and quarter-turns in the projection plane, and then closed by the prescribed cylindrical matching. Each twist region has its original crossing circle: a small auxiliary circle bounding a disk punctured by the two main strands. The [strict Conway construction](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md), Sections 1–3, specifies the endpoint order, closing convention, and angle conditions. In its positive angle domain the leaf angles satisfy \(0<x<1/2\), and every retained product cell satisfies \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. \] Write \(T\) for the actual quarter-turn and \(C\) for this cylindrical closure. The symbol \(R\), when used as a tangle rather than a quadrilateral parameter, denotes the original positive checked crossing. An elementary piece \(h_\epsilon\) contains its retained crossing circle and the half twist \(\epsilon\), after the quarter-turn; \(p_\epsilon\) denotes the same piece before that turn. The forced flat final product is removed with its exact complementary-label relation. These hypotheses supply the actual complete augmented geometry, not just a combinatorial diagram. The [original ribbon cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) identifies the two geometric balls and their face pairings with the augmented link exterior. The [marked deformation](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) continues those maps, keeps the main meridian parabolic, and fixes the primitive auxiliary filling curves. We use those geometric inputs throughout. The proof below first adds the translations of a specified longitudinal path, then determines its framing by homology. In particular, it does not identify a preferred longitude solely from a parabolic trace or from a quantum asymptotic. The geometric result applies to the full strict class with one main knot component. Section 9 gives the quantum consequence for these strict presentations when the fixed signed twists are independently sufficiently long. Those analytic hypotheses are stated there; the geometric calculation is proved directly from the marked representation. ## 1. Statement and conventions Fix a strict ordered Conway construction whose main strands form one component, with no additional internal main circle. Retain all original crossing circles and choose each half-twist sign \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\) in its original leaf frame. The existing marked construction gives a holomorphic representation near its complete augmented holonomy, keeps the main meridian parabolic, and retains the original primitive auxiliary slopes. Let \(U_i,V_i\) be the continued squared-eigenvalue logarithms of the primitive auxiliary meridian and disk longitude, respectively. Fill the auxiliary circles with the original equations \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i,\qquad n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i. \tag{1} \] The main knot cusp is not filled. Group consecutive products with no intervening quarter-turn into a product junction. The resulting calculation tree has a quarter-turn on each edge between junctions; an original crossing-circle operator is retained at its own vertex. Let \(\mathcal E_T\) be these actual quarter-turn edges, including those incident to an original circle vertex. If the ordered quadrilateral at the input of this turn has normalized angle label \(b_e\), define \(x_e=1-b_e\). This is also the label shared by the two ends of the edge in the paired polynomial calculation, where it is called the covariant Newton label. A pair of successive turns may be retained or removed; its two cotangent terms cancel. Let \(w_\epsilon\) be the oriented writhe of the original main diagram with its retained half twists, using the same positive braid convention as the actual \(R\). Let \(\ell_i\) be the linking number of the main component with crossing circle \(i\), in its primitive disk marking. The preferred main-cusp shape on the filled branch is \[ \boxed{\quad \tau_{\mathrm{main}} =2i\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_T}\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}) -\sum_i\epsilon_i-w_\epsilon+\sum_i p_i\ell_i^2. \quad} \tag{2} \] The meridian translates by one, and the orientation is chosen so the cusp shape at the complete point has positive imaginary part. A crossing circle has \(\ell_i=0\) when its two original strands are antiparallel, and \(\ell_i=\pm2\) when they are parallel. Full twists do not change this orientation relation. Consequently, if \(w_{\mathbf n}\) is the oriented writhe after the indicated fillings, the integer in (2) is \[ A=-\sum_i n_i-w_{\mathbf n} =-2\sum_{\text{parallel }i}n_i. \tag{3} \] The first expression is convention-safe: both its integers are taken in the actual original braid convention. In particular the statement does not identify an unmarked cusp lattice with a preferred longitude merely by choosing a positive imaginary part. We prove (2) by first constructing a definite framed longitude in the augmented exterior, computing its translation by local composition, and then determining its homology. The proof is valid for the entire nearby geometric representation, before the auxiliary filling equations are imposed. ## 2. Meridians, endpoint signs, and additive displacement Normalize each ordered quadrilateral to \((C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)=(0,\infty,1,R)\), and put \(E=e^{2\pi i b}\). In these charts, a white face is a piece of an original projection region; the other, shaded faces are pieces of the crossing disks. Use the actual white matrices \[ \begin{split} W_0&=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&E\end{pmatrix}, &W_1&=\begin{pmatrix}1&E-1\\0&E\end{pmatrix},\\ W_2&=\begin{pmatrix}E-R&R(1-E)\\E-1&1-ER\end{pmatrix}, &W_3&=\begin{pmatrix}R&0\\1-E&ER\end{pmatrix}. \end{split} \tag{4} \] At an open shaded boundary some of these are completion maps. The marked geometry theorem proves that every occurrence used in the final closed peripheral paths is supplied by the actual adjacent white face. Set \(d_j=(-1)^j\) and \[ \mu_j=(W_{j-1}^{-1}W_j)^{d_j}. \tag{5} \] The coordinates \[ \begin{split} \xi_0(z)&=\frac{ER}{(E-1)z}, &\xi_1(z)&=-\frac{z}{E-1},\\ \xi_2(z)&=-\frac{E(R-1)}{(E-1)(z-1)}, &\xi_3(z)&=-\frac{R(R-1)}{(E-1)(z-R)} \end{split} \tag{6} \] send the corresponding corner to infinity and send \(\mu_j\) to \(u\mapsto u+1\). These identities follow by multiplying (4). The endpoint sign has a geometric meaning. Orient a main arc into its leaf at corner \(j\). Its positively oriented small meridian is \(\mu_j^{d_j}\); orient the arc out of the leaf and it is \(\mu_j^{-d_j}\). This is the right-hand meridian convention in the ordered projection chart \(0,1,2,3\): crossing one white sector and returning through the preceding one gives \(W_{j-1}^{-1}W_j\) for an inward arc. Formula (5) therefore supplies exactly the displayed signs. At infinity use the finite local coordinate \(1/z\). Reversing the strand orientation reverses both its meridian and the direction of its longitude. Consider an open main arc from corner \(j\) to corner \(k\), including its specified peripheral push-off. In the local coordinates its actual transport has the form \[ u_k=-d_jd_k\,u_j+\beta. \tag{7} \] The multiplier follows by transporting the same oriented meridian: it is \(d_j\) times the local unit at the incoming endpoint and \(-d_k\) times the local unit at the outgoing endpoint. Define the displacement of this arc to be \[ D_{\mathrm{arc}}=-d_k\beta. \tag{8} \] This definition does not depend on the direction in which the arc is followed. The inverse affine map has translation \(-\beta/(-d_jd_k)\), and its displacement is \(-d_j[-\beta/(-d_jd_k)]=-d_k\beta\). This simultaneously reverses the path and the oriented meridian; it does not add raw translations from incompatible meridian frames. When two endpoints are joined by an actual identity segment, its coordinate change from \(j\) to \(k\) has the same affine multiplier \(-d_jd_k\). Its contribution is instead \[ D_{\mathrm{join}}=d_k\beta. \tag{9} \] Here the path leaves the first arc and enters the next. The same inverse-map calculation proves direction independence. These displacements add under concatenation. For an arc \(i\to j\), a joining segment \(j\to k\), and an arc \(k\to l\), write their shifts as \(\beta_X,\beta_J,\beta_Y\). Multiplying the three affine maps gives shift \[ (-d_kd_l)(-d_jd_k)\beta_X +(-d_kd_l)\beta_J+\beta_Y. \] Multiplying by \(-d_l\) gives exactly \[ -d_j\beta_X+d_k\beta_J-d_l\beta_Y. \tag{10} \] The product multiplier is \(-d_id_l\), as required. The same identity applies when a join creates a closed component. A closed component has multiplier one and its displacement is its actual longitude translation in the consistently oriented unit-meridian frame. Let \(S(Q)\) be the sum of these displacements for the two open arcs and any already closed main components inside a tangle. If a boundary coordinate at a corner changes by \(u'_j=\alpha_j u_j+\beta_j\), with \(\alpha_j=d_j/d'_j\), then \[ S(Q')-S(Q)=-\sum_{\text{four endpoints }j}d'_j\beta_j. \tag{11} \] This follows from (8), once at each endpoint. Closed components do not change. Equations (7)–(11) are a local chain lemma: they apply regardless of how many odd leaves a component visits or which direction is used to evaluate it. For an open expression, this is boundary-chart bookkeeping in the original two-ball cut, with its completion maps still labeled as such. It does not declare its metric quadrilateral to be a physical four-punctured tangle boundary or assign virtual white maps to new group generators. The product identities transport this bookkeeping. At the final closure every used white completion is the actual adjacent original white transition, by the marked mask theorem. Only then do the assembled paths give the asserted closed peripheral words. Equivalently, for any one step write \(\xi_bF\xi_a^{-1}(w)=\kappa w+\beta\), and let the globally oriented meridian be the local unit raised to \(\alpha_a,\alpha_b\in\{1,-1\}\). Consistency is \(\alpha_b\kappa=\alpha_a\); the actual translation contribution is \(\alpha_b\beta\). Reversing the traversal replaces the shift by \(-\beta/\kappa\), and reversing the oriented meridian replaces the target sign by \(-\alpha_a\). Their product is again \(\alpha_b\beta\). Equations (8) and (9) are this rule at an arc and a joining segment respectively. This explicitly includes the multiplier-minus-one odd routes below. ## 3. The exact product potential Define the boundary potential \[ P(E,R)=\frac{E+R}{E-1},\qquad I(Q)=S(Q)-P(E,R). \tag{12} \] For the original ordered product prism we claim \[ I(FG)=I(F)+I(G). \tag{13} \] This is an identity of actual coordinate transports, not an equality of their absolute values. Here is a rational verification retaining every translation. Write the prism angle phases as \(a,b,c\), so its vertices are \[ v_0=1,\quad v_1=a,\quad v_2=ab,\quad v_3=abc,\qquad P_*= 1+a-a\,\frac{ab(1+c)-1-a}{a^2b^2c-a}. \tag{14} \] The lower, upper and output ordered quadrilaterals are \((1,a,P_*,\infty)\), \((\infty,P_*,ab,abc)\), and \((1,a,ab,abc)\). Their \(E\) parameters are \(bc,ab,abc\). Their normalized fourth vertices are \[ \begin{split} R_F&=\frac{a(b-1)(bc-1)}{(ab-1)(abc-1)},\\ R_G&=\frac{c(b-1)(ab-1)}{(bc-1)(abc-1)},\\ R_o&=\frac{(b-1)(abc-1)}{(ab-1)(bc-1)}. \end{split} \tag{15} \] Apply (6) after the unique normalized three-point map for each quadrilateral. The two joining and four external rebasing maps all have multiplier one. Their translations are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} F_2\longrightarrow G_1&bc/(bc-1)\\ F_3\longrightarrow G_0&-a(b-1)/[(ab-1)(abc-1)]\\ F_0\longrightarrow o_0&0\\ F_1\longrightarrow o_1&0\\ G_2\longrightarrow o_2&ab(c-1)/[(ab-1)(abc-1)]\\ G_3\longrightarrow o_3&(b-1)(c-1)/[(ab-1)(bc-1)(abc-1)]. \end{array} \tag{16} \] For example a world quadrilateral \((q_0,q_1,q_2,q_3)\) is normalized by \((z-q_0)(q_2-q_1)/[(z-q_1)(q_2-q_0)]\), with the corresponding limits at infinity. Inserting this map into (6) gives (16). By (9) and (11), the correction \(S(FG)-S(F)-S(G)\) is minus the first entry of (16), plus the second, minus the fifth and plus the sixth. Substituting (15) into (12) gives exactly that expression: \[ S(FG)-S(F)-S(G) =P(abc,R_o)-P(bc,R_F)-P(ab,R_G). \tag{17} \] This proves (13). All variables in (14)–(17) are independent wherever the displayed charts are nondegenerate. Thus the identity continues to the original complex deformed branch. In particular hidden binary resolutions inside a product hub contribute no uncancelled term. ## 4. Turns and the final closure The actual quarter-turn is \[ T_Q(z)=\frac{R-1}{z-1},\qquad (E,R)\longmapsto(E^{-1},1-R),\qquad j\longmapsto j-1. \tag{18} \] In the coordinates (6), the four rebasing maps have multiplier minus one. In old corner order \(j=0,1,2,3\), their shifts are \[ \frac{ER}{E-1},\quad-\frac1{E-1},\quad0,\quad\frac R{E-1}. \tag{19} \] Equation (11) gives \(S(TQ)-S(Q)=(ER-R+1)/(E-1)\). Subtract the two potentials in (12). The result is \[ I(TQ)-I(Q)=\frac{2(E+1)}{E-1}=-2i\cot(\pi b). \tag{20} \] This calculation retains the minus multipliers in (19); summing their shifts without (11) would give the wrong sign. At the final reverse-order closing gluing, the two input parameters are \((E,R)\) and \((E^{-1},R)\), and the actual map from the second to the first is \[ C_Q(z)=\frac{z-R}{z-1},\qquad j\longmapsto3-j. \tag{21} \] Its four affine multipliers are one. In old corner order their shifts are \[ \frac R{E-1},\quad-\frac E{E-1}, \quad-\frac1{E-1},\quad\frac{ER}{E-1}. \tag{22} \] The joining correction (9) is \(R-1\), whereas \(P(E,R)+P(E^{-1},R)=1-R\). Therefore the total translation of the closed main components is exactly \[ I(F)+I(G). \tag{23} \] The original closed component decomposition is retained throughout. When the main strands form a knot, (23) is the translation of one primitive longitudinal traversal. ## 5. Pure and odd leaf paths The actual pure and odd shaded maps are \[ S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-ER\\1&-1-E\end{pmatrix},\quad A=\begin{pmatrix}R&-R\\1&ER-1-E\end{pmatrix},\quad B=\begin{pmatrix}R/E-1-1/E&R\\-1&R\end{pmatrix}. \tag{24} \] The pure arcs \(0\to1\) and \(2\to3\) use \(S^{-1}\) and \(S\). From (6), the translations of \(S:1\to0\) and \(S:2\to3\) are \((E+1)/(E-1)\) and \((R-1)/(E-1)\). Thus \[ S(h_0)=\frac{R-E-2}{E-1},\qquad I(h_0)=-\frac{2(E+1)}{E-1}=2i\cot(\pi x). \tag{25} \] At an odd leaf the main arcs pair \(0\) with \(2\) and \(1\) with \(3\). The shaded maps \(B:0^+\to2^-\), \(A:1^+\to3^-\) switch projection balls. To express a path again in the plus frame, use the indicated actual adjacent white return. For the physical sign \(\epsilon=+1\), choose \[ L_{02}^{+}=W_1^{-1}B,\qquad L_{13}^{+}=W_2^{-1}A. \tag{26} \] For \(\epsilon=-1\), choose \[ L_{02}^{-}=W_2^{-1}B,\qquad L_{13}^{-}=W_3^{-1}A. \tag{27} \] These are specified peripheral paths. We will determine their framing by homology rather than assuming that an adjacent white-side choice is the preferred longitude. In the plus \(\xi\) coordinates, all four maps have multiplier minus one, as (7) requires for equal-parity endpoints. Their shifts, in the order \(02,13\), are \[ \begin{split} \epsilon=+1:\quad& \frac E{E-1},\quad\frac{R-E-1}{E-1},\\ \epsilon=-1:\quad& \frac1{E-1},\quad\frac{R-2}{E-1}. \end{split} \tag{28} \] Using (8), rather than summing these raw shifts, gives \[ S(h_\epsilon)=S(h_0)-\epsilon,\qquad I(h_\epsilon)=2i\cot(\pi x)-\epsilon. \tag{29} \] The relations hold at independent nearby \(E,R\). The selected hidden auxiliary color affects \(R\) but does not change (29). Every original \(h_\epsilon\) is the turn of its unturned crossing-circle piece \(p_\epsilon\). Its input label is \(1-x\). Equation (20) therefore says \(I(p_\epsilon)=-\epsilon\). Equations (13), (20) and (23) now prove for the specified closed longitudinal path \[ \tau_{\mathrm{path}} =2i\sum_{e\in\mathcal E_T}\cot(\pi x_e)-\sum_i\epsilon_i. \tag{30} \] This explains precisely why the sum is over physical turn edges, not arbitrary unturned edges in a binary product resolution. Lowering a turn makes its covariant index \(x_e\) complementary to its unturned input. Consecutive double turns contribute opposite cotangents and may be suppressed. Root changes merely reassociate this same geometric sum. ## 6. The integer framing of the constructed path The original marked threading calculation identifies the actual auxiliary meridians as \[ M_+=W_0^{-1}B\quad\text{for physical }R,\qquad M_-=A^{-1}W_0\quad\text{for physical }R^{-1}. \tag{31} \] These signs are fixed geometrically in [the marked geometric deformation](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md), Section 6, from the original threading word; they are not chosen from a quantum asymptotic. The exact odd edge relations give \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} &L_{02}&L_{13}\\ \hline R&\mu_1M_+&M_+^{-1}\\ R^{-1}&M_-&\mu_0M_-^{-1}. \end{array} \tag{32} \] For example \(W_2^{-1}A=M_+^{-1}\), and \(W_1^{-1}B=(W_1^{-1}W_0)M_+=\mu_1M_+\). For the second row use \(W_2^{-1}BW_0^{-1}A=I\) and \(W_3^{-1}W_0=\mu_0\). These are identities of actual group paths, using the already established edge words, and hence also identities in homology. Orient the main knot. At an odd leaf let \(t_0,t_1\in\{1,-1\}\) record whether it follows the canonical arcs \(0\to2\), \(1\to3\) or their reverses. By the endpoint convention in Section 2, \[ [\mu_0]=t_0[\mu_K],\qquad [\mu_1]=-t_1[\mu_K]. \tag{33} \] The first row of (32), traversed with these signs, contributes \[ -t_0t_1[\mu_K]+(t_0-t_1)[M_+] \tag{34} \] to the longitudinal homology. The second contributes \[ t_0t_1[\mu_K]+(t_0-t_1)[M_-]. \tag{35} \] The same coefficient \(t_0-t_1\) is the oriented intersection of the main strands with the original crossing disk. Thus it is their linking number with the circle. The main-meridian coefficients in (34)–(35) are exactly the oriented writhe contributions. To check the convention, undo the literal quarter-turn \(h=T(R^\epsilon)\). Parallel upward strands of the unturned positive braid become \(t_0=1,t_1=-1\): one diagonal is reversed by this quarter-turn. Hence the positive crossing has sign \(-t_0t_1\), and the negative crossing has sign \(t_0t_1\). Reversing just one strand reverses both signs. This is the usual oriented crossing definition, applied to the actual ordered terminal map. For a pure leaf its auxiliary meridian is \(M_0=S^{-1}\). Its two paths are \(M_0,M_0^{-1}\), so their homology contributes only \((t_0-t_1)[M_0]\), and no main-meridian term. Products and turns outside the leaf boxes are actual crossing-free identity strips and rotations. They do not introduce an additional homology contribution. Thus the full path from (30) has \[ [L_{\mathrm{path}}] =w_\epsilon[\mu_K]+\sum_i\ell_i[\mu_i]. \tag{36} \] It traverses the main knot once because every original segment and disk puncture is followed once in its actual oriented component. Therefore it differs from the preferred augmented longitude by exactly \(w_\epsilon\) main meridians: \[ \lambda_K=L_{\mathrm{path}}\mu_K^{-w_\epsilon},\qquad \tau_{\lambda_K} =2i\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e)-\sum_i\epsilon_i-w_\epsilon. \tag{37} \] This step determines the integer part; parabolicity alone would not do so. ## 7. Actual auxiliary fillings and the preferred remaining longitude The original crossing circles are pairwise unlinked: their disk boxes are disjoint, and no circle threads another. In the first homology of the augmented exterior, \[ [\lambda_i]=\ell_i[\mu_K],\qquad [\lambda_K]=\sum_i\ell_i[\mu_i]. \tag{38} \] Here \(\lambda_i\) is the primitive disk longitude used in (1). Filling kills the slope \(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\), so \[ [\mu_i]=-p_i\ell_i[\mu_K],\qquad [\lambda_K]=-\sum_i p_i\ell_i^2[\mu_K] \tag{39} \] in the filled knot exterior. The original main meridian remains primitive. The image of \(\lambda_K\) still traverses the main knot once. Its preferred zero-linking correction is therefore \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{fill}} =\lambda_K\mu_K^{\sum_i p_i\ell_i^2}. \tag{40} \] The two peripheral elements commute, so their unit-meridian translations add. Equations (37) and (40) prove (2), including its surgery sign. ![Two fundamental parallelograms on the filled cusp: the image of the augmented longitude and its preferred correction by four meridians.](../book/figures/main-cusp-longitude-shear.svg) The figure uses one filling with \(p=1\) and \(\ell=\pm2\), so \(c=4\). Both parallelograms belong to the same filled cusp lattice; \(\lambda_{\mathrm{aug}}\) denotes the image of \(\lambda_K\) on that cusp. Finally let \(o_i=1\) for parallel original strands in the unturned braid box and \(o_i=-1\) for antiparallel strands. Equations (34)–(35) give \[ \ell_i^2=2(1+o_i),\qquad w_\epsilon=\sum_i o_i\epsilon_i,\qquad w_{\mathbf n}=\sum_i o_i n_i. \tag{41} \] Use \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\) to obtain \[ -\sum_i\epsilon_i-w_\epsilon+\sum_i p_i\ell_i^2 =-\sum_i(1+o_i)(\epsilon_i-2p_i) =-\sum_i n_i-w_{\mathbf n}. \tag{42} \] This proves (3) and matches the separately derived exact scalar exponent. No cancellation of a carrier or framing factor has been assumed to identify the cusp. ## 8. Scope and analytic continuation The proof uses only the original ordered face maps, actual cusp paths, and homology of the specified disk fillings. It holds for the full small auxiliary deformation furnished by the marked geometric theorem, including arbitrary strict product/turn syntax and arbitrary retained half-twist patterns whose main strands form a knot. The calculation uses no analytic source-growth assumption. The general source theorem now has the same strict-tree scope under its separate long-twist hypotheses. On a sufficiently long filled branch the representation is the actual complete hyperbolic knot holonomy by the existing marked metric completion. Substituting its original critical wire values gives the geometric cusp shape in (2). This is not an identification made from the volume asymptotic, nor a claim that the polynomial annihilator is the knot A-polynomial. For multiple main components the additive calculation tracks each component with its own meridian orientation, but their mutual linking and surgery change require a matrix of preferred-longitude corrections. The statement above deliberately assumes one main knot component. ## 9. The first quantum correction in the established moving class The geometry above and the [filled meridian-profile theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) apply to every fixed strict Conway construction under the stated knot, marking and long-twist hypotheses. The [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) removes the former adjacency, valence and path restrictions from the analytic theorem. Fix such a strict presentation and its original knot and parity pattern. In the strict two-leaf knot case, retain the linked theorem’s pure-leaf qualification. Fix independently sufficiently long signed integers \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\), with no bound on their ratios. The source-dependent lower threshold is chosen once and is independent of the later radius \(R<1\). The presentation and the integers are fixed before the level \(N\) tends to infinity. Let \(F_N(M)\) be its actual zero-framed reduced ADO invariant, with unknot value one and the marked coordinate \(M=q_N^s\), \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\). Its complete value \(F_N(1)\) is the reduced Kashaev invariant. The filled-profile theorem gives, uniformly on every fixed \(|s|\le R<1\), \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)A_N(s)H_N(s)} =1-\frac{\pi s^2}{N}\sum_e\cot(\pi x_e^{\mathrm{fill}}) +O_{\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}), \qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}. \tag{44} \] The [exact scalar calculation](actual_main_meridian_exact_scalar.md) independently proves \[ A_N(s)=q_N^{A s^2/2},\qquad A=-w_{\mathbf n}-\sum_i n_i. \tag{45} \] It retains the full crossing, the prescribed changes of tensor order, the reduced closing trace and the zero-framing correction. In particular it does not discard a carrier or a linear Cartan term by assumption. That scalar proof is separate from the geometric argument above. Now set \(z=2\pi i s\). Then \(M=e^{z/(2N)}\), and define \[ \mathcal H_N(z)= \frac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}, \qquad \mathcal H_N(0)=1. \] Expanding the explicit exponential in (45), and using the geometric identity (2)–(3), yields \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{F_N(e^{z/(2N)})}{F_N(1)\mathcal H_N(z)} =1+\frac{\tau_{\mathrm{main}}z^2}{8\pi iN} +O_{\mathbf n,R}(N^{-2}), \qquad |z|\le2\pi R,\quad R<1.} \tag{46} \] The shape here is the preferred cusp shape of the actual filled knot complement. All crossing circles have been filled; the main knot cusp remains unfilled. The correction is evaluated at the filled geometric branch, not the complete augmented optimizer. Both level parities are included, and uniform holomorphy gives the corresponding fixed derivative statements on smaller disks. In particular, \[ N\left.\frac{d^2}{dz^2} \frac{F_N(e^{z/(2N)})}{F_N(1)\mathcal H_N(z)} \right|_{z=0} \longrightarrow\frac{\tau_{\mathrm{main}}}{4\pi i}. \tag{47} \] For the full modified-trace ADO invariant, the modified-dimension ratio is exactly \(1/\mathcal H_N(z)\). Its complete-normalized profile is therefore the left side of (46), with the same correction. The reduced invariant retains \(\mathcal H_N\). Neither statement crosses the first ordinary-color resonances \(z=\pm2\pi i\). The implication uses the moving asymptotic and the independent geometric translation identity proved above. The geometric proof determines the actual preferred cusp; the analytic proof determines the quantum correction. Neither statement identifies a classical factor of a quantum annihilator. ## 10. Exact finite reproduction The [symbolic reproduction script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.py) checks 75 local identities. It constructs the meridian frames and the three-point maps of the prism directly, checks every product, turn and root translation, verifies the four odd path words, and checks the finite endpoint-orientation and filling-sign formulas. The [saved record](../experiments/main_meridian_preferred_cusp_results.json) lists the checks. The matrix identities are exact rational identities in independent variables, not numerical samples of knots. They support the local calculations in the proof. They do not replace the global identification of the original face pairing, the single longitudinal traversal, the homology calculation, or the marked metric completion. With Python and SymPy installed, run from the repository root: ```bash python3 experiments/audit_main_meridian_preferred_cusp.py ``` The default output is written beside the script. Pass `--output PATH` to select another file. The script performs no network access and uses no private inputs.

title: The trace at a product junction on a regular index window
status: Uniform traces of regular low-index products
text: # The trace at a product junction on a regular index window A product junction without a crossing-circle operator contributes a polynomial trace to the Conway source. When its incident Newton indices lie in a compact part of the strict low-index region, that trace changes by an exponentially small relative amount under a bounded main-meridian deformation. The exact Fourier expansion groups Laurent coefficients whose indices differ by multiples of the level; these groups are called aliases below. Its first alias is independent of the meridian parameter, and strict log-concavity makes every higher alias exponentially smaller. The [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 2, supplies the exact Fourier trace and the finite interval-tail inequality used here. The [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) applies the result at the regular maximizing state. For signed coefficient arrays the conclusion is first an error relative to a positive absolute majorant; control of the whole signed contraction is a separate step. ## 1. The exact kernel and the regular window Let \(N\ge2\), \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), and \[ S_r=\prod_{v=1}^r2\sin(\pi v/N),\qquad e_n(z)=S_n^{-2}\prod_{v=0}^{n-1} \bigl(2\cos((2v+1)\pi/N)-z\bigr). \] Fix a number \(B\) of incident factors. For low indices \(0\le n_i\le M\), put \[ F_N(z)=\prod_{i=1}^{B}e_{n_i}(z),\qquad F_N(-u-u^{-1})=\sum_{k=-D}^{D}a_ku^k, \qquad D=\sum_i n_i. \tag{1} \] The actual finite q-binomial identity gives, for one factor, \[ e_n(-u-u^{-1})=\sum_{k=-n}^{n}a_k^{(n)}u^k, \qquad a_k^{(n)}=\frac{S_{2n}}{S_n^2S_{n+k}S_{n-k}}>0. \tag{2} \] The sequence is symmetric and unimodal. In particular \[ \frac{a_{k+1}^{(n)}}{a_k^{(n)}} =\frac{\sin((n-k)\pi/N)}{\sin((n+k+1)\pi/N)}\le1 \quad(0\le k<n). \tag{3} \] Products correspond to convolutions, so the coefficients \(a_k\) in (1) are also symmetric and unimodal. Choose a fixed \(0<\delta<1/4\). The regular window is \[ \delta\le u_i:=n_i/N\le\frac12-\delta, \qquad \sum_i u_i\ge1+\delta. \tag{4} \] An empty such family causes no difficulty. The upper bound keeps the sine-binomial factors uniformly away from the flat odd-endpoint case; the total bound keeps the old trace in its strict nonzero domain. The number of factors is fixed as \(N\) varies. For \(P_s(z)=\mathsf T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s)\), use the exact normalized top trace \(\phi_s=(-1)^{N-1}N^2[z^{N-1}]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}\). Let \[ d_\ell=a_{\ell N-1}-a_{\ell N+1}\ge0, \qquad L=\left\lfloor\frac{D+1}{N}\right\rfloor. \] The proved finite Fourier identity, with both parities retained, is \[ \phi_s(F_N)=N^2\sum_{\ell=1}^{L} (-1)^{(N-1)(\ell+1)} U_{\ell-1}(\cos(2\pi s))\,d_\ell. \tag{5} \] The coefficient of \(d_1\) is exactly one for every \(s\). All these are fixed complete Newton factors; no moving-basis change or auxiliary color identification has been made. ## 2. Uniform coefficient rates and strong concavity Write \[ J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv, \qquad b_u(t)=J(2u)-2J(u)-J(u+t)-J(u-t),\quad |t|\le u. \tag{6} \] Uniform sine-factorial estimates give \[ \log a_k^{(n)}=N b_{n/N}(k/N)+O(\log N), \tag{7} \] uniformly over (4) and the whole coefficient support. The estimate follows from \(\log S_r=NJ(r/N)+O(\log N)\), including \(r=0\); the two endpoint logarithmic cells contribute only \(O(\log N)\). For \(|t|<u\), \[ b_u''(t)=-\pi\bigl[\cot\pi(u+t)+\cot\pi(u-t)\bigr] =-\frac{\pi\sin(2\pi u)} {\sin\pi(u+t)\sin\pi(u-t)}. \tag{8} \] Consequently on the compact range (4), \[ b_u''(t)\le-\lambda_\delta, \qquad \lambda_\delta:=\pi\sin(2\pi\delta)>0. \tag{9} \] The continuous function \(b_u\) remains strongly concave on its closed interval; its endpoint derivatives may be infinite. Define the convolution action \[ \mathcal B_{\mathbf u}(t)= \max_{\substack{\sum_i t_i=t\\|t_i|\le u_i}} \sum_i b_{u_i}(t_i). \tag{10} \] It is even and strongly concave with constant \(\lambda_\delta/B\). Indeed, interpolate two maximizing vectors at two total indices. The sum of (9)'s strong-concavity remainders is at least \(\lambda_\delta\|\mathbf t-\mathbf v\|_2^2/2\), and \(\|\mathbf t-\mathbf v\|_2^2\ge B^{-1}|\sum_i(t_i-v_i)|^2\). Therefore \(\mathcal B_{\mathbf u}(t)+\lambda_\delta t^2/(2B)\) is even and concave. It is nonincreasing on its nonnegative interval. In particular, \[ \mathcal B_{\mathbf u}(t_2)-\mathcal B_{\mathbf u}(t_1) \le-\frac{\lambda_\delta}{2B}(t_2^2-t_1^2) \quad(0\le t_1\le t_2\le\sum_i u_i). \tag{11} \] The finite convolution has the uniform rate \[ \log a_k=N\mathcal B_{\mathbf u}(k/N)+O_{B,\delta}(\log N) \quad(|k|\le D). \tag{12} \] For the upper bound, use (7) and the polynomial number of tuples in the convolution. For the lower bound, round a maximizing real tuple in (10) to integers with its prescribed sum \(k\), changing each coordinate by at most one. This is possible by flooring all coordinates and then increasing the required number with nonzero fractional parts; the integer endpoints \(\pm n_i\) are respected. The uniform modulus \(|J(x+h)-J(x)|\le C|h|\log(e/|h|)\) on \([0,1]\) bounds the resulting action error by \(O(\log N/N)\), even if a coordinate lies at an endpoint. One positive summand then proves the lower bound. Thus (12) does not assume an unproved derivative asymptotic for the convolution. ## 3. Higher aliases are exponentially small relative to the first difference For \(\ell\ge2\) with \(\ell N-1\le D\), apply (11) with \(t_1=1-1/N\), \(t_2=\ell-1/N\). Since \[ t_2^2-t_1^2=(\ell-1)(\ell+1-2/N)\ge2, \] equation (12) gives \[ \frac{a_{\ell N-1}}{a_{N-1}} \le N^C\exp(-\lambda_\delta N/B). \tag{13} \] The denominator exists because (4) implies \(D>N-1\). If the numerator lies outside the support, set it to zero. It remains to compare a coefficient to its first discrete difference. The elementary interval-tail inequality for a convolution of \(B\) symmetric unimodal sequences supported in \([-M,M]\) states \[ a_k\le(2M+1)^B(a_k-a_{k+2})\qquad(k\ge M). \tag{14} \] Its proof is finite: decompose each sequence into a nonnegative sum of interval indicators. For a product of such indicators, the convolution count strictly drops by step two beyond the largest interval radius whenever the first count is nonzero; that positive integer difference is at least one, whereas the count is at most \((2M+1)^B\). Summing the interval decompositions proves (14). This is the same all-index lemma used in the adjacent-level source comparison. Applying (14) at \(k=N-1\) gives \[ d_1\ge N^{-B}a_{N-1}>0. \tag{15} \] Combining \(0\le d_\ell\le a_{\ell N-1}\), (13), and (15) proves \[ \sum_{\ell=2}^{L}\frac{d_\ell}{d_1} \le N^{C'}\exp(-\lambda_\delta N/B). \tag{16} \] Here \(L\) is bounded in terms of \(B\). The conclusion is uniform throughout (4). ## 4. The local deformed trace has the same leading kernel For every fixed complex disk \(|s|\le R\), \[ |U_{\ell-1}(\cos(2\pi s))| \le\ell\exp(2\pi(\ell-1)R). \tag{17} \] This follows from its finite exponential sum and holds through all sine resonances. At \(s=0\), the value is \(\ell\). Equation (16) therefore shows, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \phi_0(F_N)=N^2d_1\bigl(1+O(e^{-\kappa N})\bigr)>0, \qquad \boxed{\quad \frac{\phi_s(F_N)}{\phi_0(F_N)} =1+O_{B,\delta,R}(e^{-\kappa N}).\quad} \tag{18} \] One can take any fixed \(\kappa<\lambda_\delta/B\), after absorbing the polynomial factors. The sign alternation at even levels is included in (5) and is harmless once (16) is proved. The opposite-color relation remains constant, so its corresponding statement is exact without a deformation. For fixed \(B\le4\), there are no higher aliases for any low indices: \(D\le4M\le2N-2\), so \(L\le1\). Then \[ \phi_s(F_N)=\phi_0(F_N) \tag{19} \] for every \(s\), with no regular-window hypothesis; a zero trace remains zero. This also follows by the one-division degree bound. The ratio in (18) is entire in \(s\), with a constant positive denominator. Applying (18) on a slightly larger fixed disk and using Cauchy's estimate gives the same exponential error for every fixed derivative in \(s\). No contour avoiding a resonance is needed for this local trace statement. ## 5. Applying the local estimate to a source The result concerns the exact raw polynomial trace of the prescribed fixed-coordinate factors. It has not replaced a physical auxiliary color by a coefficient index. Any original color dependence remains in the coefficients multiplying those factors. The typed turn, circle pivot, crossing scalar and primitive main-cut normalization are separate parts of the compiler. On a compact bulk index window, the proved paired-turn formula also gives \(W_n(s)/H_N(s)=1+O_R(N^{-1})\), and the six type scalars \(q^{\pm s^2/2}\) are \(1+O_R(N^{-1})\). Thus a fixed product of the local trace kernels in (18) and those specified bulk turn factors has the same leading fixed-state weight, with the appropriate \(O(N^{-1})\) turn error. This statement retains the actual types; it is not a replacement of the moving multiplication law by the complete one globally. For arbitrary signed coefficient arrays supported in a common window satisfying (4), (18) implies an error bounded by \(e^{-\kappa N}\) times the corresponding complete positive absolute contraction. It does not imply a relative error with respect to a possibly canceling signed contraction. Similarly the turn errors have an \(O(N^{-1})\) absolute-majorant bound. To conclude a whole-source microscopic profile, one must also control the literal main-meridian deformation of the physical input coefficients, establish suitable conditioning or stationary cancellation for their contraction, and bound the complement of the regular window. None of these follows just from (18). The [regular circle trace](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md) gives the physical input deformation and its canonical analytic interpolation. The [component extension](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md) controls grouped high-index errors, while the [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) proves the finite-window and contour statements needed to use these local estimates. The [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) combines those inputs with a joint charge comparison. The present result is the regular-window trace estimate; it does not obtain a whole-source relative error from a potentially cancelling coefficient sum.

title: Circle traces and leaf coefficients near the complete meridian
status: The circle trace and exact sine-factorial interpolation
text: # Circle traces and leaf coefficients near the complete meridian A crossing circle contributes its ordinary quantum character, and an adjacent half-twist contributes the physical crossing operator. This note studies their trace, and the leaf coefficients obtained by a quarter-turn, while the main meridian varies near completeness. The formulas keep the crossing scalar, the ordinary-circle pivot, and the orientation-dependent quarter-turn. It proves an exact formula for pure leaves, and a relative asymptotic for half-twisted leaves on any compact interval of regular low Newton indices. In particular the moving leaf ratio is derived from its finite source, rather than inferred from the bounded turn multiplier. The [Newton compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) fixes the orientation spaces and cut pairing; the [turn comparison](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) fixes the coordinate formula used below. Section 10 constructs the canonical Gamma interpolation needed in the [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md). The [direct crossing trace](actual_main_meridian_direct_crossing_trace.md) then treats arbitrary fixed crossing powers. A relative profile for a whole knot requires the additional global comparisons in the [filled-volume theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md). ## 1. Coordinates and the exact coefficient extractor Put \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad d=N-1,\quad Q=q^2,\quad M=q^s, \qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N), \] \[ S_n=\prod_{a=1}^n2\sin(\pi a/N),\qquad e_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(c_a-z),\qquad 0\le r<N. \tag{1} \] These are the fixed complete Newton polynomials. The input algebra is the equal-color algebra \[ P_s(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2\cos2\pi s, \qquad \phi_s(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F. \tag{2} \] Here \(\mathcal T_N(u+u^{-1})=u^N+u^{-N}\). The actual circle polynomial and equal-color checked crossing are \[ L_j(z)=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2),\qquad \kappa_s=q^{(d+s)^2/2},\qquad \lambda_a=(-1)^a q^{a(a+1)}q^{-2sa}. \tag{3} \] The full crossing has values \(\kappa_s\lambda_a\) at the moving roots, with its holomorphic repeated-root continuation. Its inverse is interpreted in the same physical quotient. Write the typed fixed-coordinate turn as \[ T_s=\frac{\gamma_N(s)}{H_N(s)}\mathcal R\operatorname{diag}(W_n(s)), \qquad \mathcal R e_n=e_{d-n}, \tag{4} \] \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_n(s)=\prod_{a=1}^n \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi a/N)}\right). \tag{5} \] The scalar \(\gamma_N(s)\) is the prescribed one among \(1,q^{s^2/2},q^{-s^2/2}\). In particular the turn from equal-color \(++\) endomorphisms to the mixed morphism space has \(\gamma_N(s)=q^{-s^2/2}\). All values at zero are removable. The exact identity \(W_rW_{d-r}=H_N^2\) gives the physical coefficient \[ h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,j) :=[e_r]T_s(R_s^\epsilon L_j) =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_r(s)} \phi_s(e_rR_s^\epsilon L_j),\qquad \epsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}. \tag{6} \] Every scalar in (6) is retained. The formula is in a specified input/output frame, not an identification of all orientation types without their carriers. ## 2. Pure leaves: an exact identity at every auxiliary color For every physical \(1\le j\le N\) and every \(0\le r<N\), \[ \boxed{h_{N,s}^{0}(r,j) =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_r(s)}h_{N,0}^{0}(r,j).} \tag{7} \] Indeed \(\deg(e_rL_j)\le2N-2\). If this polynomial is divided by \(P_0\), its quotient has degree at most \(N-2\). Replacing \(P_0\) by \(P_s=P_0+\Delta_s\) changes the remainder by \(-\Delta_s\) times that quotient, of degree at most \(N-2\). Its top coefficient is unchanged. Thus \(\phi_s(e_rL_j)=\phi_0(e_rL_j)\), proving (7). This includes zeros of the complete coefficient; it is an identity of coefficients rather than a ratio asserted at those zeros. For the complete ordinary color \(j=N\), the low coefficient is exactly \[ h_{N,0}^{0}(r,N)=N^2\frac{S_{2r}}{S_r^4},\qquad 2r<N. \tag{8} \] The pure result therefore already includes every physical deficit, both parities, and every pre-resonance compact main disk \(|s|\le R<1\). ## 3. Complete auxiliary color: exact shifted-grid formula Let \[ \tau_a(s)=\frac{2\pi}{N}\left(\frac d2+s-a\right),\qquad C_{N,\epsilon}(s)=q^{\epsilon(d^2/4-s^2/2)}. \tag{9} \] The full crossing values, including the Cartan scalar, obey \[ (\kappa_s\lambda_a)^\epsilon =C_{N,\epsilon}(s) \exp\left(\frac{i\epsilon N\tau_a(s)^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{10} \] Since \(L_N=(-1)^dP_s'/N\), ordinary Lagrange interpolation first at generic \(s\), followed by holomorphic continuation, proves \[ \phi_s(e_rR_s^\epsilon L_N) =N C_{N,\epsilon}(s)\,\mathcal Q_{N,r}^\epsilon(s), \tag{11} \] \[ \mathcal Q_{N,r}^\epsilon(s) =\sum_{a=0}^{N-1} e_r(-2\cos\tau_a(s)) \exp\left(\frac{i\epsilon N\tau_a(s)^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{12} \] Formula (11) retains the full confluent trace at \(s=0\), including the simple last node at odd levels. It is not a replacement of a repeated-root trace by arbitrary nodal values: the factor \(P_s'\) makes this particular root sum exact. Fix a compact \(I\subset(0,1/2)\), and write \(x=r/N\in I\). For \(|\tau|\) small, the numerator of \(e_r(-2\cos\tau)\) is nonzero. Direct differentiation gives \[ \frac{d^2}{d\tau^2}\log e_r(-2\cos\tau)\bigg|_{\tau=0} =-\frac12\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi(a+1/2)}N\right) =-\frac{N}{2\pi}\tan\pi x+O(N^{-1}). \tag{13} \] All fixed higher derivatives are \(O_I(N)\) on a fixed smaller disk. The complete Newton angular estimate also gives constants \(c,C,y_0>0\), uniformly in \(x\in I\), such that \[ |e_r(-2\cos(t+iy))| \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{Ng(x)} e^{-Nc t^2+NCy^2},\qquad |t|\le\pi,\quad |y|\le y_0. \tag{14} \] Here \(g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x)\), with \(J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\). The factor at zero satisfies \[ e_r(-2)=\frac{e^{Ng(x)}}{2N\sin\pi x}\,[1+O_I(N^{-1})]. \tag{15} \] The numerator uses midpoint Euler--Maclaurin; the denominator uses the usual sine-factorial expansion. Both expansions are uniform on \(I\). ## 4. Exponentially accurate grid shift and a nonzero anchor For every \(R_0<1/2\), there is \(c_0>0\) such that \[ \mathcal Q_{N,r}^\epsilon(s) =\frac{N}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} e_r(-2\cos t)e^{i\epsilon Nt^2/(4\pi)}\,dt +O\left(e^{N(g(x)-c_0)}\right),\quad |s|\le R_0, \tag{16} \] where polynomial factors have been absorbed by decreasing \(c_0\). The same statement holds for \(\epsilon=0\). Here is the quadrature proof, including the nonperiodic endpoints of the chirp. Set \(\eta=(-1)^{N+1}\), \(a_s=\eta e^{2\pi is}\), and \[ K_s(\tau)=\frac{iNe^{iN\tau}}{e^{iN\tau}-a_s}. \tag{17} \] On a rectangle with vertical sides \(\operatorname{Re}\tau=\pm\pi\) and horizontal sides \(\operatorname{Im}\tau=\pm y\), its residues select exactly the \(N\) points in (12). On the upper horizontal side \(K_s=O_R(Ne^{-Ny})\); on the lower side \(K_s=iN+O_R(Ne^{-Ny})\). On the vertical sides \(|K_s|\le C_RN\), by the same positive-ray denominator estimate used for the paired-grid contour. The integrand apart from \(K_s\) is bounded by \(\operatorname{poly}(N)\exp N(g-ct^2+Cy^2+|ty|/(2\pi))\). Choose fixed \(y>0\) small. Completing the square makes the horizontal error at most \(\exp N(g-y+C'y^2)\). The vertical sides have a fixed strict deficit. Move the lower straight integral to the real segment; its two connecting vertical integrals have the same deficit. This proves (16) without making the chirp periodic or discarding an endpoint current. The integral in (16) is nonzero for large \(N\). Its elementary local Gaussian expansion, using (13), is \[ \frac{N}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} e_r(-2\cos t)e^{i\epsilon Nt^2/(4\pi)}\,dt =\frac{\sqrt N\,e_r(-2)}{\sqrt{\tan\pi x-i\epsilon}} [1+O_I(N^{-1})]. \tag{18} \] The square root has positive real part. The complement of a fixed small neighborhood is exponentially smaller by (14). On that neighborhood, the analytic fourth-order remainder and Gaussian integration give the uniform \(O(N^{-1})\) relative error. Thus (16) has a lower bound of a fixed multiple of \(\sqrt N e_r(-2)\). In particular, \[ \frac{\mathcal Q_{N,r}^\epsilon(s)}{ \mathcal Q_{N,r}^\epsilon(0)} =1+O(e^{-c_0'N}),\qquad |s|\le R_0. \tag{19} \] ## 5. The actual complete-color leaf ratio and first correction Combining (6), (11), and (19) gives \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,N)}{h_{N,0}^{\epsilon}(r,N)} =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_r(s)}q^{-\epsilon s^2/2} [1+O_{I,R}(e^{-cN})],} \tag{20} \] for every compact \(I\subset(0,1/2)\), every fixed \(R<1\), both parities, and \(\epsilon=0,\pm1\). For \(\epsilon=0\), (20)'s error is exactly zero. To justify the full radius \(R<1\), first use (19) on any fixed smaller disk \(R_0<1/2\). Divide the actual coefficient by the explicit nonvanishing prefactor and its nonzero complete coefficient. The resulting error is holomorphic on \(|s|<1\). On every larger fixed disk \(R'<1\), the physical leaf coefficient cone in the [source-bound theorem](actual_main_meridian_source_bounds.md), Section 1 bounds its magnitude by a power of \(N\): its numerator is \(\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{Ng(x)}\), while (15),(18) bound its complete denominator below by \(\operatorname{poly}(N)^{-1}e^{Ng(x)}\). Hadamard's three-circles inequality between \(R_0\) and \(R'\) keeps a strictly negative exponential exponent on every intermediate radius. This extends (20). This step uses actual holomorphy through the removable collision at \(s=\pm1/2\), not the chosen unwrapped grid as a formula outside its original rectangle. The paired bulk product has the uniform expansion \[ \log\frac{W_r(s)}{H_N(s)} =\frac{\pi s^2}{N}\cot\pi x+O_{I,R}(N^{-2}). \tag{21} \] For completeness, compare \(r\) to the midpoint. At odd \(N\), \(H_N=W_{(N-1)/2}\); at even \(N\), \(H_N=W_{N/2-1}\cos(\pi s/N)\). Expand only the intervening factors, whose indices lie in a compact interior interval. Their logarithmic sum is \(-\pi^2s^2N^{-2}\sum\csc^2(\pi a/N)+O(N^{-3})\), and the elementary integral of \(\csc^2\) gives (21). The even extra cosine changes only the \(O(N^{-2})\) term. Write \(\gamma_N(s)=q^{\alpha s^2/2}\), with \(\alpha\in\{-1,0,1\}\) fixed by the actual orientation. Then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,N)}{h_{N,0}^{\epsilon}(r,N)} =1+\frac{s^2}{N} \left[-\pi\cot\pi x+\frac{i\pi}{2}(\alpha-\epsilon)\right] +O_{I,R}(N^{-2}).} \tag{22} \] Every fixed \(s\)-derivative has the corresponding error on smaller disks by Cauchy's estimate. This identifies the leading amplitude and its first main-meridian correction. The physical chirp scalar and the typed-turn scalar both contribute, even though the leading ratio tends to one. For the \(++\) input, \(\alpha=-1\). For an opposite-color input expressed in the prescribed mixed reference, the quotient is constant and the crossing polynomial is the fixed complete \(r_0\), up to its explicitly retained scalar monodromy factors. In that case the trace itself is independent of \(s\); its ratio is exactly \(\gamma_N(s)H_N/W_r\) times those scalar factors. The extra factor \(q^{-\epsilon s^2/2}\) in (20) belongs to the moving equal-color crossing, not to a constant opposite-color crossing. Frame factors must be applied according to the actual six-type table. ## 6. A joint continuation for small auxiliary deficits This section gives a concrete holomorphic continuation of the actual physical grid near \(j=N\). It does not assert that every possible off-integer continuation is equal to it. Put \(h=Nt\), with \(t\) complex and small, and retain the unwrapped grid from (9). Let \[ F_{N,r}^{\epsilon}(\tau)=e_r(-2\cos\tau)e^{i\epsilon N\tau^2/(4\pi)}, \] \[ A_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)=\sum_aF_{N,r}^{\epsilon}(\tau_a(s))\cos(Nt\tau_a(s)), \quad B_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)=\sum_aF_{N,r}^{\epsilon}(\tau_a(s))\sin(Nt\tau_a(s)). \tag{23} \] Define \[ \widetilde h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,t) =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_r(s)} N C_{N,\epsilon}(s) \left[A_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)-\cot(2\pi s)B_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)\right]. \tag{24} \] The value at \(s=0\) is removable: the grid is symmetric there, the first factor is even in \(\tau\), and \(B(0,t)=0\). Formula (24) is holomorphic jointly for \(|s|<1/2\) and all finite \(t\). At every physical integer \(h\), \(j=N-h\) in its original range, it is exactly the physical coefficient. This follows directly from the generic-root trace and \[ \sin((N-h)\tau_a(s)) =\eta\left[\sin2\pi s\cos(h\tau_a(s)) -\cos2\pi s\sin(h\tau_a(s))\right]. \tag{25} \] Its complete value therefore keeps the true repeated-root normal contribution, including the derivative implicit in \(\cot(2\pi s)B(s,t)\). For each \(R<1/2\) and compact \(I\), choose a sufficiently small fixed \(t_0>0\). The same rectangle proof gives, uniformly on \(|s|\le R\), \(|t|\le t_0\), \[ A_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)=\frac N{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} F_{N,r}^{\epsilon}(\tau)\cos(Nt\tau)\,d\tau +O(e^{N(g(x)-c)}),\qquad B_{N,r}^\epsilon(s,t)=O(e^{N(g(x)-c)}). \tag{26} \] The integral of the sine term vanishes by oddness. On a slightly larger \(s\)-disk, the same bound and \(B(0,t)=0\) bound the product \(\cot(2\pi s)B(s,t)\) holomorphically through zero. The additional exponential cost \(e^{N\pi|\operatorname{Im}t|+N|t|y}\) is absorbed by taking \(t_0\) small before fixing the gap. The integral in (26) has a unique analytic saddle near zero and a nonzero leading amplitude. Define the analytic logarithmic action near \(\tau=0\) \[ b(x,\tau)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi v+2\cos\tau)\,dv-2J(x), \] \[ \Psi_\epsilon(x,\tau,t)=b(x,\tau)+\frac{i\epsilon\tau^2}{4\pi}+it\tau, \qquad \partial_\tau\Psi_\epsilon(x,\tau_*,t)=0,\quad \tau_*(x,0)=0. \tag{27} \] Its Hessian at zero is \(-(\tan\pi x-i\epsilon)/(2\pi)\), bounded away from zero. A small analytic contour displacement through \(\tau_*\), retaining exponentially small vertical endpoints, proves a uniform relative \(1+O(N^{-1})\) saddle expansion. In particular its modulus is at least \(\operatorname{poly}(N)^{-1}\exp N(g(x)-C|t|^2)\) after shrinking \(t_0\). Thus \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{\widetilde h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,t)}{ \widetilde h_{N,0}^{\epsilon}(r,t)} =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{W_r(s)}q^{-\epsilon s^2/2} [1+O(e^{-c'N})],\quad |s|\le R<1/2,\quad |t|\le t_0.} \tag{28} \] The first correction (22) consequently holds for this joint continuation as well, uniformly in its small complex \(t\)-disk. At physical integer deficits this is a statement about the actual leaf. No analytic continuation through the additional resonances of (24) at \(s=\pm1/2\) is claimed for noninteger \(h\). For physical integer deficits alone, (28) extends to every fixed \(R<1\) after possibly shrinking \(t_0\) depending on \(R\). On a larger disk \(R'<1\), the actual coefficient cone and the complete saddle lower bound give a normalized bound \(\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{Ct_0^2N}\). On a fixed disk below \(1/2\), the error in (28) is \(O(e^{-cN})\). The three-circles inequality bounds its logarithmic rate on the intermediate disk by \[ -\beta c+(1-\beta)Ct_0^2, \qquad \beta=\frac{\log(R'/R)}{\log(R'/R_0)}>0. \tag{28a} \] Choose \(t_0\) so that this is negative. The constants are uniform over all physical \(0\le h/N\le t_0\) and all wire indices in \(I\). This extension uses the actual physical polynomial at each integer color; it does not assert that the off-integer function (24) is regular through \(s=\pm1/2\). ## 7. The auxiliary action and leading amplitude are the old selected ones The saddle of (27) also identifies the continuation's complete asymptotic. Midpoint Euler--Maclaurin gives, uniformly on a small complex \(\tau\)-neighborhood, \[ e_r(-2\cos\tau)=\frac{1}{2N\sin\pi x} e^{Nb(x,\tau)}[1+O(N^{-1})]. \tag{29} \] After removing exactly the old unit phase \(e^{i\epsilon\pi d/4}\), (24) at \(s=0\) has leading action and amplitude \[ f_\epsilon(x,t)=\Psi_\epsilon(x,\tau_*(x,t),t),\qquad \beta_\epsilon(x,t)= \frac{e^{-i\epsilon\pi/4}} {2\sin\pi x\sqrt{2\pi[-\partial_\tau^2\Psi_\epsilon(x,\tau_*,t)]}}, \tag{30} \] \[ e^{-i\epsilon\pi d/4}\widetilde h_{N,0}^{\epsilon}(r,t) =N^{1/2}\beta_\epsilon(x,t)e^{Nf_\epsilon(x,t)}[1+O(N^{-1})]. \tag{31} \] The square root continues the positive-real branch when \(\epsilon=t=0\). At completeness, \[ f_\epsilon(x,0)=g(x),\quad \beta_0(x,0)=\frac{1}{2\sin\pi x\sqrt{\tan\pi x}},\quad \frac{\beta_\epsilon(x,0)}{\beta_0(x,0)} =\sqrt{\sin\pi x}\,e^{-i\epsilon\pi x/2}\quad(\epsilon=\pm1). \tag{32} \] These agree with the actual complete phase and amplitude; no parity phase has been changed. The pure saddle action is \[ g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t). \tag{33} \] One direct verification uses \[ b_\tau(x,\tau)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{artanh} \left(\tan\pi x\tan\frac\tau2\right). \tag{34} \] At the pure saddle, \(\tan(\tau_*/2)=i\tan(\pi t)/\tan(\pi x)\), and hence \(i\tau_*=\partial_tg(x,t)\). The actions agree at \(t=0\), proving (33). With a half-twist, introduce \(u\) by \[ t=u-\frac{\epsilon}{2\pi i}g_u(x,u). \] Then substitution into (27) gives exactly \[ f_\epsilon(x,t)=g(x,u)-\frac{\epsilon}{4\pi i}g_u(x,u)^2. \tag{35} \] This is the shear selected in the [complex-color source packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md). Equations (30)--(35) provide its nonzero leading amplitude on every compact regular low-index interval. They do not by themselves identify all subleading terms of every alternative off-integer factorial interpolation; (24) is the explicitly chosen continuation in the moving parameter. ## 8. Scope of the coefficient statements The exact pure identity holds for every physical auxiliary color. The half-twisted complete-color theorem (20)--(22) holds for every compact regular low-index interval and every main disk \(R<1\). The joint small-deficit continuation (24)--(35) is proved on \(R<1/2\); it agrees exactly with every physical color on its grid and has an exponential relative grid-shift error.
