The statements are all-level, with the original parity, crossing and typed-turn factors intact. The proof does not control the entire coefficient range or supply a deformed global source lower bound. It also does not compare a filled invariant to its own smaller volume. The estimates through Section 9 are uniform over the physical integer low-index window. Section 10 supplies a specified analytic factorial-and-integral continuation in the complex wire coordinate, with exponential agreement on that physical grid. ## 9. A whole circle-carrying junction The same argument applies to a fixed number \(B\ge1\) of low Newton factors. Define \[ E_{N,\mathbf n}(z)=\prod_{a=1}^B e_{n_a}(z),\qquad V_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf n) =\phi_s\left(R_s^\epsilon L_NE_{N,\mathbf n}\right), \qquad 0\le n_a\le\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor. \tag{36} \] The raw product is retained inside the trace; its degree need not be less than \(N\). Lagrange interpolation still gives exactly \[ V_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf n) =N C_{N,\epsilon}(s) \sum_{r=0}^{N-1}E_{N,\mathbf n}(-2\cos\tau_r(s)) e^{i\epsilon N\tau_r(s)^2/(4\pi)}. \tag{37} \] No quotient norm or termwise estimate of the new multiplication sectors enters this identity. There is an all-index bound by the complete positive tensor: \[ \boxed{|V_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf n)| \le C_{B,R}N\,V_{N,0}^{0}(\mathbf n),\qquad |s|\le R<1.} \tag{38} \] Here every low index, including zero and the endpoint, is allowed. To prove it, use the positive Laurent coefficients \[ e_n(-u-u^{-1}) =\sum_{k=-n}^{n} \frac{S_{2n}}{S_n^2S_{n-k}S_{n+k}}u^k, \qquad 2n<N. \tag{39} \] At the shifted grid, \(|\operatorname{Im}\tau_r(s)|\le2\pi R/N\). Therefore \[ |e_n(-2\cos\tau_r(s))| \le e^{2\pi Rn/N}e_n(-2)\le e^{\pi R}e_n(-2). \tag{40} \] The chirp and its full scalar in (37) are bounded there by a constant depending only on \(R\). Thus the left side of (38) is at most \(C_{B,R}N^2\prod_a e_{n_a}(-2)\). At completeness every low factor is nonnegative at every Casimir node: it vanishes at a previous node, and otherwise all its defining factors have the same positive ordering. Consequently \[ V_{N,0}^0=N\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}E_{N,\mathbf n}(-2\cos\tau_r(0)). \tag{41} \] At odd levels a node is exactly \(-2\), giving \(V_{N,0}^0\ge N\prod e_{n_a}(-2)\). At even levels put \(N=2m\), \(\theta=\pi/N\). The closest node is \(-2\cos\theta\), and \[ \frac{e_n(-2\cos\theta)}{e_n(-2)} =\prod_{a=0}^{n-1} \frac{\cos(a\theta)\cos((a+1)\theta)} {\cos^2((a+1/2)\theta)}. \tag{42} \] Each factor is positive and at most one, by the concavity of \(\log\cos\) on this interval. Hence (42) decreases with \(n\). The ordinary cosine products at the maximal allowed \(n=m-1\) give \[ \prod_{a=1}^{m-1}\cos(a\theta)=\frac{\sqrt m}{2^{m-1}},\qquad \prod_{a=0}^{m-1}\cos((a+1/2)\theta)=2^{1/2-m}, \] \[ \frac{e_{m-1}(-2\cos\theta)}{e_{m-1}(-2)} =m\tan(\theta/2)\ge\frac\pi4. \tag{43} \] This includes \(m=1\) with the empty-product interpretation. Thus \[ V_{N,0}^0(\mathbf n) \ge N(\pi/4)^B\prod_a e_{n_a}(-2) \tag{44} \] at every parity, proving (38). The comparison is with the actual complete pure tensor at the same level; no adjacent-level substitution or unproved signed lower bound is used. Now assume all \(x_a=n_a/N\) lie in a fixed compact \(I\subset(0,1/2)\). The product satisfies (14) with summed curvature \[ T(\mathbf x)=\sum_{a=1}^B\tan\pi x_a>0. \tag{45} \] The rectangle quadrature and nonzero Gaussian anchor become \[ \sum_r E_{N,\mathbf n}(-2\cos\tau_r(0)) e^{i\epsilon N\tau_r(0)^2/(4\pi)} =\frac{\sqrt N\prod_a e_{n_a}(-2)} {\sqrt{T(\mathbf x)-i\epsilon}}[1+O(N^{-1})]. \tag{46} \] Every constant is uniform on the fixed product window. Equations (37), (46), and the same three-circles argument prove \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{V_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf n)}{V_{N,0}^{\epsilon}(\mathbf n)} =q^{-\epsilon s^2/2}[1+O_{B,I,R}(e^{-cN})], \qquad |s|\le R<1.} \tag{47} \] For the extension step, (38) and (46) bound the normalized holomorphic family polynomially on every larger compact main disk, since the complete pure and half-twisted Gaussian anchors have the same nonzero rate. No moving high-degree canonical polynomial stability is assumed. The first correction is therefore \(-i\epsilon\pi s^2/(2N)+O(N^{-2})\), before any typed-turn scalar belonging to an adjacent edge is applied. Multilinear expansion of (38) also bounds arbitrary complex low arrays by the complete pure tensor of their absolute coefficient arrays. Equation (47), in contrast, is a local kernel statement on the regular product window. For signed sums it gives an error bounded by the absolute complete-window majorant; a relative statement for the sum still requires a noncancellation comparison. Finally, replacing \(e_r\) by \(E_{N,\mathbf n}\) in (23)--(28) gives the same small-deficit continuation for a whole circle-carrying junction. Its saddle uses \(\sum_a b(x_a,\tau)+i\epsilon\tau^2/(4\pi)+it\tau\), with Hessian \(-(T(\mathbf x)-i\epsilon)/(2\pi)\). The relative factor is again \(q^{-\epsilon s^2/2}\) with exponential error on \(R<1/2\) and a sufficiently small complex \(t\)-disk. The original integer auxiliary colors, pivot, and full crossing are retained. This local extension does not by itself establish the filled source's absolute-window/noncancellation comparison. ## 10. An explicit joint analytic interpolation in the wire variable The grid-only qualification in Section 8 can be removed locally by constructing, rather than postulating, an analytic interpolant. This does not change any finite coefficient. Use the existing canonical sine-factorial function \[ G_N(z)=\left(\frac{2\pi}{N}\right)^z\Gamma(z+1) \prod_{k\ge1}\frac{\Gamma(Nk+z+1)} {\Gamma(Nk-z)(Nk)^{2z+1}},\qquad -1<\operatorname{Re}z<N, \tag{48} \] with its fixed positive-base logarithms. It is holomorphic and nonzero on this strip, obeys \(G_N(0)=1\), \(G_N(r)=S_r\), and \(G_N(z+1)/G_N(z)=2\sin(\pi(z+1)/N)\). The [exact factorial interpolation theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) proves these facts and the uniform complex bulk expansion. The normalization in (48) is fixed; it cannot be changed by multiplying by an unspecified periodic function. For complex \(x\) near \(I\) and small complex \(\tau\), define \(u=N\tau/(2\pi)\) and \[ \mathcal E_N(x,\tau)= \frac{G_N(d/2+u)G_N(d/2-u)} {G_N(d/2-Nx+u)G_N(d/2-Nx-u)G_N(Nx)^2}. \tag{49} \] At every physical \(x=r/N\), the exact shift identity shows \(\mathcal E_N(r/N,\tau)=e_r(-2\cos\tau)\). Indeed the two numerator-to-denominator ratios are the products of \(2\cos((a+1/2)\pi/N\mp\tau/2)\), whose product is the defining Newton numerator. All arguments in (49) stay in fixed complex bulk strips after choosing the \(x\)-neighborhood and the \(\tau\)-disk sufficiently small. Hence (49) is analytic there, with the uniform expansion (29). Likewise set \[ \mathcal W_N(x,s)= \frac{G_N(Nx-s)G_N(Nx+s)} {G_N(Nx)^2G_N(-s)G_N(s)}. \tag{50} \] At physical \(x=r/N\) this is exactly \(W_r(s)\). The two endpoint factors in (50) are nonzero on \(|s|<1\), and the other factors are in the same regular bulk domain. The canonical product makes the endpoint cancellation explicit. Gamma reflection and the paired factors in (48) give \[ G_N(s)G_N(-s) =\frac{\pi s}{\sin\pi s} \prod_{k\ge1}\left(1-\frac{s^2}{N^2k^2}\right) =\frac{N\sin(\pi s/N)}{\sin\pi s} =\frac1{H_N(s)}. \tag{50a} \] Consequently \[ \frac{H_N(s)}{\mathcal W_N(x,s)} =\frac{G_N(Nx)^2}{G_N(Nx-s)G_N(Nx+s)}. \tag{50b} \] Thus the exact turn factor in the local interpolation is a ratio of three regular bulk factorials; it has no unknown endpoint normalization. Choose a fixed small real \(a>0\) inside that domain, and define the concrete interpolant \[ \mathfrak h_N^\epsilon(x,s,t)= \gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{\mathcal W_N(x,s)} \frac{N^2 C_{N,\epsilon}(s)}{2\pi} \int_{-a}^{a}\mathcal E_N(x,\tau) e^{i\epsilon N\tau^2/(4\pi)}\cos(Nt\tau)\,d\tau. \tag{51} \] It is jointly holomorphic on fixed smaller neighborhoods in \(x,t,s\). Its saddle remains strictly inside the integration endpoints after shrinking these neighborhoods. The endpoint contributions are exponentially smaller uniformly, and the saddle amplitude is nonzero. Equations (16),(26) and the real-grid Newton tail estimate show \[ \widetilde h_{N,s}^{\epsilon}(r,t) =\mathfrak h_N^\epsilon(r/N,s,t) [1+O(e^{-cN})] \tag{52} \] uniformly over the physical regular wire indices, \(|s|\le R<1/2\), and a sufficiently small fixed complex \(t\)-disk. For integer \(Nt\) in the physical range, the left side is the literal physical coefficient. The same construction at \(t=0\), combined with Section 5, works on every fixed main disk \(R<1\). More generally, (28a) proves that (51) is an exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of all the physical integer-deficit rows on any fixed \(R<1\), with the small \(t\)-neighborhood chosen depending on that radius. The interpolant itself is holomorphic for complex \(t\) throughout that neighborhood. Its comparison beyond \(R=1/2\) is asserted on the physical integer rows, not as equality with the resonant unwrapped continuation (24). The interpolation itself has the exact ratio \[ \frac{\mathfrak h_N^\epsilon(x,s,t)}{ \mathfrak h_N^\epsilon(x,0,t)} =\gamma_N(s)\frac{H_N(s)}{\mathcal W_N(x,s)}q^{-\epsilon s^2/2}. \tag{53} \] There is no unknown meridian-dependent amplitude in (53). Its first correction is (22), now holomorphically in \(x\) on a smaller neighborhood, by the same bulk factorial expansion. The full leading action and amplitude are (30),(31). The construction is valid on either side of \(x=1/4\), since its Gaussian Hessian is nonzero throughout the entire compact interval \(I\subset(0,1/2)\). For a circle-carrying junction, replace \(\mathcal E_N(x,\tau)\) in (51) by \(\prod_{a=1}^B\mathcal E_N(x_a,\tau)\), and omit the turn factor if the quantity is the junction trace itself. This gives the corresponding joint analytic interpolation of (37) and its small-deficit version. Its exact main ratio is \(q^{-\epsilon s^2/2}\); edge turn factors remain separate. The comparison to the physical grid is exponentially accurate with the same proof. These interpolants supply the local analytic input needed for a complex wire saddle. They do not supply a global bound for a signed contraction, its off-window states, or a filled invariant. The [component extension](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md) supplies the grouped high-index comparison, and the [grouped wire packet](actual_main_meridian_grouped_wire_packet.md) supplies the finite-window and contour arguments. Those are separate inputs from the local meridian dependence identified here.

title: Why a moving multiplication trace cannot be bounded at the same indices
status: An exponential counterexample to a trace bound at unchanged indices
text: # Why a moving multiplication trace cannot be bounded at the same indices 1 November 2026. A product junction in a Conway calculation multiplies several tangle operators before taking their trace. After expanding those operators in the complete Newton basis, one obtains traces of products of basis polynomials. A tempting estimate would bound each moving trace by a polynomial in the level times its complete trace at exactly the same basis indices. This estimate is false, even for a junction with nine incident factors and a strictly positive complete trace. Here “high” refers to a Newton basis index greater than \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). It does not refer to the physical color of an auxiliary crossing circle. The example has exactly one high index and satisfies the complete pairwise support inequalities. Its moving-to-complete ratio grows exponentially along both level parities. The proof below keeps the exact quotient trace, including derivatives at repeated roots. The conclusion concerns an individual tensor entry, not a knot invariant or a whole tangle contraction. The [reflected Fourier estimate](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md) and the [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) explain how the full source can still be controlled: they compare the change in the trace with a different, reflected index and retain the neighboring branch profiles. ## 1. Conventions and the family Let \(\mathcal T_N\) be the monic normalized Chebyshev polynomial characterized by \(\mathcal T_N(u+u^{-1})=u^N+u^{-N}\). The level is \(N\), the complete meridian is \(s=0\), and the moving meridian is \(M=q^s\). Set \(S_0=B_0=1\). Use the fixed complete Newton polynomials \[ \begin{gathered} N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\\ S_n=\prod_{r=1}^n2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad B_n(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(c_j-z),\qquad e_n=B_n/S_n^2,\\ P_0(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2,\qquad P_s=P_0+\Delta_s,\qquad \Delta_s=2\cos(2\pi s)-2,\\ \phi_s(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F. \end{gathered} \tag{1} \] The node index runs over \(0\le j\le d\), and the basis consists of \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\). Here \(\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F\) is the unique remainder of degree less than \(N\) after division by the monic polynomial \(P_s\), and \([z^d]\) extracts its coefficient of \(z^d\). All products in the trace are ordinary polynomial products followed by this single exact quotient reduction. Thus repeated-root derivative data are retained, rather than replacing the trace by evaluations only. For an integer \(a\ge7\), take \[ N=5a+1,\qquad d=5a,\qquad h=4a, \qquad \mathcal Z_a(s)=\phi_s(e_h e_a^8). \tag{2} \] There are nine factors. Exactly one index, \(h\), is high. The other eight indices equal \(a=d-h\). Each high/low pair has sum \(d\), each low/low pair has sum \(2a<d\), and the total is \(12a>d\). These are the complete pairwise and total-sum support conditions; a tuple satisfying them is called complete-admissible here. Its support is on a pair-equality face; no assertion of strict interior admissibility is being made. We prove an exact identity \[ \mathcal Z_a(s)=\mathcal Z_a(0)+(-1)^a\Delta_s\mathcal B_a, \qquad \mathcal Z_a(0)>0,\quad \mathcal B_a>0, \tag{3} \] and the explicit lower bound \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{\mathcal B_a}{\mathcal Z_a(0)} \ge\frac1{3(5a+1)} \left(\frac{25000}{6561}\right)^a.} \tag{4} \] For every fixed \(s\) with \(\Delta_s\ne0\), (3)–(4) imply \[ \frac{|\mathcal Z_a(s)|}{\mathcal Z_a(0)} \ge \frac{|\Delta_s|}{3(5a+1)} \left(\frac{25000}{6561}\right)^a-1. \tag{5} \] In particular no power of \(N\), even with a constant depending on a fixed disk \(|s|\le R<1\), can bound this ratio for any \(R>0\). One may choose one fixed nonzero real or imaginary \(s\) in that disk. As \(a\) varies, the levels in (2) include both parities. For even \(a\) and imaginary nonzero \(s\), both summands in (3) are positive; (5) does not require this favorable sign. ## 2. An exact complementary-index identity The reflection of the complete nodes gives \(B_N=(-1)^NP_0\) and \(B_hB_{a+1}=B_N\), since \(h+a=d\). Also \(S_hS_a=N\). Consequently \[ e_he_a=\frac{(-1)^d}{N^2}\frac{P_0(z)}{z-c_a}. \tag{6} \] The denominator on the right divides \(P_0\); the expression is a polynomial. Put \(F=e_a^7\) and \[ D(z)=\frac{F(z)-F(c_a)}{z-c_a}. \tag{7} \] Then \(\deg D=7a-1<2N-1\). A single division by \(P_0\) has quotient degree at most \(N-2\). Replacing \(P_0\) by \(P_0+\Delta_s\) therefore does not change the top trace coefficient: \[ \phi_s(D)=\phi_0(D). \tag{8} \] The same degree argument gives \(\phi_s(e_he_a)=1\). Multiplying (6) by \(F\), using (7), and reducing \(P_0=-\Delta_s\) proves \[ \mathcal Z_a(s) =F(c_a)-\Delta_s\frac{(-1)^d}{N^2}\phi_0(D). \tag{9} \] There is no quadratic or higher term in \(\Delta_s\). The exact complete value is \[ \mathcal Z_a(0)=F(c_a) =\left(\frac{S_{2a}}{S_a^2}\right)^7>0. \tag{10} \] Here \(B_a(c_a)=S_{2a}\), obtained by multiplying \(c_r-c_a=4\sin((a+r+1)\pi/N)\sin((a-r)\pi/N)\) for \(0\le r<a\). ## 3. Removing the repeated upper nodes A divided difference records polynomial interpolation at several points; when points repeat, it records derivatives there as well. For a real node multiset \(\Lambda=(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_m)\), including repetitions, write \(F[\Lambda]\) for the Hermite divided difference. It has the algebraic description \[ F[\Lambda]=[z^{-1}] \frac{F(z)}{\prod_{j=0}^m(z-\lambda_j)}, \tag{11} \] where the coefficient is in the Laurent expansion at infinity. This is the top coefficient of the polynomial remainder, so (11) requires no limiting choice of distinct roots. Let \(\Lambda_N=(c_0,\ldots,c_d)\), the roots of \(P_0\) with their actual multiplicities. Equations (7) and (11) give \[ \frac{(-1)^d}{N^2}\phi_0(D) =D[\Lambda_N]=F[c_a,\Lambda_N]. \tag{12} \] The last equality follows by writing \(F=(z-c_a)D+F(c_a)\); the constant term divided by a monic polynomial of degree \(N+1\) has no \(z^{-1}\) coefficient. The nodes \(c_0,\ldots,c_{a-1}\) are all larger than \(c_a\), and each occurs twice in \(\Lambda_N\). Cancel their quadratic factor \(B_a(z)^2\) between numerator and denominator in (11). Since \(F=B_a^7/S_a^{14}\), this gives \[ F[c_a,\Lambda_N] =G[\Lambda_a],\qquad G(z)=\frac{B_a(z)^5}{S_a^{14}}. \tag{13} \] The remaining multiset \(\Lambda_a\) consists of the \(N-2a=3a+1\) uncanceled complete nodes, together with the one extra \(c_a\). It therefore has \(3a+2\) nodes, every one at most \(c_a\), and the divided-difference order is \[ m=3a+1. \tag{14} \] This cancellation includes repeated-node derivatives exactly. Put \(\delta_r=c_r-c_a>0\) for \(0\le r<a\). On the entire interval below \(c_a\), \[ G(c_a-v)=\frac1{S_a^{14}} \prod_{r=0}^{a-1}(\delta_r+v)^5, \qquad v\ge0. \tag{15} \] Every coefficient in this polynomial in \(v\) is positive. Hence \((-1)^mG^{(m)}(z)>0\) for \(z\le c_a\), and its magnitude is at least its magnitude at \(c_a\). The real divided-difference formula is \[ G[\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_m] =\int_{\substack{t_j\ge0\\\sum t_j=1}} G^{(m)}\!\left(\sum t_j\lambda_j\right)\,dt, \tag{16} \] with simplex measure of total mass \(1/m!\). It follows by repeated use of the fundamental theorem of calculus and remains valid for repeated nodes by continuity. Since all the nodes in (13) are at most \(c_a\), (15)–(16) prove \[ \operatorname{sign}G[\Lambda_a]=(-1)^m, \qquad |G[\Lambda_a]| \ge\frac{|G^{(m)}(c_a)|}{m!}. \tag{17} \] Equations (9), (12) and (14) now give (3), with \(\mathcal B_a=|G[\Lambda_a]|\): the coefficient of \(\Delta_s\) has sign \(-(-1)^{3a+1}=(-1)^a\). ## 4. An explicit exponential lower bound Let \(L_a=c_0-c_a\), so \(0<\delta_r\le L_a\). The coefficient of \(v^m\) in (15), divided by \(F(c_a)\), is \[ \frac1{B_a(c_a)^2} e_m(\delta_0^{-1},\ldots,\delta_0^{-1}, \ldots,\delta_{a-1}^{-1},\ldots,\delta_{a-1}^{-1}), \tag{18} \] where each reciprocal appears five times and \(e_m\) in this formula denotes the elementary symmetric polynomial, rather than a Newton basis element. Each of its \(\binom{5a}{m}\) summands is at least \(L_a^{-m}\), while \(B_a(c_a)^2\le L_a^{2a}\). Therefore \[ \frac{\mathcal B_a}{F(c_a)} \ge \binom{5a}{3a+1}\,L_a^{-(5a+1)}. \tag{19} \] For \(a\ge7\), \[ \frac{2a+1}{5a+1}\le\frac5{12},\qquad c_a\ge2\cos\frac{5\pi}{12}>\frac12, \qquad L_a<\frac32. \tag{20} \] The middle term of a binomial distribution with \(5a\) trials and success probability \(3/5\) is a mode. Its mass is at least \(1/(5a+1)\). Thus \[ \binom{5a}{3a}\ge\frac1{5a+1} \left(\frac{5^5}{3^3 2^2}\right)^a, \qquad \binom{5a}{3a+1}=\binom{5a}{3a}\frac{2a}{3a+1} \ge\frac12\binom{5a}{3a}. \tag{21} \] Insert (20)–(21) into (19). The remaining factor is \[ \frac{1}{2(5a+1)} \left(\frac{5^5}{3^3 2^2}\right)^a \left(\frac23\right)^{5a+1} =\frac1{3(5a+1)}\left(\frac{25000}{6561}\right)^a, \tag{22} \] which proves (4). In particular, for any fixed \(\Delta_s\ne0\), \[ \liminf_{a\to\infty}\frac1{5a+1} \log\frac{|\mathcal Z_a(s)|}{\mathcal Z_a(0)} \ge\frac15\log\frac{25000}{6561}>0. \tag{23} \] ## 5. What the obstruction rules out The family disproves a uniform pointwise estimate \(|\phi_s(\prod e_i)|\le N^{C_R}\phi_0(\prod e_i)\) on all complete-admissible tuples of a fixed valence. Allowing a prefactor depending on \(R\) does not help. There is a strictly positive complete denominator, exactly one high input, and an explicit exponential lower bound. The same construction applies at both even and odd levels. The indices lie on complete pair-equality faces. The example does not disprove an estimate restricted to a fixed strict compact interior window. More fundamentally, a tensor entry does not include the neighboring physical coefficient profiles or the sum over shared indices. Those additional factors and correlations are part of the whole Conway source. This is therefore not a counterexample to a knot-volume theorem. The useful replacement is a bound on the difference between the moving and complete traces. In the exact Fourier formula for that difference, the first Fourier contribution cancels. The [reflected Fourier theorem](actual_main_meridian_high_fourier_reflection.md) bounds the remaining contribution by a complete trace with the high index \(h\) replaced by the low index \(d-h\), with a strict exponential improvement on the relevant regular windows. It does not assert the false comparison at unchanged indices proved impossible here. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) combines this reflected estimate with exact Frobenius contraction and the original coupled positive action. Reflection can fuse two junctions in a comparison tree; the geometric pressure of that tree is no greater than the original pressure. These comparison operations bound correction terms without changing the actual knot, the original finite source, or its marked filling action. Thus the obstruction explains why that proof retains whole contractions instead of using an estimate on each unchanged tensor entry.

title: Source growth near the complete main meridian
status: Source growth near the complete main meridian and the augmented volume
text: # Source growth near the complete main meridian The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) extends this result to every fixed strict Conway tree. The proof below establishes the original separated-junction case and its physical input estimates. The general theorem retains the same invariant, normalization and radius restrictions. Fix a knot construction made by stacking and turning two-strand tangles, with \(H\ge2\) original pieces. Before inserting their long twists, keep the crossing circle around each piece. The resulting **augmented complement** is the complement with these crossing circles left unfilled. Their integer colors \(j_i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) label the ordinary representations used in the quantum calculation; they have not yet been summed with filling coefficients. A **product junction**, also called a hub below, is a place where several tangle operators are multiplied without intervening turns. Combine adjacent product junctions until every remaining internal edge carries a quarter-turn. Mark a junction when one of its original crossing-circle operators occurs there without that outer turn; such a junction is called flagged. A junction without this operator is called bare. We assume that **no two bare junctions are adjacent**. The number of junctions and their valences may be any fixed finite numbers. The construction must also satisfy the existing [strict Conway conditions](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md): its retained angle inequalities have an interior solution, its prescribed endpoint tracing gives one main component, and it has no internal closed component. These conditions refer to the original ordered tangle diagram. For two pieces, retain the knot-producing half-twist choices; those contain the pure leaf needed by the two-leaf asymptotic theorem. **Supremum-volume theorem.** Let \(\mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(M)\) be the reduced quantum scalar obtained by cutting the specified main strand, with reduced unknot value one and the original framing retained. The main meridian color variable has complete value \(M=1\). Write \(M=q^s\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\); bounded \(s\) describes a neighborhood of size \(O(1/N)\) in \(M\). Let \(Y^\epsilon\) be the complete augmented complement of the original construction. For every fixed \(0\le R<1\), \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\sup_{\substack{|s|\le R\\\mathbf j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}^{H}}} \left|\mathcal F_{N,\mathbf j}^{\epsilon}(q^s)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}(Y^\epsilon).} \] The limit runs through both parities. The upper bound is uniform over the displayed meridian disk and every auxiliary color. The matching lower bound uses the particular complete value \(s=0\), \(\mathbf j=(N,\ldots,N)\). It is therefore an equality for the supremum, not a lower bound at each displaced meridian or at each color tuple. ![Two bare multiplication junctions feed a central junction carrying the original crossing-circle operator, with a quarter-turn on each internal edge.](../book/figures/separated-product-junctions.svg) Two bare product junctions are separated by a junction carrying the original crossing-circle operator \(p_0\). Multiply each outer pair, apply the quarter-turn \(T\) along each junction edge, and close after multiplying by \(p_0\). The definitions \(p_i=R^{\epsilon_i}L_{j_i}\), \(h_i=T(p_i)\) retain every original auxiliary color. Here \(R^{\epsilon_i}\) is the prescribed half-twist and \(L_{j_i}\) encircles the strands by the circle of color \(j_i\). The drawing represents algebraic operations and their order; it is not a knot projection. The theorem concerns the quantum sum **before the auxiliary fillings**. It does not identify the generally smaller volume of the resulting filled knot at a displaced main meridian. The [general component comparison](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) extends the source bound to arbitrary connected bare regions. The separate [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) proves the normalized profile and the filled knot-complement volume limit, using additional local and joint filling estimates. Moving the main meridian changes both the multiplication of polynomial operators and the physical turn. The extra multiplication terms have alternating signs; estimating them separately can lose the correct exponential rate. The proof instead first controls a turn preceded by the actual crossing-circle operator, and then compares a whole bare junction with the positive complete calculation after summing its signed terms. At even levels, an adjacent odd level is used only inside the estimate; an exact map of positive summation paths returns the bound to the original level. The detailed definitions of the polynomial norm, repeated-root derivatives, and geometric action follow below. The finite physical inputs are the [typed main-meridian compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md), the [six physical turn formulas](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md), the [actual crossing-circle normalization](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md), and the [positive complete Newton multiplication law](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md). The needed crossing, loop, quotient, Fourier, and adjacent-level estimates are proved explicitly below. The complete geometric pressure comparisons are identified where they enter. ## 1. Actual decorated turns: coefficients, norms, and angular localization ### 1.1. The fixed coordinates and the two actual algebras Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor d/2\rfloor, \quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i\theta},\quad Q=q^2, \quad x=-q^{-1}q^s,\quad y=-q^{-1}q^{-s}. \tag{D1} \] The microscopic main meridian is \(M=q^s\). The two roots \(x,y\) give the actual dual modules, denoted by signs \(+,-\). Write \(\mathsf T_N(t+t^{-1})=t^N+t^{-N}\). Equal-color ordered pairs have relation \[ P_s(z)=\mathsf T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s), \tag{D2} \] whereas opposite-color pairs have the constant relation \(P_0\). The same relation (D2) applies to the two equal-color orders, since it is even in \(s\). At every vertex use the relation of its actual ordered object; these two quotient multiplications are not identified. All polynomial coordinates below are in the fixed complete basis \[ S_n=\prod_{r=1}^n2\sin(r\theta),\qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\qquad e_n(z)=S_n^{-2}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(c_j-z),\quad0\le n<N. \tag{D3} \] Empty products are one. A canonical polynomial always has degree less than \(N\), independently of the relation used to obtain it. Let \[ \|F\|_{\mathrm J}=\max\bigl\{|F(c_j)|:0\le j\le m; \ |F'(c_j)|:c_j\text{ is a double root of }P_0\bigr\}. \tag{D4} \] At odd levels the last node \(-2\) is simple and has no derivative coordinate. This is a norm on canonical polynomials. It is polynomially equivalent, uniformly in level and parity, to the canonical sup norm on \([-2,2]\) and to the Chebyshev coefficient norm. This comparison uses full Hermite interpolation; it does not discard first normals or evaluate only on the moving simple nodes. For either relation define \[ \phi_{\sigma}(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_\sigma}F, \qquad \sigma=s\text{ or }0. \tag{D5} \] Then the exact fixed-basis metric is \[ \phi_\sigma(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=d}. \tag{D6} \] Indeed, at \(\sigma=0\) this is the complete Newton metric. For \(\deg(e_i e_j)\le2N-2\), divide \(e_i e_j=P_0A+B\). The degree of \(A\) is at most \(N-2\), so the moving remainder \(B-\Delta_s A\), \(\Delta_s=2\cos2\pi s-2\), has the same coefficient of \(z^d\). This proves (D6), including the return sectors of the multiplication. If \(F=\sum f_n e_n\) is canonical, it follows that \[ f_{d-k}=\phi_\sigma(e_kF). \tag{D7} \] The product in (D7) is reduced in the input object's relation. ### 1.2. Polynomial quotient estimates, with returns retained Set \(C_n(t+t^{-1})=(t^n+t^{-n})/2\), \(C_0=1\), and use \(\|\sum a_nC_n\|_{\mathrm{Ch}}=\sum|a_n|\). The identity \(2C_iC_j=C_{i+j}+C_{|i-j|}\) makes this norm submultiplicative. In (D2), \(C_N=-b\), \(b=\cos2\pi s\), so \[ \operatorname{rem}C_{N+r}=-2bC_r-C_{N-r}\quad(0<r<N), \qquad \operatorname{rem}C_{kN+r}=-2b\operatorname{rem}C_{(k-1)N+r} -\operatorname{rem}C_{(k-2)N+r}. \tag{D8} \] For \(r=0\), start with \(1,-b\). For \(|s|\le R\), put \(L_R=2\cosh(2\pi R)+1\). Induction gives \[ \|\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F\|_{\mathrm{Ch}}\le L_R^h\|F\|_{\mathrm{Ch}} \quad(\deg F\le hN). \tag{D9} \] The same estimate includes the opposite-color relation by setting \(s=0\). It is a polynomial identity argument, valid even at repeated roots. In particular, a fixed number of canonical factors obeys \[ \left\|\operatorname{rem}_{P_\sigma}\prod_{a=1}^h F_a\right\|_{\mathrm J} \le C_{R,h}N^{C_h}\prod_a\|F_a\|_{\mathrm J}. \tag{D10} \] Here and below a displayed power of \(N\) is independent of the physical auxiliary colors and of \(s\) in its specified disk. It can depend on fixed word length or tree size. The sup-to-Chebyshev comparison follows from the cosine integral for coefficients, and the derivative bound from Markov's inequality. Combining it with full complete Hermite interpolation proves (D10). For a canonical polynomial, its top monomial coefficient is a fixed multiple of its top Chebyshev coefficient: \([z^d]C_d=1/2\) for \(d\ge1\). Hence \[ |\phi_\sigma(F)|\le C N^2\|\operatorname{rem}_{P_\sigma}F\|_{\mathrm{Ch}}. \tag{D11} \] Equations (D9)--(D11) control the whole quotient operation. They do not majorize a return term separately by an old positive gate and do not require an increasing return-permitting open profile. ### 1.3. The physical crossing and circle character On the equal-color object \(++\), the actual checked crossing has common scalar and stripped spectral values \[ \kappa_s=q^{(d+s)^2/2},\qquad t_j=q^{-2j-1}Q^s,\quad c_j(s)=t_j+t_j^{-1},\qquad \lambda_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}Q^{-sj}. \tag{D12} \] For a fixed integer crossing power \(n\), including negative \(n\), let \(r^{[n]}_{N,s}\) denote the canonical polynomial with values \(\lambda_j^n\). Its full physical representative is \(\kappa_s^n r^{[n]}_{N,s}\). The \(--\) object uses \(-s\). For every fixed \(0\le R<1\) and \(n\), \[ \sup_{|s|\le R}\|r^{[n]}_{N,s}\|_{[-2,2]}+ \sup_{|s|\le R}\|\partial_zr^{[n]}_{N,s}\|_{[-2,2]} \le C_{R,n}N^4. \tag{D13} \] Here is the collision-safe argument. Away from \(\sin2\pi s=0\), exact Lagrange interpolation is \[ r^{[n]}_{N,s}(z)= -\frac1{N(U-U^{-1})}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \lambda_j^n(t_j-t_j^{-1})\frac{P_s(z)}{z-c_j(s)}, \qquad U=e^{2\pi is}. \tag{D14} \] The quotient is a divided difference of \(\mathsf T_N\). Nodes lie in a Bernstein ellipse of angular height \(2\pi|\operatorname{Im}s|/N\), on which its first two derivatives are \(O_R(N^2),O_R(N^4)\). Integrating along the segment from a real point to a node gives (D13) with the extra factor \(|\sin2\pi s|^{-1}\). Distinct-node collisions inside \(|s|<1\) occur only at \(s=0,\pm1/2\). Their paired indices satisfy \(j+l+1-2s=N\), and exactly \[ \lambda_l/\lambda_j=(-1)^{l-j}q^{(l-j)(j+l+1-2s)}=1. \tag{D15} \] Both the value difference and the node difference vanish, the latter simply. The resulting divided differences are holomorphic, and the confluent interpolation matrix is invertible. Thus the polynomial coefficients extend holomorphically across those collisions. Apply the maximum principle on a fixed larger parameter circle of radius less than one and different from \(1/2\) to remove the apparent denominator uniformly. This proves (D13). The common scalar \(\kappa_s^n\), its inverse, and each prescribed fixed framing correction are bounded on the same disk: their ratio to the complete scalar has exponent \(O_{R,n}(1)\). They are retained, not set equal to one. For mixed orders use the physical carrier convention of the turn theorem: \[ G_{-+}=\check R_{x,y}r_0(\Omega_{x,y})^{-1},\qquad G_{+-}=I, \qquad r_0=\kappa_0\sum_{n=0}^{d}(-q)^ne_n. \tag{D16} \] The forward mixed crossing has reference polynomial \(r_0\). Reversing the reference order adds the exact monodromy scalar, since \[ \check R_{y,x}\check R_{x,y}=q^{-s^2}r_0(\Omega)^2. \tag{D17} \] Thus reverse crossings, inverses, and every fixed composable crossing word have the corresponding fixed powers of \(r_0\) and the retained powers of \(q^{-s^2}\). Formula (D13) at \(s=0\) and (D10) bound their canonical norms polynomially. These assertions concern the specified Casimir intertwiner spaces, not arbitrary physical matrix norms. For an ordinary auxiliary color \(1\le j\le N\), the actual encircling operator is exactly \[ L_j(\Omega)=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(\Omega/2). \tag{D18} \] To retain its normalization, take the auxiliary module of weights \(j-1-2a\), \(0\le a<j\), with actual closing pivot \(K_j^{1-N}=(-1)^{j-1}K_j\). First take independent generic target roots. Their tensor product has distinct typical highest summands. On a summand of highest root \(w\), the nilpotent transfers cannot contribute to the highest coefficient of the encircling monodromy, and the Cartan and standard-pivot trace is \[ \sum_{a=0}^{j-1}(qw)^{j-1-2a} =U_{j-1}\bigl((qw+q^{-1}w^{-1})/2\bigr). \tag{D19} \] The actual pivot supplies the sign in (D18). Since the loop intertwines, the generic highest coefficients prove the whole matrix identity. All finite auxiliary transfer denominators are \([r]!\) with \(r<j\le N\), nonzero at this root, so its matrix entries are Laurent regular in the independent target roots. Specialization proves (D18) on equal and opposite objects with every confluent coefficient retained. Rigid duality and the braid carriers transport the same central polynomial; the Casimir is fixed by the antipode. This keeps the prescribed encircling direction and framing. No auxiliary dimension division, extra carrier scalar, or modified main-cut factor is part of (D18). Finally \(\|U_{j-1}(z/2)\|_{[-2,2]}\le j\le N\), and Markov bounds its derivative by \(CN^3\). Combining (D13), (D16)--(D18), and (D10), the actual fixed-power decorated coupon, written \(R_s^\epsilon L_j\) in its specified frame, has polynomial canonical norm, uniformly in \(j\). The original \(\epsilon\in\{0,\pm1\}\) is allowed; the same argument allows any fixed composable integral crossing power. ### 1.4. Every typed turn gives the same coefficient estimate Put \[ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_n(s)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}\left(1-\frac{\sin^2(s\theta)}{\sin^2(r\theta)}\right), \quad \mathcal R e_n=e_{d-n},\quad \mathcal D_s e_n=W_n(s)e_n. \tag{D20} \] Removable values at zero are understood. The exact physical turn in fixed polynomial coordinates is \(\gamma_N(s)H_N(s)^{-1}\mathcal R\mathcal D_s\), with the following domains. Mixed morphisms are expressed in (D16)'s reference. | Input | Output | \(\gamma_N(s)\) | | --- | --- | --- | | \(\operatorname{End}(++)\) | \(\operatorname{Hom}(-+,+-)\) | \(q^{-s^2/2}\) | | \(\operatorname{Hom}(-+,+-)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(--)\) | \(q^{s^2/2}\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(--)\) | \(\operatorname{Hom}(+-,-+)\) | \(q^{s^2/2}\) | | \(\operatorname{Hom}(+-,-+)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(++)\) | \(q^{-s^2/2}\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(+-)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(-+)\) | \(1\) | | \(\operatorname{End}(-+)\) | \(\operatorname{End}(+-)\) | \(1\) | The source proof in the turn theorem uses actual currying, with \(J_xw_a=(-x)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}\varphi_{d-a}\), followed by the carrier. Thus the table retains the duality ratios, cup scalar, and order-change monodromy. It is not obtained by replacing all six spaces by one untyped algebra. The remaining scope The separation condition is essential to this proof's recursive invariant. A general adjacent bare hub receives an A module whose low coefficient profile is not \(g+c\); a small spectral remainder also need not retain the full saving required by the next bare hub. Nothing above resets that module for free. Conversely, every bare hub in the stated class is fed only L modules, so this missing step is never used. For this same separated-junction class, the [auxiliary-color gap theorem](actual_main_meridian_auxiliary_color_gap.md) additionally proves a strict exponential loss below the rate \(F_0\) whenever at least one original color satisfies \(j_i\le(1-\delta)N\). It retains every other color, both parities, and the actual half-twist and cut factors. Its parameter disks satisfy \(R<1/2\), whereas (T31)'s upper bound holds for \(R<1\). Both results concern the unsummed auxiliary-colored source at the complete augmented action. They do not supply a cancellation-preserving filling contour, a lower bound for a filled invariant, or a bound at the generally smaller filled-knot volume. They also do not prove convergence of the ordinary-color-subtracted microscopic meridian profile. Those conclusions require additional control of the signed filling transform or normalized profile. The subsequent [component theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md) provides the intermediate-profile estimate under an explicit condition on paths through adjacent bare junctions. The [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) combines that estimate with a joint Fourier calculation and the original marked filling geometry. For the resulting class it proves a pointwise normalized profile and a uniform knot-complement volume limit on every \(|s|\le R<1\). These conclusions use those additional arguments, not just the supremum in (T33). ## 5. Finite reproduction The portable [reproduction script](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_source_bounds.py) compares the trace formula with direct polynomial division in exact cyclotomic fields. It separately checks the interval-tail inequality by integer convolutions and the first-slack map by enumerating positive paths. The [saved results](../experiments/main_meridian_source_bounds_results.json) record 131 exact trace identities, 911 interval-tail inequalities, 148 mapped positive paths, and 255 adjacent-factorial ratio checks at 80-digit precision. The factorial checks are numerical; the trace and combinatorial checks are exact. From the repository root, with SymPy and mpmath installed, run ```sh python3 experiments/audit_main_meridian_source_bounds.py --output /tmp/main_meridian_source_bounds_results.json ``` These finite checks test the identities and boundary conventions used by the proof. The uniform estimates, the terminating source induction, and the geometric identification are proved in the sections above; they are not inferred from the checked levels.

title: Controlling meridian deformations in trivalent Conway regions
status: Simultaneous boundary comparison for arbitrary trivalent product regions
text: # Controlling meridian deformations in trivalent Conway regions This special-case argument is retained in full. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) and [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) now permit every fixed strict bare component, without an additional valence or path condition. 1 November 2026. A Conway construction joins two-string tangles by ordered products and physical quarter-turns. Consecutive products with no intervening turn can be collected into a single product junction. A junction is **bare** if it contains no original crossing-circle operator. A connected bare region can have many such junctions. This note proves a uniform source estimate when each junction in that region is **trivalent**, meaning that exactly three branches meet there, including branches attached to the rest of the construction. The valence is measured in the reduced tree of actual operations. A junction with four or more branches cannot be made eligible by drawing it as several binary products: the new edges would have no physical quarter-turn. That distinction is used in the proof. The number of trivalent junctions is otherwise unrestricted, provided the whole construction is fixed before the level tends to infinity. Moving the main meridian changes the polynomial relation used by the quantum calculation. A product that was zero in the complete quotient can acquire an additional term. We will call these **additional trace terms**; in a finite expansion one chooses either the complete term or an additional term at each junction. Such a choice is a *sector*. The theorem controls every sector with at least one additional term by the same original complete geometric action, with a strict loss. It retains all labels on internal edges. In particular an internal maximizing label is allowed to equal or exceed one half. ## The component estimate Set \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and let \(s\) be the microscopic main-meridian parameter, so the marked meridian is \(M=q^s\). The fixed complete Newton polynomials and the moving quotient are \[ \begin{gathered} c_j=2\cos\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{N},\qquad S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin\frac{\pi a}{N},\quad S_0=1,\\ e_r(z)=\frac{\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z)}{S_r^2},\qquad P_s(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2\cos(2\pi s)=P_0(z)+\Delta_s,\\ \mathcal T_N(2\cos t)=2\cos Nt,\qquad \Delta_s=2\cos(2\pi s)-2,\\ \phi_s(F)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_s}F. \end{gathered} \tag{T1} \] Here \(\operatorname{rem}\) is the polynomial remainder of degree less than \(N\). The [typed polynomial compiler](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md) places equal-color operators in this moving quotient and opposite-color operators in the constant quotient \(P_0\). Its orientation types, circle pivots and physical turn scalars remain fixed throughout the argument. Polynomial identities retain the first derivatives at repeated spectral nodes as well as the nodal values; these derivatives are the first Hermite normal coordinates of the invariant. A boundary operator has an independent coefficient array \(F_i=\sum_r f_{i,N,r}e_r\). Put \(M_N=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), and call \(r\le M_N\) low and \(r>M_N\) high. Assume, uniformly in all specified physical colors and on every fixed \(|s|\le R<1\), \[ |f_{i,N,r}(s)|\le e^{N(c_i+\epsilon_N)} \begin{cases} e^{Ng(r/N)},&r\le M_N,\\ 1,&r>M_N, \end{cases} \qquad \epsilon_N\longrightarrow0, \tag{T2} \] where \(g\) is defined in (1), and the real constant \(c_i\) records the action already accumulated in that boundary branch. These are bounds on the entire coefficient array; no physical alias decomposition is assumed for an effective branch. View the region as an unturned expression \(A\) with one output, and let \(Q=T(A)\). Replace its boundary profiles by the pure complete profiles \(g+c_i\), and close it against the usual pure comparison leaf. The resulting strict positive source has action \[ \Omega_Q=\Phi_{C(hA^0)}+\sum_i c_i. \tag{T3} \] The comparison leaf specifies a scalar inequality; it is not an extra crossing circle in the knot. The [intrinsic-probe geometry](actual_conway_unflagged_probe_geometry.md), Sections 1–4, identifies (T3) with the pressure assigned to this same original branch. **Theorem.** Suppose every junction of the region has full valence three, every internal edge is an original physical quarter-turn, and the pure complete comparison has its original strict state. Then, for some fixed \(\delta>0\), its actual canonical output obeys \[ \|Q_{N,s}\|_{\mathcal J} \le e^{N(\Omega_Q+o(1))}. \tag{T4} \] The norm \(\mathcal J\) includes values and first derivatives at the complete double nodes, and the value at the odd simple node. The terms with at least one additional trace term, or with a high boundary input or high output probe, have norm at most \[ e^{N(\Omega_Q-\delta+o(1))}. \tag{T5} \] The remaining part has low boundary inputs and low output, but keeps every complete-supported internal label. It is bounded coefficientwise by a subexponential multiple of the same complete positive reference. The estimates hold at both parities and on every fixed disk \(R<1\); the geometric loss can be chosen independently of that radius. All constants may depend on the fixed region. An inherited loss in one full boundary coefficient array decreases the entire estimate by that same loss. The exact turned coefficient and its norm comparison make the output probe concrete. Let \(w_{N,r}=e_r(-2)\) for low \(r\), and \(w_{N,r}=1\) for high \(r\). In the actual output type, \[ \begin{gathered} [e_r]T_\gamma(A)=\frac{\gamma_N(s)W_{d-r}(s)}{H_N(s)}\, \phi_\sigma(e_rA),\\ H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad W_r(s)=\prod_{a=1}^{r} \left(1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi s/N)}{\sin^2(\pi a/N)}\right),\\ \|T_\gamma(A)\|_{\mathcal J} \le C_RN^C\sum_{r=0}^{d}w_{N,r}|\phi_\sigma(e_rA)|. \end{gathered} \tag{T6} \] The parameter \(\sigma\) is \(s,-s\) or zero according to the actual orientation type. The prescribed scalar \(\gamma_N(s)\) is \(1\) or \(q^{\pm s^2/2}\). The [turn theorem](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) proves uniform boundedness of the paired ratios on \(R<1\); the [full-node Newton estimate](actual_conway_root_star_full_jet_localization.md), Sections 2–3, proves the polynomial norm conversion. The sum in (T6) has the same low profile \(g\) and high profile zero as another boundary input. Thus the component theorem treats that probe with its complete finite support and all first normal coordinates. Sections 1–3 prove a simultaneous boundary inequality for the complete positive action. Sections 4–5 use it to replace all additional terms by a feasible boundary state of the same coupled complete source. Section 6 passes from actions to the finite source. Appendix A derives the exact finite tensor, including its signs, support and uniform endpoint bounds. ## 1. The complete cubic action and a constrained region Let \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x),\quad 0\le x\le\tfrac12. \tag{1} \] The complete symmetric cubic action is \[ t(x,y,z)=J(x+y)+J(x+z)+J(y+z) -J(x)-J(y)-J(z)-J(x+y+z-1), \tag{2} \] on the closed domain \[ x,y,z\ge0,\qquad x+y,\ x+z,\ y+z\le1, \qquad x+y+z\ge1. \tag{3} \] Its strict domain has all three labels positive, all pair sums less than one, and total greater than one. Writing its third covariant label as \(z=1-b\) identifies (2) with the original product action \(m(x,y,b)\). Thus it is concave, continuous on (3), and has negative definite Hessian in the strict domain, by the [three-tetrahedron decomposition](actual_conway_general_core_packet_and_gap.md), Sections 1 and 3. Here and below, an action is the limiting logarithm of a coefficient divided by the level. The explicit sine-factorial formulas determine these limits. Consider a finite connected tree of complete trivalent vertices. Its external incidences have two kinds. An ordinary incidence carries the profile \(g(a)\) with freely varying \(a\in[0,1/2]\); additive constants may be retained separately. A marked incidence has a prescribed label \(z_i\) and no boundary action. Each vertex has at most one marked incidence. Internal edges identify equal covariant labels. Let \(\Psi(z_1,\ldots,z_r)\) be the maximum of the sum of all complete cubic actions and all ordinary profiles. Its domain is the projection of the closed linear support polytope, hence convex. The maximization is over a compact polytope. Concavity of the summands implies joint concavity of \(\Psi\) on its finite domain. The case \(r=0\) is just an ordinary complete region; no clamping is required. **Half-boundary lemma.** If \(r\ge1\), the point \(\mathbf z=\tfrac12\mathbf1\) has a unique strict constrained optimizer. The pressure is analytic near that point and \[ \frac{\partial\Psi}{\partial z_i} (\tfrac12\mathbf1)\le0\quad(1\le i\le r). \tag{4} \] Consequently, for every feasible \(\mathbf z\) with \(z_i\ge1/2\), \[ \Psi(\mathbf z)\le\Psi(\tfrac12\mathbf1). \tag{5} \] This is a simultaneous assertion. It does not assert coordinatewise monotonicity while other marked labels are held above one half. ## 2. Strict feasibility and the boundary barrier Set every marked label to \(1/2\), every internal label to \(3/8\), and every ordinary boundary label to \(3/8\). A vertex without a marked incidence has triple \((3/8,3/8,3/8)\): its total is \(9/8\) and its pair sums are \(3/4\). A marked vertex has triple \((1/2,3/8,3/8)\): its total is \(5/4\) and its largest pair sum is \(7/8\). Both are strict. Ordinary leaf profiles are strict. This assignment remains feasible and strict when the marked labels vary in a small open box around \(1/2\). Root the region at one marked incidence. Each complete vertex is now an ordinary binary product with output equal to one minus its outgoing covariant label; each internal edge supplies the physical turn between these output and input coordinates. Other marked incidences are fixed primitive terminals with label \(1/2\), and have no leaf volume atom. Ordinary terminals have the original leaf action \(g\). The [boundary barrier](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md), Section 2, applies with this one change in the list of terminals. Join any boundary state to the strict state just constructed. A tetrahedron with angles \((0,a,1-a)\), \(0<a<1\), has directional derivative \(+\infty\) along this segment. A vertex-flat tetrahedron \((0,0,1)\) has a finite derivative; a positive tetrahedron has a finite derivative. Thus none can cancel a nonvertex-flat infinite derivative with a negative infinite term. No variable wire at a maximum can equal zero or one. An output zero forces both product inputs zero. An output one either has two interior inputs summing to one, which gives a nonvertex-flat atom, or it has an endpoint child and the descent continues. Turns exchange zero and one. A finite descent cannot terminate at a marked terminal, because that terminal is fixed to \(1/2\). It must reach an ordinary leaf at zero, with its nonvertex-flat leaf atom, or an interior pair summing to one. The distinguished root output is fixed to \(1/2\) and cannot be the endpoint causing the descent. This excludes all variable endpoint wires. An ordinary leaf at \(1/2\) has its own nonvertex-flat atom and is also excluded. No atom is assigned to a fixed marked terminal; its prescribed half value is not being varied. With every variable wire interior, each saturated gate inequality gives the same barrier as in the original strict source. In product coordinates put \(p=b-x,q=b-y,r=x+y-b,w=1-x-y\). If \(w=0\), the first tetrahedron has angles \((y,x,0)\). If \(r=0\), the third has \((b,0,1-b)\). If \(p=0,q>0\), the second has \((0,q,1-q)\); the case \(q=0,p>0\) is symmetric. If \(p=q=0\), the third has \((0,x,1-x)\). All are nonvertex-flat because the relevant wires are interior. Hence every retained gate at the constrained maximum is strict. Each strict gate Hessian is negative definite in its three labels. Every free variable occurs at a gate. Thus their sum, together with the concave leaf Hessians, is negative definite on the constrained free-coordinate space. The maximum is unique. The implicit-function theorem gives an analytic critical branch under small independent variations of the marked labels; compactness and uniqueness show that it remains the maximum. This proves the asserted interiority and analyticity at the all-half assignment. It uses the existing tetrahedron barrier, not a claimed metric completion for an artificial terminal. ## 3. Boundary derivatives from the actual product equations At a stationary subtree with output coordinate \(b\), write \[ B=\cot\pi b,\qquad \kappa=e^{-f'(b)},\qquad X^2=\frac{1+B^2}{1+\kappa},\qquad Y^2=\kappa X^2. \tag{6} \] At an ordinary leaf \(f=g\), these variables satisfy \(B=X>0,Y=1\). At a fixed marked half terminal there is no intrinsic profile derivative. Instead use its incident strict prism to define its positive boundary response: in an input coordinate take \(\kappa=e^{m_x}\), or the prescribed reciprocal after a turn. Since the terminal has \(B=0\), every such positive response gives \[ -Y<0<X. \tag{7} \] This is all that is needed from that terminal. It is not an added physical leaf and carries no leaf action. At internal variable wires the usual stationarity equations identify the child response with the reciprocal prism response. The [product derivative identities](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md), Section 1, obtained by direct differentiation of the unchanged action, give a common positive \(X\) at a product, and, if \(B_1,B_2\) are its input cotangents, \[ B=\frac{B_1B_2+X^2-1}{B_1+B_2},\qquad Y=\frac{Y_1Y_2}{B_1+B_2},\qquad B_1+B_2>0. \tag{8} \] A turn takes \((B,X,Y)\) to \((-B,Y,X)\). In the rooted region an ordinary boundary is an input directly, with \(B=X,Y=1\); a fixed half terminal is a proper input by (7). Every product of these ordinary or proper inputs has a proper output \(-Y<B<X\). Only such completed product outputs are followed by internal physical turns, which preserve the proper condition. No turn of an uncompleted ordinary leaf is invoked. Indeed, rooting a covariant cubic at its outgoing incidence makes the output coordinate one minus that incidence, and each original physical-turn edge supplies exactly the subsequent complement before the next product. Thus this rooted induction is literal for the stated edge convention. Here is the relevant product verification. The inputs obey \(-Y_i<B_i\le X\). If \(X\ge1\), then each \(B_i>0\) and \(B_i\ge\sqrt{X^2-1}\), with strict inequality for a proper input. Formula (8) gives \(B>0\), and \[ B-X=\frac{(X-B_1)(X-B_2)-1}{B_1+B_2}<0. \tag{9} \] If an input is an ordinary leaf its first factor is zero; otherwise each factor is less than \(X-\sqrt{X^2-1}\le1\). Thus the strict inequality holds, including \(X=1\). If \(0<X<1\), put \(h=\sqrt{1-X^2}\) and write \(B_i=h\cot\alpha_i,Y_i=h\csc\alpha_i\), with \(0<\alpha_i<\pi\). The upper input bound gives \(\alpha_i\ge\arccos X>0\), and \(B_1+B_2>0\) gives \(\alpha_1+\alpha_2<\pi\). Equation (8) becomes \(B=h\cot(\alpha_1+\alpha_2),Y=h\csc(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)\), proving \(-Y<B<X\). Turns exchange the two strict inequalities. This proves the needed bound \(B_i\le X\) at every input. Now root the region separately at marked boundary \(i\), still with all marked labels equal to half. Its last product has output \(b=1-z_i=1/2\), so \(B=0\). Strict support makes its two input labels less than \(1/2\), hence \(B_1,B_2>0\). From (8) and the hyperboloid identity, \[ 1-X^2=Y^2=B_1B_2\le X^2. \tag{10} \] The envelope derivative in this root output is therefore \[ f'_{\mathrm{out}}(1/2)=\log(X^2/Y^2)\ge0, \qquad \partial_{z_i}\Psi(\tfrac12\mathbf1)=-f'_{\mathrm{out}}(1/2)\le0. \tag{11} \] The fixed marked terminals elsewhere were used only through (7), so the argument works for every \(i\) on the same constrained maximum. Joint concavity and the supporting plane at the all-half point now give \[ \Psi(\mathbf z)\le\Psi(\tfrac12\mathbf1) +\sum_i\partial_{z_i}\Psi(\tfrac12\mathbf1)(z_i-1/2) \le\Psi(\tfrac12\mathbf1). \tag{12} \] This proves the half-boundary lemma, including arbitrary feasible boundary points by continuity of the supporting inequality. ## 4. Where the additional trace terms can occur The fixed Newton basis and the normalized trace were defined above. At completeness the three-input tensor is supported on \(i+j,i+k,j+k\le d\) and \(i+j+k\ge d\). Its logarithmic rate is (2). The exact polynomial calculation in Appendix A proves that the difference from this complete tensor has support \[ i+j,\ i+k,\ j+k\ge N,\qquad i+j+k\ge2N-1. \tag{13} \] Writing \(t_0=i+j+k-(2N-1)\), it is exactly \[ V_{\mathrm{ret}}(i,j,k) =-\Delta_s(-1)^{i+j+k-d} \frac{N^2}{S_iS_jS_kS_{t_0}S_{i-t_0}S_{j-t_0}S_{k-t_0}}. \tag{14} \] For the finite-to-continuous rate comparison use \(d=N-1\) and complementary variables \(a=1-i/d,b=1-j/d,c=1-k/d\). The exact additional support then gives \(a,b,c\ge0\) and \(a+b+c\le1-1/d\), so every argument below lies in the real domain of \(J\). Its absolute closed rate is \[ \mathcal R(a,b,c) =J(a)+J(b)+J(c)+J(a+b+c) -J(a+b)-J(a+c)-J(b+c) =-\pi^2\int_0^a\int_0^b\int_0^c \csc^2\pi(u+v+w)\,dw\,dv\,du\le0. \tag{15} \] To justify the integral, first translate the arguments of \(J\) by a small positive number and keep \(a+b+c<1\). Three applications of the fundamental theorem of calculus give the finite difference in (15), since \(J^{(3)}(u)=-\pi^2\csc^2(\pi u)\). Passing to the limit is legitimate at the origin, and at the opposite corner when the total is one: the inverse-square singularity is integrable in three dimensions. Continuity gives the result on the closed domain. In particular it is strictly negative when all three complementary labels are positive, but only nonpositivity is used in the whole-component comparison. Replacing the factorial arguments divided by \(N\) by these \(d\)-normalized arguments changes each by \(O(1/N)\). The endpoint modulus of continuity of \(J\) is \(O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))\); hence uniform closed factorial rates still have only \(O(\log N)\) error in the logarithm. In particular, no finite tuple with complementary sum \(1+1/N\) is substituted into (15). The exact coefficient itself is uniformly polynomially bounded after its displayed common \(\Delta_s\) factor. This retains every endpoint and repeated-root normal. In the [actual six-type table](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md#the-six-ordered-orientation-types) an equal-color endomorphism turns into an opposite-order mixed morphism, and the next turn into the other equal-color endomorphism; the two opposite-color endomorphism spaces turn into one another. Only the equal-color endomorphism classes have moving relations. Thus two moving vertices cannot be joined by an original physical turn. Compatible products share their Casimir class. Vertices carrying an additional term must be moving, and consequently form an independent set in the original reduced trivalent tree. A vertex carrying an additional term has at least two high incidences, where high means the exact index exceeds \(M_N=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). A complete vertex has at most one. In a closed limiting sector, retain which incidences were high before taking the limit; those recorded labels may become exactly half. An additional term with two recorded high arms has one remaining low arm; an additional term with three has none. This convention prevents false counts at tied endpoints. ## 5. Replacing the additional terms simultaneously Consider one trivalent component after its output has been closed against the comparison probe with effective boundary profiles \(g+c_i\) on low indices and \(c_i\) on high indices. Its complete positive comparison replaces all boundaries by their pure profiles \(g+c_i\). Assume the original strict-source hypotheses, so that this complete reference has a compact support polytope, a unique strict maximizing state, and action \(F_0\). For an open component closed by the probe, this \(F_0\) is precisely \(\Omega_Q\) in (T3). The output probe is one of these effective boundary profiles when bounding an open component. Fix a sector containing at least one additional term, including its recorded high/low pattern. Remove every vertex carrying an additional term. Since vertices carrying additional terms are nonadjacent, every remaining edge from an additional term ends either at a complete region or directly at an original boundary leaf. Mark each high incidence on a complete region, including any high original external boundary. There is at most one such marked incidence at each complete vertex, by complete support. A low arm of an additional term requires special accounting. After its two high arms are clamped to half, the replacement complete vertex has action \[ t(1/2,1/2,x)=g(x)\ge0. \tag{16} \] For the identity in (16), the left side reduces to \(2J(1/2+x)-2J(x)\). Its derivative is \(2\log\cot(\pi x)=g'(x)\), and both functions vanish at zero. Continuity includes both endpoints. If that low arm ends in a complete region, regard this additional \(g(x)\) as an ordinary boundary profile of that region and optimize \(x\) there. At the starting sector state this adds a nonnegative amount, whereas the discarded additional-term action is nonpositive. Because vertices carrying additional terms are nonadjacent, the low arm belongs to exactly one complete region and this \(g\) is counted exactly once. If a low arm ends directly in an original low boundary leaf, retain its original label or optimize it independently. The new complete vertex and original boundary contribute \(g(x)+g(x)+c\), at least the complete boundary contribution \(g(x)+c\). A high original boundary incidence is replaced by half; its original high profile is \(c\), and the new pure boundary profile is \(g(1/2)+c=c\). An additional term with three high arms becomes \((1/2,1/2,1/2)\), whose complete action is zero. No boundary constant is lost. Apply the half-boundary lemma to each complete region, including the new pure low-arm profiles just described. It jointly reoptimizes that region at all its marked half boundaries, with action at least its previous complete action plus the assigned nonnegative profiles. Regions without any marked boundary can simply be optimized with their ordinary profiles. Distinct regions have disjoint free variables. Their low-arm values are determined by their own optimizers; each is used by exactly one replaced vertex carrying an additional term. All high interfaces agree at half. Reassemble the unchanged tree. At every replaced vertex carrying an additional term use either \((1/2,1/2,x)\) with the optimized adjacent low-arm value, or \((1/2,1/2,1/2)\). These are feasible complete triples. Equation (16) makes their action exactly the profile assigned to the adjacent complete region, not an extra copy. Every remaining vertex is a complete feasible vertex, and each original boundary now has a feasible pure label. The total action of the resulting complete state is at least the action of the entire original sector after absolute values have been taken. At least one replaced vertex has a pair sum equal to one. The resulting state therefore lies in the fixed complete boundary stratum \[ \mathcal B=\{\text{complete feasible states with at least one retained cubic pair sum equal to }1\}. \tag{17} \] The original maximizing state is strict. Compactness gives \[ \delta=F_0-\max_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A_0>0. \tag{18} \] Thus every sector containing an additional term has absolute action at most \(F_0-\delta\). This uses a feasible comparison state in the same coupled complete source. It does not add separately optimized caps or assign a representation to a stationary point of the absolute additional-term action. All endpoint and exact-half configurations are included. The record of finite high incidences gives at most one marked incidence per complete vertex and at least two per vertex carrying an additional term; it persists in the closed sector. The entropy functions are continuous on their closed domains. Equation (12) applies to closed feasible boundary values, so no limiting division by a zero sine or a strict-label counting shortcut is needed. ## 6. Consequence for the finite source and the remaining scope At a fixed finite trivalent component there are finitely many choices between complete and additional terms and polynomially many integer states. The paired edge factors and all prescribed typed scalars are bounded on \(|s|\le R<1\). Uniform closed coefficient rates and (18) therefore bound the entire absolute sum of all nonempty additional-term sectors by \[ e^{N(F_0-\delta+o(1))}. \tag{19} \] No cancellation between additional terms is used for this estimate. In sectors with no additional term, the bounded paired weights are compared termwise with the original positive complete contraction. A high original boundary input or high output probe has the complete-component strict gap. This is the [complete coefficient-probe theorem](actual_conway_unflagged_core_probe_bound.md); it permits low rates \(g+c\) and high rates \(c\). Thus the component has its original full norm budget, and its clean part retains all complete-supported internal labels while keeping its boundary inputs and output low. The remainder has a strict spectral deficit. Inherited full-cone deficits pass by affine homogeneity in the constants, as in the [grouped-error argument](actual_main_meridian_component_extension.md), Section 6. The [global trivalent extension](actual_main_meridian_trivalent_filled_volume.md) proves the remaining source-to-window and filling interfaces. Near the original strict maximizing state, every cubic has total normalized degree less than \(3/2\). Consequently its raw polynomial trace has degree less than \(2N-1\) on a fixed window, and the moving trace equals the complete trace exactly there. The internal labels in this regular neighborhood may cross half, but stay in a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\), where the canonical paired-edge interpolation is regular. Circle-incident labels remain in the original regular low interval. These are the local inputs for the grouped-window argument; no high cutoff is imposed on bare–bare edges. The theorem established here is a component comparison for arbitrary-size **trivalent** bare components in the actual typed tree. It is independent of the earlier many-boundary condition. It can coexist with singleton higher-valence components and other already controlled components in the mutual source induction. The [global theorem](actual_main_meridian_trivalent_filled_volume.md) supplies the additional conditioned window, joint filling contour and marked scalar arguments required for the volume and meridian-profile conclusions. Those conclusions do not follow from the component norm bound alone. Higher-valence bare components are not settled by this proof. Their binary resolutions have unturned complementary-label edges, on which adjacent moving vertices carrying an additional term can occur. A raw low higher-valence product can also have an additional trace term without a high exterior incidence. The nonadjacency and unique-low-arm accounting above must not be applied to such artificial resolutions. ## Appendix A. The exact additional tensor and its endpoint bounds The finite calculation below justifies the tensor used in Section 4 before any exponential estimate is taken. It takes place in fixed polynomial coordinates, so it includes the full repeated-root information. ### A.1. The polynomial quotient producing the additional term Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\quad S_n=\prod_{r=1}^n2\sin(r\theta),\quad S_0=1. \] Put \[ B_n(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(c_j-z),\qquad e_n=B_n/S_n^2, \qquad P_0(z)=\mathcal T_N(z)+2. \] Here \(\mathcal T_N(2\cos t)=2\cos Nt\). The actual same-color quotient at meridian displacement \(s\) has relation \[ P_s=P_0+\Delta_s,\qquad \Delta_s=2\cos(2\pi s)-2. \tag{A1} \] The coefficients below are in the fixed basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\), not in the moving basis. All equalities are polynomial quotient equalities and therefore retain every repeated-node normal. For canonical polynomials \(f,g\), one division gives \[ fg=P_0Q+R,\qquad \deg R<N,\quad\deg Q\le N-2, \qquad f*_sg=R-\Delta_sQ. \tag{A2} \] Thus the change of multiplication is affine in \(\Delta_s\). When \(i+j<N\), the product \(e_ie_j\) has degree less than \(N\), and its fixed-basis coefficients are exactly the positive complete coefficients. When \(i+j\ge N\), the complete product is divisible by \(P_0\). Indeed \(c_{d-j}=c_j\), so \[ B_iB_{N-i}=B_N=(-1)^NP_0. \] Assume \(i\ge j\) and set \[ a=N-i,\quad b=N-j,\quad h=i+j-N=N-a-b\ge0. \] Then \(j\ge a\), and the quotient producing the additional term is the ordinary polynomial \[ Q_{ij}=\frac{e_ie_j}{P_0} =\frac{(-1)^N}{S_i^2S_j^2} \prod_{r=a}^{j-1}(c_r-z). \tag{A3} \] Its degree is \(h\le N-2\). Consequently \[ e_i*_se_j=-\Delta_sQ_{ij}. \tag{A4} \] This exact divisibility is special to the complete fixed basis. It is different from the nonzero first derivative of multiplication coefficients in moving coordinates. ### A.2. An exact alternating Newton expansion The quotient in (A3) has the expansion \[ \boxed{\quad Q_{ij}=\sum_{k=0}^{h}(-1)^{N+h-k}\Lambda_{ijk}e_k, \qquad \Lambda_{ijk}= \frac{S_hS_k} {S_iS_jS_{h-k}S_{a+k}S_{b+k}}>0. \quad} \tag{A5} \] Every factorial in (A5) has index between zero and \(d\). Here is a direct derivation from the [finite factorial connection](actual_main_meridian_newton_compiler.md), Sections 2–3. The interval polynomial in (A3) is \(B_h(-a,z)\), since shifting the meridian parameter by \(-a\) changes \(c_r\) into \(c_{r+a}\). In the finite connection, take \(p=q^2\), initial parameter \(q p^a\), and target parameter \(q\). If \(m=h-k\), cancellation gives \[ B_h(-a,z)=S_h^2\sum_{k=0}^h C_{hk}e_k, \qquad C_{hk}=(-1)^m \frac{S_kS_jS_{j-k-1}} {S_hS_mS_{a+k}S_{a-1}}. \tag{A6} \] For completeness, the two finite Pochhammer products have indices \(a+k+1,\ldots,a+h\) and \(a,\ldots,a+m-1\). Each factor \(1-q^{2r}=-iq^r(2\sin r\theta)\). Their combined phase is \((-1)^m q^{m(2a+h)}\). The connection prefactor and the Gaussian binomial have inverse phase \(q^{-m(2a+h)}\), leaving precisely \((-1)^m\). This argument includes \(m=0\) by empty products. Use \[ S_iS_{a-1}=N,\qquad S_{j-k-1}S_{b+k}=N. \] Substitution of (A6) into (A3) gives (A5), including its sign and normalization. The finite connection is a polynomial identity; no division by a sampled Casimir difference is used. The complete turn reverses the fixed basis, so \[ T_0Q_{ij}=\sum_{k=0}^{h}(-1)^{N+h-k}\Lambda_{ijk}e_{d-k}. \tag{A7} \] The [actual fixed-frame typed turn](actual_main_meridian_turn_comparison.md) multiplies each displayed term by its retained Gaussian scalar and \(W_k(s)/H_N(s)\). These factors and their inverses are uniformly bounded on every fixed \(|s|\le R<1\). The alternating sum in (A7) remains present. ### A.3. Uniform polynomial size, including all endpoints The individual positive numbers in (A5) obey \[ \Lambda_{ijk}\le C N^2 \tag{A8} \] for one absolute constant, every level, and every admissible \(i,j,k\). First, \[ \Lambda_{ij0}= \frac1{N^2(2\sin a\theta)(2\sin b\theta)}\le\frac1{16}. \tag{A9} \] For \(1\le k\le h\), the exact consecutive ratio is \[ \frac{\Lambda_{ijk}}{\Lambda_{ij,k-1}} =\frac{\sin(k\theta)\sin((a+b+k-1)\theta)} {\sin((a+k)\theta)\sin((b+k)\theta)}. \tag{A10} \] The elementary identity \[ \sin((a+k)\theta)\sin((b+k)\theta) -\sin(k\theta)\sin((a+b+k)\theta) =\sin(a\theta)\sin(b\theta)>0 \tag{A11} \] therefore implies, when \(k<h\), \[ \Lambda_{ijk} \le\Lambda_{ij0} \frac{\sin((a+b)\theta)}{\sin((a+b+k)\theta)} \le\frac N{32}. \tag{A12} \] The first inequality follows by multiplying (A10) and telescoping the one-step sine shifts. At the final index, if \(h\ge1\), retain its last ratio separately: \[ \Lambda_{ijh} \le\Lambda_{ij0} \frac{\sin^2((a+b)\theta)}{\sin(a\theta)\sin(b\theta)} \le\frac{N^2}{64}. \tag{A13} \] The case \(h=0\) is (A9). We used only \(\sin(r\theta)\ge\sin\theta\ge2/N\) for \(1\le r<N\). Thus no endpoint can conceal an exponential factor. This bounds the coefficients of the additional quotient in fixed coordinates. It is not a bound for the positive Newton coefficient norm after all later operations: the basis element \(e_{d-k}\) itself can have exponential spectral size, and the alternating signs in (A7) can matter. ### A.4. The symmetric three-input tensor Let the fixed closing functional be \[ \begin{aligned} \phi_s(F)&=(-1)^dN^2\operatorname{coeff}_{z^d}F. \end{aligned}\tag{A14} \] for the canonical representative modulo \(P_s\). At every \(s\), \[ \phi_s(e_i*_se_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}. \tag{A15} \] For \(i+j<d\), this follows from degree. At \(i+j=d\), it uses \(S_iS_j=N\). At \(i+j\ge N\), that quotient has degree at most \(N-2\), so its top coefficient is zero. Thus the Frobenius metric is the same anti-diagonal matrix in these fixed coordinates. Define the covariant, symmetric vertex tensor \[ V_s(i,j,r)=\phi_s(e_i*_se_j*_se_r). \tag{A16} \] Its complete part is supported on \[ i+j,\ i+r,\ j+r\le d,\qquad i+j+r\ge d, \] and there the [positive Newton multiplication formula](actual_main_meridian_newton_multiplication.md), Section 3, gives \[ V_0(i,j,r)= \frac{S_{i+j}S_{i+r}S_{j+r}} {N S_iS_jS_r S_{i+j+r-d}}. \tag{A17} \] The only additional support is \[ i+j,\ i+r,\ j+r\ge N,\qquad i+j+r\ge2N-1. \tag{A18} \] On (A18), \[ \boxed{\quad V_s(i,j,r) =-\Delta_s(-1)^{i+j+r-d} \frac{S_{i+j-N}S_{i+r-N}S_{j+r-N}} {N S_iS_jS_r S_{i+j+r-2N+1}}. \quad} \tag{A19} \] Elsewhere it is zero. To prove (A19), use (A5) and the metric (A15): the sole coefficient selected is \(k=d-r\). The resulting expression is symmetric after the sine-product reflection. This also proves that the listed support is independent of which two inputs are multiplied first. Equivalently, writing \(t=i+j+r-(2N-1)\ge0\), the positive coefficient in (A19) is \[ \Lambda(i,j,r)= \frac{N^2} {S_iS_jS_r S_t S_{i-t}S_{j-t}S_{r-t}}. \tag{A20} \] This is the same number as (A5), with \(k=d-r\). It has the uniform bound (A8). There is an important convention for a network built from (A16). In this fully covariant tensor convention, an unturned composition contracts **complementary** incident labels, through the inverse metric (A15). Inserting the complete reversal changes this to **equal** incident labels. At a deformed typed turn there is an additional bounded diagonal paired factor. Thus the edges of a reduced-hub tree, which carry turns, join equal cubic labels. In the alternative raw product input/output convention, a turn reverses the output label; these statements are compatible but must not be interchanged in a flow argument. The complements of the three labels in (A18) have total at most \(d-1\). They satisfy the complete pair-sum inequalities but fail its required total at least \(d\). Thus complementing the labels does not turn the additional tensor into a complete positive tensor: the required total-degree condition fails. ## Reproducing the finite calculations Run the dedicated group from the repository root: ```sh python3 repro/run_research_checks.py trivalent-components ``` The [program](../experiments/audit_main_meridian_trivalent_components.py) constructs the original Newton polynomials over exact cyclotomic fields, divides their products by \(P_0+\Delta\), and extracts the closing trace. It then compares that independently obtained trace with the complete and additional tensor formulas. The [saved results](../experiments/trivalent_return_comparison_results.json) cover levels two through ten, including old supported triples with an internal index above one half and the smallest possible total degree in the additional support. The program also checks the unchanged pairing, the endpoint permutation of the six physical types, and the elementary algebra used in the boundary derivative. Python and SymPy are sufficient. These are finite algebraic checks. The simultaneous inequality, the strict exponential gap, and the passage to the filled volume are proved in the text and its companion theorem.

title: Meridian profiles and volume with arbitrary trivalent Conway regions
status: Uniform meridian volume and cusp profile with arbitrary trivalent regions
text: # Meridian profiles and volume with arbitrary trivalent Conway regions This special-case argument is retained in full. The [general component theorem](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md) and [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) now permit every fixed strict bare component, without an additional valence or path condition. 1 November 2026. This theorem allows arbitrarily large connected regions of trivalent products in the moving-meridian calculation for a Conway knot. The construction is fixed; its twist integers can be chosen independently, with either sign, once their absolute values exceed a fixed threshold. The resulting reduced ADO invariant has a nonzero microscopic meridian profile, and its exponential growth is the volume of the actual knot complement after the auxiliary circles have been filled. Begin with two-string tangles with four ordered endpoints. Their products are the prescribed stacking operations, their turns are physical quarter-turns, and their final closure is the prescribed cylindrical matching. Keep the original crossing circles, each bounding its twice-punctured crossing disk, and its retained half twist \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\). The main strands must form one knot component with no additional internal circle. Assume the [strict source condition](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md): there is an assignment of original leaf angles in \((0,1/2)\) for which every retained multiplication gate satisfies \[ \max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. \tag{V1} \] The forced final flat gate is removed with its exact complementary-index relation. For a strict two-leaf construction, retain the knot-producing parity pattern containing a pure leaf; the two-odd-leaf link pattern is excluded. Collect consecutive products with no intervening physical turn into a product junction. A junction containing an original crossing-circle operator is a circle vertex; an ordinary original leaf is a circle vertex of valence one. A junction without such an operator is bare. The reduced graph is a tree of source operations, with an actual quarter-turn along every edge. This description preserves the ordered tangle construction; it does not assert that arbitrary tangles commute. For every maximal connected component \(\mathcal U\) of bare junctions, assume at least one of the following: - \(\mathcal U\) consists of one junction, of any allowed valence; - every junction of \(\mathcal U\) is trivalent in the full reduced tree, counting branches attached outside \(\mathcal U\) as well as its internal edges; - \(\mathcal U\) satisfies the component path condition below. ![Two possible trivalent bare components, with all outside attachments included in the degree count.](../book/figures/trivalent-bare-components.svg) There is no size bound on the second type of component.
