(3) In particular (3) retains WHICH ordered meridian is sent to which; it is stronger than matching the target trace alone. ## 2. The physical rectangle determines its eigenratio For the certified complete geometry the actual primitive marking gives `b=-i/(2c)`, independently of the retained half-twist sign. Suppose first `0<c<=1`, and write c=sech eta, eta>=0, Tr T=-2cosh(2eta), J=-exp(-2eta)=exp(2pi i xi), xi=1/2+i eta/pi. (4) This specifies the target eigenflag. On the two T-eigenlines the conjugator D has eigenvalues J-alpha and J^-1-alpha. Its selected eigenratio is therefore R_target=(J-alpha)/(J^-1-alpha) =(1+i sinh eta)/(1-i sinh eta) =exp(2i atan(sinh eta)). (5) The opposite eigenflag inverts (5). Both (3) and the chosen expression in (5) extend through eta=0. In the normalization that gives eigenvalue one on the other flag, the parabolic limit is D_normalized=I+(i/2)(T+I) at eta=0. (6) This coefficient is a target transport parameter; it is not an independently introduced crossing-circle cusp shape. In particular there is no reason to assign it the orientation inequality of an original auxiliary cusp. ## 3. The actual scalar source fixes the generating derivative Let a_N/N->1/2 in the original folded range. The root-location theorem proves local uniform convergence of the actual canonical logarithms N^-1 Log p_(a_N)(z) -> Psi_(1/2)(z) on C minus [2,infinity). Define the scalar action along the actual target trace by F(eta)=Psi_(1/2)(-2cosh(2eta)). (7) For eta real and nonnegative, the positive finite-product proof gives F(eta)=max_(0<=v<=1/2) integral_0^v log[cos^2(pi s) *(cosh^2 eta-sin^2(pi s))/sin^4(pi s)] ds. Its unique maximum is `v=atan(cosh eta)/pi`, the actual rectangle parameter. Differentiation at the maximum gives an elementary exact formula. In c=sech eta coordinates, dF/dc=-2/c * integral_0^(atan(1/c)/pi) ds/(1-c^2 sin^2(pi s)) =-2 arccos c/(pi c sqrt(1-c^2)). Using `dc/deta=-c tanh eta` proves F'(eta)=2 atan(sinh eta)/pi. (8) The limit at eta=0 is zero. Its additive constant is fixed by the ACTUAL positive source evaluation at z=-2: F(0)=4 integral_0^(1/4) log cot(pi s) ds =4 Catalan/pi=v8/pi. (9) Thus no arbitrary period constant or logarithm winding was selected: F(eta)=v8/pi+(2/pi) integral_0^eta atan(sinh r) dr. (10) These formulas hold holomorphically on `|Im eta|<pi/2`, with the branch continued from eta=0. Indeed `-2cosh(2eta)` avoids [2,infinity) on that strip. The analytic arctangent in (8) is its continuation from zero; its derivative is `1/cosh eta`, with no pole inside the strip. The identity theorem extends the real calculation. One must not substitute a pointwise principal inverse trigonometric value after leaving the real axis. Because `xi=1/2+i eta/pi`, equation (8) is precisely partial_xi Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1) =-2i atan(sinh eta), exp[-partial_xi Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1)]=R_target. (11) The sign in (11) is the actual spectral-multiplier sign. Let Theta be the original fully normalized algebraic two-column generating phase. We use it here as the already proved classical character relation, not as a new asymptotic for a column at the complex target color. Its algebraic critical-character map says `exp(partial_xi Theta)=R_target`. Multiplication by the scalar source polynomial adds `Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1)` to that phase. Target-channel stationarity is therefore exp(partial_xi[Theta+Psi])=1, exactly (11). It is NOT `R_target=exp(partial_xi Psi)`. This calculation uses the original inverse turn (1), the physical ordered matrices (3), and the canonical scalar branch (7). ## 4. General input color gives the actual four-parabolic character relation The same comparison holds for EVERY fixed real INPUT parameter `0<alpha<=1/2`, not only the complete input alpha=1/2. Keep it distinct from the TARGET parameter `xi=1/2+i eta/pi`. Put lambda_input=2cos(2pi alpha), s=sin(pi alpha), z=J+J^-1=-2cosh(2eta), F_alpha(eta)=Psi_alpha(z). Here Psi_alpha is again the actual selected scalar limit proved by the finite polynomial root theorem. For eta>0 its positive variational formula has unique maximum satisfying sin^2(pi v_*)=s^2 cosh^2 eta/(s^2+cosh^2 eta). Differentiate its original integral at that maximum. With `t=tan(pi v)`, the integral of `1/(cosh^2 eta-sin^2(pi v))` is elementary. It gives partial_eta F_alpha =(2/pi) atan[s sinh eta/sqrt(1+(1-s^2)sinh^2 eta)] =(2/pi) asin(s tanh eta). (12) Both inverse functions in (12) are continued from zero; for positive real eta their values lie in `(0,pi alpha)`. For example the equivalence follows by squaring the tangent and using `1+sinh^2 eta=cosh^2 eta`. Thus the selected scalar multiplier gives the eigenratio R_alpha=exp[-partial_xi Psi_alpha(J+J^-1)] =exp[2i asin(s tanh eta)], R_alpha+R_alpha^-1 =2-(2-lambda_input)(z+2)/(z-2). (13) This is precisely the ACTUAL four-parabolic trace equation in the inverse-turn convention (1), as can be proved without importing a character-variety formula. Diagonalize the target product `T=diag(J,J^-1)` and write its second incoming meridian as B_t=[[b11,b12],[b21,b22]], Tr B_t=Tr(B_t^-1 T)=-2, det B_t=1. The two trace equations give b11=-2J/(J+1), b22=-2/(J+1), b12 b21=-(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2. (14) For a target centralizer with eigenratio R, take `D=diag(R,1)`. The original input product is, BY THE ACTUAL INVERSE TURN, `(D B_t D^-1)^-1 B_t`. Therefore lambda_input=Tr(D B_t^-1 D^-1 B_t) =2-[(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2](2-R-R^-1). (15) Since `(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2=(z-2)/(z+2)`, equations (13) and (15) are identical. This proves the generating relation for general input trace, not just the number of its roots. At alpha=1/2 the explicit physical collar computation (3)--(5) fixes WHICH of the two inverse eigenratio branches is the marked one. Continuing that branch in alpha gives (13); no new arbitrary sign is selected at each input value. The expressions extend on `|Im eta|<pi/2` using the same scalar slit branch. The parabolic target eta=0 has the finite normalized limit D_normalized=I+(i s/2)(T+I). Its source trace is `2+16(i s/2)^2=lambda_input`, as it must be. This is a classical parabolic limit, not a substitute for an actual generic-q normal. For the analytic rectangle parameter c>1 one may take `eta=i arccos(1/c)` inside the same strip; the continued marking agrees with the real physical target in the preceding theorem. This statement does not assert that any finite real-color contour can be moved there without poles or without additional contributions. The additive value of each general-input scalar action is already fixed by its actual positive finite-source limit at any z<-2, followed by the slit-domain continuation. No additive period is inferred from (13) alone. Equation (9) is the explicit complete-input anchor. ## 5. What has and has not been compared The target trace, the ordered target conjugator, its selected eigenratio, and the entire scalar generating derivative now agree with the actual recoupled geometry. The scalar action has its finite-source anchor (9). The original generic identity remains `D_a^-1 p_a(Omega)` before every normal extraction; at root `D_a=1`, and its fixed scalar generic jets have the already proved polynomial relative bound on compact real targets below -2. No generic normal is replaced by a root derivative. Equation (11) is a comparison at the actual classical critical point. The algebraic ordinary-column character map is valid on its regular complex channel chart, but the existing ordinary-column ASYMPTOTIC theorem keeps that channel real and discrete. This note does not extend that theorem to (4). Nor does scalar convergence in (7) establish the action of the degree-O(N) polynomial p_a(Omega) on the complementary selected boundary state. Establishing that action, its actual phase, and its contribution to the original finite source remains necessary. In particular (9) is a scalar anchor, not a new proof that an assembled marked critical action equals the complement volume. Any such assembly must also retain the pivotal clock, original row and half-twist factors, native measures, shared wires, and the full physical normal already specified by the exact source identities. Audit: [actual inverse turn, ordered transport and scalar generating action](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.py). It proves four symbolic ordered-matrix identities, all four cyclic prefix identities, the exact eigenratio and parabolic normalization, and the rational Cayley identity fixing the sign. Five further symbolic identities check the generic target pair and its original-input trace relation. At 90 digits it checks three independent action integrals, twelve actual source-polynomial actions and first derivatives, four endpoint second derivatives, and twelve general-input scalar derivatives and character equations, at both level parities. No operator or network asymptotic is tested. The action uses the stated analytic c>1 continuation without claiming that it is realized by a complete geometric rectangle. No polynomial-operator substitution or source-cycle contribution follows.

title: A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge
status: All-target positive scalar; fixed generic jets
text: # A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge 30 October 2026. This is a specialization of the actual generic four-port coefficient theorem to the two halves of ONE crossing-circle matching edge. Its four outside objects are all the original physical V_(N-1). The scalar is positive after the retained single root zero is removed, including every new high recoupling channel and both level parities. All fixed generic scalar jets have polynomial relative cost. Each full recoupled tensor term has at most one pole, so its first normal needs Taylor order two after clearing that pole. This theorem controls the explicitly stated scalar and Laurent budget. It does not estimate the native boundary change-of-frame costs, the completed Hermite operator, or the surrounding coherent contraction. ## 1. The full actual channel range is uniformly saturated Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), and fix 0<=a<=floor(d/2), (A,B,C,D)=(d,d,d,d), E=2a, G=2g, 0<=g<=d. (1) The G range in (1) is the ENTIRE generic four-port recoupling range. No high partner is discarded. These are the four-port highest-weight conventions of [the actual coefficient theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md). The corresponding six spins are (d/2,d/2,d/2,d/2,a,g). Its faces and opposite sums are F=(d+a,d+a,d+g,d+g), Q=(2d,d+a+g,d+a+g). (2) Every face is at least d, and all its triangle deficits are among k,k,d-k for k=a or g. They lie in [0,d]. All four faces and three opposite sums are INTEGERS, also when N is even and the four physical spins d/2 are half-integral. Consequently the true Racah range is d+max(a,g)<=z<=min(2d,d+a+g), (3) and all seven denominator factorial indices are in [0,d]. Every numerator [z+1]! contains exactly one [N] and contains NO [2N]. Thus this special physical block is tail-free even when g>d/2. This is not a claim that arbitrary high recoupling partners are tail-free. For the genuine generic symmetric factorial at zeta define S_ag(zeta)=sum_(z in (3)) (-1)^z [z+1]! / ([z-d-a]!^2 [z-d-g]!^2 [2d-z]! [d+a+g-z]!^2), G_ag(zeta)=(-1)^d S_ag(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) The division in (4) is performed in every original summand before root specialization. It is an analytic germ at q, not a derivative of a root-only replacement. ## 2. An exact positive squared-trinomial formula Set s_k=product_(v=1)^k 2sin(pi v/N), s_0=1. The elementary identity s_(d-k)=N/s_k gives the explicit root scalar R_N(a,g)=G_ag(q) =sum_(r=max(0,a-g))^(min(a,d-g)) [s_(g+r)/(s_(g+r-a)s_r s_(a-r))]^2 >0. (5) To verify every factor, put k=z-d. The removed-numerator formula is N sum_k s_k / [s_(k-a)^2 s_(k-g)^2 s_(d-k) s_(a+g-k)^2]. Replace s_(d-k) by N/s_k and then set r=k-g. All indices in (5) are between 0 and d. The signs of the factors [N+1],...,[z+1] combine with (-1)^(d+z) to give +1. No half-spin phase was omitted: A+B+C+D+E+G=4d+2a+2g is even. The full high partner has the SAME root scalar: R_N(a,g)=R_N(a,d-g). (6) This is termwise: replace g by d-g and r by a-r, and use s_(d-k)=N/s_k in the numerator/first-denominator ratio. The actual ranges in (5) are carried onto one another. Equation (6) is proved at both parities and does not discard any generic normal. The face metric is especially simple. For a face (d/2,d/2,k), put Delta_k^2=[k]!^2[d-k]!/[d+k+1]!, D_k(zeta)=(-1)^k [N]_zeta Delta_k^2. (7) All D_k are analytic and nonzero at q, and D_k(q)=s_k s_(d-k)/N=1. (8) There are two faces of each kind k=a,g. The generic normalized scalar therefore has the single-valued form H_ag(zeta)=G_ag(zeta)D_a(zeta)D_g(zeta), H_ag(q)=R_N(a,g). (9) Its branch-independent identity is the exact actual scalar convention H_ag^2=[N]^2 S_ag^2 product_(four faces) Delta^2. (10) All powers and signs in (10) are the original ones. A scalar diagonal gauge relating (10) to the physical recoupling matrix is still required; root value 1 of the face factors alone does not make that matrix unitary. ## 3. Every fixed generic scalar jet has polynomial relative cost There are universal c,C>0 such that, for ALL labels in (1), on zeta=q exp(t), |t|<=c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) G_ag/G_ag(q), D_a, D_g and H_ag/H_ag(q) are holomorphic and remain in a fixed small disk about 1. In particular they are nonzero. For every fixed m>=0 this implies |partial_t^m G_ag(0)|+|partial_t^m H_ag(0)| <=C_m [N^2(1+log N)]^m R_N(a,g). (12) The same relative estimate holds for their inverses. For clarity, the proof applies to the COMPLETE generic germ in (4). After the one [N] factor is canceled, each summand and each face metric is a quotient of factors zeta^u-zeta^(-u), 1<=u<2N, u!=N, with fixed factorial multiplicities. Its logarithmic change on (11) is bounded by C N^2(1+log N)|t|, using |sin(pi u/N)| bounded below by a constant times dist(u,NZ)/N and the finite harmonic sum. At the root every summand of G_ag is positive by (5). On a sufficiently small common disk these summands remain in one narrow sector, so their sum has the same uniform relative bound. Equations (7),(8) give it for D_a,D_g. Cauchy's estimate proves (12). This is the direct supported-scalar argument, with (2),(3) proving its hypotheses for the entire present range, including half-integral physical spins and high g. In particular no missing [2N]T normal survives here: such a numerator factor is absent from every term before differentiation. The result does not say that a normal equals the derivative of the positive root expression (5); (4) remains the differentiated source. ## 4. The actual physical coefficient has only a simple pole Let L_(2g,2a) be the actual inverse Racah coefficient, with its original pivotal turn and first-highest-entry-one Clebsch bases. The exact source formula is L_(2g,2a)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) S_ag, n=d-g, S0=[2d+1]!/([d-a]!^2[a]!^2), V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-d-g-1);Q)_n / [(Q;Q)_n^2 (Q^(-2d-1);Q)_n], Q=zeta^2. (13) The four prefactors chi_E,X_E,b_G,J_n are root units. This follows from their actual boundary product formulas: E=2a<N; their physical endpoint factorial indices are all in [0,d]. No first-normal channel norm is divided out. S0 has exactly one root zero. The numerator of V_n has a single root zero exactly when 2g<d. (14) Indeed its negative exponents run from -(d+g+1) to -(2g+2), and the only possible root multiple is -N. Its denominator factors are all units: the negative product starts at -(2N-1) and has length d-g, ending strictly before -N. The two (Q;Q)_n factors have n<N. By the strict positivity in (5), S_ag has exactly one root zero. Thus the ACTUAL coefficient orders are ord_q L_(2g,2a)=-1 for 2g<d, ord_q L_(2g,2a)= 0 for 2g>=d. (15) This includes a=0 and all endpoints. It does not assert positivity or regularity of the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix. Let T_(2g) be the actual generic target invariant tensor. Its Clebsch entries have the regular canceled physical coproduct formulas; the only possible pole is the canonical intermediate cup, with denominator (Q;Q)_(2g). Hence T_(2g) is regular for 2g<N and has at most a simple pole for 2g>=N. These two ranges never overlap the pole range in (15). Consequently pole_order [L_(2g,2a) T_(2g)] <=1 (16) for EVERY channel and level parity. The fixed source tensor S_(2a) is regular, so the simple poles on the right of its exact recoupling identity cancel in their full sum. After multiplication by a local parameter t, each recoupled term is holomorphic. Its contribution to the first normal of the regular whole contraction is extracted from Taylor coefficient t^2. Thus this special block has a uniform first-normal budget TWO, improving the general all-port budget four. If a regular surrounding contraction is present, it must be included when extracting that coefficient; its derivatives are not discarded. ## 5. Relation to the geometric pair localization The [prescribed-facet corollary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) allows the two physical-support exceptions to be placed at the two halves of any chosen crossing-circle matching edge. Their four outside objects are then all V_d, so the present specialization applies regardless of the ribbon order of the other matching edges. A physical MAIN edge does not have that automatic property: its two channel legs can be adjacent instead of opposite in the actual cyclic order. The exact typed bend from the original W_a pi_a block to S_(2a), its fixed gamma factor, and the unchanged physical mark belong to the separate source interface. The normal must be extracted from the complete generic contraction, with all channels in (1) retained. Even after that interface, this is not a sharp completed block norm or a bound on the full source. Its scalar gauge factors can carry nontrivial boundary cost; the other local columns are not automatically in the central domain; and a global selected cycle and coherent bound remain necessary. The theorem makes the exceptional matching block an explicit tail-free scalar/finite-jet problem, without declaring those remaining tasks solved. Audit: [exact matching-edge scalar, original recoupling and normal budget](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.py). It passes 21,772 support/phase/pole cases, ten independently reconstructed generic source tensor families with all 47 recoupling coefficients, 529 retained root germs, 1,257 termwise partner checks, and 1,058 exact face-unit jets. In 406 comparisons the partners have the same root value but DIFFERENT generic first derivatives. The audit retains that distinction; its finite cases test conventions, while the written harmonic-product argument proves the uniform jet bound. The positive scalar Racah model does not supply a norm for the native matrix source or control a whole source from root-face values.

title: The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two
status: Roots above two; selected scalar action
text: # The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two 30 October 2026. For EVERY folded original channel, the exact matching-edge Casimir polynomial has simple real zeros strictly greater than 2. A positive matrix factorization proves this, including maximal channels at both level parities. Its canonical logarithm and leading action consequently continue to the whole slit plane C minus [2,infinity), including every real geometric target below 2. No continuation of a finite target color g is required. This theorem concerns the actual scalar polynomial. It does not prove a relative amplitude, control moving-q normal derivatives, estimate the complementary tensor contraction, or select a global source cycle. ## 1. The exact original polynomial at the root Use the generic source identity proved in [the geometric target polynomial theorem](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md). Its normalization is D_a G_ag D_g=p_a(lambda_g), lambda_g=zeta^(2g+1)+zeta^(-2g-1), with all generic source factors retained. Put q=exp(pi i/N), theta=pi/N, d=N-1, 0<=a<=M=floor(d/2), and specialize to q. Let s_k=product_(r=1)^k 2sin(r theta), and set lambda_r=2cos((2r+1)theta), phi_k(x)=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(lambda_r-x). The generic terminating formula becomes EXACTLY p_a(x)=sum_(k=0)^a c_(a,k) phi_k(x), c_(a,k)=s_(a+k)/(s_(a-k)s_k^4). (1) Indeed [d-r]=[r+1] and [d+r+2]=-[r+1] at q, so the generic alternating signs cancel. Also [g-r][g+r+1]=(lambda_r-lambda_g)/(4sin^2 theta), product_(r<k)(lambda_r-lambda_a)=s_(a+k)/s_(a-k). These identities yield (1) without changing the original spectral variable. In particular p_a(lambda_0)=1 and its leading coefficient is kappa_a=(-1)^a s_(2a)/s_a^4. (2) All displayed denominators are nonzero for 2a<N. For a=0 the polynomial is identically one. ## 2. An own three-term recurrence For 0<=n<M define A_n=-4sin^4((n+1)theta) /[sin((2n+1)theta)sin((2n+2)theta)], B_n=2/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], C_n=-4sin^4(n theta)/[sin(2n theta)sin((2n+1)theta)], C_0=0. Then the finite polynomials (1) satisfy x p_n(x)=A_n p_(n+1)(x)+B_n p_n(x)+C_n p_(n-1)(x). (3) Here is a direct coefficient proof. Since x phi_k=lambda_k phi_k-phi_(k+1), the coefficient of phi_k on the left is lambda_k c_(n,k)-c_(n,k-1). The required ratios are c_(n+1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta), c_(n-1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta), c_(n,k-1)/c_(n,k) =4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)]. (4) Substitution in (3), followed by the sine addition identities, gives equality. More explicitly the identity after division by c_(n,k) is lambda_k-4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)] =A_n sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta) +B_n+C_n sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta). It is a rational identity in exp(i theta), exp(i n theta) and exp(i k theta); clearing its displayed denominators gives zero. The top coefficient k=n+1 is A_n=kappa_n/kappa_(n+1). The case n=0 follows directly from p_0 and p_1. Thus no presumed orthogonality or external q-Racah recurrence enters the proof. Set P_n=p_n/kappa_n, the monic polynomials. Equation (3) becomes P_(n+1)=(x-B_n)P_n-e_n^2 P_(n-1), e_n^2=A_(n-1)C_n =4sin^6(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]>0. (5) Consequently P_a(x)=det(xI-J_a), where J_a is the real symmetric Jacobi matrix with diagonal B_0,...,B_(a-1) and adjacent entries e_1,...,e_(a-1)>0. ## 3. The positive shift by two Let Dpos_a be the previously proved positive q-Hahn matrix; the distinct scalar face factor retains its original name D_a: (Dpos_a)_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], (Dpos_a)_(n-1,n)=sqrt(beta_n), beta_n=sin^2(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. For completeness, its leading principal minors are det Dpos_m=2^m product_(r=1)^m sin(r theta) /product_(r=m+1)^(2m)sin(r theta)>0. This finite formula was proved by the determinant recurrence in [the original q-Hahn determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md#4-a-positive-definite-real-part). Every factor is positive because 2m<N, so Dpos_a is positive definite also at a=M. Put H=diag(sin((n+1/2)theta))_(n=0)^(a-1), s0=sin(theta/2). There is the exact matrix factorization J_a-2I=2 H Dpos_a H+2s0^2 Dpos_a. (6) The diagonal identity is sin^2((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =1-cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta). The adjacent identity is sin((n-1/2)theta)sin((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =sin^2(n theta). These are precisely the entries in (5),(6). The right side of (6) is positive definite. Therefore EVERY eigenvalue of J_a is strictly greater than 2. The nonzero adjacent entries also imply simple spectrum: an eigenvector is determined by its first coordinate through the tridiagonal recurrence, and that coordinate cannot vanish. Hence ALL zeros of p_a are simple, real, and strictly greater than 2. (7) This is uniform in the folded channel, with no restriction to odd levels or to channels bounded away from the fold. ## 4. The canonical logarithm and its uniform derivative bounds Write the zeros as r_1,...,r_a>2. Since p_a(lambda_0)=1, p_a(x)=product_(h=1)^a (r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0). On Omega=C minus [2,infinity), define Log p_a(x)=sum_h Log((r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0)), (8) where each logarithm is continued from its positive real value at any x<2. Equivalently its argument has the principal logarithm in each individual factor. This is a single holomorphic branch on Omega, real on the whole interval x<2. For m>=1, |partial_x^m Log p_a(x)| <=(m-1)! a/dist(x,[2,infinity))^m. (9) Thus the original scalar itself, rather than a complexly continued finite color g, supplies a canonical selected branch at every geometric real target x<2. ## 5. Leading source action continues through the physical endpoint Here the scalar leading limit can also be proved directly. Let a_N/N tend to alpha in (0,1/2]. For a real x<-2, every term in (1) is positive. Uniform sine-factorial estimates and Riemann sums give N^-1 log p_(a_N)(x) -> max_(0<=t<=alpha) E_alpha(t;x), E_alpha(t;x)=J(alpha+t)-J(alpha-t)-4J(t) +integral_0^t log(2cos(2pi u)-x) du, J(v)=integral_0^v log(2sin(pi u)) du. (10) The endpoint logarithmic singularities in the sine factorials cost O(log N), uniformly in their integer indices. The final integrand in (10) is smooth and positive-argument for x<-2. The number of summands is at most N, so maximum-term comparison proves (10), including sequences approaching the folded channel. The maximum is unique and interior. Put A=sin^2(pi alpha), v=2-x and z=sin^2(pi t). Its derivative is partial_t E=log[(A-z)(v-4z)/(4z^2)]. For x<-2 this strictly decreases from +infinity to -infinity. The critical equation is linear after cancellation of its z^2 terms, and gives z_*=A v/(v+4A), t_*=pi^-1 arcsin(sqrt(A v/(v+4A))). (11) Now fix an anchor x0<-2. The bounds (9), divided by N, make N^-1 Log p_(a_N) a locally bounded normal family on the connected slit domain Omega: its value at x0 is bounded by (10), and its derivative is uniformly bounded along any fixed compact path. Every subsequential holomorphic limit agrees with (10) on the real interval x<-2. The identity theorem therefore makes the limit unique. Consequently N^-1 Log p_(a_N)(x) -> Psi_alpha(x) (12) locally uniformly on ALL of Omega, with every fixed x derivative. This is the actual source logarithm (8), not a formally chosen solution of a characteristic equation. On the entire real interval x<2 the continuation is explicitly Psi_alpha(x)=E_alpha(t_*(x);x), (13) with (11). Indeed 0<z_*<min(A,v/4), so all logarithms in the integral up to t_* have positive arguments. Formula (13) is real analytic on x<2 and agrees with (10) on x<-2, proving the claimed continuation. In particular the passage through x=-2 is regular. There is no claimed uniformity at the removed boundary x=2. The result proves a leading selected SCALAR action. It does not turn the original tensor contraction into a scalar evaluation, or justify discarding its generic first normals. Those distinctions remain essential to the global volume problem. Audit: [original root values, the own recurrence and positive matrix shift](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.py). The result concerns the scalar polynomial and its leading action. It does not replace the contracted operator by that scalar.

title: A real exceptional target cannot preserve the selected global complement
text: # A real exceptional target cannot preserve the selected global complement 30 October 2026. The [real-target classification](actual_matching_edge_real_target_frames.md) constructs local real cross-central frames for every strict geometric target c<1. They cannot also preserve the selected physical ordinary complement in the present one-matching-edge reduction of a certified right-angled link. This is a precise frame obstruction for that route, not a rate gap or a contradiction to the source invariant or conjecture. ## 1. Statement and retained hypotheses Fix an actual labeled right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, its literal Morse prefixes, retained half twists, primitive markings, and original source. Choose one matching edge as the exceptional four-port block. Assume its actual rectangle satisfies 0<c<1; the parabolic case c=1 is not treated here. There is NO common regular frame with all the following properties: * Every original input/output factor outside this edge lies in the strict physical domain on its source-selected complete geometric sheet, as in the selected-factor localization theorem. * After the ACTUAL inverse pivotal turn, both target magnetic rows and the normalized total are real and strictly physical, in either degree adapter. The two limiting target rows are distinct. * The limiting target row distance is positive and at most 1/2, the folded polynomial bandwidth. In particular this includes any strict candidate for a nonzero real exceptional matrix entry. The real-target classification shows that such rows must be on its minus anti-diagonal branch. The key additional fact proved below is that undoing the turn puts BOTH original factors at this edge in the strict physical domain on their selected sheets as well. The geometric white-normal argument then excludes the resulting all-factor frame. ## 2. Undo the actual turn before testing the disk strips Retain the original incoming pair and transport A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=BA, C=I+b(P+I), b=-i/(2c), A_o=C A C^-1, B_o=C B C^-1. The target input/output pair is (A_o^-1,A) and (B_o,B^-1), with target product T=B^-1 B_o=A A_o^-1. Let Pi be the original frame, and Pi_t its inverse-turn frame. The actual basepath change is Pi_t=A_o Pi/Tr(A_o Pi). (1) Here Pi is the prefix-normalized local projector `W Pi_global/Tr(W Pi_global)`, followed by the common local normalizing conjugacy. Its flags are the actual prefix image Wv and the same global kernel w. This notation does not choose a new independent frame at the edge. In the target notation, let E=e^2, e=exp(+/-pi i tau), and q=rho+i sqrt(1-rho^2), q_out=conjugate(q), rho=rho_-<0, k=sinh^2 eta, c=sech eta. First use the displayed ordering; exchanging q and its conjugate will be included below. Since q is unit, the target prefix equations and (1) give the EXACT original prefix diagonals Tr(A Pi)=e/q, Tr(A_o Pi)=e^-1/q, Tr(P Pi)=q^-2. (2) Indeed Tr(A_o^-1 Pi_t)=1/Tr(A_o Pi), while T A_o=A and B_o A_o=P. These identities fix the basepoint and all ratios; (2) is not obtained by identifying Pi with Pi_t. Write the original image and kernel flags in the disk coordinate eta(s)=1/(2s+1) as z and w. Put H=1/c=sqrt(1+k). In this coordinate A=[[-1,0],[-2,-1]], P=[[-1,-2],[0,-1]], C acts by eta -> eta+iH, A_o=[[-1-2iH,-2H^2],[-2,-1+2iH]]. (3) For Pi represented by these flags, Pi=[[z,-zw],[1,-w]]/(z-w). Direct traces in (3) give Tr(P Pi)=-1-2/(z-w), Tr(A Pi)=-1+2zw/(z-w), Tr(A_o Pi)-Tr(A Pi) =[-2H^2-2iH(z+w)]/(z-w). (4) Use q+q^-1=2rho and (2) in (4). It follows that z-w=-q/rho, z+w=iH+(e^-1-e)/(2iH rho). (5) The second term in the sum is REAL for both target adapters. Hence Im z=[H-sqrt(1-rho^2)/rho]/2, Im w=[H+sqrt(1-rho^2)/rho]/2. (6) Exchanging the trace signs exchanges these heights. They are finite: rho_- is strictly negative. Both flags lie strictly in the ACTUAL original disk strip 0<Im eta<H precisely when |rho|>1/sqrt(k+2). (7) For rho_-=(-sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k), inequality (7) is equivalent to c0>-1/sqrt(k+2). This is exactly the lower inequality in the strict physical interval already required by the real-target classification. Thus every viable real minus-branch target satisfies its original disk's selected strip test, including when tau<1/2. The real plus branch fails (7), but it is already excluded from a direct nonzero folded entry by its exact row distance greater than 1/2. No source support is discarded in this argument. ## 3. Both original factors are also strictly physical Let q=exp(i alpha), pi/2<alpha<pi, and set delta=1-alpha/pi in (0,1/2), u=(tau-delta)/2, v=(tau+delta)/2, 0<u<tau/2<v<tau<1. These are the target low and high rows. The original physical coordinate dictionary applied to (2) is U_in=-q/e, U_out=-q e, T_original=q^2. (8) For q in the upper half-plane, the original two factors have total degree tau_original=alpha/pi=1-delta in (1/2,1), and their magnetic rows are u and 1-v, in one order or the other depending on the target adapter. Their physical wire pairs are (u,1-v) and (1-v,u). Every entry is strictly between zero and one, and their sum is tau_original. Thus both factors lie strictly in the ordinary complete-channel physical domain. For q in the lower half-plane, the actual physical total is instead 1+delta, with physical magnetic rows v and 1-u. Applying the original high-degree adapter subtracts delta from those rows and reverses the total. The normalized total and rows are again 1-delta, u and 1-v. (9) This explicitly covers both trace orderings and both target adapters. There is no implicit assumption that the normalized target total tau itself exceeds 1/2. Combine (6),(7) with (9). The selected-sheet continuation throughout the full strict physical domain, proved in [the selected-factor theorem](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md), identifies these strip tests with the actual source-selected input and output sheets. Therefore BOTH original factors at the chosen edge are now physical and selected, in the same original frame Pi. ## 4. Why the geometric global obstruction applies beyond its old headline The original [white-normal obstruction](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) was initially stated for an all-central source frame. Its geometric sections 4--5 prove a stronger conditional assertion: simultaneous STRICT physical support and the oriented disk-strip tests are impossible in one common frame for the literal certified cut. Here is the precise use, with no extension of an unproved source sheet outside its domain. Write Pi_global=v ell, let w=ker ell and w_0=r_(F_0)(v). The literal prefixes are Q_i=r_(F_i)r_(F_0). Each adjacent white reflection preserves the two disk halfspaces. Consequently all input/output strip tests imply w,w_0 belong to the common shaded exterior K. In the white-normal polyhedron C, K lies strictly inside C on its unit sphere. Actual prefix diagonals are positive normal rescalings of the polarized real-linear forms L_n(w,w_0). Their real kernel meets int C. Following a line in that kernel to a triangular boundary facet gives a nonnegative relation among the three actual prefix diagonals of that facet. Thus zero lies in their real convex hull. This contradicts that original factor's strict physical-support criterion. The proof includes coincident flags and nongeneric facet-edge intersections; it does not require exactly two generic failures or an all-central hypothesis. By assumption every factor outside the selected matching edge is physical and source-selected; the full-domain theorem supplies its strip test. Sections 2--3 supply both properties on the edge as well. The preceding geometric contradiction proves the stated obstruction. ## 5. What must change in the proposed method The exact real-row Green action and real exceptional operator packets remain valid local theorems. The new conclusion is that this real slice cannot contain the complete geometric point while retaining the currently selected physical ordinary complement in a single common frame. Within that one-block setup, a geometric contraction must use complex target coordinates or change which grouping or complementary source description is controlled. No numerical exponential gap, vanishing of the invariant, absence of a geometric contribution on another cycle, or impossibility of a different source-preserving resummation is inferred. The parabolic target c=1, boundary support, and exact limiting row coincidences remain outside the strict local classification used here. Focused audit: [actual inverse-turn flags and both physical adapters](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_real_frame_global_obstruction.py). Distinct limiting target rows are required. The argument uses the explicit local-prefix projector. It makes no conclusion about a different global source route.

title: Which actual geometric target frames have real magnetic rows?
text: # Which actual geometric target frames have real magnetic rows? 30 October 2026. This is a local classification for the ACTUAL inverse-turn target, not a common-frame existence theorem for the whole link. It supplies a real cross-central frame for every strict certified target c<1. Its total degree can be below 1/2; the existing Green theorem allows that range. One other apparently favorable branch is killed by the exact finite-source bandwidth, including all generic-q normals. ## 1. Keep the actual ordered target and both degree adapters Use the marked inverse turn of [the polynomial generating-action theorem](actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md). For a certified crossing-circle rectangle with 0<c<1, write c=sech eta, eta>0, k=sinh^2 eta, J=-exp(-2eta), T=diag(J,J^-1), R=(1+i sqrt(k))/(1-i sqrt(k)), D=diag(R,1). After a centralizer normalization, its first target input and output are A=[[a,1],[kappa,d]], A_out=D A D^-1, a=-2J/(J+1), d=-2/(J+1), kappa=-(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2. (1) The second input is T A^-1. These are the actual inverse-turn pair, whose product trace is 2-4/c^2, and its actual conjugator eigenratio. In particular D is not chosen to fit magnetic coordinates. The [rectangle bound](actual_matching_circle_rectangle_bound.md) proves c<=1 in the certified class; the parabolic equality c=1 is excluded from the present diagonalization argument. A physical frame is represented by a rank-one trace-one projector Pi. Let the normalized target degree be real, 0<tau<1. The low adapter has E=Tr(T Pi)=exp(-2pi i tau), e=exp(-pi i tau). The high adapter instead has E=exp(+2pi i tau), e=exp(+pi i tau). In BOTH cases put c0=-cos(pi tau) in (-1,1), and write Pi=[[p,q],[r,1-p]], p=(E-J^-1)/(J-J^-1), X=r/e, Y=kappa q/e, K=(c0^2+k)/(4k^2), d0=-c0/k. The determinant-zero condition and the two actual prefix traces are exactly XY=K, z_in=Tr(A Pi)/e=d0+X+Y, z_out=Tr(A_out Pi)/e=d0+R X+R^-1 Y. (2) For example the diagonal trace in (2) follows from `k=-(J+1)^2/(4J)` and `c0=-(e+e^-1)/2`; the same substitutions give `kappa p(1-p)/e^2=K`. Here z_in,z_out denote normalized traces, not tetrahedron shapes. In the low adapter the physical coordinate is U=-1/Tr(A Pi), so the centered exponential is U/exp(pi i tau)=-1/z_in. In the high adapter the actual dictionary is T_phys=1/T_low, U_phys=U_low/T_low, and U_low/exp(pi i tau)=-1/z_in again. The output is identical with A replaced by A_out. Thus in both adapters the two rows are REAL if and only if |z_in|=|z_out|=1. Their strict physical support is equivalent to Re z_in<c0, Re z_out<c0. (3) Indeed the centered magnetic argument has the unique marked lift in (-pi tau,pi tau), and z=-exp[-2pi i(nu-tau/2)]. This proves (3) also for tau<1/2; that range must not be discarded merely because an ordinary complete-channel column needs a larger total degree. The present exceptional operator is the polynomial p_a(J_t). ## 2. All strictly physical real solutions are anti-diagonal Since K>0, parameterize every solution of XY=K by X=sqrt(K) exp(sigma+i phi), Y=sqrt(K) exp(-sigma-i phi), sigma,phi real. Put beta=atan sqrt(k), chi=phi+beta, and L=2sqrt(K). Then z_in =d0+L[cosh(sigma)cos(chi-beta) +i sinh(sigma)sin(chi-beta)], z_out=d0+L[cosh(sigma)cos(chi+beta) +i sinh(sigma)sin(chi+beta)]. (4) Their squared-modulus difference factors as |z_in|^2-|z_out|^2 =4L sin(chi)sin(beta) [d0 cosh(sigma)+L cos(beta)cos(chi)]. (5) If sin chi=0, the two traces are complex conjugates. To exclude the other possibility from strict support, put M=cosh^2 sigma and use the vanishing of the bracket in (5). The common unit-modulus equation then gives M=k/(1-c0^2)+1/(1+k), cos^2 chi=c0^2 M(1+k)/(c0^2+k). (6) Consequently Delta=1-c0^2(k+2)>=0 is necessary. Directly computing the mean and difference of the two real parts gives (c0-Re z_in)(c0-Re z_out) =-Delta [c0^4(k+2)-2c0^2+k^2+k+1] /[(1-c0^2)^2(1+k)^2]. (7) The bracket is strictly positive: Delta>=0 implies c0^2<=1/(k+2)<1/2, so already 1-2c0^2>0 and all other terms are nonnegative. Thus (7) is nonpositive, contradicting BOTH strict inequalities (3). This also excludes the equality Delta=0. It follows that every strictly physical real pair is conjugate. Write z_in=rho+i sqrt(1-rho^2), z_out=conjugate(z_in), allowing their exchange. Substitution in (2) gives precisely [(1+k)rho+c0]^2=k+2, rho_+=(sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k), rho_-=(-sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k). (8) The value rho=-1 gives the common central row; strict cross-central rows require -1<rho<c0. Conversely every branch of (8) with this inequality supplies an actual projector: solve the two linear equations (2) for X,Y, set r=eX and q=eY/kappa, and (8) gives XY=K. The linear determinant is nonzero because R!=R^-1 for k>0. Both target prefix traces are units. No purely formal independent choice of the input and output rows is involved. The two marked row coordinates are nu_low=(tau-1)/2+acos(rho)/(2pi), nu_high=tau-nu_low, 0<nu_low<tau/2<nu_high<tau. (9) For the displayed upper-half-plane z_in, the INPUT is nu_high and the OUTPUT is nu_low. Exchanging the signs of both trace imaginary parts swaps input and output. Their exchange has the same support and distance. This proves the classification in BOTH actual degree adapters. ## 3. Exact bandwidth selects only the minus branch The original target matrix J_t(zeta) is tridiagonal at generic zeta. The exact matching-edge operator is a scalar normalization times p_a(J_t), where p_a has degree a. Therefore EVERY generic entry with |u-v|>a vanishes identically. This remains true after taking any fixed generic-q derivative, clearing its scalar normalizers, or combining the retained partner normal. It is not a semiclassical estimate. For (9) the row distance is delta=nu_high-nu_low =1-acos(rho)/pi=1/2+asin(rho)/pi. (10) The plus branch is strictly physical precisely when c0>1/sqrt(k+2). It always has rho_+>0. Thus delta>1/2, and for actual folded degrees a/N->1/2 every sufficiently nearby integer matrix entry is IDENTICALLY ZERO. Its real frame cannot serve as a direct nonzero exceptional kernel. The finite-propagation identity for a whole continuant vector does not contradict this entrywise fact. The minus branch has rho_-<0, hence delta<1/2. It avoids this exact support obstruction. This does not by itself prove a nonzero matrix element, an asymptotic, a contributing spectral saddle, or absence of cancellation in the full marked contraction. ## 4. Real cross-central local frames exist for every strict target The minus branch is strict cross-central and physical exactly when -1/sqrt(k+2)<c0<min(1,k+1-sqrt(k+2)). (11) The interval is nonempty for EVERY k>0, since k+1-sqrt(k+2)+1/sqrt(k+2) =(k+1)(1-1/sqrt(k+2))>0. Choose any c0 in this open interval and set tau=acos(-c0)/pi. Equations (2),(8) construct a common local frame with the strict real cross-central rows (9) and distance below 1/2. It therefore lies in the real parameter range of the [cross-central Green action](actual_matching_edge_cross_central_green_action.md). That theorem allows every 0<tau<1, so no additional tau>1/2 hypothesis is needed for this local application. There IS a useful limitation if one insists on tau>1/2: then c0>0, and (11) has a solution precisely when k>(sqrt(5)-1)/2, c<sqrt((sqrt(5)-1)/2). (12) For larger rectangles the required real total must be below 1/2. The already certified isolated cylinders C(h^s), s>=5, have c=cos(pi/s) above this threshold by [the arbitrary-width seed theorem](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md). They illustrate why imposing the ordinary complete-column domain on the exceptional Green operator would falsely create an obstruction. No theorem about a universal global choice of frame follows instead. ## 5. The original selected frame is still an additional constraint The inverse pivotal turn changes the basepoint. With A_old,out the original first output meridian, the projectors obey Pi_target=A_old,out Pi_old/Tr(A_old,out Pi_old), Pi_old=A_old,out^-1 Pi_target/Tr(A_old,out^-1 Pi_target). (13) For a direct check, the actual first lower factor is L_1=[[1,0],[-G_21,G_11]], and L_1^-1 E_11 L_1=G E_11/G_11. Conjugating back gives (13). The denominator in the inverse formula is the nonzero first target prefix trace, so the local projectors constructed here pull back. The selected-strip conditions for EVERY other disk must be imposed on this Pi_old and its actual prefixes. They are not conditions on independently selected target diagonals. The present classification neither proves nor disproves their simultaneous compatibility with (11). In particular it does not replace the global prescribed-pair theorem by a real-slice assertion, identify the complementary state with a continuant, or infer that a real spectral saddle contributes. Focused audit: [actual target traces, classification and bandwidth](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_real_target_frames.py). The input/output ordering in (9) is part of the statement. Compatibility with the other disks of the link is not established by the local-frame theorem.

title: The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window
status: Full real norm rate in shrinking fold windows
text: # The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window 30 October 2026. Let j_N/N tend to 1/2, with 0<=j_N<=floor((N-1)/2). The FULL physical completed projector and, when paired, its actual nilpotent have exponential norm rate 5v3/pi. No restriction such as (N-1-2j_N)log N=o(N) is needed here. This concerns real integer physical degrees and magnetic indices, their Euclidean operator norms, and fixed generic-q jets. It does not extend the complex-normal corridor, supply a confluent complex amplitude, or estimate a marked whole-network contraction. ## 1. Statement and the exact source interfaces Put d=N-1, j=j_N, l=d-j and s=l-j. If j<l, let Q_j and M_j be the ACTUAL completed target pair in the [native projector theorem](actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md). If j=l, retain the ordinary isolated midpoint projector Pi_j. Then, for every sequence j/N->1/2, N^-1 log ||Q_j||op ->5v3/pi, N^-1 log ||M_j||op ->5v3/pi (1) on its paired subsequence, and the same limit holds for Pi_j on its simple subsequence. All statements remain true for the Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Every FIXED generic-q jet of these operators has upper exponential rate at most 5v3/pi; equality is not asserted for a derivative that can vanish. We prove the paired claim; the isolated midpoint is already covered by the [full folded profile](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md). Here s/N->0, while s itself can tend to infinity at any sublinear rate. All original physical degrees are retained. For complete degrees l<=t<=d, the exact Parseval comparison is N/(j+1) Z_(t,j) <= E_(t,j) <=N Z_(t,j), Z_(t,j)=|fhat_j(t/2)|^2/|sigma_(t,j)|. (2) The exact center source and double CD measure give Z_(t,j)=A_(N,t,j) R_j(1;c_t)^2, A_(N,t,j)=a_j^2/N *s_(2j)^2/s_j^4 *s_(t-j)/s_(t-l), c_t=-cos(pi(t+1)/N), a_j=|1-q^(4j+2)|. (3) All factorial indices lie in 0,...,d. The monic determinant R_j is the original source determinant, not an auxiliary positive replacement. It is increasing at z=1 for real c>=0. In (3), c_t ranges from cos(pi j/N) to 1, so this monotonicity applies. Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi y))dy on [0,1]. Its continuity, J(0)=J(1/2)=J(1)=0, and the uniform factorial estimate give sup_(l<=t<=d) |N^-1 log A_(N,t,j)| ->0. (4) Indeed the factorial part divided by N is 2J(2j/N)-4J(j/N) +J((t-j)/N)-J((t-l)/N)+O(log N/N). The first two terms tend to zero. The last two arguments differ by s/N->0, uniformly over t, so their difference tends to zero by uniform continuity. The remaining a_j and N factors have logarithms O(log N), since a_j>=4/N at a nonself-paired node. Thus (2)--(4), at the endpoint and throughout the complete range, prove max_(l<=t<=d) E_(t,j)=R_j(1;1)^2 exp(o(N)). (5) This is a maximum over one genuine physical degree. It does not maximize independently over degrees of adjacent network coupons. ## 2. The actual endpoint selects the same cubic limit Put u=floor(d/2), v=d-u and w_N=q^j. At t=d the positive coefficient polynomial appearing in the original physical column is P_N(w)=sum_(a=0)^j beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a) w^a, C_j(d,u)=q^((d-j)u) P_N(w_N). (6) The denominator beta(d,j) is exactly one. The finite negative-root theorem applies to this original polynomial. Uniform factorial estimates and j/N,u/N,v/N->1/2 give uniformly over the whole support N^-1 log[beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a)] =-3[J(a/N)+J(1/2-a/N)]+o(1). (7) Replacing j/N by 1/2 uses only uniform continuity of J, including both endpoints. There is no assumed bound on s log N here. For every positive real w, (7) gives the same strict real Laplace action as in the full folded theorem. Its selected saddle is alpha(w)=pi^-1 arctan(w^(1/3)). The actual negative-root product bound makes N^-1 Log(P_N(w)/P_N(1)) a normal family on the slit plane. Uniqueness from the positive real axis therefore gives the same holomorphic action for this whole sequence of actual polynomials. In particular at w_N->i, N^-1 log |C_j(d,u)| ->5v3/(2pi). (8) This is the selected complex rate, not a conclusion from comparing positive coefficients at w=i. The exact constant was computed from alpha(i)=1/4+i log(3)/(4pi) and D(i/sqrt(3))=5v3/6 in the preceding theorem. At degree d the magnetic polynomial has all j roots negative real. If u differs from d/2 by one half, its root-product formula gives cos(pi/(2N))^j <= |C_j(d,u)|/|fhat_j(d/2)| <=1; (9) if d is even the ratio is one. Finally the exact center scalar is |fhat_j(d/2)|=R_j(1;1) s_(2j)/s_j^3. (10) Its normalized logarithm tends to zero, since J(2j/N)-3J(j/N)->0. Equations (8)--(10) prove N^-1 log R_j(1;1)^2 ->5v3/pi. (11) ## 3. The incomplete band is smaller, using its own actual formula It remains to control j<=t<l, where the completed pair contains only its simple physical branch. The complete-range Fourier factorization is NOT assumed in this band. Instead start with the original generic finite column. Its highest-vector factor at the root is exactly F_(N-j+a-1) F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-j-1)F_(N-1)) =Q^(a(a-j)) [j choose a]_Q. (12) This follows by complementing each factor 1-Q^(N-r)=-Q^(-r)(1-Q^r). Every denominator index is below N; (12) is valid for ALL 0<=j<=t< N, not just complete channels. Since [n choose k]_Q=q^(k(n-k)) beta(n,k), substitution into the original divided-descendant sum gives the exact identity C_j(t,u)=q^((d-j)u) sum_a E(t,j,u,a) q^(a(t+j-d)), E=beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (13) To check its phase directly, the Gaussian-binomial phases, divided-descendant powers and root highest ratio leave a(t+j-1)-ju before the factor (-1)^a x^(-2a). Combining that factor with x^u and q^N=-1 gives precisely (13). Thus its real positive envelope is an authorized bound for this ACTUAL root source outside the complete chamber. Set r=t-j<s=o(N). Every allowed a satisfies 0<=u-a<=r. Uniform factorial estimates, j/N,t/N->1/2, and that inequality imply N^-1 log E(t,j,u,a) =-J(x)-J(1/2-x)+o(1), (14) uniformly throughout the incomplete band and its full support. Here x can be chosen as min(u/N,1/2). The possible excess of u/N above 1/2 is o(1), so this harmless clipping and all arguments of J are justified by its uniform continuity. In detail the beta(j,a) term supplies the displayed profile, while beta(u,a), beta(t-u,j-a), and the denominator beta(t,j) each have normalized logarithm tending uniformly to zero because their complementary indices are at most r. There are at most N summands in (13). A triangle bound therefore gives the uniform upper estimate from (14). This step is used only in the collapsing boundary band and claims no selected oscillatory rate for an interior column. The simple CD measure there is |sigma_(t,j)|=s_(t-j)s_(t+j+1)/(s_t^2 a_j). Its normalized logarithm tends uniformly to zero: its three factorial arguments tend respectively to 0,1,1/2. Summing the squared column bound over at most N magnetic indices yields max_(j<=t<l) E_(t,j) <=exp[N(v8/(2pi)+o(1))]. (15) The smaller constant comes from the strict maximum at x=1/4 of -2J(x)-2J(1/2-x). This estimate retains endpoints and all source phases until the explicitly stated upper-bound step. ## 4. Assemble the real operator and retain the scope The exact generic high adapter duplicates the same physical low blocks. On each complete block M_j has norm E_(t,j); it is zero on the incomplete band. Hence (5),(11) give its full operator and Hilbert--Schmidt rate in (1). On a complete block M_j=(J_t-c_j)Q_j, with uniformly bounded J_t-c_j, providing the matching lower bound for Q_j. The native projector theorem gives its upper bound by a polynomial times the maximum or square sum of ALL energies. Equations (11),(15), and v8/(2pi)<5v3/pi prove the other claim in (1). Fixed generic-q derivatives add only the uniform polynomial factors already proved there. Thus every shrinking SCALED fold window has the same explicit real boundary cost, even when s log N is not o(N). The stronger width here comes from positivity and real physical norms, not from a larger joint complex domain for paired normal currents. No fixed nonzero scaled-width assertion or whole-source volume conjecture follows from this corollary. Audit: [original incomplete-band formula and shrinking-fold source](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.py). The indices remain real and physical. This result does not enlarge the complex-normal corridor or assert a whole-source limit. The continuity, root-product and operator arguments prove the shrinking real-window bounds. Finite samples check their conventions, not their uniformity.

title: The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase
text: # The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase 30 October 2026. In the exact positive Fourier partition, every Clebsch endpoint phase and every ordinary cup/cap constant cancels explicitly. The remaining original phase is a quadratic form in the shared integer labels, with the original half-twist phases and marked Fourier charge retained. This is an exact source identity, not a claim that its stationary point contributes to the finite sum. ## 1. Exact paired endpoint phase Use the original definitions in [the positive Fourier partition](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md). Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, r=a+w, t=d-|w|, and B_N(a,w)=k_a N s_(a+|w|) /(s_a^2 s_|w|^2 s_(a-|w|)). The actual first endpoint scalars c_W,c_pi and the actual finite polynomial scalar c_(t,a) satisfy the stronger COMPLEX identity h0_a c_W c_pi c_(t,a)^2 = B_N(a,w) q^[(2a-d)t]. (1) Indeed, the original reversed-conjugate white map gives c_W c_pi=|c_W|^2 conjugate(f_(t,a)(t))/G_(a,r). The original generic physical endpoint specializes to f_(t,a)(t)=(-1)^a q^[dt+a^2+a]. (2) This retains the actual endpoint convention; the term -2Na in its generic exponent has become the root unit q^(-2Na)=1. Meanwhile F_a=(Q;Q)_a=(-i)^a q^[a(a+1)/2]s_a gives c_(t,a)^2 =(-1)^a q^[2a(t-d)+a(a-1)]/s_a^2. (3) Multiplying (2),(3), the signs cancel and the exponent is (2a-d)t-2a(d+1). Its final term is -2aN and hence contributes one. The remaining modulus is exactly the already-proved B_N. This proves (1), including high-degree columns and both level parities; no choice of a Chevalley square root remains in the phase. ## 2. Center every actual physical port Work on the same shared state space S_N as in the positive partition: exact bounded Kirchhoff flows w, coefficient indices k_v, and ALL physical-cycle congruences, including charge one on the original marked cycle. On a restored physical cycle, let x be its integer base coordinate and write the actual FIRST coordinate at each node n as u_n=epsilon_n x+B_n, epsilon_n in {+1,-1}. Here B_n is the literal integer affine offset. At a Clebsch node v incident to edge i the actual total is T_n=d+w_i. At a cup or cap it is T_n=d. Define delta_n=B_n-T_n/2, gamma_v=d-2a_i+2k_v, gamma_b=d at cups/caps. (4) In particular delta_n can be a half-integer. Its definition is independent of the low/high adapter: the compiler offset b_v satisfies b_v+t_i/2=T_n/2 exactly. The residual exponent of a vertex in the original finite expansion can therefore be written as gamma_v(B_v-b_v)-t_i k_v =gamma_v delta_v+(d-2a_i)t_i/2. (5) Each matching edge has TWO such vertices. Their last terms in (5) cancel exactly against the paired endpoint phase (1). This uses their shared a_i,w_i,t_i; independent vertex normalization would hide the cancellation. For a cup or cap, its coordinate monomial contributes d B_b=d delta_b+d^2/2. There are H original cups and H restored ordinary caps. Their 2H constant terms add to H d^2, exactly canceling the H original cup constants q^(-d^2). Their powers of N have already canceled in the positive partition. The original marked cap is still represented by its specified charged-cap ratio; that ratio's global q^(-d^2) remains outside the sum. Consequently the COMPLETE residual phase is Theta_N(a,w,k) = product_i omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i * q^Lambda_N(a,w,k), Lambda_N=sum_(all ordinary vertices v) gamma_v delta_v +d sum_(all cups/caps b) delta_b. (6) The epsilon_i in the first line is the recorded half-twist sign, whereas epsilon_n in (4) is a physical-coordinate slope. Their roles are distinct. Although individual terms in Lambda_N may be half-integral, Lambda_N itself is an INTEGER. Modulo two, every gamma_n is d, and every physical matching total occurs at two vertices. There are an even number of cup/cap totals. Hence sum_n gamma_n T_n =0 modulo 2, Lambda_N=sum_n gamma_n B_n-(1/2)sum_n gamma_n T_n in Z. (7) Thus (6) uses the original q itself, unambiguously at both level parities. No new half-character choice has been introduced. The original omega factors retain their already-specified root convention. ## 3. The resulting exact shared quadratic sum The original complete-circle source is exactly A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(S_N) product_i[omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i B_N(a_i,w_i)] *q^Lambda_N(a,w,k) *product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). (8) For a fixed recorded Morse graph, every B_n is affine in the matching variables w_i and d, obtained by the literal propagation u_next=T_n-u. Equation (6) is therefore an explicit quadratic polynomial in (a,w,k,d), restricted to the actual shared lattice. In particular the absolute values |w_i| in the positive amplitudes do not appear in this residual polynomial. The retained omega factors add their original quadratic channel phases. For an unmarked cycle, writing its new integer base coordinate as x'=x+h changes Lambda_N by -h m_c, where m_c is its total Fourier frequency. On the retained congruence m_c=0 modulo 2N this leaves q^Lambda_N unchanged. On the marked cycle the base coordinate is fixed as the SECOND original marked coordinate; its one-unit charge must not be discarded in making a similar reparametrization. This exact simplification preserves the positive upper comparison. It also isolates what that comparison removes: the bilinear interaction between the Fourier labels gamma_v and the actual centered affine offsets delta_v. In an interior coefficient chart the normalized logarithmic phase is N^-1 log(q^Lambda_N)=i pi Lambda_N/N^2. Its derivative with respect to lambda_v=k_v/N is 2pi i delta_v/N, precisely the real-center data in [the radial reconstruction obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md). No equality of exponential rates, geometric maximum, holomorphic coefficient-index continuation, or contributing cycle follows from the quadratic form alone. Audit: [original paired phases and full centered cycle convolutions](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_centered_fourier_phase.py). The result is an exact phase identity, not an assertion of a contributing saddle or equality of exponential rates.

title: A common head chart for the original charged Ward currents
status: Common charged head lattice and actual meromorphic Ward currents
text: # A common head chart for the original charged Ward currents 30 October 2026. This makes the off-diagonal Ward construction on a specified tensor source explicit before its finite head sums. The charge-zero and neighboring charge-one bands use one primitive head lattice. Cutting a spanning tree reduces the proof to the independent-head identities of the actual tensors. Reclosing the auxiliary cuts gives explicit difference currents. The original support cycles and their endpoint differences remain part of the result; a common affine chart does not make those cycles equal. ## 1. Typed incidence equations and their component obstruction Fix one channel assignment in the original generic source, including the full generic channel expansion of every routed R and R inverse. Keep all small and large partners, scalar denominators, physical turns and ordinary caps. Intermediate scalar poles are treated meromorphically before root specialization; to take a finite normal one first clears their known finite pole order and retains the required higher Taylor coefficients. No root projector replaces this generic expansion. Each wire e carries its fixed integral highest weight L_e and an actual head h_e. At a typed vertex the K equation is sum_out h_e-sum_in h_e =(sum_out L_e-sum_in L_e)/2. (1) These are ordinary signed INCIDENCE equations. A contracted wire is an output at one end and an input at the other. Cups and caps are vertices, not an unrecorded change of orientation. Their constants are respectively L and -L. At W:V_(2a)->V_d tensor V_d the constant is d-a; the dual has the opposite constant. Thus every constant in (1) is an integer in the actual source. Delete the original exposed cut and the routed first-head cut. For their band delta put the first input/output heads a,a+delta and the second input/output heads l,l+delta. Let B be the incidence matrix of the remaining INTERNAL graph. Its equation is B h=b(a,l)+delta q. (2) The signs of q come from the literal four port orientations. They are opposite unit charges at the two shifted boundary ends; they are not an assigned independent color. Integer degree conservation is retained, without reduction modulo N. Check connectedness after THESE cuts on the actual typed graph. For a connected graph the only incidence relation is the sum of its rows, and the source makes the right side of (2) have sum zero. A spanning tree therefore gives an integer-affine solution for arbitrary complex a,l,delta. With x the heads on the non-tree edges, h=h_*(a,l)+delta w+A x, (3) where h_* and w have zero non-tree coordinates, w is the signed unit tree path for q, and A is the integral fundamental-cycle basis. The non-tree rows of A are the identity. All three bands delta=0,1,-1 therefore have the SAME primitive free coordinates x. No division by a quantum number or passage to an index-N cover occurs. The internal CURRENT terms also have a specified chart: place the compensating charge on the auxiliary edge carrying the generator, instead of on the second actual cut, and use its signed unit tree path w_e in place of w. Its non-tree coordinates are again zero. Thus all possible placements have the same h_* and A and differ only by their recorded integral charge-path offsets. We do not mistake a charged intermediate tensor for a zero-band density. For a disconnected graph the exact criterion is zero total charge in EACH component. Components containing neither cut are retained as their original scalar factors. If a charged right side fails the component criterion, its affine band has no original states; one must not invent a path joining those components. If the component conditions constrain a,l, keep those original affine strata rather than asserting a two-dimensional chart. On a geometric two-position chart the required connected deleted graph is the explicit criterion in the [two-cut construction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). For a chosen route U the graph is checked after its actual expansion; connectedness of a different uncut diagram is not a substitute. The physical inequalities 0<=h_e<=L_e remain separate from (3). In particular a dimension-one channel can give a thin or empty physical support even though the incidence graph is connected. ## 2. The specified meromorphic bands and local identities Use the actual large finite white polynomial and the specified moving-period factorial, with d and every L_e fixed as zeta varies. The independent-head W identities, proved in [the source Ward calculation](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md), are polynomial identities, not equalities only on root samples. Its cup/cap equations follow from the same exact unit-step factorial recurrence. They apply meromorphically also to fixed L_e>=N: the finite scalar factorial can then have a root zero and its pole is retained as just specified. Integer-affine source characters are kept; their unit-step multipliers are the actual recorded ones. One may instead keep an original R as a four-port vertex only when using its specified literal factorial continuation. Its exact independent-variable Ward ratios are those of the [original crossing currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md). This is a second permitted primitive presentation, not an assertion that two different off-grid presentations coincide merely because their physical matrices agree. The full spectral W/cup presentation above already suffices for the routed source. In (3), let s_delta(a,l,x) be the product of these actual factors with the indicated band charge, BEFORE applying the exposed coherent or root functional. It includes the fixed scalar, turn and peripheral characters of that convention; any extra generic boundary row must be separately specified and transported covariantly. No bare root mark is moved through this generic calculation. On the allowed physical lattice its original finite period is the actual coefficient of C(E_(l+delta,l)) from first input a to output a+delta. The zero band gives J_(a,l). For the next displayed interior identity use UNTRUNCATED analytic coefficients f(y)=1-Q^(y+1), k(y)=zeta^(d-2y), gamma(y)=zeta[Q^(y-N)-1]=e(y)/k(y). (4) For example f(d)=1-Q^N here, whereas the finite matrix arrow f_d is zero. The distinction is indispensable at a genuine quantum normal. The physical endpoint will be restored by its source cycle, not by substituting a root simplification in (4). ## 3. The tree construction of the common difference currents In addition to the two actual cuts, cut each non-tree edge of the internal graph. What remains is a typed TREE with auxiliary pairs of boundary heads. Its internal heads are uniquely determined by its boundary heads and (1). Its tensor entry is consequently a literal product of the specified factors, with no internal head sum. Propagating the original Hopf generator through this tree using the local identities proves its meromorphic Ward identity. Every coproduct prefix K factor and every ordered dual map stays in that propagation. Now identify the two auxiliary heads of edge e with its common coordinate x_e, using the original identity contraction. The two insertions on this cut give a discrete product rule. With their ACTUAL coefficient and tensor factors denoted j,c, it is j T_e c-(T_e^-1 j)c =(T_e-I)[(T_e^-1 j)c], (5) where T_e shifts x_e by one. The shift acts on the WHOLE indicated product, including its insertion and all prefix characters. A reverse shift is put in this form by (T_e^-1-I)u=-(T_e-I)T_e^-1 u. These are actual array translations, not new single-port matrix actions. This specifies the current algorithm: cut the stated tree, propagate the original generator in its original tensor order, and for each auxiliary cut collect the literal product on the right of (5), with its sign. Tree edges cancel pointwise. Each non-tree edge gives its own current j_(F,e) or j_(E,e). Equivalently the charge paths for the two placements of its insertion differ by exactly its fundamental cycle, which is x_e->x_e+1 in (3). This proves that the construction uses the same head chart, rather than silently comparing different charge lattices. The currents are finite sums of specified source products and shifts, not solutions chosen by interpolation. At the two remaining cuts the result is the explicit interior band identity f(l)s_+(a,l,x)-f(l-1)s_+(a,l-1,x) -f(a)[s_0(a,l,x)-s_0(a+1,l,x)] =sum_e (T_e-I)j_(F,e), (6) gamma(l)s_-(a,l,x)-gamma(l+1)s_-(a,l+1,x) -gamma(a)[s_0(a,l,x)-s_0(a-1,l,x)] =sum_e (T_e-I)j_(E,e). (7) The boundary head changes do not shift x: the latter are the literal heads of the fixed internal non-tree edges. All tree heads do change by their exact affine formulas in (3). Equations (6),(7) are meromorphic identities in independent complex a,l,x and generic zeta on every regular source chart, and hence after clearing their denominators. All genuine quantum derivatives are retained. Their signs can also be checked directly at the finite matrix boundary. For a diagonal C(E_ll), ad_F has its (a+1,a) entry f_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a+1,l)]; C(ad_F E_ll) has the other two terms in (6). For ad_E the (a-1,a) entry is gamma_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a-1,l)], and C(ad_E E_ll) has the other two terms in (7). The interior construction proves these same equations modulo the displayed actual internal currents BEFORE finite contraction. ## 4. An explicit two-crossing interior current Here is a source-level calculation with an internal cycle. Let r(a,b,k) be the literal positive crossing coefficient, sending (a,b) to (b+k,a-k), and write K(y)=x Q^-y, f(y)=1-Q^(y+1). Retain its common full Cartan scalar. For two consecutive crossings take external target c+d=a+b+1 and internal transfer k. Put T1=f(a) r(a+1,b,k) r(b+k,a+1-k,c-a-1+k), T2=K(a)^-1 f(b) r(a,b+1,k) r(b+1+k,a-k,c-a+k), T3=f(c-1) r(a,b,k) r(b+k,a-k,c-a-1+k), T4=K(c)^-1 f(d-1) r(a,b,k) r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k). Then for S_k:k->k+1 the exact independent-head equation is T1+T2-T3-T4=(S_k-I)J_F, J_F=r(b+k,a-k+1,c-a+k-1) *[K(a)^-1 f(b)r(a,b+1,k-1) -f(b+k-1)r(a,b,k-1)]. (8) Apply the first crossing's literal F identity at k and the second one at k, keeping the middle insertion. Their shared middle terms cancel except that the first-head middle insertion is evaluated at k and k+1. This gives (8) with its displayed sign. It is not an identity obtained by summing a finite row. The source's proper ratios verify it rationally in independent Q,x,Q^a,Q^b,Q^c,Q^k. For the E calculation use c+d=a+b-1 and the actual analytic e(y)=q^-1[x^-1-Q x Q^-y]. The four boundary terms are U1=K(b)e(a)r(a-1,b,k)r(b+k,a-1-k,c-a+k+1), U2=e(b)r(a,b-1,k)r(b-1+k,a-k,c-a+k), U3=K(d)e(c+1)r(a,b,k)r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k+1), U4=e(d+1)r(a,b,k)r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k). Its exact current is U1+U2-U3-U4=(S_k-I)J_E, J_E=r(b+k-1,a-k,c-a+k) *[K(a-k)e(b+k)r(a,b,k)-e(b)r(a,b-1,k)]. (8a) The middle first-input insertion now appears at k+1 in the first local equation and at k in the second. This proves (8a), including the displayed K prefix and its sign. Both identities keep the same two original crossing scalars on their two sides. The coefficients in (8) are interior functions. Its physical finite support and truncated endpoint arrows must still be retained when it is summed. In particular a generic f(d) is not set to zero as a meromorphic function merely because the physical matrix has no arrow there. ## 5. Original period chains, endpoints and the remaining global step For every charged band keep its original support polytope in (3) and its ordered product-cotangent tori Gamma_delta. These supports are different at neighboring bands and at adjacent a,l. A constant forbidden polar stratum remains its original zero state. When a separately proved source-null torus is added, its proof and ordered residue convention are retained. Equations (6),(7) may be integrated against any common regular test cycle. To replace the resulting band periods by the original ones, keep the differences between each Gamma_delta and that test cycle. For every internal current its translated-cycle correction is exactly integral_Gamma c w(T_e-I)j =integral_Gamma c(T_e^-1 w-w)j +integral_(Gamma+e-Gamma)c(T_e^-1 w)j, c=product_i pi cot(pi x_i). (9) The source normalization is (2pi i)^(-dim x). A chain filling the last cycle difference contributes ALL its crossed source residues and its remaining ends. Coincident cotangent/source poles require their actual finite parts and complement derivatives. The specified moving-P factorial and fixed highest weights remain in this process. No periodicity of the summand identifies the support cycles. On the original finite arrays the actual endpoint arrows and support rules recover the already proved [braided coherent flux](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md). Pairing the first head with beta_a requires only its exact finite sum; no new meromorphic interpolation of beta is used. The first-head and second-head ends of a selected finite window remain the interval terms in that theorem. The individual meromorphic continuations of an outside-head term are not set to zero; its original source cycle is empty, and transport out of that source domain is accounted for by these chain differences. Thus the local meromorphic Ward equation and its actual charged source lattice are now specified together. This still does not identify the original cycle with a geometric descending cycle or compute the coefficient of the framing-diagonal residue. The stationary pushforward must carry the currents (6),(7) and the explicit chain differences (9), including all resonant characters and generic normals. A zero closed finite flux alone cannot make that relative coefficient nonzero. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current_results.json) check the actual expanded two- through five-bridge plat graphs, including routed inverse pairs and all fixed channel weight types: 92 primitive cycles, 196 integral charge paths, and the disconnected component test. The two composed currents (8),(8a) are verified rationally in independent head exponentials. A separate comparison with the original generic crossing matrices checks 539 value/first-jet entries, including their full Cartan scalar, and seven nonzero untruncated endpoint-normal defects. These checks do not establish equality of the different charged support cycles or a geometric-cycle coefficient. The reduction requires the routed graph to be connected, the primitive chart to be fixed, and the endpoint divisors to be retained. It does not identify the charged cycles or a geometric period.

title: A positive Fourier partition with the original shared constraints
status: Exact shared positive partition; upper bound
text: # A positive Fourier partition with the original shared constraints 30 October 2026. The exact shared-cycle compiler admits a fully positive coefficient comparison whose scalar weight is explicit in the original source normalization. Every matching label, integral Kirchhoff equation and physical-cycle Fourier congruence is retained. This is an upper bound for the original complete-circle source, not a volume equality or a noncancellation theorem. ## 1. Original endpoint scalars, including the high-degree adapter Use the notation and recorded physical-port orders of [the exact shared-cycle compiler](actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md). Thus q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, s_j=product_(h=1)^j 2sin(pi h/N), 0<=a<=floor(d/2), r=a+w, |w|<=a. The physical total and its low adapter are T=d+w, t=d-|w|. Write c_W=W_a(b,T-b;r), b=max(0,T-d), for the actual first endpoint of the original Clebsch column. Then |c_W|=s_a/(s_|w| s_(a-|w|)). (1) Here is a proof retaining the normalization. If r<=a, the endpoint has first physical index zero. In the original coproduct Delta F=F tensor 1+K^-1 tensor F, only its second summand can reach that endpoint from the highest column. Dividing by the original ordinary-channel descendant factors gives, with F_j=(Q;Q)_j, c_W=q^(-dr) F_(d-a+r)/(F_(d-a)F_r). (2) The highest endpoint is one. Taking absolute values and using s_(d-j)=N/s_j proves (1) when w<=0. For the other half use the ACTUAL Chevalley maps J_L |u> = q^(-(L+1)u) |L-u>, S=P(J_d tensor J_d). For the balanced source generators, J_L exchanges F and Ecal and exchanges K and K^-1. The flip in S consequently gives S Delta F=Delta Ecal S and S Delta Ecal=Delta F S. In the original generic Clebsch image, uniqueness of its highest vector gives S W_a=kappa W_a J_(2a). This is a rational generic identity, then specialized; it does not assume semisimplicity at the root. Squaring it yields kappa^2=q^(-2Nd+2a(2a+1)). (3) The original W column and its Chevalley image have nonzero finite highest endpoints at the root, so the identity specializes there; alternatively (3) already makes any scalar singularity removable. All coefficients of the two J maps and kappa have modulus one at the root. The low endpoint (0,t) maps to the HIGH endpoint (d-t,d), exactly the endpoint used in the compiler. Thus its modulus is unchanged under r->2a-r. This proves (1) for both halves and both level parities. The original white map is pi_a(r;u,v)=G_(a,r)^-1 conjugate(W_a(v,u;r)), G_(a,r)=s_(2a)/(s_r s_(2a-r))>0. The normalized physical column has unit-modulus final endpoint, so its first-endpoint scalar satisfies |c_pi|=|c_W|/G_(a,r). (4) Both physical vertices have the same t and a. Their positive Fourier polynomials are normalized by c_(t,a) from the compiler, with |c_(t,a)|=1/s_a. Finally retain the actual complete-circle weight h0_a=k_a N s_(2a)/s_a^2, k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. Equations (1)--(4) give the exact positive scalar B_N(a,w) :=h0_a |c_W c_pi c_(t,a)^2| =k_a N s_(a+|w|) /(s_a^2 s_|w|^2 s_(a-|w|)). (5) There is no omitted exponential row, face or ordinary-channel metric in (5). The original physical cups have modulus N and ordinary caps modulus 1/N. Their numbers agree in the closed Morse diagram, so those moduli cancel globally. The original marked cap is handled by the exact charged-cap ratio in the compiler, rather than included in this cancellation. ## 2. The shared state space and all Fourier congruences Let R be the number of original matching circles and C the number of restored physical cycles. Collapse those cycles to the graph Gamma, orienting each matching edge from its pi cycle to its W cycle. A shared state consists of a_i in {0,...,floor(d/2)}, w_i in {-a_i,...,a_i}, div_Gamma w=0, k_v in {0,...,a_i} at EACH of the two ends v of i. Set t_i=d-|w_i|. On a fixed physical cycle, propagate its actual indices as literal affine functions of one starting coordinate x. Let epsilon_v in {+1,-1} be the slope of the recorded FIRST physical coordinate at vertex v, and epsilon_b the same slope at a physical cup or restored cap b. The total character is m_c(a,k)=sum_(v on c) epsilon_v(d-2a_i+2k_v) +d sum_(b on c) epsilon_b. (6) The actual bipartite cycle proof shows m_c is always even. All affine offsets, high-degree shifts and the terms -t_i k_v are retained in the remaining coefficient phase. They do not affect (6). Put b_c=0 except b_(c_*)=1 on the marked cycle, whose variable is the SECOND marked coordinate. Retain EVERY equation m_c(a,k)=2b_c modulo 2N. (7) Write S_N for this finite state space: the capacities, exact Kirchhoff equations, and all congruences (7), jointly. There are at most N^(4R) states: N choices for each a_i and each w_i, and N choices for each of the 2R coefficient indices. Constraints can only decrease this bound.
