No variables on separate vertices or cycles have been optimized independently. ## 3. Exact phase-bearing sum and one Cauchy inequality For a state in S_N, let Theta_N(a,w,k) be the phase left by the EXACT compiler after removing the positive factors (5) and the positive coefficients p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). Its modulus is one. This definition is explicit: multiply the original endpoint phases, c_(t_i,a_i), cup/cap monomials, recorded half-twist omega phases, and the affine-offset terms in compiler equation (7), then divide by their moduli. The global q^(-d^2) marked phase is written separately below. All these factors are nonzero; no arbitrary phase or framing normalization is introduced. The original complete-circle source is therefore EXACTLY A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(S_N) Theta_N(a,w,k) product_i B_N(a_i,w_i) product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). (8) Define the fully positive shared coefficient partition Z_F(N)=sum_(S_N) product_i B_N(a_i,w_i)^2 product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v)^2. (9) ONE finite Cauchy inequality applied to the full sum (8) gives |A_(D,N)|^2 <= N^(4R+2C-2) Z_F(N). (10) The sharper factor |S_N| N^(2C-2) is equally valid. If S_N is empty, both sides of (8) vanish and (10) is immediate. The half-twist phases disappear only in (9),(10); they remain in the exact source (8). In particular, (9) retains the marked charge, all other cycle charges and the same matching magnetic label at both ends of every edge. Dropping these restrictions would give a different, generally weaker comparison problem. ## 4. Its local variational interface and its limit For a fixed diagram, the loss in (10) is polynomial in N. The local positive coefficients in (9) are precisely those in [the proved coefficient variational theorem](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md), with complete-channel parameters tau=t_i/N and xi=a_i/N. Its interior coefficient action may therefore be used in this JOINT constrained partition, with the original scalar (5). Its theorem does not supply uniform boundary asymptotics where these parameters or k_v/N approach the boundary. For clarity, the exact finite cycle charge also controls the limiting local momentum. Set lambda_v=k_v/N, xi_i=a_i/N and Y_v^*=exp[2pi i(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i)]. This is the selected radial coefficient saddle momentum on the interior parameter domain of that theorem. Since q^(d-2a_i+2k_v)=q^-1 Y_v^*, equations (6),(7) give EXACTLY product_(v on c) (Y_v^*)^epsilon_v (-1)^(sum_(b on c) epsilon_b) =Q^(E_c/2+b_c), E_c=sum_(v on c)epsilon_v+sum_(b on c)epsilon_b in 2Z. (11) The finite pivotal correction and original marked charge have not been dropped. Equation (11) is a phase constraint supplied by the Fourier extraction; it is not yet a proof of all marked complex gluing equations. In particular, the positive partition can lose cancellation between its states, and a constrained maximum alone need not supply a contributing original cycle. Neither equality in exponential rate in (10) nor identification of the constrained maximum with hyperbolic volume is asserted. Audit: [original endpoint norms and shared coefficient partition](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.py). The exact constrained coefficient partition does not establish noncancellation or a volume statement.

title: The actual matching source as shared cycle Fourier periods
status: Exact shared flows and marked Fourier charge
text: # The actual matching source as shared cycle Fourier periods 30 October 2026. Fixing the matching magnetic labels reduces every physical component of the original complete-circle source to a one-variable cycle or marked path. The matching magnetic labels are bounded integral Kirchhoff flows. The exact unused-node zeros permit a full N-node Fourier sum, with literal affine lifts and no wrapping of the physical indices. The actual cups and caps cancel the half-character parity at BOTH level parities. The original mark selects a specified Fourier charge. This supplies a joint positive comparison energy of coherent cycle periods. It does not identify that energy's maximum with hyperbolic volume or prove survival of the original summed contribution. ## 1. Freeze the actual matching labels, not the physical wires Use the original complete-circle source of [the full matching-graph theorem](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). Put q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2). At circle i retain its folded label a_i and its ordinary matching magnetic index r_i: 0<=a_i<=M, 0<=r_i<=2a_i, W_(a_i) pi_(a_i)=sum_(r_i) W_(a_i)[r_i] pi_(a_i)[r_i]. All original white maps, including their reversal and positive ordinary channel metric, are the actual pi maps. No paired norm pi_a W_a is inverted. The original circle multiplier is still h0_a omega_a^epsilon, as in the full source theorem. After these indices are fixed, every W or pi vertex has two physical ports. Its only support condition is the EXACT integer equation u+v=T_i=d-a_i+r_i. (1) Every physical cup or ordinary cap has support u+v=d. Straight segments identify their endpoint indices. Thus the physical graph is a disjoint union of cycles. The one original unrestricted mark cuts its cycle into a path with a dense endpoint functional. The matching labels are still shared by their two incident vertices; they have not been maximized or summed independently. At the root the original physical cup, cap, and mark are pV(u,d-u)=N q^(-d^2) q^(du), ellV(u,d-u)=N^-1 q^(du), mark(u,v)=N^-2 q^(dv). (2) These are the given source tensors, in their recorded order. The last row is unrestricted; it is not an invariant cap substituted for the physical mark. Any exterior framing line remains the one already recorded for the original invariant. Let F_c(a,r) denote the coherent physical contraction of component c, with every actual local scalar in it. The source is EXACTLY A_(D,N)=sum_(a,r) product_i[h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] product_c F_c(a,r). (3) This is the root source identity itself. Its circle normals are already retained in h0_a pi_a, and its physical mark remains (2). It is not obtained by differentiating a truncated root formula. ## 2. Every fixed physical vertex has the same finite continuation For a vertex with (a,r), define T=d-a+r, t=min(T,2d-T), b=max(0,T-d). Then d-a<=t<=d. In its actual first physical coordinate u its nonzero entries have the form V(u,T-u)=c_V f_(t,a)(u-b), (4) where c_V is the ACTUAL endpoint entry V(b,T-b), and f_(t,a)(0)=1. For W, this follows by normalizing its physical column and using the original root partner identity. The high-degree block is the actual translated low block, not a freely changed framing. For pi, the exact relation pi_a(r;u,v)=G_(a,r)^-1 conjugate(W_a(v,u;r)) and the root column reflection f_(t,a)(t-y)=f_(t,a)(t) conjugate(f_(t,a)(y)) give (4), with its own actual endpoint c_V. The endpoint has modulus one before the W/metric scalar. Both local maps therefore use the same normalized finite f; their different constants are retained. The [literal magnetic polynomial](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md) gives a degree-a polynomial G_(t,a) satisfying f_(t,a)(y)=q^[(d-2a)y] G_(t,a)(Q^y), G_(t,a)(q^t z)=c_(t,a) P_(t,a)(z), P_(t,a)(z)=sum_(k=0)^a p_(t,a,k) z^k, p_(t,a,k)>0, c_(t,a)=q^[a(t+a-d)]/(Q;Q)_a. (5) For a=0 the polynomial is one. Every power in (5) has its literal specified exponent. In particular this is a finite continuation at ALL integer y, including values outside the physical range. Its unused-node zeros are G_(t,a)(Q^y)=0, t+1<=y<=d. (6) The positivity and zeros in (5),(6) were proved from the original coproduct. They are not inferred from a Fourier fit to samples. Equivalently, each physical vertex in (4) has the finite expansion V(u,T-u)=c_V c_(t,a) sum_(k=0)^a p_(t,a,k) q^[(d-2a+2k)(u-b)-tk]. (7) The scalar and the t-dependent phase in (7) must both be retained. Only the p coefficients are declared positive. ## 3. The first-failure zero lemma permits a full grid Choose a starting physical leg with value x in {0,...,d}. Along an ordinary vertex the other leg is T-x; at a cup or cap it is d-x. Straight intervals preserve the value. Hence all succeeding leg indices are literal affine functions u_e=epsilon_e x+b_e, epsilon_e in {1,-1}, b_e integer. (8) No modulo-N reduction is made in (8). The admissible x originally form an integer interval, with the final cycle closure imposed. Nevertheless the product of the continued factors (7) is zero at every x outside that interval. To prove this, take the FIRST vertex where a legal incoming index u in [0,d] would produce an illegal outgoing index. Cups and caps cannot cause that failure. If T=t<=d, it means u>t. If the incoming port is the first port, the polynomial argument is u in the unused range of (6). If it is the second port, the argument is t-u<0; its residue modulo N lies in {t+1,...,d}, again a zero of G. If T=2d-t>d, failure means u<T-d. On the first port the normalized argument is u-(T-d)<0, whose residue modulo N is in {t+1,...,d}. On the second port it is d-u, directly in that unused range. The same zeros hold for the actual white dual by (4), or directly by conjugating its reversed column. Thus that first illegal vertex has zero continued coefficient. Later affine indices need not be repaired; all later finite exponential polynomials remain defined. Therefore the cycle or path variable may be summed over ALL x=0,...,d. This lemma does not make f periodic: at even levels it is antiperiodic under y->y+N. Literal exponents in (7),(8) avoid losing precisely those signs. For an unmarked cycle the final value is epsilon x+B. Its exact closure may be replaced by delta_N((epsilon-1)x+B). (9) Indeed, whenever the product is nonzero all propagated leg values are in [0,d], so congruence of the final and initial values implies their equality. There is no surviving false winding state. At the marked component the final and initial values are instead inserted in the original dense row in (2); no closure delta is imposed. ## 4. Integral Kirchhoff flow and the actual mark Restore the ordinary cap only for the purpose of recording the physical graph. Its nodes have a canonical bipartition: W and cup nodes have two outgoing ports; pi and cap nodes have two incoming ports. Every original straight physical interval joins opposite types. Each physical cycle therefore has an EVEN number of nodes, including its cups and caps. Contracting these bivalent cup/cap nodes prematurely would hide this parity statement. Collapse every physical cycle to a vertex of a graph Gamma, and orient matching edge i from its pi cycle to its W cycle. Set w_i=r_i-a_i, -a_i<=w_i<=a_i. (10) An ordinary physical cycle closes if and only if its signed alternating sum of total degrees is zero. With the bipartition just specified, that defect is B_c=sum_(W on c)(d-a_i+r_i)-sum_(pi on c)(d-a_i+r_i) +d(#cups on c-#caps on c) =sum_(W on c) w_i-sum_(pi on c) w_i =(div_Gamma w)_c. (11) All d terms cancel because the two bipartite classes on a cycle have equal size. Each matching edge contributes with opposite signs to its two ends, so sum_c B_c=0 identically. Nonzero unmarked cycle contractions force their EXACT defects B_c=0, not just congruence modulo N. The omitted equation on the marked cycle then follows from the others. Thus (3) can be restricted EXACTLY to the bounded integral flow space w in ker(div_Gamma:Z^R->Z^C), |w_i|<=a_i. (12) There may be further quantum cancellations inside this support. The assertion is not that every flow gives a nonzero source term. On such a flow the marked endpoints are complementary. Let x be the SECOND coordinate of the original mark, so its first coordinate is d-x. Only now compare it with the ordinary cap in (2): mark(d-x,x)/ellV(d-x,x) =N^-1 q^(-d^2) Q^(dx). (13) This is the original specified mark, not a redefinition of it. Since d=-1 modulo N, it supplies a one-unit Fourier character. If instead the first marked coordinate were called x, its charge and constant phase would have the opposite displayed convention. ## 5. The exact shared-cycle Fourier compiler Insert (7) at every W or pi vertex of a physical component, and insert the monomials (2) at its cups/caps or marked endpoint. By (8), the dependence on x in each term is a SINGLE character q^[m_c(k)x], where m_c(k) is an explicitly determined integer affine function of the LOCAL Fourier indices k_v. All remaining factors consist of the positive product product_v p_(t_v,a_v,k_v), the original scalar endpoint/cup factors, and explicit q phases depending on the SAME matching labels and Fourier indices. For an arbitrary formal cycle one could expand its closure as delta_N((epsilon-1)x+B) =N^-1 sum_(h=0)^d q^[2hB+2h(epsilon-1)x]. (14) Thus its x sum is evaluated exactly by S_N(m)=sum_(x=0)^d q^(mx) = N if m=0 mod 2N, = 0 if m even but not 0 mod 2N, = 2/(1-q^m) if m odd. (15) For the ACTUAL source the odd case in (15) disappears for a proved reason. Every W/pi node has carrier parity d-2a=d modulo 2; every cup/cap and the dense mark has carrier parity d as well. The sign of the affine coordinate does not change that parity. Since the restored component has an even number of nodes, its total frequency m_c(k) is even for every Fourier tuple, at both level parities. The marked path has one fewer ordinary node and the mark supplies the last carrier. Thus the same conclusion holds before replacing the mark by its charged cap. The terms 2k and the closure terms in (14) do not alter the parity. Omitting a pivotal cup/cap carrier would destroy this argument. On a flow (12), let L_c(X) be the finite Laurent polynomial obtained by multiplying the ACTUAL continued ordinary vertex and cup/cap factors on c, with X=Q^x. It exists by this even-frequency result. Use the second marked coordinate for the variable on the marked cycle c_*. Let [X^b]_N denote cyclic coefficient extraction modulo X^N-1, summing every Laurent coefficient of exponent b modulo N. The full-grid lemma and (13)--(15) give A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(a,w:div w=0, |w_i|<=a_i) product_i[h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] *[X_(c_*)^1]_N L_(c_*)(X_(c_*)) *product_(c!=c_*) [X_c^0]_N L_c(X_c). (16) Here C is the number of restored physical cycles. Every constant endpoint, cup, cap and source phase is included in L_c. For the marked cycle the Fourier sum contributes N and the original ratio (13) contributes 1/N; this explains the exact N^(C-1), including its phase q^(-d^2). Formula (16) is valid at BOTH level parities. It can be evaluated by cyclic convolution of coefficient arrays of length N, without enumerating all Fourier tuples. In an expanded form it is a finite sum with positive local p coefficients, the original scalar factors, explicit t_v-dependent phases, integral Kirchhoff constraints (12), and coupled Fourier congruences from (16). Those phases are not removed by positivity of the p's. ## 6. A joint energy, with every shared state retained Define the explicit positive comparison Z_cycle(N)=sum_(a,r) product_i h0_(a_i)^2 product_c |F_c(a,r)|^2. (17) Each cycle period in (17) is evaluated coherently BEFORE its absolute square. The matching labels and their magnetic indices remain common to both incident vertices and to all components they connect. If there are R original circles, the number of matching states is at most N^(2R), so finite Cauchy gives |A_(D,N)|^2 <= N^(2R) Z_cycle(N). (18) The circle half-twist phases have modulus one, but are removed only in this stated upper bound, not from the exact identity (3). This is one joint comparison energy for arbitrary fixed bridge width. It neither maximizes each vertex independently nor replaces each F_c by a product of column norms. To turn (17) into the desired geometric theorem, one must still control the coherent cycle periods with their shared labels and identify the resulting constrained action, including its phases, with the actual marked gluing equations. The real Legendre action of positive Fourier coefficients alone is not such an identification. A lower bound or contributing-cycle argument for (3) is still required; (18) allows complete cancellation in the original source. Audit: [original fixed-label cycles and full Fourier kernels](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.py). The exact Fourier compiler does not assert a global energy asymptotic or noncancellation of the source.

title: A finite angle-flow certificate for matching-edge smoothing
status: Sufficient angle-flow criterion for a smoothing rate gap
text: # A finite angle-flow certificate for matching-edge smoothing 30 October 2026. This note gives a sufficient, source-compatible strict capacity comparison after replacing ONE untwisted crossing-circle operator by L_1=I. It is not a theorem that every proper small-color subset has an exponential gap. In particular the finite test below has not been proved to follow from the labeled right-angled certificate for every matching edge. ## 1. Literal smoothing and the capacity being compared Start with the connected original marked source and labeled geometric certificate of the [complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Let one matching edge have its two actual ordered triangles (x,b,y), (x,c,y). Replacing its untwisted operator by L_1=I deletes these two triangles and identifies the two middle faces b,c. This is the literal identity on the two physical strands, with their original order. It is not an evaluation of the old source at unrelated b,c. Require for this lemma: * the resulting projection is connected; * the original two marked faces remain distinct; * b,c,x are distinct unmarked faces, and y is distinct from them (y may be a marked face); * all remaining incidences are the actual ones after this smoothing. No positive polyhedron for the smoothed graph is assumed. The [exact marked face coefficient](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md) still defines its complete source, including repeated incidences or bigons. A disconnected source, a merged pair of marked faces, and a retained half twist at the deleted port require separate treatment. They are not discarded or renormalized here. Write F(l_0,l_1,l_2) for the exact maximal-fold determinant rate from [the absolute source normalization](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md), section 6. It has logarithmic homogeneity one half. Set the two marked face variables to zero, and use one positive variable for every other face, with one common scale fixed. The smoothed capacity is Phi_sm = inf_l [sum_(remaining triangles t) F(l_t) -sum_(smoothed finite faces f) log l_f]. (1) Assume this infimum is attained at finite positive shared radii l. In particular the split labels b,c both have the SAME radius z>0. This is an explicit regularity hypothesis on the smoothed capacity; it is not supplied by the old circle packing. Let Phi_old denote the original packing evaluation, already proved to equal Vol(Y_original)/(2pi). ## 2. Angle duality with its absolute normalization For theta_j>=0 and sum_j theta_j=pi, put V(theta)=2 sum_j [Lambda(theta_j/2) +Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin u| du. The source-normalized local identity is 2pi F(l)=max_theta [sum_j theta_j log l_j+V(theta)]. (2) A zero l_j forces theta_j=0; its product theta_j log l_j is then interpreted by continuity. To prove (2), differentiate V on the open angle simplex: partial_j V=-log tan(theta_j/2), Hess V=diag(-1/sin theta_j). Thus the objective is strictly concave, and its critical point is exactly the source angle formula theta_j=2atan(l_j/sqrt(l_0 l_1+l_1 l_2+l_2 l_0)). The absolute constant is zero by F(l,0,0)=(1/2)log l and V(pi,0,0)=0. Continuity gives the one- and two-positive-face cases. Apply (2) at the positive minimizer in (1). The radius stationarity conditions say that the corners at every smoothed finite face have sum 2pi. Hence its actual local angles theta maximize total V subject to these face sums and the triangle sums pi, and sum_t V(theta_t)=2pi Phi_sm. (3) This also proves the required dual equality without an external duality theorem: (2) bounds any feasible total entropy above by the right side of (3), and the displayed local angles attain it. Split the merged face's corners into their OLD b-side and c-side sets. Write their sums as pi+Delta and pi-Delta, respectively. This split is part of the original incidence, not an arbitrary partition. The single merged-face constraint gives their sum, not their individual values. ## 3. A finite source-incidence feasibility test A corner transfer moves angle between two allowed corners of ONE remaining triangle. It preserves its triangle sum. Fixed zero corners and fixed pi corners are excluded. The graph of allowed face transfers joins two face labels when their allowed corners occur in one such triangle, retaining the original incidences. The possible face-divergence vectors are exactly those having zero sum on each connected component of this graph. One direction follows by summing the triangle transfers. For the other, route the required balances along a spanning forest. The path construction uses only actual remaining triangles; it is not a new quantum routing of a cut. There is also an exact finite test with prescribed corner slack. Give each allowed corner a lower bound e_tf>=0. For proposed face demands d_f, put r_t=pi-(fixed row sum)-sum_f e_tf, q_f=d_f-(fixed column sum)-sum_t e_tf. Nonnegative angles with these lower bounds, triangle sums and face demands exist if and only if r_t,q_f>=0, their total sums agree, and for EVERY subset S of the split face labels, sum_(f in S) q_f <= sum_(t incident to S) r_t. (4) Here fixed corner values are first subtracted from both their row and column demands. A triangle with repeated labels is still one row. To prove (4), use a finite network with capacities r_t from the source to triangle nodes, unlimited edges to their allowed face nodes, and capacities q_f from the face nodes to the sink. A finite cut is precisely one of (4), after minimizing over its triangle nodes. Augmenting along residual paths until none remains proves the converse and constructs the angles. Real capacities follow by the usual limiting argument from rational capacities on this finite network. In particular d_b=d_c=pi and d_f=2pi elsewhere tests a balanced DEGENERATE insertion. It is stronger than the merged 2pi condition. Feasibility alone gives no volume inequality: redistribution can lose entropy. The following test includes that loss. ## 4. Quantitative strict comparison Suppose every allowed movable corner of theta lies in [sigma,pi-sigma], sigma>0. Choose two actual corner directions D_bc,D_x with zero sum in each remaining triangle and face divergences div D_bc = e_c-e_b, div D_x = e_b+e_c-2e_x. (5) They are zero at the excluded corners. Such directions exist, for example, whenever b,c,x belong to the same allowed transfer component; they can be constructed by the preceding spanning-forest rule. Their finite norms, not just their existence, enter the test. Choose 0<eta<pi and set v=Delta D_bc+eta D_x. Require ||v||_infinity <= sigma/2, G := 2V(eta,pi-eta,0)+2eta log(l_x/z) -||v||_2^2/[2sin(sigma/2)] > 0. (6) Then the exact capacity comparison is Phi_sm <= Phi_old-G/(2pi) < Phi_old. (7) Proof. The adjusted old angles theta+v have sums pi+eta at b,c, 2pi-2eta at x, and the required unchanged sums elsewhere. Insert the deleted triangles with angles (eta,pi-eta,0) in their literal orders (x,b,y),(x,c,y). This is a feasible angle assignment for the original source. The new triangles are permitted boundary points; no positive geometric realization of this assignment is presumed. At the smoothed maximizer the entropy gradient at a movable corner is -log l_f plus a constant depending only on its triangle. The two old middle-face multipliers agree. The first variation on v is therefore EXACTLY 2eta log(l_x/z): the Delta term cancels. Taylor's integral remainder and the first inequality in (6) give sum_t[V(theta_t+v_t)-V(theta_t)] >=2eta log(l_x/z)-||v||_2^2/[2sin(sigma/2)]. (8) Add the two new entropies. Formula (2), evaluated at the original packing radii, bounds the entropy of every feasible original angle assignment by 2pi Phi_old. Equations (3), (6), (8) imply (7). This comparison retains the shared variables and the actual target face sums throughout. The test is not confined to zero imbalance. Indeed 2V(eta,pi-eta,0)=4eta log(1/eta)+O(eta). At Delta=0 the left positive term dominates the linear and quadratic costs for sufficiently small eta. Once a strict test succeeds, it continues to succeed under small changes of its regular input data. This is an openness statement about the explicit finite data subject to the hypotheses; it does not assert an open family of knot diagrams, or that every certified diagram satisfies the test. ## 5. Consequence and remaining source requirement The zero patterns created by smoothing need an explicit extension of the old local upper bound. At fixed nonnegative shared radii set A=x+y and retain the exact circle B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_s(x,y). There are precisely the following cases. * If A>0, the determinant-rate proof remains valid for every b,c>=0. A single positive matrix summand uses the exact LDL product, already treated separately in that proof. Its circle derivative is log(E_b E_c/D_xy)>=0, since E_b,E_c>=A and D_xy<=A^2. Thus the fold is still an upper bound, though strictness may be lost. The newly possible case b=c=0, xy=0 has EXACTLY B_(N,a)=A^d for every label: beta_a D_a=A^a and P_s=A^s. * If A=0 and b,c>0, P_s(0,0)=0 unless s=0. Even N therefore gives zero for every channel. At odd N only a=d/2 survives, beta_a=1, and B_(N,a)=(bc)^(d/2). Its rate is (1/2)log(bc), exactly the sum of the two fold rates F(0,b,0)+F(0,c,0). * If A=0 and b=0 or c=0, every channel contribution is zero. These statements include empty determinants at a=0; when A=0 the positive-degree forced factor still kills that channel. They do not apply the old strict geometric zero-pattern theorem to a new bigon. For a literal untwisted L_1 deletion satisfying the certificate, evaluate the EXACT smoothed positive face coefficients at the shared minimizer l in (1). The preceding cases bound every remaining local circle, including its beta factor, by its fold rate. There are only polynomially many channel choices, and the multiplicities, measure and mark have polynomial cost. Hence the whole smoothed complete source has upper rate at most Phi_sm and the strict gap (7). An identically zero local case is already stronger. Half-twist phases on retained ports may be bounded in modulus for this upper bound; they are not removed from the finite identity. This does not yet prove the proper-small-subset estimate needed for external colors N-h. A genuine L_h insertion has actual tridiagonal paths of displacement at most h-1. With the original outgoing/incoming first-head convention, displacement p imposes c=Q^p b, and its clock monomials shift face targets. At marked zero faces they can be Laurent; one must extract the shifted coefficient before setting those faces to zero. Their unwrapped intervals and possible Fourier aliases must still be controlled. A signed removed port also retains its actual braid. Neither those finite-source requirements nor arbitrary degenerate or JSJ smoothing limits follow from (7). Focused audit: [finite flow and source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity_results.json). It checks 79 literal Morse box-deletion/face-identification maps; 74 exact rational Hall systems against an independent linear program (175,680 cut inequalities, including 26 infeasible systems); seven finite entropy-flow comparisons, four with nonzero imbalance; and 270 original degenerate channel factors through both parities. The entropy examples use stated combinatorial bipyramid/split incidences, not newly asserted labeled right-angled knot certificates. They audit the sufficient inequality, not its universal applicability. The attained shared-capacity and explicit finite-flow inequality hypotheses remain essential; no universal contraction or h>1 source estimate was inferred.

title: The boundary term and repeated monodromy sector of the Mellin equation
text:
# The boundary term and repeated monodromy sector of the Mellin equation 31 October 2026. The Fourier--Mellin construction packages the ordinary color invariants of a knot into a generating function. Its equation has a nonzero inhomogeneous term, determined by finitely many starting colors. That term is essential: after converting the equation to a homogeneous companion system, it provides a linear functional that detects the selected solution. For a knot with positive exponential growth of its Kashaev invariant, this homogeneous companion necessarily has at least two independent rational directions fixed by root monodromy. Thus a simple monodromy eigenvalue is not the reason its actual solution is selected. The selection also uses the prescribed source and the allowed expansion at the origin. The proof below keeps those data and explains why the Mellin and main-meridian realizations cannot be identified by merely renaming their variables. ## 1. The meridian equation and its ordinary colors Work over $\mathbb C(q)$ and set $Q=q^2$. The meridian multiplication operator $Y$ and shift $T$ satisfy \[ TY=QYT. 	ag{1} \] At level $N\ge2$, put $q_N=e^{\pi i/N}$ and $Q_N=q_N^2$. The marked meridian eigenvalue is $M=-q_Nx$, where $x$ is the exponential unrolled color parameter, and $Y=M^2$. Write $f_N(Y)$ for the actual reduced, zero-framed ADO state. Its fixed normalization is \[ f_N(1)=K_N,\qquad f_N(Q_N^r)=C_r(q_N)\quad(1\le r\le N), \qquad C_1(q)=1. 	ag{2} \] Here $K_N$ is the reduced Kashaev invariant, and $C_r(q)$ is the reduced ordinary invariant in dimension $r$. The equality at $r=N$ means $C_N(q_N)=K_N$. These are the [actual color specializations](root_orbit_pointing.md), with the [squared-meridian convention](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) retained. Choose a specified all-level annihilator, whose existence follows from the [finite cut-state construction](finite_sum_annihilator.md). After clearing its coefficient denominators and shifting its order once, write it as \[ P=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,Y)T^j,\qquad a_j\in\mathbb C[q^{\pm1},Y^{\pm1}],\qquad d\ge1,\quad a_0a_d
e0. 	ag{3} \] Its root equation holds at all sufficiently large levels. Keeping $\mathbb C(q)$ as the coefficient field avoids assuming that a chosen operator descends in its coefficients to $\mathbb C(Q)$. For every fixed positive integer $n$, apply its root equation at $Y=Q_N^n$, taking $N>n+d$. Equation (2) gives a relation among fixed ordinary colors at infinitely many distinct $q_N$. Since those colors are Laurent polynomials, rational-function rigidity proves \[ \sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,Q^n)C_{n+j}(q)=0 \qquad(n\ge1). 	ag{4} \] This is the color recurrence used below. Its coefficients, ordering, and initial colors are those of the specified knot equation. ## 2. Starting the generating series creates a nonzero source Let $A_q$ be the difference between the largest and smallest $q$ exponents in the collected Laurent monomials of $a_d(q,Y)$. Choose a fixed starting color \[ n_0\ge d+A_q+1, \qquad Z(q,X)=\sum_{n\ge n_0}C_n(q)X^n. 	ag{5} \] The series is initially formal at $X=0$. No convergence for generic $q$ is assumed. The choice of $n_0$ makes every substitution $a_d(q,Q^r)$ with $r\ge n_0-d$ nonzero. Indeed, distinct monomials $q^uY^v$ become $q^{u+2rv}$; a collision with different $v$ would require $2r\le A_q$. Monomials with the same $v$ were already collected. Let $S_Xg(X)=g(QX)$. The exact quantum-torus Fourier map is \[ \Phi(Y)=S_X,\qquad \Phi(T)=X^{-1},\qquad X^{-1}S_X=QS_XX^{-1}. 	ag{6} \] Write $a_j(q,Y)=\sum_m a_{jm}(q)Y^m$. Its ordered action on (5) is \[ A:=\Phi(P)=\sum_{j,m}a_{jm}(q)Q^{-mj}X^{-j}S_X^m, \qquad AZ=\mathcal B, 	ag{7} \] where \[ \mathcal B(q,X)= \sum_{j,m}a_{jm}(q)Q^{-mj}X^{-j} \sum_{r=n_0}^{n_0+j-1}C_r(q)Q^{mr}X^r. 	ag{8} \] To obtain (8), multiply (4) by $X^n$ and sum over $n\ge n_0$. For a term with shift $j$, the substitution $r=n+j$ leaves out exactly the colors $n_0,\ldots,n_0+j-1$. Those omitted terms are the inner sum in (8); it is empty for $j=0$. The factor $Q^{-mj}$ comes from the operator ordering in (6). The source is a Laurent polynomial in $X$, supported between $n_0-d$ and $n_0-1$. Its least coefficient is \[ [X^{n_0-d}]\mathcal B =C_{n_0}(q)a_d(q,Q^{n_0-d})
e0. 	ag{9} \] Only $j=d$ contributes to this coefficient. The second factor is nonzero by the monomial argument above, and $C_{n_0}(1)=1$ makes the first nonzero as well. Thus this finite-start construction has a nonzero source. Its least coefficient is a fixed nonzero rational function of $q$, so its specialization is nonzero at all but finitely many $q_N$. The source equation also determines the actual series uniquely in the prescribed space $X^{n_0}\mathbb C(q)[[X]]$. If a nonzero homogeneous difference had least exponent $r\ge n_0$, its image under $A$ would have a nonzero coefficient at $X^{r-d}$, namely $a_d(q,Q^{r-d})$ times that least coefficient. This is impossible. This is the [finite-start source construction](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md); it is stronger than choosing any rational solution of its root specialization. ## 3. Root rationality and the finite Fourier comparison The [actual root color-periodicity theorem](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives $C_{n+N}(q_N)=C_n(q_N)$ for all $n\ge1$, including the multiples of $N$. Consequently, for $N\ge n_0$, \[ Z_N(X):=Z(q_N,X) = rac{\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r+K_NX^N} {1-X^N} -p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}(X),\qquad p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}(X)=\sum_{r=1}^{n_0-1}C_r(q_N)X^r. 	ag{10} \] This is the rational function with the same formal expansion at zero. Where the fixed operator specializes regularly, it satisfies $A_NZ_N=\mathcal B_N$ as a rational identity. It has at most simple poles at the $N$th roots of unity, and its residue retains the original scalar: \[ \operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty}Z_N(X) rac{dX}{X}=K_N. 	ag{11} \] Indeed the fraction in (10) tends to $-K_N$ at infinity, while $p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}$ has no constant term. The full modified ADO value remains $i^{N+3}K_N/N$ at completeness; (11) does not replace its whole meridian normalization by a different one. The central coordinates explain the limit of this Fourier comparison. At a primitive level-$N$ root, write \[ U=Y^N,\quad V=T^N,\qquad U_X=X^N,\quad V_X=S_X^N. 	ag{12} \] The algebra map (6) sends them to \[ \Phi(U)=V_X,\qquad \Phi(V)=U_X^{-1}. 	ag{13} \] In the rational main-meridian realization, $T$ acts by the root shift of $Y$, so $V=1$ and $U$ varies. Its Fourier image is therefore supported on $U_X=1$, with $V_X$ variable. In the rational Mellin realization, $S_X$ acts by the root shift of $X$, so instead $V_X=1$ and $U_X$ varies. In the original coordinates this is $U=1$, with $V=X^{-N}$ variable. These are two different central divisors, meeting at $(1,1)$. An isomorphism over a fixed center cannot equate their distinct annihilator ideals. At their intersection there is a genuine finite Fourier map. Its domain is the orbit ring $\mathbb C[Y^{\pm1}]/(Y^N-1)$, equivalently the functions on the $N$ meridian root points. A rational function may be used only when it is regular at those points; the actual $f_N$ is Laurent polynomial and meets this condition. Put \[ \mathscr F_N(h)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}h(Q_N^r)X^r \quad	ext{in }\mathbb C[X]/(X^N-1). 	ag{14} \] Termwise multiplication and cyclic reindexing prove $\mathscr F_N(Yh)=S_X\mathscr F_N(h)$ and $\mathscr F_N(Th)=X^{-1}\mathscr F_N(h)$. For $h=f_N$, this produces $K_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r$. It is precisely the class of the numerator \[ (1-X^N)(Z_N+p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}) =\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r+K_NX^N. 	ag{15} \] modulo $X^N-1$. Thus the finite map compares the meridian orbit with the Mellin pole numerator. It does not evaluate $Z_N$ at a pole or identify their meridian neighborhoods. In particular it does not replace the retained normal coordinate of the [ramified Weyl fibre](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) by an ordinary orbit value. ## 4. Why the root clock cannot be lifted as a finite matrix gauge The distinction persists in the first quantum-normal direction. Vary the parameter through dual numbers by $Q=Q_N(1+\epsilon)$, $\epsilon^2=0$; the compatible half-root is $q=q_N(1+\epsilon/2)$. In the whole quantum torus, (1) implies \[ VU=Q^{N^2}UV=(1+N^2\epsilon)UV, \qquad [V,U]=N^2\epsilon UV. 	ag{16} \] Suppose a nonzero finite free matrix realization of the intersection fibre lifted through this parameter change, with both central actions reducing to identity. It would have $U=I+\epsilon E$ and $V=I+\epsilon F$, whose commutator is zero modulo $\epsilon^2$. Equation (16) instead gives $N^2\epsilon I$, a contradiction in characteristic zero. For the usual $N$-dimensional clock matrices the same obstruction follows by taking determinants in $TY=QYT$, which would require $Q^N=1$ rather than $1+N\epsilon$. This rules out lifting (14) as an ordinary finite matrix gauge through the quantum-normal direction. It does not rule out a comparison with differential normal operators or retained relative sources. The [first quantum-normal construction](first_quantum_normal_connection.md) includes a derivation because an off-root shift no longer has finite order. That derivation and its source cannot be inferred from the root Fourier matrix alone. ## 5. Positive growth forces two rational companion directions Assume now that the knot has positive exponential complete growth: \[ \liminf_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|K_N|>0. 	ag{17} \] This is supplied, for example, by the established [strict-tree](actual_conway_all_strict_tree_long_twist_volume.md) and [net-twist](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) volume theorems for their stated knot classes. The next argument only uses (17). For every coefficient in (3), form the fixed Laurent polynomial $r_i(q)=a_i(q,q^{-2i})$. If it were nonzero, it would have a finite vanishing order $
u_i$ at $q=1$, and hence $|r_i(q_N)|\ge cN^{-
u_i}$ for all large $N$. Evaluate the actual root equation at $Y=Q_N^{-i}$. When $N>d$, its $i$th term is $r_i(q_N)K_N$ and all other terms are ordinary-color values. Those values are polynomially bounded in $N$ by the [positive ordinary-color trace](regularized_kashaev_period.md). The fixed Laurent coefficients are bounded on the root torus, so this equation would bound $K_N$ polynomially as well, contradicting (17). Therefore every $r_i$ is identically zero. Laurent-polynomial division now gives the exact right factor \[ P=B(Y-1),\qquad A=\Phi(B)(S_X-1). 	ag{18} \] Indeed the $i$th coefficient of $B(Y-1)$ is $b_i(q,Y)(Q^iY-1)$. This is the [boundary-column argument](peripheral_normal_period.md), applied here to the positive growth already known. In particular $A(1)=0$. Any fixed left shift used to give $A$ nonnegative $S_X$ order is applied to its source as well and preserves this identity. In that normalization $A$ has positive $S_X$ order. Otherwise it would be multiplication by a nonzero rational function, which cannot annihilate $1$. Retain the canonical homogeneous equation of the sourced Mellin system: \[ \widehat A=(S_X-\sigma(\mathcal B)/\mathcal B)A, \qquad \sigma g(X)=g(QX). 	ag{19} \] For every sufficiently large $N$, both $1$ and $Z_N$ are rational solutions of (19). They are independent over $\mathbb C(X^N)$: if $Z_N$ were central, then $A_NZ_N=Z_NA_N(1)=0$, contradicting $\mathcal B_N
e0$. This gives two independent vectors in the monodromy eigenspace, not merely two scalar formulas. Let $\mathsf C_N$ be the forward solution companion of (19), let $Jf=(f,S_Xf,\ldots)^t$ be its finite jet vector, and set $\mathsf T_0=\mathsf C_N^{-1}S_X$, $H_0=\mathsf T_0^N$. The positive order of $A$ makes (19) have at least two companion coordinates. Both $J1$ and $JZ_N$ are fixed by $\mathsf T_0$. If these vectors were dependent over $\mathbb C(X)$, their first coordinates would force $JZ_N=Z_NJ1$. Their second coordinates would then give $S_XZ_N=Z_N$, again making $Z_N$ central. Thus \[ \dim_{\mathbb C(X)}\ker(H_0-I)\ge2, \qquad \left. rac{d}{dt}\det(tI-H_0)ight|_{t=1}=0. 	ag{20} \] The source and the companion endpoints exclude only finitely many specialization levels. Equation (20) concerns this canonical homogenization of a denominator-cleared reduced-state operator. It does not assert a Jordan block, specify the full dimension of the eigenspace, or apply to every alternative minimal operator. Nor does it contradict selection of the actual series. The extra constant solution is outside $X^{n_0}\mathbb C[[X]]$. The source equation and that starting condition still distinguish $Z$ from the larger rational solution space. At roots, the [cyclotomic quantum-jet theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) retains further source and pole-lattice data when selecting the entire rational function. ## 6. The source row still detects the selected solution Write the normalized Mellin operator as $A=\sum_{j=0}^{r}c_j(q,X)S_X^j$. Its canonical homogenization (19) has order $r+1$. On its companion vectors there is the explicit row \[ \ell= rac1{\mathcal B}(c_0,\ldots,c_r),\qquad \ell Jf=Af/\mathcal B. 	ag{21} \] Equation (19) says that this quotient is shift-invariant. In companion form, $\sigma(\ell)\mathsf C=\ell$, so at a root \[ \ell H_0=\ell,\qquad \ell J1=0,\qquad \ell JZ_N=1. 	ag{22} \] The row kills the image of $H_0-I$ but does not kill the selected vector. Therefore the natural map from the kernel to the cokernel of $H_0-I$ is nonzero on $JZ_N$. This is the [observable-source criterion](actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.md), which remains valid even though the simple-root test in (20) fails. It detects a specified direction rather than asserting semisimplicity of the entire monodromy. The algebraic boundary module explains the distinction. Before localization it is $\Delta_Y=\mathcal R_Q/\mathcal R_Q(Y-1)$, where $\mathcal R_Q$ is the quantum torus (1). Passing to rational meridian coefficients kills it because $Y-1$ becomes invertible. Its Fourier image is $\mathcal R_X/\mathcal R_X(S_X-1)$, which survives over $\mathbb C(q,X)$ as a rank-one trivial difference module. The two rational localizations thus retain different boundary data. The row (21) is an observable of the sourced Mellin presentation; it is not automatically a row for a localized main-meridian companion. The [source-symbol comparison](source_symbol_duality_and_presentation.md) also gives explicit examples where an extra homogeneous factor changes that test. What remains is a source-and-lattice comparison, not a choice of a preferred eigenvalue by its size or multiplicity. A proposed geometric realization must retain the finite-start source, the cyclotomic pole numerator, the normal derivatives, and the marked period functional through the change of polarization. The root Fourier identity proves the finite numerator comparison, while (16) explains why it does not supply the quantum-normal lift. Neither (20) nor (22) identifies a geometric factor of the classical main-meridian operator.

title: The actual Mellin source has a rigid selected quantum-normal line
text:
# The actual Mellin source has a rigid selected quantum-normal line Research theorem, 27 October 2026. For every knot, the actual bounded Fourier--Mellin source gives an observable monodromy covector which detects its selected rational root section. Its first quantum-normal symbol is therefore nonzero without a simple-root or semisimplicity hypothesis. The actual coefficientwise whole-Q lift makes that selected section horizontal for the rational kernel-to-cokernel normal operator. Together these facts exclude nonconstant central scalar multipliers compatible with the same whole operator. The retained scalar is exactly the Kashaev residue at infinity. This does not estimate that residue, identify its regulator norm, or transfer rigidity to a different meridian source object. ## 1. The specified actual source and its admissible roots Retain the [actual finite-color construction](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md): \[ Z(Q,X)=\sum_{n\ge n_0}C_n(Q)X^n,\qquad A(Q,X,S)Z=B(Q,X),\qquad Sf(X)=f(QX). 	ag{1.1} \] The coefficients \(C_n(Q)\) are the original reduced color periods, Laurent polynomial in \(Q\), with \(C_n(1)=1\). The specified fixed starting color makes \(B\) a nonzero fixed Laurent polynomial in \(X\), with rational Q-coefficients, built from finitely many actual colors. Its lowest coefficient is explicitly nonzero. The formal lattice \(X^{n_0}\mathbb Q(Q)[[X]]\) and (1.1) specify the actual series uniquely. No generic rationality of \(Z\) is assumed. Apply any fixed left S-power needed to make A's shift support \(0,\ldots,r\), and apply the same shift to B. Write \[ A=\sum_{j=0}^{r}a_jS^j,\qquad a_0a_r
e0. 	ag{1.2} \] Order zero is allowed. For all sufficiently large N, at \(\zeta=\exp(2\pi i/N)\), all coefficients required below are regular over \(E=\mathbb C(X)\), and \(a_0,a_r,B\) remain nonzero in E. Indeed each possible failure says that one of finitely many fixed nonzero rational functions of Q vanishes or has a pole. Thus only finitely many Q-values, hence finitely many levels, are excluded. An X-dependent zero or pole is retained as an element of E; it is not removed by choosing a numerical X-point. By the independently proved [actual all-color root periodicity](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md), the specialization \(Z_N=Z(\zeta,X)\) is rational. Explicitly, \[ Z_N= rac{\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}C_j(\zeta)X^j+K_NX^N}{1-X^N} -\sum_{j=1}^{n_0-1}C_j(\zeta)X^j. 	ag{1.3} \] This is equality with the same formal expansion at zero. It holds even if \(K_N=0\). The rational source equation is still \(A_NZ_N=B_N\). ## 2. An observable source quotient detects the selected symbol Use the canonical homogeneous operator attached to this source: \[ \widehat A=(S-\sigma_Q(B)/B)A,\qquad \sigma_Q f(X)=f(QX). 	ag{2.1} \] It has order \(d=r+1\), with both endpoint coefficients nonzero. Let C be its forward solution companion, so \(\sigma_Qv=Cv\) for \(v=J_df=(f,Sf,\ldots,S^rf)^t\), and put \(T=C^{-1}\sigma_Q\). There is a literal observable row \[ \ell= rac1B(a_0,\ldots,a_r),\qquad \ell J_df=Af/B. 	ag{2.2} \] The coefficient identity (2.1), with no chosen solution, implies \[ \sigma_Q(\ell)C=\ell,\qquad \ell T=\sigma_Q\circ\ell. 	ag{2.3} \] For example, the first equality says that the source quotient of any homogeneous solution of (2.1) is shift-invariant; its coefficient of the highest jet is precisely the companion relation. The second follows by right multiplication by \(C^{-1}\). At the root let \(T_0=T|_{Q=\zeta}\), \(H_0=T_0^N\), and \(v_0=J_dZ_N\in E^d\). Since \(\sigma_\zeta^N=1\), (2.3) gives \[ T_0v_0=v_0,\qquad \ell_0H_0=\ell_0,\qquad \ell_0v_0=1. 	ag{2.4} \] Set \(L_0=H_0-I\), \(K=\ker L_0\), \(\mathcal C=\operatorname{coker}L_0\), and let \(\iota:K	o\mathcal C\) be inclusion followed by quotient. The row \(\ell_0\) kills \(\operatorname{im}L_0\). Consequently \[ \ell_0\iota(v_0)=1, \qquad \iota(v_0)
e0. 	ag{2.5} \] This is a dual source certificate, not a characteristic-polynomial guess. No assertion about other eigenvalue-one Jordan blocks is needed. In fact \(p=v_0\ell_0\) is a root difference-equivariant projection onto \(Ev_0\): (2.3)--(2.4) give \(pT_0=T_0p\) and \(p^2=p\). Thus this selected line is a direct summand of the root module even if the complementary module is nonsemisimple. The quotient is observable in the original scalar state and its shifts. It is not an unused unit line adjoined to force (2.5). For another supplied original annihilator, including a left multiple, one may rebuild its finite-color source B and apply the same proof. One may not erase that source and apply the conclusion to an arbitrary homogeneous left multiple. For order zero, (1.1) itself already determines a rational function \(Z=B/a_0\) generically. The same rank-one homogenization and observable row remain valid for this selected normal statement; they assert no geometric block or additional geometric order. ## 3. The actual formal lift kills the rational normal obstruction Put \(Q=\zeta(1+\epsilon)\), \(D_X=X\partial_X\), and retain every moving argument in the specified whole companion. As in the [first quantum-normal construction](first_quantum_normal_connection.md), \[  egin{split} T(Q)^N-I&=L_0+\epsilon L_1+O(\epsilon^2),\ L_1&=H_1+NH_0D_X,\ D_N:K\longrightarrow\mathcal C,\qquad D_N(v)&=[L_1v]/N^2. 	ag{3.1} \end{split} \] Every \(C_n\) is regular at the root. Coefficientwise differentiation therefore gives an actual first lift \(Z=Z_N+\epsilon Z_1+O(\epsilon^2)\) with \(Z_1\in F=\mathbb C((X))\) and the same fixed lower X-bound. No convergence in X, uniform Q-radius, or bound on color derivatives is needed. Rational coefficients of the companion and of \(B^{-1}\) expand in \(E[[\epsilon]]\subset F[[\epsilon]]\); the orders of their X-poles may depend on the epsilon coefficient. The actual formal whole solution of (2.1) has jet \(v=v_0+\epsilon v_1+O(\epsilon^2)\), \(v_1\in F^d\), satisfying \[ L_0v_1+L_1v_0=0. 	ag{3.2} \] Both \(L_0\) and \(L_1v_0\) are over E. For a matrix over any field E and any extension F/E, \[ \operatorname{im}(L_0:F^d	o F^d)\cap E^d =\operatorname{im}(L_0:E^d	o E^d). 	ag{3.3} \] To prove it, row-reduce over E. The zero rows and the corresponding augmented consistency conditions stay zero or nonzero under field extension. Thus (3.2) implies that its right-hand side lies in the rational image, and \[ D_N(v_0)=0. 	ag{3.4} \] This proves vanishing of a rational obstruction class. It does not assert that the actual \(Z_1\), actual jet \(v_1\), or normal cut functional is rational, and does not replace them by a rational lift. The usual cyclic descent applies to K, \(\mathcal C\), and this normal map. Its constant field is \(\mathbb C(U)\), \(U=X^N\), and its symbol on that field is \(U\partial_U\,\iota\). ## 4. Whole first-normal compatibility removes central scalars Let \(c(U)\in\mathbb C(U)\), or more generally \(\mathbb C((U))\). Suppose \(c(U)v_0\) has a first-order lift for the SAME specified whole homogeneous companion (2.1). Then \[ 0=D_N(cv_0)=cD_N(v_0)+Uc'(U)\iota(v_0) =Uc'(U)\iota(v_0). 	ag{4.1} \] After scalar extension if necessary, applying the source covector (2.5) gives \(Uc'=0\). In characteristic zero, c is constant. The actual source value one or a fixed nonzero color-prefix anchor then fixes that constant to one. For all sufficiently large N a fixed anchor \(C_{n_0}(\zeta)\) is nonzero, since the fixed Laurent polynomial \(C_{n_0}\) is nonzero and has finitely many roots. There is a direct scalar check which avoids choosing a rational normal lift. For any compatible whole first-order solution W set \(h=AW/B\). Equation (2.1) says \(\sigma_Qh=h\) modulo \(\epsilon^2\). If \(W_0=c(U)Z_N\), then \(h_0=c(U)\). Iterating N times yields \[ (\sigma_Q^N-I)h=\epsilon N D_Xc(U)+O(\epsilon^2) =\epsilon N^2Uc'(U)+O(\epsilon^2)=0. 	ag{4.2} \] Thus this rigidity uses only the actual source quotient and the first whole quantum jet. It excludes a central scalar change of the selected section, not arbitrary source-kernel additions. ## 5. Actual presentations distinguish the selected criterion The actual unknot has \(C_n(Q)=1\). With start one, \(Z=X/(1-X)\), \(g=X^{-1}-1\), its Mellin source is \(gZ=1\). The canonical homogeneous operator is \((S-1)g\). After the exact gauge \(h=gf\), its selected solution is \(h=1\), with visible source row one and nonzero selected symbol. The equally actual annihilator \((S-1)^2g\) has, in h coordinates, forward companion \[ C= egin{pmatrix}0&1\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=I+J, \qquad J^2=0,\quad J
e0. \] At a level-N root, \(H_0=C^{-N}=I-NJ\). Its actual selected vector \((1,1)^t\) lies in both \(\ker(H_0-I)\) and \(\operatorname{im}(H_0-I)\), so its selected symbol vanishes. Indeed \((\sigma_Q-1)^2c(X^N)=O(\epsilon^2)\) for EVERY c. The unnecessary left factor destroys the first-normal scalar test if the observable source is forgotten. This is a diagnostic on the actual unknot, rather than a replacement knot state. Conversely, simplicity is stronger than needed. Still for the actual unknot, use the supplied original operator \((Y-1)(T-1)\) and start two. Its exact Mellin pair is \[ A=(S-1)g,\quad Z=X^2/(1-X),\quad B=(Q-1)X. \] Canonical homogenization is \((S-Q)(S-1)g\). In h coordinates its companion has distinct eigenvalues 1 and Q. At every primitive level-N root its monodromy is \(I_2\), so the eigenvalue one is double and semisimple, while the observable selected symbol is nonzero. A simple norm root is not an all-knot premise of Sections 2--4, even for canonically rebuilt nonminimal source objects. ## 6. A genuine affine nonresonance criterion and an actual input For a supplied rational affine equation \(\sigma v=C_Av+c\), its augmented monodromy has the form \[ H_{\mathrm{aug}}= egin{pmatrix}H_A&s\0&1\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{6.1} \] If \(I-H_A\) is invertible, its characteristic polynomial satisfies \[ \Delta_{\mathrm{aug}}(t)=(t-1)\det(tI-H_A),\qquad \Delta'_{\mathrm{aug}}(1)=\det(I-H_A)
e0. 	ag{6.2} \] Thus it has a simple eigenvalue one. Translation by the unique rational particular solution block-diagonalizes (6.1). This uses a genuine supplied source equation; it cannot be inferred merely from an arbitrary homogeneous root annihilator. The [actual quantum extremal-coefficient criterion](affine_quantum_a_period.md#4-a-simple-algebraic-criterion-for-nonresonance) proves \(I-H_A\) invertible whenever the homogeneous scalar operator has a unique strictly least Y-order coefficient (or unique greatest degree at infinity). Its proof already includes cyclic descent; no growing determinant or classical-symbol inference is needed. There is a concrete actual input here. The independently proved [whole figure-eight identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) and its [explicit root source operator](peripheral_normal_period.md#9-independent-operator-and-actual-state-calibration) give, at every level N, \[  egin{split} (c_-S^{-1}+c_0+c_+S)F_N&=D(Y)(3-U-U^{-1}),\ U&=Y^N,\ D&=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1),\ g_0&=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2,\ c_-&=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1),\ c_0&=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g_0,\ c_+&=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). \end{split} 	ag{6.3} \] Here \(c_0\) alone has Y-order zero, with coefficient Q; both neighbors have order two. This persists at EVERY primitive root, including level two. Hence the homogeneous order-two monodromy has no eigenvalue one. The genuine rank-three source homogenization has a simple eigenvalue one for every N over \(\mathbb C(Y)\). Its selected observable source is \(3-U-U^{-1}
e0\); one may normalize the covector by that central factor generically. This is an actual root-module statement. The known off-root finite cyclotomic calibration is not thereby the original auxiliary finite-Verma Q-lift. No assertion identifying those whole normal connections is made, and no intrinsic norm is identified with the classical geometric A-polynomial. At a special U-value where the source factor vanishes, its marked lattice must be retained instead of dividing by it. ## 7. The original period and the remaining comparison For the SAME section (1.3), \[ K_N=\operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty} Z_N(X)\,dX/X. 	ag{7.1} \] The full ideal ADO factor remains \(\eta_NK_N/N\), with its specified parity and meridian germ. Nothing in the normal argument replaces that factor by a number before cancellation or estimates the exponential growth of (7.1). The central coordinate in Sections 3--4 is X^N in the Mellin polarization. A comparison to an original meridian profile in Y^N requires an actual source/co-source map. In particular, for the earlier regularized equation \(\mathcal A R=b_N\), a meridian change of the original F acts as \[ (R,1)\longmapsto(cR+(c-1)p,1), \] rather than multiplying the full augmented section by c. It is a homogeneous source-kernel addition, so the scalar theorem above does not remove it automatically. The selected regulator norm, geometric source comparison, and asymptotic residue bound remain additional problems. The stronger [cyclotomic jet reconstruction](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) also handles arbitrary homogeneous source-kernel additions in this canonical Mellin realization. It retains the exact pole lattice and a bounded number of quantum levels of the same inhomogeneous source equation. Under those additional conditions the entire rational root function is unique, not just its selected scalar line. This remains a uniqueness theorem rather than a regulator or residue-growth estimate. [Independent proof audit and presentation certificates](source_symbol_duality_and_presentation.md). [Exact diagnostics](../experiments/audit_actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.py). [Results](../experiments/actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity_results.json).

title: Actual memory-charge clocks and first-normal transfer carries
text: # Actual memory-charge clocks and first-normal transfer carries Research theorem and exact audit, 27 October 2026. A transfer clock has an exact head/Frobenius memory-charge expression on the actual high integral color. At the root its carry vanishes. In the first quantum normal only one carry can occur on a tracked strand, and its entire correction is a bounded whole scaled-clock unit. Together with the actual quadratic first-normal R theorem, this gives a finite differential source realization of these inserted transfer clocks and their bounded moments. The root clock identity alone is a rewriting of the old position clock factorization. The additional content is its original first-normal block carry, bounded Frobenius differential degree, and canonical actual source germ. This is not yet a Gaussian two-framing current map. ## 1. The integer charges and exact operator formulas Use the actual high integral color with basis \(w_{a,s}\), \(0\le a\le r\), \(0\le s<N\). Define diagonal operators \[ Rw_{a,s}=aw_{a,s},\qquad Sw_{a,s}=sw_{a,s},\qquad J=NR+S,\qquad C=R-S=(N+1)R-J . \] Here C is a MEMORY CHARGE, not a critical-field observable. All three operators are actual finite matrices with their constant integral grading before root specialization. Track input strand 1 to output strand 2. The literal checked crossing routes are \[ R_+:(i,j)\mapsto(j+k,i-k),\qquad R_-:(i,j)\mapsto(j-k,i+k). \] Writing \(\Delta R=R_{\mathrm{out,2}}-R_{\mathrm{in,1}}\) and likewise \(\Delta C\), exact integer arithmetic gives \[ k=\Delta C-(N+1)\Delta R\quad(+),\qquad k=-\Delta C+(N+1)\Delta R\quad(-). \tag{1} \] These are identities of UNWRAPPED positions, not congruences. Let \(R_\pm(w)\) multiply each literal transfer-k coefficient by \(w^k\), with \(w\ne0\). Define the charge-twisted crossings \[ R_+^C(w)=(I\otimes w^C)R_+(w^{-C}\otimes I),\qquad R_-^C(w)=(I\otimes w^{-C})R_-(w^C\otimes I). \] Then at every generic q, \[ R_+(w)=(I\otimes w^{-(N+1)R})R_+^C(w) (w^{(N+1)R}\otimes I), \] \[ R_-(w)=(I\otimes w^{(N+1)R})R_-^C(w) (w^{-(N+1)R}\otimes I). \tag{2} \] The retained Cartan and mixed half-Cartan signs are unchanged: (2) multiplies the ACTUAL coefficients in their original order. Thus no initial diagonal projector is needed for the clock identity. A projector correlating R and S has a separate source/current role; it is not an R-invariant subspace. ## 2. Root and first-normal support sharply bound the carry Put \(\delta=1-Q^N\). By [the actual first-normal crossing theorem](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md), all transfers \(k\ge2N\) vanish modulo \(\delta^2\). For \(k<N\), the tracked head can cross at most one boundary. For a resonant \(k=N+b\), its first normal factors through \(E^{(N)}\otimes F^{(N)}\) and a root b-transfer. The latter cannot cross another head boundary: its ordinary root E or F edge would be zero. Hence \[ \Delta R=0\text{ at order zero}, \] \[ \Delta R\in\{0,-1\}\quad(+),\qquad \Delta R\in\{0,+1\}\quad(-) \quad\text{through first order}. \tag{3} \] A putative two-boundary carry has zero first-normal coefficient. The negative assertion also follows by differentiating the actual inverse crossing and its root block permutation. Denote a first-normal charge-twisted component of block shift d by \(R_{\pm,1}^{C,[d]}(w)\). Equations (1)--(3) give \[ R_{\pm}(w)=R_\pm^C(w) +\delta\,(w^{N+1}-1) R_{\pm,1}^{C,[\mp1]}(w)+O(\delta^2). \tag{4} \] The same positive carry unit appears for both recorded signs because their nonzero tracked shifts have opposite signs. For arbitrary components the exact unit is \(w^{\mp(N+1)\Delta R}\), as in (2). The interaction first normal has Frobenius PBW degree at most two. Charge twists rescale raising/lowering operators and act on head matrices; selecting a fixed block shift is its ordinary weight grading and does not raise PBW degree. Consequently the memory/carry form (4) has the SAME degree bound. The exact one-sided source dictionary of [the two-clock source](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md) turns it into an operator of differential order at most two, with the original normalized source terms retained. These q-derivatives belong to the original generic integral matrix family. Replacing its ordinary pivot by a frozen root ADO pivot before differentiating would require the previously retained route adapter. ## 3. Whole scaled clocks and finite transfer moments For the needed source r=N, the charge eigenvalues lie in \([-(N-1),N]\). Put \(w=e^{z/N}\). Then \(w^C\) and its inverse have operator norm at most \(e^{|\operatorname{Re}z|}\) in EVERY common diagonal metric. On the first-normal carry, \[ w^{N+1}=e^{z(1+1/N)}\longrightarrow e^z, \tag{5} \] with all fixed z-derivatives uniformly bounded on compact sets. No exponential normalization cost in N occurs in this carry. This is a statement about clock units, not an estimate of the whole crossing norm or the source's quantum-normal derivatives. Equation (1) also transports bounded normalized transfer moments: \[ (k/N)^h= [\Delta C/N-(1+1/N)\Delta R]^h\quad(+), \] \[ (k/N)^h= [-\Delta C/N+(1+1/N)\Delta R]^h\quad(-). \tag{6} \] Expand these finite binomials on the carry components (3). Equivalently differentiate the WHOLE identity (2) in z. Every fixed h has finitely many charge-moment/carry terms; no endless WKB expansion is needed. Unnormalized \(k^h\) retains its explicit \(N^h\). The endpoint R=N is distinct from R=0 as an integer memory. A root Q-clock cannot separate them, but the actual block clock \(Z^R\) does so in its first normal: \(D_Q Z^R|_{Q_N}=NR\). Folding these endpoints together would lose precisely the additional normal current. Zero-extended current tails and their literal cut endpoint coupons must likewise remain; no cyclic identification is made by (1)--(6). ## 4. The memory clock has an actual whole source For the canonical high-color two-flag source, write \(x=tu\) and retain its actual normalization \(U_s(q;t,u)\). The charge character is exactly \[ \Phi_{h;t,u}(w^C)= \sum_{s=0}^{N-1}H_s(h)\,w^{-s} \frac{U_s(q;tw,u)}{U_s(q;t,u)}. \tag{7} \] At the root this becomes \[ \left(\frac{1+h/w}{1+h}\right)^{N-1} \left(\frac{1+xw}{1+x}\right)^r . \tag{8} \] Away from the root the source-unit derivatives do NOT cancel for this insertion, since \(w^R\) depends on the block. They are the actual derivatives of U_s, not an arbitrary continuation of (8). Alternatively, for the normalized ordinary TRACE co-source, \(w^C=w^R\otimes w^{-S}\) has the product of the exact [dual clock lifts](dual_clock_normal_cut_source.md), in source dimensions \(r+1\) and N respectively. Tensor products, actual source permutations and their duals are transported as matrix operators. They are not pointwise products of coherent symbols. A source permutation need not have bounded norm in every coherent metric; no such assertion is used. The trace extension agrees with the original average cut on the actual conserving diagonal arrays. It is not a replacement for that average on arbitrary off-diagonal Ward matrices. ## 5. What advances beyond the old factorization At root order, (2) is algebraically equivalent to splitting a transfer into input/output POSITION clocks. By itself it introduces no independent geometric co-source. In a closed uninserted root knot, Frobenius labels are transparently transported around the component; their normalized source dependence cancels. The new source content is the first-normal carry in (3)--(4): it is an original high-color block arrow with a concrete quadratic Frobenius operator, actual source-unit derivatives, and a whole bounded scaled-clock factor. It can be compared to the second current without guessing an abstract Borel isomorphism or discarding an unwrapped carry. A complete current map must still transport the inserted source/coupon and its endpoints through the whole word, including its contravariant star action. This theorem does not identify the resulting insertion with the independent geometric framing flow, nor equate the low/high whole color jets or prove Gaussian naturality. It specifies the exact finite operator data that such a map must use. ## 6. Exact audit [The script](../experiments/audit_actual_memory_clock_and_normal_transfer.py) uses independently assembled original positive and negative integral R entries over a finite field with dual numbers. At \((N,r)=(2,3),(3,3),(4,4),(5,3)\), it checks 13,188 coefficient routes, their exact integer clock factors, all root/first-normal carry restrictions and the correction (4). It also multiplies the full positive and negative total-position blocks and checks their inverse relation to first normal order. [Results](../experiments/actual_memory_clock_and_normal_transfer_results.json) record the signs, carries and block counts.

title: The actual meridian period and the companion source are different pointed objects
text: # The actual meridian period and the companion source are different pointed objects Actual-state compatibility audit, 27 October 2026. The polynomial companion unfolding is a valid source-frame theorem. It is currently AUXILIARY to the selected meridian/regulator comparison: the actual rational meridian state does not satisfy its highest-clock pointing. Canonical ordinary-color subtraction does produce an actual highest residual, but its unnormalized pairing is precisely the unknown K_N. The existing regular-period theorem supplies the finite affine source extension retaining that datum. These facts do not advance gates C--E of [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md). ## 1. The actual orbit and a universal failure of the highest-clock equation Fix q=q_N, Q=q^2 primitive of order N, y=M^2, U=y^N. The actual reduced state is the NONZERO Laurent polynomial f(y)=F_N(y), with f(1)=K_N, f(Q^j)=C_j(q), 1<=j<N, C_1=1. These are the original quotient-color identities, not an independently chosen rational solution. On E=C(y) over K=C(U), sigma(y)=Qy. After the marked splitting cover alpha^N=U, identify functions with their values at y=alpha Q^j. Multiplication by y/alpha is B=diag(Q^j); sigma inverse is the cyclic shift P e_j=e_(j+1). The actual state vector is f_j=f(alpha Q^j). At U=1,alpha=1, [(B-I)f]_1=(Q-1)C_1=Q-1 !=0. (1.1) Thus the actual state fails Xv=v for EVERY knot and N>=2 in the complete-clock normalization. This is not just a possible failure for a manufactured state. Its complete evaluation row is e_0^t, which obeys e_0^t P=e_(N-1)^t, not ell P=ell. The invariant row is the all-ones row; its value is instead sum_j f_j=K_N+sum_(j=1)^(N-1)C_j(q). (1.2) For the actual orbit these two co-sources cannot be silently identified. Normalizing the invariant row to its value on f would introduce an unknown scalar, rather than reconstruct it. ## 2. A root rational ratio supplies only a cyclotomic line The actual ratio a_N(y)=f(Qy)/f(y) is rational and has exact norm product_(j=0)^(N-1) a_N(Q^j y)=1. (2.1) The horizontal operator a_N inverse sigma is conjugate to sigma by multiplication by f. Its N-th power is I and, on restriction of scalars to K, its characteristic polynomial is z^N-1. Its actual horizontal vector f has orbit dimension ONE under this operator, so it is not the cyclic source required in the rank-N companion theorem. Using the base shift sigma instead does not repair the highest-clock failure (1.1). More generally, for a supplied actual order-r homogeneous operator, the rational solution defines a surjective difference-module pairing pi_f: M_P -> (E,sigma), pi_f(T^j e)=sigma^j f, 0 -> ker pi_f -> M_P -> (E,sigma) ->0. (2.2) Its kernel has E-rank r-1. On the last quotient monodromy is I; therefore the actual central characteristic polynomial has a factor W-1, but the remaining module and extension data have been discarded if only this quotient is retained. This proves neither its equality with the geometric A-curve nor the multiplicity/semisimplicity of the ENTIRE 1-sector. Its generalized multiplicity is between one and r and is not determined by the rational solution. Extraneous annihilator left factors can change it; no general actual minimal rank assertion is made here. The ratio does retain the value when its ACTUAL pointing is carried: K_N=[product_(j=1)^(N-1) a_N(Q^j alpha)]_(alpha=1), (2.3) since it telescopes to f(alpha)/f(Q alpha) and f(Q)=1. Canceled whole germs are required at any zero/pole. Constructing a_N from f does not provide an independent uniform quantum-A construction of that ratio: it already uses the selected state being studied. Multiplication by f can fail to be an integral unit above U=1 when one of its orbit values is zero. The Laurent state is primitive there because its anchor is one, but its multiplication determinant Norm(f) need not be a unit. Thus the generic Hilbert-90 gauge in (2.1) is not an automatic regular pointed-lattice comparison. ## 3. An actual highest residual exists after canonical subtraction Use the EXISTING actual regular-period theorem and its notation: S_N(y)=1+y+...+y^(N-1), P_N degree<=N-2, P_N(Q^j)=C_j(q), 1<=j<N, R_N=(F_N-P_N)/S_N, p_N=P_N/S_N. Define the known zero-complete interpolation and actual remainder c_N=P_N-[P_N(1)/N]S_N, H_N=R_N+P_N(1)/N. These definitions give WHOLE Laurent identities F_N=c_N+S_N H_N, c_N(1)=0, c_N(Q^j)=C_j(q), K_N=N H_N(1). (3.1) In the central fiber the residual is exactly Fbar_N-cbar_N=K_N e_0, e_0=S_N(y)/N modulo y^N-1. (3.2) Consequently it satisfies the highest CLOCK equation, but its original invariant-row pairing is K_N, not one. A nonzero unit normalization making it the companion source e_0 would divide by the target. If K_N vanished it would not even be a cyclic source. This is an exact source compatibility statement, not a new state or a choice of a favorable residual. Let the supplied actual operator have order r. The fixed gauge and denominator clearing from [the regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md), Section 4, give an order-r A with A R_N=b_N, b_N=-A p_N. Therefore the SAME actual construction gives A H_N=B_N, B_N=b_N+[P_N(1)/N]A(1). (3.3) This is a restatement/compatibility consequence of that existing theorem, not a new generic rational inhomogeneous factor. B_N is known from ordinary colors, has fixed Laurent support and polynomial coefficient bounds. Its rootwise augmented companion has rank r+1 with distinguished LAST source coordinate one. The original period is the first-coordinate evaluation N H_N(1). The source-one quotient is not the actual scalar period itself. This extension is ROOTWISE. It does not establish one rational source in indeterminate q or bound its transverse q-jets. The original all-level/finite-pointing and Mellin reconstruction results retain those coherence requirements separately. No equality between their source objects and a geometric regulator extension follows from (3.3). If a different actual generic affine factor is supplied, it may have smaller rank; no universal minimal source rank is claimed. ## 4. The full peripheral line keeps its sign, pole and first normal The actual full state is N_N(M)=epsilon_N M^(N-1)F_N(y)/S_N(y). Its N-step meridian character is (-1)^(N-1). It is a parity line on the M-cover at even N; replacing it by a rational function in y without this character would change the object. Its root shift ratio equals kappa sigma(y-1)/(y-1) times a_N, with kappa=-q^-1. The corresponding WHOLE q-normal adapter is the full g_N, not just that root restriction, as proved in [the peripheral-shift audit](full_peripheral_shift_root_and_normal_audit.md). The central regular frame is (U-1)N_N=epsilon_N M^(N-1)(y-1)F_N. (4.1) At the anchor M=-q this has the nonzero marked residue epsilon_N(-1)^N(q-q^-1). At M=1 it vanishes; its first U-normal coefficient along y=U^(1/N),M=U^(1/(2N)) is epsilon_N K_N/N. Thus that zero must be kept until differentiation. A normalized companion eigenvector at the root alone loses this selected normal functional. Equations (3.1) and (4.1) preserve the whole original S_N and central norm factors rather than substitute 1/N early. ## 5. A genuine meridian prototype, with its rank qualification [The whole figure-eight identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) proves the original state satisfies the explicit second-order inhomogeneous meridian equation (c_- T^-1+c_0+c_+ T)F_N =D(y)(3-U-U^-1), (5.1) with the EXACT source and coefficients in [the normal-period calculation](peripheral_normal_period.md), Section 9. Here c_0 has unique smallest y-order zero, coefficient Q; c_-,c_+ have order two. A rational homogeneous solution cannot exist, because all its shifts have the same valuation and the least term would be unique. The proved cyclic descent then gives det(I-H_hom)!=0 over C(U). Its actual homogenized rank-three source module consequently has SIMPLE central eigenvalue one: its monodromy is [[H_hom,s],[0,1]]. This is GENERIC central nonresonance, not regular invertibility at the complete special fiber U=1. The normal-period construction explicitly retains its enlarged special kernel and first normal. The full source 3-U-U^-1 has not been canceled or replaced by one. This exact prototype illustrates an actual meridian/source module; it is not supplied merely by the clock/companion frame theorem. ## 6. Impact on the original proof goal The companion shell is not yet on the selected regulator path. An actual map must intertwine the EXISTING meridian insertion and word, carry the original co-source and all norm/normal factors, kill actual zero-source currents in the selected quotient, and send the uninserted selected class to a proved NONZERO geometric class. No such general map is constructed by the source-shell classification. The established actual reconstruction and regularized affine source remain exact. Gate C, the nonzero selected geometric image, is still open; the source coefficient bound at D and global logarithmic estimate at E are also unchanged. No completion percentage or claim that these are routine normalization steps follows from this audit. [Exact actual-orbit/source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_meridian_companion_compatibility.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_meridian_companion_compatibility_results.json).

title: Mesoscopic diagonal currents on the actual cup-slide packet
text: # Mesoscopic diagonal currents on the actual cup-slide packet 29 October 2026. The original cup-slide normalization packet admits a coherent subexponential estimate with operator-valued diagonal clock couplings of growing, sublinear Laurent bandwidth. This uses the source-exact packet before taking absolute values, not a dephasing of its individual factorial coefficients. The statement is about the specified exposed recorded packet. It is not automatically an operator identity on an arbitrary remaining physical head. The all-input distinction is explicit in Section 4. ## 1. Literal source packet and its exact controlled-clock contraction Use the original notation and full Cartan factor of [the all-input cup slide](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md): N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=exp(pi*i*d/N), F_j=(Q;Q)_j, b_j=x^(-d)Q^(-j) conjugate(F_j), Gbar_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^d conjugate(F_j) z^j. This is exactly b=T R12 R23 p, with the original physical recorded middle-color projectors, ordinary cap and specified lowest marked cut. All original external framing/peripheral factors chi_N stay outside. The finite identity Q^(j+1)F_j=F_j-F_(j+1), F_N=0, gives P_N(z):=sum_(j=0)^d Q^(-j) conjugate(F_j) z^j =Q[(1-1/z)Gbar_N(z)+1/z]. (1) The apparent singularity at zero is removable. In particular P_N(1)=Q and the original packet closes to x^(-d)Q, with its full unit phase. Let A_r(t), |r|<=D, be operators on any spectator space. Define the EXPLICIT diagonal recorded-color exterior f_j(t)=sum_(|r|<=D) A_r(t) (tQ^r)^j. The exact contraction, preserving original operator order, is sum_j f_j(t)b_j=x^(-d) sum_(|r|<=D) A_r(t)P_N(tQ^r). (2) Only distributivity is used in (2). The A_r need not commute with one another or be scalar. Their norm is retained below. In particular an arbitrary exterior with O(N) Laurent bandwidth is not silently replaced by a fixed-band clock polynomial. ## 2. Mesoscopic source bound The independently proved [clock-disk theorem](actual_normalization_clock_disk_bound.md) gives, for 0<C<=N/2, sup_(|z-1|<=C/N)|G_N(z)| <= B_N(C), B_N(C)=2exp(2C)N^2 (1+2N/(3C))^(C/4). (3) Coefficient conjugation gives the SAME bound for Gbar_N. Suppose |t-1|<=c/N and put C=c+2pi*D. Then |tQ^r-1| <= |t-1|+|Q^r-1| <= C/N, |r|<=D. (4) When C<=N/2, every argument in (2) has modulus at least1/2. Equations (1)--(4) consequently prove the actual coherent inequality ||sum_j f_j(t)b_j|| <= (sum_r ||A_r(t)||) [2+(2C/N)B_N(C)]. (5) Any supplied norm on the spectator coefficient space may be used. No N-dependent change of physical source metric appears in (5). The phase x^(-d) has modulus one and remains in the exact identity (2). Let now c=c_N and D=D_N grow with N. If c_N+D_N=o(N), log^+ sup_(|t-1|<=c_N/N) sum_r||A_r(t)|| = o(N), (6) then the right side of (5) is exp(o(N)). Indeed log B_N(C)=O(log N+C+C log(1+N/C))=o(N), since s log(1+1/s) tends to zero as s=C/N tends to zero. The cases C=0 or D=0,t=1 follow directly from P_N(1)=Q. Fixed bandwidth, fixed c, and polynomial spectator mass give a polynomial bound. This controls a genuinely growing set of diagonal clock observables on the known original packet. Individual |F_j| can still be exponential; the coherent identity (1) has been used before estimation. ## 3. Normal jets and compatible normalization leaves If the coefficient operators are holomorphic on a slightly larger disk with the same subexponential mass condition, Cauchy's formula also bounds fixed clock-normal derivatives. For a radius r_N>0 with log^+(1/r_N)=o(N), || (1/s!) partial_t^s sum_j f_j(t)b_j |_(t=1)|| <= r_N^(-s) sup_(|t-1|=r_N)||sum_j f_j(t)b_j||. (7) Thus fixed s costs exp(o(N)); growing orders are allowed whenever s log^+(1/r_N)=o(N), in addition to the stated supremum bound. This is a derivative of the recorded packet, not a meridian identification or a physical two-color raising/lowering insertion. The [normalization-current quotient](actual_normalization_boundary_current_quotient.md) may be composed with (2) when its literal all-input pointing map exposes this packet and its spectator coefficients in exactly this slot. For example, its fixed-forest radial Mellin Taylor coefficients have polynomial coefficient mass; (5) then retains that mass and gives the same subexponential clock bound. Each leaf contraction must be an actual tensor/source identity before it is estimated. No independent mark or new 1/N average is introduced for such a leaf. The assertion is deliberately typed.
