It does not say that any internal recorded-color seam can be moved to the marked cut, or that arbitrary original crossings preserve this filtered clock class. Their factorial dependence and frequencies can have order N. ## 4. Why the scalar packet does not already solve physical gluing There is a simple all-input test. The original cup slide is (R12 R23)(p12 tensor I)=I tensor p23. Keep an arbitrary physical input color a on the remaining head, record the middle color n, and perform the SAME terminal R23^2 and ordinary cap as before. Write L=kappa^(-1)R12 on degree d. The resulting actual open-head operator is diagonal, with entries C_a(t)=sum_(n=0)^d t^n x^(n-a)Q^(-a)(L^2)_(d-a,n). (8) To derive (8), multiply the literal cup coefficient N x^(n-d), the full crossing square kappa^2(L^2)_(d-a,n), and the cap x^(-a)Q^(-a)/N, using kappa^2=x^d. All original turns and phases are therefore fixed. At t=1, Hopf closure gives C_a(1)=kappa^2 for EVERY a. At a=d, (8) is exactly x^(-d)P_N(t), the scalar packet estimated above. A scalar bound for this last row does not prove a uniform all-a operator bound for (8). Likewise applying a unilateral shift to the RECORDING register is not automatically inserting physical Ecal or F before the projector: Pi_j Ecal Pi_k retains two colors and changes the remaining terminal coefficients. Such a move needs an actual two-color/all-port identity. Equations (2)--(7) apply to diagonal controlled-clock exteriors on the already exposed original packet; they do not assume those missing identities. This is a quantitative source-current class, not a sharp full-knot volume theorem. Binding the complete internal currents to the knot's geometric regulator remains unproved. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_mesoscopic_clock_packet_currents.py) checks the original physical packet, its full phase and operator-valued controlled-clock contractions; it also tests the quantitative disk comparison on growing bandwidths without separating factorial modes.

title: The literal middle five-point configuration and its actual crossing factor
text: # The literal middle five-point configuration and its actual crossing factor Research note, 28 October 2026. The middle five-point certificate in [the classical crossing cycle, Section 3](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) is +partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_M), p_1=a p, s_M=a s_0. (1) This note puts those **actual shared quantum flags** in an explicit canonical frame, identifies one of its tetrahedral arguments in an exact factorization of the original crossing, and gives a corrected finite reciprocal-coordinate transition with its original source. The transition has an unavoidable spectral projector. Its omitted term has a nonzero pairing in an actual one-crossing cup network. This is not a full five-factor quantum realization of (1). It does give a literal configuration, factor and correction against which such a realization can be checked. In particular, scalar auxiliary region flags cannot remove the determinant wall: a rank identity below proves this for every generic choice of that flag. ## 1. A finite two-factor decomposition of the original crossing Use the original balanced matrices from [the shared quantum flags note](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md). Let P be the original finite Euler polynomial P(A)=sum_(h=0)^(N-1)(-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)A^h/F_h, F_h=(Q;Q)_h, Q=exp(2pi*i/N). The original uncheck crossing is R_0=D P(e_1 f_2), including its original Cartan diagonal D. Its common scalar Cartan line kappa remains external throughout; the full checked crossing is kappa times flip R_0. Neither its framing nor its peripheral normalization is changed. Choose any cyclic completion S_2 of the actual raising shift. Since f_2=(1-Z_2)S_2 is already the original nilpotent F_2, R_0=D P(-e_1 Z_2 S_2) P(e_1 S_2) (2) is an exact identity at every level N and every pair of nonzero colors. Indeed put A=e_1S_2, B=-e_1Z_2S_2. Then BA=QAB, so the finite binomial identity gives P(A+B)=P(B)P(A). Every apparent product term of total degree >=N contains e_1^N and vanishes. Thus no root specialization of separate infinite compact products is involved. The cyclic wrap in S_2 cancels in A+B and (2) is the original crossing, not a cyclic replacement. The individual factors in (2) are nilpotent Euler kernels with exact finite coefficients. They are not asserted to be single nondegenerate basic matrix dilogarithms. ## 2. An exact canonical frame for the actual five flags Now take complete colors x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1), and the typed marks S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu. As in the shared-flag note let G_1=[[K,e],[fK,2lambda-QK]], a=(1,S_1)^t, b=(1,t_2)^t, t_2=f_1+K_1^(-1)S_2. These are the fixed flags of the actual shared meridians H_1 and H_2. Choose the same Gauss auxiliary flags as the classical calculation: p=(0,1)^t and s_0=(1,0)^t. Keep their images as homogeneous columns: p_1=G_1p=(e_1,2lambda-QK_1)^t, s_M=G_1s_0=(K_1,f_1K_1)^t. (3) No inverse of e_1 is used. Set Z=Z_1, Y=-ZS_1, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), L=[[Y,0],[-S_1,1]]. (4) All these frame factors are units, and XZ=QZX, X^N=Z^N=1. The five original columns have the following exact form: | Original flag F | Canonical column F_c | Retained right tag R_F in LF=F_c R_F | | --- | --- | --- | | a | (1,0)^t | Y | | b | (1,1-X)^t | Y | | p | (0,1)^t | 1 | | p_1 | (1-Z,1)^t | lambda | | s_M | (1,1)^t | YK_1 | For example (t_2-S_1)Y^(-1)=1-X, Y e_1=lambda(1-Z), and (2lambda-QK_1)-S_1e_1=lambda. These prove the table by multiplication. Thus it is the literal middle configuration of (1), with every right normalization retained. A projective coordinate such as (1-Z)^(-1) is not asserted to exist in the finite module: its homogeneous column is what the table gives. This frame is uniformly controlled at unit marks. If |mu|=1, then S_1,Y,K_1 and lambda are unitary. The norm of L and L^(-1) is the golden ratio (1+sqrt(5))/2; each right tag has norm and inverse norm one. The frame neither diagonalizes all five flags nor uses the generally exponential full coherent Fermat basis. These assertions therefore do not contradict the previously calculated exponential coherent-frame norms. ## 3. Its classical boundary and an actual tetrahedron factor In the commutative limit the five flags of the table are (a,b,p,p_1,s_M)=(0,1-X,infinity,(1-Z)^(-1),1). Put H=X+Z-XZ. In the exact cross-ratio convention of the classical certificate, the omitted-vertex tetrahedra have | Omitted vertex j | Cross-ratio r_j | Boundary sign | | --- | --- | --- | | a | H/[X(1-Z)] | + | | b | 1/(1-Z) | - | | p | X/H | + | | p_1 | X | - | | s_M | H | + | This is a direct determinant computation on those five points, so it is precisely the middle certificate (1). The first tetrahedron has positive quad coordinate 1/(1-r_0)=-X(1-Z)/Z. But the last factor of the **original crossing** in (2) has the exact argument n=e_1S_2=(Q-Z^(-1))X, n^N=0. (5) Its classical symbol is exactly -X(1-Z)/Z. Hence a genuine tetrahedron of this specific certificate, not a freely chosen auxiliary atom, occurs in (2). The tetrahedron omitting b has positive quad coordinate Z. The boundary is equivalently [n_cl]-[Z]+[X/H]-[X]+[H]=0. (6) Equation (6) is the classical statement. At the quantum level neither X, Z, nor the homogeneous columns alone authorize replacing the whole right factor in (2) by five uncorrected cyclic dilogarithms. ## 4. Two explicit issues in a naive quantum lift For the usual cyclic pentagon center pattern, a classical parameterization of (6) is U=1-Z,V=X, with 1-U+UV=H, -UV/(1-U)=n_cl, V/(1-U+UV)=X/H. Its left centers are X and (1-X)(1-Z)=1-H. Applying the ordinary complement relation gives exactly (6). But its literal quantum candidates do **not** form a quantum torus: X(1-Z)-Q(1-Z)X=(1-Q)X !=0. (7) Thus simply substituting the classical five-point coordinates in the generic cyclic pentagon is false. A scalar root phase or retained numerical multiplier does not remove (7). This does not rule out a nonlinear quantum change of coordinates with additional face factors; it locates the change that is needed for this actual configuration. The reciprocal coordinate also has a precise finite correction. The would-be expression (1-QZ)^(-1)X cannot exist as a right solution to (1-QZ)U=X, since 1-QZ has a kernel and X is a unit. Let E_d be the Z=Q^(-1) spectral projector, and define the finite group inverse H_Q(Z)|j>=1/(1-Q^(j+1))|j> (j<d), H_Q(Z)|d>=0, U=H_Q(Z)X. Then exactly UZ=QZU, U^N=0, (1-QZ)U=X-E_dX. (8) The projector in (8) is compulsory. It is not permission to replace the generic reciprocal coordinate by U without transporting the right-hand side as well. ## 5. An explicit corrected transition in the original crossing There is a closed factorial gauge, rather than an unknown similarity, connecting (5) to the regularized primitive (8): Gamma|j>=g_j|j>, g_j=(-1)^j Q^(-j(j-1)/2)F_j^2, Gamma n Gamma^(-1)=U. (9) Here Gamma acts on the first actual head. To prove (9), use X|j> proportional to |j-1> on the first head. For 1<=j<N, the coefficient of n is Q(1-Q^(-j)) times that of X, whereas the coefficient of U is 1/(1-Q^j) times that of X. The required ratio is precisely g_j/g_(j-1)=-Q^(1-j)(1-Q^j)^2. Both operators have zero arrow at j=0. This proves every entry, including the wrap, independently of parity and mu. Consequently the original crossing has the exact refactor R_0=D P(-e_1Z_2S_2) Gamma^(-1)P(U)Gamma. (10) Equations (8)--(10) give a corrected finite coordinate change at a tetrahedron of the literal middle five-point configuration, with every factor of the original R specified. They do not yet give the entire five-factor quantum identity for (6). Gamma is not a negligible unit. At complex roots, g_j=Q^j|F_j|^2. (11) Its absolute weights are positive, but generally exponential in N. For example the already proved factorial estimate in [the coherent-frame note](actual_four_line_fermat_crossing_and_conditioning.md) gives log||Gamma||=2gamma_*N+O(log N) and log||Gamma^(-1)||=2gamma_*N+O(log N), with gamma_*=Vol(4_1)/(4pi)>0. Thus the explicit frame contributes at the scale being studied. It must stay in the period. The same factorial square appears numerically in the existing degree-d Rogers cap row: at completeness its entries satisfy mu_r=x^(d+r)g_r/N^2. This does not cancel Gamma here. The Rogers index belongs to the relative fusion frame, whereas (9) acts on the original physical clock. A fusion comparison must carry the actual matrix and all of its sources before identifying those two diagonals. ## 6. Original source and the nonzero omitted wall Keep the original complete cup and full marked cap p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. The unstripped common scalar line is kappa. The checked crossing B with kappa external obeys Bp=p. Directly, Xp=Q^(-1)p, m E_d X Bp=Q^(-1)/N. (12) For the full crossing the second value is kappa Q^(-1)/N, with its same exterior framing and peripheral factors. Thus (8)'s correction is visible in an actual one-crossing source contraction, not only in an arbitrary matrix entry. The five-point canonical frame also has its literal right source tags. At the a and b vertices put p'=Yp and m'=mY^(-1). Then Xp'=p', m'p'=1, m'E_dXp'=1/N. (13) The Q phase in (12) has therefore not been discarded; (13) is the correctly typed changed source. Under the further factorial transition (9), use Gamma p and mGamma^(-1). Their pairing is again one. Neither vector can be replaced by the old vector individually in (10). The cap still has its original affine charge (J_1+J_2+1)p=Np. The corrected clock transition (8) has not been identified with the internal integer edge winding of a positive Pachner move. Its projector and source tags are exactly part of what that identification must transport. ### Endpoint wall removal preserves every original knot exponent There is an unconditional, quantitative boundary consequence. Let C_N be the actual cut operator of any knot, with its original exterior scalar normalization retained. Its Hopf intertwining implies C_N=K_N I: commuting with the original K forces a diagonal matrix, and commuting with the original F, whose consecutive arrows are nonzero, makes all diagonal entries equal. This argument holds at every N and at the complete color, without an asymptotic or a Schur hypothesis. Consequently m E_dX(C_N tensor I)p=Q^(-1)K_N/N, m(1-E_dX)(C_N tensor I)p=(1-Q^(-1)/N)K_N. (15) The scalar in the second line satisfies 1/2 <= |1-Q^(-1)/N| <= 3/2 (N>=2). Thus removal of this projector at the **marked endpoint** preserves the limsup and liminf of N^(-1)log|K_N|; the normalized logarithms change by at most (log 2)/N. This removes this specific boundary normalization issue without assuming a volume conjecture or a noncancellation statement. The wall itself has exactly the same exponential rate as K_N, with the polynomial factor 1/N, and cannot be declared exponentially suppressed. The boundary sewing algebra is equally explicit. For any integers r,s and clock indices j,k, E_jX^r E_kX^s=delta_(j,k-r) E_jX^(r+s), m E_jX^r(C_N tensor I)p=Q^(-r)K_N/N. (16) Thus a fixed specified endpoint sewing word has an exact finite coefficient multiplying the original scalar. A claim that an **interior** five-point wall has moved to that endpoint must still prove its current/source transport. Equation (15) alone supplies neither that transport nor a comparison with a separately selected geometric saddle. ## 7. A generic scalar auxiliary flag cannot remove this wall The obstruction is not caused by choosing p=infinity. Let P=(r,s)^t have scalar entries and ell_P=(-s,r). The original complete meridian has the factorization G-lambda=(1,S)^t(K-lambda)(1,-S^(-1)). Since ell_P P=0, it follows exactly that ell_P G P=(rS-s)(K-lambda)(r-S^(-1)s). (17) For a generic scalar flag both outer factors are units; for example, r=1 and s^N!=mu. The middle factor has rank N-1. Hence the determinant between P and GP is singular of rank N-1 for **every** such generic scalar auxiliary choice. Inverting it inside the original finite module is impossible. This rules out repairing the naive generic five-point field construction merely by moving a scalar auxiliary flag. This is a specific obstruction to that construction, not to a relative quantum five-point period. A valid continuation can retain a normal variable and the projector/source in (8), or add a genuine quantum auxiliary module with its originally specified reduction. It must then prove that the resulting combined five-factor product gives (10) with its typed source. Neither (7) nor (14) excludes that possibility. No such complete product or geometric saddle coefficient is asserted here. ## 8. The actual unwrapped-period coordinates match these flags The [actual cyclic/Hardy graph](actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.md) uses S_i as multiplication by z_i and Z_i=B_i as the shift f(z_i)->f(Qz_i). In that realization the same dictionary is literal: X=x z_2/z_1, Z=B_1, n=(Q-B_1^(-1))X=q Ecal_1 z_2. (18) Here Ecal is the actual rho^2 E. Indeed at completeness Ecal_1=z_1^(-1)(B_1^(-1)-1), and -xQ=q. All homogeneous frame identities of Section 2 and (5) use only these Weyl relations and the complete color. They therefore hold on that actual graph as well, before selecting its root center. The central powers must be distinguished. On the unwrapped graph, X^N=x^N z_2^N/z_1^N is a variable central multiplication operator. On the typed finite heads used in Sections 2 and 6, S_2^N=k S_1^N gives X^N=1. That is a source/period restriction, not an identity in the unwrapped Laurent algebra. Equation (18) supplies the operator dictionary but does not prove its source pushforward or equate a central root value with a semiclassical shape. ## 9. Exact audit Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_middle_five_point_wall.py This checks 28 original-R factorizations (2), 21 typed five-point frames and corrected factorial transitions, and 21 generic scalar-flag rank obstructions, over exact prime fields for N=2,...,8. It includes (12)--(13), both wraps, the actual original coefficient evaluator, and the full input cup. The all-level proofs above are finite identities; these tests are independent diagnostics.

title: An actual dressed middle wall is a Fourier-mode projector
text: # An actual dressed middle wall is a Fourier-mode projector 28 October 2026. A literal aggregate of the original middle-wall operators has an exact Fourier/Plancherel reduction. Its two Euler factors can separately have exponential norm, and its wall has both zero and positive integer carry. Their COMPLETE packet is nevertheless a known unitary clock times N times a rank-N cyclic Fourier projector. The full wrap parameter, Cartan line and marked source are retained. This is a boundary/current-kernel simplification, not a substitution for the original knot invariant. Its precise placement is essential. It does not bound an arbitrary F_H-conjugated wall or the complete unmodified knot scalar, and gives no volume lower bound. ## 1. The actual literal factors and the failed separate damping Use the conventions of [the literal middle certificate](literal_middle_full_phi_certificate.md): Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x=-exp(-pi*i/N), k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu, X=x S_2 S_1^(-1), Z=Z_1, n=e_1 S_2, n_-=-e_1 Z_2 S_2, P(A)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2) A^h/F_h, F_h=(Q;Q)_h, W=E_d(Z)X=x mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor S_2. (1) The full original checked positive crossing is B_plus=kappa Flip D P(n_-)P(n), D|a,b>=x^(-a-b)Q^(ab)|a,b>. (2) All displayed factors in (1)--(2) are actual finite operators. The original kappa has not been normalized away; it is external only to simplify writing the following packet. The split W=W_0+W_+ has W_0=x k |d,0><0,d|, W_+=x mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor sum_(b<d)|b+1><b|. (3) Their integer degrees are 0 and +N. Between whole original crossings the positive part is source-null. INSIDE (2), however, the adjacent Euler factors have negative carries. In fact pi_0(n W_+)=k(1-Q)|d-1,0><0,d-1| !=0. (4) Conjugation by r^D scales W_+ by r^N and the negative part of n by r^(-N); (4) is unchanged. The [positive-carry damping theorem](actual_exponentially_tame_carry_completion.md) therefore cannot be applied separately to these internal factors. The following identity controls the actual aggregate instead. ## 2. The complete aggregate is exactly a Fourier projector Define the specified checked wall packet L=Flip D P(n_-) W P(n). (5) Then, for EVERY N>=2, parity and nonzero typed wrap mu, L=x^2 Z_1^(-1) sum_(j=0)^d X^j =N x^(N+1) g_1 E_0(X), g_1=x^(1-N) Z_1^(-1), E_0(X)=N^(-1)sum_(j=0)^d X^j. (6) The full original Cartan scalar gives kappa L, with the same original framing/peripheral source lines as (2). No unknown scalar or numerical norm factor is used in (6). Here is an entry proof including the cyclic wrap. Let (a,b) be the input and (c,e) the output BEFORE the final Flip. Put r=[a+b]=[c+e], and epsilon_in=(a+b-r)/N, epsilon_out=(c+e-r)/N. The entry is zero unless these residues agree. The right P(n) must lower the first input a to zero, hence only its power a contributes. Since e_1|a>=lambda(1-Q^(-a))|a-1>, (Q^(-1);Q^(-1))_a =(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)F_a, its coefficient simplifies EXACTLY to x^a times S_2^a. The wall then raises that first index to d. The left P(n_-) must have power s=d-c. Root reflection (Q^(-1);Q^(-1))_c F_(d-c)=N cancels its entire factorial denominator. Its remaining coefficient is lambda^s Q^[s(a+b+1)+s^2]. The total S_2 power is N+a-c, so its wrap count is 1+epsilon_in-epsilon_out. Its first wrap k mu cancels the mu^(-1) in W. Simplifying the remaining powers gives the FULL entry (P(n_-)WP(n))_(c,e;a,b) =x^(a+c+2)Q^(-(c+1)e) (k mu)^(epsilon_in-epsilon_out). (7) This includes all positive, zero and negative total-degree paths; none was discarded after taking absolute values. Multiplication by D and then Flip, with output written (u,v), makes (7) L_(u,v;a,b)=x^(a+u+2) (k mu)^(epsilon_in-epsilon_out). (8) On the other hand, exactly one summand X^j, j=[a-u], connects these states in the same total-degree residue class. Its coefficient is x^(a-u)(k mu)^(epsilon_in-epsilon_out). Multiplying by the output factor x^2 Q^(-u)=x^(2u+2) proves (6). ## 3. Plancherel, exact norm and reduction to one channel head For |mu|=1 the literal X is unitary and X^N=1. It has N disjoint cycles, labeled by total degree modulo N, and its eigenvalue-one space has dimension N. Thus E_0(X) is an ORTHOGONAL projector. Equation (6) gives rank L=N, ||L||=N, L^dagger L=N^2 E_0(X), LL^dagger=N^2 Z_1^(-1)E_0(X)Z_1. (9) This is an exact two-copy positive contraction. It is not inferred from positivity of the original pivotal trace, which is false. For explicit normalized channel vectors, set b=[r-a] and epsilon=(a+b-r)/N, and put U|r>=N^(-1/2)sum_(a=0)^d x^(-a)(k mu)^(-epsilon)|a,[r-a]>. Different r have disjoint support, and XU=U. Therefore U^dagger U=I_N, E_0(X)=UU^dagger, L=N x^2 Z_1^(-1) U U^dagger. (10) It follows that every occurrence of this actual two-head packet can be replaced by two known isometries with ONE N-dimensional internal channel. Its previous two-head cut had dimension N^2. A normalized root Fourier transform on the r-channel is unitary; Plancherel preserves both exterior channel norms exactly. For example retain any specified exterior row Lambda, state psi and original surrounding operators A,B. Equation (10) gives Lambda A(kappa L)B psi =kappa N x^2 <alpha,beta>, alpha=U^dagger Z_1 A^dagger Lambda^dagger, beta=U^dagger B psi. (11) Original spectator indices can remain as tensor factors in (11). Every original cap, pivot and normalization remains in Lambda, psi,A,B; these are not chosen from the unknown knot value. Hence |Lambda A(kappa L)B psi|^2 <=N^2 ||alpha||^2 ||beta||^2. (12) The same identity holds after a unitary DFT of both channel vectors. Formula (11) is an actual local channel reduction, not the tautological Fourier transform of an already evaluated scalar. Its two exterior vectors need not agree or be conjugates; (12) does not give a lower bound or geometric alignment. For a fixed compact nonunit wrap, each X^j has norm at most max(|mu|,|mu|^(-1)), because each head can wrap at most once. Thus ||L||<=N max(|mu|,|mu|^(-1)); the unitary formulation is used only for |mu|=1. No exponential source conditioning is hidden by fixing a regular nonzero wrap. ## 4. Precise original-source placement and marked face normalizers Let P=P(n), H=P^(-1)ZP and define the CORRECT transported wall W_H=P^(-1) W P. (13) Then the actual input insertion has exactly the packet (5): B_plus W_H=kappa L. (14) This is valid inside every original signed word and with its ENTIRE fixed co-source, simply by the literal matrix identity. It is not the false relocation B_plus W -> W B_plus. Bare W and the transported W_H are different coupons. The marked full-Phi clocks are the original ones, F_Z=phi_N diag_j(1/F_j), F_H=P^(-1)F_ZP. Since W has first input zero and first output d, F_d=N gives F_Z W F_Z^(-1)=W/N, F_H W_H F_H^(-1)=W_H/N, B_plus F_H^s W_H F_H^(-s)=kappa N^(-s)L. (15) The exact phi_N cancels only in this specified conjugation; it has not been deleted from a one-sided face or source. Similarly for the original factorial face frame Gamma_j, Gamma_d=N^2 Q^(-1), Gamma_0=1, so Gamma W Gamma^(-1)=N^2 Q^(-1)W. (16) Transporting BOTH Gamma and W by P gives the same relation in the H frame. Any bounded number of these MATCHED conjugations therefore changes the packet by known polynomial powers of N and recorded root phases, despite exponential standalone norms of Gamma, P or F_H. These identities do not bound arbitrary one-sided F_H factors or an untransported wall in an unrelated slot. A full middle-move comparison must exhibit (13)--(15), or another exact matching of its actual interfaces, before invoking (9)--(12). For a concrete source check, the original cup has Xp=Q^(-1)p. Thus Lp=0, while the bare wall has the known nonzero mWp. This distinction is compulsory: the packet cannot be substituted for the bare wall in the old endpoint formula. If an explicitly transported source has X-eigenvalue one, its E_0(X) channel instead survives, with its actual transported dual still retained. ## 5. The original affine cap is a charged Fourier mode There is an exact bridge from (6) to the FULL original nilpotent source, before replacing a knot cut by its scalar value. Put T=Z_1 Z_2, P_d=E_d(T), P_cap=P_d E_0(X). T commutes with X. Since the integer degree of two physical heads lies in [0,2d], its eigenvalue Q^d has exactly the ONE lift D=d; the putative second lift d+N exceeds 2d. Thus P_d is precisely the original positive affine cap charge D+1=N, with no zero-winding alias. At r=d the isometry vector in Section 3 is w=N^(-1/2)sum_a x^(-a)|a,d-a>, P_cap=|w><w|. (17) It is independent of mu. Even for a nonunit mu, X restricted to this degree-d sector is unitary: its two simultaneous endpoint wraps cancel the mark. Hence P_cap is an orthogonal rank-one projector for every nonzero typed mark at complete color. Use the original cup and ordinary right cap p_(a,b)=N x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), l_(a,b)=x^b g_a/N delta_(a+b,d), Pi_N=p l. Direct substitution of (17) proves Pi_N=N g_1 P_cap, Pi_N^dagger Pi_N=N^2 P_cap, P_d(kappa L)=kappa x^(N+1)Pi_N. (18) The pivot is indispensable. It moves the ket's X-eigenvalue from one to Q^(-1), the exact original cup mark; <w,g_1 w>=0, so Pi_N^2=0. This positive two-copy identity therefore does not contradict the failure of a positive one-copy pivotal trace. Retain the actual partial closing Phi_g(A)=Tr_2[A(I tensor g)]. The same original turns give Phi_g(Pi_N)=I. Consequently for ANY finite matrix C on the open cut, not merely a scalar intertwiner, C=(kappa x^(N+1))^(-1) Phi_g[(C tensor I)P_d(kappa L)]. (19) This is a source-normalized opening through the actual wall packet. Its factor is a known original Cartan/root phase, not a scalar chosen from the value of a knot period. The external modified dimension, framing and peripheral line multiply both sides unchanged. The vector w is maximally entangled: Tr_2(P_cap)=I/N. Equation (18) therefore also proves, for EVERY C, ||(C tensor I)Pi_N||_HS^2=N||C||_HS^2. (20) For the actual knot cut C=K_N I this is N^2|K_N|^2. Unlike a Fourier transform of an already scalar K_N delta, (17)--(20) specify the original charged source and an explicit local Fourier projector before that scalar reduction. They may be inserted into the full uncontracted original tensor network. Plancherel then acts on known head or channel variables with all normalization fixed. There is a source-preserving positive averaging at this TERMINAL opening. Set P_k=Z_1^k P_cap Z_1^(-k), Pi_k=N g_1 P_k, k=0,...,d. The vectors Z_1^k w are an orthonormal Fourier basis of the degree-d sector. Every P_k has marginal I/N. Thus exactly sum_k P_k=P_d, Phi_g(Pi_k)=I, ||(C tensor I)Pi_k||_HS^2=N||C||_HS^2, sum_k ||(C tensor I)g_1 P_k||_HS^2=||C||_HS^2. (21) For the partial closing, the only nonzero traced entry has b=d-a, and its two pivotal factors obey g_a g_(d-a)=1; the Fourier phases cancel. This proves the middle identity for an arbitrary nonscalar C, independently of an intertwining or scalar-cut assumption. The other identities follow from the orthogonal modes and their identical marginals. Equivalently the positive terminal density N P_cap can be replaced by its clock average P_d when testing ANY operator on its FIRST leg alone. This is an exact positive mixed boundary source, with the factor N retained. It does not average an internal paired source on which the exterior acts on both legs. In particular it does not justify replacing local doubled Euler coefficients c_a conjugate(c_b) by their diagonal a=b terms. Such an internal dephasing would require another source identity. Equations (19)--(20) still contain the original exterior pivotal contractions. Their norm is not determined by the nonzero local projector. In particular they provide no lower bound for its geometric overlap and no Rivin-volume estimate for the whole doubled network. ## 6. Integer degree and the remaining geometric limitation The degree-zero part of (7) has c+e=a+b, and its total-degree blocks have rank one and unit-modulus entries. Its norm is N. If all OTHER exterior factors preserve total integer degree, the original pivotal first-cut and marked-plat sources kill the packet's +/-N parts. This gives an exact source replacement by that degree-zero packet, not a scalar relocation to an endpoint. Retaining the full Fourier projector (10) is often the simpler representation: integer-degree projection would split its N modular blocks into 2N-1 ordinary blocks. Neither operation makes the entire knot source positive or bounds its other crossings. The projector in (6) is a position-ratio clock X, not a physical head clock Z_1. Its correctly transported version can be a relative H-wall. Therefore the finite physical-projector action-zero theorem cannot simply be applied to (6). A regular geometric source can meet an auxiliary face degeneration. The useful rigorous conclusion is the polynomial norm and explicit one-head Plancherel reduction; geometric support and source overlap of the remaining exterior are still additional work. ## 7. Audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_middle_wall_fourier_packet.py The audit compares (6)--(8) directly with the literal finite Euler operators for both parities and nontrivial wrap marks. It retains the actual Cartan, checked flip, original cup/marker, and complete figure-eight pivotal source. It checks the transported-source identity (14), marked normalization (15), and independent complex isometries/double-layer Plancherel identities. It tests all terminal Fourier modes, their positive average, and arbitrary nonscalar cut matrices in (21). The entry calculation above proves the all-level formula.

title: Every actual auxiliary color in the arbitrary-plat source compiler
text: # Every actual auxiliary color in the arbitrary-plat source compiler 30 October 2026. The original augmented-plat compiler extends to ALL ordinary auxiliary colors 1<=n<=N and signed local coupons R^epsilon L_n, epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Its value and first-normal columns, inverse measures, color phases and source are explicit. No unknown recoupling inverse remains. The additional normal and color factors have uniform polynomial bounds; all exponential factorial profiles are displayed rather than absorbed in that claim. This is a finite ROOT-LEVEL source theorem at arbitrary fixed bridge width. It does not assert a coherent global gap or a uniform complex color interpolation, and is not yet an arbitrary-plat filling theorem. In particular the exact root normal below must not be confused with the generic-q normal of the whole original pointed invariant. ## 1. The circle polynomial is fixed by the original typed source Use d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The ordinary n-dimensional auxiliary module has its ACTUAL pivot K_n^(1-N), with no new factor 1/n. The typed threading [2,1,1,2] followed by that pivot trace gives, as a full physical matrix, L_n=l_n(Omega), l_n(z)=(-1)^(n-1) P_(n-1)(z), P_r(z)=U_r(z/2), P_0=1, P_1=z, P_(r+1)=z P_r-P_(r-1). (1) Thus L_1=I and L_2=-Omega. This normalization, including the sign, is the proved [original mixed-circle identity](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). It is not a replacement of an ordinary module by an N-dimensional ADO component at a putative meridian value. For an actual physical pair degree S set t=min(S,2d-S) and translate the first index by max(0,S-d), exactly as in the complete compiler. Use the canonical physical columns v_j=f(c_j), w_j=f'(c_j), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. All j=0,...,t are retained, grouped by equal nodes. The only double pair is j,l=d-j. The self-paired odd-level node is SIMPLE. Ordinary colors also retain the unpaired simple nodes killed by L_N. ## 2. An exact generic finite formula for the normal column The root formula for v_j is the q-Hahn sum in the [complete phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). To compute its first NORMAL, one must first use the actual generic highest-weight-d family, not differentiate a root-only simplification. Let zeta vary near q, Q=zeta^2, x=zeta^d and F_b=(Q;Q)_b. Define R_(j,a)=F_(N-j+a-1) F_(N-a-1) / [F_(N-j-1) F_(N-1)], C_(j,u,a)(zeta)=(-1)^a x^(u-2a) Q^[a(t-u)+a(a-1)/2] R_(j,a) [u choose a]_Q [t-u choose j-a]_Q/[t choose j]_Q, C_(j,u)(zeta)=sum_(max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u)) C_(j,u,a). (2) Every factorial index lies in 0,...,d, so these are regular finite functions at the actual root. They are the normalized actual generic Clebsch columns. One direct derivation starts with the highest vector of degree j, whose a-th coefficient is (-1)^a x^-a Q^[a(j-1)-a(a-1)/2] R_(j,a). Apply F_tot^(t-j)/F_(t-j), with F_tot=F tensor I+K^-1 tensor F. The q-binomial expansion contributes x^[-(t-j-u+a)]Q^[a(t-j-u+a)] [u choose a][t-u choose j-a]. Its first component is x^[-(t-j)] [t choose j], which is a unit. Dividing by it gives precisely (2). Thus its eigenvalue is lambda_j(zeta)=zeta^(2N-1-2j)+zeta^(-2N+1+2j). (3) At the root, R_(j,a)=Q^[a(a-j)] [j choose a]_Q, recovering the previous physical column and its exact Fourier phase. This equality is used for the VALUES, not for their zeta derivatives. For a double pair j<l=d-j, put D=zeta d/dzeta. Then exactly w_(j,u)=[D C_(j,u)(q)-D C_(l,u)(q)] / [-2N(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))]. (4) Indeed C_(j,u)=f_u(zeta,lambda_j(zeta)); subtracting derivatives cancels the common derivative of f with respect to zeta. The remaining eigenvalue gap derivative from (3) is the displayed denominator. This retains the actual generic confluence. The differentiated sum in (4) is fully explicit. Write H_b=D log F_b=-2 sum_(r=1)^b r Q^r/(1-Q^r), H_0=0, Hbin(v,w)=H_v-H_w-H_(v-w). At the root each summand derivative is its original root value times Gamma_(j,u,a)=d(u-2a)+2a(t-u)+a(a-1) +H_(N-j+a-1)-H_(N-j-1)+H_(N-a-1)-H_(N-1) +Hbin(u,a)+Hbin(t-u,j-a)-Hbin(t,j). (5) Thus (4) is a difference of two finite factorial/Fourier sums with known q-harmonic coefficients. No chosen solution of a homogeneous recurrence or unidentified normal amplitude has been inserted. ## 3. Explicit bilinear measures and every signed mixed kernel Put CalP_t(z)=product_(r=0)^t(z-c_r) and B_t=(-1)^t s_t^2. At a simple node define sigma_j=x^t nu_j CalP_t'(c_j)/B_t. At a double node c=c_j=c_l put Q_j=CalP_t/(z-c)^2 and sigma_j=x^t nu_j Q_j(c)/B_t, rho_j=-(d-2j)/[2(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))], eta_j=rho_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). (6) These are the actual Christoffel--Darboux measures. In particular sigma_j never vanishes. The bilinear Gram block of (v_j,w_j) is sigma_j [[0,1],[1,eta_j]], with inverse sigma_j^-1 [[-eta_j,1],[1,0]]. The value rho_j is the spectral logarithmic derivative of the original normalized crossing R/kappa. For EVERY auxiliary color n and either sign, the entire contribution of a double node to R^epsilon L_n is therefore kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon /sigma_j * { [l_n'(c)+(epsilon rho_j-eta_j)l_n(c)] v_j v_j^T +l_n(c)(v_j w_j^T+w_j v_j^T) }. (7) A simple node contributes kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon l_n(c_j) v_j v_j^T/sigma_j. (8) Proof: in the actual Jordan chain, a function A(Omega) has matrix [[A(c),A'(c)],[0,A(c)]]. Multiplying by the displayed bilinear inverse gives sigma^-1[(A'-eta A)vv^T+A(vw^T+wv^T)]. Here A(c)=kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon l_n(c) and A'(c)=kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon[l_n'(c)+epsilon rho_j l_n(c)]. This proves (7), including epsilon=-1. It is a bilinear physical identity; conjugating a column would give the wrong coupon. Summing (7),(8) over ALL distinct nodes gives the original full matrix. In particular n=N collapses to the complete-circle formula: at a double node l_N(c)=0, leaving its specified first normal, and at an unpaired simple node l_N(c)=0. The self-paired simple value is treated separately. This reduction checks, rather than assumes, the complete-image formula. ## 4. Color dependence and uniform polynomial factors The color dependence is explicit and coherent. With theta_j=(2j+1)pi/N, l_n(c_j)=(-1)^(n-1) sum_(b=0)^(n-1) q^[(2j+1)(n-1-2b)]. (9) All its n-dependent phases remain. The derivative is the derivative of the SAME polynomial in z; it is not a derivative of a chosen eigenvalue lift. Away from sin theta=0 it can also be written l_n'(2cos theta)=(-1)^(n-1) [sin(n theta)cos theta-n cos(n theta)sin theta] / [2sin(theta)^3]. (10) At the odd self-node c=-2 use its polynomial limit, with l_n(-2)=n. There is no 0/0 cancellation left to a numerical prescription. Uniformly for every 1<=n<=N and every real node in [-2,2], |l_n(c)|<=n, |l_n'(c)|<=n(n^2-1)/6. (11) For the second bound group the finite Laurent expression for U into pairs 2cos(m theta). Its z derivative is m sin(m theta)/sin theta, whose absolute value is at most m^2 by the finite geometric sum. The sum of these positive-frequency squares is n(n^2-1)/6. This also proves the endpoint bound by continuity, without dividing by an endpoint sine. Every H_b in (5) has magnitude O(N^2(1+log N)), since sin(pi r/N)>=2min(r,N-r)/N. The remaining exponents in (5) are O(N^2). The denominator of (4) has modulus at least eight. Consequently, with Ebar_(t,j,u) the sum of the two positive q-Hahn envelopes at j,l, |v_(j,u)|<=E_(t,j,u), |w_(j,u)|<=C N^2(1+log N) Ebar_(t,j,u). (12) The known node gap bound also gives |rho_j|<=N^2/8 and |eta_j|<=C N^3. Thus every color and every extra normal factor in (7) is polynomially controlled, uniformly over the ENTIRE physical color interval, with normal order at most one on each local column. The inverse measure is NOT hidden in this statement. If a_j=|1-Q^(2j+1)|, its exact magnitudes are unpaired simple: |sigma_j|=s_(t-j)s_(t+j+1)/(s_t^2 a_j), double: |sigma_j|=N s_(t-j)s_(t+j-d)/(s_t^2 a_j^2), odd self-paired: |sigma_j|=N s_(t-j)^2/s_t^2. (13) Its phase is explicitly fixed by (6) or the simple product. All factorial indices are below N. Therefore an all-input bound for (7),(8) is a fixed polynomial times the sum of the products of the stated column envelopes divided by |sigma_j|. The exponential growth of those factorial profiles has not been proved to disappear. ## 5. Arbitrary fixed plats and the remaining filling problem Insert (7),(8) at every original augmented region of any fixed 2k-head plat and perform the literal wire contractions. Retain the original cup, ordinary caps, unrestricted marked cap, pivots and external line. The whole-source integer-degree argument permitting the final marked-pair restriction is the same as in the complete compiler. This yields an exact finite formula for EVERY physical auxiliary-color tuple (n_1,...,n_b), not merely a coefficientwise upper envelope or a complete-color value. Expanding (4),(5),(9) makes all color/normal couplings explicit: they are the original finite Fourier factors, factorial weights and bounded-order q-harmonic prefactors. For a fixed diagram the number of discrete variables and the total number of normal factors are fixed. Contracting does not increase that normal order with N. One may also use the finite polynomial values (1) directly; the two expressions are identities of the original matrices. This supplies a concrete all-color input to the existing exact full-twist resolution for any fixed signed slopes p_i. A prospective geometric threshold T(D) concerns the fixed skeleton and the sizes of those integer twists, not the quantum level N. The compiler alone gives no such threshold or nonzero geometric period. In particular an explicit finite formula is NOT automatically the uniform holomorphic packet required by analytic filling transfer. The naive expression sin(n theta)/sin theta is singular at the odd self-node theta=pi for nonintegral n; its cancellation at integer n does not authorize that continuation. A valid complex-color packet must specify its whole finite continuation and prove its uniform estimates, preserving all these endpoint and normal contributions. Likewise the polynomial bounds in (11),(12) leave the column and inverse-measure factorial rates present. A geometric global gap, source-preserving complex deformation, selected nonzero amplitude germ and actual marked regulator identification are separate tasks. The new result removes the UNKNOWN mixed local kernel and normal formula; it does not replace those analytic and geometric proofs. Audit: [generic normals and all original mixed signed operators](../experiments/audit_actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.py). Fresh exact finite-field checks pass N=2,...,12: 143 physical blocks, 2,904 canonical value entries, 1,177 generic-confluence normal entries, and 231 full signed mixed-color operator identities. The normal columns from (2)--(5) are compared with independent continuant derivatives. title: The actual mixed crossing-circle longitude, flag and central sign
text: # The actual mixed crossing-circle longitude, flag and central sign 29 October 2026. The literal auxiliary loop [2,1,1,2] has the crossing-disk preferred longitude, with no hidden meridian power. For the actual auxiliary meridian M_aux=-q^j and H=Q^(N-j), the source coordinate L_H=(H-X)/(1-HX) gives preferred SL2 longitude lambda=-L_H^(-1), centered longitude ell=-lambda=L_H^(-1). (0) The minus is forced by the original ordinary auxiliary pivot. It is not a choice of a different geometric component. This note proves the mixed local transport/framing certificate and records the exact central character. A geometric representation lift and regulator calibration must still use that character explicitly. ## 1. The literal mixed universal crossing and its color contiguity Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, eta=q^(1/2), and colors x_1=q^alpha, x_2=q^beta. In the factorial basis, a positive checked mixed crossing sends input (a,b) to (b+k,a-k). Its coefficient is EXACTLY \[ r^+_{\alpha,\beta}(a,b,k) =q^{\alpha\beta/2}(-1)^k q^{k^2-k} x_1^{-b-2k}x_2^{-a+k}Q^{(a-k)(b+k)} \frac{F_{b+k}}{F_bF_k}(Qx_1^2/A;Q)_k, \quad A=Q^a,\ B=Q^b,\ C=Q^k. \tag{1} \] All indices have their actual physical support and F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The half-Cartan is the unwrapped q^(alpha beta/2), not an inferred square root after reducing indices. Derive (1) directly by expanding the finite universal nilpotent factor followed by its full Cartan: Ecal_(a-1,a)=q^(-1)(x_1^(-1)-x_1 Q^(-a+1)), F_(b+1,b)=1-Q^(b+1), q^(k(k-1)/2)rho^k/[k]! =(-1)^k q^(k^2)rho^(2k)/F_k. The two independent positive color shifts therefore obey \[ \frac{r^+_{\alpha+1,\beta}}{r^+_{\alpha,\beta}} =K_{2,\mathrm{in}}^{-1/2}\tau_q^{-1},\qquad \frac{r^+_{\alpha,\beta+1}}{r^+_{\alpha,\beta}} =K_{1,\mathrm{out}}^{1/2}, \quad \tau_q=\frac{BC}{x_2} \frac{1-Qx_1^2/A}{1-Qx_1^2C/A}. \tag{2} \] These are common-index identities: changing the ordinary dimension does not authorize dropping its new boundary states. At zeros the first relation means the CLEARED finite-product identity (1-Qx_1^2/A)r_shift =K_2^(-1/2) x_2/(BC)(1-Qx_1^2 C/A)r. It remains valid when a displayed ratio is 0/0. Every square root in (2) is its literal q^(H/2) from (1). ## 2. Four mixed crossings cancel the full Cartan color density Start with ordered strand labels (A,B,C), where C is the auxiliary color j. Chronological positive crossings [2,1,1,2] give (A,B,C) -> (A,C,B) -> (C,A,B) -> (A,C,B) -> (A,B,C). The auxiliary is UNDER first B then A, and OVER first A then B. Each main head's K after its first crossing is exactly its K before its second crossing. Hence the two K^(1/2) factors in (2) cancel the two inverse factors EXACTLY, even before taking q to one. No square-root sign is chosen from a cyclic exponent. The original auxiliary closing pivot is g_j=K_j^(1-N), with NO 1/j. On its physical weights g_j=(-1)^(j-1)K_j at the root. The shift j->j+1 changes a common closing weight by q^(1-N). Consequently its common-state source multiplier is q^(1-N) (tau_(3,q)tau_(4,q))^(-1). (3) The classical central factor is -1, since q^(1-N)=-q. This factor must be kept when interpreting a color derivative. Taking only the Cartan monodromy and silently replacing the pivot by K would miss it. There is also a FULL all-input identity retaining every dimension endpoint and every root normal jet: L_j=(-1)^(j-1)U_(j-1)(Omega/2), L_(j+1)+Omega L_j+L_(j-1)=0. (4) It is the proved literal mixed-loop theorem, not an N-dimensional ADO replacement for a separate ordinary component. Thus the characteristic positive color-shift roots Lambda satisfy Lambda+Lambda^(-1)=-Tr(P), consistently with (3). Formula (3) fixes their flag and orientation on a regular chart; (4) retains the states that are not common under a dimension change. ## 3. Mixed-color eigenvector transport fixes the actual flag Use the original classical triangular matrices b_+(K,e)=[[K,e],[0,1]], b_-(K,f)=[[1,0],[-Kf,K]], G=b_-^(-1)b_+, K_i=x_i/A_i, e_i=(x_i^(-1)-K_i)p_i, f_i=(1-A_i)/p_i. Their Casimir is x_i+x_i^(-1), without assuming equal colors. The actual universal crossing has the Gauss/Hurwitz map d=1-e_1 f_2, K'_1=K_2 d, K'_2=K_1/d, f'_1=K_1f_2/d, e'_2=e_1/(K_2d), e'_1=[d e_2+e_1(dK_2-K_2^(-1))]/K_1, f'_2=K_2[d f_1+f_2(d/K_1-K_1)]. This map and its three triangular factorizations are independent of the individual Casimir values; it swaps x_1 and x_2. Let H_i be its prefix-transported raw meridians and mu_i=-H_i the actual meridians. The global flag vector v_i is the lower-prefix transport of (p_i,1)^t. It has mu_i eigenvalue -x_i^(-1), the M_i^(-1) flag for M_i=-x_i classically. Direct matrix multiplication, with different x_1 and x_2 retained, gives v'_under=-mu_over^(-1)v_under, v'_over=tau_+ v_over, tau_+=BC/x_2 * (1-x_1^2/A)/(1-x_1^2C/A). (5) For example p'_under=(p_2-e_1)/K_1, while tau_+=1/[K_2(1-x_1^(-1)p_1 f_2)]. These prove (5) directly. They agree with the q->1 limit of (2), including its orientation. ## 4. The disk word is preferred, not a meridional shear In global ACTUAL meridians the positive Hurwitz rule is (A,B)->(A^(-1)BA,A). Multiplying the four specified moves gives C_out=P^(-1)CP, P=BA; A_out=C^(-1)AC, B_out=C^(-1)BC when [C,P]=1. (6) Closing the auxiliary therefore imposes [C,P]=1. Its underpass vector transport is W=A^(-1)B^(-1)=P^(-1): B is encountered first and A second, in the literal operator order. Including its two overpasses, flag closure reads v_C=(tau_3 tau_4)P^(-1)v_C. (7) The positively oriented blackboard parallel of C has word W^(-1)=P. This is checked by pushing the parallel across the two underpasses: the inverse vector transport records their positively oriented puncture meridians in reverse product order. It is also the boundary of the crossing disk with its two punctures removed. The loop has NO auxiliary self-crossing. Its self-writhe is zero, so the disk parallel has zero self-linking; no power of C is subtracted or inserted. Thus the preferred crossing-disk longitude is lambda_C=P=BA. (8) The disk may have nonzero linking with other components; that does not change its zero SELF-linking or its preferred framing. If a target leg is dualized, its oriented puncture meridian is inverted by the actual duality, rather than by altering (8) with a power of C. On the M_C^(-1) flag, (7) gives eigen(lambda_C)=tau_3 tau_4. On the positive M_C flag the eigenvalue is the inverse: lambda=(tau_3 tau_4)^(-1). (9) Equations (3),(9) prove that the actual positive j shift has symbol Lambda=-lambda. Its complete central sign is therefore fixed, not selected from a metric cusp shape. ## 5. The main half twist and actual quarter-turn retain this framing The original base box is R^(-1)L_j. The retained R^(-1) crosses only the two MAIN strands. Its Hurwitz action preserves their product P, and algebraically it commutes with the Casimir loop L_j. It creates no auxiliary self-crossing and does not change (8) by a meridional power. Its full original Cartan phase remains in the box; it is not removed from the scalar source. There is an elementary surgery-coordinate check of the slope sign. Let theta run along the positively oriented auxiliary meridian and phi along the oriented boundary of its crossing disk. Straightening a filling meridian (theta,phi)=(t,pt) uses phi'=phi-p theta. Hence one positive normal turn rotates the two disk punctures by -p FULL turns. In the displayed checked-braid convention its inserted tangle is R^(-2p). The retained R^(-1) therefore gives R^(-(2p+1)), while the primitive killed curve is mu_C+p lambda_C. This derives the integer sign; it is not assigned by matching an asymptotic volume. The genuine unscaled quarter-turn is formed with the original main cup and ordinary main cap. It bends target legs by their actual Hopf duality and is an orientation-preserving movement of this ribbon tangle; the auxiliary circle and its crossing disk move together. It introduces no auxiliary curl or new auxiliary pivot. Consequently the image of the disk word (8) is still its preferred zero-self-linking longitude. This does NOT assert that rotating a polynomial is multiplicative. All statements concern the literal typed turn of R^(-1)L_j with its actual cup/cap. The metric cusp has the two possible half-twist meridians differing by one disk longitude. Once the port representation lift is made, (8)--(9) fix the longitude's sign/flag, so the source derivative may calibrate which corner meridian represents the retained R^(-1). It is not permissible to infer (8) from the cusp derivative alone. ## 6. Match the actual mixed source and retain the central character For j=N-h, the literal auxiliary meridian is M_aux=-q^j=q^(-h), so H=Q^h=M_aux^(-2). The source phase has G_(LogH)=Log L_H, L_H=(H-X)/(1-HX). The positive j shift sends M_aux->qM_aux and H->Q^(-1)H. Its symbol is therefore L_H^(-1). Combining with the ACTUAL mixed pivot and disk certificate (3),(9) proves precisely (0), rather than identifying a same-color cut theorem with a closed ordinary loop. In particular Tr(P)=-(L_H+L_H^(-1)), M_aux=e^u, centered ell=e^v=L_H^(-1), preferred lambda=-ell, Log lambda=pi i+v. (10) The sign agrees with the literal circle recurrence (4); at complete color L_H=1, the preferred SL2 disk longitude has eigenvalue -1. The squared geometric peripheral coordinates are M_aux^2=H^(-1), lambda^2=L_H^(-2). Their uncentered logarithmic lift retains its 2pi i deck shift. Centering lambda by -1 is represented on the PHYSICAL color lattice by the explicit character (-1)^(j-1)=(-1)^(N-1)(-1)^h from g_j. At complex color this character must be transported together with the full filling kernel; it is not an identically one gauge. A preferred logarithmic action may differ from the centered action by the corresponding +/-pi i LogH term, whose two choices differ by 2pi i LogH and agree on the physical lattice. It must not be dropped separately from its kernel or regulator trivialization. Finally the actual filled saddle equation LogH+2p LogL_H=2pi i m gives M_aux ell^p=(-1)^m, hence M_aux lambda^p=(-1)^(p+m). (11) Thus its PSL2 relation is exactly the primitive disk-framed slope mu_C+p lambda_C, with the retained half twist in its base meridian. The displayed central lift is part of the marking; no replacement of p by p+1 or hidden longitude shear was used. Geometric action calibration must retain this lift and its explicit source character. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.py) compares (1) with the original mixed universal matrices, checks both independent color contiguities and literal four-crossing path weights, and verifies the unequal-color eigenvector and disk-word transport.

title: Exact full-dilogarithm circle moments with a controlled original boundary source
text: # Exact full-dilogarithm circle moments with a controlled original boundary source 28 October 2026. The original finite Euler atoms are exactly moments of the full rational Faddeev dilogarithm, with a specified radial correction. At radius one the correction has polynomial operator norm in the actual unit-shift metric. The function itself is regular across every intervening cyclotomic root on its selected logarithmic strip. This removes the norm-one cyclic function's artificial root barriers without discarding the original coefficient source. This does **not** identify the original knot period with a bare Faddeev state integral. The radial corrections remain part of its relative cycle. Polynomial local operator norms do not imply a smaller exponential rate after multiplication by the other crossing factors. ## 1. Use the full literature function, including its central period Put N>=2, epsilon=+1 or -1, Q_epsilon=exp(epsilon*2*pi*i/N), and V_epsilon(t)=(1-t^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(ell=1)^(N-1) (1-Q_epsilon^ell*t)^(-ell/N). All these factors are anchored at t=0. On the logarithmic cover write t=exp(z) and define Psi_epsilon(z)=V_epsilon(exp z) (1-exp(Nz))^((N+1)/(2N)+epsilon*i*z/(2*pi)) exp[epsilon*i*Li_2(exp(Nz))/(2*pi*N)]. (1) For Re z<0 every logarithm and dilogarithm in (1), except the explicitly displayed z, is its convergent power-series branch. The independently proved [rational evaluation](rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md) identifies Psi_+(z) with Phi_(1/sqrt(N))(sqrt(N)*z/(2*pi)-c_(1/sqrt(N))). (2) The negative version is its conjugate-reflected function. Thus (1) uses the literature function with its fixed normalization, not a new invariant or an arbitrarily chosen periodic multiplier. The underlying rational evaluation is standard; the proof in the linked note is independent. For coverage see [Garoufalidis--Kashaev, 1411.6062](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062). Conversion of Kashaev sums into full-dilogarithm integrals also predates this note; no novelty is claimed for that general idea. The first N ordinary coefficients of V_epsilon are v_(epsilon,a)=(-1)^a Q_epsilon^(a(a-1)/2) /(Q_epsilon;Q_epsilon)_a, 0<=a<N. Equation (1) gives the stronger local statement Psi_epsilon(z)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) v_(epsilon,a) exp(az) +O_N((1+|z|)exp(N Re z)) (3) uniformly on any bounded imaginary interval as Re z tends to -infinity. The omitted logarithmic terms do not vanish in an ordinary fixed-radius Cauchy integral. Their exact contribution is the radial correction below. ## 2. The selected full turn is regular, including the unit circle For Re z<0, (1) immediately gives the marked monodromy Psi_epsilon(z+epsilon*2*pi*i) =Psi_epsilon(z)/(1-exp(Nz)). (4) The elementary quantum shift, with the logarithmic lift retained, is Psi_epsilon(z+epsilon*2*pi*i/N) =Psi_epsilon(z)/(1-exp z). (5) These are different statements from norm-one cyclic transport. The full central factor in (1) is necessary for both. There are no zeros or poles in the open strip 0<epsilon*Im z<2*pi. (6) One can check the apparent cyclotomic singularities directly, without assuming a cancellation of fractional powers. Differentiating (1) cancels its two logarithmic terms and gives the meromorphic expression d_z log Psi_epsilon =sum_(ell=1)^(N-1) (ell/N) Q_epsilon^ell exp(z)/(1-Q_epsilon^ell exp(z)) -N(1+epsilon*i*z/(2*pi)) exp(Nz)/(1-exp(Nz)). (7) At z=epsilon*2*pi*i*j/N, 1<=j<N, the two residues are -(N-j)/N and 1-j/N, so they cancel. The derivative is holomorphic there and the continued function is nonzero. At z=0 it has residue one: Psi has a simple zero. At z=epsilon*2*pi*i the residue is zero and Psi is nonzero. These statements also follow from (2), but (7) checks the exact norm and the selected strip directly. Consequently the path z=log R+epsilon*i*theta, 0<=theta<=2*pi, is a regular lifted circular path for EVERY R>0, including R=1. When R=1 its initial endpoint is a zero, and its terminal endpoint is regular. The radial correction has a removable singularity at t=1. ### A uniform geometric phase on the whole selected strip The full function also has the correct leading phase beyond the unit disk. For every delta>0 and delta<=epsilon*Im z<=2*pi-delta, uniformly in ALL Re z, the independently derived defining-integral estimate in [the literature-state audit](literature_state_volume.md#21-a-uniform-complex-remainder-on-an-entire-horizontal-strip) gives Psi_epsilon(z)=(1-exp z)^(1/2) exp[Li_2(exp z)/(epsilon*2*pi*i/N)] (1+O_delta(1/N)). (7a) For epsilon=+1 substitute b=N^(-1/2) and w=z-i*pi*(1+1/N) into that estimate. Its leading argument is -exp(w)=exp(z-pi*i/N). Taylor expansion by this exact half-step gives Li_2(exp(z-pi*i/N))/(2*pi*i/N) =Li_2(exp z)/(2*pi*i/N)+(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O_delta(1/N). The second logarithmic derivative of Li_2 is bounded on the smaller angular strip, for every real part. The original defining-integral remainder is O_delta(1/N) there as well. This proves (7a), including its nonzero amplitude. Conjugate reflection proves the negative case. All branches are those continued through the selected strip. On smaller strips Cauchy's estimate gives the same remainder control for every fixed number of logarithmic derivatives. Thus (7a) applies at any nonreal positive geometric shape, irrespective of whether its modulus is below, equal to, or above one. This is a uniform statement about the actual full function in (9), not an analytic continuation of the norm-one cyclic atom's disk asymptotic. It still does not assert a uniform estimate on the radial edges at the strip's boundary; their exact bound is retained separately below. #### Independent finite-product verification on compact subsets There is also a direct proof of (7a) on every compact subset of 0<Im z<2*pi, using only (7). Put s_*=1+i*z/(2*pi), R_z(s)=exp(z+2*pi*i*s)/(1-exp(z+2*pi*i*s)), g_z(s)=(s-s_*)R_z(s). The finite root identity sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)R_z(ell/N)=N exp(Nz)/(1-exp(Nz)) rewrites the EXACT logarithmic derivative as d_z log Psi_+(z)=sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)g_z(ell/N). (7b) At s=s_* the apparent pole of g is removable. Its other poles are s=s_*+k, nonzero integers k. Since 0<Re s_*<1 in this strip, on any compact z-set the function g is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on a fixed complex neighborhood of [0,1]. This remains true at Re z=0, including every apparent cyclotomic root. Equation (7b) extends across those points by these removable values. Euler--Maclaurin, with a uniform first remainder, now gives sum g_z(ell/N)=N integral_0^1 g_z(s)ds +(g_z(0)-g_z(1))/2+O_K(1/N). For Re z<0 the convergent Fourier series proves integral g_z=-Log(1-exp z)/(2*pi*i): the constant Fourier coefficient of R_z is zero and integral s exp(2*pi*i*m*s)ds is 1/(2*pi*i*m). Holomorphic continuation proves the same formula throughout the strip. Also g_z(0)-g_z(1) =-exp z/(1-exp z). Hence d_z log Psi_+(z)=-N Log(1-exp z)/(2*pi*i) -exp z/[2(1-exp z)]+O_K(1/N). (7c) Integrate (7c) from a fixed left-half-plane anchor. At that anchor the convergent small-disk expansion already gives log Psi_+=Li_2(exp z)/(2*pi*i/N)+(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O(1/N). Bounded paths in a compact substrip preserve the O_K(1/N) error and fix its logarithmic mark, proving (7a) there. Cauchy's estimate on larger compact sets gives every fixed derivative version. Conjugate reflection treats epsilon=-1. This finite-product proof is independent of the stronger all-real-parts defining-integral estimate above. ## 3. Exact generalized coefficient extraction For a<N and R>0 define B_(epsilon,a)(R)=1/(2*pi) integral_0^(2*pi) Psi_epsilon(log R+epsilon*i*theta) (R exp(epsilon*i*theta))^(-a) dtheta, E_(epsilon,a)(R)=epsilon/(2*pi*i) integral_0^R Psi_epsilon(log t) t^(N-a-1)/(1-t^N) dt. (8) The function on the real radial path is its continuation from t<1. At t=1 the quotient in (8) has its removable value. Then exactly v_(epsilon,a)=B_(epsilon,a)(R)-E_(epsilon,a)(R). (9) Proof: take the rectangular logarithmic contour between Re z=log r and Re z=log R, with imaginary endpoints 0 and epsilon*2*pi. Its vertical sides are the two lifted circles. Pair its horizontal sides using (4). The resulting radial difference is Psi_epsilon(log t)-Psi_epsilon(log t+epsilon*2*pi*i) =-t^N Psi_epsilon(log t)/(1-t^N). Use the orientation factor epsilon/(2*pi*i). By (3), the inner vertical integral tends to v_(epsilon,a), since its error is O_N(r^(N-a)(1+|log r|)). The paired radial integral converges at zero for precisely the required indices a<N. Equation (7) justifies continuation through R=1 and arbitrary positive R. This proves (9) with its sign and every scalar fixed. Thus the coefficient source is a relative cycle consisting of one lifted circle and one paired radial edge. It is not the circle alone. ## 4. Exact radial modulus and a uniform boundary bound For 0<t<1, conjugate-pair the finite factors in V_epsilon. This gives |V_epsilon(t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N)^(-1/N). The remaining modulus in (1) is (1-t^N)^((N+1)/N); the explicitly imaginary logarithmic and dilogarithmic terms have modulus one. Hence |Psi_epsilon(log t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N). (10) In fact (10) holds for all t>0. For t>1 its two factors are both negative. To check this extension without choosing fractional powers across the zero, take the real part of (7). On the real radial line, the paired finite terms give d_(log t) log|Psi_epsilon| =-t/[2(1-t)]-N t^N/[2(1-t^N)]. This is the logarithmic derivative of the positive square root of |(1-t)(1-t^N)|. The simple zero at t=1 fixes the same multiplicative constant on both sides by continuity of its nonzero first derivative. For 0<R<=1, (10) gives the UNIFORM estimate |E_(epsilon,a)(R)| <=1/(2*pi) integral_0^R t^(N-a-1) sqrt((1-t)/(1-t^N)) dt <=R^(N-a)/[2*pi*(N-a)]. (11) This includes a=N-1 and R=1; no fixed-distance-from-the-endpoint condition is needed. For R>1 the same calculation yields the explicit bound |E_(epsilon,a)(R)| <=1/[2*pi*(N-a)] +1/(2*pi) integral_1^R t^((N-1)/2-a) dt. (12) Here t^N-1 >= t^(N-1)(t-1). In particular an exterior-radius radial term need not have polynomial size. Its possible exponential rate is retained in (12), rather than discarded in a geometric deformation. If T^N=0 and ||T||<=1, define B_epsilon(T) and E_epsilon(T) using the finite resolvent (tI-T)^(-1). Equivalently sum (8) times T^a. Then (9) and (11), at R=1, give v_(epsilon,N)(T)=B_epsilon(T)-E_epsilon(T), ||E_epsilon(T)|| <= H_N/(2*pi), H_N=sum_(j=1)^N 1/j. (13) This bound is on the FULL source correction, not on its logarithm. The nilpotent resolvent retains the finite original head and introduces no unknown scalar normalization. ### 4a. The shifted full turn and its exact negative-ray source There is a second useful coefficient cycle for the SAME full function. Write Psi=Psi_+ and v_a=v_(+,a). For every R>0 and 0<=a<N put C_a(R)=1/(2*pi) integral_(-pi)^pi Psi(log R+i theta)(R exp(i theta))^(-a) dtheta, J_a(R)=(-1)^(N-a)/(2*pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t+i*pi) t^(N-a-1) dt. Then, with the indicated logarithmic marks, exactly v_a=C_a(R)-J_a(R). (13a) The shifted rectangle is holomorphic even though it contains zeros: in the lower half-strip, a cyclotomic point z=-2*pi*i*j/N has residues -j/N and 1+j/N in (7), hence a simple zero of Psi, not a pole. The upper half-strip has the cancellations already proved. Thus the rectangle with imaginary endpoints -pi and pi requires no additional pole residues. Its paired rays satisfy Psi(log t-i*pi)=(1-(-t)^N)Psi(log t+i*pi). Substituting this into the same rectangular argument as Section 3 cancels the central denominator in its radial difference. The phase of (t exp(-i*pi))^(N-a) is exactly (-1)^(N-a), giving (13a). The inner circle tends to v_a for the same reason as before. The selected upper negative ray has the particularly simple EXACT modulus, for ALL t>0, |Psi(log t+i*pi)|^2=1+t. (13b) Indeed in (7) put exp z=-t. Pairing the finite terms gives real part (1/2)[N(-t)^N/(1-(-t)^N)+t/(1+t)]. The second term of (7) cancels its first summand because Re(1+i(log t+i*pi)/(2*pi))=1/2. The remaining logarithmic derivative is t/[2(1+t)]. The anchor Psi->1 at t->0 fixes the constant. When N is even and t=1, the apparent terms cancel at a regular interior-strip point, so the same identity extends through it. Consequently |J_a(R)| <= (1/(2*pi)) integral_0^R sqrt(1+t)t^(N-a-1) dt <=sqrt(1+R) R^(N-a)/[2*pi(N-a)]. (13c) At R=1 this again gives a polynomial original-head bound: the nilpotent unit-shift correction has norm at most sqrt(2)H_N/(2*pi). For R>1 the factor R^(N-a) is retained; no exterior polynomial bound is asserted. The epsilon=-1 identity is the conjugate-reflection of (13a)-(13c). Thus BOTH full angular choices [0,2*pi] and [-pi,pi] have exact original coefficient cycles. In particular the cut prescribed by [the all-radius angular maximum theorem](all_radius_angular_geometric_cycle_and_polarization.md) need not be imposed as a new source choice: its matching ray is specified by (9) or (13a). This fixes the local coefficient cycle, not its whole-word geometric dominance. Carrying those ray terms through the actual positive chart, and proving their total contribution cannot cancel the geometric term, remains necessary. ## 5. Application to every original crossing and its boundary factors At the complete unit meridian the actual transfer shifts have norm at most one in the standard balanced head metric. Their scalar color factors have modulus one. For the actual Q=e^(2*pi*i/N), exactly u_(Q,N)(T)=v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)T). (14) This is the finite factorial reflection, not an asymptotic equality. Equations (9), (13), and (14) therefore treat both types of actual transfer with the literature full function and their retained radial sources. In particular no reciprocal full function with a divergent radial endpoint is needed to represent u. All original factorial diagonals have the same coefficient realization: 1/F_a=Q^(-a) v_(-,a), F_a=N Q^(N-1-a) v_(+,N-1-a), 0<=a<N. (15) At R=1 the radial-error operator norms for these DIAGONAL kernels are, respectively, at most 1/(2*pi) and N/(2*pi). These are maxima of the coefficient bounds, not sums. The positive factorial's original factor N and phase are retained exactly. Insert (9) and (14)-(15) in the strict original signed crossing word. Keep its Gaussian, Cartan, framing, peripheral and original input/output functionals. Expanding the finite product gives an EXACT finite sum over choices of circle or radial source at each atom. The number of choices is fixed by the word, independently of N. Each term is an ordinary full-dilogarithm relative period with the original finite rational kernel/source. Absolute convergence at each fixed N follows coefficientwise from the finite nilpotent resolvents and (8)-(10). This applies to the full original knot scalar, not just an unpointed operator. It does not require a nonzero knot value or division by one. The previous ordinary-Gaussian replacement can also be retained: its diagonal acts on the same finite degrees and the initial domination argument is unchanged. This construction is distinct from the [Hardy forest reduction](actual_hardy_forest_residue_reduction.md). It supplies full-function relative moments on the original finite heads; one must not replace every scalar atom in the unwrapped Laurent graph by (1) and assume that its nonanalytic logarithmic tails are source-null. The radial terms in (9) are exactly what such a substitution would miss. ## 6. What this changes on the path to the geometric period The cyclic atom's accumulating root divisors are not intrinsic barriers to the selected full-function transport. Equations (1), (7), and (9) give the full dilogarithm and its exact coefficient cycle, with an explicit locally polynomial correction at radius one. The independently proved Fourier and pentagon identities for that full function can now be tested against this specified source, rather than against an unspecified state integral or an assumed equivalence of formal jets. Two conclusions do NOT follow. First, a positive geometric change of coordinates must carry the radial edges and finite resolvents as well as the circle integrand. Second, a polynomial norm bound for one radial factor does not make its whole-word contraction exponentially small: the remaining factors and their source can still carry the volume rate. The nonzero geometric image and the global comparison with the marked Rivin period remain unproved. Those, rather than a further choice of local quantum-dilogarithm normalization, are the next required steps. ## 7. Reproducible checks [The main audit](../experiments/audit_actual_modular_dilog_circle.py) checks 30 exact shift/monodromy/modulus instances, 16 entire circle-plus-radial moments, 14 original diagonal/reflection families, and 12 full-strip phase instances at interior, unit, and exterior radii. The moments use the full function, not its truncated polynomial; the bare circle is explicitly checked to give the wrong coefficient. [Results](../experiments/actual_modular_dilog_circle_results.json). [The shifted-circle audit](../experiments/audit_actual_modular_shifted_circle.py) separately checks the negative-ray formula and its exact modulus. These checks supplement the all-level proofs above. Neither audit computes a geometric cycle coefficient or verifies a volume limit.

title: The geometric contribution and all Fourier charges
status: Nonzero geometric contribution; complementary estimate remains
text:
# The geometric contribution and all Fourier charges For a fixed link diagram, the exact finite formula is a coefficient in face variables followed by a linear functional in each crossing variable. Its local polynomial splits into three specified pieces. The central piece, called CROSS in the source formulas, contains paths passing through the middle of the finite recurrence. The other two pieces contain paths restricted to one side. Selecting CROSS at every crossing region gives a contribution to the original invariant; it does not define another topological invariant. This note proves a nonzero asymptotic for that entire geometric contribution, including all Fourier charges, both level parities, the derivatives at repeated spectral nodes, and the original scalar factors. The diagram may have cups and caps between crossing regions: it need not be a flat plat. Its white triangulation must be a simple sphere with the specified matching and marked strand edge. The local balance inequalities used to bound the other two pieces are not needed here. The [geometric companion](actual_morse_geometric_contribution.md) constructs the actual complement and identifies the selected action with its hyperbolic volume after sufficiently long fixed signed fillings. A strict estimate for the full contribution minus this geometric term remains a separate requirement for a full-invariant volume theorem. ## 1. Exact assumptions and statement Fix a finite connected Morse diagram whose actual white triangulation is a simple sphere, with its actual matching, cyclic orders, crossing-disk frames and marked MAIN edge. Let the marked edge join the two protected white faces \(u,v\). The diagram has \(R\) matching edges, \(R+2\) white faces, and \(R\) ordinary face targets. Assume the labeled positive convex right-angled certificate and its marked complete packing are supplied. Set the protected curvatures to zero and retain the same positive finite curvatures \(ho_f\) at every occurrence of each other face. The geometric existence of this certificate is a separate input to the present analytic argument. The exact general Morse source identity is the one in [A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md), §§5–6, equivalently the finite-source part of [Balanced terminal decorations and volume limits beyond tangle-operation trees](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md), §5. In particular all physical cups, caps, the unrestricted marked row, the integrated even-level coset and the original component/framing factors are retained. With \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), define \[  egin{split} C_N( oldsymbol\delta) &=\left[\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^dight] \left.\prod_{e=1}^{R} H_{V_N,\mathrm C}(L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e};\sigma_e) ight|_{L_u=L_v=0},\ \sigma_e&=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e). \end{split} 	ag{1} \] Here CROSS means the literal central-cut path support. It is selected by polynomial linearity after the full physical source has been identified; it is not declared an independent covariant coupon. Write \(P_{\mathrm C}=(-1)^dH_{V_N,\mathrm C}\) for the positive endpoint convention. Thus (1) is the raw coefficient and contains \((-1)^{dR}\). For fixed nonzero signed crossing powers \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\), its exact all-CROSS period is \[  egin{split} I_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm C} ={}&q^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-i)^R \sum_{ oldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \left(\prod_e\ell_eight) (-1)^{(N+1)\sum_e\ell_e}\ &\quad	imes\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} C_N( oldsymbol\delta)\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_e) \exp\left\{N\sum_e (\pi i n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\ell_e\delta_e)ight\} d oldsymbol\delta . \end{split} 	ag{2} \] No additional power of \(N\), modified dimension, or spectral square-root Jacobian appears. The displayed \(q\) power is the original unwrapped scalar \(\exp(\pi i d^2\sum n_e/(4N))\). An exterior framing/component character multiplies the raw contraction when converting to the specified invariant convention; it has modulus one at complete color. The full one-cut modified convention additionally retains its stated \(i^{N+3}/N\). These conventions are not changed by a CROSS projection. There is a fixed small complex polydisk and finite holomorphic actions \(A_N\), face Hessians \(H_N\), such that the following two source estimates hold: \[ C_N(\delta)=  rac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{NA_N(\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\delta)}} (1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{H1} \] uniformly and holomorphically on that polydisk, and, for every \(\eta>0\), \[ |C_N(\delta)|\le e^{N(\Phi-\gamma_\eta)} \quad	ext{if }\max_e|\operatorname{Re}\delta_e|\ge\eta, \quad\operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in[-1/2,1/2], \quad|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le	au_\eta, 	ag{H2} \] for some \(\gamma_\eta,	au_\eta>0\) and all sufficiently large \(N\). All fixed derivatives satisfy the corresponding bound on smaller domains. Here \[ A_N\longrightarrow A_0,\qquad A_0(0)=\Phi,\qquad A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_e),\quad C_e>0, 	ag{3} \] with every fixed derivative; \(A_N\) is separately even and real on the real chart. The marked complete action satisfies \(2\pi\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)\) under the supplied geometric certificate and its calibrated source action. There is a diagram-dependent \(n_0\) such that, for every fixed independently signed vector with \(|n_e|\ge n_0\), the entire period (2) has the relative asymptotic \[  egin{split} I_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm C} ={}&q^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\ &	imes  rac{\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_{N,\mathbf1,e})} {\sqrt{\det H_N( oldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1})} \sqrt{\det Q_{N,\mathbf1}}} e^{NS_{N,\mathbf1}} \left(1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1}) +O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-\kappa_{\mathbf n}N})ight). \end{split} 	ag{4} \] The quantities in (4) are the finite critical point, critical value and negative Hessian of \[ \Phi_{N, oldsymbol\ell}(\delta) =A_N(\delta)+\pi i\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2 +2\pi i\sum_e\ell_e\delta_e. 	ag{5} \] The face determinant root is continued from the positive complete Hessian. The spectral root is the Gaussian branch on matrices with positive real part. The coefficient in (4) tends to a nonzero number after the explicit level factors and action are removed. In particular the period is nonzero for all sufficiently large levels of either parity, and \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{2\pi}{N}\log|I_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm C}| =2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{0,\mathbf1}. 	ag{6} \] All powers are fixed before \(N	o\infty\); no bound on their ratios is required. There is no assertion here that the full invariant differs from (2) by a smaller term. ## 2. The graph facts replacing a flat-plat assumption Deleting \(u,v\) from a simple triangulated sphere leaves a connected ordinary graph. Indeed reroute a path around the first deleted vertex along its cyclic link, then around the second along its link with the first vertex removed. That remaining link is connected. Every surviving edge belongs to an original shaded triangle with two positive finite-face variables. No matching edge can have the protected pair as its endpoints: their unique sphere edge is the marked MAIN edge. Consequently every crossing circle has \(x+y>0\). At least one of its two triangles is nonmonomial. If both outers are positive, \(xy>0\); if one outer is protected, at most one middle can be the other protected face, so the other middle is positive. These facts also cover the smallest simple sphere. They require neither complete-radius balance nor a tree in the ordinary graph. At the actual complete packing, the circle-center angle sums make the common face action stationary. Its Hessian is positive on the common-scale quotient: each nonmonomial triangle detects the differences of its finite logarithmic face radii, and the connected ordinary graph leaves only common scaling in the kernel. The active rows are literal \(+1,-1\) differences. Thus the quotient lattice is primitive, has dimension \(R-1\), and has no additional angular aliases. This is the content needed from [The positive face coefficient has one global saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md), §§2–4, and [The original boundary source has exactly two flat face directions](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md), §2. Their proofs use the actual triangle graph and finite determinant matrices. Morse bends introduce no new face coordinate, while the exact source identity has already dealt with their cup/cap and mark factors. The old global theorem's phrase “flat plat” is therefore removed at this specific interface, rather than by an unproved equivalence of presentations. ## 3. Local analytic inputs, including the odd normal At each original crossing region let \(\mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L)\) be the exactly anchored even fold interpolation. It retains the actual maximal-channel factor, beta factors, forced products and half-index. In particular its anchor is at \(\delta_{\min}=0\) for odd levels and \(\delta_{\min}=1/(2N)\) for even levels. The local rigidity theorem gives \[ P_{\mathrm C,e}(\delta_e;L) =N^2\mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L) (1+O(e^{-cN})) 	ag{7} \] on a fixed complex spectral and face neighborhood, with protected variables still exactly zero. This is [Actual all-CROSS cofactors and the complete-fold interpolant](actual_cross_cofactor_interpolant_rigidity.md), §§1–4, based on [An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors](actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) and the independent complex packets of the actual cofactors. For precision, the odd central formula has the form \[ P_{\mathrm C}=G_bG_c+\omega s_ms_{m+1}xyD_bD_c, \qquad\omega=-4\sin^2(\pi\delta). 	ag{8} \] The second term in (8), including its derivative at \(\omega=0\), is retained. The even formula is its original sum of three central-cut products. Their central factors are analytic units near completeness. The proof of (7) uses the independently bounded complex cofactor ratios and a finite Cauchy–Lagrange formula on both parity grids; it does not differentiate a value-only interpolation. Thus all repeated-node normals and the odd simple node are already in (7). There is no odd regularized surrogate in (1). The local global-angular theorem applies to each terminal cofactor with row \(N/2+O(1)\). Two positive faces with separated circular phases give a fixed exponential loss, uniformly over the entire real spectral interval and a sufficiently thin complex strip. Its proof retains the exact original node adapter, positive nodal tails, all start rows and the polynomial cost of the finitely omitted terminal nodes. One-variable triangles are exact monomials and impose no angular condition. This local theorem has no global topology or Morse-order hypothesis. Every summand of the even or odd central formula contains a cofactor from both original triangles.
