Outside the common ordinary-face phase, a bounded-length path in the connected ordinary graph has a separated edge; one triangle at that edge supplies the exponential loss in every central summand at its crossing region. Every other cofactor has its polynomial endpoint majorant and the fixed strip growth \(e^{O(N|\operatorname{Im}\delta|)}\). There are finitely many crossing regions, so shrink the common strip to absorb the sum of those growth costs. This proves the shared angular complement bound, on the original common radii and with every central prefactor retained. ## 4. H1 from the actual face torus Fix one ordinary face as the scale reference, and write \(L_f=ho_f e^{z_f}\) for the others. Define the finite phase \[ \Psi_N(z,\delta)= rac1N\sum_e\operatorname{Log} \mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L(z)) - rac dN\sum_{f
e u,v}\operatorname{Log}L_f(z). 	ag{9} \] Every finite anchor and any \(O(\log N)/N\) term remains in (9); only the explicit \(N^{2R}\) in (7) lies outside. The local theorems give uniform convergence with derivatives to \[ \Psi(z,\delta)=\sum_e  igl[Q_{b_e}(\delta_e;L)+Q_{c_e}(\delta_e;L) igr] -\sum_{f
e u,v}\operatorname{Log}L_f. 	ag{10} \] The logarithms are real on the positive complete chart. The positive face Hessian and the holomorphic implicit function theorem give the actual nearby finite saddle \(z_N(\delta)\), uniformly on one fixed polydisk. Put \(A_N=\Psi_N(z_N,\delta)\) and \(H_N=\partial_z^2\Psi_N(z_N,\delta)\). The exact homogeneous numerator degree is \(dR\), equal to the total ordinary target. Hence the common angular variable integrates to one, and the actual Cauchy measure on the quotient is \((2\pi)^{-(R-1)}d	heta\). The integration lattice is primitive by the general Morse face-potential identity; no additional multiplicity is chosen here. Use (7) near the saddle and the preceding angular gap on its complement. Translating the original Cauchy torus by the small vector \(z_N(\delta)\) crosses no pole: all finite faces remain in their annuli, the numerator is polynomial and the target is its original Laurent monomial. If the translation is localized, its side faces are retained in the fixed angular gap. Uniform positive real Hessian and bounded higher derivatives then give the Gaussian with coefficient one and the determinant in (H1). Shrinking the spectral polydisk makes the absolute cost of its complex perturbation smaller than the exponential precision in (7), so the relative error remains \(O(N^{-1})\), holomorphic with fixed derivative bounds. Uniqueness of this finite face saddle preserves separate evenness and reality. At zero, the mixed \(z,\delta\) derivatives vanish by evenness, so eliminating \(z\) does not change the diagonal spectral second derivative. Explicitly \[ C_e= rac{\pi(T_{b_e}+T_{c_e})}{x_e+y_e}>0, \qquad T_t=\sqrt{(x_e+y_e)t+x_ey_e}, 	ag{11} \] at the actual complete packing. Section 2 ensures that at least one summand is positive. Thus (3) holds, and on a smaller fixed complex chart \(\operatorname{Re}A_N''\) is uniformly negative definite. This proves H1 directly for CROSS. The full-numerator restoration in §4 of [The original full spectral numerator has the marked geometric packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) is not used. ## 5. H2 on the entire spectral cube The needed real-spectral estimate is a value bound, not coefficientwise domination at arbitrary spectral parameters. The exact cleared cofactor has the original start decomposition \[ R_j(b,\delta)=\sum_{i=0}^{j}b^i \prod_{r<i}\alpha_r(\delta)K_{i,j},\qquad \alpha_r=4\cos^2 rac{(r+1/2)\pi}{N}-4\sin^2(\pi\delta). 	ag{12} \] The normalized two-step tail transfer has limiting spectral radius \[ ho(t,\delta)=(x+y)\sin(\pi t) +\sqrt{4xy\cos^2(\pi\delta)+(x-y)^2\sin^2(\pi t)}, \qquad\Lambda=2\sin(\pi t)ho. 	ag{13} \] The proof in [Global real-spectral gap of the actual all-CROSS source](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md), §§1–2, handles the possible repeated transfer root by its Cayley–Hamilton power formula. It uses fixed finite blocks away from \(t=0\), a uniform \(O(\eta\log(1/\eta))\) endpoint allowance, and uniformly integrable truncated logarithms for the exact prefix. It therefore gives a uniform upper bound for every starting row, including in small fixed complex face neighborhoods and a thin spectral strip. No ill-conditioned eigenbasis or lower bound on distance to a physical node is assumed. The exact maximization of the resulting start action is \[ \limsup rac1N\log|R_j(b,\delta)| \le\max\{Q_b(\delta),	frac12\log b\}; 	ag{14} \] for \(b=0\), only the first branch is present. This comes from its unique pre-sign-change maximum and the final start endpoint; the entire prefix integral is zero. For a nonmonomial triangle, \(Q_b(0)>	frac12\log b\) when that branch is present, and \(Q_b(\delta)<Q_b(0)\) for \(0<|\delta|\le1/2\). The derivative formula is strictly negative whenever \(b>0\) or \(xy>0\). The sole exception is the exact one-variable monomial, already excluded from any asserted local gap. Every crossing region has at least one nonmonomial triangle. Thus a separated \(\delta_e\) supplies a strict loss relative to that crossing region's complete rate; all other crossing regions have their complete upper rates with arbitrarily small prescribed errors. On the small common-face-phase region this estimate and its complex face extension control the original integrand. On the complementary face torus use the angular gap of §3, which is uniform for all real spectral parameters. Combining the two regions on the same original radii proves H2. To make endpoint neighborhoods precise, first use separation \(\eta/2\), then shrink the strip. Cauchy's estimate gives the fixed derivative version. Neither the inequality comparing LEFT/RIGHT rates with complete radii nor a choice of different radii at separate crossing regions occurs in this proof. ## 6. The first packet, its phase, and charge comparison Write, by evenness, \[ \partial_e A_N(\delta)=-2\delta_e B_{e,N}(\delta_1^2,\ldots,\delta_R^2), \qquad B_{e,N}\longrightarrow B_e,\quad B_e(0)=C_e. 	ag{15} \] Shrink the chart until \(|B_{e,N}-C_e|\le C_e/8\). Choose first a fixed outer real cube \(K_B=[-B,B]^R\) inside that chart. Choose the scaled charge cutoff \(a>0\) sufficiently small relative to \(B\). Finally choose a separate inner radius \(0<b<a/4\), to be used only for the bounded bad charges in §7. All three constants are fixed from the source before the powers are chosen. For positive real charges with \(\ell_e/|n_e|\le a\), the critical equation is exactly \[ \delta_e=- rac{\ell_e/n_e} {1+i B_{e,N}(\delta^2)/(\pi n_e)}. 	ag{16} \] Uniform contraction on a small polydisk gives its unique solution for all independent signed \(|n_e|\ge n_0\). In particular \[ |\delta_e|\le2\ell_e/|n_e|,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\delta_e=  rac{\ell_e}{\pi n_e^2}  rac{\operatorname{Re}B_{e,N}} {|1+iB_{e,N}/(\pi n_e)|^2}>0. 	ag{17} \] The imaginary part is positive for either sign of \(n_e\); all coordinates and all sine factors are nonzero. Translate the outer cube \(K_B\) to the horizontal plane through this critical point. Reality on the real chart gives \(\operatorname{Re}A_N(x+iv)\le A_N(0)-c|x|^2+C|v|^2\), with no linear imaginary cost. On each actual side face, one \(|x_j|=B\), while \(0\le v_e\le\operatorname{Im}\delta_e\). The quadratic chirps cost at most \(CB\sum_e\ell_e/|n_e|\), and the charge terms have nonpositive real part. The critical real value is at least \(A_N(0)-C\sum_e(\ell_e/|n_e|)^2\). The already chosen \(a\ll B\), followed by sufficiently large \(n_0\), therefore puts every side strictly below that value. Thus the original local contour on \(K_B\) has saddle coefficient \(+1\), with its side currents explicitly smaller. The inner radius \(b\) is not used for this local saddle contour. On the translated horizontal plane the real Hessian is \(\operatorname{Re}A_N''<0\). Hence the negative spectral Hessian \(Q_{N,\ell}\) has positive real part. The Gaussian determinant branch is fixed even for mixed signs. Applying the spectral Gaussian to H1 contributes \((2\pi/N)^{R/2}\), and the two measures combine exactly as \[ N^{2R}(2\pi N)^{-(R-1)/2}(2\pi/N)^{R/2} =\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}. 	ag{18} \] The holomorphic relative H1 error remains \(O(N^{-1})\); the ordinary cubic Gaussian term integrates to zero, while its square and the quartic term have this same order. Constants may depend on the fixed charges and powers. The limiting prefactor is nonzero by (17) and the determinant units. Differentiation of the critical value, rather than comparison of independent saddle remainders, gives \[ \partial_{\ell_e}\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\ell} =- rac{2\ell_e}{n_e^2}  rac{\operatorname{Re}B_{e,N}} {|1+iB_{e,N}/(\pi n_e)|^2}. 	ag{19} \] Therefore, throughout the positive local charge box, \[ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}-\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\ell} \ge\sum_e rac{C_e}{2n_e^2}(\ell_e^2-1). 	ag{20} \] This comparison is valid for arbitrarily unbalanced fixed powers. Separate evenness makes every sign choice of the same positive charge magnitudes contribute equally: reflecting a coordinate reverses both its sine integral and its charge factor. For the unit charges the raw sign cancels the parity character, \((-1)^{dR}(-1)^{(N+1)R}=1\), leaving the exact factor \((-2i)^R\) in (4). ## 7. Whole-domain currents and every other charge For any entire polynomial in the \(\sigma_e\), multiply it by the original sines and quadratic chirps. In each variable the resulting \(B\) has zero endpoint values and equal first derivatives at \(\pm1/2\). This remains true after spectator derivatives. Three integrations by parts give exactly \[ \int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B(t)e^{2\pi iN\ell t}\,dt =(2\pi iN\ell)^{-3} \left\{[B''(t)e^{2\pi iN\ell t}]_{-1/2}^{1/2} -\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B'''(t)e^{2\pi iN\ell t}\,dtight\}. 	ag{21} \] The second-derivative current is retained. With the original charge weight this yields summable \(|\ell|^{-2}\) at fixed \(N,\mathbf n\). Nothing about this step assumes a plat. H1 and H2 first imply the shared real supremum \(e^{N(\Phi+o(1))}\). Since the degree in each cosine variable is at most \(d\), the elementary polynomial exterior bound gives \[ |C_N(\delta)|\le e^{N(\Phi+o(1))+2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|}. 	ag{22} \] This is a bound for the whole shared coefficient. Source derivatives are estimated by Cauchy, while spectator chirps are differentiated on their real intervals, so no exponentially large spectator-slope cost is inserted. For a positive far charge in coordinate \(i\), shift its whole interval upward by a fixed small height \(	au\). Both endpoint sides are kept together. Their exact difference, with spectator factors suppressed, is \[  egin{split} B_i(1/2+iv)-B_i(-1/2+iv) ={}&2i\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi n_iNv)\ &	imes e^{\pi i n_iN(1/4-v^2)} C_N(1/2+iv,\delta_{\mathrm{other}}). \end{split} 	ag{23} \] The endpoint Fourier phase combined with the original parity is \((-1)^{\ell_i}\), of modulus one. H2 gives a fixed gap at these separated endpoints. Applying (21) in all spectator coordinates bounds the weighted vertical term by \[ C_{\mathbf n}|n_i|N\ell_i\, e^{N(\Phi-\gamma_e)}\prod_{j
e i}|\ell_j|^{-2} \int_0^	au v^2e^{-2\pi N(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)v}\,dv. 	ag{24} \] For \(\ell_i>|n_i|/2+D\), its integral is bounded by \(C/[N^3(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)^3]\), and the resulting sum converges. The horizontal interval uses (22) and has exponential rate at most \(\Phi+o(1)+2\pi R	au-2\pi	au(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)\). Choose fixed \(D\) large enough to make this uniformly smaller than \(\Phi\). The union over any far coordinate, summed with all spectators on their entire real intervals, has a fixed exponential gap. Negative charges obey the same bound by reflection. No infinite series restricted to a sharp small cube has been introduced. The remaining charges satisfy \(|\ell_i|\le\lceil|n_i|/2+Dceil\), a finite set after the powers are fixed. Consider first a bounded bad charge for which one ratio \(|\ell_i|/|n_i|>a\). Outside the inner cube \(K_b\), H2 supplies a fixed gap. Inside \(K_b\), reflect the chosen charge to positive sign and shift only that coordinate by \(ib/|n_i|\). Since \(0<b<a/4\), the horizontal charge loss is at least \(2\pi b(a-b)>0\); the complex-source error is \(O(b^2/n_i^2)\). On each actual vertical side \(|x_i|=b\), the fixed real quadratic loss persists, and the chirp plus charge has nonpositive real part. This proves a fixed gap for these bounded bad charges, independently of power ratios. For the remaining finite local charge box, with all ratios at most \(a\), use H2 outside the outer cube \(K_B\), and the actual translated \(K_B\) contour and comparison (20) inside. Every nonunit magnitude has a positive fixed-\(\mathbf n\) gap. The unit drop from \(\Phi\) is \(O_D(\sum_e n_e^{-2})\). Enlarge the common diagram-dependent threshold until this drop is smaller than the previously fixed endpoint, far-charge, bounded-bad and outer-cube-complement gaps. Also ensure \(a n_0\ge1\). All complementary contributions are then exponentially smaller than the nonzero unit packet. This proves (4)–(6) for the whole all-CROSS period. ## 8. The geometric interface and the precise remaining problem The analytic proof retains the untwisted selected action \(A_0\) and the original half twists exactly once. Put \[ A_{\epsilon}=A_0+\pi i\sum_e\epsilon_e\delta_e^2, \qquad U_{\epsilon,e}=\partial_{\delta_e}A_{\epsilon}, \qquad V_e=-4\pi i\delta_e. 	ag{25} \] The actual stationary equation of (5), with \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\), is \[ U_{\epsilon,e}+p_eV_e=-2\pi i\ell_e. 	ag{26} \] Once the original ordered Morse diagram has the marked action/primitive collar adapter and smooth long-filling completion, its regulator boundary term cancels the Gaussian terms at \(\ell_e=1\). Then \(2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{0,\mathbf1}\) is the actual filled exterior's hyperbolic volume. This identifies the asymptotic of the sector (2), not automatically that of the full invariant. The independent issue remains a bound or cancellation statement for the entire original LEFT/RIGHT remainder. Complete-radius balance is one sufficient mechanism in the terminal-fan theorem. The present proof does not assume it and supplies no replacement. In particular a nonzero sector with the correct geometric rate can still be canceled by another sector unless that remainder is controlled. ## 9. Proof dependencies and scope The following table records the inputs and the hypotheses used in each part of the proof. | Input | Part used here | Dependence on a flat plat or balance | | --- | --- | --- | | [A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) §§5–6 | Exact coefficient, primitive integer face grid, both parity cosets, mark and whole Hermite functional | Proved for the actual general Morse construction; no balance | | [An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors](actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) §§1–6 | Exact finite anchor and exponential interpolation in fixed complex face neighborhoods | Local actual triangles and protected-zero patterns only | | [Actual all-CROSS cofactors and the complete-fold interpolant](actual_cross_cofactor_interpolant_rigidity.md) §§1–4 | Actual off-node CROSS polynomial, including odd derivative term | Independent actual cofactor growth plus interpolation; local only | | [A global angular gap for the actual cleared cross cofactors](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) §§1–4 | Whole real-spectral angular gap and omitted-terminal-node interpolation | Local positive finite matrices and physical recurrences only | | [The positive face coefficient has one global saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) §§2–4 | Positive Hessian, primitive phase constraints and coefficient Gaussian | Actual connected ordinary triangle graph; no flat gap forest | | [The original boundary source has exactly two flat face directions](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) §2 | Ordinary graph connectivity after the protected pair is removed | Simple sphere and marked MAIN edge | | [Global real-spectral gap of the actual all-CROSS source](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) §§1–4 | Uniform start-row/tail estimates, strict real-spectral decrease and shared strip gap | Local recurrences plus the same ordinary graph and complete radii | | [The original full spectral numerator has the marked geometric packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) §§1–3 | Finite phase, exact quotient measure and actual Cauchy contour | Reproved above with the Morse source; its full restoration §4 is unused | | [The original localized spectral period has a nonzero unit-charge filling contribution](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) §§2–5 | Fixed independent signed saddle, actual side currents, nonzero first packet | H1 and exact scalar/evenness only; the old flat-plat opening is not used | | [The entire original all-CROSS Fourier period from its local packet and global spectral gap](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) §§2–5 | Whole-domain charge tails and finite bad-charge separation | H1, H2 and entire polynomial degree only | | [Balanced terminal decorations and volume limits beyond tangle-operation trees](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) §§6–8 | Explicit existing Morse version of these same analytic steps | Balance is used in §9 for the omitted full remainder, not in §§6–8 | No new analytic hypothesis is imposed on a certified simple-sphere Morse source beyond these literal inputs. The original presentation's physical normalization and its marked geometric applicability must still be supplied, as stated in §1. There is no full undeformed simple-sphere volume theorem in this note.

title: The original complement and its geometric contribution
status: Original filled-volume rate for the geometric contribution
text:
# The original complement and its geometric contribution A simple triangulated sphere with a perfect matching of its cubic dual determines an actual augmented link diagram when the cyclic orders, strand pairings and crossing disks are retained. This note follows that diagram through its exact finite source, its geometric critical point, and the filling of its original auxiliary cusps. For independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists, the geometric contribution to the original invariant is nonzero and has the exponential rate of the actual filled hyperbolic volume. The proof keeps the primitive peripheral words, the finite scalar factors and both parities of the quantum level. No terminal tangles are inserted, and no local balance assumption is imposed. The name CROSS denotes the central recurrence-path piece of each original homogeneous numerator. Selecting it at every crossing region is an algebraic decomposition of the original evaluation, not a new invariant. The [analytic companion](actual_morse_cross_filling_period.md) proves its full Fourier asymptotic. To conclude the same limit for the full invariant of an undecorated diagram, one must additionally control the remaining pieces. ## 1. Precise diagram and filling scope Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite simple triangulated oriented sphere with at least four vertices. Choose a perfect matching of its cubic dual. The two triangles in each matched pair form a quadrilateral with four distinct white vertices. Record a cyclic order \((x_e,b_e,y_e,c_e)\); its common diagonal is \(x_ey_e\), its input middle is \(b_e\), and its output middle is \(c_e\). There are \(R\) matched pairs and \(R+2\) white vertices. Mark a nonmatching edge \(uv\). It is a strand edge in the link diagram. There are two equivalent permitted inputs: * an actual connected augmented diagram in \(S^3\), whose projection and crossing-disk cut has exactly these labels and orders; or * the literal inverse-cut construction in section 2 below. Fix the retained half twist \(\epsilon_e\in\{-1,0,1\}\) and its sign at every disk. Its auxiliary peripheral basis \((\mu_e,\lambda_e)\) is the original disk-framed primitive basis. The longitude \(\lambda_e\) is represented by the ordered two-head product \(P_e=B_eA_e\). Integer filling coordinate \(p_e\) means filling the slope \(\mu_e+p_e\lambda_e\); the main crossing power is \[ n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e. 	ag{1} \] The original outside terminal matching and the even/odd pairing at each disk determine the main components. When their terminal graph is connected, denote the filled knot by \(K_{ oldsymbol p}\). We keep this original parity test. We do not change the parity vector to obtain a different knot. A supplied labeled positive right-angled cut certificate is sufficient for everything below. In this simple-sphere class such a certificate also follows from the constructive packing theorem in [the balanced-fan note, section 2](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md). That section constructs the packing **before any fan is inserted**. Only that initial geometric construction is used here. **Theorem.** For each fixed diagram and the recorded choices above there is a number \(T_D\) such that, for every fixed integer vector \( oldsymbol p\) with \(\min_e|n_e|>T_D\), independently in sign and relative size, the following assertions hold. 1. Filling the specified auxiliary components gives a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the original filled link exterior, with every main cusp unfilled. If the recorded component test is a knot, it is \(S^3\setminus K_{ oldsymbol p}\). 2. The all-CROSS term of the original complete-color Morse contraction has a nonzero relative first-charge asymptotic, at both parities of the level \(N\). Its selected critical action \(S_{ oldsymbol 1}\) satisfies \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{ oldsymbol 1} =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{ oldsymbol p}) 	ag{2} \] in the knot case, and the analogous original link-complement identity otherwise. 3. In particular, for that all-CROSS contraction \(\mathcal I_{N,\mathrm C}\), \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{2\pi}{N} \log|\mathcal I_{N,\mathrm C}| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{ oldsymbol p}). 	ag{3} \] The exact raw phase is retained in section 3. An ordinary zero-framing phase does not change (3). The diagram, its matching, its signs, and all powers are fixed before \(N\). The threshold can depend on this entire finite diagram. There is no short-filling assertion and no uniformity in a growing sphere. The theorem does not yet assert (3) for the full invariant: that requires a bound on the remaining sectors. ## 2. Why the manifold and its complete anchor are the original ones Take disjoint small neighborhoods of the matched edges of the cubic dual. Each is a four-terminal disk. In cyclic terminal order \(0,1,2,3\), the two shaded halves group \((1,2)\) and \((3,0)\). Draw the physical untwisted strands instead with pairs \((0,1),(2,3)\), and connect outside terminals along the nonmatching dual edges. In the corresponding disjoint three-balls put the perpendicular crossing circles and their twice-punctured disks. This constructs a link in \(S^3\), not a manifold assigned to an abstract tensor graph. Retained odd half twists use the physical pairing \((0,2),(1,3)\), with their original signed collar paths. The two main pairings and the shaded grouping must not be confused. The graph of main components is the union of the outside terminal matching and these physical pairings. Every terminal has degree two. Its connectedness is exactly the knot test, and adding full twists does not change it. Cut along the projection sphere. In each projection ball a crossing circle semicircle is boundary parallel by its original half disk. Drilling that semicircle and opening that same half disk cancels the introduced handle. These operations occur in disjoint collars, so opening all of them leaves one ball in each projection copy. The boundary cellulation is the prescribed medial sphere. Thus cycles in the matched graph create no unidentified handle or extra gluing. Let \(Q\) be its positive ideal right-angled cut polyhedron. The even shaded pairing fixes the crossing-circle vertex and sends \(C_1\mapsto C_0,\ C_2\mapsto C_3\). An odd pairing exchanges the projection copies and the two punctures, using the literal signed half-twist collar. The two odd signs have the same corner permutation but different primitive paths. White faces pair by their original projection labels. At every ideal vertex, the link of \(Q\) is a rectangle. Normalize its opposite shaded sides to length one. Each shaded triangle map then preserves the canonical horocycles at all three corners, including the odd corner permutation. Each alternating white/shaded edge cycle has four right-angle pieces. It fixes both ideal endpoints, preserves the chosen horospheres there, and rotates by \(2\pi\), so its whole holonomy is the identity. The ideal links are the actual link's torus links and have no cone or dilation defect. Their horoball ends are complete. Hence \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)=2\operatorname{Vol}(Q), \qquad \Phi_D= rac{\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)}{2\pi}. 	ag{4} \] Here \(Y_D\) is the same augmented exterior, with the recorded half twists and peripheral bases. These are the local cut and gluing arguments in [the matching-geometry proof, sections 4–6](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). They use a sphere projection, disjoint half disks, and the prescribed corner maps. Moving cups and caps to a flat plat is not a premise. The inverse construction and its general Morse realization are spelled out in [the matched-sphere source, sections 1–4](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md). For completeness, the initial simple-sphere packing theorem does not require the absence of separating triangles. Remove one triangular face and pool its three boundary angle demands. Strict Hall inequalities for every nonempty proper destination subset give a positive allocation of angles. The strictly concave calibrated triangle entropy has an interior maximizer, whose multipliers give positive radii. The center triangles have zero interior rotational and translational holonomy. Their boundary develops once around a convex triangle, so the degree argument makes the development injective. Vertex-disk sectors stop before opposite center edges; this proves disjointness, including across separating triangles. The contact circles and outward halfspaces therefore give the labeled strict support certificate. Sending the marked contact to infinity gives the two protected parallel lines. No radius-balance inequality enters this construction. ## 3. The exact source and the phases which remain outside the action Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\). In the recorded four-leg order the full local homogeneous numerator is \(H_e(L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e})\). The original reduced Morse contraction is \[ [\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^d]\, \prod_e H_e(L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e})  ig|_{L_u=L_v=0}. 	ag{5} \] This statement includes the complete root Hermite normals and the unrestricted physical mark. Here is the part of its proof that matters for changing the Morse height function. Each full coupon contributes \(N^{-1}H_e/(b_ec_e)^{d/2}\). If \(M_f\) counts middle passages and \(T_f\) counts outside minus inside turns, the actual boundary turning number gives \[ M_f-T_f=2 \quad(f
e u),\qquad M_u-T_u=-2. 	ag{6} \] The ordinary caps and cups give the same powers as these winding numbers; replacing the exposed cap by the original reduced mark contributes \(N^{-1}(L_v/L_u)^d\). Thus the full summand is \(N^{-R-1}\prod H_e/\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^d\). The primitive face-potential lattice has \(R+1\) independent \(N\)-point grids after the exterior gauge is fixed. Their count cancels \(N^{-R-1}\). Exact endpoint support is imposed before the root reduction, so no coefficient is aliased into a wrong endpoint. This proves (5) with its original phases at arbitrary Morse height and both level parities. Replace each homogeneous factor in (5) by its CROSS cofactor factor and retain the physical spectral trace. Write \(C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}( oldsymbol\delta)\) for the resulting entire spectral numerator, with each node \(-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e)\). It is even separately in every coordinate, has degree at most \(d\) in each node, and satisfies \(C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}=(-1)^{dR}C_N^+\) in the positive cofactor normalization. The exact original filling period is \[  egin{split} \mathcal I_{N,\mathrm C} ={}&q^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-i)^R \sum_{ oldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\ell_e\Bigr)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_e\ell_e}\ &\quad\cdot \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_e)\Bigr) C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}( oldsymbol\delta) \exp\!\left[ N\sum_e\{\pi i n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\ell_e\delta_e\} ight]\,d oldsymbol\delta . \end{split} 	ag{7} \] The sum is the original trace identity with its endpoint currents; it is not defined by an unqualified termwise Poisson rearrangement. The odd-level simple node and the double-node normals are included. The same finite proof is [the matched-sphere source, sections 5–7](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md). No operation in (5)–(7) changes a disk, a strand pairing, or a peripheral curve. In particular the all-CROSS source for the original sphere exists before a fan construction, and its ordinary-face targets are still \(d\). ## 4. One marked circle pattern on the whole sphere Normalize the complete protected white disks to \(\operatorname{Im}z\le0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}z\ge1\). For each finite face use center \((X_f,Y_f)\) and radius \(r_f\). At a strand edge set \(I_{fg}=1\); at matching edge \(e\) set \(I_{fg}=\cos(2\pi\delta_e)\). The equations are \[  egin{aligned} (X_f-X_g)^2+(Y_f-Y_g)^2 &=r_f^2+r_g^2+2I_{fg}r_fr_g,\ Y_f&=r_fI_{fu},\qquad 1-Y_f=r_fI_{fv}, \end{aligned} 	ag{8} \] where the last two equations are imposed at the appropriate marked line incidences. Fix one horizontal translation. The marked line-line edge is automatic; the remaining system has \(3R-1\) equations and variables. Its complete Jacobian is invertible. The infinitesimal angle sums and the positive finite-face source Hessian first force all logarithmic radius variations to be one common scale. Each of the two triangles adjacent to \(uv\) contains a finite circle tangent to both fixed lines. Its radius is \(1/2\), so its scale variation is zero. All radius variations are therefore zero. With radii fixed, each finite center triangle has one infinitesimal Euclidean motion. A one-line triangle has only a horizontal translation. Removing the two triangles at \(uv\) leaves a triangulated disk with connected triangle adjacency, containing all finite vertices and at least one one-line triangle. Two adjacent finite triangles agree at two distinct centers; two adjacent one-line triangles agree at their finite center. These comparisons propagate one horizontal translation through the disk, and the normalization removes it. The kernel is zero. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem now gives one circle pattern on a fixed polydisk in all \(\delta_e\). The variables \(X,Y,r\) are complexified independently, without conjugating parameters. The solution is real on real parameters and even in each \(\delta_e\). For one source triangle put \(x=1/r_x,\ b=1/r_b,\ y=1/r_y\), \[  egin{aligned} A&=x+y,& s&=\sin(\pi\delta),\ D&=A^2-4xy s^2,& T_b&=\sqrt{bA+xy+b^2s^2},\ E_b&=A+2bs^2+2sT_b . \end{aligned} 	ag{9} \] Use positive complete roots and their analytic continuations. The original determinant, beta, and forced-product rate \(Q_b\) obeys \[ \partial_\delta Q_b=-\operatorname{Log}(E_b/\sqrt D), \qquad \partial_{\log L_f}Q_b= rac{	heta_f}{2\pi}, \qquad Q_b(0)=F(x,b,y). 	ag{10} \] The angles are those of (8), with their marked-line limits. Thus the developed angles sum to \(2\pi\) exactly when the finite-face source is stationary. Uniqueness of the finite-face critical point identifies these curvatures with the limiting source saddle. The common strip also handles a triangle containing both protected lines. If its finite radius is \(r\), its strip width is \(r(1+\cos(2\pi\delta))\). This shared width cannot be chosen independently at two triangles. The corresponding repeated scalar root does not remove the selected eigenflag: the noncentral complete parabolic has a nonzero off-diagonal matrix entry, and its eigenline for \[ J=-e^{-2\pi i\delta} 	ag{11} \] continues holomorphically, including its collision at zero. This is the complete rank and face-identification mechanism in [the marked-pattern proof](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md). No part of it refers to the number of strands at a Morse slice. Simplicity is important: in particular a matching edge cannot join the two protected faces, since their unique common edge is the marked strand edge. Hence \(A>0\) in every local formula. ## 5. Full group relations and the original primitive peripheral words Choose the two holomorphic white-reflection matrices \(\mathcal R_f^\pm\), with \(\mathcal R_f^-\mathcal R_f^+=I\), from the one pattern. At a regular Morse slice with regions \(F_0,\ldots,F_k\), the original heads and prefixes are \[ H_j=\mathcal R_{F_j}^+\mathcal R_{F_{j-1}}^-, \qquad H_j\cdots H_1=\mathcal R_{F_j}^+\mathcal R_{F_0}^- . 	ag{12} \] Their marked lifts give the original parabolic main meridians. Shared physical wire ends have the same adjacent region labels. At a cup or cap the consecutive regions are \(F,G,F\), so the inserted ordered pair has product \(I\), and all later prefixes are unchanged. This proves the relations also when \(k\) changes. At one crossing disk the ordered input pair is \[ A_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathcal R_b\mathcal R_x,\qquad B_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathcal R_y\mathcal R_b,\qquad P=B_{\mathrm{in}}A_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathcal R_y\mathcal R_x, 	ag{13} \] and the output pair replaces \(b\) by \(c\). The labeled contact map of the disk, taking \(C_1\mapsto C_0,\ C_2\mapsto C_3\), is \[ R_0= rac{E_bE_c}{D},\qquad C=I+ rac{R_0-1}{J-J^{-1}}(P-J^{-1}I). 	ag{14} \] It sends both input generators to their respective output generators by simultaneous conjugation and commutes with \(P\). The primitive normalization in (14) is geometric. Sending the two outer intersection points to \(0,\infty\) makes the two shaded contact circles concentric, with radii \(\sqrt D/E_b\) and \(E_c/\sqrt D\). Their ordered corner map is multiplication by \(R_0\); the product of their reflections would instead give \(R_0^2\). The original threading word \([2,1,1,2]\) follows the inverse of the first map. At zero, (14) retains the nontrivial parabolic divided-difference limit. Setting \(C=I\) merely because its eigenratio is one would give the wrong group representation. Marked lines are treated by one common Möbius regularization of the whole pattern. The input/output side signs are calibrated by the same complete cusp rectangle. Nonvanishing middle contributions have the original opposite signs; an exceptional two-line triangle has \(T_b=0\) and contributes ratio one. Its actual eigenflag still comes from (8). This proves (14) with the correct labels at every zero pattern, not just at positive local curvatures. The positive crossing acts by \((A,B)\mapsto(A^{-1}BA,A)\), represented by \(P^{-1}-I\). For \(\epsilon\) equal to \(0,1,-1\), put \[  egin{aligned} U&=-\operatorname{Log}R_0-\epsilon\operatorname{Log}(-J),\ V&=2\operatorname{Log}(-J)=-4\pi i\delta,\qquad m=e^{U/2}. \end{aligned} 	ag{15} \] All logarithms are the germs vanishing at the complete point. The actual determinant-one auxiliary meridian is \[ {\mathsf M} =mR_0(J^{-1}-1)^{-\epsilon} C^{-1}(P^{-1}-I)^\epsilon. 	ag{16} \] Its selected eigenvalue is \(m\), and \(\det{\mathsf M}=m^2R_0(-J)^\epsilon=1\). The factor \(J^{-1}-1\) is a unit near completeness, including for negative \(\epsilon\). Formula (16), not just (15), verifies the original threading and signed Hurwitz relations. Equations (12)–(16) cover every shared wire, cup, cap, drilled box, and half twist in the actual Morse van Kampen presentation. There is no extra consistency equation at a cycle of the matched graph: all heads came from the same global reflections and all ordered box maps use those heads. The resulting family \(ho_{ oldsymbol\delta}\) is an actual framed representation of \(\pi_1(Y_D)\). At zero it is the complete cut representation. Every main meridian remains noncentral parabolic; its commuting longitude has multiplier one. Thus every unfilled main peripheral group is parabolic. These are full matrix and based-word assertions from [the primitive collar proof](actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) and [the global assembly, section 2](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md). The latter's displayed \(2k\) head count is replaced event by event by the actual \(k(t)\) in (12). No other part of its proof changes. ## 6. Absolute action and the first-charge filling equations Let \(A_0\) be the pure limiting face-critical value \[ A_0( oldsymbol\delta)= \operatorname{crit}_{L} \left\{\sum_e(Q_{b_e}+Q_{c_e}) -\sum_{f
e u,v}\operatorname{Log}L_fight\}. 	ag{17} \] It is separately even, real on real parameters, and anchored by \(A_0(0)=\Phi_D\). Put \[ A_\epsilon=A_0+\pi i\sum_e\epsilon_e\delta_e^2. \] Envelope differentiation of (10), retaining (15), gives \[ dA_\epsilon=\sum_e U_e\,d\delta_e,\qquad d(2\pi i A_\epsilon)=- rac12\sum_e U_e\,dV_e. 	ag{18} \] This derivative identifies the actual primitive variables, including the half-twist shear; it is stronger than a cusp-Hessian match. The marked regulator boundary formula, in squared multiplier logs, is \[ d\operatorname{Vol}(ho) = rac12\sum_e \{\operatorname{Re}V_e\,d\operatorname{Im}U_e -\operatorname{Re}U_e\,d\operatorname{Im}V_e\}. 	ag{19} \] The main terms vanish. Equations (18),(19) have the same differential after the boundary correction, and (4) fixes the real constant. Therefore on this one selected branch \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}A_\epsilon =\operatorname{Vol}(ho) - rac12\sum_e \operatorname{Im}U_e\,\operatorname{Re}V_e. 	ag{20} \] The logarithms are not reset during continuation. For the positive unit charge in (7), the limiting phase is \[ S_{ oldsymbol1}( oldsymbol\delta) =A_0( oldsymbol\delta) +\pi i\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\sum_e\delta_e =A_\epsilon-2\pi i\sum_e p_e\delta_e^2 +2\pi i\sum_e\delta_e . 	ag{21} \] Its stationarity equation is exactly \[ U_e+p_eV_e=-2\pi i. 	ag{22} \] For each fixed diagram, existence and uniqueness near zero hold for all independently long signed powers. Indeed \[ A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_e),\qquad C_e= rac{\pi(T_{b_e}(0)+T_{c_e}(0))}{x_e+y_e}>0, 	ag{23} \] and separate evenness makes \(\partial_e A_0=\delta_e B_e\). After multiplying the critical equations by \(1/n_e\), the derivative in \( oldsymbol\delta\) at reciprocal slopes zero is the invertible diagonal \(2\pi i I\). The several-parameter implicit-function theorem gives \(\delta_e=O_D(1/|n_e|)\). It allows independently unbalanced signed \(n_e\); it does not compare a minimum error rate with a sum of unrelated filling losses. At a critical point, substitute (22) into (20). Since \(V=-4\pi i\delta\), the real part of the two explicit added terms in (21) is \[ \operatorname{Re}(-2\pi i p\delta^2+2\pi i\delta) = rac{1}{4\pi}\operatorname{Im}U\,\operatorname{Re}V . 	ag{24} \] The boundary corrections cancel exactly: \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{ oldsymbol1} =\operatorname{Vol}(ho). 	ag{25} \] There is no omitted complex endpoint term. To replace the right side by the hyperbolic volume of the filled topology one still needs the following metric argument. ## 7. Completing the specified hyperbolic filling The construction in [the general metric completion theorem, sections 1–5](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) applies to any complete finite-volume exterior. Its neighborhood is a neighborhood of the **framed representation**, not only of the peripheral traces. We recall the points preventing an exponentiated filling equation from being mistaken for a metric. On a compact truncated core choose a finite lifted partition of unity \(\eta_{j,\gamma}\). In the future unit hyperboloid form \[ Y_ho(x)=\sum_{j,\gamma}\eta_{j,\gamma}(x) ho(\gamma)ho_0(\gamma)^{-1}x,\qquad E_ho(x)= rac{Y_ho(x)} {\sqrt{-\langle Y_ho(x),Y_ho(x)angle}} . 	ag{26} \] The future cone is convex; this is defined and equivariant. On a compact fundamental part it is \(C^1\)-close to the identity, so is a positive local diffeomorphism. In a selected cusp frame the peripheral transformations are affine: \(A_ho(\lambda)z=a_\lambda z+b_\lambda\), on the original translation lattice \(\Lambda\). A periodic partition of unity gives \[  egin{aligned} d_ho(w)&=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \eta(w-\lambda)A_ho(\lambda)(w-\lambda),\ F_ho(w,t)&=(d_ho(w),e^{t+\chi_ho(w)}), \end{aligned} 	ag{27} \] where \(\chi_ho\) is the real-linear extension of \(\lambda\mapsto\log|a_\lambda|\). These maps are exactly equivariant. The first is a positive local diffeomorphism on a compact fundamental parallelogram, and by equivariance everywhere. The second has positive triangular differential on the entire tail. It can be joined to (26) by a \(C^1\)-small equivariant interpolation on a fixed compact collar. At the selected unit-charge critical point, the limiting version of (33) gives \(\operatorname{Im}\delta_e>0\) for either sign of \(n_e\), since the limiting \(B_{e,N}\) in (33) has positive real part. Consequently \(\operatorname{Re}V_e=4\pi\operatorname{Im}\delta_e>0\), so the longitude multiplier has \(|e^{V_e}|>1\). This is a nonunit **modulus**, not merely the weaker assertion \(e^{V_e}
e1\). The commuting affine maps therefore have a second common fixed point \(q=b/(1-a)\), using \(a=e^{V_e}\) for the longitude. As \(ho	oho_0\), \(q\) escapes to infinity, whereas the developed fundamental parallelogram and its fixed generator paths remain bounded. They miss \(q\); equivariance makes the entire development miss it. On its simply connected cover set \(f=\log(d_ho-q)\). The nonsingular invariant metric \(|df|^2\) descends to a compact flat torus and is complete. Consequently its development is the plane and its log periods are an injective rank-two lattice. For each fixed generator path of image length at most \(L\), in \(|d_ho|\le R\), its logarithmic increment is at most \(L/(|q|-R)\), hence tends to zero. Its exponential is the corresponding similarity multiplier. The difference from the small prescribed log \(U\) or \(V\) is a multiple of \(2\pi i\) tending to zero, so is exactly zero. This proves the actual log periods **before** multiplying them by \(p_e\). One neighborhood works for all slopes. After moving \(q\) to zero, the tail contains a full epigraph \(y>A|d_ho|\). With \[ R_{\mathrm{tube}}=\operatorname{arsinh}(|d_ho|/y),\quad \vartheta=\operatorname{Im}f,\quad X=\operatorname{Re}f+	frac12\log(1+y^2/|d_ho|^2), \] its metric becomes \[ dR_{\mathrm{tube}}^2+\cosh^2(R_{\mathrm{tube}})\,dX^2 +\sinh^2(R_{\mathrm{tube}})\,d\vartheta^2 . 	ag{28} \] The primitive slope in (22) has angle \(-2\pi\) and zero axial period. A complementary primitive period has nonzero real part, because the lattice has rank two. Adding \(R_{\mathrm{tube}}=0\) therefore adds a smooth solid torus with precisely that meridian. Its holonomy fixes both \(q,\infty\) and has multiplier one, so is the identity; the representation descends to the filled group. This excludes the parabolic-slope defect which a bare equation \(\exp(U+pV)=1\) would permit. At every main cusp all multipliers are one, so (27) gives a complete Euclidean torus link and a full horoball quotient. The resulting metric is complete and finite-volume. Its universal developing local isometry covers \(\mathbb H^3\), proving discrete faithful holonomy. The representation volume agrees with this filled metric's volume using the same finite boundary triangulation: compare its cusp map with the axis-valued map by the common conical boundary homotopy, whose volume tends to zero, and extend that triangulation through the solid torus with all vertices on the core axis, so every added tetrahedron has zero volume. This is the filling-chain comparison in [the general regulator theorem, section 6](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md); it retains the same oriented fundamental class. Our family satisfies the neighborhood hypothesis: (8), (14), (16), and their chosen flags are holomorphic at zero and converge to their original complete matrices as all \(|n_e|	o\infty\). The first-charge solution above therefore lies in this fixed neighborhood after one diagram-dependent threshold. Inserting (25) now gives the volume of the actual filled manifold. Finally, filling a crossing circle along its recorded \(\mu_e+p_e\lambda_e\) is the local surgery in the original twice-punctured disk collar which inserts \(-2p_e\) crossings. The disks and collars are those constructed in \(S^3\) in section 2. Thus the filled topology is the original diagram with powers (1), not a comparison diagram, a tree replacement, or an unnamed representation component. ## 8. Analytic interface and the remaining full-source problem The independent analytic verification is recorded in [the analytic packet and whole-period proof](actual_morse_cross_filling_period.md). Its inputs are the exact source (5)–(7), the positive complete radii and the original primitive face lattice. The relevant graph facts hold here: deleting the protected adjacent vertices from a simple triangulated sphere leaves its surviving ordinary graph connected; a matching outer pair is not the protected pair; every matching factor has \(x+y>0\) and at least one nonmonomial triangle. These give the ordinary Hessian rank and primitive angular differences used by the complex coefficient saddle. They do not require a flat gap forest. The companion proof establishes the local holomorphic packet and global complex-strip spectral gap, including all odd simple-node normals. It then applies the original contour proof to (7), with real spectators during infinite-tail removal, exact endpoint currents, and independent signed reciprocal slopes. That proof returns the nonzero first-charge asymptotic, not just an upper bound on its action. Section 9 records its exact normalization. For an unchanged opposite-offset even bipyramid, its displayed circle packing is a positive certificate and its oriented top and bottom quartets are exactly the general Morse source (5). Consequently this theorem applies to its all-CROSS term at every fixed size, with the original parity/knot qualification. No Conway-tree decomposition or new plat presentation is required. What remains for its **full** invariant is a strict estimate of the signed contribution outside CROSS, for example \[  igl|\mathcal I_{N,\mathrm{full}} -\mathcal I_{N,\mathrm C} igr| \le \exp\!\left[ N\left\{ rac{\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{ oldsymbol p})} {2\pi}-\etaight\}+o(N)ight]. 	ag{29} \] Failure of complete-radius balance at every mark neither invalidates the all-CROSS theorem nor proves (29) false. It removes one known sufficient method of proving (29). The present result makes no claim of cancellation or domination for those remaining sectors. ## 9. The nonzero asymptotic with its finite normalization Here is the analytic statement actually joined to the geometry, with the finite quantities retained. On one fixed complex polydisk there are even holomorphic face-critical actions \(A_N\) and face Hessians \(H_N\), converging with every fixed derivative to their limiting quantities, such that \[ C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}( oldsymbol\delta) = rac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}\exp(NA_N( oldsymbol\delta))} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N( oldsymbol\delta)}} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{30} \] The action includes all finite anchors, sine and beta terms and any \((\log N)/N\) terms; only the displayed \(N^{2R}\) was removed. Its limit is (17). The square root in (30) is continued from the positive complete face Hessian. For every fixed \(\eta>0\), there are \(\gamma_\eta,	au_\eta>0\) such that, on the entire real spectral cube and the indicated thin strip, \[  egin{gathered} |C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}( oldsymbol\delta)| \le e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_\eta)},\ \max_e|\operatorname{Re}\delta_e|\ge\eta,\quad \operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in[-1/2,1/2],\quad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le	au_\eta . \end{gathered} 	ag{31} \] Fixed derivatives satisfy the same type of bound on smaller domains. The local cofactor interpolation retains the odd simple-node derivative, while the shared angular estimate uses the connected ordinary graph and its primitive face-difference rows. The separated real-spectral estimate comes from the exact cofactor starting-row maximum. Its only monomial exception is harmless because every crossing factor has a nonmonomial triangle. These prove (30),(31) for the all-CROSS projection of the exact coefficient (5); they are not inferred from a value-only local recurrence. Let \( oldsymbol\delta_{N, oldsymbol1}\) be the finite critical point of \[ A_N( oldsymbol\delta) +\pi i\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\sum_e\delta_e , \] let \(S_{N, oldsymbol1}\) be its critical value, and let \(Q_{N, oldsymbol1}\) be its negative spectral Hessian. Then the **entire** period (7) is \[  egin{split} \mathcal I_{N,\mathrm C} ={}&q^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\ &\ \cdot  rac{\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_{N, oldsymbol1,e})} {\sqrt{\det H_N( oldsymbol\delta_{N, oldsymbol1})} \sqrt{\det Q_{N, oldsymbol1}}} \exp(NS_{N, oldsymbol1})\ &\ \cdot \left(1+O_{ oldsymbol n}(N^{-1}) +O_{ oldsymbol n}(e^{-\kappa_{ oldsymbol n}N})ight). \end{split} 	ag{32} \] The spectral determinant uses the Gaussian branch on the cone with positive real part. The sine and both determinant factors have a nonzero limiting product for fixed sufficiently long powers. For clarity, the charge proof has four logically separate parts. Separate evenness writes \(\partial_eA_N=-2\delta_e B_{e,N}( oldsymbol\delta^2)\), where \(B_{e,N}	o C_e>0\). The critical equations for positive charge magnitudes give \[ \delta_e=- rac{\ell_e/n_e} {1+iB_{e,N}( oldsymbol\delta^2)/(\pi n_e)},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\delta_e = rac{\ell_e}{\pi n_e^2}  rac{\operatorname{Re}B_{e,N}} {|1+iB_{e,N}/(\pi n_e)|^2}>0. 	ag{33} \] An actual outer local cube is shifted to this saddle, with every side current retained below the saddle value. Its negative Hessian has positive real part and its Gaussian coefficient is one. The face and spectral Gaussian powers combine to \[ N^{2R}(2\pi N)^{-(R-1)/2}(2\pi/N)^{R/2} =\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}. 	ag{34} \] Next, differentiating the critical value gives the joint comparison \[ \operatorname{Re}S_{N, oldsymbol1} -\operatorname{Re}S_{N, oldsymbol\ell} \ge\sum_e rac{C_e}{2n_e^2}(\ell_e^2-1) 	ag{35} \] on a fixed scaled local charge box. This is why unequal slopes cause no loss of the theorem: it compares the critical values in one joint family, rather than discarding local errors independently. Third, infinite far charges are removed on whole real intervals, with the other coordinates kept as real spectators. The sine factor gives zero endpoint values and equal first derivatives; three integrations by parts retain the second-derivative endpoint current. On the shifted contour the two vertical endpoints are paired before estimation. Their hyperbolic-sine difference and (31) give a summable strict gap. The degree-\(d\) cosine bound controls the remaining horizontal interval. Only then is the remaining finite charge set divided into local and bounded-bad charges. A separate smaller cube, not the outer saddle cube, controls the latter by a one-coordinate shift. All connectors and all original endpoints are included. Finally, reflecting any charge sign changes both its sine integral and its charge weight, so all \(2^R\) unit signs agree. The raw parity sign cancels exactly: \[ (-1)^{dR}(-1)^{(N+1)R}=1 . 	ag{36} \] This leaves the original \(q\) phase and the factor \((-2i)^R\) in (32). Neither the sign choice of a power nor the parity of \(N\) can force cancellation of that leading coefficient. Equations (30)–(36) give the nonzero lower as well as the upper asymptotic. Taking its logarithm and using (25) and the metric construction proves (2),(3). Thus the flat-plat wording in the older all-CROSS theorem is a limitation of its stated input, not a remaining mathematical restriction after these separate Morse source, analytic, and geometric arguments.

title: Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads
status: Actual factorial normals for logarithmically escaping heads
text: # Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads 30 October 2026. source estimate. The marked Gamma factorial remains controlled when a head has imaginary part of order N log N. This is a bound for the actual factorial factors and fixed quantum jets. It does not provide a packet for a polynomial whose critical points merge, or cross an original zero or pole divisor. ## 1. The precise source factors and growing charts Use EXACTLY the interpolant Fhat_P and its logarithmic mark in [the moving-period factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), with P=pi i/(pi i/N+epsilon), d=N-1 fixed. Put L_N=1+log N. Fix positive constants delta,C. The new interior arguments satisfy delta <= Re(z/N) <= 1-delta, |Im(z/N)| <= C L_N. (1) An exterior argument may instead have |Re(z/N)|<=C and delta<=|Im(z/N)|<=C L_N. Choose a fixed integer shift k_N=O(N) which puts its real part in a smaller interior strip, and use the original unit recurrence for that SAME function. The shift stays fixed when epsilon moves. Fixed physical integer arguments 0,...,d are also allowed, by their exact finite factorials. For a fixed finite number of these arguments, there are constants c,C_1, independent of N and the arguments, such that on |epsilon| <= rho_N=c/[N^2 L_N^2] (2) every factor is holomorphic and nonzero, and its relative value and inverse are bounded by C_1. In particular, for every fixed j, |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_(epsilon=0) <= j! C_1 (C_1 N^2 L_N^2)^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (3) The same assertion holds for products and inverses of a fixed number of those factors, their normalized local square-root gauges, and retained powers zeta^E with |E|<=C N^2 L_N^2. All exponential root values and integer-linear characters remain part of the source. ## 2. A direct differentiated Gamma-product bound The convergent product defining G_P gives, at FIXED z, partial_P Log G_P(z)=-z/P +sum_(k>=1) { k psi(Pk+z+1)-k psi(Pk-z) -(2z+1)/P }. (4) It suffices first to work on |P-N|<=c/L_N. All Gamma arguments have positive real part there. Their real parts are at least c_delta N for k=1 and comparable to Nk for k>=2. Take K=ceiling(C_2(1+|z|/N)), C_2 sufficiently large. For k<=K, the uniform right-half-plane digamma expansion psi(w)=Log w+O(1/|w|) applies. Both arguments have size at least c_delta N. Their modulus ratio and the difference of their marked arguments are bounded uniformly: the large imaginary parts enter with opposite signs, and the real-part distance to the strip endpoints is fixed. Hence |psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)|<=C_delta, and the first K terms of (4) have total size O(K^2+K L_N)=O(L_N^2). This includes the case that z stays bounded in scaled coordinates. For k>K, |z+1|/|Pk|<1/4. Expanding the two digammas about Pk shows that their 1/(Pk) term is (2z+1)/(Pk), while their 1/(Pk)^2 terms are EQUAL and cancel. More explicitly the latter coefficient of psi(w+a) is -a^2/2+a/2-1/12, which has the same value at a=z+1 and a=-z. The uniform next remainder gives |k[psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)]-(2z+1)/P| <=C(1+|z|)^3/(N^3 k^2). (5) One may obtain (5) directly by differentiating the convergent Gamma-ratio expansion on a fixed larger relative P disk; the same 1/k cancellation and uniform |z/(Pk)|<1/4 give its bound. Summing (5) costs O((1+|z|/N)^3/K)=O(L_N^2). The initial -z/P term is smaller. Therefore |partial_P Log G_P(z)|<=C L_N^2. (6) The marked elementary exponential converting G_P to Fhat_P has P derivative -pi i z(z+1)/(2P^2), also O(L_N^2). Since |P'(epsilon)|=O(N^2), |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C N^2 L_N^2. (7) Disk (2) lies inside the P neighborhood just used. Integrating the actual logarithmic derivative along that disk proves the two-sided relative bound, and Cauchy's formula gives (3). No principal logarithm is reset, and no root-only reflection is differentiated. For completeness, the digamma estimates used here follow from the same uniform complex-sector Stirling expansion used to construct the original product. The Gamma arguments lie in the right half-plane, so its fixed sector can include angles up to pi/2. The finite sum and tail bounds above make explicit their dependence on the growing imaginary argument; a compact-set estimate is not silently reused. ## 3. Exterior rows, fixed endpoints and original gauges For an exterior row the O(N) fixed unit shifts introduce factors 1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]. Their scaled imaginary parts remain at least delta/2 on (2). Thus |exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]/(1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta])|<=C_delta. Each logarithmic epsilon derivative has size O(N L_N), so the whole shift product costs O(N^2 L_N), within (7). Large or small absolute magnitudes of individual factors are NOT bounded away: only their relative variation is being estimated. These magnitudes and all phases remain in the root value. For a fixed physical integer n<=d, the original finite product has logarithmic derivative O(N^2 L_N), including n=d. Its known relative disk contains (2). This keeps the endpoint N-1 fixed rather than replacing it by P-1. Combining the bounds proves the statement for any fixed product, ratio and locally normalized square root. A marked monomial zeta^E has logarithmic derivative E, so it has precisely the additional cost claimed after (3). Consequently the actual moving-factorial cup and cap factors at heads of size O(N log N) have polynomial fixed-jet cost whenever their arguments obey these hypotheses. The same is true of their specified boundary gauges. This does not give a relative estimate for a SUM of white-polynomial terms, and does not replace the actual large generic white by its root-colliding small partner. ## 4. What this resolves at the resonant framing boundary For an actual clock X(r) asymptotic to c r^(2e), e=+1 or -1, on a marked ray r=N R with R in a compact set avoiding zero, its head z=Log X/(2Log q0) has |Im(z/N)|=O(log N). On a fixed logarithmic sheet with bounded real part it falls into the nonreal exterior class above for all sufficiently large N. Thus its large imaginary lift by itself is tame for the actual factorial normals. No bounded-lift hypothesis is falsely invoked. In contrast, a clock tending to one can give a factorial argument approaching an integer zero or pole. Nor does this theorem control a white numerator's endpoint saddle or its resonant coefficient sum. Those need their own exact small-argument products or turning analysis. The original finite support, generic normal, cotangent measure and selected global period remain unchanged and unproved by this estimate. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape_results.json) retain 12 independent Gamma-tail comparisons, 48 two-sided relative disk checks, 12 genuine fixed-index normals, 12 exact marked unit recurrences and 12 actual opposite-head cup gauges, at 85 digits. The maximum identity error was 2.18e-75. These are diagnostics of the specified function; the uniform estimate is proved above. The estimate concerns relative factorial/cup quantities and their genuine fixed jets. It does not bound an absolute magnitude, establish a turning packet or give a global period.

title: The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period
status: Exact two-period section and finite unipotent jet transport
text: # The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period 30 October 2026. The existing convergent Gamma product extends to the ACTUAL moving quantum parameter. It matches every original finite integer factorial, including the fixed endpoint d=N-1, before taking derivatives. On specified complex index charts it has uniform relative bounds and polynomial cost for every fixed genuine q derivative. The index d stays N-1 when the analytic period moves; no root reflection is differentiated as though d were the moving period minus one. ## 1. The same convergent product at a complex period Fix N>=3, q0=exp(pi i/N), and let zeta=q0 exp(epsilon), P=pi i/Log zeta=N/[1+N epsilon/(pi i)], Q_P=exp(2pi i/P)=zeta^2. (1) The logarithm of zeta is the local one pi i/N+epsilon. Use the analytic Log P near the positive number N and Log(Pk)=Log P+log k. Define, initially where all Gamma arguments have positive real part, G_P(z)=(2pi/P)^z Gamma(z+1) *product_(k>=1) Gamma(Pk+z+1) /[Gamma(Pk-z)(Pk)^(2z+1)], Fhat_P(z)=exp[pi i z(z+1)/(2P)-pi i z/2]G_P(z). (2) This uses the infinite Gamma product from the [exact interpolation theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), not its finite Barnes product whose number of factors was an integer. The log of the kth factor is locally uniformly O(k^-2), with leading term -z(z+1)(2z+1)/(6P^2 k^2). Its 1/k coefficient vanishes. The Gamma-ratio expansion therefore proves local uniform convergence, including P and z derivatives. The function is holomorphic and nonzero on the initial domain and G_P(0)=1. The Gamma functional equation and the convergent sine product give EXACTLY G_P(z+1)/G_P(z)=2sin(pi(z+1)/P), Fhat_P(z+1)=[1-Q_P^(z+1)]Fhat_P(z), Fhat_P(0)=1. (3) They also define its meromorphic continuation in z. Consequently, with n a fixed nonnegative integer, Fhat_P(n)=(zeta^2;zeta^2)_n. (4) In particular (4) holds for EVERY 0<=n<=d=N-1 on a neighborhood of the original root. This is equality of generic analytic germs, not merely of their root values. The marked power Q_P^z is always exp(2z Log zeta). There is also an exact SECOND difference equation, G_P(z+P)=-2sin(pi z)G_P(z), Fhat_P(z+P)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]Fhat_P(z). (4a) To prove its constant, first take -1<Re z<0, so both z and z+P are in the defining Gamma domain. The quotient of the products truncated at k=K is (2pi/P)^P/[Gamma(z+1)Gamma(-z)] *Gamma(P(K+1)+z+1)Gamma(PK-z) /[P^(2PK)Gamma(K+1)^(2P)]. The last ratio tends to (2pi)^(1-P)P^P by the same uniform complex-sector Stirling formula, with all powers marked by Log P. The Gamma reflection identity then gives -2sin(pi z); equivalently that elementary Gamma identity follows from its convergent product and the sine product already used in (3). Meromorphic continuation proves the first equation globally. The exponential in (2) has P-shift quotient i exp(pi i z), proving the second equation with the displayed scalar ONE. The complex-P reflection is consequently exact as well: G_P(z)G_P(P-1-z)=P, Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(P-1-z) =P exp[pi i z(z-P+1)/P]. (4b) Indeed the z derivative of the first logarithm, truncated at K, telescopes to psi(PK+z+1)-psi(P(K+1)-z), which tends to zero. Its constant is G_P(P-1). Differentiating (4a) at z=0 gives G_P'(P)=-2pi. Differentiating (3) at z=P-1 gives G_P'(P)=-(2pi/P)G_P(P-1), hence the constant is P. The marked exponentials in (2) then give the second equation of (4b). ## 2. The complex-period asymptotic is uniform Let K be a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Uniformly for z=Nx, x in K, and P in a sufficiently small relative complex disk about N, put y=z/P. On a slightly smaller disk y stays in a fixed compact of the same strip. The DIRECT Stirling proof in the interpolation theorem then gives Log G_P(z)=P J(y)+(1/2)Log(2P sin(pi y)) +pi cot(pi y)/(12P)+O_K(|P|^-3), (5) where J'=Log(2sin(pi y)) has its original mark, continued from 0<y<1. Formula (5) is proved for complex P term by term: the Gamma arguments z,Pk+z,Pk-z remain in fixed right-half-plane sectors; the kth Stirling remainder is O_K(|P|^-3 k^-3). Summing it is uniform. The sine product sums the leading terms and the cotangent identity sums the 1/P terms just as before. This argument does not interpolate an identity known only at integer periods. The remainder is holomorphic on a larger relative P disk, so its P derivative at FIXED z is O_K(N^-4) by Cauchy's formula. The derivative of the leading term is partial_P[P J(z/P)]=J(y)-y J'(y). The two elementary exponential factors in (2) also have bounded P derivatives on this chart. Thus |partial_P Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C_K. (6) Since |P'(epsilon)|=|P|^2/pi=O(N^2), (6) implies |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|<=C_K N^2 (7) for fixed marked z=Nx in this interior chart. The logarithm here is the relative one at epsilon=0. There is no principal-root or dilogarithm reset when epsilon varies. ## 3. Fixed integer shifts cover the nonreal exterior rows Let K be any compact scaled-index set with |x|<=M, |Im x|>=delta>0, z=Nx. (8) Choose on each of finitely many smaller charts an integer k_N, FIXED as epsilon moves, with |k_N|<=C_K N and (z+k_N)/N in a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Such charts cover K by shifting the real part into the middle of the strip. For k_N>=0, use the exact formula Fhat_P(z)=Fhat_P(z+k_N) /product_(j=1)^(k_N)(1-Q_P^(z+j)); (9) for k_N<0 use the reciprocal-direction finite product. These are evaluations of the SAME meromorphic function by (3), not new independent factorial choices. For epsilon on the disk used below, all intermediate (z+j)/P have imaginary part bounded away from zero. Their real and imaginary parts remain bounded. Therefore each finite sine or Pochhammer factor in (9) and its inverse is bounded by constants depending only on K. Its logarithmic epsilon derivative is -2(z+j) zeta^[2(z+j)]/[1-zeta^[2(z+j)]]=O_K(N). There are O_K(N) factors. Combining this with (7) proves the same O_K(N^2) logarithmic derivative for these exterior rows. In particular negative rows and rows above N are controlled when their scaled imaginary parts stay away from zero. The statement does NOT give a bound across their real integer zeros or poles. Those are retained by the exact interpolation. ## 4. The fixed endpoint and all physical factorials For every original fixed integer 0<=n<=d, use (4) itself. On a sufficiently small disk about epsilon=0, partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n) =sum_(j=1)^n -2j zeta^(2j)/(1-zeta^(2j)). (10) At the root |1-q0^(2j)|>=c min(j,N-j)/N. Perturbing epsilon by at most c/[N^2(1+log N)] keeps every denominator comparable to its root value. Summing the displayed elementary bounds gives |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n)| <=C N^2(1+log N), (11) UNIFORMLY in n, including n=d=N-1. No asymptotic estimate at the endpoint x=1 is being inferred from an interior compact. The finite index n, and specifically d, is fixed throughout. At the root one may use the already proved exact identity with N-1-z for evaluating root values. It is NOT an identity with that same fixed endpoint after P moves. For example its generic integer factorial factors have the nonzero logarithmic derivatives (10). Replacing the fixed d by P-1 during differentiation would change the source and is not part of this construction. The second period also supplies an exact normal-transport equation. Put H_N(z)=partial_epsilon Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0, with z FIXED. Since P'(0)=iN^2/pi, differentiating (4a) gives H_N(z+N)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]H_N(z) -(iN^2/pi)partial_z Fhat_N(z+N). (11a) The undivided identity remains meaningful at the physical zeros. The last term is essential: the left argument in (4a) moves with P. Thus actual generic normals do not obey a root-only N-shift rule obtained by omitting that index derivative. More generally put Delta=N-P and c(z)=1-exp(2pi i z). There is the exact local analytic identity Fhat_P(z+N)=exp(Delta partial_z)[c(z)Fhat_P(z)]. (11b) Indeed z+N=(z+Delta)+P, so this is just (4a) at z+Delta. Modulo epsilon^(J+1), Delta belongs to the ideal (epsilon), and the exponential in (11b) is the FINITE differential operator sum_(j=0)^J Delta^j partial_z^j/j!. On a chart where c is a unit, divide by the root multiplier and write U=c^-1 exp(Delta partial_z)c =exp[Delta(partial_z+c'/c)]. The conjugation identity follows by applying partial_z to c times a test function. Its logarithmic connection has explicit simple poles at the integers. On the order-J jet module, U-I raises the epsilon filtration and therefore (U-I)^(J+1)=0. Its inverse is the finite geometric series in -(U-I). This is an actual unipotent transport of finite quantum jets, with the differential correction (11a) at order one. The localization excludes the original c-divisors; the statement does not remove physical support zeros, prove convergence of an infinite jet expansion, or select a global degree cycle. The two exact shifts themselves form a flat rank-one difference connection. With a_P(z)=1-exp[2pi i(z+1)/P], one has a_P(z+P)=a_P(z) and c(z+1)=c(z), so applying the unit shift and the P shift in either order gives the same multiplier. At P=N, their compatibility includes the literal cyclotomic norm product_(j=1)^N(1-exp[2pi i(z+j)/N]) =1-exp(2pi i z). The Gamma product (2) chooses a section of this connection. These equations alone do not establish global uniqueness of a section: a factor periodic under both shifts preserves them. Nor do they determine the original source period or its cycle. ## 5. Uniform relative disks and genuine normal bounds Consider a fixed finite list of factorial arguments, each either * a fixed original integer between 0 and N-1; * z=Nx in a fixed compact of the interior strip; or * z=Nx in a fixed compact satisfying (8), continued by (9). All indices are held fixed when the generic parameter varies. Affine O(1) offsets are allowed by enlarging the compacts slightly. For sufficiently small c_K>0, on |epsilon|<=rho_N=c_K/[N^2(1+log N)] (12) every listed factorial is nonzero and holomorphic, and C_K^-1 <= |Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)/Fhat_N(z)| <= C_K. (13) The same holds for any fixed finite product or quotient of the listed factors. Equations (7),(9),(11), integrated along the epsilon segment, prove (13), with a consistent relative logarithm. Cauchy's formula on (12) proves for every fixed j |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0 <=C_(K,j)[N^2(1+log N)]^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (14) Inverse factorials have the corresponding relative bound. In particular the entire assertion holds on the smaller actual normal disk |epsilon|<=c N^-10, at cost at most C_(K,j)N^(10j). The marked factors exp(pi i z), zeta^[z(L-z-1)] and the original physical cup scalar N zeta^(-d^2) cause no further difficulty: L and all indices are O(N), so the epsilon derivative of their logarithms is O_K(N^2), and higher derivatives follow on (12). Thus the original continued cups and inverse cups formed from these factors also satisfy (13),(14). No unit phase is discarded. One can specify the formerly ambiguous off-grid symmetric gauge as well. For a fixed integer L<N, set b_L(epsilon,z)=zeta^[z(L-z)] Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(L-z)/Fhat_P(L), g_L(epsilon,z)=[b_L(epsilon,z)/b_L(0,z)]^(1/2). (15) Use the analytic square root equal to 1 at epsilon=0. Whenever the two index arguments satisfy the preceding hypotheses, (13) on a smaller disk makes this a specified holomorphic unit with the same relative jet bounds. It is symmetric under z->L-z and agrees with the original physical gauge at every admissible integer index. Its continuation is now fixed by (2), rather than inferred from bounded values on a finite integer set. At epsilon=0 the displayed phases cancel exactly, giving b_L(0,z)=G_N(z)G_N(L-z)/G_N(L). The already proved FIXED-root reflection therefore gives b_d(0,z)=1 meromorphically, also at noninteger z. This is useful for evaluating the root cup. It does not say that b_d(epsilon,z) is constant when P moves. In fact (4b) gives the exact fixed-endpoint correction b_d(epsilon,z)=P/Fhat_P(d) *exp[pi i z(N-P)/P] *Fhat_P(d-z)/Fhat_P(P-1-z). (16) The final quotient retains the difference between the original fixed d=N-1 and the moving endpoint P-1. Formula (16), or its derivative, may be used for boundary transport; replacing that quotient by one away from the root changes the genuine normal. ## 6. Application scope at the slightly nonreal geometric degree For the actual channel cup, the needed arguments are r=a-h and 2a-r, while the physical cups use v,d-v,l,d-l. In the joint deficient geometric corridor take a small but fixed NONZERO imaginary part of the degree. Then r/N and (2a-r)/N lie in nonreal exterior compacts, with opposite imaginary signs; the physical cup arguments have real parts strictly inside (0,1). The remaining factorials F_a,F_m,F_(2a),F_d have fixed integer indices below N. The lemma therefore controls all these explicit boundary factors and their genuine generic derivatives together. It does not justify crossing their real degree poles, deform the original support cycle, or prove a nonzero geometric contribution. Source assembly must still use the actual large-partner white columns and all original tensor marks. The present result is the moving-period analytic input for that assembly, not a replacement for its finite tensor identity or its global period argument. ## 7. Finite checks and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_normals_results.json) check the actual generic integer factorials, independent Gamma/Barnes evaluations, relative disks, fixed-endpoint derivatives, exterior gauges, second-period and complex-period reflection identities, and fixed-N first and second normal transport. Its largest relative identity error at 85 digits was below 5.3e-82. These finite checks support, and do not replace, the proofs above. The moving-period theorem does not transport degree globally across retained divisors or identify a contributing quantum cycle.

title: Actual multichannel Newton transport beyond the tame figure-eight source
text: # Actual multichannel Newton transport beyond the tame figure-eight source 28 October 2026. The actual five-crossing Newton source does NOT have a polynomially bounded coefficient vector. This can be proved directly, without using its volume theorem: a uniformly dominated initial transfer branch forces exponential growth of a genuine Newton coefficient. Consequently a polynomially bounded source-preserving comparison to the previous tame UL response cannot exist in this universal Newton basis. There is nevertheless a source-exact two-channel replacement. Both endpoint source vectors have polynomial norms. Forward and backward Green transport therefore give a strictly sharper coefficient barrier than the one-sided largest-root bound. Combining it with the original complete evaluation, and then the audited root-color Plancherel identity, gives an unconditional quantitative upper bound for this full source. Its barrier is about 0.57776, whereas the selected invariant's known rate is about 0.45011. The remaining outer phase cancellation has not been eliminated. The matrix estimate in Section 4 applies to fixed-channel recurrences generally. No new knot class or general volume bound is claimed. ## 1. The original coefficients and their exact monic recurrence The independently proved WHOLE-source transform in `five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md` gives, at every primitive root, F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) C_n T_n(Y), T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^-1-Q^r-Q^-r), C_n=(-1)^n t^(n(n+3)/2) J_n(t), t=Q^-1, J_n(t)=sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (1) All original turns, Cartan scalars and framing are included in that identity. No coefficient is chosen to fit an unknown scalar. The phases preceding J_n have modulus one at the specified root. The coefficients satisfy, GENERICALLY in t, J_0=1, J_1=1+t^2, J_n=(1+t-t^n+t^(2n))J_(n-1) -t(1-t^(n-1))J_(n-2). (2) Here is an elementary derivation. Put F_n=(t;t)_n and, formally, E(z)=sum_(k>=0)z^k/F_k, G(z)=sum_(j>=0)t^(j(j+1))z^j/F_j, H(z)=sum_(n>=0)J_n z^n/F_n=E(z)G(z). Coefficient comparison gives E(tz)=(1-z)E(z) and G(z)-G(tz)=t^2 z G(t^2z). Eliminating E yields (1-z)(1-tz)H(z)-(1-tz)H(tz)-t^2zH(t^2z)=0. Its n-th coefficient is (2). This is a formal identity before root specialization; at n<N no vanishing factorial is divided out. With w_n=(J_n,J_(n-1))^t, n>=1, the actual transfer is w_n=M_(N,n)w_(n-1), M_(N,n)=[[1+t-t^n+t^(2n), -t(1-t^(n-1))], [1, 0 ]]. (3) Its leading coefficient is ONE, so there is no singular forward division. Its determinant is t(1-t^(n-1)), nonzero for 2<=n<=N-1. ## 2. The terminal source is known and polynomial too At t^N=1, root reflection gives {N-1 choose j}_t=(-1)^j t^(-j(j+1)/2). Thus J_(N-1) is the explicit quadratic Gauss sum sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(-1)^j t^(j(j+1)/2), of modulus at most N. Likewise {N-2 choose j}_t={N-1 choose j}_t (1-t^(-1-j))/(1-t^-1). Since |1-t^-1|>=4/N, (1) proves |J_(N-2)|<=N^2/2. Therefore both w_1 and the ACTUAL terminal w_(N-1) have polynomial norms. These endpoint bounds are finite coefficient identities, not an assumption that the desired Kashaev value is small. ## 3. A direct all-level obstruction to a tame UL coefficient response For x=n/N let z=exp(-2pi i x). The continuous transfer limit is M(x)=[[2-z+z^2, -(1-z)], [1,0]], p(z,L)=L^2-(2-z+z^2)L+1-z. (4) For 0<=x<=1/32, |z-1|<=pi/16<1/5. Hence |2-z+z^2-2|<1/5 and |1-z|<1/5. On |L-2|=1/2, the unperturbed |L(L-2)| is at least 3/4, whereas the perturbation is at most (1/5)(5/2)+(1/5)=7/10. Rouche's argument gives a single analytic root L_+ in that disk, so |L_+|>=3/2. The other root has modulus at most (1/5)/(3/2)=2/15. The eigenvectors (L_+,1) and (L_-,1) give a uniformly smooth, invertible eigenframe on this interval. In that frame each finite step (3) equals diag(L_+,L_-)+O(1/N), uniformly, including the frame change at adjacent x. Its initial vector w_1 tends to (2,1), the L_+ eigenvector at x=0. The ratio of the second component to the first is O(1/N) initially and remains O(1/N): the offdiagonal entries are O(1/N), while |L_-/L_+|<=4/45<1. Induction therefore keeps a fixed O(1/N) cone. The first component is multiplied at each step by L_+(x)+O(1/N), and the resulting product error is bounded above and below by constants on this fixed-length x interval. The original first coordinate J_n has the same exponential rate. For n=floor(N/32), this proves the unconditional lower estimate liminf_N (1/N)log||C^(N)||_2 >=log(3/2)/32>0. (5) The tame fixed-window UL theorem has polynomial coefficient response. Equation (5) therefore rules out representing THIS actual coefficient vector by that response under a comparison whose map AND inverse have polynomial norms and preserve the pointed source. In particular a diagonal unitary phase gauge cannot fix it. This statement does not rule out a different metric, a genuine multichannel transport, or later source-exact fusion; their exponential evaluation cost must stay. ## 4. A uniform two-boundary matrix estimate Let T_(N,n) be a fixed-size matrix family converging uniformly to continuous T(x). Suppose rho(T(x)) and rho(adj T(x)) are positive on the parameter interval, and every actual determinant in its interior is nonzero. For a specified solution with polynomial endpoint norms, forward and backward propagation give (1/N)log||w_n|| <=min{ H_f(n/N), H_b(n/N)}+o(1), (6) uniformly in n, where H_f(x)=integral_0^x log rho(T(s))ds, H_b(x)=integral_x^1 log rho(adj T(s))ds -lim (1/N)sum_(ell=n+1)^(N-1)log|det T_(N,ell)|. An endpoint factorial product or leading-germ identity must justify the last limit uniformly; it is not silently inferred at an exact zero. To prove the numerator estimates, fix epsilon>0 and use the positive Lyapunov metric H_eps(x)=sum_(k>=0)(T(x)^*)^k T(x)^k /(rho(T(x))+epsilon)^(2k). For bounded matrices of fixed size this converges uniformly, is continuous, is at least I and bounded above.
