With the second cut immediately after the first positive crossing, the actual one-crossing and three-crossing words have, in the SAME retained normalization, \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{word}&\Phi(C_I)&F_{-1}\\\hline \sigma_1&-i/2&1/2\\ \sigma_1^3&3i/2&1/2. \end{array} \tag{8} \] Their closed braids are the unknot and trefoil. No common rescaling calibrated on the former makes the moment agree with the latter's original source. The common external conventions in (8) matter; they have not been separately normalized to preferred knot values. Equations (3)-(4), not equality to the identity source, explain the nonzero moment. ## 4. An actual Ward factorial has the required inverse-norm pole There is also a constructive local atom, retaining both the physical edge clock and its quantum normal. Use the actual unfolding F(Q,z) of the original factorial block. Ward iteration gives the EXACT whole negative N-step ratio \[ R_N^-(Q,B) =\frac{F(Q,BQ^{-N})}{F(Q,B)} =\frac1{(BQ^{-N};Q)_N} =\frac1{(1-B/Z)\,V_N(Q,B)},\quad Z=Q^N, \tag{9} \] where V_N=product_(r=1)^(N-1)(1-BQ^r/Z). Near the actual corner Q=Q_N,B=1 it is a unit with V_N(Q_N,1)=N. In particular the off-root divisor is B=Z, not B=1 obtained by first forgetting Q^N. Every scalar and this moving divisor are retained in (9). At the physical root, \[ R_N^-(Q_N,B)=\frac1{1-B^N}. \tag{10} \] The scaled physical boundary B=exp(w/N) makes (10) exactly 1/(1-exp w), for EVERY N. Its pole at w=0 has coefficient -1. This is a uniform root-slice boundary model. No uniform growing-N off-root estimate for V_N is inferred from its fixed-N unit property. The fixed-N exceptional normal ratio of the same actual atom, Q=Q_N exp(epsilon), U=exp(tN epsilon), is (1-B^N)^t. Formula (9) is its t=-1 case as an exact whole finite-product identity, with U=Q^(-N). Thus the pole is an original negative Ward circuit and its norm zero, not a pole supplied by a chosen unrelated amplitude. Its place in an actual factorial crossing coefficient can be specified without discarding the other factors. For any literal block C_k(z)=(z;Q)_k, the whole N-carry identity is \[ \frac{C_{k+N}(z)}{C_k(z)}=(zQ^k;Q)_N, \qquad \frac{C_k(z)}{C_{k+N}(z)}=(zQ^k;Q)_N^{-1}. \tag{10a} \] The actual balanced R coefficients in [the marked holonomy construction](marked_braid_holonomy.md), Section 3, are products and quotients of precisely these blocks and Cartan lines. For a denominator block, put B=zQ^(k+N) in (9); (10a)'s inverse is exactly the same atom. At the root its full norm is 1-(zQ^k)^N, rather than an unmarked numerical multiplier. This identifies a specific original denominator-block carry that supplies the pole. It does not treat that block in isolation as the full crossing coefficient: its numerator blocks, resonant factorials, Cartan line and actual source remain necessary and can cancel it. For the pure-prefix GEOMETRIC chart, take c=U_21 nonzero, s nonzero. Its principal relation is \[ k-1=-\frac{c\eta_{geo}}{s(1-\eta_{geo})^2},\quad B=k^{-1}, \quad \Omega_{cut}=\frac{d\log A\wedge d\eta_{geo}} {s(1-\eta_{geo})^2}. \tag{11} \] If the actual negative Ward circuit (9) is inserted and this principal geometric chart is used, its amplitude (10) has the nonzero polar coefficient \[ [\eta_{geo}^{-1}]R_N^-(Q_N,B(\eta_{geo}))=-\frac{s}{Nc}, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Res}}_{\eta_{geo}=0} (R_N^-\Omega_{cut})=-\frac1{Nc}d\log A. \tag{12} \] This follows from B-1=(c/s)eta_geo+O(eta_geo^2), so 1-B^N=-(Nc/s)eta_geo+O(eta_geo^2). Only that first polar coefficient enters (12). It is a nonzero actual-atom boundary coefficient. It is NOT a theorem that the original full knot co-source contains this negative circuit, or that its Fourier cap cycle maps to this geometric boundary. An actual crossing can carry several factorial, source and norm factors whose products change the pole order or cancel its coefficient. The exact coefficient (12) identifies what one original Ward factor can supply; (4) and (7)-(8) forbid recovering the selected source by a universal normalized negative-band moment. ## 5. Exact audit and remaining concrete target [The audit script](../experiments/audit_actual_negative_band_boundary_moment.py) checks actual signed tensor instances of (2)-(4), the complete characteristic-zero examples (7)-(8), the original inverse-norm factorization and the simple residue (12). Results are in [the reproducible output](../experiments/actual_negative_band_boundary_moment_results.json). The remaining target is an actual relative source transform carrying the independent physical B sum, Fourier eta_F cap, (3)-(4)'s Ward row and all normal/divisor factors into the geometric chart. The bare equality of a regular transverse Gaussian with the original identity source is not supplied by this local calculation.

title: Exact coherent turn reduction in the original Newton source
text: # Exact coherent turn reduction in the original Newton source 29 October 2026. The full original Newton alphabet obeys a projective modular relation, with its Cartan scalar retained. It removes arbitrary numbers of redundant twist/turn packets BEFORE a norm estimate. In one arbitrary-length class the complete reflected original source is exactly 1 or N and has zero exponential rate. A same-sign run of two-crossing packets reduces to one twist with explicit boundary adapters. These are source-exact coherent reductions, not a new hyperbolic-volume family. ## 1. All-input relation, including the original Cartan line Use the COMPLETE Newton packet of [the positive turn metric](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md). Let T=T_1, P=P_rev, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and nu_j=(-1)^j Q^(j(j+1)/2). Its actual entries are T_ij=kappa nu_j (-q)^(i-j) [i choose j]_Q, i>=j, T^(-1)=conjugate(T). All matrices below act on the FULL N-dimensional Newton packet, including every original confluent derivative. Put theta_N=kappa^3(-q)^d, |theta_N|=1. In fact theta_N=kappa, since kappa^2(-q)^d=1 at the specified root. Keeping the unsimplified form below displays the original phase sources. Then T P T=theta_N P T^(-1)P, (T P)^3=theta_N I. (1) Here P is the genuine unscaled physical turn in this packet. No eigenvalue-only quotient or assumed ordinary positive trace is used. For a finite own proof of (1), the Gaussian identity needed is sum_(k=0)^i (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2-jk) [i choose k]_Q [j+k choose j]_Q =(-1)^i Q^(i(i-1)/2-ij) [j choose i]_Q. (2) To prove it, expand [j+k choose j]_Q=(Q^(k+1);Q)_j/F_j =F_j^(-1) sum_(l=0)^j (-1)^l Q^(l(l+1)/2)[j choose l]_Q Q^(kl). The finite binomial theorem performs the inner k sum as (Q^(l-j);Q)_i. If i>j every term is zero. If i<=j, only l<=j-i survive; insert (Q^(l-j);Q)_i =(-1)^i Q^[-i(j-l)+i(i-1)/2] F_(j-l)/F_(j-l-i). The remaining sum is sum_(l=0)^(j-i) (-1)^l Q^[l(l+1)/2+il] /(F_l F_(j-i-l)) =(Q^(i+1);Q)_(j-i)/F_(j-i)=[j choose i]_Q. This proves (2) by two finite binomial expansions. At the root every denominator used here has index<N. If j+k>=N the product expression for [j+k choose j] is zero and exactly supplies the original cutoff. Now use the exact root reflection [d-k choose j]_Q=nu_j^(-1) Q^(-jk)[j+k choose j]_Q. The (i,j) entry of TPT becomes kappa^2(-q)^(i+d-j) times the left side of (2). For i>j it is zero. For i<=j, the reflected inverse entry is (P T^(-1)P)_ij =kappa^(-1) nu_j^(-1)(-q)^(-(j-i)) nu_(j-i)[j choose i]_Q. Since nu_(j-i)/nu_j=(-1)^i Q^[i(i-1)/2-ij], (2) gives (1) entry by entry. Thus all repeated-root normal data are retained. These are the full CASIMIR Hermite normals at the fixed quantum root. No differentiation in q is being asserted: the actual generic-q turn need not be constant reversal in this root Newton frame. ## 2. An arbitrary-turn complete original source with an exact rate Let C=TP and let 1=e_0 be the original numerator-source vector. The first and last T columns give C e_0=kappa e_d, C^2 e_0=kappa^2 ((-q)^i)_(i=0)^d. Together with (1), for every integer h, C^(3h)e_0=theta_N^h e_0, C^(3h+1)e_0=theta_N^h kappa e_d, C^(3h+2)e_0=theta_N^h kappa^2 ((-q)^i)_i. (3) The exact positive Newton metric consequently gives, for EVERY N, ||C^m 1||^2 = 1, m=0 or1 mod3; N, m=2 mod3. (4) Its literal adjoint-word closure, with the original unrestricted marked cap and original cups, is exactly this norm by the positive metric theorem. Thus the ENTIRE original reflected circuit has zero exponential rate for arbitrarily many fixed turns. This does not say C is unitary: (4) itself distinguishes norms1 and N. It says that these particular large coherent turn networks are projectively periodic. This is a useful normalization class, not a new hyperbolic class. It shows why assigning an independent positive angle capacity to each expanded crossing cannot give the actual rate even in the positive reflected-source formulation. ## 3. Exact reduction of arbitrary same-sign two-crossing runs There is also a useful reduction of the newly solved T_2 kernel: T^2 P=theta_N C T^(-1)C^(-1), (T^2P)^m=theta_N^m C T^(-m)C^(-1). (5) These follow algebraically from (1), for all signed integers m. The original source endpoint satisfies C^(-1)e_0=kappa^(-2)(-q)^(-d) T e_0. Consequently the source-selected whole run is exactly (T^2P)^m e_0 =theta_N^m kappa^(-2)(-q)^(-d) T P T^(1-m)e_0. (6) Thus a run with unbounded turn count has ONE retained turn and one signed twist packet, with all original phase and endpoint adapters displayed. The adapters are actual Newton operators; no assertion of polynomial conditioning or unitarity is made for T. Equation (6) is an exact coherent source reduction, not a sharp estimate for its remaining mixed packet. The same relation can remove unit digits inside a general rational twist/turn word, with (1)'s scalar recorded. Reduced mixed-sign words still contain real oscillatory interactions. Neither (5) nor finite order of C diagonalizes those words or proves a geometric maximum. ## 4. Remaining analytic scope The source of a genuinely reduced word is not determined by the modular relation. In particular the norm of TPT_(-p)e_0 generally contains a nontrivial coherent finite sum; unit nodal twist phases do not make it a polynomially bounded operator. A new sharp variational estimate must control that remaining packet and its integer marks, then identify its full critical graph and regulator. This note proves the exact reduction and the nonzero rate statement (4), not those unproved assertions for arbitrary rational/arborescent sources. Audit: [full original physical alphabet, all-input modular identity and actual reflected closures](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_coherent_turn_reduction.py).

title: The original Newton and complete-core local actions on the reciprocal branch
status: Local marked action equality; finite cycle open
text: # The original Newton and complete-core local actions on the reciprocal branch 30 October 2026. Original untwisted port; x,b,c,y>0, with the literal input b/output c convention. The theorem is an equality on the selected HOLOMORPHIC GERM near alpha=0 and any fixed positive face base. The real formulas below use 0<alpha<1/2 to describe the reciprocal algebraic branch; they do not assert a global continuation of the marked core or its source period over that range. This compares classical generating functions on one explicitly continued sheet. It neither moves a finite source cycle nor identifies its amplitude or contribution. Use the [exact Newton action and its localized critical equations](actual_alternating_newton_peripheral_branch.md). Put A0=x+y, L=A0+b+c, D=xy-bc and kappa=4cos(pi alpha)^2. For 0<alpha<1/2, let z be the smaller positive root of (L^2+kappa D)z^2-(2LA0+kappa xy)z+A0^2=0. The existing proof gives 0<z<A0/L<1. Set theta=acos(cos(pi alpha)sqrt(z)), r=theta/pi, rho=1-r, W=exp(-2i theta), k=(A0-Lz)/(2cos theta)>0, sinh(pi beta)=sin(pi alpha)sqrt(z/(1-z)), delta=i beta. The two useful algebraic identities are k^2=xy(1-z)+bc z, A0-Lz=2k cos theta. (1) The actual selected primitive collar obeys R0=exp(2pi i alpha), with meridian M=exp(-pi i alpha). The reflected Newton root W is chosen, not the first-half root exp(2i theta). ## 1. The exact marked Newton lifts Write phi_b=Arg(k+b exp(i theta)), phi_c similarly, and set xi=Arg(k-x exp(-i theta))/pi, eta=Arg(k-y exp(-i theta))/pi, mu=1-phi_c/pi. (2) All arguments in (2) are the indicated real arguments between0 andpi. The exact reverse reconstruction has t=-k exp(-i theta), A=exp(2pi i xi)=(k-x exp(-i theta))/(k-x exp(i theta)), B=exp(2pi i eta)=(k-y exp(-i theta))/(k-y exp(i theta)), Z=exp(2pi i mu)=(k+c exp(-i theta))/(k+c exp(i theta)). (3) This is precisely the earlier t=W(Lz-A0)/(W+1), followed by its original A,B,Z reconstruction. Moreover its t equation gives AB/Z=(k+b exp(-i theta))/(k+b exp(i theta)). Now 0<phi_b,phi_c<theta and 0<pi xi,pi eta<pi-theta. Consequently xi+eta+(phi_b+phi_c)/pi is an integer strictly between 0 and2, hence exactly1. Thus mu-xi-eta=phi_b/pi, 1-mu=phi_c/pi. (4) This proves that ALL four Newton face loads are positive and add to1. It also proves the strict four-binomial K-polytope inequalities: rho<mu<1, 0<xi,eta<rho, xi+eta<mu, mu+rho-xi-eta=rho+phi_b/pi<1. Only the low-color Newton termination is violated: rho>1/2>alpha. The principal log mu=-phi_c/pi is NOT the original marked lift (2); already its face monomial would change by Log(c/b), before any additional entropy-sheet changes. ## 2. Full face momenta equal the core angles Let Q_b(delta) be the actual one-triangle determinant-plus-beta rate plus HALF of the forced-factor rate, normalized by Q_b(0)=F(x,b,y). Then Q_b'=-Log(E_b/sqrt(Dg)), where Dg=A0^2-4xy sin(pi delta)^2, T_b^2=b A0+xy+b^2 sin(pi delta)^2, E_b=A0+2b sin(pi delta)^2+2sin(pi delta)T_b. All roots and logarithms are the source-selected ones at completeness. The [proved source circle-pattern identity](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md), section3, gives partial_(log l_j)Q_b=theta_j^(b)/(2pi), the three actual center angles. At delta=i beta the angles remain real and positive on the selected near-complete germ. Directly from (1), with C=cos theta,S=sin theta, cosh(pi beta)=S/sqrt(1-z), T_b=(k+b C)/sqrt(1-z), T_c=(k+c C)/sqrt(1-z). (5) Therefore the middle-angle formula tan(theta_b/2)=b cosh(pi beta)/T_b is tan(phi_b). Since both angles lie in(0,pi), theta_b=2phi_b, and similarly theta_c=2phi_c. This proves the two middle derivatives. Here is an explicit algebraic proof for the outer derivatives too. Put H=1-z and R0x=xH(y-x)+2i x S k, R1x=H A0+2x(z-C^2)+2i x S C, R_b=R0x+b R1x, R_c=R0x+c R1x. The actual deformed center-triangle sine/cosine formulas say exp(i theta_x^(b))=R_b/[(x+b)H sqrt(Dg)]. The identity R_b R_c (k-x C-i x S) =(x+b)(x+c)H^2 Dg (k-x C+i x S) (6) follows by substitution of b+c=[A0 H-2kC]/z, bc=[k^2-xyH]/z, S^2=1-C^2. In particular exp(i(theta_x^(b)+theta_x^(c)))=exp(2pi i xi). Both angle sums lie strictly between0 and2pi, so they agree as marked angles, not merely modulo2pi. Exchange x,y for the other outer face. Thus the full homogeneous face gradients are exactly (xi,mu-xi-eta,1-mu,eta) =partial_(log x,log b,log c,log y)[Q_b(delta)+Q_c(delta)]. (7) Equation (6) was independently expanded symbolically; its residual is identically zero after the three displayed substitutions. The angle branches extend to a sufficiently small complex neighborhood. Regularity of the reconstructed critical point comes from the earlier localized four-branch reconstruction and its simple quadratic roots, not from the outer-angle identity alone. ## 3. The actual sine continuation and stationarity Let J(t)=int_0^t Log(2sin(pi u))du, initially real for0<t<1. Continue rho BELOW the two real divisors rho=alpha and rho=1/2. On the final real reciprocal branch this specifies J(t)=-J(-t)+pi i t, -1<t<0, J(t)= J(t-1)+pi i(t-1), 1<t<2. (8) Both negative sine factors have Log=log(abs(sine))+pi i. The opposite approach sides in their arguments are essential: alpha-rho passes above0, while2rho passes below1. A continuation exists without any extra K divisor: the K-polytope is convex. Join an initial strict physical point with rho<alpha to (2) inside this polytope, and detour its parameter below the two specified rho crossings. All K arguments stay near(0,1); rho and alpha+rho also stay in(0,1). Use the FULL homogeneous action, not just its critical-variable part: Psi_New=K+B_alpha+pi i(alpha+rho)+Log c +mu Log(b/c)+xi Log(x/b)+eta Log(y/b), (9) with the literal K,B_alpha of the Newton theorem. On the selected real branch K has only positive sine arguments. By (8) the imaginary part of B_alpha is pi(1-alpha-rho). Thus the full action has constant imaginary part pi, and all four critical-variable derivatives have zero imaginary part. Their exponentiated equations are the exact uncleared Newton equations, so their real derivatives are exactly0. There is no concealed integer stationarity subtraction. The envelope external derivative retains the pi i alpha character: partial_alpha Psi_New,crit =Log[-sin(pi(alpha+rho))/sin(pi(alpha-rho))] =log[sin(theta-pi alpha)/sin(theta+pi alpha)] =-2pi beta=2pi i delta. (10) For the last step, tanh(pi beta)=tan(pi alpha)cot theta, by (5). Omitting pi i alpha would give the wrong external derivative. ## 4. Complete-core action and the additive constant Define the [original untwisted local core generating function](actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md) by S_core(alpha;x,b,c,y)=Q_b(delta)+Q_c(delta)+2pi i alpha delta, Log R0(delta)=2pi i alpha, delta(0)=0. (11) Its delta stationarity is exact, so its external derivative is 2pi i delta and its four face derivatives are (7). Consequently Psi_New,crit-S_core is constant on the selected connected germ. It is important that (9) contains Log c: without it one face derivative would differ by1 and the action difference would not be constant. Calibrate at x=b=c=y=1 and alpha=0. Then rho=2/3, mu=5/6, xi=eta=1/3, K=-4J(1/6)-4J(1/3), B_0=-5J(1/3)+pi i/3. The elementary reflection J(1-t)=-J(t) and duplication J(2t)=2J(t)+2J(t+1/2) imply2J(1/6)=3J(1/3). Also F(1,1,1)=-3[J(1/6)+J(1/3)]. Therefore Psi_New,crit = S_core + pi i. (12) This equality is exact on the specified holomorphic germ; it is not only equality of trace squares or exponentiated derivatives. Other continuation windings need their corresponding explicit characters. Both sides have been compared in the SAME homogeneous face normalization. The [literal source adapter](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), equation(7a), multiplies either local homogeneous kernel by N^-1(bc)^(-d/2) on the same original lifted face variables. Thus the corresponding physical-box actions both subtract (Log b+Log c)/2, and (12) is unchanged. The original global cup, cap, target and mark characters are likewise common and retained; none is reset to obtain the equality. At leading semiclassical level the additive constant is the actual phase exp(pi i N)=(-1)^N. The literal finite Newton sign is (-1)^(h-1+r)=exp[pi i N(alpha+rho)]*(-1); its additional order-one minus sign remains in the finite amplitude, as do all factorial +/-1 shifts. This result does not compare those amplitudes. The branch is outside the low terminating Newton support. Nothing here deforms the original finite cycle to it, excludes other branches or endpoint currents, or proves its contribution coefficient nonzero. It provides a source-normalized local classical generating-function interface only; global face identification still uses the original shared variables and their exact target/mark characters. ## 5. Physical support and verification The calibration at alpha=0 is an analytic germ limit, not an evaluation of L_0, which is exactly zero. Nor does the same exterior action prove a complete exponential rate for fixed low color. For h=1, alpha=1/N tends to zero, but the actual L_1 is the identity and its finite Newton sum contains ONLY r=0. The selected critical index has rho>1/2 and is absent from that terminating sum. Its local homogeneous identity kernel has the already proved rate log max(b,c), not an automatically selected complete-circle rate. These facts are consistent with (12): the theorem compares phase functions, not finite amplitudes, cycles or their contribution coefficients. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_complete_local_action.py) checks the exact polynomial identities, the explicitly marked loads, raw critical derivatives on the prescribed sine sheets, the unsquared collar, and the full action including its imaginary constant. Its [results](../experiments/actual_newton_complete_local_action_results.json) are classical identity checks, not numerical evidence for a finite source cycle deformation or a selected asymptotic contribution. The action identity is local and holomorphic. It does not determine the amplitude or a contributing cycle.

title: Actual ideal prism cells and geometric Newton associativity
text: # Actual ideal prism cells and geometric Newton associativity 29 October 2026. Every strictly positive Newton multiplication action is the volume of an explicit convex IDEAL TRIANGULAR PRISM. Its three ordered quadrilateral faces have cross ratios given by derivatives of the actual source action. Thus internal source stationarity is exactly the isometry condition for the prescribed quadrilateral face gluing. Two stationary multiplication cells form an ideal cube; its alternative diagonal cut gives the other parenthesization. The equality holds for the full conjugate-antisymmetric pre-Bloch class, not just its regulator. This supplies local geometric incidence and composition. It does not by itself identify every closed Conway expression with a complete hyperbolic link complement. Boundary degenerations, the global diagram identification and complete ends still require their own arguments. ## 1. The actual source action Use [the positive full-Newton multiplication](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md), whose uniform action is m(x,y,z)=L(x+y)+L(z)-L(x)-L(y) -L(z-x)-L(z-y)-L(x+y-z), L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du. Work first in its STRICT domain p=z-x>0, q=z-y>0, r=x+y-z>0, w=1-x-y>0, p+q+2r+w=1, x=q+r, y=p+r, 1-z=r+w. (1) For positive a+b+c=1 let V(a,b,c) be the actual volume of an ideal tetrahedron with angles pi(a,b,c). The proved source identity is pi m=V(y,x,w)+V(p,q,1-p-q)+V(p+q,r,r+w). (2) The source remains its original multiplication table, including its normal directions; no new state sum is being substituted here. ## 2. Explicit six vertices of a convex ideal prism In the upper half-space model, use the ideal point infinity and four points on the unit circle in the boundary plane: v0=1, v1=exp(2pi i p), v2=exp(2pi i(p+r)), v3=exp(2pi i(p+r+q)). (3) The consecutive half-arc lengths are p,r,q,r+w. They are all positive and sum to one. Let P be the intersection of the Euclidean lines (v0,v1) and (v2,v3). The inequalities in (1) imply that P lies beyond v1 on the ray from v0, and beyond v2 on the ray from v3. Indeed the exterior triangle (P,v1,v2) has angles angle(v1)=pi y, angle(v2)=pi x, angle(P)=pi w. Their sum is pi and all are positive. The elementary sine rule gives the explicit formula P=v1+kappa_x(v1-v0)=v2+kappa_y(v2-v3), kappa_x=sin(pi x)sin(pi r)/(sin(pi w)sin(pi p)), kappa_y=sin(pi y)sin(pi r)/(sin(pi w)sin(pi q)). (4) In particular |P|>1. Form the ideal quadrangular pyramid with apex infinity and base (v0,v1,v2,v3), and attach the ideal tetrahedron (infinity,P,v1,v2) along their common triangular face (infinity,v1,v2), on opposite sides of that face. The pyramid has dihedral angles p,r,q,r+w along its four base edges. Its dihedral angle at an apex edge is one minus the sum of the two adjacent half-arcs. Along the shared face the two apex-edge angles therefore add to pi after the attachment, while the base-edge angle adds to pi(r+w)<pi. The two coplanar face pairs merge. The resulting six-vertex polyhedron is the ideal triangular prism with faces triangles: (P,v1,v2), (infinity,v0,v3), quadrilaterals: Fx=(infinity,v0,v1,P), Fy=(infinity,v3,v2,P), Fz=(v0,v1,v2,v3). (5) Convexity is literal. The two merged vertical side planes are the planes over (v0,v1) and (v2,v3). The third vertical side plane is over (v3,v0). The remaining supporting hemispheres have boundary circles (v0,v1,v2,v3) and (P,v1,v2). P is outside the first circle, and v0,v3 are outside the second circle on the side opposite its arc through P. These five half-spaces contain both attached cells, and their intersection has exactly the vertices and faces (5). Thus the union is their convex intersection, not an immersed volume chain. Equivalently one may use the elementary convex-union argument: the two convex cells lie on opposite sides of the attaching support plane, and all its finite seam angles are at most pi. The union is locally convex. Between any two finite points, a length-minimizing path exists by compactness of a bounded hyperbolic ball containing a minimizing sequence; local convexity makes that path an ambient geodesic. Thus the union is convex, without an assertion at a missing ideal vertex. The complete edge-angle table is | Edges | Dihedral angle divided by pi | |---|---:| | P-v1 and infinity-v0 | x | | P-v2 and infinity-v3 | y | | v1-v2 and v0-v3 | 1-z | | P-infinity | w=1-x-y | | v0-v1 | p=z-x | | v2-v3 | q=z-y | Each ideal vertex has three incident angles summing to pi. The three longitudinal angles have sum pi(1-2r)<pi. This last strict inequality is visible directly in the construction; no polyhedron existence theorem is being invoked. Conversely any convex ideal triangular prism with these ordered ports has this explicit form after an isometry. Send its selected quadrilateral port circle to the unit circle, and one of its two remaining ideal vertices to infinity. The other two quadrilateral faces then lie in vertical planes through the remaining vertex P; their boundary lines are (v0,v1) and (v2,v3). Thus P is exactly their intersection, and its position on the exterior side of the base support hemisphere gives |P|>1. Orient the cyclic base order so that the finite triangular wall is (P,v1,v2). Its positive triangle angles make the four half-arcs (p,r,q,r+w) with w>0. The same sine rule recovers (4), and the edge-angle table recovers x=q+r, y=p+r, z=p+q+r. This verifies that the alternative prism pieces used in section 6 are actual cells of this family. Triangulating the quadrangular pyramid across (v0,v2) gives tetrahedral angle triples (p,r,1-p-r) and (p+r,q,r+w). Their volume sum is Lambda(pi p)+Lambda(pi q)+Lambda(pi r)+Lambda(pi(r+w)), because the complementary intermediate angles cancel. This is also the sum of the last two volumes in (2). The attached tetrahedron has volume V(y,x,w). Therefore this ACTUAL convex prism has volume pi m. ## 3. The ordered face metrics are the source derivatives For cyclically ordered ideal points (a,b,c,d) on a circle or line set kappa(a,b,c,d)=(a-b)(c-d)/((a-d)(b-c))>0, (6) using the limit when one point is infinity. This positive real number determines the ordered ideal quadrilateral up to hyperbolic isometry: send three vertices to (infinity,0,1) and the fourth is determined by (6). A one-step cyclic change of vertices, or reversal fixing the first vertex, replaces kappa by its reciprocal. For the orders in (5), direct substitution and the sine rule give kappa(Fx)=sin(pi x)sin(pi r)/(sin(pi w)sin(pi p)), kappa(Fy)=sin(pi y)sin(pi r)/(sin(pi w)sin(pi q)), kappa(Fz)=sin(pi p)sin(pi q)/(sin(pi z)sin(pi r)). (7) Differentiating the actual source action, with all other boundary variables fixed, proves the exact equations log kappa(Fx)=-partial_x m, log kappa(Fy)=-partial_y m, log kappa(Fz)=-partial_z m. (8) There is no normalization constant: all factors of 2 in L' cancel. The actual h-leaf action g(x)=-2L(x)-2L(1/2-x), 0<x<1/2, likewise has a literal ideal pyramid. Its apex is infinity and its base is the rectangle with vertices (1, exp(2pi i x), -1, -exp(2pi i x)). Its four base angles alternate x and 1/2-x, its four apex-edge angles are right angles, and its volume is pi g(x). Its ordered base metric is kappa_leaf=tan(pi x)^2=exp(-g'(x)). (9) ## 4. Source stationarity gives the actual corner-preserving gluing Mark any child output quadrilateral by C0,C1,C2,C3 in its source order. In a multiplication prism use the lower and upper input maps lower child: (C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (v0,v1,P,infinity), upper child: (C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (infinity,P,v2,v3). (10) These are the literal identity-stack corner identifications: the lower child's top left and right corners map to infinity and P, which are respectively the upper child's bottom left and right corners. Thus no unrecorded four-punctured-sphere mutation is inserted. Relative to (5), the first map is a cyclic shift and the second a reversal. Each replaces kappa by its reciprocal. At an internal wire u, source stationarity says that the child output derivative plus the parent input derivative is zero. Equations (8),(9) therefore give kappa_child kappa_parent=1. (11) By the complete metric invariant (6), (11) is EXACTLY the condition that (10) is an ideal-quadrilateral isometry. This proves metric matching of the whole face, rather than merely equality of a formal edge product. For the relevant angle bookkeeping, call output edges C0-C1 and C2-C3 FREE, and the other pair CAP. A leaf output has FREE angles x and CAP angles 1/2-x. A completed product output has FREE angles z and CAP angles 1-z. The input maps (10) send CAP edges to the prism's two edges with angle x or y, and FREE edges to its longitudinal edges. Thus a leaf-to-prism seam produces right angles on the CAP pair; a product-to-prism seam has angle pi on that pair and becomes flat. The edge common to both inputs has total angle pi(w+x+y)=pi, while the output's two longitudinal edges acquire angles pi(p+x)=pi z, pi(q+y)=pi z. (12) These identities explain the local right/flat boundary pattern. They do not alone prove the global closure or cusp completeness of an arbitrary expression. A genuine turn rotates a product output quadrilateral once, exchanges FREE and CAP, and replaces its label x by 1-x. It also inverts kappa, exactly as the derivative of the turned profile requires. ## 5. Equality of the full antisymmetric pre-Bloch class Write A(z)=[z]-[bar z] in the rational pre-Bloch group. For an ideal tetrahedron with positive angle triple (a,b,c), let its positive shape be z=exp(pi i a)sin(pi b)/sin(pi c), and put u_a=exp(2pi i a), and cyclically. Applying the defining five-term relation to (z,bar z) gives A(z)=-[u_a^-1]+[u_c]-[u_b^-1]. Subtract its complex conjugate. One obtains the uniform identity A(z)=1/2 (A(u_a)+A(u_b)+A(u_c)). (13) No integral inversion identity or unproved regulator injectivity is used. In particular A(exp(2pi i(1-a)))=-A(exp(2pi i a)) directly from its definition. Consequently the sum of A over a pyramid's two tetrahedra depends only on the sum of A(exp(2pi i theta)) over its four half-arcs; complementary diagonal terms cancel. The source ordering (p,q,r,r+w) and the actual prism ordering (p,r,q,r+w) give exactly the SAME class. Equation (13) therefore upgrades (2) to sum_(three source atoms) A(z_j) = sum_(an actual prism triangulation) A(z_j) (14) in the rational pre-Bloch group of any common field containing the displayed phases and shapes. For algebraic source stationary points this is a number field, as in the proved source-regulator theorem. No assertion of zero boundary for this open cell is made. More generally the antisymmetric class of a convex ideal polyhedron is independent of its ideal triangulation, directly from five-term relations. For equal boundary triangulations the difference of two tetrahedral chains is a 3-cycle in the full abstract simplex on their ideal vertices. Coning it to one vertex gives a 4-chain bounding it; the boundary of each 4-simplex is precisely a five-term relation. Different triangulations of a boundary polygon can first be corrected by tetrahedral chains whose four vertices lie on that face's circle. Their shapes are real, hence their A-symbols are zero. This proves the assertion without assuming a general Pachner-connectivity theorem. ## 6. Actual ideal-cube geometry proves stationary associativity Fix positive a,b,c,d with a+b<1, a+c<1, b+c<1, max(a,b,c)<d<min(1,a+b+c). (15) For the left parenthesization put F_L(t)=m(a,b,t)+m(t,c,d), max(a,b,d-c)<t<min(a+b,d,1-c). (16) This interval is nonempty precisely under (15). Its derivative is F_L'(t)=log[sin(pi(t+c)) sin(pi(a+b-t)) sin(pi(d-t)) /(sin(pi(t-a)) sin(pi(t-b)) sin(pi(t+c-d)))]. It tends to positive infinity at the lower endpoint and negative infinity at the upper endpoint. Strict concavity of the two actual source actions gives a UNIQUE interior maximizer t*. Therefore the two multiplication prisms glue by (10),(11). Their two wall-edge seams with angles (1-t*)+t* become flat. The four triangular walls merge into two quadrilateral walls. The union is an ACTUAL convex ideal cube with four input/output port faces. Its wall-edge angles, in order around either wall, are pi(a,b,c,1-d), and its four edges between consecutive port faces have angles pi(1-a-b), pi(1-b-c), pi(d-c), pi(d-a). (17) They are all positive and less than pi by (15). The seam's remaining edge angles are respectively (t*-a)+(d-t*)=d-a and (t*-b)+(1-t*-c)=1-b-c. Thus the two convex cells have no reentrant seam, and their union is the convex ideal hexahedron with these faces. There is an explicit common reflection, which supplies the other diagonal cut without invoking a rigidity theorem. For the single prism in section 2 define the reflection in the hemisphere centered at P with squared radius |P|^2-1: R(z)=P+(|P|^2-1)/(bar z-bar P). (18) It exchanges infinity with P. The elementary power-of-a-point identity for the unit circle shows that it exchanges v0 with v1 and v3 with v2. Its reflecting plane is perpendicular to all three quadrilateral port planes: it is perpendicular to the two vertical planes through P and orthogonal to the unit hemisphere. It exchanges the prism's two triangular walls. The corner maps (10) intertwine the corresponding vertex exchanges. Hence the two reflecting planes agree after gluing, and the ideal cube has a common reflection plane. Its section by that plane is a convex hyperbolic quadrilateral; its four vertices lie on the four edges between port faces. Each such edge is perpendicular to the reflection plane, and its two ideal endpoints are exchanged. The OTHER diagonal of this quadrilateral determines a hyperbolic plane perpendicular to the reflection plane. It contains both full perpendicular port edges at its endpoints. Consequently it cuts the cube in an IDEAL QUADRILATERAL with those four ideal endpoints. The two pieces are convex ideal triangular prisms. Their external ports are (b,c) and (a,d), exactly the right parenthesization. If u* denotes the new internal source label, the angle table in section 2 gives their actions m(b,c,u*) and m(a,u*,d). Their common face is already isometric, so (8) gives right-side stationarity. The same endpoint and strict-concavity argument makes u* its unique maximizer. Both parenthesizations thus decompose ONE actual ideal cube. They have equal volume and equal full antisymmetric pre-Bloch class by section 5. This is a source-local geometric associativity theorem; it is stronger than deducing equality of exponential rates from the finite algebra's associativity. There is also an exact algebraic check of the critical point. Put X=exp(2pi i a), Y=exp(2pi i b), Z=exp(2pi i c), W=exp(2pi i d), T=exp(2pi i t*). The sine equation in (16) is the polynomial identity (ZT-1)(XY-T)(W-T)=(T-X)(T-Y)(ZT-W). Its cubic and constant terms cancel, and its nonzero root is T=(XYZW-XYZ+XY-XW-YW+W) /(XYZ-XZ-YZ+ZW-W+1). (19) The denominator is nonzero under (15): otherwise the polynomial would have no nonzero root or would vanish identically, contradicting existence and strictness of the real stationary point. The root for u* follows by cyclically permuting (X,Y,Z). The selected angle interval, not the rational formula alone, fixes the geometric branch. The proof above concerns positive local cells and their stationary composition. Flat source faces, boundary maxima and full closed-link incidence must still be handled before turning these local results into a general hyperbolic-volume theorem. Audit: [explicit cells, symbolic classes and actual stationary cubes](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity_results.json). It checks 163 prisms with exact rational circle coordinates and exact reflection maps, the symbolic five-term phase conversion and critical polynomial, and 20 actual stationary ideal cubes at high precision. The cube checks construct the face-gluing Mobius map, verify all six supporting face planes and convexity, check the common reflection, and test coplanarity of the four endpoints of the alternative cut. The uniform proof is the geometric and algebraic argument above; the finite checks do not infer arbitrary link geometry. The explicit converse normalization in section 2 identifies the alternative pieces with this source prism family; no general polyhedron rigidity theorem is assumed there.

title: A rank-three actual source: two endpoint envelopes give a sharp norm
text: # A rank-three actual source: two endpoint envelopes give a sharp norm 29 October 2026. The next repeated Newton twist/turn word has a genuine cubic spectral cover and an interior forward dominant-modulus switch. Nevertheless its ENTIRE positive original-source norm has a sharp limit. The proof keeps its exact source currents, uses a gapped backward branch only for the lower bound, and overlaps two full spectral-radius envelopes for the upper bound. The required profile comparisons have finite outward-rounded interval/Rouche certificates. No hyperbolic volume or link identity is inferred from the resulting constant. ## 1. The actual source and both of its boundary vectors Use T=T_1,P=P_rev and the unchanged original Newton metric. By the [universal endpoint identity](actual_newton_run_endpoint_vectors.md), (T^2P)^4 1 has, up to a unit scalar, coefficients v_i=kappa^(-2)(-q)^(i-d)K_i, K_i=sum_(j=0)^i nu_j [i choose j]_Q conjugate(P_(d-j)). (1) Here P_i is the original Green sequence, not the turn matrix. Its rank-three forced Ward, with G_i=K_i/F_i and M_i=F_i^3G_i, is proved in [the endpoint theorem, section5](actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.md). Write its coefficients as B_i,C_i,D_i there. The exact monic equation is M_i+B_i M_(i-1)+C_i(1-Q^(i-1))^3 M_(i-2) -Q^3(1-Q^(i-1))^3(1-Q^(i-2))^4 M_(i-3) =Q^2 delta_(i,1). (2) Negative-index terms are absent. Its literal data are M_0=conjugate(P_d), M_1=(1-3Q+Q^2)conjugate(P_d)+Q^2; D_2=0 fixes the next datum. In particular the source forcing has not been deleted. There is a regular exact backward equation. Put g_k=conjugate(F_k)^4 M_(d-k), Z_k=Q^(-k). For every3<=k<=d, g_k=a_k g_(k-1)+b_k g_(k-2)+c_k g_(k-3), (3) a_k=1+Q^(-1)+Q^(-2)-(4+Q^(-1))Z_k, b_k=[-Q^(-3)-Q^(-2)-Q^(-1) +(3+4Q^(-1))Z_k-3Q Z_k^2](1-Q Z_k), c_k=Q^(-3)(1-Q Z_k)(1-Q^2 Z_k)^4. All original currents are encoded in its INITIAL VECTOR. Let S_0=sum_(j=0)^d conjugate(P_j). Exactly, for N>=3, g_0=N^2 S_0, g_1=N^2 Q^(-1)[(Q-3)S_0+2N], g_2=N^2 Q^(-4)[(Q^4-3Q^3-3Q^2+6Q+3)S_0 +2(Q^3+Q^2-3Q-1)N]. (4) For a direct proof of(4), root reflection gives K_(d-h)=nu_h sum_(j=h)^d [j choose h]_Q conjugate(P_j). Writing S_m=sum_j Q^(mj)conjugate(P_j), the original finite Green equation yields (1-Q^m)S_m+2Q^(m-1)S_(m-1)-Q^(m-2)S_(m-2) =N delta_(m,1 modN). The actual inverse-crossing last row also gives S_(-1)=NQ: equivalently sum_j Q^jP_j=NQ^(-1). These evaluate S_1,S_2 from S_0,N and give(4). Reversing(2) and multiplying by the displayed fourth factorial proves(3). The independently evaluated original endpoints give |M_0|~N^(3/2), S_0=N^(3/2)exp[-i pi(3-N)/4]+O(N). Consequently (g_2,g_1,g_0)/g_0=(4,-2,1)+O(N^(-1/2)). This is the nonzero dominant eigenvector at the backward endpoint. The N terms in(4) are retained source currents, not arbitrary choices. ## 2. Spectral envelopes, and a source-selected backward lower bound Put Y=e^(2iu),Z=e^(-2iu). The forward and backward principal cubics are f_u(lambda)=lambda^3+(-3+7Y-3Y^2)lambda^2 +(3-5Y)(1-Y)^3lambda-(1-Y)^7, b_u(lambda)=lambda^3+(5Z-3)lambda^2 +(3-7Z+3Z^2)(1-Z)lambda-(1-Z)^5. (5) Let rho_f,rho_b be their largest root moduli. They are continuous and bounded below by1/3,2/3 respectively, by their traces. Set I_e(u)=pi^(-1)integral_0^u log rho_e(t)dt, e=f,b. Uniformly for all indices in any indicated compact u interval, the actual matrix product has the spectral-radius upper bound log|M_i|<=N I_f(pi i/N)+o(N), log|g_k|<=N I_b(pi k/N)+o(N). (6) This remains valid at modulus switches and the initial double fast zero. Here is an elementary proof avoiding an ill-conditioned full eigenframe. A bounded3x3 matrix of spectral radius at most1 has ||A^l||<=C(l+1)^2, uniformly in repeated roots: Newton interpolation of z^l bounds its order0,1,2 confluent differences by the corresponding complete homogeneous polynomials, of size at most (l+1)^2. The matrix factors in that interpolation are uniformly bounded. Freeze the exact smooth companion over blocks of length L=floor(N^(1/8)). Its step error is O(L/N). Expanding the product in those errors bounds one block by rho^L C L^2 exp(C L^4/N). Multiplying the blocks costs O(N log L/L+L^3)=o(N) in its logarithm. Uniform continuity of log rho gives the Riemann integral, uniformly also for partial final blocks. Polynomial initial data add only O(log N). This proves(6). The upper-bound mechanism is valid for ANY FIXED companion rank r, not only this cubic. A uniformly bounded rank-r matrix with spectral radius at most one has powers bounded by C(l+1)^(r-1), by the same order-(r-1) confluent divided-difference formula. Freezing L steps therefore costs at most rho^L C L^(r-1) exp(C L^(r+1)/N). Over O(N/L) blocks the extra logarithm is O(N log L/L+L^r). Taking L=floor(N^(1/(2r))) makes this o(N). This requires a fixed-rank uniformly smooth actual recurrence, a positive lower spectral-radius bound, and subexponential initial data; it permits eigenvalue collisions and modulus switches. It is a FULL spectral-radius upper envelope, not a lower bound or a license to replace the radius by an arbitrarily selected single branch. For every strict backward prefix0<=u<=u_0<pi/2 there is also a lower: log|g_k|=N I_b(pi k/N)+O_(u0)(log N). (7) The [independent exact dominant-root certificate](actual_backward_cubic_dominant_source_certificate.md) proves a unique simple dominant branch of b_u beginning at-2 on the ENTIRE strict half-circle. Its two fast roots may coalesce at0. Its regular dominant projection and a uniformly stable complement power-Gram give source transport without diagonalizing those fast roots. Equation(4) supplies the required actual nonzero projection with relative O(N^(-1/2)) error. The exact backward equation is homogeneous for k>=3, so no interior forcing is omitted in applying that certificate. Summed dominant logarithms prove(7). This argument does not transport a branch through the forward modulus switch. ## 3. One algebraic profile maximum and two finite comparisons Let Lambda be Lobachevsky and define J_e(u)=I_e(u)+2Lambda(u)/pi, e=f,b. Since M_i=F_i^2K_i and s_i s_(d-i)=N, (6) gives the two original coefficient envelopes J_f(pi i/N) and J_b(pi(d-i)/N). The lower(7) gives J_b at every fixed strict backward prefix. The backward profile has exactly one first-half maximum u_*. Put p_6(z)=z^6-9z^5+29z^4-38z^3+10z^2+2z+1. Its unique root z_* in[1,4] lies in(19/5,77/20), and u_*=arcsin(sqrt(z_*)/2), so 2pi/5<u_*<pi/2. Indeed J_b'(u)=pi^(-1)log[rho_b(u)/(2sin u)^2]. Imposing |lambda|=z=4sin^2u in b_u and its conjugate and eliminating lambda,Z gives z^24 p_6(z)^2=0. Exact Sturm counts give just two positive roots of p_6 in[0,4]: one in(2/3,7/10) and z_* above. The smaller cannot give rho_b=z because the product of the three root moduli gives rho_b>=z^(5/6)>z when0<z<1. At u=pi/2 all roots of lambda^3-8lambda^2+26lambda-32 have modulus<4: its unique real root lies in(2,3), and the conjugate pair has modulus sqrt(32/r)<4. Continuity now proves the claimed maximum. These eliminations use full polynomials, not a sampled eigenvalue branch. The forward profile is increasing: its root trace has modulus1+3z, so rho_f>=z+1/3>z. Two further finite inequalities suffice for a global overlap: integral_0^(2pi/5)log(rho_f/rho_b)du<0, integral_(2pi/5)^(pi/2)log[rho_b/(2sin u)^2]du<0. (8) The audit supplies rigorous interval bounds on WHOLE parameter cells. For each cubic it chooses rational complex root centers and verifies three disjoint disks by |p'(c)|_lower r > |p(c)|_upper+|p''(c)|_upper r^2/2+r^3. Rouche therefore encloses all roots for EVERY parameter in that cell. Their moduli bound rho and its logarithm. The small initial interval uses a monic Cauchy bound and rho_b>=2/3. At4096 outward-rounded cells the two certified upper bounds in(8) are respectively less than -.0327 and-.0114. This is a finite proof of the comparisons, not extrapolation from samples. The first inequality makes J_f(2pi/5)<J_b(2pi/5). The second makes J_b(pi/2)<J_b(2pi/5). Root-conjugation symmetry gives J_b(pi-u)=2J_b(pi/2)-J_b(u), so J_b(3pi/5)<J_b(pi/2). The only profile criticals before3pi/5 are u_* and its reflected minimum. Therefore the maximum of J_b on[0,3pi/5] is J_b(u_*). Use the forward envelope for i/N<=2/5 and the backward envelope for i/N>=2/5. They cover EVERY physical index and neither exceeds this backward maximum. ## 4. Whole original-source conclusion and scope The polynomial number of positive norm terms gives the upper rate; a rounded backward index near u_* and(7) give the matching lower. For the literal original halfword A=(T_2P_rev)^4, lim_N N^(-1)log||A1||_Newt^2=2J_b(u_*). (9) Its original adjoint-word marked closure equals this positive norm exactly. All Cartan lines and all fixed-root Casimir normals remain. No value-only trace or arbitrary diagonal Newton coupon was substituted. The assertion concerns fixed word depth before N tends to infinity. This extends the source-aware folded Ward method to a genuine cubic with an interior modulus switch. Its inputs are explicit resets, the full opposite source vector, finite algebraic dominant-mode tests, and finite certified envelope comparisons. It is not a general theorem that an arbitrary scalar A-polynomial selects its largest root, and it is not a new broad bridge-family or hyperbolic-volume claim. Audit: [original source, exact folded current, algebraic criticals and interval spectral profiles](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_rank_three_folded_packet.py). The proposed roots are used only after the stated Rouché validation. Finite source/current families, exact resultants and Sturm counts, and outward-rounded whole-cell disks check the formulas. No topological or volume identification follows.

title: Finite Gaussian boundary data for arbitrary repeated twist/turn runs
text: # Finite Gaussian boundary data for arbitrary repeated twist/turn runs 29 October 2026. For every fixed integer m, the actual source of (T_2 P_rev)^m has explicit first AND last fixed-rank endpoint vectors. They reduce to original signed-twist sources with fixed Newton insertions. Each such source has a finite algebraic Gaussian leading coefficient, so testing a candidate recurrence's boundary projection does not require an unknown knot invariant or an unspecified solution. No interior branch-survival theorem for all m is asserted. ## 1. Universal exact source endpoint identities Use the full original Newton algebra/metric, Bhat_h=B_h/s_h^2, T=T_1,P=P_rev,R=kappa r. The actual Cartan identities give kappa^2(-q)^d=1, theta=kappa^3(-q)^d=kappa. Thus the [coherent modular reduction](actual_newton_coherent_turn_reduction.md) simplifies, for every integer m, to v_m:=(T^2P)^m1=kappa^m T P T^(1-m)1. (1) For a polynomial f, its Newton endpoint coefficient satisfies alpha_(d-j)(f)=phi(f Bhat_j). Lower triangularity of T therefore gives (v_m)_h=kappa^m sum_(j=0)^h T_(h,j) phi(R^(1-m) Bhat_j). (2) There is an equally explicit right endpoint formula. Define E_h=sum_(r=0)^h nu_h^(-1)nu_(h-r)(-q)^(-(h-r)) [h choose r]_Q Bhat_r. Then, on the FULL algebra and with every confluent normal retained, mathscrR(R Bhat_h)=R^(-1)E_h, (v_m)_(d-h)=kappa^m phi(R^(-m)E_h). (3) Proof. TPT=kappa PT^(-1)P implies PT=kappa T^(-1)PT^(-1)P. Apply this to e_h. The middle vector PT^(-1)e_(d-h) is supported on indices0,...,h. The actual reflected inverse kernel gives kappa (T^(-1))_(d-r,d-h) =nu_h^(-1)nu_(h-r)(-q)^(-(h-r))[h choose r]_Q. This proves (3)'s first equality. The Frobenius identity phi(mathscrR(f)g)=phi(f mathscrR(g)) then proves its second. It is a full operator/source calculation, not a claim about eigenlines. In particular (v_m)_0=kappa^(m+1)phi(R^(1-m)), (v_m)_d=kappa^m phi(R^(-m)). (4) For fixed endpoint rank h, all sums in(2)--(3) have at most h+1 terms, with explicit coefficients. There is no inverse Clebsch minor. ## 2. Fixed endpoint insertions still have a finite Gaussian certificate Keep a(s)=(1-2s)sin(2pi s), epsilon=k mod2, and s_l=(2l-epsilon)/(2k), as in [the actual twist endpoint theorem](actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.md). For every FIXED k>0 and FIXED h>=0, set G_(k,h)(N)=sum_(0<s_l<1)(-1)^l a(s_l)sin(pi s_l)^(2h) exp[-i pi N(l-epsilon/2)^2/k]. (5) This is algebraic and periodic in N modulo8k. With C_(N,k) exactly the phase in that theorem, the original source obeys phi(r^k Bhat_h) = C_(N,k) N^(3/2+2h)/(pi^(2h)(h!)^2) G_(k,h)(N) +O_(k,h)(N^(1+2h)). (6) For odd k the error is O_(k,h)(N^(1/2+2h)). Negative k follows by coefficient conjugation. The statements concern fixed h<N as N tends to infinity; h may not be sent to a fraction of N here. An own proof retains the full source derivative. Its exact folded form is phi(r^k Bhat_h)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 sum_j nu_j^k { Bhat_h(c_j)[c_j-(k/2)(d-2j)A_j]+A_j^2 Bhat_h'(c_j)}. (7) Uniformly with all fixed-order s derivatives, Bhat_h(2cos(2pi s)) =N^(2h)sin(pi s)^(2h)/(pi^(2h)(h!)^2)+O_h(N^(2h-2)). This follows directly from its h factors and s_h^2=(2pi/N)^(2h)(h!)^2[1+O_h(N^(-2))]. Insert this into(7) and apply the proved half-grid Gaussian argument to the leading a(s) term. The remaining source terms have no extra N factor and are O(N^(1/2+2h)), except the possible even-k endpoint contributions already bounded by O(N^(1+2h)). This proves (6), including normals. For each specified k,h, nonvanishing of(5) is a FINITE cyclotomic test; a zero leading coefficient is not silently discarded. For k3, G_(3,h)=4^(-h)G_(3,0), and for k4, G_(4,h)=2^(-h)G_(4,0). Both are nonzero on every N residue class. For k5 the two paired weights are a_1 sin(pi/10)^(2h), a_2 sin(3pi/10)^(2h). At h0 the first is larger; at every integer h>=1 the second is larger: a_2/a_1=cos(pi/5)>1/2 and sin(3pi/10)/sin(pi/10)=(3+sqrt5)/2>2. Their strict difference gives a uniform triangle lower bound exactly as in the scalar theorem. Thus fixed endpoint insertions for powers3,4,5 all have nonzero leading terms, with no parity restriction. The exceptional powers have exact fixed-root boundary data instead: phi(Bhat_h)=delta_(h,d), phi(r Bhat_h)=(-q)^(d-h), phi(r^2 Bhat_h)=(-q)^(d-h)F_(d-h). (8) Negative powers are their conjugates. These follow from the literal r and r^2 source columns and the full Frobenius pairing. Thus the vanishing leading Gaussians at k0,1,2 leave no unknown endpoint data. ## 3. Every fixed twist power has nonzero resolved Gaussian boundary modes There is a stronger UNIVERSAL vector statement even when the scalar Gaussian sum cancels. Fix any k>=3, put epsilon=k mod2 and rho=floor((k-1)/2), and define s_j=(2j-epsilon)/(2k), t_j=sin(pi s_j)^2, 1<=j<=rho, 0<t_1<...<t_rho<1, w_j(N)=2(-1)^j(1-2s_j)sin(2pi s_j) exp[-i pi N(j-epsilon/2)^2/k]. (9) Then, for EVERY integer N, G_(k,h)(N)=sum_(j=1)^rho t_j^h w_j(N). (10) To prove it, pair the stationary index j with k+epsilon-j. Their positions are s and1-s, their a values and sin(pi s)^(2h) agree, and their (-1) signs agree. Their quadratic phase difference is pi N(k+epsilon-2j), an even integer multiple of pi. The remaining middle position s=1/2 has a=0. Thus every pair adds, proving(10). Moreover |w_j(N)|=2(1-2s_j)sin(2pi s_j)>0 (11) independently of N or any coprimality condition. Let V_(h,j)=t_j^h, 0<=h<rho. This fixed Vandermonde is invertible: its determinant is product_(i<j)(t_j-t_i)!=0. Form from the ACTUAL source entries the normalized vector b_(h,N)=pi^(2h)(h!)^2 phi(r^k Bhat_h)/(C_(N,k)N^(3/2+2h)). Equation(6) is uniform over this fixed finite vector. Consequently V^(-1)b_N=(w_j(N))_j+O_k(N^(-1/2)), (12) with O_k(1/N) error for odd k. Every individual resolved coefficient therefore has a uniform positive lower bound for all sufficiently large N. Negative powers give its conjugate statement. One may use an EXACT algebraic normalization at every root instead: btilde_(h,N)=s_h^2 phi(r^k Bhat_h) /(4^h C_(N,k)N^(3/2)). (12a) Since s_h^2/4^h=pi^(2h)(h!)^2 N^(-2h)[1+O_h(N^(-2))], the same conclusion(12) holds with btilde. All its finite-level normalizing factors, and the Vandermonde entries, are algebraic. The normalizations and V inverse are explicit, depend on k, and have only polynomial cost in N. They do not use an unknown knot invariant. Thus scalar residue-class cancellations do NOT leave unknown source incidence if one retains the full fixed-rank endpoint vector. These are resolved GAUSSIAN endpoint modes. Identifying them with a chosen interior Ward branch requires the exact boundary-to-Ward projection and a propagation estimate on the domain in question. Neither follows from the names or from nonzero individual entries; a finite endpoint projection alone does not control subsequent mode conversion. ## 4. What this gives a finite-depth source criterion For any fixed m and any proposed finite-rank Ward recurrence for v_m, (2)--(7) specify its endpoint vectors by finitely many exact Gaussians and known N powers/phases. A dominant-eigenprojection test can therefore be made against actual source data. It must retain a possible linear combination/cancellation between those finite coefficients; nonzero individual entries do not imply a nonzero projection. The repeated run is modularly PARABOLIC and conjugate to one twist. Its unbounded count of displayed turns is not a new general bridge family. The reusable result here is the actual finite boundary-data formula; it is not counted as completion of the broad source problem. The next m4 vector and its exact rank-three inhomogeneous Ward are already displayed in the endpoint theorem. Its forward source has an interior modulus switch; distinct roots alone cannot select one branch. The data here remove an unknown boundary value from that problem, rather than asserting that the remaining conversion or global source gap has been solved. All statements are ROOT-VALUE identities in the actual original source. Bhat insertions encode endpoint coordinates and full Casimir Hermite normals. They are not Taylor derivatives in q of an arbitrary generic turn family. No recorded Newton clock is promoted to a peripheral deformation or an additional actual knot coupon without its own proof. Audit: [full original endpoint matrices and finite Gaussian data](../experiments/audit_actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.py). Its modal-residue checks use exact primitive cyclotomic-root images in finite fields, with the prime and image recorded in the results. They supplement the all-k pairing/Vandermonde proof above; a successful specialization is not itself a proof of an identity over the complex cyclotomic field. The finite audit checks original source families, coefficient identities, Gaussian profiles and cyclotomic modal residue vectors. These checks supplement the universal pairing proof; they do not extrapolate it from the tested twist powers.

title: A positive Newton metric for genuine original tangle turns
text:
# A positive Newton metric for genuine original tangle turns 29 October 2026. The genuine quarter-turn of ANY original two-head Hopf box is a unitary reversal in an explicit full-dimensional Newton packet. Both original marked closures have dual norm ONE. Signed crossings have an explicit adjoint in this same metric, so a specified class of reflected rational/arborescent circuits is an exact positive norm of its coherent half-network. This is not positivity for an arbitrary fully augmented diagram, and no general sharp energy or new volume-equality class is inferred. ## 1. Actual operators and the normalized Newton packet Keep the full original algebra and source of [the pair commutant theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) and [the circle sewing theorem](general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md): \[ \mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N,\quad P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad d=N-1,\quad Q=q^2 . \] All \(c_j\) are real, with \(c_{d-j}=c_j\). Let \[ F_r=(Q;Q)_r,\quad s_r=|F_r|,\quad B_r(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/s_r^2,\quad 0\leq r\leq d . 	ag{1} \] Here \(s_0=1,\ s_d=N,\ s_rs_{d-r}=N\). The basis (1) is a CASIMIR Newton basis, distinct from earlier normalized homogeneous interval/length blocks. In particular its zero slot is exactly \(1\). The original marked functional and genuine UNSCALED turn are \[ \phi(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f mod P_N),\qquad (\mathscr R f)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{a-e}f(\Omega)_{(d-a,c);(b,d-e)}. 	ag{2} \] The turn preserves the full Hopf algebra, satisfies \(\mathscr R^2=I\), and includes both actual cup/cap factors; it is not the scaled \(Z\) and is not multiplicative. ## 2. Full physical proof of the Newton turn identity For the physical degree block \(W_t\), \(0\leq t\leq d\), the Casimir is an irreducible tridiagonal matrix with characteristic AND minimal polynomial \[ \prod_{j=0}^t(z-c_j). 	ag{3} \] The characteristic formula follows by the explicit generic highest-weight/descendant triangular decomposition before regular specialization, as in the pair commutant proof. The root offdiagonal entries are nonzero; hence a boundary vector is cyclic, and (3) is the minimal polynomial even when some \(c_j\) coincide. Thus \(B_r\) annihilates \(W_t\) whenever \(t<r\), INCLUDING its Jordan normals. Every degree block of \(B_r(\Omega)\) has first-color bandwidth at most \(r\). In (2) the difference of its first colors is \((d-a)-b=d-(a+b)\). Therefore \(\mathscr R B_r\) annihilates every physical degree \(t<d-r\). Applying (3) at \(t=d-r-1\) shows that its representing polynomial is divisible by \(B_{d-r}\); when \(r=d\) this assertion is vacuous. For the reverse degree bound, use the middle block \(A=\Omega|_{W_d}\). Its turned first column is \[ (\mathscr R B_r(A))_{a0} =x^{a-d}(B_r(\Omega))_{(d-a,0);(d-a,0)} . \] This vanishes for \(a>d-r\), by (3). A polynomial of degree \(k<N\) in the irreducible tridiagonal \(A\), applied to \(e_0\), has nonzero component \(k\) from its unique outermost path. Hence \(\deg(\mathscr R B_r)\leq d-r\). It follows that \(\mathscr R B_r=C_rB_{d-r}\). The scalar comes from ONE literal physical entry: \[ (\mathscr R B_r)_{(0,d-r);(d-r,0)} =(B_r)_{(d,d-r);(d-r,d)}=s_r^2 . \] For clarity, in the latter high-degree block the unique \(r\)-step path increasing the first color has entries \[ Q^{j-r}(1-Q^{r-j})(1-Q^{j+1}),\quad0\leq j<r . \] Multiplying and including the leading coefficient \((-1)^r\) gives \((-1)^rQ^{-r(r+1)/2}F_r^2=s_r^2\). Similarly the unique decreasing path for \(B_{d-r}\) in the LOW block of degree \(d-r\) gives \(s_{d-r}^2\). All turn monomials in this chosen entry equal one. Consequently \[  oxed{\quad \mathscr R B_r= rac{s_r^2}{s_{d-r}^2}B_{d-r}, \qquad \mathscr R\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{d-r}. \quad} 	ag{4} \] This proof works for all \(N\geq2\), all \(r\), and all repeated Casimir nodes. It uses physical matrix support and full minimal polynomials, not an equality only on distinct eigenvalues. ## 3. Positive Gram, all ports open, and the exact original source The full Frobenius pairing in this basis is especially simple: \[ \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}. 	ag{5} \] For \(i+j<d\) use degree. For \(i+j=d\) use its leading coefficient and \(s_is_j=N\). If \(i+j\geq N\), the product is divisible by \(P_N\): indeed \(B_N/B_j=B_{N-j}\), since \(c_{d-k}=c_k\), and \(B_i\) is divisible by \(B_{N-j}\). This is polynomial divisibility with FULL multiplicities, so (5) retains all normals. Write \(f=\sum_r\alpha_r\widehat B_r\) and let \(f^\sharp(z)=\overline{f( ar z)}\). All basis polynomials in (1) have real coefficients. Equations (4)--(5) prove the positive definite all-input identity \[  oxed{\quad \langle f,gangle_{\mathrm{Newt}} :=\phi(f^\sharp\mathscr Rg) =\sum_{r=0}^d\overline{\alpha_r} eta_r,\qquad \|\mathscr R f\|_{\mathrm{Newt}}=\|f\|_{\mathrm{Newt}}. \quad} 	ag{6} \] The metric is prescribed independently of any knot or exterior. It is not the canonical unweighted Hermite-channel Gram whose energy was excessive in a previous figure-eight test, nor the terminal \(T^*T\) metric. Its change of frame can have exponential condition number. The exact packet transform is \[ \alpha_r=(-1)^rs_r^2 f[c_0,\ldots,c_r], 	ag{7} \] with confluent divided differences at repeated nodes. Thus it is explicit and invertible on the COMPLETE algebra and retains every first derivative, including even/composite levels. Equivalently let \(B\) be the ACTUAL complete source-Hom bidiagonal Casimir \[ Be_j=c_je_j+b_je_{j-1},\qquad b_j=Q^j+Q^{-j}-2=-|1-Q^j|^2 . \] Its cyclic column obeys \(f(B)e_d=(\alpha_d,\ldots,\alpha_0)^T\). This follows either from its confluent divided-difference formula or from \(\widehat B_r(B)e_d=e_{d-r}\). Consequently \[ \phi(f\,\mathscr Rg)=(f(B)e_d)^T(g(B)e_d),\qquad f(B)e_d\mapsto P_{\mathrm{rev}}f(B)e_d 	ext{ under }\mathscr R . 	ag{8} \] The original closures, with unrestricted marked cap and actual pivot, are \[ m f(\Omega)p=f(c_0)=\alpha_0,\qquad \phi(f)=\alpha_d . 	ag{9} \] Their proof and original \(N\) factors are in the circle sewing note, section 3. Both are unit coordinate rows in (6), so have dual norm EXACTLY one. No arbitrary local marked cap was replaced by an ordinary cap. Any physical exterior can still be attached before using (4); it is a full operator identity. ## 4. Explicit twist matrices, their physical star, and coherent sewing In Newton coordinates multiplication by \(z\) is the real LOWER bidiagonal matrix \[ Z_{rr}=c_r,\qquad Z_{r+1,r}=-|1-Q^{r+1}|^2,\qquad Z^T=P_{\mathrm{rev}} ZP_{\mathrm{rev}}. 	ag{10} \] Every literal signed crossing power acts by \[ T_p=R(Z)^p,\qquad R=\kappa r_N,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. 	ag{11} \] Its nodal values and first derivatives are the original complete ones, with no Jordan term omitted. In particular its all-entry form is \[ (T_p)_{ij} =\left(\prod_{k=j+1}^i b_kight) R^p[c_j,\ldots,c_i]\quad(i\geq j); \qquad (T_p)_{ij}=0\quad(i<j). 	ag{12} \] One can also use the entirely finite Newton alphabet \[ R=\kappa\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^r\widehat B_r,\qquad R^{-1}=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^{-r}\widehat B_r . 	ag{13} \] These follow from the literal cup-slide \(R_{23}^{-1}p=N\kappa^{-1}e_d\), equivalently \(R_{23}e_d=\kappa p/N\), and (8); that original-source identity is proved in [the normalization packet](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md). Equations (11)--(13) retain the common Cartan scalar. There is a simpler ALL-ENTRY one-crossing kernel. Define the positive sine Gaussian \( eta_{ij}=s_i/(s_js_{i-j})\), \(0\leq j\leq i\leq d\), and \(
u_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}\). Then \[  oxed{\quad (T_1)_{ij}=\kappa
u_j(-q)^{i-j}{i rack j}_Q =\kappa(-1)^iq^{\,i(j+1)} eta_{ij},\qquad (T_{-1})_{ij}=\overline{(T_1)_{ij}}\quad(i\geq j), \quad} 	ag{13a} \] with zero entries above the diagonal. This includes ALL confluent channels; it is not an eigenline expansion. Here is an independent finite proof. Call the first displayed triangular matrix \(C\). Its first column is \(\kappa(-q)^i\), exactly \(R(Z)e_0\) by (13). For \(i\geq j\), Gaussian factorial cancellation gives \[ b_i rac{C_{i-1,j}}{C_{ij}} =-q^{-1}Q^{-i}(1-Q^i)(1-Q^{i-j}),\qquad b_{j+1} rac{C_{i,j+1}}{C_{ij}} =q^{-1}(1-Q^{j+1})(1-Q^{i-j}). \] Their difference is \(-(c_i-c_j)\), so \(CZ=ZC\). The boundary terms vanish by their displayed factors. Since \(e_0\) is cyclic for the irreducible lower-bidiagonal \(Z\), two commuting matrices that agree on \(e_0\) agree on the whole space. Thus \(C=R(Z)\), with no separation of repeated nodes. Finally \({i rack j}_Q=q^{j(i-j)} eta_{ij}\) proves the second expression in (13a), and \(R^\sharp=R^{-1}\) proves the inverse. Thus an arbitrary genuine rational circuit has an explicit alphabet: unitary reversal, the lower sine-binomial kernel (13a), and its coefficient conjugate. Its oscillation is the original half-clock \(q^{ij}\); replacing it by \(Q^{ij}\) would change the source. Its absolute entry also has the exact angle identity \[  eta_{ij}=N\,w_d(j,i-j,d-i),\qquad w_d(a,b,c)= rac1{s_as_bs_c},\quad a+b+c=d. 	ag{13b} \] This follows from \(s_is_{d-i}=N\). It supplies one actual angle-simplex amplitude with its phase and incidence labels. It is the amplitude \(Nw_d\), NOT its square root. Any proposed square-root-energy comparison must still prove its metric and source compensation rather than silently replacing (13a). Two adjacent crossings have a further COHERENT all-input elimination: with \(m=i-j\), \[  oxed{\quad (T_2)_{ij}=\kappa^2
u_j^2(-q)^m {i rack j}_Q (Q^{j+1};Q)_m =\kappa^2
u_j^2(-q)^m  rac{F_i^2}{F_j^2F_m}, \quad i\geq j .\quad} 	ag{13c} \] The negative two-crossing kernel is its coefficient conjugate. To prove it, expand the actual product \(T_1T_1\), use \({i rack k}_Q{k rack j}_Q ={i rack j}_Q{m rack k-j}_Q\), and set \(r=k-j\). The remaining sum is exactly \[ \sum_{r=0}^m {m rack r}_Q (-1)^rQ^{r(r-1)/2}(Q^{j+1})^r=(Q^{j+1};Q)_m . \] This finite identity follows by inserting the last Pochhammer factor and the Pascal recursion. Every index is below \(N\). Its cancellations are retained BEFORE taking an absolute value. Thus the all-entry magnitude is \(s_i^2/(s_j^2s_{i-j})\), not a sum of positive one-crossing path magnitudes. Equivalently, for \(D_F=\operatorname{diag}F_i\) and \(D_
u=\operatorname{diag}
u_i\), \[ T_2=\kappa D_F T_1D_F^{-1}D_
u . 	ag{13d} \] This is a typed packet identity preserving arbitrary adjoining input and output arrays. Its factorial gauge is on the NEWTON register; it is not an unrecorded physical-head gauge. Although its endpoint factors at \(0,d\) are only \(1,N\), its interfaces with a turn must remain explicit: \(P_{\mathrm{rev}}D_FP_{\mathrm{rev}}=ND_
u D_F^{-1}\). Consequently (13d) alone is not a polynomial-cost global replacement of every twist/turn network. At a real node the original ratio \(R'(c)/R(c)\) is purely imaginary, and its value has modulus one. Hence full Hermite uniqueness gives \(R^\sharp=R^{-1}\), not only equality of distinct nodal values. For ANY multiplication coupon \(M_f\), its exact adjoint in (6) is \[ M_f^\dagger=\mathscr R M_{f^\sharp}\mathscr R . \] Indeed the Frobenius pairing is symmetric and (4)--(5) imply its turn is selfadjoint and orthogonal. In particular \[  oxed{\qquad \mathscr R^\dagger=\mathscr R,\qquad T_p^\dagger=\mathscr R T_{-p}\mathscr R . \qquad} 	ag{14} \] The turn is unitary; the crossing is GENERALLY NOT. Its real bidiagonal Casimir is nonnormal and has repeated-node derivative channels. Thus unit nodal phases do not bound a whole twist/word norm polynomially. Formula (14) is the required typed interface, not an assertion that every plane-reflected diagram supplies it. For an arbitrary genuine two-port word \(W\), starting with \(1\), the original numerator closure now has the exact source Cauchy bound \[ |m\,W(1)(\Omega)p|^2\leq\|W(1)\|_{\mathrm{Newt}}^2 . 	ag{15} \] All internal turns in this energy are the fixed unitary reversal and all twist kernels are the known matrices (12). No terminal word or unknown invariant is used to define the metric. ## 5. An exact positive class with genuine extra turns Let \(A\) be ANY finite typed word in genuine turns and signed crossing multiplications. Form its ADJOINT WORD by reversing the order and using the exact replacements (14). It is again a literal rational tangle circuit with the original turns and signed crossings. The original numerator closure of its doubled circuit satisfies \[  oxed{\qquad m\,[A^\dagger A(1)](\Omega)p =\langle1,A^\dagger A1angle_{\mathrm{Newt}} =\|A1\|_{\mathrm{Newt}}^2>0 . \qquad} 	ag{16} \] All generators of \(A\) are invertible, so the strict inequality holds at EVERY level. A recorded outer framing or component enhancement unit may multiply this raw positive scalar; its modulus is unchanged. This class includes words with arbitrary numbers of genuine internal turns, for instance \(A=T_p\mathscr R T_q\). Its doubled word is \(\mathscr R T_{-q}\mathscr R T_{-p}\mathscr R T_p\mathscr R T_q\), with no unjustified crossing/turn commutations. Thus the positivity is for an actual specified entire source circuit, not one expanded crossing state or an arbitrary positive model. As a calibration, the normalization packet's exact \(R_{23}p\) formula gives \[ R^2=\kappa^2\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^rF_r\widehat B_r . \] Taking \(A=T_2\) in (16) therefore gives \(\sum_rs_r^2\), the already proved whole-source figure-eight scalar. The general statement (16) is not inferred from that one example. For longer \(A\), the energy in (16) retains coherent cancellations INSIDE \(A1\); the norm only reflects the second half afterwards. Bounding it by independent absolute-entry capacities would lose the very coupling this construction preserves. A sharp Rivin-constrained bound or a nonzero geometric saddle for these arbitrary half-networks is still needed for a new volume-equality family. This note proves the all-exterior positive kernel and a genuine full-source noncancellation operation, not that remaining geometric estimate. ## 6. A complete-circle reflected source with a proved exponent The known complete packet \(z_N=\mathscr R(R^{-1}L_N)\) now gives an ENTIRE positive original source with an explicit exponential rate: \[ E_N:=\phi(z_N^\sharp\mathscr Rz_N)=\|z_N\|_{\mathrm{Newt}}^2, \qquad  oxed{\ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log E_N= rac{v_8}{\pi}\ } . 	ag{17} \] In particular the original quantum scaling gives rate \(2v_8\). This uses the already proved actual finite coefficient/endpoint theorems, rather than a guessed positive envelope. Write \[ z_N=N^2\sum_{r=0}^{M} b_{N,r}B_r,\quad |b_{N,r}|= rac{s_{2r}}{s_r^6}|U_r|,\quad M=\lfloor d/2floor. \] The exact norm is \[ E_N=N^4\sum_{r=0}^{M} rac{s_{2r}^2}{s_r^8}|U_r|^2 . 	ag{18} \] The [all-index original-source estimate](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) gives \(|U_r|\leq CN^B\exp[N\mathcal E(\pi r/N)]\), with \[ \mathcal E(u)= rac2\pi\int_u^{\pi/4}\log\cot v\,dv \quad(0\leq u<\pi/4),\qquad \mathcal E(u)=0\ (u\geq\pi/4). \] Uniform sine-factorial bounds, INCLUDING both endpoints, give the remaining exponential profile \[ T(u)=\{8\Lambda(u)-2\Lambda(2u)\}/\pi,\qquad T'(u)=4\log\cot u/\pi . \] Hence \(T+2\mathcal E\) is exactly constant \(j_0=v_8/\pi\) below \(\pi/4\), and \(T\) decreases above \(\pi/4\). The polynomial number of summands and their uniform polynomial errors prove the upper bound in (17). For each FIXED \(u\in(\pi/4,\pi/2)\), the nonzero coherent high-index asymptotic in [the complete packet theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), section 2 equation (3), gives \(|U_{\lfloor Nu/\pifloor}|^2 	o\sin u>0\). Its one positive summand proves a lower rate \(T(u)\). Let \(u\downarrow\pi/4\) AFTER the quantum limit to obtain (17). Both parities and all composite levels are covered. The actual raw diagram is specified without an unverified link name: \[  oxed{\qquad E_N=\phi\!\left(\mathscr R(RL_N)\,R^{-1}L_Night). \qquad} 	ag{19} \] Here \(\mathscr R\) commutes with coefficient reflection by (4), and \(L_N^\sharp=L_N\); thus (19) follows from the literal signed boxes, not a replacement by a positive model. It has two ordinary complete crossing-circle components. Deleting those two components leaves the genuine diagram \(\phi(\mathscr R(R)R^{-1}) =\phi(R^{-2})\): the quarter-turn of the single crossing is the opposite single crossing, and the two-strand closure has two main components. Thus the complete reflected diagram has FOUR components. It must not be identified with the three-component Borromean rings merely from the numerical value \(2v_8\). The separate [literal octahedral certificate](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md) now identifies its complement by a reversible projection/disk cut, the actual labeled face table, and four complete torus links. This proves that (17) equals the actual volume of that specified link. The original single-cut normalization comparison changes only the recorded unit phase (or the optional one-cut modified factor \(1/N\)), so it does not alter (17). Audit: [literal turn, full Newton/Frobenius packet, signed star and reflected original sources](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.py). Its geometric identification is supplied by the separate octahedral certificate above; neither proof supplies a sharp energy bound for arbitrary words.

title: Exact Newton twist equations, original source, and the parabolic Fricke graph
text: # Exact Newton twist equations, original source, and the parabolic Fricke graph 29 October 2026. The actual Newton crossing has a denominator-free finite Weyl system. Its classical map is the genuine parabolic braid/Fricke map, with the original four-plat cup and cap retained by an explicit matrix intertwiner. Arbitrary rational words therefore have an actual complete- meridian character gluing description without an unknown 6j frame. The Newton clock is NOT the knot meridian or the Casimir eigenvalue. This does not construct a generic-meridian A-curve or prove a sharp asymptotic/survival theorem for all rational words. The exceptional cup boundary and its normal source cannot be replaced by a regular torus point. Those distinctions are made explicit below. ## 1. The exact kernel and its actual generic normalization Use the [full Newton packet](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md): q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The actual full crossing kernel is C_ij=kappa(-1)^i q^(i+j^2) [i choose j]_Q, 0<=j<=i<=d; C_ij=0 above the diagonal. (1) It is multiplication by the original checked R, including its common Cartan, all Jordan derivatives, and the true q^(ij) half-clock phase. The actual turn is the reversal P_rev and both original closures are coordinate rows. None of these facts is an independent-eigenline model. There is a useful analytic generic-q extension of(1), but its physical scalar must remain. For zeta near q, put Q=zeta^2 and s_r^2(zeta)=(-1)^r zeta^[-r(r+1)](Q;Q)_r^2, c_j(zeta)=zeta^(2j+1)+zeta^(-2j-1), kappa(zeta)=zeta^(d^2/2). The normalized Newton basis uses these s_r^2; multiplication by z is the lower bidiagonal Z with diagonal c_j and subdiagonal b_j=Q^j+Q^(-j)-2. The generic matrix (1) commutes with this Z by the same finite Gaussian identities, and its diagonal is kappa nu_j, nu_j=(-1)^j zeta^[j(j+1)]. The literal generic highest-weight-d physical braiding, however, has at the Casimir node c_a the highest-vector eigenvalue lambda_(d-a)=(-1)^(d-a) zeta^[d^2/2-(d-a)(N+a)] =kappa gamma_N(zeta) nu_a, gamma_N(zeta)=(-1)^d zeta^(-Nd). (2) Consequently its Newton matrix is gamma_N C, not just C. Generic distinctness and equality of all nodal values prove the matrix identity; regular specialization retains the full confluent polynomial. At the root gamma_N(q)=1, but its normal derivatives are NONZERO. All q-normal calculations must keep(2). This generic q deformation is not a deformation of the knot meridian. The inverse of the finite Gaussian kernel is also explicit: (C^-1)_ij=kappa^-1(-1)^i q^[j^2-2ij-i] [i choose j]_Q. (3) This follows from the finite q-Pascal inverse and equals coefficient conjugation of(1) at the original root. The physical generic inverse has the additional scalar gamma_N^-1. ## 2. Finite Weyl equations, including the actual normal wall Let X=Q^i,Y=Q^j on the kernel. Direct adjacent-factor cancellation gives (QX-Y) C_(i+1,j)=qY(1-QX)C_ij, (QY-1) C_(i,j+1)=q(X-Y)C_ij. (4) These equations are CROSS-MULTIPLIED; they include the triangular diagonal and its zero neighbors. One must not divide their vanishing coefficients to change the support. For the finite zero extension C_(N,j)=0, the first equation has the explicit generic last-row current (QX-Y) C_(i+1,j)-qY(1-QX)C_ij =-qY(1-Q^N) delta_(i,d) C_(d,j). (5) It vanishes at the root, but its first q-normal coefficient does not. Multiplying by gamma_N preserves(4)--(5), with that scalar retained. The backwards-j version is globally valid without another source: (Y-1)C_ij=q(X-Q^-1Y)C_(i,j-1), C_(i,-1)=0. (6) Together with triangular support and C_(i,0)=kappa(-q)^i, these are finite pointed equations determining the actual kernel. They do not identify an arbitrary cyclic-shift solution with the original one. For strict forward shifts S f_i=f_(i+1), (6) gives the exact matrix identity X C S=C Y S+q^-1 C(Y-I). (7) The first equation similarly gives a cleared operator relation with the wall(5). Inverting its factor S+q(1-QX) at the root is invalid: that factor has a zero last diagonal entry. The finite source is part of the operator identity, even when studying a regular classical chart. ## 3. The regular canonical graph and its preserved Casimir For i/N=x,j/N=y in 0<y<x<1 the leading exponent of(1) is Phi(x,y)=J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y)+pi i(xy+x+1/2), J'(x)=log(2sin pi x). The common Cartan produces the displayed pi i/2; the remaining known subleading phase is retained in the finite kernel. Put X=exp(2pi i x), Y=exp(2pi i y), U=exp(Phi_x), V=exp(-Phi_y). The negative sign in the INPUT momentum is essential for composing kernel critical equations. Equations(4) give precisely X=Y+(Y-1)/V, U=-Y(1+V), equivalently XV+U+1=0, Y(V+1)+U=0. (8) It preserves dlog U wedge dlog X. Indeed 2pi i Phi is a generating function with differential log U dlog X-log V dlog Y. The same graph comes from the exact cleared equations, not merely a guessed phase. The actual Newton multiplication-Casimir symbol is A(X,U)=X+X^-1+(X+X^-1-2)/U. (9) Substitution in(8) proves A(output)=A(input). The turn has the exact root clock relation P_rev X P_rev=Q^-1 X^-1 and interchanges strict forward and backward shifts. Its principal graph is (X,U)->(X^-1,U^-1). Thus the second trace symbol is B(X,U)=X+X^-1+(X+X^-1-2)U. With {log X,log U}=-1, define the ordered third trace C(X,U)=(8-AB+{A,B})/2 =2-(X-1)^2(U+1)^2/U. (10) Direct algebra gives the ACTUAL parabolic Fricke equation A^2+B^2+C^2+ABC-8(A+B+C)+28=0. (11) On these trace coordinates, the active point map(8) is (A,B,C)->(A,C,8-AC-B). (12) The inverse occurs on observables: Ad(R) is pullback by the inverse state map. Thus(12) agrees with the actual positive braid formula Ad(R):(A,B,C)->(A,8-AB-C,B), rather than reversing a physical crossing based on an isolated eigenphase. ## 4. Actual quantum trace matrices and original source matching This graph has an exact physical source realization. In the already audited three-head complete multiplicity basis let A_phys=Omega_12, B_phys e_j=c_j e_j+b_j e_(j-1). A_phys is the original symmetric tridiagonal matrix with (A_phys)_jj=4qQ^j-q(1+Q)Q^(2j), (A_phys)_(j-1,j)=(A_phys)_(j,j-1)=-(1-Q^j)^2. (13) The actual R_23 is C^T, by multiplication functional calculus in the upper-bidiagonal B_phys. Finite Gaussian cancellation gives the FULL matrix identity R_23^-1 A_phys R_23=B_phys^T. (14) For an entrywise proof substitute(1) transposed in A_phys C^T=C^T B_phys^T.
