On the interior the needed three ratios are U_(i-1,j)/U_ij=q^(-2i+1)(1-Q^i)/(1-Q^(j-i+1)), U_(i+1,j)/U_ij=q^(2i+1)(1-Q^(j-i))/(1-Q^(i+1)), U_(i,j+1)/U_ij=-q(1-Q^(j+1))/(1-Q^(j-i+1)). Cross multiplication proves the identity, including the adjacent zero diagonal. The end terms vanish by b_0=b_N=0 and (1-Q^N)^2=0 at the root. No nodal or semisimple substitution is used in(14). Set the explicit source intertwiner S_source=P_rev R_23^-1. Then EXACTLY S_source B_phys S_source^-1=Z_lower, S_source A_phys S_source^-1=Z_upper=Z_lower^T. (15) The original cup slide gives R_23^-1 p=N kappa^-1 e_d. Moreover ell_i=x^i/N, x=q^d=-q^-1, and the finite q-binomial identity gives ell R_23=(kappa/N)e_0^T, S_source p=N kappa^-1 e_0, ell S_source^-1=(kappa/N)e_d^T. (16) For the first formula the j-th component is kappa(-q)^j/N times sum_i [j choose i]_Q(-1)^iQ^[i(i-1)/2], namely kappa(-q)^j(1;Q)_j/N. It is zero for j>0. Thus the original N and kappa factors cancel in the WHOLE marked four-plat scalar: ell W_phys p=e_d^T W_Newton e_0, W_Newton=S_source W_phys S_source^-1. (17) The original enhancement/framing line multiplies both sides unchanged. In the complete four-head invariant reduction, physical generators1 and3 use A_phys and generator2 uses B_phys. Therefore they become P_rev T_1 P_rev and T_1, respectively, with literal signed inverses. This is a complete source-exact alphabet for ANY original four-plat word, including all composite/even levels and all Casimir normals. No unknown Racah eigenframe is present. The exact quantum trace triple in these coordinates is Z_lower,Z_upper, and the tridiagonal matrix(13). Expanding its band entries gives the denominator-free quantum Fricke identities from [the actual adjacent-trace theorem](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) with single/total Casimirs -2 and central coefficients8. In particular it is the actual physical character slice, not an arbitrary surface inferred only from(11). Equation(14), or its transpose, fixes the braid orientation on the full matrices. At N=2 no division by q+q^-1 is allowed; the same explicit matrix identities still hold. ## 5. The original cap is an exceptional curve, not a torus point Both exact boundary vectors in(17) have the correct source eigencondition: Z_upper e_0=c_0 e_0, e_d^T Z_upper=c_d e_d^T=c_0 e_d^T. (18) Consequently their reduced classical cap is B=2. The Fricke equation then gives C=4-A on its reduced locus, but has a NONREDUCED normal there. The exact finite source(16)--(18) retains that normal data. Naively putting X=1 with finite nonzero U in(9)--(10) collapses all three traces to2. It loses the real cup family. To retain a finite free A!=2 one must resolve the actual corner by U ~ (X-1)^2/[X(A-2)] as X->1. Then B->2 and C->4-A. Thus the correct cap is an exceptional divisor of the Newton chart. It cannot be removed from an endpoint estimate by calling it a regular stationary point on (C*)^2. There is a direct group certificate on this cap. For z=A-2 use mu_1=-[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=-[[1,0],[z,1]], mu_3=mu_2^-1, mu_4=mu_1^-1. (19) Their total product is identity, all meridian traces are -2, and their trace triple is (A,2,4-A). For z!=0 it is irreducible. Actual Hurwitz propagation of(19) gives the trace dynamics(12), with its direction fixed by the finite conjugation identities. On an irreducible four-punctured representation, a terminal cap trace2 forces the actual inverse pair matrices: if their product were a nontrivial unipotent, both meridian pairs would share its flag and the whole representation would be reducible. This is the four-port case of [the faithful cap certificate](actual_parabolic_cap_trace_certificate.md). Thus any REGULAR irreducible intersection of the transported cap with the closing cap is an actual representation of the original rational word closure. This is global parabolic character gluing for arbitrary rational words, not merely a formal cubic at each isolated crossing. Reducible and escaping/normal intersections are not discarded, and their source contributions require separate analytic control. This also gives a finite univariate character test for any specified word. Start with the four literal matrices(19), apply the corresponding signed Hurwitz substitutions (with the source adapters in(15)--(17)), and impose the SAME closing inverse-pair matrix equations as the cap pattern(19). Matrix inverses are adjugates since determinant is1, so these are polynomial equations in z. Saturate by z and any denominators introduced by a chosen auxiliary chart; the irreducible solutions are the zeros of an explicit ideal in C[z]. It can be computed by a gcd and, for reduced character support, its square-free part. This retains the actual group/peripheral marking without a generic-meridian A-polynomial elimination. The original nonreduced quantum source is still(16)--(18); taking this reduced ideal does not replace it in the finite period or prove a nonzero geometric coefficient. ## 6. Exact limits of the statement The Newton clock X is exp(2pi i times a NEWTON INDEX/N). The spectral Casimir is the function(9), and the geometric eigenvalue w is obtained only by solving w+w^-1=A. Neither is the physical meridian M. This theorem fixes the actual COMPLETE-meridian slice M=1, with meridian trace-2 and the original source framing. It does not create the generic M-dependent quantum A-module. That requires the actual meromorphic color/dual/turn family and its peripheral currents; the generic q scalar(2) is not a substitute for that meridian deformation. The older [actual-color Newton transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) uses different nodes Q^j+Q^-j and the knot's meridian variable. The two Newton transforms must not be identified by their names. The reversal identity is exact at the original root. Its actual generic-q turn family need not be the same reversal matrix off the root, so whole normal derivatives of a turned circuit must retain that family. Likewise(5) is not deleted in a q-normal recurrence. Finally actual character support and an explicit source alphabet do not prove that the geometric branch is accessible, noncanceling, or largest in the complete finite source. A sharp coherent action bound and a nonzero full-source coefficient remain necessary. This result provides the exact finite recurrence, actual braid graph and pointed boundary data for that next analysis; it does not infer a new universal volume equality from a principal curve alone. ## 7. What the universal local dilogarithm does identify There is a precise useful boundary-symbol statement. On the logarithmic lift of the regular triangle, put S=2pi i Phi. Directly from the actual factorial ratio in(1), its leading action is S=-Li_2(X)+Li_2(Y)+Li_2(X/Y)-Li_2(1) +(Log Y)^2/2+pi i Log X-pi^2. (19a) The last real constant is the leading original kappa, not a chosen imaginary calibration. The q^i factor in(1) is subleading and remains in its exact amplitude. Differentiation gives the same actual graph: partial_(Log X) S=Log U, partial_(Log Y) S=-Log V. Thus the rational pre-Bloch symbol of this local phase is beta_Newt=-[X]+[Y]+[X/Y], delta beta_Newt=-X wedge U+Y wedge V. (19b) For an elementary verification, ignore the torsion class of -1, write a=1-X, b=1-Y, c=X-Y, and expand the wedge of U=Ya/c and V=-b/c. Bilinearity gives exactly the boundary of the three displayed dilogarithms. The Bloch--Wigner identity also gives D(beta_Newt)=Im S-log|X| Arg U+log|Y| Arg V, (19c) on compatible logarithmic branches. Regular composed seams telescope in(19b); a turn preserves X wedge U. This does NOT yet identify the resulting closed symbol with the topological fundamental class. Boundary wedges do not fix a closed Bloch period, and the actual cap lies on the exceptional corner in section5, where a regular seam-telescoping argument cannot replace its normal source. A chain-level comparison with the actual signed crossing blocks and marked boundary is still required. Such a global comparison is already proved for the original factorial crossing symbols in [the fundamental-cycle note](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), for arbitrary diagrams and their regular complete representations. It supplies the classical regulator bound, not the missing global source estimate. In particular(19b) alone neither supplies a generic meridian nor proves access or noncancellation for any new word class. ## 8. Focused verification [The new exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_twist_canonical_graph.py) passes symbolic symplectic/Fricke/inverse-Hurwitz and resolved-cap group identities; six generic physical families using the literal full-Cartan universal R and its gamma_N scalar; and seven original root families N=2,...,8. The latter include every finite Weyl boundary equation, the physical three-head Hom action, all quantum Fricke relations/cubic, the source intertwiner, and twenty-one full marked four-plat words using all three physical braid generators. Finite-field arithmetic is exact. These checks supplement the all-entry proofs and do not claim an asymptotic or a meridian deformation from finite tests.

title: A coherent two-twist/turn source packet with a sharp norm rate
text: # A coherent two-twist/turn source packet with a sharp norm rate 29 October 2026. Set A=T_2 P_rev T_2 in the COMPLETE original Newton metric. The whole source vector A1 has an exact second-order Ward recurrence, an exact reflected boundary equation with an inhomogeneous current, and a sharp all-level norm exponent. The proof uses both actual source endpoints and never assumes that distinct spectral roots alone prevent conversion. It does not identify the reflected circuit with a hyperbolic link or prove the rate for arbitrary longer reduced words. ## 1. Exact original coefficient and Ward equation Use the original N,d,q,Q,kappa,F_i,s_i of [the Newton metric](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md). Define W_i=F_i^2 sum_(j=0)^i (-1)^j Q^[(3j^2+j)/2]/(F_j^3 F_(i-j)), H_i=F_i W_i, 0<=i<=d. The all-entry T_2 formula and F_j F_(d-j)=N nu_j give the exact SOURCE vector, with no phase or endpoint discarded, (A1)_i=kappa^4 N(-q)^(i+d) W_i. (1) Indeed T_2 1 has entries kappa^2(-q)^j F_j. Apply the genuine reversal and then T_2; its inner j coefficient is nu_j^3 Q^(-j), exactly (-1)^j Q^[(3j^2+j)/2]. The whole-index recurrence is (1-Q^i)W_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)W_(i-1) -Q(1-Q^(i-1))^2 W_(i-2), H_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)H_(i-1) -Q(1-Q^(i-1))^3 H_(i-2), (2) H_0=1, H_1=1-2Q. At i=1 the second coefficient is ZERO; no H_(-1) is needed. These equations hold for every physical index i<=d and all N>=2. For an own derivation, put a_j=(-1)^jQ^[(3j^2+j)/2]/F_j^3, G_i=sum_j a_j/F_(i-j), and use formal generating series modulo z^N. The shift T:f(z)->f(Qz) gives (1-T)^3 a(z)=-Q^2 z T^3 a(z), E(Qz)=(1-z)E(z), E(z)=sum z^k/F_k, G=aE. Consequently (1-z)(1-Qz)G(z)-3(1-Qz)G(Qz) +3G(Q^2z)-G(Q^3z)=0. Coefficient extraction gives (1-Q^i)^3G_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)G_(i-1)-QG_(i-2), hence (2). This argument can first be made at generic Q and then specialized coefficientwise below degree N. It never divides a zero root factorial. The physical source identification (1) uses the root complementation identity. A generic-Q continuation of this displayed scalar recurrence is not thereby identified with the actual generic-q tangle/source germ. All estimates here use its exact physical root values. ## 2. The second source endpoint is exactly the known Gaussian Let P_d be the original normalization endpoint, with its already proved identities and all-parity Gaussian asymptotic: P_d=N^2 sum_(j=0)^d Q^j/F_j^2 =sum_(j=0)^d F_j =N^(3/2) exp[i pi(1/4-N/12+1/(4N))]+O(sqrt N). See [the endpoint proof](actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian_asymptotic.md). In particular cN^(3/2)<=|P_d|<=CN^(3/2) for all large N. Root factorial complementation in the actual sum gives W_d=N sum_j Q^(j^2)/F_j^2 =(Q/N)sum_j Q^j F_j^2=conjugate(P_d)/N, H_d=conjugate(P_d). (3) The penultimate coefficient is also fixed, not a free backward datum: (conjugate(F_1))^3 H_(d-1) =(1-2/Q)H_d+Q^(-1). (4) For completeness set C(t)=sum_j F_j^2t^j. Its exact finite Ward is (1-t)C(t)+2Qt C(Qt)-Q^2t C(Q^2t)=1. At t=1 this evaluates C(Q^2) from C(Q); substituting the complemented finite expression for H_(d-1) gives (4). Define J_0=0,J_1=1 and evolve J by (2) only for i>=2. Direct reversal of (2), with g_k=conjugate(F_k)^3 H_(d-k), now proves g_k=H_d conjugate(H_k)+Q^(-1)conjugate(J_k), 0<=k<=d. (5) The corresponding PHASED source coefficient, useful before any future color-contour deformation, is exactly (A1)_(d-k)=kappa^4 Q^(-1) q^(k^2)/s_k^2 [H_d conjugate(H_k)+Q^(-1)conjugate(J_k)]. (5a) Indeed W_(d-k)=nu_k g_k/(N s_k^2); the actual factor (-q)^(2d-k)nu_k=Q^(-1)q^(k^2) gives (5a). The constant term Q^(-1) in (4)--(5) is a retained original boundary current. It is not set to zero. The independent J solution does not satisfy the resetting i=1 source equation, which is why that current cannot be absorbed into a second homogeneous source at the endpoint. ## 3. A regular gapped half-circle and a uniform envelope Put u=pi i/N and Y=exp(2iu). The classical monic transfer has roots mu_±(u)=[2-3Y ± Y sqrt(4Y-3)]/2. (6) Choose the square root continuously from +1 at u=0. On 0<=u<=pi/2, the minus root mu is nonzero and dominant until the terminal equality of moduli; write rho(u)=|mu(u)|. The eigenvalue difference has modulus |sqrt(4Y-3)|>=1, so its eigenframe and first derivatives are uniformly bounded on this entire closed half-circle. Here is a direct modulus check. For a=2-3Y, b=(1-Y)^3 and 0<u<=pi/2, a^2/b=(9+16sin^2u)/(8sin^2u) -i cos(u)(1-16sin^2u)/(8sin^3u). Two roots of lambda^2-a lambda+b have equal modulus exactly when a^2/b belongs to [0,4]. The imaginary part vanishes only at sin u=1/4 or cos u=0. The first gives 20, outside that interval; the second gives25/8. Thus the only modulus equality is u=pi/2. At u=0 the roots are -1,0 and the source selects -1. Let I(u)=pi^(-1)integral_0^u log rho(v)dv. Uniformly for all physical i with 0<=i<=d/2, the exact transfer matrix differs by O(1/N) from its classical matrix. In the bounded moving eigenframe, each normalized step has norm at most rho(u_i)(1+C/N). Hence |H_i|+|J_i| <= C exp[N I(pi i/N)]. (7) The constants do not deteriorate at the terminal modulus equality: the eigenVALUES remain separated. The sum-to-integral error is O(1). On every smaller interval 0<=u<=u_0<pi/2 the source is sharper: log|H_i|=N I(pi i/N)+O_(u0)(1), |J_i/H_i|<=C_(u0). (8) To justify the nonzero statement, write h_i=H_i/H_(i-1). The exact Riccati map is h_i=a_i-b_i/h_(i-1). Its derivative at the dominant classical root is mu_other/mu, of modulus uniformly less than one. An O(1/N) disk around the smooth nonzero dominant root is therefore invariant under every step, by induction. The literal reset H_1=1-2Q starts inside that disk. Thus every h_i is nonzero and h_i=mu(u_i)+O(1/N). Summing logarithms proves (8)'s first assertion. For the second, the difference of successive J_i/H_i has consecutive ratio b_i/(h_i h_(i-1)), uniformly less than one; its first difference is1/H_1. This proves the uniform bound. No claim of adiabatic survival is made across the modulus crossing. ## 4. Sharp whole-source norm from the two actual endpoint solutions For the first half, (7) and the uniform sine-factorial estimate give log|W_i| <= N[I(u)+Lambda(u)/pi]+O(log N). For the second half put k=d-i, u=pi k/N. Equations (3),(5), and s_i s_k=N give |W_i|=|g_k|/(N s_k^2), log|W_i| <= N[I(u)+2Lambda(u)/pi]+O(log N). (9) These bounds cover EVERY index, including the middle and endpoints. Since Lambda(u)>=0 on [0,pi/2], the backward profile dominates the forward one. Write B(u)=I(u)+2Lambda(u)/pi. For each fixed u in(0,pi/2), (3),(5),(8) also give the matching lower rate in(9): the J term is relatively O(N^(-3/2)) and cannot cancel the main term. There is a unique maximizer u_* of B. Indeed B'(u)=pi^(-1)log[rho(u)/(2sin u)^2]. For 2sin u<1, rho>=|b|^(1/2)=(2sin u)^(3/2)>(2sin u)^2. For u>=pi/6, an equality rho=(2sin u)^2 can occur only when z^3-4z^2+3z-1=0, z=4sin^2u. (10) One can verify this without choosing a root phase: impose |mu|^2=z^2 in mu^2-a mu+b=0 and its conjugate. The resulting equality is z(1-z)^2=1-2z+2z^2, exactly (10); here |conjugate(b)a-conjugate(a)z^2|^2=z^3(1-2z+2z^2)>0. The polynomial has a unique root z_* in[1,4], in fact in(3,4). At pi/6 the ratio rho/(2sin u)^2 is greater than one, whereas at pi/2 it is1/sqrt2<1. Continuity and uniqueness therefore prove the claimed strict maximum, with u_*=arcsin(sqrt(z_*)/2). Using (1), the polynomial number of positive norm terms and a rounded index near the backward maximizer now prove the ALL-LEVEL estimate log||T_2 P_rev T_2 1||_Newt^2 = N L+O(log N), L=(2/pi)[integral_0^(u_*)log rho(v)dv+2Lambda(u_*)]. (11) Numerically L is approximately .9060724478038353. This number is only a calibration; formula (11) is the proved constant. It comes from the fully coherent source vector before taking its positive norm. ## 5. Scope and reuse The actual adjoint-word closure of A^dagger A is the original numerator source ||A1||^2, with the unrestricted marked cap and kappa retained. Thus (11) is a new coherent estimate for an ENTIRE specified original source circuit, not an expanded positive path. Its link topology, hyperbolicity and regulator identification are separate questions; no volume equality is asserted from its numerical rate. This proof offers a checkable recurrence mechanism beyond distinct eigenvalues: an exact resetting source endpoint, a regular half-domain modulus gap, an independently evaluated nonzero opposite endpoint, and a reflection identity retaining the inhomogeneous current. Those inputs allow the two gapped solutions to be estimated separately. There is no unsupported propagation through a general modulus crossing. The [modular reduction](actual_newton_coherent_turn_reduction.md) removes arbitrarily many redundant turns; genuinely longer reduced mixed words still require their own coherent packet/current estimate. Audit: [literal original matrices, exact sums/recurrences/endpoints and norm calibration](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_two_twist_interaction_packet.py). The finite profiles check the normalization and reflected recurrence. They do not replace the uniform endpoint, Riccati and maximum arguments.

title: The nilpotent Mobius action is not the actual framing Ward action
text: # The nilpotent Mobius action is not the actual framing Ward action 28 October 2026. A common fractional-linear change of the charged nilpotent anchors is an exact algebra automorphism. Its effect on the original source is computable. However, it does not provide a second geometric framing integral: invariance of a homogeneous top-degree state is automatic, while the ordinary common action fails covariance with an original crossing. Its source-preserving weighted lift also has the wrong nilpotent Jordan type to be the actual Hopf current on a head. This rules out that specific identification. It does not rule out a coupled quantum dressing which transforms clocks, crossings and source currents together, or the independent positive selection theorem for a network already satisfying its stated hypotheses. ## 1. Exact automorphism and source Jacobian Put d=N-1 and A_N=K[X]/(X^N), in characteristic zero. The source is the original functional lambda(P)=[X^d]P. For a!=0 define phi_(a,c)(X)=aX/(1+cX) mod X^N. (1) The inverse is X/(a-cX), so this is an algebra automorphism. Its SOURCE formula, valid for EVERY polynomial exterior, is lambda(P(phi_(a,c)(X))) =lambda(P(X) J_(a,c)(X)), J_(a,c)(X)=a(a-cX)^(N-2). (2) Proof. In the specified residue lambda=Res P(X)dX/X^N, make the formal invertible change Y=aX/(1+cX). Then X=Y/(a-cY) and dX/X^N=a(a-cY)^(N-2)dY/Y^N. This proves (2) with its exact scalar and exponent. For k anchors the source factor is the product of the k displayed J factors. At a=1, its infinitesimal identity is lambda(-X^2 partial_X P)=-(N-2)lambda(XP). (3) Thus ordinary Mobius substitution does NOT preserve the original source on arbitrary exteriors. The coefficient norm of its source multiplier at a=1 is exactly ||(1-cX)^(N-2)||_1=(1+|c|)^(N-2). (4) At fixed nonzero c this is exponential in N. This is a norm statement about the full normal source, not a claim that the original scalar acquires that factor. ## 2. Why homogeneous-source invariance is automatic For k original charged anchors let Omega=product_i X_i^d. The top homogeneous piece of A_N^(tensor k) has degree kd and is the ONE line K Omega. Every actual whole-source P_h is homogeneous of that degree before projection, including after the proved closure contractions. Under common (1), each variable starts with aX_i and all remaining terms have strictly higher degree. Since no degree above kd survives, phi_(a,c)(P_h)=a^(kd) P_h in A_N^(tensor k). (5) In particular c-invariance at a=1 holds for EVERY top-degree state, whether its selected coefficient is nonzero or zero. The induced c-action on this socle line is trivial. It therefore contains no information identifying a geometric relative period or selecting a nonzero second framing fiber. This is the same original homogeneous socle, not a substituted favorable source. It remains possible to retain lower-degree normal classes and the full Jacobian (2). Their covariance must actually be proved; (5) cannot replace it. ## 3. The exact source-preserving lift has the wrong Ward generator There is a specified weighted action preserving lambda on ALL states: U_(a,c)P(X)=a^(-d)(1+cX)^(N-2)P(phi_(a,c)(X)). (6) Indeed (2), or direct substitution in it, gives lambda(U P)=lambda(P). At a=1 its infinitesimal generator is L=(N-2)X-X^2 partial_X, L X^j=(N-2-j)X^(j+1). (7) For N>=3 its Jordan blocks are N-1 and 1: it acts in one full chain on 1,X,...,X^(N-2), and kills the separate socle X^d. At N=2 it is zero. The UNWEIGHTED substitution generator -X^2 partial_X likewise has blocks N-1 and 1, with the separate constant line instead. The original complete quantum E and F on one physical head have a single Jordan block of size N. For F its consecutive coefficients in the actual balanced basis are 1-Q^(j+1), 0<=j<=N-2, all nonzero. The corresponding E coefficients are also nonzero along their whole chain. Consequently no invertible head gauge conjugates (7), or its unweighted version, to the actual E or F. Nilpotent Jordan type is unchanged by any such gauge. One can instead use the ordinary coherent weight (1+cX)^d, obtaining the regular classical generator dX-X^2 partial_X. But then the source is NOT fixed; exactly lambda((1+cX)^d P(X/(1+cX))) =lambda(P(X)/(1-cX)). (8) Moreover the primitive two-head coherent generator has nilpotency index 2N-1, whereas the actual root Hopf coproduct has its N-th power zero. Thus even this alternative is not a factorwise identification with the actual quantum tensor action. Its source and tensor adapter would have to be constructed and retained separately. ## 4. A literal original crossing fails common Mobius covariance This is also visible without a representation classification. Let B be the original positive checked crossing in the actual balanced factorial basis and retain its common Cartan scalar kappa. Complete color means x=-q^(-1), Q=q^2, hence x^(-2)=Q. Its k=0 entries give [|0,1>] B |1,0>=kappa x^(-1), [|0,2>] B |2,0>=kappa x^(-2). (9) For N>=3 put D=-X^2 partial_X and D_tot=D_1+D_2. Then [|0,2>] [B,D_tot] |1,0> =kappa(x^(-1)-x^(-2)) !=0. (10) To see the two terms, D_tot|1,0>=-|2,0>; after B only its k=0 term can yield |0,2>. Conversely B|1,0> has |0,1> coefficient in (9), and D_tot sends it to -|0,2>. This proves (10), with no lost factorial, source normalization or Cartan scalar. At the actual half-root x^(-1)=-q and x^(-2)=q^2, so the difference is -q(1+q), nonzero for every N>=3. Therefore the common ordinary Mobius action cannot be slid through the unchanged actual crossing. Full E/F Ward identities do not supply that missing covariance, since they concern the different Hopf action in Section 3. At N=2 the unweighted Mobius substitution is already the identity on K[X]/X^2 and supplies no framing direction at all. ## 5. Consequence for the proposed second framing fiber The [nilpotent source](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md) and [closure contractions](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) are exact. The ordinary common Mobius changes do not add a selected nonzero fiber to them. On the original top-degree state they act trivially by (5). On general exteriors they require the source multiplier (2), and on the fixed actual network they have the explicit covariance defect (10). This leaves a precise constructive possibility: a COUPLED quantum framing transformation, including the underclock feedback, Hopf tensor factors and boundary co-source, might have a controlled nonzero relative fiber. It cannot be identified with the common automorphism (1) merely from nilpotent-source invariance. The existing warning about ordinary coherent Mobius action versus actual quantum dressing in [the Springer boundary note](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md) is consistent with, and now has the explicit selected-source and crossing calculations (2)-(10). No broad knot-volume lower bound or nonzero global geometric coefficient is proved by this test. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_nilpotent_mobius_source.py): exact source Jacobians and inverse maps, both weighted source actions, their Jordan indices, original quantum E/F chains and the full original crossing witness (10), with kappa retained.

title: Projected nodes, actual local periods, and the surviving Ward source
text: # Projected nodes, actual local periods, and the surviving Ward source 28 October 2026. A collision of two preferred-longitude values need not be a collision of the original critical points. On two disjoint regular Morse charts of the original coefficient density, the local periods have a bounded separating insertion frame even at that projected node. Internal shift identities have explicit exponentially small relative-boundary errors on these charts. No inverse longitude difference is used. This does not prove that the selected finite knot source splits into these local periods with a bounded connection. The exact original figure-eight Ward equation below shows why the missing source step cannot be replaced by the classical separating projectors. The distinction concerns a projected node, not a genuine collision on the full normalized character scheme. ## 1. Actual density and the analytic hypotheses Keep the actual whole coefficient array, integral closure lattice, cut average, pivots, Cartan/framing constants and peripheral line of [the geometric normal-period theorem](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Fix its two framing coordinates on a transverse slice. Write the remaining scaled internal coordinates as z in C^r and u=Log M. The preferred meridian half-step is u -> u+pi*i/N. Use the exactly normalized factorial interpolant, equivalently [the exact full-Psi quotient](actual_factorial_full_psi_identity.md), with the original affine arguments and their marks. Denote this holomorphic density on a regular chart by omega_N(u,z). No new finite-state values or co-source are assigned. Here are the analytic premises needed below. They are more than a formal stationary series. On fixed neighborhoods of two sections z_p(u), p=1,2, suppose omega_N = chi_N(u) N^beta exp[N Phi(u,z)] a_N(u,z) dz_1...dz_r, (1) a_N=a_0+O(1/N), a_0(u,z_p(u)) != 0, uniformly holomorphically, with all fixed derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. The external normalization chi_N is retained as a line; it is not assumed tame or dropped. Phi=S/(2pi*i) is the actual marked action. Suppose partial_z Phi(u,z_p(u))=0, det partial_z^2 Phi(u,z_p(u)) != 0, z_1(u) != z_2(u). (2) All bounds and separations are uniform after shrinking the u-disk. When a separating actual monomial is used below, the two exponentiated critical configurations must also be distinct; different logarithmic lifts of the same configuration are not enough. For the reduced coefficient density chi_N is nonzero and holomorphic on the chosen chart. If the full ADO dimension is included, its possibly meromorphic line stays external: analyticity and nonvanishing below refer to the normalized sections Z_p,N/chi_N, and scalar ratios are asserted on the regular locus of that line. No fixed-size pole-free disk for the full ADO dimension is assumed. For a finite product of original factorial interpolants, (1) follows from the proved uniform complex Stirling estimate whenever every scaled factorial argument stays in a compact subset of 0<Re s<1. The powers N^beta and scalar marks are literal ones. Other regular full-Psi charts can be used only where their marked uniform symbol has actually been established. The formal normal theorem alone does not establish (1) on an arbitrary continued chart. If an exact cotangent or window factor is included in a chosen local source presentation, (1) must hold for that factor too, with its retained mode/action. A bare coefficient estimate is not automatically an estimate for every relative source sector. The [actual critical correspondence](marked_braid_holonomy.md) identifies (2), on its full regular locus, with distinct framed knot representations. The nondegenerate transverse Hessian is supplied at the geometric branch by the normal-period theorem. Its conjugate has the same algebraic nondegeneracy. A projected coincidence L_1(u_0)=L_2(u_0) (3) does not invalidate either of these full critical charts. ## 2. Analytic local periods have a bounded frame at the node **Local theorem.** Under (1)--(2), after shrinking the u-disk, there are disjoint truncated Gaussian cycles Gamma_p(u) and exact analytic periods Z_p,N(f;u)=integral_(Gamma_p(u)) f(u,z) omega_N(u,z), (4) such that Z_p,N(1;u)=chi_N(u) N^(beta-r/2) exp[N phi_p(u)] [b_p,0(u)+O(1/N)], phi_p=Phi(u,z_p), b_p,0 != 0. (5) The cycles in (4) are specified local relative cycles for the unchanged actual density. They are not asserted to be summands of the selected finite lattice cycle. Choose a holomorphic insertion theta with |theta(u,z_1(u))-theta(u,z_2(u))| >= delta > 0. For distinct exponentiated critical configurations such a theta is a fixed linear combination of the actual internal monomials: each distinct pair excludes only a proper hyperplane of choices. For the two literal insertions 1,theta, form M_N(p,0)=1, M_N(p,1)=Z_p,N(theta;u)/Z_p,N(1;u). (6) Then uniformly on a smaller disk, M_N(p,1)=theta(u,z_p(u))+O(1/N), ||M_N||+||M_N^-1|| <= C. (7) In particular, (3) does not cause an insertion-frame singularity. The normalized sections Z_p,N/chi_N are nonzero for all sufficiently large N, as are the scalar periods on the regular nonzero locus of the external line. The exact diagonal meridian ratios in this LOCAL period object are b_p,N(u)=Z_p,N(1;u+pi*i/N)/Z_p,N(1;u). (8) After retaining chi_N's exact ratio, they have the actual marked leading longitude ratio. Indeed N times the action increment tends to partial_u S_p/2=Log L_p. The common prescribed external scalar line must be included in whichever longitude convention is used. Proof. A parameter-dependent holomorphic Morse coordinate y exists near each section, with Phi(u,z(y,u))=phi_p(u)-(y_1^2+...+y_r^2)/2. One elementary construction first solves partial_1 Phi=0 for z_1 by the implicit-function theorem, completes that square using the analytic square root of its nonzero coefficient, and repeats on the Schur complement. A fixed complex linear change makes the needed pivots nonzero at the base point. Shrinking the disk keeps these pivots and square roots holomorphic and bounded. This proves the asserted coordinate without an asymptotic summability premise. Take the image of the real cube [-eta,eta]^r with its fixed orientation. The two images remain disjoint. In these coordinates ordinary Gaussian integration, a Taylor expansion on a smaller cube and an exponentially small outside tail give (5). Its leading coefficient is (2pi)^(r/2) times the original a_0 and the marked Morse-coordinate Jacobian. Every factor is nonzero. The same calculation with theta gives (7). Analyticity follows by integrating over a fixed cube in y; the exponentially small tails are analytic as well. Formula (8) is then an exact analytic ratio. This proof does not divide by L_1-L_2 or solve a scalar companion eigenvector problem at the projected node. For clarity, transporting a LOCAL branch vector in the insertion frame produces the matrix M_N(u+pi*i/N)^t diag(b_1,N,b_2,N) M_N(u)^(-t). (9) Its frames are bounded by (7). This is a statement about the direct sum of the specified local periods. Equation (9) is not identified with the global finite-source companion, nor is it an explicit new all-level operator. Such an identification would require the source pushforward which is still missing. ## 3. Exact local Ward errors are relative-boundary currents There is a source-relevant quantitative refinement. Let v be one actual internal integer shift, scaled as delta_N=v/N (with the corresponding convention if logarithmic coordinates are used). The original factorial functional equations give EXACTLY omega_N(u,z+delta_N)=R_v,N(u,z) omega_N(u,z), (10) on the common regular chart, including the original Gaussian and all characters. Let f be holomorphic on that common chart. Let H_p,N be the translation cylinder of Gamma_p by delta_N, and B_p,N the cylinder of its boundary. With consistent boundary orientations, holomorphic Stokes gives the exact identity Z_p,N(R_v,N f(u,z+delta_N)-f(u,z);u) = integral_(B_p,N) f omega_N. (11) There are c>0,C,B independent of N for which the right side satisfies |integral_(B_p,N) f omega_N| <= |chi_N(u)| C N^B ||f|| exp[N(Re phi_p(u)-c)]. (12) Here ||f|| is the supremum on a fixed neighborhood of the cylinder. To prove it, the unshifted boundary has |y|>=eta and hence an action drop at least eta^2/2. Its O(1/N) translation changes Re Phi by O(1/N), uniformly by holomorphy. Thus a fixed positive fraction of the drop remains. The cylinder's volume and Jacobians have uniform polynomial bounds; (1) proves (12). No discarded boundary term is set to zero. Relative to its own nonzero local period, this error is at most C N^B exp(-cN). Consequently the full regular phase has separate analytic quantum blocks with exponentially accurate local Ward relations even when the scalar longitude roots coincide. Genuine complex collisions of the FULL critical points, a vanishing Hessian, a source pole crossing, or continuation outside these neighborhoods are excluded. Also, an external action gain can amplify (12). The comparison of its c with the full action width is an extra estimate, just as in [the local analytic transport barrier](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md). ## 4. An exact original-source test at an actual projected node The original figure-eight identity gives, at M=1 and EVERY level, K_N=sum_(n=0)^d w_n, w_n=|(Q;Q)_n|^2, mu_N(f)=sum_n w_n f(Q^n), d=N-1. (13) This is the complete reduced source with its original pointing, not an arbitrary normal-state co-source. Its two classical critical clocks are z_+=(1+i sqrt(3))/2, z_-=(1-i sqrt(3))/2, the distinct geometric/conjugate character lifts with the same complete preferred longitude. The two saddles of the exact sine interpolant G_N(Ns)^2 lie at s=1/6,5/6. Its phase is 2J(s), with nonzero second derivatives +2pi sqrt(3),-2pi sqrt(3), respectively. Thus this is an actual source example satisfying the local analytic premises: the two full critical points are regular while their peripheral projection is nodal. Their calibrated regulators have opposite signs. The real positive finite source is not replaced by the sum of both local Gaussian cycles. The full finite Ward equation retains an endpoint. Put A(Z)=2-Z-Z^-1, (B_Q f)(Z)=A(QZ) f(QZ). The exact weights satisfy w_(n+1)=A(Q^(n+1))w_n, w_0=1,w_N=0. Therefore, for EVERY Laurent polynomial insertion, mu_N((I-B_Q)f)=f(1). (14) Now take the classical separating functions e_+(Z)=(Z-z_-)/(z_+-z_-), e_-=1-e_+. They separate the two classical critical points, but [B_Q,e_+]f =(Q-1) Z A(QZ) f(QZ)/(z_+-z_-), (15) mu_N((I-B_Q)e_+)=z_+/(z_+-z_-) != 0, mu_N((I-B_Q)e_-)=-z_-/(z_+-z_-) != 0. (16) These are exact original-source identities, not asymptotic errors. The pointwise commutator is O(1/N) on the unit clock grid, but it is not zero. Such algebraic smallness cannot alone establish an exponential conversion barrier. Moreover e_+ and e_- are not exact idempotents in C[Z,Z^-1]/(Z^N-1); their idempotent defect is proportional to Z^2-Z+1. In the SAME source, N mu_N((Z^2-Z+1)(Z^-2-Z^-1+1))/K_N -> 2pi sqrt(3), (17) as proved in [the source-quotient theorem](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md). Thus the positive paired insertion of that idempotent defect still has the full geometric exponential rate. The exact global source cannot be replaced by the reduced critical projectors while discarding only exponentially smaller terms. This does not show harmful node conversion occurs in this knot. It shows exactly which source identity a proposed exact separation would have to improve. In fact this prototype has a separate positive whole-source proof; (14)--(17) explain why the node's local classical idempotents are not that proof. ## 5. The remaining quantum test The [pointed commutant theorem](actual_pointed_commutant_and_critical_observable.md) already proves that every horizontal endomorphism preserving the raw Mellin source lattice acts scalarly on its selected source. Its partial insertion module supplies formal critical observables, with a covariant rule rather than a zero commutator. The local analytic construction above strengthens the regular-node statement but does not evade that exact source obstruction. To exclude harmful nodal conversion for the original whole period, one must still do one of the following with the original source: identify a bounded analytic pushforward to these separated local periods and bound all the currents in (11), or construct a different covariant multioperator module whose actual connection has the necessary equal-calibrated-action support/exponential barrier. Classical sheet separation and a nondegenerate full Hessian supply neither identification automatically. A formal direct sum alone cannot detect a nonzero exponentially small entry. In particular, this note proves a regular projected node introduces no LOCAL Morse or insertion-frame singularity. It does not prove that the actual global connection contains no conversion there, that the geometric coefficient of the selected cycle is nonzero, or a sharp whole-knot upper bound. [Finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_node_source_ward.py): exact original cyclic weights, affine Ward endpoint, classical separating commutator and nonzero two-node source values over finite fields. The analytic statements above are proved by the uniform Morse and side-cylinder estimates, not inferred from the finite audit.

title: A source-exact quotient for normalization boundary currents, including normal jets
text: # A source-exact quotient for normalization boundary currents, including normal jets 29 October 2026. There is a genuine class of singular relative-source components that can be eliminated before positivity: the zero-pointing part of a complete visible Markov normalization cell. This is an operator identity with spectators retained. It composes through any fixed forest of such cells at arbitrary braid width, even when the spectator coefficients are not scalar or mutually commuting. For the original full-Psi radial current, even at radius one, every normalized Mellin Taylor coefficient of its pointed scalar is at most N/(2pi). The entire radial operator on a nilpotent contraction has normalized coefficients bounded by H_N/(2pi). On a fixed radius below one, oscillation gives the sharper bound C r! log(eN)^r for raw pointed derivatives. Thus these actual logarithmic normal currents have no additional exponential normalization cost after contraction. This extends the known normalization-cell evaluation and its tame radial value to an operator-valued relative-current quotient with a quantified normal germ. It does not eliminate internal head/cap alias currents, identify Mellin order with the knot meridian, or prove a sharp bound for the remaining knot period. ## 1. The exact selected cell, with all original scalar factors Use the literal positive equal-color factorization and pivot of [the Markov source proof](actual_markov_ray_normalization_and_pruning.md): R+=kappa C D U C^-1, g_b=x^(-d) Q^(-b), d=N-1, alpha=kappa x^(-d). For every diagonal function r of the second RELATIVE channel, Tr_new[(I tensor g) kappa C D U (I tensor r) C^-1] =alpha r_0 I. (1) The trace has NO additional 1/N. The original sole cut average, turns, marked row and full peripheral/framing line are unchanged. Zero framing cancels the original alpha only when the complete original Markov cell is contracted. A current with r_0 != 1 keeps that extra factor. For completeness, the direct finite coefficient proof of (1) computes the k-th channel's cut diagonal as alpha x^(-2k) Q^(-k) (1;Q)_k = alpha delta_(k,0). Its intermediate q-binomial identity is sum_(j=0)^s (-1)^(s-j) Q^[j(j+1)/2] (Q^(a-j+1);Q)_s/[F_j F_(s-j)]=(-1)^s. Expand the Pochhammer as a polynomial in Q^a. All its positive-degree coefficients contain (Q^(1-ell);Q)_s and vanish; the constant is the right side. A second finite binomial sum gives (1). This proof retains the forbidden-index zeros of the original finite head and works at all levels, including even and composite N. ## 2. Operator-valued pointing and exact cancellation of its kernel Let S be ANY spectator space. Replace r_k by arbitrary operators A_k on S, acting at the same relative-channel slot in (1). Then Tr_new[(I tensor g tensor I_S) kappa (C D U tensor I_S) (sum_k I_cut tensor |k><k| tensor A_k) (C^-1 tensor I_S)] =alpha I_cut tensor A_0. (2) To prove (2), expand in any basis of End(S) and apply (1) to every coefficient. No positivity, simultaneous diagonalization or assumption about an exterior knot value enters. In particular A_k may be coupled to arbitrary tensors outside the cell, but not silently moved through the cut head or the inside of C. Define the pointing map epsilon(A)=A_0. The difference A_k-A_0 for every k (3) is annihilated by the COMPLETE cell. Thus a source-current packet may be replaced by its pointing after the whole cell has been assembled. It is not necessary for the norms of its individual channels to be small. Equation (2) remains valid after arbitrary exterior composition and the original full marked functional. The same statement holds coefficientwise for a holomorphic or meromorphic normal germ A_k(sigma), on a common domain where the cell expression is defined. If epsilon(A(sigma)) is identically zero, ALL its normal Laurent/Taylor coefficients pair to zero. A pole in separated channel pieces is canceled only after their common complete packet is formed; (2) is not a prescription to drop those poles first. Now suppose a fixed tensor diagram contains a forest of visible cells: each leaf has the precise form (2), and after contracting a leaf the next prescribed cell has that form. Contract leaves in this order. Induction proves that every zero-pointing leaf packet disappears exactly, and each surviving cell is replaced by its specified A_0, in the original operator order. This is an all-width source theorem, not a claim that every braid admits such a pruning or that arbitrary internal projectors can be slid to a cap. ## 3. The actual radial current and its Mellin-normal germ Fix a real 0<R<1, independent of N. Let Psi be the fully normalized positive function from [the original circle/ray source](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). The actual positive atom's radial part in the displayed cell has channel coefficients r_k(0)=-N Q^(d-k) E_(d-k)(R)/F_k, where E_a(R)=1/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(N-a-1) dt. Consequently its pointed scalar is EXACTLY h_N(0)=-N Q^-1 E_d(R). (4) It must be retained: the original ray group is h_N(0) times the whole exterior invariant, and need not have a smaller exponential rate. The circle group is (1-h_N(0)) times that same exterior. There is a natural logarithmic normal of this specified relative radial current: multiply its radial integrand by t^(-sigma). For Re sigma<1 set h_N(sigma)=-N Q^-1/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(-sigma) dt. (5) This is holomorphic there, by integrable domination on compact sigma-sets. Its derivatives are the literal insertions (-log t)^r in the original radial current. At sigma=0 (5) is (4), with the original phase and coefficient, not a rescaled boundary state. Sigma is a Mellin-normal coordinate of this atom source. It is NOT being identified with the knot's meridian parameter or with a normal Cartan coupon elsewhere in the word. ## 4. Uniform normal currents through radius one The exact real-ray modulus, with the complete central factor retained, is |Psi_epsilon(log t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N), 0<t<=1. Consequently its quotient has modulus A_N(t)=sqrt((1-t)/(1-t^N))<=1, A_N(1)=1/sqrt(N). (6a) There is no pole at t=1. This proves, for EVERY 0<R<=1 and r>=0, |h_N^(r)(0)|/r! <=N/(2pi*r!) integral_0^R A_N(t)(-log t)^r dt <=N/(2pi). (6b) For Re sigma<1 it also proves |h_N(sigma)|<=N/[2pi(1-Re sigma)]. (6c) All normal coefficients are those of the actual Mellin current (5). No fixed-distance-from-one assumption, separated root branch, or pointwise phase approximation enters (6a)--(6c). There is an operator version BEFORE the normalization cell is closed. For a literal nilpotent contraction T on its supplied finite relative head, T^N=0 and ||T||<=1, retain the full source correction E_sigma(T)=epsilon/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi_epsilon(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(N-sigma-1) sum_(a=0)^d t^(-a)T^a dt. (6d) It is a holomorphic operator germ for Re sigma<1 and includes every original finite resolvent coefficient. Differentiation and (6a) give || E_sigma^(r)(T)|_(sigma=0) /r! || <=(1/(2pi)) sum_(j=1)^N j^(-r-1) <=H_N/(2pi), r>=0. (6e) The first inequality uses integral_0^1 t^(j-1)(-log t)^r dt=r!/j^(r+1). Similarly, for |sigma|<=rho<1 the whole operator germ is at most [1/(1-rho)+H_N]/(2pi). (6f) This applies in the stated nilpotent-contraction metric. No assertion is made that every conjugated interior atom is a contraction in one common physical metric; changing that metric or composing with an unrestricted exterior still requires its actual estimates. The first Mellin pole at the other endpoint is also explicit. The actual small-t expansion starts with Psi(log t)=1+O(t), up to higher logarithmic terms which do not affect this first pole. Therefore Res_(sigma=1) E_sigma(T)=-epsilon T^d/(2pi*i), Res_(sigma=1) h_N(sigma)=N Q^-1/(2pi*i). (6g) Subtract the constant term in the a=d coefficient of (6d); the remaining integral is holomorphic through sigma=1. Every other coefficient is already integrable there. This proves (6g), with its sign and full original normalization. It is a retained source current, not zero. For a fixed ordered collection of such atom endpoints the iterated residues are the corresponding ordered products of T_j^d; their norm is at most one in the supplied contraction metrics. After the displayed normalization-cell pointing their scalar cost is polynomial in N. No reordering of noncommuting atoms is used. For a fixed normalization forest, (6b) bounds an independent normalized multijet by (N/(2pi))^L. If all cells share one normal coordinate, the order-r coefficient has the additional count binom(r+L-1,L-1). Thus even growing normalized jet orders cost only a polynomial in N and r for this fixed forest. These coefficients may be nonzero; they are retained scalar source factors, not declared negligible. ### Sharper pointed estimate at a fixed interior radius There is C_R, independent of N, such that sup_(|sigma|<=1/log(eN)) |h_N(sigma)| <= C_R. (6) Here is a direct proof, including the t=0 endpoint. The exact small-disk full-Psi expansion, with one fixed derivative, gives Psi(log t)/(1-t^N)=a_N(t) exp[-iN phi(t)], phi(t)=Li2(t)/(2pi), ||a_N||_(C^1[0,R])<=C_R, 0<c_R<=phi'(t)<=C_R, |phi''(t)|<=C_R. (7) It follows from the normalized full function, including its central period; the proof and two-derivative version are given in the Markov source note. The finitely many small levels can be absorbed in C_R. Split the integral at 1/N (or at R if R<1/N). On the first interval, with rho=1/log(eN), N integral_0^(1/N) |t^(-sigma) a_N(t)| dt <=C_R N^(Re sigma)/(1-Re sigma)<=C_R. On [1/N,R], integrate the oscillatory exponential once by parts, keeping BOTH endpoint terms. Multiplication by N cancels its 1/N. The endpoint terms are bounded since N^(Re sigma)<=e and R is fixed. The derivative of a_N/phi' gives a bounded integral. The only remaining term is bounded by C_R |sigma| integral_(1/N)^R t^(-Re sigma-1) dt <=C_R |sigma| log N max(1,N^(Re sigma))<=C_R. This proves (6). No claim of pointwise smallness of the original ray has been used, and its lower endpoint contribution is not discarded. In particular Cauchy's formula on that normal disk gives |h_N^(r)(0)| <= C_R r! log(eN)^r, r>=0. (8) For a fixed forest of L cells with independent normal coordinates, the resulting pointed scalar germs are products in the specified operator order. In the scalar radial case their multijets satisfy |partial^nu product_(j=1)^L h_(N,j)(0)| <=C^L product_j(nu_j!) log(eN)^(|nu|). (9) For fixed L and fixed total order this is polynomial (indeed polylogarithmic). Raw derivative orders with |nu| log((|nu|+1)log(eN))=o(N) still cost exp(o(N)); normalized Taylor coefficients need only |nu| log log(eN)=o(N). The conjugate radial integral has the same analytic estimate. The operator-valued pointing assertion here is for the displayed POSITIVE cell. A negative cell may be contracted as its complete original normalization, but no unstated negative arbitrary-channel formula is assumed. In particular no original pivot is replaced by a fresh average. ## 5. Scope for the global contour question This is a source-specific cancellation before positivity, valid with all original spectators and marked data. The full radial current is not thrown away: its pointed scalar and its controlled normal germ remain. The zero-pointing part vanishes as a complete original-source pairing, without assuming a thimble comparison. The operation can remove normalization boundary components even when separate circle/ray pieces individually carry the whole knot rate. It changes individual-state evaluation tests and so evades the genuine obstruction to a UNIVERSAL cotangent chart homotopy. Its hypothesis is the literal visible-cell/forest structure, not merely a rational spectral relation or a matching character value. For genuinely internal head, transfer and alias clusters that structure has not been proved. Their complete currents may not lie in this pointing kernel. No sharp upper bound for the remaining pruned period, no all-face descending cycle, and no original-source lower bound follow from (1)--(9). Extending source-specific contraction to those internal clusters remains substantive work. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normalization_boundary_current.py) checks the operator-valued all-input identity with original crossings, ordinary pivots and marked exteriors, and independently evaluates the full-Psi Mellin current and its first logarithmic normal derivatives.

title: A source-specific backward Ward estimate on shrinking clock disks
text: # A source-specific backward Ward estimate on shrinking clock disks 29 October 2026. The exact normalization packet identified in [the original cup-slide calculation](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md) has a polynomial bound on a disk of radius 1/N about its original clock. This controls the entire clock germ, not only its value. The proof uses an exact backward recurrence; its contraction product cancels the exponential size of the original factorial coefficients. More generally the packet is subexponential on EVERY shrinking disk. This supplies a genuine sharp, zero-exponent estimate for this actual normalization source and for specified sublinear-frequency exterior couplings. It does not prove the hyperbolic-volume bound for an arbitrary braid, or a uniform bound on a different open physical head. ## 1. The original finite polynomial and its exact Ward equation Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j| and H_N(t)=sum_(j=0)^d F_j t^j. (1) Every statement below also holds with Q replaced by its conjugate. Since F_j=(1-Q^j)F_(j-1), and F_N=0 exactly, the polynomial satisfies (1-t)H_N(t)+t Q H_N(Qt)=1. (2) This is an identity of the original finite function. No endpoint remainder, coefficient, or peripheral factor has been discarded. Let k=floor(N/6). The elementary sine sequence obeys min_(0<=j<N) s_j=s_k, s_j s_(d-j)=N, max_j s_j=N/s_k. (3) For the first assertion use s_j/s_(j-1)=2sin(pi*j/N): this ratio is at most one up to N/6, at least one from N/6 to 5N/6, and then at most one. The final value s_d=N exceeds s_0=1. Reflection follows from F_d=N and the complementary conjugate factors, and proves the last assertion, including ties and small N. In particular, for any t with |t-1|<=c/N, |H_N(tQ^r)| <= exp(c) N^2/s_k (4) for every integer r. This coarse bound uses absolute values and is exponential by itself. The next step retains a coherent recurrence before using it. ## 2. Exact backward propagation cancels that exponential Iterate (2) from tQ^(-k) to t. With empty products equal to one, H_N(t)=sum_(r=0)^(k-1) (-1)^r t^(-r-1) Q^[r(r+1)/2] product_(j=1)^r(1-tQ^(-j)) +(-1)^k t^(-k)Q^[k(k-1)/2] product_(j=1)^k(1-tQ^(-j)) H_N(tQ^(-k)). (5) This follows by substitution, so phases as well as moduli remain specified. For k=0 it is simply the original polynomial. Assume 0<c<=N/2 and |t-1|<=c/N. For 1<=j<=k, 4j/N <= |1-Q^(-j)| <= 1, |1-tQ^(-j)| <= |1-Q^(-j)|+c/N. Consequently product_(j=1)^k |1-tQ^(-j)| <=s_k product_(j=1)^k(1+c/(4j)). (6) Also |t|^(-k)<=exp(c/3). For an intermediate product in the sum of (5), its modulus is at most (1+c/N)^r<=exp(c/6). Thus the whole forcing sum has modulus at most 2k exp(2c/3). For b=c/4 and k>0, a decreasing-function integral estimate gives sum_(j=1)^k log(1+b/j) <=integral_0^k log(1+b/u)du =k log(1+b/k)+b log(1+k/b) <=b[1+log(1+k/b)]. (7) Since k/b<=2N/(3c), the combination of (4)--(7) bounds the remainder by exp(19c/12) N^2 (1+2N/(3c))^(c/4). (8) The decisive cancellation is the factor s_k in (6) against 1/s_k in (4). There is no estimated adiabatic eigenbranch or untracked mode conversion in this first-order finite identity. Adding the forcing sum, and treating k=0 directly by (4), proves the uniform, all-level bound SUP_(|t-1|<=c/N) |H_N(t)| <= B_(N,c):=2 exp(2c) N^2 (1+2N/(3c))^(c/4), 0<c<=N/2. (9) A simpler bound sufficient when c is fixed is SUP |H_N(t)| <=2 exp(2c) N^(2+c/4). (10) For (10), use sum_j log(1+c/(4j))<=c H_k/4 and H_k<=1+log(k+1), with k+1<=N, directly in (6). At t=1 the same argument is sharper and especially elementary: |H_N(1)|<= k+N^2. (11) All forcing products then have modulus at most one, and (6) is exactly s_k. Thus this independently bounds the original endpoint sum without a spectral trace formula or a saddle argument. ## 3. Whole shrinking germs and their derivatives If c_N=o(N), equation (9) gives log SUP_(|t-1|<=c_N/N) |H_N(t)|=o(N), (12) as an upper bound: c_N log(1+N/c_N)=o(N), and log N=o(N). More explicitly, the logarithm is at most log 2+2log N+2c_N+(c_N/4)log(1+2N/(3c_N)). (13) For a fixed c>0, ordinary complex Cauchy on this actual holomorphic disk gives, for EVERY integer r>=0, |H_N^(r)(1)|/r! <= B_(N,c) (N/c)^r. (14) The bound is polynomial in N at every fixed normal order. It is also an explicit quantitative estimate when r grows; no claim of subexponential cost is inferred for arbitrary r=O(N). ## 4. The exact original source packet to which the theorem applies The complete physical cup slide gives R12 R23 p=N e0. After the specified terminal R23^2 and actual cap, its recorded rows are b_j=x^(-d) Q^(-j) conjugate(F_j) =x^(-d) Q[conjugate(F_j)-conjugate(F_(j+1))], x=Q^(d/2), conjugate(F_N)=0. (15) Here x has its original mark x=q^d, q=exp(pi*i/N); the notation Q^(d/2) retains that mark. Every full crossing scalar and source factor in (15) is the one in the linked original-source proof. Define Hbar_N(t)=sum_j conjugate(F_j)t^j. The exact phase-generating function of these rows is f_N(t)=sum_j b_j t^j =x^(-d) Q[(1-t^(-1))Hbar_N(t)+t^(-1)]. (16) Its apparent pole at zero is removable. In particular f_N(1)=x^(-d)Q has unit modulus, whereas the full-circle packet energy sum_j|b_j|^2=sum_j s_j^2 is exponential. Thus (9) resolves an actual full-source normalization test that the flat packet norm fails, not merely an arbitrary polynomial example. On the disk of (9), |f_N(t)| <=2+(2c/N) B_(N,c). (17) For the weighted Cayley-arc energy of [the exact Cauchy metric](actual_shrinking_arc_cauchy_metric.md), put t=(1+i a s)/(1-i a s), -1<=s<=1. Then |t-1|<=2a. Choose c=2Na (for large N so that c<=N/2). Equations (12),(17) and (1+a^2s^2)^d<=exp(Na^2) show log E_arc(f_N)=o(N) whenever a=a_N->0. (18) The equality of the exponential rate to zero also uses the exact evaluation lower bound E_arc>=|f_N(1)|^2/kappa_d>=1/N. For a<=C/N the upper bound is polynomial. All fixed derivatives of f_N at one are polynomially bounded as well, by (17) and Cauchy. The original external scalar chi_N, if used, multiplies f_N and its squared energy by chi_N and |chi_N|^2 respectively. It remains explicit. The raw source identity above already retains all common crossing phases; no auxiliary positive invariant is substituted. ## 5. Precise scope of the exterior and global problem For an exposed recorded packet with operator-valued diagonal exterior A_j(t)=sum_(|ell|<=D_N) A_ell(t) Q^(ell*j), its actual contraction is sum_ell A_ell(t) f_N(tQ^ell), with the original order of each spectator operator retained. Since |tQ^ell-1| <= (c_N+2pi D_N)/N, (9),(17) give subexponential norm whenever c_N+D_N=o(N) and sum_ell||A_ell(t)||=exp(o(N)) uniformly. Fixed degrees and fixed polynomial spectator costs give polynomial bounds. This is a statement about the specified exposed RECORDING slot. It is not automatically a uniform estimate for every physical input color of the open normalization tangle. Inserting physical raising or lowering operators can expose a different two-color packet and requires its literal source calculation. Likewise a general original crossing has degree N-1 in the adjacent observable; it is not a sublinear-frequency perturbation covered by this result. For a general exterior sequence A_j the exact Ward equation instead retains the forcing term (1-t)H_A(t)+t Q^(-1)H_A(Q^(-1)t) =A_0+sum_(j=1)^d conjugate(F_j)(A_j-A_(j-1))t^j, H_A(t)=sum_(j=0)^d conjugate(F_j) A_j t^j. (19) Equation (19) follows coefficientwise from the original recurrence. Dropping its finite differences would lose genuine spectator feedback. Controlling this forcing for complete interior crossings, with the geometric exponent, remains part of the broad goal. The present theorem proves source-specific cancellation at a nontrivial normalization germ, not a general hyperbolic knot-volume estimate. ## 6. Where the excessive full-circle energy actually resides The same exact Ward equation also bounds all root samples, so its nonlocal energy is not an unspecified error. Write H_k=H_N(Q^k), H_0=H_N(1), m=floor(N/6). Then H_1=Q^(-1), |H_k|<=N+2N s_(k-1), 1<=k<N. (20) For k<=m+1, forward propagation of (2) from H_1 uses only factors |1-Q^j|<=1 and proves |H_k|<=k. For k>=m+1, backward propagation from H_N=H_0 gives exactly the modulus bound |H_k|<=s_(k-1)[|H_0|/N+sum_(r=k)^d 1/s_r]. (21) After its minimum at m, the sine factorial rises to its unique maximum interval and then decreases to N. Hence min_(r>=k)s_r>=min(s_(k-1),N). Substituting (11) into (21) yields (20). All inverses here have indices strictly between zero and N; no zero root factor is divided out. For the actual normalization polynomial (16), reflection now gives |f_N(Q^r)| <=1+2N+4N^2/s_r, 1<=r<N, |f_N(1)|=1. (22) Indeed Hbar_N(Q^r)=conjugate(H_N(Q^(-r))), and s_(N-r-1)=N/s_r. Thus the full macroscopic clock cost has the uniform leading envelope log |f_N(Q^r)| <= N max{-J(r/N),0}+O(log N), J(u)=integral_0^u log(2sin(pi v))dv. (23) This uses the already proved uniform sine-factorial estimate; at a zero of f it is simply an upper bound. The function -J has its unique maximum c_*=v_3/(2pi) at u=1/6. Finite Plancherel for the original coefficients (15) is exact: sum_(r=0)^d |f_N(Q^r)|^2 =N sum_(j=0)^d |F_j|^2 =exp(2c_*N+O(log N)). (24) Consequently, for every fixed delta>0 small enough to give a proper neighborhood of 1/6, there is eta_delta>0 such that [sum_(|r/N-1/6|>=delta)|f_N(Q^r)|^2] /[sum_r |f_N(Q^r)|^2] <= N^C exp(-eta_delta N). (25) To prove it, use the strict gap of the continuous envelope in (23) off that neighborhood and (24). There are only N samples. No pointwise lower estimate for an individual root sample is needed. Thus the excessive ROOT-SAMPLED Fourier energy of this literal normalization source is concentrated away from t=1, near phase exp(pi*i/3). This discrete concentration statement alone does not prove a corresponding continuum-arc concentration statement. Equations (9),(18) control the original phase neighborhood and its normal germs by a separate uniform complex-disk argument, while (22)--(25) describe the sampled large-phase energy quantitatively. No analogous concentration or local bound is inferred for a general hyperbolic source. There is also a sharp reason to retain the frequency restriction in Section 5. Choose r_N maximizing |f_N(Q^r)|. Equations (23)--(25) and the average in (24) imply r_N/N ->1/6, log |f_N(Q^(r_N))|=N v_3/(2pi)+O(log N). (26) The inserted diagonal clock Q^(r_N j) is UNITARY in the recording space, yet produces this exponential scalar on the known packet. It is an additional observable, not the original closed knot value. Thus mere norm-one control of an arbitrary diagonal exterior cannot replace the sublinear-frequency or geometric conditions in the source estimate. The [independent audit](../experiments/audit_normalization_clock_disk_independent.py) checks exact finite recurrences, all backward phases, factorial reflection and the product/integral bounds at ten levels through N=192, as well as three noncommuting spectator-mode packets. Its 1,152 complex-disk samples supplement the all-disk proof; they are not a numerical supremum certificate. The original physical source identification is separately checked on every input column by the [cup-slide audit](../experiments/audit_actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.py).

title: The original factorial endpoint has a nonzero Gaussian leading term
text: # The original factorial endpoint has a nonzero Gaussian leading term 29 October 2026. The endpoint in the exact normalization/Green source has the following all-level asymptotic, with its phase fixed: \[ P_{N-1}:=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(Q;Q)_j =N^{3/2}\exp\!\left[i\pi\left(\frac14-\frac N{12} +\frac1{4N}\right)\right] +O(\sqrt N),\qquad Q=e^{2\pi i/N}. \tag{1} \] The implied constant is independent of every integer N>=2; no parity or residue class is omitted. In particular |P_(N-1)|>=N^(3/2)/2 for all sufficiently large N. This is a polynomial endpoint lower bound, not a positive hyperbolic-volume rate. Its use below is to keep a nonzero coefficient in an actual neighboring-crossing Green current. ## 1. A finite original-source formula Write d=N-1, q=e^(pi i/N), F_j=(Q;Q)_j. The original source identity already proved in the [terminal Green calculation](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md) is P_d=-q Phi_N(r_N^3), with its full Cartan and pivotal factors. For k=0,...,d put \[ c_k=q^{2k+1}+q^{-2k-1},\quad A_k=q^{2k+1}-q^{-2k-1},\quad \nu_k=(-1)^kq^{k(k+1)}. \] The literal spectral-jet source gives the exact finite formula \[ P_d=\frac q2\sum_{k=0}^{d}\nu_k^3 \left[c_k-\frac32(d-2k)A_k\right]. \tag{2} \] To verify the fold, at every double node the original contribution is -nu_k^3[c_k-3(d-2k)A_k/2] to Phi_N(r_N^3). The index d-k has the SAME c and nu, and the opposite A and d-2k. Thus (2) counts each double contribution exactly once. When N is odd the remaining node has c=-2 and A=0; its half-sum contribution to Phi is precisely nu_k^3, the original simple-node term. N=2 is included. This uses the exact [spectral-jet source proof](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#8-the-actual-closing-trace-is-a-spectral-jet-functional), not a chosen semisimple trace or a fitted endpoint value. Set s_k=(k+1/2)/N, and define fixed smooth functions on [0,1] \[ a(s)=(1-2s)\sin(2\pi s),\qquad b(s)=\cos(2\pi s),\qquad S_N(A)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}A(s_k)e^{i\pi N(3s_k^2+s_k)}. \] Since nu_k^3=-i exp[-3pi i/(4N)] exp[i pi N(3s_k^2+s_k)], (2) becomes EXACTLY \[ P_d=e^{i\pi/(4N)}\left[-\frac{3N}{2}S_N(a)-iS_N(b)\right]. \tag{3} \] In particular every phase needed in (1) is specified before taking a limit. The external original period line, if present, remains external; it is not used to change the finite endpoint (2). ## 2. An elementary half-grid quadratic-sum lemma For a fixed smooth A on [0,1] with A(0)=A(1), finite Fourier inversion of its periodization gives \[ S_N(A)=N\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^m I_{m,N}(A),\qquad I_{m,N}(A)=\int_0^1 A(s) e^{i\pi N[3s^2+(1-2m)s]}\,ds. \tag{4} \] Indeed the periodized function A(s)exp[i pi N(3s^2+s)] is continuous at its endpoints, since exp(4pi iN)=1. Its piecewise smooth derivative has bounded variation, so its Fourier coefficients are absolutely summable: integrating twice, with the possible derivative jump retained, gives O_N((1+|n|)^-2). Summing its Fourier series at s_k keeps exactly the coefficients n=Nm, with factor exp(pi im)=(-1)^m. This proves (4), including the half-grid sign. The following estimates are uniform in m and N and justify its asymptotic use. Only m=1,2,3 have stationary points in (0,1), namely \[ s_m=(2m-1)/6,\qquad 3s^2+(1-2m)s=3(s-s_m)^2-(2m-1)^2/12. \tag{5} \] There is no omitted endpoint resonance: the endpoint derivatives are the odd integers 1-2m and 7-2m, never zero. The endpoint PHASES still matter, and agree exactly at every integer N as used below. If m is outside this set, the phase derivative has absolute minimum delta_m>=c(1+|m|)>0. Two integrations by parts give \[ |I_{m,N}(A)|\le \begin{cases} C_A/(N^2\delta_m^2),& A(0)=A(1)=0,\\ C_A/(N\delta_m^2),& A(0)=A(1). \end{cases} \tag{6} \] For clarity, the first boundary term in the second case is exactly A(0)/(i pi N) times [1/(7-2m)-1/(1-2m)]. Both endpoint phases are one, so this difference is O(delta_m^-2), rather than an unsummable O(|m|^-1). If A vanishes there, that term is zero; the next boundary and integral terms have the stronger N^-2 bound. All derivatives of A in (6) are fixed. Summing the nonstationary terms in (4) therefore costs O(1/N) in the first case and O(1) in the second. At each of the three stationary points choose a fixed smooth cutoff inside (0,1). Completing the square gives \[ I_{m,N}(A)=\frac{e^{i\pi/4}}{\sqrt{3N}} A(s_m)e^{-i\pi N(2m-1)^2/12} +\begin{cases}O(N^{-3/2}),& A(0)=A(1)=0,\\ O(N^{-1}),& A(0)=A(1). \end{cases} \tag{7} \] Here is an elementary error proof. For a compactly supported smooth amplitude B in the centered variable, Fourier inversion and the damped Gaussian integral give \[ \int B(u)e^{3\pi iNu^2}du =\frac{e^{i\pi/4}}{\sqrt{3N}} \int\widehat B(\xi)e^{-i\pi\xi^2/(3N)}d\xi. \] Subtracting B(0)=integral Bhat and using |exp(iv)-1|<=|v| bounds the error by C N^-3/2 integral xi^2|Bhat(xi)|dxi. This integral is finite. The identity follows first with Gaussian damping and then by its limit; compact support and rapid Fourier decay justify that passage. The portion outside the cutoff has no stationary point; the same integrations by parts as (6) give O(N^-2) for zero endpoints and O(N^-1) otherwise. This proves (7) without assuming a selected WKB branch or an asymptotic theorem for a knot invariant. Combining (4),(6),(7), when A has zero endpoints one obtains \[ S_N(A)=e^{i\pi/4}\sqrt{N/3} \sum_{m=1}^3(-1)^m A(s_m)e^{-i\pi N(2m-1)^2/12} +O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{8} \] For a smooth amplitude with matching nonzero endpoints the same formula has error O(1); in particular S_N(A)=O(sqrt N). ## 3. The two surviving Gaussian terms reinforce at every level For a(s) above, \[ a(1/6)=a(5/6)=\sqrt3/3,\qquad a(1/2)=0. \] The half-grid signs for m=1 and m=3 are BOTH minus. Their phases coincide at every integer N, since their quotient is exp(-2pi iN)=1. Thus (8) simplifies to \[ S_N(a)=-\frac23\sqrt N\, e^{i\pi/4-i\pi N/12}+O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{9} \] The function b has matching endpoints, so S_N(b)=O(sqrt N). Substitution in the exact source equation (3) proves (1). There is no parity cancellation between the two leading points, and the possible odd simple node was already retained in (2). ## 4. A quantitative consequence for the actual Green current The original first-order current obeys \[ P_t=F_t^2\left[\frac{P_d}{N^2} -\sum_{r=t+1}^d\frac{Q^r}{F_r^2}\right]. \tag{10} \] If t/N stays in a compact subinterval of (1/2,1), with t<=d, the tail in (10) is O(1/N^2) uniformly. To see this, reflect r=d-k: it is Q^-1/N^2 times a partial sum of Q^-k conjugate(F_k)^2. Here k runs only up to (1/2-delta)N. Its k=0 term is one, and the rest is uniformly bounded: up to a small fixed fraction of N the factorials decrease geometrically, while on a fixed interval below 1/2 they are exponentially small. Thus the partial absolute sum is O(1). This argument needs no cancellation in that reflected short tail. Together with (1), this proves on every such compact interval \[ P_t=\frac{F_t^2P_d}{N^2}\,[1+O(N^{-3/2})],\qquad |P_t|=N^{-1/2}|F_t|^2[1+O(1/N)]. \tag{11} \] The endpoint source in (1) therefore supplies a nonzero polynomial coefficient of the interior factorial current. It does NOT justify dropping that current or bounding it by its tame endpoint. This is the coefficient needed in an all-physical-input neighboring-crossing test; it does not assert that the full closed knot has a positive volume contribution from this sector. ### A sharp all-input normal current of one complete original crossing There is a direct local consequence, with an ordinary original pivotal closure and arbitrary outside spectators retained. Put g_b=theta Q^(-b), theta=x^(1-N), x=q^d, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and define \[ \mathcal M_\pm(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_2[(I\otimes g\,t^J)R_\pm], \qquad J|b\rangle=b|b\rangle . \] This partial trace has NO extra factor1/N. Literal integer-degree conservation makes it diagonal on the remaining physical head. Its complete original coefficients are \[ \mathcal M_+(t)=\kappa\theta\,\operatorname{diag}(D_a(t)),\qquad D_a(t)=F_a^2\sum_{b=0}^a\frac{Q^{b^2}t^b}{F_{a-b}F_b^2}, \tag{12} \] \[ \mathcal M_-(t)=\kappa^{-1}\theta^{-1} \operatorname{diag}\!\left(t^dD_{d-a}^{\overline Q}(t^{-1})\right). \tag{13} \] The superscript in (13) replaces every Q coefficient by Q^(-1). Both known scalar Markov factors have modulus one. For (12), a diagonal positive R coefficient has transfer a-b and value kappa x^(-2b)Q^(b^2)F_a^2/(F_(a-b)F_b^2). The original pivot cancels x^(-2b)=Q^b. The negative formula follows from its literal inverse coefficient by b->d-b and factorial reflection; theta^2Q=1 retains its displayed phase. Thus these are full crossing/source identities, not new favorable traces. They tensor with every spectator identity. The actual finite packets close under a second-order Ward recurrence: \[ D_0=1,\quad D_1=1-Q+Qt,\qquad D_a=(1+Q-2Q^a+Q^{2a-1}t)D_{a-1} -Q(1-Q^{a-1})^2D_{a-2}. \tag{14} \] One coefficient check proves this including all endpoints. For b<a, divide by the nonzero t^b coefficient in D_(a-1), and set u=Q^(a-b), v=Q^b. The required identity is \[ \frac{(1-uv)^2}{1-u} =1-2uv+u+\frac{u^2(1-v)^2}{1-u}. \] The top coefficient b=a is Q^(a^2) on both sides. Initial values therefore show D_a(1)=1 at EVERY physical a. At the other source endpoint, root reflection gives an exact whole-polynomial identity \[ D_d(t)=Qt^d H_N(Q/t),\qquad H_N(z)=\sum_jF_jz^j. \tag{15} \] Its apparent inverse powers cancel, so it is a polynomial. The Ward equation for H_N at one gives Q^2H_N'(Q)=P_d-1, whence \[ u_a:=D_a'(1),\qquad u_0=0,\quad u_d=N-P_d,\qquad u_a-u_{a-1}=Q^aP_{a-1}. \tag{16} \] To verify the last equality directly, differentiate (14); its successive difference obeys v_a=Q(1-Q^(a-1))^2v_(a-1)+Q^(2a-1), v_1=Q. The original Green recurrence identifies v_a=Q^aP_(a-1) exactly. The retained current in (16), rather than a dropped exterior forcing, is what a neighboring crossing generates. The original finite bound |P_j|<=N+4s_j^2 gives \[ \max_a|u_a|\le N^2+4\sum_js_j^2,\qquad |u_a|\le4N^3(1+s_a^2)\quad\text{for every }a. \tag{17} \] Here is a source-aware proof of the pointwise version. Let p=d-floor(N/6) be a factorial maximum index. If a-1<=p, sum (16) forward. The largest factorial on that prefix is at one of its endpoints, so |u_a|<=N^2+4N max(1,s_(a-1)^2). Use s_(a-1)<=N s_a/4. If a-1>p, sum (16) BACKWARD from the literal endpoint u_d=N-P_d; the remaining factorials decrease, giving |u_a|<=N+|P_d|+N^2+4Ns_a^2. The proved bound |P_d|<=N^2+floor(N/6) implies (17), with the generous constant displayed. The negative normal current has the corresponding bound with s_(d-a), by (13). No exponentially conditioned eigenframe is used. Conversely choose p/N->5/6 with p+1<=d. Equation (11) and (16) give \[ \max_a|u_a|\ge\tfrac12|u_{p+1}-u_p| =\tfrac12|P_p|\asymp N^{-1/2}s_p^2. \] The uniform factorial estimate in (17) now proves the SHARP all-input first-normal norm for BOTH original signs: \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \log\|\mathcal M_\pm'(1)\|_{\mathrm{op}} =\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O(\log N).} \tag{18} \] At phase one the same complete operators are only the known scalar Markov units. Nevertheless Cauchy's derivative inequality implies that a uniform subexponential bound on a c/N COMPLEX disk, for every physical input, is impossible. More generally its supremum is at least exp[Nv_3/pi-o(N)] on every radius exp[-o(N)]. This does not contradict the [specific normalization-clock disk theorem](actual_normalization_clock_disk_bound.md): that theorem keeps one specified recording/source packet, not every physical input of an opened normalization tangle. It also does not contradict a bound with the explicit factorial energy (17), a coherent multi-crossing reduction, or a statement on the actual fixed marked source trajectory. No off-phase change of the chosen cut is made here. ## 5. Audit [The independent finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian.py) checks the original factorial sum against the complete spectral-jet formula, the full centered quadratic sum and all source phases. It also checks the nonzero leading normalization and the reflected Green tail on growing levels. These tests supplement the uniform proof in Sections2--3; no lower bound is inferred from a fitted numerical rate. The finite audit checks nine literal full-R-cubed original pivotal sources N=2,...,10, including every open-cut column and the full Cartan scalar; 768 literal signed twisted-Markov polynomial coefficients at ALL physical inputs, their exact Ward recurrences and normal endpoints; thirteen exact quadratic-source/Green/current levels through N=768; and three finite-integral Poisson boundary checks. The latter use an exact finite Gaussian-erf formula with both endpoints, independently checked against direct integration before testing truncated Poisson sums.

title: An actual positive central-sector period for the primitive cube
text: # An actual positive central-sector period for the primitive cube 29 October 2026. For every odd level the all-Steinberg sector of the original ordered cube source is an explicit strictly positive Newton period, times its recorded edge-twist phase. The physical mark, all circle factors and all root normals are retained. The reduction is a generic pivotal contraction followed by a regular specialization; it does not replace the marked source by a Euclidean spin-network norm. This evaluates ONE specified joint channel of the cube. It does not identify the whole color sum with this sector, prove its dominance, handle even levels, or establish a full cube volume conjecture. ## 1. The original cube, its pointing and the statement Put N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), s_0=1, beta(m,r)=s_m/[s_r s_(m-r)], S_N=sum_(r=0)^m beta(m,r)^4, A_N=q^[m(2-m)] S_N, omega_m=kappa(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)], kappa=q^(d^2/2). The exact A_N is the [original odd black source](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md). Use this actual ordered, noncrossing cube, with increasing port orders: black 0:(0,1,2), 1:(3,4,11), 2:(5,9,10), 3:(6,7,8), white 4:(0,10,11), 5:(1,8,9), 6:(2,3,7), 7:(4,5,6). The original unrestricted mark is on the EXPOSED outer cap of white vertex 4. A nested bare mark is not substituted for it. On every edge retain the actual complete-circle sector with j=m, and a fixed signed crossing exponent e_l. This sector is R^(e_l)L_St=omega_m^(e_l) N E_St. Let H_N=C[z]/P_N, P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2, be the complete physical pair commutant, including its double-node normals. Its full original functional and genuine turn are denoted phi and Rturn. Define E_St=the isolated c_m=-2 pair projector, h_N=Rturn(E_St). Then the original RAW marked central-sector cube contribution is Z_cube,St=N^12 S_N^8 phi(h_N^4) omega_m^(sum_(l=0)^11 e_l), (1) and phi(h_N^4)>0 (2) at every odd N>=3. External line/framing normalizations, if present in the original invariant, remain external to (1). No factor depending on an ordinary root quantum dimension is divided out after it has been specialized to zero. ## 2. The generic cups, cyclic clocks and the literal rung reduction All generic statements in this section use zeta before root specialization, with Q=zeta^2 and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. On highest weight L use the canonical cup with FIRST coefficient one: P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)] F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). The actual physical highest-d cup is instead pV(u,d-u)=N zeta^(-d^2)P_d(u). (3) It specializes exactly to the recorded root physical cup. Both its factorials and its overall scalar are retained. In particular the genuine generic turn of a pair map A is (Rturn_zeta A)_((u,b);(v,e)) =pV(d-e)/pV(d-u) A_((d-u,v);(b,d-e)). (4) Its root simplification x^(u-e) is NOT continued generically. The global scalar in (3) cancels in (4), but its factorial ratios do not. Let W:V_d->V_d tensor V_d be the generic ordinary Clebsch map of spin (m,m;m), whose first highest entry is one. Put eta=D(W)W, where D is the genuine bilinear pivotal dual, with reversed abstract dual order. The finite unequal-Clebsch norm calculation in [the four-port kernel](actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.md), equations (4)--(6), gives eta_m=(-1)^m zeta^[-m(3m+1)] F_(3m+1)/(F_m F_(2m+1)). That calculation is the coefficient of a single contiguous product of reciprocal finite Pochhammers, not a fitted norm. Write a_m=(-1)^m zeta^[-m(m+3)], Theta=(W tensor I)p_d/a_m, e_m=W D(W)/eta_m, c_m=eta_m/a_m^2. (5) Thus Theta(2m,m,0)=1, exactly the canonical ordered invariant used in the first-normal source theorem. Equations (3)--(5) involve two uses of the same highest-d object: its ordinary canonical cup in Theta, and its scaled physical cup in the original source. These are not conflated. The scale cancels in the turn and every closed cup/cap snake, while the physical source factors are kept below.
