Likewise the explicit nonzero finite sample of the fiber residue in that theorem is only a sample of the underlying form. It does not show that the actual quantum period has degree (n_0,n_1). There is a useful CONDITIONAL sampling corollary. Suppose a specified closed cycle on EVERY canonical first-head fiber has the SAME integer winding pair (m_0,m_1) about R=0,1. Its underlying fiber period is 2pi i c_D(m_1+q0 m_0)/s_a, where A_a=q0 Q0^a and s_a=A_a^-1-1. Keeping the original coherent sample and its normalization gives exactly 2pi i c_D(m_1+q0 m_0) G_N(t)/kappa_N(t), G_N(t)=sum_a beta_a(t)/s_a. (8a) For real t, Re G_N=-1/2; on any fixed interior real t compact, |kappa_N|<=C/N. Thus a nonzero common pair gives a lower bound c|c_D| in (8a), even if m_1=-m_0!=0. This is algebra of the SPECIFIED underlying cycles; their realization by the quantum source is not proved. A restricted window is not covered without an explicit bound for its weighted remainder: a small binomial tail alone does not bound unspecified winding integers on the discarded fibers. Uniform matching is also separate: at r=N rho, the actual q-retained symbol has size N^-1, and separate O(N^-1) errors in the two quantum bands do not determine their normalized difference. For a relative chain, (6) retains the boundary term (1-q0)c_D integral_(boundary Gamma) lambda. Its argument integrals need not be integers. Every source-divisor tube, the primitive cotangent measure, the finite-head carries and the retained Poisson characters must be transported with that chain. The [H-period theorem](actual_root_channel_H_period_transport.md) gives explicit corrections for the two normal insertions; it does not provide the missing geometric pushforward or its ends. There is no known identification of those integers with the original physical head cycle. If Psi and g_0,g_1 extend as nonvanishing functions over a particular small head polydisk, its local torus has zero degree by contraction within that disk. This observation has that EXPLICIT regular-extension hypothesis; it says nothing about integer nodes where source or geometric divisors degenerate. An N-head carry fixes the physical clocks, so it does not by itself assign degree one. Nonzero winding can only be asserted after the actual pushforward and its relative end/divisor terms have been computed. Thus the new checkable criterion is precise: for an explicitly constructed CLOSED underlying framed cycle, a nonzero pair (n_0,n_1) prevents cancellation in (7). For the original invariant one must additionally justify its weighted quantum realization. ## 5. Class-wide geometric and long-twist quantifiers Fix k>=2 and a finite ordered 2k-plat skeleton D, with every crossing in a designated two-strand box, actual cups/caps, cut, primitive crossing-disk markings, and fixed half twists epsilon_i in {0,+1,-1}. Combine adjacent powers of the same generator before treating their full twists as independent. The outside terminal matching together with the parity restoration must be one cycle. This finite test ensures that all exponents epsilon_i-2p_i give knots; full twists do not change connectivity. Here k is a presentation width, not a claim of minimal bridge number. For geometry alone, the least restrictive proved sufficient input is an [actual positive marked gluing certificate](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md): the correct labeled manifold quotient, torus links, positive shapes, complex edge equations and complete primitive peripheral equations. It proves the complete metric and volume of the actual marked exterior. The current common boundary-chart route uses the STRONGER labeled right-angled certificate of the [matching-graph theorem](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Its ideal vertices and supporting Lorentz normals have the original medial incidence, strict nonincident inequalities, and orthogonal adjacent face normals. The actual white-reflection prefixes and signed shaded pairings are retained. These are finite algebraic equalities/strict inequalities on supplied exact data. The certificate constructs a positive marked triangulation; the reverse implication has not been proved. There is no restriction to a Conway tree or to one fixed width, but existence of such data for EVERY essential hyperbolic augmented plat is not asserted. No EXTRA noncommuting-route hypothesis is needed in that class. At an actual complete box Tr A=Tr B=Tr BA=-2, so its punctures cannot all preserve the reference cusp flag. The literal Hurwitz routes and induction in the odd-period theorem therefore supply a fixed routed first head with c!=0. Its exact source-preserving odd observable, nonzero kappa_N, and the nontrivial forms (4),(6) are now proved at arbitrary fixed width. This removes the old need to POSTULATE an orientation-sensitive observable representing the same scalar. It removes none of the original global-cycle or mixed-color asymptotic hypotheses. The [geometric filling corollary](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) already supplies T_geom(D) for all independently long signed fillings, and all partial subsets, under the positive marked certificate. The full conjecture remains: for every fixed essential hyperbolic augmented D as above, there exists T(D) such that for EVERY FIXED integer vector p with all |p_i|>T(D), lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N(K_D(p))| =Vol(S3 minus K_D(p)). (9) The broad conjecture assumes hyperbolicity of the actual augmented exterior; it is not restricted to diagrams already carrying our right-angled certificate. The present boundary construction applies to the certified subclass and does not prove that certificate exists for every diagram in the conjecture. Both level parities and composite levels are included. Signs and relative slope magnitudes are unrestricted. The slopes are fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity; thresholds may depend on the entire D, not just k. No uniform statement for p=p(N) follows. The existing [source-to-filling theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) proves (9) CONDITIONALLY on the original uniform complex external-color packet, its nonzero contracted amplitude, full alias/normal/color gap, and actual marked geometric action selection. A unit amplitude, or a controlled coordinate monomial times a unit, gives every long tuple. A merely nonzero germ permits an exceptional analytic divisor, as the [source-divisor theorem](general_long_filling_source_divisor.md) states. The internal Casimir deficits N-1-2a_i controlled by the boundary envelope are not the external filling-color defects N-j_i. The new logarithmic integer criterion isolates a concrete part of the needed cycle calculation; it is not a replacement for that packet or its global complementary-color estimate. This elementary note has no separate numerical audit. Its identities follow by the displayed changes of variables, Stokes argument and integer-degree calculation; the finite source and routed geometry are audited in the cited odd-period theorem. The logarithmic-class calculation supplies neither the geometric winding nor a mixed-color packet. The logarithmic criterion remains separate from the actual weighted quantum cycle and the three-manifold regulator.

title: The original odd pretzel and its complete mixed-circle transfer source
text: # The original odd pretzel and its complete mixed-circle transfer source 29 October 2026. The literal original turns and disjoint twist boxes give an exact cyclic transfer formula for EVERY odd number of odd pretzel boxes. It keeps one unwrapped integer charge, the entire marked row and all original crossing-circle normal channels. It is not a replacement by a Jones polynomial, a TV state, or an AK integral. The formula is a concrete source for the arbitrary-region augmented pretzel survival question. Its complete-color base does not become entrywise positive by a diagonal phase gauge, even after retaining the half twists. A positive reflected network or an original relative-cycle calculation still needs proof. ## 1. Diagram, signs and literal original source Use \(N\geq2,d=N-1,q=e^{\pi i/N},Q=q^2,x=q^d\). Label \(2s\) vertical heads from left to right. Box \(i\) acts on heads \((2i-1,2i)\). At BOTH ends the planar matching is \[ (1,2s),(2,3),(4,5),\ldots,(2s-2,2s-1). \tag{1} \] The outer bottom turn is the original \(p_{a_1,b_s}\); the other bottom turns are \(p_{b_i,a_{i+1}}\). At the top the inner turns are \(\ell_{d_i,c_{i+1}}\), and the outer turn is the sole original marked row \(m_{c_1,d_s}\). All port orders here are part of the definition, including that of the nested outer turn. The original formulas are \[ p_{uv}=N x^{-v}\mathbf1_{u+v=d},\quad \ell_{uv}=x^u/N\,\mathbf1_{u+v=d},\quad m_{uv}=x^v/N^2. \tag{2} \] In particular \(m\) has NO degree indicator before the contraction. For degree-preserving physical boxes \(B_i\), define the RAW marked source \(\mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s)\) by this tensor diagram. Its original peripheral/framing line \(\chi_N\) remains outside it. For odd box integers \(n_i\), the usual odd pretzel diagram is (1) with \(B_i=R^{-n_i}\), with this explicit crossing convention. Choosing \(R^{n_i}\) instead gives the global mirror. This fixes the sign by the one-crossing boxes: rotating their original cup/cap diagrams and applying the two snake identities concatenates them into the literal central \(s\)-crossing four-plat, with no curl. Thus the all-\(n_i=1\) raw source agrees with the original four-plat \(\sigma_2^s\). This is an equality of the specified tangle sources, not an identification inferred from a colored polynomial. There is one component when \(s\) is odd. Indeed each odd box has the swap permutation of its two endpoints. Following the two planar matchings advances the box index by two modulo \(s\). For odd \(s\) this visits every box; for even \(s\) there are two components. This proof is independent of the odd twist magnitudes and signs. We use only odd \(s\geq3\), so the sole marked source is an admissible original one-component cut. Reduction, hyperbolicity and long filling are further topological hypotheses, not consequences of this source formula. ## 2. Exact unwrapped-charge transfer theorem For \(-d\leq h\leq d\) put \[ I_h=\{\max(0,h),\ldots,\min(d,d+h)\},\quad D_h=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in I_h}x^{2a}, \] \[ M_i^{(h)}[a,a'] =x^{-2a+h} (B_i)_{(a-h,\,d-a'+h);\,(a,\,d-a')}, \qquad a,a'\in I_h. \tag{3} \] These are finite physical matrix entries; no cyclic index is allowed. Then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s) =\frac{x^{(s-1)d}}N \sum_{h=-d}^d\operatorname{Tr} \bigl(D_hM_1^{(h)}\cdots M_s^{(h)}\bigr).} \tag{4} \] The statement holds for arbitrary degree-preserving boxes on their specified physical pairs, not merely for one eigenchannel or for root-sampled continuations. In particular it includes every actual signed power of \(R\), every literal mixed-color circle, and their products. Proof. Write the inputs of box \(i\) as \((a_i,b_i)\), its outputs as \((c_i,d_i)\). The bottom source forces \(b_i=d-a_{i+1}\), cyclically, where the exceptional outer source has the ordered coefficient \(p_{a_1,b_s}\). The inner caps force \(d_i=d-c_{i+1}\), \(i<s\). The total input degree is \(sd\); each \(B_i\) preserves its actual integer degree. Therefore the remaining outer pair has \(c_1+d_s=d\), including when evaluated against the FULL marked row (2). Only now may that forced equality be used to write \(d_s=d-c_1\). Each box conservation equation is now \[ a_i-a_{i+1}=c_i-c_{i+1}. \] Thus \(h=a_i-c_i\) is a common UNWRAPPED integer, and each \(a_i\) lies exactly in \(I_h\). No mod-\(N\) aliases have been introduced or discarded. The total turn coefficient before using this conservation law is \[ \frac1N x^{(s-1)d+2a_1-\sum_i a_i-\sum_i c_i} =\frac{x^{(s-1)d}}N x^{2a_1} \prod_i x^{-2a_i+h}. \tag{5} \] The \(N^{-1}\) in (5) is exactly \(N^s/N^{s+1}\) from the cups, ordinary caps and single marked cap. Summing the resulting cyclic product gives (4). This proves the literal source normalization; there is no new trace average of size \(N^{s}\) or \(2N\). ## 3. Simultaneous original full-twist filling For \(n_i=2p_i+1\), keep the half twist \(R^{-1}\) and use the already proved ALL-INPUT circle kernel on \(R^{-2p_i}\): \[ R^{-n_i}=\kappa^{-2p_i}\sum_{j=1}^N \beta_{N,-2p_i,j}\,R^{-1}L_j, \qquad\sum_j|\beta_{N,-2p_i,j}|\leq2N(1+|p_i|). \tag{6} \] Every \(L_j\) is the ordinary \(j\)-dimensional mixed auxiliary circle with its original pivot, not an extra complete component identified by a quotient lemma. Define \[ \mathcal A_{s,N}(j_1,\ldots,j_s) =\mathcal A_{s,N}(R^{-1}L_{j_1},\ldots,R^{-1}L_{j_s}). \] Equations (4) and (6) give the exact original pretzel scalar \[ K_N=\chi_N\prod_i\kappa^{-2p_i} \sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_s}\left(\prod_i\beta_{N,-2p_i,j_i}\right) \mathcal A_{s,N}(j_1,\ldots,j_s). \tag{7} \] The \(\chi_N\) here is the original filled pretzel's line. It is not replaced by a guessed normalization or framing of the augmented diagram. For each fixed \(s\) the coefficient mass is at most \(\prod_i2N(1+|p_i|)\). The formula treats arbitrary odd \(s\), so it is not restricted to bounded braid width or one variable slope. Its large-\(N\) constants may depend on the fixed diagram \(s\). ## 4. Exact complete-base channel formula and a positivity test At complete circle colors every box is the SAME \(B_*=R^{-1}L_N\). Hence (4) becomes a sum of weighted powers \(\operatorname{Tr}(D_h(M_*^{(h)})^s)\). The [positive reflected-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) gives a complete all-degree expansion of \(B_*P\). In a low total degree block \(T\), its coefficients are \[ B_*P=\sum_jh_{T,j}(\kappa\nu_j)^{-1}v_{T,j}v_{T,j}^*, \quad h_{T,j}>0, \tag{8} \] including the odd simple node and every even-level normal channel. Thus the transfer (3) retains the HALF-TWIST phase \((\kappa\nu_j)^{-1}\); it is not the plain PSD matrix \(L_NP\). Its two physical ports can belong to different total degrees \(T=d+a-a'\). A partial transpose or reshuffling of the PSD matrix is not assumed positive. For an exact illustration, at \(N=3,h=0\) the literal transfer is \[ M_*^{(0)}= \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac92+\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2i&-\tfrac32-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2i&0\\ 3&\tfrac{21}2+\tfrac{9\sqrt3}2i&-\tfrac32+\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2i\\ 0&-\tfrac32-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}2i&9 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{9} \] Its diagonal entries do not have a common phase. No scalar and diagonal similarity can therefore make this matrix entrywise nonnegative or Hermitian positive. This is a failure of that specific Perron/diagonal-gauge shortcut, not an obstruction to a coherent reflected-source formula or geometric survival. The complete raw base scalar at \(N=3,s=3\), including ALL charges in (4), is exactly \[ \mathcal A_{3,3}(3,3,3)=-189+81\sqrt3\,i. \tag{10} \] Its nonzero value is an exact source check. It is not an all-level nonvanishing theorem, an asymptotic volume calculation, or a proof that its geometric coefficient is nonzero. Establishing an original positive reflected base or a selected relative cycle in an open cusp-color corridor remains the geometric step. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.py) compares (4) with direct physical tensor contraction, all single crossing pretzels with the original central four-plat, mixed-circle ports and the simultaneous filling, and reconstructs (9)--(10) over the exact quadratic field.

title: The actual Fourier source reduces exactly to one exterior index
text: # The actual Fourier source reduces exactly to one exterior index Research theorem, 27 October 2026. For the original root family the fully reclosed one-cut operator is scalar. Hence ANY fixed first input column, paired with the original output row, gives the original period. Applied to the actual second-wire Fourier polarization, this removes the first exterior average exactly and leaves one finite Fourier-label sum. A whole actual Ward homotopy records every normal defect of this source reduction; off-root scalarity is not assumed. ## 1. The scalar root closure and its precise source Use the actual nilpotent color at q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, with M left as its original meridian parameter. In the balanced head frame K=x diag(Q_N^(-j)), x=-M/q_N, F_(j+1,j)=1-Q_N^(j+1), 0<=j<N-1. The original signed local crossings intertwine the true coproduct. Closing every other strand with its original root pivotal cap therefore makes the one-cut matrix C_N(M) a module endomorphism. The literal closure proof, including the root cap and all full peripheral factors, is given in [the closed-braid period construction](closed_braid_period_line.md), Sections 2--3. No extra pivot is attached at the opened identity wire. One can prove scalarity directly with just the actual K and F rows. Distinct K eigenvalues make C_N diagonal. The F commutator then gives (1-Q_N^k)(C_(k-1,k-1)-C_(k,k))=0, 1<=k<N. Every prefactor is nonzero, so all entries agree. This proves C_N(M)=P_N(M) I. (1.1) If C_N includes the original external d_N, then P_N=d_N F_N; if that line is recorded externally, P_N=F_N. Use the SAME choice on every side. The equality first holds on the admissible generic M chart and continues as its actual rational-map/source-lattice identity. It includes every regular complete value M=1. It does not invert a peripheral norm-zero factor or assert off-root q scalarity of the compressed auxiliary family. Let 1 denote the all-ones column, and retain the actual source Phi(C)=(1/N)1^t C 1, lambda_a(C)=1^t C e_a=sum_c C_(c,a). (1.2) Equation (1.1) proves, for EVERY a in the physical head, lambda_a(C_N)=Phi(C_N)=P_N. (1.3) This fixes only the INPUT column. The output row still sums all c. It is not the diagonal source E_aa when applied to current tensors. ## 2. One remaining Fourier-label sum, with its original normalization For the literal two-cut tensor let T^V=(I tensor V)T(I tensor V^-1), V_(j,b)=Q^(jb), Jtilde_(a,j)=sum_c T^V_(c,j;a,j). Use the WHOLE actual inverse from [the Vandermonde source theorem](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md). Its exact partial-trace identity gives, even before specializing Q, sum_j Jtilde_(a,j)=lambda_a(C). (2.1) At the actual root the scalar closure therefore proves P_N(M)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Jtilde_(a,j)(M) (2.2) for ANY chosen first input a. There is no remaining first average and no extra 1/N outside this last sum. The inverse Fourier matrix still supplies its own 1/N INSIDE each raw Jtilde. For charge-zero T, Jtilde_(a,j)=(1/N)sum_(b,q) Q_N^(jq)T_(a-q,b+q;a,b). (2.3) Thus fixing a does not force q=0 and does not remove the second momentum coordinate. The original first output row is essential. The specified proper-root partial lift with Q^(jq)/N has the same values in (2.2) at every original root. Off root its inverse need not equal V(Q)^-1. Equation (2.1) with the whole inverse and (2.2) with the root/proper-root inverse have these stated different scopes. Their q-normal source jets are not silently identified. ## 3. A whole balanced Ward contraction for the source change This section is an exact finite-matrix identity, before jets. It uses the actual balanced finite K,F matrices at whole Q,M. Put D_K(C)=K C K^-1-C, D_F(C)=F C-K^-1 C K F, delta C=(D_K(C),D_F(C)), p(C)=Tr C/N. (3.1) At a genuine Hopf fiber these are the actual Hopf-adjoint rows. Elsewhere (3.1) remains its specified compressed finite-matrix formula; its whole network defects must be retained. Work only over the localization where Q^l-1 is a unit for 0<|l|<N. These units do not invert 1-Q^N. For X=(X_K,X_F), set O(X)_(i,j)=(X_K)_(i,j)/(Q^(j-i)-1), i!=j, O(X)_(i,i)=0, d_k(X)=(X_F)_(k,k-1)/(1-Q^k), 1<=k<N. Let Q_k be the centered diagonal step (Q_k)_(i,i)=(N-k)/N-1_(i>=k), h(X)=O(X)+sum_(k=1)^(N-1) d_k(X) Q_k. (3.2) Off-diagonal recovery is immediate from D_K. The selected F entry has NO off-diagonal pollution, since both left F and right F have only one arrow in that direction: (D_F C)_(k,k-1) =(1-Q^k)(C_(k-1,k-1)-C_(k,k)). (3.3) Telescoping the centered steps proves the WHOLE identity h delta C=C-p(C)I, p h=0, delta I=0. (3.4) In particular the actual image complex End -> im delta contracts onto the scalar line. No cokernel assertion is made for the entire unrestricted two-row space. No integral-factorial basis change has been introduced; this is the original balanced head. Write Q_a=e_a 1^t, e=(1/N)1 1^t, gamma_a(C)=lambda_a(C)-Phi(C)=Tr[(Q_a-e)C], b_a(X)=gamma_a(h(X)). Since gamma_a(I)=0, applying gamma_a to (3.4) gives lambda_a-Phi=b_a delta (3.5) as an exact WHOLE source/current identity. For the actual reclosed matrix this says sum_j Jtilde_(a,j)-Phi(C)=b_a(delta C). (3.6) At its root Hopf fiber delta C_N=0, so (3.6) becomes (2.2). For whole q/M auxiliary arrays, or inserted Green/current coupons, the right side records the actual remaining closure/current row; it is not discarded by an off-root Schur argument. Normal derivatives follow by differentiating (3.5). In Taylor coefficients at any specified actual normal path, gamma_a(C_n)=sum_(i+j+k=n) (b_a)_i delta_j(C_k). (3.7) This includes the derivatives of the whole operators, source and unit denominators. For an uninserted scalar C_0 at first order, delta_1(C_0)=0 because delta_t(I)=0 for all t, and delta_0 C_0=0. Hence gamma_a(C_1)=(b_a)_0 delta_0(C_1). A current insertion with nonscalar C_0 retains the other terms in (3.7). On a full diagram use the original ordered Hopf/coprod and pivotal row, including prefixes, to evaluate delta C. The whole frozen pivotal cap is chi^-1 ptr_K M_(Z^J), not ptr_K by itself, with Z=Q^N. Its exact moment-clock and divided rows are retained in [the actual cap theorem](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md). This source homotopy does not set those cap/Green endpoints to zero. ## 4. A polynomial root bound in the original balanced metric Give the balanced head its flat positive metric and End its Hilbert--Schmidt norm, with the orthogonal product norm on the two current rows. The K-row inverse gap at Q_N is bounded by 1/[2 sin(pi/N)] <= N/4. (4.1) For the diagonal part integrate edge gradients from the middle vertex m=floor(N/2), then subtract the mean. This is the SAME centered step operator in (3.2); only its norm estimate changes. For left edges k<=m, 1/|1-Q_N^k| <= N/(4k). The relevant tail-sum matrix is A_(i,k)=1/k for 1<=i<=k<=m. With weights w_i=i^(-1/2), elementary sums give sum_(k>=i) A_(i,k)w_k <=3w_i, sum_(i<=k) A_(i,k)w_i <=2w_k. The weighted Cauchy--Schwarz inequality then gives ||A||<=sqrt(6)<3. The right half has the same estimate with k replaced by N-k. The two edge sets and anchored outputs are disjoint; subtracting the mean is orthogonal projection. Thus ||h_diag|| <=3N/4, ||h||<=3N/4. (4.2) For completeness the matrix bound follows by writing |sum_k A_ik x_k|^2 <= (sum_k A_ik w_k) sum_k A_ik |x_k|^2/w_k and then summing i. This proves the estimate without importing a Hardy inequality. Complex reciprocal phases are bounded by the same positive kernel. No q-factorial condition number has been omitted. The original row difference has exactly ||Q_a-e||_HS=sqrt(N-1). Consequently its actual source primitive satisfies ||b_a|| <=(3N/4)sqrt(N-1). (4.3) These are root metric bounds for this specified Ward/source map, not bounds on the whole word or the geometric quantum period. They make no uniform-neighborhood estimate for its normal units. ## 5. Choosing a good first-position anchor at every large level Assume the established geometric framing model has a nonempty regular algebraic chart for (A,p_e), with nondegenerate Fourier normal block as in [the actual Fourier construction](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md). This is its stated complete positive geometric/marked branch input, not a new conclusion from (1.1). Over the fixed marked representation/half-density cover, remove every denominator and critical discriminant used for that chart. These are finitely many nonzero algebraic functions on its selected connected component. For a finite algebraic marking cover, take their nonzero field norms first, then clear denominators on the rational (A,p_e) chart. Since A=1/(1+s) is a nonconstant framing coordinate, only FINITELY many A-values have their entire fiber excluded. Explicitly, clear denominators of each defining function as a polynomial in the other coordinate; a fiber is identically zero only when all its coefficient polynomials in A vanish. They have finitely many common roots. Choose a root of unity A_*=exp(2pi*i p/d) outside that finite set, with 0<p<d, gcd(p,d)=1. Its finite marked-cover lifts are retained. There is no assertion that the particular choice A_*=-1 is good for every knot. Set a_N=floor(pN/d), r_N=pN-d a_N in {0,...,d-1}. Then a_N is an original physical head index, and A_N=Q_N^(a_N)=A_* exp[-(r_N/d)H_N], H_N=2pi*i/N. (5.1) Along each residue class of N modulo d, r_N is constant. The classes may be refined by every previously retained parity/phase modulus; no existing root sign or source branch is reset. The selected good geometric point deforms on its fixed marked cover to A_N for all sufficiently large N; the remaining framing/ Fourier coordinate is still free on a nonempty open. Formula (2.2) therefore computes the SAME original root period using a good fixed first-position sequence and just one exterior j sum. Existence of this formal geometric branch does not prove its survival in that last selected finite sum. The WHOLE clock before normal differentiation is A=Z^(p/d) Q^(-r_N/d), Z=Q^N, (5.2) on its MARKED power cover: the root value of Z^(p/d) is A_*. One may realize it with v^d=Q, W^d=Z, W=v^N and A=W^p v^(-r_N). This equals Q^(a_N) exactly on the actual power graph. Keeping Z and its phase branch is essential. Replacing its marked value by the constant A_* FIRST would lose D_Q log A=a_N, and would give only -r_N/d instead. Thus residue-class root selection does not identify off-root q-normal germs. Equation (3.7) and the whole inverse must be used for those germs. ## 6. Scalarity is necessary, and the source is not a diagonal probe There is an actual WHOLE auxiliary counterexample even for the one-positive-crossing unknot. At N=2 use x=-M/q, Q=q^2 and remove only the common Cartan scalar as in the actual residual matrices. In the ordinary F-shift frame its checked crossing is Rplus=[[1,0,0,0], [0,0,x^-1,0], [0,x^-1,1-x^-2,0], [0,0,0,Q*x^-2]]. The frozen cap is g=x^-1 diag(1,Q); the original zero-framing multiplier is theta^-1=x. Taking the literal partial trace gives C(Q,M)=d_2(M)diag(1,1+Q(Q^2-1)/M^2), d_2(M)=i M/(1+M^2). (6.1) The balanced diagonal frame does not change this diagonal cut. At Q=-1 it equals d_2(M)I, including the original complete value. Nevertheless the whole source difference and its first normal are gamma_0 C=-d_2(M) Q(Q^2-1)/(2M^2), D_Q(gamma_0 C)|_(Q=-1)=d_2(M)/M^2 !=0. (6.2) Here M is held fixed and the original phase i is fixed. At M=1 this normal value is i/2. Equation (3.5) reproduces (6.2) exactly from (D_F C)_(1,0)/(2(1-Q)). Thus the whole Ward row genuinely survives differentiation; scalar root closure cannot erase it. Using the ordinary generic ribbon cap instead of the specified frozen auxiliary cap would be a different off-root source. For the literal two-cut unknot T is the flip. Inserting the actual matrix-unit coupon X=E_00 at the second identity wire gives the one-cut matrix C=X. Its selected average is Phi(C)=1/N, whereas lambda_0(C)=1, lambda_a(C)=0 for a!=0. The fixed-input reduction therefore fails without scalarity. Its exact discrepancy is (3.5), with the nonzero F/K current of that specified coupon. Similarly a charged C=E_(c,a), c!=a, has lambda_a(C)=1 while its diagonal probe at a is zero. Removing the output sum would change the current/source problem even when the eventual uninserted knot matrix is scalar. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_one_index_fourier_source.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_one_index_fourier_source_results.json) check the whole two-row contraction and sources, actual signed root braid/Fourier tensors at complete and generic meridians, off-root current defects, metric bounds and marked clock exponents. No hyperbolic-volume or global selected-cycle conclusion is claimed.

title: A triangle upper bound for every one-sided relative-energy coefficient
status: Uniform general coefficient-energy bound by a triangle
text:
# A triangle upper bound for every one-sided relative-energy coefficient 31 October 2026. **local theorem.** Every actual LEFT or RIGHT coefficient has relative spectral energy bounded by one complete-triangle entropy, uniformly through both parities and all closed degree boundaries. The original middle degrees remain unchanged. A shared global entropy comparison is a separate problem. Use the actual coefficient and reference conventions in the [endpoint-conditioned source theorem](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md). For a nonnegative triangle load of total one half, put $$ C(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=\sum_{j=1}^3f(\alpha_j),\qquad f(t)= rac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}\pi, \quad \Lambda(a)=-\int_0^a\log|2\sin u|\,du. $$ If an actual one-sided exponent is \(v=(v_x,v_b,v_c,v_y)\), write \(q=v/(N-1)\). The result is $$  oxed{\displaystyle \sup_{\substack{v	ext{ one-sided}\\sigma\in[-2,2]}} \left[  rac1N\log rac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} -C(q_x,q_y,	frac12-q_x-q_y)ight]\le o(1).} 	ag{T} $$ Zero coefficients have logarithm minus infinity. The error is uniform; the outer sum is at most one half on either original one-sided support. Protected incidences retain their exact zero targets. ## 1. Positive dependence on a single spectral parameter Write $	heta=\pi/N$, $s_j=2\sin(j	heta)$, and normalize the original tail by $$ q_{i,j}=K_{i,j}/\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r^2. $$ It satisfies $q_{i,i}=1$, $q_{i,i+1}=x+y$, and $$ q_{i,j}=(x+y)q_{i,j-1}+(\eta_j-1)xyq_{i,j-2}, \quad \eta_j= rac{\lambda}{d_j}, \quad d_j=\cos	heta-\cos((2j-1)	heta)>0, \quad \lambda=\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta). 	ag{1} $$ The actual start has $j\geq i+2$ in the last term, so no zero sine denominator occurs. On the entire interval $0\leq\delta\leq1/2$, one has $|\lambda|\leq\lambda_0=1+\cos	heta$ for $N\geq3$. The parameter $\lambda$ may be negative near the last spectral endpoint. For an interval of length $r=j-i$, expand the continuant in the parameters $\eta$. A chosen set of disjoint edges contributes $(xy)^{|S|}\prod_{e\in S}\eta_e$. The remaining vertex intervals contribute their baseline continuants $$ h_\ell(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}x^ky^{\ell-k}, $$ which solve (1) with $\eta=0$. Thus every outer coefficient $q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)=[x^ky^{r-k}]q_{i,j}$ is a polynomial in $\lambda$ with nonnegative coefficients. This expansion follows by grouping the selected $\eta$ terms in the usual matching expansion of a tridiagonal determinant; the deleted-edge complements are disjoint intervals. Let $\lambda_0=1+\cos	heta$. Cauchy applied to these nonnegative polynomial coefficients gives the exact finite inequality for **every real** $\lambda$ $$  rac{|q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)|^2}{q_{i,j,k}(\lambda_0)} \leq q_{i,j,k}\left( rac{\lambda^2}{\lambda_0}ight). 	ag{2} $$ Indeed, if $q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)=\sum_r c_r\lambda^r$ with $c_r\geq0$, use the vectors $\sqrt{c_r}\lambda^r/\lambda_0^{r/2}$ and $\sqrt{c_r}\lambda_0^{r/2}$. The first may have signed entries; Cauchy still applies. It is a coefficient inequality for the actual tail, not a positivity assertion for the original tail on the final spectral cap. It does not assume real negative roots or a coefficient central-limit theorem. ## 2. The original prefix and suffix normalization For the actual LEFT exponent $v=(k,i,d-j,r-k)$, write, up to a common unit sign, $a_N(v;\sigma)=B_N(\delta)q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)$ with $\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)$. Here $B_N$ contains the exact omitted-half scalar, all unused lower prefix and suffix diagonals, and $\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r^2$. The original endpoint reference is $p_N(v)=B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}q_{i,j,k}(\lambda_0)$, $B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}>0$. At even levels the reference is $-V_N(-2)$; at odd levels it is $V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2)$. For a one-sided odd path the central zero is unused, so the derivative removes precisely that zero; its remaining normalization has only polynomial size. Bare odd $V_N(-2)$ is not the reference. Consequently (2) implies $$ \sum_{k=0}^{r} rac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)}x^ky^{r-k} \leq rac{|B_N(\delta)|^2}{B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}} q_{i,j}\left(x,y;\lambda^2/\lambda_0ight). 	ag{3} $$ All unused local rows remain in $B_N$; the original external character and marked source targets are unchanged. We will estimate (3) by the uniform tail upper bound and logarithmic prefix/suffix estimates in [the global CROSS proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md), also used for arbitrary tail intervals in [the LEFT theorem](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md). ## 3. The effective weighted kernel Put $\mu=i/N$, $
u=j/N$, $w=
u-\mu$, and, for $0<t<1/2$, $$ s=\sin(\pi t),\quad c=\cos(\pi t),\quad z=\sin^2(\pi\delta),\quad k_\delta^2=1-z, \quad A=x+y,\quad ho=4xy/A^2. $$ The effective parameter in (2) satisfies $\cos^2(\pi\delta_{\mathrm{eff}})	o k_\delta^4$ uniformly in $\delta$. More precisely, with $	heta=\pi/N$, $$ \cos(2\pi\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}) = rac{(\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta))^2}{1+\cos	heta} -\cos	heta. $$ Thus $|\lambda|\le\lambda_0$ gives $0\le\lambda^2/\lambda_0\le\lambda_0$, in the original positive-tail range. Its coefficients $ eta_j$ may be negative; no positive-matrix or separated-eigenvalue hypothesis is added. Define $$ \Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)=2s\left[As+ \sqrt{(x-y)^2s^2+4xy k_\delta^4}ight], \qquad \alpha_\delta(t)=4(c^2-z). $$ The uniform transfer upper bound, the upper Riemann bounds for both unused products, and the uniform positive reference estimate yield the weighted upper action $$ \int_\mu^
u\log\mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\,dt, \qquad \mathcal L_\delta=  rac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}\alpha_0}{|\alpha_\delta|^2}. 	ag{4} $$ This rewriting uses $\int_0^{1/2}\log|\alpha_\delta|=0$ only AFTER estimating the actual unused products. No finite division at a spectral zero is made. The tail estimate is uniform in both endpoints and the real spectral parameter, including the repeated-root case. The logarithmic errors are $o(N)$ uniformly, at fixed positive $x,y$ in a compact set. Let $$ R_\delta(t)= rac{sc}{c^2-z} = rac{\sin(2\pi t)}{\cos(2\pi t)+\cos(2\pi\delta)}, \qquad B_ho(v)= rac{1+\sqrt{1-ho+ho v^2}}2. $$ A direct simplification of (4) gives $$ \mathcal L_\delta=A R_\delta^2 B_ho(k_\delta^2/s). 	ag{5} $$ The complete positive half-block root, in the normalization of the [uniform half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), is $$ L_0(t;x,y)=A	an^2(\pi t)B_ho(1/\sin(\pi t)). 	ag{6} $$ It is strictly increasing in $t$ and its logarithm is integrable. ## 4. An elementary rearrangement Define $t'=\pi^{-1}\arctan|R_\delta(t)|\in[0,1/2]$. The algebraic identity $$ (c^2-z)^2+s^2c^2-k_\delta^4c^2=z^2s^2\geq0 	ag{7} $$ implies $k_\delta^2/s\leq1/\sin(\pi t')$. Since $B_ho$ is nondecreasing, $$ \mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\leq L_0(t';x,y). 	ag{8} $$ The map $t\mapsto t'$ preserves the uniform distribution on $[0,1/2]$. To prove this, set $\vartheta=2\pi t$, $a=\cos(2\pi\delta)$ and $\varphi=\arg(e^{i\vartheta}+a)$. For $|a|<1$ this angle increases from $0$ to $\pi$, and $$ \vartheta=\varphi+\arcsin(a\sin\varphi). $$ The set $|R_\delta|>r$ has endpoint angles $\varphi_1=\arctan r$ and $\varphi_2=\pi-\arctan r$. Their arcsine corrections agree. Its length in $t$ is therefore $1/2-\pi^{-1}\arctan r$, exactly the distribution of $	an(\pi t)$. The endpoint cases are $t'=t$ and $t'=1/2-t$. For any measurable set of length $w$, the integral of an increasing function of a uniformly distributed $t'$ is at most its upper-tail integral of length $w$. Apply this elementary rearrangement to the interval $[\mu,
u]$ and to $\log L_0$, using truncation for its integrable endpoint singularities. Equations (8) and the distribution identity prove $$  oxed{\displaystyle \int_\mu^
u\log\mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\,dt \leq\int_{1/2-w}^{1/2}\log L_0(t;x,y)\,dt.} 	ag{9} $$ ## 5. The coefficient consequence and its current scope Write $\xi=k/N$. Weighted coefficient extraction in (3), (9), and the original complete-triangle Legendre formula give $$ \limsup rac1N\log rac{\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} \leq C(\xi,w-\xi,1/2-w). 	ag{10} $$ The statement is uniform on the entire closed one-sided simplex. For this, the terminal weighted action minus the outer linear weights has infimum $C(\xi,w-\xi,1/2-w)$ by the proved terminal-triangle Legendre formula. At each limiting degree choose a fixed finite positive tilt within any prescribed error of this infimum. Continuity of the terminal integral in $w$, of the linear degree weights, and of $C$ gives a neighborhood on which that same tilt works. Compactness supplies finitely many such tilts. Apply the uniform weighted estimates only to this finite set. The original $d=N-1$ normalization differs by $O(1/N)$; uniform continuity of $C$ absorbs it into the $o(1)$ error. This includes outer degree zero and collapsing intervals. The finite signed-parameter Cauchy inequality already covers the entire real spectral interval, including its final $O(N^{-2})$ cap; no cap extension is needed here. Both parity reference normalizations are kept. RIGHT follows by the original row reflection. If a protected outer is zero, only its exponent-zero coefficients survive, and the [sharp protected-outer formula](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md) attains (10). The middle degrees remain $\mu$ and $1-
u$ in the original shared flow. Although the entropy bound depends only on the two outer degrees, it is not permission to reassign middle loads independently. The global energy comparison still requires a proof using the original shared targets. ## 6. Validation and scope The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy_results.json) check exact finite identities and selected original coproduct coefficients. They do not use sampled large levels as a proof of the uniform theorem. The theorem bounds local coefficients before their original shared extraction. It does not move middle degrees to new faces, identify the bound with a representation volume, or prove the global inequality. The [joint shared-flow criterion](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md) records the precise conditional consequence.

title: Actual open meridian transport has a source-preserving horizontal polarization
text: # Actual open meridian transport has a source-preserving horizontal polarization Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The actual open R-word has an explicit endpoint half-character under M->qM. An M-dependent SECOND- wire gauge removes that half-step and preserves the whole source on arbitrary current tensors. A first-wire alternative has its separate explicit Cartan Ward correction. This constructs a real word-induced meridian/current connection, retaining the original finite source, power characters, cyclic wrap and peripheral factor. It does not yet turn the selected word class into the marked geometric period. The remaining insertion/current equation is stated explicitly in Section 7; no principal rational-density filter is substituted for the actual period. ## 1. The exact endpoint character of an arbitrary open braid word Use the original zero-framed knot braid on b strands, with writhe w. The first cut is at strand zero. The second is an INTERNAL IDENTITY wire at a specified braid level and strand slot ell, counted from zero. Use the literal tensor convention T_(c,d;a,b0)=ptr_other[A E_(b0,d)^(ell) B]. Thus d is the position immediately BEFORE the removed identity and b0 immediately AFTER it. Every original pivotal matrix remains in ptr_other; opening this wire neither removes its old cap nor adds a new pivot. Put nu=d-b0. Conservation gives c=a-nu for the uninserted tensor. All four physical head bounds and internal finite supports remain the original ones. For one actual crossing with first input i and first output c_1, the already proved finite coefficient identity is r_sign(qM)=x^(-sign) q^(c_1-i) r_sign(M)/tau_sign, x=-M/q, Y=M^2, tau_+=BC/x *(1-Y/A)/(1-YC/A), tau_-=x/A *(1-Y/B)/(1-YC/B). (1) The ratios in (1) mean their CANCELLED WHOLE finite products, as in the actual longitude-insertion theorem. No zero Pochhammer or peripheral denominator is divided separately. To telescope the half-character use the INTEGER position potential J(a_vec)=-sum_i i a_i. At every checked crossing, J_out-J_in=c_1-i. The final/initial closed strands have identical positions and the first position has coefficient zero in J. The matrix-unit insertion at the second cut changes J by -ell(b0-d)=ell nu. Therefore exactly sum_crossings(c_1-i)=-ell nu. (2) No root square root or cyclic interpretation is used in this equality. Write n=N-1, kappa_D=w-b+1, and retain the whole scalar gamma_N=q^(n kappa_D), L=gamma_N x^(-w) product_crossings tau_sign^-1. (3) The original closed pivotal/framing lines give gamma_N, just as in the closed calculation: each old closed pivot contributes q^(1-N), and the residual zero-framing line contributes q^(w(N-1)). The opening has not changed them. All common full Cartan scalars are kept with their original twist cancellation. At a knot root only, kappa_D is even and gamma_N=q^(-kappa_D). Off root keep gamma_N=q^(-kappa_D)(q^N)^(kappa_D), with its mark. For every raw finite open weight I the result is I(qM)=q^(-ell nu) L I(M). (4) Let T^[L] mean the SAME finite tensor with that cancelled whole insertion on every actual path. Put rho=q^(-ell) and D_rho=diag(rho^j) on the SECOND cut. Then (4) is the literal matrix identity T(qM)=(I tensor D_rho)T^[L](M)(I tensor D_rho^-1). (5) For the full ADO period multiply L by the ACTUAL whole ratio g_N=d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =q^(N-1)(q^2M^2-1)/(M^2-1) *(M^(2N)-1)/(q^(2N)M^(2N)-1). (6) Its original phase cancels only by using the SAME phase lift on both sides. The root reduction of (6), its complete norm-zero lattice and all q-normal source terms are not suppressed. ## 2. The raw Fourier source and independent alias powers Keep the full band kernel F(M,eta)=sum_nu f_nu(M)eta^nu, with the first input fixed and original output row still summed. Equation (4) reads F(qM,eta)=F^[L](M,rho eta). (7) The actual co-source is its constant coefficient, so CT_eta is unchanged by rho dilation, for WHOLE functions and every finite tail. No physical-position sum is replaced by a Fourier evaluation. For one uninserted first-input head a, the band interval [a-(N-1),a] has length N; root averaging computes CT exactly. For unwrapped currents keep an independent V_eta=eta^N: Av_(N,V_eta)F=sum_k f_(kN)V_eta^k, V_eta ->rho^N V_eta=(q^N)^(-ell)V_eta. (8) Thus an odd ell changes the physical root grid V_eta=1 to the antiperiodic grid -1. The original head CT agrees on these grids, but alias powers of a current do not. They retain the sign and the whole (q^N)^(-ell) character before normal differentiation. On the complete root head-band window, dilation by rho is a genuine finite matrix on the Fourier-label array: conjugate diag(rho^nu) by its finite Fourier evaluation matrix, using the ACTUAL unwrapped representatives in that interval. It fixes the constant-mode source, commutes with cyclic Fourier-label shifts, and is unitary when |rho|=1. It is not obtained by silently identifying every tail with its residue modulo N. In a whole generic-Q Vandermonde frame, use the original full tensor and its last-row carry, not a root permutation extended without corrections. ## 3. The second-wire horizontal gauge preserves the entire source functor On the SECOND identity wire put D_2(M)=diag(M^(-ell b)), T_h=(I tensor D_2^-1)T(I tensor D_2). Its coefficient factor is M^(ell(d-b))=M^(ell nu) for EVERY tensor entry, including charged current tensors. It therefore cancels (4) for the uninserted open word: I_h(qM)=L I_h(M), F_h(M,xi)=F(M,M^ell xi). (9a) The second partial trace is invariant under this conjugation on ALL matrices, not only diagonal or scalar reclosures: ptr_second T_h=ptr_second T. (9b) The first source, original caps, peripheral line and every source current are unchanged. On other internal pieces transform their ordered operators by the same basis map. This is a strict whole source/current functor before normal jets. No Schur argument or source replacement is used in (9b). There is an equally explicit GLOBAL braid-frame construction. On a level of b strands use G(M)=tensor_j M^(-j J_j), with first strand j=0. For one crossing its coefficient in G^-1 R G is M^(-(c_1-i))r. Thus (1) immediately loses its q^(c_1-i) factor under M->qM. All adjacent level gauges cancel in a word; the original closed diagonal pivots commute with them, and the first source is untouched. Cutting this global gauge at the second wire gives exactly D_2 above. In the actual generic-Q Fourier frame this is a SCALED Vandermonde isomorphism, not a root-only kernel substitution: W(M,Q)=V(Q)D_2(M)^-1, W_(j,b)=(M^ell Q^j)^b, W^-1=D_2 V^-1. The node gaps are only M^ell(Q^i-Q^j), so no additional source norm-zero divisor has been inverted. Equations (5) and (9a) give the exact whole matrix meridian identity (I tensor W(qM))T(qM)(I tensor W(qM)^-1) =(I tensor W(M))T^[L](M)(I tensor W(M)^-1). (9c) Indeed W(qM)D_rho=W(M). The raw first-output sum of the diagonal j entries therefore has fixed exterior xi=Q^j under the meridian step. Its remaining action is the ACTUAL insertion L, not a scalar chosen from the geometric branch. The forced normal connection on this whole frame is A_M=(D_M W)W^-1=ell V J V^-1, A_Q=(D_Q W)W^-1=(D_Q V)V^-1 (M fixed). Thus D_M T^W=W(D_M T)W^-1+[A_M,T^W] on that wire; the commutator has zero second partial trace entrywise. At a complex root, ||A_M||<=ell(N-1) and the old bound for A_Q is unchanged. On |M|=1, W/sqrt(N) is unitary. These are source-frame bounds, not full crossing-word bounds. Along M(q), retain the chain-rule connection and the marked M^N and q^N powers. There is a precise ROOT-only cyclic current corollary. For a charge-zero fixed-input packet put F_a[j,c]=Q_N^(j(a-c)), 0<=c,j<N, H_a(M)=F_a diag(M^(ell(a-c)))F_a^-1. Then J_h=H_a J, Sigma H_a=Sigma, H_a 1=1. Every factor is diagonal in the same finite Fourier basis, so H_a commutes with the cyclic shift, its normalized difference and its centered primitive. Its M-connection is A_a=ell F_a diag(a-c)F_a^-1, Sigma A_a=0, A_a1=0, ||A_a||<=ell(N-1). For |M|=1 this is an ISOMETRY of the actual cyclic source/current complex. In particular its distance to the zero-source current space is unchanged. This finite-packet statement is not extended to charged/unwrapped tails by forgetting their alias powers; those use the strict whole tensor map and (8). The packet connection A_a is NOT the full matrix A_M and is not independent of the unwrapped input window. For 0<=a<N-1, let Pi_(a+1) be the root Fourier projector on residue a+1. Then A_(a+1)-A_a=ell N Pi_(a+1), H_(a+1)H_a^-1=I+(M^(ell N)-1)Pi_(a+1). This is the exact branch carry as that head window moves by one. It is trivial in value at M=1 but not in its normal jet. The full tensor functor retains it, rather than treating A_a as a window-independent current connection. ## 4. Optional first-wire gauge and its exact Ward correction On the FIRST wire define D(M)=diag(M^(ell a)), T_hor=(D(M)^-1 tensor I)T(D(M) tensor I). (9) For a charge-zero path its coefficient is M^(ell(a-c))=M^(ell nu). Substituting (4) at qM cancels the factor q^(-ell nu). Hence I_hor(qM)=L I_hor(M), F_hor(M,xi)=F(M,M^ell xi), F_hor(qM,xi)=F_hor^[L](M,xi). (10) This is an alternative meridian-horizontal polarization, with no guessed quiver transport. Its endpoint half-character has been absorbed by a specified whole diagonal gauge, while L itself remains the actual word insertion rather than its critical value. The first-wire reclosure C=ptr_second T is diagonal for every whole uninserted auxiliary word by total position conservation. Therefore ptr_second T_hor=D^-1 C D=C (11) even OFF root. The selected uninserted state and full d_N line are exactly unchanged. For a current tensor of total charge d, c+nu=a+d; its factor is M^(ell nu)M^(-ell d). This extra source character is retained, rather than extending (11) to nonscalar charged matrices without their row correction. There are two equivalent complete current presentations. Transport all source data by the actual gauge: psi_hor=D^-1 psi and ell_hor=ell D, with the corresponding transformed coupon. Then the pairing is identical on EVERY matrix. If one keeps the convenient original fixed-input/all-ones row instead, its exact whole defect is the Cartan Ward row lambda_a(D^-1 C D)-lambda_a(C) =sum_(c!=a) [M^(ell(a-c))-1]/[Q^(a-c)-1] (D_K C)_(c,a), D_K C=K C K^-1-C. (12) Only genuine head units are inverted. No color edge or 1-Q^N is removed. Equation (12) handles all ordered/Green current tensors. On homogeneous charge d its selected line factor is M^(-ell d). The forced M-connection in the horizontal matrix frame is (D_M+ad_(ell J_head)) C_hor =D^-1(D_M C)D, D_M=M partial_M. (13) Its sign follows by differentiating D^-1 C D. The q-normal connection is zero with M held independent; on an actual path M(q) retain its chain-rule multiple of ell J_head. This does not freeze the fixed-level power graph or any normal source character. On the physical unit-meridian arc D(M) is unitary. The row in (12), in the original balanced flat metric, satisfies ||beta_(a,ell)(M)||^2 <=(N^2-1)/3, |M|=1, beta_(a,ell)(1)=0, ||D_M^k beta_(a,ell)(1)|| <=ell^k N^(k+1)/sqrt(12), k>=1. (14) Proof: numerator modulus is at most two and the denominator runs once through all nontrivial N-th root gaps; their inverse-square sum is (N^2-1)/12. For k derivatives use |a-c|<N. These are polynomial bounds for the SOURCE GAUGE and its fixed normal jets, not for the whole R-word, the external d_N pole or a complex neighborhood of the physical arc. ## 5. The pointed cyclic polynomial and wrap cannot be dropped The MAIN second-wire construction leaves the original first source and its supplied chi polynomial untouched. On any wire carrying a pointed cyclic source, an actual basis change transports its source vector, co-source and spectral polynomial simultaneously. For the optional first-wire gauge, the original first source is highest input and the orbit output row; in a cyclic frame its repair P=U+W has P^N=I. Equation (9) gives EXACTLY P_hor=D^-1 P D =M^(-ell)[P+(M^(ell N)-1)W], P_hor^N=I, ell_hor P_hor=ell_hor. (15) The marked source vector and row transform as just specified. Thus its characteristic polynomial and FORCED pointed factor are retained: chi(z)=(z-1)chi_red(z). In the actual cyclic repair chi=z^N-1. For an unfolded sourced companion the full conjugation also preserves its supplied chi and transports its chi_red row. Replacing (15) by bare M^(-ell)P would instead change the characteristic polynomial and its source eigenvalue. Its wrap character M^(ell N) is essential, including at a normal root. None of this identifies chi_red with the knot A-polynomial. ## 6. Compatibility with the geometric pole, with the exact scope The horizontal open phase adds ell Log M times the boundary displacement t=Hnu. Its principal incidence is therefore xi=M^(-ell)p_e^-1, p_hor=M^ell p_e. (16) The critical displacement is still zero, so its marked geometric action is unchanged. The nondegenerate Fourier block persists on the same regular meridian germ. At COMPLETENESS the proved Möbius framing coordinate and its pole lambda_e apply. Away from it, only a supplied marked polar branch, if it persists, can be said to rescale to lambda_hor=M^ell lambda_e(M). No global generic-M Möbius or single-pole theorem is assumed. For the rational principal coefficient T(p)=G p/(p-lambda)^2, sampling p^N=S gives EXACTLY Av_(N,S)T=G N S lambda^(N-1)/(S-lambda^N)^2. (17) Thus the antiperiodic source grid changes 1-lambda^N to 1+lambda^N with the corresponding numerator sign. In horizontal coordinates the retained candidate norm is 1-M^(ell N)lambda_e(M)^N. (18) The differential Jacobian is essential: at fixed M, dr expressed in p_hor=M^ell p gives G_hor=M^ell G as well as the rescaled pole. Where both expressions are regular, the RATIO of the two principal filters under this coordinate rescaling alone is M^(ell N)[(1-lambda_e^N)/ (1-M^(ell N)lambda_e^N)]^2. (19) At M=1 its extra logarithmic derivative is ell N(1+lambda_e^N)/(1-lambda_e^N), retaining the pole. Equation (19) is a geometric filter comparison, NOT a proved adapter of the actual selected quantum period. The exact main tensor gauge (9a)--(9c) preserves that period while its raw principal filter may be singular. Its missing whole word numerator/current correction must cancel or account for such poles; (17) alone cannot do it. ## 7. The remaining source-current equation is now explicit On any regular proper-array chart let R_i=S_i I_hor/I_hor be the actual internal ratios. Since the main identity (9a)--(9c) is exact, sigma_M(R_i)/R_i=S_i(L)/L. (20) For the finite Green insertion operator d_R,i=R_i S_i-I, this gives the coefficientwise chain identity L d_(sigma R),i(f)=d_R,i(Lf). (21) The global meaning is the zero-extended array identity, retaining all original endpoints and cancellation lattices. Together with the semilinear shift of f, it is the actual word-induced meridian connection on the insertion/current complex. After finite source pushforward it is the exact period equation T_M P_N=source(L I_hor), (22) with (6) in full normalization. Finite coefficient elimination already supplies a nonzero actual scalar meridian operator. What (20)--(22) do NOT prove is a geometric quotient of this SELECTED class. On ordinary finite-array currents multiplication by L leaves the exact residual sum_s L(s)(S_i-I)H(s) =sum_s [L(s-e_i)-L(s)]H(s). (23) Discarding it, or replacing L by its critical longitude inside the sum, would change the current/source comparison. A solution of gate C must transport (21), its MAIN whole source functor (9b)--(9c), its supplied pointed spectral/co-source data and the norm-pole corrections (18), then prove that the resulting original class is nonzero on the marked geometric period. This note removes a concrete endpoint twist and supplies tame actual source transport, but does not assert that last global map. The first-wire rows (12),(15) describe only the optional alternative. [Exact local/path/source/normal audit](../experiments/audit_open_meridian_horizontal_transport.py) and [saved results](../experiments/open_meridian_horizontal_transport_results.json). The audit passes 2,680 literal local meridian shifts, 1,268 open paths in 44 genuine signed-word/cut families, 20 generic/root scaled-Vandermonde matrices with 9,096 full port-source units, 60 root cyclic-packet isometries, 56 exact window branch carries, 812 optional source Ward rows, 588 independent alias-power cases, 42 periodic/antiperiodic principal filters and 72 checks of the proved unit-arc source metric estimates. Generic q and root q cases are kept separate.

title: Adaptive resonant sampling of the actual source and the raw-quotient obstruction
text: # Adaptive resonant sampling of the actual source and the raw-quotient obstruction 28 October 2026. There is a constructive EXACT adaptive Fermat sampling which puts the complete original finite source on the resonant divisor; Section 5 proves it entrywise for either crossing sign. This is a genuine base change before the original finite windows. It evades, rather than contradicts, the fixed-scalar raw-quotient obstruction proved first below. No arbitrary exterior coupon, renormalized invariant, or generic oscillatory countermodel is involved. Other original Newton/Rogers currents remain compulsory after this sampling. ## 1. The closure character is invisible to the complete finite crossing Keep the ports and complete signed Laurent kernels of [the actual trivalent crossing](actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.md). Inputs are z0,z1 and outputs are z6,z7. Put d=N-1. For fixed t0!=0, independent of the head variables, the character in [the exact resonant Fourier source](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md#11-an-exact-resonant-fourier-source-including-its-closure-current) is A=(z7/z1)^N-(z7/t0)^N, D=1-A. (1) For the positive crossing it is exactly exp(N lambda)(1-exp(N z)), with the retained marks lambda=Logz7-Logz1+2pi*i and z=h+Logz1-Logt0. Equation (1) is a Laurent polynomial, so its monodromy notation does not introduce an additional choice here. Let K_sigma(t) be the COMPLETE raw signed kernel, including all finite Newton/Rogers factors and the original shared negative Gaussian when sigma=-. Let Pi_phys extract the original finite input/output block. Then, identically before taking the t constant term, Pi_phys[A K_sigma(t)]=0, Pi_phys[D K_sigma(t)]=Pi_phys[K_sigma(t)]. (2) This also holds after the exact finite root-orbit average, for every N, every original color, and either crossing sign. The proof is the actual finite output support. In the positive layer the last Newton factor is B_N(x^(-1)z7/z6,x^(-2)z7/t), and in the negative layer the last Rogers factor is R_N(g_- z7/t,x^(-1)z7/z6). Every monomial in either has second-output exponent e between 0 and d; none of the other factors contains z7. Both monomials of A contain z7^N. They therefore force second-output exponent at least N, which the original finite output window excludes. The first monomial also raises the required second input by N, but that additional exclusion is not needed. Gaussian integration changes coefficients and cannot change these exponents. The same proof works term by term on any fixed scalar root orbit. This proves (2) without assuming that the meromorphic homogeneous/current pieces separately have finite support. More generally Pi_phys[A^k K_sigma]=0 for every k>=1. If a polynomial f(A) is inserted directly on this complete local kernel, its finite physical projection is f(0) times that of the uninserted kernel. ## 2. This is an exact statement for the whole original knot source Apply (2) at any physical crossing of an actual signed word, retaining all original input/output barriers, pivots, markings, and framing. The physical local operator is unchanged if it is multiplied by D. Consequently its contraction with the original source is unchanged. This applies to nonzero hyperbolic-knot periods as well as to general words; for example the independently proved original figure-eight source is K_N(4_1)=sum_(n=0)^d |(Q;Q)_n|^2>0. (3) Thus there is no exact raw restriction of this original source to A=1 which retains the COMPLETE inserted crossing and its D-inserted source pairing: restriction would send D K_sigma to zero, whereas its original pairing is the nonzero quantity (3). This does NOT authorize the opposite algebra quotient A=0. Equation (2) is a statement about a specified finite projection of a specified complete kernel. The finite projection is not multiplicative on the Laurent algebra: A has a factor z7^N, while multiplication first by z7^(-N) can return those exponents to the physical output window. An arbitrary later operator/coupon need not retain (2). Accordingly the precise assertion is the actual insertion-functional identity (2), not an algebraic support statement for the whole coupon algebra. Nor can (2) be applied separately to the meromorphic S/I sectors. Those sectors are not finite Laurent kernels; their continued high Fourier modes are exactly what restore the original finite source in their sum. ## 3. What the orbit and deck equations do determine The root-orbit map proves equality of the COMPLETE original sourced functional with its finite-orbit version. The only unwanted orbit alias has positive integer degree N, and the original closure kills every nonempty alias selection. Invariance under changing the fixed scalar t0 is therefore exact. These are consequences of the original finite degree/source data; they are not new constraints forcing A=1. Likewise the local exact formula T_N=H_N F_ref+Psi_+(z)(1-A) I_- has a completely normalized, nonzero reference coefficient H_N on the regular part of A=1. Its compulsory current restores the source away from that divisor. Equation (2) shows why one cannot obtain the original global geometric coefficient by setting that current to zero through a raw multiplicative restriction of the complete source. Beyond the adaptive map in Section 5, the wanted additional structure is a SOURCE map to an action-normalized geometric vanishing-cycle/formal block, including the finite window and its currents. One must calculate the image of the actual marked class there and show that its coefficient is nonzero with subexponential normalization. This would be a genuinely derived or microlocal source comparison; its local resonant residue cannot simply be substituted for the complete finite pointing. ## 4. Exactly what compact divisor rigidity would and would not prove If two meromorphic sections of the same line on a connected compact normal variety have the SAME complete divisor, their ratio is a nowhere zero global holomorphic function, hence constant. One exact nonzero value fixes that constant. This is a valid rigidity principle. Its present application is missing two pieces of actual data: a globally defined geometric component with its full divisor, and the map of the original source/cosource to that component. Known local homogeneous divisors and total deck invariance do not supply either piece. The complete section includes currents with different divisors and different continued homogeneous components. Even uniqueness of the COMPLETE exact section would not by itself compute its decomposition into action-normalized geometric periods. The obstruction (2) is stronger than an abstract caution: the original finite pointing already pairs nontrivially with the closure defect which raw resonant restriction would erase. Therefore a successful global compact-torsor rigidity argument must explicitly transport that pointing, rather than infer its balanced support from the fixed-scalar orbit map. The following adaptive construction does transport it to a balanced sampling of the COMPLETE finite kernel. ## 5. A constructive adaptive Fermat sampling evades the obstruction Define a head-dependent orbit radius by the algebraic equation t0^(-N)=c(z1,z7):=z1^(-N)-z7^(-N). (4) On c!=0 choose any of its N roots and sample the COMPLETE raw kernel on the orbit t=t0 Q^j. The finite sum is independent of that root choice. Since K_sigma(t) has t exponents in [-2d,d], its average is exactly CT_t K_sigma+c(z1,z7) C_sigma, C_sigma=[t^(-N)]K_sigma. (5) Now apply the original physical windows. Every monomial of C_sigma has incoming second exponent -b with b>=0 and outgoing second exponent e with 0<=e<=d. The first term z1^(-N)C_sigma in (5) requires incoming second index b+N>=N, and the second term z7^(-N)C_sigma has outgoing second exponent e-N<0. Both are excluded. Therefore, ENTRYWISE, Pi_phys [(1/N)sum_(j=0)^d K_sigma(t0 Q^j)] =Pi_phys CT_t K_sigma. (6) This is true at either sign and every original color, with the same continuous Gaussian retained for a negative crossing. It consequently preserves every original whole-word source, without needing a global degree argument to cancel residual local aliases. Its scalar and all finite barriers are unchanged. By (4), the actual character (1) is identically A=1 on this algebraic sampling. Thus the local resonant Fourier comparison has its exact reference coefficient H_N and no additional closure current. This closes a source-balancing step which a fixed scalar orbit did not close. The construction does not erase the OTHER original B/R current sectors created before that one-function comparison. An additional balanced external Fourier-frame completion can remove those local currents too. Its degree proof must be performed before the original whole source is applied; it is not a consequence of (6) alone. That construction is now proved in the [local balanced Fourier theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) and the [whole-word source theorem](regular_balanced_fermat_word_source.md). It uses independent regular local grids and retains the exact rational Fourier adapters. The remaining geometric source problem concerns that explicit sewn network, rather than an unidentified local normalizer. At c=0 an individual sampled radius tends to infinity. The COMPLETE finite average nevertheless has the explicit Laurent-polynomial extension (5), and its physical projection has the extension (6). Separated homogeneous/current expressions require their matched joint continuation there; one cannot infer separate finite limits from (5). There is no contradiction with (2): substituting (4) before projection changes the head dependence of the moment variables. It is not an A-linear restriction of the fixed-scalar inserted source. Algebraic base change and the physical projection do not commute. This is the precise mechanism by which the adaptive source map evades the no-go. ## 6. The remaining adaptive local norms form a two-generator boundary ideal There is a concrete algebraic target for that additional transport at complete color. Write a=z0^N, b=z1^N, c=z6^N, d=z7^N, s=x^N, s^2=1, T=t0^N=bd/(d-b). On the regular torus, the first Newton, final Newton, and middle Rogers norms in the original positive layer are, respectively, D_first=T[1/(s a)-1/d], D_B=d[1/b-1/(s c)], D_R=1-c/a-c/(s T) =-(s c/T)D_first-(c/(s d))D_B. (7) The last equality uses only 1/T=1/b-1/d and s^2=1. Thus the THREE norms generate exactly the two boundary-exchange relations d-s a and b-s c after localization at the displayed nonzero coordinates. They vanish jointly precisely when c=s b, d=s a. (8) Keep the source-selected decompositions B0=S0+D_first I0, R=T_R+D_R J, Bf=Sf+D_B If, with all logarithmic marks. Their complete scalar kernel obeys the exact aggregate identity B0 R Bf-S0 T_R Sf =D_first[I0 R Bf-(s c/T)S0 J Bf] +D_B[S0 T_R If-(c/(s d))S0 J Bf]. (9) It follows by expanding in the stated order and then substituting (7). This reduces the remaining local current transport to TWO specified boundary relations, rather than three unrelated local normalizers. It does not assert that the raw finite projection annihilates each meromorphic term of (9). Regular balanced external sampling can impose (8) before the finite projection, and must retain its Fourier changes of frame when the local blocks are sewn. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_orbit_closure_source_obstruction.py) checks the full raw signed finite layers, the actual physical R matrices, nonzero discarded terms, finite-orbit aliases, and original pivotal whole-word source identities. The grading/output-support proof above is uniform in N.

title: Ordered small-circle insertions and the original marked face
text: # Ordered small-circle insertions and the original marked face 30 October 2026. This note extends the exact polynomial insertion to several untwisted ports in a specified literal Morse class. The operators act in reverse source order, including on all coefficients created by later ports. It also supplies a one-port adapter when the outgoing middle face is the original marked or exterior face. No mark is moved and no generic-q transpose identity is inferred. The general subset with several protected outgoing faces or disconnected smoothing remains outside the statement below. ## 1. Literal face births, not an arbitrary operator order Use the flat 2k-plat sweep and actual region labels of the [marked face coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md). Number boxes in their original bottom-to-top order. At box i write (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i) for the outside, input-middle, output-middle and final faces. Only its middle gap changes. The output region is created at this box and remains in that gap until its next box or the top cap. Only the top exterior gap identifications can identify such a new region with a region already present earlier: those identifications all give the exterior face u. Every bounded output face c_i is therefore a distinct face with a unique birth i. In particular c_i does not occur as ANY face of a box j<i. This includes outer faces, not only the two middle positions. A bounded middle face is distinct from the two outer faces at its incident box; the outer faces may coincide with one another. The other protected face v is the bounded face of the original marked cap. Choose a set S of ports such that epsilon_i=0 and c_i not in {u,v}, for every i in S. (1) The input b_i may equal u. All other physical turns, the mark and the retained half twists outside S are unchanged. No one-main-component assumption is made. The relations c_i=b_i, i in S, form a forest directed from an older face to a newer one. Each c_i has one birth and at most one such incoming edge. A directed cycle would contradict the strict birth order, and an undirected cycle would have a newest vertex with two incoming edges. Neither protected face is eliminated. In the flat plat one can also see this forest as consecutive deleted segments in the original gaps. Each even gap retains its last box, whose outgoing face is u; connectedness of the original plat requires a box in each internal even gap. Thus the identity-smoothed projection remains connected. The marked gap retains its last box if it has one, so the two original marked faces remain distinct. For clarity, this is a source-coordinate class with a proved order. It is not a claim that an arbitrary untyped graph or a differently routed collection of coupons has this triangular incidence. ## 2. The exact reverse-ordered polynomial Retain N,d,q,Q and the operators T_h(x,c,y) of the [one-port theorem](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md). They preserve polynomials and total degree; their coefficients retain the full source phase q^(pd), where p is output-minus-input first head. Each h_i is an actual integer in 1,...,N. Let P_rem be the product D_a D_a Ptilde_s over all ports outside S, in ALL original face variables before any identifications. Starting with this polynomial, process i in S in STRICTLY DECREASING original Morse order. At step i apply T_(h_i)(x_i,c_i,y_i) to the CURRENT polynomial, then substitute c_i=b_i everywhere. Apply the same region identification to the remaining notation. Call the result Q_S. This instruction acts on every factor created at preceding steps. For example an earlier output c_i may occur as an outer variable in a later port's operator. Its q-shifts must then act on that operator's coefficients as well. Commuting the operators or applying them only to the initial product is not the stated formula. Why this order is exact can be checked before any coefficient extraction. Keep the original finite physical paths at every small port. For the latest pending port i, its bounded output c_i occurs in no earlier pending port, by section 1. Thus summing its paths and eliminating c_i=Q^(-p_i)b_i acts ONLY on the current remaining source polynomial; the other pending port weights are independent of c_i. The true factor q^(p_i d) is unchanged because the eliminated face c_i has the ordinary exponent -d, whereas b_i is retained. The local path calculation is therefore exactly T_(h_i), followed by the merge. Repeating proves the algorithm. If later eliminated faces were merged into c_i, all their factors already occur in the current polynomial and are shifted along with it. This is precisely the cross-shift contribution required by the original paths. Let r=R-|S|, and let F_sm be the r faces other than u,v in the identity-smoothed diagram. Then Q_S is homogeneous of degree dr and the actual fixed-sector source is A_(N,a;h_S)=N^r product_(i not in S) [k_(a_i)beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] [product_(f in F_sm)L_f^d] Q_S(L)|_(L_u=L_v=0). (2) All physical endpoint factors remain those of the original Casimir. Each elimination reduces the primitive grid by exactly one variable; there are N^(r+1) final grid points and the unchanged single N^-1 marked factor. All exponents in Q_S are nonnegative integers, so its degree dr excludes every whole-N alias exactly as in the one-port proof. Neither positivity of Q_S nor independent periodicity of a local half-integer source factor is needed. ## 3. Uniform cost at an actual compatible smoothing radius Choose fixed positive values l on the final smoothed faces, including both marked faces. Give each old face the value of its merged class. For each i put C_i(l)=3+4(l_(x_i)+l_(y_i))/l_(c_i) +4l_(x_i)l_(y_i)/l_(c_i)^2. (3) These use the literal old incidences followed by the final region map. The weighted polynomial norm in the one-port theorem applies at every step; merging variables of equal weight cannot increase it. Therefore |[L^(d F_sm)]Q_S| <= product_(i in S) C_i(l)^(h_i-1) P_sm(l)/product_(f in F_sm) l_f^d, (4) where P_sm is the original positive polynomial obtained by identity smoothing all ports in S. This includes all dependence of later operator coefficients on earlier shifted faces. The original scalar factors in (2) are retained outside (4). A proved strict coefficient-rate gap at the SAME positive smoothed variables thus survives with only O(sum_i h_i) added logarithmic cost. This is subexponential for a fixed number of ports with h_i=O(sqrt N), and preserves a fixed strict gap for sufficiently small h_i<=delta N. An optimized or fixed-radius gap is a separate geometric/capacity input; none is asserted for every smoothing by this algebra. ## 4. A one-port adapter at the original mark or exterior There is a useful boundary extension that does not require moving the mark. The original root Casimir is TRANSPOSE-SYMMETRIC in the balanced physical basis. Indeed its true coefficients satisfy A_+(U,V)=A_-(Q U,Q^-1 V), (5) including the endpoint zeros, and its diagonal is unchanged. Hence L_h^T=L_h at the root. This is ordinary transpose, not Hermitian conjugation and not a statement about its genuine generic-q jet. For ONE port suppose its middle faces b,c are distinct, at least one is unmarked, and the identity smoothing is connected with u,v still distinct. Eliminate an unmarked middle face. If it is c, use the original T_h in c. If instead c is protected and b is unmarked, use (5), regard the outgoing pair as input for this local calculation, apply the SAME T_h(x,b,y) to P_rem, and then set b=c. The displacement is now S-R and the exact source phase is q^((S-R)d), because the eliminated variable b has exponent -d. All other variables and the actual original mark are retained. Formula (2) with |S|=1 and bound (4) follow without changing the marked functional. If the incoming b is protected and outgoing c unmarked, no transpose is required: the q^(pd) computation only uses that the ELIMINATED face c is unmarked. Its merged target is then zero rather than d, as required by the same original mark. The degree/alias argument again applies with the two protected faces retained. In a flat plat a middle gap has fixed parity. The exterior belongs to even gaps and the marked-cap face belongs to an odd gap, so they cannot be the two distinct middle faces of one box. A nondegenerate certified port has distinct middle faces. Thus every such single untwisted port whose smoothing stays connected admits this adapter, irrespective of which actual top cap was marked. This one-port transpose does NOT justify arbitrary compositions of forward and reverse eliminations. A reversed elimination can act on earlier pending port weights, unlike the ordered class in section 1. Several protected outgoing ports, disconnected smoothings, and retained R^epsilon at the small ports remain separate source problems. ## 5. Original-source verification and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions_results.json), checks 81 original Morse charts, 1,143 bounded output births, 9,056 earlier-face exclusions, 243 deleted forests and connected literal smoothings, and 1,836 genuine cross-coefficient incidences. It compares 27 whole original multiport contractions and 122 original one-port mark/exterior adapters with the stated coefficients, retaining the other half twists, actual cups and unrestricted mark. The root transpose check uses 4,659 original coproduct entries. All 86 surviving modular targets are the asserted unique coefficients. An explicit original source gives a different answer when the reverse order is replaced by forward order. Coincident outer labels are also tested literally. The theorem does not extend to arbitrary mixed-direction subsets, disconnected smoothings or signed small ports.

title: Independent audit of the ordinary-color identification
text: # Independent audit of the ordinary-color identification 28 October 2026. This checks the two representation comparisons needed before applying the positive path trace in [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md#2-a-positive-trace-bounds-all-the-ordinary-colors). Neither comparison assumes a published colored-Jones or ADO comparison proof. They are exact finite-matrix statements, including the Cartan scalar and zero framing. The positive path trace itself is a separate algebraic step. The conclusion is that, for a **one-component** zero-framed closure of a fixed b-strand braid and every 1 <= j < N, F_N^M(-q^j) = F_N^Y(Q^j) = C_j(q), C_j(q) = theta_j^(-w) tau(P rho(cable(word)) P)/[j], q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, theta_j=q^((j^2-1)/2). (1) The coordinate superscripts in (1) are essential. In `root_orbit_pointing.md`, the reduced family is a function of M=-q x=-q^(alpha+1); here it is denoted F_N^M(M). In `regularized_kashaev_period.md`, the symbol F_N denotes its even descent to Y=M^2; here that function is denoted F_N^Y(Y). Thus F_N^M(M)=F_N^Y(M^2), alpha=j-1 <=> x=q^(j-1), M=-q^j, Y=Q^j. In particular one must NOT insert -q^j into the Y-coordinate function. The complete point is M=1, Y=1. All these are reduced periods; the full modified-dimension factor can have poles at the ordinary orbit points and is not asserted polynomially bounded there. For an independent check that this descent is legitimate, use the actual stripped Laurent crossing formulas. Under x -> -x, a transfer of order h contributes (-1)^(u+v+h) for either crossing sign, where u,v are its inputs. Modulo two this is (-1)^(c-u), with c its first checked output: c=v+h for a positive crossing and c=v-h for a negative one. Conservation of the integer pair sum makes c-u the negative change of the sum of index times strand position. Its total is zero on every diagonal cut state. The remaining pivot/framing sign is (-1)^((N-1)(b-1-w))=1 for a knot. Hence the reduced Laurent family is even in x, equivalently in M. Since it is Laurent polynomial, it descends uniquely to a Laurent polynomial in Y=M^2. This proof uses the original reduced framing; the unreduced/full state has the separate sign line and pole factors described in the pointing notes. Here tau is the algebraic fundamental pivotal closure trace, P is the product of the actual Jones--Wenzl idempotents p_(j-1), and every crossing in rho is the full fundamental matrix, with its common Cartan scalar. The usual value of q^(1/2) is exp(pi*i/(2N)). The source is the original reduced cut; the modified-dimension line is not divided out in a new way. ## 1. The invariant quotient is genuinely the ordinary color At alpha=j-1 the original N-dimensional unrolled color V has H v_a=(j-1-2a)v_a, K v_a=q^(j-1-2a)v_a, E v_a=[a][j-a]v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1).
