All missing vectors are zero. The subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)) is invariant: its only possible downward escape is E v_j, whose coefficient is zero. H,K,F preserve it as well. The quotient V/U has basis v_0,...,v_(j-1), with exactly the ordinary j-dimensional highest-weight matrices. At j=1 this quotient is the trivial color. The actual uncheck R is R=q^(H tensor H/2) sum_(h=0)^(N-1) c_h E^h tensor F^h, c_h=q^(h(h-1)/2)(q-q^(-1))^h/[h]!. (2) Every summand preserves U on each input strand separately, as does the Cartan factor. The inverse has the same preservation property, either from its finite inverse formula or from invertibility of its induced diagonal blocks. Its induced quotient is the defining ordinary R: all terms h >= j vanish there. The checked R exchanges the two typed strands; it does not exchange the status of a strand with an unrelated one. The quotient maps consequently satisfy, for both crossing signs, (pi tensor pi) B_N = B_j (pi tensor pi). (3) The pivot and twist preserve U. There is no singular factorial in this calculation: h < N in (2), and h < j on the quotient. ## 2. Why quotienting only the open strand quotients the entire knot This is the essential one-component trace lemma. Choose a basis adapted to U and V/U on every physical strand. Along each underlying oriented strand segment, attach status 1 to a basis vector in U and status 0 to a quotient-basis vector. For every nonzero crossing coefficient, status can change from 0 to 1, but cannot change from 1 to 0. This is exactly preservation of U by each uncheck factor, with the strand types followed through the check permutation. The diagonal pivot preserves status, and a closing partial trace identifies the status at the two ends of each traced strand. To calculate the induced open cut on V/U, its two open ends both have status 0. If the closed braid is a knot, there is one underlying component, and it passes through those ends. Following that entire component from its open input to its open output, a status-1 segment could never return to the final status 0. Therefore **every** segment of every contributing state has status 0. The contributing summands are precisely those obtained by replacing every color by V/U and taking the same cut trace there. This proves the all-strands color comparison; Schur's lemma alone would not prove it. This argument is termwise and works for arbitrary positive/negative words and any number of strands. It does not require a splitting V=U direct-sum W into modules. The original reduced cut on V is scalar even at this reducible color: it commutes with K and F, K has N distinct eigenvalues, and every internal arrow of F has coefficient one. Thus its scalar is the same scalar found on the nonzero quotient. The component assumption cannot be omitted. For the identity two-strand braid, a separate closed N-color component has pivotal trace zero, whereas replacing it by the trivial quotient gives trace one. Our audit checks this failure as well as the knot identities. No analogous unqualified statement for links is used. ## 3. Pivotal, framing and half-root scalars Write m=j-1 and epsilon_j=(-1)^m. On the quotient, K^(1-N)=epsilon_j K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j theta_j, theta_j=q^(m(m+2)/2). (4) Indeed K^N=q^(Nm) I=epsilon_j I, since the other weight term is q^(-2Na)=1. Also theta_ADO/theta_j=q^(-Nm)=epsilon_j from the defining ADO twist q^((alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2). For a cut of a b-strand knot with writhe w, the b-1 traced pivots and the framing correction therefore produce the total factor epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. (5) The braid permutation is a b-cycle, so w and b-1 have the same parity. This proves the first equality in (1) without an unspecified phase. The same bookkeeping can be performed in the stripped matrices used by the exact audits. The common positive Cartan scalar is q^(m^2/2), and its inverse occurs at a negative crossing. After removing it, the ordinary residual twist is theta_j/q^(m^2/2)=q^m=x. The ADO residual twist is x^(1-N)=epsilon_j x. Both conventions give (5). In particular no half-root factor is silently rounded to an integer q power. The proof covers even N and both parities of j. ## 4. The fundamental cable is the literal colored R This comparison is needed to use a positive fundamental path trace for the actual j-color; calling a cable a color is not a proof. Work first over rational functions of q^(1/2), and retain the coproducts Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Formula (2), now as a locally finite operator on highest-weight modules, has the directly verifiable identities (Delta tensor 1)R=R_13 R_23, (1 tensor Delta)R=R_13 R_12. (6) For detail, put Q=q^2 and h=r+s. The finite q-binomial expansion gives (Delta E)^h = sum_(r+s=h) {h choose r}_Q E_1^r E_2^s K_2^r, (Delta F)^h = sum_(r+s=h) {h choose r}_Q F_2^r K_2^(-s) F_3^s, c_h {h choose r}_Q = Q^(rs)c_r c_s. (7) For the first identity of (6), move the R_23 Cartan factor left through E_1^r F_3^r in R_13. It supplies K_2^r; moving it past E_2^s supplies Q^(rs). This is exactly the first expansion in (7). For the second identity, moving the R_12 Cartan factor through the R_13 nilpotent term supplies K_2^(-s), and ordering it with F_2^r again supplies Q^(rs). The second expansion in (7) follows. These coefficient identities prove (6), including the Cartan scalar; they do not assume a tensor-category comparison theorem. The q-binomial identities themselves follow by induction from AB=QBA. Let V_f be the fundamental two-dimensional module. In V_f^(tensor m) put J_m(v_r)=(Delta^(m-1)F)^r(v_0 tensor ... tensor v_0), 0 <= r <= m. (8) The coproduct relations give E J_m(v_r)=[r][m-r+1]J_m(v_(r-1)), F J_m(v_r)=J_m(v_(r+1)), K J_m(v_r)=q^(m-2r)J_m(v_r). The endpoint at r=m+1 is zero. There is a nonzero vector at every weight for m < N, so J_m is an injective intertwiner at the roots under consideration. Repeated use of (6), followed by naturality under this explicitly verified intertwiner, proves B_fused (J_m tensor J_m)=(J_m tensor J_m) B_j, (9) where B_fused is the ordinary m-by-m crossing cable with its m^2 fundamental crossings. The inverse identity follows by invertibility. Equivalently (9) follows by expanding the two sides with (7). The highest-highest entry on each side is q^(m^2/2), so no additional central scalar is available or required. On fundamental 01,10 the operator U=q I-q^(1/2)B_f has block [[q,-1],[-1,q^(-1)]] and is zero on 00,11. The kernel of all adjacent U_i in a fixed weight has dimension one: each adjacent exchange fixes the q-ratio between the two coefficients, and exchanges connect all binary words of that weight. It is the vector in (8). Thus the common kernel has dimension m+1 and is exactly im J_m. The Jones--Wenzl recursion used in the regular-period note has image this common kernel: its image is annihilated by the U_i, and it acts as identity on every common-kernel vector, by induction. Consequently its actual tensor image is precisely the j-color. All specializations in this paragraph are regular for m <= N-2. The recursion uses only [1],...,[m], which are nonzero, and the ordinary R uses only [h]!, h <= m. No projector on a color of zero quantum dimension is used in the bound. The constant-color j=1 case is the empty tensor power and is immediate. ## 5. The trace identification and bound The fundamental coproduct pivot is K^(tensor m), and (8) identifies its restriction with the ordinary pivot K_j. For any operator preserving the idempotent image, finite matrix trace on that image equals Tr(K^(tensor m) p_m A). Applying this to every block of (9) gives the second equality in (1). The framing scalar theta_j is exactly the one in (4). It also follows directly from the positive crossing's pivotal partial trace: its highest-input entry has just the zero-transfer, zero-closed-index summand q^(m^2/2)q^m=theta_j. The fundamental trace obeys tau_(l+1)(A tensor I)=(q+q^(-1))tau_l(A), tau_(l+1)((A tensor I)U_l)=tau_l(A). The second equation is the literal partial pivotal trace of the displayed 2-by-2 block of U. These recursions identify it with the path trace whose local positivity is audited separately. At the principal root q=exp(pi*i/N), that trace is positive, the fundamental braid is unitary, and p_m is an orthogonal projection there. Its trace is [j], and the b-fold projection has trace [j]^b. Therefore |F_N^M(-q^j)|=|F_N^Y(Q^j)|=|C_j(q)| <= [j]^(b-1) <= sin(pi/N)^(1-b) <= (N/2)^(b-1). (10) This applies to every j<N uniformly, with the original one-component source and framing. At j=N the quantum dimension vanishes, so the division in (1) and the positive-color argument do not apply. ## 6. Independent exact audit [The new audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordinary_color_comparison.py) constructs the defining full colored R independently, builds the fundamental coproduct highest-weight embedding (8), constructs the literal crossing cable, and tests both signs of (9). It also assembles the tensor-basis Jones--Wenzl projector, checks its image, generator intertwining and quantum trace, and restores the full Cartan/twist factors. The quotient tests use a separate original N-dimensional matrix construction and compare all colors j<N through complete knot cuts, including four-strand words and non-highest open inputs. A separate closed-component failure is checked explicitly. The finite fixtures check the stated ordinary comparison. They do not establish a full-state pole bound. The checks supplement the all-level arguments above. The result is a verification of the ordinary-color polynomial bound's input, not a volume estimate for the Kashaev color or a claim of reflection positivity of its modified source.

title: An actual generic four-port Clebsch recoupling kernel
text: # An actual generic four-port Clebsch recoupling kernel 29 October 2026. This gives a finite factorial kernel for a typed four-port recoupling, with the ordered unequal-pair norm and pivotal cyclic turn derived directly. All intermediate channels are retained, including high root partners. The coefficients are bilinear ribbon coefficients, not a unitary or positive 6j matrix. No quoted recoupling formula is a premise. Single-sum completion: the independent source construction below is now evaluated by the [generic all-port single Racah theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), including its exact seven-factorial prefactor, half-integral-spin cyclic sign and retained root normals. The two-sum formula here is preserved as an independent actual-source proof and audit input; it is no longer the final unresolved summation gate. The construction supplies an exact local identity before root specialization. Its explicit pole bookkeeping retains the normal data needed in the original marked source. A positive or asymptotic estimate for the primitive cube remains a separate question. ## 1. Generic unequal Clebsch maps Write Q=zeta^2, F_r=(Q;Q)_r. The highest-weight L object has the actual balanced matrices K|u>=zeta^L Q^-u|u>, F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=zeta^(-L-1)(1-Q^(L+1-u))|u-1>. Its canonical cup has first coefficient one: P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)]F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). (1) Take physical highest weights A,B, target C=A+B-2m, with 0<=m<=min(A,B). The first-entry-one highest vector in V_A tensor V_B has entries at (s,m-s) h_s=(-1)^s zeta^[s(A-2B+2m-s-1)] F_(B-m+s)F_(A-s)/(F_(B-m)F_A), 0<=s<=m. (2) The direct highest equation gives h_(s+1)/h_s=-zeta^(A-2B)Q^(m-s-1) (1-Q^(B-m+s+1))/(1-Q^(A-s)). Let W_AB^C[r]=Delta(F)^r h/F_r, 0<=r<=C. Its full finite entry is W_AB^C[r](i,j)=F_i F_j sum_s h_s zeta^(-A t) Q^(st) /[F_s F_(m-s)F_t F_(r-t)], i+j=m+r, t=j-m+s. (3) All indices are required to be physical: 0<=s<=m, 0<=i<=A,0<=j<=B,0<=t<=j,0<=r-t<=i. Otherwise the term is zero. Formula(3) is the direct finite coproduct binomial, with F_r canceled BEFORE specialization. If A,B<N, every denominator in(2),(3) has index<N, even if C or r is >=N. Thus W itself has no root pole. The final F endpoint follows from the commutator and injectivity of E above the physical middle degree, exactly as for the previously proved equal-pair Clebsch map. This proves generic covariance without assuming a decomposition or a semisimple root replacement. ## 2. The ordered bilinear norm, by finite convolution The right dual of W_BA^C is a map on the original A,B order: D(W_BA)=p_C^T W_BA^T(ell_B^T tensor ell_A^T)P_AB, where P_AB changes the displayed A,B input to B,A. The actual norm is D(W_BA^C) W_AB^C=n_AB^C I, n_AB^C=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+m(m-1)] F_(A+B-m+1)/(F_m F_(C+1)). (4) Using D(W_AB) without reversing the object labels is not a typed composition when A!=B. Equation(4) is a rational generic identity; its zeros and any canceled factors are retained. Here is an own finite derivation. The lowest F recurrence gives W_BA^C[C](B-m+s,A-s) =ell_BA zeta^[(B-A)s] h_AB(s), ell_BA=zeta^[-AB+3Bm-2m^2] F_(B-m)F_A/(F_(A-m)F_B). (5) At s=0 the coproduct entry reduces to sum_u(-1)^u Q^[u(u-1)/2] F_(B-u)/(F_u F_(m-u)F_(B-m-u))=Q^[m(B-m)]. This is the elementary finite second Chu identity, proved by finite binomial expansion in the earlier source calculations; all endpoint powers give exactly(5). The recurrences then prove the entire slice. Schur's K,F equations make the composition in(4) scalar. In its highest entry substitute(1),(2),(5). The only remaining convolution, with X=B-m,Y=A-m, is sum_s Q^[-(X+1)s] [X+s choose s]_Q[Y+m-s choose m-s]_Q =Q^[-(X+1)m][X+Y+m+1 choose m]_Q. (6) It is the coefficient of u^m in 1/[(uQ^(-X-1);Q)_(X+1)(u;Q)_(Y+1)], a single contiguous reciprocal product. Its elementary finite-product coefficient formula proves(6). The factorials cancel to those in(4); the sign is (-1)^m and the remaining zeta exponent is -AB+m(m-1). The equal case A=B=d is exactly the independently proved physical norm of the generic six-head tetrahedral source. The generic projectors are consequently Pi_AB^C=W_AB^C D(W_BA^C)/n_AB^C. (7) Different generic Casimir eigenvalues make them mutually orthogonal, and the dimension identity sum_C(C+1)=(A+1)(B+1) proves completeness. This generic identity is not a claim that the individual projectors are regular or orthogonal positive projections at the root. ## 3. Four-port columns and the actual cyclic turn Now use integer spin labels a,b,c,d, with external highest weights 2a,2b,2c,2d. Let e range over I_S=[|a-b|,a+b] intersect [|c-d|,c+d] in integer steps. Write W_ab^e for (2),(3) with highest weights 2a,2b,2e. Define the actual invariant column Psi_e^S=(W_ab^e tensor W_cd^e)p_(2e). (8) The first canonical cup has to be kept, including its possible root pole. It is not replaced by a Euclidean Bell vector. For the other pairing let f range over I_T=[|b-c|,b+c] intersect [|d-a|,d+a]. First form Psi_f in the order B,C,D,A. Bring its last A leg to the front by the GENUINE pivotal cyclic map: Psi_f^T(u,v,w,z)=K_a(u) [(W_bc^f tensor W_da^f)p_(2f)](v,w,z,u). K_a(u)=zeta^(2a-2u). (9) To prove the clock, moving a first highest-L leg to the end by the actual cap/cup has matrix ell_L^T p_L=(-1)^L K_L^(-1). The inverse move multiplies by (-1)^L K_L. Here L=2a is even, giving(9). It is an invariant-column identity; a plain cyclic permutation would give a different kernel. Let Psi_e^rev be (8) with external order d,c,b,a, and dualize it with those actual four cups and reverse the abstract dual order. The exact diagonal norm is D(Psi_e^rev) Psi_g^S=delta_(e,g) N_e, N_e=n_ab^e n_cd^e [2e+1]_zeta. (10) Indeed each ordered pair composition is(4), and the surviving cup and cap give their actual pivotal quantum dimension. No norm square or conjugation is used. All N_e are nonzero generic rational functions. ## 4. A finite all-entry recoupling kernel The complete kernel and all-entry source identity are R_(e,f)=D(Psi_e^rev) Psi_f^T/N_e, Psi_f^T=sum_(e in I_S) R_(e,f) Psi_e^S. (11) Equations(1)--(3),(8),(9) make every entry an explicit terminating factorial sum, with no quoted 6j formula. Weight conservation removes one external magnetic sum. More specifically, for external colors u,v,w,z with u+v+w+z=a+b+c+d, the S column has the single product Psi_e^S(u,v,w,z)=W_ab^e[r](u,v) P_(2e)(r) W_cd^e[2e-r](w,z), r=u+v-(a+b-e). (12) The T column has the analogous product from(9). The dual in(11) uses the reverse complementary external colors and division by their canonical cup coefficients. All those entries are given in(1)--(3). For completeness, the S columns span the generic four-port invariant space: resolve the first pair by(7). The remaining invariant couples that target to the second pair; its homogeneous highest recurrence allows exactly the matching target e, once. Thus the dimension is |I_S|=|I_T| and the diagonal pairing(10) proves(11). It follows that the local four-port invariant tensor can be replaced by(11) against ANY exterior row, including a source-dependent row. A planar source disk with incoming ports is first bent using its actual cups; the inverse bends are retained when using(11) in the original network. ## 5. Root partners and the necessary higher normals Suppose now 0<=a,b,c,d<=M=floor((N-1)/2). All W entries in(3) are holomorphic at q. The cup p_(2e) is regular for e<=M and has at most a simple pole for e>M. The exact norm factors give the following orders, without treating high partners as low ordinary simple modules. For a PAIRED low node 2e<N-1, including e=M at even N, put e*=N-1-e. Then ord_q n_ab^e =1 if e* is in [|a-b|,a+b], else0. The same holds for c,d. At the odd simple 2e=N-1, each n is a unit and [2e+1] has a simple zero. At e>M the zero in the numerator and denominator factorial of(4) cancels, so each n and [2e+1] are units. Thus the low N_e can have order TWO, the odd simple N_e has order one, and high N_e have order zero. These are actual source zeros. In particular each coefficient in(11), and each summand R_(e,f)Psi_e^S, has a pole of order at most THREE. For low e its dual column is regular and N_e has at most two zeros; the input f has at most one pole. For high e the dual and input have at most one pole each, N_e is a unit, and the extra output column supplies at most one more. The odd simple case is smaller. Therefore a local Laurent identity(11) can be checked through its first normal by retaining Taylor ORDER FOUR (five coefficients, degrees0 through4) after multiplication by the cube of a local root parameter. This is a pole-order bound, not a magnitude bound. The pair spectral projector also has at most one pole: only its partner eigenvalue can collide, and that eigenvalue gap has a simple zero away from the odd self-paired node. Summing complete colliding clusters, or retaining the Laurent terms in(11), is necessary BEFORE specialization. Dropping high channels, taking only nodal values, or bounding each singular term separately changes the normal source. The finite kernel does not yet make R unitary or sign-coherent at the principal root. Factorial coefficients and confluence frames can be exponentially large. A primitive cube reduction must retain its entire recoupling sum and original fixed normal, rather than infer positivity from a diagonal norm or real spectral values. ## 6. An explicit highest-chart kernel with just two terminating sums The four-port coefficient can also be evaluated without the full four-color magnetic pairing. Put H=a+b+c-d and use the highest chart w_i=Psi(i,H-i,0,2d), max(0,H-2b)<=i<=min(2a,H). (13) Bending the last leg by the actual canonical cup makes this the third-color-zero slice of a highest-weight-2d three-object vector. The original highest recurrence recovers all its other slices, then the ordinary F descendants recover the entire four-port column. Thus this chart is injective; it is not an arbitrary packet truncation. The MIDDLE-pair Casimir on a valid highest chart is the upper-bidiagonal operator B e_i=lambda_i e_i+b_i e_(i-1), lambda_i=zeta^(2d-2a+1)Q^i+zeta^(-2d+2a-1)Q^-i, b_i=-zeta^(2b+2c-2a-1)Q^(i-H) (1-Q^(2a+1-i))(1-Q^(H-i+1)). (14) To derive it, lift w into the third object using its actual highest recurrence. In the third-color-zero extraction of Omega_bc only third colors0 and1 can contribute. Their F_b E_b terms cancel, leaving -zeta^(2c)F_b E_a K_b plus the two Cartan terms, which is (14). If c=0 the absent color1 is not introduced; the same formula agrees on the valid kernel E_ab w=0. Thus (14) is always used on the actual highest-source subspace. For f in I_T put i0=a+f-d, and define the generic left eigenrow ell_f(i)=0 for i<i0, ell_f(i0)=1, ell_f(i)=product_(j=i0+1)^i[-b_j/(lambda_j-lambda_i0)]. (15) The row equation directly proves ell_f B=c_f ell_f. For the T_f column, (9) shows its chart is zero when i>i0. Its value at i0 is the following explicit NONZERO normalization: beta_f=zeta^(2a-2i0) h_bc^f(b+c-f) *(-1)^(d+a-f) *zeta^[-4da+4d(d+a-f)-(d+a-f)(d+a-f+1)]. (16) The last factor is the lowest physical endpoint of W_da^f; it follows by substituting s=m in(5). There is no unspecified eigenvector scale. For the S_e chart, put u_e=c+e-d. Its exact scalar is w_e(i)=chi_e W_ab^e[u_e](i,H-i), chi_e=(-1)^u_e zeta^[u_e(2e-u_e-1)-2c(d-c+e)] F_(u_e)F_(2d)/(F_(c+d-e)F_(2e)). (17) This is the unique s=0 coproduct contribution at the external colors (third=0,fourth=2d) in (12). Hence the INVERSE recoupling has the explicit finite formula Psi_e^S=sum_(f in I_T) L_(f,e)Psi_f^T, L_(f,e)=chi_e/beta_f *sum_(i=i0)^min(2a,H) ell_f(i) W_ab^e[u_e](i,H-i). (18) There is one displayed magnetic sum, and each W entry is the single finite factorial sum(3). All remaining factors are finite products. To prove (18), eigenrows with different generic c_f kill the other right channels; the support just noted gives ell_f(w_f)=beta_f. Injectivity of the highest chart then proves the ALL-ENTRY identity. Equivalently the matrices in(11),(18) are inverse. This is a concrete finite two-sum Racah kernel derived from the original operators, not a quoted hypergeometric recoupling coefficient. It also exposes cancellations hidden in the diagonal norm. At the principal root beta_f is a unit: all its factorial indices are external physical indices <N. Chi_e has at most one pole, precisely from F_(2e) on a high channel. In ell_f there can be at most one colliding denominator, from f*=N-1-f; its zero is simple, and it is absent for a high f or an odd self-paired node. Therefore each coefficient in (18) has pole order at most TWO. The cyclically interchanged formula gives the same bound for(11). Its product with an output column still has at most three poles, so the fixed-normal instruction in section5 is unchanged. No pole is discarded by evaluating an individual partner at the root. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.py) passes 44 exact unequal Clebsch/norm channels, 61 four-port external families and all185 recoupling entries, the separate highest-chart two-sum inverse at all61 families/185 entries, and eight full-partner/root families N=2,...,9. The latter construct high-channel W by(3) without dividing by the vanished F_N, check their actual E,F,K covariance, and compare the uncanceled norm-factor zero count with the exact partner condition. Both even central PAIRED and odd central SIMPLE nodes are included. These checks supplement the finite proofs, not a growing-color asymptotic or conditioning assertion.

title: The original marked boundary source and its transverse stationary point
status: Marked stationary force and absolute volume
text: # The original marked boundary source and its transverse stationary point 30 October 2026. This concerns the specified original six-type boundary source, at fixed real integer channel labels approaching the fold. Its actual marked cap cancels the limiting linear magnetic force. This gives a nearby transverse stationary point and a constructed local period. It does not identify their coefficient in the original support cycle. An independent coning calculation below identifies its absolute leading real rate with Vol(Q)/pi, where Q is the actual right-angled half-polyhedron; it does not use a finite-r sheet assertion. The logarithmic source coordinates, exact scalar factors and original mark are part of the statement. No additional winding character is introduced in the marked-source conclusion. ## 1. The literal regular circle lift has no extra root character Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, 0<=a<=floor(d/2), m=d-a, s=d-2a, and F_j=(Q;Q)_j. Write S_j for the positive sine factorial and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2. Retain the original constants h0_a=k_a N beta_a, gamma_a=q^(2-a^2)/N^2, P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j). All heads in this section use the specified moving-factorial continuation of the [regular original source](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md). Let sigma=i+j, r=sigma-m, x=2a-r=d+a-sigma, T=Q^sigma. At the root its ordinary channel cup is exactly p_(2a)(x)=F_s q^[2m(d+a)] T^(-a)/P_s(T). (1) This is a meromorphic identity, including its removable specializations. Indeed the fixed-root factorial reflection first gives p_(d-s)(x)=F_s exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)). At x=d+a-sigma its denominator is T^(-s)P_s(T), and exp(pi i x)q^[(s-1)x]=q^(2mx). This proves (1) with its literal logarithmic character. The actual generic reversal, specialized only after it is used, gives W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=q^[s(a-r)] W_a(i,j;r), pV(d-j)pV(d-i)=N^2 q^(-d sigma). Thus the literal categorical dual is retained in the product. For an output row R and input row S at the same total sigma, substitute W_a(R,sigma-R;r) =(-1)^m q^[d(R-sigma)+m(a+1)] H_m(Q^R,Q^(sigma-R))/F_m and the same formula for S. Use the exact root collision H_m=P_s(T)H_a and H_a=q^(a sigma)K_a R_a, where K_a=F_(2a)/F_a^2 and R_a has its actual monic normalization. The remaining head dependence of h0_a W_a pi_a is q^[d(R+S)-2m sigma] P_s(T) R_a(q^(sigma-2R);c_sigma)R_a(q^(sigma-2S);c_sigma). The entire coefficient C_a in the [absolute regulator normalization](actual_matching_edge_deficient_packet_regulator.md) has precisely this dependence, because its residual sine product obeys V_a(d-sigma)=q^(-sd-s sigma)P_s(T). The ratio of the two scalars, retaining gamma_a and h0_a, reduces by F_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]S_j and S_j S_(d-j)=N to q^[-2N(-2N+a+3)]=1. Consequently, as the SPECIFIED root continuations, h0_a W_a pi_a = C_a. (2) This uses both actual LARGE numerators and the actual dual cups. It does not differentiate a root collision, identify moving-q germs, or replace the separately recorded bare canceled/turned continuation by this one. The retained half twist is a fixed-channel scalar on both sides and changes no magnetic derivative. There is a useful exact homogeneous form, valid for EVERY folded label; the [positive face-polynomial theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md) gives its independent local proof, both-parity carry convention, full coefficient positivity and the physical support-zero audit. Define D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y). For positive formal face diagonals x=L0, y=L2 and the two middle diagonals b,c, use the marked raw clocks -x/b,-b/y and -x/c,-c/y. Then (2) is exactly h0_a W_a pi_a =k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)Ptilde_s(x,y) /(bc)^(d/2). (2a) Indeed H_a=(-q^-1)^a K_a D_a/L2^a and P_s(Q^sigma)=q^(-2s)L2^(-s)Ptilde_s. Substitute these into the calculation above. Its remaining scalar phase is (-1)^d q^[d-sd-2s-2a]=(-1)^(d+s)=1. In this computation q^sigma=-q^-1 sqrt(x/y) and the two negative physical raw clocks have their canonical argument pi. The identity extends with those marked half powers; at odd N the powers are integral. This is not a replacement of an even-level marked square root by an unrecorded principal branch. The numerator in (2a) has degree 2a+s=d. ## 2. Source coordinates and the local angle-force input Fix the labeled certified diagram and the common boundary sample r_frame=N rho, s_frame=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1. The parameters range in the compact sets of the [common boundary chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). Keep the actual physical half-index shifts, auxiliary integer offsets, all original turns, the ordinary or marked exposed cap, and fixed labels with S=sum_i(d-2a_i)=o(N). Use LOGARITHMIC CLOCK potentials Z_f, not normalized head potentials. Their homogeneous physical variations are delta h_e=N(delta Z_left-delta Z_right)/(2pi i). (3) The [literal face-lattice theorem](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) proves that the integer face differences give the original primitive homogeneous lattice. A common additive constant is immaterial. Exactly two faces have constant prefixes; write Qcal for the other, quadratic faces. The actual sample has Z_f=Log L_f with all source marks retained. For clarity the local analytic input needed here is stated explicitly. At an ordered white triangle with faces f0,f1,f2, let theta_j be the angle at the center of its j-th circle in the tangent-circle triangle. A constant-prefix line has limiting angle zero. At the common sample, the normalized logarithmic derivative of its literal W numerator and white monomial tends uniformly to sum_(j=0)^2 theta_j dZ_fj/(2pi) - dZ_f1/2. (4) The theta sum is pi. This statement is obtained from the actual finite cores, not from a finite-r identification of their sheets with the geometric critical branch. For 222, with alpha_*=a_f0/(2a_f1), beta_*=a_f2/(2a_f1), its derivatives are theta_0/(2pi)=atan(2alpha_*/sqrt(2alpha_*+2beta_*+4alpha_*beta_*))/pi, theta_2/(2pi)=atan(2beta_*/sqrt(2alpha_*+2beta_*+4alpha_*beta_*))/pi. The actual H Ward equations and positive finite determinant select these angles. The 220 and 022 formulas are their one-line limits. The 202 positive polynomial gives theta_0=2atan(sqrt(T_raw)) and theta_2=pi-theta_0. The 200 and 002 top terms give respectively (theta_0,theta_1,theta_2)=(pi,0,0) and (0,0,pi). All root partner products and near-fold cup corrections are retained; their normalized first-derivative errors tend to zero when S=o(N). Here are source proofs of the force limits, including the boundary cases. Put p=N^-1 partial_logU Log H and r=N^-1 partial_logV Log H. The exact two white Ward equations, the O(N) second-log-derivative bounds, and Q=exp(2pi i/N) give at the fold (1-U)t_U+U(1-V)t_V=1+UV, (1-U)/t_U+U(1-V)/t_V=1+UV, t_U=exp(2pi i p), t_V=exp(2pi i r). (4a) The errors before taking the limit are O((s+1)/N) on a 222 compact. Its positive matrix gives p,r in a compact subset of (0,1/2): each relevant positive trace has a bulk lower bound, as does its complement. For U=-u,V=-v the unique upper-semicircle solution is p=atan(u sqrt(v)/sqrt(1+u+uv))/pi, r=atan(sqrt(v(1+u+uv)))/pi. Its triangle discriminant is positive and separated from zero on the specified compacts. Thus it gives uniform derivative convergence, not just an identity satisfied by a putative geometric saddle. The elementary circle cosine law makes these exactly the angles in (4). For 220 the determinant-rate theorem extends to its zero second coefficient uniformly using H_+<=2H_-+8I. Its fixed holomorphic logarithmic bounds give derivative convergence. At the fold the derivative integral is integral_0^(1/2) [1-cos(pi t)/sqrt(cos^2(pi t)+u)]dt =atan(sqrt(u))/pi. The last equality follows by y=sin(pi t). The other H force tends to 1/2. Exact reciprocity gives 022. For 202 the positive coefficient ratios give the mode equation tan(pi kappa)=sqrt(T_raw)sin(pi a/N) /[1+sqrt(T_raw)cos(pi a/N)]. The already proved Gaussian weight bound and variance O(N) imply mean/N-kappa=O(N^-1/2), uniformly. This tends to the stated atan formula. Finally the exact top terms of 200/002 have H forces (m/N,m/N)+O(N^-1) and (0,0)+O(N^-1), respectively. Their nonzero Bessel remainders have bounded logarithmic derivatives. Multiplication by the original white monomial subtracts d/(2N) from the second H force. The large partner and root cup corrections cost O((s+1)/N) in normalized first derivatives, using the actual separated factors. These arguments prove (4), locally uniformly with its marked phases. No uniform quantitative rate beyond o(1) is needed below. ## 3. The integer covector is computed from the original turns At a literal physical cup or cap write its first-head variable as its actual signed face difference plus the affine offset. The exact root cup pV(x)=N q^(-d^2)q^(dx), and its ordered inverse cap, contribute in the normalized limit one half of a SIGNED face difference. Let epsilon_(b,f) be that signed incidence for the original turn b. This is read from the cup or cap entry; it is not chosen afterward. Let chi_f be the integer face-incidence vector of the retained marked versus ordinary cap character. For the specified mark this follows directly from Xi_N(x)=N^-1 q^(-d^2)Q^(dx). Here x is the SECOND ordered cap head: the original cap and mark are q^(di)/N and q^(dj)/N^2 at (i,j)=(d-x,x). If u is the cap's outside face and v its inside face, the raw second clock is -L_v/L_u; the mark therefore contributes +1 at v and -1 at u. A retained literal cyclic turn is treated by its actual monomial in the same way. Let M_f count the middle white corners at the trivalent vertices. Then the limiting normalized logarithmic derivative of the original full root product S_N is the explicit covector nu_f=1_(f in Qcal)-M_f/2 +(1/2)sum_b epsilon_(b,f)+chi_f. (5) The angle contribution is 1 on a bounded circle because the consecutive tangent-circle triangles sweep its full 2pi angle. It is zero at each of the two constant-prefix lines. This is the actual circle-packing incidence, not a sum of independently optimized vertices. Every nu_f is an INTEGER. To prove this in the original uncontracted Morse graph, traverse the closed boundary of a white face and record whether its direction agrees with the source-edge orientation. At a middle corner the two main legs are both incoming or both outgoing, so this agreement flips. At a main-matching corner one leg is incoming and one outgoing, so it does not flip. It flips at a literal cup or cap. Returning to the start implies that M_f plus the number of turns at f is even. The sign of a turn is irrelevant modulo two, proving the integrality in (5). This argument is unchanged by the literal pi reduction. Before that reduction dualization reverses all THREE ports; each adjacent face meets two of these local turns. Deleting them preserves turn parity. Algebraically its cup/physical-inverse-cup ratio has no leading magnetic derivative at the fold: when 2a=d its q exponent is d[(d-r)-(2d-i-j)]=d(m-d), which is label-only. The exact near-fold remainder is not deleted. Thus the parity calculation and the reduced two-W calculation of (4) refer to the same source. Also sum_f nu_f=0. There are 2R white vertices and R quadratic faces; the total middle count is 2R, while every turn and mark incidence has sum zero. Hence (5) defines an integral covector on face potentials modulo their common constant. For the original flat-plat presentation the signed count is stronger. At a horizontal slice let the gaps between its 2k ordered heads carry the actual white-region labels. A box in slot a removes the old middle gap a+1 at its pi vertex and introduces a new one at its W vertex. Each odd gap begins at a bottom cup and ends at a top cap. Every bounded segment of such a region has exactly two endpoints: middle vertices or inside cups/caps. The internal even gaps begin and end in the exterior. Each must be met by at least one box: otherwise the plat separates across that gap, contrary to the one-main-component hypothesis. Its bounded intermediate segments have two middle endpoints. Thus, with the LITERAL cup signs, every bounded face has M_f-turn_f=2, turn_f=sum_b epsilon_(b,f). The exterior has M_out=2(k-1) and turn_out=2k, hence index -2. An inside cup/cap contributes -1 to turn and its outside contributes +1; this follows directly from its raw first-head ratio -L_out/L_in. Consequently the exact physical monomial after (2a) is L_out^d product_(bounded f) L_f^(-d). (5a) The two constant faces are precisely this exterior and the inside face of the marked cap. The mark contributes -d at the former and +d at the latter. In fact its scalar is exactly Xi_N=N^-1 (L_in/L_out)^d, (5b) since q^(-d^2)(-q^-1)^d=(-1)^d q^(-Nd)=1. This proves nu_f=0 for EVERY face of the original marked source. (5c) The ordinary closed source instead has the two charges +1 at the exterior and -1 at the other constant face. They are canceled by the actual mark, not by an invented winding choice. For the specified compact parameter sets, (4) therefore implies (1/N)d Log S_N(Z_N) = o(1) (6) uniformly for shrinking folded deficits. Fixed-channel h0, gamma and half-twist phases have zero magnetic derivative but stay in S_N. ## 4. Retained normalization and the distinction from a winding change The preceding signed count also records the complete formal-face normalization. On the positive face-log branch each original bottom cup has scalar N q^(-d^2/2), and each ordinary top cap has scalar N^-1 q^(d^2/2); their k pairs cancel. Equation (5b) supplies the remaining 1/N. Hence the uncontracted original marked sector is N^-1 product_i[k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] * product_i[D_(a_i,in)D_(a_i,out)Ptilde_(s_i)] /product_(quadratic f)L_f^d. (7) The original exterior framing line remains separate and unchanged. The identities extend with the specified source marks. Formula (7) does not itself convert a physical finite sum to an unrestricted face torus, or settle its support and alias conditions. For comparison, if one keeps the ordinary cap, or uses another already proved presentation with the integer cochain (5), an exact lattice-one winding change can be specified as follows. This comparison is NOT used to obtain (5c). Choose an INTEGER affine source origin h^0 for the fixed labels and support stratum. Its corresponding potential origin Z^0 includes the actual half-index constants. Every original integer source state has Z-Z^0=(2pi i/N)n, n integral modulo constants. The entire character C_nu,N(Z)=exp[-N sum_f nu_f(Z_f-Z_f^0)] equals one at every such state. Multiplying the original summand by this displayed character preserves its original finite sum, and all residues on its original small node tori. It does not equate differently transported support chains. The affine-origin factor exp(N nu dot Z^0) is retained, even when its real logarithm has leading size. Define the particular sector logarithm g_N(Z)=Log S_N(Z)-N nu dot(Z-Z^0). (8) For the original MARKED source nu=0 and g_N=Log S_N exactly. For the comparison presentation its normalized gradient at the boundary sample tends to zero after the displayed explicit correction. The subtracted character can change the real off-grid action. Accordingly (8) is a specified winding representative, not an assertion that the original global cycle selects this representative or that its critical value is the marked geometric volume. The exact identity (2) prevents an additional accidental circle character; it does not compute an unproved global winding coefficient. ## 5. Local transverse critical point and a constructed local period Fix the two neighboring original physical heads from the primitive slice theorem. Equivalently take its fixed integral complementary log-clock basis C and write Z=Z_N+Cw, w in C^n, n=R-1. The existing rank theorem and [finite core curvature](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md) give, in this basis, a real positive reference Hessian bounded between cN I and CN I. The exact finite clocks and near-fold corrections change it by o(N). On a fixed complex neighborhood all fixed derivatives of order at least two are O(N). These statements include both parities. Set e_N=|N^-1 partial_w g_N(0)|, so e_N tends uniformly to zero by (6). The Hessian divided by N has inverse bounded uniformly, and its derivative is bounded on a smaller fixed ball. Newton's contraction, using that Hessian at zero, therefore gives a unique zero w_N in a ball of radius C e_N. Explicitly the Newton remainder is at most C|w|^2, so the map sends that ball into itself and has contraction constant at most C e_N for sufficiently large N. Thus partial_w g_N(w_N)=0, |w_N|<=C e_N=o(1). (9) This is a transverse sector-critical point; it does not assert that the finite-label geometric sample itself is stationary. Nor does it assert that the two remaining finite framing forces vanish. Without a quantitative rate for (6), the head displacement is only o(N). Let H_N be the w Hessian at w_N. Its real part remains at least cN I. For fixed sufficiently small eta>0 the oriented local contour w=w_N+i x, x in [-eta,eta]^n, obeys Re[g_N(w_N+i x)-g_N(w_N)]<=-cN|x|^2. Taylor's theorem proves this from the Hessian and O(N) third derivative. The standard rescaling x=N^-1/2 y can here be verified directly: the cubic correction is odd and integrates to zero on the symmetric box against the even complex Gaussian; the quartic correction and square of the cubic have relative size O(N^-1), and the remaining tails are exponentially small. Uniform higher derivative bounds give integral_(w_N+i[-eta,eta]^n) exp(g_N(w)) dw = i^n (2pi)^(n/2) exp(g_N(w_N))/sqrt(det H_N) *[1+O(N^-1)]. (10) The square root is the continuation from the positive reference matrix. All source scalars and the affine-origin character remain in the displayed exponential. If the chosen flat source measure is the actual unscaled free-head measure, the exact coordinate Jacobian contributes (N/(2pi i))^n. Any cotangent kernels or additional boundary currents must be retained separately; they are not implicitly replaced by that flat measure. Equation (10) is a nonzero explicitly constructed LOCAL period. No intersection with the original finite-support cycle, residue transport, mixed-color comparison, or asymptotic for the fully contracted source is inferred. ## 6. The absolute rate from the actual coned polyhedron This section supplies an absolute geometric normalization without identifying the finite-r selected sheets with a geometric critical branch. The potential and coning identities themselves require only the connected certified right-angled graph and a marked main edge; they do not require that all main strands form one component. The one-main-component hypothesis remains in the earlier finite-r six-type boundary-chart and local-period assertions. Let a_f>0 be the actual curvatures of the bounded white circles in the marked coordinate p=infinity, and set a_f=0 at its two white lines. A common positive scale is immaterial. For one shaded triangle write its three curvatures as (x,b,y), and let F(x,b,y)=lim_(a/N->1/2) N^-1 Log D_a(x,b,y). The limit and its first derivatives follow from the actual finite determinant rate and the preceding boundary limits. It is homogeneous in the logarithmic sense F(tx,tb,ty)=F(x,b,y)+(1/2)log t. For three positive curvatures set Delta=sqrt(xb+by+yx), theta_j=2atan(a_j/Delta). These are the center-triangle angles, their sum is pi, and (4) says partial_log a_j F=theta_j/(2pi). Consequently V_tri=2pi F-sum_j theta_j log a_j has differential -sum_j log(tan(theta_j/2))dtheta_j. The common log Delta disappears because sum_j dtheta_j=0. Define the usual Lobachevsky function by Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin u|du. Direct differentiation now gives V_tri=2 sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2) +Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)] + constant. (11) The constant is ZERO, with the source normalization still retained. Indeed at (x,0,0), D_a=(x/2)^a det H_-. The exact original LDL pivots give det H_-=product_(n=1)^a sin(n pi/N)/[cos(n pi/N)sin((2n-1)pi/N)]. Their normalized logarithm tends to (1/2)log2, by the elementary log-sine Riemann sum. Thus F(x,0,0)=(1/2)log x and V_tri=0. This is also the continuous boundary value of the determinant rate: set the second matrix coefficient to zero by H_+<=2H_-+8I, then let the identity coefficient tend to zero in its explicit rate integral. After subtracting (1/2)log alpha its integrand is dominated by C+2|log cos(pi t)| and tends to -log2-2log cos(pi t). The right side of (11) tends to zero at (pi,0,0). This fixes the absolute constant and includes all one-line degenerations. The actual facets identify the sum in (11) with volume. Cone the marked ideal vertex p=infinity to every nonincident facet of the convex Q. These positive pyramids partition Q, as in the existing positive polyhedron triangulation. For a WHITE ideal polygon on a finite circle, let delta_j be its consecutive central arcs. Its cone volume is sum_j Lambda(delta_j/2). To verify this, triangulate the actual cyclic polygon from one of its vertices. Each ideal tetrahedron with fourth vertex infinity contributes the three Lobachevsky values of its Euclidean triangle angles. Internal diagonals occur with complementary half-arcs t and pi-t, and cancel by Lambda(pi-t)=-Lambda(t). Only the boundary half-arcs remain. No new ideal vertex or unsigned overlapping decomposition is introduced. At a shaded triangle the consecutive contact arcs on a neighboring white circle are exactly its center angle theta_j. Orthogonality of the white and shaded circles gives two right angles in the quadrilateral of their centers and their two intersections. Hence the shaded arc between those intersections is pi-theta_j. The shaded ideal triangle coned to infinity therefore has volume sum_j Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2). Summing the white pyramids and shaded tetrahedra over their ACTUAL facet incidences proves Vol(Q)=sum_(shaded triangles) sum_j [Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)] =(1/2)sum_(shaded triangles) V_tri. (12) The two incident white lines have zero cone volume. Incident shaded triangles give the (pi,0,0) limiting angles and contribute zero as well. Thus (12) retains the marked cusp and every actual facet; it is not a separately maximized local-polyhedron comparison. Evaluate the homogeneous source polynomial at these curvatures, with the two constant faces set to zero. Its limiting normalized real log, including the target monomial of (7), is Phi=sum_(shaded triangles)F(a_f0,a_f1,a_f2) -sum_(quadratic f)log a_f. The angle sums at every bounded white circle are 2pi. Equations (11),(12) therefore give the ABSOLUTE identity 2pi Phi=sum_tri V_tri=2Vol(Q), Phi=Vol(Q)/pi=Vol(actual augmented complement)/(2pi). (13) The remaining original fixed-channel scalars have not been discarded. For shrinking folded deficits, N^-1 log beta_a^2 tends to 2J(2a/N)-4J(a/N), hence to zero because J(1)=J(1/2)=0. The positive root forced product has logarithmic size O(s) on these curvature compacts, including a zero endpoint curvature; its normalized rate also tends to zero. The factors k_a and 1/N are polynomial, and the retained half-twist powers have modulus one at actual integer labels. Their exact values stay in (7). The original finite-r face diagonals have one common quadratic scale (b_ref/s_frame)N^2 rho^2 and relative error O(N^-1); their two constant diagonals divided by that scale tend to zero. Total homogeneity of degree dR cancels this common complex scale against the target monomial EXACTLY. The six source packets, with their retained top monomials and nonzero Bessel factors, then give the same normalized real rate (13). Their finite transport factors are not reset to one; they have zero normalized logarithmic rate. The nearby critical displacement in (9) changes N^-1 Re g_N by o(1), so it has the same value (13). This proves the absolute rate of the original marked boundary sample and of the constructed local transverse period. It still does not prove that an original finite-support period contains that local contour with nonzero coefficient, or control cancellation in the full auxiliary-label sum or in external filling colors. ## 7. Focused source and absolute-normalization checks The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_original_boundary_stationary_character_results.json), checks 34 literal marked-cap ratios and 34 physical cup/cap scalar pairs, 60 actual Morse charts with 810 signed face indices and zero marked forces, 48 original LARGE-H Ward identities in all six boundary regimes, 40 original LDL products, nine reciprocal-radius circle-angle identities, three absolute determinant-rate/Lobachevsky comparisons, and seven cyclic-polygon fan cancellations. The arithmetic is at 90 digits. Twenty-four finite force errors are retained as convergence diagnostics, not substituted for the uniform derivative proof. The Morse region compiler is shared with the independently audited full marked coefficient transformation. The local all-label circle identity has its separate original-white/dual/cup audit in the positive face-polynomial theorem. No new source-cycle assertion is attached to these numerical checks. The original cycle and the full auxiliary-label sum remain separate from the local transverse result.

text: # The original boundary source has exactly two flat face directions 30 October 2026. On the labeled original right-angled matching graph, the finite boundary models detect every homogeneous magnetic direction except two explicit face potentials. Two neighboring original physical heads give a primitive slice for those directions. This statement includes the closed source and the common fixed-charge two-cut lattice; arbitrary routed extra factors are excluded. Together with the separate local curvature estimates, the result gives a uniformly invertible transverse Hessian for the actual nonzero ROOT source product at the resonant boundary sample, in a shrinking folded-channel window. It does NOT say that this sample is stationary, perform a Gaussian contraction, or assign a coefficient in the original relative period. ## 1. The literal graph and its homogeneous lattice Use the labeled certificate and original reference meridian of the [common boundary chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). Let Delta be its plane cubic graph, with R matching edges D and 2R vertices. The [full original source](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), section 2, identifies this SAME graph with the actual W/pi contraction: matching edges carry V_(2a_i), and all other edges carry V_d, d=N-1. Cups, caps, reversals, and the cyclic order at every vertex are retained. No new routing braid is inserted. For an oriented typed edge of highest weight L_e center its head by z_e=h_e-L_e/2. The actual degree equation at each vertex is exactly sum_out z_e-sum_in z_e=0. (1) Changing an edge orientation replaces z_e by -z_e. A literal cup or cap replaces h by L_e-h, which makes precisely this sign change in centered variations. Thus degree-two bends can be contracted without changing the integral HOMOGENEOUS lattice. Half-integral centered basepoints when L_e is odd do not change that lattice: its variations remain integral. For fixed channel labels, the retained half twist multiplies the original circle term by its exact scalar omega_a^epsilon. The full-source identity already includes the physical reversal in pi. Consequently half twists do not add a magnetic constraint, remove a graph edge, or add a free magnetic variable to (1). Their scalar phases remain in the source. Write B for the oriented incidence matrix of Delta. Its homogeneous lattice is V_Z=ker_Z B, dim_C V=|E|-|V|+1=R+1. (2) The certificate makes Delta connected. Its white faces are the actual projection regions, not freely identified copies of developed faces. There are R+2 of them. Let P_f be one additive potential per white face, modulo a common additive constant. Assign to an oriented edge the difference of its left and right face potentials, with the sign chosen to agree with (1). This gives an integral isomorphism Z^(white faces)/Z(1,...,1) = V_Z. (3) Here is an elementary proof of surjectivity, including primitivity. Given an integral divergence-free edge assignment, integrate it along paths in the dual graph from a fixed face. Around a dual face, the sum is the original vertex divergence, hence zero. Every closed dual walk on the sphere is a sum of these oriented face boundaries; cutting it at repetitions and filling its simple components proves this directly. The potential is therefore well defined and integral. Its only ambiguity is the initial constant. Conversely differences have zero divergence because the consecutive faces around a vertex telescope. This proves (3) over the integers, not only by a dimension count. At an ordered shaded triangle with white regions (f0,f1,f2), the physical variations are, up to the fixed orientation, P_f0-P_f1, P_f1-P_f2, and the auxiliary variation is their sum P_f0-P_f2. This is also the differential of the actual prefix clocks X=-L_f0/L_f1, Y=-L_f1/L_f2. For a literal dual white, its heads are (d-j,d-i), so the two physical variations are reversed and negated and the auxiliary variation is negated. No dual row is incorrectly identified with the physical row. ## 2. The exact finite-clock rank In the common reference normalization, precisely two white faces contain the marked ideal vertex p: call them u,v. Their prefixes have zero lower-left entry. Every other white face has strictly positive normal coefficient and a quadratic prefix diagonal. This follows from the strict supporting inequalities of the labeled certificate. A right-angled ideal vertex has exactly two incident white and two incident shaded faces. The [white-normal polyhedron](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), sections 2--3, is a convex three-dimensional polyhedron C whose vertices are these white faces and whose facets are the original shaded triangles. Its boundary is a triangulated sphere. An edge of C corresponds to an edge of Delta; u,v are joined by the original marked MAIN edge e0. Define L on (3) from each literal numerator by the following head rows: | Numerator type | Rows of L | | --- | --- | | 200, 002 | none | | 220 | first physical variation | | 022 | second physical variation | | 202 | sum of the two physical variations | | 222 | both physical variations | Pull these rows back through the actual dual reversal when the numerator is in pi. Row signs or invertible local changes of these rows do not change their common kernel. All six types, including 202/202 pairs, are allowed. No exclusion at rectangle parameter c=1 is made. The equations L P=0 say exactly that every pair of QUADRATIC white-face potentials belonging to one shaded triangle is equal. The induced graph on all vertices of C other than u,v is connected. To prove this without an external connectivity theorem, start with any path in the connected 1-skeleton. Remove occurrences of u by rerouting through its cyclic vertex link. In the resulting graph, occurrences of v can be rerouted through its link with u removed. This link is a cycle or a path and is connected. The replacement never returns to u. Thus any two surviving vertices remain joined. Every surviving edge is in a shaded triangle and its endpoints are both quadratic, so its equality is among the equations of L. Consequently all quadratic-face potentials coincide. After subtracting that common value, ker L={P_u,P_v arbitrary; P_f=0 for f!=u,v}, dim ker L=2, rank L=R-1. (4) This is a theorem about independent original source variables. It does not extend the critical-scheme/representation inverse off criticality. The two directions are precisely the LIMITING geometric framing tangents. At r=N rho the quadratic prefix logarithms have common varying part 2 Log rho-Log s. Write the two constant prefixes as e_u(1+z_u s), e_v(1+z_v s). The original marked primitive meridian makes z_u-z_v=+1 or -1: in the reference convention these are I and -J or its recorded reciprocal. After subtracting one quadratic face potential, the two remaining variable parts are P_u=-2 Log rho+Log s+Log(1+z_u s), P_v=-2 Log rho+Log s+Log(1+z_v s). (4a) The exact constant signs, face coefficients, and common 2 Log N are retained additive constants and disappear only on differentiation. The Jacobian of (4a) in (Log rho,s) has determinant 2(z_u-z_v)/[(1+z_u s)(1+z_v s)] != 0. (4b) It and its inverse are uniformly bounded on the specified compact chart. Thus these two complete-geometry tangent directions span (4). This is not a stationarity claim for the actual finite auxiliary labels. ## 3. A neighboring physical-head slice is primitive The marked main edge e0 separates u,v, so its homogeneous head is P_u-P_v up to sign. Choose either shaded triangle adjacent to e0 and let w be its third white vertex. It is different from u,v and hence quadratic. Each shaded triangle has exactly one matching edge and two main edges. Since e0 is main, exactly one of its other two edges is also MAIN. Call that edge e1. It joins w to u or to v. On ker L, the two actual head functionals at e0,e1 therefore have matrix, up to the recorded row and column signs, [[1,-1],[1,0]] or [[1,-1],[0,1]]. (5) Their determinant is +1 or -1. Thus fixing these two actual physical heads removes exactly the two flat directions, with a primitive, diagram-independent integer minor. This chooses source integration coordinates; it does NOT authorize a new single-port co-source, move an observable through a braid, or claim that e1 is first in an existing Morse slice. The slice W={head_e0=head_e1=0} in homogeneous variations has dimension R-1, and L|_W is injective. Because the diagram is fixed, choose an integral basis of W once. In that basis its smallest singular value is a positive diagram-dependent constant, independent of N and the frame. Alternatively fixing the two constant-face potentials directly is a primitive complementary slice with the same conclusion. An arbitrary second physical head need not work. If both its adjacent white faces are quadratic, its restriction to ker L is zero. In general the exact test is the rank of the two cut-head rows restricted to (4). The corresponding kernel dimension after fixing the heads is 2 minus that rank. No generic-cut transversality is silently assumed. ## 4. Closed, marked-open, and fixed-charge two-cut sources For the original marked source, equality of the two exposed heads is the permitted WHOLE-SOURCE consequence of integer degree conservation. It is not a local replacement of the unrestricted mark by an invariant cap. After that equality, restoring the exposed edge gives exactly (2), with its actual marked scalar weight still attached. The marked-open chart including the one free exposed head therefore has the same homogeneous space V. Fixing that head imposes its one displayed linear functional. For two cuts on DISTINCT original edges use the actual port orientations of the [common charged chart](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md): the heads are (a,a+delta) and (l,l+delta). At a FIXED charge delta, subtract one recorded affine particular solution. Variations then have equal heads across each cut and restore exactly a cycle flow on Delta. Thus, when a,l are included as coordinates, the homogeneous space is again V and (4) applies unchanged. Fixing a,l gives the slice obtained by setting their two cut-head functionals to zero, so (5) is the promised sufficient condition for a full transverse slice. The deleted graph is connected for two distinct edges of this certified Delta. Indeed it is the dual of the triangulated sphere boundary of C. If deleting at most two dual edges disconnected its triangles, the boundary between a nonempty proper set of triangles and its complement would be a nonempty edge cycle with at most two edges. A simplicial sphere has no such cycle. This also proves that a single original edge is not a bridge. If two cut positions lie on the SAME edge, or a routed source uses a different graph, retain the component conditions of the common charged-chart theorem instead; the preceding conclusion need not apply. Varying delta itself adds an affine relative-boundary direction. It is not a closed cycle flow and is NOT counted as a third flat framing variable by (4). The neighboring-band quotient fixes delta to +1 or -1 after its single analytic interpolation. The two physical support cycles still differ; (3)--(5) do not identify them or erase an endpoint current. ## 5. Assembly of the finite transverse curvature bounds This section uses the separately proved local estimates in [the finite boundary curvature theorem](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md). Retain the exact models of the [correlated-band theorem](actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.md), their scalar phases, the literal pi reversal, and every cup and mark. The statement concerns the original uncontracted root product. It does not include the nonlinear binomial co-source or replace its actual weight. Use logarithmic face coordinates, so a physical clock is multiplied by exp(P_f-P_g). Equivalently the finite head changes by N(P_f-P_g)/(2pi i); the integral lattice in sections 1--4 is the same after this fixed scalar normalization. At the real limiting boundary clocks, the local 220/022 scalar curvature, 202 positive-total curvature, and 222 two-variable curvature are bounded below by cN and above by CN on their displayed rows of L. Their non-affine phases have already been retained in the local source formulas; the positive reference Hessians are taken in the corresponding real logarithmic clock coordinates. Thus their sum is a real symmetric matrix H0_N with cN ||L P||^2 <= P^T H0_N P <= CN ||L P||^2 (6) for real P, with a fixed finite number of local rows. Sign changes from 022 or the literal dual are included in L. In a fixed basis of the primitive slice W of section 3, (6) gives c_D N I <= H0_N|_W <= C_D N I. (7) Now retain the exact finite-r clocks at r=N rho. Their relative errors from the finite nonzero limiting clocks are O(1/N). The uniform complex logarithmic derivative bounds through order three in the local curvature theorem make their Hessian correction O(1). The 200/002 zero-free Bessel factors have O(1) Hessian on the common compact neighborhood; their endpoint-product corrections have Hessian O(1/N). Linear head monomials and all fixed channel scalars contribute zero Hessian. Let S=sum_i(d-2a_i). The retained 202/222 partner products and auxiliary root cups have Hessian O(S), since their factors are uniformly separated from zero. Mixed-type cup/partner residuals are smaller after their linear monomials are removed. These are estimates of the actual root identities; no root reflection or partner collision is differentiated as a generic-q identity. Physical cup/cap characters are linear. The nonzero actual product and finite model satisfy a relative O(1/N) estimate on a fixed source polydisc. Cauchy's formula gives an O(1/N) Hessian error for their local logarithms. Consequently the actual root source Hessian H_N at the boundary sample satisfies, on W, ||H_N-H0_N|| <= C_D(1+S). (8) For S=o(N), (7),(8) imply invertibility and ||(H_N|_W)^-1|| <= C_D/N. (9) This is a complex Hessian statement; positivity is asserted for the reference matrix H0_N, not for an arbitrarily perturbed complex point. All constants are uniform in the stated alpha/rho compacts and through both maximal-fold parities. The shrinking s-window is an INTERNAL channel window, not the external auxiliary-color h-window needed for the eventual filling theorem. Genuine q normals are not estimated by (8),(9). ## 6. What this does not yet prove The complete geometric framing sample is not automatically stationary for the finite labels a_i. Even at the folded limit the actual linear source characters and retained Poisson sector must be checked against the boundary action before invoking a stationary reduction. A Hessian bound alone does not bound the gradient or the displacement of a nearby critical point. The binomial base localization, transverse amplitude, Jacobian, square-root branch and common descending cycle would all have to be retained in a Gaussian theorem. The exact critical-scheme inverse remains a statement on the critical representation germ. No off-critical flat representations were used to obtain (4) or (9). In particular a generic unframed perturbation of a zero lower-left prefix is not assigned the same scale as a primitive source-head perturbation. Finally, selecting the primitive neighboring-head slice does not expose those heads as two first slots without additional source algebra. The original relative cotangent periods, their support/carry boundaries, the global nonzero coefficient and the mixed-color/alias estimates remain separate. No hyperbolic-volume equality follows here. ## 7. Focused audit and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank_results.json) pass 56 exact rank cases, 1136 ordered triangle/dual checks, 224 oriented chain maps, 112 primitive neighboring slices, 336 fixed-charge affine restorations, 56 deliberately nontransverse cut witnesses, and 56 cup/cap subdivisions. Original finite tensors at both parities separately check 5732 degree entries, 42 retained half-twist sectors and 540 cup/cap entries. Five exact prefix/frame identities include (4b). The actual cube and octahedral combinatorics are distinguished from supplemental combinatorial sphere regressions; the latter certify no additional geometric realization. The local curvature theorem has its own source-matrix audit. No numerical knot list replaces the class-wide proof. The transverse-rank theorem does not identify a stationary point, first-slot routing, Gaussian contraction or relative-period coefficient. The rank calculation does not establish a stationary sector, a descending cycle or a nonzero original period.

text: # The original marked source is one positive face coefficient 30 October 2026. For every fixed folded channel assignment, the literal complete-circle plat source equals one coefficient of an explicit homogeneous polynomial with nonnegative real coefficients, times its known scalar and retained half-twist phases. The proof retains the original marked cap, finite support, primitive measure and both level parities. It does not substitute a newly chosen period for the physical source. The identity below is finite and exact. It does not yet estimate that coefficient, prove it nonzero for every channel assignment, or establish a hyperbolic-volume asymptotic. ## 1. Literal source and polynomial Fix a connected 2k-plat projection, k>=2, with all crossings in R recorded two-strand boxes. The exterior contains the actual k bottom cups and k top caps, one of the latter carrying the original unrestricted mark. Retain each box's half twist epsilon_i in {0,+1,-1}. The source is the [original complete-circle contraction](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), not a routed replacement. Any separately recorded exterior framing line multiplies both sides of the identity below and is not erased. Remove half twists only in the planar graph used to name its regions; their exact scalars omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i remain in the source. The plane matching graph Delta has R+2 white faces. Let u be the exterior face and v the bounded face inside the actual marked top cap. These are the two faces adjacent to the marked physical edge. Write F_* for the other R faces. The geometric certificate is not needed for the finite identity; when it is present these are exactly the two constant-prefix faces of the resonant chart. Connectedness here concerns the planar source graph, not the number of main link components. Multiple main components are allowed. In particular the all-untwisted standard 2k-plat generally retains k main components; the positive untwisted specialization is a statement about that augmented LINK source, not automatically a family of k-bridge knots. Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. For each actual integer label 0<=a_i<=floor(d/2), set s_i=d-2a_i and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), k_a=1 if s=0, and k_a=2 otherwise. Use the exact local factors proved in the [positive-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md): D_a(x,z,y)=det[z I+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=sum_(j=0)^s S_s/[S_j S_(s-j)] x^(s-j)y^j. At box i let (f0,fin,fout,f2) be its original outer, input-middle, output-middle and final white regions. Define P_(N,a)(L)=product_i D_(a_i)(L_f0,L_fin,L_f2) D_(a_i)(L_f0,L_fout,L_f2) Ptilde_(s_i)(L_f0,L_f2). (1) Repeated region labels, if the actual plane diagram has them, are substituted literally. Every coefficient of (1) is nonnegative real, and its total degree is sum_i(2a_i+s_i)=dR. Define C_(N,a)=[product_(f in F_*) L_f^d] P_(N,a)(L) evaluated at L_u=L_v=0. (2) The fixed-channel contribution A_(N,a)^epsilon to the original marked root source is EXACTLY A_(N,a)^epsilon =N^R product_i[k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] C_(N,a). (3) Thus C_(N,a)>=0, with zero allowed. The full original source is the finite sum of (3) over its original folded labels. In particular the untwisted terms have a positive coefficient description; signed half twists retain their actual channel phases. No cancellation between different half-twisted channels is ruled out by (3). ## 2. A signed face index in the original flat-plat sweep Use the actual bottom-to-top order of physical heads and adjacent boxes. Number the gaps between strands by g=1,...,2k-1. Odd gaps start inside a bottom cup and end inside a top cap. Even gaps start and end in the exterior. A box on zero-based slot a replaces ONLY the region in gap g=a+1: its old middle region ends at the input pi vertex, and its new middle region starts at the output W vertex. All other gap regions continue through the box unchanged. Let M_f count these middle corners in face f. Let T_f be the signed ordinary physical turn incidence: each original cup or cap contributes +1 to its outside face and -1 to its inside face. These signs are the literal source signs: both cup and ordered ordinary cap have the same positive first-head monomial q^(d i) on i+j=d. In particular a top cap does not acquire an independently reversed sign. Every bounded segment in an odd gap has two ends, each either a middle corner or an inside cup/cap. Every bounded segment in an even gap has two middle ends. Therefore M_f-T_f=2 for every bounded face. (4) Connectedness forces at least one box in each internal even gap: an unused such gap would separate the source projection into two disjoint plat blocks. Each of the k-1 even gaps therefore contributes two middle ends to the exterior, whereas all 2k cups/caps contribute their outside incidence there. Hence M_u=2(k-1), T_u=2k, M_u-T_u=-2. (5) This is the signed Euler turning identity in the literal Morse convention. Equivalently, middle corners and inside turns contribute +1 to twice the tangent winding of a face boundary; outside turns contribute -1. The sweep proof specifies all signs without selecting an arbitrary face orientation. The literal pi dualization does not invalidate (4). It reverses all three ports, and each adjacent face sees two of these local reversals. More directly the exact complete-circle factor already combines its auxiliary cup and two inverse physical cups, leaving precisely the two middle denominators with exponent d/2. There are no unrecorded turns to add after applying that exact factorization. ## 3. The original mark gives exactly the two missing face exponents Use centered face logarithms. For an ordered physical pair with outside face x, middle face z and final face y, i=d/2+N(Log L_x-Log L_z)/(2pi i), j=d/2+N(Log L_z-Log L_y)/(2pi i). (6) On each actual cup/cap y=x. The exact complete-circle expression is its scalar k_a beta_a^2 times its numerator in (1), divided by the product of its two middle variables to power d/2. Thus the ordinary whole-source face monomial has exponent (d/2)(T_f-M_f). Equations (4),(5) give L_u^d product_(f != u) L_f^(-d). (7) This holds also at EVEN levels: d/2 may be half-integral locally, but the assembled exponents in (7) are integers. Every local logarithmic lift is retained until this assembly. The mark sign is fixed by the original ordered matrices. At its cap with first head i and SECOND head j=d-i, ordinary cap(i,j)=N^-1 q^(di), mark(i,j)=N^-2 q^(dj). The original mark is unrestricted before contraction. The k bottom cups fix total physical degree kd, every actual box preserves that integer degree, and the other k-1 top caps use degree (k-1)d. Thus the two surviving marked endpoints necessarily have i+j=d. This is a consequence of whole-source conservation, not an early diagonal replacement of the marked tensor. Their ratio is N^-1 q^(-d^2)Q^(dj). The second head is the one whose raw face clock is -L_v/L_u. On the centered lift (6), the ratio is N^-1 (L_v/L_u)^d. (8) Using the first head in (8) would reverse the marked character and give an incorrect target coefficient. Equation (8) changes exponent +d to zero at u, and exponent -d to zero at v. All other exponents remain -d. No integral character has been selected anew or discarded. For completeness, the source constants also agree exactly. There are k cups N q^(-d^2)q^(di), k-1 ordinary caps N^-1 q^(di), and one marked cap N^-2 q^(dj). Each centered physical head contributes the constant q^(d^2/2); these 2k constants cancel the k cup factors q^(-d^2). Their total scalar is therefore precisely N^-1. Consequently the assembled meromorphic root product is N^-1 product_i[k_(a_i)beta_(a_i)^2omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] P_(N,a)(L) product_(f in F_*) L_f^(-d). (9) The local root cup poles have been canceled by the proved complete-circle identity before (9) is used. No generic-q cancellation is inferred. ## 4. Primitive face grids at both parities and exact physical support The centered homogeneous source lattice is the cycle lattice of Delta. Its integral identification with face-potential differences modulo a constant is proved in [the original rank theorem](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md), section 1. Fix the exterior face potential to zero. There are R+1 independent integral face potentials, with no finite-index Jacobian. At ODD N, d/2 is integral. Set L_u=1 and let every other L_f range independently through mu_N={Q^p:0<=p<N}. Formula (6) gives integral heads. At EVEN N there is an exact specified coset. Give each main edge the Z2 value1 and each matching edge the value0. Every shaded triangle has two main edges and one matching edge, so this cochain sums to zero on each triangle of the dual sphere. It integrates to face values t_f in Z2, unique after setting t_u=0. In the literal plat sweep this is simply the parity of the gap in which a region is born; the exterior has parity0. In particular t_v=1. Use the grid L_f=q^(t_f) Q^(p_f), p_f in Z/N, L_u=1. (10) On a main edge, d+t_left-t_right is even, so (6) is integral. On a matching edge, its auxiliary row is a plus a face-potential difference; the matching parity0 makes that integral too. The physical cup complements and all channel equations hold on the chosen affine lifts. The number of grid points is exactly N^(R+1) at either parity. There are no extra physical states hidden in this modular grid. Reduce physical heads to 0,...,d. The local support theorem proves that a surviving circle has BOTH physical totals in the actual interval [d-a,d+a], which contains at most N integers. Their congruence modulo N therefore forces equality as UNWRAPPED totals, with the original auxiliary row in [0,2a]. Unsupported pairs are killed by the small white or by the ONE forced factor retained after the cup cancellation. This is a zero of the entire root circle, not an undefined zero times a pole. Cups/caps similarly have unique physical total d in their congruence class. Thus every nonzero grid point gives an actual allowed state. Conversely every allowed state defines one grid point by the primitive face-potential isomorphism. Distinct allowed states cannot differ by N times a nonzero flow, since every head lies in an interval of length less than N. The actual allowed states are therefore exactly the possibly nonzero grid points, with zero points harmlessly included. Finally retain the even-level carry signs rather than canceling them locally by fiat. A surviving canonical state and its chosen affine lift differ by N times an integral CLOSED source flow. By the integral face-potential theorem this is N times integral face shifts. The full expression (9) has integer face exponents and is unchanged by such shifts. Hence the product of the local recorded carry multipliers is one. This proves the global carry cancellation in the actual source; it does not assert independent periodicity of each physical tensor. ## 5. A unique alias and the exact measure Write the nonnegative-coefficient polynomial as P_(N,a)=sum_n c_n product_f L_f^(n_f), with n_f>=0 and sum_f n_f=dR. In (9), the target exponents are0 at u,v and d at the R other faces. Averaging independently over (10) annihilates a monomial unless n_v=0 modulo N, n_f=d modulo N for f in F_*. Because 0<=d<N, nonnegativity forces n_v>=0 and n_f>=d. Their minimum total already equals dR. Homogeneity therefore forces n_u=n_v=0, n_f=d for every f in F_*. There is exactly ONE possible alias, namely the actual coefficient (2). At that exponent the even coset multiplier is1. The normalized face average equals C_(N,a), and the unnormalized source sum multiplies it by N^(R+1). Together with the single N^-1 in (9), this proves (3). No second boundary average or matching-edge trace factor is inserted. The same calculation also checks the original unmarked ordinary root closure. Its monomial is (7), so every one of the R+1 bounded faces would require polynomial degree at least d. This exceeds the total degree dR. Its whole root sum is consequently zero, as required by the original trace-normal identity. The mark is essential to the nonzero admissible target, not an optional renormalization. ## 6. Scope Formula (3) is the original fixed-channel ROOT contraction, not merely an equality of off-grid interpolants or local density values. It uses the proved canceled root circle and its exact modular-support zeros. It does not replace genuine generic-q lifts or their normal derivatives. The source weights h0 already include the actual complete-circle normal. The finite formula is valid at both parities and composite levels. All folded labels occur. A positive geometric certificate supplies additional candidate angle data but is not inferred from positivity of the polynomial. Estimating (2), proving a sharp full-channel bound with retained signed phases, and identifying the filled mixed-color limit remain separate tasks. No volume conjecture is asserted here. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_original_marked_face_coefficient_results.json), checks 735 signed flat-plat sweeps and 15,386 exact marked face exponents. It compares 17 original fixed-sector W/pi matrix contractions, including the unrestricted original mark, with the independently built determinant coefficient. Its full face-grid checks cover 19,737 assignments: 2,179 supported states, 17,558 forbidden states, and 117 nontrivial even-level carry cancellations. Both level parities and composite levels occur; ordinary root closure zero is checked separately. These are finite identities over exact cyclotomic finite fields, not numerical evidence for an asymptotic or a nonzero coefficient in every sector. The finite coefficient identity allows the stated connected multi-main-component case. It does not assert an asymptotic or a nonzero coefficient.
