text: # One common resonant chart for the original certified network 30 October 2026. A fixed certified right-angled augmented diagram with one main component admits ONE original boundary chart in which all six permitted root-numerator regimes hold simultaneously. The first-cut phase is small and positive, and the boundary parameter rho is positive real. No independent local conjugations, reference changes or optimized heads are used. This is a statement about the original white numerators sampled from the COMPLETE geometric representation. It is not a finite-channel stationarity theorem, a generic-normal theorem, or a selected-period calculation. The full source still retains its cups, measures, marks, band sums and original support cycles. ## 1. Actual data and the common chart Fix the labeled positive right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, the original exterior spine and white-prefix dictionary, and a fixed retained-half-twist pattern for which the main strands form ONE component. Auxiliary crossing circles remain present. The statement applies to every original input and output white factor with that dictionary; it does not label an arbitrarily routed extra band by an original face. All constants below may depend on this fixed diagram. Use its original exposed primitive meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]], with fixed point infinity, and its incident reference face F_ref. Retain the actual reflection lifts of the [signed-prefix theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md): H_f=[[a_f,b_f],[bar b_f,d_f]], det H_f=-1, Q_f=J_f bar J_ref, (Q_f)21=-a_f bar b_ref, a_f>=0, with equality precisely at incident faces. (1) There is a useful further consequence of this original meridian normalization. text: # A finite original-network source envelope at the resonant boundary 30 October 2026. Fix the labeled positive right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, actual cut and original white-prefix dictionary of an augmented diagram with one main component. On its single common boundary chart, the actual complete ROOT tensor summand is nonzero. Its specified regular complete-circle Hopf lift has fixed-quantum-jet upper bounds of polynomial cost times (CN^C) to the sum of the channel deficits. This includes all six original numerator types, both folded parities, 202/202 pairs and c=1. A positive triangulation alone does not supply the required polyhedron and prefix data. This is an UNCONTRACTED finite-network theorem. It retains the exact first-normal identity for the original complete source, but supplies no bound or noncancellation statement for its contracted finite sum or relative period. The generic lift is the regular W pi lift already proved for that identity, not the exceptional K/E germ and not the entire moving-q germ of a complete crossing circle. ## 1. Specify the original generic tensor summand Fix the original marked 2k-plat D with R complete-circle boxes and retained half-twist signs epsilon_i. (1) They are all nonzero, including both maximal folded parities. In particular h0_M=N at odd N and h0_M=2N/sin(pi/N) at even N. Gamma_a is a FIXED root constant, not a generic norm to invert. The original generic white has the specified finite continuation W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^(Q^-N)(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m. For a fixed highest weight L<N define the original continued cup p_L(x)=exp(pi i x) zeta^[x(L-x-1)] Fhat_P(x)Fhat_P(L-x)/F_L, pV(x)=N zeta^(-d^2)p_d(x), P=pi i/Log zeta. (3) Here Fhat_P is the specified moving-period Gamma product, agreeing with the exact generic finite factorial at its admissible integer arguments. The ordered cap is 1/p_L(L-x), with the same physical scale when L=d. The complete-circle retraction is literally pi_a=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)^T W_a^T (ellV^T tensor ellV^T)P_rev. (4) An explicit coefficient, useful for retaining every orientation, is pi_a(r;i,j) =gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)]. (5) The exact generic Chevalley identity also gives W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=zeta^[(d-2a)(a-r)]W_a(i,j;r). Thus (5) retains the original channel cup, TWO physical inverse cups, reversed tensor order and gamma_a. It divides by no paired root norm: pi_a W_a=0 at a paired node is not a denominator in this theorem. Expand every original coupon with (2),(4), and use the original physical cups/caps and cyclic turns. Impose their literal integral affine head constraints on an admissible stratum, with any primitive free-lattice chart h=h0+A x. Let S_F(epsilon,h) be this ordinary CLOSED tensor summand, including product_i h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i and an ordinary cap at the exposed marked arc. At admissible integer heads it is the actual finite summand of this specified regular Hopf lift. No head is wrapped, and no support inequality is removed. Constant forbidden strata retain their original zero value rather than being assigned a meromorphic 0/0 continuation. ## 2. The one common geometric head assignment Use the [original common boundary chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md), with r_frame=N rho, rho in a positive real compact, and s_frame=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1, alpha in a fixed sufficiently small positive compact. These are samples of the complete geometric representation, not assertions of finite-a stationarity. Require the shrinking-fold range S log N=o(N). For the estimates it is enough first to assume each 0<=s_i<=eta N, for a sufficiently small fixed eta. Then a_i/N stays in a fixed interior neighborhood of one half and all the following margins are uniform. Every physical i and d-i has real part divided by N in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), with imaginary part divided by N of size O(log N). For auxiliary heads put sigma=i+j. Exactly, r0=a+N(x+y-1), 2a-r0=a-N(x+y-1). (6) For 202/222, the canonical total gives x+y=1-i Log(T_infinity)/(2pi)+O(1/N), T_infinity>0. The actual root and nearby generic factors avoid its poles and zeros. This includes 202/202 and either folded parity; no physical-head half-index offset is assigned to an auxiliary head. ## 3. Nonzero root product, with every exact factor retained At the common chart every original white numerator has one of the six proved boundary models. (7) In particular the uncontracted original root summand is nonzero for large N. The original h0_a, gamma_a, omega_a, white monomials, factorials, cups, pivotal clocks, half-index shifts and every integral character remain in B_F,N. They are not normalized to modulus one. Some have exponential or N log N size individually. Equation (7) retains their exact joint product rather than bounding them separately. The finite-clock determinant in 220 and the trace correction in 222 cannot be replaced by their limiting-clock values without their specified order-one factors. At the original exposed root mark, degree conservation after the other caps forces complementary indices (d-x,x). The literal ratio of that marked row to the ordinary cap is Xi_N(x)=N^-1 q0^(-d^2) Q0^(d x), Q0=q0^2. (8) Consequently the actual marked root summand on this same affine chart is S_M(0,h_N)=Xi_N(x_N)S_F(0,h_N), and has the corresponding nonzero packet Xi_N(x_N)B_F,N. The character in (8) is retained as written: Q0^(dx)=exp(2pi i x)Q0^-x on a literal complex head, not merely Q0^-x. No bare root mark is moved through a cap or promoted to a generic covariant tensor. For the chosen original first-cut chart its exposed physical clock is A=(1+s_frame)^-1=exp(2pi i alpha), or the recorded complementary clock according to the cap orientation. Thus x_N is real, equal to N alpha-1/2 or N(1-alpha)-1/2, and |Xi_N(x_N)|=1/N. (9) This modulus statement is specific to that chosen real-alpha boundary chart. It is not a claim that the marked character is harmless on an arbitrary complex framing chart. ## 4. Every fixed generic jet of the specified lift There are constants c_D,C_D and, for each fixed k, C_(D,k) such that on |epsilon|<=c_D N^-10, |S_F(epsilon,h_N)/S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_D(C_D N^40)^S, (10) and hence |partial_epsilon^k S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_(D,k) N^(10k)(C_D N^40)^S |S_F(0,h_N)|. (11) The derivative holds EVERY marked head h_N fixed. Its common geometric construction is not rerun as epsilon varies. Here is the proof from the actual factors. The genuine 200/002 theorem gives bounded relative numerator variation on this smaller disk when the nonzero Bessel factor is retained. The [paired220 theorem](actual_q_hahn_paired_resonant_circle_packet.md) gives cost C(CN^20)^s for 220; exact GENERIC reciprocity gives the same for 022, including its marked complement and scalar. The [positive-total theorem](actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.md) gives that bound for 202/222, including possible zero single root edges. Each matching edge has TWO original white numerators after (5) is expanded. Their total cost is at most C_D(C_D N^20)^(2 sum_i s_i)=C_D(C_D N^40)^S. The factorial domain verification in section 2 gives bounded two-sided relative variation for every cup factor, its inverse and fixed factorial on the larger disk c/[N^2(1+log N)^2]. All monomial exponents have size O_D(N^2(1+log N)^2), so their ratios are bounded on our smaller disk. Gamma_a, h0_a and omega_a are the fixed root constants of the specified lift and have relative ratio one. There are only finitely many factors for fixed D. This proves (10) and its holomorphy directly in the original regular factors. Cauchy's formula proves (11). Thus the cost is polynomial for bounded total deficit S, including maximal folded channels at both level parities, and subexponential whenever S log N=o(N). No fixed nonzero scaled channel-width estimate is asserted. Nor is a nonzero leading normal amplitude inferred from this relative UPPER bound. ## 5. The unchanged original first-normal identity and its limit Let A_D,N be the original complete root source before its separately recorded exterior framing line. On each label sector the specified regular Hopf lift has ordinary closed value F_a(epsilon)=D_N(epsilon)z_a(epsilon), with D_N(epsilon)=(-1)^d[N]_(q0 exp(epsilon)), nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1)!=0. The exact source theorem therefore remains A_D,N=nu_N^-1 sum_a sum_(h in original support(a)) partial_epsilon S_F(0,h). (12) All sums in (12) are finite and retain their original affine constraints, support, parity and mark. The full paired-circle first normal is already contained in h0_a W_a pi_a at the root. No paired norm is inverted, and no Hermite sector is removed. The regular lift need not be the whole moving-q circle: any two regular generic Hopf lifts with the same root coupon give the same marked scalar, because their closed difference is D_N times a holomorphic open scalar vanishing at zero. Combining (9),(11) with |nu_N|=N/sin(pi/N) gives the local bound |nu_N^-1 partial_epsilon S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_D N^9(C_D N^40)^S |S_M(0,h_N)|. title: The original outer color has a squared Fourier kernel
text: # The original outer color has a squared Fourier kernel 29 October 2026. The full original Hermite source cancels the dangerous outer-color alias exactly. A finite contour with a SQUARED denominator then turns a coherent spectral packet into a genuine auxiliary-color packet, with a strict bound on every complementary physical color. This is a source identity and estimate, not an identification of a Casimir coordinate with a meridian. ## 1. Actual color, values, and normals Let N>=2, d=N-1 and theta_j=(2j-d)pi/N, 0<=j<N. The actual Casimir nodes are c_j=-2cos(theta_j). Use the literal circle L_j=(-1)^(j-1)U_(j-1)(Omega/2) and original functional phi from [the full physical trace theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). For a full Hermite element f set F(theta)=f(-2cos(theta)). For each ACTUAL auxiliary color N-h, 0<=h<N, that trace gives exactly A_N(h)=phi(L_(N-h) f) =sum_j [(N-h)cos(h theta_j)F(theta_j) -sin(h theta_j)F'(theta_j)]. (1) Here the prime is the theta derivative. In particular it retains the first Casimir normal at every double node. At the odd simple node theta=0 its contribution is (N-h)F(0), as required. To derive (1), sin(theta)L_(N-h)(-2cos(theta))=sin((N-h)theta). The double-node trace is twice (-1)^d times the theta derivative of that last sine times F. At a node cos(N theta_j)=(-1)^d and sin(N theta_j)=0. Combining the two equal terms at theta and -theta gives (1). The simple node is checked by its removable value. No generic-q derivative is substituted for this fixed-root normal. An even analytic function F may replace the polynomial on any symmetric set of nodes if it has the SAME values and theta derivatives there. Symmetry of those nodes then also gives A_N(h)=sum_j exp(i h theta_j)[(N-h)F(theta_j)+i F'(theta_j)]. (2) ## 2. The exact Fourier alias that disappears Write F(theta)=sum_k Fhat_k exp(i k theta), with Fhat_k=Fhat_(-k). For a polynomial f the sum is finite. Since sum_j exp(i k theta_j)=N(-1)^(d ell) if k=ell N, (1) gives the exact all-normal formula A_N(h)=N^2 sum_(ell in Z) (1-ell)(-1)^(d ell) Fhat_(ell N-h). (3) If f has degree less than N, every noncentral possible alias is killed and A_N(h)=N^2 Fhat_h, 0<=h<N. (4) Thus the physical auxiliary-color vector is precisely the Fourier coefficient vector of the FULL Hermite representative of f. Reducing f modulo P_N is allowed here; reducing only its values is not. Most importantly, ell=1 has coefficient ZERO in (3). For h near N this would otherwise be the low frequency N-h, with the complete source growth. The normal term in (1) removes it. This is why an unweighted node sum is inadequate for the whole-color gap. For a nonperiodic analytic representative of the same node jets, one must not assume the separately weighted infinite Fourier aliases are absolutely summable. The finite contour below avoids this issue. ## 3. A finite residue identity, with its entire boundary retained Choose a symmetric rectangle [-b_N,b_N]+i[-eta,eta], with vertical sides halfway between physical theta nodes. Thus E(theta)=(-1)^d exp(iN theta)=-exp(-N Im theta) on either vertical side. Assume F is even and holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed rectangle. Put K_N(theta)=iN/(E(theta)-1). Its poles at the enclosed physical nodes have residue one. Apply residues to (2) and integrate F' by parts around the CLOSED contour. This is an exact identity: sum_(|theta_j|<b_N) exp(i h theta_j) [(N-h)F(theta_j)+iF'(theta_j)] =(1/(2pi i))oint exp(i h theta)F(theta) [-iN^2/(E(theta)-1)^2]dtheta. (5) Indeed K_N'=N^2 E/(E-1)^2 and N K_N-iK_N'=-iN^2/(E-1)^2. Equivalently the squared pole has principal part i/(theta-theta_j)^2 +N/(theta-theta_j); its residue is exactly the expression on the left. Every vertical and horizontal piece of the contour remains. For 0<=h<=N the oscillatory part of the kernel has these bounds: * upper side: at most C N^2 exp(-h eta); * lower side: at most C N^2 exp(-(2N-h)eta); * vertical sides: at most N^2, because exp(-h y)/(1+exp(-Ny))^2<=1 for every real y. The lower-side frequency is 2N-h, rather than N-h. This is the finite-contour version of the missing alias in (3). ## 4. A uniform physical-color theorem Here are explicit sufficient inputs, independent of any knot class. Let f_N be an actual full Hermite source. Suppose it has an even holomorphic representative F_N on a fixed rectangle |Re theta|<=2b, |Im theta|<=eta_0, and constants a,B,gamma>0 such that |F_N(u+iv)|<=C N^C exp[N(F0-a u^2+B v^2)]. (6) On the enclosed physical nodes require that F_N and its first theta derivative approximate the ACTUAL f_N node jets with error poly(N)exp[N(F0-gamma)]. On the complementary physical nodes require the actual values and first theta derivatives to have the same strict exponential gap (with possibly another fixed positive gamma). These are quantitative source assumptions; a principal symbol alone does not imply them. Choose halfway endpoints b_N=b+O(1/N). For every fixed delta>0, there is g_delta>0 such that max_(delta N<=h<N)|phi(L_(N-h) f_N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F0-g_delta)]. (7) Proof. The approximation and omitted-node errors in (1) cost only powers of N. In (5) choose a fixed small eta with B eta^2<min(a b^2/16,delta eta/2,eta/2). For large N, b_N>=b/2. The upper and lower edges then lose at least delta eta/2 and eta/2 respectively; the vertical edges lose a fixed fraction of a b^2. There are finitely many edges of bounded length. This proves (7) uniformly through h=N-1, without an infinite charge-tail argument. There is also an exact specified analytic corridor interpolation: C_N(t)=N^2/(2pi) integral_(-b_N)^(b_N) F_N(theta) exp(iNt theta)dtheta. (8) It is even and entire in t. For 0<=h<=delta_0 N, with delta_0 fixed and small, |A_N(h)-C_N(h/N)|<=poly(N)exp[N(F0-g)] (9) for a fixed g>0. To see this, on the upper edge of (5) write the kernel as -iN^2+O(N^2 exp(-N eta)). The constant part, with the counterclockwise upper-edge orientation, is N^2/(2pi) times the upper translated integral in (8). Move that integral to the real segment and retain its two vertical connectors. They are gapped by (6); the upper remainder and lower side are gapped as above. The same actual node-jet errors are then added. This proves (9) for the exact finite integral, before any asymptotic expansion. The argument is uniform over additional REAL physical parameters satisfying these source estimates. If F_N is holomorphic and separately even in their complex continuations, (8) has the same properties. For that continuation an additional C||Im y||^2 in the exponent is allowed; (6) with the unchanged F0 is not asserted on a full complex parameter disk. Shrink this disk so its growth spends less than the fixed endpoint/current gap before using the complex saddle below. No analyticity of a merely pointwise error on the physical color lattice has been assumed. ## 5. The nonzero complex corridor saddle Suppose additionally on the fixed local rectangle and parameter disk F_N(theta,y)=eta_N N^mu b(theta,y) exp[N varphi(theta,y)] (1+O(1/N)), uniformly holomorphically, where b(0,0)!=0, varphi is even in theta and separately even in y, varphi(0,0)=F0, and varphi_theta,theta(0,0)=-D/(2pi), Re D>0. (10) Keep the known nonzero unit eta_N outside C_N. The implicit equation varphi_theta(theta_*,y)+it=0 has a unique small holomorphic solution. After shrinking the fixed disks, contour translation within the same rectangle and the gapped endpoint connectors give eta_N^(-1) C_N(t,y) =N^(mu+3/2) B(t,y) exp[N Phi(t,y)](1+O(1/N)), Phi=varphi(theta_*,y)+it theta_*, B=b(theta_*,y)/sqrt(2pi[-varphi_theta,theta(theta_*,y)]). (11) The square root continues the convergent Gaussian at t=y=0. It is nonzero. The local quadratic bound gives an integrable Gaussian majorant; outside a fixed saddle neighborhood (6) and the retained connectors give a strict gap. Taylor expansion and Gaussian moments prove the displayed uniform error. The analytic O(1/N) source error is bounded on this same contour. Both Phi and B are separately even. At the complete point, Phi(t,0)=F0-pi t^2/D+O(t^4), B(0,0)=b(0,0)/sqrt(D). (12) Since Re(1/D)>0, the physical outer-color curvature is strictly negative. Equations (7)--(12) are exactly the outer source gap and fixed complex color corridor needed in the general filling theorem. They do not yet assert that this action is a marked Bloch regulator. ## 6. Application to actual octahedral belt stacks [The inner physical-color theorem](actual_belt_stack_auxiliary_color_inner_packet.md) supplies the exact analytic inputs to this result for every fixed nonempty sign word of n pieces and every fixed outer crossing power a. Let sigma_i=+1 for a z_(N,h_i) piece and -1 for its typed reflection, e=sum_i sigma_i, and m=e+a. Its local representative is the actual product of finite inner packets times q^(m d^2/4) exp[iNm theta^2/(4pi)]. (13) The literal q^(m d^2/4) is used, not a principal square root. The original crossing and (13) have the same node values AND theta normals: partial_theta log R=iN theta/(2pi). The inner theorem retains exponentially small full-Hermite replacement errors and the strict angular complement bound. It also bounds every physical color tuple with an inner color outside its corridor, for ANY physical outer color. Consequently the WHOLE (n+1)-color original stack has an exact separately even complex corridor, a nonzero leading amplitude and a strict bound on its entire complementary physical color cube. Writing x_i=h_i/N, its action is Phi(x)=n j0-pi x_0^2/[n-i(e+a)] +(pi/2)sum_(i=1)^n(-1+i sigma_i)x_i^2+O(||x||^4), j0=v8/pi. (14) Thus in the notation Phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_i) of [the long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md), tau_0=i/[n-i(e+a)], tau_i=(sigma_i+i)/2, Im tau_i>0. (15) All analytic source hypotheses of that theorem now hold for these stacks, at every fixed n>=1. It supplies their nonzero original long-integral-filling asymptotic with the stated analytic critical action and original normalization. There is no width threshold in this source assertion. Width, a and all filling slopes are fixed before N tends to infinity; both level parities are retained. The independent geometric requirement is the ACTUAL deformed peripheral map and absolute regulator comparison for this SAME mixed packet. Matching (15) to cusp derivatives alone would not prove it. The [typed global lift](actual_belt_stack_typed_character_composition.md) now supplies that map, all complete face/collar checks and the absolute regulator. Combined with the source theorem above, it gives the [any-subset long-filling volume equality](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md). The spectral-to-color transform alone is not used to infer that equality. The focused audit checks the polynomial identity with exact arithmetic, literal physical marked traces over finite fields, and separately labeled high-precision Gaussian examples. Such examples do not prove the analytic source hypotheses for an unrelated diagram.

title: A macroscopic clock current surviving exact source fusion
text: # A macroscopic clock current surviving exact source fusion 28 October 2026. Fixed overclock sectors cannot separately be bounded by the regulator of the closed knot, even after exact closure/full-block fusion. This is an all-level calculation in the original enhanced source. It identifies a remaining macroscopic current whose coherent clock sum is essential. It does not establish a new hyperbolic case or obstruct a source-specific upper bound after that sum. ## 1. Exact original source and its clock sectors Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and exactly the enhanced crossing/pivot conventions of [the original crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md): mu=-q S and alpha=-q. Take the positive two-strand word [1,1,1], with its original fixed first cut. The exact cyclic-source peeling proof gives K_N=Q^(-1) (T_+^3)_(0,1). (1) Here K_N is the original reduced enhanced period with unknot value one. In the full modified-trace convention multiply EVERY sector and both sides of the subsequent identities by its original known external line. That common line is retained and has no exponential modulus at completeness; it is never replaced by an unknown scalar. The factor Q^(-1)=(-q)^(-2) includes the original closing coefficient and full writhe correction. No new average, source or normalization is introduced. The entries of this actual boundary operator are T_(0,j)=Q^(1-j), T_(k,0)=0 for k>0, T_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[k+(j-1)(j-2)/2] [k-1 choose j-1]_Q, 1<=j<=k<=d. (2) All other entries vanish. These are the directly proved q-Pascal entries of the original crossing, including T_(0,0)=Q. Every supported cut path has first head zero throughout. At a positive crossing its actual overclock is h=[b-a-1]+[a-c]=[b-1]. Thus its three clocks are (0,H,J), with H,J in 0,...,d, and its intermediate second-head values are i(H)=H+1 if H<d, i(d)=0; i(J)=J+1 if J<d, i(d)=0. (3) There is exactly ONE such peeled path for each supported clock pair. The positive-index triangular block and the wrap row in (2) give K_(N;H,J)=0, H>J, K_(N;H,J)=(-1)^H Q^[1+H(H+1)/2] [J choose H]_Q, H<=J. (4) This is an identity of actual original clock contributions, not an arbitrary inserted coefficient. For J<d it follows by multiplying T_(i(H),1), T_(i(J),i(H)) and T_(0,i(J)) and the factor Q^(-1). For J=d it follows from [d choose H]_Q=(-1)^H Q^[-H(H+1)/2], which is exact factorial reflection. This also includes H=J=d and the absorbing wrap state zero. There is no excluded parity or prime level and no division by F_N. ## 2. The same current after all charged full-block reductions The source of (4) is also visible in the [whole charged bridge coefficient](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). After its three full contractions and one loop extraction, put X,Y for the two surviving anchors. Up to the explicitly retained unit root phases its clock sector is (Q^(-J);Q)_J [X^d Y^(d-J)] B_(d-H)(Y,X;Q) B_H(X,Y;Q^(J+1)) B_(d-J)(X,Y;Q^(H+J+1)), (5) where B_L(U,V;a)=product_(r<L)(U-Q^r a V). The two parallel X-to-Y intervals concatenate to length d+H-J. If H>J this contains a FULL N-orbit, hence vanishes in the actual nilpotent source X^N=Y^N=0. This recovers the exact support condition in (4). If H<=J, the degree-complement identity at charge d fuses the two remaining edges. Its binomial is [d-H choose J-H]_Q. Its last loop has scalar (Q^(J+1);Q)_(d-J)=N/F_J, while the first loop in (5) has modulus |F_J|. Therefore the COMPLETE charged coefficient has modulus N |[J choose H]_Q|. (6) The N is canceled by the original single exterior 1/N. The other original W_h, kappa, pivot, framing and normalization factors are retained; in this alternating singleton-bridge diagram they have unit modulus, up to the common tame source line. Thus the large sector survives the existing full-block/zero-charge/loop reduction. Equation (4) independently supplies its exact normalized phase. ## 3. Two successive macroscopic cancellations Choose H=floor(N/3), J=floor(2N/3). The uniform actual factorial estimate gives log |[J choose H]_Q| =N[v_3/pi]+O(log N)>0, (7) where v_3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Indeed, with I(s)=integral_0^s log|2sin(pi*t)| dt, the rate is I(2/3)-2I(1/3)=v_3/pi. This is the figure-eight volume rate, despite the present closed word being the trefoil, whose volume is zero. No figure-eight asymptotic theorem is a premise of (7). The FIRST coherent sum is itself an exact general q-binomial identity inside this actual source: sum_(H=0)^J K_(N;H,J)=Q F_J, F_J=(Q;Q)_J. (8) Use the finite q-binomial theorem with argument Q. This collapses the entire H current before estimation. It lowers its maximal rate, but does not make it polynomial: at J=floor(5N/6), log |F_J|=N[v_3/(2pi)]+O(log N)>0. (9) Thus even the partially summed current in (8) cannot be assigned the closed knot's zero regulator or dropped as a small boundary. The complete original scalar is exactly K_N=Q sum_(J=0)^d F_J. (10) The last sum has polynomial size. This follows independently from the already derived ACTUAL spectral-jet closing functional, not a named torus-knot asymptotic. Write its normalized crossing as r_N. At double nodes c=q^a+q^(-a), a odd, 0<a<N, it obeys r_N(c)=nu, |nu|=1, r_N'(c)/nu=-(N-a)/[2(q^a-q^(-a))]. The original pivotal functional is Phi(f)=-sum_double [c f(c)+(c^2-4)f'(c)] + one simple-node value if N is odd. For f=r_N^3, each first term has modulus at most 2 and each derivative term at most 3N, because c^2-4=(q^a-q^(-a))^2. The possible simple-node term has modulus one. The full writhe factor is (-q)^3, of modulus one. Hence, at EVERY level, |K_N|<=3N^2. (11) All node derivatives and the original pivotal source are retained in this bound. These formulas were independently proved from the finite R and its generic tensor specialization in [the spectral source note](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md). They do not rely on semisimplicity at the root. ## 4. Consequence for the next source-specific operation The first fusion (8) is constructive and exact, but a second macroscopic cancellation is still needed. A bound on individual fixed-h charged coefficients, or even on the first fused current at each J, cannot equal the closed knot regulator. Those currents are not separately honest closed-knot representation periods. The new physical-face outward estimates can control their actual endpoint continuations; they do not remove the internal coherent sum exhibited by (8)--(11). A proposed broad source fusion must retain and use that final clock connection, rather than fixing the clocks and then applying a knot-volume bound. This is an explicit failure of that sectorwise route, not a no-go for phase-aware fusion of the entire original source or the volume conjecture. No arbitrary consecutive-run or arbitrary-width positive-kernel extension is claimed here. The theorem is restricted to the actual source and exact current proved above. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_overclock_sector_obstruction.py) checks every sector against the literal original crossing, both coherent sums, the original spectral normalization, the fully reduced charged coefficients and the displayed exponential rates.

title: The full physical pair commutant, true box rotation, and its marked trace
text: # The full physical pair commutant, true box rotation, and its marked trace 29 October 2026. Every endomorphism commuting with the original two-head E,F,K action is a polynomial in its Casimir, at EVERY level N>=2. No generic semisimplicity or omission of projective normals is needed. The literal bent pretzel boxes remain in this full algebra. Their original source is one explicitly weighted Hermite-Casimir period. This is a finite exact reduction, not a volume or asymptotic theorem. ## 1. The actual module and a generating middle weight Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, rho=q-q^(-1). On the original balanced physical V_N use E=Ecal: E|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, K|a>=x Q^(-a)|a>, 0<=a<=d, with outside-basis arrows omitted. The actual pair coproduct is \[ E_t=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F_t=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2, \qquad K_t=K_1K_2, \qquad\Omega=F_tE_t+qK_t+q^{-1}K_t^{-1}. \tag{1} \] Let W_T have the physical basis |a,T-a>, max(0,T-d)<=a<=min(d,T). The K_t eigenvalue there is x^2Q^(-T)=Q^(d-T). Its eigenvalue ONE occurs ONLY on W_d: the other possible degrees d+N and d-N lie outside [0,2d]. Thus an arbitrary E_t,F_t,K_t intertwiner preserves W_d, even if integer-degree preservation was not assumed. The following surjections are literal bidiagonal matrix facts: \[ E_t:W_{T+1}\twoheadrightarrow W_T\quad(0\leq T<d), \qquad F_t:W_T\twoheadrightarrow W_{T+1}\quad(d\leq T<2d). \tag{2} \] For the first use domain columns a=0,...,T and target rows a=0,...,T. The second-head E entry has nonzero diagonal Q^(-(T+1-a))-1; the other E entry is strictly off that diagonal. For the second use source a=T-d,...,d-1 and target a+1. The first-head F entry has diagonal 1-Q^(a+1), all nonzero, and the second-head term is off diagonal. These prove the two maximal ranks, including every composite and even N. Consequently \[ V_N\otimes V_N =\sum_{r=0}^d E_t^r W_d+\sum_{r=1}^d F_t^r W_d. \tag{3} \] This is generation by a specified physical weight space, not a claim that some abstract projective generator exists. ## 2. Exact commutant theorem, with all Jordan derivatives retained The middle block J=Omega|_(W_d) is the original complex symmetric tridiagonal matrix, with offdiagonal J[a,a+1]=J[a+1,a]=-(1-Q^(a+1))^2, 0<=a<d. All these entries are nonzero. In the vectors e_0,J e_0,...,J^d e_0, the k-th vector has last possible nonzero component k, equal to the nonzero product of the first k offdiagonals. They are a basis. Hence any X_d commuting with J is a UNIQUE polynomial f(J), deg f<N: choose f by X_de_0=f(J)e_0 and commute with J on this cyclic basis. Now let X commute with E_t,F_t,K_t. It preserves W_d by section 1 and commutes with Omega. Choose that f and put Y=X-f(Omega). Then Y annihilates W_d and commutes with E_t,F_t. Equation (3) forces Y=0 on the ENTIRE pair. We have therefore proved \[ \boxed{\operatorname{End}_{E_t,F_t,K_t}(V_N\otimes V_N) =\mathbb C[\Omega],\qquad \dim\mathbb C[\Omega]=N.} \tag{4} \] It follows in particular that every such endomorphism preserves full integer degree and is complex symmetric in the original pair basis. The actual Casimir is symmetric on every physical block. The familiar complete characteristic polynomial can also be recovered without a representation-theoretic endomorphism assertion: \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2 =\prod_{j=0}^{d}(z-c_j),\qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}. \tag{5} \] For example continue the explicit highest-weight N-module in q; its generic pair highest weights 2d-2j give these limiting middle-block eigenvalues. The middle characteristic polynomial is (5). The cyclic basis makes it also the minimal polynomial, and (3) propagates its vanishing to the full pair. Alternatively its original continuant recurrence gives the same polynomial. Thus the only simple root is -2 for odd N; every other distinct root is DOUBLE. Equality (4) is the full Hermite algebra C[z]/P_N, not the algebra of values on its distinct roots. In particular projective first derivatives survive. ## 3. Literal turn rotation agrees with the charge-block formula Keep the actual pair turns, with their original scalars: p_ab=N x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a/N delta_(a+b,d). They are the original invariant cup and cap; E_t p=F_t p=0, K_t p=p and the corresponding cap identities follow directly from their displayed entries. They obey the two snake identities. For an actual Hopf box B, define its genuine bend by \[ \mathcal R(B)=(I^{\otimes2}\otimes\ell) (I\otimes B\otimes I) (p\otimes I^{\otimes2}). \tag{6} \] Composition of the just specified intertwining matrices makes this an E_t,F_t,K_t intertwiner. The cup adds integer degree d and the cap removes d. No separate quantum-group covariance hypothesis on an arbitrarily framed head is used. Direct contraction gives \[ \mathcal R(B)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{a-e} B_{(b,d-e);(d-a,c)}. \tag{7} \] By (4) the original B is symmetric. Its degree support and a+b=c+e turn (7) into the concrete source-normalized rotated box \[ \boxed{(Z_B)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{c-b-d}B_{(d-a,c);(b,d-e)},\qquad Z_B=x^{-d}\mathcal R(B)\in\mathbb C[\Omega].} \tag{8} \] The scalar x^(-d) is retained; it is part of the source port convention. Both original N factors cancel in (6). Formula (8) is injective as a reshuffling of all four indices, so it is a linear automorphism of the N-dimensional algebra (4). It is NOT an algebra homomorphism. For example \[ Z_I=x^{-d}p\ell,\qquad Z_{R^{-1}}=x^{-d}R. \tag{9} \] For the second identity use the literal original inverse R^(-1)=P conjugate(R) P and factorial reflection F_(d-a)=N(-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2)/F_a. After these substitutions the factorial ratio is exactly the original positive crossing ratio. Writing k=a-e=c-b, the residual Q exponent, before reducing modulo N, is b(e+1)-(b+k)N. The remaining Cartan/x factors use kappa^2=x^d and x^2=Q^(-1), giving precisely (9), without a parity or normalization exception. In the pretzel notation T=d+h, I_h=[max(0,h),min(d,d+h)], put S_h=diag_(a in I_h)x^a and let P_h reverse a to T-a. For the literal transfer M_B in the [original all-width source](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md), equation (8) says EXACTLY \[ Z_B|_{W_{d+h}}=P_hS_hM_B^hS_h^{-1}P_h. \tag{10} \] This fixes the true turn conjugation rather than identifying a reshuffled positive tensor with a physical crossing by analogy. The same four-index formula also supplies its exact inverse: \[ Z_{Z_B}=x^{-2d}B. \tag{10a} \] Indeed the two exponents in the composition add to -2d and all four original indices return. Consequently Z_R=x^(-d)R^(-1) and Z_(p ell)=x^(-d)I as well. These are coherent full-Hermite Fourier identities; the rotation is still not multiplicative. ## 4. The original fixed-root trace is an explicit Hermite period Let g=K^(1-N) be the original physical pivot and define \[ \phi(f)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{V_N\otimes V_N} [(I\otimes g)f(\Omega)]. \tag{11} \] At this root K^N=(-1)^d I, hence g=(-1)^d K EXACTLY. For each distinct double node c in (5), retain both f(c) and f'(c). Then \[ \boxed{\phi(f)=(-1)^d\sum_{c\ {\mathrm{double}}} \{(4-c^2)f'(c)-c f(c)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\mathrm{odd}}}f(-2).} \tag{12} \] Here is an independent finite-matrix derivation, including its germ scope. Use a generic variable z near q and the explicit ordinary highest-weight N-module with K_a=z^d z^(-2a), F_a=1-z^(2a+2), and E_a=z^(-N)-z^N z^(-2a), missing endpoints omitted. It specializes to the original module. Its K-pivotal partial trace of f(Omega_z) is a scalar C(z) I. This follows directly from the coproduct: tracing [f(Omega_z),E_1K_2+E_2]=0 over head2 yields [C,E_1]=0; the F equation, K conservation and cyclicity of the head2 trace yield [C,F_1]=0. Distinct K weights and nonzero internal F entries make the partial trace scalar. No generic Schur assertion at the root is used. Explicitly K conservation gives A K_1^(-1)=K_1^(-1)K_2^(-1) A K_2 for A=f(Omega_z), so Tr_2 K_2[A,K_1^(-1)F_2] =K_1^(-1) Tr_2(A K_2F_2-K_2F_2 A)=0. Tracing the F coproduct commutator now gives [C,F_1]=0 directly. For generic z, solve the bidiagonal highest-weight equations and take their F descendants. They give one summand of highest weight 2d-2j for each j=0,...,d; their dimensions sum to N^2 and their distinct generic Casimirs prove independence. Their K traces are [2d-2j+1]_z. Taking one further K trace therefore gives \[ C(z)=\frac{\sum_{j=0}^d[2N-1-2j]_z f(z^{2N-1-2j}+z^{-2N+1+2j})}{[N]_z}. \tag{13} \] The actual finite matrices make C(z) regular at z=q. Keep f fixed and differentiate this removable ratio in log z. The denominator derivative is -2N/rho. At a pair with r=2j+1 and m=2N-r, the dimension weights cancel at the root; their derivatives sum to 2Nc/rho. The sum of weight times the node derivative is 2N(c^2-4)/rho. Their ratio is (4-c^2)f'(c)-cf(c). At the odd self-paired m=N, the removable ratio contributes f(-2). Finally multiply by (-1)^d to replace K by the ACTUAL fixed-root g. For odd N this sign is one. This proves (12). This use of a generic K trace COMPUTES A FIXED-ROOT FUNCTIONAL. It does NOT differentiate the original whole q-dependent source g(z)=K(z)^(1-N), and does not identify that source germ with a generic K-pivotal germ. Any such q-normal-jet assertion requires its own pivot derivative. It is unnecessary for (11)--(12). In particular phi(1)=0, phi(L_N)=N^2 and phi(R)=kappa x^(-d), with the actual crossing and auxiliary-circle normalizations. Also phi(p ell)=1. The trace weights in (12) have only polynomial size: \[ |\phi(f)|\leq (N+1)\max_c|f(c)|+2N\max_{c\ {\mathrm{double}}}|f'(c)|. \tag{14} \] There is no exponentially costly hidden source conversion in this period. This does not control the actual rotated nodal values or their phases for a given family of boxes. There is a useful exact endpoint form of the SAME functional. If r_f is the degree-at-most-d remainder of f modulo P_N, then \[ \boxed{\phi(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]r_f(z) =(f(J))_{0,d},\qquad J=\Omega|_{W_d}.} \tag{14a} \] To see the coefficient identity directly, at a double c the factor Q_c=P_N/(z-c)^2 has Q_c(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_c'(c)/Q_c(c)=c/(4-c^2), as follows by differentiating the elementary Chebyshev equation. Thus the residues of f/P_N, multiplied by (-1)^d N^2, are exactly (12). At odd N, P_N'(-2)=N^2 supplies the simple-node term. Their sum for the proper fraction r_f/P_N is its coefficient of z^(-1) at infinity, namely [z^d]r_f. Finally the tridiagonal path from 0 to d has length at least d, and its sole length-d coefficient is product_(a=1)^d[-(1-Q^a)^2]=(-1)^d N^2. This proves the last identity in (14a). It is the original selected endpoint matrix element; it is not a positive trace or permission to select only one logarithmic/Fourier winding of a residue formula. ## 5. All-width pretzel reduction, including the original mark The original source theorem gives the transfer trace with D_h=diag x^(2a). Under (10), P_h D_h P_h=x^d (I tensor g)|_(W_(d+h)). Conjugating the PRODUCT of all transfers by the SAME S_h,P_h and retaining its original prefactor x^((s-1)d)/N proves \[ \boxed{\mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s) =x^{sd}\phi(Z_{B_1}\cdots Z_{B_s}).} \tag{15} \] This uses every h=-d,...,d and the unrestricted original marked row until the already proved whole-degree restriction. Its original external chi_N is multiplied afterwards without modification. There are two convenient normalization conventions for this same rotation. For the unscaled genuine quarter-turn mathscrR(B)=x^d Z_B, equation (15) is equivalently phi(product_i mathscrR(B_i)), with NO external x phase. The explicit polynomial z_N in the [complete-base calculation](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) uses this unscaled mathscrR convention. Thus its source-normalized Z_B polynomial here is x^(-d)z_N. These scalar conventions must not be mixed. Writing Z_(B_i)=z_i(Omega), (12) makes (15) an explicit finite sum: at each double c, its derivative is sum_i z_i'(c) product_(k!=i) z_k(c), alongside the value product; the odd simple node contributes its full product. Thus all s boxes couple through the same actual Casimir channel, with the original normal source retained. No independent summation of unphysical channel maxima, deletion of a zero value's derivative, or assumed positive pairing is involved. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.py) uses original finite generators to check the full E/F/K commutant, the middle cyclic basis and both generating surjections, literal rotations of a complete polynomial basis, source-normalized crossing rotation, fixed-root trace on values AND derivatives, and the marked all-width product identity. The general geometric growth estimate for the rotated channel packets remains a separate task.

title: The meridian profile near completeness
status: Figure-eight profile and cusp correction; general signed-sum criterion
text: # The meridian profile near completeness 31 October 2026. Fix the quantum parameter \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\). The reduced ADO invariant of the figure-eight knot is a Laurent polynomial \(f_N(Y)\) in the squared meridian eigenvalue \(Y=M^2\). Its value at \(Y=1\) is the reduced Kashaev invariant \(K_N\). Here we vary this meridian while keeping the quantum parameter at its exact root of unity. Write \(Y=e^{z/N}\), with \(z\) in a fixed compact subset of the complex plane. We prove \[ \frac{f_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N}\longrightarrow H(z)=\frac{2\sinh(z/2)}z. \] After subtracting the polynomial determined by the ordinary colors and dividing by their common vanishing factor, the centered regular profile \(\rho_N\) tends to one. Section 3 gives these operations explicitly. Both statements hold through every fixed ordinary-color resonance and with every fixed derivative. The regularized Laurent polynomial has the same hyperbolic volume rate there. Its first correction is \(\tau z^2/(8\pi iN)\), where \(\tau=2\sqrt3\,i\) is the cusp shape for the preferred meridian and longitude. We obtain that coefficient from the finite sum and compute the cusp shape separately from the knot group. The proof starts from the actual finite cut formula. A general estimate for paired sine factors is then passed through its positive complete sum. Section 2 states exactly what would suffice for a signed source; those contraction hypotheses remain to be established for a general Conway main-meridian deformation. The parameter \(z\) is fixed before \(N\) grows. No assertion about a fixed open neighborhood in \(M\) is obtained by this microscopic scaling. ## 1. Uniform estimates for paired sine products For \(N\ge2\), \(0\le n<N\), and complex \(z\), put \[ P_{N,n}(z)=\prod_{r=1}^{n} \left(1+\frac{\sinh^2(z/(2N))}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right), \qquad H_N(z)=\frac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}. \tag{1} \] The latter expression has its entire continuation. For every fixed \(R\), all \(P_{N,n}\) are bounded on \(|z|\le R\), uniformly in \(N,n\). Indeed \(|\sinh(z/(2N))|\le C_R/N\) and \(\sin(\pi r/N)\ge2\min(r,N-r)/N\). Hence the product of absolute values is at most \[ \exp\left(C_R\sum_{r=1}^{N-1} \min(r,N-r)^{-2}\right)\le C'_R. \tag{2} \] For fixed \(0<\delta<1/2\) and all sufficiently large \(N\), there are holomorphic units \(U_{N,n}\) on \(|z|\le R\) such that \[ P_{N,n}=H_N U_{N,n},\qquad \sup_{|z|\le R}|U_{N,n}-1|\le C_{R,\delta}/N, \quad \delta N\le n\le(1-\delta)N. \tag{3} \] This is a factorization across the zeros of \(H_N\), rather than pointwise division by a possibly vanishing value. To prove it, let \(T_N\) be the monic Chebyshev polynomial determined by \(T_N(v+v^{-1})=v^N+v^{-N}\). The root factorization of \(T_N(w)-2\), evaluated at \(w=2\cosh(z/N)\) and divided by its value after removing the root \(w=2\), gives \[ P_{N,N-1}(z)=H_N(z)^2. \tag{4} \] The normalization uses \(T_N'(2)=N^2\). Factors at \(r\) and \(N-r\) coincide. Matching values at \(z=0\) therefore proves \[ \begin{array}{ll} N=2m+1:&P_{N,m}=H_N,\\ N=2m:&P_{N,m-1}=H_N/\cosh(z/(2N)). \end{array} \tag{5} \] The quotients in (5) are identities of entire functions; on the fixed disk the displayed cosh is also a unit for large \(N\). Starting at this midpoint, reach any \(n\) in (3) by multiplying or dividing only the intervening factors. Every intervening index lies a fixed positive fraction of \(N\) away from both endpoints. Each factor is consequently \(1+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-2})\), is a unit on the disk, and there are at most \(N\) of them. Their product or inverse product is \(1+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1})\). The cosh correction in the even case is \(1+O_R(N^{-2})\). This proves (3). Repeating the estimate on a larger disk and applying Cauchy's formula gives the same \(O(N^{-1})\) estimate for each fixed derivative in \(z\). Also \(H_N\to H\) locally uniformly, with all fixed derivatives and error \(O(N^{-2})\), where \[ H(z)=\frac{2\sinh(z/2)}{z},\qquad H(0)=1. \tag{6} \] This follows from \(H_N=H\,[z/(2N)]/\sinh(z/(2N))\). ## 2. Passing the estimate through a signed sum Let \(\Sigma_N\) be a finite set of states and let \(K_N=\sum_{\sigma}w_{N,\sigma}\ne0\). Suppose the actual deformed source is exactly \[ F_N(z)=\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma_N}w_{N,\sigma} \prod_{j=1}^{m}P_{N,n_j(\sigma)}(z), \tag{7} \] with fixed \(m\). Call a state interior if \(\delta N\le n_j(\sigma)\le(1-\delta)N\) for every \(j\). Assume constants \(C,c>0\), independent of \(N\), satisfy \[ \sum_\sigma|w_{N,\sigma}|\le C|K_N|, \qquad \sum_{\sigma\text{ not interior}}|w_{N,\sigma}| \le Ce^{-cN}|K_N|. \tag{8} \] Then, on every fixed complex disk and with every fixed derivative, \[ \frac{F_N(z)}{K_N}=H_N(z)^m+O(N^{-1}) =H(z)^m+O(N^{-1}). \tag{9} \] On the interior states, (3) gives a difference from \(H_N^m\) bounded by \(C_R/N\); (8) bounds its contracted absolute error relative to \(K_N\). On the other states, (2) bounds both terms uniformly, so their total error is exponentially small by (8). This proves (9) as a whole holomorphic estimate; Cauchy's formula on larger disks proves the derivative statement. Positivity is one sufficient reason for the first inequality in (8), but is not assumed in the theorem. The same argument works for an integral over a specified cycle if the sum of absolute weights is replaced by its total variation. It is essential to prove these inequalities for the actual contraction or its exactly equivalent cycle. An estimate on individual insertions is not (8). More generally, if the first ratio in (8) is \(\kappa_N\), the proof gives error \(O_R(\kappa_N/N)\) plus the normalized absolute tail. Thus \(\kappa_N=o(N)\) is also sufficient for convergence. An unspecified polynomial bound on \(\kappa_N\) does not suffice for this first-order estimate. ## 3. The figure-eight knot The [exact figure-eight source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), equation (1.1), proves directly from the original cut crossings and cups that \[ f_N(Y)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\prod_{r=1}^{n} (Y+Y^{-1}-Q_N^r-Q_N^{-r}), \qquad Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}. \tag{10} \] Put \(Y=e^{z/N}\). Its exact decomposition is \[ f_N(e^{z/N})=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}t_{N,n}P_{N,n}(z), \quad t_{N,n}=\prod_{r=1}^{n}4\sin^2(\pi r/N)>0, \quad K_N=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}t_{N,n}. \tag{11} \] The same source note proves, by monotone Riemann sums at the logarithmic endpoints, \(\log t_{N,n}=N\Phi(n/N)+O(\log N)\) uniformly, where \(\Phi(x)=\int_0^x\log(4\sin^2\pi u)\,du\). Its unique maximum is at \(x=5/6\). Choose, for example, \(\delta=1/12\). Compactness gives a fixed positive gap between this maximum and the complement of \([\delta,1-\delta]\). A lattice term within \(O(1/N)\) of the maximum supplies the lower bound for \(K_N\). The polynomial Riemann-sum errors and the at most \(N\) tail terms are absorbed into a smaller exponential gap. This proves (8), with \(C=1\) in its first inequality. Consequently the actual reduced meridian profile satisfies \[ g_N(z):=\frac{f_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N} =H_N(z)+O_R(N^{-1}) =H(z)+O_R(N^{-1}). \tag{12} \] The estimate is locally uniform on the whole \(z\)-plane, including all fixed resonances \(z=2\pi i k\), and holds for every fixed derivative. It follows from a whole finite source identity, without using a colored-Jones comparison or a chosen solution of a recurrence. Let \(P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}\) be the canonical degree-at-most-\(N-2\) ordinary-color interpolant and \(R_N=(f_N-P_N^{\mathrm{ord}})/S_N\), with \(S_N(Y)=1+\cdots+Y^{N-1}\). Retain the full-state centering and put \[ \rho_N(z)=e^{(N-1)z/(2N)} \frac{N R_N(e^{z/N})}{K_N}. \tag{13} \] The exact identity is \(g_N=H_N\rho_N+\pi_N\), where \(\pi_N=P_N^{\mathrm{ord}}(e^{z/N})/K_N\). The positive volume growth of (11) and the [polynomial ordinary-color bound](regularized_kashaev_period.md) imply \(\pi_N\) and all its fixed derivatives are exponentially small on every compact disk. For any prescribed disk, choose a larger boundary circle avoiding the zeros of \(H\). On that circle \(|H_N|\) is bounded away from zero. The exact numerator \(g_N-\pi_N-H_N\) is divisible by \(H_N\), so the maximum principle and (12) prove \[ \rho_N(z)=1+O_R(N^{-1}) \tag{14} \] locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. This is the canonical regular quotient. The unsubtracted full modified invariant still has actual poles at ordinary-color resonances; (14) does not remove them without their specified subtraction. In particular, for every fixed compact set of \(z\)-values, this regularized Laurent polynomial has the uniform volume limit \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|R_N(e^{z/N})\right| \longrightarrow\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus4_1). \tag{14a} \] Indeed (14) is bounded away from zero on that compact set for large \(N\), and (13) gives \(R_N(e^{z/N})=K_N e^{-(N-1)z/(2N)}[1+O_R(N^{-1})]/N\). The centering and the factor \(N^{-1}\) do not change the exponential rate. The source note identifies the complete rate with the volume of the actual figure-eight complement. Thus (14a) uses that same complement, and includes the ordinary-color resonance values of the regular quotient. This is a microscopic meridian theorem for the actual figure-eight source, used as a test of (8). The broad strict Conway volume theorem does not yet supply (7)–(8) for its main-meridian deformation. Its auxiliary color estimates leave the main meridian parabolic. ### The first correction The exact midpoint product also determines the first nonconstant regular term. Uniformly on the same bulk interval and compact \(z\)-sets, \[ N\bigl(U_{N,n}(z)-1\bigr) =-\frac{z^2}{4\pi}\cot(\pi n/N)+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}). \tag{14b} \] Indeed, for every intervening midpoint-to-\(n\) factor, \[ \log\left(1+\frac{\sinh^2(z/(2N))}{\sin^2(\pi r/N)}\right) =\frac{z^2}{4N^2}\csc^2(\pi r/N)+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-4}). \] The signed sum of these logarithms is a Riemann sum from \(1/2\) to \(n/N\); its integral is \(-\cot(\pi n/N)/\pi\). The midpoint offset and the even cosh correction contribute \(O(N^{-2})\) before multiplying by \(N\). Exponentiating gives (14b), as a whole holomorphic estimate. The positive probability weights \(t_{N,n}/K_N\) concentrate at \(5/6\). On the bulk interval the cotangent is bounded, so its weighted mean tends to \(-\sqrt3\). The exponentially small tails remain negligible after multiplication by \(N\). Equations (11) and (14b) therefore give \(N(g_N-H_N)-H_N\sqrt3 z^2/(4\pi)\to0\) locally uniformly. Subtract \(N\pi_N\) and divide on the same fixed boundary circles as above. The quotient is entire before applying the maximum principle. Hence \[ N\bigl(\rho_N(z)-1\bigr) \longrightarrow \frac{\sqrt3}{4\pi}z^2 \tag{14c} \] locally uniformly with every fixed derivative. Since \(\rho_N\) is close to one on each fixed disk, its logarithm there satisfies the same first-order limit. In particular \(N(\log\rho_N)''(0)\to\sqrt3/(2\pi)\). ### Why the coefficient is the cusp shape We compute the peripheral curves with their orientations, since the sign of the coefficient cannot be read from an unmarked polynomial. Use the braid \((\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2\) for the figure-eight knot and the meridian matrices \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}M&1\\0&M^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}M&0\\t&M^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad C=A^{-1}BAB^{-1}A. \] The braid closure gives \(t^2+(M^2+M^{-2}-3)t+3-M^2-M^{-2}=0\). Put \(D=A^{-1}BA\) and \(E=CAC^{-1}\). The successive meridian triples under the four crossings are \[ (A,B,C),\quad(D,A,C),\quad(D,C,E),\quad (D^{-1}CD,D,E),\quad(D^{-1}CD,E,EDE^{-1}). \] The closure relation reduces the final triple to \((A,B,C)\). Track each original strand through the crossings: its accumulated underpass transport is respectively \(C\), \(BA^{-1}\), and \(D^{-1}\). Following the closed knot visits these strands in that order, so the transport is \(W=D^{-1}BA^{-1}C\). The writhe is zero. With the preferred-longitude convention of the [peripheral calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md), the longitude is \(\lambda=W^{-1}=C^{-1}AB^{-1}A^{-1}BA\). At \(M=1\), direct multiplication using \(t^2-t+1=0\) gives \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \lambda=\begin{pmatrix}-1&4t-2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}. \] The meridian translates the boundary plane by one. The projective action of the longitude translates it by \(2-4t\). The [positive Bloch specialization](figure_eight_bloch_specialization.md) selects \(t=(1-\sqrt3\,i)/2\), paired with the ideal tetrahedron shape \((1+\sqrt3\,i)/2\) in the upper half-plane. Thus the oriented cusp shape is \(\tau=2-4t=2\sqrt3\,i\). The preferred longitude lift still has eigenvalue \(-1\) at completeness. To check its variation without dropping that sign, the upper-left entry of the same matrix word is \[ L_{\mathrm{intr}}(M) =M^4-2M^2-1+M^{-2}+(M^2-M^{-2})t(M). \] It satisfies \(L_{\mathrm{intr}}(1)=-1\) and \(\left.d\log L_{\mathrm{intr}}/d\log M\right|_{M=1}=2-4t=\tau\). Centering the longitude as \(\ell=-L_{\mathrm{intr}}\) changes neither this derivative nor the recorded sign of its lift. In the squared coordinates \(U=2\log M\), \(V=2\log\ell\), the ratio \(dV/dU\) is again \(\tau\). Consequently the coefficient proved from the finite sum is \[ N(\rho_N(z)-1)\longrightarrow\frac{\tau}{8\pi i}z^2,\qquad N\rho_N''(0)\longrightarrow\frac{\tau}{4\pi i}. \] Here \(M=e^{z/(2N)}\). Both this scale and the primitive peripheral curves are needed for the factor \(8\pi i\). The calculation proves the match for this knot; it does not infer an analogous asymptotic for other knots merely from their peripheral equations. ### Illustration and reproduction ![Finite figure-eight meridian profiles at levels 24, 47 and 80, together with the limiting sine profile and the error after ordinary-color subtraction.](../book/figures/figure-eight-meridian-profile.png) Set \(z=it\) with real \(t\). The left panel compares \(g_N(it)=f_N(e^{it/N})/K_N\) with \(H(it)=2\sin(t/2)/t\). The right panel shows \(\lvert\rho_N(it)-1\rvert\). At \(t=\pm2\pi,\pm4\pi\), the displayed quotient for \(\rho_N\) has a removable zero in both numerator and denominator. The values plotted there use their derivatives, as required by the definition of the regular quotient. The proof above applies on every fixed complex compact set; the figure shows one real slice. Run the [plot script](../experiments/plot_figure_eight_meridian_profile.py) to regenerate the PDF, SVG, PNG and [finite numerical data](../experiments/figure_eight_meridian_profile_plot.json): ~~~sh python3 experiments/plot_figure_eight_meridian_profile.py ~~~ The script evaluates the finite sum and its specified interpolant. The plotted curves are illustrations of the theorem. ## 4. Individual shifted factorials There is a useful more general local calculation. For \(\delta N\le n\le(1-\delta)N\), let \[ A_{N,n}(s)=\prod_{r=1}^{n} \frac{\sin(\pi(r+s)/N)}{\sin(\pi r/N)}. \tag{15} \] Uniformly for \(s\) in any fixed compact complex set, \[ A_{N,n}(s)= \frac{[N\sin(\pi n/N)/\pi]^s}{\Gamma(1+s)} V_{N,n}(s), \qquad V_{N,n}=1+O(N^{-1}). \tag{16} \] Here the positive real base fixes its logarithm. The factor \(V\) is a holomorphic unit, including at negative integers where the reciprocal Gamma factor vanishes, for all sufficiently large \(N\). Each fixed derivative of \(V-1\) has the same bound. For a direct proof, separate each sine into its linear factor and \(\operatorname{sinc}\). Euler's product for Gamma, with its tail estimated by \(\sum_{r>n}O_R(r^{-2})\), gives \[ \prod_{r=1}^{n}\frac{r+s}{r} =\frac{n^s}{\Gamma(1+s)}[1+O_R(n^{-1})]. \tag{17} \] One first removes the finitely many factors whose zeros lie in the chosen compact set. The remaining logarithms have no zero there, so (17) is a holomorphic-unit estimate through those zeros as well. The harmonic-sum correction \(H_n-\log n-\gamma=O(1/n)\) and the convergent logarithmic tail justify the bound without assuming the ratio is nonzero at a Gamma pole. Now \(b(t)=\log[\sin(\pi t)/(\pi t)]\) is holomorphic on a fixed complex neighborhood of \([0,1-\delta]\), with \(b(0)=0\). Taylor expansion and a Riemann-sum estimate yield \[ \sum_{r=1}^{n}\bigl[b((r+s)/N)-b(r/N)\bigr] =s\,b(n/N)+O_{R,\delta}(N^{-1}). \tag{18} \] Exponentiating (18) and combining with (17) proves (16). It explains the paired result: set \(s=z/(2\pi i)\) and multiply the shifts \(s,-s\). Their powers of \(N\sin(\pi n/N)/\pi\) cancel, and \(1/[\Gamma(1+s)\Gamma(1-s)]=\sin(\pi s)/(\pi s)=H(z)\). The exact midpoint argument additionally retains \(H_N\) and its finite-level resonance zeros. For a finite product of shifted factors with shifts \(a_j s\) and integer powers \(\varepsilon_j\), (16) shows explicitly that the power of \(N\) is \(s\sum_j\varepsilon_j a_j\). It cancels when that signed sum is zero. The remaining leading multiplier is \[ \prod_j\Gamma(1+a_js)^{-\varepsilon_j} \exp\left(s\sum_j\varepsilon_j a_j \log[\sin(\pi x_j)/\pi]\right), \quad x_j=n_j/N. \tag{19} \] When negative powers occur, this statement is made first on compact sets avoiding the denominator zeros; any continuation across them must be justified in the original whole source. Formula (19) does not by itself identify its exponential with a longitude or its Gamma factor with the single-knot factor \(H\). Those are explicit source and geometric matching obligations. Likewise, the local factorial estimate does not supply the contraction estimate (8). ## Relation to earlier asymptotic questions Colored Alexander asymptotics for the figure-eight knot were already studied by Cho and Jun Murakami in [*Some limits of the colored Alexander invariant of the figure-eight knot and the volume of hyperbolic orbifolds*](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216509007464). The statement proved here fixes \(q_N\) at its exact root and varies the main color by a bounded complex offset, then retains the canonical ordinary-color subtraction and every fixed derivative. The available bibliographic check did not settle whether this precise normalized profile appears in that earlier work. No priority claim is made. The proof here is the finite-product and concentration argument given above.

title: Faithful parabolic cap certificates on the complete original character support
text: # Faithful parabolic cap certificates on the complete original character support 29 October 2026. The complete three-head source cubic has an elementary finite representation atlas, including its pair-trace endpoints. Its source line imposes the LITERAL cap relation on every irreducible point. At larger plat width a pair trace and a total trace do not suffice. A finite list of cubic witness traces, inherited from the original matrix cap relation, is faithful on the irreducible locus. Nilpotent normal directions are explicitly distinguished from this statement about the reduced geometric support. There is also a uniform bounded-representative construction from bounded pair traces. For a one-component knot it gives an elementary quantitative separation from the all-parabolic reducible character. These are genuine geometric support/compactness results. They do not estimate the quantum Racah transport or the positive word energy. ## 1. Unipotent trace tests All matrices below lie in SL2(C). Write a trace-two unipotent as mu=I+N, where tr N=0 and N^2=0. A nonzero N has rank one and its image equals its kernel, the fixed flag of mu. For two NONCENTRAL trace-two unipotents, Tr(mu nu)=2 iff they have the same fixed flag. (1) Indeed N=u phi, M=v psi with phi(u)=psi(v)=0. The extra trace is phi(v)psi(u). In dimension two either factor vanishes precisely when the two fixed lines agree. Central matrices are included separately. Suppose mu_1,mu_2,mu_3 have trace two and Tr(mu_2 mu_1)=2, Tr(mu_3 mu_2 mu_1)=2. (2) If their tuple is irreducible, then mu_2 mu_1=I. To prove this, put P=mu_2 mu_1. If P!=I, (1) implies that mu_1,mu_2 and P share one fixed flag, also when one input is central. P is a noncentral trace-two unipotent. The second equation in (2), together with (1), makes mu_3 share that flag or be central. The tuple is reducible, a contradiction. This proof has no affine-position or finite shear assumption on an individual flag. ## 2. The actual three-head cubic, and both original caps For the original complete heads set mu_i=-H_i, so Tr mu_i=2. The full source Hom module has D=Tr(H_3H_2H_1)=-2, hence Tr(mu_3mu_2mu_1)=2. Write A=Tr(mu_2mu_1), B=Tr(mu_3mu_2), C=Tr(mu_3mu_1), X=A-2, Y=B-2, Z=C-2, S=X+Y+Z. The [actual character cubic](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) is F(X,Y,Z)=S^2+XYZ=0. (3) Every finite point except the origin has an explicit irreducible representative. On X!=0 use mu_1=[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=[[1,0],[X,1]], mu_3=[[1+S/X,Y/X],[Z,1-S/X]]. (4) Its determinant minus one is -F/X^2, its trace is two, its pair traces are exactly A,B,C, and the triple trace is exactly two. The first two flags are distinct. Cyclically permuting the meridians supplies the other pair-coordinate charts and preserves the triple trace. The only missing point is X=Y=Z=0: all pair traces are two, so (1) makes every such tuple reducible. This proves the finite atlas without assuming a character variety reconstruction theorem. The actual initial ordinary-cup source has A=2. On the irreducible locus (2) therefore gives mu_2mu_1=I. Its reduced source line is explicitly (A,B,C)=(2,2-t,2+t), t!=0, mu_1=[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=mu_1^(-1), mu_3=[[1,0],[t,1]]. (5) At X=0 equation (3) is (Y+Z)^2=0. The square is important: the reduced line is honest inverse-pair geometry, while its polarization has a quadratic normal ramification. It is not permission to remove the actual c_0 Hermite derivative source. Every actual Hurwitz word preserves the ordered total product mu_3mu_2mu_1 and irreducibility. Applying (2) at both ends shows: an irreducible character on the initial A=2 source and final A=2 source has BOTH literal inverse-pair caps. Preservation of the total product then matches the remaining meridian as a matrix, not merely by its trace. Following the actual crossing assignments and these cap identifications therefore gives an honest representation of that original one-component cup--braid--cap knot. This applies to the complete source support, not just its geometric branch. Finite intermediate pair traces A=+/-2 or B=+/-2 do not invalidate (4)--(5): another nonzero pair coordinate supplies a chart, unless the entire character is reducible. This statement is about finite characters, not about ignoring a polar spectral-coordinate Jacobian. ## 3. A faithful witness certificate at arbitrary plat width For a tuple mu_1,...,mu_b of trace-two unipotents and a selected cap pair, put P=mu_v mu_u. On the irreducible locus the following finite trace conditions are EQUIVALENT to the literal matrix relation P=I: Tr P=2, Tr(mu_k P)=Tr mu_k=2, every k=1,...,b. (6) The reverse implication is immediate. For the forward implication, if P!=I it is a noncentral unipotent. Every noncentral mu_k shares its fixed flag by (1), making the whole tuple reducible. This proves the equivalence at arbitrary fixed width, with no chosen flag chart. These are genuine source witnesses, not new favorable constraints. The exact original cup obeys the framed matrix identity (H_v H_u-I)p=0, as proved in [the original plat source theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md). Left multiplication by ANY specified based quantum meridian and taking its ordered quantum trace gives another exact annihilator. Its commutative principal equation is the corresponding witness in (6). The same applies to the outgoing ordinary cap, with its actual row order. Under the original Hurwitz transport these equations give literal incoming and outgoing cap relations on irreducible reduced support. The full marked co-source is retained separately; it is not replaced by an invariant cap on arbitrary exteriors. For the original even plat, use its WHOLE invariant-tensor source identification first. The input cups impose the full ordered total meridian product I, which the exact Hurwitz word preserves. At the output, literal inverse pairs at the ordinary caps then force the last pair to be inverse by that total MATRIX equation. This is how the marked pair acquires the faithful classical cap relation in the assembled source. It is not an annihilator assertion for an arbitrary unrestricted marked row; its quantum values and normal components remain in the scalar and its norm estimate. Pair traces and the total product alone are insufficient. For example, take six heads with mu_1=upper(1), mu_2=upper(-1), mu_3=mu_4=lower(1), mu_5=mu_6=lower(-1), upper(t)=[[1,t],[0,1]], lower(t)=[[1,0],[t,1]]. All three cap-pair traces are two and their total product is I. The tuple is irreducible, but the second and third pair products are lower(2) and lower(-2). A witness with mu_1 detects the failure: Tr(mu_1 lower(2))=4. Thus the all-width assertion uses the actual witnesses (or literal framed matrix constraints), not a total trace. There is also an exact nonreduced qualification. Localize where two witness meridians are upper(1) and lower(a), a!=0. Write P=I+T, T=[[u,v],[w,-u]]. Its trace and determinant equations give u^2+vw=0. The two witness equations give w=0 and av=0, leaving u^2=0. Thus their REDUCED support is P=I, but a square-zero normal direction can remain in the trace scheme. The original framed matrix relation is stronger, and the quantum source jets must remain. No amplitude bound for such jets is inferred from radical equality. ### Exact interval-Casimir Ward identities already provide a faithful list There is a particularly direct original quantum certificate which does not need independent single-head witness operators. Let iota_p insert the original cup into two adjacent tensor positions a,a+1. It is a Hopf map from the trivial representation: E_p p=F_p p=0 and K_p p=p. Coassociativity of the LITERAL coproduct therefore gives, for j>=a+1, Omega_[a,j] iota_p=iota_p Omega_[a+2,j], (6a) with spectators unchanged. An empty interval is the trivial module, whose Casimir is q+q^(-1), not an invented constant two at finite N. For i<=a there is also the left version Omega_[i,a+1] iota_p=iota_p Omega_[i,a-1]. (6b) Both identities hold for EVERY original E,F,K element before taking the Casimir: on the cup its counit values reduce the coproduct to the remaining ordered factors. This proves them including endpoints, all N normalizations, and arbitrary spectator vectors. It is not a scalar source argument or a commutative approximation. Their commutative principal trace equations, with the two meridian minus signs canceled by deleting a pair, are Tr P=2, Tr(S_j P)=Tr S_j, S_j=mu_j...mu_(a+2), j>=a+2, Tr(P T_i)=Tr T_i, T_i=mu_(a-1)...mu_i, i<=a-1. (6c) This shorter list is faithful on the irreducible locus. If P!=I, put P=I+tau E_12 in a common frame, tau!=0. Each deletion equation says exactly that the corresponding S_j or T_i has lower-left entry zero. Thus every such partial product preserves the flag. Taking successive quotients shows that ALL meridians to the right and to the left preserve it. The two members of the cup pair do so by (1). This is a reducible tuple, a contradiction. The proof also covers a pair at either endpoint; for an interior pair BOTH sides are retained, so no cyclic recut or unavailable prefix is assumed. The entire exact annihilator list is transported by the actual signed braid intertwiner, or its actual Hurwitz map on meridians, rather than being reimposed after a selected channel was dropped. The outgoing ordinary cap has the dual interval identities. The assembled marked pair is treated by total-product preservation as stated above. Equations (6a)--(6c) therefore give an original-source-derived, all-width faithful REDUCED geometric cap certificate. The nonreduced qualification preceding this paragraph still applies; none of these arguments removes the retained quantum Hermite normal data. ## 4. Bounded characters have bounded representatives For ANY irreducible trace-two parabolic tuple choose a pair maximizing M=max_(r,s)|Tr(mu_r mu_s)-2|>0. After relabeling, a common SL2 conjugation puts that pair in the form mu_r=upper(1), mu_s=lower(a), |a|=M. Write any other meridian as I+[[u,v],[w,-u]]. Its pair traces give |w|<=M, |v|<=1, |u|^2=|vw|<=M. (7) Consequently every mu_k AND its inverse have operator norm at most B_M=2+sqrt(M)+M. This gives uniformly bounded representatives on every bounded pair-character set, even when a previous affine flag coordinate escaped. If M tends to zero, after a subsequence these representatives tend to upper unipotents and hence a reducible tuple. For a ONE-COMPONENT knot there is a stronger quantitative separation. Following its fixed crossing/cap identifications expresses any two oriented head meridians as conjugate or inverse-conjugate by a fixed word of length at most L in the head meridians and their inverses. The finite L is determined by the original diagram; it follows by successive substitution of its literal Hurwitz and cap equations. Enlarge L to at least one. If M<=1, the representatives above have all generator/inverse norms at most four. For the maximizing pair, ||upper(1)-I||=1 and ||lower(a)-I||=M. Their fixed conjugacy relation therefore gives 1<=4^(2L) M, hence M>=4^(-2L). (8) If M>1 the same lower bound is automatic. Thus irreducible boundary-parabolic representations of this fixed knot are separated from the all-pair-traces-two character. On a set M<=M_0, every individual meridian also satisfies ||mu_k-I||>=B_(M_0)^(-2L). (9) This follows by comparing it to the normalized upper(1) generator. The conclusion does not assume that distinct meridians have distinct fixed flags: honest cap partners have the same flag. It rules out central-meridian degeneration within this bounded irreducible family. ## 5. Geometric consequence and precise remaining scope Initial and final faithful cap certificates, sewn by the actual Hurwitz graph, give the original Wirtinger/cap representation space on irreducible reduced support at every fixed plat width. The above finite atlas and bounds treat finite pair-character degenerations; an escaping unbounded-character family is a separate boundary problem. Every resulting honest boundary-parabolic representation satisfies [the independently proved representation-volume bound](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md). Accordingly a FULL canonically calibrated critical action on this closed character support is bounded by knot volume. The present proof identifies the source geometry; it does NOT establish that every constrained face critical of a scalar kernel follows that full canonical graph, nor bound its exit currents. It does not identify an arbitrary balanced Racah action with the regulator without its normalizer and branch constants. Most importantly, it does not prove the remaining positive word-energy estimate or geometric noncancellation. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_parabolic_cap_trace_certificate.py): exact symbolic cubic reconstruction, source-line caps, all-width counterexample/witnesses, nonreduced normal qualification, and bounded representatives for explicit irreducible unipotent tuples. The finite audit checks 37 literal all-position quantum cup AND ordinary-cap E/F/K/Casimir interval deletions, including empty intervals and levels of both parities; exact symbolic cubic/source/prefix-witness/normal identities; the six-head insufficiency example; and four bounded irreducible reconstruction families. Compilation passes.

title: A general two-current reduction of the first Racah normal
status: Historical reduction; remaining currents now bounded
text: # A general two-current reduction of the first Racah normal **Later result, 29 October 2026:** the [full all-partner first-normal theorem](actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.md) now bounds the remaining actual currents, using a positive presentation of the complete generic source on face-supported branches. The reductions and sharp rank obstructions below remain valid for the particular Ward/Fourier relations studied here. Their undetermined components are not counterexamples to the later source theorem. General higher normals and completed physical transport remain open. 29 October 2026. The exact physical cluster Ward identity first reduces the first normal of all sixty-four reflected Racah branches to at most THREE potentially live-tail currents. Combining it with the independently proved Fourier partner involution reduces this to at most TWO, uniformly for every supported folded sextuple. The remaining entries have the proved positive-core normal bounds. In particular, when at least two opposite edge pairs have equal folded labels, every partner first normal has a uniform polynomial bound, including branches with a nonempty second-zero tail. This is a first-normal statement, not an all-order or physical Hermitian transport theorem. ## 1. The actual scalar and its opposite-pair Ward equation Use the integer-spin supported folded sextuple and actual generic normalization of [the partner reflection theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md): D=N-1, 0<=j_i<=D/2, K_B(zeta)=[N]^2 S_B(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_B^2, k(B)=D_log(zeta) K_B(q), q=exp(pi i/N). Here B is a choice of six partner bits, and the generic seven-factorial sum, all face normalizations and every [2N] current remain present. All root values are the same strictly positive number W_N^2. In the label order (a,b,c,d,e,f), the opposite edge pairs are (a,c), (b,d), (e,f). (1) For either internal pair e,e*=D-e and f,f*=D-f, the proved generic source-projector identity gives sum_(i,j=0,1) d_(e_i)d_(f_j) K_(i,j) =[N]^2 tr(E_e E_f)=O(t^2), d_j=[2j+1], t=log(zeta/q). (2) If both pairs are nontrivial, d_e*(q)=-d_e(q) and likewise for f. When differentiating (2), the part differentiating the dimensions is exactly W_N^2 times the derivative of (d_e+d_e*)(d_f+d_f*), which vanishes at t=0 because both factors vanish there. The remaining coefficient in (2), divided by the two nonzero root dimensions, is k(0,0)-k(0,1)-k(1,0)+k(1,1)=0. (3) If one partner is simple, its two bit choices label the same generic function, so (3) is tautological. Tetrahedral edge relabeling proves (3) for each of the three pairs in (1), for EVERY choice of the other four partner bits. This is the actual generic first normal; it is not a differentiated equality of root values. Thus k belongs to the tensor product of three three-dimensional spaces of functions on a square satisfying its additive equation. Equivalently its multilinear Boolean expansion has no coefficient containing both members of any opposite pair. Its dimension is at most 27; simple/duplicate branches may reduce that dimension. ## 2. An explicit interpolation with at most three unbounded inputs For each folded edge put delta_i=D/2-j_i>=0. Within each opposite pair order the edges so that delta_big>=delta_small, and write s_r=delta_big+delta_small, d_r=delta_big-delta_small>=0, r=1,2,3. (4) A partner bit zero means a low label D/2-delta, and one means D/2+delta. On the r-th pair retain these three bit states: 0=(0,0), -=(0,1), +=(1,0). Their deviations of the pair's label sum from D are respectively u_r(0)=-s_r, u_r(-)=-d_r, u_r(+) = d_r. (5) The omitted state (1,1) is reconstructed, by (3), as k(...,11,...) = k(...,-,...) + k(...,+,...) - k(...,0,...). (6) Apply (6) independently to the three pairs. Every one of the 64 first normals is an explicit signed sum of at most 27 entries in the grid {0,-,+}^3. Its coefficient absolute sum is at most 27; no division by a small color difference or by a quantum dimension occurs in this interpolation. The opposite sums in the actual seven-factorial range are exactly Q_1=2D+u_1+u_2, Q_2=2D+u_1+u_3, Q_3=2D+u_2+u_3. (7) The existing tail-free theorem applies whenever min Q_r<=2D. A grid point failing that condition has all three pairwise sums u_i+u_j strictly positive. It must therefore have at least two positive u's, hence at least two '+' states. The only possibilities are: * (+,+,+), if all pairwise sums d_i+d_j are positive; * '+' on two pairs and '-' on pair r, only if d_r<min(d_i,d_j); * '+' on two pairs and '0' on pair r, only if s_r<min(d_i,d_j). In each of the last two cases r must be the UNIQUE strict minimum of the three d's, since s_r>=d_r. Consequently there are at most THREE such grid points. This is an exact all-label assertion, with strict inequalities at the boundary handled as written. Let E be this explicit exceptional set. By the proved tail-free bound there are absolute C,c such that, for every partner B, |k(B)| <= 27 C N^c W_N^2 + sum_(v in E)|k(v)|. (8) The coefficient of any retained grid entry in the expanded formula is 0,+1 or -1, explaining the unit coefficient on the exceptional sum. No claim that its terms are individually polynomial is needed to prove (8). ## 3. A complete first-normal theorem with genuine live tails If at least two of the three opposite pairs have equal folded labels, at least two d_r vanish. Every point of the interpolation grid has a nonpositive pairwise sum, so E is empty. Equation (8) then proves, uniformly on this supported class and all its partner branches, |D_log(zeta) K_B(q)| <= C' N^c W_N^2. (9) This includes every supported disphenoid label pattern (a,b,a,b,e,e), and permits one of those opposite equalities to be removed. It controls a first normal even if B itself has min Q_B>2D. For example N=3m+1 and folded labels all m have all-high partners all 2m, whose range z=6m,...,8m has a nonempty [2N] tail for every m>=1. All those first normals satisfy (9). The same conclusion bounds the coherent tail VALUE T(q)/C(q) polynomially for this class. Indeed the exact scalar has K_B=U_B G_B^2, G_B=C_B+[2N]T_B, U_B=[N]^4 product_faces Delta_B^2, where U_B is a nonzero analytic unit after the four face zeros are canceled.
