Its logarithmic derivative and C_B'(q)/C_B(q) have the proved polynomial unit-factorial bounds. Divide the derivative of K_B by its root value U_B(q) C_B(q)^2 and use (9). This bounds G_B'(q)/C_B(q), hence T_B(q)/C_B(q), because D_log(zeta)[2N](q)=4N/(q-q^-1) is nonzero with a polynomially bounded inverse. The independent [finite Fourier residue theorem](actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.md) now proves the sharper all-high cotangent formula and controls every branch with a repeated maximal face. Those are additional identities; they are not obtained by differentiating the Ward interpolation. Neither argument supplies a bound for derivatives of T_B. ## 4. Why the first-order identity does not determine higher normals The right side of (2) is only O(t^2), and its second coefficient contains the actual finite cluster overlap tr(E_e(q)E_f(q)). Second differentiation also produces first derivatives of quantum dimensions multiplying k(B). Thus the homogeneous equation (3) cannot be imposed on second or higher normals. No positive physical metric, small condition number, or complete marked-source bound is inferred from the first-normal interpolation. Even at first order the remaining exceptional currents cannot in general be recovered from tail-free values and (3) alone. In fact THREE is sharp for this method. Choose delta=(5,19,3,9,4,16) in the original edge order and D=80, hence folded labels (35,21,37,31,36,24). All faces satisfy the support inequalities. Exact linear algebra on the 27-dimensional space shows that its 48 tail-free vertices impose rank 24, leaving THREE unconstrained directions. The audit constructs this rank over the rationals. This is an obstruction to that interpolation method, not a counterexample to a bound for the actual source function. The proof consists of the actual projector identity (2), its careful first derivative, and the finite interpolation and support inequalities above. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_partner_first_normal_ward_reduction.py) also checks the full generic normal coefficients in finite root fields; it does not replace the proof by sampled values. ## 5. The Fourier partner involution reduces three currents to two The [finite Fourier theorem, section 6](actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.md#6-the-residual-is-an-exact-partner-involution) now proves an additional ACTUAL first-normal relation. For a live branch with a unique largest face, let B* flip the three complementary edges while retaining that face. Then |k(B)-k(B*)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (10) This includes all face normalizations. It follows from the exact coherent tail difference, equality of the two positive cores, and their separately bounded generic core and face-factor derivatives. Together, (3) and (10) reduce EVERY supported sextuple to at most TWO uncontrolled partner first normals. Here is a uniform proof, including the only case not already settled by section 2. If its exceptional set E has at most two elements, there is nothing to do. If E has three elements, relabel the opposite pairs so that s_1 < min(d_2,d_3). (11) On the FULL 64-vertex cube, the live-tail condition is now exactly that the larger-deficit edge of pair 2 and the larger-deficit edge of pair 3 both have their high bit set. Indeed a high dominant bit in pair i gives u_i>=d_i, while a low one gives u_i<=-d_i. Also |u_1|<=s_1. Thus both dominant bits high make every pairwise sum positive, while either dominant bit low makes its sum with u_1 negative. The live set is a 16-vertex cylinder, independent of the other four bits. Call those two dominant edges p and q. They belong to a unique tetrahedral face together with one edge r of pair 1; call its opposite edge r*. That face is the UNIQUE largest face everywhere in the live cylinder. To check this without an incidence guess, the four faces are (p,q,r), (p,q*,r*), (p*,q,r*), (p*,q*,r). Writing each label as D/2 plus its signed deficit, the first face exceeds the second by at least d_3-s_1>0, the third by at least d_2-s_1>0, and the fourth by at least d_2+d_3>0. Thus (10) applies everywhere in this cylinder, and its move flips precisely r*,p*,q*. Changing the bit p* with p high changes k by a controlled quantity: the Ward equation (3) says that this difference equals the same difference with p LOW, and both of those entries are tail-free by the cylinder description. The identical assertion holds for q*. Consequently their two flips in (10) can be removed at polynomial cost. What remains is a polynomial bound for changing r* alone within the cylinder. In the 27-point interpolation grid the three exceptional entries are exactly the three pair-1 states 0,-,+, with pairs 2 and 3 in state '+'. The last relation identifies, up to polynomial cost, the state 0 with either '-' or '+', according as r* is the smaller- or larger-deficit edge of pair 1. Eliminate state 0. At most two actual partner values remain. Explicitly there is a set R of at most two partner branches such that max_B |k(B)| <= C N^c W_N^2 + 2 sum_(v in R)|k(v)|. (12) All constants are uniform in N and the supported labels. No small matrix determinant is inverted: the proof uses the signed Ward interpolation, at most two tail-free bit differences, and one controlled Fourier partner difference. This is a reduction of the remaining problem, not a bound for the two residual currents. TWO is sharp for these relations. For the D=80 example in section 4, the live cylinder is exactly b=f=1. Its unique largest face is (b,c,f), and its Fourier partner move flips (a,d,e). In Boolean notation both functions h_1(B)=b f, h_2(B)=b c f vanish on all tail-free vertices, obey every opposite-pair Ward equation, and are unchanged by every applicable Fourier partner move. They are linearly independent. There is no live repeated-maximal-face vertex in this example. Equivalently the exact combined constraint matrix has rank 25 in the 27-dimensional Ward space. Hence these relations alone leave two free components, even after every known bounded vertex and every applicable involution is used. They do not prove the general first-normal estimate or higher-order transport. The focused audit freshly passes 33 actual source families, all 64 first-normal reconstructions for each family, 3,000 deficit-pattern classifications (including the cylinder and unique-face implications), and exact rational ranks 24 and 25 for the separate and combined constraints. These checks supplement the uniform argument above.

title: Spectral control and the tail-free boundary of Racah normal transport
text: # Spectral control and the tail-free boundary of Racah normal transport 29 October 2026. The new estimate here is a polynomial spectral gap for the ACTUAL folded root polynomial and bounds for every fixed SPECTRAL derivative. It also records a general sufficient criterion for full generic-q partner-normal transport: the actual factorial range must stop before its [2N] current. A one-edge partner always has that property, so its normal bound is a corollary of the existing positive-core theorem, not a bound on a nonzero discarded current. The first-normal spectral identity below is exact, but the general nonempty-tail normal problem and a physical confluent-frame norm bound remain open. ## 1. Exact source convention and the restricted transport theorem Put D=N-1, M=floor(D/2), q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and theta=pi/N. All six spins below are integers. Let a,b,c,d,e,f<=M and assume a+b+e,c+d+e,a+d+f,b+c+f >= D. (1) Use the SAME generic seven-factorial sum S(zeta), face factors Delta_F^2, and normalized squared scalar K_e(zeta)=[N]^2 S(zeta)^2 product_F Delta_F^2 (2) as in [the common-phase/normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md). This is the scalar diagonal gauge of the ACTUAL generic four-port source proved in [the full source theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), not a substituted root 6j value. Let e*=D-e and form K_e* by changing ONLY e in the same generic formula. Both germs are analytic at q. More generally let B be ANY of the sixty-four partner branches and let Q_B be its three opposite sums. If min Q_B <= 2D, (3a) then, for every fixed r, in t=log(zeta/q), |D_t^r K_B(q)| <= C_r N^(c_r) W_N^2. (3b) The constants are independent of labels and N. Indeed its actual z range ends at min Q_B. Every term therefore contains exactly one [N], and no [2N]. After [N] cancellation, the generic expression has a positive common-phase root core and only unit denominator factors. The uniform positive-core germ theorem applies to all its fixed jets; its normalized root value is W_N^2 by the all-partner value theorem. This proves (3b) without discarding any term. For the single partner e*=D-e, the untouched opposite sum a+b+c+d<=2D automatically proves (3a). In particular there is an absolute C such that K_e(q)=K_e*(q)=W_N^2>0, |dot K_e*(q)| <= C N^8 W_N^2. (3) The value equality follows from the stronger [all-sixty-four VALUE reflection theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md). The proof below only needs its single-internal-edge case. By tetrahedral relabeling, (3) applies to ANY ONE partner of a folded sextuple. Its first-normal estimate is rederived in section4 to identify exactly the spectral term which higher-order transport would require. A local square root with positive root value also has polynomial fixed-jet bounds under criterion (3a). Criterion (3a) can fail already for TWO adjacent partners: N=5, folded labels (1,1,2,2,2,2), partners (3,3,2,2,2,2), give the true range z=8,9, so z=9 contains [2N]. Here the exact regularized sum is C+[2N]T with C(q)=(3+sqrt(5))/2 and T(q)=-1: the current is really nonzero, not merely allowed by an index bound. The spectral theorem below does not control it. No assertion for such branches is made. ## 2. The actual root polynomial and its degree recurrence Set p=min(a+d,b+c), s=a+b+c+d, t0=s-2p, h=max(|a-b|,|c-d|), rA=a+b-h, rC=c+d-h, L=2p-D, n=p-f, t=p+f-D. (4) The supports imply 0<=t<=n, n+t=L, and rA,rC>=L. In particular L>=0. If t=0 (possibly with L>0) the root polynomial below is 1, all its positive-order spectral derivatives vanish, and no killed matrix is needed. Let alpha=q^(2h+1), lambda=z+z^-1. The actual generic source polynomial is G_n(z;zeta)=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,P Q^(n-1),alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q^(t0+1),Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_k, P=Q^(-2p), (5) where in the GENERIC formula Q=zeta^2 and alpha=zeta^(2h+1). The denominators are root units. At the root P=Q^(1-L), the second upper parameter is Q^-t, and (5) becomes the degree-t polynomial R_t(lambda)=sum_(k=0)^t A_k product_(i<k)(c_(h+i)-lambda), c_j=2cos((2j+1)theta), A_k= [s_n/s_(n-k)] [s_t/s_(t-k)] [s_(rA-k)/s_rA] [s_(rC-k)/s_rC] s_t0/(s_k s_(t0+k)) >0. (6) Here s_j=product_(u=1)^j 2sin(u theta). This is an identity of root polynomials, not a deletion of the GENERIC k>t terms. The phase in (6) cancels exactly: the residual exponent is Nk and the remaining sign is (-1)^k, so (-1)^k q^(Nk)=1. It also follows directly by converting each finite Pochhammer to sine factors. For completeness the following recurrence is an OWN finite-product calculation. For arbitrary generic alpha,beta,gamma,delta, put P=alpha beta gamma delta, and define R_j by the finite sum (5) with upper parameters Q^-j,PQ^(j-1) and denominators Q,alpha beta,alpha gamma,alpha delta. Then lambda R_j=A_j R_(j+1) +(alpha+alpha^-1-A_j-C_j)R_j+C_j R_(j-1), A_j=product_(u=beta,gamma,delta)(1-alpha u Q^j) (1-PQ^(j-1)) /[alpha(1-PQ^(2j-1))(1-PQ^(2j))], C_j=alpha(1-Q^j) product_(uv=beta gamma,beta delta,gamma delta)(1-uvQ^(j-1)) /[(1-PQ^(2j-2))(1-PQ^(2j-1))]. (7) To verify it without invoking a polynomial-family theorem, use M_k=(alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k and lambda M_k=(alpha Q^k+alpha^-1 Q^-k)M_k -alpha^-1 Q^-k M_(k+1). If h_jk is its coefficient in R_j, the three required ratios are h_(j+1),k/h_jk=(1-Q^(-j-1))(1-PQ^(j+k-1)) /[(1-Q^(k-j-1))(1-PQ^(j-1))], h_(j-1),k/h_jk=(1-Q^(k-j))(1-PQ^(j-2)) /[(1-Q^-j)(1-PQ^(j+k-2))], h_j,k-1/h_jk=(1-Q^k) product_u(1-alpha u Q^(k-1)) /[Q(1-Q^(k-j-1))(1-PQ^(j+k-2))]. Substitution proves (7) after one common-denominator multiplication; the k=0 and terminating endpoints are obtained before division, or by the same cleared polynomial identity. Thus it remains valid at our root whenever j<t. Here C_0 is identically zero and is set to zero BEFORE root specialization; after omitting it, the remaining recurrence denominators are units. ## 3. A killed birth-death operator with a polynomial spectral gap At the parameters in (4), A_j=-a_j and C_j=-b_j, where b_0=0 and for 0<=j<t a_j=4 sin((t0+1+j)theta) sin((rA-j)theta) sin((rC-j)theta) sin((L-j)theta) /[sin((L-2j)theta) sin((L-2j-1)theta)], b_j=4 sin(j theta) sin((rA-L+j)theta) sin((rC-L+j)theta) sin((s+2-N-j)theta) /[sin((L-2j+1)theta) sin((L-2j)theta)]. (8) Every numerator sine index of a_j is in 1,...,D, and hence a_j>=64/N^4, a_j>=b_j>=0. (9) Here is a proof of the second inequality, which is important for the uniformity. First t0<=2h and rA,rC>=L follow from the four choices of the largest difference in h and a,b,c,d<=D/2. For example, when h=a-b>=|c-d|, p=b+c, rA-L=D-2c>=0 and rC-L=D-a-b-c+d>=0 because c-d<=a-b. The other cases follow by exchanging the two pairs and their ends. For j>=1 put v=L-2j, x=t0+1+j, y=rA-L+j, z=rC-L+j, and Delta_v(u)=log sin((u+v)theta)-log sin(u theta). All indices used are strictly between 0 and N. The function Delta_v is decreasing, and Delta_v(N-v-u)=-Delta_v(u). Moreover y+z=t0+D-2h-v<=D-v<N-v, so Delta_v(y)+Delta_v(z)>=0. Since x>=j+1, (8) gives log(a_j/b_j)>=Delta_v(j)-Delta_v(j+1) +log[sin((v+1)theta)/sin((v-1)theta)]>=0. For the last step clear its positive denominators and use EXACTLY sin((v+j)theta)sin((j+1)theta)sin((v+1)theta) -sin(j theta)sin((v+j+1)theta)sin((v-1)theta) =sin(theta)[cos(theta)-cos(v theta)cos((v+2j+1)theta)]>=0. The final inequality uses 1<=v<=D. This proves the drift inequality; at j=0 it is immediate. The lower bound in (9) uses sin(u theta)>=sin(theta)>=2/N and denominators at most 1. For t>=1 let B_t be the t by t tridiagonal matrix with diagonal c_h+a_j+b_j, upper diagonal -a_j and lower diagonal -b_j. Its characteristic roots are EXACTLY those of R_t, by (7), R_0=1, and the nonzero leading coefficients. It is diagonally similar to a real symmetric matrix, since a_j b_(j+1)>0. Put M_t=B_t-c_h I. The maximum principle with a Dirichlet boundary at t and reflection at 0 proves M_t^-1 is entrywise nonnegative. To bound its row sums, solve M_t u=1, u_t=0, and set d_j=u_j-u_(j+1). Then a_j d_j-b_j d_(j-1)=1, 0<d_j<=(j+1)/a_min, ||M_t^-1||_infinity=max_j u_j <=t(t+1)/(2a_min)<=N^6/64. (10) The real eigenvalues of M_t are positive (also by the same maximum principle), so every zero rho of R_t satisfies rho>=c_h+64/N^6. (11) This proof does not need the stronger observed but unproved claim that all these zeros exceed 2. Every supported folded e has lambda_e=c_e<=c_h. Factoring R_t over its real roots and using (11) now proves, for each fixed r, |R_t^(r)(lambda_e)|/R_t(lambda_e) <=(N^7/64)^r. (12) The same argument bounds fixed derivatives of 1/R_t by a polynomial times 1/R_t(lambda_e). This is a root SPECTRAL statement, not an assertion about the coefficients of the disappearing generic tail. ## 4. Convert spectral control to the actual first partner normal The proved full-source formula is S=S0(E)(V_n/C_n)G_n(E). The factor V_n/C_n is independent of E and is kept generically. Write K_e=J_e G_n(lambda_e;zeta)^2, R_J=J_e*/J_e =[product_F D_F(e*)/product_F D_F(e)] [S0(e*)/S0(e)]^2, (13) where D_F=(-1)^(F-D)[N]Delta_F^2 is analytic and nonzero at q. The total face sign is even. All numerator [N] zeros in (13) cancel before evaluation; every remaining factor is a root unit. The exact root value symmetry, or its elementary factorial reflection s_(D-r)=N/s_r, gives R_J(q)=1. Each fixed logarithmic derivative of R_J is polynomially bounded uniformly in the labels: it is a quotient of O(N) unit quantum-integer factors with index O(N). In particular |dot R_J(q)|<=C N^3. Set z_e=zeta^(2e+1), z_e*=zeta^(2N)/z_e. Because G_n is symmetric in its spectral argument, its partner evaluation is EXACTLY G_n(zeta^(-2N)z_e;zeta). The two spectral coordinates satisfy lambda_e*-lambda_e =(zeta^(2N)-1)(zeta^(2N)-z_e^2)/(zeta^(2N)z_e), |dot lambda_e*-dot lambda_e|<=4N. (14) At q they coincide. Differentiating the FULL generic polynomial only ONCE therefore cancels its common coefficient normal and gives the exact identity (dot K_e*-dot K_e)/W_N^2 =dot R_J+2(dot lambda_e*-dot lambda_e) R_t'(lambda_e)/R_t(lambda_e). (15) Equation (15) differentiates the full source identity (13), rather than its value alone. In THIS one-edge case its [2N] tail is empty by (3a); thus (15) must not be presented as a new bound for a nonzero T. Equation (12), the root-unit derivative bound in (13), and the uniform folded-germ bound from the common-phase theorem imply (3). At SECOND order the common coefficient derivative no longer cancels: mixed spectral/generic-q derivatives of G_n appear. Its generic degree is n, whereas its root degree is t, and the vanished k>t coefficients can contribute to precisely these mixed derivatives. Consequently (12) ALONE cannot be iterated to higher generic-q jets. The already proved tail-free criterion still handles every fixed order in the one-edge case, by its separate positive-core proof. Neither argument yet bounds a nonempty [2N] tail or the relevant mixed coefficient/spectral derivatives after external partners. ## 5. An exact central normal check by a finite product derivative For odd N=2m+1 and a=b=c=d=f=m, R_m is the actual turned Steinberg projector h_N. Its endpoint c_0 obeys h_N(c_0)=1 and h_N'(c_0)=-[2sin(theta)]^-1 sum_(u=1)^m cot(u theta). (16) This is an exact identity, not a fitted asymptotic. To prove it, specialize the OWN [balanced Sears identity](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) by canceling its parameter c=d. The transformed sum has an upper parameter 1 and only its k=0 term survives, giving the finite product sum_(k=0)^m (Q^-m,Q^-m,A;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q,AQ^-2m;Q)_k =(Q^(m+1),Q/A;Q)_m/(Q,Q^(m+1)/A;Q)_m. (17) At Q^N=1, Q^-2m=Q and (A)_k/(AQ)_k=(1-A)/(1-AQ^k). Differentiate (17) at A=1. Pairing u with N-u on its right gives sum_(k=1)^m (Q^-m;Q)_k^2 Q^k /[F_k^2(1-Q^k)] =-i sum_(u=1)^m cot(u theta). Differentiating the finite Newton expression (6) at c_0 gives (16), with its factor -i/[2sin(theta)]. In particular |h_N'(c_0)|<=C N^2(1+log N), consistent with the general polynomial bound. This identity tests a genuine normal direction and does not replace the source germ by its value. Audit: [degree recurrence, positive drift, spectral derivatives and exact first normals](../experiments/audit_actual_partner_normal_transport.py). The finite tests supplement the recurrence, drift and generic source proofs above. They do not certify transport for a nonempty [2N] tail or an all-partner higher-jet theorem. The one-flip case has an empty tail. The nonempty-tail boundary remains unestimated. The theorem is restricted to the tail-free case; it does not extend to the nonempty [2N] current.

title: An explicit coherent Gram for an actual split source
text: # An explicit coherent Gram for an actual split source 29 October 2026. The finite q-Pascal matrix gives an explicit, invertible, source-independent local packet transform. Pulling back a positive factorial metric produces a full-rank NON-DIAGONAL Gram. For the original figure-eight four-plat split packet its co-source norm is exactly `sqrt(N)` and its positive energy has the sharp volume exponent. No unknown knot value defines the transform or its metric. This is a constructive instance of the proposed special-inner-product Cauchy inequality. It does not yet transport the three-braid complete clock decomposition to this split packet or provide a sharp energy estimate for arbitrary knots. Those distinctions matter after the [complete clock-sector obstruction](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md). ## 1. A local all-exterior Pochhammer packet identity Let `Q` be a primitive Nth root, `N>=2`, `d=N-1`, and let `Y,u` be arbitrary nonzero variables. Write `F_n=(Q;Q)_n`. For `0<=k<=n<N` define the actual split-route tensor T_(n,k)(Y)=Y^(2k-n) [n choose k]_Q (Q/Y;Q)_k (YQ^(-n);Q)_(n-k). (1) These are precisely the surviving finite routes `a=n-k` of the [original four-plat proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md#4-forced-transfer-elimination-and-its-whole-scalar). That proof derives them from the original E/F entries, unrolled dual colors, full Cartan scalar, actual turns and the specified `g E_00` cut coupon. In particular (1) has no unspecified peripheral scalar. Set C_n(Y)=(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+1)/2)(Q/Y;Q)_n, v_k(Y,u)=(-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)(uYQ)^k, P_(n,k)=[n choose k]_Q if k<=n, and 0 otherwise. Then the following is an ENTRYWISE identity of whole Laurent polynomials, retaining the complete internal-clock fugacity: u^k T_(n,k)(Y)=C_n(Y) P_(n,k) v_k(Y,u). (2) Proof. Reverse the `n-k` consecutive Pochhammer factors in (1): (YQ^(-n);Q)_(n-k) =(-Y)^(n-k)Q^[-(n(n+1)-k(k+1))/2] (Q^(k+1)/Y;Q)_(n-k). Their product with `(Q/Y;Q)_k` is `(Q/Y;Q)_n`. The remaining monomial is exactly the one in (2). No division by `(Q/Y;Q)_n` is used; its zero fibers and all meridian jets are retained. Consequently the whole k-fiber is sum_(k=0)^n u^k T_(n,k)(Y) =C_n(Y)(uYQ;Q)_n. (3) The finite q-binomial theorem proving (3) follows by inserting the last factor, using q-Pascal. All Gaussian factorial indices are below N, so even levels and composite levels cause no exception. The exterior scope is precise. The `n` boundary port, `Y`, and all other exterior variables remain open. An ARBITRARY polynomial or matrix-valued exterior `E_n(Y,u,Z)` may be paired with (3). More generally (2) is a tensor factorization and preserves arbitrary external arrays on BOTH the n and k ports when those ports are retained. If an exterior depends on k, it stays attached to that port; it cannot be deleted while using (3) with input v. This is the ordinary typed local-contraction rule, not an assumed independence of the physical underclock feedback. The variable u records a literal internal-transfer fugacity. It does not assert that the clocks or spectator arguments of an arbitrary original knot are independent. Equation (2), rather than the special value `u=1`, is the reusable bridge packet identity. Here Y and u are central coefficient variables. Substituting noncommuting boundary operators would require its actual ordered intertwiner; the commutative identity does not authorize that step. ## 2. The universal Pascal transform and its inverse The matrix P is N by N, triangular with unit diagonal, and depends only on Q. Its explicit inverse is (P^(-1))_(n,k)=(-1)^(n-k) Q^((n-k)(n-k-1)/2) [n choose k]_Q, k<=n. (4) Indeed `[n choose j][j choose k]=[n choose k][n-k choose j-k]`; the convolution in a product with (4) is `(1;Q)_(n-k)`, hence zero unless `n=k`. This proves the inverse without a root-zero denominator. Thus the packet move is not contraction to the unknown K_N and not replacement by a rank-one co-source. It retains N independent boundary channels. For any adjoining tensor A, changing packet coordinates `f -> Pf` changes that tensor to `A P^(-1)`; their contraction is exactly unchanged. This proves source-independent composition at arbitrary width wherever the stated packet occurs. It makes no claim that the transported tensor has small norm for arbitrary A. Both P and its inverse have explicit finite coefficients. The map may be exponentially conditioned; that conditioning is part of the coherent metric, not an omitted norm cost. ### 2.1 These Pascal matrices are actual current operators On an original balanced physical head write the lowering-generator convention as mathsfF|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, mathsfF|d>=0. Then `mathsfF^r[n,k]=F_n/F_k` for `n-k=r`. Consequently P=p_N(mathsfF), p_N(t)=sum_(r=0)^d t^r/F_r. (4a) Its inverse is the opposite finite Euler polynomial, reproducing (4). This is a literal original nilpotent-current realization, not an auxiliary matrix with only the same classical symbol. At completeness let `Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>` and `U_a=Q^[-a(a+1)/2]`. The actual unitary chirp obeys U Ecal U^(-1)=mathsfF^T, P^T=U p_N(Ecal) U^(-1). (4b) The same Pascal blocks occur in the ACTUAL two-head Borel fusion, including every total integer degree. For `0<=T<=2d` set `I_T={max(0,T-d),...,min(T,d)}`. Index the relative input by `(a,T-a)` and the physical output by `(u,T-u)`, with `a,u in I_T`. The proved physical fusion kernel is C_T[u,a]=x^(u-a) F_a F_(T-u)/(F_(a-u)F_(T-a)), u<=a, 0 otherwise. It factors EXACTLY as C_T=D_out,T (P|I_T)^T D_in,T, D_out,T[u]=x^u F_u F_(T-u), D_in,T[a]=x^(-a)/F_(T-a). (4c) All indices of these factorials lie in `0,...,d`. The principal interval `P|I_T` has the same explicit inverse (4) restricted to that interval: every intermediate convolution index stays in it. There is no omitted high-total-degree wrap, including `T>=N`. This follows directly by writing `F_a/(F_(a-u))=[a choose u]_Q F_u` in the actual fusion formula. Thus (4c) supplies a typed current/physical embedding of the Pascal move on arbitrary neighboring heads. Its diagonal factors are compulsory. Nothing here silently identifies an arbitrary fusion-relative clock with a physical head or with a chosen total Ward current. On the actual dual pair with total degree d this also checks the original turns explicitly. In physical pair coordinates `(u,d-u)`, write the original cup, ordinary cap and degree-d marked row as p_u=N x^(u-d), ell_u=x^(-u)Q^(-u)/N, m_u=x^(d-u)/N^2. Then the SAME fusion block obeys C_d e_d=p, ell C_d=e_0^T/N, (m C_d)_a=x^(d-a) s_a^2/N^2. (4e) The first is the a=d column of (4c). For the second, root reflection reduces its a-th entry to `(1;Q)_a`; the marked row instead gives `(Q;Q)_a`. Thus (4e) retains the full marked density, which is NOT a corner row on arbitrary tensors. Its familiar further corner reduction requires the actual invariant exterior Ward relation. This note does not make that reduction for an arbitrary packet. Finally `H=N G_0^2`, where `G_0=diag(s_a/sqrt(N))=L^(1/2)` is the source-fixing physical factorial gauge. Hence (7) below is exactly `G=N P^*G_0^2P`. If an actual current J commutes with the nilpotent generator C and `S=p_N(C)`, then for ANY positive H_0, ||J||_(S^*H_0S)=||S J S^(-1)||_(H_0)=||J||_(H_0). (4d) This is the useful current-compatible Gram mechanism. Applying it to a total two-head current requires the actual typed module identification and the commutation relation; (4a)--(4c) exhibit the relevant possibilities, but do not assert that every clock in a knot is simultaneously that same current. ## 3. The actual figure-eight Gram and controlled co-source Now take the principal `Q=exp(2pi*i/N)`, put `s_n=|F_n|`, and set `Y=u=1`. Define `v_k=(-1)^k Q^(k(k+1)/2)`. Equation (3) says Pv=F=(F_0,...,F_d)^T, C_n(1)=conj(F_n). (5) The second equality is the exact identity `conj(F_n)=(-1)^nQ^(-n(n+1)/2)F_n`. The original whole-source calculation therefore gives, with its actual zero framing and all Cartan/turn factors already accounted for, K_(4_1),N=C(1)^T P v=F^*F=sum_n s_n^2. (6) This normalization comes from the literal original four-plat source, not from fitting (6) to a known value. Any separately attached original modified-dimension germ multiplies both sides unchanged. Let `H=diag(s_0^2,...,s_d^2)` and define the coherent packet metric G=P^* H P, G_(k,l)=sum_(n>=max(k,l)) s_n^2 conj([n choose k]_Q)[n choose l]_Q. (7) G is explicit and positive definite because every s_n is nonzero and P is invertible. It has rank N, including the n=0 channel. Its off-diagonal terms retain the q-binomial phases. In particular it is not the diagonal absolute value of P. The Riesz vector of the original linear co-source `C^T P` is `a=P^*F`. Its squared dual norm in (7) is EXACTLY a^*G^(-1)a=F^*H^(-1)F=N. (8) The actual packet energy is likewise explicit: ||v||_G^2=(Pv)^*H(Pv)=sum_(n=0)^d s_n^4. (9) Cauchy--Schwarz in this coherent, full-rank inner product proves the original-source bound |K_(4_1),N|^2<=N sum_(n=0)^d s_n^4. (10) This is useful precisely because the co-source norm (8) is polynomial while the state energy (9) retains the cancellation in each Pascal fiber. It is not a norm estimate for every possible packet input. ## 4. Exact compatibility with the b-length frame, including length zero Use the [actual length normalization](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) D_n=A_n^2=s_n^(1/2)/N^(1/4), b_n=B_n/D_n. The row n of the coefficient tensor of b_n is the corresponding Pascal row divided by D_n, with its original monomial phases. Thus in that typed row frame the exact packet factorization is P_b=D^(-1)P, C_b=D C, C_b^T P_b v=C^T P v. (11) Transport the positive row metric as well: H_b=D^2 H, P_b^*H_bP_b=G. (12) The squared source dual norm remains N, and the energy remains `sum s_n^4`. These are identities, not an asymptotic cancellation. In particular `D_0=N^(-1/4)`, `b_0=N^(1/4)`; the row-zero factor in `P_b` and its inverse factor in `C_b` are compulsory. Omitting zero-length slots changes the original source. Other length registers of an exterior are retained with their own inverse frames, exactly as in the length-normalized star theorem. Equation (11) normalizes the EXPOSED length n row and does not identify its coefficient index k with a physical-head length. ## 5. The positive energy has the sharp exponent For `J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi x))dx`, the elementary uniform factorial estimate gives log s_n=N J(n/N)+O(log N), uniformly 0<=n<N. J has its unique global maximum at `t=5/6`, and `4pi J(5/6)=4Lambda(pi/6)=Vol(4_1)`. Bounding the N-term positive sum by its maximum and using a nearest integer to `5N/6` gives log(sum_n s_n^4)=N Vol(4_1)/pi+O(log N). (13) Thus (10) has exactly the desired sharp upper exponent. The positive sum (6) separately gives the matching lower exponent. This recovers the verified figure-eight benchmark by a genuine coherent Gram, rather than by flattening its original overclock sectors. The Gram here acts on the explicitly exposed split-transfer packet. The much larger COMPLETE sectors in the three-braid clock state are different coordinates, after different contractions. Equality of their final scalar with (6) does NOT by itself provide an invertible packet map between them. No diagonal-clock obstruction is evaded by silently identifying those two spaces. ## 6. Exact composable updates and the remaining general question If a specified invertible packet operator S acts before the packet, the energy and Riesz vector on its INPUT coordinates update as G -> G_S=S^* G S, a -> a_S=S^*a, a_S^*G_S^(-1)a_S=a^*G^(-1)a. (14) For a Gaussian clock chirp `U_ell=diag(Q^(ell*k(k+1)/2))`, this is unitary congruence: its phases and the spectrum of G are retained. For a pure coordinate change `v'=Sv`, rather than an inserted operator, the unchanged pairing instead uses `G'=(S^(-1))^*G S^(-1)` and `a'=(S^(-1))^*a`. Likewise (4) permits exact Pascal/inverse-Pascal changes. These are actual local tensor-coordinate operations with arbitrary retained exteriors, not changes of the knot invariant. They do NOT imply that the same simple factorial diagonal H survives an arbitrary coherent word of such moves. A chirped input generally has energy `sum s_n^2 |(P U_ell v)_n|^2`, not `sum s_n^4`. The internal phase must be evaluated or controlled before its modulus is taken. A known actual example is the Rogers coefficient packet `J_n(t)=sum_k [n choose k]_t t^(k(k+1))`: it is exactly a Pascal transform of a unitary Gaussian input, as proved from the original [five-crossing whole source](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). Its remaining Newton evaluation is coherent; the [multichannel proof](actual_multichannel_newton_green_transport.md) already shows why a tame coefficient norm cannot simply be assumed. The proved general local move is (2)--(4), with exact Gram transport (11)--(14). A broad sharp theorem still requires (i) an actual source-preserving decomposition into these packet moves and (ii) a geometric bound on the resulting coherent energy, including all spectator feedback and dual metrics. Neither condition is inferred from the figure-eight benchmark alone. ### 6.1 An exact Pascal/Gaussian alphabet for original braid crossings For the original SAME-COLOR braid there is a further explicit local decomposition, at every integer total degree T. It resolves the crossing into known coherent packet moves rather than assuming such a decomposition. Use `C_T` from (4c), `I_T` as there, and define t_T[a]=x^(-a)/F_a, U_T[a',a]=x^(-(a'-a))/F_(a'-a) if a'>=a, else 0, D_T[a]=(-1)^(T-a) Q^((T-a)(T-a-1)/2) x^(-2(T-a)). Then EXACTLY U_T=t_T (P|I_T) t_T^(-1), R_(+,T)=kappa C_T D_T U_T C_T^(-1), R_(-,T)=kappa^(-1) C_T U_T^(-1)D_T^(-1)C_T^(-1). (15) Here kappa is the original common Cartan entry `R_(00,00)`, with its given meridian continuation. It has not been reset. At completeness `|x|=1`, both kappa and every D_T entry have modulus one. The other diagonals in (4c),(15) retain their explicit factorial magnitudes and root phases. The inverse of U_T is obtained from (4), so no unknown diagonalization enters. Proof with the strict physical support retained. In the actual flat Borel basis `f^a e_j`, `a,j<N`, the original crossing is right multiplication by the independently derived coefficient a_R=kappa sum_(r+k<N) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2) x^(-r-2k) f^r e_k/F_r. That formula follows by the actual triangular fusion inversion on `R(e_0 tensor e_j)=kappa x^(-j)e_j tensor e_0`; its finite Euler inverse is precisely (4a). For an input `f^a e_j` the r,k term has `j=k+r modulo N`, with output `f^(a+r)e_k` when `a+r<N`. Within the SAME total INTEGER degree `T=a+j`, one must have `j=k+r` as an integer, not `k+r-N`. Thus `a'=a+r`, `k=T-a'`, and its coefficient is exactly `kappa D_T[a']U_T[a',a]`. Conversely all the entries specified in (15) satisfy `r+k=j<N`, so none is extra. Conjugation by the actual C_T proves (15). In particular high blocks `T>=N` have been retained. No completed positive-N carry or source-null approximation is used in (15). Taking the direct sum over T gives the FULL original crossing as an operator identity, with its literal negative inverse. Therefore (4c),(15) can be inserted into an arbitrary signed braid of arbitrary width, with arbitrary adjoining tensors. All ordinary/marked turns, pivots, framing and peripheral factors stay original. The shared head indices enforce the actual overlap/feedback of neighboring total-degree registers; those T labels are not independent clocks. This is an explicit coherent alphabet of principal Pascal blocks, their inverses, known factorial diagonals and unitary Gaussians. For a repeated-generator block its C_T interfaces cancel exactly before any norm is taken. Neighboring generators generally have different overlapping degree registers and leave genuine recoupling. Their remaining positive energy is not estimated by (15) alone. The fusion/Euler formulas themselves were previously proved in [the actual Borel theorem](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) and [the original crossing coefficient theorem](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md). The use here is their exact integer-degree Pascal factorization, its explicit coherent metrics and its retained original co-source. It is not a claim that a generic R factorization is new, nor that known factorial weights already satisfy the global Rivin constraints. ## 7. The precise overlap compatibility problem There is a local sufficient metric condition for composing the alphabet without defining a metric from the unknown terminal word. Choose a family of positive packet metrics specified by LOCAL typed data (Q, meridians, retained integer degrees and length ports), before choosing the braid. It must include the explicit Pascal pullbacks above, the intended positive factorial/angle row energies, and the original turn co-sources with their controlled dual norms. For every elementary THREE-head reassociation, let A be its actual finite coordinate-change matrix. The required local compatibility is N^(-c) G_left <= A^* G_right A <= N^c G_left, (16) uniformly in all its admissible integer ports, for one fixed c. Every diagonal factor in (4c),(15), and every required source adapter, is included in A or in its explicitly assigned endpoint metric. This is a finite local matrix inequality; its data do not involve K_N or a terminal braid product. If (16) holds, a fixed sequence of L reassociations compares the state energies by `N^(cL)` and the transported source dual norms by the same factor. This follows by congruence and inversion of (16), then induction. Thus its Cauchy budget costs at most `N^(2cL)`. The estimate tensorizes with untouched exterior heads. A positive geometric angle-fiber factorization of the assigned row energies, with the actual integer edge and peripheral constraints, would then give the desired comparison to its partition function up to a polynomial. That last identification is an explicit requirement, not a consequence of (16) alone. Using exact pullbacks of ONE arbitrary physical metric makes tree coordinate changes isometric tautologically, but does not establish that the resulting dense Gram has the stated positive-angle energy. The problem is to obtain BOTH the controlled local energy model and the compatible overlaps, with the same retained source. It cannot be solved by defining G from the unknown completed word. ### The obvious fixed factorial tensor metric fails (16) This failure can be proved on the ACTUAL fusion reassociation, after removing its trivial column factorial. Put C'=C diag_(a,k)(F_a^(-1)), A=(I tensor C')^(-1)(C' tensor I) on three heads. (17) This is the genuine change from the first-pair divided-power fusion coordinates to the second-pair coordinates. All its original turns are transported by the same matrices; the assertion is a local all-exterior norm test, not a knot scalar estimate. At total pair degree d, (4c) and reflection give C'_d=V (P^T) V^(-1), V_a=x^a(-1)^aQ^(a(a+1)/2), |V_a|=1. (18) An input `|0,u,d-u>` is fixed by the first-pair C', because its first relative divided-power index is zero. Hence |<0,a,d-a| A |0,u,d-u>|=|[u choose a]_Q|, 0<=a<=u<=d. (19) Now use ANY fixed positive diagonal tensor metric whose last two head weights have constant complementary product `h_2(a)h_3(d-a)=constant`. In particular every fixed physical factorial metric `(L^t)^(tensor 3)` has this property. The input and output basis vectors in (19) have equal metric norm. Therefore its induced operator norm satisfies ||A|| >= |[u choose a]_Q|. (20) For `N=3k+1`, `u=2k`, `a=k`, the uniform factorial estimate gives lim (1/N)log|[2k choose k]_Q|=v_3/pi>0. (21) Thus (16) with the SAME fixed factorial tensor metric on both coordinate systems is false, even after the column factorial has been removed and even before any unknown braid is present. Its complementary source property does not imply tame reassociation. This does not rule out the coherent family sought in (16), an angle-weighted recoupling rather than a tame one, or a source-specific smaller invariant packet. It pinpoints the next required estimate: the overlap of the actual Pascal packets needs its OWN coherent Gram/angle factorization. Flat or fixed diagonal factorial gluing cannot silently replace it. The interface is already an EXACT positive affine-angle weight: root complementation gives |[u choose a]_Q|=N w_N(a,u-a,d-u), a+(u-a)+(d-u)=d. (22) Thus its squared matrix coefficient is `N^2 w_N(a,u-a,d-u)^2`. The test (21) has the regular-angle triple `(k,k,k)`; its exponential cost is genuine tetrahedral angle energy to be allocated and glued, not an unexplained norm loss. A coherent global comparison may retain these weights or change their Gram placement. It must prove their actual incidence and dual/source compensation rather than omit them. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pascal_coherent_gram.py): original mixed E/F four-plat contractions, arbitrary Y/u local packets and exterior insertions, exact Pascal inverses, full positive Gram/source normalization, b_0, the sharp positive-energy rate, and both original signed crossings in every total-degree block with full pivotal words. The final tests also check the actual three-head reassociation and its fixed-factorial metric obstruction (19)--(21).

title: Actual peripheral action, fusion poles, and the normal boundary lattice
text: # Actual peripheral action, fusion poles, and the normal boundary lattice Research note, 26 October 2026. This reconstructs a peripheral-module comparison directly from the literature ADO matrices. The two elementary boundary curves act by specified difference operators, and the fusion pole at the complete meridian has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue. The proof is uniform in the knot and in every level N>=2. It does not identify the actual quantum period with a geometric gluing period or prove its exponential norm. The [positive ideal triangulation](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md) supplies the marked geometric Bloch class. The [crossing/action comparison](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) already identifies the classical action of the actual state with that class. The present calculation specifies additional *quantum boundary data* that a period comparison must preserve, including its singular specialization at M=1. ## 1. Fixed colors, parameter, and duality Use exactly the conventions of [the ADO definition audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md): q=exp(pi*i/N), D=q-q^(-1), x=q^alpha, M=-qx, [z]=(q^z-q^(-z))/D, T h(M)=h(qM). On V_alpha, with 0<=j<N, E v_j=[j][alpha-j+1]v_(j-1), F v_j=v_(j+1), K v_j=xq^(-2j)v_j, H v_j=(alpha-2j)v_j, Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Let W be the two-dimensional highest-weight-one color, with basis w_0,w_1. Its E,F entries are one and its K eigenvalues are q,q^(-1). The actual pivot and twist on W are g_W=K_W^(1-N)=diag(-q,-q^(-1)), theta_W=q^(3/2-N)=-q^(3/2). (1.1) A right partial trace over W uses g_W; a left partial trace over the first factor W uses g_W^(-1). Interchanging these is an actual error: it changes the fusion weights derived below. For completeness, choose A=q^(1/2)=exp(pi*i/(2N)), with that root retained. An invariant cup and cap on W are b(1)=w_0 tensor w_1-q^(-1)w_1 tensor w_0, d(w_0 tensor w_1)=-q, d(w_1 tensor w_0)=1, d(w_0 tensor w_0)=d(w_1 tensor w_1)=0. Direct contraction gives both zigzags equal to identity and db=-q-q^(-1). For e=bd, the actual fundamental crossing satisfies checkR_WW=A*I+A^(-1)*e, e^2=-(q+q^(-1))*e. (1.2) Indeed its only nontrivial two-by-two block, in order 01,10, is q^(-1/2)[[0,1],[1,D]], while e has block [[-q,1],[1,-q^(-1)]]. Closing (1.2) gives the twist in (1.1). Thus a link colored by W obeys the framed Kauffman bracket relations in this root convention. This is checked from the matrices, not imported as a skein-comparison theorem. It remains valid at N=2, when the loop value is zero. ## 2. An explicit fusion basis and its exact degeneracy For generic alpha, define in W tensor V_alpha h_+=w_0 tensor v_0, h_-=[alpha]w_1 tensor v_0-x w_0 tensor v_1. The coproduct kills both by E. Their H weights are alpha+1 and alpha-1. Iteration of the displayed Delta F gives, with v_N=0, F^j h_+=q^(-j)w_0 tensor v_j+[j]w_1 tensor v_(j-1), F^j h_-=-xq^(-j)w_0 tensor v_(j+1) +[alpha-j]w_1 tensor v_j. (2.1) Both chains have length N: the next terms vanish by [N]=0 and v_N=0. The commutator [E,F]=(K-K^(-1))/D now gives on a chain of highest weight beta exactly E F^j h=[j][beta-j+1]F^(j-1)h. This can also be verified directly in (2.1). The two chains are therefore the specified colors V_(alpha+1) and V_(alpha-1). Set delta=[alpha+1]=-(M-M^(-1))/D. (2.2) In each intermediate weight space, in the basis w_0 v_r,w_1 v_(r-1), the two columns of (2.1) are (q^(-r),[r])^t, (-xq^(1-r),[alpha-r+1])^t. Their determinant is exactly delta. The top weight is one-dimensional; the last coefficient is [alpha-N+1]=-delta. Hence the whole fusion change of basis has determinant +/-delta^N, with the sign depending only on the ordering of columns and weight spaces. Consequently W tensor V_alpha = V_(alpha+1) direct-sum V_(alpha-1) if delta!=0. (2.3) This is a direct basis proof, including composite and even levels. It identifies the precise divisor where the splitting fails. ### Casimir projectors, with their poles retained The Casimir in these conventions is C=FE+(qK+q^(-1)K^(-1))/D^2. The generator relations show that it commutes with E,F,K,H. On a highest-weight beta color it has value c_beta=(q^(beta+1)+q^(-beta-1))/D^2. On W tensor V_alpha put c_-=(x+x^(-1))/D^2, c_+=(q^2*x+q^(-2)*x^(-1))/D^2, A_alpha=C_total-c_-*I. Then c_+-c_-=delta, and (2.3) gives A_alpha^2=delta*A_alpha, P_+=A_alpha/delta, P_-=I-P_+. (2.4) These are the actual projectors at delta!=0. Equation (2.4), after clearing delta, is a Laurent identity, so its first equation also holds on the divisor. No projector is evaluated separately there. ## 3. The two elementary boundary curves act on the actual period Let F_N^L(M) be the reduced cut evaluation of a zero-framed knot colored V_alpha, with any fixed framed W-colored link L in its complement. In particular F_N^empty=F_N is the already specified knot period. This construction also makes sense for linear combinations of such links. Write lambda for adding a W-colored, zero-framed preferred parallel of the knot and mu for adding a positive W meridian. The exact formulas are F_N^(lambda L)(M) =-f(qM)/f(M)*F_N^L(qM) -f(q^(-1)M)/f(M)*F_N^L(q^(-1)M), F_N^(mu L)(M)=(M+M^(-1))*F_N^L(M), f(M)=M-M^(-1). (3.1) These are identities of whole meromorphic germs; apparent poles in the first line cancel when the actual finite evaluation is regular. ### Proof of the longitude weights Coloring the knot by W tensor V_alpha is the framed parallel construction by the following finite-product check. Write R=D_Cartan*sum_(k=0)^(N-1)c_k E^k tensor F^k, with c_k=q^(k(k-1)/2)*D^k/[k]!. The two summands of Delta E q^2-commute. Their ordered q-binomial coefficients give c_(i+j)*binomial_(q^(-2))(i+j,i)=c_i*c_j, which follows at once by writing [k]!=q^(k(k-1)/2)*(q^(-2);q^(-2))_k/(1-q^(-2))^k. Moving the Cartan factors past E and F then gives, term by term, (Delta tensor id)R=R_13 R_23, (id tensor Delta)R=R_13 R_12. Only i+j<N contributes, because the remaining E^N or F^N is zero; all factorial denominators used here are nonzero. The common Cartan scalars agree by additivity of the highest weights. Tensor-product cups, caps and pivots contract directly. This proves the required local parallel replacement, retaining its framing. It retains the preferred zero framing; its twist is the twist of the tensor color, not a scalar twist chosen for one summand. Naturality with the two explicit submodule inclusions in (2.3) gives its cut map Z_alpha^L=F_N^L(qM)P_++F_N^L(q^(-1)M)P_-. (3.2) For generic alpha each summand is simple; its cut endomorphism is therefore its scalar by the same quantum-group intertwining argument as for the original ADO cut. Possible exceptional colors are handled after clearing the explicit denominators. Taking the left pivotal partial trace over the first W gives the weights. On the highest vector v_0, P_+ has coefficient one in w_0 v_0 and x/delta in w_1 v_0, by the two-column inverse above. Consequently, with g_W^(-1)=diag(-q^(-1),-q), ptr_W^left(P_+)=-q^(-1)-qx/delta =-[alpha+2]/[alpha+1], ptr_W^left(P_-)=-[alpha]/[alpha+1]. (3.3) The partial trace is an intertwiner of a generic simple V_alpha, so this highest diagonal entry is its scalar on the whole module. Substituting x=-M/q in (3.3) gives the first line of (3.1). There is no assumed modified-trace additivity theorem in this proof. The full modified dimension d_N(M)=eta_N*f(M)/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=i^(N+3) has exactly these ratios: d_N(q^(+/-1)M)/d_N(M)=-f(q^(+/-1)M)/f(M). (3.4) Here q^N=-1 changes the sign of the denominator; it is essential. Thus for the full period N_N^L=d_N F_N^L, equations (3.1) become N_N^(lambda L)=(T+T^(-1))N_N^L, N_N^(mu L)=(M+M^(-1))N_N^L. (3.5) ### Proof of the marked meridian On V_alpha tensor W use the actual unstripped double crossing R_21 R and take the right trace over W. This is an intertwiner of V_alpha, so evaluate its highest diagonal entry. The two W weights contribute -q*x and -q^(-1)*x^(-1), respectively. Terms containing E kill the highest vector or change its index and cannot contribute to that diagonal entry. Hence the scalar is -(qx+q^(-1)x^(-1))=M+M^(-1). (3.6) This fixes the meridian sign in the marking M=-qx. At the trivial highest-weight color alpha=0, M=-q, it gives the actual fundamental loop -q-q^(-1). At completeness M=1 it gives +2. The preferred longitude and meridian signs must not be independently guessed from a trace convention at q=1. ### A direct route from peripheral relations to actual annihilators Let P be a finite linear combination of words in the two specified boundary curves. Suppose P acting on the empty link is zero in the Kauffman bracket skein module of the knot complement. Evaluate that relation using (1.2), with its coefficient square roots retained. Repeated use of (3.5), valid for every intermediate L, gives P(M+M^(-1),T+T^(-1)) N_N=0. (3.7) The order in each word is preserved. Rational coefficient poles allow only the usual finite exceptional set of levels. When the word coefficients lie in C(q), (3.7) belongs to the literature all-level ADO ideal. Coefficients in C(q^(1/2)) are kept over that explicit extension; no descent to C(q) is silently asserted. Thus peripheral skein relations yield actual knot-state annihilators by an independent local proof. No equality of the peripheral ideal with the full annihilator ideal, and no AJ specialization theorem, is inferred. Such an equality or a survival argument would still be needed to force its geometric classical component into a primitive minimal operator. ## 4. A regular boundary lattice and the exact normal functional Define w_N^L=f(M)F_N^L(M). Conjugating (3.1) gives regular Laurent boundary operators on this specified normal state: lambda_w=-(T+T^(-1)), mu_w=M+M^(-1). (4.1) The denominator f(M) in the reduced-state action is therefore a genuine change of boundary lattice with a divisor at M=1. It is not a numerical multiplier. The original reduced period is still recovered from that lattice and its normal derivative. For the empty link, the [actual Weyl theorem](actual_weyl_descent.md) makes F_N invariant under M->M^(-1), so w_N is odd. With u=Log M, w_N(1)=0, K_N=F_N(1)=(1/2)*d_u w_N|_(u=0). (4.2) This is the prescribed normal functional, not a choice of a new solution. Put Y=M^2, U=Y^N and v_N=(Y-1)F_N=M*w_N. Then lambda_v=-q^(-1)T-qT^(-1)=kappa*T+kappa^(-1)T^(-1), kappa=-q^(-1), kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1), K_N=N*partial_(U-1)v_N|_(U=1,M=1). (4.3) These agree with the independently derived full ADO character and [normal period](peripheral_normal_period.md). The full period has the regular whole-germ value eta_N*K_N/N at M=1. In particular, a peripheral word relation P as in (3.7) has a regular normal representative B_w=P(M+M^(-1),-(T+T^(-1))), B_w*w_N=0, (B_w*f(M))*F_N=0. (4.4) Thus the cleared reduced operator has its right boundary factor f(M) without assuming positive volume growth. Passing from w_N to v_N conjugates each T by q^(-1); the right factor becomes Y-1, with the unit M explicitly retained. If the word has even meridian parity and coefficients in C(q), its normal coefficients descend to C(q,Y) and this is exactly an integral operator B_v*(Y-1) of the preceding normal-period theory. It need not be the primitive minimal operator, and taking an additional left factor can introduce extra root-fiber kernels. Adding a fundamental meridian changes meridian parity. Thus mixed W-colored links are kept on the marked M cover; one must not assume their reduced evaluations are even in M just because the original knot period is. In the even meridional subalgebra, mu^2-2 becomes Y+Y^(-1). Formula (4.3) retains the half-root and the even-level longitude sign rather than passing to an unsigned 2N-th norm. ## 5. The complete fusion fiber has a nonzero square-zero residue At alpha=N-1 we have M=1 and delta=0. The matrix A_alpha in (2.4) is regular. Write A_0 for its value there. Each of its intermediate two-dimensional weight blocks is [[q^(-r)[r], -q^(-2r)], [[r]^2, -q^(-r)[r]]], 1<=r<N. (5.1) Each block has rank one and square zero; [r]!=0 in this range. The top and bottom weight blocks are zero. Consequently, uniformly, A_0^2=0, rank(A_0)=N-1, ptr_W^left(A_0)=I_(V_(N-1)). (5.2) The last equality also follows from delta*ptr(P_+)=-[alpha+2] in (3.3) and [N+1]=-1. It fixes the residue normalization exactly. The colliding Casimir eigenblocks have N-1 Jordan blocks of size two and two blocks of size one. In particular the generic split fusion cannot be specialized as a direct sum of scalar-Casimir blocks. No classification of projective modules is needed for this conclusion, nor is indecomposability of the whole tensor module asserted. There is also an exact knot-dependent coefficient of this nilpotent residue. The pointing and Weyl identities give F_N(q)=F_N(q^(-1))=1. Apply (3.2) as a whole germ, rewriting it as Z_alpha=F_N(q^(-1)M)*I +(F_N(qM)-F_N(q^(-1)M))/delta * A_alpha. The quotient has a removable singularity. Using (2.2) and the reflection identity to differentiate, its complete value is Z_0=I+tau_N*A_0, tau_N=-(q-q^(-1))*(M partial_M F_N)(q). (5.3) Closing the fundamental color gives F_N^(lambda)(1)=-(q+q^(-1))+tau_N. (5.4) This is a specified nilpotent extension coefficient in the actual state, computed without assuming a geometric contribution. It is not K_N itself: (4.2) evaluates a normal derivative at M=1, while (5.3) evaluates one at the adjacent ordinary color M=q. No equality of their exponential rates is asserted. For the unknot F_N=1, tau_N=0 even though the universal residue A_0 is nonzero. Thus the local extension's existence does not force its excitation by the selected knot period. ## 6. Where this meets the ideal triangulation theorem The ideal triangulation provides the positive representative beta_T with D(beta_T)=Vol and fixes the marked regulator norm. The [actual classical action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) already matches that regulator without an imaginary additive constant. The present calculation adds exact quantum peripheral operators, a regular normal boundary lattice, and its nonsemisimple specialization. These are specific data available for every knot. A geometric gluing construction can now be asked to match these operators and this normal functional, rather than merely a generic central equation. It must also carry the actual vacuum/source class. One concrete common object is the skein module of the knot complement: (1.2) and (3.5) give its actual ADO evaluation as a peripheral-module map. A proposed triangulation evaluation must intertwine the same boundary action, preserve the retained normal lattice, and send the same empty-link class to the selected period. An isomorphism of unpointed modules alone would not prove those evaluation maps agree. Equation (3.7) supplies one direction of peripheral-operator compatibility, not equality of modules. The nonzero geometric contribution of the selected normal period, and its norm (4/N)log|K_N| -> log||P_hyp||=2Vol/pi, remain unproved. Existence of a positive triangulation supplies the geometric representative; it does not identify or bound the knot-dependent extension coefficient or the selected inverse pairing. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre construction](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) now realizes the prescribed normal functional as an ordinary algebraic evaluation on a descended fibre. The ramification retains the first negative-sector coefficient; evaluating on the root orbit before descent would discard it. An explicit equivariant frame change shows that agreement on that ordinary root fibre is insufficient to fix the period. The marked ramified fibre is therefore additional comparison data; its regulator norm remains unproved. The subsequent [threaded-character proof](ado_threaded_shadow.md) extends the boundary calculation to arbitrary interior loops. Explicit integral Weyl exact sequences replace singular root-level projectors, and filtered auxiliary traces give the exact degree-N phases and degree-2N abelian even character. This supplies an interior central-data test for a geometric comparison and a separating-observable criterion for an actual source extension; it does not identify that extension or its regulator norm. ## 7. Coverage and independent verification Representation theory and projective colors of this unrolled quantum group are covered by Costantino--Geer--Patureau-Mirand, [Some remarks on the unrolled quantum group of sl(2)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0410). The torus skein/noncommutative-torus relationship is covered by Frohman--Gelca, [Skein Modules and the Noncommutative Torus](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9806107). The coverage check uses their abstracts and bibliographic scope; none of their representation, skein, or comparison proofs is a premise of the calculations above. No novelty is claimed for these general constructions. The relevant concrete results here are the normalization-matched formulas and their independently checked wall. Derivative-valued knot invariants from the radical of the restricted quantum-group center also have coverage in Murakami, [From colored Jones invariants to logarithmic invariants](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287). Its abstract is used for coverage only. No identity between tau_N and its named invariants, or any asymptotic theorem, is assumed. [audit_actual_peripheral_fusion.py](../experiments/audit_actual_peripheral_fusion.py) constructs the coproduct, Casimir, and actual R matrices independently of the displayed projectors. It checks 45 fusion/wall cases, 30 heterogeneous Hopf cases, and 15 fundamental skein/duality cases at 15 levels including even and composite levels through 24. Six additional tensor-color cases verify both parallel-crossing identities through level 8, including their common Cartan scalars. A separate 16 cabled-knot checks construct the actual R and twist of the full 2N-dimensional tensor color, rather than defining its knot map by fusion. They verify generic decomposition and the nilpotent derivative coefficient at the ideal color, at levels 2,3,4,5 for two signed two-strand braids. Results are in [actual_peripheral_fusion_results.json](../experiments/actual_peripheral_fusion_results.json). The finite diagnostics support the uniform proofs; they establish no asymptotic statement.

title: A nonzero outward action gradient at every physical state face
text: # A nonzero outward action gradient at every physical state face 28 October 2026. In the original one-component scalar source, adjacent head factorials can be combined before estimating a boundary. Their exponents are even, whereas every independent transfer has exponent minus one. This elementary parity forces a nonzero radial logarithmic coefficient at EVERY proper physical face. Each face admits an outward direction lowering the complete marked action. Individual factors need not go to their separate preferred sides. The statement is uniform over the finitely many faces of any fixed NONEMPTY braid word with one-component closure, at arbitrary width. The empty one-strand unknot has constant density and is excluded. It is not yet a deformation of the whole original cycle or a sharp bound for its scalar. In particular, local changes of integer cotangent charts have their own side currents. ## 1. The exact gathered factorial source Use the original averaged cut before splitting the state, as justified in [the scalar completion](actual_scalar_cardinal_source_completion.md). Follow the one physical component once, listing its 2m crossing visits. Visit i has transfer k_(j(i)) and increment eta_i k_(j(i)), eta_i=+/-1. Each crossing appears twice, with opposite increments. Thus h_0=t, h_(i+1)=h_i+eta_i k_(j(i)), h_(2m)=t. (1) The variables (t,k_1,...,k_m) are independent integer coordinates. Every arc form h_i has coefficient one on t. Its other coefficients are 0,+1,-1. The physical source is exactly 0<=t,k_j<=d, 0<=h_i(t,k)<=d, d=N-1. (2) The original signed coefficients at one visit contribute a factorial exponent -eta_i at its input and +eta_i at its output. This is true for both crossing signs after the EXACT conversion Fhat_-(s)=exp[i*pi*s-i*pi*s*(s+1)/N] Fhat_+(s). (3) Equation (3) follows from the common real Gamma product, not just from equality at integer s. Its quadratic factor is retained. Therefore the full scalar has gathered factorial part product_i Fhat_+(h_i)^(c_i) / product_j Fhat_+(k_j), c_i=eta_(i-1)-eta_i in {-2,0,2}. (4) All cyclic indices in c_i refer to the physical component. Coincident arc forms may be kept as separate occurrences; their exponents add. Every original Cartan, pivotal and framing scalar and the chirps (3) remain outside (4). The combined quadratic factor has unit modulus on real indices, but is not discarded on complex contours. ## 2. Integral face coordinates and vertices Scale (2) by d and call the resulting polytope P in R^(m+1). It has strict interior: t=1/2 and all k_j sufficiently small and positive put every h_i strictly between zero and one. Its defining integer matrix is totally unimodular. Here is a direct proof. In traversal order, each transfer column of the arc matrix is +1 or -1 on ONE contiguous interval between its two visits and zero elsewhere. The t column is all ones. Negate negative columns. For any square minor, selected arc rows retain this interval property. Successive row differences turn each column into at most one +1 and one -1. This row operation has determinant one. Such a square matrix has determinant 0,+1,-1: expand a column with at most one nonzero; if none exists, all column sums vanish and the determinant is zero. Adjoining unit transfer rows preserves the assertion by expansion along those rows. Upper inequalities only negate rows; duplicate opposite rows give zero minors. This proves the claim for (2). At a vertex, m+1 independent active rows consequently have determinant +/-1. Their right sides are integers, so the vertex is integral. Since t,k_j are all in [0,1], EVERY vertex lies in {0,1}^(m+1). All its physical arc forms are also zero or one. Any r independent active rows at a face have a nonzero r-by-r minor of determinant +/-1. Adjoin the complementary original coordinate rows to obtain an affine GL_(m+1)(Z) chart. Its r normal coordinates are actual physical indices h, k, d-h or d-k. There is no fractional lattice, root-grid multiplicity or unrecorded counting Jacobian. At a nonsimple face the other active inequalities remain explicit. ### A finite unimodular simplex atlas of the physical polytope Every physical facet has lattice width ONE on P. Its primitive defining form takes only the values zero and one on the vertices, by the preceding binary-vertex result. Every face inherits the same property: a facet of a face is cut out by one of the original physical inequalities, and its defining form takes both values on that face's vertices. Their integer difference evaluates to one, so the restricted form is primitive on the face lattice as well. Fix an order on the finitely many vertices and form the pulling triangulation. Inductively triangulate all opposite facets of a chosen vertex, using the same order on every shared face, and cone their simplexes to that vertex. This covers the polytope with disjoint relative interiors and compatible intersections. The assertion is elementary by following each ray from the chosen vertex to its first opposite boundary face. All resulting simplexes are unimodular. Dimension zero is the base. At the inductive step the chosen vertex has primitive lattice height one over the opposite facet. Appending its edge to a determinant-one facet basis therefore gives determinant +/-1 in the face lattice. Thus P has a finite unimodular triangulation depending only on the fixed word. No imported triangulation theorem or N-dependent refinement is needed for this statement. For the ACTUAL source polytope dP, each cell is consequently u=d v_0+B n, n in d*Delta, B in GL_(m+1)(Z), where Delta is the standard simplex and B is independent of N. The cell d*Delta itself has N-dependent size; it is not asserted to have lattice volume one. Its change of source coordinates has counting Jacobian one. Shared cell faces must be assigned once by a fixed half-open convention if their finite lattice sums are split. This finite real simplex atlas supplies controlled integral charts. It does not identify or glue their COMPLEX cotangent residue cycles. ## 3. The radial logarithmic coefficient never vanishes Let F be a nonempty proper face of P. Let H(F) list its active head occurrences h_i=0 or1, and J(F) its active transfers k_j=0 or1. The row vector governing the radial logarithmic term is q_F=sum_(i in H(F)) c_i grad h_i -sum_(j in J(F)) grad k_j. (5) The SAME sign applies at the lower and upper endpoint. Indeed, for I(s)=integral_0^s log|2sin(pi u)| du, either real endpoint a=0,1 satisfies I(a+delta v)-I(a)=delta v log delta+O_v(delta) (6) on a continuously marked side. At the upper endpoint this also follows from I(1-s)=-I(s). Full-function branch changes add recorded integer linear terms; along a real normal displacement they do not change the real logarithmic coefficient. If J(F) is nonempty, choose j in it. Every head contribution to the k_j coefficient of (5) is even, while its own transfer contributes -1 and other transfers contribute zero. That coefficient is ODD. Hence q_F!=0, regardless of simultaneous head collisions. If J(F) is empty, all transfers are positive and below one on the relative interior of F. A head h_i=0 must be a strict local minimum along the component: its preceding increment is negative and its following increment is positive. Otherwise a neighboring head would be negative. Thus c_i=-2. Similarly a head h_i=1 is a strict local maximum, so c_i=+2. Writing a_f for the active INWARD inequalities h_i>=0 or 1-h_i>=0, we obtain q_F=-2 sum_f grad a_f. (7) This cannot vanish. At a real relative-interior point x of F, all a_f(x)=0; at a strict interior point x_* all a_f(x_*)>0. If their gradient sum vanished, their sum would be constant and these two values would coincide, a contradiction. This completes the proof for EVERY proper face. ## 4. An outward direction with strict action decrease For every F there is a fixed integer vector v_F and an active inward inequality a_g such that a_g'(v_F)<0, q_F(v_F)>0, a_f'(v_F)!=0 for every active a_f. (8) For a facet the verification is explicit. A transfer k_j=0 facet has q_F=-grad k_j. A k_j=1 constraint cannot be a facet: its crossing forces physical head endpoints as independent equalities. A head endpoint facet has q_F a negative positive-integer multiple of its inward normal, by the local-minimum/maximum argument above. Choose v outward, then perturb within its open halfspace if needed. For codimension at least two, active inward normals span a space of dimension at least two. Since q_F!=0, at least one normal a_g' is not a positive multiple of q_F. There is then a real vector v with a_g'(v)<0 and q_F(v)>0: these two strict halfspaces are incompatible only for positive proportional normals. Avoid the finitely many other normal hyperplanes, choose v rational, and clear denominators. This gives (8) with integer v_F. All its constants depend only on the fixed word and face, not on N or the tangential source values. The direction need not make EVERY active inequality negative. It remains outside the physical polytope because a_g<0. This is why it also handles the all-zero corner, where shifting every transfer outward negatively was uphill. At that corner one can instead increase all transfers and decrease t sufficiently: all heads move outside while q_F(v_F)>0. The COMPLETE product descends. ## 5. Uniform local phase estimate Write the original scalar density as exp(N S) times its retained amplitude, with the gathered factorials (4), and include any fixed integer character sector from the actual cardinal/norm packets. Let y_F be a point of the COMPLEXIFIED affine face: its active indices equal 0 or1 exactly. Assume its inactive factors are regular on the chosen marked tube. If G is the nonsingular part, suppose |grad G|<=C_0+C_1 epsilon log N. (9) The original shrinking-strip hypotheses supply (9); it is not a bound on an unknown knot scalar. Choose delta=N^(-alpha), with alpha>C_1 epsilon/q_F(v_F), allowing fixed norm-comparison constants. The finitely many endpoint expansions (6) give Re S(y_F+delta v_F)-Re S_face(y_F) =delta log delta q_F(v_F) +O_word(delta(1+epsilon log N)) <=-c_F delta log N (10) for all sufficiently large N. Choose alpha<1 and epsilon small. The estimate is uniform on the regular tangential tube. Any fixed integer mark has exactly constant modulus under this real displacement. The active full-function resets change only those marks, so (10) holds for all retained outgoing marked sectors. A pole in a separated cardinal coefficient is not crossed independently of its full packet. Small complex offsets of size delta'=N^(-beta), beta>alpha, change the active-factor height by O(delta'|log delta'|), and the regular height by O(delta'(1+epsilon log N)). They therefore do not remove the far-edge decrease in (10). The shift of the quantum upper endpoint d/N from1 costs O(log N/N), also smaller than the stated drop. This is a local inner-to-outer normal estimate, not a monotone flow assertion at every intermediate point of every small corner. There are finitely many physical faces for a fixed word. Thus the vectors, charts and admissible exponents can be chosen uniformly over this entire finite list. At every vertex Re S_face=0: all factorial arguments are 0 or1 and all retained polynomial phases are pure imaginary on the real vertex. This agrees with the independent subexponential all-transfer-endpoint operator bound. ## 6. Exact source scope and what remains The cardinal-completed scalar is holomorphic in any prescribed fixed O(N) box and has the exact original values at every valid integer state, zero at every invalid one. Therefore its COMPLETE finite residue sum can be represented in any affine unimodular chart from Section 2. This is equality of residue functionals on holomorphic scalars, with orientation retained. It is not a pointwise identity between the different products of cotangents. Consequently (8)--(10) identify a descending normal for every physical face without assuming independent output positions or individual-atom zero sides. They do not by themselves glue those charts into one global deformed cycle. Partial chart changes retain diagonal cotangent walls and side currents; a sweep through valid physical integers retains their original residues. Nonphysical integer poles of separated window modes must still cancel in their complete packet. The remaining global claim must control this entire assembled source, the cumulative transport mass and any escaping tangential charts. Neither geometric survival nor a sharp whole-source volume upper bound follows merely from nonvanishing q_F or from the existence of the local vectors (8). These are constructive boundary action estimates for the proposed boundary-to-interior transport, with the exact source gluing still required. ## 7. A uniform quantum bound for the complete active cluster The preceding real radial estimate has an exact finite-N counterpart. It concerns the WHOLE cardinal-completed active factorial packet, not separate polar Gamma or cardinal modes. All constants below may depend on the fixed face, word, chosen integer direction and bounded normal-height set, but not on N or the bulk amplitude. ### 7.1 A primitive outward direction with a literal source coordinate One can strengthen (8) to choose grad a_g(v_F)=-1, q=q_F(v_F)>0, grad a_f(v_F)!=0 for every active a_f. (11) Every physical row a_g is primitive. If q_F is a negative multiple of grad a_g, any integer solution of grad a_g(v)=-1 has positive q_F(v); perturb it within the integer kernel to avoid the finitely many other normal hyperplanes. Otherwise q_F is nonzero on its integer kernel. Start with one integer solution v_0 and add Lw, where w lies in that kernel, q_F(w)>0, and avoids all active normal kernels except those forced by proportionality to a_g. Such w exists by an open rational halfspace argument; choose L sufficiently large and avoid the finitely many exceptional values. This proves (11). The vector v_F is automatically primitive, since its pairing with an integer row is -1. Use a_g as the FIRST affine integer source coordinate and complete the others by an integer basis dual to v_F and ker a_g. The resulting chart has determinant +/-1. With its tangent coordinates fixed, the outward normal path is u=u_F+z v_F, a_g(u)=-z EXACTLY. (12) This selected zero offset is important. Other active factorial arguments may have bounded complex offsets nu_f in a small face tube, but the selected a_g has zero offset for every value of those tangent coordinates. Every positive integer z in (12) is therefore an INVALID physical state through this selected head or transfer. The complete cardinal factor for that physical form vanishes there, even when the remaining tangent coordinates are complex. This is stronger than an assertion just on integer tangent slices. Re-present the COMPLETE residue source in this affine integer chart before taking the normal homotopy. Its first factor is pi*cot(pi*a_g) da_g=pi*cot(pi*z) dz with induced orientation. Moving the original outward edge from Re z=1/2 to Re z=M+1/2 crosses only these zero-residue nonphysical integers. Both finite-height horizontal connectors remain. This source statement uses the full holomorphic completion, not a pointwise substitution of one cotangent product for another. No valid-state cotangent residue is swept away. ### 7.2 All upper normalizers and window reflections are exact Write an active argument at its lower endpoint as s, and one at its upper endpoint as d+s. Its exponent c is one of the actual head exponents -2,0,2 or a transfer exponent -1. The exact identities are Fhat(d+s)/N=exp[i*pi*s*(s+d)/N]/Fhat(-s), w_N^+(d+s)=w_N^-(-s), w_N^-(d+s)=w_N^+(-s). (13) The first identity retains the complete reflected chirp and the factor N=F_d. The other two follow from S_N(d-s)=-S_N(s) in the literal cardinal sum. Thus the complete active packet, including its windows, becomes N^(C_upper) exp(P_upper(z)) product_i [Fhat(s_i)^(r_i) w_N^+(s_i)^(p_i^+) w_N^-(s_i)^(p_i^-)], s_i=nu_i+beta_i z, beta_i integer nonzero, C_upper=sum_(active upper occurrences) c, sum_i r_i beta_i=q_F(v_F)=q>0. (14) Here lower occurrences have r_i=c and their original slope; upper occurrences have r_i=-c and the reflected slope. P_upper is the explicit sum of the chirps in (13). The powers are those of the original scalar cardinal completion, with orientations exchanged under (13). They are never reset to one. Total window powers are strictly larger than every positive Gamma pole order; in particular p_i^++p_i^->max(r_i,0). An active physical window with r_i=0 is kept as well. It may be precisely the selected window in (12). The integer power N^(C_upper) is the ACTUAL upper-endpoint factor, not a tame normalization chosen by the proof. It may be negative. It will remain explicit in the bound below. On bounded normal imaginary height the chirp exp(P_upper) has at most exp(O(M+1)) modulus for Re z of size M. ### 7.3 Uniform regularized Gamma estimate through all collisions Put h=2*pi*i/N and use the fixed branch Log(-h)=log(2*pi/N)-pi*i/2. The actual Barnes product gives EXACTLY Fhat(s)=(-h)^s Gamma(s+1) A_N(s), A_N(s)=exp[i*pi*s*(s+1)/(2N)] product_(k>=1) Gamma(Nk+s+1) /[Gamma(Nk-s)(Nk)^(2s+1)]. (15) For |s|<=delta_0*N with any fixed sufficiently small delta_0, A_N is holomorphic and zero-free, including at the negative integers. The common Gamma divisor in (15) has been canceled BEFORE evaluating there. Uniformly in this disk, |A_N(s)|+|A_N(s)^(-1)| <=2 exp[C(|s|+1)^2/N]. (16) For completeness, apply the elementary uniform Stirling expansion to t+s+1 and t-s, t=Nk. Its 1/t term cancels exactly: LogGamma(t+s+1)-LogGamma(t-s)-(2s+1)log t =O((|s|+1)^3/t^2). Both arguments have positive real part, uniformly away from zero. The error sums absolutely over k. Its total is O((|s|+1)^3/N^2), bounded by C(|s|+1)^2/N on the disk. The explicit quadratic chirp in (15) has the same latter bound. This proves (16) without a periodic ambiguity or a choice of a replacement factorial. Let Re z=M+theta with theta in a fixed bounded interval, |Im z|<=T, and let all nu_i range over a fixed bounded complex set. For M sufficiently large the sign of Re s_i is the sign of beta_i. For negative Re s_i use the exact reflection Gamma(s_i+1)=-pi/[sin(pi*s_i) Gamma(-s_i)]. The COMPLETE window is w_N^+/- (s)=exp(+/-pi*i*s) sin(pi*s) S_N(s)/pi. On Re s<=-1/2, |S_N(s)|<=C log(N+1). The retained window powers cancel every negative-integer Gamma pole in the same product, and leave only nonnegative powers of sin(pi*s). These are uniformly bounded on the stated fixed-height strip. For positive Re s_i, the original Gamma is regular and the whole-plane cardinal bound is polynomial in N on that strip. Stirling for the remaining Gamma or reciprocal Gamma factors now gives, for the complete product, log |active packet/N^(C_upper)| <=-q M log[N/(M+1)] +C M+C M^2/N+C log N. (17) Offsets nu_i contribute only O(log N), since they are bounded; all constants beta_i are fixed. For bounded M the same assertion, with enlarged C, follows from (15) after the already-canceled Gamma poles. Thus (17) is uniform through dependent and coincident active collisions. No estimate is made on individual polar modes. ### 7.4 Coupling to the actual bulk and the quantitative collar Let G_N(u_F) contain all INACTIVE factorials and the full original Cartan, conversion, pivot, kappa and external chi_N/N factors. Do not divide by a completed face amplitude, which may vanish. The explicitly retained N^(C_upper) stays outside G_N. Assume the inactive marked tube gives the normal allowance |G_N(u_F+zv_F)| <=exp(CM) N^(C_1*epsilon*M+C_2) |G_N(u_F)|. (18) This is the quantitative form of (9). On a regular marked bulk branch with uniform factorial-symbol control, inactive clocks and their complements bounded above and below by N^(+/-epsilon), and a displacement smaller than their singularity distance give the stated O(1+epsilon log N) leading logarithmic derivative. In a continued chart the EXACT allowance (18) additionally retains and controls its central norm factors and full symbol; it does not follow merely from bounds on B and 1-B if an outside-band integer factorial divisor is approached. Finite bulk-window modes keep their actual integer-marked exponential in G_N; the HEAD/active windows remain whole as in (14). Their bounded-height polynomial factors are already included in (17). Combining the exact active bound and (18) gives the following bound for each retained bulk-window mode, with the active packet WHOLE: |Atilde_N(u_F+zv_F)| <=|N^(C_upper) G_N(u_F)| N^C exp[CM+CM^2/N] N^(C_1*epsilon*M) [(M+1)/N]^(qM). (19) For a general nonreal tangent chamber the COMPLETE scalar is the fixed finite sum of these modes. Its bound uses the SUM of the absolute reference amplitudes on the right of (19), not the absolute value of their potentially canceling sum. On a fixed-height joint contour the inactive windows themselves cost only a polynomial; there the unwindowed original bulk G_N suffices directly.
