The unproved geometric gate is therefore explicit source-compatible adjoint/filtration transport, including conversion terms at complex turning points and the actual boundary source. Full-space positive metrics with subexponential conditioning cannot be presumed to provide that improvement. Source-dependent nonquadratic methods, explicitly controlled exponential metrics, and a genuinely verified semidefinite adjoint certificate remain possible. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pointed_metric_transport.py) checks the exact metric inequalities, their pointed lower bound, the finite Gramian identity and the adjoint residual formula.

title: Positive whole sources for actual complete-circle Conway trees
text: # Positive whole sources for actual complete-circle Conway trees 29 October 2026. This gives an explicit family of WHOLE original sources closed under arbitrary finite binary Conway composition and genuine quarter-turns. Every circle color and every root normal is retained. For the robust seed below every such source is strictly positive at every level N>=3, at either parity and at composite levels. This is a source theorem, not a hyperbolic-volume theorem. A Conway seam is a four-punctured sphere, which has moduli; its hyperbolic energy cannot be added by the rigid thrice-punctured-sphere argument used for belt sums. No geometric realization, bridge-number lower bound, or noncancellation result for an arbitrary primitive graph is inferred. ## 1. Compile a literal four-port ribbon diagram Use the original physical V_N, its cup p, ordinary cap ell and unrestricted marked cap m. Put d=N-1. A box has two incoming lower and two outgoing upper main ribbon ports. Its auxiliary complete-circle coupon is the ACTUAL threaded loop L_N: the original four mixed crossings [2,1,1,2], the original auxiliary pivot, and its ordinary auxiliary closure. No additional factor 1/N is attached to that loop. Its literal normalization was proved in [the crossing-circle source theorem](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). Define operations on actual boxes as follows. * Product: stack two boxes, connecting their two matching intermediate main ribbons by identity wires. The operator is ordinary composition. * Turn: rotate a box through a quarter-turn, retaining its four oriented boundary ribbons by bending with the SAME p and ell. On its matrix A, in the all-primal recorded chart, this is (Rturn A)_((u,b);(v,e)) =p(d-e)/p(d-u) A_((d-u,v);(b,d-e)). (1) At the root p(d-r)=N x^(-r), x=q^d, so the factor is x^(u-e). This is not a free leg permutation or an added physical crossing. These two constructions are precisely the vertical and turned four-port Conway operations on a planar ribbon tangle. Boundary dual objects are transported by the displayed original snakes; one does not silently replace a bend by an identity. A parenthesized expression therefore specifies an actual tangle recursively, including its port order, orientation and all auxiliary circles. No scalar three-port Frobenius vertex is introduced at a branching node. Close a resulting box by the original one-cut closure phi: close one main object by its original ordinary pivotal trace, and point the remaining physical component with m. In matrices this is phi(A)=(1/N)Tr[(I tensor g)A], g=K^(1-N)=(-1)^d K. (2) The partial pivotal trace of a Hopf box is scalar on the simple physical V_N; evaluating its remaining cup with m p=1 gives (2). Thus (2) retains the actual one unrestricted mark. For an expression in the pair Casimir algebra its exact scalar is the established [original Frobenius functional](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). Any external line/framing conversion factors remain those of the original diagram; they are not altered or suppressed here. ## 2. A robust all-channel seed Use the FULL Newton algebra and basis of [the positive multiplication theorem](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md): H_N=C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2), Bhat_r=product_(j<r)(c_j-z)/s_r^2, 0<=r<=d, c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), M=floor(d/2). The physical operations and closure are Rturn Bhat_r=Bhat_(d-r), phi(sum_r a_r Bhat_r)=a_d. (3) The full complete circle, including its paired nilpotents, has h_N=Rturn L_N=sum_(v=0)^M a_v Bhat_v, a_v=N sum_(j=v)^M k_j s_(j+v)/[s_(j-v)s_v^2]>0, k_j=2 at a paired node, 1 at the odd simple node. (4) Set the ACTUAL seed box A_N=h_N h_N h_N. (5) It contains THREE separate complete-circle coupons, each turned by the literal operation (1); it is not a cube of L_N on the same unturned pair. This distinction is essential: L_N^2=0 at even N. For every N>=3, A_N has STRICTLY positive coefficients at every Newton coordinate 0,...,d. Indeed 3M>=d. For each k<=d choose 0<=i_1,i_2,i_3<=M with sum k. Multiply the corresponding positive terms in (4), always choosing the upper output index in the exact rule Bhat_i Bhat_j=sum_(t=max(i,j))^(i+j) [s_(i+j)s_t/(s_i s_j s_(t-i)s_(t-j)s_(i+j-t))] Bhat_t, i+j<N. (6) Both partial sums are <=k<=d<N. Hence the selected product is strictly positive. All other surviving terms are nonnegative. No sign is deduced from a finite-field residue, and no root normal is omitted. ## 3. Arbitrary trees give exact strictly positive whole sources Let expressions be generated by E ::= A | Rturn(E) | E E. (7) An expression is fixed before taking the level limit. It can have arbitrary finite binary branching and turn depth. Compile it to the literal ribbon tangle of section1, and denote its physical operator E_N. Then, for every N>=3, E_N=sum_(r=0)^d e_r Bhat_r, e_r>0, original_raw_closed_source(E_N)=phi(E_N)=e_d>0. (8) Proof. The seed has full strict support by section2. The actual turn reverses all coordinates, preserving strict support. If f and g have full strict support, their product does too: its r-th coefficient contains f_r g_0 times the exact unit coefficient of Bhat_r Bhat_0. Every other term has nonnegative coefficient by (6), or is zero by FULL repeated-root divisibility when i+j>=N. Structural induction proves (8). The coefficient operations are faithful actual physical turn/product identities, so induction also proves equality with the compiled original source, including its mark and all circle colors. The N=2 exception is real. Then M=0 and h_N is a scalar; a turn can move its support to d=1, and a subsequent product of two such turned terms can vanish. The theorem makes no N=2 strictness assertion. This finite exception has no bearing on a large-level limit but is not erased from the exact source statement. More generally a tangle built from L_N by turn and product, without the robust seed restriction, has a nonnegative exact source. Its zero/nonzero test is the finite flow problem (6), turn r->d-r, and closure r=d. It need not be nonzero: redundant serial complete circles retain the genuine even-level zero. The robust seed supplies an explicit class in which the global flow problem is always feasible. ## 4. Exact positive partition, remaining geometry and graph scope Expand (7) as a tensor circuit. At a seed use (4) three times; at a product use (6); at a turn identify output d-r; at the final closure fix output d. This is an exact finite POSITIVE partition function for the WHOLE original scalar in (8), with at most N to the number of internal index slots terms. It supplies a genuine global conservation problem, not independent maximization of unglued local capacities. The repeated-root algebra, rather than only its nodal quotient, determines every multiplication and the final coefficient. This coordinate cone is not a claim that each physical reflected box is a positive matrix. In particular Rturn L_N belongs to the cone, whereas its literal swap-reflected form has mixed inertia even on the actual two-vector source plane; see the [typed reflection-inertia theorem](actual_turned_circle_reflection_inertia.md). The positive scalar statement (8) uses the exact Newton multiplication and original functional, rather than a product of physical Hilbert norms. Each expression is an explicit operational class of augmented ribbon diagrams. Its constituent boxes have four ports and can be sewn along four-punctured Conway spheres. The source algebra does not certify that these surfaces are essential or that the complement is hyperbolic. It also does not establish that different trees are topologically distinct or that their main-component bridge numbers grow. Those are separate topology questions. In particular no equality of this source partition with a Casson–Rivin angle functional is being asserted here. The full primitive cube is not replaced by a Conway tree. It still requires a multiport identity or coherent estimate after removing its central cycle projections. The separately computed full-cube finite values are diagnostics, not a consequence of (8). For reproducibility the [full-cube diagnostic script](../experiments/diagnose_actual_full_cube_complete_circle_source.py) contracts the literal complete physical CD factorization against the original J, ordinary caps and exposed unrestricted mark. Its [recorded complex128 values](../experiments/actual_full_cube_complete_circle_diagnostic_results.json) include approximately 7.601732064e9 at N=3 and 3.314692220e20 at N=5; all twelve circle-color sums are retained. The recorded imaginary residual grows with level. No certified error bound, positivity, central dominance, or full-cube volume limit is inferred from them. Audit: [literal physical turns, full Casimir matrices and tree closures](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.py). Finite exact-field identities supplement the ribbon compilation and positive-support proof. Principal-root sign conclusions use (4),(6), not signs of residues. No volume theorem is inferred from the audit. The theorem is restricted to the stated source and four-punctured seam, including the N=2 exception. Its finite audit checks physical levels and whole tree operators with all-input pivotal closures.

title: Hyperbolic volume of the whole cylindrical positive Conway source
text: # Hyperbolic volume of the whole cylindrical positive Conway source 29 October 2026. The positive source's volume problem has an actual geometric realization. Every retained CYLINDRICAL factor in the robust Conway class is the complement of its literal compiled augmented link, with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric, and its WHOLE original quantum limit equals that metric's volume. The distinction between cylindrical factors and cap products matters. The [cap-sum reduction](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md) gives exact componentwise connected sums, which generally are not hyperbolic. First apply that boundary reduction. The theorem below applies to every remaining factor whose closure flag is C. It does not assert that an arbitrary unreduced Conway expression is hyperbolic. The construction is elementary and source-specific: leaf pyramids, multiplication prisms, actual ordered quadrilateral ports, the original crossing-disk cut, and canonical cusp horospheres. No polyhedron existence theorem or identification inferred from a numerical volume is used. ## 1. The exact class and result Use the [literal physical compiler](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md): h is the genuine quarter-turn of the complete crossing-circle box, A=h^3, and robust expressions are generated by E ::= A | R E | E E. R is the actual quarter-turn with its original cups and caps; product is the actual identity-wire stack. Write C(E) for the original marked cylindrical closure phi(E), and D(E)=C(RE) for the cap closure. Every auxiliary circle remains a complete original-color component. A retained cylindrical factor means C(A), or C(FG) with F,G robust expressions, with their entire internal turns and products retained. Initial turns at the closure can be removed by the exact C/D boundary rules; a D product splits by the cap-sum theorem. This produces the stated factors without pretending that they exhaust arbitrary knots. Let L_E be the ACTUAL unframed link of such a cylindrical factor, and Z_(E,N)>0 its original raw one-cut source for N>=3. Then lim_(N -> infinity) (2pi/N)log Z_(E,N) =2 max_(P_E) V_E =Vol(S^3 minus L_E). (1) The first equality is the proved whole-source variational theorem, with all colors, all repeated-root normals, both parities and all composite levels. This note proves the second equality and supplies the actual complete metric. The recorded conversion from raw source to the original enhanced reduced invariant is a unit framing phase; the one-cut modified normalization has its recorded additional 1/N. Neither changes (1). No framing or peripheral character is suppressed inside the finite-level source identity. There is also an open version. For every robust E and every b in (0,1), its coefficient volume profile v_E(b)=max_(P_E(b)) V_E is the volume of a convex ideal polyhedron P_E(b) with ONE ordered quadrilateral port. All edges away from that port are right angled; the port's two opposite edge pairs have angles pi b and pi(1-b). The original coefficient asymptotic and its algebraic boundary branch are those in the [boundary profile theorem](actual_conway_boundary_volume_relation.md). The port is a geometric ideal quadrilateral, not a meridian eigenvalue or an automatically totally geodesic four-punctured boundary sphere. ## 2. The source maximum is strict in every unforced cell Expand every A into three h leaves and two products. A leaf output x has 0<=x<=1/2. A product (x,y)->z has p=z-x>=0, q=z-y>=0, r=x+y-z>=0, w=1-x-y>=0. The source atoms are the two leaf tetrahedra with angles (x,1/2-x,1/2), and the three product tetrahedra (y,x,w), (p,q,2r+w), (p+q,r,r+w). (2) Turns impose output 1-input and add no atom. First there is a strict feasible assignment for EVERY proper robust output b in (0,1). At a product choose both child outputs in (b/2,min(b,1/2)); then p,q,r,w are all positive. At a turn use 1-b for the child. For the seed h^3, choose its last leaf c with 0<c<min(2b/3,1-b), t=b-c/2, and choose both first leaves a in (t/2,min(t,1/2)). Their first product has output t and the second has output b. All leaf and product inequalities are strict. This proves feasibility by induction. For a closed C(FG), the last product is forced to output 1, so its inputs obey x+y=1 and its three atoms are identically flat. DELETE ONLY this forced final gate from the volume list and eliminate its forced wires. Choosing x=y=1/2 and applying the preceding construction to F,G gives a strict feasible point of the reduced problem. For C(A)=C((hh)h), choose last leaf c in (0,1/2), first-product output 1-c, and its two leaves in ((1-c)/2,1/2). Again every retained cell is strict. The finite source has not been changed: the final exact multiplication coefficient is one on its forced support. Here is the barrier which rules out any other boundary maximum. Along a segment from a boundary point toward the constructed strict point, an ideal tetrahedron with angles (0,a,1-a), 0<a<1, has volume directional derivative +infinity. This follows from Lambda(t)=-t log t+O(t) near zero, or directly from its log-sine derivative. A vertex-flat tetrahedron (0,0,1) has only a finite one-sided derivative: the t log t terms cancel, leaving the finite entropy expression in the two positive angle speeds. A positive tetrahedron has finite derivative. Thus no other atom can cancel a +infinity derivative by contributing -infinity. Any proper wire equal to 0 or 1 forces such a nonvertex-flat atom somewhere below it. A turn exchanges 0 and 1. A product with output 0 has both inputs 0. A product with output 1 has inputs summing to 1: either both are strictly between 0 and 1, giving the atom (y,x,0), or one child is an endpoint and the argument continues downward. A finite descent ends at a leaf, whose only possible endpoint in {0,1} is 0; its leaf atom is (0,1/2,1/2). The sole excluded root gate is never used in this descent. Therefore no maximum has a proper endpoint wire. A leaf at 1/2 likewise has the nonvertex-flat atom (1/2,0,1/2). Now all proper wires lie in (0,1). If w=0 at a retained product, its first atom is (y,x,0). If r=0 its third atom is (z,0,1-z). If p=0 and q>0 its second atom is (0,q,1-q), with 0<q<1; the q=0 case is symmetric. If p=q=0, the third atom is (0,x,1-x). Each is a nonvertex-flat atom. All boundary cases are therefore excluded by the same strict feasible segment. Every maximizing leaf and retained prism is STRICT. The maximum is also unique. Each positive tetrahedron has negative definite angle Hessian, and the product's three angle maps recover x,y,z. The leaf angle recovers its wire as well. Thus a tangent annihilating every retained angle map annihilates every leaf and product wire; turns then annihilate their wires too. The only deleted gate had its output fixed and its inputs already belong to the two children. The negative Hessian on the reduced tangent space is positive definite. Strict concavity gives uniqueness. For fixed proper output b this argument applies on every slice. The implicit-function theorem consequently gives one real analytic interior maximizing branch throughout b in (0,1). No hidden change of maximizing face is needed for this robust class. ## 3. Literal local cells and their ordered port maps The [local ideal-cell theorem](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md) constructs the following actual convex cells and proves their volumes and entire ordered face metrics. A leaf is an ideal quadrangular pyramid. Its apex O is infinity; its base corners C0,C1,C2,C3 lie successively at 1, exp(2pi i x), -1, -exp(2pi i x). Its base-edge angles on C0C1,C2C3 are pi x; on C1C2,C3C0 they are pi(1/2-x). Its four apex edges are right angled. Its volume is pi g(x), exactly the two leaf atoms. Color the two triangles (O,C1,C2) and (O,C3,C0) SHADED; color the other two side triangles WHITE. The base is an uncolored output PORT. Call the output edges 01,23 FREE and the other pair CAP. A completed product has FREE angles pi z and CAP angles pi(1-z). A genuine turn rotates its port once, exchanges these pairs, and replaces its label z by 1-z. The white and shaded faces elsewhere are carried with the actual box. A product is the explicit six-vertex ideal prism of the local theorem, with vertices infinity,P,v0,v1,v2,v3. Its two triangular faces are WHITE. Its input quadrilaterals and output are Fx=(infinity,v0,v1,P), Fy=(infinity,v3,v2,P), Fz=(v0,v1,v2,v3). The actual stack maps are lower F: (C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (v0,v1,P,infinity), upper G: (C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (infinity,P,v2,v3). (3) Label C0 bottom-left, C1 bottom-right, C2 top-right, C3 top-left. Then the lower top-left is infinity, the same as the upper bottom-left; both right interface corners are P. The four remaining outer corners are v0,v1,v2,v3 in exactly their original order. Thus (3) glues the actual identity stack, with no Conway mutation. For an ordered ideal quadrilateral define kappa(C0,C1,C2,C3) =(C0-C1)(C2-C3)/((C0-C3)(C1-C2))>0. The local theorem proves kappa_leaf=exp(-g'), and kappa(Fx)=exp(-m_x), kappa(Fy)=exp(-m_y), kappa(Fz)=exp(-m_z). Both input maps (3) invert kappa. Stationarity at each actual internal wire says that its child and parent action derivatives sum to zero; hence kappa_child kappa_parent=1. These are precisely the ordered ideal-quadrilateral isometry conditions. A turn inverts kappa and changes the derivative sign, so the same conclusion holds through any number of actual turns. ## 4. Convexity and the colored boundary survive every product Attach the two child cells to their prism by the isometries (3), with interiors on opposite sides of each attaching face. A child CAP edge meets a prism edge with angle pi x or pi y. For a leaf child the sum is pi/2, separating its shaded triangle from a prism white triangle. For a completed child it is pi, so two WHITE faces merge flatly. The edge shared by both inputs has total angle pi(w+x+y)=pi. Its incident faces are white and merge. The two other longitudinal edges on the output acquire angles pi(p+x)=pi z and pi(q+y)=pi z. The other output pair retains pi(1-z). This proves the claimed FREE/CAP output pattern. All nonport edges that remain are right angled and separate one white and one shaded face. Convexity can be checked without a global polyhedron theorem. When two convex cells are put on opposite sides of their common supported face, their intersection is exactly that face. Their union is locally convex at its finite seam points whenever the incident boundary angles add to at most pi. For the first child attachment the sums are pi or pi/2 on CAP edges, pi z on one FREE edge and pi(1-y) on the other; the second attachment makes the common edge flat and gives the stated output angles. All are at most pi. Here local convexity implies convexity directly. The union is closed in hyperbolic space and connected by finite-length paths. A minimizing sequence of paths between two finite points, with lengths bounded by one competitor, stays in a compact hyperbolic ball. Constant-speed parametrization and compactness give a shortest path. Local convexity forces it to be an ambient geodesic locally, including at finite seam edges. It is therefore the unique hyperbolic geodesic segment. The entire segment lies in the union. Ideal vertices are outside hyperbolic space and cause no extra finite seam exception. Thus the inductive union is an actual convex ideal polyhedron. Its output quadrilateral remains a genuine supported face because its two edge angles lie strictly between zero and pi. Distinct vertices not in the attaching face cannot accidentally be identified: they lie on opposite supported sides. The cell adjacency graph is a tree, and all volume contributions add with degree one. The colored vertex pattern is equally explicit. A leaf apex is four-valent with alternating shaded and white faces. A leaf port corner is three-valent. After a product, each output corner has the cyclic pattern PORT,WHITE,SHADED,WHITE, with its two port angles z and 1-z and its other two angles right. The input-interface vertices become four-valent, with alternating shaded/white faces, after the just-listed flat white seams are merged. The same pattern is preserved under a turn. In particular every leaf retains its TWO shaded ideal triangles, meeting only at its original apex O. The resulting open cell P_E(b) has volume exactly v_E(b). Its ordered port metric is kappa_E(b)=exp(-v'_E(b)/pi), (4) by the envelope identity and the local derivative formulas. Equation (4) assigns a literal geometric quadrilateral modulus to the source boundary conjugate variable. It does not rename that modulus as a knot longitude or meridian. ## 5. The actual CLOSED projection cut and its oriented ribbon graph The [independent bowtie-cut proof](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) identifies the closed metric polyhedron with the actual link exterior. It uses the original crossing disks and literal main-wire matching, without treating an open quadrilateral port as half of a physical four-punctured tangle boundary. That earlier open-port description was too strong: restoring its shaded pairings already identifies two pairs of its corners. The ordered metric port remains valid auxiliary cut data, but it does not alone specify the physical boundary holonomy. Here is the closed argument. In each projection ball every auxiliary semicircle is boundary parallel by its original half crossing disk. Drilling these disjoint arcs and then cutting along those recorded half disks returns a ball. Its ideal vertices are the original semicircles and the main segments between consecutive disk punctures. Each disk contributes exactly the two shaded triangles (O,C1,C2) and (O,C3,C0). Its remaining boundary regions are white. The original identity stack pairs F2 with G1 and F3 with G0, and leaves exposed corners (F0,F1,G2,G3). Turns cyclically rotate those corners; the final cylindrical closure pairs 0 with 3 and 1 with 2. At each paired main segment the two local oriented shaded sectors concatenate in the original projection sphere. This determines the entire oriented bowtie ribbon graph and every white facial walk. The metric prism maps in (3) give exactly the same segment pairings and cyclic orders. After closure, every nonflat edge belongs to one of the original shaded leaf triangles; all other edges are flat white/white seams and merge. Thus the stationary polyhedron has the same FULL oriented ribbon boundary as the actual projection cut, including every white face cycle and every original shaded pairing. The labeled sphere cellulation extends across each cut ball, and reversing the matching disk/projection pairings gives the actual closed link exterior. This establishes the required topology and degree one. It does not rely on matching only face or cusp counts. The separate audit reconstructs this ribbon graph directly from original wires, without prisms, and compares all oriented face cycles and all vertex cyclic orders after fixing one global orientation. ## 6. The actual cylindrical closure makes a right-angled polyhedron For C(FG), delete the final forced-flat product and take the two already constructed child cells at outputs x and y=1-x. Their ordered port metrics agree: stationarity in x gives v'_F(x)=v'_G(1-x), hence kappa_F=kappa_G. The actual closed port map is F:C_j -> G:C_(3-j), j modulo 4. (5) It sends the lower top-left to the upper bottom-left and the lower top-right to the upper bottom-right, giving the stack interface. It sends the remaining lower bottom-left/right to the upper top-left/ right, giving the two original outside cylindrical closing wires. It preserves the FREE and CAP edge pairs and preserves kappa. Thus (5) is the required orientation-reversing ideal-face isometry. Glue the child polyhedra on opposite sides of this face. FREE angles sum to pi. If both children are completed cells, CAP angles also sum to pi. If one child is a leaf, as in the last product of A=h^3, the CAP sum is pi/2 instead. Two leaf children cannot satisfy the closed constraint strictly. In every case the previous convexity argument applies, flat white seams merge, and the result is a convex ideal RIGHT-ANGLED polyhedron P_E with all boundary edges separating white from shaded. Every ideal vertex is four-valent with alternating white/shaded faces. Its shaded faces are the two triangles of each original retained crossing circle, with their actual disk labels. Its volume is the sum of all retained leaf and prism cell volumes, namely max V_E. If H is the number of h leaves, the resulting face counts are 3H ideal vertices, 6H edges, 2H shaded triangles and H+2 white polygons. These are consistency checks on the literal cut, not its topological proof. For H=3 they recover the actual nine-vertex four-octahedron theta construction after doubling. ## 7. Restore the original link and verify complete cusps Take two oppositely oriented copies P_E^0,P_E^1. Glue each white face across the copies by its original projection label. For each leaf glue its two shaded triangles WITHIN each copy, fixing its apex and matching the two pieces of each original main arc. In the leaf labels this matches C1 to C0 and C2 to C3. These are exactly the two sides of the crossing disk cut in section 5. The port maps and turns have carried these labels unchanged. Reversing all cuts therefore gives S^3 minus the ACTUAL compiled link L_E, with no component deletion and no change of ribbon source. The shaded faces are ideal triangles, so each prescribed vertex bijection is an isometry. Every finite edge cycle alternates its white gluing with its shaded gluing and has FOUR right angles. The two shaded faces of one disk meet only at their apex, so no premature edge identification shortens this four-step cycle. The cycle returns pointwise on the edge: the white maps identify identical copies and the two shaded maps are inverse vertex-labeled triangle isometries. There is consequently no residual translation along the edge in addition to the angle check. All finite edge neighborhoods therefore have angle 2pi, not a multiple-winding or cone singularity. Completeness follows from a simultaneous explicit decoration. At every ideal vertex of P_E the horospherical link is a Euclidean rectangle. Its two opposite shaded sides have equal lengths. Scale that vertex's horosphere so that this common length is one. Every shaded triangle now has corner horocycle segments of length one at all three vertices, its canonical mutually tangent decoration. Thus EVERY shaded gluing preserves these horospheres. White gluing joins identical labeled copies and preserves them as well. Uniformly shrink the horospheres to make them disjoint. Their links glue without dilation to compact nonsingular Euclidean surfaces; the reversible link cut identifies those surfaces as the actual link's cusp tori. The complement of the cusp neighborhoods is compact. These are complete finite-volume hyperbolic ends, and the entire assembled metric is complete. Its volume is 2 Vol(P_E)=2 max V_E. Together with the original full-source limit this proves (1). ## 8. Algebraic classes, generality and the remaining knot problem The selected stationary shapes are algebraic by the existing [algebraic maximum theorem](positive_source_algebraic_volume_period.md). The local cell theorem identifies the conjugate-antisymmetric class of the three source product atoms with that of an actual prism triangulation, by an exact five-term calculation. The leaf atoms are already the pyramid triangulation. This gives an equality of RATIONAL GEOMETRIC BLOCH CLASSES, not only equality of regulators. Here B_E is the source-selected sum sum_j([z_j]-[bar z_j]) over all its nonflat source atoms, as defined in the [source Bloch theorem](actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.md). Here is its precise field and orientation convention. Choose a number field K stable under complex conjugation and containing all source phases and shapes, all local AND glued ideal vertex coordinates, and all shapes of a geometric ideal triangulation of P_E. In particular every auxiliary five-term/coning cross ratio lies in K. Such a finite extension exists: the local coordinates are algebraic expressions in the source phases; an ordered ideal-face isometry is a Mobius or anti-Mobius map fixed by three algebraic vertices. Each finite successive gluing therefore introduces only algebraic coordinates. No identification of K with the source shape field or a manifold trace field is asserted. Write A(z)=[z]-[bar z]. The local five-term identities and ideal-chain triangulation independence give image_K(B_E)=sum_(T in a geometric triangulation of P_E) A(z_T) in P(K)_Q. (6) For clarity, this comparison does not presume that arbitrary choices of cell-face diagonals already match. A mismatch on a planar ideal face is filled by a coplanar tetrahedral chain, whose shapes are real and whose A-symbols vanish. After correcting those face chains, the difference between the cell sum and a triangulation of P_E is a 3-cycle in the full abstract simplex on their finite ideal vertex set. Coning that cycle gives a 4-chain; every 4-simplex boundary is a five-term relation. This is the exact triangulation argument in the local cell theorem, applied to the actual degree-one polyhedron. One geometric ideal triangulation of P_E is obtained by coning its nonincident faces to a chosen ideal vertex, triangulating those faces by fans. The incident faces use the induced fan at that vertex. Use IDENTICAL face triangulations on the oppositely oriented second copy. White faces then match triangle by triangle under their labeled copy maps; shaded faces were already triangles. Thus the two oriented tetrahedral chains form a degree-one ideal fundamental chain for the ACTUAL link complement from sections 5--7. Normalize the first copy so its positively oriented tetrahedron has shape z_T. Choose mirrored coordinates for the second copy by complex conjugation and give it the opposite abstract orientation, as required by the white-face gluing. The inherited vertex ordering of its mirrored tetrahedron has shape bar z_T and coefficient -1 in this fundamental chain. Its contribution is therefore -[bar z_T], not +[bar z_T]. In particular its regulator contribution is +D(z_T), consistent with the positive metric volume of the second copy. Consequently the actual oriented geometric fundamental chain has symbol sum beta_geom(L_E;K)=sum_T([z_T]-[bar z_T]). (7) Equations (6),(7) prove image_K(B_E)=beta_geom(L_E;K) in B(K)_Q, R_K(beta_geom)=Vol(S^3 minus L_E). (8) The first equality is already an equality in the rational pre-Bloch group; the source theorem proves that its boundary is zero. The geometric construction supplies the actual degree-one fundamental class which the earlier abstract source-regulator theorem did not identify. We compare the images in this COMMON number field; no injectivity of Bloch groups under field extension is assumed. Integral flattenings, integral torsion, preferred logarithmic peripheral lifts and a generic-meridian knot A-operator remain outside this statement. The class allows arbitrary finite branching and turn depth in the robust expression grammar. Its actual diagrams are retained-circle LINKS; it is not a theorem for arbitrary hyperbolic knots. No claim that every alternating link admits this exact four-port grammar is made. Extending to fillings still requires the original deformed source packet and its full complementary-color estimates. Those conditions must not be inferred solely from the complete positive source theorem proved here. For an arbitrary robust closed expression, first use the exact boundary cap-sum reduction. The remaining cylindrical factors have the actual complete hyperbolic metrics just constructed. Their sources multiply and their limits add; pure cap leaves retain their previously proved polynomial factors. This is a topology-compatible sum of exhibited geometric factor volumes, not a claim of a single complete hyperbolic structure on a connected sum. Audit: [strict support and literal colored-cell incidence](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume_results.json). The finite checks supplement the strict-maximum proof, ordered geometric cells, reversible disk cut and complete-cusp construction. They do not identify manifolds from sampled quantum values. The conclusion concerns the complete retained-circle link. It does not imply a knot-filling theorem or a theorem for arbitrary knots. Section 8 compares rational geometric Bloch classes using a common algebraic coordinate field, compatible face triangulations, opposite mirror orientations and a degree-one fundamental chain; it does not assert field-extension injectivity or an integral lift. **Long-filling extension, 29 October 2026:** the [uniform mixed-source gap](actual_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md), [complex packet](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md), and [actual marked deformation](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) now yield actual hyperbolic volume equality after independently sufficiently long signed integral fillings of any subset of auxiliary circles. The [assembly](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) retains all source normalizations and both parities. These full-twist fillings remain links; they cannot produce knots from the pure robust seed.

title: A whole-source variational limit for every positive Conway expression
text: # A whole-source variational limit for every positive Conway expression **Later geometric result, 29 October 2026:** the [actual cylindrical Conway theorem](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) now identifies this maximum with the complete hyperbolic volume for every retained cylindrical factor after cap-sum reduction. Its proof supplies the actual ordered cell incidence and complete cusps. Cap products keep their connected-sum scope; arbitrary knots and fillings are not included. The earlier geometric gap below is retained as the scope of this original variational argument. 29 October 2026. Every fixed expression in the actual complete-circle Conway class has a full-sequence exponential limit. The limit is the maximum of an explicit concave sum of ideal-tetrahedron volumes on a rational polytope. This uses the original source, at both parities, including all circle colors and repeated-root normal directions. The tetrahedral angle triples below are not yet a triangulation of the actual complement. Identifying their maximum with its hyperbolic volume remains a separate geometric task. In fact some expressions have zero exponential rate, so hyperbolicity cannot be inferred from their positive coefficients. ## 1. The actual expressions and the fixed rational polytope Use the literal four-port compilation and exposed original closure of [the Conway source theorem](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md). Write h_N=Rturn L_N, A_N=h_N^3, d=N-1 and M=floor(d/2). Fix an expression generated by A, genuine quarter-turn and product. Expand each A into its three h leaves and two product gates. Repeated copies are distinct vertices of this finite expression tree. Attach a real label x in [0,1] to every output wire. Define P_E by: * At an h leaf, 0<=x<=1/2. * At a turn with input x and output y, x+y=1. * At a product with inputs x,y and output z, max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1. * The final phi closure fixes its output label to 1. This is a compact rational polytope. Its exact level-d lattice points are integer wire labels satisfying the SAME homogeneous inequalities after multiplying all constants by d. In particular 2r<=d at a leaf is exactly r<=M, and a product has i+j<=d, not i+j<=N. Thus states at level N = (d P_E) intersect Z^(number of wires). (1) Every state has strictly positive weight. Its leaf factor is the actual coefficient a_(N,v)=N sum_(j=v)^M k_j s_(j+v)/(s_(j-v)s_v^2), s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), k_j=2 at paired nodes, 1 at an odd simple node. Its product factor is the actual full-Newton coefficient mu_(i,j,k)=s_(i+j)s_k/ (s_i s_j s_(k-i)s_(k-j)s_(i+j-k)). (2) Turn and closure factors equal one on their stated constraints. The exact positive partition Z_E,N is phi(E_N), not a comparison model. The previously proved physical identities identify it with the whole original raw source of the compiled ribbon diagram. ## 2. A uniform action on the entire polytope Put L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du on [0,1], extended continuously to both endpoints. Set g(x)=-2L(x)-2L(1/2-x), m(x,y,z)=L(x+y)+L(z)-L(x)-L(y) -L(z-x)-L(z-y)-L(x+y-z). Define A_E to be the sum of g over its leaves and m over its product gates. Turns contribute zero. This is one function on P_E with all shared labels retained; its factors are not maximized independently. Uniformly for every exact state with scaled labels r/d, log(weight)=N A_E(r/d)+O_E(log N). (3) For the leaf, z_j(v)=s_(j+v)/(s_(j-v)s_v^2) is increasing in j: z_(j+1)(v)/z_j(v) =sin(pi(j+v+1)/N)/sin(pi(j-v+1)/N)>=1. Indeed the difference of these sines is 2cos(pi(j+1)/N)sin(pi v/N)>=0 in the actual range. Therefore N z_M(v)<=a_(N,v)<=N^2 z_M(v). (4) The uniform estimate log s_r=N L(r/N)+O(log N), including endpoints, gives the claimed g action from (4). Here M/N differs from 1/2 by O(1/N), and r/N differs from r/d by O(1/N). The modulus of continuity of L changes N L by O(log N) under these shifts, even at sine zeros. The same estimate applied directly to (2) gives its m action. There are a fixed number of factors, proving (3). ## 3. Integer support supplies an all-level lower bound It is insufficient to approximate a maximum only along denominator subsequences. The exact support here is an additive semigroup in (d,wire labels): sums of two feasible integer labelings are feasible at the sum of their levels d. Every displayed constraint is linear and homogeneous in these variables, including 2r<=d and turn sums. Moreover a feasible integer labeling exists for EVERY d>=2 and every prescribed root coordinate r in [0,d]. Here is a constructive proof. At a seed h^3, distribute r among three integers <=floor(d/2); this is possible since 3floor(d/2)>=d. Choose the upper output index at both products. At a turn use the child coordinate d-r. At a product of two already compiled expressions, use child coordinates r and 0 and output r. All chosen product sums are <=d. This proves feasibility by induction, including r=d for the final closure. Take any rational y in P_E and a positive integer D such that Dy is an integer vector. For each residue modulo D choose d_r>=2 in that residue and a fixed feasible integer labeling b_r at level d_r. For all sufficiently large d in that residue, d=kD+d_r with k>=0, and n_d=k(Dy)+b_r is an exact integer state at level d. Its normalized label n_d/d tends to y as d tends to infinity through that residue. There are only finitely many residues. Thus every rational y is approached by actual states along the ENTIRE sequence of sufficiently large levels. Rational points are dense in the nonempty rational polytope P_E: express a point as a convex combination of rational vertices and approximate its coefficients by rational simplex coefficients. Continuity of A_E therefore lets one choose rational y arbitrarily close to its maximum value, even when a maximum is on a boundary. There are at most N to a fixed power states. Equation (3) gives the upper bound by max A_E. The single sequence n_d just constructed gives liminf at least A_E(y). Taking rational y with values approaching the maximum proves the unconditional full-source limit lim_(N->infinity) (1/N)log Z_E,N=max_(P_E) A_E. (5) No parity subsequence, Gaussian hypothesis, strict interior maximum, or lower-overlap conjecture is needed. Positivity and the additive integer support are what supply the every-level lower bound here. ## 4. A finite concave ideal-angle volume problem Let V(a,b,c) be the ideal-tetrahedron volume with dihedral angles pi a,pi b,pi c, for nonnegative a+b+c=1, including its continuous zero-volume boundary. Then pi g(x)=2V(x,1/2-x,1/2). For a product put p=z-x, q=z-y, r=x+y-z, w=1-x-y. They are nonnegative and p+q+2r+w=1. The exact identity is pi m(x,y,z)=V(p+r,q+r,w) +V(p,q,2r+w)+V(p+q,r,r+w). (6) It follows by substituting V=-pi sum L and L(1-t)=-L(t), as in the [cuboctahedral period proof](actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.md). All displayed triples have sum one on the whole allowed domain. Thus V_E=pi A_E is an explicitly prescribed sum of tetrahedral volumes with affine angles, and (5) becomes lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log Z_E,N=2 max_(P_E) V_E. (7) Each tetrahedral volume is concave on its angle simplex; consequently V_E is concave on P_E. This is a finite convex optimization problem for -V_E. Strictness or an interior maximizer requires its own check; the all-level limit (7) does not depend on either assertion. ## 5. Algebraic critical equations and the exact geometric gap On any selected face of P_E, omit angle terms identically zero there. At a critical point where the remaining angles are positive, write A_E=sum_b sigma_b L(ell_b(x)), with integer sigma_b and rational affine ell_b. For an integer basis vector v of that face's tangent space, constrained stationarity is exactly product_b (2sin(pi ell_b(x)))^[sigma_b dell_b(v)]=1. (8) The exponents are integers in the unreduced wire coordinates. Set u_j=exp(pi i x_j). Each 2sin(pi ell_b) is a Laurent expression in the u_j with coefficients in Q(i), since the only affine constants are integers and half-integers. The linear face equalities likewise become monomial equations. Clearing denominators makes (8) polynomial. The actual angle branches and positive sine signs remain selected; the resulting algebraic equations alone do not choose them. In particular an isolated complex solution of these finite equations has algebraic phase coordinates. Its displayed tetrahedral shapes, obtained from their angle sine rules, are algebraic as well. This is a precise finite algebraic critical-period construction. It does not by itself identify this circuit ideal with a knot's A-polynomial. The later [quotient-Hessian theorem](positive_source_algebraic_volume_period.md) removes the extra isolation hypothesis at a global maximum: after restricting to its minimal face and removing the rational flat kernel, the Hessian supplies isolation automatically. Thus all nonflat shapes at every robust source maximum are algebraic, even with boundary or nonunique wire coordinates. Its [conjugate-antisymmetrized symbol sum](actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.md) is moreover a rational Bloch class with this maximum as regulator. These statements still do not provide the actual manifold incidence. Nor do (6)--(8) supply the missing global face identifications: they give positive angle triples, not yet the actual edge/peripheral equations of the diagram complement. A future geometric comparison must use the [full source-volume certificate](source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md), including the absolute normalization and all angle tangent directions. Two calibrations clarify the scope. The seed closure phi(h_N^3) is the whole untwisted theta source, already proved to have actual volume 4v8; hence its maximum V_E is 2v8. But phi(Rturn(h_N^3)) is the constant Newton coefficient of h_N^3, exactly (N^2)^3=N^6. Its limit and the maximum in (7) are zero. No claim that every expression is hyperbolic can be appended to this variational theorem. Audit: [exact support and positive partition checks](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_positive_conway_variational_limit_results.json) supplement (1)--(8). They verify 800 additive integer support cases, 1008 all-residue approximations, and ten full positive-partition levels, including an independent whole-theta formula and the exact polynomial turned closures. Numerical rates are diagnostics, not the proof of (5). No manifold-volume claim for arbitrary Conway expressions follows from this variational result.

title: A common positive face radius gives the global channel maximum
status: Uniform all-channel rate and strict maximum
text: # A common positive face radius gives the global channel maximum 30 October 2026. This is a finite determinant/rate theorem for the original positive face polynomials. The exact marked coefficient interface is proved separately. No external filling-color packet or filled-knot equality is claimed here. ## 1. The original finite factors and one common radius Use the matrices and scalar normalization in [the exact positive circle](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md). Put d=N-1, a in {0,...,floor(d/2)}, s=d-2a, and mu=a/N. Write D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], P_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y), B_(N,a)(x,b,c,y)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_s(x,y). The fixed multiplicity k_a is between1 and2 and does not change a normalized logarithmic rate. The retained half-twist omega_a^epsilon has modulus1 for an integer channel; it must still be kept in a channel SUM. Each circle uses the SAME face radius for every shared face. Set the two original marked face variables u,v to zero, and put all other face radii in a fixed positive compact set. The actual simple white-face sphere has no matching edge between u,v, because their edge is the original MAIN cut. Consequently x,y are not both zero. Each triangle has at least one positive radius. If one outer radius vanishes, at least one of b,c is positive: otherwise three distinct faces would be u or v. These are exactly the nondegenerate patterns used below. The result also holds when all four radii are positive. ## 2. Uniform logarithmic determinant rate, including both endpoints Let c(t)=cos(pi t), E_b(t)=x+y+2b c(t)^2 +2c(t)sqrt[b^2 c(t)^2+b(x+y)+xy], lambda_b(t)=E_b(t)/(4c(t)^2). Then, uniformly over ALL integer a and the stated positive compact sets with their fixed zero pattern, (1/N)log D_a(x,b,y) = integral_0^mu log lambda_b(t) dt + o(1). (1) All logarithms in (1) are real. Here is a direct finite-matrix proof. Away from t=0,1/2, the actual diagonal and squared adjacent modulus converge uniformly, with error O(N^-1), to A_b(t)=b+(x+y)/(2c(t)^2), B_b(t)=[(x+y)^2-4xy c(t)^2]/(16c(t)^4). Thus lambda_b=(A_b+sqrt(A_b^2-4B_b))/2. No matrix of virtual size beyond the maximal folded channel is introduced. If b>0, every principal matrix is bounded below by bI. If x,y>0, the exact [sum gap](actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.md) H_-+H_+>=cos(pi/N)I gives the same uniform positive lower bound. On an interior index interval the matrices also have a uniform upper bound. Partition that interval into blocks of length ell tending to infinity with ell/N tending to zero. Removing each connecting adjacent entry is a rank-two perturbation. Both the original matrix and its block diagonal pinching lie between the same positive lower bound and a fixed upper bound. Eigenvalue interlacing, or integration of log det along this positive interpolation, bounds the log-determinant change by a constant times the number of removed edges. Within a block, freezing the coefficients changes operator norm by O(ell/N); the positive lower bound makes its log-determinant change O(ell^2/N). After a diagonal unitary gauge the frozen block is the real constant Jacobi matrix. Its eigenvalues are A_b+2sqrt(B_b)cos(j*pi/(ell+1)). Their logarithmic Riemann sum is (1/pi)integral_0^pi log(A_b+2sqrt(B_b)cos theta)dtheta =log[(A_b+sqrt(A_b^2-4B_b))/2]. For the last identity, factor the expression as lambda_b |1+sqrt(B_b)/lambda_b * exp(i theta)|^2; the second logarithm has mean zero by its convergent Fourier expansion. The positive spectral gap keeps the ratio below1 uniformly on this interior interval. The total block error is O(N/ell+ell), hence o(N). The same estimates allow a last shorter block, uniformly in a. For completeness the endpoint truncations are uniform, not a fixed-a argument. At either cut index a removed connecting edge has bounded size depending only on the chosen endpoint cutoff epsilon, and its rank-two cost is O_epsilon(1). A terminal block has a positive constant lower spectral bound and the Hadamard upper bound from the ACTUAL diagonal. Its log determinant is bounded in absolute value by C epsilon N(1+|log epsilon|)+O(log N) at the fold, and C epsilon N+O(1) at zero. Indeed the diagonal is at most C/[cos(n*pi/N)cos((n+1)*pi/N)]; summing its logarithm gives the displayed integrable endpoint bound through both parities. The limiting log lambda has the same integrable majorant. First let N increase, then let epsilon decrease. This proves uniform (1). The only remaining allowed case is b=0 and exactly one of x,y positive. Here D_a is a scalar multiple of det H_+ or det H_-, and the ACTUAL Cholesky pivots are p_(n-1)=sin(n*pi/N)/[cos(n*pi/N)sin((2n-1)*pi/N)]. Their exact product proves (1) directly by the same endpoint-truncated Riemann sums; its bulk ratio is x/(4cos(pi t)^2) or its y counterpart. This avoids using a positive spectral gap in this single-summand case. The empty determinant at a=0 is included. ## 3. The circle rate increases strictly to the fold Define I(v)=integral_0^v log(2sin(pi t))dt, J_mu(x,y)=integral_mu^(1-mu) log|x-exp(2pi i t)y|dt. The exact sine products, with their integrable endpoint logarithms, give uniformly in a (1/N)log beta_a = I(2mu)-2I(mu)+o(1), (1/N)log P_s(x,y) = J_mu(x,y)+o(1). (2) When x=y the second integrand has endpoint logarithmic singularities; the elementary sine-product comparison gives the same uniform o(1). If one outer radius is zero, the assertion is immediate from the single monomial. The positive coefficient identity fixes P_s>0. Combine (1),(2) to obtain the continuous uniform circle rate F_mu=2I(2mu)-4I(mu) +integral_0^mu [log lambda_b(t)+log lambda_c(t)]dt +J_mu(x,y). (3) For 0<mu<1/2, put D_xy(mu)=(x-y)^2+4xy sin(pi mu)^2. Direct differentiation, retaining the scalar beta and forced product, gives the cancellation partial_mu F_mu = log[E_b(mu)E_c(mu)/D_xy(mu)] >0. (4) Indeed the scalar derivative is4log(2cos(pi mu)), while the two determinant denominators multiply to16cos(pi mu)^4. The derivative of J is minus log D_xy. If xy>0, then E_b,E_c>=x+y and D_xy<(x+y)^2. If exactly one outer radius vanishes, at least one of b,c is positive, making at least one E strictly larger than x+y. Thus strictness holds in every actual pattern. Formula (3) is continuous at both endpoints even when the derivative at zero diverges. There is therefore a strict diagram-dependent gap on every region mu<=1/2-epsilon. For a fixed graph, multiplying the original factors at their shared radii and summing any polynomial number of channel choices preserves that exponential gap whenever at least one channel stays epsilon away from the fold. This upper estimate is at one common radius; it does not sum incompatible independent local optimizers. Near the fold (4) also gives the explicit classical quadratic gap. Write A=x+y>0 and T_b=sqrt[bA+xy], T_c=sqrt[cA+xy]. At mu=1/2-delta, partial_mu F_mu = 2pi delta(T_b+T_c)/A+O(delta^2), F_(1/2)-F_(1/2-delta) = pi(T_b+T_c)delta^2/A+O(delta^3). (5) The coefficient is strictly positive in the actual patterns. This is a statement about the limiting action. Uniform finite relative asymptotics on delta of order N^-1/2, and cancellation of the retained half-twist phases in the whole channel sum, require a further proof; the o(1) in (1)--(3) is NOT used as such a relative estimate. ## 4. Scope of the whole-source upper bound The [exact marked coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md) makes every coefficient nonnegative before the explicit half-twist scalar. Evaluating its polynomial at the SAME positive radius bounds the selected coefficient by that value divided by its prescribed radius monomial. Equations (1)--(4) then control the entire finite channel sum from above, with all original scalar factors and only polynomial counting cost. The absolute endpoint value is computed separately from the actual facet coning and marked source normalization. A positive central coefficient with that value supplies a lower bound for an UNTWISTED channel sum, as assembled in the [complete untwisted theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). Signed half twists require a noncancellation theorem. External crossing-circle colors needed for long Dehn fillings are not the internal a labels in this note and are not estimated here. Focused audit: [original finite channel factors](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_channel_rate.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_channel_rate_results.json). It checks six symbolic identities, 704 all-label circles, 1408 original determinants, 528 independent Newton comparisons, 176 exact LDL products and 576 adjacent-channel ratios, including 64 maximal folds of each parity. The 72 rate samples are diagnostics only. No finite-window signed Gaussian or external-color theorem follows from the channel-rate estimate.

title: The positive face coefficient has one global saddle
text: # The positive face coefficient has one global saddle 30 October 2026. The coefficient below has an exact compact torus integral and a uniform finite Gaussian asymptotic through both folded parities. The determinant contraction proves the global angular gap. This is a coefficient theorem; its identification with the original source uses the separately checked marked face-grid identity. It does not estimate external filling colors. Setting the two marked face variables to zero uses only a connected geometric certificate; it needs neither the finite-r Bessel chart nor a one-main-component hypothesis. ## 1. The polynomial and its prescribed coefficient Fix the labeled original right-angled matching graph with R crossing circles and R+2 white faces. Let u,v be the two marked faces. Set their variables to zero. Give the other R faces positive variables l_f. For each actual label vector a=(a_i), let P_N(l)=product_i [D_ai(x_i,b_i,y_i)D_ai(x_i,c_i,y_i) P_si(x_i,y_i)], s_i=N-1-2a_i, d=N-1. Every argument here is its original shared face variable, including its specified zero when the face is u or v. The [local source factorization](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md) proves that P_N is homogeneous of degree dR with nonnegative coefficients. The coefficient of interest is A_N=[product_(f!=u,v) l_f^d] P_N(l). (1) All scalar factors k_ai beta_ai^2, original half twists, and the exact finite-grid measure are outside P_N and must be restored by the source identity. They are not absorbed in A_N. Assume S=sum_i s_i=o(N), with the graph fixed. Both maximal-fold parities and arbitrary integer near-fold label sequences are included. Let l^geom be the positive finite white-circle normal coefficients from the certified packing with u,v represented by parallel lines. Fix one finite face variable to1 by homogeneity, leaving n=R-1 logarithmic variables. ## 2. An exact global determinant contraction For any positive semidefinite matrices X_1,...,X_t with M=sum X_j>0, put A_j=M^-1/2 X_j M^-1/2. Then sum A_j=I. For real theta_j put B(theta)=sum_j exp(i theta_j) A_j. This is a contraction: Vz=(A_j^1/2 z)_j is an isometry and B=V* diag(exp(i theta_j))V. Cyclicity of trace gives exactly Tr(I-B*B)=sum_(j<k)|exp(i theta_j)-exp(i theta_k)|^2 Tr(A_j A_k). (2) Every pair trace is nonnegative. Since the squared singular values lambda_l of B are at most1, log lambda_l<=lambda_l-1 proves |det B|<=exp[-(1/2)sum_(j<k)|exp(i theta_j) -exp(i theta_k)|^2 Tr(A_j A_k)]. (3) A zero determinant satisfies the same bound by continuity. No limiting matrix, independent-entry positivity, or commutativity is required. Apply (3) to each original D_a, with its nonzero summands bI, xH_-/2,yH_+/2. When all three are present, the two pair traces involving the identity summand have lower bounds cN from the exact bulk-square argument in the [curvature theorem](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md). For a two-variable220/022 determinant its single pair trace has the same bound. For202, with b=0, the pair trace is precisely its log-radius variance; the exact positive-polynomial variance proof gives cN. A one-variable200/002 determinant is a monomial and has no angular gap. All constants are uniform on positive compact radius sets near l^geom. The resulting active pair graph connects all R finite faces. Indeed each shaded triangle equates its finite-face potentials, and the [exact rank proof](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) shows that deleting u,v leaves a connected graph. The forced polynomials P_s also have nonnegative coefficients, so their modulus ratio on the torus is at most1 and cannot weaken (3). Consequently, after fixing one phase, |P_N(l exp(i theta))/P_N(l)| <=exp[-c_D N dist(theta,0)^2] (4) on the entire n-dimensional torus, with its usual periodic distance. To see the uniform comparison, use a fixed spanning tree: the complex unit phase difference of any vertex from the fixed vertex is at most the sum of the edge differences along its path. Compactness then compares their squared sum with squared torus distance. The only common zero is the constant phase. Every edge row has literal coefficients +1,-1, so there are no other angular aliases. ## 3. The finite positive critical radius In logarithmic finite-face coordinates define Phi_N(z)=log P_N(l^geom exp z)-d sum_f z_f. (5) The actual circle-center angle force at the fold gives N^-1 partial Phi_N(0) ->0. (6) For each shaded triangle the determinant derivative tends to sum_j theta_j dlog l_j/(2pi). The consecutive center triangles give angle sum2pi at each finite white circle, so the total is1 per finite face; d/N tends to1. The retained P_s derivatives are O(S), and hence vanish after division by N. This uses the uniform original finite angle-force theorem, not independent local maximization. The finite Hessian is real positive on the fixed gauge slice, and its bounds are c_D N I<=H_N<=C_D N I on a fixed small real neighborhood. Its fixed higher derivatives are O(N) on a uniform complex neighborhood: preconditioning a D determinant gives a small perturbation of I, while near-fold forced roots stay separated from the positive radius compact. These are the same finite curvature and holomorphic bounds already proved. The quantitative implicit-function argument now gives a real critical radius l_N=l^geom exp z_N with z_N=o(1). Use the Hessian at zero as preconditioner: the normalized gradient error tends to zero, and the Newton remainder is O(|z|^2) with uniform constant, so contraction on a ball of radius C|partial Phi_N(0)|/N gives existence and uniqueness there. Strict convexity of log P_N on the gauge slice implies that no other real critical radius exists. Strictness follows directly from the positive determinant monomial support and the connected active pair graph. Let H_N be the Hessian at this actual finite critical radius. ## 4. The exact coefficient integral and its nonzero asymptotic The Cauchy coefficient formula, with one variable fixed by homogeneity, is exactly A_N=P_N(l_N)/product_f l_N,f^d *(2pi)^(-n) integral_[−pi,pi]^n [P_N(l_N exp(i theta))/P_N(l_N)] exp[-i d sum_f theta_f] dtheta. (7) There is no unknown source-cycle coefficient in this integral for A_N. Equation (4) makes the part outside any fixed small neighborhood exponentially small relative to its prefactor. At the origin the exact critical equation removes the linear term and the exponent equals -(1/2)theta^T H_N theta + O(N|theta|^3). Uniform fourth and higher derivative bounds, rescaling by N^-1/2, and symmetry of the Gaussian give A_N= P_N(l_N)/product_f l_N,f^d /[(2pi)^(n/2) sqrt(det H_N)] *[1+O(N^-1)]. (8) The cubic term is odd, so its first Gaussian integral is zero; its square and the quartic term cost O(N^-1). Gaussian domination from (4) controls the remaining expansion and tails. The square root is positive. Thus the coefficient is strictly positive for all sufficiently large N in this near-fold window, and has the displayed global relative asymptotic. This proves more than a constructed local contour statement. ## 5. Absolute value and remaining source tasks The [absolute facet-coning computation](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md) of the endpoint determinant action is 2pi lim (1/N)log[P_N(l^geom)/product_f(l_f^geom)^d] =2 Vol(Q)=Vol(Y_D). (9) For clarity its geometric input is explicit: each white cyclic-face pyramid contributes the sum of Lambda(theta_j/2), and each shaded contact triangle coned to the marked ideal vertex contributes the sum of Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2). These actual coned facets tile Q. The source Legendre potential is twice this sum, with additive constant fixed by the exact single-positive-variable Cholesky product. This uses the absolute marked action proof, not a volume chosen to normalize P_N. The shift z_N=o(1) changes the normalized saddle value by o(1), and the Hessian prefactor is subexponential. All exact circle scalars beta_ai also have normalized log tending to zero when S=o(N). Therefore the original fixed near-fold sector, ONCE the exact marked coefficient identity is restored, has absolute rate Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). Its retained half-twist scalar has modulus1 but may affect sums of different sectors. Combining this coefficient theorem with a common-radius all-channel upper bound gives a whole-source equality for the untwisted complete source, since all its sectors are nonnegative in the specified common normalization. The [complete untwisted source theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md) performs this combination with the exact measure and scalar. Signed sums and mixed external filling colors remain distinct tasks. No filled-knot volume equality is asserted. Focused audit: [finite determinant contraction and original coefficients](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle_results.json). It checks 256 original matrix torus cases, 96 pair traces, and 16 literal tetrahedral-graph coefficients against exact finite Cauchy quadrature. Gaussian profile errors are diagnostics; the global graph-wide estimate is proved above. The coefficient theorem does not settle the whole signed channel sum or external colors.

title: An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors
status: Exponential actual-grid interpolation; fixed complex faces
text: # An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors 30 October 2026. The construction below uses analytic contractions on shrinking disks, then the actual positive finite recurrence. It produces an even holomorphic fold interpolation whose error on the original channel grid is exponentially small, uniformly on a fixed complex face-radius neighborhood. Formal WKB existence alone is not used. This is a local complete-circle factor theorem; the shared coefficient period and the ordinary-color alias subsets remain separate. ## 1. Statement with the original finite anchor Fix a compact set of positive face radii in any one of the actual zero patterns of the [signed source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Zero faces stay zero. Set B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M, delta_a=(d-2a)/(2N), delta_min=s0/(2N), h=1/N. Use the explicit analytic functions E_b,J_b,a_b,V of [the fixed-fold theorem](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md), equations(1),(2). In particular V is even, V(0)=0 and V''(0)=2pi(T_b+T_c)/(x+y)>0. The T_b=0 triangle is treated as the exact constant-pivot case, with J_b=1. There are fixed positive delta_*,rho,c,C, a complex logarithmic radius neighborhood O_rho of the given real compact, and even holomorphic functions H_N(delta;l) on |delta|<2delta_*, l in O_rho, such that H_N(0;l)=0 and H_N(delta;l)=-N V(delta;l) -(1/2)Log[J_b(delta;l)J_c(delta;l)]+O(N^-1). (1) The bound is uniform on smaller closed disks and neighborhoods, with all fixed derivatives by Cauchy estimates. Define the specified finite-N interpolation mathcal B_N(delta;l)=B_(N,M)(l) exp[H_N(delta;l)-H_N(delta_min;l)]. (2) The original B_(N,M) is retained exactly; it is a holomorphic unit on O_rho by positive-matrix preconditioning and the original forced factor. Then for EVERY original integer a with delta_min<=delta_a<=delta_*, B_(N,a)(l)/mathcal B_N(delta_a;l)=1+O(e^(-cN)), uniformly l in O_rho. (3) The right side of (2) is even in delta. No noninteger-dimensional matrix is introduced. For an actual retained half twist, the factor omega_M^epsilon exp[pi i epsilon N(delta^2-delta_min^2)] (4) agrees exactly with omega_a^epsilon on this grid, including its common q^(d^2/2) phase. Thus (2)--(4) preserve the entire local root complete-circle factor. They do not interpolate a different generic-q germ or ordinary small-color coupon. ## 2. A regular analytic equation in the squared fold variable First consider one triangle with T_b>0. Let z denote the pivot coordinate (N/2-a)/N. On a fixed small complex disk the functions E(z)=E_b(z), D(z)=(x+y)^2-4xy sin^2(pi z) obey E(z)E(-z)=D(z). Write B0(w)=[E(z)+E(-z)]/2, C0(w)=[E(z)-E(-z)]/(2z), t(w)=tan(pi z)/z, w=z^2. All are holomorphic in w near zero; t and C0 are units. Seek a reflection-preserving approximate pivot in the form e_v(z)=E(z) exp[z v(z^2)], (5) where v is holomorphic in w. Thus e_v(z)e_v(-z)=D(z) EXACTLY. Clear the actual recurrence residual as in the fixed-fold proof: Rcal_v(z,h)=tan(pi(z+h))e_v(z)+tan(pi z)e_v(-z-h) -[tan(pi(z+h))+tan(pi z)] [A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))]. (6) It vanishes at z=0,-h and is odd under z -> -z-h. Set z=zeta-h/2. Division therefore defines a holomorphic function of w=zeta^2: G_h(v)(w)= Rcal_v(zeta-h/2,h) /[zeta(zeta^2-h^2/4)]. (7) The values at the apparent three divisors in (7) are their removable limits. Holomorphic divisibility follows successively by the two zeros and centered oddness, including h=0 where the zeros coalesce. It does not require estimating separate singular quotients. At h=0 and v=0, G_0(0)=0. Its linearization is multiplication by the nonzero analytic function L(w)=2t(w)C0(w), L(0)=4pi^2 T_b. (8) This normalization resolves the formal fold pole in the analytic equation; it does not cancel the peripheral factors of the finite four-component operator. ## 3. The single-loss analytic estimate Here is the estimate that controls arbitrarily many corrections. Use sup norms on w disks, with radii in a fixed compact interval 0<R_1<=R<=R_0. For small v and 0<Delta<R-R_1, with h small enough that Ch<Delta, analytic differentiation gives ||D G_h(v)-L||_(R to R-Delta) <=C(||v||_R+h/Delta). (9) All constants are uniform on a fixed complex radius neighborhood. There is only ONE loss of analytic radius, not two independent derivatives in z. We give the cancellation explicitly. Write the even and odd parts of (5) as e_v(z)=B0(w)+w F_v(w)+z[C0(w)+G_v(w)]. Both F_v,G_v are pointwise analytic functions of (w,v(w)), and F_v=C0 v+O(v^2), G_v=B0 v+O(v^2). For example they follow directly from cosh(zv) and sinh(zv)/z, which are analytic in (w,v). For zeta^2=w put a=zeta-h/2, b'=zeta+h/2 and w_-=a^2,w_+=b'^2. The v-dependent part of (7) is exactly t_+ F_-+t_- F_+ +(h/(2zeta))(t_- F_+-t_+ F_-) +(1/zeta)(t_+ G_--t_- G_+), (10) where subscripts indicate evaluation at w_+ or w_-. The same formula with pointwise derivatives of F,G holds for D G_h. Every apparent divided difference is controlled by [K(w_+)-K(w_-)]/zeta =2h integral_0^1 K'(w_-+t(w_+-w_-))dt. (11) The segment stays in the outer disk when Ch<Delta. Cauchy's bound for K' costs Delta^-1. Comparing the first line of (10) with its h=0 value uses the same first-derivative estimate, since |w_+-w|+|w_--w|<=Ch. The nonlinear h=0 difference from (8) costs O(||v||). These facts prove (9), including w=0 by holomorphy. ## 4. Exponentially accurate analytic pivots The explicit first correction already proved in the fixed-fold note provides the starting function v^(0)(w)=h a_b(z)/z, w=z^2. It is holomorphic and O(h); the joint residual divisibility there gives G_h(v^(0))=O(h^2) on one fixed disk. Iterate v^(m+1)=v^(m)-L^-1 G_h(v^(m)) (12) on nested w disks, losing Delta=Kh at each step. Choose fixed K sufficiently large, then h sufficiently small. Equation (9) makes the map in (12) a contraction with Lipschitz factor at most1/2 between consecutive disks, as long as ||v||<=C_1 h. The first change is O(h^2), and subsequent changes decrease geometrically. Their sum is O(h^2), so that norm condition closes by induction. More explicitly put R_m=R_0-m Delta and T(v)=v-L^-1 G_h(v). Then v^(m) is defined on the disk of radius R_m. On the next disk, v^(m+1)-v^(m)=T(v^(m))-T(v^(m-1)), with the previous iterate restricted to R_m. Estimate (9) therefore gives ||v^(m+1)-v^(m)||_(R_(m+1))<= (1/2)||v^(m)-v^(m-1)||_(R_m). This is a contraction between nested analytic domains, not an assertion that translation is bounded on one unchanged disk. Perform m=floor(c_0/h) steps, with c_0 small enough that all disks still contain one fixed smaller disk. Keep one more radius margin to evaluate the final residual. The resulting analytic v_N obeys v_N=v^(0)+O(h^2), ||G_h(v_N)||<=C e^(-c_1/h). (13) Each operation is analytic in the face parameters, and all estimates are uniform there. The finite iteration count may depend on N; no analyticity in a varying quantum level is claimed. All functions are real on positive real radii and real w. Put e_N^*(z)=E(z)exp[z v_N(z^2)]. (14) It preserves reflection exactly, has the original first correction, and its ACTUAL Riccati residual is exponentially small on a fixed complex z disk. The removable divisions in (7) only multiply it by bounded analytic factors. For T_b=0 take e_N^*=A exactly. ## 5. Match the actual finite pivots, including complex face radii Choose a fixed real cutoff 2delta_0 within the disk of (14). Start the ACTUAL physical recurrence at the nearest k0 to 2delta_0 N, and estimate only k<=delta_0 N. At real positive radii the original pivots have A<=e_a<=2A+4b. Also e_N^*(k/N)/A>=exp(c k/N) for sufficiently large N in a nonconstant triangle. Consequently the exact error multiplier is bounded by [tan(k theta)/tan((k+1)theta)] exp[-c(k+1)/N]. (15) This is the same source-derived positive contraction as before. The initial error is bounded, and its propagation to k<=delta_0 N is O(e^(-c_2 N)). The sum of exponentially small local residuals remains exponentially small, with at most a polynomial loss. The matching extends to a FIXED complex face neighborhood, not just to a shrinking neighborhood. At each original principal matrix, positive-summand preconditioning gives M_j(l)=M_j(l_real)^(1/2)(I+E)M_j(l_real)^(1/2), ||E||<=C rho, uniformly j,N. The last inverse-entry formula then gives the original Schur-pivot ratio e_a(l)/e_a(l_real)=1+O(rho) uniformly, with no lower eigenvalue assumption beyond the stated positive matrices. The same bound holds for (14) by its uniform analytic unit bounds. Thus each complex error multiplier is at most exp(C rho) times (15). Over the entire finite interval the extra cost is at most exp(C rho N). Choose rho FIRST below both the initial-damping and analytic-residual exponential rates. It follows that e_a(l)/e_N^*((N/2-a)/N;l)=1+O(e^(-c_3 N)) (16) uniformly in the smaller complex face neighborhood and at EVERY physical pivot in the chosen real window, including the two parity endpoints. This step identifies the constructed analytic function with the actual polynomial source. No choice among homogeneous recurrence solutions has been assumed. ## 6. An analytic discrete primitive with the exact folded anchor Apply the construction to the two actual triangles. Their exact reflection makes the marked logarithm ell_N(z)=Log[e_(b,N)^*(z)e_(c,N)^*(z)/D(z)] odd and holomorphic on a fixed disk. Moreover ell_N=V'+h(a_b+a_c)+O(h^2), (17) uniformly and holomorphically. We now construct the logarithm of the channel product itself with exponential precision, instead of summing a finite-order Euler--Maclaurin error. Let A_h f(z)=h^-1 integral_(-h/2)^(h/2) f(z+t)dt. It preserves odd analytic functions. On nested z disks its difference from the identity has norm at most Ch/Delta. Start f^(0)=ell_N and iterate f^(m+1)=f^(m)+ell_N-A_h f^(m), losing Delta=Kh at every step. The first change is O(h^2), by the centered integral and bounded second derivatives. The same geometric contraction argument as in (12), now linear, gives an odd analytic f_N with f_N=ell_N+O(h^2), A_h f_N=ell_N+O(e^(-c_4 N)). (18) Define H_N(z)=-h^-1 integral_0^z f_N(t)dt. It is even, has value zero at zero, and obeys H_N(z+h/2)-H_N(z-h/2) =-ell_N(z)+O(e^(-c_4 N)). (19) Equations (17),(18) give exactly (1), since integral_0^z(a_b+a_c)=(1/2)Log[J_b(z)J_c(z)]. For adjacent ACTUAL channel indices the forced product contributes exactly D at the midpoint, and the two original pivots contribute their reciprocals. By (16) their ratio is exp[-ell_N(midpoint)] with exponentially small relative error. Compare this with (19) and sum at most O(N) steps from the physical maximal channel. The resulting error is still O(e^(-cN)). At the starting index (2) uses B_(N,M) EXACTLY and delta_min=s0/(2N). This proves (3). ## 7. What the theorem supplies and what it does not The comparison (3) is exponentially accurate on the actual channel grid, uniformly for fixed complex face radii, while (2) is even and holomorphic in a fixed fold disk. It therefore supplies the local interpolation input that a fixed-frequency Fourier contour argument requires. It is substantially stronger than a real-grid relative O(N^-1) approximation. Its phase and amplitude are those of the actual finite source, with all beta, forced factors, parity offsets and half twists retained. The full shared-face coefficient must still be assembled with its original Cauchy period, angular tails and finite channel endpoints. The entire complete-image core must then be distinguished from the nonempty ordinary-color subsets in the exact external reflection identity. No global alias gap, filled-knot conclusion, or generic-q normal theorem is inferred here. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.py) and its [recorded results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation_results.json) check 20 symbolic identities and 24 complex-face residual identities. Numerical analytic-iteration prototypes are compared with the original beta/D/P factors: four pivot cases through N=1024 and eight complete-circle comparisons at both parities, including fixed complex face parameters. These finite projections are diagnostics of the construction; they are not premises for the uniform exponential estimate proved above. No full mixed-color packet, ordinary-subset gap, or generic-q normal claim follows from this interpolation theorem.

title: The actual face factor on a fixed real fold interval
status: Exact finite difference period; fixed real fold packet
text: # The actual face factor on a fixed real fold interval 30 October 2026. An analytic first continuant correction improves the folded relative estimate to O(N^-1) on a FIXED real interval. The action and displayed amplitude extend holomorphically across the fold. This does not by itself continue the actual finite-degree source, or control its Fourier transform with an exponentially accurate error. An exact reflected finite sequence is proved separately below using the original large q-Hahn numerator. ## 1. Actual finite factors and analytic functions Use the original D_a, beta_a, P_s and B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y) of the [signed source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). The radii are in one of its fixed actual nonnegative patterns, with positive entries in a compact set. In particular A=x+y>0 and T_b+T_c>0, where T_b^2=bA+xy and T_c^2=cA+xy. Put d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M and h=1/N. On a fixed sufficiently small complex z disk choose the square roots at their positive value at zero and define D(z)=A^2-4xy sin^2(pi z), E_b(z)=A+2b sin^2(pi z) +2sin(pi z)sqrt[T_b^2+b^2 sin^2(pi z)], J_b(z)=cos(pi z)sqrt[T_b^2+b^2 sin^2(pi z)]/T_b, a_b(z)=(1/2) partial_z log J_b(z). (1) If T_b=0, define instead E_b=A, J_b=1 and a_b=0; this is the exact single-summand case. Define the c functions in the same way. All these are holomorphic on a disk uniform over the radius compact. The E functions and J functions are nonzero there. Direct algebra gives E_b(z)E_b(-z)=D(z), J_b(-z)=J_b(z), a_b(-z)=-a_b(z). Consequently the following action is holomorphic and even, with V(0)=0: V'(z)=Log[E_b(z)E_c(z)/D(z)], V''(0)=2pi(T_b+T_c)/A>0. (2) The logarithm in (2) is zero at zero. This fixes the branch and the additive constant from the actual source, not from an interpolated color index. ## 2. Analytic cancellation of the first correction For the actual scaled Schur pivot e_a=(beta_a D_a)/(beta_(a-1)D_(a-1)) write z=(N/2-a)/N. Its exact recurrence is e(z)=(1+tau)[A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))] -tau D(z+h)/e(z+h), tau=tan(pi z)/tan(pi(z+h)). (3) Equation (3) denotes the original sequence only at its specified physical lattice. Define a holomorphic approximation on the disk by e_b^*(z,h)=E_b(z) exp[h a_b(z)]. (4) It obeys the exact reflection e_b^*(z,h)e_b^*(-z,h)=D(z). Clear the denominator in its recurrence residual, using this reflection: Rcal(z,h)=tan(pi(z+h)) e_b^*(z,h) +tan(pi z)e_b^*(-z-h,h) -[tan(pi(z+h))+tan(pi z)] [A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))]. (5) This is holomorphic jointly in z,h near zero. Its values at z=0 and z=-h are zero, because e_b^*(0,h)=A. Therefore Rcal=z(z+h)F(z,h) with F holomorphic.
