A finite rigorous upper certificate and the width-nine margin The bound B_*<81/100 has a direct finite interval-arithmetic certificate, described explicitly here so it is reproducible as a proof rather than as sampled evidence. In variable t in[1,3], put u(t)=asin sqrt((t^2-1)/8). For a rational interval [a,b] in[1,3], (t+1) is increasing and sqrt((t+1)(3-t)) is decreasing. Therefore rho(u(t)) <= K(a,b) =(b+1)/2 * [2+sqrt((a+1)(3-a))]. Divide [1,3] into512 equal rational intervals. This gives the EXACT analytical upper sum B_* <= (1/pi) sum_[a,b] [u(b)-u(a)] log K(a,b). (9) Outward-rounded Arb evaluation at100-bit precision encloses the right side in [0.80908894192172909372913834 +/- 5e-26] <81/100. Only a fixed finite sum of square roots, asin, log and pi is evaluated; no large-N experiment enters this certificate. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.py) reconstructs the upper sum and proves the strict comparison by its enclosing interval. For the complete augmented rate A_s=V_s/(2pi), put j_0=v_8/pi. Its exact alias margin is g_s=A_s-(s-1)j_0 =j_0-(2s/pi) integral_0^(pi/s) (pi/s-v)sec(v)dv. (10) For alpha=pi/s<1, cos v>=1-v^2/2 gives g_s >= j_0-pi/s -pi^3/[12s^3(1-pi^2/(2s^2))]. (11) Use pi<22/7 and the first32 alternating terms of G=sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k/(2k+1)^2 as a rational LOWER bound for Catalan's constant; j_0=4G/pi. At s=9 the resulting rational lower bound is greater than0.812633708, hence greater than13/16 and81/100. The loss in (11) decreases with s>=9. Consequently g_s>B_* for EVERY odd s>=9. (12) This strictly improves the previous threshold25. The same constants do not prove the condition at s=3,5,7. ## 6. Transfer to the ENTIRE actual source and the remaining widths Every original auxiliary color is already covered by the exact two-band identities: high colors are c_(N,h)+RP_(N,h), low colors are pure (-1)^N RP_(N,j), including even j=N/2. The global coherent core bound remains j_0, with a strict macroscopic-color contraction. Every term containing m>=1 aliases therefore has upper rate (s-m)j_0+mB_* <=(s-1)j_0+B_* < A_s for odd s>=9. The full value-plus-normal functional costs only a polynomial, and the fixed subset count2^s is harmless. The all-core term outside a fixed cusp corridor has its separately proved strict gap. This proves the SAME entire-color-cube source gap as the old global theorem at EVERY odd s>=9. All subsequent analytic inputs were already proved for every fixed odd s>=5: the exact even complex high-window packet, whole filling Fourier endpoint/current bounds, nonzero unit-charge sum, original normalization, and the actual geometric filling construction. Thus they transfer unchanged once their long-slope threshold is increased as necessary. The original full volume equality consequently extends to every fixed odd s>=9 with all independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes. No width or slope is allowed to grow with N. For s=5 and7 the present phase-free per-alias margin test remains insufficient; at s=3 the old limiting margin is exactly zero and its local corridor alias estimate was also only proved for s>=5. Those are TWO distinct remaining gates. Extending the theorem there needs a stronger coherent alias/source estimate, not a changed declaration of the existing condition. No fabricated all-width conclusion is inferred from (8). ## 7. Why another constant improvement in this termwise route is insufficient The monic bound used above is exponentially sharp at the actual endpoint z=-2. This identifies exactly which ABSOLUTE-TERM step must be replaced to reach the remaining widths; it is not a claim that the full coherent alias P_h has this rate or that the whole source fails to cancel. For l=floor(N/2)-1 one has log|p_l(-2)|=N B_*+O(1). (13) Here is a direct uniform proof. Use tau=l/N and epsilon=1/N in the literal companion (2), and write it as T_epsilon(tau). Its leading eigenvalues lambda(tau),sigma(tau) can be chosen smoothly on the WHOLE closed interval[0,1/2], with lambda(0)=-4, sigma(0)=0, |lambda(tau)|=rho(pi tau)>=4, |sigma(tau)|<=|lambda(tau)|, |lambda(tau)-sigma(tau)|>=4. (14) The last inequality follows from the explicit discriminant in section2. There is no equality of the two eigenvalue moduli in the open interval: for u>0 and u<pi/2 the normalized d_(-2) has nonzero imaginary part, whereas two roots of equal modulus and positive real product would have real sum. Their moduli meet only at the terminal endpoint, where their eigenvalues remain distinct. Thus the branch starting at -4 is the dominant branch throughout; no hidden exchange of expanding channels is used. Take the uniformly invertible eigenframe S(tau)=[[lambda,sigma],[1,1]]. Taylor expansion of the explicit smooth companion gives S(tau+epsilon)^(-1)T_epsilon(tau)S(tau) =diag(lambda,sigma)+epsilon A(tau)+O(epsilon^2), with all coefficients and two derivatives uniformly bounded. An explicit bounded off-diagonal matrix X, determined by X_ij=-A_ij/(D_i-D_j), makes the near-identity change I+epsilon X diagonal through first order. The resulting matrix is diag(lambda+epsilon A_11,sigma+epsilon A_22)+O(epsilon^2). Divide each step by d_1=lambda+epsilon A_11. Its normalized form is diag(1,r_tau)+O(epsilon^2), with |r_tau|<=1+Cepsilon. All normalized products therefore have uniformly bounded norm. The original initial vector (p_0,p_(-1))=(1,0) has first eigen-coordinate -1/4+O(epsilon). At the first step the second coordinate is O(epsilon), because sigma(0)=0. Over at most N/2 steps the O(epsilon^2) residual changes the first coordinate by O(epsilon), and keeps the second O(epsilon). The first physical coordinate consequently has a uniformly nonzero bounded prefactor times product d_1. Finally log|product d_1|=sum_j log rho(pi j/N)+O(1) =N I(l/N)+O(1). This proves (13), including the endpoint of equal moduli without an inverse eigenvalue-modulus gap. The proof applies equally to bar p_l. Now choose the ACTUAL h=floor(N/2) and the top term l=h-1 in (1). Its Gaussian coefficient is EXACTLY [2h-1 choose 2h-1]_Q=1, and its other displayed coefficient is a unit phase. Therefore any termwise-absolute estimate of the expansion (1) has rate at least B_* already from this single EXACT monic term. Since g_7 and g_5 are both smaller than B_*, this specific route cannot remove those widths by a sharper frozen-radius constant or a better estimate of that term. That comparison can also be certified without a numerical limiting fit: rho>=4 everywhere and rho>=5 on[pi/6,pi/3]. The latter follows from its displayed unimodal (1+sin theta+cos theta)^2 expression and the two explicit endpoint values, both greater than5. Hence B_* >= (log5)/6+(log4)/3 > .73. On the other hand sec v>=1 in (10) gives g_s<=j_0-pi/s. The elementary bounds G<11/12 and pi>157/50 give j_0<1.17, so g_5,g_7<1.17-157/350<.73. The finite interval audit checks the two endpoint and logarithmic comparisons with outward rounding. This is an obstruction to the STATED ABSOLUTE-TERM METHOD, not to the actual source. A further improvement must combine the P_h terms coherently, or pair the complete alias with the other boxes and the original Phi_2 functional before estimating. The exact Frobenius/ circle-source pairing under investigation is eligible for that task; deleting the alias or a normal jet is not. ## 8. Parity of the number of boxes: the even-width link statement The same proof applies to every fixed INTEGER s>=9, if even widths are stated as LINKS rather than knots. This is a source/parity audit, not an inference that a link is a knot. The exact unwrapped-degree and Phi_2 product identities use the original cups, ordinary caps and ONE marked cap and hold for any integer box count. The only use of oddness in their topological conclusion is the component count: following the main strand advances its box label by2 modulo s. Thus there are gcd(s,2) main components. With all crossing circles present the augmented diagram has s+gcd(s,2) components; after their prescribed fillings it has gcd(s,2) main components. In particular an even s gives a two-component pretzel link. The analytic checks are likewise independent of oddness of s: * The complete polynomial is the SAME z_N and the source is the SAME full-Hermite Phi_2(z_N^s). The coherent inner bounds have no s in them. The enclosing-circle saddle has s j'(eta_s)=1 and alpha=pi/s in(0,pi/2) for every integer s>2. Its two Gaussian constants are nonzero and the higher winding bound is unchanged. * The mixed packet remains exactly even in EACH color. The complex saddle Hessian and the real color curvature are nonzero for s>2. Local source replacement uses a strictly positive alias margin; (12) supplies it for all integer s>=9. * The exact filling formula is applied once per port. Under every unit charge reflection both m_i and its sinh factor change sign. Its level character is (-1)^((s+sum_i m_i)(N-1))=1, because sum_i m_i is congruent to s modulo2. This conclusion does not require s odd. All endpoint/tail estimates depend on the fixed number of ports and continue verbatim. The original LINK normalization is already proved in [the complete source-normalization theorem](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), section3: a cut partial trace is a scalar Hopf endomorphism of the remaining simple V_N regardless of connectivity. Thus the same single-cut reduced Kashaev link value has the modulus of the raw source. Its enhancement sign is (-1)^((N-1)(c-1)) with the ACTUAL component count c. There is still only one modified dimension if that optional convention is used, not one per main component. The literal port matrices, reversed-cap ordering, shaded/white face geometry, and primitive auxiliary filling equations also do not use oddness. For even width the two main-component meridians remain noncentral parabolic. The general geometric completion theorem keeps BOTH unfilled cusps complete; it does not collapse them to one. Consequently, with the same sufficiently long independently signed fixed twists, the source and volume equality extend to the original single-cut reduced two-component pretzel LINK for every fixed even s>=10. The knot conclusion is the odd s>=9 part. No assertion for a normalization that modifies every component independently is made. The even widths4,6,8, like the odd widths3,5,7, are not supplied by the present full-color gap. The audit includes literal even-width full marked sources against the unwrapped transfer and exact rotated Phi_2 product; numerical checks supplement the parity-independent derivations above.

title: Actual pretzel circle sewing: a coherent positive factorization and a half-twist test
text:
# Actual pretzel circle sewing: a coherent positive factorization and a half-twist test 29 October 2026. For the specified arbitrary-width pretzel port graph, the complete circle has an exact source-preserving Kraus/Cauchy factorization. The half twists remain diagonal unitary channel phases. The original marked cap produces TWO explicit boundary states; local positivity alone does not identify them. A level-three exact calculation rules out a literal positive norm-square identity for the half-twisted base, even after multiplying by any unit root framing phase. A separate untwisted calculation shows that the two source states remain different in the complete positive-circle quotient itself. This excludes their automatic identification by a choice of positive factor or consistent unitary duality gauges. It does not rule out another global reflection pairing for the genuinely untwisted base or a sharp positive majorant. ## 1. Specified original port graph Let s>=3 be odd, with boxes on adjacent head pairs (1,2),(3,4),...,(2s-1,2s). The bottom matching and top matching are S={(1,2s),(2,3),(4,5),...,(2s-2,2s-1)}. The outer top pair (1,2s) has the original marked row m; all other top pairs have the original ordinary cap ell. Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and retain the original common Cartan kappa=q^(d^2/2). Use the original physical pair operators R and L=L_N. Each box considered here is \[ B_i=R^{e_i}L,\qquad e_i\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{1} \] The [literal all-width port/source calculation](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md) fixes this graph and its signs. Its augmented odd-pretzel base has e_i=-1. The genuinely untwisted circle graph has e_i=0. These are different graphs; removing the half twists is not a scalar framing operation. Let p_S be the tensor product of the genuine cups p_ab=Nx^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), placed on S in its displayed order. Let P_o swap each ordinary-cap pair (2,3),(4,5),... and leave the marked outer pair alone. Let P_b swap every box pair. Both are literal permutations of tensor legs, not added physical crossings. All boxes preserve total INTEGER physical degree. Thus the total incoming degree sd and the ordinary caps force the final marked pair to degree d. Only on this assembled source the top row is \[ \Lambda_S=N^{-(2s+1)}p_S^\dagger P_o. 	ag{2} \] Indeed ell=p^dagger P/N^2 and m_d=p^dagger/N^3 on their respective pairs. The unrestricted marked row has not been replaced locally on an arbitrary exterior. Consequently the full raw source scalar, before its existing external framing/peripheral factor chi_N, is \[ Z_N=N^{-(2s+1)}p_S^\dagger P_o (B_1\otimes\cdots\otimes B_s)p_S. 	ag{3} \] This graph identity is the source input; no geometric triangulation or hyperbolic volume formula is assumed. ## 2. Full physical coherent channel factorization Use the canonical full physical positive resolution [of the original complete circle](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md). For every physical degree T and admitted distinct Casimir node j, let v_(T,j) have first component one, embedded in its actual degree block, and let h_(T,j)>0 be its exact positive CD coefficient. Form a rectangular matrix F with columns sqrt(h_(T,j)) v_(T,j). Then \[ FF^\dagger=H=LP,\qquad R F=F\,\operatorname{diag} (\kappa
u_j),\quad 
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}. 	ag{4} \] Every high physical block is retained by the explicit low-block mirror; both even paired nodes and the odd simple node are included. This is not a value-only replacement of a root Jordan block. The original circle has already selected its entire image, with its actual normal source, before (4) is used. Since |kappa nu_j|=1, define the diagonal unitary U_i=diag((kappa nu_j)^(e_i)). Equations (1) and (4) prove the ALL-INPUT factorization \[  oxed{B_i=F U_i F^\dagger P.} 	ag{5} \] This retains every half twist and its full Cartan phase. It does not use the false assertion that the original R is an H-isometry; the isometry on H would instead involve the correctly leg-exchanged R. Put F_s=F^(tensor s), U=U_1 tensor...tensor U_s, and define the two source packets \[ u=F_s^\dagger P_b p_S,\qquad v=F_s^\dagger P_o p_S. \] Inserting (5) in (3) gives the exact coherent formula and its positive Cauchy estimate: \[  oxed{Z_N=N^{-(2s+1)}v^\dagger Uu,\qquad |\chi_N Z_N|^2\leq |\chi_N|^2N^{-(4s+2)} \|v\|^2\|u\|^2.} 	ag{6} \] The two energies are explicit positive original-source contractions: \[ \|u\|^2=p_S^\dagger C^{\otimes s}p_S,\qquad \|v\|^2=p_S^\dagger P_oH^{\otimes s}P_op_S. 	ag{7} \] All original integer labels, cap constraints and CD factors are kept before these contractions. The local once-power angle coefficient is the exact h_(T,j), not its independent maximum. Formula (6) works at arbitrary s and for arbitrary signed e_i; neither packet is defined by the unknown closed scalar. For e_i=0, the middle U is the identity, but v and u are still different specified source packets. A global reflection theorem must supply an additional relation between them, or another controlled pairing. This does not follow from FF^dagger>=0 or from a consistent dual-object basis change. In particular (6) is a structural positive comparison, not a sharp geometric energy estimate. For clarity, the equivalent literal transfer entries retain the phases as follows. If h is the conserved input-left minus output-left charge, I_h=[max(0,h),min(d,d+h)], T=d+a-a', then \[ M_i^h[a,a']=x^{-2a+h} \sum_{j\ {\mathrm{admitted\ at}}\ T} h_{T,j}(\kappa
u_j)^{e_i} v_{T,j}(a-h)\overline{v_{T,j}(d-a')}. 	ag{8} \] The total physical degree T varies with the two open transfer indices. It cannot be replaced by a common fixed degree before contraction. ## 3. Exact half-twisted source certificate at N=3 Take N=3, s=3 and every e_i=-1. Build the literal original factorial R, the actual coproduct Casimir Omega, and L=Omega^2-I. The complete source contraction (3), or equivalently the already specified transfer trace, gives exactly \[  oxed{Z_3=-189+81i\sqrt3=27(-7+3i\sqrt3).} 	ag{9} \] This calculation includes kappa=q^2 and the original marked N factors. The exact transfer trace used to verify it is \[ Z_3= rac{x^4}{3}\sum_{h=-2}^2 \operatorname{Tr}\{D_h(M^h)^3\},\qquad D_h=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in I_h}x^{2a}. \] The five traces, in order h=-2,-1,0,1,2, are 270+243 i sqrt3, 27-351 i sqrt3, 2781/2+(189/2) i sqrt3, -540+162 i sqrt3, -999/2+(27/2) i sqrt3. Moreover \[ Z_3/\overline{Z_3}=(11-21i\sqrt3)/38. 	ag{10} \] This cannot be a root of unity: its rational field trace is 11/19, whereas a root of unity is an algebraic integer and a rational trace of an algebraic integer must be an integer. Thus multiplying (9) by ANY unit root framing phase cannot make it real. In particular the original half-twisted scalar is not a positive norm square times the retained framing phase and a positive scalar normalization. This is an obstruction only to that literal norm-square identity. The positive comparison (6) remains valid. The certificate is not an upper-volume counterexample and does not identify a hyperbolic knot or link from a numerical invariant. The graph without the half twists (all e_i=0) instead has Z_3=270, consistent with the still-open genuinely untwisted reflection question. No extrapolation from this calculation settles arbitrary untwisted fully augmented diagrams. ### 3a. The untwisted source mismatch survives the positive-circle quotient There is a stronger, source-exact check than merely observing that the two permutations in Section 2 are different. Set N=3, s=3, and every e_i=0, with the original cups and the one marked cap as in Section 1. For ANY factor F satisfying FF^dagger=H, the actual packet Gram is \[  oxed{\quad  egin{pmatrix} u^\dagger u&u^\dagger v\v^\dagger u&v^\dagger v \end{pmatrix} =3^{10} egin{pmatrix}18&10\10&119\end{pmatrix}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] This is an exact quadratic-field calculation directly in the original physical modules. One can verify it without choosing square roots or CD columns: put \[ p_{a,b,c}=27x^{-(d-a+d-b+d-c)},\qquad (i_1,\ldots,i_6)=(a,b,d-b,c,d-c,d-a), \] for a,b,c in {0,1,2}. These are precisely the 27 nonzero entries of p_S. Permute them by P_b or P_o, and contract the two resulting vectors against H tensor H tensor H. The literal coproduct Casimir gives L=Omega^2-I and H=LP; their entries, and all the displayed source coefficients, lie in Q(sqrt(-3)). The three resulting finite contractions are respectively 18,10,119 times 3^10. The audit performs these operations in that exact number field, separately from the numerical CD tests. In particular \[ \|u-v\|^2=117\,3^{10}>0,\qquad \det\operatorname{Gram}(u,v)=2042\,3^{20}>0. 	ag{12} \] The difference therefore survives the actual image quotient: it is not a radical vector discarded by the positive complete circle. The packets are not even collinear. The original closed value and the two proposed canonical packet norms are \[ Z_3=3^{-7}v^\dagger u=270,\qquad 3^{-7}\|u\|^2=486,\qquad 3^{-7}\|v\|^2=3213. 	ag{13} \] Every equality (11)--(13) is independent of the Kraus factor: its Gram depends only on H. Replacing a minimal F by another such factor applies a common isometry to its channel space and cannot change it. Consistent unitary physical duality changes, with the original sources transformed at their ports, likewise leave these closed contractions unchanged. Consequently removing the half-twist phases and transporting the true dual objects do NOT turn formula (6) into either canonical norm square. This is deliberately a limited obstruction. It does not exclude a different projection-plane cut, a nontrivial global pairing with its own proved source normalization, or coherent elimination before taking a norm. The untwisted value in (13) is positive. What fails is the specific proposed inference that the original marked source identifies the two positive-circle boundary states after quotienting. In particular this calculation does not replace a genuine six-port junction by a two-port Frobenius multiplication. ## 4. Validation and remaining estimate The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_circle_coherent_reflection.py) constructs the full original generators, crossings, complete circle, actual marked/cup source and canonical CD columns. It compares (3) directly to (6), with all physical box ports still open before their literal source contraction. A separate exact quadratic-field calculation reconstructs (9) from the original matrices rather than from guessed channel phases. It also computes (11) exactly from H and the literal 27-term original cup state; positivity, noncollinearity, and the quotient-level mismatch are consequences of that exact Gram matrix. The remaining sharp task is a bound for the ACTUAL constrained packets (7), or a stronger coherent pairing than their product. Independent local capacities do not establish this. Neither polynomial duality transport nor the complete-circle local PSD theorem supplies the missing global geometric incidence or selected-source energy estimate.

title: Coherent circle control and the full original augmented pretzel period
text: # Coherent circle control and the full original augmented pretzel period 29 October 2026. The analytic proof and its full two-branch recurrence estimate have passed independent proof audits. The statement below concerns the COMPLETE augmented pretzel source, with every crossing-circle color equal to N and every retained half twist equal to the original R^(-1). It is a link-source theorem at arbitrary fixed odd box count s, not a theorem for its fixed Dehn fillings or for an arbitrary alternating knot. ## 1. Statement, including the original phase and leading constant Use the [literal complete-base polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) z_N and the unchanged marked functional Phi_2. For each fixed odd s>=3 put alpha=pi/s, eta=2 asinh(tan alpha), R=exp(eta), T=R+R^(-1)=4 sec(alpha)^2-2, u_*=atan(sec alpha), d=N-1, V_s=8s[Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)], C_s=(R-R^(-1)) exp(i s u_*/2) /[sqrt(s cos alpha) 2^s ((T+2)(T+6))^(s/4)]. Here Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2 sin v|dv. The asserted full-source asymptotic is A_(s,N)=Phi_2(z_N^s) =N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi(N-1)/4) C_s exp[N V_s/(2pi)] (1+o(1)). (1) In particular C_s is nonzero. The formula treats both parities of N with their actual original Cartan factors, and includes all repeated Casimir nodes and normal derivatives through Phi_2. Any external normalization must still be applied explicitly; no unexamined factor is declared harmless. The [explicit face-gluing and tetrahedron calculation](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md) identifies V_s with the complete augmented link volume. This assertion concerns the specified RAW marked source A_(s,N); an external chi_N is not implicitly set to one or assigned a growth rate. The [complete-point normalization proof](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) now checks that the original reduced Kashaev link evaluation has |<L_s>_N|=|A_(s,N)|. Its framing and component-dependent enhancement characters have modulus one. Thus (1) proves the actual link statement lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<L_s>_N| =Vol(S^3 minus L_s)=V_s. (1a) The full one-cut modified ADO convention instead multiplies the reduced value by i^(N+3)/N at completeness. That changes the leading N-power from N^(3/2) to N^(1/2), and preserves (1a)'s exponential rate. ## 2. The coherent Newton coefficients and the permitted envelope Write q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, M=floor((N-1)/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and c_a=2cos((2a+1)pi/N). Set B_r(w)=product_(a=0)^(r-1)(c_a-w-w^(-1)), A_r=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/(F_v^3 F_(v-r)), D_r=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/F_r^3, U_r=A_r/D_r. The finite source identity is exactly z_N(w+w^(-1)) =N^2 sum_(r=0)^M b_(N,r) B_r(w), b_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)(-1)^r q^(2r^2+r) A_r/F_r^3. (2) Consequently |b_(N,r)|=(s_(2r)/s_r^6)|U_r|. The [coherent finite inner transformation](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) proves |U_r|<=2N for r>=ceil(N/4), and, uniformly on compact subintervals of 0<u=pi r/N<pi/2 lying above pi/4, b_(N,r)=exp(-i pi d/4) (s_(2r)/s_r^6) sqrt(sin u) exp(iu/2) [1+O(1/N)]. (3) The error is complex, uniform, and relative to the nonzero displayed amplitude. This formula is the same for BOTH parities. It follows from the exact half-shift phases before taking their asymptotics. The [all-index backward estimate](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) retains the entire lower range and gives constants C,B independent of r,N such that |U_r|<=C N^B exp[N E(pi r/N)], E(u)=(2/pi) integral_u^(pi/4) log(cot v)dv, 0<=u<pi/4, E(u)=0, pi/4<=u<=pi/2. (4) This estimate expressly ALLOWS the second recurrence branch to grow. No assertion that |U_r| is polynomial below N/4 is needed. ## 3. A uniform circle estimate for each original Newton factor Fix R>1 and write w=-R exp(i theta), rho=R^(-1), g(t)=log|1-rho exp(it)|, eta=log R. The exact factorization gives log|B_r(w)|=r eta +sum_(a<r)[g(pi+theta+(2a+1)pi/N) +g(pi+theta-(2a+1)pi/N)]. (5) This is a midpoint sum on the symmetric arc [-2u,2u], u=pi r/N. Its difference from N/(2pi) times the integral is O_R(1), uniformly in r,N,theta. Indeed the total variation of g on one circle is 2log((R+1)/(R-1)); on each cell the midpoint error is at most half the variation on that cell. For any 0<=a<=pi, the function I_a(theta)=integral_(-a)^a g(theta+t)dt has its maximum at theta=pi: its derivative is g(theta+a)-g(theta-a), which is nonnegative on [0,pi], since cos(theta+a)-cos(theta-a)=-2sin(theta)sin(a)<=0 and g decreases as a function of cos. For 0<a<pi the maximum is unique modulo2pi. It follows in particular that max_(|w|=R)|B_r(w)| <=((R+1)/(R-1))^2 B_r(-R). (6) The right side is positive because every c_a>-2 and R+R^(-1)>2. This is a bound for the original finite Newton factor; no positivity of its monomial coefficients or unproved root-location assertion is used. ## 4. The second-branch envelope stays below the geometric maximum Uniform sine-factorial summation, including the endpoints, gives log s_k=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi k/N)+O(log N), 0<=k<N. Equations (2),(4),(5) therefore bound each term by a fixed polynomial in N times exp[N(H_R(u,theta)+E(u))], where H_R(u,theta)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi+u eta/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_(-2u)^(2u)g(pi+theta+t)dt. At theta=0 put J_R(u)=H_R(u,0). Equivalently, with T=R+R^(-1), J_R(u)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv. (7) It has the derivative J_R'(u)=(1/pi)log[(T+2cos(2u))cos(u)^2/(4sin(u)^4)]. In t=tan u its zero is 4t^4-(T-2)t^2-(T+2)=0, tan(u_*)^2=(T+2)/4. The other algebraic root is -1. Thus J_R has a unique strict global maximum at u_* in (pi/4,pi/2). In the entire lower range, (J_R+E)'(u) =(1/pi)log[(T+2cos(2u))/(4sin(u)^2)]>0, 0<u<pi/4. (8) Hence max_(u<=pi/4)(J_R+E)=J_R(pi/4)<J_R(u_*). This is the essential quantitative comparison: the allowed growth from switching recurrence branches never reaches the geometric maximum of the OUTER original sum. The exact diagonal/interior equality in the old two-variable presentation is handled coherently by (2), not ignored. It follows that, with j(eta)=J_(exp eta)(u_*(eta)), limsup_N (1/N)log max_(|w|=R)|z_N(w+w^(-1))|<=j(eta). (9) There is also a stronger local bound needed for the full period. For some c,epsilon,delta>0 and finite B,C depending only on R, |z_N(-R exp(i theta)-R^(-1)exp(-i theta))| <=C exp[Nj(eta)] [exp(-cN theta^2)+N^B exp(-delta N)], |theta|<=epsilon, (10) and the same expression with only C N^B exp[N(j-delta)] holds on epsilon<=|theta|<=pi. To prove it, first use (8) and compactness to remove the lower range and all u outside a small neighborhood of u_*. At that maximum the real mixed derivative H_(u theta) vanishes, while H_(uu)=J_R''(u_*)=-(T+6)^2/[pi(T+2)^(3/2)]<0, H_(theta theta)=-sin(2u_*)/[pi(T+2cos(2u_*))]<0. Thus H<=j-c[(u-u_*)^2+theta^2] locally. On this compact u range, (3) and the uniform sine-product expansion give a summand prefactor O(N^(-5/2)); the outside factor N^2 and the discrete Gaussian sum O(sqrt N) give O(1). This proves (10). Away from theta=0, the strict arc inequality in section3 supplies the missing global gap; u=0 and u=pi/2 are already below j by section4. ## 5. A nonzero central Gaussian from the actual finite sum For complex zeta near real eta>0 define Psi(u,zeta)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u) Log(2cosh zeta+2cos v)dv. (11) The logarithm is analytic in a fixed neighborhood, since its argument is positive at real eta. In a compact neighborhood of u_*, s_(2r)/s_r^6 =(2N)^(-5/2) sqrt(sin(2u))/sin(u)^3 exp[N(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi][1+O(1/N)], and the midpoint expansion of B_r has leading prefactor one. These follow respectively by factoring sin(pi k/N)/(pi k/N) before ordinary Euler--Maclaurin, and by the smooth midpoint rule. Both are uniform in the neighborhoods in use. Insert (3) and set zeta=eta+i t/sqrt N, u=u_*+x/sqrt N. Taylor's formula in the REAL index x gives N Psi=N j+i sqrt N Psi_eta t +(1/2)Psi_uu x^2+i Psi_(u eta)xt -(1/2)Psi_(eta eta)t^2+o(1). (12) For bounded x,t this is uniform. The Gaussian bound (10), together with its index-level proof, justifies summing (12) by dominated Riemann sums and removing the remaining x tails. The resulting Fourier transform of a real Gaussian has coefficient j''(eta)=Psi_(eta eta)-Psi_(u eta)^2/Psi_uu>0. No contour deformation of the r sum or assertion about an unknown cycle is being made. The exact finite-sum asymptotic is, uniformly for bounded real t, z_N(-exp(eta+i t/sqrt N)-exp(-eta-i t/sqrt N)) =exp(-i pi d/4) a(eta) exp[Nj(eta)] exp[i sqrt N j'(eta)t-j''(eta)t^2/2](1+o(1)), a(eta)=exp(iu_*/2)/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)]. (13) The displayed constant comes directly from the index Gaussian: 2^(-5/2)pi^(-1)sqrt(2pi/|Psi_uu|) times sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2). In particular it is nonzero. At t=0, (13) also turns (9) into equality. Elementary differentiation under the integral in (11) yields j'(eta)=alpha(eta)/pi, alpha(eta)=atan(sinh(eta/2)), j''(eta)=1/[2pi cosh(eta/2)]=cos(alpha)/(2pi). (14) For example j' follows by substituting tan(v/2) in its integral and using tan(u_*)=cosh(eta/2). Also j(eta)-eta/2 tends to zero as eta tends to infinity. Integrating (14), or differentiating the Lobachevsky expression with this boundary value, gives j(eta)-alpha eta/pi =(4/pi)[Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)]. (15) ## 6. The original marked residue has a surviving leading term The exact full source, including its normal coefficients, is A_(s,N)=(-1)^d N^2/(2pi i) integral_(|w|=R) z_N(w+w^(-1))^s w^N(1-w^(-2))/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (16) This is the proved coefficient/partial-trace identity for Phi_2, not a newly defined period. Choose eta=2asinh(tan(pi/s)), so that s j'(eta)=1. Parametrize w=-R exp(i theta). Uniformly on this circle, the rational factor is w^(-N)(1-w^(-2))[1+O(R^(-N))]. The error is exponentially smaller by (9),(10). In the central window theta=t/sqrt N, the original factor (-1)^d cancels the exact sign of w^(1-N). Equations (13),(14) cancel the linear Fourier phase as well. The remaining Gaussian is exp[-s j''(eta)t^2/2]. Bound (10) permits dominated convergence in this final integral; its complement is exponentially negligible. Consequently A_(s,N)=N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi d/4) [(R-R^(-1))a(eta)^s/sqrt(2pi s j''(eta))] exp[N(sj(eta)-eta)](1+o(1)). (17) Equations (14),(15) are precisely the constant and exponent in (1). The double-pole factor 1-w^(-2) is nonzero at -R and has been kept. Equivalently, all higher positive windings in the exact source have an extra R^(-(m-1)N) factor on this same circle; none was dropped before estimating it. Together with the independently proved finite-source and backward-envelope lemmas, this proves survival of the specified original raw period with its stated normalization. The bounds and local expansion used above are all at fixed s. No uniform assertion as s grows with N, no fixed Dehn-filling theorem, and no general-knot volume conjecture follows from (1). ## 7. Independent checks and the normalization boundary Two independent analytical audits checked the midpoint maximum, the lower-index envelope comparison, the all-parity coefficient phase, the two real Gaussian integrations and the marked residue constant. The explicit harmonic-error backward proof was separately audited before use. The [finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.py) checks the exact stationary polynomial/Hessian, literal Newton-circle factors, and the predicted full complex leading constant against the original value-plus-normal period at N=32,33,64,65,128,129 and s=3,5,7,9. Those samples are calibration of the proof, not a replacement for its estimates. The original pretzel source theorem keeps a peripheral/framing line chi_N outside A_(s,N). Formula (1) has NOT silently absorbed that line. The [normalization proof](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) retains the whole modified-dimension meridian germ before evaluating it: |chi_red|=1 and |chi_full|=1/N at THIS complete point. It also checks that the exact enhanced Kashaev comparison extends to this multicomponent link, with component-dependent sign (-1)^(d(c-1)). No polynomial-size assertion for an arbitrary moving peripheral germ is inferred. The fixed filled-knot source also contains the ENTIRE coherent auxiliary-color sum; taking only its complete-color value is not a filling theorem. ## 8. The requested special inner product is an explicit Fourier norm Write the SAME finite Laurent polynomial as z_N(w+w^(-1))^s=sum_(k=-sM)^(sM) a_k w^k. For N>=3 use the positive inner product on its coefficient space <a,b>_R=sum_k conjugate(a_k)b_k R^(2(k-N)), Z_(s,N)=||a||_R^2 =R^(-2N)/(2pi) integral_(-pi)^pi |z_N(-R exp(i theta)-R^(-1)exp(-i theta))|^(2s)dtheta. (18) The equality is finite Fourier--Plancherel. It retains all coherent inner sums BEFORE squaring. The exact original source functional is b_N(a)=(-1)^d N^2 sum_(m>=1)(-1)^(m-1)m (a_(mN-1)-a_(mN+1)), (19) with coefficients outside the finite support equal to zero. Its squared dual norm is bounded explicitly by ||b_N||_(R,dual)^2 <=N^4(R^2+R^(-2)) sum_(m>=1) m^2 R^(-2(m-1)N) =N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+x)/(1-x)^3, x=R^(-2N). (20) There is no index overlap for N>=3. Omitting absent coefficients can only decrease this bound. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore proves EXACTLY |A_(s,N)|^2<=N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+x)/(1-x)^3 Z_(s,N). (21) This metric is specified by the polynomial source and the geometric radius; it does not use the unknown contracted value A_(s,N). Equations (10),(13) additionally prove, at the radius in section1, Z_(s,N)=[|a(eta)|^(2s)/sqrt(2s cos alpha)] N^(-1/2) exp[N V_s/pi](1+o(1)). (22) Thus for this complete augmented source the original question is literally Cauchy in a specified inner product, AND its positive energy has now been independently estimated at the sharp volume rate. The additional Gaussian argument in section6 proves the lower bound/survival that Cauchy by itself cannot supply. For an external normalization chi_N, (21) retains |chi_N|^2 on its right. There is also an exact way to separate the upper-bound question from survival. Let D_(s,N) be the ACTUAL squared dual norm of (19) on the finite coefficient space, and let v be its Riesz vector for (18). Then |A_(s,N)|^2 = D_(s,N) Z_(s,N) cos(theta_N)^2, cos(theta_N)^2=|<v,a>_R|^2/(||v||_R^2 ||a||_R^2). (23) Here theta_N denotes the Hermitian angle, so cos(theta_N) is defined as the nonnegative normalized absolute overlap. For each fixed s>=3, both first-winding indices N-1,N+1 eventually lie in the coefficient space. Consequently D_(s,N)=N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+O(R^(-2N))). For fixed odd s>=3, equations (1) and (22) now give the quantitative survival statement cos(theta_N)^2 ~ [(R-R^(-1))^2/(R^2+R^(-2))] sqrt(2/(s cos alpha)) N^(-1/2). (24) Thus Cauchy's upper estimate loses only a polynomial factor for this particular original source. The nonzero-overlap asymptotic (24) uses the independently proved original-period asymptotic (1); it is not inferred from positivity or Plancherel. For a general filled source, the geometric energy estimate and exclusion of exponentially small overlap remain separate requirements.

title: Exact coherent inner elimination for the original pretzel polynomial
text: # Exact coherent inner elimination for the original pretzel polynomial 29 October 2026. Reversing the TWO ACTUAL finite sums in the complete pretzel box gives a balanced terminating finite transformation. It retains the half shift and proves a nonzero, uniformly tame inner packet throughout the geometric range r>=N/4, at BOTH parities. An explicit nonzero leading amplitude follows on compact subintervals of 1/4<r/N<1/2. No stationary-cycle assumption is used for this inner sum. The remaining outer sum and the all-r upper bound are separate. The exact all-r recurrence below retains the same original source, including the part below N/4 which has NOT been discarded. ## 1. The unchanged source and a generic finite identity Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a. In formula (11a) of [the original complete box](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), interchanging the FINITE v,r sums gives exactly kappa z_N(z)/N^2 =sum_(r=0)^M (-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2) P_r(z) A_r/F_r^3, A_r=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/(F_v^3 F_(v-r)), P_r(z)=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r, z=w+w^-1. (1) This retains every original coefficient, all half-twist and Cartan phases, and the full polynomial BEFORE its marked Hermite period. There is no removal of boundary r=v. Put n=M-r and D_r=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/F_r^3, U_r=A_r/D_r. Then U_r=sum_(k=0)^n (qQ^r;Q)_k(-qQ^r;Q)_k(-Q^(r+1);Q)_k Q^(-rk) /[F_k(Q^(r+1);Q)_k^2]. (2) Exactly one of the three numerator parameters is Q^(-n): -qQ^r at odd N, and -Q^(r+1) at even N. All denominators are nonzero throughout the TRUE finite ranges. Here is the finite transformation used in both cases. For generic parameters with nonzero displayed denominators, sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_k(a;Q)_k(b;Q)_k (cdQ^n/(ab))^k/[F_k(c;Q)_k(d;Q)_k] =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j(a;Q)_j(d/b;Q)_j Q^j /[F_j(d;Q)_j(aQ^(1-n)/c;Q)_j]. (3) This is proved here by finite summation, not assumed from a named transformation theorem. The terminating identity sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(t;Q)_j Q^j/[F_j(d;Q)_j] =t^k(d/t;Q)_k/(d;Q)_k (4) was proved by two finite binomial expansions in [the elementary q-Chu proof](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md#2-elementary-finite-q-chu-and-durfee-identities). Its balanced version is sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(a;Q)_j(cQ^k/a)^j /[F_j(c;Q)_j]=(c/a;Q)_k/(c;Q)_k. (5) For completeness, reverse the summation in (5). After its last term is factored out, the remaining sum is (4) with parameters t=Q^(1-k)/c and d=Q^(1-k)/a. The factorial reversal (Q^(1-k)/a;Q)_k=(-a)^(-k)Q^(-k(k-1)/2)(a;Q)_k cancels that last-term factor and gives (5). To prove (3), expand (b;Q)_k/(d;Q)_k =(b/d)^k sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(d/b;Q)_j Q^j/[F_j(d;Q)_j] using (4), interchange the finite k,j sums, and put k=j+l. The l sum is (5) with parameters Q^(j-n),aQ^j,cQ^j and argument cQ^(n-j)/a. It equals (c/a;Q)_(n-j)/(cQ^j;Q)_(n-j). Cancel (c;Q)_j(cQ^j;Q)_(n-j)=(c;Q)_n and use (c/a;Q)_(n-j)/(c/a;Q)_n =(-c/a)^(-j)Q^(-nj+j(j+1)/2) /(aQ^(1-n)/c;Q)_j. All remaining powers combine to Q^j. This proves (3) exactly, and rational continuation gives every root specialization used here. ## 2. Odd levels: a coherent quarter-phase series Let N=2M+1, n=M-r. Substitution in (3) gives U_r=(q;Q)_n/(Q^(r+1);Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^(2r+1);Q^2)_j(-1;Q)_j Q^j /[(Q^(2r+2);Q^2)_j F_j]. (6) Every summand on the second line is EXACTLY i^j h_j, h_j>0. Its consecutive positive magnitudes obey, with delta=pi/N, h_(j+1)/h_j =sin((2r+1+2j)delta)/sin((2r+2+2j)delta) *cos(j delta)/sin((j+1)delta). The prefactor has phase q^(-n(r+1/2)), so its product with i^n has the EXACT phase q^(n^2), using N=2M+1. Reverse the series. Direct cancellation of its positive products gives U_r=q^(n^2) B_(N,n) sum_(l=0)^n (-i)^l g_l, (7) B_(N,n)=product_(k=0)^(n-1) cos(k delta)cos((k+1)delta)/cos((k+1/2)delta)^2, g_l=product_(k=1)^l [sin((2k-1)delta)/sin(2k delta)] [sin((n-k+1)delta)/cos((n-k)delta)], g_0=1. Equation (7) holds for EVERY 0<=r<=M, not just the geometric range. All its factors are retained. In particular a half-shift amplitude has not been replaced by one before an exponentially canceling sum. Now suppose r>=ceil(N/4), hence n delta<=pi/4. Then h_j is strictly increasing: its sine ratio is at least one on the descending half of the sine interval, and cos(j delta)>sin((j+1)delta). Thus g_l decreases. The real part of the reversed alternating parity sum is at least 1-g_2 (or exactly one for n=0,1). For n>=2, g_2 <= tan(n delta)^2/[2cos(delta)] <=1/[2cos(pi/9)]<1-5/12, since then N>=9. Concavity and |(log cos)''|<=2 on [0,pi/4] give exp(-pi^2/(8N))<=B_(N,n)<=1. These elementary bounds, with the n=0,1 cases separately, prove 1/3<=|U_r|<=N, r>=ceil(N/4), N odd. (8) Moreover g_l<=tan(n delta)^l. On any compact subinterval of 1/4<r/N<1/2, put beta=n delta. The product formula gives g_l=((1/2)_l/l!)tan(beta)^l[1+O(l^2/N)] for l in a fixed small linear fraction of N; the exact geometric bound controls the remaining tail. Choosing that fraction small enough that tan(beta)exp(C epsilon)<1, summing the errors proves UNIFORMLY U_r=q^(n^2)[(1+i tan beta)^(-1/2)+O(1/N)]. (9) The square root is the branch with positive real part. Its modulus is sqrt(cos beta), so the amplitude is nonzero, with no unknown cycle coefficient. The error statement uses the actual discrete beta=n pi/N, not a reset parity-independent angle. ## 3. Even levels: an alternating series with a retained small chirp Let N=2M+2, n=M-r. A different permissible ordering in (3) gives U_r=(-q;Q)_n/(Q^(r+1);Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (-Q^(r+1);Q)_j(-qQ^r;Q)_j(q;Q)_j Q^j /[F_j(Q^(r+1);Q)_j(q^3Q^r;Q)_j]. (10) The j-th term is EXACTLY (-q^(1/2))^j h_j, h_j>0. The principal q^(1/2)=exp(pi i/(2N)) is retained; the series is not declared real. Its positive ratio is h_(j+1)/h_j =cos((r+1+j)delta)cos((r+1/2+j)delta)sin((j+1/2)delta) /[sin((r+1+j)delta)sin((r+3/2+j)delta)sin((j+1)delta)]. For r>=ceil(N/4), every ratio is below one and in fact h_j<=cot(r delta)^(2j). Pair consecutive even/odd terms. Each pair's real part is nonnegative because h_j decreases and the cosine of its retained phase decreases on the range 0<=j delta/2<=pi/8. The first pair alone gives Re(sum)>=1-h_1>1/3; n=0 gives one. Indeed h_1<=1/[2cos(delta/2)], with N>=8 when n>=1. The prefactor's positive magnitude is R_(N,n)=product_(k=0)^(n-1) cos((k+1/2)delta)/cos((k+1)delta), 1<=R_(N,n)<=1/cos(n delta)<=sqrt(2). Its EXACT phase is sigma_r=i^n q^(-n(r+1/2))=q^(n(n+1/2)). Therefore 1/3<=|U_r|<=2N, r>=ceil(N/4), N even. (11) On compact subintervals 1/4<r/N<1/2 the geometric domination and the fixed-j sine products prove, by the same summable estimate, sum in (10)=sin(r delta)+O(1/N), R_(N,n)=(cos(n delta))^(-1/2)[1+O(1/N)]. Consequently, uniformly on those compact sets, U_r=q^(n(n+1/2))[sqrt(sin(r delta))+O(1/N)]. (12) Equations (8),(11) prove the genuine all-level exponential equivalence |A_r|=|D_r| exp(O(log N)) throughout the geometric range. Equations (9),(12) sharpen it to an explicit nonzero amplitude and phase. ## 4. Newton phases and the precise remaining lower-index problem For odd N, use P_r(z)=q^(r^2)product_(a<r)(c_a-z), c_a=qQ^a+q^(-1)Q^(-a). The factorial phases in (1),(7) cancel: kappa z_N(z)/N^2 =q^(M^2) sum_(r=0)^M [s_(2r)/s_r^6] B_(N,M-r) Srev_r product_(a<r)(c_a-z), Srev_r=sum_(l=0)^(M-r)(-i)^l g_l. (13) For r>=ceil(N/4), Re Srev_r>0 and Im Srev_r<=0, with the uniform quantitative lower bound above. Thus the high-index Newton packet has a common quadrant at a real z<-2, with no macroscopic phase cancellation. This is an EXACT coherent packet of the original box, not a sum of separate absolute-valued expanded states. For r<N/4 the transformed identities STILL HOLD but the monotonicity and geometric domination used in (8)--(12) fail. No polynomial bound for all such Srev_r, or a global common quadrant, is inferred here. In particular these lower indices remain in the original outer sum. Even (10) is decreasing only in the displayed high-index range. No sharp global circle bound, original outer-cycle survival, or full pretzel volume theorem has been proved by this inner calculation. ## 5. An exact all-r source Ward equation There is nevertheless a low-order equation controlling the ENTIRE remaining sequence, including the lower-index range. With Y=Q^r, QY^2(1-Q^2Y) A_(r+2) +Y(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1) A_(r+1) -Q(QY+1)(QY^2-1) A_r=0, (14) A_M=Q^(-M^2)F_(2M)/F_M^3, A_(M+1)=0. Here A_r=0 for r>M. The backwards coefficient in (14) is nonzero for r<M at both parities, so these are the LITERAL selected endpoint conditions, not an unspecified solution of an annihilating equation. Proof. For t(v,r)=Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/(F_v^3F_(v-r)), z=Q^v, t(v+1,r)/t(v,r) =Y^(-1)(1-Qz^2)(1+Qz)/[(1-Qz)^2(1-Qz/Y)]. The rational certificate g(z)=(1-z)^2(1-z/Y)/z^2 obeys g(Qz)t(v+1,r)/t(v,r)-g(z) =(1/(YQ^2)-1)z^-2 +(1/(YQ)+2+1/Y)z^-1-1/(YQ)-1-2/Y. The sum telescopes: g(Q^r)=0 and t(M+1,r)=0 by its literal root factor. Finally t(v,r+1)/t(v,r)=z^-1-Y^-1, so its first two moments are A_(r+1)+Y^-1 A_r and A_(r+2)+(1+Q^-1)Y^-1A_(r+1)+Y^-2A_r. Substitution yields (14). The classical characteristic ratios of (14) are (Y+1)^2/[Y(Y-1)] and (Y-1)/Y; their moduli cross at r/N=1/4. Their equality has no finite nonzero solution. This makes the source-calibrated continuation a concrete remaining analytic problem, not a reason to substitute a uniform norm or an arbitrary branch. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.py) checks (3) at independent generic parameters, both literal root sums for EVERY r, their exact phases, the all-input source Ward endpoints, the uniform high-index inequalities, and the explicit amplitude limits. ## 6. Exact parity alignment and the high-packet Gaussian This section concerns the ACTUAL high packet r>=ceil(N/4) of (1); the lower indices are retained separately, not declared zero. Write z_N^hi for that partial polynomial. Its Newton coefficient before the outside N^2 is b_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)(-1)^r q^(2r^2+r) A_r/F_r^3. For odd N, factorial phases and (7) give exactly b_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)q^(M^2) [s_(2r)/s_r^6] B_(N,n) Srev_r. The leading Srev_r in (9) is sqrt(cos beta)exp(-i beta/2), where beta=n pi/N=pi/2-pi/(2N)-u and u=pi r/N. Since kappa=q^(d^2/2), M=d/2, its total leading phase is EXACTLY kappa^(-1)q^(M^2)exp(-i beta/2) =exp(-i pi d/4)exp(iu/2). At even N the prefactor in (10) has exact phase q^(n(n+1/2)); the remaining factorial phases give kappa^(-1)q^(M^2+M/2)q^(r/2). The first two factors are EXACTLY exp(-i pi d/4), since d=2M+1. Together with (12) this proves, uniformly on every compact 1/4<r/N<1/2 at BOTH parities, b_(N,r)=exp(-i pi d/4)[s_(2r)/s_r^6] sqrt(sin u)exp(iu/2)[1+O(1/N)]. (15) No parity-dependent sign or unknown root phase remains in (15). Fix a real T>2, eta=arcosh(T/2), R=exp eta, and define J_T(u)=[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv, u_*=atan(sqrt(T+2)/2). Its derivative is pi^(-1)log[(T+2cos(2u))cos(u)^2/(4sin(u)^4)]. The difference of the numerator and denominator in this logarithm has the sign of T+2-(T+6)sin(u)^2. Hence u_* is the unique strict maximum on 0<=u<=pi/2, and u_*>pi/4. Direct differentiation gives J_T''(u_*)=-(T+6)^2/[pi(T+2)^(3/2)]. The original sine-factorial and smooth midpoint products give uniformly near this maximum s_(2r)/s_r^6=(2N)^(-5/2) sqrt(sin(2u))/sin(u)^3 *exp{N[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi}[1+O(1/N)], product_(a<r)(c_a+T) =exp{N/(2pi) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv} *[1+O(1/N)]. All other high indices have a strict profile gap, using (8),(11) and the uniform logarithmic endpoint factorial estimate. The real discrete Laplace sum has step du=pi/N. Inserting (15), its Gaussian prefactor is 2^(-5/2)pi^(-1)sqrt(2pi/|J_T''(u_*)|) *sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2) =1/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)]. Thus this ENTIRE coherent high packet has the asymptotic z_N^hi(-T) =exp(-i pi d/4) exp(iu_*/2) /[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)] *exp[N J_T(u_*)][1+O(1/N)]. (16) It also has a uniform central-window extension without deforming its index contour. Let j(eta)=J_(2cosh eta)(u_*(eta)), and let tau be bounded real. Taylor-expand the analytic midpoint logarithm at eta+i tau/sqrt N and the REAL index u=u_*+x/sqrt N. Its quadratic part is Nj+i sqrt N j' tau +(Psi_uu/2)x^2+i Psi_(u eta)x tau -(Psi_(eta eta)/2)tau^2. The real index Gaussian dominates all x tails uniformly for bounded tau, and the remaining high indices retain their fixed profile gap. Dominated Riemann sums therefore evaluate the mixed term by the exact Fourier transform of this real Gaussian. The Schur complement is j''=Psi_(eta eta)-Psi_(u eta)^2/Psi_uu, giving z_N^hi(-exp(eta+i tau/sqrt N)-exp(-eta-i tau/sqrt N)) =exp(-i pi d/4) a(eta)exp[Nj(eta)] *exp[i sqrt N j'(eta)tau-j''(eta)tau^2/2][1+o(1)], a(eta)=exp(iu_*/2)/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)]. (17) The error is uniform for bounded tau. The displayed limiting Gaussian and a(eta) are nonzero, so the error is relative as written. This is an actual finite-sum calculation with every coherent inner factor; it does not assert an unknown r-cycle incidence. To replace z_N^hi by the FULL z_N requires the independent all-index upper envelope and its strict lower-range profile gap. The [whole-period assembly](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) states that additional gate explicitly before applying (17) to the original marked residue. The finite audit checks eight independent generic finite transforms, 39 complete root families N=2,...,40 (EVERY r, both exact transformed phases and the source Ward), six complex-amplitude profiles through N=256, and four literal high-packet central-window families at N=63,64,127,128. The latter compare tau=-1,0,1 with (17), retaining the full kappa and both parity phases. These tests supplement the finite and analytic proofs; convergence samples are not their premise.

title: Coherent radial capacity of the original augmented pretzel source
text: # Coherent radial capacity of the original augmented pretzel source 29 October 2026. These diagnostics evaluate the exact polynomial and original source in [the complete-base theorem](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). They retain all nodal derivatives and all true winding channels. They do not prove an asymptotic limit, a global circle supremum, or geometric survival. ## 1. A genuine full-source finite Cauchy bound Let \(z_N\) be that explicit half-degree polynomial and let \(R>1\). The exact enclosing residue, with the original source normal terms, immediately gives \[ |\mathcal A_{s,N}| \leq N^2\frac{R+R^{-1}}{(1-R^{-N})^2} R^{-N}\max_{|w|=R}|z_N(w+w^{-1})|^s. \tag{1} \] No inner factorial sum is replaced by absolute values. Its only maximum is the coherent actual polynomial on the specified circle. For each fixed \(R,s\) the prefactor is polynomial in \(N\). The classical candidate circle for the primitive winding is \[ c_s=2-4\sec^2(\pi/s),\qquad R_s=\frac{-c_s+\sqrt{c_s^2-4}}2. \] The compared classical action rate is \[ V_s/(2\pi)=\frac{4s}{\pi} \left[\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2s}\right) +\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4-\frac\pi{2s}\right)\right]. \] The identification and accessibility of that classical critical point are separate from the finite inequality (1). ## 2. Coherent values, with precision replay The capacity column below is \(s\log\max_{|w|=R_s}|z_N(w+w^{-1})|/N-\log R_s\), before the polynomial prefactor of (1). The period column is the FULL original \(\log|\mathcal A_{s,N}|/N\), calculated with the source derivative terms, not only the largest spectral value. | Boxes | N | Coherent capacity rate | Original period rate | Candidate action rate | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 3 | 128 | 2.282542848771 | 2.358391191770 | 2.332487232247 | | 3 | 256 | 2.307490060173 | 2.349466791768 | 2.332487232247 | | 5 | 128 | 5.113656771500 | 5.175096842135 | 5.180738545635 | | 5 | 256 | 5.147131188299 | 5.181900345453 | 5.180738545635 | | 7 | 128 | 7.617877073877 | 7.673538626889 | 7.707108672092 | | 7 | 256 | 7.662390577692 | 7.694267916927 | 7.707108672092 | | 9 | 128 | 10.031081747751 | 10.083088667235 | 10.143508359858 | | 9 | 256 | 10.087158750074 | 10.117206848457 | 10.143508359858 | The apparent circle maximum is near the negative real axis, with a finite-level angular shift of order \(1/N\). At \(N=256\), its angles divided by \(\pi\) are respectively 0.998640430, 0.999300037, 0.999527662, 0.999641617. title: An explicit half-degree Casimir polynomial for the original augmented pretzel base
text: # An explicit half-degree Casimir polynomial for the original augmented pretzel base **Subsequent analytic theorem.** This exact source now feeds the [full coherent period asymptotic](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), which proves a nonzero leading coefficient and the actual augmented link volume rate at arbitrary fixed odd width. The formulas below retain their role as independently checked finite algebraic inputs. 29 October 2026. The COMPLETE mixed-circle base of every odd pretzel has a single, explicit pair-Casimir polynomial. Its degree is at most \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). Its coefficients in the physical continuant basis are positive finite cosine/factorial products, with the actual half-twist phase retained. This yields all nodal values AND first normal jets, and an original one-variable coefficient source for every odd number of boxes. No geometric saddle or noncancellation theorem is inferred from this exact reduction. ## 1. Literal quarter-turn, not a partial transpose of a positive form Use the original \(N,d,q,Q,x,\kappa,p,\ell,m,R,L_N\) of the [pretzel source theorem](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md). For any two-head box define its actual rigid quarter-turn by \[ (\mathscr R B)_{(u,b);(v,e)} =\sum_{r,t}\ell_{u,r}B_{(r,v);(b,t)}p_{t,e} =x^{u-e}B_{(d-u,v);(b,d-e)}. \tag{1} \] This is a linear tangle rotation using the original turns. It is not a multiplicative map for vertical box composition and is not asserted to preserve matrix positivity. The original crossing rotation/snakes give \(\mathscr R(R^{-1})=R\), with full Cartan retained; also \(\mathscr R(I)=p\ell\), rather than the identity matrix. The charge transfer in the pretzel theorem makes this rotation source exact. On degree \(T=d+h\), if \(S_h=\operatorname{diag}(x^a)\) and \(P_h\) is physical reversal, then \[ (\mathscr R B)|_T=x^dP_hS_hM_B^{(h)}S_h^{-1}P_h. \tag{2} \] Under this conjugation \(D_h\) becomes the clock \(Q^{-b}\) of the second physical head. Its factor relative to the original pivot \(g_b=x^{-d}Q^{-b}\) cancels every remaining phase in the pretzel source. Precisely, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s) =\Phi_2\bigl((\mathscr R B_1)\cdots(\mathscr R B_s)\bigr), \quad\Phi_2(X)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{V\otimes V} [(I\otimes g)X].} \tag{3} \] This is the same original marked source, not a new \(2N\) average. ## 2. Why the rotated box is a SINGLE full pair polynomial An actual pair intertwiner rotates to another pair intertwiner by the Hopf cup and cap equations. Work first at generic nearby \(q\), with the ordinary finite highest module of dimension \(N\), its genuine dual turns, and the literal mixed-circle polynomial. These data specialize regularly to the displayed root source: all turn factorials have indices below \(N\). Generic pair decomposition is multiplicity-free, with \(N\) distinct Casimir nodes, so every rotated box here is a unique polynomial in the generic pair Casimir of degree less than \(N\). These polynomial coefficients have NO root pole. Indeed the middle degree block of the Casimir is tridiagonal, and all its adjacent entries remain nonzero at the root. The map from its first \(N\) polynomial coefficients to its first physical row is triangular with these nonzero products on the diagonal. Its inverse is regular. Consequently the polynomial identity specializes on the ENTIRE physical pair, including high-degree blocks and all Jordan normals. It is not only a statement about distinct root eigenvalues. Apply this to \(B_*=R^{-1}L_N\), using the generic ordinary circle with its standard pivot before specialization. At the root its \((-1)^d\) pivot factor is exactly the original auxiliary pivot. Thus \(\mathscr R B_*=z_N(\Omega)\) for one degree-\(<N\) polynomial. ## 3. Explicit positive coefficients and the half-degree truncation Let \(A=\Omega|_{\deg d}\) in physical order \(|u,d-u\rangle\). Write its diagonal as \(D_u\) and adjacent entry as \(a_u=-(1-Q^{u+1})^2\). Define its canonical continuant polynomials \[ f_0(z)=1,\quad f_1(z)=(z-D_0)/a_0, \] \[ f_{u+1}(z)=\frac{(z-D_u)f_u(z)-a_{u-1}f_{u-1}(z)}{a_u}. \tag{4} \] Tridiagonality gives \(e_0^Tf_u(A)=e_u^T\). Thus the first physical row determines the polynomial by this specified basis. Put \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\) and \[ C_L=\prod_{r=0}^{L-1}2\cos\frac{\pi(2r+1-L)}{2N}, \qquad C_0=1, \] \[ b_v=\frac{s_{d-v}^2 C_{d-2v}}{s_{d-2v}}>0, \qquad 0\leq v\leq M. \tag{5} \] At exactly these lengths the cosine product simplifies further: \[ C_{d-2v}=\frac{F_{d-v}}{F_v}=\frac{N}{s_v^2},\qquad \boxed{\quad b_v=\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^4},\quad b_vx^v=N^2\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^4}.\quad} \tag{5a} \] Indeed \(-q^{1-(d-2v)}=Q^{v+1}\), so the product is precisely the interval \((Q^{v+1};Q)_{d-2v}\). Root factorial complementation gives the real positive value displayed. All integer lengths are below \(N\); this retains the exact root phases, rather than taking absolute values inside an unknown sum. Then the COMPLETE original base polynomial is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle z_N(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^{M}b_v f_v(z).} \tag{6} \] Proof of its first row. Equation (1), restricted to the middle degree, gives \((\mathscr R B_*)_{0,v}=x^{v-d}(B_*)_{(d,v);(d,v)}\). In the high block of physical degree \(d+v\), the original \(R^{-1}\) has only its first column in its last row, with coefficient \(\kappa^{-1}x^{d-v}\). Therefore the two phases cancel exactly and \[ (\mathscr R B_*)_{0,v} =\kappa^{-1}(H_N|_{d-v})_{0,0}. \tag{7} \] The [positive reflected-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) proves that this corner vanishes if \(2v>d\), and otherwise equals \[ s_{d-v}^2\sum_{a=0}^{d-2v}\frac1{s_as_{d-2v-a}}. \] The finite sum FACTORIZES. At any \(0\leq L<N\), the finite q-binomial theorem and \(F_a=(-i)^a q^{a(a+1)/2}s_a\) give \[ \sum_{a=0}^L\frac1{s_as_{L-a}} =\frac{(-q^{1-L};Q)_L}{s_L}= rac{C_L}{s_L}. \tag{8} \] In the middle expression the product is real and positive: its individual phases sum to zero, and all its cosine factors are positive. This proves (5)--(7), including the exact truncation. In particular the top coefficient of \(z_N\) is nonzero. For odd \(N=2m+1\), it has the especially simple exact value \[ [z^m]z_N(z)=\kappa^{-1}q^{-m(m+1)}, \tag{9} \] of modulus one. No absent leading channel is being supplied by a normalization choice. At even \(N=2m\), its degree is \(m-1\) and the top coefficient has modulus \(8/s_1\), also polynomial and nonzero. ## 4. All nodal values and normal jets without a large crossing matrix For every original node \(c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\), define \[ \lambda_j=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^M b_v f_v(c_j),\qquad \xi_j=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^M b_v f'_v(c_j). \tag{10} \] These give the FULL node values and first derivatives of the actual rotated base box. Paired nodes have exactly the same data. At the possible odd simple node only the value is required. Differentiate (4) to compute every derivative with no divided zero: \[ f'_{u+1}= \frac{f_u+(z-D_u)f'_u-a_{u-1}f'_{u-1}}{a_u}, \quad f'_0=0,\quad f'_1=1/a_0. \tag{11} \] For a formula entirely in finite q-factorials, use the actual q-Hahn value formula in the [complete physical packet](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md), Section5, at \(T=d\): each \(f_v(c_j)\) is its displayed finite sum of three Gaussian binomials and an explicit quadratic \(Q\) phase. Equation (10) with (5) is therefore a finite factorial/quadratic-phase formula, not an unspecified eigenvector or a spectral fit. Equations (4),(11) retain all normal data even at even and composite levels. There is a shorter polynomial factorial formula. Define \[ P_r(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(1-qQ^a z+Q^{2a+1}),\qquad P_0=1. \] Direct substitution in the explicit recurrence (4), coefficient by coefficient in this product basis, gives \[ f_v(z)=x^v\sum_{r=0}^v \frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r(z), \] \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{\kappa z_N(z)}{N^2}= \sum_{v=0}^M\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^4} \sum_{r=0}^v\frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r(z).} \tag{11a} \] This is an OWN finite polynomial identity: its proof uses the coefficient recurrence (4), the root relation \(x=-q^{-1}\), and \(P_{r+1}=P_r(1-qQ^r z+Q^{2r+1})\). It does not assume a named orthogonal-polynomial transformation or an asymptotic formula. More explicitly, with \(C_{v,r}=x^v(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r/F_r^3\) and zero coefficients outside \(0\leq r\leq v\), the coefficient identity to check is \[ a_vC_{v+1,r}=(c_r-D_v)C_{v,r} -q^{-1}Q^{1-r}C_{v,r-1}-a_{v-1}C_{v-1,r}. \] It follows by inserting the finite products and clearing their nonzero factorial denominators; the initial coefficients are those of \(f_0,f_1\). This also specifies all boundary terms of the check. Writing \(z=w+w^{-1}\) factors \(P_r=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r\), so all node values for \(0\leq j\leq M\) have the explicit quadratic sum \[ \frac{\kappa\lambda_j}{N^2} =\sum_{v=0}^M\sum_{r=0}^{\min(v,j)} \frac{Q^{r(r-v-j)}F_{2v}F_{j+r}} {F_v^3F_{v-r}F_{j-r}F_r^3}. \tag{11b} \] The NORMAL source must not truncate the same way. For every double node let \(w_j=q^{2j+1}\), and \[ A_{v,r}=\frac{F_{2v}(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_v^4F_r^3}, \quad B_{j,r}=(Q^{j+1};Q)_r(Q^{-j};Q)_r. \] For \(r\leq j\) put \[ D_{j,r}=\sum_{a=0}^{r-1} \left[\frac{Q^{a-j}}{1-Q^{a-j}} -\frac{Q^{a+j+1}}{1-Q^{a+j+1}}\right]. \] Every denominator in this expression is nonzero. Differentiating the full polynomial BEFORE specializing gives the exact normal \[ \frac{\kappa\xi_j}{N^2} =\frac1{w_j-w_j^{-1}}\sum_{v=0}^M \left[\sum_{r=0}^{\min(v,j)}A_{v,r}B_{j,r}D_{j,r} +\sum_{r=j+1}^v A_{v,r}(-1)^jQ^{-j(j+1)/2} F_{j+r}F_{r-j-1}\right]. \tag{11c} \] The second sum is essential. For \(r>j\), the value of \((q/w;Q)_r\) vanishes at \(w_j\), but its logarithmic derivative does not: removing its unique zero gives exactly \((-1)^jQ^{-j(j+1)/2}F_jF_{r-j-1}\). Thus (11c) keeps the first-normal source terms which are invisible in the terminating node-value sum (11b). At the odd simple node \(w=-1\), no first normal is required; the safe polynomial derivative (11) remains available if desired. The audit checks (11a)--(11c) against the original full physical Hermite blocks. ## 5. The unchanged one-variable source and what it does not prove The actual pair source has the exact expression \[ \Phi_2(f(\Omega))= (-1)^d\sum_{j<d-j} [(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)] +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd}}f(-2). \tag{12} \] This follows directly from the generic ordinary pair decomposition and original pivotal partial trace, not from an imported polynomial invariant. At generic angle \(\theta\) the coefficient is the ratio \(\sum_j\sin(n_j\theta)f(2\cos n_j\theta)/\sin(N\theta)\), where \(n_j=2N-1-2j\). At \(\theta=\pi/N\) numerator and denominator vanish. Differentiate: a paired pair has \(n_j+n_{d-j}=2N\), giving the summand in (12). The unpaired \(n_j=N\) gives \(f(-2)\). The original root pivot differs from the ordinary \(K\) pivot by \((-1)^d\), exactly the displayed sign. The actual partial trace is regular, so this computes its value rather than a new derivative source. Equivalently, reduce \(f\) modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), retaining its double roots. Then \[ \Phi_2(f(\Omega))=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f\bmod\mathcal P_N). \tag{13} \] For a direct verification, put \(w_k=q^{2k+1}\). The right side of (12) is \(-(-1)^d\sum_k(w\partial_w)[(w-w^{-1})f(w+w^{-1})]/2\). For degree below \(d\), root Fourier orthogonality annihilates it; at degree \(d\), the coefficients at \(w^{\pm N}\) give \((-1)^dN^2\). This proves (13). Consequently the COMPLETE raw augmented pretzel base at every odd number of boxes is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}(N,\ldots,N) =(-1)^d\sum_{j<d-j} [(4-c_j^2)s\xi_j\lambda_j^{s-1}-c_j\lambda_j^s] +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd}}\lambda_{d/2}^s =(-1)^dN^2[z^d](z_N(z)^s\bmod\mathcal P_N).} \tag{14} \] The literal original marked cut, all half-twist phases and all normal channels remain. For \(N=2\) the polynomial has degree zero and the base is exactly zero. For \(N=3\), (6) is \(z_3(z)=q^2z-1-5i\sqrt3\); (14) at \(s=3\) recovers exactly \(-189+81i\sqrt3\). There is also an exact original one-variable residue and its finite integer windings. For any \(R>1\), parametrizing the enclosing \(z\)-ellipse by \(z=w+w^{-1}\) gives \[ \mathcal A_{s,N} =\frac{(-1)^dN^2}{2\pi i}\int_{|w|=R} z_N(w+w^{-1})^s \frac{w^N(1-w^{-2})}{(1+w^N)^2}\,dw. \tag{15} \] Indeed the coefficient in (13) is the enclosing residue of \(z_N(z)^s/\mathcal P_N(z)\), and \(\mathcal P_N(w+w^{-1})=w^{-N}(1+w^N)^2\). Expanding on the ACTUAL outer circle yields the finite coefficient identity \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}=(-1)^dN^2 \sum_{m=1}^{\lfloor(sM+1)/N\rfloor}(-1)^{m-1}m \left([w^{mN-1}]-[w^{mN+1}]\right) z_N(w+w^{-1})^s.} \tag{16} \] Coefficients outside the Laurent degree range are zero. The \(m\) weight is exactly the double-pole/normal source from (12); it must not be dropped. For \(s=3\) only \(m=1\) can occur. This gives a fixed finite set of true winding channels at each fixed \(s\), not an identification of independent logarithmic aliases. No separation of the unit-circle poles or omission of the \(w=0\) Laurent behavior is used: (15) is an exact parametrization of the original enclosing residue, and (16) is its convergent outer Laurent expansion. The source in (14) is oscillatory. Positive \(b_v\) do not make the \(f_v(c_j)\) real positive, and taking separate absolute values of the nodal terms need not give the sharp antiprism volume. A selected asymptotic evaluation retaining these phases and integer Fourier marks is still required. No nonzero geometric coefficient, open cusp-color corridor or simultaneous long-filling survival is claimed by this exact finite reduction.

title: An exact cusp-color split with a controlled original normal-source remainder
text: # An exact cusp-color split with a controlled original normal-source remainder 29 October 2026. For every \(j=N-r\) with \(0\leq r\leq\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), the literal rotated pretzel circle box has a positive half-degree core plus an original crossing times a degree-\(r-1\) polynomial. The entire second band, including every Casimir normal jet, has norm at most \(56^r\) in a faithful source-compatible Hermite norm. Thus it costs \(\exp(O(\delta N))\) on a fixed cusp-color corridor \(r\leq\delta N\), and subexponentially when \(r=o(N)\). No term is deleted. This is not yet a geometric survival theorem. The low core still requires its selected asymptotic analysis; estimates of a remainder do not prove that the whole original coefficient is nonzero. ## 1. The entire rotated polynomial, with its two support bands Use the original conventions and actual rotation \(\mathscr R\) of [the complete-base polynomial theorem](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). Let \(f_v\) be the physical middle-degree continuant polynomials, \(s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|\), \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), \(d=N-1\). Then \[ \mathscr R(R^{-1}L_{N-r})=z_{N,r}(\Omega),\qquad z_{N,r}(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^d a_{r,v}f_v(z), \] \[ \boxed{\quad a_{r,v}=s_{d-v}^2q^{r^2-v^2} {2v\brack v-r}_Q.\quad} \tag{1} \] The Gaussian coefficient is its finite polynomial, not an invalid factorial ratio at a root. A negative lower index gives zero. For the displayed cusp corridor its support and all phases are exactly \[ a_{r,v}=\frac{s_{d-v}^2s_{2v}}{s_{v-r}s_{v+r}}>0, \quad r\leq v\leq M, \tag{2} \] \[ a_{r,N-t}=(-1)^{N-t-r} \frac{s_{t-1}^2s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}}, \quad 1\leq t\leq r, \tag{3} \] and it is zero elsewhere. In particular the middle band is exactly zero. For \(r=0\), (2) is the positive complete-base coefficient \(b_v=N^2s_{2v}/s_v^4\), and there is no upper band. Proof by a finite resolvent, not a semiclassical approximation. In the low block of degree \(K=d-v\), the first-to-last entry of \((I-tJ_K+t^2I)^{-1}\) is \[ \frac{t^K B_K}{\prod_{k=0}^K(1-q^{2k+1}t)(1-q^{-2k-1}t)}, \qquad B_K=(-1)^Ks_K^2. \] Its \(t^{j-1}\) coefficient is the first-to-last entry of \(U_{j-1}(J_K/2)\). The full two-copy root orbit factors the inverse denominator as \[ \frac{(q^{1-2v}t;Q)_{2v}}{(1+t^N)^2}. \] The needed remaining coefficient has degree \(v-r<N\), so the denominator contributes exactly 1. The finite q-binomial theorem, the original circle sign \((-1)^{j-1}\), and the literal \(R^{-1}\) last-row coefficient give precisely (1). This derivation retains both the actual pivotal circle normalization and its half twist. If \(2v<N\), the Gaussian phase in (1) cancels, giving (2). If \(2v\geq N\) and \(v-r<N\), split one whole root orbit from the finite q-binomial product. Its factor has no coefficient in degrees \(1,\ldots,N-1\). Thus \({2v\brack v-r}_Q={2v-N\brack v-r}_Q\), which is zero unless \(v+r\geq N\). Taking its explicit phase and complementing the remaining sine factorials gives (3). This proves the exact bands without division by a vanished factorial. ## 2. The upper band is an original crossing times a SHORT polynomial Let \(\bar f_l\) mean coefficient conjugation at the specified principal root. Reversing the physical Jacobi recurrence gives \[ f_{d-l}(\Omega)=f_d(\Omega)\bar f_l(\Omega), \qquad f_d(\Omega)=x^d r_N(\Omega). \] Indeed \(e_0^Tf_d(A)=e_d^T\) and \(e_d^T\bar f_l(A)=e_{d-l}^T\); the cyclic first row proves the polynomial identity modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N\), including every double root. Since \(x^d=\kappa^2\), define \[ c_{N,r}(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=r}^M a_{r,v}f_v(z), \quad P_{N,r}(z)=\sum_{t=1}^r(-1)^{N-t-r} \frac{s_{t-1}^2s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}} \bar f_{t-1}(z). \] The exact ALL-INPUT identity is \[ \boxed{\quad z_{N,r}(\Omega)=c_{N,r}(\Omega) +R P_{N,r}(\Omega).\quad} \tag{4} \] For \(r=1\) its remainder is \((-1)^N R\). Thus the short sector is not identically zero, and it cannot be removed by restricting to the original cup or by retaining only the complete-circle quotient. ## 3. Uniform quantitative bound WITH every original normal jet On \(\mathbb C[z]/(\mathcal P_N)\) use the faithful Hermite norm \[ \|f\|_{\mathrm H}= \max\left\{\max_{c\ \mathrm{double}} (|f(c)|+N^{-2}|f'(c)|),\quad |f(-2)|\ \mathrm{if\ }N\mathrm{\ is\ odd}\right\}. \tag{5} \] It includes values and ALL first-normal coefficients; the simple node has only its value. It is submultiplicative. The literal crossing has \(\|R\|_{\mathrm H}\leq9/8\), by its original unit nodal values and \(|r_N'/r_N|\leq N^2/8\). The original source has \[ |\Phi_2(f)|\leq3N^3\|f\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{6} \] This follows immediately from the exact source values and derivatives in the complete-base theorem. In particular this norm does not discard the nilpotent source as an ordinary semisimple quotient would. There is a constant independent of \(N,r\), explicitly \[ \boxed{\quad \|R P_{N,r}\|_{\mathrm H}\leq56^r, \qquad 1\leq r\leq M.\quad} \tag{7} \] Here is a direct proof of the bound, including the cancellation of small factorial denominators. Write the MONIC physical continuant as \(p_l=(a_0\cdots a_{l-1})f_l\), so \(|a_0\cdots a_{l-1}|=s_l^2\). On \(|z|\leq2\), its recurrence has \(|z-D_l|\leq12\) and \(|a_{l-1}^2|\leq16\). Induction gives \[ |p_l(z)|\leq14^l,\qquad |p_l'(z)|\leq l14^{l-1}. \] The coefficient in (3) divided by \(s_{t-1}^2\) has magnitude \[ \frac{s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}} =\left|{t+r-1\brack 2t-1}_Q\right| \leq {t+r-1\choose 2t-1}\leq4^r. \] The first inequality follows from the nonnegative integer coefficients of the finite Gaussian polynomial (or its elementary Pascal induction), since its argument has modulus one. Therefore the \(s_{t-1}^2\) CANCELS the full denominator of \(\bar f_{t-1}\) before estimating any normal derivative. Summing the geometric series in \(14^{t-1}\), and multiplying by \(9/8\), proves (7) with room to spare. No \(N^{O(r)}\) loss occurs. There is also a full physical operator bound \[ \|P_{N,r}(\Omega)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq120^r, \qquad \|R P_{N,r}(\Omega)\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq120^r\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}. \tag{8} \] Indeed every physical \(\Omega\) block has norm at most18; the same monic recurrence is bounded by \(30^l\) when evaluated at this operator. The preceding factorial cancellation proves (8). The factor \(\|R\|\) cannot be discarded: already \(r=1\) the remainder is the whole original crossing. Thus (7), which is the faithful normal-source bound needed here, is stronger than a claim of uniform physical contraction would be and has a different scope. ## 4. Exact simultaneous original-source error accounting For arbitrary fixed \(s\), substitute (4) at every augmented pretzel box BEFORE applying the original source. The difference between the complete mixed-color period and its low-core product is exactly the sum over nonempty subsets of the retained remainder boxes. Equations (5)--(7) give the explicit bound, with \(\epsilon_0=0\) and \(\epsilon_r=56^r\) for \(r\geq1\), \[ \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,r_i} -\prod_i c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq3N^3\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subset\{1,\ldots,s\}} \prod_{i\in S}\epsilon_{r_i} \prod_{i\notin S}\|c_{N,r_i}\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{9} \] For \(r_i\leq\delta N\) the individual retained source remainders have rate at most \(\delta\log56\); for \(r_i=o(N)\) that rate is zero. This is an independently quantified actual source term. It does not make the TOTAL right side negligible relative to the geometric period without estimates of the coherent core and its selected action gap. No open-corridor noncancellation or long-filling survival is asserted from (9) alone.

title: Survival of the original filling sum restricted to a cusp-color corridor
text: # Survival of the original filling sum restricted to a cusp-color corridor 29 October 2026. For every fixed odd box count s>=5 there is a fixed complete-color corridor in which the ENTIRE original coherent filling sum has a nonzero selected asymptotic, for all independently sufficiently large signed integer slopes. This includes all physical normal jets, the actual half-color weight, every Fourier charge and the original marked source. It does not estimate the complementary physical colors, and therefore is not yet a theorem about the whole filled knot. ## 1. The precise truncated original scalar Use q,Q,kappa,d and the original mixed marked source A_(s,N)(h). For an integer P let beta_j^(P) be the ACTUAL circle-basis coefficient of r_N^(2P); the full R^(2P) includes the factor kappa^(2P). Choose a sufficiently small fixed delta>0 and H=floor(delta N). For fixed nonzero integers p_i define \[ \mathcal K_{N,\delta}^{\boldsymbol p} =\kappa^{-2\sum_i p_i} \sum_{h_1,\ldots,h_s=0}^{H} \prod_i\beta_{N-h_i-1}^{(-p_i)} A_{s,N}(h_1,\ldots,h_s). \tag{1} \] This is the indicated physical color corridor of the actual boxes rotation(R^(-(2p_i+1))). It is not a single color term. No new modified dimension is placed on the ordinary auxiliary loops. There is p_0(s,delta) such that for EVERY FIXED tuple |p_i|>=p_0, with no comparability condition between slopes, (1) has \[ \boxed{\mathcal K_{N,\delta}^{\boldsymbol p} =N^{3/2}e^{-is\pi d/4}\kappa^{-\sum_i p_i} D_s(\boldsymbol p)e^{N\mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p)} (1+O_{s,\boldsymbol p}(N^{-1})),} \tag{2} \] where D_s is explicitly specified below and is NONZERO. This holds at both parities and all composite levels as N tends to infinity. The slopes are fixed before this limit; no claim uniform in growing slopes is made. ## 2. The source action, actual Fourier amplitude and leading constant Let C_N be the EXACT finite packet in [the analytic color-source theorem](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md). It has the SAME original full-Hermite Phi_2 functional. Its uniform complex asymptotic supplies A_s(chi),Phi_s(chi), with F_0=Phi_s(0)=V_s/(2pi), A_s(0)=C_s !=0, phi(x)=Phi_s(pi x), phi''(0)=2pi i tau_s I, tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, Im tau_s>0. The exact Fourier-packet theorem in [the source Fourier estimate](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), section6, gives holomorphic even functions xi(z),Psi(z),B(z): grad phi(xi)+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi)+2pi i xi dot z, B(z)=(2pi)^(s/2) A_s(pi xi)/sqrt(det[-phi''(xi)]). Thus Psi=F_0-i pi sum z_i^2/tau_s+O(||z||^4), and B is nonzero near zero. These are defined by the original selected packet, not an arbitrary classical branch. Put T_m(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). For sufficiently large |p_i| the all-unit charge m=(1,...,1) has the unique nearby critical point z_*=z_(1,...,1). Define \[ \mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p)=T_{\boldsymbol1}(z_*),\qquad D_s(\boldsymbol p)= \frac{2^s(2\pi)^{s/2}B(z_*)\prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_{*,i})} {\sqrt{\det[-T_{\boldsymbol1}''(z_*)]}}. \tag{3} \] Every square root is the one from the actual translated real Gaussian contour. Equivalently it is the analytic Gaussian branch on complex symmetric matrices with positive definite real part, fixed positive on real positive matrices. This retains the signed slope Gaussian phases, rather than choosing their moduli. The [local charge theorem](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md) proves that every z_(star,i) is nonzero, |z_(star,i)|<1/4, and the Hessian is nondegenerate. Consequently every factor in (3) is nonzero. In particular D_s is not a postulated cycle coefficient. The actual critical action has Re A_s(p)=F_0-pi Im(tau_s) sum_i |1+2p_i tau_s|^(-2)+O(sum_i |p_i|^(-4)), where the exact holomorphic action in (3), not this truncation, is used in (2). Its geometric peripheral interpretation is separate. ## 3. Exact source replacement and finite charge reduction The source theorem proves, on the physical grid in (1), |A_(s,N)(h)-C_N(pi h/N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F_0-gamma)], gamma>0. Since |beta_j^(-p)|<=2(1+|p|), replacing A by C in the WHOLE truncated sum costs poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-gamma)]. The upper color aliases need not be even and are estimated here, BEFORE folding. No full physical source is analytically continued by fiat. The exact C_N is even in each color. Apply the physical Weyl half weight and the full normal kernel in every coordinate. With mathcalF_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(pi h/N)exp(2pi i h dot z), the SAME truncated packet is exactly \[ (-1)^{s(N-1)}\kappa^{-\sum_i p_i} \sum_{m_i\ne0}(-1)^{(N-1)\sum_i m_i}\prod_i m_i \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^s} e^{-2\pi iN\sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i)} \prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_i)\mathcal F_N(z)\,dz. \tag{4} \] The source Fourier theorem proves a UNIFORM exponentially gapped tail outside |m_i|<=M_i, where one may take M_i>=2|p_i|+2delta+2. Its gap depends only on the SOURCE, not on the largest slope: the paired vertical current keeps its growth exp(2pi|p_i|Nv), which the larger charge absorbs. Shrinking the contour as 1/|p_i| would not give the needed independent-slope conclusion.
