The faithful norm and all source normalizations are retained from [the two-band theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_color_two_band_bound.md). ## 1. A bounded dual Casimir on a coherent circle Let \(\mathscr R\) be the literal quarter-turn, and define \(\mathcal D=\mathscr R\circ(\Omega\cdot)\circ\mathscr R^{-1}\) on the physical pair commutant. In the physical continuant basis, \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal D f_v=c_v f_v+b_v f_{v-1},\qquad c_v=q^{2v+1}+q^{-2v-1},\quad b_v=Q^v+Q^{-v}-2.\quad} \tag{2} \] Here \(b_0=0\). This operator preserves polynomial degree, including in the full degree-\(d\) algebra, so it preserves the low core. For completeness, (2) follows from an actual Hopf Ward identity. For a pair intertwiner \(B\), write \(\beta_v=B_{d,v;d,v}\). The original coproduct of \(F\) gives \[ B_{d-1,v+1;d,v}= x^{-1}Q^d\frac{1-Q^{v+1}}{1-Q^d} (\beta_{v+1}-\beta_v). \tag{3} \] The last row of the physical \(\Omega\) block of total degree \(d+v\) has off-diagonal \(Q^{-1}(1-Q)(1-Q^{-v-1})\) and diagonal \(2q^{-1}+(q-q^{-1})Q^{-v-1}\). Inserting (3) gives \[ (\Omega B)_{d,v;d,v} =c_v\beta_v+ q^{-1}(1-Q^{v+1})(1-Q^{-v-1})\beta_{v+1}. \] The first row of the rotated box is \(x^{v-d}\beta_v\); its adjacent phase converts the second coefficient to \(b_{v+1}\). The cyclic first row of the middle Casimir block proves (2) for the entire commutant, not just its semisimple quotient. In the symmetric Laurent variable \(z=w+w^{-1}\), (2) is the explicit rational difference operator \[ (\mathcal D F)(w)=a(w)F(Qw)+a(w^{-1})F(Q^{-1}w)+c(w)F(w), \tag{4} \] \[ a(w)=\frac{(qw-1)^3}{q(w^2-1)(qw+1)},\qquad a(w^{-1})=\frac{(w-q)^3}{q(w+q)(w^2-1)},\qquad c(w)=\frac{8qw}{(w+q)(qw+1)}. \] Here \(F(w)\) means \(f(w+w^{-1})\). This formula is exact at the specified root and retains every normal coefficient. Its apparent poles are removable on symmetric Laurent polynomials. An all-degree algebra check of (4) is short. Put \(P_r(w)=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r\). The two shifted product ratios give \[ \mathcal D P_r=c_rP_r- \frac{(Q^r-1)^4}{qQ^r}P_{r-1}. \tag{5} \] Expand the physical continuant by its finite identity \[ f_v=x^v\sum_{r=0}^v \frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r. \] The ratios of adjacent coefficients are \((1-Q^{r-v})Q/(1-Q^{r+1})^3\) and \(x^{-1}(1-Q^{r-v})/(1-Q^{-v})\). Substitution in (5) proves (2) coefficient by coefficient. All denominators \(F_r\) here have \(r<N\); no root-zero division or omitted self-pair is used. For every fixed radius \(\varrho>1\), let \(\|f\|_{\varrho}=\max_{|w|=\varrho}|f(w+w^{-1})|\). Since \(|Q|=1\), the shifts preserve that circle, and (4) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathcal D f\|_{\varrho} \leq K_{\varrho}\|f\|_{\varrho},\qquad K_{\varrho}=2+\frac{16\varrho}{(\varrho-1)^2}.\quad} \tag{6} \] Indeed each shifted coefficient is at most \((\varrho+1)^2/(\varrho-1)^2\), and the central one at most \(8\varrho/(\varrho-1)^2\). The constant is independent of \(N\), polynomial degree and color deficit. ## 2. All low cores are generated from the complete core Let \(\mathsf T_r(z)=2\cos(r\arccos(z/2))\), including \(\mathsf T_0=2\). The elementary sine addition identity, reduced modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N=\mathsf T_N+2\), gives \[ L_{N-r}=(-1)^N L_r+ \frac{(-1)^r}{2}\mathsf T_r(\Omega)L_N. \tag{7} \] Multiply by the literal half twist \(R^{-1}\), then rotate. For \(1\leq r\leq M\), the rotated \(R^{-1}L_r\) has only the high continuant band \(v\geq N-r>M\); this is the same finite Gaussian support computation used in the two-band theorem. The second term of (7) has degree at most \(M\) after rotation, by (2). Consequently the low-degree projection is exactly \[ \boxed{\quad c_{N,r}=\frac{(-1)^r}{2} \mathsf T_r(\mathcal D)z_N.\quad} \tag{8} \] The Chebyshev recurrence and (6) imply, also for \(r=0\), \[ \|c_{N,r}\|_{\varrho} \leq (K_{\varrho}+1)^r\|z_N\|_{\varrho}. \tag{9} \] This keeps the coherent complete-base polynomial. Bounding its continuant summands separately is unnecessary. The interval \([-2,2]\) lies inside the ellipse \(w+w^{-1}\), \(|w|=\varrho\). By the maximum principle and the ordinary degree-\(M\) Markov inequality, applied to a real part after a unit phase rotation at each derivative evaluation, \[ \|c_{N,r}\|_{\mathrm H} \leq(1+M^2/N^2)\|c_{N,r}\|_{\varrho} \leq\frac54(K_{\varrho}+1)^r\|z_N\|_{\varrho}. \tag{10} \] Thus the passage to the faithful normal-source norm costs only a constant. It does not drop the source derivative. ## 3. A strict source alias gap for every odd \(s\geq5\) The proved coherent-circle theorem in [the complete-base asymptotic](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) gives, for each fixed \(\eta>0\), \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log\|z_N\|_{e^\eta}\leq j(\eta),\qquad j(0)=\frac{v_8}{\pi},\qquad j'(\eta)=\frac1\pi\arctan\sinh(\eta/2). \tag{11} \] In particular \(j(\eta)-j(0)=O(\eta^2)\). Uniformly over every integer color choice \(0\leq r_i\leq\delta N\), a source term with a nonempty alias set \(S\), \(|S|=m\), has upper rate \[ \frac1N\log\left|\Phi_2\left( \prod_{i\in S}RP_{N,r_i} \prod_{i\notin S}c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq (s-m)j(\eta) +\delta\big[(s-m)\log(K_{e^\eta}+1)+m\log56\big]+o(1). \tag{12} \] The \(o(1)\) is uniform in these colors. This is (1), (10), submultiplicativity of the faithful norm, and the exact estimate \(|\Phi_2(f)|\leq3N^3\|f\|_{\mathrm H}\). The finite sum of at most \(2^s-1\) such terms has the same upper rate. All original circle, half-twist and source phases remain in the exact terms being bounded. Let \[ A_s=\frac{V_s}{2\pi} =\frac{4s}{\pi} \left[\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2s}\right) +\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4-\frac\pi{2s}\right)\right]. \] The complete-base theorem proves the original source has rate \(A_s\). Its margin over the worst alias envelope at \(\delta=0\) is \[ g_s=A_s-(s-1)j(0)>0\qquad(s\geq5). \tag{13} \] Here is an elementary uniform proof. With \(A(\alpha)=\Lambda(\pi/4+\alpha/2)+ \Lambda(\pi/4-\alpha/2)\), \(A(0)=G\) (Catalan's constant), \(A'(0)=0\), and \(A''(\alpha)=-1/(2\cos\alpha)\). Hence \[ g_s\geq\frac{4G}{\pi}- \frac{\pi}{s\cos(\pi/s)}>0 \qquad(s\geq5). \] Indeed the second summand is less than 1 for \(s\geq5\), while \(4G/\pi>1\), for example from \(G>1-1/9\). Fix \(\eta>0\) with \((s-1)(j(\eta)-j(0))<g_s/4\), and then fix \(\delta>0\) so that \(s\delta[\log(K_{e^\eta}+1)+\log56]<g_s/4\), and also \(\delta<1/4\). Equations (12)--(13) prove the genuine uniform original-source bound \[ \boxed{\quad \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,r_i} -\prod_i c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq \exp\{N(A_s-g_s/2+o(1))\}, \quad 0\leq r_i\leq\delta N, \quad s\geq5\text{ odd}.\quad} \tag{14} \] One may choose \(\eta\) of order \(\sqrt\delta\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\); (12) then loses \(O_s(\delta\log(1/\delta))\) above \((s-1)j(0)\). This optimization is not needed for the fixed-corridor theorem. The proof does not estimate the low-core **selected period** from below, does not supply a gap for all colors outside the corridor, and does not sum the filling kernels. Those are separate questions. ## 4. The other color-cube corners are also controlled For an actual small ordinary color \(1\leq j\leq M\), the same finite Gaussian support computation gives a pure high band. Exact sine-factorial complementation gives the particularly simple identity \[ \boxed{\qquad z_{N,N-j}=(-1)^N R P_{N,j},\qquad \|z_{N,N-j}\|_{\mathrm H}\leq56^j.\qquad} \tag{15} \] For example \(j=1\) is exactly the original crossing \(R\). To see that the uniform constant does not acquire an extra \(N^{O(j)}\) factor, the apparent upper-band ratio is \[ \frac{s_{N-j+t-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{N-j-t}} =\frac{s_{j+t-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{j-t}},\qquad1\leq t\leq j. \] It is the SAME short Gaussian ratio as in the \(56^j\) proof. All large factorial indices are complemented before estimating. Consequently let every actual color \(j_i\) lie either in the low corner \(1\leq j_i\leq\delta N\) or the complete corner \(N-\delta N\leq j_i\leq N\). If at least one color is in the low corner, expand only the complete-corner colors by (1). Every resulting term has at least one short crossing sector. The proof of (14) therefore gives uniformly \[ \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,N-j_i}\right)\right| \leq\exp\{N(A_s-g_s/2+o(1))\},\qquad s\geq5\text{ odd}. \tag{16} \] Thus all the OTHER binary corners of the original color cube have a rigorous gap. This does not cover its intermediate-color slabs. ## 5. The three-box endpoint is genuinely source-sensitive For \(s=3\), \(A_3=2j(0)\), so (13) has zero margin. The full source \(\Phi_2(Rz_N^2)\) is a useful diagnostic: its nodal maximum has rate approaching \(2j(0)\), but direct evaluation of the complete derivative-plus-value source at levels \(N=16,32,64,128\) gives respectively \[ N^{-1}\log|\Phi_2(Rz_N^2)|= 1.2930259621,\ 1.2612009276,\ 1.2297272136,\ 1.2060473620. \] These finite values suggest an additional source cancellation. They neither prove its rate nor justify a uniform mixed-color gap. The accompanying audit retains the exact crossing derivative in this diagnostic and replays the high-level value at doubled precision. ## 6. The global intermediate-color test remains a diagnostic [The separate exact-source diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_pretzel_global_colored_source.py) evaluates all equal-color and all single-changed-color periods at \(N=24,48,72\), \(s=3,5\), using the literal all-color two-band coefficients and the complete derivative-plus-value functional. It also checks 544 sorted mixed-color samples at \(N=48\), and replays the selected source values at doubled precision. The sampled maximum is complete color; the largest noncomplete sampled tuples are \((0,0,4)\) and \((0,0,0,0,4)\) in color deficits. This supplies no uniform asymptotic upper bound for intermediate colors or for the unsampled mixed-color cube. In particular it is not an input to (14) or (16).

title: Survival of the full original mixed-color pretzel period near completeness
text: # Survival of the full original mixed-color pretzel period near completeness 29 October 2026. Proof assembly for source reconstruction, marked normalizations, analytic interpolation and contour estimates. The discrete summation proof below uses the exact finite cotangent contour, retaining every endpoint current. For every fixed odd s>=5, a fixed open cusp-color corridor has a nonzero selected asymptotic for the FULL original mixed-color augmented source. The upper color band, lower inner indices, finite-grid residuals and original Hermite marked functional are all estimated. This is a mixed-source theorem; the subsequent coherent filling sum is not replaced by one of its terms. ## 1. Statement and unchanged source Let z_(N,h)=rotation(R^(-1)L_(N-h)) be the full physical polynomial from the two-band source theorem, and put A_(s,N)(h_1,...,h_s)=Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)). All auxiliary colors are actual integers j_i=N-h_i. For each fixed odd s>=5 there is delta_s>0 such that, uniformly for 0<=h_i<=delta_s N and chi_i=pi h_i/N, A_(s,N)(h)=N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi(N-1)/4) A_s(chi) exp[N Phi_s(chi)](1+O(1/N)). (1) The functions Phi_s and A_s below are holomorphic on a fixed complex neighborhood of chi=0, even separately in each chi_i, and A_s has no zeros there. At the complete point, Phi_s(0)=V_s/(2pi), A_s(0)=C_s, with the SAME V_s,C_s as the complete augmented-period theorem. Evenness of the amplitude follows from the full low-core coefficients; its definition by analytic continuation is fixed at the complete point. The full physical polynomial contains a non-even alias band, but that band is exponentially smaller in this corridor. In particular (1) is actual uniform noncancellation on an OPEN macroscopic corridor h_i<=delta_s N, not only fixed normal jets or h_i=o(N). The choice s>=5 is used for the independently quantified alias gap; no assertion for s=3 is inferred from that estimate. ## 2. The analytic high-index phase is attached to the finite source Use the notation S(tau,chi), C(tau,chi) of the [mixed inner source theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md), and define the analytic sine primitive J_sin(tau)=integral_0^tau Log(2sin(pi t))dt. On a fixed high-index neighborhood tau>1/4 and small complex chi put B(tau,chi)=S(tau,chi)-S(tau,0) +2J_sin(tau)-J_sin(tau-chi/pi)-J_sin(tau+chi/pi), D(tau,chi)=[C(tau,chi)/C(tau,0)] sin(pi tau)/sqrt(sin(pi tau-chi)sin(pi tau+chi)). (2) All roots and logarithms continue from their positive real complete values. These functions are even in chi, B(tau,0)=0, D(tau,0)=1, and D is nonzero after shrinking the neighborhood. These expressions follow from the actual coefficient, not a new semiclassical normalization. Indeed q^(h^2)D_(h,r)/D_(0,r) =G_N(r)^2/[G_N(r-h)G_N(r+h)], where G_N is the positive sine-factorial completion. Its bulk asymptotic has exponential part 2J_sin(tau)-J_sin(tau-chi/pi) -J_sin(tau+chi/pi) and prefactor sin(pi tau)/sqrt(sin(pi tau-chi)sin(pi tau+chi)). Multiplying by the SELECTED inner U_(h,r), including its exponentially accurate analytic interpolant, gives (2). For w=-exp(eta), define the analytic phase Psi(u,eta,chi)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2u)Log(2cosh eta+2cos v)dv +B(u/pi,chi). (3) The analytic continuation of Lambda on this regular u-neighborhood is fixed by its real values. At chi=0 this is the already calibrated complete Newton phase. For real eta near eta_s=2asinh(tan(pi/s)), its complete critical index is u_0(eta)=atan(cosh(eta/2)), Psi_uu(u_0,eta,0)<0. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem therefore specifies a unique critical u_*(eta,chi) near u_0, and j(eta,chi)=Psi(u_*(eta,chi),eta,chi). (4) The local amplitude is explicitly a(eta,chi)=1/(4sqrt(pi)) [sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2)] exp(iu_*/2) D(u_*/pi,chi)/sqrt(-Psi_uu(u_*,eta,chi)). (5) All factors are nonzero near completeness. At chi=0 this reduces to exp(iu_0/2)/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)], T=2cosh eta. ## 3. Discrete analytic Laplace lemma, including its actual error barrier Here is the precise local summation argument used in (4),(5). Choose a fixed real index window [a,b] about u_0, strictly within (pi/4,pi/2). Choose its physical endpoints on the grid pi r/N; their O(1/N) motion does not change any of the fixed gaps below. The source theorem supplies an analytic interpolation of its inner packet on a FIXED complex window, with relative grid residual O(exp(-cN)), uniform in small complex chi. Retain that residual. The original Newton factor has an analytic interpolation there too. With alpha_+=(N+1)/2-iN eta/(2pi), alpha_-=(N+1)/2+iN eta/(2pi), take Bhat_N(r,eta)=q^(-r^2) Fhat_N(alpha_++r-1)Fhat_N(alpha_-+r-1) /[Fhat_N(alpha_+-1)Fhat_N(alpha_--1)]. (6) At every integer r this is EXACTLY product_(k<r) (2cos((2k+1)pi/N)+2cosh eta). All four factorial arguments remain in regular compact substrips. Their marked bulk expansions give the integral term in (3), with leading prefactor ONE: the half-step in alpha_± cancels the two endpoint square-root factors. This continues uniformly to complex u=pi r/N and eta in fixed smaller neighborhoods; no extrapolation from real integer values is used. The remaining original factorial factors use the same Fhat/G_N completion. Thus the interpolated high-window summand is holomorphic and equals its explicit nonzero amplitude times exp(N Psi), with a uniform analytic relative O(1/N) error. On the physical grid it agrees with the original summand up to the RETAINED exponentially small inner residual. Use the following EXACT finite cotangent formula, which avoids any conditional sum of Poisson endpoint terms. For the integers k<=r<=l in this window, place its vertical sides at the HALF-grid points a_N=(k-1/2)pi/N and b_N=(l+1/2)pi/N. Let f_N(u) denote the analytic interpolated r-summand, with all the prefactors just specified, and let Gamma be the positively oriented rectangle with these vertical sides and fixed imaginary heights +/-d. Then sum_(r=k)^l f_N(pi r/N) =N/(2pi i) integral_Gamma f_N(u)cot(Nu)du. (3a) This is the interpolated-grid sum; its retained difference from the original source grid is bounded separately below. The residue of cot(Nu) at each enclosed physical point is 1/N, so (3a) has no endpoint half weights or new lattice multiplicity. Choose d>0 inside the fixed holomorphic tube. The complete real phase has a fixed gap at both window endpoints. By continuity, the full vertical sides stay below Re j by a fixed amount, uniformly after making d and then the eta,chi neighborhoods sufficiently small. On those sides cot(N(a_N+it))=-i tanh(Nt), and similarly at b_N, so its modulus is at most one. Their ENTIRE integrals are therefore poly(N)exp[N(Re j-gamma)] for some gamma>0. They are retained currents, not terms assigned value zero. On the upper and lower horizontal sides, respectively, cot(Nu)=-i+O(exp(-2Nd)), cot(Nu)=+i+O(exp(-2Nd)). At the complete real parameters, holomorphic Taylor expansion gives sup Re Psi(x+/-id)<=j_0+C d^2 for real x in the window: its first normal derivative is imaginary there. The eta and chi perturbations change this bound and Re j continuously by O(|eta-eta_s|+|chi|^2). Choose d first with C d^2<d/4, and then the fixed parameter neighborhood with this perturbation less than d/4. The horizontal cotangent remainders consequently have a uniform fixed exponential gap. This bounds ALL nonzero Fourier modes together, without an unsupported absolute summation of individual 1/m endpoint terms. Shrink that neighborhood also so that |Im u_*|<d/2 and Re u_* stays a fixed positive distance from both vertical sides. With the counterclockwise orientation, the two constant cotangent parts give N/(2pi) times the sum of the lower and upper left-to-right ordinary integrals. Deform EACH ordinary integral inside the analytic rectangle to the horizontal segment through u_*(eta,chi). The connecting vertical segments at a_N,b_N have the already proved endpoint gap. Away from a small central neighborhood, the shifted segment has the same strict gap by the complete profile and small parameter continuity. In the center, Re Psi<=Re j-c_1|u-u_*|^2. Thus both ordinary integrals give the SAME saddle integral, with total coefficient N/pi. Uniform analytic Gaussian expansion gives exactly (5), with relative O(1/N). No unknown original-cycle intersection number is assigned. The total grid-residual contribution is at most poly(N)exp[N(j_0+C|eta-eta_s|+C|chi|^2-c)], by the source theorem, where j_0 is the complete action at eta_s. Choose the fixed eta neighborhood and chi disk so small that this remains exponentially below Re j. This is WHY relative O(1/N) accuracy on the real grid alone would not suffice, and why the exponential interpolation is used here. ## 4. The lower indices and the rest of the circle are genuinely smaller The full physical real-color bound in the mixed source theorem gives |q^(h^2)A_(h,r)/D_(0,r)| <=poly(N)exp[N(E(pi r/N)+C chi^2)], (7) including r<h. The complete-circle proof showed that the positive Newton envelope J_R(u)+E(u) has a unique maximum at u_0>pi/4, with a strict gap on u<=pi/4 and on every complement of a fixed neighborhood of u_0. Its angular envelope also has a strict gap away from the negative axis. Both gaps persist for fixed sufficiently small REAL chi by (7) and continuity. The high-index WKB provides the same bound on the remaining compact index intervals. Consequently the box's original low core satisfies, uniformly on a fixed complex neighborhood of the negative point of the circle, for the physical REAL chi on its specified integer-color grid, c_(N,h)(-exp eta-exp(-eta)) =exp(-i pi(N-1)/4)a(eta,chi) exp[Nj(eta,chi)](1+O(1/N)), (8) up to an exponentially smaller retained remainder. On the original circle outside that neighborhood, the entire low core has a fixed exponential gap relative to the complete maximum, persisting for small chi. These assertions use the actual real-grid lower packets; no off-grid extension of the region r<h is needed. The leading functions a,j are holomorphic in chi; this statement does not identify an unexamined off-grid continuation of those lower physical packets with that holomorphic leading expression. In (8) eta varies in a fixed complex neighborhood, while chi is a PHYSICAL REAL color pi h/N. The leading functions and high-index interpolants are holomorphic in chi; no analytic continuation of the full low-index physical packet is asserted here. ## 5. The original marked period, followed by the alias estimate For the product of low cores the exact marked residue is (-1)^(N-1) N^2/(2pi i) integral_(|w|=R_s) product_i c_(N,h_i)(w+w^(-1)) w^N(1-w^(-2))/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (9) Let eta_*(chi) be the unique nearby solution sum_i partial_eta j(eta_*,chi_i)=1. It exists since the complete derivative of the left side is s cos(pi/s)/(2pi)>0. Define Phi_s(chi)=sum_i j(eta_*,chi_i)-eta_*, A_s(chi)=2sinh(eta_*) product_i a(eta_*,chi_i) /sqrt(2pi sum_i partial_eta^2 j(eta_*,chi_i)). (10) The branch of the square root is fixed at the complete real point. The same finite complex-contour argument as in section3, now in eta=log(-w), moves the central arc to eta_*. No pole of (9) is crossed: Re eta remains strictly positive. The global circle gaps in section4 control its complement. The real Gaussian integral along the local vertical direction gives (1) for the low-core product, with the original sign and N^(3/2) normalization exactly as in the complete-period proof. Finally the [uniform original alias source gap](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) proves for odd s>=5, and a sufficiently small fixed corridor, |Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)-product_i c_(N,h_i))| <=poly(N)exp[N(Phi_s(0)-gamma_s)], gamma_s>0. (11) Shrink delta_s until Re Phi_s(chi)>Phi_s(0)-gamma_s/2. Then (11) is exponentially smaller than the just computed nonzero core period. This proves (1) for the FULL original source, keeping every normal derivative and every nonempty alias subset. ## 6. Quantitative curvature and what filling still requires The leading action is even in each chi_i. Its quadratic term can be calculated directly from the actual mixed recurrence, without assuming a topological longitude convention. Normalize by D_(0,r), put u=pi r/N, Y=exp(2iu), c=cot(u)^2, and write its classical backward eigenvalues as Y^(-1)v. Then v^2-[(c-1)cos(chi)^2-2i sqrt(c)sin(chi)^2]v-c=0. The selected high-index root is v=-1 at chi=0. Differentiation in chi^2 gives delta Log(Y^(-1)v)=Y chi^2+O(chi^4). The actual endpoint factor has zero leading action. Therefore j(eta,chi)=j(eta,0) -(1+Y_*(eta))chi^2/(2pi i)+O(chi^4). Envelope differentiation at the outer critical point gives Phi_s(chi)=V_s/(2pi) -(1+Y_s)/(2pi i) sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4), Y_s=exp(2iu_s), u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)). (12) In particular on the real physical corridor, Re Phi_s(chi)=V_s/(2pi) -sin(2u_s)/(2pi) sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4). (13) This proves strict quadratic decay away from complete color within that corridor, as well as a nonzero analytic leading amplitude. The next operation is still the ENTIRE original filling-color sum. Its exact Weyl fold and normal-weighted Gaussian kernel must be combined with (1), and intermediate colors outside this corridor must be bounded. No independent full-twist factor may be discarded. The identification of the filled critical action with the marked geometric volume must also respect the actual meridian/longitude orientation. A complete augmented-source or mixed-cusp theorem is not a fixed filled-knot volume theorem.

title: Mixed cusp-color inner packets: exact source and uniform holomorphic WKB
text: # Mixed cusp-color inner packets: exact source and uniform holomorphic WKB 29 October 2026. The low core of the ACTUAL rotated circle of color j=N-h has a second-order selected recurrence at every integer h. Near the complete color it admits a source-fixed, nonzero analytic amplitude on any fixed high-index interval r/N>1/4. A literal zero in the endpoint recurrence also provides a uniformly holomorphic ratio interpolant which is EXACT at the physical r-grid. Optimal analytic Euler--Maclaurin gives an exponentially accurate action interpolant, with its residual source explicitly retained. This is a theorem about the low core. The original upper band R P is the separate, nonzero term in [the exact two-band theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_color_two_band_bound.md). It is not discarded or incorporated into the following amplitude. No mixed-color period, fixed filling, or knot-volume theorem follows without the remaining outer-source comparison. ## 1. Literal finite packets and their fixed factorial continuation Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, M=floor(d/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and the original continuants f_v. For an INTEGER 0<=h<=M the low core is exactly c_(N,h)=kappa^(-1)sum_(v=h)^M a_(h,v)f_v, a_(h,v)=N^2 s_(2v)/[s_v^2 s_(v-h)s_(v+h)]. Its marked phase is not optional: a_(h,v)x^v=N^2 q^(h^2) F_(2v)/[F_v^2F_(v-h)F_(v+h)]. Interchanging the actual two finite sums therefore gives kappa c_(N,h)(z)/N^2 =q^(h^2)sum_(r=0)^M (-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2)P_r(z) A_(h,r)/F_r^3, A_(h,r)=sum_(v=max(h,r))^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/[F_vF_(v-h)F_(v+h)F_(v-r)]. (1) All original normalizations remain. For r>=h define D_(h,r)=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/[F_rF_(r-h)F_(r+h)], U_(h,r)=A_(h,r)/D_(h,r). On a high interval r/N>=tau_0>1/4 and |chi| small, put h=N chi/pi. The source's complex continuation means replacing ONLY F_(v-h),F_(v+h) in (1), with v=r,...,M, by the canonical Fhat_N(v-h),Fhat_N(v+h) of [the exact original factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). All these arguments stay in regular compact factorial substrips. The same replacement defines D_(h,r). This is holomorphic in complex chi on a fixed disk and agrees with every physical integer h there. No assertion about the off-grid continuation of the omitted low indices r<h is needed for this high-index theorem. ## 2. Exact finite transformation and the all-index Ward equation For r>=h, n=M-r, the exact normalized finite sum is U_(h,r)=sum_(k=0)^n (qQ^r;Q)_k(-qQ^r;Q)_k(-Q^(r+1);Q)_k Q^(-rk) /[F_k(Q^(r+1-h);Q)_k(Q^(r+1+h);Q)_k]. (2) It is balanced because the product of its two lower parameters is independent of h. The OWN finite transformation (3) in [the coherent inner proof](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) applies exactly, with no absent amplitude. For example at odd N, choosing its lower parameters in the safe order gives U_(h,r)=(qQ^h;Q)_n/(Q^(r+1+h);Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^(2r+1);Q^2)_j(-Q^(-h);Q)_j Q^j /[(Q^(2r+2-2h);Q^2)_jF_j]. (3) For physical integers r>=h all magnitudes on the second line are positive after its exact term phase (i q^h)^j is removed. The monotonicity used at h=0 is NOT asserted when h is macroscopic. There is a stronger exact source equation. Write H=Q^h and T_h=H+H^(-1). For EVERY physical 0<=h<=M and 0<=r<=M, QY^2(1-Q^2Y)A_(h,r+2) +Y(T_h Q^3Y^2+Q+1)A_(h,r+1) -Q(QY+1)(QY^2-1)A_(h,r)=0, Y=Q^r, (4) A_(h,M)=D_(h,M), A_(h,M+1)=0. The equation includes r<h. For its direct proof use the summand in (1), z=Q^v and the rational certificate g_h(z)=(1-z/H)(1-Hz)(1-z/Y)/z^2. The v-step ratio is Y^(-1)(1-Qz^2)(1+Qz)/[(1-Qz/H)(1-QHz)(1-Qz/Y)]. Consequently the telescoping difference is (1/(YQ^2)-1)z^(-2) +(1/(YQ)+H+H^(-1)+1/Y)z^(-1) -1/(YQ)-1-(H+H^(-1))/Y. The lower endpoint vanishes at z=H or z=Y, according to whether the actual sum starts at h or r. Its upper endpoint has F_(2M+2)=0. The r-step ratio is z^(-1)-Y^(-1), so the first two moments yield (4). On the high interval r>|Re h| the SAME proof holds for the specified complex-h factorial completion: the lower endpoint is z=Y and all shifted-factorial identities are exact. Thus this is the continuation of the original finite source, not a selected formal solution of an annihilator. Normalize (4) by its actual D_(h,r). With den_r=(1-QY/H)(1-QYH), one obtains exactly U_r=p_N U_(r+1)+q_N U_(r+2), p_N=-Q^(-2)Y^(-1)(T_hQ^3Y^2+Q+1)/den_r, q_N=-Q^(-4)Y^(-2)(1-Q^2Y)(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y) /(den_r den_(r+1)). (5) Here den_(r+1)=(1-Q^2Y/H)(1-Q^2YH). At r=M-1, q_N=0 at BOTH parities, independently of H. Thus the selected source is U_M=1 and U_(M-1)=p_N(M-1); no value of D_(h,M+1) is divided out. The recurrence is used where its displayed denominators are nonzero; this holds uniformly in the small complex cusp corridor below. At extreme colors outside that corridor one uses the uncanceled exact equation (4), rather than evaluating a spurious 0/0 at r=M. ## 3. A uniform dominant channel, with its endpoint included Fix tau_0>1/4, tau_0<1/2. Put epsilon=1/N, tau=r/N, Y=exp(2pi i tau), H=exp(2i chi), and Q=exp(2pi i epsilon). Regard the rational coefficients (5) as analytic functions p(tau,chi,epsilon),q(tau,chi,epsilon). Let p_0,q_0 denote their values at epsilon=0. Explicitly, p_0=-Y^(-1)(2cos(2chi)Y^2+2) /[(1-Y/H)(1-YH)], q_0=-Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)^2/[(1-Y/H)^2(1-YH)^2]. The roots of mu^2-p_0 mu-q_0=0 at chi=0 are mu_1=-Y^(-1), mu_2=Y^(-1)cot(pi tau)^2. On every compact real interval I contained in (1/4,3/4), there is a fixed complex neighborhood and a fixed chi disk on which the continuation mu=mu_1 is analytic, nonzero, and satisfies |mu_2/mu|<=kappa<1, Re mu>=m>0. (6) These hypotheses are CHECKABLE from the displayed rational quadratic: at chi=0 the ratio is cot(pi tau)^2<1 and Re(-Y^-1)>0; compactness and sufficiently small complex neighborhoods preserve both strict inequalities. All coefficient denominators stay nonzero. No eigenvalue selection from unknown period data occurs. In particular tau=1/2 is INCLUDED: mu(1/2,chi)=1, q_0 has a double zero there, and the epsilon derivative q_1 also vanishes there. The eigenvalue and source frame do not become singular at the physical terminal point. ## 4. A holomorphic ratio interpolant which matches the source exactly Choose sigma>0 small enough that [tau_0-sigma,1-tau_0+4sigma] lies strictly inside (1/4,3/4), and shrink its complex tube and the chi disk until (6) holds. Let L_N=ceil((1/2-tau_0+2sigma)N), F_tau(z)=p(tau,chi,epsilon)+q(tau,chi,epsilon)/z. For tau in a fixed complex neighborhood of [tau_0,1/2], define v_N(tau)=F_tau o F_(tau+epsilon) o ... o F_(tau+(L_N-1)epsilon) (mu(tau+L_N epsilon)). (7) Every iterate is within C epsilon of its corresponding nonzero mu. Indeed F_tau(mu(tau+epsilon))-mu(tau)=O(epsilon), while its z derivative has modulus at most kappa+O(epsilon)<kappa'<1 on those disks. A sufficiently large C gives an invariant disk at each backwards step. This proves that (7) is uniformly holomorphic, nonzero and bounded, with a uniform bounded inverse. At EVERY physical tau=r/N with tau_0N<=r<M, the continued fraction reaches r=M-1. There q_N=0 EXACTLY, so it forgets its entire remaining analytic tail and takes the value p_N(M-1). Hence v_N(r/N)=U_r/U_(r+1) EXACTLY, (8) and every physical high-index U_r is nonzero. This works also for complex chi in the fixed disk because the wall zero is independent of H. There is no assertion that v_N(M/N) equals a nonexistent physical ratio U_M/U_(M+1); the source product stops at M-1. Moreover the Riccati defect of (7) is O((kappa')^L_N): adding one future step changes its terminal value by O(epsilon), which is contracted by the preceding L_N steps. Thus the chosen terminal function cannot hide a macroscopic source change. ## 5. The selected action and a nonzero joint amplitude All derivatives in the following formula are derivatives of the EXPLICIT rational functions (5). Let p_1=partial_epsilon p|_0, q_1=partial_epsilon q|_0, nu=[p_1+q_1/mu-q_0(partial_tau mu)/mu^2] /[1+q_0/mu^2]. The denominator equals 1-mu_2/mu and is bounded away from zero. The analytic trial ratio mu+epsilon nu has Riccati residual O(epsilon^2), obtained by Taylor expansion at tau+epsilon. Applying the same strict contraction as in section4 gives uniformly on a fixed complex neighborhood v_N=mu+epsilon nu+O(epsilon^2). (9) The principal log is well defined by Re v_N>0. Define S(tau,chi)=integral_tau^(1/2) Log mu(s,chi) ds, C(tau,chi)=sqrt(mu(tau,chi)) *exp[integral_tau^(1/2)nu(s,chi)/mu(s,chi)ds]. (10) The square root is its branch equal to one at tau=1/2. Both are holomorphic on fixed neighborhoods, and C has a uniform nonzero lower bound on compact subsets. The physical selected packet is U_(h,r)=C(r/N,chi)exp[N S(r/N,chi)](1+O(1/N)), (11) uniformly in physical r/N>=tau_0 and complex chi in a fixed small disk. The proof is to sum Log v_N, use (9) and one-step Euler--Maclaurin. Since Log mu(1/2,chi)=0, replacing the true endpoint M/N by 1/2 introduces O(1/N), at BOTH parities. There is no extra unknown endpoint matching constant. In particular U_M=1 is its original source normalization, not an imposed WKB scale. At chi=0, the formulas calibrate against the independent finite transformation: S(tau,0)=i pi(1/2-tau)^2, C(tau,0)=sqrt(sin(pi tau)) *exp[-3pi i(1/2-tau)/2]. (12) This calibration also follows directly without that transformation: substitution in the rational derivatives gives nu/mu=-(pi/2)cot(pi tau)-(5pi i/2), and Log mu=i pi-2pi i tau. Integrating these two expressions in (10) proves (12), with its constant fixed by C(1/2,0)=1. Thus the joint amplitude is an analytic nonzero deformation of the already proved complete-color amplitude. This is not a formal normal-jet assertion: it is uniform for h up to delta N with a fixed sufficiently small delta, and for the displayed complex factorial completion. ## 6. Exponentially accurate analytic action, with residual source kept This strengthening matters before taking an oscillatory outer sum. An O(1/N) error on individual real-grid terms alone cannot justify a complex saddle at a fixed nonzero chi. The functions f_N=Log v_N are uniformly bounded and holomorphic on a FIXED larger complex neighborhood of [tau_0,1/2]. On an inner neighborhood there are constants B,a>0, independent of N, such that |f_N^(k)|<=B k! a^(-k). Put b_N=M/N and, for K_N=floor(pi a N/4), define the analytic Euler--Maclaurin expression E_N(tau)=N integral_tau^b_N f_N(s)ds +(f_N(tau)-f_N(b_N))/2 +sum_(k=1)^K_N B_(2k)/(2k)! N^(1-2k) [f_N^(2k-1)(b_N)-f_N^(2k-1)(tau)]. (13) The Bernoulli polynomial remainder is bounded by C N (K_N/(pi a N))^(2K_N), after shrinking a if necessary. This follows from |B_(2k)(x)|<=4(2k)!/(2pi)^(2k) and the displayed Cauchy derivative bound. Hence, for some c>0, U_(h,r)=exp[E_N(r/N)](1+R_(N,r)), |R_(N,r)|<=C exp(-cN), (14) uniformly on the physical high grid and the complex chi disk. There is NO approximation of source values prior to this bound: the product of the exact grid ratios (8) is precisely U_r. Its endpoint product is empty and equals one at r=M. The interpolant E_N is holomorphic in complex tau,chi. Equations (9) and (13) also give, uniformly on an inner complex neighborhood, exp(E_N(tau))=C(tau,chi)exp[N S(tau,chi)](1+O(1/N)). (15) Indeed the higher Bernoulli terms in (13) sum to O(1/N), and f_N=Log mu+N^(-1)nu/mu+O(N^-2) there. The grid residual R is retained explicitly; it is not relabeled a homogeneous solution or zero current. One may use exp(E_N) in an outer analytic estimate ONLY after bounding that residual in the whole original sum. For example on a fixed negative-w neighborhood and |chi| small, its total high-packet contribution is at most poly(N)exp{N[j_0+C|chi|^2-c]}, (16) where j_0 is the complete-color real action envelope on that neighborhood. This follows by the original factorial estimates, the even analytic perturbation S(tau,chi)-S(tau,0)=O(chi^2), and (14); no unrestricted exterior operator norm is inserted. For a fixed small enough chi disk the error barrier survives any O(|chi|^2) action perturbation, in particular a smaller O(|chi|^4) loss from a nearby complex index saddle. This supplies the quantitative source input for a finite-Poisson or cotangent contour argument in the outer r variable. Its endpoint currents, the lower r packets, and the R P upper color band still require their own estimates. No such current is erased by (14). ## 7. A full real-color upper envelope retains the lower indices For physical integer h define V_(h,r)=q^(h^2)A_(h,r)/D_(0,r). Its normalized recurrence has EXACTLY the complete-color q_N and in the shifted variable Z=Q^(r+1) its other coefficient changes by p_(h,N)-p_(0,N)=-Z(T_h-2)/(1-Z)^2. (17) For 0<=r<=tau_0N, the old full branch envelope rho=max(1,cot(pi(r+1)/N)^2) gives |p_h-p_0|/rho<=C|chi|^2, uniformly even at r=0. The globally conditioned frame of [the all-index source bound](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) therefore changes its one-step bound only by the factor 1+C|chi|^2. The selected high-index anchor (11), together with s_r^2/(s_(r-h)s_(r+h))<=1 for real physical h<=r<=M, is at most exp(CN chi^2) times a fixed polynomial. Iteration proves |V_(h,r)|<=poly(N)exp{N[E(pi r/N)+C chi^2]}, E(u)=(2/pi)integral_u^(pi/4)log cot v dv for u<pi/4, E(u)=0 for u>=pi/4. (18) The exact mixed Ward (4) proves this also for r<h; its lower telescoping endpoint is then v=h. Thus no low-index terms have been omitted. At a fixed complete-color outer radius the strict old lower-index profile gap persists for sufficiently small |chi|. This is a controlled continuity estimate, not a claim that the second recurrence branch disappears. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.py) checks the original finite mixed coefficients, balanced transform, all-r Ward and normalized endpoint wall at both parities; verifies the holomorphic source ratios and the calibrated selected amplitudes. The finite audit checks 17 complete finite-field families N=2,...,18, with EVERY admissible integer color and inner index, the original low-core marked phases and odd mixed finite transformation; four independent canonical complex-Fhat source cases; and six full selected analytic-WKB families at N=32,33,64,65,128,129. The last families include complex chi and compare the literal finite source, its exact continued-fraction ratios and its normalized nonzero amplitude. The exponential Euler--Maclaurin barrier is proved analytically above; finite tests are supplementary, not an inference of that barrier. ## 8. The actual analytic Newton factor has prefactor one Let w=-exp eta, initially eta>0 real, and set alpha_+=(N+1)/2-iN eta/(2pi), alpha_-=(N+1)/2+iN eta/(2pi). Then Q^(alpha_+)=qw and Q^(alpha_-)=q/w EXACTLY, with the negative-argument logarithmic marks retained. Define Bhat_N(r,eta)=q^(-r^2) Fhat(alpha_++r-1)Fhat(alpha_-+r-1) /[Fhat(alpha_+-1)Fhat(alpha_--1)]. (19) At physical integer r it is EXACTLY the original Newton product product_(a<r)(c_a+2cosh eta). The claim below holds uniformly on fixed complex neighborhoods with tau=r/N in a compact subinterval of (0,1/2), eta near a fixed positive real value, and all four scaled factorial arguments in compact subsets of 0<Re a<1: Bhat_N(N tau,eta) =exp{N/(2pi) integral_0^(2pi tau) Log(2cosh eta+2cos v)dv} *[1+O(1/N)]. (20) There is no missing periodic multiplier or square-root factor. Here is the branch calculation. Put a_+=1/2-i eta/(2pi), a_-=1/2+i eta/(2pi), and f(a)=[Li2(1)-Li2(exp(2pi i a))]/(2pi i). The canonical factorial expansion on its marked strip gives Fhat_N(Na-1/2)=sqrt(iN) exp[Nf(a)] [1+O(1/N)]. Indeed the displacement contributes -f'(a)/2, where f'(a)=Log(1-exp(2pi i a)); it cancels the variable part of the factorial square-root prefactor. The remaining sqrt(iN) has the same fixed mark exp(i pi/4)sqrt N at all four arguments, so it cancels between numerator and denominator. In particular one must NOT reset Log[i(1-X)] to an unrelated principal logarithm. The exponent of (19) divided by N is f(a_++tau)+f(a_-+tau)-f(a_+)-f(a_-)-i pi tau^2. Its tau derivative is Log(1+exp(eta)Y)+Log(1+exp(-eta)Y)-2pi i tau =Log(2cosh eta+2cos(2pi tau)). At real 0<tau<1/2 the two arguments on the left have positive imaginary parts, their arguments sum to 2pi tau, and the argument on the right is positive. Thus the integer logarithmic ambiguity is ZERO. Holomorphic continuation gives the same identity on the specified complex neighborhood. Both primitives vanish at tau=0, which proves (20) with its constant. This is sufficient for a fixed high-index Poisson window whose upper cutoff is STRICTLY below 1/2. It is not a uniform bulk asymptotic through tau=1/2: there an upper scaled factorial reaches the edge of its strip, and using a reset dilogarithm could lose a second-shift current. Physical indices beyond such a fixed cutoff must first be bounded by their strict profile gap, or their upper continuation treated separately. Formula (20) makes no such endpoint current vanish. The updated audit includes four marked Newton-factor cases: exact integer-r identities at N=8,9 and complex-r,complex-eta bulk asymptotics at N=12,24, computed independently with the canonical finite Barnes product. Fresh full replay passes these together with the finite mixed-source and selected-WKB families listed above.

title: The selected mixed pretzel packet has an explicit regular character lift
text: # The selected mixed pretzel packet has an explicit regular character lift 29 October 2026. This identifies the regular algebraic branch selected by the original mixed inner source with an explicit auxiliary meridian. It does not identify a representation by matching cusp Hessians. The source Riccati ratio fixes the internal critical root, the literal factorial ratios fix its two remaining conjugate variables, and a two-by-two matrix calculation realizes the resulting disk-product character. The literal quarter-turn port identification and global concatenation are supplied separately; neither a trace equation alone nor this local calculation is being substituted for that gluing proof. ## 1. Recover the internal critical point from the selected finite source Use the exact original mixed sums, normalizations, and source endpoint in [the mixed inner theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md): A_(h,r)=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr) F_(2v)/ [F_v F_(v-h) F_(v+h) F_(v-r)], D_(h,r)=Q^(-r^2) F_(2r)/[F_r F_(r-h) F_(r+h)], U_(h,r)=A_(h,r)/D_(h,r). Here r is in its fixed high window, h is in the small cusp corridor, H=Q^h, Y=Q^r, and the prescribed factorial completion is used for complex h. In particular no arbitrary solution of the Ward equation is chosen. The exact source has U_M=1 and its last backward coefficient vanishes. Its proved selected ratio tends to the simple dominant root mu of mu^2-p mu-q=0, den=(1-Y/H)(1-YH), p=-Y^(-1)[(H+H^(-1))Y^2+2]/den, q=-Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)^2/den^2. (1) The adjacent D ratio has the limit d(Y,H)=Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)(1+Y)/den. There is also a literal, exact moment identity. The ratio of the v-th summand of A_(h,r+1) to that of A_(h,r) is Q^(-v)-Q^(-r). The v=r endpoint on the second sum is zero, so this holds after summing, with no missing boundary term. Consequently the effective internal root selected by that source is X^(-1)=Y^(-1)+d(Y,H)/mu, X=Y mu/[mu+Yd(Y,H)]. (2) Substitution of (2) in (1), followed by clearing its regular denominators, gives precisely (Y+T+1)X^2-(TY+2)X+Y-1=0, T=H+H^(-1). (3) This equivalence is algebraic on the stated regular chart. At H=1 the SOURCE-selected root mu=-Y^(-1) gives X=(Y-1)/(Y+3), rather than the other normalized channel. Thus (2) also fixes the branch on a small complex neighborhood by holomorphic continuation. All denominator exclusions in (1)--(3) are retained. ## 2. Literal phase and its conjugate coordinates The complete phase S_0 is the finite-factorial phase in [the independent symbol audit](actual_pretzel_geometric_symbol_audit.md). The exact mixed summand changes it by S=S_0-2Li2(X)+Li2(X/H)+Li2(XH)+(Log H)^2/2. (4) The last term is the original q^(h^2) factor, not an adjustable flattening. The original common kappa and all quarter-turn phases remain as in the source theorem. Differentiating the actual product-log chart gives exp(S_x)=(1+X)^2(X-1)/[(X-Y)(1-X/H)(1-HX)], exp(S_y)=(1-Y/X)(1-wY)(1-Y/w)/(1-Y)^3, U=exp(S_t)=(wY-1)/(w-Y), L=exp(S_LogH)=(H-X)/(1-HX), (5) where x=Log X,y=Log Y,t=Log w. Equation exp(S_x)=1 is exactly (3). The second equation exp(S_y)=1 is (1-Y/X)[1-(w+w^(-1))Y+Y^2]=(1-Y)^3. (6) On the regular branch the same integer inner mark as in the complete source is retained by continuation. Equations (5)--(6) do not erase that mark. They identify the exponentiated critical coordinates; the marked primitive remains the one fixed by the finite source. The displayed L is also fixed directly by the exact physical h-shift: the original q^(h^2), F_(v-h), F_(v+h) factors have limiting ratio H(1-X/H)/(1-HX)=L. Thus no undetermined square root of an auxiliary longitude is inserted. The auxiliary physical meridian is M=H^(-1/2), with branch M=1 at h=0. A positive physical-color/meridian shift reverses the h-shift. Its preferred longitude marking also retains the original ordinary-circle pivot sign. The [typed longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) proves that the preferred M-eigenflag longitude is precisely -L^(-1). ## 3. The dual Casimir is an actual four-punctured trace The literal quarter-turn dual-Casimir operator in [the original alias theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) has principal symbol D(w,U)=((w-1)/(w+1))^2(U+U^(-1))+8w/(w+1)^2. (7) This symbol has an explicit trace realization. Put t=(w-1)/(w+1), P_0=diag(w,w^(-1)), and define mu_1=[[2w/(w+1),1],[-t^2,2/(w+1)]], mu_2=P_0 mu_1^(-1), mu_3=[[2/(w+1),wU],[-t^2/(wU),2w/(w+1)]], mu_4=(mu_3 mu_2 mu_1)^(-1). (8) Each matrix has determinant one and trace two. Their ordered product is I, and direct multiplication gives Tr(mu_2 mu_1)=w+w^(-1), Tr(mu_3 mu_2)=D(w,U). For w not in {0,1,-1} and U!=0 this tuple is irreducible: the first pair alone has distinct fixed flags. This is an explicit character lift, rather than an inference from the dimension of a trace variety. Substituting (5) and using (3),(6) gives the exact identity D(w,U)=-(L+L^(-1)). (9) For a reproducible rational verification, solve (3) as Y=[1+2X-(T+1)X^2]/[1-TX+X^2], then solve (6) for w+w^(-1); substitute these in (7). No equation at a collision divisor is canceled and then reintroduced as a regular solution. At completeness D=-2 although L=1; the central minus sign in (9) must therefore be retained. ## 4. A framed auxiliary meridian, including its parabolic limit Let P be the actual unrotated disk-product matrix, with determinant one and trace D in (9). Define beta=-(H-X)(1-HX)/[sqrt(H)(H+1)(1-X^2)], C=beta(P-YI). (10) All square roots are the branch through H=1. Equations (3),(9) imply det C=1, Tr C=sqrt(H)+1/sqrt(H), [C,P]=0. (11) More precisely, on the P-eigenflag with eigenvalue lambda=-L^(-1), C has eigenvalue M=H^(-1/2); on the reciprocal flag it has M^(-1). These assertions follow by the scalar identities beta(lambda-Y)=H^(-1/2), beta(lambda^(-1)-Y)=H^(1/2). The formula has a removable complete-color degeneration. At H=1, equation (3) on the selected branch gives Y=(1+3X)/(1-X), so C=I-(P+I)/(1+Y), Tr P=-2. (12) For noncentral P this is a NONCENTRAL trace-two unipotent. Thus the auxiliary meridian does not collapse to I merely because its eigenvalue becomes one. Formula (10) is finite in a bounded port frame at this limit, although a frame diagonalizing P becomes singular there. Here is a direct tangle test. For actual meridians a,b,C, put P=ba. The positive Hurwitz convention is (a,b)->(a^(-1)ba,a). The literal auxiliary threading word [2,1,1,2] sends the auxiliary meridian to P^(-1)CP. Closing that physical auxiliary component is therefore EXACTLY [C,P]=1; under this condition the main outputs are (C^(-1)aC,C^(-1)bC). Following it by the retained negative half twist gives r=C^(-1)bC, s=C^(-1)bab^(-1)C. (13) For generic H!=1 diagonalize P as diag(lambda,lambda^(-1)), with lambda=-L^(-1), and set t_lambda=(lambda-1)/(lambda+1). One may take a=[[2lambda/(lambda+1),1], [-t_lambda^2,2/(lambda+1)]], b=P a^(-1), C=diag(M,M^(-1)). Then (13) gives Tr(r^(-1)a)=2-t_lambda^2 [2+lambda H+lambda^(-1)H^(-1)]. (14) Substitution of L=(H-X)/(1-HX) and the two actual stationary equations (3),(6) makes (14) exactly w+w^(-1). Thus the selected factorial branch satisfies the mixed threaded-half-twist character relation, with the original auxiliary meridian and a specified flag. The regular formula (10), not this singular diagonal frame, is used at H=1. ## 5. Scope of the local certificate This proves a source-selected regular local character lift and an explicit auxiliary-meridian matrix. The additional literal quarter-turn ordering, conjugating frames, and global source/cap equations are proved in [the global port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md). The [preferred-longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) retains its sign and framing. The [marked action comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) then identifies the source action with the regulator of the extended filled representation. These separately proved steps are not inferred from matching a cusp Hessian. They give a representation-volume upper bound; identifying the deformed representation as the filled geometric holonomy is an additional requirement for equality. In particular the global propagation is RIGHT TO LEFT in the original left-to-right box label b. If its rotated input is t_b and output t'_b=U_b t_b, the actual original bottom ports are (h(t'_b),h(t_b)^(-1)) and top ports are (g(t'_b)^(-1),g(t_b)). Both original neighboring caps therefore impose t_b=t'_(b+1); the outer turns impose t_s=t'_1. The condition product U_b=1 closes this propagation in the order s,...,1. One must not replace these literal relations by a forward box-label traversal. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.py) checks the cleared rational identities, full two-by-two character and threading formulas, complete parabolic limit, and the exact finite source moment on both level parities. Finite computations supplement the algebraic proof above. ## 6. Absolute complete crossing-circle holonomies match the geometric cusp The [literal port and geometric-anchor proof](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) identifies the main meridians with the white-face holonomies of the explicit four-antiprism construction. Here is an absolute matrix check for the AUXILIARY generators; it is stronger than comparing cusp Hessians or only a ratio of translations. Set alpha=pi/s, c=cos(alpha), t=csc(alpha), rho^2=sec(alpha)+tan(alpha), R=rho^4, w=-R, U=exp(2i alpha), z_i=t rho^(-1) exp((2i+1)i alpha), and use the actual raw port matrices g(z)=[[-2w/(w+1),z],[-t^2/z,-2/(w+1)]]. Their fixed flags are z/t. The unrotated disk product is P_i=g(z_i)g(Uz_i)^(-1), with trace -2 and fixed flag Z_(i+1)=rho U^(i+1). Direct multiplication gives (P_i)_21=t^2(1-t)(1-U^(-1))/z_i. Rotate the boundary coordinate by zeta'=U^(-i-1)zeta and then use m_i(zeta)=1/(zeta'-rho). The new lower-left entry before this last Mobius map is c'=U^(i+1)(P_i)_21=2i rho(1-t). For any trace-minus-two matrix fixing rho, write P=-I+N. The kernel of N is (rho,1), so N=c'[[rho,-rho^2],[1,-rho]]. Conjugating by the matrix [[0,1],[1,-rho]] of m_i gives m_i P_i m_i^(-1)=-I+[[0,c'],[0,0]]. Consequently its PROJECTIVE translation is -c'. Since rho^2(t-1)=ct and the actual cusp rectangle has width W=1/(rho sin(alpha))=t/rho, this translation is exactly -c'=2ic W. (15) The source-selected complete Y equals exp(2i atan(sec(alpha))), hence 1+Y=2ic/(1+ic). Using (12), the same coordinate m_i sends the actual auxiliary meridian to the translation -c'/(1+Y)=(1+ic)W. (16) Equations (15)--(16) are precisely the primitive disk longitude and the POSITIVE diagonal half-twist meridian in [the face-labeled cusp calculation](actual_augmented_pretzel_crossing_circle_cusp.md). Thus the complete auxiliary matrices, not just their flags or their first deformation derivative, match those of the actual half-twisted augmented geometry. The central minus sign of the SL2 disk product is retained throughout. Together with the independently checked white and shaded face pairings in the port proof, this anchors the actual complete representation, not merely its numerical volume. Reversing the cyclic TRAVERSAL label to respect that operator order does not change the oriented complete geometry. There is an explicit holomorphic Mobius isometry F(zeta)=rho^2/zeta. It sends Z_k -> Z_(-k), U_k^+ -> U_(-k-1)^-, U_k^- -> U_(-k-1)^+, Q_k -> Q_(-k-1), T_k^+ <-> T_(-k)^-, W_+ <-> W_-. Under the literal cross-copy shaded gluing, applying F to both sides gives the SAME gluing at index -k read in its inverse direction: the original U_(k-1)^+ -> U_k^- becomes U_(-k)^- -> U_(-k-1)^+, and the other outer vertex behaves likewise. Thus the reverse traversal is matched by an orientation-preserving isometry, not by an assumed mirror identification. The original boxes and their source labels are not permuted in the quantum formula.
