# Literal port gluing and the complete geometric holonomy anchor 29 October 2026. The selected regular mixed source has an explicit matrix lift to the original augmented pretzel diagram. Its common \(w\) and outer equation \(\prod_iU_i=1\) glue the actual ports. At completeness, every white AND shaded face map agrees with the explicit four-antiprism geometry. Thus its base representation is the oriented geometric holonomy, not merely a character with the same cusp Hessian or a representation with similar trace equations. This note uses the actual stationary identities in [the local mixed-character lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md). It does not infer a source cycle or a quantum asymptotic from those identities; those were proved separately from the finite source. The lift below is a DIRECT algebraic construction: its group relations, framed peripheral eigenvalues and cap equalities are verified explicitly. It does not require a further assertion identifying the canonical state graph of an arbitrary scalar operator \(F(\Omega)\) from its unwrapped eigenphase. In particular a state-versus-observable Hurwitz convention is not silently used to choose between \(U\) and \(U^{-1}\). ## 1. A common two-head frame and the literal turned ports Let \(w
e0,\pm1\), set \(k=(w-1)^2/(w+1)^2\), and for \(z
e0\) put \[ g(z)= egin{pmatrix} -2w/(w+1)&z\-k/z&-2/(w+1) \end{pmatrix},\qquad h(z)=g(-wz),\qquad A=\operatorname{diag}(w,w^{-1}). 	ag{1} \] They have determinant one and trace \(-2\), and \(h(z)g(z)=A\). Neither meridian is central on this chart. The fixed flag of \(g(z)\) is \(z/r\), where \(r=(w-1)/(w+1)\); the fixed flag of \(h(z)\) is \(-wz/r\). For a rotated box with character \(U
e0\), take incoming pair \((g(z),h(z))\) and outgoing pair \((g(Uz),h(Uz))\). The original turn index map is \[ (\mathscr R B)_{(u,b);(v,e)} =x^{u-e}B_{(d-u,v);(b,d-e)}. \] The actual cup/cap identifies the bent meridian with its inverse. Choose based paths along these turn arcs. Therefore the original UNROTATED box has incoming and outgoing ordered meridians \[ (a,b)=(h(Uz),h(z)^{-1}),\qquad (r_{\mathrm{out}},s_{\mathrm{out}})=(g(Uz)^{-1},g(z)). 	ag{2} \] Their common product is the actual crossing-disk product \[ P=ba=h(z)^{-1}h(Uz)=g(z)g(Uz)^{-1} =s_{\mathrm{out}}r_{\mathrm{out}}. 	ag{3} \] This is the literal turn convention, rather than a free choice of independent strand gauges. At the quantum level the same turns and their scalars are those of the exact rotated source. Their normalization does not alter the group inverse relation. ## 2. The auxiliary circle is an explicit regular centralizer On the local regular stationary branch write \[ U= rac{wY-1}{w-Y},\qquad L= rac{H-X}{1-HX},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}P=-L-L^{-1}. \] The stationary \(X\) equation also gives the exact identity \[  rac{1+YL}{1+Y/L}= rac{L^2}{H}. 	ag{4} \] These are the rational equations certified from the actual finite factorial phase, with its selected branch, in the linked local theorem. Put \[ \Delta=(1+YL)(1+Y/L)=1-Y\operatorname{Tr}P+Y^2, \] \[ J= rac{I-YP}{\sqrt\Delta},\qquad C= rac{YI-P}{\sqrt\Delta}. 	ag{5} \] The square root is its analytic branch tending to \(1+Y\) at \(H=1,L=1\). It is nonzero near the complete branch. Both matrices have determinant one, commute with \(P\), and \(JC=-P\). On the \(P\)-eigenflag with eigenvalue \(\lambda=-L^{-1}\), equation (4) gives \[ C	ext{ eigenvalue }M=H^{-1/2}, 	ag{6} \] on the branch tending to \(+1\). The reciprocal flag has eigenvalue \(M^{-1}\). Thus this is the actual auxiliary meridian together with the preferred disk-longitude eigenvalue \(-L^{-1}\); its SL spin character is kept. These data realize the actual threaded half twist, not just its trace. Direct substitution of (1), with \(Y=(Uw+1)/(w+U)\), gives \(Ja=g(z)J\). Together with (3), and \(JC=-P\), this proves \[  oxed{\quad r_{\mathrm{out}}=C^{-1}bC,\qquad s_{\mathrm{out}}=C^{-1}bab^{-1}C.\quad} 	ag{7} \] This is precisely the physical \(R^{-1}\) half-Hurwitz convention with its typed auxiliary circle, as independently derived in the local theorem. The formulas are valid with every exterior port retained. At completeness, \[ C=I- rac{P+I}{1+Y},\qquad J=I- rac{Y}{1+Y}(P+I). 	ag{8} \] Here \(P\) is a NONCENTRAL trace-\(-2\) parabolic and \(Y
e-1\), so \(C\) is a finite noncentral parabolic. No singular diagonal frame or semisimple deletion of the complete circle is used. ## 3. Global gluing and the actual filled-knot representation Keep the original left-to-right box label \(b=1,\ldots,s\). For that box let its incoming rotated parameter be \(t_b\) and its outgoing parameter \(t'_b=U_bt_b\), with the SAME \(w\) at every box. Formula (2) says that its original bottom ports are \((h(t'_b),h(t_b)^{-1})\) and its top ports are \((g(t'_b)^{-1},g(t_b))\). The literal original caps pair bottom port 2 of box \(b\) with bottom port 1 of box \(b+1\), and likewise the corresponding top ports. They therefore impose EXACTLY \[ t_b=t'_{b+1},\qquad	ext{equivalently }\quad t_{b-1}=U_b t_b, 	ag{8a} \] with cyclic box indices. This is right-to-left operator composition: the product \(\mathscr R(B_1)\cdots\mathscr R(B_s)\) applies the rightmost box first. Starting at \(t_s
e0\) and propagating in the order \(s,s-1,\ldots,1\), the outer marked stationary equation \(\prod_bU_b=1\) closes both ports exactly. Every individual bottom and top cap is an inverse pair by (8a). Below we index this reverse cyclic TRAVERSAL by \(i\), so its successive incoming and outgoing parameters are denoted \(z_i,z_{i+1}=U_bz_i\). This notation does not change or permute the physical source boxes. The geometric face labels follow this same traversal. The explicit orientation-preserving reversal isometry (13) below checks that its half-twist pairings describe the SAME oriented manifold. No mirror, arbitrary mutation or omission of a cap is used. The [independent literal cap-order audit](actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order_audit.md) also checks this multiplication direction on generic NONCOMMUTING physical boxes; commutativity of the special Casimir polynomials is not being used to hide the order of these individual ports. The independently proved odd-width connectivity makes the main component one component. The pivot and marked normal source have already been retained in the source derivation of the outer equation; no missing half-angle closure is inserted here. This constructs a representation of the actual augmented-link group, with its main meridians parabolic, and its \(i\)-th auxiliary meridian/longitude represented by \(C_i,P_i\). At a selected filling point put \(z_i^{\mathrm{eig}}=\operatorname{Log} H_i\), \(\ell_i=\operatorname{Log} L_i\), using the source's continuous logarithms. The actual unit-charge filling equation is \[ z_i^{\mathrm{eig}}+2p_i\ell_i=2\pi i m_i,\qquad m_i=\pm1. 	ag{9} \] By (6), \(C_iP_i^{p_i}\) has BOTH eigenvalues \((-1)^{p_i-m_i}\). The nearby selected filling has \(L_i
e\pm1\): its nonzero small Fourier saddle \(\zeta_i\) satisfies \(\ell_i=-2\pi i\zeta_i\), by the actual Fourier stationarity, so \(\ell_i
e0\) and \(|\ell_i|<\pi\). Thus these commuting matrices are diagonalizable together and their product is that scalar matrix. Hence \(C_iP_i^{p_i}=1\) in PSL(2,C). The relation also extends by continuity if needed. Substituting it into (7) gives \(\operatorname{Ad}(P_i^{p_i})(b,bab^{-1})\), which is exactly the \((2p_i+1)\)-st power of the physical half-Hurwitz map. The representation therefore descends to the literal original filled pretzel knot. No faithfulness is assumed at this step. ## 4. Every complete geometric face pairing is matched Put \(\alpha=\pi/s\), \(U=e^{2i\alpha}\), \(ho^2=\sec\alpha+	an\alpha\), \(R=ho^4\), \(w=-R\), and \(r=\csc\alpha=(w-1)/(w+1)\). Choose the allowed common scale \[ z_i= rac rho e^{(2i-1)i\alpha}. \] The fixed flags of \(g_i=g(z_i)\), \(h_i=h(z_i)\) are now \[ U_{i-1}^+=ho^{-1}e^{(2i-1)i\alpha},\qquad U_{i-1}^-=ho^3e^{(2i-1)i\alpha}, \] and \(P_i=g_i g_{i+1}^{-1}\) fixes \(Z_i=ho e^{2ii\alpha}\). These are exactly ALL ideal vertices of the explicit polyhedron \(\mathcal P_s\) in [the geometric-volume construction](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md). Let \(r_F\) denote reflection in the white face plane \(F\), acting antiholomorphically on its boundary circle. The two polygon circles are \(|\zeta|=ho^{-1},ho^3\), so \[ r_{W_+}(\zeta)=ho^{-2}/ ar\zeta,\qquad r_{W_-}(\zeta)=ho^6/ ar\zeta. \] The white quadrilateral \(Q_i\) has circle center and radius \[ c_i=ho\sec\alpha\,e^{(2i+1)i\alpha},\qquad R_{Q}=ho	an\alpha. \] Its reflection is \(r_{Q_i}(\zeta)=c_i+ R_Q^2/( ar\zeta- ar c_i)\). Their products give EXACTLY \[ r_{Q_i}r_{W_+} = rac1{	an\alpha}  egin{pmatrix}-ho^2&c_iho^{-2}\ - ar c_i&ho^{-2}\end{pmatrix} =g_{i+1},\qquad r_{W_-}r_{W_+}=-A. 	ag{10} \] All equalities are literal SL matrices as displayed, except the explicit harmless central sign in the last equality. Also \(h_{i+1}=r_{W_-}r_{Q_i}\) in PSL. Thus every white-face holonomy has been identified, not merely its fixed flags. Develop the second projection polyhedron as \(r_{W_+}(\mathcal P_s)\), using \(W_+\) as the face tree. Define \[ \gamma_i^+=J_i g_{i+1},\qquad \gamma_i^-=h_{i+1}J_i^{-1}=J_i^{-1}g_i. 	ag{11} \] These are the TWO shaded face pairings at the \(i\)-th retained half twist. They act on the ideal vertices as \[ \gamma_i^+:r_{W_+}(Z_i,U_i^-,U_{i-1}^-) \longmapsto(Z_i,U_{i-1}^+,U_i^+), \] \[ \gamma_i^-:r_{W_+}(Z_i,U_{i-1}^+,U_i^+) \longmapsto(Z_i,U_i^-,U_{i-1}^-). 	ag{12} \] Here is a direct reason for each map. The white reflection product fixes its \(Q_i\) vertices, while \(J_i\) fixes \(Z_i\) and maps the flag of \(a=h_{i+1}\) to that of \(g_i\), by \(J_i a=g_iJ_i\). The other outer vertex uses \(h_{i+1}^{-1}=r_{Q_i}r_{W_-}\): \(r_{W_-}\) fixes \(U_{i-1}^-\), and the inverse-Hurwitz relation in the proof of (7) maps the remaining flag to \(U_i^+\). For the second shaded pairing use \(h_{i+1}J_i^{-1}=J_i^{-1}g_i\) and \(P_i=g_i g_{i+1}^{-1}\), with \(J_i\) commuting with \(P_i\). They give the crossing-circle vertex and both outer vertices in the second line of (12). Three distinct ideal vertices determine the orientation-preserving hyperbolic face isometry uniquely. Equations (12) are precisely the cross-copy, outer-label-swapping shaded gluings in the literal half-twisted source geometry. This checks ALL \(2s\) shaded pairings, not only one per crossing circle. The white generators and (11) are words in the actual main and auxiliary meridians: \(J_i=-P_i C_i^{-1}\). Conversely the actual meridians are words in these face generators. The same labeled oriented cellulation is therefore developed by our source representation and by the complete geometric face pairings. Its oriented fundamental Bloch regulator is exactly \(V_s\). This is the needed absolute geometric anchor. Here is also an explicit check of the reverse traversal used in section3. The HOLOMORPHIC Mobius isometry \[ F(\zeta)=ho^2/\zeta 	ag{13} \] acts by \(Z_k\mapsto Z_{-k}\), \(U_k^+\mapsto U_{-k-1}^-\), \(U_k^-\mapsto U_{-k-1}^+\). It sends \(Q_k\) to \(Q_{-k-1}\), interchanges \(W_+,W_-\), and sends \(T_k^+\) to \(T_{-k}^-\) and conversely. Conjugating the literal cross-copy, outer-label-swapping shaded pairing by \(F\) gives the inverse of that SAME pairing at \(-k\), not a pairing with the opposite half twist. Since (13) is holomorphic, it preserves the hyperbolic orientation. Thus the right-to-left traversal forced by the source cap indices has the exact same oriented geometric anchor, rather than its mirror or a different permutation of the source boxes. The [independent cusp lattice](actual_augmented_pretzel_crossing_circle_cusp.md) and the absolute peripheral translation calculation in the local mixed-character note identify \(P_i\) with the primitive disk longitude and \(C_i\) with the positive-diagonal meridian. They retain the SL longitude sign \(-L_i^{-1}\); a metric ratio alone would not fix that marking. ## 5. Scope The result supplies a regular, source-compatible representation lift and its actual complete geometric anchor. The geometric meaning of the SOURCE ACTION also requires a regulator comparison, not just these matrices or their cusp shapes. Its separate proof can use the actual peripheral Bloch boundary formula, the anchor above, and a finite filling-chain comparison. Neither faithfulness of every deformed representation nor a filled-volume equality is asserted just from (9).

title: A direct positive ideal triangulation and the full source angle critical point
text: # A direct positive ideal triangulation and the full source angle critical point 29 October 2026. The ACTUAL half-twisted augmented pretzel polyhedra admit a positive geometric ideal triangulation with compatible face pairings. The proof below checks every homogeneous face map; no general Epstein--Penner existence theorem is used. This removes an optional dependency from the Casson--Rivin presentation. The already proved finite-center/equivariant-map geometric completion does not need it. ## 1. An explicit homogeneous section of every original ideal cell Use alpha=pi/s, rho^2=sec(alpha)+tan(alpha), and the actual P_s vertices Z_i=rho exp(2ii alpha), U_i^+=rho^-1 exp((2i+1)i alpha), U_i^-=rho^3 exp((2i+1)i alpha). The face cycles and their literal half-twist pairings are those of [the geometric cellulation](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md) and [the complete port anchor](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md). Put O=(0,rho) in upper half-space. The rotation R(z)=exp(2i alpha)z and the holomorphic half-turn F_i(z)=rho^2 exp(4ii alpha)/z (1) are genuine global P_s isometries: substitution permutes its vertices, and hence its convex hull. In particular F_i: (Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+) ->(Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-). (2) The finite dihedral group generated by R and F_0 fixes O. Conversely a point fixed by the rotation lies on the vertical axis, and F_0 fixes only height rho on that axis. Averaging any finite interior point in the future hyperboloid over this finite group and normalizing stays inside every strict supporting halfspace. The average is O. Thus O is STRICTLY interior to P_s, not merely a guessed symmetry center. In the Lorentz model use the ideal light lift l(z)=(|z|^2+1,2Re z,2Im z,|z|^2-1), V(z)=rho l(z)/(|z|^2+rho^2). (3) Then -<O,V(z)>=1, using the unit hyperboloid representative of O. All lifted ideal vertices of this cell lie in the SAME affine three-plane A_O={v:-<O,v>=1}, which does not contain the origin. Since F_i fixes O, its Lorentz action carries V(z) EXACTLY to V(F_i z), without an additional scalar on the light ray. ## 2. Every actual face map preserves these lifts Let r_+ be the reflection in the white W_+ plane. Develop the second cell as r_+ P_s and give it center r_+ O and light lifts r_+ V(z). These satisfy its analogous affine normalization. For a white face Q or W_-, the literal transition from the second cell to the first is r_face r_+. Applied to its face vertices it gives (r_face r_+) r_+ V(z)=r_face V(z)=V(z), (4) because a Lorentz plane reflection fixes the ENTIRE plane, including the normalized light vectors, not only their projective endpoints. For W_+ the transition is identity and r_+ itself fixes those vectors. Thus every white face preserves the homogeneous lifts exactly. For shaded faces, the complete port proof gives actual orientation- preserving transitions gamma_i^+ and gamma_i^- with the ordered maps gamma_i^+ r_+ : (Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-) ->(Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+), gamma_i^- r_+ : (Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+) ->(Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-). (5) They agree on those three ideal points with the GLOBAL isometry F_i in(1). This statement checks all three vertices, not only a fixed flag. The maps gamma_i^plusminus r_+ reverse ambient orientation, whereas F_i preserves it. Consequently their precise difference is reflection in the source triangle plane: composing with that plane reflection makes an orientation-preserving Mobius map fixing three distinct points, which is identity. Such a plane reflection fixes each V(z) exactly. It follows that on the actual face vertices gamma_i^plusminus r_+ V(z)=F_i V(z)=V(target z). (6) Equation(6) is the needed scalar-normalization check. It does NOT assert that gamma_i maps the second CELL CENTER to the first center. Only its homogeneous face section is required, and that has now been proved. The literal reverse-cap traversal is the same holomorphic F_0 combined with an index reversal; it preserves(3) and is not a mirror gluing. Thus the two cells, every face pairing and all their translates have Gamma-equivariant ideal lifts with affine face maps. The complete face-pairing identities make this assignment consistent. This proof uses the actual retained half twists; it does not replace the source by its untwisted partner. ## 3. A finite compatible subdivision, proved directly Here is the elementary affine subdivision argument for these cells. For a three-dimensional convex cell with v vertices, vertex heights modulo affine functions have dimension v-4. For a paired n-gonal face, requiring the two height restrictions to differ by an affine function imposes at most n-3 linear conditions. Under such a condition the two lower-face subdivisions match, since adding an affine function does not change a regular subdivision. For a finite paired affine cellulation, the total remaining dimension is at least sum_cells(v-4)-sum_facepairs(n-3) =(1/2)sum_cells(f-4). (7) Use twice the edge count for the sum of face side counts and v-e+f=2 for each convex three-cell. Every cell has f>=4, and equality means a tetrahedron. If some cell is not tetrahedral, (7) is positive. Choose a nonzero compatible class of heights and take its lower convex subdivision. At least one cell refines nontrivially; all new cells are three-dimensional, use only old vertices and have matched affine faces. Every original vertex is extreme in projection, so the lower subdivision does not discard an original boundary vertex. Repeat. This terminates: assign each resulting three-cell one affine- independent quadruple of its original vertices. Two cells with disjoint interiors cannot contain the same nondegenerate tetrahedron. Within each original cell only finitely many quadruples exist, while every nontrivial refinement increases the cell count. If a non-tetrahedral cell remained, (7) would permit another refinement, contradicting this finite bound. Thus a finite compatible tetrahedral subdivision results. Apply this argument in the affine planes from(3)--(6). Four affine- independent light vectors in A_O are LINEARLY independent because A_O does not contain zero. Hence their ideal hyperbolic tetrahedron is nonflat. Convex subdivision gives its positive orientation. The result is a finite POSITIVE GEOMETRIC IDEAL triangulation of the actual complete augmented manifold. No literature triangulation existence theorem is needed for this class. At the selected sufficiently long filling, move its ideal vertex orbits by the actual bounded framed representation and its marked peripheral flags. Every one of the finitely many shapes stays in the upper half-plane by continuity. Contractible edge transitions are identity, so positive edge angle sums remain exactly2pi. This gives a positive source angle point on the ACTUAL ideal triangulation. ## 4. The full edge/peripheral tangent space, not just the source-family tangent For t tetrahedra and h cusp tori let E be the edge-Hamiltonian space in the 2t-dimensional real shape symplectic space. Its rank is t-h. The rank statement can be checked directly: an edge-row relation has equal sums on opposite edge pairs in every abstract tetrahedron. Its six local coefficients therefore have the form lambda_ij=a_i+a_j. The formula a_i=(lambda_ij+lambda_ik-lambda_jk)/2 shows that a_i agrees across matched faces. Connected ideal vertex links propagate it to one constant per cusp. Conversely every cusp constant gives a relation. The ideal Euler count gives t global edges, so precisely h independent relations leave rank t-h. The edge rows are isotropic: the local skew corner counts cancel across paired faces. The peripheral rows belong to E^perp; the same local normal-curve count pairs a primitive meridian and longitude by -2, with different cusp tori pairing zero. Thus their 2h rows span the ENTIRE symplectic quotient E^perp/E. This is the actual marked incidence calculation underlying the [boundary pairing proof](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), not a claim that stationarity on a small source family exhausts the angle tangent. Use centered projective logs U_i,V_i, so the reduced form is Omega_red=-(1/2)sum_i dU_i wedge dV_i. (8) At any positive full complex gluing solution, its real shape-log vector lies in E^perp. EVERY affine angle tangent satisfying the edge equations lies there too. The sine rule for a positive tetrahedron gives dVol(delta theta)=Omega(Re shape,delta theta) =(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i delta Im U_i -Re U_i delta Im V_i]. (9) Consequently an incomplete gluing point is critical on its FULL fixed- peripheral-ANGLE slice, even though it need not maximize the larger unfilled cusp angle domain. No nonlinear gluing condition is imposed on the tangent delta theta in(9). For the actual filled source, Re(U_i+p_iV_i)=0. On the larger affine slice fixing only Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=the actual primitive2pi angle, its contribution in(9) is (1/2)Re V_i delta Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=0. Every unfilled main cusp has U_i=V_i=0, so it contributes zero as well. Thus the source is stationary on the FULL filled-slope angle slice, not merely on its selected critical representation curve. ## 5. Concavity, boundary maxima and the actual hyperbolic value For angles alpha,beta,gamma>0 with sum pi, the negative Hessian of Lambda(alpha)+Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma) in (alpha,gamma) is [[cot alpha+cot beta,cot beta], [cot beta,cot gamma+cot beta]]. Its determinant is1 and its first diagonal entry is sin(gamma)/(sin(alpha)sin(beta))>0. It is strictly positive definite. Thus total ideal volume is strictly concave on every affine positive angle slice. At the positive source point its full constrained derivative vanishes by(9). Every straight segment from it to a different point in the closed angle polytope stays positive before its final endpoint; its volume is strictly decreasing after its initial zero derivative. Continuity at zero/pi angles then makes EVERY different boundary value strictly smaller as well. The source point is the unique GLOBAL maximum. The value is the marked source regulator because the shapes develop the same actual representation and oriented fundamental class. The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) and [general geometric completion](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) identify it with the complete filled metric and its hyperbolic volume. The complete augmented maximum V_s and the finite filled maximum V_src(p) are different: each uses its OWN affine peripheral constraints. This proves the optional Casson--Rivin certificate for the current explicit augmented family, with all existence/rank premises checked. For an arbitrary base, the general geometric completion remains valid without an ideal triangulation. A universal Casson--Rivin presentation still needs a verified positive ideal angle chart; it does not follow from an arbitrary original source critical point or a matching action alone. [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.py) passes 90-digit NUMERICAL checks of all labeled homogeneous white/shaded vertex maps for six widths, including even widths and the literal half twists. It compares FULL Lorentz/Hermitian light matrices in the normalization(3), not projective point images alone. It also checks the analytical identity F_i(O)=O to that precision. The exactness assertions are supplied by(1)--(6), not by finite-precision arithmetic. The finite compatible-subdivision, rank and strict-concavity arguments above are analytical and do not rest on these samples.

title: The proposed pretzel radial homotopy has no strict boundary-action gap
text: # The proposed pretzel radial homotopy has no strict boundary-action gap **Subsequent resolution for this source.** The obstruction proved below remains valid, but the [full coherent period theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now combines the equal-height contributions by an exact finite inner transformation and controls all remaining indices with both recurrence branches. It proves complete-base survival without the false strict boundary gap. The unfilled augmented link, not a fixed knot filling, is the scope of that result. 29 October 2026. For the EXACT phase of the double sum in [the complete original pretzel polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), the original-radius diagonal boundary attains the SAME action as the candidate shifted interior saddle, for EVERY fixed real w<-1. Consequently no uniform strict boundary gap holds on the proposed closed homotopy rho_X in [rho_*,0]. This does not refute a deformation which coherently fills or combines that endpoint current. It identifies the endpoint contribution such a deformation must retain. ## 1. Phase, branches, and the candidate saddle Write w=-W, W>1, X=exp(rho+i theta), Y=exp(i phi), with 0<phi<theta<pi and rho<=0. Use the principal dilogarithm, taking the boundary value of Li2(Y/X) from Im(Y/X)<0. Thus its continuation to theta=phi at rho<0 is its LOWER-side value on (1,infinity). The phase is S=-6Li2(1)-Li2(X^2)+4Li2(X)+Li2(1/X)-Li2(Y/X) +Li2(w)+Li2(1/w)-Li2(wY)-Li2(Y/w)+3Li2(Y). Put F=Im S. The lower-side convention is essential at the diagonal; resetting its logarithm changes F by a radial mark. Set A=W+W^(-1) and phi_*=2 arctan(sqrt(A+2)/2), Y_*=exp(i phi_*), X_*=(Y_*-1)/(Y_*+3), rho_*=log|X_*|, theta_*=arg X_*. Then rho_*<0 and 0<phi_*<theta_*<pi. These are the specified exponentiated stationary equations. On this chart D_X S=0 and D_Y S=2pi i at the point. The retained mark -2pi i Log Y makes the latter an actual zero derivative; because |Y|=1 this mark is real on the angular triangle and does not change F or the result below. ## 2. An exact identity equates the diagonal and interior actions For ANY 0<phi<pi, set Y=exp(i phi), X(Y)=(Y-1)/(Y+3), and define G(X;Y)=-Li2(X^2)+4Li2(X)+Li2(1/X)-Li2(Y/X). The following equality is exact: Im G(X(Y);Y)=3 Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi)=Im G(Y;Y). (1) Here Cl2(a)=Im Li2(exp(i a)); it uses the same continuous principal boundary values, not a changed dilogarithm sheet. Proof. X(Y) is in the upper unit disk. Indeed Im X=4sin(phi)/|Y+3|^2 and |X|^2=(2-2cos(phi))/(10+6cos(phi))<1. Moreover 1-Y/X=(1+Y)^2/(1-Y) has argument (pi+phi)/2, so Y/X lies in the lower half-plane and arg X>phi. All the displayed logarithms therefore vary continuously. Direct differentiation gives D_X G=2Log(1-X^2)-4Log(1-X) +Log(1-1/X)-Log(1-Y/X). Its exponential is one at X=X(Y). Its limit as phi decreases to zero is zero, fixing the integer logarithmic ambiguity, hence D_X G=0 on the entire interval. Thus d_phi Im G(X(Y);Y)=log|1-Y/X| =2log|1+Y|-log|1-Y|. The same derivative is obtained from 3Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi), since d_a Cl2(a)=-log|1-exp(i a)|. Both sides of (1) tend to zero as phi increases to pi. This proves (1), including its constant. The other terms of S depend only on Y,w, so (1) proves F(rho_*,theta_*,phi_*;w)=F(0,phi_*,phi_*;w). (2) In particular the diagonal boundary of the original radius is not strictly below the candidate interior action. ## 3. It is precisely the maximum on that boundary edge On rho=0, theta=phi, inversion of the two w-dependent dilogarithms gives the explicit real function B_W(phi)=6Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi) -2Im Li2(-exp(i phi)/W)+phi log W. (3) There is no omitted imaginary constant: Li2(-W),Li2(-1/W) are real, and Log(-wY)=log W+i phi in the inversion formula. With t=tan(phi/2)>0, differentiation and elementary sine algebra give B_W'(phi)=log([(A+2)+(A-2)t^2]/(4t^4)). (4) The numerator minus 4t^4 equals -(1+t^2)(4t^2-A-2). Hence B_W has a UNIQUE maximum, at t^2=(A+2)/4, which is exactly phi_*. Combining (2)--(4), max_(0<=phi<=pi) F(0,phi,phi;w)=F_* . (5) Equations (2) and (5) disprove the requested strict uniform boundary gap for every w<-1. They do not assert that another boundary edge or an intermediate radius exceeds F_*, nor that a fixed strictly shifted triangle lacks its own boundary gap. No such extra statement is needed. For reference, the opposite far corner has the exact lower-side value F(rho,pi,pi;w)=pi(log W-rho). It rises under the radial shift and therefore also cannot be dismissed by an unmarked endpoint rule. ## 4. The equal-action boundary is present in the original finite source The exact double summand in formula (11a) of the original polynomial is, with F_j=(Q;Q)_j, A_(v,r)=F_(2v)/F_v^4 * (Q^(-v);Q)_r Q^r/F_r^3 *(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r, 0<=r<=v<=M=floor((N-1)/2). At the DIAGONAL physical endpoint r=v it is exactly A_(v,v)=(-1)^v Q^(-v(v-1)/2) *F_(2v)(qw;Q)_v(q/w;Q)_v/F_v^6. (6) Every factor in (6) is nonzero for w<-1 and 0<=v<=M. In particular this is not an outside-support zero of (Q^(-v);Q)_r: that zero first occurs at r=v+1. The outer polynomial/source factors N^2/kappa remain as in the original formula. No nonzero coefficient for the ENTIRE period is inferred by taking a single endpoint term. An exact factorial completion also makes the retained endpoint plain. Put h=2pi i/N, delta=v-r, alpha_+=d/2+Log(W)/h and alpha_-=d/2-Log(W)/h. With the exact Fhat_N of [the original factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), the following meromorphic function takes the literal values A_(v,r): Ahat(v,r)=exp(pi i r+h[-vr+r(r+1)/2]) *Fhat(2v)/[Fhat(v)^3 Fhat(v-r)Fhat(r)^3] *Fhat(alpha_++r)/Fhat(alpha_+) *Fhat(alpha_-+r)/Fhat(alpha_-). (7) Both alpha choices satisfy Q^(alpha_++1)=qw and Q^(alpha_-+1)=q/w. Their sum uses the actual negative-w logarithmic marks; the product has no unspecified periodic factor. Formula (7) follows from the exact factorial shift and (Q^(-v);Q)_r=(-1)^r Q^(-vr+r(r-1)/2) F_v/F_(v-r) at the physical integers. The physical change (v,r)->(delta,r) is unimodular, so its local lattice residues have no new Jacobian. This constructs the SAME finite residue functional in the new coordinates; it is not a pointwise identity between two products of cotangents or permission to omit their chart-change currents. Near delta=0 and a compact tangential neighborhood of the equal-action point, Fhat(delta) is holomorphic, nonzero and Fhat(0)=1; all other scaled factorial arguments lie in regular compact substrips. Thus the cot pole at delta=0 has its original NONZERO residue (6). Conversely 1/Fhat(delta) has simple zeros at delta=-1,-2,...,-m for any fixed small normal collar m<N, canceling those newly enclosed cot poles provided the remaining factors stay regular. This permits the familiar zero-side local filling; it does not delete delta=0 or supply a strict action gap there. Finite-height connecting contours and all their currents must be retained exactly as in the proved simple seam filling. An exact residue cycle is the sum of small product circles about (delta,r) in Z_>=0^2 with delta+r<=M, with density Ahat times the two unit-residue cotangent factors. It is the original finite sum. Moving it to the shifted saddle requires an actual relative-cycle operation through this equal-action endpoint packet. Its coefficient, possible coherent cancellation, and any resulting uniform asymptotic remain unproved by radial concavity alone. The subsequent [coherent finite inner elimination](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) does handle this packet without postulating that radial homotopy: an exact balanced finite transformation keeps the half shift and proves its nonzero amplitude in the geometric range. The [whole circle/period assembly](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) uses that coherent sum and an all-index two-branch upper envelope, rather than the false strict boundary-gap premise disproved here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_radial_boundary_gap.py) supplements the proof with high-precision branch/derivative equalities and literal finite-factorial diagonal identities. It is not used to infer an asymptotic or a selected thimble coefficient.

title: The actual pretzel winding period and its explicit positive saddle family
text: # The actual pretzel winding period and its explicit positive saddle family **Subsequent global proof.** The [coherent circle and period theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now proves survival for this complete augmented source, with explicit nonzero leading constant and original normalization. The local symbol calculations below alone do not imply that result; its additional finite transformation, global recurrence bound and Gaussian estimates are supplied in the linked proof. 29 October 2026. The complete augmented odd-pretzel source has an exact one-variable residue with finitely many integer windings. Its literal factorial coefficients give a positive-shape stationary family for every fixed odd number of boxes. The action and the full Hessian can be computed explicitly. This identifies candidate exponential rates of the original period; it does not prove that its selected cycle has a nonzero coefficient at those saddles or that every other contribution is smaller. In particular a proposed strict radial-homotopy boundary gap is false: an original diagonal face has the same action height. That face must be combined with the interior contribution using the exact source, not discarded as exponentially small. ## 1. Exact winding, including its normal multiplicity Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and M=floor(d/2). The [literal complete base polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) is denoted z_N(z). It is the actual quarter-turn of R^(-1)L_N, with degree at most M and every scalar retained. For s odd boxes the unchanged raw marked source is A_(N,s)=Phi_2(z_N^s), Phi_2(F)=(-1)^d N^2 [z^d](F mod P_N), P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. The [full commutant and marked-trace proof](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) establishes this on all physical channels, not a semisimple projection. Any existing external framing/peripheral line still multiplies A_(N,s). Polynomial division or residues at infinity give EXACTLY Phi_2(F)=(-1)^d N^2/(2*pi*i) integral F(z)/P_N(z) dz, (1) around every finite node. Put z=w+w^(-1). On |w|=R>1 this is a positively oriented ellipse enclosing those nodes, and P_N(w+w^-1)=(1+w^N)^2/w^N. Consequently A_(N,s)=(-1)^d N^2/(2*pi*i) integral_(|w|=R) z_N(w+w^-1)^s w^N(1-w^-2)/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (2) The full squared denominator is compulsory. Expanding it on |w|>1 gives the finite coefficient identity A_(N,s)=(-1)^d N^2 sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1)m ([w^(mN-1)]-[w^(mN+1)]) z_N(w+w^-1)^s. (3) Only m<=floor((sM+1)/N) can occur. At fixed odd s these are eventually m=1,...,(s-1)/2. The coefficient m is the retained confluent/normal source. There is no authorization to keep only m=1 before estimating the others. The existing complete-base audit checks (3) against literal original sources at all tested even and odd levels. An immediate exact upper bound is |A_(N,s)| <= N^2 (R+R^-1)/(1-R^-N)^2 * R^-N *max_(|w|=R)|z_N(w+w^-1)|^s. (4) The [coherent capacity diagnostic](actual_pretzel_coherent_radial_capacity_diagnostic.md) tests (4) with the actual polynomial and all normal channels. A sampled circle maximum is not a certified analytic upper bound. ## 2. The phase comes from the literal finite coefficient Write F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The complete-base theorem gives kappa*z_N(w+w^-1)/N^2 =sum_(v=0)^M sum_(r=0)^v F_(2v)/F_v^4 * (Q^-v;Q)_r(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r Q^r/F_r^3. (5) The positive continuant coefficient used to prove this simplifies to b_v=N^2 |F_(2v)|/|F_v|^4. Indeed the original cosine product is (Q^(v+1);Q)_(d-2v)=F_(d-v)/F_v=N/|F_v|^2. The fixed phase in the continuant then gives b_v x^v=N^2F_(2v)/F_v^4. This removes no phase from the finite sum (5). Set X=exp(2*pi*i*v/N), Y=exp(2*pi*i*r/N). On a regular compact subdomain the leading phase of a summand in (5), derived by integrating its exact factorial/Pochhammer logarithms, is S(X,Y;w)=-6Li_2(1)-Li_2(X^2)+4Li_2(X)+Li_2(1/X) -Li_2(Y/X)+Li_2(w)+Li_2(1/w) -Li_2(wY)-Li_2(Y/w)+3Li_2(Y). (6) The exponent convention is exp[N*S/(2*pi*i)]. At the points below use principal dilogarithms continued on their indicated upper/lower sides. The overall kappa^-1 contributes a real leading action constant pi^2, and thus does not change the volume rate. Endpoint-uniform expansions and contour selection do not follow from the interior phase calculation. Its exponentiated logarithmic derivatives are exp(S_logX)=(1+X)^2/[(X-1)(X-Y)], exp(S_logY)=(1-Y/X)(1-wY)(1-Y/w)/(1-Y)^3, exp(S_logw)=(wY-1)/(w-Y). (7) These also follow directly from the exact consecutive-term ratios in (5). They are algebraic equations for the stationary support, with the logarithmic marks still to be specified. ## 3. All box counts have an explicit positive-shape stationary branch For one winding m with 0<m<s/2 put alpha=pi*m/s, eta=2 asinh(tan alpha), beta=atan(sec alpha), w_*=-exp(eta), Y_*=exp(2i beta), X_*=(Y_*-1)/(Y_*+3)=i sec(alpha)/(2-i sec(alpha)). (8) Then |Y_*|=1, |X_*|<1 and 0<arg Y_*<arg X_*<pi. Eliminating X from the first two equations in (7) gives Y=(3X+1)/(1-X), w+w^-1=6-16Y/(1+Y)^2. (9) With U=exp(2*pi*i*m/s), the third equation gives Y=(Uw+1)/(w+U). Substitution factors exactly as (w-1)^2[(U+1)^2w^2-2(U^2-6U+1)w+(U+1)^2]=0. The positive branch (8) is the root outside the unit circle and obeys w+w^-1=2-16U/(1+U)^2=2-4 sec^2(alpha). (10) The factor w=1 is not silently identified with this branch. There is an essential inner mark: on the specified dilogarithm sheets, S_logX=0, S_logY=2*pi*i, S_logw=2i alpha. (11) Thus the genuinely stationary marked phase for the s separate factors of z_N^s is W_m=sum_(i=1)^s [S(X_i,Y_i;w)-2*pi*i Log Y_i] -2*pi*i*m Log w. (12) Equation exp(S_logY)=1 does not justify omitting that mark. At (8) it changes only the real part of the action, since |Y_*|=1. ## 4. Exact action and nondegeneracy Let Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log|2sin t|dt. The action on (8) is Im W_m=8s [Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)]. (13) One direct proof uses the stationary equations with their marks. For the action per box, differentiation in alpha gives dV/dalpha=-2log|w_*|=-4asinh(tan alpha). Elementary differentiation of the right side of (13), divided by s, gives the same derivative. Both sides tend to zero as alpha tends to pi/2; on the phase side this follows from dilogarithm inversion and (pi-2alpha)log|w_*|->0. This fixes the additive regulator constant. In particular s=3,m=1 gives 4v_8, where v_8=8Lambda(pi/4). Among this specified positive branch family the action strictly decreases with m, so m=1 has the largest action. This is not a classification of every complex or endpoint contribution of the original cycle. The Hessian is nondegenerate, without an assumed Gaussian coefficient. In logarithmic coordinates (X,Y,w), let H_3 be the Hessian of S and H_2 its X,Y block. On the stationary loci, det H_3=-Y(Y-1)(Y+3)^2(w^2-6w+1) /[4(w-Y)(Y+1)^2(Yw-1)], det H_2=-Y^2(Y+3)^2(w-1)^2 /[(w-Y)(Y+1)^3(Yw-1)]. (14) All factors are nonzero at (8). The effective outer Schur entry is i cos(alpha). For the full 2s+1 variables of (12), block elimination therefore gives det Hess W_m=s (det H_2)^(s-1) det H_3 !=0. (15) These are local phase statements. A nondegenerate stationary point with nonzero local factorial amplitude is not yet a nonzero coefficient in the selected original global period. ## 5. The equal-height original face is a genuine remaining obstruction The proposed shift of log|X| from zero to log|X_*| cannot be justified by a strict boundary gap. For every upper unit Y and X=(Y-1)/(Y+3), the X-dependent part of (6) has exactly the SAME imaginary part as at X=Y. The original diagonal edge X=Y has its unique maximum at Y_*. Hence it reaches the height of the shifted interior stationary point for every w_*<-1. The [independent exact boundary calculation](actual_pretzel_radial_boundary_gap.md) proves this identity with its branch marks. The actual r=v summand in (5) is nonzero, and its endpoint residue survives the exact factorial interpolation. It cannot be dismissed as an exterior zero or an exponentially smaller boundary prism. The next analytic requirement is to combine that diagonal-face period and the interior contribution coherently, or eliminate the redundant inner sum by an exact transformation. Until this is done, (13)--(15) and numerical agreement with (4) do not prove augmented-base survival, and still less the volume limit after fixed long fillings. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_winding_phase_and_geometric_saddles.py) checks the algebraic elimination, all logarithmic marks, Hessian factors, and the action formula. Exact finite winding/source checks remain in the linked complete-base audit. No selected-cycle claim is inferred.

title: The actual primitive gauge has a Gaussian resonant endpoint
text: # The actual primitive gauge has a Gaussian resonant endpoint 27 October 2026. The canonical finite Hilbert-90 gauge from the original source has an exactly computable resonant endpoint. Its polynomial Ward identity contains two retained highest-degree terms. The endpoint is a quadratic Gauss period, of size N^(-1/2), despite the gauge's exponential operator norm on the flat relative module. This settles the endpoint of THIS specified source gauge. It does not evaluate the knot-dependent endpoint sum or identify the marked geometric A-period. In particular it supplies no additional knot-volume conjecture proof. ## 1. Canonical polynomial and exact unreduced Ward equation Use Q=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2, F_r=(Q;Q)_r, and v_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2)z^r/F_r. Let g_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)c_r z^r be the CANONICAL degree-<N representative of v_N(z)v_N(Qz) modulo z^N. It is the actual primitive source gauge in [the Fourier transport theorem](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md), whose regular-disk action was proved in [the gauge-action note](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md). As an ordinary polynomial, before setting z^N=0, it obeys (1-z)(1-Qz)g_N(Qz)-g_N(z) =-(2/N)z^N+c_(N-1)z^(N+1). (1) To prove this, first keep the full ordinary product w_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz), including its degrees N,...,2N-2. The exact Euler Ward equation is (1-z)v_N(Qz)=v_N(z)-z^N/N. Multiplying its versions at z and Qz gives (1-z)(1-Qz)w_N(Qz)-w_N(z) =-z^N[v_N(z)+v_N(Qz)]/N+z^(2N)/N^2. (2) Hence the coefficient of z^N is -2/N, and coefficients below N vanish. Removing the high tail of w_N does not alter that z^N coefficient: its own degree-N contribution to the left side is (Q^N-1)[z^N]w_N=0. The left side for g_N has degree at most N+1; its top coefficient is Q^N c_(N-1)=c_(N-1). This proves (1). Equivalently it gives the exact coefficient relation c_(N-2)=(1+Q)c_(N-1)-2Q/N. Setting the polynomial argument z=1 in (1) now yields g_N(1)=2/N-c_(N-1). (3) Both source terms in (1) are required. If (1) were replaced by its homogeneous identity in z^N=0 before evaluation, the selected endpoint would be changed. ## 2. The retained coefficient is an exact Gauss period The root factorial identity F_(N-1)=N gives, coefficient by coefficient, [z^(N-1-r)]v_N(z)=Q^(r+1)F_r/N, 0<=r<N. For example this follows from F_(N-1-r)=N(-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2)/F_r. Substituting it into the convolution for c_(N-1) cancels every factorial and gives c_(N-1)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2). (4) Thus (3)-(4) are an exact algebraic period evaluation of the canonical endpoint at every level, including composite N. They are not an identification of the nilpotent algebra with scalar points. The representative and the degree-N source were fixed before evaluation. ## 3. Direct Gaussian asymptotic, with the finite boundary retained Put T_N=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2), omega_N=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)/4-pi*i/(4N)]. Then T_N=sqrt(N) omega_N+O(1), (5) c_(N-1)=omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N), g_N(1)=-omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N). (6) Here is a proof of (5) without importing an incomplete-Gauss-sum estimate. On integer r the summand equals exp(2pi*i*f(r)), where f(x)=[x^2-(N+1)x]/(2N). Periodize exp(2pi*i*f(x)) times the indicator of [-1/2,N-1/2]. This is a piecewise smooth periodic function, and zero is away from its discontinuities. Its symmetrically summed Fourier series therefore gives the finite Poisson identity T_N=sum_(m in Z)^sym I_m, I_m=integral_(-1/2)^(N-1/2) exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x)) dx. (7) For N>=4, f' lies in [-3/4,1/2]. For every nonzero m, integration by parts expresses I_m as [exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x))/(2pi*i*(f'(x)-m))]_a^b +(1/(2pi*i)) integral_a^b f''(x) exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x))/(f'(x)-m)^2 dx, with a=-1/2, b=N-1/2. The second term is O(m^-2), uniformly in N: f''=1/N, the interval has length N, and |f'(x)-m|>=|m|/4. The boundary terms also have an absolutely summable PAIRED bound. Both endpoints have exp(-2pi*i*m*x)=(-1)^m, and 1/(t-m)+1/(t+m)=2t/(t^2-m^2)=O(m^-2) uniformly for -3/4<=t<=1/2. Hence the sum of all m!=0 terms in (7) is O(1). No separate divergent boundary sums have been discarded. For m=0, complete the square around a_0=(N+1)/2. This gives I_0=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)^2/(4N)] sqrt(N) *integral_(-(N+2)/(2sqrt(N)))^((N-2)/(2sqrt(N))) exp(pi*i*y^2) dy. The complete Fresnel integral is exp(pi*i/4). It follows by Gaussian regularization, and its two tails are O(1/R) by one integration by parts beyond |y|=R. The displayed endpoints have size comparable to sqrt(N), so replacing them by infinity changes I_0 by O(1). Its complete value is sqrt(N) omega_N. Together with the nonzero Fourier modes this proves (5). The finitely many smaller levels do not affect the asymptotic. Equations (3)-(4) finish (6). In particular the exact resonant source gauge satisfies |g_N(1)|=N^(-1/2)[1+O(N^(-1/2))], log|g_N(1)|=-(1/2)log N+O(N^(-1/2)), (1/N)log|g_N(1)| -> 0. (8) It is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. No all-level nonvanishing claim beyond this is needed for (8). ## 4. Consequence for the actual source comparison The operator gauge has a positive exponential norm on a regular flat-metric chart, as already proved, while its canonical resonant endpoint (8) has no positive exponential rate. Neither its operator size nor a regular-chart dilogarithm value determines this selected endpoint. The high coefficient in (1) becomes the leading term of the endpoint; the source carry must be retained. This endpoint is not the original figure-eight invariant. Already at N=2, g_2(1)=1 whereas the original source identity for 4_1 gives Kashaev_2(4_1)=1+4=5. The whole-source proof for that knot uses a separate positive product sum, not this universal gauge. No equality with that invariant or a general knot period is introduced here. Thus this is a usable fully evaluated local source period, but it does not close the selected geometric-period or volume-norm gate for a general actual word. It specifies what has to be composed with that word and its other source sectors before any volume conclusion can follow. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_primitive_gauge_endpoint.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_primitive_gauge_endpoint_results.json) check the canonical polynomial coefficients, the FULL unreduced Ward equation and Gauss-period identity exactly at finite-field roots. High-precision samples separately diagnose (5)-(8); the uniform proof above establishes their asymptotic scope.

title: Original output Fourier projection removes the colliding negative-transfer poles
text: # Original output Fourier projection removes the colliding negative-transfer poles 28 October 2026. Keeping the original finite physical output projection resolves the simultaneous endpoint collisions left by the scalar simple-seam calculation. There is an exact matrix-valued total-transfer interpolant. At EVERY newly crossed negative integer its projected operator has a zero, including when its unprojected scalar coefficient has a pole. Consequently the complete cotangent density is holomorphic across the whole negative normal collar. Its operator norm and contour mass cost are exp(o(N)) on any collar of width N^alpha, alpha<1, uniformly in ALL physical input basis states. This is an actual full-source normal-boundary operation, not a favorable scalar interpolation with its output tails deleted. The Fourier/sinc factors are retained explicitly. It neither discards the original k=0 residue nor bounds an unrestricted bulk exterior by hyperbolic volume. ## 1. Literal physical Fourier projection and the interpolated crossing Use the original balanced complete heads, N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), with orthonormal basis |j>,0<=j<=d. In L^2 of the unit circle use normalized measure dtheta/(2pi) and the specified logarithmic lift 0<=theta<=2pi. The orthogonal projection of exp(i nu theta) to the physical Fourier band is the ENTIRE vector v_N(nu)=sum_(j=0)^d s_j(nu)|j>, s_j(nu)=(exp(2pi*i*nu)-1)/(2pi*i*(nu-j)), (1) with its removable value one at nu=j. Thus v_N(j)=|j> inside the physical band, and v_N(j)=0 at every other integer. At an invalid integer its vector zero is at least simple. Orthogonality proves ||v_N(nu)||<=||exp(i nu theta)||_L2 <=exp(2pi |Im nu|). (2) No N-dependent conditioning or a nonpositive pivotal metric is used. Let the scalar r_N(a,b;z), 0<=a,b<=d, be the EXACT factorial interpolation of the original positive crossing: r_N(a,b;z)=kappa x^(-a-b+z)Q^(b(a-z)) *Fhat(b+z)F_a/[Fhat(z)F_b Fhat(a-z)]. (3) The normalizers, Gaussian, Cartan and completed factorial are those of [the total-transfer theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md). Define the operator-valued continuation by its actual input columns, Rhat_N(z)|a,b>=r_N(a,b;z) v_N(b+z) tensor v_N(a-z). (4) This is precisely the contraction of the two original output Fourier projections with the scalar monomials of the physical crossing kernel. It is not an arbitrary change of its output source. At an integer 0<=k<=d it equals the original kth transfer slice: valid outputs give their literal basis vectors and forbidden transfers have their exact factorial zeros. The opposite crossing uses its actual conjugate mirror. Therefore the half-integer closed cotangent rectangle gives an OPERATOR identity before applying any knot closure, R_plus=integral_Gamma pi cot(pi z) Rhat_N(z) dz/(2pi*i), (5) where Gamma encloses precisely 0,...,d. The full original kappa is in (3); all physical head projections and any external pivotal, framing, peripheral or marked source are unchanged. Fubini on finite contours applies (5) simultaneously to every crossing of a fixed signed word. ## 2. Exact cancellation at a simultaneous negative endpoint collision Fix z=-s, with 1<=s<N. In this normal range Fhat has a simple pole at each negative integer, and a simple zero at N,...,2N-2. These orders follow directly from its convergent Gamma product or its shift continuation. Put I_1=1 if b<s, otherwise 0, I_2=1 if a+s>=N, otherwise 0. The scalar coefficient (3) has local order ord_(z=-s) r_N = 1-I_1-I_2. (6) The first invalid output is b-s<0, and the second is a+s>d. Formula (1) supplies a simple vector zero at EACH invalid output. Thus the complete column in (4) has order at least (1-I_1-I_2)+I_1+I_2=1. (7) In particular the double collision I_1=I_2=1 is not discarded: its scalar pole is canceled by TWO actual physical projection zeros, leaving another zero. This is exactly the source factor lost if one studies the scalar factorial coefficient alone. All scalar singularities in this collar lie at these integers. Consequently Rhat is holomorphic on the negative collar and vanishes at all its integers. Its complete density pi cot(pi z)Rhat_N(z) is holomorphic there too. No derivative residue or logarithmic source term has been omitted; the ENTIRE sinc vectors in (1) are retained before taking the removable limits. ## 3. Uniform polynomial base bound at every physical input endpoint Fix T>0 and let 0<=Re nu<=1, |Im nu|<=T. Uniformly in 0<=n<=d, |Fhat(n+nu)/F_n|<=C_T N^(C_T), |F_n/Fhat(n-nu)|<=C_T N^(C_T), |1/Fhat(nu)|<=C_T N. (8) Here is a direct estimate, including the input endpoints. On the fixed nu rectangle, its defining product gives Fhat(nu) bounded by C_T N^(-Re nu), and its reciprocal by C_T N^(Re nu). For the first ratio use the exact product Fhat(n+nu)/F_n=Fhat(nu) product_(j=1)^n (1-Q^(j+nu))/(1-Q^j). Each ratio is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j); the sum of their logarithms is O_T(log N). For the second ratio when n>=1, start at Fhat(1-nu) and use factors j=2,...,n. Its ratios are bounded by 1+C_T/min(j-1,N-j), and |F_1/Fhat(1-nu)| is polynomially bounded. For n=0 use 1/Fhat(-nu)=(1-Q^(1-nu))/Fhat(1-nu), which is regular and satisfies the same bound. Thus (8) does not hide a large F_n or its inverse at the physical endpoints. Since the Cartan multiplier in (3) is bounded on this fixed-height rectangle at physical a,b, (8) gives |r_N(a,b;nu)|<=C_T N^(C_T), uniformly for ALL a,b. Together with (2), this is the required bounded normal base for the actual projected operator. ## 4. A subexponential-cost compensated collar for the entire word The same exact ratio used for the sourced Ward equation gives r_N(z+1)/r_N(z) =c(1-Q^(b+z+1))(1-Q^(a-z))/(1-Q^(z+1)), c=xQ^(-b). (9) Take the rectangle -s-1/2<=Re z<=-1/2, |Im z|<=T, with s<N/2. On either half-integer vertical side or either nonzero-height horizontal side, write z=nu-M, 0<=Re nu<=1. Inverting (9) M times costs at most (C_T N^2)^M: each denominator 1-Q^(integer+nu) has magnitude at least c_T/N there, while the numerator is bounded. The distance from an integer is bounded below by min(1/2,T). The base estimate (8) and (2) therefore give on this ENTIRE boundary ||pi cot(pi z)Rhat_N(z)|| <=N^(C_T)(C_T N^2)^(s+1). (10) The matrix operator norm costs only another factor N from its N^2 input columns. The cotangent is bounded on these edges. Its apparent interior poles have already been removed in Section 2. The maximum principle applied to every scalar matrix coefficient <u,Rhat v>, or to this holomorphic complete density, extends (10) through the interior with the same bound. The added contour has length O_T(s+1). Moving the original left edge from -1/2 to -s-1/2 and retaining BOTH finite-height connecting pieces changes (5) by zero: all enclosed new poles are removable. Thus this is an exact source-preserving collar move with quantitative operator cost exp[O_T((s+1)log N)]. (11) For s<=N^alpha with any fixed alpha<1 this is exp(o(N)). The number of crossings and physical heads of a fixed diagram does not grow with N, so finitely many such original operator collar operations have the same subexponential additional cost. Every original cup, cap, pivot, phase and external line remains as prescribed. For an artificial positive split k=R the adjacent contours have opposite interface currents; moving them together retains the same integer residues with opposite signs. Equations (5)--(11) address the ACTUAL outer normal source as well, including the simultaneous collisions which a scalar split had left uncontrolled. ## 5. Scope of the advance This removes an artificial negative-transfer exit of normal width N^alpha at the full finite physical source, with explicit tame cost. The original integer residues 0,...,d remain enclosed. In particular it does not contradict the full-rate low Markov packet: no original residue has been declared zero or individually lower-rate. The physical input labels in (4) are the original finite basis labels. The bound is uniform over all of them, so it is an operator/source statement rather than a selected fixed-clock phase claim. If those input indices are themselves replaced by independent complex contour variables, one must retain the corresponding input projections and their joint sources; (7) is not an assertion for an arbitrary scalar continuation with those physical projections removed. Nothing here assigns a sharp geometric bound to an unrestricted bulk exterior, a real radial cutoff face, or a transfer collar of macroscopic width whose cost in (11) is no longer subexponential. It does not identify every stationary branch of a split sinc density with a knot representation: the entire physical projection must stay. The theorem is a quantitative full-source normal-boundary filling, not the global sublevel transport or volume conjecture. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.py): original physical integer transfer slices, all simultaneous negative endpoint pole cancellations, fixed-height projected density limits, and finite-source tests including both physical input endpoints. The literal positive test includes the original common Cartan factor kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2), with its inverse in the negative crossing. The same audit now checks the [upper extension](actual_projected_transfer_upper_collar.md), its exact N-shift and fractional base identity, all physical upper collision orders and the two-sided expanded cotangent residue sum.

title: Both outer transfer collars admit a controlled original-source filling
text: # Both outer transfer collars admit a controlled original-source filling 28 October 2026. This completes the upper-end counterpart of the [all-input projected lower-collar theorem](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md). The original positive and negative physical crossings admit exact cotangent contours with BOTH ends extended by N^alpha, alpha<1. Every new integer pole is removable, uniformly over all physical input states. The added contour pieces have exp(o(N)) operator cost. This is a local operator identity which may be inserted in any fixed original signed word with its closure unchanged. It does not estimate the unrestricted bulk factors or identify a geometric saddle of the full Fourier-projected density. ## 1. Retain the same original projected interpolation Use d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), and the full original Cartan scalar kappa. With the exact completed factorial Fhat, set r(a,b;z)=kappa x^(-a-b+z)Q^(b(a-z)) Fhat(b+z)F_a/[Fhat(z)F_b Fhat(a-z)], Rhat(z)|a,b>=r(a,b;z) v_N(b+z) tensor v_N(a-z), v_N(nu)=sum_(j=0)^d [(exp(2pi*i*nu)-1)/(2pi*i*(nu-j))]|j>. (1) The removable component at nu=j is one. The vector is the actual orthogonal Fourier projection onto the original physical head; it vanishes at every integer outside 0,...,d and obeys ||v_N(nu)||<=exp(2pi|Im nu|). (2) No physical head is replaced by a different representation or metric. At integer k in 0,...,d, Rhat(k) is the original kth transfer slice. The lower-collar proof establishes its zero at every negative integer -s with 1<=s<N, including scalar poles canceled by invalid-output projection zeros. ## 2. Exact N-shift and the upper base strip Iterating the original first-shift equation gives an additional exact identity of the SAME meromorphic factorial, Fhat(z+N)=(1-exp(2pi*i*z)) Fhat(z). (3) Indeed product_(r=1)^N(1-Q^(z+r))=1-exp(2pi*i*z). This retains the full central factor; it is not replaced by its value at a root. Put z=d+w. Applying (3) to the three affected factorials gives the identity Fhat(b+d+w)F_a/[Fhat(d+w)F_b Fhat(a-d-w)] =[Fhat(b-1+w)/F_b] [F_a/Fhat(a+1-w)] [1-exp(-2pi*i*w)]/Fhat(w-1). (4) The shared factors 1-exp(2pi*i*w) in numerator and denominator have been canceled as meromorphic functions, not evaluated separately at an integer. The remaining central factor in (4) is still explicit. Fix T>0. On the fixed fractional strip 0<=Re w<=1, |Im w|<=T, away from integers by a fixed positive distance, each expression on the right of (4) has modulus bounded by a fixed power of N, uniformly over every a,b in 0,...,d. Only such fractional points are needed on the half-integer vertical and fixed-height horizontal edges below. Here is the endpoint-uniform bound in detail. Set nu=1-w. The basic fixed-argument Gamma product gives polynomial upper and inverse bounds for Fhat(w), Fhat(nu) and Fhat(1-nu). For b>=1, Fhat(b-nu)/F_b =[Fhat(1-nu)/F_1] product_(j=2)^b (1-Q^(j-nu))/(1-Q^j). Every quotient is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j), so the product is polynomial by the harmonic sum. For b=0 use Fhat(-nu)=Fhat(1-nu)/(1-Q^(1-nu)); the single denominator is at least c_T/N on the stated fractional edges. Likewise F_a/Fhat(a+nu) =Fhat(nu)^(-1) product_(j=1)^a (1-Q^j)/(1-Q^(j+nu)). For j<=N-2 each quotient is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j-1). If j=N-1 occurs, treat it separately: its denominator is at least c_T/N away from the excluded integer w=0, and its numerator is bounded. This adds only a polynomial factor. Finally 1/Fhat(w-1)=(1-Q^w)/Fhat(w) is polynomially bounded, as is 1-exp(-2pi*i*w) at fixed height. These statements prove the uniform polynomial base bound for (4) without hiding a large complete factorial or its inverse. The original Cartan in (1) has bounded modulus at this fixed height, since a,b are physical integers and its prescribed logarithms have bounded imaginary coefficients. ## 3. All newly crossed upper integer poles are removable Take k=N,...,2N-2. The factorial orders, directly from (3) and its nonzero original strip, are: ord Fhat(k)=1, ord Fhat(b+k)=1+1_(b+k>=2N), ord [1/Fhat(a-k)]=1+1_(k-a>=N+1). Thus the scalar r(a,b;z) at z=k has order 1+1_(b+k>=2N)+1_(k-a>=N+1)>=1. (5) Both outputs b+k and a-k are outside the physical band. The two vectors in (1) therefore each supply one further zero. In particular Rhat has a zero of order at least three at every such k, and its complete cotangent density is holomorphic there. Even the scalar coefficient already has a zero on this upper collar; the full physical projection remains part of the operator identity. The only factorial singularities in the collar are at these integer points. There is no unrecorded noninteger pole. Formula (5) includes the physical input endpoints and all their simultaneous collisions. ## 4. Uniform collar estimate and the two-sided contour identity The exact step recurrence is r(z+1)/r(z) =xQ^(-b)(1-Q^(b+z+1))(1-Q^(a-z))/(1-Q^(z+1)). (6) On a half-integer vertical edge or a fixed nonzero-height horizontal edge, each forward step costs at most C_T N: its single denominator is bounded below by c_T/N, and the two numerators are bounded. Starting with the base strip (4), for 1<=s<N/2 this proves ||pi cot(pi z)Rhat(z)|| <=N^(C_T)(C_T N)^(s+1) (7) on the boundary of d+1/2<=Re z<=d+s+1/2, |Im z|<=T. The finite number N^2 of input columns adds only a factor N to the operator bound. Equations (2) and (5), followed by the matrix maximum principle, extend (7) throughout the filled upper collar. The original contour encloses exactly the physical transfers 0,...,d. Extend its left edge to -s-1/2 and its right edge to d+s+1/2, retaining both finite-height connecting pieces. The added integers are -s,...,-1 and N,...,N+s-1. The lower theorem and (5) show that every new pole of the complete density is removable. Consequently, as an original physical operator, R_plus=integral_(extended rectangle) pi cot(pi z)Rhat(z) dz/(2pi*i). (8) Each added collar has length O_T(s+1), and both have the conservative uniform operator cost exp[O_T((s+1)log N)]. (9) For s<=N^alpha, alpha<1, this is exp(o(N)). The negative crossing uses its exact antiunitary mirror Rhat_minus(z)=Flip conjugate(Rhat_plus(conjugate z)) Flip, with the conjugate full Cartan scalar. Its residue identity and both collar bounds follow with the same orientations at the integer residues. Finitely many such identities can be composed inside any fixed signed braid word before its original marked closure is taken. The scale is compatible with the earlier regular descent window. In the normalized transfer variable z/N, a width s=N^(1-epsilon) is a collar of width N^(-epsilon). The regular-region flow cost is exp(O(N^(B epsilon) log^2 N)), while (9) costs exp(O(N^(1-epsilon) log N)). Both are subexponential whenever 0<epsilon<1/B. Thus these two local quantitative estimates do not require incompatible cutoff scales. Compatibility of scales alone does not identify the off-grid Fourier-projected density with the previous scalar phase or estimate its projection-angle currents. The cost in (9) concerns the added operator contours, not the norm of an arbitrary exterior contraction. The original residues 0,...,d, the whole sinc/Fourier source and every framing/pivotal/peripheral line remain. A claimed full-volume bound must still estimate the remaining bulk current with this source retained. The expanded [projected audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.py) checks every physical input a,b at N=2,...,8. It checks the exact N-shift and fractional identity (4) off the integer lattice, the full upper matrix zero orders at N through N+min(3,N-2), and both-collar cotangent residue sums against the original positive and negative E/Cartan crossing matrices. The positive kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2) and its negative inverse are included explicitly. These tests supplement the uniform proof and do not change its full physical-source scope or establish a sharp whole-knot volume estimate.

title: The projected transfer word, its degree repair, and its remaining source seams
text: # The projected transfer word, its degree repair, and its remaining source seams 28 October 2026. The two projected outer-collar theorems are genuine original-operator contour identities. They can be inserted simultaneously in a fixed signed word. A contractive degree average makes the entire off-grid word preserve the original integer degree, without changing its integral or its collar estimates. This does not yet reduce the sharp bound to the known regular critical regulator theorem. The retained physical interpolation still has Fourier interval currents and fails the other crossing Ward equations pointwise. This is a limitation of THIS phase representation, not an impossibility of tame linear projections onto the intertwiner space. ## 1. Exact full word and a cost-free degree average Use Rhat_sigma(z) of [the lower](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md) and [upper](actual_projected_transfer_upper_collar.md) collar theorems. It acts on the original orthonormal two-head space H_N tensor H_N. Every physical input index remains an integer in 0,...,d, d=N-1. The full original Cartan factor kappa is included. Write D|a,b>=(a+b)|a,b> and E_D(A)=sum_T P_T A P_T =integral_0^(2pi) exp(itD) A exp(-itD) dt/(2pi), B_sigma(z)=E_D(Rhat_sigma(z)). (1) This is a completely positive contraction in operator norm and a contraction in Hilbert--Schmidt norm. It is a fixed linear map of the matrix entries, so holomorphy, removable zeros, and the collar bounds survive unchanged. The integer transfer slices are also graded, hence E_D fixes EACH original integer slice in this case. Consequently, for any of the enlarged finite-height rectangles Gamma_i, R_sigma=integral_(Gamma_i) pi cot(pi z) B_sigma(z) dz/(2pi i). For a fixed braid word the SAME original scalar is exactly K_N=chi_(beta,N) integral_(product Gamma_i) Phi_N(B_m(z_m)...B_1(z_1)) product_i [pi cot(pi z_i) dz_i/(2pi i)]. (2) Here B_i is embedded on its actual neighboring heads, all spectators are identities, and Phi_N is the original marked pivotal closure or cup/cap functional. All integrals are compact and all head spaces finite, so their ordered composition and Fubini in (2) are exact. The product is now degree preserving POINTWISE in every transfer z_i. The original marked cap may therefore be restricted to its forced degree-d fiber after the ordinary caps, exactly as for the original whole word. This removes a real potential source error; the degree leak of the unsymmetrized interpolant is not unavoidable. For any fixed number of factors the added individual collars have exp(o(N)) operator cost, uniformly over their physical inputs. This is not an estimate on an unrestricted exterior word, which may itself have an exponential norm or scalar period. ## 2. What the repaired physical kernel actually is Put s_c(nu)=[exp(2pi i nu)-1]/[2pi i(nu-c)], sinc(pi w)=sin(pi w)/(pi w). The removable values are retained. If T=a+b, the positive kernel (1) is B_+(z)|a,b>=r(a,b;z) sum_(c=max(0,T-d))^(min(d,T)) sinc^2(pi(b+z-c)) |c,T-c>. (3) Indeed s_(T-c)(a-z)=exp(-2pi iz)s_c(b+z), and the two phase factors cancel in their product, leaving the ENTIRE square in (3). For complex z it is not the modulus square. For real z its coefficients are nonnegative before multiplying by the original scalar r. The exact Fourier representation is sinc^2(pi w)=integral_(-1)^1 (1-|t|) exp(2pi iwt)dt. (4) Thus (2) retains physical interval data even after repairing degree. Splitting (4) into its two analytic intervals leaves endpoints t=+/-1 and a common interface t=0. The weight vanishes at the outer endpoints only to first order; its derivative has a jump at zero. These are not automatically exponentially negligible. Integrating explicitly gives sinc^2(pi w)=[2-exp(2pi iw)-exp(-2pi iw)]/(4pi^2 w^2), (5) with the complete removable value at w=0. Splitting the numerator without its joint cancellation would introduce a false double pole. At an INTERIOR stationary point of (4) the missing output relation b+z=c is restored. At an interval endpoint or interface it is not an available stationarity equation. Such a restricted critical scheme must not simply be substituted into the previously proved FULL original critical ideal. The existing uniform vector bound exp(2pi|Im nu|) is tame at the FIXED transfer height of the collar theorems. At a macroscopic complex transfer z=N zeta, however, (5) can itself have exponent 2pi N|Im zeta|. This is a leading source phase, not a half-density which may be discarded. For example for w=N xi with Im xi>0 and xi bounded away from zero, sinc^2(pi N xi) =-exp(-2pi iNxi)/(4pi^2N^2xi^2)(1+o(1)). (6) The analogous opposite exponential occurs when Im xi<0. These are the original Fourier endpoint sectors. They may subsequently cancel in the complete source, but the outer-collar estimate does not prove that cancellation or identify their coupled stationary support. ### A quantitative whole-word bound for the COMPLETE projection There is a stronger estimate than bounding the individual sinc entries. It controls the complete interval/interface aggregate, with no N-dependent conditioning. Embed the original finite head space isometrically in L^2([0,2pi],dtheta/(2pi)). If S is the head swap and D_r(z) is diagonal on the original finite input basis with entries r(a,b;z), then literally Rhat_+(z)=P_N^(tensor 2) M_z S D_r(z), (M_z f)(theta1,theta2) =exp(iz(theta1-theta2)) f(theta1,theta2). (6a) The output coefficients of (6a) are exactly the two sinc vectors, so no boundary source has been changed. Multiplication has norm exp(2pi|Im z|), the swap is isometric and P_N is orthogonal. Thus ||B_+(z)||op <= ||Rhat_+(z)||op <=exp(2pi|Im z|) max_(a,b physical)|r(a,b;z)|. (6b) The same holds for the literal negative antiunitary mirror. In particular REAL-transfer projection is contractive: it adds NO N factor and no exponential rate to the scalar diagonal coefficient envelope. This is not an estimate on a new norm or a changed source. There is also an exact sharp absolute-column version. For nu=u+iv, sum_(c in Z) |sinc^2(pi(nu-c))| =sinh(2pi|v|)/(2pi|v|), (6c) with value 1 at v=0. Indeed the original Fourier coefficients satisfy |s_c(nu)|^2=exp(-2pi v)|sinc^2(pi(nu-c))|. Plancherel for exp(i nu theta) gives sum |s_c|^2=(1-exp(-4pi v))/(4pi v), which proves (6c). Restricting to the finite allowed c in (3) only decreases the sum. Thus (3)'s physical output column has l1 norm at most |r| times the right side of (6c). At real transfer the weights form a subprobability distribution. For any original b-head one-cut source, or fixed-width marked plat, its actual functional norm is polynomial in N at complete color. Tensoring the local operators with spectators changes none of (6b). Consequently the COMPLETE interval sources in any fixed word satisfy the genuine bound |Phi_N(B_m(z_m)...B_1(z_1))| <=poly_beta(N) exp(2pi sum_i |Im z_i|) product_i max_(a,b)|r_sigma_i(a,b;z_i)|. (6d) Every original cup/cap normalization and the explicit external chi in (2) is retained. This is a quantitative full-source statement, not a claim that separately cut Fourier sectors obey the same bound. On fixed-height cotangent contours, the projection cost in (6d) is O_T(1)^m. Their lengths, cotangent bounds and fixed word length add only polynomial factors. Thus the endpoint/interface aggregate does not create a new exponential envelope ON THOSE CONTOURS. Conversely the macroscopic complex cost in (6b) cannot be replaced by a uniform polynomial for this same scalar interpolation. If z=N zeta, Im zeta!=0, and Re(b+z) lies in the physical output band, choose an allowed c with |b+Re z-c|<=1. Formula (3) then has an individual output coefficient of size |r(a,b;z)| exp(2pi N|Im zeta|)/poly(N), (6e) provided its total-degree block contains that c. For example a+b=d contains every physical c. The denominator in (5) is O(N^2), while its numerator has the stated exponential size. Hence the rate 2pi|Im zeta| is sharp already for the retained physical kernel. This does not prove it survives the exterior knot pairing; it proves that such a cancellation must be retained in a sharp complex-contour argument rather than absorbed into a polynomial projection norm. ## 3. An exact remaining E-coproduct defect Use the original complete scaled currents Ecal|a>=(Q^-a-1)|a-1>, K|a>=x Q^-a|a>, E=Ecal tensor K + I tensor Ecal, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1. The original complete R commutes with E. Its repaired interpolation B_+(z) does not. An exact entry at z=1/2 is <0,0|[E,B_+(1/2)]|1,0> =(Q^-1-1) r(0,0;1/2) (4/pi^2) (1-Q+q^-1). (7) To check it, the two degree-one output weights in (3) are both 4/pi^2, while r(1,0;z)/r(0,0;z) =x^-1 (1-Q)/(1-Q^(1-z)). At z=1/2 this gives (7) directly. It is nonzero at EVERY N>=2: r(0,0;1/2)=kappa x^(1/2)/Fhat(-1/2) is nonzero, and 1-Q+q^-1=0 would imply q^3=q+1. The latter is impossible since |q+1|>=sqrt(2)>1. Therefore degree repair alone does not turn the pointwise five-function density into the complete crossing Ward solution. This defect is visible to an original source. At N=2 use precisely the balanced cup and FULL marked row p_(a,b)=2 x^(a-1) delta_(a+b,1), m_(a,b)=x^b/4, x=i. A direct four-state calculation gives m [E,B_+(1/2)] p =(-16-52i)/(9pi^2 Fhat(-1/2)) != 0. (8) All original kappa and x phases are included in this formula. A marked-fiber replacement must not be applied AFTER the degree-lowering insertion E; (8) uses the full marked row. In contrast, the complete cotangent integral of this commutator is [E,R]=0. Its compensating source currents are therefore essential to any argument based on pointwise Ward equations. This is not a new nonzero knot invariant with an arbitrarily inserted coupon; it tests the proposed density identity before the exact integral is assembled. ## 4. Tame projections exist; they do not supply a free phase theorem No impossibility of a further tame algebraic repair follows from (7). For example the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto the common E,F,K intertwiner space always exists, has HS norm one, and has operator-to-operator norm at most N on a two-head space of dimension N^2. It preserves the complete R integral and every added zero. It need not preserve the separate original transfer residues. More importantly E,F,K intertwiners need not implement the specified braid crossing: they also include other functions of the two-head Casimir. Their phases and canonical relations have to be derived afresh. The same warning applies to the full Hurwitz intertwiner line. If the complete physical algebra makes that solution space span{R}, its HS projection is exactly P_R(A)=<R,A>_HS R / ||R||_HS^2. (9) It is still tame as a linear operator. At an integer transfer k the scalar coefficient is lambda_k=||R_k||_HS^2/||R||_HS^2, sum_k lambda_k=1, because the original transfer slices have disjoint matrix-entry supports. But the entire known exponential crossing matrix R is now a CONSTANT factor in the density P_R(Rhat(z))=lambda_N(z)R. The original word asymptotic is not obtained by analyzing the harmless scalar lambda alone. Such a projection changes the phase representation and packages its difficulty into the retained R factor; it does not contradict (7) or provide the requested sharp geometric bound. ## 5. Critical-path conclusion The theorem removes both artificial OUTER transfer collars, with the physical projections and source retained. Formula (2) is an exact full-word representation, and (1) repairs its pointwise degree at no norm cost. This is substantive source control. What is not yet proved is a bulk-only estimate with exponential rate at most the knot volume. The regular critical-regulator theorem applies to the genuine full crossing/gluing equations. To use it here one must either control the complete Fourier interval currents in (4)--(6), show their coupled stationary support belongs to that actual saturated graph, or give a different phase-preserving source transport. Keeping the finite physical head sums avoids these new complex-head seams, but then the remaining positive matrix bound still loses the global outer phase and is not sharp by knot volume. These alternatives are not supplied by the two local collar estimates alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_word_source.py): exact degree-averaged columns and contraction, original R and E Ward, the all-level entry (7), the full original source (8), the retained triangle Fourier identity, and the exact full-intertwiner projection weights. No sharp bound for a knot family is inferred.

title: Exact spectral coefficient energy at a protected outer face
status: Exact closed relative-energy entropy; both parities
