# Exact spectral coefficient energy at a protected outer face 31 October 2026. **theorem.** A one-sided original coefficient with one outer degree zero has an explicit real-spectral maximum, uniformly through all closed index boundaries and at both level parities. Its endpoint-conditioned energy is exactly a triangle entropy in the limit. This is a local coefficient theorem, not a global shared-flow bound or a new filling theorem. ## 1. The actual coefficient and its positive reference Put \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), and $$ c_r=2\cos rac{(2r+1)\pi}{N},\qquad s_r=2\sin rac{\pi r}{N},\qquad V_N(\sigma)=\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega_N)^{-1}. $$ Use the original homogeneous polynomial \(H_{V_N}\). On LEFT support set \(y=0\) and take $$ v=(j-i,i,d-j,0),\qquad0\le i\le j<m. $$ Every dimer vanishes; every lowering step must use \(x\). The original coefficient has one physical path. Up to its recorded sign, $$ \left|a_N(v;\sigma)ight| =\left(\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r^2ight) \left(\prod_{\substack{0\le r<N\r
otin\{i,\ldots,j\}}} |\sigma-c_r|ight).	ag{1} $$ All unused rows are present, including the entire omitted half. This is the exact [triangular-source path formula](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md), not an absolute replacement inside a recurrence or a division at a node. The coefficient before absolute values has sign \((-1)^{j-i}\) times the displayed product with its signed linear factors. Retain the [positive reference](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) $$ F_N=  egin{cases} -V_N(-2),&N\ 	ext{even},\ V_N(-2)-N^{-2}V_N'(-2),&N\ 	ext{odd}, \end{cases} \qquad p_N(v)=[x^{v_x}b^{v_b}c^{v_c}y^{v_y}]H_{F_N}>0.	ag{2} $$ Write \(\mu=i/N\), \(
u=j/N\), \(w=
u-\mu\), and define on \([0,1/2]\) $$ f(t)= rac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}{\pi}, \qquad f'(t)=\log\cot(\pi t),\qquad f(0)=f(1/2)=0.	ag{3} $$ The closed triangle entropy is \(C(\alpha)=\sum_r f(\alpha_r)\), \(\sum_r\alpha_r=1/2\). ## 2. Uniform theorem Define the exact coefficient supremum $$ k_N^*(v)= rac1N\log\max_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|. $$ Uniformly over all indices in (1), at both parities, $$  egin{aligned} k_N^*(v) &=f(\mu)+f(
u-\mu)-f(
u) +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight),\  rac1N\log p_N(v) &=2 igl(f(\mu)-f(
u) igr) +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight). \end{aligned}	ag{4} $$ Consequently the exact relative-energy profile is $$  oxed{\quad  rac1N\log  rac{\max_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} =2f(w)+O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight) =C(w,	frac12-w,0)+O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight). \quad}	ag{5} $$ The constants are independent of \(i,j,N\). The formula includes diagonal limits, \(\mu=0\), and the limiting upper edge \(
u=1/2\). Outer reflection gives \(x=0\); original row reflection gives RIGHT. Replacing the \(N\)-normalized degrees by \(v/d\) preserves the same continuous limit. ## 3. Uniform control of the exact product Set \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\), \(0\le\delta\le1/2\), and $$ K(\mu,
u;\delta)=\int_\mu^
u \log rac{\sin^2(\pi t)} {|\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)|}\,dt.	ag{6} $$ Every logarithmic singularity is integrable. We first prove $$ k_N^*(v)= \max_{0\le\delta\le1/2}K(\mu,
u;\delta) +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight)	ag{7} $$ uniformly on the closed index domain. A contiguous mesh sum of \(\log|2\sin(\pi(t-a))|\) has upper Riemann error \(O(\log N)\), uniformly in its shift and interval endpoints. Remove at most two cells nearest a zero. Their integral is \(O(\log N/N)\), while a sample exceptionally close to the zero can only improve the upper bound. On the other cells, \(\lvert f'(t)vert\le C/\operatorname{dist}(t,a+\mathbb Z)\) gives an accumulated harmonic-sum error \(O(\log N)\). If every sampled distance to a zero is at least \(c/N\), the same proof gives a two-sided error. Cosine factors follow by translation. For \(t_r=(r+1/2)/N\), the unused factors in (1) satisfy $$ |\sigma-c_r| =4|\cos(\pi(t_r+\delta))\cos(\pi(t_r-\delta))|. $$ The integral of this logarithm over \(0\le t\le1\) is zero. Apply the uniform upper mesh estimate separately to the unused prefix and suffix, and the sine estimate to the used monomer factors. Their difference is exactly (6), with only \(O(\log N/N)\) error. No sampled vanishing factor has been divided out. For the lower bound in (7), choose a point within \(O(1/N)\) of a maximizing \(\delta\) on the lattice $$ \delta_N\in  egin{cases} N^{-1}\mathbb Z,&N\ 	ext{even},\ N^{-1}(\mathbb Z+	frac12),&N\ 	ext{odd}, \end{cases} \qquad0\le\delta_N\le	frac12.	ag{8} $$ At these points \(\chi_N(\sigma)=4\), and every sampled cosine stays at least half a mesh step from its zero. Thus the two-sided estimate applies to all unused intervals. The modulus of continuity of each logarithmic integral under an \(O(1/N)\) shift is \(O(\log N/N)\), uniformly in the interval. This proves (7), including its endpoint cases. Nonempty monomer products start at \(r\ge1\), so their lower endpoint uses the same elementary sine estimate. At even levels (2) is the product (1) at \(\delta=0\). At odd levels LEFT skips the unique central zero row. The derivative in (2) removes exactly that factor; its \(N^{-2}\) scalar and the single removed mesh factor have only \(O(\log N)\) logarithmic cost. Hence, uniformly, $$  rac1N\log p_N(v) =2\int_\mu^
u\log	an(\pi t)\,dt +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight) =2 igl(f(\mu)-f(
u) igr) +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{N}ight).	ag{9} $$ In particular this is not a comparison with bare odd \(V_N(-2)\), whose one-sided coefficients vanish. ## 4. The exact maximizing spectral point For \(0<\mu<
u<1/2\), differentiation of (6), or of its explicit logarithmic primitive, gives $$ \partial_\delta K =\log\left|  rac{\cos(\pi(\mu+\delta))\cos(\pi(
u-\delta))} {\cos(\pi(
u+\delta))\cos(\pi(\mu-\delta))} ight|.	ag{10} $$ It is positive before the pole interval \((1/2-
u,1/2-\mu)\) and negative afterwards. Inside that interval its sign is the sign of $$ \cos(\pi(\mu+
u)) +\cos(\pi(
u-\mu))\cos(2\pi\delta). $$ This expression strictly decreases. There is a unique maximum, given by $$  oxed{\quad \cos(2\pi\delta_*) =- rac{\cos(\pi(\mu+
u))}{\cos(\pi(
u-\mu))}. \quad}	ag{11} $$ The quotient has modulus less than one. For \(\mu=0<
u<1/2\), the maximum is \(\delta_*=1/2\) and \(K^*=0\); for \(0<\mu<
u=1/2\), it is \(\delta_*=0\). The diagonal interval has zero action. At \(\mu=0,
u=1/2\) the maximum need not be unique. Continuity treats all these overlaps. For an explicit primitive, let \(J(t)=-\Lambda(\pi t)/\pi\), extended periodically. Then $$  egin{aligned} K(\mu,
u;\delta) ={}&2[J(
u)-J(\mu)]\ &-J(	frac12+
u+\delta)+J(	frac12+\mu+\delta)\ &-J(	frac12+
u-\delta)+J(	frac12+\mu-\delta). \end{aligned}	ag{12} $$ ## 5. Simplification to a triangle entropy Put \(a=\pi\mu\), \(b=\pi
u\), \(w=
u-\mu\). Equation (11) gives the exact unsquared identities $$  egin{aligned} \cos(2a)+\cos(2\pi\delta_*)&=\sin(2a)	an(\pi w),\ \cos(2b)+\cos(2\pi\delta_*)&=-\sin(2b)	an(\pi w). \end{aligned}	ag{13} $$ Let \(h_0=2(f(\mu)-f(
u))\) and \(e=2K(\mu,
u;\delta_*)-h_0\). Directly from (6), $$ e=2\int_\mu^
u \log\left|  rac{\sin(2\pi t)} {\cos(2\pi t)+\cos(2\pi\delta_*)} ight|dt.	ag{14} $$ The spectral derivative vanishes at the maximizer, so the envelope rule and (13) yield $$ \partial_\mu e=-2\log\cot(\pi w),\qquad \partial_
u e= 2\log\cot(\pi w). $$ Thus \(e\) depends only on \(w\), and its zero-width value is zero. Integrating \(f'(w)=\log\cot(\pi w)\) gives $$ e=2f(w),\qquad K^*=f(\mu)+f(w)-f(
u).	ag{15} $$ Continuity proves these equalities on the full closed domain. Since \(f(1/2-w)=f(w)\), equations (7), (9), and (15) prove (4)–(5). ## 6. Global limitation and validation The limiting LEFT degree vector is \((w,\mu,1-
u,0)\). The triangle entropy in (5) is the entropy of the complete boundary allocation $$ (w,	frac12-w,	frac12,0). $$ This moves \(1/2-
u\) units from the overloaded middle to the other middle, while preserving the outer degree. It does **not** preserve the shared global face targets by itself. On a middle-edge forest, fixing the other triangle allocations generally fixes the middle transport uniquely. A global redistribution argument remains necessary before (5) can bound the [shared conditioned energy](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md). The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.py), with [results](../experiments/actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy_results.json), builds the physical coproduct Casimir and extracts coefficients by the original three-clock inverse DFT. It checks 144 monomer coefficients, 6,408 original grid entries including 2,082 illegal-total zeros, 29 reference coefficients, 21 exact \(\chi_N=4\) samples and 125 node avoidances, three symbolic identities and six fixed integral identities. These exact checks supplement the proof; no large-\(N\) rate samples are used as proof of (4) or of a shared energy bound. The coefficients are extracted from the physical coproduct, independently of the monomer product against which they are compared.

title: Exact auxiliary colors of the pure Conway leaf
text: # Exact auxiliary colors of the pure Conway leaf 29 October 2026. The literal turned crossing circle has an exact positive core and a disjoint, signed alias at every ordinary auxiliary color. Every alias coefficient is at most N/2 in absolute value, uniformly in the color and at both parities. The complete-circle core also simplifies to one positive factorial ratio. These are identities in the FULL pair Casimir algebra, so they retain its projective normal directions. The leaf here is `h_j=Rturn(L_j)`, the one used in the [positive complete-circle Conway grammar](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md). It has no extra half-twist. The older belt leaf `Rturn(R^-1 L_j)` has a different alias and is not covered by this bound. This local theorem alone does not prove a global mixed-color gap or a long-filling theorem. ## 1. Literal source and notation Set \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad D=N-1,\quad M=\lfloor D/2\rfloor, \quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad s_r=\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(u\theta),\quad s_0=1. \] Write \(\mathsf T_n(z)=2T_n(z/2)\), so \(\mathsf T_0=2,\mathsf T_1=z\), and put \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(\mathsf T_N(z)+2),\qquad c_k=q^{2k+1}+q^{-2k-1},\qquad B_r(z)=\prod_{k=0}^{r-1}(c_k-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/s_r^2. \tag{1} \] The [original crossing-circle calculation](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) gives, for the actual auxiliary module of dimension j and its original pivot, with no extra factor 1/j, \[ L_j=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2),\quad 1\le j\le N, \qquad h_j=R_{\mathrm{turn}}L_j. \tag{2} \] The [actual turn and marked closure](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md) satisfy \[ R_{\mathrm{turn}}\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{D-r},\qquad \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)=\delta_{i+j,D},\qquad \phi(L_Nf)=N\sum_{k=0}^{D}f(c_k). \tag{3} \] The sum counts each of the N listed roots, including repetitions. These equations hold in the repeated-root algebra (1), not just its quotient consisting of values at the distinct nodes. In particular the \(\widehat B_v\) coefficient of \(R_{\mathrm{turn}}f\) is \(\phi(f\widehat B_v)\). ## 2. A generic Chebyshev--Newton identity With q initially generic and \({a\brack b}_q\) the symmetric quantum binomial, one has the polynomial identity \[ U_{j-1}(z/2)=\sum_{r=0}^{j-1}(-1)^r {j+r\brack 2r+1}_q B_r(z). \tag{4} \] Here is a direct derivation. For a formal variable t, successive division of \(1-zt+t^2=(1-c_rt+t^2)+t(c_r-z)\) gives \[ \frac1{1-zt+t^2} =\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(-t)^rB_r(z)} {\prod_{i=0}^{r}(1-c_it+t^2)}. \tag{5} \] The remainder after r stages is divisible by \(t^{r+1}\), which justifies the formal identity. The denominator in its rth term is \[ \prod_{a=0}^{2r+1}(1-q^{-(2r+1)+2a}t). \] Its reciprocal has coefficient of \(t^n\) equal to \(q^{-(2r+1)n}{n+2r+1\brack 2r+1}_{q^2}\), where the binomial on the right is the ordinary Gaussian one. This formula follows by induction on the number of factors using the finite geometric series and the Gaussian Pascal recurrence. Converting to the symmetric binomial cancels the displayed q power. Taking \(n=j-r-1\) proves (4), since the left side of (5) generates the Chebyshev polynomials. For \(1\le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), all factorial arguments in (4) are less than N. Specialization therefore gives, without any zero-over-zero division, \[ \boxed{\quad h_j= \sum_{r=0}^{j-1}(-1)^{j-1+r}b_{j,r}\widehat B_{D-r},\qquad b_{j,r}=\frac{s_r^2s_{j+r}}{s_{2r+1}s_{j-r-1}}>0.\quad} \tag{6} \] This is an equality of full polynomials of degree below N after the actual turn, so it includes every repeated-node derivative. For larger j one must retain the Laurent-polynomial binomial in (4), rather than substitute a factorial quotient containing zeros. The next identity avoids all such zero quotients. ## 3. Positive core plus the actual low-color alias For \(0\le h\le M\), define \(L_0=h_0=0\). Then exactly \[ \boxed{\quad h_{N-h}=\sum_{v=h}^{M}A_{N,v}(h)\widehat B_v+(-1)^Nh_h, \qquad A_{N,v}(h)=\frac{N^2s_{2v}} {s_v^2s_{v-h}s_{v+h}}>0.\quad} \tag{7} \] The first sum is the core. If h>0, (6) puts the entire alias in indices \(v\ge N-h\); these are disjoint from the core indices \(h\le v\le M\). At h=0 the alias is zero. In particular the complete-circle coefficients are simply \[ h_N=\sum_{v=0}^{M}a_{N,v}\widehat B_v,\qquad a_{N,v}=\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^4}. \tag{8} \] To prove (7), first use the elementary Chebyshev identity \[ U_{N-h-1}=\tfrac12(\mathsf T_hU_{N-1} -\mathsf T_NU_{h-1}). \] It follows either by multiplying sines and cosines at \(z=2\cos t\), then extending as a polynomial identity, or directly from the Chebyshev recurrence. In the full algebra (1) it becomes \[ L_{N-h}=(-1)^h\frac{\mathsf T_h}{2}L_N+(-1)^NL_h. \tag{9} \] No passage to root values was made in (9). To compute the turn of its first term, it is now legitimate to use the special trace identity (3). Its coefficient at v is \[ (-1)^hN\sum_{k=0}^{D}\cos(h(2k+1)\theta) \widehat B_v(c_k). \tag{10} \] For v>M, \(B_v\) vanishes at all the nodes c_k, so (10) is zero. For v<=M, a finite Laurent expansion gives \[ B_v(w+w^{-1})= \sum_{u=-v}^{v}(-1)^u \frac{[2v]_q!}{[v+u]_q![v-u]_q!}\,w^u. \tag{11} \] For example this follows from \[ B_v(w+w^{-1}) =q^{-v^2}(qw;q^2)_v(q/w;q^2)_v =(-1)^vw^{-v}(q^{1-2v}w;q^2)_{2v}, \] and the finite binomial expansion; its q powers cancel on conversion to symmetric binomials. Evaluating at \(w=q^{2k+1}\), the Fourier average in (10) selects u=+h and u=-h. There are no other Fourier aliases because \(v+h\le2M<N\). The two equal terms cancel the factor 1/2 in the cosine; at h=0 there is just its constant term. This is exactly (7). Moreover the core is pointwise dominated by the complete core: \[ 0<A_{N,v}(h)\le a_{N,v}\quad(0\le h\le v\le M). \tag{12} \] Indeed the ratio \(a_{N,v}/A_{N,v}(h)\) is \(s_{v-h}s_{v+h}/s_v^2\). Its successive ratio as h increases is \[ \frac{\sin((v+h)\theta)}{\sin((v-h+1)\theta)}\ge1, \] since the two arguments sum to \((2v+1)\theta\le\pi\). For h>0 this is strict except at the odd-level endpoint \(v=(N-1)/2\), where equality holds for every allowed h. ## 4. An exact uniform N/2 bound for every alias coefficient For all N>=2, \(1\le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and \(0\le r<j\), \[ \boxed{\qquad 0<b_{j,r}\le N/2,\qquad \sum_{r=0}^{j-1}b_{j,r}\le jN/2\le N^2/4.\qquad} \tag{13} \] The stronger final N^2/4 follows from j<=N/2. The proof uses the actual sine product, not its limiting action. Rewrite (6) as \[ b_{j,r}=\frac{s_r^2}{s_{2r+1}} \prod_{u=-r}^{r}2\sin((j+u)\theta). \tag{14} \] For fixed r this positive product, regarded as a function of real j on \(r<j<N-r\), is symmetric about N/2 and log concave: each summand \(\log\sin((j+u)\theta)\) has strictly negative second derivative. Hence its maximum occurs at j=N/2. The value of (14) there is \[ B_r=2\, \frac{\prod_{u=1}^{r}2\sin(2u\theta)} {\prod_{u=0}^{r}2\sin((2u+1)\theta)}. \tag{15} \] Here one cancels \((2\sin u\theta)(2\cos u\theta) =2\sin2u\theta\). The ratio \[ \frac{B_{r+1}}{B_r} =\frac{\sin((2r+2)\theta)}{\sin((2r+3)\theta)} \] is <=1 and then >=1, with at most one change: the comparison changes at \((4r+5)\theta=\pi\). Thus the maximum over \(0\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\) occurs at an endpoint. At r=0 it is \(\csc\theta\). If N=2m, the other endpoint is \(B_{m-1}=m\), because the even sine product in (15) is m and the odd product is 2. These product evaluations follow directly by factoring \(t^m-1\) and \(t^m+1\) at t=1. If N=2m+1, reflection \(\sin(k\theta)=\sin((N-k)\theta)\) cancels the even factors against the odd factors other than the first, and gives \(B_{m-1}=\csc\theta\). Finally \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\), proving (13). Consequently the alias in (7) has a uniform polynomial coefficient norm, even when its physical color h grows proportionally to N. This is not a positive-source assertion: its coefficients genuinely alternate. For odd N and h=1 the alias is \(-\widehat B_D\). For even N>=4 and h=2, it has coefficient \(-c_0\) at \(\widehat B_D\). These signs cannot be dropped in the original mixed-color source. ## 5. Its real action and a marked local complex interpolation Let \(J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt\). Uniformly at all integer arguments between 0 and N-1, the elementary endpoint-aware sum estimate is \(\log s_r=NJ(r/N)+O(\log N)\). For a direct proof, subtract \(\log t+\log(1-t)\) from the integrand. The remainder extends smoothly to [0,1] and has an O(1) Riemann-sum error. The two subtracted logarithms give ordinary factorial ratios, whose sum-minus-integral errors are O(log N) uniformly, including r=0 and r=N-1. Writing \(x=v/N\) and \(\chi=h/N\), (7) therefore has rate \[ \log A_{N,v}(h)=Ng_\chi(x)+O(\log N),\qquad g_\chi(x)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-\chi)-J(x+\chi), \tag{16} \] uniformly over \(0\le h\le v\le M\). On the interior \(0<\chi<x<1/2\), \[ \partial_\chi g_\chi(x) =\log\frac{\sin\pi(x-\chi)}{\sin\pi(x+\chi)}<0, \qquad \left.\partial_\chi^2g_\chi(x)\right|_{\chi=0} =-2\pi\cot(\pi x)<0. \tag{17} \] The loss is uniform on compact interior sets with chi bounded away from zero. At x=1/2 the continuum loss vanishes, consistently with the exact odd-level endpoint equality in (12); an arbitrary global color gap cannot be inferred without controlling endpoint sources. There is also a fixed, even, holomorphic continuation of this actual core coefficient, without assigning a formal Newton index the role of a peripheral holonomy. Let G_N be the sine-factorial interpolation proved in [the exact interpolation note](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), with \(G_N(r)=s_r\), and define \[ \mathcal A_N(x,\chi)= \frac{N^2G_N(2Nx)}{G_N(Nx)^2G_N(N(x-\chi))G_N(N(x+\chi))}. \tag{18} \] It is holomorphic and nonzero wherever the four scaled arguments lie in the interpolation's strip, and it agrees EXACTLY with (7) at its lattice arguments. On any fixed compact complex corridor where 2x, x, x-chi and x+chi have real parts strictly between 0 and 1, the proved uniform factorial expansion gives \[ \mathcal A_N(x,\chi) =N^{1/2}\, \frac{\sqrt{\sin(2\pi x)}} {2^{3/2}\sin(\pi x) \sqrt{\sin\pi(x-\chi)\sin\pi(x+\chi)}} e^{Ng_\chi(x)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{19} \] All logarithms and square roots are continued from the positive real corridor. The error and every fixed derivative are uniform on a smaller corridor. Thus the local coefficient is an even analytic function of the ACTUAL auxiliary-color deficit chi, with the exact finite values and their marks fixed. This does not assert that the whole finite source already has a single analytic saddle packet: its original support, alias pieces, boundary contributions and contour still require their separate estimates. ## 6. Consequence for arbitrary fixed Conway circuits, and scope There is a useful intrinsic description of the alias subspace: \[ \mathfrak n_N=\operatorname{span}\{\widehat B_v: v\ge\lceil N/2\rceil\} =\operatorname{Nil}(H_N),\qquad \mathfrak n_N^2=0. \tag{20} \] Indeed \(B_{\lceil N/2\rceil}\) contains every distinct factor of \(\mathsf T_N+2\) once, including its simple factor at odd N. The subspace on the left is therefore the kernel of evaluation at all distinct nodes. Every remaining root has multiplicity two, so this is precisely the square-zero nilradical. Equivalently the exact Newton multiplication vanishes when its two input indices sum to at least N. Formula (6) is triangular with nonzero last coefficient \(b_{j,j-1}=s_{j-1}^2\), so \[ h_1,\ldots,h_{\lfloor N/2\rfloor} \quad\text{are a basis of }\mathfrak n_N. \tag{21} \] Thus the signed alias is exactly part of the source's radical data. In a product of any number of mixed pure leaves, terms with two aliases vanish identically. In particular each robust three-leaf seed contains at most one alias term in its exact expansion. The actual turn reverses the Newton indices and does NOT preserve this nilradical; it cannot be quotiented out of a Conway circuit. Each ordinary circle color in an arbitrary fixed robust Conway expression can now be replaced exactly by (6) or (7), followed by the existing full Newton multiplication and actual coordinate reversal for every turn. This gives a finite, source-preserving signed circuit with polynomial alias leaf coefficients and positive core coefficients bounded by the corresponding complete ones. All original colors, marked cuts, pivots and normal directions are retained. It is an exact deformation through ordinary AUXILIARY COLORS; it is not yet a deformation in a separately identified geometric meridian or longitude. Polynomial leaf aliases can acquire exponential growth when multiplied by other circuit factors. Consequently (13) alone is not a proof of an exponentially negligible whole alias sector. That global source comparison, the complex whole-source saddle, and the geometric peripheral interpretation are the additional steps needed before invoking a long-filling transfer theorem. Audit: [generic polynomial identities, all root coefficients and literal physical turns](../experiments/audit_actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.py). The principal-root inequalities are proved above; finite-field calculations are used only to verify exact identities.

text: # Finite local curvature of the original boundary models 30 October 2026. The actual 220/222 determinants and the actual 202 positive polynomial have logarithmic curvature bounded above and below by constant multiples of N, uniformly through the fold. The other retained factors have nonlinear derivatives of size O(s+1), where s is the channel deficit. These are finite local source statements. No graph-rank, stationary-point, Gaussian reduction or original-period assertion is made. ## 1. Actual clocks and the finite core factors Put N>=3, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2. Keep an ACTUAL integer channel a with a0 N<=a<=floor(d/2), a0>0, m=d-a, s=d-2a. All estimates are for sufficiently large N, including either maximal folded parity. Coefficients below range in fixed positive compact sets. Use the exact physical half-index clocks U=q^-1 X, V=q^-1 Y, QUV=XY. (1) The half-index is not dropped, and a is not replaced by a limiting continuous color. The actual source determinant is H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. (2) The a-by-a Hermitian positive matrices H_-,H_+ have diagonal d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], 0<=n<a, and upper adjacent entries h_n^+/-=sqrt(b_n)[sin(n theta)+/-i cos(n theta)], b_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)], 1<=n<a. We take H_+ to have the plus upper entry and H_- the minus entry, as in the [source determinant](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). These are the original finite coefficients, including the fold endpoint. For negative raw clocks X,Y set alpha=-X/2>0, beta=-1/(2Y)>0, M=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+. The finite nonlinear core factors of the six models are: * 220: det(I+alpha H_-), depending on the first raw log clock; * 022: det(I+beta H_-), after the literal reversed reciprocity, depending on the second raw log clock with opposite sign; * 222: det M, retaining BOTH actual finite clocks; * 202: P_a(w)=sum_(k=0)^a beta_(a,k)^2 w^k, w=QUV=XY>0, beta_(a,k)=S_a/(S_k S_(a-k)), S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(r theta); * 200 and 002: no order-N nonlinear core is extracted here. Every source scalar, affine phase, monomial and large-partner product remains in the finite models of the [correlated-band theorem](actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.md). The word "core" separates a derivative calculation, not a change to the source. Positivity below refers to real LOGARITHMIC RADII. A change of normalized magnetic head nu changes its clock by exp(2pi i nu), so pullback to those heads retains the factors 2pi i and the literal incidence signs. No positivity in real magnetic-angle directions is asserted. ## 2. An exact noncommutative determinant Hessian Write Xmat=alpha H_-, Ymat=beta H_+, and A=M^-1/2 Xmat M^-1/2, B=M^-1/2 Ymat M^-1/2. For real u,v let D differentiate alpha->alpha exp(tu), beta->beta exp(tv). The finite matrix differentiation identity gives D^2 log det M =Tr[u^2 A+v^2 B-(uA+vB)^2] =u^2 Tr(Xmat M^-2)+v^2 Tr(Ymat M^-2) +(u-v)^2 Tr(AB). (3) Indeed A+B=I-M^-1. Substitute this in Tr(A-A^2) and Tr(B-B^2) and use cyclicity of trace. No commutativity of H_- and H_+ is assumed. Each term on the last line is nonnegative: for example Tr(AB)=Tr(A^1/2 B A^1/2)>=0. Since A,B are positive and A+B<I, the first line also gives D^2 log det M<=a(u^2+v^2). (4) For actual raw log-clock directions (u,v), equation (1) instead changes alpha by exp(tu) and beta by exp(-tv). Thus the last square in (3) is (u+v)^2, while the first two squares are unchanged. This sign is part of the original second-clock normalization. The one-variable beta=0 specialization of (3) is (alpha partial_alpha)^2 log det(I+alpha H_-) =Tr[alpha H_-(I+alpha H_-)^-2]. (5) ## 3. A finite bulk argument gives the lower bound through the fold The actual Cholesky pivots are p_(n-1)=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)], 1<=n<=a. Consequently, for h_n the upper entry of either H matrix, z*Hz=sum_(n=1)^(a-1) p_(n-1) |z_(n-1)+(h_n/p_(n-1))z_n|^2 +p_(a-1)|z_(a-1)|^2. (6) This is the original square decomposition; it follows by multiplying its factors and the displayed finite trigonometric pivot identity. Only ACTUAL rows appear. No virtual endpoint or singular extension beyond the maximal folded matrix is used. Select every other adjacent square whose two indices lie in a fixed bulk interval, for example a0 N/4<=n<=a0 N/2. Their supports are disjoint, and their number is at least cN. The pivots, h_n, row norms and reciprocal row norms are bounded on this interval independently of N and a. If w_j are the normalized column vectors of those squares, they are orthonormal, and (6) gives Xmat>=c P, P=sum_j w_j w_j*, rank P>=cN. (7) On the support of each w_j all entries of M are uniformly bounded, since it is wholly inside that same bulk interval. Thus <w_j,Mw_j><=C. For the spectral probability measure of M at w_j, convexity of lambda->lambda^-2 gives <w_j,M^-2 w_j>>=<w_j,Mw_j>^-2>=C^-2. Taking the trace of (7) against the positive M^-2 proves Tr(Xmat M^-2)>=cN. (8) Apply the same argument separately to the squares of H_+ to prove Tr(Ymat M^-2)>=cN. Their selected projections need not coincide. The uniform lower and upper compact bounds on alpha,beta are used here. Together with (3),(4), this proves cN(u^2+v^2)<=D^2 log det M<=CN(u^2+v^2). (9) The same proof with beta=0 and (5) proves cN<=log-radius curvature of the 220 core<=CN. Exact reciprocity gives the 022 statement with its recorded inverse clock. These estimates require a/N bounded below, but no upper gap from the fold. Large final entries do not affect the selected bounded bulk squares or their expectations. ## 4. Exact 202 curvature is a uniformly nondegenerate variance For positive w define the probability weights pi_k=beta_(a,k)^2 w^k/P_a(w), 0<=k<=a. Direct differentiation, with all finite coefficients retained, gives (w partial_w)^2 log P_a(w)=Var_pi(k). (10) Here is a uniform two-sided estimate without differentiating a limiting Laplace formula. The EXACT consecutive weight ratio is R(k)=w[sin((a-k)theta)/sin((k+1)theta)]^2. Extend its logarithm to real 0<=x<=a-1. It satisfies (log R)'(x) =-2theta sin((a+1)theta) /[sin((a-x)theta)sin((x+1)theta)]. (11) Since a0 N<=a<=floor(d/2), this is at most -c/N throughout its interval. For w in a fixed positive compact the crossing of R through one is a distance cN from both ends: for x<=cN the numerator sine is bounded below while the denominator is at most Cc, and the reverse holds for x>=a-cN. Choose c small using the two bounds on w. Thus any modal integer k_* lies in [cN,a-cN]. On a fixed smaller bulk neighborhood of k_*, (11) has absolute value at most C/N. The adjacent modal logarithmic ratios are consequently O(1/N). Multiplying the exact ratios away from k_* now yields, for every k, weight(k)/weight(k_*)<=C exp[-c(k-k_*)^2/N]. (12) The bulk upper bound on the ratio drops also gives a fixed positive lower bound for that ratio whenever |k-k_*|<=2sqrt(N), for large N. It follows by summing (12) and those central terms that c sqrt(N) weight(k_*)<=P_a(w)<=C sqrt(N) weight(k_*). The upper Gaussian bound gives E[(k-k_*)^2]<=CN, hence Var(k)<=CN. Each of the two integer shells k_*-2sqrt(N)<=k<=k_*-sqrt(N) and k_*+sqrt(N)<=k<=k_*+2sqrt(N) has probability at least c>0. For independent samples K,K', the identity Var(K)=E[(K-K')^2]/2 therefore gives Var(K)>=cN. This proves cN<=(w partial_w)^2 log P_a(w)<=CN. (13) In the actual two raw log-clock directions this is the quadratic form Var(k)(u+v)^2, because w=QUV=XY EXACTLY. The affine phase (-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2] contributes no curvature. ## 5. Fixed holomorphic logarithmic derivatives are O(N) The preceding finite bounds have uniform complex neighborhoods. For a positive reference M and complex z_1,z_2 near zero, M(z)=I+exp(z_1)Xmat+exp(z_2)Ymat. Conjugating its increment by M^-1/2 gives (exp(z_1)-1)A+(exp(z_2)-1)B, whose norm is less than one half on a fixed polydisc, because A,B are positive with A+B<I. The matrix logarithm series is therefore convergent and |Log(det M(z)/det M)|<=C a. Cauchy's formula on a smaller fixed polydisc proves that every fixed positive-order logarithmic derivative is O(N), including mixed derivatives and both maximal-fold parities. The same proof covers 220 by setting Ymat=0. The normalization of the logarithm is relative to its positive reference determinant; no absolute O(N) bound on unrelated scalar logs is needed. For 202 the proved original negative-root theorem factors P_a(w)=C_a product_j(w+rho_j), rho_j>0. For w in a positive compact and small complex z, every factor w exp(z)+rho_j stays a fixed relative distance from zero. Its marked logarithmic ratio is O(1) uniformly in rho_j; summing over a factors and using Cauchy gives the same O(N) bound for every fixed positive-order derivative. In particular, changing the logarithmic base clocks by O(N^-1) changes each core Hessian by O(1), by the third-derivative bound and integration along that short path. This controls the ACTUAL finite-r clock correction to the real signed limiting clocks. It does not discard the order-one transport term in the determinant or its source phase. ## 6. The retained noncore factors have O(s+1) nonlinear cost Use the EXACT finite models from the correlated-band theorem on its fixed complex clock polydisc. Let z_1,z_2 denote logarithmic clock variations; marked heads are pulled back by their actual affine lifts. All statements below concern fixed derivatives of total order at least two. A function linear in these logarithms has zero such derivatives, even when its value or first derivative is large. The root cup identity is exactly p_(d-s)(x)=F_s exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)). (14) Its character is retained. At finite auxiliary clocks every denominator is uniformly separated from zero, so each logarithmic derivative of order at least two costs O(s). At an escaping clock of size N^2 or N^-2, first factor its full linear monomial if necessary; the remaining derivatives cost O(s/N^2). Physical cups have s=0 and are EXACT linear characters, as are their inverse caps. Literal dual reversals and their Chevalley scalar are affine substitutions with their recorded signs. For 202/222 the retained partner product P_s(T)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r) has fixed logarithmic derivatives O(s): its positive total neighborhood is separated from the forced arc. For 220/022 its total has size N^2 or N^-2; after retaining the exact leading linear monomial its nonlinear derivatives cost O(s/N^2). These statements hold uniformly in a sufficiently small near-fold neighborhood s<=eta N, including both folded parities. The 200 model retains (-1)^m Q^{m(m+1)/2}(UV)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q^r/U) times its zero-free Bessel factor. The monomial has zero nonlinear derivatives. The product contributes O(m/N^2)=O(N^-1), and the Bessel logarithm contributes O(1) on its fixed zero-free complex compact. For 002, extract the exact constant product of -Q^r from product_(r<m)(V-Q^r); its remaining product has the same O(N^-1) cost, and its Bessel factor has O(1) cost. No Bessel factor or phase is discarded. The 022 reciprocity prefactor is also exactly linear in the logarithmic heads. All other original white monomials, half-twist channel weights, fixed root gamma/h0 factors and physical pivotal characters are affine in the varying logarithmic heads, or independent of them. Their actual values and first derivatives remain part of the source; this theorem does not assert that they satisfy a stationary equation. An exposed coherent binomial row, including its actual first-head normalization, is not one of these local tensor factors. Its separate nonlinear action and curvature are not removed by this decomposition. Consequently, for one actual local boundary model, its logarithm decomposes locally as an AFFINE retained source term, the applicable core from section 1, and a remainder whose every fixed nonlinear logarithmic derivative is O(s+1). For any fixed collection of these local factors with the literal bounded affine head substitutions, the correction is O(S+1), S=sum deficits. This is just a derivative bound on a finite product; it asserts no rank of that affine substitution. Finally the actual root numerator/model ratio has a holomorphic O(N^-1) remainder on this same fixed normalized-head neighborhood. The logarithm and all its fixed derivatives are O(N^-1) on a smaller polydisc. Thus it adds only that error to the local curvature estimates. Generic quantum normals are a separate calculation and are not obtained by differentiating this ROOT identity. These facts identify the finite local sources of order-N curvature and bound their retained corrections. They do not prove a transverse rank, stationarity of the complete geometric sample for the actual labels, a nonzero Gaussian coefficient, or an original relative-cycle pairing. text: # Actual complementary heads and the outgoing large-clock packet 30 October 2026. Two exact source identities extend the proved boundary packets. Generic Chevalley complementation transports the retained 0F1 normals to the small second-clock regime. A separate positive-matrix comparison controls the outgoing large-second-clock numerator at the root, through the fold. The original scalar factors and large partner remain explicit. This does not yet assemble every cup factor or select a global period. ## 1. An exact generic reciprocity, before any root collision Let H=H_m^B(U,V) be the actual generic white polynomial, and put A0=Q^d=(BQ)^(-1), d=N-1 fixed. Then H(A0/V,A0/U)=A0^m(UV)^(-m)H(U,V). (1) Here U=Q^x,V=Q^y use their marked logarithms, and the complementary heads are EXACTLY d-y,d-x. In particular d does not move with the quantum period, and (1) may be genuinely differentiated. There is a direct independent-variable proof from the actual [white Ward equations](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md). Set Htilde=(UV/A0)^m H(A0/V,A0/U). It is polynomial of degree at most m in each variable. Substituting X=A0/V,Y=A0/U shows that the E equation for H becomes the F equation for Htilde, and the F equation becomes its E equation, with the original coefficients. For example multiply the E equation at X,Y by UV/A0^2; it reads U(1-V)H(QX,Y)+(1-U)H(X,QY)=(Q^m-UV)H(X,Y), which is precisely the transformed F equation. These two equations determine the polynomial up to one scalar. To see this without a finite-grid continuation assumption, expand in the Newton basis P_b(U)=product_(r<b)(U-Q^r). After removing the first b basis terms, evaluate the F equation at U=Q^b. The coefficient h_b(V) must satisfy Q^b(1-V)h_b(V/Q)=(1-VQ^(b-m))h_b(V). Among polynomials of degree at most m its solutions are exactly the multiples of V^b P_(m-b)(V), as follows by coefficient comparison, starting at its lowest power. Induction gives the actual Newton basis used in the source. The E equation then fixes its adjacent coefficients by the original generic ratio. This is a rational-function proof for generic Q,B; specialization follows after clearing denominators. Finally H(0,0)=(-1)^m Q^[m(m-1)/2]. The coefficient of U^mV^m in Htilde is A0^(-m)H(0,0)=(-B)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2], exactly the top coefficient of H. This proves (1) with scalar ONE, and in particular retains the actual Chevalley normalization. ## 2. The genuine small-second-clock packet Suppose at the root U_N is in a fixed compact subset of C*, V_N=N^(-2)v_N with v_N in such a compact, and the fixed marked heads have size O(N log N). Retain t=N^2 epsilon and all moving quantities from the [generic resonant hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.md). The transformed clocks U'=A0/V,V'=A0/U satisfy its hypotheses. At t=0 define kappa'_N=A0(0)/v_N, V'_N=A0(0)/U_N, K'_N=sin^2(pi m/N)(V'_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa'_N V'_N). Equation (1) transports the exact normalization as well: Z_low(t)=c_m(t)A0(t)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q(t)^r V(t)/A0(t)) =(-1)^m Q(t)^[m(m-1)/2] product_(r<m)(1-B(t)Q(t)^(r+1)V(t)). (2) Thus, uniformly on each fixed |t|<=rho<pi, H_m^B(U,V)/Z_low(t) =0F1(;1-t/(pi i);-K'_N)+O((1+log N)/N). (3) All fixed scaled genuine quantum jets have the same convergence. The transformed heads d-y,d-x are fixed as epsilon varies; neither the A0 derivative nor the marked character is suppressed. Equation (2) notably cancels the B powers in c_m A0^m exactly. The estimate remains absolute across zeros of the limiting function. ## 3. A uniform comparison of the two actual positive matrices At the ROOT let a<=floor((N-1)/2), theta=pi/N, and use the actual Hermitian matrices H_+,H_- from the [full physical determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). Their diagonal is d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], and their adjacent upper entries are sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta)+/-i cos(n theta)], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. They satisfy, uniformly in N,a including the maximal folded a, H_+ <= 2H_-+8I, H_- <= 2H_++8I. (4) Here the inequalities are Hermitian quadratic-form inequalities. The proof retains their exact endpoint coefficients. Both matrices have the same Cholesky pivots as the positive D matrix, namely p_(n-1)=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)]. Write their quadratic forms as sums of squared adjacent Cholesky terms and the final positive pivot. Flipping an offdiagonal phase changes its term by 2i sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta)/p_(n-1) times the next coordinate. The inequality |x+y|^2<=2|x|^2+2|y|^2 gives an additional diagonal cost 8 B_n cos^2(n theta)/p_(n-1) =4sin(2n theta)/sin((2n+1)theta)<=8. Indeed sin(2n theta)=2cos(theta)sin((2n+1)theta) -sin((2n+2)theta), and the last sine is nonnegative for every actual offdiagonal n<=a-1. This proves the first inequality in (4), and complex conjugation proves the second. No lower eigenvalue estimate or inverse channel norm is introduced. ## 4. The actual root numerator when the second clock is large Put K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. The exact source determinant, with its retained scalar, gives H_a^1(U,V)/V^a =K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+]. (5) For example derive this from R_a(z;-cos gamma) =det[zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2], with z=q^t/U, e^(i gamma)=q q^t and (q^t)^2=UV, before canceling the displayed powers. This proves (5) as a polynomial identity and does not make a square-root choice in its final formula. Let qU range in a fixed compact subset of Re z<0, and let V=N^2 kappa_N with kappa_N in a fixed compact subset of C*. Set M0=I-(qU/2)H_-. Then H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) This is a UNIFORM RELATIVE estimate, including folded a. To prove it put D0=I+(eta/2)H_-, where -Re(qU)>=eta>0. The conjugated M0 has inverse norm at most one, while (4) bounds D0^(-1/2)H_+D0^(-1/2) uniformly. Thus the relative perturbation from the last term in (5) has norm O(N^-2). Expanding Log det costs at most a O(N^-2)=O(N^-1). This also proves nonvanishing and a marked relative logarithm on the stated domain. At qU negative real, det M0 is strictly positive. K_a and V^a retain their original phases. For the actual LARGE root channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity supplies H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). Consequently its corresponding packet is H_m^1(U,V)=V^m U^(m-a) K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (7) The added product differs from (UV)^(m-a) by 1+O(N^-1). This is explicitly a ROOT identity: it is not differentiated as a generic large/small collision. Generic normals in this second large-clock regime remain separate from (6),(7). ## 5. The genuine paired 200/220 circle There is an exact geometric use of the negative ray in (6). Take the root theorem's 200 box with B=-J, J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and write A=[[a,-(a+1)^2/4],[4,-2-a]], P=BA, C=I+b(P+I), Aout=C^-1 A C, Q1=e[[1,z],[0,1]], W=A^-1Q1, e=+/-1. Direct multiplication, with the ACTUAL inverse collar transport, gives W_21=-4e, (Aout W)_21=16e b^2, U_geom,out=-W_21/(Aout W)_21=1/(4b^2). (8) Here C names the auxiliary collar, so its inverse gives the displayed transport. Conventions naming the transport itself C write C A C^-1 instead. The lower-left entry and ratio in (8) are unchanged under b->-b, so this squared-ray certificate is identical in those two notations; it does not change any primitive peripheral mark. The [marked complete rectangle collar](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md) has b=-i/(2c), c>0, including its retained half-twist convention. Thus U_geom,out=-c^2. The physical half-index argument is U=q^-1 U_geom,out up to the retained finite-r correction, so qU approaches precisely this negative ray. Formula (7) therefore gives the nonzero outgoing 220 numerator paired with the incoming 200 Bessel packet. No independent phase of U has been chosen. The actual white monomial, F_m denominator, categorical dual, channel cup, physical caps and exterior source scalar still have to be retained when assembling the full box. Their exact lifts and logarithmic-escape estimates remain available; they are not set equal to one by (8). Other prefix patterns, original boundary currents and the global relative-cycle coefficient are not resolved by this local paired-numerator statement. Focused audit: [original generic reciprocity and complementary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 126 original generic reciprocity four-jets, retaining 504 coefficients; three exact paired-circle matrix identities; 17 folded positive-matrix comparisons and 173 pivot evaluations; 21 small and 21 large original-source determinant identities; and eight each of root220 relative-rate, generic002 packet and genuine002 first/second normal diagnostics. These finite checks supplement the proofs and do not prove their uniform asymptotic estimates. The result gives exact reciprocity, genuine 002 normals and a root 220 numerator packet. It supplies neither generic 220 normals, a completed boundary-circle packet nor a global period coefficient.

title: The actual q-Hahn numerator at a deficient integer degree
status: Forced support zeros and selected fixed-degree packet
text: # The actual q-Hahn numerator at a deficient integer degree 30 October 2026. Fix an actual integer degree t below the small channel a. The original generic numerator has an exact forced factor, which persists BEFORE root specialization. Its residual root polynomial is a positive-spectrum real Jacobi determinant. This gives a nonzero relative root amplitude at complex magnetic coordinates away from its explicit cuts, and polynomial cost for genuine q derivatives of this original numerator. The degree t stays an integer. A joint complex-degree estimate and the full exceptional operator's generic boundary factors are not asserted. Nor does a nonzero off-grid local packet change the fact that every original physical entry in the forbidden degree slice, including its q normals, is zero. ## 1. The forced factor is an identity of the original generic source Use the exact generic source and recurrence of [the small-channel normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md). Thus N>=3, d=N-1, q varies near q0=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, B=Q^-N, and H_a^B is the original finite Newton numerator. Its monic reverse polynomial is R_a(q;t,z)=z^a S_a^B(q^t/z,Q^t)/(Q^(ta) K_a), S_a^B(U,T)=U^a H_a^B(U,T/U), K_a=(B^2 Q^(a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a. (1) Throughout 0<=t<a<=floor(d/2). All coefficients and K_a are holomorphic root units where required; in particular K_a(q0)!=0. At U=Q^r, 0<=r<=t, every kth summand of H_a^B contains product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) *product_(j<a-k)(Q^t/U-Q^j). Either k>r or a-k>t-r, so it vanishes. This is true at GENERIC q, with all the original B factors retained. Consequently F_t(q,z)=product_(r=0)^t(z-q^(t-2r)) divides R_a(q;t,z). (2) The nodes are distinct near q0. At a=t+1 monicity gives R_(t+1)=F_t exactly. Write the genuine generic recurrence as R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n(q;t))R_n+beta_n(q;t)R_(n-1). When a>=t+2, its next step, together with (2), forces beta_(t+1)(q;t)=0 IDENTICALLY. (3) Indeed a nonzero scalar times the lower-degree monic R_t cannot be divisible by F_t. It follows that the quotient V_m(q;t,z)=R_(t+1+m)(q;t,z)/F_t(q,z) has its own exact tail recurrence V_0=1, V_1=z+alpha_(t+1), V_(m+1)=(z+alpha_(t+1+m))V_m +beta_(t+1+m)V_(m-1). (4) When a=t+1 the quotient is simply V_0=1, and no recurrence at a larger degree is needed. No q derivative couples a nonempty tail back across the vanished bridge (3). This differs from differentiating a factorization that holds only at a root of unity. ## 2. Exact root locations in the deficient chart Put theta=pi/N and c=-cos((t+1)theta)<0. The root recurrence is alpha_n=c/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], beta_n=B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (5) For n>=t+2, n<a, beta_n<0. Hence V_(a-t-1) is the characteristic polynomial of a real symmetric Jacobi matrix: its diagonal entries are -alpha_n for n=t+1,...,a-1, and its adjacent entries are sqrt(-beta_n), n=t+2,...,a-1. Its roots are in fact POSITIVE, not merely real. The exact root recurrence has R_a(z;-c)=(-1)^a R_a(-z;c). Set t_hi=N-t-2, -cos((t_hi+1)theta)=-c. Then t_hi>=d-a lies in the original complete-column chamber. Its proved root factorization has forced LEFT unit-arc roots and a negative-real residual. Reflection z->-z gives precisely the forced roots in (2) and positive-real roots for V. Their simplicity also follows from the irreducible real Jacobi matrix in (4). Thus every zero of the ACTUAL root polynomial R_a is on {q^(t-2r):0<=r<=t} union (0,infinity). (6) Choose compact real parameter ranges 0<sigma_0<=sigma=t/N<=sigma_1<1/2, sigma+eta<=alpha=a/N<=1/2, eta>0. (7) Take the common slit domain Omega=C\([0,infinity) union {exp(i phi):|phi|<=pi sigma_1}). (8) It is connected and simply connected: in the logarithm plane with 0<Arg z<2pi the removed unit arc is two finite vertical slits attached to the two edges of the strip. In particular negative real z belongs to Omega. The root polynomial is nowhere zero there, uniformly for the levels and parameters in (7). ## 3. The actual selected leading phase and relative amplitude Fix z0=-1. There are functions S_(sigma,alpha),A_(sigma,alpha), holomorphic in z on Omega, with S(z0)=0,A(z0)=1 and A nowhere zero, such that on each fixed compact in Omega R_a(q0;t,z)/R_a(q0;t,z0) =A_(sigma,alpha)(z) exp[N S_(sigma,alpha)(z)] *(1+O(N^-1)). (9) The error and all its fixed z derivatives are uniform. The ACTUAL ratios sigma=t/N and alpha=a/N are used. No uniform continuation in complex sigma is claimed. Here is a proof and a normalization that determines the functions. From (6), logarithmic derivatives of N^-1 Log[R_a(z)/R_a(-1)] are uniformly bounded on compact subsets of Omega; the logarithm is zero at -1. Its higher derivatives have the same local bounds. For z=-r<0 use the exact reflection R_a(q0;t,-r)=(-1)^a R_a(q0;t_hi,r), t_hi=N-t-2. (10) The right side is the already proved ACTUAL high-degree packet. Consequently every normal-family limit agrees there with S_(sigma,alpha)(-r) =Phi_alpha(1-sigma,v_r)-Phi_alpha(1-sigma,v_1) -pi i(v_r-v_1), v_r=(1-sigma)/2+i log(r)/(2pi), v_1=(1-sigma)/2. (11) The identity theorem fixes its continuation uniquely on Omega. The finite offset -2 in (10) is retained for the absolute anchor; only its limit is used in (11). Sequential compactness gives the claimed uniform leading convergence over (7), even when the actual parameters approach their limits slower than 1/N. For an explicit transport proof of the relative error, put D=z partial_z, kappa=2pi i, U=exp(pi i sigma)/z, T=exp(2pi i sigma), J=exp(2pi i alpha). The SAME root finite polynomial satisfies exactly (QU-1)(U-T) R(z/Q)+(QT-U)(1-U) R(Qz) +[2U+2QTU-(1+Q)U^2-T(Q^-a+Q^(a+1))]R(z)=0. (12) This is the original generic Casimir identity for S, with the monic reverse substitution (1); it is valid at these deficient degrees too. Write A0=(U-1)(U-T), C0=2U(1+T-U)-T(J+J^-1), H(p,z)=A0(exp(kappa p)+exp(-kappa p))+C0. For p=D S the selected characteristic is H(p,z)=0. Its derivative H_p is nonzero on Omega. Indeed C0^2-4A0^2=-16 T^2 sin^2(pi alpha) W/z^2, W=1-2cos(pi sigma)z+cos^2(pi alpha)z^2. (13) When sigma<alpha<=1/2, all finite roots of W are positive real: for alpha<1/2 its quadratic has positive sum and product and cos^2(pi sigma)>cos^2(pi alpha); at alpha=1/2 it is linear with positive root. Also A0 vanishes only at the excluded unit-arc endpoints. This proves uniform simplicity on the stated compacts. The first coefficient of (12), after its exact shifts are expanded, is H1=kappa[U(U-T)exp(-kappa p) +T(1-U)exp(kappa p)+2TU-U^2-TJ], rho=-(H1+(D p)H_(p,p)/2)/H_p. (14) Define A by D Log A=rho and A(-1)=1. Simplicity and the larger- compact Cauchy bounds first give D(N^-1 Log R)-p=O(N^-1). Cauchy gives that bound for its fixed derivatives too. Substituting a second time into (12) then gives D(N^-1 Log R)=p+rho/N+O(N^-2). Integrate along compact paths from -1. The exact normalized ratio at the starting point is one, proving (9) and its error. This is an actual finite-shift bootstrap, not a formal transport ansatz. The coefficients are smooth in the real parameters (7), by the simple characteristic and the actual anchor (11). The absolute anchor in (9) is explicitly known from (10) and the original ordinary normalization: R_a(q0;t,-1)=(-1)^a b_a^-1 product_(r=0)^(a-1)2sin[pi(t_hi-r)/N] *q0^[-d t_hi/2-(a^2-da)/2] *fhat_a(t_hi,t_hi/2), b_a=s_(2a)/s_a^2. (15) The fhat on the last line is the proved nonzero ordinary packet evaluated at its ACTUAL high total t_hi=N-t-2, including a half-integer magnetic center when necessary. Thus (9) has no unfixed multiplicative phase or scale. One may apply that packet and the elementary sine-product estimate directly to (15). ## 4. Polynomial cost of genuine generic-q numerator derivatives Let z=q^(t-2u), with the complex physical coordinate u held fixed while q=q0 exp(epsilon) varies. Require a FIXED logarithmic lift: the root z lies in a fixed compact of Omega and |u|<=C N. For example, take u=(t-Log(z)/(pi i/N))/2 with the marked branch of Log on Omega. The fixed integer t and a obey (7). Then for each fixed m |partial_epsilon^m R_a(q;t,q^(t-2u))|_(epsilon=0) <=C_m N^(10m) |R_a(q0;t,q0^(t-2u))|. (16) Here the polynomial is the original generic R from (1), with B=Q^-N. It is not obtained by differentiating the root recurrence (5) while discarding B. A root value z alone does not fix this jet: replacing u by u+N L preserves z(q0) but changes its q derivative by -2N L z. The bounded marked lift is therefore necessary. To prove (16), first split off the genuine factor (2). On a small generic disk its explicit logarithmic derivative is O(N^2), since all root distances from the compact to the unit arc are bounded below. For the residual determinant (4), freeze each upper entry at its positive root value sqrt(-beta_n(q0)); put the generic lower entry equal to -beta_n(q)/sqrt(-beta_n(q0)). Its diagonal is z(q)+alpha_n(q). The determinant is precisely the actual V. At the root this matrix is the alternating-sign unitary conjugate of zI minus the positive-spectrum real Jacobi matrix in section 2: the frozen positive offdiagonals differ from its negatives by that diagonal sign gauge. Its inverse is bounded by the inverse distance of the compact from [0,infinity). Moreover, for n>=t+2, cos^2((t+1)theta)-cos^2(n theta) =sin((n+t+1)theta)sin((n-t-1)theta)>=c/N, uniformly on (7). Since B_n>=1/4, every frozen upper entry has size at least c N^-1/2. The original generic recurrence estimates give alpha_n'=O(N^5), beta_n'=O(N^7), uniformly for all required n<=a. Thus the perturbed determinant matrix differs from its root matrix by at most C N^(15/2)|epsilon| in operator norm. On |epsilon|<=c N^-10 its determinant ratio is bounded uniformly above and below: apply det(I+M0^-1(M-M0)) with dimension at most N. The forced product has the same property there. Cauchy's formula proves (16). The same argument bounds the exact scalar K_a and monomial factors in (1), whose relative logarithmic derivatives are polynomial. Therefore (16) also controls the original unnormalized Newton numerator at these complex magnetic arguments. It does not divide by D_a(Q^t), which vanishes here. ## 5. The local kernel application and the remaining period problem The [entire exceptional source](actual_matching_edge_entire_operator_kernel.md) uses two copies of these root R polynomials at the SAME deficient integer degree. If both determinant arguments lie in fixed compacts of Omega, (9),(15) give their actual nonzero root packet, with the residual sine product and original normalization retained. This includes large genuinely nonreal determinant arguments; the forbidden physical nodes on the unit arc remain outside Omega. This is the chart supplied by the [actual global real-deficient frame](actual_augmented_plat_real_deficient_frame.md). For each level choose t_N near N/6 and set d_N=tan(pi t_N/N) in that construction. Its two failed factors then have the EXACT real normalized degree t_N/N, with the determinant arguments in the upper and lower half-planes. Fixing one sufficiently large geometric X and an interior midpoint keeps these arguments in fixed compact subsets of Omega as N grows. The marked magnetic lifts stay bounded after division by N. In the folded limit alpha->1/2, the original magnetic momentum associated to this numerator is Y=-exp(-2pi i D S). Its selected branch is Y(z)=(z-i sqrt(1-2cos(pi sigma)z))^2 /[1-2cos(pi sigma)z+z^2], (17) where the square root is positive at z<0 and continued through the respective half-plane. To check the sign, (10) sends z=-r to high z=r>0, whose proved selected characteristic has the PLUS square root. Replacing r by -z gives exactly (17). Characteristic simplicity continues it uniquely. This is the actual geometric branch established in the frame theorem, with its output disk normalization retained. It does not identify a contributing global period or the absolute action with the link volume. Equation (16) controls the actual generic q-Hahn NUMERATORS. A full generic exceptional-kernel continuation still has its original boundary factors; it is not proved merely by replacing q in the root entire formula. Nor is this a joint complex-degree theorem. Finally, each real integer forbidden separation h>a gives an IDENTICALLY ZERO original physical operator slice, including every generic-q normal. Deforming only its magnetic finite sums cannot turn that zero slice into a nonzero original period. A local geometric contribution in such a representation must cancel or fail selection there. Actual transport of the degree period, or another source-preserving grouping, remains necessary for a global nonzero contribution. No general long-twist volume theorem is inferred from this local chart result. Focused audit: [original generic factorization, actual finite shifts and selected complex packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_deficient_degree_packet.py). The selected geometric branch is distinct from the identically zero physical slice. Numerical rate tests check normalization; the uniform estimates are proved above.

title: Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial
text: # Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial 30 October 2026. The positive coefficients of the actual magnetic polynomial are log-concave. Consequently a positive-radius evaluation recovers each coefficient within a factor at most j+1. The selected ordinary source action then gives a uniform coefficient rate, with an explicit optimal radius, throughout the interior coefficient-slope domain. This theorem keeps the source's physical total and integer channel. It neither deletes the Fourier phases when coefficients are sewn nor proves cancellation control for the original graph contraction. ## 1. The original polynomial and its positive coefficients Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and retain the ACTUAL complete range 0<=j<=floor(d/2), d-j<=t<=d. The proved magnetic factorization is fhat(u)=q^(du) Q^(-ju) G_t(Q^u), G_t(q^t z)=c_t P_(N,t,j)(z), c_t=q^[j(t+j-d)]/(Q;Q)_j, P(z)=B_h(z) A_n(z)=sum_(k=0)^j p_k z^k, h=d-t, n=t+j-d, h+n=j. (1) Here B_h has the positive coefficients beta(h,k)=s_h/(s_k s_(h-k)), where s_r=product_(a=1)^r 2sin(pi a/N). The actual residual A_n has positive leading coefficient and n negative real roots. These are properties of the original coproduct polynomial, proved in [the magnetic corridor theorem](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md), not a replacement of its values by an interpolating polynomial. In particular p_k>0 for every 0<=k<=j. The source condition t+j>=d is essential here. Although its ordinary analytic continuation has a larger domain, positivity of this factorization is not asserted for arbitrary nonphysical t or for limiting tau+xi<1. ## 2. Log-concavity and an exact polynomial-loss duality The coefficient sequence p_0,...,p_j is log-concave: p_k^2>=p_(k-1)p_(k+1), 1<=k<j. (2) An elementary proof is enough. The consecutive ratio of B_h is beta(h,k)/beta(h,k-1) =sin((h-k+1)pi/N)/sin(k pi/N). Its decrease follows by cross multiplication: the difference of the two adjacent numerators is sin(pi/N)sin((h+1)pi/N)>0. The h=0 sequence consists of one coefficient and is included. Now let a_k be any nonnegative log-concave sequence with interval support, extended by zero elsewhere. Multiplication of its polynomial by z+rho, rho>0, gives b_k=rho a_k+a_(k-1), and b_k^2-b_(k-1)b_(k+1) =rho^2(a_k^2-a_(k-1)a_(k+1)) +rho(a_k a_(k-1)-a_(k-2)a_(k+1)) +(a_(k-1)^2-a_(k-2)a_k)>=0. (3) The middle term is nonnegative by the decreasing consecutive ratios; zero endpoints cause no problem. Factoring A_n into its positive linear factors and iterating (3) proves (2). For EVERY k=0,...,j the exact finite statement is p_k <= inf_(w>0) P(w) w^(-k) <= (j+1)p_k. (4) The first inequality holds because p_k w^k is one positive summand. For an interior k choose p_(k-1)/p_k <= w <= p_k/p_(k+1). This interval is nonempty by (2). At such a tilt, the kth term is a mode of the entire sequence p_l w^l, again by decreasing ratios. Its sum is at most j+1 times that term, proving the upper inequality. For k=0 and k=j, take w to zero and infinity respectively; the infimum equals the endpoint coefficient. For j=0 all statements are identities. Thus (4) is a two-sided estimate for actual coefficients, with no unknown exponentially small cancellation or probability prefactor. It is not an asymptotic Gaussian coefficient formula. ## 3. The correct radial free energy and its explicit derivative Set tau=t/N, xi=j/N and w=exp(y), y real. Because the polynomial coordinate in (1) is z=Q^u/q^t, the corresponding magnetic variable is nu=u/N=tau/2-i y/(2pi). (5) The reciprocal determinant coordinate is 1/w, not w. Taking absolute values in the EXACT source normalization (1) gives log P(exp y)=log s_j-(d-2j)y/2+log|fhat(N nu)|. (6) Use the actual selected action Phi_xi from [the full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). For complete physical indices with tau in a fixed compact subinterval of (1/2,1), xi bounded away from zero, and y in a fixed finite interval, N^(-1)log P(exp y)=F(tau,xi;y)+O(log N/N), F=J(xi)-(1/2-xi)y +Re Phi_xi(tau,tau/2-i y/(2pi)). (7) The scaled parameters in (7) are their ACTUAL values at level N. The possible complete boundary displacement tau+xi=1-1/N is retained; its limiting parameters satisfy tau+xi>=1. The packet and the factorial estimate are uniform for these indices. The derivative in y of the error in (7) is O(1/N) on smaller compact intervals. The log s_j term is independent of y and has not been dropped. There is an explicit derivative requiring no new saddle selection. Put c=-cos(pi tau)>0, C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi)>0, B=w^2+2cw+C^2. On (5) the selected multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i sqrt(B))^2/(1+2cw+w^2), Arg Y=2 arctan(sqrt(B)/s) in (0,pi). (8) It has modulus one, and the square root is positive real. This is the already calibrated ordinary branch on this central vertical line. Differentiating (7), with its MINUS sign in (5), yields F_y=xi-1/2+pi^(-1) arctan(sqrt(B)/s), F_yy=s w(w+c)/[pi sqrt(B)(1+2cw+w^2)]>0. (9) As y tends to minus or plus infinity, F_y tends respectively to 0 and xi, including the folded endpoint C=0. Every interior slope 0<lambda<xi therefore has a unique finite optimal tilt. It is explicitly a=pi(1/2-xi+lambda), w_*=sqrt(c^2-C^2+s^2 tan(a)^2)-c>0, y_*=log w_*. (10) The quantity s tan(a) is strictly greater than C for lambda>0, which proves positivity of this root. Formula (10) also gives uniform finite tilt bounds on compact interior slope families. Equivalently, the selected magnetic momentum at that coefficient is Y_*=exp[2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi)], Log Y_*=2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi) in i(0,pi). (10a) Thus the Fourier index prescribes the FULL local phase on this selected radial saddle, not only the modulus of a multiplier. Its radial boundary variable is the positive root (10), equivalently w_*^2+2cw_*+C^2=s^2 tan^2(pi(1/2-xi+lambda)). Actual network orientation and incidence are still needed to combine these local characters into global equations. ## 4. Uniform actual coefficient rates Take any compact family of limiting complete parameters with 1/2<tau<1, 0<xi<=1/2 and tau+xi>=1. Keep the coefficient slope lambda strictly inside (0,xi), uniformly on that family. For all legal integer sequences N,t,j,k approaching this family, use the actual scaled values tau_N=t/N, xi_N=j/N, lambda_N=k/N. Define L(tau,xi,lambda) =F(tau,xi;y_*)-lambda y_*, (11) where (10) fixes the unique positive tilt. Then log p_k=N L(tau_N,xi_N,lambda_N)+O(log N), (12) uniformly over that family and both level parities. The value in (11) is also the infimum over all real y of F-lambda y. Its slope derivatives obey L_lambda=-y_*, L_(lambda lambda)=-1/F_yy(y_*)<0. (13) For completeness, no unbounded minimizer is hidden in (12). The finite function F_N(y)=N^(-1)log P(exp y) is convex, and its derivative is the tilted mean of k/N. Choose fixed endpoints y_-<y_+ beyond the compact set of optimal tilts (10). By (9) there is a uniform strict gap between F_y(y_-) and the target slopes, and between those slopes and F_y(y_+). The derivative convergence in (7) puts every finite minimizer of F_N-lambda_N y in [y_-,y_+] for large N. The uniform value estimate (7), followed by (4), proves (12). Boundary slopes k/N approaching zero or xi, unbounded tilts, and physical degree endpoints tau=1/2 or tau=1 are outside this uniform statement. Their exact finite inequality (4) remains valid; a rate or relative amplitude at those boundaries needs its own estimates. No relative coefficient amplitude is claimed even in the interior. ## 5. What this supplies for a sewn source Each original coefficient has now an actual positive radial variational description, retaining its normalizer and its Fourier index. This permits the index k to remain a shared variable in an exact affine wire/cycle compiler. If a positive comparison partition is assembled from these coefficients, their actions must first be summed on that shared incidence set before taking any maximum. The original magnetic source is reconstructed with its displayed Fourier factors and scalar c_t. A positive coefficient theorem does not erase those phases, identify a graph contraction with the product of coefficient envelopes, or prove a nonzero geometric overlap. Those are separate requirements for the full volume conjecture. Focused audit: [original positive coefficients and radial duality](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.py). Three formal identities check the log-concavity step, curvature and inverse tilt. At 90 digits, 794 actual positive polynomials satisfy 3,938 log-concavity and tilted-mode checks; nine literal off-lattice source values check the radial sign and normalization. Eighteen interior coefficient sequences check the stated rate and tilt gradient. The uniform theorem is proved above, not inferred from those sequences. The variational theorem concerns discrete channels and interior slopes. Positive coefficients are distinct from a coherently sewn graph source.

title: The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube
status: Selected full physical complex amplitude; finite correction
text: # The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube 30 October 2026. A second exact Hermitian realization of the original q-Hahn determinant puts its zeros in a sharp angular cone. It extends the ordinary joint action and nonzero relative amplitude from the central wedge to the FULL strict physical tube. Both magnetic coordinates vary complexly; the channel remains an actual integer. The finite source has a small upper-boundary correction, which is necessary: an explicit one-channel counterexample is given below. Every fixed compact in the full physical tube is covered for all sufficiently large N. No contributing global cycle or coherent whole-source estimate is asserted. ## 1. Exact source and a second determinant Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1 and 1<=j<=floor(d/2). Write t=N tau, u=N nu, xi=j/N, z=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], gamma=pi(tau+1/N). The original joint source is exactly fhat_j(u,t-u)=x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(z;-cos gamma)/Delta_j(Q^t), x=q^d, Delta_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). (1) All powers and scalar factors are those of [the original joint amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md). Let b_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. The exact monic recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z+c/cos(theta), R_(n+1)=[z+c/(cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta))]R_n +b_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]R_(n-1). (2) Define j-by-j real matrices A and K, indexed by 0,...,j-1: A_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], A_(n-1,n)=A_(n,n-1)=sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta), K_(n-1,n)=sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n-1)=-sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n)=0. Then the SAME polynomial has the second exact determinant R_j(z;-cos gamma)=det[zI-cos(gamma)A-sin(gamma)K]. (3) Indeed the upper and lower adjacent entries of J_gamma=cos(gamma)A+sin(gamma)K are sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta+gamma) and sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta-gamma). Their product is b_n[cos^2(gamma)-cos^2(n theta)], so the continuant of zI-J_gamma is exactly (2). The two Hermitian matrices H_+=A+iK, H_-=A-iK (4) are POSITIVE DEFINITE. Their adjacent entries have modulus sqrt(b_n) and their diagonal equals that of the proved positive matrix D in [the first determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). A diagonal unitary phase gauge makes each of these tridiagonal offdiagonals positive real. Thus each H_+ and H_- is unitarily equivalent to D, including the maximal channel. Consequently J_gamma=(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. (5) This is a source-exact matrix identity, not an asymptotic model. ## 2. A sharp finite angular exclusion, and its necessary correction For any eigenvector v of J_gamma with norm one, its eigenvalue is zeta=(h_-/2)e^(i gamma)+(h_+/2)e^(-i gamma), h_-=v*H_-v>0, h_+=v*H_+v>0. (6) If pi/2<Re gamma<3pi/2, these two rays bound a left angular cone. Put a_gamma=min(Re gamma,2pi-Re gamma). Every nonzero eigenvalue satisfies |Arg zeta|>=a_gamma; the inequality is strict when the two boundary rays are distinct. When Re gamma=pi all eigenvalues are strictly negative real. Positive coefficients in (6) also exclude a zero eigenvalue in this range. Define the full physical tube P={ (tau,nu) in C^2: 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }, and its finite-level subdomain P_N={ (tau,nu) in P: Re tau<1-1/(2N) }. (7) For a physical point the principal argument of z in (1) is exactly pi(Re tau-2Re nu), with absolute value <pi Re tau. On P_N, a_gamma>pi Re tau. Therefore (3) is nonzero there. The factors Delta_j(Q^t) are also nonzero: their zeros require tau=r/N modulo an integer, 0<=r<j<N/2. All remaining factors in (1) are nonzero. Thus the original finite source is holomorphic and nowhere zero on P_N. The case j=0 is its explicit nonzero exponential. The correction in (7) cannot simply be deleted for every finite N. Already j=1 has its zero at z_N=cos[pi(tau+1/N)]/cos(pi/N). Take tau_N=1-1/(4N)+i and delta=3pi/(4N). Then z_N=[-cos(delta)cosh(pi)+i sin(delta)sinh(pi)]/cos(pi/N), Arg z_N=pi-arctan[tan(delta)tanh(pi)] <pi Re tau_N. (8) For the strict inequality, set a=pi/(4N): tan(a)/tan(3a)<1/3<tanh(pi), valid for N>=3. Define nu_N=[tau_N-Log(z_N)/(pi i)]/2 with the principal logarithm. It satisfies 0<Re nu_N<Re tau_N, but (1) vanishes. The denominator is nonzero. This is an exact finite-source counterexample on P. These points approach the boundary of P as N grows and therefore do not obstruct the fixed-compact theorem below. ## 3. Uniform inverse and logarithmic bounds on full physical compacts Fix a compact K0 contained in P. For all large N, K0 lies in P_N and gamma has real part between pi/2 and pi. Put M=zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. The three coefficients z, -e^(i gamma), -e^(-i gamma) lie in one open half-plane through zero. To see this, write a=Re gamma and psi=Arg z. The latter satisfies |psi|<a. The other two arguments are pi-a and -(pi-a). Their angular span together with psi is strictly less than pi. On a fixed physical compact the span stays uniformly below pi, because Re nu and Re(tau-nu) are bounded below and Re tau stays away from 1/2 and 1. Their moduli also have positive lower and finite upper bounds on K0. Rotate the half-plane by a phase beta. Locally, and uniformly on a finite cover of K0, this gives Re(e^(-i beta)M)>=delta I+eta_- H_-+eta_+ H_+, delta,eta_-,eta_+>=c_(K0)>0. (9) Hence ||M^(-1)||<=C_(K0). Conjugating M by H_+^(-1/2), or by H_-^(-1/2), also gives |tr(M^(-1)H_+)|+|tr(M^(-1)H_-)|<=C_(K0)j. Since partial_z M=I and partial_gamma M=-(i/2)e^(i gamma)H_-+(i/2)e^(-i gamma)H_+, both logarithmic derivatives of R_j with respect to z and gamma are O_(K0)(j). No lower eigenvalue bound for D, H_+ or H_- is used. The result is uniform through the folded channel. The scalar factors in (1) have the same explicit O(N) logarithmic derivative bounds as before. Thus the first derivatives of N^(-1)Log fhat_j are uniformly bounded on full physical compacts. Choose its scalar holomorphic logarithm on the convex P_N by continuation from its already fixed central value. The exact real center phase remains Im Log fhat_j(t/2,t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (10) The principal matrix logarithm of the old central realization is not being asserted outside its domain. A central anchor bounds the continued normalized scalar logarithm, and Cauchy estimates give all its fixed derivatives on smaller physical compacts. The normal-family argument now extends the ACTUAL selected leading action throughout P. Any subsequential limit agrees on the central open subset with the already proved Phi_xi, and hence everywhere by the holomorphic identity theorem. This gives local uniform convergence with all derivatives, uniformly for xi=j/N in compact real subintervals of (0,1/2], always using its actual value. ## 4. The characteristic is simple on the entire tube Set gamma0=pi tau, s=sin(pi xi), C=cos(pi xi), and W=1-2cos(gamma0)z+C^2 z^2, V=1-2cos(gamma0)z+z^2. (11) Both are nonzero on P. This has a two-dimensional positive-cone proof which includes C=0. Let u=(1,0)^T, v=(s,C)^T and B_gamma0=e^(i gamma0)u u*+e^(-i gamma0)v v*. Its trace is 2cos(gamma0), its determinant is C^2, and det(I-z B_gamma0)=W. Every nonzero eigenvalue is a NONNEGATIVE combination of the same two left-cone rays, with at least one positive coefficient. It therefore lies in the closed cone |Arg lambda|>=pi Re tau. Reciprocation preserves that cone, so its reciprocal cannot be the physical z, whose argument has smaller absolute value. This proves the assertion for W. Taking s=0,C=1 proves it for V. The full source characteristic from the exact Casimir shift is H=A(Y+Y^(-1))+D-(J+J^(-1))=0, A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, U=e^(2pi i nu), T=e^(2pi i tau), J=e^(2pi i xi). Here A!=0 on P, and xi is bounded away from zero. Its two solutions are Y_+=(s z+i sqrt(W))^2/V, Y_-=(s z-i sqrt(W))^2/V. (12) The square root is the holomorphic continuation from the selected central branch on the simply connected P. It is NOT necessarily the pointwise principal square root outside the central wedge. The numerators in (12) are nonzero because W+s^2 z^2=V. The two roots are distinct because s,z,W,V are nonzero. Thus H_a!=0 for a=Log Y on the selected sheet throughout P, including xi=1/2. The second source characteristic remains simple in Phi_tau: its derivative is (1-T)exp(Phi_tau), which is nonzero. The leading action in section 3 already supplies this actual holomorphic logarithm, rather than selecting a new solution of that equation. ## 5. The actual nonzero amplitude, with its original normalization The two finite source shifts (11),(12) of [the original joint amplitude proof](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) are rational identities for the SAME finite function (1). They therefore hold on the enlarged domain. The proof's two derivative bootstraps now apply on full physical compacts: the preceding section supplies uniform characteristic simplicity, and section 3 supplies uniform Cauchy bounds on slightly larger compacts. Explicitly let G_N=N^(-1)Log fhat, a=Phi_nu and b=Phi_tau. The exact Casimir shift first gives partial_nu G_N-a=O(N^(-1)); Cauchy's formula gives the same bound for its derivatives. A second substitution gives partial_nu G_N=a+N^(-1)r+O(N^(-2)). The exact coproduct shift then gives, by the same two substitutions, partial_tau G_N=b+N^(-1)s1+O(N^(-2)). (13) Here r and s1 are EXACTLY the coefficients (16),(17) in that proof, with its original integer offsets and actual xi=j/N. Their formulas are holomorphic on P by the simplicity just proved. The errors and their fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller compacts. The one-form s1 d tau+r d nu is closed: equate the mixed derivatives of the actual G_N in (13), use Cauchy bounds on the remainders, and pass to admissible xi sequences. The coefficient functions depend locally analytically on xi by the simple characteristic and their already normalized central values. Thus closedness holds at every real xi in the stated interval, including its folded end. On the simply connected P this form defines a nonzero holomorphic B_xi, normalized by the ALREADY PROVED central real-lattice amplitude. Integrating (13) from a nearby genuine central sample along compact paths gives fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(N^(-1))) (14) on every compact subset of P. Fixed derivatives of the relative error have the same bound on smaller compacts. At the initial sample Log fhat-N Phi+(1/2)log N-Log B is O(N^(-1)), and its gradient has that same bound by (13). Thus no additive phase, sample character, or normalization constant is introduced during continuation. In the original overlap B is the exact coefficient Acal(w_*)exp[pi i(alpha(w_*)-nu)] from the central proof. Both level parities, arbitrary fixed complex magnetic displacements, and the discrete folded limit are included. ## 6. The generic-normal bounds use the same enlarged corridor The proved small-channel generic-normal and near-fold paired-normal bounds also extend to any fixed compact K0 in P. There is one necessary change in their matrix perturbation argument. Use M in (9) as the root tridiagonal realization. For each adjacent pair, freeze whichever of its two root entries has larger modulus, and set the opposite generic entry so their product is -beta_n(q) in the original generic recurrence. One must not always freeze the upper entry: sin(gamma+n theta) can vanish at an integer degree. The chosen entry is uniformly bounded below because sqrt(b_n)>=1/2 and |sin(gamma+n theta)|^2+|sin(gamma-n theta)|^2 =2|sin gamma|^2 cos^2(n theta) +2|cos gamma|^2 sin^2(n theta). On fixed physical compacts, for all large N, both |sin gamma| and |cos gamma| are bounded below. Therefore the larger adjacent entry has a positive uniform lower bound. The diagonal is unchanged. The old generic coefficient bounds give ||M(q)-M(q0)||=O(N^7|epsilon|), and (9) supplies the bounded root inverse. All scalar factors and their derivatives retain their former estimates. It follows that the original small-channel N^8 fixed-jet bound holds on K0. Its last inverse cofactor still equals R_(j-1)/R_j, so the EXACT large-channel recurrence and scalar argument of [the near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) give the same paired bound |w_(j,l)/C_j|<=C_(K0)N^8(C_(K0)N^16)^(l-j) (15) when l-j<=eta_(K0)N. Thus its subexponential consequence for (l-j)log N=o(N) holds on the full strict physical tube's fixed compacts as well. The fixed positive scaled-channel limitation and the distinction between an upper bound and an amplitude remain unchanged. ## 7. Scope The ordinary local packet now covers the full strict physical domain, and its selected sheet is continued from the original central source. Membership in that physical domain, matching the geometric sheet, choosing a contributing original cycle, and controlling the coherent contraction remain separate global tasks. The finite boundary example (8) explains why the theorem is stated on fixed compacts for sufficiently large N rather than by deleting the exact finite correction everywhere. Focused audit: [cone, literal source and full physical amplitudes](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet_results.json). The three formal cone identities and 242 exact actual-source determinants passed. Six explicit finite-boundary counterexamples were checked.
