Eight original generic adapters passed, including four cases with a genuinely vanishing upper root entry. At 180 digits, 16 independent terminating-source comparisons and 16 amplitude calibrations strictly OUTSIDE the central wedge passed; 16 actual subprincipal gradient corrections also passed. The largest N-scaled relative amplitude error was 1.184 and the largest N-squared gradient remainder was 16.406. These are normalization regressions; the cone and two-shift argument give the uniform result. The theorem has fixed-compact, discrete-channel scope. It does not identify a global contributing cycle or give a coherent source estimate. The finite-boundary caveat remains essential, including for the larger-entry generic adapter.

title: The actual generic white numerator at the resonant hard edge
status: Genuine quantum normals through the boundary hypergeometric parameter
text: # The actual generic white numerator at the resonant hard edge 30 October 2026. source theorem. A genuine quantum deformation of the original white numerator has a uniform boundary packet. Its root limit is a Bessel function, while its retained quantum normals differentiate the ORDER parameter of a confluent hypergeometric function. The exact large monomial normalization stays in the answer. No zero of the limiting function, cup divisor, or global selected cycle is removed. ## 1. The original generic polynomial and its exact reindexing Use the ACTUAL polynomial H_m^B(U,V) in the [generic white-source theorem](actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md), not a small root-colliding replacement for the large white channel. Write Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), and H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m c_k V^k product_(r<k)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-k)(V-Q^r), c_k=(-1)^k B^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q (BQ^(m-k+1);Q)_k/(BQ;Q)_k. (1) In particular c_m=(-B)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2], EXACTLY. Divide by the actual k=m term Z_m=c_m(UV)^m product_(r=0)^(m-1)(1-Q^r/U). (2) Setting k=m-l gives the identity H_m^B/Z_m=sum_(l=0)^m T_l, T_0=1, T_l=(-1)^l B^(-l)Q^[-ml+l(l-1)/2] [m choose l]_Q (BQ^(m-l+1);Q)_l/(BQ;Q)_l (UV)^(-l) product_(r<l)(V-Q^r) /product_(r=m-l)^(m-1)(1-Q^r/U). (3) This is a termwise identity of the original generic source. The additional Pochhammer ratio in (3) is essential: replacing it by another Gaussian binomial before differentiating would erase the normal proved below. To verify the ratio directly, cancel (BQ^(l+1);Q)_(m-l)=(BQ;Q)_m/(BQ;Q)_l in c_(m-l)/c_m. ## 2. A joint boundary packet with the actual moving parameter Fix delta>0, and suppose m=m_N is an integer with delta<=mu_N=m/N<=1-delta. At the original root q0=exp(pi i/N), choose marked, possibly complex head lifts x_N,y_N such that U_N(0)=q0^(2x_N)=N^2 kappa_N, V_N(0)=q0^(2y_N)=V_N^0, |x_N|+|y_N|<=C N(1+log N). (4) The kappa_N and V_N^0 range over fixed compact subsets of C minus zero. Their logarithms are the specified head marks, not reset principal values. Set epsilon=t/N^2, q_N(t)=exp(pi i/N+t/N^2), Q_N=q_N^2, B_N=Q_N^(-N), U_N(t)=exp[2x_N Log q_N(t)], V_N(t)=exp[2y_N Log q_N(t)]. (5) All integers N,m and all marked head lifts stay fixed under this quantum deformation. Define K_N=sin^2(pi mu_N)(V_N^0-1)/(pi^2 kappa_N V_N^0), b(t)=1-t/(pi i), F(t;K)=sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l/[l! (b(t))_l]. (6) The last line DEFINES the function customarily written 0F1(;b(t);-K); no hypergeometric transformation is imported. On any fixed |t|<=rho<pi, the actual normalized source satisfies H_m^(B_N(t))(U_N(t),V_N(t))/Z_m(t) =F(t;K_N)+O((1+log N)/N), (7) uniformly in all the displayed compact parameters. At t=0 this is sum (-K_N)^l/(l!)^2=J_0(2sqrt(K_N)), interpreted by its entire series so that no square-root choice is necessary. The root specialization is the same actual boundary model as in [the resonant root hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). The result is holomorphic in t on a larger disk of the same type. Consequently, for every fixed j and a smaller disk, N^(-2j) partial_epsilon^j[H_m^B(U,V)/Z_m]|_0 =partial_t^j F(t;K_N)|_0+O((1+log N)/N). (8) These are GENUINE generic-q normals of the specified source at fixed marked heads. They are not derivatives of its root Bessel formula. Across zeros of F the estimates are absolute in the normalization (2). Relative estimates require a compact avoiding the relevant zeros. For example, with H_l=sum_(r=1)^l 1/r and H_l^(2)=sum_(r=1)^l 1/r^2, the first two retained limits are partial_t F(0;K)=(pi i)^(-1) sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l H_l/(l!)^2, partial_t^2 F(0;K)=(pi i)^(-2) sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l[H_l^2+H_l^(2)]/(l!)^2. (8a) They follow by differentiating the actual denominator in (6), and are generally nonzero even though the root Bessel formula alone has no moving-q parameter. ## 3. Proof: fixed terms, uniform domination and the error For each fixed l and r, the actual small denominator factors are 1-Q_N^r=(-2pi i/N)r(1+O(N^-1)), 1-B_N Q_N^r=(-2pi i/N)[r-t/(pi i)](1+O(N^-1)). (9) The second line follows from B_N Q_N^r=exp[(2pi i r-2t)/N+2rt/N^2]. This fixes the sign of b(t). The first limiting singular parameter is t=pi i, corresponding to the nearby moving period N-1. Our disks stay strictly away from it. The two numerator products in (3) each tend to (1-exp(2pi i mu_N))^l. Combining their phase with (-1)^l Q_N^(-ml) and the two factors (-2pi i/N)^l gives (-N^2 sin^2(pi mu_N)/pi^2)^l. Moreover U_N(t)/U_N(0) and V_N(t)/V_N(0) are 1+O((1+log N)/N), and the last denominator product in (3) tends to one. Thus the lth term tends to (-K_N)^l/[l!(1-t/(pi i))_l], (10) with the ACTUAL generic denominator rather than a squared factorial. Here is a uniform summable bound, including large l. On a slightly larger fixed t disk with radius less than pi, for all 1<=r<=m, |1-Q_N^r|>=c_delta r/N, |1-B_N Q_N^r|>=c_(delta,rho) r/N. (11) For r bounded, (9) and |r-t/(pi i)|>=r(1-rho/pi) prove the second estimate. For larger r it follows from the root sine bound and its O(N^-1) perturbation; dividing at a sufficiently large fixed r makes this comparison uniform. All numerator factors are bounded by a constant. The powers of B,Q in (3) have bounded modulus (or may be absorbed in C^l). Since |U_N(t)|>=c N^2 and |V_N(t)|>=c, the two binomial-type factors and (UV)^(-l) cancel their N^(2l) costs. Finally product_(r=m-l)^(m-1)|1-Q_N^r/U_N(t)|^(-1)<=exp(C/N). It follows that |T_l|<=C^l/(l!)^2, uniformly for 0<=l<=m. The limiting terms satisfy the same type of bound. This proves normal-family convergence by the actual finite series, not by matching a formal solution of a differential equation. The error in (7) can also be quantified directly. For l<=cN, with c chosen below delta/2, compare each product in (3) with (10). The numerator phases and the two denominator products have relative logarithmic error O(l^2/N), and the retained moving heads add O(l(1+log N)/N). Apply |exp(w)-1|<=|w|exp(|w|), and absorb exp(C l^2/N)<=exp(C' l) into the preceding factorial majorant. Summing gives O((1+log N)/N). This comparison is made factorwise for product_(r<l)(V-Q^r), without dividing by V_N^0-1; it is therefore uniform when K_N=0 as well. A telescoping product difference gives the same bound there. For l>cN both factorial tails are smaller than every inverse power of N. This proves (7), uniformly on the larger t disk. Cauchy's formula then proves (8) and all fixed t derivatives of the error. ## 4. The exact normalization is not a harmless constant Equation (2) is kept at the moving parameter. In particular it contains U_N(t)^m even though U_N(t)/U_N(0) tends to one. For standard fixed marks Log U_N(0)=2log N+Log kappa_N, U_N(t)^m/U_N(0)^m =exp[mu_N t Log U_N(0)/(pi i)] =N^[2mu_N t/(pi i)] exp[mu_N t Log kappa_N/(pi i)]. (12) Other retained head carries give their actual additional factors; they are not removed from (2). The exact top coefficient contributes c_m(t)/c_m(0)=exp[t(-2Nm+m(m+1))/N^2]. (13) The remaining product in (2) is nonzero on the stated disks. Its logarithmic t derivatives are uniformly bounded with the same marked heads. Equations (12),(13), V_N(t)^m and that product give the original unnormalized jets by ordinary Leibniz. In particular they are not obtained by simply differentiating J_0 at fixed K. On any compact where F(0;K_N) stays away from zero, (7),(8) give a nonzero local root packet and relative fixed-normal bounds. If the limiting Bessel factor vanishes, the normalized series and its true parameter derivatives are still covered, but no nonzero leading amplitude is asserted. The theorem concerns the actual white numerator; all scalar, cup and marked contraction factors must still be restored before discussing an operator or its original finite period. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge_results.json) check 20 symbolic reindexed coefficients, 54 nonroot and 54 root original-H four-jet identities with 432 coefficients, 48 complex scaled-parameter packets, 24 genuine scaled first/second normals, 12 independent terminating source values, six retained top-term normalizations and both harmonic normal formulas. Finite convergence errors are recorded as diagnostics, separately from the uniform proof. The result is restricted to the specified white numerator and its normalization, with limiting zeros retained; it is not a full-operator or selected-period theorem.

title: The physical selected Fourier action has a global Legendre chart
text: # The physical selected Fourier action has a global Legendre chart 30 October 2026. The local action change of [holomorphic Legendre transport](actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.md) is globally one-to-one on the full physical tube. This removes a possible multiple-chart ambiguity for the selected classical action. It does not provide analytic continuation of individual finite Fourier coefficients. ## 1. Statement Fix 0<xi<=1/2 and the original marked selected action Phi_xi. Retain all the source constants and logarithmic characters in the local theorem. Write P={1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau}, y=2pi i(nu-tau/2), F=J(xi)+(xi-1/2)y+Phi_xi(tau,nu) -i pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2, lambda=F_y=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i). (1) Let O be the image of P in (tau,y). Then (tau,y) -> (tau,lambda) (2) is a biholomorphism from O onto its open image D_xi. In particular the selected Legendre action F-lambda y is a SINGLE holomorphic function on D_xi, with its original additive phase fixed by (1). The image D_xi is not asserted convex, a product, or the whole complex coefficient plane. ## 2. A source-selected square root is injective on each physical fiber Fix tau. Put a=pi Re tau in (pi/2,pi), w=exp(y), c=-cos(pi tau), C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi), B(w)=w^2+2cw+C^2, V(w)=w^2+2cw+1. The physical w-domain is exactly the sector S_tau={w!=0: |Arg w|<a}. (3) The marked y-strip has imaginary width 2a<2pi, so exp maps that strip bijectively onto (3). The full physical packet proves B and V nonzero there. Therefore both roots alpha,beta of B belong to the complementary closed cone K_tau={0} union {w!=0: |Arg(-w)|<=pi-a}. This cone is convex: its angle is 2(pi-a)<pi. The whole segment [alpha,beta] consequently misses S_tau. This conclusion also covers xi=1/2, when one root is zero. For distinct roots, the function r(w)=(w-alpha) sqrt((w-beta)/(w-alpha)) (4) is holomorphic on C minus [alpha,beta], using the principal square root in the displayed ratio. Indeed that ratio is a nonpositive real number precisely on the removed segment. It satisfies r(w)^2=B(w), r(w)=w+c+O(1/w) at infinity. (5) The reflection R(w)=alpha+beta-w=-2c-w preserves the slit domain and B. Thus r(R(w))/r(w) is a constant sign on its connected domain. The asymptotic condition (5) fixes that sign to be minus: r(-2c-w)=-r(w). (6) If r(w_1)=r(w_2), the equation B(w_1)=B(w_2) gives either w_1=w_2 or w_2=-2c-w_1. The second alternative, by (6), would force r(w_1)=0, impossible off the slit. Hence r is injective on the slit complement, and in particular on S_tau. If alpha=beta, the normalized root is simply r(w)=w+c and the same conclusion is immediate. The root in (4) is the ACTUAL selected source root. For real tau and positive w it is the positive square root used to calibrate the source. For any compact path in the allowed tau strip, a sufficiently large positive w makes B(w)/w^2 uniformly close to one. Its continuation remains the root with (5), so the same calibration holds at the end of the path. Equality then extends through the connected physical w-sector. No pointwise principal square root of B is substituted for this continued root. ## 3. The selected momentum and action are globally single-chart The actual selected source multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i r)^2/V=(s+i r)/(s-i r). (7) The last equality uses V=s^2+B. Its two factors do not vanish on the physical domain because V is nonzero. Since s>0, the last expression is an injective Möbius function of r. Equations (6),(7) prove that Y is injective on each physical w-sector. If two marked lambda values in (1) agree, their exponentials Y agree. They therefore have the same w, and the marked strip then gives the same y. The map (2) is thus globally injective. Its Jacobian F_yy is everywhere nonzero by the local theorem. The holomorphic inverse theorem supplies local holomorphic inverses; injectivity makes them agree on overlaps. This proves the stated biholomorphism onto D_xi and the single-valued Legendre action. This is a global coordinate result for the ALREADY selected ordinary action. It does not choose a different source sheet, complexify the actual integer channel, or turn the coefficient label into an available complex finite-source variable. The real integer coefficient rate, exceptional block, partner normals and global period questions keep the scopes of their separate theorems. Focused audit: [reflection and momentum injectivity identities](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_global_fourier_legendre_chart.py). The chart is a global inverse onto its open image. It does not define finite complex-index coefficients or identify a contributing global-source cycle.

title: The selected Fourier action has a nonsingular holomorphic Legendre chart
text: # The selected Fourier action has a nonsingular holomorphic Legendre chart 30 October 2026. The actual selected ordinary q-Hahn action admits a local holomorphic Legendre change at EVERY point of the full strict physical tube. Restoring the exact coefficient phase recovers the original magnetic coordinate and action. This is a theorem about the selected classical action. It does not continue a finite coefficient index away from its integer lattice or prove a source integration-cycle statement. ## 1. The actual source fixes the additive phase Fix a real channel parameter 0<xi<=1/2. Use the selected holomorphic action Phi_xi(tau,nu) of the [full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md), on P={1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau}. The actual finite channel remains an integer j, with j/N tending to xi. No complex finite-channel interpretation is made here. Put y=2pi i(nu-tau/2), w=exp(y), C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi), c=-cos(pi tau). The image O of P in (tau,y) coordinates is convex. On a real radial slice, tau and y are real, and the source polynomial P_(t,j)(w) is positive when its actual complete support t+j>=d is imposed. The finite source identity, including its scalar, is fhat_j(N nu)=q^[(d-2j)N nu] c_(t,j) P_(t,j)(exp y), c_(t,j)=q^[j(t+j-d)]/(Q;Q)_j, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1. (1) Use the original product logarithm (Q;Q)_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2] s_j, s_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N). At nu=t/(2N)-iy/(2pi), with real y, the exact argument supplied by the prefactors of (1) is pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N), (2) independent of y. This is a marked product logarithm, not a principal argument chosen anew after reducing (2) modulo 2pi. Dividing its logarithm by N yields the absolute phase C_0(tau,xi)=i pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2. (3) Consequently define on O F_xi(tau,y)=J(xi)+(xi-1/2)y +Phi_xi(tau,tau/2-iy/(2pi))-C_0(tau,xi). (4) On the real complete radial slice this is precisely the REAL positive-polynomial action in the [coefficient variational theorem](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md). The constant and linear terms in (4) are fixed by (1), not by an arbitrary integration constant. Formula (4) also defines its holomorphic continuation in tau and y. Throughout this note xi is a fixed real parameter. ## 2. The Legendre derivative has no critical point on O Write B=w^2+2cw+C^2, V=w^2+2cw+1. The selected square root of B is continued from its positive value on the real radial slice. The full packet proves B and V nonzero: they are w^2 times its two nonzero characteristic factors. Since O is convex, the selected square root is globally defined there. The selected source multiplier has the exact expression Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i sqrt(B))^2/V. (5) This retains the continued root. It does not assert that sqrt(B) is pointwise principal outside the real slice. Differentiating (4),(5) on that slice and continuing the identity gives F_y=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i), F_yy=s w(w+c)/(pi sqrt(B) V). (6) The only possible new zero in the second line is w+c=0. It is AUTOMATICALLY excluded by the strict physical domain. Indeed put T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i nu). Then w+c=0 is equivalent to U=(1+T)/2. The principal argument of T is theta=2pi(Re tau-1), strictly between -pi and 0. The argument of the positive sum 1+T lies strictly between theta and 0, for every |T|>0. But an allowed physical U has its argument lift in (0,2pi Re tau); its principal argument is either in (0,pi] or in (-pi,theta). It cannot equal that of (1+T)/2. Because s>0, w!=0, B!=0 and V!=0, equation (6) proves F_yy never vanishes on O. (7) This includes the endpoint xi=1/2. The real radial curvature is positive, but the proof of (7) uses the full complex physical domain, not positivity of a complex Hessian. ## 3. Local action transport with its exact phase Let lambda=F_y. By (7), (tau,y)->(tau,lambda) is locally biholomorphic at EVERY point of O. In each such chart define L_xi(tau,lambda)=F_xi(tau,y)-lambda y. (8) These are local Legendre charts on the marked action graph. No global injectivity of the projection to (tau,lambda) is asserted. They satisfy L_lambda=-y, L_lambdalambda=-1/F_yy, lambda=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i), L_tau=Phi_tau+pi i(lambda-xi). (9) On real complete radial parameters and 0<lambda<xi, this L is the actual coefficient rate already proved. At other complex lambda it is an analytic ACTION chart, not yet an asymptotic formula for individual finite Fourier coefficients. For an arbitrary physical nu in the same local chart, consider H(tau,nu;lambda)=L_xi(tau,lambda) +2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi)(nu-tau/2). (10) Stationarity in lambda gives y=2pi i(nu-tau/2). (11) Substitution of (4),(8) then yields the exact critical-value identity H_crit=J(xi)+Phi_xi(tau,nu)-C_0(tau,xi). (12) The original prefactor contributes -J(xi)+C_0(tau,xi), by (1), and therefore restores precisely Phi. In particular no discarded quadratic phase has to be guessed from a Hessian or a volume value. Differentiation of (12) also preserves the original magnetic momentum and the tau momentum; the latter includes the explicit shift in (9). ## 4. Actual affine cycle coordinates and retained characters At a vertex of the exact shared-cycle compiler, let u_v=epsilon_v x_c+B_v, b_v=max(0,T_i-d), t_i=min(T_i,2d-T_i), delta_v=(B_v-b_v)/N-t_i/(2N), X_c=x_c/N. The normalized magnetic coordinate is nu_v=epsilon_v X_c+(B_v-b_v)/N. The exact finite coefficient phase contains the linear term 2pi i(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i)(delta_v+epsilon_v X_c), up to the explicitly retained finite d/N correction. Thus its classical lambda equation is (11), with y_v=2pi i(delta_v+epsilon_v X_c). It recovers the original coordinate nu_v, with either actual degree adapter and the original white-map reversal. It does not force the new y_v to be real. This is the precise action-level distinction from the [all-radial obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md). For a closed physical cycle, the exact coefficient constraint is sum_v epsilon_v(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i) +(1/2)sum_b epsilon_b =n_c+(b_c+E_c/2)/N. (13) The original marked charge b_c, finite pivotal shift E_c/2 and the integer Fourier winding n_c remain specified. In a leading stationary action the multiplier includes the term -2pi i n_c X_c. It must remain in a critical-value calculation. Likewise a factor (-1)^a has its original product logarithm; replacing it by another logarithm differing by 2pi i a is invisible on integer colors but changes a continued action character. The local identity (12) does not authorize either omission. ## 5. The remaining quantum statement is separate This theorem gives an everywhere nonsingular LOCAL selected-action change for ordinary physical factors. It explains how restoring the exact phase permits nonradial magnetic critical coordinates; it does not construct their finite coefficient asymptotics, select a contributing global period, bound a complementary contraction, or prove that complex critical contributions survive. Completed partner normals and the exceptional four-port block retain their previous scope. In particular, the finite positive coefficient theorem still concerns actual integer indices and real complete parameters with interior slopes. Holomorphic action transport alone cannot replace the missing analytic statement about those coefficients or the full source cycle. Focused audit: [source prefactor and Legendre derivative identities](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.py). Both degree adapters and the white-map reversal retain their stated domains. The local transport theorem does not introduce complex finite coefficient indices, prove global injectivity, or identify a contributing source cycle.

title: An exact accretive determinant for the joint magnetic source
text: # An exact accretive determinant for the joint magnetic source 30 October 2026. The finite rational continuation specified in [the magnetic corridor note](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md), section 6, has an exact tridiagonal determinant. Its Hermitian part is positive on a joint complex domain in the pair degree and the magnetic coordinate. This proves joint zero exclusion and uniform logarithmic derivative bounds for the original finite source, including both parities, composite levels and the folded channel endpoint. The domain is a central wedge; it is smaller than the fixed-real-degree strip. No global source cycle, magnetic stationary point, or volume limit is selected by this theorem. ## 1. The exact finite source, including its scalar Put d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, x=q^d and 0<=j<=floor(d/2). Gaussian binomials below have base Q. The source is fhat_j(u,v)=x^u H_j(U,V)/D_j(UV), U=Q^u, V=Q^v, T=UV=Q^t, t=u+v, D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r), H_j(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j [j choose a]_Q^2 q^[a(a-d)] V^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(V-Q^r). (1) All exponential powers use these displayed logarithms. At physical integer u,v this is the original normalized complete-circle column; (1) also specifies its continuation, without interpolating samples. Set S_j(U,T)=U^j H_j(U,T/U). Since q^[a(a-d)]=(-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2], this is the polynomial S_j(U,T)=sum_(a=0)^j (-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [j choose a]_Q^2 T^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(T-UQ^r). (2) It has degree at most j separately in U and T. Two exact evaluations are S_j(U,0)=(-1)^j Q^[j(j-1)/2] U^j, S_j(0,T)=T^j [2j choose j]_Q. (3) For the second, the finite coefficient identity sum_a Q^(a^2)[j choose a]_Q^2=[2j choose j]_Q follows by comparing z^j in product_(r=0)^(2j-1)(1+Q^r z), split into its two j-factor blocks. All scalar factors in (3) are nonzero: 2j<N. ## 2. A joint Casimir identity, proved before continuation The exact polynomial identity is -Q^(-j)(U-T)(1-QU) S_j(QU,T) -Q^j(U-QT)(1-U) S_j(U/Q,T) +[2(1+QT)U-(1+Q)U^2 -T(Q^(j+1)+Q^(-j))] S_j(U,T)=0. (4) Here is a finite proof which does not extend an integer-t recurrence without justification. For the j+1 original complete slices T=Q^(d-j),...,Q^d, the exact physical Casimir equation gives (4). The entire-U equation on each slice is already proved in section 4 of the magnetic corridor note: its leading U^(j+2) coefficient cancels, and its U=0 value and all original t+1 column nodes make the remaining polynomial of degree at most j+1 vanish. This includes t=d-j=j when N is odd and the channel is maximal. The left side of (4) has degree at most j+1 in T. At T=0, substitute the first identity in (3); the remaining factor is -U(1-QU)-U(1-U)+2U-(1+Q)U^2=0. The j+1 distinct nonzero complete slices and T=0 are j+2 distinct zeros, so (4) holds identically in T and U. This argument proves the complex-degree source identity at every admissible N directly. The focused audit also verifies (4) coefficientwise at formal Q for j=2 through 6; the proof does not depend on those checks. Write c=-cos((t+1)theta), P_j(z;c)=S_j(q^t z,Q^t)/[Q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q]. (5) The constant coefficient is 1. Substitution into (4), followed by coefficient comparison, gives, with p_(j,-1)=0 and p_(j,0)=1, sin(k theta) sin((2j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k) =2c sin^2((j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k-1) +sin((j+2-k)theta) sin((j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k-2). (6) All denominators for 1<=k<=j are positive. Thus this identity determines P_j for every complex t, not only for physical slices. Define the monic reverse polynomial R_j(z;c)=z^j P_j(1/z;c). Equation (1) is exactly fhat_j(u,t-u)=x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(q^t/U;c)/D_j(Q^t). (7) In particular no root-dependent normalization is discarded. ## 3. The ordinary three-term recurrence For 1<=n<floor(d/2), put B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (8) The recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z+c/cos(theta), R_(n+1)=[z+c/(cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta))]R_n +B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]R_(n-1). (9) We prove that no lower-degree terms are hidden in (9). Set [r]=sin(r theta)/sin(theta) and D_q z^r=[r]z^(r-1). Equation (6) is equivalent to L_c R_n=[n][n+1]R_n, L_c=D_q ((z^2+2cz+1)D_q). (10) Indeed L_c z^r=[r][r+1]z^r+2c[r]^2z^(r-1)+[r][r-1]z^(r-2). The eigenvalues for n=0,...,J, J=floor(d/2), are distinct: their successive differences are [2n]>0. Define finite moments mu_0=1, mu_(-1)=0, and [r+1]mu_r+2c[r]mu_(r-1)+[r-1]mu_(r-2)=0 (1<=r<=2J-1). (11) No denominator vanishes, since 2J<N. On available degrees let <z^m,z^n>=mu_(m+n). The difference <z^m,L_c z^n>-<L_c z^m,z^n> is [n-m] times the left side of (11) at r=m+n, by the elementary sine addition identities. Thus the R_n are pairwise orthogonal whenever the requisite total degree is at most 2J-1. Inductively assume the lower norms are nonzero for generic c. In the expansion of zR_n-R_(n+1), pairing with R_k, k<=n-2, kills every coefficient below R_(n-1), since multiplication by z is symmetric. The two remaining coefficients are read from the top powers. Equation (6) gives p_(n,1)=c tan(n theta)/sin(theta), p_(n,2)=[2c sin^2((n-1)theta)p_(n,1) +sin(n theta)sin((n-1)theta)] /[sin(2theta)sin((2n-1)theta)], (12) where p_(1,2)=0. Subtracting these coefficients at n and n+1 gives exactly (9). The norm identity is <R_n,R_n>=-B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]<R_(n-1),R_(n-1)>. It proves the generic nonvanishing needed for the next induction step, starting at norm 1; hence there is no assumption of positivity of this auxiliary moment functional. Polynomial continuation in c then gives (9) for every c. Only moments through 2J-1 are used, including for the maximal channel. The moment functional is a proof device, not a new quantum inner product. ## 4. A positive definite real part For a chosen size j, define real j-by-j matrices D and K, with indices 0,...,j-1. Their diagonal and adjacent entries are D_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], D_(n-1,n)=D_(n,n-1)=sqrt(B_n), K_(n-1,n)=sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n-1)=-sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n)=0. (13) All other entries are zero. Thus D is symmetric and K is skew-symmetric. The tridiagonal determinant recurrence and (9) give R_j(z;c)=det(zI+cD+K). (14) Every leading principal minor of D is explicitly det D_m=2^m product_(r=1)^m sin(r theta) /product_(r=m+1)^(2m) sin(r theta)>0, 1<=m<=j. (15) To see the formula without solving a separate determinant problem, compare the leading c^m coefficient of R_m(0;c)=p_(m,m)(c) in (14). Iteration of the highest-c terms of (6) gives precisely (15). All factors are positive because 2m<N. Sylvester's criterion gives D positive definite, including when j=floor(d/2). If Re c>0, the Hermitian part of cD+K is (Re c)D>0. For any eigenvector, its eigenvalue therefore has positive real part. The zeros of R_j all lie strictly in Re z<0; reversal gives the same statement for P_j. No real-rootedness assertion is needed or made for noninteger t. For positive real c the coefficients in (6) are positive, so R_j(1;c)>0. More generally A=zI+cD+K is invertible whenever Re z>=0 and Re c>0. In the open product of right half-planes its logarithmic derivatives satisfy |partial_z log det A|<=j/Re z, |partial_c log det A|<=j/Re c. (16) The first follows from Re A>=(Re z)I and the inverse operator norm. For the second conjugate by D^(-1/2): D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2) =zD^(-1)+cI+D^(-1/2)KD^(-1/2). Its Hermitian part is at least (Re c)I, and its inverse has trace partial_c log det A. Thus (16) uses no uniform lower eigenvalue bound for D, which could degenerate as the channel approaches 1/2. ## 5. An N-independent joint central wedge Use scaled variables tau=t/N and upsilon=u/N, retaining j as its actual integer channel. Consider the convex domain W={ (tau,upsilon) in C^2: 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re upsilon-Re tau|<1/2 }. (17) For every admissible N and j, c=-cos(pi(tau+1/N)), z=exp(pi i(tau-2upsilon)). (18) The first has positive real part on (17): for N>=2 its cosine argument has real part strictly between pi/2 and 3pi/2. The second has positive real part by the second inequality. Also D_j(Q^t) has no zero on W. Such a zero would require tau=r/N plus an integer, with 0<=r<=j-1<N/2, contrary to 1/2<Re tau<1. Consequently the exact original finite function (7) is holomorphic and nowhere zero throughout W, simultaneously in tau and upsilon. The zero channel j=0 is the explicit nonzero exponential and needs no matrix. On every compact subset of W the quantities Re c, Re z and the separation from the denominator zeros have positive lower bounds uniformly for sufficiently large N. Equations (7), (16), and the product formula for D_j show that both first logarithmic derivatives of N^(-1)log fhat are uniformly bounded. Higher derivatives on smaller compacts follow from Cauchy's formula. Since W is convex, a logarithm is fixed by one marked base value, and normalized logarithmic ratios are locally bounded uniformly in N and j. There is a convenient exact phase normalization at a REAL center upsilon=tau/2 with 1/2<tau<1, even when t=N tau is noninteger. Here c>0 and R_j(1;c)>0. Writing each D_j factor as 2i q^(t+r)sin((t-r)theta), and using [2j choose j]_Q=q^(j^2) times a positive sine-binomial, gives Arg fhat_j(t/2,t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (19) This is a specified continuous argument, rather than its value modulo 2pi. Thus the joint continuation carries the same marked center phase as the original real-degree corridor. ## 6. What this removes, and what it leaves The pair degree is now genuinely complex in an exact source-defined zero-free domain. Neither integer sampling nor a formal WKB solution is used to declare that continuation. The logarithmic estimates are uniform at the folded endpoint and can support a subsequent normal family or finite-shift argument for a joint selected action. The present theorem does not assert a joint amplitude asymptotic, a globally admissible frame for an arbitrary plat, or intersection of its original cycle with the geometric critical point. In particular W is a central wedge, not the whole fixed-t magnetic strip, and simultaneous membership of all source coupons in W is an additional global question. These distinctions remain even though (14) is an exact algebraic identity. Audit: [exact joint determinant and source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.py). This is a local joint theorem. It does not supply a global source frame, asymptotic amplitude or selected cycle.

title: The actual joint magnetic and pair-degree amplitude
text: # The actual joint magnetic and pair-degree amplitude Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. This note continues the original terminating q-Hahn kernel jointly in the pair degree t and the magnetic coordinate u. The channel j remains an integer. The exact accretive determinant, the canonical center phase and two original finite-shift equations give an actual nonzero amplitude, not only a formal stationary ansatz. The domain is a central complex wedge. It is independent of N on compact subsets and includes the folded limit j/N=1/2. This is not yet a contributing-cycle or whole-source theorem for an arbitrary plat. ## 1. The source and the domain Put h=1/N, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and x=q^d=-q^(-1). Let 1<=j<=floor(d/2), xi=j/N. The literal terminating sine-product continuation is the function fhat_j(u,v) in section 6 of [the magnetic corridor](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md). Its Gaussian-binomial coefficients, denominator and exponential prefactor are unchanged. Set t=N tau, u=N nu, v=t-u, U=exp(2pi i nu), T=exp(2pi i tau), z=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], c_h=-cos[pi(tau+h)]. (1) Use the convex, simply connected tube D={ (tau,nu) in C^2 : 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re nu-Re tau|<1/2 }. (2) It lies inside 0<Re nu<Re tau. On each compact subset of D, for all sufficiently large N, Re c_h>0 and Re z>0. All factors T-Q^r, 0<=r<j, are nonzero there. The channel ratio xi lies in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,1/2], with its actual value j/N used in every coefficient function below. The [exact determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md) supplies the monic polynomial R_j(z;c_h)=det(z I+c_h D_j+K_j), D_j real symmetric positive definite, K_j real skew-symmetric. (3) The letter D_j in (3) denotes the matrix, not the product denominator in the rational H_j formula. In this note write that product as Delta_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). The exact scalar normalization is fhat_j(u,t-u) =x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(z;c_h)/Delta_j(T). (4) It follows by taking the U^0 coefficient of U^j H_j(U,T/U): the finite Gaussian Vandermonde identity gives T^j[2j choose j]_Q. This identity follows by taking the middle coefficient in the product of two finite Gaussian binomial products; it has no division by [N]. Here 2j<N, so its scalar is nonzero. ## 2. A canonical joint logarithm, including its finite phase Let beta(2j,j) be the positive sine binomial. Factoring each sine in Delta_j makes (4) equivalent to fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =beta(2j,j) exp{pi i[d nu+(j^2-dj)/(2N)]} R_j(z;c_h)/product_(r=0)^(j-1) 2sin[pi(tau-r/N)]. (5) Every sine has positive real part on D. The matrix in (3) has positive Hermitian part when Re z,Re c_h>0, so its principal matrix logarithm exists. Define Log R_j by the trace of that matrix logarithm. This is holomorphic on the product of the two right half-planes and is real on z,c_h>0. With the positive real logarithm of beta(2j,j), equation (5) therefore specifies a holomorphic Log fhat on each fixed compact portion of D for all large N. These specifications agree on overlaps; no interpolation or sampling character is introduced. For REAL tau with 1/2<tau<1, at the noninteger center u=t/2, R_j(1;c_h) and all the sine factors are positive. The prescribed phase is exactly Im Log fhat_j(t/2,t/2) =pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (6) In particular (6) holds between adjacent integer degrees. It fixes the possible pair-degree sampling alias as well as the magnetic one. For A=zI+cD_j+K_j, accretivity gives |partial_z Log det A|<=j/Re z, |partial_c Log det A|<=j/Re c. (7) For the second estimate conjugate by D_j^(-1/2): the resulting matrix has Hermitian part at least (Re c)I, and its c derivative is I. No lower bound for the smallest eigenvalue of D_j is needed. Consequently the estimates remain uniform at the folded limit. The explicit prefactors in (5) and (7) give locally uniform bounds for all first derivatives of G_N(tau,nu)=N^(-1)Log fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)). (8) A real complete-chamber lattice anchor bounds G_N itself. Cauchy estimates then bound every fixed holomorphic derivative on smaller compact subsets. ## 3. The actual selected joint leading action For real tau,nu with tau+xi>=1 and 0<nu<tau, the preceding real amplitude theorem has the phase Phi_xi(tau,nu)=psi_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*)+pi i nu(1-xi), w_*=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. (9) Its magnetic continuation is already proved at integer t. The canonical logarithm there agrees with (5): at nu=tau/2 their prescribed phases are (6), and continuation in nu fixes the rest. The bounds in section 2 give a normal family jointly in tau and nu. For any real complete-chamber tau, choose nearby actual integer degrees t_N with |t_N/N-tau|<=1/N. The derivative bound changes G_N by O(1/N) between those degrees. On each such slice the existing magnetic theorem identifies the limit (9), with the canonical logarithm just checked. Thus every subsequential joint limit agrees with (9) on a real open set, and hence throughout the connected tube D by the holomorphic identity theorem. This proves for the WHOLE sequence, locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives, G_N(tau,nu)-Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu) ->0, xi_N=j/N. (10) Here Phi is the resulting holomorphic continuation on D. The same subsequence argument gives uniformity for compact real channel-ratio families, including xi=1/2. The elementary characteristic equations below also make its local analytic dependence on xi explicit. There is no finite continuation of the discrete index j in this assertion. ## 4. Two source-exact finite shifts The determinant note proves the entire Casimir identity for complex T by polynomial degree: its cleared residual has T-degree at most j+1, vanishes on the j+1 complete physical slices and also at T=0. Thus the fixed-t Casimir equation is valid for the ACTUAL joint kernel. With f=fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)), it is A_+ f(tau,nu+h)+A_- f(tau,nu-h)+(D_h-C_h)f=0, (11) A_+=(U-T)(1-QU)/T, A_-=(U-QT)(1-U)/(QT), D_h=(U/T)[2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U], C_h=q J+q^(-1)J^(-1), J=exp(2pi i xi). The original normalized coproduct gives a SECOND exact identity: (1-QT)f(tau+h,nu) =x(1-U)f(tau,nu-h)+(U-QT)f(tau,nu). (12) One direct finite proof of (12) uses the Newton summands of H_j. Each summand separately satisfies (1-Q^(-j)UV)H(U,V) =(1-U)H(U/Q,V)+U(1-V)H(U,V/Q). Replace V by QV and use Delta_j(QT)/Delta_j(T)=(1-QT)/(1-Q^(1-j)T), together with the exact x^u factor. This proves (12) for the original sum. The Newton identity alone does not determine the Gaussian-squared coefficients; it is used together with (11), not as a characterization. Put a=Phi_nu, b=Phi_tau, and A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, H(tau,nu,a)=A(e^a+e^(-a))+D-(J+J^(-1)). (13) Passing to the limit in the ACTUAL shifted ratios gives H(tau,nu,a)=0, (1-T)e^b=(U-1)e^(-a)+U-T. (14) The first equation is simple throughout D. Indeed its discriminant, apart from nonzero factors, vanishes only if cos^2(pi xi) z^2+2c_0 z+1=0, c_0=-cos(pi tau). For Re z>0 this would require c_0=-(cos^2(pi xi)z+1/z)/2, whose real part is negative, contrary to Re c_0>0. The same argument includes xi=1/2. Also A!=0 and J!=1 on the stated domain. Hence H_a!=0. The second equation is simple in b, since (1-T)e^b!=0. The prescribed real-chamber values and these simple equations also give local analytic dependence on xi, including through xi=1/2. This concerns the coefficient functions of the asymptotic, not an interpolation of the finite discrete channel. ## 5. Two actual derivative bootstraps and a closed amplitude form Let a_N=partial_nu G_N and b_N=partial_tau G_N. The joint Cauchy bounds and exact finite shifts imply f(tau,nu+/-h)/f=exp(+/-a_N)[1+(h/2)partial_nu a_N+O(h^2)], f(tau+h,nu)/f=exp(b_N)[1+(h/2)partial_tau b_N+O(h^2)]. (15) All errors here and below are uniform on compact subsets, with actual xi_N used. Define A_1^+=-2pi i U(U-T)/T, A_1^-=-2pi i U(1-U)/T, D_1=2pi i U(T-1)/T, C_1=pi i(J-J^(-1)), H_1=A_1^+e^a+A_1^-e^(-a)+D_1-C_1. Equation (11), simplicity and (10) first imply a_N-a=O(h). Cauchy's estimate gives the same derivative bound. Substitution a second time then proves a_N=a+h r+O(h^2), r=-[H_1+(Phi_(nu,nu)/2)H_(a,a)]/H_a. (16) Use this in (12). Its simplicity and the already bounded derivatives first give b_N-b=O(h), and the second substitution gives b_N=b+h s+O(h^2), (17) s={ (1-U)e^(-a)[pi i+r-Phi_(nu,nu)/2] +2pi i T(e^b-1) -(1-T)e^b Phi_(tau,tau)/2 }/[(1-T)e^b]. No logarithmic alias is introduced when solving these equations: a_N and b_N already converge to the prescribed derivatives in (10). The holomorphic one-form omega=s d tau+r d nu (18) is closed. To see this directly, use the equality of the mixed derivatives of the ACTUAL G_N in (16)--(17), and Cauchy bounds for the O(h^2) remainders. It gives partial_tau r-partial_nu s=O(h). Take sequences of admissible xi_N tending to any fixed xi; the coefficient functions are continuous, so that difference is exactly zero. This proves closedness without assuming a formal transport solution equals the finite source. On the simply connected tube D there is therefore a nonzero holomorphic B_xi with d Log B_xi=omega. Fix its constant by the known real physical amplitude at a strict real complete-chamber point, for example tau=1-xi/2, nu=tau/2. Nearby actual lattice samples supply the same normalization to relative error O(h). Integrate (16)--(17) from such a sample along compact paths in D. The gradient of Log f-N Phi+(1/2)log N-Log B is O(h), and its initial value is O(h), choosing the logarithm of its near-one ratio at that sample. Thus the ACTUAL original kernel satisfies fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(N^(-1))). (19) The relative error has the same bound under each fixed derivative on smaller compact subsets. This proves the joint complex amplitude, including arbitrary O(1/N) noninteger shifts of t, fixed complex scaled displacements, both level parities and composite levels. Near the original physical real chamber, comparison with the prior amplitude theorem identifies the coefficient with B_xi(tau,nu)=Acal_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*) exp[pi i(alpha_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*)-nu)]. (20) Both integer offsets are retained. Formula (18) continues (20) wherever a particular internal-saddle coordinate ceases to be a convenient chart. It does not redefine the finite kernel. ## 6. What this removes from the general problem Pair degree and magnetic coordinate may now vary together in a uniform complex central domain. A finite product of these ordinary column factors, composed with the actual affine wire maps of a fixed plat, has the corresponding joint estimate on any compact common preimage of D. The number of factors is fixed with the diagram, so the relative errors still multiply to 1+O(1/N). This statement does not itself place the geometric critical point in that domain, match its sheet to the selected one, choose a contributing physical cycle, or estimate a coherent sum over wires and channels. It also does not continue the discrete channel j or bound new generic-q normal currents. Those remain explicit tasks in the general original-source volume conjecture. ## 7. An explicit algebraic test for the selected local sheet The preceding continuation has a useful exact branch description. Put s=sin(pi xi), C=cos(pi xi), c_0=-cos(pi tau), W=1+2c_0 z+C^2 z^2, V=1+2c_0 z+z^2. (21) Both W/z and V/z have positive real part when Re c_0,Re z>0. Their arguments and the argument of z lie in (-pi/2,pi/2), so W and V avoid the nonpositive real axis. In particular the PRINCIPAL square root sqrt(W) is holomorphic and has positive real part. The actual selected magnetic multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s z+i sqrt(W))^2/V. (22) To prove this, substitute U=exp(pi i tau)/z into (13). It gives Y+Y^(-1)=2-4W/V. The two solutions are (s z+/-i sqrt(W))^2/V. Their numerators are nonzero, since a zero would force V=0; the two solutions are distinct. At a real center c_0>0,z=1, the actual canonical derivative has imaginary part strictly between 0 and pi, fixing the plus sign. Holomorphic continuation on D then proves (22) everywhere. This also includes the folded endpoint C=0. Suppose a candidate marked geometric multiplier Y_geo satisfies the same characteristic equation at a point of D. Then r_geo=[V Y_geo-s^2 z^2+W]/(2i s z), r_geo^2=W. (23) Consequently it belongs to the source-selected local sheet if and only if Re r_geo>0. This is a strict algebraic inequality after the already selected peripheral square roots in z,c_0 are retained. It is a checkable additional condition on a geometric candidate, not a proof that every coupon of a general plat satisfies it in one common frame. The contributing-cycle problem remains separate. Audit: [the original joint source, both shifts and amplitudes](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.py). The finite comparisons test the normalization and correction formulas; sections 2--5 supply the uniform analytical proof. The joint amplitude theorem retains the integer-channel hypothesis. It does not identify a contributing global cycle or bound an assembled coherent sum. The theorem does not supply a common physical frame, select a whole-source cycle, or continue the discrete channel. Two formal polynomial identities verify the characteristic equation and recovered square root in Section 7. Four complex saddle comparisons distinguish the selected and opposite signs; they do not establish a global sheet or cycle.

title: A joint complex packet in the deficient geometric chamber
status: Joint complex packet at the actual geometric frame
text: # A joint complex packet in the deficient geometric chamber 30 October 2026. The actual monic q-Hahn numerator has an N-independent joint complex-degree and magnetic corridor around the real deficient frame. Both its selected root amplitude and its genuine generic-q numerator derivatives are controlled there. The proof uses the original finite determinant, an explicitly bounded low block, and a positive tail matrix. This does not continue the full exceptional operator's generic boundary factors or select a nonzero global period. The original forbidden integer-degree slices remain identically zero. ## 1. The finite determinant and the joint domain Fix 0<sigma_*<kappa<alpha_0<1/2. Put theta=pi/N, a/N=alpha in [alpha_0,1/2], with the actual integer channel 0<=a<=floor((N-1)/2). The degree t=N sigma may be complex. Use the original root monic numerator R_a(z;c) from the joint source theorem, with c=-cos(pi(sigma+1/N)), C=-c, d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], b_n=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta) sqrt(sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta))]. (1) Its exact recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z-C d_0, R_(n+1)=(z-C d_n)R_n -b_n^2[C^2-cos^2(n theta)]R_(n-1). (2) No physical integer-degree assumption is used in (2): it is the already proved polynomial identity for the literal finite Newton numerator, for every complex degree. For each fixed sufficiently small angle vartheta>0 there are epsilon>0 and R>1, independent of N and a, such that R_a has no zeros on the PRODUCT domain |sigma-sigma_*|<epsilon, Omega_R={z: |z|>R, vartheta<Arg z<2pi-vartheta}. (3) Here Arg is the logarithm cut on the positive real axis. Both epsilon and R may depend on vartheta; R can be chosen O(1/sin vartheta), while epsilon can be chosen proportional to vartheta. All statements below concern sufficiently large N and fixed compact subsets of (3), uniformly in the allowed discrete channels. ## 2. A positive tail plus a bounded error Choose m=floor(kappa N), so 0<m<a for large N. In the determinant matrix with characteristic polynomial (2), take indices 0,...,m-1 as a low block. Its diagonal entries are C d_n; take its upper entries to be 1 and its lower entries to be b_n^2(C^2-cos^2(n theta)). These entries and their C derivatives are uniformly bounded. Indeed n/N<=kappa+o(1)<1/2, and b_n cos^2(n theta) =sin(2n theta)/[2 sqrt(sin((2n-1)theta) sin((2n+1)theta))]<=1. (4) The last inequality holds throughout the used range, for N>=5: sin(2n theta)>=sin(2theta), and sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta) =sin^2(2n theta)-sin^2(theta). Thus the low block J_L has operator norm at most a constant L, independent of N. On the tail m,...,a-1 choose the analytic square root sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta)) positive at C=cos(pi sigma_*), and take the symmetric adjacent entry b_n times this square root. All these branches exist on a fixed C disk: kappa>sigma_* separates every radicand uniformly from zero. Let D_T be the principal tail submatrix of the positive matrix whose diagonal is d_n and whose adjacent entries are b_n. Its positivity is already proved by the exact principal minors in the joint source determinant theorem. The tail matrix is EXACTLY J_T(C)=C D_T+E_T(C), (E_T)_(n-1,n)=(E_T)_(n,n-1) =-b_n cos^2(n theta) /[C+sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta))], (5) with zero diagonal. Formula (4) and the strict cutoff show ||E_T(C)||+||partial_C E_T(C)||<=E_0. (6) The same conclusion for every fixed C derivative follows on a slightly smaller disk. No lower eigenvalue bound for D_T, and no uniform bound on its largest eigenvalue, is required. Keep the interface upper entry equal to 1 and the lower entry gamma_m=b_m^2(C^2-cos^2(m theta)), which is uniformly bounded. The resulting tridiagonal determinant is exactly R_a by (2). This bounded nonsymmetric low block avoids choosing square roots at the moving integer-degree zero of a recurrence coefficient. If C stays in a sufficiently small disk about cos(pi sigma_*), and z is in (3), then dist(z,C[0,infinity))>=c |z| sin(vartheta). (7) The inverse of zI-C D_T therefore has norm at most the reciprocal of the right side. Choosing R sufficiently large, (6) gives the same bound, up to a factor two, for (zI-J_T)^-1. The low inverse has norm at most (|z|-L)^-1. Its Schur complement changes the tail by the rank-one matrix gamma_m [(zI-J_L)^-1]_(m-1,m-1) e_0 e_0^T. (8) Its norm is O(1/|z|). A second Neumann estimate proves that the FULL determinant is nonzero and that its displayed tridiagonal matrix M has ||M^-1||<=C_vartheta/|z|. (9) This proves (3) using the actual finite determinant, including both parities and the folded endpoint. ## 3. Joint logarithmic bounds and the source-selected amplitude Fix a negative reference z_*=-R_* with R_*>R. The product domain (3) is simply connected. Define the logarithm of R_a(z)/R_a(z_*) to be zero at z_*, for every sigma. Then |partial_z Log R_a|+|partial_sigma Log R_a|<=C_K N (10) on each fixed compact K, with analogous normalized higher derivative bounds on smaller compacts. For completeness the large D_T causes no loss in (10). The Schur tail is S=zI-C D_T-E_T-gamma e_0e_0^T, with gamma the bounded expression in (8), and C S^-1 D_T=z S^-1-I-S^-1 E_T -gamma S^-1 e_0e_0^T. (11) Thus its trace against a C derivative is O(N) by (6),(9). The low-block derivative is bounded; gamma and its derivatives are bounded by the low resolvent formula. This proves (10). There are functions S_(sigma,alpha)(z), A_(sigma,alpha)(z), holomorphic jointly in sigma and z on (3), with S(z_*)=0, A(z_*)=1 and A nowhere zero, such that R_a(z;c)/R_a(z_*;c) =A_(sigma,alpha)(z) exp[N S_(sigma,alpha)(z)] (1+O(N^-1)). (12) The error and its fixed derivatives are uniform on compacts. The phase and amplitude depend smoothly on the real channel parameter alpha, which always remains the ACTUAL a/N. The anchor is selected by an exact source identity, not by a choice of an algebraic root. For every complex sigma put t_hi=N(1-sigma)-2, u_hi=t_hi/2+iN log(R_*)/(2pi), beta_a=s_(2a)/s_a^2. The reflection R_a(z;-c)=(-1)^a R_a(-z;c) and the original ordinary normalization give exactly R_a(-R_*;c)=(-1)^a beta_a^-1 product_(r=0)^(a-1)2sin(pi(t_hi-r)/N) *q^[-(N-1)u_hi-(a^2-(N-1)a)/2] *fhat_a(t_hi,u_hi). (13) This is in the already proved JOINT high-degree physical packet: Re(t_hi/N)>1/2, its real magnetic coordinate is centered, and the complete-channel margins follow from alpha_0>sigma_*. Its two wire coordinates remain strictly inside their domains for a small fixed complex sigma disk. The offset -2, the actual half-integer center when present, and every phase in (13) remain literal. All sine factors have a fixed distance from their zeros. Consequently (13) supplies a nonzero relative absolute anchor, jointly in sigma, by that ordinary packet and an elementary finite-product Euler--Maclaurin estimate. It also does so on an open interval of negative z around z_*. The bounds (10) give a normal family for the normalized logarithms. Every limit agrees on that negative interval with the anchor's source-selected leading phase. The identity theorem fixes it on Omega_R, for each complex sigma; compactness makes convergence uniform jointly in sigma and the real parameter alpha. There is no interpolation from integer degree samples in this argument. Here are explicit transport equations proving the relative error. Put D=z partial_z, kappa_q=2pi i, U=exp(pi i sigma)/z, T=exp(2pi i sigma), J=exp(2pi i alpha). The original finite numerator satisfies the exact root equation (QU-1)(U-T)R(z/Q)+(QT-U)(1-U)R(Qz) +[2U+2QTU-(1+Q)U^2-T(Q^-a+Q^(a+1))]R(z)=0. (14) Set A0=(U-1)(U-T), C0=2U(1+T-U)-T(J+J^-1) and H(p,z)=A0(e^(kappa_q p)+e^(-kappa_q p))+C0. The selected p=D S satisfies H=0. Its discriminant is C0^2-4A0^2=-16T^2 sin^2(pi alpha) W/z^2, W=1-2cos(pi sigma)z+cos^2(pi alpha)z^2. (15) All roots of W remain in the excluded small positive sector. Indeed write C_s=cos(pi sigma), b=cos(pi alpha), and use the analytic sqrt(C_s^2-b^2) positive at the real center. The roots are 1/(C_s+sqrt(C_s^2-b^2)) and (C_s+sqrt(C_s^2-b^2))/b^2, with the second omitted at b=0. The gap alpha_0>sigma_* gives uniform branches and a uniform argument bound, even as b tends to zero. Shrink epsilon if necessary. Also A0 has zeros only near the unit circle, outside Omega_R. Hence H_p is nonzero throughout the domain. The exact first transport term is H1=kappa_q[U(U-T)e^(-kappa_q p) +T(1-U)e^(kappa_q p)+2TU-U^2-TJ], rho=-(H1+(D p)H_(p,p)/2)/H_p. (16) Larger-compact Cauchy bounds, the exact shifts in (14), and the proved actual leading convergence first give p_N-p=O(N^-1), where p_N=D(N^-1 Log R_a). A second substitution then gives p_N=p+rho/N+O(N^-2), uniformly jointly in sigma and z. Define D Log A=rho and A(z_*)=1 and integrate along compact paths from z_*. This proves (12), including fixed derivatives. It is the actual finite-shift bootstrap, not a formal WKB choice. ## 4. Genuine generic-q numerator normals Now use the original generic recurrence with B=Q^-N, not the root-only recurrence (2). Hold t=N sigma and a fixed while q=q0 exp(epsilon_q) varies. A marked magnetic lift u is also held fixed, with |u|<=C N and z(q)=q^(t-2u). Assume its root parameters lie in a compact subset of (3). Then |partial_(epsilon_q)^r R_a(q;t,z(q))|_0 <=C_r N^(10r) |R_a(q0;t,z(q0))|. (17) The same estimate applies to the original unnormalized Newton numerator after retaining its exact K_a and monomial factors. The bounded marked lift is necessary: u->u+NL leaves the root coordinate unchanged but changes its genuine q derivatives. To prove (17), first conjugate the root matrix above by the diagonal unitary with entries (-1)^n, so its offdiagonal signs are positive in the following convention. Its inverse bound (9) is unchanged. In the low block and at the interface freeze the upper entries at 1. In the tail freeze each upper entry at its ROOT complex value b_n sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta)); it is bounded away from zero. Set every generic lower entry to minus the actual generic recurrence coefficient beta_n divided by that frozen upper entry. The diagonals use the actual generic alpha_n. This determinant is exactly the original generic R_a. The previously proved generic recurrence estimates, with t/N in a fixed complex compact, give |alpha_n'|<=C N^5 and |beta_n'|<=C N^7 on the required small generic disk. The same bounds follow directly by differentiating their finite rational formulas: the only small denominators are the original spectral gaps, while q^t and its marked derivatives have bounded scaled parameters. Thus the matrix changes by at most C N^7 |epsilon_q|; z(q) changes by O(N|epsilon_q|). By (9), on |epsilon_q|<=c N^-10 the determinant ratio and its inverse are bounded, since its dimension is at most N. Cauchy's formula gives (17). The original K_a and monomials are controlled on this same disk by their finite root-unit products. No derivative of a root-only reflection is used. ## 5. The actual geometric chart and the remaining period The real-deficient-frame theorem has sigma_*=1/6. Its two determinant arguments have |z| asymptotic to a positive constant times X^2 and imaginary parts of opposite sign, each comparable to X, with X arbitrarily large. Keep the midpoint in a compact subinterval of its allowed range. Choose vartheta proportional to 1/X and then X sufficiently large. The proof above needs only R=O(1/sin vartheta)=O(X), so BOTH actual arguments lie strictly in (3). A small fixed complex neighborhood of this chosen geometric frame, or a fixed compact family around it, is therefore covered. One fixed vartheta does not cover the entire unbounded X-family, whose arguments approach the cut. The negative-real anchor in (13) is exactly the reflected source branch calibrated in that framing theorem. At the folded limit its magnetic characteristic is Y=(z-i sqrt(1-2cos(pi/6)z))^2 /[1-2cos(pi/6)z+z^2], (18) with the square root continued from positive values at negative z through the upper or lower half-plane respectively. The two values agree with the actual input/output geometric momenta, including the output's C^-1 disk shift. This comparison uses the proved anchor and corridor, not arbitrary root selection. The entire completed root kernel is a residual sine product times two such R polynomials. In this deficient corridor the residual sine arguments, after removing their recorded integer sign, lie in a strict zero-free strip because alpha>Re sigma by a fixed margin. Thus its exact product and (12),(13) give a nonzero joint ROOT packet, including complex degree, in a neighborhood of the actual geometric frame. At a maximal folded channel the residual product remains empty or one factor as specified by the exact source, so both level parities are kept. The normal estimate (17) is for the original q-Hahn numerators. The full exceptional generic operator still has its unspecialized boundary factors and requires its own lift; it cannot be obtained by varying q in the canceled root kernel. In particular, an actual large-partner column cannot be replaced by the small-channel numerator in (17) solely because their root values coincide; their genuine generic derivatives are different. Most importantly, the complete fixed forbidden integer-separation physical slice is identically zero. Its magnetic deformation alone must retain that zero. Joint degree analysis now has a local analytic input, but no degree contour, nonzero global coefficient, complementary source gap, or general volume equality has been proved here. Focused audit: [original joint numerator, tail determinant and selected amplitude](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.py). It checks 248 independent-degree original four-jet identities, 124 exact finite-shift equations, 72 determinant and Schur identities, 24 positive tail matrices and 586 endpoint coefficient bounds. At 120 digits, 12 literal reflected high anchors, 24 joint complex amplitudes and 72 genuine numerator checks pass. The finite matrix and asymptotic samples remain diagnostics; the uniform estimates are proved above. The full generic operator and selected degree period remain open. The small/large generic partner distinction and the exact zero-slice limitation are retained.

title: The actual magnetic polynomial and its complex corridor
status: Complex magnetic corridor; fixed degree and channel
text: # The actual magnetic polynomial and its complex corridor The subsequent joint-domain theorem retains the central magnetic domain and discrete channels. This note treats the larger fixed-degree magnetic strip; the two domains are distinct. 30 October 2026. This note concerns the original complete-circle column, at fixed integer pair degree t and channel j. Its finite continuation in the magnetic coordinate u is specified by its terminating factorial sum, not chosen from an interpolation class. An exact coproduct recurrence places every zero outside the physical magnetic strip. The original Casimir difference equation then upgrades the real magnetic amplitude theorem to a complex corridor in u/N. The continuation keeps t and j REAL and discrete. It is not a joint continuation in all magnetic/channel variables of an assembled plat. In particular it does not choose the global source integration cycle. ## 1. A literal finite continuation, with all prefactors Write d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and assume the actual complete-circle inequalities d-j<=t<=d, 0<=j<=floor(d/2). For a nonnegative integer a define the entire function beta(z,a)=product_(r=0)^(a-1) 2sin(pi(z-r)/N) / s_a, s_a=product_(r=1)^a 2sin(pi r/N). The original continuation is the finite sum fhat_(N,t,j)(u)=exp(pi i u) q^[-(j+1)u] sum_(a=0)^j q^[(t+j-d)a] beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j). (1) All exponential powers in (1) use their displayed logarithms. At an integer 0<=u<=t, a term outside the original support vanishes because one of its numerator sine factors is zero. Thus (1) is EXACTLY the physical Casimir column, including its original scalar and phase. Off that lattice those terms are retained; no fictitious support truncation is made. Put U=Q^u and T=Q^t. There is a polynomial G_t of degree at most j with fhat_(N,t,j)(u)=x^u U^(-j) G_t(U), G_t(1)=1. (2) An explicit polynomial, with m=j-a and w=q^(t+j-d), is G_t(U)=i^(-j)s_j/beta(t,j) sum_(a=0)^j w^a q^[-mt-(a(a-1)+m(m-1))/2] product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(m-1)(T-UQ^r) / (s_a^2 s_m^2). (3) Indeed each first product in the sine expression contributes i^(-a)q^[-au-a(a-1)/2], and the second contributes i^(-m)q^[-mt-mu-m(m-1)/2]. Their common u factor is q^(-ju). This proves (2)--(3), including the degree, rather than inferring an interpolation from its values. ## 2. The original coproduct proves the root factorization Keep N and j fixed and let t range from d-j to d. The actual divided coproduct F, normalized by the first component, gives G_(t+1)(U)=[Q^j(1-U)G_t(U/Q) +(U-Q^(t+1))G_t(U)]/(1-Q^(t+1)). (4) To check its normalization directly, the unnormalized component at degree t+1 is (1-Q^u) f_t(u-1)+q^(-d+2u)(1-Q^(t+1-u))f_t(u). Its u=0 value is x^(-1)(1-Q^(t+1)). Dividing by this value and using (2) gives (4). The term of degree j+1 cancels, so its right side is again a polynomial of degree at most j. Equality on the t+2 original physical nodes proves the polynomial identity as well. At t=d-j the actual highest vector gives the exact base G_(d-j)(U)=(UQ;Q)_j/(Q;Q)_j. (5) For example its u-th component is (-1)^u q^[-(2j+1)u](Q^(u+1);Q)_j/(Q;Q)_j, directly from the original highest-vector equation. There are d-j+1>=j+1 physical nodes, so this determines the degree-j polynomial in (5). Set h=d-t and n=j-h=t+j-d. Define B_h(z)=product_(r=0)^(h-1)(1+q^(h-1-2r)z). Its coefficients are the positive sine binomials beta(h,a). Equations (4)--(5) prove the factorization G_t(q^t z)=c_t B_h(z) A_n(z), c_t=q^(jn)/(Q;Q)_j, A_0=1. (6) Here A_n is a real polynomial of degree n with positive coefficients and n simple negative roots. The following direct argument proves these assertions at every step, not merely at sampled levels. When h decreases to h-1, n increases to n+1. The residual update is A_(n+1)(z)=-Im[q^(-j-h)(1+q^h z)^2 A_n(qz)]/sin(h pi/N), (7) where (7) is stated for REAL z. Its holomorphic polynomial meaning is the corresponding coefficientwise difference of conjugate polynomials. Explicitly, if A_n=sum a_k z^k, then a'_k=[sin((j+h-k)theta)a_k +2sin((j-k+1)theta)a_(k-1) +sin((n-k+2)theta)a_(k-2)]/sin(h theta), theta=pi/N, a_k=0 outside 0<=k<=n. (8) All coefficients of degrees 0 through n+1 are positive. The putative degree n+2 coefficient is zero, since j=h+n. The scalar in (6) changes by c_(t+1)=q^j c_t. To obtain (7), use B_h(q^(-1)z)=(1+q^(-h)z)B_(h-1)(z), B_h(qz)=(1+q^h z)B_(h-1)(z) in (4); its residual numerator is q^(2j)(1+q^(-h)z)^2 A_n(q^(-1)z) -q^(-2h)(1+q^h z)^2 A_n(qz). Now suppose A_n(z) has roots -rho_k, rho_k>0. At z=-r, r>0, the continuous argument of the quantity inside Im in (7) is -(j+h)theta+2Arg(1-q^h r)+sum_k Arg(rho_k-qr). It strictly decreases from -(j+h)theta, which lies in (-pi,0), to -(n+2)pi as r tends to infinity. The limiting endpoint is not reached at finite r. Each factor stays nonzero and each individual argument strictly decreases. Therefore exactly n+1 multiples of pi are crossed, with nonzero derivative. Equation (7) has n+1 distinct negative roots. Since its degree is at most n+1, these are all its roots and the degree is exactly n+1. This starts from A_0=1 and proves (6). **Exact zero theorem.** G_t has its h forced zeros U=Q^(t+1),...,Q^d, and its n residual zeros lie on U=-q^t rho with rho>0. The residual zeros are simple; a residual zero can coincide with a forced zero, which causes no problem below. In the scaled magnetic variable upsilon=u/N, the latter zeros have Re upsilon=(1+t/N)/2 modulo 1. Every zero therefore lies OUTSIDE S_tau={upsilon in C: 0<Re upsilon<tau}, tau=t/N. (9) The exact finite function (1) is nonzero on this entire strip, at both parities and composite levels. This conclusion is special to the original physical Fourier argument w=q^(t+j-d); it is not an assertion of joint zero-freeness in independent w and upsilon. ## 3. The canonical magnetic logarithm and its selected limit Let (tau,xi)=(t/N,j/N) remain in a compact strict real parameter set with 0<xi<tau<1, xi<=1/2, tau+xi>=1 in the limiting complete chamber. The actual integer parameters may have tau+xi=1-1/N; all constructions use those actual parameters and are uniform for this O(1/N) boundary displacement. Consider compact subsets inside S_tau, uniformly away from both vertical boundaries. Factorization (6) gives locally uniform bounds for N^(-1)Log[fhat(N upsilon)/fhat(N upsilon_0)] (10) and all its fixed derivatives. Here upsilon_0 is near tau/2 and the logarithm is continued in the simply connected strip. For each root, the logarithmic derivative is 2pi i U/(U-zeta). The possible root locations in section 2 are uniformly separated from the image of the chosen compact set; radial roots are compactified by their radius in [0,infinity]. Integrating along compact paths bounds each root's logarithmic ratio uniformly. There are j<=N/2 roots, and the explicit exponential in (2) supplies only a bounded normalized term. The phase at the noninteger center is fixed exactly, not guessed: B_h(1)A_n(1)>0 in (6), and hence a specified argument is Arg fhat(t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (11) This uses (Q;Q)_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]s_j with its original product phase. The leading imaginary action at the center is therefore pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2. A nearest integer to t/2, together with the bounded logarithmic derivative in (10), supplies its real leading value from the actual real-magnetic theorem. Write the previously selected physical action, for REAL upsilon, as Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon)=psi_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star) +pi i upsilon(1-xi), w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. (12) At the center its internal saddle is alpha=xi/2+i eta. The paired J terms make Ecal(alpha) real, so Im Phi(tau/2) is exactly pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2, agreeing with (11) to leading order. The same pairing gives Ecal'' real negative and A(alpha)B(alpha)>0. Therefore the continued Acal amplitude is positive real there. The remaining order-one phase exp[pi i(alpha-tau/2)] is -pi(tau-xi)/2, exactly the difference between (11) and N Im Phi. This checks both the additive logarithmic mark and its finite phase. The actual real-magnetic amplitude theorem supplies its values on all physical samples. Normal-family limits of (10) must have the same real part there. More precisely, adjacent physical sample ratios and bounded second derivatives give exp(g'(upsilon))=exp(Phi'(upsilon)) on the real interval. Thus g'-Phi' is a constant 2pi i integer. This sampling alias must be removed; dense samples alone do not remove it. At the center, positivity of all coefficients of B_h A_n gives 0<=Im[N^(-1)partial_upsilon Log fhat(N upsilon)]<=pi in the limit, with real part zero. The selected derivative in (12) lies STRICTLY between 0 and pi on that imaginary axis. Indeed the internal saddle there is alpha=xi/2+i eta, eta>=0. Its exact phase equation is 4Arg sin(pi(xi/2+i eta)) +2Arg sin(pi((tau-xi)/2+i eta))=pi(tau+xi-1). Consequently Phi'(tau/2)=pi i(1-xi) +2i Arg sin(pi((tau-xi)/2+i eta)) has imaginary part in [pi(1-xi),pi tau], a compact subinterval of (0,pi). The integer alias is zero. Equation (11) fixes the remaining additive constant. Compactness and the identity theorem now prove convergence of the WHOLE actual sequence, including derivatives: N^(-1)Log fhat(N upsilon) -> Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon). (13) The right side is the holomorphic continuation selected by the actual polynomial. The same subsequence argument gives uniformity for compact real parameter families. It does not interpolate t or j. ## 4. The exact magnetic difference equation and its simple branch Let f(upsilon)=fhat(N upsilon), h_N=1/N, U=exp(2pi i upsilon), T=exp(2pi i tau), and Jc=exp(2pi i xi). The original symmetric physical Casimir gives the exact finite difference equation A_+(upsilon,h_N) f(upsilon+h_N) +A_-(upsilon,h_N) f(upsilon-h_N) +(D_(h_N)(upsilon)-c_(h_N))f(upsilon)=0, (14) where q=exp(pi i h_N), Q=q^2 and A_+=(U-T)(1-QU)/T, A_-=(U-QT)(1-U)/(QT), D_h=(U/T)[2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U], c_h=q Jc+q^(-1)Jc^(-1). It is an identity for the entire continuation (1). One direct check uses (2): after removing its exponential, the residual is a polynomial in U of degree at most j+1, since its top degree j+2 cancels. Its constant coefficient is zero. It also vanishes at the t+1 original physical nodes U=1,Q,...,Q^t, by the actual Casimir eigenvector equation, including both boundary rows. Since t>=j, these zeros plus U=0 force the polynomial to vanish identically. No generic contiguous identity or missing endpoint equation is presumed. Put A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, H(upsilon,a)=A(e^a+e^(-a))+D-(Jc+Jc^(-1)). (15) The branch selected in (13) satisfies H(upsilon,Phi')=0. It is simple throughout the strip in the limiting complete chamber. Its characteristic discriminant is exactly (Jc+Jc^(-1)-2) [Jc+Jc^(-1)+2-4U(1+T-U)/T]. (16) The second factor's zeros, after U=exp(pi i tau)X, obey X^2-2cos(pi tau)X+cos^2(pi xi)=0. Because tau>=1-xi and xi<=1/2, its finite nonzero roots are negative real. They lie on the same excluded magnetic line as the residual roots in section 2. A zero root at xi=1/2 is not a finite U. Also A has no zero inside S_tau and Jc!=1. Hence H_a!=0 there. On compact subsets it remains bounded away from zero, also for the actual O(1/N) displacement below tau+xi=1. ## 5. Actual complex amplitude from the magnetic finite shifts This section proves a fixed complex corridor theorem around any compact real magnetic interval inside (0,tau). The preceding root and discriminant estimates also permit compact paths farther inside the strip, with the continued functions specified in sections 3--4. Write G_N=N^(-1)Log f and a_N=G_N'. The exact zero theorem and (13) give bounded holomorphic derivatives and a_N->Phi' on larger compact sets. Taylor expansion of the ACTUAL shifted ratios in (14) yields f(upsilon+/-h_N)/f(upsilon) =exp(+/-a_N)[1+(h_N/2)a_N'+O(h_N^2)]. (17) Expand the displayed finite coefficients as A_+=A+h_N A_1^++O(h_N^2), A_-=A+h_N A_1^-+O(h_N^2), and similarly for D and c. Explicitly, A_1^+=-2pi i U(U-T)/T, A_1^-=-2pi i U(1-U)/T, D_1=2pi i U(T-1)/T, c_1=pi i(Jc-Jc^(-1)), H_1(upsilon,a)=A_1^+e^a+A_1^-e^(-a)+D_1-c_1. Equations (14) and (17) imply 0=H(upsilon,a_N) +h_N[H_1(upsilon,a_N)+(a_N'/2)H_aa(upsilon,a_N)] +O(h_N^2). Uniform simplicity first gives a_N-Phi'=O(h_N). Cauchy's estimate on a larger compact set improves its derivative to the same order. Substitution a second time proves the ACTUAL correction a_N=Phi'+h_N b+O(h_N^2), b=-[H_1(upsilon,Phi')+(Phi''/2)H_aa(upsilon,Phi')] /H_a(upsilon,Phi'). (18) Let Btilde solve the scalar holomorphic equation Btilde'/Btilde=b, with its nonzero value at the real center fixed by the previous [actual amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.md). Then Btilde is holomorphic and never zero on the corridor. The center may be noninteger: use the nearest physical sample to fix the constant to relative error O(1/N), since both Btilde and the previous explicit amplitude are smooth and nonzero there. Integrating (18) from that physical sample proves fhat_(N,t,j)(N upsilon) =N^(-1/2) Btilde_(tau,xi)(upsilon) exp[N Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon)](1+O(N^(-1))). (19) The error is uniform on the complex corridor, with each fixed derivative on smaller compact subsets. Thus the transport solution in (18) is justified by the original polynomial and a known actual constant; it is not a formal ansatz substituted for it. The amplitude in (19) is the continuation of the earlier explicit one: Btilde_(tau,xi)(upsilon) =Acal_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star) exp[pi i(alpha_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star)-upsilon)]. (20) To see this without assuming an unproved transport identity, compare (19) with the previous actual theorem at physical real samples. Taking sequences of parameters and samples tending to any strict real point proves equality of the two nonzero amplitudes there. Their holomorphic continuations are therefore identical. The local coefficient functions are analytic across tau+xi=1, so the identity also covers the actual O(1/N) boundary displacement. This analytic identity between coefficient functions is NOT a claimed finite interpolation of t or j. The phases and the order-one factor in (20) retain both original integer offsets. No root-normal derivative has been taken. The theorem supplies an actual complex magnetic packet at fixed real t,j; global magnetic/channel summation, complex pair-degree or channel continuation, and the original global cycle remain separate. ## 6. A canonical joint rational continuation, without a joint estimate There is also a source-defined joint continuation in u and v=t-u. Set U=Q^u, V=Q^v and retain the phase x^u=exp(pi i d u/N). For fixed N and j define the finite polynomial H_j(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j [j choose a]_Q^2 q^[a(a-d)] V^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(V-Q^r), D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). (21) The original terminating formula, extended with its own finite sine products, is exactly fhat_j(u,v)=x^u H_j(U,V)/D_j(UV). (22) The denominator and the marked exponential are retained. This is a specified finite rational function, not a choice of factorial interpolation. In (21) the binomial is the GAUSSIAN binomial. If one uses the positive sine binomial instead, the same coefficient is beta(j,a)^2 q^[a(2j-a-d)] V^a. (23) Indeed [j choose a]_Q=q^[a(j-a)] beta(j,a). Confusing these two binomials changes the original phase, already at j=2. For a direct derivation, substitute the two finite sine products used in (3), and use beta(t,j)=i^(-j)q^[-jt-j(j-1)/2] D_j(Q^t)/s_j. Removing this denominator leaves the phase q^[a t+a(j-a)] before the original w^a is included. Since w=q^(t+j-d), and Q^(at)U^(-a)=V^a, the remaining phase is exactly q^[a(2j-a-d)]. This proves (22). Restricting UV=T to an actual integer degree recovers G_t(U)=U^j H_j(U,T/U)/D_j(T). (24) No joint zero-location theorem for H_j(U,V), or joint complex asymptotic in pair degree and magnetic coordinate, is asserted here. The preceding strip theorem uses the essential restriction that UV=Q^t with t real and integer. Formula (22) specifies a possible next object without supplying the missing estimates for it. Audit: [exact magnetic polynomial and complex corridor](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.py). The theorem still fixes real discrete pair degree and channel; it supplies neither a joint complex estimate nor a selected whole-source cycle. The conclusion is a fixed-degree estimate, not a global source bound. The joint complex-domain extension is a separate theorem.

title: The actual paired normal on a fixed complex corridor near the fold
status: Complex paired-normal bound; shrinking channel window
text: # The actual paired normal on a fixed complex corridor near the fold Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. The original paired normal admits a polynomial bound on every fixed compact magnetic corridor when the two channel indices remain a bounded number of steps apart. More generally it has only subexponential relative cost when their separation s satisfies s log N=o(N). The magnetic corridor is genuinely complex and has width independent of N. This follows from the original generic source, not from interpolation of its physical-grid values. The channel window in this statement shrinks in scaled coordinates. It does not give subexponential cost at a fixed nonzero scaled channel displacement, a relative normal amplitude, or a whole-source estimate. ## 1. Statement and exact source Let q0=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, and let 0<=j<l, j+l=d, s=l-j. For q=q0 exp(epsilon) put Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), x=q^d and t=N tau, u=N nu, U=Q^u, T=Q^t, sigma=q^t, D_m(T)=product_(r=0)^(m-1)(T-Q^r). Use the literal generic finite source from [the small-channel generic theorem](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md) and [the collision theorem](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md): C_m(q;t,u)=x^u H_m^B(U,T/U)/D_m(T), H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^m (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [m choose a]_Q (BQ^(m-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-a)(V-Q^r). (1) All powers use log q=pi i/N+epsilon. In particular this is the original generic highest-weight-d deformation, not the root-only squared-binomial formula. Its paired normal is w_(j,l)(t,u)=[D C_j(q0;t,u)-D C_l(q0;t,u)] /[-2N Delta_j], Delta_j=q0^(2j+1)-q0^(-2j-1), D=q d/dq. (2) Let K be a compact subset of the joint central wedge W={ (tau,nu): 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re nu-Re tau|<1/2 }. There exist eta_K,c_K,C_K>0 such that, for all sufficiently large N and all 1<=s<=eta_K N of the required parity, |w_(j,l)(N tau,N nu)/C_j(q0;N tau,N nu)| <= C_K N^8 (C_K N^16)^s, (tau,nu) in K.
