(3) Every function in this quotient is holomorphic on a neighborhood of K, and C_j(q0) is nonzero there. No omitted tail is used in (3). Consequently, for bounded s the cost is polynomial in N. Uniformly over any windows 1<=s<=h_N with h_N log N=o(N), |w_(j,l)| <= exp(o(N)) |C_j(q0)| (4) on the SAME fixed complex compact K. This includes windows of size O(N^a) for every fixed a<1, in particular square-root windows. ## 2. The generic recurrence is valid beyond the small channel Keep B temporarily independent of Q. Put A=B^(-1) and K_m=(B^2 Q^(m+1);Q)_m/(BQ;Q)_m, S_m(U,T)=U^m H_m^B(U,T/U), R_m(z)=z^m S_m(sigma/z,sigma^2)/(sigma^(2m) K_m). These are monic polynomials for generic parameters. Their exact source normalization is C_m=x^u q^(mt) K_m R_m(sigma/U)/D_m(T). (5) Write Lambda_n=AQ^(-n)+BQ^(n+1), b_n=[(1+A)+Q sigma^2(1+B) -Q^(-n)(Q sigma^2+A)-Q^n(BQ sigma^2+1)]/sigma, d_n=Q^(1-n)+Q^n-1-Q, u_0=0, u_n=b_n/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1)), v_0=v_1=0, v_n=(b_(n-1)u_n+d_n)/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2)), n>=2, alpha_n=u_(n+1)-u_n, beta_n=v_(n+1)-v_n-alpha_n u_n, n>=1. Then, as RATIONAL identities in generic B,Q,sigma, R_0=1, R_1=z+alpha_0, R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). (6) The small-channel note proves these formulas by its original Casimir identity and finite moment argument. Their use at a large channel requires an additional justification. Fix n and clear the denominators in (6). The residual is a finite Laurent polynomial in B,Q,sigma,z, independent of the source size N. For every N>=2n+3 the proved small-channel result makes it vanish at B=Q^(-N), identically in generic Q,sigma,z. Writing the residual as sum_a B^a p_a(Q,sigma,z), choose N larger than all its finite Q-exponent widths. The supports of Q^(-Na)p_a are then disjoint. Therefore every p_a is zero. This proves (6) formally for every n. The scalar identity for K_m already has the independent finite Vandermonde proof and no small-channel restriction. Thus (5),(6) describe the actual large generic source wherever their generic factors are defined. At the actual root some monic R_m have poles because K_m vanishes. We do not assume these monic polynomials are holomorphic there. ## 3. A small generic circle controls every intervening row Let a_K=inf_K(Re tau-1/2)>0. Choose 0<eta_K<min(1/4,a_K). Then l/N<1/2+eta_K/2 and every extra source divisor T=Q_0^r, j<=r<l, remains uniformly separated from K. The same holds for the factors already present in D_j. All elementary exponentials q^n, B and sigma, and their inverses, are uniformly bounded for |epsilon|<=c N^(-3), n<=N, (tau,nu) in K. Use the circle |epsilon|=rho_N=c_K N^(-8), (7) with c_K chosen from the small-channel theorem, decreasing it if needed. That theorem supplies a tridiagonal matrix M_j(epsilon) with det M_j=R_j(z), z=sigma/U. At zero it is the original accretive matrix zI+cD+K_skew, c=-cos((t+1)pi/N), and its change in operator norm is O(N^7 |epsilon|). Consequently, throughout the disk enclosed by (7), ||M_j^(-1)||<=C_K, |C_j(q)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K, |R_(j-1)(z)/R_j(z)|<=C_K. (8) The last identity follows from the last diagonal entry of M_j^(-1): the cofactor is its leading (j-1)-row determinant, exactly R_(j-1). Thus the initial two values for propagating (6) are controlled. For every n<=l, the only spectral denominators in (6) are Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1) =(1-Q)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n)), Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2) =(1-Q^2)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n-1)). (9) At the root a vanishing last factor in (9) occurs only at 2n=N or 2n-1=N, respectively. All other last factors have modulus at least c/N, and both first factors have modulus at least c/N. These nonresonant differences therefore stay at least c/N^2 on the circle (7). At a resonant n the last factor is exactly 1-Q^(-N)=1-exp(-2N epsilon), whose modulus is at least c N rho_N on that circle. Multiplication by the first factor gives a lower bound c rho_N. Hence EVERY required denominator on (7) obeys |Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-r)|>=c_K rho_N, r=1,2, (10) with r=2 used only for n>=2. This explicitly retains the folded resonance rather than pretending its root denominator is a unit. The numerators b_n,d_n are O_K(1). The definitions in section 2 and (10) give, on the circle, |u_n|+|alpha_n|<=C_K rho_N^(-1), |v_n|+|beta_n|<=C_K rho_N^(-2). Propagating the two-component recurrence (6) exactly s times, from R_(j-1),R_j to R_l, now gives |R_l(z)/R_j(z)|<=(C_K N^16)^s. (11) No positivity, missing-current cancellation, or interpolation of physical samples enters this estimate. ## 4. The scalar ratio and holomorphy of the FULL source The scalars in (5) cannot be discarded. Their exact cancellation is K_l/K_j= product_(r=2j+1)^(2l)(1-B^2 Q^r) /[product_(r=j+1)^l(1-B^2 Q^r) product_(r=j+1)^l(1-BQ^r)]. (12) There are 2s numerator and 2s denominator factors. The denominator indices lie uniformly near N/2 under s<=eta_K N, so all those denominators are bounded below on (7). The numerator factors are uniformly bounded above. One numerator factor vanishes at the center of the circle; it is retained in (12). Thus |K_l/K_j|<=C_K^s, |D_j(T)/D_l(T)|<=C_K^s, |q^((l-j)t)|<=C_K^s. (13) Equations (5),(8),(11),(13) prove on the circle |C_l(q;t,u)/C_j(q0;t,u)| <=C_K(C_K N^16)^s. (14) We apply Cauchy's formula to C_l, NOT to its singular monic factor. The original finite expression (1) proves C_l is holomorphic throughout the enclosed disk: its factors (Q;Q)_a and (BQ;Q)_a have indices a<=l<N and are units at q0; their possible zeros stay outside this polynomially small disk. Its factors D_l(T) are uniformly nonzero by the separation at the beginning of section 3. The finite numerator is entire in the displayed exponentials. Thus every apparent monic pole inside (7) is already canceled in the original source, before Cauchy's estimate is used. Consequently (14), and the small-channel bound for C_j, imply |D C_l(q0)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K N^8(C_K N^16)^s, |D C_j(q0)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K N^8. (15) Finally |Delta_j|=2sin(pi s/N) and 2N |Delta_j|=4N sin(pi s/N)>=8s>=8 in this near-fold range. Dividing the two ACTUAL generic derivatives in (15) by the original gap in (2) proves (3). ## 5. What the estimate supplies The full paired normal, including its large-channel tail, is holomorphic and has at most subexponential relative cost on a fixed complex magnetic corridor for s log N=o(N). This can accompany the proved ordinary-column complex action in a shrinking channel window at the complete endpoint. It is an upper bound: no nonzero normal amplitude or leading coefficient is asserted. For s proportional to N the bound (3) is too large to identify an exponential rate. In particular it does not control a fixed nonzero scaled channel shift that might arise at a filling saddle. The extra-pole obstruction outside the near-fold corridor remains valid. Neither physical-grid interpolation nor an assertion that the generic monic determinant is regular has been used to avoid it. Focused audit: [full generic large source and resonant circle](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound_results.json). Exact dual arithmetic passed 208 all-degree source recurrences, 582 original large-channel generic value-and-normal comparisons, and 110 scalar-ratio identities. At 220 digits, 120 literal nonphysical large-source circle comparisons, 5,080 spectral-gap checks, 30 original-versus-transverse paired normals, and 120 retained scalar identities passed. The maximum source comparison error was below 1.1e-206. Both bounded and square-root-sized channel separations occur in these checks. The uniform conclusion is the proved circle estimate, not an inference from the samples. The estimate requires s log N=o(N). It does not include a fixed positive scaled-channel displacement or an amplitude theorem. The conclusion remains a relative upper bound in the stated shrinking channel window on a fixed magnetic corridor.

title: The actual finite-clock boundary determinant through the fold
status: Positive finite-clock boundary determinant and retained trace transport
text: # The actual finite-clock boundary determinant through the fold 30 October 2026. The original 222 boundary has two finite negative raw clocks, by the literal [right-angled prefix sign theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md). At the ROOT this puts its actual white numerator in a positive definite determinant, including the maximal folded channel. This note proves a uniform relative perturbation formula which retains the order-one transport term, and an explicit leading logarithmic rate through the fold. The proof uses the finite determinant, matrix traces and elementary sums, not a saddle selection assumption. These are numerator results. Scalar phases, partner products and all source normalization remain explicit. No genuine generic quantum derivative, full source cycle, or volume equality follows. ## 1. The literal source and its negative raw clocks Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2 and 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Let H_a^1(U,V) be the root white polynomial in the [resonant boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Its exact determinant, proved in the [complementary boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md), is H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. (1) The empty determinant for a=0 is one. The Hermitian positive definite matrices H_-,H_+ have common diagonal d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], 0<=n<a, and upper adjacent entries sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta) -/+ i cos(n theta)], 1<=n<a, B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (2) Their positivity follows from the original exact Cholesky pivots; it holds at both level parities and through the folded endpoint. Use the ACTUAL half-index arguments U=q^-1 X, V=q^-1 Y, X<0, Y<0, alpha=-X/2>0, beta=-1/(2Y)>0. Then the matrix in (1) is EXACTLY M=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+ > I. (3) In particular its determinant is positive, while V^a and K_a retain their original phases. This statement concerns the raw clocks X,Y, not an independently rotated pair of physical heads. The original 222 geometry supplies precisely these limiting signs. The exact finite-r arguments differ from their limits, and are handled next; they are not silently set equal to their limits. ## 2. Uniform relative transport, with its first correction retained Change the coefficients in (3) to alpha(1+e_-), beta(1+e_+), allowing complex e_-,e_+. Set eta=|e_-|+|e_+|<1 and E=M^(-1/2)[alpha e_- H_-+beta e_+ H_+]M^(-1/2). Both alpha M^(-1/2)H_- M^(-1/2) and beta M^(-1/2)H_+ M^(-1/2) are positive semidefinite, and their sum is I-M^-1<I. Hence ||E||<=eta, with no dependence on N,a, or a small eigenvalue of an individual H matrix. The marked logarithm, zero when e_-=e_+=0, therefore satisfies Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)=tr E+R, |R|<=a eta^2/[2(1-eta)], |Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)|<=-a log(1-eta). (4) Indeed expand tr Log(I+E) in its absolutely convergent matrix power series, use |tr E^j|<=a eta^j, and sum the terms j>=2. This also proves nonvanishing and specifies the relative branch. If X is changed to X(1+u) and Y to Y(1+v), the exact choices are e_-=u, e_+=(1+v)^(-1)-1. (5) Thus O(N^-1) relative clock corrections give det(M+Delta M)/det M=exp(tr E)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) The trace need not tend to zero: it is an order-one source transport term and must stay. Corrections O(log N/N) have at most O(log N) logarithmic cost, with a nonzero relative factor. The estimates are uniform through the fold. The factors V^a, K_a and all other source factors remain outside this comparison and are kept EXACTLY. These are clock perturbations at one root, not the moving-Q or moving-B generic quantum derivatives. ## 3. The determinant's leading rate Suppose a/N tends to xi in [0,1/2] and alpha,beta tend to positive limits. The convergence below is uniform when alpha,beta stay in compact subsets of the positive reals. For 0<=t<1/2 write c(t)=cos(pi t), D(t)=1+(alpha+beta)/c(t)^2, b(t)^2=[(alpha+beta)^2-4alpha beta c(t)^2]/[4c(t)^4], lambda_+(t)=[D(t) +sqrt(1+[2(alpha+beta)+4alpha beta]/c(t)^2)]/2. The square root here is positive real. Then (1/N)log det M -> I(xi;alpha,beta), I(xi;alpha,beta)=integral_0^xi log lambda_+(t) dt. (7) The endpoint xi=1/2 is included. The improper integral converges because log lambda_+(t)=O(1+|log(1/2-t)|). An a=0 subsequence has empty determinant and rate zero. Here is a proof from the actual finite matrices. The diagonal of M is 1+(alpha+beta)d_n; the squared modulus of its upper entry is B_n[(alpha+beta)^2 sin^2(n theta) +(alpha-beta)^2 cos^2(n theta)]. (8) Away from t=1/2 these converge to D(t), b(t)^2. On each fixed closed interval below 1/2, entries are uniformly bounded. The few initial n, for which the B_n continuum approximation is not uniform, do not affect the Riemann limit: after removing an arbitrarily short initial interval convergence is uniform, while all the removed entries have a common bound. Their contribution to each fixed matrix trace moment is bounded by that interval's length times a constant depending only on the moment. For a fixed integer j, expand tr M^j into closed nearest-neighbor walks of length j. Away from the two ends, each walk sees entries whose variation over j indices tends uniformly to zero. The constant-coefficient walk sum is the zeroth Fourier coefficient of [D(t)+2b(t)cos(phi)]^j; complex offdiagonal phases cancel because a closed walk traverses each edge equally in both directions. Endpoint walks contribute O(j/N) to the normalized trace. Consequently, for every polynomial P and xi<1/2, (1/N)tr P(M) -> integral_0^xi (1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2pi) P(D+2b cos phi) dphi dt. (9) All eigenvalues of M lie in [1,C_xi] by (3) and the bounded row sums. The limiting symbol lies in the same type of interval: D-2b>=1. Approximate log on this interval by truncating log z=log R-sum_(j>=1)(1-z/R)^j/j, R>C_xi. The tail converges uniformly geometrically since z>=1. Its trace error divided by N is bounded by (a/N) times the uniform error. Thus (9) holds for log as well. Finally D+2b cos phi=lambda_+ |1+(b/lambda_+)exp(i phi)|^2, where b/lambda_+<1. Expanding the scalar logarithm in powers of exp(i phi) shows that its second factor has mean logarithm zero. This proves (7) below the fold, without invoking a limiting matrix theorem. To include the fold, cut off the last h<=delta N+O(1) indices. Write M in these two principal blocks. Its Schur complement S on the last block satisfies I<=S<=M_tail: the lower bound follows by minimizing the quadratic form of M>=I over the first block. The upper bound is the explicit positive Schur subtraction. Hence 0<=log det M-log det M_bulk <=log det M_tail<=sum_tail log[1+(alpha+beta)d_n]. (10) The last inequality follows, for example, from its Cholesky pivots being no larger than its diagonal entries. With j_n=N-2n-2>=1 at every allowed diagonal entry, d_n<=C N^2/j_n^2. The j_n have step two. Integral comparison for the sum of log j therefore bounds (10) by C h[1+log(N/max(1,h))]+O(log N). After division by N this tends to zero as delta tends to zero. The same integrable bound handles the tail of (7). This proves the endpoint, including every sequence of actual folded colors. For varying positive parameters, (4) bounds the normalized logarithmic change by C(|Delta log alpha|+|Delta log beta|), uniformly in the channel and N on positive compact sets. Thus the fixed-parameter argument extends uniformly to compactly varying alpha,beta; the integral in (7) has the same continuity by its integrable fold bound. ## 4. The original scalar and large partner Let Lambda(x)=-integral_0^x log|2sin v| dv. The exact magnitude of K_a is s_(2a)/s_a^2, where s_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N). Elementary Riemann sums, splitting off the integrable endpoint logarithms, give (1/N)log|H_a^1(q^-1X,q^-1Y)| -> xi log|Y|+[2Lambda(pi xi)-Lambda(2pi xi)]/pi +I(xi;alpha,beta). (11) Equation (1), not just (11), retains its complex scalar phase. For the actual large channel m=d-a, keep the exact root identity H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). (12) For xi bounded away from zero and XY in a positive compact, the product in (12) is uniformly away from its factors' zeros. Its additional logarithmic rate is integral_xi^(1-xi) log|XY-exp(2pi i t)| dt. (13) The finite q^-2 in UV=Q^-1 XY and the exact endpoints stay in (12). At small colors, or under complex perturbations near any forced divisor, use that exact product, not a claimed uniform relative replacement of it. No derivative of (12) is used to assert a generic quantum normal. This is a boundary extension of the earlier strict physical-tube theorem: the canonical raw negative clocks have limiting real total degree one, which lies on that tube's boundary. Unlike the whole rational column, the numerator determinant has no omitted Delta_a(UV) denominator. This note estimates the numerator only. The action in (7) has the original selected normalization. To check this directly, rotate both raw clocks to X_delta=e^(-i delta)X and Y_delta=e^(-i delta)Y, with fixed small delta>0. Their actual heads lie in the earlier strict physical tube for all sufficiently large N. The two determinant coefficients become alpha e^(-i delta) and beta e^(i delta), so (4) bounds the difference of their normalized marked logarithms from the negative-clock value by C delta, uniformly in N and through the fold. The strict-tube theorem gives the original selected action at each fixed delta. Taking N to infinity and then delta to zero identifies its boundary value with (7). The branch is transported by (4) from the positive determinant; at X=Y=-1 this is the old real center, where the determinant is positive, so the two branches agree there. Continuation through the connected negative-clock quadrant retains that equality. The exact factors V^a and K_a are still those of (1). No unrelated solution of the characteristic equation or new additive constant is being selected by the trace-walk calculation. This comparison uses the strict-tube theorem for xi>0. At xi=0, the present small-a/N trace bounds and scalar sums give rate zero; the selected boundary value there follows by continuity, without invoking the earlier fixed-positive-color packet at zero color. It supplies one piece of the original boundary source, not its global cycle coefficient or the full complementary-color gap. Focused audit: [original numerator and determinant checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary_results.json). At 90-digit precision it compares 48 literal source numerators, 30 independent dense determinants and 48 large-partner identities. It checks 36 retained trace corrections against the proved remainder bound, six independent dense trace calculations and 42 positive Schur-tail inequalities. The 36 leading-rate diagnostics supplement the written proof; they are not its justification. The conclusion concerns the root numerator. It does not establish generic-$q$ normal data or a global period. The selected boundary calculation retains the original half offsets and the positive branch specified above.

title: Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial
text: # Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial 30 October 2026. The finite polynomial inside EVERY physical complete-channel q-Hahn column has only negative nonzero roots. They are simple; its sole possible zero at the origin is the forced support power. This is an all-level theorem for the ACTUAL finite coefficients, not an inference from the stationary quadratic or a sampled real-root plot. In particular the physical Fourier evaluation of that polynomial never vanishes. The proof uses an exact two-binomial recurrence and an elementary sine coefficient multiplier. An independent sine-operator peeling proof of the two-binomial step is retained in section5. ## 1. The exact source polynomial and its support Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), and s_r=product_(k=1)^r 2sin(k theta), s_0=1, beta(n,a)=s_n/[s_a s_(n-a)] for 0<=a<=n, beta(n,a)=0 outside that integer range. For physical 0<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t and 0<=j<=t set v=t-u and P_(t,j,u)(z)=sum_a E_a z^a, E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j). (1) Its nonzero support is exactly a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u), n=a1-a0. (2) All coefficients in this interval are strictly positive. The actual [complete augmented-plat compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) uses the further restrictions j<=floor(d/2), t+j>=d and the exact physical evaluation f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] P_(t,j,u)(q^delta), delta=t+j-d>=0. (3) Equation (1) is precisely that finite compiler coefficient, with no q-factorial normalizer omitted. The theorem holds even without those further complete-image restrictions: P(z)=C z^a0 product_(h=1)^n(z+rho_h), C>0, rho_h>0, and all rho_h distinct. (4) If n=0 this is a positive monomial, with no nonzero roots to list. ## 2. A two-binomial polynomial has simple negative nonzero roots For u,v>=0 with t=u+v<N define Q_j^(u,v)(z)=sum_a beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a) z^a, 0<=j<=t. (5) The symmetric quantum-binomial product is the finite identity B_k(w)=sum_a beta(k,a)w^a =product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1+q^(k-1-2r)w). (6) For an elementary proof, use B_k(w)=(1+q^(k-1)w)B_(k-1)(q^-1 w). The two coefficient terms combine to beta(k,a) by the sine addition identity; B_0=1 starts the induction. No root-location assertion for B_k is made: its roots usually lie on a unit-circle arc. Let F(w,z)=B_u(zw)B_v(w)=sum_j Q_j(z)w^j. Its q-shifts obey (1+q^-u zw)(1+q^-v w)F(qw,z) =(1+q^u zw)(1+q^v w)F(q^-1 w,z). Comparing the coefficient of w^j and dividing by 2i gives the EXACT three-term recurrence sin(j theta) Q_j =[z sin((u-j+1)theta)+sin((v-j+1)theta)] Q_(j-1) +z sin((t-j+2)theta) Q_(j-2), (7) with Q_0=1 and Q_1=[sin(u theta)z+sin(v theta)]/sin theta. First suppose j<=min(u,v). For 2<=j<=min(u,v), every sine coefficient shown in (7) is strictly positive, since t<N. At any negative zero r of Q_(j-1), the sign of Q_j(r) is opposite to that of Q_(j-2)(r). Starting with Q_0,Q_1, a direct induction therefore gives j SIMPLE negative roots of Q_j strictly interlacing those of Q_(j-1). For completeness, adjacent roots of Q_(j-1) give j-2 alternating sign intervals; its rightmost root has Q_j<0 while Q_j(0)>0; and its leftmost root has sign opposite to the sign of Q_j at negative infinity. These provide all j roots. The leading and constant coefficients are positive by (5). All other j are reduced to this case by the following EXACT identities: Q_j^(u,t-u)(z)/beta(t,j) =Q_u^(j,t-j)(z)/beta(t,u), (8) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^u Q_(t-j)^(u,v)(1/z), (9) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^j Q_j^(v,u)(1/z). (10) Identity (8) follows coefficientwise by canceling six sine factorials; (9),(10) follow from beta(k,a)=beta(k,k-a). Their Laurent expressions are exactly polynomials because the same forced support zeros are present on both sides. Choose the smallest of j,t-j,u,v. If it is j, use (7). If it is t-j, use (9). If it is u, use (8). If it is v, use (10) and then (8). The new degree parameter is at most both new group sizes, so the previous Sturm induction applies. Reversal replaces each nonzero negative root by its reciprocal and multiplication by a positive constant or a forced power of z does not change its sign or simplicity. Thus (5) has exactly its forced zero of order a0, followed by n simple negative roots, for EVERY 0<=j<=t<N. ## 3. The sine multiplier preserves negative roots Let D=z d/dz and define the REAL coefficient operator S_r=sin[theta(D+r)], S_r A(z)=[e^(ir theta)A(e^(i theta)z) -e^(-ir theta)A(e^(-i theta)z)]/(2i). (11) Suppose A has degree n and only negative roots, with positive leading coefficient, and 0<r, r+n<N. Then S_r A has n SIMPLE negative roots. Here is a direct proof. Write A(z)=C product(z+rho_h), rho_h>0. For x>0 follow the continuous argument arg[e^(ir theta)A(-e^(i theta)x)]. Each factor rho_h-x e^(i theta) has strictly decreasing argument, with derivative -rho_h sin(theta)/|rho_h-x e^(i theta)|^2. The total argument decreases from r theta to (r+n)theta-n pi. It crosses exactly 0,-pi,...,-(n-1)pi, once each. Those crossings are exactly the n negative roots of (11); the factors being measured never vanish on x>0. Its leading and constant coefficients are positive. Repeated roots of the input do not spoil the strict argument monotonicity. A forced power z^a is retained: S_r[z^a A]=z^a S_(r+a)A. Thus the same assertion applies if 0<r+a and r+a+n<N. The elementary root reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives beta(j,a)=s_j/N product_(r=1)^(d-j) 2sin[(a+r)theta], 0<=a<=j. (12) Consequently multiplication of the a-th coefficient by beta(j,a), on a polynomial of degree at most j, is the exact operator M_j=(s_j/N) 2^(d-j) product_(r=1)^(d-j) S_r. (13) Every factor in (13) satisfies r+degree<=d<N. On a polynomial with its forced zero at the origin the shifted inequality in section3 is the same one. It therefore preserves that zero and all remaining negative roots. Applying M_j to Q_j and dividing by the positive beta(t,j) gives precisely (1). Equations (5)--(13) prove (4). The empty product j=d causes no exception: then j=t=d and n=0. ## 4. The actual Fourier value and its logarithmic branch In the complete-image chamber, 0<=delta<=j<=floor(d/2). Thus q^delta has argument between 0 and pi/2, strictly below pi/2 at finite N. It lies away from every zero in (4), so the ACTUAL canonical column (3) is nonzero, including all magnetic endpoints. More generally P(z)/P(1) has a canonical holomorphic logarithm on C minus the nonpositive real axis, fixed to be zero at z=1. Its exact factorization is Log[P(z)/P(1)]=a0 Log z +sum_h Log[(z+rho_h)/(1+rho_h)]. (14) For real |phi|<pi this also gives the elementary bound cos(phi/2)^n <= |P(e^(i phi))|/P(1) <= 1. (15) This follows from |e^(i phi)+rho|^2=(1+rho)^2-4rho sin^2(phi/2). The loss in (15) can be exponential in N. It is not a subexponential whole-source bound, a Gaussian amplitude estimate, or a proof of noncancellation after summing different physical magnetic variables. The zero-free logarithm is the rigorous input for a separate local complex asymptotic argument. ## 5. Independent sine-operator peeling proof of section2 There is a second own proof that does not use the recurrence or the intersection duality. Begin with the finite Laurent polynomial A_initial(z)=z^j B_v(1/z)=z^(j-v) B_v(z). Apply the coefficient multiplier beta(u,a). By (12) with j replaced by u, it is proportional to product_(r=1)^(d-u) S_r. The same product is zero on every unwanted Laurent power: for a<0 the factor r=-a occurs, and for a>u the factor r=N-a occurs. This uses v<=d-u and j<=u+v<=d. On the wanted powers it equals beta(u,a) exactly, so its output is the polynomial (5). The factors commute. If j>u, apply first r=N-j,...,d-u in increasing order. The identity S_(N-k) B_k=sin(k theta) B_(k-1) removes each forced high power, with the fixed prefactor z^(j-v) accounted for in the shift. If j<v, next apply r=v-j,...,1 in decreasing order. The identity S_0 B_k=sin(k theta) z B_(k-1) removes each forced negative Laurent power. All extracted constants are positive. The remaining polynomial is a positive multiple of z^a0 B_n(z), with a0,n as in (2). The unused factors have r from max(0,v-j)+1 to d-max(u,j). After extracting z^a0 their parameters are s=r+a0. They satisfy 0<s and s+n<N, and their number is n+(d-t) >= n. (16) Use at least n of these factors to strip B_n. More generally, S_s[B_k(z) A(z)]=B_(k-1)(z) T_(s,k)A(z), T_(s,k)A=Im{e^(is theta)(1+q^k z)A(qz)} (17) for real z; equivalently take the two conjugate polynomial terms as in (11). If A has m negative roots, positive leading coefficient, and k+m=n, the argument at z=-x decreases strictly from s theta to (s+k+m)theta-(m+1)pi. Here 0<k<N and 0<s+n<N. It therefore crosses exactly m+1 multiples of pi, giving T_(s,k)A exactly m+1 SIMPLE negative roots and positive leading/constant coefficients. Starting with A=1, each step reduces k by one and increases m by one. After n steps no B factor remains and all roots are negative. The remaining d-t ordinary S_s factors preserve them by section3. This independently proves the complete support and root assertion for Q. It also explains why a reciprocal sine factorial by itself need not be a multiplier: the proof uses the whole paired coefficient structure. Audit: [exact recurrence, dualities, finite source coefficients and root counts](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.py). Numerical root counts remain regression checks, not the all-level proof.

title: A source-normalized paired resonant circle packet
status: Paired boundary normalization and genuine large-channel bounds
text: # A source-normalized paired resonant circle packet 30 October 2026. The incoming200 and outgoing220 packets combine into the FULL original root circle coefficient with its measure, turn character and finite clock corrections. The actual generic220 numerator also has polynomial-cost fixed quantum jets near the fold. With the specified moving-period cup lift, this bounds genuine normals of the literal exceptional operator on the same paired chart. A nonzero normal amplitude or global period coefficient does not follow. ## 1. Keep both roots, the measure and the original character Put d=N-1, a<=floor(d/2), m=d-a, s=m-a, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Use the normalized original circle coordinates (sigma;R,S), and put U_o=Q^R, V_o=Q^(sigma-R), U_i=Q^S, V_i=Q^(sigma-S), T=U_o V_o=U_i V_i, P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j), beta_a=s_(2a)/s_a^2, K_a=[2a choose a]_Q=q^(a^2)beta_a. The logarithms of all four heads are the literal source lifts. The [regulator normalization](actual_matching_edge_deficient_packet_regulator.md) gives the exact full circle coefficient C_a. Substituting the original normalization H_a=T^(a/2)K_a R_a and the actual root partner identity H_m=P_s(T)H_a gives C_a(sigma;R,S) =k_a V_a(d-sigma) q^[d(R+S-sigma)-2a^2] H_m^1(U_o,V_o) H_m^1(U_i,V_i) /[T^a P_s(T)^2]. (1) Here V_a(h)=product_(j=a+1)^m 2sin(pi(h+j)/N) and k_a is the original multiplicity, including k_a=1 when 2a=d. Equation (1) is used where its displayed denominator is nonzero; the original coefficient has its previously proved removable continuation elsewhere. It is an identity of the actual circle coefficient, not of its scalar spectral symbol. The h0_a-normalized literal turned W pi coefficient is exp(-2pi i R)C_a. The specified generic exceptional lift has the inverse root character already recorded in its source theorem. These characters must either be retained or canceled by that EXACT restoration. The retained half twist multiplies C_a by its original kappa^epsilon nu_a^epsilon. No cup, turn, fold multiplicity or channel unit is absorbed into an unspecified constant in (1). ## 2. A relative full root packet Assume m/N lies in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), U_i=N^2 kappa_i, V_i in a fixed compact subset of C*, qU_o in a fixed compact subset of Re z<0. Then V_o=T/U_o=N^2 kappa_o, with kappa_o bounded and bounded away from zero. These hypotheses hold in a fixed sufficiently large-N paired200/220 chart from the actual collar calculation in the [complementary theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md). Set Z_i=(-1)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2] T^m product_(j<m)(1-Q^j/U_i), K_i=sin^2(pi m/N)(V_i-1)/(pi^2 kappa_i V_i), M_o=I-(qU_o/2)H_-, A_N=k_a V_a(d-sigma) q^[d(R+S-sigma)-2a^2] Z_i V_o^m U_o^s K_a det M_o/[T^a P_s(T)^2]. (2) Every factor in A_N is exact at the actual finite N and actual finite-r frame. In particular det M_o has NOT been replaced by its limiting-clock determinant: an O(1/N) change in qU_o can have an order-one effect. The incoming whole-polynomial Bessel theorem and the uniform relative220 determinant theorem imply C_a/A_N=J_0(2sqrt(K_i))+O(N^-1). (3) The entire series sum_l (-K_i)^l/(l!)^2 defines this Bessel notation. The error is uniform and absolute. On a compact where that series is bounded away from zero, (3) is relative and C_a is nonzero for large N. All factors in (2) are nonzero in this chart: |T| is comparable to N^2, P_s and V_a have the same zeros there, and the matrix M_o is uniformly accretive. For the actual first-slot resonant chart r=1/(1-Q^-j)-b0 s_frame, with fixed j!=0 and a first-cut clock A=exp(2pi i alpha), 0<alpha<1, the incoming limit is the proved I_0(2j s_frame sin(pi m/N)), s_frame=A^-1-1. Its nonvanishing for Re s_frame<0 was proved from the elementary radial ODE in the [root boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Thus this paired circle has a nonzero ROOT packet at those frames, through both folded parities. The j=0 boundary and other prefix patterns are not included in this statement. There is also a nonzero off-node version: take r=N rho with rho in a positive real compact and alpha in a compact subset of (0,1/2). The actual geometric Bessel argument is s_frame sin(pi m/N)/(pi rho), which is nonreal. The elementary radial energy argument in the [signed-prefix theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md) shows that J_0 has only real zeros. Thus (3) is relative on this paired chart too. The original off-node source functional retains its separate, nonzero limiting factor rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t_coh/rho); this does not identify t_coh with alpha or determine its unknown whole-source coefficient. ## 3. Genuine generic220 control by a scaled original recurrence Keep the heads sigma,R fixed with size O(N log N), put q=q0 exp(epsilon), and use their actual powers U_o(q),V_o(q). Let q0 U_o(q0), V_o(q0)/N^2 obey the preceding compact hypotheses. For s=d-2a with 0<=s<=eta N, eta sufficiently small, the actual LARGE generic numerator satisfies |H_m^B(U_o(q),V_o(q))/H_m^1(U_o(q0),V_o(q0))| <=C(C N^20)^s, |epsilon|<=c N^-10. (4) For s=0 the right side is C. For s>0 the proof first bounds the boundary circle and then uses holomorphy. Consequently every fixed k has the corresponding Cauchy bound with the extra factor C_k N^(10k). This is an upper bound for the original B=Q^-N deformation. It does not differentiate the root collision in (1). Here are the source and uniform estimates. Use the all-degree generic monic recurrence R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1) proved in the [paired-normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md). Its variables are b=q^sigma, z=b/U_o, so |b| and |z| are comparable to N. Set G_n=R_n/z^n. Exactly, G_(n+1)=(1+alpha_n/z)G_n+(beta_n/z^2)G_(n-1), H_n^B(U_o,V_o)=V_o^n K_n G_n. (5) For n<=a, all required spectral differences are at least cN^-2 on a small polynomial disk. The recurrence's original coefficient b_n is O(N), b_n'=O(N^2 log N); its d_n is O(1), d_n'=O(N). Using the original quotient formulas gives conservative bounds u_n=O(N^3), u_n'=O(N^6 log N), v_n=O(N^6), v_n'=O(N^9 log N), (alpha_n/z)'=O(N^5 log N), (beta_n/z^2)'=O(N^7 log N). (6) These follow by the quotient rule with the ACTUAL spectral factors (1-Q)B^-1Q^-n(1-B^2Q^(2n)) and their two-step analogues. Every marked exponent remains O(N log N), and z'/z=O(N log N). At the root the determinant for G_a is exactly M=I-(q0 U_o/2)H_--(q0^-1/(2V_o))H_+. The proved H_+<=2H_-+8I shows Re M>=cI uniformly for large N. Freeze its upper entries; their absolute values are bounded below, since they are at least sqrt(B_n)(|q0 U_o|/2-|1/V_o|/2). Set the corresponding generic lower entries to -beta_n/(z^2 upper_n) and the diagonals to 1+alpha_n/z. This is the determinant in (5). By (6) its operator perturbation is O(N^7 log N |epsilon|). On |epsilon|<=cN^-10, the determinant ratio and its inverse are bounded, as is the inverse matrix. Its final cofactor gives |G_(a-1)/G_a|<=C. (7) The actual scalar K_a has logarithmic derivative O(N^3); V_o^a has logarithmic derivative O(N^2 log N). Thus H_a has bounded two-sided relative variation on that disk. On the boundary |epsilon|=cN^-10, each folded resonant spectral difference is at least c|epsilon|; all others remain at least cN^-2. Since b_n=O(N) and |z| is comparable to N, the scaled recurrence coefficients in (5) are at most C|epsilon|^-1 and C|epsilon|^-2. Propagating s rows from (7) therefore costs at most (CN^20)^s. The exact scalar ratio K_m/K_a has 2s numerator and 2s denominator factors; its denominator indices stay near N/2, so it costs only C^s. Finally |V_o(q)^s/P_s(T(q0))|<=C^s. This last estimate is why no artificial N^(2s) loss occurs: |T(q0)| and |V_o(q0)| are both comparable to N^2, and the root partner product is retained. It proves (4) on the circle. The original finite H_m sum is holomorphic inside it, since m<N and all its generic factorial denominators stay away from zero. The maximum principle and Cauchy's formula apply to that full H_m, not to the potentially singular monic R_m factors. ## 4. Restore the specified generic operator factors For the paired chart also require the stated logarithmic-factorial conditions for the actual cup arguments. Namely each canonical physical argument lies in an interior real strip with imaginary part O(N log N), or is an exterior argument with scaled imaginary part bounded away from zero and bounded real part. Fixed original integer factorials, including d=N-1, retain their fixed endpoints. All marked heads are O(N log N). This hypothesis is concrete for the paired reference box. With its actual middle prefix Q1=e[[1,z0],[0,1]], the finite incoming second clock is (1+z0 s_frame)/(1+(z0+1)s_frame), while the finite outgoing first clock tends to -c^2. Choose a fixed first-cut compact on which the former has an interior physical logarithmic lift. Such a choice exists: for small positive alpha, s_frame=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 and that ratio is 1+2pi i alpha+O(alpha^2), independently of fixed z0. When z0=0 it is exactly the first-cut A. The other physical and channel-cup heads escape logarithmically with nonzero imaginary part. Exclude the stated factorial divisors and retain every affine offset. Use EXACTLY mathscr K_a and mathscr E_a=D_a^-1 mathscr K_a in the [generic exceptional lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md), equation (9), including its original moving scalar c_a. Its two white numerators are the incoming200 and outgoing220 factors above. On the N^-10 disk, the genuine200 theorem bounds the first factor relative to its nonzero root value; (4) bounds the second. The [logarithmic-factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md) bounds every cup factor and inverse relatively on its larger disk. The fixed factorials, D_a and c_a are root units with polynomial logarithmic derivatives. All retained monomial exponents have size O(N^2 log^2 N). Therefore |partial_epsilon^k mathscr E_a|_0 <=C_k N^(10k)(CN^20)^s |mathscr E_a(q0)|, (8) and the same holds for mathscr K_a. For s log N=o(N) this is a subexponential relative cost, and for bounded s it is polynomial. The root value and its physical turn are those used in (1)--(3). This uses the literal generic exceptional polynomial germ. It does not identify it with a generic W pi lift whose dual was fixed only at the root. Equation (8) does not give a nonzero leading normal amplitude. The local nonzero circle packet (3), even together with (8), does not evaluate the original coupled band cycles or determine the global relative framing coefficient. The 140-digit run checks 24 exact full-circle normalizations against the original white/channel-cup/physical-cap contraction, 24 retained turn characters, two independent root Barnes-factorial contractions, eight actual paired-frame root packets through both folded parities, 32 original scaled generic determinant identities and 32 independent cofactor identities, 32 genuine large220 circle ratios, and 16 genuine first/second numerator normals. The source error was below 4.2e-135. The packet and disk samples are diagnostics, not proofs of the uniform estimates. The full generic operator bound is the stated exact factor-by-factor consequence; no full leading normal amplitude is claimed by those finite tests. The result is a nonzero local root-circle packet and the stated upper bound on genuine generic operator normals, with the marked source germ retained. title: The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision
text: # The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. The large partner in the original mixed-circle column can be compared with the small column BEFORE specializing q. Their equality holds on a generic spectral-collision hypersurface. This gives an exact transverse derivative formula for the original first normal, and an explicit finite tail. The tail has genuine additional poles; there is no individual-normal holomorphic theorem on the entire joint central wedge. No polynomial relative bound for that normal on a smaller corridor is proved here. Nor does a pole of an individual continued column imply a pole of the full physical coupon after all measures and terms are combined. ## 1. The original generic column in a symmetric finite form Use Q=zeta^2, d=N-1, B=Q^(-N), x=zeta^d, U=Q^u, T=Q^t and X=U^(-1). Write (a;Q)_k=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1-a Q^r). The actual generic Clebsch column from [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, has the finite expression C_m=x^u F_m, F_m(Q,B;X,T)=sum_(k=0)^m (Q^(-m);Q)_k (B^2 Q^(m+1);Q)_k (X;Q)_k Q^k /[(BQ;Q)_k (T^(-1);Q)_k (Q;Q)_k]. (1) In (1), B is temporarily an independent variable. Its specialization B=Q^(-N) is the original generic source; B is not a replacement quantization. All displayed denominator factors are units near a primitive N-th root with B=1, except the indicated T divisors. For clarity, the finite transformation in (1) has a direct proof. The original bivariate numerator is H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^m (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [m choose a]_Q (BQ^(m-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-a)(V-Q^r), F_m=H_m^B(U,T/U)/product_(r<m)(T-Q^r). (2) The normalized generic Casimir operator, after removing x^u, has eigenvalues Lambda_m=B^(-1)Q^(-m)+B Q^(m+1). On the Newton basis P_k(X)=(X;Q)_k its action is triangular: L P_k=Lambda_k P_k+eta_k P_(k-1), eta_k=(B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T)(1-Q^(-k)). (3) One can check the lower term without a summation transformation. At X=1,Q^(-1),...,Q^(2-k), the shifted polynomial vanishes, so the lower term is divisible by P_(k-1). At X=Q^(1-k), only the X/Q shift remains; its coefficient is (B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T), and P_k(X/Q)/P_(k-1)(X)=1-Q^(-k). The leading coefficient gives Lambda_k. Consequently the coefficients of a degree-m eigenfunction normalized to F_m(1)=1 satisfy a_(k+1)/a_k=Q(1-Q^(k-m))(1-B^2 Q^(m+k+1)) /[(1-BQ^(k+1))(1-Q^k/T)(1-Q^(k+1))]. (4) For generic parameters these eigenvalues are distinct. The degree-m normalized eigenfunction is unique, and (4), with a_0=1, gives (1). Rational continuation then proves the identity wherever defined. There is no small-channel restriction hidden in this argument. To justify the generic operator identity for a fixed arbitrary m, first take every integer source size N>=2m+1. The original generic Clebsch calculation and its sufficiently many complete physical t slices give the identity at B=Q^(-N), after clearing denominators. The cleared residual is a FIXED finite Laurent polynomial in B,Q,U,T. Write it as sum B^a p_a(Q,U,T). For N larger than its finite Q-exponent widths, the supports of Q^(-Na)p_a are disjoint. Its vanishing at all such N forces every p_a=0. Thus (3) and the actual numerator identity are formal in B,Q, and apply equally to a large m<N. The physical slice count at one fixed N is not being applied to a large partner. ## 2. The collision identity is generic Fix 0<=j<l and j+l=N-1. The eigenvalue difference factors as Lambda_l-Lambda_j =B^(-1)Q^(-l)(1-Q^(l-j))(1-B^2 Q^N). (5) On the generic hypersurface B^2 Q^N=1, the two numerator parameters of (1) for m=j are the two numerator parameters for m=l in the opposite order. In the large series the second parameter is Q^(-j), so its terms k>j vanish. Therefore, IDENTICALLY in X,T, F_l=F_j on B^2 Q^N=1. (6) Work locally near the actual primitive root Q_0, B=1, with the denominators in (1) inverted. The collision is smooth there because its B derivative is nonzero. Equation (6) gives a regular rational function R_(j,l) such that F_l-F_j=(1-B^2 Q^N) R_(j,l). (7) At even N another algebraic component of the collision can meet denominator divisors. This does not affect the stated local germ: every factor 1-BQ^r, 1<=r<N, is a unit at Q_0,B=1. The assertion does not cancel a denominator identically zero on an irrelevant component. At the actual root, (6) also proves the useful bivariate factorization H_l^1(U,V)=H_j^1(U,V) product_(r=j)^(l-1)(UV-Q_0^r). (8) This is an identity of the continued source numerator, not just an equality on the physical integer magnetic grid. ## 3. The actual generic-q normal becomes a transverse B derivative Return to B=Q^(-N), q=exp(pi i/N), Q_0=q^2, x=q^(N-1), and put Delta=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1), D=zeta d/dzeta. The actual tensor Casimir eigenvalue is lambda_m(zeta)=zeta^(2N-2m-1)+zeta^(-2N+2m+1), D(lambda_j-lambda_l)(q)=-2N Delta. The root-only expression q^(2m+1)+q^(-2m-1) has the same value but would give the WRONG derivative sign. The actual mixed compiler uses w_j=[D C_j(q)-D C_l(q)]/[-2N Delta]. (9) Along this ACTUAL generic family, D(1-B^2 Q^N)=2N at the root. Since F_l-F_j vanishes identically in X,T on the collision, the derivatives of x^u, X=zeta^(-2u), and T=zeta^(2t) do not contribute to the derivative of the difference. Equations (7),(9) give exactly w_j=x^u R_(j,l)(Q_0,1;X,T)/Delta =x^u [B partial_B(F_j-F_l)]_(Q_0,1)/(2 Delta). (10) The partial derivative in the second line holds Q,X,T fixed. This is an exact consequence of generic collision divisibility. It is NOT differentiation of the root-only identity F_l=F_j. In particular the large partner's generic normal has not been dropped. ## 4. The explicit surviving derivative tail All expressions in this section are at Q=Q_0. Put a=Q^(-j), b=Q^(-l), c_k=(a;Q)_k(b;Q)_k(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k], L_k(y)=-sum_(r=0)^(k-1) y Q^r/(1-y Q^r). For k<=j, every factor in L_k(a),L_k(b) is a unit. Differentiating (1) in B and subtracting cancels the common denominator derivative. For k>j the single vanishing numerator factor has derivative [y partial_y(y;Q)_k]_(y=Q^(-j)) =-(a;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(k-j-1). Thus the original normal is w_j=x^u/Delta * { sum_(k=0)^j c_k [L_k(b)-L_k(a)] +(a;Q)_j sum_(k=j+1)^l (b;Q)_k(Q;Q)_(k-j-1)(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k] }. (11) The second line is a nonempty tail whenever j<l. Bounded harmonic coefficients in the first line do not bound this coherent sum relative to F_j; nor do they remove the tail. Equation (11) records all of it with the original normalizer. ## 5. Genuine extra poles obstruct a whole-wedge normal theorem As a polynomial in X, w_j/x^u has EXACT degree l. Only the k=l tail term contributes its highest coefficient, which is (-1)^l Q^[l(l+1)/2] (Q^(-l);Q)_l(Q^(-j);Q)_j(Q;Q)_(l-j-1) /[Delta (Q;Q)_l^2(T^(-1);Q)_l]. (12) Its numerator is nonzero: all nonzero factorial indices are less than N, and 2j+1<N gives Delta!=0. Therefore each divisor T=Q^r, j<=r<l, (13) is a genuine SIMPLE pole of the normalized normal for generic X. The highest-coefficient residue is nonzero and cannot be canceled by lower powers of X. Its residue polynomial has degree l, so it does not vanish on an open set of magnetic coordinates. The ordinary small column F_j has no pole at any of (13). Its denominator only uses r<j. If N/2<r<l, the scaled pair degree tau=r/N lies strictly inside the joint central wedge. An open set of its central magnetic coordinates avoids the finitely many roots of the residue polynomial. Thus the actual terminating continuation of this INDIVIDUAL first normal cannot be holomorphic on that whole wedge, let alone admit a uniform relative polynomial estimate there. These additional divisors lie below the physical high-partner range t>=l. On a fixed compact tau>1/2 they disappear when j/N is sufficiently close to 1/2. Consequently (13) does not disprove a smaller corridor near the folded endpoint. It also does not prove such a corridor estimate: the tail in (11) still requires control. Finally, (13) is not a theorem about poles of the entire mixed coupon. The original inverse measure and the other terms may cancel individual-column poles. Nor does it exclude a separately specified whole-source continuation. It rules out silently extending the ordinary-column joint theorem to this canonical generic normal. Audit: [generic collision, original normal and pole certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.py). The collision calculation does not imply a smaller-corridor estimate or a pole of the full coupon.

title: Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column
status: All physical generic column and divided-pair jets
text: # Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column 30 October 2026. This note extends the physical prefix estimate to the original generic deformation. Every fixed generic-q derivative of every admissible physical column has polynomial cost relative to its nonzero root value, including large channels. The actual divided pair also has polynomial fixed generic jets. The upper half of the column is treated by its backward generic recurrence, not by differentiating a root-only reflection identity. The statement is on integer physical degrees and magnetic indices. It supplies no fixed complex magnetic neighborhood, no nonzero confluent amplitude, and no completed four-port or network norm. ## 1. The actual generic column and its endpoints Fix N>=3, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and integers 0<=m<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t. Write q=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=q^2, x=q^d, v=t-u, and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. The original finite source is C_m(q;t,u)=sum_(a=max(0,m-v))^(min(m,u)) (-1)^a x^(u-2a) Q^[av+a(a-1)/2] F_(N-m+a-1)F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-m-1)F_(N-1)) [u choose a]_Q [v choose m-a]_Q/[t choose m]_Q. (1) These are precisely the genuine generic highest-vector ratios of the [mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), not the squared-binomial formula obtained after root specialization. All factorial indices in (1) are below N. The function is regular near q0. Its endpoints are exact monomials: C_m(q;t,0)=1, C_m(q;t,t)=(-1)^m q^[dt-2Nm+m^2+m]. (2) For the second equality only a=m survives; the original ratio of F-factorials is then one. These formulas hold before differentiating. There are universal c,C>0 such that, simultaneously for all the integer indices above, C_m(q0;t,u)!=0, |C_m(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C for |epsilon|<=cN^(-8). (3) The functions in (3) are holomorphic on that disk. In particular, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C_r N^(8r)|C_m(q0;t,u)|, D=q d/dq. (4) There is no small-channel restriction on m in (3),(4). ## 2. The original generic physical Casimir block The degree-t balanced tensor basis has entries indexed by u=0,...,t. Let J_t(q) have diagonal D_u, upper entries A_u^+ and lower entries A_u^- (the superscripts refer to the matrix positions). A direct application of the original generic coproduct gives D_u=q^-1 Q^(u-t)(1-Q^(N-u))(1-Q^u) +q^(-2d-1)Q^u(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(t-u)) +q^(2d+1)Q^-t+q^(-2d-1)Q^t, (J_t)_(u,u+1)=A_u^+ =q^-N Q^(2u+1-t)(1-Q^(N-u-1))(1-Q^(t-u)), (J_t)_(u+1,u)=A_u^- =q^-N(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(u+1)), 0<=u<t. (5) For example the lower offdiagonal is the contribution of F on the first head after E on the second; the upper offdiagonal retains both Cartan factors of the opposite path. Their generic values differ. Replacing them by their equal root values before differentiating would change the source. The vector (1) satisfies J_t(q) C_m(q;t,.)=lambda_m(q) C_m(q;t,.), lambda_m=q^(2N-2m-1)+q^(-2N+2m+1). (6) This follows from its highest degree m, highest weight 2d-2m, and the original coproduct Casimir. Alternatively, substitution of the finite highest-vector and its divided descendants yields (5),(6) entry by entry. Thus the normalization C_m(0)=1 in the magnetic index fixes the SAME source vector, not an auxiliary eigenvector. At q0 the two offdiagonals in (5) coincide, and (5) simplifies to D_u=U/T [2(q0^-1+q0 T)-(q0+q0^-1)U], A_u=(U-T)(1-Q0 U)/T, U=Q0^u, T=Q0^t, Q0=q0^2. (7) For the reversal matrix P_t, (7) also gives P_t J_t(q0) P_t=conjugate(J_t(q0)). (8) Only this ROOT identity is needed below. No generic version of (8), or a flat high-degree adapter, is assumed. ## 3. A polynomial generic neighborhood from prefix coercivity The [physical prefix theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md) proves, for every 1<=h<=floor(t/2), Im J_[h](q0) >= 4 sin^3(pi/N)/h^2 * I. (9) Although that note applies the estimate to complete double channels, its weighted-row identity and positive Dirichlet proof use only 1<=t<=d and h<=floor(t/2). In this entire range the weights 1/sin((t-r)pi/N) are positive, its row residual is 4 sin(r pi/N) sin^2(pi/N) sin(t pi/N) /sin((t-r-1)pi/N)>=0, and every retained conductance is at least 4sin(pi/N). The same Poincare step therefore proves (9) for all t used here. It requires no sign assumption on -cos((t+1)pi/N) and no channel condition t>=l. The bound is independent of the real spectral parameter. Since lambda_m(q0) is real, it implies ||(lambda_m(q0)I-J_[h](q0))^-1||<=C N^5. (10) The reversed prefix has the conjugate root matrix by (8), hence has the same inverse bound. This holds for every m<=t, not merely for the two members of a double node. Every elementary exponent in (5),(6) is O(N). On a fixed disk |epsilon|<=c/N the entries and eigenvalues are O(1) and their epsilon derivatives are O(N), uniformly over all indices. The bandwidth is fixed. For either the forward or reversed prefix, ||M(epsilon)-M(0)||<=C N|epsilon|, M(epsilon)=lambda_m(q)I-J_prefix(q). (11) Combining (10),(11), on rho_N=cN^(-8) the relative perturbation has norm at most Cc/N^2. Decrease c so that it is below 1/2. For prefix size h<=N, |det M(epsilon)/det M(0)| <=(1+Cc/N^2)^h<=C, (12) and the determinant is nonzero throughout the disk. The offdiagonal products introduce only polynomial local costs. At the root |A_u^+|=|A_u^-| =4 sin((t-u)pi/N) sin((u+1)pi/N) >=4 sin^2(pi/N)>=16/N^2. (13) Equation (5) gives derivative O(N), so these entries remain nonzero on the same disk. Their relative logarithmic changes are bounded by C N^3|epsilon|. A product of at most N such entries therefore has a uniformly bounded ratio to its root value, and so does its inverse. In fact its logarithmic change is O(N^4|epsilon|). For u<=floor(t/2), the exact forward recurrence gives C_m(q;t,u)=det(lambda_m(q)I-J_[u](q)) / product_(r=0)^(u-1) A_r^+(q). (14) The empty determinant and product at u=0 are one. Equations (10)--(14) prove root nonvanishing and (3) on this half. For u>=ceil(t/2), put h=t-u and reverse the ACTUAL generic recurrence. Normalize its endpoint by the exact nonzero C_m(q;t,t) in (2). The normalized reversed column has initial entry one and is again a leading-prefix determinant divided by its own upper offdiagonal product. Its prefix has size h<=floor(t/2). Equations (8)--(13) apply to this reversed generic matrix because its ROOT is conjugate to the forward one and its generic entries satisfy the SAME bounds. The endpoint exponent in (2) is O(N^2), so its ratio on the small disk is also uniformly bounded. This proves (3) on the upper half, including t=0,1 by the endpoint formulas alone. Cauchy's formula now gives (4) for the genuine generic source. The derivative holds N,t,u fixed, as the original compiler does. ## 4. The completed divided pair also has fixed generic jets Suppose j<l, j+l=d and l<=t. Put s=l-j and define the original generic divided pair W_(j,l)(q;t,u)= (C_j(q;t,u)-C_l(q;t,u))/(lambda_j(q)-lambda_l(q)). (15) The [exact collision identity](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) gives C_j(q0;t,u)=C_l(q0;t,u), and its actual gap is lambda_j-lambda_l=(q^s-q^-s)(q^N-q^-N). (16) The second factor has a simple zero at q0; the first does not. Thus (15) has a removable singularity, with root value exactly the retained physical paired normal W_(j,l)(q0;t,u) =[D C_j-D C_l]/[-2N Delta_j], Delta_j=q0^(2j+1)-q0^(-2j-1)=q0^s-q0^-s. (17) On |epsilon|=rho_N, the first factor in (16) has modulus at least c/N and the second at least cN rho_N. There are no other zeros inside this disk. The two bounds (3), using their equal root values, therefore give |W_(j,l)(q;t,u)|<=C rho_N^-1 |C_j(q0;t,u)| on |epsilon|=rho_N. Cauchy's formula applied AFTER the removable singularity is filled proves, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r W_(j,l)(q0;t,u)| <=C_r N^[8(r+1)] |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (18) For r=0 the earlier N^6 physical paired-normal estimate is sharper. The additional content here is the higher genuine generic-q jets, including the variation of the matrix, both original columns, and the gap. Equation (18) is not obtained by treating a q derivative as a spectral derivative. For example D W at the root contains second q derivatives of the original columns, as it must. ## 5. Interface and limits The [matching-edge rewrite](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) needs Taylor order two after clearing its simple poles. Equations (4),(18) remove a possible physical-column obstruction to controlling such jets. To apply them to a completed target pair one must STILL prove its exact expression in these normalized columns, their divided pair, and its actual scalar measures. The native boundary cost of that four-port tensor has not been replaced by a polynomial in this note. Nor is a surrounding contraction estimated here. The estimates concern integer t,u. They do not prove a fixed complex magnetic corridor or control the extra poles of the large partner's unrestricted continuation. The separate shrinking-channel complex theorem and the present physical generic theorem address different domains. No lower bound for W or a nonzero selected global contribution follows from either upper estimate. Audit: [original generic physical matrix and retained divided-pair jets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.py). The focused exact audit passed 1,204 original physical column four-jets, 1,204 generic eigenvector equations, 2,408 forward/backward comparisons, 432 generic endpoint jets, and 378 divided-pair jets through order two. It retains 4,816 column and 1,134 pair coefficients; 323 tested second pair jets are nonzero. Those checks verify source and normal conventions, while the prefix perturbation proof supplies the uniform bounds. The theorem retains the integer physical domain. It gives neither a completed four-port norm nor a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood.

title: A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid
status: All physical paired first normals; complex corridor open
text: # A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. Every original physical magnetic entry of a complete double Casimir channel has a polynomially bounded confluent normal relative to its nonzero ordinary value. This includes both halves of every physical degree block, both parities, and every complete double channel. The estimate is for the ACTUAL generic divided difference. It is not an estimate obtained by differentiating a root-only formula. The argument is a positive-imaginary-part estimate for a half-prefix of the original complex symmetric Casimir matrix, followed by its exact reflection symmetry through first order at a double spectral node. No complex magnetic continuation, global magnetic contour, or whole marked-source estimate follows from this physical-grid statement. ## 1. The source and the quantitative statement Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d. Let 0<=j<l, j+l=d, l<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t, c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), Delta_j=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1). All these indices are integers. Let C_(j,u) be the original root column normalized by C_(j,0)=1. Let w_(j,u) be its actual confluent normal as specified by [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md): w_(j,u)=[D C_(j,u)-D C_(l,u)]/[-2N Delta_j], D=zeta d/dzeta, evaluated at zeta=q. (1) Both generic columns in (1) use the original highest weight d and its full factorial ratio. Then EVERY C_(j,u) is nonzero and |w_(j,u)/C_(j,u)|<=N^6/256+N^2/8. (2) If t/N stays in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), the right side can be replaced by C_K N^4. In the present complete range t>=l this only requires a fixed upper separation from t/N=1. No separation from the folded channel is required. ## 2. The actual prefix has positive imaginary part The original degree-t Casimir block J_t is complex symmetric tridiagonal, as proved directly from the balanced tensor operators in [the complete Hermite packet](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md). For r=0,...,t put U_r=Q^r, T=Q^t. Its entries simplify exactly to D_r=U_r/T [2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U_r], A_r=(U_r-T)(1-QU_r)/T, 0<=r<t. (3) Every A_r is nonzero. For 1<=m<=floor(t/2), let J_[m] be its leading m-by-m principal submatrix. Because the matrix is symmetric, its Hermitian imaginary part is the entrywise imaginary-part matrix. Set h_r=(t-2r)theta and c=-cos((t+1)theta). Its diagonal and upper offdiagonal imaginary parts, including the next boundary coefficient, are d_r=4 sin(h_r)[c+cos(theta)cos(h_r)], o_r=4 sin(h_r-theta)sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta). (4) For 0<=r<m these o_r are positive. Introduce positive weights a_r=1/sin((t-r)theta), 0<=r<=m. A direct sine expansion gives the EXACT weighted row identity d_r-o_(r-1)a_(r-1)/a_r-o_r a_(r+1)/a_r =4 sin(r theta)sin^2(theta)sin(t theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta) >=0, (5) where the r=0 term involving o_(-1) is absent. The right side is zero at r=0. All denominators in (5) are positive in the stated range. One elementary verification expands sin(b-a) and cos(a+b+theta), with a=r theta and b=(t-r)theta. After multiplying by sin(b-theta)/4, the residual is precisely sin(a)sin^2(theta)sin(a+b). Conjugate Im J_[m] by diag(1,-1,1,...), so its offdiagonals are -o_r. For a vector v write v_r=a_r y_r, and set y_m=0. Equation (5) expresses its quadratic form as sum_(r=0)^(m-1) k_r |y_r-y_(r+1)|^2 +sum_(r=0)^(m-1) V_r a_r^2 |y_r|^2, k_r=o_r a_r a_(r+1) =4 sin((t-2r-1)theta)sin((r+1)theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta), V_r=the nonnegative right side of (5). (6) There is a genuine Dirichlet term at the right endpoint; it is not discarded when the prefix is taken. The conductances obey k_r>=4 sin(theta). (7) Indeed the two numerator sine arguments alpha,beta are at least theta, with alpha+beta=(t-r)theta<pi. On the interval theta<=alpha<=alpha+beta-theta, their product is minimized at an endpoint, so sin(alpha)sin(beta)>=sin(theta) sin(alpha+beta-theta), which is (7). Since a_r<=1/sin(theta) and sum|y_r|^2<=m^2 sum|y_r-y_(r+1)|^2, equations (6),(7) prove Im J_[m] >= [4 sin^3(theta)/m^2] I. (8) The sign-conjugation is unitary and does not change this lower bound. For t/N in a fixed compact inside (0,1), all a_r in this half-prefix are uniformly bounded; the stronger lower bound is c_K/N^3. ## 3. Lower-half spectral derivatives Let f_r(z) be the original normalized forward column, f_0=1, f_r(z)=det(zI-J_[r])/(A_0 ... A_(r-1)). (9) The real point c_j is a double eigenvalue of J_t. The actual source and normal are exactly C_(j,r)=f_r(c_j), w_(j,r)=f_r'(c_j). (10) This is the generic-confluence identity in the complete Hermite packet and the mixed compiler: differentiating the two normalized generic columns cancels the common q derivative and retains the original eigenvalue-gap derivative -2N Delta_j. For ANY real z, (8) gives ||(zI-J_[m])^(-1)||<=m^2/[4 sin^3(theta)]. In particular the determinant in (9) is nonzero there. Taking its logarithmic derivative gives |f_m'(z)/f_m(z)| =|tr((zI-J_[m])^(-1))| <=m^3/[4 sin^3(theta)]. (11) Since m<=N/2 and sin(theta)>=2/N, (11) is at most N^6/256. The compact-degree improvement of (8) gives C_K N^4 instead. For m=0 the normal is zero and the value is 1. ## 4. Reflection extends the bound through the full physical block Let P reverse the indices 0,...,t. Formula (3) gives exactly P J_t P=conjugate(J_t). (12) The characteristic polynomial is p_(t+1)(z)=product_(m=0)^t(z-c_m), and the forward column satisfies (J_t-zI)f(z)=-p_(t+1)(z)e_t/(A_0 ... A_(t-1)). (13) At a double node c_j, both the residual and its first derivative vanish. Reflecting and conjugating (13), and using uniqueness of the forward recurrence with its first component fixed, therefore gives, at that node, f_(t-r)=f_t conjugate(f_r), f'_(t-r)=f'_t conjugate(f_r)+f_t conjugate(f'_r). (14) This is a first-order identity at a DOUBLE node. It is not inferred by differentiating a value identity known only at isolated points. One may justify (14) as an identity modulo (z-c_j)^2: the reflected column has first entry conjugate(f_t(conjugate z)); its first-row error is a multiple of p_(t+1)(z), so its forward recurrence agrees to this order. Setting r=t in the value identity gives |f_t|=1. The endpoint normal has a particularly simple original generic calculation. At u=t only a=m survives in the generic Clebsch sum, and its highest-vector ratio R_(m,m) is identically 1. Thus C_(m,t)(zeta)=(-1)^m zeta^[d(t-2m)+m(m-1)]. (15) The two exponents for j,l differ by N(l-j). Combining (15) with the actual gap in (1) gives f'_t(c_j)/f_t(c_j)=-(l-j)/(2 Delta_j), |f'_t/f_t|<N/[4 sin(theta)]<=N^2/8. (16) For r>t/2 apply (14) with t-r in the lower half. Its value is nonzero and f'_r/f_r=f'_t/f_t+conjugate(f'_(t-r)/f_(t-r)). (17) Equations (11),(16),(17) prove (2) for every physical entry. ## 5. Scope of the estimate The paired normal, including its formerly hidden large-channel contribution, is controlled on the entire physical grid. Its exponential rate there cannot exceed that of its ordinary column by more than O(log N)/N. This is a relative entrywise statement; it does not control cancellations after a whole graph is sewn. The high-total-degree blocks are transported by the constant Chevalley-plus-flip adapter in the complete Hermite packet. Thus the same root spectral-column estimate applies after the stated physical index translation. It is the root confluent column being transported here, not a new generic-q adapter assumed to be flat. The estimate does NOT extend by continuity to a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood. The canonical large-partner continuation has the additional degree poles proved in [the generic collision note](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md), and its finite tail requires a separate complex estimate. A bound on integer magnetic samples, even at all levels, supplies no such analytic continuation theorem. Focused audit: [original normal, positive prefix and reflection](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound_results.json). The symbolic weighted-row identity passed. Exact arithmetic checked 131 original Casimir blocks, 726 weighted-row identities, 8,578 actual generic paired normals and their first-order reflections, and 571 original endpoint normals. At 90 digits, 10,164 actual relative-normal bounds passed; the audit also checked 288 positive prefix matrices and 2,384 conductance inequalities. These finite checks supplement the uniform proof above. The high-degree adapter transports the root spectral column without assuming that an individual generic derivative is flat. The theorem is restricted to the physical grid. No complex magnetic continuation or whole-source bound is inferred.

title: Genuine numerator normals at positive-total framing boundaries
status: Actual positive-total boundary determinants and generic normals
text: # Genuine numerator normals at positive-total framing boundaries 30 October 2026. A uniform spectral gap for the SUM of the two original positive matrices controls the actual generic numerator in both the202 and222 boundary regimes. The actual total square root and every logarithmic head lift remain in the source normalization. Near the fold, all fixed genuine quantum derivatives have subexponential relative cost when the partner separation satisfies s log N=o(N). This is a numerator theorem. It does not assign a generic amplitude to a root collision or prove a global source period. The separate root222 determinant action and the root202 coefficient packet retain their own normalizations and hypotheses. ## 1. An exact uniform gap, including the folded endpoint Let theta=pi/N, N>=3, and 1<=a<=floor((N-1)/2). Use the actual Hermitian H_-,H_+ from the [source determinant](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md), with diagonal d_r=1/[cos(r theta)cos((r+1)theta)] and upper entries sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta) +/- i cos(n theta)], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. Then EXACTLY H_-+H_+ >= cos(theta) I >= I/2. (1) Here is a direct weighted-path proof. Put J=(H_-+H_+)/2 and w_r=sqrt(sin((2r+1)theta)), 0<=r<a. Alternating-sign conjugation turns its real offdiagonal e_n=sqrt(B_n)sin(n theta) negative. For an interior row r, subtracting its two weighted neighbors from the diagonal gives d_r-e_r w_(r-1)/w_r-e_(r+1)w_(r+1)/w_r = [sin(r theta)cos(r theta)/(1+sin(r theta)) +sin((r+1)theta)cos((r+1)theta) /(1+sin((r+1)theta))] /sin((2r+1)theta) >= cos(theta)/2. (2) For the equality, use sin((2r+1)theta)=sin(r theta)cos((r+1)theta) +sin((r+1)theta)cos(r theta). For the inequality, bound both denominators 1+sin by 2 and use sin(r theta)cos(r theta)+sin((r+1)theta)cos((r+1)theta) =sin((2r+1)theta)cos(theta). The r=0 formula has its left term zero. At the final row r=a-1, subtracting the finite positive quantity sin^2(a theta)/[cos(a theta)sin((2a-1)theta)] from the ACTUAL one-neighbor residual gives exactly the expression in (2). Thus that actual residual is larger. This last comparison does not introduce a virtual B_a or w_a: at the maximal odd fold those separate quantities would be singular or zero. All weights and coefficients actually used in the matrix are positive. For a=1 the same finite comparison applies with no actual neighbor. Finally, for x_r=w_r y_r the quadratic form is the sum of e_n w_(n-1)w_n |y_n-y_(n-1)|^2 and the weighted residual diagonal terms. Thus (2) proves J>=cos(theta)I/2 and hence (1). No limiting matrix or unproved eigenvalue asymptotic is used. ## 2. The actual total phase and the two boundary domains Fix the actual logarithmic heads sigma,u and put, GENERICALLY, q=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=q^2, B=Q^-N, U=q^(2u), V=q^(2(sigma-u)), b=q^sigma, X=qU, Y=qV, T=XY=q^2UV, w=qb=q^(sigma+1), z=b/U. In particular T=w^2 and z/w=1/X exactly. The square root w is the original exponential, not a freely chosen branch. At the root, the exact normalized source is H_n^1(U,V)=(qUV)^n K_n det M_n, M_n=X^-1 I-H_-/2-H_+/(2T), (3) where K_n=[2n choose n]_Q for the small channel n and the matrices are its n-row truncations. Indeed the original monic determinant is R_n(z)=det[zI-(wH_-+w^-1H_+)/2]; divide its matrix by w and use H_n=b^n K_n R_n. Thus the factor w^n, including its sign and every integer logarithmic character, is retained in (qUV)^n. For physical half-index heads write X=exp(2pi i x), Y=exp(2pi i y), sigma=N(x+y)-1. Then w=exp(pi i(x+y)) exactly. On the canonical physical logarithms, when T is positive and both arguments lie strictly between 0 and 2pi, their sum is 2pi and w is the NEGATIVE square root of T. The same sign persists in that marked neighborhood. If another actual integral lift changes this sign, (3) retains the change; none of the estimates below replaces it by the canonical sign. Let T at epsilon=0 range in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of a compact subset of (0,infinity). Two domains are allowed: * 202: X/N^2 belongs to a fixed compact subset of C*. * 222: X belongs to a fixed compact neighborhood of a negative real compact subset of C*. Require the marked heads to satisfy |sigma|+|u|<=C N(1+log N). These are conditions on the actual arguments, not on an arbitrarily reset logarithm. In202, Y=T/X is small; in222 both raw finite clocks are near negative reals. The [actual prefix-sign theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md) supplies precisely these limiting signs where its dictionary applies. For all sufficiently large N, on both domains the matrix in (3) satisfies Re(-M_n)>=cI, ||M_n^-1||<=C, (4) uniformly for all small n through the fold. Indeed Re(1/T)>=eta>0, and (1) bounds H_-+eta H_+ below by a fixed positive multiple of I. For202 the term 1/X is O(N^-2), so it cannot close that gap. For222, Re(1/X)<0 adds a positive diagonal term. Thus the root numerator is nonzero. This proof retains the additive identity term and does not infer an inverse bound from positivity alone. ## 3. A genuine generic disk and its cofactor The all-degree original generic recurrence, with B=Q^-N retained, is R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). Its coefficients and rational all-degree proof are in the [actual paired-normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md). Here the generic scalar is K_n(q)=(B^2Q^(n+1);Q)_n/(BQ;Q)_n, whose root value is the Gaussian binomial in (3). Its generic derivatives are not those of that root simplification. Set G_n=R_n/w^n. As exact generic identities, G_(n+1)=(X^-1+alpha_n/w)G_n+(beta_n/w^2)G_(n-1), H_n^B(U,V)=(qUV)^n K_n G_n. (5) For n<=a the nonzero original spectral differences are bounded below by cN^-2 on a small polynomial disk. Here b and w are bounded above and away from zero; their derivatives have size O(N log N). The quotient formulas for alpha_n,beta_n therefore give (alpha_n/w)'=O(N^5(1+log N)), (beta_n/w^2)'=O(N^7(1+log N)). (6) The original b_n,d_n in those formulas are O(1), with derivatives O(N(1+log N)); the preceding u_n and v_n have sizes O(N^2),O(N^4). This gives (6) directly, with no generic specialization of a root reflection. The derivative of X^-1 is no larger than O(N log N) in either domain and is smaller in202. For each edge of the actual root matrix M_a, freeze whichever of its upper and lower entries has larger absolute value. Their SUM is -sqrt(B_n)sin(n theta)(1+T^-1). Since sqrt(B_n)>=1/2 and |1+T^-1| is bounded below, the frozen entry has absolute value at least c/N for every n=1,...,a-1. The first bound follows directly from sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)<=sin^2(2n theta) and the displayed formula for B_n. Keep it in its original orientation and put the other generic entry equal to -beta_n/(w^2 frozen_entry). The diagonal is X^-1+alpha_n/w. At the root this is exactly M_a, with all edge phases intact. At generic q its determinant and every leading principal minor are exactly the recurrence in (5), since each adjacent product is the original one. No constant choice of upper versus lower is required, and no parameter-dependent similarity is silently dropped. By (6) this generic matrix differs from its root by O(N^8(1+log N)|epsilon|) in operator norm. Choose |epsilon|<=rho_N=cN^-10. (7) Equations (4),(6) give uniformly bounded inverse and two-sided determinant ratio. Indeed the logarithm of the determinant ratio costs at most O(N^9(1+log N)rho_N), which is bounded and tends to zero. The last diagonal inverse entry is the actual cofactor, so |G_(a-1)/G_a|<=C. (8) The exact source scalar K_a has logarithmic derivative O(N^3), and (qUV)^a has logarithmic derivative O(N^2(1+log N)). Their two-sided ratios are bounded on (7). Thus the small H_a itself has bounded two-sided relative variation on this disk. ## 4. The actual large partner and every fixed normal Let m=d-a, s=m-a, with 0<=s<=eta N and eta sufficiently small. The literal root identity is H_m^1=P_s(UV)H_a^1, where P_s(UV)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). Since UV=q0^-2T is near a positive real compact and these r lie near N/2, every added factor is bounded above and away from zero. In particular H_m^1 is nonzero. On the boundary of (7), the original folded spectral differences are at least c rho_N; all others are at least cN^-2. The original generic recurrence coefficients alpha_n/w and beta_n/w^2 are therefore at most C rho_N^-1 and C rho_N^-2. Starting from (8), propagating the s rows costs at most (CN^20)^s. The exact generic K_m/K_a ratio has 2s numerator factors and 2s denominator factors. Those denominator indices stay near N/2, so the ratio costs only C^s. The factor (qUV)^s also costs C^s relative to the retained root P_s(UV). Thus on the circle, and then throughout its disk, |H_m^B(U(q),V(q))/H_m^1(U(q0),V(q0))| <=C(CN^20)^s. (9) The passage inside uses the original finite H_m sum: all its generic factorial denominators have indices below N and are units on this disk. Singular monic R_m factors were never assigned a holomorphic root value. Cauchy's formula now gives, for each fixed k, |partial_epsilon^k H_m^B|_0 <=C_k N^(10k)(CN^20)^s |H_m^1(U(q0),V(q0))|. (10) For s=0 this follows directly from the small determinant argument. For bounded s the cost is polynomial, covering both maximal folded parities. For s log N=o(N) it is subexponential. This does not cover a fixed nonzero scaled partner separation and does not give a nonzero leading normal amplitude. The source factor (qUV)^n, the integer characters and every marked head are retained before taking the derivative. The result applies to the individual actual202/222 numerator factors. Any surrounding white monomials, cups, pivots, marks and finite support cycles must still use their literal source identities and their own estimates. Neither the positive gap nor finite-jet control selects the original global relative period. Focused audit: [positive-total source and retained-normal checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals_results.json). The 120-digit run checks both exact trigonometric identities, 389 actual weighted rows including 24 finite last-row comparisons, 24 folded matrix gaps, 12 original root phase/determinant identities, 48 original generic determinants and 48 cofactors, 48 actual large-partner generic-circle values and 24 first/second normals. Four cases have one root edge EXACTLY zero and retain the opposite edge. Twelve tests keep identical root clocks but change sigma to sigma+N; their genuine first normals differ, verifying why marked lifts cannot be reset. Maximum source error was below 3.3e-119. These finite checks supplement the proof; they do not establish its uniform estimates by numerical sampling. The result remains the stated individual-numerator, shrinking-channel normal bound; no leading normal amplitude, whole-network contraction estimate or global relative-cycle coefficient is inferred.

title: The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary
status: Original resonant boundary packets and retained source zeros
text: # The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary 30 October 2026. The actual prefix words give an explicit degeneration of the original white arguments when the residual framing parameter tends to infinity. One of its large-clock regimes has a uniform, source-normalized Bessel limit.
