The numerator is the actual LARGE generic-channel numerator specialized at the root; neither a scalar symbol nor an off-lattice channel is substituted. This is a local root-value boundary model. Genuine quantum normals are separate. It neither puts every box in this regime nor computes the coefficient of the geometric component in the original global period. ## 1. Actual prefix words determine the escaping heads Normalize the reference positive meridian to J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and keep the original common framing F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], with s nonzero. For every actual based prefix Q=[[a,b],[c,d]] put L_Q(r)=Tr(Q F E11 F^-1) =-c r^2/s+(a-d+c/s)r+d+b s. (1) These are the actual prefix diagonals. On a fixed horizontal cut the physical clock of its i-th wire is X_i=-L_(Q_(i-1))/L_(Q_i). No independent local frame is chosen. For the complete discrete faithful holonomy, each prefix is either genuinely quadratic in (1), or constant. Indeed c=0 implies a=d=+/-1. To see this directly, conjugating J by Q supplies translations a^(2n). If |a^2| differs from one these accumulate at the identity. If |a^2|=1, the discrete additive group generated by these translations has rank at most two; rotations preserving it form a finite group. Thus a^2 is a root of unity. If a^2 is not one, the upper triangular Q has finite projective order, contrary to the free deck action. Consequently Q=+/-[[1,b0],[0,1]], whose L_Q is constant. This argument uses actual holonomy words, not arbitrary matrices assigned to ports. Fix s so all the finitely many constant L_Q are nonzero. Let e(Q)=0 in this constant case and e(Q)=1 in the quadratic case. At r=N rho, with rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, X_i=C_i(s) r^k_i (1+O(1/r)), k_i=2(e(Q_(i-1))-e(Q_i)) in {-2,0,2}. (2) For two quadratic prefixes the limiting ratio is the ratio of their lower-left entries, with the displayed minus sign. These are actual geometric limiting data. They are not independently optimized. The k_i obey the homogeneous original cup/cap/coupon incidence equations, since the exact products of the corresponding clocks do. Thus the logarithmic escape is one coupled integral flow. On a cut, each run of quadratic prefixes has paired -2/+2 boundary transitions. The exact finite affine offsets have a uniform convenient realization. If X_i=exp(2pi i x_i) with the recorded logarithmic lift, set i_i=N x_i-1/2, Q_N^(i_i)=q_N^-1 X_i. (3) This prescription applies to the PHYSICAL V_d heads. It gives every physical cup/cap i_1+i_2=N-1 and q_N^(d-2i_i)=-1/X_i. At a white vertex define the channel row by its original equation r0=i_1+i_2-(d-a), with the actual discrete a retained. An auxiliary V_(2a) head is not assigned the same universal -1/2 offset. Its finite color is equivalently (a+1/2)/N. Thus degree constraints remain exact, but this is not evaluation of every finite channel at the complete parabolic stationary point. It samples the principal geometric germ without asserting finite-N stationary equations. For k_i!=0, the imaginary index has size N log N. For X_i=1+zeta/r+O(r^-2), instead, i_i=zeta/(2pi i rho)-1/2+O(N^-1), (4) up to its retained integer logarithmic lift. The -1/2 is essential. A point near a negative half-integer is not an original integer support zero. An O(1/N) perturbation of a clock near one must not be discarded. The same caution applies to characters: exp(2pi i i_i)=-X_i^N. (5) Its magnitude need not be one, and can be N^(2N) in (2). ## 2. The literal white, dual and exceptional arguments At a circle write a0=L_W, a1=L_(AW), a1'=L_(Aout W), a2=L_(PW), where P=BA=Bout Aout and W is its original prefix. Its incoming geometric clocks are U=-a0/a1, V=-a1/a2, T=UV=a0/a2, (6) and the output replaces a1 by a1'. By the actual generic white formula, the numerator is H_m^B(q_N^-1 U,q_N^-1 V), with m=d-a, B=Q^-N. The channel a remains the actual discrete integer. For prefix degrees (deg a0,deg a1,deg a2), the root arguments have the following orders; the factors q_N^-1 in (3) remain in each entry. | Degrees | U | V | T | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 000 | finite | finite | finite | | 002 | finite | r^-2 | r^-2 | | 020 | r^-2 | r^2 | finite | | 022 | r^-2 | finite | r^-2 | | 200 | r^2 | finite | r^2 | | 202 | r^2 | r^-2 | finite | | 220 | finite | r^2 | r^2 | | 222 | finite | finite | finite | Here "finite" means a nonzero limit, which can still meet a further chart divisor, including one. For the original complete-circle boxes, 000 and 020 are impossible: a0 and a2 constant would make P preserve the reference main cusp, although P is a nontrivial longitude of a different, auxiliary cusp. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint small horoballs and cannot have the same center. For routed crossing bands one must retain all eight rows unless that extra hypothesis is proved. There is no implicit Hermitian adjoint. The literal pi dual uses the reversed complementary indices (d-j,d-i). The exact Chevalley identity W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r0) =zeta^[(d-2a)(a-r0)] W_a(i,j;r0) (7) reduces it to the incoming white with its actual scalar retained. Alternatively its two raw H arguments are the reversed reciprocals Q^d/Q^j,Q^d/Q^i. All routing spectra and their paired partners remain. For the exceptional inverse turn retain its actual coordinates h=v-u, ell=t-v, sigma=d-h, r0=a-h. Its two numerator pairs are exactly (Q^(sigma-u),Q^u), (Q^ell,Q^(sigma-ell)). (8) With physical half-index sampling these are the original outgoing and incoming pairs in (6), respectively. The moving factorial arguments are r0,2a-r0 in the channel cup and v,d-v,ell,d-ell in the inverse physical cups; ordinary pi has the analogous original complemented indices. This specifies their whole marked logarithmic lifts. The specified generic exceptional lift has root character exp(-2pi i v). Restoring the original physical turn contributes the inverse exp(2pi i v), exactly as in the [source lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md), equation (13). They cancel BEFORE an estimate. Bounding them separately at (2) could introduce artificial N log N growth. None of this proves uniform asymptotics for the listed moving factorials or numerators. ## 3. A uniform original-root packet when the first clock is large Put Q=exp(2pi i/N), and keep an actual integer m with delta <= mu=m/N <= 1-delta, delta>0. At the root the exact polynomial is H_m^1(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) product_(j<m-k)(V-Q^j), c_k=(-1)^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q^2. (9) This includes the actual large m=d-a. Suppose U=N^2 kappa_N, V=V_N, where kappa_N and V_N range in fixed compact subsets of C*. Keep the EXACT last Newton term E_N=c_m (UV)^m product_(j<m)(1-Q^j/U), c_m=(-1)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2]. (10) It is nonzero for large N. Define the entire function Bessel(K)=sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l/(l!)^2 =J_0(2sqrt(K)), K_N=sin^2(pi mu)(V_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa_N V_N). (11) The series, not a square-root branch, defines the notation. Uniformly on those compacts, H_m^1(U,V)/E_N=Bessel(K_N)+O(N^-1). (12) In particular U=N^2 kappa(1+O(N^-1)), V=V0+O(N^-1) gives the same formula with K=sin^2(pi mu)(V0-1)/(pi^2 kappa V0). The finite m/N, the phase c_m, and the product in (10) have not been discarded. Equation (12) is an absolute normalized estimate. A relative packet is asserted only on a compact set where Bessel(K) is nonzero. Here is a proof retaining the WHOLE finite polynomial. Set k=m-l. The exact ratio of that summand to (10) is (-1)^l Q^[-ml+l(l-1)/2] [m choose l]_Q^2 * (UV)^(-l) product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) /product_(j=m-l)^(m-1)(1-Q^j/U). (13) For j<=m<=(1-delta)N, |1-Q^j|>=c_delta j/N. Consequently |[m choose l]_Q|<=(C_delta N)^l/l! for EVERY l<=m. The denominator in (13) has inverse bounded independently of N,l, since |U|>=cN^2. Thus every term is bounded by C^l/(l!)^2. This proves uniform summable tail domination, not just convergence of the fixed-l terms. For fixed l, expand the exact Gaussian products. The identity exp(-2pi i mu)(1-exp(2pi i mu))^2/(-2pi i)^2 =sin^2(pi mu)/pi^2 gives precisely (-K_N)^l/(l!)^2. Uniformly for l<=N^(1/4), the product expansion has absolute error at most C^l(1+l)^C/[N(l!)^2]. This follows by expanding each of the l numerator and denominator factors; their relative errors are O(l/N), while product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) is compared in absolute value if V=1. The factorial bound makes the remaining tail smaller than every power of N. Summing proves (12). ## 4. A geometric transition with an explicit nonzero model Consider a 200 box whose second raw puncture is the reference B=-J. Then Q1=AW=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q2=BQ1, epsilon=+/-1. Write A21=c_A. The actual complete disk relation Tr(BA)=-2 and Tr A=-2 give c_A=4. Since W=A^-1Q1, its lower-left entry is -epsilon c_A. Substituting (1),(6), at r=N rho gives kappa=Q0_21 rho^2/[s L_Q1], V0=-L_Q1/L_Q2, K=sin^2(pi mu) s^2/(4pi^2 rho^2). (14) The q_N^-1 argument corrections are included in the O(N^-1) allowed in (12). They were not dropped in (4), where their size is decisive. The inverse orientation B=-J^-1 gives the same squared expression. In the actual first-slot Fourier convention eta_j=Q^j and p=eta_j^-1, the resonant scale for each fixed nonzero integer j is r=1/(1-exp(-2pi i j/N))-beta s, rho -> 1/(2pi i j). Hence this local boundary factor tends Bessel(-j^2 s^2 sin^2(pi mu)) =I_0(2j s sin(pi mu)). (15) For Re s!=0 it is nonzero. An elementary proof avoids a zero theorem: if I_0(z)=0, f(t)=I_0(zt) obeys (t f')'=z^2 t f, f(0)=1, f'(0)=0,f(1)=0. Integration against conjugate f gives z^2 integral_0^1 t|f|^2=-integral_0^1 t|f'|^2<0. Thus z is purely imaginary. The ordinary regular framing exclusions remove finitely many s values; Re s!=0 can also be imposed wherever that first-cut frame is legitimately varied. In particular on the legitimate real interior first-cut slice A_cut=exp(2pi i alpha), 0<alpha<1, one has s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 and Re s=cos(2pi alpha)-1<0. The local nonvanishing condition is therefore automatic on that slice, after its other regular exclusions. This is not a proof that an arbitrary selected global frame path reaches every required box in the 200 regime. The j=0 node is the exact resonance r=infinity, not an additional finite rho value. No uniform result in growing j or across all eight regimes is claimed. In particular 202 leaves a nontrivial whole boundary polynomial in T; it does not reduce to the last term in (10). ## 5. The paired small-second-clock endpoint The 002 regime has an equally direct original-source proof; it does not use an unrecorded interchange of the two physical legs. Let V=kappa_N/N^2, U=U_N, E_N^0=product_(j<m)(V-Q^j), K_N^0=kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(1-U_N)/pi^2, (16) where kappa_N,U_N lie in fixed compact subsets of C*. Then H_m^1(U,V)/E_N^0=Bessel(K_N^0)+O(N^-1). (17) The EXACT ratio of its kth Newton term to E_N^0 is c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) /product_(j=m-k)^(m-1)(V-Q^j). (18) The denominator product differs from (-1)^k Q^[mk-k(k+1)/2] by a relative O(k/N^2), uniformly for k<=m. Together with the same Gaussian bound as before, this gives C^k/(k!)^2 domination for EVERY k. Its fixed-k limit is [kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(U_N-1)/pi^2]^k/(k!)^2. The product-error argument in section 3, including absolute comparison when U_N=1, proves the uniform O(N^-1) remainder. Both the exact phase and the full endpoint product are retained in (16),(18). For a genuine 002 disk with first puncture A=-J write Q0=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q1=AQ0 and Q2=BQ1. The complete trace relation gives B21=4. Substitution into (1),(6) now gives U0=(1+b s)/(1+(b+1)s), kappa=s(1+(b+1)s)/(4rho^2), K^0=sin^2(pi mu)s^2/(4pi^2rho^2). (19) Thus the same fixed-Fourier I0 factor and its legitimate real first-cut nonvanishing apply. The exact physical argument shifts q_N^-1 change U0,kappa by the permitted O(N^-1); the actual endpoint product is still kept. This proves paired 200/002 models, not the unproved reduction of 022/220 or 202 to either one. ## 6. The mixed 202 boundary retains a whole positive polynomial Put V=T/U and define the exact boundary polynomial A_b(T)=(-1)^b Q^[b(b-1)/2] P_b(QT), P_b(w)=sum_(k=0)^b beta(b,k)^2 w^k, beta(b,k)=s_b/[s_k s_(b-k)]. (20) Termwise in (9), A_b is the limit as U tends to infinity with T fixed. For the actual small channel a<=floor((N-1)/2), P_a is precisely the two-binomial polynomial Q_a^(a,a) in the [proved negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md). Its roots are negative real and simple. Retain this whole polynomial; it is not a replacement by its largest coefficient. If U=N^2 kappa with kappa in a fixed compact subset of C*, and T in a fixed compact subset of C minus (-infinity,0], then H_a^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T)(1+O(N^-1)), (21) uniformly in the actual discrete a. There is no lower bound on the distance of a/N from zero needed for this statement. For the ACTUAL large channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity gives H_m^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r)(1+O(N^-1)). (22) The forced unit-arc factors in (22) are displayed, including their zeros. At such a zero both sides are zero exactly. No generic normal is inferred by differentiating this root collision identity. Here is a uniform relative proof, including complex cancellation. After taking out its exact phase, H_a is sum_(k=0)^a beta(a,k)^2(QT)^k product_(r<k)(1-Q^r/U) product_(r<a-k)(1-(T/U)Q^-r). (23) Expand BOTH correction products by the finite quantum binomial identity, proved by multiplying their linear factors. The term of degree i in the first is a polynomial in Q^k proportional to U^-i product_(r<i)(1-Q^(k-r))/(Q;Q)_i; the degree-j term in the second is proportional to (T/U)^j product_(r<j)(1-Q^(-a+k+r)) /(Q^-1;Q^-1)_j. (24) The omitted factors in (24) have modulus one. These identities hold also when i>k or j>a-k: the corresponding numerator contains zero. Therefore expanding (24) gives an EXACT finite linear combination of A_a(Q^hT), with 0<=h<=i+j. Since i,j<=a<N/2, the sum of absolute coefficients of this combination is at most (C/N)^(i+j)/(i!j!). (25) Indeed |(Q;Q)_i|>=(c/N)^i i!, and each numerator polynomial in Q^k has coefficient sum at most 2^i; the second factor is identical. The i=j=0 term is exactly A_a(T). Write P_a(w)=C_a product_l(w+rho_l), rho_l>0. On the indicated compact T domain, w=QT remains a fixed distance in angle from the negative ray for large N. For 0<=h<=cN, choose c small enough so the rotation from QT to Q^(h+1)T remains in this domain. The bound |w P_a'(w)/P_a(w)|<=C a then gives |A_a(Q^hT)/A_a(T)|<=exp(C h). For EVERY other h one still has the crude bound exp(CN), by applying (|w|+rho)/|w+rho|<=C to each root. Sum (25) first over 1<=i+j<=cN; the exp(C h) factor leaves O(N^-1). For i+j>cN, the factorial tail in (25), even multiplied by exp(CN), is smaller than every inverse power of N. This proves (21) without replacing a complex sum by its positive envelope. The original root identity H_m=H_a product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r) proves (22). For the ACTUAL right-angled matching-polyhedron source, the 202 condition gives a useful geometric certificate: T_infinity is POSITIVE. Use precisely the literal white-reflection prefixes proved in [the original cut dictionary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3: Q_i=r_(F_i)r_(F_ref). The exterior first-slot reference white face F_ref contains the fixed point p of the original marked main meridian. The 202 middle prefix is upper triangular and fixes p. Thus r_(F_1)r_(F_ref)(p)=p and r_(F_ref)(p)=p force r_(F_1)(p)=p. In other words p lies on the MIDDLE white circle. This is a consequence of the actual common prefix, not a new local framing choice. In the recorded disk coordinate eta that circle has diameter [0,1]. Its puncture lifts and product are A=-[[1,0],[2,1]], B=-[[3,-2],[2,-1]], P=BA=-[[1,2],[0,1]]. (26) Writing eta0 for p and conjugating by [[0,-1],[1,-eta0]] sends p to infinity. Direct multiplication gives A21=-2 eta0^2 and B21=-2(eta0-1)^2. Since Q1 is upper triangular, Q0=A^-1 Q1 and Q2=B Q1 have leading lower-left ratio T_infinity=-A21/B21=-eta0^2/(eta0-1)^2>0. (27) Indeed eta0/(eta0-1) is purely imaginary on that circle. The two outer prefixes are genuinely quadratic, so eta0 is neither 0 nor 1; the positive value is finite and nonzero. Therefore the actual T=T_infinity+O(1/N) at r=N rho lies in a fixed compact subset of the domain of (21). This applies with every retained half twist, since the proved outside white-reflection prefixes are unchanged. The certificate requires this actual right-angled cut and its marked first-slot reference. It is not asserted for arbitrary routed 202 crossings lacking that dictionary. No basing or reference meridian is changed. The 022/220 boundary polynomials still require their separate source treatment, and no global contributing cycle follows from (27). The full matched source still needs its original boundary current, remaining factors, normal extraction and selected relative cycle. The local nonzero Bessel factor proves none of their noncancellation. Focused audit: [original coefficients, marked prefix signs and boundary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 9 exact geometric identities, all 8 incidence patterns, 72 literal-source comparisons, 72 endpoint packets, 24 mixed-boundary identities and 24 complex relative 202 packets. These are focused checks of the proof, not a global-period experiment. The root-value results do not imply a generic-normal or global-cycle statement.

title: The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action
text: # The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action 30 October 2026. The negative-root theorem gives an asymptotic for the ACTUAL local Fourier sum, including its cancellation. The normalized logarithm converges on the entire slit plane to the analytic continuation of its positive real variational action. In the right half-plane this selects a nondegenerate internal saddle with its original logarithms. This is a local leading-order theorem at both level parities. It does not give a complete amplitude expansion, a uniform generic-q normal, or a noncancellation theorem for the assembled plat source. ## 1. The exact finite polynomial and its logarithm Use the original coefficients of the [phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md): P_N(w)=sum_a E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a) w^a, E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), a0_N=max(0,u_N-t_N+j_N), a1_N=min(j_N,u_N). Here 0<=j_N<=t_N<N and 0<=u_N<=t_N. Every beta is the positive sine binomial at theta=pi/N. No fitted scalar or knot value enters this definition. The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) proves the exact factorization P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0_N product_(r=1)^(a1_N-a0_N) (w+rho_(N,r))/(1+rho_(N,r)), rho_(N,r)>0. (1) Consequently on Omega=C minus (-infinity,0] the actual polynomial has a unique holomorphic logarithm that is real at w=1. Define L_N(w)=Log(P_N(w))/N. (2) This is a specified logarithm, not the principal argument of a possibly many-times-wound numerical value. Its real part is always log|P_N(w)|/N, independent of that qualification. ## 2. The real variational problem is strict Suppose (t_N,j_N,u_N)/N -> (tau,xi,upsilon), 0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau. (3) Set a0=max(0,upsilon-tau+xi), a1=min(xi,upsilon), and use J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, B(v,a)=J(v)-J(a)-J(v-a), Ecal(alpha)=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). The interval (a0,a1) is nonempty. For every real w>0 the function Ecal(alpha)+alpha log w has a unique interior maximum, denoted alpha(w), and write its value as psi(w). Its derivative is Ecal'(alpha)=log[sin^2(pi(xi-alpha)) sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / (sin^2(pi alpha) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha)))]. The derivative tends to +infinity at a0 and -infinity at a1. Its second derivative is strictly negative: Ecal''=-pi{2[cot(pi(xi-alpha))+cot(pi alpha)] +cot(pi(upsilon-alpha)) +cot(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))}<0. (4) For the sign, the first paired arguments sum to pi xi in (0,pi); the second pair sums to pi(tau-xi) in (0,pi). Apply cot A+cot B=sin(A+B)/(sin A sin B). All displayed individual arguments lie in (0,pi) on the support interior. Uniform sine-factorial estimates give log E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a)=N Ecal_N(a/N)+O(log N), over the ENTIRE finite support; Ecal_N uses the actual scaled parameters. The support is an interval of the full integer lattice. An upper bound by its largest term and a lower bound by a nearest lattice point to the unique maximizer therefore prove L_N(w) -> psi(w), w>0. (5) The argument is uniform when (3) ranges over a compact subset of its strict domain and w ranges over a compact positive interval. Factorial endpoints are included in the upper bound; none is silently removed before taking the maximum. ## 3. Negative roots prove the complex limit For each compact K in Omega, sup_(w in K,rho>=0) |Log((w+rho)/(1+rho))| < infinity. (6) Indeed (w+rho)/(1+rho) is on the segment between w and 1. Its modulus stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly on K, and its argument stays on the single branch between Arg w and zero. Equivalently compactify rho by rho/(1+rho) in [0,1]. The same bound applies to Log w. Since a1_N<N, (1) implies that L_N(w)-L_N(1) is locally uniformly bounded on Omega. Equation (5) bounds L_N(1). Cauchy estimates and subsequence compactness now give holomorphic subsequential limits, uniformly on compact subsets. All such limits agree on the positive real axis by (5); the identity theorem makes them identical on the connected slit plane. Thus the WHOLE sequence converges: L_N(w) -> psi_hol(w), locally uniformly on Omega. (7) All complex derivatives converge locally uniformly as well. This proves existence and uniqueness of the analytic continuation in (7), instead of assuming that an arbitrary algebraic saddle has that role. The same subsequence argument proves uniformity for compact strict parameter families in (3): any proposed failure has a convergent parameter subsequence, to which the preceding proof applies. Continuity of psi_hol in those parameters follows by the same compactness and positive-axis uniqueness argument. Only elementary compactness for holomorphic functions is used here: Cauchy estimates give equicontinuity on a compact exhaustion; successive subsequences converge there, and the real-axis values determine their unique holomorphic limit. No contour replacement of the finite source or unproved saddle coefficient is inserted. ## 4. A positive root measure fixes the branch Put alpha_hol(w)=w psi_hol'(w). Differentiating (1) yields w L_N'(w)=a0_N/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_(N,r)). (8) The measures (1/N)sum_r delta_rho have total mass tending to a1-a0. Compactify their domain by adjoining zero and infinity. Any weak limit mu obeys alpha_hol(w)=a0+integral w/(w+rho) dmu(rho). (9) For real w, the envelope derivative of the strict maximum gives alpha_hol(w)=alpha(w). The barrier equation shows alpha(w)->a0 as w decreases to zero and alpha(w)->a1 as w increases to infinity. Thus mu has no mass at zero or infinity and has total mass a1-a0 on (0,infinity). Formula (9), rather than a chosen ordering of quadratic roots, specifies the actual selected branch. For Im w>0 its imaginary part is strictly positive. If additionally Re w>=0 and w!=0, then a0<Re alpha_hol(w)<a1. (10) For (10), each integrand w/(w+rho) has real part strictly between zero and one. At positive real w, alpha_hol is the original real interior maximum. Along the physical first-quadrant arc all four sine arguments in (4) stay nonzero: their imaginary parts are nonzero away from the positive real axis, and their real-axis initial values lie in the support interior. More explicitly, (10) keeps each argument in the vertical strip 0<Re s<1. There Re(sin(pi s))>0, so its logarithm has one analytic branch agreeing with the positive real logarithm. The saddle equation therefore continues there without an arbitrary logarithm reset: Ecal'(alpha_hol(w))+Log w=0. (11) It is nondegenerate throughout that quadrant. In fact alpha_hol'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu(rho) never vanishes there. For 0<=Arg w<pi/2 the integrands lie in an open angular sector of width less than pi; at Arg w=pi/2 each has strictly negative imaginary part. Their positive integral is nonzero. Differentiating (11) gives Ecal''(alpha_hol(w))=-1/[w alpha_hol'(w)] !=0. (12) Thus on the physical arc psi_hol is exactly the continued critical value Ecal(alpha_hol)+alpha_hol Log w, with its positive-axis normalization. This conclusion concerns the leading logarithm. It does not by itself compute a Gaussian prefactor or an error O(1/N). ## 5. Consequence for every actual complete-circle column On a complete-circle channel, the exact column is f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))=(-1)^u_N q^[-(j_N+1)u_N] P_N(q^delta_N), delta_N=t_N+j_N-(N-1). If (3) holds and xi<=1/2, tau+xi>=1, then q^delta_N -> w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)], 0<=Arg w_star<=pi/2. Equation (7) supplies the actual, cancellation-sensitive limit lim_N (1/N)log|f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))| =Re psi_hol(w_star). (13) Both level parities and all composite levels are included. The explicit unit prefactor gives the unwrapped leading complex phase psi_hol(w_star)+pi i(upsilon-xi upsilon) in the compiler's convention. At the folded endpoint xi=1/2 this selects the actual local branch of its previously derived quadratic. The high physical degree block uses its already proved exact index translation, so (13) applies there in those translated variables too. For comparison, negative roots give the finite bound cos(phi/2)^(a1_N-a0_N) P_N(1) <= |P_N(exp(i phi))| <= P_N(1), |phi|<pi. (14) The lower factor can be EXPONENTIAL in N. It is not a polynomial normalization loss. Formula (13) determines that cancellation rate through the selected analytic action instead of dropping it. This does not yet control cancellations among different magnetic or channel states in a whole plat, the mixed-color aliases, the original generic first normals, or the selected global geometric period. Those remain necessary for the general long-filling volume equality. Audit: [actual Fourier columns and selected complex action](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.py). The analytic proof above is uniform; finite numerical checks only verify the formula conventions and the selected continuation. The selected-complex-action theorem retains its actual logarithmic sheets and the stated global and amplitude limitations. The real magnetic-parameter theorem does not imply a complex global-source packet.

title: Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals
status: Polynomial fixed generic derivatives; small channels
text: # Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals 30 October 2026. This note concerns the original generic highest-weight N-1 columns, including the factors that simplify only at the root of unity. On compact subsets of the joint central wedge, every fixed generic-q derivative of a small-channel column has at most polynomial cost relative to that column's root value. The estimate includes the folded small channel and both parities. It does not bound the paired large-channel derivative, the confluent spectral normal formed from both channels, or the whole marked source. ## 1. The exact generic deformation Fix N>=3, d=N-1 and q0=exp(pi i/N). Let q vary near q0; put Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), A=B^(-1), x=q^d, t=u+v, U=Q^u, V=Q^v, T=UV, s=q^t, D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). All complex powers use log(q)=pi i/N+epsilon. Gaussian binomials and Pochhammer products below have base Q. Define H_j^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [j choose a]_Q (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<j-a)(V-Q^r), C_j(q;t,u)=x^u H_j^B(U,V)/D_j(T), S_j^B(U,T)=U^j H_j^B(U,T/U). (1) This is the actual generic column in [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, at physical t,u. It also specifies a finite rational continuation for complex t,u. To check the source before differentiating, its highest-vector ratio is exactly R_(j,a)=(Q^(N-j);Q)_a/(Q^(N-a);Q)_a =Q^[a(a-j)] (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a. (2) Converting the three Gaussian binomials in that compiler into finite Newton products gives (1). In particular the additional factor is B^a times the displayed Pochhammer ratio. Merely inserting a power of -q^(-N) into the root-only squared-binomial formula would give the wrong generic source and the wrong first derivative. The exact leading scalar is S_j^B(0,T)=T^j K_j, K_j=(B^2 Q^(j+1);Q)_j/(BQ;Q)_j. (3) Here is an elementary proof of the finite identity used in (3). For generic a,c,Q and integer n>=0, sum_(k=0)^n (Q^(-n);Q)_k (a;Q)_k / [(Q;Q)_k(c;Q)_k] (c Q^n/a)^k =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (4) Multiply both sides by a^n(c;Q)_n. Each side is a polynomial of degree at most n in a. At a=c Q^m, 0<=m<n, the quotient (a;Q)_k/(c;Q)_k=(c Q^k;Q)_m/(c;Q)_m is a polynomial in Q^k of degree m. For each of its powers Q^(rk), r<=m, the finite binomial sum on the left is (Q^(r-m);Q)_n=0. Thus the left polynomial has all the n roots of product_(r<n)(a-cQ^r). Its constant term, from k=n alone, is (-1)^n c^n Q^[n(n-1)/2], fixing the multiplier to 1. This proves (4) as a rational identity. Taking n=j, a=B^(-1)Q^(-j), c=BQ gives (3), after converting (Q^(-j);Q)_a to the Gaussian binomial. No asymptotic identity is used here. ## 2. The generic Casimir polynomial and its three-term recurrence The exact equation for S=S_j^B is Q^(-j)(QU-A)(U-T) S(QU,T) +Q^j(BQT-U)(1-U) S(U/Q,T) +[(1+A)U+QT(1+B)U-(1+Q)U^2 -T(AQ^(-j)+BQ^(j+1))]S(U,T)=0. (5) It follows from the actual generic coproduct Casimir, whose column eigenvalue is q^(2N-1-2j)+q^(-2N+1+2j). Alternatively, one can verify its extension from physical columns by exactly the finite degree argument used for the root equation in [the joint determinant note](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). The residual has degree at most j+1 in U: the top degree cancels; its constant coefficient also vanishes. At each original complete slice t=d-j,...,d, its original t+1 column values and U=0 force the whole U polynomial to vanish. The residual has degree at most j+1 in T. These j+1 slices, together with T=0, force its vanishing identically. At T=0 use S(U,0)=(-1)^j Q^[j(j-1)/2]U^j; the residual cancels directly. This proves (5) in a neighborhood of the actual root, where all these finite source columns and distinct slice values are defined. Let R_n(z) be the monic reverse polynomial obtained from (1): R_n(z)=z^n S_n^B(s/z,s^2)/(s^(2n)K_n). Equation (5) says L R_n=Lambda_n R_n for the triangular operator L z^n=Lambda_n z^n+b_n z^(n-1)+d_n z^(n-2), Lambda_n=AQ^(-n)+BQ^(n+1), b_n=[(1+A)+Qs^2(1+B)-Q^(-n)(Qs^2+A) -Q^n(BQs^2+1)]/s, d_n=Q^(1-n)+Q^n-1-Q. (6) Terms with negative powers are absent, since b_0=d_0=d_1=0. Write the two coefficients below the leading one as u_n,v_n. Their exact expressions are u_0=0, u_n=b_n/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1)), n>=1, v_0=v_1=0, v_n=(b_(n-1)u_n+d_n)/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2)), n>=2. For 0<=n<j, put alpha_n=u_(n+1)-u_n, beta_n=v_(n+1)-v_n-alpha_n u_n (n>=1). Then exactly R_0=1, R_1=z+alpha_0, R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). (7) For completeness, a finite moment argument rules out extra lower terms in (7). Set mu_0=1, mu_(-1)=0 and impose (BQ^(r+1)-A)mu_r +[(Qs^2+A)-(BQs^2+1)Q^r]mu_(r-1)/s +(Q^r-Q)mu_(r-2)=0, 1<=r<=2j-1. (8) The difference of the two monomial pairings for L factors as (Q^n-Q^m)Q^(-n-m) times (8) at r=m+n. Thus L is symmetric for this finite moment functional. Its eigenvalues of degrees 0,...,j are distinct near the root. The usual finite orthogonality argument now kills the terms below R_(n-1) in zR_n-R_(n+1); the top two coefficients give (7). This argument can first be made at generic s, where the preceding norms do not vanish: the norm recursion is h_n=-beta_n h_(n-1). At B=1 the beta_n are the nonzero polynomials in c displayed below, so generic nonvanishing follows inductively. Rational continuation then proves (7) also when a particular beta_n vanishes. No positive generic moment functional is assumed. Combining (1),(3) gives the exact normalized source C_j=x^u q^(jt) K_j R_j(q^t/U)/D_j(Q^t). (9) All the generic coefficients in this section retain B=Q^(-N). Equation (7) is not a deformation chosen after specialization. ## 3. A uniformly controlled generic neighborhood Let W be the joint wedge 1/2<Re(t/N)<1, |2Re(u/N)-Re(t/N)|<1/2. For every compact K contained in W there are constants c_K,C_K>0, independent of N and 0<=j<=floor((N-1)/2), such that |C_j(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_j(q0;t,u)|<=C_K whenever |epsilon|<=c_K N^(-8), (t/N,u/N) in K. (10) In particular the denominator on the left is nonzero. The power 8 is a convenient conservative bound; no optimal power is claimed. Here are explicit estimates proving the assertion. At epsilon=0, put theta=pi/N, c=-cos((t+1)theta), z=q0^(t-2u). On a fixed K, Re c and Re z have positive lower bounds for all sufficiently large N. The root recurrence (7) is alpha_n=c/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], beta_n=Bcal_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2], Bcal_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. Thus its determinant is M_0=zI+cD+Kskew, with the actual positive D and real skew matrix Kskew in the joint determinant note. Accretivity gives ||M_0^(-1)||<=1/Re z, uniformly in the channel, including the fold. Construct the generic tridiagonal matrix M_epsilon with diagonal z(q)+alpha_n(q). Freeze its upper entries to their ROOT values r_n=sqrt(Bcal_n)[c+cos(n theta)], 1<=n<j, and use lower entries -beta_n(q)/r_n. Its determinant is R_j by (7), and at epsilon=0 it is exactly M_0. There is no square-root choice for the generic beta_n. Since sqrt(Bcal_n)>=1/2 and Re c is uniformly positive, |r_n| is bounded below independently of N. The only spectral differences in (6),(7) factor as Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1) =(1-Q)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n)), Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2) =(1-Q^2)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n-1)). (11) At the root their nonzero factors give lower bounds c/N^2 for all required n<=j. All elementary exponents have size O(N), so these bounds persist in a disk |epsilon|<=c N^(-3). On a smaller such disk, direct differentiation of (6),(7) gives uniformly |u_n|=O(N^2), |u_n'|=O(N^5), |v_n|=O(N^4), |v_n'|=O(N^7), |alpha_n'|=O(N^5), |beta_n'|=O(N^7). (12) Here primes mean d/d epsilon. The coefficients b_n,d_n,Lambda_n are O(1), with derivatives O(N); (12) follows by the quotient rule and (11). Consequently the tridiagonal operator norm satisfies ||M_epsilon-M_0||<=C_K N^7 |epsilon|. On the disk in (10), ||M_0^(-1)(M_epsilon-M_0)||<=C_K c_K/N. Choose c_K small. The determinant ratio is bounded by (1+C_K c_K/N)^j, and hence uniformly bounded; it is also nonzero. The remaining scalar factors in (9) have controlled ratios on the same disk. The exponents of x^u q^(jt) have size O(N^2). Each root factor of K_j has size at least c/N, its derivative is O(N), and there are O(N) factors; thus |(log K_j)'|=O(N^3). The factors of D_j(Q^t) are separated uniformly from zero on K, so its logarithmic derivative is O(N^2). Integration over the N^(-8) disk bounds all these scalar ratios. This proves (10). Finitely many remaining N can be absorbed by changing constants; j=0 follows immediately from C_0=x^u. ## 4. Consequence for actual generic derivatives, and its limit Cauchy's estimate applied to the exact source in (10) gives, for every fixed integer m>=0, |(q d/dq)^m C_j(q0;t,u)| <=C_(K,m) N^(8m) |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (13) The derivative holds t,u,N fixed, exactly as the original generic compiler does. At physical integer t,u it is its actual generic normal; at complex t,u it is the derivative of the finite source continuation (1). Combining (13) with the proved joint root-value amplitude preserves its leading exponential action, as an upper bound, for these fixed-order small-channel derivatives. The mixed compiler's confluent column is proportional to D C_j-D C_(N-1-j). Except at the simple folded endpoint, its second term is a LARGE channel. In that channel K_l vanishes at the root and the monic recurrence crosses resonant eigenvalue differences. The argument above does not apply. In particular (13) is not a bound for that difference, its spectral derivative, a complete mixed kernel, or a generic normal of the whole pointed invariant. Focused audit: [actual generic values and normals](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals_results.json). It passed 1,304 original generic value-and-derivative comparisons, 216 generic determinant identities, 216 generic Casimir identities, 216 Vandermonde value-and-derivative identities, and 1,041 original root-normal comparisons in exact finite-field dual arithmetic. At 100 digits, 48 nonphysical generic comparisons and 24 original root-normal comparisons passed; 96 points on the stated polynomial disk were also sampled. The disk samples are regressions, not the proof of uniform control. The result is restricted to the stated small-channel domain and fixed-t,u Cauchy derivative convention. The paired large channel is excluded.

title: A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column
text: # A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column Subsequent extension: [joint pair-degree and magnetic amplitudes](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) are now proved on a central complex domain, using the original finite kernel and an exact accretive determinant. The present theorem and its proof retain the real-parameter hypothesis stated below. 30 October 2026. The original finite q-Hahn polynomial has a full leading asymptotic, with a specified nonzero amplitude and relative error O(1/N), uniformly on compact subsets of the right half-plane. Its magnetic parameters are the ACTUAL scaled integers, varying in a compact strict REAL parameter set. No rate of convergence of those parameters is assumed. The proof starts with the previously proved actual logarithmic limit, then uses the exact finite difference equation to improve its error. A positive real Gaussian sum fixes the actual multiplicative constant. Thus the transport equation below describes the original polynomial, not merely a formal solution with an unspecified connection coefficient. This theorem does not interpolate the discrete magnetic parameters holomorphically, take a generic-q first normal, or control the assembled global magnetic/channel sum. ## 1. Original finite source and theorem Let 0<=j<=t<N, 0<=u<=t, v=t-u, theta=pi/N, and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2 sin(r theta), beta(n,a)=s_n/(s_a s_(n-a)), E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j), P_N(w)=sum_(a=a0)^a1 E_a w^a, a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u). (1) These are exactly the coefficients of the [original complete-circle phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). Put lambda_N=(tau,xi,upsilon)=(t/N,j/N,u/N), D={0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau}. All uniform statements below take lambda_N in a fixed compact subset K of D. In particular all saddles at w=1 stay a uniform distance from the factorial boundaries, even when the two descriptions of a support endpoint exchange at upsilon=xi or upsilon+xi=tau. Use the original energy J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, Bcal(b,a)=J(b)-J(a)-J(b-a), Ecal_lambda(alpha)=Bcal(xi,alpha)+Bcal(upsilon,alpha) +Bcal(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-Bcal(tau,xi). For positive real w, let alpha_lambda(w) be the unique interior maximum of Ecal_lambda(alpha)+alpha log w. The [selected complex action theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) continues both alpha and its critical value psi_lambda holomorphically to Re w>0, with psi_lambda(w)=Ecal_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) +alpha_lambda(w) Log w, w psi_lambda'(w)=alpha_lambda(w). (2) All logarithms continue from their real values at w=1. Define, with derivatives in the variable s, A_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi s) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+s)), B_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi(xi-s)) sin(pi(upsilon-s)), F_lambda(s,w)=A_lambda(s)-w B_lambda(s), C_lambda=(sin(pi xi)/2) sqrt[sin(pi upsilon) sin(pi(tau-upsilon)) sin(pi(tau-xi))/sin(pi tau)]. The root selected in (2) satisfies F_lambda(alpha,w)=0. Define Acal_lambda(w)=sqrt(2 pi) C_lambda /sqrt[B_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) F_(lambda,s)(alpha_lambda(w),w)]. (3) The square root is the holomorphic continuation of its positive real value at w=1. It is well-defined and never zero on Re w>0. **Theorem.** Uniformly for lambda_N in K and w in any compact subset of Re w>0, P_N(w)=N^(-1/2) Acal_(lambda_N)(w) exp[N psi_(lambda_N)(w)] (1+O(N^(-1))). (4) The relative error is holomorphic in w. On smaller compact subsets each fixed number of its w derivatives is O(N^(-1)) as well. Formula (4) uses the actual lambda_N, not an arbitrarily chosen limiting triple. Replacing lambda_N by its limit without controlling the displacement would in general change the leading exponential and the amplitude. ## 2. Exact finite difference equation, including endpoints Let D_w=w d/dw and h=1/N. The coefficient ratio in (1) gives the exact identity sin^2(pi h D_w) sin(pi h(D_w+v-j)) P_N(w) =w sin^2(pi h(j-D_w)) sin(pi h(u-D_w)) P_N(w). (5) For every supported a, its coefficient equation is sin^2(a theta) sin((v-j+a)theta) E_a =sin^2((j-a+1)theta) sin((u-a+1)theta) E_(a-1). At the lower endpoint either a=0 or v-j+a=0. At the first integer above the upper endpoint either j-a+1=0 or u-a+1=0. Thus the zero coefficients outside the support satisfy the SAME equation; there is no endpoint source term in (5). In functional calculus notation, [A_lambda(h D_w)-w B_lambda(h D_w)]P_N=0. (6) Every sine product in (6) is a finite linear combination of the four shifts w -> exp(i pi k h)w, k=-3,-1,1,3. In particular (6) is an exact finite-shift identity, not an infinite differential expansion. ## 3. Uniform simplicity and the actual derivative bootstrap The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) gives positive rho_r and P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0 product_r (w+rho_r)/(1+rho_r). It fixes a holomorphic Log P_N real at w=1. Put G_N(w)=Log P_N(w)/N, a_N(w)=D_w G_N(w). The actual leading-limit theorem proves a_N-alpha_(lambda_N) -> 0 (7) uniformly on larger compact subsets of the right half-plane, also when the real parameters vary in K. Fixed w derivatives converge there too. Alternatively the explicit expression a_N=a0/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_r) directly bounds every fixed derivative on those compact subsets. These bounds are independent of the positions of the negative roots. For completeness, the selected branch is uniformly simple here. Its positive limiting root measure gives alpha_lambda'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu_lambda(rho). For Re w>0 the integrands lie in an angular sector of width less than pi, so their positive integral cannot vanish. Its measure has positive mass strictly between zero and infinity. The support-strip property of alpha makes A and B nonzero. Differentiating its saddle equation gives F_s(alpha,w) D_w alpha=w B(alpha)=A(alpha), Ecal''(alpha)=-F_s(alpha,w)/A(alpha). (8) Consequently F_s is nonzero. Continuity in the real parameters and compactness make its modulus bounded away from zero on each of the sets used below. Complex conjugation supplies the same statement in the lower right quadrant. Fix nested compact neighborhoods within Re w>0. For each fixed c=i pi k, k in {-3,-1,1,3}, all small shifts stay in the larger one. Taylor's theorem along the short logarithmic segment, using the uniform derivative bounds, yields P_N(exp(c h)w)/P_N(w) =exp(c a_N(w)) [1+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N(w)+O(h^2)]. (9) Indeed the exponent before exponentiating is N[G_N(exp(c h)w)-G_N(w)] =c a_N+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N+O(h^2). This is an estimate for the actual polynomial ratios. Inserting all four shifts into (6), with their exact sine coefficients, proves 0=F(a_N,w)+(h/2)(D_w a_N) F_ss(a_N,w)+O(h^2). (10) Equation (7) and the uniformly simple zero first imply a_N-alpha=O(h). To justify this improvement, use the uniform expansion F(a_N,w)=F_s(alpha,w)(a_N-alpha)+O(|a_N-alpha|^2), absorb the quadratic term using (7), and use boundedness of D_w a_N in (10). Cauchy's estimate on a slightly larger compact set then gives D_w a_N-D_w alpha=O(h) and the analogous estimate for every fixed further derivative. Substitution back into (10) now proves the sharper actual estimate a_N=alpha-(h/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w) +O(h^2). (11) The order h^2 remainder is justified by the first improvement and Cauchy, not assumed as a WKB ansatz. Differentiating (3) and using (8) gives the exact transport identity D_w log Acal_lambda =-(1/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w). (12) For example, differentiate log(B(alpha)F_s(alpha,w)). Its two extra terms cancel: (B'/B)D_w alpha+w F_sw/F_s =(B'/B)(wB/F_s)-wB'/F_s=0. Thus (11) identifies the logarithmic derivative of the ACTUAL source with the explicit amplitude to error O(h^2). ## 4. The real sum fixes the constant, with arbitrary lattice offset On a compact interior subinterval the sine-factorial estimate is s_n=sqrt[2N sin(pi n/N)] exp[N J(n/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). One elementary derivation subtracts log x from log(2 sin pi x), applies the trapezoidal estimate to the resulting smooth function, and applies the usual integral remainder estimate for log(n!). The errors and their required finite derivatives are uniform away from 0 and 1. Applied to every factor of (1), this gives E_a=N^(-1) C_lambda /sqrt[A_lambda(a/N)B_lambda(a/N)] exp[N Ecal_lambda(a/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). (13) The positive real saddle alpha=alpha_lambda(1) stays uniformly inside the support. Strict concavity and the global factorial O(log N) bound give an exponential loss outside a fixed saddle neighborhood. Inside that neighborhood put z=(a-N alpha)/sqrt N. Taylor expansion of the phase and the smooth prefactor in (13) gives a Gaussian times H(alpha)+N^(-1/2)[H'(alpha)z +H(alpha)Ecal'''(alpha)z^3/6] +O(N^(-1)(1+|z|^8)), with a uniformly integrable Gaussian majorant; one may first restrict |z|<=N^(1/20), whose complementary tails are exponentially small. Here H=C_lambda/sqrt(AB). The term of order N^(-1/2) is ODD. No arithmetic assumption about N alpha is needed. For any shifted grid h_Z(Z+eta), h_Z=N^(-1/2), and a smooth Gaussian times a fixed polynomial f, the centered-cell Taylor formula gives |h_Z sum_(n in Z) f(h_Z(n+eta))-integral_R f| <= (h_Z^2/8) integral_R |f''|. (14) The bound is independent of eta: integrate the Taylor remainder over each cell centered at its grid point, then sum the disjoint cells. The same estimate applies to the odd term, whose integral is zero. Hence the arbitrary fractional saddle offset introduces an error O(N^(-1)), not an uncontrolled O(N^(-1/2)) correction. Gaussian tails allow the finite interval to be replaced by that whole translated grid. The resulting ACTUAL positive sum is P_N(1)=N^(-1/2) [sqrt(2 pi) C_lambda /sqrt(A(alpha)B(alpha)(-Ecal''(alpha)))] exp[N psi_lambda(1)](1+O(N^(-1))). By (8), A(-Ecal'')=F_s, so the bracket is precisely Acal_lambda(1). This proves the real normalization in (4), uniformly in lambda_N. ## 5. Integrating the proved derivative error The function H_N=Log P_N-N psi_(lambda_N)+(1/2)log N-log Acal_(lambda_N) uses the branches fixed at w=1. Sections 3 and 4 prove D_w H_N=O(N^(-1)), H_N(1)=O(N^(-1)). Join 1 to each w in a chosen compact subset of Re w>0 by its straight segment. The union of these segments is a compact set bounded away from zero and the imaginary axis. A slightly larger compact set supplies all the preceding derivative estimates. Integrating H_N' on those bounded-length segments proves H_N=O(N^(-1)) uniformly. Exponentiation proves (4). Cauchy's estimate on nested compact sets then proves the asserted relative derivative bounds. This is where both inputs are essential: negative roots gave the actual leading selection and bounded holomorphic derivatives, while the positive real sum fixed the multiplicative constant left open by the finite difference equation. ## 6. The original physical column and both integer offsets In the complete-circle chamber the exact compiler uses f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] P_N(q^delta), q=exp(pi i/N), delta=t+j-(N-1). Let w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. Then q^delta=w_star exp(pi i/N). Keeping both occurrences of +1, formula (4) gives f_u(c_j)=N^(-1/2) Acal_(lambda_N)(w_star) exp[pi i(alpha_(lambda_N)(w_star)-upsilon)] exp{N[psi_(lambda_N)(w_star) +pi i upsilon(1-xi)]} (1+O(N^(-1))). (15) In detail, moving w_star to w_star exp(pi i/N) contributes exp(pi i alpha)(1+O(N^(-1))), while q^[-(j+1)u] contributes the otherwise easily lost factor exp(-pi i upsilon). For actual complete-circle channels xi<=1/2 and tau+xi>=1-1/N. On a fixed strict compact parameter set tau<1, these w_star and their exact shifted values stay in a compact right-half-plane set. Thus (15) holds at both level parities, at the folded endpoint, and at composite levels. The high physical degree block inherits the formula by its already proved exact index translation, with the same transported column convention. The scope is a single ACTUAL local column, with real magnetic indices. Nothing here selects a global magnetic integration cycle, proves cancellation bounds for the assembled plat, or differentiates the root formula in the generic-q normal direction. Audit: [finite equation, amplitude, and physical offsets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.py). The finite computations test conventions and the predicted error; the all-level uniform statement is proved by (5)--(14). The magnetic parameter remains strictly real. No assembled-source conclusion follows from the local complex-amplitude theorem. The theorem does not extend to complex magnetic parameters or an assembled-source asymptotic.

title: Actual middle-Pachner saturation with its compulsory source current
text: # Actual middle-Pachner saturation with its compulsory source current 28 October 2026. The literal middle five-point crossing identity has an exact ordered version of the polynomial which removes the spurious cleared Pachner component. It holds on the original finite heads with their missing arrow retained. The ordinary commutative polynomial is not zero as an actual sourced operator: its error is an explicitly retained commutator current. A two-component source presentation keeps this current by polynomial, invertible row and column operations. This is a local exact source relation, applicable inside any original word and to all formal normal coefficients. It is not an estimate on all analytic endpoints of the scalar period, nor a proof of its nonzero geometric coefficient. In particular, no exponential estimate on the inverse of a face frame is asserted. ## 1. The actual middle faces Use the complete original heads and conventions of the [literal middle identity](literal_middle_full_phi_certificate.md): Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x_c=-q^(-1), S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x_c^N mu, X=x_c S_2 S_1^(-1), Z=Z_1, XZ=QZX, X^N=Z^N=1. The cyclic heads have the required opposite wrap when N is even. Let E_0 be the original first-clock projector onto index zero. Thus E_0(1-Z)=0. The actual nilpotent crossing argument and its fifth clock are n=(Q-Z^(-1))X, P=P(n), H=P^(-1)ZP=Z(1-n)=Z+(1-QZ)X, H^N=1, where P is the finite Euler polynomial of the original crossing. Only H is inverted below. It is an actual clock unit; neither 1-Z nor E_0 nor another nilpotent face wall is inverted. For the present Pachner coordinates put x=1-X, y=1-Z, w=xy, H=1-w, K=X(1-E_0), u=1-KH^(-1), v=1-ZH^(-1). (1) The equality H=1-(1-X)(1-Z) follows from XZ=QZX. These are the specified actual middle faces after the required quad changes, not independently chosen shapes. Indeed the developed cut argument in the literal middle identity is QK, and its ratio is r=QKH^(-1). Consequently u=1-Q^(-1)r, v=-Q^(-1)n(1-Q^(-1)n)^(-1). (2) The latter follows by conjugating n with Z. Thus the Q-shift and the nilpotent quad inverse are explicit. At a commutative regular symbol, (1) gives exactly w=xy, u=x(1-y)/(1-w), v=y(1-x)/(1-w), (3) the rational Pachner map in the [saturated critical compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md). ## 2. The finite wall and an ordered saturation theorem The right-cleared graph equations of (1) are EXACTLY uH-x+w=XE_0=:E, vH-y+w=0, E y=XE_0(1-Z)=0. (4) The first wall E is retained. It is not zero, and it cannot be deleted inside an arbitrary original word. It is the same missing arrow seen in the literal middle certificate, in its present orientation. Define the bounded-degree ordered polynomial g_q=uv-u w v+u w+w v-w. (5) Then g_q=0 (6) as an actual finite operator, for every N and every nonzero typed wrap mu. The proof only uses (4) and that H=1-w is a unit: g_q H=(w+uH)(w+vH)-w =(x+E)y-xy =E y=0. (7) In the first equality H commutes with w; no other factors are commuted. Cancelling H is valid since H^(-1)=H^(N-1) here. Equation (7) is a source-level replacement for dividing the commutative cleared equations by a vanishing determinant. Its wall is killed by its actual adjacent face y, rather than discarded. There is also a representation-independent version. In any unital algebra, choose X,Z,E_0 satisfying E_0(1-Z)=0 and assume H=1-(1-X)(1-Z) is a unit. Definitions (1) then satisfy (4)--(7), without a q-commutation or a cyclic-power hypothesis. The root representation establishes the required unit for the actual crossing, while this universal form proves the normal-jet result below. ## 3. Why the classical polynomial alone changes the source Choose the ordering of the ordinary saturated polynomial to be g_bare=uv-w(1-u)(1-v), C=[u,w]. Expansion without any commutations gives g_q=g_bare+C(1-v), g_bare=-C(1-v). (8) Thus for ANY input psi, output functional Lambda and original exterior operators A,B, including all other heads, Lambda(A g_bare B psi) =-Lambda(A C(1-v) B psi). (9) This uses exactly the same exterior/source on both sides. No Hopf-invariance of the inserted coupon is assumed and no cut is relocated. Tensoring by identities and applying any original closure, framing, peripheral scalar or divided co-source preserves the equality. The current is compulsory even for the smallest actual cup. At N=2, Q=-1, x_c=i, with the original balanced ordered basis, take S_1=[[0,1],[1,0]], S_2=[[0,-1],[1,0]], X=i S_1 tensor S_2, Z=diag(1,-1) tensor I, p=(0,-2i,2,0)^t, m=(1,i,1,i)/4. These are the original cup and full marker, with mp=1. Direct exact calculation gives m g_bare p=1, m C(1-v)p=-1. (10) The audit also inserts both sides of (9) at an interior position of the original figure-eight braid, retaining both original pivotal closures and the original averaged first cut. They cancel there exactly. The test does not replace that cut by a highest entry after the inserted nonintertwining coupon. In particular, (6) does not authorize imposing g_bare=0 in the actual coupon algebra. That would contradict (10) and the already proved [faithful-source obstruction](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md). A commutator current may cost powers of the semiclassical parameter while retaining the full exponential rate. No smaller exponential rate is claimed for the right side of (9). There is a stronger, fixed-degree description of this current on the actual q-torus. The cut K satisfies KZ=QZK, H=Z+K-KZ. The second identity uses XE_0(1-Z)=0, so it retains precisely the same physical missing arrow. Expanding the commutator gives [K,H]=(Q-1)(1-K)ZK, C=[u,w]=[K,H]H^(-1) =(Q-1)(1-K)Z(1-u). Substitute K=(1-u)H and Z=(1-v)H. The result is the exact bounded-degree polynomial identity C=(Q-1) Pi, Pi=[1-(1-u)H](1-v)H(1-u), g_bare=-(Q-1) Pi(1-v), H=1-w. (10a) In particular the right side contains no clock projector, no inverse of H, and no polynomial degree growing with N. This is stronger than relying on an unspecified principal-symbol rule for commutators. It gives an explicit integral quantum correction to the classical saturated equation. Formally setting H=0 in this polynomial face relation gives u+v=1, even before setting Q=1; thus the spurious cleared point w=1,u=v=i fails the retained quantum boundary relation too. The fixed-factor assertion in (10a) requires KZ=QZK. It is not asserted for arbitrary off-torus normal perturbations from Section 5. The more general ordered relation (6), current equation (8), and source extension below hold for those perturbations as stated. When a formal q-torus family does retain KZ=QZK, (10a) also holds over that parameter ring. No claim of a small operator norm follows from a fixed-degree expression in possibly large face operators. ## 4. An exact polynomial source-current presentation The relation can be retained as an explicit finite extension. Put K_sat=[[g_bare, C], [-(1-v), I]], U=[[I,-C],[0,I]], V=[[I,0],[1-v,I]]. Then the exact ordered matrix identity is U K_sat V=diag(0,I). (11) Both U and V have polynomial unipotent inverses. There is no face localization or division by a quantum scalar in (11); on the actual q-torus its upper-right entry is explicitly (Q-1)Pi from (10a). Its solutions are precisely psi_ext=(psi,eta), eta=(1-v)psi, K_sat psi_ext=0. (12) The original source is embedded by (12), and the original co-source is Lambda_ext=(Lambda,0), so that Lambda_ext psi_ext=Lambda psi. (13) The second copy is a retained current variable, not a new summation weight chosen to change the invariant. Eliminating that copy by the unit block gives the exact quantum relation (6), not the false classical relation g_bare=0. Conversely, deleting the current copy without this elimination loses (10). This construction works on each specified local state in a whole word. For a sequence of L local uses, retain the actual time states and append eta_j=(1-v_j)psi_j at the j-th position. There is one current copy per use. The block eliminations (11) act in their own constraint rows and remove these copies successively; the physical state transitions and their original endpoint functional are unchanged. This is a linear-size constraint/source extension for arbitrary bridge count. It is not a quotient or a semisimplification of the original full coupon algebra. ## 5. All normal coefficients and the limited leading consequence Let R be any formal parameter ring, for example the joint formal meridian and quantum-normal ring. Suppose X_R,Z_R and E_(0,R) deform the actual matrices with E_(0,R)(1-Z_R)=0. Since the constant term of H_R=1-(1-X_R)(1-Z_R) is invertible, H_R has a unique formal inverse by the finite-coefficient Neumann construction. Apply the universal algebra proof after (7). Thus (6), (8), and (11)--(13) hold over R, to ALL normal orders. Every original exterior/source and any defined residue or divided coefficient functional may be applied coefficientwise to (9). This does not assume that an auxiliary off-root Euler completion is the original crossing; those two objects have a known quantum normal discrepancy. Nor does it identify the quantum-normal filtration with the meridian-normal filtration. The claim is the stated universal zero insertion for the actual deformed coordinates where defined; the geometric face interpretation in Sections 1--2 was established on the physical root family. In a commutative leading-symbol chart compatible with multiplication for these actual face operators, with Q tending to one, the fixed polynomial correction in (10a) has zero leading symbol. Equation (6) then imposes uv-w(1-u)(1-v)=0. (14) It imposes this bounded-degree relation without having to invert the leading value of H. For example the false cleared point x=y=w=1,u=v=i has (14) equal to -1+2i and cannot be such a commutative leading face character. This is a formal support statement, conditional only on having that multiplicative symbol chart. It does not construct a uniform symbol chart at every singular scalar endpoint. The missing analytic step is specific. One still has to prove that all exponentially relevant pieces of the original relative cycle admit such a compatible source/current reduction, or bound the remaining pieces directly. The exact current in (9) can have the same exponential rate as the underlying period; neither local unimodular equivalence nor the classical saturation certificate proves it negligible. Likewise this one literal middle-port calculation does not supply all first/third-port identifications with a global positive triangulation. No volume lower bound or global geometric intersection is inferred. ## 6. Reproducible audit Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_quantum_pachner_saturation.py The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_quantum_pachner_saturation.py) checks 24 actual level/wrap families (N=2 through 9), the retained wall (4), ordered relation (6), nonzero bare relation, the polynomial source extension, fixed-degree divisibility (10a), five normal coefficients under off-torus perturbations, and four original whole figure-eight closures. It also checks (10) exactly over Q(i), independently of finite fields. The adjacent JSON records the outputs. These computations audit the universal proofs; finite coverage is not used as their proof.

title: The original source is a tame nilpotent extension, not a positive trace
text: # The original source is a tame nilpotent extension, not a positive trace 28 October 2026. There is a universal, source-specific obstruction to obtaining geometric nonvanishing from an ordinary faithful positive trace on the actual root quantum-group category. Its tensor-closing map sends the identity to zero but a canonical nilpotent cup/cap to the identity. This holds at every level and can be inserted into ANY original knot cut without changing its value. The source extension is polynomially tame in the actual flat metric. Consequently this is not an obstruction to a later geometric norm comparison or emergent positive integral. It rules out deriving that comparison just from positivity/unitarity of the original categorical trace, or from a positive semisimplification which discards its jets. ## 1. Keep the actual turns and boundary projector Put N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and x=-q^(-1). Use the original balanced factorial basis w_a. The actual pivot is g_a=x^(1-N)Q^(-a), sum_a g_a=0, |g_a|=1. (1) At this color the dual color x^(-1)Q^(-1) equals x. The exact actual turns in [the bridge-source proof](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) give the cup column p and right-cap row l on V_N tensor V_N: p_(i,j)=N x^(-j) delta_(i+j,d), l_(i,j)=x^j g_i/N delta_(i+j,d). (2) These retain the actual N, 1/N and pivot, rather than rescaling the turns to obtain a desired state. Define Pi_N=p l. Then l p=sum_i g_i=0, Pi_N^2=0, rank Pi_N=1. (3) The original pivotal partial closing is Phi_N(T)=Tr_2[T(I tensor g)]. (4) By direct evaluation of (2), Phi_N(I_(N^2))=0, Phi_N(Pi_N)=I_N. (5) For the second identity the only retained diagonal term has j=d-i; its coefficient is g_i g_(d-i)=1, using x^2=Q^(-1). The actual snake normalization is therefore fixed. No zero quantum dimension is divided out and no full peripheral multiplier is replaced by its root value. On the open cut retain its original e=psi phi, psi_i=1, phi_i=1/N. Thus e is an orthogonal rank-one projector in this flat metric. Define the actual two-head scalar functional Lambda_N(T)=Tr[e Phi_N(T)]. It has the exact values Lambda_N(I)=0, Lambda_N(Pi_N)=1. (6) The positive open-cut functional Tr(e C) has not been replaced. The failure of positivity is at the compulsory pivotal tensor-closing map Phi_N, before that boundary functional is applied. ## 2. No positive realization of that closing map or full source Suppose Phi_N were positive as a linear map between operator algebras with ANY positive definite Hermitian metrics. Every positive A obeys 0<=A<=r I for some r. Positivity and Phi_N(I)=0 then force 0<=Phi_N(A)<=0. This proves that no change of positive head metric makes the SAME original pivotal closing a positive map. The argument does not assume the flat metric, a particular knot or an asymptotic expansion. Similarly no positive functional on a unital star algebra can have both values in (6). Cauchy--Schwarz gives |tau(a)|^2<=tau(I) tau(a^*a)=0 if tau(I)=0. It would vanish on every a. Therefore the restriction of Lambda_N to the unital actual intertwiner algebra cannot be a positive state or trace for any involution respecting that algebra. This makes Pi_N a CENTRAL nilpotent in the quantum-group intertwiner algebra. Every positive star realization of a finite-dimensional algebra kills a central nilpotent: its image commutes with its adjoint, hence is a normal nilpotent and is zero. Equivalently Cauchy--Schwarz iterated on the nilpotent selfadjoint Pi_N^* Pi_N proves its positive functional vanishes. This applies even if the corner's identity has nonzero trace. Equation (7) is the retained actual confluence, proved in [the meridian Casimir-source theorem](meridian_casimir_source.md), not an assumed property of an abstract quantum topology construction. Thus a positive reduced spectral quotient cannot preserve (6). It must retain a source/normal extension outside that ordinary quotient. ## 3. This obstruction is functorial for EVERY original knot For ANY finite cut matrix C, not only a scalar intertwiner, linearity of the partial closing and (5) give Phi_N[(C tensor I)Pi_N]=C, Lambda_N[(C tensor I)Pi_N]=Tr(e C). (8) In particular let C_K be the actual cut operator of a knot with its specified crossings, pivots and framing convention. Its original external line chi_N is retained, so its scalar is P_(K,N)=chi_N Tr(e C_K) =chi_N Lambda_N[(C_K tensor I)Pi_N]. (9) This is a canonical cup/cap realization of the SAME period for all knots and levels, not an arbitrary inserted coupon chosen to defeat a positivity claim. The actual complete cut is scalar by the already proved original quantum-group intertwining and irreducibility. If C_K=f_(K,N)I, the state in (9) is f_(K,N)Pi_N, a nilpotent multiple. Dropping the nilpotent source would erase its whole original value, not just a dispensable local correction. This explains why ordinary-color positive traces do not extend by formal faithfulness to the Kashaev color. The exact ordinary-color positive realization has zero quantum dimension at this endpoint; its positive semisimplification kills precisely the object/source which (5)-(9) retain. The separate regular-period theorem correctly uses that positivity only below color N, not for the volume target. ## 4. Original braiding is also not positively unitarizable The all-N actual Casimir interpolation retains the nonzero derivative at c_0. If B=R_checked/kappa removes only the recorded common Cartan scalar, its double-node block obeys e_0(B^2-I)=(-1)^(N+1)(N-1)(q-q^(-1))Pi_N !=0, (10) and the right side has square zero. Therefore B^2, hence B, has a nontrivial Jordan block. A unitary matrix in a positive definite metric is diagonalizable. No positive metric and no common phase normalization makes the original checked crossing unitary. This is an exact all-N consequence of the original R coefficient and the actual cap jet. The derivative interpolation and its direct matrix derivation are already in [the Casimir braiding proof](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) and [the meridian source proof](meridian_casimir_source.md). We use them with their scalar and parity, rather than assuming a literature unitarity theorem. ## 5. Also ||Phi_N||_(op->op)=N and ||Lambda_N||=N. The upper bounds follow from summing N unitary-pivot diagonal blocks. Equality for Phi uses T=I tensor g^(-1); equality for Lambda uses T=e tensor g^(-1). Thus the universal source extension costs only polynomial factors, not an unknown exponential normalization. For the assembled scalar cut there is the exact positive norm identity |P_(K,N)|=|chi_N| ||(C_K tensor I)Pi_N||_op/N. (11) Equation (11) is useful normalization information but NOT a new noncancellation mechanism: C_K already contains the original internal pivotal sums. The right side is the same unknown scalar in a canonical nilpotent line. A local geometric amplitude or ambient operator norm does not supply a lower bound for it. No source-specific broad positivity/nonvanishing theorem has been obtained here. What is decided is that the actual cyclic/Hopf source does not force it through ordinary positive trace, unitarity or a positive reduced torsor. A successful positive geometric comparison must explicitly transport the retained nilpotent/relative source and prove its nonzero geometric image. Emergent positivity of a suitably reduced global integral is not excluded by this result.
