In particular the ACTUAL inverse block, with row u and column a, is C_(x,s)^-1(u,a) =x^(u-a)(-1)^(a-u)Q^((a-u)(a-u-1)/2) F_(s-u)/[F_u F_(a-u) F_(s-a)] for u<=a, and zero otherwise. This follows by reversing the two diagonal gauges in (2), and specifies every inverse kernel used below. On the cap block s=d, let R(k,n)=Q^(n-k+1){n choose k}_Q, 0<=k,n<N. This is the matrix in the arbitrary-x Rogers convolution proved in [the finite whole-source transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). It is literally an actual fusion block with the following gauges: R(k,n) = L_k C_(x,d)(k,n) B_n, L_k=Q^(1-k)x^-k/[F_k F_(d-k)], B_n=Q^n x^n F_(d-n). (4) Thus that finite transform is available as a change of actual fusion coordinates; it is not merely an unrelated operator on Newton coefficients. Equation (4), however, realizes one degree block, not an invariant subspace for an arbitrary plat word. ## 2. Actual ordinary turns become corners Write `xvee=x^-1 Q^-1` for the actual dual color. All formulas below use the original balanced turns from [the bridge source calculation](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), including their factors N and 1/N and the original pivot. For a physical pair `(V(x),V(xvee))`, coev_L(x) = C_x |d,0>, ev_R(x) C_x = (1/N)<0,d|. (5) For the opposite order `(V(xvee),V(x))`, coev_R(x) = C_(xvee) |d,0>, ev_L(x) C_(xvee) = (1/N)<0,d|. (6) For the cups, (1) at `(a,b)=(d,0)` gives the coefficient `N x^(u-d)`. This is exactly the original left cup. With the first color xvee it is exactly the original right cup, because `(xvee)^(u-d)=x^(d-u)Q^(d-u)`. For completeness, a supported physical row `ell(u,d-u)=kappa lambda^u` has (ell C_x)(a,d-a) =kappa N x^-a (Q lambda x;Q)_a/F_(d-a). (7) Indeed use F_u F_(d-u)=N(-1)^u Q^(u(u+1)/2) in (1), and then the finite q-binomial theorem. The actual right cap has `kappa=1/N`, `lambda=xvee`, so `Q lambda x=1`. All a>0 entries vanish and the a=0 entry is 1/N. This proves (5), and the same argument proves (6). The vanished Pochhammer is the WHOLE polynomial factor, rather than a numerical value selected after specialization. ## 3. The original marked cap is an explicit nonconstant row The actual reduced source is represented by the marked right cap ev_R^D(u,v)=x^v/N^2, (8) with no restriction on u+v. This is the original averaged source; it is not an ordinary intertwining cap. Pulling (8) through (1) gives the following exact row on the ENTIRE relative two-head space: m_x(a,b) := (ev_R^D C_x)(a,b) = x^b F_a/N^2 sum_(h=0)^min(a,d-b) {b+h choose b}_Q. (9) To check (9), substitute v=a+b-u in (8). The x powers become `x^(v+u-a)=x^b`. Set `h=a-u` in the remaining factorial quotient; then `F_(b+h)/(F_h F_b)={b+h choose b}`. This calculation includes every source wall and every total-degree block. There is a useful further simplification in a whole plat. All k cups start in total degree kd, every actual crossing preserves that integer degree, and each of the k-1 ordinary output caps in (5)--(6) forces degree d. Therefore the marked pair is automatically in degree d. There (9) is the closed row mu_x(r) := m_x(r,d-r) = x^(d-r)(-1)^r Q^(-r(r+1)/2) F_r^2/N^2, 0<=r<N. (10) For a direct proof of its inner sum, reflect the Gaussian: {d-r+h choose h}_Q =(-1)^h Q^(-rh+h(h-1)/2){r choose h}_Q. Summing h=0,...,r gives `(Q^-r;Q)_r=(-1)^r Q^(-r(r+1)/2)F_r`, yielding (10). In particular every mu_x(r) is nonzero for x!=0, and mu_x(r+1)/mu_x(r) = -x^-1 Q^(-r-1)(1-Q^(r+1))^2. (11) No normal direction in x, and hence no meridian derivative at fixed Q, has been discarded. For example `x d/dx mu_x(r)=(d-r)mu_x(r)`. At the canonical unit root `Q=exp(2pi i/N)`, mu_x(r)=x^(d-r)/N^2 product_(j=1)^r [2 sin(pi j/N)]^2. (12) Put `w_N(r)=|F_r|^2/N^2>0`. There is an explicit coherent gauge of the WORD implementing the positive boundary row, rather than merely an observation about its coefficients. Choose the same designated pair at every horizontal slice and let G_boldx |a_1,b_1;...;a_k,b_k> = x_*^(b_*) |a_1,b_1;...;a_k,b_k>. Here x_* is that pair's current first color, updated after crossings. For every letter replace (14) below by B_i^(epsilon,G)=G_boldx' B_i^epsilon G_boldx^-1. The input cup corners have b_*=0, so G_initial fixes them. Therefore the final scalar can use weights w_N(r) and the entries of `B_beta^G=G_final B_beta G_initial^-1` exactly. All intermediate gauges cancel. On |x_j|=1 this is a unitary diagonal change at every slice; for general nonzero x_j it remains an invertible Laurent change retaining the whole meridian. The crossing kernels remain complex, so positivity of this actual SOURCE row is not a no-cancellation theorem for the whole contraction. The empty one-bridge word has r=d as its sole input/output entry. The full identity `(-1)^d Q^(d(d+1)/2)=1` gives mu_x(d)=1. Hence (10) reproduces the original unknot normalization at both parities without replacing the marked cap by an ordinary cap. ## 4. Strict actual crossing cores, including both signs and colors Let `J_+|a>=|a+1>` and `J_-|a>=|a-1>`, with their actual top and bottom arrows zero. Put `X_+=J_+ tensor J_-`; this preserves the integer total degree and has `X_+^N=0`. Set u_N(t)=sum_(h=0)^d t^h/F_h, v_N(t)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)t^h/F_h, D_(x,y)|a,b>=(-1)^b Q^(b(b-1)/2)(xy)^-b |a,b>. Then `u_N(X)v_N(X)=I` for every nilpotent X of order at most N. The original checked crossings satisfy R_+^(x,y) = kappa_(x,y) C_y D_(x,y) u_N(x^-1 X_+) C_x^-1, R_-^(x,y) = kappa_(y,x)^-1 C_y v_N(y^-1 X_+) D_(x,y)^-1 C_x^-1. (13) Here every common Cartan scalar kappa is the original unrolled one, or its prescribed external Hom-line factor; it is not reset to one. The negative formula is the inverse of the positive formula with input colors reversed. Formula (13) is STRICT for these noncyclic head shifts. It differs from extending the coefficient algebra by cyclic right multiplication, whose positive-degree-N completion is only source-equivalent on the closed-braid algebra. One proof of (13) is to multiply its triangular kernels and use the finite q-binomial theorem. Equivalently, the already checked actual right coefficient is kappa sum_(h+b<N) (-1)^b Q^(b(b-1)/2)x^-h(xy)^-b f^h e_b/F_h. Its degree-preserving action on a relative input `(a,b)` has output `(a+h,b-h)`, coefficient `x^-h/F_h` followed by the displayed Gaussian at b-h. These are precisely `D u_N(x^-1 X_+)`. The omitted cyclic paths raise physical integer degree by N; the literal actual crossing contains exactly the degree-preserving part. This proves (13) on every total-degree block, including s>=N and both truncated endpoints. Taking the inverse proves the negative formula with its stated operator order. ## 5. An exact recursion for every admissible 2k-plat At a horizontal slice with colors `bold x=(x_1,...,x_(2k))`, define C_boldx = C_(x_1) tensor C_(x_3) tensor ... tensor C_(x_(2k-1)). This is the actual pair-fusion frame. At a crossing i let boldx' be the color order after swapping i and i+1, and set B_i^epsilon(boldx) = C_boldx'^-1 R_i^epsilon(boldx) C_boldx. (14) All entries of C and C^-1 are explicit in (1)--(3); all entries of R are explicit in (13). Equation (14) is therefore a fixed finite convolution rule, not an unspecified intertwiner. For a crossing within one fused pair, (14) is exactly the triangular Euler/Gaussian core in (13). A crossing between consecutive pairs acts on ONLY four relative heads. If their current physical colors are `(x,y,z,w)`, its rule is B_middle^epsilon = (C_x^-1 tensor C_y^-1) (I tensor R_epsilon^(y,z) tensor I) (C_x tensor C_z). (15) Thus it consists of a fixed number of the actual Pascal, inverse Pascal, Euler and Gaussian factors, independent of N and of k. It retains the whole set of total-degree channels I_s. Other pairs are unchanged. No source-dependent adjustment is introduced at an interior crossing. For any word beta update colors after EACH letter and iterate (14). The frames at consecutive slices cancel exactly, giving B_beta=C_final^-1 R_beta C_initial. (16) In particular these kernels satisfy every colored braid relation EXACTLY, with the original scalar lines retained: both words in such a relation have the same boundary frames in (16). This is stronger than claiming braid relations modulo the completion's positive-degree error ideal. The actual noncyclic Euler cores and all the degree blocks in (2) are what make the present statement strict. Transporting an extra coupon means conjugating that coupon by its slice frame as well; it does not mean leaving its old relative matrix in place. At every cup the initial state is `|d,0>`. At each ordinary cap the final row is `(1/N)<0,d|`. Designate one final pair with first color x_* for the original marked right cap; by choosing the standard orientation of that marked pair, (8) applies. Let `e_in=|d,0> tensor ... tensor |d,0>` and let `e_out(r)` put `(r,d-r)` at the marked pair and `(0,d)` at all other pairs. The original reduced scalar is exactly P_(beta,N) = chi_beta N^(-(k-1)) sum_(r=0)^d mu_(x_*)(r) <e_out(r)|B_beta|e_in>. (17) The factor chi_beta retains the original common Cartan and framing lines if they were recorded externally rather than in R. Any original peripheral modified-dimension germ multiplies both sides unchanged. There are k cups, k-1 ordinary caps, and exactly ONE marked cap, as in the original reduced closure. An ordinary cap has not been placed at the marked pair. The proof of (17) is (5)--(10) together with (16). It holds for arbitrary bridge number, arbitrary signed word with admissible output pairing, and the whole original meridian family. Reversing an ordinary pair uses (6); no further scalar is generated. Its full moments and meridian jets follow by differentiating the same Laurent identities at fixed Q. Moving-q normal jets are not asserted. Explicitly, the same truncated matrices obey `C_(q x)(u,v;a,b)=q^(u-a) C_x(u,v;a,b)`. Thus meridian half-step transport is an exact frame change on the fixed-root family; its dual color changes by q^-1. None of the whole factors `1-x^N` or `1+x^N` in the original cyclic boundary descriptions has been inverted to obtain this recursion. ### The zero-current quotient is one corner, with no genericity hypothesis For actual plat words without extra nonintertwining coupons, the source can be reduced further. Contract the k-1 ordinary final caps and leave the designated pair open. The resulting physical two-head vector v is invariant under the actual coproduct, because the input cups, crossings and the contracted ordinary caps are actual Hopf intertwiners. In particular, F_total v=0, K_total v=v. (18) On the remaining ordered dual pair `(x,xvee)`, the literal actual fusion identities are C_x^-1 F_total C_x=S_a, C_x^-1 K_total C_x|a,b>=Q^(-1-a-b)|a,b>, where `S_a|a,b>=|a+1,b>` for a<d and is zero for a=d. The first identity follows from the definition `C_x|a,b>=F_total^a(|0> tensor |b>)`, including its top endpoint; `F_total^N=0` is the actual root coproduct identity. Therefore ker S_a intersect ker(Q^(-1-a-b)-1) = span{|d,0>}. (19) Indeed the first kernel has a=d. The second equation then becomes Q^-b=1, which forces b=0 in the actual head range. This uses neither Schur's lemma nor irreducibility of the color module. It holds on the whole meridian family, including reducibility divisors. Consequently the amplitudes in (17) satisfy the exact Ward zeros <e_out(r)|B_beta|e_in>=0 for 0<=r<d. (20) There is no sum over hidden intermediate states in (20): the other output pairs are already fixed to their ordinary cap corners. Since mu_x(d)=1, the original scalar is the SINGLE original fused corner P_(beta,N)=chi_beta N^(-(k-1)) <e_out(d)|B_beta|e_in>. (21) The diagonal source gauge above also fixes e_out(d), because its marked b coordinate is zero. Thus (21) is unaffected by that gauge. The original marker is still necessary: an ordinary cap evaluates the remaining invariant cup to zero, whereas the marker evaluates it to one. Equations (19)--(21) describe the quotient by the actual zero-current equations; they do not authorize replacing a marker in a network containing nonintertwining current coupons. In that more general network the full row (9), not (21), is required. Equation (21) removes the final source-row cancellation problem at the exact finite level. It does not say that the remaining corner coefficient has positive summands, or that its geometric critical coefficient cannot vanish in an asymptotic decomposition. ## 6. Why the cap-block Rogers rule alone cannot unwind every bridge The degree-d block in (4) is NOT stable under crossings between pairs. For every N>=2, take the actual cup-supported physical input `(0,d,0,d)`. The zero-raising route of the positive middle crossing takes its middle pair `(d,0)` to `(0,d)` with a nonzero original coefficient. The resulting four-head state is (0,0,d,d), whose pair degrees are 0 and 2d, rather than d and d. This is an all-N literal coefficient statement; it uses no semiclassical model. Later crossings can return these channels to degree d. Discarding them does not define an exact iterative actual-plat transform. Equations (14)--(17) supply the necessary larger rule. This explains the distinction from the auxiliary Newton operators in [the whole-source Newton note](whole_source_newton_transport.md): one actual cap block realizes their Rogers matrix, but arbitrary actual bridge transport requires the full physical channel system. ## 7. The source meets a fusion boundary, not the regular fusion torus The [already proved regular fusion graph](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md) has relative clocks A,J, physical clocks U,V, and momenta satisfying AJ=UV, H=A/U, p_U=(1-A)p_A, p_V=(1-V)p_J/(1-J), H=1-(1-A)(1-J)/(x p_J/p_A). (22) It is the actual Borel multiplication chart: in particular physical total lowering has symbol `f_total=1/p_A`. The physical ordinary bridge source has `f_total=0`, because its two Borel holonomies multiply to I. Therefore it is outside this chart with finite nonzero p_A. A regular interior symplectic map alone cannot move the bridge source into a chosen positive geometric chart. The same issue is visible directly in the original marked row, without assigning a symbol to a finite nilpotent matrix. Fix total degree d, a=r, and multiply the physical-u summand of (1) by (8). Apart from a factor independent of u, this summand is `F_(d-u)/F_(r-u)`. Its consecutive ratio is exactly [1-Q^(r-u)]/[1-Q^(d-u)]. (23) On an interior principal chart its limit is `(U-A)/(U-1)`. The stationary equation setting this ratio to one forces A=1, which is a divisor excluded from (22). Thus the exact nonzero row (10) is a boundary/resonant transport calculation. It is not an interior critical point of the regular fusion kernel with the original marker inserted. This is a specific constraint on the route to a positive quad or Rivin chart. The source-boundary contribution must be included in an actual compactified/relative chart transform; merely composing the interior canonical graphs would lose it. The exact row (9)--(10), its endpoint recurrence (11), and its exact Ward corner (19)--(21) give that transform a specified source to carry. They do not prove that its selected geometric coefficient is nonzero after the full word contraction. ## 8. Verification and precise remaining comparison The [independent original-matrix audit](../experiments/audit_actual_rogers_bridge_transport.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_rogers_bridge_transport_results.json) pass fourteen root/color families at N=2,...,8, all total-degree Pascal blocks, the Rogers gauges, all four turn corners, the full marked row, the degree-d simplification, and six mixed signed crossings per family. Six whole pointed plats with two and three bridges compare literal original contractions with (17), verify all the zero-current channels (20), and verify the single corner (21). Seven all-parity leakage witnesses verify Section 6. These checks fix conventions; the finite identities above prove the all-N formulas. What is now explicit is the actual arbitrary-bridge kernel system AND its marked source. A further source-preserving local transform must turn these all-channel kernels into positive quad/2↔3 kernels while carrying (9), its boundary (23), the Ward corner (19), and all central factors. Neither a Pascal basis change nor the ordinary matrix pentagon by itself performs that comparison. No broad hyperbolic growth or geometric-cycle selection claim follows from (17) alone.

title: The original Rogers sink is an opposite-root beta source
text: # The original Rogers sink is an opposite-root beta source 28 October 2026. The remaining U/U/F sink has an exact finite order-reversal identity with the already solved Newton sink at the opposite root. Applying its ACTUAL relative source gives an explicit two-full-Psi residue and a uniformly bounded retained current on a nonempty geometric chamber. No new normalization, guessed contour, or substitution of a positive invariant is required. Together with the literal three-sink crossing partition, this supplies local analytic source formulas for all nine original crossing atoms. It does not prove that the simultaneous exterior knot cycle selects their geometric product. ## 1. Original Rogers polynomial and field tags Put Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), h=2*pi*i/N and d=N-1. The actual U/U/F finite convolution is R_N(u,v)=sum_(i+j<N) (Q;Q)_(i+j) u^i v^j/[(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j]. (1) Its q-Pascal recurrence gives the exact endpoint Ward equations (1-u)R_N(u,v)-v R_N(Qu,v)=D_R, (1-v)R_N(u,v)-u R_N(u,Qv)=D_R, D_R=1-u^N-v^N. (2) For example h_(a+1)(u,v)=u h_a(u,v)+v h_a(Qu,v), while h_N=u^N+v^N at the primitive root. Summing a=0,...,d gives (2). The nonzero inhomogeneous endpoint is part of the source. For the complete reflected moment field F_R(L;U,V)=r^d Psi_-(Log U-L) Psi_-(Log V-L)Psi_+(-L), r=exp L, the EXACT original tags are N Q^d [r^0]F_R=R_N(Q^2 U,Q^2 V). (3) Indeed the two minus coefficients are Q^i/(Q;Q)_i and Q^j/(Q;Q)_j, while p_(d-i-j)=Q^(i+j+1)(Q;Q)_(i+j)/N. No Q tag or N factor is dropped. The exact field step and norm are F_R(L+h)/F_R(L)=Q^d (1-Q^(-1)/r) /[(1-U/r)(1-V/r)], F_R(L+2*pi*i)/F_R(L) =r^N(r^N-1)/[(r^N-U^N)(r^N-V^N)]. (3a) Subtracting one in the latter has numerator [(U^N+V^N-1)r^N-U^N V^N]. Its multiplier-one locus is the Frobenius copy of the classical linear gluing equation (U+V-1)r=UV. The retained source does not become a homogeneous solution merely because that polynomial is displayed. ## 2. A finite source-preserving order reversal Write B_(q,N)(a,b)=sum_(k=0)^d product_(j<k)(a-q^j b). Then the WHOLE polynomial kernel satisfies R_N(u,v)=v^d B_(Q^(-1),N)(v^(-1),Q^(-1)u/v). (4) This is an identity of every boundary coefficient and can therefore be paired with the SAME exterior functional and original cups/caps. The apparent negative v powers cancel to the original polynomial; they are not a new source support assumption. Here is an all-N coefficient proof. Let q=Q^(-1). The right side is sum_(a=0)^d v^(d-a)(q u;q)_a. The coefficient of u^i v^j has a=d-j and is (-1)^i q^(i(i+1)/2) (q;q)_(d-j)/[(q;q)_i(q;q)_(d-j-i)]. The numerator quotient equals (Q;Q)_(i+j)/(Q;Q)_j by the root complement, and (q;q)_i=(-1)^i Q^(-i(i+1)/2)(Q;Q)_i. The phases cancel EXACTLY, leaving the coefficient in (1). This uses no asymptotics. ## 3. Carry the opposite-root contour and the full norm Define the opposite-root current by the actual conjugate source I_-(a,b)=overline(I_+(overline(a),overline(b))), with its conjugate logarithmic marks. The conjugate of the upward Barnes contour is a DOWNWARD contour; this orientation is retained. Equivalently it is minus the upward integral with denominator exp(2*pi*i*z)-1 and the opposite full-Psi function. Its chamber is a upper and b/a lower. Its uniform compact bound is the conjugate of the proved original Newton bound. Apply the EXACT opposite Newton decomposition to (4), using a=v^(-1), b=Q^(-1)u/v, Log a=-Log v, Log(b/a)=Log u-h. The complete norm transforms by v^d(1-a^N+b^N)=-v^(-1)(1-u^N-v^N). The original Rogers source is consequently R_N=T_N+D_R J_N, J_N(u,v)=-v^(-1) I_-(v^(-1),Q^(-1)u/v), T_N(u,v)=phi_N exp[-Log u Log v/h] Psi_-(Log u-h)Psi_-(Log v-h). (5) All constants are exact: N/phi_-=phi_+ because |phi_N|^2=N, and v^d a^N times the shifted Gaussian contributes v^(-1)*v=1. Thus (5) is an actual relative-cycle pushforward, not a normal determinant calculation. The opposite circle/ray source, its endpoints and deck choices are transported by (4) and conjugation. For u,v both strictly lower, the transformed opposite chamber is valid uniformly on compact subsets for all sufficiently large N. It follows immediately that |J_N(u,v)|<=C_K. (6) Its principal normalization symbol is also explicit: J_N=1/(1-u-v)+h*u*v/(1-u-v)^3+O_K(h^2). (6a) This follows by substituting the exact Q^(-1) tag into the proved opposite Newton symbol, or by expanding (2). Its all-order rational recursion has poles only on the bubble locus u+v=1. Exact current continuation and exponentially small sectors are still retained. At smaller N, or after continuation outside that chamber, (5) keeps its transported logarithmic marks and currents; no bare replacement by a principal contour is assumed. There is a useful full-positive-function version that displays the norm factors. The exact identity Psi_-(z-h)=(1-exp(Nz))/Psi_+(z) gives T_N=phi_N (1-u^N)(1-v^N) exp[-Log u Log v/h] /[Psi_+(Log u)Psi_+(Log v)]. (7) The factor is (1-u^N)(1-v^N), NOT (uv)^N. On the balanced Fermat locus u^N+v^N=1 these agree, but off that locus their difference is D_R. Replacing one by the other changes the retained current by an explicit full-Psi term. Such a change cannot be declared tame or ignored at an ideal specialization. ## 4. Balanced Fourier check and both homogeneous Ward equations On u^N+v^N=1, the source recurrence is homogeneous. The finite u-orbit has R_N(Q^k u,v)=R_N(u,v) (u;Q)_k/v^k. Summing the orbit and taking the zero Fourier coefficient of the polynomial gives R_N(u,v) B_(Q,N)(v^(-1),u/v)=N u^N/(1-v). (8) The balanced Newton sum is nonzero. Using its independently proved normalizer, (8) yields exactly (7) with its balanced factor (uv)^N. This is an independent finite-source normalization check. Off balance, (5) supplies the actual full norm extension. Its geometric block obeys BOTH exact homogeneous equations (1-u)T_N(u,v)=v T_N(Qu,v), (1-v)T_N(u,v)=u T_N(u,Qv), (9) and J_N obeys (2) with right side one. The all-level source choice is therefore fixed by order reversal, not just by data on D_R=0. ## 5. An actual growing local source on a full open chamber For u,v strictly lower, write l=Log u,m=Log v on (-pi,0). The actual negative-strip full-Psi symbol and exact shift yield T_N=phi_N/ sqrt[(1-u)(1-v)] exp[W_R(u,v)/h](1+O_K(1/N)), W_R=-Li_2(u)-Li_2(v)-l*m. (10) Every density is explicit and nonzero, with all fixed derivative bounds uniform on compact lower-half-plane families. Put Lambda_R=Im W_R/(2*pi), delta_R=max(0,log|u|,log|v|). If Lambda_R>=delta_R+eta on a compact family, (5)--(6) prove R_N(u,v)=T_N(u,v)[1+O_K(N^(-1/2)exp(-N eta))]. (11) The original residue has coefficient one; its entire retained normalization current is exponentially smaller. This is a genuine source theorem on a nonempty open family, not a knot-family claim. For |u|=|v|=1, with both lower, delta_R=0 and Lambda_R=[-Im Li_2(u)-Im Li_2(v)]/(2*pi)>0. The cross term l*m is real. A compact pair of lower unit arcs has a uniform positive gap, which persists in a full open neighborhood. In particular, uniformly for theta,eta on compact subsets of (0,pi), lim_(N->infinity) (2*pi/N) log|R_N(exp(-i*theta),exp(-i*eta))| =D(exp(i*theta))+D(exp(i*eta)). (12) The identical limit holds with the ACTUAL Q^2,Q^2 tags in (3). These are original local polynomial volume identities. They are not asserted to be Kashaev invariants of a new family of knots. There is a genuinely positive three-side bipyramid subfamily too. At u=exp(-i theta),v=exp(-i eta), its three-side shapes are A=(u+v-1)/v, B=(u+v-1)/u, C=(u+v-1)/(uv). C is upper for all theta,eta in (0,pi). Both A and B are lower when eta<pi/2+theta/2 and theta<pi/2+eta/2. These strict inequalities hold in particular near every equal-angle pair. Thus the three signed shapes -[A]-[B]+[C] and the two negative output shapes -[u]-[v] are strictly positive and nondegenerate there. The five-term relation identifies their equal positive volume. This verifies a nonempty open geometric family without asserting that every possible unit-angle pair is a positive 2-to-3 move in this ordering. ## 6. What is now available globally The literal crossing assembly has three disjoint finite sinks. For a positive crossing, exact Gaussian absorption leaves two Newton kernels and one Rogers kernel. For a negative crossing there are again two Newton kernels and one Rogers kernel, with its original Gaussian retained. Equations (4)--(11) thus fill the missing analytic local entry in that assembly, including its source and norm factors. This does not permit independent sector integrations on arbitrary new circles. The simultaneous original boundary pairing, logarithmic seams, caps and residual Gaussian remain compulsory. The full exterior cycle and its geometric noncancellation are the next global issue. ## 7. Sew the actual opposite face BEFORE taking an asymptotic symbol In the literal positive crossing, the final Newton and Rogers kernels share the EXACT variable w=v_B/u_B=v_R. Write their paired polynomial kernel as F(a,c,w)=B_N(a,a w) R_N(c,w), alpha=Log a, chi=Log c, sigma=Log w, A=a^N, C=c^N, W=w^N, D_B=1-A+AW, D_R=1-C-W. (13) The Newton positive growth chamber asks w upper while the Rogers negative growth chamber asks w lower. There is NO simultaneous principal positive chamber for the two unsewn face factors. The literal product must first use the exact shifted identity Psi_+(sigma)Psi_-(sigma-h)=1-W. Consequently its full residue product is exactly P(a,c,w)=(1-W) G(a,c,w), G=N a^N exp[-sigma(alpha+chi)/h] Psi_+(h-alpha)Psi_-(chi-h). (14) The ordinary factor 1-w is absent: the EXACT h shift removes it. The central factor 1-W is retained. All remaining original currents are the explicit aggregate F=P+D_B I_B(a,a w) T_R(c,w) +D_R J_R(c,w) S_B(a,a w) +D_B D_R I_B(a,a w)J_R(c,w). (15) This is an identity of actual marked functions; their relative cycles and overlaps are inherited from the original finite pair. It does not assign independent principal contours to the three terms in the incompatible half-plane chambers. The paired endpoint Ward identity is also explicit and polynomial: F(a,c,w)-a c F(a,c,Qw) =D_B R_N(c,w)+a D_R B_N(a,Qa w). (16) It follows by multiplying the two exact finite Ward equations. No artificial denominator 1-w is introduced. The source norms obey D_B+A D_R=1-AC. (17) Thus the two simultaneous balanced constraints force the single external central relation AC=1. Their coupling must not be replaced by two independent local angle-domain choices. The remaining field G has no dilogarithm in sigma; its sigma phase is the explicit linear Fourier coupling -sigma(alpha+chi). Its regular remaining shape functions can both be on selected strips when a and c are lower, irrespective of the removed face's sign. The OTHER factors of the complete crossing still depend on this same internal variable, so this observation alone does not evaluate its full Fourier integral or select its exterior cycle. One full sigma deck gives P -> P/(AC), (F-P) -> (F-P)+(1-(AC)^(-1))P. (18) The original pair F remains fixed. This is the inherited shared-face source extension, with the exact norm currents. It shows both the benefit of sewing the opposite face first and why its currents cannot then be deleted independently. ### 7.1. The exact locus for an aggregate geometric quotient The sewn pair permits a precise algebraic statement stronger than deleting its individual current sectors. Keep a,c,w nonzero and the same marked function P in (14). Its three full logarithmic turns have characters mu_a=(A-1)/(AW), mu_c=(1-C)/W, mu_w=1/(AC). (18a) For example an alpha turn contributes W^(-1) from its Fourier exponential and 1-A^(-1) from Psi_+(h-alpha); a chi turn contributes W^(-1)(1-C). Equation (18) gives the sigma turn. All factors and logarithmic marks are exact, including the h shifts. On this regular central torus, the CHARACTER-ONE IDEAL is exactly the joint balanced ideal, since 1-mu_a=D_B/(AW), 1-mu_c=-D_R/W, 1-mu_w=-(D_B+A D_R)/(AC). (18b) Thus (1-mu_a,1-mu_c,1-mu_w)=(D_B,D_R) after the indicated unit localization. The weaker shared-face condition AC=1 alone does not make the other two characters one. Let H=F-P be the AGGREGATE current. Under each turn it changes by (1-mu)P. A deck-compatible pointwise quotient killing H therefore has geometric image supported on this joint balanced locus (or on its retained normal/derived thickening). Conversely on its regular matched base change D_B=D_R=0, the exact finite source identities give F=P!=0. (18c) Indeed the Newton and Rogers balanced polynomials are each nonzero by their finite Fourier proofs. Their exact marked residues equal those polynomials there, so (18c) is a nonzero local source-preserving restriction, not a section defined from an unknown knot value. One is killing the COMBINED current on a specified algebraic base; one is not declaring its separate summands zero off that base. This identifies a possible local geometric quotient and the exact support it requires. It does NOT prove that the remaining original head/cap co-source factors through this base change, nor replace its finite degree relations by scalar norm equations. Normal source jets, the other head factors and the actual exterior integration still have to be transported. Character-one and nonzero local pointing do not by themselves determine a nonzero global period coefficient. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source_results.json) check original finite reversal and actual tags, the two conjugate Barnes source identities, balanced Fourier normalization and the paired polynomial Ward relation. The proofs do not infer their all-level statements from finite checks. ## 8. The ACTUAL shared-head source combines the currents into a ground channel There is a stronger physical identity once the first, still unsplit Newton factor is included. In the literal positive crossing put E=x^(-1)z_6/z_1, s=x^(-1)z_1/z_0, a=x^(-1)z_7/z_6, c=z_6/z_0, B_0(w)=B_N(E/w,sE/w), K_m=Pi_+^(6) CT_w B_N(Q^m E/w,Q^m sE/w)F(a,c,w). The common original scalar kappa remains external. These are literal operators on the original finite input space; Pi_+^(6) is the original nonnegative first-output barrier. K_0 is the original positive crossing without kappa. K_m inserts the ACTUAL internal Cartan clock Q^(mJ) on the t=z_4 head just after C^(-1), before its remaining gates. The first factor has w degree between -d and zero. Therefore pairing the polynomial Ward equation (16) with it kills every w^N times a nonnegative polynomial. The exact source equation before the physical barriers is CT B_0[F-acF(Qw)] =(1-a^N) CT B_0 R+corr, corr=a(1-c^N) CT B_0 B_N(a,Qaw). (19) No D_B or D_R has been set to zero. Their w^N parts have vanished by the FINITE DEGREE of the actual third sink, rather than a branchwise replacement of the source. Rotating w in the second left term gives the next clock insertion K_(m+1). The remaining physical barriers have precise effects: * H_m=CT B_N(Q^m E/w,Q^m sE/w)R_N(c,w) has first-output degree at most d, so a^N H_m has negative first-output degree and is killed by Pi_+^(6). * Every term of a CT B_0 B_N(a,Qaw) has first-output degree -i-1<0, so this entire term is killed by the SAME barrier. * Multiplication of that last expression by c^N can remove the negative output degree, but then it requires first INPUT index at least N. The original finite input space kills it. These claims hold with every clock m: the clock changes coefficients, not the indicated index supports. Thus on the original finite heads, K_m-(ac)K_(m+1)=H_m. (20) The boundary source is explicit. For input indices alpha,beta and alpha+beta<N, H_m |alpha,beta> =Q^(m beta)x^(-beta) {alpha+beta choose alpha}_Q (Q^m x^(-2);Q)_alpha |alpha+beta,0>, (21) and it is zero if alpha+beta>=N. To derive (21), expand the Euler factor (s;Q)_j in the first Newton kernel. If its Euler order is k, the surviving indices are j=beta+k and i=alpha-k. The q-binomial sum is exactly (Q^m x^(-2);Q)_alpha. This proves all normalizations with the actual color x retained. H_0 has rank N: the inputs (0,beta) span every output (beta,0). It is a ground-SECOND-output channel, not a rank-one operator and not a negligible error. At complete color x^(-2)=Q its coefficient is x^(-beta)(Q;Q)_(alpha+beta)/(Q;Q)_beta; it is nonzero on every supported input and can have bulk factorial growth. This growth is quantitative in the complete flat balanced metric. Rows have disjoint input total degrees, so the exact operator norm is ||H_0||^2=max_(0<=t<N) |F_t|^2 sum_(b=0)^t |F_b|^(-2). With J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, the uniform factorial estimate log|F_k|=N J(k/N)+O(log N) gives log||H_0||=N integral_(1/6)^(5/6) log(2 sin(pi y))dy+O(log N). Indeed the largest profile rise is J(5/6)-J(1/6). Thus the physical ground-output source is not an exponentially small boundary error. Its exact endpoint support does not justify discarding its period after composition with the remaining word. The fusion operation itself is associative multiplication with explicit weights. On e_a=t^a/F_a in C[t]/(t^N), ordinary multiplication has m(e_a tensor e_b)={a+b choose a}_Q e_(a+b), with zero output when a+b>=N. Consequently H_m is this multiplication after diagonal weights (Q^m x^(-2);Q)_J on the first input and (Q^m/x)^J on the second, followed by the ground-second-head inclusion. The exact identity (z;Q)_(a+b)=(z;Q)_a(Q^a z;Q)_b describes the weight transport under further fusion. This structural description preserves all original factorial frames; it is not a new positive state model. Equation (20) has an exact nilpotent Green solution. Multiplication by ac=x^(-1)z_7/z_0 raises the second output index and increases the first input demand by one. Hence (ac)^N times any K_m is zero on the original finite input space. Iterating gives K_0=sum_(j=0)^d (ac)^j H_j. (22) This reconstructs the ACTUAL crossing, including the combined current endpoints, from explicit fusion-to-ground channels. For example its only possible output from input (alpha,beta) has the form (alpha+beta-j,j), with j<=alpha and alpha+beta-j<N, and coefficient x^(-beta-j)Q^(j beta) {alpha+beta-j choose alpha-j}_Q (Q^j x^(-2);Q)_(alpha-j). (23) All identities are literal finite operators and may be inserted in ANY original signed word with the same caps and pivotal source. They do not assert that every H_m insertion has a degenerate global representation, or that the remaining bulk sums have no cancellation. What has been proved is an actual sourced boundary/Green identity, without discarding the norm currents or changing the invariant. The independent [finite-head audit](../experiments/audit_actual_crossing_green_ground_fusion.py) compares (20)--(23) with the original gate word, including whole signed words and their original pivotal source.

title: Root-channel H insertions and their actual relative-period transport
status: Exact algebraic root insertions, polynomial bounds and relative carry residues
text: # Root-channel H insertions and their actual relative-period transport 30 October 2026. The two root insertions in the [normal adapter](actual_explicit_root_channel_normal_adapter.md) admit a specified meromorphic representative with polynomial size on the original resonant chart. This is an exact change of representative of the original finite root period. Its different relative boundary currents are computed below; no off-grid equality with the generic descendant or finite clock polynomial is asserted. ## 1. The finite insertion and three continuations Put N>=2, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), Q=q0^2, and H_l=2N sum_(j=1)^l (1-Q^j)^-1, 0<=l<=d; H_0=0. The actual adapter uses H=diag(H_l) and X(p)H in the SAME routed root channel C0. It proves eta I=(C0-z0 Id)(H), Delta'_0(p)=eta X(p)-(C0-z0 Id)(X(p)H), X(p)_(r,s)=p^(r-s)/N. (1) Here Delta_e=C_e(X(p))-z(e)X(p). The scalar derivative z'(0) is separate. The following calculation transports the literal ROOT insertions in (1), not a differentiated root simplification of C_e. Let Fhat_P be the specified [moving-period factorial](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), P=pi i/Log(q0 exp(e)), and P'=iN^2/pi. Its logarithmic index derivative f'(z)=partial_z Log Fhat_N(z) is single valued meromorphic. Define Hhat(x)=P'[f'(d-x)-f'(d)]. (2) This function has Hhat(l)=H_l on the physical interval. In contrast, the actual finite diagonal descendant has the specified continuation h_e(x)=exp(pi i x) zeta^[x(x+1)] Fhat_P(d)/[Fhat_P(x)Fhat_P(d-x)]. Exact moving-period reflection, with d FIXED, gives h_0(x)=Y, partial_e h_e(x)|0=Y Hhat(x), Y=exp(2pi i x)=U^N, U=exp(2pi i x/N). (3) Here b_d is the exact fixed-endpoint gauge b_d(e,x)=zeta^[x(d-x)] Fhat_P(x)Fhat_P(d-x)/Fhat_P(d). Indeed h_e=exp(pi i x)zeta^(Nx)/b_d(e,x). Differentiating the exact fixed-endpoint reflection gives partial_e Log b_d=P'[f'(d)-f'(d-x)-pi i x/N]; hence partial_e Log h_e=Nx-partial_e Log b_d=(2). The character Y in the LITERAL derivative (3) has not been dropped. There is also the unique polynomial in the actual clock of degree<N: Hpol(U)=meanH-2 sum_(r=1)^d r U^r/(1-Q^-r), meanH=2 sum_(r=1)^d r/(1-Q^-r). (4) Finite Fourier inversion in the adapter proves Hpol(Q^l)=H_l. Thus Hpol(U), Hhat(x), and Hlit(x)=Y Hhat(x) have identical physical values, but they are DIFFERENT meromorphic functions. ## 2. An exact algebraic formula for the tame representative The Gamma-defined function (2) is in fact the following finite rational expression in U and the retained logarithmic head x: S(U)=sum_(r=1)^d U^r/(1-Q^-r), Hhat(x)=2N[x-d/2+S(U)]/(1-Y)+meanH+N/(pi i). (5) Physical singularities in (5) are removable. Here is a direct proof, including the normalization. Write Halg for its right side. Since S(QU)-S(U)=sum_(r=1)^d (QU)^r, one obtains Halg(x+1)-Halg(x)=2N/(1-QU), Halg(x+N)-Halg(x)=2N^2/(1-Y). (6) This is an explicit additive cyclic descent. For any rational b(U), let sigma U=QU, let mean_b=N^-1 sum_(j=0)^(N-1) sigma^j b, and put R=N^-1 sum_(j=0)^(N-1) j sigma^j b. One telescoping sum proves sigma R-R=b-mean_b. Extending sigma by sigma x=x+1, the function x mean_b+R therefore solves its full, possibly nonzero-trace, difference equation. Here b=2N/(1-QU), mean_b=2N/(1-Y), and R=2N[d/2+S(U)]/(1-Y). Formula (5) makes the invariant correction -d mean_b+meanH+N/(pi i). The zero-trace part is solved rationally; the nonzero trace requires the retained logarithmic head x. This is the elementary descent calculation itself, not an imported cohomology theorem or a choice of a source-period coefficient. At l=0,...,d, S(Q^l)=d/2-l. L'Hopital's rule in (5) gives Halg(l)=meanH-2 sum r Q^(rl)/(1-Q^-r)=H_l, including Halg(0)=0. At every integer l its residue is P' floor(l/N). The factorial unit equation gives the SAME unit difference (6) for (2). The original Gamma product has no zeros or poles off the integer lattice when P=N: its initial Gamma factor and numerator factors give the negative-integer poles, while its denominator factors give the positive-integer zeros. Counting these factors in f'(d-x) gives residue P' floor(l/N), exactly as above. Consequently Halg-Hhat is entire and 1-periodic. For completeness, this entire difference has polynomial vertical growth at fixed N. In the direct formula for partial_P Log Fhat_P, split the convergent digamma sum at K comparable to 1+|Im x|/N, with 0<=Re x<=1. The first K terms cost O_N(K^2); the tail, by the same canceled digamma expansion used in the [logarithmic-escape estimate](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md), costs O_N((1+|Im x|)^3/K). Thus (3) gives Hhat=O_N(1+|Im x|^2). Halg is at most linear vertically, as follows directly from (5) at U->0 and U->infinity. All nonzero Fourier coefficients of the entire periodic difference therefore vanish: move their horizontal integration line to the half-plane where the Fourier exponential decays. The difference is constant, and its value at zero is zero. This proves (5), without selecting an unproved periodic correction. The two exact marked transport rules are consequently Hhat(x+N)-Hhat(x)=2N^2/(1-Y), Hlit(x+N)-Hlit(x)=2N^2 g(x), g(x)=Y/(1-Y). (7) Hpol is N-periodic. Even their unit differences are distinct: Hpol(QU)-Hpol(U) =2N Y/(1-QU)-2QU(1-Y)/(1-QU)^2, Hlit(x+1)-Hlit(x)=2N Y/(1-QU). (8) The extra term vanishes at interior physical nodes. It cannot be discarded in a continuation through the missing endpoint arrow. ## 3. Exact finite periods and the polynomial insertion bound Retain an original charged band delta, its primitive integral head lattice, actual finite support, original marked co-source, and every outside tensor. In that band X(p)H has the finite weight p^delta H_l/N at the second INPUT head l. H alone is the zero-band diagonal weight. Replace H_l by Hhat(l) in the original finite sum; this changes no term, at every N and either parity. The equivalent initial cotangent realization uses the original ordered small tori with normalization (2pi i)^(-n_free). On an admissible node where the retained source germ is holomorphic, the cotangent residue evaluates the multiplier at that node, so each of the three representatives gives EXACTLY the same inserted period. An original representation with extra source poles must first retain its actual cancellations or its recorded ordered finite parts; agreement of point values alone never identifies such finite parts. The external finite head weights may always be kept outside those internal periods until this condition is met. No source-null polar torus is added merely by choosing a new interpolation. On the physical-head logarithmic strips of the [common original chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md), delta<=Re(x/N)<=1-delta, |Im(x/N)|<=C(1+log N), both x and d-x obey the moving-factorial estimates. The exact identity Hhat(x)=x(x+1)+g_d-g_x-g_(d-x), g_z=partial_e Log Fhat_(P(e))(z)|0, first gives a polynomial bound. Formula (5) sharpens it to, with L_N=1+log N, |partial_x^j Hhat(x)|<=C_j N^(2-j) L_N (9) for each fixed j, on a slightly smaller strip. Here is a direct proof. The elementary sine lower bound gives sum_(r=1)^d |1-Q^-r|^-1=O(N log N) and meanH=O(N^2 log N). When |Im x|>=1, |1-Y| is comparable to max(1,|Y|), and each |U^r|/max(1,|Y|)<=1. With |x|=O(N L_N), (5) gives the bound. When |Im x|<=1, use fixed-radius disks about the physical integers. The numerator B=x-d/2+S(U) vanishes at their centers, and |B'|=O(N log N) on those disks; the denominator has a uniformly simple zero there. Outside the disks it is bounded away from zero. This proves the same bound across every removable physical point. Higher derivatives follow by Cauchy on a pole-free head disk of radius cN. The proof also covers the nonreal exterior class |Re(x/N)|<=C, delta<=|Im(x/N)|<=C L_N, with a smaller such disk. It does not include approaches to an outside-head integer pole. This is an ABSOLUTE bound, not nonvanishing or a relative estimate at a zero of Hhat. The factor p^delta/N is retained; it is at most e^A/N when |log|p||<=A/N. This advantage belongs to the NEW root-period representative. For example, on |U| comparable to N^2, the literal clock polynomial has the asymptotic Hpol(U)=-2d U^d/(1-Q^-d) [1+O(N^-2)]. (10) Indeed every nonconstant coefficient is O(N^2), the top one has magnitude at least cN^2, and the geometric tail is O(|U|^-1); the constant coefficient is O(N^2 log N). The exact power U^d remains. The literal descendant normal has its own factor U^N in (3). Neither can silently be replaced by the bound (9) OFF GRID. Only the exact finite-period replacement and its boundary corrections justify choosing Hhat for a subsequent deformation. ## 4. Inserted-period translation and explicit endpoint anomalies Let S0(x) be an original root source on a primitive free lattice, after its recorded scalar Laurent cancellations. For an integral translation b suppose the actual tensor connection gives S0(x+Nb)=chi(b)S0(x). Let l(x) be the second physical head and k=D_b l its integral slope. Keep delta fixed in the X(p)H band. Any retained external weight not covered by this proved quasiperiod keeps its shifted value explicitly; an interpolated coherent row, for example, is not assigned the tensor's parity character. Write I_Gamma for the original cotangent period, with its complete marked source and normalization. Changing variables and using (7) gives the exact identities I_(Gamma+Nb)[Hhat(l)S0] =chi(b){I_Gamma[Hhat(l)S0] +2N^2 k I_Gamma[S0/(1-Y_l)]}, I_(Gamma+Nb)[Hlit(l)S0] =chi(b){I_Gamma[Hlit(l)S0] +2N^2 k I_Gamma[g(l)S0]}. (11) They apply bandwise with p^delta/N and to their original finite sum. The displayed root quasiperiod is a hypothesis on the genuinely canceled root coefficient. For an uncleared Laurent sector use the full finite-jet connection first: its constant coefficient can mix lower Laurent coefficients under translation. For Hpol there is no insertion correction in this N-translation, but its difference from the other representatives carries precisely the opposing current. These are continued-cycle identities, not permission to wrap any physical head or identify Gamma+Nb with Gamma. The first two outside-head Laurent coefficients are explicit. If y=x-x0, write Hrep=R/y+B+O(y). Then representative x0=-1: (R,B) x0=N: (R,B) Hhat (-P',-N) (P',N^2) Hlit (-P',2N^2-N) (P',-N^2) Hpol (0,N(N-1)) (0,0). (12) For Hhat these follow from (6), Hhat(0)=0 and Hhat(d)=N(N-1). Multiplication by Y changes the finite part by 2pi i R, where 2pi i P'=-2N^2. Hpol has its literal periodic node values. More generally, write ANY integer l=mN+r with 0<=r<=d. The same translation gives the complete carry table Hhat(l+y)=mP'/y+H_r+mN^2+O(y), Hlit(l+y)=mP'/y+H_r-mN^2+O(y), Hpol(Q^(l+y))=H_r+O(y). (12a) Thus every integral deck carry has an explicit anomaly, including negative carries; none is turned into an allowed physical state. Against pi cot(pi x) and a complement regular at x0, the crossed residue is therefore B S0(x0)+R partial_x S0(x0). (13) In particular the two correction densities in (11), at a primitive integer head with regular complement, have residues respectively 2N^2 Res[pi cot(pi l) S0/(1-Y_l)]=P'S0'+N^2 S0, 2N^2 Res[pi cot(pi l) g(l)S0]=P'S0'-N^2 S0. (14) The derivative of the actual complement is required. If l=A x_j+B is not itself primitive, its pulled-back measure is (pi/A)cot(pi(l-B)/A) dl. Use that measure and its Jacobian; if it is regular at a crossed head wall its value multiplies the residue instead. When l is constant on the free lattice there is no such head deformation. Intersections with other source divisors require their original iterated or multivariable residues, not (13). To deform either initial representative to a proposed geometric relative cycle, apply the [common-band chain identity](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md) to its actual support. Every crossed source tube, the anomalies (12)--(14), and all remaining relative ends stay in that identity. The polynomial bound (9) supplies no reason for those ends to vanish. Explicitly, for a difference D of two representatives and a specified oriented deformation Gamma_phys=Gamma_new+sum T_j+Gamma_end, the initial equality gives I_Gamma_new[D S0]=-sum_j I_T_j[D S0] -I_Gamma_end[D S0]. (14a) Here the T_j are the ACTUAL crossed-divisor tubes and the last term retains the actual relative end. Formula (14a) is used only when that deformation is constructed; it does not supply one. In particular, pointwise growth of Hpol on the boundary is not an obstruction to using Hhat, but replacing it there without (14a) is not justified. ## 5. What the H-weighted Ward equation does and does not compute The literal truncated relation [H,F0]=2N T_1 proves scalarity in (1): K covariance makes (C0-z0 Id)(H) diagonal, and F covariance forces its diagonal entries equal. It does not give eta. More explicitly use the ACTUAL coherent current M_l and L_a in the [braided current theorem](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md), with beta_a the legitimate first-cut binomial row. Weight its finite interval identity by H_l. On the WHOLE physical interval its endpoint arrows vanish, and the identity reduces to sum_(l=0)^(d-1) M_l/(1-Q^(l+1)) =z0 sum_(a=0)^(d-1) L_a/(1-Q^(a+1)) =z0[1-q0-beta_d+q0 beta_0]. (15) The eta I term disappears because the dual Ward row annihilates I. At the root M_l/(1-Q^(l+1)) is the actual pairing of C0(E_(l+1,l)-q0 E_(l,l+1)); thus (15) is precisely the already known unwrapped Toeplitz identity. On a proper interval the terms H_R M_R-H_L M_(L-1) remain. They are not determined by scalarity. Equations (5), (9), and (11)--(14) give a concrete reduction: the adapter's TWO inserted root periods may use tame, algebraically specified head weights, with explicit relative-transport currents. What remains is the pushforward of those original charged cycles and their endpoint/divisor chain to the geometric framing boundary. Neither a nonzero relative end, a geometric contribution coefficient, a bound for the full root channel, nor z'(0) is computed here. Focused verification: [source/transport audit](../experiments/audit_actual_root_channel_H_period_transport.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_root_channel_H_period_transport_results.json). It checks 299 removable physical nodes, 912 unit/level transports, 228 exact cyclic descents, 1495 general carry expansions, and 24 residue/Jacobian identities. Nine original routed sources supply 54 inserted-period comparisons and nine actual weighted Ward identities. Twelve logarithmically escaping moving-factorial heads give 24 independent reflection/algebraic comparisons, 12 retained characters, and six clock-growth checks at 75 digits; the maximum identity error is below 6.05e-72. These finite and analytic checks do not assert a global contour deformation or a relative contribution coefficient. The H-period transport retains the end contribution in (14a). The source quasiperiod is conditional, and the Ward conclusion is scalarity only. The theorem does not evaluate the geometric relative end.

title: A pole-free scalar cardinal completion of the original joint source
text: # A pole-free scalar cardinal completion of the original joint source 28 October 2026. Fixed powers of explicit cardinal windows remove every factorial pole in a prescribed O(N) joint-state box, while leaving ALL original integer physical state values unchanged and killing every invalid integer state. This keeps the unwrapped linear output and closure relations. It is a scalar completion of the original finite source, not a new positive invariant or a replacement boundary state. The windows are not innocuous on general complex contours. Their wrong-side exponential growth and exact finite integer-mode packets are calculated below. Their separated mode currents must remain at outside-band integer collisions. No global volume bound is inferred. ## 1. Exact cardinal functions and quantitative half-plane bounds Put d=N-1 and S_N(s)=sum_(j=0)^d 1/(s-j), w_N^+(s)=(exp(2pi*i*s)-1)S_N(s)/(2pi*i), w_N^-(s)=exp(-2pi*i*s)w_N^+(s). (1) Both functions are entire. Their values are EXACTLY one at each integer 0,...,d, and zero at every integer outside that range. The outside zeros are simple: S_N(n) is a sum of strictly positive terms if n>=N, and strictly negative terms if n<0, so is nonzero. These are sums of the literal unit-circle Fourier coefficients in [the physical projection theorem](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md). Orthogonality and Cauchy--Schwarz therefore give, on the WHOLE plane, |w_N^+(s)|<=sqrt(N) exp(2pi max(0,-Im s)), |w_N^-(s)|<=sqrt(N) exp(2pi max(0,+Im s)). (2) The normalizations dtheta/(2pi) and the complete turn 0<=theta<=2pi are retained. Thus a fixed number of fixed window powers costs exp(o(N)) on any joint tube |Im s|<=N^alpha, alpha<1, and polynomial cost on its favorable half-plane. It may cost exp(cN) on the wrong side of a macroscopic complex contour. There are also N-1 additional real, noninteger zeros, one in each (j,j+1). Indeed S_N'(x)=-sum_r1/(x-r)^2<0 there and its endpoint limits are +infinity and -infinity. There are no nonreal zeros of S_N, since Im S_N(s)=-Im s sum_j|s-j|^(-2). These zeros are kept; one cannot replace the window by a nowhere-zero scalar unit. ## 2. An exact finite-mode formula, with its endpoint currents Let psi be the ordinary digamma and define H_N(s)=psi(s+1)-psi(N-s), A_N(s)=1/2-H_N(s)/(2pi*i), B_N(s)=1/2+H_N(s)/(2pi*i), t=exp(2pi*i*s). The digamma recurrence and reflection, equivalently the convergent partial fractions of pi cot(pi s), give exactly S_N(s)=pi cot(pi s)+H_N(s), w_N^+(s)=A_N(s)+B_N(s)t, w_N^-(s)=B_N(s)+A_N(s)t^(-1). (3) Thus any fixed integer power has a finite, explicit binomial packet of INTEGER Fourier modes. No limit is used in (3). On the physical strip -1<Re s<N the coefficients A_N,B_N are holomorphic. In a scaled compact substrip, their asymptotics and derivative bounds are those of the elementary uniform digamma expansion; for example H_N(Nz)=Log(z)-Log(1-z)+O(1/N), 0<Re z<1. (4) The logarithms in (4) are the consistent ones in this simply connected strip. On nonreal compact scaled chambers the finite packets therefore add only integer linear logarithmic marks to the original leading phase. This decomposition is NOT a license to discard its endpoint currents. At s=-r<0, H_N has residue -1; at s=N+r, H_N also has residue -1 in the s coordinate. In either case A_N and B_N have opposite simple polar parts. In their COMPLETE combination (3) these parts cancel; the derivative of t supplies the finite correction which makes the window zero rather than one at that integer. Higher powers cancel their complete principal parts and finite jets as well. Splitting the modes and crossing those poles independently loses that source cancellation. For the macroscopic off-real symbol one may use S_N(Nz)=integral_0^1 du/(z-u)+O(1/N). The integral is nonzero off [0,1]. On Im z>0, w^+ has no exponential factor; on Im z<0 its leading factor is exp(2pi*i*Nz). For w^- the roles reverse, with factor exp(-2pi*i*Nz) on Im z>0. Thus (2)'s wrong-side growth is a REAL leading effect, precisely an integer mark, not a tame multiplier that may be erased. There is a useful precise local choice. On any compact scaled chamber K disjoint from the real axis, the uniform digamma expansion gives H_N(Nz)=h(z)+O_K(1/N), h(z)=Log z-Log(1-z). Use w^+ when Im z>0 and w^- when Im z<0. Uniformly with every fixed number of z derivatives, that FAVORABLE window is respectively 1/2-h(z)/(2pi*i)+O_K(1/N), 1/2+h(z)/(2pi*i)+O_K(1/N). (4a) Both limiting functions are nonzero: a zero would require h(z)=+pi*i or -pi*i, hence exp(h)=z/(1-z)=-1, an impossibility. Compactness therefore gives fixed positive upper and lower bounds for the favorable window on K, for all sufficiently large N. The discarded exponential in deriving (4a) is only an ESTIMATE inside that specified chamber; the exact packet (3) is still used for transport. Consequently, at any supplied regular joint critical point where all physical forms ell/N are nonreal, choose each window orientation favorably there. The completed scalar has the SAME leading phase and a nonzero bounded local amplitude multiplier. This is an exact completion with a controlled microlocal symbol, not an assertion that the original cycle reaches that point. When some forms are real, one must keep both modes and their real zeros; (4a) supplies no such local ellipticity there. ## 3. Fixed powers cancel ALL factorial poles in a fixed joint box The actual factorial interpolant has the exact integer divisor ord_(s=n) Fhat_N(s)=floor(n/N), n integer. (5) It has no noninteger zero or pole. For n>=0 the zeros come from the denominator Gamma(Nk-s) of its defining product, one for each Nk<=n. For n<0 its numerator Gamma(s+1) and Gamma(Nk+s+1) give 1+floor((-n-1)/N)=-floor(n/N) poles. This also follows from its exact N-shift, with the original strip nonzero. The conjugate negative-root factorial has the SAME divisor. Suppose a physical linear state form ell takes values with |Re ell|<=Lambda N in the chosen complex box. For either exponent epsilon=+1 or -1 and either window orientation eta, choose a fixed integer p>Lambda+1. Then G_(epsilon,eta)(ell) =Fhat_(+ or -)(ell)^epsilon *w_N^eta(ell)^p (6) is holomorphic on that box and vanishes at EVERY outside-band integer ell. At a physical integer it is exactly the original factorial or its inverse. Indeed its divisor there is p+epsilon floor(n/N)>=1 outside the band. The half-open endpoints are exactly 0,...,N-1; there is no division by F_N or a substituted value at a pole. Use (6) for EACH factorial occurrence of the original coefficient. Add an entire cardinal factor for any physical head/transfer form not already present. This proves holomorphy also at dependent or simultaneous collisions: each individual meromorphic factor has already been canceled, so no appeal to a generic transverse intersection or an unproved saturation quotient is needed. The original positive coefficient has factorial forms input a,b; transfer k; outputs c=b+k, e=a-k, Fhat(c)Fhat(a)/[Fhat(k)Fhat(b)Fhat(e)]. (7) The negative coefficient is its actual mirror. Thus every physical input, output and transfer is one of the forms in (7). All Cartan Gaussians, kappa, pivot and external source factors stay unchanged. Formula (6) only changes the off-lattice analytic completion. ## 4. Exact whole original scalar with unwrapped gluing preserved Start with the original COMPLETE balanced-basis scalar, after the justified whole-word marked trace conversion, K_N=chi_N/N Tr[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)W_N]. (8) Let v consist of the b initial physical head labels and the m nonnegative physical transfer indices. At each signed crossing the exact update is (a,b)->(b+sigma*k,a-sigma*k). Every intermediate physical head label is an INTEGER LINEAR form in v. The ordinary trace closure is the EXACT integer linear equation Lv=0, not equality modulo N. A fixed integral basis B of ker_Z L gives a bijection v=B u from Z^r to all integer closed paths. It is obtained by integer row and column operations on the fixed diagram matrix; no quantum-level or source normalization factor occurs. Every physical closed path has all initial/transfer coordinates in [0,d], so a fixed rational left inverse of B bounds |u|<=C N. Choose an integer coordinate box containing them. All physical forms ell(Bu) then satisfy |Re ell|<=Lambda N on a slightly enlarged fixed O(N) complex box, with Lambda depending only on the diagram and box. Use the window powers in Section 3 on its actual scalar summand, calling the resulting holomorphic function F_N(u). At EVERY valid integer state F_N has its EXACT original value. At EVERY invalid integer state at least one physical form lies outside 0,...,d, and its completed factor is zero; all other completed factors are holomorphic. Hence it contributes zero even when the unwindowed formula had simultaneous poles. Therefore, exactly, K_N=chi_N/N sum_(u in integer box) F_N(u). (9) The same sum is its product cotangent residue contour. Any additional integer states crossed while enlarging it inside the specified box have zero residue unless they are original physical states. All intersections are ordinary multivariate residues of a HOLomorphic scalar summand, so no derivative residue is silently omitted. This is a genuine complete-source comparison for arbitrary fixed braid width, preserving unwrapped routing and all marked scalar factors. ### Explicit knot coordinates, dimension and forced-cut faces For a ONE-component closure the lattice above has the particularly simple explicit coordinates u=(t,k_1,...,k_m), dimension m+1. (9a) Start at the distinguished cut with color t and follow the oriented physical knot once. At the two visits to crossing j, the strand color changes respectively by +sigma_j k_j and -sigma_j k_j. Hence every physical arc color is exactly ell_r=t+sum_j epsilon_(r,j) k_j, epsilon_(r,j) in {0,1,-1}. (9b) Each k occurs with both signs on the complete traversal, so the final color is t for EVERY integer transfer vector. Conversely any original closed path has one t and its unique transfers, and this traversal recovers all its colors. This is an integer bijection with counting Jacobian ONE, not a modulo-N or rational parametrization. Equivalently the one-cycle closure permutation has rank b-1 after subtracting the identity, so its m+b variables have kernel dimension m+1. The exact original state polytope is 0<=k_j<=d, 0<=ell_r(t,k)<=d for every physical arc. (9c) The summand in these coordinates is the product of the original signed r(a_j,b_j;k_j), every original ordinary-head pivot evaluated on its closure arc, and chi_N/N. Thus the construction is concrete for arbitrary braid width and involves no unknown knot scalar. The cube 0<=t,k_j<=d contains all states; (6) analytically kills the invalid intermediate colors inside that cube. A larger fixed O(N) complex box is chosen only for contour transport and pole accounting. Its STRICT real interior is nonempty for every nonempty one-component diagram: set t=d/2 and all k_j=delta d, with 0<delta<1/(4(m+1)). Formula (9b) puts every arc in (d/4,3d/4), and each transfer is strictly between zero and d. There is no assumption that a quantum coefficient has no cancellations at that point; this is an exact source-domain assertion. A fixed highest-cut t=0 presentation is different and can force k_j=0 or other boundary equalities. It must then be treated on its actual affine face, with the corresponding constant factorials kept; one cannot impose a missing normal stationary equation or pretend that face has a full strict interior. The construction used here instead makes the justified WHOLE original marked-trace conversion to I/N BEFORE decomposing paths, yielding the original average over t. It does not replace a cut separately in any clock sector or inserted current. Thus the strict interior in (9c) is obtained without changing the original selected scalar or discarding its fixed-cut boundary mechanism. Links may retain the general lattice formulation above. For a completely explicit contour, take each t,k_j on a rectangle with real edges -1/2 and N-1/2 and any fixed nonzero imaginary height. Its product encloses exactly the integer cube 0,...,d in these m+1 coordinates. Since the coefficients in (9b) are 0,+1,-1, every arc form on that contour has |Re ell|<=(m+1)N. Thus, for example, the fixed choice p=m+4 at EACH factorial occurrence suffices there. For a larger box |Re(t,k_j)|<=C N, choose p>C(m+1)+2 instead. The exact integral is (9)'s original chi_N/N times (2pi*i)^(-(m+1)) integral F_N(u) product_j [pi cot(pi*u_j) du_j]. (9d) There is no geometric Jacobian or root-grid multiplicity in (9d). ### Explicit original action at complete color For clarity the leading action in Section 5 can be read directly from the retained original coefficients, not an unspecified operator. Let x=-q^(-1), Q=q^2=exp(2pi*i/N), and use the continuous choice Log x=i*pi-i*pi/N. The two exact signed coefficients are r_+(a,b;k)=kappa x^(-a-b+k) Q^(b(a-k)) Fhat_+(b+k)Fhat_+(a) /[Fhat_+(k)Fhat_+(b)Fhat_+(a-k)], r_-(a,b;k)=kappa^(-1) x^(a+b-k) Q^(-a(b-k)) Fhat_-(a+k)Fhat_-(b) /[Fhat_-(k)Fhat_-(a)Fhat_-(b-k)]. (9e) Here Fhat_-(z)=conjugate(Fhat_+(conjugate(z))). The second formula is the actual complete-color swap/conjugation relation, including the unit Cartan scalar; it is not a replacement R matrix. All its physical inputs and outputs are the unwrapped forms in (9b). On a regular marked chamber put L_+(s)=integral_0^s Log(1-exp(2pi*i*v)) dv, L_-(s)=integral_0^s Log(1-exp(-2pi*i*v)) dv. The branches are the actual factorial branches continued from 0<s<1. For instance L_+(s)=[Li2(1)-Li2(exp(2pi*i*s))]/(2pi*i) on that marked continuation. With A=a/N, B=b/N and K=k/N, the state-dependent leading actions in (9e) are explicitly s_+=i*pi*(-A-B+K)+2pi*i*B*(A-K) +L_+(B+K)+L_+(A)-L_+(K)-L_+(B)-L_+(A-K), s_-=i*pi*(A+B-K)-2pi*i*A*(B-K) +L_-(A+K)+L_-(B)-L_-(K)-L_-(A)-L_-(B-K). (9f) Thus S_0 is the sum of (9f), with every A,B,K replaced by its ACTUAL source linear form in y=(t,k)/N. The exact kappa factors, the original external chi_N, and x^(1-N) factors in the pivots remain in (9d); their state-independent phase is not discarded. The pivot's remaining Q^(-a)=exp(-2pi*i*A) and the O(1) correction from Log x are explicit amplitudes, not additional N-order state actions. The usual uniform factorial symbol is applied only on regular compact marked chambers, never across a factorial zero by assertion. Equation (9f) therefore gives the actual complete bulk stationary problem in the m+1 physical coordinates. ## 5. Leading equations and the still necessary global estimate Write y=u/N, and suppose a regular open chamber admits the original leading scalar action N S_0(y). Expand each power by the EXACT finite mode formula (3), retaining its coefficients and all matched endpoint currents. A mode indexed by integers n_ell has leading action N[S_0(y)+2pi*i sum_ell n_ell ell(B y)]. (10) Its full stationary equations are partial_(y_j) S_0+2pi*i sum_ell n_ell partial_(y_j)ell(B y)=0. (11) All added numbers are integers. Exponentiating (11) gives the SAME original classical gluing equations. At a regular FULL stationary point its retained integer marks are included by the already proved phase/regulator identity. It is not an identification of a selected geometric cycle from nonzero density alone. Equations (10)--(11) have only been asserted on regular leading chambers with the appropriate slow symbol control. Across a real window layer one must retain its whole finite-mode packet, and at outside-band integers the matched currents in Section 2. The function F_N is holomorphic there, but its separated mode terms may have poles. Nor does holomorphy bound the original factorial action or a global transport mass. The window bound (2) is subexponential on normal tubes, but a macroscopic wrong-side contour changes the leading integer-marked action and must be calibrated as such. These facts are retained, rather than claiming the windows are harmless weights. The construction removes scalar factorial POLE exits in a fixed box without imposing a new invariant or changing discrete gluing. It does not yet supply the full high-action deformation, a sharp bulk bound, or geometric noncancellation of the original knot state. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_scalar_cardinal_source_completion.py): exact window values and finite packets, factorial divisor cancellation, half-plane growth, both literal signed coefficients and original full signed-source lattice comparisons. The audit checks 288 finite-mode packets, 96 whole-plane bound checks, 108 Barnes divisor packages, 670 exact original signed coefficient checks, and eight complete-source lattice comparisons on braid widths two through four. These finite checks supplement the proofs above; they are not all-level proofs or tests of a volume claim.

title: Actual shared quantum flags and their charged exchange
text: # Actual shared quantum flags and their charged exchange Research note, 28 October 2026. This derives an explicit quantum flag exchange from the **original** finite crossing, including its actual cup and marked cap. It is more than independent choices of four Fermat frames: the flags below belong to the same quantum meridians and are transported by the original crossing. The result is a cleared quantum cross-ratio relation, with a compulsory finite wall and even-level wrap sign. It does not lift the three five-point certificates of [the classical crossing cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) to a complete quantum Pachner identity. In particular, no positive geometric kernel or nonzero geometric coefficient is inferred. The new calculation identifies exactly which finite relative wall such a lift must preserve. ## 1. The actual quantum meridian Use the original balanced factorial basis, with q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, rho=q-q^(-1), Z e_a=Q^a e_a, K=x Z^(-1), e=q rho^2 E, f=F. Here E and F are the original nilpotent matrices. Introduce a cyclic completion S_mu of the raising shift: S_mu e_a=e_(a+1) (a<d), S_mu e_d=mu e_0, S_mu^N=mu I, mu!=0. Then, exactly, f=(1-Z)S_mu, e=(x^(-1)-K)S_mu^(-1) -(x^(-1)-Qx)mu^(-1)|d><0|. (1) The first identity already has its original zero endpoint. The second subtracts its one extra endpoint. Set L_+=[[K,e],[0,1]], L_-=[[1,0],[-Kf,K]], G=L_-^(-1)L_+=[[K,e],[fK,fe+K^(-1)]]. (2) All entries are original finite matrices. The lower left entry is fK, including its quantum ordering. Direct multiplication using fe=c-QK-K^(-1), ef=c-K-QK^(-1), c=x^(-1)+Qx, gives the ordinary matrix identity G^2-cG+Q I=0. (3) The cyclic column is an exact relative eigenflag: G (1,S_mu)^t=x^(-1)(1,S_mu)^t -(x^(-1)-Qx)(P_d,0)^t. (4) Thus its failure away from completeness is the original (1-M^2) endpoint, with M=-qx. It has not been deleted. At completeness x=-q^(-1), write lambda=x^(-1)=Qx and k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1). The endpoint in (4) vanishes for every mu. In particular, the same original e,f admit all these completed flag marks. One has G-lambda I=(1,S_mu)^t(K-lambda)(1,-S_mu^(-1)), (G-lambda I)^2=0, [[1,0],[-S_mu,1]] G [[1,0],[S_mu,1]] =[[lambda,e],[0,lambda]]. (5) The off-diagonal translation is the original nilpotent e. Normalizing it to a unit by inverting e would annihilate this finite module, since e^N=0. ## 2. Exact mixed-color Hurwitz transport On two original heads define H_1=G_1, H_2=L_(-,1)^(-1)G_2 L_(-,1). Let B be the original checked positive crossing from (x_1,x_2) to (x_2,x_1). A superscript o denotes these output colors. The common scalar Cartan line can be included in B or retained externally; it cancels from each intertwining identity below. There is no change to that line, the framing, the pivot, or the peripheral normalization. At every level and nonzero colors, B H_1=H_2^o B, B H_2=H_2^o H_1^o (H_2^o)^(-1) B. (6) Here is a finite proof. Before the flip, write the original crossing as R_0=D P(e_1 f_2), where P(z)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)z^h/(Q;Q)_h. Since (e_1f_2)^N=0, its finite recurrence is P(Q^(-1)z)=(1-Q^(-1)z)P(z). Cartan conjugation gives D e_1 D^(-1)=e_1 K_2 and D f_2 D^(-1)=K_1^(-1) f_2. Therefore R_0 e_1=e_1 K_2 R_0, R_0 K_1=(K_1-e_1 K_2 f_2)R_0. (7) After flipping, these are exactly the upper row of the first identity (6). Its lower right follows from (3) and fK=QKf. For completeness, its remaining lower-left error X satisfies e'X=Xe'=0 by (3), where e'=e_2 K_1. At generic colors, the original e_2 has one-dimensional kernel and cokernel. Consequently X could only map a state (a,d) to (u,0). Every lower-left term has integer total degree +1, forcing u=a+N, which is outside the original head. Thus X=0. Laurent continuation proves the exceptional-color identities as well. For the second identity, note H_2 H_1=(L_(-,2)L_(-,1))^(-1)L_(+,2)L_(+,1). The original Hopf intertwiner preserves both displayed coproduct matrices. Together with the first identity, this proves the second. Thus the shared meridians themselves have the actual quantum Hurwitz law, before taking a symbol. ## 3. The original complete crossing exchanges coupled flags For the rest of the note both colors are complete. Choose the convention that B has its original common Cartan scalar kappa retained externally, as in coefficient (11). All conjugation identities are independent of this convention; the unstripped crossing has B_full p=kappa p in Section 5. Choose the two cyclic wrap marks to be S_1^N=mu I, S_2^N=k mu I. (8) From this section onward, B denotes the original checked crossing with its common Cartan scalar kappa retained in the unchanged external line: the full crossing is kappa B. The conjugation identities are insensitive to this convention, while the cup identity in Section 5 reads Bp=p and therefore (kappa B)p=kappa p for the full crossing. The second mark is compulsory: it is not generally mu when N is even. Let S_1,S_2 act on the first and second original head and put t_1=S_1, t_2=f_1+K_1^(-1)S_2, Delta=t_2-t_1=Z_1(lambda S_2-S_1), gamma=(K_2-lambda)S_2^(-1)K_1=-e_2K_1, v=Z_2^(-1)+S_1e_2. (9) The column (1,t_2)^t is L_(-,1)^(-1)(1,S_2)^t, so these are flags of the shared H_i of Section 2, rather than four independently chosen lines. The original crossing satisfies B S_1 B^(-1)=t_2, B S_2 B^(-1)=lambda S_1 v^(-1). (10) In particular, (10) supplies an explicit generator for the flag transport; its right side does not contain an unknown conjugated crossing kernel. Here is a coefficient proof, including its endpoint. The original coefficient from (a,b) to (b+h,a-h), after stripping only its common external Cartan scalar, is r(a,b,h)=x^(-a-b-h)Q^(ab-(b+1)h) F_a F_(b+h)/(F_(a-h)F_b F_h), F_j=(Q;Q)_j, 0<=h<=min(a,d-b). (11) This follows directly from the original E coefficient and Cartan diagonal, using Qx^2=1. Its two finite Pascal recurrences are r(a+1,b,h)=(1-Q^(b+h))r(a,b,h-1) +lambda Q^(b+h)r(a,b,h), Q^(-(a-h))r(a,b+1,h) +(lambda-xQ^(-(a-h)))r(a,b+1,h-1) =lambda r(a,b,h). (12) Illegal transfer indices are zero. In the interior these follow simply by dividing successive factorial products. The first recurrence is B S_1=t_2 B. The second is v B S_2=lambda S_1 B. (13) At a=d, the first wrap row equates mu x^(-b) to mu_2 k^(-1)x^(-b). At b=d, the second wrap row equates mu_2 x^(-a)Q^(-a) to mu k^(-1)x^(-a)Q^(-a). The other terms in the first endpoint row cancel by the first recurrence with F_N=0. For the second endpoint row, the nonzero wrapped input coefficients have r(a,0,h)/r(a,0,h-1)=x(1-Q^(a-h+1)); substitution gives the required adjacent cancellation directly. Both rows therefore hold precisely for mu_2=k mu, since k^2=1. These are the original endpoint rows, not cyclic replacement crossings. Finally v^N=1, as shown below, so (13) implies (10). Freezing both wraps to one at even N fails (10): even a single original crossing detects the missing wrap sign. ## 4. Cleared quantum cross-ratio and finite collision wall The following identities are exact in the original finite matrix algebra: Delta gamma-Q gamma Delta=lambda(Q-1), v=1+lambda^(-1)Delta gamma, Delta v=Q v Delta, v^N=1, Delta^N=gamma^N=0. (14) For example, put a=S_1,b=lambda S_2. They commute, and Delta=Z_1(b-a). With gamma=(xZ_2^(-1)-lambda)b^(-1)Z_1^(-1), direct multiplication gives the first two identities. The third then follows from the first. In v, the summands Z_2^(-1) and S_1e_2 Q-commute, with N-th powers 1 and 0, respectively, proving v^N=1. In Delta, the two summands Q-commute, and their root binomial powers give Delta^N=lambda^N(k mu)-mu=0. The identity gamma=-e_2K_1 immediately gives gamma^N=0. Let t_3=B t_2 B^(-1). Since the original B preserves F_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2 and K_tot=K_1K_2, equation (10) gives t_3=t_2-Q Delta v^(-1). (15) Indeed t_2=F_tot+x K_tot^(-1)S_2, so substitution of (10) reduces (15) to S_2v-Q Z_2^(-1)S_2 +lambda Z_2^(-1)S_1=lambda S_1. This is just the original complete formula for e_2. Thus the four shared flags obey the **cleared** ordered cross-ratio identities v(t_3-t_2)=t_1-t_2, (1-v)(t_3-t_2)=t_3-t_1. (16) The mnemonic fraction (t_3-t_1)(t_3-t_2)^(-1)=1-v would require an inverse of t_3-t_2. It is **not defined or asserted in this finite module**. Equation (16) is the actual cleared relation; no difference was inverted to prove it. Equivalently, the Möbius denominator for H_2(1,t_1)^t is exactly (H_2)_11+(H_2)_12 t_1=xv, (17) which is invertible, with N-th power x^N. Thus the relevant transport does not fail because of its Möbius denominator. It fails to belong to an ordinary generic cross-ratio field because Delta, and hence t_3-t_2, is nilpotent. This is a precise obstruction to a direct generic five-flag field lift: localizing this actual finite module at Delta gives the zero module. The same applies to inverting e in (5). It does not obstruct an identity first established in a tagged generic module and then compressed with a retained relative source, or a contour/residue construction that keeps this collision wall. Such a construction is still needed for the three classical certificates. ## 5. The original cap selects the charged wall with unit pairing At completeness the actual dual color is again x. The original left cup and averaged marked cap, in the same balanced basis used above, are p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, m p=1. (18) They retain their original scalar factors. The full exterior Cartan, framing and peripheral line multiply both sides as before; they have not been assigned new values. Directly, Bp=p, Delta p=0, vp=Qp, (D+1)p=Np, D=J_1+J_2. (19) The first identity follows as well from the original Hopf cup intertwiner and its zero-transfer coefficient. For a direct check of Delta p, the ordinary raising terms cancel using lambda x=1. The two exceptional (0,0) terms cancel using mu_2=k mu and x^N=k. For v, on the degree-d fiber its diagonal is Q^(a+1) and its raising entry is lambda(1-Q^(a+1)); the ratio p_a/p_(a-1)=x gives vp=Qp. Define its exact spectral projectors by E_j(v)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^d Q^(-jr)v^r. Then the original, full marked pairing satisfies m E_j(v) p=delta_(j,1), (20) for every N, including N=2. Hence the collision is not an auxiliary source choice or an unmarked matrix singularity. The actual source lands on v=Q, and this wall has pairing one. In a classical limit v tends to 1 on this cup and the corresponding 1-v cross-ratio tends to 0. This describes the **cap** wall; it does not say that a bulk geometric tetrahedron in an entire closed word must degenerate. The finite integer carry is also explicit. Write B_i for |0><d| on head i. Then [D,Delta]=Delta-N Z_1(lambda k mu B_2-mu B_1), m Z_1 lambda k mu B_2 p=m Z_1 mu B_1 p=mu/N. (21) Thus the signed endpoint currents cancel on the cup, while each original endpoint has nonzero augmented weight. A cyclic congruence or the cancellation of the two currents does not erase this wall. The separate identity (D+1)p=Np retains the actual affine charge. Equation (21) does not by itself identify that cap charge with a Pachner internal edge winding; the required typed gluing of the five-point move remains to be constructed. Equations (6), (10), and (16) can be composed at every crossing of an arbitrary bridge or braid word, with its actual cups and caps. They provide closed local shared-flag updates and the exact boundary ideal (19), rather than an assumed scalar preservation under a hypothetical tetrahedral kernel. They do not prove that the three quantum five-point moves preserve that boundary ideal after a change to a positive triangulation chart. ## 6. A finite mixed cyclic/nilpotent two-to-three identity There is a constructive local identity on precisely these original heads. It uses the same literature cyclic atom as [the four-atom note](four_cyclic_atoms.md), not a new definition of a quantum invariant. For an auxiliary parameter t with t^N!=1 retain the marked root nu^N=1-t^N and set C_t=mathfrak_d_N(tv;Q), mathfrak_d_N(z;Q)=(1-z^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(j=1)^d(1-Q^j z)^(-j/N), P(A)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)A^h/F_h. (22) The functional calculus is well defined because v^N=1. All roots, including the half roots needed at even N, are anchored at t=0 and then continued together.
