Thus C_t is the actual determinant-normalized literature atom, including its scalar and root marks. Its finite functional equation is mathfrak_d_N(Qz;Q)/mathfrak_d_N(z;Q) =nu/(1-z). Using Delta v=QvDelta gives C_t Delta C_t^(-1) =nu^(-1)Delta(1-Q^(-1)t v). (23) For every scalar a there is consequently the exact finite two-to-three identity C_t P(aDelta) =P(a nu^(-1)Delta) P(-a nu^(-1)Q^(-1)t Delta v) C_t. (24) To prove it put X=a nu^(-1)Delta and Y=-a nu^(-1)Q^(-1)t Delta v. Then XY=QYX. The finite Q-binomial theorem with this ordering gives P(X+Y)=P(X)P(Y). Every term of total Delta-degree >=N vanishes, including the apparent extra degrees in the product on the right. Equations (23) and this polynomial identity prove (24) at the actual root; no individual infinite compact product is specialized. The same retained cyclic atom C_t, with exactly the same determinant and root scalar, occurs once on each side. This identity is boundary compatible in a literal sense: C_t p=mathfrak_d_N(tQ;Q)p, P(aDelta)p=P(-a nu^(-1)Q^(-1)t Delta v)p=p, m C_t P(aDelta)p =m P(a nu^(-1)Delta) P(-a nu^(-1)Q^(-1)t Delta v) C_t p =mathfrak_d_N(tQ;Q). (25) The factor in (25) has not been replaced by one. Each side also retains the original common exterior scalar line. After dividing the **equality** by its same displayed factor, both sides are the original marked unit pairing; this is a check of source transport, not a redefinition of the original invariant. At t^N=1 the separate nu^(-1) factors cannot be evaluated. The whole source comparison in (25), with its displayed common factor, is the retained relative expression. Its quotient is identically one and extends as such. An independent insertion of C_t into a closed invariant would change its value; (24) authorizes replacing a specified local factor product by its equal product, with the exterior source left intact. Thus there is an all-level mixed cyclic/nilpotent 2<->3 identity on the actual coupled quantum flags, preserving their charged cap ideal and source factor. The auxiliary t has not been identified with a geometric tetrahedral edge parameter. In particular, (24) alone does not exhibit the factor products of the three classical certificates inside the actual four-atom crossing word. That specific identification, together with its shared flags and all central factors, is the next missing local equality. ## 7. What is new, and what remains on the critical path The existing [four cyclic atoms](four_cyclic_atoms.md) and [Verma transport](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) already prove compact-dilogarithm factorizations and generic/tagged pentagons. The [classical crossing cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) already identifies the shared shadow octahedron and gives its three five-point certificates. The [four-line Fermat calculation](actual_four_line_fermat_crossing_and_conditioning.md) already gives independent coherent-frame matrix elements. The additional result here is an explicit **actual** coupled quantum flag/Ptolemy update (10), (14)--(16), including its typed even-N wrap, the original selected wall (18)--(21), and the mixed finite identity (24) on these same heads. It neither chooses new independent face flags nor merely renames a conjugation of the crossing. It supplies algebraic relations and a boundary ideal that any claimed lift of the three classical certificates can now be tested against. The missing local theorem is still a refactorization of those certificates with this finite collision source and all central/root factors retained. No resulting positive geometric kernel, geometric intersection coefficient, or volume estimate is asserted here. ## 8. Reproducible exact audit Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_shared_quantum_flags.py The independent evaluator starts from the original E coefficients and Cartan diagonal, rather than (10). It checks 21 mixed-color quantum Hurwitz families, 21 complete typed shared-flag families, all projectors (20), and four even-level frozen-wrap failures, for N=2,...,8 over exact prime fields. It additionally checks 42 identities (24) at nonzero finite-field Fermat parameters t^N+nu^N=1, including their literal source factors. This test uses the cyclic functional equation to construct a scalar representative of C_t. Identity (24) is homogeneous in that same scalar on both sides; the proof (22)--(24) retains the actual determinant-normalized atom and its marked roots. The audit also checks the original cup, marked pairing, and affine charge. The all-level proofs are the finite recurrences and matrix identities above, not an extrapolation from these tests.

title: A strict separation between shared-radius certificate classes
status: Exact obstruction and strict refinement on one marked source
text: # A strict separation between shared-radius certificate classes 31 October 2026. Exact rational certificates and rigorous interval bounds. The [finite-cover theorem](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md) allows a shared positive radius vector for each branch of genuine source labels. Here one original marked source provably fails the simpler anchored test but passes a forty-branch refinement. This separates the certificate classes without asserting that an actual quantum invariant exceeds volume. ## 1. The original source and an impossible anchor Take width $k=3$, the first original top-cap mark, and the zero-based word $$ (1,3,0,2,4,1,3,0,2,4,1,3,0,2,4,1,3).\tag{1} $$ The original compiler gives $17$ ports and $19$ white faces. Faces $0$ and $16$ are protected; all other faces have target $d=N-1$. The white sphere has $34$ distinct triangular cells and $51$ edges, each incident to two cells. The marked edge is MAIN. The existing labeled simple-packing certificate therefore applies to this actual source. Write $X_e=Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y)$ and $H_e=\max(X_e,\log b,\log c)$, omitting protected logarithms. The RIGHT anchor at zero-based port $12$ has quartet $(0,11,16,14)$. Its retained triangle has only one ordinary coordinate, so $$ A_{12,R}(L)=\max\left(\log L_{11}, \tfrac12\log L_{11}+\tfrac12\log L_{14}\right). $$ Use $H_e$ at every spectator, as in the anchored criterion. The [rational anchor certificate](../experiments/actual_shared_radius_anchor_obstruction_certificate.json) contains $84$ nonnegative rational variables. At spectators $2,4,7$ it assigns mass $\lambda_e$ to the complete pair of triangle rows and mass $1-\lambda_e$ to the pure-$b$ endpoint. Other spectators retain both complete rows. At the anchor it assigns loads $\beta$ to face $14$ and $1-\beta$ to face $11$, with $0\leq\beta\leq1/2$ and zero entropy. Each weighted triangle row has total mass $\lambda_e/2$. Every ordinary face target is exactly one after including the pure-middle and anchor loads; protected loads are zero. The verifier checks these rational identities, both spectator rows, and the original compiler and mark. For every shared vector $L$, the triangle Fenchel formula and $\max(a,b)\geq\lambda a+(1-\lambda)b$ give $$ C_{12,R}(L)\geq E_{\mathrm{flow}}. $$ All logarithmic terms cancel by the exact face equations. This is weak duality; it requires neither an attained optimizer nor an interchange of an infimum and a supremum. A separate positive rational vector $L^{\mathrm{up}}$ gives the complete upper bound $$ \Phi_D\leq\sum_eX_e(L^{\mathrm{up}})-\sum_f\log L_f^{\mathrm{up}}. $$ Arb arithmetic at 192 bits, with 8,192 Fourier terms and the explicit Lobachevsky tail bound $1/(2M)$, proves $$ \begin{aligned} E_{\mathrm{flow}}&>19.95975965735,\\ \Phi_D&<19.92324700353,\\ \inf_{L>0}C_{12,R}(L)-\Phi_D&>0.025. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ The certified excess actually exceeds $0.03651$. No shared vector, including an escaping limiting sequence, can pass this anchor. The anchored theorem remains a valid sufficient theorem; its applicability is not universal. The spectator mixtures are comparison atoms of $H_e$. They are not one fixed genuine LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT source sector. Thus (2) does not disprove a universal fixed-sector estimate or the volume conjecture. ## 2. A complete forty-branch cover for the same source Set $B=\{2,4,7,12\}$. Cover all actual non-CROSS strings as follows. * For each nonempty subset $J\subseteq B$, require RIGHT on $J$, allow CROSS/LEFT on $B\setminus J$, and allow all labels elsewhere. This gives $15$ branches. * If no port of $B$ is RIGHT, choose any surviving one-sided label as an anchor, allow CROSS/LEFT at the other ports of $B$, and allow all labels elsewhere. Omitting protected-zero sides leaves $25$ branches. Every non-CROSS string belongs to a branch; none of these branches contains the all-CROSS string. Overlap in the second group is harmless, since each string can be assigned to its first eligible anchor. The [branch certificate](../experiments/actual_sector_cover_certificate.json) contains one positive rational shared vector for each of these forty branches. Protected coordinates remain exactly $0$ and $16$. Each branch uses the actual local label bounds, including $\max(A_C,A_L)=\max(X,\log c)$ on CROSS/LEFT spectators. The same file contains a feasible complete triangle flow with $83$ nonnegative rational corner variables. Every original triangle row sums to $1/2$ and every ordinary face sums to one. Its entropy is a lower bound for $\Phi_D$, independently of any numerical packing calculation. The [portable verifier](../experiments/audit_actual_sector_cover.py) checks the exact original incidence, all face equations, the full branch-cover list, and every shared-radius inequality. At 192-bit precision, using 2,048 Fourier terms and the explicit tails, it proves $$ \begin{aligned} \Phi_D&>19.90751095350,\\ \max_B G_B(L^B)&<19.85303956990,\\ \min_B\bigl[\Phi_D-G_B(L^B)\bigr]&>0.04. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ The smallest certified gap exceeds $0.05447$. The refined criterion therefore succeeds on the same source where the anchored criterion is impossible. This is strict inclusion of **fixed marked-source certificate classes**; unmarked knots may admit other presentations or marks. Giving the first $(1,3)$ layer odd exponents and every later box even exponents makes the original standard plat a knot. The finite-cover theorem then proves the full original volume limit for all seventeen independently sufficiently long fixed signed parameters. This is not a theorem for all three-bridge knots. ## 3. Rigorous evaluation For a half-degree triangle allocation $\alpha$, use $$ C(\alpha)=\frac1\pi\sum_j \left[\Lambda(\pi\alpha_j)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi\alpha_j)\right], \qquad \sum_j\alpha_j=\frac12. $$ A summand is exactly zero at $0$ and $1/2$. For positive weighted triangles, $Q$ uses the original angle formula $\theta_j=\arctan(w_j/\sqrt{\sum_{i<j}w_iw_j})$ and the Legendre identity; a one-positive-coordinate triangle is exactly a half logarithm. Every Lobachevsky evaluation uses its absolutely convergent Fourier series and an enclosing tail ball of radius $1/(2M)$. Both [anchor](../experiments/audit_actual_shared_radius_anchor_obstruction.py) and [cover](../experiments/audit_actual_sector_cover.py) verifiers read saved rational data. Numerical optimization helped locate witnesses but is absent from verification. A general bound for every genuine fixed sector remains open. The endpoint volume theorem does not imply it: the weighted comparison permits concave fractional mixtures that need their own global estimate.

title: A shrinking-arc inner product for the original terminal packet
text: # A shrinking-arc inner product for the original terminal packet 29 October 2026. Weighted Cauchy does not require the full Fourier circle. The exact evaluation norm on a suitably weighted arc is polynomial, uniformly in the arc width. This constructs an additional positive metric on the original complete module. It does not by itself bound its energy by hyperbolic volume. ## 1. An exact polynomial evaluation theorem Let f(t)=sum_(j=0)^d z_j t^j, let a>0, and write t_a(s)=(1+i a s)/(1-i a s), -1<=s<=1, Q_a(s)=(1-i a s)^d f(t_a(s)). (1) The latter is an ordinary polynomial of degree at most d. Define E_(a,d)(f)=1/2 integral_(-1)^1 |Q_a(s)|^2 ds =1/2 integral_(-1)^1 (1+a^2 s^2)^d |f(t_a(s))|^2 ds. (2) Then the SHARP all-polynomial evaluation inequality is |f(1)|^2 <= kappa_d E_(a,d)(f), kappa_d=(2m+1)^2 [binom(2m,m)/4^m]^2 <= d+1, m=floor(d/2). (3) In particular the exact constant does not depend on a. A very small arc need not have an exponential dual-source cost. Proof. Let P_j be the Legendre polynomials, normalized by P_j(1)=1. Integration by parts in their Rodrigues formula gives (1/2) integral P_j P_k = delta_(j,k)/(2j+1), P_(2r)(0)=(-1)^r binom(2r,r)/4^r, P_(2r+1)(0)=0. Expand Q_a in this orthogonal basis and apply Cauchy at zero. Its evaluation norm squared is sum_(r=0)^m (4r+1) b_r^2=(2m+1)^2 b_m^2, b_r=binom(2r,r)/4^r. The equality telescopes using b_r/b_(r-1)=(2r-1)/(2r). Induction gives b_m^2<=1/(2m+1), hence the last bound in (3). Equality in the evaluation bound holds for the reproducing polynomial sum_(j=0)^d (2j+1)P_j(0)P_j(s). The map f->Q_a is an invertible linear map between degree-d polynomial spaces: its inverse is the inverse fractional linear substitution with its denominator cleared. Thus the constant is sharp for every a>0. For the unweighted normalized arc energy E^0_(a,d)(f)=1/2 integral_(-1)^1 |f(t_a(s))|^2 ds, the same proof gives |f(1)|^2 <= kappa_d (1+a^2)^d E^0_(a,d)(f). (4) If d=O(N) and a=N^(-A), A>0 fixed, this extra factor is exp(o(N)). For a=1/N it is 1+O(1/N). The measure in (2) is specified in the Cayley coordinate s; it is not silently replaced by uniform angle. ## 2. The explicit finite Gram and its original co-source Let V_(k,j) be the coefficient of s^k in (1+i a s)^j (1-i a s)^(d-j), and let H_(k,l)=0 for k+l odd and 1/(k+l+1) for k+l even. The coefficient-space Gram of (2) is exactly W_(a,d)=V^* H V >0. (5) All entries are explicit finite rational combinations of powers of a and i. For the row e=(1,...,1), equation (3) says more precisely e W_(a,d)^(-1) e^* = kappa_d. (6) This is an algebraic inner product construction, not an unknown period inserted into the definition of its own norm. Its condition number can be large; no polynomial condition number is asserted or needed. Now use the ACTUAL original terminal packet rows T_j from [the complete terminal construction](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md). They satisfy sum_j T_j=lambda U on every input of the complete module, and are defined before the preceding braid B is chosen. Put f_v(t)=sum_j t^j T_j v, G_(a,epsilon)=T^* W_(a,d) T+epsilon I, epsilon>0. (7) This is a positive definite metric, including when T is singular. Its original final contraction b=sum_j T_j obeys b G_(a,epsilon)^(-1) b^* <= kappa_d <= d+1. (8) For example, factor W=A^*A and use (6) and Cauchy on ATv. The resulting inequality holds for every v; its optimal squared dual norm in G is therefore at most kappa_d. No inverse of T is used. For the complete unchanged original source v=B w_0, |K_N|^2 <= |chi_N|^2 kappa_d [E_(a,d)(f_v)+epsilon ||v||^2]. (9) All external and peripheral factors remain in chi_N. Taking epsilon=exp(-N^2) makes the added term negligible for every fixed original braid, by the already proved exp(O(N log N)) source bound. At arbitrary fixed plat width one can record a fixed number r of physical colors, use the product arc measure, and apply (3) in each variable. The dual cost is product kappa_(d_j)<=product(d_j+1), still polynomial. No source channel is removed. For the original figure-eight, T_j Bp=|(Q;Q)_j|^2>=0 exactly. On every unit-circle arc |f_v(t)|<=f_v(1). Equations (2)--(3) give |K_N|^2/kappa_d <= E_(a,d)(f_v) <=(1+a^2)^d |K_N|^2. (10) Hence any a=N^(-A), A>0, has the same known sharp benchmark rate. This uses the original finite positive formula; it is not a general noncancellation assertion. ## 3. Precisely what localization does and does not accomplish With a=1/N, the extra Cartan parameter in the norm stays within O(1/N) of its original value t=1. The comparison no longer requires a sharp estimate at every fixed t on the unit circle. This is a useful change in the proposed metric, not a proof that the local energy is sharp. Even a degree-one polynomial can have exponentially amplified local energy. Set f_N(t)=1+exp(cN)(t-1), c>0, use d=1 in (1), and obtain Q_a(s)=1+i a s[2exp(cN)-1], E_(a,1)(f_N)=1+(a^2/3)[2exp(cN)-1]^2. (11) For a=N^(-A) this has rate 2c although f_N(1)=1. This is an elementary diagnostic, not a knot counterexample. Polynomial degree, localization and controlled evaluation norm alone do not bound jets of the original source. Using d=N-1 only increases the energy of this same f by the weight (1+a^2s^2)^(d-1), so the issue also occurs in the degree-N ambient space. Conversely choosing an excessively small arc can make the energy arbitrarily close to the unknown |K_N|^2. That would be an exact reformulation, not an independent geometric estimate. The useful remaining assertion is a source-derived bound on (2), at a prescribed scale such as a=1/N, by exp[N Vol(M)/pi+o(N)]. There is also no automatic compactness argument from t->1. The [complete coupon kernel](actual_terminal_effective_cartan_kernel_and_graph.md) has an additional orbital channel; its Fourier coordinates can escape while its character coordinates remain bounded. Arc endpoints need not satisfy the full-circle interior phase stationarity equation. Both the calibrated action and accessibility of such contributions remain to be checked before using representation volume. The finite Cauchy step, including an explicit metric and polynomial dual cost, is proved. The sharp global quantum-energy estimate and geometric survival remain open. ## 4. A quantitative test for amplified source derivatives The same finite polynomial argument gives a useful lower bound on the proposed energy. For d>=1 let r=floor((d-1)/2) and put D_d=sum_(j=0)^d (2j+1)P'_j(0)^2 =[(2r+1)(2r+3)b_r]^2/3 <= (d+2)^3/3. (12) Indeed P'_(2r+1)(0)=(-1)^r(2r+1)b_r; the sum telescopes as in Section 1. Evaluation of the derivative at zero therefore gives E_(a,d)(f) >= a^2 |2f'(1)-d f(1)|^2 / D_d. (13) Here Q'_a(0)=i a[2f'(1)-d f(1)] exactly. The upper bound on D_d follows from b_r^2<=1/(2r+1), 2r+1<=d and 2r+3<=d+2. For the unweighted arc energy divide the right side by (1+a^2)^d. Thus an actual source with an excessive exponential first derivative would refute sharpness of every polynomially shrinking arc in this metric family. A numerical growth trend alone does not prove that derivative exponent. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_shrinking_arc_cauchy_metric.py): The audit checks nine exact rational Gram inverses, sharp evaluation constants and derivative norms; seven complete original terminal source Gram matrices, positive completions and benchmark energy comparisons; and the exact degree-one localization diagnostic. The audit uses rational arithmetic for (6) and independent polynomial quadrature for the complex source.

title: Exact simultaneous unwinding of signed overbridge interiors
text: # Exact simultaneous unwinding of signed overbridge interiors 28 October 2026. Every interior strand contraction within an original overbridge has an exact closed root-of-unity formula, for arbitrary signs and arbitrary regular spectator grids. This is a degree-complement identity, not a Vandermonde formula requiring a central norm to be one. It eliminates ALL such interior variables simultaneously in the original network. Surviving clocks are monotone along each bridge, and the finite binomial factors telescope to a q-multinomial. The spectator-dependent original crossing normalizers and the entire original boundary source remain. The result is still a coupled sum; it does not prove scalar noncancellation or permit an automatic second pass through the underbridges. ## 1. Original port coordinates and all four signed roles Use N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), so x^2=Q^(-1). The actual signed crossing is in its proved regular propagated Fourier frames. Denote inputs by z0,z1 and outputs by z6,z7. The physical OVER pair is (z0,z7) for a positive crossing and (z1,z6) for a negative crossing. The other pair is the UNDER pair. Root propagation is positive: (r6,r7)=(x r1,x r0), negative: (r6,r7)=(x^(-1)r1,x^(-1)r0). (1) Every grid has its actual label in 0,...,N-1, written i,j,k,l at ports 0,1,6,7 respectively. With the opposite physical pair fixed on its original grids, the exact conditional two-leg kernel is rank one. Write it as M_sigma(Zout,Zin)=c_sigma Pout(Zout) Pin(Zin). (2) The full scalar is fixed, for ANY old-grid reference pair, by c_sigma=M_sigma(Zout*,Zin*) /[Pout(Zout*)Pin(Zin*)]. (3) Here M_sigma is the original exact balanced Fourier entry, including kappa, the actual Gaussian, every affine logarithmic mark and all central factors. It is not an unknown knot period. Every denominator in (3) is nonzero on the regular old grids. Crucially c_sigma depends on BOTH spectator labels and roots and retains a leading phase. The closed formulas below show its modulus is tame on the original fixed-central grids. It is never discarded in the contractions. After reordering an opposite-root product by (aZ;Q^(-1))_L=(a Q^(1-L) Z;Q)_L, the signed table has a particularly uniform form. Write (w;Q)_L=product_(j=0)^(L-1)(1-Q^j w). | Sign, physical role | Clock h in 0,...,d | Pin(Z) | Pout(Z) | b | a | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | +, over (0,7) | (j-k) mod N | Z^(-h)(b/Z;Q)_(d-h) | (aZ;Q)_h | z1/x | Q^(-h)/(x z6) | | -, over (1,6) | (l-i) mod N | Z^(-h)(b/Z;Q)_(d-h) | (aZ;Q)_h | Q^(h+2)x z0 | Qx/z7 | | +, under (1,6) | (i-l) mod N | (b/Z;Q)_h | Z^h(aZ;Q)_(d-h) | Q^(1-h)x z0 | Q^(h+1)/z0 | | -, under (0,7) | (k-j) mod N | (b/Z;Q)_h | Z^h(aZ;Q)_(d-h) | x^(-1)z1 | Q/z1 | The positive entries are the actual [paired port interpolants](actual_fourier_port_polynomials_and_profiles.md). For the negative entries apply the COMPLETE antiunitary relation R_minus=P conjugate(R_plus)P, including kappa, and then reorder the Q^(-1) products. This is a finite polynomial identity; no contour shift or unrecorded Gaussian removal is used. The changed clock representatives in the table include the reversed Fourier labels. On the corresponding spectator grids, ALL four rows also satisfy a b=Q^2 x. (4) For example in the positive over row z6=x z1 Q^(-h), so a b=Q^(-h)z1/(x^2 z6)=Q/x=Q^2x. The other rows follow directly from (1) or x^2=Q^(-1). This identity is useful but is not required by the arbitrary-parameter contraction below. ### Closed original normalizers, with no hidden exponential modulus In fact the scalar (3) is elementary for EVERY signed role: c_(+,over) =kappa/N (-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z6^h, c_(+,under)=kappa/N (-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z0^(-h), c_(-,over) =kappa^(-1)/N (-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z7^h, c_(-,under)=kappa^(-1)/N (-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z1^(-h). (4a) These include the original full Cartan scalar. Here is a derivation from the physical matrix, independent of an asymptotic full-function normalizer. The original positive coefficient, for input (a,b), output (a+b-j,j), is kappa x^(-b-j) Q^(jb) F_(a+b-j) F_a/[F_(a-j) F_b F_j], F_t=(Q;Q)_t. For the over factor extract the Fourier coefficient z0^(-h)z7^0. The lowest Pin coefficient and constant Pout coefficient are both one, so this coefficient is exactly c. The original two-head Fourier normalization gives c=kappa z6^h/N^2 *F_h sum_(t=0)^(d-h) [h+t choose t]_Q Q^(-ht). The spectator grid gives z6/(x z1)=Q^(-h), including the cyclic representative. Root complementation turns the summand into (-1)^t Q^(t(t+1)/2)[d-h choose t]_Q. The finite q-binomial theorem therefore makes the sum F_(d-h). Finally F_h F_(d-h)=N (-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2), by factoring F_d=N into the last h factors. This proves the first formula. For the under factor extract input degree zero and output degree h; the same sum has z0^(-h) in place of z6^h. The original antiunitary flip proves the two negative formulas. Reordering its opposite-root Pochhammers permutes factors and adds no scalar. If all central moduli range in a fixed compact subset of (0,infinity), then uniformly in ALL spectator labels and clocks c_0/N <= |c_sigma| <= C_0/N. (4b) Indeed |z|^h=|z^N|^(h/N), 0<=h<N, and every other factor in (4a) has modulus one. The constants depend only on the chosen central compactum. The phase Q^(+/-h(h+1)/2) remains exponentially oscillatory as h scales with N; (4b) does not make the weights positive. During a later deformation to fixed nonunit port radii the monomials in (4a) must still be retained; (4b) concerns the original fixed-central sampling grids and bounded changes of their centers. ## 2. The degree-complement contraction Let 0<=L,s<=d and a,b be arbitrary nonzero parameters. Then CT_Z Z^(-s)(aZ;Q)_L(b/Z;Q)_(d-s) =0, if s>L, =(-a)^s Q^(s(s-1)/2) [L choose s]_Q *(ab Q^(-1);Q)_(L-s), if s<=L. (5) This is a polynomial identity in a,b; it holds at every primitive root of order N, including even and composite N. There is NO condition (ab)^N=1. The mirrored identity is CT_Z Z^r(aZ;Q)_(d-r)(b/Z;Q)_K =0, if r>K, =(-b)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2) [K choose r]_Q *(ab Q^(-1);Q)_(K-r), if r<=K. (6) Proof of (5). Only powers i=s+j from the first polynomial and j from the second can contribute. Root complementation gives [d-s choose j]_Q =(-1)^j Q^(-sj-j(j+1)/2)[s+j choose j]_Q. Use [L choose s+j]_Q [s+j choose j]_Q =[L choose s]_Q [L-s choose j]_Q. After extracting (-a)^s Q^(s(s-1)/2)[L choose s]_Q, the remaining sum is the finite q-binomial expansion of (abQ^(-1);Q)_(L-s). There are no zero denominator factorials: every index is at most d. If s>L the two frequency intervals are disjoint. Exchanging Z with Z^(-1), and a,L with b,K, proves (6). For comparison the general contraction of Z^(r-s)(aZ;Q)_L(b/Z;Q)_K is a terminating 2phi1. For s>=r its argument is ab Q^(L+K), and its three parameters are Q^(s-r-L), Q^(-K); Q^(s-r+1). In (5), K=d-s and r=0, so Q^(-K)=Q^(s+1) cancels the denominator AUTOMATICALLY. This explains why an ordinary tuned Vandermonde test misses the actual generic bridge identity. ## 3. Exact arbitrary-length signed bridge contraction Consider an overbridge with m crossing encounters, in their physical strand order, and with every spectator pair fixed on its actual grids. Put h_j,a_j,b_j,c_j for the data of (2)--(3) at encounter j. This includes arbitrary changes of crossing sign. Let Zin and Zout be the first input and last output grid values. Every ordinary internal physical strand edge is a finite Fourier contraction. Its summand has frequencies between -d and d, so root averaging has NO nonzero alias. Consequently summation over its N labels is N times the constant term in (5). The exact conditional bridge kernel is zero unless d>=h_1>=h_2>=...>=h_m>=0. (7) If (7) holds, put Delta_j=h_j-h_(j+1). Its kernel is exactly N^(m-1) (product_(j=1)^m c_j) *Zin^(-h_1)(b_1/Zin;Q)_(d-h_1) *(a_m Zout;Q)_(h_m) *product_(j=1)^(m-1) W_j, W_j=(-a_j)^(h_(j+1)) Q^(h_(j+1)(h_(j+1)-1)/2) *[h_j choose h_(j+1)]_Q *(a_j b_(j+1) Q^(-1);Q)_(Delta_j). (8) The factor N per eliminated wire is essential: it is a SUM of normalized Fourier matrix entries, rather than an already averaged constant term. Formula (8) retains every c_j and original local normalization. Untouched physical heads simply identify their successive grid labels and do not alter the formula. The q-binomial factors telescope: product_j [h_j choose h_(j+1)]_Q =F_(h_1)/[F_(h_m) product_j F_(Delta_j)], F_r=(Q;Q)_r. (9) This is a q-multinomial with total charge h_1. The lengths in the new bridge Pochhammers sum to h_1-h_m<=d, independent of m. Including the two endpoint Pochhammers, their total length is EXACTLY (d-h_1)+h_m+sum_j Delta_j=d. (9a) There is a stronger bound for the COMPLETE non-Pochhammer, non-multinomial prefactor, uniform even in bridge length. Let u_j be its spectator output, z6 for a positive encounter and z7 for a negative encounter. The signed table gives |a_j u_j|=1. Combining (4a), all link monomials and the endpoint Zin^(-h_1), its modulus is EXACTLY 1/N * [ product_(j<m) |u_j^N|^(Delta_j) *|u_m^N|^(h_m)/|Zin^N|^(h_1) ]^(1/N). (9b) The positive exponents in the numerator sum to h_1<=d. If all central moduli lie between c_min>0 and c_max, (9b) therefore lies between c_min/(N c_max) and c_max/(N c_min), independently of bridge length. Thus the displayed q-multinomial and total-degree-d Pochhammer products carry ALL of this conditioned bridge's exponential modulus. Their phases and the phases in (4a) all remain. Using (4), their arguments can also be written a_j b_(j+1)Q^(-1)=x^(-1)a_j/a_(j+1). (10) For a fixed bridge, if every (a_j b_(j+1))^N differs from one, all Pochhammer factors in (8) are nonzero, so (7) is exactly its support condition. If a central ratio is one there can be further zeros. The complete Pochhammer in (8) must then remain; no such boundary factor is divided out. The formula itself is valid there. The analogous underbridge statement follows from (6): its clocks are nondecreasing, and its q-binomial factors and lengths telescope in the opposite order. This is a separate conditional statement. ## 4. Simultaneous whole-source overbridge unwinding Take ANY signed braid network in the regular propagated frames, with the original endpoint source. Include every specified cup, ordinary cap, FULL marked cap, pivot and external scalar exactly. At an existing source coupon stop a bridge; this does not remove or replace the coupon. A pure pivotal continuation could instead be included as its exact Q-shift and scalar, but this is unnecessary. Select all ordinary strand edges whose first endpoint is an OVER output and whose second endpoint is an OVER input. After suppressing untouched identity-head layers, these edges form disjoint directed paths of crossing over-pairs. Time order excludes directed cycles in an open braid. Each crossing belongs to exactly one path, possibly of length one. These are the maximal overbridges relative to the retained original source cuts. Freeze the labels on every unselected wire, including all original source ports. A selected variable is incident only to the two OVER ports of its neighboring crossings. In particular it occurs in NO spectator UNDER pair. Thus at every crossing (2) applies throughout the selected sums. All sums are finite and all selected paths are disjoint. Their factors separate, so (8) can be applied simultaneously to EVERY path, without invalidating any other path's grid hypothesis. Then sum the remaining labels and apply the SAME endpoint source. This proves exact equality with the original whole knot scalar, and in fact with the entire endpoint operator before its final source. This is an arbitrary-width, arbitrary-sign, arbitrary-bridge-count identity. It is not limited to a twist family or to a special knot. For a diagram source with a nonordinary continuation or a turning coupon, keep that coupon and its incident endpoint labels; no unproved sliding or deletion of it is part of the theorem. ## 5. The coupling that remains Every reduced path coefficient still depends on its spectator under-port labels through h_j,a_j,b_j and the explicit phases and monomials c_j in (4a). Those ports occur in other paths' coefficients and in the original boundary source. The remaining label sum is therefore coupled. Monotonicity (7) and the multinomial (9) survive exactly within every path, but do not make different paths independent. One cannot automatically repeat the operation on ALL underbridges. After the first pass, an under-port variable appears in the new coefficients (8), the length choices h_j, and the original c_j of several overbridges. Its dependence is no longer the isolated complementary pair of (6). A second elimination would need a new identity for this whole transformed source. Likewise, conditional nonzero coefficients in (8) do not exclude cancellation in its remaining whole knot sum. The proved advance is a closed, source-preserving integration of all original overbridge interiors and an explicit monotone charge simplex on each bridge. Relating the remaining coupled period to the global geometric cycle and proving its selected coefficient are still required for a volume limit. ## 6. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.py The audit checks every complementary clock pair at several primitive roots and arbitrary parameters, all four signed port tables against original physical crossing matrices, arbitrary-length mixed-sign bridge contractions, and simultaneous whole signed-word elimination with the original full cup/cap/marked source. No replacement invariant or arbitrary boundary vector is used for the whole-source tests.

title: Actual signed ports and a quantum-multinomial face kernel
status: Exact signed kernel; sufficient one-port corridor
text: # Actual signed ports and a quantum-multinomial face kernel 30 October 2026. This gives the exact original crossing on the polynomial face source, two radius bounds, and a sufficient local geometric certificate for a signed one-port color corridor. It does not claim a universal signed smoothing gap or a simultaneous signed norm estimate. ## 1. Exact kernel, all polynomial degrees Use the original root conventions N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and lambda0=q^(d^2/2), with its prescribed square-root lift. Let T be the [original small-circle face operator](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md), with outer variables x,y and outgoing middle variable c: T c^j = -(q Q^j+q^-1 Q^-j)c^j +(2-Q^j-Q^-j)(x+y)c^(j-1) +(q+q^-1-q Q^-j-q^-1 Q^j)xy c^(j-2). (1) The displayed lowering coefficients vanish at the actual bottom two rows. They are N-periodic in j. Therefore T(c^(mN) f)=c^(mN) T f, (2) and C[x,y,c] is the direct sum, over C[x,y], of invariant blocks c^(mN) span{1,c,...,c^(N-1)}. The characteristic polynomial on each block for C=-T is product_(j=0)^(N-1) [X-q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1)] = 2 ChebyshevT_N(X/2)+2. (3) Cayley--Hamilton proves this annihilator on the WHOLE polynomial space. In particular all confluent root conditions are retained. Let R_+ = r_N(-T), where r_N is the actual crossing polynomial, and R_- its inverse modulo (3). For 0<=j<N, R_+ c^j = (-1)^j sum_(i+k+l=j) q^(j+i^2) {j;i,k,l}_Q c^i x^k y^l. (4) Here {j;i,k,l}_Q=(Q;Q)_j/[(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_k(Q;Q)_l]. Every denominator is nonzero. R_- is the same formula with q replaced by q^-1 (and hence Q by Q^-1). For an arbitrary j=mN+r, 0<=r<N, multiply (4) for r by c^(mN). This is an exact polynomial formula, not a reduction of c^j modulo c^N-1. The actual source crossing is lambda0 R_+; its inverse is lambda0^-1 R_-. All quantum and Cartan phases are present. Proof of (4). Work first at an indeterminate q for this auxiliary triangular interpolation. It is not being identified with the original generic-q crossing germ. The matrix defined by the right side is triangular with diagonal nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)). It commutes with -T. One direct coefficient proof divides the c^i x^k y^l coefficient by (-1)^j q^(j+i^2) (Q;Q)_j/[(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_k(Q;Q)_l]. Put I=Q^i, K=Q^k,L=Q^l,J=IKL and c(Z)=qZ+1/(qZ), b(Z)=2-Z-Z^-1, e(Z)=q+q^-1-q/Z-Z/q. The required identity is c(I)-b(QI) qI (2-K-L)/(1-QI) -e(Q^2 I) Q^2 I^2 (1-K)(1-L)/[(1-QI)(1-Q^2 I)] =c(J)+b(J) q^-1 (2-K-L)/(1-J) -e(J) Q^-1 (1-K)(1-L)/[(1-J)(1-J/Q)]. (5) Clearing denominators gives zero by expansion. Boundary rows follow by the polynomial identity before division. Distinct generic diagonal nodes imply that this is the unique interpolating polynomial in -T with values nu_j. At q=exp(pi i/N), the paired nodes j,d-j collide. Their divided difference has limit -nu_j (N-1-2j)/[2(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))], (6) exactly the derivative of the [original crossing polynomial](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md), not only its nodal values. The finite coefficients of (4) specialize regularly. This proves (4) including the nilpotent component. The inverse follows either from the inverse Hermite conditions or q->q^-1: (1) is invariant under that substitution, whereas every nu_j is inverted. There is also a useful exact alternating Newton expansion. Put S_r=product_(j=1)^r 2sin(pi j/N) and Bhat_r(z)=product_(j=0)^(r-1)(c_j-z)/S_r^2, S_0=1. Then r_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^d (-q)^r Bhat_r(z), r_N^minus(z)=sum_(r=0)^d (-q^-1)^r Bhat_r(z) (6a) modulo (3). Indeed Bhat_r(-T)c^m=0 for r>m. For r<m its x-degree is at most r, whereas the x^m coefficient of Bhat_m(-T)c^m is one: it is product_(j=1)^m (2-Q^j-Q^-j)/S_m^2. Formula (4) gives the x^m coefficient (-q)^m. This triangular comparison determines every Newton coefficient, including the folded nilpotent part. ## 2. Original one-port marked source Use the literal input b/output c convention in the frozen one-port theorem. For displacement p=R-S, c=Q^(-p)b, and the original middle monomial contributes q^(dp). Let P_rem be the full remaining positive face polynomial BEFORE merging b,c. Its marked and exterior faces and all remaining twists are unchanged. If L_h=P_(h-1)(-Omega), put T_h=P_(h-1)(T), with T_1=I,T_2=T. Then the signed deleted-port polynomial is exactly Q_(h,eps) = [lambda0^eps R_eps T_h P_rem]_(c=b), eps in {+1,-1}. (7) R_eps and T_h commute. The original physical endpoints are included because (7) agrees with the actual finite matrix L_h R^eps; this is not a newly cyclically truncated source. The frozen connected one-port argument applies: Q is polynomial, homogeneous of degree d(R-1), and the original finite grid has exactly one target coefficient, with no omitted level alias. The source is N^(R-1) product_remaining[k_a beta_a^2 omega_a^epsilon] [product_ordinary L_f^d] Q_(h,eps)|protected faces=0. (8) This section assumes connected identity smoothing and distinct unmarked middle faces, as in the frozen one-port theorem. The root transpose adapter treats a single protected middle face separately. No ordered or arbitrary simultaneous signed norm bound is inferred from (7). An exact target restriction will be useful below. The merged face is ordinary, so its target is d<N. Both T_h and R_eps preserve the ideal (c^N), and their output is polynomial in every face variable. Therefore every input term divisible by c^N gives, after c=b, a term divisible by b^N and contributes ZERO to (8). One may discard exactly those input terms before bounding this coefficient. This statement holds for all h, not only h=1; it does not discard terms from an arbitrary period. ## 3. Explicit radius penalty and sufficient certificate At fixed positive merged radii let x,y,b be the numerical outer/middle radii, X=x/b,Y=y/b, and S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), S_0=1. The absolute value of every multinomial in (4) is S_j/(S_i S_k S_l). Consequently the EXACT operator norm of R_eps on the weighted coefficient l1 norm in independent x,c,y variables is K_N(X,Y)=max_(0<=r<N) sum_(i+k+l=r) S_r/(S_i S_k S_l) X^k Y^l. (9) For additional variables, or identified outer variables, (9) remains an upper bound. Formula (2) is essential: higher powers of c introduce no larger norm. The original unit lambda0 has absolute value one. The one-port norm theorem therefore gives ||Q_(h,eps)||_ell <=K_N(X,Y) [3+4X+4Y+4XY]^(h-1) P_sm(ell). (10) Every old variable has its final merged weight; evaluation at c=b cannot increase this coefficient norm. P_rem has nonnegative coefficients, so its norm is exactly P_sm(ell). There is a finite, explicit limiting penalty. Put f(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u)) du, kappa(X,Y)=max_(i,k,l>=0, i+k+l<=1) { f(i+k+l)-f(i)-f(k)-f(l)+k log X+l log Y }. (11) Then log K_N(X,Y)=N kappa(X,Y)+O(log N), locally uniformly for positive X,Y. To prove this, the monotone sine-product Riemann sums give log S_j=N f(j/N)+O(log N) UNIFORMLY for 0<=j<N; isolate the first and last unit intervals of the integrable logarithmic endpoint singularities. There are O(N^3) terms in (9), and the uniform modulus of continuity of f is O(eta log(1/eta)). A nearest grid point to a maximizer therefore changes N times (11) by O(log N). These facts give both bounds. The elementary weaker estimate K_N(X,Y)<=(1+X+Y)^(N-1) (12) follows from sin(n theta)/sin(r theta)<=n/r for 1<=r<=n<N, which bounds every sine multinomial by its ordinary counterpart. There is also an exact transfer bound between TWO different norms. Keep all other face weights fixed, use c=b+x+y in the input norm, and c=b in the output norm. For c^(mN+r), its output-to-input norm ratio is at most b^(mN)(b+x+y)^r/(b+x+y)^(mN+r)<=1. (12a) Hence R_eps has norm at most one for this transfer, for BOTH inverse signs. Applying T_h afterwards at the output weights and then merging gives the alternative exact source bound ||Q_(h,eps)||_ell <=[3+4X+4Y+4XY]^(h-1) P_rem(...,b,c=b+x+y,...). (12b) The target denominator is STILL the actual merged face weight b^d. The right side is a split-radius evaluation of the original remaining polynomial; it is not its identity-smoothing evaluation. In particular it has no established geometric volume interpretation. More generally the target restriction permits ANY positive independent input weight c and output weight b. Set B=b/c,X=x/c,Y=y/c. The finite block norm is K_N(B,X,Y)=max_(r<N) sum_(i+k+l=r) S_r/(S_i S_k S_l) B^i X^k Y^l. (12c) Unlike a norm on the whole untruncated polynomial space, (12c) has no condition b<=c: all higher blocks were excluded by the actual target. Define the homogeneous potential G(b,x,y,c)=max_(xi_j>=0, sum xi_j=1) [sum_(j=1)^4 Lambda(pi xi_j)/pi +xi_1 log b+xi_2 log x+xi_3 log y+xi_4 log c], (12d) where Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin u|du. Since f(1-t)=-f(t), the preceding uniform Riemann-sum proof gives log K_N(b/c,x/c,y/c)=N[G(b,x,y,c)-log c]+O(log N). (12e) The actual one-port upper rate is thus the remaining source evaluated at its original, INDEPENDENT middle weights b,c, plus (12e), with the original merged target denominator b^d. This is an exact source norm consequence, not a new side-pairing or a representation theorem. The ordinary multinomial bound gives the useful elementary inequality G(b,x,y,c)<=log max(c,b+x+y). (12f) The entropy in (12d) is strictly concave in the simplex interior. Indeed its negative Hessian, up to a positive factor, is sum cot(alpha_j)v_j^2 on sum v_j=0, where alpha_j=pi xi_j. If all alpha_j<=pi/2 this is positive definite. Otherwise alpha_0>pi/2 is the only such angle. Put beta=sum_(j>0)alpha_j=pi-alpha_0<pi/2. Weighted Cauchy and tan(beta)>sum_(j>0)tan(alpha_j) show that the positive terms strictly dominate -cot(beta)v_0^2; when v_0=0, they are themselves positive unless v=0. This proves the assertion. For positive weights a boundary point with at least two positive coordinates cannot maximize, because inserting a missing coordinate gains a positive epsilon log(1/epsilon) term. At a corner j the largest directional derivative is log(sum_(k!=j) l_k)-log l_j. Thus the maximum is interior exactly under the four strict polygon inequalities, and otherwise it is the dominant corner, with G=log(max l_j). At an interior maximum sin(alpha_j) is proportional to l_j. The alpha_j are half-arcs of the cyclic quadrilateral with those side ratios. Coning it to infinity and triangulating by a vertex fan gives volume sum Lambda(alpha_j): the internal half-arc terms cancel in pairs. This is a local ideal-pyramid interpretation, not a global gluing claim. In particular strict concavity and symmetry give the exact constant G(1,1,1,1)=4 Lambda(pi/4)/pi=:G_*. (12g) For an actual compatible positive radius ell, let Phi_sm(ell) denote the full smoothing upper rate INCLUDING its original sine scalars, and let F0=Vol(Y)/(2pi) be the original complete rate. If g=F0-Phi_sm(ell)-kappa(x/b,y/b)>0, (13) then (8)--(11), together with the existing uniform all-channel rate, give a strict exponential upper gap for this signed small-port source when h=o(N), in particular for h=O(sqrt N). The same conclusion holds for h<=delta N with a sufficiently small fixed delta depending on g and the explicit constant in (10). Polynomial channel counts and the retained k_a factors do not change the rate. This is a SUFFICIENT fixed-radius certificate, not a claim that (13) always holds. The analogous sufficient certificate replaces Phi_sm+kappa by the all-channel upper rate of the split evaluation (12b), with that same merged target denominator. No equality of either optimized certificate with a smoothing capacity is used. ## 4. A local original-packing certificate Assume the selected signed port has distinct unmarked middle faces, connected identity smoothing, and four POSITIVE curvatures x,b,c,y in the original marked right-angled packing. Let F(x,b,y) be the original fold determinant rate, with its proved absolute normalization in [the stationary-character theorem](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md), section6. Define g_port=F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y)-G(b,x,y,c). (13a) If g_port>0, the signed small-port source is exponentially below the original complete rate for h=o(N), or for h<=delta N with a sufficiently small fixed delta. This is a local certificate valid for any certified fixed-width graph satisfying these hypotheses. In particular let A_N have external color N-h at this ONE signed port and N at every other port, with every original half twist retained. Let F_N^(port)(h) denote its exact empty-subset complete-image term in the [original reflection identity](actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md), including that identity's scalar sign. Under (13a) there are fixed delta,gamma>0 and K such that, for both parities and all integer 0<=h<=delta N, |A_N(N-h,N_else)-F_N^(port)(h)| <=N^K exp[N(Phi_D-gamma)]. (13c) There is just one nonempty reflection subset here, the actual L_h R^eps source of (7). Ports whose external colors remain N may have arbitrary retained signs. Equation (13c) is not asserted when additional ports are simultaneously varied. Proof. Evaluate the remaining positive factors at the original packing. Before deletion the two ordinary middle targets contribute -log b-log c, and the removed fold circle contributes F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y). Its beta and short forced-product factors have zero limiting logarithmic rate at the fold, including both parities. After the exact target restriction and (12e), the upper bound has the same remaining factors, the target -log b, and the added term G-log c. Their difference is exactly (13a). Thus it is g_port below the proved original capacity Phi_D. The two marked zero radii elsewhere can now be replaced by sufficiently small fixed positive values. Continuity preserves a fixed portion of the strict gap; the resulting small-color constant in (10) is finite. The [uniform all-channel fold upper bound](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) handles every remaining label. Their number is polynomial; all their retained half-twist phases and the removed lambda0 phase are units. This proves the stated corridor. No optimum for the split-radius potential is identified with the identity-smoothing capacity. There is an explicit open geometric class for this criterion. Put F_*=F(1,1,1) =3[Lambda(pi/6)+Lambda(pi/3)]/pi. If the four curvatures lie in [t,rho t], monotonicity and homogeneity of both actual potentials, together with (12g), give g_port>=2F_*-G_*-log rho>0 whenever 1<=rho<exp(2F_*-G_*). (13b) The threshold is approximately 2.807257219. It is strictly greater than one without relying on that decimal: F_*>F(1,1,0)=G_*>0. Thus (13b) describes a nonempty open locus of local positive-curvature data. Realization of this comparable-ratio locus by a fixed labeled right-angled diagram is a separate requirement; its rigidity does not follow from this local inequality. The criterion does not cover ports adjacent to a marked zero face or arbitrary curvature ratios. Several signed deleted ports would require a separate simultaneous source/norm argument; (13b) is not multiplied over interacting ports. ## 5. A precise obstruction to a uniform small-h norm bound Even for h=1, no bound poly(N) C^h can hold for the weighted polynomial coefficient norm at all positive radii. Take x=y=c=1, let i,k,l be integers each N/4+O(1), and j=i+k+l=3N/4+O(1)<N. A single coefficient of R_+ c^j has size S_j/(S_i S_k S_l) = exp{N[-4 f(1/4)]+O(log N)}. (14) Here f(3/4)=-f(1/4), and -4 f(1/4)>0 (it equals v_oct/(2pi)). The input monomial has norm one. Thus exponential growth is already present in an actual one-port polynomial action, not merely in a poorly chosen Hermite coefficient representation. This does not rule out cancellation in the FINAL marked coefficient or a more adapted source norm. It explains exactly what (13) must pay for, and why the untwisted C^h estimate cannot be imported unchanged. ## 6. Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.py) and [saved result](../experiments/actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel_results.json) pass. It checks (5) as an exact rational identity, then compares the kernel against 8,312 original balanced crossing monomial paths for R and R^-1, including 3,620 high totals and degrees through 2N+1. Thirteen full polynomial blocks check the annihilator, inverse and commutation identities, and 26 independently summed Newton expansions. It does not build the original R matrices from the interpolating polynomial. There are 144 whole original marked signed-source comparisons, 106 nonzero, at both parities and both original mark positions. Their remaining polynomial includes 534 monomials above the first c-period; 18 comparisons explicitly check that the removed higher blocks have zero actual target. At 80 digits the audit also checks 1,972 original quantum coefficient magnitudes and 366 split-radius norm transfers, with maximum relative error 8.63e-80. The finite determinant/rate and exponential-norm samples are explicitly diagnostics, not proofs of a uniform asymptotic theorem or a geometric certificate for a fixture. The theorem is a ROOT source result. It supplies no genuine-q normal identity, no universal signed smoothing gap, and no simultaneous signed norm estimate through dependent ports. The local radius test concerns one varied signed port; all other external colors remain complete. The kernel bound does not imply a simultaneous signed estimate or a global quadrilateral representation.

title: A source-preserving polynomial-cost filling of a simple transfer seam
text: # A source-preserving polynomial-cost filling of a simple transfer seam 28 October 2026. In the original coherently summed physical crossing, a transfer-clock-one seam can be filled on its zero side without discarding any endpoint residue. The closed half-integer contour can be extended across a fixed small negative classical-transfer collar. All newly enclosed cotangent poles are canceled by actual factorial zeros. The entire added collar has polynomial pointwise size relative to its retained zero-transfer kernel, polynomial contour length, and an exponentially suppressed far edge. This is a LOCAL exact source operation on regular bulk head charts. It does not make that zero-transfer exterior small, remove a retained integer residue at k=0, or bound simultaneous physical/factorial collisions. It supplies a controlled replacement for a simple artificial normal endpoint, not a sharp whole-knot estimate. The subsequent [projected operator completion](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md) retains the original physical output Fourier projectors. It extends the negative normal filling to ALL physical input labels, including the simultaneous scalar collisions below, with subexponential operator cost. The sharper scalar far-edge estimate here still requires its displayed regular chart; it is not transferred to unrestricted exteriors. ## 1. Exact kernel and the required regular chart Use N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N) and the EXACT factorial Fhat_N of [the original interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). The original positive total-transfer coefficient with its port monomial is K_N(z)=r_0 (c t)^z *Fhat(b+z)/Fhat(b) *Fhat(a)/Fhat(a-z) /Fhat(z), r_0=kappa x^(-a-b)Q^(ab), c=x Q^(-b). (1) Every power in (1) has its specified logarithm. At physical integers a,b,z this is the original coefficient with output(b+z,a-z), including its source normalization. The exact equality with the same full-Psi completion is in [the normalization comparison](actual_factorial_full_psi_identity.md). No bare compact Euler function is substituted outside its valid disk. Fix a compact set of normalized head variables a/N,b/N in the open strip 0<Re w<1, with bounded imaginary parts, and a bounded logarithmic chart for t. Fix a finite imaginary height T>0. Choose epsilon>0 so small that, for -epsilon N-1<=Re z<=0 and |Im z|<=T, BOTH (b+z)/N and (a-z)/N stay in a fixed compact substrip of 0<Re w<1. The finite set of small N can instead be excluded by N>=N_0. This explicit condition keeps the two outside factorial ratios nonzero and holomorphic throughout the collar. It is essential. A physical head at a=0,d or b=0,d is not automatically in this chart. The same construction works in an arbitrary original word by retaining independent head/port variables before interpolation. In that network all dependence on this crossing's total transfer is (1); it is not permissible first to eliminate neighboring head indices and then assume their additional z dependence is absent. All other original couplings, caps, pivots and external factors remain in the exterior. ## 2. A uniform small-normal-factor estimate For z=-u+i v in the collar, u>=0, set M=ceil(u), nu=z+M. Then 0<=Re nu<1 and |Im nu|<=T. The exact shift equation gives 1/Fhat(z)=product_(r=1)^M(1-Q^(z+r))/Fhat(nu). (2) On this fixed nu rectangle, the convergent Gamma product gives Fhat(nu)=(-2pi*i/N)^nu Gamma(1+nu)(1+O_T(1/N)), |1/Fhat(nu)|<=C_T N^(Re nu)<=C_T N. (3) Only the upper bound is needed. It is uniform on the closed rectangle: Gamma(1+nu) has neither a zero nor a pole there. The product remainder in its defining logarithm is O_T(N^-2), and its explicit Gaussian factor changes (3) by O_T(1/N). Each factor in (2) is at most C_T(M+1)/N, since |z+r|<=M+T+1 and M<=epsilon N+2. Hence |1/Fhat(z)|<=C N [C_0(M+1)/N]^M. (4) The exact bulk-factorial asymptotic and its proved derivative bounds give |d_w log Fhat(w)|<=C on the two retained bulk substrips. Integrating along the segments from b to b+z and a to a-z bounds their ratios in (1) by exp(C(M+1)). Its explicit Cartan factor and t^z obey the same bound: Log c and Log t are bounded on the specified chart. Absorbing these factors into C_1 proves the complete estimate |K_N(z)/r_0|<=C N [C_1(M+1)/N]^M. (5) If an explicitly retained finite-mode Gaussian is also present, a factor exp(A z^2/N+B z), with |A|,|B| bounded, is at most exp(C(M+1)) on this collar and is absorbed by the same estimate. Thus neither its connecting horizontal pieces nor the monomial phase has been omitted from (5). No analogous claim is made when those logarithms or Gaussian coefficients are unbounded. Choose epsilon so that 2C_1 epsilon<1/2. Then the ENTIRE added collar has |K_N|<=C N |r_0| for large N. On the far half-integer edge Re z=-m-1/2, m=floor(epsilon N), equation (5) gives |K_N(z)/r_0|<=C N [C_1(m+2)/N]^(m+1) <=poly(N)exp(-c_epsilon N), (6) where c_epsilon>0. This is suppression RELATIVE to the actual retained r_0 and exterior. An unrestricted exterior may still have a larger exponential rate; (6) has not assigned it the knot volume. ## 3. Exact closed-contour filling, including the horizontal pieces Consider the original closed transfer rectangle with vertical edges -1/2 and d+1/2 and horizontal edges Im z=+/-T. Its density is omega_N=pi cot(pi z) K_N(z) dz/(2pi*i). (7) Its residues at k=0,...,d are exactly the original finite transfer terms, with forbidden physical terms zero as proved in [the endpoint theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md). Replace its LEFT edge by Re z=-m-1/2 and extend BOTH horizontal pieces to that edge. The difference of the rectangles encloses the integers -1,...,-m and no noninteger cotangent pole. At each such integer Fhat(z) has a simple pole, so 1/Fhat(z) has a simple zero. The other two factorial ratios are regular and nonzero by Section 1. Therefore every new cotangent pole in (7) is REMOVABLE. The full density is holomorphic throughout the added strip, after these explicit cancellations, and the two closed contour integrals are EXACTLY equal. In particular the pole at k=0 remains enclosed; it has not been deleted by rounding a corner. There is a quantitative chain estimate as well. On a half-integer vertical edge |cot(pi z)|<=1. On Im z=+/-T it is bounded by a constant depending only on T. The added horizontal segments have total length O(N), and the far vertical segment length 2T. Equations (5)--(6) therefore give polynomial mass and pointwise cost for the ENTIRE closed filling and the strictly smaller far normal face. Pointwise equality in the other variables and Fubini on compact source pieces preserve every original exterior contraction. No boundary piece from the two finite-height horizontal connections has been called zero or put into an unproved error term. An artificial internal split at k=R is simpler: the two adjacent rectangles have exactly opposite shared vertical edges. Moving this interface across an integer moves its actual residue from one piece to the other with opposite signs. Their TOTAL current is unchanged. For a sublinear interface width, the operator costs of those actual residues are subexponential by the endpoint theorem. This paired statement is distinct from deleting the nonzero sourced Ward current of either packet separately. ## 4. Precise remaining collision and global scope The filling resolves a SIMPLE transfer-clock-one boundary while the other four physical-coefficient factors remain regular. A second factorial collision can cancel the zero used in Section 3. For example at b=0 the ratio Fhat(b+z)/Fhat(z) is identically one; at a=d the factor Fhat(a-z) meets a zero across z=-1, so its reciprocal has a pole. The scalar density can then retain cotangent poles. This scalar proof does not remove them. Keeping the original physical output Fourier projection instead supplies the additional zeros counted in the [projected completion](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md), which proves all newly enclosed NEGATIVE cotangent poles removable, with tame normal operator cost. It still retains every original nonnegative transfer residue and hence does not discard the full-rate Markov corners in the endpoint theorem. The bound is uniform on compact regular head/port charts, not across those collisions, zero/infinity positions, or arbitrary logarithmic deck changes. It removes one artificial simple boundary from a descent construction with polynomial local cost. It does not bound the mass of a complete global deformation or the rate of a remaining mixed bulk/endpoint period. Joint collision strata and the original full clock source remain necessary for a sharp volume theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.py): actual coefficient normal identities, source interfaces and forbidden transfer zeros; supplementary direct checks of the negative-side removable poles and finite-height density are recorded there. The closed contour equality follows from the residue proof above.

title: Exact simultaneous small-circle face correspondences
text: # Exact simultaneous small-circle face correspondences 30 October 2026. For ANY subset of untwisted small-circle ports whose literal identity smoothing is connected, the full original source is one coefficient of a simultaneous polynomial face correspondence. It includes protected outgoing faces and genuine cross-shift dependency cycles. The fixed-positive-radius cost is only exponential in the sum of the small colors. No global ordering of the individual face operators is asserted. If identity smoothing is disconnected, the full original source instead vanishes exactly in the small-degree window of section 6. Signed small ports remain separate. ## 1. The exact simultaneous object Fix any subset S of untwisted small ports of the literal flat plat, with actual external colors 1<=h_i<=N. Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. The remaining circles retain their folded labels and all original half-twist phases. Assume the identity smoothing is connected. Let G have the original white faces as vertices and a deleted edge b_i--c_i for each i in S. The ordinary Morse gap parity t_f is available at EVERY N: middle faces have the same parity, outer faces the opposite parity. In particular every component of G is monochrome and contains at most one of the protected faces u,v. G is a forest. One proof uses the actual gap segments. In an odd gap its middle regions form a path. In an even gap they form a path with its two ends identified to exterior u. Connected smoothing retains a box in each internal even gap, so no entire such cycle is deleted. Distinct gap paths meet only at u; their remaining pieces do not form a new cycle. Thus every deleted component is a tree. The same fact follows from the literal face count: smoothing |S| boxes in a connected source loses exactly |S| faces. Root each component at its protected face if there is one, otherwise at any face in that component. Retain variables Z_C for the roots. Every other face is unmarked. Orient each deleted edge from parent to child. If this reverses its original physical input/output order, use the exact ROOT transpose L_h^T=L_h. No marked functional or half twist is moved. Expand each L_h into its original finite Chebyshev sum of ALL FORMAL CYCLIC STEP WORDS, before selecting any physical state. This is a fixed finite algebraic sum, not a state-dependent set of admissible paths. For a path at oriented edge e let p_e be first-head output-minus-input. Its middle correspondence is L_child=Q^(-p_e) L_parent. Thus L_f=Q^(k_f(p)) Z_C, k_root=0, uniquely on the tree. Keep all path coefficients BEFORE expanding away endpoint factors. They are Laurent polynomials with denominators ONLY in their input middle face, and nonnegative powers of their two outer faces. This holds for every word: the L2 local weights are l0=2(x+y)/b+(q+q^-1)xy/b², l+=(1+qx/b)(1+qy/b), l-=(1+q^-1x/b)(1+q^-1y/b). Subsequent steps replace b by Q^(-p)b, a unit phase, and Chebyshev only forms finite signed sums. All forbidden physical wraps have an exact zero at their first illegal step ON THE ACTUAL PHYSICAL GRID. Those endpoint factors remain in the formal words used off grid. Let P_rem be the positive polynomial product of remaining circles. The simultaneous source correspondence is the finite sum over all oriented small-port formal words of their coefficients times P_rem, after these face substitutions, and with the ACTUAL background phase. ## 2. Exact phase and target Before imposing constraints, the scalar face factor is N^-1 scalar_rem prod_f L_f^(-d 1_(f unmarked)) prod_(e in S)(L_be L_ce)^(d/2). On a tree component, its total root exponent is -d if the root is unmarked and zero if it is protected. Its phase exponent divided by d is sum_f (deg_G f-2 1_(f unmarked)) k_f =sum_(parent->child)(k_parent-k_child)=sum_e p_e. The root term has k_root=0, so the formula holds for either root type. Hence the retained phase is exactly prod_e q^(d p_e). This is the phase of the [known polynomial operator T_h](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md), in either literal orientation. The original matrix transpose and its protected-face adapter were proved in [the ordered-source theorem](actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions.md), section 4. This uses no generic-q transpose identity. ## 3. Componentwise polynomiality, including dependency cycles The simultaneous expression, denoted Q_S, is a finite LAURENT polynomial in the roots Z_C. Fix one component C and hold every formal word in all other components fixed. Their denominators involve only their own middle roots, never a variable in C: outer and middle parity are opposite, so an outer face of a port cannot lie in its own merge component. Their numerators are polynomial in all C-face variables. P_rem is polynomial too. Now sum the paths in C. Eliminate its tree leaves toward the chosen root. At a leaf f, no other remaining edge of C has f as a middle face, and no edge of C has f as an outer face (parity). All held external path factors are polynomial in f. Thus the exact one-port calculation applies over the Laurent coefficient ring in OUTSIDE component roots: T_h acts on the ENTIRE current polynomial, including the held other-component coefficients, then merges f into its parent. It preserves polynomiality in all C-face variables. Repeat to the root. Consequently after summing C the expression has no negative power of Z_C, for each fixed selection of all outside paths. Summing those paths cannot change this conclusion. This argument can be performed separately for every component because all sums are finite. The FINAL simultaneous Laurent polynomial therefore has no negative exponent of ANY root, hence is an ordinary polynomial. No single global elimination order is claimed. The two-cycle example ports0,2 of [1,0,2,1] has no valid naive order, but is covered because the two mutually shifted roots have opposite parity and each partial sum is polynomial with the other paths fixed. ## 4. Exact original coefficient, degree and unique alias Every local path weight is homogeneous of degree zero. Hence the final polynomial has degree d(R-|S|). There are R-|S| unmarked merged faces and the original two distinct protected components. The primitive final grid has N^(R-|S|+1) points. Exact physical support follows from the original complete-circle zeros and the small-path endpoint zeros. Global carries are retained by the phase computation above. Nonnegative exponents and the degree force the unique Fourier target d on each unmarked component, zero on the two protected ones. Writing r=R-|S| and F_sm for the unmarked merged components, the actual fixed-sector contribution is therefore EXACTLY A_(N,a;h_S)=N^r product_(i not in S) [k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] [product_(C in F_sm)Z_C^d] Q_S(Z)|_(Z_u=Z_v=0). (1) The original unrestricted mark, ordinary caps, cups and all exterior phases are unchanged. Any separately retained exterior framing unit multiplies both sides. The scalar and measure are precisely those of identity smoothing; no extra auxiliary trace or new boundary average has been inserted. Q_S need not have positive coefficients. This proof does not assert that two different ordered products of one-port T operators coincide. In the dependency-cycle fixture described above no such naive order gives the simultaneous correspondence in general. Its polynomiality is proved by separate component partial sums. ## 5. Fixed-positive-radius bound and capacity interface At fixed positive root values assign every old face the value of its component. All Q phases have modulus one. The sum of weighted absolute coefficients of the three L2 paths is A_i=2+4(x_i+y_i)/b_i+4x_i y_i/b_i². Chebyshev bounds the weighted path sum by (A_i+1)^(h_i-1). This estimate can be applied BEFORE polynomial cancellation, directly to the finite Laurent correspondence. For a Laurent polynomial use the weighted coefficient norm sum_n |c_n|l^n, with all l_C>0. Unit clock phases do not change it and identifying equally weighted variables cannot increase it. Thus ||Q_S||_l <= P_sm(l) prod_i (A_i(l)+1)^(h_i-1), |[Z^(d F_sm)]Q_S| <= prod_i (A_i(l)+1)^(h_i-1) P_sm(l)/product_(C in F_sm)l_C^d. (2) After division by the actual target radius monomial this gives C^sum(h_i) times the original smoothed positive coefficient bound, without any whole-N shifted target. All marked radii are fixed positive for this bound. A proved strict compatible smoothing gap therefore transfers to the arbitrary connected untwisted small subset, including protected outgoing ports. Bound (2) concerns connected identity smoothing; section 6 treats disconnected smoothing in a small-degree window. No signed deleted crossing is covered. The smoothed graph need not have a positive geometric certificate; P_sm is its literal nonnegative-coefficient source polynomial, and the required gap remains a separate capacity theorem. Taking absolute values of the remaining folded-label phases is permitted in the upper bound, but those phases remain in the exact identity (1). ## 6. Disconnected smoothing gives exact small-degree vanishing Let S now be any untwisted small subset whose literal identity smoothing is disconnected, and put H=sum_(i in S)(h_i-1). Then the FULL original fixed-sector source is zero whenever 2H<d=N-1. (3) Every remaining complete coupon and its retained half twist are still present. This is an exact root identity, not a bound obtained by discarding an unmarked physical component. It applies to every fixed number of mesoscopic h_i=O(sqrt N), for all sufficiently large levels of both parities. To prove it, use the actual gap decomposition again. A fully deleted internal even gap gives a cycle u->...->u. If a gap retains a box, its deleted segments give trees. Distinct gaps meet only at u. Thus G has beta>=1 independent cycles, ALL in the exterior component C_u, and every other component is a tree. There are beta+1 connected physical blocks after identity smoothing. With r=R-|S| remaining complete ports, G has r+beta+2 components: r+beta ordinary roots, the original marked root v, and the exterior root u. Parity keeps u and v distinct. Orient each fully deleted even-gap cycle in its actual Morse direction u->...->u; orient attached trees away from u, and root all other trees as in section 1. Every nonroot face then has indegree one, and all extra indegrees occur at u. Keep ALL formal cyclic words. Their cycle charge constraints are initially congruences modulo N. The absolute value of each cycle sum is at most H<N under (3), so every such congruence is actual integer zero. This restriction depends only on the formal words in C_u; it is not a state-dependent restriction and does not constrain the words in any other component. Consistent integer lifts k_f with k_root=0 therefore exist. The same phase telescoping remains exact: sum_f(deg_G f-2 1_unmarked)k_f =sum_(oriented edges)(k_parent-k_child)=sum_e p_e. For a nonroot vertex, deg-2 equals outdegree-indegree. The exceptional root terms vanish because k_u=0, including all extra cycle indegrees. Hence the actual phase is still q^(d sum p_e); no newly chosen scalar or marked character appears. The original background monomial now has exponent +d beta at Z_u, exponent -d at each ordinary root, and zero at the marked root. Indeed C_u has e=v-1+beta edges and one protected vertex, so its exponent is -d(v-1)+de=d beta. The primitive compatible grid has N^(r+beta+1) points, retaining the unchanged single N^-1 marked factor. No trace normalization is assigned independently to the disconnected blocks. The componentwise polynomial proof applies to EVERY component other than C_u. When its words are summed, the cycle constraints only concern the held C_u words and impose no new restriction on this tree sum. Consequently its root has no negative exponent. The resulting Q is homogeneous of degree dr and polynomial in every root except possibly u. A formal L_h word has at most h-1 Casimir steps, so its denominator degree in its own middle root is at most 2(h-1). No word outside C_u has a Z_u denominator. Therefore every surviving Laurent monomial obeys n_u>=-2H_u>=-2H, where H_u sums only ports in C_u. Restriction to compatible cycle tuples and cancellation cannot lower this bound. The original face average requires n_C=d modulo N at each of the r+beta ordinary roots, and n_v=0 modulo N at the mark. These exponents are all nonnegative, hence their sum is at least d(r+beta). Homogeneity forces n_u<=-d beta<=-d, contradicting n_u>=-2H>-d. No monomial survives. This proves (3) with its actual finite measure and mark. Summing the remaining folded labels and phases preserves the exact zero. The bound is sufficient, not claimed sharp. Outside (3) a disconnected small subset can be nonzero. For example the original four-box source [1,0,2,1], with ports 0 and 3 replaced by L_3 at N=5 and the other ports in maximal folded channels, is nonzero. A fixed number of small ports with h_i<=delta N satisfies (3) when delta is sufficiently small; no disconnected capacity theorem is needed in that window. Retained R^epsilon at a small port and genuine generic-q normals remain excluded. ## 7. Original-source verification and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence_results.json), checks 61,743 original full-color operator entries, 4,278 formal-word endpoint zeros and 544 high-total columns. The actual connected-subset charts supply 457 subsets, 2,659 component phase/parity checks, 2,776 opposite-outer incidences and 218 genuine operator-dependency cycles. Twenty-three whole original simultaneous contractions agree with the coefficient correspondence, including both parities, protected faces, several small colors and width three. Their formal sums contain 865,463 negative-exponent terms before the full cancellations. For section 6 the audit checks 208 disconnected original subsets, 232 exterior cycles, 1,164 background exponents and 956 tree-component phases. Four full cycle correspondences retain the exact compatibility constraints, even coset phase and N^(r+beta) source measure. Ten further original whole matrix contractions check the zero window at both parities, both mark positions, width two and three, with the remaining half twists retained. One original source outside the sufficient window is nonzero. The scalar is computed from the complete background exponent sum, independently of the simplified product q^(d sum p). The correspondence does not imply a signed-small-port bound, a generic-q normal estimate, or a strict capacity gap.

title: Exact sink convolution and a growing actual trivalent source
text: # Exact sink convolution and a growing actual trivalent source 28 October 2026. The original trivalent sink source has a finite q-binomial polynomial, an explicit inhomogeneous central current, and an exact balanced-residue/Barnes decomposition. The balanced source has an exact POSITIVE norm ratio. This removes phase cancellation from its magnitude, including geometric root lifts. On a nonempty open boundary chamber its marked geometric rate strictly exceeds the retained current rate, so the original sink has that growing rate with a nonzero coefficient. This is a local source theorem, for a literal original sink. No claim is made that every vertex of a broad knot class lies in the required gap chamber or that this proves its global volume limit. The exact source-cycle construction and its infinite Barnes bound are also developed in [the companion beta theorem](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md). The subsequent [exact Fermat normalizer](exact_balanced_source_normalizer_fermat.md) fixes the entire central source function, not merely its magnitude. It extends the growing-source rate and gap theorem below to the ENTIRE positive boundary chamber, with norm-rate max(0,log|u|,log|v|). Sections 4--5 retain the independent elementary positive-norm proof on |u|<1. ## 1. The actual finite source, with every Q tag Put Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, and p_a=(-1)^a Q^(a(a-1)/2)/F_a, p_a^-=Q^a/F_a. These are respectively the Psi_+ and Psi_- coefficients below order N. At the original sink its U-diagonal, V-transfer and positive-factorial orders satisfy h_0+h_4+h_2=d. Reflect the last order: a=d-h_2=h_0+h_4. The original coefficients are then F_a * (1/F_(h_0)) * p_(h_4). Consequently its two-boundary generating kernel is exactly B_N(u,v)=sum_(i+j<N) F_(i+j)/F_i * p_j u^i v^j =sum_(a=0)^d product_(j=0)^(a-1)(u-Q^jv). (1) For fixed a, the second equality is precisely the finite q-binomial theorem. It retains EVERY boundary coefficient; therefore it may be paired with the same arbitrary exterior boundary functional, not just evaluated at a selected color. For the reflected full-Psi field in [the actual bipyramid note](positive_bipyramid_source_transport.md), F_N(L;U,V)=r^d Psi_-(Log U-L) Psi_+(Log V-L)Psi_+(-L), r=exp L, its first-jet Laurent constant is C_N(U,V)=sum_(i+j+k=d) p_i^- p_j p_k U^i V^j, NQ^d C_N(U,V)=B_N(Q^2U,QV). (2) Indeed p_(d-a)=Q^(-(d-a))F_a/N. The remaining inner q-binomial sum is the product in (1). Thus the actual tags are u=Q^2U,v=QV, with NQ^d retained. Equivalently the original reciprocal coefficient has its Q^(-1) tag and the reflected factorial window its Q^(-1) tag. They have not been simplified at Q=1. The companion relative moment theorem retains the complete circle/outer-ray chain represented by (2), including mixed individual-ray terms; (2) does not delete those terms. Set P_a(u,v)=product_(j<a)(u-Q^jv). Its recurrence gives (u-v)B_N(u,Qv)=B_N(u,v)-1+u^N-v^N. (3) The last term is P_N=u^N-v^N. The inhomogeneous source is therefore the explicit central current D_N=1-u^N+v^N. (4) No homogeneous descent or scalar normalization is assumed. ## 2. Balanced nonvanishing and its exact positive norm ratio Suppose u^N-w^N=1, uw!=0. Define p_a=product_(j<a)(u-Q^jw), r_k=w^(-k)product_(j<k)(u-Q^(-j)). Then p_N=p_0=1, and the cyclic vector p satisfies p_(a+1)=(u-Q^aw)p_a. For the UNNORMALIZED discrete Fourier transform p_hat_k=sum_(a=0)^d Q^(ka)p_a, the recurrence becomes w p_hat_(k+1)=(u-Q^(-k))p_hat_k, p_hat_k=r_k B_N(u,w). (5) Every factor is nonzero: w!=0 and u^N-1=w^N!=0. The Fourier transform is invertible, and p is nonzero. Thus B_N(u,w)!=0. (6) More quantitatively Parseval gives the exact identity |B_N(u,w)|^2 =N * [sum_(a=0)^d |p_a|^2]/[sum_(k=0)^d |r_k|^2]. (7) Both sums are strictly positive. This identity holds for ALL root choices w and gives the entire magnitude, not merely nonvanishing of a formal leading term. It is the appropriate replacement for assuming that the finite oscillatory sum selects its growing branch. Fixed small logarithmic lifts can give polynomial Fourier coefficients, as in the earlier Fermat source comparisons. That estimate does not apply automatically to geometric lifts whose logarithms or clock rotations grow with N. Section 4 uses (7) directly along those actual lifts instead. ## 3. Exact original source as a balanced residue plus its current Use compatible logs in the chamber -pi<phi=Arg u<0, 0<gamma=Arg(v/u)<pi, Log v=Log u+Log(v/u). Write h=2pi*i/N, c=Log(v/u) and use the original full function g(a)=exp(a Log u) Psi_+(c)/Psi_+(c+ha). (8) Its integer values are P_a(u,v). Off integers its exact norm is VARIABLE: g(a+1)=(u-v exp(ha))g(a), g(a+N)=[u^N-v^N exp(2pi*i*a)]g(a). (9) Replacing the second bracket by u^N-v^N off integers is false. Put t=exp(2pi*i*a), lambda(t)=u^N-v^Nt and t_*=(u^N-1)/v^N, exp(2pi*i*alpha)=t_*, w=v exp(h alpha). Assume first D_N!=0 and u^N!=1. The marked meromorphic form omega=2pi*i D_N * t g(a) da/[(t-1)(1-lambda(t))] (10) has residues P_k at integers k, EXACTLY the original source. Its other poles alpha+k have residue -g(alpha+k). Their monodromy is exactly one, and u^N-w^N=1. Thus their full N-orbit residue is -R_N(u,v), R_N=g(alpha)B_N(u,w). (11) This residue is nonzero. The marked full function in (8) is regular and nonzero at c. Its denominator at alpha cannot be a zero or pole: exp[N(c+h alpha)]=1-u^(-N) differs from both zero and one at a regular parameter. Changing alpha by an integer changes g(alpha) and the balanced B by inverse factors in (5), so their product R_N is unchanged. A finite rectangle of width N enclosing k=0,...,d and the corresponding alpha-orbit gives, with all FOUR edges retained, B_N=R_N+(1/(2pi*i))integral_boundary omega.
