Define the equivalent first-normal operators \[ J_{\mathcal E,r}=\left[\frac{\mathcal E_r^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}\right]_q, \qquad J_{F,r}=\left[\frac{F_r^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}\right]_q. \tag{4} \] They equal their divided operators times the same nonzero scalar \[ \alpha_N= \left[\frac{[N]_\zeta!}{1-\zeta^{2N}}\right]_q =\frac{Nq^{-N(N-1)/2}}{(1-Q)^N}. \tag{5} \] They lower or raise integer degree by exactly \(N\). Every actual adjacent \(R^{\pm1}\) commutes with these total operators: the literal finite generic \(R\) intertwines (2), hence their powers, and scalar division followed by regular specialization proves the claim. This keeps the full original crossing, not its eigenvalue-only quotient. ## 2. An elementary divided commutation calculation For the standard \(E=\mathcal E/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^2\), a vector of weight \(H\) satisfies the generic finite identity \[ E^{[a]}F^{[b]}v_H =\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)} {H+a-b\brack t}_\zeta F^{[b-t]}E^{[a-t]}v_H. \tag{6} \] Negative upper Gaussian indices, when needed, are interpreted by their finite product. A direct proof starts with \[ EF^{[b]}=F^{[b]}E+ F^{[b-1]}\frac{\zeta^{1-b}K-\zeta^{b-1}K^{-1}} {\zeta-\zeta^{-1}} . \] This is the sum of \(b\) elementary commutators; the geometric sum is \([b]_\zeta\). Repeating it \(a\) times, dividing by \([a]_\zeta!\), and grouping equal \(F^{b-t}E^{a-t}\) terms gives (6) by the Gaussian Pascal recursion. Equivalently its Cartan coefficient is \({K;2t-a-b\brack t}\). Acting AFTER \(E^{[a-t]}\) turns its upper integer into \(H+a-b\), which explains the weight in (6). This is a polynomial/rational identity derived from (1), not an assumption about root-module decomposition. Now consider FOUR physical heads and the two specified degree spaces \[ W=(V_N^{\otimes4})_{2N-2},\qquad L=(V_N^{\otimes4})_{N-2}. \tag{7} \] Vectors of \(L\) have weight \(H=2N\). For \(a=b=N\), all matrices in (6) have the regular specialization (3). The root Gaussians obey \[ {2N\brack t}_{q}=0\quad(0<t<N),\qquad {2N\brack N}_{q}=2(-1)^N. \tag{8} \] For a direct proof use \(\prod_{j=0}^{2N-1}(1+Q^jz)=(1-(-z)^N)^2\) and compare coefficients; the symmetric Gaussian has the additional phase \(q^{-t(2N-t)}\). Also \(E_4^{[N]}L=0\), simply because its output degree would be negative. Thus (6)--(8) give the exact RIGHT INVERSE \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal E_4^{[N]}F_4^{[N]}|_L =2(-1)^N\rho^{2N}I_L,\qquad J_{\mathcal E,4}J_{F,4}|_L=-2N^2I_L . \quad} \tag{9} \] For the second equality use (5), \(1-Q=-q\rho,\ q^{-N(N-1)}=(-1)^{N-1}\). Both signs in (9) include even levels. In particular \(J_{\mathcal E,4}:W\to L\) is surjective, with explicit right inverse \(-J_{F,4}/(2N^2)\). ## 3. Original six-head invariants and extraction of this constraint The [complete original source construction](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), section 5, gives an isomorphism between the FULL root invariant space in six heads WITH unrolled \(H=0\) and \(W\). Throughout this note \(\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathrm{root}}\) includes this \(H=0\) condition, not only the periodic equation \(K=1\). Write its map as \(\Phi\). Explicitly, \[ H_2(w)=\sum_{c=0}^d\frac{(-xQ)^c}{(Q;Q)_c} \mathcal E_4^cw\otimes|c\rangle,\qquad \Phi_w=N\sum_{a=0}^d \frac{x^{a-d}}{(Q;Q)_a}F_5^aH_2(w)\otimes|d-a\rangle . \tag{10} \] Its inverse \(\mathsf{ext}\) extracts last two colors \((0,d)\) and multiplies by \(x^d/N\), where \(x=q^d\). Using (3) on (10) yields \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathsf{ext}\bigl(J_{\mathcal E,6}\Phi_w\bigr) =J_{\mathcal E,4}w .\qquad} \tag{11} \] Here the extraction is also defined on the shifted output degree. The details prevent a false deletion of endpoint terms: output last color \(d\) forces \(a=0\) and local lowering on head six equal to zero. For fifth input color \(c\), its local divided exponent must equal \(c\). If \(c>0\), the first-four-head factor contains \(\mathcal E_4^{[N-c]}\mathcal E_4^c =\mathcal E_4^N/[N-c]_q!=0\) at the root; its denominator is a unit. For \(c=0\), it is the FULL divided operator \(\mathcal E_4^{[N]}\). The remaining two Cartan factors multiply to \(K_5^NK_6^N=1\), and the original \(Nx^{-d}\) cancels the extraction factor. Multiplication by the common scalar (5) proves (11). ## 4. Equality with saturated generic source, at all levels Let \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C\{\zeta-q\}\) and \(\mathcal K=\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal O\). Inside the free balanced six-head lattice take \[ \Lambda=\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathcal K}(V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes6}) \cap\mathcal O^{N^6},\qquad S_N=\Lambda/(\zeta-q)\Lambda. \] The [generic-source saturation proof](actual_six_port_deformable_source_and_recoupling.md) shows that \(S_N\) injects into the full root invariants, with dimension \((N^3+N)/2\). Saturation matters: \(\Lambda\) is a free direct summand over this DVR, so reduction is injective. It is not the kernel obtained by substituting the root into a generic rank formula. Every vector in \(\Lambda\) is annihilated by the generic ordinary \(E_6,F_6\), hence by the regular divided operators (3). Therefore \(S_N\subset\ker J_{\mathcal E,6}\cap\ker J_{F,6}\). By (11), \(\mathsf{ext}(S_N)\subset\ker J_{\mathcal E,4}\). The actual dimensions and (9) are \[ \dim W=\frac{2N^3+N}{3},\qquad \dim L={N+1\choose3},\qquad \dim\ker J_{\mathcal E,4}=\frac{N^3+N}{2}. \] The first is the central coefficient of \((1+z+\cdots+z^d)^4\); the second counts the unconstrained compositions of \(N-2\) into four parts. The last now follows from PROVED surjectivity, not assumed flatness. Equal dimensions give the all-level identification \[ \boxed{\quad \mathsf{ext}(S_N)=\ker(J_{\mathcal E,4}:W\to L),\qquad S_N=\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathrm{root}}\cap\ker J_{\mathcal E,6} =\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathrm{root}}\cap \ker J_{\mathcal E,6}\cap\ker J_{F,6}. \quad} \tag{12} \] Thus the extra \({N+1\choose3}\) root invariants are precisely the divided-current obstruction. No tilting decomposition, classical semisimplicity, or numerical braid-cyclic rank was used for equality. ## 5. Explicit source projection and its exact scope On \(W\), define \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathsf P=I_W+\frac{J_{F,4}J_{\mathcal E,4}}{2N^2}. \qquad} \tag{13} \] By (9), \(\mathsf P^2=\mathsf P\), \(J_{\mathcal E,4}\mathsf P=0\), and its range is exactly the source space (12). The complement is \(\operatorname{im}J_{F,4}\), and its rank is \({N+1\choose3}\). This is an explicit SOURCE-INDEPENDENT algebraic projection defined by known tensor generators; it is not evaluation at an unknown invariant. It is generally oblique, and no polynomial bound on its norm is claimed. The orthogonal projection onto the same known kernel has norm one. The original three-cup source lies in \(S_N\). This follows either from its regular generic lift or directly: every nontrivial local divided power on a two-head cup is zero (ordinary powers by its Hopf equations, and the \(N\)-th powers by physical degree). The block coproduct (3) then kills the three-cup tensor. Every literal signed braid preserves \(S_N\) by its regular generic intertwining. Any polynomial interval Casimir coupon has the same property. A complete circle has such a regular polynomial lift; no actual generic-\(q\) pivot germ is replaced when using this statement AT THE FIXED ROOT. Consequently \(\mathsf P\) can be inserted between reduced gates on an original source orbit without changing any original exterior co-source. It need not commute with every reduced boundary generator on the UNRESTRICTED root space. An arbitrary root-only intertwiner without a regular generic lift is not asserted to preserve \(S_N\). All genuine original Casimir Hermite derivatives remain in the restricted braid/coupon operators. Restriction (12) removes root invariants absent from the generic source; it is not a semisimplification or an instruction to set their normal currents to zero. A derivative of the whole source in \(q\) satisfies an INHOMOGENEOUS differentiated Ward equation; (12) is a root-value theorem and does not replace that equation by a homogeneous one. For the six-head original plat, \(w_0=p\otimes p\) and \(\lambda=\ell\otimes\ell\) in \(W\). The literal marked cap is evaluated only after the whole invariant identification (10); it gives this \(\lambda\), as already proved in the complete-source note. Physical orthogonal compression to (12) therefore preserves the word scalar and keeps the boundary Cauchy cost at most \(\|w_0\|\|\lambda\|=N^2\). No new boundary normalization is inserted. This supplies a concrete smaller six-port source for subsequent recoupling and energy estimates. It does not yet prove a positive geometric norm bound or a new noncyclic volume-equality class. Audit: [literal divided coproduct, right inverse, source and braid matrices](../experiments/audit_actual_six_port_divided_power_source_kernel.py).

title: Actual six-port complete-circle support and the limits of tensor sampling
text: # Actual six-port complete-circle support and the limits of tensor sampling 29 October 2026. Three disjoint complete-circle insertions have a genuine source restriction: their observed joint channels lie in a tetrahedral simplex, rather than an independent spectral cube. This necessary support and a rank bound follow from the original saturated source, without an assumed regular-cube eigenframe. The subsequent [all-channel positive scalar theorem](actual_trivalent_all_channel_positive_scalar_and_regular_cubes.md) now proves nonvanishing on EVERY surviving block, identifies its actual regular cube with the nested cup as cyclic generator, and makes the rank bound below an equality. The original support argument is retained. The positive all-value circle quotient is not a faithful norm for the whole marked source. A faithful tensor Hermite reconstruction exists on the scalar joint polynomial algebra, but its polynomial coefficient cost does not bound the actual recoupling energy. These statements must be kept distinct when proposing a six-port DCT sewing theorem. ## 1. The original source and its joint root blocks Use d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), the original V_N, and the saturated source S_N=(Inv_K V_d(zeta)^tensor6 intersect V_d(O)^tensor6)/t, dim S_N=(N^3+N)/2, where O is the analytic DVR at zeta=q_N and t=zeta-q_N. Equivalently S_N is the literal divided-current kernel already proved in [the six-port source theorem](actual_six_port_divided_power_source_kernel.md). The three ACTUAL commuting pair Casimirs are A_1=Omega_12, A_2=Omega_34,A_3=Omega_56. Generic pair nodes are c_a(zeta)=zeta^(2a+1)+zeta^(-2a-1), 0<=a<=d. At the root, fold a to j=min(a,d-a), 0<=j<=M. The root cluster J(j)={j,d-j} is double unless N is odd and j=M, in which case it is the simple Steinberg node. Write E_J for the REGULAR joint cluster idempotent and S_J=E_J S_N. Its dimension is the number of generic triples (a,b,c) in J(j_1) x J(j_2) x J(j_3), |a-b|<=c<=a+b. (1) This is the actual flat-rank statement, not an ordinary semisimple root quotient. The [bounded-confluence theorem](actual_six_port_bounded_confluent_blocks.md) keeps all normal coefficients and proves the regular cluster splitting. On a double axis put N_i=A_i-c_(j_i); then N_i^2=0 on that cluster. The full ordinary complete circle L_N has exactly L_N(A_i)=ell_i N_i, ell_i!=0, on a double cluster, L_N(A_i)=N I, on the odd simple Steinberg cluster. (2) For example ell_i=(-1)^d N/[2 sin^2((2j_i+1)pi/N)]. Thus the product of the three circles is a nonzero scalar times the TOP product of the r double-axis nilpotents, where0<=r<=3. ## 2. A missing generic corner kills the top product EXACTLY Suppose a triple alpha in the cluster cube violates(1). Its generic joint eigenprojector p_alpha is ZERO on the generic invariant space. On the regular cluster lattice it is a product of r factors (A_i-c_(partner(alpha_i)))/(c_(alpha_i)-c_(partner(alpha_i))). Each denominator is t times a unit. Clear all those denominators. The resulting regular numerator annihilates the cluster lattice over K, hence over O, since that lattice is torsion free. Specializing at t=0 gives product_(double axes i) N_i=0 on S_J. (3) No condition-number, choice of generic eigenbasis, or maximal minor enters(3). It is a cleared ACTUAL projector identity. In particular, the result does not infer a Jordan module just from its eigencharacters. All corners of the folded cube satisfy(1) if and only if j_1+j_2+j_3>=d. (4) Indeed, if their sum sigma is<d, the allowed corner (d-j_i,j_j,j_k) violates the triangle inequality. If sigma>=d, any chosen coordinate is at most d-j_i, while the other two have sum at least sigma-j_i>=d-j_i. Every triangle inequality follows. The same proof includes a simple Steinberg axis, for which the two possible labels happen to coincide. Consequently L_N(A_1)L_N(A_2)L_N(A_3) is ZERO on EVERY source block outside(4). This is a necessary all-level source support theorem. ## 3. On a surviving block its rank is at most one For a block satisfying(4), dim S_J=2^r. The commuting nilpotents give it a module over R_r=C[epsilon_1,...,epsilon_r]/(epsilon_1^2,...,epsilon_r^2). Every nonzero ideal of R_r contains its one-dimensional socle C epsilon_1...epsilon_r. To prove this, start with a nonzero ideal element and multiply by a maximal nonvanishing product of epsilon_i. The result is killed by every epsilon_i; expansion in the monomial basis shows it is a nonzero multiple of the top monomial. If the top product acts nontrivially on v in S_J, its annihilator cannot contain a nonzero ideal, hence Ann(v)=0. Then R_r v has dimension2^r and is all of S_J. The module is the regular cube module, and its top product has rank1. Otherwise that top product has rank0. For r=0 the block has dimension1 and the product in(2) is already nonzero. Thus the restricted three-circle rank is always0 or1 per surviving cluster; regular-cube structure is a CONSEQUENCE of a nonzero top product, not an assumption used to prove it. Put h_i=M-j_i and K=3M-d. Condition(4) is exactly h_1,h_2,h_3,e>=0, h_1+h_2+h_3+e=K. (5) Since K<=M, no further h_i upper bound is needed. If K<0 the observed source is zero; otherwise rank[L_N(A_1)L_N(A_2)L_N(A_3)|S_N] <=binom(K+3,3). (6) The support/rank argument ALONE does not prove that every allowed top product is nonzero. Generic rank2^r does not force that: a diagonal O-lattice with the same generic corner eigenvalues specializes to zero nilpotents, whereas the cube coordinate order specializes to the regular module. The actual physical source lattice distinguishes these examples. The new all-channel theorem supplies the missing nonzero actual coefficient by an own finite positive factorial identity, at both parities, and consequently proves every surviving cube regular. There is one constructive nonzero family at every ODD N. Fix two axes at the simple Steinberg j=M. Their generic highest weight2M=d and all ladder factorials have index<N, so their pair embeddings are regular O-direct summands isomorphic to the original V_N. The projected source is therefore the FOUR-logical-head invariant source. That already proved complete source is the regular N-dimensional Casimir algebra H_N; its remaining pair Casimir has its full double Jordan blocks. The third circle consequently has rank1 at every (M,M,j), and likewise for the two other permutations. These give3M+1 nonzero channels, including their shared simple corner. No norm bound on the embedding or its inverse is being inferred. This was the first nonzero family. The new positive scalar identity now provides the actual top coefficient for all interior allowed channels and at even levels as well. ## 4. Positivity, marking, and what tensor DCT does not imply Let P_i be the physical leg exchange in pair i and C_i=P_i L_N(A_i). The exact reflection theorem makes C_1 tensor C_2 tensor C_3 positive semidefinite. Its radical on S_N is the kernel of the three-circle product, since the product of the exchanges is invertible. Sections2--3 therefore describe a genuine observed quotient. It is not faithful on S_N, and its nodes have simplex support(5), not tensor-product support. The original marked co-source cannot silently be replaced by three ordinary cap functionals. The companion [actual marked-metric calculation](actual_three_belt_saturated_source_and_marked_metric.md) retains the ordinary C/marked H distinction and the full marked row. In particular the all-C form cannot give a finite Riesz dual for that whole original marked functional. The marked H form changes the source/leg wiring and must be analyzed on its own; its extra channels are not licensed by the ordinary simplex theorem above. There is now a constructive correctly marked alternative, proved in [the actual multiport Chebyshev packet](actual_marked_multiport_chebyshev_source_packet.md). Extract the physical degree-d component of each final pair AFTER using the total-degree constraint. Its full CD transform uses f_a on the ordinary variables and f_a# on the marked variable. For six ports it gives the exact original corner K_raw=x^d N^(-4) F_N(c_0,c_0,c_0) and positive energy N^3 sum_grid m_1m_2m_3|F_N|^2. Folding only after this actual CD identity gives degree<=M in every variable, with exact tensor DCT/Parseval and squared marked dual norm1/(8N^5) in its coefficient norm, equivalently1/(8N^11) against that energy. It avoids the ordinary three-C radical by keeping the marked conjugation and its current. The transform's coherent energy is not yet bounded by the geometric partition, and the observation kernel is not assumed stable under arbitrary interior split-pair braids. Thus this is a source-compatible positive correction, not a contradiction of(3)--(6). A tensor version of the exact one-variable Hermite DFT is nevertheless available on the FULL scalar algebra H_N^tensor3. Set ||F||_(H,3)=sum_(nu in {0,1}^3) N^(-2|nu|) max_jointnodes |partial^nu F|, where a differentiated axis ranges only over its double nodes and an undifferentiated axis includes the odd simple node. This is faithful and submultiplicative. Applying the explicit one-variable reconstruction in [the full circle algebra](general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md), section4, in each variable gives, for coefficients beta in the basis L_a tensor L_b tensor L_c, ||F||_(H,3)<=(3/2)^3 N^(9/2)||beta||_2, ||beta||_2<=6^3 N^(9/2)||F||_(H,3). (7) All eight mixed jets are retained; no confluent Vandermonde inverse or hidden Casimir normal is discarded. This is a coefficient theorem on the full commutative algebra. Identifying its quotient with an actual six-port source frame, or bounding a recoupling map in it, still needs the actual frame/measure and marked dual norm. In particular it is not ordinary DCT with independent positive product weights on(5). There is already an exact actual norm warning in one variable. At N=4r the complete Newton multiplication kernel has |(T_1)_(2r,r)|=s_(2r)/s_r^2, lim_(r->infty) N^(-1)log|(T_1)_(2r,r)|=v_8/(4pi)>0, whereas the faithful Hermite norm of the SAME full original crossing obeys ||R||_H<=9/8. Thus a polynomial Hermite/Fourier coefficient reconstruction does not imply a polynomial bound for its actual Newton multiplication energy. The four-head packet embeds regularly in the six-head source by tensoring its original cup. This warns against the proposed automatic metric identification; it does not rule out a different coherent marked geometric Gram. ## 5. Coverage only Van der Veen's [primary main theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/0805.0094#S1.T2) already treats sufficiently augmented knotted trivalent graphs from each fixed construction sequence. Its quantum statement uses odd N; the theorem explicitly gives zero at even N and concludes the SO(3) volume conjecture. Its singly augmented outside is described by regular ideal octahedra; additional parallel augmentation circles can contribute Seifert JSJ pieces. These are important coverage and normalization qualifications, not an all-N original-source six-port estimate supplied by that theorem. Only the introduction/main statements were inspected; no proof technique or state-sum replacement is used here. The next useful actual calculation is the coherent trivalent top-normal coefficient and its positive/marked measure on(5), followed by its recoupling energy. Neither(7) nor the generic triangle count proves that analytic comparison. The support restriction(3)--(6) itself is an exact source theorem and is available before that estimate. Audit: [exact folded incidence, simplex count and truncated-cube rank lemma](../experiments/audit_actual_six_port_three_circle_support.py). The finite audit checks all folded channels at N=2,...,40 and the four r=0,1,2,3 regular-cube algebra models. These integer/model checks supplement the cleared-projector proof; they do not extrapolate actual interior top-normal nonvanishing from finite examples.

title: A small untwisted circle is an exact polynomial face operator
text: # A small untwisted circle is an exact polynomial face operator 30 October 2026. At one actual untwisted port, the complete sum of the original small-color paths preserves the polynomial face ring. Its physical endpoint zeros cancel the negative powers that occur in individual path or clock terms. Consequently the whole source still selects one coefficient, with no level-shift aliases. A fixed-positive-radius bound costs only C^(h-1). The port has distinct unmarked input/output middle faces, and its literal identity smoothing is connected with the two original marked faces still distinct. Multiple small ports, a marked middle face, and a retained crossing at the replaced port are not included in this theorem. ## 1. The original operator and its endpoint factors Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Keep the original complete physical module and balanced basis. The external circle operator is L_h=(-1)^(h-1) P_(h-1)(Omega), 1<=h<=N, P_0=1, P_1=X, P_(r+1)=X P_r-P_(r-1). (1) These are the actual operators of the [external reflection theorem](actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md), not their eigenvalues on a selected channel. Write U=Q^u,V=Q^v for the two INPUT physical indices. Directly from the original coproduct, Omega has diagonal and upward/downward transition coefficients D(U,V)=2q U+2q^-1 V^-1-(q+q^-1)U/V, A_+(U,V)=(V^-1-1)(1-Q U), A_-(U,V)=(Q^-1 V^-1-1)(1-U). (2) Here A_+ sends (u,v) to (u+1,v-1), and A_- sends it to (u-1,v+1). Formula (2) is valid for every physical total, including the high blocks. For example expanding F_12 Ecal_12+qK_12+q^-1K_12^-1 gives (2) directly, with no low-block reflection. One may use cyclic shifts modulo N in (2) EXACTLY: A_+ is zero at u=d or v=0, and A_- is zero at u=0 or v=d. Hence any cyclic path that attempts to leave the physical square has zero weight at its first illegal step. Every power and the polynomial (1) therefore retain the original unwrapped endpoints. This is a root statement; it does not differentiate a root-periodic operator in generic q. At the chosen original port let x,b,c,y be its ordered outer, incoming-middle, outgoing-middle and final face variables. In the literal convention of the [complete-circle factorization](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md), S=d/2+N(Log x-Log b)/(2pi i), R=d/2+N(Log x-Log c)/(2pi i). Thus p=R-S (OUTPUT minus INPUT FIRST head) gives c=Q^(-p)b. The alternative formula c=Q^p b uses input-minus-output, or the opposite second-head displacement. These conventions must not be mixed. In particular U=-q^-1 x/b and V=-q^-1 b/y. ## 2. The exact polynomial operator Temporarily retain b and c as independent variables. Let T act on polynomials in c, with every other original face variable fixed. The unmarked bounded middle face c is distinct from either outer face x,y in the literal Morse region chart, so this prescription is well-defined. The outer labels x=y are allowed and substituted literally: T f(c)= -q^-1[1+q(x+y)/c+q^2 xy/c^2]f(Q^-1 c) -q[1+q^-1(x+y)/c+q^-2 xy/c^2]f(Q c) +[2(x+y)/c+(q+q^-1)xy/c^2]f(c). (3) Despite the displayed denominators, T preserves the POLYNOMIAL ring. Indeed for each integer j>=0, T c^j = a_j c^j+b_j(x+y)c^(j-1)+e_j xy c^(j-2), a_j=-(q Q^j+q^-1 Q^-j), b_j=2-Q^j-Q^-j, e_j=q+q^-1-q Q^-j-q^-1 Q^j. (4) The term with b_0 vanishes, and e_0=e_1=0. Thus no negative power occurs. T also preserves total homogeneous degree in ALL face variables. Define T_1=I, T_2=T, T_(h+1)=T T_h-T_(h-1). (5) Every T_h preserves polynomials and their homogeneous degree. Here the phases in (3) are essential. For L_2=-Omega, substitution of the actual clocks into (2) gives the three path weights l_0=2(x+y)/b+(q+q^-1)xy/b^2, l_+=(1+q x/b)(1+q y/b), l_-=(1+q^-1 x/b)(1+q^-1 y/b). (6) The WHOLE remaining source supplies the factor q^(pd) for a path with displacement p. Since q^d=-q^-1, the weighted shifts in (6) are exactly (3), evaluated at c=b. For several successive steps, the current middle clock is Q^(-p)b, so the ordered path weights are exactly the successive applications of T. The physical Chebyshev recurrence (1) gives (5). This argument uses the original path product before expanding its endpoint factors; it does not discard forbidden paths one Laurent monomial at a time. ## 3. Whole-source coefficient and the retained measure Fix a connected original plat with R complete-circle ports and its literal unrestricted main mark. Replace just the chosen untwisted port by L_h. All other ports retain fixed folded labels a_i and their original half-twist phases omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i. Assume b,c are distinct unmarked faces, and that deleting this port leaves a connected flat projection. The literal identity smoothing merges b,c; its two original marked faces u,v remain distinct. Let P_rem be the product of the R-1 remaining positive circle polynomials D_a D_a Ptilde_s, retaining their original face incidences and keeping b,c independent. Define the polynomial on the smoothed face graph Q_h(L)=[T_h P_rem(L)]_(c=b). (7) It is homogeneous of degree d(R-1). It need not have positive coefficients. Let F_sm be the R-1 faces other than u,v after merging. The actual fixed-sector small-circle contribution is EXACTLY A_(N,a;h)=N^(R-1) product_(i!=port) [k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] [product_(f in F_sm)L_f^d] Q_h(L)|_(L_u=L_v=0). (8) Every cup, ordinary cap, exterior phase and the original mark are as in the [marked coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md). Any separately recorded exterior framing unit multiplies both sides. To prove the phase used in section 2, first use the exact full-source monomial of that theorem BEFORE merging. Removing the chosen complete coupon removes its two middle denominators, so the remaining scalar face factor is N^-1 product_(i!=port)[k_a beta_a^2 omega_a^epsilon] (bc)^(d/2) product_(f!=u,v)L_f^(-d). (9) Since b,c are unmarked, c=Q^(-p)b converts their part to q^(pd)b^(-d), exactly. No root clock or half-integer power has been reset. This proves (3) with its true scalar and chosen direction. For fixed paths at the small port, sum over the remaining primitive face grid. All surviving complete coupons enforce their original unwrapped support, and (2) enforces the small port's physical endpoints. The chosen path specifies c=Q^(-p)b; the input and output middle faces have the same even-level parity, so this relation respects the original coset. Summing paths gives (7) on the smoothed grid. The globally assembled exponents are integers, and the remaining carry signs cancel by the same integral face-flow argument, with the displacement p fixed. There are N^R smoothed grid points. A monomial of Q_h survives that average only if its exponent is 0 modulo N at the marked bounded face and d modulo N at every face in F_sm. POLYNOMIALITY and total degree d(R-1) force the unique possibility: exponent zero at both marked faces and exactly d at every face in F_sm. No coefficient positivity is needed for this argument. The even coset multiplier at that exponent is one. Combining N^R with N^-1 in (9) proves (8). Individual clock or diagonal-path pieces can have genuine whole-N aliases. It is the exact sum (3)--(5), including both off-diagonal bands, that cancels their negative powers and restores this argument. ## 4. A fixed-positive-radius cost of C^(h-1) Give EVERY smoothed face a fixed positive value l_f, including u,v. Give the two unmerged variables b,c that same value l_b. For a polynomial P write ||P||_l=sum_n |P_n|l^n. From (4), ||T P||_l <= A(l)||P||_l, A(l)=2+4(l_x+l_y)/l_b+4l_x l_y/l_b^2. (10) Thus (5) implies ||T_h P||_l <= [A(l)+1]^(h-1)||P||_l. (11) The elementary induction retains the subtraction in (5); it bounds its norm rather than asserting positivity. Merging two variables of equal positive weight cannot increase this weighted coefficient norm. Since P_rem has nonnegative coefficients, ||P_rem||_l=P_sm(l), where P_sm is the original identity-smoothed positive polynomial. Coefficient extraction in (8) therefore gives |[L^(d F_sm)]Q_h| <= [A(l)+1]^(h-1) P_sm(l)/product_(f in F_sm)l_f^d. (12) This avoids separate estimates of shifted targets or their modular aliases. Equivalently, the finite lowering expansion changes each ordinary exponent by at most 2(h-1), with total displacement bounded by 4(h-1), only AFTER its exact polynomial cancellations. At fixed l, all remaining label weights are the original ones. Sum their absolute values and use the existing uniform all-label circle rate bound. If the identity-smoothed coefficient bound at these SAME positive variables has a strict gap g below the original volume rate, then the whole one-small-port source has that gap up to (h-1)log[A(l)+1]/N and o(1). In particular h=O(sqrt N) has no rate cost, and sufficiently small h<=delta N preserves a strict gap. The marked variables may be chosen fixed positive as in the [fixed-radius smoothing bound](actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.md); their targets remain zero. They are not set to zero before (12). This implication requires an established compatible smoothing gap. It does not assert that every smoothing has one. Nor does it cover several deleted ports, a marked middle face, disconnected smoothing, or an R^epsilon crossing retained at the small port. Those cases need their own exact scalar, incidence and endpoint analysis. ## 5. Focused source verification The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion_results.json), checks seven symbolic operator/endpoint identities, 15,316 actual coproduct entries and 154 physical endpoint zeros. It compares 1,512 literal L_h path pairings with polynomial monomials, including 504 high-total cases. The whole-source check compares 139 actual marked fixed-sector contractions with (8), for every h=1,...,N in its fixtures, both level parities and both original mark positions. It includes width two and three, maximal/mixed/zero folded channels, and the other ports' retained half twists. The 121 surviving modular monomials all have the unique asserted target. These checks concern the original finite tensors; the all-diagram identity and norm bound are the preceding analytical arguments. The face-insertion theorem does not include multiple, marked-middle or signed small ports. The theorem retains its one-port scope.

title: Connected untwisted smoothing has a strict source-capacity gap
text: # Connected untwisted smoothing has a strict source-capacity gap 30 October 2026. Let D be a fixed connected augmented flat plat with the original labeled nondegenerate convex ideal right-angled certificate. Its original two marked white faces and literal physical/matching port orders are retained. Delete a nonempty subset S of UNTWISTED circle ports by the actual L_1 identity smoothing. Assume the resulting source is connected. The surviving ports may retain their original signed half twists. The [exact capacity decomposition](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) supplies simple white blocks and zero-capacity double triangles. If a loop occurs, its capacity is -infinity. Otherwise the construction below gives a representation of the original drilled group, killing every deleted meridian, with volume 2 sum_blocks Vol(Q_block)=2pi Phi_sm < Vol(Y_D)=2pi Phi_D. (1) The two original marked faces remain distinct and adjacent: in the literal flat-plat merge forest they have opposite gap parity. No one-main-component assumption is needed. The proof uses the actual white/shaded cut balls and their original pairings. It neither asserts a three-manifold JSJ identification nor factors the finite quantum source into block sources. ## 1. The common circle data can be assembled along the digon tree Choose a root block. Each simple block has its proved positive circle packing; a double-triangle block is represented by three mutually tangent circles, with its two shaded triangles having the SAME three contact points and zero three-dimensional volume. Normalize the latter, for example, as two opposite lines and one disk tangent to both. At a digon attachment its boundary vertices a,b are adjacent in each closed block. There is an orientation-preserving Mobius map carrying the child's ORDERED oriented tangent disks a,b to the already assigned parent disks. To see this explicitly, send their common contact to infinity. Both pairs become ordered opposite parallel halfplanes; positive scaling and a translation match their width and position. The remaining freedom is horizontal translation inside the strip. Thus every shared white face receives exactly the same reflection on both sides. Recursing along the actual cut tree assigns circles to all original smoothed white faces. The free translations can avoid any additional finite accidental equalities of distinct circles. A globally embedded packing is NOT required here; only every block's packing and the shared ordered circles are retained. ## 2. The two types of digon cuts have different actual pairings The digon encloses 2v source vertices. Since each vertex has one matching incidence, its number of crossing matching edges is even. Thus the two crossed source edges are both MAIN or both MATCHING. MAIN/MAIN: the matching pairs stay within the pieces. The same raw physical head r_b r_a (or its literal inverse when the port is reversed) appears at the two cut ports. Topologically the cut is the actual two-main-arc sphere, or the corresponding meridional annulus after deleting cusp neighborhoods. This is the familiar componentwise connected-sum situation, with the actual meridian identified. MATCHING/MATCHING: the two original shaded pairings cross the cut pieces. They must not be replaced by gluing entire artificial cusp tori. In particular no equality of the two blocks' cusp shapes is required. The local algebra gives the needed actual collar directly. The oriented boundary of the proper cut disk traverses its two cut edges in opposite directions. Closing either side therefore records one input and one output side. The original cross-piece pairing keeps these opposite sides and its prescribed vertex permutation; it is not an arbitrary input-to-input identification of two block triangles. Let the common outer white pair be a,b and put P=r_b r_a=-I+H. It is a noncentral parabolic: H^2=0. For either side write its ordered raw main pair as (A,B), with BA=P and Tr A=Tr B=-2. Then Tr(H A)=4. After H=[[0,h],[0,0]], this means A_21=4/h. Its trace and determinant give A_22=-2-A_11 and A_12=-(A_11+1)^2/A_21. Hence the normalized centralizer I+tH acts SIMPLY TRANSITIVELY on these ordered pairs. For any original input/output triangles across a cut matching edge, there is a unique C=I+tH with C A_in C^-1=A_out; it also transports B. This C fixes the common a/b contact and sends the a/middle and middle/b contacts to their recorded output contacts, because those are the unique main parabolic eigenpoints. It is therefore exactly the ordered three-point map of the two actual ideal shaded triangles. This proves the contact/peripheral adapter; it does not infer one from a scalar eigenratio. For a retained half twist epsilon, use the literal primitive matrix M=C^-1 (I+H/2)^epsilon. It has determinant1 and commutes with P. The original threading word [2,1,1,2] followed by the recorded signed Hurwitz move transports the input pair to the output pair, exactly as in the proved critical-scheme and primitive-collar identities. The signs are the actual parabolic specialization of (P^-1-I)/(-2), not a freely chosen peripheral shear. Both P and M fix the same cusp point. MAIN cuts match their meridian; MATCHING cuts instead retain BOTH original M matrices separately. ## 3. The actual group representation, including each deleted meridian Use the same white reflections at every occurrence of an original smoothed face. At a Morse slice the raw physical heads are H_j=r_(F_j) r_(F_(j-1)). Their prefixes telescope; literal cups/caps have product I, and unchanged wires have unchanged based heads. Every surviving box has the contact map of section2 and its original half twist. These are all the [literal Morse/van Kampen relations](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), so the construction gives an actual SL2 representation (with the existing raw trace-minus-two / physical trace-plus-two lift convention). Restore each deleted UNTWISTED box in the original drilled diagram. Its middle faces satisfy b=c by the literal smoothing. Thus its input and output ordered main pairs are equal. Set its actual auxiliary meridian to I. The original threading word is then the identity and the four physical ports are unchanged, including the case where the outer product happens to be central. This explicitly factors the representation through the actual meridional filling quotient. It does not wrap a source head or alter the original mark. ## 4. The ideal bigon collapse and the fundamental chain The connected augmented projection has the usual TWO literal cut balls obtained by cutting along the projection sphere and the recorded crossing disks. This is a topological cut before any convexity claim. Its white/shaded boundary cellulation is the rectified white graph; the surviving half twists specify the same recorded shaded face maps. For a loopless triangular sphere, the source cubic dual is bridgeless, so these white faces have disk boundaries; degree-two faces are allowed. In either cut ball, a digon CUT between white faces a,b bounds a proper disk D whose boundary has one arc in white face a, one in white face b, and whose two ideal endpoints are the crossed source edges. Cutting the ball along D gives two balls. Collapsing D in either boundary to a point gives exactly the two closed block balls of the combinatorial digon decomposition. All shaded triangles are unchanged; only the two cut ideal vertices coalesce. Iterating constructs the actual block tree separately in both cut balls. This does not claim that the doubled disk separates the full exterior when its shaded pairings cross the cut. Under the circle assignments of section1, BOTH cut ideal vertices develop to the SAME contact p=a intersect b. Thus D is assigned a constant ideal image p. Each remaining block ball, after collapsing its cut disks, maps with degree ONE to its actual convex Q_block. The double-triangle block maps into its single ideal triangle and has volume zero. Here is a finite-chain way to retain the multiplicity. First decorate each tangency of an ordered white pair by its CANONICAL horosphere. Send the contact to infinity and normalize the strip between the two white planes to width1. The horosphere at height1 is independent of the remaining horizontal translation, and pulling it back gives the decoration. Swapping the ordered pair preserves the same horosphere. Reflection in a boundary white plane preserves heights in this model. An actual shaded face map carries each of its three adjacent white planes: such a plane is the unique plane orthogonal to the shaded plane along the specified ideal triangle edge. Therefore the actual three-point shaded map, including its retained vertex permutation, carries these pair decorations. All finite replacements can consequently be chosen face-compatibly before passing to the quotient. These are the finitely many INCIDENCE points and truncated corners of a fundamental chain. They are not a single finite point assigned equivariantly to an ideal cusp vertex: a nontrivial parabolic stabilizer would forbid the latter. Translated corners on the same horosphere are retained, with their actual pairing maps. The TWO cut endpoints have the same white pair a,b, not merely the same ideal image. In their common normalized strip choose every replacement vertex of the collapsed disk at height T, with bounded horizontal coordinates. Reflected white maps and the actual shaded maps preserve the preceding decoration. Since the triangulation and its face maps are finite, all coordinates stay bounded in their respective normalized strips. In particular any two replacement vertices on one cut disk have distance 2 asinh(|z_1-z_2|/(2T))=O(1/T). Complete the truncated chain with the original conical cusp tails. Their boundary comparison is the previously proved horospherical O(T^-2) flux estimate; no artificial finite cusp fixed point is used. This specific common-height construction is essential: arbitrary sequences of ideal vertices converging to the same p need not have vanishing tetrahedral volume. We use the following uniform elementary bound. If a possibly partly ideal tetrahedron has two FINITE vertices at distance ell, then |Vol(tetrahedron)| <= 2pi integral_0^ell cosh(t)^2 dt <= 2pi ell cosh(ell)^2. (4a) Indeed take the plane through one of these vertices and the other two vertices. The tetrahedron lies in the one-sided distance-ell slab over this plane. In Klein coordinates adapted to the plane, orthogonal projection is the linear coordinate projection; its image is the convex hull of at most four points in the plane and has area at most 2pi. Fermi coordinates have volume element cosh(t)^2 dA dt, proving the bound. Degenerate plane choices follow by a finite approximation. The estimate is uniform when either of the last two vertices is ideal. Triangulate the proper disks and both adjacent balls compatibly. Collapsing a boundary disk of a ball to a point again gives a ball, with relative degree1. Refine against a vertex-fan triangulation of Q_block. One can perform the refinement by coning triangulated disk faces and their mapping cylinders; every additional tetrahedron in the collapse region then has at least TWO disk replacement vertices. By (4a) their total volume is O(1/T). The remaining block chain has relative degree1 and tends to an ordinary ideal triangulation of its actual Q_block. Thus its developed volume tends to Vol(Q_block). This is the degree of an explicit ball quotient, not an assumed global covering degree, and the vanishing of the correction is supplied by (4a), not by a continuity claim at coincident ideal flags. All original face boundaries cancel. White face maps use the SAME reflection on every piece of that face, including the collapsed arcs. For a MAIN cut the original matching/shaded pairs remain in their pieces. For a MATCHING cut the original shaded triangles are not cut internally at all, and the contact maps of section2 identify their three actual ideal vertices across pieces. Their retained Hurwitz versions are precisely the original signed face maps. Consequently the straightened chain is the actual marked exterior's relative fundamental chain, not a sum obtained by changing the face pairings. Choose ONE reflection r_u to develop the whole second cut ball from the first. Use this same choice on every block; the remaining white gluing transformations are r_f r_u in the original convention. Thus the second ball is not assembled from independently reflected blocks. Its original opposite topological orientation and this one reflected geometric development give the SAME positive volume. Therefore Vol(rho_sm)=2 sum_(simple blocks) Vol(Q_block) =2pi Phi_sm. There is no additional contribution from the cut annuli or from the double-triangle blocks. No JSJ identification or finite tensor-product identity is used. All remaining cusp images are parabolic (possibly rank deficient) with their actual commuting peripheral words. Finally restore the original deleted solid-torus cusps. Their meridians are trivial. The [proved axis/parabolic flattening](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) gives a zero-volume filling cap, so the representation of the original drilled exterior has exactly the same volume. The complete original meridian was nontrivial; the strict-kernel theorem therefore gives Phi_sm<Phi_old for every such nonempty connected untwisted smoothing with finite capacity. ## 5. A uniform corridor for the actual untwisted external colors Fix any set E of original UNTWISTED external circle ports. Let A_N(N-h_E,N_else) denote the literal original mixed contraction, with external color N-h_i at i in E and color N at every other port. The other ports may carry their original signed half twists. Let F_N^E(h) be its EXACT empty-subset cosine term from the [external reflection identity](actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md), with deficit zero at ports outside E. Put Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). There exist delta(D)>0, gamma(D)>0 and a fixed power K(D) such that, for every sufficiently large N of EITHER parity and every integer 0<=h_i<=delta(D)N, |A_N(N-h_E,N_else)-F_N^E(h)| <= N^K(D) exp[N(Phi_D-gamma(D))]. (5) All constants are allowed to depend on the fixed labeled diagram; there is no width-independent or twist-independent uniformity claim. One can choose them simultaneously for all subsets E of its untwisted ports. This is a near-complete REAL INTEGER color corridor, not an off-grid identity or a genuine-q normal theorem. Proof. Expand by the exact full-matrix reflection identity. A nonempty subset S contains literal L_(h_i) at its ports; a term with h_i=0 is zero. If its identity smoothing is connected, the [simultaneous polynomial correspondence](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md) bounds its full finite source by C(l)^sum h_i times the smoothed positive-coefficient bound at ANY fixed positive shared radii l. This retains the original mark, all carries and the actual tensor endpoints. Equation (1), or the loop capacity -infinity, gives Phi_sm<Phi_D. Choose fixed positive finite-face radii with marked radii zero making the fold capacity strictly below Phi_D. Then choose both marked radii small and POSITIVE, still below that value with a fixed margin. This is permitted by continuity of the local fold entropy, with the limit -infinity allowed when every local argument vanishes. The resulting C(l) is finite; it need not be uniformly bounded as marked radii tend to zero. The [all-channel determinant upper bound](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) at these now strictly positive radii bounds every remaining folded label by the same fold value, up to a uniform o(N) logarithmic error. There are only polynomially many such labels. Multiplicities and measures are polynomial, the remaining cosine factors have modulus at most one, and the retained integer-label half-twist phases are units. There are finitely many S. Fix one such radius choice for each connected S and take the minimum positive capacity margin and maximum log C(l). Choose delta small enough that C(l)^sum h_i consumes less than half that margin. Absorb the uniform o(N) and polynomial factors by decreasing gamma. For disconnected smoothing the exact correspondence instead vanishes whenever 2 sum_(i in S)(h_i-1)<N-1. Choosing also delta<1/(4 max(1,|E|)) guarantees this for all large N. Summing the finitely many subsets proves (5), with the original subset signs intact. This proves the missing proper-subset suppression in this corridor. It does not bound colors outside the corridor or vary a signed circle port: an odd half twist retained at a small port is not an identity smoothing. Full filling-source transfer still requires those separate inputs. No finite tensor product over the capacity blocks was used. ## 6. Verification and precise scope The finite-chain construction uses common horospheres and the specified fixed second-ball reflection. Section 5 requires fixed positive-radius regularization and finite subset margins, retaining signed complete ports and exact disconnected vanishing. The representation may be nondiscrete and the global circle configuration may overlap. The argument uses convexity of each individual block, not global packing embeddedness.

title: Smoothed source capacity, simple blocks and their actual polyhedra
text: # Smoothed source capacity, simple blocks and their actual polyhedra 30 October 2026. This concerns the L_1 opposite smoothing, not deletion of the old white edge xy or an asserted three-manifold JSJ decomposition. The new source is assumed connected and its two original marked white vertices u,v are distinct and still joined by their actual marked MAIN edge. The source white cellulation is a spherical triangular cellulation, allowing repeated incidences, loops and parallel edges. ## 1. Remove the attainment hypothesis by finite convex duality Use the [already normalized local entropy](actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md) V(theta)=2 sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], 2pi F(l)=max_(theta>=0,sum theta=pi)(theta.log l+V(theta)). Marked corners are fixed to zero. Let Theta be the product of the remaining compact row simplexes (possibly empty), A its finite-face incidence, and d_f=2pi for each finite face. Define H(d)=max{sum_t V(theta_t):theta in Theta,A theta=d}, with H=-infinity when infeasible. Then the literal log-radius capacity is EXACTLY H(d)/(2pi), even if its positive-radius infimum is not attained. There is no additive constant. Proof. H is concave and upper semicontinuous on its compact domain, by compactness and concavity of V. Weak duality is the local displayed identity. Conversely separate (d,H(d)+epsilon) strictly from the closed hypograph of H. The coefficient of the vertical coordinate is positive: it is nonnegative since the hypograph extends downward; if it were zero, strict separation would contradict d belonging to the projection. Normalize that coefficient to one. The resulting finite affine majorant gives logarithmic radii with capacity at most (H(d)+epsilon)/(2pi). Let epsilon decrease. If d is outside the projection, separation in the finite face coordinates and scaling that separator make the log-radius infimum -infinity instead. ## 2. A loop is infeasible; a two-edge cycle splits exactly For a triangular disk with a simple m-edge boundary and v interior vertices, Euler and 3t=2e_internal+m give t=2v+m-2. This uses incidences with multiplicity and remains true for a one-edge loop or a two-edge parallel cycle, whose boundary has respectively one or two vertices. Because u,v are joined by an actual embedded edge, any simple separating loop or two-edge cycle has a side with NO marked vertex in its interior. An edge joining strictly opposite sides would cross the cycle. Marked vertices on the boundary cause no problem. For a one-edge loop choose that side. It has 2v-1 triangles, with total available angle (2v-1)pi. Its v interior vertices alone demand 2v pi. Thus the angle polytope is empty and the capacity is -infinity. This statement is only about this source capacity; a source vanishing theorem would additionally retain the finite label/forced-factor support. For a two-edge cycle with distinct boundary vertices a,b, the chosen side has 2v triangles. Its interior demands exhaust their entire angle 2v pi. Consequently every a- and b-corner on that side has angle zero. Identify its two boundary edges to obtain a triangular sphere D_in, marked at a,b. Identify the same two edges on the other side to obtain D_out with the original marked pair u,v. The original feasible angle polytope is EXACTLY the Cartesian product of the two resulting angle polytopes. The boundary contributions of D_in are zero, so the full demands on D_out are unchanged, including when a or b was originally marked. Conversely any pair of such assignments glues to a feasible original assignment. Entropy is a sum over the unchanged triangles. Therefore Phi(D)=Phi(D_in;a,b)+Phi(D_out;u,v). The identity includes nonattainment and infeasibility by section1. The new marks a,b are adjacent along the glued boundary edge, so the argument iterates. It does not reset an actual quantum mark or assert factorization of the finite source: it is an exact statement about the already normalized classical source capacity. ## 3. Terminal blocks and finite positive multipliers Repeatedly split parallel-edge two-cycles. Each split has a positive number of triangles on both sides, so the process terminates. If a loop occurs its block is infeasible. Otherwise the terminal blocks have simple underlying graphs. A three-vertex sphere consists of two copies of the same triangle. With its adjacent marked pair a,b the remaining vertex c receives angle pi in each triangle. Its entropy is zero and 2F(0,0,l_c)-log l_c=0. Every other terminal block is a genuine simple triangulated sphere with at least four vertices. Its graph is 3-connected: deleting one or two vertices preserves connectivity by rerouting through their cyclic links (equivalently use the elementary triangulated-sphere argument in the frozen transverse-rank theorem). Such a block has a strictly feasible relative angle assignment. Here is a finite Hall proof rather than a circle-packing existence assumption. Let there be R finite vertices and 2R triangles. Every triangle has at least one finite vertex. For a nonempty proper subset S of finite vertices, put T=finite\S. In the sphere punctured at any vertex of S, the original triangles supported on T union{u,v} are bounded faces of a simple planar graph on |T|+2 vertices. There are at most 2|T|-1 such faces. Hence at least 2|S|+1 original triangles touch S. The required angle of S is only 2|S|pi. The full finite set gives equality of total supply and demand. These strict finite Hall inequalities allow a common small lower bound epsilon>0 on every allowed corner. Singleton rows (the two uv triangles) are fixed at pi and are understood relatively. Maximize total V on this compact feasible polytope. An allowed zero angle cannot occur at a maximizer: moving toward the strictly feasible assignment gives a positive epsilon log(1/epsilon) contribution at every new zero corner, also nonnegative at an old pi corner, while all other contributions have finite first derivative. Thus all nonfixed allowed angles lie strictly between zero and pi. Finite-dimensional Lagrange multipliers now give tan(theta_tf/2)=k_t l_f, l_f>0. The row sum pi forces k_t=(sum_(f<g in t)l_f l_g)^(-1/2), including the two-positive-face rows. These are exactly the local source angles. They attain the radius capacity. Strict concavity makes the angle maximizer unique; connectedness of the finite-face adjacency graph makes its multipliers unique up to common scale. Thus no global attainment hypothesis is needed for these simple terminal blocks. ## 4. Constructing the simple block's actual circle packing Here is an elementary construction, including the development step. It supplies the simple block with its labeled convex polyhedron rather than inferring geometry from the existence of radius multipliers alone. Remove one triangular face abc of the simple sphere. Fix three positive boundary radii r_a,r_b,r_c, hence three mutually externally tangent boundary disks. The remaining triangulated disk has v interior vertices and 2v+1 triangles. Give each interior vertex demand2pi and leave the three boundary demands free, with total pi. Maximize sum_t V(theta_t)+sum_(boundary corners tf)theta_tf log(1/r_f). A strictly positive angle assignment exists by the same finite Hall argument. Treat the three boundary vertices as one supply destination of demand pi, retaining their separate corners. An interior subset S touches at least2|S|+1 disk triangles. Indeed puncture the sphere at a vertex of S and put T=interior\S. The complementary simple planar graph has |T|+3 vertices and at most2|T|+1 bounded triangular faces. The removed boundary face abc is one of them, so at most2|T| are disk triangles; subtracting from2v+1 gives the asserted strict bound. A proper subset consisting of the boundary destination and some interior vertices also has strict Hall slack: its complement T contains only interior vertices, and triangles wholly supported on T are bounded faces of a simple planar graph, at most2|T|-5 when |T|>=3 and none when |T|<=2. The full set has equal total supply and demand. Thus a common positive lower bound on all corners is feasible. The entropy boundary derivative argument of section3 places the maximizer in the open angle simplexes. The fixed boundary log terms have bounded derivatives and do not alter that argument. In particular each boundary angle sum is positive; their sum is pi, so each is strictly less than pi. Lagrange multipliers now give the same tangent-circle angle formula with the prescribed boundary radii and positive finite interior radii. Glue Euclidean triangles with side lengths r_f+r_g. Their angles are exactly those just obtained. Every interior vertex has total angle2pi. The disk therefore has a global orientation-preserving Euclidean development: continuation around each interior vertex has rotation 2pi and zero translation, and such loops generate the punctured disk's holonomy. Its boundary consists of three straight sides, with positive angle sums less than pi and the prescribed strict triangle lengths. It maps once around a convex triangle. This development is an embedding. Indeed it is locally an orientation-preserving isometry at every interior point, including interior vertices. For a point off the developed finite edges, the number of its preimages is its boundary winding number. That number is1 inside the boundary triangle and0 outside. Continuity and local injectivity extend the conclusion across the finite edges and vertices. Place a disk of radius r_f at every developed vertex. The three disks in each triangle are mutually externally tangent. The sector of a vertex disk between that triangle's two incident edges lies inside the triangle: its opposite center segment is covered by the other two tangent disks, which are disjoint from the vertex disk. The separation from that segment is strict: its two pieces lie in the other disks, their unique mutual contact is strictly outside the third positive disk, and the third disk's contacts with those disks lie on the two different incident center edges. Thus it cannot meet a nonincident triangle or acquire an accidental nonedge contact. These sectors assemble to the full disk at an interior vertex because its angle sum is2pi. At a boundary vertex they assemble to the part of the fixed boundary disk inside the carrier triangle. Thus different disks have disjoint interiors, and the only contacts are the actual triangulation edges. Restoring the omitted outer face gives the exact labeled sphere packing. Arbitrary separating triangles cause no problem: the development uses every triangle, not an assumed three-connected drawing of only part of the graph. For completeness, its right-angled polyhedron has a direct support certificate. For each bounded triangle the circle through its three contact points is its Euclidean incircle: on a center edge fg the incircle contact is at distance r_f from f. It is orthogonal to the three vertex disks. Its disk lies in that center triangle and contains no other packing contact. For the omitted outer triangle take the opposite side of its contact circle; all interior disks and contacts lie in its bounded curvilinear gap and hence inside that circle. Consequently every packing contact lies in all the prescribed inward white and shaded halfspaces, strictly unless incident to that face. The convex hull of the contacts has precisely the white cyclic facets and these shaded triangles: they form the closed labeled sphere of supporting faces, with no missing face or extra ideal vertex. At each contact, its two white and two shaded planes have the prescribed cyclic order and successive right angles. This is the actual convex ideal right-angled polyhedron Q_block of this labeled block. ## 5. Absolute capacity and independence of the adjacent marked pair Choose ANY adjacent pair of white vertices in this simple block, and send their contact to infinity by one orientation-preserving Mobius map. The two corresponding disks become the opposite marked halfplanes; all other disks stay bounded and disjoint in their common strip. Their positive curvatures satisfy the source angle equations, and therefore attain the capacity with that marked pair. The already proved actual facet-coning normalization gives Phi(block;any adjacent marked pair)=Vol(Q_block)/pi. It is independent of that pair. There is no source scalar or additive volume constant: the local normalization V(pi,0,0)=0 and section1's exact duality fix it. The double-triangle block has capacity0 instead and is not declared a nondegenerate ideal polyhedron. Combining this construction with section2 expresses every finite smoothed capacity in the stated class as a sum of these actual block polyhedron volumes divided by pi, with zero from double-triangle blocks. The new pair on a cut block is a geometric/capacity choice; no original quantum mark has been moved. ## 6. The remaining topology and strict-comparison questions This does not by itself identify the blocks as the hyperbolic JSJ pieces of the smoothed marked exterior. That assertion requires the actual cut gluing, peripheral maps and possible Seifert pieces. Nor does the decomposition compare their summed capacity strictly with the original unsmoothed capacity: the L_1 operation merges the opposite b,c faces, and is not the old white-edge xy contraction. These two remaining questions are not consequences of circle-packing existence. Finite-N care: a two-cycle can cut two MAIN edges or two MATCHING edges. In the latter case retained forced polynomials couple the two sides away from the odd maximal fold. Thus this capacity product is not a claimed all-level source product. Degree-two blocks can have zero capacity while still enforcing exact even-level zeros, as the parallel Belt examples already demonstrate. ## 7. Focused verification [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.py) and its saved results check eight digon LP systems and their separate factors, five genuine loop cellulations with infeasible demands,474 exact marked planar Hall cuts with21 independent positive LP assignments, and158 fixed-boundary Hall cuts with seven positive disk assignments. Fourteen actual disk developments include tetrahedral, bipyramidal and separating-triangle stacked spheres, with equal and unequal boundary radii. The audit checks232 disk pairs,1572 shaded supporting inequalities,348 white/shaded right angles and42 independent adjacent mark capacity evaluations. The geometric solve uses floating-point arithmetic, with maximum residual below3.2e-13; the subsequent entropy evaluation uses40 digits. Its marked-capacity spread is below2.6e-26. These are independent numerical diagnostics of the finite construction, not a numerical substitute for the all-block proof. A glued two-block example also checks the genuinely nonattained primal capacity against its exact dual block sum at four diverging radius scales. The positive primal excess decreases toward zero; the double-triangle capacity is checked separately. No finite quantum factorization or strict smoothing loss is tested or inferred. Capacity decomposition, finite quantum factorization and an actual JSJ decomposition are different claims. The universal strict smoothing comparison remains unproved.

title: A fixed-radius smoothing bound and its explicit limitation
status: Sufficient source bound; matched-graph capacity obstruction
text: # A fixed-radius smoothing bound and its explicit limitation 30 October 2026. ; source-coverage correction below. A one-variable test at the original positive face variables gives a strict source upper bound after a literal untwisted L_1 insertion. It needs neither a balanced split nor an attained smoothed capacity. The test is not universal: an explicit certified family below makes its best possible gap tend to minus infinity. This is a failure of fixed old radii, not a counterexample to a fully optimized smoothing gap or a volume conjecture. The family is proved as a labeled right-angled MATCHED-GRAPH capacity example. Its identification with the fixed flat-plat source coefficient is conditional on an additional source-preserving presentation adapter; section3 does not supply that adapter. ## 1. An exact sufficient source test Use the original connected certified source, actual marked faces u,v, and the normalization of [the smoothing capacity theorem](actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md). Let a specified UNTWISTED port have triangles (x,b,y),(x,c,y). Its replacement L_1=I deletes those two triangles and identifies b,c. Assume the resulting projection is connected, the marked faces remain distinct, and b,c are distinct unmarked faces. All repeated incidences after the identification are retained. The deleted port's original half twist must be zero; a remaining R^epsilon is not an identity. Let l^0 be the original positive finite face curvatures (reciprocals of Euclidean circle radii), with the two marked line variables zero. The established term "fixed-radius bound" refers to these face variables; it does not identify them with Euclidean radii. Write F for the source-normalized local fold rate, with F(t l_0,t l_1,t l_2)=F(l_0,l_1,l_2)+(1/2)log t, partial_(log l_j) F=theta_j/(2pi), theta_j=2atan(l_j/sqrt(l_0 l_1+l_1 l_2+l_2 l_0)). (1) At a one-positive-variable triple the nonzero angle is pi. These are the continuous boundary values, not a different local model. The exact original action is Phi_old=sum_(all triangles) F(l_t^0) -sum_(old finite faces) log l_f^0. For s real, replace BOTH b,c by z=exp(s), leaving every other finite face variable at l^0. Sum over the actual remaining triangles, and count the merged face only once in the target monomial. Define P_sm(s)=sum_(remaining triangles) F(l_t(s)) -sum_(smoothed finite faces) log l_f(s), G(s)=Phi_old-P_sm(s). (2) If G(s_*)=g>0 for one finite s_*, then the original marked contraction with that L_1 insertion and all other circles complete satisfies limsup_(N->infinity) N^-1 log|A_N^(L1)| <=Phi_old-g. (3) Every retained half twist on another port stays in its exact source sum. Its channel phase has modulus one, so the upper bound is valid with those phases. The original mark, N-power measure, multiplicities, beta factors, and full range of every remaining channel are retained. Proof: the exact marked face-coefficient theorem applies to the literal shorter diagram. For each label assignment its positive coefficient is bounded by evaluation at the shared radii in (2), divided by its actual target monomial. The degenerate local cases in the smoothing theorem bound every original beta^2 D D P factor by its fold rate at these same radii. Finite labels and original scalar factors contribute only a polynomial in N. Taking the sum in absolute value proves (3). No minimizer of the smoothed capacity is used. If a remaining source factor is identically zero, the bound is already stronger. The statement does not move the mark or substitute a second boundary trace. Log-radius convexity of F makes P_sm convex, hence G concave. Its derivative is the explicit actual incidence sum G'(s)=1-(1/(2pi))sum_(remaining b/c corners) theta_corner(s). (4) If a triangle acquires the merged label twice, both corners occur in this sum. Thus the best test in (2) is a one-dimensional convex minimization, with no split-side imbalance hypothesis. It may hold when the full smoothed minimizer escapes to a boundary. It is only a sufficient test; section3 proves that it need not hold at all. ## 2. Boundary regularization and the precise charged extension The strict bound has a useful continuity margin. Set the two marked face variables to small FIXED positive values eta_u,eta_v before coefficient extraction. Keep their target exponents zero, and keep all other target exponents d=N-1. Each nonzero local triple in (2) has a continuous F limit as eta_u,eta_v tend to zero. Hence these values can be fixed sufficiently small that the new evaluation rate is at most Phi_old-g/2. This does not assign target degree d to a marked face and does not take a quantum-level-dependent limit. More precisely, let P_N be one of the actual nonnegative-coefficient polynomial products after smoothing, including beta factors, and let n* be the actual target vector. At the fixed positive evaluation l*, any integer shift nu obeys |[L^(n*+nu)]P_N| <= P_N(l*)/(l*)^(n*) exp(C_l ||nu||_1). (5) A negative target exponent gives zero. Phased identifications such as c=Q^p b cost nothing in this bound: take absolute values of the polynomial coefficients before evaluation. A finite sum of such specified coefficients with total scalar norm at most N^C C_0^H and ||nu||_1<=C_1 H therefore costs only N^C exp(C_2 H) in addition to the regularized capacity. If H<=delta N with delta sufficiently small, it still has a strict exponential gap. Equation(5) is a coefficient bound, NOT an already proved L_h source expansion. Actual L_h paths retain their unwrapped physical endpoints, their c=Q^p b identifications and all clock charges. In particular, after a charged modular face average a target congruence can cross N and admit a new exponent shifted by an ENTIRE N, not merely O(h). Those aliases are not controlled by (5) with H=O(h). They must either be excluded by the actual support or be estimated separately. The fixed positive marked radii resolve the elementary Laurent-coefficient bound; they do not silently remove these finite-source questions. No signed deleted-port R^epsilon norm is discarded. ## 3. A certified matched-graph family where the capacity test fails The initial white triangulation is the octahedral sphere with equator 0,1,2,3 and poles4,5: its triangles are (p,j,j+1 modulo4), p=4,5, j=0,1,2,3. Mark the actual MAIN edge23. Choose the matching edges of the dual cubic source by the white edges {01,12,34,35}. (6) They cover each triangle exactly once, and do not contain the marked edge. Starting with b_0=5, insert b_n into the triangular interstice (0,1,b_(n-1)), replacing that triangle by its three subdivisions. Add the matching white edge b_(n-1)b_n at each step; the matching edge01 stays. This is again a perfect matching: the new triangle (0,1,b_n) inherits01, while the other two new triangles are paired by b_(n-1)b_n. The complement is the actual union of main cycles. To specify the marked diagram, use this EMBEDDED dual cubic graph, not just its abstract isomorphism class. Replace a small neighborhood of every selected matching edge by the standard untwisted complete crossing-circle box, with its four main half-edges in their inherited cyclic order. Join these half-edges along the complementary embedded edges, and put the original mark on edge23. This is an explicit augmented-link diagram. Each subdivision above replaces one trivalent source vertex in a small disk by a three-vertex triangle, retaining its three external ports and adding the specified matching edge. It therefore preserves this literal construction and its marking; no assertion that an arbitrary abstract cubic graph is an admissible source is needed. A Morse presentation gives its actual cups, caps, and complete-circle tensors. This construction does NOT prove that the diagram has the fixed flat-plat presentation required by the [marked face-coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md), sections1--3, with the same designated circle ports and mark. That theorem's gap sweep and marked conservation argument cannot simply be imported into an arbitrary Morse presentation. Neither a uniform bridge width over this family nor a source-preserving flat-plat adapter at a fixed depth is established here. Here is the labeled geometric certificate, not just a combinatorial example. In the boundary plane use the two marked parallel lines y=0 and y=2 for faces3 and2. The four finite initial circles have face0: center(0,1/2), radius1/2; face1: center(0,3/2), radius1/2; face4: center(-sqrt2,1), radius1; face5: center(+sqrt2,1), radius1. The inserted circles have center and radius center(b_n)=((2n+sqrt2)/B_n,1), radius(b_n)=1/B_n, B_n=4n^2+4sqrt2 n+1. (7) They are tangent to circles0,1 and b_(n-1), and lie strictly inside that triangle's old interstice. These statements follow directly by squaring the center distances; equivalently their curvatures satisfy the positive Descartes recurrence with the two fixed curvatures2,2. All other old circles and contacts are unchanged. Thus this is a labeled packing with precisely the stated triangulation at every n. Its halfspace certificate can also be read directly. Take the geodesic planes of these white circles and the circles through the three contact points of each complementary triangle. The latter are orthogonal to its three white circles. Their inward halfspaces give the initial ideal right-angled cuboctahedron. Each insertion attaches the ideal right-angled octahedron with the three old and three new contact points along the old shaded triangle. Its adjacent white planes are the same planes, so the seams are flat and all remaining dihedral angles are pi/2. The three new outward shaded disks are contained in the old outward shaded disk and tangent to its boundary at the old contacts. Every new ideal vertex satisfies all the other old supporting inequalities, strictly when it is not incident to that facet. Thus the coplanar seams disappear and the union is the intersection of precisely the retained and new inward halfspaces; it is convex, rather than merely locally right-angled. Induction gives a convex ideal right-angled polyhedron with the exact new labeled facets. No unlabeled volume match is used as a certificate. Consequently the labeled packing face curvatures are exactly l_0=l_1=2, l_4=l_5=1, l_2=l_3=0, l_(b_j)=B_j. The dual cubic graph is 3-connected: the initial cube is 3-connected, and replacing a vertex by its three-edge triangle preserves this property. Remove the matching port01 and its two triangles (0,1,b_n),(0,1,4), and merge b_n with4. The remaining projection is connected (already deleting the two old cubic vertices leaves a connected graph), and the marked faces2,3 remain distinct. Thus this is the literal opposite matching-edge smoothing of this marked graph. Applying section1 to its actual quantum source would additionally require the presentation adapter just specified. The geometric and capacity calculations do not require the main cycles to have one component. Only five remaining triangle terms depend on the new common radius z: two are (2,B_(n-1),z), two are (2,z,0), and one is (z,0,0). The graph capacity functional (2) is therefore exactly G_n(z)=C_n-2F(2,B_(n-1),z)-2F(2,z,0)+(1/2)log z, C_n=F(2,B_n,2)+2F(2,B_(n-1),B_n) +F(2,1,2)+2F(2,1,0)-log B_n. (8) This includes both deleted triangles and the changed face-target monomial. In particular it is not just a comparison of local volumes. We prove the obstruction uniformly over ALL z>0. Monotonicity and homogeneity of F give 2F(2,B_(n-1),z)>=log B_(n-1), 2F(2,z,0)>=log max(2,z). Thus the z-dependent expression in (8) is bounded above by its n-dependent constant minus (1/2)|log(z/2)|. Evaluation at z=2 and the following limits show that its maximizers stay in one fixed compact subset of (0,infinity). On that compact, continuity and homogeneity give uniformly F(2,B_n,2)=(1/2)log B_n+o(1), F(2,B_(n-1),B_n)=(1/2)log B_n+F(0,1,1)+o(1), 2F(2,B_(n-1),z)=log B_(n-1)+o(1). The limiting z-dependent function is -2F(2,z,0)+(1/2)log z. Its derivative vanishes only when the angle at z is pi/2, namely at z=2; strict log-radius convexity makes this its unique maximum. Substituting in (8) proves sup_(z>0) G_n(z)=-log n+K+o(1), K=F(2,1,2)+2F(2,1,0)-(3/2)log2. (9) In particular the best fixed-old-radius test is NEGATIVE for every sufficiently large n. Full radius readjustment is essential here. This does not say that the fully optimized smoothed capacity exceeds the original capacity: the former is an infimum over ALL remaining radii, whereas (8) varies only the merged radius. ## 4. Remaining general comparison Literal smoothing identifies opposite middle faces. It is not ordinary deletion of the shared white edge01, and a generic graph-minor volume inequality is not automatically its capacity inequality. Section3 also rules out promoting the one-variable test to a theorem forced by every positive labeled certificate. The general connected untwisted smoothing gap and its near-complete small-color corridor are now [proved separately](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) in the original fixed flat-plat scope. That theorem does not provide the missing presentation adapter for the family in section3. The present note retains its exact sufficient source bound in section1 and its independent matched-graph functional limitation. Signed varied ports and far-color source bounds remain separate. Focused audit: [original source and labeled certificate checks](../experiments/audit_actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap_results.json). At 80 digits it checks ten literal original marked L_1 contractions against the shorter face-coefficient source, retaining every remaining half twist and the original cups, mark, and measure. These original matrix fixtures test section1; they are NOT the Apollonian graphs of section3 and do not establish the missing adapter. The audit also checks two symbolic tangency identities; nine perfect matchings, three-connected graphs, and connected literal smoothings; 2,340 white and 3,816 shaded support values; and 432 original right-angle incidences. Seven finite optimized one-variable profiles and one positive-marked regularization check diagnose the exact normalization. The analytic argument, not those finite profiles, proves the all-n limitation in (9). No full optimized smoothing gap or L_h alias bound is inferred. Condition (3) is sufficient. The charge and alias qualifications after (5), and the fixed-old-face scope of the counterfamily, remain essential. ### Source-coverage correction, 30 October 2026 The family in Section 3 proves the geometric matched-graph capacity obstruction (9). It is not a source counterexample to the fixed-radius strategy: the exact face identity proves a fixed flat-plat formula, whereas that inference would require a general Morse formula. A link-to-plat isotopy alone does not preserve the designated complete-circle tensors, mark or face-coefficient normalization.

title: Adversarial audit of the source-volume Casson--Rivin argument
text: # Adversarial audit of the source-volume Casson--Rivin argument 29 October 2026. The filled-volume identification uses several geometric and source inputs before strict concavity. This note explains those dependencies and distinguishes the complete augmented volume from the volume after filling. ## 1. The two volumes must remain distinct The notation \(V_s\) is the volume of the COMPLETE AUGMENTED base, with its crossing-circle cusps UNFILLED. The source limit for the actual filled link is \[ V_{\mathrm{src,s}}(\boldsymbol p)=2\pi\operatorname{Re}\mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p). \] The whole-source theorem establishes this number as the original quantum limit before asserting geometric equality. It is not set equal to \(V_s\).
