In particular, an eigenvalue-ratio equation at \(Q_v=\pm1\) is not used to discard a possibly nontrivial parabolic filling word. The [marked mask geometry](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md) supplies the original complete and long-filled holonomies. The [all-circle longitude theorem](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md) supplies its full rational representation and longitude identity after circles have been inserted. The argument below connects the two at the level of ordered group words and of the [filtered stationary action](actual_main_meridian_filtered_characteristic.md). It imposes no new restriction on bare-junction valence or adjacency and adds no short-filling quantum claim. ## 1. The literal insertion Use the reduced tree of original product junctions, with consecutive unturned products already grouped. A bare vertex has full valence at least three. Its incident edges are the original quarter-turns; a binary resolution used to describe its positive kernel does not add physical edges. At a bare vertex insert the literal unturned box \(R^0=I\), at the distinguished position immediately before the original ordered child product. Encircle its two strands by a new crossing circle. Keep every child in its original order. Put \[ \epsilon_v=p_v=n_v=0 \tag{1} \] at this new circle. Filling its original primitive meridian removes the auxiliary circle and restores the literal identity box. Thus the filled tangle, its endpoints, its framed main strands and its original peripheral curves are unchanged. No new quarter-turn is inserted. Repeating the operation at all bare vertices produces a literal all-circle tree on the same physical edge set. ![A crossing circle is added around two straight strands in a fixed framed collar. Meridian filling removes it. The transported based meridians satisfy \(a_{\mathrm{out}}=a_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(b_{\mathrm{out}}=b_{\mathrm{in}}\); their chosen disk-boundary word is \(ba\).](../book/figures/zero-circle-junction.svg) The fixed access paths make these ordered equalities precise. They are constructed in section 5; the figure records the collar without choosing additional paths. For a holonomy representation, the added meridian must be projectively identity: its matrix must be a scalar. An eigenvalue ratio of one would also permit a nontrivial parabolic matrix. Section 2 excludes this ambiguity by exhibiting an auxiliary longitude with distinct eigenvalues. The original crossing powers, writhe and integer \[ a(D)=-w(D)-\sum_v n_v. \tag{2} \] are unchanged. The added circles have filling parameter zero, so their preferred-longitude surgery correction \(p_v\ell_v^2\) also vanishes. ![An ordered page attachment glues an edge block along a shaded triangle, retaining circle v and introducing circle w.](../book/figures/octahedral-page-attachment.svg) After the zero-power circles have been inserted, the [ordered all-circle cut](actual_all_circle_octahedral_decomposition.md) uses this attachment at every tree edge. The labels fix the page order. The representation comparison below also permits a flat added subdivision; it uses the original strict geometry to identify the knot holonomy. ## 2. A unique regular zero-power angular saddle Let a bare hub have \(m\ge3\) incident covariant labels \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), with \[ 0<x_j\le\tfrac12,\qquad \#\{j:x_j=\tfrac12\}\le1,\qquad \sum_jx_j>1. \tag{3} \] The [complete physical-edge theorem](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md#4-complete-physical-edge-labels-are-at-most-half) and the [original wire-window argument](actual_main_meridian_general_component_comparison.md#8-the-original-complete-wire-window-and-complex-angular-parameters) give these conditions at the original complete strict optimizer. All physical labels are strictly below half except for the internal edge of the two-trivalent-hub component; that exception supplies at most one half label to either hub. Strict whole-hub support gives the final inequality. Hidden resolution labels are not included in (3). The angular variable \(\tau\) describes the auxiliary disk longitude by \(Q=e^{i\tau}\). The [circle-incidence action](actual_main_meridian_regular_circle_trace.md) is \[ b(x,\tau)=\int_0^x \log(2\cos(2\pi r)+2\cos\tau)\,dr-2J(x), \qquad J'(x)=\log(2\sin\pi x). \tag{4} \] Here \(J(0)=0\); its derivative specifies its continued branch. For \(\tau=-iy\), \(y>0\), every logarithm in the integral is real and finite. Put \(k=\tanh(y/2)\). Direct integration gives \[ b_\tau(x,-iy)=\frac{i}{\pi} \arctan\bigl(k\tan(\pi x)\bigr), \quad 0<x<\tfrac12, \tag{5} \] with value \(i/2\) at \(x=1/2\). Indeed \[ \int_0^x\frac{\sinh y}{\cosh y+\cos2\pi r}\,dr =\frac1\pi\arctan\bigl(k\tan\pi x\bigr). \] The zero-power first-charge equation is therefore \[ \sum_jb_\tau(x_j,\tau)-i=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_j\arctan(k\tan\pi x_j)=\pi. \tag{6} \] A half label contributes \(\pi/2\). The left side is strictly increasing for \(0<k<1\), starts at zero or \(\pi/2\), and tends to \(\pi\sum_jx_j>\pi\). Thus (6) has exactly one solution \(0<k<1\). Consequently \[ y=2\operatorname{arctanh}k>0,\qquad Q=e^{i\tau}=e^y=\frac{1+k}{1-k}>1. \tag{7} \] At least two labels are strictly below half. Differentiating (6) shows that its derivative is strictly positive, so the angular Hessian is nonzero. The saddle and its selected logarithms extend holomorphically to a complex neighborhood of the fixed label tuple. The half-label case causes no singularity: the integrand of (4) remains nonzero at \(y>0\), and (6)'s derivative still has the contributions of the other labels. In particular the new auxiliary longitude has distinct eigenvalues. If its meridian has similarity one and commutes with that longitude, it is projectively identity. The possible unipotent ambiguity at \(Q^2=1\) is absent. ## 3. Exact elimination of the angular action Let \(V_m(\mathbf x)\) be the complete positive action of the whole hub. It is defined by the [ordered product kernel](actual_main_meridian_component_pressure.md#1-complete-actions-boundary-variables-and-product-junctions): resolve the original ordered product by any fixed binary association, sum its cubic gate actions, and optimize the hidden complementary labels. The conditional optimizer is strict and has negative definite Hessian on the strict whole-hub support. Then on (3), \[ V_m(\mathbf x)= \underset{\tau}{\operatorname{stat}} \left\{\sum_jb(x_j,\tau)-i\tau\right\}, \qquad \tau=-iy \text{ from (6)}. \tag{8} \] The equality includes its constant. Here is one derivation retaining the exact complete normalization. The Newton factors are the finite polynomial basis used for the tangle evaluation. For a factor with normalized index \(0<x<1/2\), the logarithm of its Laurent coefficient at normalized exponent \(r\), divided by the level, has rate \[ B_x(r)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x+r)-J(x-r),\qquad |r|\le x. \tag{9} \] The complete trace of a product has first Fourier charge one with coefficient exactly one. Its higher charges have strictly smaller rate; this follows from strict concavity of the positive coefficient convolution, or directly from the [regular bare-trace theorem](actual_main_meridian_regular_bare_trace.md). The same exact complete trace is the positive binary-resolution sum. Therefore its rate is both \(V_m(\mathbf x)\) and \[ \max_{\substack{\sum_jr_j=1\\ |r_j|\le x_j}} \sum_jB_{x_j}(r_j). \tag{10} \] The two expressions evaluate the same finite polynomial trace. Their equality determines the local action with its constant and uses no global quantum-volume asymptotic. For \(0<x<1/2\), \[ B_x'(r)=\log\frac{\sin\pi(x-r)}{\sin\pi(x+r)}. \] The unique maximizer of \(B_x(r)+yr\) is \[ r=\frac1\pi\arctan\bigl(\tanh(y/2)\tan\pi x\bigr). \tag{11} \] Moreover \[ b(x,-iy)=\max_{|r|\le x}\{B_x(r)+yr\}. \tag{12} \] To verify the constant, at \(y=0\) both sides are \(J(2x)-4J(x)\). Their \(y\)-derivatives are the same \(r\) by (5) and (11). The constrained maximizer (10) has common multiplier \(y>0\), determined by \(\sum r_j=1\). Equations (10)--(12) prove (8). A half label follows by continuity. Equivalently \(B_{1/2}(r)=0\), so its tilted maximum is \(y/2\), as also follows directly from (4). For a cubic vertex one can avoid the finite trace altogether. The old action is \[ t(x_1,x_2,x_3)= \sum_{i<j}J(x_i+x_j)-\sum_iJ(x_i)-J(x_1+x_2+x_3-1). \tag{13} \] Writing \(a_j=\tan\pi x_j\), equation (6) gives \(k^2=(a_1+a_2+a_3)/(a_1a_2a_3)\). The derivative of the right side of (8) in \(x_j\) is \[ \log\frac{\cosh y+\cos2\pi x_j}{2\sin^2\pi x_j} =\log\frac{k^2+\cot^2\pi x_j}{1-k^2}, \tag{14} \] which is exactly \(\partial_jt\). As \(\sum x_j\downarrow1\), \(y\to\infty\), and both actions tend to \(-2\sum_jJ(x_j)\). This proves the cubic identity with its absolute constant. Both sides of (8) are holomorphic near the fixed strict tuple. Their equality on an open real set proves equality of the continued germs. At the possible half label, use their holomorphic continuation from labels below half; both Hessians remain invertible there. ## 4. The actual added longitude in the old prism geometry The previous section identifies actions. The following matrix calculation identifies the new circle inside the original marked geometry. A white map is the full Möbius transition between a white face in one projection copy and its partner in the other copy. Its translation as well as its fixed points is retained. In an ordinary output port of the bare product write \[ E=e^{2\pi ib},\qquad R=\frac1{1+\kappa},\qquad \kappa=e^{-f'(b)}. \] The [marked product construction](actual_conway_general_mask_marked_filling.md#4-actual-and-virtual-white-maps-for-every-mask) gives the universal white maps \[ W_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&E-1\\0&E\end{pmatrix},\qquad W_3=\begin{pmatrix}R&0\\1-E&ER\end{pmatrix}. \tag{15} \] They are the actual top and bottom white-face maps at an unmasked bare product. Through every original binary product, the full matrix identities give \[ W_{F,1}=W_{G,1}=W_{o,1},\qquad W_{F,3}=W_{G,3}=W_{o,3} \tag{16} \] in the original world frame. Consequently the same ordered side word is seen at every port of that hub. Insert the zero-crossing box in the original disk frame. Its primitive disk-longitude path crosses these two white sides, giving \(W_1^{-1}W_3\), up to the inversion required when the circle's orientation is reversed. The determinant-one normalization is \[ P=\frac1R W_1^{-1}W_3,\qquad \operatorname{tr}P =2-\frac{4\sin^2\pi b}{R}. \tag{17} \] This is the same \(W_1^{-1}W_3\) disk word used at the corresponding end of an all-circle edge; it is not a trace chosen to fit (6). The response metric records the ordered quadrilateral shape at a product boundary. Its coordinate \(X_{\mathrm{met}}\) is distinct from the exponential wire variable \(X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}\). It is \[ X_{\mathrm{met}}^2=\frac{1+\cot^2\pi b}{1+\kappa}. \] Therefore \[ \operatorname{tr}P=2-\frac4{X_{\mathrm{met}}^2}. \tag{18} \] At a boundary incidence with covariant label \(x\), the ordinary output is \(b=1-x\), and the conditional action satisfies \(f'(b)=-\partial_xV_m\). Using (14), valid at any valence by the envelope identity (8), gives \[ X_{\mathrm{met}}^2 =\frac1{\sin^2\pi x\,[1+\exp(\partial_xV_m)]} =\operatorname{sech}^2(y/2)=1-k^2. \tag{19} \] Thus \[ \operatorname{tr}P=-2\cosh y=-(Q+Q^{-1}). \tag{20} \] This proves that the actual added longitude has the regular eigenvalues required by the angular saddle. The proof retains the old group word, and shows why a bare hub has a common \(Q\) across all its pages. When an incidence is viewed through its physical turn, the old identity \(T W_{j+1}(E,R)=W_j(E^{-1},1-R)T\) takes the \(W_1^{-1}W_3\) word to the appropriate inverse of the \(W_2^{-1}W_0\) word. Its trace is unchanged. The auxiliary flag may be selected on the eigenvalue \(-Q\), \(Q>1\); the main meridian flags are not changed by this auxiliary choice. ## 5. What the edge equations see at the complete bare representation Pull the original complete holonomy back along the exact filling quotient obtained in section 1. This gives a representation of the enlarged augmented link with every newly added meridian equal to identity. It is a representation-theoretic pullback; no assertion that the drilled link carries this metric is needed. ### The marked zero-crossing collar Choose the box in a framed ball \(D^2\times[0,1]\), with its two strands \(\{p_1,p_2\}\times[0,1]\). Choose a basepoint \(z_*\in\partial D^2\), an ordered pair of disjoint access paths from it to small circles around \(p_1,p_2\), and transport that entire system by the product framing. Orient and name the resulting based puncture loops \(a,b\) so that the oriented disk-boundary word is \(ba\). The boundary basepath is \(\{z_*\}\times[0,1]\). Transport across this literal zero-crossing box gives \[ a_{\mathrm{out}}=a_{\mathrm{in}},\qquad b_{\mathrm{out}}=b_{\mathrm{in}}. \tag{22c} \] These are equalities in the based fundamental group, before taking any representation. No permutation of punctures, turn of an access path, or power of the disk-boundary curve is included. Place the new auxiliary circle at the disk boundary in the middle of this collar, with the original disk framing. Its longitude is the parallel copy of that boundary and retains the based word \(ba\). The meridian filling deletes the auxiliary circle and returns exactly the framed collar just described. Its quotient on fundamental groups fixes \(a,b\), their access paths, and the boundary basepath. Thus it also fixes the ordered maps by which this collar is joined to all earlier and later product factors. This remains true when there are several child factors: transport the same system through them in their recorded order. It never requires the factors to commute. For comparison with a pair of projection faces, transport the framed loops to the face basepoints along the original specified paths. If the old transport is \(C_0\), (22c) becomes the simultaneous conjugacy \(C_0aC_0^{-1}=a'\), \(C_0bC_0^{-1}=b'\). Reading the other side of a puncture changes the corresponding native generator to its inverse. Those inversions are recorded explicitly in (22b) below; they do not change (22c) into a braid. This is the marked van Kampen statement used at every added seam. Only a retained nonzero half twist changes (22c), by the separately calibrated Hurwitz action. A port here is the ordered quadrilateral chart supplied by the original cell construction. It is not assumed to be a new four-punctured topological boundary. On a physical turn edge use its original coordinate \((0,\infty,1,R)\) and its phase \(E=e^{2\pi ix}\). This is the transported physical-edge frame from the last paragraph of section 4; its phase is the reciprocal of the ordinary-output phase \(e^{2\pi ib}\), with the corresponding change \(R\mapsto1-R\). At \(M=1\) the four [native all-circle white matrices](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md#2-the-local-face-maps) are exactly the universal old \(W_j(E,R)\), projectively. This follows by putting \(m=1\) in the explicit native chart, without specializing the auxiliary eigenvalues to one. The two disk words have normalized traces \(-\beta,-\gamma\), where \[ \beta=\frac{2R-(E+E^{-1})}{1-R},\qquad \gamma=\frac{2-(E+E^{-1})-2R}{R}. \tag{21} \] At an inserted hub these are supplied by (20); at an original circle they are its original marked longitude trace. Eliminating \(R\) yields \[ A=\frac{4-\beta\gamma}{\beta+\gamma+4}, \qquad A=E+E^{-1}, \tag{22} \] which is exactly the all-circle edge equation at \(M=1\). Thus the old phase is one of its two reciprocal roots. The native white maps retain \(E\) itself, not just \(E+E^{-1}\); the existing native/character comparison identifies the all-circle source variable with that \(E\). All character-chart denominators are units at this point: \(\beta,\gamma\ge2\), \(E\ne1\), and the displayed original port vertices are distinct. The allowed value \(E=-1\) on the two-hub half edge does not cause a character-matrix singularity. In that case the edge quadratic may ramify over its endpoint parameters; one must use the full stationary branch or another local coordinate, not assert that \(E\) is a simple quadratic root. Indeed \(E=-1\) gives \[ (\beta-2)(\gamma-2)=16 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X_{\mathrm{met},v}^{\,2}+X_{\mathrm{met},w}^{\,2}=1, \tag{22e} \] by (18). This is the possible half-edge fold of the old geometry. The normalized matrices and the two irreducible puncture pairs below remain regular there. Here is the boundary-group comparison, including the tuple that has to be retained. First choose the normalized native matrix representatives for the four old projective white maps. In terms of the raw universal representatives used in (15), their scalar factors are respectively \[ E^{-1},\quad E^{-1},\quad [E(1-R)]^{-1},\quad (ER)^{-1}. \tag{22d} \] Each normalized matrix has determinant \(E^{-1}\) at \(M=1\). The raw universal representatives do not all have that determinant: in particular the factors involving \(R\) and \(1-R\) cannot be discarded when taking an SL trace. With \(W_j\) now denoting these normalized native representatives, put in each original edge frame \[ N_j=W_{j-1}^{-1}W_j,\qquad (A,B,C,D)=(N_3,N_0,N_1,N_2) \tag{22a} \] with the subsequent determinant-one puncture normalizations from the all-circle chart. These subsequent powers of \(M\), not the scalar factors in (22d), are one at \(M=1\). Thus every \(N_j\) has determinant one and trace two. The actual page table is \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{end}&(a,b)&(a',b')&ba=b'a'\\ \hline v&(B,A)&(C^{-1},D^{-1})&AB\\ w&(B^{-1},C^{-1})&(A,D)&(BC)^{-1}. \end{array} \tag{22b} \] The entries refer to paths, with the inverse on each puncture determined by its side of the disk. They are exactly the table of the literal all-circle cut, not a new identification of equal traces. To apply that table to the old holonomy, first insert the zero-crossing box in the actual diagram, before assigning matrices. The main strands and their ordered endpoint paths are unchanged. Add the new circle and perform the literal projection/disk cut. The filling quotient takes every old main meridian and its old basepath to itself and kills the new circle meridian. In particular the four small corner paths reduce to the original consecutive-white words in (22a). A white face split by the added cut retains the same transport on both of its pieces: crossing the extra cut and returning differs by the new meridian, whose image is identity. This is also the full-map invariant (16) through every prism of the original product. Thus the developed four white transitions of the pulled-back representation are exactly the four \(W_j\) already compared above. The paths across the added disk pages are still the paths of this cut. By van Kampen they intertwine both generators in the appropriate row of (22b), with precisely the displayed inversions; the product column is their original primitive disk boundary. The inserted box has no crossing, so no Hurwitz exchange is made at its distinguished seam. The old retained half twists keep their original exchanges. At \(M=1\), either input pair in (22b) is irreducible. Both punctures have trace two, and the products in the two rows have traces \(-\beta\) and \(-\gamma\), respectively, with \(\beta,\gamma\ge2\). Their irreducibility obstructions are \((\beta+2)^2\ne0\) and \((\gamma+2)^2\ne0\). Two intertwiners of either full ordered pair differ by its scalar centralizer. Therefore the pulled-back page transport equals the native pure transport in PGL. At an original odd seam the same argument is applied after the already calibrated full Hurwitz action. The corner flags on the main cusp are the old parabolic flags, and the extra auxiliary flags are chosen from (20); these choices do not alter a group generator. All white and shaded generators of the cut now agree, in their original tree frames. This proves equality of the complete representations, not only of the local character triples or the main-cusp translation. It identifies the selected all-circle algebraic point with the pullback of the original bare-tree holonomy. The newly introduced ideal vertices need not form positive tetrahedra in this pulled-back representation. In particular an edge with \(E=-1\) can make that added subdivision flat. No metric on the enlarged unfilled exterior is asserted or required. ## 6. Stationary elimination at a nonparabolic main meridian Let \(t\) be the actual main deformation parameter, \(M=e^{\pi it}\). In the existing strict-tree filtered action it enters only through \[ \sum_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \{2J(x_e)-J(x_e+t)-J(x_e-t)\} +\frac{\pi i a(D)}2t^2. \tag{23} \] It does not enter the old bare tensor action or its hidden resolution wires. The enlarged all-circle action replaces a bare hub by \(\sum_jb(x_j,\tau_v)-i\tau_v\), with \(n_v=0\). Eliminating \(\tau_v\) by (8) returns exactly the old whole-hub action, including its constant, for complex physical wires in the regular neighborhood. The edge set and (23) do not change, and neither does \(a(D)\). Hence the two full critical-value germs are equal after stationary elimination. The new angular Hessian at each bare hub is nonzero. To state the comparison precisely, first eliminate the old hidden binary-resolution variables. Their conditional Hessian is invertible by strictness. Let \(z\) collect the remaining original variables and let \(\tau_{\mathrm{new}}\) collect only the added angular variables. The enlarged Hessian has blocks \[ H_{\mathrm{new}}= \begin{pmatrix} H_{zz}&H_{z\tau}\\ H_{\tau z}&H_{\tau\tau} \end{pmatrix},\qquad H_{\mathrm{old,red}} =H_{zz}-H_{z\tau}H_{\tau\tau}^{-1}H_{\tau z}. \tag{23a} \] The block \(H_{\tau\tau}\) is diagonal over the added hubs, with nonzero entries from (6). Equality (8) identifies its Schur complement with the old reduced Hessian. The original full Hessian and its eliminated hidden block are invertible, so \(\det H_{\mathrm{new}} =\det H_{\tau\tau}\det H_{\mathrm{old,red}}\ne0\). No individual edge Hessian is inverted, including at (22e). The enlarged analytic branch therefore exists with all the original logarithms retained. Original sufficiently long fillings keep their auxiliary \(Q_v^2\ne1\); every added zero-power circle has \(Q_v^2\ne1\) by (7), and this persists near the complete branch. By section 5 this branch reconstructs the original filled knot representation, rather than only an algebraic solution of the slope eigenvalue equations. Near the old augmented complete point the original auxiliary deformation is fixed by its primitive peripheral rows. Equality at completeness and the marked gluing/representation local inverse identify the two nearby deformations. The original sufficiently long filling point lies on that same small branch. There every original filled circle, as well as every added zero circle, has \(Q_v^2\ne1\); the filling words are projectively identity by section 2. The nondegenerate main-meridian branch is then the geometric germ of the original filled knot. The all-circle squared longitude identity is a rational identity on its integral source variety. It extends to this regular representation, including the half-edge fold, without solving for an individual edge root. The added zero fillings contribute no surgery exponent, the Seifert sign is that of the same original complete knot, and stationary elimination leaves the effective longitude unchanged. Consequently \[ L_{\mathrm{geom}}(M) =-M^{a(D)} \prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)} \tag{24} \] on the original strict-tree filled branch, with \(X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}\). This proves the theorem on the geometric germ of the original filled knot. The same physical edges occur before and after the zero-circle elimination, and the added circles contribute neither a crossing power nor a preferred-longitude shear. The geometric identification uses the full ordered boundary-group comparison in section 5. The equality of actions in section 3 supplies the stationary branch, while the marked face maps identify its representation. These are distinct parts of the proof. The established strict-tree quantum estimates retain their existing long-filling hypotheses; this argument adds no estimate for short fillings. ## 7. The geometric factor selected by the actual recurrence The geometric theorem identifies the curve already selected by the full asymptotic expansion of the original strict-tree invariant. This extends the operator consequence beyond trees whose junctions all carry crossing circles. It requires no quantum estimate for the newly drilled diagram: the quantum source remains the original strict presentation. Fix an oriented strict ordered Conway knot presentation \(D\), with its original cut, endpoint orders, framing and signed integral crossing powers. Assume the powers are independently sufficiently long for the [filled-meridian theorem](actual_main_meridian_filled_volume.md) and the geometric theorem above. The entire diagram and every power are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. All original knot-pattern and absence-of-internal-component qualifications remain in force. Both level parities and all sufficiently large composite levels are included. Write \(F_N(M)\) for the actual zero-framed reduced ADO invariant, with \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad M=-q_Nx,\qquad F_N(1)=K_N(K). \tag{O1} \] Here \(x\) is the raw highest-weight parameter, distinct from an internal normalized index \(x_e\). The marked complete meridian is \(M=1\), and \(X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}\) denotes the original physical-edge variable. Let \[ P(q,M,T)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,M)T^j,\qquad a_j\in\mathbb C(q,M),\qquad TM=qMT, \tag{O2} \] be any specified nonzero fixed operator that annihilates the whole function \(F_N(M)\) at every sufficiently large level. The shift \(T\) replaces \(M\) by \(qM\). Such an actual all-level annihilator exists by the [finite-sum construction](finite_sum_annihilator.md); it is not defined by fitting the complete values or adjoining a desired factor. An operator with negative shift powers can first be multiplied by a power of \(T\). Clear fixed rational denominators, remove the common \(q-1\) valuation of the coefficients, and denote the resulting first nonzero classical symbol by \(P_0(M,L)\). Let \(A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb C}(M,L)\) generate the Laurent prime of the actual geometric eigenvalue germ through \((1,-1)\), in the preferred meridian and longitude of the original knot. The longitude coordinate is its eigenvalue on the \(M\) line, equivalently the inverse eigenvalue on the source \(M^{-1}\) line. Then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle A_{\mathrm{geom},\mathbb C}(M,L)\mid P_0(M,L) \quad\text{in }\mathbb C[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}].} \tag{O3} \] Thus every genuine all-level annihilator has the same selected irreducible geometric factor in its first classical symbol. ### Proof and normalization The [filtered characteristic theorem](actual_main_meridian_filtered_characteristic.md), Sections 2–6, already applies to the full strict long-filling class, including arbitrary bare components. It proves the complete microscopic expansion with its degree filtration on all the finitely many translated parameter charts needed by (O2). This shifted-chart statement follows from the exact source and its endpoint estimates, not from continuation of an asymptotic formula on a single disk. The normalized full state is \[ \mathcal Z_N(s)=\frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)},\qquad H_N(s)=\frac{\sin\pi s}{N\sin(\pi s/N)}. \tag{O4} \] It retains the exact modified-dimension gauge \[ d_N(M)=\eta_N\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}},\qquad d_N(1)=\eta_N/N,\qquad \frac{d_N(q_N^s)}{d_N(1)}=H_N(s)^{-1}. \tag{O5} \] Here \(\eta_N=i^{N+3}\). Put \(f(M)=M-M^{-1}\). The operator on the full state has shift coefficients \[ \widetilde a_j(q,M) =a_j(q,M)(-1)^j\frac{f(M)}{f(q^jM)}. \tag{O6} \] After multiplication on the left by \(\prod_{j=1}^{d}f(q^jM)\), its first classical symbol is \(f(M)^dP_0(M,-L)\). The meridian divisor and the shift sign are therefore present before any formal cancellation. The filtered theorem defines the selected critical value \(S(t)\) using the original phase and the insertion \[ \sum_{e\in\mathcal E_T} [2J(x_e)-J(x_e+t)-J(x_e-t)] +\frac{\pi i a(D)}2t^2. \tag{O7} \] Its expansion has coefficient of order \(N^{-r}\) of degree at most \(r+1\) in \(s\). The top-degree coefficients come from \(S\); lower Gaussian amplitudes cannot change them. With \(\mathcal S(u)=\pi i[S(u/(\pi i))-S(0)]\), the exact operator equation and this filtration give the formal domain identity \[ f(e^u)^dP_0(e^u,-e^{\mathcal S'(u)})=0. \tag{O8} \] The full argument, including injectivity of the substitution \(u=hs\), is in [the all-circle operator proof](actual_all_circle_geometric_characteristic.md#11-the-geometric-factor-of-an-actual-quantum-recurrence), Section 11.3. That argument depends on the filtered source expansion and the exact gauge, not on the absence of bare vertices. The nonzero series \(f(e^u)^d\) can be cancelled in this proved integral domain identity. The new geometric input identifies its entire selected germ: \[ -e^{\mathcal S'(\log M)} =-M^{a(D)}\prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)} =L_{\mathrm{geom}}(M). \tag{O9} \] The zero-circle elimination above preserves the whole critical-value germ and the original physical-edge set. Its ordered boundary-group anchor identifies the original filled geometric representation. The preferred-longitude sign is fixed at that filled knot point. Thus (O9) is not inferred from the cusp tangent or from a choice among unmarked exponentiated solutions. It follows that \(P_0\) vanishes on the geometric eigenvalue germ. Its Laurent evaluation kernel is a nonzero prime and contains no nonzero polynomial in \(M\) alone, because \(M\) varies. It is therefore a height-one prime in a Laurent polynomial unique factorization domain, proving (O3). If the operator coefficients lie in \(\mathbb Q(q,M)\), contract that same germ prime to \(\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]\). Its irreducible generator divides the rational symbol. Its complex factorization contains the selected geometric factor and any conjugate factors required over \(\mathbb Q\); an individual complex component need not itself be defined over \(\mathbb Q\). ## 8. Transfer to presentations with net twists and arbitrary closures The conclusion is intrinsic to the zero-framed knot with its marked peripheral curves. Suppose the [ordered net-twist reduction](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md) gives an actual ambient isotopy from the input knot to a strict knot presentation covered by Section 7. The isotopy carries the knot orientation, meridian, preferred zero-linking longitude and cut mark. Correcting any transported ribbon framing to zero gives exactly the same reduced ADO function \(F_N(M)\) at every level and every meridian value where it is defined. Its rational continuation is therefore the same function as well. The geometric eigenvalue germ is also the same under this marked isotopy. An actual all-level operator for the input family thus satisfies the hypotheses of Section 7 for that same intrinsic family. Its first classical symbol contains the selected geometric factor. This transfers the factor statement without identifying presentation-specific recurrence formulas or their unreduced polynomial representatives. The same argument applies to the [arbitrary-closure reduction](actual_conway_arbitrary_closure_volume.md) when its hypotheses yield one covered strict knot factor and only unknot factors. In particular, under its long surviving-factor hypotheses, a hyperbolic knot input has exactly that form. Removing the exhibited unknot summands is an actual orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. The preferred peripheral pair is carried by the induced map of exteriors. No multiplicativity assertion for quantum growth over connected sums is required. For a fixed original expression there are finitely many recorded reduction and parity branches. If a uniform net-weight statement is desired, take the maximum of the strict source and geometric thresholds over those finitely many possible strict outputs. The threshold concerns their surviving signed net powers. Large individual powers that cancel to a short surviving power do not satisfy it. This does not assert that an earlier, smaller complete-value threshold automatically supplies the stronger moving-meridian hypotheses. The integer \(a(D)\) and the individual edge factors in (O9) are computed on the covered strict diagram. They are not claimed to equal those read from an unreduced input presentation term by term. The preferred geometric longitude and its selected irreducible factor are the intrinsic objects that transfer. The conclusions concern one irreducible geometric factor, not the full A-polynomial, its multiplicity, or an equality of quantum operator ideals. They do not provide a fixed-\(M\) large-level WKB theorem, nonvanishing through ordinary-color resonances, or a general short-twist theorem. The wider quantitative all-circle alternatives remain available under their own source and geometric hypotheses; this section neither narrows those results nor extends them to arbitrary short bare-junction fillings.

title: A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current
text: # A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current 29 October 2026. This is an independent finite FACTORIAL theorem. It does not assume that a proposed four-port source coefficient is a Racah sum. On the full folded supported chamber it proves a common phase, a positive root normalization, a uniform positive Laplace principle, and polynomial relative bounds for every fixed generic-q normal jet. Complementary high partners have the same positive value core but an additional explicitly retained normal current. Connecting these formulas to the actual source requires its separate typed coefficient identity. A positive root value is not by itself a bound on a complete Hermite recoupling operator. ## 1. Seven factorials, with a root unit at every denominator Fix N>=3, D=N-1, M=floor(D/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and six INTEGER folded spins 0<=a,b,c,d,e,f<=M. Define four faces and three quads F=(a+b+e, c+d+e, a+d+f, b+c+f), Q=(a+b+c+d, a+c+e+f, b+d+e+f). (1) Assume every F_i>=D. Every face is an ordinary triangle: its two smaller entries sum to at least D minus its largest, which is at least its largest because D>=2M. Moreover EVERY face deficit F_i-2ell lies in [0,D]. Every difference Q_k-F_i is one such deficit of a complementary face. Therefore z_-=max F_i <= z_+=min Q_k, D<=z_-<=z_+<=4M<=2D, 0<=z-F_i<=D, 0<=Q_k-z<=D. (2) Use the GENUINE generic symmetric factorial [n]!_zeta, with [u]_zeta=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1). Set S(zeta)=sum_(z=z_-)^(z_+) (-1)^z [z+1]! /[product_i [z-F_i]! product_k[Q_k-z]!]. (3) No negative factorial is assigned a value: the displayed interval is the true finite range. By (2), every denominator is a unit at q. The numerator contains EXACTLY ONE factor [N]. Factoring it BEFORE specialization defines the analytic function G(zeta)=(-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) Let s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), s_0=1. The exact positive root value is R_N:=G(q)=N sum_z s_(z-D) /[product_i s_(z-F_i) product_k s_(Q_k-z)]>0. (5) Indeed the signs of [N+1],...,[z+1] multiply to (-1)^(z+1-N). Together with (-1)^(D+z) this is +1. Also s_D=N. The powers of 2sin(pi/N) cancel, since sum_i(z-F_i)+sum_k(Q_k-z)=z, sum_i F_i=sum_k Q_k=2(a+b+c+d+e+f). Thus (5) is a finite exact identity, including boundary faces F_i=D, collapsed z intervals, both level parities and composite levels. ## 2. The exact positive face metric For a face (x,y,z) of sum F, define the generic squared triangle factor and its regular normalization by Delta_F^2=[F-2x]![F-2y]![F-2z]!/[F+1]!, D_F(zeta)=(-1)^(F-D)[N]_zeta Delta_F^2. It is analytic and nonzero at q, with positive root value d_F=D_F(q) =s_(F-2x)s_(F-2y)s_(F-2z)/(N s_(F-D))>0. (6) The natural positive normalized scalar is W_N=R_N sqrt(product_faces d_F). (7) This metric is not optional in a geometric interpretation. The branch-independent generic squared identity is EXACTLY [N]^2 S(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_F^2 =G(zeta)^2 product_faces D_F(zeta). (8) The root of its right side is W_N^2>0. There is no residual sign, because sum_faces(F-D)=2(a+b+c+d+e+f)-4D is even. Equation(8) defines a finite factorial normalization; it is not a claim that an as-yet-unproved physical recoupling matrix is unitary in this metric. The ordered physical Clebsch norms, source gamma factors and any intermediate quantum dimensions must still be matched by an actual coefficient theorem. A quantum dimension can vanish at the odd simple endpoint. It is not canceled by evaluating (7) alone; its generic source limit must be retained before interpreting this as a physical Gram. ## 3. A uniform positive action on the ENTIRE folded chamber Put L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du on [0,1], continuously at both endpoints. Write x=(a,b,c,d,e,f)/N, D_N=D/N, and use the same linear forms F_i(x),Q_k(x). On I_N=[max_i F_i(x),min_k Q_k(x)] define A_N(x,Z)=L(Z-D_N)-sum_i L(Z-F_i(x)) -sum_k L(Q_k(x)-Z), V_N(x,Z)=A_N(x,Z) +(1/2)sum_faces[sum_(ell in face)L(F(x)-2x_ell) -L(F(x)-D_N)]. (9) Uniformly over ALL allowed integral labels, log R_N=N max_(Z in I_N) A_N(x,Z)+O(log N), log W_N=N max_(Z in I_N) V_N(x,Z)+O(log N). (10) Proof. Every factorial index is in [0,D], so the uniform elementary sine-factorial estimate log s_r=N L(r/N)+O(log N) applies to every term, including endpoints. There are at most 2N positive terms. Their maximum gives the upper bound and one term gives the lower. The modulus of continuity of L is O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)); rounding Z to a feasible integral index changes N times the action by at most O(log N). All constants are independent of the labels. The same estimate applied to the four explicit factors (6) proves the second line. Thus no cancellation or selected complex saddle is required. For any convergent scaled-label sequence, (10) yields the corresponding max-action limit, with D_N replaced by 1. This is an action theorem; identification with an actual geometric tetrahedron is a separate task. Two calibrations expose the metric's role. At all six scaled labels 1/3, the bare action maximum is 3v3/pi, whereas the face metric adds -2v3/pi and the normalized maximum is v3/pi. At all six labels 1/2, the metric action is zero and the normalized maximum is v8/pi. Here v3=3Lambda(pi/3), v8=8Lambda(pi/4). The maxima occur respectively at Z=7/6 and Z=7/4, by direct differentiation of (9). The independently proved [local hyperideal geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) now identifies this normalized maximum with actual truncated-tetrahedron volume. Its exact Casimir angle coordinates are a_ell=(ell+1/2)/N. Using Z=(z+7/4)/N shifts the numerator factorial argument by 3/(4N), each denominator argument by 1/(4N), and every face-metric argument by 1/(2N). The same uniform endpoint modulus gives the SHARP scalar bound log W_N=(N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))+O(log N) (10a) on the entire supported chamber, with a universal error constant. Vol_ext denotes the continuous boundary-volume extension when an odd simple channel has zero dihedral angle. This is a local scalar energy calibration, not a proof that a source graph supplies the corresponding cell gluing or a completed Hermite metric. ## 4. Polynomial relative generic normal jets, not just root values Take zeta=q exp(t), with ALL integer labels fixed, and cancel the single displayed [N] in each term of (3). This is the actual generic factorial germ, not a formal root recurrence continued off the root. There is a universal c>0 such that on |t|<=r_N=c/[N^2(1+log N)] (11) the functions G and each D_F are holomorphic and nonzero, and their ratios to their positive root values differ from one by less than 1/4. The canonical analytic square roots of D_F, positive at t=0, therefore define H(t)=G(t) product_F sqrt(D_F(t)), with H(0)=W_N. Shrinking the SAME universal c if necessary gives |H/H(0)-1|<1/4. Here is a uniform proof. After cancellation, all factors zeta-zeta^-1 cancel too, by the factorial degree equality used in section1. Every remaining factor is zeta^u-zeta^-u, 1<=u<2N, u!=N. At t=0 its absolute value is at least 4 dist(u,N Z)/N. For |t|<=N^-2, its derivative has absolute value at most 30N. Thus each unit factor's logarithmic change is bounded by 15N^2|t|/dist(u,N Z) when that relative change is small. Across a summand there are at most eighteen copies of the harmonic sum sum_(k=1)^N 1/k; the four face factors have the same fixed bound. Consequently each product ratio has logarithmic change at most C N^2(1+log N)|t|, with universal C. Choosing, for example, a sufficiently small c<=10^-6 makes every summand stay in a small common sector around its POSITIVE value in (5). A positive weighted sum stays in that sector as well. This proves (11), including the nonzero lower bound and analytic square roots. Cauchy's inequality now gives, for every fixed k>=0 and F=G or H, |F^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k F(0), |(1/F)^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k/F(0). (12) Thus finite normal jets and inverse scalar jets have polynomial relative cost UNIFORMLY throughout this folded supported chamber. This scalar assertion does not estimate a change of physical frame. Together with (10a), it bounds squared fixed normal jets by a polynomial times exp[(2N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))], with all joint labels still shared. ## 5. Complementary partners: positive value core and a real missing current Now replace ANY subset of the six folded labels ell by D-ell. At each face, its new deficits are old deficits, their complements D-old_deficit, the old excess F-D, or its complement D-(F-D). They all lie in [0,D]. Its new sum lies in [D,2D]. Therefore (2)'s denominator-unit assertion survives at EVERY one of the up to 64 partner assignments, and the new z range is nonempty with z_-<=2D. Also the sum of its six labels is at most 4D, because every new face has sum at most 2D. Hence z_+<=8D/3<3N-1. The generic sum still contains [N] in every term, but some terms now contain [2N] too. The EXACT decomposition is (-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta=C(zeta)+[2N]_zeta T(zeta), (13) where C sums the TRUE terms z<=2D after deleting the numerator [N], and T sums the terms z>=2N-1 after deleting BOTH [N] and [2N]. All their denominators are units. At q the nonempty core is exactly the positive expression (5), with z truncated at 2D. The positive metric (6) and squared identity (8) apply at every partner value too. The core C has the same polynomial scalar-jet bound as section4. The term [2N]T is NOT zero as a generic normal. In particular ((-1)^D S/[N])'(0)=C'(0)+(4N/(q-q^-1))T(0). (14) Writing z=2N-1+k, its retained root value is explicitly T(0)=-2sin(pi/N)N^2 sum_k (-1)^k s_k /[product_i s_(2N-1+k-F_i) product_j s_(Q_j-2N+1-k)]. (15) Every index in (15) is physical. The alternating sum must remain coherent. Its absolute-value envelope is not a substitute for it. For example N=4, partner labels (2,2,2,2,2,1) arise by five flips from the supported folded labels (1,1,1,1,1,1). Their faces are (6,6,5,5), quads (8,7,7). Core z=6 gives C(0)=sqrt(2), while the single tail term z=7 gives T(0)=-1. The EXTRA first normal in (14) is exactly 8sqrt(2)i. Deleting the tail loses actual data. Accordingly (12) is a theorem for the complete LOW-fold scalar germ and for partner value cores. It is NOT asserted for the full partner germ without a further coherent estimate for T. Nor are the partner columns deleted from a physical Hermite cluster. This is the remaining normal interface for using the positive factorial in a full recoupling energy argument. A research lead, originally unproved, is preserved by the [64-partner value diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_supported_racah_partner_value_reflection.py) and its [recorded root images](../experiments/supported_racah_partner_value_reflection_diagnostic_results.json). For three specified folded tuples per level when distinct, every one of the 64 complement bit patterns was checked at N=3,...,10: 1408 comparisons showed no failure of W_squared invariance. These are exact finite cyclotomic-root images, not a uniform complex identity proof. No symmetry of generic germs, bound on the [2N] current, completed physical Gram or volume theorem is inferred from that observation. The subsequent [actual partner-reflection theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md) now proves the root-value symmetry uniformly from the actual reciprocal source and analytic projector residues. Its exact first-normal counterexample shows why this does not establish generic-jet symmetry. ## 6. An exact valuation interface to the separately proved physical kernel The preceding factorial theorem has not used a source identity. One can now APPLY the independently proved [actual inverse four-port theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), equations (23),(24). Put its external highest weights (A,B,C,D_ext)=(2a,2b,2c,2d), E=2e and G=2f. It states L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) *S, p=min(a+d,b+c), q=max(a+d,b+c), s=p+q, n=p-f, t0=q-p, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n]. (16) Throughout the fully supported folded chamber, chi_E X_E, b_G and J_n are root units, while S0 has exactly one [N] zero. This follows directly from the source product formulas: all their physical factorial indices are <=D, whereas the numerator of S0 is [s+1]! with D<=s<=2D. For X_E at its endpoint, its numerator index is <=A when that endpoint is H, and <=B when it is A. Hence no endpoint root zero has been hidden in that assertion. Both f faces imply p+f>=D and q+f>=D. The sole possible numerator zero of V_n is at index k=p+f-D. It is INSIDE 0,...,n-1 exactly when 2f<D. Its denominator has no root zero: t0+n=q-f<=D, and the first potential zero in (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n has index s-D>=n. Consequently the actual inverse coefficient has exact order ord_q L_(G,E)=-1 if 2f<D, ord_q L_(G,E)= 0 if 2f=D. (17) Its leading coefficient is nonzero by the positive finite sum (5). Thus a positive root factorial does NOT turn the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix into a finite positive operator: paired output channels have genuine simple poles and must be combined with their partners in a regular Hermite frame. The same bookkeeping in the actual ordered invariant norm N_E=n_(ab)^e n_(cd)^e [2e+1] gives order two for paired e and order one for odd simple e. These are source-frame orders, not optional quantum-dimension factors. Equations (16),(17) supply an explicit local interface for matching the positive metric (6) to a completed physical recoupling energy; they do not complete that matching or bound the partner current (15). Audit: [true root factorials, partner ranges and retained Taylor coefficients](../experiments/audit_actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.py). The common phase, metric, uniform action and jet arguments above are independent of the proposed actual four-port source identity. The result does not include a full partner-jet bound or a positive completed physical recoupling Gram.

title: A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel
text: # A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel 29 October 2026. The colliding c_0 Casimir channel containing the original cup has an explicit generalized vector with harmonic-sum coefficients. Its source-adapted Hermite frame has UNIFORMLY bounded physical condition number after a common N^(3/2) scale. In that frame the original marked and ordinary caps are exactly the two coordinate rows, and the full crossing is a unit scalar times a Jordan matrix with uniformly bounded off-diagonal coefficient. This proves an actual source-controlled Hermite Gram for the selected T=N-1 channel, including its derivative direction. It does not estimate recoupling from this channel into all other channels on overlapping pairs. No full-channel q-Racah norm or sharp knot bound follows yet. ## 1. The original physical source and Casimir Fix `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `rho=q-q^(-1)`, `x=q^d=-q^(-1)`, `N>=2`. On balanced heads use exactly mathsfF|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, K|a>=xQ^(-a)|a>, F_tot=mathsfF_1+K_1^(-1)mathsfF_2, E_tot=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2, Omega=F_tot E_tot+qK_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). Missing endpoint arrows are zero. Work on the physical integer-degree d subspace with basis `|u,d-u>`, `0<=u<=d`. Let `c_*=q+q^(-1)`. The original cup, ordinary pivotal cap and marked row restrict here to p_u=N x^(u-d), ell_u=x^(-u)Q^(-u)/N, m_u=x^(d-u)/N^2. (1) The unrestricted marked row is not replaced by this restricted row on other degrees; every vector constructed below has degree d. These are the fixed actual turns, with no invented scalar frame. Define finite harmonic sums H_0=0, H_u=sum_(j=1)^u 1/(1-Q^j), g_u=x^(u-d)=p_u/N, v_u=-g_u H_u/rho. (2) Then the exact Jordan equations are (Omega-c_*)g=0, (Omega-c_*)v=g. (3) In particular g,v are independent, and their span is the actual size-two c_* block inside integer degree d. This block, rather than the entire 2N-dimensional c_* generalized eigenspace across degrees, is the source channel treated in this note. ## 2. Derivation from generic q with actual cup duality retained Use a variable z near q and the ordinary highest-weight representation of highest weight d=N-1. Put `Q_z=z^2`, `x(z)=z^d`, `F_a(z)=product_(j=1)^a(1-z^(2j))`. Keep the standard highest-weight endpoint, including `mathsfF|d>=0`. All factorials with `a<N` are nonzero near q. The top-channel descendant and spin-zero invariant cup may be normalized as g_u(z)=x(z)^(u-d), h_u(z)=g_u(z) R_u(z), R_u(z)=(-1)^u z^[-u(u+1)] F_u(z)F_(d-u)(z)/F_d(z). (4) Indeed `g(z)=F_tot(z)^d|0,0>/F_d(z)`. The finite coproduct binomial proves its displayed components. The E equation for an invariant degree-d vector gives the successive ratio h_(u+1)/h_u=-z^[d-2u-2] (1-z^(2u+2))/(1-z^(2d-2u)), which is (4); direct F and K equations give `F_tot h=0`, `K_tot h=h`. Thus h is the ACTUAL self-duality cup up to the stated analytic unit normalization. Its paired evaluation is transported reciprocally. One does not extend the root-only expression `K^(1-N)` as a generic-q pivot or assume a root cyclic endpoint away from q. The exact Casimir eigenvalues are Omega(z)g(z)=c_top(z)g(z), Omega(z)h(z)=c_triv(z)h(z), c_top(z)=z^(2N-1)+z^(-2N+1), c_triv(z)=z+z^(-1). (5) These follow from the defining coproduct: the top highest vector has K-root `z^(2d)`, while h is invariant. They can also be checked directly from the entries above. Root complementation gives `R_u(q)=1`, so `h(q)=g(q)`. Meanwhile D_logz(c_triv-c_top)|q=2N rho, D_logz R_u|q=-2N H_u. (6) For the second equation, differentiate (4) and pair its last u factorial terms with indices `N-j`. Their sum reduces to `-2N sum_(j<=u)(1-Q^j)^(-1)`; the quadratic integer terms cancel. All derivatives are at fixed N and the actual root, at either parity. Consequently lim_(z->q) [h(z)-g(z)]/[c_triv(z)-c_top(z)]=v. (7) Applying (5) before the limit proves (3). This is a normalized divided difference of actual Clebsch channels, with the original cup kept. It does not use the fixed-q common-meridian splitting at a dual cap; that cap's exact dual-color product keeps its Casimir nodes collided. An analytic rescaling of h or g, equal to one at q, can add a multiple of g to v. The source-adapted vector in Section3 removes precisely that ambiguity. Thus the final Hermite frame does not depend on the unphysical first derivative of an eigenvector normalization. ## 3. Exact original co-sources and the canonical Hermite lift The finite sums in (1)--(2) give ell g=0, m g=1/N, gamma_N:=ell v=q x^(-d)/(N rho^2) =(-1)^N/(N rho^2), mu_N:=m v=-(sum_(u=0)^d H_u)/(N^2 rho). (8) In particular gamma_N is NONZERO at every level. To check its value, interchange the two finite sums: sum_(u=0)^d Q^(-u)H_u =sum_(j=1)^d [sum_(u=j)^d Q^(-u)]/(1-Q^j) =-1/(1-Q^(-1)). Also `q x^(-d)=(-1)^N`, by `x=q^d` and the actual half-period q. This accounts for the full parity sign. Define the SOURCE-ADAPTED generalized vector t_N=(v-mu_N p)/gamma_N. (9) Then all original source pairings are exactly m p=1, m t_N=0, ell p=0, ell t_N=1, (Omega-c_*)t_N=theta_N p, theta_N=1/(N gamma_N)=(-1)^N rho^2. (10) Thus the two original co-sources, not newly chosen dual rows, are the inverse frame on this actual Jordan channel. In particular `(Omega-c_*)|span(p,t_N)=theta_N p ell`, agreeing with the retained rank-one nilpotent source. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. The generalized direction and the marked co-source remain. The replacement `v->v+lambda g` changes `mu_N` by `lambda/N`, so the numerator in (9) is unchanged. This proves the normalization independence asserted after (7). ## 4. Fourier--Plancherel gives uniform physical conditioning For `1<=j<N`, |1-Q^j|>=4min(j,N-j)/N, |rho|>=4/N. Hence, with `Harm_N=1+log N`, max_u |H_u| <=(N/2)Harm_N, ||v||_2 <=(N^(5/2)/8)Harm_N, |mu_N| <=(N/8)Harm_N, |gamma_N|^(-1)=N|rho|^2<=4N. These estimates already give polynomial frame bounds without a spectral projector. A stronger exact Fourier calculation removes their condition growth. On degree d the original marked row is `m=p^*/N^3`, so (10) gives `p^*t_N=0`. If `Hbar=(1/N)sum_u H_u`, (9) becomes (t_N)_u=(-1)^(N+1)N rho g_u(H_u-Hbar). (11) Use the unnormalized cyclic Fourier transform `Hhat_k=sum_(u=0)^d H_u Q^(-ku)`. Pairing j with N-j gives `H_d=d/2`. The cyclic difference of H therefore has value `-d/2` at zero and `(1-Q^u)^(-1)` at `u=1,...,d`. Its Fourier transform is EXACTLY `-k`, for `1<=k<=d`: successive transforms differ by `sum_(j=1)^d Q^(-kj)=-1`, starting at zero for k=0. Consequently Hhat_k=-k/(1-Q^(-k)), 1<=k<=d, ||t_N||_2^2=N|rho|^2 sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2. (12) This is ordinary finite Plancherel on the FULL physical N-window; no Fourier channel is omitted or independently dephased. The elementary root identity is sum_(k=1)^d |1-Q^k|^(-2)=(N^2-1)/12. For a direct proof differentiate `P(z)=(z^N-1)/(z-1)` twice at one. The first reciprocal sum is d/2 and the sum of squared reciprocals is `d(5-N)/12`; their difference is the displayed absolute sum. Pairing k and N-k then gives N^2(N^2-1)/48 <=sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2 <=N^2(N^2-1)/24. Since `4/N<=|rho|<=2pi/N`, it follows that N^3/4<=||t_N||_2^2<=pi^2 N^3/6, p^*t_N=0, ||p||_2^2=N^3. (13) For the two physical columns `V=[p,t_N]` this proves sigma_min(V)>=N^(3/2)/2, sigma_max(V)<=pi N^(3/2)/sqrt(6), kappa(V)<=2, uniformly EVERY N>=2. (14) For the last bound use the known first column norm N^(3/2), not just the two extreme singular-value bounds: the other column's relative norm lies in `[1/2,pi/sqrt(6)]`, and `pi/sqrt(6)<2`. The condition number is therefore at most two; N=2 attains two. The exact inverse on its range is still the two original rows m,ell by (10). The ordinary row on the full physical degree-d space has a larger norm because it also sees other channel directions; its restriction here is precisely the coordinate dual of t_N. No inverse of a possibly ill-conditioned whole Casimir projector was used. ## 5. An actual positive Hermite Gram and crossing bound On `S_N=span(p,t_N)` define the positive inner product ||w||_(Herm)^2=|m w|^2+|ell w|^2. (15) It makes p,t_N orthonormal. It has rank two on S_N, not rank one, and retains BOTH the value and derivative channels. Both original co-sources have dual norm one. Equation (14) compares this Gram uniformly with N^(-3) times the physical metric. This is an explicit source-controlled Hermite Gram, not a metric defined from an unknown knot scalar or terminal word. Keep the original crossing's common Cartan scalar kappa. The independently derived Casimir polynomial has r(c_*)=1, r'(c_*)=-d/(2rho). Therefore in the p,t_N frame the EXACT original signed crossing is R_+=kappa [[1,tau_N],[0,1]], R_-=kappa^(-1) [[1,-tau_N],[0,1]], tau_N=(-1)^(N+1)d rho/2, |tau_N|<=pi. (16) Thus, for every signed integer l, ||R_+^l||_(Herm)<=1+pi|l| (17) at the original complete root, since `|kappa|=1`. The original full Cartan, pivot, framing and modified-dimension line have not been renormalized; (16) is a basis expression for that same operator. The PHYSICAL operator norm on this SAME invariant source channel is consequently at most `2(1+pi|l|)`, uniformly in N. The Gram (15) is asserted on the SELECTED TWO-DIMENSIONAL invariant channel only. Adjacent crossings may take it into other intermediate Casimir channels. Extending it through the full q-Racah transform, with the source, is the remaining problem. Declaring the rest of the physical tensor space orthogonal would not control that leakage, and no such full-channel estimate is claimed here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.py): literal original E/F Casimir and signed R, all original source rows, generic-q cup/descendant divided difference, parity and frame singular values at both odd and even levels.

title: Exact transport of quantum derivatives in a tensor contraction
status: Explicit rational source gauge and commuting finite-jet connection
text:
# Exact transport of quantum derivatives in a tensor contraction A quantum tensor contraction is a finite sum over representation indices. This note studies one summand before those indices are summed. Its indices satisfy affine conservation equations at vertices, cups and caps. After choosing independent coordinates for those equations, we ask what happens when one coordinate is shifted by the quantum period. The quantum parameter is allowed to vary near its root value. The period then moves, so a shift by the fixed integer \(N\) differs from a shift by the moving period. That difference produces derivatives in the independent index coordinates. The result is an explicit system of commuting differential operators on every fixed finite list of quantum derivatives. The term *finite jet* means this list of Taylor coefficients; *flat connection* means that the directional operators commute. All formulas concern the specified continuation of the original tensors, including cups, categorical duals, parity signs and the marked trace normalization. They do not turn the finite admissible sum into a periodic sum. Moving an integration or residue cycle would require its own boundary and divisor calculation, which is not supplied here. ## 1. The moving period and the original local factors Fix an integer \(N\ge3\), put \(d=N-1\), and write \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\zeta=q_0e^\epsilon\). Here \(\epsilon\) is the small generic-quantum-parameter displacement, not a half-twist sign. Choose the logarithm near \(q_0\) and define \[ P= rac{\pi i}{\operatorname{Log}\zeta},\qquad Q=\zeta^2, \qquad\eta=e^{2\pi iP},\qquad\Delta=N-P. 	ag{1} \] At \(\epsilon=0\), \(P=N\), \(\eta=1\), and \(\Delta=0\). The highest weights and polynomial degrees remain fixed integers as \(\epsilon\) varies. Only their specified coefficients and continued index arguments vary. At a white vertex, let \(W_a:V_{2a}	o V_d\otimes V_d\) be the actual generic intertwining tensor, with \(0\le a\le\lfloor d/2floor\). The variables \(i,j\) are its two ordered physical indices and \(r\) its channel index. Let \(F_m=(Q;Q)_m=\prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-Q^k)\), with \(F_0=1\). The fixed finite polynomial \(H_m^B(U,V)\) is the q-Hahn numerator specified in the [generic source formula](actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md). Its polynomial arguments, rather than a newly chosen interpolation of matrix values, define the continuation: \[  egin{aligned} W_a(i,j;r)&=(-1)^m\zeta^{-dr+di-m(m-1)}  rac{H_m^{Q^{-N}}(Q^i,Q^j)}{F_m},\ m&=d-a,\qquad i+j=m+r. \end{aligned} 	ag{2} \] The degree is the actual large-channel degree \(m=d-a\). Replacing it by its colliding small partner \(a\) would preserve some root values but change their generic derivatives. For integers \(p,q\), shifting the indices in their conservation equation gives \[ W_a(i+Pp,j+Pq;r+P(p+q))=(-1)^{dq}W_a(i,j;r). 	ag{3} \] Indeed \(Q^P=1\) leaves both polynomial arguments unchanged, and the remaining exponent changes by \(-dPq\). In particular, shifting \(i\) by \(P\) and \(j\) by \(-P\) at fixed total multiplies the tensor by \((-1)^d\). The asymmetric sign records the order of the two physical legs. The cup has a different multiplier because it contains factorials. Use the specified continuation \(\widehat F_P\) from the [moving-factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), which satisfies \[ \widehat F_P(z+P)=(1-e^{2\pi iz})\widehat F_P(z). \] For an actual fixed highest weight \(0\le L<N\), its ordered cup is \[ p_L(x,L-x)=e^{\pi ix}\zeta^{x(L-x-1)}  rac{\widehat F_P(x)\widehat F_P(L-x)}{F_L}. 	ag{4} \] The physical cup also has the head-independent scalar \(N\zeta^{-d^2}\), which remains in the tensor contraction. Set \(Y=e^{2\pi ix}\). Retaining both the quadratic monomial and \(e^{\pi ix}\) gives \[  egin{aligned} p_L(x+nP,L-x-nP)&=\mu_{L,n}(P,x)p_L(x,L-x),\ \mu_{L,n}(P,x)&=(-1)^{Ln} rac{1-Y}{\eta^{-n}-Y}, \qquad n\in\mathbb Z. \end{aligned} 	ag{5} \] For \(n=1\), the two factorials contribute \((1-Y)/(1-\eta^{-1}/Y)\); the monomials contribute \((-1)^{L-1}/Y\). Their product is (5). Repeated shifts telescope, and reversing the shift gives negative \(n\). These are meromorphic identities, interpreted after clearing denominators where necessary. The cap is the actual matrix inverse of the cup. Its ordered entry is therefore \[ \ell_L(x,L-x)= rac1{p_L(L-x,x)}. 	ag{6} \] Its multiplier is \(1/\mu_{L,-n}(P,L-x)\), not simply \(1/\mu_{L,n}(P,x)\). This reversal is needed for the cyclic and pivotal normalizations. The physical cup and cap scalars remain unchanged. The other elementary multipliers are explicit. The Chevalley monomial \(\zeta^{-(L+1)x}\) gains \((-1)^{(L+1)n}\), while the original pivotal clock \((-1)^L\zeta^{L-2x}\) gains one. An integer affine character \(e^{2\pi i\ell(\mathrm{heads})}\) gains \(\eta^{\ell(n)}\), where \(\ell(n)\) denotes its linear change under the integer shift. Categorical dual tensors are expanded into their original ordered white maps, cups, caps and reversal factors. Thus the same calculation applies without replacing a dual by a Hermitian adjoint or dividing by a vanishing root norm. Scalar channel weights, fixed generic normalizers and retained half-twist eigenvalues do not depend on these indices and do not change under their shifts. ## 2. Solving the index constraints before transporting Fix a typed tensor network and an admissible assignment of its finite channel labels. A *head* in the compiler means a basis index on a specified oriented end of an edge. Impose all its literal equations: for example, \[ i+j=m+r\quad	ext{at a white vertex},\qquad x+y=L\quad	ext{at a cup or cap}, \] together with equality of contracted indices. Write the resulting integer affine system as \(B\mathbf h=\mathbf b\). Choose one integer solution \(h_0\) and a matrix \(A\) whose columns form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\ker_{\mathbb Z}B\). Then \[ \mathbf h=h_0+Ax,\qquad x\in\mathbb C^k. 	ag{7} \] The columns span the whole integer kernel, not a proper sublattice. This kernel is saturated because \(\mathbb Z^n/\ker_{\mathbb Z}B\) is isomorphic to the free subgroup \(\operatorname{im}_{\mathbb Z}B\). They also span the complex kernel. An inconsistent channel assignment contributes no summands. The original finite inequalities are retained separately: writing (7) neither removes nor wraps them. Let \(S(\epsilon,x)\) be the meromorphic summand obtained from (2), (4) and (6), with all original ordering, characters and scalars. It agrees with the generic quantum summand at every admissible integer assignment. Exposed boundary indices are either fixed or included with their explicitly specified factors and constraints. No continuation is silently assigned to an arbitrary external state. Constant arguments need particular care. On the chosen affine chart, a tensor factor whose head argument is constant remains its original constant source factor. An admissible fixed integer cup is evaluated by finite factorials. A forbidden constant polar assignment is not defined by substituting into a ratio \(0/0\): retain its original zero summand, or invoke a separately proved generic cancellation. The construction makes no assertion about an undefined constant interpolation. For a direction \(b\in\mathbb Z^k\), the shift \(x\mapsto x+Pb\) changes every local head by an integer multiple of \(P\). Multiplying the local identities gives \[ S(\epsilon,x+Pb)=C_b(P,x)S(\epsilon,x). 	ag{8} \] The multiplier \(C_b\) is computed directly: multiply the white signs, cup ratios, reversed inverse-cap ratios, clocks and characters. If \(z_l(x)\) is an integer affine head argument, set \[ Y_l=e^{2\pi iz_l(x)}. \] Then \(C_b\) is rational in \(\eta\) and these \(Y_l\). Since \(N\) is an integer, it is \(N\)-periodic in every free coordinate. Away from the divisors \(Y_l=1\), its root value is the explicit sign character \[ C_b(N,x)=\chi(b)\in\{1,-1\}. 	ag{9} \] The character includes the ordered white-leg signs and the actual highest-weight parities. It is not reset to one when \(N\) changes parity. Any additional boundary character must be transported as well before enlarging the class of networks. This construction also applies term by term in a finite channel sum. For the usual matching network, the homogeneous head equations are the same for all channel assignments, the channel weights \(2a\) are even, and \(h_0\) is integral. A common multiplier for the sum further requires that the integer linear coefficients of every separately recorded head character be unchanged across assignments. With a common primitive basis and this condition, \(e^{2\pi ih_0}=1\) and all local parities agree, so the same \(C_b\) applies. Otherwise retain a finite vector of summands with diagonal transport. Even in the common-multiplier case, the support-dependent summation cycles remain separate. ### An explicit rational gauge The multiplier is not merely known to exist: the cup formula gives a particular function that produces it. Define \[ g(z)= rac{e^{2\pi iz}}{1-e^{2\pi iz}}. \] A direct calculation yields \(g(z+nP)/g(z)=(1-Y)/(\eta^{-n}-Y)\). Thus dividing a cup by \(g\) leaves the constant shift character \((-1)^{Ln}\). For every nonconstant cup argument put one factor \(g\) into \(G\); for every inverse-cap argument put its inverse. Include all separately retained integer exponential characters: \[ G(x)=\left(\prod_{	ext{cup/cap arguments }l}g(z_l(x))^{e_l}ight) e^{2\pi i\ell(h_0+Ax)},\qquad e_l\in\{1,-1\}. 	ag{9a} \] Only nonconstant arguments enter this product. A constant argument has shift number zero and multiplier one, so adding its \(g\)-factor would be unnecessary and could introduce an undefined pole at a fixed integer. In particular, simplify \(\mu_{L,0}=1\) before evaluating a constant argument. For a cap whose first matrix index is \(x\), the cup argument used here is \(L-x\), as required by (6). White maps, Chevalley factors and clocks need no further rational gauge. The specified \(G\) is rational in the marked head exponentials and independent of \(P\), and the exact multiplier is \[ C_b(P,x)=\chi(b) rac{G(x+Pb)}{G(x)}. 	ag{9b} \] Equivalently, \(S/G\) is quasiperiodic with period \(P\) and character \(\chi\). This is an identity of meromorphic functions, including the zeros and poles of \(G\). It does not authorize deleting \(G\) from a period integral. Nor is the gauge automatically negligible in an asymptotic estimate. For \(z=N(x+iy)\) with fixed \(y>0\), \( |g(z)|=e^{-2\pi Ny}(1+o(1))\). Hence \(G\) can change the leading exponential action and contribute residues. A change of variables in the transport formula must retain both effects. ## 3. From the moving shift to finitely many quantum derivatives Choose a head chart on which the actual source is regular in \(\epsilon\) after its proved generic cancellations. Its order-\(J\) jet is its Taylor polynomial modulo \(\epsilon^{J+1}\). If an intermediate expression has a known scalar pole of order \(M\), first multiply by \(\epsilon^M\); recovering the desired Laurent coefficients then needs the corresponding higher Taylor order. No principal part is discarded. For a direction \(b\), let \(D_b\) denote directional differentiation in \(x\), and let \(M_f\) denote multiplication by a function \(f\). Since \(x+Nb=(x+\Delta b)+Pb\), equation (8) gives \[  egin{aligned} S(\epsilon,x+Nb)&=T_bS(\epsilon,x),\ T_b&=e^{\Delta D_b}M_{C_b}. \end{aligned} 	ag{10} \] Composition acts from right to left, so the translation differentiates both \(C_b\) and the summand. Because \(\Delta=O(\epsilon)\), only finitely many translation terms can affect an order-\(J\) jet: \[ T_b^{(J)}= \sum_{r=0}^{J} rac{\Delta^r}{r!}D_b^rM_{C_b} \pmod{\epsilon^{J+1}}. 	ag{11} \] The required Taylor coefficients of \(C_b\) are rational in the \(Y_l\), with their divisors retained. This is a finite calculation for any specified derivative order. The operators commute on local meromorphic functions, not only when applied to the particular summand. Since \(G(x+Nb)=G(x)\), equations (9b) and (10) give \[ T_b=\chi(b)M_Ge^{\Delta D_b}M_{G^{-1}}. 	ag{11a} \] They are simultaneous conjugates of ordinary translations. This proves their group law. One can also check it directly from the multiplier relation \[ C_{b+c}(P,x)=C_b(P,x+Pc)C_c(P,x). 	ag{12} \] Its \(N\)-periodicity gives \(C_b(x-\Delta c)=C_b(x+Pc)\), and consequently \[  egin{aligned} T_bT_c &=e^{\Delta D_{b+c}}M_{C_b(x-\Delta c)C_c(x)}\ &=T_{b+c}=T_cT_b. \end{aligned} 	ag{13} \] The same equality survives finite-jet truncation. Remove only the recorded root sign, setting \(U_b=\chi(b)^{-1}T_b^{(J)}\). Then \(\Delta\in(\epsilon)\) and \(C_b/\chi(b)=1 mod\epsilon\), so \[ (U_b-I)	ext{ raises the power of }\epsilon,\qquad \prod_{r=1}^{J+1}(U_{b_r}-I)=0. 	ag{14} \] Thus the normalized transport is unipotent on finite jets. Its inverse is a finite geometric series, or simply \(U_{-b}\). This is a local statement over a meromorphic coefficient field; it is not a norm bound near the poles or a nilpotence statement about the final sum. The commuting logarithmic derivatives are explicit: \[  egin{aligned} U_b&=e^{\Delta
abla_b}\pmod{\epsilon^{J+1}},\ 
abla_b&=D_b-D_b\operatorname{Log}G =M_GD_bM_{G^{-1}}. \end{aligned} 	ag{14a} \] Here \(D_b\operatorname{Log}G\) acts by multiplication. Its logarithmic poles occur on the recorded integral-head divisors. This is the flat finite-jet connection referred to in the title. ### The first derivative as a concrete example Write \(S=S_0+\epsilon S_1+O(\epsilon^2)\) and \(C_b=\chi(b)(1+\epsilon c_{b1}+O(\epsilon^2))\). Since \(P'(0)=iN^2/\pi\), equation (10) becomes \[  egin{aligned} S_0(x+Nb)&=\chi(b)S_0(x),\ S_1(x+Nb)&=\chi(b) igl(S_1-P'(0)D_bS_0+c_{b1}S_0 igr). \end{aligned} 	ag{15} \] The root value is quasiperiodic, but its first quantum derivative also contains the derivative caused by the moving period and the derivative of the multiplier. For a cup argument \(z_l\) shifted by \(n_lP\), the latter contribution is \[  rac{2\pi iP'(0)n_l}{1-e^{2\pi iz_l}}. 	ag{16} \] An inverse cup uses its literal reversed argument and the negative contribution. A character \(\eta^k\) contributes \(2\pi iP'(0)k\); white and clock signs have zero derivative. These poles are genuine normal terms, not an error that can be removed by setting \(\eta=1\) too early. ## 4. The three-coordinate exceptional kernel The [specified generic exceptional operator](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) provides a concrete network with free coordinates \((t,u,v)\). Retain its channel \(a\) and define \[  egin{gathered} r=a-v+u,\qquad \ell=t-v,\qquad s=d-2a,\ Y_r=e^{2\pi ir},\qquad Y_v=e^{2\pi iv},\qquad Y_\ell=e^{2\pi i\ell},\ A(Y)= rac{1-Y}{\eta^{-1}-Y},\qquad B(Y)= rac{1-Y}{\eta-Y}. \end{gathered} \] Here the local functions \(A(Y),B(Y)\) are unrelated to the integer constraint matrices of Section 2. Applying (3)–(6) to the two actual large white tensors, Chevalley scalar and three ordered cups gives \[ C_u=(-1)^sA(Y_r),\qquad C_v=(-1)^s rac{B(Y_r)}{A(Y_v)B(Y_\ell)},\qquad C_t= rac1{A(Y_\ell)}. 	ag{17} \] These multipliers apply to the full generic polynomial kernel and its completed version, because the moving face scalar is independent of \(t,u,v\). The retained character \(e^{-2\pi iv}\) is one under a fixed integer \(N\)-shift but not under a moving \(P\)-shift. Erasing it before forming (17) would lose part of the derivative. The rational gauge is short in these coordinates: \[ G_K= rac{g(r)}{g(v)g(\ell)} =e^{2\pi i(u-v-t)}  rac{(1-Y_v)(1-Y_\ell)}{1-Y_r}. 	ag{17a} \] Substitution into (9b) recovers all three multipliers, with \(\chi_u=\chi_v=(-1)^s\) and \(\chi_t=1\). This checks the abstract-looking construction on the actual kernel, retaining its integer exponential and its channel-row pole. It does not replace the kernel by its phase-cancelled root value before differentiation. ## 5. Closing the source with its original normalization For the marked invariant, use the same exposed physical index and its actual generic ordinary pivotal closure. Let \(F(\epsilon)\) be that finite closed source. With the symmetric quantum integer \([N]_\zeta=(\zeta^N-\zeta^{-N})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\), its normalization is \[  egin{aligned} D_N(\epsilon)&=(-1)^d[N]_{q_0e^\epsilon},\ 
u_N=D_N'(0)&= rac{2N(-1)^N}{q_0-q_0^{-1}},\ Z&= rac{F'(0)}{
u_N}. \end{aligned} 	ag{18} \] The transport applies to the continued ordinary summand and its first jet before this normalization. It does not create a generic continuation of a bare dense root mark. If an off-root marked row is prescribed, that row must be transported covariantly with its original cup. Otherwise the available statement is the ordinary closure and (18). Likewise, a regular Hopf lift of a complete-circle coupon and the literal moving-quantum-parameter exceptional polynomial are different generic germs. The proof uses whichever germ has actually been specified. Agreement at the root is not enough to identify their derivatives. At the physical integer lattice, \(Y_l=1\). Individual rational transport factors can therefore have poles even when the complete source has a removable cancellation. Equations (8) and (10) hold meromorphically and can be cleared of denominators before specialization. They do not authorize applying a singular factor to a root value without its full germ, or discarding a residue. Finally, shifting a summand does not preserve its finite admissibility polytope. A residue representation has its own cotangent factors and boundary. A global period identity would have to carry that cycle, its crossed divisors and every affine marking character. No such cycle deformation or selected contribution is proved in this note. ## 6. Finite checks and their scope The [calculation script](../experiments/audit_actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection_results.json) check the rational gauge, the three exceptional-kernel multipliers, their composition laws, the first-derivative connections and a shared integral head chart. Direct evaluations of the original large white polynomial, moving-factorial cups and full generic completed kernel check 24, 6 and 6 moving-period shifts, respectively. Three fixed-\(N\) transports include first and second normals; the largest recorded relative identity error at 85 digits was below \(1.2	imes10^{-82}\). Those finite checks test the formulas and their implementation. The arbitrary-network assertion follows from multiplying the local identities and the operator proof above. Neither the numerical checks nor the local connection claim a transported global period or a volume equality.

title: The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle
status: Adjoint connection on the original cotangent period
text: # The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle 30 October 2026. The exact tensor-source transport has a corresponding identity for the original cotangent period. Its adjoint acts on the cotangent density as well as on the explicit source gauge. The resulting double-pole and finite-part terms are retained. This does not make the finite head sum periodic or move its cycle to the geometric critical point. ## 1. The actual period and the specified source connection Use the [actual tensor-source connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). After the original integral affine head equations, write the primitive free lattice as h=h0+A x, x in C^k. Constant head factors remain their original source constants. Fix the finite channel labels, or retain the finite vector of label sectors when their characters differ. Every outside tensor, turn and peripheral character is part of the specified meromorphic source S(epsilon,x). At the original marked arc use its ordinary generic pivotal closure and subsequent exposed-trace normal, or an explicitly chosen covariant generic marked row. No generic continuation of the bare root mark is supplied by this theorem. Initially assume S is root-regular in epsilon on a common neighborhood of the cycle, after retaining its actual meromorphic cancellations. If a chosen representation has a finite Laurent pole of order M, apply the statements to epsilon^M S through order J+M to recover the original Laurent jet through order J. One must not use only J translation terms before multiplying a source with such a pole. Put P=pi i/Log(q0 exp(epsilon)), Delta=N-P, and P'=iN^2/pi. For b in Z^k, let D_b=sum b_j partial_(x_j). The source theorem proves S(epsilon,x+Nb)=chi(b) G(x) exp(Delta D_b)[G(x)^-1 S], (1) where chi(b) is the actual parity character and G is the explicit P-independent rational cup/character gauge. Its construction omits constant head factors; in particular it never inserts g(integer) for an identically constant cup argument. Formula (1) is meromorphic and its exponential is a FINITE differential operator modulo any fixed epsilon^(J+1). The original lattice density and normalized period are W(x)=product_(j=1)^k pi cot(pi x_j), I_Gamma[S]=(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma W(x) S(x) dx, (2) with dx=dx1 wedge ... wedge dxk. Gamma is the original sum of compact local tori, or a specified closed cycle on the same source chart. It avoids the divisors of S, W, G and G^-1 on its surface on a common epsilon germ, or the genuinely canceled meromorphic integrands are used throughout. Its interior may contain the original cotangent and source poles. The [source-null extension theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md) allows its explicitly proved zero ordered tori to be included as well. Other polar strata are not implicitly added or removed. ## 2. Exact adjoint transport of every finite quantum jet For every fixed J, on the original CLOSED cycle one has I_Gamma[S(epsilon,x+Nb)] =chi(b)(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma G^-1 exp(-Delta D_b)(W G) S dx mod epsilon^(J+1). (3) All derivatives in (3) act on the actual top-form density W G. This is not a replacement of the original period by a period of S/G. The final meromorphic integrand is used with every cancellation and divisor retained, rather than evaluated factor by factor at G=0 or G=infinity. Proof: for meromorphic f,g with no pole on the cycle, integral_Gamma f D_b g dx=-integral_Gamma (D_b f) g dx. Indeed D_b(fg) dx=d(fg contraction_b(dx)), whose integral on a closed cycle is zero. This argument needs no pole-free interior. Apply it r times to the r-th term of (1), with f=W G and g=G^-1 S. Since Delta is independent of x and belongs to (epsilon), only r<=J occurs for the root-regular source specified in section 1. For a Laurent source use the cleared source and the enlarged order stated there.
