The inserted matrix unit replaces the identity on that one edge; no extra color, trace, state, cap or pivot has been introduced. The same definition works in any cup/cap/plat diagram: replace that literal wire identity by E_bd and contract all other original tensors. It is independent of how the finite contraction is parenthesized. Since sum_b E_bb=I, re-closing just this identity edge gives C_(c,a)=sum_b T_(a,b)^(c,b). (2.2) If the original diagram happens to put a diagonal transport on this edge, it is retained on its original side in (2.1), or its known entries are included in T. An independently added g_b would change (2.2). In particular cutting an ordinary internal identity edge does NOT authorize a second pivotal trace. Set J_(a,b)=T_(a,b)^(a,b). (2.3) Actual total-index conservation makes the reclosed C diagonal termwise for the original kernel and all scalar Green moments. The original cut coupon has diagonal entries 1/N, hence original reduced period=(1/N)sum_(a,b) J_(a,b). (2.4) This is 1/N, not 1/N^2. Every original pivot, zero-framing line, meridian lift character, base compact factor and external d_N(M) remains where it was in (2.1); multiplying (2.4) by the retained external line gives the original full state. Equivalently the exact weighted family is F(x,y)=(1/N)Tr_cut[ x^J P(A y^(J_t) B)]. (2.5) Its coefficient of x^a y^b is J_(a,b)/N. Thus the two-position array is realized by two physical wire couplings before any formal completion. It is not only an arbitrary array relabeled as a matrix. ## 3. Actual Hopf transport through the cut coupon In a genuine integral q-family use the ordinary cap P_o. At the original root use the original pivotal cap with its retained scalar adapter. For any actual h, pivotal Hopf naturality gives the exact insertion identity D_h P_o(A X B)=P_o[A D_h,tot(X) B], (3.1) where X is ANY inserted operator at the chosen intermediate level, and D_h=ad_h-epsilon(h). The words A,B intertwine the respective actual coproduct representations; their boundary object orders are not silently identified. For a plat, the same proof uses its actual intertwiners and duality maps before and after the chosen wire. Thus (3.1) is valid with all actual cups/caps present. For X=E_bd^(t), (3.1) is a specified current map from the physical second cut to the original cut. It contains the TRUE total adjoint, including its mixed terms; the local coupon is not presumed to be a tensor-product submodule. For example, in a parallel ordered tensor object E_tot=sum_i E_i K_(i+1)...K_l, F_tot=sum_i K_1^(-1)...K_(i-1)^(-1) F_i. For a local coupon X in slot t, put k_X X=K_t X K_t^(-1) when X is a weight matrix unit. Then D_E,tot(X)=[E_tot,X] K_tot^(-1), D_F,tot(X)=F_tot X-k_X^(-1) X F_tot. (3.2) The E commutator has its local term [E_t,X]K_(t+1)...K_l and, for EVERY i<t, the term E_i K_(i+1)...K_(t-1) [K_t,X] K_(t+1)...K_l. The F expression has its local term K_1^(-1)...K_(t-1)^(-1)(F_tX-k_X^(-1)XF_t), and the prefix terms (1-k_X^(-1))X K_1^(-1)...K_(i-1)^(-1)F_i for i<t. Terms i>t cancel exactly. These are the actual induced off-diagonal/prefix rows; omitting them amounts to replacing the true coproduct by a different one. In a dual tensor slot use its actual contragredient matrices, with the same ordered formula. If the weighted word or scalar Green insertions occur, (3.1) has the explicit additional local crossing/weight currents from [the whole Ward construction](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md). For the frozen off-root ADO cap add its recorded defect R_h=chi^(-1)ptr_K[M_(Z^J),ad_h]. (3.3) Thus this construction does not assume auxiliary truncated generic-q/M matrices are genuine Hopf intertwiners. It applies directly on the original root family or on the genuine integral q-family, and keeps the actual defect rows on another lift. ## 4. The off-diagonal port bands and the original source Retain the complete bands J^(p,q)_(a,b)=T_(a,b)^(a+p,b+q), (4.1) zero outside all four actual port ranges. This is a lossless finite encoding of T. In a parallel oriented charge convention the original scalar tensor has p+q=0. A contragredient cut uses its recorded sign or index reversal, not a new conservation law. The source on these bands is essential. With the original cut row e_0, (2.2) gives on EVERY current tensor Phi^(2)(T)=sum_(a,b,p) (e_0)_(a,a+p) J^(p,0)_(a,b). (4.2) In the original balanced source e_0 has every entry 1/N. Thus a homogeneous current of cut degree d uses its p=d band with the same factor 1/N. Only a charge-zero scalar kernel reduces to (2.4). Applying the J^(0,0) source to all Hopf currents would delete precisely the original off-diagonal cut co-sources. For illustration the first output/input port actions are exactly (L_A T)^(p,q)_(a,b) =sum_r A_(a+p,a+r) J^(r,q)_(a,b), (R_B T)^(p,q)_(a,b) =sum_s B_(a+s,a) J^(p-s,q)_(a+s,b). (4.3) The second-port formulas interchange a,p with b,q. Substituting the actual E,F,K, antipodes or dual matrices gives every shifted band and its endpoint coefficient. The [independent band-current audit](two_cut_port_band_current_audit.md) records these rows explicitly. All divided rows are obtained with the full actual coproduct, not by raising a projected scalar row. The grouped array matrix has ROW=a and COLUMN=b. It is not the ordinary matrix of a one-cut tangle. Even the actual two-cut unknot has T_(a,b)^(c,d)=delta_(c,b)delta_(d,a), so J=I. Then the double diagonal of (E tensor I)T is zero, whereas EJ=E is nonzero. Thus a single physical Hopf port action does NOT descend to ordinary left multiplication on J. Actual boundary reordering may also require braidings or dualities. Those matrices, and their transported coproduct order, must be kept rather than assigning the grouped T a naive Delta action. There is nevertheless an explicit scalar-coordinate lift. For matrix units define the balanced port channel L_ij(T)=(E_ij tensor I)T(E_ji tensor I). Its double diagonal is E_ij J. On the second port the channel (I tensor E_ji)T(I tensor E_ij) has double diagonal J E_ij. These formulas produce exact row and column position shifts and clocks. Their matrix-algebra unit on the full tensor space is a diagonal projection, not its identity. A physical crossing can leave that projection and return through an exchange band, so these channels are NOT a product-preserving replacement of the whole R network. The [two-coordinate Green/coherent construction](two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.md) supplies the full left/right Toeplitz shifts with both row/column tails and their corner. Apply its relative endpoint construction bandwise to the actual allowed windows in (4.1). No tail created by a Green translation is folded back into a physical port. ## 5. A canonical nonzero local Gaussian map for bounded bands This physical opening supplies more than scalar coordinate names. Remove both cut edges. The remaining internal graph is connected. Prescribing port shifts p,q with the balanced total charge gives an integer boundary-divergence vector of total zero. The incidence matrix of the chosen spanning tree solves it integrally: the flow on an oriented tree edge is the signed sum of divergences in its child subtree. All internal chord flows remain free. Consequently each fixed band has actual coefficients I^(p,q)(a,b,j), j in Z^(m-1), on an affine integral flow coset, with the same free chords as I^(0,0). Relative to the latter parametrization, every local edge position and crossing transfer changes by an integer constant, bounded in terms of the diagram and |p|+|q|. Actual proper factorial/Cartan ratios therefore give, on the strict interior, I^(p,q)=R_(p,q)(q,M,clocks) I^(0,0). (5.1) This is an identity derived from the original coefficients. R_(p,q) is a finite product of the recorded rational shift ratios and meridian/lift monomials. Every common base-only Cartan, compact-factor and peripheral line remains common; it is not reset to a numerical ideal value. On the regular geometric chart, the variable shape arguments avoid 0 and 1, so for FIXED bounded port shifts its leading coefficient is a unit. The strict-support cone remains nonempty for all large N after such a fixed shift. Equation (5.1) is an INTERIOR identity; its finite zero-extension endpoint rows remain their separate relative data. Because (a,b) is etale on the critical torsor, the remaining m-1 Hessian is nondegenerate. Let G_(a,b) be the original transverse Gaussian and define Z^(p,q)=G_(a,b)[R_(p,q) I^(0,0)]. (5.2) This has the same marked action/base line as Z^(0,0), and its leading amplitude is R_(p,q)|_crit times the nonzero amplitude of Z^(0,0). In particular it is nonzero on the stated chart. The construction is independent of the integral particular-flow choice. Two choices differ by a cycle supported entirely in the internal graph, hence by an integer translation of the transverse chords. The exact formal Gaussian translation identity, with its correspondingly shifted insertion and critical point, identifies the two formulas when these choices are fixed independently of N (or differ by uniformly bounded shifts). Adding an N-dependent full cycle is a finite logarithmic-deck move and also requires transport of its separate flattening/period mark. A different fixed unimodular chord basis changes only the actual recorded orientation/half-density frame. This is a canonical LOCAL band-kernel after those original marks are fixed. Every bounded ordinary port Ward row in Sections 3--4 is a finite linear combination of shifts and insertions in these same actual affine arrays. Formula (5.2), with the exact opposite shift on its insertion, is consequently a linear COCHAIN pushforward of their INTERIOR current identities. The exact finite support and framing endpoints stay in the explicitly recorded relative summand; this assertion does not evaluate their geometric images. This is the translation-covariant Wick formula of [the residual-current theorem](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md), now with BOTH external coordinates represented by physical cuts. The principal B1 fields project independently to (a,b) by (1.1). Their scalar position directions therefore have the left/right array realization above; their complete Hopf rows retain the off-diagonal and prefix data of (3.2)--(4.3). This is not an identification of a finite fixed-N matrix algebra with a scalar function algebra. It is a linear map on an actual local coefficient/current completion. It also makes no claim for port shifts growing like N, for summing all such bands, or for the behavior at the two external finite-window boundaries. ## 6. The nearest actual bands measure the physical wave momentum Their principal ratio can be computed without guessing an extra source. Use the ACTUAL balanced/factorial boundary frame. The crossing generating functions satisfy dS_vertex=sum_out Log(p_new) du -sum_in Log(p_new) du. (6.1) This follows from the exact generating relations already derived from the actual crossing ratios in [the marked holonomy calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md), with the canonical boundary form in [the determinant-line proof](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md). The actual diagonal factorial frame change adds its output-minus- input boundary primitive; accordingly its momentum is p_new=(1-A)p_old. Using p_old in (6.1) while keeping the new constant source would change the band marks. Sum (6.1) over the open network at its original geometric critical point. All internal edge terms cancel by momentum continuity. The only boundary terms are Log p_(0,out) du_(0,out)+Log p_(e,out) du_(e,out) -Log p_(0,in) du_(0,in)-Log p_(e,in) du_(e,in). (6.2) The original cut has p_(0,in)=p_(0,out)=1. At the second identity edge p_(e,in)=p_(e,out)=p_e. The original closed pivotal phases can add 2pi i integer multiples to the logarithmic momenta. Their exponentiated multipliers are one; their finite coefficients and flattening/period marks remain retained in the exact ratios. In the band J^(p,q), the inputs a,b are held fixed and the outputs are a+p,b+q. Hence the first action change is (S_(p,q)-S_0)/H=p Log p_(0,out)+q Log p_(e,out)+O(H). The integral tree particular flow makes no additional term: its internal contributions cancel in (6.2). The shifted regular amplitude tends to the original amplitude. Thus the ratio in (5.1) has the EXACT marked principal symbol R_(p,q),0=p_cut^p p_e^q. For the nearest charge-zero exchange bands this gives R_(+1,-1),0=p_e^(-1), R_(-1,+1),0=p_e. (6.3) These are the ACTUAL local edge wave momenta in the physical Gauss matrix. If a developed Wirtinger meridian is written in a common global frame, its prefix conjugation must be retained: that matrix is not silently identified with the local Gauss matrix solely because both are meridians. There is a useful precise parity consequence on a physical two-parabolic chart. Suppose the matrices in the same ACTUAL physical cut frame are as follows, with Tr(g_cut g_e) a FIXED representation invariant on that framing chart: g_cut=[[1+s,-s],[s,1-s]], g_e=[[k,(1-k)p_e],[(k-1)/p_e,2-k]]. Put z=s(k-1), c=Tr(g_cut g_e)-2 and c=z(2-p_e-p_e^(-1)), D=-z(p_e-p_e^(-1)). The two branches at fixed position clocks exchange p_e and its inverse. On the regular chart z!=0,p_e!=0, (6.3) therefore proves R_(+1,-1),0-R_(-1,+1),0=D/z. (6.4) The principal ODD orientation section is realized by two actual nearby port bands. It was not imposed by a field trace or by a postulated Weyl action. If the two-position density is Omega_cut=dlog A wedge dlog B/(B D), its product with this actual odd-band symbol is the nonzero DECK-EVEN density dlog A wedge dlog B/(B z). (6.5) Equations (6.4)--(6.5) require the displayed physical Gauss chart (including any prefix adapter); they are not a replacement of that dictionary for an arbitrary pair of developed word matrices. ## 7. The remaining orientation and global-source datum An etale two-position chart need not have degree one. On a two-sheeted framing chart its leading density can be odd under the deck involution. The local choice of geometric critical point and marked square-root/orientation in (5.2) then selects a local sheet; ordinary field trace of that odd density would be zero. The literal source (4.2) and full relative finite-window tails do not authorize replacing a selected cycle by that field trace. Section 6 now computes an actual local odd-band observable that distinguishes those sheets, when the physical chart is fixed. However the original second-edge closing operation is the q=0 identity-cap source (4.2). It has not been proved that its global relative current/cycle selects the odd combination in (6.4). Substituting that inserted observable for the uninserted scalar state would be a different problem. The construction supplies a specified physical current/source problem, a nonzero local band map and two independent position directions. It does not yet determine the global marked cycle or prove that its geometric coefficient survives the final contraction. Exact actual tensor audits: [script](../experiments/audit_actual_two_cut_ports.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_two_cut_ports_results.json).

title: Polynomial-cost inversion of the actual two-head Ward current
text: # Polynomial-cost inversion of the actual two-head Ward current 28 October 2026. The actual two-head lowering current admits a uniformly polynomial inverse on the orthogonal complement of its exact kernel, at EVERY total integer degree. This is a statement in the original Euclidean head metric, uniformly on compact meridian annuli. It does not use the potentially exponentially conditioned fusion matrix to estimate an inverse. In particular, a local current equation cannot introduce an extra exponential loss merely through its inversion. Kernel and cokernel charges remain explicit. Neither this fact nor nilpotence of the current proves that the whole knot's selected geometric contribution is nonzero. ## 1. The actual current and the bound Fix N>=2, Q=exp(2pi i/N), d=N-1, and x!=0. In the balanced physical basis the current is F |a,b> = (1-Q^(a+1)) |a+1,b> + x^-1 Q^a (1-Q^(b+1)) |a,b+1>, (1) where arrows outside 0,...,d vanish. This is the actual coproduct current F_1+K_1^-1 F_2 in the fusion conventions of [the original kernel](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md). Let H_s be the span of a+b=s, and F_s:H_s -> H_(s+1). For every nonzero F_s, all its nonzero singular values obey sigma >= min(1,|x|^-1) 2 sin(pi/N)/N. (2) Consequently its Moore--Penrose inverse satisfies ||F_s^+|| <= max(1,|x|) N/[2 sin(pi/N)] <= max(1,|x|) N^2/4. (3) Here the last inequality is sin(pi/N)>=2/N. F_(2d)=0 has zero pseudoinverse; its kernel is retained, not inverted. In particular this is uniform on every fixed compact meridian annulus. ## 2. Unitary reduction to a weighted path The only nonzero entries of F_s are on two adjacent diagonals. Their bipartite support graph is a path. Independent unitary phases on its row and column vertices therefore make all entries real, with opposite signs on the two diagonals: choose one vertex phase and propagate along the path. There is no loop consistency condition, and these changes of frame have norm and inverse norm exactly one. For 0<=s<=N-2, F_s^* is unitarily equivalent to A_L with L=s+1. For N-1<=s<=2N-3, F_s is unitarily equivalent to A_L with L=2N-2-s. In both cases 1<=L<=N-1, and (A_L f)_i = a_i f_i-b_i f_(i+1), 0<=i<L, a_i=2sin(pi(L-i)/N), b_i=2sin(pi(i+1)/N) (4) when |x|=1. For general x, multiply a_i by |x|^-1 in the lower-degree case, and b_i by |x|^-1 in the upper-degree case. At |x|=1, for the lower degrees the coefficient on row a=i is |1-Q^(s-i+1)|=a_i, and on row a=i+1 it is b_i. For the upper degrees put a=s-d+i. The output degree starts at a=s-d+1, so each row has the two coefficients |1-Q^(s-d+i+1)|=2sin(pi(L-i)/N), |1-Q^(d-i)|=2sin(pi(i+1)/N), as claimed. In particular every coefficient in (4) is at least a_min=min(1,|x|^-1) 2sin(pi/N). (5) The adjoint reduction in the lower degrees preserves nonzero singular values; it is not a replacement of the original current by another quantum operator. ## 3. A unimodal exact kernel supplies a spectral estimate The row rank of A_L is L, and its kernel is spanned by the positive vector eta defined by eta_0=1 and eta_(i+1)/eta_i=a_i/b_i. Equivalently, eta_i= r^i |(Q;Q)_L/[(Q;Q)_i (Q;Q)_(L-i)]|, (6) where r=|x|^-1 for the lower-degree case and r=|x| for the upper-degree case. The ratios are nonincreasing in i. One direct verification extends the ratio to real i and differentiates its logarithm: d/di log[sin(pi(L-i)/N)/sin(pi(i+1)/N)] = -(pi/N) sin(pi(L+1)/N) /[sin(pi(L-i)/N)sin(pi(i+1)/N)] <= 0. (7) Thus eta, and hence the probability weights p_i=eta_i^2 / sum_j eta_j^2, are unimodal. They may have very different magnitudes; no lower bound on every p_i is assumed. The constant ratio factor r does not change (7). When L=N-1 the ratios are constant; the kernel is uniform when |x|=1. Set w_i=a_i^2 p_i=b_i^2 p_(i+1), P_i=sum_(j<=i) p_j. Unimodality gives min(P_i,1-P_i) <= (L+1) max(p_i,p_(i+1)). (8) Indeed before a mode the prefix is at most (i+1)p_i; at or after a mode the suffix is at most (L-i)p_(i+1). Together with (5), this implies w_i >= [a_min^2/(L+1)] min(P_i,1-P_i). (9) For a complex-valued function g on the path, the exact variance identity and Cauchy--Schwarz along each interval give Var_p(g)=sum_(i<j) p_i p_j |g_i-g_j|^2 <= L sum_(r=0)^(L-1) P_r(1-P_r)|g_(r+1)-g_r|^2 <= [L(L+1)/a_min^2] sum_r w_r |g_(r+1)-g_r|^2. (10) For f_i=sqrt(p_i)g_i, orthogonality to ker A_L is exactly sum_i p_i g_i=0, while ||f||^2=Var_p(g), ||A_L f||^2=sum_r w_r |g_(r+1)-g_r|^2. Equation (10) proves the stronger estimate sigma_min(A_L)>=a_min/sqrt(L(L+1))>=a_min/N. (11) This proves (2)--(3) in every degree without an asymptotic limit. ## 4. The exact retained charges and use in transport Let h_s=F_s^+. Orthogonal projections P_s onto ker F_s and Q_(s+1) onto ker F_s^* satisfy the exact equations h_s F_s=I-P_s, F_s h_s=I-Q_(s+1). (12) All projectors are explicit: pull the normalized rank-one vector (6) through the unitary path gauges. For s<N-1 the kernel of F_s is zero and its cokernel has rank one. For N-1<=s<2d the kernel has rank one and its cokernel is zero. At s=2d the whole one-dimensional source is kernel. At the invariant dual-pair degree s=d, L=d and eta_i=|x|^i. Putting back the actual phases gives the normalized invariant cup with coefficients proportional to x^a. Thus the original cup charge survives this contraction exactly; it is not a zero-current term to be removed. The full K=1 constraint singles out this degree's charge as in [the original Ward corner reduction](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md). For a compatible physical equation F_s v=j, (12) produces the unique minimum-norm solution v=h_s j, with ||v|| <= max(1,|x|)(N^2/4)||j||. (13) For an incompatible j the exact retained obstruction is Q_(s+1)j. Similarly a row annihilating ker F_s factors through F_s with a coefficient row of norm at most max(1,|x|)(N^2/4) times its own norm. Thus, for a fixed finite sequence of such compatible local solves, the inversion cost alone is polynomial in N. The currents or retained charges themselves can still be exponentially large. This is complementary to the cyclic-character contraction used for the sewn wall currents. Here the metric and operator are those of the literal nilpotent physical heads, not a cyclic replacement. It gives a genuine local flow estimate for the proposed torsor transport. It does not assert that arbitrary interbridge kernels obey each separate pair's Ward equation, nor that a simultaneous many-head reduction has the same estimate. Those compatibilities must be established before iterating (13) across a knot diagram. ## 5. A holomorphic contraction on the actual scaled meridian tube The Moore--Penrose inverse used in (12) depends on a Hermitian metric. Pointwise bounds on a fixed annulus do not by themselves give a holomorphic torsor map there. On the meridian scale used by the quantum jets, however, an algebraic contraction has the same polynomial cost. Fix |x_0|=1, write x=z x_0, and on H_s put D_s(z)|a,s-a>=z^a |a,s-a>. The literal coefficients in (1) give F_s(z x_0)=z^-1 D_(s+1)(z) F_s(x_0) D_s(z)^-1. (14) Define the holomorphic matrix and projections h_s^hol(z)=z D_s(z) h_s(x_0) D_(s+1)(z)^-1, P_s^hol(z)=D_s(z) P_s(x_0) D_s(z)^-1, Q_(s+1)^hol(z)=D_(s+1)(z) Q_(s+1)(x_0) D_(s+1)(z)^-1. Equations (12) hold EXACTLY with these matrices and F_s(z x_0). All entries are Laurent polynomials in z with fixed coefficients. When x_0 is algebraic, the coefficients are algebraic: the appropriate full-rank Gram inverse computes h_s(x_0) over the field generated by Q,x_0 and their complex conjugates. For z=exp(u/N) and |Re u|<=C, every diagonal D and its inverse has norm at most exp(C). Consequently ||h_s^hol(exp(u/N))|| <= exp(2C+C/N) N^2/4, (15) ||P_s^hol||, ||Q_(s+1)^hol|| <= exp(2C). Every fixed-order u derivative has the same polynomial bound with an additional constant depending only on its order and C. To see this directly, differentiation acts on h by a scalar 1/N and left/right multiplication by diag(a/N), of norms at most one. The rth derivative therefore costs at most (2+1/N)^r. This is a genuine holomorphic, source-compatible local contraction on the entire marked quantum meridian tube. It avoids inferring analytic transport from a nonholomorphic inverse. On a fixed-width annulus, (14) can instead have exponentially large diagonal norms; no bound like (15) for that particular holomorphic contraction is asserted there. Likewise a many-head compatibility problem cannot be solved by applying (14) to pairs whose separate Ward equations are not satisfied. ## 6. Verification [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_two_head_ward_contraction.py) compares the singular spectra of the literal complex current and the weighted-path reduction, checks the bound on every degree at small levels, and tests the kernel, projector and compatible-solve identities. Larger levels test the balanced and unbalanced path regimes. These are diagnostics of the formulas; (4)--(11) are the uniform proof.

title: The selected endpoint source is a marked two-pole cycle
text: # The selected endpoint source is a marked two-pole cycle 27 October 2026. The exact all-strand coefficient source has an ordinary one-variable contour representative, with two nearby marked pole cycles. Neither pole is an invariant by itself: a characteristic-zero actual figure-eight braid calculation changes BOTH endpoint values under braid conjugacy while leaving their difference unchanged. The coalescing-root limit also has a precise cyclotomic boundary layer. Replacing it by one ordinary double-pole contour loses even the constant source. This gives a concrete contour input for gate C. It does not prove a nonzero geometric thimble intersection. The final section records the derived source-symbol test that a whole geometric comparison would need. ## 1. Exact contour of the original all-strand source Use the canonical degree-<N endpoint polynomials from [the original all-strand theorem](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md), and combine all tail heads BEFORE attempting a source limit: T_N(Z)=sum_lambda Q^-j B_lambda(Z), S_N=T_N(1)-T_N(Q^-1), Q=exp(2pi*i/N). No unknown invariant is divided out in forming T_N. Its coefficients are determined by the actual complete word, its actual fusion/Euler frames and every off-diagonal tail transition. The original full peripheral and framing line is retained in that theorem; in modulus the reduced original invariant satisfies |Kashaev_N(K)|=N|S_N|/|1-Q|. (1) Define the source differential omega_N(T)=T(z) dz/[z^N(1-z)(1-Qz)]. (2) Its residue at zero is the original rational-kernel coefficient functional. Since degree T<N, its order at infinity is at most -3, so there is no residue at infinity. Its two other residues are Res_(z=1) omega_N=-T(1)/(1-Q), Res_(z=Q^-1) omega_N=T(Q^-1)/(1-Q). (3) Here both centers have z^N=1. Thus the global residue theorem gives the EXACT all-level source identity Res_(z=0) omega_N =[z^(N-1)] T(z)/[(1-z)(1-Qz)] =[T(1)-T(Q^-1)]/(1-Q). (4) Equivalently the small positive circle around zero can be deformed to the negative sum of the two pole circles. The opposite signs in their scalar periods come from the residues, not a choice to discard one contour. Formula (4) is a representation of the existing finite source, not the definition of a replacement state. ## 2. An actual braid conjugacy changes both endpoint values At N=2 use q=i, Q=-1, x=i and eta=exp(pi*i/4). The original balanced positive crossing, with its actual common Cartan line, is R_+=[[eta,0,0,0], [0,0,eta^-1,0], [0,eta^-1,2i eta^-1,0], [0,0,0,eta]]. Use its literal inverse, K=diag(i,-i), F_(1,0)=2 and the original pivot K^-1. Form the original three-strand word, tail-head fusion and right Euler conjugation from the all-strand theorem. Exact matrix multiplication over Q(i,sqrt(2)) gives beta=(1,-2,1,-2), T_beta(Z)=-1+(5/2)Z, beta'=(1,1,-2,1,-2,-1)=sigma_1 beta sigma_1^-1, T_beta'(Z)=2+(5/2)Z. (5) Both words have the same braid index and writhe, so all external source, peripheral and framing factors agree. Their endpoint pairs are beta: (T(1),T(-1))=(3/2,-7/2), beta': (T(1),T(-1))=(9/2,-1/2). (6) Both endpoints change by three, while both differences are exactly five, the same original reduced cut value. The change is a constant polynomial, which the source (4) annihilates. Thus neither individual endpoint can be identified with an intrinsic marked knot period using only a scalar adapter depending on N, color, braid index and writhe. The transported co-source or the complete two-endpoint difference is required. This is an exact actual-word countertest, not an arbitrary polynomial chosen to mimic a knot. ## 3. The pole collision has a cyclotomic boundary layer There is a simple all-level warning against merging the two poles before retaining the normal clock. For the constant polynomial one, [z^(N-1)]1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)]=0 at every original root, since this coefficient is (1-Q^N)/(1-Q). If one sets Q=1 in that rational kernel first, the same coefficient instead becomes [z^(N-1)](1-z)^-2=N. (7) This is a failure of the premature specialization, not a failure of the exact residue formula. The original source is normalized on the cyclotomic relation Q^N=1 and must retain it through the pole collision. To see the correct normal geometry, put H=2pi*i/N and z=exp(H xi). The two source poles are xi=0 and xi=-1 on their local logarithmic lifts. The pullback of (2) is EXACTLY H T_N(exp(H xi)) exp(H xi) exp(-2pi*i xi) /[(1-exp(H xi))(1-exp(H(xi+1)))] dxi. (8) On compact xi charts away from 0,-1 this has the kernel form H^-1 exp(-2pi*i xi) T_N(exp(H xi)) /[xi(xi+1)] * (1+O(H)) dxi. (9) The poles stay one unit apart, and the cyclotomic exponential survives. A fixed-z double-pole model that omits these data is not the source normal limit. In particular an ordinary residue of the principal geometric framing density alone cannot decide the selected endpoint class. ## 4. What a whole geometric source calculation would have to show There is a precise local source-symbol criterion once a uniform WHOLE asymptotic near the two endpoints has been proved. Let D=z partial_z and suppose on a fixed complex neighborhood of one T_N(z)=H^alpha exp(S(z)/H) [a_0(z)+H a_1(z)+O(H^2)], (10) with holomorphic S,a_0,a_1, uniform errors (including the required derivatives), and a_0(1)!=0. This hypothesis concerns the complete selected tail sum T_N, not one unsummed local geometric block. Set mu=exp(-D S(1)). Direct Taylor expansion at z=exp(-H) gives S_N=H^alpha exp(S(1)/H) {(1-mu)a_0(1) +H[(1-mu)a_1(1)+mu D a_0(1) -(mu/2)D^2 S(1)a_0(1)] +O(H^2)}. (11) If mu!=1, the first coefficient is nonzero. If mu=1, the principal coefficient cancels and the next source coefficient is D a_0(1)-(1/2)D^2 S(1)a_0(1). (12) The uniform Taylor expansion proves these formulas: write S(exp(-H))=S(1)-H D S(1)+(H^2/2)D^2 S(1)+O(H^3) and do the same for the amplitude. No contour or thimble selection is assumed during that algebraic expansion. If the first nonzero coefficient of the resulting derived source series occurs at some fixed finite order, and (10) holds to that order with controlled error, the original invariant has the same exponential rate Im S(1)/(2pi). In particular a calibrated action with Im S(1)=Vol(X) would imply the required volume rate. This is a sufficient conditional source criterion, not a proof that (10) holds for the knot state or that its derived coefficient is nonzero. The source variable here is the right-Euler coefficient variable. Its identification with a geometric framing or peripheral clock is still required. Only AFTER such a marking could a classical closure relation be used to assert mu=1. The actual source-wall and fusion-orientation audit in [the canonical-chart theorem](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md) prevents making that substitution by inspection. Thus the cycle problem is not settled by Rivin uniqueness: it must transport the marked TWO-pole functional and establish its first nonzero derived coefficient on the actual selected geometric image. Exact finite source jets or the unsourced nonzero Gaussian alone do not establish these hypotheses. No broad knot class is proved here. ## 5. Exact checks [The actual-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_two_pole_source_contour.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_two_pole_source_contour_results.json) pass 15 literal signed-word cases, levels N=2,...,6, and three same-index/same-writhe figure-eight braid conjugacies. The N=2 pair (5)-(6) is additionally checked by exact characteristic-zero matrix multiplication. All original word, pivot, fusion and Euler factors are used. Finite-field tests verify conventions; the residue and boundary-layer proofs above are all-level.

title: Uniform bounds for inserting twist powers
status: Finite norm theorem; shared source estimate remains
text:
# Uniform bounds for inserting twist powers The finite formula for a diagram can be organized in two steps. First, take the prescribed coefficient in its shared face variables. This gives a polynomial \(S_N\) in one spectral variable for each crossing region. Then apply a linear functional in each spectral variable to insert the chosen signed twist power. This note bounds the second step. Inserting \(n\) crossings costs at most \(1+|n|/2\) in the supremum norm on the real spectral interval, independently of the quantum level \(N\). There is a stronger estimate for the two one-sided pieces of the local polynomial: their values vanish at all spectral nodes, and the cost is then at most \((N-1)/N\), independently of \(n\) as well. The derivatives at repeated nodes remain in the calculation. The estimate applies after the face coefficient has been taken. All crossing regions therefore retain their common face constraints. To obtain a volume theorem from it, one must still bound this shared polynomial and prove that the geometric contribution survives. Here is the precise statement. Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and let \(\mathcal L_N^{n}\) be the full-Hermite functional for the actual crossing power \(R^n\), with \(n\in\mathbb Z\), defined below. For a polynomial \(H\) of degree at most \(d\), \[ |\mathcal L_N^{n}H| \le \left(1+ rac{|n|}{2}ight) \|H\|_{[-2,2]}. 	ag{1} \] If \(H\) vanishes at every root of \(\chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), including the simple root \(-2\) when \(N\) is odd, the stronger bound is \[ |\mathcal L_N^{n}H|\le  rac dN\|H\|_{[-2,2]}. 	ag{2} \] Vanishing means values only; the derivatives at double roots are retained. For \(r\) crossing regions, let \(S(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\) have degree at most \(d\) in each variable. Suppose that for every \(e\) in a set \(J\), \(S\) vanishes whenever \(\sigma_e\) is a spectral node, with its other variables arbitrary. Then \[ \left|\left( igotimes_{e=1}^r\mathcal L_N^{n_e}ight)Sight| \le \left( rac dNight)^{|J|} \prod_{e
otin J}\left(1+ rac{|n_e|}{2}ight) \|S\|_{[-2,2]^r}. 	ag{3} \] In particular this applies to each term containing a specified lower or upper one-sided factor, with \(J\) its one-sided crossing regions. The case \(J=\varnothing\) is the full-source bound. There is also a bound for the whole complementary source without expanding it into sectors. If \(\mathcal D\) vanishes on the Cartesian product of all spectral node sets, then \[ \left|\left( igotimes_{e=1}^r\mathcal L_N^{n_e}ight)\mathcal Dight| \le \left\{\prod_e\left(1+ rac{|n_e|}{2}ight) -\prod_e\left( rac1N+ rac{|n_e|}{2}ight)ight\} \|\mathcal D\|_{[-2,2]^r}. 	ag{4} \] For the actual numerator one may take \(\mathcal D=S_{\mathrm{full}}-S_{\mathrm{CROSS}}\). The coefficient in braces has degree at most \(r-1\) in the quantities \(|n_e|\): the highest product cancels exactly. None of (1)–(4) assumes positivity of spectral coefficients, asymptotic localization, or dominance of a Fourier charge. ## 1. The exact source and its normalization Use the original pair Casimir \(\Omega\), not an operator reconstructed from its spectral values. It satisfies \(\chi_N(\Omega)=0\), and polynomial division gives the degree-\(d\) resolvent numerator \[ V_N(z;\Omega)=\chi_N(z)(z-\Omega)^{-1}. 	ag{5} \] The right side means the resulting matrix polynomial, including at every spectral node. It is not the determinant adjugate of the full \(N^2\)-dimensional matrix. The [original homogeneous face source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) associates to (5) a four-face polynomial \(H_V(x,b,c,y;z)\), with literal input/output middle faces \(b,c\). Fix a connected original diagram at \(N\ge3\), with its actual cups, caps, unrestricted marked cap, protected face targets, and every ordered box. The applications include connected flat plats and the connected matched simple-sphere Morse diagrams of [the general Morse source theorem](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md), §§1,5–6, and [the terminal-fan source proof](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md), §§5–7. For the latter, the actual cyclic orders and crossing-disk frames are retained, and the marked main edge determines the two protected faces. The exact coefficient identity is the only input here: no complete-radius balance or geometric certificate is required for this finite norm estimate. The shared spectral polynomial is \[ S_N( oldsymbol\sigma)= [	extstyle\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d] \prod_{e=1}^{r}H_V(L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e};\sigma_e), 	ag{6} \] with the two protected face exponents zero. Every variable \(\sigma_e\) has degree at most \(d\). The original marked source after inserting the signed powers is exactly \[ Z_N( oldsymbol n)= \left( igotimes_{e=1}^r\mathcal L_N^{n_e}ight)S_N. 	ag{7} \] The face-grid factors, cup/cap factors and the original \(N^{-1}\) marked scalar have already canceled as in those source theorems; there is no additional \(N^r\) in (7). Thus \(Z_N\) is the original reduced ribbon contraction. Conversion to the prescribed zero-framed enhanced Kashaev convention uses the recorded framing/component character, of modulus one at complete color; for a knot the enhanced component sign is one. In the specified full one-cut modified convention, retain the additional factor \(i^{N+3}/N\). Original exterior Cartan and framing factors remain in their prescribed locations throughout. These are the physical normalization choices; no new quantum dimension or color average is introduced by the norm theorem. The polynomial degree and the identities (5)–(7), rather than a hypothesis about arbitrary polynomial solutions of a recurrence, are the source assumptions used here. The scalar inequalities (1)–(4) themselves hold for every polynomial of the indicated degree and every \(N\ge2\). ## 2. Repeated roots, the odd simple root, and the midpoint identity Write \[ c_a=2\cos rac{(2a+1)\pi}{N},\qquad 0\le a<\lfloor N/2floor. 	ag{8} \] These are the distinct double roots. The only remaining root is \(-2\), simple, when \(N\) is odd. At a double root \(c\), put \(h(z)=\chi_N(z)/(z-c)^2\). The Chebyshev differential equation gives \[ h(c)= rac{N^2}{4-c^2},\qquad  rac{h'(c)}{h(c)}= rac{c}{4-c^2}; \qquad \chi_N'(-2)=N^2\quad(N\ \mathrm{odd}). 	ag{9} \] Indeed \((4-z^2)\chi_N''-z\chi_N'+N^2(\chi_N-2)=0\). Evaluate it and its derivative at \(c\), using \(\chi_N(c)=\chi_N'(c)=0\), to obtain (9). If the resolvent at \(c\) is \(P_c/(z-c)+Q_c/(z-c)^2\), then \(V_N(c)=h(c)Q_c\) and \(V_N'(c)=h(c)P_c+h'(c)Q_c\). Consequently the [original spectral derivative functional](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md), on any scalar entry \(H\), is \[ \mathcal L_N^fH= \sum_a rac{(4-c_a^2)(fH)'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)H(c_a)}{N^2} +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd}} rac{f(-2)H(-2)}{N^2}. 	ag{10} \] It sends \(V_N\) to \(f(\Omega)\), with \(f'(c)Q_c\) included. The prime in (10) is a derivative in \(z\). Let \[ \phi_k= rac{(2k+1)\pi}{N},\quad 0\le k<N,\qquad P(\phi)=H(2\cos\phi). 	ag{11} \] Each double root appears twice in this grid. At the odd simple root, \(\phi=\pi\) occurs once, and differentiating the sine supplies exactly its weight in (10). Thus (10) is equivalently \[ \mathcal L_N^fH =- rac1{2}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left. rac{d}{d\phi}  rac{2\sin\phi\,f(2\cos\phi)H(2\cos\phi)}{N^2} ight|_{\phi=\phi_k}. 	ag{12} \] There is no omission or doubling of the odd simple node. For the actual positive or negative integral crossing power, the [full-Hermite Gaussian](actual_direct_long_power_source.md) is \[ f_n(2\cos\phi)=q^{nd^2/4} \exp\left( rac{inN(\phi-\pi)^2}{4\pi}ight), \qquad 0\le\phi\le2\pi. 	ag{13} \] Here \(q^a\) means \(e^{\pi ia/N}\), fixing the original square-root lift even for nonintegral \(a\). In particular \[ |f_n|=1,\qquad |\partial_\phi f_n|\le rac{|n|N}{2},\qquad f_n(c_a)=q^{nd^2/2}(-1)^{an}q^{na(a+1)}. 	ag{14} \] The nodal phase is the actual crossing phase, not its absolute value substituted into the source. Formula (13) is symmetric about \(\pi\); it has the required holomorphic germ at the odd simple node. The possible endpoint cut at \(z=2\) does not occur at a spectral node and does not enter the finite identity (12). Expanding (12), with primes now in \(\phi\), gives \[ \mathcal L_N^{n}H=- rac1{N^2}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}  igl(\cos\phi_k f_kP_k+ \sin\phi_k f_k'P_k+\sin\phi_k f_kP_k' igr). 	ag{15} \] This finite formula is sufficient for every norm below; no interchange of an infinite Fourier series or a contour limit is needed. ## 3. An elementary exact derivative inequality For every complex trigonometric polynomial \(P\) of degree at most \(d\ge1\), set \(	heta_j=(2j-1)\pi/(2d)\), \(1\le j\le2d\). The finite Riesz interpolation identity is \[ P'(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{2d}  rac{(-1)^{j+1}}{4d\sin^2(	heta_j/2)}P(x+	heta_j). 	ag{16} \] For completeness, invert the finite Fourier matrix on modes \(-d+1,\ldots,d\). If \(z=e^{-i	heta_j}\), so \(z^{2d}=-1\), differentiating the finite geometric sum gives its weight \[  rac1{2d}\sum_{\ell=-d+1}^{d}i\ell e^{-i\ell	heta_j} = rac{i z^{-d+1}}{d(1-z)^2} = rac{(-1)^{j+1}}{4d\sin^2(	heta_j/2)}. 	ag{17} \] The extra mode \(-d\) has samples opposite to those of \(d\), and its derivative at zero is opposite too. Thus (16) holds on all modes \(-d,\ldots,d\); translation gives arbitrary \(x\). The elementary sine product \(\prod_{j=0}^{2d-1}\sin(x+j\pi/(2d))=C_d\sin(2dx)\), with \(C_d
e0\), yields after two logarithmic derivatives and substitution \(x=\pi/(4d)\) \[ \sum_{j=1}^{2d} rac1{4d\sin^2(	heta_j/2)}=d. 	ag{18} \] Taking absolute values in (16) therefore proves \[ \|P'\|_{\mathbb R}\le d\|P\|_{\mathbb R}. 	ag{19} \] The argument works without real coefficients or positivity. The same finite identity and triangle inequality hold when the coefficients lie in any finite-dimensional normed space. Thus (19), and consequently (1)–(4), hold for such vector-valued polynomials without a dimension factor. The intended application here remains the original shared scalar coefficient (6); no change of the source norm is required. ## 4. Full and vanishing-node bounds Since \(H\) has degree at most \(d\), \(P(\phi)=H(2\cos\phi)\) has trigonometric degree at most \(d\), and its supremum is exactly \(\|H\|_{[-2,2]}\). Equations (14), (15), and (19) give \[ |\mathcal L_N^{n}H| \le rac{N}{N^2}\left(1+ rac{|n|N}{2}+dight)\|H\| =\left(1+ rac{|n|}{2}ight)\|H\|, 	ag{20} \] because \(d+1=N\). This proves (1). If \(H\) vanishes at every node, the first two terms of (15) vanish exactly. Only the derivative of the original numerator remains. Applying (19) to that term gives (2), uniformly in every signed \(n\), including zero. Here is why the original lower and upper one-sided numerators satisfy this hypothesis. Put \(D_-(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{\lfloor N/2floor-1}(z-c_a)\). The exact lower-row restriction leaves the factor \[  rac{\chi_N(z)}{D_-(z)}=  egin{cases}D_-(z),&N\ \mathrm{even},\ (z+2)D_-(z),&N\ \mathrm{odd}. \end{cases} 	ag{21} \] Every lower one-sided entry is divisible by (21); literal row reflection gives the same statement for the upper piece. Thus values vanish at all nodes. On the lower invariant block \(\Omega_-\), whose eigenvalues \(c_a\) are distinct, (10) reduces exactly to \[ \mathcal L_N^nH_{V,\mathrm L} =\sum_a f_n(c_a) rac{4-c_a^2}{N^2} H_{V,\mathrm L}'(c_a). 	ag{22} \] These numerator derivatives are the original lower-block spectral projectors. The derivative of \(f_n\) disappears, but the semisimple source is not zero. For example the literal local diagonal coefficient obeys \[ [c^d]H_{V,\mathrm L}(z)= rac{\chi_N(z)}{z-c_0}, \qquad [c^d]H_{R^n,\mathrm L}=q^{nd^2/2}. 	ag{23} \] Its modulus is one. This is an actual local coefficient, not a claim that the same boundary can maximize a closed source. ## 5. Shared polynomials and the unsplit complementary source The other finite functionals preserve each partial node-vanishing condition. Applying (1) and (2) successively to the original shared polynomial proves (3). Coefficient extraction in (6) is performed first and is never replaced by independent local maximization. For clarity, (4) needs only joint grid vanishing, not vanishing on every node hyperplane. In each coordinate (15) is a sum of an evaluation term and a term differentiating \(P\). Before summing its \(N\) grid entries, the two coefficient bounds are \(1+|n_e|N/2\) and \(1\), respectively. For a subset \(A\) of differentiated variables, iterating (19) gives \[ \|\partial_A\mathcal D(2\cos oldsymbol\phi)\| \le d^{|A|}\|\mathcal D\|_{[-2,2]^r}. 	ag{24} \] The term \(A=\varnothing\) vanishes pointwise at the tensor grid. Every other term is bounded by \(\prod_{e\in A}(d/N)\prod_{e
otin A}(1/N+|n_e|/2)\|\mathcal D\|\). Adding the nonempty subsets proves (4). In the [original central-cut decomposition](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), the lower and upper pieces have the factor (21). The full numerator is the sum of those pieces and the central crossing piece, denoted CROSS in the source formulas. At odd levels the central row belongs to that crossing piece. Hence every local full numerator agrees with CROSS at every spectral node. Multiplication and the one original shared coefficient extraction show \[ (S_{\mathrm{full}}-S_{\mathrm{CROSS}}) (c_{a_1},\ldots,c_{a_r})=0 	ag{25} \] for all choices of nodes, including odd simple nodes. Applying (4) to this unsplit difference avoids summing the absolute values of exponentially many path terms. The statement is finite and exact even though its remaining shared supremum can be large. ## 6. What the norm theorem does and does not supply There is already a level-independent dual filling cost in the [positive Fourier–Hermite Gram construction](actual_filling_fourier_hermite_gram.md): its squared Hilbert dual norm is exactly \(1+n^2(N^2-1)/(12N^2)\). That theorem uses a specified positive energy of the entire mixed-color packet. The present bounds use instead the supremum of the original shared resolvent numerator. The additional statements here are the twist-independent vanishing-node estimate and the unsplit product-grid cancellation. Neither construction by itself supplies the geometric exponential bound for its remaining source norm. For a fixed diagram and fixed powers, all constants in (1)–(4) are independent of \(N\). Thus any sharp exponential estimate for the same shared spectral supremum passes to its actual filled source without a new exponential cost. The theorem also shows precisely where a derivative of the crossing phase drops out and why this saves one or more twist factors. It does not prove that \(\|S_N\|\), or the complementary norm in (4), grows at the geometric volume rate. Neither node vanishing nor the uniform functional norm controls this remaining between-node polynomial. Separate absolute local envelopes may exceed that rate, and (23) prevents an argument that every one-sided channel is identically killed. The theorem asserts no new saddle dominance, peripheral representation, or knot-volume equality. The finite reproduction `experiments/audit_actual_uniform_filling_supremum_bound.py` takes `--repo` pointing to the research checkout. It checks the Chebyshev double/simple-root identities at levels 2–12 and the Riesz formula at degrees 1–12 exactly in cyclotomic fields. It also compares the midpoint reconstruction with independently built original coproduct/Casimir and signed braid matrices at levels 3–8, for powers \(\pm1,\ldots,\pm5\), and checks the lower-block compression including its normal data. The JSON output distinguishes the exact rational cyclotomic calculations from exact finite-field matrix checks. These finite cases check algebraic identities; the all-level inequalities follow from the proofs above, not from sampled norm ratios. ## 7. The estimate needed for long fillings It is useful to state the remaining comparison with its quantifiers. Fix the diagram, and write \[ \mathcal D_N=S_{N,\mathrm{full}}-S_{N,\mathrm{CROSS}}. \] This polynomial does not depend on the twist powers. Suppose one proves, for some fixed \(\eta>0\), \[ \|\mathcal D_N\|_{[-2,2]^r} \le \exp igl(N(\Phi-\eta)+o(N) igr). 	ag{26} \] Here \(\Phi\) is the complete augmented action in the normalization of the source. When it is identified geometrically, \(\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(M_{\mathrm{aug}})/(2\pi)\). For each fixed tuple \( oldsymbol n\), equation (4) then gives \[ \left|\left( igotimes_e\mathcal L_N^{n_e}ight)\mathcal D_Night| \le \exp igl(N(\Phi-\eta)+o(N) igr). 	ag{27} \] The finite factor in (4) is absorbed in \(o(N)\); this argument does not claim uniformity in twist powers growing with \(N\). Suppose separately that the crossing contribution has a nonzero asymptotic \[ Z_{N,\mathrm{CROSS}}( oldsymbol n) =a_N\exp(N\mathcal A_{ oldsymbol n}),\qquad N^{-1}\log|a_N|\longrightarrow0, 	ag{28} \] where \(\Re\mathcal A_{ oldsymbol n}>\Phi-\eta\). Equations (27) and (28) show that the complementary contribution divided by the crossing contribution tends to zero exponentially. Consequently \[ \lim_{N	o\infty}N^{-1}\log|Z_N( oldsymbol n)| =\Re\mathcal A_{ oldsymbol n}. 	ag{29} \] The subexponential normalization factors in section 1 preserve this limit. Identifying \(2\pi\Re\mathcal A_{ oldsymbol n}\) with the hyperbolic volume still requires the geometric filling argument for that diagram. This implication explains why a strict gap in (26) is useful for sufficiently long fixed fillings. The desired filled action approaches the augmented action as the auxiliary fillings become long. A bound for the full twist-independent polynomial at the augmented rate alone would give only that larger rate; it would not prove the smaller filled volume. The norm theorem proves the passage from (26) to (27). It does not prove (26) or supply (28) for a new diagram.

title: Exact cotangent source atlases and their universal-transport limitation
text: # Exact cotangent source atlases and their universal-transport limitation 28 October 2026. The TU pulling atlas of the original physical source has a finite compatible residue implementation, with explicit fixed integer coefficients and no exponentially conditioned chart adapter. Elementary cotangent changes retain calculable side currents. Artificial chart divisors cancel in their complete aggregate. There is an essential limit: these are UNIVERSAL identities on every holomorphic test function. Such identities cannot move the whole source to a cycle on which the completed original state is smaller than its largest physical lattice value. This follows from a direct holomorphic hull argument below, and does not require an unproved knot example. Thus the atlas solves an algebraic source-coordinate problem, not the state-specific cancellation needed for the sharp volume bound. ## 1. The exact original source functional Fix a nonempty one-component signed braid with m crossings, put r=m+1 and d=N-1, and keep its actual integral coordinates u=(t,k_1,...,k_m). Let Lambda_N=dP intersect Z^r, T_N(f)=sum_(n in Lambda_N) f(n). (1) Here P is the physical polytope in [the physical-face proof](actual_physical_face_outward_action.md). The cardinal-completed original scalar F_N is holomorphic on the specified O(N) complex box D, equals the EXACT original state at each valid n, and vanishes at every invalid integer state in the box. The complete original invariant is chi_N/N times T_N(F_N), with kappa, pivots, half-Cartan and every conversion phase inside F_N. No scalar line is altered below. Let kappa_0(s)=1/(1-exp(2*pi*i*s)); this symbol denotes a cotangent kernel, NOT the original crossing scalar kappa. At an integer n its residue is -1/(2*pi*i). Thus, on a sufficiently small product torus Gamma_n around n, integral_(Gamma_n) f(u) product_i[-2*pi*i*kappa_0(u_i) du_i] /(2*pi*i)^r=f(n). (2) The same is true with product_i pi*cot(pi*u_i) du_i. Exactly, pi*cot(pi*s)=-2*pi*i*kappa_0(s)+pi*i. (3) Every term in the difference of these PRODUCT kernels lacks at least one coordinate pole and integrates to zero on the FULL small torus. These terms are not zero on arbitrary partial chart chains. If (3) is used on a partial domain, its explicit 2^r-1 lower-pole terms are retained as source currents. The original finite source is therefore the coherent middle-dimensional cycle sum Gamma_Lambda=sum_n Gamma_n with either COMPLETE kernel. It has at most N^r local components. No norm estimate on F_N is used. ## 2. Finite compatible affine-unimodular charts The proved pulling triangulation gives finitely many cells u=d v_j+B_j y, y in d*Delta, B_j in GL_r(Z), (4) with their number and matrices depending only on the fixed diagram. Assign shared lattice faces once using a fixed half-open convention. Let Lambda_j be the resulting disjoint partition of Lambda_N. This is a partition of the original finite states, not a new source. Put A_j=B_j^(-1). Since d v_j is integer and A_j is unimodular, the joint poles of the new chart kernel are the SAME integer lattice. For each n in Lambda_j take Gamma_(j,n)=n+A_j^(-1) T_epsilon, omega_j=(-2*pi*i)^r det(A_j) product_i kappa_0((A_j u)_i) du_1...du_r. (5) The affine translation in (4) is harmless by INTEGER periodicity; no exponential monomial multiplier has been canceled. The induced orientation in (5) retains its determinant +/-1. The ordinary multivariate Cauchy residue calculation gives exactly integral_(Gamma_(j,n)) f omega_j/(2*pi*i)^r=f(n). Consequently T_N(f)=sum_j integral_(sum_(n in Lambda_j) Gamma_(j,n)) f omega_j/(2*pi*i)^r. (6) This identity is valid for EVERY f holomorphic near these cycles and their enclosed local polydiscs. All coefficients are one, all counting Jacobians are one, and it is the exact original functional (1). There is a simultaneous quantitative initial-cycle construction. Collect the finite integer row forms appearing in all chart matrices and in the elementary side currents of Section 3. Choose small radii epsilon_1 >> epsilon_2 >> ... >> epsilon_r with ratios less than 1/(4rC), where C bounds their integer coefficients in any chosen chart. Choose epsilon_1 so every linear form has modulus below 1/4. Its FIRST nonzero term then dominates the remaining terms, so every such form has modulus at least a fixed positive multiple of epsilon_r on the corresponding hierarchical torus. It cannot hit an integer. These radii depend on the diagram, not on N or n. All source kernels and chart Jacobians on this initial atlas are bounded by diagram constants. Its total logarithmic/Euclidean mass is O_word(N^r). This is a polynomial INITIAL mass bound, not a bound for an unconstructed global steepest-descent deformation. The union may still pass near individual large state values. ## 3. Explicit elementary side-current algebra Write x,y for two affine integer row forms. Their integer constants do not affect the periodic kernels. The exact identities are kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x+y)kappa_0(y) -kappa_0(x+y)kappa_0(-x), kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x-y)kappa_0(y) +kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y-x), kappa_0(-x)=1-kappa_0(x). (7) For example they follow immediately, with all terms retained, from kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x+y)[kappa_0(x)+kappa_0(y)-1]. The first line changes the first row from x to x+y and leaves y; the second changes it from x to x-y. The extra product is an EXPLICIT side-current kernel in another unimodular basis. A sign change has the displayed lower-pole current. A row swap only changes the recorded coordinate orientation. Multiplying by all spectator kernels gives the r-dimensional identities without hidden factors. Factor each fixed GL_r(Z) chart matrix into unit row shears, row swaps and sign changes. This is constructive integer elimination. Follow just the intended main basis through this fixed sequence; at each step retain its one extra kernel from (7). Telescoping gives K_reference=c_main K_chart+sum_n c_n K_side,n, (8) where every c is +1 or -1, and every side kernel is specified by that step. The number of terms is at most the number of steps plus one. It is independent of N. The ordinary powers of 2*pi*i and all determinants in converting (8) to normalized forms are fixed diagram constants. Products of lower-pole terms from (3) are also explicit and finite. None is silently declared source-null on a partial cycle. The side currents can carry the ENTIRE selected residue. Already in two local variables, the leading Cauchy identity is 1/(xy)=1/[(x+y)y]+1/[x(x+y)]. (9) On |x|<<|y|, the first right-hand term has integral zero, the second integral one, while the left integral is one. Thus retaining only the main new chart fails even for f=1. This is not an exponentially large adapter; it is a compulsory unit source current. ## 4. Aggregate cancellation and its exact chain qualification Equations (7)--(8) are pointwise meromorphic identities. In any common compact domain remove the SAME small tubes about the union of all appearing chart divisors. Apply Stokes on the remaining chains, retaining every tube boundary and every partial-chart side prism. Sum the kernels BEFORE taking the tube limit. At a divisor artificial to the reference kernel, every principal part cancels exactly in that aggregate. The same is true at dependent intersections: on each common regulator boundary the sum IS the reference meromorphic form, so it is not necessary to pretend that the individual singular currents have independent limits. Original coordinate divisors remain genuine source divisors and retain their original residues. No physical point is deleted by (8). This proves tame gluing on any PROVIDED compatible common chain homotopy. If neighboring chart homotopies have the same embedded interface with opposite induced orientations and the same regulator, their full side-current sums agree with the reference form and cancel. No exponential chart-change coefficient is introduced. On regions whose distances to all appearing integer hyperplanes are at least N^(-A), every kernel is bounded by N^C: globally |kappa_0(z)|<=C[1+dist(z,Z)^(-1)]. (10) In a fixed O(N) real box there are O_word(N) parallel translates per row form, hence polynomially many arrangement cells in fixed dimension. Piecewise-linear common chains with polynomial complexity therefore have polynomial source-kernel overhead. What is NOT proved is that separately chosen descending chart cycles have compatible interfaces or that their remaining side currents have small phase. The local identity does not construct that homotopy. Replacing each chart by an independently convenient contour and then omitting the difference currents is invalid. In fact there is a general obstruction to closing that gap by UNIVERSAL cot algebra alone. ## 5. Universal source rewrites cannot lower the state maximum Let D be a complex domain, Lambda a finite nonempty set in D, and w_p nonzero fixed complex weights. Suppose a compact union C of contours and finite complex source measure mu satisfy sum_(p in Lambda) w_p f(p)=integral_C f dmu (11) for EVERY holomorphic f on D. Each p belongs to the O(D)-holomorphic hull of C. Here is a direct proof, independent of any source model. If p is outside that hull, choose a holomorphic g with |g(p)|>sup_C|g|. Choose an ordinary polynomial L_p equal to one at p and zero at every other point of Lambda; for instance interpolate a generic linear coordinate separating the finite set. Apply (11) to f=L_p g^k. The result is |w_p| |g(p)|^k <=||mu|| sup_C|L_p| (sup_C|g|)^k, which is impossible as k tends to infinity. Therefore, for EVERY holomorphic F on D, max_(p in Lambda)|F(p)|<=sup_C|F|. (12) The conclusion holds for any finite number of chart cycles and kernels: combine their measures on their union. It still holds if the cycle was chosen after inspecting F, provided the resulting source identity remains valid for all holomorphic test functions. No polynomial-versus-exponential estimate is needed for this obstruction; finite total variation is enough. All constructions in Sections 1--4 are universal in this sense. Thus they cannot, by themselves, produce a low-|F_N| source cycle below a larger original lattice summand. An ordinary homotopy in the complement of every genuine integer source divisor is an even more restrictive instance: it separately preserves each Cauchy evaluation. Rewriting the cotangent form does not defeat that issue while its full test-function functional is preserved. The issue occurs in the actual model: the independently derived [signed Markov source family](actual_cotangent_homology_and_global_gluing_criterion.md) keeps the SAME hyperbolic knot and normalized period while each additional alternating-sign stabilization adds v_8/(2pi) to one valid original state's exponential rate. Its complete original pivotal traces are checked directly. Exact normalization pruning evades this family by composing the ACTUAL source cell first; it is not an identity on arbitrary multipliers of each intermediate state. This does NOT forbid a sharp upper bound for the original scalar. That bound concerns cancellations among the values of the PARTICULAR original F_N. Exact q-binomial fusion, Hopf-Ward equations and matched normalization cells can relate those values in ways invalid for an arbitrary holomorphic multiplier. Such an operation can change the individual-evaluation source homology while preserving its actual scalar. Pure coordinate changes and the universal algebra (7) do not. ## 6. Result and the precise outstanding step The original finite residue functional has a finite affine-unimodular atlas, polynomial initial mass, explicit fixed-coefficient side currents, and exact aggregate cancellation of ARTIFICIAL cotangent divisors. These statements include its complete original source. A global phase-small cycle does not follow. Beyond choosing compatible interfaces, one must use an original-STATE-specific Ward/fusion identity to recombine genuine evaluation residues. The transport must then control the resulting full currents. A construction that stays universal on all holomorphic test functions cannot accomplish that step, by (12). This is a mathematical limitation of that proposed route, not a claim that the volume conjecture is false. [Supplementary audit](../experiments/audit_actual_unimodular_cot_source_atlas.py) checks the exact shear algebra, compulsory unit side current and whole original source reindexing in fixed affine-unimodular charts.

title: An actual unprojectivized Frobenius source is a marked Borel torsor
text:
# An actual unprojectivized Frobenius source is a marked Borel torsor Research proof and independent audit, 27 October 2026. The actual high-color coherent source, its scale character, and one first descendant recover the complete framing two-form explicitly. The scale must be retained before normalizing the projector. A marked Kummer cover is necessary: the actual Sym^N data know the N-th power of that scale, not its unmarked root. This is a source/framing moment map. It does not yet intertwine the full network Gaussian coefficients or prove the selected volume norm. ## 1. Original divided matrices give the whole coherent source Use the actual high integral color with r=N and the root Frobenius matrices e,f,h: \[ ev_k=(N-k+1)v_{k-1},\quad fv_k=(k+1)v_{k+1},\quad hv_k=(N-2k)v_k . \] The pure-power source is \[ \psi(a,b)=\sum_{k=0}^Na^{N-k}b^kv_k . \] Its exact root differential laws are \[ e\psi=b\partial_a\psi,\quad f\psi=a\partial_b\psi,\quad h\psi=(a\partial_a-b\partial_b)\psi . 	ag{1} \] Thus this is the actual Sym^N source cone, not an auxiliary representation. It also has a specified original whole q-germ on every residue string s: \[ \psi_s(q;a,b)= \sum_{k=0}^N rac{a^{N-k}b^k}{k!} (F^{(N)}(q))^kw_{0,s}. \] The divided matrices have regular integral Gaussian entries, so this is polynomial in a,b and regular in q, including a=0. The corresponding whole duals use the actual \(\exp(u	au E^{(N)}(q))\), with their actual pairing units retained. The linear SL2 formulas (1) are root formulas; their full normal deformations are the actual bounded-PBW operators already proved. The distinguished fixed root co-source is \(\lambda_+(v_k)=2^{-N} inom Nk\). Its scale pairing is \[ \lambda_+\psi(a,b)=((a+b)/2)^N. 	ag{2} \] Normalizing by this quantity is legitimate only off its source wall and must not erase the character or its quantum derivatives. ## 2. Retain the scale AND the contragredient dual flag For the actual cut-Borel generators \[ M_1=h+2f,\qquad M_2=e+f , \] the standard ket \(w_+=(1,1)^t\) is an eigenvector of BOTH. Its vector cone alone has a one-dimensional orbit at that anchor. The correct paired source retains its contragredient dual flag. Write the standard ket and dual as \[ w=\alpha(1,1)^t,\qquad \ell= rac{(1,u)}{\alpha(1+u)},\qquad \ell w=1 , \quad \alpha
e0,\quad u
e-1 . \] Their ACTUAL Sym^N source and normalized co-source are \[ \psi_\alpha=\alpha^N\sum_kv_k,\qquad \lambda_{\alpha,u}(v_k)=  rac{ inom Nk u^k}{\alpha^N(1+u)^N}. 	ag{3} \] They pair to one. These are the source vector and co-source separately, not only their scale-invariant rank-one projector. Let g preserve the projective ket line \(w_+\), act on w by g, and on the dual by \(\ell g^{-1}\). Direct differentiation gives \[ Y_1=\alpha\partial_\alpha+2u(1+u)\partial_u,\qquad Y_2=\alpha\partial_\alpha+(u^2-1)\partial_u . 	ag{4} \] These have rank two at \((\alpha,u)=(1,1)\). The normalized projector alone would forget alpha and lose that direction. Here u is an affine flag chart. Include u=infinity as well: in the global affine coordinate m=(1-u)/(1+u), write \[ \ell= rac{(1+m,1-m)}{2\alpha},\qquad \lambda_{\alpha,m}(v_k)=\alpha^{-N} inom Nk \left( rac{1+m}{2}ight)^{N-k} \left( rac{1-m}{2}ight)^k . \] These formulas are regular for every m in A^1, including m=-1 (the chart point u=infinity). The FULL marked paired space is G_m times A^1; the displayed finite-u chart alone is not preserved by every Borel element. This full space is genuinely a Borel torsor on the STANDARD marked cover. A group element fixing w and its normalized dual fixes the complementary dual kernel as well; determinant one then forces identity. The Borel has the same dimension as this open paired source space and acts transitively: scale w, then use its unipotent subgroup to move the dual with its fixed nonzero pairing. Equivalently use \(m=(1-u)/(1+u)\); (4) become \[ Y_1=\alpha\partial_\alpha+(2m-2)\partial_m,\qquad Y_2=\alpha\partial_\alpha+2m\partial_m , \] the ordinary free affine Borel action on \(\mathbb G_m	imes\mathbb A^1\). More explicitly, in the standard basis \(w_+=(1,1),w_-=(1,-1)\), the unique group element from the reference \((\alpha,m)=(1,0)\) is \[ g(\alpha,m)=  egin{pmatrix}\alpha&-m/\alpha\0&\alpha^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. \] It sends the ket to the stated ket and the reference dual contragrediently to the stated dual. ## 3. The exact equivariant internal-frame map For constants \(C
e0,D\), put \[ s=C\alpha^2,\qquad r= rac1{1+u}+D\alpha^2,\qquad A= rac1{1+s}. 	ag{5} \] The regular A/Omega_cut chart additionally requires 1+C alpha^2!=0. The framing map and invariant Haar form have their stated rational meanings on the larger open alpha!=0, u!=-1; the cut-density pole is retained at the omitted divisor. The letter r here is the framing coordinate; the color highest weight was fixed to N. Calculation in (4) gives \[ Y_1(r)=2(r-1),\quad Y_2(r)=2r-1,\quad Y_1(s)=Y_2(s)=2s . \] Thus the actual paired-source Borel fields map EXACTLY to \[ \xi_1=2(r-1)\partial_r+2s\partial_s,\qquad \xi_2=(2r-1)\partial_r+2s\partial_s, 	ag{6} \] the original compensated cut-framing fields. The map has nonzero local Jacobian on this open set. It is a marked sign cover of the PGL2 framing torsor, not an identification of every Fr generator with an old head current. Choose \(C=-2,D=0\). The actual source anchor \((\alpha,u)=(1,1)\) maps to \[ (r,s)=(1/2,-2),\qquad A=-1. \] It is a regular frame with nonzero Borel fields. This repairs the vanishing-vector obstruction of the normalized compact Fr projector at its anchor. The original complete meridian signs, full peripheral dimension line, and half-form marks remain separate. Formula (5) does not equate the OLD physical clock with the new diagonal Q^R clock; the controlled Fourier polarization dictionary is still required. ## 4. A scale character and ONE actual descendant give the full two-form The Berry form of (3) is \[ \lambda_{\alpha,u}d\psi_\alpha=N\,d\log\alpha . \] Its curvature is zero on this Borel. It must NOT be called the framing area form. The missing covector comes from an actual first descendant: \[ U=\lambda_+\psi_\alpha=\alpha^N,\qquad m= rac1N\lambda_{\alpha,u}h\psi_\alpha = rac{1-u}{1+u}. 	ag{7} \] Both are literal source/co-source pairings of original divided matrices. Define \[ \omega_H= rac1N d\log U=d\log\alpha,\qquad \omega_U=- rac{dm}{2\alpha^2} = rac{du}{\alpha^2(1+u)^2}. \] They satisfy \(d\omega_H=0\), \(d\omega_U=-2\omega_H\wedge\omega_U\), the explicit Borel Maurer differential law. The invariant Haar form and the actual compensated framing form are respectively \[ \widehat\Omega=- rac{dr\wedge ds}{s^2},\qquad \Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}=- rac{dr\wedge ds}{s(1+s)} . \] Substitution of (5) gives the exact source identities \[ \widehat\Omega=- rac2C\,\omega_H\wedge\omega_U, \qquad  oxed{\ \Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}= rac A N\,d\log U\wedge dm\ }. 	ag{8} \] The constant D drops out. Hence the rank-two co-source form is recovered from SCALE plus DESCENDANT, not from Berry curvature. Its covariance under (6) is exactly \(\operatorname{div}_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}}\xi_i=2A\). The Haar form instead is invariant. This retains the source-density correction needed by the actual geometric Ward currents. For C=-2, the exact power character is \[ U^2=\left( rac{A-1}{2A}ight)^N. 	ag{9} \] In particular \(Y_iU=NU\). The factor \(2^N\), the power N, and its marked root cannot be replaced by their value at one point. Equation (9) is a SOURCE/frame character. It is not, without the missing network map, the knot meridian's ADO modified-dimension character. ## 5. The old cut-clock normal really detects this scale The specified actual whole divided-source construction has a concrete old-clock normal pairing, derived in [the controlled Fourier/current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md). Let \(U_s(q;a,b)\) be its actual fixed-cut pairing and use the root-one ratios \(U_0/U_s\) on the head strings. The resulting UNNORMALIZED whole source satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(I)=U_0(q;a,b),\qquad \left[ rac{\Phi_Q(Q^SZ^R)}{1-Q^N}ight]_{Q_N} = rac{((a+b)/2)^N}{N(1-Q_N)},\quad Z=Q^N. 	ag{10} \] With a=b=alpha its numerator is exactly U of (7). The scalar multiplier is nonzero, has modulus between \(1/(2\pi)\) and \(1/4\), and tends to \(-1/(2\pi i)\). For completeness, put \(\delta=1-Q^N\). The per-string ratio \(U_s(q;a,bZ)/U_s(q;a,b)\) has first coefficient \(-N b/(a+b)\), independent of s at the root. The sums \(\sum_sQ_N^s=0\) kill that contribution and all overall source-unit derivatives. The remaining exact identity \(\sum_s sQ_N^s=-N/(1-Q_N)\) proves (10). The reduced head clock gives the same SELECTED scalar after these cancellations, although its operator Ward commutators differ. Thus (10) detects the scale line; it is not by itself a new independent Fr scalar-current theorem. Dividing the whole functional by U_0 returns the normalized original same-high-color scalar. Retaining U_0 separately keeps the actual source line and all its derivatives. This compares the high color with itself; its off-root jets are not equated with the low N-color jets. ## 6. The Kummer marking and remaining global comparison The ACTUAL pure-power source is unchanged under \((a,b)\mapsto(\zeta a,\zeta b)\), \(\zeta^N=1\). Likewise the paired Sym^N data (3) know alpha^N, not alpha. To use the standard Borel torsor and (5), retain the marked Kummer cover \(\alpha^N=U\), anchored by alpha=1. The unmarked actual Sym^N orbit is a homogeneous quotient by this finite isotropy, which need not be normal in the Borel. For N>2 it inherits neither a Borel quotient group nor a free SL2 Borel torsor action; the central-sign N=2 exception is below. The common marked SL2-Borel cover, rather than that quotient, carries the free source action and the frame sign-cover map. One cannot silently descend (5) to the unmarked Sym^N cone: alpha^2 generally changes under a mu_N root when N>2. Its frame sign cover only removes mu_2. At N=2 this subgroup is central: the quotient does inherit the PGL2 Borel group and its free torsor action, although the SL2 Borel action has kernel mu_2. For N>2 the finite isotropy is not normal in the Borel, so no quotient group structure is silently imposed. The unframed geometric character is gauge-invariant, but the relative endpoints, log sheets and period characters still require their own descent. This is precisely why the root mark belongs to the source torsor. At \(U=0\), or at the missing dual flag \(u=-1\), source vectors and inverse duals cannot be specialized separately. The actual paired fractional lattice or normal source complex must remain. On a physical cut loop the scale may approach this boundary, so no growing-neighborhood norm or cycle comparison follows from the regular local torsor. Equations (4), (6), (8), and (10) are concrete actual source/framing data. The remaining theorem is specific: map the whole network's ordinary/divided Ward currents and their charged normal neighbors to these source forms, preserving the final co-source and relative endpoints. The geometric Gaussian coefficients and global selected contribution have not been identified by an abstract Borel isomorphism. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_frobenius_borel_torsor.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_frobenius_borel_torsor_results.json) check the ACTUAL divided-source and dual matrix fields, scale/descendant pairings, frame pushforward, area form, and co-source covariance in 63 symbolic checks at N=2 through 9.

title: Every regular full wall critical action has the actual representation regulator
text: # Every regular full wall critical action has the actual representation regulator 28 October 2026. The nine-atom full-Psi scalar crossing has the SAME Bloch--Wigner regulator as the original five-dilogarithm ADO crossing, for both signs, on its entire regular rational graph. This is proved without inferring a regulator from holonomy alone: their Bloch wedges are identical, the parameter chart is connected, and a real chart fixes the regulator constant. Integer norm/carry marks add 2*pi*i times logarithms to the action. At every regular FULL interior critical point these terms cancel from the imaginary critical value by an exact real-quadratic identity. Consequently the critical value is the regulator of the actual boundary-parabolic knot representation, after the existing marked fundamental-cycle comparison. This controls critical VALUES, not the original cycle's selected coefficient or its singular/escaping contributions. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_wall_critical_regulator.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_wall_critical_regulator_results.json) verify both rational crossing maps in all six Gauss coordinates, factor the Bloch wedges identically over Q(A,B,z,w), check the real normalization and complex regulators, and verify the off-critical integer-mark identity. No literature proof is used in these calculations. ## 1. The actual nine atom graphs Use physical clocks A,B and head coordinates z,w at complete color x=-1. At a current pair (a,b,p,r), the elementary principal maps are: | Gate | Bloch contribution | Position/clock update | | --- | --- | --- | | U diagonal on i | -[1-B_i] | z_i -> z_i(1-B_i) | | F diagonal on i | +[1-B_i] | z_i -> z_i/(1-B_i) | | U_- | -[t], t=-r/p | a -> a/(1-t), b -> b(1-t) | | V_- | +[t], t=-r/p | a -> a(1-t), b -> b/(1-t) | | U_+ | -[t], t=-p/r | a -> a(1-t), b -> b/(1-t) | | V_+ | +[t], t=-p/r | a -> a/(1-t), b -> b(1-t) | | D_+ | 0 | r -> -r/b | | D_- | 0 | r -> -br | Read the original strict factorization in traversal order: C^(-1): U_2, V_-, U_1, F_2; positive center: U_+, D_+; negative center: D_-, V_+; C: U_2, F_1, U_-, F_2. (1) The nine nonzero Bloch entries define beta_9^+ or beta_9^-. All are explicit rational functions of A,B,z,w. This is the [actual scalar full-Psi action](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md), with its reflected monomials and Gaussian retained. The physical generators are K=-1/a, e=(a^(-1)-1)/p, f=(1-a)p. (2) Direct rational substitution in (1) gives EXACTLY the independently proved actual crossing maps (4.6)--(4.7) of [the marked braid calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md). This is checked algebraically for every one of the six output Gauss coordinates; equality of maps is not inferred from equality of finite root-level matrices or from a presumed saddle selection. ## 2. Regulator equality with the original coefficient symbol Let C_+=(1-e_1 f_2)^(-1), and C_-=1-(B/A)e_2 f_1. The original coefficient Bloch symbols are beta_5^+=[B]+[C_+]+[1/A]-[BC_+]-[C_+/A], beta_5^-=[A]+[C_-]+[1/B]-[AC_-]-[C_-/B]. (3) On the common regular rational crossing graph, delta(beta_9^sign-beta_5^sign)=0 in Lambda^2(Q(A,B,z,w)^* tensor Q). (4) There are two independent ways to check (4). For a signed dilog generating expression, its wedge is its incoming symplectic boundary minus the outgoing boundary; the internal monomial coordinates cancel, and symmetric real quadratic/Gaussian terms contribute zero. Both graph maps in Section 1 are the same actual map. In the physical position convention the common boundary is z wedge A+w wedge B-z_out wedge A_out-w_out wedge B_out. In the original coefficient convention it is A wedge p_in,1 plus B wedge p_in,2 minus the two outgoing terms, with p=z^(-1), so these are identical. The complete color -1 is torsion and disappears rationally. Alternatively factor every rational shape and its complement into irreducibles; the audit verifies the full antisymmetric coefficient matrix of (4) is identically zero for BOTH signs. Rational constant factors are retained in this check, not silently discarded. The differential of the Bloch--Wigner regulator D is a homomorphism of the multiplicative wedge: for one shape its differential is log|a| dArg(1-a)-log|1-a| dArg a. Thus (4) gives d D(beta_9^sign-beta_5^sign)=0. (5) The regular parameter space is a nonempty complex Zariski-open subset of (C^*)^4, obtained by removing finitely many rational zeros, poles and shapes equal to 1. It is connected: connect generic points by complex affine lines avoiding the finitely many excluded points on each line. Hence (5) is a single real constant on this space. Every rational argument in (1)--(3) has REAL coefficients. A generic real input avoids the finite excluded algebraic sets. Every shape is then real, so EVERY D value is zero. Therefore that constant is zero: D(beta_9^+)=D(beta_5^+), D(beta_9^-)=D(beta_5^-). (6) This fixes exactly the regulator information needed here. No claim is made that wedge equality alone identifies an integral Bloch class, an integral flattening, or a complex period torsor. ## 3. Exact cancellation of integer wall marks at full critical points Use logarithmic coordinates Z=rho+i theta. Consider W(Z)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(A_j(Z)) +1/2 Z^t C Z+i kappa^t Z+c, A_j(Z)=exp(a_j^t Z+i*pi*nu_j), (7) where a_j,nu_j,C,kappa are real, C is symmetric, and Im c=0. Branches of Li_2 and Log(1-A_j) are matched; D remains its single-valued Bloch--Wigner value on the recorded local sheet. On its ordinary unflattened local branch the exact identity is Im W-sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j) =rho^t Im(gradient W). (8) Indeed Im Li_2(A)=D(A)-log|A| Arg(1-A), and log|A_j|=a_j^t rho. Also Im(1/2 Z^t C Z)=rho^t C theta, while Im(i kappa^t Z)=kappa^t rho. The right side of (8) is precisely this difference.
