Consistent alternative dilog branches carry their explicit integer logarithmic marks into kappa and the real constant; one must not change the Li_2 sheet without its mark. A simple atomic negative-ray source has its retained factor A_j^N. In exp(W/h), h=2*pi*i/N, it adds 2*pi*i Log A_j. Transverse iterated wall charges add integer sums of such logarithms. They only change kappa by real integer multiples of 2*pi*a_j and add a REAL constant from i*pi*nu_j. Equation (8) remains true. At a FULL critical point, gradient W=0 ==> Im W=sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j). (9) The integer norm charges therefore do not create an additional critical exponential rate log|A_j| after the critical equations are imposed. Dropping full stationarity would make this conclusion false: the residual term on the right side of (8) is then present. The actual scalar action is of the form (7). Put eta_s=sqrt(2*pi*i*s)xi_s at each Gaussian. Its original Gaussian term -pi*i*xi_s^2 becomes -s*eta_s^2/2, a REAL quadratic. The actual atomic arguments are signed monomials in the head positions and exp(eta_s). For each coupled cap put p=2*pi*i*s_cap; its interval term is p Log r, a REAL bilinear form in logarithmic coordinates. Original reflected monomials and complete-color signs give the i*kappa terms. Thus Gaussian and cap variables must be retained in the FULL stationarity condition of (9). ## 4. What regular wall stationary points represent An integer logarithmic wall mark shifts derivatives by multiples of 2*pi*i but leaves the EXPONENTIATED canonical equations unchanged. At a finite regular full interior critical point these are the same actual rational crossing/Hurwitz maps as in Section 1 and the same inverse-meridian cap equations proved in [the coupled-cap note](actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.md). They define a representation of the original oriented knot group, with the original marked source and preferred peripheral convention. For a noncentral complete meridian the peripheral longitude commutes with a nontrivial unipotent matrix, whose centralizer in PSL(2,C) is the unipotent one-parameter group. Thus this is a genuinely boundary-parabolic representation. A cut wall is not generally a physical clock B=1: its DILOG argument A_j is negative real, and an auxiliary flat atom can occur over a noncentral representation. The restriction "full" includes regular wall chains whose remaining real tangent directions span the full complex cotangent space. Their interior complex stationary equation is gradient W=0. It excludes endpoint extrema, rank-deficient/nontransverse corner strata, escaping flags, and singular sources where a constrained stationary equation does not imply the full equation. ## 5. The marked fundamental-cycle comparison extends beyond faithfulness The proof in [the crossing fundamental-cycle note](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) uses unipotence, the actual Hurwitz words, oriented crossing balls, face cancellation and a degree-one peripheral reconstruction. None of its determinant/five-term certificates requires the DEVELOPING representation rho to be faithful. The group used in its relative configuration complex is the original hyperbolic knot group Gamma; its peripheral malnormality concerns Gamma, independently of rho. For any boundary-parabolic rho with noncentral meridians, choose its fixed peripheral flags and generic auxiliary flags. Forced repeated DEVELOPED vertices map to zero in the normalized alternating configuration complex. This is a chain map: repeated-vertex face terms cancel in pairs. The same explicit three five-term boundaries therefore give the rho-developed relative fundamental cycle. Unipotent cancellation uses a nonzero translation because the meridians are noncentral; central representations are handled separately and have trivial PSL image in the one-component case. Consequently, summing (6) over the actual word and keeping the original turn orientations gives sum_crossings D(beta_9)=Vol(rho). (10) Caps contribute their original pairing/marking, not an additional independently assigned tetrahedral regulator. The preferred-longitude correction is the same determinant-one writhe shear as in the fundamental-cycle proof. When a finite developed shape approaches 0,1 or infinity, D extends continuously by zero, so normalized degenerate tetrahedra do not add an unknown constant. This continuity does not justify a quantum source limit at a singular chart. Combining (9)--(10), EVERY regular FULL interior wall critical action in the recorded actual source has its actual representation regulator. The separately proved [sharp representation-volume bound](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) therefore gives |Im W_critical|<=Vol(M) for all these regular full critical values. This statement alone gives neither a global contour bound nor a selected geometric lower bound. Normalization ray cells can have the full geometric rate, as the retained source calculations already show; they must be grouped exactly rather than called negligible.

title: Source-preserving weighted Fourier energy for the original plat
text: # Source-preserving weighted Fourier energy for the original plat 28 October 2026. There is an exact positive factorial gauge which fixes every original plat turn. It gives a concrete family of weighted Fourier norms and a finite convex upper-bound problem for the **original** scalar. Its gauges can be exponentially conditioned; no such condition number is paid at the paired source. Whole inverse crossing pairs can be contracted before taking positive norms. This does not give the sharp hyperbolic-volume estimate. In particular, same-frame diagonal scaling cannot reduce the local crossing's flat Hilbert--Schmidt norm. A short exact doubled-source calculation below identifies the coherent sewing probability which still needs an estimate. ## 1. The physical factorial gauge fixes the original paired source Put Q=exp(2 pi i/N), d=N-1, x=-exp(-pi i/N), F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The exact root reflection identity is F_a F_(d-a)=N (-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2). (1) Consequently the actual middle-certificate frame and its positive part, Gamma_a=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a-1)/2) F_a^2 =Q^a |F_a|^2, L_a=|F_a|^2/N, obey at EVERY index Gamma_a Gamma_(d-a)=N^2 Q^(-1), L_a L_(d-a)=1. (2) The second relation is an exact equality of positive real numbers. It is not an asymptotic bound near a selected cap index. Use the original physical cup, ordinary cap, and full marked row: p_(a,b)=N x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), ell_(a,b)=x^b g_a/N delta_(a+b,d), m_(a,b)=x^b/N^2, g_a=x^(1-N)Q^(-a). For EVERY real t, positive powers defined by their real logarithm give (L^t tensor L^t)p=p, ell(L^(-t) tensor L^(-t))=ell. (3) The marked row has the same identity on pair degree d. It is not an identity of the unrestricted row m. In an assembled original k-cup plat the exact integer-degree argument forces the final marked pair to have degree d after the ordinary caps are taken. Diagonal gauges preserve that argument. Thus (3) holds for the full marked source in its legitimate whole-network scope. More generally, choose arbitrary positive numbers A_(r,a) on the odd head of pair r and set the even-head entries to A_(r,d-b)^(-1). The product gauge G fixes p^(tensor k) and its original ordinary/marked co-source exactly. L^t on both heads is the special case (2). These are physical-head transformations; they do not identify a fusion-relative index with a physical one. For clarity, retain the proved original whole-source normalization from [the actual plat Gram theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md): P_N=chi_N N^(k-1) <phi,W uhat>, uhat=p^(tensor k)/||p^(tensor k)||, phi=G_top^dagger uhat, ||phi||=||uhat||=1. (4) Here G_top is the original unitary product of ordinary pivots; the marked pair has none. The external chi_N, framing and peripheral line are exactly those in that theorem. The gauge G just defined commutes with G_top and fixes uhat and phi. Therefore, for ANY two such endpoint gauges G_in,G_out, <phi,G_out W G_in^(-1) uhat>=<phi,W uhat>. (5) This provides a genuine source-preserving positive gauge freedom. It does not declare one isolated Gamma in a local five-point word removable; such a local replacement still needs its typed interfaces. ## 2. Exact weighted Plancherel and the dual metric Let F be the normalized unitary finite Fourier matrix, F_(r,a)=Q^(ra)/sqrt(N). For a physical head vector v put vhat_t=F L^t v, H_t=F L^(-2t) F^dagger. Then exactly, for arbitrary v,w, <v,w>=<vhat_t,H_t what_t>, (H_t)_(r,s)=N^(-1)sum_a Q^((r-s)a)(N/|F_a|^2)^(2t). (6) H_t is positive definite. These are the compulsory dual norm weights of this factorial Fourier transformation. Flat Fourier energy of L^t v is a different norm from that of v. Equation (2) pairs the weights reciprocally on the original cap charge, explaining the source cancellation in (3); it does not make H_t the identity. The usual unitary Fourier changes can now be made at every physical wire, with all turns transported. In the G=L^t frame their original turn arrays are unchanged before the unitary Fourier transform. All interior inverse frames cancel literally. Thus this weighted duality extends to any signed original word and its doubled norm, including the marked pair, with no exponential source renormalization. The size of the weights remains explicit. Uniformly in a, log L_a=2N J(a/N)+O(log N), J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi u))du. (7) Hence (6) carries the full factorial dilogarithm action. It cannot be replaced by a flat positive trace merely because its source normalization is exact. ## 3. A computable positive energy upper-bound hierarchy Partition a fixed original word into consecutive actual blocks W=B_l ... B_1. Choose arbitrary positive diagonal tensor gauges G_j on all live physical heads between blocks; only the endpoint gauges are required to satisfy the paired-source condition of Section 1. Define C_j=G_j B_j G_(j-1)^(-1). All factors, pivots, and sources in (4) remain original. From (5), ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz and submultiplicativity give the finite-N bound |P_N| <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) product_j ||C_j||_op <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) product_j ||C_j||_HS. (8) This is not a largest-root or a favorable-source prescription. The right side is an explicit optimization problem in known original block matrices. At the finest partition the blocks are literal crossings, whose entries are given by the finite factorial formula. There is no unknown knot scalar in that objective. Write a diagonal gauge entry as exp(s_j(I)), where s_j(I) is the sum of its head log entries. Each summand in its logarithmic HS objective is (1/2)log sum_(I,J) |(B_j)_(I,J)|^2 exp(2s_j(I)-2s_(j-1)(J)). (9) It is convex in every gauge logarithm: the Hessian of log-sum-exp is the positive covariance matrix of its exponent vectors. The paired endpoint conditions are linear equations in these same logarithms. No minimum-attainment hypothesis is needed to take the infimum in (8). The factorial choices in Section 1 are legitimate points of this feasible set, even when they depend exponentially on N. Merging neighboring blocks never worsens the best HS bound, since ||AB||_HS <= ||A||_HS ||B||_HS with the intervening gauge cancelled. In particular an actual neighboring R R^(-1) block is exactly the identity, of polynomial HS norm N^k. Its exponential cost is zero. Thus one can perform exact signed-pair and other verified word reductions before taking norms, rather than charging their separate positive crossing energies. This is a constructive renormalization of those pairs with the original source retained. The same block principle applies to a local contraction containing an actual turn. In particular the defining complete ADO Markov calculation gives, for either sign with its own original zero-framing correction, Tr_2[Rhat_+ (I tensor g)]=I, Tr_2[Rhat_- (I tensor g)]=I. (9a) For arbitrary one-head exterior matrices A,B it follows that Tr_2[(A tensor I) Rhat_sigma (B tensor I) (I tensor g)]=AB, sigma=+,-. (9b) No division by AB or by a knot period occurs. Thus a genuine curl subnetwork, including its original cap, can be replaced by the identity **before** forming its doubled positive block energy. Its doubled map is then the identity trace-preserving channel and has zero exponential cost. This works inside any larger knot word. It does not replace an unclosed crossing by a trace-preserving channel. More generally any verified exact local tensor contraction can be used as a block, with its original boundary source retained, before applying (8). The finest flat bound already proves an unconditional whole-period estimate. For a word of m crossings, the independently proved [actual crossing norm theorem](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) gives log||R_+||_HS=log||R_-||_HS =N v_8/(2pi)+O(log N). Tensoring with a fixed number of spectator identities adds only O(log N). All complete external lines in chi_N have polynomial magnitude. Therefore limsup_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|P_N| <= m v_8. (10) The same holds for the original reduced Kashaev scalar, since its complete modified-dimension factor is a known root phase divided by N. This is a crossing bound, not the desired sharp Vol(S^3-K) bound. The convex bound (8)--(9), including exact block reductions, is an operative way to improve it; no assertion is made that it has already reached the hyperbolic volume for a broad knot class. ## 4. The remaining positive coherent sewing probability The precise cost of closure can be stated before any scalar-cut reduction. Let W act on one open head tensor an environment of dimension D=N^(b-1), and keep the original unitary environment pivot g. Group vec(W) by its open input/output pair and environment pair. Put h_g=vec(g^dagger)/sqrt(D), P_g=I_(open pair) tensor |h_g><h_g|, C=Tr_env[W(I tensor g)]. P_g is an orthogonal positive projector. Direct expansion of the matrix indices proves ||C||_HS^2=D <vec(W),P_g vec(W)>. (11) This identity holds for nonscalar C. Under any unitary Fourier transform of the half-edge indices, BOTH vec(W) and h_g transform, and the right side is unchanged. It is not the same as replacing the projector by an identity or dephasing its channels. If the original cut is C=K_N I, the normalized projection probability on the free vectorized word is p_g=N|K_N|^2/(D||W||_HS^2), 0<=p_g<=1. (12) The positive source opening Pi=N g_1 E_d(Z_1Z_2)E_0(X) in [the exact cap Fourier theorem](actual_middle_wall_fourier_packet.md#5-the-original-affine-cap-is-a-charged-fourier-mode) satisfies ||(C tensor I)Pi||_HS^2=N||C||_HS^2 for arbitrary C. Thus it supplies a normalized local positive realization of (11), but leaves its exterior coherent projection in place. For a normalized single positive crossing (the unknot curl), C=I exactly. With b=2, (12) becomes the all-N identity p_curl=||R_+||_HS^(-2), log p_curl= -N v_8/pi+O(log N). (13) This uses the original residual twist and pivotal cap; they have not been reset. It explains why local positive energies can have a larger rate than the closed period. The block renormalization in Section 3 is one exact way of contracting such source effects before bounding; it is not permission to discard the coherent probability for a general knot word. There is also a sharp restriction on improving a local block by a same-frame positive diagonal gauge. The actual balanced crossing is symmetric, R^t=R. For ANY positive diagonal D, ||D R D^(-1)||_HS^2 =sum_(i,j)|R_(i,j)|^2 D_i^2/D_j^2 >=sum_(i,j)|R_(i,j)|^2=||R||_HS^2, (14) by pairing i,j and j,i and using r+r^(-1)>=2. Fourier changes do not alter this norm. Thus isolated same-frame factorial scaling cannot remove the regular octahedral rate; an improvement must use actual coupled block contraction or a controlled whole-source estimate. ## 5. Audit and current scope [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.py) passes N=2,...,12. It checks exact factorial reflection, preservation of the original cup/cap and the correctly restricted marker for positive and negative real gauge powers, the non-flat dual Fourier metric, the nonscalar source projector identity, unitary transport of its coherent source, actual crossing symmetry, the local norm minimum, and the normalized unknot-curl probability. Eight complete original four-head plats additionally test the literal ordinary plus full marked source, its whole-degree reduction, unequal paired endpoint gauges, arbitrary internal gauges and the positive block energy bound. The extra external Cartan/framing lines are common unit phases on both sides of those source comparisons. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy_results.json). The new constructive point is the original-source-preserving paired factorial gauge and its explicit positive convex energy hierarchy. The sharp geometric estimate for that hierarchy, or a direct bound on its remaining coherent sewing probability, has not been proved. No global geometric coefficient or hyperbolic-volume lower bound is inferred here.

title: Weyl symmetry of the actual state and automatic operator reciprocity
text: # Weyl symmetry of the actual state and automatic operator reciprocity Research note, 26 October 2026. This removes the extra quantum-reciprocity hypothesis from the preceding normal-period formulation when the operator is the primitive minimal operator of the actual normalized ADO family. The state symmetry, its peripheral factors, and the monomial reciprocity are proved directly. They hold for every knot at every level, with the usual finite exceptional set for a chosen operator's specialization. They do not prove injectivity of its relevant root-fiber sector, identify its classical geometric factors, or establish the regulator norm. The state is the literature one fixed in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Its all-level annihilator is nonzero by [the finite-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). No new ordering of a classical polynomial or replacement state is chosen here. ## 1. The actual reduced and full periods have reflected meridians Use q=exp(pi*i/N), x=q^alpha, M=-qx and Y=M^2. On the actual N-dimensional color the matrices and coproduct are H v_a=(alpha-2a)v_a, K v_a=x q^(-2a)v_a, E v_a=[a][alpha-a+1]v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1), Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Let a= N-1 and alpha'=2a-alpha. Then x'=q^(-2)x^(-1), M'=M^(-1), theta_(alpha')=theta_alpha, theta_alpha=q^((alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2). (1.1) The conclusion is the exact state identity F_N(M)=F_N(M^(-1)), N_N(M)=N_N(M^(-1)). (1.2) Here N_N is the full modified-trace period. The evenness already proved in [the meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) therefore also gives F_N(Y)=F_N(Y^(-1)). The shift in x in (1.1) is essential; unshifted inversion of x is not the statement. ### A generator proof of the turnover Define the Chevalley algebra involution chi(E)=F, chi(F)=E, chi(K)=K^(-1), chi(H)=-H. The displayed coproduct and antipodes S(E)=-E K^(-1), S(F)=-K F give directly, on every generator, Delta chi=(chi tensor chi)Delta^op, chi S=S^(-1)chi, chi(K^(1-N))=K^(N-1). (1.3) For the actual finite universal R, termwise substitution gives (chi tensor chi)(R)=R_21. (1.4) Indeed its Cartan q^(H tensor H/2) is unchanged, and each E^k tensor F^k becomes F^k tensor E^k, with the same coefficient. This also checks inverse crossings. Pullback by chi reverses tensor order; with the ordinary flip as tensor-order map, (1.4) is precisely the positive-crossing identity for turning the diagram through pi about its vertical axis. For clarity, this turnover includes the cups and caps. Right duals use the action through S. Equation chi S=S^(-1)chi identifies the pulled-back right dual with the left dual of the pulled-back module. The evaluation f(v) and coevaluation sum_i v_i tensor v_i^* then become the left evaluation and coevaluation after reversing tensor order. In the common right-dual presentation, the left closing maps are evaluation with the pivot and coevaluation with its inverse. The last identity in (1.3) therefore sends the closing matrix g to g^(-1), exactly as the spatial turnover does. The zigzag contractions remain identity maps. Equation (1.1) checks the twist on the color; the balancing identity extends that check to its tensor products. Consequently the turnover identity holds for each crossing, inverse crossing, cup, cap and twist, and hence for their compositions. This is a generator proof for the actual ribbon-tangle evaluation. A rotation of the marked framed knot is an ambient isotopy. If the boundary ribbon frame is moved by the rotation, it conjugates the cut endomorphism by the same endpoint map on both sides; that has no effect on its scalar. No knot-invertibility assumption is involved. Thus the reduced knot scalar is unchanged by replacing its color by its Chevalley pullback. Here is the explicit identification of that color, including all normalizations. In the Chevalley pullback of V_alpha set w_b=d_b v_(N-1-b), d_0=1, d_b=product_(s=1)^b [s][alpha'-s+1]. (1.5) For generic alpha these are a basis. The root identities [N-s]=[s] and [z-N]=-[z] give [b][alpha'-b+1]=[N-b][alpha-(N-b)+1]. Substitution now proves E_chi w_b=[b][alpha'-b+1]w_(b-1), F_chi w_b=w_(b+1), K_chi w_b=q^(alpha'-2b)w_b, H_chi w_b=(alpha'-2b)w_b. So this color is exactly V_(alpha'). Combined with the turnover identities, it proves the first part of (1.2) at generic colors. The cut scalar is Laurent polynomial in x at zero framing, so the identity extends through all exceptional colors as a whole germ. One can also keep the stripped Cartan scalar throughout the calculation. If R_0,theta_0 denote the normalized crossing and residual twist used in the finite cut formulas, their reflected comparison has the same explicit multiplier h_N(x)=q^(-2)x^(2N-2), C R_(0,alpha') C^(-1)=h_N P R_(0,alpha) P, theta_(0,alpha')=h_N theta_(0,alpha). (1.6) Here C is the tensor square of the basis map in (1.5), and P flips the two factors; use h_N^(-1) for the inverse crossing. The product h_N^w is cancelled by the exact zero-framing correction h_N^(-w). Thus there is no unrecorded scalar or branch factor in (1.2). This cancellation is before any ideal-color specialization. Finally the full factor is d_N(M)=eta_N*(M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=i^(N+3). It is exactly invariant under M inversion. Hence the full equality in (1.2) also holds as a meromorphic whole-germ identity, including its poles, residues and the cancelled value d_N(1)=eta_N/N. ## 2. The actual normal-state ideal is reflected Put f=Y-1 and v_N(Y)=f F_N(Y). On rational meridian functions use R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), J=-Y R. Equation (1.2) gives, for the actual state at every level, J v_N=v_N. (2.1) On the formal quantum torus T Y=q^2Y T, write Q=q^2. Direct composition gives J^2=1 and the algebra involution jmath(B)=J B J, jmath(Y)=Y^(-1), jmath(T)=Q T^(-1). (2.2) Let I_v be the actual all-level annihilator ideal of v_N. It is nonzero and satisfies jmath(I_v)=I_v: apply J to its exact root equations and use (2.1). There is no assumed AJ theorem in this argument. This is the existing full ADO operator ideal in recorded conventions. Indeed, with U=Y^N at a root, u_N=F_N/S_N=f F_N/(U-1), N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)u_N(Y). The shift fixes U and has the character q^(N-1)=-q^(-1) on M^(N-1). Thus I_v=I_u, and it is obtained from the full literature ideal by that explicit character twist. It also equals the fixed rational gauge f I_F f^(-1). These statements retain all actual period factors; they do not algebraize v_N as a function of q. ## 3. Primitive minimality forces unitary monomial reciprocity Over C(q,Y)[T^(+/-1)] choose the actual least-order operator B, with support 0,...,d. Clear its rational denominators and remove the common coefficient content, recording those operations. Then B=sum_(j=0)^d b_j(q,Y)T^j, b_j in A=C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)], gcd_A(b_0,...,b_d)=1, b_0*b_d!=0. (3.1) This primitive representative is unique up to C^* q^r Y^s. The state lattice remains the actual one from v_N and the full formula in Section 2, rather than a newly chosen companion lattice. Since the ideal is reflected, T^d jmath(B) is another actual order-d operator. Minimality gives B=h(q,Y)T^d jmath(B). (3.2) Its coefficient list is Q^j b_j(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1)), in reversed order. It is primitive because this substitution is an automorphism of the Laurent UFD and each Q^j is a unit. Comparing the valuations at every irreducible of A in the two primitive lists forces h to be a unit: h=c_0 q^a Y^b, c_0 in C^*. The reflection is involutive, but the degree-restoring map S_d(B)=T^d jmath(B) satisfies S_d^2(B)=Q^d B. Applying it twice to (3.2) gives h(q,Y)h(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))*Q^d=1. Hence c_0=epsilon in {1,-1} and a=d(b-1). Multiplying (3.2) by J on the right therefore yields the exact intertwiner B J=J' B, J'=c(q,Y)T^d R, c(q,Y)=sigma*q^(dm)*Y^m, sigma in {1,-1}, m in Z. (3.3) Here m=b+1 and sigma=-epsilon. In particular c(q,Y)c(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))=1, |c(q,Y)|=1 when |q|=|Y|=1. (3.4) Thus the two root-fiber reflections are unitary involutions. The primitive minimal operator of the actual normal state automatically has exactly the reciprocity required by the preceding period note. This is uniform for every knot. It does not require primeness, alternatingness, a prescribed coefficient ordering, or a conjectured classical symbol. The original half-root q is retained: q^(dm) must not be replaced by a guessed integer power of Q. Primitivity also makes its q=1 symbol B_cl nonzero: otherwise every coefficient would have the common factor q-1. Specializing (3.3) gives the balanced polynomial identity B_cl(Y,L)=-sigma*Y^(m-1)*L^d*B_cl(Y^(-1),L^(-1)). This is a proved symmetry of the actual classical symbol. Its geometric A-component still needs a separate survival theorem. ## 4. The Weyl sector of the normal source is now automatic For this B, choose the actual F-annihilator P=B*f. It is an operator identity, with right factor f retained. This construction does not assert that every primitive reduced-state annihilator has that factor; the necessary positive-growth test in [the normal-period note](peripheral_normal_period.md) still concerns each such annihilator separately. On the central fiber U=1 write B_N(t)=B_0+t B_1+..., t=U-1, using the fixed roots Y_r(t)=Q_N^r(1+t)^(1/N). The actual vector v_N(t) has (v_0)_r=(Q_N^r-1)C_r(q_N), (v_0)_0=0, B_0 v_1=-B_1 v_0, K_N=N*(v_1)_0. (4.1) The state symmetry proves J v_0=v_0 at every level, including any level with K_N=0 and without a rank-one assumption. Inversion sends t to -t+O(t^2), while the derivative of J(t) is J/N. Differentiating (3.3) and applying it to v_0 gives exactly J' B_1 v_0=-B_1 v_0. (4.2) The complete evaluation vector e_0 has J-parity -1. Thus both the source and the desired functional live in the -1 sectors. The unwanted symmetry sector has zero overlap in this pairing. Let B_- be B_0 restricted from the -1 domain to the -1 range. It suffices that B_- be injective; surjectivity onto the entire range sector is unnecessary. The actual derivative guarantees that the source is in its image. Then its left inverse, or its Moore--Penrose inverse, gives K_N=-N e_0^* B_-^+ B_1 v_0. (4.3) Extra +1 kernel vectors do not change the complete value. More generally the value is unique whenever e_0 annihilates the kernel of B_-, even if that restriction is not injective. Those root-fiber conditions remain to prove for a broad class of actual operators. The bounded source estimates from the preceding note apply: ||B_1||=O(1/N), ||v_0||=O(sqrt(N)D_N). Consequently the exponential part must come from the specified inverse pairing, with its actual source overlap. Reciprocity alone supplies neither its inverse norm nor a nonzero geometric contribution. ## 5. The metric period is independent of primitive generator units Another primitive minimal generator is B'=u B with u=c_0 q^a Y^b. At the root, let D_u be its diagonal multiplication matrix on the orbit. It is |c_0| times a unitary matrix. Differentiation gives B_0'=D_u B_0, B_1'v_0=D_u B_1v_0, because the extra derivative of u multiplies B_0 v_0=0. Thus the normal equation and its complete period are unchanged. The range reflection is conjugated by D_u, so its Weyl-sector norm is changed only by the fixed scalar |c_0|. The positive exponential rate and the exact pairing (4.3) are therefore well defined for the primitive minimal operator, with the marked actual lattice. This does not license dropping a nonunit meridian factor. Such a factor is outside the remaining generator ambiguity and its zeros, poles, state gauge and normal jets must be kept as before. The ambient relation J T J=Q T^(-1) also gives, with the exact ADO character kappa=-q^(-1), J(kappa*T)J=(kappa*T)^(-1), (kappa*T)^N=(-1)^(N-1). (5.1) The even-level sign is part of the descended data. This concerns the ambient orbit module, not an assertion that the scalar solution line is invariant under T. ## 6. The bounded polar source is a finite sine transform The actual symmetry also proves the ordinary-color identity C_(N-j)(q_N)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. (6.1) In the notation of [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md), write a_r=[Y^r]p_N for the Taylor coefficients of its proper polar function at zero. Pair j with N-j in its already proved formula. With theta_j=pi*j/N this gives exactly a_r=-(2/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N) sin((2r-1)theta_j)sin(theta_j). Define the usual real sine matrix S_(a,j)=sqrt(2/N)sin(pi*a*j/N). For 1<=a,j<N, its rows are orthonormal: expand the sine products as differences of cosines and sum the two finite geometric series. Integer row labels outside that interval are zero or signed copies of these rows. Thus a_r=-sum_j S_(2r-1,j)S_(1,j)C_j(q_N), |a_r|<=D_N, r>=0. (6.2) The bound follows either from the operator norm of S diag(C_j)S^t, or by Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular a_0=sum_j S_(1,j)^2 C_j(q_N), sum_j S_(1,j)^2=1. Therefore the fixed Laurent-window source of the regular period is a finite linear combination of these explicit sine moments, with coefficients from the chosen fixed operator. No surgery or TQFT comparison theorem is being assumed for this description. It improves the earlier 2D_N bound and specifies its exact Weyl structure. It does not give a lower bound on the source's projection to a geometric singular vector or algebraize these moments in q. ## 7. Coverage, verification, and the remaining norm problem This symmetry has existing coverage: the abstract of [Martel--Willetts, 2112.15204](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15204) advertises the inherited ADO symmetry and orientation independence. Quantum-torus Weyl reciprocity is also covered in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). No unified-invariant, homological, AJ or asymptotic proof from those sources is a premise here. The proofs above use the actual finite R, the pivotal pairings, primitive minimality and Laurent arithmetic. No novelty claim is made for Weyl symmetry or balanced operators. [The independent audit](../experiments/audit_actual_weyl_descent.py) checks 27 local Chevalley comparisons through level 15, including the ideal color; 63 actual cut turnovers at generic meridians; 25 complete Laurent-state reflections, with their ordinary-color and sine-source identities; 60 monomial-reciprocity cases; and sine orthogonality at nine even/composite/odd levels. These exact finite-field checks validate the uniform formulas, rather than proving their scope by enumeration. Results are in [the output](../experiments/actual_weyl_descent_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_actual_weyl_descent.py The [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) already fixes the marked geometric Bloch action and its volume norm on the actual classical critical branch. This note now makes the quantum Weyl descent uniform for the actual knot state and its primitive minimal normal operator. What remains is the root-fiber solvability and inverse-pairing norm in (4.3), together with survival of the geometric factor in the actual operator. No equality D_N=A_K or volume conjecture is inferred. The subsequent [peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) also derives these boundary conventions directly from adjacent-color fusion and heterogeneous crossings. In the odd normal state w_N=(M-M^(-1))F_N, the fundamental parallel acts as -(T+T^(-1)); in v_N=M*w_N it acts as kappa*T+kappa^(-1)T^(-1), with the same kappa=-q^(-1). At M=1 the fusion has an explicitly retained square-zero Casimir residue with normalized pivotal trace. This provides exact quantum boundary data, while the geometric source and norm comparison above remain unproved. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre proof](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) extends the quadratic descent to the actual branch-point lattice. Explicit units U^(1/(2N)) and U^(m/(2N)) linearize both involutions; the invariant lattice over s=((U-1)/(U+1))^2 retains the first negative coefficient as a special-fibre coordinate. The full ADO period is (eta_N/2)e_0^*b_0 there. The half-root in (3.3) also determines the exact sector dimensions, exposing signatures for which the optional injectivity condition cannot hold. This algebraic evaluation supplies no additional volume-growth theorem.

title: Whole-domain large Fourier charges: exact paired currents and a vanishing-rate operator tail
status: Whole-domain operator tail; mixed environment kept
text: # Whole-domain large Fourier charges: exact paired currents and a vanishing-rate operator tail , 31 October 2026. This concerns the actual fixed-root operator coupons and their original marked contraction. It does not split an infinite charge series at an artificial real cutoff. Twists are fixed before $N$. The resulting all-far-sector bound is proved; a partial-far mixed-source estimate is isolated explicitly in Section 5. ## 1. Original one-port Fourier coupons Put $d=N-1$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, $\Omega$ equal to the original pair Casimir, $\chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2$ and $V_N(z)=\chi_N(z)(z-\Omega)^{-1}$, interpreted as its degree-$d$ polynomial. Work in the original balanced physical basis used by the [full endpoint-resolvent theorem](actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.md), including its high-total adapter. All physical degrees form its orthogonal direct sum. For a fixed integer $n$ define $$ \begin{aligned} B_{N,n}(\delta)&=\sin(2\pi\delta)e^{\pi i nN\delta^2}V_N(-2\cos(2\pi\delta)),\\ J_{N,n,\ell}&=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B_{N,n}(\delta)e^{2\pi i\ell N\delta}\,d\delta,\\ F_{N,n,\ell}&=q^{nd^2/4}(-i)\ell(-1)^{(N+1)\ell}J_{N,n,\ell}. \end{aligned} $$ The [exact full-Hermite formula](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md) gives $$ R^n=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}F_{N,n,\ell}.\tag{1} $$ The series is absolutely convergent for each fixed $N,n$. Its endpoint regularity is that of the WHOLE interval. Since $B$ is odd, $J_{-\ell}=-J_\ell$; therefore $F_{-\ell}=F_\ell$, including the original parity character. There is no $\ell=0$ term. For integer $M\geq1$ put $$ T_{N,n;M}=\sum_{|\ell|>M}F_{N,n,\ell}.\tag{2} $$ This is a literal operator in the actual Casimir quotient, not an auxiliary scalar source or a truncated physical head sum. ## 2. Exact contour shift and the paired endpoint current For positive $\ell$ shift the WHOLE interval vertically UP to height $\tau>0$. The integrand is entire. If $H_{N,n,\ell;\tau}$ denotes the upper horizontal integral, the two actual side currents give $$ \begin{aligned} J_{N,n,\ell}={}&H_{N,n,\ell;\tau}\\ &-i(-1)^{N\ell}\int_0^\tau e^{-2\pi\ell Nv} \left[B_{N,n}\!\left(\tfrac12+iv\right)-B_{N,n}\!\left(-\tfrac12+iv\right)\right]dv. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ Both endpoints have the SAME spectral value $z(v)=2\cosh(2\pi v)$. Their sine values are $-i\sinh(2\pi v)$, whereas the two Gaussian values are $e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}e^{\mp\pi nNv}$. Consequently EXACTLY $$ B\!\left(\tfrac12+iv\right)-B\!\left(-\tfrac12+iv\right) =2i\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v)).\tag{4} $$ In particular the paired current vanishes to order TWO at $v=0$. The second factor is a hyperbolic sine, not a bounded oscillatory sine. Its growth $e^{\pi|n|Nv}$ is kept in every estimate. Substitution in (3) gives the plus-sign version $$ J=H+2(-1)^{N\ell}\int_0^\tau e^{-2\pi\ell Nv} \sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))\,dv.\tag{5} $$ Thus multiplication by the original Fourier character in $F$ leaves the vertical character $(-1)^\ell$, not a level-dependent endpoint sign. No individual vertical side is set to zero. Formula (3) is an equality before any summation or norm bound. ## 3. Uniform original operator bound for the tail There are absolute $\tau_0>0$ and constants $c,C,C_0$ such that the following holds for every fixed $n$, $0<\tau\leq\tau_0$ and integer $M$ with $$ D=M-\frac{|n|}{2}-1\geq1. $$ After increasing the constants when needed, $$ \begin{aligned} \|T_{N,n;M}\|\leq{}&C_{n,\tau}N^Ce^{C(\log N)^2} \Bigl\{(M+1)e^{-N(2\pi\tau D-C_0)}\\ &\qquad+\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right]e^{N\varepsilon(D)}\Bigr\},\\ \varepsilon(D)&=Ce^{-cD}\longrightarrow0\quad(D\longrightarrow\infty). \end{aligned}\tag{6} $$ Only fixed-$n$ uniformity in $N$ is asserted. In particular, for every $\eta>0$ there is $L_\eta$, independent of $n$, such that choosing $$ M\geq\frac{|n|}{2}+1+L_\eta, $$ (with an integer ceiling) makes $$ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|T_{N,n;M}\|\leq\eta.\tag{7} $$ The constants multiplying (6) may depend on the fixed $n$. The cutoff in (7) has the natural Gaussian threshold $|n|/2$ and an additional fixed allowance. This is a bound for the original FULL-V Fourier coupon, including semisimple data. Proof of the horizontal part. In the original balanced root basis $\|F\|,\|\mathcal E\|\leq2$ and $K$ is unitary. The literal coproduct gives $\|F_{\mathrm{tot}}\|,\|\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}}\|\leq4$, hence $\|\Omega\|\leq18$ on the ENTIRE physical tensor product. This includes high totals without changing the norm by a basis adapter. Equivalently the actual blocks have fixed bandwidth and uniformly bounded entries. The exact divided-Chebyshev identity is $$ V_N(z)=U_{N-1}(\Omega/2)+2\sum_{h=1}^{N-1}T_{N-h}(z/2)U_{h-1}(\Omega/2). $$ The scalar recurrences imply $\|U_j(\Omega/2)\|\leq C_*^{j+1}$ for an absolute $C_*>1$. On $\delta=x+i\tau$, $|x|\leq1/2$, $$ |T_k(-\cos(2\pi\delta))|\leq e^{2\pi k\tau}. $$ Thus $\|V_N(-2\cos(2\pi\delta))\|\leq CN e^{N(C_0+2\pi\tau)}$ for a fixed $C_0$. The sine is bounded, the Gaussian modulus is at most $e^{\pi|n|N\tau}$, and the Fourier modulus is $e^{-2\pi\ell N\tau}$. The resulting geometric sum of $\ell$ times horizontal integrals is bounded by the first term of (6), after a harmless adjustment from $M+1$ to $M$. It introduces no false coefficientwise real-spectral bound. Proof of the vertical part. Use the already proved [original closing-region estimate](actual_casimir_closing_region_bound.md) on the right real ray, with $r=2\cosh(2\pi v)-2$: $$ \|(2\cosh(2\pi v)-\Omega)^{-1}\| \leq CN^3e^{CNf(r)+C(\log N)^2},\qquad f(r)=\sqrt r\log(2+1/r). $$ It applies at $v=0$ by the polynomial endpoint bound as well. Since $\chi_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))=2\cosh(2\pi Nv)+2$, and $r$ is comparable to $v^2$, $$ \|V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))\| \leq CN^3\exp\!\left\{N\left[2\pi v+Cv\log(C/v)\right]+C(\log N)^2\right\}.\tag{8} $$ All constants are uniform for $0\leq v\leq\tau_0$, and $v\log(C/v)=0$ at $v=0$. Also $$ |\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)|\leq C|n|Nv^2e^{\pi|n|Nv}. $$ For $D_\ell=\ell-|n|/2-1$, (5) therefore gives, up to polynomial factors, $$ |n|N^4\ell e^{C(\log N)^2}\int_0^\tau v^2 \exp\!\left\{N\left[-2\pi D_\ell v+Cv\log(C/v)\right]\right\}dv.\tag{9} $$ Reserve half the damping for the integral. Elementary one-variable optimization yields $$ \sup_{v\geq0}\left[Cv\log(C/v)-\pi Dv\right] \leq C'e^{-cD}=\varepsilon(D). $$ Since $D_\ell\geq D$, the remaining integral is at most $$ e^{N\varepsilon(D)}\int_0^\infty v^2e^{-\pi ND_\ell v}\,dv =\frac{2e^{N\varepsilon(D)}}{(\pi ND_\ell)^3}. $$ Finally $$ \sum_{\ell>M}\frac{\ell}{D_\ell^3} \leq C\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right].\tag{10} $$ This proves (6), with both charge signs included using their exact symmetry. The bound is an ABSOLUTE summation of paired whole-domain currents. It never uses convergence of an infinite sharp-cube series. Choose $D$ so $2\pi\tau D-C_0>0$ and $\varepsilon(D)<\eta$ to obtain (7). The $n=0$ case has zero vertical current; its finite-band Fourier formula in fact has no charges $|\ell|>1$, consistent with this proof. ## 4. A genuine source consequence when ALL ports are far Keep the original diagram order, the original physical cups/caps and its single mark. Replacing every $R_i^{n_i}$ by $T_{N,n_i;M_i}$ gives EXACTLY the subseries of the original whole-domain Fourier period with $|\ell_i|>M_i$ for EVERY port. Finite-$N$ absolute convergence and multilinearity justify this identity; physical coupons are never commuted. Call this marked contraction $Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}$. In the same balanced physical basis, the finitely many actual turns, closures and single marked cap have polynomial operator/Euclidean norms in $N$. Their entries are the original $N$ times unit-phase cup, $N^{-1}$ ordinary cap and $N^{-2}$ marked cap. More explicitly, cups and ordinary caps have $a+b=d$; the marked cap $m_{ab}=x^b/N^2$ is UNRESTRICTED. Their Euclidean norms are respectively $N^{3/2}$, $N^{-1/2}$ and $N^{-1}$, and the retained right-turn pivots are unit phases. The number of wires and contractions is fixed by the diagram. Hence $$ |Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}|\leq\operatorname{poly}_D(N)\prod_i\|T_{N,n_i;M_i}\|, \qquad\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log|Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}|\leq\sum_i\varepsilon(D_i).\tag{11} $$ once each horizontal term has been made exponentially decreasing. This is an actual shared-source estimate, not a replacement of its coefficient by arbitrary face radii. All $n_i$ are fixed before $N$. The [geometric local unit theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) gives $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}\geq\Phi_D/2$ for ALL independently sufficiently long fixed twists, after increasing a threshold depending only on the original diagram. Choose fixed $D_i$ so $\sum_i\varepsilon(D_i)<\Phi_D/4$ and all horizontal exponents in (6) are negative. These $D_i$ depend on the fixed diagram, not on ratios or magnitudes of the long slopes. The actual cutoffs can therefore be chosen as $M_i=\lceil|n_i|/2+1+D_i\rceil$. Then (11) gives a uniform strict RATE gap from the proved local contribution throughout that general long-filling class. Prefactor and relative-error constants may still depend on the fixed twists; no joint growing-twist/level limit follows. This does not cover the much larger UNION of sectors in which only one or some charges are far. ## 5. Partial far subsets: the exact missing mixed-source estimate Let $\mathcal E_{D,S,N}$ be the literal original marked exterior functional with $R_j^{n_j}$ retained, in their original order, on every $j$ outside a nonempty set $S$. Define its norm on the remaining tensor product of operator spaces by $$ \|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\|= \sup_{\substack{\|A_i\|\leq1\\ i\in S}} \left|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}A_i\right)\right|. $$ Then the immediate correct bound for that subset is $$ \left|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}T_i\right)\right| \leq\|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\|\prod_{i\in S}\|T_i\|.\tag{12} $$ There is no established reason for the first factor to have rate less than $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}$. The remaining signed $R$ powers are NOT uniformly unitary in this basis. Their individual exponential norm bounds only supply a crude upper rate depending on the retained twists. Equation (7) alone therefore cannot remove a partial-far sector. The exact finite inclusion-exclusion identity for the union is $$ Z_{\mathrm{full}}-Z_{\mathrm{all\,low}} =\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathrm{ports}}(-1)^{|S|+1} \mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}T_i\right).\tag{13} $$ It retains the original full $R$ powers on the complement of $S$, rather than replacing them by an uncontrolled collection of infinitely many spectator charge pieces. A direct sufficient new input would be a strict bound on these actual mixed exteriors, or a narrower estimate on the paired-current families $$ \mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}V_i(2\cosh(2\pi v_i))\right), \qquad0\leq v_i\leq\tau.\tag{14} $$ with a rate strictly below $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}$ as $v$ tends to zero, uniformly on a small fixed closing box, including simultaneous endpoint subsets. Every sine, Gaussian and charge character in (4)-(5) would then remain explicit and summably controlled. Horizontal pieces can be made as small as needed by increasing the fixed charge cutoffs, using a crude finite exponential norm for the fixed remaining coupons. The difficult input is thus the SHARED endpoint environment in (14), not a missing local +2 resolvent estimate. Neither the positive Fejer endpoint theorem at $\sigma=-2$ nor the noncross local gap proves (14) at $\sigma=+2$ with arbitrary remaining $R$ powers. Nor does a local norm estimate prove the needed shared rate. This distinction is preserved in (11)-(14). No full invariant or partial-far complement theorem is claimed here. ## Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_domain_large_charge_tail.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_whole_domain_large_charge_tail_results.json) check paired endpoint entries, whole-interval contour identities and charge-sign identities from the physical blocks. These are finite normalization checks, not proofs of an asymptotic rate or a mixed-source gap.

title: The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system

text: # The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system 30 October 2026. The original four-component circle system admits a polynomial source gauge that preserves its first component. Tensoring it on the actual shared face variables gives an exact whole-source system coupling only finitely shifted face coefficients. The original finite support and a source-selected fold adapter determine its polynomial solution. Its reduced characteristic is identified algebraically with the existing ORDERED local character transport. This is a system for the complete-image external-color core. It does not erase its ordinary small-color subsets, eliminate the coefficient family to a scalar A-polynomial, or establish a complex asymptotic of its period. ## 1. A polynomial four-component source gauge Use N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and the actual polynomial Z_j(x,b,y), 0<=j<=d, of the [fixed-fold source theorem](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md), equation(10). Write Z_-1=0 and Delta_j=(x-Q^j y)(x-Q^(-j)y), Pcal_j=P_d(x,y)/product_(r=1)^j Delta_r, P_d(x,y)=product_(r=1)^d(x-Q^r y). The rational presentation of Pcal_j is used only to define the following source; its canceled polynomial expressions are proved below. Retain omega_j=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)], U_j=omega_j^epsilon Pcal_j (Z_j^b Z_j^c, Z_j^b Z_(j-1)^c, Z_(j-1)^b Z_j^c, Delta_j Z_(j-1)^b Z_(j-1)^c)^T. (1) Here the superscript b or c indicates the middle face, not a power. The first component is precisely the original reflected complete-circle polynomial omega_j^epsilon B_ext,j. In the notation of the fixed-fold note, U_j=G_j V_j with G_j=diag(1,1,1,Delta_j). ALL FOUR components of (1) are polynomials in x,b,c,y. Below the fold, Pcal_j is the ordinary forced polynomial, so the claim is immediate. Above the fold put r=d-j and s=d-2r. The actual large-H reflection gives Z_j=P_s Z_r, Pcal_j=P_s^-1. For s>=2, Z_(j-1)=P_(s-2) Z_(r+1), so the second and third components reduce respectively to P_(s-2) Z_r^b Z_(r+1)^c and P_(s-2) Z_(r+1)^b Z_r^c. At the even first bridge s=1, they instead reduce to Z_M^b Z_M^c, where M=floor(d/2). Finally (U_j)_4=omega_j^epsilon B_ext,(j-1), j>=1, because Delta_j Pcal_j=Pcal_(j-1). It is zero at j=0. This proves polynomiality, including zero-face evaluations, without choosing a Laurent expansion at a pole. The component degrees are d,d-1,d-1,d. The gauge G is not invertible on Delta_j=0; no such divisor is discarded. Put theta=pi/N and retain the actual finite coefficients u_j=cos((j-1)theta)sin(j theta), v_j^b=sin((2j-1)theta)[x+y+2b cos(j theta)cos((j-1)theta)], barw_j=sin((j-1)theta)cos(j theta), w_j=barw_j Delta_(j-1), L_j=u_j^2 Delta_j, r_j=(-Q^j)^epsilon. The exact polynomial-gauge recurrence is L_j U_j=r_j N_j U_(j-1), (2) N_j= [v_j^b v_j^c, -v_j^b w_j, -w_j v_j^c, barw_j^2 Delta_(j-1)] [u_j v_j^b, 0, -u_j w_j, 0] [u_j v_j^c, -u_j w_j, 0, 0] [Delta_j u_j^2,0, 0, 0]. Indeed N_j=G_j M_j G_(j-1)^-1 on the localized field. Its only apparent denominator is w_j^2/Delta_(j-1), and it cancels exactly as displayed. Thus (2) is polynomial and extends across that divisor. The original finite sequence is zero outside 0,...,d. The equations at j=0 and j=N remain true: the first uses u_0=0 and U_-1=0; the last uses the two actual terminal scalar relations and u_N=0. There is no periodic closing arrow or omitted endpoint current. Every coefficient of (2) is Laurent in Q^j. Its face degree is at most three. If mathcal U(z)=sum_(j=0)^d U_j z^j and Theta f(z)=f(Qz), then exactly [L(Theta)-z(-Q Theta)^epsilon N(Q Theta)]mathcal U(z)=0. (3) The Laurent Theta powers lie between -5 and5; the z-degree is at most1. These bounds are independent of N. The first component is unchanged from the original finite core. For its full Fourier gauge S(chi)=exp(pi i d chi)mathcal U(exp(-2pi i chi)), retain exactly exp(pi i d chi)Theta mathcal U=q^d S(chi-1/N). (4) ## 2. The original source selects the fold crossing This section concerns the finite source, not a choice of formal WKB solution. Work over the face coefficient field localized at the Delta_j that occur, and put M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M and h=M+s0+1=d-M+1. The known initial vector is U_0=omega_0^epsilon P_d(x,y)(1,0,0,0)^T. Let R4 reverse the four components. The ACTUAL source has the exact polynomial fold adapter U_h=q^((s0+1)epsilon) R4 U_M. (5) A direct proof uses h=d-(M-1) and h-1=d-M in the large-H reflection. The first and fourth components exchange because B_ext,(d-j)=B_ext,j; the two cross products exchange with their forced factors. Finally Delta_h=Delta_M and omega_h/omega_M=q^(s0+1). These give every component of (5), including the even bridge s0=1. No new square root is required. The adapter is a unit phase times a permutation. Near the actual fold Delta_M=(x+y)^2-4xy sin^2((s0+1)pi/(2N)) is uniformly positive on the stated positive radius compact. The adapter advances one step at odd levels and TWO at even levels. To see why this matters, write N=2H, M=H-1. At j=H the leading coefficient is nonzero and the transfer has rank one: U_H=(1,A^-1,A^-1,1)^T (U_(H-1))_1, A=x+y. (6) At j=H+1 its leading coefficient is zero, while N_(H+1) has just one nonzero row, sin^2(theta)(A^2,-A^3,-A^3,A^2). It annihilates (6), so this row places no condition on U_(H+1). An invertible analytic gauge cannot change this rank loss. For generic face data and every even N>=4, the finite system (2), with zero support outside 0,...,d and prescribed U_0, therefore has a THREE-dimensional affine freedom whenever it has a solution. States through U_H are determined. The new U_(H+1) is an arbitrary four-vector; all later transfers through d are invertible. The terminal row at N imposes one nonzero condition. The determinant of N_j is [Delta_j/Delta_(j-1)](u_j w_j)^4, so these assertions retain the relevant factors. At odd N, u_j never vanishes inside 1,...,d, and the prescribed U_0 already determines every state. The source adapter (5) fixes the even free vector and restores uniqueness. Its compatibility with the terminal equation is provided by the literal Newton source and its reflection. This is not a claim of three different original sources: the unsupplemented operator has extra solutions, while its specified source data fixes one. ## 3. Exact whole-source coefficient equations Use the actual labeled planar source graph. Each circle i has its literal four incident faces (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i), with all repeated or shared face names identified. Tensor the local polynomial vectors: W(z_1,...,z_R;L)=tensor_(i=1)^R mathcal U_i(z_i;L). It has 4^R components and is polynomial in EVERY face variable. For any nonnegative exponent vector n, define the finite coefficient family C_n(z)=[product_f L_f^(n_f)] W(z;L), (7) and set it to zero if some n_f<0. The component indexed by alpha has face degree dR-m(alpha), where m counts its local second/third indices. Thus the entire family is finite. It is not a choice of rational-series expansion or a coefficient integral through newly introduced divisors. Let S_i be the operator (3) acting on tensor factor i. Expand its actual face-polynomial coefficients as S_i=sum_nu L^nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i). All nu are nonnegative and |nu|<=3. Exact coefficient extraction gives sum_nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i) C_(n-nu)(z)=0, i=1,...,R, for every n. (8) These are the sought finite FACE SHIFTS. No scalar equation for only one selected coefficient is inferred. The operators commute before extraction: they act on separate external registers and separate tensor factors, while their shared face multiplications commute. The coupled coefficient equations inherit this compatibility. The local initial vectors and adapters (5) tensor to give the actual finite solution. Over the localized face field, uniqueness follows by advancing each register through its regular rows and its specified fold jump; the constructions in different registers commute. Polynomiality then follows from (1), not from an assertion about arbitrary operator solutions. The adapters can equally be recorded coefficientwise in (7). Let u,v be the two original marked faces and define n* by n*_u=n*_v=0, n*_f=d for every other face f. For the all-first tensor component, the exact original entire complete core is F_N(h)=chi_(D,N) N^R exp[pi i d sum_i h_i/N] (C_(n*))(exp(-2pi i h_1/N),...,exp(-2pi i h_R/N))_(1,...,1). (9) This follows from the source-exact reflected Fourier pairing and the original marked face-coefficient theorem. It retains the common twist phase, N^R measure, original mark and finite parity. The two marked faces are set to zero only AFTER polynomial extraction. Equation (9) is the empty subset in the external reflection formula; ordinary-color subsets are not represented by deleting them from this statement. ## 4. The principal characteristic is the actual ordered character map There is an exact algebraic identification with [the original local critical-character map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Use its variables T,U,V,J and internal roots Z,W. On a regular chart, P(X,Y)=T(J-Y)^2(X-Y)+(Y-1)^2(TY-XJ)=0. (10) The source convention has b incoming and c outgoing. Thus the OLD ordered map has T=x/y, U=-x/c at the output and V=-x/b at the input. Put r=(J+1)^2/(4J), A=x+y, and D=A^2-4xy r, B_b=A+2br, B_c=A+2cr, e_out(Z)=-y Z(J-1)^2(TZ-UJ)/[J U(J-Z)^2], e_in(W)=-y W(J-1)^2(TW-VJ)/[J V(J-W)^2]. (11) Then (10) implies exactly e_out^2-2B_c e_out+D=0, e_in^2-2B_b e_in+D=0. (12) Here is a finite polynomial certificate. By homogeneity set y=1, x=T. For one generic triangle with middle face z=-T/X, write e=-Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ)/[J X(J-Z)^2] and B_z=T+1+2zr. Then e^2-2B_z e+D=-P(X,Z) K(X,Z)/[J X^2(J-Z)^4], K=J^3 X(J-T) +[JT(1-J^2)+2J^2X(T-1)]Z +[X(1-JT)+2T(J-1)]Z^2. Conversely the resultant of P(X,Z) and J X(J-Z)^2 e+Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ) is J^4 X^2(J-1)^4(T-X)^2 (e^2-2B_z e+D). Thus, away from the displayed degeneracies and the quadratic discriminant, the two local roots correspond to the two continuant roots. This is an elimination of the ACTUAL critical equation. The same character map's ordered centralizer eigenratio is R0=ZW(J-1)^4(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ) /[JUV(J-Z)^2(J-W)^2(T-J)(TJ-1)]. Since D=y^2(T-J)(T-J^-1), its exact factorization is R0=e_out e_in/D. (13) It is therefore the lambda in the reduced continuant quartic D(lambda^4+1)-4B_bB_c(lambda^3+lambda) +(4B_b^2+4B_c^2-2D)lambda^2=0. (14) The polynomial gauge changes no full principal determinant: with u=(1/2)sin(2pi mu), J=exp(2pi i mu), the retained determinant is u^8 D^3 Pquartic(z(-J)^epsilon), (15) where Pquartic is the left side of (14). This polynomial identity follows by similarity where D!=0 and hence extends as a polynomial; it does not license canceling u or D on their zero strata. The finite Fourier equation has the stationary relation z(-J)^epsilon lambda=1. With z=exp(-2pi i chi), equations(13)--(15) give precisely R0(-J)^epsilon=exp(2pi i chi)=M_aux^-2. (16) This is the marked meridian relation of the original threading word, including its half-twist shear and inverse eigenratio, rather than a new normalization of the trace curve. The magnetic and total momenta agree as well. For one original H Newton summand, let its two raw heads be X,Y with XY=T and internal root Z. Differentiating the two literal Newton products, at their stationary root, gives the exponentiated logarithmic forces p1=Z(X-1)/(X-Z), p2=JZ(Y-1)/(YZ-J). For example the first product contributes integral_0^kappa Log(X-exp(2pi i t))dt; exponentiating 2pi i times its logarithmic X derivative gives p1. The second product and its literal Y^k factor give p2. The retained white monomial q^(d i) contributes the additional minus sign in the fixed-total first-head momentum. Thus -p1/p2=(1-X)(TZ-XJ)/[J(X-Z)(T-X)], (16a) which is exactly the old magnetic Y(X,Z), with no Hermitian reversal. For the full circle, the original residual sine product contributes -(T-J)/(TJ-1) to the total-degree force; the monomial q^[d(R+S-sigma)] T^-a contributes -J^-1. Consequently e^(Theta_tau)=J^-1 (T-J)/(TJ-1) p2(U,Z)p2(V,W) =JZW(T-J)(T-U)(T-V)/[(TJ-1)(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ)]. (16b) Here each p2 uses its own second head T/U or T/V. These are the literal normalization factors from the source circle formula, not functions adjusted to fit the character equation. Equations(13), (16a),(16b) recover all three derivatives used by the original ordered-character theorem. Its typed incoming/output construction therefore preserves the entire ordered product P=BA and transports the two punctures by the same centralizer. The integer logarithmic marks are still required before turning these exponential equations into additive stationary equations. ## 5. Branch calibration and what has not been eliminated For positive regular face radii and mu=1/2-delta with small delta>0, the actual positive continuants select e_out=E_c(delta), e_in=E_b(delta), as in the fixed-real fold theorem. Equation(13) then selects the positive product branch. Put C=pi[sqrt(bA+xy)+sqrt(cA+xy)]/A. At delta=0, R0=1, J=-1, and (1/2) dR0/dJ=C/(2pi i). The derivative follows from dJ/ddelta=2pi i and d Log R0/ddelta=2C. In the original ordered map this is exactly the additive parabolic conjugator coefficient: the matrix transport is `I+[C/(2pi i)](P+I)`, not the identity merely because R0=1. With the retained half twist, its primitive cusp ratio is tau=1/[C/(2pi i)-epsilon/2]=2pi i/(C-pi i epsilon), agreeing with the independently marked rectangle calculation. Equations(10)--(16) hold first on the stated regular character chart. Their cleared polynomial relations have zero-face limits, but taking such limits can lose flag or branch information. The original source and the large-H adapters, rather than an arbitrary quartic root, specify those limits. In particular no new geometric branch is inferred merely from the quartic at u=0. In a prospective coefficient saddle, a face shift n->n-nu has multiplier L^nu, with L_f=exp(-partial_(n_f/N) action). The actual shared-face incidence in (8) is therefore retained. The Cauchy stationary equations for the original coefficient use its literal target n*, not independent triangle radii. Under the primitive face/head change of variables they are the original magnetic conservation/gluing equations wherever the full local character chart is regular. This last comparison is a stationary-equation identification, not a theorem that a solution is selected by the finite period. At the two marked zero faces one must retain the actual boundary limit and co-source. The equations do not eliminate the neighboring coefficient indices, prove a scalar A-polynomial for an arbitrary network, or identify every component of their characteristic variety with a geometric component. Nor do they prove a fixed complex external-color packet, its nonzero saddle coefficient, or the needed bounds for the nonempty small-color subsets. Their exact finite source solution, primitive normalization and local ordered-character interface are what is established here. Focused [exact source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system_results.json): It constructs 50 literal homogenized Newton polynomials and checks 300 canceled source components, 360 polynomial recurrence rows, 15 exact core Fourier pairings, 192 coupled rows with 27,254 shared-face coefficient equalities, and 12 marked tetrahedral-graph coefficient extractions. Seven symbolic certificates check the polynomial gauge and original ordered magnetic/total/channel character maps. The independently developed fold block uses 336 original Newton values, 48 source jumps, 2,208 system rows and 48 full finite-system rank checks through N=18 and both parities. The rank counts concern the explicitly localized operator field; finite fixtures do not assert a geometric certificate or an asymptotic theorem. The incoming-b/output-c convention and magnetic, total and channel characters are part of the regular-chart identity. It does not reconstruct a marked zero-face representation. The geometric-boundary and period qualifications in Section 5 remain part of the finite difference-system result.

title: Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain
text: # Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain 29 October 2026. The correlated six-head marked boundary Gram has POLYNOMIAL source cost on EVERY supported folded color cell, at both level parities. No fixed central corridor is required. The second-root- zero Racah terms do not need a uniform strict exponential gap: a global elementary sine-product inequality bounds every such term by the same action as a positive main term. All low/high partner branches, the original marked normal and every lower moment are retained. This controls the pointed algebraic Gram from the [actual six-pants boundary](actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). It does not identify its constructed reflection with a physical mirror, bound the physical change of frame or general recouplings, or prove a graph's sharp geometric energy/noncancellation. ## 1. The whole-support theorem Let N>=2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and take ANY 0<=l_1,l_2,l_3<=M, l_1+l_2+l_3>=d. (1) There is one paired axis for each 2l_i<d; let their number be r<=3. The actual regular source cell, complete-circle coordinates eta_i, original marked co-source lambda and nested-cup vector v_l are those of the proved boundary theorem. In particular m_I=lambda(eta_I v_l), tau_l=m_all=Z_N(l)/N^(3-r)>0, q_l(eta)=sum_I (m_(I^c)/tau_l)eta_I, q_l(0)=1, K_l=sum_I |coeff_I(q_l^(1/2))|^2. (2) There are absolute constants C,C0, independent of N and of ALL labels satisfying (1), such that max_I |m_I/tau_l|<=C0 N^C, 1<=K_l<=C0 N^C. (3) The exponent may be increased between the two estimates. Thus the actual source and dual costs of this prescribed Gram are exactly K_l and tau_l^2 K_l, with log K_l=O(log N)=o(N) uniformly on the whole support. The estimates include saturation faces, edges, corners, nearest paired neighbors and odd simple axes. Unsupported open source cells are not deleted. They lack the positive top moment in (2), so (3) is asserted precisely on (1). The theorem does not assert a polynomial norm for the embedding of this finite coordinate cell into the physical tensor product. ## 2. The original generic trace and all its normal factors The [proved generic source identity](actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md) and the genuine ordered physical trace give, for each unfolded ordinary triangle j=(a,b,c), the EXACT rational function T_j=(-1)^d product_i[2j_i+1] *[r_1]![r_2]![r_3]!/[J+1]! *product_i([j_i]!^2[d-j_i]!/[N+j_i]!) S_j^2, J=a+b+c, r_i=J-2j_i, S_j=sum_t (-1)^(d+t)[N+t]! /{[d+t-J]! product_i[t-j_i]![J-j_i-t]!}, max(j_i,J-d)<=t<=J-max(j_i). (4) Here [n] and [n]! are symmetric quantum integers and factorials at zeta=q(1-Z)^(1/(2N)), with the branch through q. These are the actual source functions, not a separately normalized 6j model. The unfolded choices are j_i=l_i or d-l_i on a paired axis, and the single l_i on a simple axis. With the original paired-circle unit ell_j(Z)=L_N(c_j(zeta))/Z, the physical moment formula is m_I=(-1)^d(q-q^(-1)) [Z^(r+1-|I|)] sum_unfolded Z^r T_j product_(i in I)ell_(j_i)(Z). (5) There are at most eight summands and the coefficient order is <=4. The original marked physical trace is exactly the one in (5). No ordinary quantum dimension is specialized to zero before this coefficient is extracted. Two elementary integer facts now hold on the ENTIRE supported domain. For every unfolded branch, d<=J<=2d, 0<=r_i<=d. (6) To verify them, increase a coordinate from l_i to d-l_i. The maximum J is 3d-sum l_i<=2d and the minimum is sum l_i>=d. For r_i, its maximum over the flips is 2d-sum l_i<=d and its minimum is sum l_i-2l_i>=d-2l_i>=0. In particular every unfolded branch is an ordinary triangle. Moreover EVERY one of the seven denominator factorial indices in S_j is less than N, for every true term. Indeed 0<=d+t-J<=d-max j_i<=d, 0<=t-j_i<=some other label<=d, 0<=J-j_i-t<=some other label<=d. (7) For example t<=j_i+j_k bounds t-j_i, and t>=j_k bounds J-j_i-t. No root denominator appears in any Racah summand. Its numerator contains [N] once for t<N and both [N],[2N] for t>=N; t<=2d<2N excludes a third zero. This is the only termwise change at the second band. ## 3. A uniform global profile, including the second-zero band Let L(t)=integral_0^t log|2sin(pi u)|du, extended periodically to R. Its period is 1 and L(-t)=-L(t). Define the EXACT half-step scaled colors a_i=(j_i+1/2)/N, S=sum a_i, x_i=S/2-a_i (i=1,2,3), x_4=1-S/2. Equations (6) imply 0<x_i<1/2 for all four i, sum_i x_i=1. (8) The half-step is useful: a high-partner replacement j_i->d-j_i is exactly a_i->1-a_i. It permutes the four x coordinates while replacing each by its complement 1/2-x. There is no O(1/N) error in this assertion. For instance flipping the first color sends (x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4) ->(1/2-x_4,1/2-x_3,1/2-x_2,1/2-x_1). (9) For a summand put s=(t+3/4)/N and v=s-S/2=(t-J/2)/N. Its three child pairs obey x_i+v=(t-j_i+1/4)/N>0, x_i-v=(J-j_i-t+1/4)/N>0, i<=3. (10) Also x_4+v=1-(J-t+3/4)/N is in (0,1). The fourth minus argument is x_4-v=1-s=(N-t-3/4)/N: it is positive for t<N and negative for t>=N, precisely the second-zero band. After removing its one or two root zeros, the absolute factorial summand has, up to polynomial factors, the profile H_x(v)=-sum_(i=1)^4 [L(x_i+v)+L(x_i-v)]. (11) For t<N the numerator is s_t; for t>=N it is s_(t-N), apart from the complete root-orbit polynomial factors. Both have rate N L(s) up to O(log N), because L has period 1. The denominator d+t-J has rate L(1+s-S)=-L(S-s). Substitution of (10) then gives (11). This same argument covers endpoints: changing an argument by O(1/N) changes N L by O(log N), uniformly even at a zero of sine. One may prove this modulus of continuity by integrating |log u| over an interval of length O(1/N) near the nearest integer. The decisive inequality is H_x(v)<=H_x(0)=Phi(x):=-2sum_i L(x_i) (12) for EVERY actual term, including the second-zero band. Here is a direct elementary proof. The function is even in v, and (10) gives |v|<min(x_1,x_2,x_3). For v>0 away from its logarithmic corner, put alpha_i=pi x_i and theta=pi v. Then H_x'(v)=log |P_minus/P_plus|, P_plus=product_i sin(alpha_i+theta)>0, P_minus=product_i sin(alpha_i-theta). (13) If theta<alpha_4, every factor is positive and sin(alpha_i+theta)-sin(alpha_i-theta) =2cos(alpha_i)sin(theta)>0. Thus |P_minus|<P_plus. If theta>alpha_4, exactly the fourth minus factor is negative. Expand the sum of the two products: P_plus+P_minus =2 sum_(A subset {1,2,3,4}, |A| even) cos(theta)^(4-|A|)sin(theta)^|A| product_(i in A)cos(alpha_i) product_(i notin A)sin(alpha_i)>0. (14) Every factor is nonnegative, and an interior term is strictly positive by (8). Since P_minus<0, (14) again says |P_minus|<P_plus. Continuity across theta=alpha_4, where (13) tends to minus infinity, proves (12). Evenness treats negative v. No local concavity or uniform strict exponential tail gap was used. The integer nearest t=J/2 is a true term of the FIRST band: (6) gives max(j_i,J-d)<=floor(J/2) and ceil(J/2)<=min(J-max j_i,d). At that term |v|<=1/(2N), so the same uniform modulus of continuity gives H_x(v)=Phi(x)+O(log N/N). ## 4. Positive main value and polynomial normal envelopes For t<N, the exact root identity is ([N+t]!/[N])|_q=(-1)^t[d]![t]!. All denominators in (4) are positive symmetric factorials at q. Thus S_main/[N] has ONE common phase (-1)^d. Its positive absolute sum is Rcore_N(j)=N sum_(true t<N) s_t/{s_(d+t-J) product_i s_(t-j_i)s_(J-j_i-t)}. It has at most N terms and contains the midpoint term identified above. The uniform two-sided sine-factorial estimate and (12) therefore give, throughout the whole support and every branch, N^(-C)e^(N Phi(x))<=Rcore_N(j) <=N^C e^(N Phi(x)). (15) The estimate uses only ONE midpoint summand for its lower bound; no bulk Hessian, saddle width or distance from a saturation face is assumed. Second-band terms, after removing [N][2N], obey the same upper bound by (12). They may approach the leading action at boundary scales, which is why a uniform strict gap is unnecessary. Use the common disk |Z|<=c/N^2. A quantum-factorial ratio with a fixed number of factors and indices <=3N has, after explicitly removing its zeros, a polynomial envelope relative to its nonzero root product on this disk. This follows either from the proved [bounded normal factorial estimate](bounded_normal_quantum_factorial_envelope.md) or directly: a nonzero 1-q^(2k) has magnitude >=c0/N; its change is O(|Z|), and O(N) such factors accumulate only bounded relative growth here. Removed [N] and [2N] factors and the symmetric-int normalization cost fixed powers of N. Their count is uniformly bounded. Equations (7),(12),(15) hence bound the ENTIRE holomorphic S_j/Z by poly(N)e^(N Phi(x)). Cauchy estimates for four fixed normal orders add only another fixed power of N. No alternating-sum cancellation is needed for the second-zero terms. To include the complete prefactor of (4), note first that ([N] [j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!)|_q=(-1)^j. (16) Its zero-removed envelope is polynomial, with no factorial action. All three r_i are <N, while N<=J+1<2N. The zero-removed triangle factor therefore has rate P(x)=sum_(i=1)^3 L(2x_i)-L(S-1), up to O(log N). Each simple axis contributes one dimension zero [2j+1]=[N]; the other dimensions and all ell_j in (5) have polynomial fixed jets, uniformly to the nearest paired neighbor. If s0=3-r is the number of simple axes, the prefactor without S^2 has zero order s0-4. Multiplication by Z^r and S^2, whose order is at least two, leaves order at least ONE. Consequently Z^r T_j product ell is holomorphic on the common disk; it is never estimated as a bare singular expression. The preceding bounds give for its fixed jets |[Z^k]{Z^r T_j product ell}|<=N^C exp(N E(x)), k<=4, E(x)=P(x)+2Phi(x) =sum_(i=1)^4[L(2x_i)-4L(x_i)] =-2sum_(i=1)^4[L(x_i)+L(1/2-x_i)]. (17) The second equality uses L(S-1)=-L(2x_4), and the third is the elementary duplication identity for L. This expression is unchanged by every permutation or individual complement x_i->1/2-x_i. Equation (9) therefore makes E EXACTLY the same function for all unfolded branches of a fixed folded triple, with these half-step coordinates. Finally the PROVED actual positive top moment has the exact weight Z_N(l)=N^2 product_i k_(l_i) s_(J_l-2l_1)s_(J_l-2l_2)s_(J_l-2l_3) /s_(J_l-d) *R_N(l)^2. The same midpoint argument (15), uniform factorial bounds and its positive prefactor give N^(-C)exp(N E_fold)<=tau_l<=N^C exp(N E_fold) (18) on the ENTIRE supported domain. Endpoint factors s_0=1 cause no problem, and replacing their scaled arguments by the half-step ones changes logarithms by only O(log N). Combine (5),(17),(18), sum at most eight branches, and absorb the polynomial |q-q^-1|: this proves the first estimate in (3). The finite square root of q_l=1+n_l is sum_(k=0)^r binom(1/2,k)n_l^k, with n_l^(r+1)=0. It is a polynomial of degree <=3 in at most seven normalized moments. Thus the first estimate implies the second, with constants independent of the labels and N. Its constant coefficient is one, so K_l>=1. This completes the whole-support actual Gram theorem. ## 5. Scope and verification The new ingredient beyond the central-corridor bound is the global sine-product inequality (12)--(14), together with the half-step folding coordinates. A second-zero action gap may vanish at boundary scales; uniform positive factorial comparison replaces it. The result controls the correlated marked Gram on its actual regular source cells. It supplies neither a physical mirror interpretation of that Gram nor a bound for genuine transitions between different pair decompositions. Those remain separate global source/geometry tasks; polynomial K alone has no hidden cuboctahedral volume term. The [multiprecision source diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning.py) uses the proved generic trace (4), every partner and the original physical circle normal. It compares two precisions and two normal steps on saturation faces/corners and interior examples. These are diagnostics; the uniform theorem follows from the finite generic source identity, (12), common-disk factorial envelopes and the positive midpoint bound, not sampling. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope_results.json) verify the universal even-product polynomial with an identically zero cleared numerator; 46,495 unfolded integer branches and 257,107 true Racah terms at N=2,...,32; 215 independent generic physical-double-sum versus Racah traces; and five all-moment original marked crosschecks. Floating-point action comparisons in that audit are labeled diagnostics; the proof of (12) is the exact sign argument (13),(14). The separate [paired-precision data](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning_diagnostic_results.json) include ten boundary/interior cases through N=256, both parities, simple axes and saturation corners. The largest displayed K is below 2.78; this finite observation is not used to choose the polynomial exponent or prove its uniformity. The whole-support boundary envelope is not a global source-volume theorem.

title: The original whole word as a marked cyclic-dilogarithm resolvent period
text: # The original whole word as a marked cyclic-dilogarithm resolvent period 28 October 2026. Every actual signed braid word admits an exact period on a product of the literature cyclic-dilogarithm curves. The marked cycle and its full original cap are specified, and the finite-head walls are retained inside rational resolvents. There is no restriction on a geometric atom argument, or asymptotic replacement of a finite polynomial by a chosen phase. The cyclic dilogarithm and its nilpotent anchoring were already proved in [the unfolded Ward calculation](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) and [the Rees crossing calculation](rees_whole_crossing_source_factorization.md). The [full-atom note](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) also gives their exact scalar Taylor Cauchy formula. The new content here is their contraction into the original strict signed word with the specified source and an explicit product cycle. This constructs a global algebraic period representation; it does not prove a geometric intersection number or a volume estimate. ## 1. The marked curve realizes the literal nilpotent operators Put `Q=exp(2pi*i/N)` and let C_N be the normalization of y^N=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j t)^j. (1) At t=0 choose the sheet y=1. On its disk `|t|<1` this specifies the analytic function D_N(t)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j t)^(j/N). All powers have their common constant-one mark, rather than independent roots chosen after specialization. Weighted root summation gives for `1<=a<N` [t^a]log D_N=1/[a(1-Q^a)]. (2) Consequently the first N Taylor coefficients of D_N and its inverse are precisely those of the literal u_N and v_N. For ANY actual nilpotent matrix T with `T^N=0`, and any `0<r<1`, u_N(T)= (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y(t)(tI-T)^-1 dt, v_N(T)= (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y(t)^-1(tI-T)^-1 dt. (3) Here gamma_0 is the positively oriented circle `|t|=r` lifted to that sheet of C_N. It is closed. Expand the exact resolvent (tI-T)^-1=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)T^a t^(-a-1). (4) Termwise Cauchy evaluation and (2) prove (3). Thus this is exact holomorphic functional calculus on the actual finite head. It does not claim that the scalar evaluations u_N(z) and D_N(z) agree away from a nilpotent argument. ## 2. The full original rational source kernel Use the strict factorization in [the original Euler/Gaussian network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md): C=F_2 U_- F_1 F_2^-1, C^-1=F_2 F_1^-1 V_- F_2^-1, R_+=kappa C D U_+ C^-1, R_-=kappa^-1 C V_+ D^-1 C^-1, where `U_±=u_N(T_±)`, `V_±=v_N(T_±)`, `T_-=x^-1 S_1^-S_2^+`, `T_+=x^-1 S_1^+S_2^-`. Every T has Nth power zero. Spectator heads are extended by identity. Every crossing has exactly three such Euler atoms; its factorial and Gaussian factors remain the specified matrices. Let beta have b heads and m signed crossings, and let `A_L ... A_1`, `L=10m`, be its literal stripped matrix word in the correct order. Mark its `r=3m` Euler slots by `j=1,...,r`. At slot j set `sigma_j=+1` for u and `-1` for v and replace its factor by the rational matrix mathscr R_j(t_j)=(t_j I-T_j)^-1. (5) All other factors retain their actual values. Write B_l for the resulting factors. Let the original averaged first-cut functional be Phi_(b,N)(W)=(1/N) sum_(a,c,k_2,...,k_b) (product_(i=2)^b g_(k_i)) W_((c,k_2,...,k_b),(a,k_2,...,k_b)), g_k=(xQ^-k)^(1-N). (6) One may instead keep the original fixed-first-input-zero source by fixing a=0 and removing 1/N. The equality of their original uninserted knot closures is the prior scalar-closure theorem; no equality for arbitrary inserted resolvents is assumed here. Choose one of these original sources and keep it throughout. Define the rational scalar R_(beta,N)(t_1,...,t_r)=Phi_(b,N)(B_L ... B_1). (7) This is an entirely explicit rational function with poles only at the coordinate loci `t_j=0`; its Laurent powers in each variable run from -1 through -N. It retains every finite-head projector because each T_j is the literal truncated transfer. It also retains all pivotal closures and the first-cut coupon. There is no quotient that kills the degree-zero wall terms. If chi is the original external dimension, framing and common Cartan factor, included exactly once, then the original scalar is P_(beta,N)(M)=chi_(beta,N)(M)/(2pi*i)^r integral_(gamma_0^r) R_(beta,N)(t) product_(j=1)^r y_j^(sigma_j) dt_j. (8) The proof applies (3) to each slot, in its original order, and then the finite linear functional (6).
