No Fubini convergence issue arises on the compact small circles: the matrices have finite dimension and the curves are regular there. Equation (8) holds for the full root meridian family, with the same external factors as the actual invariant. It is not an assertion about generic-q normal derivatives. Thus the desired first step of the torsor route is concrete: the algebraic curve, the meromorphic differential, and the original marked cycle are all supplied. The number r of curve factors depends on the braid word, not on N. The curve and source rational function themselves do depend on N. There is also a FULL version with no factorial constants hidden in the rational source. The exact reflection identity is F_a=N Q^(-a-1) [t^(N-1-a)]D_N(t)^-1. Consequently replace each factorial diagonal on its head by F^-1=(1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y diag_(a)(t^(-a-1)) dt, F=(1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y^-1 diag_(a)(N Q^(-a-1)t^(a-N)) dt. (9) Every crossing has six such factorial diagonals and three transfer Euler atoms. Apply (9) to all six. Formula (8) now holds on `C_N^(9m)` with a new rational source formed by the same ordered matrix contraction; its only remaining local constants are the specified Gaussian diagonals and explicit powers of N,Q,x. Their marked Gaussian phase and all external Cartan, dimension and framing factors are retained. All actual factorial growth is inside the cyclic-dilogarithm differential. Both the minimal `3m` and full `9m` representations are exact. ## 3. An all-inverse realization with no growing infinity factors An exact change of auxiliary completion makes the cut-cycle problem simpler. Write `v_(Q^-1)` for the SAME finite factorial formula with Q replaced by its inverse. Directly, (Q^-1;Q^-1)_a=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)F_a, [t^a]v_(Q^-1)(t)=Q^a/F_a, u_Q(T)=v_(Q^-1)(Q^-1 T). (10) These are identities of the actual finite polynomials and operators, not conjugations of the physical invariant. Define C_(N,epsilon) by (1) with `Q^j` replaced by `Q^(epsilon*j)`; its y=1 sheet at zero is the corresponding cyclic dilogarithm. Equation (10) replaces each u resolvent in (8) EXACTLY by (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0 on C_(N,-1)) y^-1(tI-Q^-1 T)^-1 dt. (11) For the full factorial version replace F^-1 by (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0 on C_(N,-1)) y^-1 diag_(a)(Q^-a t^(-a-1)) dt, (12) while F still uses the inverse-y formula in (9) on C_(N,+1). The v transfers likewise keep their original inverse-y curve. Thus the full original word is an exact period on a product of `9m` oriented curves C_(N,epsilon), with EVERY algebraic factor equal to y^-1. All physical Gaussian, pivotal, Cartan, framing and dimension factors are unchanged. The rational source is formed by the same original ordered contraction. This auxiliary completion changes the analytic function beyond its first N Taylor coefficients. It does not discard the infinity contribution of the old positive-y representation; it supplies a different exact period for the same finite operator. No generic-q continuation follows from it. For every variable in this all-inverse realization, the rational matrix kernel is `O(t^-1)` at infinity. Also |y^-1|=O(|t|^(-(N-1)/2)). (13) Every outer cut arc therefore has integral tending to zero in absolute value, for every fixed N>=2. At a root `t=Q^(-epsilon*j)` the exponent of y^-1 is `-j/N>-1`, so each cut endpoint is integrable. Consequently all variables admit convergent radial cut deformations without an infinity regularization. The banks and monodromy of these cuts must be kept on the chosen sheet. For even N a large base circle need not close on a single sheet; (13) applies to its cut arcs, not to an unmarked closed lift asserted without proof. On the normalization the finite branch endpoints do not in fact produce poles of the differential. If `g=gcd(N,j)`, a uniformizer has `t-alpha=s^(N/g)` and `y=unit*s^(j/g)`. Hence `y^-1 dt` has nonnegative order `(N-j)/g-1`. The rational matrix kernel is regular at alpha. The cut deformation is genuine sheet and homology transport, not a sum of residues at those branch points. The [explicit Hankel cycle theorem](actual_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.md) computes these banks and their exact nonzero sine weights, and carries them through the entire original ordered source. ## 4. The full original source is polynomially bounded on these cuts At `|M|=1` one has `|x|=1`. Equip the actual head basis with its ordinary Euclidean norm. Each truncated transfer and its Q^-1 multiple have operator norm at most one. Therefore on the ENTIRE exterior `|t|>=1`, including its endpoint circle, ||(tI-T)^-1|| <= sum_(a=0)^(N-1)|t|^(-a-1) <= N/|t|. (14) The full all-inverse factorial kernels obey ||diag_(a)(Q^-a t^(-a-1))||<=1/|t|, ||diag_(a)(NQ^(-a-1)t^(a-N))||<=N/|t|. (15) Every Gaussian diagonal is unitary here. The averaged original cut in (6) is `Tr[(E tensor G^(tensor(b-1)))W]`, where `E=J/N` is the rank-one orthogonal projection onto the constant head vector and G is the unitary pivotal diagonal. Its trace norm is exactly `N^(b-1)`. Thus `|Phi(W)|<=N^(b-1)||W||`. Each crossing contains three transfer resolvents, three direct factorial kernels and three inverse-factorial kernels. Taking the norm of their original ordered product proves the uniform bound for the full all-inverse rational source |R_(beta,N)(t)| <= N^(b-1+6m) product_(j=1)^(9m)|t_j|^-1, whenever all |t_j|>=1 and |M|=1. (16) For the retained fixed-first-input-zero source, its first coupon has trace norm sqrt(N); the right side acquires only that additional factor. No actual source is replaced to obtain a bound. A fixed total number k of logarithmic t-derivatives costs at most a constant depending on k,m times an additional factor `N^k`, by differentiating the finite resolvents and diagonal monomials. Thus the whole rational source has no hidden exponential growth on the canonical exterior cut chain. This global upper-amplitude control is unconditional for the specified root source. It supplies neither a lower bound nor a nonzero geometric coefficient. A complex rational source bounded by a polynomial may still carry rapidly varying phase or vanish on the relevant critical image. Those remain part of the cycle-selection and lower-bound question. ## 5. What a global cut deformation must retain Unlike the finite scalar Euler polynomials, the y factors in (8) have genuine branch divisors at `t=Q^-j`. This puts a possible cut deformation on an actual marked algebraic cover. The resolvent expression avoids replacing a finite projector by a spurious reproducing pole. Any subsequent deformation must still be an equality of marked cycles on this cover, with its infinity and branch-boundary terms retained. For example the leading magnitude of `y` at infinity is `|t|^((N-1)/2)`; its inverse decays by that order. Formula (4) therefore gives automatically decaying infinity behavior for each v-variable coefficient. For a positive-y u-variable coefficient of T^a, the absolute-decay argument applies when `a>(N-1)/2`; it gives no automatic vanishing below that threshold. Lower powers may need a boundary or Taylor regularization. Whether the original source cancels their coefficients is an explicit question about (7), not a freedom to discard them. Nonzero examples occur in the actual figure-eight word in the audit. The all-inverse realization above avoids that particular regularization problem by an exact change of auxiliary curve. The marked small circle in (8) is now a definite cycle whose branch-cut or relative-chain image can be computed. It has not been proved to project with degree one to a positive Rivin angle domain, nor to have nonzero geometric thimble coefficient. Equation (8) avoids assuming that coefficient; it is a suitable starting point for proving or disproving the needed cycle map. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent.py) checks the Taylor identification from the fractional product, each original signed crossing, whole signed words with their original cap, and the retained low-power u-source terms.

title: An elementary balance certificate for one zero middle
status: Exact 9/4 curvature certificate for source balance
text: # An elementary balance certificate for one zero middle source-normalized lemma, 31 October 2026. This is a local analytic test on actual complete curvatures. It does not by itself construct a family of diagrams or assert that the test holds for one. Let a port have middle curvatures $0$ and $e>0$, outer curvatures $x,y\geq0$, and $A=x+y>0$. Retain the original complete triangle potential $Q$ from the [calibrated source](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). If $$ \frac eA\leq\frac94,\tag{1} $$ then its strict complete-radius balance gap satisfies $$ Q_e(0)+Q_0(0)-\log e>\frac1{2500}.\tag{2} $$ Here $Q_e(0)=Q(x,e,y)$ and $Q_0(0)=Q(x,0,y)$. Either outer curvature may vanish. If $e=0$ as well, both one-sided sectors vanish exactly and no positive-middle balance inequality is required. ## 1. The worst outer split has one zero outer curvature For fixed $A$ and $P=xy$, the zero-spectral lower-tail Perron factor is $$ \Lambda_P(t)=2\sin(\pi t) \left[A\sin(\pi t)+\sqrt{A^2\sin^2(\pi t)+4P\cos^2(\pi t)}\right]. $$ It increases with $P$ for every $t\in(0,1/2)$. The original weighted start action is $$ F_b(\mu;P)=\mu\log b+\int_0^\mu\log[4\cos^2(\pi t)]\,dt +\int_\mu^{1/2}\log\Lambda_P(t)\,dt. $$ Its maximum over $\mu$ is exactly $Q(x,b,y)$; for $b=0$ the sole start is $\mu=0$. Each $Q$ is therefore nondecreasing in $P$ at fixed $A,b$, by taking the maximum after the pointwise comparison of these actual actions. This is a local comparison, not a shared minimax exchange. Consequently $$ Q(x,e,y)+Q(x,0,y)\geq Q(A,e,0)+Q(A,0,0). $$ The exact half-degree homogeneity and monomial normalization give $$ \begin{aligned} Q(A,e,0)+Q(A,0,0)-\log e&=F(r)-\log r,\\ r&=e/A,\qquad F(r)=Q(1,r,0),\qquad Q(A,0,0)=\tfrac12\log A. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ No additive source constant has been removed. ## 2. Exact one-variable formula and monotonicity At outer weights $1,0$, the actual saddle is $$ \mu(r)=\frac1\pi\arctan\sqrt r,\qquad \frac{dF}{d\log r}=\mu(r),\qquad F(0)=Q(1,0,0)=0. $$ Define $T(z)=\int_0^z\arctan(t)\,dt/t$. Then $$ F(r)=\frac2\pi T(\sqrt r).\tag{4} $$ The derivative of $F(r)-\log r$ with respect to $\log r$ is $\mu(r)-1<0$, so it suffices to bound its value at $r=9/4$. Direct differentiation using $\arctan z+\arctan(1/z)=\pi/2$ for $z>0$ proves $$ T(z)-T(1/z)=\frac\pi2\log z. $$ At $z=3/2$, (4) therefore yields $$ F(9/4)-\log(9/4)=\frac2\pi T(2/3)-\log(3/2).\tag{5} $$ ## 3. A rational lower bound without numerical quadrature Integrating the alternating power series of $\arctan$ gives $$ T(t)=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{(-1)^jt^{2j+1}}{(2j+1)^2},\qquad0<t<1. $$ Four terms, ending with the negative term $j=3$, give a strict lower bound at $t=2/3$. The inequality $\pi<22/7$ follows, for example, from the positive integral $$ \frac{22}7-\pi=\int_0^1\frac{x^4(1-x)^4}{1+x^2}\,dx>0. $$ Hence $$ \frac2\pi T(2/3)> \frac7{11}\sum_{j=0}^3\frac{(-1)^j(2/3)^{2j+1}}{(2j+1)^2} =\frac{155342}{382725}.\tag{6} $$ For the logarithm, use $\log(3/2)=2\operatorname{artanh}(1/5)$. Its positive series and a geometric tail bound give $$ \log(3/2)<2\sum_{j=0}^2\frac{(1/5)^{2j+1}}{2j+1} +\frac{2(1/5)^7}{7(1-1/25)} =\frac{177391}{437500}.\tag{7} $$ Subtracting (7) from (6), $$ F(9/4)-\log(9/4)> \frac{57269}{136687500}>\frac1{2500}.\tag{8} $$ Equations (1), (3), (5), and (8) prove (2), including the exact one-zero-outer limit. The estimate does not depend on normalization scale, because the balance gap is scale invariant. ## 4. Interface with an actual symmetric plat construction Suppose an actual certified source has only the following port types in its one complete marked packing: - Equal middle curvatures $b=c$, with $A>0$. - One zero middle and the other $e$ satisfying $e/(x+y)\leq9/4$. Every such port is balanced. For equal positive middles, this follows from $Q_b(0)>\tfrac12\log b$; if both are zero, the one-sided sectors vanish. For the second type, it follows from (2). The [conditional full-invariant balance theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) therefore applies to any literal source for which these actual geometric statements have been proved. The [reduced-layer family theorem](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes the required packing, reflection, original mark and uniform ratio bound for its literal words at every $k\geq4$. Those are separate geometric conclusions, not consequences of the local inequality alone. ## Validation and scope The bound follows from scalar comparison, monotonicity, exact rational inequalities and protected-zero limits. Numerical quadrature or a sample of diagrams cannot establish its uniformity.

title: Independent proof of additive full-cyclotomic descent
text: # Independent proof of additive full-cyclotomic descent Research audit and proof, 27 October 2026. The additive analogue of the full rank-one theorem is valid with the weighted exponential--Puiseux uniqueness lemma. The pole-order induction needs the whole orbit function, not just its highest principal coefficient. The proof below makes that cancellation explicit. This concerns additive comparison torsors with trivial homogeneous action. It does not by itself solve a residual twisted by a nontrivial geometric companion matrix, or construct the selected knot comparison. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. Statement and full-root propagation Let c(Q,Y) belong to ℚ(Q,Y), sigma(Y)=QY. Suppose that for every sufficiently large N, sum_(j=0)^(N-1)c(zeta_N,zeta_N^jY)=0 (1.1) as a rational identity in Y. Then there is b in ℚ(Q,Y) such that c(Q,Y)=b(Q,QY)-b(Q,Y). (1.2) For coefficients in a field K contained in C the same conclusion over K(Q,Y) holds if the hypothesis is supplied at every primitive root for the fixed coefficient embedding. The rational coefficient case obtains these conjugate identities by Galois action. An appropriate sufficient condition over a number field is the full coefficient-conjugate marking of the multiplicative theorem. For fixed k, xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N) has order m=N/gcd(k,N). Its true m-step sum is zero for all sufficiently large N; the N-step sum repeats it gcd(k,N) times. Thus these scaled roots are available without a coprimality restriction on k,N. ## 2. Exact pole-cluster cancellation Over a finite algebraic splitting field write the unique partial fraction expansion c(Q,Y)=sum_l c_l(Q)Y^l +sum_(mu,r) a_(mu,r)(Q)/(1-mu(Q)Y)^r, (2.1) with finitely many Laurent monomials, distinct nonzero algebraic mu, and positive pole orders r. The Laurent coefficients belong to the original rational field. Choose the common algebraic coefficient field large enough for all partial fractions. At a primitive m-th root, the universal orbit function is Psi_(m,r)(u)=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-zeta_m^j z)^(-r), u=z^m, Psi_(m,r)(u)=m sum_(l>=0) binom(ml+r-1,r-1)u^l. (2.2) This follows from expansion at z=0 and root orthogonality. The binomial is a polynomial in l of degree r-1. Hence Psi is rational and has an order-r pole at u=1 with highest coefficient Psi_(m,r)(u)=m^r/(1-u)^r +lower pole orders. (2.3) For example this coefficient follows inductively from Psi_(m,r+1)=Psi_(m,r)+(m*u/r) partial_u Psi_(m,r). Equivalently use the leading coefficient m^(r-1)/(r-1)! of the binomial polynomial in (2.2) and the order-r pole of sum l^(r-1)u^l. Fix a root specialization outside the finite bad set and a cluster of poles for which mu(Q)^m has the same value lambda. Let R be the largest pole order still present. At U=Y^m=1/lambda, the order-R coefficient of the averaged rational function is m^R sum_(mu^m=lambda) a_(mu,R)(Q). It must vanish. Crucially, the entire contribution of that order is the same universal function Psi_(m,R)(lambda U) multiplied by this sum. It therefore vanishes identically, including all its lower pole orders. One may now descend to R-1. Induction proves sum_(mu^m=lambda) a_(mu,r)(Q)=0 for every r,lambda. (2.4) This avoids mixing an order-R lower principal part with a genuine order-(R-1) coefficient. Moving poles and their partial-fraction weights are algebraic, so accidental collisions or poles of the weights exclude only finitely many sufficiently near Q=1 roots, unless the algebraic branches are identical and were already combined. For large m all nonconstant Laurent monomials average to zero. The pole terms tend to zero at infinity. Comparing the remaining constant there gives m c_0(Q)=0. Infinitely many root values therefore give c_0(Q)=0 identically. ## 3. Weighted scaled moments detect the generic Q-orbits At xi_N, use (2.4) at its true order m, then raise mu^m to the gcd(k,N)-th power. For every fixed r this gives sum_mu a_(mu,r)(xi_N) mu(xi_N)^N=0. (3.1) Choose the common ramification and Puiseux forms of [the full multiplicative proof](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md): mu(exp(2pi*i*t))=a t^nu exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))), A_mu(t)=exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))/t). The algebraic weights a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) are meromorphic in t^(1/e). They are precisely allowed by the weighted uniqueness lemma. At each fixed scaled root k that lemma separates the groups (nu,a), giving, after rescaling the argument, sum_(mu in (nu,a)) a_(mu,r)(Q(t)) A_mu(t)^k=0. (3.2) The weights are not raised to the k-th power. Within one group, partition the mu by identical functions A_mu. Let the distinct nonzero functions be A_1,...,A_h and let W_l(t) be the sum of their weights. For k=1,...,h, equation (3.2) is sum_l W_l(t) A_l(t)^k=0. This matrix is a Vandermonde matrix times a diagonal matrix of the nonzero A_l, and is invertible over the common function field on the ramified punctured disk. Hence every W_l=0 identically. For branches with the same (nu,a), equality A_mu=A_eta is equivalent to mu(Q)/eta(Q)=Q^j for an integer j. (3.3) One direction is immediate. For the other, their logarithmic difference divided by t has exponential one and therefore is a constant 2pi*i j, exactly as in the multiplicative proof. Thus the identical-A classes are the generic Q-shift orbits of the pole parameters. We have proved zero total weight in each such orbit, separately for every pole order r. ## 4. A finite additive flow constructs the rational primitive On an orbit mu=Q^u eta write the order-r weights as a_u(Q). Their total is zero. Define the finite cumulative flow e_u=-sum_(v<=u) a_v, b_(eta,r)=sum_u e_u/(1-Q^u eta Y)^r. (4.1) Then sigma b_(eta,r)-b_(eta,r) is the required pole contribution, because the coefficient at index u is e_(u-1)-e_u=a_u. For a nonzero Laurent exponent l, use the primitive c_l(Q)Y^l/(Q^l-1). (4.2) The constant Laurent coefficient has already been shown to vanish. The sum of (4.1)--(4.2) solves (1.2) over the splitting field. The pole flow is the unique finite-support flow on its infinite Q-orbit. Since c is rational over ℚ(Q), Galois permutations preserve the resulting whole pole part. The Laurent part is already rational. Choosing the free constant in that Laurent part to be zero therefore gives b in ℚ(Q,Y). The same descent works over K(Q). Any two rational solutions differ by a rational sigma-invariant, hence by a function of Q alone. This is generic rational descent. Pole divisors of b at the ideal meridian remain part of its lattice. A source-compatible marked cut or normal residue cannot be inferred from (1.2) alone. ## 5. The finite nilpotent extension consequence Combining the full multiplicative and additive results gives a direct finite induction for upper-triangular comparison transport. Suppose an upper-triangular rational matrix B(Q,Y) has identity cyclic monodromy at every sufficiently large primitive root. Its diagonal coefficients have norm one, so the multiplicative theorem trivializes them by rational diagonal gauges. The matrix is now unipotent and its root monodromy remains identity. The first superdiagonal of its monodromy is the cyclic sum of that superdiagonal of B. The additive theorem removes it by a rational unipotent gauge. After this removal the second superdiagonal has the same property; continue by distance above the diagonal. Only finitely many steps occur, at most the nilpotence class. This proves rational triviality for the stated upper-triangular comparison object. It does not assert nilpotence of the original braid image, nor triangularity or identity curvature for the unknown actual/geometric comparison. Those inputs must be established. A twisted source residual (sigma-C)b=Delta is not automatically the untwisted problem (1.2). [Exact independent audit](../experiments/audit_additive_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Results](../experiments/additive_cyclotomic_descent_results.json).

title: Cyclotomic descent for rational sources and unipotent torsors
text: # Cyclotomic descent for rational sources and unipotent torsors Research proof, 27 October 2026. This addresses the source extension, rather than only its multiplicative norm line. The proof uses the weighted sequence-uniqueness lemma proved in [full rank-one descent](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md), and finite flows on rational partial-fraction orbits. No published q-curvature theorem is used as a premise. The result is uniform in the number of source coordinates. It applies to a specified rational unipotent comparison with whole cyclotomic transport identities. Constructing that comparison for the actual knot period, and verifying its source and peripheral lattice, remain necessary. The volume conjecture is not proved by this conditional descent theorem. ## 1. An additive descent theorem Let k be the rational number field, let sigma(Y)=QY on k(Q,Y), and take c in k(Q,Y). Suppose that for every sufficiently large integer N, sum_(j=0)^(N-1) c(zeta_N,zeta_N^j Y)=0, zeta_N=exp(2pi*i/N), (1) as an identity of whole rational functions of Y. Then c(Q,Y)=b(Q,QY)-b(Q,Y) (2) for some b in k(Q,Y). Conversely (2) implies (1) at every level where its rational specializations are defined. There are no hypotheses on the ramification or limiting values of the moving poles at Q=1. The ambiguity in b is precisely k(Q). The theorem does not assert regularity of b at the ideal meridian. The same proof works over a subfield k of C if (1) is given at every primitive root for the chosen coefficient embedding. For rational coefficients this follows from Galois conjugation. For a number field, knowing the chosen principal root alone is not silently treated as knowing all its coefficient conjugates. ## 2. Partial fractions and the charges seen by a root fiber Over a finite algebraic splitting field of k(Q), write uniquely c(Q,Y)=sum_m c_m(Q)Y^m +sum_(mu,r>=1) a_(mu,r)(Q)/(1-mu(Q)Y)^r. (3) The first sum is a finite Laurent polynomial; all mu are nonzero algebraic functions, and the second sum is finite. The partial fraction part is proper at infinity and has no pole at zero. All identities below omit the finitely many root levels at which a coefficient specialization fails or two distinct pole functions coincide. A nonzero algebraic function has only finitely many such specialization zeros on its finite algebraic cover. At a primitive N-th root set U=Y^N and D_U=U partial_U. For r>=1, sum_j (1-mu zeta_N^j Y)^(-r) =N/(r-1)! product_(ell=1)^(r-1)(N D_U+ell) (1-mu^N U)^(-1). (4) For r=1 this is the elementary geometric-series identity, first as a power series and then as a rational identity. Applying the operators (D_Y+ell) proves the general formula. Its pole at U=mu^(-N) has exact order r with nonzero highest coefficient. Terms with the same mu^N in (4) give exactly the same rational function. Compare the highest remaining pole order in (1), then descend in r. At every cluster C of equal values mu(zeta_N)^N, sum_(mu in C) a_(mu,r)(zeta_N)=0 (5) for each r. Laurent polynomials have no finite nonzero poles and do not affect this comparison. In particular, for each r, sum_mu a_(mu,r)(zeta_N) mu(zeta_N)^N=0. (6) For xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N), with fixed positive integer k, its actual order is m=N/gcd(k,N). Apply (5) at order m and raise the common m-th powers to the gcd(k,N)-th power. This proves sum_mu a_(mu,r)(xi_N) mu(xi_N)^N=0 (7) for every sufficiently large N. It does not use a primitive N-step formula at a nonprimitive scaled root. ## 3. Generic orbit charges from the weighted rigidity lemma Choose the common convergent Puiseux forms near Q=1 provided by the elementary finite-cover argument in the rank-one note. Put t=Log Q/(2pi*i), and write mu(exp(2pi*i*t))=a_mu t^(nu_mu) exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))), A_mu(t)=exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))/t), (8) where a_mu!=0, nu_mu is rational, and lambda_mu(0)=0. The coefficients a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) are meromorphic Puiseux germs after the same further finite ramification. At xi_N, (7) becomes a sum of terms N^(-nu_mu N)(a_mu k^(nu_mu))^N a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*k/N)) A_mu(k/N)^k. (9) The weighted exponential--Puiseux uniqueness lemma separates every pair (nu_mu,a_mu). It applies to the partial-fraction weights as well as to the exponentials; those weights need not be units. For each such pair, and every positive integer k, it gives the identity of punctured analytic germs sum_(mu in pair) a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) A_mu(t)^k=0. (10) Here the argument was rescaled from kt to t after applying the lemma. These are identities of functions, not only formal jets. Group equal functions A_mu. If A_1,...,A_h are the distinct nonzero functions in one pair and w_i is the sum of its weights, then (10) for k=1,...,h has coefficient matrix (A_i^k). Its determinant is a nonzero product of the A_i and their pairwise differences in the field of meromorphic functions on the ramified punctured disk. Hence w_i=0 for every i. Within a fixed (nu,a), equality A_mu=A_eta is equivalent to mu(Q)/eta(Q)=Q^v for an integer v. (11) Indeed exp((lambda_mu-lambda_eta)/t)=1 forces the exponent to be a constant in 2pi*i Z on the connected punctured cover. Conversely (11) has this property. Thus the generic additive orbit charges vanish: sum_(mu in each Q-shift orbit) a_(mu,r)(Q)=0 (12) for every pole order r. The rational-function identities follow from the analytic germ identities because these coefficients are algebraic functions of Q. ## 4. A finite flow solves the transport equation On one infinite orbit write mu_v=Q^v mu_0, and set a_v equal to the coefficient in (3), or zero if that pole is absent. The a_v have finite support and sum zero. Define e_v=-sum_(u<=v) a_u. Then e_v has finite support, and b_orbit=sum_v e_v/(1-Q^v mu_0 Y)^r satisfies sigma(b_orbit)-b_orbit=sum_v a_v/(1-Q^v mu_0 Y)^r. The equality follows coefficientwise from e_(v-1)-e_v=a_v. This flow is unique among finite-support flows on that orbit. The total proper partial-fraction solution b_pole descends to k(Q,Y). One way to see this is to apply any splitting-field automorphism tau. The difference tau(b_pole)-b_pole is invariant under Y->QY. A rational invariant has no finite nonzero poles, since their Q-orbits would be infinite; its remaining Laurent polynomial is therefore constant in Y. Both proper parts vanish at infinity, so that constant is zero. Thus b_pole is Galois invariant. Subtract its coboundary from c. The remaining Laurent polynomial still has zero cyclic sum at all sufficiently large roots. Its nonzero powers sum to zero once N exceeds the largest absolute value of their nonzero exponents, so its constant coefficient obeys N c_0(zeta_N)=0 at infinitely many Q-values. Consequently c_0=0. Finally b_Laurent=sum_(m!=0) c_m(Q)Y^m/(Q^m-1) solves the Laurent part. This proves (2), its field of definition, and the stated constant ambiguity. The construction does not throw away the factors Q^m-1 or any Y-meridian factor in b. ## 5. Unipotent and Heisenberg descent Let C(Q,Y) be a d-by-d upper unitriangular rational matrix. Use the column transport equation sigma(v)=C v, C_[N]=sigma^(N-1)(C)...sigma(C) C. (13) If C_[N] specializes to I at Q=zeta_N for every sufficiently large N, then there is a rational upper unitriangular G such that C=sigma(G) G^(-1). (14) To prove this, filter strictly upper triangular matrices by their distance above the diagonal. In the first surviving diagonal of C-I, multiplication adds the entries, so (13) says exactly that their cyclic sums vanish. Solve each by the additive theorem and gauge by a unitriangular matrix carrying those solutions. This kills that diagonal. The cyclic curvature remains identity, because it transforms by conjugation with the specialized G. Repeat through the finite d-1 diagonals. The process terminates and gives (14). Only finitely many bad root levels are introduced by each fixed rational gauge. For the Heisenberg matrix C=[1 u w; 0 1 v; 0 0 1], G=[1 p r; 0 1 q; 0 0 1], the equations are explicitly sigma(p)-p=u, sigma(q)-q=v, sigma(r)-r=w+u q. (15) The first two are additive. With these solved, set G0=[1 p 0;0 1 q;0 0 1]. Then sigma(G0)^(-1) C G0 has only central entry w+u q. Its cyclic curvature is identity, so the additive theorem solves the last equation. This retains the central cross term; solving only the two abelian equations would miss the regulator coordinate. Two solutions of (14) differ on the right by a constant upper unitriangular matrix over k(Q). A regular specified anchor can fix that ambiguity. A generic gauge alone need not preserve the integral cut lattice or the complete meridian specialization. The combination with multiplicative descent also proves the same existence assertion for every invertible upper triangular rational C, with G upper triangular. Each diagonal entry has cyclic norm one, so the rank-one theorem supplies its rational diagonal gauge. Apply that diagonal gauge first; the remaining matrix is upper unitriangular and the finite induction above applies. This covers a rationally split full flag without assuming unipotence in advance. In particular an affine source over such a flagged homogeneous module is handled by the augmented triangular matrix C_aff=[C c; 0 1]. If its full cyclic curvature is identity, the theorem solves its source together with the homogeneous transport. A rational gauge can be chosen with bottom row (0,...,0,1), so its top-right column is precisely an affine particular solution. This is stronger than solving the homogeneous norm while leaving the source arbitrary. ## 6. What this supplies to the proposed A-torsor argument This gives the requested group-theoretic termination in a precise setting: finite unipotence makes all transport equations solvable after their whole cyclotomic curvature has vanished. It includes the Heisenberg group underlying the marked regulator torsor, and is independent of crossing number, bridge number, or knot family. It does not infer that a general quantum A-module is unipotent. If the relevant comparison is a rank-one homogeneous line with a source, first trivialize the line by the full multiplicative theorem, then apply the additive theorem to its transformed source. More generally the triangular result handles every rationally split full flag and its affine source. A flag appearing only on a formal normal completion has not thereby supplied that rational flag. Rivin's positive maximizer supplies a marked algebraic geometric branch. The theorem here would descend an already constructed rational quantum/geometric comparison from its full cyclotomic transport identities, without choosing unrelated levelwise gauges. The actual comparison, its whole transport identities, its source and cut anchor, and the selected regulator norm still have to be proved. Algebraicity of the critical shape does not supply those identities by itself. The [regulator applicability audit](regulator_curvature_obstruction.md) makes the word comparison essential. A regular rational family with identity absolute curvature has a rationally trivial differential limit, even if its initial rational gauge is singular at Q=1. The marked regulator's logarithmic residues exclude such absolute triviality. Nor does equality of two noncentral matrix curvatures make their whole Hom curvature identity. The relative comparison object and its specified flat subobject must be constructed first. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Audit results](../experiments/additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent_results.json). [Independent proof audit](additive_cyclotomic_descent_independent_audit.md).

title: Adequacy excludes a fixed algebraic meridian period
text: # Adequacy excludes a fixed algebraic meridian period Research note, 26 October 2026. There is a uniform consequence of alternatingness relevant to the torsor problem: the actual color periods cannot be the traces of a fixed algebraic function of q and M. This does not exclude an algebraic period torsor with transcendental horizontal sections, or level-dependent algebraic root sections. It excludes a proposed finite algebraic section before one attempts to identify its norm with volume. The C_j(q) and meridian convention M=-q^j are those independently fixed in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). No Jones asymptotic is used. The result concerns exact degree spans. ## 1. An elementary bound for any fixed algebraic trace Suppose, for all sufficiently large positive integers j, C_j(q) satisfies a fixed nonzero relation F(q,-q^j,C_j(q))=0, F(q,M,Y)=sum_i f_i(q,M)Y^i, f_i in C[q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1)]. (1.1) Collect coefficients first and discard zero f_i. For large j every remaining f_i(q,-q^j) is nonzero: a collision of its q-exponents a+bj requires j=(a'-a)/(b-b'), leaving only finitely many exceptional positive j. All its q-exponents have absolute value at most A+Bj, for fixed A,B depending only on F. Let d_j be the largest q-exponent of the nonzero Laurent polynomial C_j. In (1.1), the largest exponent among deg_q f_i(q,-q^j)+i*d_j must occur at least twice. Otherwise its nonzero leading coefficient cannot cancel. Thus for two distinct indices i,k, d_j=(deg_q f_k(q,-q^j)-deg_q f_i(q,-q^j))/(i-k). It follows that |d_j|<=2(A+Bj). Applying the same argument to the least exponents bounds the smallest exponent as well. Hence span_q C_j=O(j). (1.2) This applies even if a different algebraic branch is selected for each j: the fixed polynomial relation is all that was used. A single overall framing monomial, even one with exponent quadratic in j, does not change the span and cannot evade the conclusion. The rational-function case is simpler. If C_j=p(q,-q^j)/r(q,-q^j) is Laurent polynomial, span(C_j)=span(p_j)-span(r_j)<=span(p_j)=O(j). Finite algebraic covers require the valuation argument above. ## 2. Exact extreme degrees for an adequate diagram We give the diagram proof rather than importing a degree theorem. Use the Kauffman bracket with empty value one, loop value delta=-A^2-A^(-2), and crossing expansion A times its A-smoothing plus A^(-1) times its B-smoothing. Let D be a connected knot diagram with c crossings. Let v_A,v_B be the circle counts in its all-A and all-B states. D is A-adequate if changing one crossing of the all-A state merges two distinct state circles; define B-adequacy analogously. For an A-adequate diagram, the all-A summand has top degree c+2v_A, with coefficient (-1)^v_A. Every other state has degree at least four lower: if k>=1 crossings are changed, the first change loses one circle and each later change adds at most one. Its circle count is at most v_A+k-2, so its top degree is at most c-2k+2(v_A+k-2)=c+2v_A-4. Thus the top coefficient cannot cancel. The all-B argument similarly gives bottom degree -c-2v_B. Let D^(n) be the n-parallel blackboard cable. Its crossing count is c*n^2, and its all-A and all-B circle counts are n*v_A,n*v_B. To see this directly, follow the arcs through the n by n crossing tile after uniform smoothing: it becomes n parallel copies of the original smoothing and creates no internal circle. A single changed cable crossing joins parallel copies belonging to distinct original state circles. Thus cabling preserves each adequacy condition. Consequently maxdeg_A <D^(n)>=c*n^2+2n*v_A, mindeg_A <D^(n)>=-c*n^2-2n*v_B. (2.1) ## 3. Passing from parallel strands to the actual color The j-dimensional color, n=j-1, is the Chebyshev threading S_0(X)=1, S_1(X)=X, S_(n+1)(X)=X*S_n(X)-S_(n-1)(X). (3.1) Thus S_n(D)=D^(n) plus a linear combination of cables D^(n-2r), r>=1. Both extreme degrees in (2.1) strictly move outward with n. The lower cables cannot cancel either extreme of the leading cable. For completeness, the color convention in (3.1) agrees, up to an overall color sign and framing monomial, with the fixed highest-weight periods. At generic q and n>=1 the tensor product of the fundamental module V_1 with V_n decomposes as V_1 tensor V_n = V_(n+1) direct-sum V_(n-1). With Delta(E)=E tensor K+1 tensor E, highest vectors are v_+ tensor w_0 and [n]_q*v_- tensor w_0-q^n*v_+ tensor w_1. Successive F-actions give dimensions n+2 and n; the usual E F^r highest-vector formula shows that these submodules are disjoint and exhaust the tensor product. Naturality of the finite R-matrix and additivity of the pivotal trace then give (3.1). This is the representation-ring calculation behind threading, not an additional asymptotic comparison theorem. The fundamental checked R-matrix has eigenvalues q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). Writing it as A*I+A^(-1)*e with A=q^(1/2) gives e^2=(-A^2-A^(-2))*e. This is the local bracket relation. An overall mirror convention changes exponent signs, and the zero-framing correction is a monomial; neither changes the span. The unreduced colored bracket therefore has A-span 2c*n^2+2n*(v_A+v_B). The unknot color S_n(delta) has A-span 4n. Dividing by this quantum dimension gives the reduced period C_j. Spans add under products of nonzero Laurent polynomials. Since q=A^2, we obtain span_q C_j=c*(j-1)^2+(v_A+v_B-2)*(j-1). (3.2) In particular every nontrivial adequate diagram gives genuinely quadratic growth, independently of its framing. For a connected reduced alternating diagram, its two state graphs are the checkerboard plane graph and its dual. A loop in either would be a nugatory crossing, so both adequacy conditions hold. Euler's formula gives v_A+v_B=c+2. Hence span_q C_j=c*j*(j-1). (3.3) Here c is the crossing count of that diagram; no crossing-minimality theorem is required for the argument. ## 4. Consequence for the period torsor Equations (1.2) and (3.2) contradict each other for every nontrivial adequate knot. Therefore there is no fixed finite algebraic meridian section whose traces at M=-q^j equal all the actual C_j(q), even allowing arbitrary algebraic branches in those specializations. This applies in particular to the entire class of hyperbolic alternating knots considered by the user. A large degree span supplies no lower bound at a particular root of unity; it does not exclude cancellation in the volume evaluation. This conclusion is compatible with a period of an algebraic connection or difference module. The underlying equations or torsor can be algebraic while its selected horizontal section is transcendental. It is also compatible with rational sections at each individual root level: their degrees or algebraic complexity can grow with that level. It is the fixed finite algebraic presentation in (1.1) that fails. The [affine extension construction](affine_quantum_a_period.md) uses this to rule out a split source extension whenever its geometric block has either stated nonresonance property. It does not yet identify that nonsplit class with the Bloch regulator or establish its archimedean norm growth. ## 5. The perturbative coefficients are polynomial in the color A second elementary fact is useful for the extension test. For every knot, with q=exp(h), C_j(exp(h))=sum_(k>=0) p_k(j)h^k, p_k in C[j]. (5.1) Only polynomiality is asserted; no diagonal summation, Alexander identity, convergence uniform in j, or large-color limit is used. Here is a direct proof from the cut braid. Write each checked crossing as its permutation times R or R^(-1). At each fixed h-order the unpermuted factors have finite expansions in tensor products of words in E,F,H: the r-th nilpotent R-term has factor (q-q^(-1))^r/[r]_q! of order h^r, the Cartan factor is exp(h H tensor H/2), and the pivotal factors are exp(h H). Negative crossings are formal inverses with the same finiteness property. Move the permutations to one end. Each coefficient is then a finite sum of a single permutation times such tensor words. The braid closure has one component, so that permutation is a single cycle. Its cut partial trace is the ordered product of the tensor words around this cycle; it creates no separate trace loop or color-dependent dimension factor. This identity follows by identifying the intermediate matrix indices along the cycle. At fixed h-order, reorder each product into PBW form F^a H^b E^c. The relation [E,F]=(exp(hH)-exp(-hH))/(exp(h)-exp(-h)) has polynomial coefficients in H at each h-order, so the reordering is finite. On the highest vector of color j, E kills it and F lowers its weight. Its highest component consequently evaluates the a=c=0 terms at H=j-1. It is polynomial in j. The zero-framing correction is the exponential of h times a polynomial in j and preserves this property. This proves (5.1) for the actual reduced cut period. This is the elementary polynomiality part of existing perturbative color theory; see the scope of [Rozansky, q-alg/9604005](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9604005). The stronger Melvin--Morton assertions are not premises here. ## 6. Coverage and independent checks Adequate colored-degree growth is existing coverage, including [Le, math/0407521](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407521) and [Kalfagianni, 1601.03307](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03307). Their stated scope is used for comparison; the extreme-state, cabling, threading, and valuation arguments above supply the proof here. No AJ or slope-conjecture theorem is imported. The [exact diagnostic script](../experiments/audit_adequacy_algebraic_periods.py) computes brackets by Temperley--Lieb multiplication and closure, forms the Chebyshev combination, divides by the actual unknot color, and checks the spans. It separately checks the circle counts and single-crossing adequacy of the cables. Examples are diagnostics of the uniform proof, not the scope of its statement. The [results](../experiments/adequacy_algebraic_periods_results.json) also check the fundamental local braid/bracket identity.

title: The actual Mellin period is transcendental for every nontrivial adequate knot
text: # The actual Mellin period is transcendental for every nontrivial adequate knot Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The actual Fourier--Mellin section has a bounded rational source and a specified formal source lattice. For every nontrivial adequate knot that selected section is transcendental over C(Q,X). This follows from the already proved quadratic color-degree span and an elementary valuation bound for algebraic power series, proved below without an Eisenstein theorem. This is a theorem about the actual pointed period for a wide knot class, including hyperbolic alternating knots. It does not identify its geometric A-component or prove its root-value volume growth. ## 1. Algebraic power series have linearly bounded coefficient valuations Let K be a characteristic-zero discretely valued field, with valuation v, valuation ring R and uniformizer pi. Completeness is unnecessary. Let f(X)=sum_(n>=0)c_n X^n in K[[X]] be algebraic over K(X). Then there are constants A,B>=0 such that v(c_n)>=-A-Bn for all nonzero coefficients. (1.1) Here and below zero coefficients satisfy the bound by v(0)=infinity. **Proof.** Choose a polynomial P(X,Z) in K[X,Z] for which P(X,f)=0 and P_Z(X,f)!=0. Such a choice exists because the minimal polynomial is separable in characteristic zero. Put m=ord_X P_Z(X,f), choose k>m, p(X)=sum_(n=0)^(k-1)c_n X^n, f=p+X^k w. Since p-f has order at least k>m, ord_X P_Z(X,p)=m. Taylor expansion gives a polynomial F(X,W)=X^(-m-k) P(X,p+X^k W) in K[X,W]. (1.2) Indeed the linear term is divisible by X^(m+k). The terms of degree j>=2 in W have exponent at least kj, and kj-(m+k)=k(j-1)-m>0. The constant term P(X,p) is divisible by X^(m+k) because substituting w makes the entire Taylor sum zero. At X=0, therefore, F(0,W)=aW+b, a=[X^m]P_Z(X,p)!=0. Let w_0=-b/a, which is the constant coefficient of w. Set W=w_0+V and divide by a. The resulting polynomial has the exact form V+X H(X,V)=0, H in K[X,V]. (1.3) This is the useful normalization: all other monomials have positive X order. Write H=sum h_(i,j) X^i V^j. Choose an integer B>=0 with v(h_(i,j))+B(i+1)>=0 for every nonzero h_(i,j). (1.4) There are finitely many coefficients, so such a B exists. Under X=pi^B x the selected series z(x)=V(pi^B x) satisfies z+x H_B(x,z)=0, H_B(x,z)=pi^B H(pi^B x,z) in R[x,z]. (1.5) Its constant term is zero. In the coefficient recursion, the coefficient of x^n on the right depends only on earlier coefficients of z because of the outer factor x. Induction shows z belongs to xR[[x]]. Thus, writing V=sum_(r>=1)v_r X^r, v(v_r)>=-Br. For n>=k+1 one has c_n=v_(n-k), and hence v(c_n)>=-B(n-k)>=-Bn. The finitely many coefficients through c_k are covered by increasing A. This proves (1.1). No analytic convergence and no a priori integrality of the original coefficients is used. The truncation removes the possible singular derivative, normalization gives one unit linear coefficient, and a single rescaling of X makes the finite recursion integral. ## 2. Consequence for rational-function coefficients in Q Apply the theorem to K=C(Q), first with the valuation at Q=0 and then with the valuation at Q=infinity. For a Laurent polynomial c_n(Q), these valuations are respectively v_0(c_n)=mindeg_Q c_n, v_infinity(c_n)=-maxdeg_Q c_n. Consequently an algebraic f(X) with Laurent-polynomial coefficients must satisfy mindeg_Q c_n>=-A_0-B_0n, maxdeg_Q c_n<= A_infinity+B_infinity n, span_Q c_n=O(n). (2.1) The algebraic relation may have arbitrary complex coefficients; their Q-valuations are zero. Thus this conclusion applies to algebraicity over C(Q,X), not only over the rational number field. It also covers any finite algebraic cover supplying a scalar branch in the selected integer-power series lattice. ## 3. The actual adequate color coefficients violate this bound The actual fixed-color functions C_n(Q) are Laurent polynomials, and the [adequacy proof](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) establishes their extreme degrees directly from adequate states, cabling and threading. For an adequate diagram with c>0 crossings and state-circle counts v_A,v_B it gives, in the q parameter, span_q C_n=c(n-1)^2+(v_A+v_B-2)(n-1). The [actual Q-polarization](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md) has Q=q^2 and C_n even in q, so span_Q C_n=(1/2)c(n-1)^2 +(1/2)(v_A+v_B-2)(n-1). (3.1) In particular it has a strictly positive quadratic coefficient. For a reduced connected alternating diagram this simplifies to span_Q C_n=c n(n-1)/2. The zero-framing monomial does not change the span. Choose the fixed n_0 of the actual Fourier--Mellin construction and retain its exact selected section Z(Q,X)=sum_(n>=n_0) C_n(Q) X^n. (3.2) If Z were algebraic over C(Q,X), equation (2.1) would bound its coefficient spans linearly. This contradicts (3.1) for every nontrivial adequate knot. We have therefore proved Z(Q,X) is transcendental over C(Q,X). (3.3) Subtracting or adding any fixed initial-color polynomial preserves algebraicity. Thus the conclusion holds for every fixed starting color, including the start-one generating period. ## 4. The precise source/lattice conclusion The actual bounded-source identity is P^M Z=B, Z in X^(n_0) C(Q)[[X]], (4.1) where B is the fixed nonzero Laurent source from finitely many small colors. The source-lattice condition makes this solution unique, by the leading-coefficient argument of the Fourier--Mellin construction. Hence no scalar section on a finite algebraic cover, satisfying this actual source and this formal lattice, can replace Z. The selected whole period is necessarily transcendental. There is a useful operator consequence. Every nonzero actual Q-operator of a nontrivial adequate knot has positive generic Y-exponent span. Otherwise all its Y exponents would be a single m, and its Fourier image would have the form A(Q,X)S^m with A!=0. Equation (4.1) would make S^m Z=B/A rational, and hence Z rational, contradicting (3.3). Thus the actual Mellin source object has positive difference order for this whole knot class; no artificial factor is needed to create that order. This is not a claim about the operator's specialized symbol at Q=1. This does not contradict algebraicity of the underlying equations, gluing place, comparison torsor or connection. Their marked periods can be transcendental. Nor does it contradict rationality of the root fibers: the original [cyclotomic residue construction](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives a rational function at each Q_N whose degree grows with N. The assertion is not generic affine nonsplitting without the lattice. A rational or algebraic particular solution outside X^(n_0)[[X]] could coexist with the selected transcendental solution, differing by a homogeneous solution. We have not excluded that possibility. The theorem excludes a pointed algebraic splitting compatible with the actual source lattice and coefficient cut. Finally, quadratic degree span gives no lower bound for a specified root value. Cancellation can still occur at Q_N. The exact identity <K>_N=[X^N]Z(Q_N,X), or its infinity-residue version, remains the original volume target. No exponential regulator estimate is inferred from transcendence alone. [Exact valuation-normalization audit](../experiments/audit_adequate_mellin_transcendence.py). [Results](../experiments/adequate_mellin_transcendence_results.json).

title: Entire adjacent source projectors and their lattice groupoid
text: # Entire adjacent source projectors and their lattice groupoid Research note, 26 October 2026. On three strands, the two adjacent actual meridian projectors have a joint two-channel polar form. Its overlap is an explicit original pivotal cut moment. The remaining projector terms are regular at completeness. This determines their full local meridian germs, beyond the residue. There is also a uniform obstruction: these two projectors cannot both preserve one finite meridian lattice. A comparison must retain their changes of lattice. This concerns the original ADO source operators, not a replacement quantum invariant. The selected geometric period and volume conjecture remain unproved. ## 1. Adjacent cups and caps give opposite source matrix units Keep N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and x=-M/q, u=Log M, R=C[[u]], delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), nu=(-1)^N rho^2. At M=1 use the actual cup C=vec(D^(-t)) and cap L=vec(gD)^t, where D_(N-1-a,a)=q^(a^2) and g=K^(1-N). Their two snakes are identities and LC=0. This follows directly by multiplying the two antidiagonal matrices: gD D^(-t)=I and D^(-t)gD=I. The remaining scalar uses x(1)^(1-N)q^((N-1)^2)=1. On W_0=V^(tensor 3) put i_1=C tensor I, i_2=I tensor C, c_1=L tensor I, c_2=I tensor L. The snakes and zero loop give c_1 i_2=c_2 i_1=I, c_1 i_1=c_2 i_2=0. (1.1) Consequently (i_1,i_2) and (c_2,c_1)^t split two copies of V, and the two nilpotents Pi_i=i_i c_i are opposite matrix units. In particular Pi_i^2=0, Pi_1 Pi_2 Pi_1=Pi_1, Pi_2 Pi_1 Pi_2=Pi_2, Tr(Pi_1 Pi_2)=N. (1.2) Tensoring the other strands gives the same identities and trace N^(b-2). This is the loop-zero Temperley--Lieb relation derived from the actual cups and caps. ## 2. Integral numerators and the charged simple block Let E_1,E_2 be the actual last Casimir projectors on positions 12 and 23 at generic M, and set T_i=delta E_i. They are rational matrices regular at M=1. To see this without evaluating a projector there, let Omega_i be the pair Casimir and let P_i be the integral projector onto the colliding c_0,c_last cluster. That unordered cluster is separated from the other roots at M=1; polynomial Bezout interpolation therefore gives regular P_i. Then T_i=(Omega_i-c_0)P_i, T_i^2=delta T_i, T_i(1)=nu Pi_i. (2.1) All these identities use the exact branch difference delta, not just its linear coefficient 4rho*u. Use the charged color P=V_z, z=-M^3/q, required by [the meridian charge calculation](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md). Let S be the total-Casimir projector of W=V_x^(tensor 3) onto its z block. Its complete Casimir is -2 and its derivative in the central polynomial is (-1)^(N+1)N^2. Thus S is integral. This block is P with multiplicity N. Each E_i S has rank one on that multiplicity space: the pair image V_(M^2) tensored with V_x contains P once in the explicit highest-vector fusion. The remaining operators F_i=E_i(1-S) (2.2) are integral idempotents. Indeed T_i(1)(1-S(1))=0 since Pi_i factors through the complete color V with Casimir -2. Their integral numerators T_i(1-S) are therefore divisible by delta in R. Their ordinary rank is N(N-1). This already isolates all poles in the charged block, uniformly in N. ## 3. The exact overlap is an actual cut moment Normalize the highest vector of the last two-color branch by h=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) h_a v_a tensor v_(N-1-a), h_0=1, h_(a+1)/h_a=-e_(N-1-a)(x)Q^(N-a-2)/[e_(a+1)(x)x]. Its coefficients are units near the complete color where needed. The covector vanishing on the F-descendants of all other branches has unnormalized coefficients lambda_a=(-1)^a x^(-a)Q^(a(a-1)/2). This follows from lambda_(a+1)+x^(-1)Q^a lambda_a=0, the two entries of the actual total F at degree N-2. Its normalization is Z=sum_a lambda_a h_a. On the total highest vectors h tensor v_0 and v_0 tensor h, the cross-projection coefficients of E_1 and E_2 are both lambda_(N-1)/Z. Only the component of pair degree N-1 can contribute; the others have zero last-branch projection. Thus the equality of these two coefficients is exact. The finite calculation in the appendix gives, with r=x^(-2), Z=(1+r^N)(1-rQ^(-1))/(1-r^2 Q^(-3)). Using r=Q/M^2 and lambda_(N-1)=(-1)^N q M^(1-N) yields delta*lambda_(N-1)/Z=A_N(M), A_N=(-1)^N rho (M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^N+M^(-N)). (3.1) The complete value is A_N(1)=nu. In particular A_N is a unit of R. Its full M^N+M^(-N)=M^(-N)(1+U) factor is retained. Comparison with the independently proved original pair moment in Section 7 of [the cut-density note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) shows A_N(M)=Phi_pair(T_1), A_N/delta=Phi_pair(E_last). (3.2) where Phi_pair is the original scalar pivotal partial trace, before multiplication by the full modified dimension. Hence the overlap is fixed by the actual cut, with its phase and peripheral function, rather than selected by a model normalization. ## 4. A joint regular frame for the full polar source Let theta=x(1)^(1-N). Define two P inclusions by highest vectors theta*h tensor v_0 and theta*v_0 tensor h and then the original total F descendants. Call them U_0,U_1. They are regular rational intertwiners and at completeness become i_1,i_2. The common theta is necessary to keep the original complete cup frame. On their images, (3.1) gives the integral matrices t_1=[delta A_N;0 0], t_2=[0 0;A_N delta]. (4.1) Here and below scalar matrices act on the two-copy multiplicity factor, with identity on P. There are regular rational rows r_1,r_2 with T_1 S=U_0 r_1 and T_2 S=U_1 r_2. For example, extract them with any coordinate left inverse of the primitive U_i; the factorization makes them H-linear. Their values on U=(U_0,U_1) form C=[delta A_N;A_N delta]. Its determinant delta^2-A_N^2 has value -nu^2 at M=1, hence is a unit. Set R=C^(-1)(r_1,r_2)^t. Then RU=I, T_i S=U t_i R, R(1)=(c_2,c_1)^t. (4.2) This proves an exact joint normal form, retaining every meridian coefficient of the actual projectors: E_1=U [1 A_N/delta;0 0]R+F_1, E_2=U [0 0;A_N/delta 1]R+F_2. (4.3) The regular F_i annihilate S and the common source corner e=UR. Both E_i vanish on the remaining N-2 multiplicity directions of S. Thus no additional polar channel has been discarded. Tensoring the construction with the remaining colors proves it for b>=3, with P replaced by the charged P_b of the preceding note. There is an intrinsic version of the source corner. On S put G=A_N^2-delta^2, e=[T_1T_2+T_2T_1-delta(T_1+T_2)]/G. (4.4) This is the same regular projector onto two copies of P. Its matrix units follow from (t_1t_2-delta t_1)/G=E_11, (t_2t_1-delta t_2)/G=E_22, (t_1-delta E_11)/A_N=E_12, (t_2-delta E_22)/A_N=E_21. (4.5) Thus the integral numerators generate Mat_2(R) on the source multiplicity space. Their joint comparison torsor, with the charged P fixed, is R^times: End_H(P)=R and a simultaneous intertwiner of the full matrix algebra is scalar. This specifies the local torsor and its trace calibration on three strands. After tensoring, the unrestricted comparison group is instead End_H(P_b)^times unless the spectator action is also fixed. Identifying such a torsor with a triangulation realization still requires its actual source operators and overlap to be matched. The [subsequent spectral-source calculation](actual_braid_group_and_spectral_source.md#6-a-cover-can-split-the-spectral-algebra-instead-of-killing-it) places these formulas in a universal rank-four algebra. For two numerators with t_i^2=delta t_i, the expression z=t_1t_2+t_2t_1-delta(t_1+t_2) is central. On the cover A^2=z+delta^2, with A,z units, (4.5) are its explicit matrix units. The actual root is exactly (3.1). This is a spectral splitting and scalar-torsor reduction, not nilpotence of the full source group. Genuine pure braid powers have a connected SL_2 quotient; their invariant plane is not generally this particular two-cup corner. ## 5. Whole sewn cuts now have an exact source decomposition For any integral whole knot operator B(M), let B_ij=R_i B U_j. The original calibrated rectangular trace identity gives mathfrak_t_W(B E_1) =mathfrak_t_P(B_00)+(A_N/delta)mathfrak_t_P(B_10) +mathfrak_t_W(B F_1), mathfrak_t_W(B E_2) =mathfrak_t_P(B_11)+(A_N/delta)mathfrak_t_P(B_01) +mathfrak_t_W(B F_2). (5.1) These are identities of full meridian germs, not only residues. The P trace uses the original d_N(M^3), including the exact dimension ratio already recorded in the charged-source note. The full affine source coefficient 1+U^(-1) multiplies these entire identities and is retained before specialization. The regular terms can cancel the source diagonal term. For example, on three strands the full cut of E_i itself is zero, while mathfrak_t_P(I)=d_N(M^3). Consequently mathfrak_t_W(F_i)=-d_N(M^3). (5.2) No positivity or noncancellation assertion follows from the nonzero source corner or its perfect bilinear trace. There is a useful exact simplification only after retaining the whole affine coefficient. For c=1+U^(-1), equation (3.1) gives c A_N/delta =(-1)^N M^(1-N)(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^2-1). (5.3) Indeed c/(M^N+M^(-N))=M^(-N). Thus the 1+U factor cancels in the full off-diagonal source, with its phase and monomial left explicit. Its pole is precisely Y-1, the meridian divisor in [the actual normal-period construction](peripheral_normal_period.md). This is a rational identity before specialization, not a reset of a numerical factor at M=1. It does not identify the full global normal module or its selected knot period. ## 6. No one finite lattice can regularize adjacent projectors From (4.3), on the source corner Tr(E_1E_2)=N A_N^2/delta^2. The remaining trace is regular, since it comes from F_1F_2. As delta=4rho*u+O(u^2) and A_N(1)=(-1)^N rho^2, Tr_(W_b)(E_1E_2) =N^(b-2)rho^2/(16u^2)+O(u^(-1)). (6.1) The leading coefficient is nonzero in characteristic zero. If a full finite R-lattice were stable under both projectors, their product would be an integral endomorphism and its ordinary trace would belong to R. Equation (6.1), invariant under every meromorphic change of basis, contradicts this. This proof does not require H-linearity of the hypothetical lattice. In fact the traces of (E_1E_2)^m have pole order 2m, so the algebra of both unscaled projectors is not contained in a finite integral endomorphism order. Multiplying either projector by a meridian unit, including a peripheral factor with nonzero complete value, does not remove this obstruction. Each projector separately has an elementary stable lattice. For the source pair, replacing P direct_sum P by delta^(-1)P direct_sum P gives the matrices E_1 -> [1 A_N;0 0], E_2 -> [0 0;A_N/delta^2 1]. (6.2) Thus one elementary change shifts the pole into the adjacent operator with order two. The appropriate retained data form a groupoid of lattices and their source maps. The integral numerators T_i and their polar quotients must stay distinguished. This does not disprove a relative triangulation comparison with different lattices on its charts. It rules out a common finite regularization of these actual source arrows. ## 7. What remains and exact verification The entire local adjacent polar source is now explicit, with its charged object, overlap, trace, regular terms and lattice obstruction. This removes the restriction of the earlier sewn calculation to a residue. Its common comparison group is scalar only after the ordered integral numerators have been matched. These R-unit inversions are fixed-level meridian statements. The value A_N(1)=(-1)^N rho^2 tends to zero as N grows, so they are not automatically unit inversions in the joint quantum--meridian completion S=C[[u,h]] used for the point-source model. A comparison of those two realizations must retain this additional lattice information. No cross-level norm bound is inferred from the frame. The subsequent [uniform Frobenius source base](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md) now resolves this coefficient degeneration on a specified meridian chart. It retains w=M^N and the root phases, records the exceptional rho line, and extends the normalized two-channel algebra. Its marked Frobenius period also evaluates the full original cap normalization. This concerns the coefficient algebra; the full color object and selected knot period have not thereby been extended across levels. The full meridian atlas still contains its specified transitions, and their whole-germ cancellation must be compared with the relative triangulation source. The actual selected section has not been identified with the marked geometric period. Neither the formal normal-block comparison nor (5.1) proves the regulator norm across levels. The volume conjecture remains unproved. The finite sum in the appendix has existing coverage as the [first q-Chu--Vandermonde identity, DLMF 17.6.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/17.6.E2). The formula and scope were checked after deriving our independent certificate. No published proof technique is imported. The cup/cap relations and matrix-algebra facts are existing elementary theory; no novelty is claimed for them. The calculation here fixes the actual overlap, charge and pole data in the original conventions. [The audit](../experiments/audit_adjacent_polar_source.py) checks the generic telescoping certificate and the universal two-by-two relations symbolically. Six complete original tensor cases verify the opposite cup/cap units and vanishing of the regular-remainder numerators. Twelve generic pairs of actual full projectors verify the charged inclusions, retractions, overlap, regular idempotents and their ranks and full modified cuts. Forty-eight full tensor-cut decompositions for the identity and figure-eight words check (5.1), with original framing and normalization. Even and odd composite levels are included. [Results](../experiments/adjacent_polar_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_adjacent_polar_source.py ## Appendix. An independent finite-sum certificate From the actual highest-vector recurrence, at the primitive root Q, Z=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) [(r^(-1)Q^2;Q)_k/(r;Q)_k] *(r^2 Q^(-3))^k. For a generic base Q define f_(n,k)={n choose k}_Q (a;Q)_k(c Q^k;Q)_(n-k) *(-c/a)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2). Let t=Q^n, z=Q^k. The ratio f_(n+1,k+1)/f_(n+1,k) is R(z)=-(c/a)(z-Q t)(1-a z)/[(1-Qz)(1-cz)]. Set H(z)=-Q t(1-z)(1-cz/Q)/[z(1-Q t)(1-c t)]. Direct rational simplification gives R(z)H(Qz)-H(z) =1-(1-(c/a)t)(1-Q t/z)/[(1-Q t)(1-c t)]. Multiplication by f_(n+1,k), followed by summation, telescopes; the two boundary terms vanish. Hence F_n=sum_k f_(n,k) satisfies F_(n+1)=(1-cQ^n/a)F_n and F_0=1. This proves sum_(k=0)^n [(Q^(-n);Q)_k(a;Q)_k/ ((Q;Q)_k(c;Q)_k)](cQ^n/a)^k =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. Specialize n=N-1, a=r^(-1)Q^2, c=r after proving this rational identity. The factors (Q;Q)_k are nonzero for k<N, and Q^(-n)=Q cancels the matching numerator and denominator. Thus Z=(r^2 Q^(-2);Q)_(N-1)/(r;Q)_(N-1) =(1+r^N)(1-rQ^(-1))/(1-r^2 Q^(-3)). All cancellations are whole rational identities. At the complete color the displayed final denominator is nonzero and Z has its required simple zero. No infinite product or root asymptotic is used.

title: The actual ADO threaded character and a separating source projector
text: # The actual ADO threaded character and a separating source projector Research note, 26 October 2026. This proves an exact, uniform formula for Chebyshev-threaded interior loops in the specified ADO evaluation. It retains the odd-thread signs and framing phases and then isolates a parity-independent even character. A null-homologous loop separates this character from the complete hyperbolic character for every hyperbolic knot. Thus identifying fixed central eigenlines is the wrong proposed comparison in that setting. A source extension can still encode the period as a distinguished splitting; a precise projector lemma states what an actual construction would have to provide. The proof uses the fixed unrolled matrices and elementary exact sequences, not a published Chebyshev--Frobenius or quantum-trace theorem. No quantum invariant or state is replaced. The volume conjecture and the construction of the required geometric source extension remain unproved. ## 1. Fixed evaluation and actual annular threading Let K be an oriented zero-framed knot, q=exp(pi*i/N), N>=2. Use the literature color V_alpha and parameters x=q^alpha, M=-qx, Y=M^2, U=Y^N=M^(2N). The pivot is K^(1-N). The core cut evaluation is the one already fixed in [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Write F_N^L(M) for its reduced scalar with an additional framed fundamental-color link L in the complement; N_N^L=d_N F_N^L is the full period. The fundamental color W and its exact framed skein relation are those of [the peripheral-fusion calculation](actual_peripheral_fusion.md). For a further framed oriented loop gamma disjoint from L and K, let C_n(gamma) be its annular Chebyshev threading, with C_0(X)=2, C_1(X)=X, C_(n+1)(X)=X C_n(X)-C_(n-1)(X). Products mean framed parallels, and the definition is linear on the resulting link combinations. It has integer coefficients and uses no singular Jones--Wenzl projector. Choose the Seifert zero framing in S^3 as reference, and write f for gamma's framing, ell=lk(gamma,K), b=lk(gamma,L), the sum over the components of L. ## 2. Integral Weyl modules without divided-factorial denominators For m>=0 define D_m on u_0,...,u_m by H u_j=(m-2j)u_j, K u_j=q^(m-2j)u_j, E u_j=[m-j+1]u_(j-1), F u_j=[j+1]u_(j+1). These formulas have no factorial denominators. The identity [j+1][m-j]-[j][m-j+1]=[m-2j] checks the commutator, and the H and K relations follow directly from the weights. At the specified root E^N=F^N=0: every product of N consecutive quantum integers contains a multiple of N. They are therefore actual weight modules for the same restricted unrolled quantum group, even when m>=N. Only the auxiliary loop's color is changed here; the core color and its reduced or full normalization stay fixed. For every m>=1 there is the exact sequence 0 -> D_(m+1) -> W tensor D_m -> D_(m-1) -> 0. (2.1) Here are explicit maps, valid before and after root specialization: i(v_j)=q^(-j)w_0 tensor u_j+w_1 tensor u_(j-1), pi(w_0 tensor u_j)=t_(j-1), pi(w_1 tensor u_j)=-q^(-j-1)t_j, where missing endpoint vectors are zero. They preserve H and K. Substitution in Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F verifies E and F using [j+1]=q[j]+q^(-j) and q[j+1]-[j]=q^(j+1). The map i is injective, pi is surjective, and pi*i=0. Their dimensions give exactness. All these assertions use unit matrix entries and do not divide by [N]. Also W tensor D_0=D_1. Consequently in the Grothendieck group of these actual modules, [D_m]=U_m([W]/2), C_n([W])=[D_n]-[D_(n-2)], n>=2. (2.2) This follows recursively from (2.1); it is not a generic-q semisimplicity argument specialized through a pole. ## 3. Root subquotients, including their pivots and twists At m=N there is the additional exact sequence 0 -> D_(N-2) -> D_N -> C_(+N) direct-sum C_(-N) ->0, (3.1) where C_h is the one-dimensional module with H=h, K=q^h, E=F=0. The submodule map is u_a -> [a+1]v_(a+1), 0<=a<N-1. These coefficients are nonzero. The quotient consists of the two endpoint weights +N and -N. The endpoint transitions to the quotient vanish because [N]=0. This checks every generator and proves (3.1). Combining (2.2) and (3.1), C_N([W])=[C_(+N)]+[C_(-N)]. (3.2) For delta_N=(-1)^(N-1), both one-dimensional colors have dim_q(C_(+/-N))=delta_N, theta(C_(+/-N))=delta_N*i^N. (3.3) Indeed their pivot is q^((1-N)h), their crossing is q^(h^2/2), and closing that crossing gives the twist q^(h^2/2+(1-N)h). These are exactly (3.3) at h=+/-N. No framing phase is omitted. The polynomial identity C_(2N)(X)=C_N(X)^2-2 and tensoring one-dimensional colors then give C_(2N)([W])=[C_(+2N)]+[C_(-2N)]. (3.4) These latter colors have pivot one, twist one, and trivial double braiding with W. Their double braiding with V_alpha is the scalar x^(+/-2N)=M^(+/-2N). This is the even character used below. It does not silently replace the odd-thread data (3.3). ## 4. Why these Grothendieck identities compute the actual knot period The closed auxiliary-component evaluation is additive in a short exact sequence of colors. A direct proof uses a braid with the core cut and a basis adapted to the auxiliary submodule. The finite R, its inverse and the pivot preserve the filtration on each colored strand, with the strand positions exchanged at a crossing. A state can move only down the filtration along the underlying auxiliary component. Closing its trace forces it to return to its initial filtration piece; therefore every contributing state stays in one graded piece around that entire component. Summing those pieces gives exactly the two subquotient-colored evaluations. Separate closed components are treated independently. This is filtered linear algebra on the literal cut contraction, not an assumption about additivity of a modified trace on the core. Naturality of R and the tensor-product crossing identities proved in the peripheral note identify tensor colors with framed parallels. Thus (3.2)--(3.4) apply to the stated annular threadings for arbitrary gamma, including knotted gamma and diagrams with auxiliary self-crossings. For C_h, h=+/-N, the ratio between the two possible crossings with a core strand is the scalar monodromy q^(hH)=x^(+/-N). With a W strand it is -1. Unlinking the auxiliary component by crossing changes therefore records only its linking numbers. Its remaining one-dimensional knot evaluation is its pivotal dimension times its framing twist. This last statement can also be checked directly: on a one-component braid with B strands and writhe w, the zero-framing value is g^(B-w)=g, since g=+/-1 and B-w is odd. Its self-crossing scalar cancels against the twist. We obtain the exact whole-germ formulas F_N^(L union C_N(gamma)) =delta_N*(delta_N*i^N)^f*(-1)^b *(x^(N ell)+x^(-N ell))*F_N^L, F_N^(L union C_(2N)(gamma)) =(U^ell+U^(-ell))*F_N^L. (4.1) In the first line x^N=delta_N*M^N, so its multiplier can also be written delta_N^(ell+1)*(delta_N*i^N)^f*(-1)^b times M^(N ell)+M^(-N ell). In the second line every auxiliary framing and W-linking phase cancels exactly. The same equations hold for the full period N_N^L, retaining the entire modified dimension. For the boundary meridian ell=1 and f=b=0, the first equation is C_N(M+M^(-1))=M^N+M^(-N). For the preferred parallel ell=0, it is 2delta_N, agreeing with the full ADO character T^N=(-1)^(N-1). These provide independent checks of both signs. No universal Chebyshev homomorphism at degree 2N, or an unproved identification of its source skein parameter, is asserted. Equation (4.1) is the specific evaluation identity proved here, including the actual fourth-root phases at degree N. ## 5. The marked ramified fibre has the trivial even character The even eigenvalues in (4.1) are the squared-trace coordinates of the abelian character with meridian rho_U^ab(mu)=diag(U^(1/2),U^(-1/2)): (tr rho_U^ab(gamma))^2-2=U^ell+U^(-ell). (5.1) The square-root sign is irrelevant to this coordinate. At U=1 the value is two for every gamma. This includes the whole marked fibre of [ramified Weyl descent](ramified_weyl_fibre.md): in its coordinate z=(U-1)/(U+1), U^ell+U^(-ell) is even with constant term two. It multiplies both a_0 and b_0 by two. No extra odd coefficient changes the complete normal functional. In particular a null-homologous gamma has ell=0, and its even threading acts by exactly two on the entire meromorphic family, not just at the complete point. This also survives the canonical polar subtraction and its affine source equation: each part is multiplied by the same constant two. This does not require K_N to be nonzero. The ordinary anchor (a_0)_1/(Q-1)=1 makes the actual marked fibre nonzero at every level. Nor does (5.1) contradict a hyperbolic semiclassical critical point: the threading degree 2N grows with the level. Fixed small observables and fixed root-central characters are different data. ## 6. A null-homologous geometric separator for every hyperbolic knot Let rho_hyp be the complete holonomy. Two conjugates of a cusp meridian have distinct fixed points: otherwise the meridian conjugates, which generate the knot group, would all preserve one point, contradicting the non-elementary complete holonomy. After conjugation and harmless SL_2 signs, write them as p=[1 1;0 1], q=[1 0;s 1], s!=0. A direct multiplication gives tr[p^a,q]=2+a^2*s^2, (tr[p^a,q])^2-4=a^2*s^2*(a^2*s^2+4). (6.1) The choices a=1 and a=2 cannot both make the second expression zero when s!=0. Thus one of the two commutator words gamma has lk(gamma,K)=0, g_gamma(rho_hyp):=(tr rho_hyp(gamma))^2-2 !=2. (6.2) Represent the word by an embedded loop and choose its framing. The even threading formula is independent of that framing. The squared trace is independent of the lift to SL_2. The witness is uniform; no alternatingness or knot table is used. The positive ideal triangulation represents this same complete holonomy, so g_gamma-2 is a unit in its local geometric character ring. This is a precise interior-character distinction not detected by the common parabolic peripheral values alone. ## 7. What a fixed-central-character comparison can and cannot identify Suppose a proposed geometric root realization identifies the even threaded observable C_(2N)(gamma) with the scalar g_gamma(rho)=(tr rho(gamma))^2-2. This is explicit comparison data; no published quantum-trace Frobenius theorem is being assumed to establish it here. At the hyperbolic point, (6.2) and the actual evaluation (5.1) give distinct eigenvalues. Any intertwiner preserving this observable between the actual evaluation fibre and that fixed geometric central-character fibre must be zero: its matrix Phi satisfies (g_gamma(rho_hyp)-2)*Phi=0. The same holds locally because the difference is a unit. A scalar Hilbert-90 frame change or finite faithfully flat cover cannot change these scalar eigenvalues. In particular a direct equality of these two *fixed central eigenlines* cannot be the missing state comparison. This is not an obstruction to a source extension, a comparison only after the correct relative pushforward, or a varying-centre realization with a hyperbolic semiclassical saddle. Such a second realization need not have the fixed hyperbolic root character. It also does not show that the entire cyclic module of an actual operator lacks geometric factors: its selected evaluation is a particular quotient, and the distinction matters. ## 8. A separating observable can select the source period exactly There is a useful positive consequence for the extension approach. Over a difference field (F,sigma), take a specified source system sigma(w)=A_aug*w, A_aug=[ C b;0 1 ]. Suppose it carries an actual difference endomorphism X_gamma=[ G d_gamma;0 2 ], sigma(X_gamma)*A_aug=A_aug*X_gamma, (8.1) and 2I-G is invertible. Its unique eigenvector of eigenvalue two whose source coordinate is one is w=(v,1), v=(2I-G)^(-1)*d_gamma. (8.2) This vector is automatically horizontal. Applying sigma to its eigenvalue equation and using (8.1) shows that both sigma(w) and A_aug*w are eigenvectors of sigma(X_gamma) with eigenvalue two and last coordinate one. Invertibility gives uniqueness, hence sigma(w)=A_aug*w. This proves the source equation, without a monodromy computation or a root-rank hypothesis. Equivalently the eigenline projector is P_2=[0 (2I-G)^(-1)d_gamma;0 1], P_2^2=P_2. It preserves the difference structure by (8.1). If G=g_gamma I is a fixed geometric central character, the separator (6.2) makes the inverse a regular scalar near the complete point. Its denominator supplies no growing-level volume exponent. Any such exponent must remain in the actual source coefficient d_gamma and its selected period pairing. The even threading theorem supplies the eigenvalue two for the actual null-homologous observable. The geometric triangulation supplies a classical separator with g_gamma!=2. What is still missing is construction of an actual relative gluing/source system with the endomorphism (8.1), its off-diagonal coefficient, and the marked normal functional. Neither block can be chosen to force the desired value. The lemma is a criterion for that construction, not a proof that it has already been achieved. Specializing a generic nonsplit source extension to a split root-level extension causes no contradiction: its distinguished splitting (8.2) can still carry large periods. Splitting and the norm of the specified splitting are separate statements. If a specified generic source class is nonsplit, a separating endomorphism of the form (8.1) cannot exist over that generic difference field: (8.2) would split it. It cannot arise after a finite sigma-stable algebraic cover either, by the normalized-trace descent proved in [the affine note](affine_quantum_a_period.md). The actual threaded observables have degree 2N and depend on the level. Their root-level existence supplies no such fixed generic endomorphism. This retains the distinction between an algebraic evaluation at each level and a fixed-degree presentation across all levels. ## 9. Literature coverage and what has not been imported The common skein/gluing framework is already covered by [Garoufalidis--Yu, A quantum trace map for 3-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12424) and [Panitch--Park, 3d Quantum Trace Map](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12850). The later [Chen--Kricker, On 3d Quantum Trace Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13268) advertises partial comparison of these constructions. Their abstracts and the scope of the quantum-gluing definition were consulted for coverage. No global trace-map, equivalence, Frobenius-compatibility, or knot-state-comparison proof from these works is a premise here. In particular no phase identification between their quantum parameters and the actual ADO parameters is inferred by citation. Chebyshev threading and root-of-unity representation theory have existing coverage; no novelty is claimed for that framework or for the elementary spectral projector.
