In particular (4) becomes the all-level theorem P_W=chi_W sum_lambda gamma_lambda rho_0[ v(Q^2 z) a_lambda u(z) ] =chi_W sum_lambda gamma_lambda rho_0[ J_Q(z) u(z)^-1 a_lambda u(z) ]. (6) Every inverse is an honest finite polynomial in the nilpotent z. The factor Q^2 in the first line is essential, even at an original root. Both lines are exact source identities and include ALL original word factors; neither is a formal geometric saddle formula. For the original same-color b-strand word, gamma_lambda simplifies to gamma_(t,j)=N x^(b(1-N)) Q^(1-j). (7) At |x|=1 this factor has modulus N. This observation gives no bound for the transformed word coefficients a_lambda, their Euler conjugates or cancellation between lambda terms. The fusion and Euler maps have not been proved uniformly well conditioned in the required norm. The variable f in the coefficient algebra acts by LEFT multiplication when it represents the physical TOTAL F. The a_lambda and their Euler conjugation in (6) belong to the RIGHT coefficient algebra. Conjugating the physical word by u(physical total F) would instead do nothing, since that word commutes with total F. Retaining this distinction is necessary in any subsequent physical/geometric symbol comparison. ## 4. The coefficient source is exactly a two-point divided difference There is an exact polynomial-evaluation form of (6). First reduce the Euler-conjugated word in the canonical free basis of A_0: b_lambda=u(z)^-1 a_lambda u(z) =sum_(k,j=0)^(N-1) b_(lambda,k,j) f^k e_j, B_lambda(Z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) b_(lambda,k,0) x_1^-k Z^k. Then the original period is exactly P_W=chi_W x_1^(N-1)/(1-Q) sum_lambda gamma_lambda [B_lambda(1)-B_lambda(Q^-1)]. (8) Indeed the power series coefficients of J_Q(Z) below degree N are [Z^m]J_Q(Z)=(1-Q^(m+1))/(1-Q). For the term b_(k,0), the top coefficient uses m=N-1-k, so its factor is x_1^(N-1-k)(1-Q^-k)/(1-Q). Summing gives (8), with its sign, normalization and actual root branches fixed. No limiting argument or contour deformation is involved. The canonical reduction BEFORE the two evaluations is essential. Evaluation Z=1 is not a homomorphism from the nilpotent algebra Z^N=0 to the coefficient field. In particular a lift changed by Z^(N+1), which is zero in that algebra, would change the displayed two-point difference if evaluated without first reducing it. Thus (8) is an exact LINEAR source period of the normal form; it is not a regular scalar-clock specialization of the root representation. At the complex root, |1/(1-Q)|=O(N). Every explicit scalar in this conversion has at most polynomial size on the unit-color arc for fixed braid index. This does not bound B_lambda at its two arguments: their coefficients are the full N-dependent transformed word, and their differences and sum can cancel. Formula (8) supplies no unproved nonvanishing or rigidity assumption. There is a precise quantitative form for the original complete reduced invariant. Put Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), x_N=-exp(-pi*i/N). For b>=3 label the heads lambda=(t,j) as in (1); for b=2 there is one head and take j=0. Define, without dividing by any invariant, S_N=sum_lambda Q_N^-j [B_lambda(1)-B_lambda(Q_N^-1)]. (9) For the actual complete word every retained external crossing/framing factor, apart from d_N, has modulus one, and |d_N(1)|=1/N. Removing d_N to return from the full ADO period to the original reduced Kashaev period gives the EXACT modulus identity |Kashaev_N(K)|=N/|1-Q_N| * |S_N|. (10) One can equivalently keep the corresponding unit phase from chi_W, x_N and Q_N rather than pass to absolute values. It is fixed by the original word; it has not been chosen to normalize a new solution. Formula (10) also holds when either side vanishes. Since N/|1-Q_N|=O(N^2), the original volume conjecture is equivalent to the definite estimate (2pi/N) log|S_N| -> Vol(S^3 minus K). (11) Equation (11) is UNPROVED in general. It is a critical-path metric for this exact source representation, not a derived limit theorem. In particular (9) keeps all N-dependence of the actual transformed word and all possible endpoint/tail cancellation. No estimate for it follows from the polynomial size of the factors in (10). ## 5. Scope on the critical path Formula (6) reaches arbitrary braid index and in particular actual hyperbolic-knot words. It supplies the original finite cap with a universal rational kernel after a specified word transform, so there is no need to guess a double-pole weight or restrict this source calculation to a two-strand family. It does not identify z with the second-cut Fourier momentum p. It does not identify the nilpotent fixed-root Borel center with the classical geometric representation germ. It does not identify a selected nonzero geometric cycle, prove subexponential coefficients, or control the remaining sectors. It also does not supply a moving-q normal extension merely by keeping M at a fixed original root. The [exact Fourier localization](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) places the original complete value at the resonant row. The next critical comparison can now be posed with the ACTUAL all-strand coefficient source (6), instead of a hypothetical unsourced density. The [exact fusion-clock equation](actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.md) specifies a polynomial relation of its right Euler argument to physical clocks, with its nilpotent denominator retained. One still needs a source-compatible geometric period transform of that expression and the sharp regulator norm. Gates C--E remain open. ## 6. Exact and independent verification The [original-matrix audit](../experiments/audit_all_strand_cauchy_cap.py) and its [saved results](../experiments/all_strand_cauchy_cap_results.json) pass on 18 signed-word cases of braid indices 2,3,4 and levels 2--5, with 60 diagonal tail-head blocks. They independently evaluate the original physical pivotal cap, (6) and the exact two-point formula (8), retaining the actual half-Cartan, framing and complete modified-dimension factors. The unequal-color cap (5) is checked on 203 basis elements at levels 2–8 and six unequal-color tail decompositions. The theorem rests on the basis and trace proof above; these tests check its conventions and implementation.

title: Alternating generator signs do not make the charged-flow maximum a real saddle
text: # Alternating generator signs do not make the charged-flow maximum a real saddle 28 October 2026. This is an exact obstruction in the original enhanced Kashaev source. It applies at arbitrary braid width. It concerns a real charged-flow approach, not the existence of a selected complex geometric cycle or the volume conjecture itself. ## 1. A source-retaining local variation at arbitrary width Use the original crossings and actual inverse of [the charged-state note](original_crossing_winding_convexity.md). Put Q=exp(2 pi i/N). Suppose that the first crossing touching the cut head is sigma_1^epsilon, epsilon=+1 or -1. Suppose its outgoing second head next meets sigma_2^(-epsilon), before any other crossing touching that head. Crossings on disjoint heads can occur in between. This includes arbitrary width weaving blocks beginning sigma_1^epsilon sigma_2^(-epsilon), and does not restrict the rest of the word to a twist family. The [actual source theorem](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md) forces the first head to remain zero and the incoming second head of this first cut crossing to equal 1. Call its outgoing second-head color D. The first local factor is consequently T+_(D,1)=Q^D, T-_(D,1)=Q^(-1), (1) for 1<=D<N. All original pivot, framing, Cartan, and other crossing factors remain in the whole path weight W(D). At the next crossing, write its input as (D,b), its output as (c,d), and its original corner indices as u=[b-D-1], v=[D-c], t=[c-d], h=[d-b], u+v+t+h=N-1. (2) Fix every other color in the actual source path. Assume D+1<N and that the variation D -> D+1 remains in this same support chamber, so u>=1, u -> u-1 and v -> v+1 without a residue wrap. Then the WHOLE original summand obeys the exact identity W(D+1)/W(D) = sin(pi u/N)/sin(pi(v+1)/N) * exp[-epsilon*pi*i*(t+h)/N]. (3) The magnitude ratio in (3) is strictly positive. Only the two displayed crossings depend on D; none of the exterior source factors has been replaced by an arbitrary co-source or discarded. For epsilon=+1, the positive second-crossing coefficient has ratio Q^(t+h) (1-Q^u)/(1-Q^(-(v+1))). Its actual inverse has ratio Q^(-1) times the conjugate of this expression. Multiplying by the ratio Q from (1) gives Q^(-(t+h)) (1-Q^(-u))/(1-Q^(v+1)). (4) Using the sine forms of the two linear factors and the EXACT charge in (2) proves (3). For epsilon=-1 the ratio of the first factor in (1) is one; the positive second crossing gives the conjugate sine-phase in (3). This proves both signs at every N, including even and composite levels, without a semiclassical approximation. ## 2. Consequence for the proposed real-saddle mechanism Let a source-support region have a limiting interior direction D/N=z, and let tau=(t+h)/N tend to a number in (0,1]. Equation (3) says that the limiting phase derivative of the whole summand in this direction is partial_z Theta = -epsilon*pi*tau modulo 2*pi. (5) It cannot vanish, even after adding an integer lattice phase. Thus the leading complex action cannot have a REAL critical point on such a region. In particular, a real maximizer of the strictly concave absolute action is not thereby a critical point of the original complex state. If a real critical point is sought in a region where this local color variation is free, (5) forces tau=0. Since the corners are nonnegative, t=h=0 in the limiting configuration. The opposite-sign crossing then has at most two nonzero corners, with sum one, and its limiting absolute entropy is zero. This is a forced degeneracy, not the nondegenerate positive chart contemplated in a direct Laplace argument. This argument does not apply at a face where the D variation is no longer free. Nor does it rule out complex saddles or a source-preserving complex contour homotopy. It shows that such further transport cannot be replaced by the assertion that alternating generator signs automatically make the original real charged-flow optimizer stationary. ## 3. The actual figure-eight source gives an interior strict maximum For the word (sigma_1 sigma_2^(-1))^2, consider the actual supported paths (0,1,B+1) -> (0,D,B+1) -> (0,E,F) -> (0,0,F) -> (0,0,B). (6) In the full-dimensional limiting chamber 0<F<E<D<B<1, (7) letters now denote colors divided by N. The four corner lists tend to (0,0,1-D,D), (B-D,D-E,E-F,1+F-B), (E,0,0,1-E), (F,0,1-B,B-F). (8) The two cut end crossings have zero limiting absolute action. With Lambda'(theta)=-log(2 sin theta), the whole absolute action is H=(1/pi)[Lambda(pi(B-D))+Lambda(pi(D-E)) +Lambda(pi(E-F))+Lambda(pi(1+F-B)) +Lambda(pi F)+Lambda(pi(1-B)) +Lambda(pi(B-F))]. (9) This has a unique strict interior maximum on the closure of (7). Indeed fix s=B-F. The first three angles sum to s, so strict concavity of Lambda on that fixed-charge simplex makes them all s/3. For the two remaining free angles F and 1-B, their sum is 1-s; strict concavity makes both (1-s)/2. Finally Lambda(pi(1-s))+Lambda(pi s)=0 cancels, leaving H_red(s)=[3 Lambda(pi s/3) +2 Lambda(pi(1-s)/2)]/pi, H_red'(s)=log[cos(pi s/2)/sin(pi s/3)]. (10) This derivative changes sign only at s=3/5, from positive to negative. The unique maximum is therefore (B,D,E,F)=(4/5,3/5,2/5,1/5), H_max=5 Lambda(pi/5)/pi=0.7936696457597476... . (11) Here the entropy statement only concerns this actual source chamber; no identification of its maximum with a knot volume is made. The retained leading phase, computed from the original quadratic crossing phases with signs (+,-,+,-), is, modulo lattice-invisible linear phases, Theta/pi=BD-2BF-DE-D+EF+E+F. (12) At the strict absolute maximum its gradient divided by pi, in the order (B,D,E,F), is (1/5,-3/5,3/5,-1/5) modulo 2 Z^4. (13) In particular partial_D Theta=-3 pi/5. More strongly, throughout (7), partial_D Theta=-pi(1+E-B) lies strictly between -pi and zero. This is the arbitrary-width obstruction (5) realized at a strict interior entropy maximum of the original hyperbolic-knot source. ## 4. What changes in the next proof step For alternating homogeneous braids, one cannot close noncancellation by combining real source-flow concavity with automatic phase stationarity. The original state already contains a local opposite-sign phase flux (3). A viable general proof must transport that genuinely oscillatory state to its complex geometric cycle, or perform exact source-preserving summations that change this presentation while retaining its selected period. Concavity remains useful after that transport; it does not perform the transport. The [audit](../experiments/audit_alternating_braid_real_phase_obstruction.py) checks (3) against the independently implemented original crossing and actual inverse over finite fields, verifies its complex sine phase, and checks the full symbolic phase and entropy critical point. These tests supplement the uniform proof above.

title: Actual analytic bulk propagation and the forced Euler endpoint
text: # Actual analytic bulk propagation and the forced Euler endpoint 28 October 2026. The finite-head projectors in the [literal Euler/Gaussian network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md) can be removed with an exponentially small error on a specified interior analytic packet. The assertion has quantitative hypotheses on its physical momenta; it is not an inference from an ideal triangulation. Conversely, an exact forced finite-Euler equation excludes some apparently regular single-dilogarithm charts. Both statements concern the actual finite operators and retain the original source. ## 1. An exact projector decomposition and an exponential estimate Let `Pi_N` retain Laurent exponents `0,...,N-1`. If `f` is holomorphic on an annulus containing `r exp(-s)<=|z|<=r exp(s)`, its convergent Laurent series gives exactly Pi_N f=f-f_--f_+, (1) where `f_-` has negative exponents and `f_+` has exponents at least N. Put `M(rho)=sup_(|z|=rho)|f(z)|`. Cauchy's coefficient bound, summed as a geometric series, gives ||f_-||_r <= M(r exp(-s))/(exp(s)-1), ||f_+||_r <= M(r exp(s))exp(-Ns)/(1-exp(-s)). (2) Thus suppose an actual sequence `f_N` satisfies M_N(r exp(-s)) <= C_N exp(-delta Ns) M_N(r), M_N(r exp(s)) <= C_N exp((1-delta)Ns) M_N(r), (3) with fixed `s,delta>0` and `log C_N=o(N)`. Then ||Pi_N f_N-f_N||_r <= 2 C_N exp(-delta Ns) M_N(r)/(1-exp(-s)). (4) This is a norm estimate relative to the central packet envelope. It does not assert a relative pointwise estimate at zeros of the packet. For b heads, assume (3) for each of the two singly shifted tori. Since each circle projector has sup-norm at most N, telescoping the b commuting projectors proves ||Pi_N^(tensor b) f_N-f_N||_r <= 2b N^(b-1) C_N exp(-delta Ns) ||f_N||_r/(1-exp(-s)). (5) All remainders in (1) are retained exactly before (3) is used. There is no replacement of a finite projector by an unmarked Cauchy pole. Here is a useful sufficient physical condition. Write a nonzero analytic packet as `f_N=a_N exp(NS)` on the polyannular collar, allowing logarithms in S when its exponential is single-valued. Suppose the amplitude ratios between the collar and central torus are `exp(o(N))`, and every logarithmic radial momentum satisfies delta <= partial_(log|z_j|) Re S <= 1-delta. (6) Integrating (6) along each radial segment gives (3). Thus (5) proves that a genuinely interior analytic packet is insensitive to both head walls at exponential accuracy. ## 2. Application to actual transfer Euler atoms Use `Q=exp(2pi*i/N)`, `h=2pi*i/N`, `F_a=(Q;Q)_a`, and the literal polynomials u_N(t)=sum_(a<N)t^a/F_a, v_N(t)=sum_(a<N)(-1)^a Q^(a(a-1)/2)t^a/F_a. On every fixed closed disk of radius less than 1/4, the actual canonical polynomials, not just their nilpotent logarithms, obey u_N(t)=(1-t)^(-1/2) exp[-Li_2(t)/h](1+O(1/N)), v_N(t)=(1-t)^(1/2) exp[Li_2(t)/h](1+O(1/N)), (7) uniformly with fixed derivatives on smaller disks. The branches in (7) start at t=0. To check the actual truncation, the finite logarithm for v is `L_N=sum_(a<N)t^a/[a(Q^a-1)]`. On any fixed disk of radius less than one, L_N=Li_2(t)/h+(1/2)Log(1-t)+O(1/N). For the lower half of the coefficients expand `(exp(ha)-1)^-1=(ha)^-1-1/2+O(a/N)`; the upper half has a geometrically small tail. On `|t|=1/2`, the elementary bound `|Q^a-1|^-1<=N/4` gives `|L_N|<=N log(2)/4`. The degree-N Taylor remainder of `exp(plus or minus L_N)` on `|t|<=1/4` is therefore at most `2 exp[-3N log(2)/4]`. Its leading exponential is bounded below by `exp[-N Li_2(1/4)/(2pi)-O(1)]`, so this remainder is exponentially small relatively. This proves (7) for both actual polynomials. The same truncation argument was used for the [primitive Hilbert-90 gauge](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md); the individual half-density factors in (7) are retained here. For example the literal actual transfer operator is T_N f=Pi_N^(tensor b)[u_N(x^-1 z_2/z_1) f]. (8) Take an actual finite-head packet f and assume the entire polyannular collar of its transfer argument t lies in `|t|<=rho<1/4`. The new action is S_new=S-Li_2(t)/(2pi*i). Its two changed momenta differ from the old momenta by opposite signed real parts of `Log(1-t)/(2pi*i)`. Each change has size at most `-log(1-rho)/(2pi)`. Thus if the old momenta have twice that margin from the head walls, (5) and (7) give an actual analytic propagation formula for (8), with an exponentially small projection remainder and an `O(1/N)` analytic amplitude comparison. The same assertion, with opposite action, applies to v and to the reversed transfer argument. This is a local operator theorem, rather than formal substitution of a classical symbol into a finite matrix. For a finite ordered product, a telescoping error bound propagates these local estimates. A sufficient condition is that each intermediate packet satisfies (3) and that downstream propagation in the corresponding packet norms is `exp(o(N))`. More generally, an error with rate c remains exponentially small if the total downstream amplification rate is strictly less than c. These are explicit conditions to verify, not properties proved for the original marked knot source. ## 3. Actual factorial and Gaussian bulk diagonals The other nontrivial factors in the strict crossing are diagonal in the physical momentum index. Their bulk symbols also admit direct actual estimates. For `t=k/N` in a fixed compact subinterval of `(0,1)`, define A(t)=integral_0^t Log(1-exp(2pi*i y))dy, Log(1-exp(2pi*i y))=log(2sin(pi*y))+pi*i*y-pi*i/2. Then uniformly on that interval, F_k=sqrt(2N sin(pi*t)) exp[N A(t)+pi*i*t/2](1+O(1/N)). (9) This follows without a formal product-to-integral replacement. Exactly factor F_k=exp[pi*i*k(k+1)/(2N)-pi*i*k/2] (2pi/N)^k k! product_(r=1)^k g(r/N), g(y)=sin(pi*y)/(pi*y), g(0)=1. Euler--Maclaurin applied to the smooth zero-free function `log g` has uniform remainder `O(1/N)` here; Stirling's formula for k! has the same uniform remainder. Their endpoint terms combine into the precise square root and phase in (9). Inversion gives the reciprocal factorial symbol with the same relative error. The phase A and amplitude are analytic in a neighborhood of each such interior momentum interval. Pointwise diagonal relative error is therefore an actual weighted coefficient-norm estimate. It does not by itself estimate a cancelling summed kernel. Finally, with the original marked logarithm of x, the literal Gaussian diagonal is exactly d_k=exp{N[pi*i*t^2+pi*i*t-2t Log x]-pi*i*t}. (10) Thus no approximation or discarded scalar is needed for its quadratic Fourier phase. Equations (5), (7), (9), and (10) supply an actual interior analytic calculus for the elementary crossing factors. They neither prove that every intermediate geometric chart lies in these domains nor replace the original cap by an interior packet. ## 4. A forced endpoint that an actual analytic chart cannot ignore The literal Euler polynomials satisfy, at every nonzero t, u_N(Qt)=(1-t)u_N(t)+t^N/N, v_N(t)=(1-t)v_N(Qt)+t^N/N. (11) The first equality is coefficient subtraction and `F_(N-1)=N`. For the second, the top coefficient contributes `(-1)^(N-1)Q^(N(N-1)/2)/N=1/N`. Consequently each polynomial satisfies the actual two-point bound max(|w_N(t)|,|w_N(Qt)|) >= |t|^N/[N(1+|1-t|)], w=u or v. (12) Suppose a proposed uniform single-phase analytic chart has `w_N(t)=a_N(t)exp[N B(t)]`, with amplitude bounded above by `exp(o(N))` on a neighborhood. Since Qt tends to t, (12) forces Re B(t)>=log|t|. (13) This is a necessary condition, not a sufficient asymptotic theorem. In particular the homogeneous dilogarithm phases in (7) cannot describe the actual u polynomial on a neighborhood of a unit argument in the upper half-plane, or the actual v polynomial at its conjugate: there `Re B=-|Im Li_2(t)|/(2pi)<0`, whereas `log|t|=0`. At `t=exp(pi*i/3)`, (12) is at least `1/(2N)` for the pair of u evaluations, while that homogeneous phase is exponentially decreasing. A forced endpoint branch must be retained or cancelled by an exact larger network identity before using that single phase. The statement is about the literal atom argument; no unproved identification of that argument with a developed geometric tetrahedron shape is used. ## 5. The remaining source transition The original fixed-first-input cap and its averaged compact realization are exact boundary data. Their entry into an interior geometric analytic chart has not been proved. In particular (5) cannot be applied to a boundary packet by assuming (6), and (13) cannot be bypassed by citing algebraicity of a gluing solution. An exact source-preserving reduction can exploit (5) where its hypotheses hold, but must carry the remaining tail chains and the forced terms in (11). Establishing the geometric intersection degree of that complete marked chain remains the cycle-selection problem in the comparison proposition, not a consequence of this bulk calculus. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_analytic_bulk_projection.py) checks the finite Euler equations, the two-point bound, the original source-visible degree-zero wall, and explicit interior Laurent packets. Its numerical samples of (9) check the normalization; the proofs above give the uniform estimates.

title: Analytic two-channel conversion can exceed every marked branch action
text: # Analytic two-channel conversion can exceed every marked branch action 28 October 2026. A transverse crossing of eigenvalue MODULI, with distinct nonzero eigenvalues and uniformly conditioned analytic eigenvectors, does not justify replacing the integral of the largest root modulus by the largest continuously marked branch action. The following exact two-channel model quantifies the missing conversion cost. It is a general recurrence example, not an operator or source counterexample for a knot. ## 1. A uniformly separated analytic family Fix 0<theta<min(a,pi), b_N=N^(-p), p>=0 fixed, alpha(x)=exp(a(x-1/2)), beta(x)=exp(-a(x-1/2)+i theta), T_N(x)=[[alpha(x),b_N],[0,beta(x)]]. (1) The entries are entire functions of x. All their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on a fixed complex neighborhood of [0,1]. The eigenvalues are alpha,beta, independently of b_N, and |alpha(x)-beta(x)|^2 =exp(2a(x-1/2))+exp(-2a(x-1/2))-2cos(theta) >=4sin(theta/2)^2 (2) on the real interval. They have a transverse modulus crossing at x=1/2 but are distinct there. A diagonalizing matrix is S_N(x)=[[1,b_N/(beta(x)-alpha(x))],[0,1]]. Both S_N and its inverse have norm at most 1+1/(2sin(theta/2)) on [0,1]. They extend holomorphically with uniform bounds to a smaller fixed neighborhood: the closest eigenvalue collision is at x=1/2+i theta/(2a), off the real interval. Each continuously marked full-interval logarithmic action is zero: integral_0^1 log|alpha(x)|dx =integral_0^1 log|beta(x)|dx=0. (3) In contrast, the scalar spectral-radius envelope is integral_0^1 log rho(T_N(x))dx=a/4. (4) The following calculation treats the complete ordered product, including the actual conversion between the two channels. ## 2. Exact product and its Gaussian conversion entry Let later times act on the left: P_N=T_N((N-1)/N)...T_N(0). The diagonal entries are exactly exp(-a/2) and exp(a/2+iN theta). The single possible channel conversion gives (P_N)_12=b_N sum_(k=0)^(N-1) exp[a k(N-k)/N+i theta k]. (5) Indeed the term converting at time k contains alpha_j for j>k and beta_j for j<k. The sum of their real logarithms is a k(N-k)/N, and their phase is theta k. This is an exact finite product calculation, without an eigenvector or adiabatic approximation. Put Gamma=a/4-theta^2/(4a)>0, kappa=pi(pi-theta)/a>0. For ALL integer N tending to infinity, (P_N)_12=b_N sqrt(pi N/a) exp(N Gamma+iN theta/2) [1+O(exp(-kappa N))+O(N^(-1/2)exp(-Gamma N))]. (6) In particular there is no parity restriction or subsequence lower bound hidden in (6). Its leading phase is a single nonzero phase, not a cosine that might vanish. Here is an elementary Fourier proof with the tails retained. Extend the sum in (5) to every integer k. Periodize the integrable function g(t)=exp[-a(t-N/2)^2/N+i theta t]. Its m-th Fourier coefficient is the ordinary Gaussian integral integral_R g(t)exp(-2pi i m t)dt =sqrt(pi N/a) exp[-N(theta-2pi m)^2/(4a)] exp[i(theta-2pi m)N/2]. The Gaussian Fourier integral itself follows by differentiation in its frequency and integration by parts, with its value at frequency zero fixed by the real Gaussian integral. The periodized function and its Fourier series converge absolutely, so evaluation at zero gives sum_(k in Z) exp[a k(N-k)/N+i theta k] =sqrt(pi N/a) exp(aN/4+iN theta/2) sum_(m in Z)(-1)^(mN) exp[-N(theta-2pi m)^2/(4a)]. (7) Because 0<theta<pi, m=0 is the UNIQUE largest Fourier term. All other terms together are smaller relatively by O(exp(-kappa N)). The factor (-1)^(mN) therefore does not create leading cancellation. At theta=pi this argument would fail and parity would matter; that case is explicitly excluded. The omitted terms k<0 or k>=N have absolute sum at most 1+2sum_(r>=1)exp(-ar)=coth(a/2), (8) since their real exponents are at most -ar. Thus their contribution is bounded independently of N, BEFORE multiplication by b_N. Combining (7)--(8) proves (6) and its all-level nonvanishing assertion. It follows directly from the bounded diagonal entries that lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log||P_N||_2=Gamma>0. (9) The same limit holds for the unit boundary source e_2 and the scalar output e_1^t P_N e_2. These are fixed polynomially bounded boundary data. The alternative source e_1 remains bounded and has rate zero. Consequently source selection cannot be inferred from the eigenvalue curves alone. For example, a=2 and theta=1 give marked branch actions 0, the scalar envelope 1/2, and the exact coherent-product rate 3/8. There is genuinely exponentially small conversion compared with the envelope: its penalty is theta^2/(4a), but that penalty is insufficient to reduce the answer to the largest marked branch action. The same calculation also gives a precise sufficient condition in this model. Allow arbitrary a>0 and 0<theta<pi, without assuming theta<a. Formula (7) and the bounded tails give the exact norm rate max(0,a/4-theta^2/(4a)). At theta=a the conversion is only polynomial; at theta>a it is bounded, as are the diagonal products. Thus here the marked-branch bound is valid exactly when the conversion penalty is at least its action gain. Real-axis eigenvalue separation alone does not express that inequality. ## 3. Subprincipal coupling and reciprocal variants The case p=0 is one fixed analytic matrix family with uniformly separated eigenvalues. The case p=1 is stronger for a proposed semiclassical robustness argument: T_N differs from the exactly diagonal principal family by O(1/N), with all fixed analytic derivatives obeying the same estimate. The diagonal principal product has rate zero, whereas the true product still has rate Gamma. A polynomially small channel coupling changes the leading exponential rate. The same solution also satisfies a scalar second-order recurrence. Writing h=1/N and u_j for its first component, eliminate the second component to obtain u_(j+2)=[alpha(x+h)+beta(x)]u_(j+1) -alpha(x)beta(x)u_j, x=j/N, u_0=0, u_1=b_N. (10) Its literal companion is [[0,1],[-exp(i theta),alpha(x+h)+beta(x)]]. This analytic companion differs by O(h) from a principal companion with the uniformly distinct roots alpha,beta. Its initial source is polynomially bounded, and u_N is exactly (5). Thus the counterexample also applies to a scalar finite-order recurrence with an analytic subprincipal correction; it is not confined to a noncompanion matrix presentation. No claim that its coefficients are those of a knot quantum-A operator is being made. A determinant-one condition does not prevent this example. Multiplying every T_N by exp(-i theta/2) makes its determinant exactly one and changes no norm, eigenvalue modulus or rate in (3)--(9). One can also realize the modulus crossing between two distinct EXPANDING roots of a reciprocal-conjugate four-channel family. Let Ttilde=exp(-i theta/2)T_N, choose c>a/2, put B=exp(c)Ttilde, and on the real interval set A_N(x)=diag(B(x),(B(x)^*)^(-1)), J=[[0,I_2],[I_2,0]]. Use coefficient conjugation to extend the second block holomorphically off the real interval. Then A_N^* J A_N=J, det A_N=1, and its roots are lambda_1,lambda_2,1/conj(lambda_1),1/conj(lambda_2), with lambda_(1,2)=exp(c) times the two eigenvalues of Ttilde. All four are distinct throughout [0,1]. At x=1/2 the two expanding roots exp(c +/- i theta/2) have equal modulus and remain distinct. The largest marked branch action is c and the scalar envelope is c+a/4. Its coherent-product norm has rate c+Gamma. Indeed its two product blocks are exp(cN)Ptilde_N and exp(-cN)(Ptilde_N^*)^(-1), and a determinant-one 2 by 2 matrix has the same operator norm as its inverse. Thus even this reciprocal-conjugate structure does not imply the proposed branch-action shortcut. ## 4. What this does and does not decide Analyticity, a uniform real eigenvalue gap, analytic conditioned eigenvectors and polynomial boundary data are NOT sufficient to bound a coherent product by the maximum of complete marked branch actions. The exact Gaussian model identifies a real missing estimate: one must control the action gained by changing channels together with its exponentially small conversion cost and the actual source that can excite it. A simultaneous constant diagonalization, or a preserved boundary source channel, would prevent the conversion in this example; plain slow variation does not. This does not refute the lower classical 6_1 product rates already computed, nor a stronger theorem using the special knot operator and its original source. It rules out inferring that stronger theorem from generic analytic slow variation alone. No quantum-A operator, regulator identity or original knot source is asserted for (1). [Audit](../experiments/audit_analytic_two_channel_conversion.py) compares literal matrix products, the finite Gaussian sum and the Fourier formula at odd and even levels, including the O(1/N) coupling and the preserved-source alternative.

title: Feasible anchor phases are not globally flat, even on surviving knot states
text: # Feasible anchor phases are not globally flat, even on surviving knot states 28 October 2026. The new EXACT charged bridge-flow coefficient has a positive-magnitude expansion with a specified U(1) graph connection. Its phases cannot in general be removed by vertex gauges. This remains true on feasible charge flows in a nonzero source sector of a reduced alternating hyperbolic knot, and the holonomy persists semiclassically. The counterfamily also has an exact q-binomial fusion: its entire coefficient is polynomially sized. Thus this is a constructive example of source cancellation, not evidence that its particular sum remains unsolved. The next general step must use such phase-aware fusions, rather than assume vertex-gauge positivity of the charged source. ## 1. The exact positive-magnitude expansion and its proper flatness test The event polynomials of [the actual whole charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) are products of blocks product_(r=0)^(L-1)(alpha X_u-Q^r beta X_v), 0<=L<=d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. (1) Since all sine factors in F_j are positive in magnitude for 0<j<N, [L choose k]_Q=q^(k(L-k))*|[L choose k]_Q|. The coefficient of X_u^(L-k)X_v^k in (1) is therefore EXACTLY alpha^L *|[L choose k]_Q| *w_e^k, w_e=-(beta/alpha)q^(L-1). (2) The quadratic k phases cancel. Every magnitude in (2) is strictly positive for 0<=k<=L. The common alpha factors and the original clock/source factor W_h remain outside this expansion. Let k_e be the chosen head-charge on each oriented block u->v. The actual source requires degree d at EVERY anchor. Thus incoming(k)-outgoing(k) =d-sum_(e leaving anchor)L_e. (3) If w_e=eta_v/eta_u, the phase product is constant on this charge polytope. But a bare graph cycle need not be feasible: some edges may be forced to capacity zero or their full capacity. The exact test is the lattice of DIFFERENCES OF FEASIBLE FLOWS. For a feasible flow k, form its residual directed graph: use an edge forward if k_e<L_e and backward if k_e>0, carrying phase w_e or w_e^(-1), respectively. A residual cycle with nontrivial phase gives another feasible flow with a different phase by one unit augmentation. Conversely, every difference of feasible integer flows decomposes into such residual cycles, by following an available positive edge until a vertex repeats and then subtracting its minimum multiplicity. Therefore phases are constant on the full feasible support if and only if all these feasible cycle holonomies are one. This criterion retains the source capacities and charges, not only graph topology. Self-loop blocks may first be evaluated as their exact scalar Pochhammer; if one is zero the entire clock sector is zero. The counterexamples below have no such hidden zero factors. ## 2. A uniformly surviving BULK-curvature family Use the actual reduced alternating three-braid W=[1,-2,1,1,-2,-2]. (4) Its closure is the 13/5 two-bridge knot 6_3. The existing [6_3 certificate](six_three_and_two_bridge_audit.md) proves its hyperbolic geometry. An optional exact marked-triangulation check in the audit compares (4) with RationalTangle(13,5).numerator_closure(); both give isosig gLLPQccdefffhggaacv_aBBb. None of the coefficient or phase calculations below depends on a numerical knot recognition. Put N=2r+1, d=2r and choose the original overclocks h=(0,r,r,r,0,r), r>=1. (5) All bridges in this alternating diagram have length one, so (5) is in the exact monotone source domain. The nine anchors are numbered by the six bridge events followed by the three original closures. The nonempty grouped blocks are as follows; w_e=q^(k_e^phase). The last column is a feasible head-charge, not its phase exponent. | e | tail -> head | L | phase exponent | base charge | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | 6 -> 7 | 2r | 2r | r | | 1 | 8 -> 0 | r | -r | 0 | | 2 | 0 -> 1 | r | r | 0 | | 3 | 7 -> 1 | r | -r | 0 | | 4 | 1 -> 2 | r | -r | 0 | | 5 | 1 -> 2 | r | r | 0 | | 6 | 2 -> 3 | r | -r | 0 | | 7 | 0 -> 3 | 2r | -2r | r | | 8 | 3 -> 4 | r | r | 0 | | 9 | 4 -> 5 | r | r | 0 | | 10 | 2 -> 6 | 2r | 0 | r | | 11 | 5 -> 7 | 2r | -2 | 0 | | 12 | 4 -> 8 | 2r | -2 | r | The sum of the common alpha^L exponents is zero. The last three rows are the original source closures, including both pivots. Every row is obtained from the original signed event formulas; the table is not an auxiliary graph chosen to create a phase. The base charges satisfy (3), and so do k(t)=k(0)+t*(+e2+e4+e6-e7), 0<=t<=r. (6) This is a four-vertex BULK cycle 0->1->2->3->0. It uses no closure edge. All bounds are satisfied for every integer in (6); all its flow weights are nonzero. Its exact phase per augmentation is w2 w4 w6/w7=q^r -> exp(pi*i/2). (7) This is a genuine order-N exponent, not Q raised to a fixed integer. One may take t near r/2 to obtain an interior cycle margin of order N. Vertex gauges preserve relative phases of equal-charge flows, so cannot turn (6) into positive weights. The WHOLE clock-sector coefficient nevertheless survives, at every odd level: [X_0^d ... X_8^d]P_h=N q^(2-r^2) !=0. (8) Thus the example is not a nonflat graph supported only in a sector which the charged source kills. We now prove (8) by exact fusion. ## 3. Exact fusion of the surviving curved sector First the two parallel r-blocks e4,e5 concatenate their root intervals and become product_(j=1)^d(X1-Q^j X2) =sum_(j=0)^d X1^(d-j)X2^j. (9) This already performs their internal phase cancellation. Even on the resulting coarser graph, the feasible cycle through e2,(9),e6,e7 has holonomy q^(2r)=x -> -1, not one. Let C_j=|[r choose j]_Q| and B(t)=sum_(j=0)^r C_j t^j =(-q^(1-r)t;Q)_r. (10) All six remaining r-blocks supply positive C_j magnitudes. Solving the source charges after (9) gives free b in [0,r] and nonnegative a,c,f with a+f<=r,c+f<=r. The r-block head-charges, in edge order e1,e2,e3,e6,e8,e9, are a,c,b,f+c,f+a,f. The other head-charges are e0=e10=r+b-f, e45=b+c, e7=r+a-c, e11=f, e12=r+a. These are all the feasible flows, not a restricted subfamily. Using the phase table, their total exponent is -2r+r b-(2r+2)a+2r c-(r+2)f. (11) There are no further alpha^L factors. Since q^(4r+2)=1, the two correlation sums in a,c use the SAME weight q^(2r). The exact finite identity B(t)B(q^(2r)t)=sum_(j=0)^d q^(rj)t^j (12) follows directly by concatenating the two root progressions in (10) and using [d choose j]_Q=(-1)^j Q^(-j(j+1)/2). Taking the coefficient of t^(r-f) yields sum_a C_a C_(a+f)q^(2r a)=q^(r(r-f)). (13) Apply (13) twice in (11). The remaining b and f sums both equal B(q^r)=(Q^(r+1);Q)_r=N/F_r. (14) The result is q^(-2r+2r^2)(N/F_r)^2. Root reflection gives F_r^2=N(-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2); reducing the exponent modulo 2N proves (8). This supplies the actual nonzero surviving source coefficient and explains its polynomial size by explicit q-binomial cancellations. It is not an assumed asymptotic lower bound. ## 4. A second, simpler full-source cycle For the original figure-eight word [1,-2,1,-2], at ANY N choose h=(0,0,H,d),1<=H<d. The grouped feasible flows reduce to a rectangle 0<=k<=d-H,0<=v<=H. In the eight nonempty-edge ordering of the audit, k0=k5=H-v+k, k1=k7=d, k2=k, k3=k4=k6=v. There is a feasible five-edge cycle changing v down by one at fixed k, with holonomy q^(N+H+1). It includes closure edges and can have order-N residual capacity. Exact q-binomial summation gives coefficient=N q^(4+H-H^2-NH) !=0. (15) For example its two separated sums are (Q^(H+1);Q)_(d-H) and (Q^(-H);Q)_H. Their product is N times a unit phase. This demonstrates why retaining the actual closure is essential even when the bulk support happens to be phase-flat in a small example. ## 5. What the graph criterion does and does not settle The positive-sine grouping is exact and useful. It converts unknown flow-dependent phases into a finite graph character. But neither the global nor the bulk character is automatically a vertex coboundary on nonzero source support. Equations (5)--(8) prove this uniformly for an actual reduced alternating hyperbolic-knot state. The same example exhibits the constructive alternative: fuse the root progressions and their charge correlations BEFORE taking absolute values. Here that gives (8) exactly, hence only polynomial size. The example does not obstruct a further phase-aware normal form or a geometric asymptotic theorem for the full remaining clock sum. It rules out erasing anchor cancellation by a blanket flatness/positivity assertion, and provides an explicit q-cycle fusion for testing a more general rule. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_anchor_phase_cycles_and_fusion.py) and its saved certificate verify original block metadata, all source charges/capacities, the nonflat bulk cycle, exact cyclotomic coefficients, and the two finite product fusion identities. Optional --topology compares the explicit braid with the 13/5 rational tangle.

title: Eliminating every bridge: an arbitrary plat and its retained source
text: # Eliminating every bridge: an arbitrary plat and its retained source Research note, 27 October 2026. The general target is every hyperbolic knot, with no bound on its bridge number. The twist-family calculation is a diagnostic example. This note replaces its one-variable relator by a construction for an arbitrary 2k-plat and arbitrary crossing word. All elimination arguments below are proved for arbitrary k and word length; the audit is a check of the formulas, not their proof. The result is a scheme-level reduction, an explicit sourced deformation complex, and its determinant and dual transport. It does not yet prove the selected Kashaev period's regulator norm. In particular, a contraction of the classical deformation complex is not asserted to be a contraction of the full finite quantum period. ## 1. A general bridge presentation, without a twist-family hypothesis Fix a 2k-strand plat of a knot K. The upper and lower trivial tangles each have k bridges. Choose oriented puncture meridians so an adjacent cap identifies its two meridians as inverses. Work first with the noncentral trace-tau SL_2 class O_tau. Inversion preserves this class. Put X=O_tau^(2k), P(H)=H_(2k)...H_1, j(B_1,...,B_k)=(B_1,B_1^(-1),...,B_k,B_k^(-1)). (1.1) Thus P j=I. At the complete point use tau=2 (or the consistently marked negative lift). The inverse puncture meridian is an orientation convention, not a change of the knot's peripheral marking. For a positive crossing use the already derived actual holonomy map h_i(...,A,B,...)=(...,A^(-1) B A,A,...), h_i^(-1)(...,A,B,...)=(...,B,B A B^(-1),...). (1.2) Both preserve P and commute with simultaneous conjugation. They are regular mutually inverse maps on the matrix scheme: SL_2 inversion is the adjugate, so (1.2) introduces no rational denominator. Let F_beta=h_L ... h_1 be the arbitrary braid word, in actual action order. Its cap equations are (F_beta j(B))_(2i) (F_beta j(B))_(2i-1)=I, 1<=i<=k. (1.3) At a solution set A_i=(F_beta j(B))_(2i-1). Then F_beta j(B)=j(A). This eliminates every upper bridge variable A_i by just reading an odd endpoint. Van Kampen gives the knot-group presentation: each trivial-tangle complement is free on its bridge meridians, the punctured-sphere meridians restrict as (1.1), and their other restrictions are transported by (1.2). Consequently (1.3), modulo simultaneous conjugation, is the fixed-trace representation scheme of that marked knot presentation on the stated open locus. There is also an elementary scheme-theoretic elimination proof. If H_0=j(B), H_s=h_s(H_(s-1)) are retained as independent stage variables, substitution removes H_1,...,H_L in order. Each equation solves for its target with coefficient I. The inverse map sends each eliminated H_s to h_s...h_1 j(B). These two maps of coordinate rings are inverse. This holds over Artin rings and retains nilpotents. It is not a dimension count or an equality only of reduced solution sets. In particular, the crossing words do not disappear. They are all retained in F_beta and the k residual cap equations. Eliminating transport variables does not change K to an unknot. ## 2. The normal to a cap and the three global dependencies At a point (A,A^(-1)) write a boundary tangent as (v_o,v_e). Differentiating H_e H_o gives q_A(v_o,v_e)=v_e A+A^(-1)v_o, N_A=im(1-Ad_(A^(-1))) subset sl_2. (2.1) The range is precisely the two-dimensional plane N_A. Its kernel is the cap tangent dj_A(v)=(v,-A^(-1)v A^(-1)). (2.2) Indeed q_A dj_A=0, and the explicit splitting r_A(n)=(0,n A^(-1)) (2.3) is tangent to X and satisfies q_A r_A=I. To see the tangent claim, N_A is the trace-pairing annihilator of the one-dimensional traceless centralizer of A; equivalently it is the right-trivialized tangent space at A^(-1). No choice of a logarithm is involved. Take the direct sum q of (2.1) and N=direct_sum_i N_(A_i). Since every pair product is I at the cap point, the derivative of P is m_L=dP|_(j(A))=M q, M(n_1,...,n_k)=sum_i n_i. (2.4) Here dP already takes values in sl_2 because P=I. These three global dependencies are essential; treating all cap relations as independent scalar equations gives the wrong complex. Let V=T_B O_tau^k, set J_s=dh_s at its actual stage, and define D_beta=q J_L ... J_1 dj_B : V -> N, a_B(xi)=([xi,B_1],...,[xi,B_k]). (2.5) Equivariance and P preservation prove, for every k and beta, D_beta a_B=0, M D_beta=0. (2.6) We therefore obtain the endpoint complex 0 -> sl_2 --a_B--> V --D_beta--> N --M--> sl_2 -> 0, dimensions: 3, 2k, 2k, 3. (2.7) The quotient ker(D_beta)/im(a_B) is exactly the infinitesimal fixed-trace character deformation of the plat presentation. Both the upper and the lower bridge tuples generate the represented knot group. At an irreducible representation a_B is injective. Also M is surjective: an element trace-orthogonal to every N_(A_i) commutes with every A_i, so is zero in sl_2. Thus (2.7) is acyclic precisely when the fixed-trace character is infinitesimally rigid. This is a 2k by 2k map for arbitrary bridge number, independent of the number of crossings. No two-bridge reduction is assumed. ## 3. An explicit contraction, including inhomogeneous transport This step is pure linear algebra over any coefficient ring where the displayed tangent bundles have been trivialized. It does not require acyclicity of (2.7). Retain v in V and all intermediate u_s in T_(H_s) X. The full middle differential has rows e_s=u_s-J_s u_(s-1), u_0=dj_B v, n=q u_L. (3.1) Write T_(s:r)=J_s...J_r and set T_(s:s+1)=I. The triangular change of domain coordinates from (v,u_1,...,u_L) to (v,e_1,...,e_L) has diagonal I and determinant one. Its inverse is u_s=T_(s:1) dj_B v +sum_(r=1)^s T_(s:r+1) e_r. (3.2) In the target replace the last row by n'=n-sum_(r=1)^L q T_(L:r+1) e_r. (3.3) This is another determinant-one triangular change. The middle map now consists of D_beta and L identity pairs of rank 4k. Since 4k is even, grouping these blocks introduces no permutation sign. The two end maps are transported as well. Put m_s=dP|_(H_s). Product preservation gives m_s J_s=m_(s-1). The last map before elimination is (e_1,...,e_L,n) |-> M n-sum_s m_s e_s. (3.4) It kills (3.1), because m_0 dj_B=0. After (3.3) it is just M n', since M q T_(L:s+1)=m_s. Conjugation maps to (a_B,0,...,0) in the new domain. This is an explicit chain equivalence of the entire four-term complexes, not only equality of determinants. For actual inhomogeneous linear transport e_s=b_s, n=c, the retained endpoint source is therefore exactly c_eff=c-sum_(s=1)^L q T_(L:s+1) b_s, D_beta v=c_eff. (3.5) Its compatibility is M c=sum_s m_s b_s, equivalently M c_eff=0. No source term has been replaced by zero. If (2.7) is acyclic, a compatible source has a solution unique modulo conjugation. The dual source is equally explicit. If a linear functional is ell_0(v)+sum_s ell_s(u_s), its value on a solution becomes [ell_0+sum_s ell_s T_(s:1) dj_B](v) +sum_(1<=r<=s<=L) ell_s T_(s:r+1) b_r. (3.6) The second line is a prescribed affine constant. Omitting it changes the pointed pairing even when the homogeneous complex is unchanged. Equivalently, all covectors transform by the inverse transpose of the displayed changes. This is the source/co-source transport needed when eliminating every bridge's intermediate strands. ## 4. The normal determinant has a specified volume, not an arbitrary unit Use the conjugation-invariant residue two-form nu=dH_11 wedge dH_12/H_12 =-dH_11 wedge dH_21/H_21 (4.1) on the respective regular charts of O_tau. Inversion pulls nu back to -nu; that cap sign is retained. Define the volume on N_A by nu_N(n_1,n_2)=nu_(A^(-1))(n_1 A^(-1),n_2 A^(-1)). (4.2) With this definition (dj_A,r_A) identifies the product cap/normal volume with nu_A wedge nu_(A^(-1)). A different splitting changes only an off-diagonal block and has determinant one. Take product volumes on V and N and the same ordered basis (diag(1,-1),E_12,E_21) on the two copies of sl_2. At a regular irreducible representation choose columns V_c completing a_B to a basis and a right inverse W of M. The sourced endpoint torsion is T_plat=vol_V[a_B,V_c]/vol_N[D_beta V_c,W]. (4.3) It is nonzero, independent of both splittings and invariant under simultaneous conjugation. Splitting changes add image columns or multiply numerator and denominator by the same determinant. Conjugation preserves nu and has determinant one on sl_2. Equations (3.2)--(3.4) preserve this entire determinant line: each removed identity pair has torsion one in its identical stage bases. Thus no factor depending on a meridian, a crossing count or a root level is silently discarded. This statement is for the explicitly defined linear complex. It does not identify (4.3) with the original quantum Gaussian density merely because both are invariant objects. ## 5. Regularity at the complete hyperbolic representation The geometric input already audited in this repo supplies a positive complete ideal triangulation (under its recorded Epstein--Penner input). The polarized gluing argument in [the rigidity note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md#1-positive-shapes-make-marked-gluing-unramified) proves that the edge equations together with fixed meridian have invertible shape Jacobian. Here is the missing direct passage to the bridge representation tangent; no published character-rigidity proof is required. Consider a dual-number deformation of the complete representation whose noncentral meridian has constant trace 2. Its meridian has a unique free eigenline reducing to the complete cusp line. This can be checked in a chart with a unit off-diagonal entry: Cayley--Hamilton gives (mu-I)^2=0, and its rank-one kernel solves for that line. Every peripheral element commutes with mu and hence preserves it. Develop the ideal vertices using the deformed cusp line. The nondegenerate complete tetrahedra remain nondegenerate over the dual numbers, so their cross-ratios are defined and satisfy the same gluing equations. The meridian eigenvalue is still 1. The invertible marked gluing Jacobian makes every infinitesimal shape change zero. Conjugate so three vertices of one lifted tetrahedron agree with the undeformed vertices. Its fourth vertex agrees because its cross-ratio does. Propagate across adjacent faces; the connected lifted dual graph then makes every developed vertex agree. For each group element, the two representations act identically on three distinct developed points, so they agree in PGL_2 over the dual numbers. The SL_2 infinitesimal discrepancy is also zero, since the central lift is discrete in characteristic zero. Thus the original deformation is simultaneous infinitesimal conjugation. The negative trace lift gives the same argument with mu+I and eigenvalue -1. Consequently (2.7) is acyclic at the complete representation of every hyperbolic knot for which the recorded positive geometric triangulation input applies. This has no bridge-number restriction. It is not an assertion that every other parabolic character is regular, reduced or isolated. ## 6. The original finite quantum source can be bent into a plat The actual finite quantum network can be put in this presentation without defining a new invariant. Use its original crossings, unrolled weights, zero-framing correction and pivot, and the explicit turns in [the duality note](relative_pivotal_duality.md#2-double-duality-fixes-the-actual-pivot-exactly): x_dual=x^(-1)Q^(-1), J_x v_a=(-x)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2) v_(N-1-a)^*, J_x^(-t) J_(x_dual)=g=K^(1-N). (6.1) The already proved matrix snake identities permit an identity strand to be replaced by a cup followed by its paired cap. Moving a linear map through a bend uses its literal turned matrix J_V^(-1) A^t J_W. Repeating these finite matrix substitutions puts the cut tangle in plat form and preserves its entire contraction. It retains dual colors, weight lifts and all turn scalars. A same- color crossing must not be substituted for the turned crossing. Keep exactly one marked cut. If C_N=F_N(M) I is the original zero-framed reduced cut, its balanced source is still psi=1 and phi=(1/N)sum_a, or e=psi phi with Tr(e)=1. Carry this source through the same bends, rather than close the last cut by an ordinary pivotal cap. The latter has Tr(g)=0 and loses the invariant. The resulting pointed plat contraction is exactly F_N(M), hence F_N(1)=<K>_N. If using the unreduced ADO state, multiply by its same whole d_N(M); nothing in the re-expression cancels or evaluates that peripheral germ separately. This is a finite tensor re-expression of an existing pointed state. The inhomogeneous b_s in Section 3 are general tangent source data, not an assertion that the full quantum affine extension has already been expressed by those classical columns. Deriving that complete quantum-to-normal source map is still required. The subsequent [quantum boundary theorem](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) now supplies the explicit finite turns, cyclic source corners and their full meridian half-step transport. A marked defect g^(-1)e also gives a fully closed pointed plat with the exact reduced normalization 1/N for every k. Its principal cap equations give the inverse-meridian relations and original selected flag directly. This specifies the boundary input to the missing map; it does not yet construct the full quantum-to-normal period comparison. ## 7. What replaces the one-variable twist residue Equations (1.3), (2.7), and (3.5) are the replacement for a Riley polynomial and its 1/(S f') residue. They retain all k bridge meridians and the three global dependencies. The marked peripheral words can be carried along the exact representation-scheme isomorphism in Section 1; eliminating them to the eigenvalue image produces the corresponding classical A-support, with lift and saturation conventions still specified. It does not prove a minimal summed quantum operator has no lost geometric component. This directly advances the previous repo work: the old [Markov theorem](pointed_markov_reduction.md) controlled one added strand of a closed braid; the present contraction removes every intermediate stage of an arbitrary bridge presentation and gives the transported source, dual affine constant, and cap-normal determinant. Unlike the twist calculation, it has no single trace coordinate, Chebyshev recurrence, or family restriction. The unresolved theorem remains at the quantum period level: send the actual pointed affine extension and its selected evaluation to this regular geometric normal complex and marked regulator action, with a comparison whose nonzero norm is subexponential across N. Classical acyclicity solves compatible infinitesimal transport; it does not by itself prove this comparison or control cancellation in the selected finite scalar. The volume conjecture is not proved by the present elimination theorem. ## 8. Existing coverage and independent verification Plat representation intersections and their volume/torsion forms already have coverage, for example Dubois's [2005 paper](https://www.numdam.org/articles/10.5802/aif.2136/) and [2006 plat-volume paper](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-1/agt-v6-n1-p13-p.pdf). Their stated scope is SU(2) regular representation spaces. This coverage check is not a borrowed proof of our parabolic SL_2 complex, its normalization, or any quantum-period comparison. The direct proofs used here are (2.1)--(3.6) and the geometric argument above. No novelty is claimed for the underlying plat decomposition or triangular elimination. [Audit](../experiments/audit_arbitrary_bridge_source.py). [Results](../experiments/arbitrary_bridge_source_results.json).

title: Exact total-source resolution of every compact atomic Cauchy-pole cluster
text: # Exact total-source resolution of every compact atomic Cauchy-pole cluster 28 October 2026. All artificial atomic Cauchy poles in the full-Psi scalar period can be removed simultaneously by an exact WHOLE-SOURCE identity. This includes compact clusters with dependent atomic characters; no independence or transversality is needed. The resulting source uses the same full literature Psi functions and Gaussian, with one fixed interval variable per atom. Its normal critical scheme is the actual nine-atom scheme, with independent nondegenerate normal blocks. Atomic interval endpoints have no finite regular stationary points. This is a source identity, not a declaration that separately localized bare/cut terms vanish. All original cups, ordinary caps, full marked cap and external scalar lines remain unchanged. It removes the meromorphic-intersection mechanism before asymptotics. It does not prove a global geometric coefficient or control zero ends and dilogarithmic degenerations by itself. The [audit](../experiments/audit_atomic_window_total_source_resolution.py) and [results](../experiments/atomic_window_total_source_resolution_results.json) check nine original whole-word source identities at independent moment parameters, with genuinely present high tails and no intermediate head projection. They also check the normal determinant, finite endpoint exclusion, and exact interval kernels. ## 1. The source annihilates every nonempty atomic high-tail product Start with the original convergent full-Psi flow chamber, after or before its valid head-Hardy forest contraction. Write s_j=A_j/t_j for its atomic Cauchy ratios. The continuous coefficient-independent support theorem in [the flow-cycle proof](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md) states that EVERY feasible whole-source atomic order satisfies 0<=h_j<=d=N-1. (1) Let L_N denote the COMPLETE original head/source pairing, at fixed moment variables t and Gaussian tuple xi. Evaluate the exact finite cup/cap polynomials first; the full marked row is restricted by total degree as previously proved. No Ward identity is reapplied per sector. For any subset S of atoms, K(s)=1/(1-s)=K_N(s)+s^N K(s), K_N(s)=sum_(h=0)^(N-1)s^h. (2) Expand (2) in the original common chamber |s_j|<1. Every term with a nonempty tail subset has at least one order h_j>=N and therefore NO feasible whole-source route by (1). Its L_N pairing is zero, pointwise in all t and xi and independently of the coefficients at the other atoms. Consequently L_N[ product_j K(s_j) ] =L_N[ product_j K_N(s_j) ]. (3) One may replace any selected subset instead of all atoms. In the common chamber the right side is a finite Laurent polynomial in the moment variables. Equation (3) identifies the complete head pushforward with that polynomial; it is stronger than equality after a special full-Psi or Gaussian integration. The statement does NOT remove arbitrary head-reset tails or Laurent coupons. A microfactor that heals an out-of-range index can invalidate (1). No such new operator or arbitrary head-angle cutoff is inserted here. The proof applies to the original strict whole word and its authorized original source. ## 2. Pole clusters disappear in a genuine holomorphic representative Each K_N is a polynomial. At s=1, K_N(1)=N, so the numerator 1-s^N cancels the Cauchy denominator exactly. Replacing the participating atoms of ANY compact cluster by (3) makes the entire source holomorphic across that cluster. Multiplying these polynomials does not require independent characters: coincident poles, undirected circuits and all higher intersections are covered at once. Other true singularities of the full functions or coordinate boundary are a separate issue. This gives a precise regrouping of the TOTAL source represented by P_bare+W_cut in [the exact pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md). The regrouping is performed by the algebraic tail annihilator (1), not by defining W_cut to be a difference. Separate cluster cutoffs can destroy the Fourier support argument and create side prisms; their individual period values are not asserted to cancel. The whole current has the explicit pole-free representative (3). After the valid head-Hardy forest contraction, the head kernel is a finite Laurent polynomial. Its complete head Cauchy integral is independent of ALL finite nonzero head radii. The head radii can be chosen fixed, independently of t, and there are no atomic-pole residues when changing them. Positive factorial monomials, Gaussian coefficients and all original cap factors remain explicit. ## 3. Keep full Psi and resolve the window by one interval On the principal logarithmic chart put B(s)=Log s/(s-1), B(1)=1, K_N(s)=N B(s) integral_0^1 exp(Nu Log s)du. (4) The right side is exactly (s^N-1)/(s-1). Near ANY compact cluster s_j=1, choose Log_j 1=0 for each atom. Then every B(s_j) is holomorphic and nonzero. All dependent-cluster source densities are regular. The interval endpoints, original factors N and every logarithmic mark are retained. At other logarithmic sheets of s=1, do not separate a compensating pole and zero; use the polynomial or its selected local chart instead. Thus (3)--(4) give a full-Psi/continuous-Gaussian period with a fixed interval per atom and the original fixed cap intervals if desired. It has no atomic Cauchy poles and no finite matrix source. Its number of integration variables depends on the word, not on N. For absolute convergence use the principal-log estimate already proved for cap intervals: |B(s)|<=C(1+|log|s||)exp(-max(0,log|s|)). On any fixed compact u-path in 0<=Re u<=1, this bounds the interval density in (4) by C N(1+|log|s||)exp(d max(0,log|s|)+C_path N). (5) Choose arbitrary fixed head radii. The explicit Gaussian coefficients of A_j have logarithmic moduli at most C(1+sum|xi|). On a radial moment piece t_j=-r_j, (5) is therefore bounded by a polynomial in 1+sum|xi|+sum|log r_j| times N^B exp(CN(1+sum|xi|)) product_radial r_j^(-d). The exact full-Psi ray measure has modulus sqrt(1+r_j)r_j^(N-1)dr_j/(2*pi). Its power cancels r_j^(-d) because d=N-1. The remaining logarithms are integrable at zero; the continuous Gaussian dominates exp(CN sum|xi|). Fixed outer circles are compact. This proves joint absolute convergence of the new interval source directly, with fixed head radii. No divergent high-tail integral is evaluated in this new chamber: tail cancellation was proved first in the original common chamber. The source logarithm seams are explicit relative interval derivatives. For L->L+2*pi*i the difference of the two densities N L e^(NuL)/(e^L-1) is d_u{[e^(Nu(L+2*pi*i))-e^(NuL)]/(e^L-1)}. Its primitive vanishes at u=0 and u=1. Thus angular seams do not create an omitted source period. Full-Psi moment-circle endpoints and their paired radial ends still match by the original full-function monodromy. All these matches can also be checked by integrating the interval first, which recovers the single-valued polynomial K_N. ## 4. The joint interior critical scheme is the actual geometric scheme Write T_j=Log t_j and U_j=2*pi*i*u_j. On a chosen local sheet the window logarithm is L_j=Log A_j-T_j-2*pi*i*n_j, n_j in Z. On a recorded full-Psi leading-phase cell, including its exact integer monodromy expansion, the extended phase contains W_ext=sum_j [epsilon_j Li_2(e^T_j)+U_j L_j +2*pi*i*m_j T_j] +original Gaussian, reflected and cap phase. (6) Each m_j is its retained integer ray/monodromy mark. The full-function symbol is applied only where its stated uniform phase is valid; dilogarithmic divisors such as t=1 require separate treatment. At an interior joint critical point, T_j=Log A_j-2*pi*i*n_j, U_j=2*pi*i*m_j-epsilon_j Log(1-A_j). (7) The normal Hessian in (T_j,U_j) is [ epsilon_j A_j/(1-A_j) -1 ] [ -1 0 ], with determinant -1. It is independent of ALL incidence ranks and circuits. The normal blocks are independent over the external head, Gaussian and cap variables. Thus every regular compact Cauchy cluster is resolved by nondegenerate normal pairs, not an unresolved meromorphic intersection. Eliminating (T,U) in (6) yields exactly the actual nine-atom action with its original integer logarithmic marks. The extra constants from n_j are real phase constants. Its full critical equations are the original Hurwitz/cap representation equations, and its critical regulator satisfies [the proved sharp representation-volume bound](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md). The factor B(1)=1 and determinant -1 give a nonzero LOCAL normal density. They do not determine the original global normal/thimble cycle coefficient. For a positive oriented shape epsilon_j Im A_j>0 on its ordinary half-plane branch, with m_j=0, (7) gives 0<Re u_j<1/2. Thus its normal interval point lies strictly inside the actual allowed vertical strip; an endpoint-fixed compact complex interval path can pass through it while preserving (5). This is an allowed source-path statement, not a noncancellation proof. The product source cycle is maximal totally real on a regular phase chart: order its coordinates (T,Gaussian,U,cap,head Z), and the real parameters by their moment/Gaussian/interval paths and head angles. The complex Jacobian is block triangular with nonzero path derivatives and iI on the head angles. Thus interior stationarity of the complex phase is full holomorphic stationarity here. This is not merely a stationary real-part envelope. ## 5. Atomic interval endpoints cannot be finite regular stationary points At u_j=e in {0,1}, the derivative in U_j is omitted, but T_j is still a free regular moment coordinate. Stationarity in all the remaining complex directions forces -epsilon_j Log(1-e^T_j)-2*pi*i*e+2*pi*i*m_j=0. Exponentiating gives 1-e^T_j=1, so t_j=0. There is NO finite nonzero regular endpoint stationary point. The same applies to simultaneous atomic endpoints. A constrained boundary maximum without the other stationarity equations is not covered. The original CAP interval endpoints are different: they give central physical meridians and value zero under the separately proved regular endpoint theorem. Moment outer endpoints are matched parts of one full-Psi relative cycle, not independent new boundaries. Log seams are matched by the relative derivative above. True zero ends, phase singularities and escape in later contour deformations still need their recorded estimates or further source analysis. ## 6. The actual interval variables have a radial Legendre/flow interpretation The new variables also make the proposed flow/Rivin structure explicit on a stated positive chamber. Use the unshifted marks m_j=0 and set T_j=sigma_j+i*vartheta_j, U_j=2*pi*i*u_j, V=rho+i*theta, Log A_j=a_j.V+i*pi*nu_j. V contains the head and the transformed Gaussian logarithms. The original cap variables are likewise purely imaginary multiples of their real interval parameters in this calculation. All remaining quadratic coefficients are real. Consequently the WHOLE imaginary action has the form Im W_ext=sum_j [epsilon_j Im Li_2(exp T_j) -2*pi*u_j*sigma_j] +rho dot F(theta,u,cap), (8) where F is the original affine head/Gaussian flow expression. More explicitly its atomic part is 2*pi*sum_j a_j u_j; the original real quadratic, reflected, sign and cap terms supply the remaining affine terms. Thus minimizing over the unrestricted rho gives a finite value exactly when F=0. These are linear equations, not additional guessed geometric constraints. Equivalently they follow by differentiating the imaginary action in the head/Gaussian radial variables. This is an identity for the LEADING phase W_ext. Exact q half-steps and d=N-1 rather than N remain in the recorded finite-N amplitude; it is not an equality for the full finite-N logarithm of the density. The unrestricted radial minimization is in the complexified coordinate space. The original real Gaussian path has eta_s=sqrt(pi)(1+i*s)xi_s, so its real and imaginary parts are linked; it does not already supply that independent radial polarization. For one atom assume epsilon*vartheta in (0,pi). Put alpha=epsilon*vartheta, beta=2*pi*u, gamma=pi-alpha-beta. If alpha,beta,gamma are all positive, the radial expression f(sigma)=epsilon Im Li_2(exp(sigma+i*vartheta))-beta*sigma has derivative -epsilon Arg(1-t)-beta and strictly positive second derivative epsilon Im(t)/|1-t|^2. Its derivative tends to -beta at minus infinity and gamma at plus infinity. There is a unique global minimum, at exp(sigma)=sin(beta)/sin(gamma). At this minimum -epsilon Arg(1-t)=beta, so EXACTLY min_sigma f=epsilon D(t) =Lambda(alpha)+Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma). (9) Combining (8)--(9) on F=0 gives the sum of the positive tetrahedral volumes, OFF criticality in the remaining angular variables. The actual interval coordinate u is therefore beta/(2*pi). The imaginary parts of the other normal equations impose the affine angle matching vartheta_j=a_j.theta+pi*nu_j-2*pi*n_j. On any fixed marked chamber, these and F=0 are the actual linear angle/flow constraints; positivity cuts out a convex domain. The usual strict tetrahedral concavity holds on the quotient by directions leaving every angle unchanged. This is an identity for the newly constructed original source, not a newly defined positive model. Its scope is essential: the original signed nine-atom atlas is not known to place its geometric point in one simultaneous positive chamber, and such a choice cannot be assumed from geometricity alone. The previously found indefinite actual-phase Hessian precludes repairing that issue by arbitrary real Gaussian changes. Transport to a positive chart and control of the original interval cycle still require proof. Equations (8)--(9) explain which flow and volume optimization that transport must carry; they do not supply its missing geometric coefficient. ## 7. What has and has not been canceled The compact artificial Cauchy-pole clusters of the total source are removable, including arbitrary dependent circuits. The local L1-pole growth countermodel cannot be applied to the regrouped holomorphic kernel as though its uncanceled denominator were still present. This does not prove that every localized compact nonstationary piece has a sharp exponential bound: artificial cutoffs have side currents, and the new fixed-interval phase has its genuine critical/endpoint geometry. It supplies that geometry explicitly. In particular the normal interval period at fixed A is EXACTLY the original finite v_(epsilon,N)(A); its global normal-cycle coefficient cannot be read off from the local Hessian. The known coefficient-one atom region in [the full Euler-region theorem](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) is an anchor, not an assertion about every positive shape. What remains includes source-compatible analysis of the zero ends and dilogarithmic degenerations, and a nonzero selected geometric lower bound. The exact pole-free representative and normal resolution remove a specific obstruction to those steps; they do not constitute the broad volume conjecture by themselves.

title: The Fourier rank conditions follow from knot-exterior homology
text: # The Fourier rank conditions follow from knot-exterior homology Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplies a uniform independent proof of the two rank conditions in `singular_faces_and_six_two.md`. It applies to every globally branched oriented ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3. No geometricity, quantum-invariant existence theorem, or finite census assertion is used. ## 1. Statement Let X be the ideal compactification of an oriented one-cusped manifold M, with its single ideal vertex. Assume H^1(X;R)=0. For ordered face pairings put D=X_0-X_1+X_2, R=X_2-X_3, E=diag(epsilon). **Theorem.** Rank D=N. For any basis F of ker D, set T=E R F, U=X_0 F, K=basis of ker T, P=basis of im T, C=K^T U^T P. Then rank C=dim ker T. Thus the Fourier reduction of the existing charged tensor always has a well-defined convergent residual integral. The full stacked face matrix [D;R] can still be singular. For knot exteriors in S^3 the cohomology assumption is automatic, as proved in Section 4. The theorem is also valid whenever the stated ideal-compactification cohomology vanishes. ## 2. A local relation is exactly an ideal edge cocycle Introduce three numbers (a,b,c) in an ordered tetrahedron of sign epsilon. Define four local momentum coefficients and four position coefficients p=(b,b+c,c,c), q=(a,-a,a+epsilon*b,-epsilon*b). (2.1) Suppose across every glued face pair i,j they satisfy p_(t,i)=p_(u,j), q_(t,i)+q_(u,j)=0. (2.2) The vector space of such relations is naturally isomorphic to the space of cellular real 1-cocycles on the ideal triangulation X. **Proof.** In one tetrahedron give its vertices potentials n_0=0, n_1=c, n_2=b+c, n_3=b+c+epsilon*a. For the face opposite i, list its three vertices as u<v<w and let omega_i=epsilon*(-1)^i. Direct substitution gives p_i=n_v-n_u, q_i=omega_i*(n_w-n_v). (2.3) The same face has opposite omega on its two occurrences. Because face gluings preserve the three-vertex order, (2.2) is exactly equality of the two independent vertex differences on that face. Consequently all local differences lambda_ij=n_j-n_i descend to a single number on each global oriented edge. They sum to zero around every triangular face, so define a cellular edge cocycle. Conversely, a global edge cocycle is locally a gradient on each tetrahedron: set n_0=0 and n_i=lambda_0i. The triangular cocycle relations give every other edge difference. Then recover c=n_1-n_0, b=n_2-n_1, a=epsilon*(n_3-n_2). Equations (2.3) prove the face matching conditions. The constructions are inverse. This proves the claimed isomorphism, including injectivity. There is only one ideal vertex, so the cellular coboundary map from 0-cochains to 1-cochains is zero. Hence H^1(X;R)=0 says that the cocycle space itself is zero. All relations (2.1)--(2.2) must therefore vanish. ## 3. Applying the local lemma to the matrices First, if D^T a=0, use (2.1) with b=c=0 in every tetrahedron. Its position coefficients match because their paired sums are exactly D^T a; the momentum coefficients are zero. The lemma forces a=0. Thus D has full row rank N. Next suppose C has a nonzero left-null vector z. The corresponding global face assignment k=F K z obeys Dk=0, Rk=0. Let b=X_0 k. Since P spans E R(ker D), the condition z^T C=0 is b^T E R F=0. Therefore R^T E b annihilates ker D and is in im D^T. Choose a with D^T a+R^T E b=0. (3.1) Set c=X_2 k. The equations Dk=Rk=0 say that the four occurrences of k in a tetrahedron are (b,b+c,c,c), exactly the momentum coefficients in (2.1). They match on paired faces since k is a global face assignment. The local position coefficients in (2.1) sum over faces to the left side of (3.1). Thus they match as well. The lemma forces a=b=c=0, hence k=0. Since F K has independent columns, z=0, a contradiction. C has full row rank as asserted. This argument uses only real finite-dimensional linear algebra and the explicit cocycle lemma. In particular it does not infer convergence from a general TQFT theorem with an unaudited analytic proof. ## 4. Why the cohomology vanishes for knot exteriors Let M be the compact exterior of a knot in S^3. Its ideal compactification is M with its connected boundary torus collapsed to one point. Thus H^1(X;R)=H^1(M,boundary M;R). In the cohomology exact sequence of this pair, H^0(M)->H^0(boundary M) is an isomorphism. Hence H^1(M,boundary M) injects into H^1(M), with image the kernel of restriction to H^1(boundary M). Mayer--Vietoris for S^3=M union a solid torus gives H_1(M;Z)=Z and shows that the boundary meridian maps to its generator. For example H_1(boundary M)->H_1(M) direct-sum H_1(solid torus) is an isomorphism; the meridian is zero in the solid torus, and the other boundary generator generates its H_1. The meridian therefore generates H_1(M). Restriction H^1(M)->H^1(boundary M) is injective, so its kernel and H^1(M,boundary M) vanish. This proves the required hypothesis. ## 5. Consequence and the remaining distinction The full-tensor volume theorem in `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` now applies to **every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3**. Its Fourier rank assumptions have a uniform topological proof, rather than being additional census conditions. The independent geometry-to-saddle and analytic proofs remain necessary and are supplied in that note. This is still a statement about the full charged tensor at complete angles. A knot quantum A-state additionally needs its specified boundary fiber, phase, normalization, and peripheral identification. The general preferred-longitude/fiber construction and equivalence of arbitrary realizations are not consequences of the rank theorem alone. For 6_2 these are supplied by the separate finite certificates. The subsequent `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` supplies the uniform preferred-longitude relation. The ordinary-fiber construction and then `fourier_boundary_state.md` supply the normalized meridian state for both possible boundary ranks, preserving the complete geometric volume limit. Geometric realization and global triangulation identification are still separate obligations. The subsequent `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` now gives the uniform preferred-longitude relation. `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` constructs the meridian state whenever the longitude increases the B rank, with an exact correction for any rational longitude shear. The other boundary-rank case remains separate. There is also no assertion here that every ideal triangulation admits a global branching or that every hyperbolic alternating knot has the required positive geometric realization of the chosen combinatorics. Those are separate uniform construction questions. The script `reduce_singular_faces.py` checks (2.3) symbolically and recomputes the ideal edge-cocycle matrix in each finite example. As a useful boundary check, the two-component word RLRLRL has a nonzero cocycle and local-relation space; the one-vertex hypothesis should not be dropped without a replacement argument.

title: Exact deck characters of the original four-function crossing
text: # Exact deck characters of the original four-function crossing 28 October 2026. The exact balanced Fourier crossing has a specified continuation away from its sampling grids. Its four full-turn characters are explicit rational functions of the central coordinates. They compute the logarithmic seams in a contour deformation of the original period. A function that is periodic at the original grid need not remain periodic between the grid points. This calculation uses the full function, its Gaussian and every affine logarithmic mark. It does not infer a geometric cycle from a rational character or identify the central variety below with the knot A-curve. ## 1. The fixed continuation and its four characters Use the EXACT kernel (14) of [the balanced crossing theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md). Put h=2*pi*i/N, t=2*pi*i, X=pi*i-h/2, x=exp(X), s=x^N, and retain the port logarithms a,b,c,d. In particular s=(-1)^(N+1). Let A=exp(Na), B=exp(Nb), C=exp(Nc), D=exp(Nd), beta=b-a-X, f=d-c-X, rho=c-a, lambda=d-b+t, G=d-a-X, H=b-c+X, E=N f+(N+1)lambda/2+(G H+lambda^2/2)/h. The full continuation is M=constant * (C/A)(1-C/A)^2 exp(E) *Psi(beta)Psi(h-f)Psi(lambda+t+h)/Psi(rho). (1) The constant includes the original kappa*zeta_0^2/N. The old central parameters are used as the values of these exponentials, rather than replacing exp(Nrho) by a new independent constant off the grid. For a full positive turn of the indicated port, the exact ratios are M(a+t,b,c,d)/M = mu_a = s C(A-sB)/[B(A-C)], M(a,b+t,c,d)/M = mu_b = s(D-B)/(A-sB), M(a,b,c+t,d)/M = mu_c = s(A-C)/(D-sC), M(a,b,c,d+t)/M = mu_d = s B(D-sC)/[C(D-B)].
