For one exact three-head reassociation, the retained matrix entry is `|[u choose a]_Q|=N w_N(a,u-a,N-1-u)`. Its three nonnegative angle indices sum to N-1 exactly. Thus an exponential interface cost already has a concrete geometric weight; its squared norm contains the square of that weight. The global metric must account for the required power and the actual edge incidence, as well as the source compensation. The remaining upper-bound problem is now concrete: compose the explicit packet alphabet and its dual sources into a positive Gram whose coherent energy satisfies (2), including the true geometric edge constraints and retained current channels. There is no proof of that statement for a broad knot class yet. The [raw positive path model](actual_closed_pascal_route_energy.md) obtained by dephasing the shear factors has a uniform excessive closed route even with the original trace constraints. It is not the target geometric partition. Complete source and interior packets must be contracted coherently before a sharp positive comparison is made. The metric must preserve cancellations across suitable packets. [Every diagonal metric on the complete figure-eight clock sectors](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md) has an excessive Cauchy budget. Even [arbitrary individual-wire matrix gauges](actual_full_matrix_wire_gauge_optimizer.md) cannot improve the finest crossing-by-crossing norm bound for the specified alternating-sign words. These statements leave coupled packet metrics such as (3) available; they specify why choosing an inner product separately on each wire is insufficient. The critical path is therefore the geometric bound on the composed coherent norm, followed by a lower/survival argument. Cauchy itself is the final elementary step, not another unproved analytic principle.

title: A polynomial normal-jet envelope for the central Racah sum
text: # A polynomial normal-jet envelope for the central Racah sum 29 October 2026. This proves a quantitative bound for an EXPLICIT seven-factorial finite sum, including both low and high folded partners. The main terms have a common root phase; the terms activated by a second root zero have a uniform strict gap. Consequently four fixed normal jets cost only a polynomial relative to the known positive central marked partition. This is a new analytic estimate, not a numerical inference. The finite algebraic bridge to the ACTUAL boundary Gram is now proved in [the generic source identity](actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md): the original double sum equals this normalized Racah sum before root specialization, with all high partners and normal tails. Consequently the estimates here prove polynomial conditioning of the actual correlated boundary Gram on a fixed central corridor. The original mark and all-partner moment formula are those of [the generic source theorem](actual_generic_six_head_tetrahedral_source.md). No arbitrary six-port recoupling operator norm or whole-support bound is inferred. ## 1. Explicit object and the theorem Write d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), zeta=q(1-Z)^(1/(2N)), with its analytic branch through q. Use symmetric quantum integers and factorials [n]=(zeta^n-zeta^(-n))/(zeta-zeta^(-1)), [n]!=product_(k=1)^n[k]. For an ordinary integer triangle a,b,c in 0,...,d put J=a+b+c and r_i=J-2j_i. Define the finite sum S_abc(zeta)=sum_t (-1)^(d+t) [N+t]! /{[d+t-J]! product_i[t-j_i]! product_i[J-j_i-t]!}, (1) where max(a,b,c,J-d)<=t<=min(a+b,a+c,b+c). Every factorial index is nonnegative. Put D_abc^2=[r_1]![r_2]![r_3]!/[J+1]!, D_j^2=[j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!, Tcal_abc=(-1)^d product_i[2j_i+1] *D_abc^2 product_i D_(j_i)^2 *S_abc^2. (2) These are rational functions before removable zeros are peeled; no square-root normalization is part of (2). Take folded labels l_i<=floor(d/2), with sigma_i=(d/2-l_i)/N>=0. Let r be their number of paired axes. An unfolded branch j_i is l_i or d-l_i on a paired axis, and l_i alone on a simple odd axis. Use the actual paired-circle character unit ell_j(Z)=L_N(c_j(zeta))/Z, explicitly defined in the generic source theorem. For I a subset of paired axes put Hcal_I(Z)=sum_branches Z^r Tcal_abc product_(i in I)ell_(j_i)(Z), mcal_I=(-1)^d(q-q^(-1))[Z^(r+1-|I|)]Hcal_I(Z). (3) There are constants delta_0>0, C,C0, independent of N and of the labels, such that whenever max sigma_i<=delta_0, |mcal_I|<=C0 N^C tau_N(l), (4) where tau_N(l)=Z_N(l)/N^(3-r)>0 is the PROVED positive marked top moment, with Z_N given by the [all-channel marked formula](actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md). The estimate includes both parities and arbitrarily close paired neighbors of the odd simple axis. It is asserted for sufficiently large N; finitely many remaining supported labels can be absorbed in C0. ## 2. One common root phase in the main sum Choose initially delta<1/20. Every branch has j_i/N in (1/2-delta-O(1/N),1/2+delta). For every term in (1), all SEVEN denominator factorial indices are <N. For instance t-j_i<=N/2+3delta N+O(1), and d+t-J<=N/2+5delta N+O(1); the other differences have the same strict margin. Also J+1<2N. Separate (1) into t<N and t>=N. In the main part, ([N+t]!/[N])|_(zeta=q)=(-1)^t[N-1]! [t]!. All denominator quantum factorials are positive at this root. Thus EVERY term of S_main/[N] has the SAME phase (-1)^d. Its absolute sum is exactly Rcore_N(j)=N sum_(max j_i,J-d<=t<=min pair,d) s_t/{s_(d+t-J) product_i s_(t-j_i)s_(J-j_i-t)}, (5) where s_u=product_(k=1)^u 2sin(pi k/N). This is a genuine positive finite sum for the unfolded as well as folded labels. Its support is invariant under t->J-t. Sine-factorial reflection also gives Rcore_N=sum_t s_t s_(J-t) /product_i s_(t-j_i)s_(J-j_i-t). (6) The restriction t,J-t<=d is retained in (5),(6); no alias endpoint has been silently removed. On the common disk |Z|<=c/N^2, fixed-factorial zero removal and the [bounded normal factorial estimate](bounded_normal_quantum_factorial_envelope.md) give a uniform constant envelope for each nonzero root product. Here the same fact follows directly: a nonzero factor has size at least a constant/N, while its change is O(|Z|); there are O(N) factors in each fixed factorial ratio. Their accumulated relative cost is bounded on this disk. The normalization zeta-zeta^(-1) and the removed root zeros cost only fixed powers of N. Because the main root terms have a common phase, summing those envelopes costs at most a polynomial times the POSITIVE value (5). Cauchy's estimate for any fixed order k<=4 adds at most C_k N^(2k). This step uses no cancellation estimate on the original B double sum. ## 3. The second-zero tail has a strict central gap For t>=N, the numerator in (1) contains BOTH [N] and [2N]. After the first is removed, the term still vanishes at Z=0. After both are peeled, its root magnitude has, up to polynomial factors, numerator s_(t-N) instead of s_t. All denominator arguments stay physical by section2. Its continuous summand rate is therefore Htail(s,a)=L(s-1)-L(1+s-S) -sum_i[L(s-a_i)+L(S-a_i-s)], (7) where s=t/N, a_i=j_i/N, S=sum a_i and L(u)=integral_0^u log(2sin pi v)dv. The tail has at most N terms. At a_1=a_2=a_3=1/2 the tail collapses to s=1 and (7)=0. All arguments in (7) stay in [0,1] for its actual nearby support. Since L is continuous there, the supremum of the tail rate tends to zero uniformly as delta->0. This remains true at zero factorial indices; no derivative of L at an endpoint is being bounded. The main profile from (6) is H(s,a)=L(s)+L(S-s) -sum_i[L(s-a_i)+L(S-a_i-s)]. (8) At the center it is 4[L(s)-L(s-1/2)], has unique maximum j0=v8/pi at s=3/4, and has strictly negative second derivative throughout its interior. A fixed compact neighborhood of 3/4 has a strict gap from its complement. Uniform continuity first localizes every nearby maximizer to that neighborhood; there every child argument is <1/2 and both parent arguments >1/2, so the cotangent second derivative is strictly negative. Symmetry then fixes the maximum at s=S/2. Its value is Phi(a)=2[L(S/2)-sum_i L(S/2-a_i)]. (9) It tends to j0 as delta->0. Choose delta_0 small enough that the tail supremum is <j0/4 and the main maximum >3j0/4. The difference is a UNIFORM positive gap. This argument is effective using the explicit continuous functions, but no numerical choice of delta_0 is needed for the existence theorem. Fixed normal derivatives of the peeled tail cost only polynomial factors on the same disk. Even after the second zero is activated, the tail is exponentially below the main sum. Squaring S in (2) does not change that conclusion: mixed main/tail terms retain a strict gap from the main square. ## 4. All eight branch actions equal the folded marked action Let x_i=S/2-a_i, i=1,2,3, and x_4=1-S/2. These remain in a compact positive half-angle strip in the central corridor. The normalized per-edge factor has the particularly simple root value ([N] D_j^2)|_q=(-1)^j, (10) because [j]![d-j]!=[d]! and ([N+j]!/[N])|_q=(-1)^j[d]![j]!. It has no factorial exponential. An odd simple dimension [2j+1]=[N] supplies its own root zero. The remaining triple factor, after its one zero is removed, has rate sum_i L(2x_i)-L(S-1). Together with the main square (9), the FULL rate of (2) is E=sum_(i=1)^4 [L(2x_i)-4L(x_i)] =-2sum_(i=1)^4[L(x_i)+L(1/2-x_i)]. (11) Thus none of the dimension/triangle factors may be omitted from this comparison. At finite N set j_i=d/2-N sigma_i; replacing a_i by 1/2-sigma_i only changes the factorial asymptotics by polynomial prefactors, uniformly on this corridor. The four x_i are then the tetrahedral sign rows in the whole-label marked theorem. Its proof shows that (11) is SEPARATELY EVEN in every sigma_i. An actual high-partner change j_i->d-j_i is EXACTLY sigma_i->-sigma_i. Therefore every unfolded main branch has the SAME exponential rate as the folded positive marked weight. The sine-factorial envelope, the positive interior saddle and at most N summands give |[Z^k]{Z^r Tcal_abc product ell}|<=poly(N)e^(N E_fold), k<=4. (12) All apparent poles in (2) are removed by Z^r; in fact its main part starts at least at order Z because S has its first zero on every branch. Paired ell units have polynomial jets even at the nearest paired neighbor, since their nonzero root denominator is at least 2sin(pi/N). The second-zero tail is controlled by section3. These observations justify applying the common-disk Cauchy bound to the ENTIRE expressions in (12), not to a bare singular factor. The proved positive marked partition has uniformly tau_N(l)>=c N^(-3)e^(N E_fold) (13) on a smaller central corridor. This follows directly from its positive local Laplace prefactor, with the actual odd/even half-step and the paired multiplicities; alternatively an interior nearest saddle term gives a sufficient polynomial lower bound. Combine (12),(13), sum the at most eight branches, and use the coefficient order in (3). This proves (4). ## 5. The proved finite source bridge and actual conditioning The proved generic source identity for the B of the original nested cups and ordered duals is B_abc=(-1)^J zeta^[a^2-b^2+c^2-ab-ac+bc-cd] *[a]![b]![c]!/[J+1]! *S_abc. (14) It is established by the actual mixed-highest Casimir recurrence, the literal source coefficient COLUMN, the uniquely normalized finite polynomial eigenproblem and an own finite Sears conversion. The exceptional c=0 Jacobi diagonal is computed by the ACTUAL cup/cap projection; it is not obtained by canceling its identically zero Fricke factor. Polynomial continuation in X=Q^N includes the high partners. No published quantum-6j formula is a premise. Here is explicit normalization bookkeeping when substituting (14) into the proved physical trace. Its F-factor prefactor is (-1)^d zeta^E/(1-Q) F_r1 F_r2 F_r3 F_(J+1) product_j [F_(d-j)(1-Q^(2j+1))/F_(N+j)], E=d(3a+2b+3c+3)-4a^2-4c^2+2ac-2J. Write D(a,b,c)=a^2-b^2+c^2-ab-ac+bc-cd and T_n=n(n-1)/2. The two B prefactors, for (a,b,c) and (c,b,a), have total sign (-1)^(2J)=1. All (1-Q) factors cancel, and the remaining zeta exponent is IDENTICALLY zero: E+D(a,b,c)+D(c,b,a)+sum_i T_(r_i)+T_(J+1) +sum_j[T_(d-j)-T_(N+j)+2j]=0. The factorials left over are precisely Tcal in (2). This is an identity before specialization, not an equality modulo a root character. Hence the actual marked moments equal (3), including all lower moments and normal tails. Equation (4) proves max_I |m_I/tau_N|<=poly(N), K_j=sum_I |coeff_I q_j^(1/2)|^2<=poly(N) (15) uniformly throughout a fixed central corridor, at both parities, with simple axes handled by the same formula with their absent paired variables. In particular log K_j=O(log N)=o(N) there. The second implication is immediate from the finite binomial polynomial of degree <=3 in the [actual marked boundary frame](actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). Source and co-source costs remain the exact K_j and tau_j^2 K_j from that theorem. No recoupling operator norm or whole-support conditioning follows from this central result. The diagnostic [original moment implementation](../experiments/diagnose_actual_marked_boundary_conditioning.py) uses the already proved generic source/cut formula, not (14), to measure the actual moments. For nearest paired central labels K is 1.000043544... at N=128 and 1.000011164... at N=256. Macroscopic central tests remain bounded, while some saturation-boundary tests grow slowly. Those finite measurements guided the proof but are not substituted for the proved finite bridge or a whole-support estimate. The data include polynomially small normal steps and precision growing with N; further paired-precision validation is kept separate from a theorem claim. ## 6. Actual-source diagnostic and paired precision The [diagnostic audit](../experiments/audit_actual_marked_boundary_conditioning.py) evaluates the PROVED generic physical double-sum trace, groups every low/high partner before extracting the physical marked normal, and uses no instance of (14) in its measurements. It compares normal steps N^-8 and N^-8/2 while increasing precision by seventy digits. Its saved results are labeled PASS_DIAGNOSTIC, not a proof of (15). The refined values include: | N | folded triple | precisions | K_j | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 16 | (7,7,7) | 150 / 220 digits | 1.00184624542464 | | 64 | (31,31,31) | 180 / 250 digits | 1.00016536760140 | | 128 | (51,51,51) | 240 / 310 digits | 1.01103593283933 | | 129 | (32,32,64) | 260 / 330 digits | 2.59529339844986 | | 256 | (127,127,127) | 360 / 430 digits | 1.00001116412322 | The maximum difference of normalized moments is below 1.3e-16 in the smallest case and below 3e-23 in every other listed case. The independent positive tau formula checks the top moment at the same normal-step accuracy. The boundary example at N=129 has delta=0; it is outside the central theorem and illustrates why a uniform constant bound is not inferred from nearest-center samples. These tests establish numerical consistency of the original moment implementation at the stated parameters. The finite transformation (14) is proved separately; the sampling itself does not control all q-jets or establish any whole-support conditioning exponent.

title: A same-operator central freedom in the whole regular profile
text: # A same-operator central freedom in the whole regular profile Independent algebraic audit, 27 October 2026. The actual root operator, its bounded affine source, all integer-color values, reciprocity, and qualitative finite exponential type do not by themselves force a constant centered regular profile. They leave a central source freedom. This is not a modification of the literature-defined invariant: it identifies precisely which proposed uniqueness premises omit its full marked source. The starting objects are the actual [regularized period](regularized_kashaev_period.md) and [scaled meridian profile](scaled_meridian_regular_profile.md). Fix \(Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(U=Y^N\), and write \[ F_N=S_NR_N+P_N,\qquad S_N=(U-1)/(Y-1),\qquad K_N=F_N(1). \tag{1} \] The specified root operator \(P\) annihilates \(F_N\). After the fixed actual gauge, its affine operator \(A\) satisfies \[ A R_N=b_N,\qquad A p_N=-b_N,\qquad p_N=P_N/S_N. \tag{2} \] All coefficients and clearing factors of these actual operators are retained. ## 1. An exact transformation preserving the operator and source Let \(h(U)\) be any Laurent polynomial satisfying \[ h(1)=1,\qquad h(U^{-1})=h(U), \] and define an auxiliary comparison family \[ \widetilde F_N(Y)=h(Y^N)F_N(Y). \tag{3} \] The same \(h\) is used at every level. The following statements are exact: * Every specified root annihilator of \(F_N\) annihilates \(\widetilde F_N\), because \(T(U)=U\) for \(T(Y)=Q_NY\). * Every ordinary and complete orbit value is unchanged, since \(U=1\) at \(Y=Q_N^j\). Thus \(P_N\), \(K_N\), and the given ordinary-color polynomial family are unchanged. * Laurent polynomiality and actual Weyl reciprocity are preserved. * The canonical regular quotient remains Laurent polynomial and satisfies the same affine equation with the same \(b_N\). To prove the last assertion set \[ L_h(U)=\frac{h(U)-1}{U-1}\in\mathbb C[U,U^{-1}]. \] Division is in the Laurent polynomial ring and is regular at \(U=1\). The exact quotient is \[ \widetilde R_N =h(U)R_N+(Y-1)L_h(U)P_N =h(U)R_N+(h(U)-1)p_N. \tag{4} \] Since \(A\) commutes with every central \(h(U)\), (2) gives \[ A\widetilde R_N=h b_N-(h-1)b_N=b_N. \tag{5} \] In particular both regular meridian lattices used to fix the complete value are preserved, and \(\widetilde R_N(1)=R_N(1)\). This agrees with the pointed complete-value uniqueness statement: it does not imply uniqueness of the whole meridian function. This construction is rootwise and all-level. It does not supply an off-root quantum-normal lift with the same q-jets, nor a second actual knot invariant. ## 2. The freedom survives regularization and finite type Assume the precise tail domination used in the scaled-profile theorem: \[ \varepsilon_N=\frac{ND_N}{|K_N|}\longrightarrow0. \] Put \(Y=e^{z/N}\) and use the original centered full-state monomial: \[ g_N(z)=F_N(e^{z/N})/K_N,\qquad \rho_N(z)=e^{(N-1)z/(2N)}\,NR_N(e^{z/N})/K_N . \] Equation (3) gives exactly \[ \widetilde g_N(z)=h(e^z)g_N(z). \tag{6} \] By (4) the difference between \(\widetilde\rho_N\) and \(h(e^z)\rho_N\) is \[ e^{(N-1)z/(2N)}N(e^{z/N}-1) L_h(e^z)P_N(e^{z/N})/K_N. \tag{7} \] On every fixed compact z-set, \(N(e^{z/N}-1)\) is bounded uniformly and \(P_N/K_N=O(\varepsilon_N)\). Hence (7) tends uniformly to zero. Whenever the original whole regular profile exists, \[ \rho_N\longrightarrow\rho \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \widetilde\rho_N\longrightarrow h(e^z)\rho . \tag{8} \] Convergence is locally uniform, including the exact resonance centers, by (7) or by the proved uniform removable division. For the concrete choice \[ h_m(U)=\tfrac12(U^m+U^{-m}),\qquad m\in\mathbb Z_{>0}, \] the multiplier is \(\cosh(mz)\): an even entire function, normalized to one at zero, of finite exponential type. If \(\rho\) has finite exponential type, so does \(\cosh(mz)\rho\). Since \(\rho(0)=1\), the latter cannot coincide identically with \(\rho\). If a nonconstant \(\rho\) already exists the proposed constancy inference has failed; if \(\rho=1\), this same-operator construction gives the explicit nonconstant comparison profile \(\cosh(mz)\). Thus even the actual root operator and its actual bounded affine source do not make qualitative finite exponential type a constancy criterion. A sharp numerical type or Laurent-degree window can impose additional constraints; none is being discarded by this argument. ## 3. What the marked source still contributes The comparison changes the full source and its normal jets. For example \(h_m(U)-1\) has a second-order zero at \(U=1\); the first meridian jet is preserved, but the second generally is not. More generally \[ h(U)=1+\lambda(U+U^{-1}-2)^r \] preserves all orbit meridian jets of order below \(2r\), while changing the whole profile by a finite-type multiplier. Every prescribed finite jet budget can therefore be preserved by choosing a larger fixed \(r\). This does not preserve all analytic jets: the identity theorem would force an analytic multiplier with every jet equal to one to be identically one. The Laurent degree window also grows by \(O(N)\), and an exact source lattice may prohibit that change. The result therefore isolates a genuine missing premise rather than refuting uniqueness for the fully pointed actual state. The next comparison must retain its source lattice or its whole normal connection; operator support, ordinary-color values and an unspecified finite growth type do not replace it. There is a constructive first-normal remedy. The [source-corrected normal connection](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md) uses the same whole preoperator to turn its normal source into a linear rule \(R_N(v)\). If the actual root section has \(\iota(v)\ne0\), simultaneous lifting of \(v\) and \(h(U)v\) forces \(Uh'(U)\iota(v)=0\), hence \(h\) is constant and the anchor fixes it to one. That nonzero-symbol condition is not automatic; the linked note gives an exact Jordan counterexample and the actual factorial atom with its corrected connection.

title: The actual cut moments are centralizer normal-residue co-sources
text: # The actual cut moments are centralizer normal-residue co-sources Research proof, 27 October 2026. Polynomial centralizer currents have an explicit finite-pole realization on the resolved actual framing torsor. Their normal residues pair with every actual cut matrix by a specified Toeplitz row. The two Weyl charts glue by an explicit rational homotopy, while their current primitives retain exactly the two endpoint values. A whole cut-clock co-source then extends the construction beyond individual Taylor jets. This constructs a framing moment/current map. The centralizer b is a framing variable, not an unframed critical-field generator. No descent of the actual state to its geometric critical summand is inferred from this map. ## 1. Actual framing coordinates and the normal form Use the source/framing threefold and the original marked density of [the compact framing bridge](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md). On the north chart write Omega=dv wedge da, T=va, X=eta v, F=1-X, b_N=-a/eta=-T/X, nu_cut=-(d eta/eta) wedge Omega/F. (1) Here b_N is the right regular-unipotent centralizer coordinate. The south chart is V=1/v, a'=v-v^2a, eta'=-v^2eta, T'=Va'=1-T, b_S=-a'/eta', b_S=b_N+1/X, F=1+eta'V. (2) The form nu_cut is global; its factor 1/F is the actual cut/Haar adapter and is not set to its boundary value before taking moments. The original principal Gaussian multiplies (1) by its marked nonzero algebraic density c_beta and original base line. These factors tensor through the calculations below. Work over any characteristic-zero coefficient field of the marked unframed data. Polynomial coefficients below are independent of the framing coordinates. The normal residue is taken at eta=0 coefficientwise at finite pole order, with d eta/eta first. ## 2. Polynomial moments have exact normal residues For every h>=0, Res_E[b_N^h nu_cut]=-(-T)^h Omega. (3) Indeed `b_N^h=(-a)^h eta^(-h)` and `1/F=sum_(r>=0)eta^r v^r`; only r=h contributes to the normal residue. Thus for any polynomial P, Res_E[P(b_N)nu_cut]=-P(-T)Omega. (4) The adapter 1/F is decisive. Replacing nu_cut by the Haar form before multiplying by b_N^h would lose every nonconstant moment. The bounded moment h has finite normal pole order h+1. With the actual compact sphere and omega_I=-Omega/(2pi*i), the normalized identity-source period is exactly (1/(2pi*i))integral_Gamma Res_E[P(b_N)nu_cut] =integral_0^1 P(-T)dT. (5) This is not an assertion that P(b_N) is a global scalar function; the required chart gluing is provided next. ## 3. The two polynomial moment charts glue by a specified homotopy The residue-compatible south representative of the north polynomial P(b_N) is P(b_S-1). It is not P(b_S). With (2), b_S-1-b_N=F/X. (6) Direct south-chart residue gives `Res_E[P(b_S-1)nu_cut]=-P(T'-1)Omega=-P(-T)Omega`. The normal residue is therefore a global source form. There is an explicit stronger gluing identity. For P=b^h, [P(b_S-1)-P(b_N)]nu_cut=d Xi_h, (7) where Xi_0=0 and, on the overlap v!=0, Xi_h=-sum_(r=1)^h binom(h,r)(-T)^(h-r) sum_(k=0)^(r-1)binom(r-1,k)(-1)^k X^(k-h)/(k-h) Omega. (8) The denominator k-h is never zero. To verify (7), its left side is -[(F-T)^h-(-T)^h]/[X^(h+1)F] dX wedge Omega. The numerator is divisible by F. Expanding F=1-X leaves only powers X^(-j), j>=2, whose primitive is precisely (8). There is no Gauss-wall pole left and no logarithmic E residue in the overlap difference. The same formula extends linearly to every P. This gives the actual finite-pole Cech homotopy, rather than declaring the two polynomial coordinates identical. ## 4. Vertical currents retain their exact endpoint Cech class The actual right-centralizer vector field is V_b=partial_(b_N)=partial_(b_S)=-eta partial_a. It preserves nu_cut. The vertical two-current is alpha_N(P)=iota_(V_b)[P(b_N)nu_cut] =P(b_N)d eta wedge dv/F, d alpha_N(P)=P'(b_N)nu_cut. (9) Its north normal residue is Res_E alpha_N(P)=[P(-T)-P(0)]dlog v. (10) For the south representative P(b_S-1), expressed back in the north base coordinates, it is Res_E alpha_S(P)=[P(-T)-P(-1)]dlog v. (11) Thus their exact current Cech difference is Res_E alpha_S(P)-Res_E alpha_N(P) =[P(0)-P(-1)]dlog v. (12) This is the actual relative endpoint class. It has nonzero period whenever P(0)!=P(-1). Formulas (7)--(8) also give the current-level overlap homotopy explicitly by Cartan's identity: alpha_S(P)-alpha_N(P) =L_(V_b)Xi_P-d iota_(V_b)Xi_P. In particular the degree-one example P=b has P'=1 and endpoint difference one. Its differentiated top form is the nonzero unit source class. Finite moment degree and nilpotence of a logarithmic transport group do not make this endpoint class vanish. A relative source must retain it; it cannot annihilate every such current and preserve the unit period. ## 5. The correct finite cut co-source is the dual Toeplitz row Let N>=2, n=N-1, J e_j=j e_j. For a polynomial P define the literal diagonal cut row T_N(P)_j =N binom(n,j)integral_0^1 P(-T)T^j(1-T)^(n-j)dT. (13) For each monomial it is exactly T_N(b^h)_j=(-1)^h (j+1)^(rising h)/(N+1)^(rising h), (14) for EVERY h>=0. The beta integral proves this finite rational formula. The actual all-matrix trace identity is (1/N)Tr[T_N(P)C] =integral_Gamma P(-T)sigma_C omega_I. (15) For the actual one-cut and Green matrices, which are diagonal term by term, this is the original normalized cut as well. It does not replace the original rank-one cut by a trace on arbitrary off-diagonal Ward matrices. Equations (4) and (15) therefore specify the residue co-source against every actual cut-current kernel. All source coefficient matrices remain literal; their trace is not used to define T_N. If raw Green arrays already contain 1/N, first use the explicit matrix normalization C=N I_raw, as in the cut-current theorem. Actual Weyl reflection is compatible with these rows: T_N(P)_(n-j)=T_N(P(-1-b))_j. (16) This follows by T->1-T in (13). The actual weighted anti-diagonal Weyl operator has the same effect by conjugation on a diagonal row. Its diagonal source factors and the bounded Gamma units commute with the row; their original fractional source lattices are retained rather than inverted at a zero. There is an exact derivative/current identity. For any diagonal matrix C and its literal adjacent difference `Delta C_j=C_(j+1)-C_j`, j=0,...,n-1, (1/N)Tr[T_N(P')C] =P(0)C_00-P(-1)C_nn +n*(1/n)Tr_[dimension n][T_n(P)Delta C]. (17) Integration by parts and the derivative formula for Bernstein polynomials prove (17). It retains both endpoint rows and the change of source degree. This is a finite current map, not a statement that the knot has changed its quantum color. For C=I, (17) reduces exactly to P(0)-P(-1), as in (12). The same definition (13) is used at dimension one when N=2 makes the current target n=1; it is the scalar beta integral. There is a corresponding explicit product-current correction before pairing. For a general kernel f_C(v,T), d iota_(V_b)[P(b_N)f_C nu_cut] =[P'(b_N)f_C-X P(b_N)partial_T f_C]nu_cut. (17a) Indeed V_b(T)=-X and V_b(v)=V_b(eta)=0. The north current residue is `f_C[P(-T)-P(0)]dlog v`. Its derivative verifies (17a) directly with the normal residue differential sign. The finite Bernstein derivative in (17) is exactly the kernel derivative that appears here. It must not be dropped by treating the source kernel as constant along the centralizer. ## 6. Symbol quantization is distinct from co-source quantization For degree h<=n there is also a unique diagonal matrix with coherent symbol (-T)^h: Q_N(b^h)=(-1)^h (J)_h/(n)_h, (18) where the factorials are falling. This gives the useful exact symbol derivative identity Q_(N-1)(P')=-n Delta Q_N(P). (19) The trace in the left target has dimension N-1=n. Summing it gives P(0)-P(-1), with the same endpoints. But Q_N(P) is not the co-source (13) against a general C: ordinary multiplication of coherent symbols is not the matrix or star product. The rising factorials in T_N and falling factorials in Q_N must not be interchanged. For identity C their normalized traces agree with (5); for a general Green matrix, (13)--(17) are the appropriate paired identities. ## 7. The actual whole cut clock has a compatible normal co-source lift The companion [dual whole-clock source theorem](dual_clock_normal_cut_source.md) constructs the explicit polynomial P^dual_(N,w) of degree<=n with T_N(P^dual_(N,w))_j=w^j, 0<=j<N. (20) Its formula is P^dual_(N,w)(b)=sum_(h=0)^n [(N+1)^(rising h)/h!] [sum_(r=h)^n(-1)^r binom(r,h)(w-1)^r]b^h. Thus (15) becomes an exact ACTUAL cut-clock pairing, `Tr(w^J C)/N`, for every C. The map is not guessed from its limiting symbol. It obeys the exact Weyl relation P^dual_(N,w)(-1-b)=w^n P^dual_(N,w^(-1))(b). (21) Its finite polynomial endpoints are specified as well: P^dual_(N,w)(0)=sum_(r=0)^n(1-w)^r, P^dual_(N,w)(-1)=w^N-(w-1)^N. (21a) They are not identified with the two clock eigenvalues. For w=exp(z/N), it converges locally uniformly in the whole variables z,b to exp(-zb), with every fixed holomorphic jet. The centered lift converges to exp[-z(b+1/2)] and its exact identity-source period is the already marked H_N(z). The normal pole degree of the whole polynomial can reach N; it is not discarded before the residue. Differentiating (20) gives the literal normalized cut-index moments `(J/N)^h`, including the exact finite Newton correction in their normal polynomial. The h-th z derivative at zero has degree at most min(h,n), so its normal pole order is at most h+1, independently of N. Hence bounded Green LOG moments of the actual cut clock are included. For example the actual first normalized moment has P_(N,1)(b)=-1/N-(N+1)b/N, P_(N,1)(0)-P_(N,1)(-1)=-(N+1)/N. (21b) This is a nonzero endpoint/current Cech class for an ACTUAL bounded cut-log moment. It does not prove that a particular complete Green certificate has a nonzero combined boundary; it proves that bounded degree alone cannot force vanishing. The degree bound applies to the cut-clock polynomial itself; a weighted word kernel can still have full coherent degree N-1. This does not identify an independent crossing-transfer clock with that cut clock. For the latter one needs the actual network Ward/current map, not only a common polynomial or abstract Borel representation. ## 8. Scope of the framing integration The construction supplies actual source moments, all their finite endpoint terms, the global polynomial normal gluing, and the whole cut-clock limit. It is a concrete part of the missing framing pushforward. The bounded-degree example (12) also shows why a generic bounded unipotent logarithmic complex cannot by itself make every Green boundary vanish. The normal polynomial b is a framing variable. Its normalized moments are (-1)^h/(h+1), not automatically a finite unframed critical-field trace. The intended geometric critical algebra belongs after framing integration. The present maps do not construct that transverse critical observable or identify the remaining actual transfer log with the centralizer current. They also do not prove global polar control for every internal Gaussian coefficient, selected geometric source survival or a volume limit. ## 9. Exact audit [audit_centralizer_normal_cut_moments.py](../experiments/audit_centralizer_normal_cut_moments.py) and its [results](../experiments/centralizer_normal_cut_moments_results.json) verify the finite normal residues, explicit Cech primitive, both vertical-current endpoint residues and the product-current covariance correction through degree six. They verify the dual Toeplitz moments, actual Weyl reflection and paired current identity with independent matrix entries at dimensions 2 through 9 and moment degrees through seven. The separate covariant-symbol and degree-lowering map is checked as well. All these tests are exact rational identities. The whole-clock construction and its bounded moment-degree sharpening have their own exact audit linked in the companion note. The independent [Gauss-wall/current audit](gauss_wall_current_independent_audit.md) checks the signs, global polynomial clutch, distinction between trace and the original average cut, and all endpoint dimensions. No internal Gaussian or selected critical-field descent is inferred from these checks.

title: Boundary orders of the actual charged gain arrangement
text: # Boundary orders of the actual charged gain arrangement 28 October 2026. The fixed-diagram charged polynomial has an additional restriction absent from arbitrary unit-root coefficient examples: it has a bounded number of root-INTERVAL blocks. Each block has distinct roots, even though its length grows with N. This bounds the order of every noncoordinate collision at a generic linear flat independently of N. A zero logarithmic residue at such a boundary can therefore involve only a bounded coordinate cut deficit. The following statements concern actual fixed-clock binary products, before or after unit-factor-preserving fusions. They do not identify the full coupled clock phase or establish its volume bound. ## 1. Exact classification of the linear flats Write the source, with extracted scalars retained in gamma, as P=gamma product_e product_(r=0)^(L_e-1) (X_(u_e)-a_e Q^r X_(v_e)), f=P/product_i X_i^(q_i), sum_i q_i=sum_e L_e. There are B block slots, bounded by the fixed original diagram, with L_e<=N and a_e in the actual 2Nth roots of unity. Loops are first evaluated as their exact scalar monomial and their source charge adjusted by the proved source identity. A zero scalar kills the state. Thus genuine remaining factors have two distinct endpoints. The coordinate hyperplanes X_i=0 are included in the arrangement. Every intersection flat F has the following form. Some coordinates are identically zero; call their set Z. The others are partitioned into classes, with relations X_i=zeta_i T_class and |zeta_i|=1, where the T_class are independent. Indeed follow the gain equations X_i=g X_j along a connected component. A nontrivial cycle gain or one coordinate-zero equation forces that whole component to zero; otherwise path gains give precisely these proportional coordinates. Put m_Z=number of factors with both endpoints in Z, e_Z=q(Z)-m_Z, c_F=number of OTHER factor hyperplanes containing F. Every one of these c_F factors joins a pair in the SAME nonzero class and has its particular matching gain zeta_i/zeta_j. Each root-interval block contributes AT MOST ONE such factor, since its Q-roots are distinct. Consequently 0<=c_F<=B. (1) If F has codimension c, then c=|Z|+sum_nonzero_classes (class_size-1). (2) The common origin is omitted after the usual common-scale quotient; it does not supply an additional projective boundary divisor. ## 2. Its masterfunction and source-form orders are explicit Blow up the linear flat F and take a generic point of its exceptional divisor, away from smaller intersections. Every linear factor whose hyperplane contains F has order one in the normal scale t; the other factors are units. A coordinate X_i vanishes there exactly when i is in Z. Therefore the EXACT logarithmic residue/order of f is a_F=ord_F(f)=m_Z+c_F-q(Z)=c_F-e_Z. (3) In particular a_F=0 forces e_Z<=B. A macroscopic coordinate deficit cannot be neutralized by bounded noncoordinate multiplicity. If Z is empty, a proper arrangement flat has a_F=c_F>0, and f tends to zero rather than a finite nonzero value. The actual coefficient form is Omega=P dX_1...dX_k/product_i X_i^(q_i+1). The normal blow-up Jacobian has order c-1. Its exact normal order is ord_F(Omega)=a_F+c-|Z|-1. (4) This counts the extra one in each coordinate pole; it must not be confused with only the phase order (3). At ZERO phase order, a noncoordinate flat c>|Z| produces NO pole of the original form. The only possible logarithmic source poles with zero phase order are pure coordinate flats: c=|Z|, c_F=0 and e_Z=0. These are the already proved exact tight-cut factorizations. Equation (4) does not declare stationary values of a holomorphic boundary extension irrelevant; it distinguishes those from an original residue pole. For example (4) follows in explicit local coordinates: choose a basis of F and c normal vectors, put the normal displacement equal to t times a nonzero normal direction, and use its remaining c-1 direction ratios. The wedge Jacobian contributes t^(c-1), numerator factors contribute t^(m_Z+c_F), and coordinate denominators contribute t^(q(Z)+|Z|). This proves the formula with no quantum asymptotic. ## 3. Linear chart changes have polynomial conditioning Normalize the factor and coordinate rows to e_i-g e_j, g in mu_(2N), or e_i. Every nonzero s-by-s minor A of such a matrix obeys (2/N)^s <= |det A| <=2^s. (5) Here s is bounded by the fixed number of anchors. To prove this, restrict each chosen row to the chosen columns. A two-entry row is a gain edge; a one-entry row is a unit ground row. Permuting connected components splits the minor. A nonzero square block must have equal numbers of rows and vertices. Each connected block is either a tree with one ground row, or an ungrounded unicycle. Leaf elimination gives a unit determinant in the first case and a unit times (1-holonomy) in the second. An unbalanced count or trivial cycle holonomy gives zero. All gains and holonomies are 2Nth roots of unity, whose nonzero differences from one have modulus at least 2 sin(pi/(2N))>=2/N. Multiplying component factors proves (5). Thus inverse normal-coordinate matrices obtained from independent rows have entries at most a fixed-dimensional polynomial in N by Cramer's rule. No uncontrolled exponential condition number is hidden in THIS linear arrangement-coordinate step. This is not yet a bound for a global Morse-flow Jacobian. ## 4. Mixed-sign monomial corners create no new finite critical value Blowing up all linear intersection flats in increasing dimension gives local normal-crossing charts whose boundary divisors are labelled by the original flats. One can see this directly by induction: the intersection of two incomparable flat transforms has already been blown up, so only nested flat labels can meet; a basis adapted to that flag gives the successive normal ratios. Each arrangement factor is a monomial in these normal coordinates times a unit. Accordingly a local masterfunction is f=u(t,y) product_i t_i^(a_i), (6) where u is a nonvanishing holomorphic unit and the a_i are the orders (3). If at least one VANISHING normal coordinate t_j has a_j!=0, choose a local holomorphic a_j-th root of u and change t'_j=t_j u^(1/a_j). The Jacobian at the boundary is nonzero and the coordinate divisors are preserved. This absorbs the unit EXACTLY: (6) becomes a monomial, not merely its first-order approximation. Resolve its mixed-sign indeterminacy by the toric subdivision of the normal cone along a dot w=0. On an orbit mapping to a finite nonzero value, its cone sigma lies in this kernel. The nonzero character a therefore descends to a NONCONSTANT character of that orbit's torus: it annihilates sigma but is not the zero character. Its derivative in a toric-ratio direction is nonzero. Thus a new zero-order exceptional divisor from cancellation of positive and negative weights is NOT a critical stratum over C*. No assumption that the weights have one sign is needed. Possible finite nonzero boundary critical strata must instead meet a normal-crossing stratum where EVERY vanishing original-flat order is zero. By (1)--(3), every associated nonempty coordinate cut then has bounded deficit e_Z<=B. In particular the sufficient condition e_Z>B for all nonempty proper coordinate subsets Z excludes ALL nonzero finite boundary critical values of this fixed anchor masterfunction. This is a qualitative boundary-tameness statement. It still requires a separately controlled cycle construction to give a uniform quantum upper estimate. ## 5. What is left for the FULL phase The existing cut-jet source theorem controls the normal coefficient cost of the bounded deficits isolated here. It retains the lower dimensional periods and does not bound them by a regulator. Similarly the gain-minor estimate controls linear charts, not arbitrary nonlinear transport. The [polynomial logarithmic-mass lemma](actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.md) specifies what a controlled sublevel representative would accomplish. There is also an N-dependent saturation issue: an O(1) normal order is O(1/N) in the normalized log action. Quantum critical points may approach such a divisor in a 1/N boundary layer even when the limiting interior critical equations lose a normal constraint. They cannot be declared points of the SATURATED classical critical closure without an additional actual source or connection argument. The known sharp critical-regulator bound covers that closure, not every restricted boundary stationary equation. Finally all the preceding critical statements fix the integer clocks. Complex clock deformation changes the unit-gain interpretation and must retain the exact feedback and factorial interpolants. No bound for the complete knot scalar or its nonzero geometric coefficient is claimed from these anchor results alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_charged_arrangement_boundary_orders.py): actual source flats, complete gain-class/zero-class bookkeeping, bounded noncoordinate multiplicities, exact normal orders, and root-of-unity minor/conditioning bounds.

title: Actual anchor critical points obey a graph flow and a cut maximum principle
text: # Actual anchor critical points obey a graph flow and a cut maximum principle 28 October 2026. The actual binary-factor source has a direct critical flow equation. Combined with its exact cut factorization, it confines EVERY regular anchor critical point of each residual core to polynomially bounded radii. A macroscopic interior cut margin gives a bound independent of N. Exact balance is stronger: every critical point is on the original unit torus, with one nondegenerate point in each angular chamber. These assertions concern each specified integer clock sector, with its original source. They do not assert criticality in the remaining clocks, nor extend unit-modulus hypotheses to complex clock deformations. The full invariant can still cancel between sectors or between chambers. ## 1. The actual source and its exact real critical equation Take the original graph polynomial, before or after unit-factor-preserving source fusions, P(X)=gamma product_f (alpha_f X_(i_f)-beta_f X_(j_f)), |alpha_f|=|beta_f|=1, f(X)=P(X) product_i X_i^(-q_i), sum_i q_i=number of factors=M. (1) The q_i are the nonnegative integer source charges, possibly reduced by forced endpoint monomials in the [cut/core factorization](charged_source_cut_jets.md). The extracted scalar gamma stays outside. A self-loop is evaluated as its exact scalar times X_i; an identically zero factor kills the period. Count a nonzero loop twice in the incidence S_i. Put delta_i=S_i-2q_i, sum_i delta_i=0. A REGULAR anchor critical point has all X_i!=0, no zero factor, and X_i partial_i log f=0. Set rho_i=|X_i|^2. The elementary identity Re(alpha X/(alpha X-beta Y)) =1/2+(|X|^2-|Y|^2)/(2|alpha X-beta Y|^2) proves the exact graph equation sum_(f joining i,j) (rho_i-rho_j)/|alpha_f X_i-beta_f X_j|^2 =-delta_i. (2) The equation is independent of the orientation in which an edge is written. A loop contributes one to the logarithmic derivative and two to S_i, hence no flux. This is a weighted graph Laplace equation with POSITIVE weights at every regular critical point, even though the original source coefficients are complex. It is not a positivity assertion about their sum. ## 2. Cut inequalities give radial properness for every residual core For a proper anchor subset I, let C_I be the number of crossing factors and e_I=q(I)-m_I the exact source cut deficit. Counting incidences gives delta(I)=C_I-2e_I. Summing (2) over I cancels all internal edges. Suppose every radius in I is larger than every radius outside, with separating logarithmic gap g=min_(i in I)log|X_i|-max_(j notin I)log|X_j|>0. For each crossing factor, (rho_i-rho_j)/|alpha X_i-beta X_j|^2 >=(|X_i|-|X_j|)/(|X_i|+|X_j|)>=tanh(g/2). Consequently C_I tanh(g/2)<=2e_I-C_I. (3) In particular a high-radius cut must have e_I>C_I/2. If e_I<C_I, then g<=log(e_I/(C_I-e_I)). (4) Now take any nontrivial residual strongly connected core from the EXACT source factorization. It has no proper tight cut and admits a feasible endpoint assignment. The Hall inequalities and their complements therefore give integers 1<=e_I<=C_I-1 (5) at every nonempty proper subset. Sort the k core radii and apply (4) to each positive consecutive gap. Since C_I<=M, max_i log|X_i|-min_i log|X_i| <=(k-1)log(M-1). (6) Every such core has M>=2. After fixing the common C* scale, all its regular anchor critical radii thus lie between reciprocal polynomials in M. In an original fixed knot diagram, M=O(N) and k is bounded by the diagram, so (6) is a uniform POLYNOMIAL radius bound for all actual integer-clock residual cores. This uses no assumption that their defects are small. One-anchor cores have no radial variable after removing the common scale. If the stronger margin epsilon C_I<=e_I<=(1-epsilon)C_I holds for all proper cuts, with 0<epsilon<=1/2, (4) instead gives max log|X|-min log|X| <=(k-1)log((1-epsilon)/epsilon). (7) Thus macroscopic interior cuts confine critical points uniformly even when their forcing delta is of order N. Degenerating margins are exactly the cut variables whose selected finite jets were retained in the preceding source theorem; no missing denominator or boundary source has been discarded here. ## 3. Balance and sublinear forcing For a connected graph with delta_i=0 at every anchor, choose an anchor of largest radius in (2). All its summands are nonnegative, so every adjacent radius agrees. Connectivity propagates equality. Therefore EVERY regular critical point, up to common complex scale, has |X_i|=1. This is stronger than the pairing of conjugate critical points in a self-inversive polynomial. More quantitatively let lambda be the minimum nontrivial cut size and D=(1/2)sum_i|delta_i|. If D<lambda, (3) bounds each consecutive gap by 2 artanh(D/lambda), hence oscillation(log|X|)<=2(k-1)artanh(D/lambda). (8) In particular lambda>=cN and delta_i=o(N) force all regular critical radii into a shrinking tube around the unit torus. The bound does not give a source intersection number for a perturbed complex saddle. ## 4. In the balanced case the source itself reaches every critical chamber Fix the common phase by X_k=1 and write X_i=exp(i theta_i). The exact sine factorization gives the original density on this torus as f(exp(i theta))=C product_f 2sin((theta_i-theta_j+phi_f)/2), (9) with one constant complex phase C (and the retained scalar modulus). The signs vary across factor zeros. On each lifted arrangement chamber, log|f| has Hessian H(v,v)=-(1/4)sum_f csc^2((theta_i-theta_j+phi_f)/2) (v_i-v_j)^2. (10) Connectivity makes this negative definite after removing the common phase. Each chamber is a convex bounded polytope in these lifted coordinates: every edge difference lies between two consecutive factor-zero levels, and a spanning tree bounds all differences. At every chamber boundary some factor vanishes, so log|f| tends to minus infinity. Thus each chamber has exactly one maximum, with a nondegenerate Hessian. The density has constant phase on that chamber; its angular critical point is therefore a full complex critical point. The maximum principle in Section 3 shows that there are no other regular critical points off this torus. Common-scale gauge directions are not counted as Hessian degeneracies here. This proves accessibility from the ACTUAL coefficient torus for this balanced class. It does not choose the signs of different chamber contributions or assert that the remaining clock sum preserves them. There is also a precise local source multiplicity. In logarithmic coordinates at a chamber maximum, the real tangent Hessian is negative definite, while its imaginary normal Hessian has the opposite sign. The actual torus therefore intersects the dual local Gaussian normal cycle transversely with degree +1 or -1, according to orientation. The critical point is present with local multiplicity one; its constant phase and Gaussian determinant are still retained. This local statement does not prevent cancellation between different chambers and does not compute a geometric coefficient of the full coupled clock sum. ## 5. A quantitative selected-coefficient theorem with a checkable gap There is a useful uniform consequence for a sequence of balanced graphs with a fixed number r=k-1 of independent anchors and charges q_i=O(N). Put M_N=max_(unit torus)|f_N|. Suppose one sign chamber attains M_N and every chamber of the opposite sign has maximum at most M_N exp(-eta N), for a fixed eta>0. Chambers with the same sign are allowed to share the maximum. Then for all sufficiently large N, c N^(-2r) M_N <= |[X^q]P_N| <= M_N. (11) The constant c depends on the fixed degree bounds and r. In particular the selected coefficient has exactly the exponential rate of M_N. No geometric thimble coefficient is assumed in this conclusion. Proof. After removing its constant phase, (9) is a real trigonometric polynomial. Each variable has Fourier degree at most q_i: its polynomial degree is at most S_i=2q_i, before subtracting its source charge q_i. For a one-variable restriction whose sup norm is at most M_N, each Fourier coefficient has modulus at most M_N, so |partial_(theta_i) f_N|<=q_i(q_i+1) M_N. At a point attaining M_N, a box of side c_0 N^(-2) therefore has the same sign and modulus at least M_N/2. Its positive signed mass is at least c N^(-2r)M_N in normalized torus measure. All same-sign chambers add to that mass. The ENTIRE opposite-sign part has absolute integral at most M_N exp(-eta N), since the full normalized measure is one. This proves the lower bound, after reducing c. The upper bound is the integral triangle inequality. A polynomially small opposite-sign gap can replace the exponential hypothesis if its total bound is o(N^(-2r)M_N). There is also an exact top-intersection statement in this balanced setting. Suppose the highest regular critical point is UNIQUE after the common-scale gauge and torus periods. By Sections 3--4 it lies on the original torus and is its unique global modulus maximum. An upward cycle of Re log f from that point has Re log f at least its critical height; the entire source torus has Re log f at most that height, with equality only at this point. Their only intersection is therefore this critical point. The negative-definite angular Hessian and holomorphy make the upward tangent space transverse to the angular source tangent space, giving local intersection number +1 or -1 with the specified orientations. Thus the highest relative coefficient is NONZERO here; it has not been inferred from a nonzero local density alone. This statement does not make the quantitative height-gap hypothesis in (11) automatic for an N-dependent sequence, or remove cancellation between opposite-sign chambers at tied height. The gap is an extra hypothesis, not automatic. For example (X-Y)(X+Y) with charges (1,1) is balanced, has two nondegenerate unit-torus critical chambers of equal height and opposite sign, and has selected coefficient zero. Nor is an arbitrary unit-factor UNBALANCED core covered by (11): [explicit such sources](charged_torus_critical_selection.md) can exclude their unique highest critical action entirely. ## 6. Exact scope for the original knot and its A-period Equations (2)-(8) apply to every actual fixed-clock binary-factor core, with the original source charges and normalizers. They give properness and a precise graph-theoretic condition for balanced torus accessibility. For an alternating one-component diagram in the present overbridge coordinates, exact balance forces all crossing clocks to agree; it is not an automatic consequence of alternation. The stronger [actual alternating-source theorem](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) shows that every balanced sector of the original figure-eight state is zero. Indeed every nonzero sector before further clustering has max_i|delta_i|>=(N-1)/2. Thus the pointwise balanced and sublinear defect regimes are ABSENT from this already known prototype's nonzero source support in these variables. Further exact clustering can combine opposite defects; applying it is a distinct operation, not a consequence of (11). The ALL-level [original figure-eight source theorem](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) makes this limitation sharp. Its nonzero fixed-clock sectors satisfy h_0=0 and h_1+h_3>=N-1; consequently EVERY balanced diagonal-clock sector is exactly zero, and at least one individual anchor defect has modulus >=(N-1)/2. Thus the balanced chamber theorem cannot on its own select that prototype's volume contribution in these coordinates. Further exact clustering or fusion of macroscopic defects is required; sublinear individual-star jets alone do not cover that source. The knot period still includes its W_h and the coupled h sum. Anchor criticality alone is not full gluing/holonomy criticality, so a bound on the latter's regulator cannot be assigned to every chamber maximum of a fixed h. Complex h deformations can make the factor ratios nonunit, and require a separate argument. A retained deficient-star polynomial is not generally a unit binary product; its logarithmic derivative must remain unless one applies this theorem separately to its actual monomial source channels. A norm estimate does not permit dropping that derivative or its source pairing. Thus this result proves a general critical flow and source-accessible balanced selection theorem. It does not yet prove the original geometric coefficient, the broad volume upper bound, or the volume conjecture. The exact source reductions and these bounds identify the remaining macroscopic forced flow and clock coupling as the next problem rather than an uncontrolled coordinate escape. [Audit](../experiments/audit_charged_critical_flow_and_chambers.py): exact radial identities on original graph metadata, complete univariate critical sets for balanced and unbalanced unit-factor examples, and the selected-coefficient distinction between a norm and its source.

title: Exact global cut jets of the original charged source
text: # Exact global cut jets of the original charged source 28 October 2026. Every anchor cluster has an exact finite normal-jet description in the original charged source. A negative cut deficit kills the source. A zero deficit factors it. Fixed, and even sublinear, deficits have subexponential boundary-choice cost for a fixed diagram. These assertions retain the two resulting periods; they are not scalar volume estimates or claims that a nonzero period cannot cancel. The input is the actual [charged bridge coefficient](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) and its [specified nilpotent/Fermat functional](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md): K_N=chi_N/N sum_h W_h lambda(P_h), lambda(P)=[X_1^d ... X_k^d]P, d=N-1. (1) All clocks, W_h, pivots, and chi_N remain. Each statement below is termwise in these actual clocks, so summing it gives exactly (1). The number of h states is polynomial in N for a fixed diagram; the theorems do not replace their signed sum by a positive one. ## 1. A cluster has an exact normal deficit It is useful to allow remaining charges q_v>=0, not only q_v=d. Let P be a product of M nonzero binary linear factors, with sum_v q_v=M. Multiple factors and self-loops are allowed. Evaluate a self-loop as its actual scalar times X_v; if its scalar is zero, P is zero. Such a monomial is a factor with its one endpoint counted once in the definitions below. All its scalar factors are retained. For a set I of anchors put m_I=number of factors supported entirely in I, e_I=q(I)-m_I, q(I)=sum_(v in I)q_v. (2) Let J be its complement and let C_I be the set of crossing factors. Write each crossing factor with its actual coefficients as a_f X_(o_f)+b_f X_(i_f), o_f in J, i_f in I. Write P_I,P_J for the internal products. Then EXACTLY lambda_q(P)=sum_(S subset C_I, |S|=e_I) (product_(f in S)b_f)(product_(f notin S)a_f) *[X_I^(q_I)] P_I product_(f in S)X_(i_f) *[X_J^(q_J)] P_J product_(f notin S)X_(o_f). (3) An empty or impossible subset sum is zero. In particular e_I<0, or e_I>|C_I|, kills the source. For e_I=0 this is the SINGLE product [X_I^(q_I)]P_I *[X_J^(q_J)]P_J product_(f in C_I)a_f X_(o_f). (4) Thus a tight cut really factors the actual selected coefficient. No normalized knot value is used to choose the scalar. Proof. Every internal factor contributes one unit of degree in I. Exactly e_I of the crossing factors must choose their I endpoint to supply its source charge. Expanding only those choices proves (3); all other variables remain in their specified source pairings. Equivalently rescale X_v -> t X_v for v in I. Then P(tX_I,X_J)=t^m_I P_I P_J product_(f in C_I)(a_f X_(o_f)+t b_f X_(i_f)). The original source selects total t-degree q(I), so (3) is precisely the order-e_I normal jet. This is an algebraic coefficient identity, not an assumed deformation of a full-Psi contour or its logarithmic sheets. In the usual relative radial coordinate it is the same normal coefficient selected by t^(-e_I)dt/t. ## 2. What its norm controls For the original crossing factors, |a_f|=|b_f|=1. Coefficients of the boundary-jet polynomial therefore obey ||[t^e] product_(f in C_I)(a_f X_(o_f)+t b_f X_(i_f))||_1 <=binom(|C_I|,e). (5) This follows by counting the subsets before combining equal monomials. It is a norm bound only on the boundary-choice polynomial, NOT on either remaining source value in (3). Arbitrary coefficients give the corresponding sum of products of their moduli instead. Internal self-loop scalars, W_h and all extracted fusion scalars are not included in or discarded by (5). For a fixed original diagram, |C_I|<=C_diagram N. Thus fixed e costs at most (C_diagram N)^e. More generally, if min(e_I, |C_I|-e_I)=o(N), the bound (5) is exp(o(N)), using log binom(M,e)<=u log(euler_number*M/u), u=min(e,M-e), with the zero endpoint understood by continuity. No fixed jet-order hypothesis is needed for this subexponential conclusion. A genuinely macroscopic interior deficit can have exponentially many boundary choices; (5) then supplies no tame-cost assertion. ## 3. The Hall test decides support, not the selected value There exists an assignment of each factor to one of its endpoints, with exactly q_v choices at every anchor, IF AND ONLY IF m_I<=q(I) for EVERY anchor set I. (6) Necessity is immediate: every internal factor must choose inside I. For sufficiency build a largest partial assignment respecting the charges. If an unassigned factor remains, follow its endpoints, then factors already assigned there, and their alternative endpoints. If a reached anchor has spare charge, an alternating path increases the assignment. Otherwise all reached anchors are full. All their assigned factors, and the initial unassigned factor, have both endpoints among the reached anchors: otherwise that new endpoint would also have been reached. There are more than q(I) such internal factors, contradicting (6). This argument covers multiple edges and one-endpoint factors without change. The implication is a test for FEASIBLE ENDPOINT SUPPORT. It does NOT say lambda_q(P) is nonzero. The two-factor polynomial (X-Y)(X+Y), charge (1,1), satisfies (6) and has zero selected coefficient. The actual charged source also has such phase cancellations, including complete root-orbit annihilations. Tight sets (e_I=0) are closed under union and intersection whenever (6) holds. Indeed q is modular and m is supermodular. More precisely, e_I+e_J-e_(I union J)-e_(I intersection J) =number of factors joining I\J to J\I. (7) For two tight sets every term on the right is forced to zero, and both new deficits vanish. Thus their factorizations are compatible, rather than unrelated guesses about separate source sectors. ### A canonical factorization into the residual flow cores Choose ANY feasible endpoint assignment. Direct each two-endpoint factor from its assigned anchor to its other endpoint. A one-endpoint factor is a loop. Take the strongly connected components of this residual graph. A factor joining distinct components is assigned to the SAME endpoint in every feasible assignment. To see this, the edges changed between two assignments have equal indegree and outdegree at every vertex, hence decompose into directed cycles of the first residual graph. A changed edge cannot join its distinct strong components. Consequently every cross-component factor can be replaced by its forced coefficient times its forced endpoint monomial. The source then factors EXACTLY over the remaining component polynomials, with charges reduced by those forced monomials. This is also obtained by successively applying (4) to sink components. Reversing the cycles which connect two feasible assignments preserves residual strong components, so the component partition is independent of the chosen assignment. Inside a nontrivial component no proper tight subset remains relative to its reduced charges. This isolates the genuine phase-coupled cores. Their coefficients can still vanish. It is not a quantum determinant or positivity theorem. ## 4. Nested flags control coordinate corners jointly Let I_1 subset ... subset I_r be a proper nested flag of anchor sets. Scale X_v by product_(ell:v in I_ell)t_ell. Factor out product_ell t_ell^(m_(I_ell)). Let P_cell be the products of factors whose endpoints lie in the same flag layer. The other factors form a polynomial K_flag(X,t): each endpoint term carries precisely the t_ell for cuts which separate that endpoint from the other one. There is the exact joint formula lambda_q(P)=lambda_q[ product_cells P_cell *[t_1^(e_I1)...t_r^(e_Ir)]K_flag(X,t)]. (8) In particular these are not independent normal residues with unretained corner corrections. The SAME boundary endpoint choice must satisfy every cut. Its collection of selected-inside crossing factors has cardinalities e_(I_ell), and determines that choice uniquely. Therefore, for the original unit coefficients, ||[t^e]K_flag||_1 <=product_ell binom(|C_(I_ell)|,e_(I_ell)). (9) Every coordinate radial cone, after removing the common homogeneous scale, is described by an ordered nested flag. Thus (8) covers its full finite normal jet, including corners. The flag length is bounded by the fixed number of anchors. If all its normal deficits are at sublinear distance from an endpoint, (9) costs exp(o(N)). At zero deficits it reduces to compatible successive exact factorizations. ### Integral weighted rays and their exact single normal jet For arbitrary integers w_v>=0 with min_v w_v=0, scale X_v=t^(w_v)Y_v. Put l_w=sum_f min(w_(i_f),w_(j_f)), e_w=sum_v q_v w_v-l_w. A one-endpoint factor contributes its one endpoint's weight to l_w. Normalize every factor by this minimum power of t. A factor joining different weight levels has one constant endpoint and one endpoint of degree |w_i-w_j| in t. The EXACT source is the order-e_w normal coefficient of this normalized product. The layer-cake identity is e_w=sum_(r=1)^(max w) e_(I_r), I_r={v:w_v>=r}. (10) It follows either by counting the thresholds below each endpoint or by summing the indicator functions of the I_r. The charges in (10) can be the reduced q_v left after earlier exact fusions. If the source is feasible all summands are nonnegative. At e_w=0 the factors joining distinct levels are forced to their lower-weight endpoints, and the source factors over its equal-weight layers. At e_w>=0 at most e_w unequal-level factors can choose their higher-weight endpoints. Thus their boundary-jet coefficient norm is at most sum_(j=0)^min(e_w,M_cross) binom(M_cross,j) <=(e_w+1) max(1,M_cross)^(e_w). (11) This counts only boundary choices; all equal-level products and their actual remaining source pairings are retained. For a fixed diagram the displayed polynomial bound gives subexponential cost if e_w log N=o(N). The sharper binomial-sum bound gives the same conclusion already when e_w=o(N), by the elementary entropy bound and M_cross=O(N). These statements allow weighted ray directions depending on N; they do not replace an irrational radial path by an unproved uniform analytic limit. Together (8) and (10) cover the exact source jets of coordinate flags and every integral weighted coordinate escape. This does not control noncoordinate hyperplane collisions, nor the remaining component periods at an escaping critical configuration. Even a polynomially bounded boundary jet can pair to zero or to an exponentially large exterior period. A hyperbolic-volume upper or lower bound therefore still requires a phase-aware estimate or geometric source comparison for the surviving cores. The result here is the exact global source reduction and its stated normal-jet cost. [Audit](../experiments/audit_charged_source_cut_jets.py): general charges, loops and multiple factors, Hall feasibility versus phase vanishing, actual original charged polynomials, cut factorizations, residual-core factorizations, and joint nested normal jets.

title: Exact star–triangle reduction with its retained degree defect
text: # Exact star–triangle reduction with its retained degree defect 28 October 2026. The balanced root-of-unity star–triangle identity in [the general source fusion theorem](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) has an exact extension to stars below balance. It factors off the same cyclotomic pair constraints and retains a polynomial whose degree is exactly the balance defect. Its normalized coefficient norm has the explicit bound (e+1)^5 binom(N+e,e)^6, so EVERY sublinear defect e=o(N) has only subexponential cost. No claim is made that the original knot state has defects in this range, or that contracting its remaining polynomial cannot cancel the geometric contribution. ## 1. Polynomial factorization, including an unbalanced star Fix a primitive Nth root Q, put d=N-1, and write B_L(X,Z)=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(X-Q^r Z). Let 0<=L_i<=d, S=L_1+L_2+L_3, and suppose S<=2d, L_i+L_j>=d for every i!=j. (1) Define e=2d-S, k_i=d-L_i, a_i=k_i-e. Then a_i>=0, sum k_i=d+e, sum a_i=d-2e. In particular 0<=e<=d/2. The actual charged contraction is F_L(X_1,X_2,X_3)=[Z^d] product_i B_(L_i)(X_i,Z). There is an EXACT homogeneous polynomial R_L of degree e such that F_L=Delta_L R_L, (2) Delta_L= product_(r<a_3)(X_1-Q^(k_2+1+r) X_2) *product_(r<a_1)(X_2-Q^(k_3+1+r) X_3) *product_(r<a_2)(X_3-Q^(k_1+1+r) X_1). (3) This holds in the ordinary polynomial ring, BEFORE nilpotent source reduction. Arbitrary nonzero coefficients in front of Z are allowed by substituting X_i -> X_i/b_i and multiplying by product b_i^L_i. One can subsequently identify neighbor variables as required by the actual graph. Proof. Set X_i=Q^p X_j with N-L_j <= p <= L_i. The two incident products have, as roots in Z, intervals with exponents [p-L_i+1,p] and [-L_j+1,0]. The conditions on p make these intervals overlap or touch, and their union contains at least N consecutive integers. Their product is divisible by X_j^N-Z^N, up to a nonzero scalar. The remaining product has Z-degree S-N<=d-1. Therefore its product with X_j^N-Z^N has ZERO Z^d coefficient: the constant term would need degree d in the remainder, while the Z^N term is already too large. Thus every linear factor displayed in (3) divides F_L. They are pairwise nonassociate factors in the three-variable polynomial ring. Their total degree is d-2e. Since F_L has degree S-d=d-e, the quotient has degree e. The nonzero coefficient below also proves that F_L and R_L are not identically zero. This argument uses only the full cyclotomic product and polynomial divisibility. ## 2. A nonzero marked coefficient fixes the normalization Put T(n)=n(n-1)/2 and use the Gaussian binomial with base Q. The coefficient of X_2^e in R_L is exactly c_L=(-1)^(d-a_3) Q^[T(L_1)+T(k_1)-(k_2+1)a_3-T(a_3)] {L_3 choose k_1}_Q. (4) In particular c_L!=0: L_3=k_1+a_2<=d and 0<=k_1<=L_3. To prove (4), set X_1=0. The first block contributes (-1)^L_1 Q^T(L_1) Z^L_1. To get the largest X_2 exponent in the remaining Z^k_1 coefficient, take no Z from the second block and k_1 powers from the third. The resulting coefficient is (-1)^d Q^[T(L_1)+T(k_1)] {L_3 choose k_1}_Q at X_2^(a_1+a_3+e) X_3^a_2. The corresponding leading coefficient of Delta_L is (-1)^a_3 Q^[(k_2+1)a_3+T(a_3)]. Division gives (4). At e=0 the quotient is the single scalar c_L, recovering the balanced star–triangle theorem, with all phases retained. At e>0, replacing R_L by this one coefficient is NOT an exact source identity. ## 3. Growing defect jets have an explicit uniform exponential scale For EVERY admissible e, not just a fixed degree, the coefficient norm satisfies the explicit uniform estimate |c_L| <= ||R_L||_1 <= (e+1)^5 (2N)^(4e) |c_L|. (5) The norm is the sum of the ordinary complex coefficient moduli, not the value after contraction against an exterior knot source. This already covers e_N log N=o(N). The refinement (5a) below extends the conclusion to EVERY e_N=o(N). Here is a direct proof that does not hide constants growing with e. Set a=X_1/X_3, b=X_3/X_2. If c_D is the unit-modulus leading coefficient of Delta_L, then Delta_L=c_D X_2^(a_1+a_3) X_3^a_2 D(a,b), where D is a product of a_2 factors (1-unit*a), a_1 factors (1-unit*b), and a_3 factors (1-unit*a*b). The quotient R_L/X_2^e has monomials a^u b^(u+w), u+w<=e. All needed a and b exponents therefore lie between zero and e. Also F_L/(c_D X_2^(d-e) b^a_2) is an ORDINARY polynomial in a,b: in each monomial of F_L the X_2 degree is at most L_2, and d-e-L_2=a_2. Its coefficient at a^i b^j, for i,j<=e, comes from the original three Z indices L_1-i, j, k_1-j+i. The first two binomials have moduli <=N^i and <=N^j. The third differs from {L_3 choose k_1}_Q by |i-j| adjacent-index steps. Each ratio or its reciprocal along valid indices has modulus <=N: all its nonzero factors satisfy 4/N<=|1-Q^r|<=2. Thus these coefficients of F_L, after dividing by c_D, are bounded by |c_L| N^(i+j+|i-j|) <= |c_L| N^(2e). Invalid indices give zero; no vanishing factorial is inverted. The same bound holds for any complex primitive Nth root, since its nonzero factors are a permutation of the standard ones. Expand 1/D formally at (0,0). Its coefficient of a^u b^v is a sum over at most e+1 choices t for the number of factors of type ab. Each term is bounded by a product of three complete homogeneous coefficients of lengths <=d and degrees u-t,v-t,t. Their elementary counting bounds give, for u,v<=e, |[a^u b^v](1/D)| <= (e+1)(2N)^(u+v). Convolving with the needed rectangle of F_L uses at most (e+1)^2 terms. There are at most (e+1)^2 coefficients of R_L. Combining these bounds proves the upper estimate (5); (4) gives its lower estimate. This proof permits e to grow with N throughout. The counting can be sharpened uniformly, including e=0. Put B=binom(N+e,e). Then ||R_L||_1/|c_L| <= (e+1)^5 B^6 <= (e+1)^5 (2 exp(1) N/e)^(6e), e>=1. (5a) The first bound applies also at e=0, when B=1 and R_L=c_L. Indeed the kth smallest modulus among the N-1 nonzero root factors is at least 2k/N: distance min(j,N-j) occurs at most twice and 2 sin(pi*j/N)>=4 min(j,N-j)/N. Therefore the product of ANY r distinct such factors is at least (2/N)^r r!, at every primitive root. A Gaussian-binomial index shift of r steps has numerator bounded by 2^r and r distinct denominator factors, so its ratio is at most N^r/r!, in either direction when the indices are valid. The first two binomials in the rectangle have moduli at most their ordinary binomial coefficients: their elementary-symmetric expansion is a sum of binom(L,i) unit terms. These counts are <=B for i<=e and L<=d. For the third relative ratio, r<=e gives N^r/r! <= N^e/e! <= B. Thus every rectangle coefficient is bounded by |c_L|B^3. Each complete homogeneous coefficient of degree r<=e and length <=d is a sum of at most binom(d+r-1,r)<=B unit terms. The three groups in 1/D therefore give (e+1)B^3. The convolution and quotient-support counts each contribute at most (e+1)^2, proving (5a). Finally B<= [exp(1)(N+e)/e]^e<= [2 exp(1)N/e]^e for e>=1. No constant in these bounds depends on e. Consequently log(||R_L||_1/|c_L|)=o(N) for every e=o(N), since e log(N/e)=o(N). This includes all sublinear windows, not just a fixed normal depth or an O(sqrt N) window. At e=0, R_L=c_L exactly. For the ACTUAL standard root Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), the exact modulus of (4) is N/(|F_(k_1) F_(k_2-e) F_(k_3)|). The uniform endpoint factorial estimate and (5a) consequently give, for e>=1, log ||R_L||_1 = (N/pi) sum_i Lambda(pi*k_i/N) +O(e log(N/e)+e+log N). (6) The replacement of F_(k_2-e) by F_(k_2) obeys the same error bound: the intervening e factors have product between (2/N)^e e! and 2^e. At e=0 the error in (6) is simply O(log N). Here Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log|2 sin u| du. The last formula uses the uniform endpoint-aware factorial estimate already proved for the original state, together with reflection about N. In particular if e=o(N) and k_i/N -> t_i>0, then sum t_i=1. The corresponding limiting ideal tetrahedron has angles pi*t_i, and lim (2pi/N) log ||R_L||_1 = 2 Vol(tetrahedron). (7) The factor TWO is essential. A single extracted scalar must not be counted as one tetrahedron in the volume-conjecture normalization. The entire transformed source, including its new triangle factors, is what preserves the knot period. ## 4. What this permits in the proposed leading/jet reduction Equations (2)-(5) are a precise, source-compatible local meaning of "a geometric factor with a controlled quantum correction." The correction is retained as a homogeneous polynomial; it is not erased by an unsupported assertion of nilpotence or rigidity. ### The degree defect is the exact angular source-phase frequency There is an analytic interpretation on the original unit-radius anchor torus. Let a charged product, including all its explicit constant normalizers, be P(X)=gamma product_f (alpha_f X_(i_f)-beta_f X_(j_f)), |alpha_f|=|beta_f|=1, X_a=exp(i theta_a). Let S_a count the incident linear factors at anchor a, counting a self-loop twice. The source density is P(X) product_a X_a^(-d). On fixed real argument lifts, the elementary identity exp(i A)-exp(i B)=2i exp(i(A+B)/2) sin((A-B)/2) gives EXACTLY P(exp(i theta)) product_a exp(-i*d*theta_a) =C exp[(i/2)sum_a (S_a-2d)theta_a] A(theta), (8) where C is an explicit theta-independent nonzero scalar and A(theta) is the real product of the displayed sine factors. A(theta) may change sign; this is not a positivity assertion. In particular, away from its zero set the angular phase derivative equals partial_(theta_a) Arg(source density)=(S_a-2d)/2. (9) Equation (8) is global on the lifted angles. Its sine signs account for the apparent phase jumps and the periodicity of the original integer-degree density. Self-loops satisfy the same formula because their common anchor contributes one full theta_a phase. Thus the additive fusion defect S_a-2d is precisely the source's angular frequency, not only a formal incidence count. A full-block contraction adds the two endpoint defects at the identified anchor; a balanced star--triangle move removes a zero-frequency direction and preserves every outer defect. These are the exact incidence identities proved in the general fusion note. Removing an explicit self-loop monomial reduces both S_a and 2d by the same amount, when the remaining source charge is written correctly. For the below-balance central star here, S=2d-e, so this exact central frequency is -e/2. The retained degree-e polynomial and (5) quantify its actual cost, including every growing e=o(N) by (5a). A defect of order N is a macroscopic source phase. Its bound in (5) is not subexponential. At nonunit anchor radii, the real part of each logarithmic factor derivative need not be 1/2; (8)-(9) are not an exclusion theorem for complex critical points on deformed contours. There are two necessary limitations for the actual conjecture. First, the original clocks range across O(N), so a balance defect need not satisfy e=o(N); (5a) then gives no subexponential comparison. Second, a nonzero polynomial with a large norm can pair to zero with the exterior source. Equations (5)-(7) do not give a scalar lower bound after that pairing. A global theorem controlling defects and preserving the geometric contribution remains necessary. The coefficient identities are independently audited in [the defect-jet audit](../experiments/audit_charged_star_triangle_defect_jets.py). The separate exact source fusion note gives the full-length reproducing kernel and the consequent contraction of the original closure adapters. No new broad-class volume theorem is asserted here.

title: A torus generator need not select the highest regular critical value
text: # A torus generator need not select the highest regular critical value 28 October 2026. The implication original source generates H_k((C*)^k) + unique highest real regular critical action => that critical point contributes is FALSE for homogeneous polynomial coefficient periods with only coordinate poles. It remains false when every noncoordinate factor has a root-of-unity phase and the source is the specified finite-flat Fermat/nilpotent top coefficient. An explicit example below has a strict Cauchy bound BELOW its unique highest regular critical value. Thus its original torus misses that critical point's upward cycle. These examples are not asserted to arise from an original knot diagram. They refute an inference from the stated source/topology properties alone. The actual fixed-diagram clock couplings and root interval patterns may impose additional restrictions; those would have to enter a valid knot theorem. ## 1. A completely rational example with an explicit selected limit Put f(z)=z^(-1)+(91/100)z+(9/200)z^2, a_n=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral_(|z|=1) f(z)^n dz/z. The source is exactly the generator of H_1(C*). The form has only coordinate poles. Its regular logarithmic critical points satisfy 100 z^2 f'(z)=(z-1)(z+10)(9z+10)=0. Their values are EXACTLY f(1)=391/200, f(-10)=-47/10, f(-10/9)=-167/90. (1) All are nonzero and nondegenerate. The unique highest real part of log f is therefore log(47/10), at z=-10, independent of its chosen logarithmic mark. But on the original source circle the triangle inequality gives |f(exp(i theta))|<=391/200<47/10. Consequently |a_n|<=(391/200)^n.
