The cap slope remains (dW/ds)_(s=0)=tau sinh h/h, with its marked limit tau. The full joint period space also retains J. It is irregular at h=0, although every J_N has modulus one. The finite phase cover J^4=1 is valid on the prescribed root fibers; it is not invariant under the q-direction connection in (2.2): d(J^4)=-2tau^2 J^4 dh/h^2. Consequently freezing a residue-class phase, as in the meridian difference base, does not construct its joint q-direction period connection. There is no contradiction with the fixed-sheet parity statements of the preceding note, which concern meridian source coefficients on that sheet. The root graphs are therefore not Zariski dense in this enlarged Tate space: J^4-1 vanishes on all of them. The earlier density theorem applies on the specified finite phase components of the meridian difference base. It cannot reconstruct the q-direction connection from root evaluations. In particular (2.2) is a specified period lift, rather than a unique interpolation theorem for the full quantum state. The actual complete cap has a joint lift on this space: d_cap(h)=-i J(h) h/tau, dlog d_cap=(1/h-tau^2/(2h^2))dh. (5.2) At h_N=tau/N it is exactly eta_N/N, with modulus 1/N. The previous fixed-phase regular cap is the h factor after its specified Tate line is recorded. Formula (5.2) retains that line, including the even-level sign. Fixed rational Tate constants in an action are also retained by finite root lines of J. For example, Li_2(1)=pi^2/6 gives exp(Li_2(1)/(2h))=J^(-1/6) on its marked cover. Such a factor has modulus one at the prescribed roots. This observation does not control an unknown full quantum amplitude. The geometric action line retains an additional irregular factor. At the complete hyperbolic point, Im S_0=Vol(M)>0, so the term S_0/(2h) cannot be removed by the meridian blowup. This is the period carrying volume. It remains part of the marked exponential connection, rather than becoming a regular algebraic function after the Frobenius normalization has been resolved. ## 6. Rational Frobenius base change preserves source classes Let (F,sigma) be a characteristic-zero difference field and let C in GL_d(F). Adjoin an independent w with sigma(w)=-w and put E=F(w). The Laurent constant-coefficient map at w=0, r:E->F, r(t)=[w^0]t, is F-linear, is the identity on F, and commutes with sigma. This is a coefficient extraction, not evaluation of a possibly polar rational function at zero. Existence of the Laurent expansion over F gives all three assertions. Hence r((sigma-C)t)=(sigma-C)r(t). It induces a left inverse on the additive source quotients: F^d/(sigma-C)F^d -> E^d/(sigma-C)E^d. (6.1) In particular (6.1) is injective. The same argument works for sigma(w)=chi*w, chi in F^*, and for finitely many independent diagonally shifted variables, by iterated Laurent extraction. A further finite sigma-stable algebraic cover does not change the conclusion, by normalized trace as in [the affine-source proof](affine_quantum_a_period.md#2-finite-algebraic-covers-do-not-kill-a-nonzero-affine-class). Thus a nonsplit source already defined over C(q,M) remains nonsplit on the rational Frobenius base, including on each specified phase component and after finite stable covers. Principalizing its meridian lattice does not furnish a horizontal splitting. This statement does not say that two specified nonsplit extensions cannot be compared; their class difference is the actual comparison to compute. The hypothesis that C and the source descend to F matters. This does not by itself classify source matrices that genuinely depend on w, or compare an unknown homogeneous gauge over E. Nor does it apply to unrestricted completed or analytic period extensions such as the logarithmic/exponential construction above. ## 7. A degree obstruction to compressing a nonsplit root period Assume F=K(q,M), with K a fixed number field, and a specified nonsplit equation sigma(v)=Cv+c over F. Write C=A_0/D and c=b_0/D with Laurent-polynomial coefficients. Suppose a proposed root-level rational section has a presentation v=a/B in K(q,M,w)^d. Its cleared residual is R=D sigma(a) B-A_0 a sigma(B)-b_0 B sigma(B). (7.1) Some component of R is nonzero: otherwise (6.1) would produce a generic rational splitting. If v is an exact solution on the whole graph q=q_N,w=M^N, that component vanishes on the graph. The [root-graph rigidity theorem](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md#2-root-graphs-give-a-genuine-algebraic-rigidity-test) therefore implies D_M(R)>=N or [K:Q] D_q(R)>=phi(2N), (7.2) where D_M is the M exponent span and D_q is the q exponent span after a Laurent monomial is cleared. All denominators must be defined as rational whole graphs. The coefficient field must remain fixed; allowing arbitrary cyclotomic coefficients changes the stated field-degree bound. For example, if the fixed operator data have absolute M and q exponents bounded by c_M,c_q, and a,B have exponents bounded by d_M,d_q, (7.1) has D_M(R)<=2c_M+4d_M, D_q(R)<=2c_q+4d_q+2d_M. (7.3) The last term records sigma(M^j)=q^j M^j. No bound on the w degree is needed for the exponent-separation argument. Thus a fixed bounded rational presentation of a nonsplit period cannot recover every large root level merely by adjoining w. This applies to an actual knot source only after its specified generic source and nonsplitting hypotheses have been proved. The adequacy note supplies such a nonsplitting consequence under its explicitly stated actual-source hypotheses; it does not construct that source for every knot. A bounded comparison between two transcendental periods is not excluded by (7.2): the periods can be complicated while their intertwiner is simple. ## 8. A normalization criterion on this common space There is a direct extension of [the fixed central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md). Let a comparison factor have a fixed finite algebraic presentation over C(q,t,M,W,J), restricted by q=exp(tau/N), t=1/N, W=M^N, J=i^N. If its chosen whole M=1 value r_N is finite and nonzero, then log|r_N|=O(log N). Indeed J takes only four values. On each phase sheet the previous theorem applies; taking the maximum of the four bounds proves the assertion. Fixed finite roots of J have only finitely many values as well. Poles or zeros common to an entire phase must first be canceled on that restricted algebraic branch, as in the previous whole-germ theorem; an undefined restriction is not an evaluation. Consequently an actual exact comparison F_N(1)=r_N Z_N(complete) of this specified kind would prove the volume conjecture, with error O(log N/N). This is a sufficient comparison criterion, not a hypothesis being asserted for the actual period. A formal unit in h need not have such a finite algebraic presentation or control its selected root realization. Nor does the criterion permit discarding other period components or their cancellations. ## 9. Scope, existing coverage, and verification The positive ideal triangulation supplies beta, its central H mark, and the geometric A-curve used in Section 1. The construction then places its regulator action, the actual half-Frobenius mark, and the root phases in one explicit exponential-connection space. The source-class lemma prevents confusing this larger coefficient space with a splitting of the actual quantum source. The subsequent [controlled cyclic Euler source](controlled_cyclic_euler_source.md) now supplies a specific local comparison with uniform control. The literature cyclic coefficient vector is an explicit reflected factorial source vector, with its full inhomogeneous equation and co-source retained. Its scalar has a direct norm-product formula and polynomial bounds despite growing algebraic degree. This is one actual local source comparison, not the full source-to-Z map or a proof of its selected geometric coupling. What remains is the actual source-compatible map, with its cut, lattice transitions, quantum amplitude and selected relative period. No geometric factor of a minimal actual operator or nonzero geometric coupling of the selected finite sum is inferred here. Polylogarithmic period connections and Bloch regulators have existing coverage in [Hain, Classical Polylogarithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9202022). Exponential connections and rescaled twists have existing coverage in [Sabbah--Yu, 1406.1339](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1339). Only scope and the standard exponential-connection definition are used; no Hodge, strictness, pushforward or comparison theorem from these works is a proof premise. The proofs here are the displayed differentiation, monomial and coefficient calculations. No novelty is claimed for the Heisenberg connection, exponential twists, coefficient descent or elementary cyclotomic degree bound. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_common_regulator_period_space.py) checks the action differential, all three connection forms, the noncommutative integral deck composition, phase identifications, the invariant root norm, and source-class retraction with moving and polar denominators. A non-knot root example checks that an exact levelwise splitting can fail the generic source equation. [Results](../experiments/common_regulator_period_space_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_common_regulator_period_space.py

title: Independent audit of the common-Verma two-wall source
text: # Independent audit of the common-Verma two-wall source Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [common_verma_two_wall_source.md](common_verma_two_wall_source.md) is sound as stated. I checked the module, boundary maps, excursion factor, extension class, coherent action, and marked peripheral period directly. No new test run was needed. ## 1. The actual module and the two rank-one edges With \(\delta=1-Q^N\) and \(w=MQ^{-N}-M^{-1}\), the Jacobian in \((\log Q,\log M)\) at the marked point is \[ \begin{pmatrix}-N&0\\-N&2\end{pmatrix}, \] of determinant \(-2N\). The walls are independent. Adjacent products of the infinite coefficients give \([\mathcal E,F]=\rho(K-K^{-1})\), including at index zero. Thus the infinite object is a genuine module before either wall is imposed. The only head-to-tail \(F\)-edge is \(\delta U\); the only tail-to-head \(\mathcal E\)-edge is \(wL\). Their block multiplication gives \[ [F,P]=\delta U,\qquad [\mathcal E,P]=-wL, \] and the head commutator has defect \(-\delta w\,LU=-\delta wP_{N-1}\). The odd two-corner matrix squares to \(\delta w I\). The source-coupon formulas follow by the same block multiplication, with the stated signs. At \(\delta=0\) the head is a submodule. At \(w=0\) the tail is a submodule and the head is the quotient. Near \(M=1\), the latter wall is the genuine integral color \(M=-q^N\), rather than the fixed-root meridian direction. These orientations are not conflated. ## 2. The braid excursion adapter and the Bockstein The displayed balanced crossing coefficients agree with the actual canceled factorial coefficients. On head inputs, exiting through \(F\) has a Gaussian numerator \(1-Q^N\) and no zero denominator, hence a factor \(\delta\). Returning from a tail input through \(\mathcal E\) crosses index \(N\) and has the factor \[ 1-M^2Q^{-N}=-Mw. \] The inverse has the same property with its transfer directions exchanged. Every nontrivial ambient head-to-head path has a first exit and return, hence a factor \(\delta w\). All calculations take place in a finite invariant total-position sector, so the path expansion has no infinite convergence issue. At the node, division by \(\delta w\) retains exactly the single-excursion terms. The resulting adapter need not have rank one, as the note correctly states. At the fixed root, \[ \mathcal E^N=\gamma\kappa_N B,\qquad \gamma=(-1)^{N+1}. \] On the first two blocks, its derivative at \(M=1\) is \(\gamma2N\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\). The zeroth central operator is zero, so a regular first-normal change of splitting contributes a commutator with zero and cannot remove this term. A direct sum of the two head families has the central operator identically zero. This proves non-splitting of the stated first-normal extension; it is stronger than a nonzero unclosed current. ## 3. Weyl orientation and the literal centralizer action The divided \(F\)-matrix coefficient is \(\binom{a+N}{N}_Q\), whose root value is \(r+1\) on block \(a=rN+j\). Hence \(B=\partial_t,\ T=t\) on \(t^r/r!\), and \([B,T]=I\). The coherent-kernel identities have the stated orientation; treating \(B\mapsto s,T\mapsto\partial_s\) as a direct algebra homomorphism would be incorrect. For \(\lambda_b=1+\kappa_Nb\), \[ U_bf(t)=e^{bt}f(\lambda_bt). \] Direct composition gives \[ U_bU_cf(t)= e^{(b+c+\kappa_Nbc)t} f((1+\kappa_N(b+c+\kappa_Nbc))t), \] which is the exact regular-centralizer group law. Its coherent action is \(s\mapsto\lambda_bs+b\), with anchor \(s=0\); the locus \(1+\kappa_Ns\ne0\) is a genuine torsor. The infinitesimal operator is \(T(1+\kappa_NB)\), in that order. It changes the central source character and is not claimed to be a fixed-fiber quantum-group intertwiner. ## 4. The marked relative period and its scope The head projection satisfies \(\pi_0U_b\theta_0=I_H\) exactly. Applying the original normalized head cut therefore gives the scalar matrix coefficient one, before integration. With the retained endpoint \(b=M^N\), the invariant form integrates to \[ \frac{\operatorname{Log}(M^{2N})}{\kappa_N} =\frac N{u_N(M)} \frac{\operatorname{Log}(M^2)}{M-M^{-1}}. \] The complete value is one. The normalization and the direction of the adapter \(u_N/N\) are correct; the logarithm sheet and whole peripheral divisor are not discarded. The earlier unbalanced factorial basis change is singular on tail root blocks. The proof correctly does not identify the two infinite root lattices or remove the earlier Alexander denominator. The source remains an E-semicyclic/reducible centralizer object. No map to the irreducible hyperbolic framing class, selected Bloch regulator, or volume norm is asserted. The explicit source and Bockstein data are valid inputs for such a future comparison, not a substitute for it.

title: The balanced common-Verma source at the two walls
text: # The balanced common-Verma source at the two walls Research construction, 27 October 2026. A single genuine infinite balanced module realizes the finite root color as a submodule and the complete integral color as a quotient. Its boundary has two opposite rank-one edges, giving an explicit matrix factorization of the compressed Hopf defect. At the root its block completion has an exact Weyl pair, coherent source kernel and a literal action of the regular-meridian centralizer. These are actual source modules and matrix maps. They do not identify their coherent parameter with the internal geometric framing of a knot, or prove its selected Bloch-regulator period or volume norm. ## 1. One genuine module before either specialization Fix N>=2 and the marked point q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), M=1. Put Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), x=-M/q. Work over the local characteristic- zero coefficient ring R at this point, retaining the prescribed Cartan half-character. The following are regular parameters: delta=1-Q^N, w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1)=(Y-Z)/(MZ), Y=M^2, Z=Q^N. (1.1) Their Jacobian in log Q,log M has nonzero determinant -2N. On the free direct-sum module with basis v_a, a>=0, define K v_a=x Q^(-a)v_a, Ecal v_a=(M Q^(-a)-M^(-1))v_(a-1), a>=1, Ecal v_0=0, F v_a=(1-Q^(a+1))v_(a+1). (1.2) Every matrix column is finite. Direct adjacent-entry multiplication gives, for all generic q,M, K Ecal K^(-1)=Q Ecal, K F K^(-1)=Q^(-1)F, [Ecal,F]=rho(K-K^(-1)). (1.3) Thus E=Ecal/rho^2 gives a genuine unrestricted quantum-sl2 module. There is no generic-M finite-dimensional Hopf premise here. ## 2. The literal rank-one boundary and its two-wall factorization Let H=span(v_0,...,v_(N-1)) be the finite head and T the remaining tail. Use the literal inclusion i and projection p. Set U(v_(N-1))=v_N, L(v_N)=v_(N-1), zero on all other basis vectors. In head/tail block notation, F=[F_H 0;delta U F_T], Ecal=[E_H wL;0 E_T], K=[K_H 0;0 K_T]. (2.1) The head projector P=i p has exact Ward boundary currents [F,P]=delta U, [Ecal,P]=-wL, [K,P]=0. (2.2) Compression of (1.3) therefore gives precisely [E_H,F_H]-rho(K_H-K_H^(-1)) =-delta w P_(N-1). (2.3) This is the actual generic finite auxiliary Hopf defect. On the two corner lines v_(N-1),v_N the odd boundary matrix is D_boundary=[0 w;delta 0], D_boundary^2=delta w I. (2.4) It is an explicit matrix factorization of the two-wall product, with its two arrows fixed by the original generator entries. On R/(delta w) it is a two-periodic complex. No arbitrary choice of a normal identification is used to construct it. On delta=0, H is an actual invariant submodule, giving 0 -> H_root -> V_root -> T_root -> 0. (2.5) On w=0, T is invariant and the same finite head is the quotient: 0 -> T_Weyl -> V_Weyl -> H_Weyl -> 0. (2.6) Near the marked point the latter wall is x=q^(N-1), M=-q^N, the genuine complete integral color. At the intersection both boundary arrows vanish, and the two marked subquotients agree. The opposite orientations of (2.5)--(2.6) explain why their normal derivatives must not be silently identified. The source and co-source are equally explicit. For the prescribed balanced head cut e=psi phi, psi=1, phi=(1/N)sum_a, extend it to the finite-rank ambient coupon Gamma=i e p. Then [Ecal,Gamma]=i[E_H,e]p-w i e L, [F,Gamma]=i[F_H,e]p+delta U e p. (2.7) The original pivot, defect D_cut and modified-dimension line remain the ones recorded in the actual finite Ward/cut construction. Equation (2.7) supplies their boundary arrows before normal specialization; it is not a replacement cut functional. ## 3. Regular infinite R entries and an exact braid excursion adapter Use the balanced infinite crossing coefficients with no upper cutoff on a,b. After separating only the original common Cartan unit, the positive transfer has k=0,...,a and coefficient (-1)^k x^(-a-b-k) Q^[ab+(a-b)k-k(k+1)/2] {b+k choose k}_Q (M^2 Q^(-a);Q)_k. (3.1) The negative transfer has k=0,...,b and coefficient x^(a+b-k)Q^(-ab) {a+k choose k}_Q (M^2 Q^(-b);Q)_k. (3.2) Both are Laurent polynomials in the displayed nonzero variables, since the Gaussian coefficient is polynomial. They are the exact generic balanced basis changes of the existing Verma R entries; their apparent divided-factorial poles have already canceled. Every total-index shell is finite and invariant. These formulas and their original Cartan line therefore specialize regularly at the root, including terms k>=N when the input is in the tail. Let P_b project to H^(tensor b). For a local crossing R_i, (1-P_b)R_i P_b is divisible by delta, P_b R_i(1-P_b) is divisible by w. (3.3) For the first assertion all entering indices are <N and k<N. An exit through F has a Gaussian numerator 1-Q^N with no zero denominator. For the second assertion an entering tail index which returns into the head must cross the E edge at N. Its Pochhammer product contains 1-M^2Q^(-N)=-M w. The other possible entering tail index only increases and cannot return. The same reasoning applies to the inverse crossing, with the two transfer directions exchanged. Spectator indices do not alter these assertions. For a word beta=R_m...R_1, let R_beta^amb be its product on the common module, and R_beta^H the product of its individually compressed finite-head matrices. On head inputs the total index is at most b(N-1). Restrict all ambient calculations to the finite span of tuples of nonnegative indices with that total bound. No infinite summation is needed. Expanding each intermediate head/tail projector gives the exact regular identity P_b R_beta^amb i_b-R_beta^H =delta w H_beta. (3.4) Every excursion has a first exit containing delta and a return containing w. This proves divisibility even for words with many excursions and for both crossing signs. The quotient H_beta is canonical in the local domain; the path expansion computes it by finite matrix multiplication. It keeps all phases, Cartan, twist and boundary factors rather than discarding a multiplier. At the intersection its value is the sum of paths with exactly one excursion. This is a concrete mixed-normal connecting matrix. For a pair of generators F followed by Ecal it reduces to the rank-one product L U=P_(N-1) in (2.3). For a braid word its rank need not remain one. Thus the root submodule and Weyl quotient have an actual common R realization and a specified off-intersection curvature adapter. Equality of their ordinary values at the node does not make the two transverse source jets equal. ## 4. A nonzero root meridian extension Bockstein Now fix Q=Q_N and vary M. Coefficients in (1.2) are N-periodic. Put gamma=(-1)^(N+1), kappa_N=M^N-M^(-N). Directly multiplying N adjacent E edges gives Ecal^N v_a=0, a<N, Ecal^N v_a=gamma kappa_N v_(a-N), a>=N, F^N=0. (4.1) In particular the first two blocks span an actual 2N-dimensional root submodule, an extension of the finite head by an identical head quotient. At M=1 it splits. Nevertheless its first meridian normal is nonzero: [d/dM Ecal^N]_(M=1) =gamma 2N [0 I_N;0 0]. (4.2) The central operator Ecal^N is zero on both diagonal complete blocks. A regular first-normal change of splitting changes its first coefficient by a commutator with that zero operator, hence cannot remove (4.2). A direct sum of the two finite head families has Ecal^N identically zero. Therefore this actual first-normal self-extension does not split. This is a genuine nonzero boundary extension class, rather than just a nonzero entry of a current which might later be projected away. It is still a central root-source extension. It is not the irreducible hyperbolic representation, and does not by itself give a nonzero geometric coefficient in the knot period. ## 5. Exact block Weyl pair and the coherent source kernel Write a=rN+j, 0<=j<N. In the product completion of the root module let B be backward block shift, killing the first block. Then (4.1) says Ecal^N=gamma kappa_N B. This identity defines B integrally even at kappa_N=0; one does not divide two zero values. The operators are explicitly Ecal=E_H tensor I+kappa W tensor B, F=F_H tensor I, K=K_H tensor I, kappa=M-M^(-1), W=E_(N-1,0). (5.1) The second block operator is the regular divided matrix T=[F(q)^N/(Q;Q)_N]_(q=q_N). On the infinite balanced lattice its generic coefficient is the polynomial Gaussian {a+N choose N}_Q. At the root, T v_(rN+j)=(r+1)v_((r+1)N+j). (5.2) This root Gaussian value follows from the finite product formula: one zero numerator and denominator cancel, giving r+1; the remaining root factors cancel as a full cycle. No parity sign remains. Thus [B,T]=I. (5.3) Identify v_(rN+j) with h_j tensor t^r/r!. Then B=partial_t, T=t. The source kernel theta_s(h_j)=sum_(r>=0)s^r v_(rN+j) =h_j exp(st) (5.4) obeys B theta_s=s theta_s, T theta_s=partial_s theta_s and pi_0 theta_s=I. It is a coherent kernel; sending B to s and T to partial_s is not an algebra homomorphism with the same Weyl orientation. The t-model fixes that convention explicitly. The finite rank-N family induced on these kernels is E_s=E_H+kappa s W, F_s=F_H, K_s=K_H, E_s^N=gamma kappa_N s I. (5.5) It is a genuine unrestricted root quantum-group family: [W,F_H]=0 and K_H W K_H^(-1)=Q_N W preserve the generator relations. Its Casimir is unchanged since F_H W=0. The actual nilpotent head is s=0; its prescribed cyclic completion is s=1. These are fibers of the same actual source family in a common completed module, rather than unrelated matching determinants. The infinite R need not preserve a fixed s fiber; terms k>=N must remain in its action. ## 6. A literal regular-centralizer torsor representation Use kappa_N as parameter and the regular-meridian group at M^N: J_(M^N)={b:1+kappa_N b invertible}, b*c=b+c+kappa_N b c. On the Fock completion put N_block=T B and define U_b=exp(bT)(1+kappa_N b)^(N_block). (6.1) The second factor means diagonal multiplication by (1+kappa_N b)^r on block r; no logarithm choice is required. In the t model it is f(t) -> exp(bt) f((1+kappa_N b)t). Hence, exactly, U_b U_c=U_(b+c+kappa_N b c), U_b theta_s=theta_((1+kappa_N b)s+b). (6.2) The coherent locus 1+kappa_N s invertible is therefore a genuine J_(M^N) torsor with anchor theta_0, not only an equality of norm characters. Its infinitesimal operator is T(1+kappa_N B); on the kernel it is (1+kappa_N s)partial_s, in that order. At completeness it becomes the additive translation exp(bT). This action moves the source central character E_s^N; it is not asserted to be a fixed-color quantum-group intertwiner or the centralizer action on a knot's geometric framing coordinates. The finite source norm is consistent with this action: det(I+z E_s)=1+kappa_N s z^N. (6.3) Thus it pulls back the regular-centralizer character with b=s z^N, including its entire divisor. The original adapter u_N=kappa_N/(M-M^(-1)) and the phase i^(N+3) of d_N remain the ones already fixed in the actual state. Near M=1 the normalized power map from J_M is explicitly b -> [(1+(M-M^(-1))b)^N-1]/kappa_N. Its numerator has the same meridian zero; the resulting map is regular there. It sends the meridian section b=M to b'=M^N. This supplies an actual algebraic centralizer source action and its power adapter. It does not identify it with a knot's internal framing period or determine its regulator integration constant. There is also a specified source matrix coefficient for its marked relative period. Since pi_0 U_b theta_0=I_H, the actual normalized cut of this matrix coefficient is one. The invariant differential is db/(1+kappa_N b), and the recorded meridian section is b=M^N. On the marked local logarithmic branch, therefore, Phi_cut pi_0 integral_(0)^(M^N) U_b theta_0 db/(1+kappa_N b) =Log(M^(2N))/kappa_N. (6.4) It has complete value one. With kappa=M-M^(-1) and u_N=kappa_N/kappa the exact adapter is Log(M^(2N))/kappa_N =(N/u_N) Log(M^2)/kappa. (6.5) Thus obtaining the physical meridian period from the upstairs one uses u_N/N; the reverse power pullback uses N/u_N. The logarithm sheet and the whole u_N divisor remain marked. Formula (6.4) is an actual coherent-source matrix coefficient and its invariant group differential, not an arbitrary division by a group volume. It is a universal centralizer normalization period, not the knot-dependent marked Bloch regulator or its volume constant. ## 7. Comparison with the earlier source constructions The repository already has an unbalanced Verma period in [the Frobenius Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md), with the exact Alexander denominator, and genuine F-cyclic holonomy sources in [the carry-braiding note](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md). [The tetrahedral transport note](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) already supplies pointed compact-factor rewrites. No new Burau invariant or previously unavailable Verma construction is claimed. The present root lattice is different. The generic basis change v_a^unbalanced/(Q;Q)_a is a unit only for a<N at the root; it is singular on later blocks. Consequently the balanced root lattice has F^N=0 and nontrivial Ecal^N block lowering, whereas the unbalanced lattice has the opposite Frobenius behavior. One cannot substitute one root lattice for the other without its factorial carry and normal data. The new statements here are the explicit two-wall submodule/quotient comparison, nonzero extension Bockstein, dual E-cyclic coherent kernel, and literal Weyl/regular-centralizer source action. The complete-color q-normal and the fixed-root meridian normal also retain their distinct pivot/twist adapters from [the complete divided-Ward note](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md), Section 7. Those moments must accompany any closed period map. ## 8. Remaining geometric source map This constructs the common source, both branch maps, their mixed normal curvature and a genuine centralizer torsor action from actual matrices. The marked finite cut is still the head source with its original coupon and normal row. The infinite R acts on coherent parameters, so its high-transfer terms cannot be discarded when comparing a nonzero s fiber with that head. No identification of this torsor with the selected geometric framing of a hyperbolic A-curve has yet been proved. Nor has a nonzero global coefficient of the regulator period been obtained. The exact adapters above specify what such a source map must carry, rather than infer it from equal normal values or a norm character alone. [Exact matrix audit](../experiments/audit_common_verma_two_wall_source.py). [Results](../experiments/common_verma_two_wall_source_results.json). [Independent proof audit](common_verma_two_wall_independent_audit.md).

title: Independent audit of the compact coherent source period
text: # Independent audit of the compact coherent source period Audit, 27 October 2026. Sections 1--5 of [compact_coherent_source_period.md](compact_coherent_source_period.md) pass this independent check. The finite centered star derivatives, global primitive, both walls and physical Poisson scale are correct. No test rerun was needed. ## 1. Fixed compact cycle and exact products The degree \(n=N-1\) kernel is a section of \(O(n,n)\). Its quotient by the identity kernel is regular on the fixed surface \(X=(\mathbb P^1)^2\setminus D\); its form has the correct canonical degree and no poles outside \(D\). The real sphere \(w=v,z=\bar v\) is disjoint from \(D\), including infinity. Its orientation gives \[ -\frac1{2\pi i}\frac{dw\wedge dz}{(1+wz)^2} =\frac{d(\operatorname{area}v)} {\pi(1+|v|^2)^2}. \] Angular integration and the printed beta integral therefore yield \(\int_\Gamma\omega_A=\operatorname{Tr}(A)/N\). The factor \(N\) in kernel composition precisely cancels the middle beta pairing; no intermediate binomial remains. The centered star formula is exact. At the origin, its two derivatives are \(r!\binom nr A_{0r}\) and \(r!B_{r0}\), so the coefficient \((n-r)!/(r!n!)\) produces \(A_{0r}B_{r0}\). For the general point, put \(d=1+wz\) and \[ g=d^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&-w\\z&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Its column action sends \(b\) to \((z+b)/(1-wb)\); the dual row action sends \(a\) to \((w+a)/(1-za)\). The symmetric-power basis with the printed column binomials therefore gives exactly the stated two centered derivatives. Both differentiated expressions are finite polynomials of degree at most \(n\). The square-root sign cancels in conjugation. ## 2. The global rational primitive The commutator vector fields check directly: \[ \sigma_{[J_0,B]}=(w\partial_w-z\partial_z)\sigma_B,\qquad \sigma_{[J_-,B]}=(\partial_w+z^2\partial_z)\sigma_B. \] For the second identity, acting on the numerator produces \(\partial_w+z^2\partial_z-nz\); differentiating its denominator gives exactly the same correction. Both fields are global and preserve the identity two-form. The off-diagonal matrix is recovered by division by \(i-j\). For the diagonal primitive, the \(j\)-th commutator entry is \((j+1)b_j-jb_{j-1}\); the last entry is correct because the remaining diagonal has trace zero. Cartan's formula then gives \[ d(\sigma_B\iota_V\omega_I)=(V\sigma_B)\omega_I \] with the printed sign. Hence the rational primitive is global on \(X\), and Stokes on the actual compact sphere proves its zero period. The identity form itself has period one and is not being declared exact. ## 3. Whole walls and the physical Gauss scale Summing the truncated binomial kernels gives all three formulas in Section 4, including the lower-vacuum subtraction \(-\kappa(1-t)^n\) and upper-head subtraction \(-\delta t^n\). The latter uses \(n+1=N\), which fixes its coefficient and sign. Their normalized beta moments and falling-factorial number moments are exact with the stated factors of \(N\). The physical principal clock is \(A=e^{2\pi it}\), and \(p=1/w\) gives the printed balanced Gauss symbols. Direct differentiation gives \[ d\log A\wedge d\log p =2\pi i\,\frac{dw\wedge dz}{(1+wz)^2}. \] On the real sphere this is \(2\pi\,dt\wedge d\phi\). Thus the trace measure is precisely the normalized Liouville measure \(\Omega/(4\pi^2)=dt\,d\phi/(2\pi)\). The first star commutator has sign \((1+wz)^2(a_zb_w-b_za_w)/n\); division by \(h_N=2\pi i/N\) gives the inverse tensor of this same form. No fixed-root normal has been substituted for \(h_N\). ## 4. Source and asymptotic scope The original coupon functional equals normalized trace on the diagonal closed arrays and their number-moment weights, as stated. It does not equal it on arbitrary off-diagonal Ward insertions. For those, the exact compact expression would retain the coupon: \[ \Phi(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(eA) =N\int_\Gamma(\sigma_e\star\sigma_A)\,\omega_I. \] This follows immediately from the exact product and trace formulas. No such replacement is needed for the diagonal arrays considered in the note. The fixed algebraic surface and compact cycle are genuine. The symbol degree and allowed pole order still grow with \(N\); fixed dimension alone does not provide the bounded presentation required by the separate cyclotomic reconstruction theorem. Likewise the finite star formula does not imply a uniform semiclassical expansion for an arbitrary growing full-word matrix. The note correctly restricts its Poisson expansion to a controlled symbol class and leaves the global geometric source coefficient and its norm unproved. ## 5. The full top cohomology and uniform primitive bounds The added global cohomology statement also checks. Normalize the Segre matrix to have trace one: \[ \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},\qquad a+d=1,\quad ad=bc. \] Then \(h=2a-1,e=2b,f=2c\) identifies \(X\) with the smooth affine split quadric \(h^2+ef=1\). Every regular algebraic top form on \(X\) has finite pole order \(mD\) on the compactification. Since \[ \Omega^2_{\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1}(mD) =O(m-2,m-2), \] it has exactly the displayed kernel form with \(n=m-2\), after increasing the allowed pole order if necessary. The primitive therefore proves \[ H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(X) =k\left[\frac{dw\wedge dz}{(1+wz)^2}\right]. \] Its period is \(-2\pi i\), so it is nonzero. This is the fixed source's rank-one algebraic cohomology; it is not the full knot's Bloch-regulator period. For \(G_{jj}=\binom nj^{-1}\), the symbol on \(\Gamma\) is the normalized \(G\)-expectation in the column \(c_j=\binom nj\bar v^j\). Hence \(|\sigma_A|\le\|A\|_G\). Both primitive matrices actually have bounds independent of \(N\). For the off-diagonal part the exact integral \[ B_{\mathrm{off}} =\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} i(\theta-\pi)e^{i\theta J_0}Ae^{-i\theta J_0}\,d\theta \] has entry \(A_{ij}/(i-j)\) off the diagonal and zero diagonal. The conjugations are \(G\)-unitary, so \[ \|B_{\mathrm{off}}\|_G\le\frac\pi2\|A\|_G. \] For the raising part, let \(s_j=\sum_{k=0}^j(A_{kk}-\tau)\). Using both the prefix and its trace-zero complementary suffix gives \[ |s_j|\le2\min(j+1,n-j)\|A\|_G. \] Its weighted shift entry is \[ \frac{s_j}{j+1}\sqrt{\frac{j+1}{n-j}}, \] whose modulus is at most \(2\|A\|_G\). Therefore \(\|B_{\mathrm{diag}}\|_G\le2\|A\|_G\). These strengthen the polynomial estimates without changing the primitive or source. The qualification is the same-metric one: \(G\) itself is exponentially conditioned against the original Euclidean basis. These are uniform bounds for the source contraction in the coherent metric, not an unproved polynomial comparison with another metric or a bound on the actual crossing-word norm. ## 6. Fixed-order actual A-period and removal of its normal poles The subsequent fixed-matrix-size application is also valid. Use an actual order-\(r\) generic color recurrence and its companion matrices, fixed initial column \(v_0\), and last-coordinate row \(\ell\). For \[ H_N=A_{N-r}\cdots A_{j_0},\qquad R_N^{\mathrm{left}}(q)=v_0(q)\ell H_N(q) \] the all-level color theorem gives \(\operatorname{Tr}R_N^{\mathrm{left}}=\ell H_Nv_0=C_N(q)\). Applying the coherent calculus at matrix size \(r\), rather than color size \(N\), therefore gives \[ \Omega_N=r\,\omega_{(r,R_N^{\mathrm{left}})},\qquad \int_\Gamma\Omega_N=C_N(q). \] The surface, cycle and pole-order bound \(r+1\) are independent of the level. The case \(r=1\) is simply the scalar \(n=0\) coherent formula. The whole companion product has poles of order at most the uniform total leading-germ budget. Write its outer product at the marked root as \[ R_N^{\mathrm{left}}(q)=\sum_{j=-B}^{\infty}R_{N,j}\epsilon^j . \] Because \(C_N(q)\) is regular, every negative coefficient has trace zero. For each such coefficient the global primitive gives \(\omega_{(r,R_{N,j})}=d_{\mathrm{ext}}\eta_{R_{N,j}}\). Subtracting \[ d_{\mathrm{ext}}\left( r\sum_{j=-B}^{-1}\epsilon^j\eta_{R_{N,j}}\right) \] therefore removes every normal pole, leaves the period unchanged, and introduces no division by \(C_N\). In particular this works at a level where \(K_N=0\). The regularized representative remains in the same fixed pole-order top-form space. The order matters for interpreting this pole removal. The alternative matrix \[ R_N^{\mathrm{right}}=H_Nv_0\ell \] is already regular entrywise: its column \(H_Nv_0\) consists of actual Laurent-polynomial colors. The earlier ordering used in this audit was therefore valid for the period identity but made polar removal vacuous. In the revised left ordering, nonzero traceless polar coefficients can occur. The exact difference \[ R_N^{\mathrm{left}}-R_N^{\mathrm{right}} =[v_0\ell,H_N] \] has trace zero, and its global primitive identifies the two whole period classes without dividing by the selected scalar. This supplies an explicitly regular representative as well as the coefficientwise regularization above. This is a local regularization at the specified root, not a uniform bounded-height presentation of the growing companion product. Its rational coefficient degrees and heights can still grow with \(N\). Conversely, since the coherent matrix size is now fixed, its metric and primitive bounds do not acquire the exponential-in-color-size distortion mentioned in Section 5. Neither fact determines the physical norm or the geometric comparison.

title: A fixed compact algebraic period for the actual finite source
text: # A fixed compact algebraic period for the actual finite source Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual finite head admits an exact coherent-kernel calculus on one fixed algebraic surface. Its normalized trace is a period over a fixed compact sphere. Products, index moments, both wall terms, and all finite crossing words are retained. The physical large-level symbols have the same Gauss coordinates and symplectic form as the actual classical holonomy calculation. The coherent-state calculus is standard coverage; for example [Alexanian--Pinzul--Stern](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0010187) discusses coherent symbols, star products and the sphere measure. No proof from that paper is used here. The statements below give their exact normalizations for our actual balanced head and its source. No new knot invariant or replacement positive state is defined. The geometric contribution to the selected period is still unproved. In particular a compact cycle does not by itself select the geometric internal stationary point or bound its full quantum contraction. ## 1. The fixed surface, line, and cycle Put n=N-1 and use the actual head basis e_0,...,e_n. For an arbitrary matrix A define K_A(w,z)=sum_(i,j=0)^n w^i A_ij binom(n,j) z^j, sigma_A(w,z)=K_A(w,z)/(1+wz)^n. (1.1) This map is injective. It is the matrix pairing of the row (w^i) with the column (binom(n,j)z^j), whose identity pairing is K_I(w,z)=(1+wz)^n. Globally K_A is a section of O(n,n) on P1 times P1. Write D={s_0 t_0+s_1 t_1=0}, X=(P1 times P1) minus D. Thus sigma_A is a global regular algebraic function on X. In the displayed affine chart D is 1+wz=0. Define the algebraic two-form omega_A=-(1/(2pi*i)) K_A(w,z) dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^(N+1) =sigma_A omega_I, omega_I=-(1/(2pi*i)) dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^2. (1.2) The scalar 2pi*i records the period normalization. The underlying forms without that scalar are algebraic over the matrix coefficient field. The form omega_I is independent of N. The O(n,n) degree makes (1.2) a global meromorphic two-form with poles only on D. The fixed compact cycle is Gamma={w=v,z=bar(v)}, including the point at infinity. It is an oriented real sphere, disjoint from D. On its finite chart, dw wedge dz=-2i d(area v). Hence exactly integral_Gamma omega_A =(1/pi) integral_C K_A(v,bar(v))/(1+|v|^2)^(N+1) d(area v) =Tr(A)/N. (1.3) To prove the last equality integrate the angle first, killing i!=j. For i=j use r=|v|^2 and the beta identity integral_0^infinity r^j/(1+r)^(N+1) dr =j!(n-j)!/N!=1/[N binom(n,j)]. (1.4) Repeated integration by parts proves (1.4), starting with j=0. In particular integral_Gamma omega_I=1. The whole period and its normalization are specified before any local asymptotic expansion. This cycle computes the actual normalized cut on every diagonal matrix: the original coupon e_ij=1/N satisfies Tr(eA)=Tr(A)/N there. Every original one-cut state array is diagonal term by term by total-index conservation. Inserting any transfer-index or cut-index moment preserves this property. Thus the original selected knot scalar and the weighted finite arrays used by the full Green certificate use precisely this compact trace period. Equality with Tr(eA) is not asserted for an arbitrary off-diagonal A. The [whole weighted-word/current map](relative_word_green_transport.md) realizes these arrays by transfer-coupled actual crossings and Euler weight derivatives. It supplies the explicit least-moment Green currents and their relative endpoint transport, including every internal head projector. Hence the compact cycle here applies to that entire actual current family, not only its unweighted scalar specialization. ## 2. Exact composition preserves the entire word The same beta pairing gives the identity of polynomial kernels K_(AB)(w,z)=(N/pi) integral_C K_A(w,bar(v)) K_B(v,z)/(1+|v|^2)^(N+1) d(area v). (2.1) Indeed a middle index j contributes binom(n,j) twice as appropriate and the pairing (1.4) removes the middle binomial factor, leaving the coefficient of AB. The factor N in (2.1) is essential. Tensor products use product measures; the actual pivotal matrices, turns, framing factors and crossing weights stay inside the kernels. Iteration therefore represents every finite actual crossing word, including all source constraints, without changing its value. There is also a finite algebraic star product with no integrals in its definition. Set d=1+wz and introduce centered parameters a,b: z_b=(z+b)/(1-wb), w_a=(w+a)/(1-za). Then sigma_(AB)(w,z) =sum_(r=0)^n (n-r)!/[r! n!] [partial_b^r sigma_A(w,z_b)]_(b=0) [partial_a^r sigma_B(w_a,z)]_(a=0). (2.2) The one-variable expressions differentiated here are polynomials of degree at most n. For example sigma_A(w,z_b)=d^(-n) sum_(i,j) w^i A_ij binom(n,j)(z+b)^j(1-wb)^(n-j). For a proof of (2.2), at w=z=0 the derivatives extract r!binom(n,r)A_(0,r) and r!B_(r,0); the displayed coefficient makes their product A_(0,r)B_(r,0). At any other point the change of basis induced by (1/sqrt(d))*[[1,-w],[z,1]] in SL2 reduces the identity to the origin. Its dual projective coordinate changes are precisely w_a,z_b. The result is independent of the square-root sign and hence a rational identity on X. Thus sigma is an algebra isomorphism onto its finite symbol space equipped with (2.2). The trace is cyclic for this exact star product. In particular ordinary multiplication of clock symbols must not be substituted for star multiplication: sigma_clock star-powered N times is 1 because the actual clock has N-th power I. ## 3. A global rational primitive for every traceless source This period has an explicit algebraic source contraction. Let J_0 e_j=j e_j, J_- e_j=j e_(j-1). Direct differentiation of (1.1) gives sigma_[J_0,B]=V_0 sigma_B, V_0=w partial_w-z partial_z, sigma_[J_-,B]=V_- sigma_B, V_-=partial_w+z^2 partial_z. (3.1) These are global vector fields on P1 times P1, preserve D, and preserve omega_I. For V_- this follows from V_-(1+wz)=z(1+wz) and divergence(V_-)=2z; the two terms cancel. The verification for V_0 is immediate. For any A put tau=Tr(A)/N and decompose A-tau I=A_off+A_diag, Tr(A_diag)=0. Define B_off by (B_off)_ij=A_ij/(i-j) for i!=j and zero diagonal. Define B_diag to have only raising entries (B_diag)_(j+1,j)=[sum_(k=0)^j(A_kk-tau)]/(j+1), j<n. Then exactly A-tau I=[J_0,B_off]+[J_-,B_diag]. (3.2) For the diagonal identity, its j-th entry is (j+1)b_j-jb_(j-1); the last entry uses the trace-zero condition. Combining (3.1)--(3.2) and Cartan's formula proves omega_A-tau omega_I=d eta_A, eta_A=sigma_(B_off) iota_(V_0)omega_I +sigma_(B_diag) iota_(V_-)omega_I. (3.3) Every term is a global rational form on X, not a primitive defined only on a framing chart. Stokes' theorem on the actual compact Gamma proves its zero pairing. Equation (3.3) is a whole algebraic cohomology identity specifying exactly the coefficient selected by the cycle. It does not estimate that coefficient as N grows. This differs from discarding every divergence on an affine chart: omega_I has period one and cannot be globally exact on X. A local primitive for it necessarily fails to extend or has boundary/period data. The compactification retains precisely that distinction. ### The source cohomology is one fixed algebraic line The surface itself is a smooth affine quadric. Under the Segre embedding write the four coordinates as (a,b,c,d), with ad-bc=0. On X normalize a+d=1. Then h=2a-1, e=2b, f=2c, h^2+ef=1. (3.4) Conversely these formulas recover all four coordinates and the point of X. On Gamma, h is real and f=bar(e), giving the unit real sphere h^2+|e|^2=1. Every global regular algebraic two-form on X has some finite pole order m on D in P1 times P1. The space of such forms with pole order at most m is the section space of Omega^2(mD)=O(m-2,m-2). For m<2 it is zero. For m>=2 set n=m-2; its every section is exactly the form (1.2) for one (n+1)-dimensional matrix, with the inessential common normalization removed if working over Q. Equation (3.3) therefore proves on this affine surface H^2_dR(X)=k[dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^2]. (3.5) The generator is not exact because its compact period is -2pi*i. No comparison theorem or dimension count is needed for this top cohomology calculation: the explicit primitive covers every form. This is a fixed source cohomology line, not the full Bloch regulator of the knot. The latter is still carried by the knot's coefficient transport and its selected large-level class. The contraction also has a uniform norm bound. Give the original head the positive metric G_jj=1/binom(n,j). On Gamma, sigma_A is the expectation of A in its normalized coherent vector for this metric, so |sigma_A|<=||A||_G and |tau|<=||A||_G. The constructed matrices obey ||B_off||_G<=(pi/2)||A||_G, ||B_diag||_G<=2||A||_G. (3.6) For the first bound there is the exact Fourier inverse B_off=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi) i(theta-pi) exp(i theta J_0) A exp(-i theta J_0)dtheta. Its nonzero m-th Fourier coefficient is 1/m and its constant coefficient is zero. These conjugations are G-unitary, and the average absolute weight is pi/2, proving the bound. For the second, the trace-zero prefix sum S_j can be bounded from either end, giving |S_j|<=2min(j+1,n-j)||A||_G. The raising entry changes the orthonormal basis by sqrt((j+1)/(n-j)); hence its magnitude is at most 2min(j+1,n-j)/sqrt((j+1)(n-j)) times ||A||_G, at most 2||A||_G. A one-step weighted shift has norm the largest magnitude of these entries. The vector fields and omega_I are fixed smooth tensors on Gamma. This source contraction therefore has no large-level norm loss in the same coherent metric. That metric can be exponentially conditioned relative to the original Euclidean basis; no crossing-word norm bound or absence of scalar cancellation is inferred from (3.6). ## 4. Both actual wall terms are whole functions in this calculus Use the finite balanced head, with Q=q^2 and kappa=M-M^(-1): K e_j=-(M/q)Q^(-j)e_j, Ecal e_j=(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))e_(j-1), j>0, Ecal e_0=0, F e_j=(1-Q^(j+1))e_(j+1), j<n, F e_n=0. These are the actual finite auxiliary matrices off the root, with their known wall defect. Put t=wz/(1+wz) and R_+=[1+(Q-1)t]^n, R_-=[1+(Q^(-1)-1)t]^n, delta=1-Q^N. Summing the binomial kernel gives exactly sigma_K=-(M/q) R_-, sigma_Ecal=w^(-1)[M R_- -M^(-1)-kappa(1-t)^n], sigma_F=w[R_0-Q R_+-delta t^n], R_0=1. (4.1) The apparent w inverse cancels in the numerator as required by the polynomial matrix kernel. At the actual root delta=0. At the complete meridian kappa=0. Before those restrictions the lower vacuum and upper head walls are the explicit functions (1-t)^n and t^n. Their derivatives must be retained before specializing. The lower vacuum coefficient kappa is not the second normal of the common-Verma two-wall construction: that normal is M Q^(-N)-M^(-1)=kappa+M delta/(1-delta). They agree on the root wall, but their off-root derivatives differ. Formula (4.1) keeps the actual finite-head coefficients and does not identify those two normals. Indeed sigma_(E_00)=(1-t)^n and sigma_(E_nn)=t^n. Both have normalized trace 1/N, despite being exponentially small on fixed interior subintervals. For a fixed polynomial moment t^h, N integral_0^1 t^(n+h) dt=N/(N+h), N integral_0^1 (1-t)^n t^h dt =h!/[(N+1)...(N+h)], (4.2) where the empty product at h=0 is one. Thus the marked endpoint rows, including their normal factors N, are exact beta identities. Interior Taylor/asymptotic jets alone would lose them. For the actual number operator J_0, more generally, sigma_(p(J_0))(t)=sum_(j=0)^n binom(n,j) t^j(1-t)^(n-j)p(j), sigma_((J_0)_r)=(n)_r t^r. (4.3) Here (a)_r is the falling factorial. These finite Newton identities transport every bounded index moment. They coexist with the exact whole-clock formula R_+, because products use (2.2). Coupling derivatives of a crossing kernel must still obey the full Leibniz rule. There is no substitution of an ordinary coordinate for a number operator before taking products. ## 5. The physical symbol and its holonomy form This construction also addresses the physical parameter, rather than the distinct normal to one fixed root. Set Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), h_N=2pi*i/N. For t in compact sets, the whole function [1+(exp(2pi*i*s)-1)t]^(1/s-1) has a removable analytic germ at s=0, with value exp(2pi*i*t), using its logarithm near one. This follows by factoring s from that logarithm. At s=1/N it is exactly R_+. The inverse version gives R_- and has value exp(-2pi*i*t). Away from the two endpoint walls on the real cycle, at M=1 the resulting principal functions are therefore A=exp(2pi*i*t), p=1/w, x=-M, K=x/A, Ecal=(x^(-1)-K)p, F=(1-A)/p. (5.1) At generic M the same statements hold on compact interior portions where the explicit vacuum term is exponentially small; that term cannot be dropped in a whole meridian/source identity. These are exactly the Gauss coordinates of the actual classical [longitude/holonomy calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). The source geometry has the exact symplectic identity dLog A wedge dLog p =2pi*i dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^2. (5.2) On Gamma, w=sqrt(t/(1-t))exp(i phi), this becomes 2pi dt wedge dphi. Its normalized Liouville measure is precisely the trace measure dt dphi/(2pi). Formula (2.2) has first-order commutator, in a controlled smooth symbol class, (1/n)(1+wz)^2 [partial_z a partial_w b-partial_z b partial_w a]. Dividing by h_N gives the Poisson tensor inverse to (5.2), since n h_N tends to 2pi*i. For the actual generators the bracket identities also follow directly from their exact matrix relations. No uniform star expansion is asserted for an arbitrary rapidly growing matrix family, in particular not for the unknown full knot period. ## 6. A direct actual-A period has fixed pole order as well There is a second useful application, directly to the specified quantum A-operator. It uses the compact calculus at a fixed matrix size d, rather than the growing color size N. Keep these two uses distinct. The [actual all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md) supplies the generic recurrence for the actual colors, with fixed companion rank d, v_(j+1)(q)=A_j(q)v_j(q), v_j=(C_j,...,C_(j+d-1))^t. Choose the fixed sufficiently large starting color j_0 prescribed there. All initial entries v_0:=v_(j_0) are fixed Laurent-polynomial colors, and no subsequent leading coefficient is identically zero. Set H_N=A_(N-d)...A_(j_0), ell=e_d^t, R_N(q)=v_0(q)ell H_N(q). (6.1) This is a specified rank-at-most-one d by d rational matrix. Its input is only the actual operator and finite initial-color pointing. The exact recurrence proves Tr R_N(q)=ell H_N(q)v_0(q)=C_N(q). (6.2) Use the kernel (1.1) at matrix size d, denoted K^(d), and define Omega_N(q)=-(d/(2pi*i)) K^(d)_(R_N(q))(w,z) dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^(d+1). Then the literal actual A-period identity is integral_Gamma Omega_N(q)=C_N(q), [integral_Gamma Omega_N(q)]_(q=q_N)=K_N. (6.3) Thus both the algebraic surface, cycle and pole order d+1 are fixed independently of N in this operator realization. The ordered transport product still has N-dependent coefficient complexity; no bounded height, fixed degree in q, or volume estimate follows from (6.3). Apparent quantum-normal poles can also be removed as exact forms. At q_N expand R_N=sum_(r>=-s)epsilon^r R_(N,r). Since C_N(q) is the original regular color polynomial, every coefficient R_(N,r) with r<0 has trace zero. Formula (3.3) gives a specified rational one-form eta_(N,r) with omega^(d)_(R_(N,r))=d eta_(N,r). Therefore Omega_N^reg=Omega_N -d*d_deRham[sum_(r<0)epsilon^r eta_(N,r)] (6.4) is regular at q_N, has the same period and specializes to K_N. The first d in the subtracted expression is the integer companion rank; d_deRham is the exterior derivative. This procedure never divides by C_N or assumes K_N!=0. The uniform leading-coefficient pole budget from the all-level theorem bounds s independently of N. Equivalently slide the pointed source through the whole product: R_N^right=H_N v_0 ell, R_N-R_N^right=[v_0 ell,H_N]. (6.5) The right representative is regular, since H_N v_0 is exactly the vector of actual regular colors. The commutator in (6.5) has the global primitive (3.3), proving equality of the two whole period classes. In the order (6.1) apparent poles can be nonzero matrices; one must not mistake cancellation of their traces for entrywise regularity before retaining this exact source map. Projection to the one-dimensional cohomology must occur after the ordered product and source pairing. The trace-zero subspace is not a left ideal: a later matrix can give a nonzero trace when multiplied by a traceless one. Accordingly the star product and pointing in (6.1), not only the individual trace classes, remain part of the whole actual A-object. This is precisely the source information that a bare scalar norm equation would omit. ## 7. What this supplies to the global torsor problem The actual normalized finite cut now has a fixed algebraic domain, a marked compact cycle, an exact product calculus, a global rational cohomology identity, and explicit two-wall functions. Every weighted finite word and its Green-current insertions can be carried through this same construction. The original invariant is their same selected period. This is a concrete whole-function source model for the torsor program, with no change of invariant or root normalization. There is still a substantive globalization to prove. The internal geometric Gaussian sector has not been shown to define a global cohomology component of these actual forms with a controlled coefficient. Its critical framing family can degenerate or escape at the compactified poles. A local nonzero Gaussian and (5.2) do not prove that its internal cycle is selected or that its boundary contributions vanish. Nor does the algebraic identity (3.3) bound tau(A): arbitrary scalar matrices already give arbitrary periods. The next source-preserving comparison must commute with the exact product and current maps, and account for these possible critical boundary terms. The existing [Rivin optimizer](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) supplies its algebraic geometric place and strict concavity, not this global cycle comparison. The general volume conjecture remains unproved. [Universal exact checks](../experiments/audit_compact_coherent_source.py) and [results](../experiments/compact_coherent_source_results.json) verify the centered star product, global primitive commutators, compact beta trace, and both off-root walls at N=2,...,9. They also check the physical Gauss brackets and form, the retained clock star power, and the removable clock germ. The formulas above are the uniform proofs; these tests do not establish a selected volume estimate. Eight fixed-rank actual-operator tests additionally retain a nonzero traceless apparent root pole in the left source frame and remove it in the source-preserving right frame. The [independent audit](compact_coherent_source_independent_audit.md) checks the whole product, global cohomology, bounds, and direct actual-A period normalization.

title: The exponential framing detour and its exact compact-source current
text: # The exponential framing detour and its exact compact-source current Research proof, 27 October 2026. The natural exponential homotopy does not patch in the fixed complete-meridian framing space. Its precise Cech defect is a nonzero affine-cotangent cocycle. Allowing the meridian eigenvalue to vary absorbs that defect and produces a global whole-function detour. The induced compact-source current has an explicit primitive for every actual finite matrix, including all weighted Green-current matrices. Its meridian-normal poles are exact and its finite part retains the original trace. The detour changes the meridian and the physical clock. It is not an intertwiner of the actual quantum word or a proof of the geometric/source pushforward. The fixed-complete obstruction and the varying-meridian repair are kept separate below. ## 1. The fixed framing space and the failed exponential interpolation Use the actual compact-source charts V=1/v, a'=v-v^2 a, T=v a, T'=V a'=1-T, omega_0=dv wedge da, omega_I=-omega_0/(2pi*i). The resolved complete framing threefold has the additional normal coordinate eta'=-v^2 eta. Its actual principal full framing form is H=-dlog eta wedge omega_0/(1-eta v). (1) The nonzero constant `c=2pi*i` is fixed. The physical graph is eta_phys=(1-exp(-c T))/v, eta'_phys=(exp(c T')-1)/V. (2) The equality of these expressions uses `exp(c)=1`. The apparent divisions by v or V are removable at their respective compact poles. These are the explicit actual meridian/source formulas proved in [the framing bridge](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md). On the first chart consider the nonvanishing-denominator path eta_lambda=(1-exp(-c lambda T))/v, 1-eta_lambda v=exp(-c lambda T). (3) The transition forced by the fixed threefold is eta'_lambda =[exp(-c lambda)exp(c lambda T')-1]/V. (4) For nonintegral real lambda, (4) has a genuine pole at V=0. The tempting regular second-chart expression `[exp(c lambda T')-1]/V` differs by [exp(-c lambda)-1]exp(c lambda T')/V. (5) Thus (3) supplies a whole path only on the punctured source chart. It does not define a homotopy of the whole fixed compact source into the complement of the additional divisor `1-eta v=0`. This is also an elementary fixed-base relative obstruction. On the real compact sphere let T run from zero to one along a fixed angular meridian. Any continuous section with finite pole-chart coordinates has `1-eta v=1` at both endpoints. If it avoids zero, this function is a based loop in C^*. Its winding is zero for the zero section and -1 for (2). A homotopy through such sections cannot change that integer. This argument concerns sections with their two pole fibers retained. The stronger fixed-space tube statement is developed independently in the resolved-relative-cycle calculation; no conclusion about unrestricted deformations of cycles is needed here. The actual fixed-space tube and the generic-meridian source-wall charges are computed in [the meridian homotopy wall theorem](meridian_homotopy_wall_and_source_residues.md). ## 2. The Cech defect is absorbed by changing the conjugacy class Put h_lambda=exp(-c lambda), u_lambda=exp(-c lambda T), k_lambda=1-h_lambda. Define the whole matrix mu_lambda= [u_lambda, (1-u_lambda)/v; v(u_lambda-h_lambda), 1+h_lambda-u_lambda]. (6) It has determinant h_lambda and fixes the retained eigenflag `[1:v]` with eigenvalue one. The other eigenvalue is h_lambda. On the second chart `u_lambda=h_lambda exp(c lambda T')`; therefore its potentially bad lower entry is exactly h_lambda[exp(c lambda T')-1]/V, which is removable. Formula (6) is a global holomorphic matrix on the entire compact-source surface for every lambda. It equals I at lambda=0 and the physical complete meridian at lambda=1. Its 11 entry never vanishes on the real homotopy, including its two endpoints in each compact fiber. Write its upper off-diagonal coordinate as eta_N and its lower off-diagonal coordinate as eta_S. Their exact transition is eta_S=k_lambda v-v^2 eta_N. (7) For k_lambda!=0 this is the affine cotangent torsor with class k_lambda. Its class is nonzero: a correction by functions regular on the two affine base charts would have to express v, after division by v^2, as Laurent powers >=0 and <=-2. The missing v^(-1) coefficient prevents this. At lambda=0,1 the affine translation vanishes and (7) returns to the nilpotent line bundle. Thus the repair is a family of conjugacy classes, not a missing regular correction to (4) inside the fixed space. The inverse-cut-eigenflag convention of the actual knot model fixes the SL2 lift as M_lambda=exp(-c lambda/2), h_lambda=M_lambda^2, mu_tilde_lambda=M_lambda^(-1)mu_lambda, p=1/v, s=(u_lambda-h_lambda)/M_lambda. Then (6) is exactly the existing generic-meridian Gauss matrix mu_tilde_lambda= [M+s, -(M-M^(-1)+s)p; s/p, M^(-1)-s]. (8) The actual cut coordinate is consequently A_cut=M/(M+s)=h_lambda/u_lambda. (9) At lambda=1 it returns `exp(c T)`. The SL2 endpoint is the recorded M=-1 sign, whereas its projective meridian is the desired complete meridian. The full kappa term, modified dimension, pivot and other source factors cannot be replaced by their M=1 values in the interior. No analytic continuation of a knot's geometric A-branch along this eigenvalue path has been proved by (6). ## 3. A global whole-function map of the actual compact source When k_lambda!=0 set a_lambda=(1-exp(-c lambda v a))/(k_lambda v), Phi_lambda(v,a)=(v,a_lambda). (10) Equation (7) divided by k_lambda says exactly a'_lambda=v-v^2 a_lambda. Hence Phi_lambda is a global holomorphic endomorphism of the actual compact-source surface, not merely its meridian chart. It extends at lambda=0 with `Phi_0=id`. For 0<lambda<1 its fiber derivative is J_lambda=partial_a a_lambda =c lambda exp(-c lambda T)/k_lambda !=0. (11) No properness or global injectivity follows from (11). The whole exponential functions, with their marked branches, are retained rather than replaced by their jets. There is an exact global primitive Phi_lambda^*omega_0-omega_0=d B_lambda, B_lambda=-(a_lambda-a)dv. (12) Indeed differentiation gives (11) minus one. On the second chart both `a'_lambda-a'` and dV acquire their inverse factors, so B_lambda patches without a Cech remainder. In particular integral_Gamma Phi_lambda^*omega_I=1. (13) Directly on the compact cycle this is the elementary identity integral_0^1 J_lambda(T)dT=1. This supplies an exact compact cohomology/current deformation; there is no free period normalization in it. ## 4. The current formula applies to every actual finite word Let C be any actual finite N-by-N matrix, including the completed weighted word or one of its Green-current matrices. Put n=N-1. Its actual coherent scalar symbol is the regular function f_C(v,a)=sum_(i,j=0)^n C_ij binom(n,j) v^i a^j(1-va)^(n-j). (14) The source form is `alpha_C=f_C omega_0`. Define the explicit current B_(C,lambda) =-[integral_(a)^(a_lambda) f_C(v,b) db]dv. (15) The integral in (15) is finite polynomial antiderivation in b; it does not use the value of the trace or the knot period. The coordinate transformation of the scalar f_C and of `db dv` proves that (15) is a global holomorphic one-form on X. Direct differentiation proves the strict current identity Phi_lambda^*alpha_C-alpha_C=d B_(C,lambda). (16) Thus the original finite source is preserved exactly: integral_Gamma Phi_lambda^*(f_C omega_I)=Tr(C)/N. (17) For a separate verification, all off-diagonal terms of (14) have angular weight i-j and integrate to zero. A diagonal term reduces under `t_lambda=v a_lambda` to polynomial antiderivation along the complex path from t_lambda=0 to t_lambda=1: binom(n,j)integral_0^1 t_lambda^j (1-t_lambda)^(n-j)dt_lambda=1/N. Whole-word products and every original head projector are formed before (14)--(16). Pullback is not used as a replacement matrix product. Since Phi_lambda is independent of crossing couplings, all coupling Euler operators and the explicit Green moment operators commute with this current map. In particular the full weighted source identity and both remaining framing Green currents retain their literal matrix coefficients and endpoints. This gives an actual compact-current deformation of those specified sources. It has not identified their image with the internal geometric Gaussian current. ### 4.1 The actual polar-fiber support complex is preserved This map retains more than the absolute compact period. Let `L_infinity` be the actual deleted polar fiber `v=infinity`, and `U=X minus L_infinity`, with its affine coordinates (v,a). The source support complex proved in [the compact localization theorem](compact_source_localization_boundary.md) is C_(L,alg)^k=Omega_alg^k(X) direct_sum Omega_alg^(k-1)(U), D(alpha,beta)=(d alpha,alpha|_U-d beta). (17a) Here the exponential detour requires the specified extension C_(L,hol)^k=Gamma(X_an,Omega_hol^k) direct_sum Gamma(U_an,Omega_hol^(k-1)). The original algebraic source complex maps to this holomorphic complex by inclusion. All subsequent current maps and finite parts in this note take values in this holomorphic complex; they are not asserted to remain algebraic. Equivalently one can use its explicitly generated whole exponential-period subcomplex, including the stated primitives. Phi_lambda fixes the base v. It therefore preserves L_infinity and U and defines a strict pullback chain map on C_(L,hol), and hence from the actual algebraic source into this extension. This retains the actual polar-fiber co-source rather than replacing it by an unspecified integration functional. For an explicit homotopy, the affine-fiber interpolation H_tau(v,a)=(v,a+tau(a_lambda-a)) is global: the difference of two fiber coordinates transforms linearly. It preserves U as well. Its Cartan homotopy operator on one-forms and two-forms is K_lambda beta=integral_(a)^(a_lambda) beta_a(v,b) db, K_lambda(f omega_0)=-[integral_(a)^(a_lambda)f(v,b)db]dv. It satisfies `Phi_lambda^*-id=d K_lambda+K_lambda d` directly by differentiation, or by integrating the derivative in tau. In particular `K_lambda alpha_C=B_(C,lambda)`. Take the actual primitive beta_C on U with d beta_C=alpha_C; it is obtained without using its trace by polynomial integration in the v coordinate, as in the localization theorem. The complete source pair has the exact relative identity Phi_lambda^*(alpha_C,beta_C)-(alpha_C,beta_C) =D(B_(C,lambda),-K_lambda beta_C). (17b) Indeed its second component is `B_(C,lambda)+d K_lambda beta_C`, precisely the homotopy formula for beta_C. This fixes the endpoint sign in (17b). The source residue and all co-source endpoint data survive this specified relative chain map. Every coupling derivative commutes with both K_lambda and (17b). Thus (17b) applies coefficientwise to every literal finite Green-current matrix formed from the whole weighted word. It does not replace those matrices by a scalar before composing the word. Commutation with an internal formal Gaussian pushforward has not been proved here. ## 5. Exact finite-part regularization at the complete resonance Near lambda=1 use the marked normal `k=1-exp(-c lambda)` and the local branch lambda=1-Log(1-k)/c. Put `u=exp(-c T)` and `eta_phys=(1-u)/v`. Then the whole map has a_lambda=eta_phys/k+a u+O(k), J_lambda=c u/k+u(1-c T)+O(k). (18) For the identity matrix, (12) gives the explicit pole and finite part Phi_lambda^*omega_0 =(c u/k)omega_0+u(1-c T)omega_0+O(k), (c u)omega_0=d[-eta_phys dv], u(1-c T)omega_0-omega_0=d[a(1-u)dv]. (19) Thus the pole is exact and the finite-part compact period is one. In particular discarding only the pole coefficient preserves the selected source; discarding the entire current would not. More generally (14) has degree at most n in a. Therefore (15) and (16) have poles of order at most n+1=N in k, with a finite principal part. Comparing Laurent coefficients in (16) gives every negative coefficient=d(explicit coefficient of B), finite_part(Phi_lambda^*alpha_C) =alpha_C+d finite_part(B_(C,lambda)). (20) For the original relative primitive beta_C its a-degree is at most n, so K_lambda beta_C has the same pole bound N. Comparing Laurent coefficients in (17b) therefore strengthens (20): every negative coefficient is exact in the stated holomorphic support complex, and the finite part represents the identical selected relative source class after holomorphic comparison. These coefficients can contain exp(-c T) and are not generally algebraic forms. In particular all negative coefficients have zero compact period, while the finite part retains `Tr(C)/N` with the original 1/N. No inversion of that trace or nonvanishing assumption is used. The same statement holds coefficientwise for all actual coupling moments. The bound N is color dependent; it is not a color-uniform bound on the uncontracted word or on unknown geometric Gaussian loops. Here lambda is auxiliary and the coefficients of C are fixed, or regular in this source normal. If the actual meridian is coupled to M_lambda, poles of the full modified dimension and other coefficient factors must be added separately. They are not removed by the fiber current (15). ## 6. The remaining quantum/source comparison is explicit The preceding current construction is a genuine global compact source map, but it is not the full sought geometric map. At an image point its ordinary physical coherent clock would be `exp(c v a_lambda)`. The Gauss detour (6)--(9), instead, has A_cut=h_lambda/u_lambda. These are different whole functions. Pullback by Phi_lambda is not asserted to preserve the finite star product or to implement the actual quantum-group dressing. The generic-meridian word also contains the complete nonzero vacuum and source factors, which must be transported rather than omitted. Consequently (16)--(20) preserve all actual source currents as compact currents, and (6)--(9) give a global noncrossing classical matrix detour, but their compatibility with the actual whole R/base transport still requires a source-preserving map. Simply equating the two clocks would skip that missing step. Coupling lambda to the meridian likewise requires the appropriate chain rule for meridian shifts; it is not implied by their commutation when lambda is an independent auxiliary parameter. The fixed-space defect (4)--(5) and the varying-class torsor (7) supply exact data for that comparison. They do not remove the fixed-complete wall tube by a Weyl relabeling. Nor do they prove geometric-branch continuation, all-loop logarithmic extension, selected geometric source survival, or a volume limit. ## 7. Exact audit [audit_compact_exponential_cech_current.py](../experiments/audit_compact_exponential_cech_current.py) and its [results](../experiments/compact_exponential_cech_current_results.json) verify the determinant, retained eigenflag, inverse-flag meridian normalization, affine transition, whole exponential source gluing, and normal pole/finite-part coefficients. For every matrix unit at sizes 2 through 5 they also verify (16), global one-form gluing, both components and the sign of the actual relative support identity (17b), the stated pole bound, and the normalized polynomial trace endpoint. The proof applies to arbitrary N; these are convention and algebra checks, not finite-level evidence for topology or geometric period selection.

title: The actual framing, its compact-source logarithmic section, and its boundary residue
text: # The actual framing, its compact-source logarithmic section, and its boundary residue Research proof, 27 October 2026. This computes the missing common momentum gauge between the actual critical framing and the compact coherent source. The physical meridian map resolves holomorphically at both compact poles after retaining its eigenflag. The full irreducible knot family nevertheless cannot extend there as regular matrices. An explicit associated-frame Jacobian gives a nonzero principal Gaussian boundary residue on the actual compact source. These are complete-parabolic statements, with the original base and half-density lines retained. No extension of higher Gaussian loops, selected-cycle equality, or volume limit is inferred. ## 1. Common momentum is an exact diagonal gauge In the actual finite head let S_c e_a=c^(-a)e_a. Then exactly `S_c Ecal S_c^(-1)=c Ecal`, `S_c F S_c^(-1)=c^(-1)F`, and K is unchanged. A common scaling on all strands is a Hopf automorphism. Every weighted crossing preserves the integer total index, hence commutes with `S_c^(tensor b)`. Its closed diagonal cut has the same property. For the actual compact coherent kernel, direct substitution gives sigma_(S_c C S_c^(-1))(w,z)=sigma_C(w/c,c z). Thus the exact diagonal gauge preserves t_c=wz/(1+wz), and scales the physical momentum `p=1/w` by c. For unit c it preserves the compact real source cycle; its angle is the exact common diagonal gauge angle. In particular the compact angular coordinate does not automatically replace the internal geometric centralizer coordinate. The actual critical model has inverse cut flag `p_1=1`. Write its framing, at M=1, as F(r,s)=[r,1-r;s,-s], s!=0, mu_s=F^(-1)[1,1;0,1]F=[1+s,-s;s,1-s]. Adding the common momentum gives the genuine third framing coordinate D_p=diag(p,1), Ftilde=F D_p^(-1), mu(A,p)=D_p mu_s D_p^(-1) =[1+s,-sp;s/p,1-s], A=(1+s)^(-1). (1) The SL2 lift uses the marked square root of p; the displayed conjugation is projective and changes no gauge-invariant shape. For generic M the identical construction uses the already proved `F_M(r,s)` and `A=M/(M+s)`. The complete-pole conclusions below are restricted to M=1, where the actual kappa vacuum term vanishes. The physical compact-source coordinates of (1) are explicitly t_c=Log A/(2pi*i), w=1/p, z=p t_c/(1-t_c). (2) They forget r. On the original `p_1=1` framing, their image has `w=1` and rank one. Therefore there is no meridian- and momentum-preserving identification of the two original internal framing coordinates with the whole compact source. The common momentum gauge must first be restored, and the remaining centralizer direction must be treated separately. ## 2. An explicit Springer map at both compact poles Use the compact-source chart v=w, a=z/(1+wz), t_c=v a, and put `c_0=2pi*i`. The physical meridian minus identity is mu-I=eta_S[-v,1;-v^2,v], eta_S=(1-exp(-c_0 v a))/v. (3) Its eigenflag is `(1,v)`. Division by v is removable: the right side is an entire function of v,a. Moreover partial_a eta_S=c_0 exp(-c_0 v a)!=0. Thus this is an explicit holomorphic local isomorphism to the resolved parabolic Gauss chart, rather than a claim obtained by equating symplectic forms. On the second compact chart set v'=1/v, a'=v-v^2 a, t_c'=v'a'=1-t_c. Then eta_S'=-v^2 eta_S =(exp(c_0 v'a')-1)/v'. (4) This extends at `v'=0` with derivative `c_0` in `a'`. Equations (3)--(4) are precisely the two Springer/eigenflag transition formulas. At the south compact pole `(w,z)=(0,0)`, one has `eta_S=c_0 z+...`; at the north pole in `W=1/w,Z=1/z`, the corresponding normal is `c_0 Z+...`. Both meridians become identity, but their limiting eigenflags are retained. The marked inverse is rational/logarithmic: A=(1-eta_S v)^(-1), a=Log A/(c_0 v). (5) It extends at v=0 by `a=eta_S/c_0`. Other logarithm sheets are not identified. This local isomorphism need not be a proper global covering; other logarithmic sheets can escape a chart. The resolved Gauss form can now be checked from the map itself: dLog A wedge dLog p =-d eta_S wedge dv/(1-eta_S v) =c_0 dv wedge da. (6) This recovers the physical compact-source form with its sign and normalization, including at the two pole charts. ## 3. The actual logarithmic centralizer section The PGL2 conjugator from the reference meridian to (1) is `G=Ftilde^(-1)`. In the Springer chart write g_N=[1,0;v,eta_S^(-1)], n(b)=[1,b;0,1]. Direct matrix multiplication shows that G is projectively `g_N n(b)` with v=1/p, eta_S=-s p, b=(1-r)/s. (7) The renormalized associated-frame coordinate is a_B=-eta_S b=p(1-r). Its opposite-chart transition is `a_B'=v-v^2 a_B`, exactly the compact-source transition. Its associated compact radial coordinate is `v a_B=1-r`. This is initially different from the physical coordinate `Log A/c_0` in (2). They agree on one explicitly determined logarithmic centralizer section: r_*(s)=1-Log A/c_0=1+Log(1+s)/c_0. (8) Any actual frame reaches this section by the original centralizer action `r->r+b s`, with b=(r_*(s)-r)/s. This is the explicit gauge/eigenflag transport; all developed cross-ratios and knot character functions stay constant. The common diagonal momentum p is a separate gauge from this centralizer normalization. On the physical compact path `A=exp(c_0 t_c)`, the section is `r_*=1-t_c`. It tends to r=1 at the south pole and r=0 at the north pole. After one marked A loop, Log A -> Log A+c_0, r_* -> r_*-1. The centralizer transition is consequently `b=-1/s`. Its primitive co-source changes by -(1/s)dLog A=ds/[s(1+s)]. (9) Its residue at s=0 is exactly +1, and at s=-1 it is -1. This is a nonzero boundary source forced by the actual logarithmic section, with its deck orientation specified. A finite algebraic cover cannot make the logarithm single valued: it multiplies, rather than removes, its nonzero residue. ## 4. The full irreducible knot family must escape the collapsed meridian Resolving one meridian does not regularize the entire knot representation. Normalize its meridian to `mu_0=[1,1;0,1]`. Irreducibility supplies a group word with rho(g)=[A_0,B_0;C_0,D_0], C_0!=0. Otherwise every group matrix would preserve the meridian's unique eigenline. Direct multiplication gives the conjugacy invariant Tr[mu_0,rho(g)]=2+C_0^2!=2. (10) If every conjugated group matrix extended regularly while the physical compact meridian tends to identity, this commutator would tend to identity and its trace to two, contradicting (10). Therefore some other holonomy necessarily has a pole. A single Springer flag cannot eliminate this full-family escape. The pole can be seen explicitly. On the r=1 section, the conjugate of the displayed group matrix is [A_0+B_0s, -B_0sp; (A_0-D_0+B_0s-C_0/s)/p, D_0-B_0s]. It has a south-pole term `-C_0/(s p)`. On the r=0 section the conjugate is [D_0+B_0s, p(A_0-D_0-B_0s+C_0/s); B_0s/p, A_0-B_0s], with north-pole term `C_0p/s`. Along the compact real cycle these are respectively of order `t_c^(-1/2)` and `(1-t_c)^(-1/2)`, with nonzero coefficients. These sections are the limits of the canonical logarithmic section (8). Projective developed flags may still have limits, but their coincidences and normal directions require more data than an ordinary regular matrix representation at the pole. ## 5.
