The principal Gaussian has an exact compact boundary residue Retain the actual marked cut form and covector Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], lambda_flag=dLog p. The normalization of the covector is fixed by the exact diagonal gauge in Section 1: it takes value one on its common logarithmic momentum generator. It has not been selected by guessing a Haar volume. In the coordinates (7), direct differentiation gives d eta_S wedge dv wedge db =-dr wedge ds wedge dp/(s p). Consequently the exact full-form identity is Omega_cut wedge dLog p =A_cut d eta_S wedge dv wedge db =-(d eta_S/eta_S) wedge dv wedge da_B /(1-eta_S v). (11) The interior Haar adapter is `A_cut=(1+s)^(-1)`; it cannot be omitted away from the boundary. It is one at `eta_S=0`, so (11) has the canonical logarithmic residue Res_(eta_S=0)(Omega_cut wedge dLog p)=-dv wedge da_B. (12) With the actual compact trace form omega_I=-dv wedge da_B/(2pi*i), integral_Gamma omega_I=1, equation (12) is a nonzero global compact-source class. The algebraic associated-frame transition makes this statement independent of the two charts. The uniform Gaussian comparison gives, on its recorded square-root and base-line cover, Omega_(beta,0)=c_beta Omega_cut, c_beta^2=-T_beta/2, c_beta!=0. Here the common original base-only line is factored but retained; it tensors both sides back into their original normalization. Since c_beta is conjugation invariant, (11)--(12) imply (1/(2pi*i))Res_(eta_S=0) [Omega_(beta,0) wedge lambda_flag]=c_beta omega_I. (13) Thus the normalized **principal boundary form** has actual compact period c_beta, with the original half-density phase retained. This is a computed residue, not an assumption that the critical family has a proper interior limit. Real gauge-circle orientation and normal-residue orientation must be transported as specified; they are not reset by taking an absolute norm. ## 6. Exact scope The physical compact meridian map, the actual common-momentum gauge, the logarithmic centralizer section, and the principal boundary residue have now been computed from the actual frames. The original fixed-cut-flag two-dimensional torsor is not simply the compact coadjoint leaf: restoring momentum adds a third dimension, and the internal centralizer remains a separate fiber. The associated boundary and the physical section must be kept distinct. In the associated-frame threefold, `eta_S=0` is an independent divisor over the entire compact algebraic source X. On the physical logarithmic section, however, (3) imposes `eta_S=(1-exp(-2pi*i*v*a_B))/v`. At finite nonzero v, that section meets the divisor precisely where `v*a_B` is integral; at v=0 the removable formula instead requires `a_B=0`. On the real compact source with `0<=t_c<=1` these are its two endpoint poles. In particular the compact cycle in the residue divisor has not been proved to be the geometric pushforward of the original physical compact cycle. Equation (13) proves nonzero leading boundary cohomology. It does not show that every higher Gaussian coefficient has only the same logarithmic pole, that all developed-flag degenerations are resolved, or that the actual full Green currents map to this boundary class with no additional contribution. Equation (10) shows that full critical-family escape is a real issue, not a hypothetical warning. The global geometric pushforward preserving the compact current period, and the selected volume growth, remain unproved. ## 7. Audit and dependencies The exact symbolic checks in [audit_compact_framing_gauge_boundary.py](../experiments/audit_compact_framing_gauge_boundary.py) and its [results](../experiments/compact_framing_gauge_boundary_results.json) verify the finite coherent gauge at levels 2 through 5, the full frame conjugation and Jacobian, both physical Springer charts, the logarithmic residue, both unavoidable escape poles, and the principal Gaussian boundary-form coefficient. The displayed calculations are universal rational or entire-function identities; the finite levels only audit the coherent-coordinate convention. The principal determinant normalization is the one proved in [the uniform Gaussian comparison](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md), and the finite trace form and physical whole-clock limit are those in [the actual compact source](compact_coherent_source_period.md). The global associated-bundle construction and its normalization lines are developed separately in [the Springer boundary-source note](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md). The [independent joint audit](resolved_framing_boundary_independent_audit.md) also checks the logarithmic deck signs, pole escape and principal residue normalization.

title: The compact source generator is a polar-fibre boundary class
text: # The compact source generator is a polar-fibre boundary class Research proof, 27 October 2026. The fixed compact source has a precise localization obstruction: deleting just one polar fibre makes its selected two-form exact. A map through that absolute chart therefore kills the source generator. Its nonzero image must retain an explicit relative divisor class or the equivalent residue co-source. This is an obstruction in the actual compact source, not a manufactured alternative knot state. It also gives a direct algebraic residue formula for the normalized trace, including the fixed-order actual A-period. It does not prove that the geometric Gaussian pushforward preserves that residue. ## 1. One polar fibre leaves an affine plane Use the fixed surface of [the compact coherent theorem](compact_coherent_source_period.md). Normalize its Segre coordinates as \[ \begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&t\end{pmatrix},\qquad a+t=1,\quad bc=t(1-t). \] In the usual chart, \[ t=\frac{wz}{1+wz},\quad b=\frac{z}{1+wz},\quad c=\frac{w}{1+wz}. \] Thus \[ X=\{bc=t(1-t)\},\qquad \omega_0=\frac{dw\wedge dz}{(1+wz)^2}. \] Let \[ L_\infty=\{b=0,\ t=1\}\simeq\mathbb A^1_c. \] It is a smooth Cartier divisor: near it, \(t\) is a unit and \(t-1=-bc/t\). Geometrically it is the whole fibre \(w=\infty\) of the projection \(X\to\mathbb P^1_w\). Its complement is exactly an affine plane. The maps \[ U=X\setminus L_\infty\simeq\mathbb A^2_{w,b},\qquad t=wb,\quad c=w(1-wb) \tag{1} \] are inverse: \(w=t/b\) where \(b\ne0\), and \(w=c/(1-t)\) where \(t\ne1\). These two opens cover \(U\). On it, \[ \omega_0=dw\wedge db=d(w\,db). \tag{2} \] The selected class therefore restricts to zero in \(H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(U)\). Deleting both fibres \(t=0,1\) gives the still more familiar chart \[ X^\circ\simeq (\mathbb A^1\setminus\{0,1\})_t\times\mathbb G_{m,b}, \qquad c=t(1-t)/b, \] on which \[ \omega_0=dt\wedge d\log b=d(t\,d\log b). \tag{3} \] This chart has nontrivial absolute top cohomology, generated by \(d\log t\wedge d\log b\) and \(d\log(1-t)\wedge d\log b\); nevertheless the actual compact source class is zero there. A nonzero chart cohomology group alone is therefore not sufficient. These bases follow directly by Laurent expansion in \(b\) and partial fractions in \(t\): all nonzero \(b\)-weights and all rational terms except the two simple logarithmic poles have algebraic primitives. ## 2. The exact relative complex retaining the generator Define the divisor-support complex directly by \[ C^k_{L_\infty}(X)= \Omega^k(X)\oplus\Omega^{k-1}(U),\qquad D(\alpha,\beta)=(d\alpha,\alpha|_U-d\beta). \tag{4} \] Its projection to \(\Omega^\bullet(X)\) is a chain map. The standard exact sequence of this explicit cone contains \[ H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(U)\longrightarrow H^2(C^\bullet_{L_\infty}(X))\longrightarrow H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(X)\longrightarrow H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(U). \] Both outer groups vanish because \(U=\mathbb A^2\). One elementary proof is polynomial radial contraction: a closed positive-degree homogeneous form has primitive obtained by contracting with the Euler field and dividing by its positive total degree. Consequently the middle projection is an isomorphism. The compact generator has the actual lift \[ (\omega_0,w\,db)\in C^2_{L_\infty}(X). \tag{5} \] It is a cycle by (2). At \(L_\infty\), its primitive is \[ w\,db=t\,\frac{db}{b}, \] whose residue is exactly one. Thus (5) supplies a concrete generator of the divisor-support line, not just its dimension. On the real compact sphere, \(b=\sqrt{t(1-t)}e^{-i\phi}\). For the cap \(0\le t\le1-\varepsilon\), Stokes gives \[ \int\omega_0=\int_{\partial}t\,d\log b =-2\pi i(1-\varepsilon). \] Taking the limit recovers the selected period \(-2\pi i\). The removed compact-cycle point is restored by a clockwise meridian of \(L_\infty\). This is the boundary datum lost by passing from \(X\) to the absolute affine chart. For an explicit two-fibre version, the deleted divisor has four components \(L_{0,b},L_{0,c},L_{1,b},L_{1,c}\). The residues of \(d\log t,d\log(1-t),d\log b\) are respectively \[ (1,1,0,0),\quad(0,0,1,1),\quad(1,0,1,0). \] The primitive \(t\,d\log b\) has residue vector \((0,0,1,0)\). It is not in the span of those three vectors. This records directly why the source boundary class remains nontrivial even though its top form becomes exact on \(X^\circ\). ## 3. A direct residue formula for every actual coherent trace Let the coherent matrix size be \(N=n+1\). In the affine coordinates (1), its symbol is the polynomial \[ f_A(b,w)= \sum_{i,j=0}^n A_{ij}\binom nj w^i b^j(1-wb)^{n-j}. \tag{6} \] Hence the normalized top form has a primitive on the affine chart which does not require its trace as input: \[ \beta_A= -\frac1{2\pi i} \left[\int_0^w f_A(b,s)\,ds\right]db,\qquad d\beta_A=\omega_A. \tag{7} \] The integral is ordinary polynomial antiderivation. Then the original compact trace is exactly \[ \frac{\operatorname{Tr}A}{N} =-2\pi i\,\operatorname{Res}_{L_\infty}\beta_A. \tag{8} \] Here is an algebraic verification. Near the divisor use \(b,c\) with \(t\) the root of \(t(1-t)=bc\) tending to one. Substitution \(w=t/b\) makes (7) a finite-pole Laurent one-form \(F(b,c)\,db\). Since its derivative is regular on \(X\), every negative Laurent coefficient of \(F\) is constant in \(c\). In particular its residue is constant along \(L_\infty\). For \(A=E_{ij}\), torus scaling \((b,w)\mapsto(\lambda b,\lambda^{-1}w)\) gives the form weight \(\lambda^{j-i}\). A constant residue can therefore be nonzero only if \(i=j\). In that case the residue is \[ -\frac1{2\pi i}\binom ni \sum_{k=0}^{n-i} \frac{(-1)^k\binom{n-i}k}{i+k+1} =-\frac1{2\pi iN}. \] The equality follows by integrating \(s^i(1-s)^{n-i}\) on \([0,1]\), or by repeated integration by parts. Linearity proves (8). Any other regular algebraic primitive on \(U\), equivalently a rational primitive on \(X\) with poles only on \(L_\infty\), has the same residue. Its difference from (7) is closed, hence exact on \(\mathbb A^2\); an exact rational differential has zero logarithmic residue. Allowing extra poles inside \(U\) would invalidate this assertion. For the fixed-order actual A-period of the compact theorem, apply (7) at companion matrix size \(r\), with \(R_N=v_0\ell H_N\). Its selected value becomes the concrete boundary period \[ C_N(q)=-2\pi i\, \operatorname{Res}_{L_\infty}(r\,\beta_{R_N(q)}). \tag{9} \] Its normal polar coefficients have zero residue because their traces vanish. Thus the existing pole removal preserves this specified boundary functional exactly, without a nonvanishing assumption. Formula (9) does not estimate the growing coefficient product \(H_N\). ### The entire finite boundary complex is explicit There is more than the residue formula. With \(J_-e_j=je_{j-1}\), the complete polar part of (7) is \[ \operatorname{PP}_{L_\infty}\beta_A =-\frac1{2\pi i} \sum_{k=0}^n\frac{n!}{(n+k+1)!} \operatorname{Tr}(J_-^kA)\, b^{-k-1}db. \tag{10} \] To prove this, the negative coefficients are constant along \(c\), as above, so evaluate them at \(c=0,t=1,w=1/b\). The \(E_{ij}\) contribution is \[ -\frac1{2\pi i}b^{j-i-1}\binom nj \int_0^1s^i(1-s)^{n-j}ds =-\frac1{2\pi i}b^{j-i-1} \frac{n!\,i!}{j!(n-j+i+1)!}. \] For a pole write \(i=j+k\); summing that lower subdiagonal gives precisely \(\operatorname{Tr}(J_-^kA)\), proving (10). The modes \(b^{-k-1}db\), \(k\ge1\), are exact in the punctured formal neighborhood: \[ b^{-k-1}db=d(-b^{-k}/k). \] Thus the finite normal-pole complex \[ \bigoplus_{k=1}^n F\,b^{-k} \xrightarrow{\,d\,} \bigoplus_{k=0}^n F\,b^{-k-1}db \] has exactly its one-dimensional residue cokernel over the coefficient field \(F\). In particular, for each actual one-cut diagonal array and every diagonal Green weight, all \(\operatorname{Tr}(J_-^kA)\), \(k>0\), vanish. Its primitive has only a logarithmic polar part even when the color size grows. For the fixed-order companion representation the number of polar modes is at most its fixed matrix size, independently of the color level. There is a stronger canonical statement for that companion source. Slide the actual source to its regular right representative \[ R_N^{\mathrm{right}}=H_Nv_0\ell,\qquad \ell=e_r^t. \] Since \(J_-\) lowers the index, \(\ell J_-^k=0\) for every \(k>0\). Thus \[ \operatorname{Tr}(J_-^kR_N^{\mathrm{right}})=0\ (k>0),\qquad \operatorname{PP}\beta_{R_N^{\mathrm{right}}} =-\frac{C_N(q)}{2\pi i\,r}\frac{db}{b}. \tag{11} \] The scaled actual A-form \(r\,\omega_{R_N^{\mathrm{right}}}\) therefore has exactly its one logarithmic boundary coefficient \(-C_N(q)/(2\pi i)\). This representative is also regular in the quantum normal. The exact source slide from \(R_N^{\mathrm{left}}=v_0\ell H_N\) removes both apparent quantum-normal poles and higher boundary-pole modes without normalizing by \(C_N\). This is a finite explicit boundary model of the selected source. It is a linear current/cohomology model, not an algebra quotient of the star product. Projection to these boundary moments before composing the whole word would discard matrix data needed by later factors. The source and exact star product remain until the final residue. ## 4. The precise obstruction to an absolute Gaussian comparison Suppose a proposed source-to-geometric map is a chain map on the whole compact de Rham complex and factors through restriction to \(\Omega^\bullet(U)\). Its induced map on the selected \(H^2\) generator is zero, by (2). The same is true if it factors through the two-polar-fibre chart (3). It cannot simultaneously send that class to a nonzero geometric period. There are two possible ways to avoid this obstruction: retain a map of the actual support/relative complex (4), including its residue co-source, or prove a different global continuation that does not discard the polar fibre. A local stationary Gaussian only gives neither assertion. In particular one cannot claim both that all affine total derivatives are killed and that their specific primitive (2) retains a nonzero absolute class. For an actual full-word form the primitive (7) can have growing degree. A local formal Gaussian may not be defined on its entire normal or asymptotic class. Proving that extension, or carrying the missing boundary instead, is part of the comparison theorem. This statement does not assume that the existing partial Gaussian already extends to every global rational primitive. The new concrete test is therefore whether the proposed geometric current map preserves the residue in (8)--(9). Exact currents coming from forms globally exact on \(X\) have zero such residue. The selected source generator has residue \(-1/(2\pi i)\), and must not be discarded with those currents. This is an explicit divisor-source condition for the actual source, beyond a choice of normalization at an interior saddle. ## 5. Global physical Gauss coordinates require their period torsor The local physical identity in the compact theorem is correct: \[ A=e^{2\pi it},\quad p=1/w=b/t,\qquad d\log A\wedge d\log p=2\pi i\,\omega_0. \] It does not define a global algebraic map to the Gauss torus. Already on a generic \(b=\text{constant}\) curve, an algebraic function \(A\) satisfying \(d\log A=2\pi i\,dt\) cannot exist on any finite algebraic cover. At a place over \(t=\infty\), the right side has pole order greater than one; a logarithmic derivative of an algebraic meromorphic function has only simple poles. The clock must remain a period of its exponential connection, with its marked logarithmic coordinate. Globally the analytic divisor \(A=1\) is also not just \(t=0,1\): it has every fibre \(t\in\mathbb Z\). The two endpoints describe the actual real compact cycle; replacing them by a global finite algebraic divisor silently changes that analytic map. Finally, a globally regular class-preserving map from \(X\) to a split framing surface with \(\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}=d(\tau\,d\log A)\) would make \(\omega_0\) exact, contradicting its compact period. The cotangent-torsor transition \[ w'=1/w,\qquad b'=w-w^2b,\qquad \lambda=-b\,dw,\quad\lambda'=\lambda+d\log w \] exhibits exactly the missing Chern twist. On the compact sphere \(\lambda\) is the \(O(1)\) Chern connection and \(c_1=-[\omega_0/(2\pi i)]\). A twisted affine framing object or the corresponding relative/logarithmic period data can retain this class; an unmarked split chart cannot. The physical half-form scale checks exactly in this convention. For \(\Omega_{\mathrm{phys}}=2\pi i\,\omega_0\) and \(h_N=2\pi i/N\), the curvature \(\Omega_{\mathrm{phys}}/h_N\) is \(N\omega_0\), the curvature of \(O(N)\) with connection \(N\lambda\). The holomorphic half-form is \(K_{\mathbb P^1}^{1/2}=O(-1)\), so the corrected section space is \[ H^0(\mathbb P^1,O(N)\otimes O(-1)) =H^0(\mathbb P^1,O(N-1)), \qquad \dim=N. \] This explains the exact shift in the coherent head calculus. It does not identify its source connection with the internal framing connection of the knot. Neither this Chern twist nor the boundary residue is already an identification with the knot's internal geometric framing bundle. The local coefficient map, its residues and the selected regulator action still have to be transported through the actual word.

title: Independent audit of the whole pointed companion source
text: # Independent audit of the whole pointed companion source 27 October 2026. The classification and polynomial comparison in [the pointed source theorem](pointed_companion_source_and_polynomial_hilbert90.md) hold over the stated commutative coefficient rings, including nonreduced bases. They require no quantum-gap division or imported multiplicative-quiver classification. The full actual word and selected regulator norm remain additional data. ## 1. Exact scheme classification in the source orbit basis The cyclic source basis e_j=Y^jv fixes v=e_0 and makes Y the companion with last column t_i. Its determinant is (-1)^(N-1)t_0. The identities ell v=1 and ell Y=ell give ell=(1,...,1) and sum_i t_i=1, without division. The multiplicative moment equation is equivalent to requiring that XY-QYX have image in the source line, with its row then uniquely determined by the two invertible matrices. Let Xv=v. In a nonzero-index row, for column j<N-1 the companion equation is X_(i,j+1)=Q[X_(i-1,j)+t_i X_(N-1,j)]. Induction on j gives X_(N-1,j)=0 there and X_(i,j)=Q^i x_(j-i) for i<=j, and zero for i>j. Only x_0=1 and the still undetermined zeroth-row coefficients occur. In the last column put m=N-i. Dividing by the UNIT Q^i gives exactly x_m=(1-Q^m)t_(N-m) +sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l. This recursively determines every x_m and proves the converse at the same time: all nonzero-index moment rows vanish. Thus det X=Q^(N(N-1)/2), and its inverse requires only powers of Q. Y inverse requires t_0 inverse, exactly the indicated principal open. The row w is unique. Its determinant character is wv=Q^-N-1, by det(I+v w)=1+w v, which follows directly from determinant multilinearity and also holds over rings with nilpotents. Every inverse map and classification step is over the stated coordinate ring, so this is an isomorphism of schemes, not merely a classification of field-valued points. The source chart is the principal open 1-sum_(i>0)t_i!=0 in affine (N-1)-space. With a chosen free ambient basis the representation chart is GL_N times that open: the source orbit basis gives the unique gauge, and its stabilizer is trivial. ## 2. The polynomial coboundary and its retained co-source Let chi(z)=z^N-sum t_i z^i and h(z)=z^N chi(1/z). Since sum t_i=1, ordinary monic division gives chi=(z-1)chi_red, h=(1-z)h_red, h_red=z^(N-1)chi_red(1/z), h_red(0)=1. The recurrence is precisely h(z)x(z)=h(Qz) modulo z^N, where x(z)=sum_(m<N)x_m z^m. On the finite lowering shift L, L^N=0 and B L B^-1=Q^-1 L. Thus G=h(L), G B=B h(QL)=X G. G is upper unipotent and its inverse is the finite nilpotent geometric series. This proves X=G B G^-1 over the WHOLE ring. No factors 1-Q^m or 1-Q^N are inverted, canceled or evaluated. The formula remains valid at Q=1; at that value it is a canonical choice from chi, not a uniqueness assertion for every clock conjugator. Since L v=0, Gv=G inverse v=v. Since ell(I-L)=e_0^t, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). Hence the source pairing identity ell C v=[e_0^t h_red(L)] [G inverse C G] v has the printed orientation. Trivializing the clock has not made the co-source constant. The new Y, actual crossing/cap/current matrices and source must ALL be conjugated. Parameter-dependent connections also carry the forced gauge term G inverse dG. No fixed original peripheral/dimension line is normalized away. ## 3. Whole mixed moments recover the retained polynomial For 0<=j<N, Y^jv=e_j, so the mixed moments are exactly m_j=ell X Y^jv=sum_(l=0)^j Q^(j-l)x_l, m_0=1, x_j=m_j-Q m_(j-1). The second identity is ordinary telescoping. On the head-unit localization, the already proved recurrence then recovers t_(N-m) successively, by dividing only by 1-Q^m. Thus these N-1 mixed source/clock moments determine the WHOLE polynomial, not merely a normal Taylor approximation. Ordered in the reverse tail variables (t_(N-1),...,t_1), their polynomial Jacobian is lower triangular with diagonal 1-Q^m. Its determinant is product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m)=N at primitive Q_N. The last equality follows by evaluating (z^N-1)/(z-1)=product_(m=1)^(N-1)(z-Q_N^m) at z=1. It is an exact root unit, not a bound for the global inverse map. At other Q, including Q=1, those moment coordinates can be singular although the companion chart and G remain regular. Pure Y moments do NOT recover this data: ell Y^jv=1 for all integer j, by the normalized output equation and invertibility of Y. On the actual section the mixed moments are Q^j, so the reconstruction gives the original cyclotomic chi=z^N-1. This does not identify chi with a knot A-polynomial or compute an actual closed-word scalar. ## 4. The actual section and the remaining period On the source orbit chart, Y^N=I implies Y^Nv=v. Expanding this single equation in its basis forces t_0=1 and t_i=0 for i>0. Conversely those equations make Y the cyclic shift. This is valid over every supplied commutative base, not only at a root or in characteristic zero. Then chi=z^N-1, h=1-z^N, G=I, h_red=1+z+...+z^(N-1), w=(Q^-N-1)e_0^t. Thus the original finite source is a regular SECTION of the unfolding, while its two finite endpoint deletions remain the actual operators from the previous boundary theorem. This is not a change of the actual knot state to a deformed companion. The theorem determines a whole algebraic source chart and an exact comparison for any GIVEN full word. It does not determine that word's scalar closed period, identify chi_red with A_K, select a global geometric cycle, or give a growing-N norm bound for G. Its retained co-source polynomial is precisely why clock conjugacy alone is insufficient. [The exact independent script](../experiments/audit_companion_source_shell.py) and [saved results](../experiments/companion_source_shell_results.json) pass symbolic N=2,...,7 checks of every lower moment row, characteristic/pointing factor, determinant, polynomial coboundary, co-source, mixed-moment inverse/Jacobian and original section. Twelve additional primitive/generic finite-field fibers check the FULL multiplicative moment row and its determinant character, not only the linearized relation.

title: Complete-color divided Ward operators and the exact fusion ghost
text: # Complete-color divided Ward operators and the exact fusion ghost Research theorem, 27 October 2026. At the complete integral color, the first normal of a vanishing N-th quantum power gives a nonzero divided Ward action. Its tensor fusion correction is one finite unipotent exponential, with nilpotence bounded by strand number. Ordinary closure kills this correction. A specified one-wrap, relative cut-current test can detect it, but no identification of that test with the selected global geometric class is asserted. All formulas below are proved from finite matrices. In particular no extension of a generic typical meridian color to a divided-power quantum group is presumed. ## 1. The genuine complete integral color Fix N>=2 and m=N-1. Initially q is generic, Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1). On the ordinary integral Weyl color D_m(q) use the divided-F basis v_a=F^(a)v_0, 0<=a<=m. Its literal matrices are K v_a=q^(m-2a)v_a, E v_a=[m-a+1]_q v_(a-1), F v_a=[a+1]_q v_(a+1), (1.1) with arrows outside the range absent. For r>=0, E^(r)v_a={m-a+r choose r}_q v_(a-r), F^(r)v_a={a+r choose r}_q v_(a+r), (1.2) when the target exists, and zero otherwise. Braces denote symmetric Gaussian polynomials. Formula (1.2) follows by multiplying adjacent entries and dividing by [r]_q! over the generic field; its resulting Gaussian polynomial is integral. Thus E^(N)=F^(N)=0 on each color identically in q. The finite generic-q R matrix of this actual color is R_uncheck=D sum_(r=0)^m q^(r(r-1)/2) rho^r E^r tensor F^r/[r]_q!, D=q^(H tensor H/2). (1.3) It is regular near every prescribed q_N=exp(pi*i/N). Indeed its r-th nilpotent coefficient can also be written q^(r(r-1)/2)rho^r[r]_q! E^(r) tensor F^(r). The recorded Cartan half-character remains on its chosen cover. For completeness, its E intertwining does not need a literature proof. From the matrices one gets [E,F^r]=[r]_q F^{r-1} (q^(1-r)K-q^(r-1)K^(-1))/rho. Likewise [E^r,F]=[r]_q E^{r-1} (q^(r-1)K-q^(1-r)K^(-1))/rho; these are ordinary powers in both commutator formulas and follow by induction from the generator matrices. Conjugating by D reduces the R intertwining equation to the recursion c_(r+1)=c_r q^r rho/[r+1]_q for the coefficients of E^r tensor F^r. This is exactly (1.3). The last unmatched term has E^(m+1)=0. Consequently checked R commutes with Delta E and Delta K. The F calculation uses the second displayed commutator and the same coefficient recursion. It also commutes with the iterated total actions on any tensor power. Inverses have the same property. All identities are generic q matrix identities before root specialization. ## 2. The tensor divided-power formula, including its order On b tensor factors put C_E=Delta^(b-1)E=sum_(i=1)^b A_i, A_i=E_i K_(i+1)...K_b. For i<j one has A_i A_j=Q A_j A_i. The ordinary q-multinomial formula, proved by multiplying one additional factor, therefore gives the following integral matrix formula: C_E^n/[n]_q! =sum_(n_1+...+n_b=n) q^(sum_(i<j)n_i n_j) tensor_i [E_i^(n_i)K_i^(n_1+...+n_(i-1))]. (2.1) Terms with n_i>N-1 are zero. The order E^(n_i) before K powers is part of the formula. On two factors this reads Delta E^(n)=sum_(r=0)^n q^(r(n-r)) E^(r) tensor E^(n-r)K^r. (2.2) Thus the tensor divided power is regular at q_N even when [n]_q! vanishes. For b>=2 it is nonzero at n=N. For example on v_(N-1) tensor v_1 only the r=N-1 term of (2.2) survives; its output v_0 tensor v_0 has nonzero coefficient. Every actual braid word commutes with (2.1): this holds generically by commutation with C_E, and extends through the root because both matrices are regular. This is a genuine complete-color root Ward action invisible in the equality C_E(q_N)^N=0. ## 3. Exact first-normal normalization and the scaled matrix Set Ecal=rho^2 E, C=rho^2 C_E. The polynomial matrix D_n(q)=C(q)^n/(Q;Q)_n is regular near q_N for every n. Formula (2.1) proves this because D_n=rho^(2n)q^(-n(n-1)/2)(1-Q)^(-n) C_E^n/[n]_q!. The entire divided matrix C_E^n/[n]_q! is interpreted by (2.1). No zero factorial is separately evaluated. In particular define J_b=[C(q)^N/(1-Q^N)]_(q=q_N). Since (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N at the root, D_N(q_N)=J_b/N. (3.1) The corresponding unscaled conversion is [C_E^N/(1-Q^N)]root =q_N^(-N(N-1)/2)N/(1-Q_N)^N *[C_E^N/[N]_q!]root. (3.2) For Q=Q_N(1+epsilon), along the complete integral color, C(Q)^N=-N epsilon J_b+O(epsilon^2). (3.3) For q=q_N(1+h) the coefficient is -2N h J_b instead. These are specified normalizations, not unnamed scalar multiples. In the balanced basis used by the actual cut, at the root Ecal_(a,a+1)=Q_N^(-a-1)-1, K_aa=x Q_N^(-a), x=q_N^(N-1). The unique mixed term on w_(N-1) tensor w_1 gives the useful normalization check J_2(w_(N-1) tensor w_1)=-N q_N w_0 tensor w_0. (3.4) It is nonzero at every level, including even and composite N. ## 4. The general-b fusion correction is one finite exponential For any argument z define the positive-argument finite polynomial f_N(zX)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) z^r X^r/(Q_N;Q_N)_r. The actual negative factorial convention is obtained by z=-t. Order the tensor factors as f_N(zA_b)...f_N(zA_1). The finite q-multinomial identity before specializing gives exactly product_(i=b,...,1) f_N(zA_i) =sum_(n=0)^(b(N-1)) z^n D_n(q_N). (4.1) One way to see regularity on its right is its identical generic-q ordered product on the left: each A_i^N=0 identically. For 0<=r<N, Gaussian multiplication gives D_(kN) D_r={kN+r choose r}_Q D_(kN+r). The scalar Gaussian tends to one, directly from its r product factors. Thus D_(kN+r)=D_(kN)D_r at the root. Also D_N^k=k! D_(kN), (4.2) because {kN choose N}_Q tends to k: all nonmultiple product ratios tend to one, and the final ratio (1-Q^(kN))/(1-Q^N) tends to k. Equivalently (Q;Q)_(kN)/(1-Q^N)^k tends to N^k k!. Combining these exact identities gives the full factorization product_(i=b,...,1) f_N(zA_i) =exp(z^N J_b/N) f_N(zC). (4.3) The exponential is finite. For the literal negative series this is exp((-t)^N J_b/N), so an odd-N sign is not suppressed. Let position mean the ordinary integer sum a_1+...+a_b. Then J_b lowers position by exactly N. Hence J_b^b=0, more precisely its nilpotence index is at most floor(b(N-1)/N)+1. The defect exp(z^N J_b/N)-I has only lowering degrees kN. Actual checked R preserves position exactly, so its conjugates preserve this bounded lowering filtration. The group generated using only such positive lowering defects is unipotent, independently of N for fixed b. No analogous claim for both raising directions is made. ## 5. Ordinary closure kills the ghost, while one normal wrap can pair Let P lower total position by at least N, and let R_left,R_right preserve total position. Weighted pivotal partial trace over all but one strand kills R_left P R_right. Every closed-strand input index equals its output index, so the remaining cut would have to lower its index by at least N; its index range has only N values. This is a term-by-term zero, independent of the diagonal pivotal weights. Thus every positive term of (4.3) is invisible to ordinary one-cut closure, including after actual braid transport. A single missing edge W=E_(N-1,0) raises position by N-1. A single such normal insertion can therefore leave a lowering-one cut current from J_b. All higher powers J_b^k, k>=2, are still killed by one-cut partial trace after one wrap. Pairing with a specified cut cochain that raises one can then have degree zero. This is a permission by degree, not a nonvanishing theorem for an arbitrary global source. There is a universal literal nonzero example. For b=2 let W_tot=W tensor K+I tensor W and take the actual pivotal trace over the second color. Then [ptr_2(J_2 W_tot)]_(0,1)=delta N x^(2-N), delta=(-1)^(N-1), x=q_N^(N-1). (5.1) Only the closed input index zero with its second-leg wrap contributes. The coefficient follows from the unique mixed divided term. It is nonzero for every N. An even simpler formulation uses the true divided Hopf adjoint, which is described next. Both are local normal-cochain tests, not identification with the selected global relative class. ## 6. The true divided Hopf-adjoint Ward action and its SL2 block On End(D_m(q)) put A_E(X)=ad_Ecal(X)=[Ecal,X]K^(-1), A_F(X)=ad_F(X)=F X-K^(-1)X K F. These are generic-q Hopf actions on matrices. The correct divided operators are J_E^ad=[A_E^N/(1-Q^N)]root, J_F^ad=[A_F^N/(1-Q^N)]root. (6.1) They are not commutators with the individual divided matrix, which is zero. For example write A_E=U+V, U=L_Ecal R_(K^-1), V=-R_(Ecal K^-1). Then UV=Q VU and U^N=V^N=0 identically. The same divided-binomial calculation proves the regularity in (6.1). The F version uses the inverse parameter Q^(-1). Let W=E_(N-1,0) and U_0=sum_(a=0)^(N-2)E_(a,a+1). Directly from these mixed terms, in the actual balanced root basis, J_E^ad(W)=-N U_0, J_E^ad(U_0)=0, J_F^ad(U_0)=N W, J_F^ad(W)=0. (6.2) For the first equation, the term with r=N-1-a left E actions and s=a+1 right E actions is the only one contributing to E_(a,a+1). Root product cancellation gives coefficient -N for each a. Similarly J_F^ad(E_(a,a+1))=-N Q_N^(-a-1)W, whose sum gives N W. Thus the two-dimensional span of W,U_0 is invariant, and -J_E^ad/N,J_F^ad/N are opposite standard nilpotents generating SL2 on it. Both divided directions do not generate a nilpotent group. The bounded unipotence in Section 4 is specifically the one-direction relative defect. The actual E-Ward cut primitive B=E_(1,0)/(Q_N^(-1)-1) satisfies [Ecal,B]=E_(0,0)-E_(1,1), Tr(B J_E^ad(W))=-N/(Q_N^(-1)-1)!=0. (6.3) This is a specified nonzero pairing of a divided normal current, the actual missing edge, and a relative cut cochain. It does not prove that the original global selected source has this class. Ordinary pivotal partial trace with pivot K intertwines these divided Hopf adjoints before specializing: it intertwines A_E, A_F, their powers and scalar divisions, all by the actual Hopf cap identities. Regularity then gives the root divided map. At the complete root, the ADO pivot K^(1-N) differs on each individual color by the scalar delta, so it has the same root equivariance. This is the correct divided Ward naturality; replacing it by ad_(J_b) would lose the mixed terms just computed. ## 7. The two normal directions and the actual auxiliary family On the generic-M balanced auxiliary array the last raising formula before root specialization is w(Q,M)=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1) =(Y-Z)/(M Z), Y=M^2, Z=Q^N. (7.1) It equals kappa=M-M^(-1) only on the root wall Z=1. The genuine complete integral color is instead x=q^(N-1), M=-q^N, Y=Z, and (7.1) vanishes identically on that path. At the root crossing of the two walls, w=(Y-1)-(Z-1)+higher order. For Q=Q_N(1+epsilon), fixed Y gives dw=-N epsilon; the integral path has dlog Y=N epsilon and gives dw=0. Thus its normal derivative is partial_epsilon+N partial_(log Y), not the prior fixed-meridian q-normal derivative. The precise failure of the generic auxiliary matrices to be a genuine off-root Hopf module is visible without any deformation theory. With actual truncated matrices one computes [Ecal,F]-rho(K-K^(-1)) =-(1-Q^N) w(Q,M) E_(N-1,N-1). (7.2) It vanishes on either the root wall Z=1 or the complete integral color wall Y=Z. This keeps the coupled boundary source explicitly; it does not extend generic typical colors to the divided-power theory by assumption. The off-root boundary closure also has an adapter. On complete integral color the genuine ordinary pivot is K. The auxiliary ADO pivot is K^(1-N), with ratio K^(-N)v_a=q^(-Nm+2Na)v_a. At q_N it is delta I. Its q-logarithmic first derivative is the nonconstant diagonal N(2a-m), multiplied by delta. The ordinary and ADO twists have ratio q^(-Nm); this too must be differentiated if the closed q-normal sources are compared. For a zero-framed b-strand knot of writhe ell, the exact routewise adapter is q^[Nm(ell-b+1)+2N sum_(closed legs) a_j]. (7.3) It is one at the root by ell=b-1 modulo two, but its derivative contains the recorded closed-position moment. Therefore equality of root invariants does not identify their off-root source jets. ## 8. Scope The complete integral-color divided Ward action, finite fusion exponential, bounded positive lowering filtration, ordinary closure cancellation, and explicit relative normal tests are proved here. The true divided Hopf-adjoint diagram is also an exact actual matrix construction. The remaining source-survival theorem still requires a map from the partially contracted actual geometric current module to this marked relative cut module, preserving (7.1)--(7.3). The nonzero local tests (5.1), (6.3) do not supply that map or its global coefficient. No global cycle, Stokes, regulator norm, or volume limit is inferred. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_complete_color_divided_ward.py). [Results](../experiments/complete_color_divided_ward_results.json). [Independent divided-bridge audit](divided_ward_bridge_independent_audit.md). [Independent two-normal and pivotal-adapter audit](ward_source_localization_independent_audit.md).

title: Complex peripheral paths retain the absolute regulator bound
text: # Complex peripheral paths retain the absolute regulator bound 28 October 2026. Complex meridian excursions do not by themselves invalidate the representation-volume bound on a holomorphic action. There is an exact endpoint correction, which vanishes when BOTH meridian endpoints are unitary. Consequently a continuously lifted path of genuine representations, starting at regulator zero, has the desired geometric exponential upper bound even if it changes sheets at complex ramification points or winds logarithms. A bare spectral node is a different matter. This note proves that distinction; it does not identify the conversion paths of an actual quantum recurrence. ## 1. Fixed peripheral marking and the exact complex-path identity Use the actual preferred SL2 peripheral eigenvalues (M,ell) of [the longitude/action calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). Let beta be its absolutely marked fundamental Bloch chain and R=D(beta)=Vol(rho). The independently proved [general peripheral representation-volume bound](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) gives |R|<=V, where V is the hyperbolic manifold volume. On any regular representation curve, the actual boundary identity is delta beta=-2 M wedge ell. Write compatible continuously lifted logarithms as u=Log M=a+i theta, v=Log ell=b+i phi, y=Log Y=2u, Y=M^2. Here phi is an unwrapped longitude argument, not an independently reset principal argument. The Bloch--Wigner differential gives dR=2(b dtheta-a dphi). (1) Define the holomorphic action increment along a path gamma by A_gamma=integral_gamma v dy=2integral_gamma v du. (2) Direct real and imaginary differentiation gives Im(v dy)=2(b dtheta+phi da) =dR+2d(a phi). Thus the complete endpoint formula is Im A_gamma=R(end)-R(start) +2[log|M| Arg(ell)]_(start)^(end). (3) Equivalently, for the M-step action S_gamma=integral v du, Im S_gamma=(R(end)-R(start))/2+[log|M| Arg(ell)]_start^end. No integral along the complex excursion remains in the correction. These are the actual root-step constants. For h_Y=2pi i/N, (1/N)log|exp(A_gamma/h_Y)|=Im A_gamma/(2pi). (4) The M-step convention h_M=pi i/N gives exactly the same number using S_gamma. In particular the actual previously derived identity dS_flat=2v du and Im S_flat=R+2Re(u)Im(v) is precisely (3), with its absolute constant already fixed by the original Bloch chain. If both endpoints have |M|=1 and the initial regulator is zero, Im A_gamma=R(end), (1/N)log|exp(A_gamma/h_Y)|<=V/(2pi). (5) This holds for an arbitrary finite complex path of the stated type, not only a path staying on the meridian unit circle. Without the zero anchor, the bound from two absolute regulator values is 2V, not V. Without unit meridian endpoints the term in (3) must be retained. ## 2. Finite character covers and ramification There is a useful descent statement. Let pi:C->B be a connected finite cover of normalized peripheral curves on a regular algebraic open set. On C suppose the actual, single-valued regulator satisfies dR=pi^*eta, where eta is the differential (1) determined by M,ell. Then R descends to B. Proof. On the unramified open set, average R over the d points of each fiber. The average Rbar is globally defined there, since monodromy only permutes the summands, and dRbar=eta. Therefore R-pi^*Rbar is locally constant on C. Removing finitely many points from the connected normalization leaves it connected, so this difference is one constant c. Its fiber average is zero, hence c=0. Thus R=pi^*Rbar. This proof uses the absolute, single-valued R; it is not a choice of unrelated local action constants. For a map of irreducible algebraic character/peripheral curves, remove the finitely many branch and nonproper points to obtain the finite cover used here. Additional algebraic flag or shape choices may be included in C. The result does not assert finiteness for a positive-dimensional family mapping to one peripheral point. Different disconnected character components over the same B can still have different additive constants. A common independently proved zero anchor fixes those constants if its limits are controlled. At a point of B where M and ell are finite and nonzero, eta is smooth and closed, so its descended primitive extends across the finite excluded points. Its absolute volume bound extends by continuity. In particular, ordinary ramification of the meridian projection on the NORMALIZED curve creates no jump. In a local coordinate t, M=M_0+O(t^e), ell=ell_0+O(t), and v dy=2 Log(ell(t)) M'(t)/M(t) dt is holomorphic there. A path entering one meridian sheet and exiting another through this point is a continuous path on the normalization; its regulator and endpoint formula remain the same. Consequently (5) also applies on a genuinely identified normalized peripheral component with such a finite character/Bloch cover. A particular character lift need not return to itself after a loop; the regulator is nevertheless unchanged on the same peripheral fiber within this connected cover. ## 3. Loops, logarithmic marks, and different kinds of collision A closed path on the normalized lifted curve based at |M|=1 has zero imaginary action, even if u or v acquire integer 2pi i shifts. More generally a meridian loop ending on a different longitude sheet is NOT a closed path on that curve; its imaginary action is the regulator difference and still satisfies (5) from a zero anchor. Repeating such continuations cannot accumulate arbitrary positive growth, because their regulator increments telescope. Changing the initial longitude lift by 2pi i n changes A_gamma by 2pi i n(y_end-y_start). Its imaginary part is 2pi n log|Y_end/Y_start|, which vanishes for unit meridian endpoints. A longitude sign adds i pi(y_end-y_start) and likewise changes only the real action there. A fixed integral framing ell->M^w ell adds w(u_end^2-u_start^2), also real at unit meridian endpoints. These explicit phase changes must be retained in an exact quantum formula, but they create no exponential norm in (5). At a nonunit basepoint even a closed representation loop can have nonzero imaginary action on the logarithmic cover: if the longitude log winds by 2pi i n, (3) gives 4pi n log|M_base|. Thus a statement about all loops without the unit-endpoint qualification would be false. A node of a plane A-polynomial is not the same as ramification of its normalization. Its two branches can correspond to two DIFFERENT points of the normalization; they cannot be exchanged by declaring their identical (M,ell) values to be one point. They can also belong to different character components or represent different limiting characters. The normalization and the actual Bloch lift matter. A true common representation, or matching regulator limits, would make a passage regulator-continuous; equality of peripheral eigenvalues alone does not prove that condition. For a piecewise lifted path whose branches are spliced at nodes, choose matching longitude logs at each splice and write J_j=R_after-R_before. Applying (3) on each genuine piece gives Im A_total=R_final-R_initial-sum_j J_j +2[log|M| Arg(ell)]_initial^final. (6) Thus an unsupported node switch carries exactly the missing regulator jump. If the logs themselves are reset at a nonunit node, its extra 2log|M| times the argument jump must be included as well. Neither operation can be omitted by treating a spectral discriminant zero as a smooth character ramification point. ## 4. The Gaussian conversion has precisely such a node mismatch For [the independently proved analytic two-channel model](analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md), the eigenvalues are alpha(x)=exp(a(x-1/2)) and beta(x)=exp(-a(x-1/2)+i theta). Give both branches their calibrated natural primitives at x=0: sigma_1(x)=a(x^2-x)/2, sigma_2(x)=-a(x^2-x)/2+i theta x. Both complete marked actions have real part zero. Their logarithmic eigenvalues coincide at the complex point x_*=1/2+i theta/(2a). However their calibrated primitives do not agree there: sigma_2(x_*)-sigma_1(x_*) =a/4-theta^2/(4a)+i theta/2 =Gamma+i theta/2. (7) Following beta from 0 to x_* and then alpha to 1 has exactly this total action. It is precisely the exponent computed by the exact Gaussian conversion sum, including its phase. To compare constants with (2), set Y=exp(2pi i x), M=exp(pi i x) and A_i=2pi i sigma_i. At x_* the peripheral logs and hence the boundary term 2log|M| Arg(ell) agree on the two branches. Their artificial regulator lifts therefore differ by 2pi Gamma. The local spectral curve is the reducible nodal union (L-alpha(x))(L-beta(x))=0; its normalization keeps those branches separate. The conversion is not a continuation through a common smooth normalized point with one calibrated regulator. This explains exactly why the general analytic counterexample does not contradict the genuine geometric path bound. ## 5. Consequence for the actual upper-bound attack Representation geometry supplies a sharp bound for complex action paths with a genuine calibrated lift, unit meridian endpoints, and a zero regulator anchor. Finite covers, ordinary meridian ramification, and logarithmic winding do not defeat it. This is stronger than bounding only real meridian arcs. The unresolved quantum statement is specific: show that every exponentially relevant sourced conversion is represented by such a lifted path, or bound its additional node/connection jump by the corresponding calibrated action difference. The original annihilator's actual character components, its full source and its subprincipal couplings must enter that proof. No assertion that a generic analytic recurrence has this property is made here. Lower noncancellation remains separate. [Audit](../experiments/audit_complex_peripheral_action.py) checks the differential constants, the Gaussian collision mismatch, and complex Bloch-chart integrals with unit endpoints, nonunit endpoints, and logarithm-winding loops. These integrals test the identity, not the existence of a knot representation for an arbitrary one-shape chart.

title: A positive lens chart with its linear constraints retained
text: # A positive lens chart with its linear constraints retained 28 October 2026. Every supplied positive complete marked ideal triangulation admits a geometric reference chart in which ALL shape arguments lie in the closed lens |z|<=1, |1-z|<=1. No invertibility of the gluing block B is required. Its kernel is retained as exact linear constraints, rather than removed by changing some shapes to exterior arguments. On this constrained chart the complete fixed-radii reference chain has a unique volume maximum, a nonzero Gaussian coefficient, and a strict boundary gap. Every geometric atom lies inside the already proved coefficient-one finite-Euler region. This removes a classical polarization obstruction; it does not identify the original quantum cycle with this reference chain or select its logarithmic sheet. The [exact/Arb audit](../experiments/audit_constrained_lens_geometric_chart.py) and [results](../experiments/constrained_lens_geometric_chart_results.json) verify the supplied 8_1 geometry with its peripheral markings kept distinct, and six synthetic Lagrangian systems with every rank B=0,...,5. The synthetic systems check the linear construction; they are not asserted knot triangulations or a quantum source theorem. ## 1. Lens choices do not require an invertible B For a positive shape z, the Euclidean triangle with vertices 0,1,z has sides 1, |z|, |1-z|. Normalize one of its longest sides to one, preserving orientation. The three cyclic normalizations have shapes z, 1/(1-z), 1-1/z. At least one has both modulus and complementary modulus at most one. Choose it independently in each tetrahedron. All chosen shapes remain strictly in the upper half-plane. Their geometric arguments consequently belong to D_+ in the [full Euler-atom theorem](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md), including the cases of equal side lengths. On a compact family of nondegenerate positive shapes, the coefficient-one estimate is uniform after taking a finite collection of these lens charts. Use the resulting real rational marked gluing data A x+B y=c, x_j=Log z_j, y_j=Log(1-1/z_j), rank(A B)=t, AB^t=BA^t, c=i*c_R, c_R real. (1) The rotated affine signs and full peripheral mark are retained in c. Let rank B=r and k=t-r. Choose a real full-rank k-by-t matrix E whose rows span the left kernel of B. Put D=EA, d=Ec. Then rank D=k and the necessary projection equations are D x=d. (2) Indeed a row combination annihilating both A and B is zero by (1). Moreover ker B=image(D^t), (3) since BD^t=BA^t E^t=AB^t E^t=0 and both spaces have dimension k. Choose any purely imaginary solution (x_0,y_0) of (1). Such a choice exists by its full real row rank. Let L be a real t-by-r matrix with columns a basis of ker D. Solve B Y=-A L (4) for a real t-by-r matrix Y. The solution exists because EAL=DL=0. Set C=L^tY and l=L^t y_0. Then C is real symmetric and l is purely imaginary. Symmetry follows because the tangent vectors (L v,Y v) lie in the Lagrangian kernel of (A B). It is independent of the choice of Y, by (3) and L^t D^t=0. The ENTIRE affine gluing relation now reads x=x_0+L xi, y=y_0+Y xi+D^t lambda, (5) with unconstrained lambda. No inverse of B appears. There is no assertion that the coordinates xi, or the Fourier implementation of (2), already have the original quantum source. ## 2. A nondegenerate constrained potential with the original volume mark On the positive branches define F(x)=sum_j [Li_2(exp x_j)+x_j^2/2-i*pi*x_j], W_L(xi)=F(x_0+L xi)+xi^t C xi/2+l^t xi. (6) The additive constant in (6) is zero, hence real; no imaginary constant is chosen to fit a volume. Since F_x=-y_shape, its derivative is grad W_L=-L^t y_shape+C xi+l. (7) By (3), equation (7)=0 is equivalent to y_shape having the form in (5). Together with (2), these are exactly ALL the original equations (1), including their marked affine constants. On the positive chart, where each z_j=exp(x_j) lies in the upper half-plane, Im Hess W_L =L^t diag_j[Im(z_j)/|1-z_j|^2] L >0. (8) Thus the reduced Hessian is invertible, for every rank of B. If r=0 the statement is the zero-dimensional one with determinant one. No degeneracy is introduced by retaining (2). Let xi_*=rho_xi+i theta_xi be the complete solution, and write x_*=rho+i theta and y_*=sigma+i gamma. Because x_0 is purely imaginary, rho=L rho_xi. The Bloch identity gives Im F(x_*)=sum_j D(z_j)-rho^t gamma. The quadratic/linear terms in (6) have imaginary part rho_xi^t(C theta_xi+Im l). The imaginary part of (7)=0 makes this rho^t gamma. Therefore, with its stated marks, Im W_L(xi_*)=sum_j D(z_j)=Vol(M). (9) This argument uses the complete marked gluing solution and retains the constraints; it does not replace an unsaturated gluing scheme by all of its cleared boundary points. ## 3. A full constrained angular box with a strict gap Keep rho_xi fixed at its complete value. Then the allowed shape angles lie in the affine plane D theta=Im d. Define the reference polytope P={theta in [0,2*pi]^t : D theta=Im d}. (10) It has relative dimension r and the geometric angle point in its relative interior. Use theta=Im x_0+L theta_xi to parametrize it. This is a SPECIFIED lifted polytope. It is not automatically a fundamental domain of the corresponding torus: other integer logarithmic sheets and their source factors must not be identified with (10) without proof. Put r_j=|z_*j| and ell_j=log|1-z_*j|. Both r_j<=1 and ell_j<=0 by the lens choice. On the affine plane (10), direct expansion of (6) and the REAL part of (7) give Im W_L=sum_j f_j(theta_j)+constant, f_j(theta)=Im Li_2(r_j exp(i theta))+ell_j theta. (11) To verify the possibly important linear term, its coefficient in theta_xi is L^t rho+C rho_xi. The real part of (7) says C rho_xi=L^t sigma, and sigma_j=ell_j-rho_j. Thus that coefficient is exactly L^t ell. Equality (11) follows up to one fixed constant, already calibrated by (9). Each f_j has its unique global maximum on [0,2*pi] at theta_*j. On (0,pi), f_j'=ell_j-log|1-r_j exp(i theta)|, f_j''=-r_j sin(theta)/|1-r_j exp(i theta)|^2<0. The derivative changes sign at theta_*j. On (pi,2*pi) the function is convex, so its maximum is at an endpoint. The endpoint values at 0 and 2*pi are 0 and 2*pi*ell_j<=0; at pi the value is pi*ell_j<=0. Meanwhile f_j(theta_*j)>0. These statements also hold when r_j=1 by continuous boundary values. Consequently max_P Im W_L=Vol(M), max_(relative boundary P) Im W_L <=Vol(M)-min_j f_j(theta_*j)<Vol(M). (12) If r=0 the boundary is empty. In positive dimension every relative boundary point has at least one active coordinate face; the others cannot exceed their own maxima. This proves (12) on the WHOLE marked box intersection, not only the positive angle polytope. For example, let a be a FIXED continuous density on the compact polytope, smooth near xi_* and nonzero there. The reference integral I_N=integral_P a(theta_xi) exp[N W_L(rho_xi+i theta_xi)/(2*pi*i)] dtheta_xi has a nonzero Gaussian leading coefficient, a power N^(-r/2), and exponential rate Vol(M)/(2*pi). Its real quadratic part is negative definite by (8); the unique interior maximum separates the complement of a small critical neighborhood, and (12) also gives its strict boundary gap. A specified classical amplitude with a nonzero leading density gives the same conclusion under its uniform bounds. This assertion is not about arbitrary N-dependent regular densities, which can themselves carry an exponential action. For finite full-Psi amplitudes one must use their actual uniform symbols and retain any endpoint indentations or completions; the statement does not discard them. Near xi_* the original finite Euler atoms have coefficient one by their D_+ theorem. ## 4. Consequence and remaining source issue The earlier 8_1 example shows that all-subunit shapes may force B singular. It does NOT force an exterior geometric atom if one retains the linear constraints (2). In that same exact five-tetrahedron geometry the unique lens rotation is (1,1,1,1,0). Using the original meridian row and independent edge rows (0,1,2,3,5), B has rank THREE: there are two constraints and a nondegenerate three-variable phase. The constraint matrix from the exact elimination is D=[[0,0,1,1,-2], [0,0,1,0,-1]], d=0. Using the explicitly different LONGITUDE marking (0,1,2,3,6) gives rank B=FOUR, one constraint, and a nondegenerate four-variable phase. Both complete geometric points have all supplied edge and peripheral equations satisfied. The two reduced charts do not silently identify their peripheral source or polarization. Including both peripheral rows together would instead give rank(A B)=6 and a non-Lagrangian system, outside hypothesis (1); its B-rank four is not a substitute for checking that hypothesis. The audit imports the existing exact field/gluing certificate and checks rank, the entire affine parameterization, symmetry and independence of C, the marked critical equations, volume calibration, positive Hessian minors, a nonzero complex Gaussian determinant, and certified positive coordinate/boundary gaps. Its synthetic rank-zero case also checks the empty-boundary convention. Optional --topology replays the existing combinatorial identification with 8_1. This is a general construction for supplied positive triangulations, not a new knot-by-knot strategy. It avoids one reason for leaving the coefficient-one atom domain. The remaining requirement is still to transport the original source, lattice and logarithmic marks to this constrained chart and compute its geometric relative coefficient. Neither classical linear elimination nor a formal Fourier delta is being asserted to perform that quantum/source comparison. Run python3 experiments/audit_constrained_lens_geometric_chart.py or add --topology in the previously specified SnapPy environment.

title: Independent audit of the constrained common-Verma word
text: # Independent audit of the constrained common-Verma word Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [constrained_verma_word_source_extension.md](constrained_verma_word_source_extension.md) is sound, with the source-comparison qualification now explicit in Section 4. No new tests were needed. Each crossing preserves total integer index. Thus the chosen finite ambient module has dimension \(\binom{bN}{b}\), contains the entire head, and is invariant under every crossing of either sign. The two opposite first-exit/first-return factors give the printed \(\delta,w\) blocks. Only the \(m-1\) internal word times require tail variables; discarded final tail output cannot affect the head cut. This is a sufficient construction, not a minimal-rank claim. The tail matrix \(F=I-D\) has strictly lower word-time \(D\), so its inverse is a finite sum. Direct ordered block multiplication gives \[ U_FLV_F=\operatorname{diag}(E-\delta wBF^{-1}C,F). \] The memory entry \(b_jd_{j-1}\cdots d_{i+1}c_i\) records exactly one tail visit. Each such visit advances time by at least two; therefore the claimed finite excursion expansion and the bound \(\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) are correct. The original finite word is its zero-excursion coefficient, not the unrestricted ambient word. For the constrained extension, the printed unipotent matrices satisfy, over any associative ring and in the displayed order, \[ U\begin{pmatrix}A&B&0\\C&D&I\\0&I&0\end{pmatrix}V =\operatorname{diag}\!\left(A, \begin{pmatrix}0&I\\I&0\end{pmatrix}\right). \] This does not invert a wall, the head operator, or the tail operator. The source map \(h\mapsto(h,0,\delta Ch)\), residual map \(f\mapsto(f,0,0)\), and retraction \((f,g,k)\mapsto f+wBk\) satisfy all stated chain identities. The preserved cut is literally the original head functional. Differentiating those whole chain identities gives the first-normal cokernel formula. The terms involving the derivative of the embedding lie in the special-fiber image, as required; the exact whole identity also preserves all higher jets and the normal co-source. A gauge carries the tail inclusion and projection themselves, so their transformed projector retains its actual irregular exponential. Keeping a regularized generator module while deleting that projector would change the complex. An important presentation distinction was clarified during this audit. The cited scalar-to-companion construction has target \(M=T^N-I\). That target is not automatically the word-time head operator \(E\). Applying the conditional formula \(K_{\mathrm{con}}(I_0J)=(I_1R)P\) to this actual word still requires a supplied chain map \(EJ=RP\); alternatively the general algebraic extension theorem can be applied directly with \(A=M\). The revised note states this distinction explicitly and does not claim to construct the missing actual quantum-A/network map. The result is therefore a genuine whole pointed presentation of the constrained finite word. It neither identifies the unconstrained period with that word nor proves a geometric source, source-flatness, or a physical large-level norm.

title: Exact finite-word source extension with all head constraints retained
text: # Exact finite-word source extension with all head constraints retained Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual locally compressed braid word has a finite presentation inside the common Verma transport with one multiplier for each internal tail constraint. Explicit unimodular maps identify this pointed source complex with the original finite-head complex over the whole two-wall ring. Neither wall nor the head characteristic operator is inverted. The unconstrained ambient word also admits an exact finite Feshbach expansion, resumming every excursion. The two constructions distinguish the actual constrained source from the uncompressed ambient period. Their difference is a specified two-wall memory operator, not an assumed vanishing normal correction. This continues [the common two-wall source](common_verma_two_wall_source.md), [the whole crossing factorization](rees_whole_crossing_source_factorization.md), and [the actual scalar/monodromy source map](source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap.md). It constructs a source-preserving network extension for every braid word. It does not identify the unconstrained geometric period with the selected finite invariant or select its large-level phase. ## 1. A finite ambient module for an arbitrary actual word Fix N, a braid on b strands, and a specified word with m crossings of either sign. Use the genuine balanced common-Verma crossings, including their prescribed Cartan and scalar factors. Put delta=1-Q^N, w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1), t=delta w. The local coefficient ring retains Q,M and both wall parameters. Its finite head H has basis the tuples 0<=a_i<N. On head inputs every crossing preserves total integer index, so every relevant ambient path lies in the finite free module V=span{(a_1,...,a_b): a_i>=0, sum a_i<=b(N-1)}. Write V=H direct_sum T. Its ranks are h=N^b, v=binomial(bN,b), s=v-h. (1.1) The regular balanced coefficients and the first-exit/first-return calculation in the common-Verma note prove, for each actual crossing matrix A_i and its inverse sign, A_i=[[a_i, w b_i], [delta c_i,d_i]], (1.2) with all four blocks regular over the whole local ring. Here a_i is exactly the original locally compressed finite-head crossing. Equation (1.2) holds for all crossings of the specified word, not only for a particular knot or a small number of tensor factors. Consequently the original word is W_H=a_m ... a_1, whereas the ambient compressed word is p A_m ... A_1 i. Their scalar evaluations below use the same original cut, literal pivot, zero-framing scalar and full modified-dimension line. None is absorbed into a newly normalized source. ## 2. One finite memory operator resums all excursions Introduce head variables h_0,...,h_m and internal tail variables q_1,...,q_(m-1). Set q_0=q_m=0 at the endpoints. Define the head operator E by an initial or boundary row and the interior rows (E h)_i=h_i-a_i h_(i-1), 1<=i<=m. (2.1) For the open pointed word the first row is h_0. More general boundary rows involving h_0,h_m may be retained, including matrix or Ore-operator coefficients. Define (F q)_i=q_i-d_i q_(i-1), 1<=i<m, (C h)_i=c_i h_(i-1), 1<=i<m, (B q)_i=b_i q_(i-1), 2<=i<=m, (2.2) with zero in the other head rows. The ambient word equations are L=[[E,-w B],[-delta C,F]]. (2.3) The tail operator is F=I-D with D strictly lower in word time. Thus F^(-1)=I+D+...+D^(m-2) is a finite whole matrix. No tail spectral denominator has been introduced. Direct block elimination gives U_F L V_F=diag(S,F), S=E-t K, K=B F^(-1)C, (2.4) U_F=[[I,w B F^(-1)],[0,I]], V_F=[[I,0],[delta F^(-1)C,I]]. These identities keep the written order and are valid over any coefficient ring in which delta,w are central. They follow by two block multiplications. Their source maps are equally literal: an input (f,0) becomes (f,0), and its head solution is S^(-1)f where that notation is defined. Thus (2.4) is a pointed Feshbach reduction, not merely equality of determinants. The memory kernel has the explicit entries K_(j,i-1)=b_j d_(j-1) ... d_(i+1)c_i, 1<=i<j<=m. (2.5) This is one full tail visit from exit i to return j. All visits are resummed by the single matrix S. In the open initial-value case E is also unit lower triangular, so the complete expansion is finite: S^(-1)=sum_(r=0)^floor(m/2) t^r (E^(-1)K)^r E^(-1). (2.6) Every K increases word time by at least two. This proves the truncation, independently of the dimension of T. Taking the final head row and initial head column gives the exact all-excursion expansion of p A_m ... A_1 i. The r=0 term is W_H. In particular p A_m ... A_1 i-W_H=t H_beta, (2.7) with its entire quotient computed by (2.5)--(2.6). This refines the earlier divisibility assertion to an explicit memory resolvent. ### 2.1 A whole excursion-counting source Replace the upper-right block in (2.3) by -lambda w B. Equivalently, weight every return from the tail by the central variable lambda. For the open word the resulting head transfer is a polynomial W(lambda)=W_H+sum_(r=1)^floor(m/2)lambda^r t^r W_r. (2.8) Here W(1) is the compressed ambient word, and W(0) is exactly the original finite word. The constant-term extraction is therefore an actual source operation, uniform for arbitrary word length. This bookkeeper does not assert braid coherence for intermediate lambda or define a new knot invariant. It records the internal source constraints of the specified actual word. At the intersection delta=w=0 the mixed coefficient in (2.7) is the explicit one-excursion operator sum_(1<=i<j<=m) a_m ... a_(j+1) b_j d_(j-1) ... d_(i+1)c_i a_(i-1) ... a_1, (2.9) with all blocks evaluated there. Its rank need not be one. The complete integral path w=0 and root auxiliary wall delta=0 both kill all ordinary excursions, while retaining their two different normal directions. ## 3. The constrained whole-source extension needs no localization Feshbach reduction of the unconstrained word produces S=E-tK, not E. To retain the actual word on a characteristic locus where E may be singular, add internal tail multipliers l. Define the finite matrix operator K_con=[[E, -w B, 0], [-delta C, F, I], [0, I, 0]]. (3.1) Its second row is the genuine ambient tail equation with a source multiplier, and its third row imposes q=0. Thus every internal finite-head projection is retained. For an actual head solution h, the full sourced state is I_0 h=(h,0,delta C h), I_1 f=(f,0,0), K_con I_0=I_1 E. (3.2) The multipliers are the exact boundary currents needed to enforce the finite source; they are not required to vanish off the walls. **Whole constrained-extension theorem.** Over any ring, even a noncommutative Ore ring, the complex K_con is the direct sum of E and a contractible free pair, by explicit unimodular maps. There is no inverse of E,F,delta,w or any characteristic factor in these maps. Proof: the more general matrix K_gen=[[A,B_0,0],[C_0,D,I],[0,I,0]] satisfies U K_gen V=diag(A,J), J=[[0,I],[I,0]], U=[[I,0,-B_0],[0,I,-D],[0,0,I]], V=[[I,0,0],[0,I,0],[-C_0,0,I]]. (3.3) Both U and V are invertible unipotent matrices. Multiplication first subtracts B_0 and D times the constraint row, then subtracts the multiplier column times C_0. This proves (3.3) in the displayed order without commuting any coefficients. The two-term complex J is contractible because J^2=I. Taking A=E,B_0=-wB,C_0=-delta C,D=F proves the theorem. It also works for rectangular A; the free row and column operations merely have the corresponding different sizes. The exact retractions are P_0(h,q,l)=h, P_1(f,g,k)=f+w B k, P_1 K_con=E P_0, P_0 I_0=P_1 I_1=I. (3.4) Consequently kernels, cokernels and all derived two-term source classes of the actual head operator are preserved. In a presentation over a commutative coefficient ring, det K_con=(-1)^rank(T_time)det E when square. Over an Ore ring the stronger unimodular presentation equivalence is available directly, with no determinant convention. The number of extra multiplier/constraint pairs is only (m-1)[binomial(bN,b)-N^b]. (3.5) Thus the presentation has size linear in word length, despite the potentially exponentially many excursion patterns. It does not assert a rank bound independent of N. ## 4. The selected cut and the actual normal source survive exactly For the open source let f=(psi,0,...,0), with the original head source at time zero. Applying the original final cut to h_m gives the actual word evaluation. Extend any such cut by P_0 in (3.4). Then the extension (3.2) preserves it identically, including all scalar factors and the physical meridian derivative. An arbitrary pivotal matrix trace can equivalently be treated as its literal linear functional on the resulting head transfer matrix; no new rank-one normalization is needed. The preservation is stronger than point evaluation. Suppose a regular whole Q-family has E(Q)h(Q)=epsilon f_1+O(epsilon^2), Q=zeta(1+epsilon), and h_0 is in ker E_0. Write coefficient subscripts 0,1. Differentiating (3.2) and taking cokernels gives [K_(con,1) I_(0,0)h_0] =I_(1,0)[E_1 h_0] in coker K_(con,0). (4.1) The terms K_(con,0)I_(0,1)h_0 and I_(1,1)E_0h_0 disappear in this quotient. The same exact chain map preserves every higher normal jet, since (3.2) is a whole identity, and preserves the marked co-source through (3.4). If a specified scalar quantum-A/source complex has already been mapped to an actual head presentation by maps J,R satisfying E J=R P, the new whole sourced-module map is explicitly K_con(I_0 J)=(I_1 R)P. (4.2) In the cited companion-monodromy construction the target is E=M=T^N-I, with J and R=S_N r as proved there. It is not automatically the word-time head operator E of Section 2. Applying the abstract constrained-extension theorem with E=M gives an extension of that known source complex; identifying it with the specific Verma word presentation would require a supplied chain map between those presentations. Equation (4.2) does not construct that missing map. Wherever the supplied map exists, its factors N and its physical derivation D_phys=Y partial_Y+N U partial_U are unchanged. The normal X=2 cut remains a co-source on its thickened lattice; it is not replaced by an ordinary reduced-fiber evaluation. Formula (4.2) requires the supplied head presentation; it does not manufacture an all-level bounded-order scalar equation from a fixed-N matrix calculation. More generally, established elimination relations on the original pointed head network survive the contractible extension (3.3) exactly. It keeps the actual period and its established source relations without removing a lattice factor. It does not prove an equivalence with an unspecified scalar quantum-A presentation. The ambient Verma presentation of this same pointed network now has all its constraint currents visible. ## 5. Exact behavior under the actual irregular Rees transformation There is an intrinsic form of (3.1). Let i_T,p_T be the internal tail inclusion and projection. Then K_con=[[L,i_T],[p_T,0]]. (5.1) This formulation transports under any actual ambient gauge C_V, including the ramified irregular Rees gauge, by L'=C_V L C_V^(-1), i_T'=C_V i_T, p_T'=p_T C_V^(-1), K_con'=diag(C_V,I)K_con diag(C_V^(-1),I). (5.2) The source maps and cut are conjugated by the same matrices. The multiplier is an abstract copy of the discarded-state source module; no regular geometric identification of that copy is assumed. On the image of the original finite total-index module this is a finite-rank identity. Its Rees image is spanned by explicit irregular vectors and need not be a regular finite-rank submodule of the full cyclic root chart. Each finite u-jet has the known pole bounds, while the whole source retains its exponential and head flags. In particular i_T'p_T'=C_V(1-P)C_V^(-1). Its complementary head projector is the actual transformed projector, containing the factor exp[-sum p_i u_i/d]. Dropping that factor from the constraint changes (5.1) and destroys the source equivalence. The whole crossing factorization gives a regular cyclic matrix and a resonant base period, but these source constraints remain alongside both. ## 6. The remaining comparison is now a finite memory/source residual Removing the constraints gives L and the exact Schur operator S=E-tK. Keeping them gives K_con and exactly E. The mismatch is the explicitly computed operator S-E=-delta w B F^(-1)C. (6.1) Equation (2.9) is its first mixed-normal contribution to the actual word. Its Rees conjugate must be evaluated with the constraints and source poles retained; its apparent two-wall vanishing does not authorize discarding it before contraction. At a head characteristic point one cannot generally identify E with S by a regular source-preserving gauge. Already in rank one, E=x, B=C=F=1 gives S=x-delta w. Their characteristic loci differ. The augmented operator K_con is still unimodularly equivalent to diag(x,J), including at x=0. Thus the constrained extension works where an E^(-1)-based correction would have removed the actual characteristic point from the comparison. This gives a concrete next target rather than a proposed phase: transport the actual constraint/source complex (5.1) to the chosen geometric framing module, or prove that its memory and co-source residuals have the required marked transgression there. Smoothness of the geometric algebraic place alone does not make (6.1) zero. The exact source extension is uniform in braid word and works before quantum jets. It does not make the intermediate excursion-counting family topological, prove a new geometric source identification, or infer a selected exponential from its whole equality. The normal d at fixed N and the physical large-level parameter remain distinct. The [universal algebra audit](../experiments/audit_constrained_verma_word_source_extension.py) checks the finite excursion sums, two-wall coefficients, constrained source maps and stable equivalence, including noncommutative entries. The [independent proof audit](constrained_verma_word_independent_audit.md) also checks the finite-word rank, ordered Feshbach maps, constrained source equivalence and normal-jet formulas, with the distinct word-time/companion-presentation qualification in Section 4 retained.

title: Controlled cyclic completion of the actual Euler source
text: # Controlled cyclic completion of the actual Euler source Research note, 26 October 2026. The nilpotent Euler polynomial in the actual R-matrix has a canonical completion by the existing cyclic dilogarithm. We compute its entire coefficient normalization, derive its boundary pentagon through the mixed central jet, and prove polynomial bounds for its coefficient change on marked compact central charts, uniformly in N. This treats a genuine N-dependent algebraic normalization, not a fixed-degree substitute. This is local source transport. It does not identify the global meridian source extension, select a geometric period of a knot, or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The Euler polynomial is an actual quantum-group atom Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and rho=q-q^(-1). Define c_j=(-1)^j Q^(j(j-1)/2)/(Q;Q)_j, P_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)c_j X^j. (1.1) Every denominator is nonzero. In the normalized actual uncheck crossing of [the semicyclic construction](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md), the Euler part is precisely Theta=P_N(q rho^2 E_1 F_2). (1.2) Indeed [j]_q!=q^(-j(j-1)/2)(Q;Q)_j/(1-Q)^j and rho(1-Q)=-q rho^2. Substituting into its original coefficient q^(j(j-1)/2)rho^j/[j]_q! gives (1.2). The original Cartan factor, flip and full source wrap are retained. For the uncheck holonomy map the second F wrap is phi_2/K_1^N, exactly as in that note; for the checked map its input F wrap is phi_2. No new invariant or replacement crossing is defined. An exact polynomial recurrence already displays the boundary: (1-X)P_N(QX)=P_N(X)-X^N/N. (1.3) The coefficients below X^N cancel by their defining recurrence. The top one is -Q^(N-1)c_(N-1)=-1/N, since (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N, c_(N-1)=Q/N. Thus the familiar 1/N source is forced by the actual Euler atom. When X^N=0, (1.3) is its ordinary nilpotent shift identity. ## 2. The uncompleted pentagon has noncentral boundary terms Let XY=QYX, U=X^N, V=Y^N. Normal order means X before Y. For the unmodified truncated pentagon put D=P_N(X)P_N(-YX)P_N(Y)-P_N(Y)P_N(X). The coefficient of X^p Y^s on the first product is exactly sum_k c_(p-k)c_(s-k)Q^(-k)/(Q;Q)_k, (2.1) where 0<=k,p-k,s-k<N. This follows by reordering (-YX)^k=(-1)^k Q^(-k(k+1)/2)X^kY^k. For p,s<N it equals c_p c_s Q^(-ps): the generic pointed compact pentagon's coefficient uses only indices below N and can therefore be specialized without a vanishing denominator. Consequently D lies in the central ideal (U,V), with the exact three-block decomposition D=U B_X+V B_Y+UV B_XY, deg_X,deg_Y B_*<N. (2.2) The coefficients are (2.1) with the indicated wrapped exponents. Two useful nonzero coefficients are [X^N Y]D=1/[N(1-Q)], [X^(2N-2)Y^(2N-2)]D=Q^3/N^3. (2.3) For N=2 this is exactly D=U Y/4+V X/4-UV/8. A central scalar cannot repair this specific unmodified operator identity. Its U constant coefficient would have to vanish, while the nonzero UY coefficient in (2.3) would remain. This comparison retains arbitrary central scalar functions, not only their values at a complete point. It does not refute a differently normalized or source-completed move, or a particular contracted scalar identity. ## 3. Use the literature cyclic completion, with its marked root The alternate cyclic dilogarithm already defined in [the four-atom note](four_cyclic_atoms.md) is d_N(X)=(1-X^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(r=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^rX)^(-r/N). (3.1) It is normalized by d_N(0)=1, with its roots continued from that point. Write nu=(1-U)^(1/N), nu(0)=1. Direct expansion gives log d_N(X)=-sum_(k>=1,N does not divide k) X^k/[k(1-Q^k)]. (3.2) The terms with k divisible by N cancel between the factors of (3.1). In particular d_N(X)=P_N(X) when X^N=0. Finite product cancellation, or (3.2), gives (1-X)d_N(QX)=nu d_N(X), product_(a=0)^(N-1)d_N(Q^a X)=1. (3.3) This is the existing cyclic function, including its determinant normalization. It supplies a completion of the actual atom (1.2). It is not a claim that each separate compact Verma factor can be evaluated at a root without the whole compression used there. ## 4. An explicit norm-torsor formula for every coefficient Reduce d_N(X) in the free algebra with X^N=U: d_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)a_j(U)X^j. The coefficient equations of (3.3) give a_j=a_0 product_(r=1)^j Q^(r-1)/(Q^r-nu). Equivalently, with the c_j of (1.1), a_j/c_j=a_0 product_(r=1)^j (Q^r-1)/(Q^r-nu). (4.1) The entire scalar is fixed by the following product, with a_0(0)=1: a_0(U)^N=nu^(-N(N-1)/2) product_(r=1)^(N-1) [(nu-Q^r)/(1-Q^r)]^(N-r). (4.2) Here is an independent determinant proof. Put T_nu(X)=sum_j t_j X^j, t_j=product_(r=1)^j Q^(r-1)/(Q^r-nu), t_0=1, X e_j=e_(j+1), X e_(N-1)=U e_0, S e_j=Q^j e_j. The relation is (1-X)S T_nu=nu T_nu S. The cyclic bidiagonal matrix (1-X)S has characteristic polynomial lambda^N-nu^N, by its diagonal and full cyclic determinant terms. An eigenvector of eigenvalue lambda normalized to have zeroth coordinate one has v_j(lambda)=Q^(j(j-1)/2)/product_(r=1)^j(Q^r-lambda). To compute the determinant of these columns at lambda=nu Q^a, multiply each column by product_(r=1)^(N-1)(Q^r-lambda). The resulting row polynomials have degrees N-1-j. Their determinant is a fixed nonzero Q constant times the ordinary Vandermonde. The original denominator product is U^(N-1), and the zeroth coordinates of T_nu's columns have product U^(N-1)product_j t_j. Those factors cancel.
