(3.5) Retaining these source factors, the induced regulator norm on the inverse frame obeys, uniformly on compact punctured subdisks, (2pi/N)[-log|C_N(z)| +N log|z| Arg(1-z)/(2pi)] =D_Bloch(z)+O(log N/N). (3.6) This follows directly from the already proved [cyclotomic logarithmic-series estimate](cyclotomic_normalization_tower.md#4-the-local-norm-from-an-exact-logarithmic-series). The logarithmic correction is part of the regulator metric. Equation (3.6) is not an equality with the absolute value of the full knot contraction. The paired exact identity remains gamma_N(M)gamma_N(M^(-1)) =Gamma_N=M^(N-1)/[N S_N(M^2)] =d_N(M)/(N eta_N), eta_N=i^(N+3). (3.7) Consequently G(z)+G(1/z)=-abs(log|z|)/2, exactly the rate of this specified modified-dimension factor. The local large factors cancel or persist according to the actual cap and source; they cannot be omitted before contraction. ## 4. A regularized evaluation at every nontrivial N-th root Let 1<=r<N, zeta=Q^r, and choose M_zeta=exp(pi*i*r/N). Continue M from one counterclockwise to this mark. Approach z=t*zeta with 0<t<1 and set u=1-z^N=1-t^N>0. Define gamma_tilde_(N,r)=u^(r/N) gamma_N. (4.1) On the N-th-root cover this has a finite nonzero value at z=zeta, with its radial root marked as positive. Exactly, gamma_tilde_(N,r)(zeta) =M_zeta^(-(N-1)) (Q;Q)_r/N. (4.2) For a proof, isolate k_0=N-r in Dcal_N(z). This factor is (1-Q^(k_0)z)^(1-r/N), while S_N has a simple zero. Moreover (1-Q^(k_0)z)/(1-z^N) -> 1/N. Reindexing all remaining logarithms gives, with no unspecified phase on the radial branch, product_(k!=k_0)(1-Q^k zeta)^(k/N) =kappa_N N^(-r/N)(Q;Q)_(r-1). Insert these equations in (1.2); the last factor 1-zeta completes (Q;Q)_r. This proves (4.2). Thus the singular scalar is replaced by an explicit algebraic evaluation. There is more information than its norm. Write the actual Euler coefficients as c_0=1, c_s=product_(j=1)^s Q^(j-1)/(Q^j-1). Use the full factorial/source reflection a_j(z)=gamma_N(z) Q^(-j)(Qz;Q)_(N-1-j). At the same regularized fiber it gives a_tilde_j=0, j<r, a_tilde_(r+s)=M_zeta^(-(N+1)) c_s, 0<=s<N-r. (4.3) Indeed the factorial vanishes precisely in the first case. At j=r, multiplying (Q;Q)_r by the complementary factorial gives N, and Q^(-r)=M_zeta^(-2). The subsequent coefficient recurrence is the original Euler recurrence with index s. In the primitive regular module, X^N=u and its special fiber has X^N=0. The whole regularized operator is therefore u^(r/N) d_N(X)|_(z=zeta) =M_zeta^(-(N+1)) X^r sum_(s=0)^(N-1-r)c_s X^s. (4.4) Its image is X^r V, its kernel has dimension r, and its rank is N-r. These images form the standard nested source flag. In particular this operation is not an invertible change of primitive operators. Their determinant is u^r before taking the special fiber. A proposed flow lift must retain this flag or the corresponding relative lattice, rather than evaluating an unregularized inverse at the divisor. There is an exact discrete transport underlying all these fibers. Keep X and u=1-z^N fixed, and shift z->Qz, M->qM. On the common marked cover, with epsilon=q^(-(N+1)), d_N(X;Qz)=epsilon u^(-1/N) X d_N(X;z). (4.6) For a direct proof, the cyclic-product recurrence gives gamma_N(Qz)/gamma_N(z) =q^(-(N-1)) u^(-1/N)(1-Qz). Insert it into the exact reflected-factorial coefficients and use their Euler recurrence. The coefficient of X^0 wraps by X^N=u and satisfies the same identity. Equivalently, if T_z denotes the coefficient polynomial with constant term one, (1-z) T_(Qz)(X)=Q^(-1) X T_z(X). Iterating (4.6) from the principal lift z_0=(1-u)^(1/N) gives u^(r/N) d_N(X;Q^r z_0) =epsilon^r X^r d_N(X;z_0). (4.7) The last factor is an integral unit near u=0. This constructs the complete local lattice transport, not merely its limiting rank. After N steps its multiplier is epsilon^N=(-1)^(N-1), consistent with M->-M on the marked double cover. Dropping that mark would erase a phase at even levels. The shift here holds the primitive X fixed; an actual global meridian shift also changes crossing matrices and Cartan data. This local equation alone is not the knot's quantum A-polynomial. The complete integral statement is just as simple. Take R=C[[u]] and its spectral order S=R[X]/(X^N-u)=C[[X]]. The regularized coefficient a_tilde_j is divisible by u when j<r, and a_tilde_r is a unit. Consequently its multiplier is f_reg=X^r h, h in S^*, image(f_reg)=X^r S, coker(f_reg)=S/(X^r). (4.8) Indeed replace each lower term u b_j X^j by X^(N+j)b_j before dividing by X^r. Every resulting exponent is positive, except the unit constant a_tilde_r. Hence h is a unit. As an R-module, the cokernel is C^r and is killed by u. The Smith factors are exactly N-r units and r copies of u; there are no higher powers. The source comparison is an isomorphism onto the spectral line lattice X^r S, although its map into the original R-lattice loses rank. This is an explicit integral replacement for an invertible-matrix claim. For a product of m such blocks and integral invertible adapters, its inverse has poles of order at most m: each block inverse has at most one pole. Tensoring adds the same orders. This bound is independent of N for a fixed finite network. Applying it to a proposed geometric presentation requires checking that its adapters and scalar source lines are precisely the regular ones specified here. For a fixed root zeta=exp(2pi*i*theta), 0<theta<1 rational, take levels with N theta integral. Equation (4.2) gives (2pi/N)log|gamma_tilde_(N,Ntheta)(zeta)| ->-D_Bloch(zeta). (4.9) This follows by an integrable logarithmic Riemann sum for log|(Q;Q)_(Ntheta)|; subtract log N exactly as in (4.2). For zeta=exp(pi*i/3) it includes all levels divisible by six. It supplies the local resonant regulator rate, not a knot volume theorem or a restriction of that conjecture to these levels. ## 5. The regularized source frames glue by the actual cap Use the actual dual colors, J^2=Q I, and B=gamma_N J. Let u=1-z^N be the common local parameter at z=zeta. The opposite source has residue -(N-r)/N after pullback under M->M^(-1). On the common cover take B_tilde=u^(r/N) B, Bdual_tilde=u^((N-r)/N) Bdual. Both comparison matrices are finite and invertible there. The second root is transported on the common cover, rather than independently reset along an inverse radial path. Their scalar product is, exactly, gamma_tilde gamma_dual_tilde =u Gamma_N=M^(N-1)(1-z)/N. (5.1) For the actual cap C_x^t, x=-M/q, the already audited dual-frame calculation therefore gives Bdual_tilde^(-t) C_x^t B_tilde^(-1) =N C_x/[Q M^(N-1)(1-z)] (5.2) at the resonant fiber. This is finite and invertible because zeta!=1. Cups and pivots transform by the same bases. Thus this local regularization preserves actual duality, including the Gaussian and modified-dimension factors. It does not turn the ordinary trace into the modified trace. The flag pairing also shows why normal data are needed. The actual C_x is anti-diagonal with nonzero entries. Hence (X^r V)^perp=X^(N-r) V (5.3) in the indicated bases. Pairing both leading source vectors therefore gives zero, even though the cap is invertible and both vectors are nonzero. This is a local statement about these factorial source vectors, not about the knot period. Their full pairing, including its normal factor, is explicit. Write p_a(z)=(Qz;Q)_a and x=-M/q. Since C_x e_a=M^a q^(a^2) e_(N-1-a), direct multiplication gives p(z^(-1))^t C_x^t p(z)=S_N(z) G_N(M), G_N(M)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)(-1)^a M^(-a)q^(2a^2+a). (5.4) To prove it, use the exact complement identity p_a(z^(-1)) p_(N-1-a)(z) =S_N(z)(-1)^a z^(-a)Q^(a(a+1)/2). The zero of S_N at zeta is simple, and its first normal coefficient is governed by this finite Gaussian sum. For example, if N is odd and r is even, M=q^r makes it the ordinary quadratic sum with b=(N+1-r)/2, and |G_N|^2=N. Indeed expand its norm, set the index difference to k and sum Q^(2ka): only k=0 survives. If N is even and r=3 mod 4, the terms with indices a and a+N/2 cancel, so G_N(q^r)=0. This follows because their ratio is (-1)^(N/2+(N+1-r)/2)=-1. Thus even the first normal term requires its actual phase. These uniform identities locate the issue in a computable source pairing; they neither show nor imply vanishing of the full Kashaev invariant. ## 6. What this supplies for the Rivin flow The [angle flow](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) supplies a geometric path and its marked A-curve potential. Equations (1.2)--(1.3) now supply exact local transport for the scalar source line; (3.1) gives its action along specified trajectories; (4.3)--(4.4) give its degeneration and source flag; (4.6)--(4.8) construct its discrete transport on the spectral line lattice; and (5.2) gives compatible actual gluing through a resonance. This removes a local scalar and lattice ambiguity. It still does not assign every geometric shape to the actual network's norm-root coordinate or transport its selected cut cycle. In particular a covector can annihilate X^r V. The flag makes that coupling question explicit, without proving it is nonzero for the actual knot. Convexity of the classical volume cannot by itself remove this remaining selected-period question. [The audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_source_resonances.py) checks the new frame identity against independent matrix determinants, its connection against determinant derivatives, every resonant source flag and its first-order Smith factors at the tested levels, the actual regularized caps and their normal Gaussian moments, the marked complex phase and the proved error bound. [Results](../experiments/cyclic_source_resonance_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_cyclic_source_resonances.py

title: Cyclic modules, the Kashaev color, and a recoupling lattice at degeneration
text: # Cyclic modules, the Kashaev color, and a recoupling lattice at degeneration Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplies an integral extension of the local algebra used in the torsor construction. The results are uniform in every level N>=2. They are explicit representation and lattice calculations, not an appeal to a theorem about quantum knot invariants. No novelty is claimed for cyclic quantum-group representations. The distinguished Kashaev state remains the one fixed in [kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [kashaev_ado_pointing.md](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). ## 1. A regular quantum-group family through the nilpotent fiber Put q=exp(pi*i/N), omega=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and R=C[t,t^(-1)], E_t=R[x]/(x^N-t), X f(x)=x f(x), sigma f(x)=f(omega*x). The following endomorphisms are regular over R, including t=1: F=(1-X)sigma^(-1), E=(1-omega*X)/(omega*X*rho^2) sigma, K=-q^(-1)X^(-1). (1.1) All inverses in (1.1) exist over R. Direct multiplication gives K E=q^2 E K, K F=q^(-2)F K, E F-F E=(K-K^(-1))/rho. (1.2) For a short verification let f(X)=(X+X^(-1)-2)/rho^2. Then FE=f(X), EF=f(omega*X), and f(omega*X)-f(X)=(q X-q^(-1)X^(-1))/rho. The last numerator equals K-K^(-1). The normalized Casimir is rho^2 FE+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=-2. (1.3) The central powers follow by multiplying around the cyclic orbit: F^N=1-t, E^N=(-1)^(N-1)(1-t)/(t*rho^(2N)), K^N=(-1)^(N-1)/t. (1.4) Thus the inverses of F used in the generic quantum-torus chart are unnecessary in this quantum-group lattice. At t=1 both E and F are nilpotent, while the module stays simple. To see the fiber explicitly, evaluate functions at omega^j, and write e_j for the corresponding delta vectors. Put p_j=product_(a=1)^j(1-omega^a), v_j=p_j e_j. Then F v_j=v_(j+1), E v_j=[j]_q^2 v_(j-1), K v_j=q^(N-1-2j)v_j, (1.5) with the endpoint vectors zero. These are exactly the Kashaev color matrices in the crossing proof. The K eigenvalues are distinct and all adjacent E,F coefficients are nonzero. Matrix units are obtained from the K spectral projectors and these adjacent maps. For t!=1, X,F already generate the full matrix algebra because 1-X is invertible. Hence the image of this family in End_R(E_t) is the full matrix bundle: fiberwise surjectivity implies surjectivity over R by Nakayama. This concerns the image of the given family, not an assertion that every central quotient of the unrestricted quantum group is Azumaya. ## 2. The pointing also extends The cyclic vacuum equation is (X+F-1)v=0. Its kernel over R is R*1. Away from t=1 this follows from (X+F-1)=(1-X)(sigma^(-1)-1). At t=1 its rows in the evaluation basis are the N-1 independent differences v_(j-1)-v_j. Thus its rank remains N-1 and its kernel line remains primitive. In the basis (1.5), its specialized vector is v_vac=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) p_j^(-1) v_j. (2.1) It is a quantum Whittaker vector rather than the highest-weight vector. The functional eps(f)=Tr_(E_t/R)(f)/N is regular and eps(1)=1. On a knot's cut operator, which is scalar at t=1, pairing with this vector and functional gives the same Kashaev period as pairing with the highest-weight vector. No possibly large change-of-basis norm is discarded; scalarity cancels that change exactly. ### A tensor convention that must be retained The algebra extension above is not by itself a Hopf-algebra comparison. The Borel coproduct used in the pointed recoupling notes is Delta_B X=X tensor X, Delta_B F=F tensor 1+X tensor F. For the standard quantum-group coproduct and X=-q^(-1)K^(-1), Delta_q X=-q X tensor X, Delta_q F=F tensor 1-q X tensor F. (2.2) These formulas give the exact scalar mark that any tensor comparison must carry. It has the following explicit endpoint transport; an algebra isomorphism alone would not provide it. ### A matched endpoint chain for the actual coproduct Write kappa=-q. In an ordered tensor product of b factors, put U_j=K_j^(-1)=kappa*X_j, c_j=kappa^(1-j), F_j^new=c_j*F_j, E_j^new=c_j^(-1)*E_j. These are still the regular quantum-group representations (1.1), with a constant scaling automorphism of E,F. Their Borel coordinates are now U_j,F_j^new, with the actual coproduct Delta U=U tensor U, Delta F=F tensor 1+U tensor F. The unit vector of factor j solves (F_j^new+a_j U_j-b_j)1=0, a_j=kappa^(-j), b_j=kappa^(1-j), a_j=b_(j+1). (2.3) Thus these are exactly matched endpoint modules in the [endpoint formulation](pointed_period_descent.md), at all levels. The iterated coproduct acts on the unit tensor by the telescoping sum F_tot 1=sum_(j=1)^b kappa^(j-1)*c_j*x_1...x_(j-1)*(1-x_j) =1-x_1...x_b, U_tot=kappa^b*x_1...x_b. (2.4) Consequently its pointing is (F_tot+kappa^(-b)U_tot-1)1=0. More generally the substitution m:E_(t_1...t_b) -> E_(t_1) tensor ... tensor E_(t_b), f(x) -> f(x_1...x_b), (2.5) intertwines F with F_tot, and multiplication by kappa^b*x with U_tot. Each summand shifts the product coordinate by omega^(-1), so the same telescoping calculation proves (2.5) on every f, not just on the vacuum. The central marks are retained: U_j^N=kappa^N*t_j, (F_j^new)^N=c_j^N*(1-t_j), U_tot^N=kappa^(bN)*product t_j, F_tot^N=1-product t_j. (2.6) At the nilpotent fiber, the individual automorphism is the explicit basis conjugation v_h -> c_j^h v_h. It is a unit at every level, even when kappa^N=-1. Moreover c_j=(-q)^(1-j) is one fixed monomial in the generic quantum parameter; it is not an unrelated scalar chosen separately at each level. At the specified complex roots its basis-conjugation entries all have absolute value one. Thus the scalar in (2.2) is accounted for at the Borel pointing and tensor-embedding level without changing the nilpotent color. At this stage (2.5) has only been checked on the Borel action. The subsequent [Casimir comparison](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) proves its full E-action, identifies both actual crossings on the transported recoupling lattice, and derives the pivotal closing trace. The selected global geometric period and its norm remain additional comparison requirements. ## 3. Pointed Borel factorization at all levels For nondegenerate s,t, the existing relative operators are Z=Y_1 Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=ZX_2, X_tot=X_1X_2, Y_tot=X_1Y_2+Y_1, tau=(1-st)/(1-t). The generic commutation and vacuum-ideal certificates in the preceding notes do not use parity. For the central powers one must retain (ZX_2)^N=(-1)^(N-1) Z^N X_2^N. Consequently X_tot^N=st, Y_tot^N=1-st, D^N=tau, (-C)^N=1-tau (3.1) for every N>=2. The quantum-binomial argument requires primitivity, not primality or oddness. Simplicity and the common vacuum then give the pointed factorization at every level, with the same kernel C_(s,t)(u^a v^b) =w^a product_(j=1)^b(1-omega^j w)/(1-omega^j z), w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. (3.2) In the monomial bases used in the earlier note, its determinant is det C_(s,t)=sigma_N f(s,t)^(N(N-1)/2), f(s,t)=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, sigma_N=(-1)^(N(N-1)^2/2). (3.3) The earlier formula without sigma_N applies to odd N. For completeness, the change from x_1^a x_2^b to w^a z^b contributes sigma_N*t^(N(N-1)/2): translation of the z exponent by a has sign (-1)^(a(N-1)). The numerator-column norms contribute (1-st)^(N(N-1)/2). The remaining z-column determinant has sign (-1)^(N-1), phase omega^(N(N^2-1)/3), and denominator (1-t)^(N-1). Its N-th power has no sign or phase. Multiplying these factors proves (3.3), including the even-level sign. ## 4. Blow up the simultaneous nilpotent point Use the discrete valuation ring A=C(a,b)[[eps]], with a,b,a+b nonzero, and substitute s=1-eps*a, t=1-eps*b. This records a direction above (s,t)=(1,1). Its relative parameter is tau=(a+b)/b-eps*a, f(s,t)=eps^(-1) (a+b)/b^2 * (1+O(eps)). (4.1) In particular the exceptional relative parameter remains nondegenerate. The direction unit (a+b)/b^2 is part of the normalization torsor. **Integral recoupling theorem.** The invariant factors of C_(s,t) over A are eps^(-1), multiplicity N(N-1)/2, 1, multiplicity N(N+1)/2. (4.2) Thus C^(-1) is regular. The image lattice C A^(N^2) contains the basic target lattice A^(N^2), and their quotient is killed by eps and has dimension N(N-1)/2 over the residue field. This is the precise lattice change across the pole, with the vacuum retained. ### Uniform proof Pass to the w,z evaluation bases with w_i=omega^i (st)^(1/N), z_j=omega^j t^(1/N), using formal roots with constant term one. Their Vandermonde changes are units in A, so invariant factors are unchanged. Formula (3.2) becomes N blocks, whose entries are B_i(j,d)=product_(k=1)^d(1-omega^k w_i) /(1-omega^k z_j), 0<=d<N. (4.3) Define r_i=[-i]_N if i!=0, and r_0=N. The numerator has one simple zero exactly when d>=r_i; the denominator has one exactly when d>=r_j. Therefore every entry has pole order at most one. The residue eps*B_i has nonzero columns only for 1<=d<r_i, and rows r_j<=d. The square submatrix r_j,d in {1,...,r_i-1} is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Its rank is r_i-1. The denominator-column matrix, before multiplying by the numerator factors, has determinant valuation -(N-1): multiply its columns d=1,...,N-1 by eps and evaluate at eps=0. The row j=0 is supported only on column zero; the other rows are the same nonzero triangular residue matrix. Numerator factors add valuation N-r_i. Hence val(det B_i)=1-r_i. Since all poles are simple and the residue has rank r_i-1, exactly r_i-1 invariant factors have valuation -1. The remaining valuations are nonnegative, and their sum is zero, so all are zero. Summing over r_i=1,...,N proves (4.2). There is also an explicit integral frame for each block: multiply its source columns d=1,...,r_i-1 by eps. The resulting matrix has a unit determinant. This gives the lattice modification without a numerical limit or an unspecified regularization. ## 5. The determinant root retains the exceptional unit For odd N, h=(N-1)/2 and the preceding normalized frame can use gamma^N=f^(-h). For even N an explicit determinant-one cover is gamma^(2N)=-f^(-(N-1)). (5.1) Indeed sigma_N=(-1)^(N/2) in this case, so raising (5.1) to N/2 cancels the sign in (3.3). This is a genuine even-level phase. On the ramified cover eps=delta^(2N), gamma has valuation N-1. Its remaining unit retains (a+b)/b^2 through the displayed root equations. The determinant-normalized C still needs the source and target lattices of (4.2); determinant one alone does not make its entries regular in the original lattices. Generic pointed recouplings obey the categorical pentagon at all levels. Extension of their specified scalar normalizations through a whole degeneration requires compatible transported lattices and the phases above. No global path-independence is inferred merely from the determinant formula. The subsequent [common carry-lattice theorem](carry_recoupling_lattice.md) now proves the required path independence for arbitrary finite pointed recoupling trees. Its explicit image in leaf evaluation coordinates is epsilon^(-floor(sum i_j/N)) on each tuple. A nodewise carry inequality and determinant count prove this equality uniformly. Both the basic sources and the actual sublattices are preserved by every recoupling. The original cut meridian family is recovered with all wrap sources, pivot and framing retained. This extends the two-factor lattice theorem; it does not infer a global geometric gluing or regulator norm from the determinant. ## 6. Relevance and remaining comparison The cyclic vacuum now has a regular realization in the actual nilpotent Kashaev color. The simultaneous recoupling pole has an explicit two-step integral lattice, and its direction-dependent normalization unit is known. These results remove a local degeneracy restriction of the earlier generic cyclic-module arguments. They do not identify the geometric fundamental-class period with the Kashaev cut period. Equations (2.3)--(2.6) account for the tensor mark at the Borel level. The subsequent [Casimir calculation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) extends the E-action and identifies actual crossings and local pivotal traces on these lattices. The global geometric period pairing and its regulator norm must still be matched. Choosing an unpointed isomorphism of matrix algebras cannot replace that theorem. The independent checks in `experiments/audit_cyclic_steinberg_lattice.py` verify the regular quantum-group relations, nilpotent fiber, all-level pointed factorization, determinant sign, and the block lattice frames. They are diagnostics for the uniform arguments above.

title: Exact root-cyclic tetrahedral pentagons with their source frames
text: # Exact root-cyclic tetrahedral pentagons with their source frames Research note, 26 October 2026. The four-atom crossing construction has a strict local three-to-two operator identity on a compatible anchored root cover. The proof below retains the transported central frames, determinant roots, monomial shears and scalar phase. It does not identify arbitrary independent lifts of the roots, assign all face and boundary tensors to a geometric triangulation, or prove the selected regulator norm of the knot period. The local function is the literature cyclic dilogarithm already specified in [the four-atom note](four_cyclic_atoms.md). No different knot invariant is defined. The generic formal identity is proved directly in [the Verma transport note](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md). ## 1. The normalized finite atom Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. For a primitive monomial m with m^N=mu^N, choose nu^N=1-mu^N, with both factors nonzero. On the eigenvalue mu Q^j put f_0=1, f_j=nu^j/(mu;Q)_j, 0<=j<N, C(m)=f(m), F=product_j f_j, D(m)=gamma C(m), gamma^N=F^(-1). (1.1) The root of gamma is retained. Near a zero coefficient tag choose nu=gamma=1; the matrix D then extends with value I. Formula (1.1) is exactly the alternate literature cyclic dilogarithm, with its compatible branches: mathfrak_d_N(z;Q)=(1-z^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(ell=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^ell z)^(-ell/N). On a module of dimension rN, every eigenvalue has multiplicity r, so det C=F^r and det D=1. All half roots required at even N are included; no division by two modulo N is used. If m A=Q^k A m, the finite conjugation r_m obeys r_m(A) D(m)=D(m) A', A'=nu^(-k) A. (1.2) Here r_m is the rational conjugation by the generic compact dilogarithm, expressed by finite products of 1-Q^ell m. Its denominators are invertible when 1-m^N is. Equation (1.2), proved by the recurrence in (1.1), specifies the changing target frame. ## 2. The primitive cyclic pentagon Take XY=QYX, X^N=U, Y^N=V. Choose three norm roots a^N=1-U, b^N=1-V, h^N=H=1-U+UV. (2.1) Write D(m;nu) to display the root used in (1.1). Then on the compatible root component anchored at X=Y=0, D(Y;b) D(bX;h) =D(X;a) D(-YX/a;h/a) D(Y/h;ab/h). (2.2) Zero here refers to the coefficient tags of fixed clock/shift matrices, so the anchor is a regular formal matrix specialization. Away from it the monomial centers are nonzero. The five atom centers in their displayed order are left: V, (1-V)U; right: U, -UV/(1-U), V/H. (2.3) In particular (-YX)^N=-UV at every parity. A compatible spectral root of the middle monomial is qxy/a if x^N=U, y^N=V. The right norm roots h/a and ab/h are forced ratios, rather than new independent choices. The final X,Y splitting roots on both paths are bx,y/h. Here is a uniform proof of the scalar in (2.2). The directly proved compact pentagon has rational conjugations with no poles other than the indicated norm divisors. Clearing those factors and specializing Q therefore gives the same rational quantum automorphism on both sides. Equation (1.2) implements it between the same initial and final splitting representations. Those representations generate the full matrix algebra. The ratio of the two invertible products is consequently a scalar lambda. Their determinants are one, so lambda^N=1. All the matrices and normalization roots are algebraic on the specified lifted cover. Thus lambda is constant on each irreducible component. At the regular formal anchor every atom is I, so lambda=1 on its component. This proves (2.2). Independent choices of the five gamma roots can lie on other components; their residual phase is not erased by the theorem. Using raw C instead gives L_raw=lambda_raw R_raw, with lambda_raw^N=F_L1 F_L2/(F_R1 F_R2 F_R3). (2.4) The anchor fixes its compatible lift. Determinants alone fix only the power in (2.4). ## 3. Include the tetrahedral monomial shears For three leaves use uniform clock/shift pairs Z_i e_a=z_i e_(a+1), S_i e_a=s_i Q^a e_a, S_i Z_i=Q Z_i S_i. The shear C_ij is the literal permutation (a_i,a_j) -> (a_i,a_j+a_i mod N). Its target splitting roots are z_i'=z_i z_j, z_j'=z_j, s_i'=s_i, s_j'=s_j/s_i. (3.1) Indeed the source algebra images of Z_i and S_j are Z_i Z_j and S_i^(-1)S_j. Direct action on the normalized basis proves the two intertwining equations; the other generators are fixed. The shears obey exactly C_12 C_13 C_23=C_23 C_12. (3.2) In an unnormalized polynomial basis there are also carry factors from reducing exponents modulo N. Formula (3.1) uses normalized monomial frames and does not authorize dropping those factors when comparing with the actual Verma or cut basis. Evaluate m=-Q t Z_i Z_j^(-1) S_j^(-1) after the shear (3.1). In the roots before that shear, a spectral root is mu=q t z_i s_i/s_j, nu^N=1+t^N z_i^N s_i^N/s_j^N. (3.3) The commutation integers of m with (Z_i,Z_j,S_i,S_j) are (0,-1,-1,+1). Define the typed tetrahedral operator by T_ij(t;nu)=C_ij D(m;nu)^(-1). (3.4) Combining the shear with the inverse atom gives its final roots z_i''=z_i z_j, z_j''=z_j/nu, s_i''=s_i/nu, s_j''=s_j nu/s_i. (3.5) Every subsequent operator is evaluated in these new roots. Products in the formulas below are typed intertwiners from the final module to the initial one, written in traversal order. ## 4. The strict tetrahedral three-to-two identity Start with nonzero z_i,s_i and coefficient tags u,v. Put A=u^N z_1^N s_1^N/s_2^N, B=v^N z_2^N s_2^N/s_3^N, a^N=1+A, b^N=1+B, h^N=1+A+AB. (4.1) Use the root choices (a,h/a,ab/h) for the left three steps and (b,h) for the right two steps. Then, on the component anchored at u=v=0 and a=b=h=gamma_i=1, T_12(u;a) T_13(uv;h/a) T_23(v;ab/h) =T_23(v;b) T_12(u;h). (4.2) Substitution in (3.5) gives the same final roots on both paths: z_final=(z_1 z_2 z_3, z_2 z_3/h, z_3/b), s_final=(s_1/h, s_2 h/(s_1 b), s_3 b/s_2). (4.3) The rational conjugations agree by the generic tagged tetrahedral pentagon, whose proof uses only the compact pentagon and (3.2). After clearing the norm divisors, it specializes exactly as in Section 2. Both products in (4.2) therefore intertwine the same full three-pair matrix algebra, and their ratio is scalar. Each normalized atom has determinant one on the N^3-dimensional module. The determinant ratio of the shear words is one by (3.2). Thus this scalar has N^3-th power one. At u=v=0 all atoms are I and the bare shear words agree by (3.2). Algebraic root-of-unity rigidity on the anchored component fixes the scalar to one. This proves (4.2) for even and composite N as well. For raw inverse atoms retain the scalar lambda_raw. If F_Li,F_Ri are their cycle determinants from (1.1), the exact equation is lambda_raw^(N^3) =[F_R1 F_R2/(F_L1 F_L2 F_L3)]^(N^2). (4.4) The diagnostic also finds the stronger Nth-power version of (4.4) in its samples. That strengthening is not needed or asserted as a uniform theorem here. ## 5. What an external selected evaluation inherits Let two specified finite tensor presentations differ by (4.2), with the same exterior maps. After identifying their boundary frames as in (4.3), the resulting full external operators are equal. Every transported vector/covector contraction is equal, including the zero contraction. This is an exact local period transport statement, not just equality of unpointed modules. The [four-atom formula](four_cyclic_atoms.md) uses these same finite literature atoms. Its already specified braid contraction can therefore use this move wherever the typed internal and boundary identifications are supplied. The Cartan, determinant, carry, peripheral and source factors are retained by those identifications. Arbitrary new source vectors are not allowed. An uncolored ideal triangulation does not supply all these tensor leg, face, turn, source and cut identifications. Nor does (4.2) move a fixed reducible root character to the hyperbolic one. The next [triangulation comparison criterion](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md#8-the-precise-remaining-use-of-the-ideal-triangulation-theorem) spells out the additional relative comparison and its obstruction. The subsequent [controlled cyclic Euler-source calculation](controlled_cyclic_euler_source.md) extends the anchored primitive identity to a free formal central order through its nilpotent source. It computes the complete first mixed jet, including the required UV corner term. The completion agrees there with the actual R Euler polynomial. An exact reflected factorial-vector comparison transports its source and co-source, and its scalar is polynomially bounded on marked compact charts. This does not equate arbitrary root lifts, construct an uncolored geometric tensor assignment, or identify the global knot period. ## 6. The classical five-term check and its limitation Let D_B denote the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm. The arguments (2.3) satisfy exactly D_B(V)+D_B((1-V)U) =D_B(U)+D_B(-UV/(1-U))+D_B(V/H). (6.1) To verify it, use the ordinary five-term identity at x=U, y=V/H. Its three resulting arguments are UV/H, U(1-V), V. Finally D_B(z/(z-1))=-D_B(z), with z=UV/H and z/(z-1)=-UV/(1-U), gives (6.1). This also explicitly checks the changing central arguments; using frozen arguments would lose the relation. Every nondegenerate ordinary five-term move preserves the total regulator. In particular it cannot carry a zero-regulator central cycle to a positive hyperbolic fundamental cycle. This is why a strict root pentagon is local input for the selected-period comparison, rather than that comparison itself. ## 7. Coverage and exact checks Root-cyclic dilogarithm pentagons and Heisenberg-double tetrahedral operators are existing structures. The literature definitions and coverage are recorded in the linked four-atom and Verma notes; no novelty or published coherence proof is assumed here. The argument above reconstructs the root transport, scalar and frame in the actual conventions of these notes. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.py) checks nine primitive cyclic pentagons at N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12 and five full N^3-dimensional tetrahedral identities at N=2,...,6. It checks all five shear maps, the final clock/shift roots, the bare permutation identity, projective matrix equality and the recorded raw determinant equations. The normalized phase is fixed by the uniform anchored proof, rather than by unrelated finite-field choices of gamma roots. [Results](../experiments/cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.py The four-atom audit was also rerun after generalizing the cycle helper to arbitrary spectator multiplicity: all 18 crossings and 72 atom intertwiners pass. These checks do not establish the global selected-source or regulator-norm theorem.

title: The missing Ward edge gives the full peripheral norm adapter
text: # The missing Ward edge gives the full peripheral norm adapter Research calculation, 27 October 2026. The literal nilpotent raising matrix has a canonical cyclic completion with one additional edge. Its determinant character is exactly the regular-meridian character at the Frobenius peripheral parameter. The full modified-dimension factor is the ratio of the missing edge to this cyclic norm defect. This supplies a norm-character comparison and a regular degenerating finite algebra. It does not identify the full quantum Ward flow with the internal geometric centralizer, or prove the selected volume norm. ## 1. The actual raising matrix and its single missing edge Fix N>=2, Q primitive of order N, q^2=Q, x=-M/q. In the balanced actual basis, the regular scaled raising matrix Ecal=(q-q^(-1))^2 E has upper edges Ecal_(a,a+1)=epsilon_a=M Q^(-a-1)-M^(-1), 0<=a<N-1. (1) Its last cyclic edge is absent in the actual highest-weight module. Extending the same expression to a=N-1 gives epsilon_(N-1)=M-M^(-1)=kappa. (2) Define Ecyc by adding precisely the matrix entry Ecyc=Ecal+kappa E_(N-1,0). (3) This is a specified rank-one completion, not an assertion that the completed matrix defines the original quantum-group representation. The actual cut and all actual Ward equations still use Ecal unless their corresponding boundary term from (3) is explicitly retained. ## 2. The exact cyclic norm Put kappa_N=M^N-M^(-N). The primitive-root product gives product_(a=0)^(N-1) epsilon_a =(-1)^(N+1)kappa_N=:delta_N. (4) Indeed factor M^(-1) from each edge and use product_(j=1)^N(1-M^2 Q^(-j))=1-M^(2N). Every path of length N around the cyclic matrix uses every edge once. Its characteristic polynomial and determinant are therefore Ecyc^N=delta_N I, det(lambda I-Ecyc)=lambda^N-delta_N, det(I+t Ecyc)=1+kappa_N t^N. (5) The determinant formula also follows directly: only the diagonal permutation and the complete N-cycle survive in its expansion. All signs in (4)--(5) are retained, including even N. Over k(M), the algebra A_N=k(M)[e]/(e^N-delta_N) (6) has the displayed matrix as its regular multiplication operator after a diagonal basis change, whenever all edges are units. Thus (5) is also the exact algebra norm Norm_(A_N/k(M))(1+t e)=1+kappa_N t^N. (7) Generically delta_N!=0 and this is an etale finite algebra. In a neighborhood of M=1 the first N-1 edges in (1) are units. The same diagonal basis change is regular there, while the missing edge vanishes: use v_(N-1), Ecyc v_(N-1), ..., Ecyc^(N-1)v_(N-1) as the cyclic basis. Only the first N-1 edge factors enter its invertible diagonal/reversal change; no kappa inverse occurs. At M=1, Ecyc=Ecal is a single regular nilpotent Jordan block and A_N becomes k[e]/(e^N). The meridian lattice, rather than only the generic norm-one torus, retains this special source fiber. ## 3. The peripheral multiplier is the defect ratio Define the full regular-meridian adapter u_N(M)=kappa_N/kappa =M^(1-N)(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). (8) This is a Laurent polynomial, with u_N(1)=N. Equations (2) and (4) give the whole-germ ratio kappa/kappa_N=1/u_N(M). (9) The actual modified dimension in the retained convention is exactly d_N(M)=i^(N+3)/u_N(M). (10) Thus the finite raising-matrix completion accounts for the entire peripheral adapter, including its meridian normal germ and divisors. One must cancel the common kappa factor before evaluating at M=1; the result there is i^(N+3)/N. Replacing kappa and kappa_N separately by zero would discard this source value. The normal determinant coefficient is also fixed: det(I+t Ecyc)=1+N kappa t^N+O(kappa^2) (11) near M=1. It is a first eigenvalue-gap normal with multiplier N, not the N-squared trace normal described in [the Newton resolution](newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut.md). ## 4. The norm character agrees with the geometric regular centralizer The existing marked regular centralizer is C_M(b)=I+b J_M, J_M^2=kappa J_M, det C_M(b)=1+kappa b. (12) At the Frobenius peripheral value M^N it has determinant 1+kappa_N b. Equation (7) is precisely this character after b=t^N. Hence the cyclic Ward completion and the regular centralizer have an exact matching determinant character, with their marked peripheral power map specified. This is stronger than matching their numerical complete values. It is a comparison of characters, not of the entire groups. For N>2 the one-parameter family I+t Ecyc is not in general closed under multiplication, and its unit algebra has dimension N. The regular centralizer is one-dimensional. No group isomorphism or compatible bulk action follows merely from (7) and (12). The actual nilpotent Ward relative class is constructed in [the coherent-cut/Ward note](coherent_cut_obstruction_and_ward_relative_class.md). The remaining task is to transport this cyclic edge and norm data through the actual partial Gaussian/adjoint diagram, retaining the boundary source and the prescribed cut. The selected regulator period and its volume growth remain unproved. ## 5. A literal quantum-factorial gauge and its scalar cyclic source The norm comparison has an explicit affine transport realization. Define the finite quantum-factorial polynomial f_N(t,e)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) (-t e)^j/(Q;Q)_j. (13) Every denominator is nonzero at the primitive root. Its coefficients obey f_j(Q^j-1)=t f_(j-1). Consequently, as a polynomial identity, f_N(t,Qe)-(1+t e)f_N(t,e) =-t(-t)^(N-1)e^N/(Q;Q)_(N-1). (14) The primitive-root product (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N follows by evaluating (z^N-1)/(z-1) at z=1. In A_N, (14) becomes the exact affine source equation f_N(t,Qe)-(1+t e)f_N(t,e) =-kappa_N t^N/N. (15) This sign and scalar hold at even and composite levels as well. On the actual nilpotent Ecal, the right side is zero because Ecal^N=0. The gauge f_N(t,Ecal) is unipotent and invertible for every t. On the cyclic completion its failure is precisely the displayed scalar, not an unspecified numerical normalization. There is also an actual matrix shift implementing this equation. The literal root matrix K satisfies K Ecyc K^(-1)=Q Ecyc, (16) including the last cyclic edge. Thus (15) is a finite matrix Ward equation with Ad_K on its first term. At the ideal fiber it is an explicit meridian-regular Hilbert-90 gauge in k[e]/(e^N), with constant coefficient one. More generally the connected special norm-one units have a finite nilpotent logarithm; in the basis e^j the equation (sigma-1)g=log a is solved by dividing its j-th coefficient by Q^j-1, j=1,...,N-1. The disconnected constant phases mu_N remain separate: an integral unit coboundary has constant term one, so those phases cannot be silently removed by such a gauge. Here meridian regularity is over the characteristic-zero cyclotomic coefficient field. The displayed cyclotomic factorial inverses are retained; arithmetic integrality at their primes is not asserted. Dividing the scalar source in (15) by the actual missing edge kappa retains -u_N(M)t^N/N, with complete value -t^N. (17) Multiplication by the whole d_N in (10) instead gives the exact normal source -i^(N+3) kappa t^N/N. These are different recorded regularizations; neither replaces u_N by its numerical value before the common zero is canceled. The field norm, quantum-factorial transport, cyclic endpoint defect and peripheral adapter have therefore been computed in one literal matrix model. Matching this model's action on the internal geometric framing class remains necessary; an equality of norm characters alone does not construct that map or prove the volume conjecture. ## 6. Subsequent whole group and function transfers The [norm-root period theorem](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) now strengthens the character comparison to an explicit group morphism. For a unit u in the retained cyclic normal order, choose the marked root nu^N=Norm(u), nu=1 modulo kappa. Then u -> C_M((nu-1)/kappa) is a regular group morphism with norm-one kernel. On u=1+t e it takes the full marked path t=0,...,M to the regular centralizer path with endpoints b=0,M, and its invariant differential integrates exactly to Log(M^2)/kappa. The bare kappa=0 fiber does not retain this morphism's first-normal character. The [coherent Ward unfolding](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) also reconstructs the whole factorial from the actual all-level nilpotent jets. Its logarithmic cyclotomic pole is a dilogarithm, its marked regular part gives the normalized Hilbert-90 gauge, and its normal derivative gives exactly (17). On the genuine integral complete-color tensor lift, that same pole evaluates to the [finite divided-power exponential](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md) exp[(-t)^N J_b/N], with J_b^b=0. This lift follows M=-q^N; its normal must not be substituted for the fixed-root kappa normal. The [literal crossing Ward currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md) prove ordinary global cancellation of the cyclic-edge wall source. In contrast, the [marked divided-normal cut](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md) has a specified nonzero missing-edge pairing and is cohomologous to the original normalized cut. It returns exactly the original Kashaev value on every closed cut tangle. The full geometric source comparison still has to preserve this relative cut before its contraction; ordinary wall nonvanishing is no longer a premise. The [common-Verma source](common_verma_two_wall_source.md) now also realizes a literal regular-centralizer action on the actual completed block module. Its shift and divided F-power form a Weyl pair; the normalized coherent kernel carries the group action and the marked period as an explicit source matrix coefficient. The [balanced crossing comparison](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md) keeps this coherent source through the genuine root crossing. This strengthens the group transfer without identifying its reducible source base with the internal geometric framing. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_ward_norm_adapter.py). [Results](../experiments/cyclic_ward_norm_adapter_results.json).

title: The cyclic Ward norm-root transfer carries the peripheral period
text:
# The cyclic Ward norm-root transfer carries the peripheral period This gives an explicit group transfer, first-normal affine character, and marked relative logarithmic period on the literal cyclic Ward completion. It goes beyond equality of determinant characters. The transfer is a quotient of a unit-group dilatation, not an isomorphism between the \(N\)-dimensional unit group and the one-dimensional geometric centralizer. It constructs the full **peripheral** period \(\operatorname{Log}(M^2)/(M-M^{-1})\). It does not construct the internal knot Gaussian pushforward, identify a selected Bloch period, or prove volume growth. ## 1. The actual finite algebra and its retained normal Fix \(N\ge2\), \(Q\) primitive of order \(N\), and a characteristic-zero coefficient field \(k\) containing \(Q\). Work near \(M=1\), with \[ R=k[[M-1]],\quad \kappa=M-M^{-1},\quad \kappa_N=M^N-M^{-N},\quad u_N=\kappa_N/\kappa,\quad \varepsilon_N=(-1)^{N+1}. \] The quotient \(u_N\) is a Laurent polynomial and a unit in \(R\), with \(u_N(1)=N\). The actual cyclic Ward completion gives \[ A=R[e]/(e^N-\varepsilon_N\kappa_N),\qquad \sigma(e)=Qe. 	ag{1.1} \] The specified matrix realizes multiplication by \(e\), with its single missing-edge completion retained. Write \(\mathsf N=\operatorname{Norm}_{A/R}\) and \(\mathsf{Tr}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A/R}\). The exact norm is \[ \mathsf N(1+te)=1+\kappa_Nt^N. 	ag{1.2} \] These are the actual algebra and sign of [the cyclic Ward norm calculation](cyclic_ward_norm_adapter.md). The ideal \((e,\kappa)\) is topologically nilpotent, so logarithms of units congruent to \(1\) modulo this ideal are well defined in the completed order. No inverse of \(\kappa\) is taken in \(A\). ## 2. A divided-norm unit group and a genuine centralizer transfer Consider the unit dilatation with coordinates \[ u=(1+\kappa a_0)+a_1e+\cdots+a_{N-1}e^{N-1}. 	ag{2.1} \] Coefficients may lie in a complete \(R\)-algebra. Such \(u\) are units, because their reduction is a principal nilpotent unit. They are closed under multiplication and inversion. Moreover \(\mathsf N(u)\equiv1\pmod\kappa\). Retain the norm-root cover \[ 
u(u)^N=\mathsf N(u), \] and mark its identity sheet by \(
u(u)\equiv1\pmod\kappa\). Since \(N\) is invertible, Hensel recursion gives a unique such root in the completed identity chart. The other \(\mu_N\) sheets remain separate on the generic cover. Define \[  oxed{B(u)= rac{
u(u)-1}{\kappa}.} 	ag{2.2} \] This is regular on the unit dilatation. Its fully algebraic divided equation is \[  rac{\mathsf N(u)-1}{\kappa} =\sum_{j=1}^{N} inom Nj\kappa^{j-1}B(u)^j. 	ag{2.3} \] At \(\kappa=0\) the derivative in \(B\) is \(N\), so (2.3) also characterizes the completed identity-sheet map without formally dividing a zero equation by zero. Let the regular meridian centralizer be \[ J_M=\{C_M(b):1+\kappa b
e0\},\quad C_M(b)= egin{pmatrix}1+\kappa b&b\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad b*b'=b+b'+\kappa bb'. \] Then \[  oxed{\mathcal T_N:u\longmapsto C_M(B(u))} 	ag{2.4} \] is an actual group homomorphism. Indeed uniqueness of the marked root gives \(
u(uv)=
u(u)
u(v)\), and (2.2) gives the displayed centralizer law. It has the scalar section \[ C_M(b)\longmapsto (1+\kappa b)\,1_A. \] Its kernel is the marked norm-one unit group. Its generic dimension is \(N-1\); no group isomorphism with \(J_M\) is claimed. The source of (2.4) must retain the first normal coordinate \(a_0\). It is not merely the principal units of \(k[e]/e^N\). ## 3. The explicit first-normal affine class For the special fiber of the dilatation, multiplication has \[ a_0''=a_0+a_0' +\varepsilon_N N\sum_{i+j=N}a_i a_j', 	ag{3.1} \] while the nonconstant coefficients multiply by the ordinary truncated rule modulo \(e^N\). Formula (3.1) is the constant wrap term \(e^N=\varepsilon_N\kappa u_N\), divided by \(\kappa\). It is a specified central affine cocycle. Let \[ p(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}a_jz^j. \] The transfer (2.2) on this special fiber is the explicit additive character \[  oxed{B_0(u)=a_0+\varepsilon_N N[z^N]\log p(z).} 	ag{3.2} \] The coefficient is a finite polynomial: truncate the ordinary logarithm at degree \(N\). To prove (3.2), use \[ \log\mathsf N(u)=\mathsf{Tr}\log u,\quad \mathsf{Tr}(e^j)=0\ (N
mid j),\quad \mathsf{Tr}(e^N)=N\varepsilon_N\kappa_N. \] To first order in \(\kappa\), only the central term \(\kappa a_0\) and the degree-\(N\) logarithm coefficient can contribute. Thus \[ \log
u(u)=\kappa a_0+ \varepsilon_N\kappa_N[z^N]\log p(z)+O(\kappa^2), \] which proves the formula since \(u_N(1)=N\). For the literal missing-edge path \[ \alpha(t)=1+te \] it gives \(B_0(\alpha(t))=t^N\). This follows also from (1.2). The normal term is indispensable: all the units \(1+\kappa c\) reduce to \(1\) in \(k[e]/e^N\), but their transfer is the arbitrary value \(c\). Consequently no map on the **bare nilpotent special fiber** can recover (2.4). The first-normal extension removes this precise ambiguity. ## 4. The marked path maps to the actual meridian For \(\alpha(t)=1+te\), the transfer is \[  oxed{B(t)=  rac{(1+\kappa_Nt^N)^{1/N}-1}{\kappa},} 	ag{4.1} \] with the identity root retained. It satisfies \[ B(0)=0,\qquad B(t=M)=M. 	ag{4.2} \] Indeed \(1+\kappa_NM^N=M^{2N}\), whose marked root near \(M=1\) is \(M^2\); then \((M^2-1)/\kappa=M\). The endpoint \(C_M(M)\) is the original marked meridian in projective normalization. Thus this is an explicit transport of the relative path, not just its determinant value. The endpoint lift \(t=M\) uses the retained meridian marking. Other lifts \(t=\zeta M\), \(\zeta\in\mu_N\), have the same norm-quotient endpoint but need not have the same norm-one factorial gauge. They remain separate source lifts. The finite norm character alone does not select an internal knot cycle. The \(\mu_N\) marking matters. A root \(\zeta M^2\), \(\zeta
e1\), would give \(B=(\zeta M^2-1)/\kappa\), with a pole at completion. Such a sheet is not the regular identity chart. It has not been identified with the identity sheet or silently divided out. There is also an exact power-map diagram. The geometric adapter is \[ p_N:J_M\longrightarrow J_{M^N},\qquad p_N(b)= rac{(1+\kappa b)^N-1}{\kappa_N}. 	ag{4.3} \] The whole \(u_N\) is a unit near completion. By construction, \[  oxed{p_N(B(u))= rac{\mathsf N(u)-1}{\kappa_N},\qquad p_N(B(t))=t^N.} 	ag{4.4} \] The right side is regular before special evaluation. For (4.4) on a general unit, the norm-root cover is part of the input. ## 5. Exact invariant forms and the relative peripheral period The invariant centralizer form at fixed \(M\) is \[ \omega_M= rac{db}{1+\kappa b}. \] Pullback along (4.1) gives the exact identity \[  oxed{\mathcal T_N^*\omega_M = rac1{N\kappa}\,d_t\log\mathsf N(1+te) = rac{u_Nt^{N-1}}{1+\kappa_Nt^N}\,dt.} 	ag{5.1} \] This is regular at \(\kappa=0\), where it is \(Nt^{N-1}dt\). On the special fiber the transfer is \(b=t^N\), with its ramified \(\mu_N\) cover retained; one does not replace its differential by \(dt\). Use the marked relative path \(t=0\) to \(t=M\), with logarithm zero at the identity. Formal integration in \(R\), or continuation on the same marked logarithmic chart, gives \[  oxed{\int_0^M\mathcal T_N^*\omega_M = rac{\operatorname{Log}(M^{2N})}{N\kappa} = rac{\operatorname{Log}(M^2)}{\kappa}=L(M).} 	ag{5.2} \] Thus the cyclic Ward block carries the full required peripheral relative period, not merely its complete value or determinant. For the raw target \(J_{M^N}\), the invariant form pulls back as \[  rac{N t^{N-1}}{1+\kappa_Nt^N}\,dt. \] Its marked period is \(L(M^N)\). Comparing with (5.1) yields \[  oxed{p_N^*\omega_{M^N}= rac N{u_N}\omega_M,\qquad L(M^N)= rac N{u_N(M)}L(M).} 	ag{5.3} \] The whole peripheral factor is retained before evaluating the common zero. In particular \(L(1)=1\). The phase \(\eta_N=i^{N+3}\) of the actual modified dimension \(d_N=\eta_N/u_N\) remains its separately marked line; the norm-root \(\mu_N\) sheet and this phase are different data. The scalar logarithmic connection is also explicit. Its horizontal period \(Z=\kappa L\) has \[ dZ=2\,d\log M,\qquad Z(1)=0, \] or, in the divided frame, \[ dL=-L\,d\log\kappa+ rac{2\,d\log M}{\kappa}. 	ag{5.4} \] The selected regular solution is \(L=1-\kappa^2/24+O(\kappa^4)\). This is the peripheral logarithmic period; it is not the knot Bloch regulator or its undetermined constant. ## 6. The actual factorial affine source normalizes to this torsor The literal finite polynomial is \[ F(t,e)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} rac{(-te)^j}{(Q;Q)_j}. \] Its exact affine equation from the actual missing-edge completion is \[ \sigma F-(1+te)F=- rac{\kappa_Nt^N}{N}. 	ag{6.1} \] The norm-root \(
u=(1+\kappa_Nt^N)^{1/N}\) produces the norm-one transport coefficient \[ a(t,e)= rac{1+te}{
u}. \] It has \(\mathsf N(a)=1\). This normalization is forced for a homogeneous Hilbert--90 gauge: the unnormalized \(1+te\) has norm \(1+\kappa_Nt^N\), so it cannot be a cyclic coboundary generically. There is an explicit unique norm-one gauge lifting the actual nilpotent \(F\). Define \[ H(t,e)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}  rac{t^j e^j}{\prod_{r=1}^j(
u Q^r-1)},\qquad g=\mathsf N(H)^{-1/N}H, 	ag{6.2} \] with the scalar root marked by value one at \(\kappa=0\). Every denominator in (6.2) is a unit on that chart. Coefficient comparison gives \[ 
u\sigma H=(1+te)H. \] For the constant coefficient use \[ \prod_{r=0}^{N-1}(
u Q^r-1) =\varepsilon_N\kappa_N t^N; \] the other coefficients follow from their displayed recursion. Consequently \[  oxed{\sigma g=a g,\qquad \mathsf N(g)=1,\qquad g|_{\kappa=0}=F|_{\kappa=0}.} 	ag{6.3} \] For uniqueness, two gauges have \(\sigma\)-invariant ratio, which is scalar because \(1,e,\ldots,e^{N-1}\) are eigenvectors with distinct eigenvalues \(1,Q,\ldots,Q^{N-1}\). Its norm is its \(N\)-th power. The identity marking forces that ratio to be one. No disconnected constant phase is reset. The first-normal affine class is explicit: \[ \left. rac{\sigma F-(1+te)F}{\kappa}ight|_{\kappa=0} =-t^N=-B_0(1+te). 	ag{6.4} \] Thus the additive character of the unit dilatation is precisely the negative of the divided actual source at this order. One can also write the entire first-normal correction without an existence assertion. Let \(\epsilon=\kappa_N\), and use \(g=F+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)\) in the free basis. Put \(F_0=F mod\epsilon\). Then \[ (\sigma-1)(h/F_0) =- rac{t^N}{N}\left(1-(\sigma F_0)^{-1}ight). 	ag{6.5} \] The right side has zero constant coefficient in \(k[e]/e^N\). Its nonconstant coefficient of \(e^j\) is divided by \(Q^j-1\) to obtain \(h/F_0\). Its constant is fixed by the norm-one mark: \[ [e^0](h/F_0) =-\varepsilon_N[z^N]\log \left(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} rac{(-tz)^j}{(Q;Q)_j}ight). 	ag{6.6} \] Formula (6.6) follows from (3.2), since the central normal coefficient is \(N[e^0]h\) when \(\epsilon=u_N\kappa\). It retains the actual affine source, including the mixed algebra normal term \(e^N=\varepsilon_N\epsilon\). The relative \(t\)-connection of this norm-one gauge satisfies \[ (\sigma-1)d_t\log g =d_t\log(1+te)-d_t\log
u =\left( rac{e}{1+te} - rac{\kappa_Nt^{N-1}}{1+\kappa_Nt^N}ight)dt. 	ag{6.7} \] Its trace is zero. The removed scalar component is exactly the norm-root connection used in (5.1). ## 7. An exact limitation for the full external connection On \(A[\kappa^{-1}]\), the multiplicative Kummer connection is \[ 
abla e= rac eN\,d\log(\varepsilon_N\kappa_N). \] It is compatible with \(e^N=\varepsilon_N\kappa_N\), but is logarithmic at the nilpotent special fiber. There is no regular \(M\)-derivation of the order \(A\) extending \(d/dM\). Indeed such a derivation would give \[ Ne^{N-1}D(e)=(\varepsilon_N\kappa_N)'. \] Reducing at \(M=1\), the left side belongs to the nilpotent ideal \((e^{N-1})\) in \(k[e]/e^N\); the right side is the nonzero constant \(2N\varepsilon_N\). This is impossible. This no-go concerns a derivation compatible with multiplication; it does not rule out arbitrary regular connections on the underlying free module. The norm-root quotient has the regular connection \[ d\log
u= rac1N d\log(1+\kappa_Nt^N), \] and its divided relative form (5.1) extends. Thus the quotient and its first-normal source can carry the peripheral period even though a regular multiplicative full-block connection cannot. ## 8. Scope for the knot problem The rank-one missing edge, its factorial affine source, the norm-root torsor, the first-normal additive character, and the complete peripheral period now occur in one explicit transport diagram. Neither a group isomorphism nor a bare special-fiber identification was assumed. The relative path is the lift of the already specified meridian section. The norm-root quotient forgets a norm-one kernel of dimension \(N-1\); its peripheral period does not determine the kernel period or the knot state which couples to it. This is not yet a map from the actual knot's internal finite contraction to its geometric Gaussian block. In particular it does not identify its selected global source with the marked Bloch regulator or prove that the geometric contribution survives. Those assertions remain outside the norm-root peripheral theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.py). It passes 198 exact checks: 126 generic/first-normal factorial-gauge checks at \(N=2,\ldots,10\), 16 first-normal cocycle checks, and 56 peripheral form, period, and connection checks. No numerical asymptotic fitting is used.

title: A cyclotomic diagonal source and an actual endpoint-completed wall ladder
text: # A cyclotomic diagonal source and an actual endpoint-completed wall ladder Research proof, 27 October 2026. The degree-N binomial wall row can be coupled to the original head index by an intrinsic cyclotomic projector in an actual high integral color. Actual divided powers, together with their first-normal wrap entries, give an exact classical SL2 action on the resulting N+1-state string. The coupling is a controlled cyclic head-shift gauge, rather than an unspecified Kronecker insertion. This supplies an exact finite source/current realization. It does not make the projector commute with the original whole crossing. A literal first-normal charged crossing entry below proves that this stronger assertion fails. Whole gauge transport is exact if all crossings, pivots, sources and internal projectors are transported together. ## 1. Actual color, clocks and the diagonal constraint Use the integral color and constant sign basis of [the high-color source theorem](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md) with r=N. Its dimension is N(N+1), and its basis is w_(R,S), 0<=R<=N, 0<=S<N. Put q=q_N, Q=q_N^2, rho=q_N-q_N^(-1), delta=1-q^(2N), and let the head index and block index denote the literal diagonal matrices S and R in this fixed basis. They are actual color observables: the unwrapped index is J_un=NR+S, while Q^J_un=Q^S at the root. The distinct root eigenvalues determine S by spectral interpolation; then R=(J_un-S)/N. The cyclotomic charge and its zero projector are \[ C=Q^{R-S},\qquad P=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}C^\ell. \tag{1} \] The root geometric-series identity proves, on each basis vector, that P selects exactly \[ z_j=w_{j,j}\quad(0\le j<N),\qquad z_N=w_{N,0}. \tag{2} \] In particular this is an orthogonal rank-(N+1) projector in the constant sign basis. P, R and S have unambiguous constant matrix extensions in the original integral q-family. This extension makes no claim that their generic-q extensions are quantum intertwiners. ## 2. The wall row, including its endpoint and normalization Write e_+=psi_+ lambda_+ for the actual Frobenius coherent coupon, \[ \psi_+=\sum_{R=0}^{N}v_R,\qquad \lambda_+(v_R)=2^{-N}{N\choose R},\qquad \lambda_+\psi_+=1. \] The original head average is the rank-one coupon e_h=psi_h phi_h, where psi_h=sum_S v_S and phi_h(v_S)=1/N. Let e_prod=e_+ tensor e_h. This is the actual divided-coherent Frobenius source times the original head source; its Frobenius dual is binomial, and is not silently identified with a uniform average over the entire high color. Then \[ \operatorname{Tr}(e_{\mathrm{prod}}P)=\frac1N,\qquad e_D=NP e_{\mathrm{prod}}P. \tag{3} \] is an idempotent of trace one. Its source and co-source on (2) are exactly sum_j z_j and sum_j 2^(-N) binom(N,j) z_j^*. For any array J_0,...,J_N over a commutative coefficient algebra, use the actual diagonal insertion \[ \mathcal J=J(S)+(J_N-J_0)P_{R=N}, \tag{4} \] where J(S) has entries J_0,...,J_(N-1). Its restriction to (2) is diag(J_0,...,J_N). Consequently \[ \frac1N\operatorname{Tr}(e_D\mathcal J) =\operatorname{Tr}(e_{\mathrm{prod}}P\mathcal J) =\frac1{N2^N}\sum_{j=0}^{N}{N\choose j}J_j =B_N(J). \tag{5} \] This is the wall row from [the actual Gauss-wall current complex](actual_gauss_wall_cut_current_complex.md), with both its 1/N and its j=N endpoint. It applies coefficientwise to the original retained logarithmic/polynomial Green arrays. It is not a pointwise multiplication of coherent symbols. In that current complex the original arrays already contain 1/N: I_mat=N I_raw and J_mat=N J_raw. Thus (5) applies to J_mat; its raw version is N B_N(J_raw). This factor cannot be silently absorbed. The normalized source Tr(e_D C) returns the actual high-color knot scalar when C is its scalar long-knot operator. At the root this is the original K_N by the already proved all-color periodicity. The unnormalized wall source returns K_N/N. The old marked ADO/peripheral line and its full twists are retained; this construction does not replace them by a fictitious high-level normalization. There is no exponential source cost at the root. Directly, \[ \|\psi_D\|=\sqrt{N+1},\qquad \|\lambda_D\|^2=4^{-N}{2N\choose N}\le1, \qquad\|e_D\|\le\sqrt{N+1}. \tag{6} \] The same bound holds for its trace-functional norm. This is a root bound, not a bound on a growing normal neighborhood or on arbitrary quantum derivatives. This bound uses the constant coordinate metric. The [current/metric audit](frobenius_clock_and_internal_centralizer_map.md) also proves a polynomial bound for THIS selected anchor in the explicit tensor coherent metric, by exact binomial cancellation. It separately proves that the full controlled gauge, and other points of its real coherent orbit, can be exponentially conditioned in that metric. Thus (6) is not a uniform bound for an arbitrary period-line comparison or the whole coherent source family. ## 3. An exact SL2 ladder made from actual divided and normal entries Let e,f,h be the classical multiplicity matrices of the actual divided-power theorem, with \[ ev_R=(N-R+1)v_{R-1},\quad fv_R=(R+1)v_{R+1},\quad hv_R=(N-2R)v_R. \] Let V be the cyclic head shift S -> S+1 modulo N. Define the actual head spectral pseudoinverse \[ D^\dagger=\operatorname{diag}(0,[1]^{-1},\ldots,[N-1]^{-1}). \] Every displayed denominator is nonzero at the marked root. Integral divided multiplication and [N+1]_(q_N)=-1 give \[ E^{(N+1)}=e\otimes E_{\mathrm{St}},\qquad F^{(N+1)}=-f\otimes F_{\mathrm{St}}. \tag{7} \] Indeed E^(N)=(-1)^(N-1)e and ordinary E=(-1)^N E_St, and E^(N)E=[N+1]E^(N+1); the F identity is identical without the two E signs. The literal first-normal wrap matrices are \[ [E_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_0 =(-1)^{N+1}\rho^{-1}e\otimes E_{N-1,0},\qquad [F_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_0 =\rho^{-1}f\otimes E_{0,N-1}. \tag{8} \] Both are regular divisions in the original q-family, not divisions of zero root matrices. Combining (7) and (8) with the specified operator orders gives \[ \begin{split} \widetilde E &=E^{(N+1)}(I\otimes D^\dagger) +\rho(-1)^{N+1}[E_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_0 =e\otimes V^{-1},\\ \widetilde F &=-(I\otimes D^\dagger)F^{(N+1)} +\rho[F_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_0 =f\otimes V,\\ \widetilde H&=h\otimes I. \end{split} \tag{9} \] For example E_St D^dagger is the noncyclic unit backward shift; the first term misses only S=0, which (8) completes. For F the pseudoinverse acts on the OUTPUT, exactly as printed. Thus [Etilde,Ftilde]=Htilde and the other two SL2 relations hold on the WHOLE actual high-color vector space. All three commute with P. On its selected string they act as \[ \widetilde E z_j=(N-j+1)z_{j-1},\qquad \widetilde F z_j=(j+1)z_{j+1}. \tag{10} \] The missing last bulk link is supplied by the actual normal edges: F_cross/delta sends z_(N-1) to (N/rho)z_N, and E_cross/delta sends z_N to ((-1)^(N+1)/rho)z_(N-1). Equations (9)--(10), rather than a postulated auxiliary representation, therefore realize the entire N+1 wall-current string. Dividing the nonzero coefficients in (10) also gives the literal unit forward and backward current shifts, with their two endpoint projectors retained. ## 4. The coupling is an exact controlled-shift gauge Define the constant unitary permutation \[ G=\sum_{R=0}^{N}P_R\otimes V^R. \] Direct multiplication proves the simultaneous identities \[ \begin{split} G(e\otimes I)G^{-1}&=\widetilde E,& G(f\otimes I)G^{-1}&=\widetilde F,\\ G(I\otimes P_0)G^{-1}&=P,& G(e_+\otimes P_0)G^{-1}&=e_D,\\ GQ^SG^{-1}&=Q^{-R}Q^S,&GQ^RG^{-1}&=Q^R. \end{split} \tag{11} \] Thus this is also an explicit finite clock shear: the head clock becomes the inverse of the cyclotomic constraint charge. No classical geometric Egorov identification is inferred from (11). The root Fourier matrix with entries Q^(ST)/N sends psi_h to v_0 and phi_h to v_0^* under the inverse dual map. It maps e_h to P_0. It is a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix and has condition number one. Consequently H_0=G(I tensor Fourier) conjugates the divided-coherent product rank-one source exactly to e_D, including its off-diagonal entries. If every crossing is replaced by \[ R^{H_0}=(H_0\otimes H_0)R_{\mathrm{high}}(H_0^{-1}\otimes H_0^{-1}), \tag{12} \] and pivots, duals, coupons and internal projectors are conjugated with their endpoint H_0's, the full arbitrary word and all its q-jets are exactly gauge equivalent. This is ordinary finite matrix basis change in the actual integral family. It makes no assertion that P commutes with the original R, or that R^H already has the required geometric Gaussian/source comparison. ## 5. Literal whole source germs and an off-diagonal Ward adapter The generic integral divided matrices determine finite source germs Psi_S(q), Lambda_S(q), u_S(q)=Lambda_S Psi_S exactly as in the high-color source theorem; u_S(q_N)=1. Put \[ \Psi=\sum_S\Psi_S,\qquad \Lambda=\frac1N\sum_S\Lambda_S/u_S,\qquad e(q)=\Psi\Lambda,\qquad u_P(q)=\Lambda P\Psi. \] The distinct residue strings are disjoint, so Lambda Psi=1. Moreover u_P(q_N)=1/N. Thus the two WHOLE idempotent germs \[ a(q)=e(q)P/u_P(q),\qquad d(q)=Pe(q)P/u_P(q) \tag{13} \] are regular and have trace one. At the root d=e_D. On the actual generic scalar high-color long-knot operator, both return its exact scalar, with no discarded quantum jet. This comparison is with the SAME high color, not an off-root equality with the original color N. Their off-diagonal difference is an explicit Cartan Ward boundary. Set Delta=a-d and, in the original unwrapped position basis, define \[ B_{ij}=\frac{\Delta_{ij}}{i-j}\ (i\ne j),\qquad B_{ii}=0. \] The diagonal of Delta is identically zero, at every q in the germ. Consequently \[ \Delta=[J_{\mathrm{un}},B],\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(\Delta C)=-\operatorname{Tr}(B[J_{\mathrm{un}},C]) \tag{14} \] for EVERY matrix C. Hence the one-sided projected product source and the compressed source agree on weight-zero actual cut arrays, while their full off-diagonal Ward discrepancy has not been erased. The alternative whole germ G e_0(q) G^(-1), obtained by transporting one original residue-string coupon, has the same root as d(q). Its higher diagonal source weights generally differ: d samples the actual S=R mod N string, while G e_0 G^(-1) samples S=0 before transport. Their source and co-source ratios are regular units with root one. Those units and u_P must be carried when comparing whole jets; equality of their numerical root binomial rows does not remove them. These source units can also be retained by an EXPLICIT whole-germ gauge, rather than an unspecified choice of extension. Write v=Psi, w=Lambda, v_c=Pv and w_c=wP/u_P. Thus wv=w_c v_c=1 and d=v_c w_c. Put v_t=H_0v, w_t=wH_0^(-1), e_t=v_t w_t and \[ K(q)=v_cw_t+(I-d)(I-e_t). \tag{14a} \] The Fourier normalization specified in Section 4 gives v_t(q_N)=v_c(q_N) and w_t(q_N)=w_c(q_N), so K(q_N)=I. It is therefore a regular invertible matrix germ. Direct multiplication, using the four source normalizations, proves \[ Kv_t=v_c,\qquad w_cK=w_t,\qquad K e_tK^{-1}=d. \tag{14b} \] Consequently H(q)=K(q)H_0 transports that actual divided-coherent whole source to the compressed source exactly. Conjugating every crossing, pivot, dual, coupon and internal projector by H(q) gives an exact whole-word source comparison, including all source-normal derivatives and the unit u_P. This is a same-color gauge theorem. It neither equates the high and original low-color q-jets nor establishes the geometric Gaussian image of the transformed word. Only H(q_N), not its behavior on a growing q-neighborhood, has the polynomial cost established above. There is also an explicit adapter if the incoming high-color coupon is the uniform average in this fixed basis. On the Frobenius factor put lambda_av(v_R)=1/(N+1), and write lambda_bin=lambda_+. Then \[ K_{\mathrm{Fr}}=I+\psi_+(\lambda_{\mathrm{av}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bin}}),\qquad K_{\mathrm{Fr}}^{-1}=I-\psi_+(\lambda_{\mathrm{av}}-\lambda_{\mathrm{bin}}). \tag{14c} \] The rank-one correction squares to zero, since both rows pair with psi_+ to one. It fixes the source vector and sends the uniform coupon to the binomial coupon by conjugation. Both K_Fr and its inverse have norm O(sqrt(N+1)). Tensoring with the head identity and using the same near-identity construction (14a) joins the constant uniform source to the actual divided-coherent WHOLE germ. Composing it with H(q) therefore retains the precise incoming source, including all its normal jets. If a different integral/balanced basis is used, its actual source adapter must first be included; (14c) is not a license to replace its off-diagonal row by an average. All these conjugations compare the high color with itself. ## 6. An actual mixed-normal crossing changes the total charge The entire root crossing commutes with the TOTAL charge C tensor C, although it need not preserve the individual zero-charge projectors. The original first-normal crossing need not even preserve total zero charge. Here is an explicit entry of the actual positive R. Take input (R_1,S_1)=(1,0), (R_2,S_2)=(N-1,0), and transfer k=1. Its total root charge is zero. The un-checked output is (0,N-1),(N-1,1), whose total charge is -1 modulo N. The transfer coefficient has exactly one normal zero, and \[ [R_{\mathrm{entry}}/\delta]_0 =(-1)^{N+1}N\, q_N^{H_{N-1}H_{N(N-1)+1}/2}\ne0, \tag{15} \] where H_i=m-2i and the common half-Cartan character is exactly the one in the original R. This follows directly from the E wrap coefficient (-1)^(N+1)N/rho, the nonzero F head coefficient [1]=1, and the k=1 nilpotent coefficient rho. Checked R only swaps its output factors and has the same total charge defect. Thus deleting all charged neighbors at first normal order changes an actual crossing coefficient. A full-source current theorem cannot silently apply P before and after each original crossing. There is nevertheless an exact bounded-charge filtration. For any transfer k=aN+b, 0<=b<N, write the two possible head carries as c_E=1_(S_1<b) and c_F=1_(S_2+b>=N). Then \[ \Delta(R_1+R_2)=c_F-c_E\in\{-1,0,1\},\qquad \Delta(S_1+S_2)=-N(c_F-c_E). \tag{16} \] The total charge change modulo N is therefore c_F-c_E. More precisely the E^k path has a+c_E simple block zeros, the F^k path has a+c_F, and the denominator [k]! has a. Thus a nonzero entry has exact delta-order a+c_E+c_F. In particular every nonzero charge change costs at least one normal order; this conclusion retains the denominator zeros rather than counting only numerator edges. A product of actual crossing jets of total normal order B can consequently move the total charge by at most B. The same follows for inverse crossings from the exact inverse series, since the root crossing and its inverse have charge zero. For N>2B these neighbors have distinct residue labels. Diagonal pivots do not change this conclusion. This is a support statement for actual braid-word jets, not a claim that their zero-charge component or boundary cohomology vanishes. The resonant tail E^(N) tensor F^(N) has zero total charge. It does not cancel the mixed charged entry (15). The actual quadratic Frobenius-degree theorem in [the first-normal crossing note](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md) is compatible with this filtration and retains precisely these mixed terms. ## 7. Exact scope and audit We have constructed the wall-row source on an intrinsic constrained subspace of an actual color, its exact endpoint-completed ladder, its full finite gauge transport, and its literal whole source germ. Equation (14) keeps the off-diagonal source-current correction. Equation (15) isolates why the source projector alone is not a whole-network intertwiner. The missing step is to transport the actual two framing currents through the resulting charged/source complex into the geometric Gaussian/relative complex, with the peripheral endpoint class retained. Neither the normalized source nor the finite SL2 string alone supplies that map. [The audit](../experiments/audit_cyclotomic_diagonal_wall_current_source.py) checks actual integral divided entries and actual first-normal wrap entries independently, the exact source and gauge identities, Cartan boundary (14), wall endpoints, and actual charged crossing entry (15). Its checks are exact finite-field identities, not a topological or asymptotic inference. The saved [results](../experiments/cyclotomic_diagonal_wall_current_source_results.json) pass seven actual colors N=2,...,8 and four full actual crossing families N=2,...,5. They include 1708 nonzero charged first-normal entries. Those entries support, rather than remove, the retained charged-sector obstruction.

title: Uniform descent of a rank-one comparison by divisor flow
text: # Uniform descent of a rank-one comparison by divisor flow Research note, 27 October 2026. This proves cases of the proposed cyclotomic rigidity mechanism without assuming bounded degree for the levelwise Hilbert-90 gauges. The hypotheses are instead a fixed split divisor presentation, or an unramified nonresonant algebraic divisor presentation, of the generic rank-one comparison coefficient. Cyclic transport detects its divisor charges; a finite flow solves the comparison and gives an explicit bound on its support. This is a theorem about comparison lines, not about the entire quantum A-module of a knot. No claim is made that the missing actual/geometric comparison line already has the presentation or norm compatibility required here. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. The literature category is cyclotomic q-curvature For coverage, the abstract of [Di Vizio--Hardouin, 1205.1692](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1692) describes a generic difference-Galois group through specializations of q at roots of unity. Their [parameterized version, 1205.1694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1694) also records the differential structure. These are closer to the user's proposed cyclotomic rigidity question than a scalar norm equation at one root. Neither theorem nor proof is used below. Only this coverage and the original meaning of cyclic transport are invoked; all implications needed for our restricted statement are proved directly. Use the actual parameters q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and the even meridian Y=M^2. Let sigma(Y)=QY, with q fixed. For a rank-one coefficient a(q,Y), its cyclic transport at level N is C_N(Y)=product_(j=0)^(N-1) a(q_N,Q_N^j Y), Q_N=q_N^2. (1.1) For a comparison line, C_N=1 means that the two compared norm characters agree, with the full meridian function retained. This is a whole rational identity, not only its value at Y=1. ## 2. A fixed split-divisor class Assume a has the fixed finite presentation a(q,Y)=c(q) Y^s product_(c,u) (1-c q^(2u)Y)^(n_(c,u)), (2.1) where c(q) is a nonzero rational function of q, s and the n_(c,u) are integers, u ranges through finitely many integers, and the distinct labels c are nonzero complex constants. In particular c is not an unknown function of q or Y. We distinguish the scalar c(q) from the finitely many constant labels in the product. The factors are whole functions on q,Y before root specialization. This class includes finite products of linear factors in known q-shift orbits, with arbitrary integer multiplicities and composite root levels. It is not every rational function of q,Y. A general zero algebraic over C(q) need not be c q^(2u). **Divisor-descent theorem.** Suppose C_N(Y)=1 in C(Y) for every sufficiently large N. Then s=0 and sum_u n_(c,u)=0 for every distinct label c, c(q)=q^(2k) for an integer k. (2.2) There is a rational function f(q,Y), independent of N, such that a(q,Y)=sigma(f)/f. (2.3) It can be constructed explicitly. Put e_(c,u)=-sum_(v<=u) n_(c,v), f(q,Y)=Y^k product_(c,u)(1-c q^(2u)Y)^(e_(c,u)). (2.4) The e have finite support because their total charges vanish. No bound or coherence for separately chosen root-level gauges is assumed. The original fixed divisor data give the bound afterward. ## 3. Proof of the divisor and constant statements Set U=Y^N. The elementary finite product gives product_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-c Q_N^(u+j)Y)=1-c^N U, product_(j=0)^(N-1) Q_N^j Y=(-1)^(N-1)U. Writing m_c=sum_u n_(c,u), the hypothesis is exactly c(q_N)^N (-1)^(s(N-1)) U^s product_c(1-c^N U)^(m_c)=1. (3.1) All factors after U^s are units at U=0. Hence s=0, and evaluating at U=0 gives c(q_N)^N=1. It follows also that product_c(1-c^N U)^(m_c)=1. (3.2) There are infinitely many N for which the finitely many c^N are pairwise distinct. To see this, a collision requires that a ratio c/c' be a root of unity of order dividing N. Let L be the least common multiple of all these finitely many torsion orders, or one if there are none. Every N coprime to L avoids all collisions. Choose such a sufficiently large N. The distinct linear factors in (3.2) force every m_c=0. Here is a direct proof of the scalar assertion, including its half-root convention. The identity |c(q_N)|=1 excludes a zero or pole of c at q=1. Choose an analytic logarithm ell(q) near one and set L_N=N ell(exp(pi*i/N)) in 2pi*i Z. Expansion of the fixed analytic function, rather than separate level functions, gives L_N=N ell(1)+pi*i ell'(1)+O(1/N). Therefore L_(N+1)-L_N=ell(1)+O(1/N^2). These differences belong to the discrete set 2pi*i Z, so ell(1) belongs to that set and c(1)=1. Choose the logarithm with ell(1)=0. Now L_N converges in the same discrete set and is eventually 2pi*i k for a fixed integer k. Thus c(q_N)=q_N^(2k) for all sufficiently large N. The rational function c(q)-q^(2k) has infinitely many zeros, so c(q)=q^(2k) identically. This proves (2.2). The assumption of all sufficiently large levels matters here; an arbitrary subsequence need not fix the scalar character. ## 4. The remaining equation is a finite flow For each c the vertices are u in Z and the edge u->u+1 carries the flow e_(c,u). Equation (2.4) solves the divergence equation n_(c,u)=e_(c,u-1)-e_(c,u). (4.1) The vanishing of total charge is exactly the condition for a finite-support flow. Since sigma(1-cQ^uY)=1-cQ^(u+1)Y, equation (4.1) proves the product part of (2.3), and sigma(Y^k)/Y^k=Q^k gives its scalar part. If the u support for label c is between u_min and u_max, at most u_max-u_min flow factors are needed. Their total absolute exponent is at most (u_max-u_min) sum_u |n_(c,u)|. (4.2) Together with |k| this bounds the Y degrees of the rational gauge by the fixed input data. This is one way to supply the bounded comparison space required by [the whole-period reconstruction theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md). It is a divisor-flow condition, rather than a nilpotence assumption on the entire braid image. For a rank-one module T e=a e, the new frame e'=f^(-1)e satisfies T e'=e'. The remaining ambiguity in f over C(q,Y) is multiplication by C(q)^*: a rational sigma-invariant in Y has no finite nonzero pole, since its q^2 orbit would be infinite; it is Laurent in Y, and invariance then leaves only its constant term. A specified regular generic anchor fixes this scalar. Root-level central functions of Y^N have not been silently identified with generic difference constants. ### An extension to moving algebraic zeros and poles The fixed labels in (2.1) can be replaced by more general algebraic functions under a finite nonresonance condition. This supplies a second, broader sufficient condition for the comparison line.
