Write a rational coefficient, over its algebraic splitting field, as a(q,Y)=r(q)Y^s product_(i=1)^d (1-alpha_i(q)Y) /product_(j=1)^e (1-beta_j(q)Y). (4.3) Assume every alpha_i,beta_j is holomorphic and nonzero near q=1. They may coincide at q=1; the hypothesis is an unramified choice of the individual branches, not distinctness of all limiting roots. Let C be the set of their distinct values at q=1. Assume c!=c' in C => c^k!=c'^k for 1<=k<=max(d,e). (4.4) Thus distinct limiting values have no root-of-unity ratio of these bounded orders. This is a finite condition. It is automatic if all branches have the same limiting value, or if all distinct limiting values are positive real numbers. **Unramified divisor-descent theorem.** Under (4.3)--(4.4), the identity C_N(Y)=1 for every sufficiently large N implies s=0, d=e, r(q)=q^(2k_0), and a pairing of the branches such that alpha_i(q)=q^(2k_i) beta_(pi(i))(q), k_i in Z. (4.5) Consequently a=sigma(f)/f with f in C(q,Y)^*. Its Y-degree can be bounded by |k_0|+sum_i |k_i|. In particular no prior bound for root-level gauges is required. The integer shifts are read from the fixed algebraic branches: k_i=(alpha_i'(1)/alpha_i(1) -beta_(pi(i))'(1)/beta_(pi(i))(1))/2. (4.6) Here the derivatives and the nonresonance condition are in the quantum parameter q. Classical etaleness of shapes over the meridian does not automatically imply these quantum hypotheses. We first prove an elementary uniqueness lemma. If c_1,...,c_h are distinct nonzero complex numbers and F_i(t) are meromorphic germs at zero, then sum_i c_i^N F_i(1/N)=0 for all large N (4.7) forces every F_i=0. Indeed, among nonzero F_i choose those with largest |c_i|=R, and among these the least Laurent order m. Divide (4.7) by R^N N^(-m). It follows that sum a_i omega_i^N tends to zero, where omega_i=c_i/R are distinct points of the unit circle and at least one leading coefficient a_i is nonzero. Multiplying by omega_j^(-N) and taking Cesaro means gives a_j=0: each other geometric sum has mean zero and the error tends to zero. This contradicts the choice of m. It proves (4.7), including roots-of-unity ratios between the c_i. To prove the theorem, the full norm identity first gives s=0, r(q_N)^N=1 and equality of the multisets alpha_i(q_N)^N and beta_j(q_N)^N. Hence d=e; the scalar proof in Section 3 gives r(q)=q^(2k_0). Fix the logarithms of alpha_i(q)/alpha_i(1) and beta_j(q)/beta_j(1) with value zero at q=1. For a branch with limiting value c put A_i(t)=exp(Log(alpha_i(exp(pi*i*t))/c)/t), B_j(t)=exp(Log(beta_j(exp(pi*i*t))/c)/t). (4.8) These are holomorphic units at t=0 because their logarithm numerators vanish there. The k-th power-sum equality is sum_(c in C) (c^k)^N [sum_(alpha_i(1)=c) A_i(1/N)^k -sum_(beta_j(1)=c) B_j(1/N)^k]=0. For 1<=k<=d, (4.4) makes the bases c^k distinct. Lemma (4.7) therefore gives equality of the bracketed holomorphic functions, separately for each c and k. Newton identities, padding each multiset to d elements with zeros, give equal multisets of the A_i and B_j as meromorphic germs. They are units, so the numbers of branches at each c agree. A fixed pairing satisfies A_i(t)=B_(pi(i))(t) identically. The exponent of their quotient in (4.8) is a holomorphic function whose exponential is one. It is a constant 2pi*i k_i. Thus Log(alpha_i(q)/beta_(pi(i))(q))=2k_i Log q, proving (4.5) as an identity of algebraic branches and giving (4.6). For k_i>0 the corresponding rational gauge over the splitting field is product_(u=0)^(k_i-1)(1-q^(2u) beta_(pi(i))(q)Y). For k_i<0 use the inverse product over k_i<=u<0. Their product, times Y^(k_0), gives the stated degree bound. This gauge descends to C(q,Y). Its finite divisor flow is the unique finite-support solution on each infinite q-shift orbit. Uniqueness makes that divisor invariant under the Galois group of the splitting field. The product part has value one at Y=0, so its normalization is Galois invariant as well. Its coefficients therefore lie in C(q); Y^(k_0) is already rational. This completes the proof without a general q-curvature theorem. ## 5. Tests which prevent incorrect descent If only even N are used, the scalar a=-1 has C_N=1 but has no nonzero rational generic gauge for sigma(Y)=q^2Y. If f(q^2Y)/f(Y)=-1, a finite divisor is shift-invariant and hence f is a Laurent monomial; its ratio is q^(2k), a contradiction. Likewise the rational coefficient a(q,Y)=(1-q^2 Y^2)/(1-Y^2) (5.1) has C_N=1 at every odd N, but at even N its transport is C_N=((1+U)/(1-U))^2. (5.2) Indeed the exponent 2 orbit has size N/gcd(2,N). Thus odd-level agreement alone does not justify generic descent. Formula (5.2) is also a concrete reason to retain the peripheral factors 1+U before evaluating U=1. The half-step factor (1-qY)/(1-Y) has transport (1+U)/(1-U) at every actual q_N: q_N^N=-1, whereas Q_N^N=1. It is not in the class (2.1). Its two norm characters must be retained, just as in the actual bridge-source calculation. There is a stronger warning for the exact chosen half-root family. The rational coefficient a_*(q,Y)=(1-Y)(1-qY)/[(1+Y)(1+qY)] (5.3) has C_N=1 for every N at q_N=exp(pi*i/N), with no parity exception. Its numerator norm is (1-U)(1+U), while its denominator norm is (1-(-1)^N U)(1-(-1)^(N+1) U), the same product. Nevertheless a_* is not sigma(f)/f for any nonzero rational f(q,Y). Normalize a hypothetical f by its q-1 valuation. At q=1 it then has a finite nonzero value in C(Y). Since sigma(Y)=q^2Y tends to Y, sigma(f)/f specializes to one. But a_*(1,Y)=((1-Y)/(1+Y))^2 is not one. This does not contradict either descent theorem here. The roots in (5.3) include q-shifts outside (2.1), and its limiting labels 1,-1 violate (4.4). Nor is it evidence against a correctly parameterized general q-curvature theorem. The selected q_N family contains only even orders of q. At q=-q_N with N odd, which has odd order N, the same cyclic transport is ((1-U)/(1+U))^2 and detects the obstruction. Thus all selected root values alone still do not determine a generic comparison. One must supply the additional parameter symmetry or cyclotomic places, a proved divisor condition, or the bounded quantum-normal comparison required by the whole- period reconstruction theorem. The even parameter Q=q^2 and the retained half-root sign must be distinguished explicitly. In particular finite-lift evenness is not an assumed symmetry of an unknown minimal generic operator. There is a constructive way to choose the smaller parameter for the actual reduced state. The new argument in [the even-meridian note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md#a-nonzero-actual-annihilator-can-nevertheless-be-chosen-over-qq2) applies the finite-sum annihilator proof directly to its statewise even closed lift, with base Q and central variable Q^N. It supplies a specified nonzero actual operator over Q(Q,Y), with shift Y->QY. This is an existence result, not the asserted q-sign stability of the previous half-root minimal operator. The full ADO Tate/sign line remains separate and unchanged. An unknown comparison still must be placed over the correctly marked field and lattice. The gauge (2.4) can have a zero or pole at the ideal meridian. Its generic existence does not authorize deleting that divisor or changing the marked normal functional. It must be transported in the specified integral lattice. Once a comparison is a unit of the correct marked line and is fixed algebraic across levels, the existing central normalization theorem controls its norm. This note does not infer that unit condition from (2.3). ## 6. What this contributes to the knot program This supplies uniform Hilbert-90 descent theorems for the stated classes of rank-one coefficients. They start from all-level cyclic transport, derive a bounded global gauge, and give its explicit divisor flow. The proof is independent of knot-by-knot examples and of the published q-curvature proofs. To use it for the desired comparison, one still has to construct that comparison line from the actual pointed quantum A-object, prove its split divisor presentation or an appropriate extension, and match its cyclic norm characters with all peripheral factors. Rivin's algebraic geometric place is available but does not alone supply these quantum hypotheses. The regulator connection and selected source must still be retained. No volume theorem follows just from the vanishing of a rational norm-one comparison class. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_cyclotomic_divisor_descent.py). [Results](../experiments/cyclotomic_divisor_descent_results.json).

title: The actual Fourier--Mellin period has a cyclotomic residue
text: # The actual Fourier--Mellin period has a cyclotomic residue Research note, 27 October 2026. The actual operator and finitely many fixed-color values define a bounded-source Fourier--Mellin object. At every root its selected section has a rational continuation with only simple finite cyclotomic poles. Its residue at infinity is exactly the original Kashaev invariant, with no jet-rank assumption. The color-periodicity input is proved directly from integral Weyl modules and the original root ribbon evaluation. It is not assumed from a cyclotomic expansion or used as a Jones asymptotic theorem. The geometric regulator norm of this residue remains unproved. ## 1. The specified operator period Use the actual reduced fixed-color functions C_n(Q) of [the color-pointing theorem](all_level_a_period.md), with Q=q^2, and C_n(1)=1. The [Fourier--Mellin construction](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md) gives, from a specified actual operator and a fixed starting color n_0, Z(Q,X)=sum_(n>=n_0) C_n(Q) X^n, P^M Z=B(Q,X), (1.1) where P^M is the quantum-torus transform Y->S_X,T->X^(-1), S_X f(X)=f(QX). The nonzero Laurent polynomial B uses only the d fixed colors C_(n_0),...,C_(n_0+d-1). The formal lattice Z in X^(n_0) ℚ(Q)[[X]] makes this source equation unique. For N>=n_0 the selected period is already K_N=[X^N]Z(Q_N,X), Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N). (1.2) This note promotes its root fiber to a whole rational function and identifies its exact residue. The generic section in (1.1) is still defined formally; convergence at generic Q is not asserted. ## 2. Integral Weyl colors specialize through all dimensions On D_m with basis u_0,...,u_m use H u_j=(m-2j)u_j, K u_j=q^(m-2j)u_j, E u_j=[m-j+1]_q u_(j-1), F u_j=[j+1]_q u_(j+1). (2.1) These are the same integral colors used in the independently proved [threading calculation](ado_threaded_shadow.md). At q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), E^N=F^N=0 on every D_m, including m>=N. The generic universal R also specializes correctly on these colors. Indeed a coefficient of E^k tensor F^k divided by [k]_q! on u_a tensor u_b has its factorial part [k]_q! {m-a+k choose k}_q {b+k choose k}_q. (2.2) The Gaussian coefficients are Laurent polynomials. Thus every term with k>=N vanishes at the root, while each k<N term is precisely the original truncated root R. The inverse has the same property. Cartan phases are nonzero and retained. This proves specialization without dividing by [N] or evaluating a singular change of basis. The generic zero-framed long-knot operator on D_(n-1) is C_n(Q) times identity. Its regular specialization is therefore the scalar C_n(Q_N) on the integral root module. The original ordinary pivot K may be replaced by g=K^(1-N) here: on D_m they differ by the scalar (-1)^m, as do their twists. A b-strand knot of writhe w consequently has unchanged reduced scalar, since (-1)^(m(b-1-w))=1. This retains the root ribbon conventions needed to compare with the ADO color. For clarity the long-knot operator is natural under an intertwiner of its color. Follow the single component from its cut and multiply the universal R legs, antipodes and pivot factors in their traversal order. The result acts on each color; no independently colored closed component remains. Every intertwiner commutes with these actions. Equivalently, sliding its coupon along crossings and bends uses exactly R-naturality and the evaluation/coevaluation identities. Thus a nonzero color map between two scalar long-knot operators forces equality of their scalars. The matrix specialization in (2.2) makes this argument valid for root subquotients as well. ## 3. One-dimensional shifts preserve the reduced zero-framed knot Let C_h be the one-dimensional root module with H=h,K=q^h,E=F=0, where h=kN. On an integer-weight color V with weights m-2j its double braiding is the scalar q^(hH)=(-1)^(km). (3.1) Here is a direct statewise proof retaining its half-Cartan phase. Tensoring V on the right by C_h changes E to (-1)^k E, leaves F unchanged, adds h to H and multiplies K by (-1)^k. Put s_0=q^(h^2/2)(-1)^(km), g_h=q^((1-N)h) in {+1,-1}. The exact full checked crossing, on a route with first input index a and first output index c, changes by r'_sign/r_sign=s_0^sign (-1)^(k(c-a)). (3.2) Indeed the Cartan phase supplies q^(h^2/2)(-1)^(k(m-a-b)) and the k_transfer-th nilpotent term supplies (-1)^(k k_transfer). The actual index update makes a+b+k_transfer congruent to c-a modulo two for both crossing signs. Inverse crossings give the inverse constant s_0 and the same state sign. The integer position coboundary gives sum(c-a)=0 on every closed state. Thus all state-dependent signs in (3.2) cancel. The crossing constants contribute s_0^w, the closed pivots contribute g_h^(b-1), and the twist ratio is (s_0 g_h)^w. Their total is g_h^(b-1-w)=1. (3.3) This proves that the reduced zero-framed knot scalar is unchanged by tensoring with C_(kN). No auxiliary closed component or its quantum dimension has been inserted. In particular the full Cartan half-phase cancels with its specified twist before any root value is suppressed. ## 4. Exact root periodicity, including multiples of N Write n=kN+r, 0<=r<N. If r>0, the span of u_r,...,u_(n-1) is a submodule of D_(n-1): its first E coefficient is [n-r]=[kN]=0. The quotient on u_0,...,u_(r-1) is exactly D_(r-1) tensor C_(kN). (4.1) The E coefficients are (-1)^k[r-j], the F coefficients are [j+1], and the H and K shifts agree with the displayed tensor product. Naturality and Section 3 therefore give C_n(Q_N)=C_r(Q_N). If r=0, the first N basis vectors instead form a submodule: F u_(N-1)=[N]u_N=0. This submodule is D_(N-1) tensor C_((k-1)N). (4.2) The N-dimensional D_(N-1) is the actual Kashaev color after a unit rescaling by [j]_q!, j<N. Hence C_n(Q_N)=C_N(Q_N)=K_N. All maps use nonzero subquotients; no quantum dimension is divided out at a multiple of N. We have proved, for every knot and every N>=2, C_(n+N)(Q_N)=C_n(Q_N), n>=1, C_(kN)(Q_N)=K_N, k>=1. (4.3) Combining this with the original finite-color identity for 1<=r<N gives the uniform meridian form C_n(Q_N)=F_N(Q_N^n), n>=1. (4.4) The fixed-color functions are Laurent polynomials in Q with rational coefficients. Galois conjugation therefore gives the corresponding identities at every primitive Q-root. This does not alter the full ADO parity/Tate line; (4.3) concerns the reduced scalar. For coverage, periodic root values are part of the existing cyclotomic-color framework: see [Le, Section 4.8](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf) and [Murakami, 1606.00125](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00125) for explicit low-order periodic patterns. No cyclotomic integrality or periodicity proof from those sources is a premise above. ## 5. The rational fiber and its residue Define the canonical start-one series Z_1(Q,X)=sum_(n>=1)C_n(Q)X^n. Equation (4.3) gives its root rational continuation exactly: Z_1(Q_N,X) =[sum_(r=1)^(N-1) C_r(Q_N) X^r+K_N X^N]/(1-X^N). (5.1) Equality holds first as formal series at X=0 and hence as its specified rational function. For any fixed n_0>=1, Z(Q_N,X)=Z_1(Q_N,X)-sum_(r=1)^(n_0-1) C_r(Q_N)X^r. (5.2) Thus it has at most simple poles at the N-th roots of unity. The subtracted polynomial has no constant term. Since Z_1 tends to -K_N at infinity, the residue convention Res_infinity(dX/X)=-1 gives the exact operator-period identity K_N=Res_(X=infinity) Z(Q_N,X) dX/X =-sum_(gamma^N=1) Res_(X=gamma) Z(Q_N,X) dX/X. (5.3) It is also the normalized sum of values of the numerator in (5.1): each finite residue is -P_N(gamma)/N and root orthogonality kills all r=1,...,N-1 terms. The identity includes the case K_N=0. This gives a genuine whole rational root fiber of the specified bounded-source A-object. If its Fourier operator is defined at Q_N, it satisfies P^M_N Z=B_N as a rational identity, because the formal source identity specializes coefficientwise and rational functions with the same formal expansion agree. No new solution is selected after specialization. Uniqueness is the generic source/lattice statement of Section 1, not an assumed invertibility of the singular root operator. The full original ADO value at the ideal meridian remains eta_N K_N/N, eta_N=i^(N+3). The residue formula is for the reduced scalar K_N; it does not remove this marked normalization line. ## 6. The volume target in this polarization For the very same source-defined solution, the desired theorem is lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|Res_infinity Z(Q_N,X)dX/X|=Vol(S^3 minus K). (6.1) Equation (5.3) proves that this is exactly the original conjecture. It does not prove (6.1). The Fourier symbol is the transform of the actual chosen operator's symbol; its geometric component and the selected residue's regulator norm still require proof. A root pole or a rational continuation alone gives no exponential lower bound. [Exact independent module/state audit](../experiments/audit_cyclotomic_mellin_residue.py). [Results](../experiments/cyclotomic_mellin_residue_results.json).

title: Independent check of integral-color periodicity and the residue
text: # Independent check of integral-color periodicity and the residue Audit, 27 October 2026. I checked the general proof in [the residue construction](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md), independently of its finite examples. The subquotient and residue arguments check out. The one-dimensional-shift step has the following direct statewise proof, which avoids a possible ambiguity about cutting both tensor factors in a parallel-link argument. ## 1. Direct framing calculation for the one-dimensional shift Let V be an integer-weight root color of parity m, with weights m-2a, and let h=kN. On V tensor C_h the displayed coproduct gives H'=H+h, K'=(-1)^k K, E'=(-1)^k E, F'=F. Use the original full R, retaining its Cartan scalar and the fixed square-root phase. Put s_0=q^(h^2/2)(-1)^(km), g_h=q^((1-N)h). At a positive crossing the first output is c=b+u. The E^u factor changes by (-1)^(ku), while the Cartan factor changes by q^(h^2/2) q^(h(m-a-b)). Their product is exactly s_0(-1)^(k(c-a)). At a negative crossing the Cartan factor is inverse and c=b-u; its exact multiplier is s_0^(-1)(-1)^(k(c-a)). Thus for either sign, r'_sign/r_sign=s_0^sign (-1)^(k(c-a)), (1.1) meaning equality after multiplication even when a coefficient is zero. On every closed state sum(c-a)=0, by the original integer position coboundary. The crossing contribution is therefore s_0^w. The pivot on each closed strand changes by g_h. The ribbon twist changes by s_0 g_h, either directly from its weight formula or from theta_(V tensor C_h)=theta_V theta_(C_h) times the scalar double braiding (-1)^(km). Hence the reduced zero-framed knot multiplier is s_0^w g_h^(b-1)(s_0 g_h)^(-w) =g_h^(b-1-w)=1. (1.2) Here g_h is a sign and b-1-w is even for a knot braid. There is no closed auxiliary-component quantum dimension. This proves the required one-dimensional-shift invariance in the original root ribbon conventions, including its phase and pivot. ## 2. Integral specialization and subquotient naturality On D_m the coefficient of the generic R term of order u has the factor [u]! times two Gaussian coefficients, after multiplying the E^u and F^u matrix entries and dividing by [u]!. The Gaussian coefficients are Laurent polynomials. Every u>=N term therefore vanishes at the root, and u<N terms are the exact truncated root R. The inverse works the same way. This justifies specialization of the generic scalar long-knot operator even when m>=N. The ordinary pivot and root pivot differ by (-1)^m, as do their twists, so the reduced zero-framed scalar is unchanged. The root long-knot operator is natural for H,E,F,K intertwiners: the full R, inverse, evaluations, coevaluations and pivot are all natural, and a coupon can be followed along the single cut component. Consequently a nonzero inclusion or quotient between scalar root long-knot operators forces equality of their scalars. No division by a zero quantum dimension is involved. For n=kN+r, 0<r<N, the quotient of D_(n-1) on its first r vectors has E coefficient (-1)^k[r-j], unchanged F coefficient [j+1], and shifted H,K. This is exactly D_(r-1) tensor C_(kN) with the stated coproduct. The killed tail is a submodule because its boundary E coefficient is [kN]=0. For n=kN, the first N vectors form a submodule because its outgoing F coefficient is [N]=0. Its E coefficient is (-1)^(k-1)[N-j], so it is D_(N-1) tensor C_((k-1)N). The rescaling by [j]!, j<N, identifies D_(N-1) with the actual Kashaev color by unit entries. Together with (1.2) this proves the all-color periodicity claimed in the construction, including multiples of N. ## 3. The residue for an arbitrary fixed tail The periodic root series is [sum_(r=1)^(N-1)C_r X^r+K_N X^N]/(1-X^N). Its constant term at infinity is -K_N. Removing the initial colors up to any fixed n_0-1 subtracts a polynomial with no constant term; it does not change the residue against dX/X at infinity. Thus the infinity residue is K_N for every such tail. The finite residue at gamma^N=1 is -P_N(gamma)/N, since gamma times the derivative of 1-X^N there is -N. Root orthogonality makes their sum -K_N. There is no additional pole at X=0 because the selected tail starts in positive degree. For n_0>1 the rational function can acquire a higher-order pole at infinity from that subtracted polynomial. The statement about simple cyclotomic poles concerns its finite poles. This causes no change to the residue identity. These arguments establish the stated periodic rational root fiber and the exact original Kashaev residue. They do not establish its geometric support or exponential regulator norm. [Exact statewise phase audit](../experiments/audit_cyclotomic_shift_framing.py). [Results](../experiments/cyclotomic_shift_framing_results.json).

title: A local cyclotomic normalization tower and its regulator norm
text: # A local cyclotomic normalization tower and its regulator norm Research note, 25 October 2026. The normalization in the [Heisenberg torsor](heisenberg_period_torsor.md) is a finite-product object. Its compatibility between levels can be proved without a Habiro-ring or algebraic K-theory theorem. This note supplies those identities for every level, including even and composite levels, and derives its local archimedean norm directly. This is a local result, not the identification of a contracted knot invariant with a product of tetrahedron norms. The cyclic dilogarithm and its recurrence are existing definitions (Faddeev--Kashaev, [hep-th/9310070](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9310070)). No novelty is claimed for the finite products or their distribution. The larger rings and K3-indexed modules introduced in [Garoufalidis--Scholze--Wheeler--Zagier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04241v2) concern Frobenius-modified arithmetic gluing of formal series. None of their theorem claims or proofs is used below. The local identities here do not construct those modules or identify their elements with Kashaev's actual values. ## 1. One pointed root at every level For N>=1 let zeta_N=exp(2pi*i/N) and set D_N(x)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta_N^j*x)^j, Q_N(x)=D_N(x)^2/(1-x^N)^(N-1), s_N(x)^(2N)=Q_N(x), s_N(0)=1. (1.1) The last equation defines a unique formal power series in Q(zeta_N)[[x]]: raising a series with constant term one to the power 2N is a bijection in characteristic zero. It also defines its analytic branch on |x|<1. Outside that disk one retains the root torsor and a specified continuation, rather than suppressing its phase. For odd N, (1.1) reduces to the earlier normalization: s_N(x)^N=product_(j=0)^(N-1) (1-zeta_N^j*x)^(j-(N-1)/2). (1.2) This follows by squaring (1.2) and using its constant term. For even N the half-integral centering is represented by the 2N-th root in (1.1); no oddness assumption is inserted into a formula with halves. Index translation in the finite product gives exactly D_N(zeta_N*x)/D_N(x)=(1-x)^N/(1-x^N), s_N(zeta_N*x)/s_N(x)=(1-x)/(1-x^N)^(1/N). (1.3) All roots in (1.3) have constant term one. These are the cyclic intertwiner recurrence and its determinant normalization, with a pointing that fixes the local scalar. ## 2. Exact compatibility between arbitrary levels Let N=m*n and choose zeta_m=zeta_N^n, zeta_n=zeta_N^m. Then D_(mn)(x)=D_m(x^n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) D_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x)^m, Q_(mn)(x)=Q_m(x^n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) Q_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x)^m, s_(mn)(x)=s_m(x^n)^(1/n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) s_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x). (2.1) These are equalities of the pointed formal series, hence of their matched continuations. There is no restriction that m,n be coprime or avoid a set of bad primes. This statement concerns characteristic-zero finite-product identities; it does not assert integral or p-adic gluing at those primes. For the first equality write each index as j=a*m+b. The exponent a*m yields the D_n factors, while the exponent b yields product_(a=0)^(n-1)(1-zeta_n^a*zeta_(mn)^b*x)^b =(1-zeta_m^b*x^n)^b. The denominators in Q multiply correctly because (m-1)+m(n-1)=mn-1. Raise the last equality of (2.1) to the power 2mn and use the pointed root to prove it without a scalar ambiguity. For three levels, every regrouping has the same power and constant term; equivalently, one groups the index by three digits. This proves associative distribution with its phases fixed locally. The maps here include x -> x^n and deck rotations of x. Consequently this identity is not an equality of independently chosen values at one fixed central character for every level. ## 3. A direct Galois/Kummer certificate Let K=Q(zeta_N), let a be prime to N, 1<=a<N, and let sigma_a send zeta_N to zeta_N^a while fixing x. With [k]_N the residue in {0,...,N-1}, put B_(N,a)(x)=product_(k=1)^(N-1) (1-zeta_N^k*x)^((a*[a^(-1)*k]_N-k)/N). Its exponents are integers. Reindexing the product proves sigma_a(D_N)^a/D_N = B_(N,a)^N. (3.1) Thus the class of D_N in K(x)^*/K(x)^(N*) has the inverse cyclotomic Galois character, since a*sigma_a[D_N]=[D_N]. In terms of Q_N, sigma_a(Q_N)^a/Q_N =B_(N,a)^(2N)*(1-x^N)^(-(a-1)(N-1)). (3.2) This is an explicit local Kummer certificate. It does not show that these classes satisfy the global Bloch five-term relation with the required period normalization, nor identify a global Chern class. ## 4. The local norm from an exact logarithmic series On |x|<1, expand the logarithms in (1.1). The finite sums are sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j*zeta_N^(j*k) =-N/(1-zeta_N^k) if N does not divide k, =N(N-1)/2 if N divides k. The divisible terms cancel the denominator of Q_N exactly. Therefore log s_N(x)=sum_(k>=1, N does not divide k) x^k/[k*(1-zeta_N^k)]. (4.1) There is no asymptotic assumption in (4.1). For any r<1 it implies, uniformly on |x|<=r, log s_N(x)=-N Li_2(x)/(2pi*i) -(1/2)log(1-x)+E_N(x), |E_N(x)| <= pi*r/[4N(1-r)] +2*r^(floor(N/2)+1)/(1-r). (4.2) Here N>=2. One elementary proof splits the sum at k=N/2. For the first part use 1/(1-exp(2pi*i*k/N))=1/2+(i/2)cot(pi*k/N), 0 <= 1/u-cot(u) <= u/2, 0<u<=pi/2. The last inequality follows from sin(u)-u*cos(u)=integral_0^u v*sin(v)dv and sin(v)<=sin(u). This bounds each error coefficient by pi*k/(4N). In the tail, for a nondivisible k, |1-zeta_N^k|^(-1)<=N/4. Bound the difference coefficient by N and use 1/k<2/N. The same bound includes the omitted divisible terms of the two comparison series. Geometric summation proves (4.2). In particular E_N=O_r(1/N). Define the metric on the inverse of this specified local frame by log ||s_N(x)^(-1)||_reg =-log|s_N(x)|+N log|x| Arg(1-x)/(2pi). (4.3) The expression extends at x=0. On this disk the branch of Arg is the one from log(1-x). With the Bloch--Wigner function D(x)=Im Li_2(x)+log|x| Arg(1-x), equation (4.2) gives the quantified comparison (2pi/N)log ||s_N(x)^(-1)||_reg =D(x)+(pi/N)log|1-x|-(2pi/N)Re E_N(x). (4.4) It is valid at all levels. This establishes the local regulator rate of the existing normalization frame on compact subdisks. The norm is specified in (4.3); it is not a new definition of the knot invariant and is not yet its absolute-value norm. ## 5. What happens outside this chart and at resonance The restriction in (4.2) matters. Cyclic factors have zeros on the unit circle, and an independent evaluation of one frame can be undefined even when the whole period has a regular germ. For example x=exp(pi*i/3) has x^N=1 at multiples of six. A whole period identity and its lattice must be specialized before its individual factors. The [recoupling lattice](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) gives one explicit instance of such a regular integral replacement. An exact identity also detects the chart correction. With S=N(N-1)/2 and T=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)j^2, direct inversion gives D_N(x)D_N(1/x) =(-1)^S*zeta_N^T*x^(-S) [(1-x^N)/(1-x)]^N, Q_N(x)Q_N(1/x) =(-1)^(N-1)*zeta_N^(2T) (1-x^N)^2/(1-x)^(2N). (5.1) For any matched root choices away from the divisors, it follows that log|s_N(x)|+log|s_N(1/x)| =log|1-x^N|/N-log|1-x|. (5.2) One must transport the regulator metric as well as this algebraic frame. In particular, using the unchanged formula (4.3) on both sides of inversion would introduce the quadratic logarithmic term log|x| Arg(-x); it would not give D(x)+D(1/x)=0. The logarithmic connection and its frame transport supply additional data. ## 6. The remaining knot theorem This gives an exact local system across all levels and proves its local regulator estimate. The [regular cyclic/Steinberg family](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) also places the vacuum in the actual Kashaev color. Neither result says that contracting the knot tensor is a product of these scalar norms. Contraction includes phases and cancellation, and its distinguished global pairing still has to be compared with the geometric period. The required global assertion remains (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| -> Vol(S^3 minus K). No Hilbert-90 calculation or rigidity of a finite-level unpointed intertwiner fixes that pairing by itself. A proof must identify its integral pointing, its global normalization, and its archimedean norm. The identities above do not establish that assertion for a knot class. `experiments/audit_cyclotomic_normalization.py` checks distribution, Galois certificates, inversion, and the series and norm estimates. They are diagnostics for the uniform proofs, not replacements for them.

title: What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period
text: # What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period 28 October 2026. Exact cyclotomic pointing already determines the actual quantum period. It does not automatically make its geometric coefficient nonzero. Two precise facts sharpen the torsor target: 1. The SAME original figure-eight family has exponential growth on its complete meridian arc and bounded values on every fixed-color meridian arc approaching the same complete classical point. A uniform dominant geometric comparison regular on the raw central fibre is therefore impossible. The divided normal source is essential, rather than an optional choice of coordinates. 2. The explicit whole-word Kummer period has a fixed number of variables, but growing cover genus and growing character homology. It has not yet supplied the fixed finite-rank algebraic object required by the existing whole-comparison rigidity theorem. These are proofs about the original anchored state and its actual cover. No rescaled invariant or adjustable levelwise source is used. ## 1. The source is already fixed; uniqueness is not the missing datum Use the actual family and conventions of [the all-level operator theorem](all_level_a_period.md) and [the normal-period theorem](peripheral_normal_period.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(1)=K_N, F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. For each FIXED j, C_j(q) is the specified Laurent-polynomial ordinary-color period, C_j(1)=1. The exact all-level recurrence, its actual finite initial window and its bounded quantum jets determine K_N uniquely. The [Mellin theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) strengthens this to the entire rational root section with its pole lattice. There is consequently no freedom to alter the knot period while keeping those exact data. The unresolved assertion is that this unique anchored object has the required selected regulator character. Uniqueness cannot be converted into existence of a regulator comparison without producing a candidate satisfying the original source, lattice and quantum-normal equations. ## 2. Fixed algebraic coefficients have polynomial size on a fixed-color arc Put t=1/N and retain the root source coordinates (t,Q,Y) on the central slice U=Y^N=1. Let E be a fixed finite FIELD extension of k(t,Q,Y), k a fixed embedded characteristic-zero field. A specified finite residue-field mark and an etale selected place can be retained. Let a be a nonzero element of E, regular on the marked chart where the arc is tested. For all sufficiently large FIXED positive integers j, every specialized conjugate of a on gamma_j(t)=(t,exp(2pi*i*t),exp(2pi*i*j*t)) (1) has upper and lower polynomial bounds at t=1/N, for all large N. The required lower bound on j depends on the fixed presentation of a, not on N. In particular it cannot be exponentially small or zero at infinitely many large levels. Here is a direct proof, including the possible vanishing issue. Choose a polynomial relation for a with nonzero constant and leading coefficients, clear all denominators, and consider each nonzero coefficient P(t,Q,Y). Write P=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) Q^r Y^s. Let A be the span of its Q exponents. For j>A the integers r+js belonging to different collected pairs (r,s) are distinct. Thus P(gamma_j(t))=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) exp(2pi*i*(r+js)t) is not identically zero. Independence follows by successively applying the constant-coefficient operators partial_t-2pi*i*(r+js), with powers exceeding the polynomial degrees, to isolate one exponential. A nonzero resulting analytic germ has finite vanishing order at t=0. Apply this to the finitely many relation coefficients. Cauchy's root bound and the same bound for the reciprocal polynomial give c N^(-B)<=|a_(i,N)|<=C N^B. (2) The proof is uniform over all roots of the selected relation. It does not assume bounded absolute cyclotomic degree or heights. In particular, the complete figure-eight scalar itself cannot be a fixed algebraic function of (t,Q) on a finite cover: (2) would give zero exponential rate, contradicting (3) below. This does not exclude a fixed algebraic connection or torsor with a transcendental marked horizontal period. Its irregular regulator character must be retained before applying algebraic coefficient rigidity. For algebraic sections on a finite integral shape cover, apply the argument to a fixed nonzero norm or a polynomial relation on the selected irreducible component. Clearing actual poles must precede specialization. A statement about a fixed algebraic section is much stronger than algebraicity at each separate N. ## 3. An original-source obstruction to a regular central-fibre comparison Take the original figure-eight knot. The independently proved [whole-source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) gives lim_(N->infinity) N^-1 Log|F_N(1)| =Vol(4_1)/(2pi)>0. (3) For every fixed j>=1, the SAME family and SAME original cap give F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)->1. (4) No normalization, operator or source was changed between (3) and (4). Both arcs approach (Q,Y,U)=(1,1,1), and U=1 on both. More literally, the actual pivot has g_k(M)=M^(1-N)g_k(1). On these unit-meridian arcs its change is a specified common unit for every closed head. Moving that unchanged factor into its retained external line leaves the same numerical cut functional. Thus this growth contrast does not hide an independently chosen co-source. Suppose a proposed whole geometric comparison on the raw central fibre had the form F_N(Y)=a_N(Y) G_N(Y)+R_N(Y), (5) where a is a nonzero section of the fixed algebraic type in Section 2. Suppose on every fixed-color arc (1) its geometric period and remainder satisfied, for a common V>0, N^-1 Log|G_N(Q_N^j)|->V, |R_N(Q_N^j)|<=exp(N(V-delta_j)), delta_j>0. (6) Then (5) is impossible. Choose a fixed j larger than the presentation bound of Section 2. Its a_N(Q_N^j) is nonzero and polynomially bounded above and below. Equations (5)--(6), by the reverse triangle inequality, give positive exponential growth on that arc, contradicting (4). Equivalently, if bounded ordinary-color values force the coefficient to vanish on EVERY fixed-color arc, the exponential separation proof in Section 2 forces its algebraic restriction to the raw central fibre to vanish identically. It cannot then give the nonzero complete value by ordinary regular evaluation. This excludes a tempting shortcut: a uniform dominant geometric block with a regular algebraic scalar coefficient on that fibre. It does NOT exclude a source-preserving normal extension, a nonregular meridian lattice, or cancellation between blocks with the same exponential size. The latter possibilities are precisely data which raw algebraic point rigidity does not fix. ### The original divided source explains the necessary distinction The exact actual source is already known to use the normal extension. With U=Y^N and t_mu=U-1, set Y_r(t_mu)=Q_N^r(1+t_mu)^(1/N), v_N(t_mu)_r=(Y_r(t_mu)-1)F_N(Y_r(t_mu)). Then the unconditional original state identity is K_N=N e_0^*[t_mu^1]v_N, whereas the central state v_N(0) contains only the polynomially bounded ordinary-color row. The source has degree minus one; it is not ordinary evaluation of the lowest state degree. See [the source-adapted filtration](source_adapted_leading_filtration_and_actual_scale_test.md). The elementary expression (U-1)/(Y-1), U=Y^N, likewise vanishes at every proper root-orbit point and has complete whole-germ value N. It is not a regular function on the raw two-variable fibre U=1 at Y=1. This illustrates the required divided lattice; it does not define a replacement invariant or prove its regulator coefficient is nonzero. Thus the actual source-anchored example supports the user's normal-torsor viewpoint, while ruling out its regular scalar version on the unextended central fibre. ## 4. The explicit Kummer period has growing ambient rank For an odd prime p the actual one-variable cyclic cover is C_p: y^p=product_(j=1)^(p-1)(1-Q_p^j t)^j. It is connected. Its p-1 finite branch points have ramification index p, since each j is coprime to p. Infinity is unramified: the polynomial degree p(p-1)/2 is divisible by p. Counting the Euler characteristic of the punctured p-sheeted cover and filling its ramified points gives 2-2g=p*2-(p-1)*(p-1), g=(p-1)(p-3)/2. (7) The growth persists in the particular nontrivial deck character used by y^-1 dt. Remove the finite branch points from the base sphere. It retracts to a graph with one vertex and p-2 loops. In any nontrivial deck-character component the covering graph chain groups have dimensions 1 and p-2, and its boundary map has rank one: a branch generator acts by a nontrivial p-th root. Hence that character's H_1 has dimension p-3. Filling the ramification points changes only the trivial character, because each such point is deck-fixed. Therefore dim H_1(C_p)_chi=p-3 (8) for every nontrivial character chi, including the selected one. The small-circle source has an additional important feature. Removing the p preimages of t=0 adds one boundary-circle dimension to each nontrivial character. The original selected circle projects into that canonical one-dimensional boundary subspace. Thus growing ambient rank DOES NOT rule out a smaller selected period object. It does show that fixed variable count alone has not constructed such an object uniformly in p. In particular the compact C_p cannot all be the smooth proper fibres of one fixed finite-type algebraic curve family on finitely many strata: their genus is unbounded. A fixed selected torsor must be a genuinely constructed reduction or comparison, not an automatic consequence of the displayed Kummer equations. ## 5. What a successful rigidity certificate would now have to contain The existing [whole-comparison rigidity theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) can promote bounded algebraic quantum-jet identities to an exact whole comparison. The existing [critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) can then force every geometric coefficient nonzero from an irreducible descended critical line and a nonzero exact source moment, or from a faithful trace realization. Fixed algebraic coefficients automatically have polynomial norms on the root arc. Those theorems would remove a separately assumed nonzero geometric weight. Their inputs are substantive and finite: * a fixed algebraic comparison space or an explicitly bounded selected quotient of the actual Kummer/quantum object; * the source-normal pairing, its meridian pole lattice and its quantum-normal connection retained by that comparison; * an actual descended critical line/observable with its exact source moments, rather than only a classical shape field; * control of the TOTAL compact remainder after that projection. The first three have not been supplied for the selected knot period. The new exact cut construction supplies the original cycle, and its infinity bound removes a real global escape obstacle. It does not make their fixed algebraic reduction or critical source moment automatic. Equations (3)--(4) show why that reduction must retain the divided source before passing to a central or associated-graded fibre.

title: Degenerate alias faces: a general bound and two exact obstructions
text: # Degenerate alias faces: a general bound and two exact obstructions Research note, 28 October 2026. This note concerns the remaining **classical wrong-edge faces** of `general_legendre_rivin_contour.md`. It proves a uniform bound for a combinatorially specified class of triangulations. Two tempting routes to an unconditional bound fail on actual positive knot triangulations: repairing only the flat tetrahedra, and giving the complete edge multipliers an automatic favorable sign. Neither counterexample disproves volume domination. Neither the bound nor the counterexamples identify an original quantum wall with a classical face. That source comparison remains necessary. The reproducible exact/Arb audit is `experiments/audit_degenerate_alias_faces.py`, with fixture `experiments/degenerate_alias_face_fixture.json` and results `experiments/degenerate_alias_face_results.json`. ## 1. A uniform star bound for all wrong-edge faces Let an ideal triangulation of a one-cusped knot exterior have (t) tetrahedra and (t) global edges. Let (E) be its nonnegative edge-angle incidence matrix. Its three columns per tetrahedron count the two opposite local edges, so every column sums to two. Consider a weak nonnegative alias angle locus \[ \alpha_{ja}\geq0,\qquad \sum_{a=0}^2\alpha_{ja}=\pi, \qquad E\alpha=2\pi k,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^t. \tag{1} \] Summing all edge equations gives \(\sum_e k_e=t\). Consequently, if the edge winding differs from the original vector \(\mathbf1\), at least one edge has (k_e=0). All angle summands incident to that edge are then zero. Every tetrahedron meeting it has at least one zero angle, and its continuous volume \[ V_j=\Lambda(\alpha_{j0})+\Lambda(\alpha_{j1}) +\Lambda(\alpha_{j2}) \] is zero: \(\Lambda(0)=0\) and \(\Lambda(\pi-a)=-\Lambda(a)\). Write (s_e) for the number of **distinct tetrahedra** incident to edge (e), and (v_3) for the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. Since every other tetrahedron has volume at most (v_3), \[ \boxed{\quad V(\alpha)\leq(t-s_e)v_3 \quad\text{whenever }k_e=0.\quad} \tag{2} \] In particular, put \(s_{\min}=\min_e s_e\). If a positive complete triangulation satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad\operatorname{Vol}(M)>(t-s_{\min})v_3,\quad} \tag{3} \] **every wrong-edge weak nonnegative alias locus has a common strict volume gap** \[ \operatorname{Vol}(M)-V(\alpha) \geq\operatorname{Vol}(M)-(t-s_{\min})v_3>0. \tag{4} \] This is a bound on the whole cell, including all its corners, with no stationarity or repair assumption. For several zero edges, replace (s_e) by the size of the union of their tetrahedron stars. Linear constraint propagation can force still more tetrahedra to be flat. The bound applies to an actual face integral once that integral has the specified phase, a uniform subexponential density bound, and a chain of subexponential mass. It then gives the corresponding exponential loss. These quantum hypotheses are not inferred from the angle equations. Condition (3) is a useful sufficient criterion, not an assertion about all geometric triangulations. It becomes weak for triangulations with many thin tetrahedra. ## 2. Flat-only repair can fail on an actual positive triangulation A proposed universal argument was: retain every positive tetrahedron, change only flat tetrahedra, and restore the original edge winding. Such a repair would preserve or increase volume. The following exact example shows that the repair need not exist. Use the six-tetrahedron standard (7_4) triangulation with undecorated isomorphism signature `gLvQQbefdfefmexnaxk`. Its explicit face gluings and edge matrix are saved in the fixture. Index tetrahedra and edges from zero and write a tetrahedron's angles in units of \(\pi\) as \((a_j,b_j,c_j)\). The edge matrix, displayed in three-column blocks, is \[ E=\begin{pmatrix} 100&110&110&000&001&000\\ 011&011&000&001&010&001\\ 001&100&010&010&100&100\\ 010&000&001&100&010&000\\ 100&001&001&110&000&011\\ 000&000&100&001&101&110 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{5} \] Here `110` denotes the row block \((1,1,0)\). The audit reconstructs this matrix from the individual face permutations; it does not trust a transcribed gluing matrix. Consider the rational alias point \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} j&a_j&b_j&c_j\\\hline 0&3/10&0&7/10\\ 1&1/30&19/30&1/3\\ 2&1/3&2/3&0\\ 3&0&1&0\\ 4&29/30&0&1/30\\ 5&19/30&1/30&1/3 \end{array} \tag{6} \] Direct multiplication gives \[ E\alpha=2(1,1,2,0,1,1)^T. \tag{7} \] Exactly tetrahedra (0,2,3,4) are flat; tetrahedra (1,5) are strictly positive. Every original angle structure, satisfying the local sums one and \(E\alpha=2\mathbf1\), obeys the identity \[ 3(a_1+a_5)+b_1+2b_5-3 =c_0+b_3+2c_3+b_4\ \geq0. \tag{8} \] This is an elementary linear combination of the original tetrahedron and edge equations. At (6), its left side is \(-3/10\). Hence **no modification of just tetrahedra (0,2,3,4) can restore the original edge equations while retaining tetrahedra (1,5)**. For a second exact verification, let (A=(L;E)), where (L) records local sums. Let (F\) be the twelve columns belonging to the four flat tetrahedra and (P\) the other six columns. If (q\) denotes (6), a repair would require \[ A_F x=(\mathbf1,2\mathbf1)^T-A_Pq_P=:b_F, \qquad x\geq0. \] The rational vector \[ y=(0,-1,2/3,2/3,2/3,-1; -1/3,1,-1/3,-1,1/3,-1/3)^T \] satisfies \[ A_F^Ty=(0,0,2/3;\ 0,0,0;\ 0,2/3,4/3;\ 0,2/3,0)^T \geq0, \qquad y^Tb_F=-1/5. \tag{9} \] Thus nonexistence is certified by rational arithmetic, with no numerical optimization used in the proof. ### This is genuinely positive complete geometric input The shape certificate uses the upper-half-plane root (a) of \[ a^3+2a-1=0, \qquad a\approx-0.2266988257582+1.4677115087102i. \] The six positively oriented shapes are \[ \left(\frac{1+a-a^2}{2},\ a,\ \frac{1+a}{2},\ 2+a+a^2,\ 3+a+a^2,\ a\right). \tag{10} \] The audit verifies, by exact polynomial reduction, every edge product and both peripheral products. Arb root isolation proves positivity and the marked logarithmic equations: edge angles (2\pi\), peripheral angles zero. These give the complete cusp and complete metric. The Bloch--Wigner sum is rigorously enclosed by \[ 5.13794120187341776984134833947484503 <\operatorname{Vol}(7_4)<5.13794120187341776984134833947484504. \] The face permutations have one ideal vertex and torus vertex link. An optional independent Regina/SnapPy comparison verifies validity, orientability, and the stated knot label and isomorphism signature. The star sizes of (5) are \((4,5,6,4,5,4)\). Therefore (2), unlike the failed repair, bounds **all** weak wrong-edge loci for this triangulation: \[ V_{\mathrm{wrong\ edge}}\leq2v_3 =2.02988321281930725004240510854904057\ldots <\operatorname{Vol}(7_4). \tag{11} \] Thus (6) is an obstruction to a proposed proof mechanism, not a counterexample to volume domination. ## 3. Complete edge multipliers need not have the favorable sign Concavity at the complete geometric point gives the valid inequality \[ V(\alpha)\leq V_g+2\pi\sum_e\mu_e(k_e-1), \tag{12} \] where \(-\log(2\sin\alpha_{ja,g})\) is expressed as a tetrahedron multiplier plus the incident edge multipliers. Decoration changes do not change the pairing with feasible defects. However, its sign is not automatically nonpositive. Use the independently audited three-tetrahedron (5_2) chart. Its complete triples are \[ (A,B,C),(A,B,C),(B,C,A),\qquad (A,B,C)=(\pi-3\theta,2\theta,\theta),\quad 0<\theta<\pi/3. \] Set \[ b=-\log(2\sin2\theta),\qquad c=-\log(2\sin\theta). \] Stationarity gives \(-\log(2\sin A)=(2b+c)/3\). For the exact edge matrix \[ E=\begin{pmatrix} 200&011&110\\ 010&110&101\\ 012&101&011 \end{pmatrix}, \] one can take the edge multipliers \[ \mu=((b-c)/3,\ b-c,\ 0), \tag{13} \] up to their common additive ambiguity. The alias assignment \[ (0,0,1),(1,0,0),(0,0,1) \] has winding (k=(0,1,2)). Consequently, \[ \boxed{\quad \sum_e\mu_e(k_e-1) =\frac{c-b}{3} =\frac{\log(2\cos\theta)}{3}>0.\quad} \tag{14} \] All its tetrahedra are flat. Their actual volume is zero; (12) simply has the wrong sign to prove the desired bound. The positive defect is rigorously enclosed near (0.14059978716148\). ## 4. What the compact Legendre contour does and does not supply here For the original marked potential, clamped radial minimization on the whole angle cube gives the compact positive contour and its unique geometric maximum. An alias changes that potential by \[ W_m(x)=W(x)+2\pi i\,m^Tx, \qquad \operatorname{Im}W_m =\operatorname{Im}W+2\pi m^T\rho. \] The same convex/concave construction can be applied to (W_m), but it then minimizes a different function and has a different angle cell. The original upper bound cannot be transferred by dropping the linear term. Formula (14) demonstrates concretely why comparison at the fixed geometric radius need not have the desired sign. Clipping makes the contour compact; it does not, by itself, compare distinct winding cells. The surviving general routes are therefore substantive: control the actual wall charges by source/Ward cancellation, prove a stronger topological volume comparison, or use a verifiable gap such as (3). The present note proves the third route when its stated criterion holds and rules out two universal shortcuts to the second.

title: The elevated wall source is not supplied by the finite divided-Ward orbit
text: # The elevated wall source is not supplied by the finite divided-Ward orbit Research proof and two exact tests, 27 October 2026. The binomial wall co-source has a literal realization on the degree-N symmetric power of the already proved divided-source standard module. That realization does not automatically carry the true divided Hopf coproduct. A finite-head weight bound rules out a full SL2-equivariant embedding at fixed bridge number and large N. The most immediate q-binomial elevation also fails a bounded diagonal comparison. These are precise restrictions on proposed constructions, not a claim that a linear relative B1 current map is impossible. An explicit weighted stabilization shows why its second transfer coordinate needs an actual network map in addition to a cut orbit. The later [actual high-color construction](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md) evades the fixed-head dimension restriction explicitly. Integral color N(N+1) carries the required Sym^N divided multiplicity, its coherent row is exactly B_N, and its root knot scalar equals K_N with all braiding/peripheral signs retained. Its normal block arrows are actual regularized entries of E,F. This is a source enlargement, not a contradiction to the fixed-head nilpotence bound. Its full divided coproduct/current map and the geometric source projection remain separate requirements. ## 1. The actual wall row and its literal tensor-source realization The [cut-current theorem](actual_gauss_wall_cut_current_complex.md) gives B_N(J)=[1/(N2^N)]sum_(j=0)^N binom(N,j)J_j. (1) J here has the matrix normalization of equation (14a) in the cut-current note. Original raw Green arrays use N B_N instead; that coefficient is retained. Use the actual two-dimensional divided-source subspace L=span(Ubar,W), Ubar=(sum E_(j,j+1))/(N-1), W=E_(N-1,0), Phi(Ubar)=Phi(W)=1/N. On L the explicitly proved normalized divided Hopf adjoints are the standard SL2 matrices e,f,h. Let M_j be the sum of the distinct tensors with j copies of W and N-j copies of Ubar. Then the literal coupon row ell=((N/2)Phi)^(tensor N) satisfies `ell(M_j)=binom(N,j)/2^N`. Hence B_N(J)=(1/N)ell(sum_j J_j M_j). (2) This is an exact source pairing. The primitive tensor SL2 action induced from L makes their span Sym^N L, with a highest string of length N+1. That primitive action is not automatically the true global divided Hopf adjoint on the tensor-source network. Its coproduct contains the mixed ordinary divided powers already computed in the actual fusion theorem. Equation (2) does not discard those terms, nor prove a monoidal Ward intertwiner. ## 2. A fixed-head equivariance obstruction On H=V_N^(tensor b) retain the ordinary integer position grading. For a matrix unit indexed by an output tuple r and input tuple s, its matrix weight is `sum r_i-sum s_i`, in -b(N-1)<=weight<=b(N-1). The true E Hopf adjoint decreases this weight by one. Therefore its degree-N divided-normal operator J_E decreases it by N; normal division changes the coefficient, not the support degree. It follows exactly that (J_E)^(2b)=0 on End(H). (3) On Sym^N L, by contrast, `e^(2b)` is nonzero when N>=2b. Consequently there is no nonzero full-SL2-equivariant map of Sym^N L into this finite-head adjoint space intertwining its e with the actual normalized J_E when N>=2b. Indeed such a map is injective: the standard highest-weight polynomial module Sym^N L is irreducible in characteristic zero, as is seen by raising a nonzero highest weight term and then applying the lowering operator. Equation (3) contradicts injectivity. The same argument applies to a proposed nonzero full-SL2 intertwiner into any subquotient with this same weight bound. It does not rule out a non-equivariant linear current map, a Borel-only quotient, an enlarged normal/tail complex, or a source involving a number of additional factors growing with N. It identifies the additional sector a full equivariant construction would have to supply. ## 3. The first divided q-binomial row has a different whole-head lattice At Q=Q_N, all middle coefficients of `{N choose j}_Q` vanish. Their exact first divided-normal values are d_(N,j)=[{N choose j}_Q/(1-Q^N)]_(Q=Q_N) =N/[(Q_N;Q_N)_j(Q_N;Q_N)_(N-j)] =(-1)^(j-1)Q_N^[-j(j-1)/2]/(1-Q_N^j), 0<j<N. (4) The proof cancels the single numerator factor 1-Q^N before specialization and then pairs the complementary root factors. In particular `|d_(N,j)|=1/[2sin(pi j/N)]`. If the degree-zero endpoint coefficients 1 and the degree-one middle coefficients (4) are put in the same trial source row, the result is `(1,d_1,...,d_(N-1),1)`. This statement specifies the trial Rees identification: it does not identify its two normal degrees by an unproved map. A diagonal adapter to the ordinary row `(binom(N,0),...,binom(N,N))` has endpoint entry one and middle entries `binom(N,j)/d_(N,j)`. Its condition number in every common diagonal metric is at least 2^(N+1)/(N+1), N even, sqrt(3)2^N/(N+1), N odd>=3. (5) Choose a central coefficient, which is at least 2^N/(N+1), and use `2sin(pi j/N)>=sqrt(3)` (equal to 2 at even N). The endpoint-to-center ratio proves (5). Overall row normalization does not remove this condition number. Thus the most immediate q-binomial/Frobenius elevation is not the bounded full-head Gamma unit already proved at source degree N-1. A higher normal extension or a different linear current map might still repair it. Simply replacing classical binomial weights by the first divided q-binomial weights would change the actual co-source. ## 4. An actual weighted stabilization does not give a second cut Weyl identity There is a small universal test using the literal crossing, rather than an arbitrary array. Set N=2, q=i, Q=-1, M=1, x=i. Take a positive Markov stabilization, whose new crossing transfer is k, and attach a weight w^k. Its full root framing and pivot normalization has kappa_D=0. The two cut diagonal entries, computed directly from the actual finite coefficients, are C_0(w)=1, C_1(w)=2w-1. (6) For the second entry the routes are `(i,j,k)=(1,0,1)` and `(1,1,0)`, with their complete normalized weights 2w and -1. The zeroth entry has the single route `(0,0,0)` with weight 1. Thus the original normalized cut gives exactly w; at w=1 this is the correct identity tangle after the twist correction. For a preceding scalar knot cut F I, this local operation gives F times (6). Therefore the transfer distribution after the normalized cut is `(0,F)`. Its unnormalized transfer sum is F. Encoding that sum by a two-dimensional auxiliary diagonal source means the matrix diag(0,2F). The two hemisphere co-sources of that transfer source are then lambda_2^+=F/4, lambda_2^-=3F/4. (7) They are not the two equal cut values F/2. This is an exact universal local stabilization test, not a knot-by-knot argument. It shows that applying a second auxiliary Bernstein reflection to a transfer index is not already the actual cut Weyl identity. The original unweighted invariant remains unchanged. This does not rule out an adapted second framing coordinate on a hyperbolic geometric chart: the new stabilization transfer need not be etale on that critical framing torsor. It proves that such an identification must use its actual network and current equations; it cannot follow from the one-cut source orbit or its two Weyl charts alone. The concrete next map must therefore transport the degree-N wall row (1), the two actual cut endpoints, and the second network framing current together, possibly in a normal/tail extension. The finite cut-current chain map is already explicit. No selected geometric cycle, global microstalk or volume limit is asserted here. Verification is recorded in [audit_degree_elevated_wall_source.py](../experiments/audit_degree_elevated_wall_source.py) and its [results](../experiments/degree_elevated_wall_source_results.json). The coupon and stabilization tests are exact rational-complex matrix calculations. The divided q-row formula and conditioning bound are checked at 80-digit precision for N=2 through 32; their general proof is the finite product cancellation (4). No kernel of the full knot network or selected volume limit is inferred from these tests.

title: Degree elevation preserves the cut and transports the actual head Borel complex
text: # Degree elevation preserves the cut and transports the actual head Borel complex Research proof, 27 October 2026. The uniform co-source obtained by integrating the paired Fr dual has N+1 states, whereas the original head has N. A cyclic identification duplicates its endpoint and does not preserve the head row. The explicit matrix degree elevation below corrects this on ALL head matrices. Together with retained whole arrow gauges it gives an actual cut-Ward cochain map, including the original co-source homotopy. It is not a multiplicative R-network map or a proof of Gaussian/source descent. The earlier [degree-elevated wall note](degree_elevated_wall_source_and_divided_ward.md) constructed the binomial wall row and its fixed-head equivariance obstructions. It did not construct the full matrix degree elevation, its uniform-cut identity, or the actual head-current map proved here. ## 1. Full matrix elevation, with both endpoint entries Put n=N-1. In the actual Fr symbol convention sigma_r(C)=ell_r(u) C psi_r(t)/(1+tu)^r, where psi_r(t)_j=t^j and ell_r(u)_i=binom(r,i)u^i, define \[ (\mathcal E_NC)_{ij} =\frac{N-i}{N}C_{ij}+\frac{i}{N}C_{i-1,j-1}, \qquad 0\le i,j\le N. \tag{1} \] Every out-of-range old entry is zero. Both terms are required. Binomial cancellation gives the exact polynomial identity \[ \ell_N(u)(\mathcal E_NC)\psi_N(t) =(1+tu)\ell_n(u)C\psi_n(t), \qquad\sigma_N(\mathcal E_NC)=\sigma_n(C). \tag{2} \] The map is injective because the symbol numerator determines every matrix entry. It is unital and preserves BOTH actual uniform rows: \[ \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal E_NC)}{N+1} =\frac{\operatorname{Tr}C}{N},\qquad \frac{\sum_{ij}(\mathcal E_NC)_{ij}}{N+1} =\frac{\sum_{ij}C_{ij}}N. \tag{3} \] Indeed each old entry C_ij occurs with total coefficient ((N-i)+(i+1))/N=(N+1)/N, and the same holds for diagonal entries. The second identity is the original average rank-one coupon, not only the ordinary trace. For a diagonal C the elevated entries are \[ \widetilde C_R=\frac{N-R}{N}C_R+\frac RN C_{R-1}, \quad\widetilde C_0=C_0,\quad\widetilde C_N=C_{N-1}. \tag{4} \] Thus the actual paired-Fr interval, whose integrated dual is uniform 1/(N+1), gives the original head average exactly after (4). By contrast the uncorrected cyclic P_diag insertion repeats C_0 at R=N; it gives weights 2/(N+1),1/(N+1),...,1/(N+1). For C_R=Q_N^R its value is 1/(N+1), while the old head average is zero. Formula (4) is the required endpoint correction, not an identification of these different rows. The binomial wall B_N remains its separate co-source with its original factor 1/N. ## 2. Exact classical and whole Cartan covariance The actual divided Fr matrices on degree r satisfy e psi=(rt-t^2 partial_t)psi, f psi=partial_t psi and h psi=(r-2t partial_t)psi, with their corresponding dual formulas. The normalized commutator fields are independent of r. Applying them to (2) proves \[ \mathcal E_N([x_n,C])=[x_N,\mathcal E_NC], \qquad x=e,f,h. \tag{5} \] This is also checked directly from (1); it is not an assumed published quantization result. Since both terms of (1) have the same i-j, for EVERY nonzero whole parameter Q, \[ \mathcal E_N(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_n}}C) =\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_N}}\mathcal E_NC. \tag{6} \] The image therefore is a global P1 operator/co-source submodule under the ordinary divided Fr f and whole Cartan dilation. Its two extreme entries (0,N),(N,0) are identically zero. It is not the entire End(Sym^N); in particular an arbitrary degree-N wall current need not belong to it. ## 3. Actual whole head arrows give a strict cut-current map In a specified original head basis let K_j=xQ^(-j), F_(j+1,j)=f_j(q), 0<=j<N-1, with all f_j actual nonzero arrow units near q_N. This includes the original balanced f_j=1-Q^(j+1) and the integral f_j=[j+1]_q, with their actual source adapters carried. Define the WHOLE diagonal gauge \[ D_0=1,\qquad D_{j+1}/D_j=(j+1)/f_j(q). \] Then DFD^(-1)=f_n, the classical degree-n lowering matrix, and DKD^(-1)=K. Every q-factorial, source and dual in this gauge is retained; invertibility at fixed N is not an asymptotic norm bound. Put T_0(C)=E_N(DCD^(-1)). Equations (5)--(6) give the LITERAL whole matrix cochain identities \[ T_0((\operatorname{Ad}_K-I)C) =(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_N}}-I)T_0(C),\qquad T_0([F,C])=[f_N,T_0(C)]. \tag{7} \] Thus the actual two-row cut-Ward complex maps isomorphically onto its image subcomplex by T_0 in degree zero and the displayed two row maps in degree one. This is an explicit current map, not a declaration that two Borel groups are abstractly isomorphic. The actual Hopf F row is transported too, with its explicit ordered K-row correction retained: \[ \operatorname{ad}_F(C)=[F,C]+K^{-1}[K,C]F, \quad [K,C]=((\operatorname{Ad}_K-I)C)K. \tag{8} \] Use this invertible row operation before (7). Its product term is sent by the LINEAR map T_0 with its full order; T_0 is not applied to its factors separately. The target may use the ACTUAL whole divided Fr lowering matrix on any fixed residue string s. If its arrow is beta_(R,s)(q), set B_(0,s)=1 and B_(R+1,s)/B_(R,s)=beta_(R,s)/(R+1). These are regular actual units with root one, and F^(N)|_s=B_s f_N B_s^(-1). Consequently \[ T_s=\operatorname{Ad}_{B_s}T_0 \tag{9} \] has the same strict properties with actual F^(N)|_s in place of f_N. B_s commutes with the whole memory Cartan Q^(-R). This Cartan is the specified Fr memory observable; it is not silently relabeled as the original high-color quantum K, whose root action is on the head factor. The actual opposite divided generator and mixed tensor coproduct still require their specified normal rows. ## 4. Original cut co-source and its exact transported homotopy Conjugations preserve trace, so (3) gives tau_Fr T_s=tau_head. Before D,B are inserted, (3) also preserves the original average coupon on ALL matrices. After those gauges the actual source and dual are transported; a binomial or uniform row cannot simply be substituted for the conjugated row. There is nevertheless an explicit comparison of the original head average Phi_h and the uniform Fr interval row Phi_Fr on the image. Let B_h be the actual head matrix [K,B_h]=e_h-I/N. In the target let K_Fr=Q^(-J_N) and put \[ (B_{\mathrm{Fr}})_{ij}=\frac1{(N+1)(Q^{-i}-Q^{-j})} \quad(i\ne j,\ \{i,j\}\ne\{0,N\}), \] with the diagonal and the two extreme corners zero. Every displayed denominator is a unit near Q_N. The omitted corners of T_s(C) are IDENTICALLY zero, so the actual trace homotopies give \[ \Phi_h(C)-\Phi_{\mathrm{Fr}}(T_sC) =-\operatorname{Tr}(B_h[K,C]) +\operatorname{Tr}(B_{\mathrm{Fr}}[K_{\mathrm{Fr}},T_sC]). \tag{10} \] The last commutator equals T_s((Ad_K-I)C) K_Fr. Thus (10) is an explicit cochain homotopy on the actual cut-Ward complex. It holds with the whole D and B_s units present, not only at their numerical root values. On actual diagonal Green arrays these conjugations do nothing and (3)--(4) preserve the original cut exactly. On Ward-closed cut matrices the homotopy is zero as well. The raw Green 1/N normalization remains the one in the original certificate. The excluded extreme target corners and the complementary operator subspace cannot be discarded if an arbitrary Fr-valued wall or normal current leaves the image. This is where an additional endpoint/mixed-normal source may still occur. ## 5. Scope of this actual map The source and coefficient complex at the FINAL finite cut is now explicitly related to global Fr P1 operators, the integrated uniform Fr co-source, and the actual head Hopf rows. It does not turn T_s into an algebra homomorphism: already N=2, E_2(P_0)=diag(1,1/2,0), so E_2(P_0)^2!=E_2(P_0). Products, R crossings and mixed coproducts must therefore be transported as whole ordered operators, not factor by factor. Nor has an internal remaining flow index been identified with this open cut matrix index. The geometric Gaussian/source comparison must still map its two retained currents and normal endpoint classes to the explicit finite complex. The result here is a genuine cut cochain map and co-source homotopy, not a selected geometric period or volume limit. [Exact matrix and coherent-symbol audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_actual_head_ward.py). The [results](../experiments/degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_results.json) pass fourteen actual generic-q/root cases N=2,...,8 and 406 full matrix units. They check the complete symbols and both uniform rows, whole arrow gauges, the actual Fr divided string, Hopf row correction and co-source homotopy. These are actual finite cut identities, not a Gaussian or selected-cycle test.

title: The degree-elevation complement is one marked quantum-normal wall line
text: # The degree-elevation complement is one marked quantum-normal wall line Research theorem and actual crossing/source calculation, 27 October 2026. The complement omitted by actual cut degree elevation has dimension 2N+1, but its whole memory-Borel complex contracts to ONE two-term wall complex. The contraction retains the two extreme corners and uses no division by the wall parameter. Its root norm is O(N) in the natural unitary spin metric. The source on that wall is essential. The original coherent cut assigns it 2^(-N); the uniform interval assigns 1/(N+1). Their exponential ratio cannot be discarded as a Ward homotopy. An explicit charged component of the FIRST ACTUAL universal R normal hits the wall generator in an ordered current calculation. No full-network cancellation or selected geometric contribution is inferred from these local statements. ## 1. The actual missing subspace and its global boundary polynomial Use [actual matrix degree elevation](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) \(\mathcal E_N:\operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N-1} \to\operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N}\). It is injective, unital, cut-preserving and equivariant for the ACTUAL divided classical commutators. Write \[ \mathcal I_N=\operatorname{im}\mathcal E_N,\qquad \operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N} =\mathcal I_N\oplus\mathcal W_N. \] The summands have adjoint spins 0,...,N-1 and N respectively; \(\dim\mathcal W_N=2N+1\). A concrete quotient map is \[ \operatorname{ob}_N(C)(u) =u^N\ell_N(u)C\psi_N(-1/u) =\sum_{i,j}(-1)^j{N\choose i}C_{ij}u^{N+i-j}. \tag{1.1} \] Its kernel is exactly I_N: the symbol numerator is divisible by 1+ut precisely when its restriction t=-1/u vanishes. The degree bound then leaves a numerator of bidegree at most N-1, giving the unique old matrix. Its image is every polynomial of degree at most 2N. Thus W_N is the GLOBAL H0(O(2N)) boundary module, rather than an arbitrary missing collection of matrix entries. Its two endpoint corners are e^N=N!E_(0,N) and f^N=N!E_(N,0). For complete direct verification, (1.1) takes ad e,ad f,ad h to partial_u, 2Nu-u^2 partial_u, 2N-2u partial_u, and takes Ad(Q^(-J)) to g(u)->Q^N g(u/Q). The [independent incidence/source calculation](degree_elevation_wall_residual_and_source_moments.md) records this quotient and its one-sided clock residuals. One may project onto W_N algebraically without choosing a split matrix basis: the adjoint Casimir \(\mathcal C=(\operatorname{ad}h)^2/2+ \operatorname{ad}e\operatorname{ad}f+ \operatorname{ad}f\operatorname{ad}e\) has eigenvalues 2l(l+1). Its polynomial projector onto eigenvalue 2N(N+1) is \(\prod_{l=0}^{N-1}(\mathcal C-2l(l+1))/ [2N(N+1)-2l(l+1)]\). All denominators are nonzero constants. ## 2. The exact whole Borel complex Let R be the actual coefficient field completed in delta=1-Q^N, retaining Q=Q_N(1-delta)^(1/N). Work first in the untwisted target frame, with memory K=Q^(-J), rho=Ad K and F=ad f. The ACTUAL whole arrow gauge B_s(q) sends f to the original F^(N)|_s and commutes with memory K. Conjugating the complex below by B_s carries all its units and source marks. The memory K is not the old physical high-color head clock. On any invariant spin module define \[ \begin{split} d_0C&=((\rho-I)C,FC),\\ d_1(X,Y)&=(\rho-Q^{-1})Y-Q^{-1}FX. \tag{2.1} \end{split} \] The identity rho F=Q^(-1)F rho proves d_1d_0=0 exactly over R. No root specialization has occurred. For spin l choose a basis v_0,...,v_L, L=2l, satisfying Fv_j=v_(j+1) and rho v_j=Q^(l-j)v_j. Each j<L gives a separate three-term fork \[ R\ \xrightarrow{a\mapsto(A_ja,a)}\ R^2 \xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto Q^{-1}(-x+A_jy)}\ R, \quad A_j=Q^{l-j}-1. \tag{2.2} \] It contracts using h_1(x,y)=y and h_2(z)=(-Qz,0), whether or not A_j vanishes at the root. The only remaining terms are \[ [R\xrightarrow{Q^{-l}-1}R]_{0,1},\qquad [R\xrightarrow{Q^l-Q^{-1}}R]_{1,2}. \tag{2.3} \] This is a literal direct decomposition, not a numerical rank argument. In particular it keeps both possible resonance lines. For W_N take l=N and normalize the chain by \[ v_j=\frac{(-1)^N}{(2N)!}(\operatorname{ad}f)^j e^N, \quad v_{2N}=f^N. \tag{2.4} \] The last equality follows by expanding the commutator: only its middle term survives, giving ad(f)^(2N)e^N=(-1)^N(2N)!f^N. The second arrow in (2.3) is a unit since its root is 1-Q_N^(-1). The entire complement therefore contracts to \[ \boxed{\ [R f^N\xrightarrow{,Q^{-N}-1,}R f^N]_{0,1}\ }, \qquad Q^{-N}-1=\frac\delta{1-\delta}. \tag{2.5} \] The coefficient has a SIMPLE zero, with derivative one. At the root H0 and H1 are each the one-dimensional marked wall line, and H2=0. Over the whole formal DVR, H0=0 and H1=R/(delta). Its root kernel and its first-normal Bockstein must therefore be retained together; no free whole horizontal source line is being asserted. ## 3. Explicit projection and contraction retaining every unit For x=sum x_jv_j, y=sum y_jv_j and z=sum z_jv_j, projection to (2.5) is pi_0(C)=C_(2N) and pi_1(x,y)=x_(2N); inclusion uses v_(2N) in degree zero and (v_(2N),0) in degree one. Put \[ \begin{split} h_1(x,y)&=\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}y_{j+1}v_j,\\ h_2(z)&=\left(-Q\sum_{j=1}^{2N}z_jv_{j-1},\ (Q^N-Q^{-1})^{-1}z_0v_0\right). \tag{3.1} \end{split} \] Direct substitution gives h_1d_0=I-iota_0pi_0, d_0h_1+h_2d_1=I-iota_1pi_1, and d_1h_2=I. Only Q^N-Q^(-1), a unit, is inverted. The wall delta is never inverted. Conjugating all maps by the ACTUAL B_s(q) gives the same contraction on the actual whole target complement Ad(B_s)W_N. The original source/co-source must be conjugated or evaluated with those same B_s units; root B_s=I does not erase their derivatives. In the unitary Fr metric ||v_k||^2=binom(N,k), e and f are adjoints. The highest-spin Hilbert--Schmidt module has an orthonormal chain with F-arrow coefficients sqrt((j+1)(2N-j)). Its anchored F inverse has norm 1/sqrt(2N). Using those coefficients in (3.1), its fork inverses have that same bound; the remaining unit inverse has root norm 1/[2 sin(pi/N)]. The orthogonal W_N projector has norm one. Hence the root complement contraction has norm O(N), explicitly at most max(1/sqrt(2N),1/[2 sin(pi/N)]). This is a bound on the COMPLEX contraction, not on every source functional or on a uniform off-root neighborhood. ## 4. The actual global co-source on the extra module Under (1.1), the basis (2.4) is \(\operatorname{ob}_N(v_j)=N!u^j/(2N-j)!\). Thus any ACTUAL cut functional Phi restricts to the global dual Čech class \[ c_\Phi(u)=\sum_{j=0}^{2N} \frac{(2N-j)!}{N!}\Phi(v_j)u^{-j-1} \quad\text{in }H^1(O(-2N-2)). \tag{4.1} \] Its residue pairing with ob_N(C) equals Phi(C) on W_N, by the [explicit two-chart source pairing](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). The two corner components occupy different north/south Laurent modes. Neither is a zero Čech class merely because it was absent from the degree-elevation image. For the normalized wall generator w=f^N/N!=E_(N,0), ||w||_HS=1, the ACTUAL paired coherent source gives \[ \Phi_m(w)=\left(\frac{1-m}{2}\right)^N, \qquad \Phi_+(w)=2^{-N}\quad(m=0). \tag{4.2} \] The uniform interval row gives instead \[ \Phi_{\mathrm{uni}}(w)=\frac1{N+1}. \tag{4.3} \] The ratio is 2^N/(N+1), GENUINELY exponential. For the unnormalized divided generator f^N the two values are N!/2^N and N!/(N+1). Their actual normalization has not been hidden by declaring its matrix unit to be the source value one. The coupled original source makes the head endpoint explicit: \(\Phi_{e_D}(w\otimes H_{\mathrm{head}})=2^{-N}(H_{\mathrm{head}})_{00}\). The Fr endpoints 0 and N are the SAME cyclic head endpoint. The uniform interval row is not that original coherent coupon. Since w is root Ward-closed, no root co-source homotopy on the full target can equate (4.2) and (4.3). There is still an exact relative-endpoint interpretation: Phi_m(w)dm/2=-d[((1-m)/2)^(N+1)/(N+1)]. Its interval integral from -1 to +1 is 1/(N+1), while its endpoint-coherent value at m=0 is 2^(-N). Exactness of a primitive does not eliminate its marked endpoint jump. The global class (4.1), actual normal units, and relative endpoint density remain together. The OTHER omitted corner w_high=E_(0,N) has response Phi_m(w_high)=((1+m)/2)^N. It is carried by the contracted forks, not a second H0 wall: Fw_high!=0. Its interval primitive is ((1+m)/2)^(N+1)/(N+1), with a nonzero POSITIVE-endpoint jump. Thus the two corners have different cochain roles even though their uniform integrals and their coherent values at m=0 agree. Contracting the highest corner requires its recorded Ward/source homotopy, rather than deleting its relative endpoint pairing. ## 5. An unavoidable charged FIRST ACTUAL R normal sees the wall In the constant actual integral frame, put I_1=R_0^(-1)R_1. For r=N its first resonant transfer, including every head entry, is exactly \[ (I_1)_{(-1,+1)}=N e\otimes f \otimes I_{\mathrm{heads}}. \tag{5.1} \] This is the original universal R tail, not an appended operator: the first-normal coefficient is kappa_N E^(N) tensor F^(N), kappa_N=N(-1)^(N-1), and E^(N)=(-1)^(N-1)e. All nonresonant normal terms change at most ONE Fr block, while Cartan terms change neither. Thus no other first-normal term can cancel the charged component (-1,+1) of (5.1). The actual whole diagonal arrow gauges B_s(q) add first-normal gauge terms of ZERO Fr block charge. They therefore cannot erase this charged channel; their units remain in all other rows. Let n=N-1 and choose actual old-head matrix coupons P_0=E_(0,0) and C_low=E_(n,0). Put X=E_N(P_0), Y=E_N(C_low). Their entries are \[ X=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/N,0,\ldots),\qquad Y=N^{-1}E_{N-1,0}+E_{N,1}. \] Here fY=Yf=w. Consequently the charged (-1,+N) component of the ACTUAL adjoint normal current is \[ \Pi_{(-1,+N)}[I_1,X\otimes Y] =N[e,X]\otimes w\otimes I_{\mathrm{heads}}. \tag{5.2} \] Its first factor is \([e,X]=-(N-1)E_{0,1}-(N-1)E_{1,2}/N\), an elevated old head current. The second factor is precisely the wall generator, not an element of I_N. At a generic root the first factor is a memory-Cartan Ward term, since its charge has unit Q_N-1. Thus (5.2) is a concrete LOCAL Ward/carry source with a wall-valued coefficient; it is not a closed scalar knot invariant by itself. Its two legitimate paired values are different: \[ (\Phi_{\mathrm{uni}}\otimes\Phi_{\mathrm{uni}})(5.2) =-\frac{N-1}{N+1},\qquad (\Phi_+\otimes\Phi_+)(5.2) =-\frac{N(N-1)}{2^{2N-1}}. \tag{5.3} \] Both are nonzero. The relative co-source can therefore detect this actual omitted-corner channel; it cannot be dropped as a zero Čech boundary or replaced by its uniform value. Under the controlled coupled-source gauge G, the e and f factors also acquire their literal head shifts V^(-1) and V. The source coupon must be conjugated WITH the operator. Leaving a head shift behind while changing the source would give a different pairing, potentially zero. No such change is made in (5.3). For the relative interaction-commutator used here, I(0)=I and its root commutator is zero. Thus its first coefficient depends only on (5.2), even when the input coupons and paired source have their actual whole lifts. This does NOT remove the separate lift terms in the whole Euler/current formula (8d) of the [endpoint-completed clock theorem](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md). That formula still uses the prescribed H_1 and its charged head neighbors. No general current descent follows by replacing it with this one isolated interaction channel. ## 6.
