Low raw PBW order versus ordered products and clock gauges A PBW operator of degree d<N has normalized coherent numerator divisible by (1+ut)^(N-d), so ob_N vanishes. In particular raw interaction coefficients of order j lie in the elevation image on every Fr leg whenever N>2j, by the actual all-normal bound. The first possible order for a raw PBW complement is ceil(N/2). This is an exclusion bound; attainment by a particular actual crossing or closed word is a separate assertion. This does NOT say multiplication by such a coefficient preserves the image: (5.2) is already a first-normal counterexample on elevated input coupons. Nor does it apply to a controlled source gauge containing genuine whole clock dilations. Their one-sided symbols can have nonzero ob_N even at root order. Their actions must be kept as whole functions with their source characters. The [Clebsch strictification](clebsch_memory_dilation_and_actual_r_excursions.md) keeps its complementary memory sector for precisely this reason; neither that construction nor (2.5) declares the full actual R network image-invariant. Every actual offimage current must be projected by (1.1) and then checked in the explicit complex (2.1). A CLOSED residual reduces to its ONE wall component; its value there uses the original source row, not automatically (4.3). The global geometric Ward/current map, its charged head neighbors and the selected regulator norm remain to be proved. This result replaces an arbitrary 2N+1-dimensional missing source by an exact single marked Bockstein wall line and exhibits an actual R channel which makes its source normalization unavoidable. [Exact actual-matrix/complex audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_complement_wall.py). [Results](../experiments/degree_elevation_complement_wall_results.json). title: The exact degree-elevation residual and its selected endpoint source
text: # The exact degree-elevation residual and its selected endpoint source Independent proof and source audit, 27 October 2026. Degree elevation maps the original head cut-Ward complex into the Fr source and preserves its original cut. Its missing operator channel has an explicit incidence polynomial. After the two Borel rows are contracted, one resonant endpoint remains, and its ACTUAL selected co-source differs exponentially from the uniform interval row. One-sided clock moments also have an explicit auxiliary correction. These formulas identify concrete data to compute in the relative orbit co-source test. They do not construct the internal geometric Gaussian map or a selected-volume estimate. ## 1. An explicit polynomial detects exactly the missing channel Use the actual divided Fr basis v_i of Sym^N and put \[ b_D(u,t)=\ell_N(u)D\psi_N(t),\qquad \mathfrak o_N(D)(u)=u^N b_D(u,-1/u) =\sum_{i,j=0}^N(-1)^j\binom NiD_{ij}u^{N+i-j}. \tag{1} \] This is a polynomial of degree at most 2N. The [degree-elevation map](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) satisfies \[ \ker\mathfrak o_N=\mathcal E_N\operatorname{End}(\mathrm{Sym}^{N-1}). \tag{2} \] Indeed the symbol numerator of E_N(C) is (1+tu)b_C. Conversely, vanishing in (1) says that the polynomial b_D is divisible by the irreducible polynomial 1+tu. The quotient has degree at most N-1 in each variable, hence is the unique symbol numerator of an old head matrix. Formula (2) is an EXACT image criterion, stronger than vanishing of the two extreme corners alone. Every degree 0,...,2N occurs from a matrix unit, so (1) is surjective. It realizes the full highest-spin quotient directly: \[ \begin{split} \mathfrak o_N([e,D])&=\partial_u\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N([f,D])&=(2Nu-u^2\partial_u)\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N([h,D])&=(2N-2u\partial_u)\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J}}D) &=Q^N\mathfrak o_N(D)(u/Q). \tag{3} \end{split} \] For example the commutator f acts on the normalized symbol by (-partial_t-u^2 partial_u); it differentiates 1+tu by -u(1+tu). Restriction to t=-1/u gives exactly the second line of (3). The other formulas follow the same way or by matrix units. For the original whole divided string gauge B_s of the head-Ward map, use instead \[ \mathfrak o_{N,s}(D)=\mathfrak o_N(B_s^{-1}DB_s). \tag{4} \] All B_s units and their normal derivatives remain present. A Fr Green/current matrix can use the old head co-source homotopy precisely when this polynomial vanishes, or after its nonzero remainder has been accounted for separately. ## 2. Independent contraction of the quotient current complex In the quotient write weight m=-N,...,N, let B=ad_f raise weight, and let A=Ad_K-I, K=Q^-J. The actual two-row complex is \[ d_0=(A,B),\qquad d_1(X,Y)=(\operatorname{Ad}_K-Q^{-1})Y-Q^{-1}BX. \tag{5} \] It is a complex because Ad_K B=Q^-1 B Ad_K. Put a_m=Q^-m-1 and Bv_m=b_m v_(m+1). Every b_m for m<N is a nonzero integer in characteristic zero, hence a unit. For each m<N the three-term summand is \[ R\xrightarrow{(a_m,b_m)}R^2 \xrightarrow{(-Q^{-1}b_m,Q^{-1}a_m)}R, \] which contracts using b_m. This works even when a_m=0, so the other root resonances at m=0 or -N leave no hidden classes. The remaining bottom degree-one arrow has coefficient Q^N-Q^-1, a unit near a primitive N-th root for N>=2, and contracts as well. What remains is EXACTLY \[ R\xrightarrow{Q^{-N}-1}R \quad\text{in degrees zero and one}. \tag{6} \] The top generator may be taken to be f^N=N!E_(N,0). With Z=Q^N and delta=1-Z, its differential is Q^-N-1=delta/Z. Thus the first-normal Bockstein has coefficient PLUS ONE in the delta convention, or -N in the Log Q normal. There is no degree-two quotient homology. This is the quotient theorem for the specified Fr MEMORY Cartan. It does not identify it with the original high-color quantum K. For the old physical clock C_Q=Q^S Z^R, the same endpoint changes Fr block R by N, so its conjugation character is Z^N instead. Those whole normal characters must not be interchanged because their root numerical values happen to coincide. There is an equally explicit root-cycle classification. A matrix commuting with the regular nilpotent f is a polynomial in f. Cartan closure at Q_N removes every power f^j except j=0,N. Thus every scalar-coefficient root cycle is \[ D=aI+cE_{N,0},\qquad c=D_{N,0}. \tag{6a} \] The old degree-elevation image contributes only the scalar part. With head coefficients the same statement holds entrywise; the actual selected head co-source must then be applied as well. The full quotient construction is recorded in [the complement Bockstein wall](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md). The unit-fork calculation above is an independent proof audit. ## 3. The original selected endpoint co-source is not the uniform row The uniform rank-one Fr cut and the selected coherent Fr cut give \[ \Phi_{\mathrm{uni}}(E_{N,0})=\frac1{N+1},\qquad \Phi_+(E_{N,0})=2^{-N},\qquad \Phi_{\mathrm{uni}}(f^N)=\frac{N!}{N+1}. \tag{7} \] These are literal matrix pairings in the actual divided basis. Under B_s the frozen uniform row acquires the retained whole factor B_(N,s)/B_(0,s); transporting the row itself compensates it exactly. The root factor is one, but its normal coefficients cannot be erased. E_(N,0) is Ward-closed at the root: it commutes with f, and its K conjugation character is Q^-N=1. Therefore the difference of the two co-sources in (7) is NOT Ward-exact on the full Fr target. Their ratio 2^N/(N+1) cannot be inferred to be a harmless algebraic normalization. The head-map homotopy applies on the image (2), where both extreme corners vanish; it does not extend to this additional endpoint class without its retained source. An exact source gauge can still compare the two descriptions by conjugating ALL currents and the endpoint generator too. It does not justify freezing that generator while replacing its co-source. In the coordinates (6a), the two root periods are respectively a+c/(N+1) and a+2^-N c. This source character is visible as a whole function, not just as a list of matrix values. For the actual paired Borel coupon e_(alpha,m)=psi_alpha lambda_m, \[ \mathfrak o_N(e_{\alpha,m})(u) =\left[(1+u)\frac{(1+m)u-(1-m)}2\right]^N, \qquad\Phi_m(E_{N,0})=((1-m)/2)^N. \tag{8} \] The normalized scale alpha cancels; its UNNORMALIZED power line alpha^N must still be retained in the original source object. At the selected m=0 the first polynomial is 2^-N(u^2-1)^N. The actual interval average over m=-1,...,1 instead integrates the second character to 1/(N+1). This explains both agreement on closed scalar cuts and disagreement on the new endpoint. The whole retained-weight interval comparison in [the global Cech source](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md) keeps its density; it does not assert that these two endpoint co-sources are equal or Ward-homotopic on the entire target. There is a head-matrix version for the actual coupled coupon e_D. Write s(i)=i for i<N and s(N)=0. Its Fr blocks are \[ (e_D)_{ij}=2^{-N}\binom Nj E_{s(i),s(j)}. \] Consequently \[ \mathfrak o_N(e_D)(u)=2^{-N}u^N a(u)b(u)^t, \tag{9} \] where a_0=1+u^N, b_0=1+(-1)^N u^-N, and for 1<=S<N, a_S=binom(N,S)u^S, b_S=(-1)^S binom(N,S)u^-S. This expression is a polynomial despite its factored Laurent notation. Its bottom and top coefficients are respectively (-1)^N2^-N E_00 and 2^-N E_00. In particular the ACTUAL selected functional satisfies \[ \Phi_{e_D}(E_{N,0}\otimes H) =2^{-N}H_{00}. \tag{10} \] The surviving source cannot be replaced by the uniform interval row merely because both return the same closed knot scalar. ## 4. Exact one-sided clock and Green moment corrections Split E=E_0+E_1 using its two terms, so (E_1C)_ij=(i/N)C_(i-1,j-1). For every retained scalar function g on the indicated finite spectra, \[ \begin{split} E(g(J_{\mathrm{head}})C) &=g(J_N)E_0(C)+g(J_N-1)E_1(C),\\ E(Cg(J_{\mathrm{head}})) &=E_0(C)g(J_N)+E_1(C)g(J_N-1). \tag{11} \end{split} \] The functions at the extra argument -1 may be chosen arbitrarily where their multiplier is zero; they must be regular wherever that multiplier is nonzero. These identities follow directly from the row and column indices. In particular \[ E(w^J C)=w^{J_N}\{E(C)+(w^{-1}-1)E_1(C)\}, \tag{12} \] and the polynomial moment correction is exactly the backward difference [p(J_N-1)-p(J_N)]E_1(C). Ad-clock covariance is strict because the same auxiliary offset cancels between row and column. One-sided Green moments do not have that cancellation. For normalized degree-h moments the backward difference contains the explicit powers N^-s, s=1,...,h; they are retained before any period/character estimate. ## 5. Whole word strictification retains a genuine auxiliary source There is a direct positive strictification of (11). On Sym^(N-1) tensor C^2 define \[ \begin{split} i_+v_k&=v_k\otimes u_0+v_{k-1}\otimes u_1,\\ p_+(v_k\otimes u_0)&=(N-k)v_k/N,\\ p_+(v_k\otimes u_1)&=(k+1)v_{k+1}/N. \end{split} \] Then p_+i_+=I and E(C)=p_+(C tensor I)i_+. The complementary projector is I-i_+p_+; it is the Sym^(N-2) channel. EXACTLY, \[ E(CD)-E(C)E(D) =p_+(C\otimes I)(I-i_+p_+)(D\otimes I)i_+. \tag{13} \] Thus the full auxiliary operator algebra is multiplicative and preserves an ordered actual word, while a product of upper compressions omits the displayed lower-channel excursions. The original head number is J_total minus the auxiliary bit; its two blocks have total degrees J_N and J_(N-2)+1. This is the operator explanation of (11)--(12). An exact source-preserving FINAL CUT choice even has both external ends in the upper channel. Set \[ \Psi=i_+\mathbf1_{N+1}=\mathbf1_N\otimes(u_0+u_1), \qquad\Lambda=\frac{\mathbf1_{N+1}^t}{N+1}p_+. \] Its auxiliary dual is correlated with the head: \[ \Lambda(v_k\otimes u_0)=\frac{N-k}{N(N+1)},\qquad \Lambda(v_k\otimes u_1)=\frac{k+1}{N(N+1)}. \] It pairs with Psi to one, annihilates the lower channel, and gives Lambda(C tensor I)Psi=sum(C_ij)/N for EVERY head C. The same holds for a full ordered word with all internal excursions kept. A product auxiliary dual is a different source. Closed/pivotal strands require their actual transported caps and pivot operators; the unweighted final-cut identity does not substitute for those. This is an auxiliary matrix-word extension of the old head R, not an equality with the existing actual high-integral-color R. ## 6. The precise remaining relative source calculation For the norm-orbit test Lambda_rel omega, the new head map removes the cut K/F rows on its image by its actual co-source homotopy. An arbitrary Fr-valued current first has the explicit remainder (1)/(4). The quotient contraction (6) reduces its cohomological source obstruction to the one resonant endpoint; its selected weight is (7)--(10), NOT automatically the uniform row. This does not prove that the two INTERNAL framing Green currents land in that head image, or that their remaining relative endpoint and logarithmic carry classes cancel. A map of those actual currents must retain (11), all lower excursions in (13), the physical versus memory-clock distinction, charged normal head neighbors, the original chirp and full peripheral line. The explicit residual polynomials and endpoint coefficient are now finite tests for that map, rather than a general group-theoretic identification or an assumed scalar normalization. [Exact residual/source audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_wall_residual.py).

title: The divided adjoint pairs nontrivially with the actual missing edge
text: # The divided adjoint pairs nontrivially with the actual missing edge Research proof, 27 October 2026. The genuine complete integral Weyl color gives a divided Hopf-adjoint operator on its matrix space. Applied to the literal missing cyclic edge, it has an exact nonzero pairing with the prescribed marked cut. This yields a cohomologous divided-normal realization of the original knot cut functional. It does not prove survival of the geometric Gaussian period. ## 1. The two normal directions are distinct Keep `Q=q^2`, `x=-M/q`. In the balanced basis the generic truncated raising entries are Ecal_(a-1,a)=M Q^(-a)-M^(-1), 1<=a<N. The absent cyclic entry is the specified coefficient w(q,M)=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1), W=E_(N-1,0). It vanishes identically on the genuine integral Weyl color `M=-q^N`. At the fixed root `Q^N=1` it becomes `w=kappa=M-M^(-1)`. These two restrictions are different normal directions. If `delta=1-Q^N`, their exact relation is w=kappa+M delta/(1-delta). At the complete intersection `M=1,delta=0`, one has `dw=d kappa+d delta`; the Weyl curve is `w=0`, not `kappa=0`. No tensor divided power below is identified with the generic-M cyclic-edge normal by replacing one parameter with the other. ## 2. The actual divided Hopf adjoint Take the genuine Weyl family `V(q)=D_(N-1)(q)` on `M=-q^N`, as in [the factorial fusion proof](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md). For a matrix `T` its actual generic Hopf adjoint is A(T)=ad_Ecal(T)=[Ecal,T]K^(-1). Write `A=X+Y`, with X(T)=Ecal T K^(-1), Y(T)=-T Ecal K^(-1). Then `XY=Q YX` and `X^N=Y^N=0` for every generic `q`. Hence the same q-binomial cancellation as for the tensor divided power defines a regular actual operator on the root matrix space: J_ad=[A^N/(1-Q^N)]_(q=q_N) =sum_(j=1)^(N-1) c_j Y^(N-j)X^j, c_j=N/[(Q;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(N-j)]. (1) This is the divided **Hopf** adjoint. It need not equal ordinary commutation by the divided power on `V`; that latter power is zero on the individual color. Formula (1) retains the mixed antipode terms acting through `V tensor V*`. ## 3. Exact action on the missing edge At the actual root set epsilon_a=Q^(-a)-1, P_a=product_(s=1)^a epsilon_s, P_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N, K^N=(-1)^(N-1)I. Let `l=N-j`. The `j`-th term of (1) applied to `W=E_(N-1,0)` is supported only at matrix entry `(l-1,l)`. Its coefficient is c_j (-1)^l Q^(-l(l-1)/2-jl) P_(N-1) epsilon_l K^(-N). Using c_j=c_l=(-1)^(l-1)Q^(-l(l-1)/2)/(1-Q^l), epsilon_l=(1-Q^l)Q^(-l), and `Q^N=1`, every coefficient simplifies to `-N`. Therefore J_ad(W)=-N sum_(l=1)^(N-1) E_(l-1,l). (2) This holds for every `N>=2`, with the original balanced root basis. For the literal marked source and co-source, e_(a,b)=1/N, Phi(T)=Tr(eT)=Tr(g D T), equation (2) gives the exact nonzero pairing Phi(J_ad(W))=-(N-1). (3) The normalized ordinary trace of (2) is zero. Thus the marked normal pairing is visible before the ordinary scalar Ward quotient. Its degrees are explicit: `W` raises matrix index by `N-1`, `J_ad` lowers it by `N`, and the marked cut supplies the remaining one-step pairing. This is a mixed divided-normal/missing-edge cochain calculation, not a nonzero closed geometric class. ## 4. An actual cohomologous divided-normal cut Define the literal all-matrices row Phi_div(T)=-Phi(J_ad(T W))/(N-1). (4) Equation (3) says `Phi_div(I)=1`. Let `delta_W(T)=([K,T],[F,T])` and let `h_W` be the explicit actual Ward contraction in [the finite Ward note](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md), so h_W delta_W=I-i p, p(T)=Tr(T)/N, i(c)=c I. Since `(Phi_div-Phi)i=0`, one obtains the exact cochain homotopy on **all** matrices, Phi_div-Phi=(Phi_div-Phi)h_W delta_W. (5) In particular every actual closed cut tangle is Ward closed, hence equals `F_N(1) I`. Equations (4)--(5) give Phi_div(C_K)=Phi(C_K)=F_N(1)=Kashaev_N(K). (6) Thus (4) is an explicit divided-normal source realization of the original invariant, with its source and normalization fixed. It is not a new invariant or a redefinition of its numerical values. The full ADO value retains the entire external marked line; at completion it multiplies (6) by `i^(N+3)/N`. That scalar is not absorbed into (4). ## 5. Pivotal partial trace commutes with the genuine divided adjoint For the genuine generic integral colors use the generic pivotal partial trace ptr_K(T)=Tr_closed[(I tensor K_closed)T]. The generic Hopf adjoint and this trace commute on every matrix. This follows from the ordinary antipode cancellation; equivalently the generic pivotal cap is a Hopf map. Apply the generic identity to the `N`-th adjoint power and divide both sides by `1-Q^N`. The divided operators are regular by the q-binomial argument on the corresponding tensor-and-dual colors. Specialization gives ptr_K J_ad,total=J_ad,cut ptr_K. (7) At the root, the actual pivot satisfies `g_closed=K_closed^(1-N)=chi_closed^(-1)K_closed`, where the entire scalar `chi_closed=K_closed^N` is retained. Thus (7) holds also for the original actual pivotal partial trace `ptr_g`. The order of the marked edge matters. For an arbitrary full tensor matrix `T`, the cut edge lifts as `W_cut tensor I_closed`, so the exact all-matrices identity is Phi_div(ptr_g T) =-Phi(ptr_g[J_ad,total(T(W_cut tensor I))])/(N-1). (8) Here `ptr_g(T(W_cut tensor I))=(ptr_g T)W_cut` was used. There is no license to replace the argument of `J_ad,total` by `T` and move the edge unchanged outside it. The mixed Hopf-adjoint terms are essential. Equations (7)--(8) transport the new source through the actual contraction while keeping its insertion order. ## 6. What this proves about cohomology and HPL The action `J_ad` lowers matrix weight by `N`, so its square is zero on `End(V_N)`. It annihilates `I` and has zero normalized ordinary trace on every matrix. It consequently induces a chain map on the split image Ward complex: set J_ad^1(delta_W T)=delta_W(J_ad T). This is well defined because the kernel of `delta_W` is `k I` and `J_ad(I)=0`. Its action on scalar Ward cohomology is zero. Likewise the marked row `Phi J_ad` is Ward exact, by composing the old cut homotopy with this chain map. This is consistent with the nonzero cochain pairing (3): the missing edge is not Ward closed. The normalized row (4), in contrast, has the same **nonzero** cohomology class as the original cut, by (5). It is now represented using a genuine divided adjoint and the literal missing edge. This gives concrete source data for a future source-preserving Gaussian chain comparison. It does not construct that comparison or show which geometric formal class has nonzero image. Nilpotence of an inserted operator and exact scalar Ward normalization alone do not supply the missing HPL map or an asymptotic volume theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_divided_ward_factorial_fusion.py) and [results](../experiments/divided_ward_factorial_fusion_results.json) check (2)--(5) on every matrix unit at seven levels and verify the all-matrices pivotal and ordered-insertion identities (7)--(8).

title: A divided-normal source orbit and the canonical framing form
text: # A divided-normal source orbit and the canonical framing form Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual divided Hopf adjoints contain a two-dimensional standard SL2 module. Its cut Borel orbit is an explicit sign cover of the classical framing torsor, with the correct canonical two-form and leading co-source covariance. The same normal matrices admit a concrete clock/shift realization and a regular diagonal comparison with the actual cyclic source. These are algebraic source, group, and density maps. They do not identify this source orbit with the two internal critical framing coordinates of the knot network. The exact loss of information after a normalized cut is computed below, rather than suppressed. The later [unprojectivized high-color source theorem](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md) realizes a marked Borel torsor using ACTUAL Sym^N divided source vectors and their contragredient co-source. Retaining scale U and one actual descendant m gives Omega_cut=(A/N)dlog U wedge dm; an actual old-clock normal row detects that scale. This retains the prequantum character erased by a normalized projector. It does not infer the full network-current comparison from the standard group/density formulas already proved here. ## 1. The actual standard module and its cut covector At complete color fix N>=2, Q=q_N^2, and the original balanced space V_N. Let W=E_(N-1,0), U=sum_(j=0)^(N-2) E_(j,j+1), Ubar=U/(N-1). The [complete divided-Ward theorem](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md) proves for the true divided Hopf adjoints J_E,J_F that J_E(W)=-N U, J_E(U)=0, J_F(U)=N W, J_F(W)=0. Consequently on L=span(Ubar,W), the operators e_sl=-J_E/[N(N-1)], f_sl=(N-1)J_F/N, h_sl=[e_sl,f_sl] are exactly the standard two-dimensional SL2 Lie matrices in the ordered basis (Ubar,W). This action exponentiates algebraically on L. It is an action on the **linear source space**: the divided Hopf coproduct has mixed terms, so no action by automorphisms of the full matrix multiplication algebra is inferred. For the actual cut Phi(C)=Tr(e C), e_ij=1/N, one has Phi(Ubar)=Phi(W)=1/N. Thus the restricted cut covector is phi=(1,1)/N. Let G_phi be the SL2 Borel preserving its projective line. For v=a Ubar+b W, z=a+b!=0, there is a unique g in G_phi with gW=v. In these source coordinates it is g_v=[[a+1/z,a],[b-1/z,b]], det(g_v)=1, phi g_v=z phi. (1) This proves directly that the open source orbit z!=0 is a genuine G_phi torsor with anchor W, not merely a dimension count. ## 2. An equivariant sign cover of the geometric B1 framing torsor Let j(g)=z(g)g^(-T), where phi g=z(g)phi. It has row sums one and determinant z(g)^2. Since z is a character, j is a group homomorphism. Its kernel is {I,-I}; it is the usual sign cover of the row-stochastic PGL2 cut Borel, with the sign retained. Take F_0=[[0,1],[1,-1]] and define F(v)=F_0 j(g_v)^(-1) =[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], r=a/z, s=z^(-2). (2) Every regular framing matrix of this form has two lifts, related by v->-v. Source left translation g_0 sends F(v) -> F(v) j(g_0)^(-1). Thus (2) has exactly the established right-frame action convention; replacing j(g)^(-1) by j(g) would reverse it. Pull back the canonical complete framing two-form and cut coordinate: Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], A_cut=1/(1+s). On the open set 1+z^2!=0 their exact source expressions are Omega_src=2 da wedge db/(1+z^2), A_src=z^2/(1+z^2). (3) Indeed dr wedge ds=-2 z^(-4) da wedge db, and s(1+s)=(1+z^2)z^(-4). No determinant or sign is omitted. For the two geometric cut stabilizers xi_1=h+2f, xi_2=e+f, the corresponding source matrices are -xi_i^T. Their vector fields are X_1=(-a-2b)partial_a+b partial_b, X_2=-b partial_a-a partial_b. Both satisfy X_i(z)=-z and div_(Omega_src) X_i=2 A_src. (4) Their images under (2) are exactly the two compensated geometric fields in [the residual Ward proof](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md). Equation (4) is the same leading covariance as the actual cut co-source b_i/H=-2 A_cut. This is an explicit source-level density comparison with its fixed group convention. The divided action on L and the ordinary finite Ward action on the network are distinct actions. Equation (4) does not by itself intertwine them or identify their internal source coordinates. ## 3. The relative centralizer coordinate and its transgression The geometric additive centralizer coordinate is tau=r/s=a z. The source vector field V=z^(-1)(partial_a-partial_b) has V(tau)=1 and V(A_src)=0. Direct contraction gives iota_V Omega_src=dlog A_src, Omega_src=dtau wedge dlog A_src. (5) Therefore the marked interval tau=0,...,1 transgresses the source form to exactly the canonical logarithmic cut form. Translating both endpoints by a regular function tau_0(A_src) changes neither this two-form nor that relative class. Poles of such a section require their marked boundary lattice; (5) does not delete them. This gives a concrete classical source orbit for the same relative framing complex. To make it the **network's** source comparison, the actual boundary currents must still be sent to its endpoint and logarithmic-carry co-sources. The [full-certificate calculation](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md) states those unresolved currents explicitly. ## 4. The orbit matrix is an actual cyclic quantum-torus generator Put c=a/(N-1). In the original finite matrix algebra, v=c U+b W, K v=Q v K, v^N=b c^(N-1) I. (6) The last identity follows by following one complete cyclic string. For a b!=0, v and the clock K give the split cyclic torus, not only an abstract two-dimensional representation. There is an explicit regular diagonal comparison with the actual E-cyclic source from [the coherent crossing proof](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md). At M=1 write epsilon_j=Q^(-j)-1, P_j=product_(l=1)^j epsilon_l, P_0=1. Every P_j, j<N, is nonzero and P_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N. Set mu=b c^(N-1)/P_(N-1), D_jj=P_j/c^j. Then D commutes with K and direct arrow comparison gives D(Ecal_head+mu W)D^(-1)=v. (7) The transformed F is fixed by the original Casimir: Ftilde=(-2-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1))v^(-1), Ftilde^N=0. (8) Thus the orbit has a rational matrix gauge into a genuine actual source family. This does not assert that its G_phi action preserves matrix multiplication or the knot's entire intertwiner network. The source coordinate A_src in (3) is still a parameter function; it has not been identified with the physical clock x/K by (6). ## 5. The original cut has an exact marked cyclic anchor For z!=0 define the normalized matrix coupon e_v=(N/z) v e. It has rank one, trace one and e_v^2=e_v, since e v e=(z/N)e. Its entries are explicit: (e_v)_ij=r/(N-1), i<N-1, (e_v)_(N-1,j)=1-r, r=a/z. (9) The **whole coupon**, not only its diagonal restriction, loses the scale z. Its row Phi_v(C)=Tr(e_v C) is cohomologous to the original normalized cut on the actual split Ward complex, by (Phi_v-Phi)h delta=Phi_v-Phi. On closed scalar cut operators it therefore returns exactly the original invariant. At r_*=(N-1)/N, equation (9) is literally e_v=e on all matrices. Retaining the shift and its eigenvalue mark fixes the scale as well: the actual point v_*=(N-1)Ubar+W=U+W=S, S^N=I, S e=e, e=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)S^j (10) is the original cyclic shift and selected eigenprojector. It has a_*=N-1,b_*=1,z_*=N. Its image in (2)--(3) is the exact source orbit section r_*=1-1/N, s_*=1/N^2, A_*=N^2/(N^2+1), tau_*=N(N-1). (11) The companion gauge (7) has c=1 and mu=1/[(-1)^(N-1)N] there. Thus the original cut has an intrinsic cyclic-source anchor; it is not fixed by normalized coupon data alone. Equation (11) approaches a framing boundary as N grows. It is a section of the constructed source orbit, not yet a proof that the network's geometric period is evaluated at that same section. There is a second exact restriction. For any diagonal cut array, Phi_v(C)=r sum_(j<N-1)C_jj/(N-1)+(1-r)C_(N-1,N-1). (12) Every actual uninserted one-cut array is diagonal before its final internal sums. Hence (12) probes only one strand-index weight; the two orbit parameters do not themselves create two internal flow coordinates. The divided-adjoint cut is likewise precisely the endpoint functional on these arrays, as proved in the full-certificate note. A pre-collapse source-current map remains necessary. ## 6. The logarithmic normal comparison has a separate scale The [strict Fock-to-normal comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md) retains resonant U^k sectors and the relative endpoint U, on the marked logarithmic torsor. The bare geometric pullback here is u=Log U=N Log A_src, Omega_cut=(1/N)dtau_geo wedge du. It does not identify the Fock coherent parameter with tau_geo. At the physical H_N=2pi*i/N, a putative canonical phase tau_geo Log A/H_N is tau_geo u/(2pi*i), whereas the exact source kernel is exp(s_Fock u). Matching them would rescale the endpoint and change U to U^(1/(2pi*i)); that adapter has not been established. The exact orbit and density identities above do not permit discarding this marked factor. The source orbit, clock gauge, cyclic anchor, and leading density are now explicit. The selected internal framing map, endpoint and carry cancellation for the full scalar certificate, and the regulator norm are still unproved. No volume limit follows here. [Exact symbolic and actual-matrix audit](../experiments/audit_divided_source_framing_orbit.py). [Results](../experiments/divided_source_framing_orbit_results.json). [Independent proof audit](divided_source_framing_orbit_independent_audit.md).

title: Independent audit of the divided-source framing orbit
text: # Independent audit of the divided-source framing orbit Audit, 27 October 2026, of [the explicit framing-orbit note](divided_source_framing_orbit.md). The group/sign-cover, density, cyclic-source gauge and marked-anchor claims are correct in their stated domains. None identifies this orbit with the internal framing of the knot network. The actual divided Ward block is standard SL2 in the ordered basis Ubar,W: the rescalings give eW=Ubar, fUbar=W, and both opposite actions zero. The cut covector is (1,1)/N. For z=a+b!=0, g_v=[a+1/z a;b-1/z b] has determinant one, carries W to v, and multiplies that covector by z. These equations determine its first column uniquely, proving free transitivity rather than only matching dimensions. The contragredient is essential. Since (1,1)g=z(1,1), the matrix j(g)=z g^(-T) has row sums one. It is a homomorphism with kernel {+I,-I}. Conversely a row-stochastic invertible matrix has two preimages after choosing the square root of its determinant. Thus this is exactly the retained SL2 sign cover. The inverse right-frame action gives F_0 j(g_v)^(-1)=[a/z b/z;z^(-2) -z^(-2)]. The opposite choice F_0j(g_v) would not have the asserted action convention. With r=a/z and s=z^(-2), direct differentiation gives -dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]=2 da wedge db/(1+z^2). The source matrices -xi_i^T give the two vector fields in the note. Their ordinary coordinate divergence is zero, while X_i(z)=-z, so their divergence in this density is 2z^2/(1+z^2)=2A_src. This matches the actual leading co-source sign. Also tau=a z and V=z^(-1)(partial_a-partial_b) obey Vtau=1, VA_src=0, and contraction with the density gives dlog A_src. The stated relative transgression is therefore exact. For the matrix comparison, D_j=P_j/c^j sends each upper edge epsilon_(j+1) to c. Its wrap sends mu to mu P_(N-1)/c^(N-1)=b. Hence D E_mu D^(-1)=v. The clock commutes with D, so the original Casimir identity fixes Ftilde in the stated order (-2-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1))v^(-1). Its N-th power is zero because it is conjugate to the actual truncated F. This gauge requires a,b!=0, as explicitly stated; the whole source orbit only requires z!=0 and is larger than that companion chart. The normalized coupon is literally e_v=(N/z)v e, whose first N-1 rows are r/(N-1) and last row is 1-r. Thus its entire response on arbitrary matrices depends only on r. For the split Ward contraction h delta=I-i p, p=Tr/N, the difference between its row and the original row vanishes on I. Therefore (Phi_v-Phi)h delta=Phi_v-Phi; the stated cochain homotopy is valid. This proves neither equality on arbitrary matrix insertions nor an internal two-coordinate source map. At r=(N-1)/N one has v=(z/N)S, S=U+W. The exact permutation identities are S^N=I, Se=e and e=(1/N)sum_j S^j. The first condition on v alone permits z/N in mu_N. Its marked eigenvalue one on e forces z/N=1. Thus the extra clock/eigenvalue mark really restores z=N; normalized coupon data alone cannot do so. Substitution gives precisely r=1-1/N, s=1/N^2, A=N^2/(N^2+1), tau=N(N-1), and mu=1/[(-1)^(N-1)N]. Independent exact checks verified the sign-cover matrix, form and vertical current symbolically, and S^N, Se and the full projector identity at eleven integer levels N=2,...,12. The proof arguments above establish the general statements. The physical 2pi*i polarization factor and the pre-collapse network source comparison remain outside these conclusions, as the note correctly records.

title: Independent proof audit of the divided Ward / marked-edge bridge
text: # Independent proof audit of the divided Ward / marked-edge bridge Audit, 27 October 2026. I checked the current proofs in [the marked divided-adjoint note](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md), [factorial fusion](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md), [the general complete-color construction](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md), and section 5.1 of [the unfolded Ward theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md). No defect was found in the stated operator, source, pivot, or moving-representation identities. This is a proof audit; I did not rerun the authors' matrix checks. ## 1. The divided adjoint and its exact marked pairing For \(\mathcal E=\rho^2E\), the genuine generic Hopf adjoint is \[ A(T)=[\mathcal E,T]K^{-1}=X(T)+Y(T),\qquad X=L_{\mathcal E}R_{K^{-1}},\quad Y=-R_{\mathcal E K^{-1}}. \] The relation \(K\mathcal E=Q\mathcal E K\) gives \(XY=QYX\). On the individual integral Weyl color, \(X^N=Y^N=0\) identically before specialization. The mixed \(Q\)-binomial coefficients have the single canceled factor \(1-Q^N\), giving the stated regular divided Hopf adjoint. Ordinary commutation by a one-factor divided matrix would lose these mixed terms. For \(W=E_{N-1,0}\), the term \(Y^lX^j\), \(j+l=N\), has only the entry \((l-1,l)\). Its phase is \[ (-1)^lQ^{-l(l-1)/2-jl} P_{N-1}\epsilon_lK^{-N}. \] Using \[ c_l=\frac{(-1)^{l-1}Q^{-l(l-1)/2}}{1-Q^l},\quad \epsilon_l=(1-Q^l)Q^{-l},\quad P_{N-1}K^{-N}=N, \] the sign is \(-1\) and the exponent is \(-lN\). Thus every superedge coefficient is exactly \(-N\), including even and composite \(N\): \[ J_{\mathrm{ad}}(W)=-N\sum_{l=1}^{N-1}E_{l-1,l}. \] For the literal marked row \(\Phi(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(eT)\), \(e_{ab}=1/N\), this gives \(\Phi(J_{\mathrm{ad}}W)=-(N-1)\). Consequently \[ \Phi_{\mathrm{div}}(T)=-\frac{\Phi(J_{\mathrm{ad}}(TW))}{N-1} \] has \(\Phi_{\mathrm{div}}(I)=1\). Its equality with the original row on scalar cut operators is exact. The all-matrices homotopy \[ \Phi_{\mathrm{div}}-\Phi =(\Phi_{\mathrm{div}}-\Phi)h_W\delta_W \] follows directly from \(h_W\delta_W=I-ip\) and the fact that the row difference kills \(I\). It neither assumes nor supplies a geometric representative for that scalar cohomology class. ## 2. Partial trace: the generic pivot and the insertion order For the genuine generic integral color, the compatible pivot is \(K\). The all-matrices pivotal partial trace intertwines the Hopf adjoint. This can be checked on generators: the closed \(E\)-terms cancel because \(K^{-1}K=I\), and the closed \(F\)-terms cancel by the same cyclic trace identity. Thus it intertwines every power, and hence the quotient by \(1-Q^N\) before specialization. The total tensor-and-dual divided adjoint is regular: its multinomial expansion has individual nilpotent powers and the same canceled root factors. Therefore the divided partial-trace identity specializes legitimately. Only after this specialization does one use \[ g=K^{1-N}=(K^N)^{-1}K \] with \(K^N\) scalar. This proves the identity for the actual root pivot \(g\). It does not replace the generic \(g\)-pivot by \(K\) while taking a derivative. The nonconstant derivative of \(K^{-N}\) is correctly retained in the separate normal adapter calculation. For an arbitrary full matrix \(T\), \[ \operatorname{ptr}_g(T(W\otimes I)) =(\operatorname{ptr}_gT)W. \] Combining this with divided-adjoint naturality gives exactly the stated ordered formula for \(\Phi_{\mathrm{div}}\operatorname{ptr}_g\). It does not give a formula with the edge moved outside \(J_{\mathrm{ad,total}}\). The note retains the correct order. ## 3. Fusion and the even-level character The generic ordered factorial product equals the finite quantum exponential of the total raising matrix. At degree \(kN+s\), cancellation gives \[ \left[ \frac{(Q;Q)_{kN+s}}{(1-Q^N)^k} \right]_{\mathrm{root}} =N^k k!(Q;Q)_s. \] Thus the full root defect is \(\exp((-t)^NJ_b/N)\), not merely its first term. All powers terminate by total-position degree. The inherited block term is \(J_X\otimes\chi_Y\), where \[ \chi_Y=K_Y^N=(-1)^{(N-1)\operatorname{length}(Y)}. \] Expanding the two sides of the additive three-block identity cancels every inherited \(J\) term. Within each side the remaining operators commute because the inner mixed term commutes with its block's total raising operator and \(K\). Exponentiation therefore proves the displayed twisted associativity. The factor \(\chi\) is essential at even \(N\); the signs in the notes are correct. The extension to both divided \(E\) and \(F\) directions is explicitly not asserted unipotent. The invariant two-dimensional block with opposite nilpotents generates an \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) action, consistently with that qualification. ## 4. The moving representation retains exactly one resonant log term In the integral lift, \(C(Q)\) is nilpotent generically and \[ C(Q)^N=(1-Q^N)J_b(Q) \] with \(J_b(Q)\) regular. Thus evaluating the unfolded logarithm at \(-tC(Q)\) is a finite rational matrix calculation. For \(m\ge N\) not divisible by \(N\), its denominator \(1-Q^m\) is a unit at the root, while \(C(Q)^m\) has at least one \(1-Q^N\) factor. For \(m=kN\), \(k\ge2\), its numerator has \(k\) such factors and its denominator only one. These terms vanish at the root. The only extra surviving logarithm term is \[ \frac{(-t)^N J_b}{N}. \] Since \(J_b\) commutes with the root total raising operator, exponentiation gives the exact finite ghost times the literal nilpotent factorial. Higher ghost powers arise from this exponential, even though higher dilogarithm powers vanish before exponentiation. With \(Q=Q_Ne^h\), \(C(Q)^N=-NhJ_b+O(h^2)\). Substitution into the coefficientwise pole \(-\operatorname{Li}_2((-tC(Q))^N)/(N^2h)\) gives the same surviving term, with its sign. Setting \(C^N=0\) first would incorrectly discard it. ## 5. The two normals and the remaining global issue The absent generic edge \[ w(Q,M)=MQ^{-N}-M^{-1} \] vanishes on the integral Weyl curve \(M=-q^N\), but restricts to \(\kappa\) on the root wall. The exact auxiliary defect \[ [\mathcal E,F]-\rho(K-K^{-1}) =-(1-Q^N)w(Q,M)E_{N-1,N-1} \] is correct by direct adjacent-entry subtraction. The routewise pivot/twist adapter is likewise the product of the \(b-1\) closed factors \(K^{-N}\) and the writhe correction. Its root value is one by knot parity; its derivative retains the closed-position moment. The notes distinguish these normals. The marked divided row is a concrete new realization of the original cut class and is transported through exact finite partial trace. It does not yet map the partial geometric Gaussian block into that class. Ordinary full closure still kills an uncompensated positive divided ghost by position degree, and the nonzero marked-edge tests are cochain tests. No passage to a selected global geometric coefficient follows from these identities alone; the notes' scope statements correctly preserve that distinction.

title: The divided Ward power is an exact unipotent factorial fusion defect
text: # The divided Ward power is an exact unipotent factorial fusion defect Research proof, 27 October 2026. Work in the genuine generic quantum group Weyl color `D_(N-1)(q)`, whose complete root specialization is the original Kashaev color. A mixed first-normal divided power on two factors is nonzero although the individual divided powers vanish. It is exactly the multiplicativity defect of the literal finite Ward factorial. The defects have a coherent associative fusion law, with the even-level Frobenius signs retained. These are operator and normal-source statements. They do not prove that the ghost survives the selected scalar knot contraction. ## 1. The integral Weyl lift and its divided power Put `Q=q^2`, `rho=q-q^(-1)`. On `D_(N-1)(q)` use F v_a=v_(a+1), E v_a=[a]_q [N-a]_q v_(a-1), K v_a=q^(N-1-2a) v_a, 0<=a<N, with endpoint vectors zero. These are genuine finite quantum-group matrices for generic `q`. In the meridian convention `x=-M/q`, their color is `x=q^(N-1)`, hence `M=-q^N`. At `q_N=exp(pi*i/N)` this is the complete color `M=1`, including even and composite `N`. Use `Ecal=rho^2 E`; its coproduct is Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal. In the balanced basis `w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a`, the raising coefficient is Ecal w_a=(q^(-N)-q^(N-2a))w_(a-1). At the root this becomes `(Q^(-a)-1)w_(a-1)`, the actual complete matrix. These basis changes are units at the root for `a<N`. On two factors put A=Ecal tensor K, B=1 tensor Ecal, C=A+B. They satisfy `AB=Q BA`, and `A^N=B^N=0` for every generic `q`. The normal-ordered q-binomial expansion is C^N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) {N choose j}_Q B^(N-j) A^j. Every coefficient has a simple factor `1-Q^N`; its quotient is regular at every primitive `N`-th root. Thus the literal first-normal operator J=[C^N/(1-Q^N)]_(q=q_N) is well defined and equals J=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) N B^(N-j) A^j/[(Q;Q)_j (Q;Q)_(N-j)]. (1) Here `(Q;Q)_(N-1)=N`. This is the scaled divided quantum-group power, not an arbitrary operator added to the root color. It records the specified generic integral lift. Its individual one-factor counterpart is zero because `Ecal^N=0` identically there. One has `[J,C]=0`, and `J^2=0`: both follow from the generic identity, or from total-index lowering by `N` in a two-factor space whose maximum total index is `2N-2`. Every generic braid intertwines `C`, so division by the scalar and specialization show that it also intertwines `J`. ## 2. A uniform explicit nonzero entry The vector `w_(N-1) tensor w_1` has only one surviving term in (1), namely `j=N-1`. Its coefficient is `1/(1-Q)`. At the root, Ecal^(N-1)w_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N w_0, Ecal w_1=(1-Q)Q^(-1)w_0, K^(N-1)w_1=q_N^((N-1)(N-3))w_1. The phase therefore simplifies, using `q_N^N=-1`, to J(w_(N-1) tensor w_1)=-N q_N w_0 tensor w_0. (2) This proves nonvanishing at every `N>=2` with the original balanced root normalization. No odd-level restriction is used. ## 3. Exact factorial fusion, including all degrees Define the positive-argument finite factorial p_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) X^j/(Q;Q)_j. At generic `q`, q-binomial expansion gives the finite identity p_N(B)p_N(A)=sum_(n=0)^(2N-2) C^n/(Q;Q)_n. (3) Indeed the coefficient of `B^i A^j` on both sides is `1/[(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j]`; terms with either index at least `N` vanish. For `n=N+s`, cancel `1-Q^N` in (3) before taking the root. Since [(Q;Q)_(N+s)/(1-Q^N)]_root=N (Q;Q)_s, the resulting summand is `J C^s/[N(Q;Q)_s]`. Terms with `s>=N-1` vanish by total degree. Therefore the exact root identity is p_N(B)p_N(A)=(I+J/N)p_N(C). (4) The literal Ward polynomial has argument `-t Ecal`, not positive `Ecal`. Thus its corresponding form is p_N(-tB)p_N(-tA) =(I+(-t)^N J/N)p_N(-tC). (5) The sign `(-t)^N` must not be suppressed. The first missing degree is `N`, but (4)--(5) identify the **entire** finite product defect. Since `J^2=0`, its logarithm is exactly `(-t)^N J/N`. This is also the resonant logarithm of the unfolded factorial. The degree-`N` term of `log p_infinity(X)=sum_m X^m/[m(1-Q^m)]` is `X^N/[N(1-Q^N)]`. Along the specified tensor lift its regular value is `J/N`. The normal extension, rather than the bare root identity `C^N=0`, retains this term. ## 4. Coherent fusion on arbitrary ordered blocks For an ordered block `X` of Steinberg factors let `C_X` be its total `Ecal`, `K_X` its total `K`, and J_X=[C_X^N/(1-Q^N)]_root, chi_X=K_X^N=(-1)^((N-1) length(X)) I. Regularity of `J_X` follows from the ordered q-multinomial expansion: all nonzero exponent tuples have entries below `N`, while the numerator has the factor `1-Q^N`. The operator lowers total degree by `N`, and satisfies `[J_X,C_X]=[J_X,K_X]=0` at the root. For any `k,s` with `0<=s<N`, direct factor grouping gives [(Q;Q)_(kN+s)/(1-Q^N)^k]_root =N^k k! (Q;Q)_s. Consequently the root of the generic finite quantum exponential is E_X(t)=exp[(-t)^N J_X/N] p_N(-t C_X). (6) The exponential is finite: its `k`-th term lowers total degree by `kN`, so it terminates before `k=length(X)`. Formula (6) is also the ordered product of the individual factorials, with each individual raising generator dressed by all later `K` factors. For two consecutive blocks define the mixed divided power j_(X,Y)=J_(X tensor Y)-J_X tensor chi_Y-1 tensor J_Y. The coproduct q-binomial expansion gives explicitly j_(X,Y)=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) N (1 tensor C_Y)^(N-a)(C_X tensor K_Y)^a /[(Q;Q)_a(Q;Q)_(N-a)]. (7) The inherited terms `J_X tensor chi_Y` and `1 tensor J_Y` commute with both arguments in (7). Canceling them in the generic q-exponential product proves the block fusion identity p_N(-t(1 tensor C_Y)) p_N(-t(C_X tensor K_Y)) =Theta_(X,Y)(t) p_N(-t C_(X tensor Y)), Theta_(X,Y)(t)=exp[(-t)^N j_(X,Y)/N]. (8) These transitions are unipotent. In a block of length `b`, all their nonconstant terms lower total degree by at least `N`; the ideal of such endomorphisms has `b`-th power zero. This nilpotence bound is independent of the level `N`. ### Associativity, with the Frobenius character retained For three consecutive blocks, direct cancellation of the inherited `J_X,J_Y,J_Z` terms gives the exact additive identity j_(X,Y) tensor chi_Z+j_(X tensor Y,Z) =1 tensor j_(Y,Z)+j_(X,Y tensor Z). (9) Within the left pair the two operators commute: `j_(X,Y)` commutes with `C_(X tensor Y)` and `K_(X tensor Y)`, and the next mixed operator is a polynomial in that block's total raising operator and the last block's raising operator. The corresponding right pair commutes for the same reason. Exponentiating (9) therefore gives [Theta_(X,Y) embedded with degree-N factor chi_Z] Theta_(X tensor Y,Z) =Theta_(Y,Z) Theta_(X,Y tensor Z). (10) This is the coherent twisted fusion-cocycle identity. At odd `N` the displayed character is one; at even `N` it can invert the embedded unipotent transition. It is part of the tensor convention. Repeated application proves independence of parenthesization. Thus the actual divided-power normal extension has literal coherent unipotent fusion transitions on this ordered tensor category. No braided source torsor, chosen cohomology class, or selected-period survival is inferred solely from the associative identity. This nilpotence statement concerns the positive raising-factorial transitions. Adjoining lowering divided powers is a different operation and need not preserve a nilpotent group. ## 5. The Hopf-adjoint and cohomological qualifications The new normal generator avoids the finite-order-flow obstruction: it is not the logarithm of the finite-order `ad_K`. It acts nontrivially on tensor and dual multiplicity data even though its one-color action vanishes. Its first-normal coproduct is not primitive; the mixed term (7) is indispensable. A factorwise primitive flow with zero action on each individual color would miss the entire operator (2). For matrix Ward complexes one must use its **divided Hopf adjoint**, not just the ordinary commutator with `J_X`. The coproduct has the inherited `J` terms and the mixed lower-power terms in (7). The antipode is the regular specialization of the generic antipode; in this normalization it gives `S(J)=-J K^(-N)`. Hence on an endomorphism `T` its action has the form ad_J(T)=J T K^(-N)-T J K^(-N) +sum_(a=1)^(N-1) c_a Ecal^a T S(Ecal^(N-a)K^a), c_a=N/[(Q;Q)_a(Q;Q)_(N-a)]. (11) The mixed terms need not vanish on arbitrary matrices, even when `J` vanishes on the underlying single-color module. Commutation of `J` with a braid alone does not replace this all-matrices action. A compatible pivotal trace can be obtained from the genuine generic Hopf trace before dividing and specializing, retaining the actual root pivotal and peripheral scalar adapters. The separate original marked defect is still not an ordinary intertwining coupon. Moreover the mixed insertion is negligible under the ordinary full cut trace for a grading reason. Any braid operator has total-degree zero, while `J_X` lowers total degree by `N`. Closing all but one color forces the remaining color to lower by `N`, impossible in the range `0,...,N-1`. Thus the ordinary cut operator with this insertion is zero. A nonzero relative class would have to retain compensating wrap and marked-cut currents before taking this quotient. Their existence and nonzero pairing have not been proved by (4) or (10). Finally, nilpotence by itself does not identify a class in the geometric Gaussian pushforward. It makes a specified perturbation finite only after that perturbation is an actual filtered chain map on a common source complex. The map, differential, endpoint/carry terms, and the nonzero leading scalar projection are still required. The exact fusion cocycle supplies new coherent normal-source data; it does not by itself supply these HPL hypotheses or a selected volume asymptotic. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_divided_ward_factorial_fusion.py) and [results](../experiments/divided_ward_factorial_fusion_results.json) compare (1) with an independent generic-q normal derivative, check the full signed factorial identities, and verify triple fusion associativity with both Frobenius characters.
