# Independent audit: doubled Rivin phases and critical source traces 27 October 2026. The current proofs in [the doubled-phase optimizer](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) and [the irreducible critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) require that a density on a reducible etale algebra be a unit on every selected component. ## 1. The phase map and the optimizer The fixed-meridian shape Jacobian is invertible by the stated positive Lagrangian pairing. Its peripheral slopes satisfy \(	au_-=\overline{	au_+}\), \(\operatorname{Im}	au_+>0\). Thus the doubled logarithmic phase Jacobian \[  egin{pmatrix}1&-1\	au_+&-	au_-\end{pmatrix} \] has nonzero determinant \(	au_+-	au_-\). The selected normalized shape germ is genuinely etale over the two phase ratios. The conclusion is local at the chosen place and is not an assertion about the raw singular plane A-polynomial fiber. On unit phases, the conjugation involution and local uniqueness force \(w= ar z\). Positivity persists. Stationarity on the affine fixed-two-phase angle slice supplies the real edge equations; the imaginary edge equations were already imposed. Strict concavity then makes this point the unique global maximizer of that entire affine angle fiber and its closure. This does not assert such a positive optimizer at arbitrary remote phase values. Writing \(u=x+ia,v=y+ib\), the derivative is \(d\Phi=x\,db-y\,da\). Solving the phase Jacobian gives \[ \operatorname{Hess}\Phi = rac1{\operatorname{Im}	au_+}  egin{pmatrix}|	au_+|^2&-\operatorname{Re}	au_+\ -\operatorname{Re}	au_+&1\end{pmatrix}. \] It is positive definite with determinant one. The stated complex algebraic formula is exactly the same calculation before the real restriction. The rational cotangent formulas also prove the claimed algebraicity of the constrained covariance. Neither covariance is thereby the actual quantum Gaussian density. The centered complete meridian and longitude signs are explicitly retained as external characters. They must accompany any later SL2 or quantum comparison. The added global real corollary also passes. Within ONE fixed affine edge-angle and logarithmic marking, equal unwrapped boundary phases place two positive edge solutions in the same strictly concave affine fiber. They coincide; the sine rule then identifies their shapes. The phase map is a local diffeomorphism at every positive point, so this global injection is a diffeomorphism onto its open image, of absolute degree one. Fixed edge winding numbers and unwrapped phases are essential. This proves neither image convexity or surjectivity nor any degree statement for the periodic phase torus or quantum cycle. ## 2. The marked regulator primitive and the H5 connection Direct differentiation yields \[ d\left[ rac{R_--R_+}{i} + rac{\widetilde u v-u\widetilde v}{4i}ight] = rac{(u+\widetilde u)d(v-\widetilde v) -(v+\widetilde v)d(u-\widetilde u)}{4i}. \] Thus the bilinear correction and all signs are correct. Conjugate fundamental-class marks and zero centered logs at completeness give \(\Phi=-2\operatorname{Vol}\) without fitting an additional integration constant. For the displayed five-dimensional Heisenberg matrix, the central entry of \(\Pi^{-1}d\Pi\) is \[ dZ-A_{\log}\,dQ_{\log}+B_{\log}\,dP_{\log}, \] which vanishes exactly by the primitive equation. Its curvature reduces to \(2(du\wedge dv-d\widetilde u\wedge d\widetilde v)=0\). Every product of three connection matrices is zero, so marked transport is exactly identity plus the single and double ordered integrals. The central initial value \(-8i\operatorname{Vol}\) is essential; setting the four logarithms initially to zero does not determine it. This is a whole algebraic flat period connection, with generally transcendental horizontal matrix. Exponentiating its additive center is an analytic period evaluation, not an algebraic character of the additive group. ## 3. Irreducible trace descent and finite moments The trace pairing proof is exact: its Gram matrix is \(V^tV\) for the Vandermonde embedding matrix. Hence the density \(a=\eta(\psi)\) is uniquely reconstructed from the stated \(d\) moments by \(G^{-1}m\). In a rank-one line over a FIELD, nonzero source and nonzero co-source imply \(a
e0\). Every embedding coefficient is then \(\sigma_i(a)
e0\). The normalization \(\lambda(\psi)=1\) is a convenient sufficient certificate, not a necessary one. For higher-rank lines the normalization still certifies \(a
e0\), but mere individual nonvanishing does not, as stated. For a reducible etale algebra a faithful normalized matrix trace sees every primitive idempotent with weight rank/dimension. The density multiplying that faithful trace must be a UNIT on every selected etale component. Mere nonzero density is insufficient: \((1,0)\) in \(F	imes F\) would kill the second component. The current note now includes this correction. Neither critical-field irreducibility nor normalized trace descent has been proved for an actual global geometric quotient of the quantum state. The explicit component, splitting-field and already-closed-scalar qualifications are necessary. ## 4. The whole arc and height estimates Distinct exponentials with polynomial coefficients are linearly independent: the stated differential operators isolate one exponential with an invertible operator on its polynomial factor. Their order-\(m\) constant-coefficient equation bounds the zero order at the origin by \(m-1\). Hence every fixed nonzero rational coefficient on the physical source slice has finite vanishing order. Applied to a polynomial relation with nonzero constant and leading terms, Cauchy bounds and their reciprocals give polynomial upper and lower bounds for ALL specialized conjugates. This argument does not need bounded absolute cyclotomic degree. The degree-independent naive-height inequality \((1+H)^{-1}\le|\alpha|\le1+H\) is correct after removing zero constant powers and reversing the polynomial for the lower bound. The bounded-Weil-height counterexample is also correct: the displayed monic polynomial is Eisenstein at two, and all roots of modulus at least one lie in the disk centered at \(2^N\) with radius two. The fixed-point map there is a strict contraction for every \(N\ge2\), so only its one real root lies outside the unit disk. Its Weil height stays bounded while its chosen archimedean value grows exponentially. The resulting finite-sum rate theorem correctly requires a strict TOTAL dominance gap or a smaller-rate bound on any total remainder. Rivin concavity alone supplies neither global period descent nor that gap over all complex sectors. These are substantive sufficient theorems for a proposed whole source comparison. They do not prove its existence or the selected volume limit. ## 5. Precise scope of the optimizer algebraicity The current proofs already establish the claimed classical algebraicity under their stated positive gluing/rank inputs: [geometric rigidity](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) Section1, [doubled phase optimization](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) Sections3--5, and [whole comparison rigidity](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) Section1. No algebraicity correction is needed in those statements. It is not a new conclusion obtained from quantum jets. Here is an independent short proof. Let F be the peripheral coefficient field and K=F(z_1,...,z_t) the selected shape field. Differentiate the normalized polynomial gluing equations over F. The invertible shape Jacobian gives J(dz_j)=0, hence every dz_j=0 in Omega_(K/F). If K/F had positive transcendence degree, choose a transcendence basis and its coordinate derivations. In characteristic zero each extends uniquely over the remaining finite separable field extension, producing a nonzero derivation of K. But all dz_j=0 makes every such derivation zero, a contradiction. Thus K/F is finite algebraic. The complete normalized isolated point has F=Q with its recorded algebraic lift characters, and therefore has algebraic shape coordinates. For the ordinary one-cusped geometric branch the correct field is the function field of its marked peripheral CURVE, Frac(Q[M^+/-1,L^+/-1]/(A_geo)), after choosing the component and normalized place. M and L are dependent. The result is already finite algebraic over the meridian field Q(M) locally. It is not a claim that arbitrary independent complex M,L give a geometric shape solution, or that all shape coordinates are integral over the unlocalized full polynomial ring Q[M,L]. At the complete parabolic lift, M=+1 or -1 and the selected longitude character is retained. This gives algebraic numbers for the UNFRAMED ideal shapes. The raw actual braid critical scheme still has its two framing directions: its other shape/ position coordinates become algebraic numbers only after those framing marks are fixed algebraically as well. Fixing a meridian alone does not isolate that entire framed critical scheme. Strict concavity identifies the unique positive real stationary point on the stated affine angle fiber. Complex transversality and polynomial gluing, rather than uniqueness alone, supply the algebraicity. With two independent boundary PHASES the doubled curve is the appropriate algebraic cover; those phase variables are not two independent full peripheral holonomies. Algebraic shapes do not imply algebraic logarithms or regulator values. The regulator is a transcendental FUNCTION/period of its algebraic connection; this wording makes no theorem that the particular hyperbolic-volume NUMBER is transcendental. For definition/coverage only, see [Zagier, The Dilogarithm Function, Sections I.3--4](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1007/978-3-540-30308-4_1/fulltext.pdf). No proof from that source is imported here. The actual selected wall coefficient2^-N supplies a concrete reminder that even nonzero algebraic source values can have exponential size: all weight-N characters must be retained before applying a bounded whole-algebraic coefficient argument. ## 6. The whole selected-line polar criterion The [whole selected-line theorem](whole_selected_line_polar_character.md) also passes independently. On the EXACT marked ray s_N=kappa N^(-1/e), kappa^e=pi i, a meromorphic rank-one connection integrates to C s^rho exp(B(s)+H(s)), with finite B=sum b_r s^-r and convergent H holomorphic. Its normalized log modulus is exactly the displayed finite sum of distinct powers N^(r/e-1), plus O(logN/N). The r=e contribution is 2Im(b_e); terms r>e can contribute zero only when each real coefficient vanishes on that ray. A fixed meromorphic frame changes dlog only by a logarithmic pole and preserves B. The logarithmic quotient by exp(S_geo/h) gives the stated volume rate and O(logN/N) error. This is a genuinely useful sufficient GLOBAL target, not an assumption that a local Gaussian block is the actual selected invariant. For a perturbed physical ray the polar primitive must first be pulled back to that exact ray; imaginary leading high poles can otherwise produce real lower terms. The theorem uses the exact ray and does not make that mistake. The accumulating zeros of a sum of two different exponential characters correctly obstruct a single meromorphic selected line. The amplified whole-unit example has primitive -2i pi^2/h and normalized rate -4pi^2 as printed. Existence of the ACTUAL selected line, its original co-source and its marked leading regulator character is still the new theorem to prove.

title: The Rivin optimizer is a whole algebraic function of the boundary phases
text: # The Rivin optimizer is a whole algebraic function of the boundary phases Research proof, 27 October 2026. The positive geometric edge curve and its conjugate place have an étale two-parameter **phase-ratio map**. Its inverse is the unique constrained Rivin optimizer. Consequently the optimizer shapes, peripheral norms, constrained Hessian and all higher derivatives of the boundary potential are algebraic functions of two independent multiplicative boundary phases. The potential itself is a marked logarithmic regulator period, with an explicit primitive. This strengthens the earlier algebraicity over an already selected meridian: it constructs the algebraic inverse of the real boundary phase optimization. It is a classical whole-function statement, not a quantum-source selection or volume-conjecture theorem. ## 1. Assumptions and the retained marks Let T be a one-cusped ideal triangulation with t tetrahedra and a specified positive complete geometric shape point z^0, meaning Im z_j^0>0. Use the open algebraic shape space with `z_j(1-z_j)!=0` and the monomial edge/peripheral equations over Q, including their original sign characters. No branching of all tetrahedra at once is required for this local calculation. We use the independently established marked gluing linear data: * t-1 independent real integral edge rows span an isotropic space E; * its symplectic reduction E^perp/E is the marked peripheral plane; * a primitive meridian row adjoined to the edges has rank t and is isotropic; * the peripheral convention is `Omega_red=-(1/2)du wedge dv`. These are the explicit rank and marking inputs, not consequences of concavity alone. They are proved for the actual knot gluing complex in the preceding integral peripheral notes. The proof below also works for any triangulation supplied with this data. Let the original SL2 eigenvalues be calM,calL, with complete characters calM_c,calL_c in {+1,-1}. Keep those characters on their prescribed finite cover and set the centered logs u=2Log(calM/calM_c), v=2Log(calL/calL_c), m=exp(u), ell=exp(v). (1) Thus u=v=0 at the complete place. Their signs are external marked characters, not reset by squaring or centering. They must be reinserted when an SL2 A-polynomial or a quantum peripheral operator is used. ## 2. The constrained variational equation fixes moduli only after phases For each tetrahedron take compatible logs x_j=Log z_j, y_j=Log z_j'', z_j''=1-z_j^(-1), alpha_j=Im x_j, gamma_j=Im y_j, beta_j=pi-alpha_j-gamma_j. All three angles are positive. The angle domain has the usual linear tetrahedral and edge equations. Its volume is V(theta)=sum_j[Lambda(alpha_j)+Lambda(beta_j)+Lambda(gamma_j)], Lambda'(theta)=-Log(2sin theta). On each tetrahedral angle simplex the negative Hessian in alpha,gamma is [[cot alpha+cot beta,cot beta], [cot beta,cot gamma+cot beta]]. (2) Its determinant is one and its first diagonal entry is `sin gamma/(sin alpha sin beta)>0`. Hence V is strictly concave on every affine angle slice. Write Omega=sum_j dx_j wedge dy_j. The sine rule gives exactly dV(delta theta)=Omega(Re(x,y),delta theta). (3) For example Re x=Log(sin beta/sin gamma) and Re y=Log(sin alpha/sin beta), which verifies (3) by direct differentiation. Edge-angle tangents form E^perp. Fix the TWO real peripheral angles a=Im u, b=Im v. Their common tangent space is E, since their two rows give a basis of E^perp/E. Therefore an interior stationary point on this affine fixed-(a,b) slice satisfies Re(x,y) in E^perp. (4) Equation (4) is exactly the missing real part of the edge gluing equations. Their imaginary parts were imposed by the angle equations. Thus the stationary point solves full complex edge gluing. Its real peripheral logs are outputs of the optimization, not separately fixed constraints. This distinction is essential. Fixing arbitrary independent complex values m and ell overdetermines the one-dimensional geometric edge curve. Conversely imposing nonlinear full holonomy constraints in angle variables is not an affine constraint to which strict concavity can simply be applied. The correct independent real optimization parameters are a,b; the multiplicative algebraic parameters constructed below are their squared phases. Any positive stationary point is the unique global maximizer on that affine slice, and on its closure. For any other point the segment from the positive stationary point is interior until its possible final endpoint. Its second derivative is strictly negative by (2) and its initial derivative is zero, so its volume is strictly smaller, including by continuity at a degenerate final endpoint. ## 3. Positive gluing gives the required complex transversality Here is the short rank calculation, recorded to make all algebraic inverses explicit. At a positive shape dy_j/dx_j=tau_j=1/(z_j-1), Im tau_j<0. Let (A B) be the rank-t isotropic matrix of edges and the marked meridian. The fixed-meridian logarithmic shape Jacobian is J=A+B diag(tau_j). (5) If Ja=0, the shape tangent `(a,diag(tau)a)` lies in the complexification of a real Lagrangian. Its symplectic pairing with its conjugate is zero. But directly (i/2)Omega((a,tau a),conjugate(a,tau a)) =sum_j Im tau_j |a_j|^2<0 unless a=0. Hence det J!=0. The edge curve is smooth at the positive point and is étale over the complex meridian m. The conjugate place has the conjugate invertible Jacobian. Write its peripheral slopes as tau_+=dv/du, tau_-=d(v_tilde)/d(u_tilde). They are algebraic rational functions on the corresponding shape curve: solve (5) for a unit meridian variation and apply the longitude row. On the positive real pair tau_-=bar(tau_+), and the reduced symplectic identity gives Im tau_+=-2sum_j Im tau_j |dx_j/du|^2>0. (6) Thus the two peripheral slopes are distinct. This is the transversality which strict concavity by itself would not supply. ## 4. The doubled normalized curve is étale over the phase torus Let X_+ be the chosen normalized positive edge-curve place and X_- its conjugate place. Work on their product, retaining the shape cover if the peripheral curve alone forgets shapes. Define P_mu=m_+/m_-, P_lambda=ell_+/ell_-, A=m_+m_-, B=ell_+ell_-. (7) The map to the two-dimensional phase torus is algebraic over Q. Its logarithmic Jacobian in the local coordinates u,u_tilde is [[1,-1],[tau_+,-tau_-]], determinant=tau_+-tau_-. (8) It is invertible at the chosen complete pair by (6). Equivalently one may use both sets of edge equations and the two ratio equations (7); their full shape Jacobian is the product of the two fixed-meridian Jacobians and (8), up to explicit nonzero monomial coordinate factors. It follows that the selected doubled shape germ is étale over `(P_mu,P_lambda)=(1,1)`. Its shapes, norms A,B and slopes are algebraic over Q(P_mu,P_lambda). A component defined only after a number-field extension causes no loss of algebraicity over Q: the entire defining gluing/ratio system is over Q, and its selected unramified component is generically finite over the phase torus. For completeness, the algebraicity does not follow merely from a unique real optimum. For the full polynomial system at fixed phase values, invertibility of its Jacobian makes every shape differential over the phase coefficient field zero. A finitely generated characteristic-zero field of positive transcendence degree has nonzero differentials (choose a transcendence basis). Thus the selected shape field extension is algebraic and finite. This is a local étale statement with a selected place. It does not assert that all branches form a finite étale cover over a Zariski neighborhood of (1,1). Other places can ramify above the same base value. The selected completed local factor, after its finite residue-field mark, is the power-series ring in the two phase parameters and is finite étale over the completed base. Every specified nilpotent phase lift has a unique shape lift at that mark. Globally the same function field is finite over the phase field, but branch and deleted divisors must be retained in any continuation. ## 5. The algebraic inverse is the entire positive optimizer on its phase fiber For real phases near the complete point take P_mu=exp(2ia), P_lambda=exp(2ib), Log P_mu=2ia, Log P_lambda=2ib. (9) The product-curve real involution `(z,w)->(bar w,bar z)` covers `(P_mu,P_lambda)->(1/bar P_mu,1/bar P_lambda)`. It fixes the chosen conjugate pair. Uniqueness of the local inverse in (8) therefore forces w=bar z on the real phase torus. Positivity of z persists in a sufficiently small neighborhood. These shapes satisfy the full edge gluing and the fixed boundary phases, so Section 2 makes their angles the unique GLOBAL volume maximizer of that whole positive affine angle fiber. Thus the constrained optimum is not merely obtained by a flow limit: its shapes are the values of the selected whole algebraic inverse (7). The angles themselves are logarithmic phases of these shapes and need not be algebraic numbers or functions. There is also a global real statement on the fixed affine angle/log-marking. Take all positive solutions of the full edge equations in that marked angle domain. Each is stationary on its fixed-(a,b) fiber by (3)--(4). Strict concavity therefore makes the map to the UNWRAPPED angle pair (a,b) injective. Equations (5)--(8) make it a local real diffeomorphism at every such point. Consequently it is a diffeomorphism onto its open image, with one classical sheet there (absolute degree one). The image is not asserted to be all feasible phase pairs or convex. Different log-lift fibers can have the same periodic (P_mu,P_lambda), so this global assertion is not made over the unmarked phase torus. It does not assign a degree to the quantum compact source cycle or its critical projection. The complex peripheral values are recovered algebraically on this cover. They lie on the marked A-curve, rather than being two independent full holonomy parameters. Complete m=ell=1, or the original calM_c,calL_c=+1 or -1, gives the recorded algebraic complete shape field. ## 6. The multiplicative Legendre graph and its full Hessian are algebraic Let V_boundary(a,b) be this maximal volume and put Phi(a,b)=-2 V_boundary(a,b). The reduced form and (3) give dV_boundary=(1/2)(Re v da-Re u db), u=Phi_b+ia, v=-Phi_a+ib. (10) On the doubled real slice the norm coordinates in (7) therefore satisfy the whole multiplicative identities exp(2Phi_b)=A, exp(-2Phi_a)=B. (11) A and B are algebraic functions of P_mu,P_lambda. Hence the exponentiated Legendre graph is algebraic over the phase torus, while its first derivatives are marked logarithms of algebraic functions. There is an explicit algebraic Hessian. Write Delta=tau_+-tau_-. Then Hess_(a,b) Phi =(2i/Delta)[[tau_+tau_-,-(tau_++tau_-)/2], [-(tau_++tau_-)/2,1]], det Hess Phi=1. (12) On the real slice, tau_+=p+iq with q>0, this is (1/q)[[p^2+q^2,-p],[-p,1]], which is positive definite. Formula (12) follows by solving `dLog P_mu=du-du_tilde` and `dLog P_lambda=tau_+du-tau_-du_tilde`, then applying (10). Its determinant is one directly, without a period estimate. All derivatives of Phi of order at least two are algebraic on this cover: the phase derivatives are the algebraic vector fields `2iP_mu partial_(P_mu)` and `2iP_lambda partial_(P_lambda)`, extended uniquely to the finite characteristic-zero function field. The same statement holds for the full constrained angle fluctuation matrix. For example cot(alpha_j)=i(z_j+w_j)/(z_j-w_j), and similarly for the other two shape orders. Thus (2), its restriction to any fixed rational basis of the affine constraint kernel, its inverse covariance and its determinant are rational functions of the doubled shapes. Their determinants are units on the positive chart. Its positive real Gaussian square root is therefore an algebraic marked half-density on a finite cover. This variational Hessian is not thereby the actual quantum state's separately normalized Gaussian amplitude. ## 7. The potential is an explicit marked regulator period On the doubled logarithmic cover retain u,v,u_tilde,v_tilde and the sums and differences Log A=u+u_tilde, Log B=v+v_tilde, Log P_mu=u-u_tilde, Log P_lambda=v-v_tilde. Equation (10) becomes the exact closed logarithmic one-form dPhi=[Log A dLog P_lambda-Log B dLog P_mu]/(4i). (13) Its derivative is `[du wedge dv-du_tilde wedge dv_tilde]/(2i)=0`, since each pair is pulled back from a curve. All differentiated log coordinates are algebraic logarithmic differentials on the whole doubled-phase cover. Let R_+,R_- be the existing marked Heisenberg regulator periods on the two shape factors, with dR_+=-(u dv-v du)/4, dR_-=-(u_tilde dv_tilde-v_tilde du_tilde)/4. An exact primitive is Phi=(R_--R_+)/i +(u_tilde v-u v_tilde)/(4i)+C. (14) Differentiate (14): its cross term is the differential of the displayed bilinear expression, and the remaining terms give exactly (13). The bilinear term cannot be omitted away from completeness. The constant is fixed by the original fundamental-class marks, not fitted to a desired volume. With conjugate marks at the complete place, `R_-=bar R_+`, centered logs are zero, and the already proved Bloch fundamental-class evaluation is `Im R_+=Vol`. Both (14) and the definition of Phi then give `Phi=-2Vol`, so C=0 with these marks. Other sign/log sheets carry their recorded period characters and the corresponding constant; they are not identified with this sheet. Thus the optimizer is a whole algebraic shape/norm function, and its volume potential is a whole logarithmic regulator period on that cover. Its algebraic Hessian and every fixed jet are evaluations of these functions. The statement does not require treating a formal Taylor expansion as the primary object. ## 8. A fixed two-step unipotent connection carries the whole potential The logarithmic primitive has a fixed algebraic period object before any quantum jet or level is chosen. Write A_log=Log A, B_log=Log B, P_log=Log P_mu, Q_log=Log P_lambda, Z=4i Phi. Form the five-dimensional Heisenberg period matrix Pi=[[1,A_log,-B_log,Z], [0,1,0,Q_log], [0,0,1,P_log], [0,0,0,1]]. Its equation is exactly Pi^(-1)dPi=Omega, Omega=[[0,dlog A,-dlog B,0], [0,0,0,dlog P_lambda], [0,0,0,dlog P_mu], [0,0,0,0]]. (14a) The top-right entry vanishes precisely by (13). Every nonzero entry of Omega is an algebraic logarithmic differential on the fixed doubled curve. Its only possible curvature entry is dlog A wedge dlog P_lambda-dlog B wedge dlog P_mu =2(du wedge dv-du_tilde wedge dv_tilde)=0. Thus (14a) is a flat algebraic connection on that whole cover. The group law has a four-dimensional additive quotient and a one-dimensional center; commutators are central and third nested commutators vanish. In the displayed representation every product of three connection matrices is already zero. Along a marked path, transport is therefore EXACTLY the sum of the identity, single integrals of Omega, and double ordered integrals of Omega. No asymptotic expansion or infinite transport iteration is needed. The marked value of Z at the complete point is -8i Vol, by (14). It is the central fundamental-class period; zero initial logarithms alone would leave this central constant free. The connection is algebraic, while its horizontal period matrix generally is not. In particular exponentiating the central period is a specified analytic period evaluation, not an algebraic character from the additive center to the multiplicative group. This realizes the proposed whole geometric torsor explicitly. It does not make an arbitrary quantum A-module unipotent or construct the selected quantum-source map into this torsor. ## 9. Direct A-polynomial formulation and the essential normalization Let calA(m,ell) be a polynomial equation for the marked squared peripheral curve. If the chosen A-polynomial uses SL2 variables, retain the finite sign cover (1) instead. Equation (10) implies calA(exp(Phi_b+ia),exp(-Phi_a+ib))=0, calA(exp(Phi_b-ia),exp(-Phi_a-ib))=0. (15) On the whole algebraic phase cover, a necessary elimination presentation is calA(m,ell)=0, calA(m/P_mu,ell/P_lambda)=0, A=m^2/P_mu, B=ell^2/P_lambda. (16) The selected normalized places are essential. At P_mu=P_lambda=1 the raw first two equations in (16) coincide and contain the entire diagonal peripheral curve. They are not an étale zero-dimensional fiber by themselves. The opposite geometric and conjugate places on the normalization are distinct even where their plane images collide. Their product has the nonzero determinant (8). If needed, retain the finite shape cover of that normalization as well. Thus an A-polynomial formulation can encode the optimizer without a knot-by-knot calculation, but it must keep the chosen normalized A-place/torsor and its fundamental period. An unmarked plane equation and positivity at one point do not discard the diagonal or other peripheral components. ## 10. Coverage and the quantum boundary Classical angle-volume optimization and volume potentials on peripheral curves are established subjects. The coverage already recorded in the repo includes Rivin and [Futer--Gueritaud](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440), and the coverage-only search includes Guilloux--Marche, [Volume function and Mahler measure of exact polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395), and Johansson--Samuelsson Kalm, [arxiv:1412.1585](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1585). No proof from those papers is used here. The refinement proved in this note is the explicit phase-doubled algebraic inverse, its normalization requirements, and the marked primitive (14). No new Ronkin, Harnack or dimer identification is asserted. The theorem assumes a positive geometric ideal triangulation and the stated integral gluing/peripheral rank data. It does not infer right-angled geometric Menasco cells from alternatingness. Those combinatorial diagrams need their own geometric hypotheses. The classical proof makes no knot-family restriction once its explicit geometric input is supplied. The whole quantum A-state and its selected cycle are additional objects. The doubled-phase cover may supply a fixed algebraic coefficient space for a proposed comparison, but it does not construct that comparison, prove a bounded quantum comparison space, or establish a nonzero selected geometric contribution. Its regulator period is not made algebraic by algebraicity of the optimizer. No volume conjecture follows without that remaining source/period theorem. ## 11. Focused exact audit [audit_doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.py](../experiments/audit_doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.py) and its [results](../experiments/doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer_results.json) verify the phase Jacobian, algebraic Hessian and determinant one, the real positive Hessian, rational tetrahedral covariance, the marked regulator primitive and its closedness, and the exact H5 Maurer--Cartan matrix. All triple connection-matrix products vanish, and its sole curvature coefficient is exactly the stated difference of the two curve symplectic forms. An exact algebraic node chart also checks the whole phase inverse, norm-gradient/Hessian identities and the unnormalized A-equation's diagonal fiber. It is a convention stress test, not an additional knot case or a replacement for the general proof. The independent [doubled-phase and source audit](doubled_phase_and_critical_source_independent_audit.md) checks the real branch, global fixed-affine-fiber maximizer, unwrapped positive projection, sign characters, period constants, normalization requirements and the H5 transport. All focused symbolic checks passed. No quantum normal-family or selected source conclusion is inferred from them.

title: An exact dual clock lift to the centralizer normal co-source

# An exact dual clock lift to the centralizer normal co-source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. Every actual finite cut clock has an explicit polynomial centralizer-normal co-source, valid on ALL matrices. On the physical scaled clock this polynomial converges locally uniformly to a whole exponential, with uniform factorial coefficient bounds. Its derivatives transport every bounded normalized cut-position moment exactly. The lift is contravariant: it represents a trace FUNCTIONAL. It is not a multiplicative symbol map, a crossing intertwiner, or an internal Gaussian source comparison. ## 1. The dual Toeplitz map of the actual compact source Put \(n=N-1\). In the source coordinates \(T=va\), the actual coherent matrix symbol is \[ f_C(v,T)=\sum_{i,j=0}^n C_{ij} inom nj v^{i-j}T^j(1-T)^{n-j}. \] Let \(\omega_I=-\Omega_0/(2\pi i)\), whose marked compact period is one. Angular integration and the beta integral give, for every polynomial \(P\), \[ \int_\Gamma P(-T)f_C\,\omega_I = rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal T_N(P)C), 	ag{1} \] where the diagonal Toeplitz row is \[ [\mathcal T_N(b^h)]_j =(-1)^h rac{(j+1)^{\overline h}} {(N+1)^{\overline h}}, \qquad h\ge0,\quad 0\le j<N. 	ag{2} \] A bar denotes the rising factorial. Formula (2) holds at ALL polynomial degrees, not only below \(N\). On polynomials of degree at most \(n\), \(\mathcal T_N\) is an isomorphism onto the diagonal matrices: its h-th basis column is a polynomial in j of degree h with nonzero leading coefficient, evaluated at the N distinct integer points. This is different from the covariant symbol quantization \(b^h\mapsto(-1)^h(J)_h/(n)_h\). The all-matrix pairing here is the normalized ORDINARY TRACE. On the actual position-conserving weighted-word and Green cut arrays it agrees with the original average cut because those arrays are diagonal. It is not the original average functional \(\Phi(C)=N^{-1}\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\) on arbitrary off-diagonal Ward matrices. Any such Hopf-current comparison must retain and transport that original coupon separately. The trace extension is stated explicitly rather than identified with all possible actual co-sources. ## 2. Exact inversion for the WHOLE clock For any complex \(w\), define the polynomial of degree at most n \[ P_{N,w}^{\vee}(b)=\sum_{h=0}^n a_{N,h}(w)b^h, \] \[ a_{N,h}(w)=  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{h!} \sum_{r=h}^n(-1)^r inom rh(w-1)^r . 	ag{3} \] Then exactly \[ \mathcal T_N(P_{N,w}^{\vee})=w^J , \qquad Je_j=je_j. 	ag{4} \] Thus for EVERY matrix C, \[  rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(w^JC) =\int_\Gamma P_{N,w}^{\vee}(-T)f_C\,\omega_I . 	ag{5} \] Here is a direct proof. The polynomial identity \[ (j)_r=\sum_{h=0}^r(-1)^{r-h} inom rh  rac{r!}{h!}(j+1)^{\overline h} 	ag{6} \] follows, for example, by comparing coefficients in \((1+\delta)^j\): sum the right side over r with weight \(\delta^r/r!\), use \(\sum_{r\ge h}(-1)^{r-h} inom rh\delta^r =\delta^h/(1+\delta)^{h+1}\), and then the rising-binomial series. Now expand \(w^j\) in the Newton basis \[ w^j=\sum_{r=0}^n rac{(j)_r}{r!}(w-1)^r \quad(0\le j\le n). \] Insert (6), collect h, and apply (2). This is precisely (3)--(4). Useful exact endpoint formulas are \[ P_{N,w}^{\vee}(0)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}(1-w)^r,\qquad P_{N,w}^{\vee}(-1)=w^N-(w-1)^N. 	ag{7} \] These are not the actual clock eigenvalues at j=0,n. Confusing dual polynomial evaluation with a matrix endpoint would lose finite endpoint corrections. ## 3. Scaled clocks, moments, and uniform whole limits Put \(w=e^{z/N}\). On every compact complex z-set, \(|w-1|\le C/N\). For all sufficiently large N, \[ |a_{N,h}(e^{z/N})| \le  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{h!}  rac{|w-1|^h}{(1-|w-1|)^{h+1}} \le C_1\, rac{C_2^h}{h!}, \qquad 0\le h<N. 	ag{8} \] Indeed \((N+1)^{\overline h}\le(2N)^h\) for h<N, while \((1-C/N)^{-h-1}\) is bounded uniformly in that range. For each fixed h, the leading r=h term in (3) gives \[ a_{N,h}(e^{z/N})\longrightarrow(-z)^h/h!. \] The factorial majorant proves the WHOLE locally uniform limit \[ P_{N,e^{z/N}}^{\vee}(b)\longrightarrow e^{-zb} \quad	ext{on }\mathbb C_z	imes\mathbb C_b. 	ag{9} \] This also proves convergence of every fixed derivative by Cauchy's formula. No WKB asymptotic interpretation of these derivatives is used. Differentiation of (4) gives the exact normalized moment identities \[ \mathcal T_N\!\left(\partial_z^r P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\veeight) =(J/N)^r e^{zJ/N}. 	ag{10} \] At z=0 these give every fixed normalized polynomial cut-position moment. Unnormalized moments \(J^r\) retain the explicit factor \(N^r\). Formula (10) is a whole clock-coupling identity, valid before any internal flow sum. The bounded moment has a stronger finite normal-order statement. Put \[ G_{N,r}(b)=\left.\partial_z^r P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\vee(b)ight|_{z=0}. \] It has degree at most \(\min(r,n)\). In particular for every fixed r and all \(N>r\), its normal pole in (13) has order at most r+1, INDEPENDENT of N. An exact closed formula is \[ [b^h]G_{N,r}=  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{N^r h!} \sum_{s=h}^{\min(r,n)} S(r,s)(-1)^s inom sh s!, \qquad 0\le h\le\min(r,n), 	ag{10a} \] where \(S(r,s)\) are Stirling numbers of the second kind. This follows by differentiating \((e^{z/N}-1)^s\) at zero, whose r-th derivative is \(s!S(r,s)/N^r\). For r at most n the leading coefficient is \((-1)^r(N+1)^{\overline r}/N^r\), while each lower coefficient is \(O_r(N^{h-r})\). Hence \[ G_{N,r}(b)=(-b)^r+O_r(1/N) \] on every fixed compact b-set. Arbitrary bounded-degree normalized Green cut-position polynomials follow by linearity. Their actual source-normal pole depth is therefore bounded even though the WHOLE clock uses degree \(N-1\). Beta reflection gives \[ \mathcal T_N(P(-1-b))_j=\mathcal T_N(P)_{n-j}. \] Injectivity on degree at most n therefore proves \[ P_{N,w}^\vee(-1-b)=w^nP_{N,w^{-1}}^\vee(b). 	ag{11} \] The centered polynomial \[ \widehat P_N(z,b)=e^{-nz/(2N)}P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\vee(b) \] reflects z to -z and tends to \(e^{-z(b+1/2)}\). For the identity matrix, (5) is EXACTLY the retained source character \[ \int_\Gamma\widehat P_N(z,-T)\omega_I = rac1N\operatorname{Tr}e^{z(J-n/2)/N} = rac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}. 	ag{12} \] Thus this lift reproduces the same whole source norm/peripheral factor as the scaled-meridian and Gamma-source calculations. ## 4. Normal residue and global affine clutch Use the normal centralizer coordinate \(b=-a/\eta\) and \[ 
u_{\mathrm{cut}}=- rac{d\eta}{\eta}\wedge  rac{\Omega_0}{1-\eta v}. \] For every h, expansion of the geometric denominator gives \[ \operatorname{Res}_{E}(b^h
u_{\mathrm{cut}}) =-(-T)^h\Omega_0 . \] Linearity, (3), and (5) yield the exact source pairing \[  rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(w^JC) = rac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \operatorname{Res}_{E} \left(P_{N,w}^\vee(b)f_C
u_{\mathrm{cut}}ight). 	ag{13} \] This is a SOURCE-KERNEL lift; it is not asserted to be the internal Gaussian image of that kernel. The north and south torsor coordinates obey \[ b_S=b_N+ rac1{v\eta},\qquad b_S-1-b_N= rac{1-\eta v}{v\eta}. \] Use \(P(b_N)\) north and \(P(b_S-1)\) south. Their difference is divisible by the Gauss-wall factor. After multiplication by \(
u_{\mathrm{cut}}\) the Gauss-wall pole cancels, leaving only \(\eta^{-r}d\eta\wedge\Omega_0\) with \(r\ge2\). Each has an explicit normal primitive and zero E-residue. Thus (13) retains a compatible affine Cech moment marking. Bare \(P(b_S)\) would have the wrong residue polynomial. At finite N the normal pole degree can reach N, since \(\deg P^\vee=N-1\) and \(
u_{\mathrm{cut}}\) already has a simple normal pole. It must not be replaced by a bounded normal jet. After taking the explicit residue formula, (8)--(9) do allow locally uniform convergence of the whole residue to its exponential source form. No algebraicity of that limiting horizontal exponential is claimed. ## 5. Exact finite cut-current endpoints For an arbitrary zero-extended finite current \(J_j\), set \(\lambda_{N,w}^{\mathrm{head}}(J)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}w^jJ_j\). For \(w
e0\), direct summation by parts gives \[ \lambda_{N,w}^{\mathrm{head}}((S-1)J) =(w^{-1}-1)\lambda_{N,w}^{\mathrm{head}}(J) + rac{w^{N-1}J_N-w^{-1}J_0}{N}. 	ag{14} \] Including both actual tails gives the full finite row \(N^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}w^jJ_j\), for which the endpoint terms telescope and the factor is exactly \(w^{-1}-1\). Its z-derivatives retain every normalized position-moment endpoint. The original raw Green arrays already contain \(1/N\). Equations (5), (13), and (14) use matrix-normalized arrays; \(I_{\mathrm{mat}}=NI_{\mathrm{raw}}\), \(J_{\mathrm{mat}}=NJ_{\mathrm{raw}}\). Equivalently use N times these rows on raw arrays. No factor N is absorbed into an endpoint. ## 6. Whole word composition is exact; Gaussian naturality is additional An actual transfer clock can be split into literal input/output position clocks. For the recorded checked R conventions, \[ R_+:(i,j)\mapsto(j+k,i-k),\qquad R_-:(i,j)\mapsto(j-k,i+k), \] so \[ w^kR_+=(I\otimes w^{-J})R_+(w^J\otimes I),\qquad w^kR_-=(I\otimes w^J)R_-(w^{-J}\otimes I). 	ag{15} \] These are exact coefficient identities with the same Cartan and pivot lines. Products and tensor products use the actual operator composition, or equivalently the exact finite coherent STAR product. Thus all weighted words and their coupling derivatives retain their source meaning. Pointwise multiplication is not that star product. Already at N=2 the actual inverse clocks obey \(\operatorname{Tr}(w^Jw^{-J})/2=1\), whereas \[ \int_0^1[1+(w-1)T][1+(w^{-1}-1)T]\,dT =1+ rac{w+w^{-1}-2}{6}. \] At the actual root clock w=-1 this is 1/3, not one. The DUAL pairing (5) gives one exactly. Moving a dual clock through an actual crossing therefore requires the transpose of its finite star action. A scalar polynomial in b represents diagonal co-sources only; after an off-diagonal crossing one generally needs the full angular/coherent dual source as well. The normal residue is not a multiplicative operator-algebra map. Consequently this theorem supplies the actual whole CUT clock and all its normalized moments, including tails and affine clutch. The independent second framing coordinate still needs its network map. Nor is the source-dependent transverse Gaussian pushforward proved natural for this contravariant star action. These are the specific remaining couplings, rather than a defect in the finite clock formula. ## 7. Why the raw framing moments are not the finite critical field For the actual scalar closed cut \(C=F_NI\), the polynomial normal-centralizer moments from (1) normalize to \[ \mu(b^h)=(-1)^h/(h+1). \] Their Hankel matrices are signed Hilbert matrices, positive definite at EVERY size: \(\mu(p\overline p)=\int_0^1|p(-T)|^2dT>0\) for nonzero p. Hence no nonzero polynomial ideal is annihilated. This raw framing co-source cannot factor through a fixed finite algebra in b, even for the actual figure-eight. This does not contradict a finite algebra of ISOLATED TRANSVERSE geometric critical points. The framing variable is meant to be integrated first, or retained in a relative/twisted complex. It does rule out defining that critical observable as the raw Toeplitz image of b: \(\mathcal T_N\) is not multiplicative. A finite list of moments reconstructs a density only AFTER its critical polynomial relation has actually been supplied. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_dual_clock_normal_cut_source.py) and [results](../experiments/dual_clock_normal_cut_source_results.json): 337 symbolic clock, normalized-moment, reflection, endpoint and finite-current identities pass at N=2 through 11.

title: An endpoint-completed whole Jackson current from actual divided matrices
text: # An endpoint-completed whole Jackson current from actual divided matrices Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual high-color divided raising/lowering currents, with two literal anchored primitives, recover the WHOLE Jackson differential on the physical unwrapped clock. Its root value is the clock Euler derivative. The missing bottom state is repaired explicitly, so the identity holds on every state, not only in a bulk chart. A rational function and its shift are retained before matrix evaluation. This is an actual current/source map on the commutative physical character subalgebra. The exact off-diagonal correction below shows why it is not yet a map of all head Hopf currents or a full geometric Gaussian/source comparison. ## 1. Whole actual matrices and regular anchored inverses Use the original high integral color with r=N from [the actual source theorem](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). In its fixed sign frame write w_(R,S), 0<=R<=N, 0<=S<N, and set \[ Z=Q^N,\quad\delta=1-Z,\quad J=NR+S,\quad C_Q=Q^J=Q^S Z^R. \] Keep the original generic integral divided matrices \[ e(q)=\tau E^{(N)}(q),\qquad f(q)=F^{(N)}(q),\quad \tau=(-1)^{N^2-1}. \] They preserve S and change R by -1 and +1. Their nonzero arrow coefficients alpha_(R,S)(q), R>=1, and beta_(R,S)(q), R<N, are regular units near the marked root: their root values are N-R+1 and R+1. Define actual inverse arrows \[ e^\dagger w_{R,S}=\alpha_{R+1,S}^{-1}w_{R+1,S}\ (R<N), \quad e^\dagger w_{N,S}=0, \] \[ f^\dagger w_{R,S}=\beta_{R-1,S}^{-1}w_{R-1,S}\ (R>0), \quad f^\dagger w_{0,S}=0. \] These are whole rational matrix germs of the actual divided coefficients, not inverses of nilpotent matrices. With P_0,P_N the two block endpoint projectors, they satisfy EXACTLY \[ e^\dagger e=I-P_0,\quad ee^\dagger=I-P_N,\qquad f^\dagger f=I-P_N,\quad ff^\dagger=I-P_0. \tag{1} \] Their root operator norms are at most one in the fixed unit basis. No uniform estimate on a growing q-neighborhood is assumed. In the actual positive Fr metric ||v_R||^2=binom(N,R), the sharper bound is ||e^dagger||=||f^dagger||=1/sqrt(N); the two endpoint projectors still have norm one. This follows from the normalized inverse arrow 1/sqrt((R+1)(N-R)). ## 2. The whole Jackson identity, with its shifted argument Let g(Q,t) be a retained Laurent polynomial, or a rational function whose denominators at BOTH C_Q and ZC_Q are invertible in the chosen whole matrix chart. Q remains fixed when its t argument is shifted. Define the actual current \[ \mathcal J_Z(g)=\frac{-e^\dagger[e,g(Q,ZC_Q)] +P_0f^\dagger[f,g(Q,C_Q)]}{1-Z}. \tag{2} \] Then, as an exact whole rational matrix identity, \[ \boxed{\ \mathcal J_Z(g) =\frac{g(Q,C_Q)-g(Q,ZC_Q)}{1-Z}.\ } \tag{3} \] Proof. The actual block grading gives eC_Q=ZC_Qe and fC_Q=Z^(-1)C_Qf. The inverse arrows have the opposite degrees. Keeping operator order and the SHIFTED argument in (2) therefore gives \[ e^\dagger[e,g(ZC_Q)] =[g(ZC_Q)-g(C_Q)](I-P_0), \] \[ f^\dagger[f,g(C_Q)] =[g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q)](I-P_N). \] Since P_0P_N=0, their combination is the full difference, with no missing endpoint. This proves (3). In particular replacing g(ZC_Q) by g(C_Q) in the first commutator would give a different operator and would not prove this identity. The right side has a regular value at Z=1 whenever the stated function chart is regular. For every integer k, \[ \mathcal J_Z(t^k)=\frac{1-Z^k}{1-Z}C_Q^k, \] and it obeys the exact twisted product rule \[ \mathcal J_Z(gh)=\mathcal J_Z(g)h(C_Q) +g(ZC_Q)\mathcal J_Z(h). \tag{4} \] Thus the construction is a whole function calculus before its normal jets are taken. An explicit q-dependent coefficient is carried unchanged in the difference; its separate q-derivative is not silently included in a clock derivative. At the root A=Q_N^S, (3) gives \[ \mathcal E(g):=[\mathcal J_Z(g)]_0 =A\partial_A g(Q_N,A)\,I_{\mathrm{Fr}}. \tag{5} \] The shifted argument in (2) has the same leading divided commutator as its unshifted value, so equivalently E(g)=[-e^dagger[e,g(C_Q)]/delta+P_0 f^dagger[f,g(C_Q)]/delta]_0. For every remaining head matrix entry the output of (5) is the literal multiplication by the indicated head character. ## 3. The normal jet and the literal finite cut The derivative in (5) is not a derivation of the reduced finite clock algebra k[A^+/-1]/(A^N-1): it sends A^N-1 to N. The whole normal datum is essential. More precisely, for frozen coefficients k containing Q_N, the actual map g(t)->g(C_Q) modulo delta^2 has kernel \[ (t^N-1)^2. \tag{6} \] Indeed root vanishing implies g=(t^N-1)h. On w_(R,S), C_Q^N-1=-J delta+O(delta^2). Vanishing at first normal order then implies J h(Q_N^S)=0 for every R. For each S at least one of J=NR+S is nonzero, so h vanishes at all N roots. This proves (6), and the converse follows by squaring the simple normal zero. Thus (5) is the actual clock conormal-jet derivative \[ k[t^{+/-1}]/(t^N-1)^2\longrightarrow k[A^{+/-1}]/(A^N-1),\quad g\mapsto Ag'(A). \] It is a derivation relative to the root evaluation, not a discarded normal direction on the fixed fiber. Write uniquely g=g_0+(t^N-1)g_1 modulo its square, with both g_i of degree<N. For the original averaged cut phi_N, the exact source row is \[ \phi_N(\mathcal E(g))=N\phi_N(g_1). \tag{7} \] The canonical polynomial g_0 contributes no constant coefficient after Ag_0'. The factor N in (7) is explicit. An unnormalized Fr source line multiplies both sides by its retained pairing unit; normalizing it does not change the head factor. Apply this linear map coefficientwise to the sourced relative interval complex R(E) of [the literal framing transgression](relative_framing_source_transgression.md). It commutes strictly with the interval differential, its two endpoint rows and its polynomial contraction. Thus (2)--(7) give an ACTUAL Fr-current realization of the clock-normal piece of that relative cut map, with the original averaged co-source. They do not assign an independent transfer coordinate to the cut. In particular both geometric compensated fields obey xi_i(A)=-2A(1-A). Hence the actual current -2(1-A) E has precisely their common clock component on every retained character g. The difference of the two geometric fields, which moves the other framing coordinate, is not determined by this common component. ## 4. The two primitives have a global P1 realization On the actual Fr source identify v_j with binom(N,j) z^j in H^0(P1,O(N)). Then e=partial_z, and the root inverse e^dagger is exactly the anchored integral integral_0^z, with its degree-(N+1) tail projected away. This gives (1) with the constant and top coefficient projectors. The opposite f^dagger is the corresponding south-chart primitive. These operators also have explicit global differential lifts. Writing D=z partial_z, take q_N(D) with q_N(j)=1/[(j+1)(N-j)] for j<N and q_N(N)=0. Then e^dagger=F q_N(D), f^dagger=E q_N(N-D) on H^0. Their differential order generally grows with N; it is NOT the bounded PBW normal-depth filtration of a crossing. Their identities on the full Cech resolution hold up the explicit contraction homotopy constructed in [the global source/co-source complex](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). The induced H^0 identities (1)--(3) are literal finite matrices. Dual Serre residue carries the same endpoint projectors, rather than deleting the two anchored boundary terms. All q-dependent arrow inverses and source units in (2) are retained coefficientwise in this lift. This does not make the chosen cut pseudoinverses into Hopf intertwiners on arbitrary tensor products. For example a trivial classical tensor summand is annihilated by both e and f; no repair using their currents alone can produce the identity on that summand. A whole-word map must transport the actual cut projector and mixed coproduct, not blindly tensor (2). ## 5. Exact off-diagonal correction Let H(q) be a retained head-matrix insertion, and keep its order to the RIGHT of the clock function. The same current formula with g(ZC_Q)H and g(C_Q)H has the exact result \[ \mathcal J_Z(gH) =\frac{g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q)}{1-Z}\,H +\frac{-g(C_Q)e^\dagger[e,H] +g(ZC_Q)P_0f^\dagger[f,H]}{1-Z}. \tag{8} \] This follows by the ordered product commutator, using e^dagger g(ZC_Q)=g(C_Q)e^dagger and f^dagger g(C_Q)=g(ZC_Q)f^dagger. If H is an actual head operator whose root commutes with the Fr e,f, the remainder is regular, but it generally does not vanish. If H contains noncommuting Fr insertions, regularity itself requires its additional normal source correction. Thus (3) does not supply the TRUE head Hopf currents merely by relabeling a scalar derivative. Their missing terms are the two explicit inserted moments in (8). The old physical clock and its whole Fourier-resolvent lift are those in [the controlled current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md), not the distinct new position clock on the diagonal source. Conjugating (2) and every inverse/projector by the whole source gauge preserves the identity exactly, including that dictionary. ### The constant-head correction is an explicit inner connection For a head matrix H kept CONSTANT in q and R, the root remainder in (8) has a closed form. Define \[ \ell_0=0,\qquad \ell_S=-\frac12\sum_{k=1}^{S} \frac{q_N^k+q_N^{-k}}{q_N^k-q_N^{-k}},\quad L_h=\operatorname{diag}(\ell_S),\quad\Sigma=2P_0-I. \] Then the actual divided-arrow matrices give \[ \mathcal E(H)=[\Sigma\otimes L_h,H]. \tag{8a} \] To prove this, write alpha_(R,S)=a_R+delta a_(1,R,S)+... and beta_(R,S)=b_R+delta b_(1,R,S)+..., with a_R=N-R+1,b_R=R+1. Exact commutation of E^(N) with the ordinary E, and F^(N) with ordinary F, along adjacent nonzero head arrows gives BOTH recurrences \[ \frac{a_{1,R,S}}{a_R}-\frac{a_{1,R,0}}{a_R}=\ell_S, \qquad \frac{b_{1,R,S}}{b_R}-\frac{b_{1,R,0}}{b_R}=\ell_S. \tag{8b} \] For example the adjacent F ratio has normal increment -1/2 (q^S+q^(-S))/(q^S-q^(-S)); differentiating the actual q-integer gives it directly. The E ratio gives the same increment. On R>=1, -e^dagger[e,H]/delta therefore gives -[L_h,H]; the literal R=0 repair contributes +[L_h,H]. All R-only constants commute with H. This proves (8a), without setting any individual arrow derivative to zero. Pairing k and N-k in the sum proves ell_(N-1)=0. Its root size is O(N log N), and no head endpoint coefficient has been inverted at a zero. For the actual normalized paired Fr source, the selected coefficient is c_N(m)=<Sigma>=2((1+m)/2)^N-1. Thus the original cut evaluates this correction to c_N(m) Phi_h([L_h,H]). It is an EXPLICIT original head Ward boundary. Let K=xA^(-1) and let B_cut be the actual matrix of the Ward contraction, [K,B_cut]=e_h-I/N. Since [K,L_h]=0, \[ \Phi_h([L_h,H])=-\operatorname{Tr}([B_{\mathrm{cut}},L_h][K,H]). \tag{8c} \] This follows by applying the original cut homotopy and Jacobi; the ordinary head trace of a commutator is zero. Hence this coefficient part vanishes IDENTICALLY on the actual diagonal Green arrays and on Ward-closed head partial traces. The endpoint-dependent polynomial c_N(m), including its values -1 and +1 at m=-1,+1, remains in the cochain homotopy. The unnormalized scale line multiplies this identity by its retained pairing rather than being canceled by hand. Actual q-dependent insertions have an additional specified lift term. If H=H_0+delta H_1+... with H_0 a constant-head matrix, then \[ \mathcal E(H)=[\Sigma L_h,H_0] -e_0^\dagger[e_0,H_1]+P_0f_0^\dagger[f_0,H_1]. \tag{8d} \] This includes the true block-wrap and mixed Hopf-normal coefficients. They cannot be removed using only (8c). If the fully closed actual matrix and its first normal are scalar, every term in (8d) vanishes; an unsummed current or a Fr-valued moment need not have that property. ## 6. A finite spectrum does not determine the whole Jackson current Fix a head eigenvalue c=Q^S and write C_s=c Z^R on its N+1 block states. Retain the actual polynomial FUNCTION \[ p_N(t)=\prod_{R=0}^{N}(t-cZ^R). \] Although p_N(C_s)=0 identically, its shifted value is \[ p_N(ZC_s)=c^{N+1}Z^{N(N+1)/2} \prod_{k=1}^{N+1}(Z^k-1)\,P_N, \tag{9} \] where P_N is the TOP STATE PROJECTOR, distinct from the polynomial p_N. All lower shifted points remain in the finite spectrum, but the top point cZ^(N+1) does not. Therefore \[ \mathcal J_Z(p_N) =-\frac{c^{N+1}Z^{N(N+1)/2}\prod_{k=1}^{N+1}(Z^k-1)}{1-Z}P_N =(-1)^N c^{N+1}(N+1)!\delta^N P_N+O(\delta^{N+1}). \tag{10} \] Consequently the WHOLE current depends on the retained function and its shifted observable, not only on the single finite matrix g(C_s). It is invisible through every normal order B<N in this example. The degree of p_N is N+1 and grows with N, so this does not contradict a bounded-presentation cyclotomic rigidity theorem. It gives a concrete actual-source reason to retain functions before their finite evaluations and jets. ## 7. The marked Green logarithm has a carry pole, not the regular Euler value The character theorem must not silently replace the marked logarithmic torsor. Put h=Log Q near h_N=2pi i/N and retain \[ \operatorname{Log}C_Q=hJ,\qquad \operatorname{Log}Z=Nh\quad\text{near }2\pi i. \] This is not the branch of Log Z near zero. A retained polynomial moment P(J)=P(Log C_Q/Log Q) shifts to P(J+N). The SAME actual whole current therefore gives the exact identity \[ \mathcal J_Z(P(J))=\frac{P(J)-P(J+N)}{\delta}. \tag{11} \] For a coefficient function F, retain F(Q,ZC_Q,J+N) as well as P(J+N). In particular a Cartan chirp q^(J^2) has root shift factor (-1)^N; freezing that coefficient while shifting P would change the actual carry. More generally let T carry every retained coefficient and the marked index simultaneously. Then the pole residue is exactly \[ \operatorname{Res}_{\delta=0}\mathcal J_Z =(I-T_0). \tag{12} \] On a coefficient fixed by this transport, T_0=e^(N partial_J), and (T_0-I)^(h+1)=0 on moments of degree<=h. On the normalized index J/N it is translation by one. With a nontrivial coefficient transport the associated grade retains that transport minus I; polynomial degree alone does not make it nilpotent. Equation (11) is the actual divided-current realization of the bounded Green carry in [the whole carry source](green_moment_carry_filtration.md). The pole is absent for the single-valued regular characters in Section 2, and present for these marked moments. Subtracting it without its relative endpoint/period class would remove the very moment repair used in the full scalar certificate. No such subtraction or global cancellation is inferred here. [Exact actual-matrix and whole-function audit](../experiments/audit_endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler.py). The [results](../experiments/endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_results.json) pass five actual generic-q families, seven actual root-normal families, 1498 off-diagonal head matrix-unit connection identities, 40 actual marked-clock/carry matrix identities (including a Cartan chirp), six whole finite-spectrum polynomial defects, and 42 symbolic bounded-moment carry checks. The [independent whole-function audit](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) also checks the endpoint product and distinguishes this retained function algebra from a fixed finite matrix quotient. The theorem supplies a clock/source-current component and the correction (8); it does not prove full sourced geometric support or a selected-volume limit.

title: Meridian transport on the cut source and its geometric dual
text: # Meridian transport on the cut source and its geometric dual Research note, 26 October 2026. The comparison in [the cut-wall note](cut_wall_and_cyclic_source.md) matched source presentations over S=C[[u,h]]. Here their normalized presentations are compared with meridian transport included. The geometric source has the inverse marked longitude character, which is retained explicitly. The result concerns the actual local cut coefficients and a calibrated formal geometric cyclic model. It does not identify the full knot's affine source, selected section, or volume norm. ## 1. The full actual cut has a difference-constant normalization line Keep q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), x=-M/q, Y=M^2, U=M^(2N), and sigma(M)=qM. Define p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2), r=sigma(p), c_2=q^2+q^(-2). The actual two-factor modified cut in the previous note is Phi_N(f)=C_N(U)[r f_+ + p f_-], C_N(U)=-zeta_N U/[(U-1)(U+1)], zeta_N=q^(N(1-N)/2). (1.1) Thus C_N=Gamma_N/d in that note. It is not Gamma_N that is meridian-constant: the geometric gap d is not constant. At an actual root sigma(U)=U, so sigma(C_N)=C_N exactly. The physical normalization is a marked meromorphic constant line, including its central lattice and both poles. It is not declared a unit at U=1 or absorbed into a coefficientwise formal unit. All statements below about regular S-presentations concern the normalized coefficients, with this line kept separately. The elementary exact identity sigma^2(p)=c_2 sigma(p)-p (1.2) follows by expanding its two monomials. It provides a fixed transport matrix for the cut coefficients: J=[ c_2 1 ], w=(r,p), [ -1 0 ] sigma(w)=w J, det J=1. (1.3) These identities are rational in q,M; they require no formal approximation. At roots they describe the actual weights before any node specialization. ## 2. The wall presentation is meridian-equivariant Work now over S with q=exp(h), M=exp(u), sigma(u)=u+h. Give S^2 the semilinear operator T=J sigma and S the operator sigma. The exact sequence of underlying S-modules is 0 -> S --j--> S^2 --ell--> S -> S/m -> 0, j=(p,-r)^t, ell=(r,p), m=(p,r)=(u,h). (2.1) Every arrow intertwines its stated meridian transport. Indeed J sigma(j)=j, ell J=sigma(ell). (2.2) The first identity uses (1.2); the second is (1.3). Consequently the normalized point source in (2.1) has character 1. This is a specified semilinear presentation, not just an isomorphism of point modules. Tensoring its cut with the recorded C_N line preserves equivariance on its original root meridian chart. Its polar specialization remains a whole-germ operation. The ordered scalar source residue stays fixed under the base meridian change: Res du dh/[p sigma(p)] =Res du dh/[sigma(p) sigma^2(p)]=1/16. (2.3) One direct verification is that the transformation of the two equations in (1.2) has determinant one. Equivalently their two Jacobian determinants at u=h=0 both equal 16. Also sigma(du wedge dh)=du wedge dh. These are statements about the base residue; a tensor period line has its own character. ## 3. The geometric cyclic free presentation has an exact shift matrix Let a,b be the calibrated geometric ratios from the preceding note, so a-b=v p, v in S^times, a(0,0)=b(0,0)=L_c, v(0,0)=kappa/4. Keep the actual SL2 longitude sign L_c; it is not set to one. On the normalized split module V=S^2 use T=diag(a,b)sigma, e=(1,1), f=(1,0), and Lambda=S e direct_sum m S f. Its generators e,pf,rf give the free presentation 0 -> F_1 --R--> F_0 --E--> Lambda -> 0, R=(0,r,-p)^t, E=[ 1 p r ], [ 1 0 0 ] with the following semilinear transports: T_(F_1)=a sigma, T_(F_0)=B sigma, B=[ b 0 0 ], [ v 0 -a ], [ 0 a a c_2]. (3.1) These are automorphisms: det B=b a^2 is a unit. Direct multiplication proves both compatibility identities E B=diag(a,b) sigma(E), B sigma(R)=a R. (3.2) The first uses a=b+vp, and the second uses (1.2). Thus the single relation is itself a meridian line, with ratio a. This records information that an S-module presentation alone omitted. ## 4. Dualizing gives exactly the cut complex with a period-line twist For a semilinear free module T=C sigma, its S-dual transport is C^(-t) sigma. This follows directly from (T phi)(z)=sigma(phi(T^(-1)z)). The dual of (3.1) is therefore the two-term presentation [F_0^vee --R^t--> P_a^vee], where P_a denotes the line with ratio a. Its degree-one cohomology is Ext^1_S(Lambda,S). The explicit dual matrix is B^(-t)=[ 1/b -c_2 v/(ab) v/(ab) ], [ 0 c_2/a -1/a ], [ 0 1/a 0 ]. (4.1) Its first coordinate line is stable, has ratio b^(-1), and maps to zero under R^t. It is exactly P_b^vee: as a functional on V it kills f and sends e to one. Hence this zero column may be quotiented out as a difference submodule, not just deleted from an underlying linear presentation. Define the constant quotient map Q=[ 0 1 0 ], [ 0 0 -1 ]. Then the full matrix identities are Q B^(-t)=a^(-1)J Q, R^t=(r,p)Q. (4.2) They prove an isomorphism of quotient difference complexes: [F_0^vee -> P_a^vee]/P_b^vee[0] = P_a^vee tensor [S^2_(J sigma) --(r,p)--> S_sigma]. (4.3) Thus the normalized actual cut presentation is precisely the universal factor of the geometric dual cyclic presentation; the dual geometric period line is the remaining factor. All arrows and meridian matrices are specified by (4.2). Taking degree-one cohomology gives the equivariant comparison Ext^1_S(Lambda,S)=P_a^vee tensor S/m, T on the point = L_c^(-1). (4.4) The scalar base residue remains (2.3). Multiplication by the two units v,sigma(v) changes it to 1/kappa^2 in the calibrated geometric equations. The opposite sign from the two ordered density values -p,r remains the sign already recorded in the cut-wall note. Neither that sign nor L_c^(-1) is absorbed into zeta_N. This closes the local equivariance calculation for the normalized cut and the calibrated geometric cyclic model. ## 5. The original root matrices check this transport The calculation has a direct check on the original root model. For V_x tensor V_x its generic highest roots are z_j=x^2 Q^(-j), Q=q^2, 0<=j<N. The actual full projector cuts, proved from the pivotal matrices, are d_(z_j). Substitution of the original modified dimension gives d_(z_j)=C_N(U) p_j, p_j=q^(-2j-1)M^2-q^(2j+1)M^(-2), sigma(p_j)=p_(j-1 mod N). (5.1) Here p_0=p and p_(N-1)=r. The actual highest-vector meridian matrix G=H(qM)P H(M)^(-1) intertwines total E,F,K and gives the full affine crossing identity with source (1+U^(-1))E_(N-1). Its label cycle induces exactly (5.1). Thus (1.3) describes the cut weights under this original meridian comparison, not only a chosen model shift on functions. There is a useful specialization qualification. For N>2 the free wall matrix has J^N=I, since its distinct eigenvalues are q^2,q^(-2). At N=2 they coincide; J^2 is not identity. The actual cut then has r=-p and its image is nevertheless N-periodic. Its extra kernel must be retained. The formal free presentation near q=1 is not thereby a free periodic root module at every distant root. No new topological invariant is inferred. ## 6. The universal part of every tensor cut uses two Fourier moments The existing intrinsic cut formula also identifies its universal coefficient part for arbitrary strand count b>=2. At generic color the final highest roots are z_j=x^b Q^(-j), and an actual intertwiner has multiplicity-block traces A_j. Put C_b=-zeta_N/[x^(bN)-x^(-bN)], J_+(A)=sum_j Q^(-j)Tr A_j, J_-(A)=sum_j Q^j Tr A_j. The full original cut is exactly mathfrak_t_W(A)=C_b[q x^b J_+(A) -q^(-1)x^(-b)J_-(A)]. (6.1) This follows by substituting the modified-dimension numerator in the already proved full trace formula. It reduces the cut coefficients to at most two Fourier moments. It does not reduce the N-dimensional trace quotient or the knot's quantum-A module to dimension two. The block traces still depend on the entire braid and its centralizer transitions. There is also an exact parity statement. Since sigma(x)=qx and q^N=-1, sigma(C_b)=(-1)^b C_b. Every fixed-label weight d_(z_j), as a rational function of M, therefore satisfies [T^2-(-1)^b(q^b+q^(-b))T+1] d_(z_j)=0. (6.2) For even b the common frame is meridian-constant; for odd b its sign line remains. For even b the actual fusion labels also permute under the known meridian atlas. No generic EFK-module comparison for odd b is being asserted by (6.2). Individual Fourier moments can be polar in a singular fusion frame, so (6.1) must still be specialized as a whole. ## 7. Scope, coverage and checks This supplies an exact semilinear local source presentation and its comparison to the geometric dual cyclic model, with the marked period character and the actual normalization line kept. The earlier all-orders normal-block comparison can transport P_a to the dual of the corresponding actual formal normal line. It does not identify that line with the selected finite sum. The actual global source arrows, knot section, and central lattice at U=1 still have to be transported through sewing. The pole in C_N is genuine difference-constant period data; its cancellation cannot be inferred from a regular S-unit gauge. Nonzero pairing of the selected source with the geometric block, and its regulator norm across levels, remain unproved. In particular this note does not establish the global affine comparison equation for c_K,c_T. Modified-trace and formal difference-equation coverage is the existing coverage recorded in the preceding notes. No novelty claim is made for free resolutions, semilinear duality, or cyclic presentations. All displayed intertwiners and coefficient identities are proved by the direct calculations above. [The audit](../experiments/audit_equivariant_cut_source.py) checks the universal wall transport, relation transport, full free cyclic matrix, dual, stable branch line, quotient chain map and residue. Twelve generic original root cases at N=2,3,4,5,6,9 construct the actual E,F,K, original crossings and meridian matrices. All 116 projector cuts at both colors agree with (5.1); the full affine crossing identity and retained normalizer are checked. The N=2 extra kernel is recorded, not treated as periodicity of its free presentation. Four exact symbolic width checks retain the parity in (6.2). [Results](../experiments/equivariant_cut_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_equivariant_cut_source.py The subsequent [sewn-source theorem](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md) now transports the actual residue through arbitrary full knot operators and gives a regular rational lift of its projective corner. It also forces a further marking: one surviving meridian must carry charge three. Its step and full dimension factor are retained. The inverse complete longitude character above cannot distinguish that odd charge from charge one. The entire source and its selected geometric period still need comparison.

title: Equivariant peripheral roots and the remaining scalar period
text: # Equivariant peripheral roots and the remaining scalar period Research note, 25 October 2026. The local projective-frame theorem does not by itself choose compatible deck roots around a knot. This note supplies that compatibility and a scalar descent argument. Its inputs are the directly proved cyclic recoupling and frame identities; no global quantum-hyperbolic invariance theorem is assumed. Let W be a compact core of a one-cusped hyperbolic knot complement in S^3, Gamma=pi_1(W), and P=pi_1(partial W). The same proofs apply to more cusps with one copy of the peripheral data for each cusp. Let n be odd. Retain the ordered ideal vertices and all peripheral markings. Work on the nondegenerate decorated-representation locus described below. The conclusions concern finite-level algebraic tensors and their scalar phases. Identification of the selected literature period and its integration cycle, as well as its compatibility across levels, remains outstanding. ## 1. Root lines on Gamma/P are determined at the peripheral stabilizer First an elementary groupoid lemma. Let a group Gamma act transitively on V=Gamma/P. A Gamma-equivariant complex line over V is determined, up to equivariant isomorphism, by its one-dimensional P-representation chi on the fiber at v_0=P. The reconstruction is the associated line Gamma times_P C_chi -> Gamma/P. This can be checked by sending [g,z] to g.z in the fiber at gv_0; the relation [gp,z]=[g,chi(p)z] makes the map well defined and invertible. An equivariant n-th root line, with an identification of its n-th tensor power with this line, therefore amounts to a character delta:P->C^* such that delta^n=chi. Its isomorphism classes form a torsor for Hom(P,mu_n). For P=Z^2 with its marked meridian mu and longitude lambda, write M=chi(mu), L=chi(lambda). Every pair of roots m^n=M, l^n=L gives delta(mu^a lambda^b)=m^a l^b, and conversely. Thus the root-line cover has degree n^2 and deck group mu_n times mu_n. No semisimplicity of the full peripheral representation is needed: only its invariant line. At a complete unipotent or signed-unipotent character the same statement holds. The signs and the n^2 root choices are retained. These are isomorphism classes of roots of the decorating line. They do not classify the complete quantum period, its normalization phase, or its continuous dilogarithm factor. ## 2. An explicit multiplicative root of the projective denominator Choose an SL(2,C) lift rho of the decorated projective representation and a peripheral fixed point p_0. Put p_v=rho(r_v)p_0, where r_v in Gamma is a representative with r_v v_0=v and r_(v_0)=1. In an affine chart write d(g,p)=c_g p+d_g, rho(g)(p,1)=d(g,p)(rho(g)p,1). Choose a chart avoiding zero and infinity on the points in use. For a fixed representation the orbit is countable, so a complex frame can avoid the entire orbit. For algebraic families every finite diagram uses its own common nondegenerate Zariski open chart. We do not assume one finite open chart avoids every possible group-word denominator. The matrix multiplication identity gives exactly d(gh,p)=d(g,rho(h)p)d(h,p). (2.1) The peripheral character is chi(h)=d(h,p_0), h in P. Choose delta as in Section 1, and choose a_v with a_v^n=d(r_v,p_0), a_(v_0)=1. For g in Gamma define h(g,v)=r_(gv)^(-1)g r_v in P and set D(g,v)=a_(gv) delta(h(g,v))/a_v. (2.2) Substitution into (2.1) proves D(g,v)^n=d(g,p_v), D(g_1g_2,v)=D(g_1,g_2v)D(g_2,v). (2.3) For the second identity use h(g_1g_2,v)=h(g_1,g_2v)h(g_2,v). The intermediate a values cancel. This constructs the root cocycle; independently taking roots of the denominators would not prove the second equation. Changing a_v by zeta_v in mu_n changes D by the coboundary zeta_(gv)/zeta_v. Changing coset representatives gives an isomorphic root line. Conversely any such multiplicative D restricts to delta at v_0, so Section 1 proves that these are all root-line choices modulo object gauges. Internal root choices are frames, while the two peripheral characters remain actual data. For a finite diagram, every r_v is a fixed group word. Its matrix entries and d(r_v,p_0) are algebraic functions of the decorated representation; only finitely many n-th roots occur. Thus (2.2) is algebraic on its nondegenerate root chart. The construction on all configurations uses compatible charts; this statement does not assert that the entire quantum period lives on a degree-n^2 cover. An SL(2) lift exists for the knot group under discussion. The obstruction is the central two-cocycle obtained from arbitrary lifts of the projective matrices. Since W is aspherical, its class is in H^2(W;mu_2)=0: knot-exterior homology is H_1=Z, H_2=0, so the universal coefficient calculation gives zero. Trivializing that cocycle constructs a lift. Its two choices differ by a sign character of Gamma. For odd n, changing rho(g) by epsilon(g) and D(g,v) by the same epsilon(g) preserves (2.3). Ratios D(g,v_j)/D(g,v_i) are unchanged, so the triangle Weyl rescalings do not acquire an unrecorded sign from this lift choice. If peripheral coordinates are squared eigenvalues, their root cover is equivalent after choosing the lift: if u^n=chi^2, set delta=u^((n+1)/2)/chi. Then delta^n=chi and delta^2=u. The inverse is u=delta^2. This records the unhalved versus eigenvalue convention without dropping a sign. ## 3. The triangle transports can be made strictly equivariant The ideal vertices of the universal cover are Gamma/P. Assume the decorating map has infinite image; this holds on the non-elementary locus containing the geometric representation. Use configurations with distinct developing points. For each ordered triangle f=(i,j,k), lambda_f=(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k). Equations (2.3) give compatible Weyl rescalings kappa(g,f)=D(g,j)/D(g,i), nu(g,f)=D(g,k)/D(g,i). Choose endpoint roots A_v^n=p_v. Choose a marked spectral root alpha on one representative of each triangle orbit, and propagate it by alpha_(gf)=kappa(g,f)alpha_f. The action on ordered triangles is free. Indeed P is malnormal in the hyperbolic knot group: a nontrivial element in two distinct conjugate maximal peripheral subgroups would be a parabolic fixing two distinct cusp points in the faithful geometric action, which is impossible. Thus an element fixing two distinct ideal vertices is the identity. In particular the propagation is well defined. It uses this property of the underlying knot group, not faithfulness of the variable rho. The explicit H K construction in `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` now yields unnormalized maps S(g,f) with the strict law S(g_1g_2,f)=S(g_1,g_2f)S(g_2,f). (3.1) Their determinant roots can also be chosen multiplicatively. For each free triangle orbit choose f_0, write f=r_f f_0 uniquely, and choose b_f^n=det(S(r_f,f_0))^(-1), with b_(f_0)=1. Set rho(g,f)=b_(gf)/b_f, S_hat(g,f)=rho(g,f)S(g,f). Then det S_hat=1 and (3.1) still holds exactly. Different b choices are scalar frame gauges. This removes a possible triangle-level composition anomaly constructively. It does not yet make arbitrary independent tetrahedron normalizations equivariant. ## 4. The remaining tetrahedral phase is an explicit cocycle Choose shared face roots xi and the signed Racah matrices R_hat as in the projective-frame note. They have determinant (-1)^((n-1)/2) and satisfy the ordered pentagon. For t=(0,1,2,3), define Delta(g,t) by R_hat(gt)(S_hat(g,023) tensor S_hat(g,012)) =Delta(g,t)(S_hat(g,013) tensor S_hat(g,123))R_hat(t). The previously proved ordered operator comparison and Schur argument prove that this scalar exists and is nonzero. Determinants give Delta(g,t) in A=mu_(n^2). (4.1) Here A is cyclic of order n^2; it is different from the peripheral deck group mu_n times mu_n. There is no reduction of A to mu_n being assumed in this note. Strict composition of S_hat gives Delta(gh,t)=Delta(g,ht)Delta(h,t). (4.2) Apply the ordered pentagon before and after g and cancel the common invertible S maps. Its scalar part gives product_(i=0)^4 Delta(g,t_without_i)^((-1)^i)=1. (4.3) Literal tensor permutations cause no extra scalar in this calculation; they occur on both sides of the same pentagon. Thus Delta is simultaneously a group one-cocycle and a configuration three-cocycle. ## 5. Why relative degree four is the relevant obstruction Let C_k be the free abelian group on ordered (k+1)-tuples of ideal vertices whose developing points are distinct, with alternating face boundary. Its augmented complex is exact. For any finite cycle choose one vertex whose developing point avoids its finitely many points; prepending it gives a cone, and boundary(cone)+cone(boundary)=identity. Infinite image of the decoration supplies that vertex. For k>=1 the Gamma action on C_k is free by malnormality. Also C_0=Z[Gamma/P]. With I=ker(C_0->Z), the complex ... -> C_3 -> C_2 -> C_1 -> I -> 0 is therefore a free Gamma-resolution. Its invariant cochains in degrees k>=2 compute H^k(Gamma,P;A). One can see the degree shift directly: Ext^(k-1)_Gamma(I,A) is computed at C_k; applying Hom and Ext to 0->I->Z[Gamma/P]->Z->0 gives the relative cohomology exact sequence, using the induced-module identification with P-cohomology. Both W and its boundary torus are aspherical with these fundamental groups. Their cellular resolutions identify this relative cohomology with H^k(W,partial W;A). In particular H^4(Gamma,P;A)=0, H^3(Gamma,P;A)=A. (5.1) The first equation follows from the dimension-three relative cellular complex. The second evaluates a cocycle on the oriented relative fundamental class. It also follows without a field assumption from H_3(W,partial W;Z)=Z and H_2(W,partial W;Z)=Z, both free. Thus the statement holds for composite n as well. ## 6. Scalar descent theorem and its residual period torsor Equations (4.1)--(4.3), freeness on tetrahedra, and (5.1) imply that the R_hat matrices admit A-valued corrections making both equivariance and the ordered pentagon exact. Here is a proof that retains the phase. Choose t_0 in each free tetrahedron orbit and put kappa(g t_0)=Delta(g,t_0)^(-1). By (4.2), replacing R_hat(t) by kappa(t)R_hat(t) makes the tensors equivariant. Its pentagon discrepancy is the four-cochain Omega=delta kappa. Equation (4.3) implies that Omega is Gamma-invariant, and delta Omega=1. The vanishing H^4 in (5.1) gives an invariant three-cochain b with delta b=Omega^(-1). Hence R_tilde(t)=kappa(t)b(t)R_hat(t) (6.1) is equivariant and satisfies the pentagon exactly. Its determinant is unchanged because the correction lies in mu_(n^2). Two such corrections differ by an invariant three-cocycle. Modulo shared-face scalar gauges, their choices form a torsor for H^3(Gamma,P;mu_(n^2))=mu_(n^2).
