Therefore no linear operator \(B\) on all Laurent polynomials satisfies \(\mathcal E_N=B\mathcal C\). The meromorphic factors in (1.2) are not separately composable there: at \(kN
e0\), one has the essential zero/pole cancellation in (1.1). On the canonical band \(1,A,\ldots,A^{N-1}\), the finite average at \(A=1\) and the logarithmic residue coincide exactly: \[  oxed{\phi_N(f)= rac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}f(Q_N^a) =[A^0]f=\operatorname{Res}_{A=0}f(A) rac{dA}{A}.} 	ag{1.4} \] No asymptotic Euler correction is needed on this band. It does not follow that the Bernoulli factor is uniformly \(1+O(H)\): at frequency \(N-1\), its modulus is of order \(N\). In the whole normal order \(A^N=U\), an unreduced \(A^N\) gives the canonical constant \(U\). Formula (1.4) must be applied after this carry. It cannot be applied to the unreduced ordinary Laurent expression and then used to delete \(U\). ## 2. A canonical, pole-free counterexample with the actual cut For \(N\ge3\), set \[  oxed{f_N(A)=1-A^{N-1}-(1-A)^{N-1}.} 	ag{2.1} \] It is already a canonical polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\). It has \(f_N(0)=f_N(1)=0\). Consequently \[  oxed{\phi_N(f_N)=0,\qquad \phi_{S,N}(f_N)=  rac{N\phi_N(f_N)-f_N(1)}{N-1}=0,} 	ag{2.2} \] for both the original finite source and the repaired source which deletes \(A=1\). On every compact lens \[ |A|\le r<1,\qquad |1-A|\le r<1, \] one has, for each fixed derivative order \(k\), \[ \partial_A^k(f_N-1)=O_k(N^k r^{N-1-k}). \] Thus \(f_N\) has the normalized local asymptotic series identically \(1\), to every order in \(1/N\), on a nonempty open chart. Its local action is zero and its principal amplitude is the nonzero constant \(1\). There are no poles. At completeness the actual density is, up to its nonzero frame-independent torsion/base line, \[ \Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}=dt\wedge d\log A. \] Multiplying it by \(f_N(A)\) and taking the already marked relative interval \(t=0,1\), with zero endpoint co-sources, still gives the same nonzero local principal density to all orders. The relative transgression is exactly \(f_N\,d\log A\). Both finite cut pairings of it are nevertheless zero by (2.2). The example also has formally closed local Ward jets. On a slightly smaller lens, \(Q_NA\) stays in the same larger lens, so \(f_N(Q_NA)-f_N(A)\) is exponentially small with every fixed derivative. Diagonal \(K\)-commutation is exact, and the adjacent \(E,F\) Ward differences are flat there. They are not exact global Ward identities. This is not an actual knot state or a second coherent rational-\(Q\) unfolding. It proves that canonical degree, absence of poles, exact source normalization, all local asymptotic jets, and formal residual Ward closure do not imply the desired source survival. It does not contradict scalarity of the actual complete cut, nor an exact global Ward/source chain map if one is constructed. Its failure is concrete: outside the local lens its norm can be exponential, and the global source sees the resulting cancellation. ## 3. A functional leading-source theorem The following is a sufficient globalization statement whose hypotheses can be checked on functions rather than at individual levels. Let \(\mathcal D\subset\mathbb C^	imes\) be connected and contain a nonempty geometric chart \(\mathcal U\) and a circle \(\Gamma_ho=\{|A|=ho\}\) around zero. Suppose: 1. \(F_N\) is a canonical polynomial of degree \(<N\). 2. \(F_N\) is locally polynomially bounded on \(\mathcal D\): for each compact \(K\subset\mathcal D\), \(\sup_K|F_N|\le C_KN^{d_K}\), with \(d_K\) independent of \(N\). 3. On \(\mathcal U\), it has a complete uniform asymptotic expansion \(F_N\sim\sum_{j\ge0}N^{-j}F_j\), where every \(F_j\) is holomorphic on the same \(\mathcal D\). 4. \(F_0=c
e0\) is the geometric constant after the retained action, torsion and base-only lines have been factored out. Then the expansion propagates to compact subsets of \(\mathcal D\), and \[  oxed{\phi_N(F_N)=c+O(N^{-1}).} 	ag{3.1} \] Here is a direct proof of the propagation. On three concentric disks with radii \(r<ho<R\), the maximum principle on an annulus gives \[ M(ho)\le M(r)^	heta M(R)^{1-	heta},\quad 	heta= rac{\log(R/ho)}{\log(R/r)}>0. \] It follows by applying the maximum principle to \(\log|f|\) minus the radial harmonic interpolation of its two boundary bounds. A finite chain of overlapping disks therefore propagates an \(O(N^{-m})\) local error to \(O(N^{-m	heta_*+d_*})\), for fixed \(	heta_*>0,d_*\). Apply this to \(F_N-\sum_{j<m}N^{-j}F_j\). Its global bound has a polynomial exponent independent of \(m\), since each fixed truncation is bounded on a compact set. Choosing \(m\) large proves any desired target order. Compactness gives uniformity on \(\Gamma_ho\). Equation (1.4) and the residue integral then give (3.1). This proof uses no asymptotic expansion of the Bernoulli operator. The theorem also applies to a relative density with coefficients depending on \(t\), if these bounds are uniform on the marked interval and its endpoint co-sources and the coefficient functions extend on a common domain. The relative source then remains the full integral-minus-endpoints functional. For the root-deleted source, its additional term \(F_N(1)/(N-1)\) must also be controlled or compensated by its retained Ward homotopy; deletion alone is not that estimate. Alternatively, an exponentially small local error and a subexponential global bound suffice by the same disk argument. Local formal expansions without either global bound do not. ## 4. The deleted-root boundary layer has an explicit size test Deleting \(A=1\) removes the point, not its neighboring sampled values. For a fixed meromorphic coefficient with pole order \(p\) at \(1\), assume \[ |r(A)|\le C|1-A|^{-p} \] on the sampled circle away from that point. The elementary bound \(|1-Q_N^a|\ge4\min(a,N-a)/N\) gives \[  rac1{N-1}\sum_{a=1}^{N-1}|r(Q_N^a)| = egin{cases} O(1),&p=0,\ O(\log N),&p=1,\ O(N^{p-1}),&p>1. \end{cases} 	ag{4.1} \] Thus an \(H^j r(A)\) loop term need not be small after averaging if \(p\ge j+1\). A proof of suitable pole-order bounds and a global remainder estimate could establish leading source control. Merely knowing that each loop coefficient is rational on the geometric chart does not give either bound. ## 5. Consequence for the proposed geometric source map The constant action on the \(B_1\)-torsor and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{geom}}=	ext{nonzero constant}\cdot\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}\) correctly identify the **local** candidate coefficient. The specified relative geometric interval would pair it to that nonzero constant. The exact finite averaging identity does not show that the actual canonical source is that relative class after transverse elimination. The missing comparison must preserve the resonant/carry data and exclude the concrete cancellation in section 2. A global tempered function theorem of the form in section 3, or an exact source chain map with a nonzero leading projection, would do so. Neither follows from the present local principal-density identity or the formal residual Ward operators alone.

title: A finite actual Frobenius clock graph has the marked Gauss-wall flux
text: # A finite actual Frobenius clock graph has the marked Gauss-wall flux Research proof, 27 October 2026. One actual divided-source clock gives an algebraic graph in the resolved framing space. Its compact cycle has exactly the previously computed wall flux, with no limiting calibration of the constant. A near-identity logarithmic change of source coordinates relates these finite graphs to the known physical meridian graph and gives an explicit source-form homotopy. This identifies a SINGLE inserted Frobenius clock and its cycle. The old physical head clock changes polarization under the Fourier/ controlled-shift gauge; it is not this inserted position clock by default. No full word/current or Gaussian comparison is inferred. ## 1. The actual finite clock and its global normal graph Put c=2pi*i, N>=3, Q=exp(c/N), and r=N in the [actual high-color source](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). Let R be its block number. Its divided coherent source has psi(t)_k=t^k, lambda(u)_k=binom(N,k)u^k/(1+tu)^N. On the source quadric use v=t, a=u/(1+tu), T=va. The binomial theorem gives the exact actual covariant symbol F_N(T)=sigma(Q^(-R)) =[1+alpha_N T]^N, alpha_N=Q^(-1)-1. (1) It is one symbol, not an ordinary power of another clock symbol substituted for a star product. On the cyclotomic diagonal source, the inserted head position clock Q^S equals Q^R. Thus (1) is also the symbol of its inverse inserted head POSITION clock. On the resolved frame space Y of the [Gauss-wall calculation](gauss_wall_flux_and_actual_peripheral_character.md), with north coordinates eta,v,a and south coordinates V=1/v, eta'=-v^2 eta, a'=v-v^2a, T'=1-T, F=1-eta v=1+eta'V, define an algebraic source graph i_N by eta_N(v,a)=[1-F_N(va)]/v. (2) This quotient is polynomial: its numerator is divisible by v. The south clock expression is F_N^+(T')=[1+(Q-1)T']^N, F_N^-(T)=F_N^+(1-T), (3) where F_N^- denotes (1). Equation (3) follows from Q^N=1. Consequently eta'_N=(F_N^+(Va')-1)/V is also polynomial and obeys the required transition. Thus i_N is a global algebraic graph over the source quadric, retaining both compact poles. At a generic Q, the binomial model instead has the exact factor F_N^-(T)=Q^(-N)F_N^+(1-T). (4) The factor in (4) cannot be discarded before taking quantum-normal jets. Moreover the actual whole divided coherent source has its own retained normal coefficients; its off-root symbol is not asserted to be the naive binomial continuation of (1). ## 2. The real compact cycle avoids the wall with bounded clock norm Let Gamma be the marked real compact source, on which 0<=T<=1 and angular integration of Omega=dv wedge da gives integral_(angle) Omega=-c dT. Along this cycle, |1+alpha_N T|^2 =1-4sin^2(pi/N)T(1-T), cos^N(pi/N)<=|F_N(T)|<=1. (5) The lower bound is positive for N>=3. It is uniformly bounded away from zero as N varies: for example log cos(pi/N)>=-pi^2/(2N^2 cos^2(pi/3)) gives a fixed positive lower bound after multiplying by N. In fact the lower bound in (5) tends to one. Thus Gamma_N=i_N(Gamma) lies in Y minus the Gauss wall D={F=0}, and this clock and its inverse have no exponential norm loss on that cycle. The two source poles lie on the exceptional divisor E, since F_N(0)=F_N(1)=1. No unmarked identification of their clock logarithms is made. ## 3. Its marked wall flux is exact at every level Use the global closed form Xi=dlog F wedge dlog v from the Gauss-wall theorem. Pulling it back to (2) gives i_N^*Xi=-N alpha_N/(1+alpha_N T) Omega. (6) For N>=3 the segment 1+alpha_N T avoids zero. Its logarithm, continued from zero at T=0, has value Log(Q^(-1))=-c/N at T=1. Therefore integral_(Gamma_N) Xi =c N Log(Q^(-1))=-c^2=4pi^2. (7) The continuous marked logarithm of F_N is N Log(1+alpha_N T), which changes by -c even though the two endpoint values of F_N are both one. This is the full winding, not a point evaluation which forgets the period. Equation (7) reproduces the marked physical flux by direct evaluation of the actual finite clock. It does not alone identify every homology component or the selected knot's geometric contribution. The isolated level N=2 has a zero on this straight source segment; it needs a separately marked relative deformation. Nothing in the asymptotic argument requires claiming (5) there. ## 4. A whole near-identity source reparametrization On a common complex neighborhood of the compact source define Ttilde_N(T)=-(N/c)Log(1+alpha_N T), a_tilde=Ttilde_N(va)/v. (8) The log is the marked one of Section 3. Since alpha_N=-c/N+O(N^-2), these functions are holomorphic there, extend through v=0, and Ttilde_N(0)=0, Ttilde_N(1)=1, Ttilde_N'(T)=-N alpha_N/[c(1+alpha_N T)]!=0, Ttilde_N(T)=T+O(N^-1) (9) locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. In the south chart use Ttilde'_N(T')=(N/c)Log(1+(Q-1)T'), which equals 1-Ttilde_N(1-T'). Thus Phi_N:(v,a)->(v,a_tilde) respects the actual affine clutch near the entire compact cycle. The finite clock becomes exactly F_N(T)=exp[-c Ttilde_N(T)]. (10) Its meridian normal eta_N is therefore the OLD physical meridian normal evaluated at the reparametrized SOURCE coordinates. In Y the associated frame coordinate a still differs from a_tilde; the remaining centralizer translation is explicit, not omitted. It fixes eta,v and changes a to a_tilde by a->a-eta beta_N, with beta_N=[T-Ttilde_N(T)]/[1-F_N(T)]. (11) Both endpoints of (11) are removable on the marked cycle. This is a statement about the resolved framing coordinate, not an assertion that its translation is the actual internal current. There is also an exact source-form homotopy: Phi_N^*Omega-Omega =d[(T-Ttilde_N(T))dlog v]. (12) The one-form in (12) extends through both compact poles: its coefficient vanishes at T=0 and T=1, respectively, and the two opposite-chart expressions agree. It is O(N^-1) there with all fixed derivatives. Thus the source area class and its compact period are retained, including their polar clutch. ## 5. The operator-polarization qualification is essential Under H_0=G Fourier/N, the OLD head clock is sent to the NEW head shift V^(-1), while the old head shift is sent to Q^(-R)Q^S. In particular Q^(-R)Q^S is identity on the selected diagonal source. The inserted Q^S in Section 1 is not the image of the old physical head clock under this same gauge. Consequently (1)--(12) give an explicit actual-clock algebraic cycle with the correct marked geometric flux, and its regular logarithmic source reparametrization. Using it as the image of the knot's original physical cut or its independent internal centralizer current additionally requires the exact Fourier/ conormal operator dictionary and the full star/current transport. Matching functions, symplectic forms or winding alone does not supply that last identification. The exact operator adapter is derived in [the controlled Fourier current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md). The separate current/polarization and coherent-metric audit is in [the Fr-clock/internal-centralizer note](frobenius_clock_and_internal_centralizer_map.md). ## 6. Independent coefficient and period checks [The diagnostic](../experiments/audit_finite_frobenius_clock_graph.py) constructs the root source from the ACTUAL integral divided matrices, before testing the binomial clock formula and north/south equality. Its 72 finite-field cases cover N=3,...,10 and both source poles. High-precision marked integrals at nine levels N=3,...,256 check the flux, both removable centralizer endpoints, and the stated clock-modulus bound. These checks support the uniform proof; they do not identify the inserted clock with the old physical head clock. [Results](../experiments/finite_frobenius_clock_graph_results.json).

title: A finite positive certificate supplies every sufficiently long filling branch
text: # A finite positive certificate supplies every sufficiently long filling branch 29 October 2026. This is a geometric strengthening of the [finite real-algebraic certificate](finite_real_algebraic_geometric_certificate.md). When that certificate succeeds for the ACTUAL marked base exterior, its meridian-coordinate germ supplies existence, not merely a conditional completion statement, for all independently sufficiently long primitive slopes. The proof uses the certified Jacobian, elementary affine cusp commutation, and a uniform contraction. It does not supply a quantum source packet for a new diagram. ## 1. Precise scope Let the finite certificate exhibit a positive complete shape assignment on an oriented ideal triangulation of the marked manifold M. In particular its edge links are circles, vertex links are tori, edge products have winding ONE, and both primitive peripheral multipliers are one. Its marking is a verified oriented homeomorphism to M, not only a degree-one map or an agreement of trace data. Use actual peripheral bases (mu_i, lambda_i) whose complete translation ratio has positive imaginary part. Write U_i,V_i for the small logs of their complex similarity multipliers, so these are squared-eigenvalue logs, with central SL signs already removed. The certified edge-plus- meridian Jacobian gives a holomorphic shape germ with coordinates U=(U_1,...,U_h). Developing finitely many tetrahedra produces an ACTUAL framed holomorphic representation rho_U in bounded charts near the complete holonomy. The selected peripheral fixed flags are the developed ideal vertices. All shapes remain positive after one fixed shrink. For every chosen subset I of cusps and every primitive integer slope (a_i,b_i) at i in I, put ell_i=sqrt(a_i^2+b_i^2). There is a fixed L_M such that, whenever min_(i in I) ell_i > L_M, and for every independent choice epsilon_i=+1 or -1, the specified germ has a UNIQUE nearby point U_i=0 (i not in I), a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i (i in I). (1) The word UNIQUE refers to this fixed marked decorated gluing germ. It does not assert uniqueness of other character components. Its point gives a positively oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the actual indicated filling, by the [general completion construction](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). The threshold is uniform over signs and over independently unequal lengths. There is no prime-level or quantum parameter in this theorem. ## 2. Cusp commutation forces a diagonal first-order peripheral map In the moving selected-flag frame at cusp i, write its commuting affine holonomies as mu_i(w)=exp(U_i) w+B_i(U), lambda_i(w)=exp(V_i(U)) w+D_i(U). The finite developed words make B_i,D_i holomorphic, and B_i(0),D_i(0) are the nonzero complete translation periods. Commutation gives EXACTLY (exp(U_i)-1) D_i=(exp(V_i)-1) B_i. (2) Shrink so B_i never vanishes. On U_i=0, equation(2) gives exp(V_i)=1; the chosen small log is therefore V_i=0. Holomorphic division gives V_i(U)=U_i tau_i(U), tau_i(0)=D_i(0)/B_i(0), Im tau_i(0)>0. (3) This applies also while other cusps vary. In particular dV_i/dU_j=0 at zero for j!=i, and dV_i/dU_i is the ACTUAL Euclidean cusp ratio. This does not infer a physical quantum-color Hessian from a Casimir spectral coordinate. Matching a source Hessian to these logs is a separate source/peripheral calculation. ## 3. A contraction uniform over all primitive slope directions Choose a closed complex polydisk ||U||_infinity<=r on which every tau_i is holomorphic and Im tau_i>=m>0, |tau_i|<=T, sum_j |partial_j tau_i|<=L. (4) These inequalities hold after shrinking the certified germ. With c=m/sqrt(1+T^2)>0, the real two-by-two matrix with columns (1,0) and (Re tau_i, Im tau_i) has determinant at least m and Frobenius norm at most sqrt(1+T^2). Consequently, for EVERY real pair (a,b), |a+b tau_i(U)|>=c sqrt(a^2+b^2). (5) Set all unfilled U coordinates to zero, and define on the remaining closed polydisk (T_sigma(U))_i=2pi i epsilon_i/[a_i+b_i tau_i(U)]. (6) Equations(3) show that its fixed points are precisely(1). If ell_min=min_i ell_i, then(4)--(5) give ||T_sigma(U)||_infinity<=2pi/(c ell_min), ||D T_sigma(U)||_(infinity->infinity) <=2pi L/(c^2 ell_min). (7) For example any strict threshold ell_min>max(4pi/(c r),4pi L/c^2) (8) makes the image lie in the radius-r/2 polydisk and the Lipschitz constant less than one half. The mean-value estimate is valid along complex straight segments because the polydisk is convex. Iteration therefore converges uniformly to one fixed point, and any solution in this germ is that fixed point. No largest-to-smallest slope comparison is used. Primitivity is needed for the filled topology and smooth meridional angle, not for this analytic contraction itself. More precisely, for each filled cusp, |U_i|<=2pi/(c ell_i), U_i=2pi i epsilon_i/[a_i+b_i tau_i(0)] +O(1/(ell_i ell_min)), (9) with one constant for all direction/sign tuples. Subtract the two fractions in(6) and its value at zero, use |tau_i(U)-tau_i(0)|<=L||U||_infinity and |b_i|<=ell_i, to obtain the error in(9). The complete point has no unproved representation-existence input: it is the one certified shape germ. ## 4. Completion and a uniform volume check The actual bounded representation rho_U and its flags tend uniformly to the certified complete data as ell_min tends to infinity. Unfilled cusps have U_i=V_i=0 by(3), and remain nontrivial parabolic near the complete point. Filled cusps satisfy the ACTUAL small-log equation(1), not merely its exponential. Thus the explicit local developing map, log-link and primitive 2pi tube construction of the general theorem applies. It fills the specified primitive slopes on the same marked topology with a smooth complete finite-volume metric. A nonprimitive slope or a charge of magnitude greater than one would instead be a different topological/cone assertion and is not silently included. There is also a useful uniform normalization check. Let Vol(rho_U) be the absolute marked representation volume. Its already established boundary differential is dVol=(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i]. (10) Integrate along the straight path sU, 0<=s<=1, in the shape germ. Using V_i=U_i tau_i(U), the leading integrand is -s Im tau_i(0)|U_i|^2/2. All remaining terms are bounded by a constant times ||U||_infinity sum_i |U_i|^2. Hence Vol(rho_U)=Vol(M)-(1/4)sum_i Im tau_i(0)|U_i|^2 +O(||U||_infinity sum_i |U_i|^2). (11) Substituting(9) gives, uniformly over independently long slopes, Vol(M(sigma))=Vol(M) -pi^2 sum_(i in I) Im tau_i(0)/|a_i+b_i tau_i(0)|^2 +O(ell_min^(-1) sum_(i in I) ell_i^(-2)). (12) This proves the usual geometric volume here from the actual completed metric and marked fundamental class, rather than assigning a volume to a formal root of a peripheral polynomial. In particular the volume decreases strictly for all sufficiently long nonempty fillings. ## 5. What this resolves, and the source estimate it does not replace The finite positive certificate plus its deduced meridian Jacobian already removes the GEOMETRIC existence qualification in the general completion theorem for all sufficiently long primitive slopes. A separate deformation or discrete-faithfulness theorem need not be assumed. A source candidate matching this germ and the same primitive logs can therefore use this result directly. For a new original quantum source the remaining non-tautological gates are still those in [the exact long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md): an actual PHYSICAL auxiliary-color packet, its nonzero holomorphic complex-corridor asymptotic, a strict bound on the entire complementary physical color cube including aliases/normals, and its literal marked representation/action map with the absolute complete regulator anchor. The exact twist expansion is already multilinear at arbitrary width. The new [complete-circle boundary packet](actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.md) controls a spectral Casimir coordinate and all its polynomial normal derivatives. Without its exact physical-color transform and the global color estimate it does not discharge these source gates. Nor does this geometric contraction estimate the quantum Cauchy energy on a generic branched graph. No files in the frozen publication snapshot were modified in proving this addendum. Its proof is analytical; no sampled numerical evidence is used for the slope-uniform assertion. The uniform assertions follow from the proof above, not from a finite collection of slope samples.

title: A finite Fourier packet resolves the original long-twist quadrature type
text: # A finite Fourier packet resolves the original long-twist quadrature type 28 October 2026. This is a constructive extension of the [source-preserving inner quadrature](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md). It keeps the original finite lattice values, the original endpoints and an explicit convergent remainder. A long twist requires more Fourier modes, not an unproved deletion of its endpoint source. The theorem below removes the vertical-type obstruction for every fixed literal twist length. The remaining geometric selection is among a finite mode family. It does not assert that the geometric mode dominates all others in an arbitrary knot. ## 1. Exact finite-mode Abel--Plana Let n be a positive integer and f holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed strip 0<=Re z<=n. Suppose, uniformly there, |f(x+it)| <= C exp(pi tau |t|), where tau<2(K+1) and K is a nonnegative integer. Polynomial factors in |t| are also allowed if the inequality has any fixed strict margin. Then sum_(j=0)^n f(j) =(f(0)+f(n))/2 +sum_(k=-K)^K integral_0^n f(x) exp(2pi i k x) dx +R_K(f), (1) R_K(f)=i integral_0^infinity exp(-2pi Kt) [f(it)-f(-it)-f(n+it)+f(n-it)] /(exp(2pi t)-1) dt. (2) The integral at zero is interpreted by its removable continuous value; the numerator vanishes there. At infinity it is absolutely convergent. Here is a direct residue proof, rather than an assumption that Poisson modes may be discarded. Use the upper and lower kernels U_K(z)=exp(2pi i Kz)/(exp(-2pi iz)-1), L_K(z)=exp(-2pi i Kz)/(exp(2pi iz)-1). Their residues at integers are the same as for K=0. Their vertical damping is 2pi(K+1). For w=exp(2pi iz), their boundary sum is exactly U_K(z)+L_K(z)=-sum_(k=-K)^K w^k. Integrating the two rectangular contours, with half-circles at the endpoints, gives (1). The horizontal edges vanish by the stated strict growth inequality. The two vertical edges are exactly (2), with the same signs as ordinary finite Abel--Plana. This proves the full finite source identity. Taking K=0 recovers the previous theorem. One may also take unequal upper/lower cutoffs K_+,K_-; the mode range is -K_-<=k<=K_+, and the two differences in (2) are weighted by exp(-2pi K_+t), exp(-2pi K_-t), respectively. Thus an asymmetric kernel or a specified integer lattice gauge need not be artificially symmetrized. ## 2. A quantitative endpoint remainder Suppose the four endpoint values satisfy |f(a+it)| <= A exp(pi tau |t|), a=0,n, |f'(a+it)| <= A B, |t|<=1. Put gamma=2(K+1)-tau>0. Splitting (2) at t=1 gives |R_K(f)| <= C A [B+1/gamma], (3) with an absolute constant C. Near zero the numerator is O(ABt), and the denominator is at least 2pi t. At infinity its absolute value is at most C A exp(-pi gamma t). For every T>=1 the omitted t>=T part is bounded by C A gamma^(-1) exp(-pi gamma T). (4) Thus when A has a known smaller exponential rate than the main geometric period, the entire finite-mode correction has that same smaller rate up to polynomial factors. This is the same kind of source comparison as the original 5_2 error bound by K_(4_1),N. No rate for A is inferred merely from the existence of the main saddle. For the reflected factorial kernels in Section 5 of the earlier quadrature theorem, tau is bounded in terms of the displayed Gaussian coefficient and linear exponent. A finite K therefore exists even when its former single-mode inequality fails. Their original endpoint derivative bound has B=O(1+log N). This is a verifiable local kernel criterion; no contour or geometric coupling is assumed. ## 3. Application to EVERY literal p-fold crossing sector The [exact original-matrix calculation](general_bridge_quadrature_and_twist_type_obstruction.md) gives, after the specified external Cartan line, the literal relative degree-zero values d_j^p, d_j=(-1)^j Q^(j(j+1)/2), 0<=j<N, for every integer twist length p. Set n=N-1 and use their exact entire interpolation B(z)=exp[pi i p z(z-n)/N]. For every 0<=x<=n, |B(x+it)| <= exp(pi c |t|), c=|p|n/N. The smallest symmetric cutoff satisfying the strict contour-decay criterion is K_min=floor(c/2). (5) It has at most |p|+1 modes and is bounded independently of N for fixed p. The resulting remainder is polynomially bounded in N. For a margin uniform over ALL levels use instead K=floor(|p|/2), gamma=2(K+1)-c>=1. (6) The exact endpoint numerator gives the particularly transparent formula sum_(j=0)^n d_j^p =1+sum_(k=-K)^K integral_0^n exp[pi i p x(x-n)/N+2pi i kx] dx +4i integral_0^infinity exp(-pi i p t^2/N) sinh(pi p n t/N) exp(-2pi Kt)/(exp(2pi t)-1) dt. (7) No endpoint or parity factor is omitted. For p=0 the original sum is N and (1) with K=0 gives it exactly. For p!=0 the correction in (7) satisfies the explicit bound |R_K| <= (4c/pi) sum_(r=K+1)^infinity 1/(4r^2-c^2). (8) This follows by expanding the positive denominator and integrating the absolute sinh bound; strict 2(K+1)>c justifies Tonelli. For K in (6), (8) is O_p(1), uniformly in N. For the minimal cutoff (5) it is O_p(N): gamma is a positive rational with denominator N, hence gamma>=1/N. Near t=0, B'=O_p(1), so (3) gives the same polynomial conclusion directly. With the uniform cutoff (6), taking T=eta N in (4) leaves an O_p(exp(-pi eta N)) far tail. The low Fourier modes in (7) are kept exactly; they have not been put in that error. Their number depends on p and not on the quantum level. Each is an ordinary finite Gaussian integral, so for p!=0 equation (7) also directly bounds the whole clock sum by O_p(sqrt N) using the elementary Fresnel bound, plus its O_p(1) correction. The analogous formula with a different original linear lattice gauge simply shifts the retained finite mode window. There is no freedom to call one of its modes the original selected state without carrying the other modes and (2). ### 3.1 The entire marked Gaussian kernel, not only its constant argument The source-preserving extension needed for an actual word keeps a spectral argument and the meridian. The original finite Gaussian polynomial is exactly Gamma_(p,N)(t,M)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) d_j(M)^p t^j, d_j(M)=(-1)^j Q^(j(j+1)/2) M^(-2j). Choose a specified logarithm L of Z=t M^(-2p) and put f(z)=B(z) exp(Lz). This has the literal marked Gaussian coefficients at every integer. On compact annuli for t,M and any fixed bounded logarithmic branch, |f(a+is)| <= A exp(pi tau |s|), a=0,n, A=max(1,|Z|^n), tau=|p|n/N+|Im L|/pi. (9) The same bound holds uniformly over 0<=Re z<=n. The endpoint derivative bound is A times a constant depending on p and the specified compact logarithmic chart, independently of N. Hence (1)--(4), with a finite cutoff depending only on that chart and p, give an EXACT finite-mode presentation of the entire original Gamma_(p,N)(t,M), including its endpoint terms and remainder. For |Arg Z|<=pi the simple choice K=floor((|p|+1)/2) has a uniform positive type margin. A change L->L+2pi i ell is exactly a shift of the Fourier mode labels; the scalar polynomial is unchanged. This has an immediate whole-network consequence. In [the original Cauchy network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md), each Gaussian factor is literally Gamma_(+1,N)(z/w,M) or its negative-sign counterpart. Replace each by its exact expression (1). On the specified compact Cauchy circles its logarithmic arguments range over finitely many bounded branch charts, with transition by the just stated exact relabeling. More explicitly, partition each circle's parameterization into finitely many arcs carrying continuous logarithmic lifts; alternatively carry its unwrapped mark throughout. No global single-valued Log is assumed on a full circle, and individual mode integrals are not identified across marks. Their combined formula is the same original polynomial. Formula (9) gives absolute uniform integrability of the endpoint remainder. Fubini therefore carries this replacement through the complete original cap, pivot and external normalization. No source coupon is changed. This yields a finite Fourier-packet presentation for the Gaussian part of EVERY fixed original braid word. The packet size is independent of N. All its factorial/Euler and projection factors remain the same exact functions; no exponential bound for their contracted endpoint periods is asserted. ## 4. The resulting generalization target This resolves the specific long-twist vertical-type failure: every fixed p has a finite, explicitly sourced mode packet, including arbitrarily large positive or negative twists. The same theorem applies to each reflected finite-factorial bridge kernel with a known finite vertical type. It does not require p=1 or a twist-knot diagram. For many bridges, this produces finitely many mode combinations for each fixed word, together with endpoint faces and corners. Iterating it requires its uniform strip estimates at the actual intermediate parameters; after an earlier integration those may be complex, so the original finite-product reflection must be checked again. The original word is not automatically a product of independent one-variable kernels. The general finite-height residue construction remains available when an infinite-height strip is not justified. A broad knot theorem still needs a structural way to prove that the actual endpoint periods and the other retained modes have smaller rate, and that the geometric mode has nonzero original coefficient. The present result replaces an invalid one-mode shortcut by a concrete finite-dimensional selection problem. It does not solve that remaining selection by asserting an assumed geometric contour. [Exact finite-packet diagnostics](../experiments/audit_twist_vertical_type_obstruction.py).

title: A finite real-algebraic certificate for the geometric volume branch
text: # A finite real-algebraic certificate for the geometric volume branch 29 October 2026. The positive complete gluing certificate can be stated without numerical logarithms, without a separate Jacobian hypothesis, and without a restriction to alternating, pretzel, or bounded-bridge diagrams. The existence of a positive chart is an actual hypothesis; this note does not prove that every chosen triangulation has one. This is a finite test for the GEOMETRIC side of the requested equality. It does not infer the growth of an original quantum period merely from its classical support. The source value/normal and absolute regulator requirements in [the source audit](algebraic_source_geometry_criteria_audit.md) still apply. In particular, the theorem below must not be counted as an enlargement of the proved quantum-equality family. ## 1. Certificate and conclusion Supply a finite oriented ideal triangulation T of the intended manifold X, together with its actual marking. Check orientation-reversing face pairings, circular edge links, and connected torus ideal-vertex links. The identification with the intended knot/link exterior is an actual oriented homeomorphism (or a verified sequence of elementary cellulation moves proving it), carrying the relative fundamental class with degree one and the displayed peripheral curves to the intended primitive meridians and longitudes. A degree-one map alone is not this topological identification. A different manifold or an unmarked cover is not certified as X by its shape equations alone. Write t for the number of tetrahedra and h for the number of cusp tori. For every positively ordered tetrahedron specify z_j, z'_j=1/(1-z_j), z''_j=(z_j-1)/z_j. The data to check are: 1. Im(z_j)>0 for every j. All three displayed shapes then have positive imaginary part and their arguments lie strictly between zero and pi. 2. The product of the incident shapes around every actual edge is 1, with the actual incidences and multiplicities. 3. The integer winding of that edge product is ONE, computed by the finite sign rule in section 2. Product 1 alone is insufficient. 4. The actual complex similarity multipliers of BOTH marked peripheral generators on every cusp are 1. These are Laurent monomials in the shape triples, with their actual signs and orientation conventions. All denominators are kept nonzero by saturation with product z_j(1-z_j). If shapes are supplied as algebraic numbers, every test above is exact real-algebraic arithmetic. More generally the existence of such shapes is a finite semialgebraic condition over Q: write z_j=x_j+i y_j, clear denominators only on their specified nonzero locus, and retain the sign conditions. The winding condition is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests. No comparison of a numerically evaluated angle with 2pi is part of this certificate. **Geometric certificate theorem.** These data construct a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL manifold X. Its volume is Vol(X)=sum_j D(z_j), (1) where D is the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm and the orientation is the one already specified by the positive tetrahedra. This positive angle point is the unique global maximizer of ideal tetrahedral volume on the closed edge-angle polytope for T. Its complete shapes are algebraic over Q. The marked meridian multipliers give algebraic etale local coordinates on the gluing variety at this point. The last two assertions are CONSEQUENCES of positivity and the actual edge/peripheral incidence, rather than independent regularity assumptions. The local statement does not assert that the global gluing variety has one component or that its plane peripheral image is nonsingular. ## 2. Exact edge winding from algebraic signs Let w_1,...,w_m be the incident shapes in cyclic order around one edge, and set p_0=1, p_k=w_1...w_k. Under Im(w_k)>0 and p_m=1, define n=sum_(k=1)^m 1_{Im(p_(k-1))<0 and Im(p_k)>=0}. (2) Then sum_k Arg(w_k)=2pi n, Arg(w_k) in (0,pi). (3) Proof. Follow the continuously increasing argument of the partial product, adding Arg(w_k) at the kth step. Each step is strictly less than pi. A passage from the open lower half-plane to the closed upper half-plane therefore passes through, or ends on, the POSITIVE real ray. It cannot go from that lower half-plane to the negative real ray in one positive step shorter than pi. Conversely each crossing of a positive multiple of 2pi has exactly the sign change in (2). Starting on a real ray does not produce a spurious count: the positive ray enters the upper half-plane, and the negative ray enters the lower half-plane. Landing on the positive ray is counted once, while landing on the negative ray is not. Thus real intermediate products cause no ambiguity. The endpoint p_m=1 proves (3). For example eight factors i have product 1 but n=2: the angle is 4pi. Four factors i have n=1. Also let w=(3+4i)/5 and v=(-3+4i)/5. The list (w,v,w,v) has exact rational complex coefficients, product 1 and n=1, although its individual angles need not be rational multiples of pi. Each p_k is rational in the algebraic shapes. Thus (2) is a finite exact sign certificate for nonsingularity around an edge. No choice of a logarithm branch is silently suppressed in passing to polynomials. ## 3. Why the metric is the metric of X Realize each tetrahedron with its prescribed positive ideal shape. The actual face identifications have unique ideal face isometries. Away from edges they define an oriented hyperbolic metric. Around an edge the shape product fixes the real dilation and the rotational holonomy, while (2) fixes the total angle to exactly 2pi. The developed link makes precisely one turn. Hence the local metric extends across that edge without a cone singularity or a branched cover. Cut the corners by small horospheres. Their triangles form a Euclidean similarity structure on each topological cusp torus. Edge angle 2pi removes its vertex cone singularities. The similarity multiplier is trivial on a contractible loop and, by condition 4, on both generators of the torus fundamental group. Propagate the scale of one triangle across adjacent triangles: the trivial multiplier makes this propagation independent of path. This produces a genuine flat metric on the entire compact cusp torus. A compact flat torus is complete. Its simply connected complete flat cover develops isometrically onto the Euclidean plane, and its deck group is a rank-two lattice of translations. In particular the two translation periods cannot secretly vanish or be real-collinear; this follows from the completed compact metric, not from an additional numerical peripheral check. Simultaneously shrinking the finitely many corner sections gives the usual embedded complete cusp ends. Their volume is finite, and the complement of those ends is compact. The resulting metric is therefore complete on X. The sum in (1) is its actual tetrahedral volume; internal faces and edges have measure zero. Completeness of the development identifies its universal cover with hyperbolic space, so this is not merely a representation-volume bound or a possibly branched local structure on X. If X is already equipped with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric, the sharp representation-volume bound applied in both identity- marked directions identifies its volume with (1); this is the bidirectional comparison in [the general equality theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). ## 4. Positivity forces the marked Jacobian to be invertible Use local logarithms x_j=Log(z_j), y_j=Log(z''_j). Their derivative is dy_j=tau_j dx_j, tau_j=1/(z_j-1), Im(tau_j)<0. (4) Select t-h independent edge exponent rows and one primitive meridian row per cusp. In these coordinates they give a real integer matrix R=(A B), rank R=t, A B^T=B A^T. (5) These facts are properties of the ACTUAL ideal-manifold incidence. For clarity, the needed finite incidence proof is the one in section 4 of [the positive ideal certificate](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md): an edge-row relation has local coefficients lambda_ab=c_a+c_b in each tetrahedron; face matching propagates c_a to one constant per connected ideal vertex link. There are h relations among t edge rows. The local skew corner contributions cancel across paired faces, so edge rows are isotropic. Peripheral normal-curve intersections give one nonzero meridian/longitude pairing per torus and zero between different tori. Thus the peripheral quotient has dimension 2h, and adding the h meridians gives exactly the real Lagrangian system (5). One may instead verify the displayed integer rank and symplectic identities directly in a supplied certificate. This does not require guessing the rank from a reduced source or from the number of equations. The linearized edge-plus-meridian system is (A+B diag(tau))v=0. (6) Here is a direct proof that its kernel is zero. By (5), ker R is a real Lagrangian subspace for Omega=sum dx_j wedge dy_j. If (6) holds, w=(v,diag(tau)v) belongs to its complexification, as does bar(w). Consequently 0=Omega(bar(w),w)=2i sum_j Im(tau_j)|v_j|^2. Every coefficient in the final sum is strictly negative, so v=0. This proves the nonzero complex Jacobian without a numerical determinant. The remaining edge equations are locally implied by the selected ones: their exponent rows lie in the same rational span, and their logarithmic constants agree at the specified point. Thus the full gluing germ is smooth of dimension h, and the meridian map is locally etale. At the complete rational values of the meridian multipliers, the shapes give an isolated solution of a polynomial system over Q. An isolated complex point of such a system has algebraic coordinates. Equivalently its zero-dimensional component has finite residue field over Q. This also explains the precise sense in which the local optimum is algebraic over the peripheral parameters. After restricting to the selected smooth branch and its denominators, its shapes are algebraic functions of the meridian multipliers. Their marked longitudes are algebraic functions on the same branch. This statement concerns the shape germ; it does not make the regulator value an algebraic number. ## 5. The full Casson--Rivin maximum, not a restricted source maximum Let theta be the positive angle point and let r=(Re x,Re y). The real edge equations place r in the edge coisotropic subspace. For EVERY edge-angle tangent delta, the sine rule in a tetrahedron gives dV(delta)=Omega(r,delta) =(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i delta Im U_i-Re U_i delta Im V_i]. (7) The quotient identity in (7) is exactly the actual peripheral pairing from (5). At the complete point both real peripheral logs vanish, so the derivative vanishes on the full edge-angle tangent space. No surjectivity of a quantum-source parametrization is being assumed. For one tetrahedron, use independent angles alpha,gamma with beta=pi-alpha-gamma. The negative volume Hessian is [[cot alpha+cot beta, cot beta], [cot beta, cot gamma+cot beta]]. Its determinant is 1, and its first diagonal entry is sin(gamma)/(sin(alpha)sin(beta))>0. It is positive definite. The sum over tetrahedra is therefore strictly concave on every affine angle slice. On a segment from the complete point to any other point of the closed angle polytope, the derivative starts at zero and strictly decreases for every positive segment parameter less than one. Continuity at the final zero/pi angles gives a strictly smaller value at the other endpoint as well. This proves the unique GLOBAL maximum. It also proves uniqueness of the COMPLETE POSITIVE SHAPE ASSIGNMENT on this fixed marked triangulation. Any two certified assignments would both be stationary maxima on the same edge-angle polytope, and hence have identical angles. The positive ideal angles determine the complex shape by the sine rule, so their shapes coincide. Thus the finite semialgebraic existence test, when successful, selects one positive complete point and its geometric meridian germ. It makes no uniqueness assertion for other complex or nonpositive components of the gluing ideal or for the original quantum solution space. The corresponding filled-slope assertion needs the actual primitive logarithmic filling periods, in addition to its exponential equations. It is treated in [the general geometric completion](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). The complete-cusp test above does not silently replace that tube-end condition by an equation modulo 2pi i. ## 6. A simple sufficient test on the plane A-curve There is also a useful algebraic branch test at a signed complete point (M_0,L_0). Put u=M/M_0-1, v=L/L_0-1. For a reduced relevant peripheral factor write its local equation as A(u,v)=H_m(u,v)+terms of total degree greater than m, where H_m is its first nonzero homogeneous part. If H_m(1,tau)=0, partial_t H_m(1,tau) != 0, (8) substitute v=u t and divide by u^m. The strict-transform equation is H_m(1,t)+u R(u,t)=0. The implicit function theorem gives a unique algebraic analytic branch t=t(u) through tau, and hence v=u t(u). This branch is unramified over u, even if the original plane curve is singular and partial_L A vanishes at the complete point. A positive imaginary part of tau, in the correctly oriented primitive peripheral basis, selects a candidate geometric tangent. The actual positive marked gluing lift above is what certifies it as geometric. Condition (8) is sufficient, not necessary: coincident tangent lines may require further blowups, and a plane image may lose distinctions between smooth decorated branches. Neither (8) nor a nonsingular gluing scheme reconstructs the absolute Bloch class or the original normal quantum evaluation. In particular f_N(Y)=(1-Y)F_N(Y) has the same localized classical support as F_N, but f_N(1)=0 whereas -f'_N(1)=F_N(1) is the original invariant. The integral pointed source and its specified jet must accompany the curve. ## 7. Coverage and what remains on the critical path The classical implications are established territory: the coverage check found Choi's 2004 *Positively oriented ideal triangulations on hyperbolic three-manifolds* (Topology 43, 1345--1371, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.top.2004.02.002), whose statement includes smooth positive gluing varieties and local peripheral coordinates, and [Futer--Gueritaud's Casson--Rivin exposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440). They are recorded for coverage; the proofs used above are displayed directly or refer to the independently checked incidence calculation. The exact sign test exposes the integer winding that a saturated exponentiated gluing ideal alone forgets. No novelty claim for the underlying rigidity or variational theorem is intended. This certificate applies at arbitrary bridge number whenever its actual positive ideal chart is supplied. Alternatingness is not a premise. Fully augmented links with more general graphs and their independently long fillings remain a broad target, but their actual original-source packet and complementary-source estimates are additional work. There is now an exact pointed crossing alphabet and actual parabolic character gluing for [every four-plat word](actual_newton_twist_canonical_graph.md). There is also a sharp complete-source norm estimate for [the two-twist packet](actual_newton_two_twist_interaction_packet.md), using an exact reset, a reflected boundary current and an independently evaluated nonzero opposite endpoint. Those are genuine source data beyond simple-spectrum or smooth-curve assumptions. Extending that estimate to arbitrary reduced words, and controlling the corresponding original marked closure, remains the quantum critical path. The [exact winding audit](../experiments/audit_finite_real_algebraic_geometric_certificate.py) checks all eight edges of the actual reflected two-octahedron base in 284 exact shape orders, positive/negative real intermediate products, and rejection of product-one lists of winding two or three. These finite checks supplement the general proof; they do not prove the existence of positive charts or quantum asymptotics in general.

title: A nonzero all-level annihilator from the actual finite cut state
text: # A nonzero all-level annihilator from the actual finite cut state Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an independent existence proof of a nonzero all-level meridian annihilator for the reduced literature ADO state of every knot. The proof keeps the finite-sum boundaries, handles an elimination operator vanishing under summation, and removes a central factor before root specialization. It does not identify the operator's classical symbol with the geometric A-curve or prove a volume estimate. Existence of level-independent ADO recursions is existing coverage: [Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, 2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176). Proper q-hypergeometric sums and q-holonomicity are standard, with scope surveyed in [Garoufalidis--Le, 1601.07487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.07487). Their closure, Hamiltonian-reduction, and holonomicity proofs are not premises here. The proof below is a filtered dimension count with explicit boundary strata and finite exponential moments. ## 1. An auxiliary off-root lift, with the root state unchanged Choose a braid presentation of a zero-framed knot. At a fixed positive integer N, keep q generic and use the N by N matrices E v_a=[a]_q*(x*q^(1-a)-x^(-1)*q^(a-1))/(q-q^(-1)) v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1), K v_a=x*q^(-2a)v_a, 0<=a<N, with the endpoint vectors zero. These need not be a quantum-group representation away from the root. Only their finite matrix entries will be used off-root. On a crossing put D_(a,b)=x^(-a-b)q^(2ab), and Theta=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) c_k (E tensor F)^k, c_k=q^(k(k-1)/2)*(q-q^(-1))^k/[k]_q!, R_tilde=D*Theta. (1.1) This is the actual unrolled R with its common q^(alpha^2/2) factor removed, x=q^alpha. The inverse is R_tilde^(-1)=Theta_inv*D^(-1), Theta_inv=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k*q^(-k(k-1)/2)*(q-q^(-1))^k/[k]_q! *(E tensor F)^k. (1.2) For a proof, set Q=q^2 and rewrite the two coefficient series as the q-exponential and its inverse. Their coefficient convolution is the finite q-binomial identity product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+Q^j*t) =sum_(r=0)^m Q^(r(r-1)/2) {m choose r}_Q t^r. Inserting the last factor and collecting coefficients proves this identity inductively. At t=-1 its right side is zero for m>0, which is exactly the inverse-series convolution after the factorial rewrite. Finally (E tensor F)^N=0 truncates it. Thus (1.2) holds for generic q, without a root-of-unity relation. Use the checked crossings obtained by permutation, pivotal K^(1-N), and the residual framing factor x^(w(N-1)), with w the braid writhe. Take the (0,0) entry of the cut partial trace and call it L_N(q,x). No scalarity or topological invariance is asserted for this off-root lift. At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), it is exactly the actual reduced period L_N(q_N,x)=F_N(x). (1.3) The cancellation of the removed factors against the twist, and the root normalization, are those already independently checked in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). All denominators [k]_q!, k<N, and q-q^(-1), are nonzero at q_N. Consequently L_N is regular there as a rational function of generic x. ## 2. The precise finite-sum class The lift is a finite sum over crossing powers and strand labels. All matching constraints are integral linear equations. Their integer solution lattice has a fixed integral basis; use its coordinates k=(k_1,...,k_s). All actual labels and crossing powers are fixed integral linear functions of k. Their bounds 0,...,N-1 define a finite support P_N by finitely many inequalities ell_nu(N,k)>=0. (2.1) Every nonzero summand on this support is a product of: * a monomial q^Q(N,k) x^L(N,k), with Q integer-valued quadratic and L integral linear; * finitely many q-factorials (q^v;q^v)_ell(N,k) and their inverses, with nonnegative integral linear lengths; * finitely many (x^u*q^ell(N,k);q^v)_m(N,k) and their inverses, with u!=0 and nonnegative integral linear lengths; * finitely many fixed nonzero Q(q)-scalars raised to integral linear exponents, including signs. Here v!=0 is fixed. Include all factorial and Pochhammer length conditions among (2.1). A term is defined as zero outside P_N. Its value is nonzero as a rational function of generic (q,x) on P_N. This is the only regularity of a summand used below. The x-dependent Pochhammer parameters also satisfy the proper alignment condition: v divides each coefficient of k_i in ell. This ensures that an internal unit shift moves an argument by an integral number of its q^v steps. For the actual R-weights both v and those coefficients are even, with v=+/-2. The proof does not assert this shift bound for unaligned Pochhammer products. To check this class for (1.1), use E^k v_a=([a]_q!/[a-k]_q!) *product_(r=0)^(k-1)[alpha-a+r+1]_q v_(a-k). The second product is an x-dependent Pochhammer of length k. Explicitly, writing rho=q-q^(-1), it is (-x^(-1))^k q^(k(a-1)-k(k-1)/2) rho^(-k) *(x^2*q^(2-2a);q^2)_k. Also [r]_q!=q^(-r(r-1)/2)*(q^2;q^2)_r/(1-q^2)^r. These formulas verify both the alignment and the allowed linear exponents of scalar factors, with no appeal to a closure theorem. The other coefficients in (1.1)--(1.2) are q-factorials and quadratic q-monomials. Pivotal and framing entries contribute x-powers linear in (N,k) and q-powers quadratic in (N,k). Thus their shift ratios belong to the class just described. Choose a fixed positive integer B so that shifting x by q^B shifts every x-dependent Pochhammer argument by an integral number of its q^v steps. B=1 works for these R-weights: u=+/-2, v=+/-2. Write T for this x-shift and S_i for k_i -> k_i+1. Set z=q^N and t_i=q^k_i. The variable z will be retained until the last specialization. ## 3. A global shift-span bound, including the boundaries Let I_N(q,x;k) be one summand, extended by zero. For R>=1 consider the actions x^a z^c T^b S_1^beta_1...S_s^beta_s I, 0<=a,c,b,beta_i<=R. (3.1) These are functions of (N,k,x), over the coefficient field Q(q). Their joint span has dimension O(R^(s+2)). The constant depends on the fixed summand data and support, not N or R. ### Interior rational-shift estimate Where a collection of shifted terms is supported, choose one supported shift beta_0 as reference. Ratios of the shifted products to I(k+beta_0) are rational in x,z,t_1,...,t_s. They have a common Laurent-polynomial denominator of degree O(R), and after clearing it all exponents are bounded in absolute value by C R. Indeed a shift changes every factorial length and Pochhammer endpoint by O(R). All possible endpoint factors belong to finitely many types 1-q^r x^u z^v t^a, with r in intervals of length O(R). Include their required denominator factors once, with the bounded multiplicities of the original products. Quadratic q-monomials change by linear functions of (N,k), hence by Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in z,t; x-shifts of x^L contribute the same kind of monomial. Powers q^O(R^2), and the shifted scalar factors, are scalars in Q(q). Without boundaries this proves the O(R^(s+2)) estimate immediately. Ignoring the zero extension at a boundary would be incorrect. ### Boundary stratification and its codimension Choose C so |ell_nu(0,beta)-ell_nu(0,0)|<=C R for all shifts in (3.1). Partition the integer pairs (N,k) by declaring each support form either greater than C R, less than -C R, or equal to one particular integer in [-C R,C R]. A stratum with a form less than -C R contributes zero to every shifted term. On any remaining stratum the supported shifts are a fixed subset: large forms remain positive, while near-boundary forms have fixed integer values. An empty subset contributes zero. Otherwise choose beta_0 from that subset. All q-factorial ratios between it and another supported shift have nonnegative endpoint indices. Their intervening factorial factors have strictly positive indices. A common denominator can therefore be chosen nonzero on the stratum. The x-dependent factors are nonzero for generic x. Thus the interior estimate still applies there. Suppose the fixed near-boundary forms have rank r as affine constraints on (N,k). Their consistent integer labels have only O(R^r) possibilities: choose r independent forms, after which all dependent labels are determined. There are finitely many choices of forms and large/small patterns. On each such stratum, the multiplicative variables z,t satisfy r independent binomial constraints z^b product_i t_i^a_i=q^d. (3.2) The Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in x,z,t modulo these constraints span a space of dimension O(R^(s+2-r)). To see this integrally, use Smith normal form of the fixed constraint lattice. The r constrained exponents can be reduced modulo fixed integers; the other s+2-r exponents range through O(R) integers. This also keeps the finitely many components if the lattice is not saturated. The varying right sides q^d are coefficient-field scalars. Restrict the family (3.1) to all these strata. A function is determined by its restrictions, and multiplication by the nonzero reference summand or common denominator does not increase dimension. Consequently its dimension is at most sum_(r=0)^(s+1) O(R^r)*O(R^(s+2-r)) =O(R^(s+2)). (3.3) This proves the global bound. It also treats small N, intersecting boundary faces, and redundant support inequalities. In particular it does not assume that the index polytope is a box. The same estimate holds for a finite sum on the same lattice by applying it to the direct sum of their spaces. One can retain separate term components in the elimination below, so cancellation between terms is not an assumption. ## 4. Elimination without internal multiplication variables The PBW monomials of the operators in (3.1) are linearly independent in the formal Ore algebra. There are (R+1)^(s+3) of them. For large R this exceeds the bound (3.3). Finite linear algebra yields a nonzero formal operator P(x,z,T,S_1,...,S_s) I=0 (4.1) with coefficients in Q(q), and no multiplication t_i in P. Identity (4.1) is global on the zero-extended integer array, not merely an equality of ratios at interior indices. The construction is effective in principle. List the boundary strata, clear the proper denominators, reduce their monomials by the binomial constraints, and solve the resulting finite linear system over Q(q). No efficiency or minimal-order claim is made. ## 5. Finite moments repair vanishing under summation For each N introduce independent formal units w_i and the finite Laurent polynomial F_N(q,x,w)=sum_(k in Z^s) w^k I_N(q,x;k). Since the support is finite, translation of the sum is exact: sum_k w^k S_i I(k)=w_i^(-1) F_N(q,x,w). Thus (4.1) becomes P(x,q^N,T,w_1^(-1),...,w_s^(-1)) F_N(q,x,w)=0. (5.1) Expand the nonzero polynomial P in its commuting internal shifts around S_i=1: P=sum_alpha A_alpha(x,z,T)(S-1)^alpha. Choose a nonzero A_alpha at least total degree h. Set w_i=exp(v_i) in (5.1). Its coefficient of v^alpha at that least degree is (-1)^h A_alpha(x,q^N,T) F_N(q,x,1)=0. (5.2) Every term in which a positive-degree moment of F_N occurs has a lower-degree coefficient of P, and therefore vanishes. Hence A_alpha is a genuine nonzero meridian operator for the summed state, even if P(x,z,T,1,...,1)=0. This is a formal finite-moment argument, with no convergence, contour shift, or boundary omission. ## 6. Specializing q^N=-1 without losing the operator Apply (5.2) to the actual off-root lift L_N. Clear denominators and write its nonzero operator as A(x,z,T)=(z+1)^h A_0(x,z,T), where at least one coefficient of A_0 has nonzero value at z=-1. The factor is central. For every fixed positive N, q^N+1 is a nonzero rational function of generic q, so the identity for L_N also implies A_0(x,q^N,T)L_N(q,x)=0 before specialization. At q=q_N the lift is regular, as proved in Section 1. Therefore P_K(q,x,T)=A_0(x,-1,T), P_K(q_N,x,T)F_N(x)=0 (6.1) for all but finitely many N. The excluded levels are poles of the fixed rational q-coefficients. P_K is nonzero by construction. This cancels a common operator factor before specialization of an auxiliary lift. It changes neither the state nor any peripheral factor in a state comparison. In particular the actual full ADO factor d_N is still the whole rational germ of the pointing note. At the trivial quotient color the actual reduced state has value one. Thus an order-zero multiplication operator cannot annihilate it at all large levels. After removing a common shift, (6.1) has positive order and nonzero leading and trailing coefficients in Q(q,x). Its existence proves that the actual localized all-level annihilator ideal is nonzero for every knot. The exact change x=-q^(-1)M and the fixed full/reduced shift gauge transport this operator to the meridian M and to the full literature ADO normalization. In the localized skew polynomial ring over Q(q,M), left Euclidean division gives the unique monic element of least order in the actual nonzero ideal. This is the literature minimal-operator convention; the construction above need not compute that minimal element efficiently. ## 7. What this settles and what the triangulation must still supply The [all-level exact period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) can now be applied to a nonzero actual annihilator for every knot, with its finite fixed-color pointing and bounded q-jets. Existence of such an operator is no longer an unaudited premise in that application. No proof of an equality with a Jones recursion ideal is needed for this implication. This proof does not show that the minimal operator has the geometric A-component in its classical symbol, that it has a rational inhomogeneous source factor, or that its period has the geometric regulator norm. A positive ideal triangulation supplies the geometric Bloch class and gluing branch. The exact comparison between its quantum gluing period and the actual cut-state module remains necessary, as detailed in [the triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md). The subsequent [relative octahedral presentation](relative_octahedral_period.md) now rewrites these very cut-state coefficients into five tetrahedral atoms, proves their local ideal-octahedron geometry, and derives the finite factorial's source and exact cyclic boundary transition. This gives explicit local input for the remaining comparison; it does not identify this eliminated meridian operator's global geometric block or its selected regulator period. The [diagnostics](../experiments/audit_finite_sum_annihilator.py) check the generic off-root crossing lift and its inverse against the actual root matrices, explicit global boundary certificates, and the finite-moment and central-specialization repairs. Their [results](../experiments/finite_sum_annihilator_results.json) are checks of these ingredients, not a volume theorem or an efficient all-knot computation of minimal operators.

title: The finite trivalent Euler coefficient to short balanced series
text: # The finite trivalent Euler coefficient to short balanced series 29 October 2026. This completes the missing finite coefficient identity from the independent [root-Fourier source proof](actual_trivalent_root_fourier_source_certificate.md). The proof uses only the coproduct Euler coefficient, finite Newton interpolation, finite Vandermonde, and the [own finite Sears lemma](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md). It does not import a 6j evaluation. Set N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N), F_k=(Q;Q)_k. Let a,b,c be nonnegative integers <=floor(d/2), satisfying the triangle inequalities, and put r=b+c-a, delta=a+b+c-d>=0, r_1=a+b-c, r_2=a+c-b. Thus delta<=min(a,b,c,r,r_1,r_2). Every finite factorial used below has a physical index in 0,...,d. Write D_Q h(T)=[h(T)-h(QT)]/T and P=[T^d](TQ;Q)_b^2 D_Q^r (TQ^(1-c);Q)_c^2, C_delta=Q^[-b(b+1)+c(c-1)] P. (1) The EXACT identity needed by the actual source normalization is C_delta=Q^[b(a+c-b)+c(2c+1)] *F_(2b)/F_(a+b-c)*F_a^2/[F_delta F_(a-delta)^2] *4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-r,Q^-b,Q^-b; Q^(-b-c),Q^(-b-c),Q^(-2b);Q,Q). (2) The series terminates at min(delta,r). All denominator Pochhammers are nonzero up to that length. No generic-q normal limit is taken. ## 1. Jackson Leibniz and a finite moment identity The finite Leibniz formula follows by induction from D_Q(uv)=(D_Qu)v+u(QT)D_Qv. Apply it to f(T)^2, f=(TQ^(1-c);Q)_c: D_Q^r f^2=(-Q^(1-c))^r F_c^2 *sum_s [r choose s]_Q Q^[s(s-1)/2+(r-s)(r-s-1)/2] (TQ^(1-c+r);Q)_(c-s) (TQ^(1-c+r-s);Q)_(c-r+s) /[F_(c-s)F_(c-r+s)]. (3) Only max(0,r-c)<=s<=min(r,c) occurs. When multiplied by (TQ)_b^2, the Euler product in a term of (3) is EXACTLY (TQ;Q)_b (TQ^(b-a+1);Q)_a (TQ^(b-a-s+1);Q)_c. (4) To verify (4), compare exponent intervals using their endpoints; the two sides have the same multiplicity at every integer exponent. This argument works for EVERY triangle (a,b,c), not only a maximal first label. Reversing degree J=a+b+c to degree delta in (4) gives the three factors A(U)=(UQ^-b;Q)_b(UQ^-b;Q)_a, (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c. The signs cancel since r+J=2(b+c). The full phase in this reversal is P=Q^Z0 F_c^2F_r [U^delta]A(U) *sum_s w_s (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c, w_s=Q^[s^2-s(r+c)]/[F_sF_(r-s)F_(c-s)F_(c-r+s)], Z0=r(1-c)+r(r-1)/2+b(b+1)/2+ab-a(a-1)/2 +c(b-a)+c(c+1)/2. (5) The crucial moment is computed explicitly. The finite Newton identity x^ell=sum_(k=0)^ell (Q^-ell;Q)_k Q^k(x;Q)_k/F_k (6) follows by induction using x(x;Q)_k=Q^-k[(x;Q)_k-(x;Q)_(k+1)]. Put x=Q^(s-c), multiply by Q^(c ell), and sum against w_s. The factor (Q^(s-c);Q)_k cancels F_(c-s), leaving Vandermonde of lengths c-k and c. The exact result is sum_s w_s (Q^(s-c);Q)_k =(-1)^k Q^[-ck+k(k-1)/2-(c-k)r] F_(2c-k)/[F_rF_(2c-k-r)F_(c-k)F_c]. (7) This is an own finite Vandermonde calculation: after cancellation, its summand exponent is (c-k-s)(r-s), up to the displayed constant, and the product-coefficient identity gives [2c-k choose r]_Q. Out-of-range terms are zero. In the use below k<=delta<=2c-r, so every displayed denominator is regular. Expand (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c by the finite binomial theorem, insert (6), and put ell=k+v. The remaining v sum is another FINITE Euler product. Equations (6),(7) give sum_s w_s (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c =Q^(-cr) sum_k (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2]U^k *F_(2c-k)(UQ^(c-r);Q)_(c-k) /[F_rF_(2c-k-r)F_kF_(c-k)^2]. (8) All sums here are finite, so their interchange has no convergence hypothesis. In (5), the last Euler factor in (8) joins the length-a factor contiguously, because c-r=a-b. ## 2. The root coefficient collapse Let L=delta-k, so 0<=L<=b. The only remaining coefficient after (8) is [U^L](UQ^-b;Q)_b(UQ^-b;Q)_(d+L-b) =Q^[L(L-1-2b)] F_b^2/[F_LF_(b-L)^2]. (9) Here is a finite proof. Put M=d+L-b. The finite binomial expansion of the left side, extracting its zeroth summand, is (-Q^-b)^L Q^[L(L-1)/2][M choose L]_Q *2phi1(Q^-L,Q^-b;Q^(M-L+1);Q,Q^(b+1)). At this ROOT, Q^(M-L+1)=Q^(N-b)=Q^-b. The equal numerator and denominator cancel, with no zero reached because L<=b<N. The remaining finite binomial sum is (Q^(b+1-L);Q)_L. Converting its two factors to F gives exactly (9). This is the source-specific root collapse; no continuous-color replacement is used. Combining (5),(8),(9), and writing Z=Z0-cr+delta(delta-1-2b)-b(b+1)+c(c-1), one obtains C_delta=Q^Z F_b^2 F_(2c) /[F_(r_2)F_delta F_(b-delta)^2] *H_c, H_c=4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-r_2,Q^-c,Q^-c; Q^(-a-c),Q^(-a-c),Q^(-2c);Q,Q). (10) For example the raw kth term before normalization is (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2+(delta-k)(delta-k-1-2b)] F_(2c-k) /[F_(2c-k-r)F_kF_(c-k)^2F_(delta-k)F_(b-delta+k)^2]. Its successive ratio gives (10); the residual argument is Q because 2+2b+2c-r-delta=N+1. This makes the root mark explicit. ## 3. Two proved Sears transformations meet at one symmetric series Use the own finite Sears identity, with length delta, on H_c. Keep Q^-c and choose d=e=Q^(-a-c). It gives H_c=K_1 H_sym, K_1=(Q^-a,Q^(-a-b);Q)_delta /(Q^(-a-c),Q^-r_1;Q)_delta, H_sym=4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-a,Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(-a-b),Q^(-a-c),Q^(-b-c);Q,Q). The root equalities Q^(a+1-delta)=Q^(-b-c) etc fix all three denominators. Applying the SAME finite Sears lemma to the H_b on the right side of (2) gives H_b=K_2 H_sym, K_2=(Q^-c,Q^(-a-c);Q)_delta /(Q^(-b-c),Q^-r_2;Q)_delta. (11) Every factorial index is physical, since delta<=a,b,c,r_i. Thus neither transformation crosses a root pole. No division by H_sym is needed; the comparison is between their explicit prefactors. For clarity the complete phase cancellation is recorded. Let tau_u=(-1)^u Q^[u(u+1)/2], so F_uF_(d-u)=N tau_u. Converting (11) to factorials and reflecting complements gives [F_b^2F_(2c)/(F_(r_2)F_delta F_(b-delta)^2)](K_1/K_2) /[F_(2b)F_a^2/(F_(r_1)F_delta F_(a-delta)^2)] =tau_b^2 tau_(2c) tau_(a+b) tau_(b+c) /(tau_(2b)tau_c tau_a tau_(a+c)^2) =Q^K, K=-a^2+ab-2ac-a+bc+b+c^2. The residual sign is (-1)^[2(b-a)]=1. Finally direct expansion gives Z+K-[b(a+c-b)+c(2c+1)] =-(a-b+c+delta)(a+b+c-delta+1) =-N(-N+2a+2c+1). Its Q power is ONE. Substituting into (10),(11) proves EXACTLY (2) for every admissible supported triangle at both parities. ## 4. Fully symmetric, manifestly positive root form The same calculation also removes every ordering qualification. No step in (3)--(11) assumed a maximal first label. With the original source phase E_src=2a^2-ab-ac+bc-J-3, the actual scalar has the FULLY symmetric positive form A_source=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src D_sym H_sym, D_sym=N^2/[s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2)s_delta s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]. (12) Here q=exp(pi i/N), s_u=|F_u|. Every H_sym summand is POSITIVE: in (Q^-u;Q)_k each factor is i q^(-u+l) times its positive sine. The full term phase is q^[k(J-delta+1)]=q^(Nk)=(-1)^k, which cancels the denominator phase (-1)^k. All descending sine indices are nonnegative up to the true termination min(delta,a,b,c). The zeroth term is one. Thus (12) proves nonvanishing for EVERY supported triangle, at both parities and composite levels. For an explicit check of the absolute normalization, insert K_2 from (11) and the source prefactor Nq^[E+2b(b+1)-2c(c-1)]/(F_aF_bF_cF_r), with E from the Fourier theorem, into (2). Reflect complementary factorials. Their modulus is exactly D_sym. Their F-power difference is 1-N, and the remaining q exponent, after (-i)^(1-N) is included, differs from N(N+J)+E_src by 2N(-N+b+c+1). Hence the full phase is precisely the one in (12), not merely an unspecified unit. The positive candidate factorial sum, calculated in a chart with a maximal label and then transformed by the same finite Sears lemma, has R_N=N^3 H_sym/[s_a s_b s_c s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2) s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]. (13) The long/short calculation and phase equivalence are recorded with their explicit initial term in the [finite candidate transform port](actual_trivalent_general_finite_transform_port.md#1-exact-long-and-short-series-for-the-candidate-factorial-object). For a direct normalization check, in its maximal-a chart the initial term is N s_a/[s_(a-b)s_(a-c)s_(a-delta)s_b s_c s_r]. Its first Sears factor has modulus s_(b+c)s_(2b)s_(a-b)s_(a-c)/[s_a s_(r_1)s_b s_c]; the phases of its two ascending and two descending Pochhammers cancel exactly, so this factor is POSITIVE. The second factor K_2 in (11) is also positive: all four negative-parameter Pochhammer phases cancel. Its modulus is s_c s_(a+c)s_(d-a)s_(d-2b) /[s_(c-delta)s_(d-b)s_(b+c)s_(r_2)]. Multiply these three displayed factors and use sine reflection; the result is exactly the positive prefactor in (13). Both sides of (13) are manifestly symmetric, so a maximal chart can be chosen for ANY label order. Combining (12),(13) proves A_source=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src [s_as_bs_c/(N s_delta)]R_N for every supported triangle. The lower-saturation branch is zero by the independent complete-clock cancellation. ## 5. Original-source conclusion and its separate sewing scope Together with the root-Fourier coefficient theorem and the explicitly normalized candidate long-to-short series calculation, (2) proves the positive trivalent scalar identity, rather than checking it at finitely many levels. The scalar is zero for J<d; for J>=d it is the specified unit phase times C_N R_N, hence NONZERO. This scalar conclusion does not estimate the whole magnetic tensor: its descendant coefficients can carry additional exponential factorials. Ordinary white and marked white source contractions, full Hermite normals and ordered graph sewing still retain their actual independent data. In particular the scalar action maximum must not be relabelled as an already proved full vertex norm bound. Audit: [all finite coefficient stages and source phases](../experiments/audit_finite_trivalent_euler_racah_transform.py). The [square-linearization proof](actual_trivalent_square_linearization_bridge.md) reaches the same H_c without the Jackson-Leibniz/Newton route. Tests are supplementary; the finite proofs establish the identity.

title: The first quantum-normal connection of an actual root module
text: # The first quantum-normal connection of an actual root module Research construction, 27 October 2026. This gives a canonical algebraic object from the first quantum-normal germ of a specified difference module. It needs no global differential equation in the quantum parameter and no off-root horizontal extension of the actual ADO state. It retains a source and cut, and distinguishes a genuine connection from the nonsemisimple kernel-to-cokernel case. This is attached to the specified actual operator, with its pointing. It is not an identification of its classical geometric component or of its selected norm with the Bloch regulator. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. Root monodromy and its first normal differential Fix N>=2 and a primitive N-th root zeta. Put Q=zeta(1+epsilon), E=C(Y), U=Y^N, sigma_Q f(Y)=f(QY), D=Y partial_Y. Let T(Q)=B(Q,Y)sigma_Q be a specified rank-d difference module, regular and invertible as a matrix germ over E[[epsilon]]. Write H(Q,Y)=B(Q,Y)B(Q,QY)...B(Q,Q^(N-1)Y), T(Q)^N=H(Q,Y)sigma_Q^N, H=H_0+epsilon H_1+O(epsilon^2). Because Q^N=(1+epsilon)^N, sigma_Q^N=I+N epsilon D+O(epsilon^2). Thus L(Q)=T(Q)^N-I has the exact first expansion L=L_0+epsilon L_1+O(epsilon^2), L_0=H_0-I, L_1=H_1+N H_0 D. (1.1) The H_1 term differentiates every occurrence of Q in the product, including its shifted arguments. Omitting those moving-argument derivatives would give a different object. Set K=ker L_0, C=coker L_0 and let pi:E^d->C. Both are E-vector spaces. There is a natural linear map iota:K->C given by inclusion followed by quotient. Define D_N:K -> C, D_N(x)=pi(L_1 x)/N^2. (1.2) For f in E it satisfies the Leibniz rule D_N(fx)=f D_N(x)+(D f/N)iota(x). (1.3) Indeed pi H_0=pi and H_0 x=x on K. In particular for f in C(U), D f/N=U partial_U f. This is an algebraic differential operator between K and C with the specified symbol iota; it is not always an endomorphism of one line. ## 2. Exact cyclic descent The root operator T_0=B(zeta,Y)sigma_zeta commutes with H_0, so it preserves K and induces an operator on C. Its N-th power is H_0, which acts as identity on both spaces. They therefore have cyclic semilinear descent to C(U). One direct spanning formula makes the descent explicit. For a vector x in either space put Av(x)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_0^j x. Then x=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Y^r Av(Y^(-r)x/N). (2.1) This follows from the finite Fourier sum (1/N)sum_r zeta^(-jr)=delta_(j,0). Thus invariants span over E. Their independence over the invariant field C(U) follows by taking a shortest E-linear relation, normalizing one coefficient to one, and subtracting its T_0 translate: all coefficients must be invariant. The operator (1.2) respects this descent. The exact identity [T(Q),L(Q)]=0 gives at first order T_0 L_1+T_1 L_0=L_0 T_1+L_1 T_0. On K, after projection to C, the terms with L_0 vanish. Hence D_N T_0=T_0 D_N. It follows that (1.2) induces D_N:K^(T_0) -> C^(T_0) with symbol U partial_U times the descended iota. This explains the normalization N^2. Dividing L_1 only by N would leave N times the natural logarithmic derivation on the central coordinate U. If eigenvalue one of H_0 is semisimple, then E^d=ker(H_0-I) direct-sum im(H_0-I), and iota is an isomorphism. Its inverse identifies (1.2) with a genuine logarithmic connection on the descended invariant bundle. In particular a simple eigenvalue one gives an algebraic line with connection over C(U). If there is a Jordan block of size greater than one at eigenvalue one, iota need not be invertible. One must retain the full K->C operator. For a rank-two Jordan block it can have zero symbol but a nonzero order-zero part. Replacing it by an inverse matrix or a line connection in that case would lose first-normal information. This construction is initially over the rational function fields C(Y) and C(U). At a special central fiber, such as U=1, the rank of H_0-I can jump. Its fiber kernel and cokernel must not be identified automatically with those generic spaces. Evaluating the selected period there requires the original saturated lattice and its source/co-source jets, or the full first-order complex of Section 4. No complete-fiber regularity is assumed here. ## 3. Gauge invariance, including quantum-normal gauges Let v=G(Q,Y)w, with G=G_0+epsilon G_1+... regular and invertible. Then B'=G^(-1) B sigma_Q(G), H'=G^(-1) H sigma_Q^N(G). Since sigma_Q^N(G)=G_0+epsilon(G_1+N D G_0)+..., H'_0=G_0^(-1)H_0G_0, H'_1=G_0^(-1)H_1G_0 +G_0^(-1)H_0(G_1+N D G_0) -G_0^(-1)G_1G_0^(-1)H_0G_0. (3.1) Equivalently, as first-order differential operators, G_0 L'_1-L_1 G_0=L_0 G_1-G_1 L'_0. (3.2) The right side vanishes between K' and C. Thus G_0 identifies the two kernel-to-cokernel operators canonically. A pure quantum- normal gauge G_0=I changes H_1 by a commutator with H_0, invisible between K and C. A Y-dependent G_0 requires the N D G_0 term in (3.1); it cannot be omitted. This is gauge invariance of a fixed difference module and its first quantum-normal germ. Different left multiples of an annihilator can add extraneous modules. No invariance under such additions is claimed without their source and cut comparison. ## 4. The exact source and co-source normal equations Suppose a supplied section has expansion v=v_0+epsilon v_1+... and L(Q)v(Q)=epsilon s+O(epsilon^2). Then v_0 in K, L_0 v_1+L_1 v_0=s, D_N(v_0)=pi(s)/N^2. (4.1) Changing v_1 by h changes s by L_0h and leaves pi(s) unchanged. Under the gauge of Section 3, s'=G_0^(-1)s. Thus the normal source class is intrinsic to the specified first-order section problem. The full first-order source problem is the two-term block operator [ L_0 0 ] [v_0] = [0], [ L_1 L_0 ] [v_1] [s].
