(4.2) Keeping only the map K->C forgets the lift ambiguity and can lose a normal cut functional. For a supplied scalar cut p(Q)=ell(Q)v(Q)+k(Q), its first coefficient is p_1=ell_0 v_1+ell_1 v_0+k_1. (4.3) The transformed data are v'_0=G_0^(-1)v_0, v'_1=G_0^(-1)v_1-G_0^(-1)G_1G_0^(-1)v_0, ell'_0=ell_0G_0, ell'_1=ell_1G_0+ell_0G_1, and (4.3) is unchanged. This retains the normal co-source; an unpointed connection alone would not recover it. The full ADO normalization remains the original marked dimension line d_N(M), including its sign and canceled meridian germ. A chosen quantum-normal derivative of that line requires its whole lifted phase and cap data. The construction here does not replace it by its numerical complete value or infer that derivative from the root value alone. ## 5. A first-normal source from the original finite lift There is actual input for (4.1) that does not assume the ADO state is horizontal off its root. Retain the auxiliary finite lift G_N(Q,Y) and the pre-specialization annihilator from the [Q-only finite-sum construction](even_meridian_norm_descent.md): Acal(Q,Z,Y,S)G_N(Q,Y)=0 at Z=Q^N, P(Q,Y,S)=Acal(Q,1,Y,S)=sum_(j=0)^d a_j S^j. Choose the coherent Laurent Ore presentation before specializing, including any fixed shifts needed for nonzero a_0,a_d. It can be Laurent in S before specialization. At a regular root, G_N is a whole Q-germ and its value is F_N(Y). Since Q^N=1+N epsilon+..., P G_N=-N epsilon (partial_Z Acal)(zeta,1,Y,S_zeta)F_N+O(epsilon^2). (5.1) The moving shifts have already been retained in Acal; their extra derivatives multiply Q^N-1 and contribute only at second order to this difference. Define h_1 to be the displayed first coefficient. Let A(Q,Y) be the solution companion matrix of P, so that for v=(G_N,S G_N,...,S^(d-1)G_N)^t, sigma_Q v=A v+e_d(P G_N/a_d). Take T=A^(-1)sigma_Q, in the convention of Section 1. Then (T-I)v=epsilon r_1+O(epsilon^2), r_1=A(zeta,Y)^(-1)e_d h_1/a_d(zeta,Y). (5.2) The exact factorization T^N-I=(I+T+...+T^(N-1))(T-I) yields s=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_0^j r_1. (5.3) Its cokernel class is T_0-invariant, since T_0s-s=(H_0-I)r_1. Thus the actual first-normal source descends to C(U), with normalization pi(s)/N^2. Equations (5.1)--(5.3) construct a source from the central derivative of the specified finite-sum annihilator. They do not make the actual root state horizontal for the normal connection. Vanishing of this source class is a condition to prove, not a consequence of rootwise T_0-invariance. Its comparison with a geometric regulator source is still required. The later [source-corrected construction](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md) uses this very same preoperator to make the right-hand side a linear source rule R_N(v), rather than a fixed source value. Its corrected operator D_N-R_N annihilates every compatible root section. If the selected section has nonzero symbol iota(v), this removes all nonconstant central multipliers c(U) while retaining their actual source derivatives. The unsourced D_N still need not annihilate the section. The nonzero-symbol condition and the supplied whole lifting rule are essential. ## 6. A finite-factorial check which distinguishes those statements Take the local factorial G_N(Q,Y)=(Y;Q)_N. It has the exact central equation Acal=S-(1-ZY)/(1-Y), Z=Q^N. At Z=1, P=S-I, so T=sigma_Q, H_0=1, H_1=0. The descended normal connection is U partial_U. The root section is F_N=1-U. It is T_0-invariant, but it is not horizontal for this connection. The actual source calculation gives h_1=-N Y(1-U)/(1-Y), s=-N(1-U)sum_j zeta^jY/(1-zeta^jY) =-N^2 U. Consequently D_N(1-U)=-U=pi(s)/N^2, exactly as (4.1) requires. This is an explicit source identity from the same finite-factorial atoms used in the actual knot state. It is not a claim that the whole knot period is the product of these local sections. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_first_quantum_normal_connection.py). [Results](../experiments/first_quantum_normal_connection_results.json).

title: A finite whole-source proof of the five-crossing cyclotomic transform
text: # A finite whole-source proof of the five-crossing cyclotomic transform 28 October 2026. The candidate in Section 6 of [the actual five-crossing source](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md) is an exact identity for EVERY primitive Nth root Q, N>=2, and arbitrary nonzero Y. No Jones identity, ordinary-color interpolation, or published Bailey proof is used. Write q=Q in the proof, `d=N-1`, `F_a=(q;q)_a`, and H_n(x)=sum_(j=0)^n {n choose j}_q x^j, T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^-1-q^r-q^-r). Then the original reduced whole source satisfies F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^d C_n(q)T_n(Y), C_n(q)=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+3)/2)H_n(q^(-n-1)). (1) Every original turn, cap, Cartan and framing factor is already contained in the starting triple source below. No factor is changed in proving (1). The original full ADO modified-dimension germ, if attached, multiplies both sides unchanged. The proof supplies three reusable finite identities: a terminating three-factor q-Chu transform, a generic Newton connection, and a root Rogers-polynomial convolution with an arbitrary extra variable. ## 1. Elementary finite identities For k<N and arbitrary a,b, sum_(ell=0)^k (q^-k;q)_ell(a;q)_ell(b;q)_ell q^ell/F_ell =sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q a^(k-r)b^r(a;q)_r. (2) Expand `(b;q)_ell`, set ell=r+s, and use sum_(s=0)^n(q^-n;q)_s(c;q)_s q^s/F_s=c^n. (3) For completeness, expand `(c;q)_s` in (3). For each expansion index r the remaining sum is `(q^(1-(n-r));q)_(n-r)` by the finite q-binomial theorem. It vanishes unless r=n; that last coefficient is c^n. Substituting (3) into the expansion of (2), together with `(q^-k)_r/F_r=(-1)^r q^(-kr+r(r-1)/2){k choose r}`, cancels every extra sign and power. This proves (2). It is symmetric in a,b, so either factor may be expanded. We also need the finite q-Vandermonde consequence sum_(u=0)^a sum_(j=0)^b {a choose u}_q {b choose j}_q q^(ju)=H_(a+b)(1). (4) To prove (4), compare coefficients in the finite q-binomial expansion of a product of lengths a and b. It gives `{a+b choose l}=sum_(u+v=l){a choose u}{b choose v} q^((b-v)u)`. Replace v by b-j and sum over l. All denominators used in this application have indices at most d; no root-zero factorial is divided out. ## 2. Reduce the ACTUAL triple to a symmetric polynomial basis The previously proved original source is F_N(Y)=sum_(m+ell<=d)sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(d-m))q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_q {m choose j}_q (q/Y;q)_(m+ell)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_ell. (5) Replace j by m-j and put k=d-m. The ell sum becomes the left side of (2) with `a=q^-k/Y`, `b=q^(-k-j)/Y`, because `q^(m+1)=q^-k`. Use the SYMMETRIC form of its right side. After the exact prefactor cancellation `q^(m(m+2)+2)=q^(k^2+1)`, equation (5) is q sum_(k=0)^d Y^k(q/Y;q)_(d-k) *sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q sum_(j=0)^(d-k){d-k choose j}_q q^(jr)(q^(-k-j)/Y;q)_r. (6) Expand the last Pochhammer with index s. Use `{k choose r}{r choose s}={k choose s}{k-s choose r-s}`. The remaining sums over r-s and j are exactly (4), with lengths k-s and d-k. Thus F_N(Y)=q sum_(k=0)^d Y^k(q/Y;q)_(d-k) *sum_(s=0)^k {k choose s}_q(-1/Y)^s q^(-ks+s(s-1)/2)H_(d-s)(1). (7) Interchange k,s, set `n=d-s`, `k=s+r`, and reflect the root Gaussian by {d-n+r choose r}_q =(-1)^r q^(-nr+r(r-1)/2){n choose r}_q. (8) All powers simplify to F_N(Y)=q sum_(n=0)^d (-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2) H_n(1) P_n(Y), (9) P_n(Y)=sum_(r=0)^n {n choose r}_q(-Y)^r q^(r(r+1)/2)(q/Y;q)_(n-r). For the sign at either parity, the root calculation used here is `(-1)^(d-n)q^(-(d-n)(d-n+1)/2) =(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)`. It follows from the full identity `(-1)^d q^(d(d+1)/2)=1`; no even-level sign is discarded. ## 3. Generic Newton connection For generic q, and hence at the present root whenever n<N, P_n(Y)=(-1)^n q^(n(n+1)/2) sum_(k=0)^n q^(n-k){n choose k}_q T_k(Y). (10) Here is a direct verification independent of (5). The defining finite convolution for P_n gives P_0=1, P_1=1-qX, P_n=(1-q^n X)P_(n-1)+q^n(1-q^(n-1))P_(n-2), X=Y+Y^-1. (11) One way to verify (11) purely formally is to set `A(z)=sum_n P_n z^n/F_n`. Its defining convolution gives `A(qz)/A(z)=(1-z)/[(1-qYz)(1-qz/Y)]`; the two first-order series equations follow immediately by comparing successive coefficients in the finite q-binomial series. Comparing coefficients in this displayed equation gives (11). This is an identity of formal rational coefficients, not a rootwise infinite-product evaluation. Set `R_n=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)P_n`. Then (11) becomes R_n=(X-q^-n)R_(n-1)+(q^(1-n)-1)R_(n-2). (12) The sum on the right of (10), after removing its prefactor, satisfies the same recurrence and initial values. To check a T_k coefficient, use `X T_k=T_(k+1)+(q^(k+1)+q^(-k-1))T_k` and `{n choose k}={n-1 choose k-1}+q^k{n-1 choose k}`. The only remaining ratio is `{n-2 choose k}/{n-1 choose k} =(1-q^(n-1-k))/(1-q^(n-1))`, which makes the two residual terms `q^-n-q^(-k-1)` cancel. This proves (10). Substitution of (10) into (9) cancels BOTH quadratic phases and signs. Consequently the actual Newton coefficient is C_k(q)=q sum_(n=k)^d q^(n-k){n choose k}_q H_n(1). (13) ## 4. A reusable ROOT convolution evaluates every coefficient In fact for arbitrary x, as a polynomial identity in x, q sum_(n=k)^d q^(n-k){n choose k}_q H_n(x) =(-1)^k q^(-k(k+3)/2) x^d H_k(q^(-k-1)/x). (14) The right side is interpreted after multiplying by x^d, so is polynomial also at x=0. Thus every x-Euler moment can be differentiated in (14), with its source character `x^(N-1)` retained. Here is a finite coefficient proof. Put `h_x(z)=sum_(n=0)^d H_n(x)z^n`. Gaussian generating functions and the exact root product `prod_(r=0)^d(1-q^r z)=1-z^N` give h_x(z)=sum_(j=0)^d (xz)^j(q^(j+1)z;q)_(d-j). (15) Indeed both sides have degree at most d, and their first N coefficients agree by `sum_(n>=j){n choose j}z^n=z^j/(z;q)_(j+1)`. This last generating identity follows directly from q-Pascal; it is used only through degree d where all factorials are units. Set `a=q^(-k-1)=q^(d-k)`. The convolution sum_(r=0)^(d-k) a^r {r+k choose k}_q H_(d-r)(x) is the coefficient of z^d in `h_x(z)/(az;q)_(k+1)`. In (15), every term with `j<=d-k-1` cancels the whole denominator, leaving a polynomial of degree d-k-1 and hence ZERO z^d coefficient. Write the remaining j as d-k+s, `0<=s<=k`. Its quotient is x^(d-k+s)z^(d-k+s)/(az;q)_(s+1). Its z^d coefficient is `x^(d-k+s)a^(k-s){k choose s}`. Summing over s gives x^d H_k(a/x). (16) Finally use the exact root reflection `{d-r choose k}=(-1)^k q^(-rk-k(k+1)/2){r+k choose k}` in the left side of (14), setting n=d-r. Its prefactor is `(-1)^k q^(-k(k+3)/2)` and the remaining sum is (16). This proves (14) at every parity and composite level. ## 5. The candidate is proved as a WHOLE meridian identity Take x=1 in (14) and substitute into (13). This gives exactly (1), proving the candidate (6.1) of the source note. At Y=1, `T_n(1)=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)F_n^2`, so in the original Q orientation the exact reduced state is <5_2>_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)](Q;Q)_n^3 /[(Q;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(n-j)]. (17a) This is the source-preserving double sum used by the inner quadrature theorem; its endpoints are not changed. Equivalently, with t=Q^-1, F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) t^n(tY;t)_n(t/Y;t)_n sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (17) All steps were identities of Laurent polynomials in Y. Therefore every fixed-root meridian derivative, including the normal complete-color source, is retained. No conclusion about generic-q derivatives of the actual whole crossing is obtained by differentiating the root identity in Q. This proves a finite source transform; it does not establish the saddle selection or the exponential volume lower bound. Those analyses may now use (17) as an identity of the original state, with its original normalization. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) checks the reusable generic identities, every intermediate root transform, the x-polynomial convolution, and whole-Y Laurent coefficients at small levels. The uniform proof is the finite calculation above, not interpolation of test colors.

title: An unconditional finite q-Chu reduction of the actual five-crossing source
text: # An unconditional finite q-Chu reduction of the actual five-crossing source 28 October 2026. The actual three-index period in [the whole-source calculation](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md) has a two-index whole-meridian reduction by elementary finite q-binomial identities. This reduction does not assume the candidate Newton coefficients in its Section 6. The further transform is now proved in [the full cyclotomic proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md); this note records the independent double-sum route. Write q=Q here (the Gaussian base, not the half-root), `d=N-1`, `F_a=(q;q)_a`, and `H_a(z)=sum_j {a choose j}_q z^j`. Every denominator below has index less than N. ## 1. A reusable terminating three-factor transform For k with `F_1,...,F_k` nonzero, and arbitrary a,b, exactly sum_(ell=0)^k (q^-k; q)_ell (a;q)_ell (b;q)_ell q^ell/F_ell =sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q a^(k-r)b^r(a;q)_r. (1) This is a polynomial identity in a,b, without a genericity condition on their Pochhammer factors. First prove the finite q-Chu identity sum_(s=0)^n (q^-n;q)_s(a;q)_s q^s/F_s=a^n. (2) Expand `(a;q)_s` by the finite q-binomial theorem and interchange the finite sums. For its coefficient with index r the remaining sum is sum_(t=0)^(n-r)(q^(-(n-r));q)_t q^t/F_t =(q^(1-(n-r));q)_(n-r). The last equality is the same finite q-binomial theorem. It is zero unless r=n, because otherwise one factor is `1-q^0`. The r=n term simplifies to a^n, proving (2). To prove (1), expand `(b;q)_ell`, put ell=r+s, and use (2) with length k-r and parameter a q^r. The inner sum is `(a q^r)^(k-r)`. Substitute (q^-k;q)_r/F_r=(-1)^r q^(-kr+r(r-1)/2){k choose r}_q. All signs and q powers cancel, leaving exactly (1). ## 2. Applying it to the original triple source Start with the proved actual source formula F_N(Y)=sum_(m+ell<=d)sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(d-m))q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_q {m choose j}_q (q/Y;q)_(m+ell)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_ell. (3) Replace j by m-j and put k=d-m. At a primitive Nth root, `q^(m+1)=q^-k` and `q^(m(m+2)+2)=q^(k^2+1)`. The ell sum is the left side of (1) with a=q^-k/Y, b=q^(-k-j)/Y. Its r-th term is `Y^-k q^(-k^2-jr){k choose r}(q^-k/Y;q)_r`. The prefactor in (3) consequently simplifies to q Y^k. Set n=k-r and use the exact contiguous product (q/Y;q)_(d-k)(q^-k/Y;q)_(k-n) =(q/Y;q)_(d-n), which follows from q^N=1 before any Y evaluation. One obtains F_N(Y)=q sum_(0<=n<=k<=d) Y^k {k choose n}_q (q/Y;q)_(d-n) H_(d-k)(q^n). (4) This is already an exact simpler finite source transform. It preserves arbitrary Y and all of its meridian derivatives. ## 3. One more finite q-binomial sum gives a DOUBLE sum Expand H in (4). Put k=n+r and `d-k=j+s`, so `n+r+j+s=d`. The root reflection identity gives F_(n+r) F_(j+s) =N(-1)^(j+s)q^((j+s)(j+s+1)/2). (5) Fix n,j and set `L=d-n-j=r+s`. The remaining r,s sum is sum_(s=0)^L (-1)^s q^(s(s+1)/2+js)Y^-s /(F_s F_(L-s)) =(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_L/F_L. (6) Equation (6) is the ordinary finite q-binomial theorem. Thus the whole actual reduced scalar has the unconditional formula F_N(Y)=Nq sum_(n,j>=0,n+j<=d) (-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2+nj) Y^(d-j) (q/Y;q)_(d-n)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_(d-n-j) /[F_n F_j F_(d-n-j)]. (7) The factor N in (5)-(7) is the exact full root factorial, not a normalization chosen after evaluating Y. The original Cartan, turning, cut and framing factors are already included in (3), so remain included in (7). The separate full ADO modified-dimension factor multiplies both unchanged. Equivalently, with k=d-n, (7) is Nq Y^d sum_(k=0)^d (q/Y;q)_k^2/[F_(d-k)F_k] * sum_(j=0)^k (q^-k;q)_j Y^-j /[F_j(q/Y;q)_j]. (8) Formula (8) is initially read after cancelling Pochhammer denominators termwise back to (7); no division at a Y source zero is implied. ## 4. Relation to the proved cyclotomic formula Putting t=q^-1, the proved cyclotomic form in the original note is F_N(Y) =sum_(n=0)^d t^n(tY;t)_n(t/Y;t)_n sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (9) The inner normalized coefficient is the elementary Bailey convolution `sum_j t^(j^2+j)/[F_j(t)F_(n-j)(t)]`. Equations (1)-(8) give an independent double-sum expression. The [full proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) instead uses the symmetric three-factor expansion, a generic Newton connection, and an exact root Rogers-polynomial convolution to prove (9). Repeated ordinary-color nodes are not used as an interpolation proof. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) checks (1) at generic finite parameters and compares (3), (4), (7), and the original literal source at primitive roots with unrestricted whole-meridian evaluations. The displayed finite identities, not the samples, establish their scope.

title: A proved outer maximum for the cubic reduced phase
text: # A proved outer maximum for the cubic reduced phase 28 October 2026. For the exact double-sum phase supplied by the [finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md), the selected inner critical branch has a rigorously concave reduced outer action on a full horizontal band. The explicit bent contour through its cubic stationary point also has a unique global maximum there. The sloped part is controlled analytically, without a mesh-based positivity assumption. This is a theorem about the explicit reduced phase and its contour. The original outer sum still has to be carried to that contour, including its aliases and the inner endpoint pieces. Equality of the cubic critical value with the marked hyperbolic regulator is also separate: numerical agreement or equality of trace fields does not prove that action identity. ## 1. The phase and a specified inner critical branch Use the branch J'(z)=Log(2sin(pi z)) continued from 0<z<1, and set S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +i*pi*(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (1) Its added lattice characters are retained in this definition. Let 1/2<Re x<1, 0<=Im x<=Log(2)/(2pi), X=exp(2pi*i*x), T=1/X-1. The number T lies in the upper half-plane and 1<=|T+1|<=2. The quadratic v-1/v=T (2) has exactly one root in the first quadrant. Indeed its two roots have product -1 and share the sign of their imaginary parts. A root could be purely imaginary only if T belonged to i[2,infinity). The present circles, centered at -1 with radii at most 2, meet the imaginary axis below sqrt(3), so they avoid that ray. The chosen root is analytic here. Put Y=-v, y_s(x)=1+Log(Y)/(2pi*i) =1/2+Log(v)/(2pi*i), (3) where 0<Arg v<pi/2 and -pi<Arg Y<-pi/2. Then 1/2<Re y_s<Re x<1 and 0<Re(x-y_s)<1/2. For the latter inequality, (T+1)v=v^2+v-1 has positive imaginary part, so Arg(T+1)+Arg v lies strictly between zero and pi. All three J arguments in (1) therefore stay on their stated strips. The quadratic equation gives S_y(x,y_s)=0. Exponentiating that derivative gives 1-X/Y=X(1-Y). The logarithmic derivative itself is zero, rather than an unretained multiple of 2pi*i: it is constant modulo that multiple on this connected branch and tends to zero at x->1 from the real interval. Define W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)). (4) ## 2. Exact reduced Hessian Differentiating (1)--(3), or taking its Schur complement, gives exactly W''(x)=2pi*i R(v), R(v)=(v^2+v+4)(v^2+v-1)/(1-v^4). (5) Equivalently, with s=v+1/v=sqrt(T^2+4) on its marked branch, R=(T+1)/(2T)*[(3T-2)/s-5]. (6) These formulas are independent of an added constant logarithmic flattening. Such a flattening still matters for W and W'. ## 3. Horizontal strict concavity on the whole band Write v=a+ib, a,b>0, r=a^2+b^2, and d=|T+1|^2. The present band has 1<=d<=4. Equation (2) gives the exact constraint r^2+(3-d)r+1+2a(r-1)-4a^2=0. (7) Direct multiplication gives Im R=b P_0/|1-v^4|^2. Reducing its real polynomial numerator by (7) gives P=a[2r^2+(6d+4)r-8] +2r^3+2r^2+(13-5d)r+8. (8) This numerator is STRICTLY positive on the stated domain. Here is an elementary certificate. Its constant part is at least C(r)=2r^3+2r^2-7r+8>0. For 0<=r<=1 this is at least 8-7r>=1. For r>=1 it is increasing and C(1)=5. If the coefficient of a in (8) is nonnegative, this proves the claim. Otherwise r<1. Since a<=sqrt(r), replacing a by w=sqrt(r) gives a lower bound. The result is affine in d, with coefficient w^2(6w-5). For w<=5/6 its minimum over 1<=d<=4 occurs at d=4: L_4=2w^6+2w^5+2w^4+7w^2(4w-1)+8(1-w)>0. For w>=1/4 every displayed term is nonnegative. For w<1/4, the last two terms alone exceed 6-7/16>0. For w>=5/6 the minimum occurs at d=1: L_1=2w^6+2w^5+2w^4+10w^3+8(w^2-w+1)>0. Thus Im R>0. Consequently partial_u^2 Re W(u+i eta)<0 (9) for EVERY horizontal line in the band. This proves global horizontal concavity directly from the explicit phase, rather than assuming that a different positive triangulation controls these original reduced coordinates. ## 4. The cubic stationary point and its exact flattening Let rho be the unique real root of rho^3+rho^2-1=0. Elementary evaluation gives 3/4<rho<4/5. Let v_g be the upper-half-plane root of v^3-v^2+1=0, Re v_g=(1+rho)/2, |v_g|^2=1/rho. Define X_g=1/(1+v_g^2), x_g=1+Log(X_g)/(2pi*i)=u_g+i eta_g, y_g=1/2+Log(v_g)/(2pi*i). The critical identities v_g^2(1-v_g)=1 and v_g^5=-(1+v_g) give T_g=v_g^2. On the branch of Section 1, W'(x)=3Log T-Log v-Log(1+v)-i*pi. At the cubic point this is 5Log v_g-Log(1+v_g)-i*pi=0. The sign of pi is fixed: the argument difference lies between -pi/2 and 5pi/2 and is an odd multiple of pi, hence equals pi. Thus (x_g,y_g) is a genuine stationary point of (1) in its stated flattening, not merely a solution of exponentiated equations. Useful exact values are |T_g|=1/rho<4/3, Re(1/T_g)=(1-rho)/2>1/10, D:=|1+T_g|^2=3+rho-rho^2<13/4<4. It follows that eta_g=Log(D)/(4pi)<Log(2)/(2pi). Numerically x_g=.869193400032383...+.092187637885157...i, y_g=.612022435578528...-.022377151124418...i, Re W(x_g)=.450109610025218.... The last decimal is an evaluation of (1). It is not used as a proof of regulator calibration or source intersection. ## 5. Analytic dominance on the sloped outer segment Set theta_g=2pi(1-u_g)=Arg(1+T_g), c=eta_g/(1-u_g)=Log|1+T_g|/theta_g. Then 0<c<1. For completeness theta_g>pi/4: writing 1+T_g=A+iB gives A=(3-rho^2)/2, B^2-A^2=(-2+rho+3rho^2)/2>0. Also Log|1+T_g|<(1/2)Log(13/4)<pi/4. On the sloped segment x=u+i c(1-u), u_g<=u<1, write theta=2pi(1-u), T=exp[(c+i)theta]-1. The function |T| increases with theta on [0,theta_g], so |T|<=4/3. A further useful lower bound is Re(1/T)>=(1-rho)/2>1/10. (10) To prove it, let h(theta)=sinh(c theta) -(2-rho)[cosh(c theta)-cos theta]. It vanishes at both endpoints, by the exact geometric value of Re(1/T_g). Its second derivative is strictly negative: 2-rho>1 and 0<=theta<=theta_g<pi/2. Thus h>=0, which is (10) after using the elementary real coth formula. Equation (6) also gives an absolutely convergent expansion R=-3/T-9/4+E(T), E=(3/4)T+(T+1)(3T-2)/(4T) *[(1+T^2/4)^(-1/2)-1]. For r_T=|T|<2 the binomial derivative bound yields |E|<=3r_T/4+(1+r_T)(2+3r_T)r_T /[32(1-r_T^2/4)^(3/2)]. At r_T<=4/3 the right side is at most 1+63/(20sqrt(5)). Combining with (10), Re R<=(63/sqrt(5)-31)/20<0. (11) The horizontal-band theorem already gives Im R>0 here. Therefore the ENTIRE sloped reduced action satisfies d^2/du^2 Re W(u+i c(1-u)) =2pi[2c Re R-(1-c^2)Im R]<0. (12) Its first derivative vanishes at u_g, so it strictly decreases to the right. This proves the sloped dominance analytically. ## 6. An explicit sufficient outer saddle contour Fix any alpha in (1/2,u_g). The piecewise contour x(u)=u+i min(eta_g,c(1-u)), alpha<=u<=1 (13) has a UNIQUE global maximum of Re W at x_g. The left piece is covered by (9), the right piece by (12), and W'(x_g)=0. There is a strict action gap away from every neighborhood of x_g. The finite endpoint value at u=1 is submaximal by strict decrease, without requiring a separate numerical bound. For an analytic nonzero amplitude with a controlled uniform asymptotic expansion on this contour, ordinary one-variable saddle evaluation therefore has a nonzero Gaussian leading coefficient at x_g. The kink at x_g is harmless: its two tangent directions, 1 and 1-i c, lie in the same negative Gaussian cone. In fact W''(x_g) has negative real AND negative imaginary parts, and c<1, so rotating between those directions keeps the quadratic real part strictly negative. The two local half-rays give the full marked Gaussian, rather than an undetermined zero intersection factor ON THIS specified path. This is not a proof that the original outer residue cycle equals (13). That step must control the actual outer aliases and the inner connector/end-point integrals along the deformation. For example, a constant-height translation of the WHOLE triangle would retain an inner endpoint with action larger than the cubic value; reduced saddle concavity alone would miss it. The exact [inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) is an input for that separate source-preserving comparison, not permission to discard its remaining complex endpoint pieces. [Algebra and contour audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_reduced_outer_concavity.py) and [saved diagnostics](../experiments/five_two_reduced_outer_concavity_results.json).

title: Exact Bloch and hyperbolic calibration of the selected five-crossing phase
text: # Exact Bloch and hyperbolic calibration of the selected five-crossing phase 28 October 2026. This identifies the critical value of the EXACT original two-index source in [the finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). It does not infer a volume limit from the existence of that critical point. Selection of the finite contour is separate. ## 1. The algebraic point and its logarithmic marks Let rho be the positive real root of rho^3+rho^2-1=0, and put v=(1+rho)/2+i sqrt(1/rho-(1+rho)^2/4). Then v is the upper nonreal root of v^3-v^2+1=0. In particular 1-v=v^(-2), v^3=v^2-1, v^5=-(1+v). X=1/(1+v^2), Y=-v, Z=X/Y, x=1+Log(X)/(2pi i), y=1+Log(Y)/(2pi i). (1) The logarithms on the right are principal; X,Y lie in the lower half-plane. Thus 1/2<Re y<Re x<1. Use the marked primitive J(z)=integral_0^z Log(2sin(pi t))dt, S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +i pi(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (2) All three arguments have real part strictly between zero and one. The stationary equations, with the actual marks, are 3Log(1-X)-Log(1-Z)-2(2pi i x)-(2pi i y)+4pi i=0, -Log(1-Y)+Log(1-Z)-(2pi i x)+2pi i=0. (3) Their exponentials are verified by reducing in Q[v]/(v^3-v^2+1): (1-X)^3=X^2 Y(1-Z), 1-Z=X(1-Y). (4) There is no unnoticed integer in (3). For example rho is between 7548/10000 and 7549/10000 by direct polynomial signs and strict monotonicity. Formula (1) then isolates v in the first quadrant near .87744+.74486i, X near .38150-.41040i, and Z near -.02193+.48634i. Principal arguments give Arg(1-X) in (.57,.61), Arg(1-Z) in (-.50,-.40), Im(2pi i x) in (5.44,5.50), Im(2pi i y) in (3.82,3.86). The imaginary part of the first expression in (3) is therefore between -.19 and .20; its real part is zero by (4), so the integer multiple of 2pi i is zero. The second expression is handled by 1-Z=X(1-Y): both Log(1-Z)-Log(1-Y) and principal Log X have arguments in (-pi,0). This proves the marked stationary equations exactly. ## 2. The critical action is its Bloch regulator Write D for the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, D(z)=Im Li_2(z)+log|z| Arg(1-z). With l_X=2pi i x and l_Y=2pi i y, direct differentiation and evaluation at zero give 2pi i S=Li_2(1)-3Li_2(X)+Li_2(Y)+Li_2(Z) -l_X^2-l_X l_Y+2pi i(2l_X+l_Y). (5) All dilogarithms have the branches inherited from 0<Re z<1; their arguments avoid [1,infinity). Set a=Re l_X, b=Re l_Y, A=Im l_X, B=Im l_Y. The imaginary part of the polynomial term in (5) is a(4pi-2A-B)+b(2pi-A). Taking imaginary parts of (3) shows that this equals -3log|X| Arg(1-X)+log|Y| Arg(1-Y) +log|Z| Arg(1-Z). Consequently, with no unrecorded additive constant, 2pi Re S(x,y)=-3D(X)+D(Y)+D(Z). (6) ## 3. An explicit finite Bloch identity The right side of (6) is exactly 3D(v). Here is a short proof using only the six cross-ratio symmetries, duplication, and one five-term relation. First 1-v=v^-2 gives D(v^2)=D(v). Duplication D(z^2)=2D(z)+2D(-z) gives D(-v)=-D(v)/2. D(-v^2)=D(X), since X=1/(1+v^2). D(v^4)=2D(v)+2D(X). (7) The same cubic equation gives the literal field identities -v^4=(-v-1)/(-v), A_0=v(1+v)/(1+v^2)=v^8/(v^8-1). (8) Hence D(-v^4)=D(-v), D(A_0)=-D(v^8), and duplication once more gives D(v^8)=2D(v^4)+2D(-v^4)=3D(v)+4D(X). (9) The five-term identity in multiplicative form at (v,-v) is D(v)+D(-v) =D(-v^2)+D(v(1+v)/(1+v^2)) +D(-v(1-v)/(1+v^2)) =D(X)-D(v^8)+D(Z), (10) because 1-v=v^-2. Substitution of (7)-(9) into (10) yields -3D(X)+D(-v)+D(Z)=3D(v). (11) The regulator identities used here can be checked directly: their exterior derivatives vanish using dD=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z, and their real degenerate values fix the constants. Thus (11) is not a numerical rational relation or a conclusion from the degree of the trace field. ## 4. Why 3D(v) is the hyperbolic volume of the marked complement Use the explicitly paired three-tetrahedron p=0 odd family in [the face and angle audit](twist_family_audit.md) and its [independent topological and peripheral audit](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md). That marked family is the 7/3 five-crossing knot complement. Its positive symmetric angle coordinates are U=(A,B,C), V=(A,B,C), W=(B,C,A), A+3C=pi, A+B+C=pi. (12) The face audit proves that averaging into this symmetric locus preserves all edge equations and does not decrease total volume. The full volume is strictly concave. Thus an interior stationary point of the one-dimensional symmetric volume is its full maximum. Put theta=Arg v. From 1-v=v^-2 and the stated branch one has C=theta, B=2theta, A=pi-3theta, all positive. These are the three angles of the ideal shape v, up to cyclic order. The Euclidean sine rule gives |v|=sin B/sin A, |1-v|=sin C/sin A. The modulus relation |v|^2|1-v|=1 therefore says exactly sin^3 A=sin^2 B sin C. (13) Equation (13) is the derivative-zero equation for 3[Lambda(pi-3theta)+Lambda(2theta)+Lambda(theta)]. It is the interior maximum by strict concavity. The explicit multiplier construction in Section 3.5 of the face audit glues the cusp triangles isometrically, gives trivial edge dilation and complete torus cusps, and hence supplies a complete hyperbolic metric. Its three tetrahedra each have volume D(v). The topological marking fixes the complement, and the positive orientation fixes its volume sign. Therefore Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)=3D(v), Re S(x,y)=Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)/(2pi). (14) This step uses the already audited classical face geometry; it assumes no quantum state identity for that triangulation. ## 5. Scope The selected algebraic point has the exact marked volume action. This resolves the calibration of that point. The actual finite source contour and the exclusion of all competing source pieces still have to be established before (14) implies an asymptotic statement for the original invariant. [Exact field identities and marked-regulator diagnostic](../experiments/audit_five_two_selected_bloch_calibration.py).

title: A selected-contour proof for the original five-crossing prototype
text: # A selected-contour proof for the original five-crossing prototype 28 October 2026. This assembles an independent, computer-assisted proof of the volume asymptotic for the original normalized Kashaev invariant of the marked 7/3 five-crossing knot 5_2. It uses exact finite source transforms, explicit contours, and outward-rounded interval bounds. No Jones asymptotic or published quantum-state asymptotic theorem is an input. This is a prototype for the broader goal, not a proof for a broad class of hyperbolic knots. Coverage only: this knot's asymptotic is already the subject of [Ohtsuki, Quantum Topology 7 (2016), 669-735](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/14527). Only the publisher's bibliographic record and abstract were consulted for that coverage check. No novelty claim is made for the knot case, and that paper's proof is not an input to the argument below. ## 1. Statement and normalization Let K_N denote the original reduced Kashaev invariant with the cut, Cartan, cups/caps and zero framing specified in [the literal four-plat source](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md). Thus K_2=-7 in this handedness. Let v be the upper nonreal root of v^3-v^2+1=0, X=1/(1+v^2), Y=-v, x_g=1+Log(X)/(2pi i), y_g=1+Log(Y)/(2pi i). Write J'(z)=Log(2sin(pi z)) on 0<Re z<1 with J(0)=0, and S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +pi i(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2), S_g=S(x_g,y_g). Then K_N=C N^(3/2) exp(N S_g) [1+O(1/N)], (1) C != 0, Re S_g=Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)/(2pi). (2) The O constant is for this fixed knot and normalization. In particular lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N| =Vol(S^3 minus 5_2). (3) The phase S_g has its stated logarithmic mark, not a value chosen modulo a constant after taking absolute values. The constant in (1) is C=2pi a(x_g,y_g)/ [sqrt(-S_yy(x_g,y_g)) sqrt(-W''(x_g))], a(x,y)=sqrt(2) exp{[3Log sin(pi x)-Log sin(pi y)-Log sin(pi(x-y))]/2 -pi i(3x+2y)}, (4) W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)). The root y_s and both Gaussian square roots are fixed below by the actual oriented contours. In particular the principal square roots of -S_yy and -W'' at the selected point have positive real parts. Every factor of (4) is nonzero. ## 2. Exact original finite source and controlled real collars The [finite whole-meridian transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) proves, before taking any asymptotic, that K_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)], Q=exp(2pi i/N), F_n=(Q;Q)_n. (5) This identity retains the original normalization and all fixed-root meridian derivatives. It is a finite q-binomial proof, not root-color interpolation. The uniform real factorial estimate, including both endpoint rows, gives for each summand in (5) log|summand|=N A(n/N,j/N)+O(log N), A(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y). (6) Let c_*=max_[0,1]J=J(5/6), so 2c_*=Vol(4_1)/(2pi)<.324. For x<=.51, J(x)<=.01 log 2, and J(y),J(x-y)>=-c_*. Thus A<.345 throughout that low-index region. For x>.5 the REAL angular Hessian of A is strictly negative: if a=cot(pi x), b=cot(pi y), c=cot(pi(x-y)), then b+c>0, a=(bc-1)/(b+c)<0 and det Hess A/pi^2=3-2bc>1. Its inner maximum is therefore at y=x/2. For x>=.99, A(x,y)<=3J(x)-2J(x/2) <=3*.01[1-log(.04)]+.01 log 2 <.134. (7) Here 2sin(pi t)>=4t for 0<=t<=1/2 bounds J(x), and J(x/2)>=-.005 log 2 bounds the other term. Enlarging these strict bounds slightly handles a change of at most 1/N in either cutoff. Take a_N=ceil(.51N+1/2), b_N=floor(.99N-1/2). The omitted terms of (5) have total size O(N^B exp(.345N)) for some fixed B. There are only O(N^2) terms, already included in this polynomial. ## 3. Inner quadrature with the original endpoint source For n in this window, use the ENTIRE interpolation f_(N,n)(w)=Q^[-n(n+2)-w(n+1)] F_n^3/[Fhat_N(w)Fhat_N(n-w)] exp(2pi i w). It agrees with the original summand at every allowed integer w. Exact factorial reflection turns it into a Gaussian times the finite product (Q^(w+1);Q)_(N-1-n). The [inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) proves |sum_(j=0)^n f_(N,n)(j)-integral_0^n f_(N,n)(w)dw| <=C log(N+1)|F_n|^2. (8) Summing (8) costs at most C log(N+1) K_(4_1),N, whose proved exponent is 2c_*<.324. All inner discrete corrections are therefore below the selected rate; no Fourier mode is assumed. Define the holomorphic outer function using the SAME interpolation: g_N(z)=exp(4pi i z) integral_0^z Q^[-z(z+2)-w(z+1)] Fhat_N(z)^3/[Fhat_N(w)Fhat_N(z-w)] exp(2pi i w)dw. (9) At integer z=n its value is exactly the integral in (8). Thus the original invariant equals sum_(n=a_N)^(b_N)g_N(n), up to the explicitly bounded collar and inner-quadrature errors. ## 4. Exact outer quadrature, with all four source edges Set L=a_N-1/2, R=b_N+1/2, ell=L/N, r=R/N. Define u_g=Re x_g, h_g=Im x_g, c=h_g/(1-u_g), h(u)=min(h_g,c(1-u)), x_+(u)=u+i h(u), x_-(u)=u-.1i, ell<=u<=r. (10) The [finite-height outer residue formula](source_preserving_outer_finite_height_quadrature.md) expresses the original integer sum EXACTLY as the unweighted integral over z=N x_+(u), plus: * the upper contour with kernel 1/(exp(-2pi i z)-1); * the lower contour with kernel 1/(exp(2pi i z)-1); * the two upper vertical source edges with weights 1/(1+exp(-2pi t)); * the two lower vertical source edges with weights 1/(1+exp(2pi t)). The half-integer edges enclose precisely the original integers. The formula retains the off-lattice exp(4pi i z) character, rather than silently replacing the selected Poisson source. For each complex x on these paths the actual inner contour can be changed, by holomorphy, to 0 -> i lambda(x) -> Re x+i lambda(x) -> x, T=exp(-2pi i x)-1, v(x)=[T+sqrt(T^2+4)]/2, y_s(x)=1/2+Log(v(x))/(2pi i), lambda(x)=Im y_s(x). (11) The square-root branch puts v in quadrant I. All factorial arguments y,x-y have nonnegative real part, at most .99, and stay in a bounded imaginary range. The endpoint-uniform Gamma-product bound in the outer note proves |g_N(Nx)|<=C N^(3/2) exp[N G(x)], G(x)=max_(inner polygon) Re S(x,y). (12) Thus an endpoint singularity contributes at most a polynomial factor; the interior asymptotic is not being applied at zero. ## 5. The rigorous whole-contour bounds There are two independent types of evidence here. The [analytic outer concavity proof](five_two_reduced_outer_contour_concavity.md) shows that W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)) has its unique global maximum of real part on x_+ at x_g. It proves both the constant-height and sloped segments, using their explicit algebraic Hessian. The [analytic inner maximum reduction](selected_inner_angular_contour.md) shows that the full horizontal inner segment has its maximum at the selected saddle or the RIGHT endpoint. Both vertical connectors reduce to their endpoints and at most one explicit stationary point. It proves these assertions for the whole complex strip used in (10)-(11), not merely on sampled points. The resulting one-variable tests have the following certified outward-rounded Arb bounds: | Actual contour piece | Certified phase upper bound | |---|---:| | Upper inner left connector | .200 | | Upper inner right connector, including its interior maximum | .445 | | Entire lower inner polygon, after the outer kernel weight | .400 | | All four outer vertical source edges, with their prescribed weights | .440 | | Selected critical value | .45010 < Re S_g < .45012 | The executable proof is [certify_selected_inner_contours.py](../experiments/certify_selected_inner_contours.py), with [the interval certificate](../experiments/selected_inner_contour_certificate.json). It uses 192-bit acb/arb arithmetic and covers its closed parameter intervals by 1,832 verified dyadic cells. Floating-point displays are not used in a passing comparison. Boundary values use the one-sided J mark, including Re J(i tau)=-pi|tau|/2. The vertical source boxes include u in [.5099,.5101] and [.9899,.9901], so contain the rounded half-grid endpoints for all sufficiently large N. The top and bottom curve bounds hold throughout [.51,.99]. On the upper curve h>=.007, so its weighted phase is at most .45012-2pi*.007<.407, using the analytic outer maximum and the certified inner connectors. Equation (12) and the EXACT outer formula consequently give sum_(n=a_N)^(b_N) g_N(n) =integral_(N x_+) g_N(z)dz +O(N^(5/2) exp(.440N)). (13) The still retained inner connectors of the MAIN upper integral have total size O(N^B exp(.445N)). This is below Re S_g. No cancellation assumption is used to discard any of these pieces. ## 6. The surviving local Gaussian is nonzero On the upper horizontal inner segment, the selected saddle is a strict nondegenerate maximum; the analytic proof gives S_yy=-2pi i(v^2+1)/[v(v+1)], Re S_yy<0. W''=2pi i (v^2+v+4)(v^2+v-1)/(1-v^4). On a fixed complex neighborhood of x_g all connector gaps persist uniformly. The actual interpolation has its nonzero analytic interior amplitude exp(4pi i Nx)K_N(Nx,Ny) =sqrt(N) a(x,y) exp[N S(x,y)] (1+O(1/N)), (14) with a as in (4). Ordinary one-variable Gaussian integration on the specified inner segment gives g_N(Nx)=N a(x,y_s(x)) sqrt(2pi/[-S_yy(x,y_s(x))]) exp[N W(x)](1+O(1/N)). (15) Equation (15) holds uniformly on that fixed complex neighborhood; away from it only the absolute phase estimates are used. This Gaussian has coefficient one: the integral was deformed from its actual finite interval to this single horizontal maximum, with its connectors separately bounded. The analytic outer proof gives Re W''(x_g)<0 and Im W''(x_g)<0, and 0<c<1. Therefore both tangent directions 1 and 1-i c of the bent upper curve belong to the same negative Gaussian cone. The two oriented half-rays combine to the full Gaussian; there is no undetermined intersection coefficient at the kink. A local contour deformation within that cone also gives the usual integer-power expansion. Outside any fixed neighborhood of x_g the strict analytic outer maximum and the certified inner endpoint bounds give an exponential gap. Integrating (15), including dz=N dx, therefore gives (1) with precisely (4). Its power N^(3/2) is N^2 from the two integration measures, sqrt(N) from the factorial amplitude, and N^-1 from two nondegenerate Gaussian variables. Every omitted contribution in Sections 2-5 has a strictly smaller exponential rate. ## 7. Exact marked volume calibration and scope [The explicit Bloch calibration](five_two_selected_bloch_calibration.md) proves, at this same marked critical point, 2pi Re S_g=-3D(X)+D(Y)+D(X/Y)=3D(v) =Vol(S^3 minus 5_2). (16) The first equality uses the marked stationary equations, so all logarithmic modulus terms are accounted for. The second uses one explicit five-term relation and three duplications. The last uses the independently audited three-tetrahedron positive angle maximum and the actual knot marking. Neither numerical agreement nor equality of trace fields is the calibration argument. Equations (1) and (16) prove (3). The broad hyperbolic-knot goal remains open. The reusable part is concrete: an exact finite bridge transform; quadrature whose errors retain and bound the original endpoints; and a certified contour with one nonzero geometric Gaussian. Extending these properties to a sufficiently broad class is required before claiming a general torsor or A-polynomial volume theorem. [Finite-level normalization diagnostics](../experiments/audit_five_two_selected_volume.py) check the displayed nonzero prefactor and marked action against the exact original double sum through N=192. They support the normalization audit; the proof of the limit is the argument and interval certificate above, not extrapolation of those values.

title: The actual whole source for the 7/3 five-crossing plat
text: # The actual whole source for the 7/3 five-crossing plat Research note, 27 October 2026. This derives an exact finite source formula for 5_2 from the same oriented mixed-color four-plat method used for 4_1. All turns, the cut coupon, full Cartan scalar and zero-framing correction are retained. Both the three-index Gaussian/Pochhammer formula and its cyclotomic coefficient transform are proved for the whole meridian family. At completeness the transform gives an explicit two-index formula for the original state. This is a diagnostic for arbitrary-bridge source transport, not a restriction of the main volume target to the twist family. No broad selected-period or hyperbolic-volume theorem is asserted here. ## 1. The marked plat and exact framing Set q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, Y=M^2=Qx^2, d=N-1 and xvee=x^(-1)Q^(-1). Use beta=sigma_2^2 sigma_1^(-2) sigma_2. (1.1) Its action order is sigma_2, sigma_1^(-1), sigma_1^(-1), sigma_2, sigma_2. With the same rational-tangle marking as in the [figure-eight proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), T=[1 1;0 1], U=[1 0;1 1], T^2 U^2 T (0,1)^t=(7,3)^t. (1.2) This is the two-bridge 7/3 plat, with continued fraction [2,2,1] or [2,3], giving the five-crossing twist-knot diagram 5_2 in the handedness fixed by (1.1). The actual three-braid word used in the earlier prototype is retained as an independent finite evaluation check in the audit; no Jones formula is used. The top colors are [V(x),V(xvee),V(xvee),V(x)] and their orientations are [+, -, -, +]. Every crossing has positive oriented writhe, so the framing correction is the inverse fifth power of the actual color twist. Put A=alpha, B=2d-alpha, so q^A=x, q^B=xvee. The full mixed Cartan contribution is q^((3B^2-2AB)/2). Including the twist q^(-(5/2)(A^2-2dA)) gives exactly q^(3dB)=xvee^(3d). (1.3) Formula (1.3) is included in the contraction. Omitting either its Cartan or framing part would change the whole meridian identity. ## 2. The same literal source has different bottom cap types Use the exact balanced mixed R coefficients and turns from the figure-eight proof. Cut the fourth top leg at index zero. Because this cut is a left pivotal trace, its coupon is D_0=g E_00, and Tr(g^(-1)D_0 C)=C_00. Thus it is the original reduced scalar cut. The top source indices are (a,d-a,d,0), 0<=a<N, and their coefficient, including the two cups and the coupon, is N^2 x^(a-2d). The final colors are now [V(x),V(xvee),V(xvee),V(x)]. Thus the first bottom cap is ev_R(x), while the second is ev_L(x). This differs from the figure-eight contraction and is essential. If the surviving first output index is b and its dual partner is d-b, then the two cap coefficients are x^(d-b)g_b/N=x^(-b)Q^(-b)/N, x^d/N, g_b=x^(-d)Q^(-b). (2.1) All cap and cup factors are literal finite matrices. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out, and no separate modified trace is assigned to each bridge. ## 3. Forced transfer elimination Write the five transfers in action order as k_1,...,k_5. The first positive crossing has second input index d, so k_1=0. After the next two negative crossings write their transfers as k and ell. The successive states are (a,d,d-a,0), (d-k,a+k,d-a,0), (a+k-ell,d-k+ell,d-a,0), with a+k<N, 0<=ell<=k. (3.1) The fourth positive crossing has transfer j<=a. The last bottom cap forces the fifth transfer to be j-a, hence k_4=a, k_5=0. (3.2) The final state is (a+k-ell,d-a-k+ell,d,0). The first cap relation follows automatically. Thus the exact surviving routes are (0,k,ell,a,0), with support (3.1). This elimination uses only the actual unwrapped finite support. Set j=k-ell, n=a+k and m=a+j=n-ell. The whole boundary factor from the cups, cap types in (2.1), and the coupon is x^(-d-j) Q^(-a-j). Multiplying by the five mixed crossing entries and (1.3), then reflecting the two terminal Gaussian binomials, gives W_(a,k,ell)=(-1)^ell Y^(2d-2n+ell) Q^(a(k+1)+k^2+2k+2-ell*j-ell(ell+1)/2) {n choose k}_Q {k choose ell}_Q (Q/Y;Q)_k (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell (Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_a. (3.3) The reflection identities used here are {d choose a}_Q=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2), {d-j choose ell}_Q =(-1)^ell Q^(-ell*j-ell(ell+1)/2) {j+ell choose ell}_Q. They hold because Q has primitive order N and all upper indices involved are less than N. ## 4. An exact whole-source Gaussian formula Invert the ell factors of (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell in (3.3): (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell =(-Y)^ell Q^(-n*ell+ell(ell-1)/2) (Q^(m+1)/Y;Q)_ell. The signs cancel. The remaining products and binomials simplify by {n choose k}_Q {k choose ell}_Q ={m+ell choose ell}_Q {m choose j}_Q, (Q/Y;Q)_k (Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_a (Q^(m+1)/Y;Q)_ell =(Q/Y;Q)_(m+ell)(Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_ell. Their monomial exponent becomes j(m+1)+m+ell+2. We obtain the following proved identity for the actual reduced whole period: F_(5_2),N(Y) =sum_(m,ell>=0,m+ell<N) sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(N-1-m)) Q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_Q {m choose j}_Q (Q/Y;Q)_(m+ell)(Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_ell. (4.1) Every factor is finite. This is a Laurent-polynomial identity before setting Y=1 or Y^N=1. In particular the displayed Y^(2(N-1-m)) is retained, including all of its meridian jets. The exact original full ADO factor d_N(M), if desired, multiplies both sides as its unchanged whole germ. At N=2 the formula gives, exactly, F_(5_2),2(Y)=-2Y-3-2/Y, <5_2>_2=-7. The sign is fixed by the above framing and source, rather than chosen from the knot determinant. ## 5. Reciprocal Newton space and two proved boundary rows Formula (4.1) has minimum Y exponent at least -d, term by term: the minimum in a term is 2d-3m-2ell, and m+ell<=d. The already proved actual Weyl symmetry F(Y)=F(Y^(-1)) therefore bounds the maximum exponent by d as well. Consequently there are unique coefficients C_n^(N), 0<=n<=d, in F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^d C_n^(N) T_n(Y), T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^r-Q^(-r)). (5.1) This is a statement about whole reciprocal Laurent polynomials, not interpolation of a few root values. The T_n are monic Newton polynomials of degree n in Y+Y^(-1), including at a root Q. The actual anchor at Y=Q gives C_0^(N)=1. The coefficient of Y^(-d) in (4.1) comes only from m=d,ell=0. Since (-1)^d Q^(d(d+1)/2)=1, the top row is exactly C_d^(N)=Q sum_(j=0)^d {d choose j}_Q. (5.2) There is a useful source-basis simplification valid at every n: (1-Y)T_n(Y)=-Y^(n+1)(Q^(-n)/Y;Q)_(2n+1). (5.3) Thus the normal source has one contiguous Pochhammer rather than two separated products. Equation (5.3) follows by inverting (Y;Q)_(n+1) in (1-Y)T_n and joining its factors with (Q/Y;Q)_n. It may be useful when transporting sources through arbitrary bridge convolutions. It does not itself prove the remaining coefficient transform. ## 6. The proved whole-source cyclotomic transform For every primitive Nth root Q, every N>=2, and arbitrary nonzero Y, the exact simplification is C_n(Q)=(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+3)/2) sum_(j=0)^n Q^(-j(n+1)){n choose j}_Q, F_N(Y) =sum_(n=0)^(N-1) C_n(Q) T_n(Y). (6.1) Equivalently its inner summand is Q^(-j(j+1)){n choose j}_(Q^(-1)). The [direct finite proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) starts from (4.1), applies an elementary terminating three-factor q-Chu transform and q-Vandermonde, and then uses a generic Newton connection and a finite root Rogers-polynomial convolution. Every parity sign and source factor is retained. The proof is a Laurent-polynomial identity in Y; repeated ordinary-color nodes are not used as interpolation data. Thus it includes all fixed-root meridian jets and the normal complete-color source. At Y=1, use T_n(1)=(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+1)/2)(Q;Q)_n^2. Writing F_n=(Q;Q)_n, the original reduced Kashaev state is therefore <5_2>_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)]. (6.2) This is the exact double sum used by the [source-preserving inner quadrature](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md). Neither (6.1) nor (6.2) asserts saddle selection, a noncancellation estimate, or a volume limit. The full modified-dimension function remains its original separate factor when the full ADO period is used. ## 7. Independent checks The [literal-path audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_whole_source.py) starts with the original E/Cartan mixed crossing entries, the two exact cups, the fourth-leg coupon, and the differently oriented bottom caps. It sums all paths and checks the forced route pattern and each surviving weight in (4.1). Twenty-seven whole contractions at levels 2 through 10 and three meridians per level pass; eighteen are also compared with the original six-crossing three-braid cut. The audit checks (1.2)--(1.3), the normal-basis product identity, the top Newton row, the proved cyclotomic values and (6.2). The uniform proof of (4.1) is the source and transfer calculation in Sections 1--4. The proof of (6.1) is the separate [finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md), whose [audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) also compares whole-Y Laurent coefficients and checks the reusable generic and root convolution identities. The finite checks validate the formulas; they do not establish their all-level scope. [Results](../experiments/five_two_whole_source_results.json).

title: Which derivatives the current direct-power route actually requires
text: # Which derivatives the current direct-power route actually requires The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . Conclusion: the current route to the original root sequence does NOT require a genuine-q normal estimate. It does require the full spectral Hermite/Jordan data at the fixed root. Those are different derivatives. For each individual N, fix q_N=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, and the literal original pair Casimir Omega_N. In notes/actual_direct_long_power_source.md, section3, the exact identity is R_N^n=q_N^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega_N)/(2hbar)], hbar=2pi i/N, K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2. At each double Casimir node its value AND derivative with respect to sigma equal those of the actual original R_N^n. At the odd simple node only its value is required. Full Hermite uniqueness in the root Casimir quotient therefore proves the matrix equality, including negative powers and the original square-root scalar. No semisimple quotient is taken. An earlier generic argument used to establish these finite identities would not by itself introduce a uniform off-root asymptotic requirement. The source map in notes/actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md, sections1--4, applies to these exact polynomials at the SAME fixed root. It retains the original physical endpoints, Cartan factors, changing strand positions, and unrestricted marked cap. The other caps and integer total-degree conservation force the marked complementary pair only AFTER the whole contraction. Its literal mark satisfies mp=1. The cup/cap constants and mark character are assembled explicitly in (7a,b); the inverse Fourier measure and original degree constraint give the exact coefficient (9), with no extra N factor and no root limit. In particular the ordinary quantum dimension is never divided out in this direct marked evaluation. The passage from that raw marked contraction to the original enhanced Kashaev normalization is the existing fixed-root crossing/pivot/dual comparison and retained framing character. The complete-color comparison in notes/actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md uses root cut scalarity, exact basis covariance and mp=1. It is local in the crossing word and applies when a box contains the actual power R_N^n. The enhanced reduced normalization differs by a recorded unit phase. If one instead asks for the full one-cut modified ADO normalization, its additional exact factor is i^(N+3)/N at the complete pointing; that is not an uncomputed q-normal correction and has zero exponential rate. No such extra modified factor is silently attached to Kashaev's unknot-one evaluation. The exact spectral Cauchy and total-derivative periods are therefore alternative formulas for the SAME root marked scalar for every N. Their V_N(sigma) and partial_sigma V_N contain the independent nilpotent and semisimple data. Differentiating a value-only complete interpolation would be invalid, but that issue is spectral, not a requirement to deform q away from q_N. The current cofactor proofs address precisely this fixed-root spectral issue. The generic trace identity F_D(t)=D_N(t) z_D(t), with z_D(0)=F_D'(0)/D_N'(0), is a valid ALTERNATIVE presentation of the marked scalar in the matching-graph notes. Using that presentation for asymptotics would require its specified moving-q lift and normal. The direct marked/Casimir route does not use this quotient and need not inherit its analytic hypotheses. Similarly, extending the result to a generic-q or moving meridian invariant is a separate problem. Although q_N varies with the integer level N, the desired theorem is a limit of exact fixed-root identities indexed by N. It needs uniform N estimates for those identities, not a derivative with respect to q. The shared coefficient packet is now proved by the linked whole-source theorem. The subsequent localized period theorem also supplies the nonzero unit-charge contribution with its original normalization. The outstanding gate is control of its exact global spectral/charge remainder. A genuine-q normal should not be listed as another necessary gate for this route. Audited sources: actual_direct_long_power_source §§1--3; actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source §§1--4; actual_original_marked_face_coefficient §§2--4; actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization §§1--3; actual_spectral_total_derivative_source; actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp §1; general_augmented_plat_long_twist_target equation(3a). This is an analytical dependency audit, not a new numerical test. Root independently checked the cited fixed-root Gaussian, Hermite data, original coefficient normalization and reduced/modified distinction. The [localized original period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) now proves the nonzero unit-charge contribution and dominance in the finite local charge sector. The remaining gate is its exact global remainder, including the full integrals of remote charges. It does not require a generic-q continuation.

title: Fixed-root Ward data do not admit a literal scalar formalization
text: # Fixed-root Ward data do not admit a literal scalar formalization Research note, 27 October 2026. This isolates an obstruction to one proposed shortcut from the exact all-matrices Hopf-Ward diagram to the geometric Gaussian period. It also specifies what a homological perturbation argument would have to supply. The obstruction applies to a fixed-root, composition-preserving formalization. It does not rule out a linear source-compatible comparison in a larger all-level category, and does not invalidate the partially summed support theorem. ## 1. The fixed-N action cannot become a nontrivial near-identity flow Fix `N>=2`, a characteristic-zero cyclotomic coefficient field, and the actual matrices. Since K^N=x^N I, their conjugation action satisfies (ad_K)^N=I. (1.1) The same relation holds on every tensor Hopf-adjoint matrix space. **Finite-order lemma.** Let `E` be a separated, complete, H-torsion-free module in characteristic zero, with `N` invertible. If a continuous endomorphism `U` satisfies U=I+O(H), U^N=I, then `U=I`. Proof: if `U=I+H^s D mod H^(s+1)`, expansion of the fixed finite power gives `U^N=I+N H^s D mod H^(s+1)`, hence `D=0`. Induction and separatedness give the result. Equivalently the H-adic logarithm exists and `N log U=0`. Consequently a comparison preserving (1.1) cannot send the actual fixed-N adjoint action to a regular operator with principal form U=I+H A(h_sl/2)+O(H^2) and a nonzero conjugation field on a framing coefficient algebra. The same applies to the two cut-stabilizer fields obtained from actual Hopf-adjoint combinations in [the finite Ward calculation](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). If an equivariant linear map has only an invariant image, this conclusion applies only on that image: `U` acts as identity there. An invariant rank-one scalar quotient is therefore **not** excluded. The obstruction concerns simultaneously retaining the full fixed-N action and realizing its nontrivial classical framing transport on that image. ## 2. All matrices cannot map multiplicatively into scalar symbols Let `A_H` be an H-adically separated, H-torsion-free complete algebra whose special fibre is an integral domain. Then `A_H` is a domain. Indeed two nonzero elements have finite H-valuations, and the product of their first nonzero symbols cannot vanish. The same is true after inverting `H`. There is no unital algebra map End(k^N) -> A_H[1/H], N>1. (2.1) The matrix algebra is simple, so a unital map is injective, whereas its nontrivial orthogonal idempotents cannot inject into a domain. Thus the exact all-matrices finite diagram cannot be mapped multiplicatively to a scalar deformation quantization with a reduced integral geometric special fibre. Even on a smaller subalgebra, the literal nilpotent relation gives a concrete symbol obstruction. The actual raising matrix obeys `Ecal^N=0`. Any composition-preserving scalar principal-symbol map therefore sends it to `e` with `e^N=0`, so `e=0` on the reduced geometric chart. This is incompatible with the nonzero interior moment-map symbol used for the geometric conjugation fields. Matrix-valued formal targets evade the domain statement: they can retain matrix idempotents and nilpotents. They do not thereby evade the finite-order lemma if the adjoint action is required to become near identity on the image. Linear maps of current complexes need not preserve products and are not ruled out by (2.1). ## 3. Why this is a fixed-root obstruction, not a contradiction to bulk support For fixed `N`, there is no scalar base change sending the primitive root `Q_N` to `exp(H)` in a characteristic-zero formal field while retaining its defining equation: it would require exp(NH)=1, which is false as a formal power series for nonzero fixed `N`. Equivalently the formal neighbourhood of `Q=1` in `Q^N=1` is the single reduced point `H=0`. The geometric scaling instead has `N` growing and positions of order `1/H`, with `A=Q^a` and `Q^N=1` retained through an independent Frobenius parameter before specialization. It is an all-level unfolding, not the formal completion of one finite matrix algebra. This is exactly why the proper-ratio construction in [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) is legitimate: it first proves a rational contiguity identity in independent variables and only then specializes its central parameter. It does not map every fixed-N matrix and every finite relation into the scalar formal coefficient algebra. The source itself makes the distinction visible. In the finite color algebra `C_N=k[A^+/-1]/(A^N-1)`, canonical representatives obey A f_tilde-(Af)_tilde=f_(N-1)(A^N-1). The cut of `(Af)_tilde` contains `f_(N-1)`, even though ordinary multiplication by `A` followed by the zero residue does not. This degree-near-N carry is part of the exact source. A bounded-degree scalar formal coefficient expansion cannot silently replace it. The [relative source construction](relative_framing_source_transgression.md) retains it explicitly and is linear rather than multiplicative. ## 4. What homological perturbation would prove, if its hypotheses were supplied Here is a precise sufficient formal statement. Work in a common H-complete **source-unfolded** category, with all endpoint and carry components included. Suppose a complex `(C,d0)` has a contraction onto a one-degree geometric line `G`, with maps `p,i,k` satisfying p i=I, d0 k+k d0=I-i p, k^2=k i=p k=0. The line may carry its retained exponential regulator factor; scalar coefficients and formal units are taken after that factor is fixed. Suppose `d=d0+Delta` is a differential, and `k Delta` and `Delta k` raise the H filtration by at least one. Define i_D=(I+k Delta)^(-1)i, p_D=p(I+Delta k)^(-1), k_D=k(I+Delta k)^(-1), d_G=p Delta(I+k Delta)^(-1)i. All inverse operators here are the convergent geometric series in the stipulated filtration, and `p_D=p+O(H)`. These signs use `d0 k+k d0=I-i p`. The identities follow by substituting `i_D=i-k Delta i_D` and `d0 Delta+Delta d0+Delta^2=0`; for example they give `d i_D=i_D d_G`. The corresponding identities for `p_D,k_D` follow by the same multiplication, yielding the perturbed contraction. Since `G` is concentrated in one degree, `d_G=0`. If the original marked closed source `c` is a d-cocycle and p(c mod H)!=0, then `p_D c` is nonzero: its first coefficient is the displayed nonzero projection. A compatible diagram of actual partial traces and Ward complexes would carry this class to a scalar Ward line. If its leading scalar map is nonzero, the perturbed scalar map is a unit and the class survives. The exact finite cut homotopy `Phi-p=b delta` would then identify its prescribed cut with that scalar projection. This would be a formal source-survival theorem; it would still assert no convergence or selected rootwise asymptotic. The compatibility requirement is substantial. Given chain maps in a diagram, perturbation transports them to `p_D' f i_D`, but their nonzero leading action must be checked. Chain-map identities and normalization of a different class do not force it. ## 5. Which hypotheses are already available The current notes supply the following separate exact inputs: * A nonzero transverse geometric Gaussian contraction with two actual framing coordinates left external, including exact contiguity. * A literal finite relative source complex and the original `psi,phi,e,D`, with all canonical carries retained. * An exact finite Hopf-adjoint partial-trace chain map for every matrix, and a finite cut Ward contraction onto `k I`. * The uniform nonzero classical normal density in the marked cut determinant line. They do not yet supply a common source-unfolded complex `C`, its unperturbed source-compatible contraction, the perturbation `Delta` realizing the actual Ward currents after transverse elimination, or the nonzero leading scalar map on the **geometric** class. In particular the auxiliary relative coordinate of the finite source has not been identified with the internal Gaussian framing mode. The finite Ward homotopy cannot merely be inserted into the formal geometric series and declared small. Its coefficients contain 1/(k_a-k_b)=1/[x(exp(-Ha)-exp(-Hb))] =1/[x H(b-a)]+O(1) for fixed `a!=b`, and the cumulative F inverse likewise contains `1/(1-exp(H(r+1)))`. Thus an `O(H)` correction need not make `k Delta` topologically nilpotent. A suitable rescaled classical complex may repair this, but its source and endpoint compatibility must be constructed. Polynomial bounds in `N` do not establish the required H-adic smallness. There is therefore no justified HPL shortcut from the current separate inputs to scalar source survival. A literal multiplicative fixed-root-to-scalar formalization is impossible by Sections 1--2. A linear all-level comparison, retaining the Frobenius and source normal directions and explicitly transporting the currents, remains possible and is the appropriate next algebraic object. The finite all-matrices chain map alone does not construct it.

title: The flat cyclic source frame is rigid; its scalar period is separate
text: # The flat cyclic source frame is rigid; its scalar period is separate Independent algebraic theorem, 27 October 2026. The actual highest-input clock, cyclic repair and paired source have a whole matrix-algebra description BEFORE quantum jets. On the source-cyclic chart their scheme-theoretic classification is elementary. A rank-one defect must be aligned with the actual source line; rank one alone does not imply this. The rigid frame does not fix the scalar of a closed transport. ## 1. The actual source frame and its coefficient ring Fix N>=2, Q a unit, and invert only 1-Q^k for 1<=k<N. Write delta=1-Q^N, B_0=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)), P_0 e_j=e_(j+1 mod N), E_0=E_00, A_0=e_0 1^t. Here 1^t is the original all-ones output row. These are the literal highest-input data of [the actual two-wall boundary](actual_highest_whittaker_boundary_and_moving_walls.md), not an additional state. Direct entries give B_0 P_0-Q P_0 B_0=delta E_(0,N-1), B_0 P_0 B_0^-1 P_0^-1 =Q[I+(Q^-N-1)E_0], B_0 A_0=A_0, A_0 P_0=A_0, A_0^2=A_0, P_0^N=I, E_0 A_0=A_0, A_0 E_0=E_0. (1.1) The last two identities express equality of the two IMAGE lines. They do not identify the source row with the defect row: E_0 is e_0 e_0^t, whereas A_0 is e_0 1^t. That distinction is retained. The normalization A_0^2=A_0 is the specified primitive pair 1^t e_0=1. Any original external d_N(M) line remains attached as that exact separate source factor; it is not divided away at one of its zeros/poles to obtain this primitive matrix statement. Without the specified normalization, BA=A and AP=A allow every scalar multiple a A_0, so even the source scale would be free. Work with rank-N vector bundles over this coefficient ring or any specified COMMUTATIVE base algebra. Source and defect projectors have locally free image of rank one. No delta inverse is adjoined. ## 2. An explicit classification on the cyclic source chart Let E have rank N, let P be invertible with P^N=I, and let A be an idempotent rank-one source. Put L=im A. Suppose BA=A, AP=A, im(BP-QPB) contained in L, (2.1) and suppose the source orbit map Theta: direct_sum_(j=0)^(N-1) L -> E, Theta(l_0,...,l_(N-1))=sum_j P^j l_j (2.2) is an isomorphism. Then in this CANONICAL line-valued frame P=P_0 tensor I_L, B=B_0 tensor I_L, A=A_0 tensor I_L. (2.3) Proof. AP^j=A makes A act by summing the N input copies into the zeroth copy. P cycles them. BA=A makes the first column of B equal to (I_L,0,...,0)^t. Every entry of B in this frame is an endomorphism of L, hence a scalar over the base. Since the image in (2.1) lies in the zeroth copy, the other rows give B_(i,j+1 mod N)=Q B_(i-1,j), 1<=i<N. (2.4) For i>=j this recurrence and the first column yield B_(i,j)=Q^j delta_(i,j). For i<j they yield B_(i,j)=Q^i B_(0,j-i). The wrap case j=N-1 in (2.4) has left side zero, forcing every B_(0,k)=0 for 1<=k<N. This proves (2.3). In particular B is automatically invertible. No wall cancellation, eigenvalue argument or flatness theorem was needed for this proof. This is a classification over arbitrary base algebras on the specified open chart, including algebras with nilpotents. Its groupoid is the groupoid of line bundles L, by E=L^direct_sum N. If E is required to be globally free, retain the corresponding trivialization condition on that direct sum. Over a local base L is free. Choosing a source vector v trivializing L, with Av=v, makes Theta a canonical ordinary basis and removes all its automorphisms. Without that vector marking the remaining automorphisms are precisely multiplication by a central unit on L. The cyclic hypothesis is automatic near the actual root source. Indeed at a primitive Q_N the actual multiplicative relation reduces to BP=Q_N PB. If Bv=v, the N vectors P^jv have distinct eigenvalues Q_N^j. They are nonzero and independent over every residue field. Rank N makes them a basis. In a local deformation of that root point their determinant stays a unit, proving (2.2). This does not assert cyclicity on unrelated global components. ## 3. The multiplicative defect and its explicit flat saturation Suppose also that R is a rank-one idempotent with AR=R, RA=A, BPB^-1P^-1=Q[I+(Q^-N-1)R]. (3.1) The image of its commutator lies in im R=L, so Section 2 applies. In its canonical frame R=e_0 rho with rho_0=1. Equations (1.1) and (3.1) reduce EXACTLY to delta (R-E_0)=0, delta rho_j=0, 1<=j<N. (3.2) If the base is flat over the normal parameter, or more generally delta is a nonzero divisor on it, (3.2) forces R=E_0. This is the actual normalized defect, recovered before taking jets. The unsaturated presentation has the explicit coordinate algebra R_base[rho_1,...,rho_(N-1)]/(delta rho_j). (3.3) When delta is a nonzero divisor on R_base, this presentation is not flat at the wall. Its delta-saturation kills the rho_j and is just R_base. If the supplied base already has delta-torsion, saturation also removes that base torsion. At delta=0 alone the multiplicative relation cannot see these projector-row parameters. A rank-N module can be locally free over this nonflat comparison base; that is not a substitute for flatness/saturation of the base over the normal parameter. If the module itself is flat over that normal base, the nonzero-divisor hypothesis above applies. If R is marked to be the actual E_0, these excess parameters never arise. ## 4. The whole endpoint-corrected algebra is a matrix algebra Set chi(X)=product_(j=0)^(N-1)(X-Q^j), D=R[X]/chi(X), e_j(X)=product_(k!=j)(X-Q^k)/(Q^j-Q^k). The node differences are units in the stated head localization. Evaluation at them identifies D with R^N: the e_j are orthogonal idempotents summing to one. The polynomial map tau(X)=Q^-1[X-delta e_0(X)] (4.1) cycles these evaluations, so it is an algebra automorphism with tau^N=I and tau(e_j)=e_(j+1 mod N). Form the explicit algebra with basis f P^a, f in D, 0<=a<N, and multiplication (f P^a)(g P^b)=f tau^a(g)P^(a+b mod N). (4.2) Associativity follows from tau being an automorphism. Define E_(i,j)=e_i P^(i-j mod N). These satisfy E_(i,j)E_(k,l)=delta_(j,k)E_(i,l), sum_i E_(i,i)=I. They form a basis: fixing i,a recovers e_iP^a uniquely. Therefore (4.2) is EXACTLY Mat_N(R), with no rank comparison or unverified quiver theorem as a premise. The original source is recovered by A_0=e_0 sum_(j=0)^(N-1)P^j, Tr(A_0)=1. (4.3) Thus the original paired-source matrix can be recovered from the flat normalized defect and cyclic transport; the defect and source rows remain different. Every coefficient, root norm and endpoint term is retained in (4.1), rather than imposing an impossible whole BP=QPB with P^N=I. This adds the explicit finite ALIGNED SOURCE classification and whole matrix-algebra presentation to the boundary note. It does not duplicate or contradict [the whole clock function theorem](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md). That theorem concerns the UNCORRECTED infinite-order shift on a coalescing clock and requires its endpoint tower. Here the nodes Q^j are distinct at each fixed primitive root, and (4.1) changes the last shift by its actual finite endpoint defect. A fixed-N head localization is not a common neighborhood of Log Q=0 as N grows. This finite algebra does not discard whole functions, unwrapped Green tails or their separate source extension. ## 5. Rank one without source alignment is insufficient There are flat rational families through the actual N=2 root which satisfy every OTHER condition but are not the canonical clock. Put near Q=-1 delta=1-Q^2, h=Q-Q^-1, t=delta/(1-delta^2), x=delta^2/(1-delta^2), P=[[0,1],[1,0]], A=[[1,1],[0,0]], B=[[1,t h],[0,Q+x h]], R=[[1+x,-t],[t,-x]]. (5.1) All entries are rational and regular there; B is invertible. Since t^2=x(1+x), direct multiplication proves R^2=R, Tr R=1, rank R=1, BA=A, AP=A, P^2=I, BPB^-1P^-1=Q[I+(Q^-2-1)R]. (5.2) At Q=-1 these are EXACTLY B_0,P_0,A_0,E_0. Nevertheless the second eigenvalue Q+xh of B is generically different from Q, so no conjugation can identify it with B_0. The rank-N module and every displayed rational family are flat. What fails is AR=R, namely alignment of the moving defect with the actual source line. Even correct classical source/defect markings and flatness of the objects do not impose that whole relation. Taking delta replaced by delta^k in x,t makes the tilt invisible to an arbitrarily long fixed jet, without changing this conclusion. The ACTUAL fixed E_00 defect is aligned and is covered by the positive theorem, not by this counterexample. ## 6. The scalar closed period is not fixed by this frame Over any base the commutant of the matrix units in Section 4 consists of scalars: commuting with E_ii makes a matrix diagonal, and commuting with E_ij makes all its diagonal entries equal. Consequently a closed frame-intertwiner is C=c I, Tr(A_0 C)=c, (6.1) with c an ARBITRARY scalar (a unit if C is invertible). Adjoining c, or an invertible c, gives a flat finite-type extension with the exact same frame, defect and normalized source. Source-frame classification alone imposes no equation on that period. It also does not supply a regulator action or fix a leading norm. This is a statement about insufficient structural conditions, not permission to change the original actual knot state. Once the complete actual crossing word and every scalar/cap/peripheral normalization are supplied, that word fixes c. A comparison of the FULL word evaluations through the canonical source frame preserves it automatically. Merely identifying their clock/source matrix algebras does not compare their selected word sections. There is no contradiction with strict vector-pointed rigidity. An intertwiner C preserving a specified nonzero v must satisfy cv=v and hence c=1. A generic actual knot period C=cI is NOT such a source-vector-preserving automorphism; it preserves the coupon A by conjugation while its cut pairing is c. Demanding strict preservation at that final step would assume the desired normalization and exclude the actual nontrivial period. Here the actual scalar-knot example is on its original ROOT fiber with generic M. Its whole auxiliary q-normal lift need not be scalar, as the explicit unknot in [the one-index source audit](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) shows. No extension of root scalarity is used in this argument. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_flat_cyclic_source_frame.py) and [saved results](../experiments/flat_cyclic_source_frame_results.json) check the universal recurrence equations, all matrix units/source moments, arbitrary conjugate frames, wall parameters and the explicit nonaligned rational family. No geometric selected-cycle or hyperbolic-volume theorem follows from this finite-frame result. The [independent proof audit](mobius_and_flat_source_frame_independent_audit.md) checks the commutative-base classification, corrected crossed product, saturation scope and nonaligned counterexample. It also distinguishes the actual root scalar closure from its auxiliary whole q-normal lift.

title: A flat pointed torsor lifts; an etale classical optimizer need not
text:
# A flat pointed torsor lifts; an etale classical optimizer need not Independent proof and audit, 27 October 2026. This adds a constructive comparison formula and a flatness criterion to [whole cyclotomic reconstruction](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md). It also gives rational quantum objects for which a unique reduced classical pointed comparison fails to lift. Thus it distinguishes an actual sufficient theorem from an implication that classical Rivin rigidity alone does not supply. The fixed-meridian Rees Poisson map and its new whole Heisenberg primitive are checked in Section 5. Section 6 gives a concrete actual crossing obstruction to a naive positive weighted-norm proof. None of the statements below asserts the selected volume asymptotic. ## 1. A flat marked comparison has exactly one lift Let \(R=k[[\epsilon]]\), with \(k\) of characteristic zero. Suppose a whole, bounded algebraic comparison problem has been specified, including its sources, cuts and lattice. Complete its comparison algebra at a chosen classical point and call the resulting \(R\)-algebra \(B\). Assume \[ B/\epsilon B=k,\qquad  igcap_{n\geq 0}\epsilon^nB=0, \qquad \epsilon	ext{ is a nonzero divisor on }B. 	ag{1} \] Then \(R\longrightarrow B\) is an isomorphism. In particular the marked comparison exists uniquely to every formal quantum order. Here is a direct proof. Given \(b\in B\), choose its residue \(c_0\in k\) and write \(b=c_0+\epsilon b_1\). Repeat this for \(b_1\), obtaining \[ b-\sum_{j<n}c_j\epsilon^j\in\epsilon^nB. \] The element \(f=\sum c_j\epsilon^j\in R\) therefore maps to \(b\), by separatedness. Thus \(R	o B\) is surjective. A nonzero element of its kernel would be \(\epsilon^m\) times a unit, contradicting the last condition of (1) and \(B/\epsilon B
e0\). This proves the assertion. Over this DVR, the last condition is exactly \(R\)-flatness. A finite separable marked classical residue field is handled after its specified unramified base extension. With a finite algebraic presentation, this is a statement about its selected algebraic formal germ; it does not assert that an arbitrary formal period is algebraic. The same result retains several normal directions. Let \(R\) be any complete Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\) and residue field \(k\). If \(B\) is separated for \(\mathfrak mB\), is \(R\)-flat, and \(B/\mathfrak mB=k\) through the specified residue map, then \(B=R\). Choose generators of \(\mathfrak m\) and repeat the residue argument by total degree; completeness of \(R\) and separatedness of \(B\) give \(B=R/I\), \(I\subseteq\mathfrak m\).
