Flatness, applied to \(0	o I	o R\) and tensoring with \(B\), forces \(I/I^2=0\). Since \(I\) is finitely generated and \(I=I^2\subseteq\mathfrak mI\), Nakayama gives \(I=0\). Thus quantum and meridian normals can be retained together. There is a useful converse formulation. The first two conditions already imply \(B=R/I\). If comparisons exist modulo \(\epsilon^n\) for every \(n\), the maps \(R/I	o R/\epsilon^n\) give \(I\subseteq(\epsilon^n)\) for all \(n\); hence \(I=0\). No additional choice of compatible lifts is needed once the pointed comparison is unique. Comparisons at several different cyclotomic levels become such a test only after a fixed whole presentation and the reconstruction hypotheses have been supplied. This is a genuine existence theorem for a flat whole pointed comparison. Flatness of the two objects separately is a different condition. ## 2. Cyclic pointing constructs the only possible comparison Here the comparison need not be guessed. Let \(A\) be a coefficient algebra with an automorphism \(\sigma\). Let \(V_i=A^r\) carry the semilinear transport \(T_i(v)=A_i\sigma(v)\), source \(s_i\), and cut \(\ell_i\), for \(i=1,2\). Form the cyclic matrices \[ V_i^{\mathrm{cyc}}=[s_i,T_i s_i,\ldots,T_i^{r-1}s_i]. \] Assume their determinants are units on the marked lattice chart. Define \[ C=V_2^{\mathrm{cyc}}(V_1^{\mathrm{cyc}})^{-1},\qquad a_i=(V_i^{\mathrm{cyc}})^{-1}T_i^r s_i,\qquad m_i=\ell_i V_i^{\mathrm{cyc}}. 	ag{2} \] Then \(C\) and its inverse are regular on that chart, and \[ CT_1=T_2C,\quad Cs_1=s_2,\quad\ell_2C=\ell_1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a_1=a_2,\quad m_1=m_2. 	ag{3} \] Moreover \(C\) is the only pointed transport comparison. Indeed every such comparison must send each \(T_1^j s_1\) to \(T_2^j s_2\), which forces (2). Its transport residual vanishes on the first \(r-1\) cyclic vectors. On the last vector it vanishes exactly when their last cyclic relations \(a_i\) agree. Equivalently, \[ A_i\sigma(V_i^{\mathrm{cyc}})=V_i^{\mathrm{cyc}}\operatorname{Comp}(a_i); \] substituting (2) proves the transport identity. The cut identity is exactly equality of the two rows \(m_i\). Consequently, near a regular cyclic classical comparison, its whole comparison algebra is \[ B=R/I,\qquad I=(	ext{entries of }a_1-a_2,\ m_1-m_2), 	ag{4} \] with additional supplied connection residuals included if required. This makes the flatness defect an explicit finite obstruction ideal. Classical agreement says only \(I\subseteq(\epsilon)\); flatness says \(I=0\). If the objects and these finitely many iterates have a fixed bounded algebraic presentation, the [cyclotomic jet theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) tests the residuals in (3), after denominators and algebraic norms are handled in the stated lattice. Thus a regular cyclic source gives a canonical comparison and a finite exact certificate. There is no unknown unbounded family of levelwise gauges in this construction. The hypotheses are substantive: the rank must be fixed for a uniform test, both cyclic determinants must be units, and the whole transports and pointings must already exist. Generic cyclicity away from a source boundary does not imply these unit conditions. The full finite \(N\)-dimensional module and a rank-one local geometric block are also not interchangeable objects. For compatible differential period connections, horizontality can follow from this uniqueness. If the connections commute with transport, and the two source connection laws agree under \(C\), then \(E=
abla_2C-C
abla_1\) commutes with transport and kills the source. It kills every cyclic vector, so \(E=0\). For the mixed quantum and meridian law, the extra meridian intertwining in [the whole comparison theorem, Section 5](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) is required. This argument does not construct either connection. ## 3. Two explicit failures of classical-to-quantum lifting ### Flat objects with a nonflat pointed comparison Take rank-one free \(R\)-modules, with transports \(T_1=1\) and \(T_2=1+\epsilon\), and sources \(s_1=s_2=1\). Both objects are flat. A source-preserving comparison is forced to be \(C=1\), so its remaining equation is \(\epsilon=0\). Its comparison algebra is \(R/(\epsilon)\). There is one reduced classical pointed comparison and no quantum lift. The same example works for meridian-difference transports \(T_1=\sigma\), \(T_2=(1+\epsilon)\sigma\) over \(k(Y)[[\epsilon]]\), with \(\sigma(Y)=e^\epsilon Y\). It has the same classical graph \(L=1\), etale over \(Y\). Thus etaleness of that graph and flatness of the objects do not imply flatness of their pointed comparison. ### Even the unpointed algebraic gauge can fail Put \(Q=e^\epsilon\), \(\sigma(Y)=QY\), and compare the rank-one transport multipliers \[ a_1(Q,Y)=1,\qquad a_2(Q,Y)=1+ rac{Q-1}{Y}. 	ag{5} \] They are rational whole functions, regular formally at \(Q=1\), with the same classical etale graph \(L=1\). An algebraic formal unit solving the gauge equation \(\sigma g=a_2g\), with leading term \(g_0\), would satisfy \[ Y\partial_Yg_0=g_0/Y,\qquad d\log g_0=dY/Y^2. 	ag{6} \] This is impossible on every finite algebraic cover. A logarithmic derivative of an algebraic meromorphic function has only simple poles. At a place \(Y=t^e\), the right side of (6) has pole order \(e+1>1\). The analytic solution \(g_0=\exp(-1/Y)\) demonstrates precisely the excluded irregularity. Multiplying both multipliers by any common nonzero rational \(a_0(Y)\) gives the same failure over the graph \(L=a_0(Y)\). The issue is therefore not the particular constant classical graph. At first quantum order, the difference of subprincipal transport defines the necessary logarithmic connection (6); classical etaleness does not trivialize that connection. The full cyclic norm detects the failure exactly: \[ \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}a_2(Q_N,Q_N^jY) =1-\left(- rac{Q_N-1}{Y}ight)^N
e1. 	ag{7} \] For fixed \(Y
e0\), its difference from one is smaller than every power of \(1/N\). Thus even this rational transport produces a curvature error invisible to its asymptotic \(1/N\) expansion. It is visible to the *exact* whole cyclotomic test. In the opposite direction, the independently proved [full rank-one descent theorem](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md) does give a positive result: a comparison multiplier in \(\mathbb Q(Q,Y)^*\), with exact whole norm one at every sufficiently large root, has one rational gauge. Other coefficient fields require the whole-root marking in that theorem. Its source anchor fixes the residual scalar, provided the gauge and inverse are regular on the prescribed source lattice. Equations (5)--(7) explain why the whole norm hypothesis cannot be replaced by a classical optimizer or an all-orders asymptotic norm identity. ## 4. The actual Rees source has a concrete regular-lifting obstruction The [actual Rees construction](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md) has block clock \(D_Zf(u)=f(Zu)\), \(Z=Q^N\), and \[ G^{-1}D_ZG=e^{u/N}D_Z,\qquad G=e^{u/[N(Z-1)]}. 	ag{8} \] The original vacuum is fixed by \(D_Z\). There is no regular clock intertwiner sending this vacuum to a nonzero regular limiting vector. For such an intertwiner \(C\), applying (8) to the vacuum and reducing at \(Z=1\) would give \[ (e^{u/N}-1)\,C_0(1)=0 \quad	ext{in }k[[u]], \] so \(C_0(1)=0\). Allowing mixing among head clocks does not help: the equations become \((Q_N^j e^{u/N}-1)f_j(u)=0\), and each factor is a nonzero divisor. The exact irregular gauge instead sends the source to \(e^{-u/[N(Z-1)]}\), as retained in that note. This is not a claim that two identical whole-center families are inequivalent: their normal central characters differ, and the source gauge is explicitly irregular. It is a concrete warning that a regular generator-module limit and matching closed-point data do not produce a regular pointed lift through the source boundary. The newly regular Rees module has not silently made the comparison algebra flat. ## 5. Independent check of the Rees Poisson and period formulas The new Sections 6--7 of [the Rees module note](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md) are sound. With \(d=N(Q^N-1)\), \[ (Q^{N^2}-1)/d\longrightarrow1,\qquad (Q^{-N^2}-1)/d\longrightarrow-1. \] They give \(\{k,e\}=ke,\ \{k,f\}=-kf\); the actual universal Casimir gives \(\{e,f\}=k^{-1}-k\). For \(\{p,u\}=1\), \[ U=e^{up},\quad k=\gamma M^N/U,\quad e=p\gamma(M^N/U-M^{-N}),\quad f=(1-U)/p \] has exactly these brackets, and \[ du\wedge dp=d\log U\wedge d\log p =-d\log k\wedge d\log e. \] At \(M=1\), \(v=1/p,w=e/\gamma\) gives \(\Omega=dw\wedge dv/(1+wv)\), with the stated regular E-wrap limit \(w/N\). The fixed-root normal \(d\) remains distinct from the physical \(2\pi i/N\). The new [whole Gauss period transgression](rees_gauss_period_transgression.md) also checks. For \(B=M^N,t=U/B^2\), its four period coordinates satisfy the flat algebraic connection \[ d\mu=dB/B,\quad d\xi=dt/t,\quad d\ell=-dt/(1-t),\quad dH=\xi\,d\ell. \] This is a fixed Heisenberg times additive-logarithm torsor, before level restriction. With \(x=\xi+2\mu\), \[ W=H+2\mu\ell-x^2/2,\qquad 	heta_{\mathrm{Gauss}}-	heta_{\mathrm{source}} =dW+(x-2\ell)d\mu . \] Both the sign and the peripheral correction follow by direct differentiation. The resolved \(M=1\) primitives have exterior derivative \(dw\wedge dv/(1+wv)\); their difference is the derivative of the stated regular \(W-\operatorname{Li}_2(1)\). This is an actual local period connection, not merely matching symplectic dimensions. Its existence does not by itself prove a flat pointed comparison with the irregular selected source. ## 6. Scalarity does not make a positive weighted norm sharp There is an actual crossing example, requiring no speculative analytic sector. Close one leg of a positive checked crossing at complete color \(M=1\). This is the framed unknot kink. Write \[ Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad x=-q^{-1}, \qquad P_a(Q)=(Q;Q)_a. \] At fixed cut index \(a\), closure forces the crossing index \(k=a-b\), \(0\le b\le a\). Substituting the actual balanced crossing and pivot gives the diagonal cut terms \[ x^{1-N}\, Q^{b^2} rac{P_a(Q)^2}{P_b(Q)^2P_{a-b}(Q)}. 	ag{9} \] For clarity, the unsubstituted crossing coefficient is \[ (-1)^kq^{k^2} \left[\prod_{j=b+1}^{a}(Q^{-j}-1)ight] {a rack k}_Q\, x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}\, (xQ^{-b})^{1-N}; \] elementary cancellation gives (9), including its phase. The exact finite identity \[ \sum_{b=0}^{a} Q^{b^2} rac{P_a(Q)^2}{P_b(Q)^2P_{a-b}(Q)}=1 	ag{10} \] can be proved without importing a knot formula. Partitions with largest part at most \(a\) have generating function \(1/P_a\). Separate them by their Durfee square of size \(b\). Its weight is \(Q^{b^2}\); the part below it has generating function \(1/P_b\), and the rectangle to its right has generating polynomial \({a rack b}_Q=P_a/(P_bP_{a-b})\). This proves (10) as a formal rational identity, hence at every root with \(a<N\). The exact kink scalar is \(x^{1-N}\), of modulus one. Nevertheless, if \(4\mid N\), \(a=N/2,b=N/4\), the modulus of this one closed term is \[  rac{P(N/2)^2}{P(N/4)^3},\qquad P(m)=\prod_{r=1}^{m}2\sin(\pi r/N). \] The integrable logarithmic Riemann sum gives \[ \lim_{4\mid N	o\infty} rac1N\log|	ext{term}| = rac{3\,G}{2\pi}>0, 	ag{11} \] where \(G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2\). Indeed \(\int_0^{1/2}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt=0\) and \(\int_0^{1/4}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt=-G/(2\pi)\). Every internal diagonal basis weight cancels around this closed term; a normalized cut basis vector and its dual cancel their external weight too. Thus any bound obtained by replacing all entries by absolute values, including products of induced coordinate weighted norms, is at least this exponentially large term. It cannot be sharp for the unit scalar (10). This does not rule out a specially chosen wavepacket or a phase-sensitive propagation theorem. For this kink, the cut \(a=0\) is already cancellation-free. It does show why scalarity alone and strict concavity of a classical shape functional do not supply the required sharp positive norm for an arbitrary normalized source. A useful coherent-state argument must prove its phase-sensitive propagation and stability through the actual crossings and caps, rather than infer them from the algebraic optimizer. ## 7. The concrete whole-torsor task There is now a precise positive route: construct the two whole pointed objects, prove regular cyclicity on their marked lattices, and evaluate the finite residuals (3). A flat comparison algebra, or sufficiently deep exact cyclotomic tests in the fixed presentation, then gives the unique comparison; a compatible marked connection gives horizontality. Rivin rigidity supplies the unique algebraic geometric place. The new Rees--Gauss identity supplies a fixed algebraic period connection on actual source coordinates. Neither presently implies the comparison-flatness or removes the irregular projectors. Those are explicit equations and source conditions to prove. Even after that algebraic comparison, the physical large-level norm requires a calibrated nonzero selected contribution and its growth estimate.

title: A strict Fock-to-cyclic-normal Mellin map and its logarithmic obstruction
text: # A strict Fock-to-cyclic-normal Mellin map and its logarithmic obstruction Research construction, 27 October 2026. This gives an explicit linear comparison from the actual completed Fock source to the whole cyclic normal source, including its Weyl operators, cut, pivot adapter and relative endpoint carry. The target must retain a marked logarithmic torsor. A global algebraic comparison with the same nonzero vacuum and normal derivative is impossible on every finite cover. The comparison below is between specified source/normal complexes. It is not an algebra map of fixed-N matrix algebras and does not identify their full quantum-group actions. It also does not fix the physical 2pi*i adapter required for a geometric Fourier integral. ## 1. The two actual source modules and the explicit map Fix a primitive N-th root Q in characteristic zero. In [the common-Verma source](common_verma_two_wall_source.md), write the completed Fock module as Fhat=H[[t]], h_j t^r/r!=v_(rN+j), B=partial_t, T=t, [B,T]=I, 0<=j<N. Here H is the original balanced finite head, with source psi=1 and co-source phi=(1/N)sum_j. Its block vacuum projection is pi_0. Retain the whole cyclic normal algebra and physical derivative: Chat=k[[U-1]][A]/(A^N-U), D_phys=A partial_A+N U partial_U, nabla=D_phys/N. Mark alpha(U)^N=U, alpha(1)=1. Put u=Log U, u(1)=0, and epsilon_j=(1/N)sum_(l=0)^(N-1)Q^(-jl)(A/alpha)^l. These are mutually orthogonal idempotents summing to one. They evaluate to delta_(j,a) on A=alpha Q^a, and nabla epsilon_j=0. The literal topological linear isomorphism is M(v_(rN+j))=epsilon_j u^r/r!. (1.1) It is invertible because the epsilon_j form a basis over k[[U-1]] and u is a formal parameter with first coefficient U-1. Directly, M B=nabla M, M T=(Log U)M, M theta_s(h_j)=epsilon_j U^s. (1.2) Thus all integer resonant sectors U^k are present as the images of coherent kernels theta_k. They are functions of the whole normal U, rather than being set to one before transport. This is an exact normal polarization comparison. It does not say that the actual clock q-normal, block-number operator T B, and nabla are the same operator. In particular M(T B)=u nabla M; other current directions must be transported with their own marked operator adapters, not inferred from (1.2). ## 2. The original cut and its normal pivot line are preserved Let tau=Tr_(Chat/k[[U-1]])/N. The canonical A-power basis gives tau(f)=f_0(U), and tau(epsilon_j)=1/N. Hence [tau M(f)]_(U=1)=phi pi_0(f), M(psi)=1, tau nabla=U partial_U tau. (2.1) There are two different source projectors. The coefficientwise extension e_H tensor I is carried to f |->tau(f)1, retaining every normal coefficient. The actual finite-rank ambient coupon Gamma=i e_H pi_0 is instead carried to f |-> [tau(f)]_(U=1) 1. They agree on the vacuum but not on its first normal. In particular the first projector commutes with nabla, whereas [nabla,Gamma_U]f=-[tau(nabla f)]_(U=1)1. (2.2) This is the additional finite normal cut row. It cannot be discarded by identifying the whole-normal and finite-vacuum projectors. These are strict linear cut comparisons, without identifying matrix composition with scalar coefficient multiplication. The root pivot also has two distinct whole-normal lifts. With K_U=xA^(-1), define g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1), g_lit=K_U^(1-N)=U g_red, D_red=g_red^(-1)e, D_lit=U^(-1)D_red. (2.3) The reduced representative agrees with the original pivot on U=1. Only g_lit is its literal clock power off that fiber. In the horizontal epsilon frame the exact adapters are g_red=alpha^(-1) M g_H M^(-1), D_red=alpha M D_H M^(-1), g_lit=alpha^(N-1) M g_H M^(-1), D_lit=alpha^(1-N) M D_H M^(-1). (2.4) Thus their physical normal derivatives differ: D_phys(g_red)=-g_red, D_phys(D_red)=D_red, D_phys(g_lit)=(N-1)g_lit, D_phys(D_lit)=-(N-1)D_lit. Both products are exactly e and horizontal. The adapter U and its first derivative remain part of a comparison of the two lifts; the common root value does not identify their normal phases. The full external d_N(M) line is unchanged and remains distinct from this internal U normal. The underlying full quantum modules are not identified: for example the uncorrected cyclic operator (1-A)S^(-1) has N-th power 1-U, whereas the root balanced head F has N-th power zero. The map (1.1) does not suppress that endpoint source or claim to intertwine these two different F actions. ## 3. An explicit relative source-chain map with endpoint U Use an independent source-centralizer coordinate sigma with marked endpoints zero and one. Keep it distinct from any physical geometric framing parameter. On Fhat-valued series define the twisted relative complex P=H[sigma][[t]], R_T^1=P, R_T^2=P direct_sum Fhat direct_sum Fhat, delta_T h=((partial_sigma-T)h,h(0),h(1)). Every t coefficient in P is polynomial in sigma; endpoint evaluation and antiderivation are therefore defined coefficientwise. The t-adic completion permits exp(sigma T) while retaining those endpoint maps. Conjugation by exp(sigma T), with exp(T) at the second endpoint, identifies this complex with the ordinary relative source complex. Its transgression is L_T(a,b_0,b_1) =integral_0^1 exp(-sigma T)a(sigma)dsigma -exp(-T)b_1+b_0. (3.1) The inclusion is f |->(exp(sigma T)f,0,0). Both identities L_T delta_T=0 and L_T i_T=I follow by differentiating exp(-sigma T)h(sigma). They hold before applying any cut. Applying M coefficientwise gives a strict isomorphism to the whole-normal complex delta_U h=((partial_sigma-Log U)h,h(0),h(1)), L_U(a,b_0,b_1) =integral_0^1 U^(-sigma)a(sigma)dsigma -U^(-1)b_1+b_0. (3.2) The coherent inclusion becomes f |->(U^sigma f,0,0). The endpoint carry is literally U. It has not disappeared through specialization of A^N=1. The whole averaged co-source and its residue realization from (2.1) commute with this chain map. The original finite cut is obtained after evaluation U=1; its normal derivative requires the extra row (2.2), rather than a horizontal vacuum assumption. There is also an exact compatible normal connection on the entire relative complex. On degree one it is B-sigma. On degree two it is (B-sigma,B,B-1). These commute with delta_T because [B-sigma,partial_sigma-T]=0. Under M they are (nabla-sigma) and (nabla-sigma,nabla,nabla-1), respectively. Transgression carries them to B and nabla. Using bare B without the sigma term would give curvature -I and would be incorrect. This is an explicit Heisenberg normal/source complex, not a conditional lifting argument. ## 4. The logarithmic torsor is necessary, not a finite-cover choice The completed map (1.1) has a global version only after adjoining the marked logarithmic torsor of U. On any simply connected marked sheet, nabla(Log U)=1 and all formulas above are actual functions. Changing the logarithm shifts its additive torsor coordinate. There is a sharp obstruction to replacing it by algebraic functions. Suppose a linear comparison into the algebraic whole-normal field, or any finite algebraic cover, intertwines B with nabla and carries some vacuum h to a nonzero horizontal value c. Since B(Th)=h, its image f would satisfy U partial_U f=c. After applying a constant component functional if necessary, c is a nonzero constant. Thus df=c dU/U. At a zero or pole of U on the normalized compact curve, its right side has nonzero residue. An exact differential of an algebraic function has zero residues. Finite covers multiply that residue by a positive ramification index and cannot remove it. This contradiction proves that no such nonzero vacuum/cut-preserving algebraic linear map exists. The obstruction already appears on the first excited Fock vector; it is not an asymptotic or high-jet problem. It also does not contradict (1.1): Log U is a valid formal function at U=1. The required common object is a marked logarithmic differential torsor, rather than only a finite algebraic source cover. It can be presented as the algebraic bundle with coordinate t and connection dt=dU/U; the obstruction is to an algebraic horizontal section, not to the existence of that bundle. ## 5. Relation to the actual two-dimensional divided-adjoint orbit The explicit divided-adjoint source orbit and its marked geometric framing chart are proved in [the framing-orbit note](divided_source_framing_orbit.md). With its coordinates v=a Ubar+bW, z=a+b, the map is r=a/z, s_geo=z^(-2), A_cut=z^2/(1+z^2), tau_geo=r/s_geo=a z, Omega_cut=d tau_geo wedge dlog A_cut. (5.1) This establishes an explicit bare group/form comparison. It does not identify the source-relative sigma in Section 3 with tau_geo at the physical quantum scale. If u=Log U=N Log A_cut, then Omega_cut=(1/N)d tau_geo wedge du. At H_N=2pi*i/N, a geometric Fourier phase tau_geo Log A_cut/H_N is tau_geo u/(2pi*i). Matching it with the source kernel exp(s_Fock u) would therefore require s_Fock=tau_geo/(2pi*i), changing the unit source endpoint U to U^(1/(2pi*i)). A marked residue/phase adapter is required before claiming such a physical polarization identity. There is also a direct source-collapse limitation. On a diagonal cut matrix C the normalized raw orbit insertion is Phi(Cv)/Phi(v) =(a/z)/(N-1) sum_(j<N-1) C_jj+(b/z)C_(N-1,N-1). It depends only on a/z. Thus the two orbit parameters do not by themselves become two independently measured internal framing coordinates of the scalar partial knot state. The whole-normal and relative current data above are necessary to retain the additional direction before collapse. ## 6. What is new here and what remains The earlier first-quantum-normal and source/monodromy notes give the actual module/cokernel connection, its source, and the normal lattice cut. The relative-framing note realizes the finite boundary cut as a residue complex. They do not contain the explicit Fock Mellin map (1.1), its endpoint-U relative chain map (3.2), or the global algebraic obstruction in Section 4. Those maps now compare the actual Fock and whole-normal boundary objects directly, retaining both the reduced pivot lift and literal clock-power lift with their exact U adapter, the distinct finite- vacuum cut row, and every endpoint factor. They do not prove that a computed geometric Gaussian class has the original selected image under this map. Its extension through the actual source boundary, the physical 2pi*i adapter and global period coefficient remain separate requirements. No regulator volume identity is inferred. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.py). [Results](../experiments/fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map_results.json). # Independent audit of the normal Mellin and full Green maps Audit, 27 October 2026. The normal Mellin map and relative connection are sound. The revised Mellin section 2 and residual normal-current section 6 explicitly retain both pivot lifts and both projector extensions, with their correct normal rows. There is no outstanding correction. The full discrete Green/current calculation is sound and does not assert cancellation of the remaining geometric boundary terms. No test reruns were needed. ## 1. The strict normal Mellin map For \(A^N=U\), \[ D_{\mathrm{phys}}=A\partial_A+NU\partial_U \] preserves the relation, and \(
abla=D_{\mathrm{phys}}/N\) has \(
abla\operatorname{Log} U=1\). With the marked \(\alpha^N=U\), the elements \(A/\alpha\), hence every \(\epsilon_j\), are horizontal. The map \[ v_{rN+j}\longmapsto\epsilon_j(\operatorname{Log} U)^r/r! \] is therefore a topological linear isomorphism carrying \(B\) to \(
abla\), \(T\) to multiplication by \(\operatorname{Log} U\), and the coherent kernel to \(\epsilon_jU^s\). The averaged trace and its \(U=1\) value give precisely the stated original vacuum cut. There is a useful projector distinction. The coefficientwise extension \(e_H\otimes I\) maps to \(f\mapsto	au(f)1\). The finite-rank ambient coupon \(i e_H\pi_0\) instead maps to \(f\mapsto[	au(f)]_{U=1}1\). Both recover the same head cut; their whole-normal extensions are different. The revised finite-vacuum row is exactly \[ [
abla,\Gamma_U]f=-[	au(
abla f)]_{U=1}1: \] the derivative of the constant output of \(\Gamma_U\) is zero, while \(\Gamma_U
abla\) is its displayed evaluated trace row. The coefficientwise projector commutes with \(
abla\). For \(\partial_\sigma-T\), the compatible normal direction is \(B-\sigma\): \[ [B-\sigma,\partial_\sigma-T]=0. \] The two scalar commutators cancel with opposite signs. Endpoint evaluation gives the degree-two corrections \((B-\sigma,B,B-1)\), and direct differentiation of \(e^{-\sigma T}h\) proves the transgression formulas. Under Mellin transport the endpoint is exactly \(U\); no specialization to one occurs before this identity. The algebraic primitive obstruction is also valid. A vacuum-preserving intertwiner on an algebraic finite cover would give \(df=c\,dU/U\), \(c
e0\). On the compact normalized curve the right side has nonzero residues at zeros/poles of \(U\), whereas an exact algebraic differential has zero residues. Ramification multiplies rather than kills the residue. The formal logarithmic torsor avoids, rather than contradicts, this global algebraic obstruction. ## 2. Two whole-normal lifts of the finite pivot The displayed formulas in [the Mellin note](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md) are correct for the **root-reduced lift** \[ g_{\mathrm{red}}=x^{1-N}A^{-1},\quad D_{\mathrm{red}}=g_{\mathrm{red}}^{-1}e. \] They have adapters \(\alpha^{-1}\) and \(\alpha\), and physical derivatives \(-g_{\mathrm{red}}\) and \(+D_{\mathrm{red}}\), respectively. The revised note separately retains the literal power of \(K_U=xA^{-1}\): \[ g_{\mathrm{lit}}=K_U^{1-N} =x^{1-N}A^{N-1}=U g_{\mathrm{red}}. \] Its matching defect is \(D_{\mathrm{lit}}=U^{-1}D_{\mathrm{red}}\). The adapters are then \(\alpha^{N-1}\) and \(\alpha^{1-N}\), and \[ D_{\mathrm{phys}}(g_{\mathrm{lit}})=(N-1)g_{\mathrm{lit}},\qquad D_{\mathrm{phys}}(D_{\mathrm{lit}})=(1-N)D_{\mathrm{lit}}. \] Both choices give \(gD=e\) and the same finite source at \(U=1\), but their individual normal jets differ. The revised proof now states this \(U^{\pm1}\) adapter explicitly. Residual normal-current section 6 is consistent with these formulas. The divided Frobenius shift is \(-D_{\mathrm{phys}}\), the averaged trace satisfies \(	au D_{\mathrm{phys}}=NU\partial_U	au\), and its paired matrix row has the same covariance for either lift. Its coefficientwise extension is explicitly separated from \(\Gamma_U\), so the latter's extra finite-vacuum normal derivative has not been dropped. The physical \(2\pi i\) caveat is correct: \(	au_{\mathrm{geo}}\operatorname{Log} A/H_N=	au_{\mathrm{geo}}\operatorname{Log} U/(2\pi i)\). The bare kernel \(U^{s_{\mathrm{Fock}}}\) therefore needs \(s_{\mathrm{Fock}}=	au_{\mathrm{geo}}/(2\pi i)\); its unit endpoint cannot silently be identified with the geometric unit meridian interval. ## 3. The universal Green formula and its signs For \(D_i=S_i-1\), the exact product rule is \[ pD_if=D_i[(S_i^{-1}p)f]+(S_i^{-1}p-p)f. \] Iterating it in the stated word order gives the displayed current formula. For \(p_\alpha=\prod_i inom{k_i}{\alpha_i}\), backward differences of total degree \(>|\alpha|\) vanish; at degree \(|\alpha|\), only \( eta=\alpha\) survives, with value \((-1)^{|\alpha|}\). Using \(PI=0\) moves the divergence sum to the other side, producing exactly the negative sign in the definition of \(J_i\). These are identities on entire zero-extended arrays. The polynomial moment does not lose a support boundary, and all currents remain finite. External Ore operators commute with the index polynomials and internal shifts. ## 4. Transverse pushforward and the unresolved relative boundary The formal current identity follows from the already established interior identity by the same algebraic product rule, with \(k_i=u_i/H\). No separate density argument for polynomial logarithms is needed. The transverse Gaussian translation identity kills the transverse differences even with their insertions; external coordinate/base shifts commute with the recentered Wick construction. Exactly the two stated framing differences remain. For a translated chain, \(\int_\Gamma(F_H^*J-J)=\int_{F_H\Gamma-\Gamma}J\); the Cartan homotopy therefore has the stated boundary sign. Its logarithmic loop changes the index lift by \(2\pi i/H_N=N\), preserving the polynomial-current jump. The complete residual Ward ideal does not set these relative endpoints or carries to zero. Finally, on the actual diagonal one-cut array, \(CW=C_{N-1,N-1}W\). Thus the ordered divided row is exactly that endpoint value, as claimed. This does not create an additional independent framing index. The Green note correctly presents a full scalar certificate with a two-current geometric defect, not a full geometric annihilation or survival theorem.

title: Formal quantum-A periods on the classical curve
text: # Formal quantum-A periods on the classical curve Research note, 25 October 2026. This pursues the norm-torsor and A-curve direction specified in the user's pasted attachment. It constructs the formal branch and its period connection directly from a specified quantum A-operator. It does not assume equality of a root-of-unity central curve D_n with the classical A-curve. The actual Kashaev-period identification and volume conjecture remain unproved. Formal solutions of q-difference equations are existing theory; see the stated coverage of Garoufalidis--Geronimo, [math/0405331](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405331). No proof or analytic asymptotic theorem from that source is used below. The calculations here are coefficient lifting, formal connections, and algebraic local models. No novelty is claimed for formal difference-equation methods. ## 1. A branch lifts by an explicit noncommutative Hensel recursion Normalize the specified operator at q=1 so that its first nonzero h-coefficient has order zero, and write q=exp(h), delta=x*d/dx, sigma_h=exp(h*delta), Ahat=sum_(j=0)^d p_j(h,x)T^j, T f=sigma_h(f)T, p_j(h,x) in C(x)[[h]], P(x,L)=sum_j p_j(0,x)L^j. Suppose C is a normalized component of P=0 with function field k, x nonconstant and L nonzero, on which P_L is nonzero generically. In particular the selected component has multiplicity one. Extend delta to k by delta(L)=-x P_x/P_L. **Formal factor theorem.** There is a unique a(h)=L+h a_1+h^2 a_2+... in k[[h]]^* such that T-a is a right factor of Ahat. All a_j are algebraic functions on C, computed recursively from the operator. For a proof, the right remainder is R(a)=sum_j p_j(h,x)*product_(s=0)^(j-1) sigma_h^s(a). (1.1) Its constant coefficient is P(x,L)=0. Once a_1,...,a_(n-1) are known, its coefficient at h^n is P_L(x,L)*a_n + known_n. Every shift of h^n a_n agrees with h^n a_n modulo h^(n+1), which proves the displayed coefficient. Set a_n=-known_n/P_L. Formal right division by the monic T-a then gives Ahat=Qhat*(T-a). (1.2) This is an intrinsic branch of the given operator, rather than a new quantization selected for its growth. A noncharacteristic left multiple Bhat*Ahat has the same lifted branch: its symbol factor B_0(x,L) is a unit in k, so uniqueness in (1.1) applies again. A change of cyclic generator by a finite operator C(T) gives, on this branch, multiplication by the scalar obtained by the same remainder formula (1.1), with C in place of Ahat. When C_0(x,L) is nonzero this is a unit of k[[h]]. Thus the gauge law below also handles noncharacteristic changes of cyclic generator. The hypothesis that P contains the geometric classical A-component still has to be justified for the actual knot operator. This theorem does not prove an AJ statement. ## 2. The resulting period connection and its gauge law Choose a local logarithm v=Log L and put u=Log x. The Bernoulli operator defines an exact formal differential Theta_A(h)= [h*delta/(exp(h*delta)-1)] Log a(h) *du =v du+h theta_1+h^2 theta_2+... . (2.1) The quotient means its power series 1-h*delta/2+h^2*delta^2/12-... . The coefficients theta_j for j>=1 are meromorphic algebraic differentials on C. Indeed Log(a/L) has coefficients in k, and delta(Log L)=delta(L)/L belongs to k. Locally a formal solution of sigma_h(psi)=a psi is a horizontal period frame for d log psi=Theta_A(h)/h. (2.2) To verify (2.2), apply exp(h*delta)-1 to log psi. Its formal inverse on derivatives is exactly the Bernoulli series in (2.1). Local primitives supply such frames; their integration constants are additional period data. For a frame change psi -> g psi, g in k[[h]]^*, the ratio changes by a -> a*sigma_h(g)/g. Formula (2.1) gives exactly Theta_A -> Theta_A+h*d log g. (2.3) Thus (2.2) is a well-defined formal line with connection and a torsor of horizontal period frames. Changing the cyclic frame changes its presentation by the usual connection gauge; it does not alter its leading period differential. This also gives a precise formal comparison criterion. For two such ratios a,b with the same leading L, write (Theta_a-Theta_b)/h=omega_0+h omega_1+... . They are equivalent by a unit g in k[[h]]^* exactly when omega_0=d log g_0 for some g_0 in k^*, omega_j=d g_j for some g_j in k, j>=1. (2.4) One direction is (2.3). For the converse take g=g_0 exp(sum_(j>=1)h^j g_j). The comparison is unique up to delta-constant units C[[h]]^*. Equation (2.4) displays the period obstructions explicitly; finite-level Hilbert 90 does not make them vanish automatically for the infinite-order formal shift. ## 3. The first correction retains the operator's ordering Let P_1(x,L)=sum_j [h]p_j(h,x)L^j. Expanding (1.1) gives a_1=-[P_1+(L*delta L/2)P_LL]/P_L, theta_1=[-P_1/(L P_L) -(delta L/2)(P_LL/P_L+1/L)]du. (3.1) Equivalently, putting P_sub=P_1-(x L/2)P_xL, theta_1=-(1/2)d log(L P_L)-P_sub/(L P_L)*du. (3.2) The partial derivatives in P_sub refer to the displayed left-ordered symbol. Formula (3.2) follows by differentiating P_L along C. In the special case P_sub=0, this correction is the square-root line (L P_L)^(-1/2). In general the extra differential is retained. No preferred ordering or vanishing subprincipal term is assumed. ### The actual peripheral normalization includes a difference constant The reduced and modified-trace literature periods satisfy N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M), with f(M)=M-M^(-1), d_N(M)=eta_N f(M)/(M^N-M^(-N)), d_N(qM)/d_N(M)=-f(qM)/f(M), q=exp(pi*i/N). For consistent logarithms let chi=Log(-1). The formal branch ratios therefore give the exact connection-presentation change Theta_modified=Theta_reduced+chi*dlog M+h*dlog f. (3.3) The sign character and the meridian divisor are separate data. In particular the leading classical shift variable changes sign. There is further period data not recovered from this shift ratio. Write u=Log M, h=pi*i/N, and w=exp(2pi*i*u/h)=M^(2N). Then exactly d_N(M)=eta_N f(M) exp(pi*i*u/h)/(w-1). (3.4) The exponential changes sign under u->u+h, while w is invariant. Thus 1/(w-1) is a genuine difference constant. It is outside the coefficientwise meromorphic formal class used in Section 2 and is not removed by that section's Bernoulli inversion. Its pole cancels the zero of f in the whole germ and gives d_N(1)=eta_N/N. This identifies a specific piece of the actual period pointing that a formal branch alone would forget. The [central normalization lemma](algebraic_central_normalization.md) controls factors from a fixed finite algebraic central presentation; it does not supply an unknown global period comparison. The subsequent [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) also shows why a plain uniform branch amplitude for the reduced state would lose essential data at completeness. Exactly F_N=S_N R_N+P_N, where P_N interpolates the ordinary root colors and S_N vanishes at all those orbit points but has value N at Y=1. All ordinary values are polynomially bounded. In particular F_N(q_N)=1 excludes a uniform nonzero geometric WKB amplitude for F_N across M=1,q_N if its complete value has positive exponential growth. The regular period R_N removes this polar/zero structure with the full original gauge retained; its affine source has bounded Laurent support and polynomially bounded coefficients. A norm theorem for R_N is still needed to identify the actual period with the formal geometric branch. ## 4. The leading period is the regulator action, with conversion explicit First center at the marked point: use u=Log(x/x_c), v=Log(L/L_c), and replace the uncentered S by S-(Log L_c)*u. The extracted solution character exp((Log L_c)*u/h) remains explicit; it is not discarded. Now let S denote this centered leading primitive, dS=v du. Suppose the centered geometric peripheral functions used by the regulator obey m/m_c=(x/x_c)^a (L/L_c)^b, l/l_c=(x/x_c)^c (L/L_c)^d, Delta=a*d-b*c !=0. Then U=a u+b v and V=c u+d v. Direct differentiation gives dR=-Delta*(u dv-v du)/4, R=(Delta/2)S-(Delta/4)u v+constant. (4.1) This identifies the leading *differential* of the formal quantum-A period with the central coordinate of the regulator Heisenberg torsor in [the focused formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md). For example, if the geometric holonomies are m=x^2,l=L^2, then Delta=4. At the centered complete point u=v=0, (4.1) gives Im S=(1/2)Vol + Im(constant). (4.2) For the ADO root parameter h=pi*i/N, a period exp(S/h) has (2pi/N)log|exp(S/h)|=2 Im S. Thus these square-holonomy conventions give the required volume coefficient when the marked additive constant agrees. The subsequent [actual longitude/action calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) now proves this peripheral conversion for the actual classical critical correspondence. Its compatible discrete-character lift also fixes Im S=Vol/2 in this q-parameter, without an undetermined imaginary constant. This does not prove that the geometric component survives in the selected sum's minimal operator or its quantum period. Equivalently the [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) uses Y=M^2, step H=Log(q^2)=2h, and S_Q=2S. In (Y,L) the full peripheral exponent determinant is two, and R=S_Q-(Log Y)(Log L)/2. Both conversions give the same marked connection and norm. For other conventions Delta, the constant character, and the root parameter must all be retained. Merely writing the same letters for operator variables and full geometric holonomies would lose a factor. ## 5. Formal lattices at a simple collision The subsequent [geometric rigidity calculation](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) constructs regular formal ratios on the two normalized geometric gluing germs, with distinct slopes at the complete peripheral point. An exact scalarization model then has a classical meridian factor despite having no common local quantum coefficient divisor. Its all-shifts cyclic lattice retains a length-one source at (u,h)=(0,0). This gives an additional reason to keep integral factors and the cyclic generator when comparing the normalized curve with an actual operator. It does not remove the hypotheses on a given operator below. The function-field construction does not by itself allow evaluation where P_L=0. Here is an explicit extension at two common local types. Let t be a uniformizer on the normalization, with x(0),L(0) nonzero, and assume the operator coefficients are regular there. Suppose ord_t(P_L)=1, delta=b(t)t^(-mu)*d/dt, b(0)!=0, mu in {0,1}, L=L_0+O(t). Mu=0 covers an unramified branch through an ordinary double point; mu=1 covers a simple ramification of the x-projection. Then ord_t(a_n) >=-[(mu+2)n-1], n>=1. (5.1) For a proof, delta increases pole order by at most mu+1. In the known h^n remainder, a term with two positive-order a-coefficients has pole order at most (mu+2)n-2. A term with one positive-order coefficient must also contain a derivative or another h-coefficient; the same bound follows. For derivatives of L alone, delta^r L has pole order at most r(mu+1)-1, which also gives this bound. Division by P_L adds at most one. This proves (5.1) by induction. Set w=mu+2 and use the formal weighted chart h=t^w epsilon. Then a=L_0+t*A(t,epsilon), A in C[[t,epsilon]], h*delta=b(t)[t^2 epsilon*d/dt -w*t*epsilon^2*d/depsilon]. (5.2) The second expression acts at fixed h and preserves the power-series ring. Its exponential is a formal automorphism. Since a has nonzero constant term, the rank-one difference module and its lattice extend on this chart. This is an algebraic formal replacement of the poles, not an instruction to evaluate a divergent coefficient at t=0. The chart (5.2) alone does not cover the complete evaluation at fixed nonzero h. It resolves the joint formal degeneration. The other chart must retain the colliding branches, as the next construction shows. ## 6. A rank-two algebraic connection at an ordinary double point Assume the classical symbol has an ordinary double point p=(x_0,L_0), with x_0 L_0 !=0, satisfying P=P_x=P_L=0, P_LL!=0, P_xL^2-P_xx P_LL !=0. (6.1) Use h=tau^2 and x=x_0+tau*s. Extract the constant shift character L_0 from the solution, so T acts on the remaining factor as L_0 exp[tau*(x_0+tau*s)*d/ds]. Taylor expansion of the given operator has zero terms of orders tau^0 and tau^1. Dividing by tau^2 gives a formal differential operator whose leading term is L_node=A_2*d_s^2+B_1*s*d_s+C_2*s^2+D_0, A_2=x_0^2 L_0^2 P_LL(p)/2, B_1=x_0 L_0 P_xL(p), C_2=P_xx(p)/2, D_0=P_1(p). (6.2) All derivatives in this formula are evaluated at p. To check it, expand the coefficients at x_0+tau*s and each j-th shift to order two. The identities P_x=P_L=0 remove the linear terms, and sum_j j^2 p_j L_0^j=L_0^2 P_LL+L_0 P_L gives the second derivative. The mixed coefficient is x_0 L_0 P_xL*s*d_s. This proves (6.2) with the left ordering and quantum first coefficient unchanged. The complete formal operator, normalized by A_2, has the unique factorization L(tau)=U(tau)*[d_s^2+b(s,tau)d_s+c(s,tau)], U(0)=1, b,c in C[s][[tau]], (6.3) where U is a unit in the tau-adic completed differential-operator ring. For the proof, at order tau^n divide the known residual differential operator on the right by the monic leading operator of order two. Its quotient specifies [tau^n]U and its remainder, of order less than two, specifies the tau^n coefficient of b*d_s+c. Ordinary Ore division proves existence and uniqueness recursively. Each step uses polynomial coefficients and a constant nonzero leading coefficient. Thus this branch pair has a free rank-two formal connection lattice, regular at s=0. Other classical roots are excluded by the completion around L_0. The construction is unchanged up to isomorphism by a noncharacteristic left multiple of the original operator. The two slopes alpha of the classical node obey P_LL alpha^2+2P_xL alpha+P_xx=0. The leading quadratic exponent of the corresponding formal periods is alpha*s^2/(2x_0 L_0), exactly the rescaling of the leading action in Section 4. Two period constants are still required at the regular point s=0. The operator does not select their values or the actual knot's combination of branches. ## 7. What this proves toward the requested comparison For any specified operator with the geometric component in its classical symbol, its simple generic branch now has a canonical formal ratio, a gauge-covariant period connection, and the same leading regulator differential after the peripheral conversion. The local construction also retains a colliding pair in a regular rank-two lattice at an ordinary double point. This does not prove that every relevant knot operator has that symbol, that its complete point has only an ordinary double collision, or that the actual selected ADO period realizes the formal geometric branch with the marked normalization. A formal solution does not establish convergence or its root-of-unity evaluation. Multiplication by exp(c/h) already shows why the action constant matters for volume. The next comparison must identify the actual all-level pointed period, with its peripheral lattice, in this A-curve period torsor. The classical regulator fixes what its normalization must be; the present algebra does not prove the identification. The full norm statement in the focused formulation remains unproved. The subsequent [actual normal-period proof](actual_geometric_normal_period.md) constructs a nonzero formal normal block directly from the actual crossing coefficients. Positive gluing rigidity identifies its Hessian radical with the two framing directions, and the quotient of its algebraic Gaussian amplitude with the geometric one gives an all-orders formal gauge. This is additional local coefficient information; it does not prove that the selected sum's minimal operator contains that block or that its actual source and cut select it. Sections 7--8 of that note state the exact role of the ideal triangulation theorem and the remaining source-gauge equation. `experiments/audit_formal_a_curve_torsor.py` checks the noncommutative lifting, first correction, exact gauge law, collision pole bounds, and rank-two local reduction against independent exact factorizations and shift actions. These are diagnostics for the uniform proofs here.

title: Four literature cyclic-dilogarithm atoms for the actual crossing
text: # Four literature cyclic-dilogarithm atoms for the actual crossing Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an exact root-level factorization of the genuine semicyclic holonomy crossing into four literature cyclic quantum dilogarithms. Each atom transports its center; their determinant normalizations and external root factor are explicit. An anchored scalar-rigidity argument fixes the remaining phase. The factorization holds at every N, including even and composite levels. The object being factorized is the actual crossing already identified in [the semicyclic braid proof](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md). Its nilpotent boundary, cut period, pivot, twist and full ADO normalization are retained. This does not assign all colored face/turn data to an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation or prove its selected norm. ## 1. The literature atom, including its determinant Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and N>=2. On a split quantum torus let a primitive monomial m have m^N=w. Choose roots mu^N=w, nu^N=1-w, mu nu !=0. For its eigenvalues mu Q^j define the pointed cyclic function f_0=1, f_j=nu^j/(mu;Q)_j, 0<=j<N. (1.1) Its cyclic recurrence is f_(j+1)/f_j=nu/(1-mu Q^j). The last step is the identity (mu;Q)_N=1-mu^N=nu^N. Spectral idempotents define the matrix C=f(m) without choosing an analytic infinite product. If m acts on an N^2-dimensional two-pair torus, each eigenvalue occurs N times. Put F=product_(j=0)^(N-1) f_j, gamma^N=F^(-1), gamma=1 at mu=0, D_atom=gamma C. (1.2) Then det C=F^N and det D_atom=1. For a general number of spectator pairs the same normalization works by multiplicity. This is exactly the standard alternate cyclic-dilogarithm definition mathfrak_d_N(z;Q)=(1-z^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(ell=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^ell z)^(-ell/N). (1.3) Indeed, writing D_N(z)=product_(ell=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^ell z)^(ell/N), finite cancellation gives F=nu^(-N(N-1)/2) D_N(mu)^N, gamma=nu^((N-1)/2)/D_N(mu), gamma f_j=mathfrak_d_N(mu Q^j;Q). (1.4) Compatible roots are part of the formulas. Include the square roots required by half powers when N is even; no inverse of two modulo N is used. Definition (1.3) is the literature cyclic dilogarithm, not the full ADO dimension d_N(M), which remains a different function. ## 2. An atom is an intertwiner between changing centers Suppose m A=Q^k A m, k integral. Formal compact conjugation has the rational expression r_m(A)=A product_(ell=0)^(k-1)(1-Q^ell m)^(-1), k>0, r_m(A)=A product_(ell=k)^(-1)(1-Q^ell m), k<0. (2.1) The value at k=0 is A. These are finite expressions; after inverting 1-w every factor is invertible at the root. The Nth central power changes by (1-w)^(-k). In the splitting frame take A'=nu^(-k) A. The recurrence (1.1) gives exactly r_m(A) C=C A', r_m(A) D_atom=D_atom A'. (2.2) This proves the atom comparison directly, including composite levels. In particular the atom is not evaluated repeatedly in one frozen central representation. ## 3. The four monomials and the two independent norm factors Use two uniform clock/shift pairs S_i e_a=s_i Q^a e_a, Z_i e_a=z_i e_(a+1), S_i Z_i=Q Z_i S_i. Start with s_1=s_2=1, source roots z_1,z_2 nonzero, and put x=q^alpha, k=x^N, a=z_2/z_1, r=a^N=phi_2/phi_1. The quantum-group embedding is the previously proved one F_i=Z_i, K_i=x S_i^(-1), rho^2 E_i=qx Z_i^(-1)(1-S_i^(-1)) (1-Q^(-1)x^(-2)S_i), rho=q-q^(-1). Thus E_i^N=0 initially and phi_i=z_i^N. The compact four-factor identity of [the Verma proof](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) has the ordered monomials m_1=-Qx A S_1^(-1), m_2=x^(-1)A, m_3=Qx A, m_4=-x^(-1)A S_1, A=Z_1^(-1)Z_2. (3.1) Their coefficients, order and q phase are retained. Define Delta_1=1+kr, Delta_2=1-r/[k(1+kr)], nu_1^N=Delta_1, nu_2^N=Delta_2, nu_3=nu_1^(-1), nu_4=nu_2^(-1). (3.2) Assume these factors are nonzero. They are full functions, not constants selected after peripheral evaluation. The root Cartan map first changes z_1,z_2 to z_1/x,z_2/x, leaving s_1=s_2=1. Its matrix is C_cartan e_(i,j)=Q^(ij)e_(i,j). (3.3) For each subsequent atom m=c A S_1^b, the commutation integers with (S_1,S_2,Z_1,Z_2) are (1,-1,b,0). By (2.2) its target roots are (s_1,s_2,z_1,z_2) -> (s_1/nu,s_2 nu,z_1/nu^b,z_2). (3.4) Evaluate m_i in the frame reached before that atom. Compatible spectral roots and norm factors are | Atom | Spectral root mu_i | nu_i^N | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | q x a | Delta_1 | | 2 | a/(x nu_1) | Delta_2 | | 3 | Q x a/nu_1 | Delta_1^(-1) | | 4 | q a/(x nu_1 nu_2) | Delta_2^(-1) | The negative monomial signs are accounted for by q^N=-1 and (A S_1^b)^N=(-1)^(b(N-1)) A^N S_1^(bN). Multiplication verifies mu_i^N+nu_i^N=1 in every row, at every parity. For completeness the successive clock-center product factors are Delta_1, Delta_2, Delta_1^(-1), Delta_2^(-1). They restore both clock roots exactly with the compatible choices in (3.2). The final shift roots are z'_1=z_1 nu_1 nu_2/x, z'_2=z_2/x. (3.5) Their powers are precisely the genuine holonomy targets: phi'_1=phi_1/k+(1-k^(-2))phi_2, phi'_2=phi_2/k. Here Delta_1 Delta_2=1+kr-r/k. This is a direct center calculation for the complete four-factor word. ## 4. The exact normalized crossing formula Let D_i be (1.2)--(1.3) for atom i in its transported frame. Let B_src and B_tar be the changes from the standard F-circle bases to the uniform clock/shift bases: B_src e_(i,j)=z_1^i z_2^j e_(i,j), B_tar e_(i,j)=(z'_1)^i(z'_2)^j e_(i,j). These are the actual monomial frame changes: v_a=z_i^a e_a has F v_a=v_(a+1), with wrap phi_i. On the root cover anchored by nu_1=nu_2=gamma_i=1 at a=0, the uncheck crossing is exactly R^0=(nu_1 nu_2)^(-(N-1)/2) B_src^(-1) C_cartan D_1 D_2 D_3 D_4 B_tar. (4.1) Products have their displayed order and changing-frame meaning. The inverse gives the negative crossing, with its centers and all roots transported as in the genuine braid theorem. Here is a proof of the scalar, rather than an unspecified projective factorization. Conjugating the generic compact four-factor identity gives a rational quantum-torus identity. The proof in the linked Verma note is a formal algebra identity before root specialization. Its rational conjugations have finite expressions (2.1), so clearing the indicated denominators specializes that identity at every root. Equations (2.2)--(3.5) then show that the right side of (4.1) and the genuine semicyclic R^0 intertwine the same full matrix algebra with the same central data and Casimirs. They differ by a scalar lambda on the generic regular chart. Each D_i has determinant one on the N^2-dimensional pair. The exact remaining determinants are det C_cartan=Q^((N(N-1)/2)^2), det B_tar/det B_src=(nu_1 nu_2/x^2)^(N^2(N-1)/2), det R^0=x^(-N^2(N-1))Q^((N(N-1)/2)^2). The external factor in (4.1) cancels the entire extra determinant. Thus lambda^(N^2)=1. (4.2) This does not by itself discard lambda. Use the formal source anchor a=0: the matrices m_i/mu_i extend there, f_j=1, D_i=identity, and all specified norm roots equal one. The zeroth coordinate of the right side applied to v_00 has a regular value one. This coordinate does not involve an inverse singular frame entry, since (B_src)_00=(B_tar)_00=1. The genuine crossing fixes v_00. Therefore lambda has value one at this formal anchor. A root-of-unity-valued algebraic function is constant on the irreducible anchored component, so lambda=1. This proves (4.1) with its phase fixed. Other lifted components retain their phases; the theorem does not identify independent choices of normalization roots. ## 5. The raw scalar is explicit and must be retained If raw pointed C_i rather than the literature D_i are used, write R_raw=B_src^(-1)C_cartan C_1 C_2 C_3 C_4 B_tar. Then R_raw=lambda_raw R^0, with lambda_raw^(N^2) =(nu_1 nu_2)^(N^2(N-1)/2) product_i F_i^N. (5.1) The complete formula and branch on the anchored cover are equivalently fixed by (4.1) and gamma_i^N=F_i^(-1). Thus determinants control a real normalization line, with its root phase selected by the actual pointing. They are not permission to throw away an arbitrary scalar period. The external root in (4.1) also remains necessary even though the four atom norm factors multiply to one. At fixed nonzero Delta_1,Delta_2 its log-modulus is -(N-1)/(2N) log|Delta_1 Delta_2|. This is bounded across N under that fixed-central specialization. No bound for an unrecorded moving-center specialization or the entire selected knot period is inferred. ## 6. Peripheral functions that become numerical multipliers For a positive checked crossing on the common fixed line of the genuine braid theorem, its uncheck source pair is swapped. Hence its ratio r is k. Write U=k^2=M^(2N), retaining the actual sign k=(-1)^(N-1)M^N. Equations (3.2) give Delta_1=1+U, Delta_2=U/(1+U), Delta_3=1/(1+U), Delta_4=(1+U)/U. (6.1) At M=1 these specialize to 2,1/2,1/2,2. They must be transported as the functions in (6.1), including their compatible roots and the external product whose Nth power is U. This is a concrete occurrence of the peripheral factors the user asked us to retain. It does not by itself repair the earlier positive scalar model's failed move. The scalar, Cartan frame and source normalization of the actual crossing are now accounted for before any such evaluation. Taking absolute values of individual atom entries would still change the quantum contraction. There is also an exact framing norm check on this fixed line. Let beta_ext=(nu_1 nu_2)^(-(N-1)/2) be the external factor in (4.1), and theta_0=x^(1-N) the actual residual twist. Since (nu_1 nu_2)^N=U=x^(2N), (beta_ext/theta_0)^(2N)=1. (6.2) Their moduli therefore cancel exactly in a zero-framed braid evaluation. The remaining phase is part of the specified root cover and pointing; it is not discarded. This checks the normalization of the tetrahedral presentation against the actual framing, rather than adding a free global multiplier. ## 7. Boundary specialization and scope of the comparison After recombination the operator (4.1) is exactly the polynomial semicyclic crossing. Its nilpotent boundary phi_1=phi_2=0 therefore has the original regular value, even though individual atom expressions or uniform frames can be singular. Use the complete identity or its transported lattice for that specialization. The common carry theorem and its bounded normal jets describe the integral recoupling source; the cut operator remains F_N(M)I and the full ADO factor is unchanged. We have consequently identified actual finite root crossings, their genuine braid maps and selected source with explicit literature cyclic tetrahedron atoms, including scalar roots and an external frame. This is a local operator factorization that can be substituted into any already specified finite braid contraction, transporting every paired and boundary leg. It does not prove that arbitrary face turns or all colored Pachner presentations of a positive geometric knot triangulation carry that same relative source and evaluation. The external semicyclic character is still reducible, and fixed root centers still differ from fixed semiclassical shape coordinates. The geometric A-operator/source identification and the selected Bloch-regulator norm across levels remain unproved. There is a concrete check on the distinction just made. At the complete point on the fixed semicyclic center line, (6.1) gives the four central shapes (-1, 1/2, 1/2, -1). Their Bloch--Wigner regulators are all zero because they are real. Thus that fixed-center Bloch sum is not the nonzero hyperbolic fundamental-class regulator. This does not compute the selected quantum period's growth; it shows why a local factorization and matching central equations alone cannot replace the remaining source/cycle and parameter comparison. The subsequent [root tetrahedral pentagon](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md) now supplies a strict local three-to-two identity for these same finite atoms on a compatible anchored cover. It includes the monomial shears, their changing splitting frames, and all norm and determinant roots. Thus specified exterior contractions can transport this local move exactly. It does not supply the entire geometric tensor presentation. Ordinary five-term transport preserves the zero regulator of the fixed central cycle just computed, so the geometric comparison must still retain the relative source and its selected realization. ## 8. Definitions, coverage and exact diagnostics Formula (1.3) is the alternate cyclic-dilogarithm definition displayed with Definition 3.3 in [Ip--Yamazaki, 1412.5777](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5777). Only its definition is used; (1.1)--(1.4) prove the needed functional and determinant identities directly. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, 2509.02354v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354v2) already covers a four-dilogarithm holonomy factorization. No novelty or independent global invariant is claimed. No published factorization or coherence proof is a premise above. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_four_cyclic_atoms.py) constructs all transported clock/shift modules, cyclic spectral matrices, and central roots over finite fields. It checks 18 crossings at generic and Kashaev colors for N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12. All 72 atom intertwiners satisfy their four generator equations. It independently compares the complete raw product with the actual semicyclic crossing, records its nonzero scalar, and verifies the exact determinant identity (5.1). It checks both restored clock roots and the full final F central powers. Normalization phases in (4.1) are fixed by the uniform anchored argument, rather than unrelated numerical choices of roots. All checks passed. Results: [four_cyclic_atoms_results.json](../experiments/four_cyclic_atoms_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_four_cyclic_atoms.py

title: Recovering the meridian state when the shape plane moves
text: # Recovering the meridian state when the shape plane moves Research note, 25 October 2026. This extends `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` to the other possible boundary rank. We retain the original charged Andersen--Kashaev tensor and its existing level convention, rather than replacing its tetrahedral function. The new construction is inverse Fourier transformation of a specifically leveled tensor. For ordinary fibers it is exactly the state already constructed, including its Gaussian normalization. Definitions used: Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), equations (4) and (18), and the Fourier/Gaussian framework of Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1409.1208v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1208v1), Section 6. All Fourier identities, phases, and analytic arguments needed below are reconstructed here or in the preceding notes. We do not assume an analytic theorem from either source. ## 1. The two ranks and a rational angle path Let a globally branched ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3 have a complete positive geometric structure. Use the independently proved Fourier reduction and cochain identity: W=im S=im B^T, dim W=d=N-2k, G=-2Q+P_+, H=-G/2, L={(t,s):t in W, s-Gt in W^perp}=ker(A|-B). Here the full A,B use N-1 independent edge rows and the unhalved preferred-longitude row. The oriented meridian and longitude have intersection 1, so A_m B_l^T-B_m A_l^T=-2. Rank B_ed is either d-1 or d. The preceding ordinary-fiber theorem treats d-1. We call d the moving-plane case, without assuming that this is the same as any degeneration of the hyperbolic structure. Choose a rational strict reference angle structure theta0, in units of pi, with lifted angular meridian and longitude both zero. Existence follows by rational density around the complete geometric angles. Below physical angles are in radians. Write a for the first shape angle and b'' for the angle of the literature double-prime shape: d0=pi*1-a0, W0=b0''-G d0. The angular gluing equations are A_r a+B_r b''=nu_r. Their homogeneous edge block has rank N-1. Adding both peripheral rows has rank N+1: edge rows are symplectically orthogonal to both peripheral rows, while their mutual pairing is -2. Therefore a rational angle variation (a1,b1'') exists with A_ed a1+B_ed b1''=0, A_m a1+B_m b1''=0, A_l a1+B_l b1''=1. (1.1) Put d1=-a1, W1=b1''-G d1 and theta(lambda)=theta0+lambda*theta1. For real lambda in a neighborhood of zero all physical angles remain strictly positive, mu=0 and the angular longitude equals lambda. The coefficients of theta1 are rational; lambda is measured in radians. If rank B_ed=d-1, then d1 is in W, as proved in the ordinary-fiber note. If rank B_ed=d, then d1 is outside W. Indeed otherwise the projected edge identity gives B_ed W1=0, and B_l is in the row space of B_ed. The longitude variation would then also be zero, contrary to (1.1). Thus S_ext=[S,-d1] has rank d+1 (1.2) in the moving-plane case. ## 2. The exact level and inverse Fourier definition Let T_b(lambda) denote the phase-free reduced integral with all Jacobians, in the common-Phi convention: T_b(lambda)=c_X*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d) integral_R^d exp[(i y^T H y+(W0+lambda W1)^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))) dz, y=i(d0+lambda d1)+S z, h=b^2/(1+b^2)^2. For real small lambda the exact charged-kernel calculation gives Z_AK(theta(lambda);b) =exp(pi i N/12+i K0(theta(lambda))/h) T_b(lambda), with the explicit K0 of the preceding boundary-state note. Define A_ref(lambda)=lambda W1.d0+(lambda^2/2)W1.d1, K(theta(lambda))=K0(theta(lambda))+A_ref(lambda)/(2pi), L_b(lambda)=exp[-i A_ref(lambda)/(2pi h)] T_b(lambda). (2.1) Consequently L_b is exactly exp(-pi i N/12) times the existing AK leveled tensor at level ell=-4K/pi. No scalar has been suppressed. For real lambda this is an allowed real b-independent level. Complex lambda below means analytic continuation of this precise normalization from its real interval. Define the meridian state by Fourier inversion: J_b(h,x)=1/(8pi^2 h) integral_R L_b(i tau) exp[-i tau x/(4pi h)] d tau. (2.2) The factor 1/(8pi^2 h) follows from the Fourier frequency tau/(4pi h). It is essential for comparison of states, although its logarithm contributes no volume rate. In the moving-plane case this is an ordinary absolutely convergent integral. Substituting (2.1), set y=i d0+S z-tau d1 and I0_b(y)=exp[(i y^T H y+W0^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))). Then the exact formula is J_b(h,x)=c_X/(8pi^2 h)*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d) integral_R^(d+1) I0_b(y) exp{[i tau W1^T S z-i tau^2 W1.d1/2-i tau x/2]/(2pi h)} dz d tau. (2.3) Every extra quadratic coefficient is real. For real z,tau,x its extra exponential has modulus one. On the horizontal plane Im y=d0, Re(i y^T H y+W0^T y)=b0'' . Re y. Strict angles give 0<b0''_j<d0_j<pi. The exact Phi tails therefore bound the modulus by C exp(-c sum_j |Re y_j|), for fixed b; derivatives only add polynomial factors. By (1.2) this is an exponential bound in |z|+|tau|. It proves absolute convergence, Schwartz regularity, and holomorphy of (2.2) on a small horizontal x strip. The same estimates on smaller real-lambda intervals give analytic continuation of (2.1) to a vertical lambda strip. Explicitly, for lambda=s+i tau, Im y=d0+s d1. The real terms from i tau W1.y and -i A_ref cancel. The remaining modulus is exactly the charged product for theta(s), and hence decreases exponentially in |z|+|tau|, uniformly on smaller s intervals. Fourier inversion, followed by a contour shift within that strip, proves exactly L_b(lambda)=integral_R J_b(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) dx. (2.4) Equivalently, this recovers the state from the normalized tensor. Uniqueness is ordinary Fourier uniqueness. No imaginary-charge value is postulated independently of its analytic continuation. This also gives the local factorization for general angles, including nonzero angular meridian mu. Let theta be near theta0, with angular longitude lambda, and set d_bar=d0+lambda d1, W_bar=W0+lambda W1, Delta W=W_theta-W_bar, K(theta)=K0(theta)+[A_ref(lambda)+Delta W.d_bar]/(2pi). (2.5) The fixed-longitude relation gives d_theta-d_bar in W and Delta W in W^perp. Contour translation through the convex positive angle segment changes T_b by precisely exp[i Delta W.d_bar/(2pi h)]. Thus Z_AK(theta;b)=exp(pi i N/12+i K(theta)/h) integral_(R+i mu) J_b(h,x) exp(lambda*x/(4pi h)) dx. (2.6) Locally the small mu contour lies in the holomorphic x strip above; its translation changes no integral. Formula (2.5) is an explicit real angle polynomial, and ell=-4K/pi is its existing AK level. This supplies the general peripheral factorization near completeness, rather than only the zero-meridian slice used to define the Fourier transform. Continuation beyond these strips needs its own contour control; no global continuation through singularities is asserted. The factor two can also be checked directly for a variation at fixed longitude: its symplectic pairing with theta1 gives Delta W.d1-W1.(d_theta-d_bar)=-mu/2. The corresponding real tau term in the shifted z contour is -tau*mu/2; the x contour Im x=mu supplies +tau*mu/2. They cancel exactly. The audit verifies this identity on the entire balanced angle space, with both peripheral variations free, before any specialization. ## 3. Agreement with the ordinary-fiber construction Suppose rank B_ed=d-1 and retain p,beta from the preceding note. Write d1=S eta1. The zero-meridian condition gives S^T W1=p/2, p^T eta1=-beta, W1.d1=-beta/2. In (2.3) change z to z+tau eta1. The extra classical phase becomes i tau(p^T z-x)/2-i beta tau^2/4. If beta is nonzero, its Fresnel integral gives precisely J_b(h,x)=1/(2pi sqrt(h)*sqrt(2i beta)) integral exp[i(x-x')^2/(8pi beta h)] J_old(h,x') dx'. The square root is the branch recorded in the ordinary-fiber note. If beta=0, Fourier inversion gives delta(p^T z-x), recovering its positive coarea fiber exactly. These operations may be justified by a Gaussian cutoff and Schwartz Fourier inversion; no absolute Fubini assertion is made for (2.3) in this noninjective case. Also (2.1) reduces exactly to K=K_old-beta*lambda^2/(8pi). Thus the inverse Fourier definition agrees with the previously normalized meridian state in every ordinary-fiber chart. It is an extension of the same construction, including its finite-b phase. ## 4. Independence of the auxiliary angle path For vectors (a,c), where c denotes the double-prime angle, use the symplectic form Omega((a,c),(a',c'))=a.c'-c.a'. The kernel of the edge, meridian and longitude rows is the symplectic dual of the edge-row space. It is isotropic with every solution of the homogeneous edge equations. This follows directly by dimensions and the peripheral pairing -2; it is not an additional NZ theorem. Consequently, if delta d,delta W are angle variations with zero meridian and longitude, then delta d in W, delta W in W^perp, delta W.d1=W1.delta d. (4.1) Change theta1 by such a variation, keeping theta0 fixed. Contour translation in W changes T_b(lambda) by exactly exp{i[lambda delta W.d0+lambda^2 delta W.d1]/(2pi h)}. The change in A_ref is the same polynomial, by (4.1) and delta W.delta d=0. Hence L_b and J_b are unchanged, not merely equal in modulus. The argument first holds for small real lambda where both paths have positive angles and then continues analytically. Changing the reference theta0 to another strict rational reference with mu=lambda=0 gives only J_new=exp[i (W_new-W0).d0/(2pi h)] J_old. (4.2) This is the previously recorded central phase. It is retained in the level and leaves the boundary annihilator unchanged. ## 5. Exact classical equations and the extra saddle direction The moving-plane action in (2.3) is F_ext(z,tau;x)=F0(y)+i tau W1^T S z -i tau^2 W1.d1/2-i tau x/2, F0(y)=i y^T H y+W0^T y-i sum_j Li_2(-exp y_j), y=i d0+r, r=S z-tau d1. Use the lifted shape deviations u=Log z_shape-i a0=-r, v=Log z_shape''-i b0'', D=v-G r. Differentiation gives grad_z F_ext=i S^T(D+tau W1). At a z-critical point rho=D+tau W1 is in W^perp. From (1.1) and the projected cochain identities one obtains, with full lifted holonomies H_r=A_r u+B_r v, H_ed=0, H_l=-tau. (5.1) For the remaining derivative, partial_tau F_ext =-i(b1'' . u-a1 . v)-i x/2. The angle variation (a1,b1'') differs from (B_m^T,-A_m^T)/2 by a symplectic dual edge vector, because its longitude is one and its meridian is zero. Thus on H_ed=0, b1'' . u-a1 . v=-H_m/2, partial_tau F_ext=i(H_m-x)/2. (5.2) All reference constants cancel in these formulas; the holonomies are differences from their specified reference lifts. Hence the full saddle equations are the edge equations with H_m=x, and the boundary phase derivative is i H_l/2. The variable x really is the meridian coordinate, without a zero-shear assumption. At the complete shapes H_m=H_l=0. They lie in the lambda=0 plane y=i d0+W by the preferred-longitude relation. Equations (5.1)--(5.2) put their saddle at tau=0, including the new transverse direction. Its phase value is the old F0 value, whose real part is -Vol(M). ## 6. Contour deformation and the volume theorem Write d_geo-d0=S eta for the difference to the actual complete geometric angles. Move the z contour through z+i s eta, 0<=s<=1, keeping tau real. These are the convex strict angle structures with zero meridian and longitude, so (4.1) applies at each s. There is a potentially dangerous new linear tau term. It cancels exactly: if delta W=W_s-W0 and delta d=S s eta, the real linear change from F0 is tau*delta W.d1, while the cross term in (2.3) contributes -tau*W1.delta d. Equation (4.1) makes their sum zero. The modulus on every intermediate plane is therefore the charged product for its positive angles. Its exponential tails are uniform on the compact angle segment. The Phi poles stay outside 0<Im y_j<pi, and Cauchy side faces vanish. This justifies the contour deformation for the complete d+1 dimensional integral. On the geometric horizontal plane its real Hessian is -S_ext^T diag[Im(e^y/(1+e^y))] S_ext. All diagonal entries are positive and S_ext has full column rank. Thus this Hessian is negative definite. The added real quadratic chirp affects only the imaginary part. The geometric critical point is the unique maximum on this plane and has a nonzero complex Gaussian coefficient. The previously proved uniform Phi remainder and global linear tail estimates now give the ordinary multivariate complex saddle asymptotic, in dimension d+1. The prefactor in (2.3) is h^(-d/2-1), and the saddle factor is h^((d+1)/2). The resulting polynomial scale is h^(-1/2), agreeing with the ordinary-fiber normalization. In particular the state is nonzero for all sufficiently small h and lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|J_b(h,0)|=Vol(M). (6.1) Together with the ordinary-fiber theorem this proves (6.1) for every globally branched complete positive geometric knot triangulation, with its specified normalized tensor-derived meridian state. The extra boundary-rank and zero-shear hypotheses have been removed. ## 7. Quantum operator and the limits of the result Every Phi argument and Gaussian coefficient in (2.3) is rational, apart from the recorded pi offsets and powers of h. The independent finite-product, dimension-count and moment argument of `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` therefore applies to this state. It gives a nonzero annihilator and its primitive minimal generator in the existing Andersen--Malusa b-shift algebra, after the stated finite coefficient cover and descent. No Jones-polynomial input is used, and no preservation of minimal degree under a fractional Gaussian conjugation is assumed. In its conventions Q=exp(-2pi b t), E f(t)=f(t-i b), t=x/(2pi sqrt(h)), EQ=qQE, q=exp(2pi i b^2). Equations (5.1)--(5.2) give the classical branch Q=exp(-H_m), E=exp(H_l/2). The previously proved uniform saddle substitution makes its geometric peripheral factor divide the classical symbol of the minimal annihilator. All generic peripheral coefficients must still be retained. Equality to the entire A-polynomial, equality to a Jones AJ operator, and an explicit coefficient list do not follow from existence alone. This is a theorem for the specified realizations. It does not construct complete positive triangulations for all alternating knots, treat flat tetrahedra, prove arbitrary global state identifications, or establish an H-triangulation limit. Those remain parts of the original objective. It also does not identify the positive factorial sum with this complex state. The exact matrix, polynomial, branch and Fourier-normalization checks are in `experiments/audit_fourier_boundary.py`. They include a six-tetrahedron 5_2 chart with rank B_ed=rank B=4, so that its longitude really moves the shape plane. Its topology calibration uses three explicitly recorded 2--3 moves; the local quantum move identity is not inferred from this combinatorial calibration. ## 8. A certified moving-plane example The fixture has ideal triangulation signature gLLPQcdefeffikdqhtk. Its stacked face kernel has dimension k=1, its reduced dimension is d=4, both B ranks are 4, c_X=1, and S_ext has rank 5. The rational zero-meridian longitude variation can be chosen with d1=(1/2,0,0,0,0,0). Thus this is an actual instance of (2.3), not just an abstract symplectic matrix example. In its native positive convention the six shapes are a, a, (a+2)/a^2, a-1, a^2/((a-1)(a+2)), -(a+1)^2/a, a^3+3a^2+2a+1=0. Rouche's inequality on the rational disc centered at (-337641021+562279512i)/10^9, of radius 10^(-8), has remainder-to-linear ratio less than 0.044. Rational images and argument intervals put every physical angle above 0.14 radians. All native edge and peripheral products reduce exactly modulo this cubic; the argument intervals fix the six edge branches at 2pi and both peripheral branches at zero. The script separately verifies the literature shape equations after the recorded vertex reorderings, without guessing a global conjugation. Regina verifies each of the three legal 2--3 moves from the already audited three-tetrahedron twist chart. Its initial combinatorial isomorphism maps the independently marked twist meridian to minus the source meridian, with zero longitude shear and zero additive angle correction. The final preferred longitude also has a separate integral dual-boundary certificate. These are topology and marking checks; a complex quantum-state identity along this particular sequence is not asserted without its level and move-phase audit. The resulting hyperbolic volume is 2.82812208833078316276... . The 70-digit numerical diagnostic of the full five-direction saddle is recorded separately from the rational geometry and matrix certificates. ## 9. A uniform boundary phase, independent of the angle path For every balanced angle structure in the local factorization domain, let d=pi*1-a, W=b''-Gd, with fixed zero-peripheral reference d0,W0. If r is the number of tetrahedra, set L_tet(theta)=-pi*r/24+sum_j epsilon_j(c_j-b_j)/12, where b_j denotes the middle physical angle. Then exactly K(theta)=L_tet(theta) +[d0.W-W0.d-d0.W0]/(4pi)-lambda*mu/(8pi). (9.1) The first two terms are affine in the angles; the only quadratic peripheral term is universal. The auxiliary path theta1 has disappeared. For the proof, the charged phase and W=2Qd-C reduce to K0=L_tet-d.W/(4pi). Write d=d0+lambda*d1+delta d, W=W0+lambda*W1+delta W. At fixed longitude, delta d lies in the allowed shape subspace, delta W annihilates it, and the peripheral pairing gives delta W.delta d=0, delta W.d1-W1.delta d=-mu/2. Expansion of (2.5) cancels lambda^2. Its remaining quadratic term is lambda*(delta W.d1-W1.delta d)/(4pi), giving (9.1). This is the boundary Heisenberg term hidden in the separate chart normalizations. It connects the continuous level with the structural period line of `heisenberg_period_torsor.md`. The identity retains the full angle polynomials before any peripheral specialization.

title: An actual bounded source in the Fourier--Mellin polarization
text: # An actual bounded source in the Fourier--Mellin polarization Research construction, 27 October 2026. A fixed rational inhomogeneous source need not be assumed as a special factorization of the original meridian operator. It can be constructed in the Fourier--Mellin polarization directly from any actual all-level operator and finitely many fixed colors. The original Kashaev invariant is retained as an exact coefficient period. It is not replaced by point evaluation or by a new state. This gives an actual sourced quantum-A object for arbitrary knots. Its classical geometric support and selected regulator norm still require proof; the volume conjecture is not proved here. ## 1. Actual input and the Q convention Choose the nonzero rational operator supplied by the [Q-only construction](even_meridian_norm_descent.md), clear its coefficient denominators, and remove a common shift: P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Y) T^j, a_j=sum_m a_(j,m)(Q) Y^m, TY=QYT, a_0 a_d!=0. (1.1) Here d>=1, the m support is finite, and the coefficients belong to the rational function field ℚ(Q). The associated fixed-color periods are C_n(Q), normalized by C_n(1)=1. They are the actual finite reduced periods of the existing color-pointing theorem. The exact identities are F_N(Y=Q_N^n)=C_n(Q_N), 1<=n<=N, C_N(Q_N)=F_N(1)=<K>_N, Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N). (1.2) There is no large-color asymptotic premise in (1.2). For completeness these fixed-color functions descend to Q=q^2 as well. On the ordinary n-dimensional color x=q^(n-1), use the same stripped crossing coefficients, ordinary pivot K and residual twist x. The total x-power on a closed state is E_ord=b-1-w+sum_positive(-a-c)+sum_negative(a+c) =-kappa_D+2sum_negative a-2sum_positive c, because sum(c-a)=0. It is even for a knot. All remaining factors are expressed in Q and x^2. At x=q^(n-1) this is a rational function of Q.
