The local convergence (4) is uniform, so uniform dominated convergence applies, including all actual orders 0<=a<N. The limiting integral is sin(pi u)/pi * integral_0^infinity [2sinh(s/2)]^(-u) exp[-(v+1/4-i epsilon q(u))s]ds =sin(pi u)/pi * B(alpha_(epsilon)(u,v),1-u) =K_(epsilon)(u,v). (11) In the beta integral put x=exp(-s); the last equality is the Gamma reflection identity. Combining with the EXACT endpoint (3) proves (9). In particular the factors N^(u-1) and N^(-u-1/2) cancel to the universal N^(-3/2). ## 5. The resulting actual angular source and its limitation Consider the exact full all-inverse word with s=9m cut variables, and restrict its angular labels j_l/N to compact subintervals of (0,1). Expand the original rational source into its finitely many coefficient orders a_l>=0. Its exact radial integration is the product of the moments (1). Formula (9) therefore supplies product_l [C_(epsilon_l,N) N^(-3/2) F_(-epsilon_l,j_l) K_(epsilon_l)(j_l/N,a_l/N)] (12) as its uniform leading coefficient kernel, with relative o(1) in each coefficient. All head bounds, Fourier characters, Gaussian matrices and the pivotal source remain in that array. The multipliers K form a smooth, nonzero coefficient symbol. On each bulk coefficient box the diagonal multiplication by their product and its inverse have bounded norms in coefficient-space ell^p for every p. This is a statement BEFORE the final linear source contraction; it makes no claim about the physical fusion metric or a lower bound after cancellation. The uniform error is controlled by the corresponding absolute weighted coefficient sum. It need not be small RELATIVE to the selected scalar. More explicitly let J_N=diag(0,...,N-1) on the power-coefficient space of one actual atom, with its ordinary orthonormal degree basis. Define the NORMALIZED EXACT radial multiplier T_(epsilon,N,j)=diag_(0<=a<N) [R_(epsilon,N)(j,a) / (C_(epsilon,N) N^(-3/2) F_(-epsilon,j))]. (12a) For bulk j/N in U, (9) is precisely the uniform operator-norm statement ||T_(epsilon,N,j)-K_(epsilon)(u,J_N/N)|| -> 0. (12b) Let gamma_(U)>0 be the minimum of the explicit right side in (8b) for u in U, 0<=v<=1. For all sufficiently large N, Re T_(epsilon,N,j) >= (gamma_(U)/2) I, ||T_(epsilon,N,j)^(-1)|| <=2/gamma_(U), (12c) uniformly in these labels. Its norm is also uniformly bounded, so its condition number is bounded. Equivalently every coefficient vector f obeys Re <f,T_(epsilon,N,j)f> >=(gamma_(U)/2)||f||^2. The factorial and Gaussian endpoint line in (12a) remains its explicit original factor. A general pivotal source is not this positive quadratic pairing. Tensoring several such factors also does not automatically keep their arguments in a common positive half-plane. Thus (12c) is an actual radial coefficient estimate, not the missing final scalar lower bound. In a separately justified Laplace comparison on a real bulk chain, with a strictly nondegenerate maximum of the real exponent and a nonzero source amplitude, this uniform symbol changes the local leading amplitude by the explicit nonzero Gamma factors. No such chain for the whole knot is constructed here. In particular (9) alone does not justify a deformation to complex angular labels or termwise replacement after an uncontrolled oscillatory contraction. Proving that the actual angular source selects the geometric point is still necessary. This can already be seen for one coefficient in (2). The leading angular phase of its factorial and Fourier character is Phi_(epsilon)(u,v) =J(u)+(epsilon pi i/2)(u-u^2)+epsilon 2 pi i u v. Its stationary equation is [1-exp(-epsilon 2 pi i u)] exp(epsilon 2 pi i v)=1. (13) Thus the familiar complementary shape relation emerges directly from the actual cut. For arbitrary real v its critical u is complex; the real angular grid does not automatically pass through it. When u=5/6, v=1/6, the endpoint absolute-envelope maximum is a stationary point and K is positive. Those special values do not give a general knot argument: the whole network couples all v through its original heads and phases. The bulk radial theorem therefore removes one concrete possible source of exponential cancellation and supplies an actual, nonvanishing amplitude for the next angular comparison. It does not justify replacing (12) by its absolute value, deleting K, ignoring the nonbulk labels, or inferring that the selected geometric contribution cannot cancel with the rest of the word. [Profile, endpoint-phase and moment audit](../experiments/audit_full_cut_geometric_coupling.py) and [saved diagnostics](../experiments/full_cut_geometric_coupling_results.json).

title: Proven dilogarithm and endpoint regions of the full original Euler atoms
text: # Proven dilogarithm and endpoint regions of the full original Euler atoms 28 October 2026. The actual finite crossing polynomials have two rigorously distinguishable exponential modes. The dilogarithm mode is selected uniformly on an explicit fixed open domain containing the upper half unit disk and a neighborhood of the regular ideal shape. The top-degree mode is selected throughout a fixed exterior region. Along an explicit family of positive ideal tetrahedra the two regions meet at a sharp amplitude threshold. Positive ideal angles alone therefore do not justify replacing a full atom by its dilogarithm expression throughout that chamber. These are results for the full original polynomials, rather than a nilpotent evaluation, a new positive model, or a claimed finite list of all Stokes sectors. They do not identify an atom argument with a shape coordinate in every knot presentation, or construct the required whole knot contour deformation. ## 1. The full functions and their source Fix N >= 2, Q = exp(2 pi i/N), H_N = 2 pi i/N, and F_k = (Q;Q)_k, u_N(z) = sum_(k=0)^(N-1) z^k/F_k, v_N(z) = sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2] z^k/F_k. The literal unchecked crossing has Euler factor v_N(q rho^2 E_1 F_2) and its literal inverse has u_N of that same argument, as proved in [the crossing-argument calculation](euler_atom_source_family_and_crossing_argument.md). No other factors of that crossing are discarded here. As ORDINARY scalar polynomials these satisfy u_N(Qz) - (1-z)u_N(z) = z^N/N, (1) (1-z)v_N(Qz) - v_N(z) = -z^N/N. (2) The terms on the right will not be set to zero. Iterating around the full Q orbit, and using product_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-Q^j z)=1-z^N, gives the exact global finite-product representations u_N(z) = (1/N) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) product_(r=1)^k (1-Q^(-r)z), (3) v_N(z) = (1/N) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (z;Q)_k. (4) Initially the iteration may be performed at z != 0; polynomial continuation proves the formulas everywhere. Thus the cyclic norm and the affine source are retained in these functions. There is also an exact Cauchy representation useful for a future contour comparison. Mark, on |w|<1, D_N(w) = product_(j=1)^(N-1) (1-Q^j w)^(j/N), D_N(0)=1, A_(N,u)=D_N, A_(N,v)=D_N^(-1). The first N Taylor coefficients of A_(N,u) and A_(N,v) are those of u_N and v_N respectively. Indeed for 1 <= k < N, [w^k] log D_N = 1/[k(1-Q^k)]. For either atom p_N=u_N or v_N and ANY 0<r<1, p_N(z) = (1/(2 pi i)) integral_(|w|=r) A_(N,p)(w) [1-(z/w)^N]/(w-z) dw. (5) The apparent pole at w=z is removable. Formula (5) is valid for every scalar z, not just |z|<r. Separating its two terms gives, when |z|<r, the exact analytic expression A_(N,p)(z) minus a retained z^N Cauchy remainder. Agreement of nilpotent jets by itself would not remove that remainder. ## 2. The threshold constant Put J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y)) dy, 0<=s<=1, z(t)=1-exp(-2 pi i t), 0<t<1/2, r(t)=|z(t)|=2 sin(pi t). There is a unique t_* in (0,1/2) satisfying -J(t_*) - (1-t_*) log r(t_*) = 0. (6) Numerically, t_* = 0.20877342895233375656..., R_* = r(t_*) = 1.21971547612163368901.... These decimals are descriptive, not premises of the results. For B(t)=-J(t)-(1-t)log r(t), B'(t)=-(1-t) pi cot(pi t)<0, B(0+)=+infinity, B(1/2)=-log(2)/2. This proves existence and uniqueness. The equivalent exterior characterization is log R_* = max_(0<s<=1) J(s)/s. (7) To see it, the numerator of the derivative of J(s)/s is G(s)=s J'(s)-J(s), with G'(s)=s pi cot(pi s). It is positive up to a unique zero in (1/2,1) and then negative. Using J(1-t)=-J(t), that zero is s=1-t_* and (6) gives (7). ## 3. A full-polynomial dilogarithm theorem beyond the small disk Let K be any compact subinterval of (0,t_*) and W any compact subset of C. Uniformly for t in K, w in W and z=z(t) exp(w/sqrt(N)), one has v_N(z) = (1-z)^(1/2) exp[Li_2(z)/H_N] (1+O_(K,W)(N^(-1/2))). (8) Uniformly for z=conjugate(z(t)) exp(w/sqrt(N)), u_N(z) = (1-z)^(-1/2) exp[-Li_2(z)/H_N] (1+O_(K,W)(N^(-1/2))). (9) All logarithms, square roots and Li_2 continue from z=0 along the indicated upper or lower arc. In particular these full atoms are nonzero throughout those windows for all sufficiently large N. The coefficient of the displayed dilogarithm mode is exactly one in those marks; it is not an undetermined nonzero normalization. At t=1/6, z(t)=exp(pi i/3), the regular ideal shape. Thus (8) and (9) control complex N^(-1/2) windows crossing |z|=1. They are not merely estimates on a disk strictly inside that circle. Section 6 upgrades these windows to a fixed open domain by the exact finite rotation equation, retaining its affine source throughout. ### Direct proof retaining all coefficients For s=k/N in a compact subinterval of (0,1), elementary Euler--Maclaurin and Stirling estimates give P_(N,k):=|F_k| = sqrt(2N sin(pi s)) exp[N J(s)] (1+O(1/N)). (10) For example apply Euler--Maclaurin to log(sin(pi s)/(pi s)) after removing the k! factor at zero. Globally, for 0<=k<N, the weaker uniform statement log P_(N,k) = N J(k/N)+O(log N) (11) suffices. It follows by subtracting both endpoint logarithms: log(2 sin(pi s))-log s-log(1-s) extends smoothly to [0,1], and the remaining two sums are factorials. In (11), k=0 is interpreted separately as P_(N,0)=1. The exact phases are [z^k]v_N = exp[-pi i k/2 + pi i k(k-3)/(2N)]/P_(N,k), [z^k]u_N = exp[ pi i k/2 - pi i k(k+1)/(2N)]/P_(N,k). For v define S_v(s,z)=s Log z-J(s)+(pi i/2)(s^2-s). At z=z(t), S_v has its stationary point at s=t, since Log z(t)=log r(t)+i(pi/2-pi t), and S_v''(t,z(t))=-pi cot(pi t)+pi i. (12) The real part of the phase is phi_t(s)=s log r(t)-J(s). Its only interior stationary points are the maximum s=t and the minimum s=1-t. Its endpoint values are 0 and log r(t). The first is strictly below phi_t(t), and the second is strictly below precisely when B(t)>0. Thus for t in K the UNIQUE global amplitude maximum is s=t, with a uniform gap away from it. Estimate (11) therefore bounds every discarded portion of the FULL finite sum exponentially relative to the central band. In that band (10), the displayed exact phase, and the variable xi=(k-Nt)/sqrt(N) reduce the sum to a convergent complex Gaussian. Its real quadratic part is strictly negative by (12). The usual Taylor remainder is bounded by an integrable Gaussian times a polynomial; the mesh is 1/sqrt(N). Both errors are O(N^(-1/2)), uniformly also with the bounded complex tilt w. In particular no unknown stationary-cycle coefficient is inserted in this calculation. At w=0 the resulting leading coefficient simplifies exactly to exp(-3 pi i t/2) / sqrt(sin(pi t)(cot(pi t)-i)) = exp(-pi i t). Also, with the stated marks, S_v(t,z(t))=Li_2(z(t))/(2 pi i), exp(-pi i t)=(1-z(t))^(1/2). The action identity follows by differentiating along t and using Log(1-z(t))=-2 pi i t, with common value zero at t=0. For bounded w the tilted Gaussian contributes exp[-w^2/(2S_v'')]. This is exactly the quadratic Taylor term of N Li_2(z(t) exp(w/sqrt(N)))/(2 pi i), because d^2[Li_2(z)/(2 pi i)]/d(Log z)^2=-1/S_v'' at the saddle. The remaining action and amplitude errors are O(N^(-1/2)). This proves (8). The same calculation with S_u(s,z)=s Log z-J(s)+(pi i/2)(s-s^2), or the exact identity u_N(z)=conjugate(v_N(Q conjugate(z))), proves (9). Its Gaussian factor is exp(-pi i t)=(1-z)^(-1/2) on the lower arc, as required. ## 4. A uniform full exterior expansion For EVERY fixed R>R_* and integer d>=1, uniformly for |z|>=R, u_N(z) = z^(N-1)/N [ sum_(k=0)^(d-1) (-1)^k Q^[-k(k+1)/2] F_k z^(-k) +O_(R,d)(N^(-d))], (13) v_N(z) = Q z^(N-1)/N [ sum_(k=0)^(d-1) Q^k F_k z^(-k) +O_(R,d)(N^(-d))]. (14) Here N>d. In particular both are nonzero for all sufficiently large N throughout that exterior region, and their exponential rate at every fixed z there is log|z|. The leading factors are literal top coefficients of the original finite polynomials. For the proof, F_(N-1)=N gives the exact reversed coefficients [z^(N-1-k)]u_N = (-1)^k Q^[-k(k+1)/2] F_k/N, [z^(N-1-k)]v_N = Q^(k+1) F_k/N. (15) In either reversed series the modulus of its k-th coefficient term is P_(N,k)|z|^(-k). For k>=epsilon N, (7) and (11) bound their sum by a polynomial in N times exp[-epsilon N log(R/R_*)]. For k<epsilon N choose epsilon small enough that 2 pi epsilon/R<1/2. Successive term moduli then have ratio at most 2 pi epsilon/R. Since the d-th term is O_(R,d)(N^(-d)), its tail is bounded by a geometric series. This proves (13)--(14) without an oscillatory cancellation premise. ## 5. A genuine distinction inside the positive ideal-shape chamber For every 0<t<1/2, z(t) is in the upper half-plane and is a valid positively oriented ideal tetrahedron shape. Its three angles are (pi/2-pi t, 2 pi t, pi/2-pi t). For 0<t<t_* equation (8) yields lim (1/N)log|v_N(z(t))|=Im Li_2(z(t))/(2 pi). For t_*<t<1/2, r(t)>R_*, so (14) instead yields lim (1/N)log|v_N(z(t))|=log r(t) > Im Li_2(z(t))/(2 pi). (16) Indeed the difference of the right sides is -B(t)>0. The transition t=t_* itself is not evaluated here. Nor do the two proved regions assert that all other complex sectors are exhausted. Consequently a Rivin volume maximum and positivity of its ideal angles do not alone establish a uniform dilogarithm replacement of every original atom on a proposed global deformation. A whole word proof must retain the exact finite source (1)--(5), control the actual argument maps, and either stay in justified atom regions or account for the endpoint modes and any other sectors crossed. This is an obstruction to that inference, not to the volume conjecture or to a source-preserving whole-word cancellation. ## 6. Exact rotation gives a fixed open dilogarithm domain There is a larger explicit uniform result. On the upper half-plane use the principal continuation of Li_2 and put g(z)=Im Li_2(z)/(2 pi), D_+={z: Im z>0 and g(z)>log|z|}, D_-=conjugate(D_+). Then, uniformly on EVERY compact subset of D_+, v_N(z)=(1-z)^(1/2) exp[Li_2(z)/H_N] (1+O(N^(-1/2))). (17) Uniformly on every compact subset of D_-, u_N(z)=(1-z)^(-1/2) exp[-Li_2(z)/H_N] (1+O(N^(-1/2))). (18) The marks are the same ones as in Section 3. These statements therefore give a nonzero leading coefficient ONE throughout fixed open domains, not just on the arc or on shrinking windows. The exact cyclic source has been estimated, rather than discarded. In particular all large-N atoms in (17)--(18) are nonzero on those compact subsets. The domain D_+ contains the entire upper half of |z|<=1. For 1<|z|<R_* it contains an angular bulge described by its displayed inequality. It has no point with |z|>=R_*. ### Angular geometry of this domain For z=r exp(i theta), 0<theta<pi, partial_theta g=-log|1-z|/(2 pi), partial_theta^2 g=-r sin(theta)/(2 pi |1-z|^2)<0. (19) For 0<r<2 its unique angular maximum is at theta_a(r)=arccos(r/2). That point is exactly z(t) of Section 2, with r=2 sin(pi t). Its excess over log r is B(t). Consequently the superlevel set g>log r on a circle is an interval containing that anchor, nonempty precisely for r<R_*. For r>=2, |1-z|>=1 and g is decreasing in theta; its boundary maximum is g(r+i0)=log(r)/2<log r. Thus there is no additional component at larger r. For r<=1, g is strictly positive in the upper half-plane, whereas log r<=0, which proves the asserted disk inclusion. Positivity follows as well by integrating partial_r Im Li_2(r exp(i theta))=-arg(1-r exp(i theta))/r>0 from r=0. On each angular path inside that superlevel interval, concavity implies that the minimum of g-log r occurs at one of its two endpoints. For a compact target set K contained in D_+, all paths from the corresponding anchors to K therefore form a compact upper-half-plane set C and obey min_C [g(z)-log|z|] >= delta_K > 0. (20) The anchors have t in a compact subinterval of (0,t_*). In particular C avoids both the singular point z=1 and all real logarithmic cuts. An O(1/N) angular adjustment of its anchors preserves a fixed positive gap for large N. ### Propagation using the actual affine equation Put V_N(z)=(1-z)^(1/2) exp[Li_2(z)/H_N]. A Taylor expansion on a fixed compact neighborhood of C gives (1-z)V_N(Qz)/V_N(z)=1+O_C(N^(-2)). (21) To check the cancellation explicitly, D_z=z partial_z satisfies D_z Li_2=-Log(1-z) and D_z^2 Li_2=z/(1-z). The order-H_N term from Li_2(Qz)/H_N is therefore +(H_N/2)z/(1-z), and the order-H_N term from the square-root amplitude is its negative. This is why the actual prefactor in (17) is necessary. For any z in K choose an integer j so z_0=Q^(-j)z has the same radius as z and lies within pi/N in angle of its anchor. The partial rotation path z_l=Q^l z_0 from z_0 to z stays within O(1/N) of C, uses O(N) steps, and can be taken forward or backward. The anchor theorem (8) applies, since its logarithmic displacement is O(1/N), and gives v_N(z_0)/V_N(z_0)=1+O_K(N^(-1/2)). Write R_l=v_N(z_l)/V_N(z_l) and c=z_0^N/N=z_l^N/N. Dividing the EXACT equation (2) by V_N yields R_(l+1)=(1+epsilon_l)^(-1) [R_l-c/V_N(z_l)], epsilon_l=(1-z_l)V_N(z_(l+1))/V_N(z_l)-1 =O_K(N^(-2)). (22) The inverse of (22) is equally exact for a backward step. By (20) and the bounded nonzero square-root amplitude on C, |c/V_N(z_l)| <= (C_K/N) exp(-delta_K N/2). (23) Products of O(N) factors 1+epsilon_l differ from one by O_K(1/N). Summing the actual source terms (23) is exponentially small. Thus (22) proves (17), with the same leading coefficient one as at the anchor. No assumption about the exhaustion of Stokes modes or an analytic continuation of asymptotic jets is involved: the propagation is the exact original polynomial recurrence. Finally use the exact conjugation identity of Section 3. On a compact subset of D_-, Q conjugate(z) remains in D_+ for large N. Conjugating (17) and expanding by one H_N step gives (1-Q^(-1)z)^(1/2) exp[-Li_2(Q^(-1)z)/H_N] =(1-z)^(-1/2) exp[-Li_2(z)/H_N](1+O(1/N)). This proves (18), including its mark and prefactor. The selected dilogarithm domain is large enough to contain the regular ideal tetrahedron in a fixed complex neighborhood. It does not contain the entire upper ideal-shape chamber: Section 5 gives valid positive shapes where the exact endpoint mode is larger. Proving a whole-knot contour can be kept in the appropriate atom domains, or transporting it across the remaining regions with all source terms, is still a separate problem. There is nevertheless a simple classical atlas relevant to that choice. For every positive ideal shape z, the three usual quad-type shapes z, 1/(1-z), 1-1/z all belong to the upper half-plane and their product is -1. At least one therefore has modulus <=1 and belongs to D_+. Thus the three inverse images of D_+ under these transformations cover the entire positive ideal-shape chamber. On compact sets of nondegenerate positive angles, the resulting chosen atom charts have a uniform positive source gap after taking a finite subcover. This supplies possible CLASSICAL chart choices. It does not supply an exact quantum change of the actual Euler polynomial, its full word argument, the source or the contour; those transformations must still be established with their boundary terms. [The saved audit](../experiments/full_euler_atom_regions_results.json) checks the exact representations and reverse coefficients, and compares the full-polynomial asymptotics on the arc, complex windows and exterior region. The direct estimates above are the proofs.

title: A uniform comparison of the whole finite source-factor lattice
text: # A uniform comparison of the whole finite source-factor lattice Research proof, 27 October 2026. The middle-component Gamma comparison extends to every color in the actual finite head. A complementary Weyl chart is essential in the upper half: using the same partial product there would introduce extra periodic zero divisors. The result is an exact diagonal unit comparison, uniformly I+O(1/N) in the full head, including all fixed normal resonance divisors. It compares source factors and their dual fractional lattices. It does not identify the two crossing representations or the selected knot periods. The surviving crossing response is studied separately. ## 1. Actual factors and the two root Weyl charts Use the actual frame of [the integral-color source](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md) and [its whole Gamma normal](whole_gamma_frame_profile.md). Put c=2pi*i, n=N-1, L=floor(n/2), H_0=c/N, H=H_0+ca/N^2, b=a/(1+a/N), Hb=ca/N, M_col=exp(Hb/2)=-q^N, q=exp(H/2), M_+=exp(H_0b/2), M_-=M_+^(-1), Q_0=exp(H_0). For j=0,...,n, the retained source-frame residual is V_(N,j)={n choose j}_(q,sym)/M_col^j. (1) Every q-binomial in (1) means its Laurent-polynomial value, including parameters where a factorial quotient is 0/0. At such parameters V need not be a unit. The partial root Weyl factors are the actual functions beta_j(M)=(M^2 Q_0;Q_0)_j/(Q_0;Q_0)_j. (2) Their denominators are nonzero for j<N. They are the factors in the diagonal matrix of the exact root Weyl intertwiner, whose entries are M^j/beta_j(M), with the original meromorphic and source-lattice interpretation. The marked full half-adapter is beta_L at odd N, and [(1+iM)/(1+i)]beta_L at even N. The extra even factor is retained when passing to that scalar. Define the complementary target source-factor section by B_(N,j)=beta_j(M_-), j<=L, B_(N,j)=M_+^(n-2j)beta_(n-j)(M_-), j>L. (3) These are concrete root Weyl factors and their retained character, not values of an arbitrary replacement invariant. The two formulas are the actual norm/complementary charts. If H_N(cb)=S_N(M_+^2)/(N M_+^n), the exact identity is beta_j(M_+) beta_(n-j)(M_-) =M_+^(2j-n) H_N(cb). (4) Consequently the upper expression in (3) obeys beta_j(M_+) B_(N,j)=H_N(cb). (5) Thus B_(N,j) can also be written H_N/beta_j(M_+) after canceling common factors. Formula (3), rather than division at a zero, defines its holomorphic value. To prove (4), transform the last n-j factors of (M_+^2 Q_0;Q_0)_n using r->N-r. Their ratios become M_+^(-2)(1-M_+^2Q_0^r)/(1-Q_0^r). The complete product is S_N(M_+^2)/N. Multiplying its character gives exactly (4). This also retains the unpaired even residue; replacing the marked even half-adapter by beta_L alone would lose its scalar splitting, although (2)--(5) remain valid partial-factor identities. ## 2. Exact unit comparison at every color Let J(x)=2sinh(x/2)/x, J(0)=1. For 0<=k<=L set u_(N,k)=exp[-(H-H_0)bk/2] product_(r=1)^k J(H(r-b))J(H_0r)/[J(Hr)J(H_0(r-b))]. (6) There is no even prefactor in this partial-product formula. Define a diagonal matrix C_N(a) by C_(N,j)=u_(N,j), j<=L, C_(N,j)=exp[(H-H_0)b(n-2j)/2]u_(N,n-j), j>L. Then, exactly for every j, V_(N,j)=C_(N,j) B_(N,j). (7) For each compact complex a-set K, all sufficiently large N have a neighborhood of K on which every C_(N,j) is a holomorphic unit, C_(N,j)(0)=1, and sup_(a in K,0<=j<N)|C_(N,j)-1|<=A_K/N. (8) This assertion concerns the comparison unit, not invertibility of V or B at their common zeros. For k<=L the exact factorization in the Gamma theorem is V_(N,k)=exp(-Hbk/2) product_(r<=k) (1-b/r) J(H(r-b))/J(Hr). The corresponding beta_k(M_-) has H replaced by H_0. Their common zero polynomial is kept before canceling, and the remaining factors give (6). All J arguments remain in a fixed zero-free neighborhood of c[0,1/2] for a in K and large N. In particular the unit extends through integer b. Uniformity in k is the same double-difference estimate as in the middle-component proof. With F=Log J and DeltaH=H-H_0, the logarithm of one cross ratio is DeltaH[(r-b)F'(H_0(r-b))-rF'(H_0r)] +O_K(DeltaH^2 r^2). The bracket is O_K(1), because its two arguments differ by b, F' and F'' are bounded, and H_0r is bounded. Since DeltaH is O_K(N^-2), summing at most N/2 terms gives O_K(1/N), uniformly in the prefix length. The phase in (6) has the same bound. For the upper half use the exact symmetric q-binomial identity V_(N,j)=M_col^(n-2j)V_(N,n-j). (9) Combining (9) with the lower comparison gives (7); its additional character differs from the root character by the displayed unit in C_(N,j). Its logarithm is again O_K(1/N). This proves (8) uniformly in the entire head, without a bulk-color restriction. For any common diagonal coordinate or coherent metric, (8) gives ||C_N-I||<=A_K/N, ||C_N||,||C_N^(-1)||<=1+O_K(1/N). (10) The bound is independent of the dimension N. It holds for every fixed normal jet as well, on a smaller compact set, by Cauchy's formula. No sum over colors is needed to obtain these operator norm estimates. ## 3. The resonance divisors are matched, not inverted away At an integer b=r with 1<=r<=L and N>2r, the exact vanishing pattern of the residual is V_(N,j)=0 precisely for r<=j<=n-r. (11) The same pattern holds for B, with the same simple divisors in the parameter. Indeed beta_k(M_-) vanishes first at k=r, and there is no other root-periodic zero in k<=L in a fixed normal compact set for large N. The complement gives (11) in the upper half. The unit in (7) preserves these divisors. The exact parameter centers are a=Nr/(N-r), rather than a=r. No quotient V/B is evaluated there to define C_N. Defining V by a raw q-factorial quotient at an upper index would miss its removable cancellation at these lower-order roots; its Laurent-polynomial or complementary value in (1) is essential. For the paired source and co-source one may work first over the meromorphic parameter field. Equation (7) identifies the fractional source lattices generated by V_j and B_j, and also their inverse dual lattices. The dual comparison is C_(N,j)^(-1). The tensor pairing is preserved before specialization. A zero source coordinate and a pole in its dual cannot separately be discarded: their abstract pairing is still one. ## 4. The whole source chirp costs no exponential factor in N The exact balanced frame satisfies D_col^(-1)=U_col diag(V), (U_col)_j=q^[Nj-j(j+1)/2]. (12) For a root chirp (U_0)_j=exp[H_0(Nj-j(j+1)/2)/2], use the concrete root-chart source frame U_0 diag(B). Its comparison to the actual column frame is U_col diag(V)=T_N(a) U_0 diag(B), T_N=diag(U_col/U_0) C_N. (13) The chirp ratio is exactly (U_col/U_0)_j =exp{ca[ j/(2N)-j(j+1)/(4N^2)]}. (14) For a in K, T_N and its inverse have uniform operator bounds independent of N in every common diagonal metric. At j/N->T, its chirp tends to exp[ca(T/2-T^2/4)]. Thus the normal source transport has a controlled whole quadratic character, and the remaining unit tends uniformly to one. Equations (12)--(14) transport the original source column and dual row, including their fractional lattices and endpoint coordinates. They do not replace either by a constant vacuum after a change of frame. At a resonance, specialize the paired lattices, not their separately singular coordinate arrays. More explicitly, U_0 diag(B) is a meromorphic coordinate frame of the same literature-defined root head. All its root operators must be conjugated in that frame, together with the original column psi and row phi. If Gamma_root is the resulting cut coupon, then its comparison with the actual color-frame coupon is exactly psi_col=T_N psi_root, phi_col=phi_root T_N^(-1), Gamma_col=T_N Gamma_root T_N^(-1). (15) The diagonal T_N commutes with J and both endpoint projectors. Thus (15) also transports every finite position-moment insertion and the original endpoint source probes. This does not identify Q_col^J with Q_0^J; the two quantum parameters and the crossing operators remain distinct. No new state or closure is defined. ## 5. What is and is not closed The source-factor comparison now covers the entire head and both endpoint ranges with a dimension-independent unit bound. It retains the actual root Weyl norm, even-level mark, all finite normal zero divisors and the quadratic chirp. This is not a full crossing similarity. The q-normal and fixed-root crossings can have different spectral multiplicities and different periodic alias zeros. Their nontrivial bulk response and the normal base must also be transported. Nor do the source bounds bound a cancellation-prone selected knot sum. A source-preserving comparison of the actual full knot period with its marked geometric regulator, and its selected exponential norm, remains necessary. The [all-level crossing spectra](crossing_normal_spectra_obstruction.md) rule out even an arbitrary scalar-adjusted nondiagonal similarity. The compatible constructive statement is [the closed Euler/regulator response](quantum_normal_crossing_bulk_response.md), which compares the actual normal geometric blocks with their full sources. Neither statement is replaced by (15). Verification: [audit](../experiments/audit_full_head_gamma_source_transport.py) and [results](../experiments/full_head_gamma_source_transport_results.json). The [independent source audit](gamma_residual_normal_profile_independent_audit.md) also verifies the whole-head unit, chirp, zero divisors and paired coupon/lattice identities.

title: Audit of the full peripheral shift on root fibers and normal germs
text: # Audit of the full peripheral shift on root fibers and normal germs 27 October 2026. The corrected full-normalization paragraph in [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md), Section 5, passes. Its root-family and geometric-symbol conclusions are unchanged. The whole q-normal source requires the additional power-character factor below. Keep the original line d_N(M)=epsilon_N M^(N-1)(M^2-1)/(M^(2N)-1), with its actual rational-map/source lattice at canceled or uncanceled divisors. Direct division gives EXACTLY g_N(q,M)=d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =q^(N-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1) *(M^(2N)-1)/(q^(2N)M^(2N)-1). The fixed root phase epsilon_N cancels; it has not been reset. For N_N=d_N F_N, the correct gauge of an operator annihilating F_N is d_N D d_N^-1. Thus its ordered substitution is T -> g_N^-1 T, T^r -> product_(j=0)^(r-1) g_N(q,q^jM)^-1 T^r. These products follow from T f(M)=f(qM)T, not a commutative substitution for powers. With independent retained powers z=q^N,w=M^(2N), the whole factor is g_N=q^-1 z (q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1)*(w-1)/(z^2w-1). The meridian Ore step MUST act by sigma(M)=qM, sigma(z)=z, sigma(w)=z^2w. In particular w is fixed by this step only AFTER restriction to the physical root character z=-1. There that restriction is the meromorphic meridian-germ identity g_bar=-q^-1(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). The common w-1 cancels as a rational identity on the root fiber. Its complete lattice is still required at norm-zero intersections; g_bar itself has a pole at M=1 for N>1 and must not be evaluated there as a regular unit. This agrees with the original source guard. Consequently the ordered root gauge in the partial theorem is correct on every actual root meridian family. Its generic-M classical symbol has g_bar -> -1, so the preexisting geometric factor becomes A_geo(M,-L_full) in that FULL ROOT shift convention. The same applies to the Fourier and fixed-input root families; neither uses an asserted whole-normal identification. The distinction is visible before any asymptotic analysis: g_N/g_bar=-z(w-1)/(z^2w-1), (g_N/g_bar)|_(z=-1)=1, D_z log(g_N/g_bar)|_(z=-1)=-(w+1)/(w-1). On the actual whole fixed-N power graph this gives [D_q log g_N-D_q log g_bar]|_(q=q_N) =-N (M^(2N)+1)/(M^(2N)-1), where D_q=q partial_q with M fixed. Hence equality on the entire root MERIDIAN germ does not equate its q-normal jets. The discrepancy retains exactly the peripheral character and its norm divisor. Finally g_N -> +1 as q->1 at FIXED N and generic M. This is a different specialization from the root-character classical symbol g_bar -> -1. The latter is the statement of the root-family support theorem; one may not transfer it to a whole fixed-N gauge by forgetting z,w or changing their Ore action. No conclusion about the final selected geometric period is added by this audit.

title: Full rank-one cyclotomic descent, including ramified zeros and poles
text: # Full rank-one cyclotomic descent, including ramified zeros and poles Research proof for independent audit, 27 October 2026. This extends [the unramified Q-parameter proof](q_parameter_curvature_extension.md). The new ingredient is a weighted sequence-uniqueness lemma allowing finite exponential--Puiseux amplitudes. It removes both ramification and finite-nonzero limiting-root hypotheses from that rank-one result. This remains a comparison-line theorem. The actual geometric comparison line, its full cyclic transport identities and its source/cut marking must still be supplied. The original volume conjecture is not proved here. ## 1. Statement and the coefficient-field requirement Let sigma_Q(Y)=QY and a(Q,Y) be a nonzero element of ℚ(Q,Y). Assume that for every sufficiently large positive integer n, product_(j=0)^(n-1) a(zeta_n,zeta_n^jY)=1, zeta_n=exp(2pi*i/n), (1.1) as a whole rational identity in Y. Then there exists f(Q,Y) in ℚ(Q,Y)^*, a(Q,Y)=f(Q,QY)/f(Q,Y). (1.2) No unramifiedness, limiting-root separation, or levelwise degree bound for Hilbert-90 gauges is assumed. The conclusion is generic rational descent. It does not assert that f is a unit at the ideal meridian or that it preserves an unspecified period pointing. The same conclusion over a subfield K of C holds if (1.1) is known at every primitive n-th root for the chosen coefficient embedding. For ℚ-coefficients this whole-root condition follows by cyclotomic Galois conjugation. For a number field a sufficient stronger marking is to know (1.1) for all coefficient conjugates. A single geometric embedding is not silently promoted to that condition. ## 2. Scaled roots supply all powers without a nonresonance assumption For a fixed positive integer k set xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N). Its order is m=N/gcd(k,N). Whole-root (1.1) gives the m-step transport identity at xi_N for all sufficiently large N. Its N-step transport consists of gcd(k,N) repetitions and is also one. Factor a over an algebraic splitting field as a(Q,Y)=r(Q)Y^s product_(i=1)^d(1-alpha_i(Q)Y) /product_(j=1)^e(1-beta_j(Q)Y). (2.1) Every alpha_i,beta_j is a nonzero algebraic function of Q. Its value may tend to zero or infinity at Q=1. For sufficiently large root orders the values themselves are finite and nonzero. The ordinary primitive-root product first gives s=0, r(zeta_n)^n=1 and d=e. It also gives equality of the multisets of n-th powers of the alpha and beta values. The fixed-rational scalar discreteness argument yields r(Q)=Q^(k_0), k_0 in Z. (2.2) Here is that argument in full. The identities |r(zeta_n)|=1 exclude a zero or pole of r at Q=1, so choose an analytic logarithm ell of r near one. Then L_n=n ell(exp(2pi*i/n)) belongs to 2pi*i Z. The expansion of this fixed analytic germ gives L_n=n ell(1)+2pi*i ell'(1)+O(1/n), with a convergent expansion in powers of 1/n after the linear term. Hence L_(n+1)-L_n=ell(1)+O(1/n^2). These differences lie in the discrete set 2pi*i Z, so ell(1) belongs to that set and r(1)=1. Choose the logarithm with ell(1)=0. The sequence L_n now converges in the same discrete set and is eventually 2pi*i k_0 for a fixed integer k_0. Thus r(zeta_n)=zeta_n^(k_0) at infinitely many roots. The rational function r(Q)-Q^(k_0) has infinitely many zeros and is therefore identically zero. This proves (2.2). At xi_N use its actual order m, not a primitive N-step product formula. Equality of the m-th power multisets, raised to the gcd(k,N)-th power, gives equality of their N-th power multisets. In particular sum_i alpha_i(xi_N)^N=sum_j beta_j(xi_N)^N (2.3) for every fixed k and all sufficiently large N. ## 3. Convergent Puiseux forms from a finite cover Put t=Log Q/(2pi*i), with the logarithm near Q=1. There is a positive integer e_0 such that, after t=s^(e_0), all branches in (2.1) are single-valued meromorphic functions of s near zero. Here is a direct justification of the needed analytic form. Choose a punctured t-disk avoiding other discriminant zeros and coefficient poles of the finite root polynomials. Local analytic roots give a finite covering there. Its monodromy is a permutation of finitely many roots. Taking e_0 divisible by the cycle lengths kills this monodromy, so the pulled-back roots are single-valued holomorphic functions on a punctured s-disk. Cauchy's elementary root bound, after division by the leading polynomial coefficient, bounds every root by a fixed power of |t|^(-1). Multiplying by a sufficient power of s then gives a bounded holomorphic function, which extends across zero. Hence each root is meromorphic there. Since no root is identically zero, it has a convergent form alpha_i(exp(2pi*i*t)) =a_i t^(nu_i) exp(lambda_i(t^(1/e_0))), (3.1) where a_i!=0, nu_i is rational and lambda_i is holomorphic with lambda_i(0)=0. Choose the branch t^(1/e_0)>0 on the positive t-axis, which contains all scaled roots used below. The beta branches have corresponding data b_j,mu_j,eta_j. Define A_i(t)=exp(lambda_i(t^(1/e_0))/t), B_j(t)=exp(eta_j(t^(1/e_0))/t). (3.2) These need not extend meromorphically across t=0. Each is of the specific form exp(P(s^(-1))) g(s), s=t^(1/e_0), (3.3) where P is a polynomial with no constant term and degree below e_0, and g is a holomorphic unit. Indeed separate the terms of lambda(s)/s^(e_0) with negative s exponents; the remainder is holomorphic. Multiplication by any algebraic/Puiseux weight changes g to a meromorphic function after a common further ramification. The next lemma permits these weights explicitly. ## 4. Weighted exponential--Puiseux sequence uniqueness Fix e>=1. Consider finitely many triples (nu,a,P), with nu rational, a!=0 complex and P a polynomial of degree below e with P(0)=0. Let g_(nu,a,P)(s) be meromorphic germs at zero. Merge identical triples by adding their g coefficients. If sum_(nu,a,P) N^(-nu N) a^N exp(P(N^(1/e))) g_(nu,a,P)(N^(-1/e))=0 (4.1) for every sufficiently large integer N, then every merged g is identically zero. **Oscillatory estimate.** If phi(x)=theta x+sum_(r=1)^(e-1)b_r x^(r/e), theta,b_r real, and either theta is nonzero modulo 2pi or some b_r is nonzero, then the Cesaro mean of exp(i phi(N)) is zero. If theta is nonzero modulo 2pi, partial sums of exp(i theta N) are bounded. Summation by parts bounds the sum through M by O(1+M^rho), where rho<1 is the highest fractional exponent; the total variation of exp(i sum b_r x^(r/e)) has that bound. If all b_r vanish the sum is bounded directly. If theta is zero modulo 2pi, let rho in (0,1) be the highest nonzero fractional exponent. Eventually |phi'(x)| is comparable to x^(rho-1), and |phi''(x)|=O(x^(rho-2)). The sum--integral error is O(M^rho), by integrating the derivative's absolute value over unit intervals. Integration by parts with 1/(i phi') bounds the integral by O(M^(1-rho)); its derivative term is bounded by the integral of |phi''|/|phi'|^2=O(x^(-rho)). Both bounds are o(M), proving the estimate. **Proof of (4.1).** If a merged coefficient is nonzero, choose successively among the finitely many such terms: 1. the smallest nu; 2. the largest modulus R=|a| at that nu; 3. the lexicographically largest vector of real coefficients of P, ordered from the highest power down; 4. the smallest Laurent order m of g among those remaining terms. Normalize by the common positive scale N^(-nu N) R^N exp(Re P(N^(1/e))) N^(-m/e). Every term outside these selected scales tends to zero: the successive comparisons are on the N log N, N, fractional-power and log N scales. The normalized equality becomes sum_l c_l exp(i phi_l(N))+o(1)=0, (4.2) with at least one nonzero leading Laurent coefficient c_l. The residual phases are distinct modulo constants: equal phases would have the same complex a and the same complex P, and would already have been merged. Their pairwise differences therefore satisfy the oscillatory estimate above. Multiply (4.2) by exp(-i phi_j(N)) and take Cesaro means. Every cross term has mean zero, and the error tends to zero, so c_j=0. This contradicts the selection of m. It proves the lemma. In particular, distinct pairs (nu,a) remain distinguishable when their amplitudes are finite sums of (3.3). This weighted conclusion is stronger than the earlier meromorphic-amplitude lemma and is the form usable for rational partial-fraction source coefficients. ## 5. Branch pairing from all scaled power sums At xi_N, equation (3.1) gives exactly alpha_i(xi_N)^N =N^(-nu_i N)(a_i k^(nu_i))^N A_i(k/N)^k. (5.1) For fixed k the amplitudes in this formula are finite sums of (3.3), with the same common ramification. Apply the lemma to (2.3). Distinct (nu,a) remain distinct after replacing a by a k^nu. Thus for every pair (nu,a), sum_(alpha_i in (nu,a)) A_i(kt)^k =sum_(beta_j in (nu,a)) B_j(kt)^k. Rescale the argument and take k=1,...,d. For each (nu,a) this gives equality of the first d power sums of its A and B functions. Newton identities, padding by zeros to length d, identify their multisets over the common field of meromorphic functions on the ramified punctured disk. Their entries are nonzero exponentials, so the group cardinalities agree. A fixed permutation pairs A_i=B_(pi(i)) as function germs. The paired branches have the same nu and a. Their quotient is therefore exp(lambda_i-eta_(pi(i))). The equality of A and B says that (lambda_i-eta_(pi(i)))/t has exponential one. It is holomorphic on a connected ramified punctured disk, even if initially it could have a pole at zero. A holomorphic function with values in the discrete set 2pi*i Z is constant. Hence lambda_i-eta_(pi(i))=2pi*i k_i t, alpha_i(Q)=Q^(k_i) beta_(pi(i))(Q), k_i in Z. (5.2) This proves the required integral Q-shift pairing without any assumption on ramification or limiting values. ## 6. Finite divisor flow and rational descent For k_i>0 use the finite gauge product_(u=0)^(k_i-1)(1-Q^u beta_(pi(i))(Q)Y). For k_i<0 use the inverse product over k_i<=u<0. Their product, times Y^(k_0), gives (1.2) over a finite splitting field. Its numerator and denominator Y-degrees are each at most |k_0|+sum_i |k_i|. (6.1) The finite divisor flow is unique on each infinite Q-shift orbit. Consequently it is invariant under the Galois group of the splitting field over ℚ(Q). The product part has value one at Y=0, fixing its remaining scalar. It therefore descends to ℚ(Q,Y). This also proves descent over K under the stated whole-root hypothesis. The remaining generic scalar ambiguity is a function of Q alone; a specified regular anchor can fix it. The theorem does not discard a zero or pole of the gauge at the ideal meridian or replace the required source/cut lattice by a generic isomorphism. ## 7. Scope for the actual A-period program The actual reduced knot state has a rational Q-operator. This places its rational coefficient constructions in the correct cyclotomic field. However, the theorem applies to a specified rank-one comparison coefficient with the full transport identity (1.1). The current root-state data do not automatically construct that comparison or prove its norm characters agree with a geometric regulator realization. Those remain substantive inputs. The proof concerns fixed rational comparison data. It neither trivializes the whole quantum A-module nor asserts algebraicity of the selected Mellin period, which is transcendental for the adequate class. Algebraic comparison maps and transcendental marked periods remain compatible. [Ramified and weighted audit](../experiments/audit_full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Results](../experiments/full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent_results.json).

The bounded, unrescaled overlap functional has its weak support there, but may converge to ZERO. The hard exponential issue is now explicit in |P_N|=|chi_N| N^(k-1) ||W_N u_N|| |omega_N(1)|. The overlap can be exponentially small; dividing by it would invalidate the bounded-moment argument. This source-specific support theorem does not yet prove (U), geometric survival, or the singular joint regulator comparison. It makes those next estimates precise without replacing the original closing by a positive trace.

title: The fusion kernel has a rational symplectic chart with a retained source wall
text: # The fusion kernel has a rational symplectic chart with a retained source wall 27 October 2026. The explicit actual fusion kernel determines a birational symplectic relation on its regular interior symbol chart. Its right Euler argument is a ratio of relative MOMENTA, not a physical position by definition. The exact finite kernel also has a nonzero bottom wall, and the original source detects that wall after an actual crossing. The Euler basis orientation is fixed by the original cap; reversing it gives a different boundary valuation. These results make the local comparison concrete while retaining the source issue. They do not prove that the selected finite root period has a nonzero geometric image or the hyperbolic-volume exponent. ## 1. Kernel, shifts and the exact bottom wall Use the notation of [the actual fusion-clock proof](actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.md): C_(u,v;a,j)=x^(u-a) F_a F_v/[F_(a-u) F_j], F_r=(Q;Q)_r, 0<=u<=a<N, v=j+a-u<N, and zero outside that support. Let S_a increase the relative a label by one, with its top arrow zero. Let S_u similarly increase the physical first index. Put D_a=diag(Q^a), D_j=diag(Q^j), U=diag(Q^u), V=diag(Q^v), and let Pi_0 project onto physical u=0 and Pi_top onto relative a=N-1. There are the following exact finite-kernel identities: C D_aD_j=UV C, (1) C F_j=F_2 C, (2) C S_a-S_u C(1-QD_a) =Pi_0 C S_a-(1-Q^N)S_u C Pi_top. (3) Here F_j is the balanced raising matrix on the relative j head; F_2 is the same physical second-head lowering matrix. Equations (1)--(3) hold for the displayed truncated kernel also at generic Q where F_1,...,F_(N-1) are units. This generic-Q assertion is only about the explicit kernel, not full generic-q braid fusion. For (1), use u+v=a+j on every nonzero entry. Equation (2) follows by consecutive j,v coefficients, or from the fact that physical F_2 commutes with f_total and takes the seed e_0 tensor e_j to (1-Q^(j+1))e_0 tensor e_(j+1). Its two top endpoints both vanish. For (3), at u>0 and a<N-1 compare C_(u,v;a+1,j) =(1-Q^(a+1)) C_(u-1,v;a,j). The factorial F_(a+1-u) and the exponent u-a-1 agree on both sides. Excluded support also agrees. At u=0 only the first term can survive, giving Pi_0 C S_a. At a=N-1 the left first term is zero by truncation, and the other term supplies exactly the displayed top correction. This is an entry proof at EVERY endpoint. At the actual root Q^N=1, total lowering is intertwined exactly: C S_a C^-1=f_total=F_1+K_1^-1 F_2. Thus the bottom wall in (3) is the physical operator E_bottom=Pi_0 f_total=x^-1 Pi_0 tensor F_2. (4) It cannot be discarded on the strength of a regular interior symbol identity. For example at N=2 take x=i, eta=exp(pi*i/4), and the original positive crossing. Its coefficient from e_0 tensor e_1 to e_1 tensor e_0 is eta^-1. With the original pivotal cap g_0=-i, the original highest-input/all-ones-output source gives Lambda_phys(R_+ E_bottom)=-2 eta^-1 !=0. (5) This is a literal original-word/source value. No new state or unweighted trace is used. The uninserted cap of E_bottom alone can vanish; that does not make its word-dependent source zero. ## 2. A regular interior canonical graph Use commuting interior clocks A,J for the relative labels and U,V for physical labels. Let K=A/U and impose AJ=UV. With logarithms chosen locally, the factorial kernel has the generating expression S=-Li_2(A)-Li_2(V)+Li_2(K)+Li_2(J)-log(x)log(K). (6) Its exponent is obtained directly from the finite factorial atoms: the leading logarithmic primitive of F_r is [Li_2(1)-Li_2(Q^r)]/log Q. The four constants cancel in (6). Equivalently one can define the interior symbol graph by the coefficient-shift ratios; no convergence of growing-level periods is required to define or verify the following algebraic graph. Write p_A,p_J,p_U,p_V for exponentials of logarithmic covectors. The kernel convention is that theta_out-theta_in=dS+lambda*dlog[UV/(AJ)], theta_in=log(p_A)dlog A+log(p_J)dlog J, theta_out=log(p_U)dlog U+log(p_V)dlog V. Differentiating (6) and putting t=exp(lambda) gives p_U=t*x*(1-K), p_V=t*(1-V), p_A=t*x*(1-K)/(1-A), p_J=t*(1-J), AJ=UV. (7) This convention matters: a raising operator on basis indices acts on wavefunctions by a BACKWARD argument shift. It therefore has principal value the inverse of the corresponding p coordinate. Equations (7) give the explicit forward map z=x*p_J/p_A, K=1-(1-A)(1-J)/z, U=A/K, V=J*K, p_U=(1-A)*p_A, p_V=p_J*(1-J*K)/(1-J). (8) This is a birational map between nonempty open cotangent tori. All clocks and momenta are nonzero; the factors K, 1-A, 1-J, 1-V and their inverse-chart counterparts are kept invertible. Its rational inverse is K=1-p_U*(1-V)/(x*p_V), A=U*K, J=V/K, p_A=p_U/(1-A), p_J=p_V*(1-J)/(1-V). (9) Substitution proves both inverse identities. On the graph AJ=UV, the constraint differential vanishes, so (7) gives theta_out-theta_in=dS. Taking an exterior derivative proves preservation of dlog p_A wedge dlog A+dlog p_J wedge dlog J. Thus (8) is symplectic. This is a direct graph theorem rather than an inference from a dimension count or presumed quantum limit. The exact relations underlying it include (1)--(3), physical total lowering and the polynomial right-Euler relation already proved: x(1-U^-1 A_operator)f_R=(1-Q A_operator)(1-J_operator). In the interior, right multiplication by f shifts (a,j) to (a+1,j-1). Its wavefunction symbol is p_J/p_A. Thus its right Euler argument has the definite symbol z=x*p_J/p_A=(1-A)(1-J)/(1-A/U). (10) The last expression is valid on this regular commutative chart. At the actual finite root, its apparent denominator is nilpotent and has no inverse. Formula (10) is not an evaluation homomorphism from the finite root representation to a geometric character. ## 3. Exact Euler conjugation fixes the orientation On the relative regular module let R_f be RIGHT multiplication by f, and now let z=x R_f be the nilpotent MATRIX. Set u(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) z^r/F_r, v(z)=u(z)^-1, T_u=u(z), T_v=v(z). At the actual root z^N=0, all 1-Q^k z are units and u(Qz)=(1-z)u(z). The relative clocks obey D_a R_f=Q R_f D_a and D_j R_f=Q^-1 R_f D_j. Consequently T_u D_a T_v=(1-z)^-1 D_a, T_u D_j T_v=(1-Q^-1 z)D_j, T_v D_a T_u=(1-z)D_a, T_v D_j T_u=(1-Q^-1 z)^-1 D_j. (11) These are exact ordered finite matrices. Their clock product is unchanged; the Q-shift in the second factor is required for this. Let the actual word have fused RIGHT coefficient a. Its cap theorem uses b=u^-1 a u. Right multiplication reverses composition, so R_b=T_u R_a T_v, W=C R_a C^-1=(C T_v) R_b (C T_v)^-1. (12) Thus the new-to-physical basis fixed by the actual cap is C T_v, not C T_u. With D_phys=(e_0 ell) tensor K_2^(1-N), its complete matrix co-source is transported EXACTLY as D_new=(C T_v)^-1 D_phys (C T_v). (13) Weighted trace proves the same original period on every physical matrix. Restricting (13) to the right-word algebra recovers precisely Lambda_new(b)=gamma*rho_0[J_Q(z)b], J_Q(z)=1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)], gamma=N(xy)^(1-N)Q. (14) Indeed the original cap is gamma*rho_0[v(Q^2z) a u(z)]; substitute a=u b v and use v(Q^2z)u(z)=J_Q(z). All original scalar lines can be retained externally, and multiply both sides unchanged. There is an additional orientation distinction. An operator conjugation gives the PULLBACK by the inverse of a forward point map. Hence the symbol point map of T_v, which occurs in the actual basis C T_v, sends (A,J,p_A,p_J) -> (A/(1-z), J*(1-z), p_A,p_J). (15) Using the operator formula in (11) as the forward point map would reverse (15) and produce an incorrect boundary interpretation. ## 4. The two Euler orientations have different boundary valuations Put delta=1-z, and hold regular generic input A,J fixed. Compose the forward map (15) with (8), and put D_plus=A-AJ*delta+(J-1)*delta^2. For the ACTUAL new-to-physical basis C T_v one obtains U=A*z/D_plus, V=J*D_plus/z, U -> 1, V -> AJ. (16) The corresponding p_U=(1-A/delta)p_A has a simple pole for generic nonzero A. Thus there is a real singular symbol chart, but its first clock has valuation zero, with limiting value one. The OPPOSITE basis C T_u instead uses A*delta,J/delta in (8). Writing D_minus=J-AJ*delta+(A-1)*delta^2, it gives U=A*z*delta^2/D_minus, V=J*D_minus/(z*delta^2), delta^-2 U -> A/J, delta^2 V -> J^2. (17) Therefore an apparent match to a quadratic escaping geometric position can select the wrong Euler orientation if one tracks only valuations. Formula (17) is not the forward primal map of the word basis dictated by the original source in (12). Neither calculation identifies this fused first-plus-tail clock with the internal second-meridian position of the universal-cut geometric chart. Such a marking would require an actual word and source comparison. The original first source is highest input; the prior regular geometric block used a suitable high-input phase. Those are related by exact Ward identities, not by forgetting the bottom source wall (3)--(5). ## 5. Scope and independent checks The regular local canonical graph is now explicit and symplectic, and the exact source/basis transformation is specified. The finite endpoint wall is also explicit and is detected by an original word. This is usable input to a whole period transform. It is not a proof that the selected class crosses to the marked geometric A-component, that its coefficient is subexponential, or that its global norm has the hyperbolic-volume growth. The [audit](../experiments/audit_fusion_canonical_source_chart.py) and [saved results](../experiments/fusion_canonical_source_chart_results.json) pass twelve exact kernel cases and six actual root Euler/source cases at N=2,...,7. They check both boundary terms, exact Euler clock orientation, literal signed-word source transport and nonzero word-coupled bottom-wall periods. A separate symbolic calculation checks the rational inverse and all six independent logarithmic Poisson brackets, as well as both distinct Euler boundary limits. The proofs above establish the identities; finite checks verify their conventions and endpoints.

title: An exact pointed unit comparison for the factorial source factor
text: # An exact pointed unit comparison for the factorial source factor Proof and independent audit, 27 October 2026. The normal quantum factorial residual has the stated whole Gamma profile. More strongly, its middle component is exactly a holomorphic unit times the actual root Weyl splitting after the correct normal-coordinate change. The unit preserves all finite resonance zeros, is normalized at the complete point, and tends uniformly to one. This is an actual scalar source-factor comparison, not a comparison of the full knot period. Use the exact factorial frames of [the integral-color source](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md) and the marked root splitting of [the balanced Weyl cocycle](twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md). ## 1. Exact normal product and its whole limit Put \[ c=2\pi i,\quad H_0=c/N,\quad H=H_0+ca/N^2,\quad q=e^{H/2},\quad M=-q^N=e^{ca/(2N)}, \] and set \[ b=a_N=\frac{a}{1+a/N},\qquad J(x)=\frac{2\sinh(x/2)}x,\quad J(0)=1 . \] Then \(Hb=ca/N\). For the actual residual diagonal factor \[ V_{N,j}(a)=\frac{{N-1\choose j}_{q,\mathrm{sym}}}{M^j}, \] the exact identity is \[ V_{N,j}(a) =e^{-Hbj/2} \prod_{r=1}^j \frac{\sinh[H(r-b)/2]}{\sinh(Hr/2)}. \tag{1} \] There is no extra sign: \(HN=c+Hb\) gives \(\sinh[H(N-r)/2]=\sinh[H(r-b)/2]\). For \(j/N=T_N\) in a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\), uniformly on every compact complex \(a\)-set, \[ N^aV_{N,j}(a) =\Phi_a(T_N)+O((1+\log N)/N),\qquad \Phi_a(T)=\frac{G(T)^{-a}}{\Gamma(1-a)}, \tag{2} \] where \[ G(T)=\frac{e^{cT}-1}{c},\qquad \log G(T)=\log\!\left(\frac{\sin\pi T}{\pi}\right) +cT/2. \tag{3} \] Positive real \(N\) specifies \(N^a=e^{a\log N}\). Here is a proof uniform through integer resonances. Factor (1) into \[ e^{-Hbj/2} \prod_{r=1}^j(1-b/r) \prod_{r=1}^j\frac{J(H(r-b))}{J(Hr)}. \tag{4} \] The Euler product implies \[ j^b\prod_{r=1}^j(1-b/r) =\Gamma(1-b)^{-1}+O(1/j) \] uniformly on compact \(b\)-sets. One may prove this directly using \((1-b/r)e^{b/r}=1+O(r^{-2})\) and \(H_j-\log j=\gamma+O(1/j)\). The product convergence is uniform and absolute, including its zeros; no relative estimate at a zero is used. On a fixed zero-free neighborhood of \([0,cT_{\max}]\), choose \(B=\log J\), \(B(0)=0\). Taylor expansion and a Riemann sum give \[ \sum_{r=1}^j[B(H(r-b))-B(Hr)] =-bB(Hj)+O(1/N). \] The remaining factors have limits \(e^{-caT/2}\), \(T^{-a}\), and \(J(cT)^{-a}\). Their product is (3). Finally \(N^{a-b}=1+O((1+\log N)/N)\), which explains the stated error. All errors in (2) are absolute. At positive integer \(a\) the limit can vanish. ## 2. The actual Weyl factor has the opposite Gamma profile Let \(Q_0=e^{H_0}\), and let \(\beta_N\) be the exact root splitting, with its prescribed even phase: \[ L_N=\begin{cases}(N-1)/2&N\text{ odd},\\N/2-1&N\text{ even}, \end{cases} \] \[ \beta_N(M)= \prod_{r=1}^{L_N}\frac{1-M^2Q_0^r}{1-Q_0^r} \times \begin{cases}1&N\text{ odd},\\ (1+iM)/(1+i)&N\text{ even}. \end{cases} \tag{5} \] For \(M=e^{ca/(2N)}\), \[ N^{-a}\beta_N(M) \longrightarrow \frac{G(1/2)^a}{\Gamma(1+a)} =\Phi_{-a}(1/2) \tag{6} \] uniformly on compact \(a\)-sets, with absolute error \(O(1/N)\). Indeed each quotient in (5) is \[ e^{H_0a/2}\frac{r+a}{r} \frac{J(H_0(r+a))}{J(H_0r)}. \] The same Euler-product and smooth-product calculation proves (6). The even prefactor tends to one uniformly. Its marked phase introduces no extra constant. In particular \[ G(1/2)=i/\pi,\qquad\log G(1/2)=-\log\pi+\pi i/2 . \] ## 3. Exact finite comparison, including every normal zero The proper opposite meridian coordinate is \[ \widetilde M_N(a)=e^{-H_0b/2},\qquad b=a_N, \] not \(e^{-H_0a/2}\). At \(j=L_N\), there is the exact identity \[ V_{N,L_N}(a)=u_N(a)\,\beta_N(\widetilde M_N(a)), \tag{7} \] with \[ u_N(a)=e^{-(H-H_0)bL_N/2} \prod_{r=1}^{L_N} \frac{J(H(r-b))J(H_0r)} {J(Hr)J(H_0(r-b))} \times \begin{cases}1&N\text{ odd},\\ (1+i)/(1+i\widetilde M_N)&N\text{ even}. \end{cases} \tag{8} \] Equation (7) follows by factoring the two sine products; their entire factors \((r-b)/r\) cancel before evaluating zeros. Thus it holds at the resonance points by holomorphic continuation. All factors in (8) are units on \(|b|<N/2\). To check this without assuming separation from integer \(b\), the only zeros of \(J\) are \(ck\), \(k\ne0\). Using \(H=H_0/(1-b/N)\), each possible zero of the four displayed arguments has \(|b|\ge N/2\) for \(r\le L_N\). The even prefactor likewise first vanishes at \(|b|=N/2\). Thus every fixed compact normal set is contained in this unit domain for all sufficiently large \(N\). In particular \[ u_N(0)=1,\qquad u_N(a)=1+O(1/N) \tag{9} \] uniformly on compact sets. For the bound in (9), take \(B=\log J\) on a fixed zero-free neighborhood of \([0,c/2]\) and put \(\Delta H=H-H_0=O(N^{-2})\). The logarithm of each four-factor quotient is \[ \Delta H\left[(r-b)B'(H_0(r-b))-rB'(H_0r)\right] +O(\Delta H^2r^2). \] The bracket is \(O(1)\), not \(O(r)\), by differentiating \(xB'(H_0x)\) over the bounded displacement \(b\). Summing \(O(N)\) terms gives \(O(1/N)\); the quadratic remainders, phase and even prefactor have that same bound. There is no uncontrolled logarithmic loss here. The coordinate correction is essential for a unit statement. The quantum factor has zeros at \(a=kN/(N-k)\), whereas the uncorrected \(\beta_N(e^{-H_0a/2})\) has zeros at \(a=k\). Their limits agree, but their ratio is not a unit at those finite-\(N\) divisors. Using \(b=a_N\) aligns them exactly. It also matches the marked power character exactly. On the integral-color curve \(M_{\mathrm{col}}=e^{Hb/2}\), the inverse-flux period of [the peripheral-character calculation](gauss_wall_flux_and_actual_peripheral_character.md) is \[ \chi_H(M_{\mathrm{col}})=e^{-2c\log M_{\mathrm{col}}/H}=e^{-cb}. \] The root meridian used in (7) satisfies \[ \widetilde M_N^{\,2N}=e^{-cb}=\chi_H(M_{\mathrm{col}}). \] Thus its inverse-power character is the opposite oriented one. This is an identity of the specified whole functions; it does not assume an off-root horizontal equation for a knot state. ## 4. Normalized difference line and its actual Weyl norm The whole limiting function satisfies \[ \Phi_{a+1}(T)=-\frac{a}{G(T)}\Phi_a(T). \tag{10} \] Its paired norm is \[ \Phi_a(T)\Phi_{-a}(T) =\frac1{\Gamma(1-a)\Gamma(1+a)} =\frac{\sin\pi a}{\pi a} =\frac{2\sinh(z/2)}z,\qquad z=ca. \tag{11} \] The normalization can be checked without importing a reflection formula: apply (6) with \(a,-a\) to the already proved finite identity \(\beta_N(M)\beta_N(M^{-1})=c_N(M)^{-1}\). Its right side is exactly \(\sinh(z/2)/(N\sinh(z/(2N)))\), which tends to (11). The \(T\)-dependent factors cancel, so the result holds for every interior \(T\). The norm line has shift \[ (a+1)H(a+1)=-aH(a),\qquad H(a)=\sin(\pi a)/(\pi a). \] Cocycle orientation must remain explicit: \[ c_N(e^{z/(2N)})\to\Gamma(1-a)\Gamma(1+a),\qquad c_N^{-1}\to H(a). \] Equations (7)--(11) provide a pointed local functional comparison of actual scalar source factors, with their zeros and marks retained. They do not identify the full moving-\(q\) color state with a fixed-root meridian state, construct a star/current map for its whole word, or prove a geometric regular-profile norm. ## 5. Independent check of the full-head extension The stronger [full-head theorem](full_head_gamma_source_transport.md) has also been checked directly. With \(n=N-1\), \(L=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), and partial \(\beta_j(M)=(M^2Q_0;Q_0)_j/(Q_0;Q_0)_j\), its complement is \[ \beta_j(M)\beta_{n-j}(M^{-1}) =M^{2j-n}\frac{S_N(M^2)}{NM^n}. \tag{12} \] Indeed reversing the \(n-j\) suffix indices sends each ratio to \(M^{-2}(1-M^2Q_0^r)/(1-Q_0^r)\). Multiplying that suffix by the prefix gives \(M^{-2(n-j)}S_N(M^2)/N\), proving (12). Thus the upper source section is defined by the canceled complementary product; no inverse is evaluated at a zero. For \(j\le L\), the exact unit is (8) with product length \(j\) and no even-level scalar prefactor. Its \(O(1/N)\) estimate is uniform over all prefix lengths by the same double difference. For \(j>L\), symmetric q-binomial reflection gives \[ V_{N,j}=M_{\mathrm{col}}^{n-2j}V_{N,n-j}; \] the remaining upper comparison character has logarithm \((H-H_0)b(n-2j)/2=O(1/N)\), uniformly in \(j\). This proves the claimed whole-head diagonal unit estimate. The retained chirp comparison has the exact exponent \[ \log (U_{\mathrm{col}}/U_0)_j =ca\left(\frac{j}{2N}-\frac{j(j+1)}{4N^2}\right). \] It and its inverse are uniformly bounded in every common diagonal metric on a fixed compact normal set. The same conclusion holds for the whole source comparison \(T_N\). The coupon identities in the full-head theorem are exact coordinate statements. Both frames act on the same original balanced column \((1,\ldots,1)^t\) and dual row \((1,\ldots,1)/N\); their respective coordinate maps are \(U_{\mathrm{col}}\operatorname{diag}V\) and \(U_0\operatorname{diag}B\). Their quotient is \(T_N\), hence the columns, rows and rank-one coupons transform by \(T_N\), \(T_N^{-1}\), and conjugation. Position moments and endpoint projectors commute with this diagonal comparison. At a resonance this statement uses the paired fractional lattices, whose abstract tensor pairing remains one; their singular coordinate arrays cannot be specialized separately. The root chart is a meromorphic gauge of the same actual root head. All root operators must therefore conjugate with the coupon. No equality with the moving-q crossing follows: [the independent spectral proof](crossing_normal_spectra_obstruction.md) rules out even arbitrary scalar-adjusted same-fiber similarity.

title: Independent audit of the Gauss-wall finite current map
text:
# Independent audit of the Gauss-wall finite current map 27 October 2026. Both [the actual wall/cut-current theorem](actual_gauss_wall_cut_current_complex.md) and [the elevated-source restrictions](degree_elevated_wall_source_and_divided_ward.md) pass after the explicit raw-to-matrix factor \(N\) is retained. This audit checks their finite identities and scope; it supplies no internal Gaussian source comparison. ## 1. Residue, anchored primitives and the source class With \(F=1-\eta v\), direct substitution \(d\log\eta=-dF/(1-F)-d\log v\) gives \[ \operatorname{Res}_{F=0} \left(- rac{d\eta}{\eta}\wedge rac{\Omega_0}{F}ight) =\Omega_0=-dT\wedge d\log v . \] Thus both stated primitive signs are correct. The beta integral is \[  inom{N-1}{j}\int_0^1t^j(1-t)^{N-1-j}dt=1/N . \] Their difference has coefficients \(C_{ij}v^{i-j}/N\). Every off-diagonal coefficient is exact on \(\mathbb C^*\), leaving precisely \((\operatorname{Tr}C/N)[d\log v]\). For the actual unweighted cut \(C=F_N(Y)I\), the class is \(F_N(Y)[d\log v]\), nonzero as a family by its ordinary anchor. This does not assert nonvanishing of every complete value. Angular integration at \(T=1/2\) kills off-diagonal terms. The two incomplete-beta rows have total weights \(1/2\), and reversal gives \(w_{N,N-1-j}=1/N-w_{N,j}\). Hence the actual meridian Weyl matrix interchanges them, while every diagonal Gamma/frame conjugation preserves each. All normalization statements refer to the paired source lattices at a singular meridian. ## 2. Finite endpoints and the original \(1/N\) For a zero-extended array \(J\), the coefficient at an interior index in the backward difference of the positive head weights is \( inom Nj/(N2^N)\). At zero the extra coefficient is \(-1/N\); at \(N\) the binomial endpoint remains. Therefore \[ \lambda^+_{\mathrm{head}}((S-1)J)=B_N(J)-J_0/N,\qquad \lambda^-_{\mathrm{head}}((S-1)J)=-B_N(J)+J_N/N . \] The negative and positive tails in the relative extensions supply \(+J_0/N\) and \(-J_N/N\), respectively. Their sum is exactly the ordinary normalized full-index sum. The \(j=N\) entry in \(B_N\) cannot be dropped. The original Green arrays already include \(1/N\). The current note correctly sets \(I_{\mathrm{mat}}=NI_{\mathrm{raw}}\) and \(J_{\mathrm{mat}}=NJ_{\mathrm{raw}}\) before applying matrix-normalized rows. In raw coordinates the rows are \(N\lambda^\pm\), the wall row is \(NB_N\), and the endpoint terms are \(J_{{\mathrm{raw}},0}\), \(J_{{\mathrm{raw}},N}\). This is an exact conversion, not an absorbed endpoint constant. The conclusion \(B_N(J_{\mathrm{cut}})=0\) is justified for the stated UNWEIGHTED original cut: each hemisphere is \(F_N/2\), its actual scalar annihilator kills this, and all other zero-extended flow differences sum to zero. The proof does not extend scalar cut behavior to an arbitrary coupled word. Unsummed currents and their moment factors remain present before those sums. ## 3. The elevated source restrictions are exact The degree-\(N\) source pairing is the literal primitive tensor construction on the already proved two-dimensional source. Its row has binomial multiplicities and gives the desired \(B_N\) with the stated extra factor \(1/N\), not \(1/(N+1)\). It does not prove compatibility with the true divided Hopf coproduct and its mixed terms. On \(\operatorname{End}(V_N^{\otimes b})\), integer matrix weights lie between \(-b(N-1)\) and \(b(N-1)\). The finite-head divided E-adjoint lowers that weight by \(N\). Hence its \(2b\)-th power is zero, whereas the primitive \(\operatorname{Sym}^N\) action has nonzero \(e^{2b}\) for \(N\ge2b\). Irreducibility in characteristic zero proves the claimed obstruction to any nonzero full-SL2 intertwiner into this space or a subquotient with the same bound. It leaves the stated Borel, tail and non-equivariant routes open. Cancellation of \(1-Q^N\) in the quantum binomial gives exactly \[ d_{N,j}= rac{(-1)^{j-1}Q^{-j(j-1)/2}}{1-Q^j}. \] Thus the trial diagonal adapter has middle magnitude \(2 inom Nj\sin(\pi j/N)\) and endpoint magnitude one. The central binomial coefficient and sine bounds prove both displayed exponential condition-number lower bounds. This conclusion is relative to the explicitly specified trial identification of endpoint and middle normal degrees. The literal level-two stabilized crossing has cut entries \(1\) and \(2w-1\), including its original pivot and twist. Its normalized transfer polynomial is \(w\); after a scalar knot cut it is \(Fw\). The auxiliary transfer source is then \(\operatorname{diag}(0,2F)\), giving hemisphere values \(F/4,3F/4\), as stated. This directly prevents identifying a second transfer reflection with the actual cut Weyl action. These statements specify real finite co-sources and current constraints. They neither identify their Gaussian images nor show that the selected geometric contribution survives. ## 4. The centralizer normal-moment refinement also passes The subsequent [normal residue/current theorem](centralizer_normal_residue_and_actual_cut_moments.md) has been checked independently in its current form. Expansion of \(1/(1-\eta v)\) gives \(\operatorname{Res}_E(b_N^h
u_{\mathrm{cut}})=-(-T)^h\Omega\). The south representative must be \(P(b_S-1)\). Its difference from the north polynomial is divisible by the Gauss-wall factor; the stated \(\Xi_h\) integrates its remaining normal powers exactly, with no logarithmic E residue. Contraction by \(V_b=-\eta\partial_a\) gives \(P(b)d\eta\wedge dv/F\). The two current residues are exactly \([P(-T)-P(0)]d\log v\) and \([P(-T)-P(-1)]d\log v\). Their difference is the retained endpoint class \([P(0)-P(-1)]d\log v\). With a nonconstant source kernel the product correction is essential: \[ d\,\iota_{V_b}(P f_C
u_{\mathrm{cut}}) =(P'f_C-XP\partial_Tf_C)
u_{\mathrm{cut}}. \] Its residue equals minus the differential of the current residue, as required when \(d\eta/\eta\) is written first. The Bernstein integration-by-parts identity (17), including both endpoints and its dimension-\(N-1\) target, is correct. The correct paired co-source uses rising-factorial Toeplitz moments; the falling-factorial symbol map cannot replace it against a general kernel. The [exact dual clock theorem](dual_clock_normal_cut_source.md) now extends this to the whole cut clock and to bounded normalized cut-position moments with pole order independent N. This is the normalized TRACE extension. Its agreement with the original average cut holds for the actual conserving diagonal arrays, not arbitrary off-diagonal Ward matrices. The raw normalized b-moments remain uniform interval moments \((-1)^h/(h+1)\) and have Hankel matrices of unbounded rank. This prevents a shortcut to a finite critical algebra in the FRAMING variable; it does not obstruct a finite isolated TRANSVERSE critical algebra after the required framing pushforward. The internal-transfer/second-framing and Gaussian-source maps remain additional constructions.

title: Independent Gauss-wall cycle and peripheral-flux calculation
text: # Independent Gauss-wall cycle and peripheral-flux calculation Proof and audit, 27 October 2026. The fixed-meridian physical and exceptional spheres differ by a nonzero integral wall-torus class. This gives an explicit Gysin obstruction, stronger than an obstruction only to section homotopies. The meridian detour transfers the charge to a peripheral logarithm and changes the retained \(SL_2\) lift. The actual quantum wall residues and the inverse-flux character have the stated normalizations below. This independently checks [the meridian wall theorem](meridian_homotopy_wall_and_source_residues.md) and [the flux/peripheral character](gauss_wall_flux_and_actual_peripheral_character.md). It does not identify a quantum source pushforward or a volume norm. ## 1. The cut divisor and its closed detecting form are global On \(Y\), the two charts have \[ V=v^{-1},\qquad \eta'=-v^2\eta,\qquad a'=v-v^2a. \] The fixed-ambient matrix entry \[ F=\mu_{11}=1-\eta v=1+\eta'V \] is one global function. In particular the south expression has a plus sign. Using \(1-\eta'V\) would select the other diagonal entry, not another expression for this same divisor. Its zero divisor is \[ D\simeq\mathbb G_{m,v}\times\mathbb A^1_a,\qquad\eta=1/v. \] The closed form \[ \Xi=\frac{dv\wedge d\eta}{F} =d\log F\wedge d\log v =\frac{dV\wedge d\eta'}{F} \tag{1} \] is regular everywhere on \(Y\setminus D\); the displayed affine fractions remove its apparent flag-coordinate poles. Its residue is \(d\log v\). Put \(c=2\pi i\), \(T=va\), and orient the compact source by \[ v=\sqrt{T/(1-T)}e^{i\phi},\quad a=\sqrt{T(1-T)}e^{-i\phi},\quad \Omega=dv\wedge da=-i\,dT\wedge d\phi. \] For the exceptional sphere \(\eta=0\), the pullback of \(\Xi\) is zero. For the physical sphere \(\eta=(1-e^{-cT})/v\), it is \(c\Omega\). Hence \[ \int_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{phys}}}\Xi=-c^2=4\pi^2,\qquad \int_{\Gamma_E}\Xi=0. \tag{2} \] This already excludes any homology between them in \(Y\setminus D\), without requiring a proposed homotopy to preserve its flag coordinates. ## 2. Integral Gysin class and its orientation The radial three-chain \(\eta=\lambda\eta_{\mathrm{phys}}\) has \[ F=1-\lambda+\lambda e^{-cT}. \] It meets \(D\) once in the transverse \((\lambda,T)\) plane, at \(\lambda=T=1/2\), along the circle \[ \gamma_v:\quad v=e^{i\phi},\quad a=1/(2v),\quad\eta=1/v. \] Near it, \[ F=-2(\lambda-1/2)+\pi i(T-1/2)+\text{higher terms}. \] Thus the complex-normal orientation is opposite the \((\lambda,T)\) orientation, and the oriented intersection is \(-\gamma_v\). Define the tube by a positive complex-normal circle followed by the positive \(v\)-circle. Excision gives \[ [\Gamma_{\mathrm{phys}}]-[\Gamma_E]=-\operatorname{Tube}[\gamma_v]. \tag{3} \] Its period checks the sign: \[ \int_{\operatorname{Tube}\gamma_v}\Xi =(2\pi i)\int_{\gamma_v}d\log v=c^2. \] This tube is a generator, rather than a possible torsion correction. The affine-bundle projection \(Y\to\mathbb P^1\) has contractible two-dimensional fibres. A continuous section and affine fibre contraction give a deformation to \(\Gamma_E\). Hence \(H_3(Y,\mathbb Z)=0\), \(H_2(Y,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\). A normal neighborhood of \(D\) has the explicit normal coordinate \(F\), and the relative homology shifts that of \(D\simeq\mathbb C^*\times\mathbb C\) by two. Its long exact sequence gives \[ 0\longrightarrow H_1(D,\mathbb Z) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Tube}}H_2(Y\setminus D,\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow H_2(Y,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow0 . \] The following intersection map is zero because the generator \(\Gamma_E\) is disjoint from \(D\). Consequently \(H_2(Y\setminus D,\mathbb Z)\simeq\mathbb Z^2\), split by \(\Gamma_E\), and (3) is its nonzero wall component. ## 3. Meridian variation transfers the charge For a retained eigenvalue \(m\), the resolved meridian is \[ \mu=\begin{pmatrix} m-\eta v&\eta\\ (m-m^{-1})v-\eta v^2&m^{-1}+\eta v \end{pmatrix}, \quad \eta'=(m-m^{-1})v-v^2\eta. \tag{4} \] It has determinant one and the stated eigenflag. The global cut function is \(F=m-\eta v=m^{-1}+\eta'V\). The explicit path \[ m_\lambda=e^{c\lambda/2},\quad \eta_\lambda= m_\lambda(1-e^{-c\lambda T})/v \] has nonzero \(F=m_\lambda e^{-c\lambda T}\) and a removable south expression \(m_\lambda^{-1}(e^{c\lambda T'}-1)/V\). It ends at the central negative of the physical meridian. It is a cut-meridian homotopy, not continuation of an entire knot representation or its quantum word. The sign is necessary for this once-winding clock if the pole clutches remain specified. If \(m\) were instead a closed path \(1\to1\) with winding \(k\), the boundary of the \((\lambda,T)\) rectangle under a nonzero \(F\) would have winding \(2k-1\): each polar edge supplies \(k\), while the physical edge supplies \(-1\). It cannot bound a nonzero function on that rectangle. The half-path \(1\to-1\) supplies the required two half windings. The local regular varying-meridian forms differ by \[ \Xi_S-\Xi_N=2d\log m\wedge d\log v =d(2\log m\,d\log v). \] Their compact period is \[ I=-2c\log m=2c\log M,\qquad M=m^{-1}. \tag{5} \] This inverse-eigenvalue convention matters. The literal signed quantity \(\int\Xi/(c h_N)=-N\lambda\) is opposite the Chern degree convention \(c_1=-F_{\mathrm{curvature}}/(2\pi i)\) of the compact \(O(N)\) source; the latter degree is \(+N\lambda\). Either signed curvature index can be used if identified explicitly. The fixed-root Weyl matrix compares \(M\) and \(M^{-1}\); it does not by itself implement this path or identify the central sign \(M=1\) with \(M=-1\). Its full scalar and source divisors must remain when using the even reduced meridian coordinate. ## 4. Global three-form primitive and marked radial period The source connection \(\theta=-a\,dv\) obeys \(\theta'=\theta+d\log v\). Thus \[ \vartheta=d\log\eta-2\theta \] is global off \(E\), with \(d\vartheta=-2\Omega\). For \(H_G=-d\log\eta\wedge\Omega\) and \(H_{\mathrm{cut}}=H_G/F\), the exact global primitive is \[ H_{\mathrm{cut}}-H_G=dB,\qquad B=\tfrac12d\log F\wedge\vartheta =\frac{1-2va}{2F}d\eta\wedge dv. \tag{6} \] It is regular along \(E\), with poles only on \(D\). Its south expression is \((2Va'-1)d\eta'\wedge dV/(2F)\). The residue is \[ \operatorname{Res}_D B=(a-1/(2v))\,dv,\qquad -d\operatorname{Res}_D B=\Omega. \] It vanishes on the radial intersection circle. Also \(B|_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{phys}}}=-(1-2T)\Xi/2\) has zero period. This does not remove the distinct two-cycle class (3). Radial integration of \(H_{\mathrm{cut}}-H_G\) uses the logarithm along the chord from \(1\) to \(e^{-cT}\). That logarithm is \(-cT\) below \(T=1/2\), and \(c(1-T)\) above it; its compact mean is zero. The physical marked logarithm is \(-cT\) throughout. Its correction is therefore \[ (-c)\int_{T>1/2}\Omega=c^2/2=-2\pi^2 . \] At \(h_N=c/N\) the numerical exponential is \((-1)^N\). This is a marked relative-period phase. Its appearance in the actual quantum action still requires the actual action/source map. ## 5. Actual character and polynomial wall charges For the actual variable \(M\), (5) gives the direct flux \(I_{\mathrm{phys}}=2c\log M\). Its explicit inverse character is \[ \chi_H=\exp(-I_{\mathrm{phys}}/H) =\exp(-2c\log M/H). \] It is invariant under \(M\mapsto e^{H/2}M\); its marked square root changes sign. At \(H_N=c/N\) they are \(M^{-2N}\) and \(M^{-N}\), respectively. The meridian-log deck multiplier is \(e^{-2c^2/H}\), with value one but logarithmic-\(Q\) derivative \(2N^2\) at the root. For the original phase \(\epsilon_N=i^{N+3}\), \[ d_N(M)=\epsilon_N \frac{\kappa\chi^{1/2}}{1-\chi},\qquad \kappa=M-M^{-1}, \tag{7} \] is exactly its full modified dimension at those roots. Its canceled complete value is \(\epsilon_N/N\), and its half-step ratio is \(-\kappa(qM)/\kappa(M)\). This checks the root character, not an auxiliary off-root finite-matrix normal lift. Along \(M=e^{-\pi i\lambda}\), the actual source poles at \(\lambda=k/N\) have precisely \[ \operatorname{Res}\bigl[d_N(M)F_N(M^2)d\lambda\bigr] =\frac{\epsilon_N(-1)^k\sin(\pi k/N)}{\pi N} C_k(q_N). \] For \(d\log M\), multiply by \(-\pi i\). The ordinary-color bound therefore gives total absolute canonical-meridian residues below \(2D_N/\pi\), or total \(d\lambda\) contour corrections below \(4D_N/\pi\). The flux note's weaker bound \(2D_N\) for those latter corrections is valid. These charges do not estimate a transport kernel or the Kashaev point value. All matrix, cycle, sign and source statements above check.
