The remaining global continuation of the geometric A-branch, source-current pushforward and selected regular-sector norm are explicitly separate.

title: The Gauss-wall flux gives the actual peripheral character
text: # The Gauss-wall flux gives the actual peripheral character Research proof, 27 October 2026. The physical compact source and its exceptional divisor cannot be identified by a fixed-complete-meridian homotopy avoiding the Gauss pole. Their difference has an explicit tube class. Varying the meridian transfers this flux into a peripheral period. Its inverse exponential is exactly the retained Frobenius character at the actual roots, including the square-root sign in the full ADO normalization. There is also a global rational primitive for the principal Gaussian Haar adapter. It keeps the polar boundary co-source rather than discarding the adapter or changing the cycle. The geometric cycle calculation is developed independently in [the meridian homotopy note](meridian_homotopy_wall_and_source_residues.md). The fixed-cycle obstruction and its Gysin interpretation are in [the Gauss-wall cycle audit](gauss_wall_cycle_and_peripheral_flux.md). No selected-volume estimate follows from the polar character alone. ## 1. The fixed-cycle obstruction Use the actual resolved frame space Y=Tot(O_P1(-2)) times_P1 X, E={eta=0}, X=Conn(O(1)), Omega=dv wedge da. Its charts have V=1/v, eta'=-v^2 eta, a'=v-v^2a. The physical matrix entry F=mu_11=1-eta v=1+eta'V is a global function. Its zero divisor D is G_m,v times A^1,a. Keeping the south plus sign is essential: using 1-eta'V would select the other diagonal entry of the meridian. Write c=2pi*i and T=va. The physical compact section is eta_phys=(1-exp(-cT))/v, F_phys=exp(-cT). It extends at both real compact poles as already proved. On the real sphere Gamma, T ranges from zero to one and integral_(angle) Omega=-c dT. The global closed two-form on Y minus D Xi=dlog F wedge dlog v=dv wedge d eta/F has residue dlog v on D. On the physical section it equals c Omega, and on E its restriction is zero. Therefore integral_(Gamma_phys) Xi=-c^2=4pi^2, integral_(Gamma_E) Xi=0. (1) Thus the cycles are not homologous in Y minus D. The normal radial interpolation eta_lambda=lambda eta_phys has F_lambda=(1-lambda)+lambda exp(-cT). It meets D at lambda=T=1/2 along the full angle circle v=exp(i phi), a=1/(2v), eta=1/v. The local expression F=-2(lambda-1/2)+pi*i(T-1/2)+higher terms fixes the intersection sign. With the marked normal-circle orientation the actual relation is [Gamma_phys]-[Gamma_E]=-Tube[gamma_v], integral_(Tube gamma_v) Xi=c^2. (2) This is an actual nonzero correction. A chartwise exponential interpolation avoids F=0 only by violating its other-chart clutch; its missing factor is exp(-c lambda). It is not a global fixed- meridian replacement for (2). ## 2. The Haar adapter has an explicit global relative primitive Let theta=-a dv be a local source connection, so dtheta=Omega and theta'=theta+dlog v. On Y minus E define vartheta=dlog eta-2theta=dlog eta+2a dv. The chart transitions cancel, making vartheta global, and d vartheta=-2Omega. The two actual principal three-forms are H_G=-dlog eta wedge Omega, H_cut=H_G/F. The factor 1/F is exactly the interior adapter of the actual Gaussian/flag calculation. Direct exterior differentiation gives H_cut-H_G=dlog F wedge Omega=dB, B=(1/2)dlog F wedge vartheta =(1-2va)d eta wedge dv/(2F). (3) Although the first expression for B uses vartheta, the second shows that B is regular along E. It has poles only on D. In the south chart the same form is B=(2Va'-1)d eta' wedge dV/(2F). The identity (3) therefore is global, not just an affine primitive. Its boundary residue is Res_D B=(a-1/(2v))dv, -d Res_D B=Omega=Res_D(H_cut-H_G). (4) On the radial intersection circle in (2), this one-form vanishes. The pullback of B to the physical sphere is -(1-2T)Xi/2, whose compact period is zero. These facts explain the ordinary principal current calculation but do not remove the nonzero two-cycle charge (1). There is an exact marked-logarithm correction as well. Radial integration of H_cut-H_G gives Log_chord(F_phys)Omega. The log followed along the straight chord is -cT for T<1/2 and c(1-T) for T>1/2, so its compact period is zero. The actual physical mark Log F_phys=-cT differs by -c on the upper half. Its added relative period is (-c) integral_(T>1/2)Omega=c^2/2=-2pi^2. (5) At H_N=c/N its exponential is exp((c^2/2)/H_N)=(-1)^N. Equation (5) computes a marked relative-period phase. Realizing that phase as a multiplier of the actual quantum word requires the source/action map; it is not inferred from the classical primitive. The separate half-form and ribbon characters remain. ## 3. The peripheral period and its orientation The globally regular eigenvalue-varying orbit family is described in the meridian homotopy note. Its preferred eigenvalue is m and the actual inverse-eigenvalue convention is M=m^(-1). With that note's fixed orientation, its compact Gauss period is I_phys(M)=2c Log M. It changes from zero to -c^2 along M=exp(-pi*i lambda), lambda=0,...,1. For the convenient inverse-source character below, take the opposite oriented flux I_inv(M)=-2c Log M. (6) This inversion is explicit; no cycle orientation is silently reset. Both periods must be kept on the marked meridian logarithm torsor. The peripheral Cech transition records the same flux via the actual change of eigenvalue. Its endpoint lift is M=-1, so the original SL2/peripheral character remains part of the comparison. ## 4. Its inverse character is exactly the actual Frobenius coordinate Keep H=Log Q, q=exp(H/2), and define on that logarithmic torsor chi_H(M)=exp[I_inv(M)/H] =exp[-2c Log M/H]. (7) The actual meridian half-step sends Log M to Log M+H/2. Thus chi_H(qM)=chi_H(M), chi_H^(1/2)(qM)=-chi_H^(1/2)(M). (8) The square root here is the marked exponential exp(-c Log M/H), not an independently chosen algebraic root. At the actual level, H_N=c/N, chi_(H_N)(M)=M^(-2N), chi_(H_N)^(1/2)(M)=M^(-N). (9) The direct character from I_phys is its inverse U=M^(2N). Hence the geometric wall flux recovers precisely the full retained central power coordinate of the actual root object. The whole period line has connection dlog chi_H=-2c dLogM/H+2c LogM dH/H^2. (10) It is a horizontal period object with a marked logarithm, not a claim of rationality in Q,M. A log deck shift LogM->LogM+c multiplies it by exp(-2c^2/H). This equals one at every H_N but has first logarithmic-Q derivative 2N^2 there. Thus root values alone forget a nonzero quantum jet. This is a direct period calculation, not yet an identification with the actual first-normal connection of a chosen quantum A-module. ## 5. The full modified dimension is its actual polar adapter Let kappa=M-M^(-1) and retain the original epsilon_N=i^(N+3). The independently fixed full ADO normalization is exactly d_N(M)=epsilon_N kappa/(M^N-M^(-N)) =epsilon_N kappa chi_(H_N)^(1/2)/(1-chi_(H_N)). (11) This includes its square-root sign and whole meridian divisor. It follows directly from (9), with no normalization fitted to volume. Its q half-step ratio is d_N(qM)/d_N(M)=-kappa(qM)/kappa(M), (12) the exact recorded character of the full period. Under meridian inversion chi becomes chi^(-1) and kappa changes sign, leaving (11) unchanged. At M=1 its whole canceled value is epsilon_N/N. The exact Weyl scalar is (N/epsilon_N)d_N(M), as proved in [the balanced Weyl calculation](twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md). Equation (11) is an equality at the actual quantum roots, with all meridian dependence retained. The geometric H-dependent lift (7) is not asserted to equal a chosen auxiliary off-root finite- matrix source. Its quantum-normal comparison, including (10), still needs to be proved. Only its root restrictions and their actual meridian half-step character are identified here. ## 6. The actual wall charges have a polynomial budget On M(lambda)=exp(-pi*i lambda), equation (11) is d_N=epsilon_N sin(pi lambda)/sin(pi N lambda). Its possible interior simple walls are lambda=k/N, 1<=k<N. The actual reduced state at that meridian is C_k(q_N), by the proved root-color identity and meridian reciprocity. Therefore Res_(lambda=k/N)[d_N(M)F_N(M^2)d lambda] =epsilon_N (-1)^k sin(pi k/N) C_k(q_N)/(pi N). (13) A vanishing C_k makes the wall removable. The original positive ordinary-color trace bound |C_k(q_N)|<=D_N gives sum_(k=1)^(N-1)|2pi*i Res_k|<=2D_N. (14) Thus these actual polar charges are polynomially bounded for a fixed knot braid. Their phases and SL2 endpoint character remain specified. A transport kernel multiplies each charge by its wall value; (14) is not a bound for an unspecified kernel or an identity expressing the Kashaev point value as this meridian integral. ## 7. What is still missing The global wall current, its peripheral flux, the actual central character, and its polar source adapter now agree with explicit marks and signs. The eigenvalue-varying geometric detour also has a source-current transport in [the exponential Cech construction](compact_exponential_cech_current_detour.md). That transport lives in a holomorphic/exponential-period extension of the algebraic source complex. It is not automatically an intertwiner of the actual quantum clock or star product. The knot-dependent regular part of the full period is still not determined by the wall charges. The exact decomposition in [the regularized ADO theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) retains it as R_N, with K_N=N R_N(1)+P_N(1) and P_N(1) polynomially bounded. The volume norm belongs to that selected regular sector. A source- preserving comparison of the whole quantum word or A-object with the marked geometric regulator, and its large-level norm control, remain unproved. Verification: [audit script](../experiments/audit_gauss_wall_peripheral_character.py) and [results](../experiments/gauss_wall_peripheral_character_results.json) check the global rational primitive, marked phases, whole half-step character, root normalization and 91 actual polar-residue conventions. The later [integral-color frame calculation](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md) does match the principal clock by moving q and the integral color together. Its symmetric frame has a regular sphere twist; the inverse eigenflag retains two boundary bubbles. This is not an off-root identification of the generic-M finite root source or its quantum-normal connection.

title: Ge's geometric existence argument: audit and usable conclusion
text: # Ge's geometric existence argument: audit and usable conclusion Audit dated 25 October 2026, explicitly requested by the user. Source: Huabin Ge, [2609.27635v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27635v1), Sections 2--4, PDF pages 4--11. Downloaded PDF: 20 pages; SHA-256 `247c0162c4755990b05557c6ca4d2bfc765a3fe9652b4f70f3288be8f5c97999`. **Result:** the core argument checks out, conditional on the standard Epstein--Penner decomposition input. No claim is made here about the separate geodesic-boundary results or Section 6's additional applications. Writing provenance is not used as mathematical evidence. ## 1. Critical deductions checked For a polyhedron with v vertices and f polygonal faces, vertex heights modulo affine functions have dimension v-4. An n-gonal paired face imposes at most n-3 conditions. Euler's identity gives sum_i(v_i-4) - sum_pairs(n_alpha-3) = (1/2) sum_i(f_i-4). This is positive if any cell is not tetrahedral. Modulo-affine compatibility preserves face subdivisions. A nonzero height class subdivides some cell, and the new cells retain paired faces and original vertices. Refinement terminates: disjoint three-dimensional cells cannot share four affinely independent vertices. For Epstein--Penner cells, deck transformations give affine face maps in Minkowski space. Four affinely independent vertices in a hyperplane lambda=1 are linearly independent; radial projection therefore gives a nonflat ideal tetrahedron. The resulting subdivision preserves the complete metric. These are the dependencies needed for Theorem 1.1. ## 2. Independent exact stress test [audit_ge_compatible_subdivision.py](../experiments/audit_ge_compatible_subdivision.py) implements lower-face enumeration and reconstructs face identifications after every refinement. It uses rational arithmetic throughout. The test exhausts all 8^3=512 affine pairings of opposite cube faces, including quarter turns and reflections. It does not assume that a single generic compatible height produces tetrahedra. Checks include: * Constructing the quotient by affine heights independently for every cell. * Recomputing the face-dependency matrix and its nullspace at each stage. * Checking the dimension inequality, strict increase of cell count, and the finite combinatorial bound. * Matching every induced face subdivision through the original affine map. * Verifying that all terminal cells are nondegenerate tetrahedra using only the original eight vertices, with exact total volume one. All 512 systems passed. There were 448 six-tetrahedron outputs and 64 five-tetrahedron outputs, with at most three refinement stages. The test includes quotient systems that need not be manifolds; this is consistent with the generality of the affine subdivision statement. The finite tests support the audit but do not replace its uniform dimension and termination argument. Results are in [ge_compatible_subdivision_results.json](../experiments/ge_compatible_subdivision_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_ge_compatible_subdivision.py ## 3. What we may now use Under the classical Epstein--Penner theorem, the audited argument supplies a complete positive geometric ideal triangulation for every finite-volume cusped hyperbolic manifold. For a hyperbolic knot, its complete holonomy therefore has a representative beta = sum_j [z_j], Im z_j > 0, D(beta) = Vol(M). The existing regulator-line construction can use this positive representative. Alternatingness is not needed for this geometric input. This does not select a quantum state, and is not a volume-conjecture proof. There is an additional distinction specific to the earlier AK calculations. Ordering each tetrahedron positively chooses its geometric orientation. A global branching instead requires compatible edge directions, hence compatible vertex orders on every glued face. The former does not imply the latter. Thus this audit does not automatically remove the branching hypothesis from those tensor calculations. For the principal torsor approach, geometric subdivision supplies a positive representative of the intrinsic fundamental-class period. The remaining target is to identify its quantization with the distinguished Kashaev period and its literature quantum A-module, retaining normalization and peripheral factors. The AK comparison remains a separate bridge. The subsequent [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) spells out this role in the current affine A-period formulation. It derives the local quantum central gluing relation and distinguishes the geometric block from the rational period's V=1 source sector. The positive triangulation supplies the marked Bloch lift; the relative quantum source, actual cut-period comparison, and norm identity remain work to prove. The subsequent [pointed tetrahedron module theorem](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md) now proves that the geometric root gluing reduction itself is nonzero: for a knot its saturated boundary module has dimension N at every level. Exact local shape-order changes make a global branching unnecessary for that module construction. This does not supply the full colored Verma tensor presentation or remove the separate branching/cycle issues in the earlier analytic AK calculation. The projected generator, actual relative source comparison and regulator norm remain unproved. The subsequent [integral half-longitude calculation](integral_half_longitude.md) also identifies the saturated boundary lattice with the marked meridian and half of the preferred longitude, integrally before root specialization. Its quantum commutation rule matches the actual squared-meridian operator at even and odd levels, with the scalar longitude lift retained. Thus the geometric existence theorem has a correctly marked boundary algebra available for the proposed comparison. It still does not select or compare the relative quantum source and period. The subsequent [actual normal-period calculation](actual_geometric_normal_period.md) uses the positive gluing germ to prove nondegeneracy transverse to the actual two-dimensional framing torsor. It constructs a nonzero formal normal block from the original crossing coefficients and matches its connection to the regulator line by a formal unit. This is precisely a place where the existence theorem enters the quantum-A comparison. The actual affine-source extension, selected relative period and all-level regulator norm still need comparison; Sections 7--8 there give the source-compatible gauge identities. The subsequent [Rivin flow formulation](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) also uses this positive complete point as the interior maximizer of the full angle domain. Its regularized constrained flow has an explicit boundary-controlling Bregman function and converges to that point. An arbitrary ideal triangulation need not have such an interior point; the geometric input is what supplies it. The quantum source/cycle lift of this flow remains a separate comparison, with its actual paired cap now explicitly calibrated.

title: Full volume from finite covers of the actual source sectors
status: General finite-cover theorem; universal coverage open
text: # Full volume from finite covers of the actual source sectors 31 October 2026. A sufficient theorem for a fixed marked plat. Universal applicability to every eligible plat remains open. ## 1. The theorem and its geometric scope Fix an original certified simple-white augmented plat $D$, with $R$ ports, its prescribed MAIN mark, and a fixed choice of half twists giving one main knot component. Retain the original two protected face variables at zero and every ordinary coefficient target $d=N-1$. Let $$ \Phi_D=\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)}{2\pi} $$ be its complete augmented volume rate. The certification and geometric normalization are those of the [complete source theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) and the [whole-CROSS filling theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md). At each port use the actual local labels CROSS, LEFT and RIGHT. A one-sided label whose overloaded middle is protected has zero source and is omitted. A **branch** $B$ assigns a nonempty subset $S_{B,e}$ of the remaining labels to each port. Thus it denotes a Cartesian set of actual label strings. For positive shared ordinary radii $L$, put $$ \begin{aligned} X_e(L)&=Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+Q(x_e,c_e,y_e),\\ A_{e,L}(L)&=\max\{\log c_e,\ Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log c_e\},\\ A_{e,R}(L)&=\max\{\log b_e,\ Q(x_e,c_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log b_e\},\\ G_B(L)&=\sum_e\max_{s\in S_{B,e}} A_{e,s}(L) -\sum_{f\text{ ordinary}}\log L_f, \qquad A_{e,C}=X_e. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Here $x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e$ are the original face coordinates, so a face appearing at several ports has one common radius. The function $Q$ is the original half-degree triangle potential, with its absolute normalization. **Theorem.** Suppose a finite collection of branches covers every allowed non-CROSS string, and each branch has a positive shared vector $L^B$ with $$ G_B(L^B)<\Phi_D.\tag{2} $$ Then there is a diagram-dependent $T$ such that, for every independently chosen fixed signed full-twist vector satisfying $|p_e|>T$, the original invariant obeys $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N\bigl(K_D(\mathbf p)\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_D(\mathbf p)\bigr).} \tag{3} $$ The limit includes both level parities. The twist vector and diagram are fixed before $N$ tends to infinity. The right side is the smooth filled hyperbolic volume, rather than the complete augmented volume $2\pi\Phi_D$. All original framing and peripheral factors remain in the invariant. ## 2. Why a cover suffices The global weighted local estimates used in the [anchored theorem](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md) hold at every real spectral value and every face phase. Their rates are precisely the three functions in (1), with the recorded odd central convention. They are weighted value bounds; no coefficientwise one-sided majorant is asserted. Assign each non-CROSS string to one branch containing it. For a string in branch $B$, perform the ordinary coefficient estimate on the single shared torus with radii $L^B$. The local rate at port $e$ is at most the maximum in (1). Subtracting the original face targets gives $G_B(L^B)+o(1)$. The replacement of $(N-1)/N$ by one costs $o(1)$ because the witnesses are fixed. There are finitely many strings and witnesses for fixed $D$. Hence (2) gives a common strict exponential gap on the whole real spectral cube. Overlapping branches cause no multiplicity problem: each string is assigned once, and even a finite overcount would not change its exponential rate. The same conclusion holds at both level parities. The remainder has spectral degree at most $N-1$ in each coordinate. The cosine Bernstein estimate extends its gap to a fixed sufficiently thin complex spectral strip. Apply the existing source Cauchy estimate and three integrations by parts in each Fourier coordinate. These retain the original endpoint identities and second-derivative boundary currents and give a summable product of inverse-square charge weights on entire original domains. Thus the **whole** non-CROSS filling period remains strictly below $\Phi_D$ in exponential rate. The whole-CROSS theorem gives a nonzero full period of rate $\Phi_D-O(\sum_e p_e^{-2})$, equal to the actual filled volume divided by $2\pi$. Taking every fixed $|p_e|$ sufficiently large makes this rate larger than the remainder bound. The full invariant has the same rate, proving (3). This uses the entire charge sum and the existing full-domain transfer, not a sharply cut infinite Fourier sum. ## 3. Relation to the simpler criteria The triangle inequality $Q(x,t,y)\geq\tfrac12\log t$ gives the useful identities $$ \begin{aligned} \max(A_C,A_L,A_R)&=\max(X,\log b,\log c),\\ \max(A_C,A_L)&=\max(X,\log c),\\ \max(A_C,A_R)&=\max(X,\log b). \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ Terms with protected middle coordinates are omitted. For example, $Q_b+\frac12\log c\leq Q_b+Q_c=X$, which proves the second identity. These identities simplify a union of actual labels. They do not turn the comparison atoms inside $A_L$ or $A_R$ into independent source polynomials. The anchored criterion uses one LEFT or RIGHT anchor and all labels at every other port. It has at most $2R$ branches. Splitting those branches into smaller actual label sets can lower their costs; each new branch may use its own shared face vector. The [certificate separation theorem](actual_shared_radius_certificate_separation.md) proves this is a strict improvement for one fixed original marked source: an anchored certificate is impossible there, but forty finer branches pass. The strongest finite version uses one branch for every individual non-CROSS string $\sigma$. Its sufficient condition is $$ \inf_{L>0}\left[\sum_e A_{e,\sigma_e}(L) -\sum_f\log L_f\right]<\Phi_D \qquad\text{for every }\sigma\ne C^R.\tag{5} $$ If the infimum is strictly smaller, some finite positive witness exists; attainment is unnecessary. Since there are finitely many strings, (5) would establish (3) for that diagram. Whether (5) holds for **every** eligible original plat is the remaining universal question. Acyclicity of overloaded middle edges and the existing endpoint volume theorem do not by themselves prove it: the one-sided comparison allows fractional perspective flows. ## 4. Checkable input and scope The theorem admits finite certificates: the original source incidence and mark, a combinatorial branch cover, one positive rational vector per branch, and strict interval bounds compared with a feasible complete triangle flow. Numerical optimization can locate the witnesses, but is not needed to verify them. The [portable forty-branch verifier](../experiments/audit_actual_sector_cover.py) implements this distinction. This criterion includes the balanced all-width families and the independently deep [bridge-gap extensions](general_simultaneous_bridge_gap_filling_volume.md). It does not assert that every knot of bridge number $k$, or every presentation with long twist regions, has the required original geometric certificate or passes (5). Those are coverage questions to prove, not assumptions hidden in (3).

title: The entire original all-CROSS Fourier period from its local packet and global spectral gap
status: Entire CROSS period has actual filled-volume rate
text: # The entire original all-CROSS Fourier period from its local packet and global spectral gap analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This concerns the actual all-CROSS shared numerator and its **whole original Fourier/Hermite period**. The two source estimates used below have separate proofs. All twists are independently signed, sufficiently long, and fixed before the level tends to infinity. The remaining moving one-sided sectors of the full numerator are not estimated here. ## 1. Exact source, hypotheses, and conclusion Fix the original certified marked flat plat $D$ with $R$ ports, $d=N-1$ and $q=e^{\pi i/N}$. In this note write $C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$ for the raw shared all-CROSS coefficient $$ C_N=C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}= \left[\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d\right] \left.\prod_i H_{V_N,\mathrm{cross}}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0},\qquad C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}=(-1)^{dR}C_N^{\mathrm{positive}}. $$ where $C_N^{\mathrm{positive}}$ is the sign-adjusted coefficient formed from $P_{\mathrm{cross}}=(-1)^dH_{V_N,\mathrm{cross}}$ in the preceding cofactor/global-gap notes. The spectral arguments are $\sigma_i=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_i)$, with both parity definitions of CROSS retained. The absolute global gap is unchanged by this exact sign. The raw source is an entire, separately even, one-periodic function of each $\delta_i$, obtained from a polynomial of degree at most $d$ in each $\sigma_i$. It is not an independently optimized product of local norms. In particular the sign $(-1)^{dR}$ in (2) belongs to this raw convention, not to the preceding positive $C_N$. The original all-CROSS sector of the raw marked period is $$ \begin{aligned} I_{\mathrm{cross}}={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-i)^R \sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \left(\prod_i\ell_i\right)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_i\ell_i}\\ &\quad\times\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \left(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right)C_N(\boldsymbol\delta) \exp\!\left\{N\sum_i[\pi i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\ell_i\delta_i]\right\} \,d\boldsymbol\delta. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Every $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$ is its actual nonzero fixed integer crossing power. A separately recorded final-diagram framing/component character multiplies (1) when converting the raw contraction to the final invariant convention. No additional mark or power of N is inserted. Formula (1) follows by linear projection of the [exact full numerator identity](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) onto these path sectors; a separate covariance claim for an individual path sector is unnecessary. For every fixed $N$ and $\mathbf n$ the whole-domain charge series is absolutely convergent. Indeed $B_N=(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i))C_Ne^{\pi iN\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2}$ has zero endpoint values and matching first derivatives in each variable, including after differentiating other variables. Three integrations by parts in each coordinate give $O_{N,\mathbf n}(\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3})$; after the charge factors this is summable. This observation alone is not a bound uniform in $N$. The two source inputs are: (H1) On a fixed complex cube around $\boldsymbol\delta=0$, the actual all-CROSS numerator has the relative packet $$ C_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =\frac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} \left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\tag{2} $$ with its exact finite anchors and determinant branch. $A_N$ is real on the real chart, even in each coordinate, and tends with fixed derivatives to $A_0$, with $A_0(0)=\Phi_D$ and $A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_i)$, $C_i>0$. On a smaller chart $\operatorname{Re}A_N''$ is uniformly negative definite. This is the CROSS packet proved before the full-numerator restoration in the [whole-source packet theorem](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md), so it uses the same $A_N$ and $H_N$. Equivalently the full packet plus its independently controlled noncross error gives the same local asymptotic. (H2) For every fixed $\eta>0$, there are $\tau_\eta,\gamma_\eta>0$ such that $$ |C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)|\leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_\eta)}.\tag{3} $$ for all sufficiently large N, $\max_i|\operatorname{Re}\delta_i|\geq\eta$ on the centered real cube, and $|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq\tau_\eta$. Periodicity extends this to equivalent real representatives. Every fixed derivative has the same strict exponential bound on smaller strips. The [global CROSS spectral-gap theorem](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) retains the protected zero faces and all original start rows. **Theorem.** There is a diagram-dependent threshold $n_0$ such that for every fixed independently signed integer vector with $|n_i|\geq n_0$, the entire period (1) equals $$ \begin{aligned} I_{\mathrm{cross}}={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\\ &\quad\times\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_{N,\mathbf1,i})} {\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1})}\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\mathbf1}}} e^{N S_{N,\mathbf1}}\\ &\quad\times\left[1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})+O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-\eta_{\mathbf n}N})\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ for some $\eta_{\mathbf n}>0$. Here $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ is the actual finite saddle of $$ \begin{aligned} \Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta) &=A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)+\pi i\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i,\\ S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}&=\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}),\\ Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}&=-\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}''(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}). \end{aligned} $$ and the $Q$ determinant root is the Gaussian branch $\operatorname{Re}Q>0$. The coefficient in (4) is nonzero for each fixed $\mathbf n$, at both level parities. Its normalized logarithmic modulus limit is the actual smooth filled hyperbolic volume, by the [marked action and boundary correction](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). The same exact half twist $\mathbf n=\boldsymbol\epsilon-2\mathbf p$ occurs only once. The proof uses no separately summed infinite sharp-cube series. Only a finite charge set is localized. The infinite tail is estimated on whole original intervals before any charge summation. ## 2. Basic bounds, endpoint identities, and parameter choices The local packet and real concavity bound near zero, together with (H2) outside a smaller fixed cube, imply $$ \sup_{\boldsymbol\delta\ \mathrm{real}}|C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D+e_N)},\qquad e_N\longrightarrow0.\tag{5} $$ Polynomial Bernstein on each cosine variable yields, for any fixed $T$, $$ |C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)| \leq\exp\!\left[N(\Phi_D+e_N)+2\pi d\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\right], \qquad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq T.\tag{6} $$ This is a bound for the whole shared polynomial; no factorwise positive-radius majorant is used. For source derivatives, apply Cauchy to (6) in the required variables. Gaussian derivatives are evaluated separately on REAL spectator coordinates, avoiding any unwanted large-twist exponential cost. If a source factor $Z$ is an arbitrary entire polynomial in the $\sigma_i$, its product with $\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)$ and the fixed Gaussian satisfies $$ \left.B\right|_{\delta_j=\pm1/2}=0,\qquad \left.\partial_j B\right|_{\delta_j=1/2} =\left.\partial_j B\right|_{\delta_j=-1/2}.\tag{7} $$ The first derivative is solely the derivative of the sine: the two cosines are both $-1$, the spectral argument is $2$ at both ends, and the Gaussian endpoint value is $e^{\pi iNn_j/4}$. These facts remain true after arbitrary derivatives in other variables, including when one different coordinate is held complex. Thus three integrations by parts give exactly $$ \begin{aligned} \int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\,d\delta_j =(2\pi iN\ell_j)^{-3}\biggl\{ &\left[\partial_j^2B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\right]_{-1/2}^{1/2}\\ &-\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\partial_j^3B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\,d\delta_j \biggr\}. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ The second-derivative endpoint difference is retained. Repeating (8) over any spectator subset gives at most $3^{R-1}$ boundary/integral terms. Fixed source Cauchy bounds and real Gaussian derivatives cost at most $C_{\mathbf n}N^3$ per differentiated variable; these powers cancel the $N^3$ denominators. After the actual charge factors, every spectator coordinate supplies $|\ell_j|^{-2}$. Choose a small fixed outer cube $K_B=[-B,B]^R$ inside (H1). Choose $a>0$ much smaller than $B$ so the localized contribution theorem applies uniformly for all positive charges $\ell_i/|n_i|\leq a$. Next choose $0<b<a/4$, with $K_b$ inside the same chart. All these constants depend only on $D$. Below $n_0$ will be enlarged finitely many times, independently of ratios among the $|n_i|$. ## 3. The infinite far-charge union is exponentially small Use (H2) at $\eta=1/4$. Choose $\tau>0$ sufficiently small that the source and all required spectator derivatives have a strict bound $e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)}$ at $$ \delta_i=\pm\frac12+iv,\qquad 0\leq v\leq\tau. $$ with every other coordinate real or in a fixed Cauchy neighborhood of radius $\tau$. This uses the separated endpoint coordinate, regardless of the other real coordinates. Shrink $\tau$ and $\gamma_e$ once if needed. For a positive far charge $\ell_i$, shift its whole interval upwards by $i\tau$, keeping all other integrations on their whole real intervals. Write $$ B_i(z;\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}) =\sin(2\pi z)e^{\pi i n_iNz^2}C_N(z,\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}). $$ The exact pair of endpoint currents is $$ \begin{aligned} B_i(1/2+iv)-B_i(-1/2+iv) ={}&2i\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi n_iNv)\\ &\quad\times e^{\pi i n_iN(1/4-v^2)} C_N(1/2+iv,\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}). \end{aligned}\tag{9} $$ The other sine/Gaussian factors remain outside this equality. Multiplying the actual Fourier character leaves the endpoint parity $(-1)^{\ell_i}$. Its modulus is one. Both vertical sides were retained; the paired factor vanishes quadratically at $v=0$. For the paired vertical contribution, apply (8) in every spectator coordinate. The strict endpoint strip bound and source Cauchy estimates then give, after all original charge weights, an upper bound $$ C_{\mathbf n}|n_i|N\ell_i\,e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)} \left(\prod_{j\ne i}|\ell_j|^{-2}\right) \int_0^\tau v^2 e^{-2\pi N(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)v}\,dv.\tag{10} $$ Here $|\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi n_iNv)|\leq C|n_i|Nv^2e^{\pi|n_i|Nv}$. No oscillatory-sine substitution is made. For $\ell_i>|n_i|/2+D$, with $D\geq1$, the integral is at most $C/[N^3(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)^3]$. Consequently summing (10) over this far coordinate and all nonzero spectator charges is bounded by a polynomial factor times $e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)}$. The exact estimate $$ \sum_{\ell>M}\frac{\ell}{(\ell-|n|/2)^3} \leq C\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right].\tag{11} $$ makes the summability explicit. Constants may depend on the fixed $\mathbf n$. For the upper horizontal contribution, apply the same spectator integrations by parts. Source Cauchy from (6), in a fixed radius-$\tau$ neighborhood of the spectators, has exponential cost at most $2\pi R\tau N$. The shifted sine is bounded, while the bad-coordinate Gaussian and Fourier factors cost exactly at most $$ e^{\pi|n_i|N\tau-2\pi\ell_iN\tau}. $$ Thus the weighted horizontal contribution is bounded by $$ C_{\mathbf n}\ell_i\left(\prod_{j\ne i}|\ell_j|^{-2}\right) \exp\!\left\{N\left[\Phi_D+e_N+2\pi R\tau -2\pi\tau(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)\right]\right\}.\tag{12} $$ Choose a fixed $D$ large enough that $2\pi\tau D>2\pi R\tau+2\gamma_e$, and set $$ M_i=\left\lceil\frac{|n_i|}{2}+D\right\rceil.\tag{13} $$ The geometric tail of $\ell_i$ times (12) is exponentially bounded by $\Phi_D-\gamma_e$ after a harmless decrease of $\gamma_e$ and all large N. Both signs of the far charge obey the same estimate, either by downward shifts or the exact separate-evenness/reflection identity. Therefore, for some fixed $\gamma_\infty>0$, $$ \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R\\ \exists i:\ |\ell_i|>M_i}} \left|\mathcal I_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}^{\mathrm{cross}}\right| \leq C_{\mathbf n}\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_\infty)}.\tag{14} $$ Here $\mathcal I_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}^{\mathrm{cross}}$ denotes the full weighted charge term in (1). Use the union bound over $i$; multiple far coordinates cause no issue. Every other coordinate was summed on its whole original domain after (8). Finite-N absolute convergence and the displayed dominating series justify all summations. No partial-far exterior with uncontrolled $R$ powers appears: the hypothesis used is the shared all-CROSS endpoint gap, valid for arbitrary real spectator spectra. This is the stronger input missing from the local operator-tail argument. ## 4. The finite charges outside the local scaled box The remaining set $0<|\ell_i|\leq M_i$ is finite after $\mathbf n$ is fixed. Suppose at least one coordinate $i$ has $|\ell_i|/|n_i|>a$. Reflect charge signs if necessary; the source is separately even, so absolute estimates are unchanged and assume $\ell_i>0$. On the original real domain outside $K_b$, (H2) gives rate $\Phi_D-\gamma_b$. The Gaussian and Fourier factors there have modulus one. No contour estimate is needed for this finite-charge portion. Inside $K_b$, shift only coordinate $i$ upward by $$ t_i=\frac{b}{|n_i|}.\tag{15} $$ All actual side currents of this small rectangle are retained. The packet and its real-action Taylor bound give, uniformly for $x$ in $K_b$ and $0\leq v\leq t_i$, $$ \operatorname{Re}A_N(x+iv e_i) \leq A_N(0)-c|x|^2+Cv^2.\tag{16} $$ Reality makes the first Taylor term purely imaginary. The Gaussian-plus-Fourier contribution in this coordinate is $$ -2\pi n_ix_iv-2\pi\ell_iv \leq-2\pi|n_i|(a-b)v\leq0.\tag{17} $$ On the horizontal translate, $v=t_i$, this costs at least $2\pi b(a-b)$, while the source error is at most $Cb^2/n_0^2$. On either vertical side $|x_i|=b$, (16) gives at least $cb^2$ loss, and (17) is nonpositive. Enlarge $n_0$ so $C/n_0^2$ is small. Then the horizontal and both sides have a fixed strict gap $\gamma_{\mathrm{bad}}>0$ below $\Phi_D$, independently of slope ratios. The packet's amplitudes contribute only polynomial factors. Together with the exterior $K_b$ bound, every such bounded bad charge is exponentially small. There are finitely many of them, so their whole sum obeys the same strict rate with a fixed-n prefactor. No infinite sharp-cube series has been split. ## 5. Finite local charges and the actual unit contribution It remains to consider the finite set with all $|\ell_i|/|n_i|\leq a$. On the real domain outside the larger $K_B$, (H2) gives a fixed loss $\gamma_B$. Inside $K_B$ apply the [localized original contour theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) to the packet (2). It retains the exact side currents, the finite action, the Gaussian determinant branch and all sine/charge/parity factors. For positive charges the finite critical values satisfy $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}-\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq\sum_i\frac{C_i}{2n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1).\tag{18} $$ All sign-unit choices contribute exactly equally. Every other charge in this finite local box has a positive fixed-n gap. The all-unit local contribution is precisely (4), with its $O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})$ relative error and nonzero limiting amplitude. The half twists are included once through $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. The limiting unit loss from $\Phi_D$ is $O_D(\sum_i|n_i|^{-2})$. Enlarge the diagram-dependent $n_0$ until this loss is less than one quarter of the minimum of $\gamma_\infty$, $\gamma_{\mathrm{bad}}$, $\gamma_b$ and $\gamma_B$. Also require $a n_0\geq1$ so the unit charge lies in the local box. Since $S_{N,\mathbf1}$ tends to its limiting value, all complementary bounds above are then exponentially smaller than $e^{N\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}}$ for large N. The smallest nonunit gap in (18) may depend on the fixed vector $\mathbf n$, but remains positive. Combining the finite local sector, bounded bad charges and the absolutely bounded infinite union proves (4). The exact critical volume identity identifies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|I_{\mathrm{cross}}| =\operatorname{Vol}(\text{the actual smooth filled exterior}).\tag{19} $$ There is no uniform joint growing-twist/level error assertion: the twists are fixed first, while the threshold applies to arbitrary independent signs and magnitudes. ## 6. Scope of the transfer The argument proves a contribution theorem and all-charge control for the entire original all-CROSS spectral sector from the proved inputs (H1)-(H2). The original full numerator also contains moving one-sided sectors. The already established diagonal/CROSS and short-moving sector gaps can be retained separately, but they do not exhaust that remainder. Formula (19) is therefore not yet the general filled-knot invariant theorem. The crucial new analytic point is (14): a uniform shared endpoint gap makes partial far-charge tails summable without changing the actual source or creating infinite sharp-cut subseries. The old polynomial $+2$ operator bound alone would not control the spectator environment. No generic-$q$ normal theorem or unproved choice of a Lefschetz coefficient is used. ## Validation and scope The theorem evaluates the entire all-CROSS sector; the moving one-sided remainder of the original full numerator remains outside its conclusion.

title: Full original long filling from anchored shared-radius certificates
text: # Full original long filling from anchored shared-radius certificates theorem, 31 October 2026. At most $2R$ finite tests on shared face radii imply the full original independently long-filling volume theorem. These tests strictly extend balance at the complete packing for a fixed marked source. They are not asserted for every certified diagram. The proof makes no exchange of a maximum and an infimum and uses no coefficientwise LEFT comparison. ## 1. The original source and the finite certificate Fix an original marked flat plat $D$ with $R$ ordered ports $(x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e)$, the original adjacent protected MAIN faces $u,v$, and its labeled simple-white convex right-angled certificate for the complete augmented exterior $Y_D$. Write $\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$. Every ordinary face variable below is positive; the protected variables remain exactly zero. Each vector $L=(L_f)$ is shared across the entire original face incidence graph. These source variables are curvatures, not Euclidean disk radii. Let $Q(x,t,y)$ be the absolutely normalized [complete triangle action](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). Its homogeneity is $Q(\lambda x,\lambda t,\lambda y)=Q(x,t,y)+\tfrac12\log\lambda$. Define $$ \begin{aligned} X_e(L)&=Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+Q(x_e,c_e,y_e),\\ H_e(L)&=\max\bigl(\{X_e(L)\}\cup\{\log b_e:b_e>0\}\cup\{\log c_e:c_e>0\}\bigr). \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ The two possible anchored rates are $$ \begin{aligned} A_{e,\mathrm L}(L)&=\max\{\log c_e,Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log c_e\},&&c_e>0,\\ A_{e,\mathrm R}(L)&=\max\{\log b_e,Q(x_e,c_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log b_e\},&&b_e>0. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ The labels $\mathrm L,\mathrm R$ mean LEFT and RIGHT; $L_f$ is a shared face variable. If the overloaded middle is protected, that anchor is absent because the exact finite sector is zero. Set $$ \mathcal C_{e,s}(L)=A_{e,s}(L)+\sum_{f\ne e}H_f(L) -\sum_{j\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\log L_j.\tag{3} $$ Here $f\ne e$ in the first sum indexes ports. There are at most $2R$ surviving anchors. Suppose that for **each** surviving anchor there exists a fixed positive ordinary shared vector $L^{e,s}$, with the same protected zeros, satisfying $$ \mathcal C_{e,s}(L^{e,s})<\Phi_D.\tag{4} $$ Different anchors may use different whole vectors. Variables shared by several ports are never optimized independently inside one product. Equivalently, $\inf_L\mathcal C_{e,s}(L)<\Phi_D$; even if that infimum escapes, strict inequality supplies a finite positive witness. No minimizer is required. If no anchor survives, the full numerator is already all-CROSS and its existing theorem applies directly. Then every independently signed, fixed, sufficiently long filling vector in the original parity convention satisfies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N| =\operatorname{Vol}(\text{the actual filled exterior}).\tag{5} $$ For the prescribed knot parity, this is the actual knot invariant. The threshold depends on $D$ and the witnesses. There is no bound on ratios of the independent twist lengths, no joint growing-twist/level limit, and no uniformity in growing diagram size. ## 2. The source estimate at one shared vector The [global LEFT theorem](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) proves (2) as a uniform weighted absolute upper rate at all face phases and all real spectral values. It retains both outside products, both parity partitions, and the shrinking final spectral cap. Reflection gives RIGHT. This is a value bound, not a coefficientwise inequality. The [exact cofactor interpolation theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), Section 8, bounds CROSS coefficientwise by $C\log^2(N+1)$ times its positive zero-spectral CROSS polynomial on the entire real spectral interval. That polynomial has weighted rate $X_e$, by the original determinant and half-block normalization. This includes a single protected outer face and protected middles. The outer faces cannot both be protected: their original edge is MATCHING, while the protected edge is MAIN. Thus $x_e+y_e>0$ at every witness. For $t>0$ and $x+y>0$, the actual triangle action satisfies $Q(x,t,y)>\tfrac12\log t$; its nonstrict version already follows from the endpoint monomial. Therefore $$ A_{e,\mathrm L}\le H_e,\qquad A_{e,\mathrm R}\le H_e.\tag{6} $$ For example, $Q_b+\tfrac12\log c\le Q_b+Q_c=X_e$. A protected overloaded middle gives an exactly zero sector, rather than an estimate involving $\log0$. Hence $H_f$ bounds CROSS, LEFT and RIGHT at every unanchored port on the same common face Cauchy torus. Take any exact path sector with a one-sided port, and choose one such port $(e,s)$ as anchor. Evaluate its entire original shared coefficient extraction at $L^{e,s}$, using $H_f$ at the other ports. The original ordinary target is $d=N-1$ at each ordinary face and zero at $u,v$. Replacing $d/N$ by $1$ changes the fixed-radius normalized logarithm by $O(N^{-1})$. If $\gamma$ is smaller than the minimum of the finitely many positive gaps in (4), all sufficiently large $N$ therefore satisfy $$ |Z_{\mathrm{sector}}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_R)| \le e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\tag{7} $$ uniformly on the full real spectral cube. All original source scalars and normalization conventions remain those of the homogeneous theorem. Every phase stays inside the original local sector until the valid weighted absolute estimate is taken. The LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT partition is disjoint at both parities. At even $N=2m$, LEFT has $j\le m-1$, CROSS has $i\le m-1$ and $j\ge m$, and RIGHT has $i\ge m$. At odd $N=2m+1$, LEFT has $j\le m-1$, CROSS has $i\le m\le j$, and RIGHT has $i\ge m+1$; the central zero-step belongs to CROSS once. Their finite sum is the exact full numerator. There are at most $3^R-1$ sectors in full minus CROSS. Assigning an anchor to each proves (7) for that entire difference, with a smaller gap. Only $2R$ witness vectors are needed; no atomwise optimization is performed. The remainder has spectral degree at most $d$ in every variable. The cosine Bernstein bound for $\sigma_i=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_i)$ extends (7) to a fixed thin complex strip, at cost $\exp[2\pi d\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|]$. Choose its height below the fixed gap and shrink once more for source Cauchy derivatives. ## 3. The entire original Fourier period Apply the analytic argument in Section 4 of the [whole-domain sector theorem](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md) to this remainder polynomial. That argument requires the whole-strip bound, polynomial cosine dependence, and the original sine and Gaussian factors; it does not require the polynomial itself to be diagonal. The original sine factor vanishes at each endpoint $\pm\tfrac12$, and its first derivative has equal endpoint values. The source cosine and Gaussian also have equal endpoint values. Three integrations by parts in each coordinate retain the second-derivative boundary current and give charge decay $\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3}$. After the original weight $\prod_i|\ell_i|$, the whole-domain charge sum converges absolutely. Fixed-strip Cauchy bounds apply only to the source; Gaussian derivatives are taken on the real cube. Thus $$ |I_{\mathrm{full}}-I_{\mathrm{cross}}| \le C_D\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma')}, \qquad\gamma'>0.\tag{8} $$ No infinite sharp-cube series has been split. Both endpoints and their actual currents, all nonzero charges, and the original framing phases are retained. The [whole all-CROSS theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) supplies a nonzero relative asymptotic for fixed independently signed sufficiently long $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. Its actual filled critical rate tends to $\Phi_D$, with deficit $O_D(\sum_i n_i^{-2})$. Choose every $|p_i|$ above the geometric and analytic thresholds and so that this deficit is less than $\gamma'/2$. Equation (8) is exponentially smaller than the original all-CROSS contribution, giving $$ \frac{I_{\mathrm{full}}}{I_{\mathrm{cross}}} =1+O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-c_{\mathbf n}N}).\tag{9} $$ The original normalizing characters and nonzero polynomial factors do not change the exponential limit. This proves (5). The argument uses spectral identities at the fixed root and imposes no extra generic-$q$ derivative hypothesis. [Complete-radius balance](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) implies (4): use the geometric vector for every anchor. There $H_f=X_f$ at all ports and each surviving $A_{e,s}<X_e$. The following example shows that the converse fails for a fixed marked source. ## 4. An original flat plat failing complete-radius balance Use three standard adjacent cups and caps with the literal zero-based slot word $$ (1,3,2,1,3),\tag{10} $$ marking the first original top cap. Its actual ordered quartets are $$ (1,0,4,2),\ (2,0,5,3),\ (4,2,6,5),\ (1,4,0,6),\ (6,5,0,3).\tag{11} $$ The protected faces are $0,1$, and faces $2,\ldots,6$ each retain target $d$. The original compiler gives exactly these data. The ten triangles form a simple sphere with seven vertices and fifteen edges; the protected edge is MAIN. No general Morse-to-flat-plat adapter or isotopy is assumed. Let $z=\sqrt5$. An exact marked packing has lines $0:Y=0$, $1:Y=2$, and these disks, listed as horizontal center, vertical center, Euclidean radius: $$ \begin{aligned} 2&=(z-1,1,1),&6&=(1-z,1,1),\\ 3&=(0,(3-z)/2,(3-z)/2),\\ 4&=(0,(1+z)/2,(3-z)/2),\\ 5&=(0,1,z-2). \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ Every graph edge other than the marked line-line contact is an exact tangency; every nonedge pair has strictly disjoint support. These are twenty finite pair checks. The marked lines touch at infinity. The [simple-sphere packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) supplies the actual labeled right-angled certificate, retaining the original matching and source pairings. The complete curvature vector is $$ L^{\mathrm{geom}}= \left(0,0,1,\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},2+\sqrt5,1\right).\tag{13} $$ At the first and fourth ports, complete balance fails. The certified evaluation below gives $$ -0.10315<X_0(L^{\mathrm{geom}})-\log L^{\mathrm{geom}}_4<-0.10190.\tag{14} $$ The fourth port has the same value by reflection. Nevertheless, the following rational shared vectors satisfy (4). Each vector lists $(L_2,L_3,L_4,L_5,L_6)$; both protected values stay zero. | Anchor, with zero-based port index | Shared ordinary vector | Certified gap $\Phi_D-\mathcal C$ | |---|---|---| | 0 LEFT | $(3,4,3/2,5,1)$ | $>0.50$ | | 3 RIGHT | $(1,4,3/2,5,3)$ | $>0.50$ | | 1 LEFT | $(3/2,5,2,2,1)$ | $>0.71$ | | 4 RIGHT | $(1,5,2,2,3/2)$ | $>0.71$ | | 2 LEFT | $(2,6,2,18,1)$ | $>1.35$ | | 2 RIGHT | $(1,6,2,18,2)$ | $>1.35$ | These are all six surviving anchors. At the other four sides, the sector vanishes because its overloaded middle is protected. The conservative uniform gap $0.45$ certifies the full-source conclusion. In conventional braid indexing the word is $\sigma_2,\sigma_4,\sigma_3,\sigma_2,\sigma_4$. Choosing the first two exponents odd and the last three even makes one main component by the original cup/cap permutation. All five sufficiently long fixed parameters remain independent in magnitude and sign. Restricting every full exponent to a multiple of $3$ gives exact bridge number $3$ by the [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md); this congruence is not required for the volume statement. The example proves strict enlargement of the tests for a fixed marked source. It does not prove strict inclusion of the underlying unmarked knot families: another mark or presentation might satisfy the older balance test. ## 5. Rigorous interval evaluation No floating optimizer enters the certificate. For a nonnegative triangle $w$ with at least two positive entries, set $$ \begin{aligned} D&=\sqrt{w_1w_2+w_2w_3+w_3w_1},\qquad a_i=\arctan(w_i/D),\\ Q(w)&=\sum_{w_i>0}\left\{ \frac{\Lambda(a_i)+\Lambda(\pi/2-a_i)}\pi +\frac{a_i}\pi\log w_i\right\}. \end{aligned}\tag{15} $$ For a triangle with just one positive entry, use $Q(w)=\tfrac12\log w_i$ exactly. Formula (15) is the absolutely normalized original source identity, with $\sum_i a_i=\pi/2$. Hence $$ \Phi_D=\sum_eX_e(L^{\mathrm{geom}}) -\sum_{f=2}^6\log L_f^{\mathrm{geom}}.\tag{16} $$ The absolutely convergent Fourier series gives, for every real $a$, $$ \Lambda(a)=\frac12\sum_{n=1}^M\frac{\sin(2na)}{n^2}+r_M(a), \qquad |r_M(a)|\le\frac1{2M}.\tag{17} $$ The remainder bound follows from $\sum_{n>M}n^{-2}\le M^{-1}$. The [portable audit](../experiments/audit_general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.py) evaluates the $M=1024$ sum with Arb at 192 bits, then adds this analytic tail ball. Square roots, $\pi$, arctangents, logarithms, maxima and all arithmetic retain enclosing balls. There is no unproved floating solve, rounded optimizer or numerical asymptotic limit. The [saved result](../experiments/general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume_results.json) encloses $\Phi_D$ in $(5.17452,5.18696)$, and every table entry has its asserted strictly positive lower bound. The packing checks use exact algebra in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$. The checks cover five original ports, ten triangles, fifteen edges, twenty exact pair supports, two failed geometric balance tests, and six fixed rational whole-source witnesses. They certify this finite example and its quantitative inequalities; Sections 1–3 prove the general analytic transfer. ## 6. What remains open about general optimized capacities A fixed shared vector gives a valid Cauchy bound. In contrast, one cannot replace $\inf_L\max\{F_0(L),F_1(L)\}$ by $\max\{\inf_LF_0(L),\inf_LF_1(L)\}$. In particular, the LEFT value envelope is not an exact finite decomposition into an identity polynomial and a half-triangle polynomial. This distinction has a precise convex-dual form. Let $C(\alpha)$ be the original triangle coefficient entropy on $\alpha_x+\alpha_b+\alpha_y=\tfrac12$. The source identity is $$ Q(x,b,y)=\max_\alpha\bigl\{C(\alpha)+\alpha_x\log x+\alpha_b\log b+\alpha_y\log y\bigr\}. $$ Thus the concave entropy associated with the LEFT weighted envelope admits mixtures $$ q_c=1-\frac t2,\qquad(q_x,q_b,q_y)=t\alpha, \qquad\text{entropy}=tC(\alpha),\qquad0\le t\le1.\tag{18} $$ At $t=0$ this is pure $c$; at $t=1$ it is a triangle plus pure half-$c$. Protected input coordinates force their $\alpha$ entries to vanish. This is generally not the actual one-sided entropy $E$. Compact finite-dimensional convex duality converts the optimized envelope into this problem with concave local entropies, including limiting multipliers; it does not remove interior $t$. The unanchored $H$ additionally permits mixtures with complete CROSS and pure-$b$ atoms. The [identity forest reduction](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md) controls the exact identity endpoint $t=0$. A [fixed-triangle capacity loss](actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md) controls $t=1$. At fractional $t$, the positive triangle has a changed row supply. Simply retaining its unscaled geometric angles changes the face stars by $(1-t)(\alpha-e_c/2)$, which need not vanish. The old hybrid representation therefore cannot be reused for an arbitrary mixture without further proof. The present theorem supplies a strictly broader sufficient certificate for marked sources; whether every original certified diagram passes an optimized sector or anchor test remains open. ## 7. Exact certificate checks The six rational certificates and twenty exact pair checks have smallest certified gap greater than $0.5023$. They use the specified quartets, first mark, exact packing, simple-sphere certificate and six surviving sides. Numerical optimization and finite asymptotic samples are not proof inputs.

title: Annihilator existence and volume for the literature geometric state integrals
text: # Annihilator existence and volume for the literature geometric state integrals Research note, 25 October 2026. This extends the independent analysis in `literature_state_volume.md`. The quantum state remains the published integral. The annihilator convention is Definition 5 of Andersen–Malusà, [arXiv:1711.11522v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.11522v3). No new choice of a preferred recurrence solution is made here. The later `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` extends the same existence argument to the explicitly constructed meridian wavefunctions of ordinary boundary-fiber charts, including singular face matrices and their exact Gaussian framing correction. The quantum parameter and b-shift convention remain the ones specified here. The subsequent `fourier_boundary_state.md` removes the ordinary-fiber rank restriction by inverse Fourier recovery of the specifically leveled tensor. Its absolutely convergent moving-plane integral is also of class (1.1), with rational Gaussian and Phi coefficients and the required small-shift holomorphy and exponential bounds. The same independent annihilator proof therefore applies to it. The operators used are the b-shift operators of Andersen–Malusà, after the explicit spectral rescaling in Section 5. They differ at finite b from the operators used in Section 4.4 of the FAMED paper. Section 6.1 records that distinction. An identification of the canonical Andersen–Malusà knot state with these integral realizations for every knot is not assumed. The subsequent `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` identifies each fixed fiber integral exactly with a particular leveled AK tensor realization. It gives the omitted angle phase, coarea orientation, and a state-recovery theorem; its affine move criterion still has to be applied to actual connecting sequences before asserting general intrinsic knot-state equivalence. Its subsequent full-integral moment argument forces the affine boundary phase slope to vanish for compatible geometric endpoints, proving equality of selected-state annihilators along certified proper positive paths. The new point is an elementary existence proof for a boundary annihilator. It uses the finite-product shift equation, a dimension count, exponential moments, and restriction of scalars. In particular, a zero obtained by naively putting the internal shifts equal to 1 is handled rather than assumed absent. The hypotheses are still those of the published integral (4.5) in Ben Aribi–Wong, [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2), with positive complete geometric and peripheral certificates specified in Section 5 of the companion note. This proves a statement for that class of literature states. It does not establish membership for every alternating knot or audit every global TQFT move identity. ## 1. Proper finite products from the exact functional equation Use quantum parameter b>0 and q=exp(2 pi i b^2). Consider variables t=(t_0,t_1,...,t_d), of which t_0 is the boundary variable. The class of integrands needed below is I_b(t)=exp(pi i t^T H t+(b+b^(-1)) pi c^T t+C(b)) product_(j=1)^m Phi_b(v_j^T t+i(b+b^(-1))rho_j)^epsilon_j, (1.1) where H is rational symmetric, c,v_j,rho_j are rational, epsilon_j are integers, and C(b) is independent of t. Extra roots of unity in the Gaussian normalization can be included in C(b). Normalization factors independent of the boundary variable do not affect annihilator existence, but remain relevant to the volume limit and are kept in the specified state. Choose an integer L>0 such that L times every coordinate of every v_j is integral. Let S_k shift t_k by -i b L. Choose an integer D>0 clearing the finitely many rational exponents in multiplication factors and set X_k=exp(2 pi b t_k/D). The exact functional equation of Phi, derived from its defining integral in the companion note, implies that I_b(t-i b L n)/I_b(t), for n integral, is a Laurent monomial in X times finitely many factors 1+a_j q^r X^w_j or their inverses. Here a_j is a root of unity times a fixed rational power of q, w_j is an integral vector, and the integer r ranges over intervals whose lengths are O(|n|). The Gaussian contributes monomial exponents linear in n and central powers of q quadratic in n. The latter are scalars in the coefficient field and do not increase the degree in X. All coefficients belong to a fixed finite algebraic extension F of ℚ(q): adjoin finitely many roots of q and roots of unity. This is one fixed field, independent of the order of the shift n. **Bounded-denominator lemma.** For each n, all functions X_0^a S_0^n_0 ... S_d^n_d I_b / I_b, 0<=a,n_0,...,n_d<=n, (1.2) have a common Laurent-polynomial denominator D_n(X), and after multiplication by D_n their Laurent exponents in each X_k lie in [-C n,C n], for a fixed C. **Proof.** For each of the finitely many original Phi factors, include in D_n every binomial 1+a_j q^r X^w_j which can occur in a denominator for the shifts in (1.2). The possible r lie in one interval of O(n) integers. A repeated original factor only increases a bounded multiplicity. Thus D_n has O(n) binomial factors and Laurent degree O(n) in each coordinate. Every individual shift ratio has O(n) numerator factors and a monomial of degree O(n). Multiplying by the remaining factors in D_n, and by X_0^a, preserves this linear degree bound. The exact finite shift depends only on the net shift of each Phi argument; path-dependent repeated denominators need not be introduced. QED. ## 2. A nonzero elimination operator without invoking a closure theorem The relation is S_0 X_0=q^(-L/D)X_0 S_0; S_1,...,S_d commute with both of them and with each other. The PBW monomials X_0^a S_0^n_0 ... S_d^n_d, 0<=a,n_0,...,n_d<=n, are linearly independent as formal operators over F. There are (n+1)^(d+2) of them. By the bounded-denominator lemma, their actions on I_b span a space of dimension at most (2C n+1)^(d+1) over F. For sufficiently large n the first number exceeds the second. Finite linear algebra therefore gives a nonzero operator P(X_0,S_0,S_1,...,S_d) I_b=0, (2.1) which contains no internal multiplication variable X_1,...,X_d. This is constructive: form the exact rational shift ratios, clear their common denominator, and solve the finite homogeneous system. Its size may be large. The existence proof makes no efficiency or minimal-degree assertion. The output (2.1) need not survive S_1=...=S_d=1. Treating that specialization as automatically nonzero would leave a gap. The next argument resolves it. ## 3. Exponential moments recover a genuine boundary operator Suppose the state is Z_b(t_0)=integral_C I_b(t_0,t_1,...,t_d) dt_1 ... dt_d. (3.1) Assume for all sufficiently small b that: * I_b and all the finitely many shifts in (2.1) are holomorphic in the horizontal contour deformations required to shift t_k by -i b L n_k. * On those deformations they decay exponentially in every real integration direction, uniformly for the boundary variable in an open neighborhood. These are analytic assumptions to verify for the chosen state, rather than consequences of the dimension count. They imply the same properties after inserting a polynomial in the t_k or exp(z dot t_internal), for small complex z. Define the analytic exponential moment F_b(t_0,z)=integral_C exp(z dot t_internal) I_b(t) dt_internal. Contour translation gives exactly integral_C exp(z dot t_internal) S_k I_b dt_internal =exp(i b L z_k) F_b(t_0,z), k>=1. (3.2) No residue or boundary term is omitted: this is precisely where the holomorphy and exponential tail hypotheses are used. Boundary S_0 acts on F_b in its prescribed way and X_0 remains a multiplication operator. Expand the nonzero operator P in the *central* internal shift variables: P(X_0,S_0,T)=sum_alpha A_alpha(X_0,S_0)(T-1)^alpha. Let k be its least nonzero total degree, and choose |alpha|=k with A_alpha!=0. From (2.1)–(3.2), P(X_0,S_0,exp(i b L z)) F_b(t_0,z)=0. The coefficient of z^alpha of total degree k is (i b L)^k A_alpha(X_0,S_0) F_b(t_0,0)=0. (3.3) All terms in which a derivative falls on F_b have lower derivatives of P, which vanish. Thus A_alpha is a nonzero boundary annihilator of Z_b. The argument also covers k=0, when ordinary specialization is sufficient. For example, an elimination output (T-1)^2 P_0(X_0,S_0,T) has zero direct specialization, but its first surviving coefficient is P_0(X_0,S_0,1). The second moment gives 2(i b L)^2 times this operator acting on Z_b. With several internal variables the same total-degree argument handles sums such as (T_1-1)A+(T_2-1)B, without requiring a common linear factor. This does not cancel any *peripheral* factor in X_0. All peripheral factors and the exact quantum parameter are retained in (3.3). ## 4. Returning from finite covers to the prescribed peripheral algebra The preceding proof may use rational powers of q, the fractional multiplication variable X_0, and the coarse shift S_0=E^L. The desired level-one peripheral operators are Q=exp(-2 pi b t_0), E f(t_0)=f(t_0-i b), E Q=q Q E. Let K_0=ℚ(q,Q). Choose K=F(q^(1/D),X_0), enlarging the fixed finite constant extension F if necessary. It is stable under the automorphism sigma induced by E, since F and q^(1/D) are constant under this action and sigma(Q)=qQ, sigma(X_0)=q^(-1/D)X_0. For a nonzero state A_alpha cannot have degree zero, since multiplication by a nonzero rational function cannot annihilate a nonzero holomorphic germ. (If the state vanishes identically, annihilator existence is trivial.) Thus let A_alpha have degree m>=1 in S_0 and nonzero leading coefficient. The space over K spanned by Z_b,E Z_b,...,E^(mL-1) Z_b is stable under E: the next shift is reduced by A_alpha, and E acts on its coefficients by sigma. Restrict scalars from K to K_0. The resulting space has dimension at most mL[K:K_0] over K_0 and remains stable under E. Hence finitely many powers of E acting on Z_b are linearly dependent over K_0. There is consequently a nonzero annihilator in K_0[E;sigma]. Clear rational denominators and integer contents to obtain coefficients in Z[q,Q], or in the larger allowed ring Z[q^(+/-1/2),Q]. This argument does not assume that Galois automorphisms commute with the fractional-variable shift. Restriction of scalars is what justifies descent. If Z_b is nonzero, an order-zero annihilator is impossible. Existence over K_0 also proves existence over the literature field K_lit=ℚ(q^(1/2),Q). The nonzero annihilator ideal in K_lit[E;sigma] has a unique monic element of least degree by the usual left Euclidean division in a skew polynomial ring. Clearing denominators and taking primitive coefficients gives the literature minimal operator, up to the stated scalar units and sign convention. The monic generator's minimality is a consequence of well ordering and left division, not an assertion that the dimension-count output was minimal. ## 5. Verification for the published geometric FAMED state Recall the existing integral, with scaled boundary x and fiber p^T y=x+i pi gamma: J_X(hbar,x)=C_X(2 pi sqrt(hbar))^(-N) integral exp((i y^T H y+c^T y)/(2 pi hbar)) product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2 pi sqrt(hbar))) dy_2 ... dy_N, hbar=b^2/(1+b^2)^2. (5.1) All H,c/pi,p,gamma are rational as specified in the companion note. Put t_0=x/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)), t_j=y_j/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)), j>=2. Then y_1/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)) =[t_0-sum_(j>=2) p_j t_j]/p_1 +i(b+b^(-1))gamma/(2p_1). The Gaussian becomes a rational quadratic Gaussian in t, with linear coefficients rational multiples of pi(b+b^(-1)). Thus it has exactly the form (1.1), including all the boundary-dependent Gaussian factors. The scalar Jacobian from dy to dt is independent of t_0 and does not affect annihilation. At x=0 use the contour through the actual positive complete geometric saddle y*. Its imaginary coordinates have a fixed gap from 0 and pi. Any fixed finite number of the original shifts t_k->t_k-i b L n_k moves y by O(b^2). For sufficiently small b every Phi argument stays in its defining strip. The strict concavity and global linear tail estimate (5.8)–(5.9) in the companion note persist for these small contour translations and for small complex x. To see the boundary extension explicitly, write y=y*+T u+v x, p^T T=0, p^T v=1, with T,v real. The restricted complex Hessian at x=0,b=0 has negative definite real part and is invertible. The implicit function theorem gives a nearby critical point for small x and b^2. On its horizontal contour all imaginary coordinates remain in (0,pi). The negative definite real Hessian holds at every real u and gives uniform linear tails by the ray argument. These same bounds control the intermediate contours and all exponential moments near z=0. They establish both analytic hypotheses of Section 3. **Theorem 5.1 (literature minimal operator exists).** For every positive geometric FAMED state with the finite peripheral certificates in the companion note, the exact published state (5.1), expressed in boundary t_0, has a nonzero annihilating ideal in ℚ(q,Q)[E;sigma]. Its primitive minimal operator exists in the literature sense. The state is nonzero for all sufficiently small b by its independently proved Gaussian asymptotic. The proof is Sections 1–4 together with the explicit verification above. It is an existence and finite-computability theorem. It does not give an efficient uniform formula for the minimal operator's coefficients or its degree. ## 6. Its classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral curve Keep the same boundary variable and normalization. The uniform saddle calculation near x=0 gives J_X(hbar,x)=B_b(x) exp(Phi_s(x)/(2 pi hbar))(1+o(1)), s=b^2, uniformly on a small complex neighborhood. Here Phi_s is the critical value of the explicit phase F_s in (5.6) of the companion note, is holomorphic in (x,s), and B_b(x) has a nonzero holomorphic leading Gaussian coefficient times hbar^(-1/2). These properties follow from the same strip and concavity bounds, not from an arbitrary formal WKB solution. Since E translates x by -2 pi i b sqrt(hbar), fixed Q corresponds to x=-log Q/(1+s), and therefore E^j J_X/J_X -> ell(Q)^j, ell(Q)=exp(-i Phi_0'(x)), x=-log Q. (6.1) Let Ahat be the primitive minimal operator. Its coefficients are rational in q^(1/2),Q. After clearing denominators and removing their common vanishing power at q^(1/2)=1, its classical symbol A_0(Q,E) is nonzero. Applying (6.1) to the annihilator identity yields A_0(Q,ell(Q))=0. (6.2) Here the classical branch can be identified from the checked gluing data. The constrained saddle has grad F_0=(i xi/2)p, A Log z+B Log z''=i nu+xi e_N, Phi_0'(x)=i xi/2. The symplectic peripheral certificate gives x=H_m+n_1 H_l, xi=H_l, n_1=-2 e_N^T D B^(-1)e_N. Consequently the geometric peripheral curve in this polarization is Q=exp(-H_m-n_1 H_l), E=exp(H_l/2). (6.3) This records the inverse and factor-of-two conventions without silently choosing an SL(2) lift. The PSL eigenvalue ratios are exp(H_m),exp(H_l); for n_1=0 they are Q^(-1),E^2. Rational n_1 is treated on a finite peripheral cover. An SL(2) longitude lift may be -exp(H_l/2), rather than exp(H_l/2); the sign must be fixed using the exact state normalization. The figure-eight conversion below exhibits precisely this issue. The exponentiated gluing equations and (6.3), after clearing their rational exponents, are algebraic. The invertible restricted Hessian isolates the shape solution for fixed boundary near the complete point, so this branch lies on a one-dimensional algebraic component. Equation (6.2) says the irreducible geometric peripheral factor divides A_0 on the stated cover. Additional classical factors have not been excluded, and none is canceled at Q=1. Exact equality with the complete classical A-polynomial is a stronger AJ assertion, not required for the following state volume limit. ### 6.1 Two published operator conventions are not equal at finite b The present b-shift operator translates the scaled boundary x by -2 pi i b sqrt(hbar)=-2 pi i b^2/(1+b^2), and Q multiplies by exp(-(1+b^2)x). Its commutation parameter is q_b=exp(2 pi i b^2). By contrast, Section 4.4 of the FAMED paper defines multiplication by exp(x), a shift x->x+4 pi i hbar, and q_F=exp(4 pi i hbar). These are not an exact renaming of q_b,Q,E. The existence proof above therefore does not prove an annihilator statement for those different finite-b operators. It proves one for the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra acting on the explicitly rescaled literature state integral. There is also a sign to track in the displayed semiclassical substitution in that source: from its stated J~exp(i phi/(2 pi hbar)) and phi'=H_l/2, the positive shift x->x+4 pi i hbar gives exp(-H_l), rather than exp(+H_l). Thus an inverse-longitude convention must be reconciled before using its claimed classical-symbol identification. This follows by direct substitution; no conclusion about all other results in that paper is inferred from it. ### 6.2 Exact figure-eight conversion, including the boundary factor For the ordered two-tetrahedron example, the face maps give Q_f=diag(1,-1), H=diag(1/2,-1), A=[[1,-2],[0,4]], B=[[-1,-1],[0,2]], nu=(-pi,2pi), c=(pi,-pi), p=(-1,1), gamma=0, C_X=1. These finite matrices can be checked directly from the displayed face maps and gluing rows. At boundary spectral coordinate t_0, the fiber is y_1=y_2-x, x=2 pi sqrt(hbar)t_0. Writing y_2=2 pi sqrt(hbar)t gives J_F(hbar,2 pi sqrt(hbar)t_0) = exp(-pi(b+b^(-1))t_0)/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)) integral Phi_b(t)Phi_b(t-t_0) exp(pi i t_0^2-2 pi i t_0 t-pi i t^2) dt. In the Andersen–Malusà state of the companion note, substitute t=t_0-y and use the exact inversion identity. With zeta_b=exp(i pi(b^2+b^(-2))/12), the exact relation is J_F(hbar,2 pi sqrt(hbar)t_0) = zeta_b/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)) exp(pi(b+b^(-1))t_0) J_AM,b(t_0). (6.4) For small complex scaled boundary value, both contours are related within the holomorphic strip, with vanishing vertical ends. This justifies the change of variables as an identity of the selected states. The boundary factor g(t_0)=exp(pi(b+b^(-1))t_0) has E g/g=-q_b^(-1/2). Consequently the corresponding primitive operators are related by Ahat_F(Q,E)=Ahat_AM(Q,-q_b^(1/2) E), (6.5) up to the fixed allowed equation units. At the complete point the geometric FAMED root is E=1 and the Andersen–Malusà SL longitude root is E=-1. Their states have exactly the same volume rate at t_0=0; their ratio there is the explicit phase zeta_b times 1/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)). At generic boundary the factor in (6.4) is exponentially significant in the scaled semiclassical limit and cannot be replaced by an unspecified scalar normalization. The subsequent `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` now compares this two-tetrahedron realization with the p=0 even twist-family realization. For their recorded face orders and printed normalizations it proves J_3(hbar,x)=-exp[-pi i/12+11pi i/(12hbar)]J_F(hbar,x). The move initially reverses x; a certified two-tetrahedron involution proves J_F is even. Both selected states consequently have the same minimal order-two operator (6.5). Its simultaneous Q,E reflection is checked exactly, retaining every nonmonomial peripheral factor. ## 7. The volume statement now concerns a literature quantum A-state **Corollary 7.1.** Under the positive complete geometric and finite matrix certificate hypotheses above, define the quantum A-operator as the primitive minimal annihilator of the exact state (5.1). This operator exists, its classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral component in (6.3), and its prescribed state satisfies lim_(b->0+) -2 pi hbar log|J_X(hbar,0)|=Vol(M). (7.1) The existence and symbol conclusions are proved here. The limit is the independent uniform-remainder and Gaussian proof in the companion note. There is no colored Jones polynomial in these definitions or proofs. The normalization is the published integral's explicit one. An arbitrary solution of its operator is not assigned the same volume rate. Likewise a triangulation-independent scalar or boundary multiplier must be analyzed with its full generic variables before identifying two states. Remaining work for the user's full knot-family objective is concrete: 1. Extend the geometric certificates beyond the twist families to more general alternating knots. The diagrammatic identification and preferred peripheral audit for the twist data are now reconstructed in `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md`. 2. Complete the exact global state transformations, including generic peripheral factors, polarization, normalization and integration cycles, needed to identify these integral realizations as one topological knot state. The positive local charged pentagon and the fiber coarea factor are independently derived in `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`; the full tensor phase, state recovery, and affine move criterion are now in `peripheral_phase_and_state.md`. Its geometric-endpoint moment argument removes the affine slope for every certified path. The actual figure-eight connecting move and ordering changes are audited in `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md`. 3. Establish any desired stronger equality of the entire classical symbol with the classical A-polynomial and compute useful minimal operators. None of these is inferred solely from the existence of Menasco's topological polyhedra or from the abstract annihilator existence theorem. Run `python3 experiments/audit_general_annihilator.py` for exact checks of moment extraction and restriction of scalars, plus numerical checks of actual contour moments and the exact generic-boundary figure-eight conversion. A fractional-coefficient order-two example descends to an exact order-eight operator over ℚ(q,Q); this checks that the proof does not silently assume fractional coefficients can simply be replaced by their integer powers.

title: Volume equality through Conway tangle composition
