If the graph is a cellular connected sphere embedding, Euler gives r+2 white faces; the cut then has 3r vertices, 6r edges and 3r+2 faces. These counts are checks of the labeled ribbon construction, not its topological proof. ## 3. A finite sufficient geometric certificate The required input Q_Delta is a convex three-dimensional ideal polyhedron with the following EXACT labeled incidence: 1. Its ideal vertices are distinct points x_e for e in E(Delta). 2. Its shaded faces are triangles T_v, with the three incident edge labels in the original cyclic order at v. 3. Its white faces F_f follow the original face walks of Delta. 4. Every edge separates one shaded and one white face, with dihedral angle pi/2. All indicated faces and edges are nondegenerate. A concrete certificate consists of future null vertex lifts, outward spacelike face normals, their incidence equalities, strict nonincident supporting inequalities, and the labeled convex-hull face cycles. Adjacent face normals have zero Lorentz product. Finite incidence and strict inequalities certify the asserted convex three-dimensional polyhedron. An unlabeled polyhedron, matching volume or matching cusp count is not a certificate for this diagram. This hypothesis automatically excludes degenerate graph data that cannot be the stated polyhedral boundary. It is uniform in k and r; there is no restriction to a trivalent source partition or to a tree of four-port metric cells. ## 4. The actual face quotient, including every half-twist sign Cut the actual flat augmented complement along its projection sphere. In each projection ball, each crossing-circle semicircle is boundary parallel by its original half disk. Drilling it and opening THAT half disk cancels the introduced handle in the explicit semicircle collar. The half disks are disjoint, so all cancellations give one cut ball in each half. Main segments on its boundary give ideal ends and do not add an interior handle. Its boundary is precisely the labeled medial sphere of section 2. By the certificate, this is also the oriented labeled boundary of Q_Delta. The boundary cell identification extends over the ball by radial extension after choosing interior points. Take two copies Q^+,Q^- with opposite abstract orientations. White faces glue across copies by their original projection labels. At an even disk glue within each copy, fixing O_i and matching C_i1 -> C_i0, C_i2 -> C_i3. (3) At an odd disk glue across the two copies: S_i0+ -> S_i1-: C_i1+ -> C_i3-, C_i2+ -> C_i0-, S_i1+ -> S_i0-: C_i3+ -> C_i1-, C_i0+ -> C_i2-. (4) In both lines the crossing-circle vertex maps to the same disk's vertex in the indicated copy. The reverse maps are inverses. For (4), rotating one side of the twice-punctured disk by ±pi sends (y,z) to (-y,-z), with the projection line z=0. It exchanges its two punctures AND the two half disks. This gives exactly (4) for either sign. The opposite signs retain different collar paths, differing by one full twist; they are not the same peripheral marking. Reversing these literal cuts recovers the original augmented plat exterior. Thus the quotient is the ACTUAL diagram with its original disk labels, main components and half-twist pattern. No assertion about all abstract cubic graphs being realized by a chosen plat is needed: Delta was constructed from that given plat. ## 5. Edge holonomy and complete cusps Every ideal vertex link of Q_Delta is a rectangle: four right-angled faces alternate shaded and white there. Its two opposite shaded sides have equal length. Scale its horosphere so that both have length one, independently at every ideal vertex. Consequently every shaded ideal triangle has its canonical length-one horocycle at each corner. Use the identical decoration in the second copy. Every prescribed shaded triangle map, including the corner exchange in (4), preserves these canonical horocycles. White maps preserve the copied decorations. At each boundary edge the disk partner is distinct from itself: the two triangles paired along a matching edge share only their marked vertex O_i. An alternating disk/white cycle has four pieces, for both (3) and (4), and has total angle 2pi. Here is also the pointwise holonomy check. The edge cycle fixes its two ideal endpoints and preserves the chosen horosphere at each. Its translation/dilation along the edge is therefore zero. Its rotation angle is the sum of the four right angles, namely 2pi. An orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry fixing both endpoints is determined by these dilation and rotation parameters; the word is the identity. Thus there is no leftover edge translation hidden by an angle calculation alone. After a uniform horosphere shrink, the ideal links glue to finite Euclidean surfaces with no cone or dilation defect. The actual link-exterior cut identifies them as cusp tori. Their ends are complete standard hyperbolic cusps. The remaining part is compact, so the entire quotient is a complete finite-volume hyperbolic manifold. Its volume is Vol(S^3 minus L_Delta,D^epsilon)=2 Vol(Q_Delta). (5) This proves a conditional geometric theorem at EVERY fixed plat width. The hypothesis is the explicit labeled positive certificate, not an assertion that a polynomial stationary point must be geometric. The certificate also gives an actual POSITIVE ideal triangulation. Choose an ideal vertex a of Q_Delta. Triangulate every face not containing a by noncrossing diagonals, and subdivide each face that does contain a by its fan from a. Cone a to every triangle in the nonincident faces. Convexity makes these tetrahedra tile Q_Delta with disjoint interiors. Strict supporting inequalities put a strictly off every nonincident face plane, so each tetrahedron is nondegenerate with positive orientation. Use the identical face subdivisions in the second copy. All white subdivisions then match; shaded faces were already triangles. The actual quotient is therefore triangulated by positive ideal tetrahedra, with its complete edge and cusp equations inherited from the metric just proved. This is a constructive geometric triangulation, not an identification with a particular factorial source or an independently proposed potential. ## 6. Primitive crossing-circle paths are still local and explicit At any crossing-circle apex O_i put it at infinity. Its four adjacent white/shaded planes are vertical; their intersection on a horosphere is a rectangle. After a Euclidean similarity its other ideal vertices can be written (C0,C1,C2,C3)=(1,E,-1,-E), E=exp(2pi i x), 0<x<1/2. This x is a measured local geometric rectangle parameter, NOT yet a Newton source variable for a general plat. Put c=cot(pi x)>0. The actual two-white-face longitude and the collar meridians are lambda=-2(E+1), mu_0=E-1, mu_+=-2, mu_-=2E, mu_+-mu_-=lambda. (6) The elementary white and disk maps giving these translations are exactly the local maps (5) in the [half-partner cusp proof](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md). Their use requires only this rectangle and the original disk pairing, not a Conway prism decomposition. The parallelogram area of each (mu,lambda) pair equals the area of the TWO actual cusp rectangles. Thus these are primitive disk-framed bases, with shapes tau_0=2ic, tau_+=2ic/(1+ic), tau_-=2ic/(1-ic). (7) The choice of + or - is the recorded geometric collar convention. Any proposed quantum variable must be calibrated against the actual braid/loop convention; a cusp Hessian does not select that convention. Further full twists retain their actual integer meridian shear. Equations (6)--(7) give the COMPLETE marking. They do not construct the general plat's mixed-source deformation or identify its action. The main-component test is also literal. Let sigma be the outside terminal matching. At disk i let kappa_i be (01)(23) for even parity and (02)(13) for odd parity, in the cyclic chart of section 1. The main components are exactly the connected components of the graph on the 4r terminals with the sigma edges and the kappa edges. Every vertex has degree two, counting parallel edges, so these are cycles. After all crossing circles are filled, the result is a KNOT precisely when this graph is connected. Adding full twists changes neither kappa nor this criterion. This is an exact test on the supplied diagram, not a claim that every parity pattern produces a knot. ## 7. The exact relation to the older NC rectified-core theorem The existing NC theorem starts with a different cubic graph Gamma: its 2b trivalent cup/cap vertices and its 3b physical EDGE coupons. Its crossing-circle diagram has the present matching graph Delta=Fisher(Gamma). Namely replace each vertex of Gamma by the triangle of its three ordered incident slots. The original edges of Gamma become the matching D; all other edges form those facial triangles. Thus |D|=3b and Delta\D is a union of 2b facial 3-cycles. The earlier construction of Q_Gamma plus 2b octahedra produces precisely this medial Delta boundary. Its formula 4b v8+2Vol(Q_Gamma) is consistent with (5), since its half-polyhedron has volume 2b v8+Vol(Q_Gamma). An arbitrary augmented plat does NOT automatically have this Fisher structure. Its matching complement can have other cycle lengths or nonfacial cycles. Even the crossing-circle count r need not be a multiple of three. For example the actual isolated h^4 compiler has r=4 and two nonmatching 4-cycles, so it cannot literally be a source with 3b edge circles and trivalent NC vertices. Its geometry was proved separately; it is not an instance of that NC theorem by relabeling. Even facial triangles alone would not certify the existing original NC source: its black/white ordering and its two noncrossing triple partitions must also match the actual cups and caps. The graph, matching, ribbon order and original marked source all matter. ## 8. What replaces a four-port tree in the general plat The full original quantum source is a planar Morse network of actual two-strand coupons, cups and caps. A sweep may have 2k active strands; coupons at different levels can share a physical strand. The finite operator product is therefore not a product of independently chosen commuting edge scalars or of unrelated theta evaluations. On the representation side a cutting sphere disjoint from the crossing circles and meeting 2m main strands carries the ORDERED puncture meridians H_1,...,H_(2m), their flags, and H_(2m)...H_1=I, modulo the actual common frame. A pants decomposition of that punctured sphere introduces internal curve holonomies and their gluing frames. Matching their traces alone loses the twist conjugators. These frames form a centralizer torsor: with ordered eigenflags the regular semisimple gluing group in PSL(2,C) is multiplicative, and the noncentral parabolic gluing group is additive. An SL(2) formulation also retains its central signs. The original braid word supplies the literal transport, as in the all-bridge Hurwitz presentation already proved in the repo. Thus a multiport replacement must preserve those marked sewing data and the full finite quantum source, including its first normals and recoupling coefficients. The present graph theorem supplies the actual complete geometric target. It does not provide the source's selected period, its nonzero amplitude, its whole-color gap, or the identification of a general mixed-source action with this marked geometric branch. ## 9. Coverage and the precise existence gap For coverage only, [Purcell's exposition](https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/papers/expos-auglinks.pdf) already describes fully augmented links by cubic graphs with dimers, and states hyperbolicity for a nonsplittable prime twist-reduced diagram with at least two twist regions. The broad geometric-triangulation statement for sufficiently long fillings also appears in [Ham--Purcell](https://users.monash.edu/~jpurcell/papers/HamPurcell_GeomTriang.pdf). No geometric existence or filling proof from those sources is used in sections 1--8, and no novelty of the cubic/dimer viewpoint is claimed. Hyperbolicity of the original knot alone does not certify a CHOSEN plat's augmented skeleton. A nugatory kink can be inserted in the diagram of the same hyperbolic knot; its designated crossing circle bounds a disk disjoint from the knot and gives a split added component. The chosen diagram and crossing regions require their own check. For the desired all-k-bridge, all-long-twist-regions theorem, the remaining geometry existence step is therefore explicit: construct or independently prove the positive labeled Q_Delta certificate for the actual reduced augmented skeleton. The quantum source/period and marked mixed-deformation steps are separate. None follows merely from calling the diagram hyperbolic, prime, or a plat. ## 10. Independent finite checks and their scope [The executable audit](../experiments/audit_general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.py) constructs the original terminal intervals, their cubic marked graph, and the full ORIENTED medial face cycles in two independent ways. It checks 87 original Conway/compiler dictionaries, including the isolated h^s examples for 3<=s<=20, and 21 literal plat diagrams with 2<=k<=8. In every plat case all outside intervals and all upper/lower caps are retained; no free component is discarded. The 2k-plat test family has one odd layer joining the k original cap components in a chain, so the direct terminal test also gives a knot parity witness at each tested width. These finite checks audit the actual labels and construction. They do not infer a positive geometric certificate, twist reduction, or a quantum asymptotic from a graph. [Recorded results](../experiments/general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry_results.json). The matching geometry retains the stated positive-certificate hypothesis and Fisher-subclass restriction. It supplies no source asymptotic.

title: Boundary states and an exact meridian-framing correction
text: # Boundary states and an exact meridian-framing correction Research note, 25 October 2026. We use the existing charged AK tensor and the Andersen--Malusà annihilator convention. The independent preferred-longitude construction is proved in `preferred_longitude_cochains.md`; the Phi estimates and saddle argument are those already proved in `literature_state_volume.md`. This gives a uniform boundary-state theorem for the ordinary-fiber case, including singular face matrices. It permits a rational longitude shear of the intermediate spectral coordinate and corrects it explicitly. It does not assume that the shear coefficient is zero. ## 1. Hypotheses and the condition that remains Let a globally branched ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3 have a complete positive geometric structure. The Fourier reduction gives N tetrahedral Phi factors and a d-dimensional allowed real shape space W=im S, where d=N-2k. Let A,B be N by N gluing matrices formed from N-1 independent edge rows and the full preferred-longitude row. The cochain theorem gives W=im B^T, rank B=d, L={ (t,s):t in W, s-Gt in W^perp }=ker(A|-B). The additional hypothesis for this note is rank B_ed=d-1. (1.1) It means the longitude increases the B rank. All proper charts satisfy (1.1), since then d=N and the full edge B rank is N-1. Singular charts can also satisfy it, as the exact 6_2 realization does. The case rank B_ed=d, in which the affine plane moves with longitude, is not silently included. Orient a meridian m and preferred longitude l with intersection(m,l)=1. By the audited cusp formula their eliminated rows obey A_m B_l^T-B_m A_l^T=-2. Fix the geometric logarithmic lifts, normalized so that both peripheral holonomies are zero at completeness. Carry every additive pi constant in eliminating the prime coordinates. ## 2. Rational spectral coordinate and its actual peripheral meaning By (1.1), e_N is in im B. There is a unique v in W such that Bv=2e_N. It is rational. Put p=S^T v and beta=B_m v/2. (2.1) The coefficient beta is not presumed integral or zero. It records a possible longitude shear of the intermediate meridian coordinate. First B_m^T is in W. Indeed the vertical part of L has dimension N-d. The vertical part of the edge isotropic space has dimension (N-1)-(d-1)=N-d and is contained in it, so these spaces coincide. The meridian pairs to zero with every edge row and thus annihilates this vertical space. This is precisely B_m^T in W. Write S^+=(S^T S)^(-1)S^T and b_r=S^+ B_r^T. Symplectic pairing with all completed gluing rows, together with their projected G identity, then proves (A_m-B_m G)S=-p^T, (A_l-B_l G)S=0, b_l^T p=2, b_m^T p=2beta. (2.2) For example the first identity follows by testing on every B^T c in W: the meridian pairing gives -2c_N, whereas v.B^T c=2c_N. No inverse of a singular B is used. Choose a rational strict angle structure theta0, in units of pi, whose lifted meridian and longitude are both zero. It exists: the geometric angle structure lies in this rational affine subspace and in its open positive polytope; rational points are dense there. This is an existence argument, not a claim that arbitrary prescribed peripheral lifts admit such a positive point. In radians put d0=pi*1-a0, C0=E c0, H=Q-P_+/2, W0=2Qd0-C0, y=i d0+S z. All coefficients and imaginary offsets are rational multiples of pi. For any balanced angle structure theta, its first-angle variation belongs to W under (1.1). One way to see this is to eliminate the double-prime variables from the full edge block: its projected solvability space has dimension N-[(N-1)-(d-1)]=d and contains W, hence equals W. Thus d_theta-d0=S eta_theta. The angle equations and the projected Gaussian identity further give S^T(W_theta-W0)=(lambda/2)p, p^T eta_theta=mu-beta*lambda, (2.3) where mu,lambda are the actual lifted angular meridian and longitude. For the first equality, B(W_theta-W0)=lambda*e_N and B has row space W. For the second, use the first identity of (2.2) in the meridian angle equation. The zero peripheral values at theta0 fix the affine constant. ## 3. An exact fiber of the existing tensor Keep the reduction constant c_X, including its three determinant Jacobians, and define I_b(z)=exp[(i y^T H y+W0^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))), h=b^2/(1+b^2)^2, y=i d0+S z. Choose p_j nonzero. Positive Lebesgue disintegration defines J_old(h,x)=c_X/|p_j|*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d) integral_(p^T z=x) I_b(z) dz_(others). (3.1) This includes the constant imaginary Gaussian term; it has not been removed without recording a phase. Use the contour corresponding to theta0, and its holomorphic continuation near the complete fiber. After rebasing a proper chart to S=I, with the same boundary coordinate and the same eliminated coordinate p_j, the earlier printed FAMED convention is J_print=sigma*p_j^2*J_old, where sigma=sign(det(script-A)*p_j). This explicit constant is the conversion already proved in the peripheral-phase note. It leaves the annihilator and volume limit unchanged. For singular charts the printed inverse-determinant formula is undefined, whereas the original charged tensor and (3.1) are defined. Let d_theta=pi*1-a, C_theta=E c and Theta_theta=C_theta.d_theta-d_theta^T Q d_theta, k(a,c)=a c/(4pi)+(a-c)/12-pi/24, K0(theta)=sum epsilon_j*k(a_j,c_j)-pi*N_+/12 +Theta_theta/(2pi), K_old(theta)=K0(theta)+(W_theta-W0).d0/(2pi). The exact charged Fourier and inversion identities now give Z_AK(theta;b)=exp(pi i N/12+i K_old(theta)/h) integral_(R+i(mu-beta*lambda)) J_old(h,x) exp(lambda*x/(4pi h)) dx. (3.2) Thus this function is recovered from a specifically normalized existing tensor, rather than selected as an arbitrary recurrence solution. Fourier--Laplace uniqueness applies on the strip supplied by strict angles. For fixed b, the charged factors and their derivatives have exponential tails. Their injective pullback to W, and then their fiber marginal, make J_old Schwartz with exponential tails on each smaller horizontal strip. Changing the rational reference within mu=lambda=0 only gives an explicit central phase. If W1,d1 are the new reference vectors, then W1-W0 annihilates W, p^T S^+(d1-d0)=0, and contour translation gives J1=exp[i*(W1-W0).d0/(2pi h)]J0. This phase is retained in the level; it does not change the boundary annihilator. ## 4. Exact classical equations and the geometric fiber Let F0 be the classical phase in the z coordinates of (3.1), and set g=(1/i)grad_z F0. For log z_shape=i*pi*1-y and log z_shape''=Log(1+exp y), direct differentiation gives g=S^T(G log z_shape+log z_shape'')-i k0, k0=S^T(pi*G*1+W0). The constant for any gluing or meridian row is exactly zero, because pi*G*1+W0=G a0+b0'', where b0'' is the reference double-prime angle vector. Substitution leaves A_r a0+B_r b0''-nu_r, its reference lifted holonomy. Consequently H_edge=b_edge^T g, H_l=b_l^T g, H_m=p^T z+b_m^T g. (4.1) At a constrained saddle grad F0=i*xi*p/2 these equations say H_l=xi, H_m=x+beta*xi. (4.2) Thus the actual intermediate coordinate is x=H_m-beta*H_l. No assumed meridian formula or presumed zero shear was used. At the complete geometric shapes g=0 and x=0. They lie on the affine plane y=i d0+W: subtract their gluing system from the reference angular system, then use the projection of ker(A|B), which is W. The geometric fiber has all imaginary y coordinates strictly between zero and pi. The real Hessian on its real tangent is negative definite. The uniform Phi remainder, global tail bound and complex saddle proof therefore give lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|J_old(h,0)|=Vol(M). (4.3) ## 5. Converting to the true meridian by a Gaussian operator Use the boundary coordinate t=x/(2pi sqrt(h)) and P=(2pi i)^(-1)d/dt. For real beta define the existing Fourier/Gaussian polarization operator U_beta=exp(-2pi i beta P^2). Here Fourier transformation and multiplication by a Gaussian are the operators of Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1409.1208v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1208v1), Section 6, specialized to A=R. Our multiplier definition specifies the particular shear and its square-root phase, whose identities are checked below. Its definition as a Fourier multiplier fixes its normalization and phase. For beta nonzero its kernel is (2i beta)^(-1/2) exp[pi i(t-t')^2/(2beta)], sqrt(2i beta)=sqrt(2|beta|)*exp(i*pi*sgn(beta)/4). This follows by one Fresnel Gaussian Fourier integral. It also proves U_(-beta)U_beta=I exactly, with no unspecified projective multiplier. For beta=0 use the identity operator. Define the meridian wavefunction by this change of polarization: J_mer(h,x)=1/(2pi sqrt(h)*sqrt(2i beta)) integral_R exp[i(x-x')^2/(8pi beta h)] J_old(h,x') dx', (5.1) when beta is nonzero, and J_mer=J_old otherwise. The real integral is absolutely convergent since J_old is Schwartz. Its analytic continuation to a small horizontal strip is controlled by its exponential tails. Fourier transformation proves the exact Laplace relation integral J_mer(h,x) exp(lambda*x/(4pi h)) dx =exp[i beta lambda^2/(8pi h)] integral J_old(h,x) exp(lambda*x/(4pi h)) dx. For rigor, first use real Fourier frequency. Both sides extend holomorphically to a frequency strip: a small contour shift in x' preserves the old exponential tail, even after its quadratic chirp, and gives an exponential tail for U_beta J_old as well. Analytic continuation gives the displayed Laplace identity near lambda=0. Combining with (3.2) replaces K_old by K_mer=K_old-beta*lambda^2/(8pi), and its contour is R+i*mu. The existing AK level ell=-4K_mer/pi therefore recovers J_mer from that normalized tensor. This proves an exact state identification with a recorded boundary polarization. It does not depend on the unproved assertion beta=0. For the Gaussian-corrected representation this assertion is local in the peripheral variables near the reference, with continuation wherever the stated strip bounds hold. No unproved global continuation through peripheral singularities is being assumed. ## 6. Volume survives this exact correction For beta nonzero, insert (3.1) into (5.1) and perform the real coarea disintegration. Its complete integral, with every scalar retained, is J_mer(h,x)=c_X*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d-1)*(2i beta)^(-1/2) integral_R^d exp[i(x-p^T z)^2/(8pi beta h)] I_b(z) dz. At x=0 the geometric point is still critical, since p^T z_*=0. The additional classical term i*(p^T z)^2/(4beta) is a real quadratic times i, and adds nothing to the real Hessian on a horizontal real plane. The N Phi factors still supply a negative definite real Hessian. The imaginary contour shift from the rational reference to the geometric point keeps p^T z fixed, so the new chirp creates no extra growth during that deformation. The same uniform remainder, tail and Gaussian proof now applies in dimension d. Its Gaussian coefficient is nonzero. For beta=0 it applies on the original (d-1)-dimensional fiber. In both cases lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|J_mer(h,0)|=Vol(M), (6.1) and J_mer is nonzero for sufficiently small h. Both normalizations have the same polynomial saddle scale h^(-1/2); the Gaussian correction does not hide an exponentially significant modulus. ## 7. The exact quantum torus and its annihilator In the Andersen--Malusà convention put q=exp(2pi i b^2), Q=exp(-2pi b t), E=exp(2pi b P), EQ=qQE. Fourier calculation, or the exact central commutator, gives U_beta E U_beta^(-1)=E, U_beta Q U_beta^(-1)=q^beta Q E^(2beta). (7.1) The central power q^beta is essential. For rational beta use the specified finite cover for the fractional E powers and the indicated exponential branch of q^beta. The direct finite-product and moment argument also applies to the integral in Section 6, so a minimal annihilator in the ordinary b-shift algebra exists after descent. Equation (7.1) transforms full quantum-torus annihilators, including nonmonomial peripheral factors. It does not assert preservation of minimal degree after localizing only the Q coefficients. A conjugated polynomial is an annihilator; the primitive minimal generator is a separate statement supplied by the direct existence proof. The new saddle has x=H_m and phase derivative i H_l/2. Therefore its classical branch is Q=exp(-H_m), E=exp(H_l/2). The geometric peripheral factor divides the classical symbol of its minimal annihilator by the proved uniform saddle argument. Q^(-1),E^2 are the PSL(2) eigenvalue ratios; SL(2) lift signs must still be recorded. No equality with the full classical A-polynomial or a Jones-defined AJ operator is assumed. This theorem removes the extra zero-framing hypothesis from the ordinary-fiber construction. It does not treat rank B_ed=d, construct complete geometric triangulations for all alternating knots, identify arbitrary triangulations by certified moves, or prove H-triangulation limits. Those parts of the original objective remain open. `audit_boundary_framing.py` checks the peripheral identities, a Gaussian image and its Laplace multiplier, and 405 quantum-torus multiplication identities before any specialization. The full audited figure-eight operator is transformed and recovered exactly by the inverse shear; all its generic peripheral coefficients are retained. The new framed polynomial is not asserted to have minimal E degree. For 6_2 it also matches this general construction to the previously recorded compact state, including its exact central factor exp(27pi i/(70h)). The subsequent `fourier_boundary_state.md` gives a single inverse-Fourier definition for both possible boundary ranks. It recovers this Gaussian correction exactly in the ordinary-fiber case and proves the volume limit when rank B_ed=d as well. The rank restriction in this note is therefore no longer needed in the combined theorem.

title: What the selected five-crossing proof does and does not generalize
text: # What the selected five-crossing proof does and does not generalize 28 October 2026. This is an independent audit of the proposed extension from the original selected 5_2 period to many bridges or long twist regions. The result below is an exact obstruction inside the original repeated crossing, rather than an arbitrary oscillatory example. It identifies why one useful quadrature theorem cannot simply be iterated after aggregating long twists. It is not an obstruction to the volume conjecture. ## 1. The genuinely reusable input The [five-crossing proof](five_two_selected_volume_proof.md) combines four different facts: * an exact finite whole-source transform; * a lattice-to-integral comparison with every endpoint retained; * global bounds for the selected contour and every quadrature correction; * the geometric action and a nonzero Gaussian coefficient. Only the second item currently has a local criterion that can be read directly from a general finite kernel. Section 5 of [the inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) gives that criterion for a reflected factorial convolution with a quadratic Gaussian. The finite-height version is more general, but produces additional source contours instead of bounding them automatically. The arbitrary-plat reduction and positive gluing arguments supply classical equations and rigidity at arbitrary bridge number. They do not supply the exponential bounds for the finite quantum endpoint sources. Thus neither positive ideal shapes nor an acyclic classical bridge complex currently checks all four items for an infinite hyperbolic knot class. ## 2. An exact sector of an actual long twist Use the original equal-color crossing and its actual Borel fusion from [the whole-word theorem](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md). Its relative coefficient, after retaining the common Cartan scalar kappa externally, is a_R/kappa = sum_(a+k<N) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2) x^(-a-2k) f^a e_k/F_a. The ideal (f) is two-sided. Hence the image of a literal p-fold crossing in the exact quotient by (f), for any integer p, is sum_k d_k^p e_k, d_k=(-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2) x^(-2k). Equivalently these are the actual degree-zero diagonal entries of C^(-1) R^p C/kappa^p. This is an exact matrix sector, not a semiclassical replacement of the full crossing. At the complete color x=-q^(-1), Q=q^2, d_k=(-1)^k Q^(k(k+1)/2). Let n=N-1. A normalized entire interpolation of these literal lattice values is B_(p,N)(z)=exp[pi i p z(z-n)/N]. (1) Indeed its exponent differs from the displayed d_k^p exponent by -2pi i p k, so (1) agrees at EVERY integer k. All ordinary linear lattice gauges have the form B_(p,N,ell)(z)=exp(2pi i ell z) B_(p,N)(z), ell in Z. (2) The quotient calculation does not permit replacing the original knot's whole cut by this sector alone. Its role here is to test a proposed universal local quadrature rule on an actual component of that kernel. ## 3. No linear lattice gauge removes the long-twist type For a=0,n and real t, |B_(p,N,ell)(a+it)| =exp[-pi {p(2a-n)/N+2ell} t]. (3) The largest absolute vertical exponent over the two endpoints and two directions is therefore exactly pi [ |p|(N-1)/N + 2|ell| ]. (4) In particular ell=0 is optimal, and its minimal type approaches pi|p|. This is a minimization over all the linear integer lattice gauges, not a failure to find a suitable gauge. More decisively, the actual endpoint numerator in finite Abel--Plana is explicit. The identities B(n-z)=B(z) and exp(2pi i ell n)=1 give B_ell(it)-B_ell(-it)-B_ell(n+it)+B_ell(n-it) =4 exp(-pi i p t^2/N) sinh(pi p n t/N) cosh(2pi ell t). (5) There is no hidden cancellation between the two endpoints. Dividing by exp(2pi t)-1, its absolute size at infinity is asymptotic, up to a fixed positive constant, to exp{ pi [|p|(N-1)/N+2|ell|-2] t }. (6) Consequently, whenever |p|(N-1)/N>2, no gauge (2) gives the absolutely convergent endpoint integral used in the reusable infinite-height quadrature theorem. For every fixed |p|>=3 this fails at every sufficiently large level. At equality the absolute integral still diverges; no claim about a conditionally regularized formula at that threshold is needed. This exact test includes both crossing signs and every level parity. The common Cartan scalar has no head-index dependence and changes none of (3)--(6). A zero-framing scalar external to a larger braid likewise does not change the endpoint vertical type. ## 4. What a long-twist theorem would have to do differently The subsequent [finite-mode quadrature theorem](finite_mode_source_quadrature_and_long_twists.md) now resolves this particular type obstruction constructively: retain an explicit O(|p|)-sized Fourier packet and an endpoint remainder which is O_p(1) at every level. Its far tail is exponentially small at height proportional to N. The modes and near endpoint correction remain present. The finite-height residue formula remains exact for (1), so this is not a prohibition on that method. It forces one to keep and control the extra contours. At height t=N h their endpoint growth after the Abel--Plana denominator has rate pi [ |p|(1-1/N)-2 ] h. Thus a bound that keeps h fixed while aggregating an arbitrarily long twist has a linearly growing adverse rate already in this actual sector. A valid large-twist argument may instead retain the individual crossings, use heights of order 1/|p|, or prove a different exact recoupling together with all its transformed endpoint sources. The present theorem does not decide which of those succeeds. Nor does the existence of a positive geometric triangulation bound these quantum endpoint terms. Any use of volume monotonicity must first identify the endpoints with specified original lower-complexity periods; an unidentified face of a factorial sum is not automatically the invariant of a drilled or smoothed link. The next genuinely structural theorem is therefore an endpoint transport and bound for a whole bridge move: express every finite-source boundary correction as a specified lower-complexity pointed period, with a proven rate below the geometric main period, uniformly over a diagram class. That is a concrete target suggested by the 5_2 error bound by the original figure-eight invariant. It has not yet been established for arbitrary plats, arbitrary alternating diagrams, or a nontrivial infinite family with unbounded bridge number. ## 5. Coverage, not proof input The primary abstract of Jun Murakami's [double-twist preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00225) (v3 dated 2 May 2025) states a volume-conjecture result for double twist knots. The primary abstract of van der Veen's [Whitehead-chain paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611181) states an infinite family of links. The latter is not a theorem about arbitrary many-bridge knots in S^3. The published [twist triangulation theorem](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/12209830) concerns the Teichmueller-TQFT volume conjecture; its abstract does not identify that state with the original Kashaev scalar. These are coverage checks only. No proof technique or theorem from those papers is used in (1)--(6). The strongest established original-knot output of the present selected finite-source mechanism remains its independently proved figure-eight and five-crossing prototypes. A broad-class theorem is a further task, not a consequence of continuity of the classical geometric point. [Exact original-matrix and vertical-type audit](../experiments/audit_twist_vertical_type_obstruction.py).

title: What capacity can and cannot select in the actual charged source
text: # What capacity can and cannot select in the actual charged source 28 October 2026. The exact original charged coefficient is a useful place to ask for a general lower bound. Three commonly proposed shortcuts do not supply one: ordinary half-plane stability, Lorentzian positivity after taking magnitudes, and a subexponential comparison with positive capacity. The last failure occurs in an actual nonzero source sector, uniformly in the level, after its already proved parallel-edge fusion. This is an obstruction to these particular methods, not to a further phase-aware fusion or to the volume conjecture. The source throughout is the specified functional in [the global charged-flow theorem](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), with its [Fermat/nilpotent residue](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md). No scalar multiple of the invariant or replacement boundary functional is introduced. ## 1. The raw root blocks are not half-plane stable Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1. A genuine two-anchor block is B_L(X,Y)=product_(j=0)^(L-1)(alpha X-Q^j beta Y), alpha beta !=0, 2<=L<=d. (1) A homogeneous linear polynomial aX+bY, with ab nonzero, has no zero with Im X>0 and Im Y>0 if and only if b/a is positive real. Indeed a zero requires X=-(b/a)Y; two open half-planes through zero intersect unless the multiplier maps the upper half-plane exactly to the lower one. A product is stable only when every nonconstant factor is stable. After ANY nonzero diagonal changes X=cX', Y=eY', successive factor ratios in (1) still differ by Q. Since N>=3 here, Q is not positive real. Thus no such change makes (1), or a polynomial containing it, upper-half-plane stable. This also covers arbitrary complex diagonal changes, not just vertex phase gauges. Self-loop factors which have already become scalars or monomials are excluded from this statement. This does not rule out a different stable object obtained by an exact fusion. It prevents applying stable-polynomial coefficient inequalities directly to the original charged product. ## 2. Even the positive sine block is not Lorentzian The exact grouped expansion has positive magnitudes C_(L,k)=|[L choose k]_Q| =product_(j=1)^k sin(pi*(L-k+j)/N)/sin(pi*j/N). Put a_k=C_(L,k)/binom(L,k). Its successive ratios are a_k/a_(k-1) =sinc((L-k+1)*pi/N)/sinc(k*pi/N), (2) sinc(t)=sin(t)/t. On (0,pi), sinc is strictly decreasing: its derivative has numerator t cos t-sin t, whose derivative is -t sin t<0. As k increases in (2), the numerator increases and the denominator decreases. Hence a_k is strictly log-CONVEX at every interior index when L>=2. For a binary homogeneous polynomial with positive coefficients, the Lorentzian coefficient condition is log-concavity after division by binom(L,k). Thus the positive-sine block fails this condition. Already L=2 gives X^2+2 cos(pi/N)XY+Y^2: a nonpositive Hessian determinant would require the middle coefficient to be at least 2; here the determinant is positive. Ordinary positive coefficients have not restored the needed real-rooted or Lorentzian structure. ## 3. Logarithmic torus capacity forgets these root phases entirely For an actual product P_h of unit-modulus binary linear factors on DISTINCT anchor pairs, its Ronkin average is R_h(rho)=average_theta log|P_h(exp(rho+i theta))| =sum_factors max(rho_tail,rho_head). (3) To prove (3), integrate the relative angle of one linear factor. The mean of log|A-Be^(it)| is log max(|A|,|B|); for unequal moduli this follows by expanding log(1-z), and the equal-modulus value follows by an integrable limit. Linearity of the average then gives (3), irrespective of dependencies between the factor angles. If the charge d at every anchor is feasible, choose an endpoint for each factor giving that total charge. Each maximum in (3) dominates the chosen endpoint, so R_h(rho)-d sum_a rho_a >=0. At rho=0 equality holds. Consequently the logarithmic capacity exp inf_rho [R_h(rho)-d sum_a rho_a] is EXACTLY ONE in every feasible sector of this type. If self-loop factors occur, first evaluate them as an explicit scalar times a monomial. The same assertion holds after division by that scalar and subtraction of the monomial's charges; the scalar itself may carry an exponential action and is not omitted from the period. Nonzero selected coefficients in particular have feasible charge. This average is therefore not the exponential volume scale of the original source. It should not be confused with the supremum-over-angles Cauchy bound, or with a capacity which retains further phase information. ## 4. Positive capacity can exceed a surviving actual period exponentially Use the already proved uniform original-source family in [the anchor-phase and exact-fusion theorem](anchor_phase_cycles_and_exact_fusion.md): word=[1,-2,1,1,-2,-2], N=2r+1, h=(0,r,r,r,0,r). Its selected coefficient, INCLUDING every original closure block, is c_N=[X_0^d ... X_8^d]P_h=N q^(2-r^2). (4) The same theorem fuses its two parallel r-blocks into the complete d-block with every coefficient equal to one. Work AFTER this exact fusion. In the remaining flow description choose a=c=f=0, b=floor(r/2). These are feasible original source charges. The only nontrivial magnitude in this term is M_N=|[r choose floor(r/2)]_Q|. (5) Let P_h^+ mean the polynomial obtained from these fused grouped blocks by replacing their coefficient phases by one. It has positive coefficients. Its positive capacity is Cap_d(P_h^+)=inf_(x_a>0) P_h^+(x)/product_a x_a^d. The feasible term (5) contributes M_N product x_a^d. All other terms are nonnegative. Therefore, on EVERY radius, Cap_d(P_h^+) >= M_N. (6) Put J(t)=integral_0^t log(2 sin(pi*s))ds. Elementary endpoint splitting, followed by Riemann summation, gives uniformly for 0<=j<N log |(Q;Q)_j|=N J(j/N)+O(log N). Here r/N tends to 1/2 and b/N,(r-b)/N tend to 1/4. Since J(1/2)=0 and J(1/4)=-G/(2*pi), where G is Catalan's constant, log M_N=(G/pi)N+O(log N). (7) Combining (4)--(7) proves the genuine actual-source gap limsup_(odd N) (1/N)log[|c_N|/Cap_d(P_h^+)] <=-G/pi<0. (8) This family is a nonzero sector of a reduced alternating hyperbolic knot. Its phase curvature and feasibility were proved uniformly, not inferred from an isolated numerical level. For this length-one bridge diagram, all the original W_h factors have unit modulus, so an omitted clock normalizer is not causing (8). Equation (8) rules out a universal subexponential lower comparison between a surviving charged source coefficient and its positive capacity. It does NOT say this particular sector is a leading volume sector: its coefficient is polynomial in N, and its exponential loss is already explained by exact root correlations. It also does not exclude phase-aware capacities after further exact fusions. In particular the new source-exact full-length reproducing contractions and balanced star--triangle moves can change the positive majorant drastically. Equation (8) is not asserted to survive arbitrary such reorganizations. ## 5. The remaining possibility is genuinely phase-aware The finite-flat perfect pairing fixes the source functional; it does not force that functional to be large on a specified state. The calculation above gives a quantitative instance using the actual state and the actual source. A useful general theorem would have to retain the root-phase correlations, for example through exact local fusions followed by a source-compatible geometric contour. Taking magnitudes and invoking stability cannot replace that step. The new [defect-jet theorem](charged_star_triangle_defect_jets.md) makes this connection precise: on the unit-radius original anchor torus the source phase frequency is exactly (S_a-2d)/2, where S_a is incident factor degree. Balanced fusion removes a zero-frequency direction, while its bounded-defect extension retains a finite Fourier correction with polynomial cost. Macroscopic defects and the final global coefficient are still present. The audit here independently checks this phase identity on the actual unfused source graphs. Ordinary dominant-saddle Stokes persistence is consistent with this: in a proper deformation with a strictly highest-action saddle, its top action-graded coefficient is preserved against jumps involving only lower saddles. To use this observation here one still needs a NONZERO original-source coefficient in one chamber and control of singular/boundary competitors throughout the deformation. The positive constrained-lens reference chain supplies neither original cycle comparison by itself. Representation-volume rigidity at complete boundary-parabolic critical points also does not control an entire parameter path or its nonstationary boundaries. No general geometric lower bound or new knot class follows from this audit. Its constructive consequence is a restriction on methods: the exact phase-aware graph fusions address information which each of the three phase-blind shortcuts above loses. [Audit](../experiments/audit_general_charged_volume_selection.py): actual family metadata/source charges, exact small-level coefficients, the feasible positive term on arbitrary radii, the sine normalization inequalities, and the asymptotic rate in (7).

title: Full original long-filling volume under the actual complete-radius balance test
status: Full original filled-volume theorem under complete-radius balance
text: # Full original long-filling volume under the actual complete-radius balance test The subsequent [planar decoration theorem](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) constructs balanced diagrams from every simple triangulated sphere with a chosen dual matching. It includes the full general Morse source and independently long fillings. The theorem below retains its own original scope. conditional-class theorem, 31 October 2026. The condition below is imposed on the one actual complete marked circle packing. Its realization at arbitrary bridge width is not asserted. The proof controls the full original numerator and period for diagrams satisfying this condition, rather than only an all-CROSS contribution. ## 1. The finite geometric condition Fix an original certified marked flat plat $D$, with its simple labeled white sphere and actual complete positive ordinary face curvatures. Retain the original two marked curvatures exactly zero. At each port write its actual ordered quartet as $(x,b,c,y)$, with $A=x+y>0$, and put $$ X_e=Q_b(0)+Q_c(0). $$ The normalization of $Q$ is the original determinant, beta and half-forced-product normalization, as proved in the [cofactor action theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). Assume the following strict balance condition at every port: $$ X_e>\log b\quad\text{whenever }b>0,\qquad X_e>\log c\quad\text{whenever }c>0.\tag{1} $$ No logarithm of a protected zero is required. This is a finite test on one shared complete packing, invariant under its common positive scale. It does not optimize a separate radius vector for each port. For every positive middle $t$ and $A>0$, $$ Q_t(0)>\frac12\log t.\tag{2} $$ Indeed, the actual zero-spectral start action has a strict interior maximum, larger than its terminal-start value $\tfrac12\log t$. This continues to either single-outer-zero case by its exact first-order formula. The only monomial case is $t=0$ and $xy=0$; (2) is not applied there. ## 2. Every sector containing a one-sided port has a global spectral gap The [exact path partition](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) is disjoint at both parities. For $N=2m$, LEFT has $j\leq m-1$, CROSS has $i\leq m-1$ and $j\geq m$, and RIGHT has $i\geq m$. For $N=2m+1$, LEFT has $j\leq m-1$, CROSS has $i\leq m\leq j$, and RIGHT has $i\geq m+1$. The odd central zero-step path belongs to CROSS exactly once. At a fixed port, the [global weighted LEFT theorem](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) bounds the actual absolute value, at arbitrary face phases and every real spectral value, by the rate $$ L_e=\max\left\{\log c,Q_b(0)+\frac12\log c\right\},\qquad c>0.\tag{3} $$ If $c=0$, the finite LEFT polynomial vanishes identically because its $c$ exponent is at least $\lfloor N/2\rfloor>0$. Similarly, the RIGHT rate is $$ R_e=\max\left\{\log b,Q_c(0)+\frac12\log b\right\},\qquad b>0,\tag{4} $$ and the RIGHT polynomial vanishes exactly when $b=0$. Equations (1)–(2) give $L_e<X_e$ and $R_e<X_e$ whenever the corresponding sector survives. This also resolves the protected monomial exception: if one triangle has $t=0$ and $xy=0$, the sector overloading that zero middle is absent, while the opposite surviving sector uses (2) for its positive middle. If both middles vanish, both one-sided sectors vanish exactly. The [global CROSS coefficient comparison](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), Section 8, bounds its value on the same face torus by rate $X_e$, with only a polynomial or logarithmic prefactor. Thus the whole local full numerator is bounded by rate $X_e$, and any chosen LEFT or RIGHT factor supplies a fixed strict loss. Since $D$ is fixed, the minimum of its finitely many surviving one-sided gaps is positive. If none survives, the remainder is identically zero and the subsequent conclusion is immediate. Take any original path sector with at least one one-sided port and CROSS, LEFT or RIGHT assigned elsewhere. The value bounds are uniform over the original common face Cauchy torus. The same marked target extraction therefore gives, for some $\gamma>0$ and all sufficiently large $N$, $$ |Z_{\mathrm{sector}}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_R)| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)},\tag{5} $$ uniformly on the entire real spectral cube $[-2,2]^R$, at both parities. Here $\sum_eX_e$ minus the original ordinary log-radius targets is exactly $\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$, by the calibrated complete source. The protected variables stay zero throughout. No infimum of a sum of local maxima or independent-radius capacity equality is used. There are only $3^R-1$ such sectors. Their sum is exactly the full shared numerator minus its all-CROSS part. Thus (5) also holds for that remainder, after reducing $\gamma$. It is a polynomial of spectral degree at most $d$ in each variable. Multivariate cosine Bernstein extends (5) to a sufficiently thin fixed complex $\delta$ strip, at cost $\exp[2\pi d\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|]$. Reducing the strip height and $\gamma$ gives the same strict gap there. ## 3. Entire original Fourier remainder and the full invariant Apply the [whole-domain three-integration-by-parts lemma](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md), Section 4, to the remainder polynomial. The original sine factors vanish at both endpoints, first derivatives match, and the second-derivative endpoint current is retained. Source derivatives use the fixed strip; Gaussian derivatives are taken only on the real cube. Summing all nonzero original charges with their actual weights and parity gives $$ |I_{\mathrm{full}}-I_{\mathrm{cross}}| \leq C_D\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma')},\tag{6} $$ for a fixed $\gamma'>0$. No infinite sharp-cube charge series is split. All framing and component scalars remain the original ones. The [entire all-CROSS period theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) supplies a nonzero relative filling asymptotic for every fixed independently signed sufficiently long integer vector $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. Its unit critical rate tends to $\Phi_D$ as $\min_i|n_i|$ tends to infinity, with loss $O_D(\sum_i n_i^{-2})$. Choose a diagram-dependent threshold so this loss is less than $\gamma'/2$ and all existing geometric and analytic filling thresholds hold. Then (6) is exponentially smaller than the complete all-CROSS asymptotic. Thus $$ \frac{I_{\mathrm{full}}}{I_{\mathrm{cross}}} =1+O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-c_{\mathbf n}N}),\tag{7} $$ and $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|I_{\mathrm{full}}| =\operatorname{Vol}(\text{the actual smooth filled exterior}).\tag{8} $$ The same conclusion holds after multiplying by the separately recorded original normalization characters and nonzero polynomial-level factors. For the prescribed parity yielding a knot, this is the corresponding full original knot invariant, not a chosen spectral contribution. It does not assert that a given $2k$-plat has minimal bridge number $k$. The quantifiers are: for each fixed certified $D$ satisfying (1), there exists $T(D)$ such that every independently signed fixed filling vector with all $|p_i|\geq T(D)$, in the prescribed parity convention, has (7)–(8) as $N\to\infty$. No bound on ratios $|p_i|/|p_j|$ is needed. There is no joint growing-twist/level estimate or uniform threshold over different diagrams or widths. ## 4. An algebraic certificate and its coverage limit The [source-normalized triangle entropy lemma](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) gives a finite algebraic sufficient test for (1): at every port require $$ (A+b)(A+c)\geq\max(b^2,c^2),\qquad A=x+y>0.\tag{9} $$ Indeed, $Q_t(0)\geq\tfrac12\log(A+t)$, strictly whenever at least two triangle weights are positive. If either middle is positive, its triangle has that strictness, so even equality in (9) implies strict balance. If both middles vanish, the condition is vacuous and both one-sided sectors vanish. The simpler $|b-c|\leq A$ implies (9) and is also sufficient. All tests use the same actual complete marked packing. Realization of this condition for arbitrary $k$ is not proved here. Neither a condition on free local weights nor a comparability criterion alone establishes such a family of actual labeled diagrams. Nothing here asserts that every certified simple-white plat satisfies (1). When it fails, the weighted local full maximum can exceed the cross value at these particular radii, and the general shared forest and phase problem remains. No obstruction to the volume conjecture or to a weaker optimized certificate follows from that failure. ## Validation and scope The proof uses only the linked source theorems and the explicit balance hypothesis. Its conditional full-invariant conclusion does not establish arbitrary-width coverage or a universal balance condition.

title: An endpoint-conditioned energy for the original shared source
status: Explicit joint shared-flow criterion; universal comparison open
text: # An endpoint-conditioned energy for the original shared source 31 October 2026. **Conditional general theorem.** The finite shared-coefficient identities and local coefficient bounds below are proved. Sections 5–6 give an explicit compact shared-flow criterion: keep the endpoint entropy and relative-energy bound on the **same** flow, optionally taking their minimum with the older one-sided envelope. A strict score gap proves the full long-filling limit. The universal geometric inequality for that score remains open; no independent local norm or endpoint concentration supplies it. ## 1. Actual coefficients and both parity supports Fix the original certified flat plat \(D\), with \(R\) coupons, degree \(d=N-1\), ordinary face targets \(d\), and two protected targets zero. Keep the [actual homogeneous source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) and its full polynomial resolvent numerator $$ V_N(\sigma)=\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega_N)^{-1}, \qquad \chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2. $$ The [positive reference at both parities](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) is $$ F_N= \begin{cases} -V_N(-2),&N\ \text{even},\\ V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2),&N\ \text{odd}. \end{cases}\tag{1} $$ For a four-incidence exponent \(v=(v_x,v_b,v_c,v_y)\ge0\) with \(|v|=d\), define $$ p_N(v)=[x^{v_x}b^{v_b}c^{v_c}y^{v_y}]H_{F_N}, \qquad a_N(v;\sigma)=[x^{v_x}b^{v_b}c^{v_c}y^{v_y}]H_{V_N(\sigma)}. \tag{2} $$ The reference satisfies \(p_N(v)>0\) for every such exponent, at both parities. In particular none of the inverses below divides by zero. Protected targets remove every array with positive degree at a protected incidence; they are never replaced by positive marked radii. Let \(\Gamma_N\) be the exact original shared array set: an element \(\boldsymbol v=(v_e)\) satisfies all original face targets. Separate incidences retain their original quartet labels. The path endpoints are \(i=v_b\) and \(j=d-v_c\), so the original classes are determined by each monomial: $$ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} &\mathrm{CROSS}&\mathrm{LEFT}&\mathrm{RIGHT}\\ \hline N=2m&v_b,v_c\le m-1&v_c\ge m&v_b\ge m\\ N=2m+1&v_b,v_c\le m&v_c\ge m+1&v_b\ge m+1 \end{array}\tag{3} $$ They are disjoint and exhaustive. The odd central zero-step monomial is CROSS in this convention. The odd reference derivative retains the same endpoints, so the same partition applies to \(F_N\). For a subset \(A_N\subseteq\Gamma_N\) specified by these supports, put $$ \begin{aligned} W(\boldsymbol v)&=\prod_e p_N(v_e),& \mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma) &=\prod_e\frac{a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)}{p_N(v_e)},\\ Z_A&=\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v),& S_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) &=\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v) \mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma). \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ \(S_A\) is exactly the raw original shared numerator with this support restriction. There is no additional \(N^R\), pivot, or independently normalized face contraction. The sign-adjusted convention differs by a common unit sign and gives the same inequalities. The original external character and Fourier-period factors remain outside the numerator. ## 2. The finite shared Cauchy inequality Define $$ E_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) =\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v) |\mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma)|^2 =\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N} \prod_e\frac{|a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)|^2}{p_N(v_e)}. \tag{5} $$ Cauchy on this one shared array set proves $$ |S_A(\boldsymbol\sigma)|^2 \le Z_AE_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le Z_AE_{\Gamma_N}(\boldsymbol\sigma).\tag{6} $$ The full energy is a concrete positive shared coefficient: $$ \begin{aligned} E_{\Gamma_N}(\boldsymbol\sigma) &=[\text{original targets}]\prod_e K_N(\sigma_e;x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e),\\ K_N(\sigma;l)&=\sum_{|v|=d}\frac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)}l^v. \end{aligned}\tag{7} $$ Equation (7) by itself supplies no domination by the endpoint source. It retains every original face demand and does not replace extraction by a product of independent local norms. Equivalently, for \(Z=Z_{\Gamma_N}\) and \(\mu_N(\boldsymbol v)=W(\boldsymbol v)/Z\), $$ \frac{S_A}{Z}=\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[\mathcal R\,1_A],\qquad \frac{E_{\Gamma_N}}Z=\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[|\mathcal R|^2],\qquad \frac{|S_A|}Z \le\sqrt{\mu_N(A)\,\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[|\mathcal R|^2]}.\tag{8} $$ Endpoint concentration does not control an exponentially large ratio on a rare array. The new input is a second-moment bound on this same distribution. Shared face rescaling does not improve (6). Multiplying each reference coefficient by the same face monomials multiplies \(W\), on every feasible array, by the fixed scalar \(\prod_f L_f^d\). It scales \(Z_A\) and \(E_A\) reciprocally, leaving their product unchanged. ## 3. The sufficient rate and its filling consequence Write \(\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\). The [endpoint source theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) gives \(N^{-1}\log Z\to\Phi_D\). Let \(\mathrm{NC}_N\) contain every array with at least one noncross port. Its [unique-maximizer concentration](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md) gives $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log Z_{\mathrm{NC}} \le\Phi_D-\gamma_D,\qquad\gamma_D>0.\tag{9} $$ If this support is empty, its original remainder is zero. Otherwise a sufficient new estimate is $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}E_{\mathrm{NC}}(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le\Phi_D+\gamma_D-\varepsilon \quad\text{for some }\varepsilon>0.\tag{10} $$ Using the full energy in (10) is stronger. Equations (6) and (9) then give $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \le\Phi_D-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.\tag{11} $$ Thus an energy rate at most \(\Phi_D\) would suffice, but is not necessary: the endpoint mass gap leaves the additional budget \(\gamma_D\) in (10). For individual sectors with endpoint rate \(z_s\) and energy rate \(e_s\), the sufficient condition is \(z_s+e_s<2\Phi_D\). The two optimizations must retain their own shared constraints; their maximizing flows need not agree. Each \(S_A\) has degree at most \(d\) in each spectral coordinate. Under \(\sigma_e=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e)\), Bernstein's bound extends (11) to a sufficiently thin fixed complex strip, with cost at most \(\exp(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|)\). Shrink the strip to retain a positive gap and apply Cauchy for fixed derivatives. The [whole-domain current argument](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md) then bounds the entire summable charge series, retaining second-derivative endpoint currents. It uses no infinite sharp-cube localization. Together with the [ALL-CROSS long-filling theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md), (10) therefore implies the full invariant's volume limit for \(D\) and independently sufficiently long, fixed signed twists. The filled action approaches \(\Phi_D\), so its loss can be made smaller than the fixed remainder gap. This is a conditional implication, not an established universal energy estimate. ## 4. Exact reduction to spectral coefficient suprema Define $$ k_N^*(v)=\frac1N\log\max_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|, \qquad h_N(v)=\frac1N\log p_N(v).\tag{12} $$ The coefficient polynomial is nonzero: (1) excludes simultaneous vanishing of its endpoint value and first derivative. For nonempty \(A_N\), put $$ J_{A,N}=\max_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N} \sum_e\bigl(2k_N^*(v_e)-h_N(v_e)\bigr). $$ Then, exactly, $$ e^{NJ_{A,N}} \le \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}E_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le |A_N|e^{NJ_{A,N}}.\tag{13} $$ The upper bound treats each positive summand. For the lower bound choose a maximizing **shared** array, then maximize each of its coefficient polynomials in its independent spectral coordinate. All these choices occur in the same source. No shared face radius is separately optimized. Since \(|A_N|\le\binom{d+3}{3}^R\), the logarithmic error in (13) is \(O_D(\log N/N)\). The [uniform reference entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) replaces \(h_N(v)\) by \(h(v/d)\) with uniform \(o(1)\) error. Thus the energy question is exactly the finite shared-flow condition $$ \limsup_N\max_{\boldsymbol v\in\mathrm{NC}_N} \sum_e\bigl(2k_N^*(v_e)-h(v_e/d)\bigr) <\Phi_D+\gamma_D.\tag{14} $$ No continuous limit for \(k_N^*\) is assumed. A feasible array sequence exceeding this budget would disprove this sufficient route; a large local ratio without the remaining original targets would not. ## 5. A joint variational criterion on the original shared flow Let \(\mathcal P_D\) be the compact polytope of nonnegative original four-incidence loads \(q_e\), with \(\sum_vq_{e,v}=1\) at every port, ordinary face sums one, and protected face sums zero. Repeated incidences, when present in an allowed source, are counted with their actual labels. Write \(h(q)\) for the proved continuous full reference entropy. In the closed CROSS region \(q_b,q_c\le1/2\), it is the two-triangle entropy \(h_C(q)\), including the constrained split of the outer loads. The [one-sided relative-energy theorem](actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.md) and the CROSS interpolation bound give, uniformly on the actual finite supports and on the whole real spectral interval, $$ \frac1N\log\frac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} \le g(v/d)+o(1),\qquad g(q)= \begin{cases} h_C(q),&q_b,q_c\le\tfrac12,\\ C(q_x,q_y,\tfrac12-q_x-q_y),&q_c\ge\tfrac12 \text{ or }q_b\ge\tfrac12. \end{cases}\tag{15} $$ On either seam the retained triangle has middle load \(1/2-q_x-q_y\), so the formulas agree. At \((q_b,q_c)=(1/2,1/2)\) both are zero. Thus \(g\) is a well-defined continuous function on the full simplex. It does not reassign either middle load. A zero actual coefficient satisfies (15) with logarithm minus infinity. Define on the **same** original feasible flow $$ H(\boldsymbol q)=\sum_eh(q_e),\qquad G(\boldsymbol q)=\sum_eg(q_e),\qquad \mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}} =\left\{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D: \max_e\max(q_{e,b},q_{e,c})\ge\tfrac12\right\}. \tag{16} $$ The exact finite noncross set is contained in this closed set after scaling by \(d\). The set may also contain limiting boundary flows of patterns that are eventually infeasible; keeping them enlarges the maximum and is safe for this upper criterion. Empty maxima are minus infinity. For **each** feasible finite array, uniform reference entropy and (15) give $$ \prod_e|a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)| \le\exp\left\{\frac N2 [H(\boldsymbol v/d)+G(\boldsymbol v/d)]+o(N)\right\}. \tag{17} $$ The error is uniform over all arrays and real spectral coordinates. Sum (17) over the original noncross arrays. Their number is polynomial in \(N\), and compactness and continuity then prove $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}| \le\frac12\max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} [H(\boldsymbol q)+G(\boldsymbol q)].\tag{18} $$ This is an arraywise inequality. It is stronger than replacing the right side by \(\tfrac12(\max H+\max G)\), whose two maximizers may differ. It requires neither an unknown limiting spectral coefficient function \(k^*\) nor a minimax exchange. **Joint criterion.** For the fixed certified diagram, the explicit condition $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} [H(\boldsymbol q)+G(\boldsymbol q)]<2\Phi_D} \tag{19} $$ implies a fixed real spectral gap for the entire noncross numerator. The polynomial strip extension and whole-domain current argument of section 3 then prove the full invariant's filled-volume limit for independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists, with its original mark, characters, and normalization. The ALL-CROSS relative asymptotic remains the leading term. Condition (19) is a proved sufficient reduction; its validity for every certified diagram is open. ## 6. Combining the energy bound with the earlier envelope One can retain both available local estimates without comparing them. On the closed LEFT simplex let \(t=2(1-q_c)\) and define $$ h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q)= \begin{cases} t\,C(q_x/t,q_b/t,q_y/t),&t>0,\\ 0,&q=e_c. \end{cases}\tag{20} $$ RIGHT is the literal interchange of \(b,c\). This continuous perspective is the exact concave conjugate of the [proved weighted upper envelope](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) \(\max\{\log c,Q(x,b,y)+\tfrac12\log c\}\): its two atoms have loads \(e_c\) and \(\alpha+e_c/2\), respectively. Finite positive outer and middle tilts, followed by a finite compact covering as in the local energy theorem, therefore give a uniform **coefficient upper bound** \(N^{-1}\log|a_N|\le h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q)+o(1)\). This does not decompose the finite source into the two atoms or exchange an infimum over shared radii with their maximum. Protected faces continue to impose exponent zero; a sector with protected overloaded middle is identically absent. Put \(\widetilde h=(h+g)/2\) and $$ h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q)= \begin{cases} h_C(q),&q_b,q_c\le\tfrac12,\\ \min\{h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q),\widetilde h(q)\}, &q_c\ge\tfrac12,\\ \min\{h_{\mathrm{env},R}(q),\widetilde h(q)\}, &q_b\ge\tfrac12. \end{cases}\tag{21} $$ The formulas agree on their seams. Taking the minimum of two uniform bounds is valid; no assertion that \(\widetilde h\le h_{\mathrm{env}}\) is needed. Repeating the same finite-array sum proves $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}| \le\max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} \sum_e h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q_e).\tag{22} $$ **Combined criterion.** The compact, original-incidence condition $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} \sum_e h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q_e)<\Phi_D} \tag{23} $$ has the same full signed long-filling consequence. It is sufficient whenever (19) holds. It also retains every previously established genuine sector or branch-cover certificate based on the one-sided perspective envelope: (21) only lowers that comparison on each covered original sector. To handle the closed-set convention, a flow with a strict overload is approximated by the proved full-support integer flow rounding while retaining that overload; a subsequence fixes its actual finite sector. Continuity then extends the corresponding certificate. At flows with only terminal seams, the score equals the endpoint entropy, whose strict gap on this closed noncross boundary is already proved. This is an implication between criteria, not a claim of a newly verified strict enlargement of the diagram classes. No concavity of (21) is asserted or required. Equations (18) and (22) use direct compact maximization of the original flows, not unproved convexity or an independent optimization at each face. Proving (23) universally, or finding a feasible original flow that obstructs it, is the remaining geometric entropy problem. ## 7. Proved inputs and remaining limits The [CROSS cofactor interpolation theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) already gives coefficientwise \(O(\log^2N)\) domination by the CROSS endpoint polynomial. That polynomial is at most \(H_{F_N}\) at both parities. CROSS factors therefore have polynomial energy cost. The [support-preserving endpoint estimates](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md) also bound (7) on small spectral polydisks. The general one-sided theorem now supplies the local triangle bound (15). The unresolved step is the global comparison (19) or (23) on the original shared-flow polytope. A new [protected-outer theorem](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md) computes \(k_N^*\) and its relative-energy limit there, with uniform closed boundary control. It is a local input to (14), not a shared-flow estimate. Earlier metrics do not supply (10). The [complete-circle positive quotient](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) bounds transmission on an already inserted \(L_N\), not replacement by \(V_N\) or overlapping coupons. The [full Fourier–Hermite Gram](actual_filling_fourier_hermite_gram.md) has an actual whole-source excess-energy example on a redundant normalization insertion, but is not the energy (7). The [Newton-turn Gram](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) keeps turns and coherent reflected circuits; it does not bound arbitrary source energies. The [length-normalized star](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) retains both coefficient and dual weights, which cannot be dropped. The new joint and combined-score reductions use the proved uniform local theorem; their global strict inequalities remain hypotheses, not general volume comparison theorems. Sections 5–6 prove conditional reductions; their universal strict entropy hypotheses remain open.

title: General equality: proved families and the remaining problem
text: # General equality: proved families and the remaining problem The current results include a volume theorem for every fixed strict Conway tree with independently sufficiently long signed twists, and its marked net-twist and closure extensions. A second [quantitative theorem](actual_all_circle_quantitative_volume.md) covers the specified ordered circle trees under \(\sum_v d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le2^{-25}\). It constructs the original hyperbolic knot complement and proves the full invariant limit, uniform shrinking-meridian profile and preferred cusp correction. Its geometric completion is proved, including the short powers permitted by that bound. The remaining problem is to cover knots outside these sufficient conditions and to identify the selected classical geometric factor of the quantum recurrence. The [current guide](../book/chapters/frontier.md) separates those questions from the established results. ## Earlier general-plat research, 28–30 October The dated entries below record the dependencies of the general-plat approach at that stage. An open step in that approach is not a missing hypothesis of the Conway theorems stated above. 30 October 2026 update: the [complete signed augmented source](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) now has an all-level volume equality for every connected labeled right-angled certificate at arbitrary fixed width and every retained half-twist pattern. text: # The full even Fejér endpoint source has the actual complete volume 31 October 2026. general endpoint-volume theorem. This is an endpoint theorem for the original positive polynomial numerator. It does not rename that numerator Kashaev's invariant, prove its Gaussian filling transform, or assert the fixed long-filled knot conjecture. ## 1. Statement and normalization Fix a connected original flat plat D, at any fixed bridge width, with R ports and its literal ordered face incidences (x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e). Retain the original two protected faces u,v and their MAIN edge. Assume the existing labeled convex ideal right-angled certificate for its actual untwisted augmented exterior Y_D. Thus Y_D is hyperbolic and its two original cut balls, white/shaded face pairings, crossing-circle matching and primitive markings are specified. No realization of an unrelated triangulation is sufficient for this hypothesis. For even N put d=N-1 and use the original pair Casimir Omega_N and its full characteristic polynomial chi_N(sigma)=2T_N(sigma/2)+2, V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega_N)^(-1), P_N=-V_N(-2)=4(2+Omega_N)^(-1). The middle expression is the actual polynomial numerator, including its repeated-node data. H is the original homogeneous coupon compiler. Set Z_(D,N)=[prod_(f ordinary)L_f^d] prod_(e=1)^R H_(P_N)(x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e) |_(L_u=L_v=0). (1) All coefficients in (1) are nonnegative. All source scalars and the marked coefficient targets are retained; no additional N^R is inserted. Then lim_(even N->infinity) (2pi/N) log Z_(D,N) =Vol(Y_D). (2) The limit runs through all even levels, including composite levels. Its hypotheses impose no bound on the fixed bridge width or number of ports. The geometric certificate and original flat-plat incidence are essential stated assumptions. This theorem concerns the complete augmented exterior, not a metric obtained by long filling. ## 2. One continuous entropy on the full local simplex The [closed local coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) gives the one-sided entropy E(mu,nu,xi)=inf_l {integral_mu^nu g(t,l)dt-xi*l}, g(t,l)=l/2+log tan(pi*t) +asinh(tan(pi*t)cosh(l/2)), 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu. Its triangular endpoint is C(alpha)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x), for nonnegative alpha of sum1/2, and its ABSOLUTE normalization is C(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi), V(theta)=2sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)]. On q=(X,B,Cm,Y)>=0 of sum1 define h by the two E branches when Cm>=1/2 or B>=1/2, and by max[C(alpha)+C(beta)] over the actual cross split when B,Cm<=1/2. The branches agree at both terminal seams; h is continuous on the ENTIRE closed simplex and h(0,B,1-B,0)=0. Every degree-d monomial is present in the full positive H_P. Uniformly over those monomials, its coefficient p_N(n) satisfies N^-1 log p_N(n)=h(n/d)+o(1). (3) This is the [uniform full-kernel theorem](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md), proved from the closed half-block estimates, positive cross convolution, the coefficientwise cross comparison and continuous seam values. It retains the finite forced outer factor. It does not require assigning a fixed half label to a limiting seam point. Let Q_D be the compact nonnegative incidence-flow polytope: each port supplies1, each ordinary face demands1, and protected demands are0. Repeated local incidences remain distinct arcs. Scaling a flow by d and fractional-cycle rounding preserves exact integer balances with at most one unit of error per incidence. Every rounded local vector is in the full support. The number of summands is polynomial in N. Thus (3), positivity and compactness prove lim_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N) =W_D:=max_(q in Q_D) sum_e h(q_e). (4) The [all-cross comparison](actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md) and the [complete source volume theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) give W_D>=Phi_D:=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). It remains to prove the opposite inequality for a maximizer of (4). ## 3. Remove pure-middle maximizing ports by exact source identities Choose a maximizer q, including maximizing triangle allocations at its cross ports. Let J consist of ALL ports with both outer loads zero. This includes one-sided diagonals and the pure-middle cross seam. The literal identity coupon is H_1(b,c)=sum_(j=0)^d b^j c^(d-j). It has entropy zero on the whole pure-middle segment, and coefficientwise H_1<=H_P. The mixed source with H_1 on J therefore has rate at most W_D. The SAME maximizing q is feasible for its mixed flow problem and has the same entropy. The full-kernel flow theorem with identity nodes gives the reverse inequality, so these rates are EXACTLY equal. No finite cross monomial with zero outer degree is invented. The selected middle edges form a forest in the original gap graph. Every possible original middle cycle contains the protected exterior; its unit edge supplies would exceed its vertices' total demand. A tree cannot contain both protected vertices either, by the same load count. For each remaining monomial, its identity degrees along a tree are uniquely determined by subtree balances and lie between0 and d. Consequently exact coefficient extraction contracts each identity tree to its ordinary/protected merged face, with coefficient one and no multiplicity. This is the [actual connected identity smoothing](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md). The inherited maximizing local vectors at the remaining ports still have positive total outer load. A loop in the smoothed white cellulation would enclose v ordinary vertices but only v-1 whole ports and one half port. Its demand forces that half port's middle load1, making it pure-middle, a contradiction. A retained matching edge between the two protected roots would also force a pure-middle port. Thus the remaining white triangular cellulation is loopless, with distinct adjacent protected roots. Multiple edges are retained. The empty source has rate zero and is handled separately; it cannot attain W_D>=Phi_D>0. ## 4. Hybrid Hall theory resolves all remaining forced boundary degrees At the inherited maximum tag each B,Cm<=1/2 port CROSS, retaining its two triangle allocations. Every other port is GREEN, in a strict one-sided chamber with 0<=mu<nu<1/2. A CROSS port supplies two triangle nodes of mass1/2. A GREEN port supplies one node of mass1 incident to its four original faces. Its entropy is E, not two independent triangle entropies. A shared outer incidence is aggregated once for this node. For an ordinary vertex set S, merging a triangle pair changes its Hall capacity by +1/2 exactly when one triangle touches S and the other does not. It never decreases capacity. The [hybrid Hall theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) proves: * Every proper tight set is a union of actual digon interiors, after adjoining neighboring holes joined by a GREEN matching edge. * Their surviving cuts are MAIN/MAIN, or MATCHING/MATCHING with BOTH boundary ports CROSS. No GREEN pair is split. * These tight sets explain exactly the structurally forced zero arcs. Every other ordinary arc is positive in one common feasible witness. For completeness, the counting behind this classification is exact. On the induced graph of U=V\S, let p count original triangle faces and n=|U|. Euler and boundary-walk length at least2 give p<=2n-4; equality forces a connected induced graph whose other faces are genuine digons. Hybrid equality additionally forbids a GREEN edge from separating a triangle touching S from one not touching S. Adjacent such holes merge along the same parallel-edge pair. For proper S these mergers are paths, not cycles. Thus the surviving cuts have precisely the types above. The reserve-epsilon Hall test then proves the positive-witness assertion. Split along these actual permitted cuts, iterating on the inherited marked pieces. The child boundary loads are zero. At a matching cut, the separated CROSS triangles are the original additive C rows; their pure-middle closing caps have entropy zero. Formal re-pairing of two boundary C rows is only bookkeeping and creates no physical coupon. The resulting hybrid flow and entropy constraints are Cartesian across pieces. Every piece perturbation reassembles an original cross split, whose full h is at least the corresponding C+C value. Hence the inherited point is maximizing on each piece.
