Mix that point slightly with its strictly positive relative hybrid witness. CROSS allocations stay within their triangle simplexes, so no terminal seam is pushed into a losing one-sided chamber. The strict GREEN row margins persist. The [proved corner expansions](actual_fejer_nondiagonal_maximizer_regularity.md) give only nonnegative epsilon log(1/epsilon) terms and a strictly positive one at every activated ordinary zero. All other changes are O(epsilon). Maximality therefore excludes every ordinary zero except the two marked faces and the zero-dimensional closing rows. Diagonal losses are absent: all pure-middle ports were removed in section3. Finite-dimensional row-space Lagrange multipliers now exist on each piece, including when the balance equations are redundant. Exponentiating them gives finite positive ordinary curvatures. The local equations are the actual tangent-circle formula for each C row and the actual Green equations L(mu;x,y)=b, L(nu;x,y)=c for each E port, with their proved one-line/two-line limits. Every ordinary signed star sums to0 or2pi. ## 5. The entropy is the volume of a representation of the original group The [hybrid-piece representation theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_piece_representation.md) applies to exactly these data. Its essentials are included here to specify the volume being bounded. Each piece develops ONE signed circle family by finite-center star holonomy. The marked edge may be MAIN or MATCHING. In the latter case its two incident rows are the positive zero-entropy CROSS closing halves, so the same two-line strip construction applies. All permitted parallel marked chords have been split. No unproved translation holonomy remains. Along the actual cut tree, map each child's ordered tangent boundary planes to the parent's pair by ONE Mobius map. This gives one reflection for each occurrence of an actual shared white face. A GREEN port remains within one piece and retains its entire local source collar. At an original CROSS port spanning pieces, the common outer product P is noncentral parabolic. Its two raw first meridians have trace-2 and Tr((P+I)A)=4. The parabolic centralizer acts simply transitively on them, so there is a unique C mapping the WHOLE ordered input pair to the output pair and all three recorded contact flags. This is the original shaded pairing, even when its two triangles lie in different pieces. Use the two original topological cut balls and the original face maps. One global reflection develops the second ball. Their proper digon-cut disks have both ends at the same tangent-pair contact. Compatible finite incidence horospheres and the short-edge tetrahedron bound make the added cut-disk volume tend to zero. Signed cyclic polygon coning, including winding-zero faces and repeated contact images, then computes the actual relative fundamental chain: Vol(rho_sm)=sum_pieces sum_triangles sigma V(theta) =2pi*(inherited maximizing entropy). (5) Each piece uses its own genuine marked contact in this chain calculation. Mobius invariance is used for geometric tetrahedron volumes, not for an open crossing expression with a reset Gauss flag. The failed local re-framing argument is neither needed nor reinstated. Finally restore the deleted original auxiliary meridians as identities. The ordered physical pairs coincide across each identity smoothing. Their outer product need not be parabolic; the established axial (loxodromic or elliptic), parabolic, or central zero-volume filling cap retains its actual peripheral flag. Thus rho_sm extends through the actual quotient to a representation rho of pi_1(Y_D), with the SAME relative volume. Equations (4)--(5) give 2pi W_D=Vol(rho)<=Vol(Y_D). The last inequality is the [independently proved representation-volume bound](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) for the original hyperbolic exterior. Together with the all-cross lower bound this proves (2), including the absolute volume constant. ## 6. A strict identity-insertion consequence The same argument starts with any fixed nonempty set I of original identity coupons and P coupons elsewhere. If its mixed incidence polytope is empty, its coefficient is zero at every even level and its rate is -infinity. Otherwise its original identity graph is a forest with at most one protected vertex per tree, and its coefficient contracts exactly. The full-kernel theorem gives a compact maximum. Any further pure-middle maximum ports can be added to I: lifting the identity degrees gives a feasible pure-middle assignment in the original graph, so the union is again a permitted forest. The hybrid argument and actual representation assembly then apply unchanged. The resulting representation kills each specified original auxiliary meridian. Those are essential in Y_D. The [already proved strict-kernel volume bound](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) therefore gives lim_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N;H_1 on I) <Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (6) The empty remaining source has rate zero, also strictly below the positive complete hyperbolic volume. This is a strict statement about the actual positive identity-inserted source. It is not a phase-sensitive estimate for all small colors or a replacement for their normal data. ## 7. What is still required for the requested knot conjecture The theorem closes the COMPLETE even positive endpoint estimate, at arbitrary fixed bridge width under the labeled geometric certificate. It does not control the full Gaussian-resolvent contour away from this endpoint, its nonzero Fourier charges, the selected geometric cycle or its nonzero contribution. The [odd regularized numerator theorem](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) now supplies the same rate for its actual value-plus-spectral-derivative coupon, and fixed spectral jets have an explicit polynomial bound. These are spectral derivatives at the fixed root, not genuine-q normals. Independently long fixed signed fillings still require those quantum inputs, with the original peripheral normals and scalars, before the filled hyperbolic volume can be concluded. The general original Kashaev volume conjecture remains OPEN. Its target has not been replaced by (2). ## 8. Finite verification The [focused structural audit](../experiments/audit_general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume_results.json) check 41 literal loopless identity smoothings at widths two, three and four; 918 hybrid patterns; 121004 exact Hall cuts; 716 tight-set covers by independently constructed actual dual digon disks; and 816 independent positive-arc max-flow tests. The original local coefficient, physical source and signed-volume audits remain linked in the dependencies. These finite tests supplement the general proof; they do not numerically prove the asymptotic or the relative fundamental-class identification.

title: The original full spectral numerator has the marked geometric packet
status: Full fixed-complex numerator packet; spectral cycle open
text: # The original full spectral numerator has the marked geometric packet 31 October 2026. . This assembles the exact local cofactors, their independently proved relative packets and their angular estimates with the original shared coefficient period. The full Gaussian filling cycle is not selected here. ## 1. Original source and exact local reference Fix a connected original flat plat $D$ with $R$ ports, the original two protected faces $u,v$ joined by a MAIN edge, and its labeled convex ideal right-angled certificate. The ordinary white graph is the original simple triangulated sphere with $u,v$ removed. All coefficients, cups, caps and the marked target are the original ones. Put $d=N-1$ and $$ \begin{aligned}S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)&=\left[\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d\right]\left.\prod_e H_{V_N(\sigma_e)}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0},\\ \sigma_e&=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e),\qquad w_e=-\sigma_e-2.\end{aligned} $$ Write $P_{\mathrm{cross}}$ for $(-1)^d$ times the literal local CROSS numerator, and $C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$ for the same marked coefficient with $P_{\mathrm{cross}}$ at every port. The full source is $(-1)^{dR}C_N$ plus its actual one-sided remainder. Let $\mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L)$ be the exactly anchored even interpolation from [the actual complete-fold interpolation](actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md). The [local nodal-rigidity theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_interpolant_rigidity.md) proves, uniformly in one FIXED complex neighborhood of the complete positive ordinary radii and fixed small complex $\boldsymbol\delta$ disk, with the protected zeros unchanged, $$ P_{\mathrm{cross}}=N^2\mathcal B_{e,N}\left[1+O(e^{-\kappa N})\right].\qquad (1) $$ This uses independent relative estimates of the ACTUAL finite cofactors; it is not inferred from complete-node values alone. Both parities, including the odd simple node and every repeated-node spectral datum, are included. ## 2. The actual global angular complement The [global local-angular theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) supplies the following property for every actual triangle cofactor $R_n$, $n=N/2+O(1)$. Fix its positive nonzero face radii. When the arguments of two of its nonzero faces differ by at least $\varepsilon\pmod{2\pi}$, there are $c,\tau>0$ and a polynomial $B(N)$ such that $$ \left|R_n(xe^{i\theta_x},be^{i\theta_b},ye^{i\theta_y};w(\delta))\right|\leq B(N)e^{-cN}R_n(x,b,y;0).\qquad (2) $$ for every real $\operatorname{Re}\delta$ and $|\operatorname{Im}\delta|\leq\tau$. The constants can be uniform on a fixed compact of these radii. A triangle with only one nonzero face is an exact monomial and has no relative angular constraint. Zero faces stay exactly zero. The estimate covers the literal terminal indices $m-2,m-1,m$ as required by the even and odd central formulas. The proof of (2) is source-specific. Every required lower cofactor is a polynomial of degree at most its row index in $w$. Its actual physical node values are nonnegative coefficientwise and bounded by its endpoint value. Nearfold node values contain the original positive $D_a$ factor, whose established angular contraction applies to the nonzero faces. Far-node values are strictly smaller: when $xy>0$, a positive fraction of disjoint tail dimer choices enlarges the endpoint tail exponentially relative to its nodal monomer upper bound. When $xy=0,\ b>0$, small starts have the strict starting-row gap and the remaining starts have an exponentially contracting prefix product. The $b=0,\ xy=0$ case is the literal monomial exception. Exact cosine-grid interpolation loses only a polynomial, also when finitely many terminal nodes must be omitted; Bernstein growth costs $e^{2\pi n|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$, absorbed by a fixed thin strip. The separate protected-middle three-step proof supplies an independent direct check on a fixed $w$ disk. The exact central formula for $P_{\mathrm{cross}}$ is a sum of two or three products of these cofactors and factors of bounded face degree. Each summand contains a cofactor for BOTH of its original triangles. Thus if either triangle has the separation in (2), every summand contracts. The remaining cofactor has its global polynomial endpoint majorant times $e^{2\pi n|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$. Shrink the common strip height so the sum of these growth costs from ALL other cofactors and ports is smaller than half the detected angular loss. The graph is fixed, so only finitely many costs occur. Finite central coefficients cause no exponential cost. At the positive endpoint their normalized central factor is a nonzero unit, so the resulting local estimate is against $P_{\mathrm{cross}}(0;L)$, with an exponential loss. This does not assert positivity off the real node set or divide by an angularly vanishing cofactor. For clarity, the relevant ordinary-face adjacency graph is connected. A simple sphere triangulation stays connected after deleting two vertices: reroute a path avoiding the first deleted vertex along its cycle of neighbors, then reroute occurrences of the second along its neighbor cycle with the first removed, a connected path. Thus the ordinary phases can all agree only up to ONE simultaneous rotation. Fix one ordinary face $f_0$ as the scale reference. Outside any fixed neighborhood of the common-phase point on the remaining $(R-1)\text{-torus}$, a bounded-length ordinary-face path contains a separated edge. One actual triangle contains its two finite endpoints, hence has (2). It follows, uniformly for small fixed complex $\boldsymbol\delta$, that the original Cauchy integrand of $C_N$ has an exponential angular gap off that neighborhood. Its positive endpoint logarithmic scale at the complete radii is $\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$. The product of finitely many polynomial losses is $e^{o(N)}$. No different face radii are optimized at separate ports, and no independent local norms replace the shared target. ## 3. Exact finite-N phase and the original coefficient saddle Fix the positive complete ordinary radii $\boldsymbol\rho$, with $\rho_{f_0}$ held fixed. For $f\ne f_0$ write $L_f=\rho_f e^{z_f}$, and retain $L_{f_0}=\rho_{f_0}$. All protected variables remain zero. On the fixed local complex chart, choose the logarithm real at $\boldsymbol\delta=0$ and positive real radii, and define $$ \Psi_N(\mathbf z,\boldsymbol\delta)=\frac1N\sum_e\operatorname{Log}\mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L(\mathbf z))-\frac dN\sum_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\operatorname{Log}L_f(\mathbf z).\qquad (3) $$ Every original scalar in $\mathcal B$, including $B_{N,M}$, beta, finite forced factors, parity shifts and the actual half-index, stays in (3). The explicit $N^{2R}$ in (1) is kept outside (3). No amplitude is fitted to an unknown source value. The local cofactor and complete-fold theorems give uniform convergence of $\Psi_N$ and its fixed derivatives on smaller charts to $$ \Psi(\mathbf z,\boldsymbol\delta)=\sum_e\bigl[Q_{b_e}(\delta_e)+Q_{c_e}(\delta_e)\bigr]-\sum_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\operatorname{Log}L_f(\mathbf z).\qquad (4) $$ Any parameter-independent $O(\log N)/N$ terms in (3) are retained; their vanishing in the limit does not license dropping them from the finite formula. At $\boldsymbol\delta=0$, the actual complete radii are stationary for (4). Its ordinary-face Hessian $H_0$ is positive definite after fixing $f_0$, by the proved complete coefficient Hessian/connectedness theorem. The uniform holomorphic IFT therefore gives, for all large $N$, a unique nearby $\mathbf z_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$, with $\partial_{\mathbf z}\Psi_N=0$, on one fixed small complex $\boldsymbol\delta$ polydisk. It converges with fixed derivatives to $\mathbf z(\boldsymbol\delta)$. Put $$ A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)=\Psi_N(\mathbf z_N(\boldsymbol\delta),\boldsymbol\delta),\qquad H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)=\partial_{\mathbf z}^2\Psi_N(\mathbf z_N(\boldsymbol\delta),\boldsymbol\delta). $$ $H_N$ is a holomorphic unit matrix there. Its square-root determinant is continued from its positive real value at $\boldsymbol\delta=0$. $A_N$ converges with fixed derivatives to the marked ordinary-face critical action $A_0$. The original Cauchy measure is exactly $(2\pi)^{-(R-1)}d\boldsymbol\theta$ after the common phase is removed. Indeed the integrand's total homogeneous numerator degree is $dR$, equal to the total target degree. The simultaneous angular variable cancels, and its integral is exactly $1$. There is no extra $N$, mark or quotient volume inserted in this step. Use (1) on a fixed neighborhood of the saddle and (2) on its complement. Within the neighborhood the integrand is $N^{2R}e^{N\Psi_N}$, with an exponentially small relative error. Its absolute-sum cost under a small fixed complex $\boldsymbol\delta$ perturbation is at most $e^{CN|\boldsymbol\delta|}$; shrink the polydisk so this cost is less than the exponential accuracy in (1). The angular complement is likewise smaller than the local critical value after this shrink, by its fixed endpoint gap and continuity. The local complex saddle follows from the ACTUAL Cauchy torus. One can deform its logarithmic coordinates to the horizontal real-angle plane through $\mathbf z_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$. Keep the finite side faces of the local deformation; they lie in the angular gap. Equivalently translate the full Cauchy torus by the small complex vector $\mathbf z_N$, then localize it; the polynomial numerator and the fixed Laurent target have no poles in the swept annular region. Uniform positivity of $\operatorname{Re}H_N$ and bounded holomorphic higher derivatives give the ordinary multidimensional Gaussian estimate $$ C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)=\frac{N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}{(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}\left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\qquad (5) $$ All finite phase scalars are in (3) and the explicit sign convention; the original geometric-period amplitude in (5) is nonzero. No arbitrary thimble coefficient has been assigned: this is the original face torus. The estimate is uniform on a fixed complex $\boldsymbol\delta$ polydisk, including all fixed derivatives on smaller polydisks. At $R=1$ the quotient has dimension zero and the determinant/measure factor is $1$. ## 4. Restore the full numerator, including its semisimple data The already proved spectral-polydisk-complement theorem gives $$ \left|(-1)^{dR}S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma(\boldsymbol\delta))-C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)\right|\leq e^{N(\Phi-\gamma)}.\qquad (6) $$ on some fixed sufficiently small polydisk, with $\gamma>0$. Both parities are included by the independently checked odd regularization majorant. This is an absolute estimate for the actual one-sided remainder. It does not approximate that remainder by arbitrary off-node data. At zero, $A_0(0)=\Phi$. Shrink the common polydisk so $\operatorname{Re}A_0(\boldsymbol\delta)>\Phi-\gamma/4$; uniform convergence gives the same comparison for $A_N$ with an additional $o(1)$. Formula (5), its nonzero Hessian and the explicitly retained polynomial factor then make (6) exponentially small RELATIVE to the displayed main term. Consequently the original full source has $$ S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma(\boldsymbol\delta))=(-1)^{dR}\frac{N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}{(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}\left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\qquad (7) $$ In particular it is nonzero on that fixed complex neighborhood for all sufficiently large $N$. Fixed spectral derivatives, including the independent repeated-node semisimple terms, are controlled by Cauchy. The expressions are even in each $\delta_e$; the same statement descends to a fixed smaller spectral polydisk around $\sigma_e=-2$. This is a fixed-root spectral theorem, not a claim about a generic-q deformation. ## 5. What this proves about the desired volume and what remains The [absolute cofactor-action theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md) identifies $A_0$, including all face momenta and marked zeros, with the UNTWISTED longitude-polarized geometric branch. To restore the actual fixed half-twist pattern, define explicitly $$ A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}=A_0+\pi i\sum_e\epsilon_e\delta_e^2,\qquad U_{\boldsymbol\epsilon,e}=\partial_{\delta_e}A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon},\qquad V_e=-4\pi i\delta_e. $$ The EXACT Gaussian of the original powers $n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e$ therefore gives $$ A_0+\pi i\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\sum_e\ell_e\delta_e =A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}-2\pi i\sum_e p_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\sum_e\ell_e\delta_e. $$ Half twists are included ONCE. Its stationary condition is the actual primitive equation $$ U_{\boldsymbol\epsilon,e}+p_eV_e=-2\pi i\ell_e. $$ At a unit-charge sufficiently long smooth filling, the peripheral boundary correction cancels the Gaussian terms exactly. Thus the critical exponential rate supplied by (7) is that filled hyperbolic volume, with the original normalization. The source face-torus coefficient in (7) is now selected and nonzero. The original spectral Gaussian period is still a separate integral and charge sum. Its global deformation, nonzero contribution of the unit charge, and suppression/cancellation of all other spectral regions and charges are not proved here. A local packet and the correct filled critical value do not by themselves establish the general Kashaev limit. The [fixed-root scope audit](fixed_root_direct_power_scope.md) confirms that the original invariant route requires its spectral Hermite data, not a separate generic-q normal estimate. The assembly retains the common-scale quotient and measure, the finite-N phase and Hessian, and counts every half twist exactly once. The saddle theorem and spectral-cycle survival require the analytical arguments above. The subsequent [localized spectral-period theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) now proves that the original unit-charge integral on a fixed real spectral cube contributes with a nonzero coefficient. Its finite local charge sector has the actual filled volume as its growth rate, for independently long fixed signed twists. The exact remaining global sum retains every unselected charge on its full original domain; the sharp local cube must not be used to split an infinite charge sum into separately convergent pieces without justification.

title: An explicit global Legendre contour and its source-preserving radial homotopy
text: # An explicit global Legendre contour and its source-preserving radial homotopy 28 October 2026. Every supplied positive complete ideal triangulation with the marked full-rank Lagrangian gluing rows has an explicit global contour on its positive angle polytope. On this contour the WHOLE imaginary action equals Rivin volume, including off-critical points. Its complex Jacobian is everywhere invertible. An explicit radial homotopy from the geometric fixed-radii chain preserves the leading period, with every boundary prism exponentially smaller. Gaussian Schur complements preserve the same positive half-plane structure. These are general contour constructions, not assumptions of noncancellation. They do not assert that the original quantum source has already been changed into this positive chart. The original figure-eight indefinite chart and the five-crossing bent-source calculation show why that last transport is substantive. No new knot invariant is defined here. ## 1. The marked positive chart and its explicit angle polytope Use the [positive quad-chart theorem](positive_quad_chart_and_actual_torus_signature.md). After its positive rotations, the marked gluing equations are A x+B y=c, B invertible, AB^t=BA^t, x_j=Log z_j, y_j=Log(1-1/z_j), Im z_j>0. Put C=B^(-1)A=C^t. At the complete meridian the retained constant c is purely imaginary. Write B^(-1)c=i kappa, with kappa real, and retain exactly the potential W(x)=sum_j Li_2(exp x_j)+(1/2)x^t(I-C)x +i(kappa-pi*1)^t x. (1) No imaginary constant is added. This is the marked potential whose complete critical value was calibrated in the quad-chart theorem. Put x=rho+i theta and gamma(theta)=kappa-C theta, beta(theta)=pi*1-theta-gamma(theta), P={theta:theta>0, beta(theta)>0, gamma(theta)>0}. (2) This is a convex bounded open polytope. It is the positive angle domain with the marked edge and meridian ANGLE equations imposed. The three angles in tetrahedron j are theta_j,beta_j, gamma_j. The supplied complete point theta_* belongs to P. Let F(rho,theta)=Im W(rho+i theta). Directly from (1), F(rho,theta)=sum_j Im Li_2(exp(rho_j+i theta_j)) -rho^t beta(theta). (3) In particular F is separable in its radial variables, even though the affine angle constraints couple its angle variables. ## 2. A unique radial minimum constructs the contour globally For every theta in P, partial_(rho_j)F=-Arg(1-exp(rho_j+i theta_j))-beta_j, partial_(rho_j)^2 F =Im[z_j/(1-z_j)]>0. (4) As rho_j tends to -infinity the first derivative tends to -beta_j<0; at +infinity it tends to gamma_j>0. Hence F has a UNIQUE global radial minimum, with the explicit solution rho_L,j(theta)=log[sin beta_j(theta)/sin gamma_j(theta)], x_L(theta)=rho_L(theta)+i theta. (5) The equality follows from the ordinary sine rule: its positive shape has argument theta and Arg(1-z)=-beta. Existence and uniqueness also follow from (4), without assuming an optimizer or a contour intersection. On every compact angle subpolytope the radial objective is uniformly coercive. On this graph the OFF-CRITICAL identity is exactly F(rho_L(theta),theta) =sum_j [Im Li_2(z_j)-rho_L,j beta_j] =sum_j D(z_j) =V(theta). (6) Here D is Bloch--Wigner and V is the ordinary sum of ideal tetrahedron volumes. Thus the original discrepancy between off-critical dilogarithm action and volume disappears on this specified nonlinear contour. This is stronger than comparing only their critical values. Rivin strict concavity makes theta_* the unique global maximum of (6). Its value is the marked hyperbolic volume. The volume extends continuously to the compact closure of P, and every other point of that closure has strictly smaller volume. In particular its boundary has a strict uniform volume gap. The noncompact radial behavior of (5) at some faces is recorded; it has not been declared harmless for an arbitrary quantum amplitude. ## 3. The contour is an algebraic phase graph on a finite cover Set p_j=exp(2i theta_j), q_j=exp(2i gamma_j). Then (5) gives the WHOLE rational identity z_j=(1-p_j q_j)/(1-q_j), q_j=exp(2i kappa_j) product_k p_k^(-C_jk). (7) On the positive real phase locus, z_j/conjugate(z_j)=p_j, z_j''/conjugate(z_j'')=q_j, z_j''=1-1/z_j. Since C is rational, one fixed finite cover of the phase torus makes all the monomials in (7) ordinary Laurent monomials. For the actual integral logarithmic gluing marks kappa/pi is also rational, so its constants are roots of unity. The contour is therefore the positive real locus of a rational algebraic graph on that marked finite cover. It is not primarily a collection of asymptotic jets. Formula (7) retains the sign and winding marks through kappa and C. The graph also glues explicitly across the POSITIVE quad atlas. The cyclic rotation x'=y, y'=-x-y+i pi permutes the angles and acts on their squared phases by the monomial map p'=q, q'=(pq)^(-1). Substituting these into (7) gives z'=(1-p'q')/(1-q') =q(1-p)/(1-pq)=1-1/z. Thus these reference contours are the same positive angle-to-shape construction in different quad coordinates, not unrelated local saddles. This is a classical algebraic atlas identity; the corresponding EXACT finite quantum quad/source transformation is not inferred from it. ## 4. A positive Hessian structure controls its Jacobian and all Schur reductions Let H=W_xx and write H=K+iD, D=diag_j Im[z_j/(1-z_j)]>0, K=I-C+diag_j Re[z_j/(1-z_j)]=K^t. (8) This holds throughout the positive product of half-planes, not just on the contour or at its maximum. The real Hessian of F in radial/angle coordinates is Hess F=[[D,K],[K,-D]]. (9) Differentiating its radial minimum gives R:=d rho_L/d theta=-D^(-1)K, Hess V=-G, G=D+K D^(-1)K>0. (10) These formulas prove strict concavity directly in the selected angle coordinates. The complex contour Jacobian is J_L=R+iI=-D^(-1)conjugate(H), H J_L=-G. (11) It is invertible EVERYWHERE on P. Indeed H has positive imaginary part, so Hu=0 would imply u^*D u=0. Thus the contour is a totally real immersion with no vanishing holomorphic volume Jacobian. Its determinant and Gaussian half-density have continuous nonzero marks on the convex P. There is no local Maslov obstruction or a zero Jacobian to be overcome by a limit. This structure survives arbitrary successive Gaussian eliminations. If a complex symmetric matrix H has Im H>0, partition it as [[E,F],[F^t,G_0]]. The principal block E is invertible and its Schur complement S=G_0-F^t E^(-1)F obeys Im S>0. (12) For a vector v put w=(-E^(-1)Fv,v). Then v^*S v=w^*H w, whose imaginary part is w^*(Im H)w>0. This proves (12) without a diagonalization or a scalar-root argument. It is the all-rank version of the positive-half-plane phenomenon checked explicitly in the five-crossing reduction. Real full-rank linear restrictions also preserve the condition, since Im(L^t H L)=L^t(Im H)L>0. Conversely a same-dimensional REAL symplectic Gaussian change cannot repair an indefinite imaginary Hessian. If H'=(E+F H)(A+B H)^(-1) is its usual fractional action, the symplectic identities give Im H'=(A+B H)^(-*) (Im H)(A+B H)^(-1). Hermitian inertia is unchanged. This distinguishes a positive chart construction from an unproved Gaussian repair of the original indefinite flow chart. Controlled elimination or a nonlinear Euler/quad transform requires its own source map. ## 5. An exact radial homotopy with automatically lower boundary prisms Put rho_*=Re x_* at the complete point. Let Q be ANY compact convex angle polytope contained in P with theta_* in its interior. Compare the two ACTUAL chains Gamma_0(theta)=rho_*+i theta, Gamma_1(theta)=rho_L(theta)+i theta, theta in Q, Gamma_s(theta)=[(1-s)rho_*+s rho_L(theta)]+i theta. (13) The fixed-radii theorem makes F(rho_*,theta) strictly concave with its unique maximum V_* at theta_*. The Legendre chain has the same property by (6). Convexity in rho gives the WHOLE homotopy inequality F(Gamma_s(theta)) <=(1-s)F(rho_*,theta)+sV(theta)<=V_*. (14) Equality is possible only at theta_*. On the ENTIRE boundary prism [0,1] times boundary(Q), compactness yields F<=V_*-delta_Q, delta_Q>0. (15) Thus this contour deformation comes with a proof of its boundary gap; a boundary estimate is not appended as an unverified condition. Its whole image is compact for fixed Q, and stays in the original positive holomorphic chamber. For any holomorphic top form omega_N on that image, Stokes gives the EXACT period difference as the oriented boundary-prism period. In particular if its actual uniform finite-level form is omega_N=N^mu exp[NW/(2pi i)] (a_0(x)+O(1/N)) dx_1...dx_t, with its original base line retained, then (15) proves that the two selected periods differ by O(N^B exp[N(V_*-delta_Q)/(2pi)]). No coefficient is set to one by normalization. If a_0(x_*) is a unit, each chain has one selected oriented saddle (multiplicity one), with its nonzero original density, contour Jacobian and Gaussian determinant retained. The numerical coefficient is their specified product, not the number one. Nonvanishing follows directly from the unique maximum, (11), and the negative real Gaussian Hessian; its power is N^(mu-t/2). It is not an assumption that an unspecified thimble intersects a quantum source. The statement is for these explicit chains and their retained prism. Applying it to an original knot state requires an exact source-preserving positive-chart realization of that state. It does not assert that realization merely from classical gluing or from a nonzero local normal density. ## 6. Every nonzero integer alias has an explicit radial escape direction For an integer vector m, the logarithmic alias is W_m(x)=W(x)+2pi i m^t x, F_m=F+2pi m^t rho. For theta in P, (4) has the global range -beta_j<partial_(rho_j)F<gamma_j, beta_j,gamma_j in (0,pi). Consequently, whenever m_j!=0, sign(m_j) partial_(rho_j)F_m >=2pi|m_j|-pi>=pi|m_j|. (16) There is NO critical point of any nonzero alias anywhere in this marked positive chamber. Moreover the explicit flow rho_j(s)=rho_j(0)-s sign(m_j), m_j!=0, rho_j(s)=rho_j(0), m_j=0 obeys the uniform whole-function inequality dF_m/ds<=-pi ||m||_1. (17) For example start at constant rho_*. After a fixed displacement S>2||rho_*||_infinity one has F_m(S,theta)<=V_* -pi(S-2||rho_*||_infinity)||m||_1. (18) Thus all translated alias BULK chains have explicit exponential loss, uniformly even in the infinitely many alias labels. Only finitely many translation directions are used, but no claim that finitely many Stokes branches exhaust the problem is made. The decay in ||m|| controls the remaining labels. The exact radial homotopy also retains its boundary face periods. Unlike (15), those alias prisms need NOT automatically be below V_*: their initial phases include 2pi m^t rho_*. They cannot be erased because their interiors have no critical point. This construction therefore reduces positive-chamber alias competition to explicit face sources; it does not prove those face sources vanish or have smaller rate in every knot. The original finite-mode or finite-height quadrature remains the way to carry those sources into a genuine comparison. ### Topology separates positive peripheral aliases from degenerate edge walls For the actual one-cusped triangulation there is a further uniform restriction. It has t edges and t tetrahedra: compactifying its torus cusp to the ideal vertex gives Euler characteristic one, so 1-#edges+2t-t=1. Choose the rows as t-1 ACTUAL independent edge rows followed by the marked meridian, as in the supplied gluing input. An integer alias changes the imaginary equations to A theta+B gamma=Im c+2pi Bm. Undoing the fixed quad rotations, its edge totals are therefore 2pi(1+k_e), with integer k_e on those t-1 rows. For strictly positive tetrahedra every edge total is positive, so k_e>=0. But the sum over ALL edge angles is exactly 2pi t, and hence the omitted edge has total 2pi(1-sum k_e). Its positivity forces sum k_e<=0. Consequently EVERY k_e is zero. Thus any strictly positive alias cell has its original edge angle equations. If m!=0, invertibility of B makes its remaining meridian-angle shift a nonzero integer multiple of 2pi. Such cells are distinct fixed-meridian-angle slices of the SAME full Rivin angle polytope. Their closures omit the unique complete maximizer. Strict concavity and compactness therefore bound their volume maxima strictly below V_*. Only finitely many integer meridian windings are feasible because that angle polytope is compact, so the gap is uniform over all feasible nonzero POSITIVE peripheral aliases. This statement is not extended to all weak nonnegative alias loci. A nonzero edge alias can survive only on a degenerate wall, with at least one edge angle zero. Since all local angles are nonnegative there, every tetrahedron incident to that edge has a zero angle and zero volume. The remaining face source is lower dimensional, but its TOTAL period or volume is not bounded by the preceding argument. Its original quantum source terms must still be retained. In particular a bound for the positive interior modes does not prove a bound for every degenerate wall. The proposed universal extension to all weak wrong-edge loci is now **FALSE**, as proved by the [certified positive-geometric counterexample](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md). Six legal positive 2-to-3 moves on the same 5_2 knot give a nine-tetrahedron positive complete triangulation. A rational weak alias angle assignment has volume 3.76403683049..., exceeding the complete hyperbolic volume 2.82812208833.... Its complete marked meridian angle is exactly zero, and its full marked defect is Bm for an explicitly retained integer m, with det B=-2. Thus this is not an artifact of dropping the peripheral equation or enlarging the integer alias lattice. Here the strictly positive wrong-edge locus is EMPTY. The weak locus is not the topological closure of a nonempty positive cell, so the preceding positive-peripheral-alias theorem is unchanged. No coefficient of the oversized weak locus in the original quantum source has been computed. The counterexample therefore refutes universal FACE VOLUME domination; it does not assert an oversized original quantum period. Source exclusion or exact Ward/sewing cancellation remains necessary wherever such a weak locus is encountered. Compact radial clipping alone does not give the false comparison between different integer-shifted potentials. An independent useful sufficient bound remains: if s_min is the minimum number of DISTINCT tetrahedra incident to an edge, every wrong-edge weak locus has volume at most (t-s_min)v_3. The [star-bound note](degenerate_alias_faces_and_repair_obstructions.md) proves this and supplies exact counterexamples to universal flat-only repair and to an automatic favorable sign of complete edge multipliers. ## 7. Tests against the actual source and the critical-path consequence The [original figure-eight counterchart](positive_quad_chart_and_actual_torus_signature.md) has an indefinite angular Hessian on a valid transverse slice. It does not satisfy (8). Choosing new radii in that original chart cannot make this theorem apply. A source-preserving change to the positive quad chart is still necessary. The [selected five-crossing proof](five_two_selected_volume_proof.md) also needed a bent outer source and bounded lower/vertical pieces. That source theorem is not a consequence of (16). It verified exactly the face and kernel terms that a critical-point-only argument would miss. The new general advance is the explicit algebraic Legendre chain (5)--(7), its nonvanishing Jacobian and Schur-closed positive Hessian, and the radial homotopy (13)--(15) with a proved boundary gap. The target contour on every supplied positive triangulation is no longer guessed. What remains for a broad original-knot theorem is its exact quantum source transport, with the alias face periods in Section 6 retained. No broad volume conjecture is claimed proved by this lemma. There is a simple exact check on the word "automatic" in the boundary claim. In the scalar positive potential C=0, kappa=2pi/3, the angle interval is 0<theta<pi/3, gamma=2pi/3, beta=pi/3-theta. Its positive critical point is theta_*=pi/6, rho_*=-log(3)/2 and V_*=2v_3/3. But at the arbitrary initial radius rho_0=0, the angle endpoint theta=pi/3 has F(0,pi/3)=Im Li_2(exp(pi i/3))=v_3>V_*. The equalities follow from the ordinary Lobachevsky duplication identity. Thus radial boundary prisms from an arbitrary starting source radius need not be lower, even though the whole positive volume problem is strictly concave. This is a test of the analytic positive Lagrangian data, not a claim that this one-tetrahedron data is an actual knot triangulation or a substituted quantum invariant. It proves why (13) specifies rho_* and why the missing original-source transport cannot be supplied by concavity alone. The underlying angle-volume and Legendre viewpoints have the coverage already recorded in [the Rivin/flow note](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md). No novelty is claimed for Legendre duality or for the positive symplectic Hessian. The explicit whole off-critical chain, its boundary-prism inequality, algebraic phase graph and alias escape are proved here from the displayed formulas, without adopting a published quantum-cycle comparison. [All-rank identity and scope audit](../experiments/audit_general_legendre_rivin_contour.py) and [saved results](../experiments/general_legendre_rivin_contour_results.json).

title: Independent long twists: monotonicity of the local charge critical value
status: Local critical-value monotonicity for independent signed slopes
text: # Independent long twists: monotonicity of the local charge critical value The [whole-source local packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. The [localized original spectral period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) now supplies the separate contour and nonvanishing proof. Combining it with the comparison below proves dominance within a finite local charge sector. The complete global remainder remains open. 31 October 2026. . This is a local analytic statement about the actual normalized source action. It compares critical VALUES; it does not prove intersection with an original integration cycle, a nonzero amplitude, or control of remote charges. ## 1. The actual even action and a general analytic lemma Let $A_0(\boldsymbol\delta)$ be the original face-stationary complete CROSS action without the retained quadratic half-twist phase. The two original marked faces remain zero. The cofactor action identity gives each triangle as a holomorphic function of $w_i=-4\sin^2(\pi\delta_i)$. The unique ordinary-face IFT branch is therefore unchanged under reversal of ANY individual $\delta_i$. Consequently $A_0$ is even in EACH coordinate. Its coefficients are real, because the selected face/action germs are real on the real locus. The actual complete normalization and local curvature give $$ A_0(0)=\Phi_D,\qquad \operatorname{Hess}A_0(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_1,\ldots,C_R),\qquad C_i>0. $$ Spectral-independent source phases remain outside this normalized action. They do not change any derivative below. More generally assume exactly these analytic hypotheses. There are holomorphic functions $B_i$ of $\mathbf z=(\delta_1^2,\ldots,\delta_R^2)$, with real coefficients, such that $$ \partial_i A_0(\boldsymbol\delta)=-2\delta_i B_i(\boldsymbol\delta^2),\qquad B_i(0)=C_i.\qquad (1) $$ This follows coefficient by coefficient from separate evenness; the quotient at $\delta_i=0$ is removable. In particular $B_i$ is NOT inferred from only the diagonal Hessian without that evenness hypothesis. For independent nonzero REAL slopes $n_i$ and real charges $\ell_i$ define $$ \Phi(\boldsymbol\delta;\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell)=A_0(\boldsymbol\delta)+\pi i\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i. $$ In the actual source $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$ are the fixed signed integer crossing powers, and the surviving $\ell_i$ are integer charges. The analytic statement first allows real charges in order to differentiate. ## 2. Uniform existence and uniqueness in the scaled box There are $a>0$ and $n_0>0$, depending only on the fixed analytic germ, such that if all $|n_i|\geq n_0$ and $|\ell_i/n_i|\leq a$, $\Phi$ has a unique critical point in the fixed polydisc $\|\boldsymbol\delta\|_\infty\leq2a$. It depends holomorphically on $$ t_i=\frac{\ell_i}{n_i},\qquad e_i=\frac1{n_i}, $$ in corresponding complex neighborhoods. No ratio between different $|n_i|$ is required. Its Hessian is nondegenerate. Indeed the critical equations are exactly $$ \delta_i\left[1+\frac{i e_i B_i(\boldsymbol\delta^2)}{\pi}\right]+t_i=0,\qquad \delta_i=-\frac{t_i}{1+i e_i B_i(\boldsymbol\delta^2)/\pi}.\qquad (2) $$ Choose a small polydisc $\|\boldsymbol\delta\|_\infty\leq2a$ on which $|B_i-C_i|\leq C_i/8$. Let $M$ bound all $|B_i|$ and $L$ bound the sum of the absolute values of the $\boldsymbol\delta$-derivatives of every $B_i(\boldsymbol\delta^2)$. Choose $e_0>0$ such that $$ \frac{e_0M}{\pi}\leq\frac18,\qquad \frac{64}{49}\frac{a e_0L}{\pi}\leq\frac12. $$ The right side of (2) maps $\|\boldsymbol\delta\|_\infty\leq2a$ into $\|\boldsymbol\delta\|_\infty\leq8a/7$ and has sup-norm derivative at most $1/2$, uniformly for $|t_i|\leq a$, $|e_i|\leq e_0$. Uniform contraction proves existence and uniqueness; uniform iteration, or the analytic IFT, proves holomorphy on a slightly larger box after shrinking the displayed one if needed. Take $n_0\geq1/e_0$. Every critical point in the specified $\boldsymbol\delta$ polydisc satisfies this fixed-point equation, so the uniqueness is genuine there, not merely uniqueness within a chosen numerical iteration. The derivative of the left side of (2) is invertible, since it equals an invertible diagonal matrix times $I$ minus the contraction derivative. The original Hessian is this Jacobian multiplied on the left by $2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(n_i)$, hence is nondegenerate. Its conditioning in unscaled coordinates may depend on the slopes; no uniform unscaled condition number is asserted. ## 3. Exact derivative and relative control for disparate slopes Let $S(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell)=\Phi(\boldsymbol\delta(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell);\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell)$ be the selected critical value. For real $n_i$,$\ell_i$, envelope differentiation gives $$ \partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S=-2\pi\operatorname{Im}\delta_i. $$ Taking the imaginary part of (2), with the FULL generally complex $B_i$ evaluated at this coupled saddle, gives the exact formula $$ \begin{aligned}\operatorname{Im}\delta_i&=\frac{\ell_i}{n_i^2}\frac{\operatorname{Re}B_i/\pi}{|1+iB_i/(\pi n_i)|^2},\\ \partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S&=-2\frac{\ell_i}{n_i^2}\frac{\operatorname{Re}B_i}{|1+iB_i/(\pi n_i)|^2}.\end{aligned}\qquad (3) $$ In particular all cross-coordinate effects remain inside a MULTIPLICATIVE positive factor. They do not produce an additive error which could dominate $\ell_i/n_i^2$ when that individual slope is very large. The bounds selected above imply, for $\ell_i\geq0$, $$ -4C_i\frac{\ell_i}{n_i^2}\leq\partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S\leq-C_i\frac{\ell_i}{n_i^2}.\qquad (4) $$ For example $\operatorname{Re}B_i/C_i$ lies in $[7/8,9/8]$, while the denominator in (3) lies in $[49/64,81/64]$. Their ratio lies strictly between $1/2$ and $2$, which proves (4). Hence every derivative is STRICTLY negative when $\ell_i>0$, regardless of the independent signs and magnitudes of $n_i$. There is also the uniform sharper asymptotic, with $n_{\min}=\min_i|n_i|$, $$ \partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S=-2C_i\frac{\ell_i}{n_i^2}\left[1+O\!\left(a^2+n_{\min}^{-2}\right)\right].\qquad (5) $$ To verify it rather than hide a phase error, (2) first gives $\delta_i=-t_i[1+O(e_0)]$, with the bound proportional to $|t_i|$. Thus $\delta_i^2-t_i^2=O(e_0|t_i|^2)$. Since $B_i$ has real coefficients, $B_i(t_1^2,\ldots,t_R^2)$ is real, and the bounded $\mathbf z$-derivatives give $\operatorname{Im}B_i(\boldsymbol\delta^2)=O(e_0a^2)$. Therefore $$ \left|1+\frac{i e_iB_i}{\pi}\right|^2=1-\frac{2e_i\operatorname{Im}B_i}{\pi}+\frac{e_i^2|B_i|^2}{\pi^2}=1+O(e_0^2), $$ while $\operatorname{Re}B_i=C_i+O(a^2)$. Use $e_0=1/n_{\min}$ in these estimates (the existence threshold remains its previously fixed upper bound). All constants depend only on the fixed germ and chosen coordinate neighborhood, not on relative slope sizes or charge ratios. The exact formula (3) also covers $\ell_i=0$ by continuity. ## 4. Unit charge is the unique largest LOCAL positive-integer value Increase $n_0$ if necessary so $a|n_i|\geq1$. In the local positive integer box $$ 1\leq\ell_i\leq a|n_i|, $$ the all-unit vector is the unique maximizer of $\operatorname{Re}S$. More precisely, integrate (4) along successive coordinate segments from $1$ to $\ell_i$; every intermediate vector remains in the same scaled box. Then $$ \sum_i\frac{C_i}{2n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1)\leq\operatorname{Re}S(\mathbf n,\mathbf1)-\operatorname{Re}S(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell)\leq\sum_i\frac{2C_i}{n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1).\qquad (6) $$ For positive REAL charges there is strict coordinate monotonicity, not a claim that charge $1$ maximizes the interval $(0,1)$. Separate evenness and uniqueness also imply that reversing any individual $\ell_i$ reverses that $\delta_i$ alone and leaves $S$ unchanged. This is a symmetry of critical values; signs of amplitudes and cycle multiplicities require their actual source identities. For the original half-twist convention, define explicitly $$ A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}=A_0+\pi i\sum_i\epsilon_i\delta_i^2,\qquad U_i=\partial_i A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon},\qquad V_i=-4\pi i\delta_i,\qquad n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i. $$ The half-twist phase is therefore included exactly once. At the selected saddle these actual primitive logs satisfy $U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\ell_i$. The already proved Gaussian boundary-term cancellation identifies $2\pi\operatorname{Re}S$ with its representation volume. For unit charges and sufficiently long fixed twists, the existing marked filling theorem identifies this with the actual smooth filling. The monotonicity proved here compares LOCAL critical values within the specified box only. It neither bounds charges outside that box nor proves any critical point contributes to the original Gaussian period. Charge $0$ remains exactly absent from the original total-derivative source formula despite the existence of the formal local saddle there. In the intended asymptotic application the signed twists are fixed before $N$ grows; no joint growing-twist/level limit follows from this comparison of the limiting critical action.

title: A local curvature certificate for every signed color subset
text: # A local curvature certificate for every signed color subset 30 October 2026. At any fixed bridge width, a local algebraic test on one actual marked circle packing supplies ALL the shared-radius certificates for a joint signed/unsigned color corridor. If each varied port's nonzero curvatures differ by at most a factor3/2, its gap exceeds1/16. The test has O(R) inequalities; it does not require enumerating the reflected color subsets. This is a sufficient condition on the original labeled right-angled certificate. It is not asserted for arbitrary essential diagrams or claimed to be realized at every bridge number. No far-color, quantum normal or filled-knot conclusion follows. ## 1. The actual diagram and algebraic test Fix a connected original flat plat with its labeled simplicial white triangulation and original marked MAIN edge uv. Let E be any set of varied crossing-circle ports, with arbitrary retained half twists. All other ports stay complete with their actual signs. Use the actual shared marked packing of the [complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md): L_u=L_v=0, and every other curvature L_f is positive. F and G below are the source-normalized triangle and crossing-magnitude potentials in [the homogeneous theorem](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), section5. Let g*=4Lambda(pi/4)/pi=v_oct/(2pi). At each varied original port e, ignore only the actual marked zeros and require its NONZERO curvatures x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e to lie in some interval[t_e,rho t_e], with rho<exp(g*). The t_e may differ: these intervals only describe the SAME original packing, not separately chosen local frames or radii. ## 2. Every local gap has an explicit lower bound Then for every varied port g_e=F(x_e,b_e,y_e)+F(x_e,c_e,y_e)-G(b_e,x_e,y_e,c_e) >=g*−log rho>0. (1) Proof. The actual simplicial white dictionary makes x,b,c,y distinct. At most the two marked faces are zero. They cannot be the two outers: the outer edge xy is MATCHING, whereas the marked edge uv is MAIN. Hence each of the two triangles has at least one nonzero vertex and at least one has two. Scale the nonzero quartet by t_e; g is unchanged under this common scale. By monotonicity, bound each F from below by its equal-nonzero-weight value and G from above by its equal-nonzero-weight value plus log rho. The only constants needed are F(1,0,0)=0, F(1,1,0)=g*, G(1,1,0,0)=0, G(1,1,1,1)=g*. The first triangle is flat. The second has center angles (pi/2,pi/2,0), so the proved source potential gives4Lambda(pi/4)/pi; its permutations have the same value. With two nonzero equal weights, the G entropy is identically zero by Lambda(pi-a)=-Lambda(a). With four equal weights, strict concavity gives the uniform four-angle maximum and the displayed value g*. If the quartet has two nonzero faces, at least one triangle supplies g* and the other supplies at least0, while its G value is0. If it has three or four nonzero faces, BOTH triangles supply at least g*, while G is at most g* by monotonicity. This proves(1), including all actual paired zero patterns such as202/202. No presumed exclusion of those pairs is used. An entirely elementary fixed choice is rho=3/2. The Fourier series for Lambda gives g*=2Catalan/pi. The alternating series for Catalan gives Catalan>1−1/9=8/9. Also pi<22/7 follows from the positive integral integral_0^1 x^4(1-x)^4/(1+x^2) dx=22/7-pi>0, and log(3/2)<1/2 follows by integrating1/t<1 on(1,3/2). Therefore g*−log(3/2)>56/99−1/2=13/198>1/16. (2) Thus local contrast≤3/2 gives the same explicit margin1/16 at every varied port, regardless of width or number of boxes. It is the finite algebraic test 2L_f<=3L_g for each ordered pair of nonzero face weights in that port, at most12 comparisons per port. No transcendental capacity optimization or enumeration of reflected subsets is required. ## 3. One shared radius vector certifies every subset For the all-subset certificate, choose eta=g*−log rho. At the original marked packing C_empty=Phi_D. Replace both marked zero face weights by one sufficiently small FIXED positive value, retaining every ordinary weight. The source-normalized F,G are continuous on the actual nonzero boundary quartets. No continuity of I is used: I=-infinity when b=c=0, and I<=G is applied only after positive regularization. Since D is fixed, choose the regularization so that simultaneously C_empty−Phi_D<eta/4, and every g_e>eta/2. For EVERY nonempty subset S of varied ports, with its retained signs, C_S<=C_empty−sum_(e in S)g_e <Phi_D+eta/4−|S|eta/2<=Phi_D−eta/4, (3) using I<=G for unsigned replacements. A single shared radius vector therefore supplies all of the homogeneous theorem's certificates. No subset enumeration or smoothing-connectivity assumption is needed. At these fixed radii all operator constants C_b are finite. Choose a single delta(D)>0 so their total small-color exponential-rate cost on h_e<=delta N is less than eta/8, then shrink inside the established core neighborhood. Precisely, [the homogeneous theorem](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), section6, now gives constants c,delta>0 such that the original mixed source and its exact complete-image core satisfy A_N(N-h_E,N_else)/F_N^E(h)=1+O(exp(-cN)) uniformly for physical integers0<=h_e<=delta N, at both parities. For h_N/N tending to a real chi in this cube, the [actual geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md), section4, gives lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|A_N(N-h_(N,E),N_else)|=Vol(rho_chi). The other external colors remain N with their original signs. The right side is the volume of the actual nearby marked representation, not an asserted complete metric on a filled knot. There is no far-color or filled-knot conclusion. The algebraic test concerns local ratios in the original common packing; it does not impose a diagram-independent global curvature bound. Existence of this or a weaker shared-radius certificate for the full intended class remains open. This corollary does not solve the entropy redistribution problem when a mixed maximum has a middle load greater than1/2. ## 4. Verification scope The proof uses the existing exact homogeneous source and core theorems; it introduces no new quantum approximation. [The focused check](../experiments/audit_general_local_curvature_source_corridor.py) enumerates the ten possible zero-position patterns allowed by the local distinct-face/marked-edge conditions, verifies the elementary constant calculation, and bounds all corresponding equal-weight gaps with outward-rounded Arb arithmetic and analytic Fourier tails. These checks concern the local inequality; they do not construct a new family of diagram realizations. The sufficient certificate gives the stated corridor consequence. It does not prove realizability at every width or a far-color/filling theorem.

title: The original localized spectral period has a nonzero unit-charge filling contribution
status: Localized original contribution; input to whole-period theorem
text: # The original localized spectral period has a nonzero unit-charge filling contribution analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This proves a relative asymptotic on an **actual fixed real spectral cube**, with its original Fourier charges, sine factors, parity and marked coefficient. It does not estimate the integral outside that cube or the remote charge sum. The inputs are the [full spectral numerator packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md), the [local charge comparison](general_local_charge_critical_monotonicity.md), and the exact period (13a) in the [cross-cofactor source interface](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md). The finite-root spectral identity is also recorded in the [spectral total-derivative theorem](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md). ## 1. Exact original normalization and the local quantity Fix the original certified marked flat plat with $R$ ports. Put $d=N-1$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, and let $n_i$ be its actual nonzero integer crossing powers. In the long-twist convention $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. Define the ENTIRE original shared spectral numerator $$ S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)=\left[\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d\right] \left.\prod_i H_{V_N(\sigma_i)}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0}. $$ The original fixed-root Fourier/Hermite period is exactly $$ \begin{aligned} I_{D,\mathbf n} ={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-i)^R \sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \left(\prod_i\ell_i\right)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_i\ell_i}\\ &\quad\times\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \left[\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right] S_N\!\left(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)\right) \exp\!\left\{N\sum_i\left[\pi i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\ell_i\delta_i\right]\right\} \,d\boldsymbol\delta . \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Here $I_{D,\mathbf n}$ is the RAW original marked contraction. If the final $K_N$ convention is $K_N=\chi_{D,N}I_{D,\mathbf n}$, its already recorded external character multiplies every localized formula below as well. The [complete-pointing normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), especially sections 1 and 3, retains the reduced framing character (modulus one) and the enhanced component sign; a full one-cut modified ADO convention has the additional $i^{N+3}/N$ factor. None is silently absorbed into our raw amplitude. The actual final-diagram framing/component character must be used, rather than the augmented diagram's component count. Any such separately recorded scalar is still outside (1). In particular (1) has no additional $N^R$, mark, spectral square-root Jacobian or division by a quantum dimension. The displayed $q$ power is the literal unwrapped scalar $\exp[\pi i d^2(\sum_i n_i)/(4N)]$. Charge zero is absent by the exact total-derivative identity, not discarded by an asymptotic argument. The full finite-$N$ charge series in (1) is absolutely convergent; no uniform-in-$N$ summability is used below. Choose $b>0$ within the fixed complex neighborhood of the full packet. For a charge $\boldsymbol\ell$ let $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ be the integral in (1) restricted to the CLOSED real cube $K_b=[-b,b]^R$. All local charge contributions below include the factors preceding that integral in (1). This is a sharp restriction of the original real contour, with its actual boundary. There is no analytic compactly supported cutoff and no assigned Lefschetz-cycle coefficient. Only FINITELY many restricted charge terms are ever summed here. A sharp cube has boundary jumps and its individual $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ do not inherit the absolute charge summability of the original full-domain integral. The proved full packet is $$ S_N\!\left(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)\right) =\frac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} \left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\tag{2} $$ It is uniform and holomorphic on a fixed complex polydisc. Every finite scalar and logarithmic normalization stays in $A_N$; the explicit $N^{2R}$ alone is taken out. $H_N$ is the ordinary-face Hessian after fixing ONE common face scale. Its determinant root is continued from its positive value at $\boldsymbol\delta=0$. The dimension of that face quotient is $R-1$. The packet restores the full $V$ numerator, including its semisimple spectral data, by the proved noncross exponential gap. The finite interpolant used to define $A_N$ is real on the real local chart and even in each $\delta_i$. Uniqueness of the face IFT preserves both properties. On smaller fixed polydiscs, with all fixed derivatives, $$ A_N\longrightarrow A_0,\qquad A_0(0)=\Phi_D,\qquad A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_1,\ldots,C_R),\qquad C_i>0.\tag{3} $$ These are finite-source properties, not a choice of a phase fitted to the answer. In particular $$ \partial_i A_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =-2\delta_i B_{i,N}(\delta_1^2,\ldots,\delta_R^2),\qquad B_{i,N}\longrightarrow B_i,\qquad B_i(0)=C_i.\tag{4} $$ The quotients at $\delta_i=0$ are removable. After shrinking the chart, $|B_{i,N}-C_i|\leq C_i/8$ for all large N. In particular $\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}>C_i/2$, and the real symmetric matrix $\operatorname{Re}A_N''(z)$ is negative definite uniformly for ALL complex z in that chart and all large N. ## 2. Finite-N filling saddles for independent signed twists There are fixed $b,a,n_0>0$, with a much smaller than b, such that the following holds for every fixed integer vector $\mathbf n$ with $|n_i|\geq n_0$. There is no condition on ratios $|n_i|/|n_j|$. For positive real charges satisfying $\ell_i/|n_i|\leq a$ define $$ \Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta) =A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)+\pi i\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i.\tag{5} $$ It has a unique critical point $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ in the chosen small polydisc. Indeed, writing $t_i=\ell_i/n_i$, its equations are precisely $$ \delta_i=-\frac{t_i}{1+i B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)/(\pi n_i)}.\tag{6} $$ Uniform contraction proves existence, uniqueness and holomorphic parameter dependence, exactly as in the limiting charge lemma. Bounds on $B_{i,N}$ and their derivatives are uniform in N. Consequently $$ |\delta_i|\leq 2|t_i|,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\delta_i =\frac{\ell_i}{\pi n_i^2} \frac{\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)} {\left|1+i B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)/(\pi n_i)\right|^2}>0.\tag{7} $$ In particular $\operatorname{Im}\delta_i\leq C\ell_i/n_i^2$. This sign holds for BOTH signs of $n_i$. All coordinates of the saddle are nonzero when all $\ell_i>0$. Write $\boldsymbol\delta_*=x_*+iy_*$, with $y_*>0$ componentwise, and put $$ S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}=\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta_*),\qquad Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}=-\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}''(\boldsymbol\delta_*). $$ Since the Gaussian contributes a purely imaginary diagonal Hessian, $\operatorname{Re}Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ is positive definite. No real or complex eigenvalue of Q vanishes. The spectral determinant root used below is the unique Gaussian branch on the convex cone of complex symmetric matrices with positive real part, positive at a positive real matrix. Thus $$ \int_{\mathbb R^R}e^{-\frac12 t^TQt}\,dt =\frac{(2\pi)^{R/2}}{\sqrt{\det Q}}.\tag{8} $$ This fixes its phase even when the different $n_i$ have different signs. For fixed $\mathbf n$ and $\boldsymbol\ell$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ and $S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ converge to the corresponding limiting critical point and value. No convergence rate is needed and $A_N$ is NOT replaced by $A_0$ in a relative formula. ## 3. Deformation of the actual restricted real contour We prove the requisite contour coefficient, rather than postulate it. Translate $K_b$ coordinate by coordinate to $K_b+i y_*$. Cauchy's theorem on each rectangle gives equality with the translated integral plus its oriented side integrals. The exact integrand is entire in $\boldsymbol\delta$; the packet is only used to estimate it inside the common local chart. The side integrals are retained in this equality. Here is a uniform exponential bound for every side. Its points have $z=x+iv$ with x in $K_b$, at least one $|x_j|=b$, and $0\leq v_i\leq y_{*,i}$. Separate reality and the real Hessian bound give $$ \operatorname{Re}A_N(x+iv)\leq A_N(0)-c|x|^2+C|v|^2.\tag{9} $$ To see the quadratic, rather than linear, error in v, Taylor-expand at the REAL point x: the first term $i\nabla A_N(x)\cdot v$ is imaginary. The remaining derivatives are uniformly bounded. The real Gaussian and charge contribution is $$ -2\pi\sum_i n_i x_i v_i-2\pi\sum_i\ell_i v_i \leq Cb\sum_i\frac{\ell_i}{|n_i|}.\tag{10} $$ The second term is nonpositive. Equation (7) bounds the first term, without using a common sign or a bound on slope ratios. Thus every side has real phase at most $$ A_N(0)-cb^2+C|y_*|^2+Cb\sum_i|t_i|.\tag{11} $$ The critical value satisfies the complementary estimate $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq A_N(0)-C\sum_i|t_i|^2.\tag{12} $$ For completeness, $A_N(\boldsymbol\delta_*)-A_N(0)=O(\sum_i|t_i|^2)$. The critical equations imply $|n_i x_{*,i}+\ell_i|\leq C|\delta_{*,i}|$; hence the real quadratic-plus-linear phase $-2\pi\sum_i(n_i x_{*,i}+\ell_i)y_{*,i}$ has the same bound (and in fact a smaller additional factor $n_{\min}^{-1}$). This proves (12) without bounding the large purely imaginary quantity $n_i\delta_i^2$ by its absolute value. First fix b within the source chart, then choose a/b sufficiently small and $n_0$ sufficiently large. Equations (11)-(12) give a fixed $\kappa_b>0$ such that ALL sides satisfy $$ \operatorname{Re}\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(z) \leq\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}-\kappa_b.\tag{13} $$ All polynomial prefactors in (2), bounded sine factors and finite side volumes preserve this exponential loss. Thus the actual local real contour has coefficient +1 on its translated horizontal saddle plane, with only exponentially small side currents. On that plane $\Phi'$ vanishes at $x_*+iy_*$, and for every real x in $K_b$ $$ \operatorname{Re}\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(x+iy_*) \leq\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}-c|x-x_*|^2.\tag{14} $$ Indeed the real part of its real-coordinate Hessian is $\operatorname{Re}A_N''$, which is uniformly negative definite along the entire segment. The critical point stays a fixed distance from the cube boundary because $|x_*|\leq2a$ much less than b. This proves the requisite local and nonlocal estimates on the translated restricted contour. It does not say anything about the original contour outside $K_b$. ## 4. Relative asymptotic and its nonzero coefficient Define $$ a_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)}{\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}. $$ The holomorphic Gaussian estimate on (14), using (8), yields $$ J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} =(-1)^{dR}\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2} \frac{a_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell})}{\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}}} e^{N S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}} \left[1+O_{\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell}(N^{-1})\right].\tag{15} $$ The error in the full packet is holomorphic and uniformly $O(N^{-1})$; Cauchy bounds, or direct Gaussian integration of that error, preserve (15). The ordinary Taylor Gaussian error is $O(N^{-1})$, since its odd first correction integrates to zero; replacing the cube by the full real Gaussian changes the answer exponentially. The exact side integrals in (13) are likewise exponentially small relative to (15). Constants may depend on the FIXED slopes and charges. No joint large-twist/large-level error estimate is asserted. The power and constant follow directly from the TWO actual integrals: $$ N^{2R}(2\pi N)^{-(R-1)/2}(2\pi/N)^{R/2} =\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}.\tag{16} $$ There is no undetermined stationary multiplier. Every sine in (15) is nonzero: $\delta_{*,i}$ is nonzero by (6) and lies in a small disk with no other zero of $\sin(2\pi\delta_i)$. Both determinant roots are units. For each fixed $\mathbf n$ and $\boldsymbol\ell$ the coefficient in (15) converges to a nonzero number. Therefore the local integral is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. Let $U_{N,\mathbf n;b}$ denote the sum of the original contributions in (1) with $\ell_i\in\{+1,-1\}$, each restricted to $K_b$. Reflection of one coordinate $\delta_i\mapsto-\delta_i$ changes $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ by a minus sign and also changes $\prod_i\ell_i$ by a minus sign. $S_N$ and the quadratic phase are separately even, and the parity character is unchanged. Thus all $2^R$ sign choices contribute EXACTLY equally. With $S_{N,\mathbf1}$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1}$, $Q_{N,\mathbf1}$ defined above, $$ \begin{aligned} U_{N,\mathbf n;b} ={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\\ &\quad\times\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_{N,\mathbf1,i})} {\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1})}\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\mathbf1}}} e^{N S_{N,\mathbf1}}\left[1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{17} $$ The parity cancellation is literal: $$ (-1)^{(N+1)R}(-1)^{dR}=(-1)^{2NR}=1. $$ Equation (17) holds through BOTH level parities and arbitrary independent signs of the sufficiently long fixed $n_i$. The remaining $q$ scalar has modulus one and is kept exactly. This proves a nonzero contributing localized original unit-charge period, not merely the existence of the corresponding critical point. ## 5. Optional enlargement to the finite LOCAL charge sector For fixed $\mathbf n$ let $L_i=\lfloor a|n_i|\rfloor$, with $n_0$ enlarged so $L_i\geq1$. Restrict (1) to $K_b$ and to $0<|\ell_i|\leq L_i$. This is a finite set after the twists are fixed. The exact finite version of the monotonicity calculation applies to $A_N$, because (4) and $\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}>0$ hold: $$ \partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} =-\frac{2\ell_i}{n_i^2} \frac{\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}} {\left|1+iB_{i,N}/(\pi n_i)\right|^2}. $$ After the same fixed shrink, for every positive charge in this box, $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}-\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq\sum_i\frac{C_i}{2n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1).\tag{18} $$ The harmless constants can be decreased if needed to make this inequality uniform in all large N. If any nonunit positive charge exists, the right side has a strictly positive minimum $\eta_{\mathbf n}$ over that FINITE set. Formula (15), the exact charge factors $\prod_i\ell_i$, and the independent sign symmetry imply that the entire restricted local charge sector equals (17) with an additional relative $O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-\eta_{\mathbf n}N})$ error (or after a smaller $\eta_{\mathbf n}$). If all $L_i=1$, there are no extra local charges. There is no comparison of an infinite charge sum and no assertion about charges near an alias. ## 6. Geometric value and exact remaining limitation The limiting action in (5) is $$ \begin{aligned} A_0+\pi i\sum_i(\epsilon_i-2p_i)\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i &=A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}-2\pi i\sum_i p_i\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i,\\ A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}&=A_0+\pi i\sum_i\epsilon_i\delta_i^2. \end{aligned} $$ Thus the half twists occur ONCE. The [marked action and collar identity](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md) gives the actual primitive saddle equation $$ U_{\boldsymbol\epsilon,i}+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\ell_i. $$ Here $S_{0,\mathbf1}$ denotes the limiting critical value. At the all-unit long-filling branch, its Gaussian peripheral correction cancels exactly and $2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{0,\mathbf1}$ is the actual smooth filling volume. Consequently the localized quantity (17), and the finite local charge sector in Section 5, have that volume as their normalized logarithmic modulus limit. The original exterior unit framing phase does not change this conclusion. This is NOT yet the original invariant's volume limit. For the FINITE selected charge set $\mathcal L$ (the sign-unit set or the finite box of section 5), define the exact remainder as the original full period (1) MINUS that finite localized sector. It is the sum of: - the finitely many $\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathcal L$, each integrated over the original full cube minus $K_b$, with its original charge factor; and - ALL $\boldsymbol\ell\notin\mathcal L$, each kept on its WHOLE original domain $[-1/2,1/2]^R$, with the original absolutely convergent summation. Do not separately sum the remote inside-$K_b$ and outside-$K_b$ pieces. The sharp boundaries would generally destroy their separate charge summability; such a split would require a specified shared regularization and its boundary cancellation. The endpoint currents are already encoded in the exact identity (1), not additional terms to append to that identity. No endpoint cancellation was discarded in deriving the finite localized formula. This exact remainder still requires a phase-preserving global estimate excluding cancellation of the nonzero contribution (17). Generic-$q$ normal derivatives are not an additional requirement for this fixed-root route; the exact marked source and all $\sigma$-Hermite data are already retained in (1)-(2). ## Validation and scope The result proves a localized contribution and its finite local charge sector; it does not prove a bound for the remaining original period or the general filled-knot volume conjecture.

title: Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude
text: # Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude 30 October 2026. The general original-source filling theorem does not need its leading analytic amplitude to be a unit at the complete point. A NONZERO amplitude germ is sufficient away from its pulled-back analytic zero set. That exceptional set occupies density zero among large signed integer slope boxes. Suitable rational rays avoid it eventually; a coordinate monomial times a unit avoids it at EVERY independently sufficiently long slope tuple. This removes one source hypothesis. It does not construct the required whole-source gap or complex packet for an arbitrary plat, and it does not prove that an unknown original source has a nonzero amplitude germ. The source, its full normal terms and all peripheral factors remain the ones in the [general transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). ## 1. The precise weaker packet hypothesis Fix a diagram and a chosen nonempty set of b filled circle ports. Keep the exact all-input full-twist identity, known nonzero outer factor chi_N, entire physical color-complement gap, and exponentially accurate finite corridor interpolation of the general transfer theorem. The finite packet C_N is holomorphic and even separately in all b coordinates on the SAME fixed complex neighborhood required there. Replace only its relative unit-amplitude assumption by C_N(x)=N^mu exp[N phi(x)] [a(x)+r_N(x)], sup |r_N| <= C/N, (1) uniformly holomorphically on that neighborhood. Here a is a nonzero holomorphic GERM, allowed to satisfy a(0)=0; phi is separately even, phi(0)=F0 real, phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (2) The explicit original unit phase eta_N stays outside C_N, as before. An absolute holomorphic remainder in (1) is essential. A pointwise estimate on physical colors, or an estimate obtained by division by an amplitude that vanishes, does not supply this hypothesis. Separate evenness of a follows even if not assumed: the holomorphic functions N^(-mu) exp[-N phi] C_N are separately even and converge uniformly to a. The same is then true of r_N. Their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on smaller domains by Cauchy's formula. The upper Gaussian corridor estimate uses boundedness of a+r_N, not a lower bound for a, so it remains valid. If some auxiliary cusps are UNFILLED, first set their color variables to zero in the actual packet and action. The amplitude required here is the resulting restricted germ a_I(x_I)=a(x_I,0). A nonzero full germ need not have a nonzero restriction: a(x_1,x_2)=x_2^2 vanishes identically when only port 1 is filled. Such a restriction needs its own first nonzero asymptotic coefficient; it is not covered by (1). ## 2. The actual filling map and its source divisor Put epsilon_i=1/p_i for the fixed nonzero integer slopes. The minimal charge source saddle xi(epsilon) solves phi_i(xi)+pi i epsilon_i(xi_i-1)=0, 1<=i<=b. (3) The analytic implicit-function theorem gives a unique small solution, xi(0)=0, and DIRECT differentiation gives D xi(0)=diag(1/(2 tau_1),...,1/(2 tau_b)). (4) In particular xi is a local biholomorphism. The factor 2 in (4) comes from the original full-twist convention and must be retained. There is a stronger coordinatewise statement. Separate evenness writes phi_i(x)=x_i psi_i(x), where psi_i is analytic and psi_i(0)=2pi i tau_i. Equation (3) becomes xi_i=epsilon_i u_i(epsilon), u_i(epsilon)=pi i/[psi_i(xi(epsilon))+pi i epsilon_i], u_i(0)=1/(2 tau_i). (5) Every u_i is a unit on a sufficiently small common polydisk. Thus xi_i is nonzero whenever epsilon_i is nonzero, independently of the relative sizes and signs of the other coordinates. Define the pulled-back source germ f(epsilon)=a(xi(epsilon)), Z={epsilon: f(epsilon)=0}. (6) It is nonzero because xi is locally invertible. Therefore Z is a proper complex analytic zero set, with its multiplicities supplied by f. Multiplying a by a nowhere-zero analytic change of source trivialization leaves Z unchanged. This is the source divisor used here; it is not inferred from the classical A-polynomial. The map (3) involves the marked analytic action and logarithmic coordinates. Even if the exponentiated shape branch is algebraic, Z is NOT asserted to be Zariski closed in epsilon or in the slopes. ## 3. Full-source transfer off the divisor For every independently sufficiently long fixed signed tuple p with f(1/p)!=0, the full original invariant has the SAME action and N-power as the general transfer: K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) N^mu D(p) exp[N S_p] [1+O_p(N^-1)], (7) where S_p=phi(xi)+(pi i/2) sum_i (xi_i-1)^2/p_i. (8) The coefficient D(p) is nonzero. Its source-amplitude factor is exactly a(xi); no value a(0) is inserted in its place. Here is the required modification of the proof, rather than an application of a theorem whose unit hypothesis has failed. Use the same local Fourier critical map xi_F(z), action Psi(z), and determinant branches as in the general transfer. Analytic finite-window stationary phase applied to (1) gives the ABSOLUTE expansion F_N(z)=N^(mu+b/2) exp[N Psi(z)] [B(z)+O(N^-1)], B(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a(xi_F(z)) / sqrt(det[-phi''(xi_F(z))]). (9) Both the remainder and its fixed derivatives are uniform on a smaller fixed complex neighborhood. The proof expands the bounded analytic amplitude a+r_N on the translated Gaussian contour, so it never divides by a or B. Thus (9) is valid also on their zero sets. Every global-color, finite-color-endpoint, noncentral Fourier and large-charge estimate in the transfer uses an UPPER bound for C_N and its controlled derivatives. Those estimates are unchanged by (1). The strict ordering of nonminimal charges depends on phi, not on a lower amplitude bound. For fixed p their exponential losses dominate all the bounded amplitude factors. At the second saddle use (9) in its absolute form. Put z_i*=(xi_i-1)/(2p_i), T_1(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+z_i). Then T_1(z*)=S_p and the leading coefficient is D(p)=Gamma(p) a(xi), Gamma(p)=2^b (2pi)^b product_i sinh(2pi i z_i*) / [sqrt(det[-phi''(xi)]) sqrt(det[-T_1''(z*)])]. (10) The determinants are nonzero on the chosen translated contours. Equation (5) and smallness imply z_i* is nonzero for each finite p_i; also |z_i*|<1/4, so its sinh factor is nonzero. Hence Gamma(p)!=0. At fixed p with a(xi)!=0, division by this now NONZERO leading coefficient turns the absolute O_p(N^-1) into the relative error in (7). Its constant may increase as p approaches Z. The 2^b minimal signed-charge sectors still ADD. Under a sign change of one charge, its saddle coordinate changes sign; the exact packet and its leading amplitude are separately even. The charge times sinh factor, determinant branch and exact parity character have the same transformation as in the original proof. This argument uses the exact source symmetry, not positivity of a. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N(p)|=2pi Re S_p. (11) If the SAME source branch has the actual marked representation, primitive peripheral equations and complete regulator anchor required by the general geometric completion theorem, the right side is the actual filled hyperbolic volume. Nothing in this amplitude extension supplies those independent certificates. Points in Z are excluded from this particular leading-coefficient argument. They are NOT counterexamples to a volume limit: a later Gaussian or source coefficient may give the same exponential rate. The diagram and slopes remain fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity; no joint large-N/large-slope uniformity is asserted. ## 4.
