Selection, geometry, and an actual knot source The [maximal-diagonalization theorem](research_maximal_diagonalization_source_gap.md), sections 4--5, supplies three conclusions used here: 1. Every \(\mathcal Q\) in the statement has a simple diagonalization. 2. Every nonsimple diagonalization has capacity strictly below some simple one. Thus every global maximizer is simple. 3. At each maximizing chart the original closed non-CROSS degree fiber has a uniform strict entropy gap below \(\Phi\). These assertions include \(R=2\) and allow separating triangles. The combinatorial simplification removes repeated diagonal edges by flips across digons. The strict capacity comparison uses the final flip into a simple sphere, where the angle optimizer is positive at every allowed ordinary corner. It does not assume that a chosen initial chart already has a hyperbolic realization. For a simple \(\mathcal T_*\), sections 3--5 of the [simple-sphere capacity and packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) give the unique relative-interior angle optimizer, finite positive ordinary curvatures, and the labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron \(P_{\mathcal T_*}\). The normalization is exact: \[ \Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(P_{\mathcal T_*})/\pi. 	ag{4} \] This construction supplies the positive geometric certificate, rather than making it an extra unverified hypothesis on \(\mathcal Q\). The [general Morse source realization](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) constructs an actual augmented link from this matched sphere. Its physical strands use the specified pairing in every four-terminal disk; they are not the abstract cycles of the cubic graph with its matching removed. Cutting its projection sphere and crossing disks gives precisely the two labeled balls whose boundary polyhedron is \(P_{\mathcal T_*}\). The local shaded maps, including the recorded half twists, are those of the [original augmented-link cut and gluing](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), sections 1--5. The two copies therefore give the complete hyperbolic exterior and (2), with the actual disk-framed peripheral paths. A spanning tree of the graph of untwisted physical main circles selects odd boxes that merge them to one circle. This proves the existence of a knot parity pattern. Any integer filling of that fixed parity retains one main component. The [positive marked filling argument](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) applies to this actual augmented exterior: its local positive gluing and primitive disk slopes give all sufficiently long independent signed fillings. No constant number of heads in a horizontal slice is required by that geometric argument. The same general Morse source theorem supplies the exact original quantum contraction, for every \(N\), in the form \[ S_N( oldsymbol\delta)= \left[\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^{d}ight] \left.\prod_{e=1}^R H_{V_N(-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e))} (L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e}) ight|_{L_u=L_v=0},\qquad d=N-1. 	ag{5} \] It also gives the whole original Fourier/Hermite filling functional, with its original \(\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_e)\), charge weights, Gaussian \(\pi iN\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2\), and scalar \(q^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-i)^R\). Thus (5) is a polynomial of the newly constructed link, not a polynomial transported from a different diagonalization. Half twists enter this functional through \(n_e\) once. They are not also inserted in the local \(V_N\) in (5). ## 3. The new non-CROSS gap controls the full numerator Use the exact CROSS/LEFT/RIGHT decomposition of each original local polynomial, at its actual parity-dependent cutoffs. Let \(C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}\) be the all-CROSS coefficient, including its sign \((-1)^{dR}\), and set \(E_N=S_N-C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}\). The original normalized degree-flow fiber has supply one at every port, demand one at every ordinary face, and zero at \(u,v\). Its closed non-CROSS subset has at least one middle load at least \(1/2\). The [sharp Green maximum](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md) eliminates the real spectra in the local upper functional. On an overloaded LEFT row \((a,b,c,d)\) with \(
u=a+b+d=1-c\leq1/2\), it is \[ \overline H=f(a)+f(b)+f(d)-f(
u),\qquad f(t)=-\int_0^t\log	an(\pi s)\,ds; 	ag{6} \] RIGHT is reflected and CROSS has its complete triangle entropy. The formulas agree continuously on the seams. The exact load-preserving diagonal flip raises (6) by at least \(f(
u)\). Finite maximality, together with the separate pure-child and seam arguments, therefore gives \[ \max_{	ext{closed non-CROSS fiber}} \sum_e\overline H(q_e)\leq\Phi-\gamma \quad	ext{for some }\gamma>0. 	ag{7} \] If the fiber is empty its contribution is absent. Crucially, the flip comparison in (7) is classical; it asserts no quantum identity between different diagonals or links. Apply the [uniform closed coefficient upper theorem](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) to the original coefficients of \(E_N\), after imposing their shared face demands. There are only polynomially many incidence arrays for fixed \(R\). The original finite cutoffs differ from the closed degree domains by \(O(1/N)\); the proved closed continuity and uniform upper bound include those boundary arrays, protected zeros, both parities, and zero sampled factors. Equations (6)--(7) give, for all large \(N\), \[ \sup_{ oldsymbol\delta\in\mathbb T^R}|E_N| \leq e^{N(\Phi-\gamma/2)}. 	ag{8} \] The remainder is itself a cosine polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in each spectrum. Polynomial Bernstein bounds therefore give \[ |E_N(\mathbf x+i\mathbf y)| \leq\exp\{N(\Phi-\gamma/2) +2\pi d\sum_e|y_e|\}. 	ag{9} \] Choose a fixed strip sufficiently thin that the last term is less than \(N\gamma/4\). This gives a strict complex gap everywhere, including all fixed derivatives on smaller strips. This is the full-numerator restoration used here. It uses no flat-plat endpoint forest. ## 4. The CROSS packet and spectral gap on this general Morse source Here the extensions of the older flat-plat notation must be checked; the finite source construction alone does not give asymptotics. Sections 1--3 of the [original coefficient packet proof](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) use the following data: the exact coefficient (5) and its primitive Cauchy measure; the local full-Hermite cofactor interpolation and relative estimates; a positive simple-white packing with two adjacent marked vertices; and connectivity of the remaining ordinary vertices. All are present on the new source. A simple triangulated sphere remains connected after deleting two vertices. Moreover the protected MAIN edge cannot also be a matching edge, so no local outer pair consists of both protected vertices. The allowed local zero specializations are exactly those in the cofactor proofs. The angular-complement proof is local on triangles and uses that connectivity. The face saddle uses the positive finite-face Hessian after fixing the common scale. Neither proof uses the order of cups, caps and coupons in a horizontal sweep. Consequently the same finite functions \(A_N,H_N\), constructed on this new coefficient, give \[ C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}( oldsymbol\delta) = rac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{NA_N( oldsymbol\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N( oldsymbol\delta)}} (1+O(N^{-1})) 	ag{10} \] on a fixed complex neighborhood of zero. The determinant branch is continued from the positive face Hessian. All finite anchoring factors remain in \(A_N\); (10) does not define them by an unknown source value. Its limiting action satisfies \[ A_0(0)=\Phi,\qquad A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_e),\qquad C_e>0. 	ag{11} \] It is separately even and real on the real chart. The shared scale quotient has its original dimension \(R-1\) and measure; no bridge number occurs in that dimension. Similarly the [global CROSS spectral-gap proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) uses the local cofactor transfer and prefix bounds, the same complete radii, and the ordinary angular connectivity. It gives, for each \(\eta>0\), a strict gap below \(\Phi\) on a fixed complex strip over \(\max_e|\delta_e|_{\mathbb T}\geq\eta\). The [general Morse action and packet audit](research_general_morse_cross_action.md) records these dependency checks separately. In particular we do not invoke section 4 of the older packet note, whose full restoration had its own flat-layout hypotheses. Equations (8)--(11) now restore (10) to the **full** source \(S_N\) on a sufficiently small fixed complex chart: shrink the chart so its critical real part stays above the absolute remainder bound. The amplitude in (10) is a nonzero unit times explicit powers and finite anchors, so that remainder is exponentially small relative to it. Adding (9) to the CROSS gap gives the full-source strip gap away from zero. These are precisely the relative-packet hypothesis H1 and the global strip-gap hypothesis H2 of the whole-period theorem. ## 5. The entire original period and its filled-volume action Apply the proof of the [whole Fourier-period theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) to \(S_N\). Beyond H1 and H2, it needs only the exact functional already proved in section 2, separate evenness and period one, the polynomial degree bound, and the original sine/Gaussian endpoint identities. The full source has each property. The proof keeps the second-derivative endpoint currents, bounds the infinite charge tail on whole intervals, and localizes only finitely many charges. Thus no additional cycle selection or cancellation assumption is introduced by this application. For all sufficiently long independently signed fixed \(\mathbf n\), the original unit-charge orbit has a nonzero leading coefficient at both level parities. Its limiting phase is the stationary value of \[ A_0( oldsymbol\delta) +\pi i\sum_e n_e\delta_e^2 +2\pi i\sum_e\delta_e. 	ag{12} \] The fixed geometric and analytic thresholds can be enlarged so the \(O(\sum_e|n_e|^{-2})\) loss from \(\Phi\) is smaller than the fixed complementary gaps. This is uniform over all sufficiently large minimum twist magnitudes; the asymptotic error constants may depend on the fixed vector. Nothing here interchanges the twist and level limits. To identify (12), use the [general Morse group/action extension](research_general_morse_cross_action.md) of the [marked cofactor action](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). At a horizontal slice with its actual variable region sequence \(F_0,\ldots,F_{m(t)}\), the reflection prefixes telescope just as in the constant-width notation. A cup or cap inserts or deletes an inverse pair. The same local primitive collar and disk longitude therefore give the actual link representation and peripheral marking. The general face-winding computation in the source theorem leaves no additional spectral-dependent turn term. In the recorded convention put \[ A_\epsilon=A_0+\pi i\sum_e\epsilon_e\delta_e^2, \qquad V_e=-4\pi i\delta_e, \qquad \partial_{\delta_e}A_\epsilon=U_e. 	ag{13} \] The stationary equations of (12) are exactly the primitive smooth filling equations \(U_e+p_eV_e=-2\pi i\). The complete value (4), the actual geometric deformation, and the retained longitude boundary correction in the marked-action proof imply \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{crit}(12) =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\mathcal T_*,\epsilon}(\mathbf p)). 	ag{14} \] It is the filled volume, not the complete augmented volume in (2). Finally the [original source normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) changes the raw knot contraction only by its recorded unit-modulus framing character. If the separately defined one-cut modified convention is used instead, retain its factor \(i^{N+3}/N\); its logarithmic rate is zero. This proves (3). ## 6. Relation to the prescribed k-bridge target The result ranges over **every** simple spherical quadrangulation of arbitrary size, then every maximizing diagonal choice and every fixed knot parity pattern, with independently long signed twists at every box. It is not a single twist family or a fixed list of examples. Its selection condition is a finite classical optimization, with existence proved above; no quantum gap remains as an extra hypothesis for this selected class. It does not prove the same result for each preassigned diagonalization. Changing a diagonal can change the actual augmented link. Nor does the general Morse construction preserve a preassigned plat width or prove a particular minimal bridge number. The [general prescribed-plat target](general_augmented_plat_long_twist_target.md) therefore remains open beyond this and the previously certified subclasses. For that target one still needs a source comparison on the given diagram, or a topology-preserving way to reach a certified chart.

title: The odd endpoint source is the actual matching-graph first normal
text: # The odd endpoint source is the actual matching-graph first normal 30 October 2026. The complete geometric matching graph Delta is also an exact quantum-source graph at every ODD level. Splitting the actual simple complete-color projectors yields a typed trivalent pivotal network on Delta itself. Its ordinary closure has a simple quantum- dimension factor, and the original exposed marked endpoint contribution is its specified first normal. This works for every fixed actual plat, without a Conway-tree, bipartite, or NC/Fisher assumption. This is a source-compatible global graph interface. It is not a positive resummation theorem or a volume limit. It isolates exactly which global network must be compared with the geometric angle polytope; it does not replace its tensors by independently maximized local scalars. ## 1. The literal endpoint and the matching graph Fix an original augmented 2k-plat with r designated crossing circles, all outside wires/cups/caps recorded, and one exposed original physical mark. Let N=2m+1, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), and x=q^d. The genuine endpoint c_m=-2 is simple. The already proved original Clebsch formulas give W:V_N -> V_N tensor V_N, pi=W^dagger P, pi W=I, E_St=W pi, L_endpoint=N E_St, R^epsilon E_St=omega_m^epsilon E_St, (1) where omega_m=q^(d^2/2) (-1)^m q^(m(m+1)). P in (1) is the physical two-head reversal. It is part of the actual pivotal dual, not a replacement of a bilinear contraction by a norm. All formulas apply to the full physical pair, including every degree. Split each E_St into its ordered W and pi factors. Its intermediate V_N edge is the crossing-disk edge d_i. The other legs follow precisely the original outside main segments. Thus the resulting trivalent ribbon graph is Delta of [the actual matching construction](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md): its marked perfect matching D consists of these intermediate edges, and its other edges are the original main segments. Its vertex cyclic orders are the original disk-side sectors, not a subsequently chosen abstract graph isomorphism. All edges now carry the SAME object V_N. At a vertex one retains the actual W or pi arrow and any cups required by the drawn physical orientation. There is no need to color all vertices black/white or put them in two horizontal rows. General Delta need not be bipartite. Bending a leg uses its literal cup/cap and pivotal clock; it is not plain tensor-index permutation. Consequently the marked all-endpoint contribution is Z_endpoint=N^r omega_m^(sum_i epsilon_i) Z_Delta, (2) where Z_Delta is the original marked contraction of these typed W/pi vertices and original outside cups/caps. The independently recorded external framing line remains external. This formula includes its complete normalization and allows Z_Delta=0. ## 2. A regular generic lift, including the original trace quotient Keep N fixed and let zeta=q exp(t), before root specialization. Use the original balanced highest-weight-d representation V_d(zeta), its actual generic physical cup pV and inverse cap ellV. In particular pV_a=N zeta^(-d^2) (-1)^a zeta^[a(d-a-1)] (Q;Q)_a (Q;Q)_(d-a)/(Q;Q)_d, Q=zeta^2. (3) All displayed denominator indices are below N, so the physical cup and cap are regular. Their root values are the original ones. Their genuine turn retains the full ratios in (3), not just root monomials. The central generic projector e_m onto the highest-weight-d summand of V_d tensor V_d is REGULAR near q. One direct formula is e_m(t)=product_(0<=j<=d, j!=m) [Omega(t)-c_j(t) I]/[c_m(t)-c_j(t)], c_j(t)=zeta^(2j+1)+zeta^(-2j-1). (4) Every denominator at q is nonzero: the central node is isolated even though the other nodes pair with one another. Thus (4) also retains its full zero first normals on those other paired nodes. Equivalently, use the generic first-entry-one W:V_d->V_d tensor V_d and its genuine ordered bilinear dual D(W). Then e_m=W D(W)/eta_m, eta_m=(-1)^m zeta^[-m(3m+1)] (Q;Q)_(3m+1)/[(Q;Q)_m (Q;Q)_(2m+1)]. (5) The common root zero in the ratio cancels before specialization; its remaining product tends to one. Hence eta_m is a unit and this is another regular lift of the original E_St. Formula (4) avoids having to choose a root frame to see regularity. Let F_Delta(t) be the ordinary closed physical plat with e_m in every circle position, all original outside cups/caps, and an ordinary cap also at the eventually marked arc. After splitting e_m as in (5), it is the same typed trivalent network Delta with its genuine generic pivotal contractions. No high recoupling channel has been discarded. Leave the chosen exposed physical arc open. Generic Hopf covariance makes the resulting endomorphism of V_d a scalar z_Delta(t) I: its K eigenvalues are distinct and its interior F arrows are nonzero, so commuting with K and F forces this scalarity. All physical entries are regular, hence z_Delta is holomorphic. Closing that arc gives F_Delta(t)=D_N(t) z_Delta(t), D_N(t)=(-1)^d [N]_(q exp(t)), D_N(0)=0, nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q-q^-1) !=0. (6) The original marked root row satisfies m pV(0)=1 and therefore extracts precisely z_Delta(0). It follows that Z_endpoint=N^r omega_m^(sum_i epsilon_i) F_Delta'(0)/nu_N. (7) This is the full scalar derivative of the ordinary closure. It must not be replaced by first specializing that closure to its root zero, or by differentiating one guessed local coefficient. A different regular lift of the same root coupons gives the same marked root endomorphism, so the normalized derivative in (7) is lift independent. It is legitimate to use (4), but this does not call (4) the original moving-q germ of the entire complete-circle operator. ## 3. Why this is the geometric graph, and what the global polytope is Suppose the actual matching graph Delta has the labeled positive right-angled ideal polyhedron Q_Delta. Its triangular shaded faces are exactly the just-identified source vertices, and its ideal vertices are exactly the source graph edges. Thus the geometric and quantum constructions share the actual labeled incidence, not merely a cubic vertex count. The complete augmented exterior has volume 2Vol(Q_Delta). Cone an ideal vertex of Q_Delta to compatible triangulations of its nonincident faces, and use the identical subdivisions in the second copy. Keep the actual white and shaded face identifications, including all retained half twists. This gives an actual positive ideal triangulation T of the augmented exterior. Its global angle polytope is alpha_(t,0)+alpha_(t,1)+alpha_(t,2)=pi for every t, sum_(tetrahedral incidences at e) alpha_(t,e)=2pi for every e, alpha>=0. (8) The incidence matrix is calculated from these FULL face-pairing words; it is not one independent simplex per source vertex. The proved [general positive gluing theorem](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md) gives its unique positive geometric maximum max_(8) sum_t V_ideal(alpha_t)=2Vol(Q_Delta). (9) It also supplies an algebraic optimizer and its cusp-decoration gauge. A separately certified marked positive triangulation can replace Q_Delta. Equations (7)--(9) identify the precise source and geometric endpoints of a proposed coherent resummation. They do not yet identify the variables or weights BETWEEN them. To do that, an actual recoupling or face-state expansion must retain its finite physical coefficient, all pole/normal terms, and a proved map to the angle incidences (8). Its factorial action must equal the SINGLE constrained functional in (9), with the source's phases/cycle and absolute normalization. Triangle inequalities for ordinary spin colors, by themselves, are not the global edge-sum equations (8). Matching the counts of labels or tetrahedra is not an incidence proof. This also explains why locally maximizing each trivalent scalar is insufficient. The source tensors remain contracted through every physical magnetic edge. The exact six-entry phase obstruction already rules out making them all positive by independent leg gauges. A positive resummation has to use those contractions coherently. ## 4. What is actually established beyond local vertices The primitive cube supplies one nontrivial calibration. Its original odd central sector was reduced by a generic, clocked, all-input rung identity to a positive Newton period. The exact first normal survives that reduction, and its exponential rate contains the shared geometric core term, not just the product of the local source scalars. This is a concrete example of the kind of global resummation required by (7). It is not a generic identity for arbitrary Delta. For an NC source graph Gamma, the present graph is its Fisher expansion Delta=Fisher(Gamma). The original trivalent-source contractions reduce its facial triangles to the known local coefficients and leave the ordinary Gamma-network first normal. This is consistent with (7), but does not extend that special facial-triangle reduction to an arbitrary matching graph. General Delta can have nonmatching cycles of other lengths and need not satisfy the original NC ordering. At even N the endpoint node is double; the circle is nilpotent on that sector. W pi with pi W=I is NOT its all-input replacement. A full even normal or paired-channel source theorem is still required. Even at odd levels, (7) alone neither proves endpoint dominance in the whole color sum nor a nonzero endpoint value. Independently long fillings additionally require the actual mixed auxiliary-color packet, whole-color gap, marked peripheral branch and unit logarithmic charge. ## 5. Literature coverage only, with the actual scope retained [Van der Veen, arXiv:0805.0094v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094), Definitions 1--2 and Theorem 2, uses a specified sequence of KTG moves. Its main theorem gives a sufficiently large augmentation multiplicity for that sequence. Its invariant has the stated formula at ODD N and is zero at EVEN N; its conclusion is explicitly the so(3) version. The singly augmented outside is built from regular ideal octahedra. Thus its theorem is not an all-level result for every singly augmented matching graph, nor a theorem for all independently long fillings. Only those definitions and statements are used here for coverage. [Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell, arXiv:2506.09296](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296) addresses OCTAHEDRAL fully augmented links. Its stated TV result is for links without half twists and concerns a different invariant/root; its introduction explicitly sets Dehn fillings aside. It does not supply the original marked all-level mixed packet needed here. [Belletti, arXiv:2002.01904](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01904) formulates a Yokota upper-bound conjecture, proves it for a stated large family, and derives TV consequences. That also does not identify the original first normal (7) with a positive state sum for every Delta. No proof technique or unreviewed asymptotic theorem from these papers is an input to sections 1--4. ## 6. Exact source audit [The executable audit](../experiments/audit_general_odd_endpoint_matching_network.py) checks six original plat families at odd N=3,5,7 and widths k=2,3,4. It constructs the original pair Casimir and circle, checks the central projector against the independent Clebsch W/pi split, and contracts all physical wires with the original unrestricted mark. Its separate generic first-jet calculation uses (3),(4), before root specialization, and verifies the normalized trace derivative (6),(7). Retained signed half twists are checked against the original R matrices. The outside interval compiler independently checks every oriented Delta face. [Recorded results](../experiments/general_odd_endpoint_matching_network_results.json). These are source-identity tests; no asymptotic or positivity conclusion is inferred from their finite values.

title: Long-filling volume for one-end-layer plats at every bridge width
status: Full original invariant at every k ≥ 2; exact-bridge subfamilies
text: # Long-filling volume for one-end-layer plats at every bridge width theorem, 31 October 2026. This is a right-end extension of the [reduced-layer construction](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md). It retains the original flat-plat source, first-cap mark, all half twists and all independently signed full twists. The proof covers every $k\geq2$; it does not assert balance for every certified plat. ## 1. Exact word and conclusion Number physical adjacent slots from $0$ to $2k-2$, so slot $j$ is conventional braid generator $\sigma_{j+1}$. Define $$ \begin{gathered} O_k=(1,3,\ldots,2k-3),\qquad E_k^{\mathrm{right}}=(2,4,\ldots,2k-2),\\ D_k^{\mathrm{right}}=O_kE_k^{\mathrm{right}}O_k,\qquad R=3k-3. \end{gathered}\tag{1} $$ Keep the standard adjacent cup/cap pairs and mark the first original top cap on slots $(0,1)$. In conventional generator notation, the actual filled braid is $$ \begin{aligned} \beta_k(\mathbf p)={}& \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{\epsilon_j-2p_{1,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2p_{2,j}}\right)\\ &\quad\times\left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{-2p_{3,j}}\right). \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ with each $\epsilon_j=+1$ or $-1$ fixed. All products retain bottom-to-top order and increasing $j$ within the layer. The first O layer is odd; the other two layers are even. Its plat is therefore a knot, as checked again below. Write $K_k(\mathbf p)$ for this plat. **Theorem.** For every fixed $k\geq2$ and fixed first-layer sign pattern there is a threshold $T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that for every integer vector $\mathbf p$ with all $|p_{r,j}|\geq T$, fixed before $N$ tends to infinity, the full original normalized root invariant obeys $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_k(\mathbf p)\bigr).\tag{3} $$ All $3k-3$ twist parameters can have independent signs and magnitudes. The result holds at both level parities. No comparability of twist magnitudes or joint growing-twist/level limit is asserted. Moreover, in the congruence subfamily where every exponent in (2) is divisible by $3$, the minimal bridge number is exactly $k$. The congruence is used only for that lower bound, not for (3). Here $K_N$ denotes the original normalized root invariant, with the framing and component conventions of the [exact original period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). The analytic implication is the [general complete-radius balance theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md). It remains to prove its hypotheses for the actual source (1), uniformly in $k$, which occupies Sections 2–5 below. ## 2. Literal incidence, simple certificate and reflection Let $u$ be the exterior, $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$ the bottom odd-gap faces, and $e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$ the first-layer bounded even-gap faces. The middle layer changes $a_j$ to $b_j$ for every $1\leq j\leq k-1$, while $a_0$ remains unchanged. Set $b_0=a_0$ and $e_k=u$. All other names are distinct. The literal gap sweep gives $$ \begin{array}{lll} \text{first }O:&(a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{middle }E:&(e_j,a_j,b_j,e_{j+1}),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{final }O:&(b_{j-1},e_j,u,b_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1. \end{array}\tag{4} $$ Each quartet has the original two triangles $(x,b,y),(x,y,c)$. The protected pair is $u,a_0$ on its original MAIN edge. There is no graph- to-plat adapter or isotopy in this description. The MAIN edges are $u-a_i$, $u-b_i$ (sharing only $u-a_0$ at the left end) and $e_j-a_{j-1},e_j-a_j,e_j-b_{j-1},e_j-b_j$ (sharing only $e_1-a_0$). The MATCHING edges are the two chains $a_{j-1}-a_j$ and $b_{j-1}-b_j$, and the chain $e_1-e_2-\cdots-e_{k-1}-u$. All these edges have distinct endpoints; none is repeated as a separate edge. This includes $k=2$: the three matching edges are $a_0-a_1,a_0-b_1,e_1-u$. Every listed edge is incident to exactly two of the actual triangles in (4), by the same gap incidence pairing as in the reduced family, with the right middle-E box now closing against the exterior. The inherited sphere has $$ V=3k-1,\qquad E=9k-9,\qquad F=6k-6,\qquad V-E+F=2.\tag{5} $$ Thus the white cellulation is a simple triangulated sphere for every $k\geq2$. The [existing simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) gives the actual labeled convex ideal right-angled packing and its original two cut balls. There is an orientation-reversing sphere automorphism $a_i\leftrightarrow b_i$, fixing $u,a_0,e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$, and interchanging the first/final layers. Normalize the original marked tangency $u-a_0$ to infinity, with $u$ the outside lower half-plane $Y\leq0$ and $a_0$ the outside upper half-plane $Y\geq2$. Uniqueness of the marked positive curvature solution up to scale, followed by unique contact-center development, realizes the automorphism by a vertical reflection. Translate its axis to $X=0$. This is precisely the uniqueness/reflection argument in the reduced-family proof, with the same connected ordinary-face Hessian. In particular the actual curvatures satisfy $A_i=B_i$. Put $L=k-1$. The fixed graph cycle is $$ u-a_0-e_1-e_2-\cdots-e_L-u. $$ It separates the original sphere into the a-side and b-side triangulated disks. The ordered axis chain now runs from the upper marked line through $e_1,\ldots,e_L$ to the lower marked line, with no extra endpoint a-circle on the axis. All $a_i$ lie on one side, all $b_i$ on the other: this follows from the consistently oriented a-side triangles along the fixed chain, including the last triangle $(a_L,e_L,u)$. Choose the a-side to be $X>0$. The fixed disks have disjoint axis intervals, ordered strictly from top to bottom. Write $$ \begin{gathered} y_0=2>y_1>\cdots>y_{L-1}>y_L=0,\\ \operatorname{radius}(e_j)=\frac{y_{j-1}-y_j}{2},\qquad E_j=\operatorname{curvature}(e_j)=\frac2{y_{j-1}-y_j}. \end{gathered}\tag{6} $$ For $L=1$ this means $e_1$ is the unit disk centered at $(0,1)$. ## 3. Height recurrence with the correct right boundary For $1\leq i\leq L-1$ the ordinary right-side circle $a_i$ is tangent to $u$ and both $e_i,e_{i+1}$. If its center is $(X_i,r_i)$, elementary tangency gives $$ 2r_i=\frac{y_i(y_{i-1}-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i},\qquad X_i^2=\frac{y_{i-1}y_i(y_i-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i}.\tag{7} $$ These are actual squared-distance identities, not a continuation past a zero height. The final circle $a_L$ is treated separately in Section 5. Set $$ z_j=\sqrt{1-\frac{y_j}{y_{j-1}}}\quad(1\leq j\leq L), \qquad z_0=0,\qquad z_L=1.\tag{8} $$ For $L\geq2$ the first pair $a_1,b_1$ touches both marked lines, so $r_1=1$. Using $y_0=2$ in (7) gives $$ (1-z_1^2)(1+z_2)=1.\tag{9} $$ At every other interior index $2\leq j\leq L-1$ use actual tangency of consecutive right-side circles $a_{j-1},a_j$. With $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, $w=z_{j+1}$, and $q=1-z^2$, the same substitution as in the reduced proof gives $$ 1-2q(1+pw)+q^2(1-p^2)(1-w^2)=0.\tag{10} $$ For $w<1$, its second root $1/[(1-p)(1-w)]$ exceeds $1$ and is excluded by the actual height ratio $0<q<1$. At the last such index $w=z_L=1$, the quadratic becomes the exact linear equation $1-2q(1+p)=0$. Both cases, together with (9), yield $$ (1+z_{j-1})(1-z_j^2)(1+z_{j+1})=1, \qquad 1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{11} $$ There is no equation at $j=L$ and no evaluation of $f$ at $\log2$ below. This is the new boundary condition; the old zero-endpoint equation must not be imposed on the added end box. ## 4. Uniform interior bound, including $k=2$ and $k=3$ For $L\geq3$ let $v_j=\log(1+z_j)$, with $v_0=0$, $v_L=\log2$ and $0<v_j<\log2$ at all interior indices. The same strictly convex function $$ f(v)=-v-\log(2-e^v),\qquad f (0)=0,\qquad f''(v)=\frac{2e^v}{(2-e^v)^2}>0. $$ satisfies $$ f(v_j)=v_{j-1}+v_{j+1},\qquad1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{12} $$ Place the exact three-node seed $$ (\log(5/3),\log(9/5),\log(5/3)). $$ at any consecutive three positions among $1,\ldots,L$ and extend by zeros. Call the resulting vector $s$, with $s_0=0$. At every interior index, $f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1}$, while the right boundary automatically obeys $s_L\leq\log2=v_L$. Put $t=\max_{1\leq j\leq L}(s_j/v_j)$. If $t>1$, its attaining index must be interior. At that index strict convexity gives $f(s_j)>t f(v_j)$, while the neighbor comparison gives $f(s_j)\leq t f(v_j)$, a contradiction. Therefore $v\geq s$. Every interior index lies in a translated seed, so $$ z_j\geq\frac23,\qquad1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{13} $$ The inclusion of position $L$ in a translated seed is legitimate because it is compared only as a boundary value; $f(\log2)$ is never evaluated. For $L=2$, equation (9) with $z_2=1$ gives $z_1=1/\sqrt2>2/3$ exactly. For $L=1$ there is no interior index. Thus (13) holds wherever needed for every $k\geq2$, with these exact small-width interpretations. ## 5. Curvature ratios and the last physical interstice For $j<L$, let $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$ and $D_0=p^2+z^2-p^2z^2>0$. The physical formulas (7) and recurrence (11) give exactly $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{A_{j-1}}{E_j}&=\frac{p^2z^2}{D_0},& \frac{A_j}{E_j}&=\frac{z^4(1+p)^2}{D_0},\\ \frac{A_{j-1}+A_j}{E_j} &=z^2\left[1+\frac{2p(1+p)z^2}{D_0}\right]\geq z^2. \end{aligned}\tag{14} $$ At $j=1$ this includes $A_0=0$ and $r_1=1$. At $j=L-1$ it uses $w=1$ only through the valid linear boundary recurrence, and all circles in (7) are still genuine finite disks. Therefore (13),(14) give $$ \frac{E_j}{A_{j-1}+A_j}\leq\frac94,\qquad1\leq j<L.\tag{15} $$ It remains to check the actual final O ports, involving $e_L$ and $a_L$. For $L\geq2$, the circle $a_L$ has exactly three white neighbors: the lower line $u$, $e_L$, and $a_{L-1}$. These three neighbors are pairwise tangent. The a-side disk decomposition places $a_L$ in their bounded curvilinear interstice next to the $u-e_L$ contact; its reflected partner lies in the opposite interstice. The positive Descartes branch is consequently $$ A_L=A_{L-1}+E_L+2\sqrt{A_{L-1}E_L}.\tag{16} $$ There is also a direct physical branch check requiring only the already proved same-side development. Put $H=y_{L-1}$ and $p=z_{L-1}$ in $(0,1)$. Formula (7) gives $X_{\mathrm{prev}}=H/p>H$ and $2r_{\mathrm{prev}}=H/p^2$, while $\operatorname{radius}(e_L)=H/2$. For $a_L$ centered at $(X,r)$, tangency to $u$ and $e_L$ gives $X^2=2Hr$. Tangency to $a_{\mathrm{prev}}$ then gives $|1/X-1/X_{\mathrm{prev}}|=1/H$. Since $X_{\mathrm{prev}}>H$ and $X>0$, the only positive solution is $$ X=\frac H{1+p}. $$ Consequently $A_L=2(1+p)^2/H=(\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{prev}}}+\sqrt{E_L})^2$, proving (16) without an arbitrary Descartes-root choice. It also agrees with the original bounded-gap contact order. In particular $A_L\geq E_L$, so $$ \frac{E_L}{A_{L-1}+A_L}\leq1.\tag{17} $$ For $L=1$, the actual marked strip contains $e_1$ of radius $1$ at $(0,1)$ and $a_1,b_1$ of radius $1$ at $(2,1),(-2,1)$. Thus $E_1=A_1=B_1=1$ and (17) holds directly with $A_0=0$. This is the literal word $(1,2,1)$, not a changed marking of the reduced width-two word. Equations (15),(17) establish the zero-middle bound $E/(x+y)\leq9/4$ at every first/final O port. The [source-normalized nine-quarter lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) gives strict balance there, with gap $>1/2500$. At every middle-E port, including the last port with outer $u=0$, the two positive middles have equal curvatures $A_j=B_j$. Since the outer sum $E_j+E_{j+1}>0$ (with $E_{L+1}=0$), the original strict inequality $Q(x,A_j,y)>\tfrac12\log A_j$ gives balance there as well. There is no exception at a protected outer line. Thus every port passes the actual complete-radius balance test for every $k\geq2$, in one shared original marked packing. ## 6. Full source, knot parity and exact bridge subfamilies The general complete-radius balance filling theorem now proves (3), including the full original one-sided remainder, the entire all-charge period, the original normalization and both parities. Its threshold can depend on the fixed diagram and prescribed parity, and no claim is made for arbitrary certified diagrams failing balance. The first O layer has odd exponent on the zero-based slots $1,3,\ldots,2k-3$. The resulting transpositions $(1\ 2),(3\ 4),\ldots,(2k-3\ 2k-2)$ join the initially $k$ cap components successively. All remaining boxes have even exponent. Therefore the original endpoint-pairing graph is one cycle and the plat in (2) is a knot. This argument includes $k=2$ and does not confuse zero-based slots with conventional generator indices. The [Fox-coloring certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) applies without change: if every actual exponent in (2) is divisible by $3$, every full crossing box acts as the identity on ordered $\mathbb F_3$ colors, and the standard cup/cap register has exactly $3^k$ colorings. Any $b$-bridge knot has at most $3^b$ colorings. Together with the supplied $k$-bridge plat this gives minimal bridge number exactly $k$. Each required exponent congruence is compatible with its prescribed parity and independent arbitrarily large signed full twists. This identifies unbounded actual bridge complexity, without putting a congruence restriction on the volume theorem. No finite search over k or numerical packing values are used to prove this uniform statement. The reduced-family proof supplies the recurrence algebra, comparison principle and source Q normalization; this note proves the changed right boundary and the literal all-width incidence explicitly. ## Validation and scope The proof applies to every fixed width, but does not provide a single filling threshold independent of the diagram or width. It proves this explicit family, not a universal balance condition for every certified plat. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume_results.json) check the original right-end box incidences, first mark, reflection and knot parity at 39 widths, six changed-boundary identities, and all 36 exact circle-support pairs and nine port tests of the width-two and width-three seeds. This supplements the analytical proof; the old interior recurrence audit is not repeated, and finite tests are not used to infer the uniform or asymptotic conclusion.

title: Long fillings of a general original quantum source
text: # Long fillings of a general original quantum source 29 October 2026. The Fourier filling mechanism is independent of the pretzel graph. This theorem isolates its actual analytic inputs and proves that they propagate to every independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral filling. The new general geometric theorem then identifies the resulting rate with the actual filled hyperbolic volume. This is a CONDITIONAL quantum transfer theorem. It does not assert its source hypotheses for every diagram, or count them as proved merely because the diagram has a positive geometric triangulation. Establishing them for broader original sources is part of the active goal. ## 1. Exact source and hypotheses Fix a diagram with b specified crossing-circle ports on original complete target strands. Retain its entire marked closure, all Cartan factors, and its literature normalization. Let A_N(h_1,...,h_b) be its original mixed-circle scalar, with auxiliary colors j_i=N-h_i. The [all-input circle basis](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) gives the exact finite identity K_N(p)=chi_N kappa^(-2 sum p_i) sum_(j_1,...,j_b=1)^N product_i beta_(j_i-1)^(-p_i) A_N(N-j_1,...,N-j_b). (1) This substitutes each actual full twist R^(-2p_i), leaving the base coupons and retained half twists in A_N. The beta coefficients retain all confluent Casimir jets. Multilinearity of the original diagram proves(1), even if adjacent physical operators do not commute. The independent color-register functionals commute; no physical operator is moved through another. Keep chi_N explicitly and require its known normalization to be nonzero with log|chi_N|=o(N). Here A_N is defined before precisely that recorded outer factor; chi_N is not included a second time in the mixed scalar. It is not chosen using the value of the completed unknown invariant. Assume the following for this fixed source. **Global source gap.** There is a fixed sufficiently small delta>0, H=floor(delta N), a real F0 and gamma>0 such that max_(some h_i>H) |A_N(h)| <= poly(N) exp[N(F0-gamma)] (2) over the ENTIRE physical color cube 0<=h_i<=N-1. The estimate includes ordinary colors, every alias and every marked normal term. **Exact analytic corridor packet.** There is a finite holomorphic packet C_N(x), even in each coordinate, on a fixed complex neighborhood of the box |Re x_i|<=2delta, |Im x_i|<=sigma0, with |A_N(h)-eta_N C_N(h/N)| <=poly(N) exp[N(F0-gamma)] (3) for 0<=h_i<=H. Here eta_N is an explicit retained unit phase. On that fixed complex neighborhood, C_N(x)=N^mu a(x) exp[N phi(x)](1+O(N^-1)), (4) uniformly, where a and phi are holomorphic and separately even, a(0)!=0, phi(0)=F0, and phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (5) A known imaginary constant in phi(0) may instead be retained explicitly as exp[iN Im phi(0)] in eta_N. This only separates its specified unit phase; it does not change the original state or an unknown growth rate. The uniform complex statement is essential. A pointwise approximation on the physical grid is not enough for the Fourier contour estimates. One may shrink delta, with the global gap(2) required for the chosen corridor. By(4)--(5), after shrinking the neighborhood, |C_N(x+iy)|<=poly(N) exp[N(F0-a0||x||^2+B0||y||^2)] (6) with a0>0. All constants may depend on the fixed diagram, not on N. These assumptions concern a specified original source and specified interpolation, not a choice of solution of its recurrence. ## 2. The source action and theorem Define the local analytic Fourier transform by grad phi(xi(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi(z))+2pi i xi(z) dot z, B(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a(xi(z))/sqrt(det[-phi''(xi(z))]). The implicit-function theorem applies by(5). The Gaussian square root is the one from the translated original real contour. Both Psi and B are separately even; B(0)!=0 and Psi(z)=F0-i pi sum_i z_i^2/tau_i+O(||z||^4). (7) For integer nonzero charges m_i put T_m(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). For all independently sufficiently large fixed signed p_i, let z_* be the unique nearby critical point of T_1. Then K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) N^mu D(p) exp[N T_1(z_*)](1+O_p(N^-1)), (8) where D(p)=2^b (2pi)^(b/2) B(z_*) product_i sinh(2pi i z_*,i) /sqrt(det[-T_1''(z_*)]) is NONZERO. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_N(p)|=2pi Re T_1(z_*). (9) The slopes and diagram are fixed before N tends to infinity. There is no slope-comparability, same-sign, prime-level or parity restriction. The constants and threshold are source dependent. ## 3. Exact filling, including every endpoint and normal term The full Hermite coefficients obey sum_j |beta_j^(-p)|<=2N(1+|p|). Thus(2)--(3) cost only polynomial multiples of exp[N(F0-gamma)] in the WHOLE finite sum(1). No non-even alias is folded into C_N. For its exact even corridor define F_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(h/N) exp(2pi i h dot z). The [full-normal Fourier identity](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), sections4--5, is valid for ANY even packet. In each color its sampled kernel is the derivative of exp(-2pi i p N z^2) sinh(2pi i z) F_N(z). Its values vanish at z=+/-1/2 and its derivatives match at the two endpoints. Therefore the exact charge representation retains only m!=0. The complete b-port expression has integrand exp[-2pi i N sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i)] product_i[m_i sinh(2pi i z_i)] F_N(z), with the unchanged parity phases and kappa factors. Its infinite charge series converges with the paired endpoint currents retained. This identity uses both original normal contributions; a value-only Fourier kernel would not give the same zero-charge cancellation. Hypothesis(6) is precisely the source-specific input of the exact cotangent-contour Fourier estimate. Its proof applies coordinatewise to C_N: noncentral frequencies, finite color endpoints and fixed mixed derivatives all have an exponential source gap. The paired high-charge current has a double zero at the endpoint. Its weighted bound is a constant times poly(N,p) m/(m-|p|)^3 exp[N(F0-g)], for m>2|p|+2delta+2, and is summable. The imaginary contour width is fixed by the SOURCE, not divided by the largest slope. In several coordinates use the exact telescoping difference of the full color functionals and their finite-charge restrictions, as in equation(14a) of that note. All spectator chirps stay on their REAL finite grids or finite real integrals while one tail is removed. Thus these bounds do not incur exp(N|p_j|) costs from another port. This is why independently unequal slopes are permitted. ## 4. The central packet and all nonminimal charges The central Fourier calculation in section6 of the same note uses only(4)--(6), analytic implicit stationarity and a real Gaussian. It gives, uniformly on a fixed small complex z-neighborhood, F_N(z)=N^(mu+b/2) B(z) exp[N Psi(z)](1+O(N^-1)). (10) No separate pointwise error is transformed as if it had an exponential Fourier gap; the exact finite analytic C_N is used throughout. The [local charge proof](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md) also depends only on the stated analytic structure. Here is its extension when the diagonal cusp parameters tau_i are different. Put epsilon_i=1/p_i,t_i=m_i/p_i. The saddle equations become z_i=-t_i/2+epsilon_i Psi_i(z)/(4pi i). They have a unique holomorphic solution in one fixed polydisk of (t,epsilon), with z_i=-t_i/2 at epsilon=0. Completing the square isolates a purely imaginary term on real t,epsilon: T_m(z_m)=(pi i/2)sum_i t_i^2/epsilon_i+Bhat(t^2,epsilon). The remainder is analytic and even in every t_i. If b_i=pi Im(tau_i)/|tau_i|^2>0, then partial_(t_i^2) Re Bhat(0,0)=-b_i/4. Shrink one fixed polydisk so each derivative is <=-b_i/8. Integrating these inequalities along the squared coordinates gives Re T_m(z_m)<=Re T_1(z_*) -sum_i (b_i/8)(m_i^2-1)/p_i^2. (11) Thus only |m_i|=1 can be leading among local nonzero charges. Every component z_i is nonzero for m_i!=0: separate evenness writes Psi_i=z_i Q_i(z_1^2,...,z_b^2), and the saddle equation solves z_i=-t_i/[2(1-epsilon_i Q_i/(4pi i))]. The sinh factors in(8) therefore do not vanish. The real part of the translated-contour Hessian remains strictly negative, so its Gaussian determinant is nonzero for signed as well as positive slopes. The finite nonlocal charges are treated by the same source estimate: outside |z_i|<=t0/4 the real source has a fixed Fourier gap; inside, |m_i+2p_i z_i|>=|p_i|t0/2 for a charge with |m_i/p_i|>=t0. A fixed imaginary shift in that coordinate decreases its filling phase, including the endpoint connectors. The gap is independent of the largest other slope. Local connector bounds use |Im z_i|<=C|p_i|^-1 |m_i/p_i|, which follows from the same separately even factorization. These are the arguments of sections4--5 of the [corridor proof](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md); they do not use a common value of tau_i or a cyclic diagram. The 2^b minimal signed charges have identical complex action. Under (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i), m_i sinh(2pi i z_i) is unchanged; the exact parity characters are unchanged as well. They ADD. Gaussian integration of(10) supplies N^(-b/2), giving(8). Finally Re T_1(z_*) tends uniformly to F0 as max_i|1/p_i| tends to zero, so the threshold can absorb the fixed global/error gaps(2)--(3). This proves the full-source, not only corridor, theorem. ## 5. When the rate is the ACTUAL hyperbolic volume Add the following independent geometric certificates for the SAME source. The base diagram is a fixed complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic manifold Y. The analytic critical packet has an actual bounded framed representation family rho_x near the oriented complete holonomy, with the remaining components parabolic. Its original peripheral marking and absolute source action satisfy G=2pi i phi(x)+recorded real constant, z_i=2pi i x_i, ell_i=partial_(z_i)G=phi_i(x), U_i=-z_i, V_i=-2ell_i, with the literal spin kept when converting to these centered projective logs. Require the actual regulator comparison and the absolute anchor ImG(0)=Vol(Y), rather than merely a matching Hessian. The Fourier and filling stationarity equations then give EXACTLY ell_i=-2pi i z_*,i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i, 2pi Re T_1(z_*)=Vol(rho_p). The [general geometric completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) applies to this actual nearby framed representation. It gives a complete smooth hyperbolic metric on the correctly marked filled topology and hence lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_N(p)|=Vol(Y(p)). (12) That theorem handles arbitrary bases and primitive slopes. The quantum transfer proved HERE concerns the integral full-twist kernel(1); arbitrary rational quantum surgery kernels would need their own exact source and endpoint proof. No rational-filling quantum statement is silently added by the more general geometric theorem. ## 6. Current proved applications and active generalization task The established long-pretzel family supplies every hypothesis by explicit source and port proofs. The improved width estimate is being audited separately. For a general augmented diagram, identity(1) is already available, but the complete complex packet(3)--(5), its global gap(2), and its actual marked representation anchor must still be established. The theorem propagates those base certificates to all long fillings; it does not manufacture them from the A-polynomial or geometry alone. The active goal of the most general original-invariant equality remains open beyond the source classes where those hypotheses are proved. The [signed octahedral belt-stack assembly](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) now supplies all these hypotheses for another class, at every fixed nonempty stack width and fixed outer crossing power. Its literal inner color continuation, squared outer Fourier kernel, global source gaps, typed peripheral lift and complete face anchor give full equality for independently long signed integral fillings of ANY subset of auxiliary circles. Unfilled colors remain at h=0; they are not assigned p=0. This application does not turn the present conditional theorem into an unconditional statement for arbitrary graph sources. ## 7. Independent proof audit An independent read checked the exact N powers, the Cartan kernel factor, the all-unit parity cancellation, and the unequal-cusp charge estimate. It also checked the coordinate conversion dG=ell dz=(1/2)VdU and 2pi i T=G+sum p_i ell_i^2 up to its recorded REAL constant. The general theorem retains its base-source hypotheses; the audit does not establish them for a new diagram. The improved pretzel source proof currently verifies them for fixed odd s>=9. The [robust Conway filling theorem](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) now supplies every quantum hypothesis and the [actual marked peripheral branch](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) for all retained cylindrical robust factors. Arbitrary finite branching and turns are allowed; any subset of auxiliary circles may be filled along independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral slopes. Its complete mixed-color gap and uniform complex packet are proved separately. These pure full-twist fillings remain links with at least 2S+1 main components for S seeds, so this application is not a new knot-family claim. The [signed Conway extension](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) now supplies the same hypotheses for arbitrary fixed pure or signed odd-half-twist patterns on C(FG), with both children robust. Its exact complex packet retains eta_N and every integer offset, its supporting-plane estimate controls every alias and physical color, and its actual odd-link primitive meridians realize the selected action shear. Constructive parity assignments give knots after filling all auxiliary circles. The minimal C(A) and arbitrary short fillings are not included in this signed mixed-color application.

title: The representation-volume bound with general peripheral holonomy
text: # The representation-volume bound with general peripheral holonomy 28 October 2026. The independently proved smearing argument for [boundary-parabolic representations](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) also bounds representations whose peripheral images preserve a geodesic axis. Its proof needs integrable pullback volume and integrable finite- radius face errors, rather than a globally bounded derivative of the developing map. Axis-valued cusp maps supply exactly those properties. Consequently the marked regulator of EVERY actual SL2(C) representation of a finite-volume hyperbolic knot group has absolute value at most the manifold volume. This includes unit meridian and nonunit longitude. It supplies a geometric bound for a genuine peripheral-curve primitive; it does not identify a quantum-A component with that curve, or estimate the actual sourced quantum Green function. ## 1. Peripheral classification and an equivariant cusp development Let X=Gamma\H3 be an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold and rho:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its PSL2 action. Each peripheral image consists of commuting matrices. If one has distinct eigenvalues, both common eigenlines are preserved by every commuting matrix, so the image preserves their joining geodesic axis. Otherwise the image is central or has a nontrivial unipotent, whose commuting matrices preserve its unique eigenline and act parabolically there. Thus each cusp is either of axis type or of the boundary-parabolic type already treated. Central images may be treated as axis type with zero translation. No discreteness or irreducibility is required. For an axis-type cusp use domain coordinates (w,y), with w in C, y>Y and peripheral translations w->w+lambda. Choose an oriented target axis gamma(t), parametrized by hyperbolic distance. Its peripheral action is rho(gamma_0) gamma(t)=gamma(t+chi(lambda_gamma0)), where chi is the real translation character. The rotations about the same axis act trivially ON the axis. Extend chi from the lattice to a real-linear function of w and set f(w,y)=gamma(chi(w)+log y). (1) This is exactly peripheral-equivariant. It is smooth on finite cusp truncations and its image has dimension at most one. Hence f^*(vol_H3)=0 on the ENTIRE axis cusp. (2) It need not be globally Lipschitz: its horizontal derivative in the hyperbolic domain metric can grow like y. Equation (2), not a false global Lipschitz assertion, is what is used below. On parabolic cusps retain the old affine conical map, which has a uniform hyperbolic derivative bound and integrable pullback volume. Extend over the compact truncated core equivariantly by geodesic interpolation on a finite triangulation and a collar. Contractibility of the target gives the extension. The resulting f is locally Lipschitz, has a finite derivative bound on every fixed metric neighborhood of the truncated core, and has absolutely integrable pullback volume on X. Define Vol(rho)=integral_X f^*(vol_H3). (3) ## 2. Choice independence and the actual regulator normalization Two axis-cusp maps for the same noncentral peripheral image can be joined by an equivariant axis-valued homotopy. Its boundary-torus homotopy has zero 3-volume because it lies in that axis. Reversing the chosen axis endpoint is also such a homotopy. For a central peripheral image the maps may be independent of w; a homotopy then has zero horizontal derivatives and again zero boundary 3-volume. Parabolic-cusp choices have the vanishing boundary estimate already proved in the linked note. Stokes on a truncated core therefore proves that (3) is independent of these choices. Map (1) tends to a peripheral fixed ideal endpoint as y tends to infinity. Truncate an ideal fundamental chain and compare its developed straightening with f by the same face-compatible geodesic homotopy on the compact pieces. Internal faces cancel. The comparison with the IDEAL straightening is not generally axis-valued on a cusp: the other developed vertices need not lie on that axis. Its boundary term instead vanishes by the following explicit estimate. Put the selected fixed endpoint at infinity and the preserved axis at horizontal coordinate zero. An ideal straightening can be parametrized conically near that vertex, along the vertical geodesic rays to infinity. On a finite triangulation of a fundamental cusp cross-section its map has form f_cone(w,y)=(a(w),y b(w)), b(w)>0. (4a) Here a,b and their piecewise first derivatives are bounded on the fundamental cross-section, and b is bounded below there. Extend these functions using peripheral equivariance. If that peripheral acts by (z,y)->(l_gamma z,|l_gamma|y), their transformation rules are a(w+lambda)=l_gamma a(w), b(w+lambda)=|l_gamma|b(w). The conical parametrization is chosen on the common cusp cross-section and its faces before extending over the finite tetrahedral interiors; thus adjacent straight faces use the same tail parametrization. It is an allowed proper straightening of the same developed ideal chain. For a tetrahedron with vertex infinity, its faces incident to that vertex are vertical, and its deep tail is foliated by these vertical rays; this gives the claimed conical choice after subdivision. Join the axis map to (4a) by the EXPLICIT equivariant homotopy H_t(w,y)=(t a(w), y exp((1-t)chi(w)+t Log b(w))). On a fundamental cross-section the horizontal coordinates and their w,t derivatives are O(1), while its height is comparable to y and its height derivatives are O(y). The hyperbolic volume form is height^-3 dx_1 wedge dx_2 wedge dheight. Hence integral_(cusp torus at y times [0,1]) |H^*vol| <=C/y^2 ->0. (4b) This estimate is independent of any assertion of global Lipschitzness or a zero comparison volume. On parabolic cusp tails use the old vanishing horospherical estimate. Thus, with the SAME marked fundamental-cycle convention, Vol(rho)=sum_Delta oriented Vol(straight_rho Delta) =sum_Delta D(z_Delta). (4) Auxiliary ideal flags and degenerate tetrahedra are handled by the finite-chain approximation used in the linked proof. This identifies the absolute regulator normalization; it is not an arbitrarily shifted primitive of a peripheral differential. ## 3. Finite-radius smearing without a global Lipschitz bound Use the finite regular tetrahedron T_R and symmetric Lorentz straightening/homotopy of the linked smearing proof. For each fixed R its diameter is finite. That proof compares the developed straight tetrahedron with integral_(g T_R) f^*vol by a sum of FOUR oriented face-prism errors b_rho(g,face). Their integrability is the only new issue. On an axis cusp, if a domain face lies entirely in one lifted cusp horoball, both f on that face and the straight interpolation of its three vertex images lie on the SAME target axis. The complete face-prism homotopy is axis-valued, so b_rho(g,face)=0 there. (5) A cusp horoball is convex. For fixed R, every remaining domain face which encounters an axis cusp and is not contained in it has its frame basepoint in a FIXED metric neighborhood of the truncated core. That neighborhood is compact modulo Gamma. On it f has some finite Lipschitz bound L_R, so the finite-radius face-prism estimate of the old proof bounds b there. On parabolic cusps the old global cusp bound applies. Hence every fixed-R face error is absolutely integrable on Gamma\Isom+(H3). No bound uniform in R is asserted or needed. For EACH fixed R the four ordered regular faces are congruent by orientation-preserving isometries. Right Haar invariance makes their integrated error values identical; their alternating sum is exactly zero. Fubini for f^*vol is justified by its absolute integrability. With frame-fiber Haar mass normalized to one, this gives Vol(T_R) Vol(rho) =integral_(Gamma\G) Vol(straight f(g T_R)) dg. (6) Every target straight tetrahedron has absolute volume at most v3, by the independently proved ideal-tetrahedron bound. The Haar mass of the frame quotient is Vol(X). Therefore |Vol(rho)|<=v3 Vol(X)/Vol(T_R). Let R tend to infinity, so Vol(T_R) tends to v3. This proves |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(X). (7) There is no interchange of an unbounded family of face errors in this last step: their cancellation was exact separately at every finite R. Any joint projective shape limit of actual representation families has the same bound, because each D extends continuously through 0,1,infinity. ## 4. Consequence and limitation for the actual A-curve route On a genuinely identified peripheral representation curve, retain the actual eigenvalues M and ell and the marked Bloch chain. Its already proved boundary identity is delta beta=-2 M wedge ell. The Bloch--Wigner differential gives, along |M|=1, dR=2 log|ell| dArg M =log|ell| dArg Y, Y=M^2. (8) Thus R is an ABSOLUTELY normalized primitive of the logarithmic longitude modulus on a specified representation branch, and (7) bounds it by the knot volume, including along nonunit-longitude arcs. For two points on that same branch, |integral log|ell| dArg Y|<=2Vol(X). (9) If the initial marked regulator is independently known to be zero, the bound relative to it improves to Vol(X). A unitary meridian alone does not make that initial regulator zero; the complete hyperbolic representation is an immediate example. This does NOT bound the integral of the pointwise largest root of an arbitrary quantum-A symbol: that prescription may switch branches and forgets their regulator constants. Nor does it identify the classical symbol of an arbitrary all-level annihilator with a genuine peripheral curve. The existing actual-state reciprocity theorem expressly makes no such identification. Finally a quantum Green response requires its original affine/normal source, finite-jet resonance and boundary matching determinant. Bound (7) is a proved geometric input to that problem, not a substitute for the missing sourced transfer estimate.

title: Long-filling volume for reduced-layer plats of unbounded bridge number
status: Full invariant for every k ≥ 4; exact-bridge congruence subfamilies
text: # Long-filling volume for reduced-layer plats of unbounded bridge number theorem, 31 October 2026. Fix $k\geq4$ and signs $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$ for $1\leq j\leq k-1$. In conventional one-based braid-generator notation, form the standard $2k$-plat of $$ \beta_k(\mathbf p)= \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{\epsilon_j-2p_{1,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-2}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2p_{2,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{-2p_{3,j}}\right). $$ All products follow the original bottom-to-top order, with $j$ increasing within a layer. There are $3k-4$ independent integer full-twist parameters. Denote the resulting knot by $K_k(\mathbf p)$ and its original normalized root invariant by $\mathcal K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))$, retaining the framing and component conventions of the [original spectral period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). **Theorem.** For every such fixed $k$ and sign pattern there is a threshold $T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that, for every fixed integer vector with all $|p_{r,j}|\geq T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$, $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|\mathcal K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_k(\mathbf p)\bigr). $$ The twists can have independent signs and magnitudes; they are fixed before $N\to\infty$. The conclusion concerns the full original invariant. The proof below verifies the complete-radius balance hypothesis of the [general full-source filling theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) on one actual marked packing for every member of this source family. The comparison includes both level parities and the entire charge sum through that theorem. The supplied knots have bridge number at most $k$. The congruence subfamily in which every displayed braid exponent is divisible by $3$ has bridge number **exactly $k$**. This additional congruence is used only for the bridge lower bound, not for the volume theorem. Thus the family has unbounded minimal bridge complexity, rather than merely unbounded presentation width. This explicit construction does not assert balance for every simple-white plat or cover all $k$-bridge knots. Its uniform proof covers $k\geq4$; no balance claim is made here for the analogous reduced width-three word. ## 1. Literal source word, mark, and simple white sphere Use zero-based adjacent physical slots $0,\ldots,2k-2$. Slot $j$ is the braid generator usually denoted $\sigma_{j+1}$. The standard bottom and top cup pairs are $(0,1),(2,3),\ldots,(2k-2,2k-1)$. For $k\geq3$ put $$ \begin{gathered} O_k=(1,3,\ldots,2k-3),\qquad E_k^{\mathrm{int}}=(2,4,\ldots,2k-4),\\ D_k=O_kE_k^{\mathrm{int}}O_k,\qquad R=3k-4. \end{gathered}\tag{1} $$ These are the original bottom-to-top box slots, without an isotopy, Markov stabilization, or abstract graph-to-plat adapter. Mark the first original top cap, on slots $(0,1)$. Name the exterior $u$, bottom odd-gap regions $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$, and bounded even-gap regions $e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$. The internal middle layer replaces $a_j$ by $b_j$ for $1\leq j\leq k-2$. Set $b_0=a_0$ and $b_{k-1}=a_{k-1}$, because there are no boxes in slots $0$ or $2k-2$. All other named regions are distinct. The original gap sweep gives exactly $$ \begin{array}{lll} \text{first }O:&(a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{middle }E:&(e_j,a_j,b_j,e_{j+1}),&1\leq j\leq k-2,\\ \text{final }O:&(b_{j-1},e_j,u,b_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1. \end{array}\tag{2} $$ A quartet $(x,b,c,y)$ contributes the actual triangles $(x,b,y),(x,y,c)$. The protected regions are precisely $u$ and $a_0$. Their edge is MAIN. The white MAIN edges are $u-a_i$ and $u-b_i$, with the two named endpoint identifications retained; and $e_j-a_{j-1},e_j-a_j,e_j-b_{j-1},e_j-b_j$, again retaining the two endpoint identifications. The MATCHING edges are the two chains $a_{j-1}-a_j$ and $b_{j-1}-b_j$, together with the internal chain $e_j-e_{j+1}$. For $k\geq3$ no listed edge has equal endpoints, and there are no parallel edges: the two a/b chains have distinct interior vertices and share only their two endpoints. Each listed edge is incident to exactly two of the triangles in (2). At the left end, for example, $e_1-a_0$ is shared by the first-O output and final-O input triangles, while $u-a_0$ is shared by their other triangles. The right end is identical. The remaining $e_j$ MAIN incidences close against the appropriate middle-E triangle; the remaining $u$ incidences close between consecutive O boxes. Every matching edge pairs its own original box. Thus this is the actual simple triangulated sphere, with $$ V=3k-2,\qquad E=9k-12,\qquad F=6k-8,\qquad V-E+F=2.\tag{3} $$ The sphere topology and cyclic order are inherited from the original Morse construction, not inferred only from Euler characteristic. The [proved simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), §§4–5, therefore supplies the actual labeled convex ideal right-angled certificate and its two original cut balls. In particular (1) is a certified source diagram for every $k\geq3$. ## 2. The actual reflection packing and height coordinates The white sphere has the reflection automorphism $a_i\leftrightarrow b_i$ fixing $u,a_0,a_{k-1}$, and every $e_j$. It exchanges the first and last layers, with the original cyclic order reversed. Normalize the marked tangency $u-a_0$ to infinity, with the white disks $u$ and $a_0$ the outside half-planes below $Y=0$ and above $Y=2$. All ordinary disks lie inside this strip. This automorphism is realized by a reflection of the actual packing. One way to justify the needed uniqueness is the [proved strictly convex marked angle potential](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md): after fixing the common scale, its ordinary-face Hessian is a connected positive graph Laplacian. Equivalently, the maximum-ratio argument for two positive curvature solutions propagates strictness along every ordinary adjacency until it reaches a fixed normalization. The normalized radii then determine the contact-center development uniquely up to a horizontal Euclidean isometry. The orientation-reversing automorphism preserving both marked lines individually is therefore a vertical reflection; translate its axis to $X=0$. Write $a_i$ for both the named disk and its positive curvature when no confusion results. Then $a_i=b_i$. Put $L=k-1$. The fixed disks form the actual tangent chain $$ a_0\ (Y=2),\ e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_L,a_L,\ u\ (Y=0). $$ Their centers lie on $X=0$. Disjoint interiors, successive tangencies and the two endpoint lines force their intervals to be ordered strictly from top to bottom. Write $y_0=2$, and $y_j$ for the contact height between $e_j$ and the next fixed disk, $1\leq j\leq L$. Consequently $$ \begin{gathered} 2=y_0>y_1>\cdots>y_L>0,\\ \operatorname{radius}(e_j)=\frac{y_{j-1}-y_j}{2},\qquad \operatorname{radius}(a_L)=\frac{y_L}{2}. \end{gathered}\tag{4} $$ The fixed graph cycle $u-a_0-e_1-\cdots-e_L-a_L-u$ divides the original white sphere into two triangulated disks: all interior $a_i$ belong to one disk, all interior $b_i$ to the other. In the consistently oriented a-side development, the triangles $(a_i,e_i,e_{i+1})$ all lie on the same side of their downward-directed fixed-chain center edges. Their original cyclic orders therefore put every $a_i$ on the same side of $X=0$; one cannot choose these signs separately. The reflection puts all $b_i$ on the opposite side. Choose the a-side to be $X>0$. Thus for $1\leq i\leq L-1$ each reflected pair consists of two distinct disks, and the $a_i$ center is $(X_i,r_i)$ with $X_i>0$, where $r_i$ is its Euclidean radius. These disks are tangent to $u$ and to $e_i,e_{i+1}$. The first pair is also tangent to the upper line $a_0$, hence $r_1=1$. The last $a_L$ is the single axis disk. Elementary squared-distance tangency gives exactly $$ 2r_i=\frac{y_i(y_{i-1}-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i},\qquad X_i^2=\frac{y_{i-1}y_i(y_i-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i}.\tag{5} $$ For clarity, a circle of radius $r$ centered at $(X,r)$, tangent to the axis circle whose bottom/top heights are $U,V$, satisfies $X^2=V(2r-U)$. Applying this to the two neighboring fixed circles proves (5). No circle-packing approximation is used. ## 3. Exact scalar recurrence, with its branch fixed by geometry Define $$ z_j=\sqrt{1-\frac{y_j}{y_{j-1}}}\quad(1\leq j\leq L), \qquad z_0=z_{L+1}=0.\tag{6} $$ All actual $z_j$ lie strictly between $0$ and $1$. I claim $$ (1+z_{j-1})(1-z_j^2)(1+z_{j+1})=1, \qquad 1\leq j\leq L.\tag{7} $$ At $j=1$, $r_1=1$ and $y_0=2$ in (5) imply $z_2=z_1^2/(1-z_1^2)$, which is (7). At the other end, tangency of $a_{L-1}$ to $a_L$ at $X=0$ gives $X_{L-1}^2=2r_{L-1}y_L$. Equation (5) then gives $y_L=y_{L-2}-\sqrt{y_{L-2}(y_{L-2}-y_{L-1})}$, where the plus root is excluded by $y_L<y_{L-1}$. Hence $z_L^2=z_{L-1}/(1+z_{L-1})$, again (7). For an interior $j$ put $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, $w=z_{j+1}$, and $q=1-z^2$. The positive horizontal coordinates and radii of the two consecutive right-side disks, normalized by $y_{j-1}$, are $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{X_{j-1}}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac zp,& \frac{X_j}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{qw}{z},\\ \frac{2r_{j-1}}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{p^2+(1-p^2)z^2}{p^2},& \frac{2r_j}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{q[z^2+qw^2]}{z^2}. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ Their literal tangency is $(X_{j-1}-X_j)^2=4r_{j-1}r_j$. Substitution and cancellation of the positive factor $y_{j-1}^2/p^2$ gives $$ 1-2q(1+pw)+q^2(1-p^2)(1-w^2)=0.\tag{9} $$ The two possible roots are $$ q=\frac1{(1+p)(1+w)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad q=\frac1{(1-p)(1-w)}.\tag{10} $$ The second root is strictly greater than $1$ since $p,w>0$, whereas the actual height ratio $q$ lies in $(0,1)$. This excludes it before making any reconstruction or selecting a formal branch. The first root is precisely (7). The interior proof needs no order assumption on the two positive horizontal centers beyond the actual tangency. ## 4. A comparison principle gives the uniform 2/3 bound Set $v_j=\log(1+z_j)$, so $0<v_j<\log2$ and $v_0=v_{L+1}=0$. Define $$ f(v)=-v-\log(2-e^v). $$ Equation (7) becomes $$ f(v_j)=v_{j-1}+v_{j+1}.\tag{11} $$ On $[0,\log2)$, $f(0)=0$ and $$ f''(v)=\frac{2e^v}{(2-e^v)^2}>0. $$ In particular $f(tv)>t f(v)$ whenever $t>1$ and $0<v<tv<\log2$. For $L=3$ the explicit positive solution is $$ \begin{aligned} (z_1,z_2,z_3)&=(2/3,4/5,2/3),\\ (v_1,v_2,v_3)&=(\log(5/3),\log(9/5),\log(5/3)). \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ Direct substitution verifies all three equations and both zero boundary values. For any $L\geq3$, place this three-node vector at any three consecutive positions and extend it by zeros elsewhere, calling the resulting vector $s$. It satisfies $$ f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1}.\tag{13} $$ including at every zero position next to its support. If some $s_j>v_j$, let $t=\max_j(s_j/v_j)>1$ and choose an attaining index. There $s_j=tv_j$, so strict convexity gives $f(s_j)>t f(v_j)$. On the other hand (13) and the maximal-ratio property give $$ f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1} \leq t[v_{j-1}+v_{j+1}]=t f(v_j), $$ a contradiction. Thus $v$ dominates every translated three-node vector. Every index $1,\ldots,L$ belongs to such a placement, and the smallest nonzero seed entry is $\log(5/3)$. Therefore for every $k\geq4$, $$ z_j\geq\frac23\qquad\text{for every }j.\tag{14} $$ This comparison uses the actual packing solution already constructed from the source certificate. It does not require a shooting guess or a new nonlinear existence theorem. It also establishes the bound for every interior index, not just for the two ends. ## 5. Exact curvature comparison and strict source balance Let $E_j$ denote the curvature of $e_j$ and $A_i$ the curvature of $a_i$, with $A_0=0$. From (4),(5), with $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, and $D_0=p^2+z^2-p^2z^2>0$, equation (7) simplifies the two adjacent curvature ratios to $$ \frac{A_{j-1}}{E_j}=\frac{p^2z^2}{D_0},\qquad \frac{A_j}{E_j}=\frac{z^4(1+p)^2}{D_0}.\tag{15} $$ At $j=1$ the first ratio is $0$ and the second is $z_1^2$ because $r_1=1$; at $j=L$ the second formula uses the actual endpoint curvature $A_L=2/y_L$. Thus (15) includes both boundary cases with their original zero/axis interpretation, not a continued finite-circle formula imposed there. Adding gives $$ \frac{A_{j-1}+A_j}{E_j} =z_j^2\left[1+\frac{2p(1+p)z_j^2}{D_0}\right] \geq z_j^2\geq\frac49. $$ Consequently $$ \frac{E_j}{A_{j-1}+A_j}\leq\frac94.\tag{16} $$ at every first/final O port, uniformly for all $k\geq4$. The [zero-middle balance lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) uses the original absolutely normalized triangle action $Q$ and proves $$ Q(x,E,y)+Q(x,0,y)-\log E>\frac1{2500} \quad\text{if }x+y>0\text{ and }\frac E{x+y}\leq\frac94.\tag{17} $$ It retains either protected zero outer corner. Its proof is elementary: at fixed $A=x+y$ the cofactor Perron action increases with $P=xy$; the worst boundary value at $E/A=9/4$ is $(2/\pi)\operatorname{Ti}_2(2/3)-\log(3/2)$, which has an exact rational positive lower bound from four alternating $\operatorname{Ti}_2$ terms and the $\operatorname{atanh}$ series for the logarithm. Thus every O port passes the actual complete-radius balance condition. At each internal E port the two middle curvatures are equal, $A_j=B_j>0$, while both outer curvatures are positive. The original strict inequality $Q(x,A_j,y)>\tfrac12\log A_j$ gives $2Q(x,A_j,y)>\log A_j$. Thus every port in the literal diagram (1) satisfies the balance condition, using one common marked packing. No independent local radius optimization or entropy min/max exchange is involved. ## 6. General-theorem coverage, knot parity, and genuine width The general balanced-diagram long-filling theorem therefore applies to $D_k$ for every $k\geq4$ and every fixed half-twist pattern. For each fixed $k$ and source pattern there is a diagram-dependent threshold; all fixed filling powers beyond it may have independent signs and magnitudes. The family construction places no comparison constraint between these powers and no joint growing-twist/level limit. For knot parity put $\epsilon=+1$ or $-1$ on each box of the first $O$ layer, and zero on the other boxes. The first-layer zero-based transpositions $(1\ 2),(3\ 4),\ldots,(2k-3\ 2k-2)$ merge the $k$ initially separate cap cycles successively; each joins two previously different components. Every other box has even exponent and trivial endpoint permutation. Thus the filled main diagram is a knot for every integer full-twist vector. This is a direct computation on the original cups and slots. There are genuinely unbounded minimal bridge numbers inside this family, not merely arbitrarily wide presentations of two-bridge knots. Require additionally that every actual exponent $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$ be divisible by $3$. This is one residue class of $p_i$ modulo $3$, compatible with all retained parities and arbitrary independent large signs. The Fox-coloring crossing operator on ordered strand colors is $T=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ over $\mathbb F_3$; $(T-I)^2=0$ and $T^3=I$, for either signed crossing convention. Every whole box therefore acts identically on slot colors, though odd boxes still permute strand endpoints. The $k$ independent adjacent bottom-cup colors survive every top cap, so the knot has exactly $3^k$ Fox 3-colorings. Any $b$-bridge diagram has at most $3^b$ such colorings, because colors on its $b$ overpassing bridges determine every underpassing segment by the crossing rule. Reidemeister moves preserve colorings, so $b(K)\geq k$; the supplied plat gives $b(K)\leq k$. Hence $b(K)=k$ for this congruence subfamily. The independent full proof is the [Fox-coloring bridge certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md). The congruence condition is used only for this bridge lower bound. The analytic volume theorem still covers all independently long powers in the prescribed knot parity. Conversely, this explicit family is not claimed to exhaust balanced diagrams, all simple-white diagrams, or all $k$-bridge knots. The present uniform construction covers $k\geq4$; it makes no balance claim for the reduced $k=3$ word. ## Validation and scope The general statement follows analytically for every fixed $k\geq4$; finite packing samples are not used as its proof. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume_results.json) check the literal original Morse incidences, mark, reflection and knot parity at 38 widths, five symbolic tangency/root/curvature identities, the three rational seed equations, the rational balance bound, and all 44 circle-support pairs and eight port tests of the exact width-four seed. Root the audit code and replayed it with identical results. These finite checks support the source and algebra interfaces; the uniform comparison and the asymptotic invariant theorem are analytical conclusions, not extrapolations from sampled packings.
