title: Strict representation-volume loss from an actual kernel
status: Strict volume and regular smoothing theorem
text: # Strict representation-volume loss from an actual kernel 30 October 2026. This proves a geometric implication once the source capacity has been identified with the indicated representation volume. It does not identify smoothed blocks with JSJ pieces or supply that representation by itself. ## 1. Statement and the exact radial construction Let X=Gamma\H^3 be oriented, complete and finite-volume. Let rho:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its action on H^3. Its peripheral matrix images commute. In this note ker(rho) means the kernel of that PSL2 action, so a central sign is retained as acting trivially. Use the equivariant map f already constructed in the [general-peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md): on each sufficiently deep axis cusp it is exactly f(w,y)=gamma(chi(w)+log y), and on a parabolic cusp, after target normalization, it is f(w,y)=(A w,y). Here chi is real-linear, A is real-linear, and neither is assumed injective. Central peripheral images are included in the axis case chi=0. The parabolic affine height constant could be retained and does not affect the arguments. Extend f smoothly on the compact core. The conclusion is: Vol(rho)=Vol(X) => ker(rho) is trivial. (1) Orientation reversal gives the same statement for absolute equality. Together with the non-strict bound derived below from the same maps, a nontrivial kernel therefore gives |Vol(rho)|<Vol(X). For a REAL parameter s>2 put Z_s=integral_H3 exp(-s d(x,y))dy, nu_x^s=Z_s^-1 integral_H3 exp(-s d(x,y)) mu_(f(y))dy, where mu_z is the probability visual measure at z on the target ideal sphere. Z_s is independent of x. These are rho-equivariant probability measures. They have no atoms: each visual measure has none and Tonelli applies. Their Busemann potentials are finite, strictly convex, and proper, so their barycenters F_s(x) exist uniquely. Properness follows directly from nonatomicity: choose uniformly small spherical caps of mass<1/4, and compare Busemann growth along rays outside such a cap. Strict convexity follows because the support is not contained in the two endpoints of one geodesic. Thus F_s is rho-equivariant. Write v_xi=grad B_xi at F_s(x), eta_y=grad_x d(x,y), and use the joint probability measure in the definition of nu_x^s. Set H=E[v v^T], B=I-H, A=E[v eta^T]. The hyperbolic Busemann identity Hess B_xi=I-v_xi v_xi^T and differentiation of the barycenter equation give EXACTLY B DF_s=s A. (2) Radial symmetry on the DOMAIN gives E[eta eta^T]=I/3, regardless of f. Hence matrix Cauchy--Schwarz gives AA^T<=H/3 and |Jac F_s| <= s^3/(3sqrt3) sqrt(det H)/det(I-H) <= (s/2)^3. (3) The last scalar inequality holds for nonnegative eigenvalues lambda_1+lambda_2+lambda_3=1. Its maximum is attained only when all lambdas=1/3. To check this without an external rigidity theorem, differentiate log[det(I-H)/sqrt(det H)] under that constraint. An interior critical point has at most two distinct eigenvalues; on (t,t,1-2t) the ratio is 2(1-t)^2/sqrt(1-2t), minimized uniquely at t=1/3. The boundary liminf is at least2, larger than 8/(3sqrt3); other boundary approaches have infinite ratio. For s in (2,3], the first two x-derivatives of nu_x^s have uniformly bounded total variation. Indeed derivatives of exp(-s d) cost bounded powers of s and at second order at most coth d. The radial integral of its 1/d singularity is finite. More explicitly, Z_s=8pi/[s(s^2-4)], E_radial[coth d]=s/2, so the second-derivative norm is at most 3s^2/2. This also justifies differentiating the radial integral and gives the local C^2 estimates used below whenever B is uniformly positive. No global Lipschitz bound for F_s is asserted. ## 2. Cusp control, retaining the potentially large axial shift Fix s>2 throughout this section; its constants need not be uniform as s decreases to2. Let x=(w,y) lie in a chosen deep lifted cusp horoball H={y>Y}. Its kernel mass outside H is bounded by zeta(y)<=C_s y^(-(s-2)). (4) This follows because the distance from x to the complement is log(y/Y), while the radial tail is bounded by C_s exp[-(s-2)log(y/Y)]. First physical-w derivatives of the entire kernel have total variation at most s/y, since the physical vector partial_w has hyperbolic norm1/y. ### Axis cusp with nonzero chi Conditioning the kernel on H gives a rotationally symmetric mixture of visual measures whose centers lie on the SAME target axis. At a target point with distance rho from the axis, every rotationally symmetric probability measure has outward radial Busemann derivative at least tanh(rho/2). This can be checked one azimuthal circle at a time: its averaged potential is log[(cosh rho+sqrt(cosh^2 rho-b^2 sinh^2 rho))/2], 0<=b<=1, whose radial derivative is minimized at b=1 and equals tanh(rho/2). The outside mass contributes a gradient of norm at most zeta. The barycenter equation therefore implies dist(F_s(w,y),axis)<=C_s zeta(y). (5) This conclusion does NOT require control of its axial displacement. Here is the needed axial estimate. Scale domain coordinates by w'=w+y u, y'=y v. The conditional axis-center coordinate is chi(w)+log y + y chi(u)+log v, and its density in (u,v) is proportional to exp[-s d((0,1),(u,v))] du dv/v^3, v>Y/y. (6) The distribution of the center coordinate divided by y converges to that of chi(u). Its latter density is continuous, symmetric and strictly positive near zero. These facts follow by integrating the positive density in (6); tails are integrable because s>2. For clarity, the visual average of the Busemann potential on an axis at distance t from its visual center is h(t)=t coth t-1, h'(t)=coth t-t csch^2 t, h''(t)=2 csch^2 t(t coth t-1)>0. (7) Its derivative tends to the sign function. Thus the axial force of the conditioned measure, evaluated at chi(w)+log y+y a, converges to the strictly increasing median-force function of chi(u), uniformly on a small fixed a-interval. Equation (5) and the full barycenter equation imply that its axial force at the actual F_s is O(zeta). Explicitly, compare at the nearest axis point by radial parallel transport: the Busemann gradient has derivative norm at most1, and the normalized axial unit vectors differ by O(rho). Thus (5) changes that force component by only O(zeta). Consequently the actual axial coordinate lies in that central interval for all sufficiently large y. There is a quantitative lower bound which is stronger than a formal perturbation claim. Restrict v to [1,2], the coordinate of u orthogonal to chi to a fixed compact interval, and chi(u) to the interval of width2/y placing the axis center within distance1 of the actual axial coordinate. On this compact part of (6) the density is bounded below. It therefore has mass at least c_s/y. By (5), every such visual center is within target distance2 of F_s. Its visual measure has density bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of mu_(F_s). Since the visual average of Hess Busemann at its own basepoint is (2/3)I, B(F_s(w,y)) >= (c_s/y) I. (8) This bound survives arbitrary coupling of axial and transverse derivatives: it is a lower bound on the WHOLE Hessian, not just one diagonal entry. Combining (8), (2), and the raw physical-w kernel derivative bound gives ||partial_(w_j) F_s|| <= C_s. (9) One can also recover an axial displacement O(zeta y) relative to the conditioned axial barycenter from (7), but it need not tend to zero and is not used in (8)--(9). In particular this argument does not compare an O(zeta) perturbation to an O(1/y) gap as if it were small. In Fermi coordinates (rho,theta,t) about the target axis the invariant primitive of hyperbolic volume is beta_ax=(1/2)sinh^2 rho dtheta wedge dt, ||beta_ax||=(1/2)tanh rho. (10) It is invariant under every axial translation and rotation, and is smooth across the axis. Equations(5),(9) imply integral_(fundamental cusp torus at y)|F_s^*beta_ax| <=C_s zeta(y)->0. (11) ### Central axis and parabolic cusps When chi=0, after translating the target by log y, the conditioned measure converges in total variation to the mixture of visual measures at gamma(log v) with the full density(6). It has full support and a strictly positive barycenter Hessian. The outside mass tends to zero, so barycenters and Hessians converge in this normalization. Therefore the physical-w derivatives are O_s(1/y). The flux(11) again vanishes. For a parabolic cusp the same scaling changes f(w+y u,y v) to (A u,v) after the target translation by A w and dilation by y. The conditioned measure converges in total variation to the fixed full-support mixture at (A u,v). Its barycenter is at a fixed positive height and its Hessian is positive. The outside mass is o(1), so the full barycenter stays near it in scaled coordinates. In particular ||partial_(w_j)F_s||=O_s(1/y). The invariant primitive beta_par=-(1/2)height^-2 dx_1 wedge dx_2, ||beta_par||=1/2 then gives a cusp-torus flux O_s(y^-2). This includes rank-deficient A. The continuity used in these two normalized cases is elementary: the fixed nonatomic limit assigns mass less than1/8 to all sufficiently small spherical caps. Total-variation convergence makes their masses less than1/4 uniformly. The Busemann potentials are then uniformly proper by the same ray estimate as in section1, confining their barycenters to a compact set. On that set the potentials and their fixed derivatives converge; strict convexity gives the asserted barycenter and Hessian convergence. ### Identification of the integral The absolute Jacobian bound(3) makes F_s^*vol integrable. Compare it to the original cusp-adapted f on a truncated core using an equivariant homotopy. On each cusp the target volume form has the invariant primitive just displayed. The boundary homotopy integral is exactly the difference of the two primitive fluxes; paired fundamental sides cancel by invariance. Both fluxes tend to zero by (11) and its parabolic version, and by the explicit original f. Stokes therefore proves, separately for EACH fixed s>2, integral_X F_s^*vol = Vol(rho). (12) No limit in s was exchanged with a cusp estimate. Combining(3) and(12) gives directly, for every s>2, |Vol(rho)| <= (s/2)^3 Vol(X). Letting s decrease to2 proves the non-strict bound used here. Thus this note does not depend on the old smearing proof of that inequality; the linked peripheral note supplies the canonical regulator-volume normalization and the original cusp-adapted map. ## 3. Equality forces an isometric limit and excludes a kernel Assume Vol(rho)=Vol(X)>0 and take s_j decreasing to2. Equations(3),(12) give the nonnegative deficit integral_X [(s_j/2)^3-Jac F_(s_j)] =[(s_j/2)^3-1]Vol(X) ->0. (13) On any fixed compact ball there are points x_j tending along a subsequence to x_0 with Jac F_(s_j)(x_j)->1. The strict maximum in (3) forces H(x_j)->I/3. Moreover AA^T<=H/3 and (2) imply that all singular values of DF_(s_j)(x_j) tend to1; their product has positive sign. This uses no assumed convergence of rho or of the map values. Postcompose each map by a target isometry sending F_(s_j)(x_j) to one fixed point. Call the maps G_j. A kernel element of rho still acts trivially on EVERY G_j, even though these normalizing isometries can diverge. We only need this kernel-invariance, not convergence of the conjugated representations. There is one fixed source radius on which the G_j have uniform C^2 bounds. Indeed whenever B>=kappa I, equation(2) bounds DF by C/kappa; differentiating H bounds its derivative by C(1+||DF||). Starting at H near I/3, a fixed-radius bootstrap preserves B>=kappa. The uniform first and second measure-derivative bounds after(3), together with bounded target Busemann derivatives, then bound second derivatives of G_j. Arzela compactness gives a C^1 limit on that ball. On the ball the deficit tends to zero in L1 by(13), while C^1 compactness makes the Jacobians converge uniformly. The limiting Jacobian is1 everywhere. The strict matrix inequality in(3) now forces its derivative to be an orientation-preserving isometry at every point. Thus the limit is a local hyperbolic isometry. This convergence propagates across any fixed finite chain of overlapping source balls. At a point in the known overlap, uniform Jacobian convergence again forces H_j->I/3, so the same bootstrap opens the next ball with the same radius and bounded target values. Finite covers of paths, then a diagonal exhaustion, give a global local-isometry limit G_infinity:H^3->H^3. Equivalently, its initially fixed local isometry extends uniquely along paths; H^3 is simply connected and complete, so it is a global isometry. If gamma is in ker(rho), then G_j(gamma x)=G_j(x) exactly. Choose a compact path from x to gamma x and pass to this same limit. The global isometry would satisfy G_infinity(gamma x)=G_infinity(x), forcing gamma=1. This proves(1). Reducible escape cannot evade the argument: target normalization was explicit and kernel-invariance survives it. Negative maximal volume is handled by a fixed target orientation reversal before the construction. ## 4. The actual regular-smoothing corollary Suppose a nonempty set of untwisted crossing-circle components of the original connected certified augmented exterior X is deleted by the literal identity smoothing, and the resulting connected diagram has its OWN positive labeled right-angled certificate. Retain every remaining half twist and the original peripheral labels. Let Y be that actual complete smoothed exterior. Its core source capacity is Vol(Y)/(2pi), by the independently proved face-coefficient and coning normalization. No abstract existence theorem supplies this certificate. For example, when the entire literal smoothed white cellulation is one simple triangulated sphere with at least four vertices, the [capacity-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), section4, supplies exactly this labeled certificate by its proved Hall, disk-development, and supporting-halfspace argument. The topological operation is meridional Dehn filling of precisely the deleted crossing-circle components: their original crossing disks fix the slope, and the untwisted physical strands keep their original pairing. Compose the induced quotient pi_1(X)->pi_1(Y) with the actual complete holonomy of Y. This representation rho has nontrivial kernel: each deleted meridian was an essential nontrivial parabolic in the original certified complete exterior, and becomes trivial after filling. Its absolute representation volume is EXACTLY Vol(Y), with the same orientation. To check the normalization, first replace the axis cusp map gamma(chi(w)+log y) on each filled cusp by gamma(chi(w)), using an axis-valued homotopy and a collar. Its boundary homotopy has zero 3-volume, so the representation volume is unchanged. Unlike the old log y map, the new map extends continuously over the filled solid torus by its longitude core map. The extension has rank at most one and contributes zero volume. It does not require that the image core curve be embedded or even nontrivial. A filled core image may instead be parabolic. Because the killed meridian is in its kernel, its real-linear translation map A has rank at most one. Replace the cusp map (A w,y) by (A w,1). The vertical homotopy lies in the vertical plane over that one translation line, so its rank is at most two and its 3-volume is zero. The new map extends over the filled solid torus by the rank-one longitude map along that horocycle. A central image is included by taking A=0. Thus the same zero-volume filling-cap argument covers every possible commuting peripheral image of the actual quotient. On the remaining cusps keep the actual complete parabolic markings and their conical maps. The extended map from the filled topological exterior to Y induces the identity on its fundamental group and agrees with the actual peripheral homotopy classes. Since the universal cover of Y is contractible, it is properly homotopic to the actual identification with Y, using the conical maps on the remaining ends. It therefore has degree one. Integration of the target volume form, or Stokes on truncated cores followed by the already proved vanishing horospherical boundary terms, gives Vol(rho)=Vol(Y). Applying(1) and the bound just proved now yields the STRICT comparison Phi_sm=Vol(Y)/(2pi)<Vol(X)/(2pi)=Phi_old. (14) This needs neither a balanced split nor the original packing variables to remain fixed. At the attained smoothed packing the gap is positive. Replacing its marked zero variables by sufficiently small fixed positive ones preserves a strict gap, with their target exponents still zero. For a single port, the [actual polynomial small-circle insertion](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md) therefore gives the corresponding full-source small-h upper gap with cost C^(h-1). For a connected untwisted subset covered by the [simultaneous polynomial correspondence](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md), the cost is product C_i^(h_i-1), including protected outgoing faces and dependency cycles. These are applications of that exact source theorem; disconnected smoothings and signed small ports remain outside this corollary. ## 5. Scope still needed for degenerate smoothing To apply this geometric strictness result to the actual smoothed capacity one must construct a representation of the original complete source group whose volume is the sum of the proved capacity blocks, and show that the actual essential deleted crossing meridian lies in its kernel. For a connected certified hyperbolic smoothed exterior this is the literal filling quotient and its marked volume normalization. For a degenerate block decomposition it still requires the actual gluing/peripheral argument. No quantum source product or unproved JSJ identification is substituted here. ## 6. Literature coverage and validation Maximal representation-volume rigidity is established territory. The abstract of [Francaviglia, *Hyperbolic volume of representations of fundamental groups of cusped 3-manifolds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305275) states a stronger discrete-and-faithful conclusion at maximal volume. That reference is coverage and attribution only. The construction, matrix bound, cusp-flux control, and kernel-exclusion argument above are supplied here rather than importing that theorem's proof. No novelty claim is made for natural-map volume rigidity. The smoothing corollary requires its exact certificate, marking and untwisted polynomial-insertion hypotheses. It does not construct a representation from a degenerate block sum or bound signed small ports.

title: A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words
text: # A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words 30 October 2026. This extends the supplied [natural-map proof](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) to a varying sequence of representations. No quantum source estimate follows from this geometric statement alone. Let X=Gamma\H^3 be the fixed oriented finite-volume complete hyperbolic exterior, with its fixed marked complete PSL2 holonomy iota. For each n let rho_n:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its PSL2 action, and let Vol(rho_n) have the same canonical peripheral-regulator normalization as in that note. Then Vol(rho_n) -> Vol(X) implies, after passing to a subsequence and conjugating by orientation-preserving target isometries g_n, that g_n rho_n(gamma) g_n^-1 -> iota(gamma) (1) for every fixed gamma in Gamma, with one common conjugation and the actual marking. A fixed final conjugation is absorbed into g_n. For absolute volumes tending to Vol(X), pass to a constant-sign subsequence; the limit is either iota or its orientation-reversed conjugate. ## Proof with nonuniform cusp data Choose any s_n>2 tending to2. For rho_n choose its own cusp-adapted map f_n and its natural map F_n=F_(s_n,f_n). The cusp estimates are used separately at the fixed pair (s_n,rho_n), and prove exactly integral_X Jac F_n = Vol(rho_n). No uniform cusp constants, uniform cusp truncation, or exchange of a cusp limit with n is needed. The radial construction, however, gives uniform INTERIOR estimates independent of f_n: |Jac F_n| <= (s_n/2)^3, AA^T <= H/3, (I-H) DF_n=s_n A, ||D_x nu_n||_TV <= s_n, ||D_x^2 nu_n||_TV <= 3s_n^2/2. The latter bounds differentiate only the domain radial kernel. Therefore integral_X [(s_n/2)^3-Jac F_n] ->0. (2) This is a nonnegative deficit. On any fixed compact lifted ball it tends to zero in L1 as well: the projection has bounded finite multiplicity on that ball. Choose points with Jacobians tending to1. The strict matrix inequality forces H->I/3 and all singular values of DF_n to1 there. Normalize their target images by orientation-preserving isometries g_n. The same fixed-radius Hessian bootstrap as in the frozen note now gives uniform C2 bounds near those points: positivity of I-H controls DF_n; its first variation is bounded by C(1+||DF_n||), and the uniform second measure derivative controls D2F_n. A C1 subsequential limit has Jacobian1 everywhere by (2). The strict matrix inequality forces its derivative to be an orientation-preserving isometry. This convergence propagates along finite chains of overlapping fixed-radius balls; target values in the new ball stay bounded by the known overlap and derivative bound. A diagonal exhaustion gives G_n=g_n F_n -> G_infinity locally in C1 on H^3, where G_infinity is a global orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry. This construction does not assume compactness or irreducibility of the representations and does not claim that the normalizing g_n are bounded. It remains to use the equivariance, rather than only kernel invariance. Set rho'_n=g_n rho_n g_n^-1. For every fixed gamma and x, rho'_n(gamma) G_n(x)=G_n(gamma x). (3) Choose four fixed source points whose G_infinity-images are noncoplanar. Both sets of points in (3) converge. The isometries rho'_n(gamma) are precompact: their values at one fixed target point are bounded, because that point is o(1) from G_n(x), and the stabilizer of a point is compact. Every limiting isometry sends the four G_infinity(x)-points to their G_infinity(gamma x)-images. These determine an isometry uniquely, so rho'_n(gamma) -> G_infinity iota(gamma) G_infinity^-1. Absorb G_infinity^-1 in the common g_n. This proves (1) simultaneously for every fixed gamma; it also suffices to check a finite generating set. The SL2 central signs need not stabilize, and are immaterial for trace squared. No assertion about their lift is made. ## Uniform peripheral gap in the marked finite-dimensional problem Fix finitely many actual peripheral words m_1,...,m_b and delta>0. Suppose each iota(m_i) is parabolic or central, so tr^2 iota(m_i)=4. Then there is g=g(X,{m_i},delta)>0 such that EVERY actual SL2 representation satisfying max_i |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4| >= delta has |Vol(rho)| <= Vol(X)-g. (4) Otherwise a sequence violating every positive gap would have absolute volumes tending to Vol(X). Apply the proved compactness statement, passing to a constant-sign subsequence. Trace squared is continuous and conjugacy-invariant; its value at every selected word would tend to4 in either orientation, contradicting the fixed delta. This proof supplies a positive gap, not an effective numerical value. For a physical peripheral eigenvalue m=e^(pi i chi) with real chi, |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4|=4 sin^2(pi chi). Thus a selected real color parameter a fixed distance from the integer aliases meets (4), IF it is the eigenvalue of an actual representation whose volume controls the relevant source period. The latter implication is NOT proved here: it requires the source action, its cycle, its upper bound, and cancellation of all ordinary complementary terms to be established separately. This statement is not a bound on F_N or L_h. The fixed finite set is essential. One cannot take a supremum over ALL peripheral words whose exponents are allowed to grow with n: powers of a near-parabolic element may have trace far from ±2. The actual finite set of marked crossing-circle meridians is within the theorem's scope. ## Validation and scope The source action, period upper bound and cancellation of the complementary contribution remain separate requirements. The cusp normalization uses a fixed pair, whereas the interior estimates are representation-independent. The peripheral quantifier is over the specified finite set. The absolute-volume orientation alternative and source limitations remain as stated.

title: Volume equality for the original signed augmented source
text: # Volume equality for the original signed augmented source 30 October 2026. This note proves a uniform relative folded-channel estimate from the original finite continuants, then sums the actual half-twist phases. It concerns a fixed connected certified right-angled augmented diagram, at arbitrary fixed bridge width, through both parities and all sufficiently large levels. The external crossing-circle colors needed for long fillings are not the internal channels estimated here. ## 1. Exact source and statement Use the labeled geometric certificate and original marked normalization of the [untwisted theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). Let R be the number of crossing circles, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), and s0=d-2M in {0,1}. Retain any fixed vector of actual half twists epsilon_i in {0,1,-1}, and the separately specified exterior framing unit chi_(D,N). Write Y_D^epsilon for the certified complete augmented exterior with those recorded face pairings. Its volume is 2Vol(Q_D), unchanged by the half-twist pairings. The [exact marked coefficient identity](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md) is A_(D,N)^epsilon = chi_(D,N) N^R sum_(0<=a_i<=M) product_i[k_ai omega_ai^epsilon_i] F_N(a), F_N(a)=product_i beta_ai^2 * C_(N,a), (1) where C_(N,a) is the specified nonnegative face coefficient of product_i[D_ai,in D_ai,out P_(d-2ai)]. The two marked faces are set to zero; all the other face variables are shared. Here beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), omega_a=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], q=exp(pi i/N), k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. No trace normal is missing from (1): the original complete-circle coefficient is already included in these factors. This is the root complete source identity, not a differentiation of an off-grid root formula or a statement about individual generic-q normals. Let l_N be the unique positive critical radius of the all-maximal coefficient, with one finite face radius fixed by homogeneity. The [global coefficient theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) gives l_N -> l^geom. For circle i, let (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i) be its actual four face radii at l_N, including the prescribed zeros, and put A_i=x_i+y_i, C_i(l_N)=pi[ sqrt(b_i A_i+x_i y_i) +sqrt(c_i A_i+x_i y_i)]/A_i, Z_i,N=C_i(l_N)-pi i epsilon_i. (2) The actual zero patterns have A_i>0 and C_i>0. All their positive coordinates stay in compact sets, so Re Z_i,N has a uniform positive lower bound. Each square root of Z_i,N below has positive real part. We prove the stronger asymptotic A_(D,N)^epsilon =chi_(D,N) N^R F_N(M,...,M) product_i omega_M^epsilon_i *(pi N)^(R/2) product_i Z_i,N^(-1/2) *[1+o(1)]. (3) In particular the original signed source is nonzero for all sufficiently large N, and lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|A_(D,N)^epsilon| =2Vol(Q_D)=Vol(Y_D^epsilon). (4) All quantifiers hold for each fixed connected diagram with its actual nondegenerate labeled certificate; the diagram does not grow with N. Neither one main component nor a restricted graph grammar is required. The statement includes signed complete augmented link exteriors, including those whose main strands form one component, that satisfy the certificate. It does not assert the volume limit after independently long Dehn fillings of the crossing circles. ## 2. An endpoint-safe recurrence for the normalized determinant For one actual triangle write D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Z_a^b=beta_a D_a(x,b,y), e_a=Z_a^b/Z_(a-1)^b, A=x+y>0, theta=pi/N. The original tridiagonal entries and sine products give EXACTLY e_1=A+2b cos(theta), e_a=(1+tau_a)[A+2b cos(a theta)cos((a-1)theta)] -tau_a[A^2-4xy cos^2((a-1)theta)]/e_(a-1), tau_a=tan((a-1)theta)/tan(a theta), 2<=a<=M. (5) For clarity, beta_a/beta_(a-1) equals sin((2a-1)theta)sin(2a theta)/sin^2(a theta). Multiplying the literal continuant recurrence by this ratio gives (5); its off-diagonal product becomes tau_a times the displayed quadratic. No matrix of virtual size beyond M is used. Since 0<=tau_a<1 and 0<=4xy<=A^2, induction in (5) proves A<=e_a<=2A+4b. (6) If T_b=sqrt(bA+xy)=0, necessarily b=0 and xy=0, and e_a=A identically. This single-variable case is retained separately. In every other fixed zero pattern T_b/A is bounded above and below by positive constants on the positive radius compact. Set k=N/2-a, so k_min=N/2-M=(s0+1)/2, and set E_k=e_a/A, lambda_b=2pi T_b/A, E_k^*=exp(lambda_b k/N). Then (5) becomes, with tau=tan(k theta)/tan((k+1)theta), E_k=(1+tau)[1+(2b/A)sin(k theta)sin((k+1)theta)] -tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)]/E_(k+1). (7) Choose a sufficiently small fixed delta0>0. Substituting E^* in (7), its residual R_k satisfies uniformly for k_min<=k<=2delta0 N |R_k|<=C[k/N^2+k^3/N^3]. (8) Here is the cancellation behind this estimate. Uniform Taylor expansion gives tau=k/(k+1)+O(k/N^2). The two terms linear in k/N cancel. The quadratic k^2/N^2 terms cancel because lambda_b^2=4pi^2(b/A+xy/A^2). The finite k+1 offset leaves an O(k/N^2) term, which must not be dropped; the remaining Taylor terms are O(k^3/N^3). Taylor remainders are uniform when k theta is in the stated small compact interval, including k=1/2 and k=1. This approximate solution selects the actual positive solution without an asymptotic boundary condition. Start at k0 in [2delta0 N-2,2delta0 N] on the actual integer or half-integer lattice. By (6) both E_k0 and E_k0^* are bounded. Subtracting (7) for the two sequences gives an error recurrence with nonnegative multiplier K_k=tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)] /(E_(k+1)E_(k+1)^*) <=tau exp[-lambda_b(k+1)/N]. The exact telescope of the tau factors therefore bounds propagation from j to k by P_kj<=C(k/j) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N]. (9) For k<=delta0 N the starting error is exponentially small, because the recurrence was started at twice this cutoff. Summing (8) with (9) gives |E_k-E_k^*|<=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN), |log(e_a/A)-lambda_b k/N| <=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN). (10) Indeed the residual sum is at most Ck sum_(j>=k) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N](N^-2+j^2/N^3). For k<=sqrt(N), comparison with Gaussian integrals bounds it by Ck/N^(3/2)<=C/N. For k>=sqrt(N), write j=k+l and use j^2-k^2>=2kl to obtain C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]. This proves (10) at both physical fold endpoints. The exact constant case T_b=0 satisfies it with zero error. ## 3. The original circle has a relative folded packet For t=M-a>=0, the t removed pivots have k=k_min,...,k_min+t-1, hence sum k=t(t+s0)/2. Summing (10), Z_(M-t)^b/Z_M^b =A^(-t) exp[-pi T_b t(t+s0)/(AN)] *exp[O(t/N+t^3/N^2)]. (11) The original forced product changes by the EXACT paired factors P_(s0+2t)(x,y)/P_s0(x,y) =product_(k=k_min)^(k_min+t-1) [A^2-4xy sin^2(k theta)] =A^(2t) exp[O(t^3/N^2)]. (12) Combining the two triangles, the powers of A cancel. With B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)] =-C(x,b,c,y)t(t+s0)/N+O(t/N+t^3/N^2), C=pi(T_b+T_c)/A>0. (13) This is uniform on the stated radius compacts for 0<=t<=delta0 N. For any fixed 0<delta<1/6, it is a relative 1+o(1) packet uniformly for t<=N^(1/2+delta). Choosing delta0 smaller if necessary also gives B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)<=C0 exp[-c0 t^2/N] (0<=t<=delta0 N). (14) The O(t/N) term in (13) is absorbed by a constant plus a small multiple of t^2/N; the cubic term is absorbed by choosing delta0. No limiting-rate error has been used as a relative estimate. We also need finite radius derivatives, but not derivatives of the sharp error (10). For any actual principal matrix M_j at real positive radii, a fixed sufficiently small complex logarithmic radius change gives M_j(z)=M_j(0)^(1/2)(I+E)M_j(0)^(1/2), ||E||<1/4 uniformly j,N. This follows from its sum of positive semidefinite radius summands; zero faces stay zero. If v=M_j(0)^(-1/2)e_last, the ratio of the last inverse entries is v^*(I+E)^(-1)v/(v^*v)=1+O(||E||), uniformly even when M_j is ill-conditioned. Its reciprocal is the ratio of the original Schur pivots. Thus the marked logarithm of each pivot ratio is uniformly bounded on this polydisc. Cauchy estimates give all fixed logarithmic radius derivatives O(1). The paired factors in (12) have the same property near the fold. Consequently partial_z^j log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)]=O_j(t), j>=1, (15) uniformly there. This is a finite matrix estimate, including the single-variable and both maximal-fold cases. ## 4. Transfer from shared-radius values to actual coefficients Use the fixed n=R-1 log-radius gauge of the coefficient theorem. Put f_t(z)=log[product_i B_(N,M-ti)(l^geom exp z)]-d sum_f log l_f; the beta factors are constant in z. Let z_t be its unique positive critical radius, and z_0 that of the all-maximal vector. For max t_i<=N^(1/2+delta), the global coefficient theorem supplies both critical points in the same fixed neighborhood, with Hessians between cN and CN, fixed higher derivatives O(N), and its relative O(N^-1) coefficient formula uniformly. Its hypotheses hold since sum s_i=o(N). Write A_t=sum_i t_i(t_i+s0)/N, eta_t=C sum_i(t_i/N+t_i^3/N^2). Equation (13), uniformly on a real neighborhood, says f_t(z)-f_0(z) =-sum_i C_i(z)t_i(t_i+s0)/N+error, |error|<=eta_t. (16) The C_i have bounded first derivatives. Comparing the minimum of f_t with its value at z_0 and using the strong convexity of f_0 gives |z_t-z_0|<=C[A_t/N+sqrt(eta_t/N)], f_t(z_t)-f_0(z_0) =-sum_i C_i(z_0)t_i(t_i+s0)/N +O(eta_t+A_t^2/N). (17) For example, the lower comparison is obtained by completing the square in cN|z-z_0|^2-C A_t|z-z_0|-eta_t, while the upper comparison uses z=z_0. This argument does not differentiate the remainder in (16). By (15) and the O(N) third derivatives of f_0, the Hessians at their respective minima differ by O(sum_i t_i)+O(N|z_t-z_0|). Their determinant ratio therefore tends to1 uniformly in this window. For delta<1/6, eta_t=o(1), A_t^2/N=o(1), and the displacement in (17) is o(1). Restoring the uniform relative coefficient formulas yields the actual finite-source sector ratio F_N(M-t_1,...,M-t_R)/F_N(M,...,M) =exp[-sum_i C_i(l_N)t_i(t_i+s0)/N] *[1+o(1)] (18) uniformly on the whole stated window. All beta/CD normalization, the two physical fold offsets and the shared radius constraints have been retained. There is no continuous-color interpolation assumption. ## 5. The full signed channel sum, including its tails The original finite half-twist has the exact ratio omega_(M-t)/omega_M=exp[pi i t(t+s0)/N]. (19) Its (-1)^a factor cancels the apparent nearest-node alternation; it cannot be discarded before expanding the quadratic exponent. Multiply (18) by (19) and retain k_a from (1). If N is odd, k_M=1 and all other k_a=2, giving the full integer Gaussian. If N is even all k_a=2 and t(t+1)=(t+1/2)^2-1/4, giving the full half-integer Gaussian. In either case, uniformly for Z in compact subsets of Re Z>0, sum_(t>=0) k_(M-t) exp[-Z t(t+s0)/N] =sqrt(pi N)/sqrt(Z) *[1+o(1)], (20) where the notation on the left extends the corresponding multiplicity pattern to the infinite Gaussian lattice. This follows directly by the real Riemann sum for exp(-Zx^2), with Gaussian tail domination; the integral is sqrt(pi)/sqrt(Z) by analytic continuation from Z>0. The even factor exp(Z/4N) tends to1. Truncation at the window of (18) has exponentially small Gaussian tails. The uniform o(1) in (18) causes o(N^(R/2)) absolute error in the normalized signed sum, since its absolute Gaussian majorant has that order. The product of the nonzero integrals in (20) has order N^(R/2) with a fixed positive lower bound on its modulus after normalization. This proves a nonzero signed leading coefficient on the window. It remains to justify deleting every other original channel. Evaluate each positive coefficient at the SAME all-maximal critical radius l_N. The central coefficient formula gives, with n=R-1, F_N(M-t)/F_N(M) <=C N^(n/2) product_i[B_(N,M-ti)(l_N)/B_(N,M)(l_N)]. (21) When all t_i<=delta0 N but some t_i>N^(1/2+delta), (14) makes the right side at most a polynomial times exp(-cN^(2delta)). The polynomial number of labels and their bounded k factors are harmless. The proof of (14) started at 2delta0 N, so no unresolved initial continuant error remains at this mesoscopic cutoff. If some t_i>delta0 N, the [uniform all-channel common-radius theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) gives a strict macroscopic rate gap, uniformly at l_N -> l^geom. All other circle rates are bounded above by their fold values. Dividing by the central coefficient, whose rate is the same fold value, leaves exp(-cN+o(N)); again the number of labels is polynomial. All phases have modulus1. Thus neither tail affects the window's leading coefficient. Equations (18)--(21) establish (3). Finally the [absolute source coning anchor](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md) and the central coefficient theorem give N^-1 log F_N(M,...,M) -> Vol(Y_D^epsilon)/(2pi). Every additional factor in (3) is polynomial or a unit, and its displayed Gaussian product is nonzero. This proves (4). ## 6. Scope and verification This closes cancellation of the retained half-twist phases for the original complete augmented source under the stated general geometric certificate. It uses the exact marked compact-torus coefficient, not an assumed geometric intersection number or an independently normalized local thimble. The distinct external-color packet and its aliases needed to pass to independently long filled knots remain unproved by this theorem. No whole-source generic-q normal or growing-diagram uniformity is claimed. Focused audit: [original signed finite sources and folded factors](../experiments/audit_general_signed_augmented_source_volume.py), with [saved results](../experiments/general_signed_augmented_source_volume_results.json). At 90 digits it checks 1260 original normalized pivots, 280 direct original determinants, 180 exact single-summand pivots, 756 forced pairs and 756 circle ratios, 108 literal half-twist ratios and their fold multiplicities, and 476 complex-radius pivot comparisons. Ten whole original W/pi source sums at bridge widths two and three are compared with the independently summed face coefficients, retaining all phases, physical cups and the original marked cap. These finite source fixtures are normalization tests, not geometric certificates; their possible zeros do not assert a failure of the theorem's nondegenerate certificate hypothesis. Forty all-channel tetrahedral signed sums and 168 local folded packets are asymptotic diagnostics. The uniform estimates and noncancellation are proved above. The conclusion is the stated complete signed augmented-link equality; external filling colors remain separate.

title: A combinatorial geometric certificate for actual plats at every fixed width
status: Combinatorial certificate; actual examples at every fixed width
text: # A combinatorial geometric certificate for actual plats at every fixed width The subsequent [planar decoration theorem](actual_balanced_terminal_fan_volume.md) constructs balanced diagrams from every simple triangulated sphere with a chosen dual matching. It includes the full general Morse source and independently long fillings. The theorem below retains its own original scope. 31 October 2026. Combinatorial sufficient class and arbitrary-width construction. The main class is ALL actual flat plats with a simple white triangulated sphere. The explicit words below prove nonvacuity at every supplied width; they do not replace the general long-twist target by one family. ## 1. The existing simple-sphere construction applies to the actual source Start with an original ordered 2k-strand flat plat, k>=2, whose boxes cover all crossings, retaining the original cups, caps, marked top cap, cyclic port order and crossing-disk matching. Build its actual plane cubic matching graph and dual white triangular cellulation by the literal construction in [the actual matching geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), sections1–2, or equivalently by the original middle-gap sweep. Require that this white cellulation is a SIMPLE triangulated sphere: its vertices and edge occurrences are the actual regions and incidences, there are no loops or parallel edges, and every triangular cell has three distinct vertices. This is a finite combinatorial test on the supplied diagram, not an abstract graph chosen to imitate it. The nondegenerate sphere has at least four white vertices. Each source triangle still has exactly one designated matching edge. The already proved construction in [the simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), sections4–5, applies with this WHOLE sphere as its single simple block. Its fixed-boundary Hall argument gives an interior angle maximizer; Euclidean disk development is an embedding of degree1; the strict sector argument excludes unintended contacts. The contact circles of the shaded triangles then give all supporting halfspaces. Therefore it constructs a convex three-dimensional ideal right-angled polyhedron with exactly these LABELED white faces, shaded triangles, ideal contacts and cyclic orders. Separating triangles are allowed by that proof. Sections3–6 of [the actual matching geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md) identify this labeled medial sphere with the TWO actual projection/crossing-disk cut balls. They glue white faces across the copies and shaded triangles by the original retained half-twist permutations. The original meridians, primitive crossing-disk longitudes and source mark are retained. Their right-angle edge cycles and cusp decorations prove completeness for every fixed half-twist pattern. In particular the ACTUAL augmented exterior Y_(D,epsilon) is hyperbolic, with volume2Vol(Q). Its positive ideal triangulation supplies the general marked gluing certificate. Thus the simple-white test is a SUFFICIENT combinatorial geometric certificate for the exact class used by the right-angled source results. It is not a claim that every hyperbolic or prime twist-reduced plat satisfies this test. The older matching-geometry existence-gap paragraph can now be sharpened for this class using the later simple-block proof. No external alternating-link existence theorem is being imported. ## 2. Explicit literal words at all widths k>=3 Number adjacent strand slots from0 to2k-2. Put O_k=(1,3,...,2k-3), E_k=(0,2,...,2k-2), w_k=O_k E_k O_k, R=3k-2. (1) These are the original bottom-to-top box slots; no isotopy or abstract matching-to-plat adapter is needed. Denote the exterior by u, the k bottom odd-gap regions by a_0,...,a_(k-1), the k top odd-gap regions by b_0,...,b_(k-1), and the intermediate bounded even-gap regions by e_1,...,e_(k-1). Set e_0=e_k=u for formulas only. All the other named vertices are distinct. The literal gap sweep gives exactly these ordered four-face incidences: first O: (a_(j-1),u,e_j,a_j), 1<=j<=k-1; middle E: (e_j,a_j,b_j,e_(j+1)), 0<=j<=k-1; final O: (b_(j-1),e_j,u,b_j), 1<=j<=k-1. (2) The two cells of a quartet (x,b,c,y) are (x,b,y) and (x,y,c). The MAIN edges of its white sphere are exactly u-a_i, u-b_i (0<=i<=k-1), e_j-a_(j-1), e_j-a_j, e_j-b_(j-1), e_j-b_j (1<=j<=k-1), and its MATCHING edges are exactly a_(j-1)-a_j, b_(j-1)-b_j (1<=j<=k-1), u-e_1-e_2-...-e_(k-1)-u (the k cycle edges). (3) For k>=3 every listed edge has distinct endpoints and occurs only once in (3) and the MAIN list. In particular the matching cycle has length at least3. The triangles in (2) are distinct and every listed edge occurs in precisely two of them. These are the actual embedded sphere cells from the gap sweep, with vertices=3k, edges=9k-6, triangles=6k-4, vertices-edges+triangles=2. For example the MAIN edge e_j-a_(j-1) appears in the first-O output triangle and the preceding middle-E input triangle; the other three e_j MAIN incidences pair in the same way. The end u-a_0,u-a_(k-1) incidences close against the first and last middle-E cells, and the interior u-a_i incidences pair between consecutive first-O cells; the b incidences are reflected. The matching edges each pair the two triangles of their own original box. This checks the full labeled sphere, not just its Euler count. The protected mark can be the original first top cap: its two adjacent white faces are u,b_0, joined by MAIN. Consequently every w_k, k>=3, meets the simple-white certificate. ## 3. Width two and the knot parity For k=2 take the original slot word (1,0,1), with R=3. Its actual quartets are (1,0,3,2), (0,1,4,3), (4,3,0,2). The six triangles form the triangular bipyramid on vertices0,...,4, with equatorial triangle(0,2,3) and apices1,4. Thus its white sphere is simple and nondegenerate. The superficially similar word (1,0,2,1) must NOT be used for this argument: its two middle boxes produce parallel matching edges between the same white pair. For k>=3 put epsilon=+1 or -1 on EVERY box of the FIRST O layer, and zero on the other boxes. For k=2 use one nonzero epsilon on the first slot1 box and zero on the other two. Signs do not affect permutation. Starting with k disjoint cap components, the successive first-layer transpositions on slots1,3,...,2k-3 join component j to the already joined components0,...,j-1. At that step their two strands are in DIFFERENT components; cutting and cross-rejoining them merges those two cycles. Induction therefore gives ONE main component. Equivalently, the exact permutation is the product of the disjoint transpositions (1 2)(3 4)...(2k-3 2k-2), and the lower standard pairing together with the upper pairing transported by this permutation form a single alternating cycle. All full twists have trivial strand permutation. Thus for each such fixed parity pattern EVERY fixed integer vector p gives a knot with box exponents epsilon_i-2p_i. The [geometric long-filling theorem](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) gives a threshold T_geom(D,epsilon) for independently long signed p_i, with no comparability requirement. Each resulting knot has a k-bridge PRESENTATION, hence minimal bridge number at most k. This class construction alone does not prove b(K)=k. The later [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) does prove it when every box exponent is divisible by3, independently of the quantum asymptotic problem. ## 4. Exact coverage and threshold dependence The main geometric assertion applies to EVERY actual simple-white flat plat, not just (1). Its width and number/order of boxes may be arbitrary but are fixed before the quantum limit. Each fixed retained half-twist pattern and original primitive marking is part of D. The geometric threshold can depend on that full D, including cusp moduli, the positive-shape and framed-completion neighborhoods, and the common inverse-slope IFT polydisk. It is not asserted to depend only on k. A maximum over the finitely many cusp subsets gives one threshold for partial fillings as well, with unfilled inverse slopes0. The endpoint/complete-source results apply with their separately stated source and parity scopes. The later [balance theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) proves the full fixed long-filling limit under its additional geometric condition. The [one-end layer family](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes that condition for its actual words at every k>=2. This class construction alone does not prove balance or the quantum limit for all its diagrams. The direct fixed-root route needs no separate genuine-q normals; the older mixed-color route has its own hypotheses. Neither result identifies all essential hyperbolic plats with this class or certifies an arbitrary abstract matched graph as an original source. ## 5. Focused verification The [literal-source audit](../experiments/audit_general_simple_white_plat_class.py) and [recorded output](../experiments/general_simple_white_plat_class_results.json) check the original gap-sweep incidences, distinct triangle and edge occurrences, sphere counts and one-component parity at widths 2 through 30. At width 30 the source has 88 ports and 90 white vertices. These finite checks support the source dictionary; the symbolic formulas and construction above prove the arbitrary-width statement. They do not prove minimal bridge number or the phase-sensitive quantum filling limit.

title: Independent tangle depth at every initial bridge gap
status: General bridge-gap closure; all widths and fixed depths
text: # Independent tangle depth at every initial bridge gap theorem, 31 October 2026. The [one-end plat family](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) admits arbitrarily deep, independently chosen tangles at **every** first-layer bridge gap. The construction preserves its original marked cap and all core circle radii. It is checked on the literal source; it does not assert a theorem for arbitrary stacking or arbitrary plat diagrams. ## 1. The all-width, all-depth family Fix $k\geq2$, put $L=k-1$, and choose any fixed depth vector $\mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_L)$ with $m_j\geq0$. Number adjacent box slots from zero and set $s_j=2j-1$. Replace the $j$th box of the first $O$ layer by $$ (s_j,s_j+1)^{m_j}s_j.\tag{1} $$ Process $j=1,\ldots,L$ in its original order, retaining the middle $E^{\mathrm{right}}$ and final $O$ layers. The resulting literal word is $$ \left[\prod_{j=1}^{L}(2j-1,2j)^{m_j}(2j-1)\right] (2,4,\ldots,2L)(1,3,\ldots,2L-1), \qquad R=3k-3+2\sum_{j=1}^{L}m_j.\tag{2} $$ Products in (2) mean concatenation of slot lists in bottom-to-top order. A slot $s$ is conventional braid generator $\sigma_{s+1}$. Each added pair therefore means two independently powered boxes $\sigma_{2j}^{-2p}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2q}$. Retain the standard adjacent cups/caps and mark the first original top cap. The retained original first-$O$ boxes have fixed half twists $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$. All added boxes and the original middle/final layers have $\epsilon=0$. Every box has its own independent signed integer full-twist parameter. No region is merged, removed or assigned a dependent parameter. **Theorem.** Every word (2) is an original certified simple-white marked plat, and its actual complete packing satisfies $Q$-balance at every port. Its prescribed parity gives a knot. For every fixed $k$, depth vector and sign pattern, there is a threshold $T(k,\mathbf m,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that every independently signed fixed full-twist vector with all $|p_i|\geq T$ satisfies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|K_N\!\left(K_{k,\mathbf m}(\mathbf p)\right)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(S^3\setminus K_{k,\mathbf m}(\mathbf p)\right).\tag{3} $$ This is the full original normalized invariant, both level parities and the entire charge sum, through the [full-source balance theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md). Depths and twists are fixed before $N$ grows. No comparison between twist magnitudes, or threshold uniform in widths or depths, is asserted. Requiring every actual exponent to be divisible by $3$ gives a subfamily of minimal bridge number exactly $k$; that congruence is not required for (3). More generally, the same closure works for any balanced certified core with the initial $O$ layer, no slot $0$, the first-cap mark, and ordered actual initial curvatures $$ 0=A_0\leq A_1\leq\cdots\leq A_L. $$ The one-end cores satisfy strict inequalities, proved below. Neither this order nor balance is asserted for arbitrary initial-layer diagrams. ## 2. Exact simultaneous source dictionary The original first-$O$ port $j$ is $$ (a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),\tag{4} $$ where $u$ is exterior, $a_0$ is the protected first-cap face, and $a_j$ is ordinary for $j\geq1$. Set $A=a_{j-1}$ and identify the eventual last face of the local prefix with the old core face $B=a_j$. For $m_j=m>0$, let $f_0=u$ and let $b^{(0)}$ be the current bottom odd-gap face. Prefix pair $t$ has the exact original quartets $$ \begin{aligned} \text{slot }s_j &: (A,f_{t-1},f_t,b^{(t-1)}),\\ \text{slot }s_j+1 &: (f_t,b^{(t-1)},b^{(t)},u), \qquad1\leq t\leq m. \end{aligned}\tag{5} $$ The retained old box becomes $$ (A,f_m,e_j,b^{(m)}).\tag{6} $$ Identify old $B$ with $b^{(m)}$. If $m_j=0$, retain (4) unchanged. These formulas hold simultaneously. Before processing bridge $j$, earlier blocks have changed only gap positions up to $2j-1$. The face there is already the identified old $A$; the current bottom odd gap $2j+1$ has not changed. The even gaps $2j$ and $2j+2$ remain exterior $u$, the latter being exterior outright when $j=L$. The two local slots change only their own gaps. Thus (5) is the [original gap sweep](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md); after (6), the current middle gap contains old $e_j$. Induction on $j$ proves the entire first-layer dictionary. Every later core quartet is unchanged under these face identifications. The first marked face is never crossed because slot $0$ is absent. Introduce symbols $C_{j,n}$ with $C_{j,0}=a_j$. For depth $m$, $$ \begin{aligned} b^{(t)}&=C_{j,2(m-t)},& f_t&=C_{j,2(m-t)+1},\\ b^{(0)}&=C_{j,2m},& f_0&=u. \end{aligned}\tag{7} $$ Every positive-$n$ symbol is a distinct new source face. In particular the old core disk $a_j$ is preserved as $b^{(m)}$; the original bottom face is now the outermost new chain disk. The same indexing is used by the actual packing. ## 3. An exact chain inside a finite triangular gap Consider one original empty interstice $(A,u,B)$, with $u$ the baseline halfplane $Y\leq0$. First assume its actual curvatures satisfy $A,B>0$. Put the $A$-contact at $X=0$ and the $B$-contact on the positive side. The old radii are $1/A,1/B$, and the $B$ center is $(2/\sqrt{AB},1/B)$. Inside this actual bounded curvilinear interstice define, for $n\geq0$, $$ \begin{aligned} C_n&=(\sqrt B+n\sqrt A)^2,& r_n&=C_n^{-1},\\ X_n&=\frac{2}{\sqrt A(\sqrt B+n\sqrt A)},& Y_n&=r_n. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ The $n=0$ disk is old $B$. In the positive coordinate $\sqrt{C/A}$, this is the affine translation $\sqrt{C_n/A}=\sqrt{B/A}+n$. That identity describes the circle-chain construction; it is not an identification with a global quantum torsor or a theorem about its periods. Every disk is tangent to $u$ and old $A$. Consecutive disks obey $$ X_n-X_{n+1}=2\sqrt{r_nr_{n+1}}, $$ so their tangencies are exact. For nonconsecutive indices, the squared-distance support slack is $$ 4r_nr_\ell\bigl[(n-\ell)^2-1\bigr]>0.\tag{9} $$ Each next disk occupies the bounded gap toward the $A/u$ contact, with $0<X_{n+1}<X_n$. This actual contact order selects the sum of square roots in (8); the other algebraic branch is not used. The finite chain remains within the original empty interstice. Other old disks lie outside that face, and the new contact points avoid its three old vertices. Hence the only old finite contacts are with $A$, and with $B$ for $n=1$. These coordinates describe the existing original gap. They are not an independent conjugation of a local quantum word. In the common marked plane, if the $A$-contact is $X_A$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}(X_B-X_A)$, the actual new horizontal centers are $X_A+\sigma X_n$. Every old disk stays fixed. For $j=1$, old $A=a_0$ is the upper protected line and its curvature is zero. Use the [exact parallel-line construction](general_marked_unit_chain_filling_volume.md): normalize the lines to $Y=0,2$, so old $B$ has radius $1$, and add $2m$ unit disks in the empty complementary component. Here $C_n=B=1$. No finite-circle expression is divided by $A=0$. Insert $2m_j$ circles in each original first-$O$ triangular gap using (7)–(8). The original gap interiors are disjoint, including when their boundaries share old edges. The finite new disks remain in those gaps and avoid their old vertices, so different patches cannot overlap or acquire extra contacts. Each old triangular disk is replaced by the literal triangulated disk in (5)–(6), with the same boundary. The new sphere is simple, with exactly the source contact graph and cyclic order. The [proved packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), Sections 4–5, supplies its actual labeled right-angled certificate. Marked uniqueness identifies this unchanged-core packing with the complete source packing. ## 4. Balance at all new and modified ports The only order needed is $B\geq A\geq0$. For $A>0$, put $s=\sqrt{B/A}\geq1$, so $C_n/A=(s+n)^2$. A new odd port has outer curvatures $A,C_n$ for even $n\geq2$. Its positive middles are $C_{n-1},C_{n+1}$, except that the first prefix port replaces the latter by zero. Thus $$ \frac{\max\{\text{middles}\}}{A+C_n} \leq\frac{(s+n+1)^2}{1+(s+n)^2}\leq2,\tag{10} $$ because $2(1+t^2)-(t+1)^2=(t-1)^2\geq0$. A new even port has outers $C_{n+1},0$ and middles $C_n,C_{n+2}$, for even $n\geq0$. Hence $$ \frac{\max\{\text{middles}\}}{\text{sum of outers}} =\left(\frac{s+n+2}{s+n+1}\right)^2\leq\frac94.\tag{11} $$ Here $s+n+1\geq2$. Equivalently, $$ \frac94-\left(\frac{t+1}{t}\right)^2 =\frac{(t-2)(5t+2)}{4t^2}\geq0\qquad(t\geq2). $$ Apply the [zero-middle $9/4$ lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) after replacing the smaller middle by zero. The original $Q$ is nondecreasing in that middle, so (10)–(11) give strict balance at every new port, with gap $>1/2500$. For $A=0$, the parallel-line chain has all positive curvatures equal to $1$ and the same conclusion follows directly. At the retained old port, only its input middle changes from zero to $$ C_1=(\sqrt A+\sqrt B)^2\leq2(A+B).\tag{12} $$ The output middle $E=e_j$ stays fixed. Its new action sum is $Q(A,C_1,B)+Q(A,E,B)$. Against the new target $\log C_1$, use the $9/4$ lemma with $C_1/(A+B)\leq2$ and then monotonicity in $E$. Against the old target $\log E$, use monotonicity in the changed input middle and the old strict balance. This controls both targets without assuming $E\geq1$. It also covers $A=0$, where $C_1=B$. The protected zeros remain exact. Every later core port retains its weights and gap. The new minimum local margin is at least the smaller of the old minimum and $1/2500$, independently of depths. This does not assert a filling threshold uniform in the number of ports. ## 5. The one-end core has the required curvature order Normalize its marked lines to $Y=0,2$. Its a-side circles have centers $(X_i,r_i)$ and curvatures $A_i=1/r_i$. The actual cyclic list of contacts on the lower white line is $$ (a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_L,e_L,b_L,\ldots,b_1), $$ with the marked contact at infinity and the fixed $e_L$ contact at $X=0$. The embedded complete packing therefore gives $X_1>\cdots>X_L>0$. For $i<L$, the proved height formulas, with $z=z_i$ and $w=z_{i+1}$, give $$ \frac{X_i}{r_i}=\frac{2zw}{z^2+w^2-z^2w^2}\leq2,\tag{13} $$ since the denominator minus $zw$ is $(z-w)^2+zw(1-zw)\geq0$. Tangency gives $X_i-X_{i+1}=2\sqrt{r_ir_{i+1}}$. Its left side is strictly below $X_i\leq2r_i$, so $r_{i+1}<r_i$. Therefore $0=A_0<A_1<\cdots<A_L$. For $k=2$, there is no interior comparison and $A_1>0$ is immediate. An independent proof uses the already established curvature ratios in the [one-end theorem](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md), equation (14). For $2\leq j<L$, $$ \frac{A_j}{A_{j-1}} =\frac{z_j^2(1+z_{j-1})^2}{z_{j-1}^2}>\frac{16}{9}, $$ using $z_j\geq2/3$ and $0<z_{j-1}<1$. Its last positive-root identity gives $A_L>A_{L-1}$, and the small cases are exact. Thus the order does not depend only on a new reading of the contact diagram. ## 6. Full source, independent twists and bridge number Every inserted even exponent $-2p$ has identity endpoint permutation. All original odd first-$O$ boxes and other core boxes remain in their original order with their original half twists. The first marked cap is unchanged. Thus the original knot parity persists for arbitrary neighboring depth choices. The total framing character is that of the extended original diagram. Its exact normalization is retained; it is not identified numerically with the core's character, and no equality of old and new invariants is claimed. For each fixed width and depth vector, the certificate and balance meet the existing full-source theorem. Its entire spectral and charge argument proves (3) for all independent sufficiently long fixed signed twists, including the $2\sum_jm_j$ new parameters. This is not an inference from local angle volume or a selected contribution alone. The same proof permits arbitrary fixed added half twists $\epsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}$ **provided the resulting actual endpoint permutation gives a knot**. Their extended framing and peripheral conventions are retained. The white source dictionary and complete packing do not change under these retained half twists. The concrete even additions in (1) are the convenient subfamily that automatically preserves the old knot parity. If every full exponent is also a multiple of $3$, the [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) counts exactly $3^k$ colors on the standard cup/cap register. The supplied plat then has minimal bridge number exactly $k$. These congruences allow independent large parameters of either sign and preserve the prescribed parity. They are required only for the bridge lower bound. ## Validation and scope The construction gives arbitrary independent depth at every initial bridge gap; it does not cover arbitrary multilayer plat diagrams or prove a universal balance criterion. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_general_simultaneous_bridge_gap_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_simultaneous_bridge_gap_filling_volume_results.json) compare the closed dictionary against the original Morse compiler on 413 nonuniform charts, checking 11880 ports, 23760 triangles, 35640 edges, all marks and core permutations. Seven symbolic identities check tangent chains, support and inequalities. Twenty-five exact simultaneous seed packings supply 2333 circle/line supports, 168 new-port bounds and 32 modified targets. These checks supplement the general proof; finite samples do not establish its uniform or quantum conclusion.

title: A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope
text: # A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope 29 October 2026. The geometric equality step extends to EVERY oriented complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic three-manifold. No pretzel, alternating, bridge-width, polyhedral, or positive ideal-triangulation hypothesis is required. The proof below constructs the nearby local geometry explicitly by equivariant averages, rather than assuming a general deformation or Dehn filling theorem. This does NOT extend the proved original-source asymptotic to every knot. Section8 identifies the additional quantum hypotheses, their proved pretzel instance, and the currently missing broader source estimates. Neither a formal saddle nor a correct cusp Hessian supplies those inputs. ## 1. General geometric completion theorem Let M be an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with h torus cusps and geometric holonomy rho0. Fix primitive oriented bases (mu_i,lambda_i) of its actual peripheral groups. On each torus fix the complete Euclidean cusp coordinate, so its two holonomies are translations by a real-linearly independent pair of complex numbers. There is a neighborhood U of the complete FRAMED representation with the following property. A point of U consists of an actual representation rho: pi1(M) -> PSL(2,C) and, for each cusp, a common peripheral fixed flag close to its complete flag. Use a frame depending continuously on that flag to send it to infinity. The peripheral transformations are then complex similarities. Let U_i,V_i be the uniquely small logarithms of the complex similarity multipliers of mu_i,lambda_i, continued from zero at completeness. Select any subset F of cusps to fill. Suppose: 1. Every unfilled peripheral group is parabolic, so BOTH similarity multipliers are one. It remains nontrivial near rho0. 2. For each i in F, choose an arbitrary primitive integer pair (a_i,b_i) and a sign epsilon_i in {+1,-1}, and impose the ACTUAL log equation a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i. (1) Then rho descends to the Dehn filling of M along the actual slopes sigma_i=a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i. The descended representation is the holonomy of a positively oriented COMPLETE finite-volume hyperbolic metric on that filled topology. In particular it is discrete and faithful there. Any number of cusps may remain, including zero. The neighborhood U is fixed before the slopes: the conclusion applies to every slope tuple and framed representation satisfying these conditions inside U. It does NOT assert existence of such a representation for all slopes. Existence is supplied by the actual source branch in the proved application, and must be supplied in another application. For nearby representations, (1) itself forces the relevant slopes to be long. The proof is independent of a graph presentation and of any geometric triangulation existence theorem. Sections2--5 establish it directly. ## 2. A nearby equivariant developing map on every compact core Identify the universal cover of the complete M with H3, and write Gamma for pi1(M), acting by rho0. Choose a compact cusp-truncated core and a slightly larger compact collar. Cover that compact set by finitely many open balls which lift injectively to H3, and choose a smooth partition of unity subordinate to them. Write eta_(j,gamma) for the lifts using one chosen lift of the j-th ball. Thus sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x)=1, eta_(j,gamma)(rho0(delta)x)=eta_(j,delta^-1 gamma)(x). The sum is locally finite. On a fixed compact fundamental part only finitely many gamma occur. No freeness of the deformed action is assumed. Use the future unit hyperboloid in Minkowski space for H3. Form Y_rho(x)=sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x) rho(gamma) rho0(gamma)^-1 x, E_rho(x)=Y_rho(x)/sqrt(-<Y_rho(x),Y_rho(x)>). (2) Every summand is future timelike unit. A convex combination with nonnegative weights summing to one is future timelike, so normalization is defined. The Lorentz action of PSL(2,C) makes (2) unambiguous without choosing SL signs. Reindexing gamma gives exactly E_rho(rho0(delta)x)=rho(delta)E_rho(x). (3) At rho=rho0 every summand in (2) equals x, so E_rho0(x)=x. On the compact fundamental part, only finitely many matrices and derivatives of fixed smooth weights occur. Consequently E_rho tends to the identity in C1 as rho tends to rho0. For rho in one sufficiently small neighborhood, it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism. Equivariance then gives this property over the whole lifted compact core and collar. This is the needed compact-core deformation proof. It uses neither an unproved compatible geodesic mesh nor a subdivision that could invert thin tetrahedra. It also does not assume local character-variety rigidity. ## 3. An explicit positive similarity link and an entire cusp tail In one complete cusp write its cover as (w,t) in C x [t0,infinity), (w,t) -> (w+lambda,t), lambda in Lambda, dev0(w,t)=(w,exp(t)), where Lambda is the complete translation lattice. In the moving selected flag frame, denote the deformed affine action by A_rho(lambda)(z)=a_lambda z+b_lambda. It is a homomorphism from Lambda to Aff(C), tends to the original translation action, and all a_lambda are nonzero. Choose a smooth compactly supported nonnegative function eta on C with sum_(lambda in Lambda) eta(w-lambda)=1. Such eta is obtained from any bump whose translates cover a fundamental parallelogram by dividing by its positive periodic translate sum. Define d_rho(w)=sum_lambda eta(w-lambda) A_rho(lambda)(w-lambda). (4) Affine maps commute with convex combinations of total weight one, so d_rho(w+nu)=A_rho(nu)d_rho(w). (5) At completeness every term is w. On a fixed compact fundamental domain, d_rho is C1-close to w; its real Jacobian is therefore positive and nonzero. Equivariance propagates this local-diffeomorphism property everywhere. Thus (4) gives a genuine nonsingular similarity structure on the COMPACT cusp torus, not just a formal list of peripheral matrices. The developed images and Euclidean lengths of fixed generator paths are uniformly bounded near completeness. Let chi_rho:C->R be the real-linear extension of the character lambda -> log|a_lambda|. The map F_rho(w,t)=(d_rho(w),exp(t+chi_rho(w))) (6) is exactly rho-equivariant in upper half-space: its horizontal and vertical coordinates transform by a_lambda z+b_lambda and |a_lambda|y. Its differential is triangular with positive determinant exp(t+chi_rho(w)) det_R Dd_rho(w). Hence it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism for EVERY t>=t0. At completeness it is dev0. Restore the continuously varying flag frame when viewing (6) in the global target H3. Define it on one chosen lift of each disjoint cusp neighborhood and propagate by rho-equivariance to the other lifts. The exact peripheral equivariance makes the coset representative irrelevant, so this gives a well-defined map on the entire lifted end. On a fixed compact cusp collar it is C1-close to the original developing map. Interpolate E_rho and F_rho by the unique hyperbolic geodesic between their values, with a smooth Gamma-invariant cutoff in t. The interpolation is rho-equivariant and is C1-close to the identity on that compact collar. Thus it too is a positive local diffeomorphism after one further uniform shrink of U. Set it equal to E_rho on the compact part and F_rho on each deep tail. We have now constructed a global rho-equivariant developing LOCAL DIFFEOMORPHISM on the ideal-end-deleted original manifold. Pulling back the H3 metric yields an actual oriented curvature-minus-one metric. There are no polyhedral edge or vertex singularities to check: the map is a smooth local diffeomorphism everywhere at finite points. The construction is simultaneous at all finitely many cusps. It works on a single neighborhood of the complete framed representation, with no comparison between different deformation sizes or slopes. ## 4. The small multiplier logs are the actual log-link periods At a filled cusp (1) ensures at least one multiplier is nontrivial. Commutativity of affine peripheral maps implies that they have a common finite fixed point q in addition to infinity. For a generator with a!=1, this is q=b/(1-a). The two original generator translations are nonzero. As the representation approaches completeness, at least one such formula therefore gives |q|->infinity, uniformly over the small framed neighborhood with its parabolic locus removed. The image of an ENTIRE closed fundamental parallelogram under d_rho is uniformly bounded by the compact C1 estimate in section3. Fixed generator paths also have uniformly bounded developed images and Euclidean lengths. For U sufficiently small the whole parallelogram image misses q, including its interior, not only its boundary paths. Equivariance and the fact that every peripheral map fixes q then show that the ENTIRE development misses q. On the simply connected link cover choose f=Log(d_rho-q). The differential df is invariant under deck transformations and is invertible as a REAL two-dimensional differential: d_rho is a positive local diffeomorphism and the logarithm has nonzero complex derivative. Thus |df|^2 descends to a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the compact link torus. It is complete. Its lifted local isometry f is globally one-to-one onto C: lift every Euclidean line segment by completeness to get a covering of C, which is simply connected. Its periods therefore form an injective rank-two translation lattice. For each fixed generator path of length at most L and image in |d|<=R, |Delta f|<=L/(|q|-R) ->0. (7) The endpoint affine action gives exp(Delta_mu f)=exp(U) and similarly for V. Their differences are integer multiples of 2pi i. Both the actual increments in (7) and the prescribed small multiplier logs tend to zero, so these integers are EXACTLY zero in U: Delta_mu f=U, Delta_lambda f=V. (8) The neighborhood needed for (8) is independent of the slopes, because one first proves (8) for the FIXED basis before multiplying by a_i,b_i. No diagonalizing-frame singularity or hidden large winding is allowed. SL eigenvalue signs must first be centered to these projective geometric logs; an old longitude spin is not an extra geometric rotation. For completeness, q need not be bounded by the inverse of one chosen coordinate if that coordinate vanishes. Choose either generator with nonunit multiplier. Each numerator stays bounded away from zero, and max(|a_mu-1|,|a_lambda-1|) tends uniformly to zero. This proves the uniform |q|->infinity statement even when one generator is parabolic. ## 5. Primitive filling gives a complete smooth hyperbolic manifold Translate q to zero. Then d_rho=e^f. On the compact link quotient the positive function exp(t0+chi_rho(w))/|d_rho(w)-q| is bounded above: numerator and denominator transform by the same |a_lambda|. Thus the explicit end (6) contains the ENTIRE equivariant epigraph y>A|d-q| for some finite A. There is no unproved assumption that an abstract cusp link is realized by an actual full geometric end. About the axis 0--infinity put r=y/|d-q| and use R=asinh(1/r), theta=Im f, X=Re f+(1/2)log(1+r^2). Direct substitution into the upper-half-space metric gives ds^2=dR^2+cosh(R)^2 dX^2+sinh(R)^2 dtheta^2. (9) The epigraph contains the whole punctured tube 0<R<R0. A log period L acts by (X,theta)->(X+Re L,theta+Im L). By (1),(8), the actual primitive slope has period 2pi i epsilon. Choose integers c,d with ad-bc=1. Its complementary primitive period cU+dV has nonzero real part, since the log-link period lattice has real rank two. Adding R=0 in (9) is therefore an ordinary smooth hyperbolic solid torus, with meridian EXACTLY a mu+b lambda. The angular period is 2pi, not a multiple or a merely exponentiated relation. The affine holonomy of that meridian is the identity, since it has multiplier one and fixes both q and infinity. Thus rho descends to the actual filled fundamental group. Either epsilon sign changes the orientation of the meridian parameter, not the positive orientation of the metric. At an unfilled cusp all a_lambda=1. Formula (4) is an ordinary translation-equivariant local diffeomorphism. Its compact Euclidean link is complete, so its lifted development is the Euclidean plane. Here chi=0 and (6) contains a full horoball quotient: the cusp is complete and has finite volume. The remaining middle region is compact. The finitely many attached bounded-radius solid tori and the ordinary unfilled cusps prove that the whole filled metric is complete and finite-volume. Its complete universal developing cover is H3: lift geodesic segments under its complete local isometry to obtain a covering of simply connected H3. Consequently the descended holonomy is discrete and faithful. This proves the theorem in section1 without importing a deformation, Dehn filling, discrete-faithfulness, or character-uniqueness theorem. ## 6. Absolute regulator calibration for any such source branch Let rho_z now be an actual connected marked representation family near rho0, and use the small squared peripheral logs U_i,V_i above. The elementary marked Bloch boundary/fundamental-chain calculation used in [the general peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) and [the source regulator proof](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) is independent of the diagram and number of cusps. In these coordinates it says d Vol(rho_z)=(1/2)sum_i [Re V_i dIm U_i -Re U_i dIm V_i]. (10) Here Vol(rho) is the absolute representation volume of the SAME oriented fundamental class and cusp eigenflags. One way to check the factor is to use eigenlogs u=U/2,v=V/2 (with their fixed central signs): the boundary is -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i, so the Bloch--Wigner differential is 2 sum(Re v dIm u-Re u dIm v), exactly (10). Distinct boundary tori have zero mutual intersection pairing. No equal-color assumption enters. Suppose a holomorphic source potential F on this marked branch has dF=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i, Im F(0)=Vol(M). (11) These are hypotheses about the actual peripheral connection and its absolute COMPLETE anchor, not just about its Hessian. Define D_F=Im F-(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (12) Direct differentiation of (11) gives the right side of (10). Both functions equal Vol(M) at the complete point. Therefore throughout the connected marked branch D_F=Vol(rho_z). (13) This is an absolute identity. It does not reset logarithms on loops, splice different character lifts at a projected node, or infer a constant from a matching stationary polynomial. Nonzero spin terms must be retained when converting the literal source to the centered form (11); they cancel only in the paired expression (12). At an actual filled point from section1, the representation volume in (13) is the volume of its constructed complete geometric metric. If comparing with any other complete hyperbolic metric on the same marked oriented filled topology, apply the independently proved representation-volume inequality in BOTH directions. Their volumes are equal. No unproved equality case or imported rigidity theorem is needed to identify (13) with its usual hyperbolic volume. The finite filling-chain normalization is also diagram-independent: replace the old cusp map by its axis-valued comparison, whose shared conical boundary homotopy has volume O(Y^-2); then extend the SAME finite boundary triangulation through the solid torus with every vertex on that axis. All added tetrahedra have zero volume. This is the compatible construction in the cited peripheral/source proofs; putting only unrelated new vertices on the axis would not suffice. ## 7. Arbitrary primitive filling action, with the exact boundary term When a source branch has local U coordinates and (11), a primitive slope a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i with b_i!=0 has filling potential F_sigma(U)=F(U)+sum_(i in F) [a_i U_i^2/(4b_i)-pi i epsilon_i U_i/b_i]. (14) Its U_i derivative is (a_i U_i+b_i V_i-2pi i epsilon_i)/(2b_i). At its stationary filling point and with unfilled cusps complete, Im F_sigma =Im F-(1/2)sum_(i in F) Re U_i Im V_i =Vol(rho)=Vol(M(sigma)). (15) Indeed Im V_i=(2pi epsilon_i-a_i Im U_i)/b_i, which proves (15) without deleting a complex endpoint term. Constants already known to be real do not affect (15), but remain in any exact period formula. If b=0, primitivity forces |a|=1 and (1) cannot occur with small U; there is therefore no omitted near-complete filling in this chart. Equivalently one may change the primitive basis and its potential. For the existing convention U=-z,V=-2ell,a=1,b=p, epsilon=-m, (14) is G(z)+(z-2pi i m)^2/(4p) up to a REAL constant. This recovers the exact chirp/source formula, including its factor two and its retained longitude spin. ## 8. The conditional QUANTUM bridge, and what is actually proved The geometric theorem is unconditional for every actual framed representation satisfying section1. To prove the volume conjecture for a new original knot/source family one must additionally prove: * An exact original-source construction or selected-cycle argument supplies the ACTUAL near-complete representation of the base group, with the literal caps, all port equations, chosen eigenflags and true primitive preferred peripheral markings. * The selected parameter point exists in the fixed neighborhood, with all unfilled cusps complete and the actual small log equations (1) with unit charges.
