The scale and descendant are residues of ACTUAL operators: \[ U=\operatorname{Res}c_+f_\alpha dz,\quad m= rac1N\operatorname{Res}c_{U,m}(N-2z\partial_z)f_\alpha dz, \qquad c_+=2^{-N}\sum_{k=0}^Nz^{-k-1}. 	ag{6.2} \] Consequently the already proved framing identity Omega_cut=(A/N)dlogU wedge dm is an explicit expression in global source/descendant residue pairings, on its marked Kummer cover. The Berry form is still N dlogalpha and flat on this Borel; it has not been substituted for Omega_cut. There is an explicit relative framing coordinate too. On the same marked cover put s=C alpha^2, r_frame=(1+m)/2+D alpha^2, and \[ 	au=r_{\mathrm{frame}}/s = rac{1+m}{2C\alpha^2}+ rac DC, \quad A=1/(1+s),\qquad d	au\wedge d\log A=\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}.	ag{6.3} \] At C=alpha=1,D=0, one has s=1,A=1/2 and tau=(1+m)/2. Thus the literal framing interval 0<=tau<=1 is m in [-1,1], with d tau=dm/2. Averaging its ROOT global class c_(1,m) gives the uniform row class \[ c_{\mathrm{uni}}(z)= rac1{N+1}\sum_{k=0}^N  rac{z^{-k-1}}{ inom Nk}.	ag{6.4} \] The whole extension of this relative identity is Section 7, with its original pairing density retained. The actual first-normal old cut clock also has a global class here. Its previously proved value on every pure-power source is ((a+b)/2)^N/[N(1-Q_N)]. Since those source vectors span the actual Fr module, the unique linear extension of this SELECTED coherent-family character is represented by c_+(z)/[N(1-Q_N)]. Pairing it with f_alpha returns U/[N(1-Q_N)]. This localizes the actual SCALE normal class globally; it neither equates the framing A with an old clock nor supplies a second internal geometric-current map. The original normal construction has source-dependent pairing-unit ratios. No equality of its full operator action on arbitrary Fr matrices follows merely from this coherent-family character. For the original whole q-source, use (1.3) on its actual coefficients psi_s(q),lambda_s(q), including the actual units U_s(q,m). Formula (6.1) is their root restriction, NOT their replacement before quantum differentiation. Their whole source and dual remain global Čech data. ## 7. A whole retained-weight interval gives the uniform co-source Here is a function identity before any normal-jet restriction. Work over the actual rational q-coefficients near q_N on one residue string. Put E_N(q)=tau E^(N)(q), F_N(q)=F^(N)(q), and \[  egin{split} \psi_q&=\exp(F_N(q))v_0,\ c_k(q)v_k^*&=v_0^*E_N(q)^k/k!,\ \widetilde\lambda_q(m)&=\sum_{k=0}^N c_k(q)\left( rac{1+m}{2}ight)^{N-k} \left( rac{1-m}{2}ight)^k v_k^*,\ U_q(m)&=\widetilde\lambda_q(m)\psi_q,\qquad \lambda_q(m)=\widetilde\lambda_q(m)/U_q(m). \end{split} 	ag{7.1} \] Every c_k and psi coefficient comes from the original integral divided matrices. At the root c_k=binom(N,k), psi_q=sum v_k and U_q(m)=1. Thus U is an actual pairing unit formally, and analytically on the compact interval for q sufficiently close to q_N at fixed N. The literal beta integral, proved by repeated elementary integration of t^a(1-t)^b, is \[  rac12\int_{-1}^1 \left( rac{1+m}{2}ight)^{N-k} \left( rac{1-m}{2}ight)^kdm = rac1{(N+1) inom Nk}. 	ag{7.2} \] Therefore the WHOLE weighted interval co-source is rational: \[ L_q= rac12\int_{-1}^1 U_q(m)\lambda_q(m)dm =\sum_k rac{c_k(q)}{(N+1) inom Nk}v_k^*. 	ag{7.3} \] Cancellation of U in (7.3) is an identity of the WHOLE rational integrand, before integration or normal specialization. It retains that pairing line as the integration density. At q_N the row is the uniform row lambda_uni=(sum v_k^*)/(N+1). This uniform ROW is distinct from the full trace (1.5). With its uniform source it agrees with the trace on diagonal arrays, and both give the actual closed scalar period. No equality on arbitrary off-diagonal Green insertions is inferred from that fact. Nor is the uniform Fr row the original head-uniform/coherent-Fr coupon after the cyclotomic diagonal projector. Its Fr indices 0 and N both map to head index S=0, so raw Fr uniform averaging counts that head endpoint twice. A literal match to the old head co-source requires the degree-elevation/endpoint map or its retained adapter. The root-original coherent Fr row has binomial weights; it is a different co-source from lambda_uni. The root-identity gauge below compares the WEIGHTED-INTERVAL Fr uniform dual with the Fr uniform dual, not automatically with that binomial coupon. Put V_q=L_q psi_q and nu_q=lambda_uni psi_q. Both are actual rational units with root value ONE. The normalized retained-weight interval is L_q/V_q. The normalized uniform dual on the SAME actual source is lambda_uni/nu_q. Define \[ \Delta_q=L_q/V_q-\lambda_{\mathrm{uni}}/
u_q,\qquad K_q=I+\psi_q\Delta_q. 	ag{7.4} \] Since Delta_q psi_q=0, these are exact whole identities: \[  egin{split} K_q^{-1}&=I-\psi_q\Delta_q,\quad K_{q_N}=I,\ K_q\psi_q&=\psi_q,\qquad (\lambda_{\mathrm{uni}}/
u_q)K_q=L_q/V_q . \end{split} 	ag{7.5} \] Thus (7.4) is a concrete regular RATIONAL unipotent source-preserving gauge between the two whole co-sources. It is not an inference from equality of their root jets. The marked scale alpha^N is retained by multiplying psi and the dual inversely; K itself is unchanged. To compare network operators one must conjugate them too. In the convention v_old=K_q v_new, transport becomes K_q^(-1)T_old sigma(K_q), co-source becomes ell_old K_q, and a connection becomes K_q^(-1)Omega_old K_q+K_q^(-1)dK_q. Its last term is part of the actual comparison. Formula (7.5) alone is not a proof of geometric current intertwining. The chosen source gauge is not declared PBW-degree-preserving, nor is its growing-N presentation declared uniformly bounded. The UNWEIGHTED normalized integral int lambda_q(m)dm/2 is a different relative rational-function period, potentially logarithmic. No rationality or equality to (7.3) is asserted. The source density U_q(m)/V_q is essential off the root; setting it to one would lose exact actual quantum-normal data. ## 8. Precise category and remaining geometric identification At fixed N this construction works on whole algebraic source and dual bundles over the actual rational coefficient ring, retaining its marked units, phase and Kummer charts. Operators are global differential operators and bundle automorphisms, with explicit Čech lifts. Different lifts of the same actual matrix are identified by the concrete cochain homotopies (2.2)--(3.5). Relative periods retain their density and endpoints; unweighted periods need not be rational sections. Quantum jets are restrictions of these already specified whole identities. Tensoring the displayed two-chart complexes handles all Fr strands of an actual braid: source sections are multihomogeneous polynomials, dual classes are products of the Laurent basis elements, and the matrix pairing is their ordered multiple residue. The local strict operator lifts compose; identities in finite matrices lift up the explicit tensor contractions. Thus actual whole R/Green operators, their source units and named finite endpoints have a GLOBAL source model, not only a formal coordinate patch at the optimizer. The further map to the INTERNAL geometric framing interval still requires its actual Ward/current comparison, including the charged head neighbors and normal source corrections. The [actual relative endpoint analysis](actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint_period.md) also shows that exact endpoint transport can have exponentially large metric norm. Global algebraic localization and equality of source pairings do not supply a tame norm or a nonzero selected geometric contribution. [Exact global source/Čech audit](../experiments/audit_global_frobenius_cech_source.py). [Results](../experiments/global_frobenius_cech_source_results.json). title: The global Green cut tails and the exact wall-transport residual
text: # The global Green cut tails and the exact wall-transport residual Research proof and independent source audit, 27 October 2026. Integer-flow conservation excludes a direct bare wall at the final cut before summing the two framing variables. It does not discard internal returning wall excursions or the boundary tails produced by Green shifts. This note records those tails, the exact residual after the new memory contraction, and the source factor a common wall comparison would have to produce. These are actual source/current tests, not a geometric-period identification or a use of scalarity of the closed knot operator. ## 1. Primitive flow elimination preserves the unsummed cut grading Each original positive crossing sends (a,b) to (b+k,a-k), and each negative crossing sends it to (b-k,a+k). Thus every literal crossing term preserves the integer sum of positions, for each transfer separately. All original diagonal pivots, Cartan phases, zero-framing scalars and scalar moment insertions have degree zero. Close every strand except the marked cut. Equality of input and output positions on the closed strands forces equality at the cut by the same integer sum. This is TERMWISE: it uses neither an internal state sum nor a Schur argument. For a knot, primitive flow elimination uses the unit permutation cofactor already proved in [the actual geometric coefficient model](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Keep a=cut position and b=one other framing flow unsummed, and denote all remaining free flows by t. The actual kernel therefore has the literal form \[ I(a,b,t)E_{aa}. \tag{1} \] Scalar Green moments preserve this diagonal matrix index. The external meridian Ore shifts also preserve it. Hence the direct final-cut image under degree elevation is diagonal and has zero coefficient of the EXTRA root wall E_(N,0). The same statement holds after the full Clebsch word, with all caps and lower excursions retained: its upper final cut is E_N of this original diagonal matrix. It is not a claim about an upper-only word. The proof survives exact transverse SUMMATION while a,b remain unsummed. A formal Gaussian comparison must still preserve its external shifts, support boundaries and relative source; a bare interior Gaussian sector does not include those boundaries. There is a useful stronger actual charge rule. Set deg F=+1, deg E=-1 and deg K=0. The coproduct is homogeneous in total degree and the antipode preserves degree. Thus the TRUE Hopf adjoint of a homogeneous h of degree d, applied to a degree-zero word or scalar Green kernel, has degree d. Diagonal pivotal partial trace preserves the remaining cut degree, coefficientwise in EVERY actual q-normal order. This applies to divided powers and their mixed coproduct terms as well. On the actual high color r=N the fixed-head Fr wall E_(N,0) changes the physical cut position J=NR+S by N^2. Therefore its selected head-00 coefficient is absent for |d|<N^2. In particular a SINGLE divided E^(N) or F^(N) current cannot create that direct cut coefficient. The full wall head block has charges N^2+(S_out-S_in), so is absent whenever |d|<N^2-N+1. Dense source coupons inserted INSIDE a word change this charge budget; an external linear co-source does not. Under a whole source gauge the grading and every endpoint must be conjugated together rather than freezing the old grading on new matrices. ## 2. The literal cut-window map has two missing boundary rows Green currents are zero-extended arrays on ALL integer free flows. A cut-index shift can therefore create tails outside 0,...,N-1. For any such finite array retain the matrix and two exterior tails \[ C_Nf(b,t)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}f(a,b,t)E_{aa},\quad f_{<0},\quad f_{\ge N}. \tag{2} \] Put U=sum_(a=0)^(N-2)E_(a+1,a), and use S_+f(a)=f(a+1), S_-f(a)=f(a-1). Exactly, with b,t still UNSUMMED, \[ \begin{aligned} C_N(S_+f)&=U^*C_N(f)U+f(N,b,t)E_{N-1,N-1},\\ C_N(S_-f)&=UC_N(f)U^*+f(-1,b,t)E_{00}. \tag{3} \end{aligned} \] Here star denotes the transpose partial shift in this basis, not an additional analytic Hermitian choice. General powers have the corresponding finite sums of r endpoint values. In particular \[ \frac1N\operatorname{Tr}C_N((S_+-1)f) =\frac{f(N)-f(0)}N. \tag{4} \] Thus compression to the finite head is NOT a translation chain map unless its endpoint rows are included. The correct original relative cut source is \[ \Phi_N^{\mathrm{rel}}(f)=\frac1N\left[ \operatorname{Tr}C_Nf+\sum_{a<0}f(a)+\sum_{a\ge N}f(a)\right] =\frac1N\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}f(a). \tag{5} \] It annihilates the complete finite difference exactly, with b,t still unsummed. On the original kernel, whose support is in the head window, it is the original normalized-average cut. For a Green current the two tail sums are part of the source. Replacing this by another high-color co-source because closed scalar periods agree would not establish equality of these inserted rows. Equations (2)--(5) are the explicit cut part of the source for the [full finite Green certificate](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md). They explain how a relative wall can arise even though (1) has no bare off-diagonal final-cut wall coefficient. The two statements are compatible; the wall would have to be a TRANSGRESSION of these boundary rows, not an unproved final-matrix projection. ## 3. Bare wall trace zero does not remove returning wall excursions The original root pivotal operator is diagonal in the head and identity on the Fr block. Its trace on w=E_(N,0) is zero. But the original divided Fr matrices satisfy \[ e^N w=N!E_{00},\qquad w e^N=N!E_{NN}, \quad\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{Fr}}(e^Nw)=N!. \tag{6} \] With a literal head insertion H and pivot g_head the corresponding closed value is N! Tr(g_head H). A paired wall can therefore return to the degree-zero channel and survive closure. Termwise charge conservation does not set every internal wall excursion to zero. The strict Clebsch construction supplies actual inverse- crossing examples of exactly such retained excursions. For true pivotal/Hopf closure one must use the actual ordinary generic pivot and its mixed divided coproduct. The current-level partial-trace theorem and the frozen-pivot correction are retained in the corresponding closure construction. No replacement of that pivotal trace by an unweighted Fr trace is made here. ## 4. Exact residual after the new cochain contraction Let (C,d) be the specified memory current complex, with the actual contraction (p,i,h) onto the degree-elevation image plus its retained wall complex: \[ I-ip=dh+hd,\quad pd=d_{\mathrm{red}}p, di=id_{\mathrm{red}}. \tag{7} \] The explicit wall part is the already audited [Bockstein contraction](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md). Let O_1,O_2 be consecutive original transported maps (crossings, caps, projectors or source maps), and retain their actual current defects \[ \Delta_j=dO_j-O_jd. \tag{8} \] For maps between different coefficient complexes the adjacent differentials and contractions are used; external base shifts also act on their coefficients. Nothing requires a frozen same-base convention. There is the exact operator identity \[ \begin{aligned} pO_2O_1i-(pO_2i)(pO_1i) &=d_{\mathrm{red}}H+Hd_{\mathrm{red}} -p\Delta_2hO_1i+pO_2h\Delta_1i,\\ H&=pO_2hO_1i . \tag{9} \end{aligned} \] Proof: insert (7) between O_2 and O_1, move d past each O_j using (8), and use the two chain identities in (7). This proves (9) before any summation, Gaussian expansion or scalar source. Iterating gives a finite ordered excursion/current formula for the entire weighted word. For the ACTUAL relative source/ket Lambda,Psi, its scalar residual is correspondingly \[ \begin{aligned} &(\Lambda d_{\mathrm{red}})H\Psi+\Lambda H(d_{\mathrm{red}}\Psi)\\ &\quad-\Lambda p\Delta_2hO_1i\Psi +\Lambda pO_2h\Delta_1i\Psi . \tag{10} \end{aligned} \] The first two terms are the specified endpoint/carry co-sources, not automatically zero. The other two are the inserted actual intertwining currents. True pivotal naturality can remove them for the TRUE Hopf complex with its caps; it does not identify that complex with the MEMORY Cartan/F complex without the mixed head and source comparison. The known Jackson off-diagonal remainder is one explicit such inserted current. Consequently local contraction to one wall line does not imply that full words factor through that line. Equation (9), with all original operators, is the finite calculation that decides it. It is also more specific than an unspecified appeal to a regular sequence at an isolated gluing point. ## 5. The exact co-source normalization required of a tail-to-wall map Take the orientation of the positive boundary (4) and the normalized selected coupled wall w tensor E_00. Its ACTUAL source value is \[ \Phi_{e_D}(w\otimes E_{00})=2^{-N}. \] If a proposed relative comparison maps the scalar tail t=f(N)-f(0) to c_N(t)(w tensor E_00), preservation of the original co-source therefore FORCES \[ c_N(t)=\frac{2^N}{N}t. \tag{11} \] In the divided generator f^N coordinate it forces instead 2^N t/(N N!). The uniform Fr interval would require (N+1)t/N in the w coordinate. Their ratio is exactly the already measured 2^N/(N+1). This is a necessary coefficient equation, not permission to choose a new normalization of the invariant. A genuine map must derive (11) from its retained source character, or prove that the WHOLE relevant tail class cancels. A bare fixed algebraic unit at the Rivin point cannot account for the exponential factor; the actual weight-N source line is essential. The marked moment data are essential too. A coupling w^a changes the norm of an ACTUAL translation operator T to w^N T^N. Its finite moment derivatives retain P(a+N)-P(a), the chirp phase, and every memory carry. This does NOT automatically replace the Fr adjoint wall character Q^-N-1 by Q^-N w^N-1: one-sided clock multiplication simply scales the endpoint matrix, leaving its Ad K eigencharacter unchanged. Identifying those translation and memory clutches is another part of the required current map, with its Fourier/relative adapter. It must be checked, not inferred from their equal root numerical values. The current next test is therefore explicit: transport the two unsummed actual Green currents through (2)--(10), including their true pivotal caps, and evaluate their relative wall/tail pairing at the marked Rivin branch. Its regular sequence and algebraicity can control that evaluation once the map is supplied. They do not determine the inserted Delta_j terms, identify the two clutches, or supply the source factor (11). No common selected global period line follows from the Bockstein character alone. ## 6. Independent audit: the actual divided Cartan supplies a whole wall row The subsequent [actual divided Ward/cap construction](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md) provides a positive addition to this residual test. It passes the following independent audit with all sources retained. In the fixed actual beta basis the original matrices E^(N),F^(N) preserve the residue S and move the Fr index by one. Consequently \[ H(q)=\tau[E^{(N)}(q),F^{(N)}(q)] \] is diagonal for EVERY q, with root entries N-2R. On the extreme Fr block its commutator is therefore entrywise multiplication by \[ H_{N,s}(q)-H_{0,t}(q), \tag{12} \] an original rational unit of root value -2N. Inverting these entries gives a literal WHOLE wall extraction through the actual Cartan commutator. It uses neither delta division nor a guessed source comparison. The selected row remains the original one, composed with this explicit unit inverse; its root coefficient bound1/(2N) is not a bound replacing the wall's2^-N source. The global current formula also checks independently. For every actual Hopf element h, \[ [\rho(h),C]=\sum_{(h)}D_{h_1}(C)\rho(h_2). \] This follows directly from the antipode identity. Ordinary pivotal partial trace intertwines these actual adjoints on ALL matrices. Applying the whole weighted crossing-current identity therefore transports (12) through an actual word, with its finite Green difference and source row. Mixed terms of Delta H are essential; this is not a primitive Fr or geometric-Borel assignment. The ordinary pivot g=K and frozen pivot g_f=K^(1-N) are related EXACTLY by P_f=chi^-1 P_o M_(Z^J). Thus the full frozen cap defect is chi^-1 P_o[M_(Z^J),A_h]. Its first delta coefficient is -chi_0^-1 P_(o,0)[M_J,A_(h,0)]; generator and cap derivatives have not been omitted, since their commutators with M_0=I are zero. The explicit E and F cap signs, the divided-adjoint q powers and the ordered N-term telescope all check. In particular the N small-generator rows together have order at least delta^2 before division by [N]_q!, whose zero is simple. Their individual first normals cannot be substituted for a genuine divided cap. Finally the construction contains a literal nonzero actual R return, stronger than the formal trace example (6). With m=N(N+1)-1, k=N^2 and the closed coupon E_(N,0)^Fr tensor P_head0, only transfer k contributes to the open entry k<-0. Its first nonzero coefficient is \[ [\delta^N]\,\operatorname{ptr}_K[(B\otimes I)R]_{k,0} =q_N^{m-2k}\,N^N N!\, \eta_N^{m(m-2k)}\ne0. \tag{13} \] The factorial is (-1)^k q^-k(Q;Q)_k, with root prefactor one; its N zero factors give N! delta^N and its N nonzero blocks give N^N. The symmetric Gaussian is a root unit1, and constant beta phases cancel between the two legs. The frozen leading coefficient has its additional chi_0^-1. All lower orders vanish. The inserted coupon has physical degree N^2, so this returning source is fully consistent with the charge restriction in Section1. This positive whole Cartan row controls the ACTUAL finite cut wall without changing its co-source. The remaining geometric obligation is still to push this specified mixed Hopf/current row and its relative Green endpoints through the partial geometric contraction. It has not been identified with either of the two internal geometric framing rows merely by its unit inverse. The later [whole Ward-grid theorem](whole_high_color_ward_grid_contraction.md) extends this to every actual cut matrix. Its two diagonal spectra and actual ordinary/divided F grid give a rational pole-free contraction End to its trace center, with an explicit homotopy for the original source. An independent proof audit checks the whole formula, absence of off-diagonal pollution, improved comb-path norm and two-word reduction. The root selected-source cost is O(N^(3/2)) for r=N. Its degree-one target is the actual image of the four rows, so no unspecified row-compatibility cokernel has been killed. Thus the finite cut target is now completely specified; the remaining map is the pushforward of the two internal geometric Green/source rows into this target, with (2)--(11) retained. title: What rational jet rigidity fixes about a global period
text:
# What rational jet rigidity fixes about a global period Independent function-level audit, 27 October 2026. The all-level Ward unfolding and norm-root transfer have the stated local uniqueness. That uniqueness does not by itself identify the selected full knot period. The distinction is precise: an analytic function, its formal asymptotic germ, and its period functional are different data. This note gives sharp uniqueness statements, explicit counterexamples, and a minimal algebraic source criterion. No literature proof is used. ## 1. Exact coefficient rigidity really is uniqueness of a function germ Let \(Q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)\). Suppose \[ F(Q,z)=\sum_{j\ge0}f_j(Q)z^j,\qquad G(Q,z)=\sum_{j\ge0}g_j(Q)z^j \] have rational \(Q\)-coefficients, and for every fixed \(j\), \(f_j(Q_N)=g_j(Q_N)\) for every sufficiently large \(N>j\). Then \(F=G\) coefficientwise. For each fixed \(j\), a nonzero rational function cannot have these infinitely many distinct zeros. The exceptional bound can depend on \(j\). Rationality can be weakened: it suffices that each difference has a convergent finite Puiseux--Laurent germ at \(Q=1\), on the marked branch. Indeed a nonzero such germ is \(c\,t^m(1+O(t))\), \(c
e0\), after \(Q-1=t^e\), and has no zeros sufficiently near the puncture. If the resulting power series are holomorphic in \(z\) near zero on an open \(Q\)-domain, equality of coefficients is equality of actual analytic germs. On any connected continuation domain, with the same paths and logarithmic sheets marked, the functions are equal. There is no extra holomorphic function vanishing to all orders at an interior point. Thus the literal factorial function in [the unfolding theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) has no hidden local rational-coefficient freedom. The regularity condition matters. On a punctured neighborhood of \(Q=1\), choose the local logarithm and put \[ U(Q)=\exp\!\left( rac{4\pi^2}{\operatorname{Log} Q}ight). \] It is a nonzero holomorphic unit there and \(U(Q_N)=1\) for all large \(N\), but \(U
e1\). It has exponential growth of order \(1/|Q-1|\). For example \(1+(U(Q)-1)z\) preserves the constant coefficient one and specializes to one at every \(Q_N\), while being a different generic formal unit. Its coefficient is not rational or Puiseux meromorphic at \(Q=1\), so it is excluded by the actual theorem. This example does not change a fixed exact finite root contraction; it shows why punctured holomorphy and exponential-type growth alone do not replace coefficient rigidity. ## 2. Growing finite jets are not a continuity theorem for a global value Equality of a coherent local function fixes any **specified continuous formal contraction** of it: finite sums and products, substitutions of positive formal order, and finite-jet functionals preserve equality. For a \(z\)-adic linear functional into a field with the discrete topology, continuity means that it kills \((z^B)\) for some finite \(B\). This is an elementary consequence of continuity at zero. Without such a property, agreement of growing truncations has no uniform evaluation implication. For fixed \(a>1\), \[ A_N(z)=1,\qquad B_N(z)=1+a^Nz^N \] agree modulo \(z^N\), but \(B_N(1)-A_N(1)=a^N\). Each is polynomial, with algebraic coefficients; the added term is proper hypergeometric in \(N\). This family is not a second rational coefficient unfolding of section 1. It is a level-dependent tail which that theorem never claims to determine. In a nilpotent matrix algebra \(z^N=0\) the tail is literally zero and cannot change any fixed finite matrix contraction. In a whole normal order \(z^N\) can instead be a nonzero normal parameter; a divided source can see it. If a selected contraction requires at most \(B\) normal jets, knowing those jets fixes that contraction. What must be proved is that the comparison uses the same functional, with its boundary carries and finite jet budget. The local Ward unfolding alone does not construct that global comparison. This is exactly why the source and first-normal terms retained in [the norm-root period theorem](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) and in the divided-power calculations are necessary. Their equality as local operators does not license replacing the full contraction by a different cycle. ## 3. All formal WKB jets do not fix an analytic period at an irregular point This is a different issue from exact rational coefficient uniqueness. Let \(c=1-i\), and on a punctured \(h\)-neighborhood consider \[ P_0(h)=1,\qquad P_1(h)=1+\exp(-c/h). \] On a sufficiently small sector around the positive real ray, \(\exp(-c/h)=O(h^m)\) for every \(m\). Thus both have the same normalized formal power series, to every order. Both are holomorphic on the punctured neighborhood and have exponential-type growth \(\exp(O(1/|h|))\). Both even solve the same rational-coefficient equation \[ (h^2\partial_h)(h^2\partial_h-c)P=0. \] Yet on \(h=i\epsilon\), \(\epsilon>0\), \(\exp(-c/h)=\exp((1+i)/\epsilon)\). Therefore \[ \epsilon\log|P_0(i\epsilon)|=0,\qquad \epsilon\log|P_1(i\epsilon)|\longrightarrow1. \] Formal jets in one chamber do not control another marked root direction without an analytic continuation and sectorial estimate. Even on the same ray, adding a subdominant exponential changes the global period while preserving all normalized dominant WKB jets. It then leaves the leading rate unchanged, but is still an exact global ambiguity invisible to perturbative jets. Consequently “coefficients lie in the algebraic critical field” is not a convergence assertion about a formal \(h\)-series. The series \(\sum n!h^n\) already has rational coefficients and zero radius. Nor does an algebraic optimizer rule out irregular-singular exponentials or determine their global coefficients. ## 4. The missing source coefficient has a sharp linear-algebra criterion Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional global period space over a characteristic-zero field. Suppose the retained normalizations fix a functional \(\ell\) only on a subspace \(U\subset V\), and let \(g\in V\) be the geometric period vector. **Source criterion.** The value \(\ell(g)\) is forced by those data if and only if \(g\in U\). If \(g\in U\), this is immediate. If \(g
otin U\), extend a basis of \(U\) by \(g\). Its dual gives a functional \(\mu\) with \(\mu(U)=0,\ \mu(g)=1\). Then \(\ell+c\mu\) preserves every given normalization and assigns any desired value to \(g\), including zero. This is an exact criterion, without an asymptotic hypothesis. Here is a function-level counterexample with a unique rigid optimizer. Take the rigid algebra \(k	imes k\), action \(S=(V,W)\), \(V>W\), and period vector \[ \Pi(\epsilon)=(e^{V/\epsilon},e^{W/\epsilon}). \] Every normalized local amplitude is exactly \(1\), with all higher jets zero; both points and the unique maximizing point are algebraic. The two positive normalized functionals \[ \ell_+(a,b)=a,\qquad \ell_-(a,b)=b,\qquad \ell_\pm(1,1)=1 \] give leading rates \(V\) and \(W\), respectively. All local functions, actions, and normalized jets are identical. The differing datum is the global source coefficient, which vanishes on the optimizer for \(\ell_-\). A nonzero formal geometric quotient is compatible with this example. Strict positivity without quantitative control is also insufficient when the source depends on the level. The normalized functional \[ \ell_\epsilon(a,b)=e^{-a_*/\epsilon}a+ (1-e^{-a_*/\epsilon})b,\quad a_*>0, \] is strictly positive on both points, but its period rate is \(\max(V-a_*,W)\). What matters is nonzero **subexponential** geometric weight, rather than positivity at each separate level. A strictly convex/concave Rivin optimizer therefore supplies the unique geometric critical point and its local nonzero Gaussian block. Algebraicity supplies its critical field and local period identities. Neither assertion by itself constrains \(\ell(g)\). For a positive integral on a specified real domain, an ordinary uniform density bound can supply that missing constraint; it cannot be inferred for an unspecified complex quantum cycle. Even strict convexity on one connected algebraic domain does not choose that domain's integration class. For the same entire integrand \(e^{-x^2/\epsilon}\), compare the normalized positive functionals \( rac12\int_{-1}^1\) and \(\int_1^2\). Both send \(1\) to \(1\), while their period rates \(\epsilon\log P_\epsilon\) are respectively \(0\) and \(-1\). The action \(x^2\) is strictly convex with the unique algebraic optimizer \(0\). The first rate follows by bounding below on \([-\sqrt\epsilon,\sqrt\epsilon]\); the second by bounding below on \([1,1+\epsilon]\) and above by \(e^{-1/\epsilon}\). The changed datum is the marked relative cycle, not the function. ## 5. A useful sufficient global regularity hypothesis Suppose a **constructed global comparison** gives a nonzero geometric coefficient \(c(Q)\) which is meromorphic Puiseux at \(Q=1\). Then \[ c(Q_N)=C\,N^{-\alpha}(1+o(1)) \] on its marked branch, with \(C
e0\); in particular \[  rac1N\log|c(Q_N)|\longrightarrow0. 	ag{5.1} \] Proof: substitute \(Q_N-1=2\pi i/N+O(N^{-2})\) in the first nonzero Puiseux--Laurent term. Thus a nonzero rational or algebraic-meromorphic global comparison coefficient cannot hide an exponential suppression or infinitely many zero levels. This is a practical target for torsor descent: construct the global geometric projection and prove its coefficient belongs to this field and is nonzero. Proving uniqueness of such a comparison **if it exists** does not prove existence or nonvanishing. For clarity, the elementary rate-transfer statement is as follows. If \[ P_N=c_NG_N+R_N,\quad  rac{2\pi}{N}\log|G_N|	o V,\quad \log|c_N|=o(N),\quad |R_N|\le \exp\!\left( rac N{2\pi}(V-\delta)ight) \] for some \(\delta>0\), then \((2\pi/N)\log|P_N|	o V\). Indeed \(R_N/(c_NG_N)	o0\); upper and lower triangle bounds then give the conclusion. This needs a bound for the **total** remainder, not only for individual local critical points. An algebraic alternative to Puiseux meromorphy suffices for (5.1). If \(c_N
e0\) satisfies an integer polynomial of degree \(d_N\) and coefficient maximum \(H_N\), with \(\log(d_NH_N)=o(N)\), then \(\log|c_N|=o(N)\). After removing powers of \(X\), its constant and leading coefficients are nonzero integers. For \(|c_N|\le1\), \(1\le d_NH_N|c_N|\); for \(|c_N|\ge1\), the elementary Cauchy bound gives \(|c_N|\le1+H_N\). This condition is not automatic from algebraicity at each level: \(c_N=a^N\) already has exponentially large height. The later [critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) strengthens this criterion: \(\log H_N=o(N)\) alone suffices, with no degree bound, by applying the geometric-series Cauchy bound to an integer polynomial and its reciprocal. More substantively, a fixed whole algebraic source on the actual exponential root arc has polynomial upper and lower bounds without an absolute height estimate. Irreducible field descent and a retained nonzero source pairing then force the geometric coefficient to be nonzero; neither source descent nor a total remainder bound is inferred from the classical optimizer. ## 6. Consequences for the current repository claims - [The unfolded Ward theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) has exact rational-coefficient uniqueness, a marked local cyclic gauge, and a controlled norm on its stated compact chart. Its derivations and scope do not assert a global source coefficient. - [The norm-root theorem](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) transports the actual missing-edge class to the marked peripheral period. Its norm-one kernel and the selected internal knot contraction remain additional data; the full peripheral period does not determine a knot Bloch-period coefficient. - [The partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) constructs a nonzero formal geometric quotient before the final two-index contraction. The source criterion above explains exactly why this need not survive that contraction. - The divided-power drafts make operator/source statements. Their positive ghosts lower total index by \(N\), so ordinary full weight-zero closure kills them. Their present stated scope does not claim a selected global relative pairing. There is no free ambiguity in the **already specified actual** period: [the all-level pointing theorem](all_level_a_period.md) determines it from its actual operator and finite initial colors. Changing its global functional, or adding a flat solution without preserving that pointing, gives a different period and is not a counterexample to that theorem. The remaining logical step is consequently concrete. One must map the actual selected source, including its divided normal row, into the geometric quotient and prove a nonzero coefficient with subexponential control, or construct an exact global period comparison preserving that source and metric. Local jet uniqueness then removes local freedom. It cannot substitute for this source map or prove its value by itself.

title: The simultaneous many-head Ward gap is a separate problem
text: # The simultaneous many-head Ward gap is a separate problem 28 October 2026. The proved polynomial inverse for an actual [two-head lowering current](actual_two_head_ward_polynomial_contraction.md) does not yet give an inverse for arbitrary many-head constraints. This note records a reproducible test and an exact identity identifying the full system worth studying. It proves no new asymptotic spectral bound and reports no counterexample to such a bound. ## 1. The actual physical operators At the canonical complete color, put Q=exp(2pi i/N), x=-exp(-pi i/N), F_one e_a=(1-Q^(a+1))e_(a+1), Ecal_one e_a=-(1-Q^(-a))e_(a-1), K_one e_a=x Q^-a e_a. Here Ecal=rho^2 E in the original balanced physical frame. This polynomial scalar rescaling retains the actual Ward equation. For b heads use the ACTUAL coproducts F_b=sum_j K_1^-1...K_(j-1)^-1 F_j, Ecal_b=sum_j Ecal_j K_(j+1)...K_b. Let P reverse the physical heads. Since K is unitary and Ecal_one=-F_one^*, directly Ecal_b=-P F_b^* P. (1) In total-degree blocks this is Ecal_s=-P_(s-1) F_(s-1)^* P_s. Thus the simultaneous Ward normal operator is exactly F_s^*F_s+P_s F_(s-1)F_(s-1)^*P_s. (2) This identity uses the original physical metric, not a nonunitary fusion similarity. It holds in every head number at this complete color. No claim that (2) has a uniform spectral gap follows from the identity alone. There is also an exact Hermitian formulation. On the full physical tensor space put D=F_b+Ecal_b. Equation (1) gives (P D)^*=-P D. Thus iP D is Hermitian. For a vector in a single total degree, the F and Ecal outputs are orthogonal, so ||Dv||^2 is precisely the simultaneous Ward energy (2). This is a folded Hermitian Dirac formulation in the original metric. Its spectral estimate remains to be proved; Hermiticity alone does not bound a gap. There is a further exact kernel issue: the full Dirac kernel need not be graded. Already at one complete physical head, N=5, write c_r=1-Q^r and v=e_0+[c_1/conjugate(c_2)]e_2+e_4. Then (F+Ecal)v=0 by the two odd-row recurrences, whereas neither F e_2 nor Ecal e_2 vanishes. The degree-2 component is nonzero and obeys K=1, since x=Q^2. Thus even on the required K=1 slice, projection of the FULL Dirac kernel is not the joint Ward kernel. A gap for the global Hermitian Dirac would require an additional kernel-angle estimate before yielding the fixed-degree stacked inverse. This is why the target remains the actual Gram (2). ## 2. The exact Gram matrix has nontrivial magnetic triangle flux Write H_s=F_s^*F_s+Ecal_s^*Ecal_s, and let a be a physical head state of total degree s. Its diagonal is exactly H_s[a,a]=4 sum_i [sin^2(pi(a_i+1)/N)+sin^2(pi a_i/N)]. For i<j, a_i<d and a_j>0, set a'=a+e_i-e_j and M=sum_(i<h<j)a_h. Direct multiplication of the two actual coproducts gives the off-diagonal entry H_s[a',a]=8 q^-1 sin(pi(a_i+1)/N)sin(pi a_j/N) *cos((j-i)phi-pi(a_i+a_j+2M)/N), (3) where q=exp(pi i/N) and phi=Arg x=pi-pi/N. All other off-diagonal entries vanish except the Hermitian reverse edges. Equivalently the real cosine factor in (3) is (-1)^(j-i) cos[pi(a_i+a_j+2M+j-i)/N]. For clarity, the F^*F contribution before combining phases is x^(j-i)Q^(-a_i-M-1) (1-Q^(a_i+1))(1-Q^-a_j), and the Ecal^*Ecal contribution is x^(i-j)Q^(a_j+M-1) (1-Q^(a_i+1))(1-Q^-a_j). Their sum is exactly (3). No asymptotic symbol or K=1 approximation is used in this calculation. Consequently a diagonal unitary vertex gauge CANNOT in general make this Gram matrix an ordinary real weighted graph Laplacian. There is an explicit countertest inside the actual K_total=1 sector: take b=4, N=5, s=8, and the triangle a=(1,1,2,4), b=(2,0,2,4), c=(2,1,1,4). Put k=(5-sqrt(5))/2. Equation (3) and the elementary golden-angle sine identities give exactly H[b,a]=k q^-1, H[c,b]=k q^-1, H[a,c]=-sqrt(5)q, H[b,a]H[c,b]H[a,c]=-sqrt(5)k^2 q^-1. (4) The triangle product is nonreal. It is invariant under every diagonal unitary gauge, while any matrix with real off-diagonal entries has real products around all such triangles. All three states obey K_total=1 since x^4Q^-8=1. Thus this obstruction is present on the required actual invariant-weight fiber, not only on another degree or a hypothetical kernel. This does not refute a polynomial simultaneous Ward bound, a magnetic/Hodge comparison, or a nonlocal unitary decomposition. It rules out the direct real-path argument obtained by simply gauging away all global phases. The two-head path proof has no triangles and does not encounter this obstruction. There is nevertheless an EXACT norm-preserving realification at all head numbers. The entry formula and reversal of the interval i,...,j give P_s H_s P_s=conjugate(H_s). Define P_+=(I+P_s)/2, P_-=(I-P_s)/2, and U=P_++iP_-=[(1+i)/2]I+[(1-i)/2]P_s. Then U is unitary, mixes only a state and its physical reversal, and U^* H_s U=Re H_s-P_s Im H_s (5) is REAL SYMMETRIC. Indeed the real part commutes with P_s and the imaginary part anticommutes with it. This proves (5) directly. It is a sparse two-state mixing with condition number one, not an exponentially conditioned fusion transformation. The resulting real matrix has signed interactions and no automatic diagonal-dominance or Laplacian comparison. Thus the triangle test rules out a diagonal phase gauge, while (5) supplies a valid more general unitary reduction. Any use on the original source must transform the currents and source by this same specified U. ## 3. Four-head diagnostic at the actual two-cup degree For b=4 choose s=2(N-1), exactly the total integer degree of two original cups. The regular Borel decomposition has full length-N strings, so the exact rank of F_s is rank F_s=h_4(s)-h_3(s-(N-1)), where h_b(s) is the coefficient of t^s in (1+...+t^(N-1))^b. This fixes which singular values are nonzero without numerical thresholding. The original physical matrices give the following resolved nonzero F gaps: N= 4: 1.08239220 6: 0.43260052 8: 0.18973845 10: 0.08478187 12: 0.03780617 14: 0.01676550 16: 0.00740054 20: 0.00142953. The exact zero cluster remains below 9e-15 in these diagnostics. This rapid decay warns against carrying the two-head estimate over to F_b by an unproved iteration. These finite values alone DO NOT prove exponential decay or disprove every polynomial estimate. Crucially, keeping BOTH actual Ward currents changes the picture. For [F_s; Ecal_s] the computed smallest nonzero values are N= 4: 1.20597689 6: 0.62788204 8: 0.39963573 10: 0.28269084 12: 0.21347310 14: 0.16854041. The observed joint kernel dimension is N at these levels. The joint gap is consistent with a polynomial bound, which is not proved here. In particular the F-only diagnostic is not an obstruction to a polynomial simultaneous Ward contraction. ## 4. The remaining constructive target A useful many-head theorem must solve the compatible simultaneous current system with its joint kernel and cokernel retained. Its exact Gram is (2)--(3), (4) rules out a diagonal phase removal, and (5) gives a condition-one sparse realification. It must not impose a separate invariant-pair equation at an intermediate slice where interbridge crossings have mixed the pair channels. Equations (1)--(2) provide an actual fixed-metric formulation of that target. The local two-head bounds and the [cyclic Ward-wall contraction](ward_cyclic_wall_contraction_and_marked_augmentation.md) are valid inputs; compatibility and a simultaneous spectral estimate are further work. Even a proved polynomial simultaneous inverse would transport exact currents, not identify a positive geometric kernel or prove the selected scalar's volume rate by itself. [Reproduce the diagnostic](../experiments/audit_global_four_head_ward_gap.py). The default levels stop at N=12; `--larger` adds N=14,16. Larger resolved F-only values above were separately computed in the same physical basis; a contemplated N=24 dense SVD was interrupted.

title: Actual Green moments: a bounded carry extension and an exact Fock jet map
text: # Actual Green moments: a bounded carry extension and an exact Fock jet map Research proof, 27 October 2026. The polynomial moments in the full scalar Green certificate have an exact bounded triangular carry complex. Its graded differential is the **coefficient monodromy**; it is not zero in general. Actual integer-index moments also have an exact Newton/Fock normal-ordering map, and the Mellin relative source has a finite endpoint-preserving normal-jet complex. These constructions do not identify the remaining geometric Green boundary with zero. In particular a top divided-monodromy row is not the original marked cut or its full higher normal jet. ## 1. The actual Green currents have bounded logarithmic degree Let `h` be the fixed least moment degree of the actual global certificate. In [the full Green formula](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md), every current is a finite sum of terms A_beta(M,T_M) p(k) D^gamma I, degree p<=h, with the literal shifted finite coefficient array retained. After transverse Gaussian contraction, divide only by the recorded common Gaussian generator and its base line. The result belongs to sum_(|alpha|<=h) K_geo((H)) ell^alpha, (1) where `ell` is the finite list of logarithms of the actual critical flow characters. This is an all-order bound on logarithmic degree. Proof: an internal finite shift changes the coefficient by a proper rational ratio and changes `p` by a polynomial of the same degree. Write every actual index as its chosen logarithm divided by `H`. Taylor expansion about the critical point differentiates a polynomial in these logarithms and cannot increase its degree. Wick contractions and formal division by the unit Gaussian amplitude have algebraic coefficients in the same common field. A meridian shift changes a critical logarithm by its original logarithm plus a formal series with algebraic coefficients; it also preserves the degree bound. Its common exponential/base ratio is kept, as in the normal-period calculation. The fixed negative H orders of the moment are retained. The common algebraic field is finite over the marked geometric/frame field. After a fixed algebraic cover makes a chosen loop return all algebraic branches, continuation shifts the critical logarithms by specified integral multiples of `2pi*i`. Thus the logarithmic part of (1) is unipotent of length at most `h+1` for that loop. Before passing to that cover, its algebraic coefficient monodromy must also be retained. This statement concerns the actual **formal Green images**. It does not say that the entire zero-extended finite coefficient array is a unipotent monodromy module. ## 2. The exact triangular carry complex keeps the coefficients For one chosen carry coordinate let `P_h` be polynomials in `k` of degree at most `h`. Let `M` be the actual coefficient-current module and `C` its carry transport. The total carry is T_total=exp(N partial_k) tensor C. Use the Newton basis `b_j(k)=binom(k/N,j)`, `0<=j<=h`. Translation by `N` sends `b_j` to `b_j+b_(j-1)`. With `L b_j=b_(j-1)`, T_total-I=I tensor(C-I)+L tensor C, L^(h+1)=0. (2) Therefore the two-term current complex with differential `T_total-I` is a finite triangular extension of `h+1` copies of the coefficient complex `M --(C-I)--> M`. This is the correct bounded carry complex. It applies termwise to the actual polynomial-times-coefficient decomposition above. Tensor Newton bases give the multivariable version, with the actual commuting carry transports retained. If coefficient/moment relations are present, this is the explicit moment presentation mapping equivariantly onto the actual current module; those relations are retained in the quotient. No linear independence of polynomial moments on a finite support is assumed. Only when `C=I` do its invariants consist of constant polynomials and its cokernel consist of the top Newton degree. For an arbitrary coefficient transport one has the exact expansion (T_total-I)^h =sum_(r=0)^h binom(h,r) L^r tensor C^r(C-I)^(h-r). (3) Terms with `r<h` are the coefficient-monodromy correction, not discardable scalar factors. In particular even the divided h-th power need not land in the coefficient-horizontal constant line. For actual zero-extended finite arrays the stronger obstruction is elementary. Translation by `N` minus identity is injective on the space of finite-support arrays: a finite-support periodic array is zero. Hence none of its positive powers kills a nonzero such array. Multiplying by a polynomial moment does not change that fact. Consequently polynomial degree alone cannot make the **full actual array** carry nilpotent. One must either pass to the specified formal continuation (1), or retain the coefficient complex in (2). ## 3. Actual index moments are number operators in the common Fock source In the actual common Verma basis write an edge index as `a=rN+j`. The Fock operators are `B=partial_t,T=t`, with `v_(rN+j)=h_j t^r/r!`. Its actual index multiplication is therefore n_a=j+N T B. (4) It is not multiplication by `T/(2pi*i)`. Under [the exact Mellin map](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), T -> u=Log U, B -> nabla=U partial_U, n_a -> j+N u nabla. (5) This distinction applies to the Green currents themselves: each free flow index is either an edge index or an integral difference of adjacent crossing edge indices. Multiplication by its polynomial is thus a polynomial in the corresponding commuting edge-number insertions, on the appropriate sides of the actual crossing kernels. No quantum-group intertwining of that insertion is presumed. There is nevertheless an exact bounded conversion on coherent kernels. For every degree-h polynomial `p`, Newton interpolation gives p(j+Nr)=sum_(m=0)^h binom(r,m) Delta_N^m p(j), Delta_N p(a)=p(a+N)-p(a). Since `binom(TB,m)exp(st)=(st)^m exp(st)/m!`, p(n_a) theta_s(h_j) =theta_s(h_j) sum_(m=0)^h Delta_N^m p(j) (sT)^m/m!. (6) On the normal side this is the literal identity M[p(n_a)theta_s(h_j)] =epsilon_j U^s sum_(m=0)^h Delta_N^m p(j) (su)^m/m!. (7) Thus actual number moments do map to bounded logarithmic polynomials times the coherent kernel, with their full lower triangular terms. The map is not the false substitution `n_a=j+u/(2pi*i)`. Set `c=2pi*i`. Physically `U=A^N`, `H_N=c/N`, so `k=Log A/H_N=u/c` on the chosen logarithmic lift, up to the marked residue label. Choosing the coherent anchor `s_*=1/(cN)` in (7) gives the exact polynomial transform B_(N,j)p(x)=sum_(m=0)^h Delta_N^m p(j) x^m/(m! N^m), x=u/c. (8) It is unitriangular by polynomial degree, comparing with `p(j+x)`: its highest coefficient is the same. Lower terms can contain positive powers of `N`, so the transform is exact rather than an asymptotically identity adapter. Products of these transforms give the bounded multiedge map for the actual flow moments. In particular the step-N falling factorial has the exact image M[product_(r=0)^(m-1)(n_a-j-rN) theta_(s_*)] =(u/c)^m M[theta_(s_*)]. This is a linear current/kernel map, not a multiplicative map of its scalar polynomial images. For example the image of `n_a^2` is `(j+x)^2+N x`, while the square of the image of `n_a` is only `(j+x)^2`. The physical whole clock gives a sharper test. Since `a=rN+j`, exp(H_N n_a)theta_s=Q^j theta_s, whereas ordinary exponentiation of the proposed coordinate image would give exp[H_N(j+u/c)]=Q^j exp(u/N)=Q^j alpha(U). Thus the bounded polynomial conversion does not intertwine the literal whole clock `A` without its additional normal/star adapter. After rescaling by `H_N`, some fixed-degree corrections become small for fixed `u`; this is not uniform at the geometric scale `u=N Log A`, which is generally of order `N`. No whole-function or geometric gluing comparison is inferred from (8). All coherent anchors have `pi_0 theta_s=I`; the original finite cut is retained. The marked relative source path is `s->s+1`, so its endpoint ratio remains `U`, independently of choosing `s_*`. Choosing an anchor does not rescale `T` or replace that endpoint. The actual coherent crossing changes the source parameters, so moving a moment through a crossing differentiates its finite kernel coefficients as well. These Leibniz terms, of order at most `h`, must be retained. Equations (4)--(7) specify their operator order. ## 4. The marked relative source has an exact finite normal-jet complex Take the actual Mellin source differential and transgression delta_U f=((partial_sigma-u)f,f(0),f(1)), L_U(a,b_0,b_1)=integral_0^1 exp(-sigma u)a(sigma)dsigma -exp(-u)b_1+b_0. For a coefficient germ regular at `u=0`, take its normal jets `f_n=(partial_u^n f)|_(u=0)`, `0<=n<=h`. Let `E_h` be the jet vector space and define the nilpotent triangular operator (T_h f)_n=n f_(n-1), f_(-1)=0. The actual jet differential is exactly (delta_h f)_n=(partial_sigma f_n-n f_(n-1), f_n(0),f_n(1)). (9) The jet map from `delta_U` to (9) is strict: this is just the Leibniz formula for `partial_u^n(u f)` at zero. Its transgression is (L_h(a,b_0,b_1))_n =integral_0^1 sum_(j=0)^n binom(n,j)(-sigma)^(n-j) a_j(sigma)dsigma -sum_(j=0)^n binom(n,j)(-1)^(n-j)b_(1,j)+b_(0,n). (10) This is `partial_u^n L_U|_0`. In particular the endpoint-U carry survives as every displayed binomial term at the second endpoint. Replacing it by just `-b_(1,n)` is incorrect. Conjugation by the finite matrix `exp(-sigma T_h)` reduces (9) to the ordinary relative polynomial complex. It follows directly that `L_h delta_h=0`, the inclusion is `exp(sigma T_h)f`, and `L_h i_h=I`. This is an actual finite triangular relative-source complex, with top cohomology `E_h`; it uses no asymptotic hypothesis. It is a normal-jet complex, not a finite-dimensional Weyl representation. `partial_u` needs the next jet to act on the last component. One must not impose `[B,T]=I` on a fixed finite jet space; its trace would give the impossible equation `0=dim E_h`. The original finite-rank coupon is the zero-jet row `Gamma(f)=[tau(f)]_(u=0)`. Higher rows are `Gamma nabla^j`. They are distinct source data, as in the Mellin theorem. Whole coefficient projection `tau(f)1` is not substituted for `Gamma`. Both reduced and literal pivot lifts remain paired with their inverse defect lifts; each product is exactly the original `e`. ## 5. The proposed top-monodromy row has a computable extra term For a constant coefficient polynomial `p(k)=a_h k^h+...`, Delta_N^h p/(h! N^h)=a_h. (11) For the actual moment `binom(k,h)`, this row is `1/h!`, not one. The moment-normalized row is instead `Delta_N^h/N^h`, which sends `binom(k,h)` to one. Products of the corresponding factorials are required for multivariate moment indices. Even if a coefficient function has trivial loop monodromy, its normal derivatives need not vanish. Let `f(u)` be such a whole-normal coefficient and keep `c=2pi*i`. The power-normalized Fock normal row on the candidate coordinate polynomial has the exact value Gamma [c^h partial_u^h/h!][p(u/c)f(u)] =sum_(r=0)^h c^(h-r)p^((r))(0)/(r!(h-r)!) Gamma(nabla^(h-r)f). (12) Its `r=h` term is the top polynomial-monodromy row. All `r<h` terms are the explicit coefficient-normal-jet correction. Equations (9)--(10) transport these extra rows with the correct endpoint carry. Equations (6)--(8), rather than an uncorrected coordinate replacement, must first be used for the actual index-number moment. In particular, after that actual Newton conversion the averaged power-normalized row is explicitly R_(h,p)(f) =(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)sum_(r=0)^h c^(h-r) Delta_N^r p(j)/[r!(h-r)! N^r] [nabla^(h-r) f_j]_(u=0). (12a) Here `f_j` retains the whole coefficient germ, including any coherent unit and kernel/pivot factors. Thus (12a) computes the bounded additional coefficient-current rows for the actual polynomial moment, rather than assuming them horizontal. It is applied at each relevant edge/side of the kernel; derivatives through a crossing obey the literal Leibniz rule. If a coefficient is not regular at the normal point, its specified Laurent finite part and polar source must be kept instead of silently applying the regular-jet formula. Finally the full Green equation has `A_alpha I` in **polynomial degree zero**. A top-degree projection for `h>0` kills that term. It therefore cannot by itself preserve the moment repair or prove that all its carried currents vanish. The lower extension maps in (2), and the full endpoint rows in (10), are indispensable. ## 6. A singular coherent anchor repairs the whole clock sector There is a useful exact whole-function extension of the polynomial conversion, with an equally explicit source defect. Keep `Q` near its marked root, put `z=Q^N`, and set s_Q=1/[N(z-1)], G_Q(u)=exp(s_Q u). The actual whole index clock acts under Mellin by Q^(n_a)=Q^j D_z, (D_z f)(u)=f(zu). Consequently the exact conjugated operator is G_Q^(-1) Q^(n_a) G_Q =Q^j exp(u/N) D_z. (13) For every integer `m` its m-th power is Q^(mj) exp[(z^m-1)u/(N(z-1))] D_(z^m). (14) The quotient is regular at `z=1`, including negative `m`, and the limit is multiplication by Q_N^(mj) exp(m u/N)=A^m. Thus the **whole Laurent clock algebra** has a regular operator limit at this irregular coherent anchor. This is stronger than a finite polynomial symbol identity. On any fixed normal-jet space its matrices have regular coefficients by (13)--(14). The other operators retain explicit counterterms: G_Q^(-1)B G_Q=nabla+s_Q, G_Q^(-1)n_a G_Q=j+N u nabla+u/(z-1). (15) The Weyl commutator remains one. An actual degree-h Green moment therefore has pole order at most `h` from this insertion. If `p(a)=a_h a^h+...`, then [(z-1)^h G_Q^(-1)p(n_a)G_Q]_(z=1)=a_h u^h. This rescaling cannot be applied to the Green equation and then forgotten: for `h>0` it also kills a regular degree-zero operator term `A_alpha I` on the wall. Coefficient/excursion counterterms must be retained when deciding its finite part. ### The actual finite source projector is not regularized automatically The gauge commutes with `partial_sigma-u`, its relative transgression, and the endpoint `U`. The finite cut **row** satisfies `Gamma G_Q=Gamma`, because `G_Q(0)=1`. However its finite-rank projector transforms as G_Q^(-1) Gamma G_Q=exp(-s_Q u) Gamma. (16) Its image/source-one section has n-th normal jet `(-s_Q)^n`. These are poles of order `n`; equality of the zero-jet normalization does not identify this source with the constant vacuum. The whole coefficient projector `f->tau(f)1` does commute with `G_Q`; it is not the finite-rank `Gamma` in (16). The remaining normal source row is explicit: [nabla,exp(-s_Q u)Gamma] =-s_Q exp(-s_Q u)Gamma-exp(-s_Q u)Gamma nabla. (17) Thus on the finite jet complex (9) the irregular source is the specified triangular jet vector `((-s_Q)^n Gamma)_(n<=h)`, with the full endpoint terms of (10). It is not an unspecified anomaly, but it has not been shown to cancel against the actual kernel coefficients. The whole-clock regular limit alone is therefore not a regular pointed-source or knot-period limit. ## 7. The two-wall coefficient curvature must accompany this limit For the actual common Verma source, the compressed braid differs from the ambient head-to-head braid by the specified term `delta w H_beta`. Here `delta=1-Q^N=1-z`, so `s_Q=-1/(N delta)`. An r-th coherent-source coefficient can therefore turn a nominal `delta w` excursion into `delta w s_Q^r`. Its order is not fixed by the polynomial moment degree alone. One may not set both walls to zero before computing these terms at the singular anchor. The source complex (9)--(10), the finite vacuum jets (16), and the actual coefficient/current transport must be used together. They keep precisely the data that a bare top divided-monodromy row or an ordinary cyclic specialization would erase. ## 8. Exact gain and remaining comparison The actual Green currents now have a proved bounded logarithmic filtration, a coefficient-sensitive triangular carry complex, an exact number-moment/coherent-kernel conversion, and a finite normal jet relative-source map with every endpoint coefficient specified. These are concrete current/source constructions, not a statement that nilpotence alone solves the transport. They do not identify the Gaussian coefficient germs with their actual whole-source specializations at all retained cut roots. Nor do they suppress the coefficient carry `C-I` of the finite zero-extended arrays. The remaining contribution is exactly the coefficient-monodromy terms in (3), the coefficient-normal jets in (12), the marked endpoint sum in (10), and the irregular finite vacuum/excursion terms (16)--(17), applied to the actual Green currents. Their geometric source image has not been computed or shown to cancel. A nonzero sourced full geometric period and the geometric factor of the actual full scalar operator remain unproved. [Exact current/source audit](../experiments/audit_green_moment_carry_filtration.py) and [results](../experiments/green_moment_carry_filtration_results.json) verify actual Green binomial moments through degree six, their step-N falling factorials, all coefficient normal-jet terms, the relative endpoint complex, whole clock powers at the irregular anchor, and the finite-vacuum projector defect. These are universal operator/jet identities, with no knot-by-knot checks.

title: Independent audit of the printed GSWZ v2 definitions
text: # Independent audit of the printed GSWZ v2 definitions Audit date: 25 October 2026. Scope: *The Habiro ring of a number field*, arXiv:2412.04241v2, posted 27 August 2025; PDF title-page manuscript date 13 August 2025. The checked PDF has 73 pages and SHA-256 `308d1dd1c42bd979e5d5c31d9d95215a1808f604031b49c0ce2a1eb767273de9`. This audit was separately requested by the user. It checks the proposed examples against the printed definitions, rather than assuming either the paper's theorems or the proposed criticisms. Primary sources: [v2 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.04241v2) and [v2 HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.04241v2). Page numbers below are the printed PDF page numbers. PDF pages 9, 29 and 35 were also inspected visually; the relevant formulas agree with the HTML and extracted text. **Result.** The two structural counterexamples are valid under the printed definitions. Definition 1.4 is not closed under pointwise addition, and the span in Definition 1.3 need not be finitely generated. The Gaussian normalization and rank-one recurrence errors are also present in the PDF. These findings do not directly disprove the restricted arithmetic membership assertion in Theorem 5. ## 1. Printed conventions that matter Definition 1.1, equation (13), p. 7, defines the actual Habiro ring using the exact p-adic equality f_m(x+zeta_(pm)-zeta_m)=phi_p(f_(pm))(x). The coefficient Frobenius fixes rational constants. At primes inverted in R the completion is zero, so the paper explicitly treats those gluing conditions as vacuous. Definition 1.3, equations (20)--(22), p. 9, allows f_m in epsilon_m(xi)^(1/m) (R_p^[zeta_m]^*+x K_p[zeta_m][[x]]), (m,p)=1. Only the constant coefficient has an integrality/unit condition. The bracket placement really allows all higher coefficients in the fraction field; it is not the bounded-denominator ring R_p^[zeta_m][[x]][1/p]. The local module is the H_(R_p^)-span of all sections satisfying the printed logarithmic Frobenius test. Definition 1.4, equations (23)--(24), p. 10, indexes all m>=1. It imposes membership in these local spans and, for every gamma>0, f(q^gamma)^gamma f(q^(-1)) in H_(R[1/gamma])|_gamma. The restriction on the right tests only orders coprime to gamma. This is not an implicit restriction to orders prime to Delta: the paragraph immediately preceding Theorem 5, p. 14, explicitly changes the earlier all-order definition to that narrower setting. No quotient by independent root phases is printed in Definition 1.4. For xi=0 the coefficient torsor has a trivial frame and the examples below are actual rational scalar collections. A coherent change of coefficient frame changes both compared sections by the same unit; their relative sign and the addition obstruction are unchanged. Quotienting the scalar collections by arbitrary componentwise phases would also make their stated pointwise addition undefined, so would be a different construction requiring a new definition. ## 2. The global zero-class set is not an additive group Take K=Q, R=Z[1/6], Delta=6 and xi=0. Define constant series f_2=-1, f_m=1 for m!=2. Every relevant prime p is odd. On orders m prime to p, q->q^p preserves the order, so f(q^p)/f(q)^p=s/s^p=1 for s=+/-1. The regulator term for xi=0 vanishes. Hence f is itself an admitted invertible local section for every non-vacuous local test. For equation (24), at an order m coprime to gamma, both substitutions q->q^gamma and q->q^(-1) preserve that order. The tested constant is f_m^(gamma+1). If m!=2 it equals one. If m=2, coprimality forces gamma odd and it again equals one. Thus every global tested collection is identically one, so f belongs to the printed H_(R,0). Actual Habiro gluing with p=5,m=2 instead requires -1=1 in Z_5[zeta_10], which is false, even after reduction modulo 5. Thus f does not belong to H_R. This contradicts H_(R,0)=H_R in Theorem 2, p. 10. Moreover 1 and f are both admitted. Their sum h=1+f has h_2=0 and h_10=2. Its local-span condition holds because a span is additive; it is not being rejected merely because one constant term is zero. The global gamma=1 test requires h(q)h(q^(-1)) to lie in H_R. Its constants at orders 2 and 10 are 0 and 4, so p=5 gluing would require 0=4. Therefore h fails Definition 1.4. This proves directly that the global set is not closed under addition. The argument uses neither Theorem 1 nor a nonzero K-theory class. ## 3. The local span is not finitely generated Fix the same K,R,xi and p=5. Equation (14), p. 7, identifies the local base ring with H=product_((m,5)=1) Z_5[zeta_m][[x]]. Only the integral projection H->Z_5[[x]] at m=1 is needed below; no surjectivity or abstract product-decomposition theorem is used in the finite-generation obstruction. For every a>=1 define u^(a) by u_1^(a)(x)=(1+x)^(5^(-a)), u_m^(a)(x)=1 for m>1, (m,5)=1. These are formal binomial series in Q_5[[x]] with constant coefficient one, as allowed by equation (20). At the m=1 germ q=1+x, the exact formal identity (q^5)^(5^(-a))=(q^(5^(-a)))^5 makes the quotient in equation (21) equal one. Every other local component is one, and the order is preserved under fifth powers. Hence all u^(a) are admitted invertible sections, with linear coefficient 5^(-a) at m=1. Let M be their full module as defined, i.e. the H-span of every admitted invertible section. Every element of M has integral constant coefficient at m=1: all defining sections do, and finite H-linear combinations preserve it. If g_1,...,g_r generated M, write g_(i,1)=A_i+B_i x+O(x^2), A_i in Z_5, B_i in Q_5. Choose B>=0 so that every B_i lies in 5^(-B)Z_5. For h_i in H, the coefficient of x in sum h_i g_i is a sum of terms C_i B_i+D_i A_i, with C_i,D_i in Z_5. It therefore remains in 5^(-B)Z_5. It cannot produce 5^(-a) when a>B. This contradiction proves that M is not finitely generated, and in particular not free of rank one as asserted in Theorem 1, p. 9. No analytic radius condition is imposed by the printed definition. Requiring later continuation or integral slopes would be an added hypothesis, not a property established by the defining test. Lemma 3.4, equation (184), p. 39, separately requires the linear coefficient to be integral. Corollary 3.5 retains that requirement, and Lemma 3.6 equation (195), p. 41, explicitly includes it. The counterexamples exploit exactly this missing condition in (20). Adding it excludes these fractional-power examples, but a complete repair still requires checking all subsequent uses. It does not remove the constant-sign obstruction in Section 2. ## 4. The printed Gaussian normalization leaves a forbidden term Equation (110), p. 28, defines formal Gaussian contraction on R[[w,w^3/h,h]]. Equation (114), p. 29, gives the purported normalized input. Already m=1,k=0 disproves that normalization. From the defining Pochhammer product, independently, log(q*z*exp(w);q)_infty =-sum_(n>=1) z^n exp(nw)q^n/[n(1-q^n)], q=exp(h) =Li_2(z exp(w))/h+(1/2)Li_1(z exp(w))+O(h). The quadratic term in the polar Taylor expansion is Li_0(z)w^2/(2h). The printed exponential subtracts Li_0(z)w^2/h, leaving -Li_0(z)w^2/(2h). This monomial is outside the stated domain: nonnegative powers of w,w^3/h,h cannot have exponents (2,-1). At w=0 its regular logarithm is -log(1-z), so the printed psi has value (1-z)^(-1)+O(h), rather than 1+O(h). This is not merely a choice of a scalar Gaussian phase. The n-th power of the unwanted quadratic term has w^(2n)h^(-n); Gaussian contraction contributes h^n, so infinitely many nonzero terms enter the coefficient of h^0. In the formally allowed A=0 case of the t-deformed construction, equation (119) gives Lambda=-Li_0(z). The extra exponential then cancels the Gaussian kernel exactly. This example concerns the formal construction before t=1; the degenerate z=0 specialization for A=0 is not being offered as admissible data for the arithmetic Theorem 5. For general m the necessary polar subtractions are Li_2(z^m)/(m^2 h), Li_1(z^m)w/(m h), Li_0(z^m)w^2/(2h). The regular constant logarithm of the product must also be subtracted, where (114) adds it. These corrections follow by splitting the Pochhammer product into its m residue classes and expanding each factor. They identify the intended local normalization; they do not verify the repaired global identification theorem. ## 5. Equation (165) has the stated sign error Definition (32), p. 12, gives in rank one A=1,m=2,k=0 H(t)=1+q^3 t^2/[(1-q)(1-q^2)]+O(t^4). For sigma H(t)=H(qt), the coefficient of t^2 in (1-sigma)(1-q^(-1)sigma)H is q^3. The printed right side of equation (165), p. 35, gives -q^3. Thus the recurrence fails as printed independently of the Gaussian issue. For the general rank-one congruence series, let n=k+mj. Its coefficients have successive ratio c_n/c_(n-m)=(-1)^(A*m) q^(A*m*n-A*m*(m-1)/2)/(q^(n-m+1);q)_m. It follows that the corrected operator recurrence is product_(r=0)^(m-1)(1-q^(-r)sigma)H(t) =(-1)^(A*m) q^(A*m*(m+1)/2) t^m sigma^(A*m)H(t). The q-exponent in the operator prefactor is unchanged; the sign is (-1)^(A*m). The coefficient of sigma^(A*m) on the previous term is q^(A*m*(k+m(j-1))); extracting coefficients must retain that factor. The finite q-binomial expansion gives the product on the left. ## 6. Scope and implications for this project Theorem 5 explicitly restricts to root orders prime to Delta. The global collection in Section 2 becomes identically one there because its exceptional order 2 disappears. It therefore does not disprove Theorem 5's restricted arithmetic membership assertion. The local error still occurs at the good prime 5 and order 1, but it is not itself a counterexample to membership of the particular series constructed in Theorem 5. That restricted statement needs a separate audit with corrected definitions and formulas; it has not been verified or disproved here. The distinctions are: | Printed claim | Independent finding | | --- | --- | | Definition 1.3 / Theorem 1 | The admitted span need not be finitely generated. | | Definition 1.4 / Theorem 2 | The all-order zero-class set is not additive and differs from H_R. | | Equation (114) | Wrong polar subtraction and constant normalization; input leaves the stated Gaussian domain. | | Equation (165) | Wrong sign, with a direct coefficient correction. | | Restricted Theorem 5 | Not directly refuted by these examples; not independently verified here. | No result from this paper has been used as a premise of the project's A-curve torsor proofs. In particular these findings do not by themselves affect the independently derived finite cyclic norm equation or its Hilbert-90 comparison. They do rule out importing the printed unrestricted module theorems without repair. The exact diagnostics in `experiments/audit_gswz_printed_definitions.py` check the constant tests, fractional-power Frobenius identity, Gaussian expansion, and recurrence coefficients. The all-order arguments and the non-finite-generation proof are those above, not extrapolations from finite computations.

title: A Heisenberg torsor and a uniform finite period
text: # A Heisenberg torsor and a uniform finite period Research note, 25 October 2026. The purpose is structural: replace matrix-chart restrictions and individual knot calculations by an intrinsic algebraic object. Definitions of the local cyclic quantum dilogarithm already exist. The results below reconstruct its normalization as a Heisenberg torsor, give an exact finite face reduction, and identify the boundary module that any global construction must preserve. This is not a proof of the full volume conjecture. The missing assertion is identified in Section 7. In particular a splitting module, a selected period vector, and a numerical growth law are different data. The comparison with existing literature is in `structural_literature_delta.md`. No novelty is claimed for Hilbert 90, finite Heisenberg representations, cyclic dilogarithms, or Heisenberg covers of Fermat curves. ## 1. The norm equation identifies the first cover Fix an odd integer n>=3, a field k of characteristic zero containing a primitive n-th root omega, and t on U=P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. Let x^n=t. The elementary identity Norm_(k(x)/k(t))(1-x)=product_j(1-omega^j x)=1-t (1.1) is the Steinberg norm relation. It gives a direct splitting of the cyclic algebra A_t=k(t)<X,Y>/(X^n=t, Y^n=1-t, XY=omega YX). Indeed on E=k(t)[x]/(x^n-t), let X be multiplication by x and let Y f(x)=(1-x)f(omega^(-1)x). These operators satisfy all three relations. After adjoining x they are a diagonal operator with distinct eigenvalues and a cyclic shift with nonzero coefficients, and generate the full matrix algebra. Consequently A_t is already End_(k(t))(E). This proves the splitting; it does not assume a norm-residue or Brauer-group theorem. Now choose c^n=1-t. The ratio r(x)=(1-x)/c has cyclic norm one. The equation d(omega x)=r(x)d(x) (1.2) is exactly a Hilbert 90 equation over k(t,c). Its explicit solution on the cyclic spectrum, with its initial value left free, is w_0=1, w_j=c^(-j) product_(a=0)^(j-1)(1-omega^a x), d_j=s w_j, 0<=j<n. Equation (1.1) closes the recurrence at j=n. Conversely the recurrence determines all d_j from s. Thus the solution set is a G_m-torsor before normalization. This is an elementary proof of the Hilbert 90 instance needed here, rather than an invocation without a specified cocycle. One can also solve it in the cyclic function field itself. Write sigma(x)=omega*x, sigma(c)=c, and for a in k(t,c)(x) set H(a)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) w_j^(-1) sigma^j(a). The recurrence and w_n=1 give sigma H(a)=r H(a). At least one H(x^k), 0<=k<n, is nonzero: after division by x^k these expressions are the finite Fourier transform of the nonzero vector (w_j^(-1)). The Fourier matrix is invertible. This proves the required field descent constructively as well. Determinant normalization still requires its separately recorded n-th root. For the user's generic peripheral factor, put t=-M^n. Since n is odd, product_j(1+omega^j M)=1+M^n. (1.3) The factor is a cyclic norm, not a disposable numerical multiplier. An unnormalized recurrence changes its n-step central character by this factor. At M=1 it equals 2. This identifies an exact mechanism for such factors; it does not identify the multiplier of the earlier positive factorial model from its one factor-eight test. ## 2. Determinant normalization gives a Heisenberg cover Set Delta=product_(j=0)^(n-1) w_j. The determinant-one normalization of the diagonal intertwiner D=diag(d_0,...,d_(n-1)) is s^n=Delta^(-1). Because n is odd, the expression simplifies to s^n=product_(a=0)^(n-1) (1-omega^a x)^(a-(n-1)/2). (2.1) Thus all coefficients live on the finite etale cover of U T_n: x^n=t, c^n=1-t, s^n=Delta^(-1). (2.2) Its degree is n^3 as a finite locally free cover. Every factor is a unit over U, so these are actual torsors there, rather than equations silently evaluated at a branch point. There are three deck transformations, written as maps of points: A:(x,c,s) -> (omega x,c,s(1-x)/c), B:(x,c,s) -> (x,omega c,s), C:(x,c,s) -> (x,c,omega s). The norm identity and the determinant product show that they preserve (2.2). Direct substitution proves A^n=B^n=C^n=1, C central, AB=C^(-1)BA. (2.3) They give a free transitive action on every geometric fibre: A and B choose the first two roots, and C chooses the last. Therefore T_n is a torsor for the finite Heisenberg group H_n, not just an unspecified scalar normalization line. The extra central root records the failure of the first two root changes to commute on the normalized intertwiner. For comparison with the standard cyclic dilogarithm convention, let q=omega^((n+1)/2), so q^2=omega and q^n=1, and set p^-=1/c, p^+=-x/(q c). Then (p^-)^n+(p^+)^n=1 and p^-+q^(2j+1)p^+=(1-omega^j x)/c. Thus d_j is exactly the spectral cyclic-dilogarithm definition, with its determinant root retained. This is a reparameterization, not a new local quantum function. The normalization cover, viewed over t, has the explicit Heisenberg structure (2.3). If U0 e_j=omega^j e_j and P0 e_j=e_(j+1), then D U0 D^(-1)=U0, D P0 D^(-1)=P0(1-x U0)/c. (2.4) The commutant of U0,P0 consists of scalars: commuting with U0 forces a matrix to be diagonal, and commuting with P0 makes its diagonal constant. Consequently this intertwiner is unique up to scalar. Determinant one reduces the ambiguity to mu_n. A mu_n-valued algebraic function on an irreducible parameter component is constant, since its n-th power is one. This is the precise rigidity statement available for comparing two intertwiners of the same automorphism. It does not prove that two arbitrary products implement that same automorphism, nor that every projective scalar cocycle is trivial. Those are separate coherence statements. ## 3. The face contraction is an exact finite Fourier evaluation Let X be the ideal compactification of a globally branched knot exterior. Its single ideal vertex and H_1(X;Z)=0 are the topological inputs. Let r be the number of tetrahedra, and use the existing face selectors D_f=X_0-X_1+X_2, R_f=X_2-X_3, Epsilon=diag(epsilon). Work over R=Z/nZ. The following argument also works for even n; oddness is needed for the Weyl normalization in Section 5. Define the finite groups and maps V=ker D_f, T(v)=Epsilon R_f v, U(v)=X_0 v, K=ker(T:V->R^r), H=T(V), W={w in H : (U k).w=0 in R for every k in K}. (3.1) For w in W choose any v with Tv=w and put q_W(w)=-(Uv).w in R. (3.2) This is independent of the lift: changing v by k changes it by -(Uk).w, which vanishes by definition. Its polarization is bilinear, so q_W is a quadratic function on the finite abelian group W. Use self-dual Haar measure n^(-1/2) times counting measure on R. Its delta function at zero has value sqrt(n). For an arbitrary function F:R^r->C define the charged-kernel-style contraction Z_n(F)=n^(-r/2) sum_(v in V) omega^(-(Uv).Tv) F(Tv). (3.3) All signs and local spectral factors can be included in F. This is the full face measure and all r independent delta factors, not a bare unnormalized sum. **Theorem.** For every such knot triangulation, including singular face matrices and every composite n, |V|=n^r, |W|=n^r/|K|^2, Z_n(F)=|W|^(-1/2) sum_(w in W) omega^(q_W(w))F(w). (3.4) There is no limiting operation or choice of inverse face matrix. **Proof of the topological input over R.** The local cocycle lemma of `automatic_face_regularity.md` uses only addition and sign changes, so it holds over R. The universal coefficient theorem gives H^1(X;R)=Hom(H_1(X;Z),R)=0; with one ideal vertex its edge cocycles themselves vanish. Thus D_f^T has trivial kernel over R. Perfect finite character duality implies D_f is surjective, and |V|=n^r. For k in K, define a character of V/K by kappa(k)([v])=omega^(-(Uk).Tv). This is well-defined. If it is trivial, R_f^T Epsilon Uk annihilates ker D_f and hence belongs to im D_f^T. Choose a with D_f^T a+R_f^T Epsilon Uk=0. Locally write b=X_0k,c=X_2k.
