The equations D_fk=R_fk=0 give face values (b,b+c,c,c), and the last equation gives the paired position values (a,-a,a+epsilon*b,-epsilon*b). They are exactly the same local ideal edge cocycle. It vanishes, so k=0. Therefore kappa is injective. Dualizing this injection gives a surjection V/K -> K^vee. Its kernel is identified by T with W. Hence |W|=|V|/|K|^2. Finally sum (3.3) over each coset v+K. Its coefficient is omega^(-(Uv).Tv) sum_(k in K) omega^(-(Uk).Tv). Character orthogonality makes this zero outside W and |K| times the displayed phase on W. Since n^(-r/2)|K|=|W|^(-1/2), (3.4) follows, including its exact measure. QED. This formulation survives primes dividing the integer face torsion. W need not be a free R-module; its cardinality and quadratic function are the invariant data. A rational nullspace dimension cannot replace these data at such a prime. ## 4. The period is algebraic, with its normalization specified When F is a product of local cyclic-dilogarithm entries, its coefficients are algebraic functions on products of the torsors T_n. Formula (3.4) is then a finite algebraic matrix coefficient on that parameter space. Specializing an algebraic decorated holonomy gives an algebraic number, with every determinant root and Fourier factor retained. This is an exact finite period in the representation-theoretic sense. It does not yet identify it with the continuous Faddeev state. The local bridge and the additional dilogarithm period are given in `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md`. ## 5. Edge reduction gives one irreducible boundary module Here is the invariant version of the face/edge linear algebra. Let Lambda=R^(2r) with its standard alternating form. The r-1 independent edge rows span a primitive isotropic submodule E_ed. Their primitivity for odd n has a uniform proof. A dependence among all r edge rows says that in each tetrahedron the three opposite-pair sums of edge values are equal. Since 2 is invertible, such values are uniquely lambda_ij=a_i+a_j. A face's three edge values recover its three a_i, so the a_i agree across glued faces. There is one ideal vertex; the dependence is therefore the constant edge assignment. Deleting one row removes it. The same argument modulo every prime divisor of n gives a unit minor locally, hence a split injection over R. Isotropy is the local cusp-intersection cancellation already proved in `preferred_longitude_cochains.md`. The full meridian/longitude pairing is -2, a unit in R. Therefore E_ed^perp/E_ed is a free symplectic R-module of rank two, (5.1) with its generators supplied by the marked peripheral curves. It does not depend on the projection rank of a face matrix. In the r-fold clock/shift module of dimension n^r use Weyl operators W(a,b)=omega^(-a.b/2) X^a Y^b, W(v)W(w)=omega^(Omega(v,w)/2)W(v+w). For an edge character chi define the exact projector Pi_chi=|E_ed|^(-1) sum_(e in E_ed) chi(e)^(-1)W(e). All nonidentity Weyl monomials have trace zero, so rank Pi_chi=n^r/|E_ed|=n. (5.2) The boundary Weyl operators act on H_chi=im Pi_chi. For a class v in E_ed^perp/E_ed, their trace on H_chi is zero unless v=0. Their n^2 matrices are therefore trace-orthogonal and span End(H_chi). This proves irreducibility and scalar commutant directly. More generally, start with the split local cyclic algebras A_(t_j) from Section 1 over the gluing function field. The classical gluing equations make the commuting edge operators have n-th powers one. Their projector gives the same rank-n boundary module, now with the actual peripheral central characters. After a central-root extension the trace argument above applies, and descends the dimension and irreducibility assertions. Thus the interior gives a splitting of the boundary cyclic algebra on its gluing field. This is a uniform quantum Hamiltonian reduction. Singular face projections are alternate presentations of the same reduction, rather than additional species of quantum states. ### 5.1 Reduction of the torsor itself On a nondegenerate gluing chart pull back one T_n for each classical tetrahedral coordinate t_j. Push out their r central mu_n groups by multiplication, with the recorded orientation convention. The product cover becomes a torsor P for the Heisenberg extension of Lambda. In Weyl coordinates this group has law (v,z)(w,z')=(v+w,zz'*omega^(Omega(v,w)/2)). Choosing the inverse central generator matches (2.3); orthogonals and the reduction are unchanged. All fixed signs in edge central characters are incorporated before the next step. For an edge monomial product_j t_j^a_j(1-t_j)^b_j=1, its root eta=product_j x_j^a_j c_j^b_j is mu_n-valued. These roots give a moment map P -> E_ed^vee. In root coordinates the edge vector is e=(b,-a); under a deck vector v, eta_e(p.v)=eta_e(p)*omega^(Omega(e,v)). For a prescribed character chi its fibre P_chi is a torsor for the preimage H(E_ed^perp). The Weyl lift of E_ed is central in that subgroup by isotropy. Its quotient is a torsor for H(E_ed^perp)/E_ed = H(E_ed^perp/E_ed). (5.3) This is the Heisenberg group of one boundary pair. Indeed on each geometric fibre, primitivity makes Lambda -> E_ed^vee surjective with kernel E_ed^perp. Each moment fibre is nonempty and transitive with that stabilizer; quotienting its free E_ed action proves (5.3). These finite etale constructions descend. Thus a boundary H_n-torsor is constructed on every gluing chart, without a proper-face hypothesis or an angle limit. Identifying its period section on the intrinsic decorated character space remains the global task; a quotient group alone does not identify the section. The later [pointed tetrahedron gluing theorem](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md) extends the edge-lattice step to all levels for S^3 link exteriors. Its integral argument includes the missing prime 2 and proves primitivity without a global branching. With the full Weyl phases retained, the saturated boundary reduction has dimension N^c at every N for c cusps. The marked unhalved peripheral rows are a separate issue: their pairing -2 can give an index-two lattice, whose algebra has two sectors at even levels. The earlier odd-n identification with the full marked boundary algebra is therefore not extended by silently inverting 2. The subsequent [integral half-longitude proof](integral_half_longitude.md) now identifies the saturation for a knot as the marked meridian and half of its preferred longitude. A mod-two dual-face cocycle and nullhomology of the longitude give this integral result before N is chosen. The Weyl lift then has TY=q^2 YT; its square retains the full edge character. Matching the actual central longitude, source and selected period still requires comparison. ## 6. The torsor that still has to be globalized For two presentations over an identified decorated-character function field, with matched peripheral lifts, let H_X,H_Y be these irreducible boundary modules. Their module-intertwiner space I_XY=Hom_(A_boundary)(H_X,H_Y) is one-dimensional. Its invertible part is a G_m-torsor; a specified identification of determinant lines reduces it to a mu_n-torsor. Hilbert 90 handles descent of a specified multiplicative cocycle at the function-field level. It neither chooses a canonical section nor trivializes an arbitrary mu_n or degree-two obstruction. The local module has a canonical vacuum, the unit killed by X+Y-1, as proved in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md`. Tensoring these units and applying the edge projector gives an algebraic candidate J_X=Pi_chi(1 tensor ... tensor 1) in H_X. It can vanish on a locus; irreducibility of its ambient module has not removed that possibility. A face contraction such as (3.4) is a scalar period. Matching its boundary cut and frames to this projected vector is an additional comparison, not an already proved consequence of the scalar formula. The relevant object is therefore the pointed splitting module (H_X,[J_X]), together with its normalization line. An unpointed intertwiner exists uniformly; proving that it takes [J_X] to [J_Y] is the actual state-invariance assertion. Calling the unpointed intertwiner line a torsor does not discharge that assertion. The intended intrinsic object is the pointed boundary splitting module with the reduced Heisenberg/dilogarithm period torsor. Its global definition must identify the gluing charts of decorated flat local systems and verify one universal quantum five-term coherence. A list of individually certified knot triangulations cannot substitute for that statement. ## 7. What rigidity can prove, and the remaining volume assertion Once two normalized constructions are sections of the same pointed intertwiner line and implement the same quantum automorphism, their ratio is mu_n-valued and constant on each irreducible lifted parameter component. One normalization fixes their exact equality there; descent must still respect the deck transformations (2.3). This is the useful algebraic rigidity mechanism. The classical dilogarithm regulator is a value of the corresponding period torsor, rather than an asymptotic definition of hyperbolic volume. The requested conjecture still needs a uniform comparison of the normalized quantum period with that classical regulator. Fixed-level Zariski rigidity alone supplies no comparison between different n: the covers T_n and their period vectors vary with n. The theory should replace repeated saddle computations by this single compatibility theorem; at present that theorem has not been proved. The next proof obligations are consequently structural: 1. Construct the pointed period object on the intrinsic decorated character space and prove its universal five-term descent. 2. Match its normalization and cycle with the existing Faddeev state, using the exact local rational-parameter bridge. 3. Prove compatibility of its normalized size with the dilogarithm regulator on the complete geometric class, uniformly in the class of knots requested by the user. These preserve the full objective. The finite reductions and torsor identification above are tools toward it, not a redefinition of success. The subsequent pointed recoupling, period-descent and frame-transport notes now prove local selected-vector coherence and full projective matrix covariance on the stated root covers. In particular `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` supplies the operator comparison, determinant normalization and identity anchor needed to apply the rigidity mechanism of this section. Actual vector transport is essential: the unit in an endpoint frame is generally not taken to the new unit. The intrinsic equivariant knot period, its literature cycle and the regulator comparison across levels are still outstanding.

title: All finite quantum-normal orders have bounded Frobenius degree
text: # All finite quantum-normal orders have bounded Frobenius degree Research theorem and independent exact audit, 27 October 2026. For the ACTUAL integral high-color R-matrices, the coefficient of delta^j, after factoring the root signed block permutation, has Frobenius PBW degree at most 2j. The bound is uniform in the level, color multiplicity, number of crossings, and number of braid strands. The canonical actual divided sources obey the same relative bound after their root unipotent rotations. Orders two and three are sharp. This extends the [first-normal theorem](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md) using the original finite integral matrices, not an assumed formal quantum group lift. It does not identify the two geometric framing currents, bound the numerical coefficient sizes, or prove a regulator norm of the selected period. ## 1. Actual family, frame and filtration Fix N>=2 and r>=0. Use D_m(q), m=N(r+1)-1, in the constant sign frame \(w_{a,s}=(-1)^{Na(a-1)/2+as}u_{aN+s}\) of [the high-color source proof](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). Put q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and delta=1-Q^N. All quantum derivatives below use the actual local branch \[ q=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}. \tag{1.1} \] Retain its marked half-Cartan root. The root multiplicity generators are e,f,h of Sym^r, with \(ew_a=(r-a+1)w_{a-1}\), \(fw_a=(a+1)w_{a+1}\), \(hw_a=(r-2a)w_a\). Write A=(r-h)/2 for the block number. Give e,f,h degree one and arbitrary head matrices degree zero. On b strands use total degree in U(sl2^b). The root crossing is its original head matrix times the block flip and parity \(\varepsilon^{A_1+A_2}\), \(\varepsilon=(-1)^m\). This whole signed permutation is retained separately, not replaced by a bounded-degree polynomial in A_1,A_2. Root conjugation by it preserves the filtration: permutations exchange Lie factors, parity changes the signs of e,f and fixes h, and heads only conjugate the head matrix coefficients. **All-order crossing theorem.** For \(R(\delta)=\sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jR_j\), either crossing sign satisfies \[ R_0^{-1}R_j\ \in\ U_{\le2j}(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{1.2} \] Coefficients may depend on N,r and the marked root. There is no uniform archimedean bound on their sizes in (1.2). ## 2. Quantum-integer jets have controlled polynomial block degree Write an integer argument as l=AN+s, 0<=s<N. With z=Log(q/q_N), \[ [AN+s]_q=(-1)^A \frac{q_N^s e^{(AN+s)z}-q_N^{-s}e^{-(AN+s)z}}{q-q^{-1}}. \tag{2.1} \] The coefficient of z^j after the sign is a polynomial in A of degree at most j. If s!=0, the constant coefficient is nonzero and independent of A. If s=0, division by delta gives \[ \frac{[AN]_q}{\delta}=(-1)^{A+1}\frac{A}{\rho_N} \left(1+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^jP_j(A)\right), \qquad \deg P_j\le j,\quad \rho_N=q_N-q_N^{-1}. \tag{2.2} \] To prove (2.2), factor A z from the numerator sinh(ANz), and factor z from delta=1-exp(2Nz). The other factors are formal units. The remaining coefficient of z^j has A-degree at most j. Substitution \(z=\operatorname{Log}(1-\delta)/(2N)\) preserves this bound. This proves both statements without any unramified-root or nonresonance hypothesis on an algebraic shape. For a product of any number of such factors, its extra normal order j has extra block-polynomial degree at most j: the orders chosen from its factors sum to j. Denominator units depending on k,N,r but not the input block do not change this conclusion. ## 3. Every transfer has an exact valuation and divided factor Write its transfer k=aN+b, 0<=b<N. For input heads s,t, put \[ c_E=a+\mathbf1_{s<b},\qquad c_F=a+\mathbf1_{t+b\ge N}. \tag{3.1} \] These are its actual E and F block changes. The E numerator of E^(k)=E^k/[k]_q! crosses c_E multiples of N, while its denominator crosses a. The corresponding F counts are c_F and a. Hence \[ \begin{split} E^{(k)}_{s',s} &=\delta^{c_E-a}e^{c_E} \sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jP_{j,s}(A),\\ F^{(k)}_{t',t} &=\delta^{c_F-a}f^{c_F} \sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jQ_{j,t}(A),\\ \deg P_{j,s},\deg Q_{j,t}&\le j, \quad s'=s-b\pmod N,\quad t'=t+b\pmod N. \tag{3.2} \end{split} \] Constants depending on the recorded heads and parameters are included in the polynomials. Their order is literal: the polynomial is evaluated on the INPUT block before e^c or f^c acts. Both exponents c_E-a,c_F-a are zero or one. Here are the sign and boundary details. The zero numerator factors in E supply \(\prod_{h=0}^{c_E-1}(r-A+1+h)\), precisely the coefficient of e^(c_E). Those in F supply \(\prod_{h=1}^{c_F}(A+h)\), precisely f^(c_F). Every higher jet remains divisible by these products by (2.2). Thus the expression vanishes at the actual finite boundaries; it is not an interpolation outside the color. The constant beta gauge also cancels ALL input-block signs, for arbitrary k. For E, the sum of the integer parts in its k numerator arguments is -kA plus an A-independent integer. Its beta quotient has exponent \[ kA-Nc_E(c_E+1)/2+c_Es'. \tag{3.3} \] For F the numerator sign has exponent +kA plus a constant, and its beta quotient has exponent \[ -kA-Nc_F(c_F-1)/2-c_Ft'. \tag{3.4} \] The block signs cancel in each case. All remaining signs are head and transfer constants. Formula (2.1) shows the SAME sign accompanies every jet, so no hidden parity character occurs in (3.2). The actual nilpotent R term is \[ q^{k(k-1)/2}\rho^k[k]_q! E^{(k)}\otimes F^{(k)}. \tag{3.5} \] Since [k]_q! has delta-order a, this term's exact possible starting order is \[ \nu=c_E+c_F-a =a+\mathbf1_{s<b}+\mathbf1_{t+b\ge N}. \tag{3.6} \] At total nilpotent order j>=nu, its PBW degree is at most \[ c_E+c_F+(j-\nu)=j+a\le2j. \tag{3.7} \] In particular only k<(j+1)N can contribute to order j, however large the actual color is. This includes all resonant tails and all head boundary carries, not only the first one. ## 4. Cartan, inverses and arbitrary words The output unrolled weights are affine in the two input blocks. The varying part of the Cartan is \(\exp(zH_1H_2/2)\). Its delta^j coefficient is a polynomial of block degree at most 2j. Its ROOT value is the head Cartan times the original parity \(\varepsilon^{A_{1,out}+A_{2,out}}\). Relative to input parity this adds only \(\varepsilon^{c_F-c_E}\), a head/transfer sign. Combining the Cartan order j-l with (3.7) at nilpotent order l gives \[ 2(j-l)+(l+a)\le2j. \] This proves (1.2) for positive crossings. Multiplication by the inverse root head matrix changes only head coefficients. For the other sign, write R=R_0(I+sum_(j>=1)delta^j A_j). The inverse interaction coefficients obey \(B_j=-A_j-\sum_{l=1}^{j-1}A_lB_{j-l}\). Induction gives degree at most 2j. The necessary root conjugations and checked flips preserve the filtration by Section 1. Thus BOTH signs satisfy the same theorem. For every braid word W, product differentiation at any finite order is a sum of products of root-conjugated local interactions. Their normal orders add to j and their PBW degrees add to at most 2j. Hence, on arbitrarily many strands, \[ W_0^{-1}W_j\in U_{\le2j}(\mathfrak{sl}_2^b) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}).\tag{4.1} \] No growing word length changes the degree bound, although it changes its coefficients and number of terms. ## 5. Pivots, full scalar factors and knot closure A whole pivot factor K(q)^c=q^(cH) has normal order-j coefficient of block degree at most j, for any specified integer c, including c=1-N. Thus ordinary and frozen ADO pivotal families and their EXACT normal adapter K^(-N) satisfy the filtration. The matching integral twist is a scalar and does not raise the degree. A regular marked external scalar line, including the canceled complete germ of d_N(M), likewise changes no Fr degree. If a retained scalar has a genuine pole of normal order p, its Laurent coefficient at order j instead uses the reduced bound 2(j+p); its valuation must not be erased before applying the bound. For a one-knot closure, the root Frobenius permutation has one cycle. Its ordered partial trace multiplies all inserted Fr words along that component. Their total degree stays at most 2j. Moving them through the retained parity factors only changes signs; the total uninserted parity on the knot is even. Thus the full order-j long matrix is in End(head) tensor U_(<=2j)(sl2). There is a corresponding exact hierarchy of Ward identities for the ACTUAL ORDINARY integral ribbon family, with pivot K(q) and matching twist: its generic long matrix is C_(N(r+1))(Q) times identity, so every nonscalar Fr coefficient vanishes at every normal order. For r>=2j the image of U_(<=2j)(sl2) has adjoint spins 0,1,...,2j, of dimensions 1,3,...,4j+1. Highest vectors e^l and their successive commutators with f exhibit these summands; their dimensions add to (2j+1)^2. Hence precisely \[ (2j+1)^2-1=4j(j+1) \tag{5.1} \] nonscalar head coefficient identities follow. For r<2j replace 2j by r in this count. Casimir powers only change the scalar part. Frozen ADO auxiliary closures still satisfy the DEGREE bound, but need not be generically scalar. Their scalar Ward hierarchy requires the full pivotal/source adapter, not root pivot equality alone. This is a finite exact hierarchy for every prescribed normal depth. It is not the claim that the divided Hopf action on arbitrary tensor products is primitive, or that its selected geometric image is nonzero. ## 6. The actual whole divided sources have the same relative bound Set \(F_N(\delta)=F^{(N)}(q)\) and \(E_N(\delta)=\tau E^{(N)}(q)\), where tau=(-1)^(Nr-1). The case k=N of (3.2) has NO head carry and gives \[ F_N=f+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^j F_j,\qquad E_N=e+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^j E_j,\qquad F_j,E_j\in U_{\le j+1}(\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{6.1} \] The heads here are diagonal residue strings. Their exact source operators are finite exponentials, as in the actual high-color note. For a fixed source parameter t define \[ A(\delta,t)=e^{-tf}\exp(tF_N(\delta)). \] It satisfies A(0,t)=I and the exact interaction ODE \[ \partial_t A=e^{-t\operatorname{ad}f}(F_N-f)A. \tag{6.2} \] Root adjoint unipotent conjugation preserves every PBW degree. Its series is finite on each filtered piece, since ad f is nilpotent there. At normal order l>=1 the coefficient on the right of (6.2) has degree at most l+1<=2l. Solving its coefficient recursion by integration and products therefore gives \[ [\delta^j]A(\delta,t)\in U_{\le2j}. \tag{6.3} \] The same proof applies to exp(-ue)exp(uE_N), and to the right interaction exp(uE_N)exp(-ue). Consequently the original source and co-source jets, after their recorded root unipotent rotations, are obtained by degree-at-most-2j operators on their fixed rank-one source and dual. This is an operator result, not a criterion which assumes such jets exist. There is a still more concrete finite source bound. Formula (3.2) for k=N says F_j=f P_j(A) and E_j=e Q_j(A), with polynomial degree at most j. The F interaction stays in the Borel algebra generated by f,A, and the E interaction in that generated by e,A. On the highest source v_0, A v_0=0. After the root unipotent rotation the order-j source vector therefore lies in \[ \operatorname{span}\{v_0,fv_0,\ldots,f^{2j}v_0\}. \tag{6.4} \] The rotated dual is supported on the corresponding first 2j+1 dual descendants. To see it, order the Borel monomials with A against the highest source or dual; the degree bound limits the remaining raising or lowering power to 2j. Thus fixed quantum depth B needs at most 2B+1 Fr source descendants, independently of N and r, while the full root coherent/prequantum source is retained by its exact unipotent frame. The actual normalization units U_s(q;t,u) of the two-flag source are still retained. Their inverses are head-diagonal scalar formal series on 1+tu!=0, so they do not increase Fr degree. This does not bound their coefficient norms or permit evaluating them at the source wall 1+tu=0. The rank-one root coupon itself is NOT asserted to lie in PBW degree zero. The precise coupon statement is a sum of left-degree-2a and right-degree-2b operators around that fixed coupon, with a+b<=j. Conflating this relative bound with a small-degree polynomial formula for the rank-one projector would be false when r is large. ## 7. Clock gauges and the exact coherent source realization The [actual coherent dictionary](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md) turns (1.2) and (6.3), at any fixed depth B, into differential operators of order at most 2B. Its one-sided connection terms and all finite polynomial endpoints remain exact. A controlled gauge G=V^A, with V the cyclic HEAD shift, is not a plain polynomial Fr operator. In a head Fourier basis it is a finite sum of head projectors times clocks Q_N^(cA). Enlarge the filtration by giving those clocks degree zero. Their conjugation rescales e,f and fixes h, so this crossed-product filtration is multiplicative and Ad G preserves it. The coherent source realizes these clocks as the exact finite dilations and source characters of the two-clock note, not as differential operators of falsely bounded order. Thus after this controlled clock gauge the PBW part still has degree at most 2j, but genuine whole dilation factors must be retained. Arbitrary quantum-normal gauges or source-wall divisions have NOT been declared filtration-preserving. No assertion here bounds the number of dilation factors, gives a fixed finite-type whole comparison, identifies the internal framing-current image, or derives the volume limit from local jets. The result supplies actual bounded-normal-order operators and source jets for those further exact comparisons. ## 8. Independent exact checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_all_normal_filtration.py) uses polynomial Gaussian recursion and genuine truncated series through delta^3, including the full half-Cartan phase. At N=2,3,4 and r=8 it checks 83,000 actual coefficient jets and 1,584 shiftwise PBW-polynomial membership conditions. The r=8 spaces make the bounds at orders two and three nonvacuous. The k=0 Cartan component fails degree 2j-1 at both orders: 2j is sharp. It also checks 48 actual source OPERATOR jets after root unipotent rotation, rather than only their value on one vector, and verifies the full actual positive/negative R inverse through order three on a separate small high color. No division by a vanishing factorial is used in the test: Gaussian entries are multiplied by [k]! before specializing. [Results](../experiments/high_color_all_normal_filtration_results.json).

title: The actual first normal high-color crossing has Frobenius degree at most two
text: # The actual first normal high-color crossing has Frobenius degree at most two Research proof and exact audit, 27 October 2026. The first \(\delta=1-Q^N\) coefficient of the actual integral high-color crossing is a quadratic operator on the classical Frobenius multiplicity variables, with arbitrary finite head coefficients. The first resonant tail has a universal exact factorization. Both statements retain the full Cartan and mixed block signs. This is an actual first-normal crossing theorem. It does not identify whole low/high color jets or construct the full two-current Gaussian source map. The normal variable differentiates the original generic integral matrix family with its ordinary pivotal data. A frozen root ADO pivot is a different off-root source and requires its explicit route adapter; no scalarity of that frozen family is assumed. ## 1. Actual matrices and the filtration being used Use [the high integral color](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md), with dimension \(N(r+1)\), \(m=N(r+1)-1\), and the constant sign basis \(w_{a,s}\), \(0\le a\le r\), \(0\le s<N\). At the root the ordinary head matrices are independent of a. The divided matrices are \[ \mathsf E=[E^N/[N]_q!]_{q_N}=\tau e_{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \mathsf F=[F^N/[N]_q!]_{q_N}=f_{\mathrm{cl}}, \qquad \tau=(-1)^{Nr-1}. \] The root block number is \(a=(r-h_{\mathrm{cl}})/2\), so multiplication by a is a degree-one classical enveloping operator. Give \(e_{\mathrm{cl}},f_{\mathrm{cl}},h_{\mathrm{cl}}\) PBW degree one. On two strands use total degree for \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2)\). Head matrix coefficients have degree zero. The full root crossing also has its literal block flip and parity \(\varepsilon^{a+b}\), \(\varepsilon=(-1)^m\); these are retained separately, not asserted to be bounded-degree polynomials in a,b. Write \(R(\delta)=R_0+\delta R_1+O(\delta^2)\). Then \[ R_0^{-1}R_1\in U_{\le2}(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{1} \] This assertion is uniform in N and r. Its scalar coefficients may depend on N,r and the marked root. It is not a uniform numerical norm bound on those coefficients. ## 2. Transfer orders and the universal resonant factor The full positive un-checked R is \[ q^{H\otimes H/2} \sum_{k\ge0}q^{k(k-1)/2}\rho^k[k]_q!\, E^{(k)}\otimes F^{(k)}, \qquad E^{(k)}=E^k/[k]_q!,\quad \rho=q-q^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Each divided matrix has regular integral Gaussian entries. The factor \([k]_q!\) has \(\delta\)-order \(\lfloor k/N\rfloor\), since every positive multiple of N contributes one simple zero. Hence all \(k\ge2N\) transfers vanish modulo \(\delta^2\). For \(k=N+b\), \(0\le b<N\), divided-power multiplication gives \[ D_{N+b}= \frac{q^{N(N-1)/2+Nb}\rho^N[N]_q!} {{N+b\brack b}_q}\, D_b\,(E^{(N)}\otimes F^{(N)}), \tag{3} \] where \(D_k\) denotes the k-th term of the nilpotent sum in (2). This is an exact generic identity before taking a normal coefficient. At the root, \[ {N+b\brack b}_{q_N}=(-1)^b,\qquad q_N^{Nb}=(-1)^b, \] so these factors cancel. Also \[ \left[ q^{N(N-1)/2}\rho^N[N]_q!/\delta \right]_{q_N} =N(-1)^{N-1}=:\kappa_N . \tag{4} \] Indeed \(\rho^N[N]_q!= (-1)^Nq^{-N(N+1)/2}(Q;Q)_N\), and \((Q;Q)_{N-1}=N\). Therefore the entire first resonant tail is \[ [R_{\ge N}/\delta]_{q_N} =\kappa_N R_0(\mathsf E\otimes\mathsf F). \tag{5} \] Equation (5) includes checked crossings as written: the divided operator is on the INPUT, to the right. The same full root R, including the mixed parity and original common half-Cartan line, must be used. Moving an isolated factor through it without its sign would change this statement. The Frobenius degree of (5) is two. ## 3. Nonresonant head terms have degree at most one Fix \(k<N\). In \(E^k\) or \(F^k\) at most one head boundary can be crossed. If neither side crosses, every factor is \([AN+s]_q\), \(s\not\equiv0\bmod N\). With \(\delta=1-q^{2N}\), its first derivative at the root is, apart from the root sign \((-1)^A\), affine in A: \[ \left.\partial_\delta[AN+s]_q\right|_0 =-\frac{(-1)^A}{2N} \left[ \frac{(AN+s)(q_N^s+q_N^{-s})}{\rho_N} -[s]_{q_N}\frac{q_N+q_N^{-1}}{\rho_N} \right]. \tag{6} \] The constant beta gauge cancels every block-dependent root sign in the ordinary head coefficient. Differentiating a product once therefore gives a degree-one polynomial in the two block numbers. If E crosses one boundary, its one vanishing integer has first normal value proportional to \(r-a+1\). The other head factors are nonzero. In the beta gauge its remaining sign is independent of a: for input head s<k the total sign is \((-1)^{kr+1+s}\). Thus this contribution is an actual \(e_{\mathrm{cl}}\) factor with a head coefficient. The F boundary likewise gives \(b+1\), hence \(f_{\mathrm{cl}}\), with no remaining block-dependent sign. If both sides cross, their two zeros give order \(\delta^2\), so nothing survives in the first normal. The remaining factors \(\rho^k\), \(q^{k(k-1)/2}\), and \([k]_q!^{-1}\) are regular head-dependent scalars for \(k<N\). They do not raise the Frobenius degree. Hence the entire nonresonant nilpotent first-normal coefficient has degree at most one after the retained root parity is factored. ## 4. The Cartan part raises the bound to two The unrolled weight is \(H_{a,s}=m-2s-2Na\). Since \(q=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\), \[ \left.\partial_\delta q^{H_1H_2/2}\right|_0 =-\frac{H_1H_2}{4N} q_N^{H_1H_2/2}. \tag{7} \] The multiplier is quadratic in a,b. Its product with a first-normal boundary or resonant term is second order and does not enter R_1. Equations (5)--(7) prove that, after factoring the root signed block swap, every head matrix coefficient of R_1 has total Frobenius degree at most two. The root crossing is a signed block flip tensored with the original head crossing. Conjugation by it preserves the PBW degree: the flip permutes the two Lie algebras, parity changes the signs of e,f and leaves h fixed, and the head factor only changes head coefficients. This proves the interaction form (1). For a negative crossing, differentiation of the exact inverse gives \[ (R^{-1})_1=-R_0^{-1}R_1R_0^{-1}. \] The same root conjugation argument proves the identical degree bound. The root half-Cartan and zero-framing factors are never replaced by their ideal numerical values. A coherent realization of the classical multiplicity variables turns (1) into a differential operator of order at most two, with its one-sided source/dual connection terms retained. It does not make the entire divided Hopf action primitive or remove its mixed coproduct terms. ## 5. The same bound holds for every braid word and its knot closure This local filtration is stable under arbitrary word composition. Let W(delta) be any fixed braid word on b high-colored strands. The derivative of a product, written in its interaction frame, is a sum of conjugates of the local interactions R_0^(-1)R_1. Every root factor is its head crossing times a signed permutation of the Frobenius factors. These permutations exchange generators and their parity factors change only the signs of e,f. Therefore W_0^(-1)W_1 lies in U_(<=2)(sl2^b) tensor End(all heads). (8) There is no crossing-count or bridge-count restriction on (8). Its coefficients and number of terms may depend on the word; the enveloping DEGREE stays at most two. A root pivot has no block dependence, and its first normal coefficient is affine in the unrolled weight, hence of degree at most one. The original zero-framing twist is a scalar on each generic integral color and introduces no extra Frobenius degree. Now close all but one strand of a braid whose closure is one knot. For the scalar Ward corollary below, use the ACTUAL generic ordinary integral ribbon family, with pivot K(q) and its matching zero-framing twist. Its reduced scalar is C_n(q). The root comparison with the ADO pivot was proved with its explicit signs; it is not an equality of those pivotal families off the root. The root Frobenius permutation has one cycle. In its partial trace, the Frobenius factors of any inserted monomial are multiplied in their order along that component. Degrees add to at most two. Transporting them past parity operators changes only their recorded signs. The total parity around the uninserted component is even, as in the high-color closure proof. Consequently the first normal long-knot matrix has C_1 in End(head) tensor U_(<=2)(sl2), (9) with the actual pivots, twist and ordered insertions retained. This is a statement about the full matrix before choosing a new source or identifying an internal geometric frame. There are exact resulting Ward identities. The generic actual integral-color long-knot operator is C_n(q) times identity, so its first normal coefficient (9) is also scalar. For r>=2 the image of U_(<=2)(sl2) under the adjoint classical action is the sum of spins zero, one and two, of dimensions 1,3,5. This follows directly by the highest vectors 1,e,e^2 and repeated commutation with f; their distinct h-weights and the nonzero raising strings make the three summands independent. The quadratic Casimir only changes the scalar summand in the given representation. Thus all eight nonscalar spin-one and spin-two coefficients of (9) vanish as head matrices. Its scalar head coefficient is the actual derivative of C_n(q) times the head identity. These are finite exact source identities for an arbitrary knot, and their coherent differential realization is given by the [actual two-flag Ward dictionary](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md). They do not by themselves identify the relevant geometric current or prove that a selected geometric period survives. If one instead freezes the auxiliary ADO pivot to K(q)^(1-N) off the root, the matrix-degree bound (9) still holds: its normal pivot contribution is still degree one. Its generic long matrix need not be scalar, however. The eight vanishing coefficients then require the exact pivotal/normal source adapter and do not follow from root-only pivotal equality. This qualification is essential to the final Ward corollary, not to (1), (5), or (8). ## 6. Independent exact tests [The audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_first_normal_r_degree.py) assembles the ACTUAL integral R entries over a finite field and its dual numbers, using polynomial Gaussian recursion before specialization. A primitive fourth-level root retains the full half-Cartan phase. Its dual parameter is exactly \(q=q_N(1-\delta/(2N))\). At \((N,r)=(2,3),(3,3),(4,4),(5,3)\), it checks: * all transfers \(k\ge2N\) vanish to first order; * 3112 resonant coefficient identities (5), including boundaries; * all 174 nonzero head blocks of the parity-stripped first normal lie in the exact PBW-degree-two span; * some blocks do not lie in degree one, so the quadratic bound is genuinely needed in these examples. The PBW span is computed independently from the classical e,f,h matrices, with modular pivot rows and exact reconstruction; no proposed coefficient decomposition is supplied to the test. [Results](../experiments/high_color_first_normal_r_degree_results.json) record the ranks and level data. These checks support the uniform proof; they are not a selected-period or global-current theorem. The [actual-source audit](high_color_wall_source_independent_audit.md) checks the high integral matrix, divided source and Ward dictionary used here. The [memory-clock proof](actual_memory_clock_and_normal_transfer.md) then applies this crossing bound with its exact first-normal carry factors and independently checked inverse crossing.

title: Two actual clocks and the compact Frobenius source orbit
text: # Two actual clocks and the compact Frobenius source orbit Research construction, 27 October 2026. The high integral color has an exact whole source with a head clock and a Frobenius block clock. The latter is invisible at the root but survives in its first quantum normal. The divided-source orbit is the same twisted cotangent surface as the compact coherent source, with its actual weight-N prequantum clutch. These identities use original integral matrices, not an abstract extra SL2 representation. No identification of both internal geometric framing currents is made. In particular, a Frobenius block index is not a crossing transfer, and equality of low/high root periods does not equate their whole quantum-normal lifts. ## 1. The canonical actual two-flag source retraction Use [the high integral color](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md), with dimension N(r+1), basis w_(k,s), 0<=k<=r, 0<=s<N, q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and Z=Q^N. The actual whole divided matrices give on each s-string \[ \Psi_s(q)=\exp(F^{(N)}(q))w_{0,s},\qquad \Lambda_s(q)=2^{-r}w_{0,s}^*\exp(\tau E^{(N)}(q)). \] Let Rw_(k,s)=k w_(k,s). Introduce independent source/dual coordinates t,u and retain their normalization as an ACTUAL whole germ: \[ \begin{split} U_s(q;t,u)&=\Lambda_s(q)(tu)^R\Psi_s(q),\\ I_{t,u}(q)e_s&=t^R\Psi_s(q),\\ P_{t,u}(q)|_{s\text{-string}} &=U_s(q;t,u)^{-1}\Lambda_s(q)u^R. \end{split} \tag{1.1} \] Here P returns the scalar coefficient in the s-th head basis vector. At the root \[ U_s(q_N;t,u)=2^{-r}(1+tu)^r. \tag{1.2} \] Thus on 1+tu!=0, these are regular whole source/co-source germs, and P I=I_N exactly. All derivatives of U_s are retained. Their normalized weights need not be binomial away from the root. A chosen normalized head source and co-source may be attached to this retraction. For example a head coherent parameter h gives diagonal weights \[ H_s(h)={N-1\choose s}\frac{h^s}{(1+h)^{N-1}}. \tag{1.3} \] This is an explicit ordinary polynomial coherent cut in the specified head frame; transport the source and its dual together if a different actual head basis is used. Their diagonal weights (1.3) are unchanged by that diagonal frame transport. No claim that its ordinary SL2 action is the quantum braid action is required. The resulting normalized functional on the actual high color is \(\Phi_{h;t,u}(C)=\lambda_hP_{t,u}CI_{t,u}\psi_h\). For the actual scalar high-color long-knot matrix it gives the SAME whole ordinary color period C_(N(r+1))(Q), since lambda_h psi_h=1 and PI=I. At q_N this is K_N. The original external ADO modified dimension line remains the one in the high-color source note. ## 2. The two-clock character is an exact whole rational expression Let Jw_(k,s)=(kN+s)w_(k,s), and Sw_(k,s)=s w_(k,s). The fixed integer floor is retained, and \[ J=S+NR,\qquad Q^J=Q^S Z^R. \tag{2.1} \] Define A=Q^S and B=Z^R as actual diagonal operators. At the root B=I, while A is the original nontrivial head clock. For all integer a,b the source character is exactly \[ \Phi_{h;t,u}(A^aB^b) =\sum_{s=0}^{N-1}H_s(h)Q^{as} \frac{U_s(q;tZ^b,u)}{U_s(q;t,u)}. \tag{2.2} \] Equation (2.2) is an identity of whole q-germs, including their actual divided-factorial coefficients and normalization units. It is not obtained by extending root binomial weights arbitrarily. At q_N, (2.2) is independent of t,u and equals \([(1+hQ_N^a)/(1+h)]^{N-1}\). Consequently a root observable depending only on Q^J loses the independent Frobenius source coordinate. ## 3. Its first quantum normal recovers the block moment exactly Write D_Q for Q partial_Q along the actual q-family, so D_Q is one half of q partial_q. Put x=tu and \[ \mu=r x/(1+x). \] For a diagonal insertion f(A,B) independent of q except through these clocks, the exact first-normal identity is \[ \left.D_Q\Phi_{h;t,u}(f(A,B))\right|_{q_N} =\sum_sH_s(h) [sA\partial_A+N\mu B\partial_B] f(A,B)|_{A=Q_N^s,B=1}. \tag{3.1} \] Any explicit coefficient derivative of f must be added if present. To prove (3.1), write the normalized s-string weights as w_(k,s)(q). Their sum is exactly one, hence their derivatives sum to zero. At the root f(A,1) is independent of k, so every derivative of the WHOLE source/co-source weights cancels. The remaining clock derivative is \(sA\partial_A+NkB\partial_B\). The root weights are \({r\choose k}x^k/(1+x)^r\), whose mean is mu. This cancellation does not set the individual source derivatives to zero; many are nonzero in the exact audit. In particular, for r>0, \[ \Phi(A)|_{q_N}=\left(\frac{1+hQ_N}{1+h}\right)^{N-1}, \qquad \frac1{Nr}\left.D_Q\Phi(B)\right|_{q_N} =\frac{tu}{1+tu}. \tag{3.2} \] The first depends nontrivially on h, and the second nontrivially on x=tu. Their Jacobian in h,x is nonzero away from the explicit denominators and the zero of 1+hQ_N. Thus root plus first-normal data give TWO independent source coordinates, even though all zeroth-order block-clock values are one. For the required r=N, the normalization in the second expression is N^2 exactly. The block number is intrinsic to the actual root divided action: \(R=(r-[e_{\mathrm{cl}},f_{\mathrm{cl}}])/2\). Its clock satisfies \(Bf_{\mathrm{cl}}B^{-1}=Zf_{\mathrm{cl}}\) and \(Be_{\mathrm{cl}}B^{-1}=Z^{-1}e_{\mathrm{cl}}\). These are literal finite matrix identities for the graded source, not an assumed scalar holonomy character. ## 4. The actual divided-source orbit is the compact source surface For r>=1, on the root multiplicity factor the source and dual are \[ \psi(t)=\sum_{k=0}^rt^kv_k,\qquad \lambda(t,u)(v_k)={r\choose k}\frac{u^k}{(1+tu)^r}. \] The actual divided generators in the high-color proof give exact normalized moments \[ E=\lambda e_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi/r=\frac{t}{1+tu},\quad F=\lambda f_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi/r=\frac{u}{1+tu},\quad H=\lambda h_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi/r=\frac{1-tu}{1+tu}. \tag{4.1} \] They satisfy H^2+4EF=1. These are single-insertion matrix moments, not an assertion that products of expectations equal expectations of products. The corresponding coadjoint projector convention is \[ \mathcal J(t,u)= 2\frac{(1,t)^t(1,u)}{1+tu}-I =\begin{pmatrix}H&2F\\2E&-H\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal J^2=I. \tag{4.2} \] Its marked eigenflags are (1,t) for +1 and (u,-1) for -1. For a chosen meridian eigenvalue M the explicit matrix \((M+M^{-1})I/2+(M-M^{-1})\mathcal J/2\) has determinant one, trace M+M^(-1), and those marked eigenflags. This is a source moment map to the meridian conjugacy class; it has not been identified with the internal critical holonomy of the knot word. Now set \[ v=t,\qquad a=u/(1+tu),\qquad T=va. \tag{4.3} \] Then F=a, E=v(1-va), H=1-2va. The root source connection is obtained directly by differentiating the actual source vector: \[ \lambda\,d\psi=\frac{r u\,dt}{1+tu}=r a\,dv, d(\lambda d\psi)=-r\,dv\wedge da. \tag{4.4} \] On the reciprocal chart t'=1/t,u'=1/u one has \[ v'=1/v,\qquad a'=v-v^2a. \tag{4.5} \] Thus the two source connection forms differ by r dlog v. The source vectors themselves have clutch psi_n=v^r psi_s after basis reversal. The coherent SOURCE VECTOR spans the tautological O(-r) line; its dual co-source/polynomial line is O(r). The latter is the positive prequantum line, with connection -lambda dpsi. Keeping both signs explicit, this is the SAME affine cotangent torsor Conn(O(1)) as the original compact source, with exact two-form dv wedge da and its nontrivial affine clutch (4.5). For r=N the dual prequantum weight is N, obtained from the actual divided source; the original head half-form/degree-(N-1) line remains separate. This goes beyond an abstract identification of two SL2 actions: the variables, connection, clock generator T=R/r in its source expectation, density chart, and transition are all explicit actual matrix formulas. Its marked inverse/positive flags and dual/source polarization have not been swapped silently. ### Actual divided commutators give exact compact-source currents There is an exact current dictionary before any head partial trace. Use the unnormalized dual row ell(u)_k=binom(r,k)u^k and put sigma_r(C)=ell C psi/(1+tu)^r. Directly from the actual divided matrix entries, \[ \begin{array}{lll} f_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi=\partial_t\psi,& e_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi=(rt-t^2\partial_t)\psi,& h_{\mathrm{cl}}\psi=(r-2t\partial_t)\psi,\\ \ell e_{\mathrm{cl}}=\partial_u\ell,& \ell f_{\mathrm{cl}}=(ru-u^2\partial_u)\ell,& \ell h_{\mathrm{cl}}=(r-2u\partial_u)\ell. \end{array} \tag{4.6} \] The degree-r endpoints are exact: the top term is killed by rt-t^2 partial_t, and the bottom by partial_t. Consequently \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r([e_{\mathrm{cl}},C]) &=(\partial_u+t^2\partial_t)\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r([f_{\mathrm{cl}},C]) &=-(\partial_t+u^2\partial_u)\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r([h_{\mathrm{cl}},C]) &=2(t\partial_t-u\partial_u)\sigma_r(C). \tag{4.7} \end{split} \] These vector fields preserve the exact compact two-form dt wedge du/(1+tu)^2. The formulas extend entrywise when C has actual head-matrix coefficients, so no scalar symbol or head partial trace is assumed before deriving the currents. One must retain the normalized source terms for one-sided actions. For example \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r(e_{\mathrm{cl}}C)&=(\partial_u+rt/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(Ce_{\mathrm{cl}})&=(-t^2\partial_t+rt/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(f_{\mathrm{cl}}C)&=(-u^2\partial_u+ru/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(Cf_{\mathrm{cl}})&=(\partial_t+ru/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C). \end{split} \tag{4.8} \] Thus sigma is NOT being used as a multiplicative map to ordinary functions. Its exact left/right differential actions or corresponding star product transport matrix products. An actual Frobenius enveloping-degree-d operator has by (4.6)--(4.8) a differential realization of order at most d, with polynomial r-degree at most d. This is the explicit source adapter available for a bounded-degree normal crossing/current calculation. A proof that the actual mixed normal crossing operators produce the TWO required geometric framing currents is still needed. Whole block clocks also have an exact source action. For B_xi=xi^R and a matrix C independent of t,u, \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r(CB_\xi)(t,u) &=\left(\frac{1+\xi tu}{1+tu}\right)^r \sigma_r(C)(\xi t,u),\\ \sigma_r(B_\xi C)(t,u) &=\left(\frac{1+\xi tu}{1+tu}\right)^r \sigma_r(C)(t,\xi u),\\ \sigma_r(B_\xi C B_\xi^{-1})(t,u) &=\sigma_r(C)(\xi^{-1}t,\xi u). \tag{4.9} \end{split} \] Thus a head/block clock gauge can be transported as exact finite dilations, retaining its source character, rather than expanded as a polynomial Fr operator of falsely bounded degree. Its first normal generator is the Cartan moment already proved in (3.1). ## 5. The remaining source and holonomy comparisons The off-root color still follows M_high=-q^(N(r+1)), Y_high=Z^(r+1), whereas the original N-color path follows Y_low=Z. All powers q^N and M^N, including the high-color lift sign, remain in the original whole source and external peripheral line. Formula (3.1) does not equate these paths. Nor is R a literal crossing transfer. A total position is s+Nk; a crossing transfer is a difference of such total positions. The transparent root multiplicity braid merely permutes its block labels, so its block-transfer difference is zero at zeroth order. The mixed normal crossing/coproduct and the two-current coupling are needed to relate the new source variables to the TWO internal geometric framing flows. The explicit first-normal block arrows in the high-color proof are part of that map, not its conclusion. At 1+tu=0, the coherent normalization vanishes. The actual units U_s in (1.1) must be retained before taking any simultaneous normal or meridian limit. The compact source identification above does not permit evaluating a separately canceled root expression at that source wall or infer a regular geometric period there. [Exact two-clock/source audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_two_clock_source.py). [Results](../experiments/high_color_two_clock_source_results.json).

The [whole function/endpoint extension proof](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) adds the infinite-order functional-quotient obstruction, an exact flat confluent tower and its Newton lattice, and root inverse norm N^(-1/2). The Hopf F-to-commutator row operation retains its ordered K-row product. Its B_Fr homotopy is regular because the two omitted target corners vanish IDENTICALLY on its image. This image condition cannot be extended to arbitrary Fr currents. The bottom remaining arrow is a root unit and the top one is delta/(1-delta). They cannot be equated by a fixed-current co-source homotopy. The literal charged first-normal R current, its wall coefficient and both displayed source pairings check. The per-strand minimality and metric factors are correct. Its actual R leakage and inverse-pair defect are nonzero uniformly in N, so upper-only words cannot replace the strictified word. The revised hybrid-metric conclusions in [the clock/current source audit](frobenius_clock_and_internal_centralizer_map.md) Sections 7--8 retain the distinction between the two head metrics. This does not alter the selected2^-N versus uniform1/(N+1) wall source or bound the actual R word, normal neighborhood or head D gauge. The whole divided-Ward/pivotal closure identities and their actual Cartan wall inverse pass the independent proof audit recorded in [the global Green tail/current note](global_green_cut_tails_and_wall_transport_residual.md). It verifies the divided coproduct/adjoint q-powers, frozen cap clock and first-normal signs, the ordered N-term cap cancellation, the literal diagonal Cartan-unit inverse, and the nonzero sourced R return at first order delta^N. title: An actual high integral color carries the degree-N Frobenius wall row
text: # An actual high integral color carries the degree-N Frobenius wall row Research construction, 27 October 2026. The actual integral color of dimension N(r+1), specialized at the level-N root, has a classical Sym^r multiplicity space. Its generators are literal divided powers of the original quantum matrices, not an auxiliary classical source. For r=N a marked coherent co-source gives exactly the binomial wall row with N+1 entries. The original reduced knot scalar is retained by exact all-color periodicity. This constructs the wall functional as an actual color insertion. It does not yet intertwine both framing-current complexes, identify whole quantum jets of different colors, or prove selected geometric source survival or a volume norm. ## 1. The original integral matrix family Let N>=2, r>=0, m=N(r+1)-1, and let D_m(q) have its integral Weyl basis u_j, 0<=j<=m: \[ \begin{split} H u_j&=(m-2j)u_j,\quad K=q^H,\\ E u_j&=[m-j+1]_q u_{j-1},\qquad F u_j=[j+1]_q u_{j+1},\\ [a]_q&=(q^a-q^{-a})/(q-q^{-1}). \end{split} \tag{1.1} \] Out-of-range vectors are zero. These are the ACTUAL integral color matrices used in [all-color periodicity](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md), not the generic-M typical module. Put q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, and write j=kN+s with 0<=k<=r and 0<=s<N. Make the unit sign change \[ w_{k,s}=\beta_{k,s}u_{kN+s},\qquad \beta_{k,s}=(-1)^{Nk(k-1)/2+ks}. \tag{1.2} \] At the root, both ordinary block edges vanish: F at s=N-1 has coefficient [(k+1)N]=0, and E at s=0 has coefficient [(r+1-k)N]=0. With D_(N-1) denoting the Steinberg head, direct adjacent entries give \[ \begin{split} E&=I_{r+1}\otimes(-1)^rE_{\mathrm{St}},\qquad F=I_{r+1}\otimes F_{\mathrm{St}},\\ K&=I_{r+1}\otimes(-1)^rK_{\mathrm{St}},\\ H&=I_{r+1}\otimes H_{\mathrm{St}} +N\operatorname{diag}(r-2k)\otimes I_N. \end{split} \tag{1.3} \] For example the F coefficient before gauging is (-1)^k[s+1], and the consecutive beta ratio is (-1)^k. The E coefficient is (-1)^(r-k)[N-s], whose beta ratio gives (-1)^r[N-s]. The K and H identities follow from m-2j=N-1-2s+N(r-2k). Thus the ordinary small quantum action has r+1 invariant Steinberg blocks. The unrolled H is NOT constant on this multiplicity space. A map mixing k is not automatically an unrolled intertwiner. ## 2. Divided powers have a nonzero classical block action Keep the original generic matrices before specializing and define \[ \mathsf E=\left[E(q)^N/[N]_q!\right]_{q=q_N},\qquad \mathsf F=\left[F(q)^N/[N]_q!\right]_{q=q_N}. \tag{2.1} \] These ratios are regular matrix Laurent polynomials. On u_j their coefficients are the symmetric Gaussian polynomials \[ \mathsf F:u_j\longmapsto {j+N\brack N}_{q_N}u_{j+N},\qquad \mathsf E:u_j\longmapsto {m-j+N\brack N}_{q_N}u_{j-N}. \tag{2.2} \] Here boundary maps are zero. This is a regular integral division before specialization, not division of the zero root matrices. The needed Gaussian evaluation has an elementary proof. The identity \[ \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(1+Q^jz) =\sum_h Q^{h(h-1)/2}{a\brack h}_Q z^h \] follows by coefficient induction. For a=AN+s, 0<=s<N, at Q_N the product is (1-(-z)^N)^A times a product of degree s. Its z^N coefficient, divided by Q_N^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), gives \({AN+s\brack N}_{Q_N}=A\). The symmetric Gaussian convention is \({a\brack N}_q=q^{-N(a-N)}{a\brack N}_{q^2}\). Therefore before the beta gauge the signs and coefficients are exactly \[ \begin{split} \mathsf F u_{kN+s}&=(-1)^{kN+s}(k+1)u_{(k+1)N+s},\\ \mathsf E u_{kN+s}&=(-1)^{N(r+1-k)-1-s} (r+1-k)u_{(k-1)N+s}. \end{split} \tag{2.3} \] The beta ratios then give \[ \mathsf F w_{k,s}=(k+1)w_{k+1,s},\qquad \mathsf E w_{k,s}=\tau(r-k+1)w_{k-1,s},\quad \tau=(-1)^{Nr-1}. \tag{2.4} \] Consequently \[ e_{\mathrm{cl}}=\tau\mathsf E,\quad f_{\mathrm{cl}}=\mathsf F, \quad h_{\mathrm{cl}}w_{k,s}=(r-2k)w_{k,s} \tag{2.5} \] satisfy [e_cl,f_cl]=h_cl, [h_cl,e_cl]=2e_cl and [h_cl,f_cl]=-2f_cl. They are the ordinary irreducible Sym^r action on k and commute with the root E,F,K head action in (1.3). Their nilpotence order is r+1, so r=N has the degree-N string unavailable in a fixed number of original small-head factors. This is a SINGLE-COLOR divided action. Divided powers on tensor products have mixed coproduct terms. Its classical multiplicity action must not silently be substituted for that entire tensor action or for a Hopf action on all matrix observables. ## 3. The actual first-normal block edges recover the same generators Extend the sign frame (1.2) constantly in q, put Z=Q^N=q^(2N), delta=1-Z, and retain the actual generic matrices. Let F_cross and E_cross be just their between-block entries. They are divisible by delta. With rho=q_N-q_N^(-1), the exact regularized root values are \[ \begin{split} [F_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_{q_N} &=\rho^{-1} f_{\mathrm{cl}}\otimes E_{0,N-1},\\ [E_{\mathrm{cross}}/\delta]_{q_N} &=(-1)^{r+1}\rho^{-1}e_{\mathrm{cl}}\otimes E_{N-1,0}. \end{split} \tag{3.1} \] To check every sign, the F edge has coefficient (-1)^k[(k+1)N]_q and the E edge has coefficient (-1)^(k-1)[(r+1-k)N]_q. For every positive integer a, \[ \left[\frac{[aN]_q}{1-Q^N}\right]_{q_N} =\frac{(-1)^{a+1}a}{\rho}. \tag{3.2} \] This follows by factoring Q^(aN)-1 by Q^N-1 before evaluating; no derivative of a singular quotient is inferred from root values. Equations (3.1) follow immediately. In the normal variable h=Log(q/q_N), delta=-2Nh+O(h^2), so the same entries are respectively -2N f_cl/rho and 2(-1)^r N e_cl/rho at first h-order. Thus the classical source is encoded canonically in the actual quantum-normal block edges. The root decomposition is not a product decomposition of the generic high-color module. ## 4. A coherent divided source gives exactly the binomial wall row On the multiplicity space write v_k for its basis. The actual divided operators in (2.5) construct the finite source and co-source \[ \psi_+=\exp(f_{\mathrm{cl}})v_0=\sum_{k=0}^rv_k,\qquad \lambda_+=2^{-r}v_0^*\exp(e_{\mathrm{cl}}), \quad \lambda_+(v_k)=2^{-r}{r\choose k}. \tag{4.1} \] Both exponentials terminate. Direct multiplication gives lambda_+(psi_+)=1. The rank-one coupon e_+=psi_+lambda_+ is idempotent and has trace one. These are Frobenius/divided coherent operators on the ACTUAL high integral color, not an ordinary Sym^r action postulated on the old fixed-N head. Let J=(J_0,...,J_r) be any array over a characteristic-zero commutative coefficient algebra, and insert its literal diagonal block operator diag(J_k) tensor I_N. Let P_s be any rank-one head coordinate projector and tau_high=Tr/[N(r+1)]. Then \[ (r+1)\tau_{\mathrm{high}} [(e_+\otimes P_s)(\operatorname{diag}J\otimes I_N)] =\frac1{N2^r}\sum_{k=0}^r{r\choose k}J_k. \tag{4.2} \] For r=N this is EXACTLY the actual wall row B_N(J), including its 1/N and the k=N endpoint. The coupling to the original Green array is explicit: the multiplicity block k takes the original entry J_k, equivalently the Kronecker coupling delta_(k,j). Formula (4.2) is valid pointwise for all remaining flow variables and hence after their finite sums. It applies to polynomial or retained logarithmic moment coefficients as a linear functional; no multiplication or Toeplitz-symbol identification is used. If P_s is replaced by I_N, the coherent functional has value one on the identity and the right side is N times (4.2). The marked rank-one head accounts for the wall normalization; it must not be dropped while claiming equality of source rows. This realizes B_N as a marked co-source on an actual larger color. It does not prove that the delta_(k,j) coupling intertwines the second framing current or its entire divided Hopf coproduct. Those equations must still be checked, with their endpoint carries. ### The coherent source has a canonical actual whole quantum germ There is no need to extend the root binomial row arbitrarily. The generic integral divided matrices E_N(q)=E(q)^N/[N]_q! and F_N(q)=F(q)^N/[N]_q! are regular, and preserve every residue s while moving the block index k. On the fixed s-string define \[ \begin{split} \Psi_s(q)&=\exp(F_N(q))w_{0,s},\\ \Lambda_s(q)&=2^{-r}w_{0,s}^*\exp(\tau E_N(q)),\\ u_s(q)&=\Lambda_s(q)\Psi_s(q),\qquad e_s(q)=\Psi_s(q)\Lambda_s(q)/u_s(q). \end{split} \tag{4.3} \] The finite exponentials terminate. At q_N, u_s=1 by (4.1), so its whole germ is a unit, with no root pole canceled by hand. Equation (4.3) is a regular idempotent of trace one. Different s-strings are disjoint, hence E_coh(q)=sum_s e_s(q) is an idempotent of trace N. For the ACTUAL generic high-color scalar long-knot operator, \[ \frac1N\operatorname{Tr}[E_{\mathrm{coh}}(q)C_{\mathrm{high}}(q)] =C_{N(r+1)}(Q) \tag{4.4} \] identically as a whole germ. The marked string e_s(q) gives the exact whole wall weights \(N^{-1}\Lambda_s\operatorname{diag}(J_k)\Psi_s/u_s\). At the root these reduce to (4.2). Their quantum derivatives are determined by the original divided matrices and the retained unit u_s, rather than inferred from the numerical binomial row. Equation (4.4) compares this color with itself. It is not an off-root equality with C_N(Q), and does not make e_s(q) an unrolled intertwiner or prove a current-complex map. ## 5. The reduced scalar is the original one; whole Q-jets are different The actual zero-framed long-knot operator on D_m(q) is C_(m+1)(Q) times identity, by the original integral color construction. Its regular root specialization is still scalar. The independently proved all-color identity gives \[ C_{N(r+1)}(Q_N)=C_N(Q_N)=K_N. \tag{5.1} \] Thus the normalized coherent functional with unmarked head identity returns K_N. Its marked wall version returns K_N/N, as expected from B_N(1)=1/N. The full original ADO normalization is still the old marked line eta_N K_N/N, with its peripheral meridian germ; one does NOT replace it by an imagined eta_(N(r+1))/[N(r+1)] line. The high-color meridian path before specializing is \[ M_{\mathrm{high}}=-q^{N(r+1)},\quad Y_{\mathrm{high}}=M_{\mathrm{high}}^2=Z^{r+1},\qquad M_{\mathrm{low}}=-q^N,\quad Y_{\mathrm{low}}=Z. \tag{5.2} \] At the root M_high=(-1)^r. In particular r=N uses the other lift at odd N. The one-dimensional shift and its zero-framing phase must be retained in comparing it with the original ideal lift. For the external modified-dimension line the exact sign-chart law is \(d_N(\sigma e^u)=\sigma^{1-N}d_N(e^u)\), with sigma=(-1)^r. Its retained adapter sigma^(N-1)=(-1)^(r(N-1)) is identically one when r=N. This does not install a new modified trace on the large ordinary Weyl module: the original external d_N line is retained. The fixed-color whole functions C_(N(r+1))(Q) and C_N(Q) have not been identified away from Q_N. Their normal meridian slopes already differ in (5.2), and (3.1) is the actual block-extension normal data. For a nontrivial adequate knot their different quadratic degree spans prove that the two whole Laurent polynomials are unequal. Consequently this source elevation is an exact ROOT and first-normal MODULE construction, not yet a source-preserving equality of the whole Q-jets needed by Mellin reconstruction. It supplies the missing degree-N wall representation while retaining the precise additional normal comparison which remains to be established. ## 6. Verification and remaining network map The following audit checks (1.3), every divided coefficient including both boundaries, the full classical commutators, coherent source and co-source normalization, the literal wall row, and both normal block edges at even, odd and composite levels. The actual high-color braiding/closure proof and its independent audit are recorded below. The remaining network question is whether the explicit block/Green coupling in (4.2), together with (3.1), transports the FULL actual two-current relative source complex. No cancellation of the second framing current or nonzero final geometric projection follows from the existence of the coherent wall row alone. [Divided-source audit](../experiments/audit_high_integral_color_frobenius_source.py). [Results](../experiments/high_integral_color_frobenius_source_results.json). ## 7. The actual braiding retains a definite mixed half-Cartan sign Here is an independent direct crossing and closure proof, with no tensor-product theorem used as a premise. Put n=N(r+1), m=n-1, and let W be the N-dimensional root color W=D_(N-1) tensor C_(Nr), H_W(i)=m-2i, 0<=i<N. In the gauged basis of Section 1 the high color has the same ordinary E,F,K as W on every block, while H_high(w_(a,i))=H_W(i)-2Na. The generic universal R specializes integrally: on integral Weyl vectors its kth factorial coefficient is a product of two Gaussian polynomials and [k]_q!. Thus every k>=N term vanishes at q_N; there is no division by [N] at the root. For k<N its nilpotent part preserves the two block indices and is exactly that of W. The remaining Cartan ratio is q_N^(-N[a H_W(j)+b H_W(i)]+2N^2ab) =epsilon^(a+b), epsilon=(-1)^m. (7.1) All head weights have parity m, so this sign is independent of i,j and the transfer. The same calculation applies whether the Cartan is evaluated before or after the nilpotent term, since the head weights change by even integers. Inversion retains the same sign. Consequently, for BOTH checked crossing signs, Rcheck_high^(+/-)(w_(a,i) tensor w_(b,j)) =epsilon^(a+b) sum_(k,l)(Rcheck_W^(+/-))_(ij)^(kl) w_(b,k) tensor w_(a,l). (7.2) The common highest-weight half-Cartan scalar is the original one on the marked exponential sheet. It is the same for high and W in (7.2); it is not set to one. The sign in (7.1) is genuinely nontrivial for some even/odd levels and block pairs. Thus the factorization is not an unmarked flip on arbitrary inserted arrays. Mixed source or current coupons must carry this sign. The original root pivot has no additional block factor: q_N^((1-N)(H_W(i)-2Na))=q_N^((1-N)H_W(i)). (7.3) The twist is also the same on every block. Shifting a highest weight m by -2Na changes the ordinary twist exponent h(h+2)/2 by -2Na(m+1)+2N^2a^2, whose q_N-power is one. For a CLOSED BRAID whose closure is one knot, the multiplicity index is transported by the permutation without changing along the component. Closure therefore makes it a single value a. Every mixed crossing sign in (7.2) is then epsilon^(2a)=1. Equations (7.3) and the twist calculation show that its reduced zero-framed head scalar is precisely the scalar of W. To compare W with the original Steinberg color, retain the one-dimensional shift h=Nr. With b braid strands and writhe w, the actual crossing constant is s_0=q_N^(h^2/2)(-1)^(r(N-1)), g_h=q_N^((1-N)h)=(-1)^(r(1-N)). The crossing index coboundaries telescope around the knot. Crossings contribute s_0^w, closed pivots g_h^(b-1), and the specified zero-framing twist contributes (s_0 g_h)^(-w). Their product is g_h^(b-1-w)=1, since the parity of a one-cycle braid permutation gives b-1-w even. This is the same direct phase calculation used in the [all-color periodicity proof](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md). It proves for the ACTUAL high-color long-knot operator C_high(q_N)=K_N I_(N(r+1)). (7.4) In particular a normalized Frobenius source/co-source and the original head cut retain K_N exactly. The full ordinary normalized trace corresponds instead to the normalized trace on the multiplicity factor; both evaluate (7.4) to K_N. The wall coupon with a rank-one head projector has normalization 1/N, precisely as in (4.2), rather than normalization one. The old external modified-dimension line and its sign law remain those of Section 5. This proof compares actual ROOT periods. Whole generic colors and their quantum-normal slopes are different as (5.2) records. Nor does (7.4) identify inserted Green networks: their block-changing normal arrows and mixed signs require their literal couplings. [Independent signed-crossing and original-period audit](../experiments/audit_frobenius_high_color_braiding.py). [Results](../experiments/frobenius_high_color_braiding_results.json). ## 8. Coverage Divided-power quantum groups and Steinberg/Frobenius tensor structures are established representation-theoretic constructions. For coverage, [Sutton--Tubbenhauer--Wedrich--Zhu, 2105.07724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.07724) studies SL2 tilting modules, quantum-number root conventions and integral divided-power models, including the complex root-of-unity case. No tensor-product, trace, or braiding proof from that paper is a premise here. The calculations above prove the explicit all-parity module signs, actual first-normal edge, coherent wall coupon, its whole high-color source germ, and the original marked scalar adapter in the conventions used by the actual knot state.

title: Coverage audit for the hyperbolic-knot target
text: # Coverage audit for the hyperbolic-knot target **29 October: fixed long fillings.** A further primary-source coverage check distinguished our fixed-twist, N-to-infinity statement from [Lee, 2307.09903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09903): its abstract first passes to a skein/categorical limit as twist counts tend to infinity and then relates the limiting evaluation to octahedral volumes. The abstract of [Galakhov et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2015.02.029) concerns a conjectured explicit formula for colored polynomials of arbitrary pretzels. [1101.2844](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2844) concerns noncommutative A-polynomial computations for the restricted (-2,3,n) family and numerical volume-conjecture work. These scope checks supply no proof premise to the present full-source estimates or marked representation-volume comparison. They also do not justify a claim of novelty or an exhaustive absence of overlapping results. **29 October: augmented-base coverage check.** The new [complete augmented pretzel period proof](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) is an independent original-source calculation, not a novelty claim. The abstract of van der Veen's [augmented knotted trivalent graph paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0094) states volume-conjecture coverage for augmented KTGs and an arithmetic containing-link corollary. The abstract and introductory scope of [Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296) concern OCTAHEDRAL fully augmented links and a Turaev--Viro result without half twists; the published introduction also records earlier Kashaev coverage for octahedral fully augmented links. These are coverage statements, not proof inputs to the new finite-source, recurrence or Gaussian arguments. They do not by themselves classify the exact overlap with every non-octahedral s-antiprism base here. No claim that this base family was previously uncovered is made. Its complete augmented links must also be distinguished from the fixed-slope filled knots, which the new base theorem does not settle. Research record, 25 October 2026. Hyperbolicity is a standing assumption. The user permits an unbounded, sufficiently broad knot class, and requests literature checks for coverage rather than proof techniques. Accordingly, the external statements below are not hypotheses accepted on the authority of their proofs. No proof section of these papers is needed for this audit. ## 1. Keep the quantum object fixed The target is Kashaev's original invariant and volume conjecture, approached through a literature-defined quantum A-module and its distinguished period. The later Andersen--Kashaev meridian state and Andersen--Malusa b-shift annihilator are comparison objects. An annihilating equation alone does not select a solution or its normalization. An AK volume theorem does not settle the original conjecture without the corresponding comparison. The independent local and analytic arguments in the existing notes may duplicate stated literature coverage. That is independent verification, not evidence of a new theorem about previously uncovered knots. ## 2. Checked coverage statements | Source and statement checked | Stated scope | Consequence for this project | | --- | --- | --- | | Ben Aribi--Wong, [2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10776v2), abstract and introductory theorems | Jones-function existence for FAMED one-cusped hyperbolic manifolds with H2=0; geometricity adds the AK volume asymptotic. The paper includes all hyperbolic twist knots. | Our twist-family theorem and positive FAMED saddle theorem overlap this coverage. They remain useful as independently audited arguments. | | Ben Aribi--Guilloux--Wong, [2512.17437v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17437v1), abstract | FAMED geometric realizations for more than 42,000 knot complements, including the stated crossing and tetrahedron census ranges. | Additional isolated small-knot certificates do not establish an unbounded new class. The census claim is not a uniform membership theorem. | | Wong, [2512.23198v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23198v1), Definitions 1.1 and 1.5, Theorems 1.11 and 1.14, Corollary 1.16 | A full-tensor theorem for generalized FAMED semi-geometric triangulations; the Jones-function theorem imposes additional longitude/meridian conditions. Definition 1.5(2) excludes a longitude-dependent affine shape plane. Definition 1.5(3) prescribes a meridian without a longitude shear. | The generalized singular reduction already has substantial stated overlap. Our moving-plane Fourier construction removes a condition appearing in this particular statement, but this alone is not new knot-family coverage. | | Wong, [2609.33922v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33922v2#S1.SS2), Theorems 1.1 and 1.4, Remark 1.2 | A KLV volume/torsion theorem for geometric triangulations; an RT-type function for angle-supporting triangulations with a suitable quad type; a weighted squared-norm factorization. Agreement of the RT-type function with the AK Jones function is asserted on FAMED data. The remark defines an AK analogue more generally. | This is close to our Fourier constructions. Its stated general KLV theorem does not by itself identify the original AK meridian state or its quantum A-operator. The introduction also explicitly leaves full invariance unresolved. | | Liu--Ming--Sun--Wu--Yang, [2608.16560v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16560), abstract | Cusped modular-double Turaev--Viro-type invariants with an exponential volume law. | A broad volume theorem for this literature object is already claimed. Equivalence with our selected AK state would still require a precise map and normalization. | | Ge, [2609.27635v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27635v1), Theorem 1.1 and Sections 2--4 | Every finite-volume cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold admits a finite geometric ideal triangulation realizing completeness. | At the user's subsequent request, the affine-subdivision argument was independently audited, with exact stress tests. See the separate audit. A global branching and the quantum cycle comparison are additional requirements. | The last three entries are recent coverage changes. They must be retained when assessing the scope of any proposed theorem here. The user separately authorized a proof audit of Ge's geometric result; that authorization does not extend to importing the quantum papers' proof techniques. For the principal algebraic direction, Guilloux--Marche, [1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395), already studies exact polynomials, a class containing knot A-polynomials, and their volume functions. Its definitions and stated coverage identify classical regulator exactness as existing theory. A quantum theorem still has to identify the distinguished period and its normalization. The [intrinsic norm-torsor note](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) reconstructs the required elementary descent arguments independently. ### All-level state and torsor coverage The following are definitions and stated scope, not imported proofs: * Murakami--Murakami, [math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075), states the Kashaev/colored-Jones comparison for all levels. Our crossing note reconstructs the needed matrix and period identities directly. This is independent verification of known coverage. * Baseilhac--Benedetti, [1101.1851](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.1851), states an odd-level quantum-hyperbolic/Kashaev comparison. Its link specialization uses the trivial ambient character. It must not be silently replaced by a fixed hyperbolic character of the complement. * Willetts, [2003.09854](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854), states an all-knot completion unifying ADO and colored Jones, with the Alexander factor retained. That unification and its recursion-ideal theorem have not been adopted here. Our modified-dimension gauge is proved from the defining finite matrices instead. The later [Frobenius Verma calculation](frobenius_verma_period.md) independently proves the stated root normalization ADO/Delta by untruncated crossing coefficients and the polynomial-block trace. It also proves equality of the actual root annihilator ideals under this central factor. It does not identify the generic completion or adopt a colored-Jones recursion comparison. * Garoufalidis--Scholze--Wheeler--Zagier, [2412.04241v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04241v2), introduces proposed K3-graded Habiro modules. The user subsequently requested a separate [independent audit](gswz_printed_definition_audit.md). It confirms counterexamples to the printed unrestricted Theorems 1 and 2: the local span need not be finitely generated, and the global set need not be additive. It also verifies formula errors in (114) and (165). Theorem 5 restricts to specified good root orders; the supplied examples do not directly refute its restricted membership conclusion, which remains independently unverified here. No theorem from this paper is a premise of the A-curve torsor construction or its requested volume comparison. The direct [ADO pointing proof](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) also identifies a structural limitation of a fixed-level approach: rational root states have a central shift sector v=1. Retaining the original quantum family and its pointing is necessary before comparing with the geometric classical A-curve. A finite splitting torsor alone is insufficient. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now independently establishes a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. It does not adopt the literature holonomicity or recursion-ideal comparison theorems. The [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) specifies the remaining geometric-symbol, relative-source, and regulator-norm comparison. These existence results do not establish the volume conjecture for a broad knot class. ## 3. What alternatingness supplies and what it does not Menasco's diagrammatic checkerboard decomposition is useful combinatorial data. It must not be identified automatically with a decomposition into right-angled cells in the complete hyperbolic metric. Gan, [2005.07904v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.07904), classifies alternating links with both checkerboard surfaces totally geodesic as three links, with octahedral, cuboctahedral and icosidodecahedral projection graphs, and characterizes them as right-angled completely realisable. Thus the strong geometric interpretation is highly restrictive. This coverage statement does not invalidate the combinatorial Menasco decomposition. An augmented link and a knot obtained by filling its crossing circles are also different manifolds. A right-angled augmented-link realization, or a TV volume theorem for it, cannot be transferred to the filled knot without a separate quantum filling argument. ## 4. What would count as closing a broad class here The present independent theorem covers every globally branched complete strictly positive geometric knot triangulation, for its specifically normalized tensor-derived meridian state. The remaining requirements are not additional finite rank scans: 1. Uniform membership of a stated unbounded knot class in the hypotheses, established independently if a literature existence proof is not used. 2. Identification of the selected literature state across the required realizations, with its peripheral functions, phase and cycle retained. 3. Application of the independently proved volume and annihilator results to this same state. Hyperbolic two-bridge knots beyond twist knots and suitable highly twisted alternating families are possible class targets. The sources checked here do not state an unconditional all-two-bridge or all-alternating AK theorem. This search result is not a claim that no such theorem exists elsewhere. Selecting a new matrix condition on knots already in a stated census does not satisfy the uniform-class requirement. ## 5. Subsequent steering The user explicitly rejected further reduction of the main objective to FAMED or other chart-by-chart AK hypotheses. The principal direction is the intrinsic period torsor and general algebraic properties of the A-polynomial. The geometric existence input is audited separately in [ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md).

title: The identity cut has an exact orientation-cover source
text:
# The identity cut has an exact orientation-cover source 27 October 2026. This is a finite whole-source identity for the actual four-port tensor. It replaces neither the state nor its selected cap.
