It introduces an orientation factor together with its compensating measure, keeps the cap's marked sheet, and retains every finite band. The comparison with the geometric momentum below is a principal local comparison; a whole Gaussian/source comparison is not inferred. ## 1. Retain the original cap and every port band Use the literal tensor and port order of [the physical two-cut construction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). With zero extension outside all four physical ranges, put \[ \mathcal F_T(x,y;\xi,\eta) =\sum_{a,b,\mu,
u}T_{a+\mu,b+
u;a,b} x^a y^b\xi^\mu\eta^
u. \] The first original balanced cut has matrix coefficients 1/N; the second cut closes by its original identity, without a new pivotal weight. Thus, with all original pivots and external scalar lines already inside T, \[ F(\eta)=\mathcal F_T(1,1;1,\eta),\qquad \Phi_{\mathrm{id}}(T)= rac1N[\eta^0]F =\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}_{\eta=0}F(\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta}. 	ag{1} \] The sums over the first output and input remain in F. This is not the normalized trace of a reshaped two-position matrix. In particular, charged current tensors use all their first-port bands as in (1). The same formula works coefficientwise for every whole crossing or source coupling; no specialization of those coefficients is required. ## 2. An exact orientation factor with the compensating measure Introduce the quadratic cover \[ u=\eta+\eta^{-1},\qquad v=\eta-\eta^{-1},\qquad v^2=u^2-4. \] Its involution is eta to eta inverse, fixing u and changing v to -v. On this cover the following is a literal equality of rational forms: \[  oxed{\quad F(\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta} =[vF(\eta)] rac{du}{N(u^2-4)}.\quad} 	ag{2} \] Indeed du=v d eta/eta. Consequently the original source equals the marked residue of the orientation-twisted section G=vF against the new measure. The multiplication by v is the nearest-band difference on the full kernel. Its compensating measure is essential. There is a precise parity qualification. G is odd if F is even under eta inversion. For arbitrary actual T the correct law is instead \[ G\circ\iota=-v(F\circ\iota). 	ag{3} \] Thus (2) is an orientation twist without an assumed involution symmetry of the whole braid word. It does not declare the scalar function G odd when the actual tensor does not have that symmetry. Multiplication M_v identifies the full Laurent kernel space with its submodule v times that space. On this image every actual linear current A transports as M_v A M_v inverse, and its co-source transports by (2). The inverse is used only on that image. This is a strict source-preserving change of presentation, not division by a possibly vanishing selected period. All endpoint/corner summands are part of the same full kernel. ## 3. The original cap marks the sheet at infinity The point eta=0 determines a particular preimage of u=infinity: \[ v/u\longrightarrow-1,\qquad \eta=(u+v)/2,\qquad t=1/u= rac{\eta}{1+\eta^2}=\eta+O(\eta^3). 	ag{4} \] The last equality gives an actual local uniformizer of order one. Residues in eta and t therefore agree, including their signs. On this sheet v is asymptotic to -u. For a constant F, the right side of (2) is asymptotic to -F du/(Nu), whose standard residue at u=infinity is +F/N. The other preimage, eta=infinity and v/u tending to +1, has residue -F/N. Taking an unmarked sum of the two sheet residues would cancel this constant cap. The original tensor fixes the first sheet in (4); there is no additional choice of an odd cycle. The apparent poles of du/(u^2-4) at u=2,-2 introduce no new poles in the TOTAL form: at eta=1,-1 the factor G=vF cancels them. This uses the actual finite Laurent nature of F. The measure may not be evaluated independently and then assigned its own endpoint terms. ## 4. A finite tail formula, not just the nearest coefficient Write F=sum F_j eta^j and G=sum G_j eta^j. Near the marked eta=0, \[  rac{du}{Nv^2}= rac{d\eta}{N(\eta^2-1)} =- rac1N\sum_{k\geq0}\eta^{2k}d\eta. \] Consequently the exact new source is \[ \Psi(G)=- rac1N\sum_{k\geq0}G_{-2k-1}. 	ag{5} \] Only finitely many coefficients contribute for any actual tensor. Since G_j=F_(j-1)-F_(j+1), the partial sum through k=K is \[ - rac1N\sum_{k=0}^K G_{-2k-1} = rac{F_0-F_{-2K-2}}N. 	ag{6} \] The final coefficient outside the full support vanishes, proving Psi(vF)=F_0/N exactly. Formula (6) is the retained finite endpoint term. Dropping it early, using only -G_-1/N, or replacing (5) by the constant coefficient of vF changes the source. For the literal two-cut unknot tensor, which is the flip tensor, \[ F_{\mathrm{unknot}}(\eta) =\sum_{j=-(N-1)}^{N-1}(N-|j|)\eta^j. 	ag{7} \] The original cap and (5) both give one. The constant coefficient of vF is zero. Keeping only -G_-1/N gives 2/N for N at least two; the remaining finite tail contributes (N-2)/N. This actual tensor already detects the distinction between an odd insertion at the old source and the source-preserving orientation change (2). ## 5. Whole clocks and their connection term Let r be an invertible whole clock parameter. The change eta to r eta acts on the cover by \[  egin{split} u_r&=	frac12(r+r^{-1})u+	frac12(r-r^{-1})v,\ v_r&=	frac12(r-r^{-1})u+	frac12(r+r^{-1})v. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] It preserves u squared minus v squared and the marked eta=0 point. It also preserves the original logarithmic measure exactly: \[  rac{du_r}{v_r}= rac{du}{v},\qquad \iota\,	au_r\,\iota=	au_{r^{-1}}, 	ag{8a} \] where tau_r is eta to r eta and iota is eta to eta inverse. For the actual whole Q dilation set r=Q in (8). These transports form the multiplicative torus with its inversion involution; the resulting group is dihedral in this precise sense, not automatically nilpotent. At a primitive finite root the dilation itself has finite order. None of these identities drops its whole normal dependence before specialization. For G=vF the actual transformed section representing F(r eta) is \[ \widetilde S_rG= rac{v}{v_r}G(u_r,v_r). 	ag{9} \] In particular a clock does not act by an unaccompanied u substitution. Writing D=eta partial_eta=v partial_u+u partial_v, differentiation of (9) gives the exact connection \[ \widetilde D=D-u/v,\qquad M_v D=\widetilde D M_v, \qquad (\widetilde DG) rac{du}{Nv^2}= rac1N d(G/v). 	ag{10} \] Its marked residue is zero. All finite clock derivatives follow before taking any quantum normal or large-N limit. Although (9)-(10) have denominators, the corresponding sections lie in the transported image and the total original form is retained. Physical port clocks have mixed kernel actions. In the full kernel, input clocks Q^a,Q^b act by x to Qx,y to Qy; output clocks Q^(a+mu), Q^(b+nu) act by (x,xi) to (Qx,Qxi) and (y,eta) to (Qy,Qeta). Thus (8)-(10) transport precisely the eta component while keeping the simultaneous y rescaling for an output clock. General boundary braiding/prefix adapters still act in their original order. Independent whole crossing couplings commute with M_v, and differentiating them preserves (2), (5) and every finite endpoint in (6). ## 6. Compatibility with the actual prefix framing cover The independent proof of [the actual prefix chart](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md) retains U=mu_j...mu_1, V=mu_(j-1)...mu_1, k=ell_U/ell_V and \[ z=s(k-1),\qquad D=(-1)^jz(p-p^{-1}),\qquad \Omega_{cut}= rac{\ell_V}{BD}d\log A\wedge d\log B. 	ag{11} \] Here p is the actual balanced local wave momentum and B=1/k at completeness. The two nearest actual output exchange bands have principal ratios p inverse and p, respectively. Distinguish the finite Fourier-band variable eta_F in Sections 1--5 from the geometric parameter eta_geo=p inverse. The boundary action gives the principal Fourier incidence eta_F p=1. This is not a coordinate isomorphism of the original source spaces or a map of their cycles. On this incidence the geometric orientation factor is \[ v_{geo}=p^{-1}-p,\qquad D=(-1)^{j+1}zv_{geo}. 	ag{12} \] The orientation factor of the exact cap cover consequently has the correct geometric sign line. Retaining the actual inverse-prefix clock, whose whole expression is (q/M)^(j-1) product_(i<j) Q^(J_i), gives the principal equality \[ \ell_V^{-1}(R_{(+1,-1),0}-R_{(-1,+1),0})\Omega_{cut} = rac{(-1)^{j+1}}{Bz}d\log A\wedge d\log B. 	ag{13} \] The density alone is not generally odd: ell_V can differ on the two sheets. Formula (13) includes precisely the prefix factor that would be lost by substituting a developed meridian for the physical one. Equations (2) and (13) are compatible orientation formulas on that incidence; they are not an equality of their whole selected period complexes. In particular eta_F and the physical position B are independent before that correspondence. Closing the second port by the eta_F constant term does not sum its input position b or identify that sum with a physical B cycle. The marked residue in (4)-(6) involves all finite bands and their endpoint, whereas the existing transverse Gaussian theorem handles fixed bounded port offsets on a regular interior chart. Transporting that full residue/endpoint through the Gaussian comparison remains necessary. In particular (13) alone is not permission to insert a new odd observable into the original knot period. There is also a direct comparison with the UNINSERTED principal cap measure, including its rational base Jacobian. Write sigma=(-1)^j, t_W=Tr W and \[ A_0=c_U+s t_U,\qquad A_1=c_V+s t_V. \] In the reference frame Tr(JC)=c_C+t_C. In the moving cut frame it is s(beta-gamma)+(1-s)t_C. Using (4.1) of the prefix note gives \[ u_{geo}=p+p^{-1}= rac{\sigma(A_0-kA_1)}{s(k-1)},\qquad \left. rac{\partial u}{\partial k}ight|_s = rac{\sigma(A_1-A_0)}{s(k-1)^2}. 	ag{14} \] The extra s derivative vanishes after wedging with d log A. Together with D=-sigma s(k-1)v and the density in (11), this proves \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\Omega_{cut}}{\ell_V} = rac{k-1}{A_1-A_0}\,d\log A\wedge rac{du_{geo}}{v_{geo}} = rac{k-1}{A_1-A_0}\,d\log A\wedge rac{d\eta_{geo}}{\eta_{geo}}. \quad} 	ag{15} \] This equality is on the further regular chart A_1-A_0 nonzero and k not one. It includes the actual inverse-prefix clock ell_V inverse and an explicit rational Jacobian on the two-position base. Applying (2) to the final one-form in (15) gives the same orientation-twisted section and compensating measure as an algebraic formula. To use it for the period still requires an actual transform of the source and its physical input-position sum. No such transform follows from (15). For a genuine quadratic prefix this Jacobian chart is generically nonempty; a linear prefix or exceptional first-position fiber requires another coordinate rather than division by its vanishing Jacobian. Formula (15) identifies the geometric density's algebraic one-form shape with the logarithmic measure appearing in the finite cap. It does not identify their source functionals, transport the marked eta_F=0 cap, sum the independent physical input-position b, or carry the finite tail (6) through the transverse Gaussian. Those remain the precise global comparison data. ### 6.1. The geometric compactification has a zero-residue boundary There is an exact algebraic boundary test on the geometric incidence cover, not an image of the original marked finite cap or its cycle. In this subsection eta means eta_geo and u,v are its cover coordinates. Solving (14) for k gives \[ k= rac{su+\sigma A_0}{su+\sigma A_1},\qquad k-1= rac{\sigma(A_0-A_1)}{su+\sigma A_1}. 	ag{16} \] At the geometric eta_geo=0 boundary, u is asymptotic to eta inverse and v to minus eta inverse. Consequently \[ k-1= rac{\sigma(A_0-A_1)}s\eta+O(\eta^2),\qquad D\longrightarrow A_0-A_1. 	ag{17} \] At the other preimage eta=infinity the limit is D=A_1-A_0. The two points of this GEOMETRIC compactification reach k=1, or physical B=1, on two algebraic sheets. This does not say that the original eta_F cap maps to either point. At k=1 one has det(U-V)=0, so the exact discriminant is (A_0-A_1)^2. If c_U-c_V is nonzero, the root formula r=(c_C+s h_C-D)/(2c_C) shows that r, and hence ell_V, is finite at (17). On this regular boundary chart, \[  rac{\ell_V(k-1)}{A_1-A_0} =- rac{\sigma\ell_V(0)}s\eta+O(\eta^2). 	ag{18} \] Thus the full leading framing density Omega_cut itself is regular at that geometric boundary and has ZERO eta_geo logarithmic residue. The apparent eta logarithm in (15) is canceled by its rational Jacobian. A nonzero cap source cannot be obtained by discarding that Jacobian and declaring a regular constant amplitude there, even if a proposed source map assigned the cap to that boundary. This is a property of the principal prefix chart, not an assertion that such a source map exists or that the selected quantum period vanishes. For example the genuine figure-eight prefix in Section 6 of the prefix note, at s=1 and u_shape squared plus u_shape plus one equal to zero, has \[ c_U-c_V=1,\quad A_0-A_1=3+u_{shape},\quad r\longrightarrow-2,\quad \ell_V\longrightarrow2+3u_{shape}. \] All displayed regularity conditions hold there. For a scalar meromorphic amplitude a(eta), the exact residual to compute is \[ [\eta^0]\left(a(\eta)  rac{\ell_V(k-1)}{A_1-A_0}ight)d\log A. 	ag{19} \] A holomorphic amplitude gives zero. If its only negative term is a_-1/eta, the result is -sigma ell_V(0) a_-1/s times d log A; larger poles require the corresponding full finite coefficient sum in (19). The actual finite kernel has negative Fourier-band powers whose order grows with N. They cannot be substituted into a(eta_geo) without the actual source transform. That transform must retain the original source, norm, physical input-position sum, endpoints and any escaping/polar block contribution. The bounded interior Gaussian theorem does not evaluate (19) as the original cap. [The actual boundary-moment and Ward-atom calculation](actual_negative_band_boundary_moment_and_ward_atom.md) makes this distinction testable. The finite weighted negative-band functional is exactly an original source paired with a K-Ward current and does not equal the identity source on actual signed tensors. An original negative factorial circuit does supply an explicit inverse-norm pole, but its presence in the selected full geometric source is a separate transport question. ## 7. Reproducible actual tensor checks [The independent audit script](../experiments/audit_identity_cut_orientation_cover.py) uses literal signed braid tensors with their original pivotal, half-Cartan, framing and peripheral scalar lines. It checks (1), (5)-(6), the unknot formula, whole input/output clock rescalings and the connection (10). It also tests the same finite source formula on every port matrix unit with endpoint indices included. The results are recorded in [the audit output](../experiments/identity_cut_orientation_cover_results.json). These checks validate the finite source change; they are not a global geometric period or volume asymptotic calculation.

title: Actual integral-color coherent symbols, uniformly including the poles
text: # Actual integral-color coherent symbols, uniformly including the poles Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual integral N-color family admits a globally regular polynomial source frame. Its generator symbols have exact finite formulas and uniform expansions on the entire real compact source, including both poles. Moving q and the integral color together gives the expected exponential clock. An explicit flag shear compares its principal moment matrix with the varying-meridian Grothendieck chart. Every change of frame below is an exact diagonal quantum-factorial change of the actual representation and source. Its large size cannot be discarded when comparing selected periods. Uniform asymptotics of the individual generators do not prove uniform asymptotics of the full R word. The exact symmetric whole-q-difference model is developed in [the global integral-color source note](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md). The quantitative frame norm, its dilogarithmic generating function, and the root flag-current bookkeeping are given in [the quantum-factorial source comparison](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md). ## 1. The actual integral family and its polynomial frame Fix N>=2, put n=N-1, and use c=2pi*i, s=c lambda, 0<=lambda<=1, q=exp(s/(2N)), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), M=-q^N, m=q^N=exp(s/2). Write `[j]_q=(q^j-q^(-j))/rho`, with its Laurent-polynomial continuation when rho=0. In the ordinary-falling polynomial frame the actual integral module has F e_j=(n-j)e_(j+1), E e_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q/(N-j)e_(j-1), K e_j=q^(n-2j)e_j. (1) The absent boundary edges are zero. Put Ecal=rho E and Fcal=rho F. These are the operators compared below. They satisfy exactly K Ecal K^(-1)=Q Ecal, K Fcal K^(-1)=Q^(-1) Fcal, Fcal Ecal+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=(q^N+q^(-N))I. (2) For example the diagonal entry of Fcal Ecal is `rho^2[j]_q[N-j]_q`; expanding the two q-numbers proves (2). Use the same actual compact coherent kernel as before: sigma_C(v,z)=sum_(i,j=0)^n v^i C_ij binom(n,j)z^j /(1+vz)^n. Its globally regular source coordinates are T=vz/(1+vz), a=z/(1+vz), b=v/(1+vz), ab=T(1-T), a=T/v, b=v(1-T), Omega_0=dv wedge da. On the compact real source `z=bar(v)`, both |a| and |b| are at most one half, and 0<=T<=1. The pole-chart change is `V=1/v, a'=v-v^2a`. ## 2. Exact finite-N symbols have no polar singularities Let R_x(T)=1+(x-1)T, W_N(T)=q^N+q^(-N)-q^(-N)R_Q(T)^N -q^N R_(Q^-1)(T)^N. Then the exact actual symbols are sigma_K=q^n R_(Q^-1)(T)^n, sigma_(K^-1)=q^(-n)R_Q(T)^n, sigma_A=R_Q(T)^n, A e_j=Q^j e_j, sigma_Fcal=n rho b, sigma_Ecal=a H_N(T), H_N(T)=W_N(T)/[N rho T(1-T)]. (3) The apparent divisions in the last formula are removable. Indeed W_N is a polynomial which vanishes exactly at T=0 and T=1, so it is divisible by T(1-T). It is also divisible by rho^2 as a Laurent polynomial in q, making rho=0 removable. Its two endpoint values agree: H_N(0)=H_N(1)=q^n-q^(-n). (4) Thus (3) is a globally regular source function, including its two pole fibers, not just a formula on the open torus. Here is the short coefficient proof. In the Ecal kernel use binom(n,j)/(N-j)=binom(N,j)/N, rho^2[j]_q[N-j]_q =q^N+q^(-N)-q^(2j-N)-q^(N-2j). Extend the sum to j=0,N, where its summand is zero. The binomial theorem gives W_N divided by `N rho v(1-T)`; since `T/v=a`, this is exactly (3). The Fcal formula follows from `sum_j(n-j)binom(n,j)x^j=n(1+x)^(n-1)`. ## 3. Uniform asymptotics hold on the entire compact source Define the whole principal functions A_inf=exp(sT), k=m exp(-sT), f=s b, W(T)=m+m^(-1)-k-k^(-1) =4sinh(sT/2)sinh(s(1-T)/2), H(T)=W(T)/[sT(1-T)], e=a H(T). (5) Every apparent division in (5) is removable, including s=0. For each fixed nonnegative integer l there is a finite constant C_l, independent of N and lambda in [0,1], such that in smooth coordinate norms on the whole real compact source ||sigma_A-A_inf||_(C^l) +||sigma_K-k||_(C^l) +||sigma_(K^-1)-k^(-1)||_(C^l) +||sigma_Ecal-e||_(C^l) +||sigma_Fcal-f||_(C^l) <= C_l/N. (6) The following proof includes the endpoint estimates. For fixed S and l, the binomial exponent has the elementary bound ||R_(exp(s/N))(T)^N-exp(sT)||_(C^l[0,1]) <=C_(S,l)|s|^2/N (7) for |s|<=S. For large N expand the logarithm of `1+(exp(s/N)-1)T`; its difference from sT/N and its fixed T derivatives are uniformly bounded. Alternatively differentiate the binomial power explicitly. The two first s coefficients are identical, giving the |s|^2 factor. The finitely many smaller N have the same bound by compactness after dividing out s^2. Apply (7) to W_N-W with two extra T derivatives. This difference vanishes at both endpoints. For any such function g, g(T)/[T(1-T)] =-T integral_0^1 y g''(Ty)dy -(1-T)integral_0^1 y g''(1-(1-T)y)dy. (8) Differentiation of (8) bounds its C^l norm by a fixed multiple of the C^(l+2) norm of g, with no endpoint loss. Moreover `N rho/s=sin(pi lambda/N)/(pi lambda/N)` is bounded below by 2/pi on this family. Equations (7)--(8) therefore give ||H_N-H||_(C^l[0,1])<=C_l |s|/N. The corresponding Fcal bound follows from `n rho=s+O(|s|/N)`. The K and clock estimates use (7) and the one missing power n=N-1. Multiplication by the globally smooth functions a,b proves (6) in both compact pole charts. This also proves uniformity at lambda=0; it does not divide a nonzero estimate by a vanishing rho without its |s| factor. The exact star product is still required for finite matrices. Ordinary products of symbols equal the classical products only in this controlled principal limit. In particular (2) gives the principal Casimir identity `ef+k+k^(-1)=m+m^(-1)`. ## 4. The moving-q clock and the actual principal moment matrix The actual simultaneous path has `M=-q^N=-m`, so the principal Gauss parameter is x=-M=m. Its clock is precisely A_inf=exp(sT), k=x/A_inf. (9) Thus moving q really changes its frequency from c to c lambda. Changing only M at fixed q_N would not do that. Where its factors are nonzero, the old balanced momentum is p_bal=(1-A_inf)/f =(1-exp(sT))/[s v(1-T)]. (10) The full moment matrix is globally regular even where this particular momentum chart fails: mu=[k,e;k f,m+m^(-1)-k], det mu=1. (11) Its eigenvalues are m and m^(-1). The actual knot-meridian sign in the old convention is `-mu`, since M=-m. At lambda=1 its projective sign gives the complete physical meridian. All M and SL2 sign markings are retained; choosing one of the two eigenflags is additional augmented data. For the m-eigenflag use the slope v_geo in `[1:v_geo]`. Directly, v_geo=(m-k)/e=k f/(k-m^(-1)) =r_s(T)v, r_s(T)=s(1-T)/(1-exp[-s(1-T)]). (12) Consequently (11) is exactly the whole Grothendieck matrix from [the exponential detour](compact_exponential_cech_current_detour.md) evaluated at `(T,v_geo)`. The source shear (v,a)->(r_s(T)v,a/r_s(T)) preserves T and Omega_0 exactly, because `Omega_0=-dT wedge dlog v`. For lambda<1 it is regular on the whole real compact sphere. In this ordinary-falling frame it becomes singular at lambda=1,T=0. This particular singularity is frame dependent, as the next section proves. The other eigenflag, corresponding to the original inverse-cut marking `M^(-1)=-m^(-1)` on `-mu`, has slope v_inv=s v(1-T)/(1-exp(sT)). (13) Equations (12)--(13) must not be silently interchanged. ## 5. An exact quantum-factorial change removes the first flag artifact The symmetric q-falling frame has E_q e_j=[j]_q e_(j-1), F_q e_j=[n-j]_q e_(j+1). Its change from (1) is diagonal. If `e'_j=g_j e_j`, then g_0=1, g_(j+1)/g_j=(n-j)/[n-j]_q. All these factors are nonzero on 0<=lambda<=1. The exact finite symbols in this frame are sigma_(rho E_q)=[R_q(T)^n-R_(q^-1)(T)^n]/v, sigma_(rho F_q)=v[q^nR_(q^-1)(T)^n-q^(-n)R_q(T)^n]. (14) Their endpoint divisions are removable, and the same elementary binomial argument proves uniform C^l convergence on the entire compact sphere to e_sym=2sinh(sT/2)/v, f_sym=2v sinh(s(1-T)/2), k=m exp(-sT). (15) The m-eigenflag now has the regular slope v_+=exp(s(1-T)/2)v, (16) through lambda=1, including both poles. The inverse eigenflag is v_-=-exp(-sT/2) sinh(s(1-T)/2)/sinh(sT/2) v. (17) For lambda<1 it reverses the two pole flags, whereas at lambda=1 the ratio of the two sines is one and (17) equals (16). The two corner limits `(lambda,T)=(1,0),(1,1)` therefore retain the inverse-flag collision/bubble data. Regularity of (16) does not justify deleting that augmentation information. The exact principal comparison is b_s(T)=2sinh(s(1-T)/2)/[s(1-T)], e=b_s e_sym, f=f_sym/b_s. (18) Equivalently use the symplectic source shear `v_sym=v/b_s(T), a_sym=b_s(T)a`. At lambda=1,T=0, b_s vanishes; the ordinary-frame pole in (12) is thus a basis artifact. These are exact matrix and principal-coordinate comparisons, not a boundedness assertion about the changing frame. ## 6. The original balanced word and pointed source are retained exactly There is also an explicit exact adapter to the existing balanced integral module. In that frame F_bal v_j=(1-Q^(j+1))v_(j+1), Ecal_bal v_j=(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))v_(j-1). At M=-q^N define d_j=(Q;Q)_j/[rho^j(n)_j] =(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2)[j]_q!/(n)_j, D=diag(d_j), d_0=1. (19) Here `(n)_j=n(n-1)...(n-j+1)`. The second expression makes lambda=0 removable, with value `(-1)^j j!/(n)_j`. Every d_j is nonzero on the full real path, including lambda=1. Directly, D^(-1)F_bal D=rho F, D^(-1)Ecal_bal D=rho E, D^(-1)K D=K. (20) For the second identity use `M Q^(-j)-M^(-1)=-rho q^(-j)[N-j]_q`. Thus (20) is an exact quantum-factorial frame of the actual integral representation, not a newly ordered classical polynomial. Conjugating every strand by D conjugates every actual factorial R matrix by `D tensor D`. The Cartan factor, pivot, transfer weights and head projectors are kept; the diagonal factors commute with the latter three. Internal D factors telescope through an arbitrary word. Its cut matrix transforms as C_poly=D^(-1)C_bal D. The literal rank-one source transforms at the same time: psi_poly=D^(-1)psi_bal, phi_poly=phi_bal D. (21) All pointed pairings are therefore exactly unchanged. For every weighted knot word the cut matrix is diagonal by integer-weight conservation, so its actual normalized source is also its same normalized trace before and after (20). The weighted Green current identities are preserved coefficientwise. The genuine integral Hopf pivot K and the original auxiliary root-compatible pivot `K^(1-N)` must still be distinguished. Their exact closed-strand adapter is `K^(-N)`. It commutes with every displayed diagonal change of frame and remains an actual position-dependent insertion off the root: K^(-N)e_j=q^(-Nn)q^(2Nj)e_j. At q_N it becomes the retained scalar `(-1)^n`; along the moving-q path it cannot be replaced by that value. The external modified-dimension and framing factors likewise stay their original ones. The basis identity does not equate two generic quantum invariants whose pivots or external source factors were chosen differently. Equation (20) does not license replacing (21) by an unrelated vacuum or discarding the size of D in asymptotics. Likewise the symmetric q-falling adapter and its source must be retained. Their quantum-factorial norms can carry exponential size. The individual uniform generator bounds (6) and (15) prove neither a uniform full-word star expansion nor the selected geometric period. They give the exact source frames and global classical moment maps to which such a theorem would have to apply. ## 7. Exact audit and endpoint checks [audit_integral_color_coherent_symbols.py](../experiments/audit_integral_color_coherent_symbols.py) and its [results](../experiments/integral_color_coherent_symbols_results.json) verify all finite symbols, removed endpoint values, Casimir normalization, and both diagonal frame adapters at levels 2 through 6 over the rational function field in q. They also check the two principal augmented flags and ordinary/symmetric shear identities. A separate 70-digit grid check uses N=8,16,32,64,128, includes lambda=0,1, both exact T endpoints, nearby T=10^(-8), and the color-scale endpoint positions T=1/N,1-1/N. It agrees with the proved uniform rate. These numerical checks audit conventions and cancellation; the uniform whole-sphere assertion is the argument (7)--(8), not an extrapolation from that grid.

title: The actual integral-color path has a global polynomial q-difference model
text: # The actual integral-color path has a global polynomial q-difference model Research proof, 27 October 2026. Along the simultaneous path q_lambda=exp(pi*i lambda/N), M=-q_lambda^N, the finite head is a genuine integral-color quotient for every parameter. Its standard q-polynomial operators patch on O(N-1), with removable q=1 values. There is also an explicit regular frame for the original balanced source and all its crossing matrices along the entire closed path. The source, cup, cap and pivot changes are recorded. The standard ordinary closure gives the existing reduced color C_N(q); the literal auxiliary pivot gives the earlier auxiliary word with its known off-root route adapter. They agree at both endpoints but are not silently identified in the interior. Use [the common-Verma quotient](common_verma_two_wall_source.md) and [the divided-color/pivot calculation](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md). The independent [ordinary-frame symbol audit](integral_color_coherent_symbols_and_uniform_poles.md) and [factorial-frame analysis](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md) give complementary uniform symbol and frame estimates. ## 1. The simultaneous path stays on the genuine quotient wall Put n=N-1, Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and q_lambda=exp(pi*i lambda/N), M_lambda=-q_lambda^N, 0<=lambda<=1. Then w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1)=0, delta=1-Q^N=1-exp(2pi*i lambda). (1.1) The tail of the genuine balanced infinite module is invariant on this wall. Its finite head is therefore a quotient for the whole path. The truncated Hopf defect -delta*w*E_(n,n) vanishes identically; there is no generic-M finite Hopf premise. The endpoints are (q,M)=(1,-1) and (q_N,1). Both also have delta=0. The two wall parameters have not been identified: this path lies in w=0 and meets the root wall at its endpoints. Its logarithmic derivative is the integral-color direction dLog M=N dLog q, not the fixed-meridian q-normal derivative. ## 2. The integral color and the two polynomial frames In the ordinary F-shift basis v_j, 0<=j<=n, the genuine color is K v_j=q^(n-2j)v_j, F v_j=v_(j+1), E v_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q v_(j-1), (2.1) with both boundary arrows zero and [r]_q=(q^r-q^(-r))/rho. Its matrices are Laurent regular at q=1 with [r]_1=r. The user's ordinary-falling polynomial basis is e_j=v_j/(n)_j, (n)_j=n!/(n-j)!. It gives exactly F e_j=(n-j)e_(j+1), E e_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q/(N-j)e_(j-1). (2.2) On the polynomial space H_N=H^0(P1,O(n)), e_j=x^j, this is F=x(n-J), E=x^(-1)[J]_q[N-J]_q/(N-J), K=q^(n-2J), J=x partial_x. (2.3) The inverse N-J is legitimate on this space: its eigenvalues are 1,...,N. Equivalently it is the finite polynomial operation integral_0^1 t^(N-1)f(x/t)dt. Thus (2.3) is an exact operator on H_N, including q=1. It is not claimed to be a scalar first-order q-difference expression on unrestricted functions. For a simpler q-difference realization, use symmetric q-falling factorials [n]_q^(fall,j)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)[n-r]_q, f_j=v_j/[n]_q^(fall,j). Then E f_j=[j]_q f_(j-1), F f_j=[n-j]_q f_(j+1). (2.4) With the marked shift T_q f(x)=f(qx), these have the exact forms E_q=(T_q-T_(q^-1))/(rho x), F_q=x(q^n T_(q^-1)-q^(-n)T_q)/rho, K_q=q^n T_(q^-2). (2.5) The apparent x pole cancels on polynomials; the highest coefficient of F_q is zero, so all three preserve degree <=n. Their q=1 values are partial_x, x(n-J), I, respectively. Along the entire path, for 1<=r<N, [r]_(q_lambda)=sin(pi lambda r/N)/sin(pi lambda/N)>0, with value r at lambda=0. None of the q-falling frame factors vanishes or has a pole. The ordinary-falling frame differs by e_j=R_j f_j, R_j=[n]_q^(fall,j)/(n)_j. (2.6) These are units on the fixed-N path. This is not a uniform-in-N norm assertion; the factorial-frame note records its possible exponential conditioning. ## 3. The q-difference operators patch globally on O(n) The south section of a north polynomial is (J_n f)(y)=y^n f(1/y). Direct substitution into (2.5) gives J_n E_q J_n^(-1)= y(q^n T_(q^-1)-q^(-n)T_q)/rho, J_n F_q J_n^(-1)=(T_q-T_(q^-1))/(rho y), J_n K_q J_n^(-1)=q^(-n)T_(q^2). (3.1) Thus E and F interchange and K inverts, in the same line-bundle transition that defines O(n). The q=1 limits give its usual global sl2 vector-field action. This is an exact globally patched q-difference realization, not a substitution into a local symbol. The frame R in (2.6) also patches by J_n R J_n^(-1); it need not have a scalar first-order difference expression. For q!=1 on the given path, spectral interpolation in T_q expresses it and its inverse as finite q-difference matrices. Coefficients of that interpolation can have removable q=1 singularities even though the operators themselves are regular. The reciprocal polynomial chart J_n is not automatically the previously fixed balanced physical Weyl/source matrix. Transporting a specified such matrix C into the h frame below gives D^(-1)CD, with all its original phases and source factors. The chart identities (3.1) do not authorize replacing that transported matrix by J_n. ## 4. A regular frame keeps the actual balanced pointing Let w_j be the original balanced common-Verma basis. Its exact relation to (2.1) is v_j=(Q;Q)_j w_j, (Q;Q)_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r). (4.1) For example along M=-q^N the balanced Ecal arrow is -q^(-j)rho[N-j]_q, and multiplication by 1-Q^j=-q^j rho[j]_q proves (2.1), with E=Ecal/rho^2. The factors in (4.1) have zeros at q=1. Treating (4.1) as an invertible integral frame there would lose source information. The correct regular balanced-to-polynomial frame is instead h_j=D_j w_j, D_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2)/{n choose j}_q =(Q;Q)_j/[rho^j [n]_q^(fall,j)], (4.2) where the binomial is the symmetric q-binomial. Its ratio is D_j/D_(j-1)=-q^j [j]_q/[N-j]_q. Here D changes basis vectors, so its inverse conjugates old coordinate matrices. The coordinate gauge in the [independent source-detour audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md) is exactly D^(-1), expressed using the ordinary Q-binomial. All factors in (4.2) are nonzero analytic functions on the closed path. Their endpoint values are D_j(0)=(-1)^j/binom(n,j), D_j(1)=(-1)^j q_N^(j(j+1)/2). (4.3) For the second equation use [N-r]_(q_N)=[r]_(q_N), so {N-1 choose j}_(q_N)=1. In particular the root frame is a unitary diagonal phase in the original Euclidean basis. In this regular frame the actual Gauss matrices are precisely Ecal= rho E_q, F= rho F_q, K=K_q. (4.4) Both first operators are regular and vanish at q=1. The original ordinary Uq generators are E=rho^(-1)E_q,F=rho F_q on this frame; their individual lattice need not be regular at q=1. The ordinary integral Uq lattice of (2.4) is regular there. These two lattice statements must remain distinct. Their braiding matrices agree nonetheless for q!=1: the common Hopf rescaling of E and F cancels in every E^k tensor F^k term of the actual universal finite-color crossing, and K and the Cartan weights stay unchanged. Equivalently, the change from f_j to h_j divides by rho^j on every leg, which commutes with each crossing by exact total-index conservation. The finite crossing and its inverse therefore extend regularly to the usual flip at q=1 in this model. No divergent ordinary generator is inserted into a limit without this cancellation. ### 4.1 Source, dual source, cup and cap The prescribed balanced cut has psi_j=1 and phi_j=1/N. In the regular frame (4.2) it is exactly psi_h,j=D_j^(-1), phi_h,j=D_j/N, Gamma_h,ij=D_j/(N D_i), phi_h psi_h=1. (4.5) These are regular at both endpoints. They are not silently replaced by a constant vector and average covector. Their norms need not be bounded uniformly in N; already D_j(0) contains ordinary binomial factors. The dual basis is transformed inversely. Consequently the exact cup sum_j w_j tensor w_j^* equals sum_j h_j tensor h_j^*. For either diagonal pivot g, the right cap has entries ev_g(h_j tensor h_k^*)=delta_(jk) g_j, so the basis change preserves the cup/cap pair without a missing determinant or endpoint multiplier. All source and co-source normal derivatives follow by differentiating (4.2)--(4.5). For an actual one-cut closed braid array, total integer index conservation makes its remaining cut matrix diagonal, even before using a Hopf or Schur argument. Therefore its exact scalar cut is phi_h C psi_h=(1/N)Tr C. (4.6) This is why the same actual scalar is represented by the fixed compact coherent trace period in the h frame. Equality (4.6) does not identify all offdiagonal source operators or erase their derivatives before the closed network has been formed. ## 5. The ordinary and literal auxiliary closures stay distinguished The genuine ordinary pivotal closure uses K. With its original ordinary zero-framing twist and finite-color normalization, (2.5) gives exactly the existing reduced color C_N(q). For generic q the one-cut ordinary operator is scalar by actual Hopf naturality and irreducibility; the resulting Laurent period extends to the whole path, including both endpoints. Its values are C_N(1)=1, C_N(q_N)=Kashaev_N. (5.1) The root auxiliary construction uses K^(1-N). Away from q_N it differs from the ordinary cap by the diagonal K^(-N), with entry q^[-Nn+2Nj]. Its associated twist also differs. The exact zero-framed b-strand route adapter is the previously proved factor q^[Nn(ell-b+1)+2N sum_(closed legs)j_a], (5.2) where ell is writhe. It equals one at both q=1 and q=q_N because ell=b-1 modulo two for a knot. Its interior values and derivatives are generally state-dependent and are retained. Thus (4.2) is a genuine unit frame for the same balanced auxiliary pointing along the path. Identifying its literal-pivot scalar with C_N(q) in the interior requires (5.2), not a basis argument. For either specified closure, the new model preserves the entire word and original scalar. Neither the full root modified-dimension line nor an ordinary quantum dimension is declared an off-root extension of the other by this construction. ## 6. Exact finite coherent symbols and uniform endpoint behavior Use the fixed compact coherent kernel of dimension N, variables v,z, and T=vz/(1+vz). Put B_+=1+(q-1)T, B_-=1+(q^(-1)-1)T. Binomial summation of the actual matrices (4.4) gives exactly sigma_(Ecal)=[B_+^n-B_-^n]/v, sigma_F=v[q^n B_-^n-q^(-n)B_+^n], sigma_K=q^n[1+(q^(-2)-1)T]^n. (6.1) The first numerator vanishes at T=0 and the bracket in the second vanishes at T=1. Thus these are smooth entire-sphere symbols in the actual coherent charts, including both poles. For s=2pi*i lambda, q=exp(s/(2N)), their limits are e_s=2sinh(sT/2)/v, f_s=2v sinh(s(1-T)/2), k_s=exp[s(1/2-T)]. (6.2) Convergence is O(1/N) in every fixed smooth derivative norm on the real sphere, uniformly for lambda in [0,1]. To prove it, expand n Log[1+(exp(epsilon*s/(2N))-1)T], epsilon=+1 or -1. Its difference from epsilon*sT/2 and every fixed derivative is O(1/N), uniformly on the compact (lambda,T) rectangle. The endpoint zero factors may be divided using the exact integral identities g(T)/T=integral_0^1 g'(uT)du and g(T)/(1-T)=-integral_0^1 g'(1-u(1-T))du. These remove the apparent v or south-chart pole with the same derivative bound. The kernel charts then give the stated whole- sphere estimate. No such estimate is asserted for an arbitrary growing full braid matrix. These principal functions satisfy identically e_s f_s+k_s+k_s^(-1)=2cosh(s/2). (6.3) They describe the same meridian conjugacy class as the simultaneous path. At lambda=0 their multiplicative Gauss matrix is I. Its first lambda derivative retains the nonzero ordinary sl2 moment map; no dimension-N integral representation has disappeared. At lambda=1 the trace is -2, with the marked central sign of the original complete source. The plus eigenflag has the particularly simple exact principal form h_+(v,T)=exp[s(1-T)/2]v. (6.4) It is a clock-preserving canonical shear. For imaginary s and the real compact sphere its multiplier has modulus one, so the shear sends the very same sphere to itself. The root factorial-frame note records its quadratic generator, the inverse eigenflag and the two negative inverse-flag bubbles. This smoother plus flag does not permit replacing the actual inverse-flag source or its endpoint current by a different marking. The uniform estimates above concern the generator symbols only. The actual selected period has the exact nearby-root ladder C_N(q_(N+k))=C_k(q_(N+k)); in particular it equals one at lambda=N/(N+1). The independent source-detour audit proves its dense ordinary-color bounds and the resulting necessary endpoint nonuniformity. Those statements coexist with the fixed-N analytic source and uniform generator limits; no uniform full-word saddle amplitude is being inferred. ## 7. Exact gain and remaining scope The actual integral-color family now has a whole fixed-space q-difference realization with explicit global clutch. The balanced pointing, cup and both cap choices can be transported through a unit frame on the closed simultaneous path. The only singular factorial change is displayed in (4.1), and its regular network cancellation is proved rather than assumed. The scalar compact trace remains the actual one for every specified closure. This does not remove the off-root pivot adapter, compare the full root-normal source with a fixed-meridian q-jet, or bound the unknown full-word norm in (6.1). Nor does it construct a global geometric A-branch through the whole path or identify its selected regulator phase. It supplies an actual globally patched family on which those further comparisons can be posed with all source factors visible. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_integral_color_global_q_difference_source.py) checks the bases, matrices, global patch, true source/cup, actual crossing cancellation, both walls, and endpoint symbols. The [independent proof audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md) also verifies the integral quotient, source frames, pivotal distinction and exact resonance sampling constraints.

title: The integral-color path: actual sources, pivots and dense resonances
text: # The integral-color path: actual sources, pivots and dense resonances Independent proof audit, 27 October 2026. The path \(q_\lambda=e^{\pi i\lambda/N}\), \(M=-q_\lambda^N\) does give an honest \(N\)-dimensional integral-color quotient and its actual crossings. It is not automatically the same off-root source as the auxiliary finite ADO lift with its root pivot frozen. This distinction is explicit below. The ordinary-color bounds impose a second exact constraint: the actual color path has polynomial values on a sampling grid of spacing \(O(1/N)\), and its nearest higher-root value is literally one. A uniform positive dominant WKB solution on the real interval cannot describe this selected function. ## 1. Exact quotient and basis comparisons On the common balanced Verma module, \[ \delta=1-Q^N,\qquad w=M Q^{-N}-M^{-1},\qquad Q=q^2. \] The choice \(M=-q^N\) has \(w=0\). The tail is invariant and the finite head is the genuine integral quotient, with \[ K e_j=q^{N-1-2j}e_j,\quad \mathcal E e_j=q^{-N}(1-Q^{N-j})e_{j-1},\quad F e_j=(1-Q^{j+1})e_{j+1}. \tag{1} \] The original finite crossing is its literal quotient crossing. The word excursion adapter is proportional to \(\delta w\), so it vanishes on this whole path, not merely at its root endpoint. Let \(u_j\) be the ordinary highest-weight basis with \(Fu_j=u_{j+1}\), \(Eu_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q u_{j-1}\), and \(\mathcal E=\rho^2E\). Then \[ e_j=u_j/(Q;Q)_{j} \tag{2} \] gives exactly (1). For every fixed \(N\), this gauge is invertible on \(0<\lambda\le1\), including at \(q_N\); all factors have index \(j<N\). It is singular at \(q=1\). The balanced coupon \(e_{ij}=1/N\) becomes \[ e^{\mathrm{ordinary}}_{ij} =\frac{(Q;Q)_j}{N(Q;Q)_i}. \tag{3} \] Its normalization remains one, but its separate source and co-source flags need not have a regular \(q=1\) limit. There is a second useful exact gauge, regular also at \(q=1\). In the polynomial basis it gives \[ \mathcal E_{\mathrm{sym}}=v^{-1}(T_q-T_q^{-1}),\qquad F_{\mathrm{sym}}=v(q^nT_q^{-1}-q^{-n}T_q),\quad n=N-1. \] The diagonal conjugation from (1) is \[ D_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)/2-Nj}{N-1\brack j}_{Q}. \tag{4} \] Its adjacent ratio is the old \(\mathcal E\) coefficient divided by \(q^j-q^{-j}\), which proves both generator comparisons. At \(q=1\), \(D_j=(-1)^j\binom nj\); at the actual root, \[ D_j=q_N^{-Nj-j(j+1)/2}, \] of modulus one. Thus (4) is invertible along the closed path for fixed \(N\), but its condition number can be exponential in \(N\) in the interior or at the classical endpoint. Exact finite equivalence does not imply equality of naive principal symbols in these different frames. The normalized trace is basis invariant. On every one-cut diagonal array, including the scalar index-weighted arrays, the original balanced coupon equals this trace. This avoids the coordinate singularity of (3) for those evaluations. For off-diagonal Ward insertions the coupon must still be transported; normalized trace is not a replacement on all matrices. ## 2. The pivotal adapter is essential off the root The generic integral-color quantum invariant uses the ordinary pivot \(g_{\mathrm{int}}=K\). The root ADO pivot is \(g_{\mathrm{root}}=K^{1-N}\). Away from \(Q^N=1\), \[ S^2=\operatorname{Ad}K\ne\operatorname{Ad}K^{1-N}. \] For example their conjugations of \(\mathcal E\) differ by \(Q^{-N}\). Hence a frozen ADO right cap is not a generic Hopf pivotal cap, even though the quotient module and its crossings are genuine. For a \(b\)-strand knot braid of writhe \(\mathfrak w\), the ordinary integral twist and frozen ADO twist at \(\alpha=n\) are \[ \theta_{\mathrm{int}}=q^{n(n+2)/2},\qquad \theta_{\mathrm{root}}=q^{-n^2/2}. \] Their ratio is \(q^{-Nn}\). The exact difference of the two zero-framed state arrays is therefore the weight \[ q^{Nn(\mathfrak w-b+1)} (Q^N)^{\sum_{\text{closed strands}}j_a}. \tag{5} \] It retains an actual number-operator clock, not just a scalar. At \(q_N\) its clock is one and its scalar is \((-1)^{n(\mathfrak w-b+1)}=1\) by knot parity. Thus the ordinary reduced endpoint is the original \(K_N\). At \(q=1\), the ordinary reduced period is also one. Neither endpoint equality removes the nonconstant adapter in between or its quantum-normal derivatives. There is an explicit small example. For \(N=2\), use the stabilized unknot, the two-strand braid \(\sigma_1\). Its ordinary reduced value is one. With the frozen pivot \(K^{-1}\) and frozen twist \(q^{-1/2}\), its normalized one-cut value instead is \[ 1+\frac{q^2-q^{-2}}2 =1+i\sin(\pi\lambda). \tag{6} \] To check this, use the actual fundamental checked crossing \(q^{1/2}I-q^{-1/2}U\), with \(U|_{01,10}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}q&-1\\-1&q^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right]\). Closing the second leg with \(K^{-1}\), then applying the frozen twist correction, gives diagonal entries \(1\) and \(1-q^{-2}+q^2\); their average is (6). It agrees at both endpoints but is not the integral-color invariant inside the interval. This is a comparison of two explicit interpolations, not a claim that a generic ADO invariant was defined incorrectly. The valid actual interpolation is \(C_N(q)\) with its ordinary caps and twist. At the root its reduced one-cut evaluation is regular even though its ordinary quantum dimension \([N]_{q_N}\) vanishes. One must not evaluate an unreduced closure divided by \([N]\) as two separately vanishing quantities. ## 3. Exact sampling and the necessary nonuniformity Set \[ A_N(\lambda)=C_N(e^{\pi i\lambda/N}). \] For every integer \(r>N\), the value at \(\lambda=N/r\) is an ordinary color at the principal root \(q_r\). The actual unitary trace bound gives \[ |A_N(N/r)|\le [N]_{q_r}^{b-1}\le (r/2)^{b-1}. \tag{7} \] On any fixed closed interval \(J\subset(0,1)\), these sampling points have mesh \(O_J(1/N)\) and their bound is \(O_J(N^{b-1})\). Consequently a positive dominant WKB expansion with a uniformly nonvanishing subexponential amplitude cannot hold on any open real interval below one. Choose a point of positive continuous rate and a small compact interval on which it stays positive. A sampling point in that interval contradicts (7). More generally, if \[ u_N(\lambda)=N^{-1}\log^+|A_N(\lambda)| \] are equicontinuous on such a compact interval, then \(\sup_Ju_N\to0\): compare every point with its neighboring sampling point. Thus a positive exponential spike requires loss of that equicontinuity. There is an exact stronger endpoint ladder. At level \(r=N+k\), ordinary-color Weyl symmetry gives \[ C_N(q_{N+k})=C_k(q_{N+k}),\qquad 1\le k<N. \tag{8} \] For each fixed \(k\), the right side tends to one and is bounded. In particular \[ A_N\!\left(\frac{N}{N+1}\right)=1 \tag{9} \] for every knot. Its distance from the target is \(1/(N+1)\). If \(|K_N|\) has positive exponential rate, a nonzero smooth dominant WKB amplitude cannot remain uniform even across this endpoint window. An unconditional quantitative form is \[ \sup_{\lambda\in[N/(N+1),1]}|A_N'(\lambda)| \ge (N+1)(|K_N|-1), \] and hence \[ \sup_{\lambda\in[N/(N+1),1]} |q\partial_q C_N(q)| \ge \frac{N(N+1)}\pi(|K_N|-1). \tag{10} \] This follows by integrating the derivative along the interval, so it does not assume a real-valued period or a mean-value point for a complex function. The already proved figure-eight asymptotic makes (9)--(10) an actual exponential endpoint example. Ordinary-color unitarity controls values, not the normal derivatives needed here. Pointwise asymptotics at an individual nonsampled irrational parameter are not excluded. Nor do these bounds exclude a geometric branch with a resonance-dependent source coefficient. They do exclude treating that coefficient as uniformly nonzero and smooth merely because the classical optimizer is. ### A whole scaled boundary profile cannot be algebraic The same exact ladder constrains the functions-before-jets program. Use \(c=2\pi i\), \(H=\log Q\), and the scaled normal \[ z=N^2(H-c/N),\qquad \mathfrak f_N(z)= C_N\!\left(\exp\!\left[\frac{c}{2N} +\frac{z}{2N^2}\right]\right). \] The nearby principal level \(N+k\) is exactly \[ z_{N,k}=-\frac{ckN}{N+k}\longrightarrow-ck,\qquad \mathfrak f_N(z_{N,k})=C_k(q_{N+k})\longrightarrow1. \tag{11} \] Also \(\mathfrak f_N(0)=K_N\). Here is the precise conditional conclusion. Choose a subsequence with \(|K_N|\to\infty\), for example one having a positive exponential rate, and suppose \(\mathfrak f_N/K_N\) converges locally uniformly to a holomorphic function \(g\) on a connected domain containing zero and every point \(-ck\), \(k\ge1\). Then \[ g(0)=1,\qquad g(-ck)=0\quad(k\ge1). \tag{12} \] Local uniform convergence permits the moving evaluations (11), so this needs no unproved interchange of pointwise limits. Such a nonzero whole profile is not algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\). Indeed, for an irreducible polynomial relation \(P(z,g)=0\), the infinitely many zeros in (12) force \(P(z,0)\) to vanish identically. Thus \(w\) divides \(P(z,w)\), forcing \(g=0\), contrary to \(g(0)=1\). Neither the required growth nor this normal-family convergence is asserted for a general knot. A germ on a small neighborhood of zero alone is not excluded, and the conclusion does not prohibit algebraic coefficients for an individual local geometric WKB branch. It says that, if a normalized whole selected boundary profile exists through all nearby resonances, an algebraic critical coefficient cannot be that entire profile. A genuinely nonalgebraic period function is required; its resonance zeros and one normalization do not determine it uniquely. ## 4. Principal flags depend on the valid source frame The symmetric frame in (4) has principal functions \[ e=\frac{2\sinh(sT/2)}v,\quad f=2v\sinh(s(1-T)/2),\quad k=e^{s/2-sT},\qquad s=2\pi i\lambda. \] Its two eigenflags are \[ v_+=e^{s(1-T)/2}v,\qquad v_-=-e^{-sT/2} \frac{\sinh(s(1-T)/2)}{\sinh(sT/2)}v. \] The plus flag has degree \(+1\) and exactly the original Fubini--Study current on the real sphere at every level parameter. For \(0<\lambda<1\), the inverse flag has degree \(-1\), whereas at \(\lambda=1\) its interior limit equals the plus flag and has degree \(+1\). Writing \(\varepsilon=1-\lambda\), the two inverse-flag bubbles are \[ v=\varepsilon y:\quad v_-\to-1/\bar y,\qquad V=1/v=\varepsilon y:\quad v_-\to\bar y . \] Each has degree \(-1\). Accordingly its signed weak current has limit \[ \omega_{\mathrm{FS}}-\delta_{T=0}-\delta_{T=1}. \] For a direct check, the inverse-flag latitude tends to \(T\) in the interior but has endpoint values \(1,0\); integration by parts against the angularly averaged test function gives exactly these two negative endpoint masses. This verifies the current signs and shows why the earlier ordinary-falling-frame plus bubble is not intrinsic. The frame gauge can be nonuniform in \(N\). It does not permit discarding the selected inverse eigenflag, the two genuine endpoint bubbles in that frame, or the pivotal adapter (5). No whole quantum dressing or selected norm follows from the principal flag calculation alone.

title: The integral half-longitude and the marked quantum boundary algebra
text: # The integral half-longitude and the marked quantum boundary algebra Research note, 26 October 2026. This fills the peripheral index-two step left in [the pointed gluing construction](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md). The preferred longitude has an integral half-class in the saturated edge quotient. No division by two modulo the root level is used. Its scalar lift and its identification with the actual quantum state remain distinct questions. ## 1. Statement with the knot marking retained Let M be an oriented knot exterior in S^3 with an oriented ideal triangulation of t tetrahedra. Use the signed integral shape lattice Lambda = direct_sum_j Z^2, Omega_j=epsilon_j [[0,1],[-1,0]], e_0=(1,0), e_1=(0,1), e_2=(-1,-1). The opposite edge types are (01,23), (02,13), (03,12). For a global edge e its signed incidence vector has j-th block beta(e)_j=epsilon_j(a_ej-c_ej,b_ej-c_ej). Let E be their span. The independently proved integral edge theorem in the linked note makes E primitive and isotropic of rank t-1. Consequently B=E^perp/E is a unimodular symplectic lattice of rank two. The integral normal curve map delta:H_1(boundary M;Z)->B is taken with convention Omega(delta gamma,delta eta)=-2 I(gamma,eta). (1.1) Fix the actual marked meridian mu and preferred longitude lambda, oriented so I(mu,lambda)=1. Then ell=delta lambda/2 belongs to B, (1.2) Omega(delta mu,ell)=-1. The half in (1.2) is unique, and (delta mu,ell) is an integral basis of B. Thus it is the preferred longitude that is halved, while the unhalved meridian retains its prescribed marking. The original normal-curve image has basis (delta mu,2ell) and index two. The proof below needs only the knot topology and the primitive edge theorem, not hyperbolicity or positive shapes. The audited positive triangulation theorem supplies a geometric realization of this construction for every hyperbolic knot. ## 2. An intersection identity for arbitrary face permutations Here is a direct check of (1.1) without a global branching. At tetrahedron corner v let f_0<f_1<f_2 be the other three indices. For outgoing normal flows r_f satisfying r_f0+r_f1+r_f2=0 put d_v(r)=(-1)^v (r_f1 e_type(v,f2)-r_f2 e_type(v,f1)), d(r)=sum_v d_v(r). For example a single normal arc has flow -1 on its entry side and +1 on its exit side. The formula is its signed shape-exponent vector, after eliminating e_2=-e_0-e_1. The oriented cusp triangle has sign tau_v=-epsilon(-1)^v. Two closed normal flows have 2 I(r,s)=sum_(j,v) tau_v (r_f0 s_f1-r_f1 s_f0). (2.1) This is the intersection form of the thickened trivalent cusp graph: displace the two flows in its oriented ribbons; the local contribution at a vertex is half the displayed determinant, and the contributions in an edge strip cancel between its ends. The determinant is independent of the cyclic base side because both flows have sum zero. Thus (2.1) holds for integral graph cycles as well as for embedded curves. Set J_3=[[0,1,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,-1,0]]. On face f order its three vertices increasingly and collect their corner flows as r_f,s_f. Expansion in the eight independent flow coordinates gives Omega_epsilon(d(r),d(s)) +sum_v tau_v (r_f0 s_f1-r_f1 s_f0) =sum_f epsilon(-1)^f r_f^T J_3 s_f. (2.2) For every face permutation matrix P, P^T J_3 P=sign(P) J_3. Across an oriented face pairing, both outgoing flows reverse, and the oriented face signs differ by minus the permutation sign. Hence the right side of (2.2) cancels pairwise under completely arbitrary face permutations. Summation proves (1.1). A small normal circle about an endpoint of a global edge has shape vector plus or minus beta(e): each successive corner contributes its signed opposite-edge type. It is contractible in the cusp. This proves both orthogonality to E and that changing a cusp representative through a vertex changes its vector only by E. Thus delta is the stated integral homology map. ## 3. The mod-two cochain that forces divisibility Take v=(u_j,w_j) in E^perp. In one tetrahedron put, modulo two, q_0=-w, q_1=u, q_2=w-u, b_0=0, b_1=q_0, b_2=q_1, b_3=q_2. (3.1) For a local edge ij with complementary faces k,l, q_type(ij)=b_k+b_l. (3.2) For instance edge 01 gives b_2+b_3=u+(w-u)=w=-w modulo two. The other five identities follow from q_0+q_1+q_2=0. On the dual edge crossing a paired face Tf<->Ug define a_v(Tf->Ug)=b_Tf+b_Ug in F_2. (3.3) Around a dual two-cell, (3.2) identifies its coboundary with the sum of q-values at the corresponding global edge. This sum is zero by Omega(v,beta(e))=0. Thus a_v is a closed cochain on the dual spine of M. An arc at corner i entering face k and leaving face l pairs with v modulo two as q_type(ij), where j is the remaining vertex. Equations (3.1)--(3.2) make this b_k+b_l. Summing along a closed cusp curve and regrouping at face crossings gives Omega(v,delta gamma)=a_v(i_*gamma) mod 2. (3.4) The preferred longitude is zero in H_1(M;Z), so its push-in is zero over F_2. Therefore Omega(v,delta lambda) is even for every v in E^perp. (3.5) On the unimodular lattice B, a vector that pairs evenly with every vector lies in 2B: the pairing identifies B with B^vee, and its associated functional is twice an integral functional. This proves (1.2). The lattice is torsion free, so the half is unique. Equation (1.1) gives pairing -1 with delta mu, hence these two vectors form a basis of the rank-two unimodular lattice. This argument also works for any boundary class nullhomologous modulo two. For a multi-component link, a component's preferred longitude can have nonzero image determined by its linking numbers; the knot statement should not be copied without that correction. ## 4. Computing the half before specializing the quantum parameter Choose an integral basis e_1,...,e_(t-1) of E and an integral normal representative d_lambda of delta lambda. Solve over F_2 sum_i a_i e_i=d_lambda mod 2, a_i in {0,1}. The solution exists by (1.2) and is unique for this basis because E is primitive. Set e_lambda=sum_i a_i e_i, v_ell=(d_lambda-e_lambda)/2 in Lambda. (4.1) This is an integer vector, belongs to E^perp, and represents ell. In particular it makes sense before choosing N. Even N causes no need to invert two in Z/N. Using another correction changes v_ell by an element of E and does not change ell in B. An unspecified homological meridian can differ from the actual marked meridian by k lambda. The theorem uses the supplied actual meridian; a cellular algorithm that constructs a linking-one curve does not thereby fix its framing. ## 5. The square root retains an edge character At q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, use the full Weyl convention with lambda_W=-q: W(v)W(w)=lambda_W^Omega(v,w) W(v+w), W(v)^N=z^v. Let the edge eigenspace have its specified character W(e)=c(e). Write the prescribed unhalved longitude as Lambda_hat=a_lambda W(d_lambda). Since e_lambda and v_ell are orthogonal, (4.1) gives on that space Lambda_hat=a_lambda c(e_lambda) W(v_ell)^2. (5.1) On the square-root cover, choose the specified lift eta_lambda^2=a_lambda c(e_lambda), T=eta_lambda W(v_ell), Y=a_mu W(d_mu). Then, at every level including even and composite levels, T^2=Lambda_hat, T Y=Q Y T. (5.2) Replacing v_ell by v_ell+e changes e_lambda to e_lambda-2e. Taking eta_lambda to eta_lambda/c(e) cancels W(e) exactly. The remaining sign choice is a genuine mu_2 torsor, not an unrecorded numerical normalization. There is a further even-level condition. The central value is T^N=eta_lambda^N z^v_ell, (T^N)^2=Lambda_hat^N. (5.3) For even N, replacing T by -T leaves T^N unchanged. Its sign is already constrained by the edge-character lift; the mu_2 choice cannot repair an incorrectly matched central longitude. Matching the actual SL_2 marking therefore still requires this lift. With unit-normalized centers, the unhalved algebra generated by Y,T^2 has two sectors for even N, distinguished by Y^(N/2). The half-longitude T exchanges them because Q^(N/2)=-1. At odd N the half and unhalved algebras generate the same matrix algebra. ## 6. Relation to the actual ADO convention and the geometric action The [independently proved actual descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) uses Y=M^2 and sigma(Y)=QY. Equation (5.2) supplies exactly this boundary algebra with the prescribed meridian. It is an algebra and marking identification, not a source-module identification. The full ADO scalar gauge remains g(q,Y)=-q^(-1)(QY-1)/(Y-1), T_full=g(q,Y) T_reduced. On the generic central field, telescope the complete product: Norm_sigma(g)=(-q^(-1))^N=(-1)^(N-1), T_full^N=(-1)^(N-1) T_reduced^N. (6.1) At Y^N=1 this is an identity of the whole retained lattice, not permission to evaluate separate zero denominators. The actual full dimension and its meridian germ must still be kept. Classically the unhalved normal coordinates are (m,l)=(Y,L^2), while the saturated lattice has coordinates (Y,L). The scalar lift fixes the sign of L; completeness does not justify replacing it by +1. The earlier action conversion is now explained by the integral lattice: dS_Q=Log(L) dLog(Y), R=S_Q-(1/2)Log(Y)Log(L). (6.2) This is the same regulator action already derived on the actual crossing's geometric critical branch. It fixes the parameter and peripheral determinant, but not that branch's contribution to the selected quantum period. ## 7. What this supplies to the ideal-triangulation comparison A positive geometric triangulation supplies the marked Bloch lift and its volume regulator. Primitive edge reduction supplies a nonzero rank-N geometric boundary block. The theorem here identifies its saturated lattice using the actual meridian and preferred longitude, with every scalar lift visible. The remaining comparison must construct a relative geometric extension with its source and evaluation functional and identify them with those of the actual ADO/Verma period. It must then prove the selected period has the marked Bloch-regulator norm. Module rank, matching Weyl algebras, and equality of complete classical Bloch classes alone do not establish either statement. The candidate projected tetrahedron vector can still vanish. ## 8. Coverage and exact diagnostics Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 of [Neumann's integral triangulation paper](https://www.math.columbia.edu/department/neumann/preprints/cspaper.pdf) already cover the doubled boundary pairing and its mod-two compatibility with the interior. This is existing structural coverage, not a novelty claim. Only those statements were checked for coverage; the explicit face-flow and mod-two potentials above give our proof independently. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_integral_half_longitude.py) checks (2.2) symbolically at both orientations, its covariance under all six face permutations, and 192 mod-two arc identities. Its 12 cellular presentations include native knot triangulations, diagram shadows with finite sphere vertices, and arbitrary local relabelings. On a basis of all balanced mod-two vectors it checks that (3.3) is closed and that every cusp graph cycle satisfies (3.4). Integer cellular boundaries, the half representative and the saturated/unhalved Smith invariants are verified separately. At N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12 it checks the nontrivial edge-character correction, (5.2), sector exchange, the even central-sign condition, and the full gauge norm (6.1) at a generic nonsingular center. The cellular meridian is explicitly a homological meridian of unspecified framing. These tests do not identify a quantum knot state or prove the volume limit. Results: [integral_half_longitude_results.json](../experiments/integral_half_longitude_results.json). title: The entire integral knot centralizer is self-dual under its actual cut
text: # The entire integral knot centralizer is self-dual under its actual cut Research note, 26 October 2026. This extends the local two-factor residue pairing to every tensor power at the Kashaev color. The proof constructs a symmetric PBW coefficient form, realizes the actual complete-color module as a projective summand, and calibrates the induced trace to the original ADO dimension. It does not invoke a published modified-trace or projectivity theorem. The result controls the full integral centralizer, not just a chosen fusion algebra. It also proves that every complete-color E,F,K intertwiner lifts through the actual meridian deformation. The geometric quantum-A source and its selected regulator norm remain unidentified; this is no volume-conjecture proof. ## 1. Statement with the original cut and phase Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1). Put R=C[[u]], M=exp(u), x=-M/q, k_x=x^N=(-1)^(N+1)M^N, W_b=V_x^(tensor b). Use the original matrices, coproduct and pivot from [the intrinsic cut calculation](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md): Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, g=K^(1-N). Every centralizer below means commutation with these actual total E,F,K matrices. Let C_(b,R)=End_(E,F,K;R)(W_b), t_b(A)=Tr((P_0 tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))A), mathfrak_t_b(A)=d_N(M)t_b(A), d_N(M)=eta_N(M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=(-1)^(N+1)q^(N(1-N)/2)=i^(N+3). (1.1) The whole value d_N(1)=eta_N/N is a unit of R. The zero-framing factor remains theta_x^(-writhe) in the braid operator being traced. For every b>=1, C_(b,R) is a finite free symmetric R-algebra with perfect pairing (A,B) -> mathfrak_t_b(AB). (1.2) Its full cut dual is exactly itself. For b>=2 its rank is N^(2b-3); at b=1 it is R. In addition, C_(b,R)/u C_(b,R) =End_(E,F,K;C)(V_(-q^(-1))^(tensor b)). (1.3) Thus the pairing remains perfect on the entire complete-color centralizer, including its nonreduced parts. No higher-tensor matrix-algebra description over the confluent center is asserted. ## 2. A finite PBW algebra over a varying central character For any unit k in R define H_k=R<E,F,K,K^(-1)>/ (K E=Q E K, K F=Q^(-1)F K, E F-F E=(K-K^(-1))/rho, E^N=F^N=0, K^N=k). (2.1) It has R-basis F^a K^b E^c, 0<=a,b,c<N. (2.2) Here is a direct normal-form justification. Order F before K before E, reduce K powers modulo N with their full k factors, and use E F^a=F^a E+[a]F^(a-1) (q^(1-a)K-q^(a-1)K^(-1))/rho. (2.3) The only additional boundary ambiguities are commutations with K^N, E^N or F^N. K^N commutes because Q^N=1; the extra term in (2.3) vanishes for a=N because [N]=0. The corresponding formula for E^N F has the same property. The ordinary K E F ambiguity reduces to the same (K-K^(-1))/rho on both paths. Disjoint and power-overlap reductions agree. These rules are terminating and resolve the critical overlaps, proving (2.2). Define one PBW coefficient functional, with no unknown scalar: mu_k(F^a K^b E^c)=delta_(a,N-1)delta_(b,0)delta_(c,N-1). (2.4) This is symmetric. For E, the lower term in (2.3) cannot contribute to (2.4), since it lowers the F exponent. The leading commutation with K^b contributes Q^(-b), which equals one whenever (2.4) is nonzero. The F calculation is the same with E and F exchanged. Commuting K gives identical factors when a=c=N-1. Thus mu_k(g h)=mu_k(h g) for g=E,F,K and every h, hence for every pair of algebra elements. Its pairing is perfect over R. Filter by total E,F degree. In the associated graded algebra E and F commute and K retains the two inverse Q actions. Every basis monomial has a unique complementary pair of E,F exponents and a complementary K power that gives the coefficient (2.4), with a unit Q and k multiplier. This is a perfect graded pairing. Products of total degree below 2N-2 contribute zero to mu, so the ungraded pairing matrix is block triangular after ordering by complementary degrees. Its diagonal blocks are these invertible graded pairings. This proves perfection in R. ## 3. The simple complete color is an actual projective summand Use the central Casimir Omega=rho^2 F E+q K+q^(-1)K^(-1). Successive commutation gives the exact identity rho^(2N) F^N E^N =product_(j=0)^(N-1)(Omega-q^(2j+1)K-q^(-2j-1)K^(-1)). The product is T_N(Omega)+K^N+K^(-N), where T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(j+1)=z T_j-T_(j-1). Therefore H_k satisfies P_k(Omega)=0, P_k(z)=T_N(z)+k+k^(-1). (3.1) For k=k_x, the actual highest-root branch is c_x=q x+q^(-1)x^(-1)=-M-M^(-1). At M=1 it equals -2 and P_(k_x)'(c_x)|_(M=1)=(-1)^(N+1)N^2, (3.2) which is nonzero for all N. Other roots are distinct from this one at that point. Consequently the following actual polynomial is a central idempotent over R: e_St=(P_(k_x)(Omega)/(Omega-c_x))/P_(k_x)'(c_x). (3.3) The quotient denotes polynomial division before evaluation. All its coefficients belong to R; there is no inverse of a vanishing Casimir difference in (3.3). The K-root projectors on this block are pi_a=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(K/(x Q^(-a)))^r, 0<=a<N. On e_St H_(k_x), the relations FE and EF on adjacent weight spaces have scalars e_a(x) and e_(a+1)(x), respectively. Each e_a(x), 0<a<N, is a unit at M=1. Thus every interior E,F edge is invertible up to that unit. The remaining boundary F edge is zero because F^N=0 and all other edges are invertible; E^N=0 kills the boundary E edge in the same way. This leaves one length-N chain and its full matrix units. In particular e_St H_(k_x)=Mat_N(R). The primitive idempotent e=e_St pi_0 has left ideal H_(k_x)e free of rank N over R. The basis F^a e identifies it with the original V_x: F has coefficient one, K has root x Q^(-a), and E has exactly e_a(x). It is a direct summand of H_(k_x), hence is projective over that algebra. This is an explicit projective realization of the actual complete-color deformation. ## 4. Tensoring preserves this projectivity Before fixing K^N, the nilpotent algebra is a Hopf algebra. Its central group-like K^N gives coproducts Delta_(k,l):H_(kl)->H_k tensor H_l, S:H_(l^(-1))->H_l. The primitive-root binomial identity ensures E^N=F^N=0 is respected. If W is an H_l-module free over R, the explicit map Phi:H_(kl) tensor_R W -> H_k tensor_R W, h tensor w -> sum h_(1) tensor h_(2)w (4.1) intertwines the free action on the first domain factor with the diagonal action on the target. Its inverse is a tensor w -> sum a_(1) tensor S(a_(2))w, Delta_(kl,l^(-1))(a)=sum a_(1) tensor a_(2). (4.2) These are the two usual multiplication/antipode identities, checked before central reduction. They descend because K^N has character kl on the domain and character k times l on the target, while the inverse uses kl times l^(-1)=k. The nilpotent powers descend as well. Thus H_k tensor W is a free H_(kl)-module of rank dim_R W. A projective H_k-module is a direct summand of a finite free one. Tensoring its inclusion and retraction with W, and using (4.1), proves it remains projective over H_(kl). Starting with Section 3 proves W_b is projective over H_(k_x^b) for every b. ## 5. Calibrating the symmetric trace to the full ADO cut Write F=Frac(R). When k^2!=1 in F, as for k=k_x^b, H_k over F is the direct product of N full N-by-N matrix algebras. This follows from the same weight-chain construction in Section 3 applied to all distinct roots c_j=q z_j+q^(-1)z_j^(-1), z_j^N=k. On each root, the interior e_a(z_j) are nonzero and the boundary edges vanish. On each simple module pi_x has ordinary trace one. Direct PBW degree counting gives mu_k(pi_x Omega^m)=0, 0<=m<N-1, mu_k(pi_x Omega^(N-1))=rho^(2N-2)/N. The last equality uses the leading term rho^(2N-2)F^(N-1)E^(N-1); only the zeroth K coefficient of pi_x contributes to (2.4). Lagrange interpolation therefore shows that mu_k has the simple-block weight w_j=rho^(2N-2)/(N P_k'(c_j)). Use the exact, k-independent factor gamma_N=N^2 q^(N(1-N)/2)/rho^(2N-2). (5.1) Differentiating T_N(t+t^(-1))=t^N+t^(-N) gives gamma_N w_j=N q^(N(1-N)/2)/P_k'(c_j) =-q^(N(1-N)/2) (q z_j-q^(-1)z_j^(-1))/(z_j^N-z_j^(-N)) =d_(z_j). (5.2) These are exactly the original ADO dimensions from the intrinsic cut proof. No phase or finite numerical multiplier is adjusted. In particular gamma_N mu_(k_x)(e)=d_N(M), including its regular complete value eta_N/N. ## 6. From the PBW form to every integral centralizer For a symmetric finite free R-algebra (H,mu) and a finite projective left H-module P, choose a splitting P -> H^m -> P. On End_H(P), define the trace by applying mu to the diagonal of its corresponding endomorphism of H^m and summing. This is independent of the splitting: if A and B are the two rectangular matrices comparing two splittings, the required identity is sum mu((AB)_(ii))=sum mu((BA)_(jj)), which follows termwise from mu(ab)=mu(ba). It is cyclic for the same reason. It is perfect. In an idempotent presentation it is the restriction of the matrix trace pairing to e Mat_m(H^op)e. For any X in that corner, cyclicity gives t(XY)=t(X eYe) for every Y. Since the whole matrix pairing is perfect and the corner is a direct R-summand, every functional on the corner extends by projection Y->eYe and is represented uniquely by an element of the corner. This proves the corner pairing is perfect, over R itself. Apply this construction to H_(k_x^b), W_b and gamma_N mu. Over F its formula is sum_j d_(z_j)Tr(A_j), by (5.2). The [intrinsic cut proof](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) independently identifies exactly that expression with the actual d_N(M)t_b. The latter is R-valued because the actual matrices, pivot and whole d_N(M) are integral at M=1. The two linear functionals agree over F, hence agree on the entire integral centralizer. The corner argument proves (1.2). The same idempotent presentation commutes with R->R/(u), so End_H(W_b) has exactly the base change (1.3). In particular no additional complete-color intertwiner needs a separate lifting assumption. The generic multiplicity formula from the intrinsic cut proof gives rank N^(2b-3) for b>=2. This completes the theorem. ## 7. The integral gauge torsor and a comparison criterion An integral H_k-linear idempotent p on W_b gives another projective module pW_b. Its endomorphism order is p C_(b,R) p, and its inherited cut pairing is perfect by the same corner argument. In particular, regular commuting finite-order edge operators that commute with H_k can be reduced by their exact averaging projector without losing cut duality. Their character roots and all scalar factors remain part of that projector. For geometric edge gluing, this H_k-linearity and regularity must be proved in the actual relative source realization; the abstract quantum-torus edge-rank theorem does not supply them. There is a local constraint on such a construction. On just two generic colors the full H_k centralizer is commutative, by the multiplicity-one decomposition. It cannot contain an invertible Weyl pair X,Y with XY=QYX and Q!=1: commutativity would imply (1-Q)YX=0. Thus the geometric clock and shift on an individual relative face cannot both be treated as H_k-linear operators on that two-color module. The full edge products and their retained source terms are the objects whose H_k-linearity must be checked. The integral comparison group is now specified: G_(b,R)=C_(b,R)^times. (7.1) Because C_(b,R) is finite free, its units form the principal open set where left multiplication has invertible determinant. Thus this is a smooth affine R-group. Nilpotent ideals in the special-fiber algebra are retained through their unipotent units. An automorphism of the complete fiber lifts directly: lift its centralizer element using (1.3); its determinant on W_b has a nonzero constant term, so the lift is invertible. Cyclicity preserves the actual cut under its inner action. This is an integral version of the generic product of general linear groups, retaining the special-fiber algebra and its nilpotent ideals. More generally, if P and Q are finite projective H_k-modules and an isomorphism P/uP -> Q/uQ is supplied, projectivity makes Hom_(H_k)(P,Q) commute with base change. Lift that isomorphism; its determinant is a unit, so it is an isomorphism over R. This is formal local rigidity with specified common H_k data. It does not supply the common module, an algebraic comparison over the whole A-curve, or a selected period section. Let C and D be full R-orders in the same finite-dimensional F-algebra, equipped with the same symmetric F-linear trace t. Suppose both are self-dual for t. Then C subset D implies C=D. (7.2) Indeed dualizing the inclusion gives D^vee subset C^vee, or D subset C. The reverse inclusion was the hypothesis. This requires a common calibrated trace and perfection on both orders; matching generic ranks alone would not suffice. For the knot centralizer the source order and its calibrated trace are now available uniformly. If a proposed triangulation presentation supplies a second self-dual order and a compatible generic comparison, one integral inclusion will prove equality of these orders and their cut pairings. The selected section, the relevant operator action, and the prescribed lattice still need to be transported; equality of endomorphism orders by itself does not select a period vector. The subsequent [sewn-source construction](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md) now supplies an explicit two-copy projective corner for the actual cup/cap residue with one helper strand. Its regular rational lift uses V_(-M^3/q) on the first surviving strand, so the total central character remains the original one. The cut on that corner is the original calibrated trace. This application retains the full meridian charge factor and identifies sewn residues, while the entire polar projector, global source and selected period remain additional comparisons. The subsequent [adjacent-source normal form](adjacent_source_normal_form.md) now determines the full local projectors with their regular parts. It also constrains any common-order proposal: the ordinary trace of two adjacent actual polar projectors has a nonzero double pole. No one finite lattice can make both integral, even without an H-linearity requirement. The integral numerators form a regular matrix source algebra, while their unscaled projector arrows require a groupoid of lattice changes. The self-dual-order criterion above still applies to genuinely common integral operators; it does not remove this pole obstruction. At the first shifted color x=-M, e_1(x) is no longer a unit at M=1, so Section 3 cannot be applied to that color. Its actual [elementary modification and conductor](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md#the-first-meridian-wall-is-an-elementary-integral-modification) must be retained. This theorem does not turn a polar meridian comparison into an invertible integral matrix. ## 8. What this contributes to the ideal triangulation program The earlier generic cut formula and two-factor self-duality are now extended to the full integral tensor centralizer, for all N and every strand count. This identifies a precise setting for integral source descent: projective modules over symmetric finite orders, with their calibrated trace, plus the conductor modifications at the meridian wall. This is an algebraic bilinear pairing. For b>=2 it even has mathfrak_t_b(1)=0, since the ordinary quantum dimension vanishes. Perfection therefore supplies no positivity or growth bound for the selected contraction. Its norm still needs to be compared with the marked Bloch-regulator norm. The positive ideal triangulation supplies its marked Bloch lift and regulator norm. The actual quantum source still needs a compatible relative triangulated realization. Nothing here identifies the central Casimir polynomial with the knot A-curve, matches a fixed hyperbolic root character to the actual ADO character, or estimates the selected quantum period across N. Those comparisons remain necessary for the volume conjecture. ## 9.
