Coverage and diagnostics The abstract of [Beliakova--Blanchet--Gainutdinov, 1801.00321v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00321v2) covers modified traces on projectives and their realization by symmetric forms from Hopf integrals, including restricted quantum groups. That theory is existing literature; no novelty claim is made. Its theorems and proofs are not premises here. The PBW, idempotent, tensor, corner and normalization calculations above independently supply the particular statement over C[[log M]], with the exact ADO factor and every parity retained. [The audit](../experiments/audit_integral_centralizer_duality.py) checks 15 PBW Frobenius forms at N=2,3,4,5,6 with generic and both sign central characters. It verifies all left-regular generator relations, the central polynomial, symmetry and a nonzero Gram determinant. Five primitive-idempotent cases realize the original complete color as a rank-N left ideal; five generic cases calibrate every simple-block weight to the original ADO dimension. Six explicit free-tensor maps at N=2,3,4, including the shifted second color, are invertible and intertwine all E,F,K. Ten further cases compute the entire complete-color centralizer directly from its commutator equations, without specializing any fusion frame. Levels 2 through 6 and up to five strands give 279 basis elements in total. Every one is checked against the full E,F,K matrices. The original full cut is symmetric and its Gram determinant is nonzero in every case. These diagnostics test the uniform proofs rather than establishing a volume limit. [Results](../experiments/integral_centralizer_duality_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_integral_centralizer_duality.py

title: The intrinsic ADO cut and its meridian centralizer torsor
text: # The intrinsic ADO cut and its meridian centralizer torsor Research note, 26 October 2026. This proves a basis-independent formula for the actual modified ADO cut, using the original nilpotent modules and pivotal contraction. It then assembles the local meridian source maps into an atlas for every even-strand knot braid. The transition group is a product of general linear groups. Its conjugations disappear on the trace quotient, but transitions inside a braid word remain. The proof uses explicit Casimir moments and fusion matrix units, rather than an assumed modified-trace theorem. This overlaps existing modified dimension/trace theory; it is not a new invariant. The geometric quantum-A component, integral source comparison with an ideal triangulation, and selected regulator norm remain unproved. ## 1. Actual data and the claim Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1). The original nilpotent color V_x has basis v_a, 0<=a<N, with K v_a=x Q^(-a) v_a, F v_a=v_(a+1), E v_a=e_a(x) v_(a-1), e_a(x)=[a](x q^(1-a)-x^(-1)q^(a-1))/rho. F v_(N-1)=0. Use exactly Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, g_x=K^(1-N), theta_x=x^(1-N). (1.1) In highest-root coordinates the full ADO dimension is d_x=-q^(N(1-N)/2) (q x-q^(-1)x^(-1))/(x^N-x^(-N)). (1.2) For the actual meridian M=-q x this is d_N(M)=eta_N (M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=(-1)^(N+1)q^(N(1-N)/2)=i^(N+3). (1.3) The quotient at M=1 is its whole regular value eta_N/N. The constant in (1.2) is retained even though it cancels in the fusion ratios below. All intertwining and centralizer conditions in this note refer to the three actual total matrices E,F,K. Work first over the generic color field: every successive product of the chosen highest roots has 2N-th power different from one. These conditions define a nonempty open chart. All ensuing identities are rational identities on that chart. For W=V_(x_1) tensor ... tensor V_(x_b), let t_W(A) be the scalar right pivotal closure of all factors except the first. Thus the actual cut row in the original basis is t_W(A)=Tr((P_0 tensor g_(x_2) tensor ... tensor g_(x_b)) A), P_0 v_a=delta_(a,0) v_0. (1.4) For an intertwiner A this partial closure is t_W(A) times identity on V_(x_1). Define the full weighted cut mathfrak_t_W=d_(x_1)t_W. Write the actual module decomposition as W=direct_sum_z V_z tensor H_z, A=direct_sum_z I_(V_z) tensor A_z. The result is the exact formula mathfrak_t_W(A)=sum_z d_z Tr_(H_z)(A_z). (1.5) In particular this full cut is cyclic, is independent of the fusion basis, and is preserved by every U_q-module isomorphism. The zero framing factor theta_x^(-writhe) is still applied to the braid operator; it is not absorbed into (1.5). ## 2. A uniform two-color Casimir moment calculation On V_x tensor V_y put Omega=rho^2 F_tot E_tot+q K_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1), z_j=xy Q^(-j), c_j=q z_j+q^(-1)z_j^(-1), 0<=j<N. The highest vector of degree j is h_j=sum_a b_a v_a tensor v_(j-a), b_0=1, with b_(a+1)/b_a=-e_(j-a)(y)/(e_(a+1)(x)y Q^(-(j-a-1))). (2.1) It is annihilated by E_tot. Its N F-descendants form V_(z_j). Indeed all e_r(z_j), 0<r<N, are nonzero on this chart, so the commutation relation precludes a shorter descendant string. The primitive-root binomial identity gives F_tot^N=E_tot^N=0. Distinct Casimir eigenvalues make these N summands a direct sum of dimension N^2. This proves the stated two-color decomposition. Put k_x=x^N, k_y=y^N and let T_N be normalized by T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(r+1)=z T_r-T_(r-1). The Casimir polynomial is P_(x,y)(z)=product_j(z-c_j)=T_N(z)+k_x k_y+(k_x k_y)^(-1). (2.2) Here is the pivotal moment identity, before using any fusion weight: ptr_(g_y)(Omega^m)=0, 0<=m<N-1, ptr_(g_y)(Omega^(N-1))=s_x I, s_x=-N (k_x-k_x^(-1))/(q x-q^(-1)x^(-1)). (2.3) First, the closure is an intertwiner of V_x. For Z=E or Z=KF, Delta Z=Z tensor K+1 tensor Z. Multiply its intertwining identity by 1 tensor K^(-1)g_y before closing. The first terms give the commutator with Z on the open leg. The remaining terms cancel by cyclicity on the closed leg, since K^(-1)g_y=K^(-N) is central. The Delta K identity gives commutation with K as well, hence with F. V_x is simple, so it suffices to compute its (0,0) entry. For the input v_0 tensor v_d, write t=Q^(-d) and use the first index a along its fixed total-degree block. The diagonal entry (Omega^m)_(0,d;0,d) is a polynomial H_m(t) of degree at most m. To check this explicitly, the three entries of Omega along this block are diagonal at a: x^(-1)Q^a(qy+q^(-1)y^(-1)) +y Q^a((q x+q^(-1)x^(-1))-(q+q^(-1))x^(-1)Q^a)t, a -> a+1: rho^2 e_(d-a)(y), a -> a-1: rho^2 e_a(x)x^(-1)y Q^(2a-1)t. The upward coefficient is Laurent of degrees -1,0,1 in t; the downward coefficient has degree 1. A closed path has as many upward as downward steps, so its lowest exponent is nonnegative and its highest is at most its length. Invalid paths at d-a=0 vanish because e_0=0. No truncation at a=N affects these moments. Since g_y v_d=y^(1-N)Q^(-d)v_d, closing multiplies H_m(Q^(-d)) by y^(1-N)Q^(-d) and sums d=0,...,N-1. Root orthogonality proves the vanishing in (2.3). For m=N-1 only the leading coefficient of H_(N-1) survives. After removing y, the leading tridiagonal matrix L has entries L_(a,a)=Q^a((q x+q^(-1)x^(-1))-(q+q^(-1))x^(-1)Q^a), L_(a+1,a)=-q Q^a, L_(a-1,a)=rho^2 e_a(x)x^(-1)Q^(2a-1). For 0<=a<=m<N its first column satisfies the explicit identity (L^m)_(a,0)=(-1)^a q^m Q^(a(a-1)/2) {m choose a}_Q product_(r=a)^(m-1)(x-Q^r x^(-1)). (2.4) This is proved by induction in the displayed three-term recurrence. The coefficient of x uses {m+1 choose a}_Q={m choose a-1}_Q+Q^a{m choose a}_Q. For the coefficient of x^(-1), use in addition (1-Q^(a+1)){m choose a+1}_Q=(1-Q^(m-a)){m choose a}_Q; the remaining adjacent-coefficient identity is the same relation with a replaced by a-1. Thus (2.4) follows without an unproved orthogonal-polynomial or integration formula. At m=N-1,a=0, the product in (2.4) becomes q^(N-1) product_(r=0)^(N-2)(x-Q^r x^(-1)) =-(k_x-k_x^(-1))/(q x-q^(-1)x^(-1)). Root orthogonality supplies the further factor N. This proves (2.3). Every polynomial f now obeys ptr_(g_y)(f(Omega)) =s_x [z^(N-1)](f mod P_(x,y)) I. (2.5) For the spectral projector P_j, Lagrange interpolation gives top coefficient 1/P_(x,y)'(c_j). Differentiate T_N(t+t^(-1))=t^N+t^(-N) at t=q z_j to obtain P_(x,y)'(c_j)=-N(k_x k_y-(k_x k_y)^(-1)) /(q z_j-q^(-1)z_j^(-1)). Consequently ptr_(g_y)(P_j)=(d_(z_j)/d_x) I. (2.6) The left closure uses g_x^(-1), and gives d_(z_j)/d_y. One can check this by transposition and duality: S(Omega)=Omega, V_x^*=V_(x^(-1)Q^(-1)), and s_(x^(-1)Q^(-1))=s_x. The same calculation (2.5) therefore proves the left formula. No vanishing ordinary quantum dimension has been divided out. ## 3. All multiplicity spaces, including off-diagonal matrix units Iterate (2.1) along a left-associated fusion tree. A path p has successive simple roots z_1=x_1,z_2,...,z_b, with z_r=z_(r-1)x_r Q^(-j_r). A normalized inclusion i_p and projection p_p give matrix units i_p p_(p') between paths with the same final simple root. These span the entire centralizer. Close the last leaf of such a matrix unit. It becomes an intertwiner between the preceding simple roots. If those roots differ, it is zero. If they agree, their last fusion labels agree, and (2.6) gives the factor d_(z_b)/d_(z_(b-1)). Repeat. For a diagonal path all ratios telescope to d_(z_b)/d_(x_1). For distinct paths with the same final root, there is a last stage where their preceding simple roots differ; the partial closure at that stage is zero. Thus d_(x_1)t_W(i_p p_(p'))=delta_(p,p') d_(z_b). This proves (1.5) on every matrix unit, hence on every intertwiner. It also proves the claim for arbitrary fusion frames: ordinary multiplicity traces are invariant under their basis changes. For b>=2 there are N final roots z_j=(product_i x_i)Q^(-j), and each has multiplicity r=N^(b-2). In particular C_W=End_(U_q)(W)=product_(j=0)^(N-1) Mat_r(F), C_W^times=product_j GL_r(F). (3.1) The original cut functional, including its full dimension, is therefore intrinsic to W and its actual pivotal structure. ### The full cut is an algebraic residue Let k=(product_i x_i)^N and P_W(z)=T_N(z)+k+k^(-1). The center of (3.1) is F[z]/P_W, represented by the total Casimir. If a(z) is the unique degree<N polynomial whose value at c_j is Tr(A_j), then (2.2) and (1.2) give d_(z_j) P_W'(c_j)=c_N, c_N=N q^(N(1-N)/2), mathfrak_t_W(A)=c_N sum_j a(c_j)/P_W'(c_j) =c_N [z^(N-1)]a(z). (3.2) Here a is the ordinary matrix trace on every central block, hence the reduced trace of the centralizer over its center. The last functional is the algebraic residue of a/P_W. It remains defined by the displayed coefficient when roots collide. This expression retains c_N, including its phase and factor N. ### The complete two-factor centralizer has a perfect integral pairing Set M=exp(u), R=C[[u]], x=-M/q, and use the actual equal-color two-factor matrices over R. The coefficient in (2.3) is the Laurent polynomial s_x=(-1)^(N+1)N M^(1-N) sum_(j=0)^(N-1)M^(2j), s_x|_(M=1)=(-1)^(N+1)N^2. (3.3) It is a unit in R. On the finite free algebra A_R=R[z]/(T_N(z)+U+U^(-1)), U=M^(2N), the actual pivotal cut is s_x times the top-coefficient functional. In the basis 1,z,...,z^(N-1), its pairing (a,b)->ptr_g(ab) has Gram determinant (-1)^(N(N-1)/2) s_x^N in R^times. (3.4) To see this, entries with i+j<N-1 vanish and those with i+j=N-1 equal s_x. Reversing columns makes the Gram matrix triangular with diagonal s_x. This proves (3.4), regardless of the lower coefficients of P. Thus A_R identifies with its full R-dual by the original cut, including the nonreduced complete fiber. Multiplying by the full ADO factor gives exactly the constant c_N in (3.2), since d_N(M)s_x=c_N. This also identifies the entire deformable centralizer order: End_(U_q,R)(V_x tensor V_x)=A_R. (3.5) Indeed its fraction-field algebra is A_R tensor Frac(R), by the generic multiplicity-one decomposition. Any integral intertwiner therefore belongs to this fraction algebra. Its pairing with A_R is integral, because the actual matrices and pivotal closure are integral. Self-duality (3.4) places it back in A_R. Conversely every polynomial in the Casimir is an integral intertwiner. The subsequent [integral projective cut theorem](integral_projective_cut_duality.md) now proves base change and perfect cut duality for every tensor power: all complete-color intertwiners lift through R. No matrix-algebra description over the confluent center is asserted for higher tensor powers. The argument uses explicit projective summands and a symmetric PBW form calibrated to the same ADO cut. ## 4. The comparison torsor and its canonical trace quotient For two isomorphic generic modules W,W', their intertwiners form a right torsor under C_W^times. If G:W->W' is such an intertwiner, mathfrak_t_(W')(G A G^(-1))=mathfrak_t_W(A). (4.1) Changing G to G D conjugates the pulled operator by D in C_W. These inner changes act trivially on the additive quotient C_W/[C_W,C_W] = direct_sum_(j=0)^(N-1) F. (4.2) The bracket here denotes the span of commutators, not a group quotient. On each matrix block the quotient is its ordinary trace. Indeed every traceless matrix is a sum of elementary commutators; and D A D^(-1)-A=[D,A D^(-1)]. This proves both assertions directly. Thus the intertwiner torsor induces a canonical map on (4.2), and (1.5) is its specified weighted period functional. This resolves a scalar-normalization issue generically: a choice of intertwiner does not change the transported full cut. It does not say that one scalar cut determines all N quotient coordinates, or that a matrix identification preserves the integral source lattice. ## 5. Meridian atlas for an entire even-strand braid Let b=2h and W_M=V_x^(tensor b), x=-M/q. Then W_M and W_(qM) are generically isomorphic: their final highest-root sets differ by q^b=Q^h, which permutes the labels. The actual two-factor meridian map from [the Casimir-source note](meridian_casimir_source.md) therefore gives an explicit base comparison G_A(M)=G_12(M) tensor G_34(M) tensor ... tensor G_(b-1,b)(M). (5.1) All total E,F,K are intertwined. The 2N-step product is identity, because each local G=H(qM)P H(M)^(-1) telescopes and P^(2N)=1. The N-step color/parity identification is still the specified one in the Casimir-source note, rather than an omitted sign. Let B_i(M) be the actual positive crossing at positions i,i+1, with i=1,...,b-1. Put Y=M^2, U=M^(2N), a=-Y^(-1), c=1+U^(-1). Let P_i be its actual last Casimir projector. The local formula is L_i^+=a B_i+c P_i, L_i^-=a^(-1)B_i^(-1)(I-P_i)+P_i. (5.2) They are exact inverses: on P_i, B_i has eigenvalue Y/U and a(Y/U)+c=1; on its complement L_i^+=a B_i. The full factor c and the projector pole at U=1 have not been replaced separately by a numerical value. Put delta=B_1 ... B_(b-1), delta_s=delta(qM). The braid relation gives delta^(i-1)B_1 delta^(-(i-1))=B_i. The same holds for P_i, since the generic projector is a polynomial in B_i. Define G_i=delta_s^(i-1) G_A delta^(-(i-1)), D_i=G_A^(-1)G_i in C_(W_M)^times. (5.3) The genuine local meridian source formula at the first pair gives G_i^(-1)B_i(qM)G_i=L_i^+, G_A^(-1)B_i(qM)G_A=D_i L_i^+ D_i^(-1). (5.4) These are compatible meridian charts for every generator. Their transitions G_i^(-1)G_j=D_i^(-1)D_j lie in the actual centralizer and satisfy the strict cocycle identity. They need not be scalar. For any braid word beta=product_k B_(i_k)^(s_k), the whole identity is G_A^(-1)B_beta(qM)G_A =product_k D_(i_k)L_(i_k)^(s_k)D_(i_k)^(-1), (5.5) where L^(-1) means the displayed L^- and all intermediate D_(i_k)^(-1)D_(i_(k+1)) remain. Cyclicity removes a common outer conjugation, not the interior transitions of this product. The full period N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M), with the original zero-framing normalization and writhe w, therefore has the exact expression N_N(qM)=theta_(qx)^(-w) mathfrak_t_(W_M) (product_k D_(i_k)L_(i_k)^(s_k)D_(i_k)^(-1)). (5.6) Its peripheral gauge is exactly d_N(qM)/d_N(M)=-(qM-q^(-1)M^(-1))/(M-M^(-1)). (5.7) Thus the actual cut is now transported through this entire generic meridian atlas. This constructs a global matrix expression with the local source factors; it does not yet identify an all-level quantum-A source extension with the geometric gluing source. ## 6. Stabilization and singular fibers Every knot admits an even-strand braid presentation: if necessary make one ordinary stabilization. Direct right closing of the actual last crossing gives theta_x^(+/-1)I. Its new writhe factor cancels it exactly. This is a local matrix identity of the fixed enhanced crossing, so the selected zero-framed period is unchanged, including at the Kashaev color. No growing number of stabilizations is needed. Equations (1.5) and (5.6) are equalities of rational functions of M. They therefore remain equalities of whole meromorphic germs at M=1. The original d_N(M) is regular there. At shifted colors such as qM, d_N(qM) can have a pole; its full principal part is retained. For the reduced period the inverse of (5.7) can have a zero that cancels a pole in the pulled cut. These factors must be combined before evaluation. Wherever the prescribed period is regular, its whole-germ value is preserved. Individual fusion frames, meridian G_i and transition D_i generally have poles at the complete color. The meromorphic identity does not prove G_i Lambda_K=Lambda_T for the retained integral source lattices, or identify their nonreduced normal fibers. Those are additional parts of the triangulation/source comparison. ### The first meridian wall is an elementary integral modification There is a more precise local integral statement. Retain R=C[[u]], M=exp(u), A=A_R from Section 3, and put E=E_(N-1). Let c_last(M) be the last Casimir branch. Only c_0 collides with it at M=1, and their difference has a simple zero. Hence A^+=A[E]=A+R E, A^+/A=R/(u). (6.1) Indeed, write P=(z-c_last)P_rest. The resultant P_rest(c_last) has valuation one. The elementary polynomial Chinese-remainder sequence identifies A with the congruent pairs inside R times R[z]/P_rest, with cokernel R/(P_rest(c_last)). Adjoining E=(1,0) gives this full product. This is the partial normalization of the colliding c_0,c_last pair; it leaves every other local factor unchanged. Since E f=f(c_last)E, it is also exactly the displayed rank-one lattice enlargement. This enlargement is forced by the actual shifted crossing. On W_(qM)=V_(-M) tensor V_(-M), let iota_s send z to its actual total Casimir Omega_s. The local meridian equation is B_s=a r(Y,Omega_s)+c iota_s(E), a=-M^(-2), c=1+U^(-1). (6.2) The source polynomial r(Y,z) is regular at M=1 by its confluent interpolation proof. Both a and c are units in R, with c(1)=2. Since B_s and Omega_s have integral matrices, (6.2) proves that iota_s(E) is integral as well. In particular the actual order generated by the shifted crossing and Casimir is exactly R[Omega_s,B_s]=iota_s(A^+). (6.3) This is a statement about the algebra generated by these actual operators; it does not assert it is the entire shifted centralizer. The regular complete-color projector is explicitly E_s(0)=(B_s(0)+r_N(Omega_s(0)))/2, (6.4) where r_N is the already proved complete source crossing polynomial. It is an idempotent of rank N: idempotence and its constant ordinary trace N hold generically, hence extend on its integral matrix lattice. The exact source pole and its cut are [u E]_(u=0)=J_N/(4rho), [u Phi_M(E)]_(u=0)=(-1)^N rho/4. (6.5) Here Phi_M is the original scalar pivotal cut and J_N is the nonzero rank-one source Casimir nilpotent from the [meridian source proof](meridian_casimir_source.md). These coefficients include the actual cup/cap normalization. Because E_s is regular, (6.5) also proves J_N(Omega_s(0))=0. The nilpotent source is nonzero on the Kashaev module and vanishes on the shifted module; the generic comparison cannot extend as an invertible integral matrix at this wall. The dual lattice is equally explicit. Using the perfect source pairing of Section 3, (A^+)^vee={a in A:Phi_M(a E) in R} ={a in A:a(c_last) in uR} =(u,z-c_last)A. (6.6) Its quotient in A has length one. The equivalence follows from aE=a(c_last)E and the nonzero simple pole (6.5). Thus both sides of the source/cut modification are fixed; there is no choice of an arbitrary dual scalar. This same ideal is the conductor {a in A:a A^+ subset A}: it is exactly the condition that a(c_last)E return to A. Thus the dual cut lattice is the conductor of this partial normalization. This supplies a concrete normalization-and-residue description of the meridian source wall. Finally the actual dimension gauge gives on this same algebra Phi_(qM) o iota_s=-f(M)/f(qM) Phi_M, f(M)=M-M^(-1). Since this ratio is -2u/rho+O(u^2), (6.5) yields the finite value Phi_(qM)(E_s)|_(M=1)=(-1)^(N+1)/2. (6.7) This evaluates the whole regular shifted projector, rather than replacing c by 2 in a polar source expression. Equations (6.1)--(6.7) supply an actual meridian-induced integral source enlargement and its dual cut. Their global counterpart on an ideal triangulation is still to be constructed. ## 7. Consequence for the geometric triangulation program The [ideal triangulation input](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md) provides beta_T and its marked regulator. The [classical crossing comparison](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) already identifies the complete rational Bloch class. This note adds an intrinsic selected quantum cut and an explicit meridian centralizer atlas; fusion-basis changes create no additional unfixed scalar in that cut. The remaining geometric comparison must construct the relevant relative tensor presentation and its source lattice, identify its selected section, and control the period norm across levels. The rank-N quotient (4.2) is a trace quotient of an actual tensor centralizer; its dimension alone does not identify it with the rank-N geometric quantum boundary module or match central curves. The [threaded-observable obstruction](ado_threaded_shadow.md) to a literal fixed-hyperbolic-root-character identification still applies. No general hyperbolic or alternating volume conjecture follows here. ## 8. Coverage and exact diagnostics The coverage check is the abstract of [Geer--Patureau-Mirand--Turaev, 0711.4229](https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.4229): modified dimensions and renormalized nilpotent sl2 link invariants, including Kashaev invariants, are established literature subjects. No result or proof of that paper is a premise of the moment and fusion-matrix-unit arguments above. This note independently fixes the relevant formula in the exact conventions and source comparison used here; it makes no novelty claim for modified traces. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_intrinsic_cut_transport.py) checks 16 two-color cases at N=2,3,4,5,6,9,12,15, including all lower Casimir moments, their full top constant, every projector weight, and the inverse pivot in the left closure. Twenty tensor cases, with identical and heterogeneous colors and up to six strands, test all 8,700 centralizer matrix units against the actual cut density, including every off-diagonal unit. At the same eight levels, direct complete-color Casimir moments also give the nonzero Gram determinant (3.4) and the exact full-state residue constant c_N, without diagonalizing a colliding spectral frame or dividing a zero quantum dimension. Eight further shifted-color cases check (6.4)--(6.7): the regular projector is an actual E,F,K intertwiner of rank N, its cut is the full signed half, its source pole coefficient is as printed, and the rank-one source nilpotent becomes zero on the shifted module. Both signs of the actual stabilization closure are checked at the complete color as well. On four strands at N=2,3,4 the paired map (5.1) alone fails the middle-generator affine formula: the exact defects have full matrix ranks 16,81,256 respectively. The conjugated charts (5.3) satisfy the local formulas, intertwine all total E,F,K, and their transitions commute with these operators. Nine stabilized whole knot words verify (5.5)--(5.7) with the original cut, dimension and zero-framing factors; nine direct ideal-color evaluations verify stabilization without singular fusion frames. The diagnostics support the uniform proofs and do not substitute for them. [Results](../experiments/intrinsic_cut_transport_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_intrinsic_cut_transport.py

title: An intrinsic norm torsor from the quantum A-module
text: # An intrinsic norm torsor from the quantum A-module Research note, 25 October 2026. The target is Kashaev's original invariant. The noncommutative A-polynomial defined through recursions is a literature object: see Garoufalidis, [math/0306230](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306230). The construction below starts with a specified operator, without choosing a new ordering of a classical polynomial. It applies to any finite-order q-difference module and uses no triangulation or FAMED condition. This is algebraic structure and an independently proved comparison criterion, not a proof of the volume conjecture. A prescribed Kashaev solution or period pairing is additional data. The current [A-polynomial torsor formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md) puts these algebraic results alongside the regulator period, including its explicit rank-three algebraic connection, and distinguishes the norm-one torus from the scalar intertwiner torsor. It records the unproved classical-curve and selected-period comparison. For the actual knot state, the subsequent [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) applies this construction with Y=M^2 and cyclic degree N at q=exp(pi*i/N), retaining the full state's even-level sign. The [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) then supplies the exact complete scalar Tr(Y F_N)/N at Y^N=1 and a positive trace norm. The ordinary-color contribution is polynomially bounded, so these give equivalent volume targets for hyperbolic knots. Their norm comparison with the marked regulator remains unproved. The later [peripheral normal-period theorem](peripheral_normal_period.md) also identifies an integral datum invisible in this localization. Positive volume growth requires every polynomial annihilator to annihilate the complete-color delta module R/R*(Y-1). That module vanishes over C(q,Y), while its selected normal extension records the full ADO value. The theorem gives an exact derivative and inverse-matrix presentation under its explicit rank or Weyl-sector hypotheses. No general hyperbolic-knot rank or norm theorem is inferred. When its stated quantum reciprocity holds, central reflection supplies a further quadratic Hilbert-90 frame: g=(1+gamma(U))/2 for gamma(U)gamma(U^(-1))=1 and gamma(1)=1. The frame preserves the marked normal period. The ambient signed dihedral relation retains kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1); it does not assert T-stability of the scalar solution line or establish the regulator norm. The [actual Weyl-descent theorem](actual_weyl_descent.md) now proves the reflection of the literature knot state and forces a unitary monomial reciprocity for its primitive minimal normal operator. Thus its equivariant structure is not inferred from the classical A-curve. Primitive generator units preserve the selected normal metric period. The relevant root-fiber injectivity and regulator norm remain to establish. ## 1. The central curve of an actual root-of-unity module Let q=zeta be a primitive n-th root of unity. Let E=C(x), sigma(x)=zeta*x, F=E^sigma=C(u), u=x^n. Assume that specializing the specified operator is defined and its leading and trailing coefficients are nonzero in E: Ahat=sum_(j=0)^r a_j(x) T^j, T f=sigma(f) T. Its cyclic module has E-basis e,T e,...,T^(r-1)e. The relation Ahat e=0 specifies an invertible companion matrix C(x), with T=C sigma, H=T^n=C sigma(C)...sigma^(n-1)(C). The state is a solution pairing with this module; it is not identified with an arbitrary choice of its column basis. **Central-curve lemma.** D_n(u,v)=det(v I-H(x)) belongs to F[v]. Indeed sigma(H)=C^(-1) H C, so all characteristic coefficients are sigma-invariant. This proof works at composite as well as prime n. It retains all coefficients before any specialization u=1. D_n is determined by the root-of-unity module. Equality of its relevant component with a component of the classical A-polynomial is an extra compatibility statement. Neither a classical symbol at q=1 nor the existence of a quantization establishes that equality. ## 2. A simple component carries a canonical cyclic norm equation Take a component of D_n=0 on which v is a simple eigenvalue, and let k be its function field. The algebra S=k[x]/(x^n-u) is a degree-n finite etale k-algebra. It may be a product of fields; the argument does not assume that this Kummer algebra is connected. Sigma acts on it, and S^sigma=k. The eigenmodule L=ker(H-v I) in S^r has rank one over S. T preserves it because T commutes with T^n. Choose a basis e_L and write T e_L=a e_L, a in S^*. Iteration gives the exact equation N_(S/k)(a)=product_(j=0)^(n-1) sigma^j(a)=v. (2.1) Changing the basis to f e_L changes a to a sigma(f)/f. Thus the generic scalar problem is a cyclic norm torsor on the central curve of the actual operator, rather than on a chosen shape chart. As a k-vector space L has dimension n. Multiplication by x and the semilinear operator T give T x=zeta x T, x^n=u, T^n=v. This is a splitting module of the corresponding central quantum torus. Its endomorphisms commuting with x are S-linear scalars; commuting also with T restricts them to k. Simplicity follows after a separable base change: x has n distinct eigenlines and T cyclically permutes them, so there is no proper nonzero invariant subspace. ## 3. Hilbert 90 gives the comparison torsor explicitly Two scalar realizations a,b with the same norm v have ratio r=a/b of norm one. Define r_0=1, r_j=product_(i=0)^(j-1) sigma^i(r), f(c)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) r_j sigma^j(c). The norm-one equation implies r sigma(f(c))=f(c). Some c makes f(c) invertible. One elementary justification works also for an etale product: after a separable closure sigma cyclically permutes n coordinates; each coordinate of f(c) is a nonzero linear form. Their product is a nonzero polynomial. Since k is infinite, there is a k-rational c outside its zero set. Hence r=f/sigma(f). A scalar intertwiner between the two modules exists, and any two nonzero intertwiners differ by k^*. This identifies the generic intertwiner torsor as G_m. Globally, local intertwiners give a line bundle on the common regular locus; generic Hilbert 90 does not automatically trivialize that line bundle. Alternatively adjoin lambda with lambda^n=v. Then lambda^(-1)T has n-th power one, and the same calculation descends its invariant rank-one line. This is the peripheral-root realization of the torsor. Consequently, once two specified constructions have the same simple central component, their unpointed module comparison reduces to a scalar period line. Identifying their distinguished vectors, cycles and level-dependent scalar remains necessary. The [root-orbit pointing theorem](root_orbit_pointing.md) now gives an exact way to fix that central scalar on the relevant fiber. The actual reduced state has value one at M=-q, in the same root orbit as M=1. A comparison within the same rational solution line that preserves this anchor has central factor one at M^(2N)=1. For the full state one uses the specified nonzero central residue. The theorem also reconstructs the fiber period by maximal minors of the root operator matrix when its rational kernel has rank one. This does not establish the required kernel rank or the geometric period comparison for the full knot class. The subsequent [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) uses polynomial coherence of the actual integer-color traces to give an exact period formula without that rank condition. It needs only a fixed initial color window and bounded-order q-jets, whose initial values stay bounded near q=1. Its [meridian counterpart](bounded_meridian_jets.md) bounds the integral kernel's Smith exponents by the fixed leading M-span. This supplies finite pointing, not the remaining geometric norm comparison. The [affine source extension](affine_quantum_a_period.md) retains additional information when the actual homogeneous operator has the stated inhomogeneous source factor. Its root period is a cyclic affine fixed point; in the nonresonant case it is an exact resolvent. The generic source class is not killed by finite stable algebraic covers, by normalized trace. The [adequacy proof](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) excludes a fixed algebraic meridian trace for all nontrivial adequate knots. Under either stated source nonresonance test this forces the affine class to be nonsplit. Its identification with the marked regulator and its norm remains separate from multiplicative Hilbert 90 at any single root level. The [formal classical-curve construction](formal_a_curve_period_torsor.md) gives a different, complementary branch construction directly at q=1. Its Hensel lift and formal connection do not assume that D_n equals the classical A-polynomial. They still require the geometric component to occur in the actual operator's classical symbol and do not select the actual knot period from its formal branch alone. ### 3.1 Extending through coalescing eigenvalues and apparent poles Normalize the chosen central curve. Work where u and v are units, so the x-root cover Y remains finite etale. The generic rank-one eigenline can be extended as a fractional line lattice Lambda_0 on Y. Define Lambda_cyc=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) T^j Lambda_0. (3.1) **Extension lemma.** Lambda_cyc is an invertible fractional line sheaf, T Lambda_cyc=Lambda_cyc, and it is the smallest T-stable lattice containing Lambda_0. Proof: the sum is coherent and torsion-free of rank one; on a smooth curve this is invertible. The identity T^n=v and the fact that v is a unit give T Lambda_cyc=Lambda_cyc. Minimality follows by applying each T^j to the inclusion of Lambda_0. No regularity of the original companion matrix at the point is needed on this generic eigenline. After adjoining lambda^n=v, the invariant lattice for lambda^(-1)T descends to a line bundle on the peripheral-root base. This handles apparent poles or eigenvalue coalescence in the matrix presentation. It does not equate the limiting eigenline with the entire kernel of the specialized matrix, which can be larger. It also does not assign a value to a meromorphic period without its pointing. Different initial lattices can retain different divisor data. A useful exact model is T e=((x-1)/(zeta*x-1)) e, T^n=1. Its coefficient has a zero and pole above u=1. Put P_n(x)=(x^n-1)/(x-1)=1+x+...+x^(n-1). Starting from O_Y e, (3.1) gives O_Y e/P_n(x): at each root of unity other than x=1 some summand has a simple pole, while at x=1 the summand j=0 remains a unit. In the extended frame e'=e/P_n, T e'=e', e' at x=1 equals e/n. (3.2) Thus the pole is removed by an actual lattice change, and the exact specialization retains a factor n. Its exponential rate is zero. This is a uniform algebraic example of why peripheral multipliers and the integral period lattice must be tracked together. ### 3.2 Retain the full spectral algebra at a multiple root Extending one generic eigenline does not recover the whole generalized eigenspace or the operators acting on it. The [Casimir/recoupling calculation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) now gives an explicit instance relevant to the actual Kashaev crossing: its cyclic spectral algebra is C[z]/(T_N(z)+2), with double roots. The crossing and pivotal trace both use first derivatives at those roots. Its vacuum lies in the socle of a double point and does not by itself fix a module frame there. When a generalized spectral module is rank one over its finite spectral algebra A, its frame comparison is an A^*-torsor. Section 7 of that note extends Hilbert 90 to characteristic-zero Artin bases by a finite nilpotent logarithm and an explicit additive telescoping formula. This retains the jets. The rank-one-over-A hypothesis is proved there by cyclicity of the relative Casimir; it is not assumed for every specialized quantum A-module. The simple-component argument above remains valid on its stated locus. ## 4. A uniform exact check on the central-curve condition For the companion family C(x)=[[0,-1],[1,c-x]], put s_0(c)=2, s_1(c)=c, s_(j+1)=c s_j-s_(j-1). Then at every primitive level n, D_n(u,v)=v^2-(s_n(c)-u)v+1. (4.1) Here is a direct proof. The determinant of H is one. Its trace is sigma-invariant and is a polynomial in x of degree at most n, so only the constant and x^n terms survive. The constant is tr(C(0)^n)=s_n(c). The top coefficient is (-1)^n zeta^(n(n-1)/2)=-1. This proves (4.1) uniformly. For c=1, s_n(c)=2 cos(n*pi/3). Thus constants can retain a periodic level dependence even when the input coefficients are integral. This is an abstract module calculation, not a counterexample about a knot invariant. It shows what must actually be checked in any claimed quantum-Frobenius compatibility. The exact audit in `experiments/audit_intrinsic_norm_torsor.py` checks the central curve, eigenline norm, and Hilbert-90 formula at composite levels as well as prime levels. It does not assume equality with a classical knot A-polynomial. ## 5. Which normalization factors affect the volume rate Let c(q) be a fixed nonzero meromorphic germ at q=1. Along q_n=exp(2*pi*i/n), log|c(q_n)|=O(log n), provided the specialized factor is defined and nonzero. This follows by writing c(q)=(q-1)^j g(q), g(1)!=0. The same conclusion holds for a fixed algebraic Puiseux germ, with rational j. Multiplication by such a factor preserves the exponential volume rate. A regular nonzero factor 1+x^n=1+u at u=1 is harmless for that rate, although its exact value remains part of the state comparison. Finite-level Hilbert 90 by itself gives no uniform-in-n bound on its remaining k^* scalar. For instance, (u/2)^n is a central algebraic unit at each level, equals one at u=2, and equals 2^(-n) at u=1. This preserves an unpointed module while changing a chosen scalar period's exponential size. It demonstrates insufficient reconstruction data, not freedom to renormalize the already defined Kashaev invariant. Thus one needs level-compatible pointing and regulator normalization of this intrinsic period line. The all-level theorem linked above now specifies the quantum period by finite pointing once an actual operator is given; its regulator comparison remains missing. A fixed algebraic generic-q comparison could be sufficient for the rate; arbitrary unrelated finite-level gauges are not. The subsequent [central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) allows a fixed finite algebraic comparison depending also on the central variable z=M^(kN), evaluated as a whole germ. Its value is between fixed powers of N. This covers the exact ADO normalization and retains factors such as 1+M^N. The levelwise unit (u/2)^n above has no such fixed finite algebraic presentation across levels. The subsequent [local normalization tower](cyclotomic_normalization_tower.md) proves distribution between arbitrary levels and its regulator estimate directly from finite products and an exact convergent series. The [regular cyclic/Steinberg family](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) extends the selected local vacuum and gives explicit recoupling lattices at degeneration. These supply local comparison data; neither establishes the global period identification required in Section 7. ## 6. The classical A-curve and finite-cover descent Fix the peripheral monomials m,l in the unhalved conventions of the Bloch-period note. Put omega=-(1/2)(log|m| dArg(l)-log|l| dArg(m)). The previously proved identity delta(beta)=-(1/2)m wedge l gives dD(beta)=omega on an augmented character chart. This is the general exactness property of the A-curve, with its peripheral conventions retained. Exact polynomials and their volume functions are existing literature definitions; see Guilloux--Marche, [1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395). No novelty is claimed for exactness or for conjugation normalization. Here is a useful direct descent argument. Suppose p:Y->C is a connected finite cover of smooth curves, and a single-valued real function V on Y satisfies dV=p^*omega. Remove the finitely many branch values and set V_C(c)=(1/degree(p)) sum_(y over c) V(y). Then dV_C=omega. The function V-p^*V_C is locally constant on the connected punctured curve Y, so constant; its fiber average is zero, so it is zero. Thus V descends exactly. Continuous extensions at removed points agree wherever they exist. In particular, a finite peripheral cover does not prevent descent of the real regulator norm. If C is preserved by complex conjugation iota, then iota^*omega=-omega. Any primitive V_0 gives a unique conjugation-odd primitive V_odd=(V_0-V_0 composed with iota)/2. Uniqueness follows since two primitives differ by a constant, which cannot be odd. When the chosen representation component and its volume are conjugation-compatible, this fixes the real normalization. That compatibility is not assumed for every component; the marked Bloch lift retains the normalization in the general case. The subsequent [Regge/cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) distinguishes this parameter-cover descent from a manifold cover. The latter changes peripheral variables by an integer monomial map, sends the geometric A-factor by elimination and multiplies the marked regulator by the topological cover degree. Its quantum boundary inclusion changes the commutation parameter by the boundary degree. For the unordered ideal-shape parameter space, the finite Regge action also needs its orientation local system: an untwisted norm over its six orderings cancels the Bloch volume. That is a failure to descend the same differential form, rather than an exception to the descent argument above. ## 7. The general target after the geometric audit The audited geometric existence input supplies a positive fundamental- class representative for every hyperbolic knot. On the classical side the existing Bloch-period notes give the marked regulator line and log||P_hyp||=2 Vol(M)/pi. For the original Kashaev invariant, the required comparison is (4/n) log|<K>_n| - log||P_hyp|| -> 0. (7.1) The sign and scale differ from the later AK state comparison. Equation (7.1) is still unproved. Sections 1--3 identify the intrinsic algebraic comparison torsor. The subsequent [Kashaev/ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) supplies the actual normalization line and its specialization at the Kashaev point. It also proves that rational root-level states lie in a central v=1 sector. That sector need not be the geometric component of the classical q->1 A-curve. The required comparison must retain the original quantum family and its selected period, rather than assume these two curves coincide. Compatibility with the marked geometric regulator and the norm statement (7.1) remain unproved. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre theorem](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) specifies the branch-point lattice for the actual normal ADO state. Its invariant lattice retains the first negative-sector coefficient as an ordinary fibre coordinate, and its full complete period is the exact functional (eta_N/2)e_0^*b_0. Under generic rank one the saturated kernel gives a pointed line even at a special rank jump. An equivariant change of frame may fix the ordinary root fibre and still change this coordinate, so a comparison must transport the marked ramified fibre and functional. No equality of central spectra or regulator norms is deduced from that construction. The subsequent [actual threaded-character theorem](ado_threaded_shadow.md) proves an additional distinction: the selected ADO evaluation has abelian even-threaded interior data, whereas a null-homologous loop separates the fixed complete hyperbolic character. Hilbert-90 frame descent cannot identify eigenlines with those different scalar data. A source extension can instead select a horizontal source-one eigenvector of a separating observable. Its actual relative realization and norm comparison remain unproved.

title: Irreducible critical sources force nonzero conjugate coefficients
Independent audit of the irregular Rees cyclic bridge
text: # Independent audit of the irregular Rees cyclic bridge Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md) is sound. I checked its operator order, wrap sign, centers, Casimir, dense-chart coverage, transformed source and pivot. No test rerun was needed. The Green moment/source formulas audited in section 5 below are consistent with it. ## 1. The genuine block operators and the regularized wraps On \(u^r/r!\), the wrap \[ B(MD_{Z^{-1}}-M^{-1}) \] has coefficient \(MZ^{-r}-M^{-1}\) into block \(r-1\). Reversing the displayed order would change that coefficient. Similarly \[ T\frac{1-Z^{L+1}}{L+1} \] has the required coefficient \(1-Z^{r+1}\) into block \(r+1\). The integral expression in the proof is exactly the same operator, not a convergence approximation. For \(d=N(Z-1)\), the scalar conjugation gives \[ G^{-1}D_ZG=e^{u/N}D_Z,\quad G^{-1}D_{Z^{-1}}G=e^{-u/(NZ)}D_{Z^{-1}},\quad G^{-1}BG=B+1/d. \] The head factors \(\eta^j\), followed by the Hopf scaling, cancel on the nonwrap entries. They give \(d\) on the \(E\)-wrap and \(d^{-1}\) on the \(F\)-wrap. Consequently the \(E\)-wrap is exactly \[ (1+d\partial_u) [Me^{-u/(NZ)}D_{Z^{-1}}-M^{-1}], \] with that order. In the \(F\)-wrap, \(x=1+(Z-1)t\) reverses the original integral endpoints and gives the negative sign \[ -\frac uN\int_0^1 e^{tu/N}f((1+(Z-1)t)u)\,dt. \] Both are regular coefficientwise. Its root value is \(1-y\), \(y=e^{u/N}\), including the regular value at \(u=0\). The completion convention is appropriate: \(G\) belongs to the \(u\)-adic completion with Laurent \(\eta\)-coefficients, not to a ring requiring one pole bound for its entire series. The regular operator lattice and the irregular selected source are therefore genuinely different objects. ## 2. Exact root centers, Casimir, and coverage Multiplying the \(N\) cyclic arrows gives \[ K^N=\gamma M^N/U,\quad \mathcal E^N=\gamma(M^N/U-M^{-N}),\quad F^N=1-U,\qquad \gamma=(-1)^{N+1}. \] Their product is precisely \[ ef=k+k^{-1}-\gamma(M^N+M^{-N}). \] Adjacent products, or the unchanged generic Casimir, give \(F\mathcal E+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}=-M-M^{-1}\). All signs agree with these formulas. For \(U\ne1\), the cyclic \(F\)-arrows are units; distinct clock projectors and those arrows generate every matrix unit. Given \(k_t,e_t,f_t\ne0\) satisfying the central equation, the displayed \(U=\gamma M^N/k_t\) fixes \(k\). The unscaled \(e_0,f_0\) satisfy \(e_0f_0=e_tf_t\), so both are nonzero. The root \(\lambda^N=e_t/e_0\) fixes \(e\), and its inverse scaling fixes \(f\) automatically. This proves dense full fixed-Casimir module coverage on the stated cover, not coverage of a selected knot source. At \(U=1\) and generic \(M\), the wrap is \(\kappa\): this is the E-semicyclic fiber \(s=1\), rather than the nilpotent head \(s=0\). They coincide at \(M=1\). This distinction is essential and is retained. ## 3. The original source and its ramified flags Since \(\pi_0G=\pi_0\), transforming the actual source pair gives \[ \psi_{\mathrm{new}}=D_{\mathrm{head}}e^{-u/d}\psi,\qquad \phi_{\mathrm{new}}=\phi D_{\mathrm{head}}^{-1}\pi_0. \] Their pairing is one. The corresponding coupon has entries \(\eta^{i-j}e^{-u/d}/N\) followed by evaluation at zero. Its \(u^h\) term has worst pole \(\eta^{-Nh-(N-1)}\), exactly the stated bound. It remains idempotent, but is not a regular source on the limiting lattice. The coefficientwise head projector commutes with the scalar exponential; the finite vacuum coupon does not. The proof correctly preserves that distinction instead of inferring source regularity from unchanged vacuum normalization. ## 4. The literal pivot and the actual scope Conjugation preserves the literal identity \(g=K^{1-N}\). The regular root clock therefore selects \[ g_{\mathrm{lit}}=U g_{\mathrm{red}},\qquad g_{\mathrm{red}}=x^{1-N}A^{-1}. \] The paired inverse defect has the opposite \(U^{-1}\) factor. This agrees with the revised Mellin source adapters and does not identify their separate normal derivatives. The proof supplies a genuine full-cyclic module limit and an explicitly irregular marked source. It does not claim regularity of a conjugated \(R\)-network, survival of that source in the limit, or a geometric regulator norm. Those scope statements are mathematically necessary. ## 5. Additional check of the bounded Green moment/source formulas [green_moment_carry_filtration.md](green_moment_carry_filtration.md) also passes a direct formula check: - The Newton carry is \((I+L)\otimes C-I\); retaining \(C-I\) gives the stated triangular complex and power expansion. - The actual index operator is \(j+NTB\). Newton interpolation and \(\binom{TB}{m}e^{st}=(st)^me^{st}/m!\) give the exact bounded conversion, including the extra \(Nx\) in the image of the squared index. - Differentiating the relative source at \(u=0\) gives \(\partial_\sigma f_n-nf_{n-1}\), and its transgression has every stated binomial endpoint term. - The Leibniz formula gives the coefficient-normal rows (12) and (12a), with their factorials and powers of \(N\). A trivial coefficient monodromy does not kill these rows. - The whole-clock gauge and its powers have the displayed regular root values. Its finite row satisfies \(\Gamma G=\Gamma\), while its coupon is \(e^{-s_Qu}\Gamma\), whose normal commutator is exactly the two-term formula (17). Thus polynomial moment degree bounds the explicit triangular source construction, but does not remove coefficient carries, the irregular vacuum, or the two-wall excursion adapter. Neither note asserts the missing full Green boundary cancellation.

title: An irregular Rees bridge from the actual Verma source to full cyclic colors
text: # An irregular Rees bridge from the actual Verma source to full cyclic colors Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The genuine balanced infinite module admits an explicit irregular and ramified transformation whose operator coefficients extend regularly to the root. Its limit is a full cyclic root color, with both E and F central powers generically nonzero. After one root scaling it covers a dense chart of the fixed-Casimir root conjugacy class. The transformed source is specified as well. Its co-source vacuum is unchanged by the exponential gauge, but its source vacuum is irregular and its head lattice is ramified. Thus regularity of the module limit does not prove regularity or survival of the original selected period. ## 1. Exact block operators of the genuine common module Use the actual balanced infinite module from [the two-wall construction](common_verma_two_wall_source.md): K v_a=-(M/q)Q^(-a)v_a, Ecal v_a=(M Q^(-a)-M^(-1))v_(a-1), a>=1, Ecal v_0=0, F v_a=(1-Q^(a+1))v_(a+1), Q=q^2. Write a=rN+j, 0<=j<N, and identify v_(rN+j)=h_j u^r/r!, B=partial_u, T=u, L=T B, Z=Q^N, D_Z f(u)=f(Zu). These formulas are exact before specializing Q. The clock is Q^j D_Z, and K is -(M/q)Q^(-j)D_(Z^-1). For Ecal, the nonwrap and wrap entries, respectively, are E_j=M Q^(-j)D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1), 1<=j<N, E_0=B(M D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1)). (1.1) The first maps h_j to h_(j-1), the second h_0 to h_(N-1). For F the entries are F_j=1-Q^(j+1)D_Z, 0<=j<N-1, F_(N-1)=T (1-Z^(L+1))/(L+1) =u integral_Z^1 f(xu)dx on f. (1.2) For example (1.2) on u^r/r! has the required coefficient 1-Z^(r+1) into the next block. The apparent inverse L+1 is just division by the nonzero integer r+1 on that basis. ## 2. The exact irregular transformation and head gauge Put epsilon=Z-1, d=N epsilon, and choose the marked local ramification eta^N=d. Define G=exp(u/d), D_head h_j=eta^j h_j, C=D_head G^(-1). The exponential belongs to the u-adic completion with Laurent eta coefficients. Each u coefficient has a finite pole; there is no claim of a single uniform pole bound for the whole function. Conjugate first by G^(-1)(-)G, then by D_head(-)D_head^(-1), and apply the genuine Hopf scaling Ecal->eta Ecal,F->eta^(-1)F: Ehat=eta C Ecal C^(-1), Fhat=eta^(-1) C F C^(-1), Khat=C K C^(-1). (2.1) The direction of the head conjugation is essential. It cancels eta on every nonwrap E entry and contributes d on its wrap; it cancels eta^(-1) on every nonwrap F entry and contributes d^(-1) on its wrap. There is no unresolved irregular expansion in the transformed operators. Since G^(-1)D_ZG=exp(u/N)D_Z, G^(-1)D_(Z^-1)G=exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1), G^(-1)B G=B+1/d, the exact entries become Ehat_j=M Q^(-j)exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1), j>0, Ehat_0=(1+d partial_u) [M exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1)], Fhat_j=1-Q^(j+1)exp(u/N)D_Z, j<N-1, Fhat_(N-1) f =-(u/N) integral_0^1 exp(tu/N)f((1+epsilon t)u)dt, Khat_j=-(M/q)Q^(-j)exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1). (2.2) The F wrap formula follows by x=1+epsilon t in (1.2), retaining the reversed integration endpoints. Each coefficient of (2.2) is a regular formal series in epsilon,u. Integration is polynomial antiderivation coefficientwise, not a convergence assumption. The generic quantum-group relations hold because (2.1) is conjugation and Hopf scaling of a genuine module. Their regular specializations are therefore exact root identities. ## 3. The full cyclic root module and its central chart Fix q=q_N, Q=Q_N and put y=exp(u/N), U=y^N=exp(u), gamma=(-1)^(N+1). Taking the regular value of (2.2) gives K_j=-(M/q_N)y^(-1)Q_N^(-j), Ecal_j=M y^(-1)Q_N^(-j)-M^(-1), F_j=1-y Q_N^(j+1), (3.1) with j read modulo N, including both wraps. All entries act by multiplication. For F the wrap limit is -(u/N)integral_0^1 exp(tu/N)dt=1-y, including its regular u=0 value. The resulting entries are Laurent algebraic functions of M,y. Thus the module formulas extend from the marked formal y=1 neighborhood to y in G_m. This extends the module chart, not a selected irregular source or its global continuation data. Direct multiplication, or specialization of the regular relations, gives [Ecal,F]=rho_N(K-K^(-1)), F Ecal+q_N K+q_N^(-1)K^(-1)=-M-M^(-1). The exact central powers are k=K^N=gamma M^N/U, e=Ecal^N=gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N)), f=F^N=1-U. (3.2) Consequently e f=k+k^(-1)-gamma(M^N+M^(-N)). (3.3) For U!=1 the F arrows are all units. Clock projectors followed by their cyclic F arrows give every matrix unit, so this is a genuine split regular root color, rather than a Borel-only model. Apply the additional genuine root Hopf scaling Ecal->lambda Ecal,F->lambda^(-1)F. Given an admissible central triple (k_t,e_t,f_t) satisfying (3.3), with all entries nonzero, choose U=gamma M^N/k_t, lambda^N=e_t/[gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N))]. (3.4) The denominator is nonzero because its product with 1-U is e_t f_t. On the indicated N-th-root cover, (3.4) realizes e_t, and (3.3) forces the realized f to be f_t. Thus the family covers a dense full fixed-Casimir central chart. It is not restricted to the triangular source locus F^N=0. It does not itself prove that an actual knot's selected source reaches a chosen point of that chart. ## 4. The selected source is irregular and its lattice flags remain Let the original finite head source be i psi, with psi_j=1, and its co-source phi pi_0, phi_j=1/N. Its finite-rank coupon is Gamma=i e pi_0. Under the actual transformation C the exact source and co-source are psi_new=D_head exp(-u/d)psi, phi_new=phi D_head^(-1)pi_0, phi_new psi_new=1. (4.1) Here pi_0G=pi_0, but G does not preserve the source vacuum. In particular G^(-1)Gamma G=exp(-u/d)Gamma, not Gamma. The full transformed coupon has entry (Gamma_new)_(i,j) =eta^(i-j)exp(-u/d)/N times evaluation at u=0. (4.2) It is exactly idempotent by (4.1). On u jets of order at most h, its eta pole order is bounded by Nh+N-1, equivalently its d pole order by h+(N-1)/N. The head lattice has the explicit flags eta^j h_j, with the opposite dual flags eta^(-j)h_j^*. The normalized pairing does not make those flags or the essential source exp(-u/d) disappear. The coefficientwise head projector e tensor I is different: G commutes with it and only the ramified D_head changes it. It cannot be substituted for the original finite Gamma. The same issue occurs at every internal finite-head compression, not just at the final cut. For the whole-head projector P=i pi_0 (identity on H), one has exactly C P C^(-1)=exp(-u/d)P. (4.3) On b legs the scalar is exp(-(u_1+...+u_b)/d). The actual off-root finite word is the product with its intermediate head projectors retained. Each becomes this irregular source under the transformation. In particular the pre-gauge two-wall word correction delta*w*H_beta from the common-Verma note cannot be discarded after taking module Rees symbols: those source poles and normal co-sources can compensate its vanishing factors. Thus the module has a regular full-cyclic limit while the source is an explicitly recorded irregular section. Equality of finite pairings before degeneration does not provide a regular limiting selected period or a Stokes coefficient. ## 5. The literal pivot lift is selected, with its U adapter Conjugation preserves the identity g=K^(1-N). Since Khat has a regular root value, its literal power has that same regular limit: g_lit=K_U^(1-N)=U g_red, g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1), A=yQ_N^j, x=-M/q_N. Therefore this construction selects the literal whole-clock lift, not the reduced root representative. Their paired defects satisfy D_lit=U^(-1)D_red and both products give the same cut projector; their separate normal derivatives differ. The exact distinction is retained in [the Mellin comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), Section 2. The whole external modified-dimension line d_N(M), Cartan half-character, and zero-framing phases remain marked. ## 6. The actual cyclotomic-normal Poisson form There is a fixed-N normal Planck parameter already present in this construction: d=N(Q^N-1). The generic weight relations give [K^N,Ecal^N]=(Q^(N^2)-1)Ecal^N K^N, [K^N,F^N]=(Q^(-N^2)-1)F^N K^N. The two scalar ratios after division by d have root values +1 and -1. Thus the actual divided-commutator Poisson bracket on the root center satisfies {k,e}=ke, {k,f}=-kf. (6.1) It is independent of the choice of lifts: changing a lift by d times an operator adds a commutator with a central root element. The quantum Casimir is central before specialization. Its root Chebyshev relation (3.3), on a fixed-M leaf, consequently forces {e,f}=k^(-1)-k. (6.2) This follows first where e!=0 by bracketing (3.3) with e, then extends as the polynomial bracket identity. The Casimir relation is not being declared central merely because it vanishes in one representation; it is the specialization of the actual universal central Casimir. Vary the actual irregular phase to G_p=exp(pu/d), with p!=0. The Rees momentum is Pi=d partial_u, so [Pi,u]=d and G_p^(-1)Pi G_p=Pi+p. This fixes {p,u}=1. In (2.2) replace u/N in the exponent by pu/N and (1+d partial_u) on the E wrap by (p+d partial_u). The F wrap limit is (1-y)/p, y=exp(pu/N). Other entries remain the corresponding nonwrap entries. Hence its central functions are exactly U=exp(up), k=gamma M^N/U, e=p gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N)), f=(1-U)/p. (6.3) Direct differentiation with {p,u}=1 gives (6.1)--(6.2). The exact source symplectic form is Omega=du wedge dp=dlog U wedge dlog p =-dlog k wedge dlog e, (6.4) holding M fixed. The last equality follows from e=p(k-gamma M^(-N)). This is precisely the fixed-meridian Gauss leaf form used in the actual holonomy/moment-map proof, not just an unrelated symplectic parameterization. To match its usual balanced center coordinates set e_G=e/rho_N^N, f_G=-rho_N^N f. Then G=[k e_G;k f_G k^(-1)+e_G f_G] has trace gamma(M^N+M^(-N)); the physical gamma*G has trace M^N+M^(-N). Constant root scalings do not change (6.4). Varying M requires its peripheral boundary terms and is not part of this fixed-leaf identity. ## 7. A regular chart at the parabolic source boundary At M=1 set v=1/p and w=e/gamma. The same central chart is U=(1+wv)^(-1), k=gamma(1+wv), e=gamma w, f=w v^2/(1+wv), Omega=dw wedge dv/(1+wv). (7.1) These are algebraic identities. The form is regular and nonzero at v=0, including w=0. The locus w=0 maps to the identity central point; its v coordinate retains the exceptional direction. Thus (7.1) is a regular resolving chart at that collapsed point, not a claim of a complete global resolution without its other chart. The module entries also extend across v=0 on the marked y cover. Here y=(1+wv)^(-1/N), and its E wrap is [(1+wv)^(1/N)-1]/v -> w/N, while its F wrap is v[1-(1+wv)^(-1/N)] ->0. The nonwrap entries tend to the actual head values. Consequently the v=0 module is exactly the previously constructed E-semicyclic source with mu=w/N, and w=0 is the actual complete head. This is a concrete source boundary of the full conjugacy-class chart. It does not prove that the selected knot period reaches a chosen geometric point in that chart. ## 8. What has and has not been bridged The full cyclic module is obtained from the genuine actual Verma module by an explicit irregular Rees transformation. This supplies a module-level route from the original head lattice to dense root color charts with both central powers nonzero. Its construction does not assume that a generic typical finite head extends to a Lusztig module, nor identify the two regular wall normals. At U=1 its generic-M value is the E-semicyclic s=1 fiber, with wrap coefficient kappa=M-M^(-1), rather than the nilpotent s=0 head. They coincide at M=1. The previously proved whole E-semicyclic cut independence is relevant, but is a separate word/source comparison and is not a consequence of this module specialization. No regular limit of the transformed source has been asserted. The generator module limit alone also does not prove that a whole conjugated R network has a regular scalar limit with this selected source. The remaining tasks include its ramified flags, irregular source class, physical phase adapters, and actual geometric/cut comparison. No global regulator period or volume limit follows from the central-chart coverage alone. The parameter d is a local root normal for fixed N, not the physical large-N parameter H_N=2pi*i/N. If H=Log Q on the marked root sheet, then d=N^2(H-H_N)+higher order. The actual finite auxiliary state is regular at that fixed root. A nonzero polar geometric phase exp(S/d) is therefore not automatically its selected phase: polar pieces in a full source-preserving contraction must be accounted for or canceled. The root regular part can still have N-dependent growth. The exact module and Poisson maps above do not settle that separate norm problem. The uncompressed universal Verma braid has its own already proved root Alexander-normalized period in [the earlier Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md). It is not identified with the compressed selected period by dropping the projectors (4.3); their full normal adapter remains necessary. [Exact module and source audit](../experiments/audit_irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.py). [Results](../experiments/irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module_results.json).

title: A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed
text: # A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed Research note, 25 October 2026. The preceding [crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) independently identifies the normalized enhanced Kashaev period with the reduced highest-weight quantum-group period. Here we give its meridian family, its exact normalization lattice, and its implications for the norm torsor. Definitions are the unrolled quantum-group R, pivotal and modified-dimension formulas in Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, [2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176), Section 2. Their holonomicity and recursion-ideal comparison theorems are not assumed. The calculations below use the displayed definitions directly. ## 1. The zero-framed reduced family is rational in its color Fix r>=2, q=exp(pi*i/r), and x=q^alpha. On V_alpha use H v_j=(alpha-2j)v_j, K v_j=x q^(-2j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_q[alpha-j+1]_q v_(j-1), F v_j=v_(j+1), 0<=j<r. Use the finite universal R from the preceding note with k<r, pivotal matrix K^(1-r), and twist theta_alpha=q^((alpha^2+2(1-r)alpha)/2). Let F_r(alpha) be the reduced (1,1)-tangle scalar for a zero-framed knot, with unknot value one. It is the usual modified-trace ADO invariant divided by the modified dimension, not a new local weight. **Rationality lemma.** F_r(alpha) is a Laurent polynomial in x with complex coefficients at fixed q. Proof: remove the common factor q^(alpha^2/2) from each positive R and its inverse from each negative R. The remaining entries are Laurent polynomials in x, since q^((alpha-2c)(alpha-2d)/2) =q^(alpha^2/2) x^(-c-d) q^(2cd), [alpha-j+1]_q =(x q^(-j+1)-x^(-1)q^(j-1))/(q-q^(-1)). All denominators [k]_q!, k<r, are nonzero constants. For a braid word of writhe w, the total removed factor is q^(w alpha^2/2). It cancels with theta_alpha^(-w); the remainder is x^(-w(1-r)). The pivotal entries are also Laurent monomials in x. Finite products, sums and partial traces prove the assertion. Scalarity on generic typical colors and the resulting identity extend through the finite exceptional set. In particular F_r(alpha+2r)=F_r(alpha). This has a direct algebraic proof from the defining matrices; it is not a consequence imported from a holonomicity theorem. ## 2. Exact specialization to the original Kashaev period At alpha=r-1 the matrices are the r-dimensional highest-weight matrices of the crossing note. The two pivotal conventions differ by K^(1-r)=(-1)^(r-1) K. The corresponding twists differ by the same sign. For a b-strand braid closing to a knot, w has parity b-1. Hence the resulting factor (-1)^((r-1)(b-1-w)) is one. The dual convention in the crossing note is equivalent to the original highest-weight color: an explicit intertwiner with its dual is B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-r)) v_(r-1-j). For example, with Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, the antipodes are S(E)=-E K^(-1) and S(F)=-K F. Direct substitution verifies B on E,F,K. The same substitution in the finite R gives R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Consequently the already specified enhanced period satisfies F_r(r-1)=<K>_r. (2.1) This is a uniform matrix and pairing comparison for knots, with the zero framing and unknot normalization fixed. The subsequent [root-orbit pointing proof](root_orbit_pointing.md) extends this calculation to every integer color 1<=j<=r: F_r(M=-q^j)=C_j(q), where C_j is the reduced j-dimensional period. Its proof uses the invariant quotient of the color and a filtered cut-trace argument for a one-component braid closure. In particular F_r(-q)=1 supplies a nonzero reference anchor on the same central fiber as M=1. For the full state this is a residue anchor, as the modified dimension has a pole at M=-q. The [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) now uses these identities and polynomial rigidity to recover the exact Kashaev value from any specified actual all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed small colors. Whole q-germs handle singular steps with a uniform jet bound. Root-level rank one is not required. ## 3. The generic peripheral factor is an actual cyclic lattice gauge Write N_r(alpha)=d_r(alpha)F_r(alpha) for the modified-trace ADO invariant. Its defining modified dimension is d_r(alpha)=-q^(r(1-r)/2) (q^(alpha+1)-q^(-alpha-1))/(q^(r alpha)-q^(-r alpha)). Introduce the marked meridian coordinate M=-q x, so that M=1 at alpha=r-1. Then, exactly, d_r(M)=eta_r (M-M^(-1))/(M^r-M^(-r)) =eta_r M^(r-1)/P_r(M^2), eta_r=(-1)^(r+1)q^(r(1-r)/2)=i^(r+3), P_r(t)=1+t+...+t^(r-1). (3.1) Thus the modified-dimension factor is the cyclic stable-lattice generator 1/P_r(t) from Section 3.1 of the intrinsic norm-torsor note, with t=M^2, together with its explicit monomial and phase. This is an instance in the literature state itself, not just a model. At M=1 the whole rational germ is regular and evaluates to d_r(1)=eta_r/r, <K>_r=r eta_r^(-1) N_r(r-1). (3.2) Setting numerator and denominator separately to zero would discard this value. The exact comparison keeps the peripheral polynomial P_r and its specialization P_r(1)=r. No topological or norm conclusion uses a bare numerical multiplier in its place. There is also a level-independent difference equation. Since the color shift sends M to q M and q^r=-1, d_r(qM)/d_r(M)=g(q,M), g(q,M)=-q^(-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). (3.3) If f(M)=M-M^(-1), then g=-f(qM)/f(M). Thus this normalization line is a fixed rational gauge tensored with the sign character of the shift. Its root-level realization is the explicit peripheral divisor in (3.1). It is not a collection of arbitrary independent finite-level scalars. The subsequent [relative octahedral calculation](relative_octahedral_period.md) also derives 1/P_r(M^2) as the missing cyclic transition of the finite factorial actually appearing in these R entries. Its polynomial recurrence retains the source M^(2r)e_partial, and its cyclic system is nonsingular even on the completion's polar divisor. Thus this normalization has an explicit local relative origin as well as the meridian gauge calculation above. The global source/regulator comparison is not inferred from it. ## 4. The literature annihilator ideal and the pointed conjecture The all-level ADO annihilator ideal is defined in the literature by I_ADO={P(q,x,T): P(q_r,x,T)N_r(x)=0 for all but finitely many r}, T x=q x T, q_r=exp(pi*i/r). See equation (1.5) of the cited definition source. Under x=-q^(-1)M, the exact change from N_r to F_r induces the automorphism of the localized Ore algebra C(q,M)[T^(+/-1);sigma] M -> M, T -> g(q,M) T. (4.1) Indeed d_r^(-1) T d_r=g T. Therefore existence of a nonzero all-level annihilator is equivalent in the two normalizations, and their localized ideals correspond by (4.1). No unverified equality with the colored-Jones recursion ideal or AJ specialization is needed for this statement. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now supplies a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. The cited paper's holonomicity theorem remains outside the proof premises; the stronger multicomponent dimension statement is not needed for this conclusion. At M=1 the comparison uses the lattices and regular whole period germs in (3.1)--(3.2), since the localized coefficient g is meromorphic there. Localization alone does not specify this specialization. The subsequent [actual peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives this gauge from the pivotal partial traces of the two adjacent-color projectors, without a modified-trace comparison theorem. The full state has elementary boundary actions M+M^(-1) and T+T^(-1). The fusion wall at M=1 has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue with exactly normalized partial trace; its actual knot coefficient and the normal Kashaev functional are retained as distinct meridian derivatives. Peripheral skein relations thus yield actual annihilators, without identifying the entire ideals or their geometric components. For this literature family with its prescribed pointing, the desired quantum-A volume statement is lim_(r->infinity) (2*pi/r) log|F_r(M=1)|=Vol(S^3 minus K). (4.2) Equations (2.1) and (3.2) identify (4.2) with Kashaev's original conjecture. The same rate for N_r at the regular germ M=1 is equivalent, since log r/r tends to zero and |eta_r|=1. This is a precise formulation with a fixed literature state, not an arbitrary solution of an operator. Equation (4.2) is not proved here. ## 5. What a root-of-unity central torsor does and does not select There is a useful general constraint. Let a nonzero rational function h(x) solve a specialized finite-order q-difference equation with q a primitive n-th root. Let H=T^n be its companion monodromy as in the intrinsic norm-torsor note. Then det(I-H)=0. (5.1) Proof: evaluation at h is a nonzero module map from the cyclic operator module to (C(x),sigma). On the target sigma^n=1. Hence the map kills H-I, so H-I cannot be invertible. This proof uses the solution pairing, not an identification of column vectors with solutions. Both F_r and N_r are rational in x at zero framing. Thus any specified all-level operator annihilating them has a central v=1 sector at its regular root levels n=2r. This finite-level sector must not be identified automatically with the geometric component of the classical q->1 A-curve. The quantum family and its distinguished pointing remain essential. No assertion is made that the literal classical A-curve is the central spectral curve of each root-level state. The required torsor comparison is therefore a comparison of the all-level pointed period with the marked geometric regulator, retaining the normalization lattice. The cyclic norm torsor alone does not select the volume-dominant geometric sector.

title: The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing
text: # The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing Research note, 25 October 2026. This uses Kashaev's crossing weights, [q-alg/9504020](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020), equations (2.7)--(2.12), and the enhanced braid definition recorded in Murakami--Murakami, [math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075), Sections 1 and 4. Their comparison proofs are not premises. We derive the Fourier identity and normalization comparison below directly from finite products. This is an independent verification of a known comparison, not a new volume theorem. It fixes the literature state to which a quantum A-module argument must apply. All integers N>=2, including even and composite levels, are allowed. The subsequent [Casimir/lattice comparison](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) expresses this same crossing and its inverse by confluent Casimir polynomials, retaining the double-point derivatives and exact writhe phase. It also derives the actual pivotal closing trace on that spectral algebra and identifies the operators through the singular cyclic recoupling lattice. ## 1. The Fourier transform is triangular Put omega=exp(2*pi*i/N), p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^h), p_0=1, and bar_p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^(-h)). Let R^o be exactly the unbraided matrix in Kashaev's equation (2.12). Use F_ij=omega^(ij)/sqrt(N), A=(F^(-1) tensor F^(-1)) R^o(F tensor F). **Fourier identity.** With indices in {0,...,N-1}, the only nonzero entries are A_(a-k,b+k ; a,b) =omega^(1+(a-k)(b+1)) p_a p_(b+k)/(p_(a-k) p_b p_k), 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b). (1.1) In particular, conservation here is equality of ordinary integer sums, not just equality modulo N. ### Direct proof For a nonzero original entry introduce residues u=[j-i-1], v=[i-l], t=[l-k], h=[k-j]. The two theta factors say u+t<N and v+h<N. Their total is congruent to -1 modulo N, so u+v+t+h=N-1. Conversely every such composition and one free j specify exactly one original entry. In these coordinates, i=j-1-u, k=j+h, l=j+h+t (mod N), R^o_(i,j ; k,l)=N omega^(1-(t+h)(u+h)) /(p_u bar_p_v p_t bar_p_h). (1.2) The free j-sum in the Fourier transform gives the conservation delta. Put z=t+h. The remaining sum factors into A_(c,d ; a,b)=delta_(a+b=c+d mod N) sum_(z=0)^(N-1) omega^(1+c-z^2+z(a+b)) S_(N-1-z)(omega^(c-z)) S_z(omega^(z-a)), (1.3) where the elementary finite binomial identity is S_m(X)=sum_(j=0)^m X^j/(p_j bar_p_(m-j)) =product_(j=1)^m(X-omega^j)/p_m. (1.4) For a direct induction, use bar_p_m=(-1)^m omega^(-m(m+1)/2)p_m and compare coefficients in (1-omega^m)S_m(X)=(X-omega^m)S_(m-1)(X). The first factor in (1.3) vanishes unless c<=z; the second vanishes unless z<=a. Using p_(N-1)=N and the same formula for bar_p_j, the surviving sum, with m=a-c, is omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) sum_(j=0)^m (-1)^j omega^(j(j-1)/2) omega^((b+1)j)/(p_j p_(m-j)) =omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) (omega^(b+1);omega)_m/p_m. (1.5) The last equality follows from the same finite binomial identity. If b+m>=N, this Pochhammer symbol contains 1-omega^N and vanishes. Otherwise d=b+m as an ordinary integer and the symbol is p_(b+m)/p_b. This proves (1.1), with no primality assumption. ## 2. A literal comparison with the root-of-unity quantum-group matrix Let s=exp(pi*i/N), H_j=N-1-2j, and use the N-dimensional highest-weight module with H v_j=H_j v_j, K v_j=s^(H_j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_s^2 v_(j-1), F_low v_j=v_(j+1). At the endpoints the missing vectors are zero. These are the specialized usual matrices E v_j=[j]_s[N-j]_s v_(j-1), since [N-j]_s=[j]_s. Let R^q=s^(H tensor H/2) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) s^(k(k-1)/2)(s-s^(-1))^k/[k]_s! E^k tensor F_low^k. (2.1) Every denominator in (2.1) is nonzero. Put G_j=p_j/(1-omega)^j=s^(j(j-1)/2)[j]_s!, D_j=(-s)^j, gamma=omega*s^(-(N-1)^2/2). Then (1.1) gives exactly A=gamma (D G tensor G) R^q (G^(-1) tensor G^(-1)D^(-1)). (2.2) Here G,D are diagonal. To verify (2.2), substitute the matrix elements of E^k and F_low^k in (2.1), replace each [j]_s! by s^(-j(j-1)/2)p_j/(1-omega)^j, and cancel. The remaining exponent and factorials are precisely those in (1.1). Thus exponentially large factorials in G have not been declared harmless; their positions in the exact conjugations remain specified. ## 3. The published enhancement and every braid word Let P swap tensor factors, and let S v_j=v_(j+1 mod N). In the enhanced Kashaev convention used here, B_K=P(R^o)^T, mu_K=-s S, alpha_K=-s, beta_K=1. (3.1) The transpose/order in (3.1) matters. Substituting (2.8) of Kashaev in P(R^o)^T gives exactly the four-index enhanced crossing definition. For the quantum-group dual convention put B_q=P(R^q)^T, mu_q=K^(-1), alpha_q=s^((N^2-1)/2), beta_q=1. (3.2) Equation (2.2), transposed and with the tensor factors exchanged, gives a similarity of B_K with gamma*B_q. For a braid on b strands, define U_b=F^(-tensor b) tensor_(j=1)^b (G^(-1)D^(j-1)). The meaning is the product of F^(-tensor b) with the displayed diagonal tensor product. Since B_q conserves the integer weight sum, it commutes with D tensor D. Thus the same U_b works simultaneously for every adjacent generator and its inverse: rho_K(word)=gamma^(w(word)) U_b rho_q(word) U_b^(-1). (3.3) The enhancement also matches exactly: U_b mu_q^(tensor b) U_b^(-1)=mu_K^(tensor b), gamma*alpha_q=-s=alpha_K. (3.4) For the first identity, diagonal G,D commute with mu_q and F^(-1)diag(omega^j)F=S; also s^(-(N-1))=-s. The quantum-group partial traces have values alpha_q and alpha_q^(-1). One way to verify the scalars is to use the coproduct intertwining equations for (2.1) and trace cyclicity: the weighted partial traces commute with the dual module's generators. These act irreducibly because their adjacent coefficients are nonzero and the K eigenvalues are distinct. The traces are therefore scalar. The positive trace at v_(N-1) and negative trace at v_0 each have a single contributing term, giving s^((N^2-1)/2) and its inverse. The coproduct equations themselves reduce to the coefficient recurrence c_(k+1)/c_k=s^k(s-s^(-1))/[k+1]_s of the finite sum (2.1). These checks are elementary algebra and do not invoke a global state-integral theorem. For a braid closure with one component, cut the first strand and take the weighted partial trace over the others. The unnormalized operator is scalar: it is a quantum-group endomorphism of the simple color. Conjugations on the traced factors cancel by cyclicity; conjugation on the open factor cancels because this operator is scalar. Finally the factors gamma^(w) cancel against alpha_K^(-w) by (3.4). **Consequence.** The normalized enhanced Kashaev period in (3.1) equals the reduced N-colored quantum-group period at s=exp(pi*i/N), with unknot value one. This holds for every braid presentation of a knot and every N>=2. It is a direct independent verification of the standard enhanced-state comparison, not an appeal to its published proof.
