The usual quantum-group parameter for the colored Jones polynomial is omega=s^2; the chosen dual and tensor-order convention is retained. ## 4. A printed phase needs attention The literal candidate inverse printed in Kashaev's (2.15), combined with the normalization (2.12), fails the identity (2.16) already at N=2: the product is -I. This is checked in characteristic zero with rational entries. The exact cyclotomic diagnostics at further levels give omega*I. We use the actual matrix inverse in (3.3), determined by (2.2), rather than silently deleting this phase. This observation concerns a printed normalization identity, not a counterexample to the knot volume conjecture. The enhanced definition (3.1) specifies its own actual inverse and scalar normalization. ## 5. Reproducible algebraic checks and scope `experiments/audit_kashaev_crossing.py` evaluates the original four-index weight independently of (1.1), checks its complete Fourier transform, the quantum-group matrix comparison, and the enhanced partial traces. It includes even and composite levels. Prime-field diagnostics are supplementary to the characteristic-zero identities proved above. The coefficient and enhancement identities fix a literature state uniformly, with no FAMED hypothesis or knot census. They do not prove the AJ conjecture or the Kashaev volume conjecture. In particular, they do not make the AK/Faddeev contour state equal to this finite period. That is a different comparison. A standard noncommutative A-polynomial can now be discussed together with this distinguished reduced quantum-group period, rather than an arbitrary solution of its recurrence. Root-of-unity periodicity and the geometric q->1 branch must still be distinguished in its period-torsor comparison.

title: An independent audit of the Li–Wang regulator line
text: # An independent audit of the Li–Wang regulator line Research audit, 26 October 2026. The source is Weiping Li and Qingxue Wang, [On the Generalized Volume Conjecture and Regulator, arXiv:math/0610745v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0610745v1), the nine-page 2006 version. Its [version-specific HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0610745v1) was checked against the PDF. The earlier math/0604057 is not needed here. This is a correctness and terminology audit, not a claim about novelty or a proof of colored-Jones asymptotics. The core flat regulator line is valid with logarithms continued along paths. The paper does not construct our root-of-unity quantum norm torsor. There are two distinct branch qualifications: a literal use of the printed discontinuous logarithm fails, while an endpoint-only scalar reading of its later special Chern–Simons integral requires additional trivialization data. Neither qualification disproves the continued-log regulator. ## 1. What the source actually supplies The terminology is a flat line bundle: Introduction, p. 1; §3.2, equation (3.6), pp. 4–5; and Remark 2(iii), p. 7. The universal Heisenberg bundle's explicit construction is referred to Bloch and Ramakrishnan, rather than written out. The inspected text contains neither “torsor” nor “principal.” Proposition 3.2, p. 5, supplies a K2-torsion assertion; Theorem 3.3, p. 6, deduces exactness and rational periods. Equation (3.9), p. 7, remains a conjecture. [Primary text, §§3.2–3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0610745v1#S3.SS2). Removing the zero section of a complex line gives an analytic principal C* bundle. Calling that associated object a torsor is mathematically legitimate. It is a translation of the line-bundle construction, not a separate scalar norm equation or an identification with a quantum object. The calculations below independently check the relevant construction. ## 2. Rebuild the logarithmic quotient and its connection Set t=2πi. On the logarithmic cover of (C*)² write f=exp(F), g=exp(G). The following deck transformations define an analytic line: D_(a,b)(F,G,z)=(F+t a,G+t b,exp(aG) z), a,b in Z. (2.1) Indeed, applying D_(a,b) and then D_(c,d) gives the product multiplier exp((a+c)G+t cb)=exp((a+c)G). Thus the action is an actual action. Local branches F_j=F_i+t a_ij, G_j=G_i+t b_ij give local fiber-coordinate transitions z_j=exp(a_ij G_i)z_i; the same calculation checks their cocycle. Declare A=F dG/t, nabla=d-A. (2.2) Then A changes by a dG, the logarithmic differential of exp(aG). Consequently (2.2) descends. In this declared convention its curvature is F_nabla=-dA=-dF wedge dG/t. (2.3) On a smooth complex curve with f,g invertible, dF and dG are locally holomorphic multiples of the same local parameter differential. Their wedge is zero. The pullback connection is therefore flat. No K2 torsion is needed for this flatness. Lift a based loop γ starting with logarithms F0,G0. Write its endpoint as (F0+t a,G0+t b). Parallel transport in (2.2) multiplies z by exp(∫γ F dG/t). Comparing the endpoint fiber to the initial fiber requires exp(−aG0), by (2.1). The holonomy is exactly r(f,g)(γ)=exp((∫γ F dG−G0 ∫γ dF)/t). (2.4) This reproduces the source's (3.6), with continued logarithms. Shifting F by t r and G0 by t s changes the numerator by t²(rb−sa), so the exponential is branch independent. Concatenation adds an extra t²ab' to the numerator, also invisible after exponentiation. Flatness proves homotopy invariance; rank-one holonomy also gives the usual base-point independence under transport. There is a normalization issue in the printed curvature statements, Proposition 3.1(1), p. 4, and Remark 2(iii), p. 7. With (2.4) fixed as holonomy, the actual connection curvature in convention (2.2) is (2.3), not the unnormalized dF wedge dG. The discrepancy is invisible after restriction to a curve, where both vanish. A nonzero universal curvature or Chern class must retain the connection convention and its factors of 2πi. We do not use the source's unnormalized formula as such a universal Chern–Weil identity. ## 3. Verify that the holonomy descends through the K2 relations Bilinearity follows directly from (2.4). For antisymmetry, the sum of the two numerators is ∫γ d(FG)−G0 ∫γ dF−F0 ∫γ dG=t²ab, whose exponential after division by t is one. The local tame-symbol calculation can also be done without a cited proof. At a puncture with parameter w, let f=w^a u(w), g=w^b v(w), u(0)v(0)!=0. On a small positive circle, continuous logarithms give the limiting numerator/t as bF0−aG0+tab/2. Its exponential is (−1)^(ab) u(0)^b/v(0)^a. (3.1) The radius-dependent powers cancel. Flatness on the punctured disc identifies this limit with the actual small-loop holonomy. For the Steinberg relation, first use f=w,g=1−w on P1 minus {0,1,infinity}. The small-loop values at both 0 and 1 are one by (3.1). These loops generate its fundamental group, so the character is trivial. Pulling back along f proves r(f,1−f)=1 on its domain. Thus the homomorphism out of the symbol presentation of K2 is verified here, including its tame signs. One need not assume a published dilogarithm argument for these particular checks. ## 4. Exactly what torsion gives Suppose q{l,m}=0 in the function-field K2. Then (2.4) has q-th power one. If the relation is initially realized after deleting extra points, the inclusion of that smaller punctured curve surjects on the fundamental group of the larger one; the already-defined character therefore has q-th power one on the source's Y_h as well. Its image has order **dividing** q. Equality with the K2 order is not required and is not implied by applying a homomorphism. The transfer arithmetic in Proposition 3.2 is correct: if restriction to a degree-n field extension kills 2{l,m}, then transfer back gives 2n{l,m}=0. This audit has not independently rederived, from a knot presentation, the existence of that finite extension or the cited order-two statement in it. Those are the geometric K2 inputs to the paper's knot-wide application. They are explicitly kept separate from the directly verified regulator construction and its conditional consequences. For those consequences write F=log l=x+iu and G=log m=y+iv, continuing u,v on the path. Integration by parts on a closed loop gives Im(∫ F dG−G0 ∫ dF)=∫(x dv−y du), Re(∫ F dG−G0 ∫ dF)=−∫(y dx+u dv)+v0∫du. (4.1) The boundary contribution in the first identity cancels the real part of G0 ∫dF. At the paper's complete base point m0=1, choose G0=0. Finite-order holonomy then gives ∫γ (x dv−y du)=0, (q/(4π²))∫γ(y dx+u dv) is an integer. (4.2) The first integrand is a globally defined closed real form; all its periods vanish, so it is exact. The second is a continued-branch integral. Changing the initial branch u by 2πk changes its normalized value by an integer multiple of q. This verifies the substantive quantization deduction under the K2-torsion hypothesis. It gives finite monodromy and a trivial q-th tensor power of the flat line, not a pointing of the original line and not a quantum asymptotic estimate. ## 5. A literal fixed-cut reading fails; the continued-log reading survives Immediately after (3.6), p. 4, the source fixes 0≤arg z<2π and describes the discontinuity on the positive real axis. A literal pointwise insertion of this discontinuous log into the integral cannot define the asserted regulator. Continuous path logs, or equivalent transition contributions at cuts, are necessary. An exact diagnostic uses the algebraic curve l=−z, m=z, z in C*, base point z=1. (5.1) Its symbol {−z,z} is zero: the Steinberg relation applied to z and z^(-1) gives {z,z}={z,−1}, hence {z,−z}=2{z,−1}=0. Thus its K2 order is q=1. On z=exp(iθ), 0≤θ≤2π, continuous logarithms give arg l=π+θ and log m0=0. Therefore ∫ log l dlog m=−∫_0^(2π)(π+θ)dθ=−4π², r(l,m)=1. (5.2) With pointwise 0≤arg l<2π, arg l instead jumps at θ=π. The same integral becomes −∫_0^π(π+θ)dθ−∫_π^(2π)(θ−π)dθ=−2π², literal_fixed_cut_r(l,m)=−1. (5.3) The corresponding normalized real period is 1/2 rather than an integer. This is a counterexample to the **literal fixed-cut reading** of the general construction and quantization inference. It is not a knot A-curve counterexample and does not contradict (2.4) or (4.2). Interpreting (3.6) using continued logs repairs this issue. ## 6. The later special invariant needs its path or endpoint frame After Remark 2(iii), p. 7, the paper defines, for a path c from the complete base point to (l,m), the quantity U_c=−q∫c(y dx+u dv). (6.1) Remark 3, on the same page, describes U/(2π)² as well-defined in R/Z. The path is indeed present in the preceding definition. On that marked path domain (6.1) is a meaningful quantity. The assertion cannot be inferred as a single-valued function of an **unmarked endpoint** from the closed-loop statement (4.2) alone. To see the obstruction, insert a based loop γ before c and let a=wind_γ(l). The l logarithm on the following copy of c has changed by 2πia. Consequently U_(γ*c)−U_c=U_γ−2πq a∫c darg m, (U_(γ*c)−U_c)/(4π²) =−q a Δ_c arg(m)/(2π) mod Z. (6.2) The right side is generally not integral. For (5.1), let c_θ run from angle 0 to θ with continuous arguments. Direct integration gives U_(c_θ)=−πθ−θ²/2, U_(c_(θ+2π))−U_(c_θ)=−4π²−2πθ. (6.3) At θ=π/2 the difference divided by 4π² is −5/4. Thus even the valid continued-log interpretation does not make this integral a function of the unmarked endpoint on a general torsion-symbol curve. The same obstruction (6.2) applies on any curve possessing the stated winding loop and a path with the indicated nonintegral endpoint phase; we do not assert a specific knot example from (5.1). There is a precise section interpretation. Put rho=−y dx−u dv+i(x dv−y du) =F dG−d(yF). (6.4) Then d rho=dF wedge dG. Under u→u+2πa it changes by −2πa dv. Thus rho is a local connection potential, not a single global scalar form. The smooth gauge z_tilde=exp(−yF/t)z changes (2.2) to rho/t and has deck multiplier exp(i a v). Its q-th tensor power retains exp(iq a v), exactly the endpoint phase missing from an endpoint-only reading of (6.1). A path-cover value or a local coordinate of a bundle section is consistent. A chosen global endpoint frame, or explicit cut corrections, is additional data. The vanishing of the exterior derivative in Remark 2(iii) does not itself supply it. ## 7. Keep the categories and our normalization separate The universal object in (2.1) is analytic. Its nonzero vectors form an analytic principal C* bundle. Its restriction to a curve with (2.2) is a flat bundle; the sheaf of horizontal vectors is a rank-one local system. H1 with **constant** C* coefficients classifies these flat objects, rather than just their underlying holomorphic lines. The universal analytic bundle is not an algebraic G_m torsor on (G_m)². Integrating (2.3)/(2πi) on the real two-torus gives −1 in our declared convention, so the underlying topological line is nontrivial. In contrast C[f^(±1),g^(±1)] is a factorial regular ring, and its algebraic Picard group is zero. The universal line therefore cannot be the analytification of an algebraic line on that torus. This obstruction concerns the universal torus bundle, not every restriction of it. In particular a finite-monodromy restriction can be studied with a finite-cover algebraic model, but that is further category/comparison information, not the displayed analytic quotient. The associated Heisenberg group can be written (F,G,H)*(F',G',H') =(F+F',G+G',H+H'+F G'). (7.1) Its center is additive and the quotient is the additive (F,G) plane. Left multiplication by (ta,tb,t²c) sends H to H+taG+t²c. Exponentiating H/t gives precisely (2.1); dH−F dG is invariant. The noncommutative central extension, its integral lattice quotient, and the resulting analytic C* bundle are related constructions, not interchangeable names for one algebraic G_m torsor over the A-curve. There is also a factor of two in a direct comparison with [our boundary line](boundary_regulator_period.md). On a **common** torus with U=log m,V=log l, the regulator potential is V dU/t. The gauge z_sym=exp(−UV/(2t))z changes it to A_sym=(V dU−U dV)/(2t), z_sym'=(−1)^(ab)exp((bU−aV)/2)z_sym. (7.2) Squaring removes the sign and gives exactly our deck multiplier exp(bU−aV) and potential (V dU−U dV)/t. Thus, on the same torus and with these conventions, our boundary line is the **square** of the symmetrized r(l,m) line. Matching the actual papers additionally requires transporting squared eigenvalues and complete-point shifts; the literal variable names are not that transport. Reversing (l,m) dualizes the regulator. These constants should not be hidden inside a generic statement that the two lines are the same. [Our common period space](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) has an explicit algebraic unipotent connection and further exponential periods. Nothing here identifies their selected periods with the knot state. [Our quantum norm construction](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) instead begins with a specialized q-difference module, a finite etale cyclic algebra S/k, and N_(S/k)(a)=v. That solution variety is a torsor under the norm-one torus, while its scalar intertwiners form a separate G_m torsor. Neither follows from (2.4) or from calling a line's nonzero vectors a torsor. ## 8. Reproducible scope [The exact audit script](../experiments/audit_li_wang_heisenberg.py) checks the deck cocycle, connection transformation, curvature constant, antisymmetry, branch shifts, Heisenberg horizontal form, local secondary-potential transformation, factor-of-two comparison, and both explicit branch diagnostics. [Recorded results](../experiments/li_wang_heisenberg_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_li_wang_heisenberg.py The verified result is the analytic regulator line, its continued-log holonomy, and the quantization deduction conditional on K2 torsion. The knot K2 input has not been independently reproved here. The endpoint-only reading of the later special invariant needs correction or additional marking. No quantum norm-torsor comparison or volume conjecture is proved by this audit.

title: The literal FIRST five-point operator word and its original full source
text: # The literal FIRST five-point operator word and its original full source 28 October 2026. This realizes the FIRST classical certificate -partial(b,p,p_1,s_M,s_R) of [the crossing fundamental cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), with its actual flag order. It uses the original two physical heads, one compulsory second-head strict cut, the original factorial frame, and its marked full-Psi function. No auxiliary head or unrelated quantum-torus coordinates are introduced. The resulting two-to-three operator identity is embedded in the ENTIRE original crossing. Every finite projector, marked scalar, Cartan factor and original cup/cap remains. This closes this literal local certificate; it does not by itself supply a positive geometric face atlas or a global selected-cycle degree. ## 1. The actual FIRST five flags, in the same bounded frame Keep the complete original conventions Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, T=Z_2, X=x S_2 S_1^(-1). Thus XZ=QZX and XT=Q^(-1)TX. Use the actual balanced Gauss generators e_j,f_j,K_j of the [shared quantum meridians](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md). In the bounded homogeneous frame Y=-ZS_1, L=[[Y,0],[-S_1,1]], the FIRST flags have the following canonical columns and retained right tags. This is the SAME frame as in [the literal middle configuration](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). | Flag | Canonical column | Right tag in L flag = column times tag | | --- | --- | --- | | b | (1,1-X)^t | Y | | p | (0,1)^t | 1 | | p_1 | (1-Z,1)^t | lambda | | s_M | (1,1)^t | YK_1 | | s_R | (1,R)^t | YK_2K_1 | Here R=1-(1-T)X. (1) For the last row, the exact coproduct/Gauss first column is s_R=(K_2K_1,F_tot K_2K_1)^t, F_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2. Since f_1-S_1=Y and K_1^(-1)f_2Y^(-1)=-(1-T)X, one has F_tot-S_1=RY, proving the row without dividing by any nilpotent flag determinant. Every right tag is retained. At unit wrap marks these tags are unitary, as is the previous bounded-frame convention up to its fixed two-by-two condition. Classically the ordered tuple is therefore (b,p,p_1,s_M,s_R) =(1-X,infinity,1/(1-Z),1,1-(1-T)X). (2) The reciprocal in (2) is only a commutative chart notation; the actual finite flag is the homogeneous column in the table. ## 2. Its five literal cross-ratios Put n_cl=-X(1-Z)/Z, G=1-n_cl+n_cl T. Using exactly the determinant convention r(v0,v1,v2,v3) =det(v3,v1)det(v2,v0)/(det(v3,v0)det(v2,v1)), the FIRST face table is | Omitted flag | Cross-ratio r_j | Sign in -partial | | --- | --- | --- | | b | G | - | | p | G/T | + | | p_1 | 1/T | - | | s_M | (1-1/n_cl)/T | + | | s_R | 1-1/n_cl | - | These are direct determinants of the five columns in (2), not an arbitrary renamed five-term pattern. The independent symbolic audit checks all five rational identities. Define the convenient quad coordinates a_cl=n_cl(1-T), y_cl=-n_cl T/(1-n_cl), J_cl=T/G. The rational oriented pre-Bloch rules [1-z]=-[z], [1/z]=-[z], [1-1/z]=[z], and [z/(z-1)]=-[z] convert that literal table to -partial=[a_cl]-[J_cl]+[T]-[y_cl]-[n_cl]. (3) In particular (3) compares the two signed lists left: [n_cl]-[T], right: -[y_cl]-[J_cl]+[a_cl]. (4) The signed right list minus the left list is the specified FIRST negative boundary. These signs and quads are fixed below by the actual finite operators. ## 3. The genuine finite cut and the original crossing atom Let E_d(T) be the original second-head index-d projector and put n=e_1 S_2=(Q-Z^(-1))X, c=n(1-E_d(T)), a=e_1 f_2. (5) The classical n is exactly n_cl from Section 2. Its second-head cut is indispensable. It gives, at the actual finite level, cT=Q^(-1)Tc, c^N=0, a=c(1-QT). (6) Indeed c=e_1 tensor J_(+,2) uses the literal strict second-head raise. Acting on input index j, its multiplication by 1-QT supplies 1-Q^(j+1), exactly the coefficient of f_2. The possible wrap of n is killed by that same original zero. Use the original finite Euler function P_Q(A)=sum_(h=0)^d p_h A^h, p_h=(-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)/(Q;Q)_h. Let F_j=(Q;Q)_j and retain the marked scalar phi_N=sqrt(N) exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. The original marked full-Psi root clock is mathcal F_T=marked Psi(QT)=phi_N diag_j(1/F_j). The logarithmic lift at index j is 2pi*i*(j+1)/N. In particular the index-d value uses the regular TOP lift, not the bottom zero. Set F=mathcal F_T^(-1)=phi_N^(-1)diag_j(F_j). (7) Consecutive factorial ratios, including the strict top edge, prove F c F^(-1)=c(1-QT)=a. (8) Thus the ENTIRE original uncheck crossing is R_0=D P_Q(a)=D F P_Q(c) F^(-1). (9) D is its original Cartan diagonal. Its nonzero common Cartan scalar kappa, flip, writhe correction and peripheral normalization remain the original external lines. Equation (9) is a matrix identity, not a change of invariant or a replacement of the original source. ## 4. Exact two-to-three sequence and all developed arguments Abbreviate P=P_Q(c) and define the transported marked clock H=P^(-1)TP, F_H=P^(-1)FP, y=-Q cH, Y=P_Q(y). (10) All displayed inverses exist. In particular H^N=1 and y^N=c^N=0. The relation cH=Q^(-1)Hc follows by conjugating (6). Conjugating (8) gives F_H c F_H^(-1)=c(1-QH)=c+y. (11) Moreover yc=Qcy. The ordered finite binomial theorem therefore gives P_Q(c+y)=P_Q(y)P_Q(c). Every term of degree >=N vanishes because it contains that degree of c. Thus (11) yields the exact FIRST operator sequence F_H P=Y P F_H, P F_H=Y^(-1)F_H P. (12) This is a two-to-three identity at every level, including even and composite N. Its one marked full-Psi factor is the SAME transported F_H on both sides; its scalar phi_N^(-1) has not been reset. The left word P F_H develops to c and the negative clock T, since PHP^(-1)=T. The right word develops to y with negative orientation, the negative marked clock J=Y^(-1)HY=H(1+cH)^(-1), (13) and the final positive argument Y^(-1)F_H c F_H^(-1)Y=a. (14) Here (13)--(14) are exact ordered identities, not only symbols. For a proof, the finite Euler recurrences give (1-c)H=T, Y^(-1)cY=c(1-y), Y^(-1)HY=H(1-Q^(-1)y)^(-1). Since (1-y)H=H(1-Q^(-1)y), substitution in (11) gives Y^(-1)c(1-QH)Y =c(1-y)-QcH =c-Qc(1-c)H=c(1-QT)=a. The denominator 1+cH in (13) is a unit because cH is nilpotent; there is no inverse of a singular clock determinant. J is a conjugate of H, so J^N=1 with its integer clock mark transported by the same Y, not chosen afresh. Classically H=T/(1-n_cl), and (10), (13), (14) give precisely y_cl,J_cl,a_cl of Section 2. Thus the five developed signed arguments of (12) are the literal FIRST table (3)--(4). There is also a useful fixed-degree ordered Ptolemy form, involving the original unsplit atom a rather than a guessed scalar quotient: G_first=1-a=1-c+Tc, J=G_first^(-1)T, r=Jc=-y(1-y)^(-1), 1-r=G_first^(-1)(1-c). (14a) For (14a), invert (13): J^(-1)=H^(-1)+c=T^(-1)(1-c)+c =T^(-1)(1-c+Tc)=T^(-1)(1-a). Also Jc=QcH(1+QcH)^(-1), which is the displayed quad of y. All inverses in (14a) are units because a,c,y are nilpotent. The first literal face complements G_first and 1-c, the clock J, and the fourth-face quad r therefore satisfy exact ordered equations on the original physical heads, with the strict c-wall retained. They are not products of separately compressed coordinate ports. Combining (9)--(12) embeds the identity in the original crossing: R_0=D P F_H F^(-1) =D Y^(-1)F_H P F^(-1). (15) The terminal F^(-1) is a compulsory interface. Deleting it changes the operator and original period. The inverse checked crossing is the inverse of (15), with the SAME original scalars; the exact audit compares it independently with the original negative formula. The operator proof (5)--(15) actually extends over the whole original color parameters at this fixed physical q root: use the original e_1(x_1), the same strict J_(+,2), and the original mixed Cartan D(x_1,x_2). Equations (6), (8), and the finite binomial proof are unchanged. Thus it also preserves the whole meridian color germ and its normal derivatives. The literal five-flag table of Sections 1--2 and the explicit source evaluations below are stated at completeness. No off-root Hopf or generic-q invariant is being asserted. ## 5. The complete strict wall and its current Every power of the cut is explicit: c^h=n^h(1-sum_(j=N-h)^(N-1)E_j(T)), 0<=h<N. (16) For h=0 the sum is empty. The forbidden second-head wrap inputs are exactly those j with j+h>=N. The first-head nilpotence is retained independently. Thus (16) supplies the whole finite source wall, not merely its principal approximation. Write mu_2=S_2^N=x^N mu and W=nE_d(T)=mu_2 e_1 tensor |0><d|, F_tot=f_1 tensor I+K_1^(-1) tensor f_2. Its actual total-current commutator is [F_tot,W]=mu_2( [f_1,e_1] tensor |0><d| +(1-Q)K_1^(-1)e_1 tensor |1><d| -(1-Q^(-1))e_1K_1^(-1) tensor |0><d-1|). (17) This follows by applying f_2 before or after the missing wrap. It is retained in (5), (16), and all conjugated interfaces. No separate wall or radial summand is asserted Ward-invariant. Applying the ordinary typed commutator product rule to the exact operator equality (15) transports every other original current as well. At an interior position of a word the full W remains; one does not replace it by a scalar source value. ## 6. Original cup, marker, and uncanceled marked scalar Keep the original balanced cup and full marker p=N sum_(j=0)^d x^(j-d)|j,d-j>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. (18) On this whole degree-d cup, any forbidden second-head input in (16) has first index <h and is already killed by e_1^h. Thus c^h p=n^h p, m c^h p=1, 0<=h<N. (19) For the moment in (19), summing the explicit complete e_1 coefficients reduces it to (1/N)sum_(j=h)^d (Q^(-j);Q)_h=1. Extend the sum to all j modulo N: its omitted terms are zero, its constant coefficient contributes N, and all positive powers Q^(-ell j), 0<ell<=h<N, sum to zero. This proves (19) directly from the original source. The finite hockey-stick contraction already used for the original middle factor now gives Pp=N|d,0>, Hp=p, F_Hp=phi_N^(-1)p. (20) The transported T-index here is zero, hence the nonzero marked Psi argument is Q with its recorded index-one logarithmic lift. Consequently the two words of (12) have the exact source value mP F_Hp=mY^(-1)F_H Pp=1/(N phi_N). (21) Its modulus is N^(-3/2), with no adjustable normalization. Equation (21) evaluates the unadorned local word on the literal cup. In the full original embedding (15), its actual incoming source is F^(-1)p and its actual outgoing row retains flip D. Those interfaces are kept as operators. The full marked original one-crossing source therefore remains exactly its old value: m flip D [P F_H] F^(-1)p =m flip D [Y^(-1)F_H P] F^(-1)p=1, (22) before the unchanged common scalar kappa. This is also checked against the original E/Cartan coefficient evaluator. No unknown knot period enters the source or any adapter. ## 7. Full-Psi coefficient cycles and scope Every factor of (15) has the same exact full-Psi coefficient realization as in [the full-function source theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). For an explicit contractive core let J_(minus,1) and J_(+,2) be the original strict shifts and use the previously proved factorial/Gaussian frame H_e|j>=lambda^j(-1)^jQ^(j(j-1)/2)|j>/F_j. Then c=(H_e tensor I)(J_(minus,1) tensor J_(+,2)) (H_e^(-1) tensor I). The core has norm <=1. Also y=P^(-1)(-QcT)P, so its Euler factor and inverse reduce, through the explicitly retained P interfaces, to the same kind of strict shift times a unit clock. F and F^(-1) are the marked second-head factorial diagonals with the phases (7); their moment realizations retain the original reflected factorial factors N and phi_N. Every coefficient moment is kept as its FULL circle-minus-ray source, or its equivalent exact atomic-window resolution. The inverse Euler factor Y^(-1) uses the original inverse polynomial on its nilpotent argument, not an unmarked inverse of a scalar full-Psi function. All root marks, finite cuts and radial terms remain in their actual operator order. The common Cartan/writhe/ peripheral lines in (15) are unchanged. This proves the FIRST literal finite five-point operator identity and its full original source, uniformly for the crossing. It does not prove that every displayed framed face is already in a common positive geometric polarization, that separated radial pieces have a gap, or that the global geometric cycle is selected. Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_first_full_phi_certificate.py The audit verifies the five literal rational faces, 27 exact complete/wrap families through N=10, all strict-cut powers and current (17), the developed arguments, both original crossing signs, and the complete cup/marked source including (21)--(22). Eighteen additional mixed-color operator checks verify the whole-color extension, without applying the complete source formulas away from their stated color.

title: A literal middle five-point operator identity with its complete finite source
text: # A literal middle five-point operator identity with its complete finite source 28 October 2026. This realizes the middle classical certificate +partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_M) from [the crossing fundamental cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) as an exact finite relative operator identity inside the original crossing factorization. Its developed arguments are the five cross-ratios of that **specific** configuration, with the required quad/orientation changes. The X face is a strict cut of a cyclic unit; its full projector correction is explicit. The original cup selects a nonzero top marked full-Phi value. This is an identity with marked full-Phi and nilpotent Euler operators, including their factorial face frames and circle/radial sources. It does not assert that each factor separately is an already assigned positive charged tetrahedron in a regular geometric face frame. That further face/Fourier assignment, the other two certificates, and the global selected cycle remain separate work. ## 1. Fixed actual coordinates and the original crossing factor Use complete original heads with Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), XZ=QZX, X^N=Z^N=1. The literal five flags were calculated in [the middle-configuration note](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). With every right flag tag retained, an explicit bounded homogeneous frame sends them to (a,b,p,p_1,s_M)=(0,1-X,infinity,(1-Z,1)^t,1). (1) The fourth entry is a homogeneous column; no inverse of 1-Z is taken. Put P(A)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^hQ^(h(h-1)/2)A^h/F_h, F_h=(Q;Q)_h, n=e_1S_2=(Q-Z^(-1))X, P=P(n), n_-= -e_1Z_2S_2. The exact original uncheck crossing is R_0=D P(n_-)P. (2) D is the original Cartan diagonal. Its common scalar line kappa, framing and peripheral factors remain external and identical throughout. The checked crossing is flip R_0 with that same line; none of these factors is reset. ## 2. The fifth clock is an actual quantum cross-ratio Define H=P^(-1)ZP=Z(1-n)=Z+(1-QZ)X. (3) The finite Euler recurrence proves the middle equality. Thus H is invertible, H^N=1 and nH=QHn, without taking any singular reciprocal of 1-Z. Its commutative symbol is H_cl=X+Z-XZ, the H appearing in the five cross-ratios of (1). Let Psi be the full literature function with the exact normalization in [the modular moment theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). Retain phi_N=sqrt(N) exp{i pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. The elementary marked root evaluation, independently proved in [the marked-flag note](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md), gives F_Z=marked Psi(QZ) =phi_N diag_j[1/F_j], 0<=j<N. (4) The argument at clock index j is on logarithmic lift 2pi*i*(j+1)/N. Thus j=d uses the regular TOP value, not the zero on the bottom lift. The finite missing arrow of n lies at input j=0. The exact conjugation is F_Z n F_Z^(-1)=n(1-Z). (5) Transport the **entire** clock mark, rather than choosing a new one, by F_H=P^(-1)F_ZP. (6) It is the marked full-Phi function of QH in this transported integer frame. Equations (3), (5), and commutation of P with n give F_H n F_H^(-1)=n(1-H). (7) All matrices in (3)--(7) are invertible where claimed at the physical root. The inverse of 1-H is not used. ## 3. The exact two-to-three word and the original R Since n and -nH Q-commute and share nilpotent degree, the finite ordered binomial theorem proves F_H P=P P(-nH)F_H. Equivalently the literal two-to-three sequence is P(n)F_H^(-1)=F_H^(-1)P(n)P(-nH). (8) Multiplying by the displayed interface F_H gives an exact refactorization of the original crossing, including every exterior operator: R_0=D P(n_-) F_H^(-1)P(n)P(-nH)F_H. (9) The final F_H is a retained face/source adapter; deleting it would change the original period. In a network one can use (8) on that specified subword or (9) as a full crossing replacement with its adapter. These are not definitions of a new invariant. ## 4. All five developed arguments and the exact X-wall Use the actual preceding factors to transport each argument to the common input frame. The two arguments on the left of (8) are n and the negative clock Z, since PHP^(-1)=Z. The three on the right are the negative clock H and u=F_H^(-1)nF_H, w=-F_H^(-1)P nH P^(-1)F_H =-F_H^(-1)nZF_H. (10) These are explicit finite matrices, and they simplify to K=X(1-E_0(Z)), u_Z=-Z^(-1)K, u=P^(-1)u_ZP, w=QK=QX(1-E_0(Z)). (11) Here E_0 is the original first-clock zero-index projector. It is the required finite source wall, not an omitted exceptional case. For a proof, F_Z^(-1)nF_Z=u_Z follows from consecutive factorial ratios. Also n=u_Z+QK, u_Z(QK)=Q(QK)u_Z, P(n)=P(u_Z)P(QK). (12) Every term of degree >=N vanishes because K is a strict cut shift. Conjugation by P(u_Z) sends QK to QK(1-u_Z)^(-1). Substitution of (6) into w in (10) then gives w=P^(-1)[-u_Z Z(1-u_Z)^(-1)]P =P^(-1)[QK(1-u_Z)^(-1)]P=QK, proving the last identity of (11) at all levels. The corresponding exact ordered quad relation is r=wH^(-1)=-u(1-Q^(-1)u)^(-1), r^N=0. (13) The inverses in (12)--(13) exist because u is nilpotent. They are not inverses of a clock determinant with a nontrivial kernel. Classically, away from the boundary divisors, (10)--(13) become u_cl=n_cl/(1-H_cl)=-X/[Z(1-X)], w_cl=X, r_cl=X/H_cl, u_cl=r_cl/(r_cl-1). Thus u is the negative-quad coordinate of the tetrahedron with cross-ratio X/H, while w is the precisely cut X tetrahedron. The developed signed list of (8) is therefore left: [n_cl]-[Z], right: -[H_cl]-[X/H_cl]+[X]. (14) This is exactly the middle certificate of (1), since n_cl=-X(1-Z)/Z is the positive-quad coordinate of its omitted-a tetrahedron. It is not a five-point relation for freely chosen unrelated flags. Statement (14) identifies the rational geometric arguments and their quantum cuts. It does not discard the nonlinear factorial frames in assigning a positive tetrahedral kernel or its complete phase. Those frames remain in (4), (6), and the period construction below. ## 5. The complete original source is nonzero and polynomial Keep the actual cup and full marker p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. Then exactly P(n)p=N|d,0>, Hp=Q^(-1)p, F_Hp=(phi_N/N)p. (15) To prove the first identity, the coefficient of |u,d-u> is N x^(u-d) times sum_(h=0)^(d-u) Q^(-h(u+1)) {u+h choose h}_Q ={N choose u+1}_(Q^(-1)). The equality is the finite Gaussian hockey-stick identity. At the primitive root it is zero for u<d and one for u=d. The remaining identities in (15) follow from (3), (4), and (6). In particular the actual cup selects the TOP marked QH argument, with value phi_N/N. Consequently both sides of (8) have the exact source value mP(n)F_H^(-1)p=phi_N^(-1). (16) This is nonzero and has modulus N^(-1/2). In (9) the retained final adapter has factor phi_N/N on the cup. The full checked original crossing therefore has exactly its old source value, including kappa and all original framing/peripheral lines. The scalar has not been reset to one in (8). The complete cut correction is known at every order, not just to first order: w^a=Q^a X^a(1-sum_(j=0)^(a-1)E_j(Z)), mw^ap=1-a/N, 0<=a<N. (17) These formulas follow from the strict shift and the original uniform marked clock distribution. Thus the projector correction can be of order one at bulk a; it is not legitimate to remove it because an individual endpoint weight is 1/N. At an interior position of a longer word one must keep F_H as an operator and every projector of (17). The scalar simplification (15) applies to this actual input cup. The earlier counterexamples to untransported interior cut relocation are unaffected. ## 6. Full-Phi/Fourier frames and all radial components Every operator in (8)--(9) has an explicit fixed-complexity full-Phi/Gaussian relative-period realization. Let T=J_(minus,1) tensor S_2, D_n|j>=lambda^j(-1)^jQ^(j(j-1)/2)|j>, H_n|j>=D_n(j)|j>/F_j. Then the exact frames are n=H_n T H_n^(-1), u_Z=D_n T D_n^(-1), w=lambda T, H_n=phi_N^(-1)D_nF_Z. (18) D_n is a unitary linear/quadratic Gaussian at unit marks. T is the literal strict compression of a unit shift; its missing Fourier/Hardy endpoint is exactly the projector in (11), not a new boundary convention. For unit S_2 all these cores have norm at most one. Their inverses as Euler operators use the opposite root/orientation, retaining its phase. For each Euler polynomial in a contractive core use the exact circle-minus-radial operator P_epsilon(T)=B_epsilon(T)-E_epsilon(T) of the modular-circle theorem. For diagonal frames use (F_Z)_j=phi_N(-1)^jQ^(-j(j-1)/2) [B_+(j)-E_+(j)], (F_Z^(-1))_j=(N/phi_N)Q^(-j-1) [B_+(d-j)-E_+(d-j)]. (19) All phases and the factors phi_N,N are retained. For example P(-nH)=P^(-1)P(-nZ)P, and -nZ=H_n(-TZ)H_n^(-1), another contractive core. Equations (6), (18), and (19) therefore expand the full word (9) into finitely many explicit Phi/Gaussian integrals and their original coefficient cycles. Every bracket in (19), and every transfer bracket, is kept as B-E in its original order. Expanding their product includes ALL circle/radial components with their signs; no individual component is identified with the whole original scalar. The radial kernel alone has the proven harmonic or diagonal polynomial bound, while other full-Phi factors can still give an exponential period. No global domination estimate is inferred from those local bounds. The exact operator identity also transports every actual Ward current: apply the ordinary typed product rule to (8) or (9). In particular, the X-wall is QXE_0=QE_dX, whose original current is explicitly [F_tot,E_dX]=(Q^(-1)-1)mu^(-1) |d><0| tensor S_2^2. It remains in (11), (17), and (19). The other current terms are finite commutators of the displayed P, F_Z and their inverses; differentiating the exact operator word gives their equal full sum. This is not a claim of sectorwise Ward vanishing. ## 7. Scope and exact audit This provides the literal middle five-point relative operator sequence, its original R embedding, its marked full-Phi clocks, every strict projector moment, and the nonzero original cup coefficient. It is an actual finite identity at every N, including even N, with no hypothetical source replacement. To obtain a complete positive geometric tensor presentation one must still assign these framed operators to the proper oriented geometric face kernels and transport the actual relative cycle. The other two classical certificates are not declared proved by (8). A local operator equality does not give a global geometric intersection degree. Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_middle_full_phi_certificate.py The exact prime-field audit checks 27 complete/wrap families through N=10: (8), the entire original R word (9), the cut identities and every moment (17), and the original source (15)--(16). The common phi_N power is retained symbolically in those homogeneous tests; its phase and modulus were independently checked in the marked-full-Phi audit.

title: The physical THIRD five-point word with its original source
text: # The physical THIRD five-point word with its original source 28 October 2026. The THIRD certificate -partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_R) has a physical two-head realization. The construction uses the inverse of the actual shared-flag braid transport, followed by the already proved FIRST identity at the opposite root. Finite factorial reflection embeds its inverse word in the ENTIRE original crossing. All clock marks, strict cuts, scalar lines and original endpoint sources remain. This replaces the proposed use of the auxiliary vacuum pentagon for this face table. That auxiliary formula remains an exact original-R port, but its contracted source has a forced degenerate clock face. The physical construction below does not use those compressed ports. This closes the literal local operator/source certificate at the same level as FIRST and MIDDLE. It does not identify its framed factors with a positive charged geometric state or transport the original global cycle to the positive reference cycle. ## 1. The actual third flags and their useful order Keep the complete conventions of the [shared actual flags](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md): Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, T=Z_2, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), a_u=TX, n_+=e_1S_2, n_-=-e_1Z_2S_2, P_+=P_Q(n_+), M=P_Q(n_-), A=M P_+=P_Q(e_1f_2), R_0=D A, B=flip D A. The unchanged common scalar kappa is external to B and R_0; all original framing and peripheral factors are retained there. Define H=P_+^(-1)ZP_+=Z(1-n_+), R=1-(1-T)X, X_R=a_u R^(-1), Z_R=1-R(1-Z). (1) Here H is a root clock. R is a unit since ((1-T)X)^N=0. Neither is an inverse of a missing-arrow projector. In the SAME bounded homogeneous frame used by FIRST and MIDDLE, the actual THIRD tuple has columns and original right tags | Flag | Column | Right tag | | --- | --- | --- | | a | (1,0)^t | -ZS_1 | | b | (1,1-X)^t | -ZS_1 | | p | (0,1)^t | 1 | | p_1 | (1-Z,1)^t | lambda | | s_R | (1,R)^t | (-ZS_1)K_2K_1 | The fifth row is the actual total-lowering first column, as proved in [FIRST](literal_first_full_phi_certificate.md). No flag determinant has been inverted to obtain this table. At the commutative regular chart, rescaling s_R to one gives (a,b,p,p_1,s_R)=(0,1-X_R,infinity,1/(1-Z_R),1), H=X_R+Z_R-X_R Z_R. (2) The original homogeneous columns, rather than the displayed scalar reciprocals, remain the finite definitions. ## 2. Inverse actual flag transport gives the missing polarization Put a_eff=Q a_u Z^(-1), C=A^(-1)a_eff A. (3) The following are exact physical matrix identities: Z_R=A^(-1)ZA, C=H^(-1)X_R, CZ_R=QZ_R C, C^N=Z_R^N=1. (4) Thus X_R and Z_R are not renamed as a quantum torus. The actual coupled torus is C,Z_R, and its required polarization is X_R=HC, with the displayed order. There is no auxiliary compression. Here is an all-level proof of the nontrivial middle identity in (4). Use t_2,Delta,v,t_3,H_1,H_2 from the shared-flag note. Its independently proved forward relations are BS_1B^(-1)=t_2, B t_2 B^(-1)=t_3, BG_1B^(-1)=H_2, t_2=F_tot+xK_tot^(-1)S_2, t_3=t_2-QDelta v^(-1). Direct multiplication of those original Gauss matrices gives H_2(1,S_1)^t=(1,t_3)^t x v. (5) For clarity, its upper-right entry is beta=e_2K_1, its lower-right entry is lambda+t_2 beta, and its upper row on (1,S_1) is x v. The second component is consequently t_2 x v-lambda Delta, which is the second component in (5). The rank-one expression for G_1-lambda and G_1^(-1) gives G_1^(-1)(1,t_2)^t=(1,t_0)^t lambda^(-1)QH, t_0=S_1+Q^(-1)Delta H^(-1)=xS_2H^(-1). (6) The first tag in (6) follows by expanding 1-lambda^(-1)e_1Delta=QH. Its last equality follows from S_1H+Q^(-1)Delta=xS_2; S_2 commutes with H. Conjugating the ENTIRE column (6) by B and using (5) proves B^(-1)S_1B=xS_2H^(-1). (7) Both first tags are units. No uniqueness of a nilpotent eigenline is presumed. Because B preserves the original F_tot and K_tot, the formula for t_2 also gives B^(-1)S_2B=x^(-1)K_tot(S_1-F_tot). (8) Cartan and flip conjugation give, with x^2=Q^(-1), flip D a_eff D^(-1) flip=X^(-1). Hence C=B^(-1)X^(-1)B. Substitute (7)--(8), together with S_1-F_tot=RZS_1, K_tot=x^2 Z^(-1)T^(-1), [K_tot,R]=0. In order, this gives C=H^(-1)X Z^(-1)R^(-1)K_tot^(-1) =H^(-1)TXR^(-1)=H^(-1)X_R, proving the missing polarization identity without a finite-level guess. For the first identity in (4), A=P_Q(e_1f_2) and the Euler recurrence give A^(-1)ZA=Z(1-e_1f_2). The actual relation Z e_1f_2=-(1-T)X(1-Z) identifies this with (1). Finally a_eff Z=QZ a_eff and a_eff^N=1 give the last two identities in (4). Define the actual nilpotent nu=C(1-Z_R)=A^(-1)n_-A=P_+^(-1)n_-P_+. The original Euler recurrence then proves the ordered relation H=Z_R(1-nu)^(-1), X_R=HC, H=Z_R(1-C+CZ_R)^(-1). (9) All inverses in (9) exist since nu^N=0. In particular these are full coupled physical operators, not products of distinct typed ports. ## 3. All five actual face arguments The permutation (a,b,p,p_1,s_R) -> (a,s_R,b,p_1,p) is even. Computing determinants of the columns in Section 1 gives the following table, with c_cl=C and t_cl=Z_R at the classical symbol: | Omitted position in (a,s_R,b,p_1,p) | Cross-ratio | Sign in -partial | | --- | --- | --- | | a | g=1-C+CZ_R=Z_R/H | - | | s_R | g/Z_R=1/H | + | | b | 1/Z_R | - | | p_1 | (1-1/C)/Z_R | + | | p | 1-1/C | - | These are EXACTLY the FIRST table with parameters C,Z_R, on this evenly reordered ACTUAL third configuration. The calculation uses the specified five flags, not equality of two arbitrary zero Bloch sums. Put at this classical chart nu=C(1-Z_R), y=-CZ_R/(1-C). The table's signed sum is -partial_THIRD=[nu]-[H]+[Z_R]-[y]-[C]. (10) Its explicit remaining quad relations are y/(y-1)=X_R, nu/(nu-1)=1-H/Z_R. Thus (10) is also -[1-H/Z_R]-[H]+[Z_R]+[X_R]-[C]. (11) For comparison, the original THIRD order has cross-ratios (1/nu, 1/(1-Z_R), C, X_R, H). Expansion of its negative alternating boundary gives exactly (11). The cross-ratios and both quads are checked independently by symbolic determinants in the accompanying audit. ## 4. Opposite-root FIRST on the physical transported clock Set r=Q^(-1). Its original finite Euler function is P_r; this is not a replacement invariant. It is an explicit auxiliary factor inside the following identity for the original P_Q crossing. Let E_Q(Z_R) denote the actual spectral projector at Z_R=Q, transported by the SAME A in (4). Put c_3=C(1-E_Q(Z_R)), a_3=c_3(1-rZ_R)=C(1-rZ_R)=C^(-1)nu C. (12) Then c_3Z_R=r^(-1)Z_Rc_3 and c_3^N=a_3^N=0. The missing arrow is at Z_R=Q, not Z_R=1. The inverse-root clock index is j_new=-j modulo N, so that this is precisely its top index d. Keep the actual negative-orientation full function and scalar phi_-=conjugate(phi_+), phi_+=sqrt(N)exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}, F_3=[marked Psi_-(r Z_R)]^(-1). In the transported clock frame its value at old index j is F_3(j)=phi_-^(-1)(r;r)_((-j) mod N). (13) The logarithmic lift is -2pi*i*(j_new+1)/N. In particular the cut index j_new=d uses the regular negative TOP value -2pi*i, not the bottom zero. Consecutive factorial ratios prove F_3 c_3 F_3^(-1)=a_3. All these factors can be constructed without knowing A: use the explicit rational formulas (1), (4) for C,Z_R and the root-clock projectors E_(Q^j)(Z_R)=N^(-1)sum_k Q^(-jk)Z_R^k. Equations (3)--(4) prove which original transported clock mark those explicit factors carry; they do not define a new factor by an unknown conjugated crossing. Define P_3=P_r(c_3), H_3=P_3^(-1)Z_RP_3, F_H3=P_3^(-1)F_3P_3, y_3=-r c_3H_3, Y_3=P_r(y_3). The independently proved FIRST identity now applies on these physical heads. In inverse-word form it is F_H3^(-1)P_3^(-1) =P_3^(-1)F_H3^(-1)Y_3. (14) The exact developed FIRST arguments before word inversion are c_3, Z_R, y_3, J_3, a_3, with J_3=Y_3^(-1)H_3Y_3=(1-a_3)^(-1)Z_R. Their classical values are precisely C,Z_R,y,H,nu of (10). At finite N one keeps J_3, a_3, their marks and their displayed q-shifts; one does not replace them by H and nu as exact matrices. Here is the exact common-port convention, including a common-output realization if preferred. For a product acting right to left, develop an argument at the right/input port by conjugating it by the inverse of all factors to its right. The left word of (14) then develops H_3 to P_3H_3P_3^(-1)=Z_R and leaves c_3 unchanged. The right word develops its three arguments to Y_3^(-1)F_H3 c_3 F_H3^(-1)Y_3=a_3, Y_3^(-1)H_3Y_3=J_3, y_3. Thus this is the forward FIRST common-left/output table read in reverse at the inverse word's right/input port. It is not the unconjugated output table of the raw inverse word. To realize the SAME table in a common-left/output frame, put W_3=P_3F_H3=F_3P_3, hat(O)=W_3 O W_3^(-1). Conjugate EACH individual factor and its current in (14) by W_3. Its total product remains exactly the original inverse word, because W_3 commutes with W_3^(-1). The framed equality is hat(F_H3^(-1)) hat(P_3^(-1)) =hat(P_3^(-1)) hat(F_H3^(-1)) hat(Y_3). (14a) The developed arguments at its common-left/output port are (Z_R,c_3) on the left and (a_3,J_3,y_3) on the right, exactly. For example hat(H_3)=Z_R, hat(c_3)=a_3, and developing the second left argument gives c_3. All W_3/W_3^(-1) face frames in (14a) are retained; no claim of a tame size or trivial action is made. There are two orientation changes in (14): the Euler/full-Psi root is r=Q^(-1), and the FIRST word is inverted and read with its original input/output face types reversed. Relative to the original h=2pi*i/N these changes cancel. Its signed face boundary is therefore the specified negative THIRD boundary (10), with the above even flag order. All inverse-word interface marks are transported from (13), not reselected independently. ## 5. Exact reflection embeds the entire word in the original R Set B_3=P_r(a_3). Nilpotent factorial reflection gives exactly P_r(t)=P_Q(Qt)^(-1)=(1-t)P_Q(t)^(-1) for every t^N=0. Indeed (r;r)_h=(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2)(Q;Q)_h, so the P_r coefficient is Q^h/(Q;Q)_h, the inverse Euler coefficient of Qt. Apply this to (12): B_3=C^(-1)(1-nu)P_Q(nu)^(-1)C, A=P_+ C B_3^(-1) C^(-1)(1-nu). (15) Here P_Q(nu)=P_+^(-1)MP_+, proving the second equality. The factor 1-nu is a compulsory original source adapter; it is not set to one. Also B_3=F_3P_3F_3^(-1)=P_3F_H3F_3^(-1). Substitution of (14) into (15) gives the COMPLETE physical THIRD refactorization R_0=D P_+ C F_3 [F_H3^(-1)P_3^(-1)] C^(-1)(1-nu) =D P_+ C F_3 [P_3^(-1)F_H3^(-1)Y_3] C^(-1)(1-nu). (16) Either bracket in (16) may equivalently be written with its fully framed factors from (14a); its product is identical. That is the common-output face version whose literal determinants were used above. There is no unstated conjugation of a single face alone. All factors are explicit original physical matrices or their specified finite Euler/full-Psi frames. The inverse actual checked crossing is obtained by inverting the ENTIRE displayed word, with the same external scalar and closing conventions. There is no auxiliary index left to suppress. ## 6. The complete source and every cut remain Keep the original p=N sum_j x^(j-d)|j,d-j> and full marker m|a,b>=x^b/N^2. In the local identity (14), its literal input and output from (16) are psi_3=C^(-1)(1-nu)p, ell_3=m flip D P_+ C F_3. (17) The ENTIRE input adapter has the useful exact cancellation C^(-1)(1-nu)=R (TX)^(-1) Z_R. (17a) Indeed C^(-1)=X_R^(-1)H=R(TX)^(-1)H and H(1-nu)=Z_R. Thus the original incoming source requires no inverse of H or R. On unit wrap marks, X,T,Z are unitary, so ||R||<=3 and ||Z_R||<=1+||R||||1-Z||<=7. Consequently the adapter in (17a) has operator norm at most 21, uniformly in N. In the original Euclidean head metric this gives ||psi_3||<=21 N^(3/2). This is a bound on the actual input adapter, not on its inverse, the outgoing factorial frame, or the entire geometric cycle comparison. Thus both sides have exactly the original normalized one-crossing source value 1. With the unstripped original crossing that value has the same original kappa line. In a longer tangle, replace p and m by its actual exteriors in (17); equality holds before any contraction. The scalar phi_- in F_3 and F_H3 is retained and cancels in the full word because those precise interfaces have opposite powers. No selected scalar is divided out. The full transported strict cut is c_3^h=C^h[1-sum_(j=1)^h E_(Q^j)(Z_R)], 0<=h<N. (18) This follows by following C's decreasing old clock indices: its deleted input is j=1, and the forbidden inputs for h arrows are exactly j=1,...,h. It includes the wrapped index-zero path and every parity. Neither the sum nor the individual projectors is deleted on source grounds. Every actual Ward current is transported by applying its ordinary typed commutator product rule to the full equality (16). Each nilpotent Euler factor in (16) has the exact original full-Psi circle-minus-radial moment realization, using the appropriate root orientation. The new clock frame is explicitly (13) transported by A and P_3. Thus all corresponding radial relative-source terms and factorial frame factors stay in the identity. This statement uses the finite matrix theorem and the already proved moment theorem; it does not replace a generalized coefficient functional by bare evaluation of Psi. The theorem is at the physical complete root for all N and all typed wrap marks mu. An off-root Hopf identity or a complete meridian-normal version of the flag table is not asserted here. ## 7. Why the earlier auxiliary port did not supply this table In [the auxiliary construction](third_region_quantum_face_extension.md), C_0=C_B|0> and rho=<0|P_0 satisfy exactly (B_aux-1)C_0=0, rho(H_0-1)=0, <0|W=<0|. Consequently its auxiliary pentagon has a face forced to one on every regular fully contracted stationary configuration. Simultaneous controlled or Gaussian similarities only transport these eigenconstraints. They do not give the generic regular THIRD configuration by multiplying its differently typed ports. That construction remains a valid exact R formula. Equations (4), (12)--(17) instead realize THIRD on the physical coupled flags and keep its true polarization and full source. ## 8. Audit and remaining geometric obligation Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_third_full_phi_certificate.py The [audit](../experiments/audit_literal_third_full_phi_certificate.py) checks all five symbolic actual face determinants, 27 level/wrap families through N=10, both inverse actual flag transports, the coupled physical coordinates, opposite-root marking, all powers of the strict cut, the inverse-word common-port developments and all individual W_3 frames, exact reflection, the full original positive and negative crossing, and the original one-crossing source. The all-level proofs above do not depend on that finite coverage. This does not make the full operator word a product of already positive charged tetrahedral kernels. Its factorial and source adapters have to be transported through the appropriate full-Phi Fourier/quad maps with their relative cycles. The three literal certificates fix the actual face/source algebra to which those maps must apply. They do not prove that the original global cycle selects the geometric reference class or its volume rate.

title: Literature definition, independent audit, and equivalence question
text: # Literature definition, independent audit, and equivalence question Current scope, 25 October 2026: The target is Kashaev's original invariant. The AK definitions audited below are comparison objects. The subsequent [direct crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) now specify the original enhanced state and its literature all-level annihilator ideal, with independent matrix, pairing and normalization proofs. No AJ or all-level holonomicity theorem is assumed merely from accepting that ideal's definition. * Use a quantum object defined in the existing literature, with its prescribed state, operator conventions, normalization and parameter regime. * Do not assume the correctness of the published proofs. Reconstruct and check the identities and analytic arguments actually needed. * Preserve the earlier custom constructions as comparison candidates. They become results about the chosen literature object only after an equivalence has been established; a common classical A-curve or volume rate is insufficient. * Retain peripheral variables and allowed boundary factors before specializing to the complete ideal point. A numerical multiplier in a specialized 2–3 comparison is not by itself an obstruction to the appropriately normalized move identity. ## 1. An existing definition to audit Andersen–Malusa, *A Geometric Quantisation view on the AJ-conjecture for the Teichmueller TQFT*, arXiv:1711.11522v3 (30 April 2024), Section 5, Definition 5, printed page 21: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.11522v3 The object is the specified Andersen–Kashaev state J^(b,N)_(M,K), and its annihilating left ideal in the q-difference algebra. The paper singles out a primitive operator of minimal shift degree when the relevant ideal is nonzero. The state and its quantum operators are described in Sections 2.1–2.3 and 5. This is not an instruction to choose a convenient solution of a naively ordered classical A-polynomial. For general knots the same source treats existence/nontriviality and the classical-symbol identification as conjectural. Those are proof obligations here, not consequences of accepting the definition. The purported statements for 4_1 and 5_2 likewise remain to be independently checked. The source and original PDF for the underlying construction are Andersen–Kashaev, *A TQFT from quantum Teichmueller theory*: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6295 . Fix a source version before transferring formulas. ## 2. Necessary checks 1. Write the exact published state integral, quantum dilogarithm, Gaussian, Haar/spectral measure, contour and peripheral multiplication/shift operators. 2. Verify the local functional equations and quantum commutators directly. 3. Verify noncommutative elimination using explicit certificates. 4. Check the passage from integrand equations to state equations: contour changes, residues, endpoint terms and parameter domains must be accounted for. 5. Establish nonzero state, minimality and the classical limit with all removable or nonremovable factors recorded. 6. For volume, establish the appropriate asymptotic for that exact normalized state. Existing claims about contour deformation, saddle selection and uniform error estimates are not assumed. The earlier computations in `quantum_a_volume.md` do not discharge these checks for the literature state. ## 3. How to test equivalence with the custom candidate Match variables first: in the classical symbol the literature Q corresponds to m^2, so its q-commutation parameter must be compared with the square of the parameter for a shift acting on m itself. Include orientations, Fourier or Gaussian conjugations and peripheral/framing changes explicitly. Then compare operators at generic q and generic peripheral variables, allowing the units or boundary factors permitted in the stated construction. For a second-order equation with coefficients a_0(X),a_1(X),a_2(X), EX=qXE, I(X)=a_0(qX)a_2(X)/(a_1(qX)a_1(X)) is invariant under multiplying the equation by a scalar function and under a scalar gauge f(X)=g(X)u(X). It is consequently a useful test for the simplest possible equivalence, including right multiplication by scalar units. It does not test equivalence by a general matrix gauge or change of polarization. Finally relate the states themselves. An operator equivalence alone does not identify a selected integration cycle, a particular solution, or an exponentially significant normalization. ## 4. Peripheral factors and the factor-eight observation The local angle-factorial test evaluated two specialized amplitudes, 1/27 and 1/216 at N=6. Its ratio 8 establishes only failure of strict equality of those bare amplitudes. A factor such as (1+M^a) is a unit near M=1 and specializes to 2. Products of such factors can produce 8. This illustrates why the numerical observation cannot decide the correct move law; it does not identify its missing factor. For each move, the calculation should retain its boundary variables and determine whether the multiplier is an allowed unit, a change of boundary trivialization, a projective scalar, a quantum-dilogarithmic factor, or a genuine anomaly. Its behavior under composition of moves must then be checked. Factors vanishing at the ideal point require separate limit analysis. Generic localization permits division by them, while the analytic germ at M=1 may not. That distinction is already visible in right factors involving Q-1 in the literature operator comparison. ## 5. Current proof status The literature definitions are starting data. No equivalence between the custom cone-normalized states and the literature state is established. No failure of topological invariance modulo allowed boundary factors has been proved by the factor-eight test. Neither publication nor matching numerical volume asymptotics is being used as a substitute for an audited proof. An initial exact algebraic check is reproducible with `python3 experiments/compare_literature_quantum_a.py`. It compares the custom figure-eight operator with the explicit candidate q P'_q obtained from equation (13) of arXiv v3. Their scalar-gauge invariants differ for generic q, although their classical invariants agree. Thus a mere scalar normalization in the same peripheral coordinates cannot identify these two operators. This does not exclude a more general intertwiner or change of polarization, and it does not assume that the candidate is the minimal annihilator of the literature state. The same calculation finds a discrepancy among the formulas **as printed in arXiv v3**: right-multiplying q P'_q by Q-1 agrees with equation (5) in the constant and quadratic shift coefficients, but its linear shift coefficient has an additional factor qQ-1. Inserting that factor into the printed equation (5) makes the asserted right-factor identity exact. This was checked against the original v3 TeX source, not inferred from PDF text extraction. The classical prefactor stated in Theorem 17 also needs reconciliation with the explicit specialization in the proof of Theorem 19. These may be typographical errors; they do not by themselves disprove the underlying construction. The journal version and any corrections must be checked before attributing the discrepancies to the final published article. ## 6. Subsequent independent proofs and exact comparisons The full derivations are in `literature_state_volume.md` and `custom_literature_equivalence.md`. 1. The Faddeev defining integral gives a uniform *complex* O(b^2) logarithmic remainder on every smaller strip |Im z|<=pi-delta, for all Re z. The proof explicitly handles the upper indentation and normalization constant. 2. On a contour through the regular ideal saddle, the exact literature figure-eight state satisfies J_b(0)=3^(-1/4) exp(-Vol(4_1)/(2 pi b^2))(1+o(1)). The contour has a fixed strip gap; the manuscript's compact-fold pole accumulation is not being passed through. 3. The v3 Ore certificate for equation (13) is exactly correct. It was expanded in the noncommutative four-generator algebra, separately from the printed equation (5) discrepancy above. The integrand equations were recovered from the defining integral, and the finite contour shifts justified near the semiclassical parameter. A local uniform saddle expansion and the nonsquare classical discriminant rule out a rational first-order annihilator. Thus the explicit second-order operator is minimal for this level-one state on its specified analytic branch. No general-level-N theorem is inferred. 4. The same remainder estimate and a negative definite real Hessian prove a volume law for the published FAMED state integral (4.5), given positive complete shapes and the finite face, edge and peripheral matrix certificates. This does not prove a quantum annihilator exists for every member of that class, nor verify blanket knot-family or census membership claims. 5. Our compact Psi_q is an exact factor of Phi_b after its second, dual compact product is included. Functional equations and the left-end normalization independently prove this equality in the convergent complex-b regime. 6. The two figure-eight companion systems are inequivalent even under rational two-by-two gauges in the same peripheral coordinates. The proof uses finite pole propagation and formal degrees at zero and infinity; a scalar invariant alone would not suffice. Changes of polarization and nonrational transforms remain separate questions. The exact generic-q factors are retained throughout. In particular the minimal operator's classical specialization contains (Q^2-1) times the geometric quadratic; those factors cannot be canceled at Q=1 without a limit analysis. The bare factor-eight observation about the different positive factorial model continues to have only the limited interpretation in Section 4 above. There is a further scalar-normalization discrepancy to reconcile in the displayed change of variables preceding equation (4.5) of the FAMED preprint: the stated Jacobian is p_1 but the displayed fiber prefactor is p_1 rather than 1/p_1. The broad volume proof explicitly fixes the printed integral; the difference is a recorded nonzero constant, not an assumed exact equality of differently normalized states. This discrepancy was also checked in the original v2 TeX source, lines 3277–3292. The N=1 dilogarithm convention was separately checked from the finite-product definition (122) of Andersen–Kashaev, arXiv:1409.1208. ## 7. General existence and the explicit twist families `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` now proves a nonzero annihilator exists for the rescaled geometric FAMED integrals in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra. Exact finite products give a common denominator with linear degree growth. A dimension count eliminates the internal multiplication variables. If the resulting operator vanishes when the internal shifts are set to 1, exponential moments extract its first nonzero Taylor coefficient. A finite restriction-of-scalars argument returns to the prescribed peripheral field. The operator of least degree then exists by skew-polynomial division. The same exact state has a locally uniform, nonzero geometric saddle asymptotic. Consequently the classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral component with explicitly recorded PSL/SL lift, inverse and factor-of-two conventions. No claim that all other classical components have been removed is made. There are two finite-b conventions that must not be identified: the natural Andersen–Malusà algebra uses q_b=exp(2pi i b^2) and a spectral shift -i b; FAMED Section 4.4 uses q_F=exp(4pi i hbar) and scaled shift +4pi i hbar. The existence theorem here is for the former action on the rescaled published integral. It does not establish the latter's conditional AJ hypothesis. Moreover the source's displayed WKB substitution for its positive shift gives exp(-H_l) from its stated potential derivative, so its inverse-longitude convention requires reconciliation before use. For 4_1 the exact conversion of the two literature state normalizations is J_F(hbar,2pi sqrt(hbar)t) = zeta_b/(2pi sqrt(hbar)) exp(pi(b+b^(-1))t) J_AM,b(t). This boundary factor changes the classical longitude root's sign. It is retained at generic peripheral value, and only then evaluated at t=0. The factor is exponentially significant at a fixed scaled boundary value. `twist_family_audit.md` reconstructs the two explicit infinite face families, their face Gaussian, the edge/face matrix identity, and positive complete geometric angle maxima by formulas valid for every fixed twist parameter. It includes a multiplier/horosphere proof that an interior angle maximum produces a complete metric. The exact finite checks rebuild edge incidences and the matrices from the face pairings for p=0,...,8 in both parities. They support the all-p formulas; they are not used as a substitute for them. A further generic-boundary discrepancy was found in arXiv:1903.09480v5: the even-family theorem prints x(x-y_U-y_W), while the derivation at TeX lines 8791–8802 gives x(y_U-y_W-x). The direct face-matrix substitution agrees with the latter. Both expressions agree at x=0. The exact state fixed for this audit is the later FAMED integral, and the final journal version of the older twist paper has not been checked for the discrepancy. The subsequent `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md` reconstructs the knot-diagram identification and independently identifies the peripheral curves by constant-size normal-curve certificates. Its meridian separates the marked-edge germs before drilling; its primitive longitude is an integral boundary in the complement, and its angular branch correction is zero. Exact diagnostics and optional Regina recognition check eighteen examples against those uniform formulas. Global exact state transformations and the extension to every alternating knot remain unfinished. The active goal is not marked complete on the basis of the state-integral criterion or the twist-family theorem for specified literature realizations. ## 8. Independent positive local move and a fiber-normalization equivalence `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md` derives the Faddeev Fourier formula from both shift equations, fixes its constant using Fourier inversion and a Fresnel asymptotic, and obtains the generic scalar Ramanujan integral from two shift identities and its residue at zero. Pole cancellation in the contour shifts is explicit. These give the bounded operator pentagon by an integrable spectral regularization. For the charged operators defined in AK (18), the resulting exact identity is T_12(a_4,c_4)T_13(a_2,c_2)T_23(a_0,c_0) =exp(pi i c_b^2 P/3)T_23(a_1,c_1)T_12(a_3,c_3), P=2(c_0+a_2+c_4)-1/2, under the full positive charge relations recorded in that note. It holds with all face boundary variables unspecialized. The charged proof is a contour translation of the scalar uncharged kernel identity; it does not treat the separately unbounded exponential charge factors as bounded. The phase and all boundary-linear terms are also checked symbolically. The same note identifies the exact factor J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2 for the FAMED fiber Jacobian convention. It is a nonzero constant normalization, so these two states have the same annihilator and volume rate. This does not silently replace the printed state: its factor is recorded throughout. The local identity can be contracted with a convergent exterior kernel or Schwartz boundary states. An explicit invertible face matrix also makes the full positive tensor contraction absolutely convergent; this supplies the gluing justification for embedded replacements of the audited operator pentagon pattern when both full face matrices are invertible. General gluing, movement outside the positive chamber, the level/framing convention, and the exact polarized fiber-state covariance still need their own checks. No generic multiplier for the different positive factorial comparison model is inferred from it. ## 9. Exact peripheral phase and state recovery `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` upgrades the magnitude relationship to the complex identity Z_AK(X,alpha)=sigma_X exp(pi i N/12+i K_X(alpha)/hbar) integral_(R+i mu) (J_printed(hbar,x)/p_1^2) exp(lambda x/(4pi hbar)) dx, sigma_X=sign(det(script-A)p_1). It derives K_X from the charged kernel and defining inversion identity, including the imaginary lift in the boundary coordinate. Choosing the published AK level ell=-4K_X/pi removes exactly that angle phase. The fiber state is then uniquely recovered by analytic continuation and Fourier–Laplace injectivity with the proved exponential tail bounds. On balanced angles K_X is affine apart from the universal term -lambda mu/(8pi). Compatible positive moves cancel this quadratic term; the remaining scalar transform law is eta exp(i(d_0+d_1 lambda)/hbar). A zero-slope certificate identifies the same state up to its recorded scalar. A nonzero slope requires an explicit meridian translation and its contour check. The slope is not silently set to zero. The generic mixed-sign phase identity is symbolic. Eighteen twist angle spaces were checked in their entirety, and pointwise quantum checks using the independently derived real-b remainder agree within 9e-15. The raw phase varies even at fixed peripheral angles in all eighteen examples. Actual move sequences, other vertex-order patterns, and the all-alternating geometric extension remain unfinished. ## 10. A calibrated connecting move for the figure-eight state `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` derives all three adjacent vertex transposition identities from the audited Fourier formula. The published Gaussian triangle kernels supply an exact S_3 action: their cyclic product has cube scalar exp(3pi i/12-pi i/4)=1. Gaussian regularization justifies their cancellation in the proper contractions used here. The note reconstructs the actual 3–2 bipyramid in the p=0 even twist triangulation. Its canonical signs are all negative, so the adjoint pentagon is required. It transports the full positive angle space and the preferred peripheral rows, which reverse both meridian and longitude. The affine phase certificate has slope zero and constant 11pi/12. An explicit orientation-preserving automorphism of the resulting two-tetrahedron triangulation also reverses both peripheral curves and has zero phase difference. Transform uniqueness proves its selected state is even. Thus, for the stated face orders and printed normalizations, J_3(hbar,x)=-exp[-pi i/12+11pi i/(12hbar)]J_2(hbar,x). The corresponding minimal order-two operator is exactly the same; its reflection multiplier is only -q^(-6)Q^(-6), and no nonmonomial peripheral factor has been removed. The exact face, angle, phase, automorphism and operator checks are reproducible. Independent two-dimensional versus one-dimensional integration agrees within 1.2e-12 in four checked cases. General connecting sequences and the all-alternating extension remain open. The further argument in Section 6.1 of `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` removes the affine phase slope for any certified positive path with compatible complete geometric endpoints. At lambda=0 the full saddle has x(y*)=0, so hbar times the logarithmic longitude derivative of its normalized transform tends to zero. Comparing the exact affine transform laws forces d_1=0. Consequently selected-state annihilator ideals and volume limits are invariant along these certified proper positive paths; no meridian translation is discarded by convention. Path existence beyond the audited components and the all-alternating geometric certificates are still required. ## 11. An independent edge theorem and a certified non-twist example `face_edge_stokes_identity.md` proves the edge rows A_ed=B_ed G for any globally branched oriented face pairing with invertible script-A. The proof constructs a face assignment from arbitrary edge values and cancels an oriented face sum. It also proves rank B_ed=N-1 for one-cusped triangulations. This sharpens the earlier finite-certificate treatment; it neither assumes nor proves that the preferred-longitude row follows automatically. The folded-layer construction in the appendix of Guéritaud--Futer, [arXiv:math/0406242](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406242), gives explicit face permutations from an R/L word. Its combinatorics have been reconstructed in `experiments/layered_two_bridge.py`. The general geometricity proof in that paper has not been adopted as an unaudited hypothesis. For the particular word RLRL, `six_three_and_two_bridge_audit.md` supplies an independent rational Rouché certificate, polynomial gluing identities, rational logarithmic-argument bounds, and a preferred-longitude cellular boundary certificate. These prove positive complete geometric and peripheral data for the specified 6_3 state and put it under our analytic volume and annihilator theorems. Optional combinatorial isomorphism checks calibrate the standard knot marking; they are kept separate from the exact geometric and preferred-longitude calculations. No claim that all canonical two-bridge triangulations are proper is used: exhaustive branching searches find singular face matrices for every compatible ordering of several such triangulations, beginning with 6_2. ## 12. Evaluating singular face contractions before extracting the state `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` evaluates the same charged kernels using independent Fourier integration. It assumes rank D=N and a surjective kernel-to-frequency matrix C; neither assumption is replaced by a presumed TQFT existence theorem. The resulting normalization is a product of three explicit Jacobians, and the residual integral is absolutely convergent. The Stokes identity extends to its allowed shape subspace. Complete horosphere decorations then identify the geometric critical point and give a volume theorem for the full reduced tensor under the displayed hypotheses. For 6_2 a separate exact certificate produces a three-variable selected meridian fiber, the complete positive algebraic shapes and logarithmic branches, the preferred-longitude cellular relation, and its entire angle-dependent tensor-to-fiber phase. Its existence and volume law follow without inverting the singular face matrix. The boundary factorization is the type used in AK v2 Conjecture 1(1); it is not the undefined specialization of the proper FAMED formula. Minimal annihilator existence uses the same Andersen--Malusà convention as before. The full intrinsic AK conjecture, including arbitrary triangulation identifications and H-triangulation limits, has not been proved by this calculation. ## 13. The Fourier rank conditions are automatic for branched knot exteriors `automatic_face_regularity.md` identifies the exact local linear obstruction with a cellular ideal edge cocycle. It then proves that the obstruction vanishes from H^1(M,boundary M)=0 for a knot exterior, using the cohomology sequence and the boundary meridian generator. This proves rank D=N and surjectivity of C uniformly, independently of the convergence assertion in AK's Theorem 7. The completed independent full-tensor volume theorem now applies to every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3. The general selected boundary state and triangulation identifications remain separate obligations. ## 14. Preferred-longitude cochains and the meridian shear Two further primary sources were located and read in this continuation: * Kambampati, [arXiv:2610.04103v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04103v1), submitted 2 October 2026, supplies a cochain construction for the preferred longitude, including singular face matrices. * Wong, [arXiv:2512.23198v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23198v1), submitted 29 December 2025, defines generalized FAMED and additional longitude--meridian conditions. Its analytic theorems are not premises of the new positive-geometry argument. `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` reconstructs the first source's local face potentials, derives its auxiliary potentials from endpoint sums, and proves closure and peripheral period matching on the dual spine. The independent local audit checks 60 potential/arc identities. A separate integer endpoint formula, checked in all 1152 ordered arc-pair cases, proves the peripheral symplectic normalization with the full factor two. The resulting rank and preferred-longitude relations are proved using these cancellations and knot-exterior cohomology, rather than adopted from the source's theorem. `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` then proves the selected-state volume law whenever the longitude increases the B rank.
