It permits a rational meridian shear, records its exact Gaussian correction and all scalar phases, and proves volume preservation by a positive-Phi saddle argument. Its exact operator action is Q -> q^beta Q E^(2beta), E -> E, with no specialization. The additional zero-shear expectation in Wong's Definition 1.5 is not used. The other affine-plane case, flat tetrahedra, arbitrary triangulation identifications and H-triangulation limits remain outside that theorem. ## 15. Inverse Fourier recovery when longitude moves the shape plane `fourier_boundary_state.md` now treats that other boundary rank, using the same charged tensor and the same AK level definition. Its Fourier and Gaussian operators are those in the A=R specialization of Section 6 of Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1409.1208v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1208v1). The particular inverse transform, measure and angle-dependent quadratic level are specified and independently derived. No new tetrahedral function or unselected recurrence solution is substituted. The inverse Fourier integral is absolutely convergent when the longitude moves the shape plane. Its extra critical equation is the meridian equation; its real Hessian is negative definite at the complete geometric point. The full small-peripheral factorization includes an explicit real level polynomial. In the ordinary-fiber case it recovers the preceding fiber/Gaussian state exactly. Thus the combined volume theorem and the independent annihilator argument apply to every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal knot triangulation. Neither extra condition (2) nor the zero-shear expectation in Wong's Definition 1.5 is needed for this tensor-derived realization. Literal equality to a different printed complex-state formula still requires matching its specified normalization. An exact six-tetrahedron 5_2 certificate realizes the additional rank case. Its algebraic shapes, logarithmic branches, preferred-longitude cellular relation and Fourier constants are independent checks. Optional Regina calibration verifies the three legal combinatorial 2--3 moves and the initial marked meridian; this does not assume a quantum state identity along them. General global triangulation identification, flat tetrahedra, all-alternating geometric realizations and H-triangulation limits remain open. This does not claim the full intrinsic AK conjecture. ## 16. Structural period torsors instead of additional knot cases The current comparison is `structural_literature_delta.md`. It explicitly marks standard local definitions, independent reconstructions and the missing global assertion. In particular the cyclic dilogarithm and its 6j interpretation are existing constructions; renaming them is not a new proof of the conjecture. `heisenberg_period_torsor.md` derives the cyclic norm equation and its determinant root as a finite Heisenberg torsor. It evaluates every finite face contraction by character orthogonality, including composite levels at which the support is not a free module. Its coisotropic quotient constructs a boundary torsor on each nondegenerate gluing chart. `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md` identifies the local Faddeev difference module with the pointed Steinberg vacuum at rational b^2. It derives two generic quantum left-ideal identities, an explicit q-factorial kernel and its determinant unit, and proves the basis-free pentagon by coassociativity. No local integral identity is needed for that algebraic coherence theorem. Published matrix conventions and their global periods still have to be matched. `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md` independently reconstructs the existing exact local rational-parameter formula, retaining its Heisenberg period and branches. Finally `bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md` proves the rational boundary wedge identity and records the Bloch period whose regulator is the volume exactly. The target is a global pointed period carrying that lift and its regulator comparison. Neither Hilbert 90 for an unpointed module nor fixed-level rigidity alone supplies the remaining comparison across quantum levels. The later `pointed_period_descent.md` proves the explicit Racah closure and its signed shared-face normalization. `affine_frame_period_transport.md` and `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` give full projective-frame covariance of those local tensors on a compatible root cover, using explicit norm-one intertwiners and a determinant rigidity argument anchored at the identity frame. Their exact audits retain the scalar before normalization; the inversion diagnostic gives 1084/925. The unit vacuum is generally transported to a nonconstant vector, so local pointed recoupling does not by itself select the global literature period. The comparison also now includes Baseilhac--Benedetti's existing [matrix dilogarithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) and [analytic character-cover families](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261v3), Theorem 1.1 and Section 4.4. The latter already describes the classical period as a parallel Chern--Simons section. Their global theorems have not been adopted as premises; their published normalizations, weights and selected periods must be compared explicitly to ours. `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md` now constructs the root multipliers around the knot from the peripheral root characters, normalizes triangle transports multiplicatively and treats the remaining scalar pentagon/equivariance discrepancy in relative group cohomology. The residual phase is evaluated on the relative fundamental class; it is not removed by field Hilbert 90. `boundary_regulator_period.md` independently derives the classical boundary connection and invariant norm, including the centering term for affine logarithmic edge constraints. It has the ordered-coordinate form of Baseilhac--Benedetti Section 4.4, equations (56)--(57), while recording that their longitude/meridian order is reversed from ours; exchanging that order dualizes the line. It also retains a possible flat unitary phase twist. Its exact regulator norm does not prove the remaining quantum comparison for the selected literature state. ## 17. The rational state as an exact relative period `rational_period_pushforward.md` gives the exact change of variables from the prescribed rational Gaussian--Faddeev class, with the source contour, Jacobian, quantum half phases and Q^n factors retained. It proves multidimensional cubical folding and a unimodular Koszul reduction, and derives the local gluing residue and its Hessian. Garoufalidis--Kashaev [1411.6062](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062), Section 2.1, is the one-dimensional methodological comparison; its global theorem is not used in higher dimensions. The source-pole criterion requires positive factors and polar coorientation; independent argument regulators can be used only with the corresponding holomorphic period germ. The Faddeev-pair diagnostic has H=-1 and a nonzero period, so open gluing solutions alone need not retain the selected period at a special parameter. Its generic moving gluing residue has a regular value at the removed polar divisor, verified independently using the defining Phi integrals. The cycle and that specialization data remain part of the comparison object.

title: Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume
text: # Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume 29 October 2026. Coverage only: primary-source definitions and theorem statements were checked. Their proofs are not inputs to our independent [factorial/normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) or [local geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md). The local 6j–hyperideal-volume relationship is established literature; no novelty is claimed for recovering it here. Our convention is zeta=exp(pi i/N), [u]=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1), integer graph spins j<=floor((N-1)/2), and four face sums>=N-1. W_N is the positive magnitude of the regularized face-normalized scalar, with [N] removed before evaluation. Its exact Casimir angles are pi-(2j+1)pi/N. The uniform result includes closed-chamber sequences and O(log N) error for log W_N; its fixed normal jets are derivatives in zeta=q exp(t), not merely coefficients in a large-N expansion. ## Closest prior statements **Costantino (2007).** Definition3.2 gives the strict hyperbolic-type conditions 1<face sum<2 and triangle deficits between0 and1. Theorem3.9 gives a simple pole and the volume growth of the regularized [n]6j coefficient. His [u] uses q^(u/2), so q_paper=zeta^2 makes the quantum integers IDENTICAL to ours. The D-block volume is twice the tetrahedron volume, matching our pi/N normalization. This already covers the interior leading rate, without an odd-level restriction; parity/composite levels alone are not a new distinction. [Definitions3.1–3.2 and Theorem3.9](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0611399v4), [published article](https://doi.org/10.2140/gt.2007.11.1831). **Chen–Murakami (2023; preprint2017).** Theorems1–2 give the volume limit when a tetrahedron has an ideal or ultra-ideal vertex and a refined Gram-determinant prefactor for specified rational-angle sequences. They take odd r, xi_r=exp(2pi i/r), q=xi_r^2 and [u]=(q^(u/2)-q^(-u/2))/(q^(1/2)-q^(-1/2)). Their scaling is spin/r=(pi-angle)/(4pi). Substituting r=2N would match our quantum integer but violates their odd-r hypothesis. Their explicit halfshift is also prior art. [Theorems1–2 and definition in§2](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.04887v3), [journal DOI](https://doi.org/10.4310/JDG/1679503803). **Belletti–Detcherry–Kalfagianni–Yang.** Theorem1.2 gives the sharp, tuple-uniform v8+O(log r/r) upper capacity for r-admissible6j symbols; AppendixTheoremA.1 states the ideal/hyperideal volume limit under explicit face/deficit conditions. Their root is exp(2pi i/r), r odd, with doubled integer colors. This is substantial overlapping coverage, but a universal v8 bound is not the same statement as our label-dependent two-sided closed-chamber volume estimate. Setting r=2N introduces the [N] poles that their odd-root evaluation avoids. [Theorem1.2,§2 and AppendixA](https://arxiv.org/html/1807.03327v2). **Belletti–Yang (2025).** Theorem1.4 covers generalized hyperbolic volume growth under a negative diagonal-cofactor hypothesis. Theorem1.5 states a refined asymptotic along sequences with fixed sides of the color wall and a limiting tetrahedron without ideal vertices. The root remains exp(2pi i/r), r odd. Their§2 records the earlier ideal/hyperideal cases as well. These results preclude presenting the local volume mechanism as new. [Theorems1.4–1.5 and§2.2](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/topo.70033), [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13864). **Costantino–Murakami (2013).** Their graph face model and6j symbols use non-integral quantum-group representations and relate them to truncated-tetrahedron volume. This is relevant background, not an identified equality with our ordinary highest-weight Hermite source. [Publisher abstract and primary paper](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/4181). ## What this bounded check establishes The verified interior local volume claim is covered, most directly by Costantino after the explicit root substitution. Our exact all-chamber O(log N) estimate, scalar generic-normal/inverse-jet bounds and retained [2N] partner current have more specific technical statements; this bounded statement check neither proves they are absent elsewhere nor supports a novelty claim. A refined large-level asymptotic is not automatically a theorem about fixed-root generic-q jets, and a lowest-nonzero Laurent coefficient is not an arbitrary prescribed source normal. None of these local statements supplies our literal marked-source normalization, a positive completed recoupling Gram, or general graph sewing/peripheral constraints. Turaev–Viro conclusions are not silently substituted for original Kashaev invariants. The full-source problem remains separate.

title: Primary-source coverage of the root-normal planar-network period
text:
# Primary-source coverage of the root-normal planar-network period 29 October 2026. This is a definitions and theorem-scope comparison only. It neither imports nor endorses the papers' proofs. No identification of our period with a named invariant is asserted from terminology or matching growth. The source object being compared is the exact period in [the original NC Morse-graph reduction](actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md): \[ q_*=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \zeta(t)=q_*e^t,\qquad Z_\Gamma= rac{C_\Gamma}{
u_N} \left.(S_\Gamma\Xi_\Gamma)'ight|_{t=0}. \] Here \(\Xi_\Gamma\) uses the specified ordinary canonical ordered 3j tensors; \(S_\Gamma\) is the explicit product of source coefficients. The labels satisfy \(0\le j_e\le(N-1)/2\). When every vertex is supported, \(\sum_{e
i v}j_e\ge N-1\), the source factors are nonzero at the root and \(\Xi_\Gamma(0)=0\). Thus this case retains a **fixed first normal**, even when that normal itself vanishes. The distinct marked-white boundary case is retained in the cited source theorem. ## Closest root-normal definition **Costantino–Guéritaud–van der Veen, _On the volume conjecture for polyhedra_, arXiv:1403.2347, §1.2.2 (Evaluation), Conjecture 1.3 and Theorem 1.4.** Their \(\operatorname{ev}_N(f)\) extracts the first **nonzero** Laurent coefficient about \(A_*=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\); for their unitary spin network, whose square is meromorphic, they extend this by a square root, up to sign. The polyhedral volume statement uses \((\pi/N)\log|\operatorname{ev}_N \langle\Gamma,c_Nangle^U|\). Theorem 1.4 establishes the stated limit for the tetrahedron-derived local-move family shown there. The paper explicitly notes that this family excludes the cube; its general-graph statement remains a conjecture, with an additional conditional result. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1403.2347). This is the closest prescription found, but it does not fix the order to one. For a regular scalar \(f\) with a simple zero, our coordinate convention gives \(\partial_t f=(A_*/2)\operatorname{ev}_N(f)\), since \(\zeta=A^2\). At a higher-order zero our first normal is zero and their extracted coefficient is not. The canonical/unitary vertex factors, their root orders, and \(C_\Gamma S_\Gamma/
u_N\) have not been equated. The earlier **Costantino, _6j-symbols, hyperbolic structures and the Volume Conjecture_**, Geometry & Topology 11 (2007), 1831–1854, likewise explicitly studies the lowest Laurent term of quantum 6j-symbols, and gives results for fundamental shadow links in connected sums of \(S^2	imes S^1\). This is additional coverage of the leading-term prescription, not an identification of every fixed-first-normal planar network. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611399). ## Named neighboring invariants | Primary definition | Exact relevant domain and comparison | |---|---| | **Yokota invariant**, in Belletti, _An upper bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant_, Definitions 2.2, 2.5, 2.7; Theorem 4.9 | Odd \(r\), \(q=e^{2\pi i/r}\), even integer colors at most \(r-2\), with triangle sum at most \(2r-4\). For a trivalent graph, \(Y_r=|\langle\Gamma,\mathrm{col}angle^U|^2\), with unitary theta evaluation 1; higher valence uses a weighted desingularization sum. No fixed root derivative occurs in this definition. Its upper-bound theorem covers graphs generated from the tetrahedron by the two specified vertex/face moves; the geometric supremum is the volume of the right-angled rectification. Under the naive identification \(r=N\), integer colors \(2j_e\) in our supported sector have sum at least \(2N-2\), outside that admissibility cutoff. Root, color and normalization changes therefore require an explicit comparison. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.01904). | | **Renormalized Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant**, Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Turaev, _Modified quantum dimensions and re-normalized link invariants_, §3, Theorem 3 | For closed colored ribbon graphs admitting an allowed simple cut color \(V\), the definition is \(F'(L)=d_J(V)\langle T_Vangle\), where \(d_J(V)=d_0S'(V,J)/S'(J,V)\) and \(d_0
e0\) is a chosen scale. This is a cut/modified-dimension prescription, including root-of-unity examples. The theorem is not a definition by a fixed first derivative of an arbitrary ordinary integral spin network. Equality would need the cut category, vertex lifts and scale matched. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4229). | | **Logarithmic knot invariant**, Jun Murakami, _From colored Jones invariants to logarithmic invariants_, introductory Theorem 1 | At \(\xi=e^{\pi i/N}\), the named invariant obeys \(\gamma_s^{(N)}= rac{\xi}{2N}\partial_q[(q-q^{-1})(V_s+V_{2N-s})]_{q=\xi}\), \(1\le s\le N\). The paper identifies \(\gamma_N^{(N)}\) with its Kashaev normalization. This is a genuine root-derivative formula, but for knots and this prescribed combination of colored Jones polynomials, rather than our arbitrary canonical 3j network with its source factors. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1287). | | **Colored-Alexander/SL(2,C) graph invariant**, Costantino–Murakami, _On SL(2,C) quantum 6j-symbols and their relation to hyperbolic volume_ | The graph invariant uses nonintegral quantum-group representations and extends a colored Alexander invariant. Its tetrahedral volume results do not, by definition alone, cover the ordinary integral-label first-normal network above. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4277). | The word “renormalized” is also used for a separate operation in Costantino, _Integrality of Kauffman brackets of trivalent graphs_: multiplying the generic bracket by explicit quantum-factorial factors to obtain an integral Laurent polynomial. That is not itself a root-normal prescription. [Primary journal definition](https://doi.org/10.4171/QT/49). ## Augmented graphs and right-angled link complements **Van der Veen, _The volume conjecture for augmented knotted trivalent graphs_, Definition 2, Definition 7 and Theorem 2.** For a fixed KTG move sequence \(\mathcal S\), the theorem supplies a threshold \(n(\mathcal S)\): each unzip must receive at least that many augmentation rings. At \(A=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\), the normalized invariant is \(\phi_N^{	heta}N^r\mathrm{sixj}_N^{t+1}\) for odd \(N\), and zero for even \(N\), where \(t\) counts triangle moves, \(r\) rings, and \(\mathrm{sixj}_N=\sum_{k=0}^{(N-1)/2}\left[ egin{matrix}(N-1)/2\ k\end{matrix}ight]^4\). Its outside has volume \((2t+2)v_8\). Normalization divides by the bracket of the \(s\)-fold unlink for **split components**, not all link components. Thus this is substantial augmented-graph/odd-\(N\) coverage, with an exact central quartic factor. It does not state coverage of every singly augmented NC Morse graph at both parities. A literal graph mapping and the prescribed normalization are still needed. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094). **Ibarra–McQuire–Purcell, _Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture: a geometric perspective_**, Theorems 2.12 and 4.15. The paper identifies octahedral fully augmented link complements with fundamental shadow-link complements, and states the Turaev–Viro volume limit for octahedral fully augmented links with no half-twists, at \(q=e^{2\pi i/r}\), odd \(r\). For \(c\) crossing circles the volume is \(2(c-1)v_8\). This covers a related geometric class and a different quantum invariant; it does not define our derivative period. [Primary journal paper](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2026/32-1p.pdf). ## Coverage conclusion Among the checked definitions, **leading Laurent evaluation**, **renormalized RT**, **logarithmic knot invariant**, and **Yokota invariant** are different prescriptions. None of the checked statements directly names or covers the entire weighted fixed-first-normal period above for every original NC Morse graph. This is not a claim that no such identification exists elsewhere. Any claimed coverage must specify the variable and normal coordinate, root order, canonical versus unitary vertex factors, color lattice, original single marked cut and framing factors, graph construction, and parity. No proof technique from these sources is used in this comparison.

title: An independent audit of literature state integrals and their volume limits
text: # An independent audit of literature state integrals and their volume limits Research note, 25 October 2026. No novelty claim is made. The definitions below come from the cited literature. The estimates, contour arguments and algebraic checks needed here are supplied separately; a published theorem is not being used as its own proof. There are three different conclusions: * For the figure-eight knot, the specified Andersen–Kashaev state has the volume limit, and the explicit second-order literature operator is its minimal annihilator over the rational q-difference field, with the qualifications about analytic continuation below. * A multivariate argument proves the volume limit for the explicit literature integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong whenever the stated finite matrix and positive geometric certificates are supplied. This includes the certified geometric FAMED class. The subsequent `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` proves existence of a minimal operator for these rescaled integrals in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra, without an efficient coefficient formula. * Neither argument proves a theorem for every alternating knot, nor establishes all the global topological identities of Teichmüller TQFT. ## 1. Fixed sources and conventions 1. Andersen–Kashaev, *A TQFT from quantum Teichmüller theory*, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), Definition 15, equation (38), and Appendix A, equations (42)–(48). 2. Andersen–Malusà, *A Geometric Quantisation view on the AJ-conjecture for the Teichmüller TQFT*, [arXiv:1711.11522v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.11522v3), Definition 5 and Section 5.1. The algebraic certificate was checked against this version's TeX source. Corrections to other printed formulas in that version are discussed in `literature_definition_audit.md`. 3. Ben Aribi–Wong, *The Andersen–Kashaev volume conjecture for FAMED geometric triangulations*, [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2), Definitions 1.1 and 2.7–2.10 and equation (4.5). Their asymptotic theorem is not assumed below. 4. Andersen–Kashaev, *Complex Quantum Chern–Simons*, [arXiv:1409.1208](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.1208), equation (122), fixes the finite-product convention for the level-N dilogarithm. Take b>0, q=exp(2 pi i b^2), and hbar = (b+b^(-1))^(-2) = b^2/(1+b^2)^2. The level-one boundary operators are Q f(x)=exp(-2 pi b x) f(x), E f(x)=f(x-i b), E Q=q Q E. Thus classical Q is m^2. All factors in Q are retained until after taking operator identities. The complete point is Q=1 in this convention; it is not an ideal point of the algebraic curve at infinity in the Culler–Shalen sense. ## 2. Quantum dilogarithm from its defining integral Start with the literature definition log Phi_b(Z) = integral_(R+i0) exp(-2 i Z w)/(4 sinh(b w) sinh(w/b) w) dw. (2.1) The contour passes above zero. It can equally be taken on a sufficiently small positive horizontal line. The exponential of this integral is holomorphic and nonzero in |Im Z|<(b+b^(-1))/2. This assertion follows from locally uniform convergence on a displaced contour, not from an asserted zero/pole formula. ### 2.1 A uniform complex remainder on an entire horizontal strip For every delta>0 there is C_delta such that, for 0<b<=1 and |Im z|<=pi-delta, log Phi_b(z/(2 pi b)) = Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i b^2) + R_b(z), sup_z |R_b(z)| <= C_delta b^2. (2.2) The logarithm is the one prescribed by (2.1), and the dilogarithm branch is analytic on |Im z|<pi and tends to zero as Re z tends to minus infinity. The supremum includes every real part of z. **Proof.** Substitute w=b t into (2.1). Subtract the leading kernel to obtain I(z)=1/4 integral_(R+i0) exp(-i z t/pi)/(t^2 sinh t) dt, K_b(t)=1/(4 t sinh t) [1/sinh(b^2 t)-1/(b^2 t)]. First evaluate I without assuming a quantum-dilogarithm asymptotic. Put J(z)=integral_(R+i0) exp(-i z t/pi)/sinh t dt. A rectangle translated upward by i pi gives (1+exp z) J(z)=-2 pi i exp z. Indeed the integrand changes by -exp z on translation, and the enclosed pole at i pi has residue -exp z. The vertical edges tend to zero for |Im z|<pi. Consequently I''(z)=-J(z)/(4 pi^2) = i exp z/(2 pi(1+exp z)). This is the second derivative of Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i). Both I and I' tend to zero as Re z tends to minus infinity: move the t contour to Im t=a, 0<a<pi, and use its exponentially decaying kernel. This fixes both integration constants. The finite-part integrals at zero are thereby fixed by the upper contour, rather than by an unspecified regularization. On the positive real axis K_b is real, and its odd continuation has residue c_b^rem=-b^2/24 at zero. Write c=c_b^rem in the following formulas; this is not the usual quantum-dilogarithm constant i(b+b^(-1))/2. Taylor expansion, uniformly for 0<b<=1, gives K_b(t)=c/t+O(b^2 t) (0<t<=1). For t>=1 use |1/sinh v-1/v|<=C v for v>0, obtaining |K_b(t)|<=C b^2 exp(-t). Define H_b(t)=K_b(t)-c exp(-t)/t. Then integral_0^infinity |H_b(t)| exp((1-delta/pi)t) dt <= C_delta b^2. The clockwise upper indentation at zero contributes -i pi c. Pairing the positive and negative halves of the real contour therefore yields the exact, ordinary convergent formula R_b(z)=-2 i [ integral_0^infinity H_b(t) sin(z t/pi) dt + c arctan(z/pi)] - i pi c. (2.3) Here integral exp(-t) sin(z t/pi)/t dt=arctan(z/pi), with the branch analytic on |Im z|<pi. This arctangent is bounded on each smaller closed strip, including as Re z tends to either infinity. The preceding weighted L1 bound controls the remaining integral uniformly on that strip. This proves (2.2). QED. Two normalization checks follow directly: R_b(0)=i pi b^2/24, R_b(z)+R_b(-z)=i pi b^2/12. (2.4) Together with Li_2(-e^z)+Li_2(-e^(-z))=-pi^2/6-z^2/2, they give the exact inversion identity, initially on the common strip, Phi_b(Z) Phi_b(-Z) = exp(i pi Z^2+i pi(b^2+b^(-2))/12). (2.5) The scalar in (2.5) has modulus one for b>0. It has not been silently discarded in an operator or state comparison. ### 2.2 Functional equation independently recovered Subtract the logarithms (2.1) at Z-i b/2 and Z+i b/2. The factor sinh(bw) cancels, leaving -1/2 integral_(R+i0) exp(-2 i b Z t)/(t sinh t) dt. Its derivative in Z is 2 pi b exp(2 pi b Z)/(1+exp(2 pi b Z)), by the same rectangle evaluation of J. Both it and log(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) vanish at the left end of the strip. Hence Phi_b(Z-i b/2) =(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) Phi_b(Z+i b/2). (2.6) The second functional equation follows by b<->b^(-1) in (2.1). Thus neither the functional equation nor the normalization in (2.2) is imported from an unchecked asymptotic theorem. ## 3. The exact literature figure-eight state Equation (38) of Andersen–Kashaev defines chi_b(x)=integral_(R-i0) Phi_b(x-y)/Phi_b(y) exp(2 pi i x(2y-x)) dy. (3.1) In the level-one convention used for the Andersen–Malusà boundary operators, J_b(x)=exp(4 pi i c_b x) chi_b(x), c_b=i(b+b^(-1))/2. (3.2) At x=0 the two states agree. Our volume theorem refers to this specified state, rather than an arbitrarily chosen solution of a difference equation. The level identification can be checked directly from the definition, not just its functional equations: the finite product (122) in *Complex Quantum Chern–Simons* has j=0,...,N-1 and argument x/sqrt(N)+(1-1/N)c_b-i b^(-1)j/N-i b{(j+n)/N}. At N=1 and n=0 it is the single factor Phi_b(x). The change n->-n in Andersen–Malusà is trivial at N=1, the Haar measure becomes ordinary Lebesgue measure, and the Gaussian is exp(pi i y^2). Their Gaussian ratio equals exp(2 pi i x(2y-x)). The algebra below also derives the operator directly from (3.1)–(3.2), so it does not need an assumed general-N identification or a general-N proof. **Theorem 3.1.** As b tends to zero through positive real values, J_b(0)=chi_b(0) = 3^(-1/4) exp(-Vol(S^3\4_1)/(2 pi b^2)) (1+o(1)). (3.3) In particular lim -2 pi b^2 log|J_b(0)| = lim -2 pi hbar log|J_b(0)| = Vol(S^3\4_1)=2 D(exp(i pi/3)). (3.4) Here D is the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm. The geometric identification is the two-regular-ideal-tetrahedron decomposition of the complete figure-eight complement; its six tetrahedral edge angles around each edge sum to 2 pi. **Proof.** Set u=2 pi b y and eta=2 pi/3. Move the contour to u=t-i eta, -infinity<t<infinity. Both u and -u remain in the fixed strip |Im u|<pi, where the defining logarithms are holomorphic and nonzero. Equation (2.2) gives chi_b(0)=1/(2 pi b) integral_R exp(F(t)/(2 pi b^2)) exp(R_b(-u)-R_b(u)) dt, F(t)=[Li_2(-exp(-u))-Li_2(-exp u)]/i. (3.5) The last exponential is 1+O(b^2), uniformly for all t. The classical action S(u)=i F(t) satisfies S'(u)=log(1+exp(-u))+log(1+exp u), S'(-i eta)=0, S''(-i eta)=-i sqrt(3). On the stated line, the sum of logarithms is the continuous logarithm of 2+2 cosh(t-i eta). For t>0 that number has negative imaginary part, since its imaginary part is -sqrt(3) sinh t. For t<0 its imaginary part is positive. It follows that Re F has its unique global maximum at t=0, with F(0)=-2 D(exp(i pi/3))=-V, F''(0)=-sqrt(3). The real derivative tends to -eta at the positive end and +eta at the negative end. Thus Re F(t)<=-V-c|t| outside a compact interval. This gives absolute convergence and uniform control of the noncompact tails. For completeness, (R-i0) in (3.1) can first be any small negative horizontal displacement. Between two strictly negative scaled heights in (-pi,0), the same tail computation is uniform; the vertical ends of the deformation vanish. This proves contour independence and then its prescribed lower boundary value. No poles are crossed in moving to the chosen line. On a small interval around zero, expand the holomorphic F to second order. Its quadratic term is real and negative. Outside that interval the strict maximum and linear tails give an exponentially smaller contribution. Scaling t=b v and dominated convergence gives integral exp(F(t)/(2 pi b^2)) dt = exp(-V/(2 pi b^2)) (2 pi b)/3^(1/4) (1+o(1)). The uniform O(b^2) quantum amplitude cannot change or cancel this nonzero leading Gaussian term. Multiplying by 1/(2 pi b) proves (3.3). QED. This is a fixed ideal geometric saddle, separated from the quantum poles by a fixed gap in scaled coordinates. It is not the shrinking compact tetrahedron fold in Section 11 of the user's manuscript. No uniform passage through that fold has been used. ## 4. Exact quantum A-operator and minimality for the figure-eight state Let I(x,y) be the integrand of (3.1), without the outside factor in (3.2). Put Q_1=exp(-2 pi b x), Q_2=exp(-2 pi b y), and let E_1,E_2 shift x,y downward by i b. From (2.6) and the elementary Gaussian shift, E_1 I=q Q_1^2 Q_2^(-2)(1+q^(-1/2)Q_1^(-1)Q_2) I, E_2 I=Q_1^(-2)(1+q^(1/2)Q_1^(-1)Q_2)^(-1) (1+q^(-1/2)Q_2^(-1))^(-1) I. (4.1) This independently verifies the local input to the literature elimination. Clearing denominators in the proper order gives exactly g_1,g_2 in the v3 source. The explicit certificate q^(9/2) Q_1^2 P=q a_1 g_1-a_2 g_2 was independently expanded in the four-generator Ore algebra. The executable certificate, including every coefficient, is `experiments/audit_ore_certificate.py`; its residual is identically zero. This check alone does not justify integrating shifts. To do that, first take b sufficiently small, x in a small neighborhood of zero in the scaled variable X=2 pi b x, and the contour used in Section 3. All the finitely many shifts in P lie in a fixed smaller holomorphic strip. The action at X=0 has strictly decaying linear tails, and these tails persist uniformly for small complex X and small contour translations. Therefore vertical boundary terms vanish. Integrating E_2^j I gives the same integral as I; E_1 can be brought outside the integral. This proves P_q(E,Q,1) chi_b=0. The shift of the outside factor in (3.2) is q times that factor. Consequently the polynomial q P_q(q^(-1)E,Q,1) annihilates J_b. In normal order it is Ahat_q=a_2(Q) E^2+a_1(Q) E+a_0(Q), a_2=q^2 Q^2(q Q^2-1), a_1=-(q^2 Q^2-1) [q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-q Q+1], a_0=q^2 Q^2(q^3 Q^2-1). (4.2) The identity holds on the just-proved nonempty parameter domain. It extends by analytic continuation wherever the same literature state and operators are continued. This last wording is deliberate: a newly chosen contour after crossing poles is not automatically the same continued state. ### 4.1 Minimality is a separate argument We now prove that the state cannot have a rational first-order annihilator. This avoids inferring minimality from the elimination output. In scaled variables X=2 pi b x, u=2 pi b y the classical exponent numerator for chi_b is S(X,u)=Li_2(-exp(X-u))-Li_2(-exp u)-X(2u-X). (4.3) The saddle at (X,u)=(0,-2 pi i/3) is nondegenerate. The implicit function theorem gives a holomorphic saddle u(X) for small complex X. The gap at the maximum, the linear tails, and the fixed strip gap in Section 3 persist in a small complex neighborhood of X=0. Deform the contour a small amount to pass through u(X). The same Gaussian argument, uniformly on compact subsets of this neighborhood, proves a nonzero leading asymptotic and therefore J_b(x-i b)/J_b(x) -> ell(Q), Q=exp(-X), (4.4) ell=exp(-partial_X S(X,u(X))). The prefactor exp(4 pi i c_b x) in (3.2) contributes q to this ratio and hence does not change (4.4). The derivative of the saddle itself does not enter, because partial_u S=0. Put Y=exp(-u(X)). Exponentiating the critical equation and evaluating the derivative in (4.4) gives Q Y^2+(Q^2+Q-1)Y+Q^2=0, ell=(Q^2+QY)/Y^2. Eliminating Y, for Q^2!=1 and then by analytic continuation, gives Q^2 ell^2-F(Q) ell+Q^2=0, F(Q)=Q^4-Q^3-2Q^2-Q+1. (4.5) Its discriminant is F(Q)^2-4Q^4 =(Q-1)^2(Q+1)^2(Q^2-3Q+1)(Q^2+Q+1), (4.6) which is not a square in C(Q). The branch ell(Q) cannot be a rational function, even though it is holomorphic locally at the complete point. Suppose (r_1(Q,q)E+r_0(Q,q))J_b=0 with rational coefficients. Clear denominators and remove their common vanishing power at q^(1/2)=1 (or q=1 when coefficients are rational in q). At least one specialized coefficient at q=1 is nonzero. Taking (4.4) would give r_1(Q,1) ell(Q)+r_0(Q,1)=0, contradicting (4.6). A nonzero order-zero annihilator is excluded by (3.3). The coefficients in (4.2) have no common nonunit factor at generic q. Thus (4.2), up to the declared Laurent units and a choice of sign, is the primitive minimal-degree operator of Definition 5 for this state. This argument is over the rational q-difference coefficient field; it does not assert new Hilbert-space domain or all-level-N results. ### 4.2 The full classical peripheral factor The exact specialization of (4.2) is Ahat_1=(Q^2-1)[Q^2 E^2-F(Q)E+Q^2]. (4.7) The primitive generic-q coefficients acquire a common factor only in the classical limit. Dividing by Q^2-1 and then setting Q=1 is not the same operation as specializing the full operator at Q=1. In particular this is a concrete example of why the user's warning about peripheral factors matters. The independently established volume statement is (3.4) for the state of this minimal operator, with its normalization fixed by (3.1)–(3.2). It does not assign a volume rate to every solution of (4.2). ## 5. A broad state-integral theorem, with explicit certificates We now use the *existing* integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong, rather than choosing a new positive integrand. The theorem below provides sufficient data that can be checked without accepting their asymptotic proof. Let X be an ordered ideal triangulation with N tetrahedra. To avoid confusing the two pairs of matrices, write script-A, script-B for face matrices and A,B for the N-by-N Neumann–Zagier matrices. Supply the following certificates: 1. script-A is invertible and the face construction gives a real symmetric Gaussian matrix Q_f. Let H=Q_f-diag((epsilon_j+1)/4), G=-2H. 2. B is invertible and the finite identity G=B^(-1)A holds. This is the matrix identity in the literature FAMED definition. 3. Positive complete shapes z_j in the upper half plane, with compatible logarithms, satisfy A Log z+B Log z''=i nu, nu in pi Z^N, and the remaining edge and meridian completeness equations. The tetrahedra are the actual geometric triangulation, so sum D(z_j)=Vol(M). 4. For the boundary coordinate of the literature integral, set p=2 B^(-1)e_N. Supply a rational constant gamma for which p^T(-Log z+i pi 1)=i pi gamma. (5.1) It can be checked directly at the geometric solution, or obtained from the symplectic peripheral certificate described below. Choose p_1!=0 by relabeling. In this notation the literature integral at its complete boundary value is J_X(hbar,0)=C_X (2 pi sqrt(hbar))^(-N) integral exp((i y^T H y+c^T y)/(2 pi hbar)) product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2 pi sqrt(hbar))) dy_2 ... dy_N, c=B^(-1)nu-G pi 1, y_1=(i pi gamma-sum_(j>=2) p_j y_j)/p_1. (5.2) Use the exact nonzero constant C_X of the chosen literature convention and the horizontal contour through y*=-Log z+i pi 1. Its imaginary coordinates all lie in (0,pi). Thus the source's angle structure can be chosen to be the actual complete geometric angle structure. **Normalization detail.** Equation (4.5) as printed has C_X=p_1/det(script-A). The displayed preceding change of variables x=p^T y-i pi gamma has Jacobian p_1, so directly disintegrating the full Lebesgue measure instead gives 1/(p_1 det(script-A)), with signs depending on orientation conventions. This constant discrepancy needs reconciliation in an exact state comparison. The subsequent `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`, Section 7.1, makes the conversion explicit: J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2, with orientations fixed consistently. This is also independent of which coordinate is eliminated when the coarea fiber form is used. For the complex identity with positive Lebesgue disintegration, the orientation sign is sign(det(script-A)p_1). The full tensor phase and its exact state-recovery formula are derived in `peripheral_phase_and_state.md`. It is present also in the v2 TeX source, lines 3277–3292; it is not a PDF extraction artifact. The theorem uses the printed integral as its fixed definition; either explicit nonzero constant has the same volume limit. No boundary-dependent or exponentially significant factor is hidden in that observation. **Theorem 5.1.** For the exact integral (5.2), with these certificates, lim_(b->0+) -2 pi hbar log|J_X(hbar,0)|=Vol(M). (5.3) The integral is nonzero for sufficiently small b. The conclusion is not conditioned on a presumed asymptotic formula or absence of cancellations. ### 5.1 Finite identities and geometric saddle The kinematical reduction requires no stationary phase: integrating delta(script-A f+script-B t) in the face variables f gives K_X(t)=|det(script-A)|^(-1) exp(2 pi i t^T Q_f t). The determinant follows from an ordinary invertible linear change of variables. Formula (2.5) converts negative and positive tetrahedral factors to the common product of Phi_b used in (5.2), with the explicit unit-modulus constants retained when reconstructing the whole partition function. The face identity G=B^(-1)A is a supplied finite matrix identity, not a consequence of calling a triangulation geometric. The subsequent `face_edge_stokes_identity.md` proves its edge rows for every globally branched triangulation with an invertible face matrix; the specified peripheral row and its completion remain separate requirements. The subsequent peripheral-phase note explicitly reconstructs those constants and the complete angle-dependent phase, rather than using the magnitude formula as a state identity. Condition (5.1) can be certified using rational matrices C,D with A D^T-B C^T=Id, B^(-1)A symmetric, 2 e_N^T(C Log z+D Log z'')=H_m+i pi nu_m. Indeed B^(-T)=D G-C, so at the complete gluing solution p^T y*=H_m+i pi nu_m -2 i e_N^T D B^(-1)nu +2 i pi e_N^T B^(-T)1. Here H_m=0 by completeness and the other coefficients give gamma explicitly. This reconstructs the step needed from the symplectic peripheral data. The existence of particular C,D can be checked as part of the certificate; their geometric interpretation is not inferred merely from invertibility of B. The classical phase of (5.2) is F_0(y)=i y^T H y+c^T y-i sum_j Li_2(-exp y_j). Its gradient is grad F_0=-i G y+c+i Log(1+exp y). At y*=-Log z+i pi 1, Log(1+exp y*)=Log z''. Hence grad F_0(y*)=i B^(-1)(A Log z+B Log z'')+B^(-1)nu=0. (5.4) This is a full critical point before restricting to the boundary fiber. For y=h+i d, direct use of the definition of the Bloch–Wigner function gives Re F_0(y)=h dot Re(grad F_0(y))+sum_j D(-exp y_j). At y*, -exp y_j*=1/z_j, and D(1/z)=-D(z). Therefore Re F_0(y*)=-sum_j D(z_j)=-Vol(M). (5.5) Only elementary identities of the dilogarithm and the checked gluing equations enter this critical-value calculation. ### 5.2 A uniform bound, the hbar/b^2 distinction, and no cancellation It would be incorrect to replace sqrt(hbar) by b inside Phi_b without accounting for the error. Put s=b^2 and define the exact classical part F_s(y)=i y^T H y+c^T y -i/(1+s)^2 sum_j Li_2(-exp((1+s)y_j)). (5.6) Since hbar/b^2=(1+s)^(-2), (2.2) gives the exact integrand representation exp(F_s(y)/(2 pi hbar)) a_b(y), a_b(y)=exp(sum_j R_b((1+s)y_j)). (5.7) On any horizontal fiber with all (1+s)Im y_j in a fixed compact subset of (0,pi), a_b=1+O(s) uniformly over all its real directions. Parametrize the boundary fiber by y=y*+T u, u in C^(N-1), where T is the real, full-column-rank matrix implementing (5.2). On a horizontal contour its real Hessian is Hess_u Re F_s = -T^T diag( Im[exp((1+s)y_j)/(1+exp((1+s)y_j))] ) T. (5.8) Every diagonal entry inside the bracket is strictly positive, because 0<(1+s)Im y_j<pi. Hence (5.8) is negative definite at every finite real point. At s=0, the complex Hessian restricted to the fiber is invertible: its Hermitian real part is negative definite. The holomorphic implicit function theorem therefore gives a critical point u_s=O(s) of the restricted F_s. The contour can be translated a small complex amount to u_s+R^(N-1); all imaginary coordinates keep a fixed strip gap. Here are the global bounds needed for this translation and for Gaussian asymptotics. On the translated contour, Re F_s has zero gradient at its critical point and is strictly concave everywhere. On the unit ball its negative Hessian has a uniform positive lower bound for sufficiently small s. Along any outward ray concavity makes the radial derivative nonincreasing. Consequently there is c>0, independent of small s, such that Re F_s(y_s+T v) <= Re F_s(y_s)-c min(|v|^2,|v|), v in R^(N-1). (5.9) The same linear tail bound, with adjusted constants, holds during the small contour translation. The quantum amplitude is uniformly bounded by (5.7). Thus all boundary faces at infinity vanish in the contour deformation, and the noncompact tails are uniformly negligible in stationary phase. The Gaussian matrix has negative definite real part. Its Gaussian integral is nonzero, with the square root of its determinant fixed by continuation from real negative definite matrices. Equations (5.7)–(5.9) therefore give J_X(hbar,0) = C_X/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)) exp(F_s(y_s)/(2 pi hbar)) /sqrt(det(-Hess_u F_s(y_s))) (1+o(1)). (5.10) In particular a cancellation between unrelated saddles has not been assumed away: the contour has a unique strict maximum, its local Gaussian is nonzero, and the rest is exponentially smaller. Since F_s(y_s)->F_0(y*) and hbar tends to zero, (5.5) and (5.10) prove (5.3). QED. The N=1 case, if applicable, is a zero-dimensional fiber and follows directly from (5.7); the determinant and Gaussian integration are then omitted. ### 5.3 What this proves about a broad knot class For every knot exterior with a supplied positive geometric FAMED triangulation and compatible peripheral certificates, the published integral (4.5) has the volume law (5.3), by the above argument. The theorem does not depend on a claimed census computation or a claimed proof that a family has these certificates. Such membership claims need their own verification. The subsequent twist-family note supplies uniform face, angle and geometric certificates for the explicit literature families. Its [topological companion](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md) reconstructs the diagrammatic identification with the named twist knots and independently identifies the meridian and preferred longitude, including their branches. General two-bridge and alternating families are not yet covered by those formulas. Menasco's checkerboard polyhedra provide combinatorics; their existence alone does not supply the positive shape solution and matrix identity in items 1–4. A claim that they are actual all-right-angled cells of the complete metric requires additional hypotheses. Theorem 5.1 is a theorem about the specified literature *state integral*. The subsequent note `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` supplies a finite dimension-count and exponential-moment proof of annihilator existence in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra for these rescaled integrals, as well as their classical geometric component. The canonical knot-state identification and the different finite-b operators of the FAMED paper remain separate questions. `twist_family_audit.md` supplies uniform geometric and matrix formulas for the two explicit twist face families; the topological companion identifies those families and their peripheral rows. Invariance of the whole state under all triangulation changes, including the correct boundary factors, also requires its own exact identities. ## 6. Reproducible diagnostics Run python3 experiments/audit_ore_certificate.py python3 experiments/check_literature_state_volume.py The first is an exact polynomial computation. The second evaluates the convergent remainder (2.3), checks (2.6) at several points, and evaluates the full quantum integrand on the contour in (3.5). For b=0.5,0.35,0.25,0.18,0.12, the scaled state exp(V/(2 pi b^2)) J_b(0) is approximately 0.6786085741, 0.7155266487, 0.7356954991, 0.7468279065, 0.7539044805, approaching 3^(-1/4)=0.7598356857. Changing Gaussian quadrature order from 128 to 256 changes the reported answers by at most 2e-11. These diagnostics support the calculations; the bounds and proofs above carry the conclusions.

title: Literal crossing-transfer Ward currents and their partial pushforward
text: # Literal crossing-transfer Ward currents and their partial pushforward Research construction, 27 October 2026. This writes the actual R intertwining identities coefficient by coefficient in the unwrapped transfer index. They give exact divergence currents and an explicit rank-one cyclic-edge source. The current identities compose under the actual tensor contractions and have a linear formal Gaussian pushforward with all inserted moments retained. No map from the scalar partially summed Gaussian block to the full matrix Ward complex is assumed here. A nonzero local cyclic-edge source is not asserted to be a nonzero selected framing cohomology class or global geometric contribution. ## 1. Actual coefficients and conventions Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. Allow two colors x_1,x_2, with M_i=-q x_i. In the balanced basis the generator entries are K_i(n)=x_i Q^(-n), f(n)=1-Q^(n+1), 0<=n<N-1, e_i(n)=M_i Q^(-n)-M_i^(-1), 1<=n<N. Outside the displayed ranges f and e_i denote zero actual matrix edges. In particular e_i(0)=0. The last absent cyclic raising edge would instead have coefficient kappa_i=M_i-M_i^(-1). Let s=+1 or -1 and let r_s(a,b,k) be the actual checked crossing coefficient from inputs (a,b) to outputs (c,d)=(b+s k,a-s k), (1.1) with the output colors x_2,x_1. Extend it by zero unless a,b are in 0,...,N-1 and s=+1: 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b), s=-1: 0<=k<=min(b,N-1-a). The explicit balanced formulas are those proved from the literal R matrices in [the actual four-plat calculation](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), Section 2. Their common full Cartan line is retained. Every Ward identity here is homogeneous in that line: removing it only while checking an equality does not change or reset its prescribed phase. Let E_a,E_b shift the indicated input index by one, and let (S h)(a,b,k)=h(a,b,k+1). These are ordinary translations of unwrapped integer indices; k is never reduced modulo N. ## 2. The four literal F and E crossing currents The actual coproducts are Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal. Checked R intertwines the input coproduct with the same coproduct in the switched color order. Taking one matrix entry gives f(a) r_s(a+1,b,k) +K_1(a)^(-1)f(b) r_s(a,b+1,k-s) =f(b+s k-1) r_s(a,b,k-s) +K_2(b+s k)^(-1)f(a-s k) r_s(a,b,k), (2.1) and K_2(b)e_1(a) r_s(a-1,b,k) +e_2(b) r_s(a,b-1,k+s) =K_1(a-s k-1)e_2(b+s k+1)r_s(a,b,k+s) +e_1(a-s k)r_s(a,b,k). (2.2) These are exact zero-extended array identities with the actual truncated edge functions. They include every corner and endpoint. For example, (2.1) has target (b+s k,a-s k+1): raising the first input gives its first term, raising the second input changes the required transfer to k-s, and the two output insertions give its right side. The same check with target (b+s k,a-s k-1) proves (2.2). This derives the formulas directly from actual matrices, not from a guessed q-hypergeometric summation identity. They may also be checked on the strict interior as rational identities of Q,x_1,x_2,Q^a,Q^b,Q^k, using the displayed proper crossing ratios. At endpoints the truncated edges, rather than unrestricted rational interpolation, specify the actual source. For an explicit independent-variable verification put A=Q^a, B=Q^b,C=Q^k. The three ratios r(a+1,b,k)/r, r(a,b+1,k)/r, r(a,b,k+1)/r are, for s=+1, BC/x_2 * (1-x_1^2/A)/(1-x_1^2 C/A), A/(x_1 C) * (1-QBC)/(1-QB), -x_2 A/(Q x_1^2 BC) * (1-QBC)(1-Qx_1^2 C/A)/(1-QC), and for s=-1, x_2/B * (1-QAC)/(1-QA), x_1/A * (1-x_2^2/B)/(1-x_2^2 C/B), (1-QAC)(1-Qx_2^2 C/B)/(x_2(1-QC)). They follow by canceling adjacent Gaussian and Pochhammer factors. Use inverse ratios at the shifted arguments for negative shifts. Dividing (2.1)--(2.2) by r then gives zero rational functions after substitution of these ratios. In (2.2) the common q^(-1) from e_i=q^(-1)(x_i^(-1)-Qx_i/Q^n) cancels. This establishes the interior identity before any root or fixed-N evaluation. ## 3. Explicit transfer divergences Define the following literal currents, including their coefficients: J_F,s=[K_1(a)^(-1)f(b)E_b-f(b+s k)] r_s, D_F,s=f(a)E_a+K_1(a)^(-1)f(b)E_b -K_2(b+s k)^(-1)f(a-s k)-f(b+s k). Then (2.1) is exactly D_F,s r_s+(S^(-s)-1)J_F,s=0. (3.1) For the raising current define J_E,s=[e_2(b)E_b^(-1) -K_1(a-s k)e_2(b+s k)] r_s, D_E,s=K_2(b)e_1(a)E_a^(-1)+e_2(b)E_b^(-1) -K_1(a-s k)e_2(b+s k)-e_1(a-s k). Then (2.2) is exactly D_E,s r_s+(S^s-1)J_E,s=0. (3.2) For instance S^s applied to the second term of J_E replaces its coefficient by K_1(a-s k-1)e_2(b+s k+1), explaining both shifted coefficients in (2.2). Operator order is as displayed. The D operators still contain internal multiplication characters. Thus summing these identities does not give a closed scalar Ward operator on the uninserted partial sum alone. The natural exact target includes the corresponding inserted moments. ## 4. The missing cyclic edge is an explicit wall source Let W=E_(N-1,0) and put Ecyc_i=Ecal_i+kappa_i W. Define the input and output two-leg cyclic coproduct matrices by the same displayed coproduct expression in their respective color orders. The actual checked matrix R_s obeys the exact equality R_s Delta_in(Ecyc)-Delta_out(Ecyc)R_s =R_s(kappa_1 W tensor K_2+kappa_2 I tensor W) -(kappa_2 W tensor K_1+kappa_1 I tensor W)R_s. (4.1) It follows by subtracting the actual Ecal intertwining equation. This is a retained boundary source, not an assertion that the original R is an intertwiner for the completed colors. If R(a,b;c,d) denotes its ordinary four-index entry, the right side is precisely kappa_1 1_(a=0) K_2(b) R(N-1,b;c,d) +kappa_2 1_(b=0) R(a,N-1;c,d) -kappa_2 1_(c=N-1) K_1(d) R(a,b;0,d) -kappa_1 1_(d=N-1) R(a,b;c,0). (4.2) Thus the wrap is a change in the actual integer conservation sector by N, with four fully specified endpoint currents. It is not a periodic reinterpretation of the transfer bounds. For equal colors this is kappa times [R_s,W tensor K+I tensor W]. At M=1 the actual and cyclic raising matrices agree, but dividing this source by the meridian gap retains a generally nonzero matrix. For the positive crossing and N>=3 one explicit entry is from input (0,N-1) to output (N-1,N-1). After factoring only the recorded common Cartan unit, its divided source is x^(-(N-1)) [x^(2-N)Q^2-1]. (4.3) At the prescribed complete x=q^(N-1), the expression in brackets is Q-1 for odd N and -Q-1 for even N. It is nonzero for N>=3. This proves a local first-normal source survives the missing-edge division. It does not prove its class is nonzero after the global framing Ward quotient or the actual cut. ## 5. Composition and the linear partial-current pushforward For equal-color b-strand braids the iterated missing-edge operator is W_tot=sum_i I^(tensor(i-1)) tensor W_i tensor K_(i+1)...K_b. For a word R_beta=R_m...R_1 the source composes by the exact rule [R_beta,W_tot] =sum_t R_m...R_(t+1)[R_t,W_tot]R_(t-1)...R_1. (5.1) Spectator terms in W_tot commute through a local crossing because it preserves the product K_iK_(i+1); the remaining terms are exactly the local currents above. Mixed colors use (4.1) with the color list switched after every crossing. Actual cups, caps and pivots contract these matrix currents with their original Hopf-adjoint rules from [the exact Ward/cut construction](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). There is an explicit linear current pushforward which is available before any open-matrix-index identification. For a finite zero- extended transverse array, or for its nondegenerate formal Gaussian realization G, translation covariance gives G[(S^v-1)J]=0, G[h(S^v-1)J]=G[(S^(-v)h-h)J]. (5.2) The first identity is finite reindexing, respectively formal Gaussian integration by parts; the second follows by translating the entire product hJ. It is valid with all rational insertions h regular on the chosen formal chart. Therefore (3.1)--(3.2) give exact Ward identities in the partially contracted inserted-moment module, with separate finite and formal realizations. For the formal one, first take the independent-variable interior identity just proved. Endpoint indicators are not assigned an unjustified formal meaning; they remain the explicit finite boundary sources to be compared. For more than one internal coordinate use the displayed vector translation v and sum the currents. The global integral flow elimination has determinant +/-1; edge current translations are consequently integral translations of the remaining independent flow coordinates, with explicit affine offsets obtained by the same closure solver. Keeping the two framing coordinates external leaves their current operators present. The Gaussian contraction kills only transverse divergences. It does not integrate either framing direction or replace the retained moment module by an unproved scalar Ward character. This is a linear map of current identities. It is not a unital map of finite matrix algebras into a scalar quantization. In particular the fixed-N matrix relation (Ad_K)^N=I must not be silently replaced by a nontrivial formal near-identity scalar action. The interior all-level proper-ratio formalization unfolds those fixed-N relations before taking H=Log Q as a formal parameter. ## 6. The exact remaining source-survival question The local Ward currents, their cyclic endpoint source, composition, and transverse linear pushforward are now specified. The full finite operator-valued Hopf-adjoint diagram also exists. What is not yet constructed is the comparison from this partially contracted inserted-current module, with its remaining external currents, to the cut Ward complex and its normal co-source. There is an exact cancellation which makes this distinction necessary. The proof that pivotal partial trace intertwines Hopf adjoints also applies to Ecyc: it has the same K-weight, and gK^(-1)=K^(-N) is central. Write C_beta=ptr(R_beta) for the actual fully closed (1,1)-tangle matrix, with its fixed scalar zero-framing line retained. It is scalar by the actual K,F Ward contraction. Hence ptr([Ecyc_tot,R_beta] K_tot^(-1)) =[Ecyc,C_beta] K^(-1)=0. Using the actual Ecal intertwining identity and (5.1), this gives the whole meridian identity ptr([W_tot,R_beta] K_tot^(-1))=0. (6.1) It first follows away from kappa=0 by canceling that nonzero scalar, then extends to M=1 through the regular whole matrix germ. Thus the ordinary full contraction of the divided cyclic-wall source is zero even when individual local matrices in (4.3) are nonzero. A surviving source class must be relative to the marked defect and its endpoints before this ordinary contraction; it cannot be inferred from local nonzero matrix entries. That map must carry the boundary source (4.2), canonical carry and the actual normal cut row. Nondegeneracy of the transverse Hessian alone does not supply it: the D operators in Section 3 visibly retain inserted internal moments. A nonzero matrix such as (4.3) can become exact or cancel after further contraction. Neither its nonzero local coefficient nor Schur normalization proves a nonzero selected global Bockstein class or a volume limit. [Exact local-current audit](../experiments/audit_local_r_ward_transfer_currents.py). [Results](../experiments/local_r_ward_transfer_currents_results.json).

title: Equality audit: positive geometric core and primitive tube completion
text: # Equality audit: positive geometric core and primitive tube completion 29 October 2026. The whole-source theorem already fixes a nonzero limit equal to the regulator of an explicit filled representation. A sharp representation-volume bound does NOT make that representation geometric. This note isolates and proves the remaining local END-completion lemma. It uses a positive geometric deformation of the compact core, not an unfilled Casson--Rivin maximum and not convergence of volumes alone. ## 1. Exact inputs needed from the original source For each fixed odd s>=25 the [whole original source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) provides a nonzero asymptotic at every independently sufficiently long fixed signed tuple p. Its constants may depend on s and that fixed tuple; there is no assertion uniform in slopes growing with N. All auxiliary colors, both root parities, the middle color, every normal jet, and the original single marked source are retained there. The [literal port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) constructs rho_z of the ACTUAL augmented-link group. It includes the right-to-left cap order, rather than a permutation of arbitrary pretzel boxes. At z=0 its complete main and auxiliary generators are the oriented four-antiprism geometric holonomy. The [preferred-peripheral certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) fixes M_i=H_i^(-1/2), lambda_i=-L_i^(-1), including the ordinary-circle spin. The [regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) then gives, at a selected filling point, source rate = Vol(rho_p). For equality with the manifold volume one needs more than the facts that rho_p kills the slope and Vol(rho_p) tends to the augmented volume. The two additional geometric inputs used below are precise: * A FIXED finite partially ideal geometric triangulation of the complete augmented manifold, every tetrahedron strictly positive. Finite face and cell centers are allowed. An arbitrary ideal topological triangulation is insufficient. * Transporting its vertex orbits by rho_z and the selected cusp flags gives a nearby positive developing triangulation with local degree one at its finite faces, edges and vertices. Equivariance and the local degree statement concern the SAME original marked manifold. The finite-center construction of this input is proved in [the geometric-core and filling theorem](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md), sections2--4. It has been independently read in full: matched face-center fans and finite cell centers give24s positive tetrahedra, exact contractible edge transitions remove both screw and cone defects, and the finite spherical links have degree one. The result below is independent of whether an all-ideal positive subdivision is available. ## 2. A compact affine link becomes an honest translation torus Consider one ideal end of such a positive developing triangulation. Its oriented link is a compact torus T. Sending the selected peripheral fixed flag to infinity identifies the link triangles with Euclidean triangles and their transitions with orientation-preserving complex similarities. Its developing map d: universal_cover(T) -> C is a local homeomorphism, including at the link vertices. Local degree one and the positive Euclidean angle sums are essential here. Suppose the peripheral affine holonomies have a common finite fixed point q. Assume d avoids q. On the simply connected cover choose f=Log(d-q). The differential df is invariant under the deck group, because an affine holonomy has d-q -> a_gamma(d-q). It is everywhere nonsingular. Thus |df|^2 (1) is a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the COMPACT torus T. It is complete. The lifted f is a local isometry from its complete simply connected Euclidean cover to C; it is a global isometry. To see this directly, lift every straight segment starting at f(x). The corresponding unit speed geodesic exists for the whole segment by completeness. This proves surjectivity and path lifting; since C is simply connected, the local isometry is a one-sheeted covering. Consequently f gives a global coordinate on the link cover. Its deck translations form a rank-two lattice Lambda={L_gamma : f(gamma x)=f(x)+L_gamma}. (2) The map pi_1(T)->Lambda is injective. Rank one or a nonzero deck element with zero period would contradict the compact flat-torus quotient. This argument controls the DEGREE of the logarithmic development, not just its local derivative. ### Why q is avoided in the selected near-complete family Choose the peripheral flag normalization continuously from the complete geometric cusp. A fixed fundamental union of link triangles has bounded developed image, uniformly near completeness. A meridian has affine form d -> a d+b, a ->1, b -> b_0!=0. When a!=1 its common finite fixed point is q=b/(1-a), so q goes to infinity. For sufficiently small deformation it misses that entire finite fundamental image. Every other developed triangle is its affine translate; the holonomy fixes q, so none of those triangles meets q either. This proves the hypothesis globally on the link cover. The selected source family approaches the base uniformly as max_i |p_i|^(-1) goes to zero. Therefore one small geometric neighborhood works for independently unequal signed sufficiently long slopes. No comparison between the different |p_i| is required. There is no genericity exception a_i=1 at a selected finite filling. Exact separate evenness gives V_i=tau_i(z)U_i holomorphically, with tau_i near its nonreal complete cusp value. If U_i=0 then V_i=0, contradicting U_i+p_iV_i=+/-2pi i. The selected logs are small, so exp(U_i)=1 also forces U_i=0. Thus every selected auxiliary meridian has a_i!=1 and the stated finite second fixed point exists. ## 3. The actual end contains a full punctured tube Translate q to zero in upper half-space coordinates (z,y), y>0. The link development now has z=exp(f). Every incident geometric tetrahedron has its chosen ideal vertex at infinity. Its faces through infinity are vertical planes. Above a bounded lower height its part over its Euclidean link triangle is therefore a vertical product. The opposite face cannot be vertical: otherwise all four vertices would lie in one hyperbolic plane and the tetrahedron would have zero volume. This works with finite as well as ideal remaining vertices. There are finitely many such pieces in a fundamental link domain and that domain avoids zero. It follows that for some finite A>0 the end contains the full equivariant epigraph y>A|z|. (3) Indeed bound every lower cutoff y_0(z)/|z| on those finitely many compact pieces; affine deck similarities multiply numerator and denominator by the same positive number. Since f is globally one-to-one onto C, the different pieces meet coherently across their side faces and do not introduce an uncounted logarithmic covering. Put r=y/|z|. Cylindrical coordinates about the vertical 0--infinity axis are R=asinh(1/r), theta=Im f, X=Re f+(1/2)log(1+r^2). The hyperbolic metric is exactly dR^2+cosh(R)^2 dX^2+sinh(R)^2 dtheta^2. (4) A link deck translation f->f+L_gamma acts by (X,theta)->(X+Re L_gamma,theta+Im L_gamma). Equation (3) says that the end contains the WHOLE region 0<R<R_0 of this tube, not merely a narrow subset tending toward its axis. ## 4. Primitive logarithmic angle is the decisive completion condition Let alpha be a primitive filled slope and choose beta so (alpha,beta) is a basis of pi_1(T)=Z^2. Suppose its ACTUAL log-link period is L_alpha=+2pi i or -2pi i. (5) Because Lambda has real rank two, Re L_beta!=0. The quotient of (4) for 0<R<R_0 therefore has one angular period exactly 2pi and one loxodromic screw generator. Adding R=0 is the ordinary smooth hyperbolic solid torus, with core length |Re L_beta|. Its meridian is exactly alpha. Either sign in (5) gives a smooth tube; it chooses the orientation of its meridian parameter, not a mirror of the positive compact core. This proves smooth filling and discreteness directly from the local metric. Killing alpha in PSL2 alone would NOT suffice. If instead L_alpha=2pi i m with |m|>1, the same construction has cone angle 2pi|m| at its core. All punctured local geometry and the killed PSL slope could still hold, but the completion would be branched rather than smooth. If L_alpha=0, injectivity of the logarithmic period map would already contradict a nonsingular compact link torus. The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) identifies the actual periods with the source logarithms, including their integer windings. In the source conventions, U_i=Log(M_i^2)=-z_i, V_i=Log(lambda_i^2) centered at completeness=-2ell_i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i m_i. The surviving charges satisfy |m_i|=1, precisely (5). The complete SL2 longitude sign is NOT used as an uncentered 2pi i contribution to V_i. The proof of the period identification must remain separate from merely checking exp(U_i+p_i V_i)=1. At the unfilled main cusp all affine multipliers are one. Its positive compact link is an ordinary complete Euclidean torus by the same flat-metric argument, and its end contains a full horoball quotient. Thus the completed filled metric has finite volume and exactly the required complete main cusp. ## 5. What follows, without assuming a character-variety uniqueness theorem Combining the positive-core input with sections2--4 yields a complete oriented hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL filled knot complement. Its holonomy is rho_p. The developing map on its complete universal cover is a local isometry to H3. Lifting geodesic segments exactly as above makes it a covering of H3; since H3 is simply connected it is a global isometry. Hence rho_p is discrete and faithful. One can compare its volume to any specified complete hyperbolic metric on the same oriented manifold without importing an additional volume- rigidity assertion. Apply the proved sharp representation-volume inequality once with each complete structure as domain and the other structure's holonomy as target. The finite fundamental chain has the same oriented degree one in both cases. The two inequalities give Vol(rho_p)=Vol(the filled hyperbolic manifold). (6) Together with the already proved whole-source asymptotic and marked regulator comparison, this is the required equality. The proof is conditional ONLY on the explicit positive-core input and the actual primitive-period certificate, both stated above; convergence of Vol(rho_p) to the augmented volume is not used as an equality argument. ## 6. Casson--Rivin and Gromov: the exact scope of the extremal argument Strict concavity of the ideal-tetrahedron volume on an affine POSITIVE angle slice gives at most one interior critical point and makes that point its global maximum. It does not by itself prove: * that a supplied topological ideal triangulation has a positive geometric realization; * that the SOURCE point lies in that same angle slice; * that the correct filling slope and its integer log angle are used; * that a locally geometric but incomplete end completes without a branching multiplicity. In particular, the UNFILLED complete-cusp angle constraints have a different maximum from a finite Dehn filling. For actual peripheral logarithms u,v the regulator variation is dV=2 sum(Re v dIm u-Re u dIm v). On a slice fixing only the rotational filling condition Im(u+p v)=constant, this becomes dV=-2 sum(Re u+p Re v)dIm v. The real filling condition Re(u+p v)=0 is therefore the relevant stationarity condition. Replacing this modified slice by the original complete-cusp slice would be incorrect. A positive all-ideal triangulation and the full-rank marked gluing rows can make this a strict-concavity proof of uniqueness; the finite-center completion above does not need that additional representation. Likewise the Gromov/representation-volume norm inequality proves only |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(M). Equality needs an actual equality certificate. Here that certificate is the complete local isometry constructed from the positive core and the primitive tube, rather than proximity of two volumes or a formal maximum principle. ## 7. A precise local-uniqueness lemma when positive ideal rows are supplied There is also a short independent local-rigidity statement. Suppose an ACTUAL positive all-ideal triangulation has t tetrahedra and c cusps, and its t-c independent edge equations together with the c specified meridian equations form a full-rank real isotropic row matrix (A B). Thus its row space is Lagrangian, not just an arbitrary selection of cleared polynomial equations. Write shape logs x_j=Log z_j and y_j=Log(1-z_j^(-1)). At the positive complete point, dy_j=tau_j dx_j, tau_j=1/(z_j-1), Im tau_j<0. The fixed-meridian gluing Jacobian A+B diag(tau_j) is invertible. If a vector a were in its kernel, (a,diag(tau)a) would lie in the complex Lagrangian kernel of (A B). Its symplectic pairing with its conjugate would be zero; multiplied by i/2 that pairing is sum_j Im(tau_j)|a_j|^2, which is strictly negative unless a=0. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem therefore gives a UNIQUE local positive shape solution for each set of small marked meridian logs. Any sufficiently close framed representation whose equivariant ideal vertices give that same positive triangulation satisfies those gluing equations and is this shape germ, up to its already specified framing. Thus no additional near-complete branch can be substituted while keeping the SAME marked geometric gluing data. This lemma neither asserts full rank for unverified rows nor obtains the source's geometric realization from an arbitrary topological triangulation. Even with this local uniqueness, the primitive-angle and end-completion arguments in sections2--4 remain necessary to identify a smooth filled manifold rather than a branched completion. ## 8. Final independent audit verdict The primitive-angle proof and the positive-core construction have now both passed independent analytical reads, and two independent readers checked sections2--5 of this note. Thus the stated geometric inputs are supplied, rather than left as formal hypotheses. The completed metric and its degree-one fundamental chain identify the source regulator with the actual hyperbolic volume for the precise long-pretzel class. The separate [Casson--Rivin presentation](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) also checks: its coisotropic first-variation formula applies to every tangent of the marked ANGLE slice, because both the actual real log vector and an arbitrary edge-angle tangent lie in E^perp. It does not assume that every such tangent solves nonlinear gluing. The factor1/2 for squared peripheral coordinates is correct, and the source's real filling equations kill the boundary derivative on the filled rotational slice. Strict concavity then gives a unique maximum. The geometric completion remains in that proof's dependency chain; the maximum alone does not identify a smooth filled end. The conclusion remains restricted to every fixed odd s>=25 and all independently sufficiently long fixed signed p_i, with the original source and normalization. It is not a conclusion for all hyperbolic knots, short fillings, or slopes growing with the quantum level.

title: Completion audit of the original-source upper-bound milestone
text: # Completion audit of the original-source upper-bound milestone **Historical intermediate audit.** The user correctly clarified that the objective is full hyperbolic-volume equality. That equality is now proved for the same class by the subsequent geometric completion and recorded in the [full equality audit](long_pretzel_volume_equality_completion_audit.md). The upper-bound audit below is retained as a proof dependency, not as a substitute for the equality objective. 29 October 2026. The milestone was to prove geometric survival OR a sharp hyperbolic-volume bound for the full original source across a broad class. The [assembled theorem](actual_long_pretzel_sharp_volume_upper_bound.md) meets the upper-bound alternative. Full volume-conjecture equality is not part of this completion claim. For every fixed odd s>=25 there exists p_s such that, for independently chosen fixed signed integers |p_i|>=p_s, the original pretzel diagram with boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)) satisfies, if its knot complement is hyperbolic, lim_N (2pi/N)log|<K>_N|=Vol(rho_p)<=Vol(S^3 minus K). The limit uses the original normalized Kashaev invariant. Both level parities and composite levels are included. The width is unbounded over the class but fixed before N tends to infinity. The slopes are also fixed before that limit; their signs and relative magnitudes are independent. There is no claim of a uniform simultaneous width/level limit, of short-slope coverage, or of all-knot coverage. ## Proof dependencies | Required step | Certificate and scope | | --- | --- | | Full original finite source and normalization | [Whole-source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), with all colors, Cartan factors, half weights and marked derivatives. The reduced invariant has the raw source's absolute value; the optional full modified convention keeps its factor i^(N+3)/N. | | Global control away from the cusp corridor | [Global alias and color gap](actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md), including ordinary colors, the even middle color and every normal term. The explicit strict width inequality holds for all odd s>=25. | | Exact complex packet and coherent Fourier filling | [Analytic color packet](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md), [endpoint and charge estimates](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), and [corridor survival](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md). These retain paired endpoint currents, the exact zero-charge cancellation and summable high-charge tails. | | Nonzero leading term for the entire source | [Full-source assembly](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md): the minimal signed charges add, all other terms have a strict gap for each fixed allowed slope tuple, and D_s(p) is nonzero. | | Representation of the actual diagram | [Local lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md) and [global port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) verify explicit matrices, group relations and every cap in the actual right-to-left composition order. | | Preferred peripheral coordinates and filled slope | [Mixed longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md): M=H^(-1/2), lambda=-L^(-1), with no unrecorded meridian shear. Commuting regular semisimple matrices satisfy C P^p=+/-I, so the actual primitive slope is killed in PSL2. | | Absolute orientation and regulator constant | The port theorem matches every white and shaded face at the complete anchor. The [cap-order audit](actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order_audit.md) verifies the holomorphic reversal F(zeta)=rho^2/zeta, including its joint peripheral inversion. The [marked regulator proof](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) has the same differential and absolute anchor as the developed fundamental chain. | | Augmented-to-filled representation volume | The marked regulator proof uses the controlled axis-cusp homotopy of the [general peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), then one compatible finite core-plus-solid-torus chain. Both old boundary vertices and new filling vertices use the same invariant axis. | | Upper bound by the actual filled volume | The [independent representation-volume argument](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) proves |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(K) by averaging finite regular tetrahedra. It assumes hyperbolicity of K, not faithfulness of rho or a quantum conjecture. | ## Final calibration issues and their resolution The literal cap traversal is right to left. Generic noncommuting physical boxes were checked to prevent commutativity of the special Casimir source from hiding a reversed order. The complete holomorphic reversal is orientation preserving; it jointly inverts the auxiliary meridian and longitude. The corresponding filling slope is inverted as a whole, consistently with the retained pair of signed source charges. The representation lift is constructive. It verifies the actual unrotated threaded half-twist group word, the selected peripheral eigenflag and the caps. It does not infer a canonical state graph from nodal R eigenphases or use the trace identity symmetric under U inversion to choose an orientation. No additional unproved U/Ward calibration enters the theorem. The regulator chain is the developed fundamental triangulation of the actual link complement. Its boundary pairing works for the selected semisimple auxiliary meridians. The separate unipotent five-dilogarithm coefficient identity is not being extended without proof. The spin terms cancel only in the full paired regulator, and the complete anchor fixes the absolute additive constant. ## Verification The supporting finite audits calibrate signs and densities using analytic Gaussian packets. They are not substituted for the uniform estimates for the actual source; section 4 of the whole-source theorem states their scope. The finite checks are: - `audit_actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.py`: exact port matrices, six reverse-cap families, seven complete white and both shaded face families, and twelve signed filling-spin/Hurwitz cases. - `audit_actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order.py`: seven original marked noncommuting tensor families, six full-cap families and six complete holomorphic generator/peripheral families. Finite experiments verify identities and conventions; the linked analytic arguments supply the asymptotic theorem. ## What remains beyond this milestone The upper inequality does not prove Vol(rho_p)=Vol(K). A positive geometric filling/completion argument, or another equality proof, is still needed for the full volume conjecture for this class.
