General hyperbolic or alternating knots remain outside the stated theorem. The user's Cauchy observation is exact: |bv|^2<=(bG^(-1)b^*)(v^*Gv). For the complete augmented base, [the explicit weighted Fourier metric](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md#8-the-requested-special-inner-product-is-an-explicit-fourier-norm) has polynomial dual cost, a separately proved sharp geometric energy and polynomially small normalized overlap. The filled-knot theorem above instead uses the whole-source asymptotic and its representation regulator. It does not assert a sharp metric-energy theorem for arbitrary source words.

title: Completion audit: full hyperbolic-volume equality for the original source
text: # Completion audit: full hyperbolic-volume equality for the original source 29 October 2026. The objective is EQUALITY with the actual hyperbolic volume. An upper bound alone does not satisfy it. The earlier upper-bound checkpoint is an intermediate result; this audit concerns the complete equality on the same broad class. ## 1. Statement and unchanged quantifiers For each fixed odd integer s>=25 there is P_s such that, for every independently chosen FIXED signed tuple |p_i|>=P_s, the original pretzel knot with boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)) has lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N|=Vol(S^3 minus K). The invariant and its cut normalization are the original reduced Kashaev invariant. Both parities and all composite quantum levels are included. The slopes may have different signs and arbitrarily different sizes. The width is unbounded across the class, but both it and the slopes are fixed before N tends to infinity. The threshold may depend on the fixed width. No statement for arbitrary knots, short slopes, or widths/slopes growing with N is included. The standing hyperbolicity assumption can be retained. In fact the constructed smooth complete metric proves hyperbolicity in this sufficiently long range. This strengthening is not needed to reduce or change the original equality target. ## 2. Requirements and authoritative evidence | Requirement | Evidence and conclusion | | --- | --- | | Briefly audit the essential previous ingredients | Section1 of the [Casson--Rivin equality note](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) isolates the unchanged finite source, coherent inner elimination, global color gap, exact complex packet, full endpoint/charge analysis and marked representation regulator. | | Entire original invariant, rather than a selected formal block | The [whole-source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) proves the full asymptotic with D_s(p)!=0. Its global estimate includes every auxiliary color and normal derivative; original framing factors have the verified modulus. | | Actual source-selected representation and absolute regulator | The [port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md), [preferred longitude](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) and [marked regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) give Vsrc=Vol(rho_p) on the original filled topology, with its exact peripheral sign and complete oriented anchor. | | Positive geometric realization of that representation | Sections2--4 of the [geometric completion proof](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) construct24s positive partially ideal tetrahedra from the original two polyhedra. Their equivariant deformation verifies all shared faces, exact edge return, angle winding one, spherical finite-vertex links and nonsingular compact similarity cusp links. | | Smooth primitive filling, not merely scalar slope holonomy | The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) identifies the actual geometric log periods U=-z, V=-2ell and U+pV=-2pi i m, |m|=1. Bounded finite generator paths and the escaping second fixed point exclude hidden integer log windings before multiplication by p. | | Complete degree-one geometry with no branched or covered end | Sections2--5 of the [tube proof](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md) use the compact flat log-link to obtain its entire plane development and injective period lattice. The actual epigraph is a full tube; primitive angle2pi completes smoothly. The main cusp remains a full horoball quotient. | | Casson--Rivin extremal identification | Sections2--5 of the [variational proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) put the source point inside the actual filled-slope positive angle slice. The coisotropic first variation holds for ALL angle tangents and vanishes by the source equations. Strict concavity makes this the unique global maximum, including over the boundary. | | Gromov-norm comparison reaches equality | The completed metric is on the actual oriented filled manifold. Applying the independently proved [representation-volume inequality](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) in both directions between it and the specified hyperbolic metric forces equal volumes. This does not assume that an almost-maximal volume is already maximal. | | Preserve independently signed long slopes and all levels | The source critical point is holomorphic in all inverse slopes near zero. One fixed geometric neighborhood therefore works whenever max_i|1/p_i| is sufficiently small. No ratio between slopes is bounded. The original all-level asymptotic remains unchanged. | ## 3. The actual equality chain The completed and variational proofs give lim_N (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| =Vsrc_s(p) =D(beta(rho_p)) =max_(theta in A_p) V_T(theta) =Vol(S^3 minus K). Here A_p uses the filled rotational constraints Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=-2pi, not the complete UNFILLED cusp constraints. At the source point ReU_i+p_iReV_i=0, so for every tangent of A_p, dV_T=(1/2)sum_i ReV_i d(ImU_i+p_iImV_i)=0. The main cusp term is zero because its peripheral image is parabolic. The negative tetrahedral Hessian is positive definite with determinant1. Thus the source is the unique constrained maximizer. The separate primitive tube proof ensures that this maximum is realized on the actual smoothly filled knot, rather than on a branched local structure. For the customary all-ideal angle presentation, the prior audited positive ideal-subdivision input is used. The independent finite-center metric completion proves the final geometric equality without relying on that optional all-ideal presentation. These dependencies are not conflated. ## 4. Verification and limits of the checks The completion argument combines the positive core, primitive period, complete log-link tube and Casson–Rivin variation on all angle tangents. Both the source and geometric thresholds allow independently signed unequal slopes. The finite audit `experiments/audit_actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.py` checks the exact spin/angle algebra,120 signed core families,32 small-log calibrations and5 Fermi metric checks. These checks calibrate formulas; the uniform proof of smooth completion is in the notes, not inferred from those finite examples. The previous full-source audits and their precise analytical scope are recorded in the whole-source theorem and the earlier upper-bound completion audit. In particular, the new proof does not rely on any of the following insufficient substitutes: a scalar killed peripheral word; convergence of filled volumes to V_s; a positive quantum norm without survival; an arbitrary topological triangulation; or strict concavity without a verified source point in the correct constrained angle domain. The evidence establishes full equality for the class in section1. The general volume conjecture for arbitrary hyperbolic knots remains outside this theorem, rather than being declared complete by this audit.

title: The actual cut period, its flag torsor, and its classical holonomy
text: # The actual cut period, its flag torsor, and its classical holonomy Research note, 26 October 2026. This continues the [relative octahedral calculation](relative_octahedral_period.md). It identifies the global *classical critical correspondence* of the actual cut state with a framed knot representation variety, retaining the boundary vector that gives the original invariant. It also identifies a split Borel framing torsor and proves a boundary-wedge/complete-regulator rigidity statement for the crossing Bloch sum. No assertion about which critical component contributes to the finite period is made. The holonomy braid map and existence of representation-associated diagrammatic critical points have existing coverage. Section 9 records it. The proofs here are direct calculations from our fixed actual R coefficients, not imports of those papers' proofs. ## 1. An exact change of boundary vector, at every level and color Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), x=q^alpha, M=-qx as in [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Let F_a=(Q;Q)_a, 0<=a<N, psi_a=1/F_a, phi_a=F_a/N. (1.1) These coefficients are units, F_(N-1)=N, and sum_a phi_a psi_a=1. Let C_N(x) be the actual zero-framed cut operator of a knot. The previously proved intertwining and irreducibility calculation gives C_N(x)=F_N(M) I at generic color; Laurent continuation extends the matrix identity to exceptional colors. Therefore phi^t C_N(x) psi=F_N(M) (1.2) for every color, including the Kashaev color M=1. This is a bilinear algebraic pairing, with no complex conjugation. Now use the basis w_a=v_a/F_a. A matrix transforms by D^(-1)CD, where D=diag(1/F_a). In this basis psi is the constant vector 1 and phi is the normalized averaging functional (1/N)sum_a. Equation (1.2) becomes F_N(M)=(1/N) sum_(a,b) (C_N^new(x))_(a,b). (1.3) This is an exact presentation of the existing invariant. It is useful because its boundary vector has a simple geometric flag, without fixing a state coordinate to its endpoint a=0. ## 2. The actual relative meridian module in that basis Let A be multiplication by Q^a on functions of a modulo N, and let sigma f(A)=f(QA). Let e_partial be the idempotent supported at a=N-1. The actual conjugated quantum-group matrices are K=x A^(-1), F=(1-A)sigma^(-1), rho^2 E=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-x A^(-1))sigma -c(x)e_partial sigma, c(x)=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-Qx) =q^(-1)x^(-1)(1-M^2). (2.1) For F the coefficient at a=0 vanishes, so the cyclic formula already has the actual nilpotent endpoint. For E, cancellation of the adjacent factorials gives rho^2 E_(a,a+1)=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-xQ^(-a)), a<N-1. The cyclic formula would add the entry from 0 to N-1 with coefficient c(x). Subtracting it gives precisely the actual truncated E. This proves (2.1), including its exceptional row. Write E_cyc for the operator in (2.1) before subtracting this rank-one term. Multiplication around its orbit gives (rho^2 E_cyc)^N=(x^N-x^(-N))I, (rho^2 E)^N=0. (2.2) Indeed the product for the first operator is q^(-N)x^(-N)(1-x^(2N))=x^N-x^(-N). At M=1 the wall coefficient c and the central defect both vanish, and the cyclic and actual E operators agree. Away from that point E_cyc is a comparison module; replacing E by E_cyc in the knot contraction has not been justified and is not done here. The full modified dimension now has another exact interpretation: d_N(M)=q^(N(1-N)/2) c(x)/(x^N-x^(-N)) =i^(N+3) M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). (2.3) To prove it, use qx-(qx)^(-1)=-c(x) in the defining modified-dimension formula. Thus the full meridian factor is a specified phase times the ratio of a local boundary defect to the cyclic central defect. At M=1 evaluate their whole ratio, giving d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N. The two zeros must not be evaluated separately. This agrees with the missing-transition calculation in the preceding note; it retains its full peripheral function. This is the local color representation, with its internal state-index wall. Turning that wall into a specified global inhomogeneous meridian A-equation requires elimination with the source retained. That identification is not assumed here. ## 3. Crossing Bloch sums change by a boundary coboundary For a crossing with input indices a,b and output indices c,d, the basis change gives exactly r_new=F_c F_d r_old/(F_a F_b). (3.1) For the positive crossing c=b+k,d=a-k, put A=Q^a, B=Q^b,C=Q^k,X=x^2. Its non-Gaussian finite product is now F_(b+k)/(F_b F_k) * (QX/A;Q)_k. Its five-dilogarithm symbol is beta_+=[B]+[C]+[X/A]-[BC]-[XC/A]. (3.2) The Gaussian and sign in the preceding note are unchanged. For the inverse crossing c=b-k,d=a+k the product and symbol are F_(a+k)/(F_a F_k) * (QX/B;Q)_k, beta_-=[A]+[C]+[X/B]-[AC]-[XC/B]. (3.3) The difference between either new symbol and the old one is [A]+[B]-[U]-[V], U=Q^c,V=Q^d. (3.4) It cancels on each shared strand of a finite contraction. The cut vector and covector transform at the remaining endpoints as in Section 1. Thus this basis change does not lose a global period or insert an unspecified normalization. Both (3.2) and (3.3) have the form [u]+[v]+[w]-[uv]-[vw]. (3.5) They have the five ordered tetrahedron shapes v, u, 1/(uv), w, 1/(vw), with ideal vertices infinity,0,1,v,uv, v(1-w)/(1-vw), by the previous cross-ratio proof. The positive case uses (u,v,w)=(B,C,X/A); the negative uses (A,C,X/B). The inverse orientation is consistent: substituting (A,B,C)->(B/C,AC,1/C) in beta_+ gives -beta_- by [1/C]=-[C]. No additional negative sign is inserted in the negative coefficient's already computed symbol. ## 4. Deriving the rational crossing map from the actual symbols For clarity, derive it first in the old basis. Its physical coordinates do not change with (3.1). Let p,r denote the classical eigenvalues of the input Q-shifts and put P(A)=(1-A)(1-x^2/A)/x, K_1=x/A, e_1=P(A)p, f_1=p^(-1), K_2=x/B, e_2=P(B)r, f_2=r^(-1). (4.1) These are the commuting symbols of K,rho^2 E,F. They obey K_i+K_i^(-1)+e_i f_i=x+x^(-1). (4.2) In the new basis, the same coordinates are K=x/A, e=(1-x^2/A)p_new/x, f=(1-A)/p_new, p_new=(1-A)p. (4.3) Let S be the positive generating expression G_++Phi already derived from the actual R coefficient. Its output coordinates are U=BC,V=A/C. The canonical relation on the constraint UV=AB is exp(S_a)=p_out,2/p, exp(S_b)=p_out,1/r, exp(S_c)=p_out,1/p_out,2. (4.4) Here derivatives are in log A,log B,log C. Substitution of the exact contiguity symbols gives p_out,1=Ar/(Cx), p_out,2=(BC/x)*(1-A)(1-x^2/A) /((1-A/C)(1-x^2C/A))*p, C=1/(1-e_1 f_2). (4.5) The last equality follows on cancelling the common factors in the third equation of (4.4); equivalently r(C-1)=C P(A)p. It is not a guessed holonomy map. Write d=1-e_1 f_2. In physical coordinates the resulting map R is K'_1=K_2 d, K'_2=K_1/d, f'_1=K_1 f_2/d, e'_2=e_1/(K_2 d), e'_1=(d e_2+e_1(dK_2-K_2^(-1)))/K_1, f'_2=K_2(d f_1+f_2(d/K_1-K_1)). (4.6) The inverse is also derived from the negative crossing symbol. Writing c=1-(K_1/K_2)e_2 f_1, it is K'_1=K_2 c, K'_2=K_1/c, e'_1=K_1 e_2, f'_2=f_1/K_2, f'_1=f_1+f_2/K_1-f_1/(K_2^2 c), e'_2=K_2 e_1+e_2-K_1^2 e_2/c. (4.7) All equations are rational identities on their specified open charts. The symbolic audit derives both (4.6) and (4.7) from their respective generating relations and checks that they compose to the identity. ## 5. A matrix proof that this is meridian holonomy Define two triangular matrices and a determinant-one matrix by b_+(K,e)=[ K e ], b_-(K,f)=[ 1 0 ], [ 0 1 ] [-Kf K ] G=b_-^(-1)b_+=[ K e ]. [ Kf K^(-1)+ef ] The crossing map satisfies three exact factorizations: b'_(+,2)b'_(+,1)=b_(+,2)b_(+,1), b'_(-,2)b'_(-,1)=b_(-,2)b_(-,1), b'_(+,2)b'_(-,1)=b_(-,2)b_(+,1). (5.1) The last follows immediately from the four simple entries of (4.6); the other two are the preserved coproducts. Direct substitution proves all three. The map also swaps the two Casimirs K+K^(-1)+ef. For two strands define H_1=G_1, H_2=b_(-,1)^(-1)G_2 b_(-,1). Equations (5.1) imply H'_2=H_1, H'_1=H_1^(-1)H_2 H_1. (5.2) For example H'_2=(b'_(-,2)b'_(-,1))^(-1)b'_(+,2)b'_(-,1) =b_(-,1)^(-1)b_(+,1)=H_1. The total product H_2H_1 is preserved, which gives the other equality. This proves the Hurwitz/Wirtinger conjugation rule by matrix multiplication. For b strands, set B_(-,j)=b_(-,j)...b_(-,1) and H_j=B_(-,j-1)^(-1)G_j B_(-,j-1). (5.3) The same calculation applies to adjacent strands; later prefix products do not change because their two factors have the same product in (5.1). Hence (5.3) intertwines every mixed braid word with the ordinary conjugation action on meridians. Composition uses the order in which the actual operator acts: rightmost factor first when a braid is written as a matrix product. The conjugation action uses that same convention. This map is birational, with an explicit inverse. Given H_j, let P_j=H_j...H_1. When its upper-left entries are nonzero put B_-(P)=[ 1 0 ], B_+(P)=[ P_11 P_12 ], [-P_21 P_11] [ 0 1 ] so P=B_-(P)^(-1)B_+(P). Recover b_(+,j)=B_+(P_j)B_+(P_(j-1))^(-1), and the analogous b_(-,j). In particular K_j=(P_j)_11/(P_(j-1))_11. This proves the inverse, rather than only counting dimensions. The braid relations now follow from (5.2). On any common regular chart these are identities of schemes, including Artin test rings; the rational identities clear to polynomial identities with unit denominators. No reducedness or isolated-critical-point assertion is needed. The actual meridians in this convention are mu_j=-H_j. Their traces are M+M^(-1), since x=-M at the classical symbol. The central minus sign preserves (5.2). The cut's unit vector p_new=1 gives f=1-A,e=(1-x^2/A)/x, and directly G (1,1)^t=x^(-1)(1,1)^t. (5.4) Thus it selects the peripheral eigenflag 1, with meridian eigenvalue M^(-1). The inverse is explicit; this flag must not be silently called the M-eigenflag when marking holonomies. ## 6. The actual cut's critical locus and a nonempty geometric chart Close strands 2,...,b by the actual pivotal trace and use the constant vector and normalized average on the first strand. For internal variables the exponentiated stationary equations are precisely equality of the closed position and momentum coordinates. At the two cut endpoints the constant boundary vectors give p_new,in=p_new,out=1. The pivotal factor on a closed strand is x^(1-N)Q^(a(N-1)). With h=Log Q, N=2pi*i/h, its leading logarithmic expression is 2pi*i(log A-log x). Its internal momentum multiplier is one. The residual writhe factor x^(w(N-1)) depends only on x. Thus these factors do not change the exponentiated internal stationary equations. Their logarithmic branches and peripheral derivatives remain part of the period. Preservation of the product of K's forces the two cut positions to agree once all the other strands have closed. Equation (4.3) then makes their physical e,f agree as well. Consequently the critical equations are exactly R_beta(z)=z, with the first meridian eigenflag equal to 1. (6.1) Conversely every point of this open fixed locus satisfies the critical equations and the cut boundary conditions. Under (5.3), (6.1) is the familiar presentation <mu_1,...,mu_b | beta(mu_j)=mu_j> of the braid-closure knot group, with the fixed eigenflag. This presentation follows by applying van Kampen to the braid strands and identifying their endpoints: at each crossing (5.2) is exactly the understrand meridian relation. Thus we have an identification of open critical schemes with framed, augmented representation schemes. This is not yet a claim about the classical symbol of a minimal *summed* meridian operator. There is a useful uniform nonemptiness result. Fix any such representation whose meridians are noncentral, and its selected meridian eigenvector w. This includes the complete hyperbolic representation. Choose a covector alpha with alpha(w)=1, then a vector v with alpha(v)=1. In the basis (v,w-v), the chosen flag is 1. For every partial product P in every stage of the finite braid word, its upper-left entry is alpha(Pv). For one strand in such a stage, e_j=0 exactly when alpha is a left eigenline of H_j. Avoid these finitely many covector lines. Also f_j=0 exactly when v is an eigenline of P_(j-1)^(-1)P_j. These matrices are conjugate to a noncentral meridian, so again there are only finitely many forbidden lines. The conditions alpha(Pv)=0 and v=w exclude finitely many additional points of the affine line alpha(v)=1. None of alpha(Pv)=0 vanishes identically there: P is invertible. One can therefore avoid all of them simultaneously. This proves that all K_j,e_j,f_j can be made nonzero at every stage, in a frame respecting the actual cut flag. The positive and negative crossing denominators then remain nonzero. Moreover all five shapes in (3.5) avoid 0 and 1: the input conditions exclude A,B in {1,x^2}, the output conditions exclude the corresponding U,V, and e_1 f_2!=0 (respectively e_2 f_1!=0) excludes C=1. This asserts nondegenerate tetrahedron shapes; it does not assert positivity or distinctness of every pair of nonadjacent developed octahedron vertices. Thus every hyperbolic knot's complete representation lies in the actual cut state's complex, exponentiated critical locus on a chart with nondegenerate tetrahedra. A chosen such frame works on a Zariski open neighborhood of the point in the augmented representation scheme. No alternatingness is needed. ## 7. The framing torsor is explicitly split Over the irreducible augmented character locus, fixing the selected flag to 1 leaves the group B_1=Stab_(PGL_2)(1), a two-dimensional split Borel group. It acts freely on framed representations because their projective centralizer is trivial. Its orbits are precisely the framed realizations of one augmented character. The full framed locus is a B_1 torsor; the regular critical chart is an open subset of that torsor. The open chart is not asserted to be preserved by every B_1 element. It can be split algebraically. For a non-elementary representation choose fixed group words g,h such that p, rho(g)p, rho(h)p are distinct. Send this ordered triple to (1,0,infinity). The unique fractional transformation is rational in its three points and gives a section on their nondegenerate locus. If necessary choose the two words so this frame is also regular in Section 6: the infinite projective orbit is Zariski dense in P^1, its square is dense in the space of pairs, and the good frames form a nonempty open subset. The words can then be held fixed near the complete character. Equivalently, over the augmented function field H^1(k,B_1)=0. After sending the flag to infinity, B_1 is G_a semidirect G_m. For a Galois cocycle, Hilbert 90 kills its multiplicative part. Its remaining additive cocycle b_gamma is killed by averaging: a=(1/|G|)sum_gamma b_gamma satisfies b_gamma=a-gamma(a). This is a proof of the splitting, not an assumed rigidity claim for the quantum period. It removes an ordinary framing torsor; it does not kill a horizontal difference-extension class or the central Bloch regulator. ## 8. A global boundary wedge and complete-frame regulator rigidity Let beta_beta be the sum of (3.2)--(3.3) over the braid, with their actual input/output variables. Work rationally in F^* tensor Q and use delta[z]=z wedge (1-z). Let S be the total classical generating expression, including the retained Gaussian factors. Write x for the common meridian coordinate, and put L_intr=exp((1/2)[partial_(Log x) S]_critical). (8.1) This is the intrinsic conjugate coordinate from the actual meridian q-shift: h=Log Q is twice its step. Initially this is on the logarithmic/root cover specified by the coefficients. The derivative in (8.1) holds internal coordinates fixed before restricting to the exponentiated critical equations; a global flattening for a critical primitive is not being assumed. No topological longitude identification is built into its name. The subsequent [exact longitude proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) now supplies that identification. Its finite meridian insertion fixes the square-root sign by an integer-position coboundary. The knot's eigenvector transport then proves that (M,L_intr), with M=-x classically, is the preferred peripheral pair on the M-eigenflag. The actual cut uses the opposite M^(-1)-flag, whose longitude eigenvalue is L_intr^(-1). There is an exact rational wedge identity on the critical locus: delta beta_beta=-2 x wedge L_intr. (8.2) Here is the proof. For one crossing, write its five shapes as monomials z_j in A,B,C,x with signs eps_j. If X_i denotes one of these four multiplicative generators, then delta beta=-sum_i X_i wedge exp(partial_i Phi). The Gaussian G has symmetric quadratic coefficient matrix in their logarithms, so sum_i X_i wedge exp(partial_i G)=0. Its constant signs are torsion and disappear rationally. Hence Phi may be replaced by S=G+Phi in this identity. The generating relations (4.4) then give exactly delta beta=A wedge p_in,1+B wedge p_in,2 -U wedge p_out,1-V wedge p_out,2 -x wedge exp(partial_(Log x) S). For the inverse crossing use U=B/C,V=AC and S_c=Log p_out,2-Log p_out,1; the same formula results. Internal leg terms cancel. Closed legs have equal positions and momenta, and the two cut momenta are 1. The last term is -2x wedge L_intr by (8.1). This proves (8.2). It is the previous boundary coefficient -1/2 in m=x^2,l=L_intr^2. The wedge alone does not fix the marked longitude. The subsequent vector-transport proof linked above fixes its flag, sign and framing. At the complete color x=-1, (8.2) is zero in the rational wedge. Thus beta_beta is a Bloch class on this critical component. Applying the directly proved Bloch--Wigner differential shows d D(beta_beta)=0 along its framing torsor. The good complex frame locus is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the connected rational group B_1, hence connected. Its regulator value is independent of the regular frame. This is an explicit classical rigidity argument for the *actual crossing* sum. The [crossing fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) now identifies this complete rational Bloch class with the marked idealized fundamental class, and hence the constant with Vol(M). It gives a three-five-term certificate, a four-tetrahedron diagram face table, and the degree-one peripheral check. This supplies the classical datum that the wedge alone did not fix. The quantum source and selected period must additionally be transported, and its exponential norm established. Existence of the critical component does not show that its period coefficient is nonzero or that other components do not cancel it. ## 9. Coverage, verification, and the remaining target Coverage checked after deriving these formulas: * [Kashaev--Reshetikhin, braiding for quantum gl_2](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410182) covers holonomy braiding at roots of unity. We reconstruct the rational map from the actual crossing symbols and prove its conjugation rule by (5.1). * [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, cyclic modules and flat connections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354) states a four-holonomy-dilogarithm factorization. It is coverage of a comparison framework, not a theorem identifying its geometric-character invariant with the original cut period. * [Cho, existence of an optimistic-limit solution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0525) covers critical equations associated with representations. The existence statement here therefore carries no novelty claim. Its boundary and meridian conventions are instead derived from (1.1)--(2.3) of the actual literature state. The [audit](../experiments/audit_marked_braid_holonomy.py) and [results](../experiments/marked_braid_holonomy_results.json) check both symbolic generating maps, their inverse, all three matrix factorizations, the exact Hurwitz rule, and the cut flag. They check 300 mixed braid words, each of length twelve, in three finite fields, together with braid relations and Gauss reconstruction. At ten levels, including even and composite ones, they check the boundary vectors, rank-one E correction, cyclic defect and nilpotency, and dimension ratio. Thirty actual cut contractions at levels 2 through 6 give the same period under the boundary/basis change. A three-field algebraic figure-eight calibration checks a nondegenerate geometric critical chart. A high-precision complex calibration checks the regulator's sign and frame independence against its two-regular- tetrahedron value in three frames. These are validations, not the general mechanism. The original volume conjecture remains the target. This note supplies an actual-state geometric critical locus, its framing torsor, and a global rational Bloch boundary formula; the next note identifies its complete fundamental-class lift. A global quantum source comparison, the minimal meridian operator's geometric classical factor, and the selected volume limit remain unproved. The subsequent [regular holonomy-braiding note](regular_holonomy_braiding.md) derives a quantum counterpart of this classical transport. It gives rational generator formulas, the full unrestricted root-center map, and a regular module/intertwiner line through the actual color. Their checked center map is the inverse map (4.7), as required by pullback. Its pointed determinant normalization preserves the original zero-framed knot period after the explicit twist compensation. A global relative gluing source and its selected regulator period remain unproved.

title: Cyclotomic Mellin functions are fixed by bounded quantum jets
text: # Cyclotomic Mellin functions are fixed by bounded quantum jets Research proof, 27 October 2026. In the actual Fourier--Mellin polarization, a bounded number of quantum jet levels fixes the whole rational root function, not only a selected scalar multiple of it. The normal-order bound is independent of N. The source, formal starting lattice and cyclotomic pole lattice are all necessary inputs. This extends the existing [bounded-jet operator-period reconstruction](all_level_a_period.md) from one coefficient to the whole rational Mellin fiber. The sparse valuation and recurrence arguments are the same ones; no novelty is claimed for them. The new scope is arbitrary competing root sections, without a rank, semisimplicity, scalar-ratio or minimality hypothesis. The result is uniqueness, not a construction of a regulator section satisfying those exact data or an estimate of its residue. In particular it does not prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The actual operator, source and pole lattice Use the specified actual Q-only color recurrence P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Y)T^j, TY=QYT, sum_j a_j(Q,Q^r) C_(r+j)(Q)=0, r>=1, with d>=1, a_0 a_d!=0, and Laurent-polynomial coefficients after one fixed denominator clearing. Retain the actual colors, source and conventions of [the Fourier--Mellin construction](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md). Let A be the Q-exponent span, D the Y-exponent span, and s the number of collected monomials of a_d. Choose a fixed n_0>=d+A+1, B=D(s-1), k=B+1. The actual formal series and its exact source are Z(Q,X)=sum_(r>=n_0) C_r(Q) X^r, P^M Z=mathcalB(Q,X), P^M=sum_(j,ell) a_(j,ell)(Q) Q^(-ell*j) X^(-j) S^ell, S f(X)=f(QX). The Laurent polynomial mathcalB is fixed by the d actual colors C_(n_0),...,C_(n_0+d-1). Its full quantum jets are retained, rather than just its value at one root. At Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), the actual root section Z_N is rational. Let p_<(N,X)=sum_(r=1)^(n_0-1) C_r(Q_N) X^r. The exact color periodicity proved in [the cyclotomic residue theorem](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives the pole lattice (1-X^N)[Z_N(X)+p_<(N,X)] in X C[X], of degree at most N. (1) It also gives Z_N in X^(n_0)C[[X]] and K_N=Res_infinity Z_N(X)dX/X. Condition (1) is more than having simple finite cyclotomic poles: it fixes the allowed polynomial part at infinity as well. ## 2. Finite reconstruction theorem For all sufficiently large N, let W_N be a rational function with W_N in X^(n_0)C[[X]], (1-X^N)[W_N+p_<] in X C[X], degree<=N. (2) Put Q=Q_N(1+epsilon), R_k=C[epsilon]/(epsilon^k). Suppose there is a polynomial truncation Wtilde_N=sum_(r=n_0)^N w_r(epsilon)X^r, w_r in R_k, w_r(0)=[X^r]W_N, whose source equation has the correct coefficients in the finite window [X^m](P^M Wtilde_N-mathcalB)=0 in R_k, n_0-d<=m<=N-d. (3) Then exactly W_N=Z_N. In particular its residue is the original Kashaev value K_N. There are k=B+1 quantum levels in (3): orders zero through B. The number of X coefficients grows with N, but the required quantum normal order does not. No bounded X-degree is assumed for higher actual quantum jets; only the indicated finite window is used. Truncating the actual formal Z at X^N supplies one such lift, since omitted higher coefficients cannot enter that window. ### Proof Subtract that actual truncation and write its coefficients as e_r(epsilon), with e_r=0 for r<n_0. Coefficient comparison in the exact Fourier ordering gives sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Q^m)e_(m+j)=0 in R_k. (4) Indeed the factor Q^(-ell*j) in the Fourier transform cancels the j-part of the shift on the exponent m+j, leaving Q^(ell*m). No square-root or index offset is suppressed here. For r>=n_0 set h_(r-d)(Q)=a_d(Q,Q^(r-d)), mu_(r-d)=ord_(Q=Q_N) h_(r-d), M_r=sum_(t=n_0)^r mu_(t-d). All h_(r-d) are nonzero Laurent polynomials: r-d>A prevents collisions of distinct Q^uY^v monomials after Y=Q^(r-d). Each has at most s monomials, hence its nonzero-root vanishing order is at most s-1 by the logarithmic-derivative Vandermonde argument already proved in the operator-period note. The points Q_N^(r-d), n_0<=r<=N, are distinct. For all large N the Laurent polynomial a_d(Q_N,Y) is not identically zero; it has at most D nonzero roots. Thus M_N<=D(s-1)=B. (5) These statements exclude only finitely many levels of the fixed coefficient field. They do not assume regular propagation at every color. Induct in (4), with m=r-d. All earlier error coefficients are divisible by epsilon^(k-M_(r-1)). The other operator coefficients are regular in epsilon. Since h_(r-d) is a unit times epsilon^mu_(r-d), it follows that e_r in epsilon^(k-M_r) R_k. (6) This remains valid in the truncated ring: the annihilator of epsilon^mu consists of epsilon^(k-mu) multiples, with at least the divisibility claimed in (6). By (5), k-M_r>=1 through r=N. Hence every root coefficient through X^N agrees. Subtract the two pole conditions (1)--(2). The polynomial (1-X^N)(W_N-Z_N) has degree<=N, and all its coefficients through that degree are zero by (6) and the common starting lattice. It vanishes identically. This proves the theorem. ## 3. A literal unknot example shows why root data are insufficient The actual unknot has C_r(Q)=1. The following nonminimal operator is nonetheless an actual all-level annihilator: P=(T-Q)[(1-QY)T-(1-Y)] =(1-Q^2Y)T^2+(1+Q)(QY-1)T+Q(1-Y). (7) The inner bracket applied to 1 is (1-Q)Y; the outer T-Q kills it. Here D=1, s=2, so B=1 and k=2. Its exact Fourier operator and source, for any fixed admissible n_0, are P^M=X^(-2)(1-X)(1-QX)(1-S), Z(Q,X)=X^(n_0)/(1-X), mathcalB=X^(n_0-2)[1-Q^(n_0)+(Q^(n_0)-Q)X]. (8) At the root, for every constant lambda, W_N=Z_N+lambda X^N/(1-X^N) (9) has the same affine source, starting lattice, prescribed prefix and cyclotomic pole lattice. It has residue 1+lambda instead of 1. This is an alternative root section of an ACTUAL unknot operator, not a different knot invariant. No nonzero lambda in (9) has the first normal lift (3). One way to see this is (4) at m=N-2: its earlier errors are zero, and h_(N-2)=1-Q^N has a simple zero, so the first normal equation forces e_N(0)=0. There is also a whole-function obstruction, not just the coefficient argument. Write U=X^N, f(U)=lambda U/(1-U). After canceling the nonzero rational prefactor in (8), a first-order homogeneous lift would require (1-S_0)g_1=N U f'(U), S_0 g(X)=g(Q_N X). The cyclic average of its left side is zero, whereas that of its right side is N^2 U f'(U), nonzero if lambda!=0. This argument is valid in C((X)) as well as in C(X). Thus the required two jet levels are genuinely necessary in this actual example. Root operator, affine source and pole lattice by themselves do not determine the residue. ## 4. Relation to the selected-line and regulator questions [The selected Mellin-line theorem](actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.md) uses the observable source quotient to remove central scalar multipliers at first normal order, without semisimplicity. The present result also handles additions in the homogeneous source-kernel, as illustrated by (9); it uses the larger fixed jet budget and the exact cyclotomic pole lattice. The theorem gives a finite exact target for a proposed whole comparison. Such a candidate still must supply (2)--(3), with the actual source and coefficients through the stated orders. An algebraic classical optimizer or a local geometric Gaussian does not yet supply that lift or its global pole behavior. No hyperbolic-volume growth follows from uniqueness alone. Verification: [script](../experiments/audit_mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.py) and [results](../experiments/mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness_results.json). The [independent proof audit](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness_independent_audit.md) checks the finite Fourier window, truncated-ring valuation induction, pole numerator reconstruction and sharp actual unknot obstruction.

title: Independent audit of bounded-jet cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness
text:
# Independent audit of bounded-jet cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness 27 October 2026. The proof of [the whole-function uniqueness theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) passes independently. Its finite X-window, uniform quantum-jet budget, and cyclotomic numerator condition are sufficient as written. No semisimplicity, minimal operator, or scalar-ratio hypothesis is needed. ## 1. The finite window really is closed In the exact Fourier ordering, a monomial \(X^{-j}S^\ell\) takes the coefficient \(w_{m+j}\) to power \(X^m\), with factor \(Q^{\ell m}\) after the retained \(Q^{-\ell j}\). Since \(0\le j\le d\) and \(m\le N-d\), only coefficients through \(w_N\) enter. Hence a truncation at \(X^N\) is enough for the entire indicated window. Negative S-powers cause no change to this statement: they rescale the same X exponent. Subtracting the actual truncation therefore gives precisely \[ \sum_{j=0}^d a_j(Q,Q^m)e_{m+j}=0 \quad mod\epsilon^{B+1}. \] The starting lattice sets every \(e_r\) below \(n_0\) to zero. There is no unmentioned assumption on the X-degree of higher quantum-normal coefficients. ## 2. The singular-step budget and truncated valuation argument After one fixed coherent denominator clearing, \(a_d\) is Laurent polynomial in \(Q,Y\). Its Q-span \(A\) implies \(a_d(Q,Q^m)
e0\) for \(m>A\): equality of two collected exponents \(u+mv\) with different \(v\)'s would force \(m\le A\). Its at most \(s\) remaining monomials have nonzero-root multiplicity at most \(s-1\), by the logarithmic-derivative Vandermonde determinant. For all sufficiently large levels, \(a_d(Q_N,Y)
e0\) as a Laurent polynomial in \(Y\). The visited Y-values are distinct; there are at most \(D\) roots on them. Thus the sum of all leading vanishing orders through coefficient \(N\) is at most \(B=D(s-1)\). The excluded levels include any zeros or poles of fixed Q-scalar clearing factors and any specialization where all Y-coefficients of \(a_d\) vanish. There are only finitely many such root values. No uniform lower bound on their nonzero numerical magnitudes is needed. The truncated-ring step is valid despite zero divisors. If \(k=B+1\), \(h=\epsilon^\mu u\) with \(u\) a unit, and \(he\in\epsilon^tR_k\), \(t\le k\), then \[ e\in\epsilon^{t-\mu}R_k\qquad(t\ge\mu). \] The additional annihilator \(\epsilon^{k-\mu}R_k\) is already contained in that asserted ideal. Applying this at each step gives \(e_r\in\epsilon^{k-M_r}R_k\), so every root coefficient through \(X^N\) agrees. In particular no singular step was divided at its root value. For the finitely many fixed initial colors the leading trajectory polynomials are units at all sufficiently large roots, as suggested in the outline. The written proof is stronger: the total budget would handle their vanishing as well, whenever its other hypotheses hold. ## 3. The whole pole lattice is the necessary last step Subtracting the two cyclotomic conditions gives \[ H(X)=(1-X^N)(W_N-Z_N)\in\mathbb C[X],\qquad \deg H\le N . \] Both expansions have the same starting lattice and agree through power \(N\). Thus every coefficient of \(H\) through its maximal degree vanishes, proving \(W_N=Z_N\). Simple cyclotomic poles alone would not suffice: an arbitrary polynomial part of higher degree could remain invisible to the finite window. The stated degree bound and prescribed low prefix are therefore substantive source-lattice data. The residue at infinity is then fixed, including the case that the actual Kashaev value vanishes. ## 4. The exact actual-unknot sharpness example checks Direct Ore multiplication gives the displayed actual operator \[ (T-Q)[(1-QY)T-(1-Y)]. \] The inner bracket applied to the actual color \(1\) is \((1-Q)Y\), which the outer factor kills. Its exact Fourier transform is \(X^{-2}(1-X)(1-QX)(1-S)\). Applying this to \(X^{n_0}/(1-X)\) gives exactly the stated finite source. The leading trajectory is \(1-Q^r\); only \(r=N\) vanishes in the reconstruction range, and it has multiplicity one. The alternative root section \(\lambda X^N/(1-X^N)\) is shift-invariant and preserves the affine root source and all the stated root pole/prefix data. Its residue contribution is \(+\lambda\). Its first normal would require \[ (1-S_0)g_1=NUf'(U),\qquad f(U)=\lambda U/(1-U). \] The cyclic average kills the left side and gives \(N^2Uf'(U)
e0\) on the right for \(\lambda
e0\). This works in the formal Laurent field as well as the rational field. The two required jet levels in this actual example are therefore sharp. The proof and the saved exact diagnostics support the stated uniqueness theorem. They do not construct a regulator candidate in the same pole and source lattice, establish its bounded quantum lift, or estimate the selected residue. Those remain the geometric comparison and volume questions.

title: An actual meridian source on the tensor Casimir cover
text: # An actual meridian source on the tensor Casimir cover Research note, 26 October 2026. This derives an inhomogeneous meridian equation from the literature ADO crossing itself. Its source is a specified spectral projector, with the full factor 1+M^(-2N). The coincident spectral directions at completeness are the actual meridian confluence, not a separately chosen infinitesimal model. Their source residue is a fixed rank-one cup/cap operator. The result is local to two tensor factors. It is not an identification of the full knot quantum-A operator with its geometric A-polynomial, nor a proof of the selected regulator norm. The connection constructed below still has to be assembled through the whole colored network. ## 1. The fixed operator and its generic meridian spectrum Use q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), N>=2, and the actual ADO color x=-M/q. Put Y=M^2, U=Y^N=M^(2N). On V(x), the matrices E,F,K and checked crossing B_N(M) are exactly those in [the semicyclic source proof](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md), restricted here to F^N=0. In particular K v_a=xQ^(-a)v_a, F v_a=v_(a+1), F v_(N-1)=0, and E v_a=e_a(x)v_(a-1). Let Omega be the actual tensor Casimir, E_tot=E tensor K+1 tensor E, F_tot=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, Omega=rho^2 F_tot E_tot+q K_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). For generic M its N distinct Casimir nodes and crossing values are c_j(Y)=q^(-2j-1)Y+q^(2j+1)Y^(-1), lambda_j(Y)=nu_j Y^(-j), nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), 0<=j<N. (1.1) Each component has dimension N. Here is an elementary verification. At total degree j write the highest vector as h_j=sum_(a=0)^j b_a v_a tensor v_(j-a), b_0=1. Its E-equation is b_(a+1)/b_a=-e_(j-a)(x)/ (e_(a+1)(x) x Q^(-(j-a-1))). For generic x the denominators are nonzero. Multiplication gives b_j=(-1)^j x^(-j)Q^(j(j-1)/2). The defining finite R is triangular, so the coefficient of v_0 tensor v_j in B h_j comes only from its zero-th term on v_j tensor v_0. Thus lambda_j=(-1)^j x^(-2j)Q^(j(j-1)/2)=nu_jY^(-j). The N descendants F_tot^r h_j are nonzero generically: the E F^r recurrence has no zero coefficient for 0<r<N. F_tot^N=0 by the root q-binomial identity. Their different Casimir nodes imply a direct sum, and the dimensions total N^2. This proves the spectrum and complete decomposition without importing a tensor-decomposition theorem. Define T_0(z)=2,T_1(z)=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1). Since T_n(a+a^(-1))=a^n+a^(-n), (1.1) proves product_j(z-c_j(Y))=P_(N,U)(z), P_(N,U)(z)=T_N(z)+U+U^(-1). (1.2) Thus the actual local spectral algebra is A_(N,U)=C(U)[z]/P_(N,U)(z). It splits after the specified root cover Y^N=U. The polynomial r(Y,z) of degree less than N with r(Y,c_j)=lambda_j satisfies B_N(M)=r(Y,Omega). (1.3) The scalar conventions are explicit. At M=1 the usual highest-weight quantum-group R in the earlier crossing calculation has checked matrix lambda_0 B_N(1), with lambda_0=q^((N-1)^2/2). The ADO crossing used here is already B_N(1); its original pivot, zero-framing twist and full modified dimension are not changed. ## 2. The affine meridian equation and its full peripheral source Let sigma(Y)=QY and sigma(z)=z on the split spectral algebra. The nodes obey c_j(QY)=c_(j-1)(Y), with indices modulo N. For the values in (1.1), lambda_(j+1)(QY)=-Y^(-1)lambda_j(Y), j<N-1, lambda_0(QY)=1, -Y^(-1)lambda_(N-1)(Y)=-U^(-1). Let E_(N-1)(Y,z) be the spectral idempotent with value one at c_(N-1) and zero at the other nodes. Interpolation therefore proves the exact equation sigma(r)=-Y^(-1)r+(1+U^(-1)) E_(N-1). (2.1) This source has not been chosen to obtain a desired period: the exceptional last component is forced by the actual highest-weight eigenvalues. The generic idempotent is E_(N-1)=product_(j=0)^(N-2) (z-c_j(Y))/(c_(N-1)(Y)-c_j(Y)). (2.2) The homogeneous cyclic norm is exactly Norm_sigma(-Y^(-1))=-U^(-1), (2.3) because Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), at both parities. Thus 1+U^(-1) is precisely 1 minus that norm. It becomes two at completeness, but it must first be retained as a whole function multiplying (2.2). There are two different norms here. The Casimir-algebra norm of r is Norm_spec(r)=(product_j nu_j)Y^(-N(N-1)/2), det B_N=Norm_spec(r)^N. (2.4) The root phase product_j nu_j is retained. Equation (2.3) instead concerns the cyclic meridian transport. Iterating (2.1) gives an affine monodromy with homogeneous block -U^(-1) and source s=(1+U^(-1))r. Away from U=-1 the cyclic resolvent reconstructs the unique solution r. These are identities before any polar specialization. At a resonance or a node collision a displayed zero times a projector pole cannot be evaluated separately. ## 3. A genuine matrix meridian comparison, including parity There is an explicit operator realization of sigma in (2.1). Let H(M) have columns F_tot^r h_j(M), ordered by j and then r. Let P send label j to j+1 modulo N, keeping r fixed. Put G(M)=H(qM) P H(M)^(-1). (3.1) The highest K-root of component j at M is x^2 Q^(-j). It equals that of component j+1 at qM. The descendants use the same fixed F normalization. Consequently G intertwines all three actual total E,F,K operators. In particular it keeps the Casimir observable z fixed. Equations (1.1) and (3.1) give the actual matrix identity G(M)^(-1) B_N(qM) G(M) =-Y^(-1)B_N(M) +(1+U^(-1)) E_(N-1)(Y,Omega). (3.2) This is not merely equality of spectra. H and G are specified rational matrices on the generic color chart; no unrelated normalization is chosen at each shift. The meridian cover also keeps its sign. After N shifts, M becomes -M. If S_2 is the sign matrix (-1)^a on the second factor, the highest-vector recurrence gives H(-M)=S_2 H(M) diag_(j,r)((-1)^j). (3.3) Thus the N-step matrix transport is H(-M)H(M)^(-1), with both its color parity and spectral-sign unit retained. The 2N-step transport is identity. On the abstract Casimir algebra (2.1) already uses Y, whose shift has order N; forgetting the parity on the actual tensor module would require the explicit identification (3.3). The subsequent [intrinsic cut and meridian atlas](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) assembles these maps on a generic even-strand braid using explicit centralizer transitions and preserves the full selected cut. It does not construct the integral geometric triangulation comparison. ## 4. Its complete spectral jet is the actual meridian confluence Write u=Log M near M=1. Pair j with l=N-1-j, and put h=2j+1<N. Then nu_l=nu_j and exactly c_j-c_l=-(q^h-q^(-h))(Y-Y^(-1)), lambda_j=nu_j M^(-2j), lambda_l=nu_j M^(-2l). The confluent divided difference is therefore [(lambda_j-lambda_l)/(c_j-c_l)]_(M=1) =-nu_j(N-1-2j)/(2(q^h-q^(-h))). (4.1) The double point is an honest finite flat meridian algebra. In the pair factor, eta=z-c_j(M) satisfies eta(eta+c_j-c_l)=0. (4.2) At completeness it becomes eta^2=0. The unit r specializes to nu_j plus the coefficient (4.1) times eta. Replacing its value-and-divided-difference interpolation rows by the confluent rows gives an invertible Hermite Vandermonde. Thus the coefficients of r are regular at M=1. Equation (1.3) specializes to the earlier crossing polynomial, including its nilpotent part. For odd N the node with 2j+1=N is simple and has only its value condition. No inverse of two modulo an even N is used. This supplies a meridian derivation of the same jet that the earlier proof obtained by varying q. In particular it identifies a specific actual spectral jet with the meridian collision; the internal carry parameter epsilon and the auxiliary source coordinate remain different data. ## 5. The polar source residue is the actual cup/cap Let c_0=q+q^(-1), and let e_0 be the idempotent of the double c_0 factor of P_(N,1). On the actual nilpotent tensor module write J_N=(Omega-c_0)e_0, J_N^2=0. (5.1) Let J_x be the actual self-duality matrix at the Kashaev color, (J_x)_(N-1-a,a)=q^(a^2), and g=K^(1-N). Use the existing cup and right cap to form cup=vec(J_x^(-t)), cap=vec(g J_x)^t, Pi_N=cup*cap. (5.2) Then exactly Pi_N^2=0, rank Pi_N=1, ptr_g(Pi_N)=I, J_N=(-1)^N rho^2 Pi_N. (5.3) Here is a proof of the last identity. At generic q the total degree-d Casimir characteristic polynomial has labels 0 through min(d,2N-2-d), by the highest-vector decomposition already proved in the preceding Casimir note. At this root, the node c_0 occurs with multiplicity two only at degree N-1, and with multiplicity one in every other degree. Hence J_N has rank at most one and is zero off degree N-1. Commutation with E_tot,F_tot then makes its image invariant. The invariant vector and covector spaces are one-dimensional, by simplicity and the actual self-duality of V_N. Thus J_N is a scalar multiple of the cup/cap in (5.2). The independently proved closing functional in [the Casimir trace calculation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#8-the-actual-closing-trace-is-a-spectral-jet-functional) gives ptr_K(J_N)=-rho^2 I. Since g=(-1)^(N-1)K here, and direct cup/cap contraction gives ptr_g(Pi_N)=I, the scalar is (-1)^N rho^2. It is nonzero, proving both the rank and the normalization in (5.3). The generic projector (2.2) has a simple pole. Its actual first meridian coefficient is [u E_(N-1)(Y,Omega(M))]_(M=1)=J_N/(4rho), [(U-1) E_(N-1)]_(M=1)=N J_N/(2rho). (5.4) Indeed c_(N-1)-c_0=rho(Y-Y^(-1)) has u-derivative 4rho; every other denominator factor is a unit. This also follows by evaluating its full product numerator, without a small numerical parameter. Keeping the source coefficient in (3.2) gives [(U-1)(1+U^(-1)) E_(N-1)]_(M=1) =N J_N/rho=(-1)^N N rho Pi_N. (5.5) This is an actual meridian-normal source residue with its full N and parity factor. Its pivotal closing is nonzero. The individual shifted frame and projector may be polar; the regular crossing and its complete cyclic identity retain the resulting cancellation. ## 6. A pure braid detects the same nonreduced source At completeness r(c_0)=1 and r'(c_0)=-(N-1)/(2rho). On the double c_0 block the actual full twist therefore obeys, for every integer m, e_0(B_N(1)^(2m)-I) =(-1)^(N+1)m(N-1)rho Pi_N. (6.1) Its actual pivotal partial trace is the same nonzero coefficient times I. Thus closing with this specified Casimir projector detects the jet. This is an inserted operator test, not a claim that every knot period couples to this block by itself. The localized unit I+(-1)^(N+1)(N-1)rho Pi_N has determinant one and fixes the cup. Nevertheless it is nontrivial. On a two-dimensional invariant subspace it acts on a lift of its fixed quotient by a nonzero affine translation. Its m-th power multiplies that translation by m. Consequently the actual strand braiding cannot descend projectively to strand permutations on the full retained source: a transposition would have scalar square. No finite-index cover kills this unipotent holonomy in characteristic zero. This is not a contradiction to the finite cyclic Hilbert-90 theorem, whose norm-one hypothesis is different. The infinite-order conclusion uses (6.1) in characteristic zero; finite-field tests alone would not prove it. The appropriate local frame group includes the units of the nonreduced Casimir algebra, not only its reduced scalars or determinant line. This does not disprove a published decorated tetrahedral symmetry using different adapters, and does not identify strand braids with geometric tetrahedron permutations. The [subsequent actual-braid theorem](actual_braid_group_and_spectral_source.md) strengthens this test. Raising both adjacent original crossings to the power 2N gives square-zero logarithms J_12, J_23 with a strictly negative mixed ordinary trace. Their pivotal moment has the exact value -2N^2/rho. A nonzero product eigenvalue gives an SL_2 quotient in the connected braid-image closure, and every finite-index restriction retains it. This concerns the full braid-source realization, not an assertion about the selected minimal A-operator's difference-Galois group or its geometric period quotient. ## 7. Verification, coverage and the remaining theorem [The audit](../experiments/audit_braided_source_groupoid.py) compares the literal ADO crossing to its generic-color Casimir interpolation at N=2,3,4,5,6,9. It constructs H and G, checks all total E,F,K intertwinings and (3.2), the Chebyshev equation, both distinct norm calculations, and the retained N-step parity. At ten levels through 15 it also checks the actual rank-one cup/cap identity, the meridian source residue, the full-twist powers and the nonzero pivotal closing. These are exact finite-field diagnostics for the uniform arguments above. [Results](../experiments/braided_source_groupoid_results.json). The definitions remain the actual cyclic/quantum-group crossings and recouplings. The literature coverage is [Kashaev's cyclic 6j framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147) and [Kashaev--Reshetikhin's holonomy R-matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202212). Only their abstracts were consulted here for coverage; their proofs are not premises. The [braided source groupoid](braided_source_groupoid.md) supplies coherent recoupling/source transport with moving semicyclic centers. The subsequent [intrinsic cut theorem](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) proves a basis-independent full cut, with its actual modified dimension, and assembles generic braid meridian charts with their non-scalar centralizer transitions. It also identifies the complete two-factor Casimir order and its full dual by a perfect pivotal residue pairing. The integral relative geometric source still needs to be compared; it is not supplied by positive ideal shapes or by generic assembly. The cover (1.2) is the actual local tensor Casimir cover. It is not asserted to be the geometric knot A-curve. The geometric quantum-A component, selected global source and marked Bloch-regulator norm remain unproved. The original Kashaev volume conjecture remains the active goal.

title: The compact geometric homotopy has an exact wall and peripheral charge
text: # The compact geometric homotopy has an exact wall and peripheral charge Research proof, 27 October 2026. At fixed complete meridian the physical compact source sphere and the exceptional source sphere are not homologous in the Gauss open set. Their difference is one explicit wall torus, with its orientation and period determined. Varying the meridian supplies a global logarithmic orbit homotopy avoiding that wall, at the cost of the opposite SL2 lift and an explicit peripheral Cech period. The actual full quantum source has a matching, completely specified central-sign character. Along this meridian path every possible modified-dimension pole has a residue equal to an original ordinary color, with a polynomial total norm bound. This is an actual source wall theorem. It does not turn the Kashaev point evaluation into a meridian integral or continue the full geometric A-branch for free. Use [the resolved framing source](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md) and the [exact exponential Cech/current construction](compact_exponential_cech_current_detour.md). All source phases and the complete modified-dimension function remain marked throughout. ## 1. A closed form detects the fixed-meridian obstruction On the resolved threefold Y use north coordinates v,eta,a and south coordinates V=1/v, eta'=-v^2 eta, a'=v-v^2a. Put f=1-eta v=1+eta' V, and remove the Gauss divisor D_cut={f=0}. The exceptional divisor is E={eta=0}=X. The following form is globally regular and closed on Y minus D_cut: Xi=dLog f wedge dLog v =dv wedge d eta/f =dV wedge d eta'/f. (1.1) The last two expressions show that its apparent flag poles cancel. It is pulled back from the resolved meridian surface and is closed therefore also on the threefold. Let c=2pi*i. Orient the actual compact source sphere by 0<=T<=1, 0<=phi<2pi, v=sqrt(T/(1-T))exp(i phi), a=sqrt(T(1-T))exp(-i phi). Its source form is Omega_0=dv wedge da=-i dT wedge dphi, omega_I=-Omega_0/c, integral_Gamma omega_I=1. (1.2) Let Gamma_E be this sphere at eta=0. Let Gamma_phys be its actual physical-symbol section eta_phys=(1-exp(-cT))/v. (1.3) The removable pole formulas at both endpoints make these genuine compact cycles. By the exact physical Gauss identity, Xi|_(Gamma_E)=0, Xi|_(Gamma_phys)=c Omega_0, integral_(Gamma_phys)Xi=-c^2=4pi^2. (1.4) Thus no homology, and in particular no homotopy, inside Y minus D_cut can identify the two cycles. This conclusion does not assume that the flag or centralizer coordinates stay fixed during a proposed homotopy. ## 2. The necessary relative cycle is one explicitly oriented wall torus The straight normal interpolation eta_lambda=lambda eta_phys is a global compact three-chain before D_cut is deleted. Its Gauss factor is f_lambda=1-lambda+lambda exp(-cT). It hits D_cut exactly at lambda=T=1/2, for every phi. The intersection loop is C: v=exp(i phi), a=1/(2v), eta=1/v, inside D_cut, which is globally C^*_(v) times A^1_(a). Near that loop, f_lambda=-2(lambda-1/2)+pi*i(T-1/2)+higher terms. (2.1) The normal real Jacobian is negative. Define Tube(C) with first the counterclockwise f-circle and then the positive v-circle. Removing a small neighborhood of the intersection from the three-chain gives the exact relation [Gamma_phys]-[Gamma_E]=-[Tube(C)] in H_2(Y minus D_cut). (2.2) Indeed the inner boundary of the removed disk has the opposite normal orientation, and (2.1) reverses that orientation once more. This fixes the sign without a convention about an unspecified cap. The wall residue and period are Res_(D_cut) Xi=dLog v, integral_(Tube(C))Xi=c^2=-4pi^2. (2.3) Equation (2.3) independently checks (2.2). Since C winds once in the C^* factor of D_cut, it has no cap inside D_cut. A source comparison must retain this torus or an equivalent relative boundary co-source. The actual principal Gaussian flag form from the resolved source has the corresponding balanced residues: nu_cut=-(d eta/eta) wedge Omega_0/f, Res_E nu_cut=-Omega_0, Res_(D_cut) nu_cut=+Omega_0. (2.4) For the geometric Gaussian multiply (2.4) by its recorded nonzero torsion/phase coefficient c_beta and retain the original base-only quantum line. To check the second residue, on v!=0 use nu_cut=df/[f(1-f)] wedge Omega_0. On the wall Omega_0=d(v da); along the actual intersection loop v da=-(1/2)dLog v, so its primitive also has the explicit period -pi*i. The ordinary two-form residue and this lower boundary current are different degrees of data and should not be identified. ## 3. The integer winding cannot be erased at fixed meridian There is a simple relative interpretation of (1.4). A globally finite eta section has f=1 at both flag poles. Since the sphere is simply connected, choose Log f=0 at its north pole. Its value at the south pole is 2pi*i times an integer, invariant in any continuous family avoiding f=0. The exceptional sphere has integer zero; the physical sphere has integer -1. This is the source degree obstruction. The tempting logarithmic interpolation eta_lambda=(1-exp(-c lambda T))/v avoids f=0 on the north chart but does not patch at the south pole: eta'_lambda= [exp(-c lambda)exp(c lambda T')-1]/V, T'=Va'=1-T. (3.1) For nonintegral lambda it has a nonzero V^(-1) coefficient. Discarding that coefficient would remove precisely the global clutch being tested. The exact finite-current regularization in the cited Cech note keeps this defect; it is not a new quantum dressing. ## 4. Varying the meridian gives an explicit global orbit homotopy Let m be the eigenvalue on the retained flag. The Grothendieck meridian chart is mu(v,m,eta)= [[m-eta v, eta], [(m-m^(-1))v-eta v^2, m^(-1)+eta v]]. (4.1) Its determinant is one, its trace is m+m^(-1), and [1:v] is its m-eigenflag. Its second chart is the affine transition eta'=-v^2 eta+(m-m^(-1))v. (4.2) At m=1 this is the Springer bundle. Away from m=+/-1 it is a nontrivial affine cotangent torsor. The full Gauss entry f=m-eta v=m^(-1)+eta' V is global. Its two polar flag values are m and m^(-1), rather than both one. Define the marked path, for 0<=lambda<=1, m_lambda=exp(pi*i lambda), f_lambda=exp[pi*i lambda(1-2T)], eta_lambda=m_lambda[1-exp(-c lambda T)]/v. (4.3) The south expression forced by (4.2) is eta'_lambda=m_lambda^(-1) [exp(c lambda T')-1]/V. (4.4) Both are removable at the corresponding poles for every lambda. All eigenvalues and f_lambda stay nonzero. At lambda=0 the family is the exceptional sphere at the identity. At lambda=1 it is -mu_phys, with m=-1 and eta=-eta_phys. Thus (4.3) is a globally regular projective meridian-orbit homotopy avoiding the Gauss wall. Its SL2 lift changes by the central sign, explicitly. This sign change is necessary for a once-winding clock. Along a meridian family choose Log m continuously. The pole conditions give Log f(S)=-Log m modulo 2pi*i, while the physical relative clock has Log(f/m)(S)=-2pi*i. Starting with the zero clock forces 2 Log m_end=2pi*i modulo the chosen path mark. A closed path ending m=1 cannot accomplish this odd winding; ending m=-1 does. The actual inverse-eigenvalue convention of the finite source is M=m^(-1), so its path is M_lambda=exp(-pi*i lambda). Formulas (4.3)--(4.4) agree with the bridge note's determinant-h matrix after division by M_lambda. No sign is silently discarded. ## 5. The avoided wall reappears as a marked peripheral Cech period On the total varying-meridian family the naive dLog f wedge dLog v has meridian poles at the two polar flags. The regular local forms are Xi_N=(dLog f-dLog m) wedge dLog v, Xi_S=(dLog f+dLog m) wedge dLog v. (5.1) Their difference is exactly Xi_S-Xi_N=2dLog m wedge dLog v =d(2Log m dLog v). (5.2) Thus the global object is the specified peripheral period torsor, not a single absolute two-form with a forgotten patch. Along m:1->-1 the marked Log m changes by pi*i. The Cech term in (5.2) then has flag period c^2, the wall period of (2.3). Changing the meridian transfers the charge; it does not delete it. On a fixed lambda fiber the two local forms agree. Their actual compact period is integral_Gamma Xi_lambda=-c^2 lambda =-2c Log m_lambda. (5.3) For the physical h_N=c/N, its signed normalized curvature integral is (1/(2pi*i h_N)) integral_Gamma Xi_lambda=-N lambda. (5.4) The coherent source uses the Chern convention c_1=-F/(2pi*i). For curvature F=Xi_lambda/h_N its positive Chern degree is therefore N lambda, agreeing with the endpoint prequantum line O(N). The minus sign in (5.4) belongs to the stated flux orientation, not to a claim that the actual source has line O(-N). At the endpoint the prequantum exponential of the full flux is exp(-2pi*i N)=1. The integer clutch and its half-form/sign data still remain. In particular the intermediate integral-degree locations lambda=k/N are precisely the actual ordinary-color wall locations in Section 6. This is an exact equality of locations and signed curvature integrals; it is not an unproved identification of generic quantum dressing with ordinary coherent SL2 action. There is a stronger exact root identity, proved with all marks in [the flux/peripheral-character theorem](gauss_wall_flux_and_actual_peripheral_character.md). Our oriented period is I_phys(M)=+2c Log M for M=m^(-1). Its explicit inverse I_inv=-I_phys gives chi_H=exp(-2c LogM/H), chi_(h_N)=M^(-2N), d_N=epsilon_N (M-M^(-1))chi_(h_N)^(1/2)/(1-chi_(h_N)). The marked half-root is antiperiodic under the actual q half-step. Thus the wall flux supplies the actual central character and full polar adapter at the roots. This does not identify that logarithmic H-lift with a particular off-root auxiliary source or its normal jets. ## 6. Every actual meridian wall charge is an ordinary color Fix the original N-th-root state, and write its reciprocal reduced Laurent function as F_N(Y), Y=M^2. Keep the full original factor epsilon_N=i^(N+3), n=N-1, d_N(M)=epsilon_N M^n/S_N(M^2), S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1), P_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M^2). (6.1) Along the actual meridian path M_lambda=exp(-pi*i lambda), the only possible interior poles are simple and occur at lambda_k=k/N, M_k=exp(-pi*i k/N), 1<=k<N. (6.2) A pole is removable if the corresponding actual color vanishes. The actual finite-color identity and reciprocity give F_N(M_k^2)=F_N(Q_N^(-k))=C_k(q_N). (6.3) Direct differentiation of S_N gives the exact wall residue Res_(lambda_k)[P_N(M_lambda)d lambda] =epsilon_N (-1)^k sin(pi k/N) C_k(q_N)/(pi N). (6.4) Equivalently the canonical meridian one-form has Res_(M_k)[P_N(M)dLog M] =-i epsilon_N (-1)^k sin(pi k/N) C_k(q_N)/N. (6.5) Proof: at a nontrivial root Y_k, S_N'(Y_k)=-N Y_k^(-1)/(1-Y_k). Also M_k^(N-1)(1-M_k^2)=(-1)^k 2i sin(pi k/N). Substitution into the ordinary simple-pole formula proves both equations. They retain the original phase, parity and full source factor. The independently established actual ordinary-color bound is |C_k(q_N)|<=D_N=O(N^(b-1)), 1<=k<N, for a fixed b-strand knot braid. Hence sum_k |Res[P_N dLog M]| <=(D_N/N)cot(pi/(2N)) <2D_N/pi. (6.6) The corresponding total closed-contour correction is at most 4D_N. For d lambda the bound is smaller by pi. These are polynomial source-wall charges for every knot in this actual presentation, not estimates imported from a geometric saddle. More generally a transport kernel holomorphic at these walls multiplies each residue by its literal value there. A bound for that kernel is additional input. Singular kernels require their actual derivative residues and cannot be covered by (6.6) alone. Equations (6.4)--(6.6) are meridian-integral statements. They do not express the Kashaev point evaluation as such an integral or prove that an unknown geometric transport has polynomial wall values. The universal charges themselves are now exact and bounded. The [existing regular-period decomposition](regularized_kashaev_period.md) already separates these ordinary-color principal parts from the regular quotient carrying the complete value. Thus even all the residues in (6.5), with their normalization fixed, do not determine that regular part or its large-level norm. ### 6.1 The endpoint central sign is an actual source-line character The original reduced state depends on M^2, so it is unchanged by M->-M. Its full source satisfies exactly P_N(-M)=(-1)^(N-1)P_N(M), P_N(M^(-1))=P_N(M). (6.7) For the second identity use reciprocity and S_N(Y^(-1))=Y^(-(N-1))S_N(Y). Thus the semisimple detour ends at the same reduced complete Kashaev value, with a completely specified full peripheral-line sign. In particular P_N(M)/M^(N-1)=epsilon_N F_N(Y)/S_N(Y) descends as a rational function of Y. P_N itself descends in the character line of the double cover M^2=Y. This is an exact property of the actual finite source, independent of an assumed classical coherent dressing. The matrix Weyl adapter carries additional integral information; its norm is not replaced here by this scalar calculation. ## 7. The unresolved full-knot continuation is sharply separated The homotopy (4.3) is universal for the meridian orbit and compact source. To lift it to the full geometric critical family one must continue the marked A-curve branch and all crossing charts along the chosen M path. Ramification, ideal places, vanishing chart denominators and branch monodromy can occur. The local Rivin algebraic place does not establish that global continuation. A finite cover can record monodromy, and the normalization of an algebraic A-curve supplies a proper compact curve. Neither fact ensures that its lifted endpoint is the central twist of the chosen geometric representation, keeps its finite source lattice regular, or bounds a transport kernel at the walls. Such assertions must be proved with their marked source; they do not follow from the orbit homotopy alone. Nor can a finite etale cover remove the fixed-meridian wall class. Pull back Xi and sum the lifts of the two cycles. Their period difference is the covering degree times -c^2, still nonzero in characteristic zero. Equivalently pushforward of an upstairs cobordism would contradict (1.4). A cover can retain a spin or branch mark; it cannot turn this non-torsion cycle correction into zero while preserving the selected cycle. What is now explicit is the entire universal obstruction and its possible detour: one Gauss wall torus at fixed meridian; one peripheral Cech charge when varying it; one actual central-sign line; and finitely many ordinary-color source residues with total polynomial norm. These remain meaningful before quantum jets. They do not identify the normal d at fixed N with h_N, or prove the geometric selected phase or the volume norm. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_meridian_homotopy_wall_and_source_residues.py) checks the chart clutch, both homotopies, wall orientation, curvature degree, all parity signs and actual finite-source residues. The [independent Gauss-wall/flux proof audit](gauss_wall_cycle_and_peripheral_flux.md) also verifies the cycle sign, global clutch, peripheral convention and actual source residue formulas.

title: Independent audit of the Möbius framing fiber and flat source frame
text: # Independent audit of the Möbius framing fiber and flat source frame 27 October 2026. Detailed examination of [the Möbius framing and norm-pole theorem](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) and [the flat cyclic source-frame theorem](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md). The derivative and base-ring qualifications below should be retained. No new selected-period comparison follows merely from these source-frame identifications. ## 1. The actual prefix Möbius formula and its orientation Factor U-V=u v, with v=(a,b) and w=v V inverse=(c,d). Since U,V have determinant one and UV inverse is nontrivial trace two, w u=0 and U-V has rank exactly one. In the actual F(r,s) frame, the first row of F inverse(U-V)F is proportional to vF. Using the inverse of the determinant-one matrix F inverse V F gives \[ \frac p\sigma =\frac{(vF)_2\ell_V-(vF)_1(V')_{12}}{(vF)_1} =\frac{(wF)_2}{(vF)_1} =\frac{c(1-r)-ds}{ar+bs}. \] This verifies the full prefix adapter and its sign directly, without a position-discriminant square root. Solving gives the displayed inverse, and differentiating gives \[ r_p=\frac{\sigma[s(ad-bc)-ac]}{(ap+\sigma c)^2}. \] The two-form orientation also passes. Since Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] and d log A=-ds/(1+s), the coefficient of d log A wedge d log p is -p r_p/s, exactly the negative sign in the theorem. In the finite-pole chart the projective pole is lambda=-sigma c/a, independent of s. On c_U-c_V nonzero its trace-word expression follows from c_U-c_V=u_2 a and c_(UV inverse)=u_2 c. This is intrinsic to the MARKED prefix/cut data, not an asserted diagram-independent topological invariant. The actual figure-eight prefix factorization gives v=(1,2), w=(1+u,1), sigma=-1, and the theorem's numerator, inverse and derivative follow. Its pole lambda=1+u=-u squared has order six at either geometric embedding. This agrees with the independently computed exceptional-fiber limit gamma_0=u squared: its pole p=-gamma_0 is the same point. The finite- and infinite-pole charts in the proof retain their nonvanishing hypotheses correctly. ## 2. The finite cyclic norm and the required derivative qualification The rational identity \[ \frac1N\sum_{p^N=1}\frac p{(p-\lambda)^2} =\frac{N\lambda^{N-1}}{(1-\lambda^N)^2} \] follows by differentiating the finite partial-fraction expansion of 1/(1-lambda^N), or directly from the companion matrix. It has the theorem's sign and exponent. The pole-at-zero and pole-at-infinity averages vanish for N greater than one. For fixed nonzero G and absolute lambda not one, (1/N) log absolute value of G N lambda^(N-1)/(1-lambda^N)^2 tends to minus the absolute value of log absolute lambda. Hence a rational fiber coordinate does not itself force a subexponential source weight. For the WHOLE product P_N(Q,lambda), the derivative must be written \[ D_Q\log P_N =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{j\lambda Q^{-j}}{1-\lambda Q^{-j}}, \qquad D_QP_N=P_N D_Q\log P_N. \tag{1} \] The sum alone is the logarithmic derivative, not D_Q P_N. This minor wording correction was reported to the author. At a norm-zero fiber neither the apparent logarithmic poles nor their product with P_N should be evaluated separately: use the original finite product derivative. The root relation P_N=1-lambda^N is not an identity of its Q-normal extension. For N divisible by six the actual figure-eight principal-density sampling encounters its pole. The actual finite tensor remains regular. This is an explicit reason the rational principal-density average cannot be declared the whole selected source. It is not a statement that the original invariant or its selected geometric coefficient is singular or zero. ## 3. The source-cyclic classification is scheme-theoretic on its chart The flat-frame argument is valid over COMMUTATIVE base algebras, including those with nilpotents. The orbit map from N copies of the source line is its explicit open-chart hypothesis. In that line-valued frame AP=A fixes A to the summing source and P to the cyclic shift; BA=A fixes the zeroth column of B. The remaining rows of the aligned defect give B_(i,j+1)=Q B_(i-1,j). Their wrap equations force every off-diagonal zeroth-row entry to zero, and hence B=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)). This uses no delta division. The line-bundle groupoid and the removal of its automorphisms by a nonzero marked source vector follow from this canonical frame. They do not classify unrelated noncyclic components. Distinct root eigenvalues prove the orbit hypothesis in a neighborhood of the actual primitive-root source, as stated. The additional aligned defect projector is e_0 rho with rho_0=1. The whole multiplicative equation becomes exactly delta rho_j=0. If delta is a nonzero divisor on the base, its flat saturation is the actual e_00 projector and no extra row parameters remain. The statement that saturation is JUST the original base has this necessary scope. On a base with delta-torsion it also removes base torsion: for example delta=epsilon in k[epsilon]/epsilon squared makes delta-power saturation the zero ring. This qualification was reported and is now explicit in the current note. It does not affect the actual regular normal coefficient ring or the preceding classification over arbitrary commutative bases. ## 4. The whole corrected algebra and the nonaligned family Evaluation at Q^j makes tau(X)=Q inverse times (X-delta e_0(X)) the predecessor cyclic permutation of the actual clock nodes. Thus tau(e_j)=e_(j+1), with the theorem's orientation. In its crossed product the elements e_i P^(i-j) multiply as E_ij and give exactly Mat_N of the base. In particular its whole correction retains the finite wrap rather than imposing the inconsistent generic-Q relation BP=QPB with P^N=I. The explicit N=2 nonaligned family also passes. Set h=Q-Q inverse. Its conditions reduce to t squared=x(1+x); then its multiplicative commutator entries agree exactly with the displayed R. Replacing delta by delta^k in x and t preserves this identity and makes the tilt invisible to any prescribed fixed jet, while changing B's second eigenvalue. The moving projector image fails alignment with the actual source line. This is a valid counterexample to omitting WHOLE alignment, not to the positive aligned theorem. The scalar-intertwiner conclusion is exact. Root actual closure with generic meridian M is scalar; the auxiliary whole q-normal lift need not be, as the earlier literal unknot calculation shows. The current note explicitly retains that scope when mentioning an actual scalar knot transport. A central scalar is not fixed by source-frame classification. Strictly requiring the FINAL transport to fix the source vector would set that scalar to one and would be an extra normalization, not a property of the original period. ## 5. The central loop identity is exact but needs a typed endpoint map The [actual framed loop/source identity](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md), equation (5a), follows from Delta_mom S_P=Q(Z inverse minus one)Q_0 and Q_0=v ell. It is an exact whole rank-one insertion factorization, with selected divided-normal insertion Q_N Q_0. Its orbit path and source mark are necessary. It does not by itself identify a geometric endpoint crossing. Its normal divisor is 1-Q^N. The Möbius framing pole has norm divisor 1-lambda^N, which is generally NONZERO at that same actual root. Even when both vanish at a resonant level, their extensions and normal orders are independent until an actual word/source map compares them. No such identification follows from (5a) or from the rigidity of the finite source frame. Algebraically (5a) is homogeneous under arbitrary central rescalings of C_1 and C_2; their scalar periods rescale on both sides. With C_2=I it prescribes the inserted period in terms of the already unknown uninserted one, rather than determining that unknown scalar. A genuine endpoint comparison must additionally transport the actual crossing word, co-source, orbit path and normal divisor into the geometric relative endpoint complex. The audited notes correctly leave this selected comparison and the volume limit open.

title: The Fourier framing fiber is a projective line with one intrinsic pole
text: # The Fourier framing fiber is a projective line with one intrinsic pole Research proof, 27 October 2026. The new momentum coordinate has a simpler description than the quadratic position projection: on every regular fixed-cut fiber it is a Möbius coordinate. Its only pole in the framing density is fixed by the developed prefixes, independently of the cut position. This is an identity of rational functions before any quantum expansion. It also computes the exact cyclic norm of the principal density, with its exceptional factors retained. This calculation concerns the geometric framing density. Its finite root sampling is not asserted to be the Gaussian pushforward of the original finite source.
