The actual zero-source current in [the Fourier source audit](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) explains why a nonzero local geometric block alone cannot establish that assertion. ## 1. The rank-one difference removes the quadratic shell Use the signed developed prefixes U,V of [the actual Fourier polarization](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md), with det U=det V=1 and UV inverse the nontrivial TRACE-TWO meridian in that convention. Thus U-V has rank one. Choose a factorization U-V=u v, v=(a,b), w=v V inverse=(c,d). Here u is a column, v and w are rows, and w u=0. Rescaling u and v inversely has no effect on the formulas below. Keep the actual prefix sign sigma, equal to either +1 or -1. For F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], s nonzero, write V'=F inverse V F, ell_V=V'_11, k=ell_U/ell_V, C=U-kV, p=sigma (F inverse C F)_12/(k-1). The last equation is the ACTUAL balanced second-edge momentum, not a definition of the independent finite Fourier-band variable. The principal stationary incidence is eta_F=p inverse, with the same scope as the actual Fourier theorem. On the regular open where these expressions are defined, p=sigma [c(1-r)-ds]/[ar+bs], (1) r=[sigma(c-ds)-bsp]/[ap+sigma c]. (2) Here is a direct proof. The first row of F inverse(U-V)F is a scalar multiple of vF. Hence, denoting its first two entries by ell_D,beta_D, beta_D/ell_D=(vF)_2/(vF)_1. Since k-1=ell_D/ell_V, p/sigma=(beta_D/ell_D)ell_V-(V')_12. For a determinant-one matrix V', its inverse gives (vF)_2 ell_V-(vF)_1(V')_12=(v V inverse F)_2. This is exactly (1), and solving (1) gives (2). The calculation uses the full prefix matrices and the original sign. It does not pass through a choice of square root of the position discriminant. Put Delta(s)=sigma [s(ad-bc)-ac]. Then partial_p r=Delta(s)/(ap+sigma c)^2. (3) If Delta(s) is nonzero, (1)-(2) extend to mutually inverse maps of projective lines over the marked prefix field. The excluded values of s are explicit. The previously proved discrete-faithful argument ensures Delta(s) is not identically zero for an actual independent second position. No additional framing cover is needed. ## 2. The pole is intrinsic and does not move with the cut Suppose a is nonzero. Define lambda=-sigma c/a, D(s)=Delta(s)/a^2. Then r=infinity corresponds to p=lambda, and dr=D(s) dp/(p-lambda)^2 (4) on a fixed-s fiber. In particular the pole lambda is independent of s. If a=0, nondegeneracy forces c nonzero and r is affine in p; the corresponding pole is p=infinity. If c=0 and a nonzero, it is p=0. These cases are retained, rather than divided away. There is also a coordinate-free prefix expression on a regular chart. Put K=UV inverse. If c_U-c_V is nonzero, then lambda=-sigma c_K/(c_U-c_V), (5) where c_W is the lower-left entry of W in the marked cut frame. Indeed c_U-c_V=u_2 a and c_K=u_2 c. The same ratio is a marked trace-word function, since for J=[[1,1],[0,1]], c_W=Tr(JW)-Tr(W). Consequently this pole belongs to the fixed marked character field; it is not a free additional framing parameter. Formula (5) is not used on its vanishing-denominator chart; (1)-(4) remain the defining expressions there. ## 3. The actual geometric density has an explicit cyclic norm Retain the established geometric two-form and cut clock Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], A=1/(1+s). Using (3) without discarding its orientation gives Omega_cut= -Delta(s) p/[s(ap+sigma c)^2] dlog A wedge dlog p. (6) Thus in the finite-pole case its coefficient is T_s(p)=G(s) p/(p-lambda)^2, G(s)=-Delta(s)/(s a^2). (7) Let Q be a primitive N-th root, lambda^N different from one. The EXACT finite functional on this rational coefficient is (1/N) sum_(j=0)^(N-1) T_s(Q^j) =G(s) N lambda^(N-1)/(1-lambda^N)^2. (8) The original Fourier incidence samples p=Q^(-j), which has the same finite set of values and hence the same functional. Equation (8) is the logarithmic second derivative of product_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-lambda Q^(-j))=1-lambda^N. It is the SAME elementary cyclic-norm identity already proved in [the two-position density calculation](cyclic_framing_density_source.md), now on the birational Fourier fiber, with no quadratic field trace. The underlying differential (4) is exact, and its ordinary logarithmic residue vanishes. That does not make (8) zero. If lambda=0, (8) vanishes for N>1. In the pole-at-infinity case the coefficient in (6) is a scalar multiple of p, whose average also vanishes for N>1. For nonzero lambda off the unit circle, the limit of (1/N) log of the modulus in (8) is -abs(log abs(lambda)), provided G(s) is fixed and nonzero. Thus rationality and birationality alone do not provide a subexponential source estimate. Before root specialization the retained product is P_N(Q,lambda)=product_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-lambda Q^(-j)). Its logarithmic Q-normal derivative D_Q log P_N is the weighted sum sum_j j lambda Q^(-j)/(1-lambda Q^(-j)). One cannot replace P_N by 1-lambda^N before taking that derivative. The whole normal, the norm-zero fiber and any cancellation with another source factor must be kept. This is consistent with the explicit moving norm pole of [the original factorial atom](actual_negative_band_boundary_moment_and_ward_atom.md). ## 4. An actual figure-eight prefix and the scope of the theorem For the actual third prefix used in the polarization audit, u^2+u+1=0 and V=[[1,1],[-u,1-u]], U=[[u+1,2u+1],[1-u,3-u]], sigma=-1. One can take u_column=(u,1), v=(1,2), w=(1+u,1). Equations (1)-(3) become p=[s-(1+u)(1-r)]/[r+2s], r=[s-(1+u)-2sp]/[p-(1+u)], partial_p r=[(1+u)+(1+2u)s]/[p-(1+u)]^2. (9) The intrinsic pole is lambda=1+u=-u^2, of order six at either geometric embedding. It is independent of the good cut phase. For N divisible by six, principal-density sampling in (8) is undefined. The original finite tensor and its source are regular. Therefore simply sampling this principal density cannot be their whole source formula. A genuine comparison must explain this pole using the actual finite coefficients, walls and co-source. The projective-line description (1)-(4), the intrinsic pole (5), and the finite norm (8) are general prefix identities. They simplify the geometric fiber and locate its escaping boundary. They do not construct its quantum completion, show that the original last cyclic sum has a nonzero geometric coefficient, or prove the volume conjecture. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_mobius_fourier_framing.py) checks these formulas against raw conjugated matrices, including both prefix signs, finite and infinite poles, the figure-eight number field and independent companion-matrix cyclic traces. The [independent proof audit](mobius_and_flat_source_frame_independent_audit.md) also verifies the orientation, intrinsic pole, exceptional-fiber agreement and the distinction between the two normal divisors. The subsequent [universal actual-cut theorem](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) shows that the prefix-dependent pole can be normalized to p=1 by a genuine braid/inverse insertion and a first-slot physical cut, while preserving the original period and a regular geometric chart. This does not make principal sampling legitimate: the new density is resonant at every level. The full quantum source must be transported, including that escaping boundary layer.

title: The actual Newton source and its quantum canonical transform
text:
# The actual Newton source and its quantum canonical transform This note gives a generic Newton-index recurrence for the **actual** knot source, a finite pointing that determines it, and an exact selected-period formula. It also proves an explicit quantum birational transform and its classical canonical map. The classical map resolves a signed complete boundary point into the cut curve. No geometric-support or volume asymptotic assumption enters these statements. The final unresolved issue is selection and control of a geometric coefficient branch in the actual selected sum. An arbitrary root solution of the operator is insufficient. ## 1. Actual input and Newton interpolation Use the conventions of [the actual Fourier--Mellin source](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md): \(Q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)\), \(Y=M^2\), and the actual reduced periods satisfy \[ F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(Q_N)\quad(1\le j\le N),\qquad F_N(1)=C_N(Q_N)=\langle Kangle_N. 	ag{1.1} \] Here \(C_j(Q)\) are the actual finite-color Laurent polynomials over the recorded rational coefficient field, not a replacement state. Only fixed small colors will be needed as initial data. Whole reciprocity \(F_N(Y)=F_N(Y^{-1})\) is proved in [actual Weyl descent](actual_weyl_descent.md). A nonzero all-level operator over \(\mathbb Q(Q,Y)\) is proved in [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md). For generic \(Q\), put \[ a_j=Q^j+Q^{-j},\qquad t_n(X)=\prod_{r=1}^n(X-a_r),\qquad v_n(Y)=(1-Y)t_n(Y+Y^{-1}). \] The nodes \(a_1,a_2,\ldots\) are distinct in \(\mathbb Q(Q)\). Define the universal rational Newton coefficients by \[  oxed{c_n(Q)= \sum_{j=1}^{n+1}  rac{C_j(Q)} {\prod_{\substack{1\le r\le n+1\r
e j}}(a_j-a_r)}.} 	ag{1.2} \] This is the divided difference at the first \(n+1\) nodes; \(c_0=C_1=1\). Newton interpolation proves the exact identity \[  oxed{C_m(Q)=\sum_{n=0}^{m-1}c_n(Q)t_n(a_m)} \qquad(m\ge1). 	ag{1.3} \] For completeness, subtract the degree-\((m-2)\) interpolant at the first \(m-1\) nodes. Its difference from the degree-\((m-1)\) interpolant vanishes at these nodes, and hence is a scalar multiple of \(t_{m-1}\). Evaluation at the last node gives its scalar, equivalently (1.2). Induction proves (1.3). The formal series \[ \mathscr F(Q,Y)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_n(Q)t_n(Y+Y^{-1}) 	ag{1.4} \] is interpreted in the Newton completion, not as an asserted analytic series. Evaluation at \(Y=Q^m\) is finite: all terms \(n\ge m\) vanish. Thus it has exactly the actual fixed-color values \(C_m(Q)\). ## 2. Exact generic coefficient operators Let \(T f(Y)=f(QY)\), and put \[ X=Y+Y^{-1},\quad S=T+QT^{-1},\quad Z=YT+QY^{-1}T^{-1}. \] The generic banded identities proved directly in [whole-source Newton transport](whole_source_newton_transport.md) are \[ Xv_n=v_{n+1}+(Q^{n+1}+Q^{-n-1})v_n, \] \[ Sv_n=(Q^{n+1}+Q^{-n})v_n+\delta_n v_{n-1}, \] \[ Zv_n=Q^{n+1}v_{n+1}+(1+Q)Q^{2n+1}v_n +Q^n\delta_n v_{n-1}, \quad \delta_n=Q^{-2n}(1-Q^{2n})(1-Q^{2n+1}). 	ag{2.1} \] Use the bilateral index quantum torus \[ u c_n=Q^n c_n,\qquad E c_n=c_{n+1},\qquad Eu=QuE. \] Coefficients with negative index are set to zero. Set \[ d(u)=Q^{-2}u^{-2}(1-Q^2u^2)(1-Q^3u^2). \] The coefficient action, including the shifts of \(n\), is \[  oxed{\widehat X=E^{-1}+Qu+Q^{-1}u^{-1},} 	ag{2.2} \] \[  oxed{\widehat S=Qu+u^{-1}+d(u)E,} 	ag{2.3} \] \[  oxed{\widehat Z=uE^{-1}+(1+Q)Qu^2+Qu\,d(u)E.} 	ag{2.4} \] These preserve sequences supported on \(n\ge0\). In particular the possible output at \(n=-1\) from the \(E\) term vanishes because \(d(Q^{-1})=0\). This boundary fact is required: replacing unilateral shifts by invertible ones without checking the boundary would not define an exact transform. For any finite combination \(f=\sum_n c_n v_n\), (2.1) proves \[ A f=\sum_n(\widehat A c)_n v_n,\qquad A=X,S,Z. 	ag{2.5} \] It also holds for the Newton completion because each output coefficient uses only finitely many neighboring input coefficients. ### Generating-function form Let \(\mathcal C(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_n z^n\), and \(D_z\mathcal C(z)=\mathcal C(Qz)\). The same action is \[  oxed{\mathcal X=z+QD_z+Q^{-1}D_z^{-1},} 	ag{2.6} \] \[  oxed{\mathcal S=QD_z+D_z^{-1} +z^{-1} ig(D_z^{-2}-(1+Q)+QD_z^2 ig),} 	ag{2.7} \] \[  oxed{\mathcal Z=QzD_z+(1+Q)QD_z^2 +z^{-1} ig(D_z^{-1}-(1+Q)D_z+QD_z^3 ig).} 	ag{2.8} \] Each bracket multiplying \(z^{-1}\) kills a constant. Thus these preserve formal power series; there is no omitted constant-term source. The finite pointing in section 4 supplies the actual source data. ## 3. The transformed recurrence is actual at generic \(Q\) As proved in [whole-source Newton transport, section 6](whole_source_newton_transport.md), the actual all-level annihilator may be made nonzero and invariant under \[ 	heta(Y)=Y^{-1},\qquad 	heta(T)=QT^{-1}. \] Its fixed algebra is generated by \(X,S,Z\). Fix such an actual operator \[ R=R(Q;X,S,Z)
e0 \] annihilating \(f_N=(1-Y)F_N\), and form \[ \widehat R=R(Q;\widehat X,\widehat S,\widehat Z) =\sum_{k=p}^{r}b_k(Q,u)E^k. 	ag{3.1} \] Then the coefficients (1.2) satisfy the **generic exact recurrence** \[  oxed{\sum_{k=p}^{r}b_k(Q,Q^n)c_{n+k}(Q)=0 \quad(n\ge0),\qquad c_j=0\ (j<0).} 	ag{3.2} \] ### Proof by the actual whole source, not an off-root lift At a fixed root \(Q_N\), write the actual reciprocal Laurent polynomial as a polynomial in \(X\): \[ F_N(Y)=\sum_{m=0}^{D_N}c_m^{(N)}t_m(Y+Y^{-1}). \] The monic Newton polynomials remain a basis even if some nodes coincide. For a fixed \(m\), take \(N>2(m+1)\). The first \(m+1\) nodes are then distinct, so their actual values (1.1) give \[ c_m^{(N)}=c_m(Q_N). 	ag{3.3} \] Apply the exact root operator \(R\) and extract a fixed output coefficient \(n\) using (2.1). Only finitely many indices \(n+k\) occur. For every sufficiently large \(N\), all their coefficients are given by (3.3), and there are no coefficient poles. Consequently the rational function \[ H_n(Q)=\sum_k b_k(Q,Q^n)c_{n+k}(Q) \] vanishes at infinitely many distinct \(Q_N\). It is identically zero. This proves (3.2) for every fixed \(n\). No uniform limit in \(n,N\) and no claim of reciprocity for an arbitrary off-root matrix lift are used. ### Exact finite-root folding and its corner At \(Q=Q_N\), set \(U=Y^N\), \(W=U+U^{-1}-2\). If the actual finite Newton coefficients are collected as \[ C^{(N)}(z)=\sum_m c_m^{(N)}z^m =\sum_{s=0}^{N-1}z^s C_s^{(N)}(z^N), \] then the exact folded whole source is \[ f_N=\sum_{s=0}^{N-1} C_s^{(N)}(W)v_s. 	ag{3.4} \] This is \(v_{s+N}=Wv_s\); it retains the entire central corner. The finite matrices of \(X,S,Z\), including \(Wv_0\) in their last columns, are those of the whole-source transport note. Equation (3.3) concerns fixed indices and sufficiently large levels. It does **not** assert \(c_m^{(N)}=c_m(Q_N)\) simultaneously for every \(m<N\). At colliding nodes the latter expression can have poles, and whole parameter jets must be retained. There is an exact confluent extraction rule for the actual root polynomial \(P_N(X)=F_N(Y)\): \[ c_m^{(N)} =\sum_{\alpha} \operatorname{Res}_{X=\alpha}  rac{P_N(X)}{t_{m+1}(X)}\,dX, 	ag{3.5} \] where the sum runs over the distinct first \(m+1\) nodes, with their multiplicities retained in the denominator. To verify it, expand \(P_N\) in the Newton basis. Terms of index below \(m\) have no \(X^{-1}\) coefficient at infinity; the term of index \(m\) has coefficient \(1\); higher terms are divisible by \(t_{m+1}\) and have no finite residues. Repeated nodes therefore demand whole source jets rather than division by zero. For \(m<N\) their multiplicities are at most two, so values and first \(X\)-derivatives suffice. The last node at \(m=N-1\) includes \(X=2\), whose value is the selected period; this rule does not compute that missing value from nonidentity ordinary-root values. ## 4. Finite pointing and the selected Newton period The generic recurrence (3.2) determines its actual solution from finitely many fixed colors. Here is a direct bound. Left-multiply \(\widehat R\) by \(E^{-p}\), so its shifts are \(0,\ldots,d\), where \(d=r-p\). Clear a common coefficient denominator in \(Q\) and write \[ \widetilde R=\sum_{j=0}^d B_j(Q,u)E^j,\qquad B_j\in\mathbb Q[Q^{\pm1},u^{\pm1}],\quad B_d
e0. 	ag{4.1} \] The resulting recurrence is valid when \(n\ge\max(0,p)\). Let \(A_*\) be the \(Q\)-exponent span in the collected support of \(B_d\). For every integer \(n>A_*\), \(B_d(Q,Q^n)
e0\) identically: a collision between monomials \(Q^a u^b\), \(Q^{a'}u^{b'}\), with \(b
e b'\), would require \(n=|a-a'|/|b-b'|\le A_*\). Terms with equal \(b\) do not collide after collection. Choose \(n_*\ge\max(0,p,A_*+1)\). The finitely many coefficients \[ c_0,\ldots,c_{n_*+d-1} \] propagate rationally to all later indices. They require only the fixed ordinary colors \(C_1,\ldots,C_{n_*+d}\) through (1.2). For \(d=0\), the recurrence instead forces the tail \(c_n=0\) for \(n\ge n_*\). Thus no assumed order or regular-singular condition at \(n=0\) is needed. The selected period is now the following **whole regular evaluation**: \[  oxed{\langle Kangle_N= \left[ \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}c_n(Q) \prod_{j=1}^{n}  ig(Q^N+Q^{-N}-Q^j-Q^{-j} ig) ight]_{Q=Q_N}.} 	ag{4.2} \] Indeed the bracketed rational expression is exactly \(C_N(Q)\) by (1.3), and \(C_N(Q)\) is Laurent polynomial. It is regular at \(Q_N\), with value (1.1). This formula uses the actual finite pointing and actual operator. No new levelwise normalization is free. One must not replace (4.2) by \(\sum_{n<N}c_n(Q_N)t_n(2)\) unless the individual \(c_n\) are known regular there. Equation (4.2) first combines the whole germ, including all coefficient poles and cancellations. ### Uniformly bounded parameter jets Let \(D_*\) be the \(u\)-exponent span and \(s_*\) the number of monomials of \(B_d\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), the nonzero Laurent polynomial \(B_d(Q_N,u)\) has at most \(D_*\) zeros among a segment of fewer than \(N\) distinct orbit points \(u=Q_N^n\). Each nonzero substituted Laurent polynomial \(B_d(Q,Q^n)\) has at most \(s_*\) monomials. Its vanishing multiplicity at any nonzero \(Q\) is at most \(s_*-1\): otherwise its first \(s_*\) logarithmic derivatives give a Vandermonde system in its distinct integer exponents. The recurrence propagation needed to produce \(c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1}\) therefore has total pole budget at \(Q_N\) bounded by \[  oxed{B_*=D_*(s_*-1),} 	ag{4.3} \] outside finitely many levels where a fixed coefficient or initial denominator has a pole. Multiplication by the analytic weights in (4.2) does not increase it. A common propagation denominator gives a numerator whose prescribed vanishing cancels these poles, so a \(Q\)-jet of order at most \(B_*\) of the fixed initial data suffices for the regular value. This includes tangencies of the moving orbit \(u=Q^n\), not merely zeros of \(B_d(Q_N,u)\). ## 5. Exact quantum birationality Let \(\mathcal Q\) be the generic quantum torus generated by \(Y^{\pm1}\) and \(T^{\pm1}\), \(TY=QYT\), and let \(\mathcal A=\mathcal Q^	heta\). The assignments (2.2)--(2.4) give an injective homomorphism \[ \psi:\mathcal A\longrightarrow k\langle u^{\pm1},E^{\pm1}angle/(Eu=QuE). 	ag{5.1} \] To see that it is well defined, a relation in \(X,S,Z\) acts as zero on every \(v_n\), hence its coefficient action acts as zero on every finite sequence supported on \(n\ge0\). A finite difference operator \(\sum a_j(u)E^j\) doing so has \(a_j(Q^m)=0\) for infinitely many \(m\); each rational function \(a_j\) is zero. Thus the coefficient formulas respect all relations. For injectivity, if a quantum-torus element annihilates all \(v_n\), write it in normal form \(\sum_{a,b}r_{a,b}Y^aT^b\). Since \(v_n=-Y^{n+1}+\cdots\), the largest \(a\) gives \(\sum_b r_{a,b}Q^{b(n+1)}=0\) for all \(n\). The Vandermonde system in the distinct \(Q^b\) makes these coefficients zero. Descend through \(a\). The element is zero. Most importantly, the coefficient formulas obey the exact identity \[  oxed{\widehat Z=u(\widehat X+Q\widehat S)-(Q+Q^{-1}).} 	ag{5.2} \] Therefore in the quantum division ring \[  oxed{u=(\widehat Z+Q+Q^{-1}) (\widehat X+Q\widehat S)^{-1},\qquad E^{-1}=\widehat X-Qu-Q^{-1}u^{-1}.} 	ag{5.3} \] The order of the inverse in (5.3) is essential. Its denominator is nonzero since the \(E^{-1}\) coefficient in \(\widehat X+Q\widehat S\) is \(1\). These formulas prove an isomorphism of quantum fraction fields, not just a representation on special states. Here is a short justification that the fractions exist without importing a structural theorem. The quantum torus is an Ore domain: to find a common right multiple of nonzero \(a,b\), choose unknown multipliers in a large monomial square of side \(m\). There are \(2(m+1)^2\) unknown scalar coefficients and only \((m+O(1))^2\) output coefficients in \(ar-bs\), so a nonzero solution exists for large \(m\). The domain property ensures both multipliers are nonzero. The left argument is identical. Its fixed subalgebra is Ore too. For \(ar=bs\), with \(a,b\) invariant, average \(r,s\) with their images under \(	heta\). If the average is zero, both are anti-invariant; multiply both on the right by the nonzero anti-invariant \(Y-Y^{-1}\). The resulting common multipliers are invariant and nonzero. The left version is analogous. Thus (5.1) extends to fractions, and (5.3) shows its image contains the entire \(u,E\) quantum division ring. ## 6. Classical characteristic and the canonical chart At \(Q=1\), write \(e\) for the commuting symbol of \(E\). The transform is \[  oxed{ x=e^{-1}+u+u^{-1},\quad s=u+u^{-1}+(u-u^{-1})^2e,\quad z=u(x+s)-2.} 	ag{6.1} \] These obey \[ x^2+s^2+z^2-xsz-4=0. 	ag{6.2} \] They are birational coordinates on this Weyl-quotient boundary surface, with rational inverse \[  oxed{u= rac{z+2}{x+s},\qquad e= rac1{x-u-u^{-1}}.} 	ag{6.3} \] For a direct converse calculation, put \(u=(z+2)/(x+s)\); then \[ (x-u-u^{-1})(s-u-u^{-1})-(u-u^{-1})^2 =- rac{x^2+s^2+z^2-xsz-4}{z+2}. \] This proves the inverse on the displayed open chart. On the full boundary torus \(Y,L\), the same chart is \[  oxed{ u= rac{YL+1}{Y+L},\qquad e= rac{Y(Y+L)(YL+1)}{L(Y^2-1)^2}.} 	ag{6.4} \] Both functions are invariant under \((Y,L)\mapsto(Y^{-1},L^{-1})\). They generate its invariant function field, and direct differentiation gives \[ \{\log e,\log u\}=1 \quad	ext{when}\quad\{\log L,\log Y\}=1. 	ag{6.5} \] Thus this is a canonical chart on the quotient. The full boundary torus generically double-covers it; claiming birationality to the full \(Y,L\) curve would omit this Weyl cover. If \(R\) is normalized to have a nonzero classical symbol \(r(x,s,z)\), then the classical characteristic of \(\widehat R\) is precisely \(r\) after (6.1). Specialization is valid term by term; the map on classical function fields is injective, so no nonzero leading symbol is silently lost. Every curve component meeting the common open chart is carried birationally to its transformed component. This statement concerns the symbol of the **actual specified invariant operator**. It does not assume that its zero set has already been proved to be the geometric \(A\)-component. ### Exceptional curves and the signed complete point The chart has explicit exceptional factors \[ H_-=e(u-1)^2+u,\qquad H_+=e(u+1)^2+u,\qquad x+s= rac{H_-H_+}{eu^2}. 	ag{6.6} \] The curve \(H_-=0\) is collapsed to \((x,s,z)=(2,-2,-2)\), the quotient of \((Y,L)=(1,-1)\); \(H_+=0\) is collapsed to \((-2,2,-2)\). Thus the signed complete point cannot be evaluated by substituting into (6.3). A pulled-back characteristic can contain exceptional factors. Its proper transform is obtained only after removing components supported on the exceptional locus, or equivalently restricting to the common open chart and taking closure. For a branch \[ L=-1+\lambda(Y-1)+O((Y-1)^2) \] with finite generic slope, (6.4) resolves its direction to \[  oxed{u= rac{\lambda-1}{\lambda+1}.} 	ag{6.7} \] The companion resolved coordinate is \[ e= rac{1-\lambda^2}{4}=- rac{u}{(u-1)^2}. \] Both follow by substituting the first-order branch in (6.4), retaining the quadratic numerator and denominator in \(e\). If \(	au=d\log(-L)/d\log Y=-\lambda\), this is \(u=(	au+1)/(	au-1)\). For \(\operatorname{Im}	au>0\) its image has imaginary part \(-2\operatorname{Im}	au/|	au-1|^2<0\). This is an algebraic direction calculation, not a proof that the actual source selects that branch. ## 7. The kernel action and the cut curve The exact Newton kernel is \[ t_n(Y)=(-1)^n Q^{-n(n+1)/2} (QY;Q)_n(Q/Y;Q)_n. 	ag{7.1} \] On a simply connected logarithmic chart, let \(U=\log u\), \(y=\log Y\). The dilogarithmic kernel potential is \[ \mathcal K(U,y)=i\pi U- rac{U^2}{2} +\operatorname{Li}_2(Y)+\operatorname{Li}_2(Y^{-1}) -\operatorname{Li}_2(uY)-\operatorname{Li}_2(u/Y). 	ag{7.2} \] Direct differentiation, using \(d\operatorname{Li}_2(z)=-\log(1-z)\,d\log z\), gives compatible branches of \[  rac{\partial\mathcal K}{\partial U} =\log(Y+Y^{-1}-u-u^{-1})=-\log e,\qquad  rac{\partial\mathcal K}{\partial y} =\log rac{uY-1}{Y-u}=\log L. 	ag{7.3} \] Thus \(d\mathcal K=\log L\,d\log Y-\log e\,d\log u\), another direct proof of the canonical identity. These are exact local period identities; no assertion about an actual coefficient asymptotic is used. If a coefficient phase has adjacent ratio \(e\), the selected sum at \(Y=1\) has the stationary equation \[ e(2-u-u^{-1})=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad  oxed{e=- rac{u}{(u-1)^2}.} 	ag{7.4} \] It is exactly the exceptional curve \(H_-=0\) above the signed complete point. A candidate critical point is therefore the intersection of the coefficient characteristic with this resolved cut curve. Equation (7.4) identifies the algebraic stationary equation; it does not establish existence, domination, phase cancellation bounds, or selection of any actual coefficient branch. As a diagnostic only, for \(s=x^2-x-4\), substitution gives \[ s-(x^2-x-4)= rac{(e-1)H_-H_+}{e^2u^2}. \] Its proper transform is \(e=1\), and intersection with \(H_-=0\) yields \(u^2-u+1=0\). This illustrates why exceptional factors must be retained and then distinguished from the proper transform, rather than discarded before the source has been resolved. ## 8. What root operator data alone do not select There is an explicit counterexample to selection from only a root operator, reciprocity, degree, and nonidentity ordinary-root values. At each level let \[ f_0=1-Y,\qquad f_1=Y^N-Y^{1-N}. \] Both are exactly \(J\)-fixed and satisfy \((S-1-Q_N)f_i=0\). For any scalar \(\varepsilon_N\), put \[ F_N^\varepsilon(Y) =1+\varepsilon_N\left(  rac{Y^N-Y^{1-N}}{1-Y}-1ight). 	ag{8.1} \] The quotient is a Laurent polynomial of degree \(N-1\) in \(X\). This family is reciprocal, has the same fixed root operator and degree bound, and obeys \[ F_N^\varepsilon(Q_N^j)=1\quad(1\le j<N),\qquad F_N^\varepsilon(1)=1-2N\varepsilon_N. 	ag{8.2} \] In particular \(\varepsilon_N=a^N\) can have arbitrary exponential growth while remaining a proper finite hypergeometric factor. The weighted source difference is the exact normal class \[ (1-Y)(F_N^\varepsilon-1) =\varepsilon_N(U-1)(1+Y/U). \] This does **not** refute the actual all-level pointing construction. For every fixed color \(j\), the infinitely many nonidentity values in (8.2) would force \(C_j(Q)\equiv1\). Actual complete-color compatibility then requires \(F_N(1)=C_N(Q_N)=1\), excluding \(\varepsilon_N
e0\). The generic Newton recurrence and selected evaluation in sections 1--4 retain precisely this missing cross-level source condition; levelwise interpolation alone does not. ## 9. Proven outcome and remaining work For every actual knot state, a specified actual all-level operator and finitely many fixed small colors determine a generic Newton-index solution and its selected regular period (4.2), with the bounded parameter jets in (4.3). The operator transform is quantum birational. Its characteristic is the actual invariant-symbol characteristic in canonical coordinates, with an explicit exceptional cut curve at signed completion. To derive a volume theorem from this construction still requires an actual-source theorem selecting a geometric proper-transform branch and controlling its coefficient period, including its regulator normalization and the contribution to (4.2). None of those selection or dominance claims follows just from the birational transform. [The independent audit script](../experiments/audit_newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.py) checks the exact operator, source, and canonical identities without ordinary-color extrapolation or numerical asymptotic fitting. It passes 278 exact checks: 119 coefficient/power-series identities, 17 ordinary and confluent interpolation checks, 21 canonical/kernel identities, and 121 finite-root source checks at levels \(2,\ldots,12\).

title: The Newton chart resolves the complete boundary point and its cut
text: # The Newton chart resolves the complete boundary point and its cut Research proof, 27 October 2026. The exact Newton source transform has a classical meaning at the complete hyperbolic boundary character: it resolves the signed peripheral singularity and turns completeness into the stationary equation of the universal cut kernel. This is uniform in the knot and its bridge number. The actual quantum Newton transform and its coefficient recurrence are separate exact constructions. This note compares their classical chart and kernel with the marked geometric target. It does not prove that a chosen actual operator has geometric classical support, or that the actual selected period couples to that geometric branch. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. The classical Newton coordinates Use the boundary quantum-torus convention TY=QYT. Its commuting symbols are Y,L. Weighted Weyl inversion sends (Y,L) to (Y^(-1),L^(-1)). Put x=Y+Y^(-1), s=L+L^(-1), z=YL+(YL)^(-1). Direct expansion gives the Fricke surface x^2+s^2+z^2-xsz-4=0. (1) In the Newton coefficient chart write u for the index character Q^n and e for the symbol of the forward coefficient shift. The rational map to (1) is x=e^(-1)+u+u^(-1), s=u+u^(-1)+(u-u^(-1))^2 e, z=u(x+s)-2. (2) Away from the displayed denominator loci its inverse is u=(z+2)/(x+s), e=1/(x-u-u^(-1)). (3) In the full boundary torus these coordinates are u=(YL+1)/(Y+L), e=Y(Y+L)(YL+1)/[L(Y^2-1)^2]. (4) Both functions are Weyl invariant. Substitution proves (2)--(4). Their differential identity is dlog Y wedge dlog L=dlog u wedge dlog e. (5) Thus this is a symplectic birational chart on the Weyl quotient, with a degree-two map from the full torus. It does not remove the marked eigenvalue/sign cover where that cover is needed. The exact whole-source operators X,S,Z and their finite-root lattice are proved in [the whole-source transport note](whole_source_newton_transport.md). ## 2. The complete signed point and a regular exceptional curve Work at the marked complete point Y=1, L=-1, (x,s,z)=(2,-2,-2). (6) This is a singular point of (1). The sign in (6) is retained as part of the longitude lift. A convention with a different complete longitude must first apply its corresponding recorded sign change; substitution of L=1 into (4) is a different chart situation. Define g(u)=2-u-u^(-1), r=1-e g(u). (7) Equation (2) gives the exact identity r=e(x-2). (8) The curve E_cut: r=0, e=-u/(u-1)^2 (9) maps entirely to (6). Indeed x=2; also (u-u^(-1))^2/g(u)=-(u+1)^2/u, so s=-2 and z=-2. This curve is regular for u!=0,1,infinity in the Newton torus. The two-form in (5) becomes dlog u wedge dlog e =-du/u wedge dr/(1-r). (10) It is nondegenerate at r=0. Thus the chart resolves this portion of the singular boundary point symplectically, with a genuine regular normal coordinate r. Its exceptional curve is not deleted by taking the complete value first. ## 3. The geometric branch meets this curve transversely Take a marked positive geometric gluing branch etale over the meridian, as supplied by the existing positive gluing-Jacobian proof. Put y=Log Y and lambda=Log(-L), centered at (6), and write lambda(y)=tau y+O(y^3), Im tau>0. (11) The positive imaginary sign uses the recorded boundary orientation. The absence of even powers uses Weyl inversion and preservation of the marked place. Generically swap the two peripheral eigenflags. At the complete nontrivial parabolic meridian they both specialize to its unique eigenline. All developed flags and their cross-ratios therefore specialize to the same nondegenerate positive shapes. The smooth gluing germ is the same normalization place after this swap. The involution fixes it and sends y,lambda to -y,-lambda. Etaleness over y then gives the odd expansion (11). This also explains why the eigenflag cover is retained before quotienting. Substitution in (4) gives finite limits u_0=(tau+1)/(tau-1), e_0=(1-tau^2)/4. (12) For example the first quotient is -(sinh((y+lambda)/2))/(sinh((y-lambda)/2)); its common simple zero cancels since tau!=1. Formula (12) follows directly from the first-order terms of the numerator and denominator in (4). Both functions are even holomorphic germs in y. Moreover Im u_0=-2 Im tau/|tau-1|^2<0, e_0=-u_0/(u_0-1)^2!=0. (13) The trace-normal coordinate w=x-2=y^2+O(y^4) is a parameter on the normalized Weyl-quotient geometric germ. Its strict transform in the Newton chart satisfies, exactly, r(w)=e(w)w, r'(0)=e_0!=0. (14) Consequently the geometric germ is smooth there and intersects E_cut transversely. It is etale over r. Every nilpotent r-lift of that selected geometric place has a unique curve lift by the same elementary inverse-function/Newton argument. This statement requires no hypothesis that u itself be a local parameter. If its u projection ramifies, one retains the two-coordinate curve rather than dividing by du/dw. The cusp derivative tau is algebraic at the complete shape place: differentiating the integer gluing and peripheral equations gives an invertible linear system with algebraic coefficients. Hence u_0,e_0 are algebraic there too. A cusp field can be smaller than the full marked shape field. The pair (u_0,e_0) need not distinguish every representation place; the original geometric/shape marking is retained. The lower-half-plane condition alone is not a global geometric-selection theorem. ## 4. The same exceptional curve is the stationary cut equation The actual Newton kernel is t_n(Y)=product_(j=1)^n(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^j-Q^(-j)) =(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+1)/2)(QY;Q)_n(Q/Y;Q)_n. (15) For H=Log Q, U=Log u and a matched logarithmic sheet, its leading generating action is K(Y,u)=i*pi*U-U^2/2+Li_2(Y)+Li_2(Y^(-1)) -Li_2(uY)-Li_2(u/Y). (16) Its derivatives are exact dilogarithm identities: partial_U K=Log(x-u-u^(-1)), partial_y K=Log[(uY-1)/(Y-u)]=Log L. (17) The logarithms are continued together; integers in their sheets are not independently reset. Equation (17) is precisely the canonical relation (4), with e=exp(-partial_U K). It can be checked without an asymptotic argument. Formula (16) is the integral of Log(x-v-v^(-1)) dlog v from the lower endpoint of the product, on the same sheet; ordinary Euler summation recovers it wherever that product avoids its endpoint/polar divisors. No uniform selected-knot asymptotic is inferred from this local kernel calculation. If a coefficient branch has action S_c with dS_c=Log e dlog u, the stationary equation for its pairing with the cut at Y=1 is partial_U(S_c+K(1,u))=0 iff e(2-u-u^(-1))=1 iff r=0. (18) Thus the universal cut meets the transformed geometric branch at exactly the resolved complete point (12). Completeness becomes a transverse Lagrangian intersection in the regular Newton surface. This is a general geometric statement, not a recognition from the two prototype knots. The transform preserves the peripheral action differential: d(S_c+K)=Log L dlog Y (19) on its stationary relation. The marked Bloch fundamental class still supplies the integration constant and the complete volume value. Equation (19) alone does not determine that constant or show that the actual coefficient solution has this branch. ## 5. The finite-root normal adapter and its N-squared factor Let C_N(x) be the monic Chebyshev polynomial defined by C_N(Y+Y^(-1))=Y^N+Y^(-N). With U_c=Y^N retained, the exact central corner is W=U_c+U_c^(-1)-2=C_N(x)-2. (20) It has the polynomial factorization C_N(x)-2=(x-2)H_N(x), H_N(2)=N^2. (21) For the value, put x=2cosh y and differentiate 2cosh(Ny)-2=N^2 y^2+O(y^4), 2cosh y-2=y^2+O(y^4). Equivalently differentiate the polynomial identity at x=2; this is an exact algebraic leading coefficient. Thus W=N^2 w+O(w^2). The central trace normal and the ordinary trace normal have a specified, nonzero N-squared adapter. This does not identify their normalization with that of the first Bockstein normal U_c-1: W=(U_c-1)^2/U_c is quadratic in it. In logarithmic eigenvalue coordinate y, U_c-1=N y+O(y^2), so the physical first-normal cut carries N, while the trace-to-trace adapter carries N^2. Both directions and factors are retained. At U_c=1, H_N(X)/N^2 is exactly the projector onto the simple X=2 line of the full abstract source lattice fiber: it is one there, and zero with the required multiplicities at the other roots of C_N(X)-2. This is the distinguished source line proved in [the source/monodromy chain-map note](source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap.md). It is a statement about that retained source fiber, not a global rank-one projector on the unsplit generic field cover. ## 6. Remaining source-selection theorem This supplies a regular algebraic geometric target and a canonical cut equation, with the exact normal adapter. Rivin positivity and the gluing Jacobian select its marked algebraic place. The actual quantum Newton transform preserves the original period and its normal source data. To prove the conjecture one still has to establish that the actual coefficient/module object carries this geometric branch with the selected regulator period, and control its norm at the prescribed cyclotomic evaluation. Transversality proves a nondegenerate geometric candidate intersection. It does not by itself give its coefficient in the original selected quantum period, exclude cancellation, or prove a uniform asymptotic estimate. [Exact algebraic audit](../experiments/audit_newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut.py). [Audit results](../experiments/newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut_results.json). [Independent proof audit](newton_resolution_independent_audit.md). The [actual Newton canonical transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) proves the generic coefficient recurrence and exact selected whole-germ period, with finite actual pointing. The [partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) now proves a geometric factor for an actual two-index extension by transverse-only telescoping. Its final framing contraction is still required to reach the selected scalar invariant.

title: Independent audit of the geometric Newton resolution and normal scales
text: # Independent audit of the geometric Newton resolution and normal scales Audit, 27 October 2026, of [the Newton resolution note](newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut.md), especially Sections 3 and 5. The strict-transform calculation and its etaleness conclusion are correct with the marked Weyl-stability hypothesis explained below. No actual-symbol or selected-period assertion follows from them. ## 1. The logarithmic branch and its involution Write Y=exp(y), L=-exp(lambda), keeping the complete sign L=-1. Assume the selected geometric normalization germ is smooth, etale over y, and fixed by the simultaneous eigenflag-swap involution. Then its local ring is k[[y]], the involution sends y to -y and lambda to -lambda. Consequently lambda(y) is odd: lambda=tau y+c_3 y^3+... . (1.1) Etaleness over y alone does not imply oddness. For example lambda=tau y+b_2y^2 is etale over y and has any prescribed nonreal cusp derivative, but is not Weyl stable when b_2!=0. Thus the eigenflag assertion is an essential part of the proof. For the marked complete hyperbolic place, that assertion has a direct geometric justification. Generically swap the two peripheral eigenflags while keeping the representation. At the complete nontrivial parabolic meridian, both flags specialize to its unique eigenline. Develop the vertex flags and take the cross-ratios in the specified positive triangulation. At the complete point all the cross-ratio denominators are units. The swapped decoration therefore specializes to the same nondegenerate complete shapes. Equivalently, the rational involution extends over the valuation ring of the normalized curve and has the same closed shape point. Smoothness of this gluing germ means there is only one normalization place at that point. The involution fixes that place. Its action on the recorded peripheral eigenvalues is precisely inversion. This argument retains the shape place and the peripheral lift. Invariance of an unmarked A-polynomial by itself would not exclude exchanging distinct normalization places over its singular point. ## 2. Exact limits and the transverse parameter The chart formulas become the following exact identities of germs: u=-sinh((y+lambda)/2)/sinh((y-lambda)/2), e=[cosh(y)-cosh(lambda)]/[2sinh(y)^2]. (2.1) The common zeros cancel, since Im(tau)>0 implies tau!=+1,-1. Both germs are even, hence functions of w=2cosh(y)-2. Their limits are u_0=(tau+1)/(tau-1), e_0=(1-tau^2)/4, e_0=-u_0/(u_0-1)^2!=0. (2.2) For tau=a+ib, b>0, Im(u_0)=-2b/[(a-1)^2+b^2]<0. The invariant local ring is k[[y^2]]=k[[w]]. The exact algebraic identity r=e(x-2) therefore gives r=e(w)w, dr/dw at 0=e_0!=0. (2.3) It follows that the strict transform is a smooth algebraic germ, is transverse to r=0, and is etale over the algebraic coordinate r. The usual unique lifting over nilpotent thickenings follows at the retained marked place. This uses no nonzero du/dw assumption. One can see the last point even for a constant u projection. Fix u=u_0, put e_0=1/(2-u_0-u_0^(-1)), and set e(w)=e_0/(1+e_0 w), r(w)=e_0 w/(1+e_0 w). (2.4) This is still a transverse strict-transform branch. Thus division by du/dw would incorrectly discard valid branches of the chart. For reference the general first coefficient is du/dw at 0=(tau^3-tau-12c_3)/[6(tau-1)^2], which can vanish without affecting (2.3). The normalization matters: tau here is dlog(-L)/dlog Y. If the earlier meridian coordinate is M and Y=M^2, this tau is one half of dlog(-L)/dlog M. An inverse longitude convention also reverses its imaginary sign. The note's formulas are correct in its stated Y,L and boundary-orientation convention. ## 3. The N-squared adapter is trace-to-trace For C_N(Y+Y^(-1))=Y^N+Y^(-N), define w=x-2, U_c=Y^N, W=U_c+U_c^(-1)-2=C_N(x)-2. Then, exactly, C_N(x)-2=(x-2)H_N(x), H_N(2)=N^2, W=N^2w+N^2(N^2-1)w^2/12+... . (3.1) The projector H_N(X)/N^2 on the abstract source fiber is precisely the simple X=2 projector in [the source/monodromy chain map](source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap.md). The multiplicities at the other roots are retained, so the assertion is about the full possibly nonsemisimple source fiber. There are two different normal scales here. W is the Weyl-invariant central trace normal, whereas U_c-1 is the ordinary central first normal uniformizer: W=(U_c-1)^2/U_c, U_c-1=N y+O(y^2), w=y^2+O(y^4). Thus N^2 is the trace-to-trace adapter. It is not a linear identification of the first Bockstein normal U_c-1 with x-2. The physical cut still has its linear factor N: f=(U_c-1)b -> cut(f)=-N b(1). For the canonical projector generator the divided-normal value is -1/N, making its cut exactly one. This agrees with (3.1) and does not replace the first-normal row by a trace evaluation. ## 4. Scope The calculation supplies a regular algebraic target at the marked geometric place, a transverse cut equation and an exact retained normal normalization. It does not prove that the actual quantum Newton coefficient object has that geometric component or that the original selected source couples to its regulator period. [Exact independent audit](../experiments/audit_newton_resolution_independent.py). [Results](../experiments/newton_resolution_independent_results.json).

title: Independent audit of the one-index actual source and fixed-phase operator
text: # Independent audit of the one-index actual source and fixed-phase operator Proof audit, 27 October 2026, of [the actual source/Ward reduction](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) and Section 8 of [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). The normalization, whole Ward defect, polynomial bound and root-only phase specialization pass. The final selected Fourier-label sum remains unproved geometrically. ## 1. The actual fixed-input source Root K,F intertwining makes the reclosed C diagonal, then equates successive entries through nonzero arrows 1-Q_N^k. Thus C=P_N(M)I, with the SAME original peripheral line on both sides. This uses no E edge, reducibility assumption or inversion of a vanishing norm. The full original first-cut row gives lambda_a(C)=sum_c C_(c,a). Partial trace on the second wire proves sum_j Jtilde_(a,j)=lambda_a(C) for the WHOLE invertible Vandermonde change. On the root scalar closure this is P_N(M) for every a. Hence the one-index source has NO outside 1/N; its raw Jtilde still has the Fourier inverse 1/N inside. The output c remains summed. Setting c=a first would remove the momentum bands and is not this source change. ## 2. The whole current guard and its bound For D_K=Ad K-I and D_F(C)=FC-K^-1CKF, direct entries give (D_K C)_ij=(Q^(j-i)-1)C_ij, (D_F C)_(k,k-1)=(1-Q^k)(C_(k-1,k-1)-C_(k,k)). There is no off-diagonal pollution in the latter row. Dividing these head units and centering the diagonal chain therefore gives h delta C=C-I Tr(C)/N as a WHOLE matrix identity. Neither 1-Q^N nor a color-normal edge is inverted. With Gamma_a=(e_a-1/N)1^t, where 1 is the all-ones column, lambda_a-Phi=Tr(Gamma_a h delta). This proves the stated cochain source identity. It sets delta C=0 only on the actual root Hopf closure. Every whole derivative of h, delta and C remains in its printed Taylor convolution. For scalar C_0 the operator derivatives satisfy delta_j(C_0)=0, since delta_t(I)=0 for all t; the stated first-order simplification is consequently valid without off-root scalarity. The root balanced-flat norm estimate also passes. Anchor at the middle vertex. Left and reflected right edge inputs and anchored outputs are disjoint; the inverse-arrow factors are bounded by N/[4 min(k,N-k)]. Each block is dominated by N/4 times the Hardy-tail kernel 1/k for i<=k. With weights i^-1/2 its row and column bounds are respectively three and two, so its norm is at most sqrt(6). Mean subtraction is orthogonal projection. The K inverse is at most N/4 and has orthogonal output to the diagonal primitive. For the direct-sum Hilbert--Schmidt input norm this proves ||h||<=3N/4. Since ||Gamma_a||_HS=sqrt(N-1), the source primitive is bounded by (3N/4)sqrt(N-1). This is not a whole-word or geometric-period bound and does not assert a uniform root neighborhood. ## 3. Fixed phase and whole power marks The finite bad-fiber argument is valid after clearing the finitely many rational shape/Jacobian denominators. A whole excluded A fiber requires all coefficient polynomials in the other coordinate to vanish. If a unit is algebraic on a retained finite cover, its field norm gives the same sufficient test. The operator's nonzero leading symbol similarly excludes finitely many half-phase fibers. Infinite root-of-unity half-phases provide a good fixed k/d. For a_N=floor(kN/d) and r=kN modulo d, the root formulas are A_N=exp(2pi*i*k/d) q_N^(-2r/d), Ahat_N=exp(pi*i*k/d) q_N^(-r/d). Before normal differentiation their actual power graph is A_N=(Q^N)^(k/d)Q^(-r/d) and Ahat_N=(q^N)^(k/d)q^(-r/d), with logarithmic marks N Log Q and N Log q. Thus D_Q Log A_N=a_N; freezing its root phase first would give only -r/d. The notes preserve this distinction. The root operator substitution Ahat=alpha_* q^(-r/d) is an Ore homomorphism because the meridian shift fixes these characters. The good-phase choice keeps its first classical symbol nonzero; its preexisting polynomial divisibility by A_geo specializes unchanged. On q=z^d the leading order gains only the nonzero scalar d^s. The nondegenerate geometric block persists on this marked meridian/phase germ with its same frame-independent action. A common LEFT multiple may combine the finite residue-class operators; an arbitrary ordered product would not justify that claim. None of this identifies the root partial lift with whole Vandermonde normal jets or proves geometric survival after sum_j.

title: Independent audit of the actual horizontal meridian source transport
text: # Independent audit of the actual horizontal meridian source transport 27 October 2026. Detailed examination of the revised SECOND-wire construction in [the actual open-meridian theorem](actual_open_meridian_horizontal_source_transport.md). The main scaled Vandermonde is a whole source-preserving basis change on arbitrary finite tensors. The optional first-wire construction has the stated Ward correction; it is not needed to justify the main map. The regulator/selected-period comparison remains an additional theorem. ## 1. The actual local and open-word half-character has the stated sign For the positive actual coefficient the monomial x power changes by q^(-i-j-k), while the Pochhammer ratio is (1-z Q^k)/(1-z), z=Y/A. The displayed tau_+ inverse contributes that ratio times x/(BC). Multiplying x inverse and q^(j+k-i) gives exactly q^(-i-j-k). The negative coefficient similarly gives q^(i+j-k): its tau_- inverse contributes A/x and its first output is j-k. These are canceled whole finite-product identities, not separate evaluation of their zero factors. For either sign the integer potential -sum_i i a_i changes by first output minus first input. The opened matrix unit changes it by ell nu. Every old closed strand returns to its input and the first cut has coefficient zero in the potential. Thus the crossing contribution is -ell nu exactly, including unwrapped integer values. This establishes q^(-ell nu), not its inverse. Each old closed pivot contributes q^(1-N) under the common meridian step and the residual framing line contributes q^(w(N-1)). Hence gamma_N=q^((N-1)(w-b+1)) is correct. For a knot w-b+1 is even; its root simplification does not justify discarding the whole q^N character before normal derivatives. Opening the internal identity adds no pivotal cap. ## 2. The second-wire gauge preserves the source for every finite tensor Use D_2=diag(M^(-ell b)) and \[ T_h=(I\otimes D_2^{-1})T(I\otimes D_2),\qquad W=V(Q)D_2^{-1},\quad W_{j,b}=(M^\ell Q^j)^b. \] Its coefficient is M^(ell(d-b))=M^(ell nu) with NO charge qualification. This cancels q^(-ell nu) in the actual open-word meridian relation. Since the second closure is its identity trace and every original pivot is already inside T, partial trace of this conjugation is EXACTLY unchanged on all first-wire entries. The first input/output source can therefore remain literally the original one on arbitrary finite current tensors too. No Schur scalarity argument is needed. It would be incorrect to leave a separately untransformed pivotal matrix on that second trace; the literal opened-identity tensor already fixes its location. The current theorem uses the correct tensor convention. The scaled node differences are M^ell(Q^i-Q^j). Thus W introduces only the old Vandermonde head units and a meridian monomial, not a new peripheral norm denominator. Its whole inverse is D_2 V inverse. The identity W(qM)D_rho=W(M), rho=q^(-ell), proves the revised whole matrix meridian equation with its original L insertion. Consequently arbitrary ordered operators and source/current maps transport by this basis change before any jets. The separate pure L path identity concerns the stated actual word and its covariantly transported insertion complex; it is not permission to hold an arbitrary M-dependent inserted coupon fixed under a meridian step. ## 3. Whole matrix connection and packet connection are different objects Direct differentiation gives \[ \Gamma_M=(D_MW)W^{-1}=\ell VJ_{head}V^{-1},\qquad \Gamma_Q=(D_QV)V^{-1}\quad(M\text{ fixed}), \] \[ D_M T^W=W(D_MT)W^{-1}+[\Gamma_M,T^W]. \] Thus the covariant derivative has sign D_M minus ad Gamma_M. The commutator's partial trace is zero ENTRYWISE on the first wire. Every mixed/normal derivative of the exact source identity is preserved by the product rule, including the actual M(q) chain rule. At the root V divided by sqrt N is unitary, so the full matrix connection has norm ell(N-1). This is a source frame estimate, not a bound on the actual crossing word. For a charge-zero fixed-input a the scalar packet instead has unwrapped representatives nu=a-c, c=0,...,N-1. Its matrix is \[ H_a=F_a\operatorname{diag}(M^{\ell\nu})F_a^{-1},\quad (F_a)_{j,c}=Q_N^{j(a-c)}. \] The nu=0 column is the all-ones vector. It follows exactly that H_a times ones is ones and Sigma H_a=Sigma. Cyclic shifts, normalized differences and their centered primitive are diagonal in that same root Fourier basis, so H_a commutes with them. For absolute M one the map is unitary; the distance to the zero-source cyclic current space is therefore unchanged AT THE SAME M. This does not compare the norms of different meridian states or turn the L insertion into a scalar longitude. The packet connection is A_a=ell F_a diag(a-c)F_a inverse, with zero source and constant mode and norm at most ell(N-1). It is not the full Gamma_M above. More explicitly, on the common Fourier-label space, for a<N-1, \[ A_{a+1}-A_a=\ell N\Pi_{a+1},\qquad H_{a+1}H_a^{-1}=I+(M^{\ell N}-1)\Pi_{a+1}, \tag{1} \] where Pi_(a+1) is the Fourier-mode projector with residue a+1. Only one unwrapped representative has changed by N. This proves why packets for different a cannot be silently identified through their residues. Charged/unwrapped tail modules retain their own independent alias powers and the full tensor map, as the note states. ## 4. Peripheral and alias powers remain whole The complete ratio is exactly \[ \frac{d_N(qM)}{d_N(M)} =q^{N-1}\frac{q^2M^2-1}{M^2-1} \frac{M^{2N}-1}{q^{2N}M^{2N}-1}. \] The formula follows from the original finite S_N ratio, with the same phase on the two sides. It is a canceled whole meromorphic germ; norm-zero numerator and denominator are not evaluated separately. At a root its generic-M reduction agrees with the known -q inverse peripheral gauge, but that reduction does not give its whole q-normal adapter. The independent alias V_eta=eta^N transforms by V_eta to (q^N)^(-ell)V_eta. At the actual root this is the sign (-1)^ell. A head window has only its zero multiple of N, so its constant coefficient is unchanged even on the antiperiodic grid. Unwrapped current tails can have other multiples, whose retained characters and normal derivatives cannot be omitted. The optional first-wire source formula also passes. Its coefficient M^(ell(a-c))-1 is precisely the quotient by the genuine head Cartan gap Q^(a-c)-1 times the actual D_K entry. The packet derivative signs, wrap M^(ell N), and polynomial source-row bounds are correct. They are an alternative source homotopy, not a substitute for the exact all-tensor invariance of the main second leg. ## 5. The geometric filter formulas have their exact conditional scope For p_hor=alpha p, alpha=M^ell, the coordinate density transforms as \[ G\frac p{(p-\lambda)^2}d\log p =\alpha G\frac{p_{hor}}{(p_{hor}-\alpha\lambda)^2} d\log p_{hor}. \] This extra factor alpha is necessary. It makes the finite-filter ratio alpha^N times [(1-lambda^N)/(1-alpha^N lambda^N)] squared, with the printed M derivative at one. The finite sampling identity on p^N=S has numerator N S lambda^(N-1); antiperiodic S=-1 therefore retains its minus sign. The proven Möbius/single-pole framing theorem is complete-M only. The horizontal gauge alone does not extend that theorem to general M. The current note correctly makes a marked lambda(M) branch conditional and does not identify its rational filter with the actual quantum source. Its singularities must be accounted for by the actual whole word/source correction, not hidden by this gauge. ## 6. The remaining Green residual is typed and nonzero in general With sigma_M I_h=L I_h and R_i=S_i I_h/I_h, one obtains sigma_M R_i/R_i=S_i L/L. Therefore \[ L\,d_{\sigma R,i}(f)=d_{R,i}(Lf) \] with exactly the displayed order. This is a genuine semilinear connection on the proper-array insertion/current complex. Full zero extension retains its boundary strata. After source pairing, multiplying an ordinary difference by L leaves the finite residual sum_s [L(s-e_i)-L(s)]H(s). It is not generally zero and does not become zero by substituting the critical longitude into the sum. Thus the theorem removes a real endpoint half-character and supplies a tame actual source transport. It does not prove a nonzero selected geometric quotient, kill actual zero-source currents in that quotient, or bound the selected regulator norm. Those are correctly stated as remaining source/word comparisons rather than normalization choices.

title: A macroscopic polynomial quantum-normal window for every fixed plat
text: # A macroscopic polynomial quantum-normal window for every fixed plat 28 October 2026. For an original knot presented as a fixed 2k-plat, ordinary-color quantum-normal jets are polynomially bounded throughout k(j-1)+1<=N. (1) The endpoint is INCLUDED. This follows from a one-sided angular positive-path interval and elementary polynomial differentiation; no derivative of a singular root path basis is taken. Thus the conclusion controls a macroscopic part of the actual pointed quantum-A source, not only finitely many small colors. It does not bound the remaining high-color packet or independent meridian derivatives of the root ADO state. ## 1. Exact original family and statement Let C_j(q) denote the original reduced, zero-framed ordinary integral color-j knot scalar. The ordinary pivot is K(q), with its matching ribbon twist. At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), j<N, its equality with the original reduced root state is the independently proved quotient/cabling comparison, with the actual half-Cartan and parity adapters retained. Off the root this note uses that ORDINARY integral family. It does not differentiate a frozen ADO pivot as though it were the same family. Fix the plat word and k. Its actual Laurent degree in the marked variable z=q^(1/2) obeys deg_Laurent C_j <=D_j<=C_word (j+1)^2. (2) For every fixed r>=1 there is a constant C_(word,r) such that, for all N and j>=1 satisfying (1), |partial_s^r C_j(q_N(1+s/N)) at s=0| <=C_(word,r) j^(k-1)(D_j+1)^(2r+1). (3) For r=0 the sharper bound is |C_j(q_N)|<=j^(k-1). In particular the right side of (3) is polynomial in N, for example C_(word,r) N^(k+4r+1). There is no level-parity or primality restriction. The same polynomial conclusion holds for the root normal coordinate Delta=1-q^(2N), q=q_N(1-Delta)^(1/(2N)), (4) and for the actual weighted colors d_j(q)=(q^(2j)-1)C_j(q), including their fixed-order jets. The constants can change with r and the word, but not N or j in this window. For k>=2, the endpoint of (1) is below N, so these are ordinary colors. The k=1 knot is the unknot, whose reduced scalar is one; its possible j=N endpoint is harmless and can instead be handled separately. ## 2. Positivity on the full one-sided angular interval Put m=j-1 and n=2km. The fundamental cable of this colored plat has n endpoints. Work in its VACUUM path space: nonnegative paths a_0=a_n=0, |a_(i+1)-a_i|=1. Every such path has maximum height at most n/2=km. This is the important improvement over the full trace path space, whose paths need not end at zero. On pi/(2N)<=theta<pi/N, q=exp(i theta), (5) condition (1) implies that all required weights mu_a=[a+1]_q=sin((a+1)theta)/sin theta, 0<=a<=km, are strictly positive. At the upper endpoint, mu_(km) is allowed to become zero if km+1=N. Positivity is only asserted strictly BELOW that endpoint. For completeness the elementary TL generator on this orthonormal path basis has, when a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=a, the two-state matrix e_i[b,c]=sqrt(mu_b mu_c)/mu_a, b,c in {a-1,a+1}. The omitted height -1 has weight zero. Its nonzero eigenvalue is (mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1))/mu_a=2cos theta. The same elementary adjacent calculation gives e_i e_(i+1)e_i=e_i; disjoint generators commute. The maximum-height states introduce no missing term: a neighbor of an editable middle height is at most km-1, so its two weights are within the stated finite vacuum range. Thus every elementary fundamental crossing B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)e_i (6) is unitary: its eigenvalues are q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). Negative crossings are its adjoints. These are the actual ordinary full-Cartan normalizations, not a changed braid operator. Jones--Wenzl recursion on each m-strand color block has positive denominators [1],...,[m], is selfadjoint, and gives an orthogonal projection onto the original color-j cable subspace. Its quantum trace is EXACTLY [m+1]=[j]. One direct induction uses f_m=f_(m-1)-([m-1]/[m])f_(m-1)e_(m-1)f_(m-1) and the ordinary partial trace, giving [2][m]-[m-1]=[m+1]. The actual generic cabling comparison follows from the explicit highest-weight embedding and the original R coproduct. Its proof in [the ordinary-color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md) is algebraic BEFORE root specialization, so it applies throughout (5), where none of those denominators vanish. No root-only quotient has been analytically differentiated. ## 3. The original plat normalization and the improved bound A single actual colored cup has squared positive norm [j]: closing it against its adjoint evaluates precisely the quantum trace of its Jones--Wenzl projector. The k disjoint ordinary colored cups therefore have squared norm [j]^k. The actual output caps have the same norm. The required self-dual orientation and ribbon identifications retain their original signs and q monomials; on (5) these are unitary factors, not additional positive dimension factors. They stay in C_j(q), and their degree is included in (2). One can see the cup normalization directly in the orthonormal vacuum path model: one colored cup is sqrt([j]) times the unique length-2m mountain path. The k-cup source is [j]^(k/2) times the concatenation of those mountains. Every internal color projector fixes this source. The cabled braid is unitary and maps the prescribed color subspace to its actual corresponding output subspace. Consequently the raw ordinary colored plat scalar has absolute value at most [j]^k. The reduced KNOT scalar is the raw scalar divided by ONE [j]. This is its original cut/trace identity, not one division per cup or per strand. Hence throughout the CONTINUOUS interval (5), |C_j(exp(i theta))|<=[j]^(k-1)<=j^(k-1). (7) The last inequality follows from [j]=sum_(a=0)^(j-1)q^(j-1-2a) and positivity. The full zero-framing line has modulus one on this interval. Neither it nor any original pivotal factor is reset. At theta=pi/N, use continuity of the actual Laurent polynomial C_j. This includes equality in (1) even though the top path weight becomes zero. It is invalid to differentiate that singular path basis; the next step differentiates only a bounded POLYNOMIAL on the closed one-sided interval. This is why the endpoint is genuinely included. ## 4. An elementary quadratic Laurent-degree bound For clarity, (2) does not rely on a colored-Jones degree theorem. In an integral highest-weight color-j basis, the original universal R nilpotent coefficient is a Gaussian polynomial times a product of at most j-1 quantum integers and a power of q-q^(-1). Its divided-power denominator cancels in the Gaussian coefficient. The latter's Laurent degree is O(j^2), as follows by its finite Pascal recurrence. The Cartan exponent is a product of two weights of size at most j-1, and hence also has degree O(j^2). Both signs have the same degree bound. A fixed word adds only a fixed number of such degrees. The actual pivotal powers contribute O_word(j), and the matching ribbon framing contributes O_word(j^2). Use the reduced cut scalar, rather than introduce a division by [j]: it is a finite sum of these integral entries and pivots. Thus its Laurent support is contained in [-C_word(j+1)^2,C_word(j+1)^2] in z=q^(1/2). Summing paths cannot increase that support. This proves (2) with a fixed coarse word constant while retaining the half-root. ## 5. Endpoint differentiation without a cited Markov inequality Let z_N=q_N^(1/2) be its original marked branch. Put a=tan(pi/(8N)), t=a(x-1)/2, -1<=x<=1, z=z_N(1+i t)/(1-i t). The q-angle now runs exactly from pi/(2N) to pi/N. Define P(x)=(1+t^2)^D C_j(z^2), D=D_j. (8) It is a polynomial of degree at most 2D: multiplication clears every Laurent monomial's denominators. Since D a^2=O_word(1), (7) gives sup_[-1,1]|P|<=exp(D a^2)j^(k-1)<=C_word j^(k-1). (9) For any complex polynomial P of degree n, expand it as sum_(l=0)^n c_l T_l(x). The cosine integral for its Chebyshev coefficients gives |c_0|<=M and |c_l|<=2M, M=sup|P|. The elementary differential equation (1-x^2)T_l''-x T_l'+l^2 T_l=0 implies, at x=1, T_l^(r+1)(1)=(l^2-r^2)T_l^r(1)/(2r+1). Thus, for each FIXED r, |T_l^r(1)|<=C_r(l+1)^(2r), and |P^r(1)|<=C_r M(n+1)^(2r+1). (10) The derivatives of (1+t^2)^(-D) at x=1 have bounded fixed-order norms because D a^2=O_word(1). The angular chain rule costs at most C_r N^r. Applying (9)--(10) to (8) therefore proves |partial_theta^r C_j(exp(i theta)) at theta=pi/N| <=C_(word,r)N^r j^(k-1)(D_j+1)^(2r+1). (11) This is an endpoint estimate, so a two-sided positive arc is not needed. Finally q partial_q=(1/i)partial_theta on that angular curve. For q=q_N(1+s/N), the order-r operator is N^(-r) product_(l=0)^(r-1)(q partial_q-l). Its expansion uses only angular derivatives through r, and (11) gives (3). For (4) it is instead the fixed polynomial (-1)^r product_(l=0)^(r-1)((q partial_q)/(2N)-l), which has the same bound. Derivatives of q^(2j)-1 on either scale are bounded at fixed order since j<=N. This proves the weighted color statement too. ## 6. The entire low-color packet is bounded on a complex normal disk There is a useful strengthening of the fixed-jet assertion. Fix ANY A>4. Uniformly for every color satisfying (1), the ACTUAL entire ordinary family obeys |C_j(q_N exp(s/N))|<=C_(word,A)(D_j+1)j^(k-1) <=C_(word,A)N^(k+1), |s|<=2N^(-A). (12) No eigenframe, recurrence denominator, truncated Taylor polynomial or root color quotient is used on this disk. To prove (12), keep the same polynomial P in (8). The half-root ratio is now exp(s/(2N)), so its exact rational coordinate is t=-i tanh(s/(4N)), x=1+2t/a. Consequently |x-1|<=C|s|. For |x-1|<=d<1/4 the elementary formula T_l(x)=[(x+sqrt(x^2-1))^l +(x-sqrt(x^2-1))^l]/2 gives |T_l(x)|<=exp(C l sqrt(d)): the two reciprocal factors have moduli at most 1+C sqrt(d). The finite Chebyshev expansion and |c_l|<=2M from (9) yield |P(x)|<=C(D_j+1)j^(k-1) exp(C D_j sqrt(|s|)). Since D_j=O_word(N^2) and A>4, this exponential is bounded by a word constant on the whole displayed disk. The denominator in (8) is nonzero there and its inverse has modulus at most exp(C D_j |t|^2), also bounded. This proves (12), including the one-sided-positivity endpoint: only the original real-arc bound was used in its polynomial continuation. The weighted d_j(q)=(q^(2j)-1)C_j(q) has the same bound, since |q^(2j)|<=exp(4N^(-A)) on this disk. The linear normal q=q_N(1+s/N) and the normal (4) map smaller disks of comparable radius into this exponential disk by their exact logarithms. Cauchy's formula on a slightly smaller circle gives simultaneous polynomial bounds for ANY fixed jet depth of this ENTIRE packet. This stronger result is important at singular recurrence steps: one can transport the honest holomorphic low-color germs around nearby coefficient zeros, rather than infer that a finite Taylor truncation selected the correct meromorphic continuation. No recurrence denominator has been declared absent from that circle; the actual scalar colors themselves are holomorphic and bounded. ## 7. What this supplies for the original pointed source For fixed k, the interval reaches j<=1+floor((N-1)/k). At every singular recurrence step whose entire retained bounded jet packet lies within this color interval, its ACTUAL quantum-normal data are polynomially bounded without inverting that singular step. In particular a 2-bridge presentation controls the ordinary-color quantum jets through the midpoint, including the valid endpoint. The original complete/root source and all remaining high-color normal packets stay in the subsequent boundary transport. This does NOT assert a meridian-derivative bound for F_N(Y) at fixed q_N. Along C_j(q), q and Y=q^(2j) move together. Nor does pointwise unitarity at q_N extend the result beyond (1): there the continuous vacuum path space encounters nonsemisimple wall channels. Those channels and their original source must be retained. No bound for the complete K_N or the full high-color response is inferred. [Audit](../experiments/audit_ordinary_color_macroscopic_normal_jet_window.py): continuous untruncated vacuum path unitarity, colored cup/JW normalization, endpoint-inclusive angular bounds and exact Chebyshev endpoint derivative estimates.

title: Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy
text: # Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The question is the precise inequality used when replacing the original complete-color value by a positive Fourier norm. The proof below uses the actual finite crossing matrices and a reconstructed positive path trace. No published asymptotic, unitarity, ADO/Jones comparison, or volume-conjecture theorem is a premise. The root convention is essential. Set q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, [j]=sin(pi j/N)/sin(pi/N). Let a fixed braid on b strands close to a ONE-component zero-framed knot, and let C_j(q) denote its original reduced ordinary j-color, with unknot value one. Then, for every 1<=j<N, |C_j(q)| <= [j]^(b-1) <= sin(pi/N)^(1-b). (1) There is no corresponding assertion at j=N. The statement is also not asserted at arbitrary Galois-conjugate roots. The immediate consequence needed in the Fourier argument is the all-level, all-ordinary-color estimate 0 <= E_N-|K_N|^2 <= (N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2). (1a) Here the braid presentation, and therefore b, is fixed as N varies. Neither hyperbolicity nor alternatingness is needed for this bound. The positive-energy identity is exact; only the replacement of its ordinary-color remainder by a polynomial uses the estimate. ## 1. The positive algebra and its trace can be checked directly Put delta=q+q^(-1)=2cos(pi/N), and mu_a=sin((a+1)pi/N)/sin(pi/N), 0<=a<=N-2. These numbers are positive; with zero boundary values they satisfy mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta mu_a. On walks of length m in the chain 0,...,N-2 starting at zero, let U_i change only the middle height of a return (c,a,c), with coefficient sqrt(mu_a mu_a')/mu_c. Direct local multiplication gives U_i*=U_i, U_i^2=delta U_i, U_i U_(i+1) U_i=U_i, U_i U_j=U_j U_i for |i-j|>1. Consequently B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)U_i is unitary: its eigenvalues are q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). The same displayed relations prove the braid relation. Inverse crossings are the actual inverses. The weighted trace tau_m(A)=sum_walks mu_(last height) A_(walk,walk) is positive. Its weight is central in the path algebra because every generator preserves the last height, so it is tracial too. Directly, tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta tau_m(A), tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). (2) In the first identity sum over the last step using the mu recurrence. In the second identity only the unchanged middle height contributes to the diagonal: mu_c from the last vertex cancels the denominator mu_c of U_m, leaving exactly the weight mu_a on the length-m walk. These recursions identify the trace with the original fundamental quantum trace. Indeed the latter has K=diag(q,q^(-1)) and U block [[q,-1],[-1,q^(-1)]] on (01,10), zero on (00,11); its partial K-trace is I and Tr K=delta. Both traces therefore satisfy (2), with value one on the empty diagram. Uniqueness does not require semisimplicity: the Temperley--Lieb relations inductively span the next algebra by the included algebra and elements A U_m B, and traciality plus (2) determine both types. The spanning claim follows by reducing each U_m A U_m with the preceding spanning statement and the two local quadratic/adjacent relations. ## 2. Ordinary colors are positive projections in this trace Write n=j-1. The recursively defined color projector is p_0=p_1=I, p_(m+1)=p_m tensor I -[m]/[m+1] (p_m tensor I)U_m(p_m tensor I). For n<=N-2 every denominator used is nonzero and every coefficient is real. The local algebra proves idempotence and annihilation by U_1,...,U_(n-1); hence its path realization is an orthogonal projector. The trace recursion gives tau_n(p_n)=[n+1]=[j]. This is the actual highest-weight color, not a color assigned to an unrelated positive model. In the ordinary fundamental tensor space, the common kernel of the U_i has one vector at each tensor weight: the local 01/10 relation fixes their coefficient ratio and adjacent exchanges connect all words of that weight. The vectors obtained by successive coproduct F-actions on the highest tensor span those lines. Their coefficients involve only nonzero [r]!, r<=n. Thus they give the original j-dimensional highest-weight module. The projector acts as identity on this common kernel and has image in it. Restricting the cabled finite universal R to these images gives the original j-color R, by its coproduct identities. A direct coefficient proof of both identities, including the Cartan factors, is given in the [independent color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md#4-the-fundamental-cable-is-the-literal-colored-r). The retained highest-vector Cartan scalar is q^(n^2/2); the ordinary framing twist is q^(n(n+2)/2). Both have modulus one. For b colored strands let P be the tensor product of these projectors. The trace of a disjoint colored closure, or (2) successively, gives tau(P)=[j]^b. The cabled braid is unitary in the path representation and preserves P. It also preserves each last-height block. In an orthonormal basis of Im P within each such block, its diagonal entries have modulus at most one and every trace weight is positive. Therefore |tau(P B P)| <= tau(P)=[j]^b. Dividing by the NONZERO original ordinary quantum dimension [j], and retaining the unit-modulus zero-framing factor, proves (1). At j=N the relevant quantum dimension is [N]=0. In the positive path trace the corresponding negligible projector has zero image. The division just used is unavailable. This is precisely why this proof places no polynomial bound on K_N. ## 3. The ADO orbit really has these ordinary-color values At the orbit color x=q^(j-1), the original N-dimensional module has the invariant subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)); its quotient is the ordinary j-dimensional module. Every tensor factor of the finite R, its inverse, and the pivot preserves U. In a basis adapted to U, each matrix path along an underlying strand can enter U but cannot leave it. A one-component braid closure passes through the open cut. For its quotient block that cut starts and ends outside U, forcing every contributing path around the component to stay in the quotient. Thus the induced cut is exactly the all-j-colored cut, even though the other braid strands were traced first. No assertion of this form is made for a separate closed link component. The conventions agree after the explicit signs are kept: K^(1-N)=epsilon_j K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j theta_ordinary, epsilon_j=(-1)^(j-1). The braid permutation is a b-cycle, so its writhe w satisfies w=b-1 modulo 2. The resulting sign is epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. Consequently the original even meridian family satisfies F_N(Q^j)=C_j(q), with F_N(1)=K_N. This is the filtered matrix argument of `root_orbit_pointing.md`, with the precise one-component and framing hypotheses exposed. To distinguish the two coordinates used in the older notes, write this as F_N^M(-q^j)=F_N^Y(Q^j)=C_j(q), Y=M^2. The functions in this identity are REDUCED periods. The full ADO state also carries its original modified-dimension factor, which can have a pole at an ordinary orbit point. Neither its value nor a transverse derivative is bounded by (1). No such value or derivative is used in the Fourier remainder below. ## 4. An explicit positive Fourier remainder Set c_0=K_N and c_j=C_j(q) for 1<=j<N, and use the unitary transform chat_k=N^(-1/2) sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Q^(-kj)c_j. Finite character orthogonality proves exactly E_N:=sum_k |chat_k|^2 =|K_N|^2+R_N, 0<=R_N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q)|^2 <=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)[j]^(2b-2). (3) In particular this remainder is polynomial uniformly over the entire ordinary-color range, including j=N-1, rather than just at fixed j. There is an explicit sharper constant. Put r=b-1>=1 and assume N>r. The Fourier expansion of sin^(2r)(pi j/N) has frequencies -r,...,r. Only its constant coefficient survives summation over all N roots; that coefficient is binom(2r,r)/4^r. The j=0 summand is zero. Hence 0<=R_N <= N binom(2r,r)/(4^r sin^(2r)(pi/N)) <= binom(2r,r) N^(2r+1)/16^r. (4) For b=1 the closure is the unknot and R_N=N-1 instead. For small N<=r the sum bound (3) remains valid without the simplified formula. Equivalently chat=K_N u+e, where u is the constant unit vector, e is orthogonal to u, and ||e||^2=R_N. This orthogonality is exact; there is no discarded cross term. There is also an unconditional logarithmic statement, which is safer than writing an equality of unsmoothed logarithms before a positive rate has been established. The trivial ordinary color satisfies C_1=1, so R_N>=1 for every N>=2. Set P_(N,b)=(N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2)>=1. Then the exact energy identity and (1a) give 1+|K_N|^2 <= E_N <= P_(N,b)(1+|K_N|^2), (4a) 0 <= log E_N-log(1+|K_N|^2) <= log P_(N,b). In particular, uniformly without any nonvanishing assumption, (pi/N)log E_N =(pi/N)log(1+|K_N|^2)+O_b(log N/N). (4b) With log 0=-infinity this is equivalently 0 <= (pi/N)log E_N-max(0,(2pi/N)log|K_N|) <= (pi/N)log(2P_(N,b)). (4c) For any fixed V>0, (4a)--(4c) prove (2pi/N)log|K_N| -> V if and only if (pi/N)log E_N -> V. (5) The implication from positive energy to the original invariant uses the fact that a polynomial remainder is smaller than any sequence with strictly positive exponential rate. It does not assume eventual nonvanishing of K_N; that nonvanishing follows from the positive energy rate and (3). An unrestricted equality of log E_N and 2 log|K_N| at exponential scale does NOT follow merely from the polynomial remainder: zeros or exponentially small values would invalidate that inference. ## 5. What is verified, and what remains The finite Plancherel checks do not establish a volume limit. The remaining analytical questions are stated below. * [Positive path algebra](ordinary_color_positive_trace_independent_audit.md): both Markov identities on noncommuting words, the full projection induction including the first zero-dimension projection, and 42 signed colored closures including j=N-1. * [Original color identification](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md): the uniform one-component filtered trace proof and direct R coproduct calculation, supplemented by 228 exact whole-knot cut comparisons and 22 signed-cable families, with the original Cartan and twist phases. The explicit sine-energy identity in (4) was independently checked in 225 pairs (N,r), with 80-digit arithmetic; its proof is the finite character calculation above. No defect was found in either uniform proof. These checks establish the remainder estimate's stated scope, not the geometric size of the remaining Fourier energy. The polynomial remainder in (3) has an independent algebraic proof. The positive energy E_N still requires its geometric exponential estimate. In particular, the canonical cleared operator B(Y-1) becomes Bhat(S-I) in the dual cyclic coordinate and kills the constant mode u exactly. Retaining the original normal/pointed source is therefore essential when estimating that energy. Plancherel validates the positive target; it does not by itself supply its size.

title: Independent algebra audit of the ordinary-color positive trace bound
