text: # Independent algebra audit of the ordinary-color positive trace bound 28 October 2026. This independently checks the positive path algebra used in Section 2 of `regularized_kashaev_period.md`. No published volume, Jones asymptotic, positivity theorem or recoupling identity is a premise. The local path matrices, trace, projections, cabling and framing estimate are proved below. The separate identification with the original reduced ordinary-color cut is being audited in `actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md`. Verdict: the path-algebra proof is correct. The estimates include every color j<N, in particular j=N-1. The explicit arguments below fill in the two compressed steps: the Jones--Wenzl square relation and multiplicative trace of disjoint color projections. ## 1. Local matrices, without an imported positive trace For N>=3 set theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), delta=q+q^(-1), and mu_a=sin((a+1)theta)/sin(theta), 0<=a<=N-2. These weights are strictly positive. With mu_(-1)=mu_(N-1)=0 they obey mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta mu_a, including the two endpoints. The Hilbert space H_m has its orthonormal basis the length-m walks (a_0,...,a_m) in {0,...,N-2}, a_0=0, |a_i-a_(i-1)|=1. The operator U_i is zero unless a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=c. It then replaces a_i by a neighbor a_i' of c with coefficient sqrt(mu_(a_i')mu_(a_i))/mu_c. (1) It is real symmetric. On a fixed pair of equal outer neighbors its nonzero block is vv^t/mu_c, with v_a=sqrt(mu_a). The neighbor identity implies U_i^2=delta U_i. Here is the complete adjacent-product calculation. In U_i U_(i+1) U_i, suppose the original outer heights for the first U_i are c,c and a_(i+2)=d. The middle operator forces the first replacement a_i'=d; the final U_i forces the middle replacement a_(i+1)'=c. The three coefficients multiply to sqrt(mu_(a_i)mu_d)/mu_c * mu_c/mu_d * sqrt(mu_d mu_(a_i''))/mu_c =sqrt(mu_(a_i)mu_(a_i''))/mu_c. This is precisely U_i. All forced heights are allowed neighbors, so no nonexistent boundary height or zero weight is divided by. The opposite adjacent relation is identical. Distant U's commute since they change distinct middle heights and share only fixed endpoints. Consequently B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)U_i is unitary: the coefficient of U_i in B_i B_i^* is delta-q-q^(-1)=0. Expanding its braid relation reduces its difference to a multiple of q-(q+q^(-1))+q^(-1)=0. This proves unitarity and braiding directly at the chosen principal root. ## 2. The weighted trace and both Markov identities Define tau_m(A)=sum_paths mu_(a_m) A_(a,a). Every U_i and B_i preserves a_m. Hence the positive diagonal matrix of endpoint weights commutes with their algebra, and tau is a positive tracial functional. For the included operator A on H_(m+1), summing over the last neighbor b of a_m gives tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta tau_m(A). (2) For the second identity, a diagonal contribution to (A tensor I)U_m requires that the U_m replacement leave a_m unchanged, since A preserves its m-th endpoint. U_m also forces a_(m+1)=a_(m-1). Its diagonal entry is mu_(a_m)/mu_(a_(m-1)); multiplication by the trace weight cancels the denominator. Every length-m prefix has exactly this allowed final neighbor. Thus tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). (3) These arguments apply to arbitrary elements of the generated algebra, not only its diagonal or commuting words. The same identities determine the planar closure trace algebraically. Indeed the elementary TL relations inductively imply TL_(m+1)=TL_m + TL_m U_m TL_m. To reduce a word containing two U_m's, decompose its intervening TL_m word into TL_(m-1) plus TL_(m-1)U_(m-1)TL_(m-1); commute the former past U_m, then use U_m^2=delta U_m or U_m U_(m-1) U_m=U_m. Traciality, (2) and (3) therefore recursively fix the trace on every word, starting with tau_0(1)=1. Closing a planar pairing diagram and assigning delta to each resulting circle obeys the same relations and recursions: the square relation creates one circle, the adjacent relation none. Hence it is that same trace. In particular horizontal juxtaposition of two diagrams multiplies their traces, since their closed circle sets are disjoint. By linearity, tau_(r+s)(A tensor B)=tau_r(A)tau_s(B). (4) This proves the product-color trace used below rather than assuming it. ## 3. Color projections through the last permitted color Write [r]=sin(r theta)/sin(theta). Starting with p_0=p_1=I, set p_(m+1)=p_m-([m]/[m+1])p_m U_m p_m. (5) The first term is included on m+1 strands. Every denominator is positive for m+1<=N-1. For m=1 the required square relation is simply U_1^2=delta U_1, so no generator U_0 is needed. For m>=2 let g=p_(m-1), c=[m-1]/[m], and f=p_m=g-cgU_(m-1)g. Then fg=gf=f, and g commutes with U_m. Therefore x=fU_m f satisfies x^2=(delta-c)x=([m+1]/[m])x. (6) The first equality follows by inserting f=g-cgU_(m-1)g between the two U_m's and using the square/adjacent TL relations. More explicitly, commuting g past U_m and using fg=f gives fU_m fU_m=delta fU_m-c fU_m U_(m-1)U_m g=(delta-c)fU_m. Multiplication on the right by f gives (6). It follows that (5) is a selfadjoint idempotent and annihilates U_m on both sides. Earlier U_i are already annihilated by f. Conversely any vector killed by all internal U_i is fixed by p_(m+1), since p_(m+1)-I lies in their generated ideal. This verifies the intended common-kernel projection, with no generic semisimplicity assumption. Use positivity, (2)--(3), idempotence and traciality to compute tau_(m+1)(p_(m+1)) =delta tau_m(p_m)-([m]/[m+1])tau_m(p_m) =delta[m+1]-[m]=[m+2]. (7) In the middle line tau_(m+1)(p_m U_m p_m)=tau_m(p_m). The base values tau_0(p_0)=[1] and tau_1(p_1)=[2] start the induction. Thus the j-color projection is p_(j-1), with trace [j]>0 for ALL j<N. As a useful endpoint check, p_(N-1) is still definable (its last denominator is [N-1]>0), but its positive trace is [N]=0. It is therefore the ZERO operator in this path representation. There is no nonzero positive projection which may be divided by [N]; the proof explicitly stops before the Kashaev color. ## 4. Cabling, the retained trace, and framing For b strands of common ordinary color j let ell=j-1 and put P=p_ell tensor ... tensor p_ell on b ell fundamental strands. Its factors commute and are orthogonal projections, so P is one too. Equation (4) proves exactly tau(P)=[j]^b. (8) A positive crossing of two ell-strand blocks is the usual ell^2 fundamental braid word. The Yang--Baxter relation slides every internal block generator through it, moving the first block's generator to the second and vice versa. Applying the polynomial recursion (5) proves that this block crossing interchanges the two p_ell factors and hence commutes with their product. Its inverse does too. Thus every cabled colored braid is unitary and preserves P, directly in the positive path representation. No assertion that the original tensor metric itself is positive is used. Let U denote this unitary cabled word. Since the endpoint weight D is positive and commutes with both U and P, Schatten Cauchy--Schwarz gives |tau(PU)|=|Tr(D^(1/2)P U P D^(1/2))| <=Tr(DP)=[j]^b. (9) Equivalently restrict to the image of P and sum unitary diagonal entries with their positive weights. The reduced closure divides by the retained [j]>0, yielding |C_j(q_N)|<=[j]^(b-1), 1<=j<N. (10) Here identifying that reduced closure with the original cut is the separate actual-color comparison, not an extra positivity premise. The actual zero-framing factor is a power of q^((j^2-1)/2), and all retained fundamental/color Cartan phases likewise have modulus one. They do not change (9)--(10). Their exact values are retained in the comparison audit. At N=2 the only ordinary color is j=1 and C_1=1. Finally sin(pi/N)>=2/N implies [j]<=sin(pi/N)^(-1)<=(N/2), so for a fixed b-strand presentation the whole ordinary-color vector has polynomial size. This conclusion concerns the specific principal root and the ordinary range; it makes no estimate for j=N. ## 5. Independent checks [The new audit](../experiments/audit_positive_ordinary_color_path_trace.py) constructs the path matrices without importing any Jones/trace library. It checks adjacent relations, noncommuting Markov words, every permitted projection including j=N-1, the vanishing next projection, disjoint color traces, cabled-braid preservation and both crossing signs. Whole colored closures include their zero-framing unit phases. These finite checks supplement the uniform proofs above and are not a premise for (10). The path-algebra proof does not use semisimplicity. It retains both color projections, the terminal index and the empty-cable case. Comparison with the original ordinary-color cut remains separate.

title: Shared source caps, triangle orderings and the remaining tetrahedral defect
text: # Shared source caps, triangle orderings and the remaining tetrahedral defect Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives exact shared-edge cap transport, tetrahedron reversal and coherent cyclic face orderings for the existing pointed recoupling tensors. It also gives an explicit counterexample to extending those results to all vertex orderings of the bare tetrahedron tensor. Thus the ideal-triangulation comparison still requires a source-compatible tensor symmetrization. The actual endpoint caps and their finite-factorial normalization are those proved in [relative pivotal duality](relative_pivotal_duality.md). No different knot invariant or regulator realization is defined here. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. One marked cap on each edge Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. On a nondegenerate flag chart choose distinct p_i=A_i^N, with A_i nonzero. Give an oriented edge the existing affine character and endpoint module g_ij=(1,p_i-p_j), E_ij=E_(g_ij;A_j,A_i). Thus g_ij g_jk=g_ik. Choose a marked K-root x_ij with x_ij^N=1 and put x_ji=Q^(-1)x_ij^(-1). (1.1) Let J_ij be the actual source-normalized endpoint cap from the preceding note. It pairs E_ij with E_ji. In particular J_ij^(-t)J_ji=X_ij^(N-1). (1.2) The cap on the total edge ik is its already assigned J_ik. It is not chosen independently each time that edge occurs in a triangle. For example the dual of a product mark x is Q^(-1)x^(-1), whereas the product of two dual marks is Q^(-2)x^(-1). These are different marked cyclic cuts. For general multiplicative central X-characters, define omega_ijk=x_ij x_jk/x_ik, omega_ijk^N=1. Direct cancellation gives omega_ijk omega_ikl=omega_ijl omega_jkl, omega_kji=Q^(-1)omega_ijk^(-1). (1.3) Thus the root discrepancy is coherent triangle data, with a specified reversal law. It is not set to one independently on each face. No division by two or three modulo N is used. ## 2. Root changes are explicit norm-one transports with a source wall Write the finite cap scalar of the preceding note as c(x;a,b)=-1/(N xQ) product_(s=1)^(N-2)(b-a x^(-1)Q^s). At fixed endpoints and central character, c(Qx;a,b)/c(x;a,b) =Q^(-1)(b-a/x)/(b-aQ^(-2)/x). (2.1) This follows by canceling the two finite products. The product of (2.1) over the full N-orbit is one. The cap scalar itself is an explicit Hilbert-90 primitive for this transport. These ratios are functions; for N>=3 they are not generally phases or constants. All zero and pole factors remain. At the actual source choose a=x_0, b near 1 and let the mark be Q^j x_0. In the normal coordinate b-1, ord c(Q^j x_0;x_0,b) =0 for j=0,N-1, and 1 for 1<=j<=N-2. (2.2) Indeed the single vanishing factor occurs exactly at s=j in the product, and its first coefficient is nonzero. At N=2 both charts have order zero. Thus moving the cut can require a first normal coefficient even though its generic cyclic norm is one. Its finite cyclic lattice and the dual linking pairing retain that coefficient. A value at b=1 without its source lattice does not specify this transport. There is an exact cancellation law for the face metrics. If a change of marks rescales edge caps by J'_ij=u_ij J_ij, then the induced face pairing obeys M'_ijk=(u_ij u_jk/u_ik)M_ijk. (2.3) This follows immediately from the factorization defining M. The two products of these face factors around a tetrahedron are equal by cancellation. Consistent shared edge choices therefore retain their full factors without an independent tetrahedron normalization. The actual selected boundary vectors and covectors must be transported as well. ## 3. Exact tetrahedron reversal Use the pointed factorization C_ijk:E_ik tensor V_ijk -> E_ij tensor E_jk, and the triangle metrics defined by C_ijk^t(J_ij tensor J_jk)P C_kji =J_ik tensor M_ijk. (3.1) Here P is the literal flip. The total cap in (3.1) is the shared edge cap. For four flags let R_0123:V_023 tensor V_012 -> V_013 tensor V_123 be the existing pointed Racah map. Then exactly (M_023 tensor M_012)R_3210 =R_0123^t(M_013 tensor M_123). (3.2) For a proof let I_L,I_R be the two three-edge fusion tree evaluations, with I_L=I_R(I tensor R_0123). Reverse their leaf order and use the inverse affine characters. Applying (3.1) twice factors the paired leaf contraction as J_03 tensor M_023 tensor M_012 for one tree and J_03 tensor M_013 tensor M_123 for the other. Substitution of the tree relation and cancellation of J_03 gives (3.2). This fixes the whole scalar, without determinant rigidity. Equation (1.2) and the group-like pivot also give M_kji=M_ijk^t. (3.3) Indeed the double-dual operator on the two leaves is their tensor pivot, which is the pivot of the total edge. Removing that same total cap leaves the identity on the relative factor. Thus face reversal is paired exactly. Choosing a local product mark for a total cap changes (3.2). If r_ijk=c(x_ij x_jk;A_k,A_i)/c(x_ik;A_k,A_i), its defect is r_023 r_012/(r_013 r_123). (3.4) The audit finds nontrivial examples at every tested N>=3. These factors are retained as their full functions; (3.4) is not a new permitted normalization of the knot period. ## 4. The cyclic face map from the actual invariant tensor The relative triangle has operators D=X_1+Y_1Y_2^(-1), Z=-Y_1Y_2^(-1)X_2, DZ=QZD, D^N=lambda, Z^N=mu, lambda+mu=1. Its endpoint parameters are u=A_j/A_k, v=A_i/A_k. Turn the total leg of C_ijk using its assigned cap: T_ijk=(C_ijk tensor I)coev_ik. Here the relative factor is retained as the argument; in indices T_(abc,l)=sum_s C_(ab,sl)(J_ik^(-1))_(cs). It identifies V_ijk with the invariant subspace of E_ij tensor E_jk tensor E_ki. This space has dimension N: rigid duality identifies it with the N-dimensional fusion multiplicity space, and C_ijk is the explicit isomorphism. On invariants cyclic rotation is rot=P_231(g_ij^(-1) tensor I tensor I), g_ij=X_ij^(N-1). The antipode and pivot identities make this an invariant tensor again. Three rotations give the inverse total pivot, which acts as the identity on invariants. Thus there is a unique invertible matrix L_f for f=(i,j,k), r f=(j,k,i), such that T_(r f)L_f=rot T_f, L_(r^2 f)L_(r f)L_f=I. (4.1) This is a finite construction with the scalar fixed by the displayed actual tensors. It does not reset a unit. The corresponding relative algebra map is h(D)=-D^(-1)Z, h(Z)=Q D^(-1), h^3=1, D_(r f)L_f=L_f h(D_f), Z_(r f)L_f=L_f h(Z_f). (4.2) One can derive (4.2) directly on invariants. The total Y equation gives Y_2Y_3^(-1)=-D^(-1)X_1X_2 there, while D X_2=X_1X_2-Z. These give the first formula. The total X equation and the Q commutation give the second formula. Both phases in (4.2) are consequently determined. ## 5. The raw cyclic map has a matrix-valued pairing defect Let bar f=(k,j,i), and f'=(i,k,j), so r f'=bar f and bar(r f)=f'. The exact defect of the raw map is L_f^t M_(r f)L_(f')^(-1) =M_f G_(bar f), G_(bar f)=D_(bar f)^(1-N) =lambda_(bar f)^(-1)D_(bar f). (5.1) This is not a scalar for N>=2. The source cap alone does not make the raw invariant rotation a face pairing symmetry. Here is a uniform calibration of (5.1). The reversal anti-map on the relative algebra is a(D)=-Z^(-1)D, a(Z)=QZ^(-1). Substitution of a and h shows that the defect G commutes with D_(bar f) and Q-commutes with Z_(bar f). Since this pair generates the full matrix algebra, G=c D_(bar f). To determine c, edge-cap scalar gauges may be removed by (2.3); they cancel from G. Use the raw endpoint trace caps. Put alpha_f=A_k^(N-1)/(p_j-p_k). Their relative unit functional is (M_f e_0)(F)=alpha_f tau_D[D F/(v-uD)], (5.2) where tau_D is normalized multiplication trace in k[D]/(D^N-lambda). Its defining shift recurrence follows from a(Z)+u_(bar f)a(D)-v_(bar f), and its scalar follows by pairing the two endpoint units in (3.1). Finite trace cancellation gives (M_f)_(0,1)=alpha_f u^(N-2)lambda/mu, (M_f)_(N-1,0)=alpha_f lambda v^(N-1)/mu, (M_f)_(N-1,N-1)=0. (5.3) For example tau[D/(v-uD)]=u^(N-1)lambda/mu; the adjacent shifted denominator gives the first identity. The last identity reduces to tau[D^(N-1)]=0. The pointed factorial formula for C gives L_f e_0=ell_f e_(N-1), ell_f=lambda/mu, L_f^(-1)e_0=(v e_(N-1)-u lambda e_0)/(ell_f mu). (5.4) For the scalar in (5.4), with raw caps the invariant unit tensor is (A_k-A_i X_3)sum_(s=0)^(N-1)(X_1X_2X_3)^s. Apply the pointed finite-product formula to the rotated relative monomial of degree N-1. The identity product_(s=1)^(N-1)(b-aQ^s t)=(b^N-a^N)/(b-at) at t^N=1 gives ell_f=lambda/mu. The inverse in (5.4) then follows by (4.2) and Z^N=mu. Now evaluate the (0,0) entry of (5.1), use (5.3)--(5.4) on f,r f,f', and divide by (M_f)_(0,1). It gives c=(alpha_(r f)/alpha_f) mu/v^(N-1) =mu(p_j-p_k)/(p_k-p_i) =-mu/lambda=lambda_(bar f)^(-1). This proves (5.1) with its full scalar at every N. The audit checks the intermediate trace and unit formulas, as well as the complete matrix identity. ## 6. Corrected face orderings preserve the actual pairing Choose once a phase tau_N with tau_N^3=Q. This is an ordinary algebraic phase choice, including when 3 divides N; no inverse of three modulo N is required. Define U_f=tau_N lambda_f L_f D_f^(-1) =tau_N L_f D_f^(N-1). (6.1) Thus the correction is exactly the relative face pivot, with its recorded cubic phase. The second expression is polynomial; invertibility at a degenerate central point still requires the retained lattice and source. These maps have exact cyclic and dual-pairing coherence: U_(r^2 f)U_(r f)U_f=I, U_f^t M_(r f)U_(f')^(-1)=M_f. (6.2) For the cyclic identity, pulling the inverse D factors through (4.2) gives (L D^(-1))_(r^2 f)(L D^(-1))_(r f)(L D^(-1))_f =h^2(D)^(-1)h(D)^(-1)D^(-1) =-Q^(-1)I. The three central lambda values are lambda,-mu/lambda,1/mu; their product is -1. Combining this with tau_N^3=Q proves the first equation of (6.2). For the second, move D factors through the reversal pairing using a. Equation (5.1) then gives the scalar mu/lambda for L D^(-1). The lambda factors in (6.1) cancel it because lambda_(f')=mu_f. The common phase cancels as well. The lifted quantum cyclic algebra map is now h_correct(D)=-Q D^(-1)Z, h_correct(Z)=Q D^(-1). (6.3) It has order three and obeys the strict dihedral relation with the reversal anti-map a. Equations (3.3) and (6.2) therefore give coherent oriented triangular order changes with the actual dual pairing. The selected vectors and covectors are transported by these full matrices. Interior adapters cancel in a specified finite contraction. The inverse D and lambda in (6.1) are operator and central data, not discarded numerical multipliers. At a wall, whole transport is interpreted on its actual lattice and dual source, as in the preceding note. This face result does not assert all tetrahedron vertex symmetries. ## 7. The bare tetrahedron still fails the full vertex-order test This is a separate, explicitly failed proposed bridge. Use the raw R above as the positive tetrahedron map. Regard its source duals as reversed face modules using M^(-1), and place its four tensor legs in boundary-face order (123),(320),(013),(210). For a negative tetrahedron use R^(-1) with the opposite face orientations. For another ordered vertex list identify its oriented faces by the corrected U maps in (6.1) and permute its four legs back to the same boundary-face order. This completely specifies the tensor comparison being tested. It is false that the resulting tensors are always scalar multiples. An even permutation already gives a counterexample: N=2, A=(2,3,4,5), vertex order (1,2,0,3). There is a short exact reduction certificate. Work modulo 241 with primitive generator 7, q=177, Q=-1 and tau_N=16. Then q^2=-1 and tau_N^3=-1. With the face tensor flattened in the displayed boundary order, its first two coefficients and those of the reordered tensor are original: (83,239), reordered: (141,0). Their proportionality minor is 0*83-239*141=41 mod 241, which is nonzero. All denominators and required matrix minors in the construction are nonzero at this point. This is also a characteristic-zero obstruction to the proposed rational identity: 241 splits the cyclotomic coefficient field, and a zero rational identity could not have this nonzero good reduction. At the odd level N=3 the same even permutation has a regular certificate modulo 397: the two coefficient pairs are (344,139) and (10,262), with minor 207. Thus the ordering issue also occurs on the odd-level recoupling system covered by the matrix-dilogarithm framework. Consistent edge-cap scalar gauges cannot remove this counterexample. By (2.3) they rescale each face pairing, and the T-based cyclic maps rescale by the ratio of their total-edge cap scalars. Thus each compared four-tensor is only rescaled. Nonproportionality is unchanged. A scalar tetrahedron factor cannot fix it either. This refutes this bare-tensor prescription with these face adapters. It does not refute a literature charged matrix dilogarithm, a different specified tetrahedral decoration, or the actual knot invariant. The audit finds only the identity and full reversal scalar equivalent among the 24 orders in its N=2,3,4 configurations. A source-compatible tensor symmetrization or a comparison retaining additional operator trace data is still required before global gluing to an arbitrarily ordered positive ideal triangulation. The later [root-charge diagnostic](braided_source_groupoid.md#1-fixed-face-adapters-are-not-repaired-just-by-root-charges) checks a stronger repair proposal: keep these face adapters and vary both literal standard-kernel root charges. At a regular N=3 point all 81 reference/reordered charge pairs still have nonzero proportionality minors. Thus that repair does not supply the missing tetrahedron assignment. This is not a test of a different published adapter prescription. The actual source braiding and its retained spectral jets are constructed separately in the braided source groupoid. ## 8. Coverage, verification and the remaining volume comparison The abstract of [Baseilhac--Benedetti, math/0306283](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) already distinguishes a basic ordered matrix dilogarithm from its decorated symmetrization. It supplies coverage of this problem, not a proof premise or an identification with the actual source used here. No novelty is claimed for charged tetrahedral symmetry or cyclic 6j-symbols. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_oriented_tetrahedron_source.py) checks N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12. Shared-cap reversal, the raw nonscalar cyclic defect, its uniform trace calibration, the corrected cyclic and metric identities, all 24 face cap gauge and tetrahedral charge identities, and the root mark norm/source formulas pass. The separate full vertex test fails with the explicit certificate above, as recorded in [the results](../experiments/oriented_tetrahedron_source_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_oriented_tetrahedron_source.py The positive triangulation theorem supplies a geometric marked Bloch representative. The constructions here provide further actual source and orientation data for a comparison, and the failed test identifies an additional operator-level requirement. They do not identify the global selected period, its geometric A-component, or its regulator norm across levels. The subsequent [standard matrix comparison](standard_matrix_dilog_source_comparison.md) now makes the candidate charged replacement concrete: the actual pointed fusion map is written in the literature odd-level basic kernel with four face gauges, its input permutation and selected unit scalar. Root-charge changes become explicit Weyl leg operators and their Heisenberg phase, while the integer-charge prefactor remains a full function. The normal source chart has a regular standard kernel and the same integer carry poles. This identifies the local tensor and its actual source; it does not by itself prove that the globally prescribed charged face pairings are the induced ones, or repair the failed uncolored vertex-order prescription. The subsequent [shared face proof](shared_standard_face_gluing.md) now gives one frame per ordered triangle on the common flag chart. In it these actual pairings and corrected cyclic maps are explicit Gaussian matrices times their retained source-normalized scalars. Every ordered tetrahedron has a standard-kernel formula with an explicit clock/shift insertion. This is a compatible local frame description; it does not assert proportionality of the different uncolored vertex-order tensors or identify the global selected geometric period.

title: The original state has charged simplex amplitudes and a retained quadratic phase
text: # The original state has charged simplex amplitudes and a retained quadratic phase 28 October 2026. This is a statement about the original enhanced Kashaev state, before a Fourier or Fermat change of basis. Each nonzero crossing entry has four nonnegative factorial indices adding to N-1. Its absolute action is concave on that charged simplex, strictly concave on each face with at least three positive coordinates. The exact phases are quadratic and remain indispensable: reversing a crossing leaves its entire support and every absolute weight unchanged. The original cut forces the state onto proper faces. In particular, one must not assume an interior optimizer of the four-angle action is accessible to the original source. The [first-strand support reduction](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md) proves that the first head stays zero and gives the corresponding exact q-Pascal boundary operator, including the two unit-modulus end crossings. No broad volume-conjecture estimate follows from concavity alone. ## 1. Both actual crossings have the same charged support Use Q=exp(2 pi i/N), s=exp(pi i/N), F_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r), and the literature normalization proved in [the crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). Write B_+=P(R^o)^t and B_-=B_+^{-1}. For an entry with input (a,b) and output (c,d), put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-d], h=[d-b], (1) where brackets take values 0,...,N-1. Then exactly B_+[(c,d),(a,b)] =N Q^[1-(t+h)(u+h)]/(F_u conjugate(F_v) F_t conjugate(F_h)) (2) when u+v+t+h=N-1, and it is zero otherwise. This follows by substituting (i,j,k,l)=(a,b,d,c) into the original unbraided formula. The two printed theta inequalities are equivalent to this sum condition: the sum is congruent to -1 modulo N, and those inequalities bound it strictly below 2N. For the ACTUAL inverse, including the Q^{-1} correction to the printed inverse, its factorial indices are (h,u,v,t). Its numerator is N Q^[(u+v)(v+t)-1]. In particular the support is identical. Using the sum in (1) gives the stronger entrywise identity B_-[(c,d),(a,b)] =Q^(c+d-a-b) conjugate(B_+[(c,d),(a,b)]). (3) Indeed the exponent left after division by conjugate(B_+) is (u+v)(v+t)-(t+h)(u+h), congruent to h-v modulo N, and h-v is congruent to c+d-a-b. Thus if Z e_j=Q^j e_j, B_-=(Z tensor Z) conjugate(B_+) (Z tensor Z)^{-1}. (4) Conjugation in (3)-(4) is entrywise complex conjugation, not adjoint. It does not make the original braid transfer positive or unitary. The exact charged absolute weight is therefore, for either sign, |B_+[(c,d),(a,b)]|=|B_-[(c,d),(a,b)]| =N/|F_u F_v F_t F_h|. (5) ## 2. The uniform real action and its convex geometry Let Lambda(0)=0 and Lambda'(theta)=-log(2 sin theta) on (0,pi). The elementary uniform root-factorial estimate, including the two endpoints, is log|F_j|=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi j/N)+O(log(N+1)), 0<=j<N. (6) For clarity its uniformity does not require staying in the bulk. Split log(2 sin pi x) into log x+log(1-x) plus a smooth function on [0,1]. Stirling bounds for the two resulting factorial products and a bounded Riemann-sum error for the smooth part prove (6), uniformly in j. With alpha=(u,v,t,h)/N, (5)-(6) give (1/N)log|B_+|=H(alpha)+O(log(N+1)/N), H(alpha)=(1/pi)sum_(r=1)^4 Lambda(pi alpha_r), sum alpha_r=1-1/N. (7) For a fixed whole word, the error remains O_word(log N), and its number of state variables is fixed. Thus the absolute action of an actual state is the sum of these local H, with the original support and cut constraints. No scalar replacement state is needed to define this action. Here is the strict-concavity statement, including the obtuse case. For k>=3, theta_r>0 and sum theta_r=pi, the quadratic form sum_r cot(theta_r) w_r^2, sum_r w_r=0, (8) is positive definite. If every angle is at most pi/2, this is immediate; at most one coefficient can be zero in this open simplex. Otherwise exactly one angle, say theta_1, exceeds pi/2. Put s_0=sum_(r>1)theta_r=pi-theta_1<pi/2. Cauchy--Schwarz gives sum_(r>1)cot(theta_r) w_r^2 >= (sum_(r>1)w_r)^2 / sum_(r>1)tan(theta_r). The addition formula for tan gives sum_(r>1)tan(theta_r)<tan(s_0), since there are at least two positive summands and their sum is below pi/2. This strictly dominates the negative term -cot(s_0) w_1^2 whenever w_1 is nonzero. If w_1=0, the remaining positive diagonal form is positive on every nonzero vector. This proves (8). The same proof works when the angle sum is strictly below pi: then cot(sum_(r>1)theta_r)>cot(pi-theta_1), strengthening the inequality. Since the Hessian of sum Lambda is minus this cotangent form, H is strictly concave on the open charged simplex. It extends continuously as a concave function to its closure. On a face at limiting charge sum alpha=1, the same assertion holds for its k>=3 active coordinates. A two-coordinate face instead has zero action, because Lambda(theta)+Lambda(pi-theta)=0. One-coordinate faces also have zero action. Thus strictness on a forced source face must be checked, not inferred from strictness in the unattained open four-coordinate simplex. The value at the balanced point is 2 pi H(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)=8 Lambda(pi/4), the regular ideal octahedron volume. This calibrates the local absolute envelope. It is not a claim that its sum over a diagram equals the knot-complement volume. ## 3. Whole-word winding regions and their source faces Fix the original arc colors divided by N and choose integer lifts of the brackets in (1). The crossing indices are then affine functions of these colors; their sum is exactly 1-1/N. Nonnegativity defines a convex polytope for each choice of lifts. There are finitely many choices for a fixed word, independently of N. The pivotal closures must be imposed with their original shifts, not as unshifted equality of colors. On a region with all four coordinates positive at every crossing, the Hessian of the whole absolute action has kernel exactly the variations which leave every crossing index fixed. At a crossing, this requires all four incident arc variations to be equal. On a connected projection these equalities propagate to a common translation of all arc colors. Fixing the original cut color removes that translation. Therefore the whole action is strictly concave on any such nonempty region. It has at most one interior critical point; if one exists, it is the unique maximum on that region's closure. This assertion is deliberately not an existence claim. For the original one-cut source, some four-coordinate interiors are inaccessible. On a forced face, discard the zero-action one- and two-coordinate crossing faces. The exact strictness criterion is injectivity, on the remaining tangent space, of the combined corner maps at crossings with at least three active coordinates. This is a finite linear-algebra calculation. When it fails there are real flat directions, which need elimination before applying an ordinary nondegenerate Laplace argument. This gives a finite, source-dependent concavity problem. It does not put a nonzero quantum coefficient on its maximizer, or equate an absolute-state maximum with the geometric regulator. ## 4. The quadratic phase is part of the same original state The exact factorial phase is F_j=|F_j| exp[pi i j(j+1)/(2N)-pi i j/2]. (9) Write alpha_u,...,alpha_h for (1)/N, and define D(alpha)=alpha_u^2+alpha_t^2-alpha_v^2-alpha_h^2, L(alpha)=alpha_u+alpha_t-alpha_v-alpha_h, B(alpha)=-2pi(alpha_t+alpha_h)(alpha_u+alpha_h) -(pi/2)D(alpha)+(pi/2)L(alpha). Equations (2) and (9), without an asymptotic approximation, give B_+=|B_+| exp[i N B(alpha)-i(pi/2)L(alpha)+2pi i/N]. (10) The negative crossing uses the complex conjugate of (10), multiplied by the exact phase Q^(c+d-a-b) from (3). Thus on every fixed winding region the leading phase of the WHOLE original state is a real quadratic function of its arc colors, with crossing signs retained. The remaining linear phases, pivotal scalars, and writhe factor remain explicit. One may consequently define a phase homotopy by multiplying every chosen exact phase angle of the whole summand by tau in [0,1]. At tau=0 this is the absolute sum of that original presentation; at tau=1 it is the original invariant. Intermediate values are not claimed to be knot invariants. Concavity supplies a possible initial real maximum on each accessible face, but does not prove continuation of its integration cycle or nonvanishing at tau=1. There is a sharp reason that phase cannot be ignored. For a fixed braid POSITION word, (3) implies that changing any crossing signs changes neither its supported state set nor any absolute-state summand. The enhancement mu=-s S is a unit-modulus cyclic shift, and the writhe normalization also has modulus one, so the statement holds through the original full closure. Yet crossing changes can change the knot or unknot it. For example the position word (1,2,1,2) has the trefoil closure with all signs positive and the figure-eight closure with alternating signs. Their actual values differ, while their entire absolute-state sum is identical. This is an exact finite-state obstruction, not just a comparison of formal critical potentials. The new concavity therefore cannot by itself settle source selection. A reduced-alternating argument might additionally use its specified phase and projection, but those are additional information. The desired global theorem must carry (10) and the forced source faces all the way to the geometric contour. ## 5. Independent finite checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_original_crossing_winding_convexity.py) checks (1)-(5) against the independently implemented original crossing and its true inverse over finite fields, including even and composite levels. Complex checks verify (9)-(10), the full original pivotal contraction, the figure-eight normalization, and the equal absolute sums of the two signed words above. The cotangent tests supplement, and do not replace, the proof (8).

title: The original source has no automatic positive reflection form
text: # The original source has no automatic positive reflection form 27 October 2026. A universal reflection/Gram argument for the original Kashaev source fails at every level: its identity value is zero while an actual normalized unknot word has nonzero value. A two-channel reflection square has source -2. The standard alternating three-strand weaving transfer also cannot be made a positive Hermitian operator, at any level N>=3, by a positive metric or a scalar phase. These are obstructions to AUTOMATIC positivity of the original word source or transfer. They do not rule out a separately proved positive formula for a particular knot family, a word-dependent source elimination, an explicitly projected positive channel, or the existing positive squared norm of the original invariant. They do not disprove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The original source is not a positive functional Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2, complete color x=-q^-1=q^(N-1), and retain the original pivot K e_a=x Q^-a e_a, g=K^(1-N). For b>=2 the original reduced one-cut source on actual braid intertwiners is t_b(A)=Tr[(P_0 tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))A]. (1) The all-ones first output row gives the same value on these integer-weight-preserving words. The full source is its original nonzero dimension factor d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N, with the original zero-framing line. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. Since Q has exact order N, Tr(g)=x^(1-N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1)Q^-a=0, t_b(I)=0. (2) Let B_i be the original checked crossing with its own common Cartan factor recorded, and theta its original twist factor. Use the actual zero-framing normalized generator Bhat_i=theta^-1 B_i. The ordinary positive Markov chain W_b=Bhat_(b-1)...Bhat_1 closes to the unknot and has t_b(W_b)=t_b(W_b^-1)=1. (3) This can be checked directly without a knot-polynomial formula. At each last-strand pivotal closure the actual positive crossing has partial trace theta I; its inverse has theta^-1 I. For the positive crossing evaluate on the first highest vector: the closure forces both local indices zero, leaving g_0. For the inverse evaluate on the first lowest vector: only its zero transfer survives, leaving theta^-1. The root scalar-closure identity makes those the whole partial traces. Repeating the closures proves (3), with every original factor retained. **No-go theorem.** There is no involution dagger on a unital complex algebra containing these actual words, and no nonzero scalar multiple of t_b, which makes it a positive linear functional on all A^dagger A. Indeed a positive functional obeys Cauchy--Schwarz. Its value on the identity is zero by (2), so its value on every element would be zero. Equation (3) contradicts this. Equivalently, if the reflection Gram matrix on the channels I,W_b were Hermitian, its upper-left entry would be zero and its off-diagonal entry nonzero. Its determinant is negative. For the usual anti-linear inverse-word reflection, W_b^dagger =W_b^-1. The explicit formal braid combination A=I-W_b gives A^dagger A=2I-W_b-W_b^-1, t_b(A^dagger A)=-2. (4) This is an actual source evaluation of a linear combination of original braid words. It is not an invented negative test functional. The full dimension/phase line multiplies both positive and negative directions by the same fixed nonzero scalar; no phase can turn their indefinite Gram form positive. ## 2. The original cups and caps have the same obstruction The actual nonzero cup and cap obey cap cup=Tr(g)=0. They therefore cannot be Hermitian adjoints in a positive-definite reflection structure: that identity would be the squared norm of the nonzero cup. This is the actual isotropic cup/cap channel already exhibited in [the sewn-source construction](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md). One marked cap changes its specified channel and gives the normalized unknot value, but it does not convert ALL ordinary cup/cap pairings in a multi-bridge plat into positive adjoint pairings. Thus drawing a braid or plat as two reflected halves is not by itself a proof that its original scalar is a sum of absolute squares. A valid restricted formula must prove how its actual co-source becomes the required adjoint on the particular image subspace, with the marked cap and all other turns retained. ## 3. Even the basic alternating weaving transfer is not positive Let T_N=B_12 B_23^-1 on three original same-color strands. Its two crossing scalars and zero-framing factors cancel, since the word has writhe zero. It is the block repeated in the alternating weaving words (sigma_1 sigma_2^-1)^m. Consider its invariant physical total-index-one subspace with basis |100>,|010>,|001>. Literal crossing coefficients give T_N|_1=[[1-Q,0,1], [-q,0,0], [0,-q^-1,1-Q^-1]]. (5) For example the local index-one crossing block is [[1-Q,-q],[-q,0]] in the ordered pair |10>,|01>. The two coefficients are rho/x=1-Q and x^-1=-q at x=-q^-1. Multiplying the two adjacent blocks gives (5). This is a computation in the original head, without a proposed positive replacement crossing. Its exact characteristic polynomial is (lambda-1) [lambda^2-(1-Q-Q^-1)lambda+1]. (6) At N=3 it is (lambda-1)^3 but the matrix in (5) is not identity. Thus it is nontrivially unipotent and cannot be self-adjoint in any positive-definite Hermitian metric. At every N>=4 the two other roots are exp(+/-i theta_N), where cos(theta_N)=[1-2cos(2pi/N)]/2, pi/3<=theta_N<2pi/3. They are nonreal. Every positive-metric self-adjoint operator has real spectrum. Consequently T_N cannot be a positive Gram operator C^dagger C after any similarity. Multiplying it by a scalar phase cannot help: its eigenvalue 1 forces that phase to be positive real, leaving the nonreal pair unchanged. Nor does a fixed power remove the obstruction. For any fixed m>=1, the positive eigenvalue condition for T_N^m would require m theta_N to be an integer multiple of 2pi. The angle theta_N is strictly increasing to 2pi/3, so this cannot hold for all sufficiently large N. Indeed each admissible multiple can occur at most once. A fixed alternating weave block therefore cannot be converted into a positive transfer at all levels by taking a fixed number of repetitions. This statement concerns the transfer as an operator. A positive scalar identity for a particular closure could still result from source cancellation and a nontrivial finite-sum identity, as the [actual figure-eight proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) demonstrates. Operator positivity is stronger than that scalar conclusion. ## 4. What remains possible for a positive high-weight channel The unit-circle eigenpair in (6) does not exclude a separately constructed positive spectral channel elsewhere in the tensor module. Such a route would require at least: 1. An explicit source-compatible projection or relative source reduction on the actual word, rather than deleting the nonpositive channels from the invariant by definition. 2. A proved positive representation of the retained scalar with its original marked cap, phases and peripheral line. 3. A bound showing that omitted channels cannot cancel the desired leading contribution, plus a nonzero coupling to the calibrated geometric critical class. The existing positive trace for ordinary colors does not automatically give these facts on the Kashaev projective color. Its quantum dimension is precisely zero, while the modified source detects its nonsemisimple data. Nor does Rivin uniqueness establish positivity of this quantum source. No new positive high-weight channel satisfying these conditions has been constructed here. There IS already a valid positive formulation for all knots: the [original cyclic norm](regularized_kashaev_period.md#6-a-positive-trace-norm-gives-another-exact-formulation) satisfies H_N=|K_N|^2/N+O(poly(N)), and the [pointed A-Gram theorem](pointed_a_gram_period.md) expresses its equivalent pointed norm by positive polynomial coefficients. Those constructions retain the actual source and target. They are not an ordinary reflection-positive word trace, and their geometric exponential estimate and source overlap remain open. The present obstruction does not invalidate them. ## 5. Exact checks and scope [The audit](../experiments/audit_original_reflection_gram_obstruction.py) and [saved results](../experiments/original_reflection_gram_obstruction_results.json) check 17 literal original-source cases, braid indices two through four, including the normalized positive unknot chain, its actual inverse and (4). Seven exact root tests check the literal invariant block (5). Its characteristic polynomial is also checked symbolically. The complex positivity conclusion comes from the all-level proof, not from an inference about finite-field signs. This rules out the automatic Gram/reflection route and its basic alternating-transfer version. It neither rules out a separately proved positive family nor supplies a hyperbolic volume lower bound. A genuine selected geometric-cycle or source-compatible positive-channel theorem is still needed.

title: Exact cyclic variation and peeling the original Kashaev cut
text: # Exact cyclic variation and peeling the original Kashaev cut Research note, 28 October 2026. This is an exact support theorem for the original enhanced crossing in [the independently derived crossing convention](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). It uses neither a Fourier gauge nor an asymptotic estimate. It applies to every braid position word and every assignment of crossing signs. ## 1. The local cyclic interval Write Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N), and [x] for the representative in {0,...,N-1}. For a checked crossing with input (a,b) and output (c,d), put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-d], h=[d-b]. For either crossing sign the support condition is exactly u+v+t+h=N-1, [a-b]=v+t+h. (1) Thus, after lifting b to an integer, the output is in the cyclic interval b <= d_lift <= c_lift <= a_lift=b+[a-b]. (2) This follows directly from the original four-index weight and the actual inverse, including its Q^(-1) normalization. Negative crossings permute the four factorial indices, so they have the same support. Given colors x=(x_1,...,x_b) and fixed sentinels L,R, define the integer cyclic variation V_(L,R)(x)=[L-x_1]+sum_(i=1)^(b-1)[x_i-x_(i+1)] +[x_b-R]. (3) Every supported adjacent crossing makes V nonincreasing. Indeed, with neighboring colors p,s, its three affected summands satisfy [p-c] <= [p-a]+v, [d-s] <= h+[b-s], [c-d]=t, v+t+h=[a-b]. (4) The inequalities are the elementary triangle inequality for nonnegative cyclic distance. Their defects are nonnegative multiples of N. ## 2. The actual source forces a face at every cut crossing The original enhancement is mu=-q S, where S e_j=e_(j+1 mod N). Fix the first cut color to zero. Each summation path in the actual weighted partial trace runs from x_in =(0,[A_2+1],...,[A_b+1]) x_out=(0,A_2,...,A_b). (5) This is a statement about an individual nonzero path, before summing coefficients. Choose L=0 and R=[A_b+1]. The interior tail distances in (3) agree at the two endpoints. Direct subtraction gives V(x_in)-V(x_out) = 0 if A_2=0, -N otherwise. (6) Monotonicity therefore forces A_2=0, and V must be constant throughout the path. Both inequalities in (4) are consequently equalities at every crossing. At any crossing in position 1, its left neighbor is the sentinel 0, so [0-c]=[0-a]+v. (7) Only these crossings change x_1. Telescoping (7) from x_1=0 back to x_1=0 shows that the sum of their nonnegative v's is zero. Therefore x_1=0 at EVERY stage; every position-1 crossing has v=0. (8) In particular, no original source path can lie in a chamber with all four crossing angles positive at every vertex. Formal strict concavity on such a chamber is not an assertion that the original source occupies that chamber. Before the first position-1 crossing, only position-2 crossings can change x_2. Their left equality in (4) makes [0-x_2] nondecreasing. It starts at N-1, because A_2=0. Hence x_2 stays 1 until the first position-1 crossing. After the last position-1 crossing the same quantity ends at zero, so x_2 is already zero and remains zero. Consequently: first position-1 crossing: u=v=0; last position-1 crossing: v=t=0. (9) If there is only one such crossing, both statements hold. If there are none, the original source has no supported paths. These statements remain valid for links; no scalar-endomorphism assertion is required. The original absolute crossing weight is N/|F_u F_v F_t F_h|, with F_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r). The reflection |F_j F_(N-1-j)|=N shows that BOTH end crossings in (9) have absolute weight exactly one. Every other cut crossing is on the tetrahedral three-corner face v=0. This is an actual source-support reduction. ## 3. Exact q-Pascal boundary operators Set T^sigma_(k,j)=(B_sigma)_(0,k ; 0,j). All indices below lie in {0,...,N-1}. Directly from the original crossing formula, T+_(0,j)=Q^(1-j), T+_(k,0)=0 for k>0, T+_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[k+(j-1)(j-2)/2] {k-1 choose j-1}_Q, 1<=j<=k<=N-1, (10) and all remaining entries vanish. The actual inverse crossing gives T-_(k,j)=Q^(k-j) conjugate(T+_(k,j)). (11) Thus T-_(0,j)=Q^(-1), and, for 1<=j<=k<=N-1, T-_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[-j-(j-1)(j-2)/2] {k-1 choose j-1}_(Q^-1). (12) For example, (10) follows by replacing N/F_(N-k) with bar_F_(k-1) and bar_F_r with (-1)^r Q^[-r(r+1)/2]F_r. The wrap row k=0 is kept; it is not an optional endpoint correction. In fact T-=(T+)^(-1). To prove this without compressing an inverse by fiat, let P be the positive-index block of T+, indexed r,i=0,...,N-2: P_(r,i)=Q^(r+1)(-1)^i Q^[i(i-1)/2]{r choose i}_Q. The finite q-binomial theorem gives the inverse q-Pascal matrix ({r choose i}_Q)^(-1) =(-1)^(r-i)Q^[(r-i)(r-i-1)/2]{r choose i}_Q. The resulting inverse of P is exactly (12). For the wrap row, the finite q-hockey-stick identity and the root specialization imply sum_(r=i)^(N-2) P_(r,i)=-Q^(-i). This gives the constant wrap row Q^(-1) in the inverse of T+. The formula is valid at every N>=2, without a prime-level assumption. ## 4. The full original scalar after peeling Let W be the braid word in its actual operator order, let w be its writhe, and let alpha=-q. Construct a word W_peel on b-1 heads by replacing every position-1 crossing by T+ or T-, and every crossing in position i>=2 by the same original B+ or B- in position i-1. No sign, ordering, Cartan scalar, or framing factor changes. For b>=2 the exact fixed-cut scalar is K_N(W)=(-q) alpha^(-w) [ Tr_(heads 3,...,b) ( W_peel (I tensor mu^(tensor(b-2))) ) ]_(0,1). (13) The trace in (13) is over the remaining heads except its first one. For b=2 this is just (-q)alpha^(-w)(W_peel)_(0,1). The outside factor -q is the retained pivotal coefficient on the removed ordinary trace of original head 2. The original writhe w is unchanged, including crossings replaced by T. Proof: expand the original weighted partial trace into paths. Section 2 forces every first-head label to zero and A_2=0. Restrict each crossing coefficient accordingly and perform the remaining sums. This gives (13) term by term, before using cancellation. It is stronger than a formal compression identity for arbitrary sources. The first-strand shell is therefore removed uniformly for every original braid. This differs from [the classical arbitrary-bridge deformation reduction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md): (13) is an identity of the actual finite quantum scalar. Iterating it without preserving the new T boundary operators is not justified. The remaining T/B word is complex, and this theorem supplies no geometric saddle coefficient or volume lower bound. ## 5. Reproducible checks `experiments/audit_original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.py` checks the original matrices and their actual inverses over cyclotomic prime fields, both q-Pascal formulas and their product, every supported local cyclic-variation inequality at small levels, full original signed-word scalars against (13), and the forced faces path by path. The same-position trefoil and figure-eight words have identical support and absolute local weights, while their actual selected scalars differ. The source reduction therefore does not remove the need to control the original phases.

title: The oversized weak alias fails at the last Pachner norm wall
text: # The oversized weak alias fails at the last Pachner norm wall 28 October 2026. This traces the certified oversized weak alias of [the nine-tetrahedron counterexample](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md) backward through its actual last $2\to3$ move. The first inverse step already has no boundary-preserving nonnegative angular preimage. The exact five-term map locates the norm divisor and its direction data. This does not prove that the original quantum source assigns zero to the wall. The exact audit is [audit_oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.py](../experiments/audit_oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.py), with [results](../experiments/oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall_results.json). It derives the local vertex labels from the actual saved face permutations, verifies the shape map in the certified cubic field, and checks the angle and norm identities symbolically. ## 1. A universal angular preimage criterion Label a triangular bipyramid by equatorial vertices $A,B,C$ and apices $D,E$. The actual old tetrahedron orderings in this example are $$ (D,A,B,C),\qquad (B,E,C,A). $$ Its new orderings are $$ (E,D,C,B),\qquad(E,D,B,A),\qquad(E,D,A,C). \tag{1} $$ Write each new angle triple as $(\alpha_j,\beta_j,\gamma_j)$, $j=0,1,2$. The new internal edge $DE$ and its opposite equatorial edge both carry $\alpha_j$. Each triple sums to $\pi$. Boundary angle preservation uniquely forces the old triples to be $$ \begin{split} X={}&(\beta_1+\gamma_2,\ \beta_0+\gamma_1,\ \gamma_0+\beta_2),\\ Y={}&(\gamma_0+\beta_1,\ \gamma_1+\beta_2,\ \beta_0+\gamma_2). \tag{2} \end{split} $$ For example, old edge $DA$ is split between the new $\beta_1$ and $\gamma_2$ corners; the other entries follow in the same way from the actual vertex labels. Both forced old sums are $$ \sum X=\sum Y=\sum_j(\beta_j+\gamma_j) =3\pi-\sum_j\alpha_j. \tag{3} $$ Consequently: **A boundary-preserving replacement by two nonnegative angle tetrahedra exists if and only if the new internal angle is exactly $2\pi$.** When this holds, (2) supplies the replacement and every old triple sums to $\pi$. If the new non-internal angles are positive, both old triples are positive. The three equatorial angle equations are then also preserved; for instance $$ X_0+Y_1=\alpha_0,\quad X_2+Y_2=\alpha_1,\quad X_1+Y_0=\alpha_2. \tag{4} $$ This is an angular boundary statement, not an assertion that arbitrary off-critical shape moduli or quantum integration cycles are transported by this linear map. In particular the angular image of an ordinary positive Pachner chart, and its continuous closure with its angle marks retained, has internal winding **one**. Exponentiating the edge equation and then admitting every weak nonnegative winding locus forgets this local support condition. ## 2. The certified face fails at the first reverse step The last forward move in the six-move sequence is $(1,0)$: old tetrahedron 1, face opposite its vertex 0, is adjacent to old tetrahedron 0. The actual face maps identify the new tetrahedra as final tetrahedra $0,1,2$ with orderings (1). Their new edge is final global edge 7, locally $01$ in every new tetrahedron. Its three opposite equatorial edges are final global edges $8,6,3$, respectively. At the oversized rational point the three new triples are $$ (0,1/20,19/20),\quad (0,2/5,3/5),\quad (0,1/10,9/10), \tag{5} $$ in units of $\pi$. Their new edge winding is zero. Formula (2) would force the old triples $$ X=(13/10,13/20,21/20),\qquad Y=(27/20,7/10,19/20), \tag{6} $$ each summing to $3$, rather than $1$. Equivalently, preserving the three equatorial angles would require their sum to be zero, whereas the sum of those six old angles is necessarily $2\pi$. Thus the face cannot be pulled back even one step through the previous nonnegative angular contour with its boundary marks fixed. No earlier part of the six-move chain is needed to find the obstruction. Each forced old local sum has an extra $2\pi$; removing it requires a non-positive angle or a change of branch/boundary charge. ## 3. The exact actual five-term map Use the cross-ratio convention $$ [p,q;r,s]=\frac{(p-r)(q-s)}{(p-s)(q-r)}. $$ Normalize $D=\infty,A=0,B=1,C=x$. If $y$ is the old native shape of $(B,E,C,A)$, then $$ E=\frac{xy}{x+y-1}. $$ For the new native shapes $u,v,w$ of (1), direct substitution gives $$ \boxed{\quad u=\frac{x}{1-y},\qquad v=\frac{(1-x)(1-y)}{xy},\qquad w=\frac{y}{1-x},\qquad uvw=1. \quad} \tag{7} $$ The audit verifies these identities for the actual old and new geometric shapes in the field $a^3-2a^2+3a-1=0$. The inverse is $$ \boxed{\quad x=\frac{u(1-w)}{1-uw},\qquad y=\frac{w(1-u)}{1-uw}. \quad} \tag{8} $$ In the positive geometric branch the new edge has the marked relation $$ \operatorname{Log}u+\operatorname{Log}v+ \operatorname{Log}w=2\pi i. \tag{9} $$ For a positive tetrahedron with angles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, the native shape is $$ z=e^{i\alpha}\frac{\sin\beta}{\sin\gamma}. $$ At (5), $\alpha=0$ and $\beta+\gamma=\pi$, so all three radial minimum shapes are exactly $$ u=v=w=1. $$ Their marked log sum is zero, not $2\pi i$. The inverse (8) is simultaneously $0/0$, on the norm divisor $1-uw=0$. The weak point is not a limit of the positive geometric branch: near three positive real unit shapes their principal arguments are all small positive numbers and cannot sum to $2\pi$. Away from the simultaneous corner, the inverse logarithmic connection forms have genuine divisor residues $$ \operatorname{Res}_{1-uw=0}d\log x =\operatorname{Res}_{1-uw=0}d\log y=-1. \tag{10} $$ At the simultaneous corner the numerator zeros matter. Blow up by $$ u=1+\varepsilon A,\qquad w=1+\varepsilon B, \quad AB(A+B)\ne0. $$ Then $$ x\longrightarrow\frac{B}{A+B},\qquad y\longrightarrow\frac{A}{A+B},\qquad x+y\longrightarrow1. \tag{11} $$ Thus the exceptional divisor retains the direction $A:B$. Its finite old shapes cannot both lie in the upper half-plane, since their sum is real. Formula (10) is a generic divisor residue; it must not be copied unchanged to the simultaneous corner where the numerator and denominator valuations cancel. ## 4. Exact comparison with the retained cyclic pentagon norms Use the primitive pentagon of [cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md), with its actual centers and roots: $$ a_N^N=1-U,\qquad b_N^N=1-V,\qquad h_N^N=H=1-U+UV. $$ The exact substitution for (7) is $$ U=w,\qquad V=x,\qquad H=1-y. \tag{12} $$ Its left centers $(V,(1-V)U)$ are precisely $(x,y)$. Its right centers are $$ \left(U,\frac{-UV}{1-U},\frac{V}{H}\right) =\left(w,\frac1{1-v},u\right). \tag{13} $$ The middle new shape has undergone the indicated quad rotation; its center cannot be frozen at $v$. Under (11), the three right norm-root powers behave as $$ \begin{split} a_N^N&=1-w\sim-\varepsilon B,\\ (h_N/a_N)^N&=\frac{1-y}{1-w} \sim-\frac1{\varepsilon(A+B)},\\ (a_Nb_N/h_N)^N&=\frac{(1-w)(1-x)}{1-y} \sim-\varepsilon A. \tag{14} \end{split} $$ Their valuations are therefore $(1/N,-1/N,1/N)$ on a compatible root cover. The middle center in (13) goes to infinity. The anchored cyclic pentagon theorem is localized away from these norm divisors and does not itself supply this simultaneous boundary extension or its source/co-source residues. Equivalently, a small loop of $\varepsilon$ around zero, at fixed generic direction $A:B$, changes the three compatible root frames by $(Q,Q^{-1},Q)$, where $Q=e^{2\pi i/N}$. The two old norm roots $b_N,h_N$ have no local winding at a generic finite direction. This is a concrete root-torsor monodromy charge. It cannot be removed by choosing the three right roots independently. Norm-root zeros cannot justify deleting the wall. For example, in the normalized finite atom of that note put $t=1-\text{center}$ and choose the spectral root $\mu=(1-t)^{1/N}$. Its eigenvalues obey $$ f_0=1,\qquad f_j=\frac{t^{j/N}}{(\mu;Q)_j}, \qquad D_j=\gamma f_j,\qquad \gamma^N=\left(\prod_jf_j\right)^{-1}. $$ For $1\le j<N$, exactly one denominator factor vanishes: $1-\mu\sim t/N$. All other factors are nonzero at a primitive $N$th root, including composite $N$. Hence $$ \operatorname{ord}_tD_0=\frac{N-1}{2N},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_tD_j=\frac{2j-N-1}{2N}\quad(1\le j<N). \tag{15} $$ There are both zeros and poles for every $N\ge2$, while their sum is zero. A vanishing norm root does not give a vanishing operator or source. This is consistent with the original [cap-wall residue theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md): at its actual Fermat cusp a raw source has a compulsory simple pole with nonzero cap residue. The relevant boundary extension must retain those residues, the dual shift, and the central Jacobian, rather than assign zero from the norm alone. ### A removable singularity for the full normalized local product There is nevertheless a precise local extension, with a narrower claim than separate atom or source extension. Fix a generic holomorphic blow-up curve with $x(0)=x_0\notin\{0,1\}$ and $y(0)=1-x_0$ as in (11). Choose regular initial cyclic clock/shift frames and the compatible root component of the strict primitive pentagon. Then its **full normalized right three-atom product**, expressed between the common initial and final frames, extends holomorphically and invertibly across the ramified corner. Indeed the left centers are $x$ and $y$, whose limiting values are neither zero nor one. Their norm roots $b_N,h_N$ are therefore locally nonzero holomorphic functions; their normalization determinants are nonzero as well. The two left matrices are holomorphic and invertible. The common final splitting roots are $b_N$ times the initial first root and the initial second root divided by $h_N$; they remain regular and nonzero. On the punctured compatible root cover the exact pentagon identifies the right product with this left product. The equality supplies its removable extension. This conclusion retains all determinant roots and common-frame identifications. A raw product must retain its raw scalar from the pentagon theorem. No claim is made that its unnormalized individual factors have removable singularities. The argument gives no estimate uniform in $N$, no right to drop intermediate residues, and no comparison with an original knot source unless the required exterior source/co-source maps have also been transported. ## 5. The precise constructive target The local classical support test is now explicit: **an inverse positive angular Pachner replacement must retain new-edge winding one, not merely the exponentiated equation $uvw=1$.** For the certified excessive face, the failing move, its marked integer defect, the norm divisors, and the direction $A:B$ are known. The remaining quantum task is a matched source/carry extension of this last move across (14), proving how its marked $2\pi$ charge is represented and paired. Original integer degree conservation can retain information lost modulo $N$, but no identification of that integer carry with this geometric edge winding has been proved here. The existing Ward augmentation shows that some wall charge survives; it does not allow all walls to be discarded. In particular we have not proved a zero quantum coefficient for (5), nor inferred an oversized original period. What is available for a general proof is a universal local angular admissibility criterion and an exact divisor calculation on which the required quantum source theorem can be tested.

title: Independent audit of the partial geometric-support construction
text: # Independent audit of the partial geometric-support construction Audit, 27 October 2026, of [the partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). The new partial-sum argument is valid given the repository's actual critical-chart/Hessian theorem and the global zero-extended finite-array dimension lemma. In particular its transverse moment argument avoids assuming the missing covariance of a full framing-period functional. This audit does not assert the selected global period is nonzero on the geometric branch. ## 1. Why a pair of actual external coordinates suffices Let V be the tangent space of actual independent flow coordinates, with symmetric Hessian B and two-dimensional radical R. A coordinate projection p:V->k^2 whose restriction to R is invertible exists by selecting a nonzero two-by-two minor of a basis of R. Put K=ker p. Then V=R direct_sum K and B restricted to K is nondegenerate: any vector orthogonal to K is also orthogonal to R, and hence to V; if it belongs to K it is zero. Fixing those two original coordinates therefore gives precisely a nondegenerate transverse stationary problem. Its internal critical equations have a unique local solution over the external coordinates and meridian. The full two-dimensional framed critical germ maps etale to those same external coordinates, so its internal solution is that unique solution. Thus the full critical gradient vanishes on the partially contracted branch, including its external components. The critical action consequently has zero frame derivatives and retains the marked unframed meridian/longitude derivative. This is stronger than choosing an arbitrary framing section after performing the finite sum: the external labels remain genuine independent variables in both the certificate and the formal block. ## 2. Exact contiguity survives the specialization used here The global certificate annihilates the entire zero-extended array, including the finite boundary. Dividing by a nonzero common central power of z+1 is valid for every fixed generic integer N, since q^N+1 is a nonzero rational function of q. The full-array identity therefore specializes regularly at z=-1, q=q_N, after fixed scalar denominators are cleared. A nonzero fixed rational operator can have only finitely many exceptional q_N levels. Separately, the interior cone-density argument makes the divided certificate a rational contiguity identity in independent variables q,x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t. That identity can also be specialized at z=-1. This separate independent-variable identity is essential: a relation only on a finite frame grid at one root would not suffice for the formal Gaussian block. The compact-product formal solution has exactly the same interior shift ratios, since its Bernoulli series obeys the functional equation P_Q(Qz)=P_Q(z)/(1-z) coefficientwise. Fixed singular arguments such as P_Q(Q) occur only in the retained common base line; all variables on the chosen regular geometric chart avoid the polar divisors. Thus the formal identity uses rational factor cancellation, never evaluation of an individual infinite compact product at a root. ## 3. The finite and formal moment repairs agree exactly The physical logarithmic internal coordinate is u_i=Hj_i, H=Log Q. Hence exp(v dot j) is implemented in the formal period by the phase S+v dot u, divided by H. Its critical point deforms uniquely because the transverse Hessian is invertible. The weighted formal period belongs to the original WKB line times k((H))[[v]]; its negative H orders may grow with the v degree. No uniform lower H bound over all v degrees is required. Formal Gaussian contraction satisfies integration by parts. For the quadratic kernel exp(x^t B x/(2H)), Wick covariance is -H B^(-1); contraction of a derivative of a monomial cancels the contraction of (Bx)_i/H times that monomial. Expanding cubic and higher vertices gives the same identity coefficientwise, with finitely many contractions in each allowed order. Thus a formal total derivative has zero contraction. Translate one internal coordinate by H. The weighted integrand then changes by exp(-v_i) after the corresponding formal change of coordinate. Equivalently the infinitesimal translation equation is G_v(H partial_i f)=-v_i G_v(f); integrating the translation parameter gives G_v(S_i f)=exp(-v_i)G_v(f). The H-dependent shift is a valid formal translation around the unique critical germ. The determinant half-line is continued with that same germ, rather than rechoosing its square root after shifting. External multiplication and the meridian step commute with this contraction. The latter shifts log M by H/2, while Ahat,Bhat are held fixed, and carries the critical point to its unique nearby one. It leaves H and the retained common base line fixed. There are no internal multiplication variables in the certificate's operator coefficients. Therefore its expansion in (S-1) has exactly the same least nonzero multi-degree after either finite weighted summation or formal transverse contraction. At that degree every positive moment is multiplied by a lower, identically zero operator coefficient. The same nonzero D_alpha annihilates the actual partial finite family and its nonzero transverse formal block. This would not justify an unproved integration functional in either of the two remaining framing directions. They remain external. ## 4. The leading-symbol conclusion and its scope After dividing the common scalar q-1 valuation, the operator has a nonzero leading classical symbol. The transverse formal block has unit leading amplitude and the actual marked longitude as its leading meridian ratio. Its annihilation therefore forces that symbol to vanish on the marked geometric longitude branch. The external coordinates range over a dense open frame chart by the etaleness in Section 1. They are algebraically independent over the geometric branch field; a purely transcendental extension does not split its irreducible rational defining polynomial. Thus the stated A_geo factor divisibility over Q(Ahat,Bhat) is valid. The conclusion concerns the specifically constructed partial-state annihilator. It neither identifies its minimal operator nor says that the full finite scalar contraction retains that component. In particular a nonzero local formal transverse block is not yet a nonzero selected global geometric contribution. No global cycle, Stokes, cancellation, or volume conclusion has been added here.

title: A geometric A-factor for an actual partially summed quantum state
text: # A geometric A-factor for an actual partially summed quantum state Research note, 27 October 2026. This proves a bulk geometric-support theorem for the original finite coefficient model. Leave two actual integer flow coordinates unsummed, and eliminate all remaining flow coordinates. The resulting finite family has a specifically constructed nonzero all-level meridian annihilator whose first nonzero classical symbol contains the marked geometric A-factor. The construction does not append a known classical factor. This partial family retains its two framing indices. Pairing them with the selected full finite source is a further operation. The theorem does not assert survival under that operation, a statement about the minimal scalar annihilator, or a volume limit. ## 1. The actual partial family Use a knot braid with `b` strands and `m` crossings, the balanced factorial boundary frame, and the original normalized cut average. Set q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, Y=M^2. All crossings, the original pivot, the full zero-framing correction, the cut factor `1/N`, lift characters and base-only compact factors are retained. If the full ADO state is wanted, its complete original marked factor `d_N(M)` remains an external line; it is not absorbed into a formal unit or replaced by its value at completeness. Closing strands `1,...,b-1` gives a cofactor of the knot permutation matrix minus identity, with determinant `+1` or `-1`. Solve these closures integrally. The independent actual flow coordinates are k=(a_0,k_1,...,k_m), d=m+1. The remaining closure follows from total-index conservation. The summand is the actual product of the finite crossing and boundary coefficients, zero outside its finite integral support. On the regular geometric critical chart the Hessian has a two-dimensional radical equal to the tangent space of the framing torsor. This is the Morse--Bott statement for the **actual** coefficient phase proved in [the normal-period note](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Select two members `chi_1,chi_2` of the displayed actual coordinate list whose differentials are independent on this radical. Such a pair exists because the radical is a two-dimensional subspace of the coordinate tangent space. No integral change of variables is made. Keep `chi=(a,b)` external and sum only over the remaining `r=d-2=m-1` coordinates `j`. The actual partial array is F_N^chi(M;a,b)=sum_(j in Z^r) I_N(q_N,-M/q_N;a,b,j). The sum is finite and includes its exact boundary. Its final contraction over the two external indices is the original reduced scalar state. The auxiliary off-root lift uses the same normalized cut trace and the same partial array, with generic `q`; topological invariance of that off-root lift is not a premise. For coefficient bookkeeping put z=q^N, Ahat=q^a, Bhat=q^b, t_i=q^(j_i). The physical phase coordinates are `A=Ahat^2=Q^a` and `B=Bhat^2=Q^b`. Keeping `Ahat,Bhat` avoids suppressing the genuine square-root characters in a meridian half-step. Alternatively one may work on their stated finite etale cover. Let `T` send `M` to `qM` (equivalently `x` to `qx`) while holding `q,Ahat,Bhat` fixed. ## 2. A global partial-array certificate The proof in [the finite-array annihilator note](finite_sum_annihilator.md) extends with the two external multiplication variables. Its summand ratios are proper and aligned rational functions in q,x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t_1,...,t_r. For `0<=e_x,e_z,e_A,e_B,e_T,beta_i<=R`, consider x^e_x z^e_z Ahat^e_A Bhat^e_B T^e_T S^beta I, where `S_i` shifts `j_i` by one and never shifts `a,b`. These are `(R+1)^(r+5)` independent formal Ore monomials. Their image span has dimension `O(R^(r+4))` over `Q(q)`. In the interior, clear the rational shift ratios by one common denominator whose Laurent degrees are `O(R)` in the `r+4` multiplication variables `x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t`. For the boundary proof, stratify every support inequality according to whether it is far inside, far outside, or has one specified integer value in an interval of length `O(R)`. If the near-boundary forms have rank `c` on `(N,a,b,j)`, there are `O(R^c)` consistent sets of their labels. On each resulting stratum, the associated `c` binomial relations leave `O(R^(r+4-c))` Laurent monomials after the fixed Smith reductions. The total contribution is again `O(R^(r+4))`. Supported shifts have nonzero common denominators on the stratum, exactly as in the original proof. Empty and lower-dimensional supports are included. Finite linear algebra therefore constructs a nonzero certificate P(x,z,Ahat,Bhat,T,S) I=0 (2.1) on the whole zero-extended array, with no multiplication by any internal `t_i`. Separate summand components, if present, can be retained in a direct sum, giving a common certificate. The full flow support has a nonempty open cone of strict inequalities: take all transfers small and positive compared with `N` and the free cut position near `N/2`. Every position is then `N/2+O(epsilon*N)`. This is unchanged by choosing a subset of the coordinates as external. Consequently (2.1), divided by a nonzero interior reference term, is a rational identity in all independent multiplication variables. The precise lattice-cone density proof is in [the sourced-telescoping audit](sourced_telescoping_geometric_support_criterion.md), Section 2. This step is needed: a relation only on isolated discrete frame values would not suffice for the formal geometric argument. ## 3. Root specialization and transverse moment repair Clear fixed coefficient denominators and divide the largest common central power `(z+1)^s` from the **whole** certificate, obtaining `P0`. For each fixed generic `N`, `q^N+1` is a nonzero rational function of `q`, so the global array identity survives this division. The finite summands are regular at `q_N`; their crossing factorial denominators have indices below `N`. Thus P1(x,Ahat,Bhat,T,S)=P0(x,-1,Ahat,Bhat,T,S) (3.1) is nonzero and annihilates the actual root partial arrays for all but finitely many levels. The same specialization is valid for the independent-variable interior contiguity identity. Expand in the commuting transverse shifts only: P1=sum_alpha D_alpha(x,Ahat,Bhat,T)(S-1)^alpha. Let `h0` be the least total degree with a nonzero coefficient, and choose any nonzero `D_alpha` of that degree. Give the finite internal sum independent weights `exp(v dot j)`. Exact translation of the whole finite zero-extended sum sends `S_i` to `exp(-v_i)`. At degree `v^alpha`, every positive moment multiplies a coefficient of degree below `h0`, and hence is zero. Therefore D_alpha(q_N,-M/q_N,q_N^a,q_N^b,T) F_N^chi(M;a,b)=0. (3.2) This is a genuine nonzero all-level operator for the actual partial family. All external labels and all finite boundary strata are kept. ## 4. The same certificate acts on the exact formal transverse period Write `H=Log Q=2 Log q`. In logarithmic physical flow coordinates, the actual interior coefficient has a formal realization I_form=C_beta(H) exp(S/H) a(u,H), with the original characters, `a(u,H)=a_0(u)(1+O(H))`, and `a_0` a unit on the chosen geometric chart. The retained base line `C_beta(H)` includes the cut average and the fixed compact factors. It is not evaluated at an individual root. This formal realization has the **exact** rational contiguity ratios, not merely their leading symbols. One construction uses the original monomials and the compact-product series, for variable arguments different from `0,1`, log P_Q(z)=Li_2(z)/H +(1/2)log(1-z) +sum_(n>=1) B_(2n) H^(2n-1)/(2n)! Li_(2-2n)(z). Its formal functional equation is `P_Q(Qz)=P_Q(z)/(1-z)`. This follows either coefficientwise from the Bernoulli generating function or by expanding the defining geometric-series logarithm. Thus its ratios agree to all orders with cancellation of the original finite factors. Signs and logarithm sheets are the ones fixed by the actual critical-correspondence calculation. The fixed singular argument `P_Q(Q)` stays in the base-only line. Pivotal monomials and the framing correction have their literal exact shift ratios as well. Now fix the two external coordinates `chi`. The remaining coordinate space complements the radical of the symmetric Hessian. The restricted `r` by `r` Hessian is therefore nondegenerate. The critical point of `S` in the remaining variables is unique in the chosen formal germ. The full geometric critical surface is etale over `chi`, so its unique point at each nearby external `chi` supplies a solution of these transverse equations. By uniqueness this is the same partial critical germ, and all of the full critical equations hold there. Its unweighted Gaussian contraction is nonzero, with leading amplitude a_0/sqrt(det(-H_perp)). (4.1) Introduce independent weights by replacing the phase with S_v(u)=S(u)+sum_(i=1)^r v_i u_i. The formal implicit-function theorem gives a unique critical point `u(v)` with `u(0)=u_*`, because `H_perp` is invertible. Formal stationary contraction there defines `Z_chi(v)`. It is a formal power series in `v` whose coefficients lie in the original WKB line times Laurent series in `H`. Its value at zero is nonzero. The action difference divided by `H` can produce increasingly negative finite `H` orders as the `v` degree grows; this is allowed. Formal stationary contraction is invariant under a translation of an internal integration coordinate. Explicitly, for the unit shift `u_i -> u_i+H`, substituting `y_i=u_i+H` in the formal Gaussian gives G_v(S_i f)=exp(-v_i) G_v(f). (4.2) This is an identity of formal stationary expansions at their corresponding critical points, with an elementary termwise proof. For one shifted coordinate its weighted phase is S(u+H e_i)+v dot u = S_v(u+H e_i)-H v_i. Its critical point is `u(v)-H e_i`. Centering at that point gives exactly the same Hessian, higher vertices, amplitude Taylor series and coordinate volume as centering `S_v` at `u(v)`. Only the constant phase changes, by `-H v_i`. Thus every Wick coefficient is multiplied by `exp(-v_i)`. No integration-by-parts theorem is a premise of this argument. No finite-array endpoint or framing endpoint is being discarded here: this is a formal contraction of precisely the `r` nondegenerate transverse variables.
