Both framing coordinates remain external throughout. The same formal contraction commutes with the meridian step `T`. The shifted critical point is the unique nearby one with the same external `Ahat,Bhat`; the formal construction and its retained half-density are natural under that base shift. Multiplication by external rational coefficients commutes as well. Apply this contraction to the exact interior identity (3.1). By (4.2), P1(x,Ahat,Bhat,T,exp(-v)) Z_chi(v)=0. The same least-degree moment coefficient used for the **finite** partial sum therefore gives D_alpha Z_chi(0)=0. (4.3) Unlike full framed integration, this implication has no missing relative-source covariance assumption. Nondegeneracy of the transverse block and leaving both framing coordinates external provide it directly. The subsequent [full Green-certificate calculation](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md) also transports the actual fully summed scalar operator to this transverse block. Its image includes two explicitly computed framing boundary currents. Their final endpoint and logarithmic-carry functional is retained; neither the formal residual Ward ideal nor the source torsor identities currently prove its cancellation. Thus the distinction between the present partial theorem and the full scalar claim is now an explicit source defect, not an omitted ordinary Gaussian variable. ## 5. The classical symbol has the geometric factor Divide `D_alpha` by its common scalar `(q-1)` valuation and clear remaining rational denominators. Call the resulting nonzero operator `Dhat`. Scalar division is valid both in the actual root identities (for all large `N`) and in the formal WKB line. Let d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L) be its first nonzero classical symbol in the stated meridian and lift gauge. The exact preferred-longitude calculation for the actual phase gives leading [T Z_chi(0)/Z_chi(0)]=L_geom(M). Indeed the full critical gradient vanishes on the framing torsor, so the critical action has zero derivative in both frame directions. Its meridian derivative at fixed `chi` is therefore the same marked longitude derivative as on the unframed geometric branch. The transverse amplitude is a unit and does not alter this leading ratio. Equation (4.3) now gives d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L_geom(M))=0. (5.1) The two selected flow coordinates are etale coordinates on the framing torsor. Consequently their values range over a dense open part of a two-dimensional frame space over the geometric branch. Equation (5.1) is therefore a relation over the purely transcendental frame coefficient field, not only at one frame. Let `A_geo(M,L)` denote the irreducible rational polynomial defining the Zariski closure of the marked geometric longitude branch, in the same sign, inverse and preferred-longitude convention. Its irreducibility is preserved by the independent transcendental frame variables. Clearing peripheral denominators in (5.1) proves A_geo(M,L) divides d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L) over `Q(Ahat,Bhat)`, up to the recorded monomial and lift gauges. This is the claimed geometric-support theorem. In particular the constructed operator has positive meridian-shift order; a nonzero order-zero rational multiplier cannot annihilate this nonzero formal period on a dense open chart. The whole construction of `Dhat` uses actual finite coefficients, global boundary linear algebra, central specialization, and transverse moment extraction. It never multiplies an operator by an independently supplied `A_geo`. ### The actual certified module has a formal geometric line quotient There is a corresponding precise formal torsor statement. Let `K_geo` be the algebraic function field of the marked geometric gluing branch and its two retained framing coordinates, with the recorded half-density and sign covers. Put `h=Log q`, and let `Z_geo^chi` be the nonzero transverse block just constructed. On this field the shift is the formal automorphism `sigma=exp(h delta)`, where `delta=M partial_M` fixes both framing coordinates and extends uniquely to the algebraic and half-density covers in characteristic zero. Its shift ratio b_geo=T(Z_geo^chi)/Z_geo^chi in K_geo[[h]]^*, b_geo|_(h=0)=L_geom has algebraic coefficients. The meridian-independent base-only line cancels in this ratio. The exponent difference has leading `Log L`, and its higher derivatives are algebraic after exponentiating that leading logarithm; the transverse amplitudes and all their meridian derivatives are algebraic as proved in the normal-period calculation. Right division in the meridian Ore ring over `K_geo((h))` gives Dhat=Q_geo (T-b_geo)+r_geo. Applying this to `Z_geo^chi` gives `r_geo Z_geo^chi=0`. This period is nonzero in its formal exponential line, so `r_geo=0`. Thus `T-b_geo` is a right factor of an operator constructed from actual partial arrays. Equivalently its cyclic module has a formal rank-one quotient on the marked geometric branch. It is not asserted to be a rational generic factor or a quotient of the minimal full scalar operator. The action of this line is the marked actual crossing regulator action: in the `h` convention its complete imaginary value is `Vol/2`, with the original peripheral and base-only lines retained. The existing formal Gaussian comparison transports it to the positive triangulation's marked regulator line by an algebraic formal unit. No convergence, rootwise value of that formal unit, or nonzero coefficient in the selected scalar period follows from this factor. In fact every nonzero moment operator obtained from a whole partial-array certificate by this procedure annihilates the same formal block. Their generated left ideal in the localized meridian Ore ring over `Q(q,M,Ahat,Bhat)` is nonzero. Every element annihilates both the actual partial arrays and the formal block. Its unique monic least-order generator consequently also has a geometric classical factor after taking its first nonzero `(q-1)` symbol. This defines a minimal **certified partial** operator; it is not asserted to equal the minimal annihilator of one selected scalar solution. Clear its coefficient denominators in a polynomial Ore combination before evaluating discrete frame labels; this retains identities also at labels where the localized formula itself has a pole. The full literature normalization is transported exactly, if desired. For the full partial array `N_N^chi=d_N(M)F_N^chi`, retain d_N(M)=i^(N+3)M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)), g_N(q,M)=d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =q^(N-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1) * (M^(2N)-1)/(q^(2N)M^(2N)-1). At the ACTUAL root q^N=-1 its meromorphic meridian-germ restriction is g_bar(q,M)=-q^(-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). The constructed full ROOT operator is the Ore gauge Dhat_full=Dhat|_(T -> g_bar^(-1) T). This notation means ordered Ore substitution, not commutative substitution of powers. Its all-level identity is a meromorphic whole MERIDIAN-germ identity ON THE ROOT FIBERS, with the complete displayed `d_N` retained. For a whole quantum-normal source use g_N, or its actual independent powers z=q^N,w=M^(2N), before specializing. The expression g_bar is only its root restriction; their q-normal derivatives are not identified. Equivalently, g_N=q^(-1)z (q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1) * (w-1)/(z^2 w-1). Here the actual meridian step sends w to z^2 w. It is not a constant dual-nome coordinate off the root. Also g_N has limit +1 at q=1 with N FIXED, whereas the root-character-specialized g_bar below has limit -1. These are different classical regimes; the root-symbol statement is not a claim that their fixed-N whole quantum-normal symbols agree. The [independent peripheral-shift audit](full_peripheral_shift_root_and_normal_audit.md) checks this full ratio, the ordered gauge direction and its retained-character normal discrepancy explicitly. At generic classical `M`, `g_bar->-1`, so its geometric factor is `A_geo(M,-L_full)` in the full shift convention. The regular completion at `M=1` uses the original source lattice and complete normalization germ; the separate pole of the localized `g_bar` is not evaluated there. ## 6. Scope of the result The proof applies to every knot for which the audited regular geometric critical chart and Hessian-radical statement hold. In particular its braid complexity is unrestricted: it is not confined to two-bridge, twist, alternating, or a fixed bridge number. The geometric input and the retained SL2 sign cover are exactly those of the actual normal-period theorem; no literature asymptotic or creative-telescoping theorem is a premise. The finite partial state and its operator depend on the braid and the selected two flow coordinates. They have been constructed from the original coefficient model; no topological invariance of this two-index extension is asserted. Summing its remaining two indices with the original selected source requires further elimination. The geometric factor can be lost in that pushforward. The theorem does not identify the full scalar minimal quantum-A operator, the selected global geometric cycle, Kashaev's volume growth, or the value of any individually normalized compact product at a root. ## 7. A source-preserving Fourier partial family has the same geometric factor There is now a second actual partial family with a different and useful framing polarization. It requires the FULL four-port tensor, not only its double diagonal. Use the original first-cut rank-one source and Fourier-transform the second identity wire as in [the whole polarization construction](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md). At a primitive root put V_jb=Q^(jb), with V^(-1)_bj=Q^(-bj)/N, and T^V=(I tensor V)T(I tensor V^(-1)). Define the RAW partial family by Ftilde_N(M;a,j)=sum_c (T^V)_(c,j;a,j) =(1/N)sum_(b,nu,u) Q^(j nu) W_N(M;a,b,nu,u). (7.1) Here W_N is the original raw open coefficient on its integral flow coset, T_(a-nu,b+nu;a,b)=sum_u W_N, and u has m-1 internal chord coordinates. All four actual port bounds and every original phase/pivot/peripheral line remain in W_N. The Fourier factor 1/N in (7.1) is not the first-cut source normalization. The original selected scalar is exactly F_N(M)=(1/N)sum_(a,j) Ftilde_N(M;a,j). (7.2) Indeed the sum over j kills every nonzero offset nu in its actual range |nu|<N and restores the identity second closure. It does not replace the physical b sum by evaluation of a momentum function. Equivalently, partial trace on that wire is invariant under the whole invertible basis change. If its first cut were also made diagonal BEFORE this operation, charge conservation would force nu=0, and the resulting array would be independent of j. The sum over c in (7.1) is essential. The following assertions hold under the regular geometric input of this note. **Fourier partial support theorem.** There is a nonzero all-level meridian operator constructed from (7.1) by finite coefficient linear algebra and moment repair, whose first nonzero classical symbol contains the same marked geometric A-factor. On a dense geometric framing chart its nonzero normal block is parametrized by the original cut position and the second physical wave momentum. At the discrete-faithful complete point these are birational framing coordinates; no new quadratic framing cover is required. This does not assert a geometric factor after the final selected sum (7.2). Here is the certificate and specialization proof, including the distinction between root data and the whole q-normal source. First keep a,j external and b,nu,u internal. Their number is r_F=m+1. Removing both physical cuts leaves the same connected graph, so the integral tree particular flow makes W_N proper with linear finite support, exactly as in the two-cut proof. The added monomial Q^(j nu) is also proper: shifting nu multiplies it by the external character Q^j, and shifting any remaining flow has its stated rational coefficient. There is a nonempty strict cone: take all original transfers small and positive, the original positions near N/2, and the open offset nu in a sufficiently small two-sided interval about zero. The Fourier index j may independently range through a strict subinterval of its original head. The formula on the right of (7.1), with the same monomial Fourier kernel at generic q, is a convenient AUXILIARY whole coefficient lift. At every root it is the literal actual family. Its common factor 1/N can be kept as a source line or removed from a homogeneous coefficient certificate, since internal and meridian shifts fix it. The finite support-stratum count of Section 2 applies with r replaced by r_F and the second external character replaced by q^j, retaining its square-root mark when required. Thus a nonzero whole certificate with no internal multiplication characters exists. Strip its largest common q^N+1 power from the ENTIRE certificate before root evaluation. The least internal-shift moment then gives a nonzero meridian operator annihilating the actual root arrays (7.1), by the exact same zero-extended summation identity as Sections 2--3. This auxiliary lift is not identified with the actual generic-q inverse Fourier matrix. The source-preserving whole basis change uses the Vandermonde V(Q) and its Lagrange inverse, with their explicit connection and endpoint carries. Its inverse equals Q^(-bj)/N at the root but generally has different normal jets. Thus the argument proves an operator identity for the literal ALL-LEVEL ROOT partial family; it does not discard the source normal terms in the whole polarization theorem. All M-dependent identities at a fixed root still agree, since the two Fourier bases are independent of M. The geometric normal block comes from the macroscopic open coefficient phase, rather than extrapolating a bounded-band Taylor formula to offsets of order N. Put t=H nu, v=Hj. Its phase is Phi=S_open(a,b,t,u)+v t. (7.3) On the original geometric critical manifold t=0, the old internal equations hold and partial_t S_open=Log p_e, in the actual balanced boundary frame. Therefore (7.3) is stationary precisely on the selected geometric germ with v=-Log p_e, eta=exp(v)=p_e^(-1). The original cut position together with p_e is etale on a nonempty geometric open chart. The bordered-Hessian proof in [the Fourier normal-block theorem](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md) then gives a nondegenerate (m+1)-dimensional internal Hessian. Its mixed entry along the old fixed-cut framing tangent is the nonzero derivative of Log p_e. The added Fourier pair has its literal factor 1/N and supplies no new exponential action. The geometric critical value is still S_geo, since t=0. The auxiliary coefficient realization has the same exact proper ratios and full marked formal phase (7.3). It consequently has a nonzero formal Gaussian block. Translate its internal variables in the whole certificate and extract the least weighted moment as in Section 4. The operator obtained from the finite root arrays annihilates that SAME normal block. Section 5 now applies: its first nonzero classical symbol vanishes at the marked geometric longitude and has the geometric A-factor. The formal Ore right-factor statement follows by the same division argument. The original peripheral dimension line is transported using the ordered Ore gauge already displayed above. Its separate whole normal adapter is not replaced by a root norm in this proof. Nor is the sum over j interpreted as the old cap point eta=0: the correct new source is the finite j sum in (7.2), with every tail/carry retained on inserted currents. Survival and the volume norm after that last sourced pushforward remain unproved. ## 8. The original root period has a one-exterior-index Fourier presentation One of the two exterior sums can be removed EXACTLY, without replacing the first-cut source by a double diagonal. The [fixed-column/Ward theorem](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) proves that the fully reclosed one-cut word C_N(M) is scalar on the actual root family. This follows directly from its true K,F intertwining: K has distinct eigenvalues and F connects all successive head basis vectors with nonzero coefficients. Hence every first column sum is the same selected scalar. In the RAW Fourier presentation above, sum_j Ftilde_N(M;a,j)=sum_c(C_N(M))_(c,a)=F_N(M) for EVERY a in [0,N-1]. (8.1) The full peripheral factor, if present, multiplies both sides as its original line. Equation (8.1) keeps the sum over c in (7.1). Replacing it by c=a before Fourier polarization would destroy the momentum coordinate and is a different operation. This statement also has a controlled WHOLE source defect. The whole actual balanced K,F Ward contraction gives h delta C=C-I Tr(C)/N, delta C=((Ad K-I)C, F C-K^(-1)C K F). If lambda_a(C)=sum_c C_(c,a) and Phi is the original rank-one average, then (lambda_a-Phi)(I)=0 and therefore lambda_a-Phi=(lambda_a-Phi) h delta. (8.2) Its primitive and the original source adapters are explicit in the fixed-column theorem. Thus (8.1) is not extended to an arbitrary off-root lift by setting its Ward defects to zero. The actual whole normal derivatives act on every term of (8.2). There is a uniform way to fix a good interior sequence of first input indices while retaining the geometric normal block. The bad first-position fibers of its nonempty algebraic open chart form a FINITE set: after writing its finitely many shape/Jacobian units as rational functions of the first position and momentum, an entire fiber can fail only at a common zero of their nonzero coefficient functions. Also exclude the finitely many first half-phases where the already constructed operator's nonzero leading symbol becomes identically zero in M, the second exterior character and L. Clearing the specified denominators first makes this an ordinary polynomial coefficient test. Choose a rational theta=k/d in (0,1) such that A_*=exp(2pi*i*k/d), alpha_*=exp(pi*i*k/d), avoid these finite bad sets, including A=1. Such a choice exists because these algebraic phases are infinite. Put a_N=floor(kN/d), r_N=kN modulo d. At the original root its physical and half clocks are EXACTLY A_N=A_* q_N^(-2r_N/d), Ahat_N=alpha_* q_N^(-r_N/d). (8.3) These indices are in the strict interior for all sufficiently large N. For each fixed residue class r_N=r the right side is one fixed algebraic q germ on a marked d-th-root cover, and it tends to the chosen good geometric framing phase. The same nondegenerate normal block therefore persists there, with its original geometric action. Substitute Ahat=alpha_* q^(-r/d) in the operator of Section 7, after its stated coefficient localization. This is an Ore homomorphism because the meridian shift fixes q and both exterior frame characters. By the choice of alpha_* its first nonzero classical symbol stays nonzero and still has the SAME geometric A-factor. On N residue class r the specialized operator annihilates the actual one-index partial family G_(N,r)(M;j)=Ftilde_N(M;a_N,j), F_N(M)=sum_j G_(N,r)(M;j). (8.4) Its formal geometric line is now over the marked geometric representation field and ONE momentum coordinate. No restriction to a knot family or bridge number has been introduced. The values G_(N,r) still contain the original bulk finite contractions; this is one exterior source index, not an asserted closed single-product formula for the knot invariant. For a WHOLE quantum-normal source calculation, (8.3) must not freeze the underlying power coordinates. Before root restriction, the actual fixed-N clocks are A_N=(Q^N)^(k/d) Q^(-r/d), Ahat_N=(q^N)^(k/d) q^(-r/d), (8.5) with the logarithmic/finite-cover marks Log(Q^N)=N Log Q and Log(q^N)=N Log q. Their root values give (8.3), but their normal derivatives retain the N terms. The operators in (8.4) are certified ALL-LEVEL ROOT operators, as in Section 7; no whole q-normal identification is inferred from (8.3). If one wants a single operator across these finitely many residue classes, take a common LEFT multiple of their nonzero specialized operators in the localized meridian Ore ring and then clear the original denominators. A naive ordered product is not justified. The per-residue statement (8.4) already suffices for the present source reduction. It still does not prove that the final one-index sum retains its geometric block with the regulator norm. That is the remaining selected-period theorem. The [actual Fourier current theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) now provides a rigorous scope test for this last step. The literal second-port Cartan current has zero whole second partial trace, yet on the good-A chart its formal geometric block is a nonzero derivative of the block above with the SAME action. Its own partial certificate still has a geometric classical factor, while its selected scalar is identically zero. Thus a geometric partial factor is not a certificate of survival under the last source. The final theorem must control the actual class in the cyclic source/current quotient, including the polar and normal data.

title: The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period
text: # The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period Research note, 26 October 2026. This identifies a boundary component which any positive-volume proof must retain. The ordinary principal-root colors force polynomial growth if a polynomial annihilator acts nontrivially on the complete-color delta vector. When that boundary component is retained, a simple rank condition expresses the actual complete period as the first normal derivative of a homogeneous kernel line. The derivative has a polynomially bounded source. Its size is therefore an inverse-operator and source-coupling problem, in the natural cyclic trace metric. The statements below separate a necessary boundary factor from a further rank condition. The positive volume limit is now proved for the knots of the [net-twist theorem](actual_conway_net_twist_volume.md). For every such knot, Section 2 therefore proves the boundary-factor condition for every polynomial all-level annihilator. The special-fiber rank condition in Section 4 remains additional; the scalar volume theorem does not prove it or identify a full quantum module with the geometric regulator. The subsequent [actual Weyl-descent proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) constructs P=B*(Y-1) from the primitive minimal normal operator for every knot and proves its unitary reciprocity. Thus those symmetry data in Section 6 are available for the canonical actual operator. Those symmetry statements do not prove special-fiber injectivity or give direct estimates for the inverse below. Section 2's necessity test still concerns every polynomial annihilator. The subsequent [peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives the regular normal boundary lattice from the actual fundamental parallel, retaining its pole before changing lattice. Its odd normal state w_N=(M-M^(-1))F_N has K_N=(1/2)partial_(Log M)w_N at M=1. The adjacent-color splitting there has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue whose pivotal partial trace is identity. These exact quantum extension data do not establish the root-fiber rank or the regulator norm. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre theorem](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) retains this derivative as an ordinary coordinate of a descended algebraic fibre over s=((U-1)/(U+1))^2. Its - sector generator is z e_- rather than a vector discarded by setting z=0 first. The source equation and complete functional then hold in that fibre, with their original rank qualifications. An explicit dimension formula gives signatures for which negative-sector injectivity cannot hold; saturated kernels and further lifting data remain available. No regulator norm is inferred from this descent. ## 1. Fixed state, ring, and principal-root bound Use the actual literature state in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), with q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(Y) Laurent polynomial, K_N=F_N(1)=<K>_N, F_N(Q_N^r)=C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N. The [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) reconstructs the positive path trace directly from the actual fundamental crossing. For any fixed b-strand knot braid it proves |C_r(q_N)|<=D_N=sin(pi/N)^(1-b)<= (N/2)^(b-1). (1.1) Take a specified actual annihilator with denominators cleared and recorded, in the polynomial quantum torus R=C(q)[Y^(+/-1),T^(+/-1); T Y=q^2Y T], P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(q,Y)T^j, a_j in C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. (1.2) An initial power of T permits the nonnegative shift convention. The [existence](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) theorems supply such an actual operator, but do not yet identify its classical geometric factors. ## 2. A nonzero complete column forces polynomial growth For 0<=i<=d put r_i(q)=a_i(q,q^(-2i)). (2.1) If r_i is not identically zero, it has finite vanishing order nu_i at q=1. For all large N, |r_i(q_N)|>=c_i N^(-nu_i). Evaluate the actual equation at Y=Q_N^(-i). Its i-th term is r_i(q_N)K_N. If N>d, every other term uses a noncomplete orbit color, and hence has modulus at most C_P D_N by (1.1). The fixed Laurent coefficients are bounded on the unit torus. Consequently |K_N|<=C N^(b-1+nu_i). (2.2) Thus a positive exponential volume rate requires a_i(q,q^(-2i))=0 for every i. (2.3) Equivalently every coefficient is divisible in the Laurent ring by q^(2i)Y-1. Polynomial division at its nonzero root proves this equivalence. Hence the required factorization is exactly P=B*(Y-1), B in R with Laurent coefficients. (2.4) This is right multiplication: its i-th coefficient is b_i(q,Y)*(q^(2i)Y-1). A monic operator over C(q,Y) can have poles on those divisors; an ordinary evaluation of that localized operator cannot replace the cleared equation used above. The result is a dichotomy for an arbitrary knot. For the knots covered by the strict-tree and net-twist volume theorems, their positive volume limit rules out (2.2), so every polynomial annihilator satisfies (2.3). For a hyperbolic knot outside the proved class, this remains a necessary condition for its conjectured positive-volume limit. Conversely, the boundary factor alone supplies no exponential lower bound. The [nearby-zero theorem](actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) gives another consequence of the same ordinary-color values: zeros of the actual reduced state approach the complete meridian at distance $O(1/N)$. Its final section also records the two-sign version of the boundary factor for operators in the unsquared coordinate $M$. ## 3. The missing component is a fixed boundary module At generic q define Delta=R/R*(Y-1), delta=class of 1. It has C(q)-basis T^j delta, j in Z, and Y T^j delta=q^(-2j)T^j delta. Therefore P delta=0 is exactly (2.3). The module is simple at indeterminate q: polynomial interpolation in Y isolates one term of any nonzero finite combination of these distinct eigenvectors, and powers of T then generate all of them. Every vector is killed by a nonzero polynomial in Y. Localizing the meridian to C(q,Y) therefore kills Delta completely. For a polynomial annihilator ideal I, positive exponential growth would imply I is contained in R*(Y-1). Its cyclic module would have Delta as a quotient. For one specified P satisfying (2.4), this quotient already follows without a volume assumption. The generic norm torsor over C(q,Y) needs a meridian lattice to retain this boundary datum. At the actual root, impose T^N=1 as well. The resulting Delta_N is the N-dimensional clock-and-shift module with Y^N=T^N=1, at every parity and composite level. It is irreducible because the N distinct Y-eigenvalues and their cyclic shift generate all matrix units. On functions of the root orbit the complete delta vector is e_0=(1,0,...,0), e_0(Y)=S_N(Y)/N modulo Y^N-1. Thus P annihilates this vector on the central fiber when (2.4) holds. If c_N=(0,C_1,...,C_(N-1)), the actual state there is F_bar_N=c_N+K_N e_0. (3.1) Every vector in this affine line satisfies the same special operator equation and has the same ordinary-color pointing. The complete coefficient is fixed by extension away from the central fiber. This affine ambiguity is not permission to change the actual state. At q=1, (2.4) also gives the vertical factor Y-1 in the classical polynomial symbol. Removing vertical factors to state an A-curve equation discards this specific boundary-module datum. The marked integral/meridian extension must therefore accompany that curve. ## 4. The actual full period is a normal derivative Assume (2.4) for the specified operator. Work near U=Y^N=1, with t=U-1 and the fixed root germs Y_r(t)=Q_N^r*(1+t)^(1/N), 0<=r<N. Represent B by the cyclic matrix B_N(t): its row r, column r+j modulo N receives b_j(q_N,Y_r(t)). Write B_N(t)=B_0+t B_1+O(t^2), (B_1)_(r,r+j)=(1/N)(Y*d/dY)b_j(q_N,Q_N^r). (4.1) Retain the full vector of the actual state and put v_N(t)_r=(Y_r(t)-1)F_N(Y_r(t)), v_N(t)=v_0+t v_1+O(t^2). Since P F_N=0, B_N(t)v_N(t)=0. At the special fiber, (v_0)_0=0, (v_0)_r=(Q_N^r-1)C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N, B_0 v_0=0, B_0 v_1=-B_1 v_0, (v_1)_0=K_N/N. (4.2) The last identity keeps the zero of Y-1 until differentiation: Y_0'(0)=1/N. In particular the complete full ADO value is exactly N_N(1)=eta_N (v_1)_0, eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.3) Indeed the full state, before specialization, is N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)*(Y-1)F_N(Y)/(U-1). Its poles, its sign character, and its phase have all been retained. The normal derivative realizes their cancelled whole germ. Suppose now that rank B_0=N-1. (4.4) The known nonzero vector v_0 spans its kernel; the reference component is Q_N-1 because C_1=1. The solutions of the inhomogeneous normal equation in (4.2) form a genuine affine torsor under C*v_0. Since (v_0)_0=0, its complete-coordinate functional is constant. Thus (4.2) determines K_N exactly, without choosing the derivative of a central normalization unit. More explicitly replacing v_N(t) by c(1+t)v_N(t), c(1)=1, adds c'(1)v_0 to v_1. The complete value in (4.3) does not change. This is the anchored normal-period comparison, with its specified root germs. The rank condition is additional to the existence of the actual operator; it is not assumed for every knot. The regular complete scalar of the preceding note is R_N(1)=(v_1)_0-p_N(1), |p_N(1)|<=D_N. (4.5) So the normal derivative and that regularized field-trace period give the same positive-volume target. ## 5. The first obstruction selects a point of the delta torsor Let D(t)=diag(Y_r(t)-1), so P_N(t)=B_N(t)D(t). At zero, Im D(0) is the hyperplane of vectors with zero complete coordinate. Its kernel is C*e_0. Since ker B_0=C*v_0 is inside this hyperplane, rank P_0=N-2, ker P_0=span(e_0,c_N). (5.1) The first lifting obstruction is the linear map kappa:ker P_0 -> coker P_0, x -> [P_1 x]. (5.2) This is the usual first Bockstein: a lift x+t x_1 solves the equation through first order exactly when P_0 x_1+P_1 x=0. In particular P_1 e_0=(1/N)B_0 e_0. This is not in Im P_0. Otherwise e_0 would differ from a vector in Im D(0) by a member of ker B_0, also in Im D(0), a contradiction. The actual vector c_N+K_N e_0 lifts. Hence kappa has rank one on the two-dimensional kernel, and its kernel selects that exact line. Choose any left null vector ell of P_0 with ell P_1 e_0 nonzero. The period is the exact ratio K_N=-ell P_1 c_N/(ell P_1 e_0). (5.3) Changing ell subject to this condition gives the same answer, because the actual lift exists. This derivative pairing records the boundary extension that the ordinary special kernel omits. Under (4.4) the rank loss in P is exactly one simple Smith factor; no unverified higher-order lift is being used. More singular cases need the higher jets retained in the [bounded-jet construction](bounded_meridian_jets.md). ## 6. A bounded source and the exact inverse-matrix period Use the Hermitian norm on the orbit coming from the cyclic trace; the unnormalized Euclidean version differs only by the common factor N^(1/2). The fixed Laurent coefficients give ||B_1||<=C_B/N, ||v_0||<=2D_N*sqrt(N). (6.1) For the first inequality write B_1 as a finite sum of diagonal coefficient matrices times unitary cyclic shifts, and bound each Y-derivative on the unit torus. Thus the normal equation has a polynomially bounded, explicitly specified source. Let B_0^+ be the Moore--Penrose inverse. Since e_0 is perpendicular to ker B_0, every solution of (4.2) has the same complete coordinate, and exactly K_N=-N*e_0^* B_0^+ B_1 v_0. (6.2) If s_N is the smallest nonzero singular value of B_0, then |K_N|<=2 C_B D_N sqrt(N)/s_N. (6.3) Consequently positive volume growth would force an exponentially large inverse norm in this specified boundary problem. The source itself cannot supply that positive exponent. Small singular values alone are insufficient: (6.2) also retains the source and the complete-coordinate pairing. In a singular-vector decomposition it is the sum of their two overlaps divided by the corresponding singular values. No largest-eigenvalue prescription is being used. The geometric action already has imaginary value Vol at completeness, by the [actual action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). For a knot covered by the net-twist theorem, whenever the stated rank condition holds, (6.2) is an exact expression for its invariant and therefore has the scalar volume growth proved there. Deriving this growth directly from the inverse and identifying the geometric regulator at the module level remain additional tasks. Neither (6.3) nor a geometric critical point by itself controls the two overlaps. Extra left operator factors can create small singular values with zero relevant overlap. ### A Weyl symmetry isolates the relevant inverse There is a stronger reduction when the *actual operator* has a checked reciprocity. Write R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), Q=q^2, and suppose J=-Y R, J'=c(q,Y)T^d R, B J=J' B, c(q,Y)c(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))=1, |c(q,Y)|=1 on the unit torus. (6.4) Both give unitary involutions on the root orbit; B_0 intertwines them. Their -1 eigenspaces are orthogonal to the +1 eigenspaces, and e_0 has J-eigenvalue -1. The factor Y-1 is the squared-meridian form of the Weyl denominator, up to the retained monomial M. If J v_0=v_0, differentiating the operator identity at U=1 proves J' B_1 v_0=-B_1 v_0. Explicitly inversion sends t to -t+O(t^2), and the domain involution has derivative J/N. Applying the differentiated identity to v_0 kills the terms containing B_0 v_0 and leaves exactly this source parity. Thus only the -1 symmetry sector enters the complete normal period. Under (4.4) this source parity is automatic whenever K_N is nonzero. Indeed the one-dimensional kernel makes J v_0=epsilon*v_0. If epsilon=-1, the same differentiation gives source parity +1. The -1 part of v_1 would then be a multiple of v_0 and have zero complete coordinate, forcing K_N=0. More generally (4.4) can be weakened in this symmetry setting: it suffices that J v_0=v_0 and B_0 is injective on the -1 domain. The actual derivative places the source in its image. Extra +1 kernel vectors do not affect the value. Writing the restricted Moore--Penrose inverse as B_-^+, the exact period is K_N=-N e_0^* B_-^+ B_1 v_0. (6.5) It is this inverse and its specified source that need a regulator norm theorem. Small singular values in the other symmetry sector make no contribution. Reciprocity is additional quantum data; it is not assumed merely from the classical A-curve's inversion symmetry. The subsequent [actual-state proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) now derives this reciprocity for the primitive minimal normal operator of every knot, and also proves J v_0=v_0 directly. An arbitrary nonprimitive or left-multiplied operator still needs its own checked intertwiner and lattice. There is an explicit Hilbert-90 descent of the reflected kernel frame. If its generic rational kernel is a C(U)-line, reciprocity gives J v=gamma(U)v, gamma(U)gamma(U^(-1))=1. When J v_0=v_0, gamma is a unit at U=1 with gamma(1)=1. Set g(U)=(1+gamma(U))/2. Direct division gives g(U)/g(U^(-1))=gamma(U). Thus g*v is J-invariant and g(1)=1. This is an explicit frame change of the same pointed line, not a replacement knot state. Its derivative adds g'(1)v_0 and leaves the complete normal period unchanged. Zeros or poles of this frame elsewhere remain part of the lattice data. This is quadratic Hilbert 90 on the central involution, after the normal pointing has already fixed the value at the branch point. The ambient cyclic orbit also retains a precise signed dihedral relation. Direct multiplication gives J T J=Q*T^(-1). With the actual ADO character kappa=-q^(-1), put T_tilde=kappa*T. Then J T_tilde J=T_tilde^(-1), T_tilde^N=kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1). (6.6) Thus the uniform half-root lambda=-q, lambda^2=Q, is compatible with the Weyl action and with the full even-level sign. This is an action on the ambient orbit module. It does not assert that the scalar operator's rational solution line is stable under T; only its checked reflection intertwiner and central frame descent are used. Neither Hilbert-90 descent nor this finite symmetry supplies the missing regulator norm. ## 7. A fixed initial form bounds the rational root period rank There is a simple separate certificate for generic rational rank. For any Laurent polynomial operator L, let r be the least Y-exponent in its coefficients and define I_0(q,z)=sum_j [Y^r]a_j(q,Y)*z^j. (7.1) At q_N, suppose this initial form is nonzero. On E=C(Y) over C(U), U=Y^N, represent Y^(-r)L in the monomial basis 1,Y,...,Y^(N-1). Its matrix is integral over C[U]. Modulo U it is lower triangular: positive powers of Y either increase the basis exponent or wrap with a positive power of U. Its diagonal entries are I_0(q_N,Q_N^k). The principal submatrix on their nonzero indices has nonzero determinant. Therefore dim_(C(U)) ker L <=#{0<=k<N : I_0(q_N,Q_N^k)=0}. (7.2) This counts distinct lattice roots, not their multiplicities. If I_0=g(q)*z^a*(z-q^(2s))^m, with g(q_N) nonzero and m>=1, the bound is one at every such level. Any known nonzero rational period then proves generic rank one. The same applies at infinity. This is a condition on the actual quantum initial form, not on the commutative A-polynomial alone. Terms vanishing at q=1 can change the extremal Y-coefficient. The bound certifies the generic line used in Hilbert 90. It does not replace (4.4), which concerns its special fiber and the normal derivative. A rational kernel line may acquire extra special solutions; that possibility is exactly what the lattice retains. The subsequent [torsion initial-rank theorem](torsion_initial_rank.md) extends the pure-binomial test: rational-coefficient initial forms have only finitely many isolated torsion-grid exceptions outside their contained binomial torsion curves. Their eventual root count is given by finite periodic congruences. A single occupied curve therefore gives generic rank one even in the presence of non-toric initial factors. The proof keeps the q half-root and provides an explicit exceptional-level bound. It does not establish the special negative-sector injectivity or regulator norm. ## 8. The rank hypothesis cannot be suppressed For a manufactured root family let F_N(Y)=1+a_N S_N(Y), B=(T-1)(T-Q), P=B*(Y-1). Then P F_N=0 because (Y-1)F_N=Y-1+a_N(U-1), and B kills 1,Y. All ordinary orbit values are one, while K_N=1+N*a_N is arbitrary. Here B_0 has a two-dimensional kernel. Its complete-coordinate functional does not vanish on that kernel, so the first normal equation leaves this freedom. The quantum initial form also has two distinct lattice roots, consistent with (7.2). These are not knot states. In particular choosing a_N to change the complete value violates the coherent all-level color data, whose recovery is proved in [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md). The example only explains the rank requirement for the simpler normal equation (6.2), not a new ambiguity in the actual invariant. ## 9. Independent operator and actual-state calibration The audit derives a telescoping operator for the finite block H_N(Y)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) t_k(Y), t_k=product_(r=1)^k(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^r-Q^(-r)). The subsequent [whole-source four-plat proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) identifies H_N with the actual figure-eight ADO state at every level, with all peripheral factors retained. The derivation here does not take that equality as a premise. Put Z=Q^k and C(Y,Z)=(Y-1)^2 Z/((Y-Z)(1-YZ)), D(Y)=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1), g=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2, c_-=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1), c_0=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g, c_+=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). The finite products give the two Y-shift ratios and the k-ratio directly. Substitution proves the exact rational certificate sum_(j=-1)^1 c_j(Y)*t_k(Q^jY)/t_k(Y) =D(Y)*(C(Y,QZ)*t_(k+1)/t_k-C(Y,Z)). (9.1) At a root Q^N=1, C(Y,1)=-1 and t_N=Y^N+Y^(-N)-2. Telescoping therefore gives (c_-T^(-1)+c_0+c_+T)H_N =D(Y)*(3-U-U^(-1)). (9.2) The central factor is retained. Applying D(Y)T-D(QY) kills the source. Left multiplication by T removes the negative shift. The common coefficient factor removed in the audit is exactly Q^3Y(Q^3Y^2-1)^2, recorded before any specialization. The resulting polynomial P has every boundary column factor, initial form z(Q-z), and classical symbol (Y-1)^2(Y+1)^2*(z-1)*Y^2*A_geo(Y,z), A_geo=z^2-(Y^2-Y-2-Y^(-1)+Y^(-2))*z+1. (9.3) This checks the familiar geometric peripheral polynomial and the additional boundary factors in fixed conventions. It does not prove an AJ theorem for arbitrary knot operators or identify root central curves with A_geo. For this calibrated operator the exact reciprocity in (6.4) is c(Q,Y)=-Q^12 Y^8 and d=3. Substituting its coefficients verifies -Q^j Y b_j(Y)=c(Q,Y)b_(3-j)(Q^(-3)/Y). The two involution and unit-norm identities follow by multiplication. The -1 domain has dimension ceil(N/2), including every parity. The audit verifies the source parity and recovers the same period using only that folded inverse. This removes an irrelevant symmetry sector before any asymptotic estimate; it is not such an estimate. [The audit](../experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py) verifies the certificate symbolically. At levels 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10 it proves coefficientwise equality of H_N with independently computed actual figure-eight cut Laurent polynomials over the stated finite fields, and verifies their annihilation. At eleven levels through 18 it checks both matrix ranks, the derivative product rule, and exact recovery of the complete block period by (4.2), (5.2), and the Weyl-folded inverse (6.5). It also checks 50 initial-root dimension examples and six explicit rank- ambiguity examples. All checks passed. The larger block tests do not extend the actual-state comparison beyond its stated levels. That all-level comparison is now supplied by the independent four-plat proof, which also proves the selected volume limit and leading coefficient for the actual figure-eight invariant. Results are in [the output](../experiments/peripheral_normal_period_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py The boundary delta module, first lifting obstruction, Moore--Penrose inverse and initial-form argument use standard module and linear algebra. Their proofs above specify their role in the actual marked period; no novelty claim or imported analytic theorem is made. The quantum-torus Weyl involution already has explicit coverage in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). Only its scope is used for coverage; no AJ, state-comparison or analytic conclusion from that source is a premise. The weighted involutions and source parity above were obtained by direct operator identities, with all monomial phases retained. The [geometric triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) supplies the marked Bloch action for the comparison with this normal period. The scalar volume equality is established for the stated strict and net-twist knot classes. The survival and identification of the actual geometric factor, the additional rank conditions in this note, and the volume conjecture outside the established classes remain open.

title: Exact peripheral phase, state recovery, and move covariance
text: # Exact peripheral phase, state recovery, and move covariance Research note, 25 October 2026. Definitions are the charged operators in Andersen–Kashaev [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), equation (18), its real level in equation (4), and the state integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2). This note reconstructs the *complex* identities, including the phases that their magnitude formulas do not specify. It does not infer a state equality from equality of absolute values. The positive local kernel and its proper contractions are independently proved in `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`. The complete geometric saddle and annihilator statements remain those of the previous notes. The new results here are an exact tensor-to-fiber formula, uniqueness of the fiber state from that normalized tensor function, and an affine phase criterion for transporting it under the audited positive moves. ## 1. Data and conventions Write b>0 for the quantum parameter, Q=b+b^(-1), h=Q^(-2), c_b=iQ/2. The letter Q here is not the peripheral multiplication operator; that operator will be denoted mathsf-Q in Section 6. For tetrahedron j let its physical angles a_j,b_j,c_j be in radians and sum to pi. Its sign is epsilon_j. Put d=pi 1-a, C=diag(epsilon)c, delta_j=(epsilon_j+1)/2, N_+=sum_j delta_j, H=Q_f-diag(delta)/2, G=-2H. The face matrix script-A is invertible and gives the kinematical Gaussian Q_f. For the chosen longitude use the certified matrices A,B with B^(-1)A=G, p=2B^(-1)e_N, c_0=B^(-1)nu-G pi 1. On the balanced angle space its exact linear identity is W:=2Q_f d-C=c_0+(lambda/2)p, (1.1) where lambda is the angular holonomy of the chosen longitude. This follows from the actual edge/longitude angle equations, with their branch constants. It is also checked on the entire affine angle spaces in the accompanying script, rather than only at one complete structure. Fix the rational lift gamma in x=p^T y-i pi gamma, mu=p^T d-pi gamma. (1.2) The fiber contour then has Im x=mu. When mu is called a meridian holonomy, the corresponding normal-curve/peripheral certificate is required. For the twist families it is supplied by `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md`; gamma=0, mu=a_U-a_V, reversing the source's meridian orientation in the even case. For other data (1.2) alone defines a spectral coordinate, not a topological identification of a meridian. Choose p_1!=0 by relabeling. Let J_print be the literal printed integral, including its factor p_1/det(script-A), and put J_or=J_print/p_1^2, sigma_X=sign(det(script-A) p_1). (1.3) Thus J_or uses the oriented coarea fiber form. The sign sigma_X converts it to the positive Lebesgue disintegration of the full integral. It cannot be inferred from a formula for its modulus. ## 2. Charged kernel versus the phase-free dynamical convention For a positive tetrahedron, set its AK charges to a/(2pi),c/(2pi). The Fourier identity proved in the pentagon note gives its charged kernel as the phase-free dynamical factor times u(a,c;b)=exp[-pi i/12+i k(a,c)/h], k(a,c)=a c/(4pi)+(a-c)/12-pi/24. (2.1) Indeed its Fourier factor is exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c/(2pi),b_angle/(2pi)). Insert the defining psi and use a+b_angle+c=pi. The remaining x-dependent factor is exactly exp(Q c s)/Phi_b(s-iQ(pi-a)/(2pi)). For a negative tetrahedron take the adjoint and change spectral variable t=epsilon s. Its phase is u^(-1), and its remaining dynamical factor is exactly the negative factor in the FAMED definition. No sign Jacobian appears for Lebesgue integration on the real line. Let Z_AK be the contraction of the specified charged kernels and Z_D the FAMED convention with its phase-free dynamical factors. Then exactly Z_AK=U_X Z_D, U_X=exp[-pi i sum(epsilon)/12 +i sum_j epsilon_j k(a_j,c_j)/h]. (2.2) This uses the existing charged-operator definition. In the original v2 Theorem 4, formula (5) contains an alpha_3 even though the immediately following indexing only defines alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2. We avoid resolving that printed indexing by guesswork: equation (18) and its Fourier kernel fix (2.1) unambiguously. Its scalar agrees algebraically with the displayed varphi_T when alpha_0=a/pi, alpha_2=c/pi. No claim about the final journal version is made from this version-specific observation. ## 3. The exact tensor-to-fiber identity The phase-free contraction has the absolutely convergent spectral form Z_D=1/|det(script-A)| integral_R^N exp(2pi i t^T Q_f t) product_j exp(Q epsilon_j c_j t_j) Phi_b(epsilon_j(t_j-iQd_j/(2pi)))^(-epsilon_j) dt. Set u=-t+iQd/(2pi), y=2pi u/Q, with left-to-right Lebesgue contour orientations. The inversion identity Phi(z)Phi(-z)=zeta exp(pi i z^2), where zeta=exp[pi i(Q^2-2)/12], gives Z_D=zeta^(-N_+) exp[i Theta_X/(2pi h)] (Q/(2pi))^N/|det(script-A)| integral_(Y_alpha) exp[(i y^T H y+W^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(Q y_j/(2pi)) dy, Theta_X=C^T d-d^T Q_f d. (3.1) This is an affine substitution, not a deformation across a pole. In particular the constant terms have h, not sqrt(h), in their denominator. It follows by expanding 2pi i(-u+iQd/(2pi))^T Q_f(-u+iQd/(2pi)) and Q C^T(-u+iQd/(2pi)). The mixed-sign generic expansion is checked symbolically in the script. Disintegrate y into x and its fiber, using (1.1)–(1.3). The imaginary lift in (1.2) contributes exp(i gamma lambda/(4h)). Combining (2.2), (3.1), and the coarea Jacobian gives the exact result Z_AK(X,alpha;b) =sigma_X exp[pi i N/12+i K_X(alpha)/h] integral_(R+i mu) J_or(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) dx, (3.2) where K_X(alpha)=sum_j epsilon_j k(a_j,c_j)-pi N_+/12 +Theta_X/(2pi)+gamma lambda/4. (3.3) The b-independent constant pi N/12 results from combining the inversion constant and the charged normalization; it is not an unspecified projective scalar. All entries of K_X are explicit real angle polynomials. For real angles,b, the multiplier in (3.2) has modulus one, but it matters in state recovery and quantum-operator comparison. The level in the *existing* AK definition acts by F_b(X,ell)=exp(pi i ell/(4h))Z_AK(X). Consequently the explicit b-independent allowed choice ell=-4K_X(alpha)/pi gives sigma_X exp(-pi i N/12)F_b(X,-4K_X(alpha)/pi) =integral J_or(h,x)exp(lambda x/(4pi h))dx. (3.4) This identifies the fixed fiber integral with a particular realization of the published leveled tensor state. It is a choice of level, not yet a claim that this level choice is preserved by every triangulation change. ## 4. Existence, contour independence, and uniqueness of the fiber state These points can be proved directly for positive proper FAMED data. The dynamical factors in Section 3 decrease exponentially at both real ends. Thus the original spectral integrand is bounded in modulus by C exp(-c sum_j |t_j|), with c>0. On compact subsets of the positive angle space the bound is uniform. Under the substitution in Section 3 this is a corresponding bound for the weighted full y integrand. Its Phi poles have imaginary coordinate at least pi in the y variable: the first pole is 2pi c_b/Q=i pi. Hence the product numerator is holomorphic throughout the box 0<Im y_j<pi. On a fiber the extra longitude factor is constant in the internal variables. The preceding exponential bound therefore proves absolute convergence of J_or and local holomorphy in x. The real map (y_1,...,y_N)->(x,y_2,...,y_N) is invertible, so the same bound also gives exponential decrease of J_or(x)exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) on the horizontal x contour. Positive angle structures form a convex open subset of an affine space. Two choices with the same mu can be joined inside it. Their fiber contours have the same x and remain in the pole-free box. Along a compact part of this segment the tail estimate stays uniform, including when lambda varies: its factor is constant along each fiber. Cauchy's theorem with vanishing side faces therefore identifies the fiber integrals. The image of the positive angle space in (mu,lambda) has an open interior. One way to certify this is to parameterize its affine equations by a and lambda: B invertible determines the z'' angles uniquely from A a+B angle(z'')=nu+lambda e_N, and the other angles follow by their tetrahedron sums. All remaining edge equations must be included or their redundancy certified. With p!=0, mu=p^T(pi 1-a)-pi gamma and lambda have independent differentials. The twist script checks rank two directly. Thus J_or is holomorphic on the horizontal band of meridian values supplied by positive angles. For fixed mu and an interval I of compatible longitude values, its transform L_X(lambda)=integral_(R+i mu) J_or(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h))dx is holomorphic on the vertical strip Re lambda in I. Uniform exponential bounds on smaller strips justify differentiation. Varying the horizontal contour inside the compatible positive chamber does not change L_X. **Uniqueness.** Values of L_X on any real open subinterval of I determine J_or on its band. For two proposed states with the stated weighted decay, the identity theorem first gives equality on the vertical strip. On lambda=lambda_0+i tau the transform, after the explicit constant from Im x=mu is removed, is the ordinary Fourier transform of J_or(s+i mu)exp(lambda_0 s/(4pi h)). This is in L1. Fourier injectivity gives equality on that horizontal line, then holomorphy gives equality on the common band. In contrast, equality of the magnitudes of L_X supplies none of this uniqueness. ## 5. The balanced phase is affine up to one universal term Eliminating C from (3.3) by (1.1), and using a_j+b_j+c_j=pi, gives K_X(alpha)=L_X^angle(alpha)-lambda mu/(8pi) +gamma lambda/8, L_X^angle(alpha)=-pi N/24 +sum_j epsilon_j(c_j-b_j)/12-c_0^T(pi 1-a)/(4pi). (5.1) The superscript distinguishes the affine angle expression from the Fourier–Laplace transform L_X above. Equation (5.1) is an exact identity on the balanced angle space. Its only quadratic dependence is the universal meridian–longitude term. It is especially useful when comparing moves that preserve the same peripheral coordinates. For both twist families the script verifies (1.1) and (5.1) on their entire affine angle spaces for p=0,...,8. It checks the tangent Hessian, gradient and constant, so agreement at a single special angle is not the evidence. The proof of (5.1) is the displayed elimination for arbitrary N. The raw phase K_X varies even at fixed mu,lambda in every tested twist example; discarding it on account of its unit modulus would lose actual information. ## 6. Exact covariance under a certified positive move Suppose X,Y are proper positive FAMED realizations related by the audited operator-pentagon pattern or its adjoint, with compatible peripheral curves, coordinates and overlapping positive contour chambers. Write its tensor law as Z_AK(X,alpha)=exp(i rho(alpha)/h)Z_AK(Y,alpha'), where rho=-pi P/12 for the original pentagon and +pi P/12 for its adjoint. The map of angles is affine. The two scalar transforms obey exactly L_X(lambda)=eta exp(i D(alpha)/h)L_Y(lambda), eta=(sigma_Y/sigma_X)exp[pi i(N_Y-N_X)/12], D=K_Y(alpha')-K_X(alpha)+rho(alpha). (6.1) Because mu and lambda agree, the quadratic terms in (5.1) cancel. D is affine in the remaining angle variables. The transforms depend only on lambda. Where they are nonzero, varying angles at fixed lambda in (6.1) forces the continuous real function D to be constant on each such fiber. Hence, on the connected positive move chamber, D=d_0+d_1 lambda. (6.2) This is an affine linear-algebra statement, not an assumption that a quantum normalization vanishes. Nonzero transforms are guaranteed near the semiclassical regime when the previous positive geometric state theorem applies: the state is nonzero, so its transform cannot be identically zero by Section 4. Holomorphic continuation removes isolated transform zeros. For rational face/peripheral data, d_0 is in pi Q and d_1 is rational. Two generic angle evaluations, or coefficient comparison, determine them. If d_1=0, uniqueness immediately gives the exact state identity J_or,X(h,x)=eta exp(i d_0/h)J_or,Y(h,x). (6.3) Thus this finite phase certificate proves equality of the annihilator and of the volume rate for the *same selected state*, with every scalar retained. For the printed normalizations one must also multiply by p_(1,X)^2/p_(1,Y)^2. If d_1 is nonzero, (6.1) remains the exact transform relation; it must not be replaced by (6.3). Put a=4pi i d_1. When the relevant fiber band contains the required contour translation, inverse transformation gives J_or,X(h,x)=eta exp(i d_0/h)J_or,Y(h,x-a). (6.4) Without that strip/continuation check, (6.4) is not asserted. If it holds, an annihilator in the natural b-shift algebra transports by a coefficient substitution. Since mathsf-Q=exp[-(1+b^2)x], A_X(mathsf-Q,E)=A_Y(exp[(1+b^2)a]mathsf-Q,E), exp[(1+b^2)a]=exp(4pi i d_1)q^(2d_1), q=exp(2pi i b^2). The formula is in the finite root extension when required; descent to the prescribed coefficient field uses restriction of scalars as in the earlier annihilator note, and need not preserve the minimal order over that field. This retains the finite power of q and the root of unity in the meridian lift. The complete value cannot be substituted before this comparison. ### 6.1 Geometric endpoints force the affine slope to vanish There is a stronger conclusion when both endpoints have the positive complete geometric certificates of the volume theorem, with the boundary origins fixed by p^T y*=i pi gamma. Under the hypotheses of Section 6, d_1=0. (6.5) Here is a proof that does not assume state invariance. The normalized transform L_X is the full N-variable integral from (3.1), with its angle phase removed. At lambda=0 its leading potential is F_0, whose *full* gradient vanishes at the positive complete y*. This follows directly from the certified edge/longitude matrix identity and the complete logarithmic equations, just as in the earlier fiber saddle calculation. The same exact quantum remainder applies. With s=b^2, its b-dependent potential at a nearby longitude parameter is F_s(y,lambda)=i y^T H y+c_0^T y +(lambda/2)(p^T y-i pi gamma) -i/(1+s)^2 sum_j Li_2(-exp((1+s)y_j)). On the full real horizontal plane the real Hessian is -diag(Im sigmoid((1+s)y_j)), strictly negative for the positive strip. The full Hessian is invertible, so its critical point y_s tends to y*. Concavity gives the same quadratic-near/linear-far coercivity bound as in the fiber proof, now in N real directions. The exact remainder is uniformly bounded and tends to zero on a smaller strip. The nonzero Gaussian and the strict tail gap therefore prove L_X(h,0)!=0 for all sufficiently small b. Insert the linear moment x(y)=p^T y-i pi gamma. The same saddle argument applies: the additional polynomial factor is integrable against the coercive tails, and the ratio of the two Gaussian expansions tends to x(y*)=0. Differentiation under the convergent integral consequently gives lim_(b->0+) h L_X'(0)/L_X(0) =lim (1/(4pi)) integral x(y)I_b(y)dy / integral I_b(y)dy =0. (6.6) All constant measure factors cancel in this ratio. The same result holds for Y. Differentiate the exact relation (6.1)–(6.2): h [L_X'(0)/L_X(0)-L_Y'(0)/L_Y(0)]=i d_1. Taking the limit proves (6.5), since d_1 is independent of b. This proves that the translation alternative in (6.4) cannot occur for these compatible geometric endpoints with their complete origins fixed. It was necessary to retain that alternative before this argument, rather than cancel it at the ideal point by convention. The argument also applies to a finite certified path of proper positive moves. Compose its exact tensor laws first. The endpoint K polynomials cancel their common quadratic peripheral term, while the sum of local pentagon phases is affine in the path's angle variables. The transform uniqueness argument again gives d_0+d_1 lambda. Its identity, initially on the path's nonempty open longitude interval, extends analytically to zero: the intersection of the endpoint admissible longitude projections is an interval containing zero and that initial interval. The contour-independent local transform charts of Section 4 patch along this interval. Apply (6.6) only at the endpoints. Intermediate triangulations need their proper positive kernel contractions and the specified move/peripheral certificates; they need not have complete geometric saddle certificates for this step. **Consequence.** Within every such certified positive-path component of geometric endpoint realizations, the selected coarea states differ only by the recorded boundary-independent scalar eta exp(i d_0/h). Their annihilator ideals, primitive minimal operators and volume limits agree after the fixed peripheral coordinates are identified. The printed states also retain their explicit p_1^2 ratio. This is a statement for certified paths, not an assertion that an arbitrary topological Pachner path stays positive or proper. ## 7. Scope and reproducible checks Equations (3.2)–(3.4) supply the exact relationship between the specified literature fiber integral and its leveled charged tensor realization. Section 4 proves state recovery, and Section 6 reduces covariance for the audited moves to an explicit affine phase and, if needed, a contour shift. These improve the previous magnitude-only relationship. Section 6.1 rules out the nonzero slope for compatible positive complete geometric endpoints by a full-integral saddle moment. Thus only the scalar phase remains for any connecting path satisfying the stated certificates. The subsequent `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` applies this criterion to the actual figure-eight 3–2 move. It audits the ordering kernels, proves d_1=0 and d_0=11pi/12 on the entire angle space, and records the simultaneous meridian/longitude reversal. A verified automorphism then makes the two-tetrahedron state even, giving an exact scalar equivalence at the same boundary value and the same minimal operator. **Corollary for the volume theorem.** Under the positive complete geometric and finite matrix certificates in `literature_state_volume.md`, the selected inverse-transform state of the leveled tensor realization (3.4) is exactly J_print/p_1^2. Its primitive minimal annihilator exists in the prescribed Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra, its classical symbol contains the certified geometric peripheral component, and lim_(b->0+) -2pi h log|J_or(h,0)|=Vol(M). This follows from the exact state identity here, the annihilator proof in `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`, and the independently proved saddle theorem. The nonzero constant p_1^2 contributes zero to the limit. Thus the state in that theorem is an exact specified leveled AK realization, not a solution selected only for its convenient asymptotic. The uniform twist certificates give this corollary for every fixed parameter in the two stated twist families and their recorded mirror convention. What is still needed for a single intrinsic knot state across arbitrary realizations is a certified connecting sequence, its compatible peripheral lifts, the constants for the exactly normalized framed state, and any continuation outside the positive chamber. The slope is already zero for the certified geometric endpoints of Section 6.1. A path through the required geometric triangulations is not supplied just by the existence of a topological Pachner sequence. The all-alternating extension also still needs its geometric and finite matrix certificates. None of these remaining claims is inferred from the affine form (6.2). Run `python3 experiments/audit_peripheral_phase.py`. It checks the generic mixed-sign Gaussian identity, eighteen complete affine twist angle spaces, their peripheral rank, and four pointwise quantum identities using the independently derived real-b defining-integral remainder. The maximum pointwise relative error was below 9e-15. The symbolic identities and contour bounds above, rather than those finite samples, carry the proofs.

title: Exact Bell weights and a source-balanced positive Gram
text: # Exact Bell weights and a source-balanced positive Gram 29 October 2026. The phase-ratio coefficient of the original conjugate source has one positive angle-energy profile, rather than its square. Its radius factors and normalization are explicit. A second result constructs a canonical positive Gram for the ACTUAL right/left Fermat frames: both source costs reduce to a rational chord sum, polynomial away from the normalized central divisor. With the original cap normalizers retained, the cost is O(1+|epsilon|logN) uniformly at every cap index. This supplies a quantitative special-inner-product input, not a bound on the interior original word. ## 1. Exact magnitude on the Fermat fiber Use sigma=-1 and the actual normalized P,L and Bell basis of [the source-exact reflection theorem](phase_ratio_double_and_fermat_source.md). Let u^N+v^N=1 and assume the factors below are nonzero. Define t=v/barv, a=baru/u, A_j=|1-t Q^(-j)|, B_j=|1-a Q^j|, C_j=|1-at Q^j|. The two original source equations give BOTH recurrences |c_(s,r+1)|/|c_(s,r)|=A_r/(|u| C_(s-r)), |c_(s,r)|/|c_(s-1,r)|=|v| C_(s-r)/B_s. (1) For n in Z define Cprod(0)=1 and Cprod(n)/Cprod(n-1)=C_n, using reciprocal products for n<0. Put f_(s,r)=|u|^(-r)|v|^s [product_(j=0)^(r-1) A_j] Cprod(s-r) /[product_(j=1)^s B_j], 0<=s,r<N. (2) Empty products equal one. Starting at (0,0), (1) proves |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N f_(s,r), kappa_N=||P||_2^2/[sum_(s,r) f_(s,r)^2]^(1/2). (3) This determines the normalization by a specified positive finite sum, with no unknown knot period. Indeed the Bell transform is unitary and its input is P tensor barP, so sum|c|^2=||P||^4. The all-nonzero theorem on the open positive-central fiber justifies normalizing at (0,0). Other nonsingular root marks have the same formula with their actual chord factors, not principal arguments silently substituted. On the PRINCIPAL positive-central component, kappa_N=c_(0,0)>0 also fixes the scalar phase. The defining sum for c_(0,0) is real by pairing a with -a. It never vanishes on this connected component by (1), and as U=u^N tends to zero in the upper half-plane the principal roots give P_a->1 and c_(0,0)->sqrtN. Hence its sign is positive everywhere there. A different root mark must keep its own phase; this argument does not silently identify those marks. If the actual column is Gamma P, multiply c and kappa_N by |Gamma|^2. No Gamma, inverse-frame normalization or cap residue factor has been removed. The radii |u|,|v| in (2) may depend arbitrarily on N. Formula (3) remains exact and does not declare kappa_N or those radius factors subexponential. ## 2. Three shifted positive factorials, and both chambers For a Frobenius center U=u^N in the upper half-plane, take the principal marked roots and write alpha=Arg(U)/pi, beta=-Arg(1-U)/pi, gamma=alpha+beta, 0<alpha,beta,gamma<1. Define the positive shifted factorial T_N(L;delta)=product_(j=1)^L 2sin[pi(j+delta)/N], -1<delta<0, 0<=L<=N. Every displayed sine is positive. Set A_full=|1-t^N|, C_full=|1-(at)^N|. Reflection of the numerator arcs in (2) gives the exact formulas r>s: |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N A_full |u|^(-r)|v|^s /[T_N(N-r;-beta) T_N(s;-alpha) T_N(r-s;gamma-1)], (4) r<=s: |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N A_full C_full |u|^(-r)|v|^s /[T_N(N-r;-beta) T_N(s;-alpha) T_N(N-s+r;gamma-1)]. (5) Proof. A_j=2sin[pi(j+beta)/N], B_j=2sin[pi(j-alpha)/N]. For r>s the reciprocal negative-index Cprod gives the factors 2sin[pi(j+gamma-1)/N], j=1,...,r-s. Replace the A numerator by its complete product divided by the remaining arc, and reflect that arc. This proves (4). For r<=s also complement the positive C numerator by its complete product; the same reflection proves (5). The three lengths sum to N in (4), and their shifts sum to -1. On the STRICT chamber 0<s<r<N all three shifted endpoints are positive and sum to d=N-1. Thus (4) has ONE angle-energy weight, not a square-root amplitude weight and not its square. In (5) the lengths sum to 2N and the shifted endpoints sum to 2N-1. Boundary rows, including s=0, retain their literal empty products; a negative formal shifted endpoint is not declared a geometric angle. The full half-phase/sign accounting is in the reflection theorem and is not replaced by choosing the favorable chamber. For shifts in a fixed compact subset of (-1,0), lengths at most N-1, these T_N factors differ from the unshifted s_N factors by polynomial factors: separate the first factor and integrate the logarithmic derivative, bounded by the harmonic sums at the two root endpoints. If a shift approaches a divisor, retain its explicit factor. If L=N, T_N(N;delta)=|1-exp(2pi i delta)|, not the forbidden zero s_N(N). No uniform polynomial comparison through arbitrary exponentially close divisors is inferred. In particular, U fixed and u=U^(1/N) is only one parameter regime. A fixed semiclassical radius |u|!=1 has an exponentially varying Frobenius center. Equations (2)--(5) retain that regime rather than identifying it with the fixed-center estimate. ## 3. An explicit non-diagonal Bell Cauchy metric For the full positive array f in (2), give an exterior array b the norm squared sum f_(s,r)|b_(s,r)|^2. Its original source functional sum c_(s,r)b_(s,r) has exact Riesz norm squared sum |c_(s,r)|^2/f_(s,r)=kappa_N^2 sum f_(s,r). (6) Thus an explicit positive Gram exists in the Bell space; in the original doubled head coordinates it is a conjugate of diag(f) and is generally nondiagonal. It retains ALL sectors. The phase choice b=barc/|c| attains the corresponding weighted Cauchy bound, so (6) is a sharp local all-exterior statement. The coefficient c already belongs to a DOUBLED amplitude. Squaring its contraction again proves a fourth-power statement, not the desired |K|^2 estimate. Direct triangle comparison instead reads |sum c b|<=kappa_N sum f |b|. (7) If the actual remaining contraction has |b| bounded polynomially and the actual edge projector is diagonal in this SAME joint basis, (4)--(7) supply a one-power positive partition comparison. Those conditions on the remaining original contraction are not proved here. Introducing a dephasing or discarding (5) does not establish them. Normalization (6) is also explicit rather than assumed tame. ## 4. A stronger Gram balances the actual source AND co-source There is a useful quantitative alternative which does not require the Fermat equation. For the literal P,L in either orientation, when u^N!=1 and v!=0, finite cancellation gives L_a P_a=(1-u)/(1-u Q_s^a). Define H_a=|L_a|/|P_a|>0, U_a=(L_aP_a)/|L_aP_a|. Then EXACTLY L=P^* H U, U unitary diagonal, P^*H P=L H^(-1)L^* =S_N(u):=|1-u|sum_(a=0)^d 1/|1-u Q_s^a|. (8) This is a prescribed positive inner product, constructed from the known cyclic source frames, not from a knot value. For every specified exterior A, |L A P|<=S_N(u)||A||_H. (9) The phase U in (8) is compulsory; no positive pivotal trace is claimed. If the actual rows/columns are Gamma_L L,Gamma_R P, their balanced source norm squared is |Gamma_L Gamma_R|S_N. The Gamma product is part of (9), even when exponential. There is an elementary radius-uniform estimate S_N(u)<=2N^2 max(1,|u|^N)/|1-u^N|. (10) Indeed (1-u^N)/(1-uQ_s^a)=sum_(k=0)^d(uQ_s^a)^k. Its absolute value is at most N max(1,|u|^d). Sum over a and use |1-u|<=1+|u|. This proves (10) for arbitrary N-dependent radii. A polynomial lower bound on the NORMALIZED central separation |1-u^N|/max(1,|u|^N) makes this source cost polynomial. It is not a lower bound on that separation when a source pole approaches the contour. On the doubled head, use H tensor H. The original doubled source and co-source both have norm squared S_N^2. In the unitary Bell basis its Gram is explicitly Bell^*(H tensor H)Bell, generally NONDIAGONAL. Formula (4) of the reflection theorem preserves the magnitudes of P,L, so this H is invariant under the source antiinvolution, and its compulsory co-source clock is unitary for H as well. No small-root or fixed-radius argument is needed. The phase-ratio observables are unitary in the flat cyclic metric; they need not be unitary for H. Nor is a diagonal H at one quad chart automatically the diagonal metric at the next chart. Transporting this Gram and retaining its off-diagonal terms is essential. A flat diagonal edge projector need not be contractive in the transported source metric. The [selected corner-sector theorem](phase_ratio_corner_sector_metric.md) proves a precise boundary exception: the doubled metric is scalar on the actual corner's clock-sum sector for real cap parameters, and has polynomial condition number there throughout the complex cap disk. Orthogonal projectors restricted to that sector therefore have a tame norm. This does not discard the other regularized-cap sectors or prove that an interior crossing preserves the selected sector. ## 5. Polynomial cost at EVERY actual normalized cap In the literal cap orientation Q_s=Q, put epsilon=v^N, u=Q^(-j)(1-epsilon)^(1/N), |epsilon|<=rho=1/16. For j>=1 use the original normalized frames Phat_j=v^(N-j)P/alpha_j, Lhat_j=v^j L/beta_j, alpha_j beta_j=N(1-Q^(-j)). For j=0 use P,L without those factors. Let Hhat_j be their balanced positive metric as in (8). Their source norm squared is Shat_j=|epsilon| |1-u|/[N|1-Q^(-j)|] sum_a1/|1-uQ^a|, j>=1, Shat_0=S_N(u). (11) Uniformly in N,j, and the marked punctured epsilon disk, Shat_j<=C[1+|epsilon|(1+log N)], lim_(epsilon->0)Shat_j=1. (12) Proof. Write delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N). The marked logarithm gives |delta-1|<=2|epsilon|/N. The resonant denominator is bounded below by |epsilon|/[N(1+rho)] from epsilon=(1-delta)sum_(k=0)^d delta^k. Every other denominator |1-delta Q^k| is at least 3min(k,N-k)/N. Their reciprocal sum is O(N(1+logN)). For j>=1, |1-u|/|1-Q^(-j)|<=2, giving (12). For j=0 the resonant term in S_N is exactly one and the others have the same bound. The resonant term tends to one in every case and the other terms vanish. This proof keeps the actual alpha_j,beta_j, whose separate sizes need not be polynomial. Independent input/output caps may use different Hhat metrics. Their original matrix element is bounded by the geometric mean of these source costs times the operator norm from Hhat_in to Hhat_out. Tensor products preserve this statement. The actual corner source is obtained by Cauchy evaluation of Phat,Lhat at zero; on |v|=rho^(1/N), each normalized dv/v circle has mass one. Thus these cap source factors cost only polynomially in the original whole residue presentation. The INTERIOR word norm between those metrics, and all additional retained scalar lines, remain to be bounded. This does not turn (12) into a knot-volume bound by itself. ## 6. Off-Fermat/current packets are not erased Let Delta=1-u^N-v^N and F_d=product_(a=1)^d(1-uQ^(-a)). The normalized column satisfies B P=Delta e_0/F_d even off the Fermat curve. Its exact Bell equations acquire c_sr-u c_(s,r+1)-vQ^(-r)c_(s-1,r)=h_s, c_sr-baruQ^s c_(s,r+1)-barv c_(s-1,r)=k_sr, h_s=(Delta/F_d)barP_s/sqrtN, k_sr=(barDelta/barF_d)Q^(-rs)P_s/sqrtN. Consequently the recurrence behind (1) is replaced by [u-t baru Q^(s-r)]c_(s,r+1) =[1-tQ^(-r)]c_sr-h_s+tQ^(-r)k_sr. (13) Variation of constants retains the finite sum of both displayed sources, with the actual cyclic closure determinant. Resonant closure does not select a free homogeneous coefficient. Thus (2)--(5) are exact Fermat-source formulas; extending them to a complete inhomogeneous beta packet requires the currents (13), not setting their central Delta to zero. The positive metric (8)--(10) itself remains exact off the Fermat locus. [Audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_bell_weights.py): pointwise shifted-factorial profiles and Parseval normalization, varying radii/centers, source-balanced metrics and actual cap constants, and the full off-Fermat source corrections.

title: A tame phase-ratio projector on the actual doubled corner sector
text: # A tame phase-ratio projector on the actual doubled corner sector 29 October 2026. This is a boundary metric theorem for the original normalized Fermat cap, with all source normalizers retained. On its selected doubled clock sector, every flat orthogonal projector is exactly contractive for real cap parameters and polynomially bounded throughout a fixed complex cap disk. It does not prove that an interior crossing preserves that sector, or identify the character constraints of a triangulation edge. ## 1. The actual source and its periodic positive metric Let N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N), and 0<|epsilon|<=rho=1/16. Use the marked root delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), u=Q^(-j)delta, v^N=epsilon, 0<=j<N. (1) Any marked Nth root v is allowed. In the literal cap orientation, P_a=v^a/product_(r=1)^a(1-uQ^r), L_a=v^(-a)product_(r=0)^(a-1)(1-uQ^r), 0<=a<N, h_a=|L_a|/|P_a|. (2) These are the original source frames of [the source-balanced Gram theorem](phase_ratio_bell_weights_and_source_gram.md). Because 1-u^N=v^N, both P and L, and hence h, extend N-periodically. Their EXACT recurrence is h_(a+1)/h_a=|1-uQ^a| |1-uQ^(a+1)|/|v|^2. (3) For j>=1 the actual cap normalization is Phat_a=v^(N-j)P_a/alpha_j, Lhat_a=v^j L_a/beta_j, alpha_j=F_(N-j), beta_j=N/F_(d-j), F_r=product_(k=1)^r(1-Q^k), alpha_j beta_j=N(1-Q^(-j)). (4) For j=0 retain P,L unchanged. Consequently the actual balanced metric Hhat=diag(|Lhat_a|/|Phat_a|) is a single positive scalar multiple of H=diag(h_a). The scalar in question is exactly |v|^(2j-N)|alpha_j/beta_j|; it has NOT been assumed tame or omitted from the original source. It cancels in every operator norm below. The literal source cost is still Phat^* Hhat Phat=Lhat Hhat^(-1)Lhat^* =|epsilon| |1-u|/[N|1-Q^(-j)|] sum_a 1/|1-uQ^a|, j>=1, (5) and |1-u| sum_a 1/|1-uQ^a| for j=0. In particular it is bounded by C(1+|epsilon|(1+log N)), as proved in the linked Gram note. No normalizer has been replaced by a chosen unit source. At fixed N, Phat and Lhat both tend to the coordinate corner e_j as epsilon tends to zero on their marked root cover. For the resonant entry of Phat, (1-delta)/epsilon tends to 1/N and the remaining denominator factors together with F_(N-j) multiply to N. For Lhat, its j-th numerator is exactly beta_j at epsilon=0. Every other entry has a strictly positive residual power of v. The j=0 assertion follows directly from (2). ## 2. The doubled sector and the exact projector criterion Give the doubled head the product metric G=H tensor H. Its clock sum sectors are V_s=span{|a,s-a mod N>:0<=a<N}, G|_(V_s)=diag(g_a), g_a=h_a h_(s-a). (6) The original conjugate double may equivalently be written using the source-exact antiunitary reflection of [the reflection theorem](phase_ratio_double_and_fermat_source.md). That reflection preserves h and adds only its specified diagonal unitary chirp. Thus it has the same metric (6), and the doubled corner e_j tensor bare_j belongs to V_(2j mod N). The clock-sector projector is diagonal and commutes with G, so it is contractive on the entire doubled space. Inside V_s the phase-ratio shift S^(-1) tensor S has the Fourier eigenvectors w_(s,r)=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(ra)|a,s-a>, 0<=r<N. Unit-modulus scalar marks change the eigenvalues, not these projectors. A rank-one flat character projector Pi_(s,r)=w w^* has the EXACT restricted metric norm ||Pi_(s,r)||_G =[(N^(-1)sum_a g_a)(N^(-1)sum_a g_a^(-1))]^(1/2). (7) Indeed a rank-one map xy^* has weighted norm ||G^(1/2)x|| ||G^(-1/2)y||. Formula (7) is independent of r and equals one precisely when g is constant. More generally, a flat orthogonal projector Pi is contractive in a positive metric G precisely when [Pi,G]=0. Necessity follows by applying contractivity to x+t y with x in its range and y in its kernel, and varying complex t: it forces their G-orthogonality. Sufficiency follows by the resulting orthogonal splitting. In general ||Pi||_G<=sqrt(cond G). ## 3.
