Exact contractivity and its complex extension **Theorem.** For the actual normalized cap (1)--(4), every flat orthogonal projector whose range and domain lie in V_(2j mod N) satisfies ||Pi||_(Hhat tensor Hhat) <=exp[8|epsilon|(1+log N)] <=e^(8rho)N^(8rho). (8) Here the norm means the restriction to that sector, or equivalently the extension by zero on its orthogonal complement. If epsilon is real, the norm of every nonzero such projector is EXACTLY one. In particular this applies to all shift-character projectors and their orthogonal sums on the selected doubled corner sector. Proof. Put z_k=|1-delta Q^k|, periodically in k. Applying (3) to the two reflected indices gives, for 1<=ell<N, g_(j+ell)/g_j =(z_ell/z_(-ell)) product_(k=1)^(ell-1)(z_k/z_(-k))^2, g_j=h_j^2, s=2j mod N. (9) The potentially arbitrarily small resonant chord z_0 cancels EXACTLY. If epsilon is real then delta is real and positive, including when epsilon<0 and delta>1. Thus z_k=z_(-k) and every g_a=h_j^2. The metric is scalar on this sector, proving exact contractivity without a limiting argument. For complex epsilon the marked logarithm gives |delta-1|<=2|epsilon|/N. For k!=0 mod N, with m=min(k,N-k), |1-Q^k|>=4m/N, |z_(+/-k)/|1-Q^k|-1|<=|epsilon|/(2m)=:t_k<=1/32. It follows that |log(z_k/z_(-k))| <=log((1+t_k)/(1-t_k))<=3|epsilon|/(2m). (10) Since sum_(k=1)^(N-1)1/min(k,N-k)<=2(1+log N), equations (9)--(10) give |log(g_a/h_j^2)|<=8|epsilon|(1+log N). Thus the restricted condition number is at most exp[16|epsilon|(1+log N)]. The general projector estimate of section 2 proves (8). Replacing H by Hhat only multiplies the doubled metric by a common positive scalar, so the proof retains all alpha,beta factors in (4). This also proves uniformity for epsilon depending arbitrarily on N, even exponentially close to zero. If |epsilon|log N tends to zero, the upper bound tends to one. The opposite root orientation follows by Q->Q^(-1) and the corresponding reflected cap labels; the same real chord estimates and source normalization proof apply. ## 4. Exact scope at the original source The theorem controls a genuine boundary sector selected by the original corner limit, not an arbitrarily chosen geometric sector. For epsilon!=0 the complete cap column has nonzero entries in every coordinate, so its conjugate double also has other V_s components. These components cannot be discarded inside a Cauchy cap contour. A general V_s has the exact norm (7), with no scalar metric conclusion unless its own reflected products are constant. Nor has a crossing been proved to preserve the local sector s=2j, or a change to an adjacent Fermat chart proved contractive in this metric. Global total-degree conservation does not imply those local assertions. If a specified physical/edge projector acts inside the selected sector as a flat orthogonal projector, (8) bounds that projector with the actual cap metric. Identifying all interior edge projectors and controlling their intervening transport remain separate requirements. All off-Fermat beta currents and both Bell half-phase chambers of the linked notes remain in the complete original source. ## 5. Independent finite audit [The audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_corner_sector_metric.py) checks the literal normalized frames, the alpha beta product, periodic recurrence, reflected product (9), and all cap labels at a range of levels and real/complex cap parameters. It also compares (7) with direct weighted singular values of character projectors and their nontrivial sums. The tests include cap parameters exponentially small in N; none substitutes epsilon=0 before constructing the metric. The accompanying result file is written only after all assertions pass. The phase-ratio checks do not establish preservation of the interior domain.

title: A pointed Hermitian reflection for the actual cyclic source
text: # A pointed Hermitian reflection for the actual cyclic source 29 October 2026. The phase-ratio double has a genuine source-compatible realization: inverse conjugation of the quad coordinates is implemented by an explicit ANTIUNITARY on the cyclic Fermat source, together with a face swap. Its full normalizer is retained, and the construction is valid at arbitrary radii. It agrees exactly with the pointed Fourier quad rotations. It also extends to inhomogeneous cyclic packets, with their source currents transformed rather than removed. The same diagonal reflection fixes the actual fused arbitrary-plat corner functional. Thus a whole original squared scalar has an exact reflected doubled-word presentation. This does not yet identify its contraction with a positive angle partition: the local joint spectral source and all original sewing/co-source factors remain explicit. ## 1. Conventions and a radius-independent antiinvolution Let N>=2, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Use a sign sigma=+1 or -1 and set q_s=q^sigma, Q_s=Q^sigma, D_s e_a=Q_s^a e_a, S e_a=e_(a+1 modN), X=u D_s, Y=v S, B=I-X-Y. The literal cap-source convention has sigma=+1. The cyclic quad convention with Z_i Z_(i+1)=Q Z_(i+1)Z_i has sigma=-1. Define H_s(u,v)=(u',v')=(1/baru, q_s^(-1)barv/baru), A_(s,a)=(-q_s)^a Q_s^[a(a+1)/2], J_s=diag(A_(s,a)^(-1)), Theta_s=J_s conjugation. (1) All powers are ordinary integer expressions; no division by two modulo N is used. Since A_(s,N)=1, the chirp is cyclic, including its endpoint. It is unitary, Theta_s^2=I and H_s^2=id. If u^N+v^N=1, then u'^N+v'^N=1. The central shape U=u^N is sent to 1/barU, which preserves the upper half-plane. The exact matrix identity, with NO Fermat hypothesis, is B(u',v') J_s=-J_s barX^(-1) barB(u,v). (2) Indeed J_s S J_s^(-1)=-q_s^(-1)D_s^(-1)S; multiply barB on the left by -barX^(-1) and use this equality. The extra invertible left factor in (2) is not silently replaced by a similarity. ## 2. Actual right and left source frames, including their normalizers Use the literal normalized frames from the cap/source construction, with the indicated root orientation: F_a(u)=product_(r=1)^a(1-u Q_s^r), P_a(u,v)=v^a/F_a(u), L_a(u,v)=v^(-a)product_(r=0)^(a-1)(1-u Q_s^r), P_0=L_0=1. (3) They are the actual P,L of the cap theorem when sigma=+1. Whenever these expressions are defined, finite-product reflection gives P(u',v')=J_s barP(u,v), L(u',v')=barL(u,v) D_s^(-1)J_s^(-1). (4) For the right formula factor each denominator as 1-baru^(-1)Q_s^r=-baru^(-1)Q_s^r(1-baru Q_s^(-r)). Together with v'=q_s^(-1)barv/baru this gives precisely the chirp in (1). The same calculation starting at r=0 gives the COMPULSORY clock D_s^(-1) in the left formula. Both transformations preserve the Euclidean norm in this cyclic frame EXACTLY, at arbitrary radii. The cancellation uses the full Fermat/shift normalizer v'. It is not a small-root-log argument. For example |F_a(u)/F_a(1/baru)|=|u|^a can be exponentially large when a is proportional to N, but the corresponding v-power cancels it in (4). No assertion that a geometric clock radius is 1+O(1/N) is needed. For an arbitrary retained operator C, the paired scalar identity is bar[L C P]=L(u',v') D_s [J_s barC J_s^(-1)]P(u',v'). (5) Thus the actual co-source carries a unitary clock insertion. It is not merely the unshifted natural left source at the reflected point. Every external scalar Gamma is conjugated and retained. In particular Theta_s(Gamma P)=barGamma P'; it is not reset to one. There is also an exact check on polynomial normalization. Let Delta=1-u^N-v^N and Ptilde=F_d(u)P, d=N-1. Then B Ptilde=Delta e_0, Delta'=-barDelta/baru^N, F_d(u')=baru^(-d)barF_d(u), Ptilde(u',v')=baru^(-d)J_s barPtilde(u,v). (6) If the actual column is expressed in the polynomial Ptilde frame, the power baru^d must therefore stay in its transformed Gamma. It can be exponential; (4) does not license deleting it. The same warning applies to the actual cap residue constants and Jacobians. Those are retained by ordinary coordinate substitution. At a literal corner Theta_s e_d=-q_s e_d and Theta_s e_0=e_0, so its pointed normalization changes only by the specified unit phase, not an unknown central normalizer. ## 3. Pointed quad rotations compose coherently Use the original normalized Fourier matrix F_s and quad adapter (F_s)_(k,a)=Q_s^(ka)/sqrtN, W_s=F_s A_s, rho_s(u,v)=(q_s v/u,1/u). Then EXACTLY Theta_s W_s Theta_s=W_s^(-1), H_s rho_s H_s=rho_s^(-1). (7) The matrix proof is J_s barW_s barJ_s =A_s^(-1)F_s^(-1)=W_s^(-1). The parameter proof is direct substitution. No projective phase or central deck was discarded. Using q instead of q_s^(-1) in (1) with sigma=+1 would insert a root-of-unity deck; keeping the orientation makes (7) exact. If W_s P(p)=c(p)P(rho_s p) is the actual pointed source rotation, P_0=1 fixes c. Equations (4),(7) force c(H_s rho_s p) barc(p)=1. (8) Thus the exact source Gamma of a reflected pointed rotation is its reciprocal conjugate, including its nontrivial modulus. This is a genuine normalization identity, not a new unit-norm choice. The left-source clock in (4), and the corresponding clock in (5), must still be used on sewn output faces. ## 4. Full currents survive the reflection For ANY inhomogeneous packet B f=eta, (2) gives B' Theta_s f=-Theta_s(X^(-1)eta). (9) When B is invertible this is also an exact resolvent identity; meromorphic continuation keeps its poles and residues. It neither sets Delta=0 nor deletes a current proportional to Delta. Thus a local source decomposition into a balanced residue and a current is reflected LINEARLY with both parts retained. For example the complete Newton packet f_j=B_N(u,vQ^j) obeys (I-uR+vD_Q R)f=(1-u^N+v^N)1, with (Rf)_j=f_(j+1). The two terms uR and -vD_Q R form a finite Weyl pair, of central powers u^N and -v^N. A fixed unitary Weyl change puts it in the form of (9). Its source must undergo the SAME change and the factor X^(-1) in (9); no claim that the reflected packet is the same standard B_N with its source reset is made. In particular this is not a proof that the inhomogeneous beta current vanishes. The full-Psi split and its marked scalar normalizer remain part of the original packet. ## 5. The inverse-reflected triad and its positive joint basis Put Z0=X, Z1=Y^(-1), Z2=-X^(-1)Y. Their cyclic commutation parameter is Q_s^(-1), and their ordered product is -Q_s^(-1). At the reflected point, (Z0',Z1',Z2')= (J_s barZ0^(-1)J_s^(-1), J_s barZ2^(-1)J_s^(-1), J_s barZ1^(-1)J_s^(-1)). (10) Thus inverse conjugation comes with the 1<->2 face swap. The unitary map I tensor J_s takes P tensor barP to P tensor P' and takes the phase-ratio observables Z_i tensor barZ_i^(-1) to Z_i tensor Z'_(tau(i)), tau=(1 2). This is a source-compatible interpretation of the inverse factor, not arbitrary inversion of the original bra. For sigma=-1 the phase-ratio observables commute, are unitary even for complex u,v, and have ordered product Q. A joint orthonormal basis is |s,r>=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(ra)|a,s-a moduloN>. Its first two eigenvalues are (u/baru)Q^(-s) and (barv/v)Q^r; the third is Q divided by their product. This gives a genuine positive joint spectral norm. It is not yet a positive angle state or its geometric edge projector. Indeed the original conjugate source in this basis has coefficients c_(s,r)=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(-ra)P_a barP_(s-a). (11) The two source equations, BEFORE any positivity or projection, imply on the Fermat locus c_(s,r+1)=[1-(v/barv)Q^(-r)] /[u-(v/barv)baru Q^(s-r)] c_(s,r). (12) On the open family with Im(u^N)>0 and principal root marks u=(u^N)^(1/N),v=(1-u^N)^(1/N), every factor in (12) is nonzero. To check it, write alpha=Arg(u^N)>0,beta=Arg(v^N)<0. The third positive central quad angle gives -pi<beta-alpha<0. Neither beta nor beta-alpha is a multiple of pi. For each fixed s the Fourier transform in (11) is not identically zero, since all P_a barP_(s-a) are nonzero. Equation (12) therefore proves that EVERY c_(s,r) is nonzero at every N. Here u^N is a Frobenius center, not a claim about a fixed semiclassical clock radius. No tame geometric-contour estimate is inferred from choosing this center independent of N. In particular the positive half-phase square roots do not automatically select one affine tetrahedral charge. For this open family write alpha_i for the three positive CENTRAL quad arguments, sum alpha_i=pi, and let r0=-s modN, r1=r, r2=s-r modN, 0<=ri<N. The inverse-ratio upper-half-plane square roots have angles beta_i=pi-(alpha_i+pi ri)/N. Their product is q^d on the sum ri=0 or2N sectors and q^(-1) on the sum ri=N sector. Both occur with NONZERO source coefficients. Only the sum2N sector has sum beta_i=pi*d/N; the sum0 sector has sum 3pi-pi/N. Extra physical windows or source constraints are therefore indispensable. They cannot be inferred from the commuting phase-ratio algebra alone. A proposed local Cauchy norm supported ONLY on the desired angle sector is not continuous on this whole cyclic source: a discarded Bell basis vector has zero proposed norm but a nonzero source pairing in (11). This rules out that unqualified ALL-EXTERIOR local norm substitution, not a global comparison after the actual co-source or compensated length metric is used. ## 6. The whole original pointed scalar has a reflected double Use the already proved arbitrary-plat fused source K_N=chi_N N^(1-k) <e_out|B_beta|e_in>. Each input pair is (d,0); each ordinary output pair is (0,d), and the marked output pair is (d,0). On EVERY such pair the eigenvalue of J_s tensor J_s is J_(s,d)J_(s,0)=-q_s. Consequently the input and output corner eigenvalues of J_tot=J_s^(tensor2k) are equal. Hence EXACTLY barK_N=barChi_N N^(1-k) <e_out|J_tot barB_beta J_tot^(-1)|e_in>. (13) This proves a source-exact reflected doubled-word presentation of |K_N|^2, with no normalization by an unknown period. All kernel currents, original Cartan factors and external lines are conjugated and retained. On every standard cyclic quad chart, (10) identifies the inverse-reflected variables; (7) makes the pointed S3 changes compatible. It does not prove that every global cyclic/cluster adapter is unitary, or that all geometric edge isotypic constraints have been selected by this source. If an ordered edge word is reflected with reversed face order, its character transforms chi_e to 1/barchi_e. Existing UNIT characters, including the desired full-clock character, are preserved; a free character has not thereby been chosen. Nor may an exponentially conditioned physical-to-cyclic frame be discarded. The unitarity assertions here are in the specified cyclic flat metric, with the actual source/co-source transformed together. Thus the reflection is a constructive norm-compatible piece of a special-inner-product comparison. A positive angle majorant still requires the actual geometric tensor/wiring map and its controlled current or defect estimate. [Audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_fermat_source.py): exact reflected generators and sources, arbitrary-radius and inhomogeneous normalizers, pointed dihedral identities, phase-ratio spectra/source recurrence, and original complete signed plat sources.

title: A positive determinant period of the actual pointed quantum A-operator
text: # A positive determinant period of the actual pointed quantum A-operator Research note, 27 October 2026. This gives an exact finite algebraic period on the actual A-operator side for every knot. It uses any specified nonzero all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed small-color jets. Its value is a positive ratio of polynomial coefficients of two matrices of fixed bandwidth. Neither the operator's root-level kernel rank nor a separate nonvanishing source-overlap hypothesis is required for the identity. The original Kashaev volume conjecture becomes a precise growth statement for this ratio, equation (6.2). That growth statement is not proved here. Positivity of Gram coefficients is not a substitute for estimating their ratio or relating it to the marked regulator. ## 1. The actual operator, and a fixed amount of pointing Use the actual reduced quantum periods from [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md). A nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator exists by the independent [finite-cut proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). Fix one, clear its denominators, and write A=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M) T^i, T M=q M T, a_i in Q[q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1)], a_d!=0. (1.1) The same argument works over a fixed coefficient number field. All original normalization and meridian conventions are retained. The finite small-color pointing gives the exact generic identities sum_i a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0, j>=1, C_N(q_N)=<K>_N, q_N=exp(pi i/N). (1.2) Here C_j is the reduced j-dimensional highest-weight cut, with unknot value one. No large-color Jones asymptotic is an input. Equation (1.2) is the repo's own polynomial-rigidity consequence of the actual root states and quotient colors. Remove a common power of q-1 from the coefficients first, so A_cl(M,L)=sum_i a_i(1,M)L^i is nonzero. This changes neither the generic annihilation nor the original root periods. Let A_q be the q-exponent span of a_d, D its M-exponent span, and s its number of monomials. Choose a fixed j_*>=A_q+1 and put B=D(s-1). (1.3) For sufficiently large N, the total order of zeros at q_N in a_d(q,-q^j), j_*<=j<=N-d, is at most B. Briefly, its root specialization has at most D distinct zeros on that color orbit, and any nonzero Laurent polynomial with s monomials has vanishing order at most s-1. The latter is the Vandermonde argument in the all-level note. The choice j_*>A_q prevents a coefficient from vanishing identically on one of the color trajectories. Only the jets through order B of C_(j_*),...,C_(j_*+d-1) will be used. This is a fixed list, independent of N. A smaller starting color is allowed when direct factorization verifies that a_d(q,-q^j) is not identically zero for every subsequent j; the bound A_q+1 is a sufficient uniform choice. ## 2. A finite banded system retains every singular step Put t=q/q_N-1, n_c=N-j_*+1 and n=(B+1)n_c. For each color j_*<=j<=N introduce its truncated jet y_j(t)=sum_(r=0)^B y_(j,r)t^r mod t^(B+1). Define the square n by n matrix M_N by these equations: * For the first d colors, prescribe their B-jets to be the actual fixed-color jets at q_N. * For j_*<=j<=N-d, impose (1.2) modulo t^(B+1), with q=q_N(1+t). Call the right side b_N. It is supported only in the first d color blocks; its norm is bounded as N grows. These fixed Laurent polynomials and their bounded-order jets are analytic near q=1. The matrix has lower block bandwidth d and block size B+1. Its initial diagonal blocks are I; each later diagonal block is truncated multiplication by a_d(q,-q^j). A monomial q^a M^c on the j-th trajectory contributes (-1)^c q_N^(a+cj) binom(a+cj,r) (2.1) to its r-th jet. Thus every entry is O(N^B) and the matrix has fixed bandwidth and size O(N). Negative exponents in (2.1) use the ordinary generalized binomial coefficient. Let R_N select the constant coefficient y_(j,0) from each block. The actual color jets give a solution of M_N y=b_N. (2.2) Although higher jets in a truncated solution may not be unique, every constant color value is unique. Indeed the difference of two solutions has zero initial jets through order B. At a step whose leading coefficient has zero order m, division in the Laurent-series field lowers the known valuation by at most m. Induction gives valuation at least B+1-sum_(previous steps)m >=1. The argument can be performed on arbitrary polynomial lifts: every recurrence error is divisible by t^(B+1), so the same valuation induction applies. Consequently ker M_N subset ker R_N, R_N y=f_N=(C_(j_*)(q_N),...,C_N(q_N))^t (2.3) for every solution of (2.2). No division at the singular value itself was used. The nullity nu_N=dim ker M_N is at most B. In fact a leading coefficient with order m has a multiplication block of nullity m (the total budget ensures m<=B). A lower block triangular matrix has rank at least the sum of the ranks of its diagonal blocks: select invertible minors of each diagonal block and combine them. Their combined minor is lower block triangular with nonzero determinant. Summing the block nullities proves the assertion. An exact per-level pole budget may replace B in this construction. The theorem uses the uniform bound so its block size is fixed. ## 3. The pointed norm is a Gram coefficient ratio For the fixed complex embedding at q_N let dagger be the ordinary Hermitian transpose. Write P=M_N^dagger M_N, g=M_N^dagger b_N, beta=b_N^dagger b_N, Q_N(lambda)=det(P+lambda I), D_N(lambda,z)=det[ P+lambda I+z R_N^dagger R_N g; g^dagger beta ]. (3.1) The variables lambda,z are ordinary commuting polynomial variables. They have no relation to a peripheral longitude. In particular, D_N here is not the root monodromy polynomial of the norm-torsor note. Define G_N(A,j_*)=[lambda^nu_N z]D_N(lambda,z) /[lambda^nu_N]Q_N(lambda). (3.2) **Exact pointed Gram theorem.** The denominator is positive and G_N(A,j_*)=||f_N||^2 =sum_(j=j_*)^N |C_j(q_N)|^2. (3.3) For large N its numerator is positive too: any one of the fixed initial colors tends to the unknot value 1 at q=1. Thus (3.2) is a well-defined positive algebraic period, even at a level where the complete Kashaev value might vanish. Here is a direct proof which also explains the specified coefficient. Use an orthonormal decomposition C^n=(ker M_N)^perp plus ker M_N. On it P=diag(P_r,0), P_r positive definite. By (2.3), R_N is zero on the kernel. Also g has no kernel component. Hence D_N has a factor lambda^nu_N, and its remaining block has size r+1. Let y_0 be the minimum-norm solution of (2.2). Then g=P_r y_0, beta=y_0^dagger P_r y_0. At lambda=0 the Schur complement of P_r+z R_N^dagger R_N is zero at z=0. Its derivative there is y_0^dagger R_N^dagger R_N y_0=||f_N||^2. Therefore the coefficient in the numerator is det(P_r)||f_N||^2, whereas the denominator coefficient is det(P_r). This proves (3.3), without any special-fiber rank-one assumption or pseudoinverse overlap estimate. ## 4. Both polynomial coefficient families are positive Every coefficient of Q_N(lambda) and D_N(lambda,z) is nonnegative real. For the latter form the rectangular matrix Z(lambda,z)=[ M_N b_N; sqrt(z) R_N 0; sqrt(lambda) I 0 ]. (4.1) Its Gram matrix is exactly the bordered matrix in (3.1). The Cauchy--Binet formula writes its determinant as a sum over row sets of squared absolute determinants. In each summand the chosen identity and R rows contribute a definite monomial in lambda,z. Its coefficient is nonnegative. The same proof with the last column and the R rows omitted applies to Q_N. This is positivity of the displayed coefficient periods. It does not assert that the original crossing coefficients are positive, or that every complex minor has been estimated. It removes a separate arbitrary choice of a source overlap from the statement: the original overlap is already contained in the pointed border. All data in (3.1) come from the specified actual A-operator and its fixed small-color jets. No color near N is an input. Conjugation of cyclotomic coefficients uses q_N->q_N^(-1), including the conjugates of the actual initial jets. These matrices still have fixed bandwidth. The matrix P has bounded block bandwidth, and g is supported in the initial blocks: because b_N is supported on the identity initial equations, M_N^dagger b_N is just that same padded initial vector. Placing the last row and column first keeps a bandwidth bounded in terms of d and B, independently of N. The size is O(N), the nullity is bounded, and all entries grow at most polynomially. ## 5. Independence of the operator presentation If two actual all-level operators are used with a common sufficiently large starting color j_*, their ratios (3.2) are identical, by (3.3). Their orders, jet bounds, singular steps and matrix sizes can differ. The equality is exact and retains their distinct lattice presentations. Starting at two different fixed colors changes G_N only by finitely many bounded small-color terms. In particular the construction is not a largest-root prescription, and it does not require an equality between the root-central characteristic and the classical A-polynomial. Multiplying an annihilator by a harmless or singular left factor changes its finite jet system but leaves the exact ratio unchanged when the same pointing and valid pole budget are used. ### A uniformly bounded jet lattice and its classical symbol The polynomial growth in individual jet entries is removable without changing the period. Set S_N=direct_sum_(j=j_*)^N diag(1,N^(-1),...,N^(-B)), M_tilde=S_N M_N S_N^(-1), b_tilde=S_N b_N. (5.1) Since R_N S_N^(-1)=R_N, the pointed Gram theorem applied to these scaled data gives exactly the same G_N. This is a genuine change of lattice and source, not an inference from invariance of an unpointed norm. In the new matrix a jet coefficient of order r is divided by N^r. Formula (2.1) shows that every entry, the matrix operator norm, and the source norm are now bounded uniformly in N. The bandwidth, size O(N), and nullity bound are unchanged. The source border remains confined to a fixed number of initial blocks. This also identifies the bulk symbol of the positive determinant problem directly from the actual A-operator. Write x=j/N, M(x)=-exp(pi i x), delta_M=M partial_M, and let J be the (B+1)-dimensional nilpotent subdiagonal shift. For fixed r, the scaled coefficient in (2.1) tends uniformly to (-1)^c exp(pi i c x) (cx)^r/r!. Thus the banded interior recurrence has block symbol, up to the harmless scalar Fourier factor L^(-d), A_B(x,L)=sum_(i=0)^d sum_(r=0)^B x^r/r! [delta_M^r a_i(1,M)]_(M=M(x)) J^r L^i. (5.2) It is lower triangular in jet degree and satisfies det A_B(x,L)=A_cl(M(x),L)^(B+1). (5.3) No additional classical curve is introduced by the jet repair. For |L|=1 the Hermitian bulk Gram symbol is A_B^dagger A_B, with determinant |A_cl(M(x),L)|^(2(B+1)). The initial equations and source border are explicitly retained boundary terms. These are statements about the chosen actual operator's symbol. They do not assert that its classical polynomial has already been identified with A_K, or estimate the small boundary singular values of the finite matrices. Even a strictly positive bulk Gram symbol need not bound those finite boundary singular values away from zero; the growing-recurrence example below exhibits this. ### The actual quantum period is a positive regularized response There is a canonical convex quadratic problem for these same scaled data, with the original source retained. For real z>=0 put Phi_N(z)=min_y {||M_tilde y-b_tilde||^2+z||R_N y||^2}. (5.4) On the orthogonal complement of ker M_tilde its minimizer is unique. If P_r,Q_r,g_r denote the restrictions of M_tilde^dagger M_tilde, R_N^dagger R_N and M_tilde^dagger b_tilde, respectively, then Phi_N(z)=beta-g_r^dagger(P_r+z Q_r)^(-1)g_r, Phi_N(0)=0, Phi_N'(0)=G_N(A,j_*). (5.5) The second identity follows from the proof of (3.3). Thus the period is an ordinary derivative of an algebraic response function, specified by finite matrices and a fixed source. The positive gradient flow y'=-(P_r+zQ_r)y+g_r solves (5.4) for each fixed N; its existence is not an assumption about a chosen knot state. The source dependence can also be retained in a positive spectral measure. Set H=P_r^(-1/2)Q_r P_r^(-1/2), u=P_r^(-1/2)g_r. For its orthonormal eigenbasis H e_a=h_a e_a put w_a=|e_a^dagger u|^2. Then exactly Phi_N(z)=sum_a w_a z h_a/(1+z h_a), G_N=sum_a w_a h_a, sum_a w_a=beta=O(1). (5.6) All h_a,w_a are nonnegative. The response is increasing and concave in z. The weights record the original source and cannot be dropped in favor of an extremal eigenvalue. Equations (5.4)--(5.6) supply an actual quantum variational problem and its rigid algebraic response for arbitrary knots. Relating this response to the geometric angle-volume optimization and proving its exponential rate remain the geometric part of the conjecture. ## 6. The desired A-polynomial/volume identity, with the original invariant The independently proved positive ordinary-color bound in [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md#2-a-positive-trace-bounds-all-the-ordinary-colors) gives |C_j(q_N)|=O_K(N^(b-1)) for 1<=j<N, where b is any fixed knot-braid strand count. Therefore G_N(A,j_*)=|<K>_N|^2+O_K(N^(2b-1)), G_N(A,j_*)>=|<K>_N|^2. (6.1) This is also the earlier positive cyclic trace norm H_N, with its fixed small-color prefix removed: G_N(A,j_*)=N H_N-sum_(j=1)^(j_*-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2. The new content relative to that norm formulation is the explicit positive polynomial-coefficient ratio from the actual operator, its uniformly bounded banded jet lattice and its response function. No new knot state is being introduced. For a hyperbolic knot with positive volume V, its original volume conjecture is consequently equivalent to the polynomial-period identity lim_(N->infinity) (pi/N) log G_N(A,j_*)=V. (6.2) Equivalently the marked regulator norm of the existing torsor gives (2/N)log G_N(A,j_*)-log||P_hyp|| ->0, log||P_hyp||=2V/pi. (6.3) The equivalence uses only the polynomial remainder in (6.1): a positive exponential norm dominates that remainder in either direction. It does not presume that <K>_N is eventually nonzero. If (6.2) were proved, eventual nonvanishing would follow from (6.1). This is a positive determinant-period formulation with the actual quantum A-operator on the left, the original finite pointing retained, and no restriction on bridge number or alternatingness. It is an exact algebraic reduction of the required theorem, not a proof of its exponential estimate. That estimate and its link with the geometric A-curve's marked regulator are still necessary. Fixed bandwidth and polynomial matrix entries alone do not imply a polynomial bound on (3.2): a constant-coefficient recurrence y_j=c y_(j-1) already has a determinant ratio growing as sum |c|^(2j). Small singular values and the source border can encode an exponential rate. No estimate of those determinants is inferred from their construction or from positivity. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_a_gram_period.py). [Results](../experiments/pointed_a_gram_period_results.json). The subsequent [tempered leading-divisor theorem](tempered_a_growth_bound.md) gives a one-sided exponential estimate for this period under its explicit operator hypotheses. It proves the complete leading-germ normalization and a direct matrix-product upper bound through eigenvalue collisions. Its largest-root integral is not identified with the selected volume; the source and sharp lower estimate remain.

title: A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source
text: # A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. There is an explicit whole algebraic unfolding of the original cyclic boundary. Allow its cyclic repair to acquire a characteristic polynomial, while keeping the actual highest vector, normalized output row and aligned rank-one multiplicative relation. The resulting sourced moduli chart is a principal open subset of affine (N-1)-space over the Q-line. Every matrix and the full co-source have polynomial formulas. A unipotent conjugation, requiring no quantum-gap division, trivializes the clock and retains the residual spectral polynomial in the transformed co-source. This is a source-specific chart of the existing framed multiplicative-commutator problem. It is not a new definition of the knot invariant, nor a proof that its residual polynomial is the knot's geometric A-polynomial. That requires the actual crossing-word and peripheral transport. ## 1. Keep the source and relax just the fixed cyclic polynomial Let R be any commutative coefficient ring and Q a unit. Let E be locally free of rank N, N at least two. Consider invertible X,Y, a vector v, and rows w,ell satisfying Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse=I+v w, (1) Xv=v, ell v=1, ell Y=ell. (2) Require the actual source-orbit chart: v,Yv,...,Y^(N-1)v is a basis. These hypotheses retain the normalized source v ell; in particular its image is aligned with the moment vector v. They relax the additional actual finite-head equation Y^N=I. The row w in (1) is the moment covector; ell is the original co-source and must not be replaced by w. In this canonical basis write Y e_j=e_(j+1), 0<=j<N-1, Y e_(N-1)=sum_(i=0)^(N-1) t_i e_i. (3) Then t_0 is a unit, ell=(1,...,1), and sum_i t_i=1. (4) Conversely choose arbitrary t_1,...,t_(N-1), set t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i and invert t_0. Define x_0=1 and x_m=(1-Q^m)t_(N-m) +sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l, 1<=m<N. (5) The UNIQUE possible clock is X_(i,j)=Q^i x_(j-i) if i<=j, and zero if i>j. (6) It is invertible: det X=Q^(N(N-1)/2). The unique row w is the zeroth row of Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse minus I. All other rows of that matrix vanish. Consequently (3)-(6) are a complete construction and classification over R, including bases with nilpotents. They do not require Q^N-1 or any 1-Q^j to be invertible. Here is the entry proof. Equations (2) and cyclicity first fix the zeroth column of X and the row ell. Equation (1) is equivalent to saying that XY-QYX has image in Rv. In its nonzero-index rows, the first N-1 columns force (6) inductively: until the final column the additional companion term contains X_(N-1,j)=0. For i=N-m>0 the final-column equation, divided only by the unit Q^i, is x_m=sum_(l=0)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l-Q^m t_(N-m), which is exactly (5). Conversely that recurrence kills every nonzero-index row. Invertibility of X,Y then gives (1) and w. The final-column output equation ell Y=ell is precisely (4). Thus the sourced quotient in this cyclic chart is EXACTLY Spec R[t_1,...,t_(N-1), (1-sum_(i>0)t_i) inverse]. (7) If a free basis of E is included in the data, the representation chart is GL_N times (7). There are no residual stabilizers: an automorphism fixing Y and v fixes its full cyclic basis. In particular the sourced chart is smooth and flat over the whole Q-unit base, of relative dimension N-1. This follows from the displayed coordinate ring, not from a nonroot generic smoothness theorem. The surrounding [framed moment scheme](actual_resonant_framed_moment_smoothness.md) also has a direct root Jacobian proof and a cyclic-vector quotient of relative dimension 2N. The present formulas describe its full sourced subchart globally, rather than merely near that root. ## 2. The pointed spectral factor and a polynomial Hilbert-90 gauge The companion characteristic polynomial and its reversed form are chi(z)=z^N-sum_i t_i z^i, h(z)=z^N chi(1/z) =1-sum_(m=1)^N t_(N-m)z^m. (8) Because chi(1)=0, there are monic and constant-one polynomials chi_red and h_red, respectively, with chi(z)=(z-1)chi_red(z), h(z)=(1-z)h_red(z), h_red(z)=z^(N-1)chi_red(1/z). (9) Let L be the actual finite lowering shift, L e_j=e_(j-1) for j>0 and L e_0=0. Thus L^N=0. Put B=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)), G=h(L). (10) G is upper unipotent, with polynomial inverse: its nonconstant part is nilpotent. Equations (5)-(6) imply the exact WHOLE identity X=G B G inverse. (11) To verify this without matrix inversion, let x(z)=sum_(m=0)^(N-1)x_m z^m. Recurrence (5) is equivalent to h(z)x(z)=h(Qz) modulo z^N. Thus X=B h(QL)h(L) inverse. Since B L B inverse=Q inverse L, B h(QL)=h(L)B, which proves (11). This is an explicit finite polynomial coboundary, rather than a comparison obtained after truncating a quantum jet or choosing a singular eigenbasis. In particular no factors 1-Q^j or 1-Q^N have been canceled. The source is transported exactly as well: G inverse v=v, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). (12) Indeed Gv=v and ell(I-L)=e_0^t, while (9) holds at L. Therefore the coefficients of the residual spectral factor remain in the actual transformed co-source. For every whole operator C, ell C v=[e_0^t h_red(L)] [G inverse C G] v. (13) The new transport is G inverse Y G, and every crossing, cap and inserted current has to be conjugated with it. Trivializing X alone does not erase the co-source polynomial. If the original period carries an external peripheral/dimension line, retain that SAME line on both sides of (13), including its norm-zero ratios. ## 3. The actual finite head is a regular section, not a singular limit The actual data are recovered by EQUALITY at t_0=1, t_i=0 for i>0, chi(z)=z^N-1, h(z)=1-z^N, h_red(z)=1+z+...+z^(N-1). (14) Then G=I, X=B, Y=P is the original cyclic repair, and w=(Q^-N-1)e_0^t, ell=e_0^t sum_(j=0)^(N-1)L^j=(1,...,1). (15) This is exactly the original orbit co-source of [the moment/source theorem](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). The finite head itself still uses its two explicit endpoint deletions; unfolding P has not changed those actual matrices. Conversely Y^N=I FORCES (14): applying it to v and using its cyclic basis gives t_0=1 and t_i=0 for i>0. This works over every commutative base, without a distinct-eigenvalue or characteristic zero hypothesis. The fixed cyclic source is cut out by the N-1 ordinary coordinate equations t_i=0 in the smooth chart (7). It is a flat section over Q. The earlier aligned rigidity theorem is precisely this section, with the defect projector retained. The determinant of (1) supplies another retained character: 1+w v=Q^-N. (16) At a primitive N-th root the matrix v w therefore has square zero, even when w is nonzero elsewhere on the unfolded fiber. The actual section has w=0 there, and its divided normal still recovers e_0 e_0^t. Square-zero boundary monodromy does not imply nilpotence of the full braid image; the previously proved semisimple braid sector is unaffected. ## 4. Finitely many mixed source moments recover the polynomial This chart has a concrete comparison test. The uninserted source moments ell Y^j v are all one, so they cannot distinguish ANY of the residual spectral polynomials. Keep the clock insertion and define instead m_j=ell X Y^j v, 0<=j<N, m_0=1. The canonical columns give m_j=sum_(l=0)^j Q^(j-l)x_l, x_j=m_j-Qm_(j-1), 1<=j<N. (17) If the usual finite-head units 1-Q^m, 1<=m<N, are inverted, equation (5) then gives the UNIQUE recursive reconstruction t_(N-m)=[x_m-sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l]/(1-Q^m). (18) Finally t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i. The mixed moment map is therefore a polynomial coordinate change over this head localization, with polynomial inverse there; it is not just a pointwise injectivity assertion. The determinant of its Jacobian, in the ordered variables t_(N-1),...,t_1, is exactly product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m), (19) because (5) is triangular in this order and (17) is unit triangular. At a primitive N-th root (19) is N. These formulas construct a finite algebraic test for a proposed source-transport comparison and retain its whole normal derivatives. They do not yield a uniform bound on the inverse matrix's condition number; its other entries depend on the retained polynomial. For the actual fixed finite repair P one simply has m_j=Q^j and recovers chi=z^N-1. A different polynomial cannot be assigned to that same transport by relabeling its spectral factor. An actual quantum meridian transport would have to supply its own mixed moments and satisfy the sourced equations before this test could be applied to it. ## 5. What this gives to the A-torsor program There is now a fully explicit algebraic sourced family, its spectral polynomial with a FORCED pointed factor z-1, and a whole comparison carrying the remaining polynomial into the co-source. This supplies functions and a flat scheme before quantum jets. It also makes precise why an unpointed spectral equation and a bare diagonal clock omit selected-period data. Nothing here identifies chi_red with A_K. The coefficients t_i are arbitrary source-transport coordinates until an ACTUAL crossing word or quantum meridian transport produces them. No such new transport is substituted for the original P. The identity (13) compares a given full operator exactly; it does not determine its scalar period or give a growing-N norm bound. An upper-unipotent gauge can have large condition number, so its determinant one is not a subexponential estimate. In particular [the actual Fourier cancellation theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) continues to apply. A nonzero formal block with the regulator action can lie in the zero-source current sector. To prove the volume conjecture the actual word class, source polynomial and independent normal/norm divisors must be carried into the marked regulator period. The present theorem is an exact algebraic source unfolding and polynomial comparison; it does not prove that final selected norm. The underlying multiplicative-commutator terminology is covered by [Chalykh--Fairon's one-loop quiver presentation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1704.05814). Only its defining equation is used; the classification and all gauge/source formulas above follow from the entry proof. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_companion_source_shell.py) and [saved results](../experiments/companion_source_shell_results.json) check the universal formulas at six symbolic levels and twelve full generic/primitive-root moment fibers. The [independent proof audit](companion_source_shell_independent_audit.md) checks the chart, periodic section, polynomial gauge and retained co-source separately. The [actual meridian compatibility audit](actual_meridian_companion_source_compatibility.md) now proves a universal mismatch if one tries to use the invariant's meridian orbit state directly as this normalized highest source. Its canonical highest residual has pairing K_N. This chart remains a comparison tool; a division by that unknown value cannot serve as the requested geometric-period proof.

title: Markov reduction of the actual source and its geometric determinant line
text: # Markov reduction of the actual source and its geometric determinant line Research note, 26 October 2026. This continues the invariant's own quantum A/torsor program. The source is the original reduced Kashaev/ADO cut. No comparison with Jones, a custom state, or a published regulator theorem is used. We prove an exact finite source contraction, a uniform geometric Gaussian reduction, and explicit Markov chain equivalences for the linearized holonomy complex. The selected global period's volume norm remains unproved. **Uniform compatibility theorem.** Let beta be any braid whose closure is a knot, at any N>=2 with the original quantum cut normalization. For either Markov stabilization: 1. The actual finite cut contracts exactly to the old cut as a whole meridian germ, with its full modified dimension. 2. At every nondegenerate geometric critical chart, the added quadratic period complex is the old complex plus one explicit acyclic rank-one pair. Its variable principal amplitude cancels the determinant of that pair. 3. At every irreducible fixed-trace representation with ker(dF-I) equal to the infinitesimal conjugation orbit, the linearized holonomy complex is the old one plus an explicit acyclic rank-two pair, and its torsion is unchanged. It is also invariant under braid conjugation and braid relations. The proof below has arbitrary N, braid and representation. The finite computations in the audit validate the formulas; they are not the proof or an assumption on knot examples. This is a uniform structural lemma for the intended volume theorem, not the volume theorem itself. ## 1. The full finite source has an exact contraction Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, the original checked crossings B_+,B_-=B_+^(-1), pivot g=K^(1-N), and theta=x^(1-N). For every N>=2 and every whole color germ, ptr_g(B_+)=theta I, ptr_g(B_-)=theta^(-1)I. (1.1) Thus the zero-framed Markov contraction is identity. The full modified dimension d_N(M) on the remaining cut is unchanged; no peripheral factor is evaluated separately. Here is a coefficient proof, in the original finite basis. It uses the independently derived coefficients in [the actual crossing note](relative_octahedral_period.md#1-exact-formulas-for-both-actual-crossings). Integer-index conservation makes either partial trace diagonal. For the positive crossing, write k=a-b. Its diagonal entry divided by theta is x^(-2a) Q^(a(a-1)) sum_(k=0)^a (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2+(1-a)k) {a choose k}_Q (t;Q)_k, t=Q^(1-a)x^2. (1.2) The sum equals t^a. To prove this, expand t^a in the Newton basis P_k=(t;Q)_k and use t P_k=Q^(-k)(P_k-P_(k+1)). Induction and the Gaussian binomial recursion give precisely the coefficients in (1.2). Its prefactor cancels t^a, proving the first identity. For the negative crossing put n=N-1-a. Root reflection gives {a+k choose k}_Q =(-1)^k Q^(ak+k(k+1)/2){n choose k}_Q. Invert the k Pochhammer factors. With w=Q^a x^(-2), the remaining diagonal sum becomes x^(2a+1-N) Q^(-a(a+1)) sum_(k=0)^n {n choose k}_Q w^(-k)(w;Q)_k. The last sum is w^(-n). Equivalently, sum_k {n choose k}_Q w^(n-k)(w;Q)_k=1; induction follows from {n+1 choose k}_Q=Q^k{n choose k}_Q+{n choose k-1}_Q and P_(k+1)=(1-wQ^k)P_k. The x exponent is then N-1 and the remaining Q exponent is -aN. This proves the second identity in (1.1), for the whole meridian function. ## 2. The regular geometric contraction has one critical variable Use the actual balanced coefficients, with position variables A,B, transfer C and Y=M^2, as in [the principal density calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md). Closing the added strand imposes B=A/C for B_+, B=AC for B_-. The original internal shift ratios give the respective stationary multipliers R_+=-(1-YC/A)(1-B)/[B(1-C)], R_-=(1-AC)(1-Y/B)/[A(1-C)]. On the nondegenerate chart R_sign=1 has the unique solution D=1+Y-A, C_+=A D/Y, C_-=Y/(A D), B_+=B_-=Y/D. (2.1) The excluded factors are actual chart divisors, including A=1,Y and D=0; they are not deleted from the quantum source. Let c=Log C and hold a=Log A fixed. The trace-phase Hessian in its single remaining internal variable is h_+=D^2/[(A-1)(A-Y)], h_-=-h_+. (2.2) These follow by taking (0,-1,1) and (0,1,1) directional derivatives in (Log A,Log B,Log C) of the actual phase Hessian. They are units on the stated regular chart. The original principal amplitudes include their closing pivot and zero-framing factors. Their squares are b_+^2=a_+^2/B^2, b_-^2=Y^2 a_-^2/B^2. Substitution of (2.1) gives exactly b_+^2=h_+, b_-^2=h_-, b_sign^2/(-h_sign)=-1. (2.3) Thus all input- and meridian-dependent factors cancel from the one-variable Gaussian contraction. The remaining minus sign belongs to the fixed Gaussian/quantum normalization line; it is not a new adjustable peripheral multiplier. The full finite normalization is fixed by (1.1). We retain that line rather than evaluating an infinite compact product at a root of unity. The cut-momentum and meridian character multipliers both equal one at (2.1). This follows by multiplying the two input shift ratios for the former and substituting in the actual meridian half-step ratio for the latter. Locally the critical phase therefore differs by a base-only term and integer stationary windings. Those windings are retained characters equal to one on the actual integer lattice. The base-only term has its specified original normalization. ## 3. An explicit map on the quadratic period complexes Let X be the old phase coordinates and let v be the column derivative of c_sign(A(X),Y). For a fixed meridian, partial_(Log A)c_sign =sign*(1+Y-2A)/D. After the stated integer flattening, the critical added phase has no X-dependent value. Its Hessian adjoining the old quadratic form H is consequently H_new=[H+h v v^t -h v; -h v^t h]. (3.1) The unit-determinant change c_tilde=c-c_sign(X) gives U=[I 0;v^t 1], U^t H_new U=diag(H,h). (3.2) This is a chain equivalence of the two-term quadratic complexes. It identifies the old kernel with the graph (xi,v^t xi) and adds the acyclic pair [k --h--> k]. The determinant factor is h. Equation (2.3) supplies its actual amplitude correction, including the universal sign. This proves stabilization compatibility of the variable geometric normal determinant line for every regular irreducible critical representation. It is not a claim that the selected global relative cycle has already been pushed through an arbitrary pole divisor. ## 4. Markov chain equivalences for the holonomy complex We can now prove that the finite-dimensional scalar in the [density note, equation (6.4)](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md#an-invariant-finite-dimensional-complex-for-the-reduction) is invariant under Markov moves on its regular locus. Let X be the product of the noncentral fixed-trace meridian classes. At an irreducible fixed point H of the Hurwitz map F, use 0 -> sl_2 --a--> T_H X --(dF-I)--> T_H X --m--> sl_2 -> 0, a(xi)=([xi,H_j])_j, m(V)=dP(V)P^(-1), P=H_b...H_1. (4.1) It is acyclic when ker(dF-I)=im a. The earlier note proves injectivity of a, surjectivity of m and the well-defined torsion T_beta=det[a,V]/det[(dF-I)V,W], mW=I. For stabilization put A=H_b and append a new meridian Z. Writing G=F(H), the two extended maps are F_+(H,Z)=(G_<b, G_b^(-1) Z G_b, G_b), F_-(H,Z)=(G_<b, Z, Z G_b Z^(-1)). Their fixed-point schemes are exactly F(H)=H,Z=H_b. This follows by eliminating Z directly and holds over Artin rings, not just on reduced points. At such a point write w=(dF(V))_b and use the domain coordinate u=z-w. In the output use V'_b=V_b+Ad_(A^(-1)) z, V'_<b=V_<b, keeping the new last coordinate z. Both are triangular changes of determinant one. The middle differential becomes diag(dF-I,-I) for F_+, diag(dF-I,-Ad_A|_(T_A orbit)) for F_-. (4.2) The infinitesimal conjugation maps to (a,0). The extended product is P_new=Z P, and its transformed last map is m_new(V',z)=Ad_A m(V'). (4.3) Indeed the z term in d(ZP)(ZP)^(-1) cancels precisely against the correction in V'_b. Equations (4.2)--(4.3) are an explicit chain equivalence with the old complex and one acyclic two-dimensional pair. Both Ad_A on sl_2 and Ad_A on its tangent conjugacy orbit have determinant one; the latter also follows from invariance of dK wedge de/e. The signs in -I have even dimension. Therefore T_(beta stabilized)(H,H_b)=T_beta(H) (4.4) for either sign, and regularity is preserved. Braid conjugation is also a chain equivalence: a Hurwitz coordinate change is equivariant and preserves P. Its derivative changes both middle bases equally, so the torsion ratio is unchanged. Braid relations are identities of the Hurwitz maps. Thus this scalar is invariant under the braid presentation moves, with its meridian trace and irreducible representation marked. No equality with a separately defined Reidemeister torsion is used or asserted. ## 5. Consequence for the actual A/torsor program The actual finite source contraction, its geometric Gaussian pair, and the holonomy deformation complex now all have explicit stabilization maps. This is a compatibility for structures attached to the same invariant. It avoids assuming that two arbitrary periods with the same A-symbol coincide. The subsequent [uniform principal-density proof](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) now compares the variable Gaussian determinant line with (4.1), including its kernel, cut co-source and explicit presentation-parity character. The base-only quantum normalization line and transport of the selected global relative period remain separate. These local contractions do not prove that its geometric block survives with subexponential comparison factor across levels. That norm statement is still the required volume theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_markov_reduction.py). [Results](../experiments/pointed_markov_reduction_results.json).

title: A pointed Newton--Green bound for the full figure-eight Fourier energy
text: # A pointed Newton--Green bound for the full figure-eight Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The actual affine rank-two figure-eight operator has an exact positive Green presentation in its Newton lattice. Its central determinant is elementary and its boundary-source response has a uniform polynomial bound. Keeping the Newton evaluation metric then gives the sharp upper exponent for the FULL root-color Fourier energy, instead of the doubled largest-root integral of the earlier homogeneous estimate. The Green estimate is uniform for a checkable class of fixed-width boundary sources, with the broader finite-order pointed UL criterion in Section 3.1. Its application to the figure-eight is an independently proved known prototype, not a new knot class. No claim that arbitrary knot A-operators have this Newton form is made. ## 1. The specified ACTUAL affine operator and its Newton lattice Use the already independently derived operator in `peripheral_normal_period.md`, Section 9: C=c_- T^(-1)+c_0+c_+T, T Y=Q Y T, D=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1), g=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2, c_-=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1), c_0=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g, c_+=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). Set Q=exp(2pi i/N), U=Y^N, h=Y+Y^(-1), d=N-1, and a_r=Q^r+Q^(-r), s_r=2-a_r=4sin^2(pi r/N), t_0=1, t_k=product_(r=1)^k(h-a_r), c=t_N=U+U^(-1)-2. (1) The product identity in (1) follows by writing every factor as (Y-Q^r)(1-Q^rY)/(-Q^rY), or by the monic Chebyshev polynomial. For generic U, the conjugates Q^jY+Q^(-j)Y^(-1) are distinct: equality for j!=k would give Y^2=Q^(-j-k), hence U^2=1. Thus the t_0,...,t_d are a basis of the degree-N field extension C(Y)/C(U). Put A=D^(-1)C over this GENERIC field. This division is performed before the complete fiber; D's zeros at special orbit points have not been replaced by numerical values. The rational telescoping certificate gives, exactly, A t_0=3-h, A t_k=-(h-2)(t_k-t_(k-1)), 1<=k<=d. (2) Indeed its certificate coefficient is (Y-1)^2 Q^k/((Y-Q^k)(1-YQ^k))=-(h-2)/(h-a_k). Multiplying by t_k cancels that last factor, including its whole germ. Multiplication by h sends t_k to t_(k+1)+a_(k+1)t_k; at the last column use t_N=c and a_N=2. Therefore A has the following matrix in the Newton basis, with coincident entries added for small N: diagonal: 1+s_(k+1), 0<=k<d; last diagonal 1, subdiagonal: -1, superdiagonal: -s_(k+1), row k, column k+1, extra corner: -c in row 0, column d. (3) Its coefficients are regular in c. This explicitly defines the free Newton lattice through c=0, retaining the double-point jets when the ordinary orbit evaluation basis coalesces. Its generic relation to the actual operator was proved first; (3) is not a replacement quantization. ## 2. Exact central determinant and the retained source All row sums of (3) vanish except the first, which is 1-c. Hence A(c) 1=(1-c)e_0. (4) The determinant is affine in c. The cofactor of the corner (0,d) is exactly one: deleting its row and column leaves an upper triangular matrix with diagonal -1, and the cofactor sign cancels its determinant sign. At c=1, (4) gives a kernel. Consequently, at EVERY level, det A(c)=1-c=3-U-U^(-1), det C=Norm(D)*(3-U-U^(-1)). (5) No large-period or classical-curve assumption enters (5). The original affine source is C F_N=D(3-U-U^(-1)). In this lattice it is exactly (1-c)e_0, so (4) gives its solution with ALL Newton coefficients one. This is the already identified original whole state F_N(Y)=sum_(k=0)^d t_k(Y). (6) The equality with the original knot cut is the earlier all-level four-plat source theorem. No value of K_N was used to normalize A, its source, the determinant, or the Newton basis. ## 3. Uniform Green bound for fixed-width boundary sources At c=0 write A_0=A(0). It is a killed birth-death matrix: its offdiagonal entries are nonpositive, its row sums are zero except the killing rate one at state zero, and every s_r is positive for 1<=r<N. A direct Green formula proves positivity and the quantitative estimate, so no general Markov-chain theorem is needed. Let A_0 v=g. Write w_i=v_i-v_(i-1), 1<=i<=d. Then w_i-s_(i+1)w_(i+1)=g_i, 1<=i<d, w_d=g_d, v_0-s_1 w_1=g_0. (7) Backward substitution gives the inverse. In particular for g=e_j, v_k=product_(r=1)^j s_r +sum_(i=1)^min(k,j) product_(r=i+1)^j s_r, j>=1, A_0^(-1)e_0=1. (8) Empty products equal one. All entries are nonnegative. If g is supported on states 0,...,J, where J is fixed independently of N, then s_r<=4 gives ||A_0^(-1)g||_2 <=sqrt(N)(J+1)^(3/2)4^J ||g||_2. (9) Thus the source-restricted inverse is polynomially bounded, even though the inverse on unrestricted bulk sources can be exponentially large. For general c the exact rank-one formula is A(c)^(-1)g=A_0^(-1)g +[c/(1-c)]1 [e_d^t A_0^(-1)g]. (10) Its only central denominator is the explicit 1-c in (5). This is the boundary matching certificate which a mere half-orbit fold does not automatically provide. The actual source (1-c)e_0 cancels it as a whole and remains exactly (6). ### 3.1 A broader pointed UL criterion The mechanism is not confined to nonnegative coefficients. In fact A_0=T_s(I-S), where S is the nilpotent lower shift and T_s is upper bidiagonal with diagonal one and superdiagonal -s_(k+1). For a boundary-supported source, T_s^(-1) never sends its support past that same fixed boundary window; (I-S)^(-1) then only takes partial sums. Thus (9) remains valid for complex s_r with |s_r|<=4, without a positivity assertion. More generally fix integers r>=1 and J>=0. Suppose an ACTUAL pointed Newton-frame operator is L_N=U_N(I-S_N)^r, (10a) where U_N is upper triangular and invertible. In its first J+1 rows and columns assume |(U_N)_(ij)|<=N^a and |(U_N)_(ii)|>=N^(-a), for a fixed a>=0. For every original source g supported in 0,...,J, ||L_N^(-1)g||_2 <=binom(N+r-1,r)(J+1)^(J+1) N^(a(2J+1))||g||_2. (10b) Proof: the first J+1 coordinate space is invariant under U_N and its inverse, so inversion uses only that finite block. Write its inverse as the finite Neumann sum after separating the diagonal. Its norm is at most (J+1)^(J+1)N^(a(2J+1)). On the other factor, (I-S_N)^(-r)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1)binom(r+k-1,k)S_N^k, whose operator norm is at most binom(N+r-1,r). This proves (10b). Fixed r,J,a give a polynomial bound even if the unrestricted inverse of U_N or L_N is exponential. This is an independently checkable finite-order OPERATOR AND SOURCE condition, not a condition on the desired value. Any comparison to it must preserve the actual boundary source and track its evaluation metric; an exponentially conditioned basis cannot be silently dropped. An additional fixed-rank central boundary update is governed by its explicit Schur matrix I-V^t L_N^(-1)U. Formula (10) is precisely the rank-one instance with Schur factor 1-c. No polynomial inverse of that Schur matrix is asserted without a separate algebraic certificate. ## 4. The actual root metric gives an endpoint barrier The Newton lattice is NOT asserted isometric to the original orbit. Retain its evaluation matrix V_(j,k)=t_k(Q^j), 0<=j,k<N. (11) For j=0, t_k(1)=|F_k|^2, F_k=(Q;Q)_k. For 1<=j<N, t_k(Q^j)=0 if k>=min(j,N-j), |t_k(Q^j)|=|F_(j+k)| / (|1-Q^j| |F_(j-k-1)|) otherwise. (12) This follows by factoring each term into its two sine factors. The ordinary indices in the second line stay between zero and N-1, so no unmarked root wrap or division by F_N occurs. Let J_0(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi t))dt, 0<=x<=1, and put Delta=max J_0-min J_0=2 Lambda(pi/6)/pi. (13) The endpoint-uniform factorial estimate, proved by extracting log t and log(1-t) and applying Stirling to the remainder, is log|F_k|=N J_0(k/N)+O(log N). Also |1-Q^j|>=2sin(pi/N)>=4/N. Equations (12) and the logarithmic endpoint modulus of continuity imply log max_(j,k)|V_(j,k)|<=N Delta+O(log N). (14) At j=0 this uses 2max J_0=Delta; elsewhere it uses the DIFFERENCE of the two endpoint values J_0((j+k)/N)-J_0((j-k-1)/N), bounded by Delta. This is an endpoint barrier, not a full-circle integral of the pointwise largest root. For ANY polynomially bounded fixed-width source g in (9), its Newton response r=A_0^(-1)g has polynomial norm. Keeping (11) gives ||V r||_2^2<=poly(N) exp(2N Delta). (15) The unitary root-color Fourier transform has exactly that same norm. For the actual source r=1, it is the FULL energy E_N=|K_N|^2+sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2, with its original pointing. The independent ordinary-color audit bounds the second term by a polynomial, but (15) already bounds the entire norm directly. The actual marked regulator calibration gives Vol(4_1)=4Lambda(pi/6). Thus (15) yields limsup (pi/N)log E_N<=2pi Delta=Vol(4_1), (16) where the earlier homogeneous largest-root envelope was 2Vol(4_1). For this particular source the positive sum at j=0 also supplies the known matching lower rate by a bulk factorial term. This is a prototype calibration of the Green mechanism, not a new broad-class theorem. ### 4.1 Stress check: the metric estimate is uniform on the whole unit circle The upper exponent is not an artifact of sampling exactly at root nodes. Let G(t)=log|2sin(pi t)|, periodically extended, and let J_0 be its periodic primitive of mean-zero derivative. Uniformly for real u and 0<=k<N, sum_(r=1)^k G(u+r/N) <=N integral_0^(k/N)G(u+s)ds+O(log N). (16a) For completeness, partition the sampled interval into monotonicity pieces of G. Away from the at most bounded number of mesh cells adjacent to a zero of sin, the Riemann-sum error telescopes and is O(log N): the retained cell endpoints are at distance at least 1/N from that zero. In the removed cells every sampled value is at most log 2; the cell integrals are bounded below by -(log N+C)/N, including when a zero lies inside the cell. A sample arbitrarily close to zero can only DECREASE the sum. This proves the one-sided uniform estimate, with no root-separation assumption on u. For Y=exp(2pi i u), the two sine factors in t_k give from (16a) log|t_k(Y)| <=N[J_0(u+k/N)-J_0(u-k/N)]+O(log N) <=N Delta+O(log N), (16b) uniformly on the full unit circle, including all zeros by continuity. Thus the same sharp exponential metric bound applies to the continuous unit-circle Fourier norm as well as the original root-color norm. It also permits fixed q-tags in the arguments without changing the rate. Conversely the complete entry t_k(1)=|F_k|^2 at k/N near 5/6 has rate Delta. Hence the root evaluation matrix itself satisfies lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log||V_N||=Delta. (16c) All exponential scale in this pointed Green example is therefore carried by a specified, quantitatively estimated evaluation metric. It is not hidden by calling the Newton change of basis unitary. ## 5. Checkable class and genuine generalization requirement The estimate (9) is a uniform source-independent theorem for every birth-death matrix (3) with 0<=s_r<=4 and every fixed-width boundary source. The root-metric estimate (15) applies whenever the ACTUAL operator/source has the Newton representation (1)--(3), or a uniformly polynomially conditioned comparison preserving its boundary source and evaluation. Neither hypothesis is an assertion about the unknown scalar. They can be checked by finite operator identities, as above. For a general knot, Weyl symmetry alone neither supplies (3) nor controls a folded boundary determinant. The original ordinary-color bounds fix the polynomial tail, but do not prove that the pointed normal response is a tame boundary-source Green vector in a basis with a controlled geometric evaluation metric. Establishing such a source-exact basis or an analogous multichannel Green estimate would be a substantive next step. No new knot, bridge family, or general volume upper bound is claimed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_newton_green_barrier.py): actual generic-orbit conjugacy including all c/D factors, central determinant, boundary-source Green formulas and bounds, root-evaluation endpoint products, and exact full-energy Plancherel through the original colors.

title: Pointed recoupling and relative period descent
text: # Pointed recoupling and relative period descent Research note, 25 October 2026. This continues the structural program. The result is an exact comparison of selected algebraic vacua, their normalization lines and their classical Bloch labels under recoupling. It applies uniformly to finite recoupling diagrams. The remaining identification with the intrinsic knot period is stated in Section 7. Write C_(s,t) for the explicit pointed factorization in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md`, and set tau(s,t)=(1-st)/(1-t), f(s,t)=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, h=(n-1)/2, det C_(s,t)=f(s,t)^(nh). All formulae are on the nondegenerate parameter locus. Local maps are defined over its algebraic function field and extend wherever their intrinsic sections are regular. No angle-positivity assumption is used. ## 1. The pointing extends to arbitrary matched affine transports The Steinberg family is a normalization of a larger pointed family. Let g=(lambda,mu) be an affine central character with lambda*mu nonzero. Choose nonzero endpoint roots a,b such that b^n=lambda*a^n+mu. On E_(g;a,b)=K[x]/(x^n-lambda), define X f=x f, Y f=(b-a x)f(omega^(-1)x). The norm is b^n-a^n*lambda=mu. The unit is the unique vacuum line for Y+aX-b, since this operator is (b-a x)(sigma^(-1)-1). Rescaling X'=aX/b,Y'=Y/b gives exactly the Steinberg module with parameter lambda*a^n/b^n. For g,h use endpoints c->d and a->c, respectively. Assume also mu_(gh)=mu_g+lambda_g*mu_h is nonzero, so that the composite and relative matrix algebras below are nondegenerate. The tensor coproduct preserves the pointing of their composite a->d: L_tot=L_g+X_1 L_h, f(x) -> f(x_1x_2). This follows from c matching on the two factors. The injections are strictly coassociative. Thus the pointed construction is not confined to affine characters fixing the point one. The same relative operators Z=Y_1Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=ZX_2 have central character lambda_rel=mu_(gh)/mu_h, mu_rel=-mu_g*lambda_h/mu_h. Their compatible endpoints are c/a -> d/a. With L_rel=-C+(c/a)D-d/a, L_tot=L_g+X_1 L_h, L_rel=(L_g-Z L_h)/a, L_h=D^(-1)(L_tot-a L_rel). (1.1) These are exact identities at indeterminate quantum parameter. Normalizing the two endpoint modules gives the earlier C_(s,t), with s=lambda_g*c^n/d^n and t=lambda_h*a^n/c^n. The resulting factorization therefore preserves the selected unit, with all endpoint scalars known. For the unscaled monomial bases its determinant is [a^n*lambda_h*mu_(gh)/mu_h^2]^(nh). (1.2) Indeed the target basis rescaling has determinant (a/d)^(n^2 h), the source rescaling has determinant (ac/d^2)^(n^2 h), and f(s,t)=lambda_h*mu_(gh)*(ac/d)^n/mu_h^2. Substitution in the previous determinant formula gives (1.2). ## 2. The Racah map is the same explicit pointed factorization Consider three Steinberg modules E_r tensor E_s tensor E_t, with all nonempty consecutive products different from zero and one. Put a=tau(rs,t), b=tau(r,s), c=tau(r,st), d=tau(s,t). Then cd=a and tau(c,d)=b. Order the left decomposition as E_(rst) tensor E_a tensor E_b, and the right as E_(rst) tensor E_c tensor E_d. Their evaluation maps are I_L=(C_(r,s) tensor 1) P_23 (C_(rs,t) tensor 1), I_R=(1 tensor C_(s,t)) (C_(r,st) tensor 1). Here P_23 is the literal vector-space permutation. Exactly I_L=I_R (1 tensor C_(c,d)). (2.1) In particular the recoupling maps the product of the two distinguished multiplicity vacua to their product, with coefficient one. For a proof uniform in the quantum parameter, write Y_12=X_1Y_2+Y_1, Y_23=X_2Y_3+Y_2, Y_123=X_1X_2Y_3+X_1Y_2+Y_1. The two left relative pairs A,B and two right pairs C,D have X_A=Y_123 Y_3^(-1), X_B=Y_12 Y_2^(-1), X_C=Y_123 Y_23^(-1), X_D=Y_23 Y_3^(-1), Y_A=-Y_12 Y_3^(-1)X_3, Y_B=-Y_1Y_2^(-1)X_2, Y_C=-Y_1Y_23^(-1)X_2X_3, Y_D=-Y_2Y_3^(-1)X_3. Keeping these orders, direct multiplication gives X_A=X_C X_D, Y_A=X_C Y_D+Y_C, X_B=X_C+Y_CY_D^(-1), Y_B=-Y_CY_D^(-1)X_D. (2.2) For the first identity the intermediate Y_23 cancels. For the third, 1+X_2Y_3Y_2^(-1)=Y_23Y_2^(-1); the others follow by the same ordered products. These are exactly the two-factor factorization formulae of C_(c,d). Both sides of (2.1) preserve the unit in all three factors and intertwine the same full matrix algebra. The pointed uniqueness theorem proves equality, including its scalar. This identifies a recoupling operator with the explicit q-factorial kernel, rather than only defining it as a ratio of unspecified maps. ## 3. The normalization cocycle and the permutation sign The units obey the rational identity f(c,d)=-f(r,s)f(rs,t)/[f(r,st)f(s,t)]. (3.1) Let gamma_(s,t)^n=f(s,t)^(-h), so gamma C has determinant one. Put Gamma_L=gamma_(r,s)gamma_(rs,t) and Gamma_R=gamma_(r,st)gamma_(s,t). The recoupling from these normalized tree evaluations is exactly F_hat=(Gamma_L/Gamma_R) C_(c,d). (3.2) Its determinant is (-1)^h, not necessarily one. This is forced by the single permutation P_23 in (2.1): the flip on two n-dimensional factors, and its tensor extension, both have determinant (-1)^h for odd n. Dropping that sign would give a false normalization law. If one independently normalizes C_(c,d) by gamma_(c,d), the ratio epsilon=Gamma_L/[Gamma_R*gamma_(c,d)] satisfies epsilon^n=(-1)^h. For a Racah normalization with its correct signed determinant, take eta_(c,d)^n=(-1)^h*f(c,d)^(-h). Then Gamma_L/[Gamma_R*eta_(c,d)] is mu_n-valued. (3.3) It is constant on each irreducible lifted parameter component. This proves the rigidity statement with its actual hypotheses and records the root phase, rather than canceling it at a special value. ## 4. Descent of the selected finite period on a recoupling diagram For any binary tree T, iterating the pointed C maps gives an evaluation I_T into the same tensor product of leaf modules. It is invertible and takes the product vacuum to the product vacuum. For two trees the transition is I_(T')^(-1)I_T. Consequently F_(T',T'') F_(T,T')=F_(T,T''), and every loop is the identity. This proves exact pointed coherence, including the pentagon and disjoint recouplings. If the node maps are multiplied by their specified roots gamma, let Gamma_T be their product. The transition becomes F_hat_(T,T')=(Gamma_T/Gamma_(T'))F_(T,T'). (4.1) All higher coherence still holds by cancellation. The normalized product vacuum is transported with precisely this scalar. Thus the selected line, not just the unpointed module, descends on this recoupling groupoid with its normalization line. The conclusion is stable under every finite exterior contraction: a matrix identity may be tensored with any exterior tensors and paired along any chosen indices, retaining the same scalar. Sums are finite, so no face-rank or convergence assumption enters this step. It includes scalar periods and open boundary tensors, and does not require the resulting period to be nonzero. These are algebraic identities on their common parameter cover. They extend to every regular specialization of the corresponding sections. Generic units must first be retained and canceled in that identity; specializing a displayed fraction at a pole is not a definition of its section. ## 5. The Bloch label is the tetrahedral cross-ratio For the four cumulative points p_0=1, p_1=r, p_2=rs, p_3=rst, the cross-ratio in the recorded convention is z(r,s,t)=(1-rs)(1-st)/[(1-rst)(1-s)] =b/c=tau(c,d)/c. (5.1) Thus the recoupling has a natural tetrahedral Bloch label. Four consecutive parameters give five cumulative points; their alternating tetrahedral boundary is [z(s,t,u)]-[z(rs,t,u)]+[z(r,st,u)] -[z(r,s,tu)]+[z(r,s,t)]=0. (5.2) This is the same five-point relation established in the Bloch note, by deleting each of the five vertices. The classical regulator and the quantum pointed recoupling therefore have compatible local coherence diagrams. Equating their *global period classes* still requires the comparison in Section 7. ## 6. Intrinsic normalization lines from spinor brackets The extra affine-frame data in f must be distinguished from the cross-ratio (5.1). For four nonzero affine coordinates p_i, direct substitution gives the Racah unit f_R=-p_1p_2(p_0-p_2)(p_1-p_3) /[p_0p_3(p_1-p_2)^2]. (6.1) Choose nonzero homogeneous flag vectors v_i in K^2, and set lambda_ij=det(v_i,v_j). In the affine frame v_i=(p_i,1), remove the displayed vertex-frame factor to obtain f_bar=-lambda_02 lambda_13/lambda_12^2. (6.2) This is GL(2)-invariant. Under v_i -> a_i v_i it is multiplied by a_0a_3/(a_1a_2), so it is intrinsically a section of a decoration line, rather than an invariant number after forgetting those lines. The cross-ratio and its complement are z=lambda_02 lambda_13/(lambda_03 lambda_12), 1-z=-lambda_01 lambda_23/(lambda_03 lambda_12), by the elementary Plucker relation. Their n-th roots give the local Fermat norm cover on this flag torsor. There is also an exact shared-face normalization. On an ordered triangle put q_ijk=lambda_ik/lambda_jk^2. With the usual multiplicative coboundary, f_bar(0123)=-(delta q)(0123)^(-1). (6.3) Choose roots alpha_ijk^n=q_ijk^h on faces and define the tetrahedral root eta_0123=(delta alpha)(0123). Then eta_0123^n=(-1)^h*f_bar(0123)^(-h), (6.4) the signed Racah normalization of Section 3. Sharing the face roots, rather than choosing unrelated tetrahedral roots, makes their product over a 3-chain equal to the face product over its boundary. Interior face roots cancel. On the boundary of a 4-simplex it is one because delta^2=1. This proves strict compatibility of these scalar normalization sections with the five-term relation. The statement is valid for actual equivariant vector flags or for sections of their decoration lines with the corresponding transition functions. A PSL(2) lifting obstruction or nontrivial peripheral characters must remain in those line transitions; they are not set to one by choosing an affine chart. Such data can leave peripheral factors after gluing, exactly where a generic unit can specialize to a numerical multiplier. ## 7. The remaining global theorem We have proved selected-vacuum coherence on the recoupling parameter groupoid, algebraic transport through arbitrary finite exterior contractions, and relative descent of its normalization line on decorated flag charts. The local Bloch label has the same five-point coherence. These statements are uniform and use no knot census. The subsequent `affine_frame_period_transport.md` and `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` prove full matrix/frame covariance on the specified local root covers. They also prove that the selected unit must generally be transported to a nonconstant vector. A global knot period still needs an intrinsic decorated-character gluing construction, its peripheral lifts and its selected period class matched with the literature state. The exact local Faddeev comparison does not by itself identify that global cycle. The regulator comparison across levels also remains necessary for the volume conjecture.

title: Pointed Steinberg modules and a basis-free pentagon
text: # Pointed Steinberg modules and a basis-free pentagon Research note, 25 October 2026. This develops the algebraic recoupling theory suggested by the period torsor, rather than another knot case. Cyclic 6j-symbols already have this origin: Kashaev, [Quantum Dilogarithm as a 6j-Symbol](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147). The proofs below are direct; no novelty is claimed for the categorical pentagon. A particular published matrix normalization is not assumed. The subsequent [integral extension](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) extends the local algebraic factorization to every level, supplies the even-level determinant sign, and computes the recoupling lattice at simultaneous nilpotent degeneration. Its endpoint chain also accounts for the actual quantum-group Borel coproduct. The odd-level analytic and global normalization conventions below are not automatically extended by that local calculation. ## 1. A rigid local vacuum Fix odd n and a primitive n-th root omega in a characteristic-zero field K. For t and 1-t nonzero use the split cyclic algebra and module A_t=K<X,Y>/(XY=omega YX, X^n=t, Y^n=1-t), E_t=K[x]/(x^n-t), X f(x)=x f(x), Y f(x)=(1-x)f(omega^(-1)x). The norm identity in `heisenberg_period_torsor.md` proves the splitting. Its distinguished vector is the unit 1, since (X+Y-1)f=(1-x)[f(omega^(-1)x)-f(x)]. (1.1) As 1-x is a unit, the kernel is exactly K*1. Therefore X+Y-1 has rank n-1, and a -> a.1 identifies the pointed module with (E_t,1)=(A_t/A_t(X+Y-1),[1]). (1.2) A cyclic-dilogarithm matrix is a change between frames of this algebraic vacuum, rather than an additional choice of an analytic solution. Its determinant-normalized frames require the preceding Heisenberg cover. This module is the local Faddeev difference module itself. In the previously audited functional equation set q=exp(2pi i b^2), X=-q^(-1/2)exp(2pi b Z), (Y f)(Z)=f(Z-i b), where q^(-1/2)=exp(-pi i b^2). Then XY=qYX and exactly (X+Y-1)Phi_b=0. For b^2=1/n with odd n, X^n=exp(2pi sqrt(n) Z)=t and the dual functional equation gives Y^n Phi_b=(1-t)Phi_b. Moreover Y[f(X)Phi_b]=(1-X)f(q^(-1)X)Phi_b. Thus its central fibre is precisely (E_t,1), under f(x) -> f(X)Phi_b. This identifies the operator, parameter and vacuum, without an analytic limiting argument. The remaining central period multiplier is fixed by the exact identity in `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md`; the module relation alone does not determine that multiplier. ## 2. Coproduct and central characters Use the quantum affine bialgebra B=K<X,X^(-1),Y>/(XY=omega YX), Delta X=X tensor X, Delta Y=X tensor Y+Y tensor 1. Multiplication verifies the relation after Delta. Both iterated coproducts send Y to X tensor X tensor Y+X tensor Y tensor 1+Y tensor 1 tensor 1, so Delta is coassociative exactly. The nondegenerate central fibre X^n=lambda,Y^n=mu is a full n by n matrix algebra after a splitting extension. The root-of-unity q-binomial identity gives (Delta X)^n=lambda_1 lambda_2, (Delta Y)^n=mu_1+lambda_1 mu_2. (2.1) This also holds for composite n: the intermediate q-binomial coefficients vanish because 1-omega^j is nonzero for 0<j<n. Thus central characters multiply by the affine-group law (lambda,mu)*(lambda',mu') =(lambda lambda',mu+lambda mu'). The Steinberg subfamily closes as (s,1-s)*(t,1-t)=(st,1-st). For it there is a canonical pointed B-linear injection m_(s,t):E_(st)->E_s tensor E_t, f(x)->f(x_1 x_2). (2.2) For Y the two terms combine to [x_1(1-x_2)+(1-x_1)]f(omega^(-1)x_1x_2), proving the assertion. These maps are strictly coassociative by substitution of x_1x_2x_3. ## 3. A pointed factorization with an explicit ideal certificate Assume s,t,1-s,1-t,1-st nonzero. In A_s tensor A_t put X_tot=X_1 X_2, Y_tot=X_1 Y_2+Y_1, Z=Y_1 Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=Z X_2, tau=(1-st)/(1-t). The quantum torus relations alone imply X_tot Y_tot=omega Y_tot X_tot, DC=omega CD, [X_tot,D]=[X_tot,C]=[Y_tot,D]=[Y_tot,C]=0. Moreover X_tot^n=st, Y_tot^n=1-st, D^n=tau, (-C)^n=1-tau. (3.1) For the last pair, X_1Z=omega ZX_1, Z^n=(1-s)/(1-t), and C^n=t(1-s)/(1-t). Oddness gives (-C)^n=-C^n. These exhibit commuting copies of A_(st), A_tau. Their unital map from the simple matrix algebra A_(st) tensor A_tau is injective after a splitting extension and both sides have dimension n^4. The equality descends: A_s tensor A_t = A_(st) tensor A_tau. (3.2) The vacuum is preserved. Write L_i=X_i+Y_i-1. The exact identities are L_tot=X_tot+Y_tot-1=L_1+X_1 L_2, L_rel=D-C-1=L_1-Z L_2, (3.3) L_2=D^(-1)(L_tot-L_rel), L_1=L_tot-X_1 D^(-1)(L_tot-L_rel). Thus the generated left ideals coincide. These identities hold even at generic quantum parameter in the localized quantum torus; the root-of-unity equations (3.1) identify its finite central fibres. There is consequently a unique isomorphism of pointed modules C_(s,t):E_(st) tensor E_tau -> E_s tensor E_t, C_(s,t)(1 tensor 1)=1 tensor 1, (3.4) intertwining the two commuting algebras (3.2). Explicitly send x^a y^b to X_tot^a D^b(1 tensor 1). The factorized common vacuum kernel has dimension one and (3.3) puts the old unit in it. Simplicity and equal dimensions give invertibility; the unit fixes the scalar. This is a uniform statement about pointed modules, stronger than the existence of an unpointed intertwiner. It is not yet an identification of the global knot period across arbitrary triangulations. ### 3.1 The exact kernel and its normalization unit This factorization has an explicit finite-product kernel.
