In the commutative coordinate algebra E_s tensor E_t write w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. Then D f(w,z)=(w/z)f(w,z) +(1-w/z)/(1-omega z)*f(w,omega z). Induction, starting with f=1, gives D^b 1=product_(j=1)^b (1-omega^j w)/(1-omega^j z). Thus, in the monomial bases, the pointed Clebsch--Gordan map is C_(s,t)(u^a v^b) =w^a (omega w;omega)_b/(omega z;omega)_b. (3.5) No undetermined scalar remains. These are q-factorial ratios in the same local family as the earlier custom products, now with a specified module meaning, phase, and vacuum. Taking their magnitudes does not identify the entire earlier positive state with this tensor construction. Its determinant also has a uniform formula: det C_(s,t) =[t(1-st)/(1-t)^2]^(n(n-1)/2). (3.6) Here the target basis is x_1^i x_2^j and the source is u^a v^b, with the first index ordered first in both. To prove (3.6), first replace the target basis by w^a z^k. Its determinant is t^(n(n-1)/2): for each a, reducing z^(a+k) modulo z^n=t contributes t^a; its cyclic permutation has sign one for odd n. Over K(w), each column b of (3.5) is multiplied by N_b(w)=product_(j=1)^b(1-omega^j w). Its field norm is (1-st)^b. The product of these norms is (1-st)^(n(n-1)/2). The remaining columns are R_b(z)=1/(omega z;omega)_b. For b>=1, R_b(z)=product_(j=b+1)^n(1-omega^j z)/(1-t). Their degrees are n-b, while R_0=1. The triangular leading-coefficient calculation gives det(R_b in the z^k basis) =omega^[n(n^2-1)/3]/(1-t)^(n-1). The sign is one because its exponent is (n-1)^2. This determinant appears to the n-th power over K, so its phase disappears exactly. Combining the three factors proves (3.6). Writing h=(n-1)/2 and f=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, a specified cyclic determinant normalization can be taken on the mu_n-cover gamma^n=f^(-h), C_normalized=gamma C_(s,t). (3.7) It has determinant one because dim C=n^2 and det C=f^(nh). Equation (3.7) specifies a particular mu_n subcover of the general mu_(n^2) determinant choices. It retains a nonconstant algebraic unit, not just an unspecified root-of-unity scalar. Compositions must carry this unit before any peripheral specialization. For fixed nondegenerate classical parameters this normalization also has a uniform size bound, with no choice of root affecting it: log|gamma|=-(n-1)/(2n)*log|f|. Thus any fixed finite recoupling diagram accumulates a bounded logarithmic contribution from these units as n varies. Self-dual finite Fourier measures add only explicit powers of n. After the states and their period classes are identified, these recorded changes cannot alter their exponential volume rate. This assertion applies at nonzero finite f; cancellation and specialization at a zero or pole must be performed in the generic period identity first. ## 4. Recoupling without integral limits or chosen matrices For arbitrary nondegenerate affine central characters g,h,gh, take splitting modules H_g,H_h,H_(gh) of dimension n and define W(g,h)=Hom_B(H_(gh),H_g tensor H_h). The tensor product is an n^2-dimensional module over the split matrix algebra of the product character, hence n copies of its n-dimensional irreducible module. Therefore dim W(g,h)=n and evaluation is an isomorphism W(g,h) tensor H_(gh) -> H_g tensor H_h. (4.1) This only uses the specified nondegenerate central fibre, not a semisimplicity assertion for all B-modules. For three characters composition gives two canonical isomorphisms W(g,h) tensor W(gh,k) -> Hom_B(H_(ghk),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k), W(h,k) tensor W(g,hk) -> Hom_B(H_(ghk),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k). Their ratio defines the basis-free recoupling map. For four characters every parenthesization identifies in the same way with Hom_B(H_(ghkl),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k tensor H_l). Both compositions in the pentagon are the same map through this common space. This proves the pentagon exactly by coassociativity and composition. It requires neither analytic limits nor a choice of cyclic-dilogarithm branches. On the Steinberg subfamily W(s,t) is canonically a pointed Steinberg module E_tau: the commuting algebra of Section 3 acts by postcomposition and its distinguished vector is m_(s,t). Equations (3.3) put it in the relative vacuum line. This identifies (3.4) with the evaluation map (4.1). Choosing bases turns these recoupling maps into cyclic 6j matrices. Frames introduce exactly the factors and root choices that require normalization torsors. Literal equality to a particular matrix still requires its basis, roots, measure and determinant convention to match. ## 5. The global comparison that remains This supplies one uniform algebraic origin of the local 2--3 recoupling relation on the nondegenerate locus at every odd level. Individual knot integrals need not reprove this coherence statement. The finite face theorem evaluates singular presentations and edge reduction supplies the boundary module. The required intrinsic knot period still needs a functorial gluing construction joining these pieces, with its peripheral data, duality pairings and normalization line. Degenerate central fibres are not covered by the matrix-algebra argument and must be handled explicitly in that construction. The rational Faddeev identity fixes its local Heisenberg/dilogarithm period. Its global cycle and the regulator comparison remain separate obligations. Coassociativity proves coherence, but does not by itself prove the numerical volume-growth law. The next task is this global comparison, not more knot cases.

title: Pointed tetrahedron modules and all-level edge reduction
text: # Pointed tetrahedron modules and all-level edge reduction Research note, 26 October 2026. This constructs strict shape-ordering maps, including explicit pointed root intertwiners, and proves integral edge-lattice primitivity for link exteriors in S^3. It extends the earlier odd-level edge reduction to every N. In particular a positive geometric triangulation of a hyperbolic knot supplies a nonzero rank-N quantum boundary block at every level on the stated central cover, without a global branching assumption for this module construction. The projected tensor generator is specified, but its nonvanishing, its identification with the actual relative ADO source, and its marked Bloch-regulator norm are not proved. Shape-module order changes are not automatically tensor-face adapters for the full [Verma period](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md). The marked peripheral lattice at even N requires a separate distinction in Section 7. ## 1. A pointed shape module and its strict order changes For local parameter R use the quantum Laurent algebra A_R=<X^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1): XY=R YX>, D_R=A_R/A_R L, L=X+Y-1, with distinguished generator [1]. For an oriented tetrahedron R=Q^(-epsilon), epsilon=+/-1. Its shape triad is Z_0=X, Z_1=Y^(-1), Z_2=-X^(-1)Y, Z_0 Z_1 Z_2=-R^(-1). The cyclic ordering map and reflection are rho(X)=Y^(-1), rho(Y)=-Y^(-1)X, sigma(X)=Y, sigma(Y)=X, sigma(R)=R^(-1). (1.1) Reflection is understood either semilinearly in the local parameter or as a linear map to the oppositely oriented algebra. Exact noncommutative substitution gives rho^3=1, sigma^2=1, sigma rho sigma=rho^(-1), rho(L)=-Y^(-1)L, sigma(L)=L. (1.2) The unit in rho(L) is on the left. Thus these maps preserve the correct left ideal and give actual pointed module maps, with [1] sent to [1]. Their coherence is exact rather than projective. The ordinary S_4 action on the six cross-ratios factors through this S_3. This supplies shape-module changes under local vertex orderings. It does not assert that the Klein-four action on face tensor legs has been constructed merely because it is trivial on shape coordinates. The module is related directly to the compact tetrahedral operator. If psi(a)=P_Q(a)^(-1), then psi(Qa)=(1-a)psi(a). Multiplication by a and the shift a->Qa give X+Y-1 on this generator, with parameter R=Q^(-1). Multiplying by the exact monomial shear in the preceding note transports this relation to its tetrahedral kernel module. This is an algebraic statement about the local functional module, not a termwise root evaluation of psi. ## 2. Explicit pointed root intertwiners Let R=r^2 have order N, with r^N=-1. On the nondegenerate shape cover choose s,t satisfying s^N+t^N=1, st!=0. Use the clock/shift representation X e_a=s R^a e_a, Y e_a=t e_(a+1 mod N). It is the full matrix algebra. The kernel of L is one-dimensional: normalize p_0=1 and use p_a/p_(a-1)=t/(1-sR^a), 1<=a<N. (2.1) The last cyclic equation is exactly s^N+t^N=1. All components are nonzero. The left-ideal quotient D_R at this center is an N-dimensional simple module: a matrix L of rank N-1 gives a left-ideal quotient of dimension N, and a[1]->a p identifies it with this representation. The root cover itself has exact order changes rho:(s,t,r)->(t^(-1),r s/t,r), sigma:(s,t,r)->(t,s,r^(-1)). (2.2) They obey the same S_3 relations. The factor r in rho is required: its N-th power gives the minus sign in 1-t^(-N)=-s^N/t^N. There is an explicit canonical matrix adapter. For rho use (A,B)=(Y^(-1),-Y^(-1)X); for sigma use (A,B)=(Y,X). Let (s',t',r') be (2.2), and let p' be (2.1) at that target. Put P_0=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(A/s')^j, v=P_0 e_0, J e_a=(B/t')^a v. The spectral projector and cyclic arrows show that J is invertible and intertwines both clock/shift generators. Its kernel image Jp' is a nonzero multiple of p. Divide J by its zeroth component to impose Jp'=p. (2.3) This fixes its entire scalar. The module relations (1.2) imply that a composition for an S_3 relation commutes with the full matrix algebra; (2.3) makes that scalar one. Thus cyclic rotation three times, reflection twice, and the braid relation have exact pointed coherence at every N, including even and composite N. No determinant-normalized or unitary metric assertion is needed. The subsequent [Regge/cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md#the-quantum-ordering-maps-are-explicit-gaussians) now writes these same adapters as explicit Gaussian Fourier matrices divided by their actual pointing scalar. It retains the quadratic Gauss phase in the unpointed order-three cycle, and gives the scalar's exact Hermitian norm as a ratio of the two kernel norms. This solves the finite ordering part; it is not a full face-tensor S_4 or global selected-state theorem. ## 3. The integral edge lattice, without a branching Let K be a connected oriented triangulated 3-dimensional pseudomanifold whose vertex links are closed orientable surfaces; this includes an ideal triangulation of a cusped manifold and ordinary finite vertices with sphere links. Let T,E,V denote the numbers of tetrahedra, global edges and vertices. Write Lambda=direct-sum_j Z^2, Omega=direct-sum_j epsilon_j [[0,1],[-1,0]]. In tetrahedron j the opposite pairs are (01,23), (02,13), (03,12). For a global edge e let a_e,b_e,c_e be its incidence counts in these pairs. Its vector in Lambda is beta(e)_j=epsilon_j(a_e-c_e,b_e-c_e). Let E_ed=im beta. This definition uses arbitrary local vertex orders and their orientation signs, not a global branching. The sign gives the physical edge equation when an odd local reordering inverts the corresponding ordered shape. Omitting it from the incidence calculation gives an integrally symplectically isomorphic lattice, by multiplication of that tetrahedron block by -1, so the rank and saturation statements are the same. Isotropy has a direct face proof. Assign values lambda and mu to global edges, and form the local opposite-pair sums a,b,c and u,v,w. After factoring out epsilon_j, their local symplectic contribution is (a-c)(v-w)-(b-c)(u-w). For three ordered edge values put omega(l,m)=sum_cyclic(l_i m_(i+1)-l_(i+1)m_i). The displayed contribution is exactly minus the alternating sum of omega over the four ordered faces. Each pair of nonopposite edges occurs on its unique face, which verifies the formula termwise. The face expressions cancel under the orientation-reversing face identifications. Therefore Omega(E_ed,E_ed)=0. (3.1) This argument is unaffected by arbitrary local reordering, because both the face orientation and the three-edge alternating form transform by the same permutation sign. ## 4. Exact saturation and the missing prime 2 Put h=dim H^1(K;F_2). The nonzero Smith entries of beta are 1 repeated E-V-h times, 2 repeated h times. (4.1) Here is an independent proof. Over any field of odd characteristic, a row dependence says a=b=c in each tetrahedron. These equations are equivalent to lambda_ij=t_i+t_j. The local t's are uniquely recovered from the three edge values of a face by division by 2. They therefore descend to one t at every global vertex. The vertex-sum map is injective, since a triangle's three zero endpoint sums force all its t's to vanish. Hence rank beta=E-V in every odd characteristic, as well as over Q. In characteristic two, a=b=c is instead equivalent to the four triangle sums being equal. Face pairing makes their common value one global constant sigma. Subtract sigma times the constant edge assignment. The result is exactly a simplicial 1-cocycle on K. Conversely every such cocycle and every sigma give a dependence. The constant assignment has triangle sum one and is independent of the cocycles. Thus dim ker(beta mod 2)=1+dim Z^1(K;F_2)=V+h. (4.2) It remains to exclude Smith factors 4,8,..., not merely odd factors. Work with a dependence lambda valued in Q/Z. Locally one can solve lambda_ij=t_i+t_j, since multiplication by 2 is surjective on Q/Z. Two choices on a paired face differ by the same element of order at most 2 at its three vertices. Therefore 2t descends to global vertex values u, and 2lambda_ij=u_i+u_j. This is the reduction of a rational vertex-sum dependence. By Smith normal form, the quotient of Q/Z-valued dependences by reductions of rational dependences is the dual of the torsion in Lambda/E_ed. The preceding calculation kills it by 2. All nonzero Smith entries therefore equal 1 or 2; (4.2) counts exactly h entries equal to 2. This proves (4.1). For an exterior of a link in S^3, H^1(K;F_2)=0. Attach cones to each boundary component to obtain K; finite sphere vertices do not affect H_1. The cone Mayer--Vietoris sequence identifies H_1(K) with the cokernel of H_1(boundary M)->H_1(M). The meridians generate H_1(M)=Z^c for a c-component link, so this cokernel vanishes, including over F_2. Consequently E_ed is primitive in Lambda for S^3 link exteriors. (4.3) For a knot all edge-row dependences are constants, and the sum of all edge rows is zero integrally. Deleting any one edge row therefore gives an integral basis of E_ed, with no index hidden at 2. Equation (4.3) strengthens the odd-level argument in the [earlier Heisenberg reduction](heisenberg_period_torsor.md). ## 5. Edge reduction at every root level Fix nondegenerate tetrahedral central shapes satisfying the classical edge equations, and choose the recorded central-root cover. The tensor product of the root tetrahedron modules is a split irreducible quantum-torus module W of dimension N^T. This follows directly from their clock/shift matrix units. Use lambda^2=Q, lambda^N=(-1)^(N-1), for example lambda=-q_N. Use A_j=Z_(0,j), B_j=Z_(1,j), so A_j B_j=Q^epsilon_j B_j A_j. These are the first two triad variables, rather than the original X,Y pair of Section 1. For integer vectors v=(a,b) the Weyl convention is W(v)=lambda^(-sum epsilon_j a_j b_j) A^a B^b. It has the exact multiplication with factor lambda^Omega and its N-th power is precisely its classical central monomial. These statements include all even-level signs. Shape identities such as Z_0 Z_1 Z_2=-Q^epsilon and their induced edge units are part of the specified characters, not discarded constants. Choose a basis e_1,...,e_r of the primitive isotropic E_ed and specified commuting edge characters c_i with c_i^N=W(e_i)^N. All dependencies and their units must be matched. Such characters have an explicit realization on the central-root cover: if s_j,t_j are the roots of X_j^N,Y_j^N in Section 2, then eta(e)=product_j s_j^(a_j)t_j^(-b_j) is a multiplicative root character for W(e). A different compatible prescribed lift differs by a mu_N-valued character. This labels the lifts; it does not select the actual ADO source lift by nonvanishing. Then U_i=c_i^(-1)W(e_i) commute and U_i^N=1. The exact projector is Pi_chi=product_i (1/N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1)chi_i^(-a)U_i^a, chi_i in mu_N. (5.1) Every nonidentity term has zero trace: primitivity implies that a nonzero linear combination of the e_i modulo N is nonzero in Lambda/N Lambda, and noncentral clock/shift monomials have zero trace. Therefore rank Pi_chi=N^(T-r) (5.2) for every compatible prescribed character and every N>=2. The coinvariant quotient is canonically the image of Pi_chi. This supplies nonzero reductions at all levels; it does not permit choosing a character to force the desired period. The saturated lattice B=E_ed^perp/E_ed is free and unimodular symplectic. One can extend E_ed to an integral symplectic basis: choose a primitive e, solve Omega(e,f)=1 by Bezout, split off that pair and continue. Its remaining pairs act on im Pi_chi. The N-th-power central characters are retained on the same root cover. Their nonidentity Weyl operators have zero trace on the reduced space, by inserting (5.1) in the full trace. The resulting N^(2(T-r)) trace-orthogonal matrices span its entire endomorphism algebra. This proves irreducibility for the saturated boundary algebra, with no inversion of 2 modulo N. For a torus-cusped link exterior, Euler characteristic gives T-r=c. The module has dimension N^c; for a knot it has dimension N. The assertion remains valid with finite sphere vertices, since their genus contribution is zero. ## 6. The gluing vector and its ordering compatibility Let p_j be the specified tetrahedron generator in its splitting frame. The reduction has a specified candidate vector s_(T,N,chi)=Pi_chi(p_1 tensor ... tensor p_T). (6.1) The later [factorial source-torsor theorem](factorial_source_torsor.md) identifies this local tetrahedron kernel, after reversing its index, with the pointed cyclic dilogarithm phi_a. The actual factorial boundary is p_a=nu^a phi_a, nu^N=1-h^N; this is a singular frame at the Kashaev wall h=1. Its full affine source and cut-root adapters are explicit. This supplies local relative data; it does not identify the nondegenerate geometric root fiber with that degenerate actual boundary fiber. This is the root block of the usual left/right quantum gluing quotient: first impose the tetrahedron left ideals, then the edge coinvariants. A centralizer of the edge action, including the saturated boundary algebra, acts on it. The pointed order-change maps of Sections 1--2 intertwine the whole edge operators and their transported characters. Hence they intertwine (5.1), carry (6.1) to its corresponding vector, and obey the same exact cocycle relations. This proves local shape-order independence of the module and its projected vector. A global branching is unnecessary for this module construction. The vector (6.1) can still be zero even though the reduction has the nonzero rank (5.2). The trace of a projector does not prove that it is nonzero on a particular tensor. Nor has this candidate gluing vector been identified with the selected relative Verma trace or actual ADO source. In particular the root tetrahedron module was obtained by its algebraic relation, not by evaluating the four singular compact factors separately. ## 7. The marked peripheral lattice and its integral half-longitude For a knot the saturated boundary lattice B is unimodular of rank two. The earlier audited unhalved meridian/longitude rows have symplectic pairing -2. Whenever these are the chosen marked vectors, their span has index two in B. This is a peripheral index; it does not contradict the primitivity of the edge lattice. The subsequent [integral half-longitude proof](integral_half_longitude.md) identifies the missing half using the knot marking itself: B=Z delta(mu) + Z ell, ell=delta(lambda)/2, Omega(delta(mu),ell)=-1. A mod-two dual-face cochain proves that delta(lambda) pairs evenly with every balanced integral vector, because the preferred longitude is nullhomologous in the exterior. Unimodularity gives the unique half in B. An explicit edge correction constructs its integer representative before specializing N. Thus the unhalved algebra is generated by Y,T^2 inside the saturated algebra generated by Y,T, with TY=q^2 YT. At odd N these give the same finite Weyl algebra. At even N the unhalved algebra has two sectors distinguished by Y^(N/2), each of dimension N/2 after central normalization, and T exchanges them. The scalar lift satisfies T^2=Lambda_hat only after the full edge character and the specified square root are retained. In particular changing T to -T at even N does not change T^N. The actual central longitude and source pointing must still be matched. The [even-meridian ADO normalization](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) records its separate full-state sign character; no arbitrary choice of a sector or square-root sign identifies the states. If h in (4.1) is nonzero for a different manifold, the edge lattice itself can also be nonprimitive. Already E=<2f> has compatible reductions of dimension gcd(2,N) and vanishing reductions for incompatible even-level characters. Lens-space examples verify this distinction in the audit. The S^3-link hypothesis in (4.3) is doing actual work. ## 8. Consequence for the ideal-triangulation route The audited positive triangulation theorem supplies nondegenerate classical shapes for every hyperbolic knot. Sections 1--6 then supply order-compatible pointed tetrahedron modules and a nonzero rank-N geometric boundary block at every level on the specified cover, without a global branching requirement for this reduction. This upgrades the earlier local central-support calculation to an actual nonzero geometric quantum module. Placing that block in the actual affine meridian source extension, matching its projected vector and boundary functional to the relative Verma period, and identifying the marked Bloch-regulator norm are still necessary. The marked peripheral scalar lift in Section 7 must be transported explicitly. No geometric factor of the minimal actual A-operator or noncancellation in the selected period follows from module rank alone. ## 9. Coverage and independent diagnostics The integral edge complex and its 2-primary phenomena belong to Neumann's existing triangulation framework; see the statement coverage in [Combinatorics of triangulations and the Chern--Simons invariant](https://www.math.columbia.edu/department/neumann/preprints/cspaper.pdf). No integral exactness proof from it is used above. The elementary face pairing, endpoint-potential and Q/Z arguments prove the needed lattice statements here. The abstracts of [Garoufalidis--Yu, 2403.12424](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12424) and [Panitch--Park, 2403.12850](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12850) cover quantum gluing quotients and quantum trace maps. Their comparison, move and state-identification proofs are not premises. No novelty claim is made for the general quantum gluing framework. The point here is the explicit ordering/root phases and the all-level reduction with the remaining selected-period issue kept separate. [The audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.py) checks the abstract pointed S_3 maps, finite root adapters in both orientation parameters, the six-edge face identity, exact edge Smith forms and mod-2 cohomology with arbitrary tetrahedron relabelings, and finite projectors including even N. Closed nonprimitive examples and index-two peripheral sectors are included as scope checks. The [results](../experiments/pointed_tetrahedron_gluing_results.json) support the uniform proofs; no volume asymptotic is inferred. The saved full audit has 49 abstract Laurent checks, 18 pointed root-adapter cases through level 12 in both orientation parameters, 45 exact incidence/Smith/cohomology checks including arbitrary tetrahedron relabelings and nonprimitive closed examples, and 11 edge-projector checks. The figure-eight projector checks include the full saturated boundary trace basis at every listed level; the Whitehead-link checks have the predicted N^2 dimensions. Nine parity tests retain incompatible nonprimitive characters and the two marked peripheral sectors at even N. The full reproduction command in this workspace is PYTHONPATH=.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages python3 experiments/audit_pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.py --regina

title: Positive angle majorants: half-period gluing and the affine source charge
text: # Positive angle majorants: half-period gluing and the affine source charge 28 October 2026. Failure of a bare 2-to-3 identity does NOT disqualify the positive angle-factorial partition function as an upper comparison. For a fixed complete geometric triangulation its already proved exponential rate is the desired one, and fixed constants or polynomial measure corrections have zero exponential rate. There is a constructive distinction between the N-clock and the FULL 2N-clock q=exp(pi*i/N). On STRICT angle support, the full clock already forces the geometric edge lift by positivity and the total-angle identity. A second lemma shows that the AFFINE charge d=N-1 removes all winding aliases even on weak nonnegative support, provided the full clock selects edge residue 2d. The resulting positive norm has the sharp geometric upper exponent. These are genuine bounds for the stated angle tensors. An exact map from the full original source to those tensors has not yet been proved. A weak sum-N angle tensor, with zero angles permitted, does retain an exponentially excessive winding face even with the full 2N-clock. That is the precise boundary scope of the obstruction below; it must NOT be applied to the strict-support lemma. This does NOT disprove a subexponential upper comparison for the FULL original Kashaev scalar. No nonzero original-source coefficient is assigned to the bad winding. Such a comparison remains possible if the actual source removes or cancels it before positivity is taken. ## 1. The correct normalization for an upper comparison For a fixed complete positive ideal triangulation T let w_N(k)=product_i s_N(k_i)^(-1), s_N(a)=product_(j=1)^a 2sin(pi*j/N), and let P_N be its strict integral angle structures: each tetrahedral triple sums to N and each global edge sums to 2N. The positive model is Z_N(T)=sum_(k in P_N)w_N(k). On its allowed lattice progression, (pi/N)log Z_N(T)->Vol(M). (1) This is the independently proved positive-volume theorem in [the comparison note (historical context omitted)](quantum_a_volume.md). The desired upper comparison is |K_N|² <= exp(o(N)) Z_N(T), (2) or equivalently |K_N|<=exp(o(N))sqrt(Z_N(T)). The square root is essential: Z has the ENERGY rate Vol/pi, not the amplitude rate Vol/(2pi). Any unchanged full peripheral/dimension line multiplies both sides with its exact square modulus; at the marked complete point the known such lines have polynomial magnitude and do not change (1). They cannot remove an exponential gap. For a fixed T, (1) means (2) is equivalent, on that progression, to the sharp original-source exponential upper bound. Merely knowing (1) does not prove (2); the nontrivial input must be an independent source-preserving comparison. Conversely, a finite move multiplier 8, N, or any fixed-degree boundary unit is not an obstruction to (2). ## 2. Exact positive Fourier gluing gives a different norm Let H_N have orthonormal basis indexed by k_i in{0,...,N-1}, each tetrahedral triple summing EXACTLY to N. Zero angles are allowed in this finite vector space, because s_N(0)=1. The forbidden all-pi triple would require an entry N and is absent. Define the positive vector v_N=sum_k sqrt(w_N(k)) |k>. Let E be the actual integral edge-angle incidence matrix and mu,nu the marked peripheral angle rows. The geometric projection P_geo, with peripheral restrictions included, is the diagonal orthogonal projector onto E k=2N*1, mu k=nu k=0. (3) Write P_geo^edge for the projector imposing ONLY E k=2N*1. One may impose the same EXACT peripheral restrictions on both sides of a comparison, or omit them on both. No modular-to-exact peripheral conclusion is used below. On the strict coordinates its squared norm is the corresponding positive angle partition. Allowing zero angles on the SAME integer fiber still has maximum volume at most Vol(M), by the same continuous concavity argument; zeros alone are not the problem. Now use the finite root Q=exp(2pi*i/N), as in the actual quantum Fourier transform. The character average on a constraint row c is (1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Q^[r(c k-bN)] =1 if c k=bN modulo N, and0 otherwise. (4) It sees no difference between b=0,1,2. Multiplying (4) over the edge and peripheral rows gives the orthogonal projector P_cyc onto E k in N Z^edges, mu k,nu k in N Z. (5) Hence an INDEPENDENT finite-Fourier/Plancherel gluing of these positive angle tensors gives exactly ||P_cyc v_N||² =sum_(k satisfying5) w_N(k)=:Z_N^cyc(T), P_geo<=P_cyc. (6) This is an equality of positive Hilbert-space norms. Replacing this N-clock cyclic projector by the exact geometric projection decreases the norm; it is not an automatic upper-bound operation. A unitary Fourier change of basis does not alter this projection order. ### 2.1 The FULL 2N-clock is sufficient on strict support For a cusped ideal triangulation with torus cusps, the edge count equals the tetrahedron count t. Each quad angle is counted twice in the sum of all edge incidences, so for every tetrahedral sum-N state, sum_edges (E k)_e=2Nt. (6a) The full q-character average is (1/(2N))sum_(r=0)^(2N-1) q^[r((E k)_e-2N)] =1 iff (E k)_e=0 modulo2N. (6b) On STRICT support every edge sum is positive. Equation(6b) then makes every edge sum at least2N. Their total is exactly2Nt and there are t edges; hence EACH sum is exactly2N. Consequently P_(2N-edge-cyclic)=P_geo^edge on strict angle support. (6c) The equality remains true after imposing the SAME exact peripheral restrictions on both sides. The sum argument does not upgrade modular peripheral conditions to exact ones. Thus one does not need a separate EDGE integer-lift projector if an original-source comparison retains both the full 2N edge character and strict angle support. This conclusion is constructive and independent of a local Pachner equality. ### 2.2 The affine d-charge is stronger, including at zero angles There is an equally useful variant matching the original reflected trivalent source equation h0+h4+h2=d=N-1. Suppose nonnegative angle indices satisfy tetrahedral sum d, and the full q-character selects (E k)_e=2d modulo2N at EVERY edge. (6d) The least nonnegative representative of 2d is 2d, strictly positive for N>=2. Each edge sum is therefore at least2d, while their total is exactly2dt. Since the number of edges is t, all sums MUST equal 2d, even if some individual angles vanish. No bad winding sector survives. This is a finite support identity, not an asymptotic claim. Let Z_N^aff be the positive factorial sum over this nonnegative sum-d/full-clock space. Then Z_N^aff <=N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi] (6e) for a fixed triangulation-dependent C (and trivially if the set is empty). Indeed k/d is an exact weak geometric angle structure. The geometric volume bound gives sum_i Lambda(pi*k_i/d)<=Vol(M). The uniform modulus of continuity |Lambda(x)-Lambda(y)| <=C |x-y|(1+|log|x-y||) follows by integrating its two logarithmic endpoint singularities. Since |k_i/N-k_i/d|<=1/N, it changes the volume by O(logN/N). The uniform sine-factorial estimate then bounds EVERY weight by N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi], and there are at most N^(3t) states. This proves(6e), with the original zero-angle weights retained. On any allowed nonempty progression for the strict model(1), its rounding proof gives the quantitative lower bound Z_N(T)>=N^(-C')exp[N Vol(M)/pi]. Indeed the rounded geometric angles differ by O(1/N), remain in a fixed strict neighborhood, and their volume differs by O(1/N); the uniform factorial error is O(logN). Thus(6e) actually gives Z_N^aff<=N^C'' Z_N(T), and in particular Z_N^aff<=exp(o(N))Z_N(T). A source-preserving norm map to THIS affine angle space, of subexponential norm and with the actual full-clock residue(6d), WOULD give the requested upper comparison. No lower/survival theorem would be required for that step. The local actual trivalent d-charge is already established in the source notes. What is not established here is its global realization as the tetrahedral angle indices of an arbitrary geometric T, with the full edge character(6d) after all Fourier/Gaussian/source adapters. The subsequent [supporting-plane and defect theorem](positive_angle_supporting_plane_and_defect_bound.md) weakens this target further: O(1) TRUE integer edge-charge errors cost only a polynomial, and o(N) errors preserve the sharp volume upper exponent, with an explicit Gaussian deficit. This is not a statement about bounded changes of residues modulo2N. ## 3. A certified exponential gap on a complete geometric triangulation Use the actual positive nine-tetrahedron 5_2 triangulation and exact rational angle vector alpha from [the previously certified fixture](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md). The new conclusion here is the positive NORM comparison (6), not a claim about the coefficient of that fixture in the original state. All entries of alpha lie in[0,19/20], its tetrahedral triples sum to1, and its actual edge/peripheral rows obey exactly E alpha=2*(1,1,1,1,1,1,2,0,1)^t, mu alpha=nu alpha=0. (7) For 20|N, k_N=N alpha is therefore a legitimate basis vector in P_cyc H_N, with BOTH original marked peripheral equations exact. Its edge sums are even multiples of N, so it also survives the FULL 2N-clock on WEAK sum-N support. It fails the exact geometric edge lift. The three zero-angle tetrahedra are flat, and all other tetrahedra are strictly positive. The exact geometry and outward-rounded dilogarithm evaluation give 3.76403<V_alias<3.76404, 2.82812<Vol(M)<2.82813. (8) The uniform sine-factorial estimate, including k_i=0, implies log w_N(k_N)=N V_alias/pi+O(log N). Retaining this ONE nonnegative term in (6), and using (1) along a common allowed progression, proves the rigorous gap liminf (pi/N)log[Z_N^cyc(T)/Z_N(T)] >=V_alias-Vol(M)>.93590. (9) Here the common progression can be any multiple of20 and of a denominator of a strict rational geometric angle structure. Such a denominator exists: rational solutions of the fixed rational affine equations are dense in their real affine solution space, and a complete positive point has an open strict neighborhood. Thus the denominator Z_N(T) is nonempty on that progression. If peripheral rows are added to the denominator, either it is nonempty on a further progression and the same upper volume bound applies, or an attempted all-level comparison already encounters an empty denominator. For (9) it suffices to use the original edge-only Z_N(T) of (1). In amplitude norm the unavoidable loss of this cyclic relaxation is at least exp[N(V_alias-Vol)/(2pi)+o(N)]. Neither a finite fixed number of move constants nor any polynomial measure/source factor changes it. The defect in(7) is O(N), so shifting angle indices by O(1) to correct N-versus-N-1 conventions also cannot repair it. This is a triangulation-based positive Gram obstruction for the WEAK sum-N model, already after exact tetrahedral equations and both peripheral rows, and even with the full 2N-clock. The strict alias locus for this particular face is empty: its zero edge forces three flat tetrahedra. It does NOT contradict(6c) or the differently charged affine model(6d). It does not rely on an oversized raw crossing state or on positivity of an unnormalized local pentagon. ## 4. A useful exact local connection, and its limit For 1<=L<N and0<=a<=L, reflection gives s_N(L)s_N(N-L)=2N sin(pi*L/N). Consequently the modulus of a genuine Gaussian coefficient is EXACTLY a positive tetrahedral angle weight times a polynomial factor: |[L choose a]_Q| =2N sin(pi*L/N) /[s_N(a)s_N(L-a)s_N(N-L)]. (10) The three indices on the right sum to N. Formula(10) applies also at a=0,L, where the tetrahedron is flat. It connects the original root-factorial magnitudes to the positive model more directly than merely sharing the same dilogarithm asymptotic. It can be applied to the Gaussian blocks AFTER any independently proved exact fusion. It does not, by itself, prove that the resulting triples have the complete knot triangulation's GLOBAL edge constraints with the correct full character and affine residue. A coefficientwise Cauchy--Schwarz estimate, or a convex majorization of factorial magnitudes, does not specify those constraints. The full phases and relative source may supply them. Lemmas(6c),(6d) show that this is a more concrete sufficient target than independently imposing unwrapped winding after every Fourier transform. ## 5. What would still establish the requested majorant The 29 October [length-normalized star and Gram identities](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) now give exact local square-root weights with all normalizers retained. The [original singleton clock source](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md) has polynomial Riesz norm at arbitrary signed braid width. These establish a genuine original-source Cauchy framework. Its remaining energy must retain clock interference: [a fully contracted figure-eight sector](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md) excludes every positive diagonal clock metric from the sharp geometric budget. The desired global Gram can be exponentially conditioned; its actual source dual norm, state energy, and true angle defects must be bounded together. The [source-compatible Hermitian reflection](phase_ratio_double_and_fermat_source.md) provides an exact doubled-word input without selecting its angle support. The original paired factorial gauge really fixes the complete cup/cap source, and the existing [weighted Fourier theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md) retains the compulsory dual metric. It does not presently produce a map from the full original source to the strict or affine angle space above for an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation. The normalized finite Fourier transform supplies a SPECIFIED modular character, so its modulus and affine residue matter. The dual metric cannot be silently flattened. Nor does merely remembering that the scalar q has order2N prove that the source map implements(6b) or(6d). For instance, on the N-dimensional cyclic head let S|a>=|a+1 moduloN> and T|a>=q^a|a>. Then exactly T S-q S T=2|0><N-1|. (11) The strict nilpotent shift has no such wrap term. Thus changing an N-cyclic clock to a half-period clock while dropping its endpoint current is not an exact basis change. The subsequent [source-exact half-clock dilation](actual_half_clock_source_dilation.md) now supplies a faithful 2N ambient physical window: its weighted E/F shifts, genuine dual turns, original N-normalization, unrolled H, half-Cartan, pivot and selected one-component cut are all retained. It legitimately permits a unitary 2N Fourier transform of the FULL original physical network. This does not replace an auxiliary unweighted N-cyclic atom shift by the 2N shift X. Its exact lift is S_hat=X(I-P_wall)+X^(1-N)P_wall, with P_wall the two top-window projectors, and it retains T S_hat-q S_hat T=-2q X^(1-N)P_wall T. Only the weighted E/F endpoint zeros remove their corresponding wrap terms. What remains to be proved is its map to geometric tetrahedral angle indices and the GLOBAL edge characters(6b) or(6d); physical degree conservation alone does not identify those characters. The unrolled half-Cartan and source signs must still be transported through that angle-coordinate map. The local pointed tetrahedron gives a useful nonarbitrary charge check. In the conventions of [the pointed module](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md), for positive orientation, Z0 Z1 Z2=-Q. Setting zeta_i=q^-1 Z_i gives EXACTLY zeta0 zeta1 zeta2=-q^-1=q^d. (12) Thus the d-charge is consistent with the original half-period ordering, rather than chosen solely to make an optimization work. The three quad operators do not commute, however, so(12) is not itself a joint positive angle basis or a full tensor gluing theorem. There is also a central-sign constraint on transporting this local rescaling globally. If a chosen edge corner word has valence v_e, rescaling every corner by q^-1 multiplies that word by q^(-v_e). For its NEW character to equal q^-2=q^(2d), its OLD character would have to be q^(v_e-2), in that same specified ordering. But zeta_i^N =-Z_i^N. For ODD N, every ordinary corner word on the original geometric central fiber has Nth power1: all Q-commutation factors have trivial Nth-power correction and the classical edge product is1. At an ODD-valence edge, the proposed old character has (q^(v_e-2))^N=-1, (13) so it cannot simply be imposed on that SAME geometric central fiber. For example, the initial positive three-tetrahedron 5_2 triangulation has valencies7,6,5. A Weyl/Maslov normalization using an additional half-period factor, or a transported Frobenius/sign fiber, could repair this. It must be recorded; it is not supplied by the local identity(12). This is a necessary sign check, not a no-go for a properly transported charged state. In fact the existing pointed edge-module construction leaves compatible edge characters prescribed but free. Multiplying them by a mu_N character of the primitive edge lattice preserves the central data; every compatible edge quotient has its proved rank. The projected tensor generator and actual ADO source have not been identified there. Thus that module theorem does not select the specific global character(6d) for the original source. This is the exact unresolved global operator/source calculation. A valid upper proof could instead establish an exact source map whose image lies on the strict/full-clock or affine/full-clock fiber just proved sufficient, with a norm bound exp(o(N)), or prove that all excessive winding channels cancel as original relative currents with that same cost. Either would be sufficient for an angle-majorant argument. No lower-bound or nonzero geometric coefficient would be needed for this UPPER step. Nothing in the calculation rules out that construction. It identifies the exact extra statement that is missing from the proposed Fourier/Plancherel comparison, and proves that it cannot be replaced by the cyclic positive relaxation in(6). Reproduction: ```sh python3 experiments/audit_positive_angle_majorant_winding.py ``` The script independently checks the projector character identity, the exact rational full marked angle data, the certified volume gap, and(10). It asserts no nonzero original quantum coefficient for the wrong-winding state and no broad original-source upper bound.

title: A geometric supporting-plane bound for positive factorial energies with charge defects
text: # A geometric supporting-plane bound for positive factorial energies with charge defects 28 October 2026. Complete positive geometry gives a quantitative upper certificate for the angle-factorial model even when the edge charges are not exact. Bounded integer edge defects cost only a polynomial factor. Sublinear defects preserve the sharp volume exponent. There is also a uniform Gaussian deficit away from the complete angle point. This is a statement about the positive angle energy, with its specified normalization. It does not identify that energy with the original Kashaev period. In particular, the exact scalar in the original star--triangle identity is a FULL binomial, whereas the one-tetrahedron energy amplitude is its square root after division by N. Section 5 records that compulsory normalization distinction. ## 1. The complete geometric supporting plane Fix a finite complete positive ideal triangulation T with t tetrahedra. Let x* be its angle vector in units of pi, and put mu=min_i x*_i>0, V(x)=sum_i Lambda(pi*x_i), Lambda'(theta)=-log(2sin theta). Let A be the tetrahedral sum matrix and E the global edge-angle incidence matrix. Thus A x*=1, E x*=2*1, V(x*)=Vol(M). (1) No peripheral equation is required for the following upper bound. One may impose additional exact peripheral restrictions on the same angle variables; that only restricts the set being bounded. There is no claim that a modular peripheral condition becomes exact. Define the full coordinate gradient g_i=-pi*log(2sin(pi*x*_i)). There are FIXED real vectors lambda,eta such that g=A^t lambda+E^t eta. (2) Indeed, complete geometric gluing is stationary for volume on the angle slice Ax=1,Ex=2. One direct check uses fixed cusp horospheres and ideal Schlaefli: a tangent v with Av=Ev=0 has dV(v)=-(pi/2)sum_e ell_e(Ev)_e=0, with the SAME truncated global edge length ell_e on all incident tetrahedra. Hence g annihilates ker(A,E), and elementary real linear algebra proves (2). Equivalently one can fix a row basis of (A,E), solve (2) once, and retain that certificate. Row dependencies make the certificate nonunique but do not change its pairing with a consistent charge defect. For EVERY weak local angle point x>=0 with Ax=1, V(x)<=Vol(M)+eta dot(Ex-2) -c_*||x-x*||_2², c_*=pi³*mu/64>0. (3) Thus the supporting-plane linear terms telescope exactly into the integral edge defects. They are not independent per-tetrahedron errors and do not require estimating a different critical branch. ## 2. An explicit global quadratic deficit Here is a proof of the constant in(3), including boundary points. For one tetrahedron use independent coordinates x1,x2 and x3=1-x1-x2. Its negative Hessian is pi² [[cot(pi*x1)+cot(pi*x3), cot(pi*x3)], [cot(pi*x3), cot(pi*x2)+cot(pi*x3)]]. (4) Its determinant is pi^4, by the cotangent addition identity, and it is positive definite in the strict simplex. Along the FIRST HALF of the segment x_s=(1-s)x*+s x, every coordinate is at least mu/2 and at most1-mu. Consequently each cotangent has absolute value at most2/(pi*mu), so the trace of(4) is at most 8pi/mu. Its least eigenvalue is therefore at least pi³*mu/8. For a tetrahedral tangent v=(v1,v2,-v1-v2), ||v||_3²<=3(v1²+v2²). Thus its second derivative on that half-segment is at most -(pi³*mu/24)||v||_3². Integrate the Taylor remainder with weight1-s over0<=s<=1/2. Since the remaining part of the segment has nonpositive second derivative, V(x*)+g dot(x-x*)-V(x) >=(pi³*mu/64)||x-x*||². (5) For a boundary endpoint, apply the argument before reaching the endpoint and then use continuity of Lambda. Summing over tetrahedra gives(5) for the whole vector. Substitution of(2) and Ax=Ax*=1 proves(3). Global uniform strong concavity of the Hessian at every boundary point is NOT assumed; integrating its controlled first half is what gives the global deficit from the fixed interior x*. ## 3. The actual factorial weights and bounded edge-charge errors Use precisely s_N(k)=product_(r=1)^k 2sin(pi*r/N), w_N(k)=product_i s_N(k_i)^(-1), 0<=k_i<N. The uniform estimate, including k=0 and N-1, is log s_N(k)=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi*k/N)+O(log N). (6) For an explicit elementary error bound write log(2sin pi*x)=log x+log(1-x)+h(x), where h is smooth on[0,1]. The increasing log term has sum-integral error between0 and logN+1, the decreasing log term has absolute error at mostlogN, and h contributes at most its fixed total variation. Thus the constant in(6) is universal. In a fixed triangulation all weight errors are bounded by C_t logN+C'_t. Suppose A k=N*1 and let delta=E k-2N*1. Combining(3),(6) gives the finite-N Gaussian majorant w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[ N Vol(M)/pi+eta dot(delta)/pi -c_*||k-Nx*||²/(pi*N)]. (7) All original zero-angle weights are retained. In particular, for ANY set of such configurations with ||delta||_infty<=R_N, sum w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[N Vol(M)/pi+||eta||_1 R_N/pi]. (8) The number of configurations is at most N^(3t) and has been absorbed in the fixed polynomial. Thus O(1) edge defects cost only a polynomial factor; R_N=o(N) preserves the sharp geometric upper exponent. Exact full2N edge charge is sufficient but is NOT necessary for this positive-energy estimate. Here delta is the TRUE INTEGER difference E k-2N, not a distance between residues modulo2N. A bounded change of a residue need not give a bounded integer defect: for example the affine residue 2d changes to0 after adding only2, and0 permits zero or multiple edge windings. Thus robustness under bounded integer defects does not justify replacing the actual compatible quantum edge character by a nearby one. The source still has to supply the stated lift or an independent bound on its true supported defects. If ||k/N-x*||>=epsilon, the same sum has the extra factor exp[-N c_*epsilon²/pi]. More quantitatively a radius squared larger than a fixed multiple of(R_N+logN)/N controls the Gaussian tail relative to the complete geometric exponential rate. This is a consequence of the support-plane certificate, not a phase selection or an assertion about the original quantum cycle. The useful condition is even weaker than small defects in every edge: equation(7) controls any supported defect set for which sup eta dot(delta)=o(N), with the Gaussian deficit still retained. ## 4. Affine charge d=N-1 and further bounded local offsets For the source-compatible tetrahedral charge A k=d*1, set y=k/d and delta_d=E k-2d*1. Then Ay=1 and Ey-2=delta_d/d. Equation(3) applies exactly to y. The arguments k_i/N and k_i/d differ by at most1/N. Integrating the two logarithmic endpoint singularities of Lambda gives the uniform modulus |Lambda(u)-Lambda(v)| <=C |u-v|(1+|log|u-v||). It contributes only O(logN) to the logarithm of the weight. Therefore the affine version of(7) is w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[ N Vol(M)/pi+(N/(pi*d)) eta dot(delta_d) -(c_*N/(pi*d²))||k-dx*||²]. (9) Bounded or sublinear edge defects have the same conclusions as in(8), since N/d<=2 for N>=2. This retains flat tetrahedra and does not rely on endpoint vanishing. More generally let the local sums be N+u_j, |u_j|<=U_N<N/2, and normalize each tetrahedral triple by its own local sum. The normalized edge defects differ from delta/N by O(U_N/N), with constants determined by the fixed incidence matrix. The factorial action changes by at most C_t U_N[1+log(N/max(1,U_N))]. (10) Hence bounded local AND edge charge offsets still cost only a polynomial, and sublinear offsets still cost exp(o(N)). The Gaussian deficit in the normalized local angles remains valid. This extension requires the specified nonnegative angle support; it does not extend a factorial through a forbidden index N. On a common allowed nonempty progression, the strict geometric partition satisfies Z_N(T)>=N^(-C)exp[N Vol(M)/pi] by rounding the complete strict point in its integer kernel. Consequently the bounded-defect positive energies above are at most a fixed polynomial times Z_N(T); the sublinear-defect energies are at most exp(o(N))Z_N(T). ### 4.1 A bounded-defect comparison exists at EVERY level There is no lattice-progression obstruction for a sufficiently wide FIXED integer defect window. Put B=2 max_e sum_i E_(e,i), determined solely by the fixed edge incidence matrix, and define Z_N^B=sum_{k>=0, A k=d*1, ||E k-2d*1||_infty<=B} w_N(k). Then this sum is nonempty for every N>=2, and fixed constants give C^-1 N^-C exp[N Vol(M)/pi] <= Z_N^B <= C N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi]. (10a) For nonemptiness, in each complete tetrahedral triple set k_1=floor(d x*_1), k_2=floor(d x*_2), k_3=d-k_1-k_2. All entries lie in[0,d]. Their errors relative to d x* lie in (-1,0] for the first two and [0,2) for the third. Hence every edge defect has absolute value at most B. This constructs an admissible state at each N, without a rationality assumption on x*. For large N it is strictly positive and k/N=x*+O(1/N). Smoothness of the coordinate Lobachevsky sum near x* and (6) give a single weight exp[N Vol(M)/pi+O(logN)], proving the lower bound. The upper bound is (9) summed with the fixed defect bound B. Increasing C handles the finitely many remaining levels. Thus this bounded-defect positive model has the desired energy rate at all levels, independently of any exact-fiber progression. It may be used as an upper comparison target. Its polynomial two-sided estimate still proves nothing about K_N until an exact original-source comparison is established; neither nonemptiness nor rounding constructs that comparison or enforces the true edge lift. ## 5. The exact affine local weight is not its amplitude square root There is a particularly direct connection to the original charged star. If a+b+c=d, root reflection gives w_N(a,b,c)=1/[s_N(a)s_N(b)s_N(c)] =|[a+b choose a]_Q|/N. (11) The exact original source-preserving balanced star--triangle identity in [the general fusion theorem](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) has scalar modulus |[a+b choose a]_Q|, with its full phase and typed outer factors retained. It is the FULL binomial, namely N w_N, not the normalized energy amplitude sqrt(w_N). For example at a=b=c=d/3, N=1 modulo3, the scalar divided by sqrt(w_N) has modulus sqrt(N*|[a+b choose a]_Q|), log of this ratio=N v_3/(2pi)+O(logN). (12) Here v_3=3Lambda(pi/3) is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Thus a uniform local one-tetrahedron comparison which simply replaces this scalar by sqrt(w_N) pays an exponential cost. Two-tetrahedron assignments, a genuinely different doubled contraction, or the exact exponentially varying internal gauges could compensate it. Their compensation at the original full source has to be proved; it cannot be inferred from the factorial identity(11) or absorbed into an unknown knot normalization. This warning does not disprove the requested upper comparison. It keeps its amplitude/energy and source normalizations explicit. The subsequent [exact length-frame calculation](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) now supplies a constructive compensation: b_L=N^(1/4)B_L/sqrt(s_L) makes a balanced star scalar N^(-1/2) times its retained phase, and parallel fusion produces a polynomial times sqrt(w_N). The [original singleton clock co-source](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md) also has polynomial norm in that frame. Thus the flat-frame ratio in (12) is not an obstruction to a properly transported metric. The compulsory dual anchor weights and the coherent global state norm remain; [every diagonal clock metric fails the sharp budget in an actual complete figure-eight sector](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md). The supporting-plane theorem supplies a general geometric bound once a suitable positive angle energy with small charge defects has actually been obtained from the source. It does not construct that source map or bound the norm of an unproved one. ## 6. Reproduction and scope ```sh python3 experiments/audit_positive_angle_supporting_plane.py ``` The audit uses the irregular complete three-tetrahedron shape point, solves the nontrivial edge supporting-plane certificate, tests the explicit global quadratic deficit including boundary triples, checks factorial estimates with charge defects, and verifies(11). The uniform proof is(2)--(10), not the numerical tests. No broad original Kashaev upper bound or geometric survival is asserted. For coverage only, the classical optimization framework is recorded in [Rivin, Combinatorial optimization in geometry](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9907032) and [Futer--Gueritaud, From angled triangulations to hyperbolic structures](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440). The latter abstract explicitly describes the volume critical-point method on an angle polytope. Only those abstracts were consulted for coverage here; no proof or technique from either paper is an input to the supporting-plane, deficit, or finite-factorial arguments.

title: Positive bipyramid cycles and the actual reflected source charge
text: # Positive bipyramid cycles and the actual reflected source charge 28 October 2026. Two local steps are now explicit. The independently proved charged full-Phi pentagon has a genuine REAL internal cycle selecting its geometric bipyramid block with multiplicity one, uniformly on compact positive families. Separately, the original scalar head source has exact zero internal charge after its positive factorial orders are reflected, with an explicit full-Phi Gaussian field and OUTER-ray source retained. These facts are not yet an identification of that reflected circle/outer-ray fiber with the positive charged real contour. The remaining comparison is a definite twisted beta/Pochhammer contour problem described in Section 6. Its original growing source is now resolved further by the exact [norm-pole/Barnes cycle](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md), which retains its nonzero balanced block and normalization remainder. No global geometric cycle or original knot coefficient is assumed to exist here. The [audit](../experiments/audit_positive_bipyramid_source_transport.py) and [results](../experiments/positive_bipyramid_source_transport_results.json) check the rational bipyramid equations, geometric charges and Gaussian, the actual source graph before/after reflection, exact window and full-Psi reflection, and the boundary-difference source identities. ## 1. An arbitrary positive ordered bipyramid Let x,y be complex and put H=x+y-xy, s_1=x, s_3=y, s_2=H, s_0=x/H, s_4=y/H. (1) Assume ALL five s_j lie in the upper half-plane. This is the open positive bipyramid family for this ordered pentagon. No modulus restriction is imposed. On a compact subset all shapes and angles stay uniformly away from degeneration. Define its actual angle charges a_j=Arg(s_j)/(2*pi), c_j=-Arg(1-s_j)/(2*pi), beta_j=1/2-a_j-c_j. All are positive. The elementary identities s_0 s_2=x, s_2 s_4=y, 1-s_0=s_4(1-x), 1-s_4=s_0(1-y), 1-s_2=(1-x)(1-y) give, with the positive principal angles, a_1=a_0+a_2, a_3=a_2+a_4, c_1=c_0+a_4, c_3=a_0+c_4, c_2=c_1+c_3. (2) These are precisely the charges of the independently proved [full-Phi kernel pentagon](faddeev_pentagon_audit.md). The branch equalities have no hidden 2*pi term: their two positive angles add to the indicated positive shape angle, and their negative complement arguments add to its negative principal complement argument. In particular c_2+beta_0+beta_4=1 is the new internal edge charge. The ordinary five-term relation, applied to 1-x and 1-y, gives D(x)+D(y)=D(s_0)+D(s_2)+D(s_4). (3) ## 2. The exact full-Phi kernel and its selected real normal cycle Use EXACTLY the charged functions from the cited independent proof: f_(a,c)(t)=exp(-pi*i/12) psi_(c,beta)(t), psi_(a,c)(t)=nu(a-c) exp[-4*pi*i*c_b*a*(t-c_b(a+c))]/Phi_b(t-2c_b(a+c)), nu(r)=exp[-pi*i*c_b^2*(4r+1)/6], c_b=i(b+b^(-1))/2. With charges (2), the true kernel identity, including its contour, is integral_R f_4(Y-t)f_2(t)f_0(Z-t) exp[2*pi*i*(Y-t)(Z-t)]dt =mu_b f_1(Z)f_3(Y), mu_b=exp(pi*i*c_b^2*P/3), P=2(c_0+a_2+c_4)-1/2. (4) The proof in the cited note starts with the defining full function, Fourier inversion and its two shifts; its published proof is not a premise. The positive charges give an absolutely convergent real contour. For real b, |mu_b|=1; its exact phase remains attached. At b=N^(-1/2), set Y=sqrt(N)*y_0, Z=sqrt(N)*z_0, t=sqrt(N)*tau, y_0=log|y|/(2*pi), z_0=log|x|/(2*pi), tau_*=log|H|/(2*pi). (5) The REAL integration contour therefore passes through the geometric normal point. This is a specified actual local cycle, not an unspecified formal saddle or global knot thimble. To verify its selection, use the exact full-Psi conversion f_j(sqrt(N)*v)=C_(j,N) exp(2*pi*(N+1)c_j*v) /Psi_N(2*pi*v+2*pi*i*(1+1/N)a_j), C_(j,N)=exp[-pi*i/12+pi*i*c_b^2*chi_j], chi_j=4c_j(c_j+beta_j)-(4(c_j-beta_j)+1)/6. (6) All C_(j,N) have modulus one. The uniform full-Psi symbol on its selected strip gives, uniformly in real v, f_j(sqrt(N)*v)=C_(j,N) A_j(v) exp(F_j(v)/h)(1+O(1/N)), h=2*pi*i/N, F_j(v)=-Li_2(exp(2*pi*v+2*pi*i*a_j))+4*pi^2*i*c_j*v, A_j(v)=exp(2*pi*c_j*v) (1-exp(2*pi*v+2*pi*i*a_j))^(a_j-1/2). (7) All branches are the selected upper-strip branches. The first derivative grows at most linearly at infinity and is included in A_j; the next derivatives and the full-Psi relative remainder are uniform there. The amplitudes have at most exp(C|v|) growth. The three-side leading phase is W(tau)=F_4(y_0-tau)+F_2(tau)+F_0(z_0-tau) -4*pi^2*(y_0-tau)(z_0-tau). (8) For each factor the negative imaginary part is the radial Legendre function Im Li_2(s)-2*pi*c_j*log|s|. It is STRICTLY convex in its real log radius, with its unique minimum at the shape s_j. The three minima occur simultaneously at tau=tau_*. Thus Re(W/(2*pi*i)) has its unique global maximum on the entire REAL line at tau_*. Its limiting slopes have strict signs, uniformly on compact positive families, so its tails have a linear gap. The chirp in (8) is real on this contour and does not alter the modulus. The COMPLEX derivative also vanishes: it is 2*pi times Log(1-s_2)-Log(1-s_0)-Log(1-s_4)+Log s_0+Log s_4, which is zero by the identities and angle marks above. Moreover G=-W''(tau_*)/(2*pi*i) =-2*pi*i*(2+sum_(j=0,2,4)s_j/(1-s_j)), Re G=2*pi*sum_(j=0,2,4) Im(s_j)/|1-s_j|^2>0. (9) The real-contour Gaussian has its unambiguous square root Re G>0. Its leading term is C_(0,N)C_(2,N)C_(4,N) A_0 A_2 A_4 sqrt(2*pi/G) exp(W(tau_*)/h)(1+O(1/N)). (10) The sqrt(N) measure in (5) cancels the Gaussian N^(-1/2). Every factor is nonzero and bounded above/below on a compact positive family. The strict global modulus gap proves that the REAL local move cycle selects this geometric block with coefficient +1; its other normal ends are lower. This is stronger than just checking det G is nonzero. Its rate in THIS charged-kernel orientation is -[D(x)+D(y)]/(2*pi). No sign is changed to fit a different knot-state normalization. The exact identity (4) carries the selected block to the two-side product with multiplier mu_b. This is a nonzero tame map of the local geometric kernel lines; it does not create a nonzero global exterior source coefficient. ## 3. Which complete sources pass through this move unchanged For the multiplicative variables r_4=exp(2*pi*b*(Y-t)), r_2=exp(2*pi*b*t), r_0=exp(2*pi*b*(Z-t)), the internal torus acts by (r_4,r_2,r_0)->(lambda^(-1)r_4,lambda r_2,lambda^(-1)r_0). Its boundary invariants are U=r_2 r_4=exp(2*pi*b*Y), V=r_2 r_0=exp(2*pi*b*Z). The explicit coordinate change r_4=U/r_2, r_0=V/r_2 proves C[r_4^+-1,r_2^+-1,r_0^+-1]^(G_m) =C[U^+-1,V^+-1]. (11) A Laurent monomial source has internal character delta=h_2-h_4-h_0. It descends to these common scalar boundary ports if and only if delta=0. A general source descends exactly when all its nonzero Laurent coefficients have character zero. Character delta instead gives r_2^delta times a boundary function; this is a specified twisted line, not a removable scalar by fiat. For a descending complete source, (4) may be paired with its SAME exterior boundary functional. Finite Cauchy/window factors, original cap factors and external full-Psi circle/ray integrals are all carried by linearity and the stated Fubini/continuation conditions. Intervals may first be evaluated to their finite polynomial to check (11), then reinserted exactly; individual fractional-interval integrands need not descend separately. No radial or interval endpoint term is dropped in this procedure. On a compact common holomorphy chamber this is ordinary analytic contraction; a continuation outside it must keep its transported contour and residues. The precise conclusion is a kernel-line transport: if a matched exterior source has geometric coefficient c_N on one side, its coefficient on the other is mu_b c_N in the stated trivializations. It may be zero on both sides. If charges are themselves integrated, the known phase mu_b stays INSIDE that functional; it is not pulled out as though it were constant. ## 4. The original source law, checked on the actual reduced graph The original moment/head graph has positive-factorial atomic orders reflected by d=N-1. At a cap-free trivalent vertex its three atomic arrows are oriented the SAME way, with the original head charge plus or minus d. Its exact law is h_0+h_4+h_2=d, (12) not unshifted scalar descent. For example one positive crossing's nine atom slots in traversal order have the actual internal laws h_0+h_1+h_3=d, h_2+h_4+h_6=d, h_3+h_4+h_5=d, h_5+h_7+h_8=d. Each triple has one positive-factorial edge. This holds pointwise in the external moment/Gaussian variables, independently of the full-Psi coefficient values or choice of circle/ray piece. It is an incidence equation of the original full source, not a condition imposed only at its geometric critical point. There is an exact global unreflection. For each positive-factorial kernel put s=z_out/z_in and write N s^d K_N(Q/(s t)) =N Q^d t^(-d) K_N(Q^(-1)t s). (13) This is the polynomial reversal K_N(v)=v^d K_N(v^(-1)). Equivalently replace its atomic order h by a=d-h, reverse its incidence edge, and put r=t^(-1). The explicit factor NQ^d t^(-d) is retained as part of the REFLECTED FIELD density. It must not be called tame uniformly in t or deleted. All reflected-factorial head charges cancel. Every cap-free internal head vertex now has ZERO Kirchhoff charge; the original cup/cap charges remain at the boundary. At a trivalent vertex (12) becomes a=h_0+h_4, exactly the descent equation (11) in the corresponding oriented variables. Higher-valence head vertices keep their full zero-charge Kirchhoff equation rather than being called a single pentagon port. In incidence notation, if v_e is a reflected-factorial edge column, gamma its original head charge and h_e=d-a_e, then gamma+sum v_e h_e becomes gamma'=gamma+d sum_F v_e with reversed columns -v_e on F. The original reflected monomials are exactly -d sum_F v_e; therefore gamma' consists ONLY of the original boundary charges. This proves the law for every strict original word. The audit checks it after actual Hardy-forest contraction for both signs and longer original words, retaining their original source boundary rows. The finite marked full-Phi clock fixes the affine phase precisely: Psi_+(h(a+1))=phi_N/F_a, phi_N=sqrt(N)exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. Thus the unreflected head a is marked by a+1, never by the bottom zero mark. If a=b+k and all three clocks are so marked, their exact relation is Q^(a+1)=Q^(-1)Q^(b+1)Q^(k+1). The Q^(-1) and phi_N are retained. They cannot be removed because their classical limits look simpler. ## 5. The actual reflected full-Phi field AND its ray Let r=t^(-1), S=Log r, b=N^(-1/2). The original full-Phi inversion identity gives the exact reflected field formula Psi_+(-S)=zeta_b exp[pi*i*(sqrt(N)S/(2*pi)+c_b)^2] Psi_-(S), zeta_b=exp[-pi*i*(1+2c_b^2)/6]. (14) Equivalently Psi_-(S)=(1-r)(1-r^N)/Psi_+(S). This displays the full central norm when the opposite orientation is written as an inverse; it is not permission to invert a vanishing factor separately. Combining the character in (13) with (14) yields r^d Psi_+(-S)=zeta_b exp(pi*i*c_b^2) exp[i*N*S^2/(4*pi)+(N-3)S/2] Psi_-(S). (15) The prefactor is unit modulus at real b; the Gaussian and linear action in (15) are explicit and may be exponentially significant. The source CIRCLE maps to |r|=R^(-1), with its reversed logarithmic parameter, and density NQ^d r^d Psi_+(-S). The original negative RAY does not become the standard inner negative ray. It becomes r in (-infinity,-R^(-1)), +NQ^d/(2*pi*i) Psi_+(-S) dr/r^2, S=log|r|-i*pi. (16) Equation (16) uses N-d=1 exactly. Its tail at negative infinity is the image of the original integrable zero end. Thus (13)--(16) carry the COMPLETE original circle/ray/window source, with no endpoint discarded and no unspecified exponential matrix frame. ## 6. The exact internal fiber still needing contour transport For the actual sink triple consisting of a reciprocal U coefficient, a V coefficient and the reflected F field, strip its constant NQ^d and use the boundary invariants U=r t_U, V=r t_V. Its field is F_N(L;U,V)=r^d Psi_-(Log U-L) Psi_+(Log V-L) Psi_+(-L), r=exp L. (17) Its exact q-step and central norm are F_N(L+h)/F_N(L) =Q^d (1-Q^(-1)V/r)(1-Q^(-1)/r)/(1-U/r), h=2*pi*i/N, F_N(L+2*pi*i)/F_N(L) =(r^N-V^N)(r^N-1)/[r^N(r^N-U^N)]. (18) These follow from the original full-Psi steps, or by multiplying the first equation over its complete Q orbit. The factor r^d gives the retained 2*pi*i logarithmic mark in the classical phase. Its stationary algebraic relation is r=V/(1+V-U). (19) There is an exact classical/central compatibility worth recording. Put R=r^N, U_0=U^N and V_0=V^N. If M_N denotes the central ratio in (18), then M_N-1=-[(1+V_0-U_0)R-V_0]/[R(R-U_0)]. (19a) Thus its multiplier-one locus is the Frobenius copy of precisely the linear stationary gluing polynomial (19). This is a genuine local support candidate. The original relative coefficient source can be inhomogeneous under this shift, so (19a) alone does not place that source on M_N=1 or remove either denominator divisor. The denominator and all full norm factors are retained. Equations (17)--(18) specify the twisted beta/Pochhammer fiber of the actual source, including its 0/0/infinity-Hankel origin. The arbitrary positive charged REAL contour of Section 2 cannot simply be assigned to this field. Transporting that fiber, or a normalized root residue/derivative of it, into the positive separating contour with its complete monodromy is the remaining local cycle problem. The [subsequent exact source theorem](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md) does not guess this adapter: it pushes the complete coefficient source to a single circle/outer-Hankel current, then to an explicit NONZERO balanced norm-pole block plus a uniformly bounded Barnes factor times the full norm. It also gives a positive-bipyramid example where the scalar fiber remains bounded; a universal positive volume rate does not follow without its exterior source. ## 7. Exact difference transport of nonzero internal source characters For completeness the charged kernel has an exact boundary observable map. Put q=exp(2*pi*i*b^2) and alpha_j=exp(-4*pi*b*c_b*c_j), D_j=q^(-1/2)exp[-4*pi*b*c_b(c_j+beta_j)]. The original full-Phi shift gives f_j(x-i b)=alpha_j f_j(x)/(1+D_j exp(2*pi*b*x)), f_j(x+i b)=alpha_j^(-1)(1+q D_j exp(2*pi*b*x))f_j(x). For the three-factor integrand K(Y,Z;t) in (4), z=exp(2*pi*b*t), U=exp(2*pi*b*Y), V=exp(2*pi*b*Z), this yields POINTWISE z K=[alpha_4 V T_(Y+i b)-q D_4 U]K, (z+D_4 U)T_(Y-i b)K=alpha_4 V K. (20) Thus every positive polynomial source in z has an explicit boundary difference operator. For J_h=integral z^(-h)K dt, negative powers obey (alpha_4 V-D_4 U T_(Y-i b))J_h =T_(Y-i b)J_(h-1). (21) This is a source extension, not an instruction to invert that difference operator or discard its kernel. Integrated boundary shifts carry their translated contours and any residues. In particular degree O(N) shifts cannot be declared harmless from a fixed-degree pole-free contour argument. At b=N^(-1/2) the negative-power integrals themselves converge for 0<=h<=d: their left scaled-tail exponent is 2*pi*((N+1)-h), since c_2+beta_0+beta_4=1. Their right tail only improves. This keeps the affine +1 in the source law; it does not prove uniqueness or a tame scalar inverse of (21). The local positive kernel-line transport, the exact original unreflection/descent and the outstanding fiber transport have been kept distinct. Completing the last step is necessary before using the positive contour as the original knot source's cycle or claiming its geometric coefficient survives the move.

title: Independent audit of the positive-carry completion and its source scope
text: # Independent audit of the positive-carry completion and its source scope 27 October 2026. The proposed Euler completion of an actual crossing does preserve the ENTIRE first-cut matrix of every signed braid at an original root, as a meridian family. The correcting group has nilpotence bounded by braid width, independent of N. This is a genuinely general source-preserving completion, unlike a low-degree approximation of the quantum factorials. Two scopes must be retained. Local degree-lowering Ward coupons can detect its positive-carry error. Also the naive generic-Q Euler factorization changes the actual q-normal source, already at N=2. There is a direct repair with explicit normal coupons; at fixed normal depth their combined correction group is still uniformly nilpotent. No geometric-sector or volume estimate follows from nilpotence alone. ## 1. Physical integer degree proves root source preservation Use the actual balanced nilpotent heads, x=-M/q and Q=q^2 of exact order N. Put F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The actual two-leg fusion sends f^a e_k to f_total^a(e_0 tensor e_k). Every physical term of that vector has TOTAL INTEGER DEGREE a+k, not its reduction modulo N. The exact actual positive-crossing coefficient is a_+=sum_(a+k<N) x^-a d_k f^a e_k/F_a, d_k=(-1)^k x^(-2k)Q^(k(k-1)/2). The common original Cartan scalar is retained externally or on both matrices. Its Euler completion is a_+^E=u_N(x^-1 f) D, D=sum_k d_k e_k, with all a,k between zero and N-1, including a+k>=N. For a right coefficient f^a e_k to act on a relative input f^b e_j, the multiplication rule requires j=a+k modulo N. If a+k<N, input and output integer degrees agree. If a+k>=N, its output degree is input degree PLUS N. The action is zero when a+b>=N. Thus, in physical matrices, R_+^E=R_+ + E_N, E_N raises integer degree exactly N. (1) This uses the actual ROOT Borel intertwining/fusion proof. It holds for every admissible meridian x, not just M=1. For b strands let A_>=0 be the algebra of matrices whose degree changes are nonnegative multiples of N, and let n contain its strictly positive-degree matrices. Original crossings are of degree zero, so both the completed crossings and their inverses belong to A_>=0. In fact n^b=0, (2) because the physical total degree is between zero and b(N-1), whereas b positive carries would raise it by at least bN. The inverse assertion follows either by graded triangularity or the finite inverse of 1+n after factoring out the actual crossing. It holds for every signed word, with no restriction on word length. The completed word differs from the original by an element of n. Close all but the first strand with their original pivots. A possibly nonzero cut entry from first input a to first output c would have total degree change c-a, which lies strictly between -N and N. It cannot be a positive multiple of N. Consequently ptr_original(W^E-W)=0 (3) as the FULL N-by-N cut matrix. Hence every original first-input probe and the original all-ones output row agree. Every framing, full d_N(M), peripheral and external Cartan factor multiplies both sides unchanged. Equation (3) is an identity of root-level meridian rational families, including their retained regular germs; it is not obtained by replacing d_N by its complete value. This does not conflict with the full Borel source-faithfulness theorem. That theorem allows relative coupons of negative as well as positive N-degree. The present source quotient is only on the degree-restricted algebra A_>=0. Lowering an error back to degree zero is deliberately not an allowed operation there. The group 1+n has lower-central depth at most b-1, with finite logarithm and inverse formulas. Braid/coherence errors of the completed matrices lie in that group since their degree-zero parts are the actual braid matrices. Their original closed sources vanish by (3). This supplies an algebraic completion of the actual source; it supplies no bound for the entries of the degree-zero word or its hyperbolic action. ## 2. A local Ward coupon detects the carry At N=2, M=1 use x=i and remove only the shared Cartan scalar from the positive crossing. In physical basis 00,01,10,11, R_+^E-R_+=-i |11><00|. (4) Its original pivotal partial trace is zero. But use the literal balanced closed-wire Ecal=-2|0><1| and pivot diag(-i,i). The original first-input-zero/all-ones-output source gives ell ptr_g[(I tensor Ecal)(R_+^E-R_+)]e_0=2. (5) Restoring the common Cartan scalar multiplies this by the same nonzero original scalar. The full regular complete dimension and framing factors do not make it zero. Thus a single local degree-minus-one coupon can expose a positive N-carry through an off-diagonal first-cut row. One cannot replace the entire Hopf/Ward source complex by the quotient in (3). Global Hopf-adjoint partial-trace identities may still cancel their complete sums, because all their coupled terms are kept. Equation (5) says the individual local terms cannot be deleted. Meridian M shifts and derivatives, in contrast, do not change integer degrees, so the root-family equality (3) preserves them. A moving-q normal needs the separate correction below. ## 3. An explicit generic-Q counterexample and repair The same finite fusion kernel and Euler/path formulas are well-defined matrices for generic Q, with F_1,...,F_(N-1) units. They are not automatically a generic-q Hopf fusion. At N=2 the Euler matrix calculated from those formulas is R^E(Q,x)=[[1,0,0,0], [0,0,x^-1,0], [0,x^-1,1-x^-2,0], [-x^-3,0,0,-x^-2]]. The actual generic-q compressed crossing has the same first three rows but final row (0,0,0,Q*x^-2). Therefore R^E-R_actual=-x^-3 |11><00| -(Q+1)x^-2 |11><11|. (6) Only the first term survives at Q=-1. Off root the second is of degree ZERO and is visible to the full cut. With the same original pivot diag(x^-1,Q/x), the cut difference is -Q(Q+1)x^-3 E_(1,1). For the actual averaged all-ones source its first Q-normal at Q=-1, with D_Q=Q partial_Q, is -1/(2x^3) !=0. (7) Allowing x to vary with Q does not alter (7), since the source difference itself vanishes identically in x at the root. This is an explicit failure of the naive Euler extension to preserve the actual whole q-normal germ, not just a missing proof. The repair in this example is the RETAINED normal coupon R^sharp=R^E+(Q+1)x^-2 |11><11|, after which R^sharp-R_actual has only positive carry. Calling Q=-1 before taking the normal derivative would erase that coupon and give the wrong source in (7). ## 4. General normal repair and bounded nilpotence at fixed jet depth There is a direct matrix construction at every N. The generic fusion kernel preserves its integer degree exactly, and the right path matrix has only changes 0 or +N. Hence its generic Euler matrix R^E(Q,x) has only these two grades. Write pi_0, pi_>0 for those degree projections and set Delta_N=R_actual-pi_0 R^E, R^sharp=R^E+Delta_N =R_actual+pi_>0 R^E. (8) Then R^sharp has the actual degree-zero part and the Euler completion's positive-carry part for ALL Q on this chart. The proof of (3) now applies to R^sharp before root specialization, including its inverse and full normal jets. This is not a claim that R^sharp is an uncorrected Euler factorization or a full Hopf intertwiner. Delta_N vanishes at every primitive Nth root by (1). In the localized coefficient ring where intermediate factorials are units, it is divisible by delta=1-Q^N: Delta_N=delta Z_N, Z_N regular there. (9) Indeed all proper-divisor cyclotomic factors of 1-Q^N are already units; the remaining primitive cyclotomic factor divides the regular matrix difference. The normalized original crossing and the generic kernel here have rational Q,x entries; the shared full Cartan line is retained separately on both sides. At finite Q-normal depth J, work modulo delta^(J+1). In the nonnegative N-graded matrix algebra the ideal j=(delta,n) satisfies the uniform bound j^(b+J)=0. (10) Each term of a product of length b+J either contains at least b positive carries or at least J+1 central delta factors. Thus the actual-to-Euler correction lies in a unipotent group of depth bounded independently of N at fixed b,J. Units and their inverses are regular near the root. This is a useful bounded transport statement for actual finite normal data. The source DOES see the delta*Z_N terms, as (7) proves.
