This follows from degree, not an arbitrary quotient of the entire Borel commutant: partial closure would need first-output minus first-input at least N, impossible in the original N-head. All original meridian, dimension and framing factors remain assigned as before. An arbitrary negative-degree coupon can detect n_b. Thus n_b is not a null ideal in the entire endomorphism algebra, and (2) does not license keeping local E/F coupons unchanged. The transport below supplies the missing corrections explicitly. ## 2. Quantum-normal jets and a uniform finite correction depth Choose the marked original root and its normal coordinate delta=1-Q^N. The local coefficient ring contains the original meridian parameters and is regular in delta where F_r=(Q;Q)_r, 0<r<N, are units. All other original poles and source lattices remain specified; they are not discarded by working in the generic meridian coefficient field. Treat the common scalar/Hom lines in their original compatible frames. Continue the displayed finite Euler matrices by their explicit finite kernels at generic Q. They still have shifts zero and N, but their zero-degree part differs from the actual compressed crossing off root. The [independent normal audit](positive_carry_completion_independent_audit.md) proves that this difference is divisible by delta locally. For example at N=2 the extra zero-degree term is proportional to Q+1. Its first q-normal source is nonzero. On jets modulo delta^(J+1), set j=(delta F_b)+n_b. Then j^(b+J)=0, R_i^E-R_i belongs to j. (3) Every product of b+J generators either contains b positive degree shifts or J+1 factors delta. Both possibilities vanish. This proves (3) without assuming that the continued compressed matrices form a Hopf representation away from the root. Both R_i and R_i^E are invertible on the local chart, including their literal negative crossings, and have the same image modulo j. Thus their relative units belong to 1+j. If the bare co-source is to stay unchanged off root, one can instead use the explicitly repaired operators R_i^sharp=R_i+pi_(>0)R_i^E =R_i^E+[R_i-pi_0 R_i^E]. (4) Their correction is the retained degree-zero normal coupon delta Z_i. They preserve the original bare cut matrix as whole meromorphic q/meridian families by (1). They are Euler matrices plus this known normal correction, rather than uncorrected Euler matrices. Equations (3) and (4) give two compatible ways to retain the normal data; neither deletes that coupon. ## 3. Prefix gauges solve the word transport exactly Write the signed actual prefix in action order as W_j=R_j ... R_1, W_j^E=R_j^E ... R_1^E, W_0=W_0^E=I. Define the explicit relative prefix unit G_j=W_j^E W_j^-1, G_0=I. (5) By (3), G_j belongs to 1+j and R_j^E=G_j R_j G_(j-1)^-1. (6) This follows by multiplying the two adjacent prefix formulas; it includes negative letters as literal inverses. There is no unknown knot scalar in (5). The original source fixes the initial frame G_0=I. If another initial unit is specified, the same recurrence determines every G_j; the set of comparisons is a pointed torsor under the initial group 1+j. Put L=b+J. Every inverse and logarithm in this comparison is an honest finite expression, for example G_j^-1=sum_(r=0)^(L-1)(I-G_j)^r, log G_j=sum_(r=1)^(L-1)(-1)^(r+1)(G_j-I)^r/r. (7) The group 1+j has nilpotence class at most L-1, by its successive ideal-power filtration. This is bounded for fixed braid index and jet depth. It is the COMPLETION-ERROR group, not a claim that the whole actual braid transport group is nilpotent or that its semisimple part has disappeared. ## 4. Arbitrary coupons and the original co-source have exact transports For a coupon X_j acting at level j use X_j^E=G_j X_j G_j^-1. (8) There is no degree restriction on X_j. Composing (6) and (8) telescopes every internal gauge. If A is the resulting actual network, the Euler network with these transported coupons is A^E=G_m A G_0^-1. (9) Write the original full source as Phi(A)=Tr(D A); for example D includes the original first-input/output row and every pivotal closure. Its transported co-source is D^E=G_0 D G_m^-1. (10) Ordinary matrix trace cyclicity now proves the exact pointed network identity Tr(D^E A^E)=Tr(D A) (11) in the assigned coefficient/source lattice, at every jet order under consideration. The same formula applies entry by entry to the co-source family extracting the entire first-cut matrix. An externally retained peripheral/dimension/framing line multiplies both sides identically. No factor such as 1+M^(2N) is replaced by its complete numerical value during this transport. At the root with no non-weight-preserving insertions, (2) lets one keep the original bare source: its extra terms are invisible by degree. At positive normal depth or with arbitrary coupons, (10) is essential. The numerical witnesses show that omitting it can change the period. The co-source in (10) is explicit but generally nonlocal and word-dependent. No factorized local-cap or diagram-independent matrix formula is asserted for it. Although j is not an ideal on the FULL coupon algebra, this does not obstruct finite coupon transport. If B_j=log G_j, then B_j^L=0 as a matrix and (ad B_j)^(2L-1)(X)=0 for EVERY matrix X. In the binomial expansion, each term contains B_j^L on at least one side. Thus (8) can equivalently be computed with at most 2L-2 nested commutators. This is the uniform finite correction to local current coupons, including ones that could detect the positive carry before transport. ## 5. Ward defects, meridian maps and normal source lattices The original finite matrices specify the actual current/Ward rows and, away from a genuine Hopf fiber, their actual defects. Transport those generator matrices too: rho_j^E=G_j rho_j G_j^-1. Their local defect obeys the exact naturality identity rho_j^E R_j^E-R_j^E rho_(j-1)^E =G_j[rho_j R_j-R_j rho_(j-1)]G_(j-1)^-1. (12) This transports the actual defect, rather than asserting that it vanishes off root. Every specified Hopf-adjoint/current expression follows by the same multiplication/inverse naturality with its original endpoint terms and ordered coproduct retained. It does not make the old fixed Hopf action the action in the new Euler frame at every prefix. With the stipulated pointed initial frame G_0=I, a two-fiber meridian map K(M',M)=W(M')W(M)^-1 becomes K^E(M',M)=G_m(M') K(M',M) G_m(M)^-1. (13) For the logarithmic meridian connection this is A_M^E=(D_M G_m)G_m^-1+G_m A_M G_m^-1, A_M=(D_M W)W^-1. (14) These are physical finite-matrix statements and do not assume that a longitude insertion is Borel-linear in one color fiber. The assigned external meridian scalar adapter remains on its original line. Equations (11)-(14) preserve the actual source identities, hence every required fixed normal jet and meridian transport at this stage of the comparison. The source lattice matters if external rational factors have a normal pole. Either take jets in their originally assigned line lattice, or retain enough extra normal orders before multiplying by a pole of order p. A desired numerical depth J can then require depth J+p upstream, with bound b+J+p in (3). This does not permit specializing a zero-over-zero peripheral factor before its whole product has been formed. The proof uses invertible fixed-width braid prefixes. Cups, caps or stabilization maps are not asserted to be invertible prefix gauges. Their original closure is retained as D, and root invariant equality for any braid presentation follows from (2), not from inventing an off-root braided category. ## 6. What this removes on the critical path There is now a concrete exact whole-word map from the original quantum state and its current/jet sources to the Euler-completed presentation. The algebraic comparison equations are solved in bounded nilpotent depth; this does not rest on Hilbert 90 being assumed to control a growing matrix frame. The bare root period already agrees at arbitrary braid index, and the normal/current source corrections are explicit in (7)-(14). The bound concerns nilpotent DEPTH. It is not a bound for matrix dimension, coefficient degree or operator norm as N grows. It therefore does not prove subexponential source normalization, a nonzero selected hyperbolic image, or the sharp logarithmic growth. The remaining comparison must carry this specified Euler word and co-source to the marked geometric A-period. The general original volume conjecture remains unproved. [The exact jet audit](../experiments/audit_prefix_euler_source_jet_gauge.py) and [saved output](../experiments/prefix_euler_source_jet_gauge_results.json) use the actual generic-Q N=2 crossings, their literal inverses, the full original pivotal source and inserted negative-degree coupons. Twenty-four cases cover braid indices two through four, two colors and depths J=0,1,2. They verify 66 prefix comparisons, 174 transported coupon/source-jet identities and the stated nilpotence. The tests detect 122 bare coupon failures and eight bare quantum-normal source failures, all repaired by the proved transport. The all-N, all-width theorem rests on (1)-(14).

title: Extending the proved pretzel argument to general source networks
text: # Extending the proved pretzel argument to general source networks 29 October 2026. The main route is the proved pretzel mechanism: estimate the whole original source, prove survival of its geometric contribution, and identify that contribution with the actual complete or filled hyperbolic metric. The cube calculations and alternative positive circuits are retained as tests and possible ingredients. They do not replace the general objective. ## What is already proved in the pretzel case The [complete augmented pretzel theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) covers every fixed odd width s>=3, both level parities and all original normal terms. Its explicitly weighted Fourier energy has the sharp volume rate. The original marked row has polynomial dual cost, and a separate coherent calculation proves a nonzero period with only a polynomial overlap loss. Weighted Cauchy gives an upper bound; that last calculation supplies the matching lower bound. The [filled-source proof](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), with the [whole-color width improvement](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md), covers fixed odd widths s>=9 with independently sufficiently long fixed signed fillings. The geometric part is the [Casson--Rivin equality proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) on the actual filled-slope angle slice, including smooth end completion. It does not maximize the unfilled volume instead. The Karamata suggestion led to useful positive-energy and transport questions. The [separate Tauberian criterion](actual_fourier_energy_tauberian_criterion.md) is not a missing hypothesis silently assumed in the pretzel proof: the latter establishes its whole-source estimates and nonzero asymptotic directly. A cumulative Tauberian law alone would still need cross-level control to give a limit at every N. ## A general part of the weighted-Cauchy construction is now complete On every supported six-head source cell the prescribed positive correlated Gram H has actual costs ||v_j||_H^2=K_j, ||lambda_j||_(H^-1)^2=tau_j^2 K_j. Here tau_j is the explicitly evaluated positive marked top moment. The [whole-support theorem](actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.md) now proves K_j<=poly(N) uniformly over EVERY supported folded triple, including saturation boundaries, high partners, simple axes, and both parities. This removes the former central-corridor restriction. The Gram is determined by the original local source and marked row, before choosing an exterior graph. Its proof compares the entire finite Racah sum, including its second-root-zero terms, to a positive midpoint term. A global sine-product inequality replaces the need for a uniform tail gap. Thus this step transfers beyond the one-dimensional pretzel corridor. The exact [three-port sewing identity](actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) also already holds for the whole complete-circle source: Z_new=sum_j Z_A(j) Z_B(j)/Z_theta(j). The sum is over supported triples and Z_theta(j)>0. Defining F_A(j)=Z_A(j)/sqrt(Z_theta(j)) and similarly F_B gives the actual bilinear contraction sum_j F_A(j)F_B(j), and therefore |Z_new|^2 <= (sum_j |F_A(j)|^2)(sum_j |F_B(j)|^2). All shared colors remain correlated. This algebraic rewrite neither computes the two energies nor ensures that their bilinear overlap is nonzero. After the three complete circles act, each regular cell is observed through its top monomial; local Gram conditioning must not be presented as a bound on the exterior's unknown scalar response. ## The remaining general theorem must control the transported energy For an original graph source written as K_N=b_N v_N, a useful metric must establish both b_N G_N^-1 b_N^* <= exp(o(N)), v_N^* G_N v_N <= exp[N Vol(M)/pi+o(N)]. It must also prove geometric survival, equivalently no exponential loss in the original source pairing at the geometric contribution. The pretzel proof does all three jobs in its explicit Fourier frame. For branching, the unresolved operation is transport between different pair decompositions while retaining the correlated metric, phases, boundary currents and common physical normal parameter. Polynomial local costs alone do not make this transport isometric. Nor can one multiply local theta rates and omit a global contribution: the [actual graph geometry](actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md) has volume 4b v8+2 Vol(Q). The positive cube period explicitly detects that extra core term in a specified original sector. It is a useful test of any proposed sector-wise energy bound, while its full color sum remains an independent task. ## The geometric conclusion has a general finite certificate The [source-volume certificate](source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md) applies beyond pretzels once the actual source supplies a positive angle point on the actual triangulation, an absolute equality of its action with tetrahedral volume, and stationarity on the FULL edge and peripheral angle slice. Strict concavity then gives its unique global maximum; the decoration and end checks give the actual hyperbolic metric. A stationary point on a smaller source slice is insufficient. The next decisive estimate is therefore the sharp energy of the coherently transported source, with a nonzero geometric overlap. The full-support boundary theorem is a completed input to that work; it is not yet the general volume equality. ## New local transport and geometry inputs The [general actual inverse kernel](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) now has a source-normalized one-sum expression and an exact finite conversion to the seven-factorial convention. Its row/column gauge to the four-face scalar normalization is explicit. The [supported scalar theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) keeps the common root phase and bounds every fixed generic normal of the low-fold scalar at polynomial relative cost. The [local hyperideal geometry](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) proves the actual volume and all six length derivatives of that normalized action. This supplies a sharp local candidate density for weighted Cauchy. It is not the full confluent operator metric: paired coefficients have genuine poles before their partners are combined, and the high-partner [2N] terms have nonzero normal currents. The four supported faces alone also fail to determine a global geometric saddle: every interior color derivative of the normalized action is positive. The missing global incidence/boundary constraints are therefore substantive, not just a volume normalization constant. The [positive Conway variational theorem](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md) retains a complementary route with exact global support. It proves an all-level whole-source limit and a concave angle problem for every fixed robust expression. Its integer-semigroup argument gives every-level survival directly, but its angle problem still needs an actual geometric gluing certificate.

title: Independent audit of the principal-density comparison
text: # Independent audit of the principal-density comparison Audit, 27 October 2026. This checks Sections 5--6 of [the uniform comparison](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md), with particular attention to the perturbation pairing, cokernel marking, determinant signs and the factor -1/2. No substantive defect was found under the printed acyclicity, unit-chart and parity conventions. ## 1. Direct derivation of the rank-two perturbation pairing The pairing in equation (5.8) has the printed positive sign. It can be derived directly from the generating equations, avoiding any ambiguity about exact boundary terms in the Liouville form. Write P_0 for the permutation matrix, R for the transfer matrix, and w=(q,c). At the chosen fixed point, a cut-fixed kernel tangent u has a generating-family lift B_u=(q_u,c_u) and equal input/output momenta p_u. Thus P_0 q_u+R c_u=q_u, S_cq q_u+S_cc c_u=R^t p_u. (1.1) Perturb the phase by epsilon times a quadratic f centered at the critical point, while holding an input tangent v fixed. Let tau be the resulting variation of its transfers and pi the variation of its output momentum. The linearized generating equations are P_0^t pi-S_qc tau=f_q(B_v), S_cc tau-R^t pi=-f_c(B_v). (1.2) The mixed Jacobian is invertible by the stated crossing-unit hypothesis, so these variations exist uniquely. Multiply the first equation by q_u^t, use the second equation to eliminate R^t pi, and then use (1.1). The result is q_u^t pi-p_u^t R tau =q_u^t f_q(B_v)+c_u^t f_c(B_v) =Hess(f)(B_u,B_v). (1.3) The left side is exactly Omega(u,(partial_epsilon F)v), since the output-position variation is R tau and the input is fixed. This proves (5.8), including the cut source: its last covector is the fixed input momentum p_1 and therefore acquires no perturbation. ## 2. Leading determinant coefficients and the endpoint volume For a square map L of corank two, let B be its kernel basis and C its cokernel coordinate map. With the torsion convention in the comparison note, a perturbation L+epsilon E satisfies [epsilon^2] det(L+epsilon E)=det(C E B)/T_L. (2.1) To verify this, use the input basis [B,V_c] and target basis [L V_c,W], C W=I. Moving the two kernel columns past the n-2 image columns contributes (-1)^(2(n-2))=1. The two epsilon columns then give det(C E B), with the indicated torsion ratio. For the symmetric phase Hessian, C=B^t and T_H=det(B_chi)^2/det H_perp. For the endpoint, the rows in (5.5) use coordinate volume, whereas the trailing-normal target volume is its negative. Indeed the target basis (e_qj-e_q1 for j>1, all e_pj), followed by e_q1, has determinant -1 in the canonical order. Consequently the coordinate determinant's leading coefficient is -det(pairing)/T_cut^Omega. Combining (1.3), (2.1) and the nonsingular determinant elimination therefore gives exactly (product V_t) T_H=-T_cut^Omega. The perturbation need not remain a sum of local crossing phases. Its mixed Jacobian stays a unit near epsilon=0; only that unit's constant determinant contributes to the leading epsilon^2 term. This is sufficient for the argument in the source note. ## 3. The two remaining numerical factors For the stated bases of ker ell and ker b_0, the canonical pairing conversion matrix is K^t R(P) Z=[2/a^2 0;(c^2+1)/a^2 1]. Its determinant is 2/a^2. The endpoint torsion with the unconverted product co-source is -T_beta, using the ordered bases printed in Section 3 of the comparison note. Directly differentiating the framing matrix gives its coefficient matrix in K=(h+2f,e+f): C_frame=(1/Delta) [-(kappa/2+s) r-1/2; kappa+s 1-r]. Its determinant is -1/(2Delta). Kernel and canonical cokernel both change by this framing matrix, so the contribution is its square. Thus T_cut^Omega(r,s)=-T_beta/(2a^2 Delta^2). Finally det(-H_perp)=(-1)^(m-1)det H_perp, because the normal rank is m-1. Combining this with the endpoint minus sign and the specified (-1)^(b-1) parity normalization leaves (-1)^(m+b-1)=1 for a knot braid. The remaining amplitude factor is a^2/K_1^2, giving Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2) Omega_cut^2. ## 4. Scope The source and cokernel assumptions needed above are already present: acyclicity of the four-term holonomy complex, ell(Au)=1 for the removed conjugation direction, the actual fixed momentum cut, and the unit mixed Jacobian. A generic equality of critical sets alone would not supply them. The factor -1/2 is relative to the explicitly specified parity normalization and does not choose a square-root phase or its base-only quantum normalization. The audit establishes no nonzero selected global period coefficient and no archimedean volume growth. Those remain separate obligations, as the comparison note states.

title: Projective frame covariance on the normalized period cover
text: # Projective frame covariance on the normalized period cover Research note, 25 October 2026. This resolves the local full-matrix frame comparison left open in `pointed_period_descent.md`. The result uses the explicit Hilbert-90 transport and a determinant rigidity argument, with an identity-frame anchor. It applies to every finite configuration diagram at every odd level. It does not identify a global literature integration cycle or compare different levels, and hence does not prove the volume conjecture. The local tensors are the existing cyclic Weyl/Borel recoupling tensors, with their pointing, roots and measures specified in the preceding notes. No new quantum function is introduced here. All assertions below concern the common nondegenerate algebraic locus, before peripheral specialization. For the component argument take an algebraically closed constant field of characteristic zero, such as C; all matrix identities are algebraic. ## 1. The full projective change has compatible Weyl rescalings Let p_i be distinct nonzero affine flags, and let p_i'=(a p_i+b)/(c p_i+d), ad-bc != 0, d_i=c p_i+d. Assume d_i and p_i' are nonzero. The unscaled triangle algebra from `affine_frame_period_transport.md` has lambda_ijk=(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k), mu_ijk=-(p_i-p_j)/(p_j-p_k). The elementary difference formula for a fractional linear transformation gives exactly lambda_ijk'=(d_j/d_i)lambda_ijk, mu_ijk'=(d_k/d_i)mu_ijk. (1.1) Choose vertex roots D_i^n=d_i. Write kappa_ijk=D_j/D_i, nu_ijk=D_k/D_i. Thus the new triangle algebra is the old one with Weyl generators rescaled to kappa X, nu Y. A common rescaling of the matrix representing the projective transformation cancels in these ratios. Compatible root choices are part of the cover; they are not suppressed. For the tetrahedron write A=023, B=012, C=013, D=123. The six identities kappa_A=kappa_C kappa_D, nu_A=kappa_C nu_D=nu_C, kappa_B=kappa_C=nu_C/nu_D, nu_B=(nu_C/nu_D)kappa_D (1.2) follow just by canceling the vertex roots. The ordered Racah algebra embedding is X_A=X_C X_D, Y_A=X_C Y_D+Y_C, X_B=X_C+Y_CY_D^(-1), Y_B=-Y_CY_D^(-1)X_D. Equations (1.2) show that rescaling all four triangle algebras commutes with this embedding, including the two different terms in each sum. This is a full quantum-operator assertion, valid at generic q. It is the step needed before Schur rigidity can legitimately be invoked. ## 2. Explicit triangle intertwiners and their composition The old triangle module has endpoints u=A_j/A_k, v=A_i/A_k, with A_i^n=p_i. Choose new A_i'^n=p_i' and the new endpoints u',v'. In the monomial bases define K by (K f)(y)=f(y/kappa). After this basis rescaling the old generators kappa X, nu Y act as multiplication y and Y_0=(v_0-u_0 y)sigma^(-1), u_0=nu*u/kappa, v_0=nu*v. They have the new central character (lambda',mu'). The desired new module has Y'=(v'-u'y)sigma^(-1), at the same character. Choose an old marked spectral root alpha^n=lambda, and the new root alpha'=kappa alpha. Section 1 of the affine transport note constructs the exact norm-one intertwiner H from (u_0,v_0) to (u',v'), normalized by H(alpha')=1. Then S=H K, S(kappa X)=X' S, S(nu Y)=Y' S. (2.1) This is an explicit n by n matrix on the endpoint, vertex-root and marked-spectrum cover. Its scalar has been fixed; invertibility is proved by the norm-one recurrence, not assumed from an unspecified period. These unnormalized S matrices compose strictly when root data compose. Indeed their product implements the product rescaling and, after removing the product K, still has value one at the final marked root: H_2(alpha_2)H_1(alpha_2/kappa_2)=1. Uniqueness of the normalized intertwiner proves the composition law. On forgetting the marked root one obtains the scalar line and deck transformations described earlier. ## 3. Projective covariance first holds up to an explicit scalar line Let R(p):V_A tensor V_B -> V_C tensor V_D be the pointed general-endpoint Racah map. The two maps R(p') (S_A tensor S_B), (S_C tensor S_D) R(p) (3.1) intertwine the same rescaled full matrix algebra, by (1.2) and (2.1). The source and target are irreducible modules for that n^2 by n^2 matrix algebra. Therefore the two maps differ by a single nonzero scalar. This conclusion follows after the operator comparison; irreducibility alone would not compare arbitrary selected tensors. The scalar in (3.1) need not be one before normalization. It is an algebraic unit on the indicated cover. The inversion audit computes it exactly, rather than discarding it by evaluating a boundary parameter. ## 4. Shared-face signed normalization retains the pentagon In these unscaled endpoint bases, the determinant of R is det R=f_R^(nh), h=(n-1)/2, f_R=-(p_2/p_3)(p_0-p_2)(p_1-p_3)/(p_1-p_2)^2. (4.1) To see this, use the general two-factor determinant with the right triangle pair C,D: the incoming endpoint on D is A_2/A_3, its lambda is (p_1-p_3)/(p_2-p_3), its mu is -(p_1-p_2)/(p_2-p_3), and the total mu is -(p_0-p_2)/(p_2-p_3). Substitution gives precisely (4.1). This is the unscaled-basis version of the earlier Steinberg determinant; the vertex-frame factor must be retained. On each ordered face put Q_ijk=p_k*(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k)^2. Direct cancellation proves f_R=-(delta Q)^(-1). Choose shared face roots xi_ijk^n=Q_ijk^h and set eta=delta xi. Then eta^n=(-1)^h f_R^(-h), R_hat=eta R, det R_hat=(-1)^h. (4.2) The sign is the literal permutation sign from recoupling, and is the same for all frames. Products of eta cancel on the boundary of a 4-simplex by delta^2=1. Consequently this normalization preserves the exact recoupling pentagon, including its recorded permutations. It is not a choice of independent roots on unrelated tetrahedra. ## 5. Determinant rigidity fixes the full matrix scalar For each triangle choose rho^n=(det S)^(-1), and set S_hat=rho S. Its determinant is one. Include both sets of shared face roots for R_hat(p),R_hat(p') and these rho roots in the finite algebraic cover. The scalar lambda_hat between the two versions of (3.1) now satisfies lambda_hat^(n^2)=1. (5.1) Indeed all tensor-product determinants of the S_hat maps are one, and the two R_hat determinants are the same (-1)^h. This proves (5.1) without taking absolute values or suppressing a generic unit. Fix a lift of the identity projective transformation with D_i=1, A_i'=A_i, alpha'=alpha, rho=1, and identical shared face roots. There S=identity and lambda_hat=1. On any irreducible lifted component containing this anchor, the algebraic function lambda_hat takes values in the finite group mu_(n^2), so it is constant. It is therefore one: R_hat(p') (S_hat_023 tensor S_hat_012) =(S_hat_013 tensor S_hat_123) R_hat(p). (5.2) This is the precise Zariski rigidity argument and its normalization hypothesis. The root covers are finite etale over the nondegenerate open locus. Components containing an identity-frame lift dominate the connected frame locus. Thus this is a generic projective comparison on a cover, not only a statement at the identity or at a finite test point. Other deck lifts retain their root phases; the theorem does not set those phases to one. For any fixed finite flag diagram the same reasoning applies to all its tetrahedra on one common component anchored at the identity data. Normalized intertwiners are arrows of a central root extension of the marked-frame groupoid: the extra rho root composes multiplicatively. Arrows satisfying (5.2) are closed under composition and inverses, by the matrix equation itself. Together with shared-face normalization, this gives local coherent projective transport of finite recoupling diagrams. Interior S_hat maps cancel in a finite contraction using the dual map on its oppositely oriented copy. The boundary tensor and the transported period vectors carry the surviving data. ## 6. Which object has actually been constructed The construction provides a finite-level local period system on generic decorated flag charts: split Weyl modules, actual selected-vector transport, the marked spectral/Heisenberg data, shared-face normalization, and a root extension of projective frame changes. It gives exact five-term recoupling and full projective covariance there. The unit in a chart is not invariant under these transports; its image S_hat*1 is part of the data. The affine note proves this distinction explicitly. A vector chosen in one frame can now be transported coherently on this local cover. This does not yet choose an equivariant global vector for a flat knot local system. This is consistent with the existing matrix-dilogarithm and character-cover framework of [Baseilhac--Benedetti](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) and their [analytic families](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261). We reconstruct the comparisons above directly and do not assume their global proofs. Literal equality to a chosen published matrix normalization has not been established merely by the common recoupling origin. The remaining global problem is to make this local system equivariant for the decorated flat knot local system, retain its peripheral lifts, and match its selected global period with the literature state and cycle. Identifying that period includes its continuous dilogarithm factor, not just the finite splitting module. Its compatibility across levels must then be compared to the Bloch regulator. The present fixed-level rigidity theorem does not imply that comparison or the all-alternating volume conjecture. The subsequent `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md` constructs coherent deck multipliers from peripheral root characters, makes triangle transports strictly equivariant, and corrects the remaining scalar configuration cocycle using relative degree-four vanishing. It retains a relative fundamental-class phase. The continuous target and its exact volume norm are in `boundary_regulator_period.md`. These results still require the selected literature period/cycle and the comparison across levels. The later [source-flag construction](source_flag_transport.md) distinguishes moving the affine origin from holding it fixed. If that origin is retained as a marked source point and transformed with the flags, the relative modules have a unit-preserving monomial projective transport with scalar one. Changing the source point instead gives the nonconstant adapter treated here. Its actual finite-source scalar can now be fixed by edge duality, including cap and cyclic naturality, and its normal coefficient is explicit. This does not change the fixed-origin comparison or identify the global selected knot period and regulator norm.

title: Regular propagated Fourier frames move every wire adapter to the boundary
text: # Regular propagated Fourier frames move every wire adapter to the boundary 28 October 2026. The exact balanced four-Psi crossing permits a useful GLOBAL choice of polarization. For an arbitrary open signed braid, all local Fermat blocks can remain uniformly regular while every INTERIOR Fourier adapter is exactly the identity. Only the original boundary closure/cap co-source needs a change of frame. The number of remaining wire adapters is therefore at most the braid width, independently of the crossing count. This is an exact theorem for the original operator and source, not a selected-geometric-cycle theorem. It moves the explicit WIRE adapters to the boundary. The bulk full-Psi logarithmic seams during an off-grid contour deformation are a distinct issue and are not removed here. ## 1. A regular propagated multisection at arbitrary width At complete color put x=-exp(-pi*i/N), s=x^N=(-1)^(N+1). For b heads choose pairwise distinct nonzero constants c1,...,cb and initial central coordinates sigma_i(0)=s^(i-1)c_i. (1) Choose one marked N-th root r_i(0) of each coordinate. At a positive crossing on heads i,i+1 propagate the actual roots by (r_i,r_(i+1)) -> (x r_(i+1),x r_i). (2) At a negative crossing use the actual antiunitary mirror, hence the root propagation has x^(-1) in place of x. Untouched roots stay fixed. Their central propagation is in BOTH cases (A,B) -> (sB,sA), (3) because s^(-1)=s. All root phases and label permutations are retained. Let D=diag(1,s,...,s^(b-1)), and let P_j be the ordinary permutation of strands after any prefix of the braid. Then the entire vector is sigma(j)=D P_j c. (4) Indeed the signed adjacent interchange (3) is D P_i D^(-1). At the next crossing the regularity condition in [the exact local theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) is B!=sA. Equation (4) gives B-sA=s^i(c_(pi(i+1))-c_(pi(i))) !=0. (5) The permutation never assigns the same initial strand to both heads. Thus EVERY local Fermat chart is regular, for every signed word and every prefix, without any knot census or restriction to twist knots. For example c_i=i+1 gives an explicit choice for all words of width b. All central coordinates then have modulus between 2 and b+1. The local central shape ratios are ratios of two distinct c_i, so their distance from one is at least 1/(b+1). The internal norm T=BD/(D-B) and all other central arguments consequently stay in a fixed compact regular set depending only on b. No parameter depends on the unknown knot value. ## 2. All interior adapters telescope EXACTLY Let F_j be the tensor product of the normalized one-head Fourier frames F(r_i(j)) after prefix j. For the next original crossing R_j, the exact local theorem gives its regular four-Psi kernel M_j=F_j R_j F_(j-1)^(-1). (6) Untouched tensor factors in (6) are identities. This is true for either sign, with the FULL original scalar and marked full-Psi functions. The outgoing frame on every physical wire is by construction precisely its next incoming frame. Hence M_m ... M_1=F_m W F_0^(-1), W=F_m^(-1)(M_m ... M_1)F_0, (7) for the actual word W=R_m...R_1. There is no interior rational adapter, no deformation through a Cauchy pole, and no discarded current in this identity. The positive-degree intermediate allowance in the local construction has already been removed by its exact E-coproduct proof. For an original endpoint vector p and co-source row m, the whole source is therefore m W p=(m F_m^(-1))(M_m ... M_1)(F_0 p). (8) This includes all original pointed-plat cups, ordinary caps and the FULL marked row. For a trace presentation with source operator C, it is Tr(C W)=Tr[(F_0 C F_m^(-1))(M_m ... M_1)]. (9) Use the actual averaged first-cut matrix and original closed pivots in C; no scalarity or replacement of the full marked row is required. All original framing and external scalar factors remain outside the same exact equality. Already specified inserted operators can also be transported by the applicable prefix frames. ## 3. The surviving boundary source has no exponential frame cost The normalized Fourier matrix is a unitary root Fourier matrix times diag(r^a). If r^N=sigma_i(j), then ||F(r)||<=max(1,|c_(pi(i))|), ||F(r)^(-1)||<=max(1,|c_(pi(i))|^(-1)). (10) These bounds are independent of crossing count and N. The phases accumulated by (2) have modulus one. With c_i=i+1, each individual frame and inverse has norm at most b+1. For a one-cut braid closure, the boundary change on head i is the specified finite kernel F(r_i(0))F(r_i(m))^(-1), with central ratio C_i=c_i/c_(pi_W(i)). (11) Its entries are the finite-sum/removable values of [1-C_i]/[N(1-(r_i(0)/r_i(m))Q^(j-k))]. (12) The original pivot adds its retained scalar and label shift. At most b such boundary adapters remain. Each and its inverse have norm bounded by max(1,|C_i|) and max(1,|C_i|^(-1)), respectively. The actual cups, caps and marked source keep their original polynomial norms up to constants depending only on the fixed width and chosen c_i. The rational off-diagonal tails in (12) are generally only O(1/N), not exponentially small. Their bounded operator norms do not prove that the boundary co-source is nonzero on a particular geometric sector. ## 4. Why closing the final adapters by bare diagonal residues fails If the SAME grid were matched across every closure wire as well, the vector sigma(0) would be fixed by the full signed permutation. For a knot, pi_W is one cycle. Equations (1),(4) would then require c1=...=cb. (13) But (13) makes B=sA at every crossing, and its internal sampling radius T=BD/(D-B) escapes to infinity. Thus the ALL-wire-diagonal stratum is absent from the regular balanced knot chart. Bare unit Cauchy residues cannot collapse both the interior and final boundary wires while remaining in the regular multisection. Independent or propagated frames avoid that collision, but a nontrivial boundary source remains. The [wire-source calculation](whole_fermat_toric_residue_and_wire_source.md) identifies how a locally balanced section regenerates a Newton/Rogers current when pushed to a different endpoint center. Equations (7)--(12) concentrate that transport problem at the original boundary rather than creating one at every crossing. The next geometric comparison can therefore start with regular pure four-Psi bulk blocks on a coherently matched open braid, and a specified bounded wire co-source on only b boundary heads. This describes the EXACT grid network. It does not say that only boundary seams survive after an off-grid analytic interpolation: the local full-Psi deck characters equal one on the balanced multisection, but their products at a shared bulk variable need not equal one away from it. Those bulk logarithmic cut lips remain part of any contour transport. See the [exact port characters](balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md). Neither (7) nor boundedness computes the intersection with the positive constrained-lens cycle. That selected geometric coefficient remains to be proved. ## 5. Knot scalarity does not slide unequal radius gauges unchanged There is also a direct obstruction to erasing the boundary co-source by moving each radius gauge along the knot to its marked cut. Put D(t)|a>=t^a|a>. In the original complete crossing a positive transfer k has input (a,b), output (b+k,a-k); a negative transfer has output (b-k,a+k). Consequently, EXACTLY, R_epsilon (D(t1) tensor D(t2)) =(D(t2) tensor D(t1)) R_epsilon^[t1/t2], (R_epsilon^[lambda])_(transfer k) =lambda^(epsilon*k) R_(transfer k). (14) The extra factor is an actual transfer-clock insertion. It is not a scalar and is not eliminated by connectedness. To see that it is unavoidable, suppose an unchanged crossing allowed a product-diagonal slide with some other outgoing diagonal gauges. Its nonzero transfer-0 entries force those gauges to be the swapped ones in (14); a nonzero transfer-1 entry then forces t1=t2. Only the common total-degree gauge slides unchanged through an arbitrary original crossing. This is visible in the actual connected hyperbolic-knot source, with no arbitrary replacement exterior. At N=2 use the normalized original positive crossing (its unit scalar cancels in the writhe-zero word) R=[[1,0,0,0],[0,0,-i,0],[0,-i,2,0],[0,0,0,1]], g=diag(-i,i), e=ones(2,2)/2, W=R_2^(-1) R_1 R_2^(-1) R_1, mu(X)=Tr[(e tensor g tensor g) W X]. Direct exact multiplication gives the original figure-eight value mu(1)=5 and, for the same radius gauge placed on the three heads, mu(D(t) tensor I tensor I)=5(1+t)/2, mu(I tensor D(t) tensor I)=(11-t)/2, mu(I tensor I tensor D(t))=(-7+17t)/2. (15) Thus one-cut scalarity does not identify a radius factor on an ordinary closed head with the same factor at the marked cut. Sliding it requires the nontrivial current/transfer corrections (14). Applying scalarity AFTER the whole closure simply recovers the unknown knot scalar; it does not prove that a separately action-normalized geometric component has a nonzero source coefficient. [Audit](../experiments/audit_propagated_balanced_frames_and_boundary_source.py): exact original signed kernels, regular propagated centers, identity interior adapters, full-word operator and pivotal-source equality, and uniform complex frame/boundary norms.

title: The same geometric residue in the two prototype A-periods
text: # The same geometric residue in the two prototype A-periods Research note, 27 October 2026. The user suggested using 4_1 and 5_2 to guide a general proof. Here the two cases give the same exact determinant-line identity, with a simple Riley residue. The calculation uses the original coefficient model and the intrinsic linearized holonomy complex. It does not prove the selected finite period's volume asymptotic. ## 1. A precise statement in both complete trace fields Use the three-strand words, in the fixed Hurwitz action order, beta_4=[1,-2,1,-2], beta_5=[1,1,1,2,-1,2]. The first is the figure-eight braid. An independent local SnapPy recognition of the second gives 5_2. The symbolic fixed-point calculation below does not use that recognition as a representation-theoretic input. Let A=[1 1;0 1], B=[1 0;t 1]. For 4_1 take C=A^(-1)B A B^(-1)A; for 5_2 put D=A^(-1)B A, E=D^(-1)A D, C=E A E^(-1). The respective nonabelian parabolic fixed-point equations are f_4(t)=t^2-t+1=0, f_5(t)=t^3+t^2+2t+1=0. (1.1) These follow by substituting the matrices in the Hurwitz word and factoring the entries of F_beta(A,B,C)-(A,B,C). Thus the comparison uses their exact complete trace fields, not a floating-point hyperbolic representation. Conjugate by the full framing matrix F(r,s)=[r 1-r;s -s], s!=0. Let Omega_beta denote the original variable principal normal Gaussian density, retaining both framing derivatives and all crossing, pivot and writhe variable factors. Its fixed base-only quantum normalization line remains separately marked, as in the [normal-period construction](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Let T_beta be the torsion of the acyclic holonomy complex proved invariant under presentation moves in [the uniform Markov theorem](pointed_markov_reduction.md). **Prototype proposition.** In the respective exact function fields Q[t]/(f_i)(s,r), one has Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2) Omega_cut^2, Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]. (1.2) More explicitly, 4_1: -T_beta/2=(2t-1)/3, 5_2: -T_beta/2=(3t^2-6t+1)/23. (1.3) These identities hold on the full two-variable framing chart, rather than on finitely many frames. The omitted chart divisors are retained when comparing the selected relative source; (1.2) is a statement on its regular locus. ## 2. Independent sides of the determinant calculation The Gaussian side is computed directly from the actual balanced crossing Hessians and amplitudes. The integral closure lattice has d=m+1 variables: d=5 and d=7 in the two words. The Hessian has its two independently differentiated framing null vectors. Its transverse determinants are nonzero, of ranks 3 and 5. The squared normal density is a_beta^2 det(d chi/d(r,s))^2/det(-H_perp). The torsion side is computed independently from dF_beta-I, infinitesimal conjugation and d(H_b...H_1)(H_b...H_1)^(-1). It does not use the crossing Hessian or an expected density formula. Exact ranks make the holonomy complex acyclic. Its determinant ratio is evaluated at the ordinary frame (r,s)=(2,3); the general framing invariance of that ratio was proved by the chain argument, not by interpolation. The audit then proves (1.2) by exact equality of these independent expressions in the full function field. FLINT polynomial arithmetic in s,r and an explicit reduced quadratic or cubic number-field arithmetic are used. No finite-field sampling, interpolation or numerical rounding is part of this equality. ## 3. The common scalar is an ordinary algebraic residue Define S_4(t)=-1 and S_5(t)=t^2+2. The two constants in (1.3) satisfy exactly -T_beta/2=1/[S_i(t) f_i'(t)] =Res_(v=t) dv/[S_i(v)f_i(v)]. (3.1) For 4_1 this is -1/(2t-1)=(2t-1)/3. For 5_2 it is 1/[(t^2+2)(3t^2+2t+2)] =(3t^2-6t+1)/23 modulo f_5. Both S_i f_i' are units in their trace fields. The Gaussian source coefficient is therefore a nonzero algebraic residue at each simple marked parabolic place. This is a concrete instance of the requested rigid-period viewpoint: the coefficient is an evaluation in a finite spectral algebra with its residue co-source. It does not assert that the whole finite Kashaev invariant is already the trace of these classical residues. ## 4. The uniform twist lemma suggested by both cases This section records the prototype diagnostic, rather than the scope of the main program. The subsequent [arbitrary-bridge source reduction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md) uses a 2k-plat with unrestricted k and crossing word, eliminates every intermediate stage with its source and dual, and replaces the single Riley residue by an endpoint determinant complex. No twist-family assumption is imposed on that theorem or the intended volume result. For the signed twist presentation already used in [the A-curve note](a_polynomial_volume_limits.md#5-a-connected-infinite-class-from-the-twist-presentation), let S_j(z) be the second-kind Chebyshev recurrence and put f_k(t)=(1+t)S_(k-1)(t^2+2)-S_(k-2)(t^2+2). The prototypes are k=-1 and k=2. A precise next determinant lemma is the following proposed uniform identity at a simple nonabelian parabolic root: T_k=-2/[S_(k-1)(t^2+2) f_k'(t)]. (4.1) Together with a uniform Gaussian/holonomy determinant map, it would make the principal cut residue explicit for the entire regular twist family. Equation (4.1) is not claimed proved here for arbitrary k. There is a direct route to the general algebraic calculation. For A=[M 1;0 M^(-1)], B=[M 0;-u M^(-1)], W=AB^(-1)A^(-1)B, the complete relation is A W^k-W^k B=R_k(A-B), R_k=(s-u-1)S_(k-1)(z)-S_(k-2)(z), s=M^2+M^(-2), z=u^2+(2-s)u+2. At R_k=0, W^(-k)=S_(k-1)(z)(W^(-1)-(s-u-1)I). Differentiating the relator therefore exposes the factor S_(k-1) dR_k. At M=1,u=-t, dR_k=f_k'(t)dt on the parabolic slice. This explains the denominator in (4.1). What remains is the explicit determinant/source map from that one-relator complex to the braid complex, with its normalization. Merely observing the denominator is not a proof of the uniform identity. ## 5. Relation to the required volume theorem The geometric regulator action was already calibrated to hyperbolic volume. This proposition fixes its algebraic principal coefficient and its framing/cut dependence in both prototypes, with the same residue rule. It provides a testable common lemma for the general construction. To prove the original volume limit, one still has to show that the actual selected global quantum period pushes to this marked source with a nonzero, subexponential comparison factor. A nonzero local Gaussian coefficient alone does not prove that statement. Neither this proposition nor the Markov theorem is presented as a volume-conjecture proof. [Exact characteristic-zero audit](../experiments/audit_cubic_framing_density.py). [Results](../experiments/cubic_framing_density_results.json). [Finite-field diagnostic evaluator](../experiments/audit_geometric_a_density.py).

title: Full cyclotomic transport removes the limiting-root nonresonance condition
text: # Full cyclotomic transport removes the limiting-root nonresonance condition Independent extension, 27 October 2026. The coefficient field and the quantum parameter matter. For a rational coefficient in the true parameter Q, all-level principal-root transport identities propagate to all primitive roots by Galois conjugacy. Repeated shorter orbits then supply transport at scaled roots approaching Q=1. This removes the limiting-root nonresonance assumption in the unramified rank-one descent argument. The proof below is elementary and independent of any general published q-curvature theorem. It concerns a specified comparison line. It does not construct that line for the actual selected knot period, identify its marked source, or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The actual reduced state admits a Q-only annihilator I checked the new construction in [the even-meridian note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) against the exact crossing formulas and the [finite-sum annihilator proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). There is a useful stronger identity for its integer-exponent step. At a crossing write a_t for the first input index and c_t for the first output. The x-power contributed by a positive crossing is -(a_t+c_t), and by a negative crossing it is a_t+c_t. The remaining pivot/framing contribution is (N-1)kappa_D, where kappa_D=w-b+1 is even for a knot braid. Consequently E=(N-1)kappa_D +2 sum_negative a_t-2 sum_positive c_t +sum_all(c_t-a_t). (1.1) The last sum is zero on each closed state, as the exact integer position coboundary. Thus E/2=(N-1)kappa_D/2 +sum_negative a_t-sum_positive c_t. (1.2) This is manifestly integral affine-linear on the closed-flow lattice. No additional parity saturation or half-lattice assertion is needed. Replacing x^E by (Y/Q)^(E/2) therefore leaves a proper Q-product sum with integer-valued quadratic Q exponents and step-one Pochhammers. The filtered dimension bound, boundary strata and finite-moment repair of the existing proof apply with base Q, shift Y->QY and Z=Q^N. Stripping the common central factor (Z-1)^h before specialization gives a nonzero operator over the rational field in Q,Y. Factorials have lengths below N, so their root specializations are regular. This verifies the claimed existence result, conditional only on that already supplied finite-sum proof. It does not prove q-sign symmetry of a different minimal generator defined on half-roots. The full ADO sign and modified-dimension line remain exactly those of the original state. ## 2. Whole-root transport and the scaled-root lemma Let sigma_Q(Y)=QY and let a(Q,Y) be a nonzero rational function. For any complex Q where its coefficients are defined put C_n(Q,Y)=product_(j=0)^(n-1) a(Q,Q^jY). (2.1) Assume first a belongs to ℚ(Q,Y), and that for every sufficiently large n, C_n(zeta_n,Y)=1 in C(Y), zeta_n=exp(2pi*i/n). (2.2) The fixed coefficient denominators exclude only finitely many root orders. Galois conjugation over ℚ takes (2.2) to C_n(zeta_n^r,Y)=1 whenever gcd(r,n)=1. (2.3) Fix a positive integer k, and set xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N), g=gcd(k,N), m=N/g. Its order is m and it is a primitive m-th root. For all sufficiently large N, m is above the finite exceptional range, so (2.3) gives C_m(xi_N,Y)=1. The N-step orbit consists of g identical m-step orbits, hence C_N(xi_N,Y)=C_m(xi_N,Y)^g=1. One must not replace the nonprimitive orbit product by the primitive formula 1-alpha^N Y^N. Instead use its actual order m. The identity at that order gives equality of the multisets of m-th powers of the numerator and denominator roots. Raising those multisets to the g-th power gives equality of their N-th powers. This is the only root-power implication used below. The scaled-root lemma requires all sufficiently large orders, not merely primes or one residue class. The half-root alias in [the divisor note](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md) is excluded by using the true shift parameter Q and the full cyclotomic family. More generally the argument applies over any subfield K of C provided (2.3) is supplied for the fixed coefficient embedding. A sufficient condition for a number field K is that (2.2) is known for every coefficient conjugate of a in a finite normal closure of K. Indeed, apply a cyclotomic automorphism to the appropriate inverse coefficient conjugate. A statement at one chosen geometric embedding alone is not silently promoted to this stronger Galois marking. ## 3. Unramified full-curvature descent Assume a(Q,Y) belongs to ℚ(Q,Y) and has the full-order norm property (2.2). Write over its splitting field a(Q,Y)=r(Q) Y^s product_(i=1)^d(1-alpha_i(Q)Y) /product_(j=1)^e(1-beta_j(Q)Y). (3.1) Assume all alpha_i and beta_j admit holomorphic nonzero branches near Q=1. Coincident limiting roots and root-of-unity ratios between different limiting roots are allowed. There is no nonresonance assumption on those limiting values. **Theorem.** One has s=0, d=e and r(Q)=Q^(k_0). The branches can be paired so that alpha_i(Q)=Q^(k_i) beta_(pi(i))(Q), k_i in Z. (3.2) There is a rational gauge f in ℚ(Q,Y)^* with a(Q,Y)=f(Q,QY)/f(Q,Y). (3.3) Its numerator and denominator Y-degrees can each be bounded by |k_0|+sum_i |k_i|. In particular the degree bound is deduced from fixed branch data, rather than imposed on levelwise Hilbert-90 gauges. The shifts are k_i=alpha_i'(1)/alpha_i(1) -beta_(pi(i))'(1)/beta_(pi(i))(1). (3.4) If a has coefficients in K and the whole-root hypothesis (2.3) holds, the same proof gives f in K(Q,Y). ### Preliminary scalar and exponential-sequence facts At a primitive root the product formula gives r(zeta_N)^N (-1)^(s(N-1)) U^s product_i(1-alpha_i(zeta_N)^N U) /product_j(1-beta_j(zeta_N)^N U)=1, U=Y^N. Its U-valuation gives s=0, its value at U=0 gives r(zeta_N)^N=1, and its factorization gives d=e and the equality of the indicated root multisets. The scalar discreteness argument of the divisor note, now with Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), gives r(Q)=Q^(k_0): choose a logarithm ell at Q=1, use N ell(exp(2pi*i/N)) in 2pi*i Z, first take consecutive differences to get r(1)=1, then take the limit to make these integers constant. The rational identity follows from infinitely many root values. We also use the following directly proved uniqueness fact. For distinct nonzero constants c_1,...,c_h and meromorphic germs F_i(t), sum_i c_i^N F_i(1/N)=0 for all large N (3.5) implies every F_i=0. Among nonzero germs choose the largest modulus R of the c_i, then the smallest Laurent order of those germs. After division by R^N and that common power of 1/N, the identity is a finite sum sum a_i omega_i^N tending to zero, with distinct unit complex omega_i and at least one nonzero a_i. Multiplying by omega_j^(-N) and taking Cesaro means gives a_j=0, a contradiction. The lower-modulus terms vanish exponentially and the remaining errors tend to zero, so the averaging is justified. Root-of-unity ratios between distinct c_i cause no problem in this lemma. ### Separation at scaled roots, without separating c^k Let C be the finite set of distinct limiting branch values at Q=1. Use logarithms vanishing at Q=1 and define the holomorphic units A_i(t)=exp(Log(alpha_i(exp(2pi*i*t))/alpha_i(1))/t), B_j(t)=exp(Log(beta_j(exp(2pi*i*t))/beta_j(1))/t). (3.6) Fix an integer k between 1 and d. The scaled-root lemma implies equality of the N-th root-power multisets at xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N). Their first power sums therefore give sum_(c in C) c^N [sum_(alpha_i(1)=c) A_i(k/N)^k -sum_(beta_j(1)=c) B_j(k/N)^k]=0. (3.7) The bases here are the distinct c, not c^k. Apply (3.5) to the holomorphic bracketed functions of 1/N, then rescale their argument by k. It follows that for each c and every k=1,...,d, sum_(alpha_i(1)=c) A_i(t)^k =sum_(beta_j(1)=c) B_j(t)^k. (3.8) Newton identities, with zeros padding each multiset to length d, give equality of these multisets over the field of meromorphic germs. Their entries are units, so the cardinalities at each c agree. A fixed permutation pairs A_i identically with B_(pi(i)). The quotient of the logarithms in (3.6) has exponential one and is holomorphic. It is therefore a constant 2pi*i k_i. This gives Log(alpha_i/beta_(pi(i)))=k_i Log Q, proving (3.2) and (3.4). ### Rational descent and the degree bound For a pair with k_i>0 use the gauge product_(u=0)^(k_i-1)(1-Q^u beta_(pi(i))(Q)Y). For k_i<0 use the inverse product over k_i<=u<0. The product of all these gauges, times Y^(k_0), proves (3.3) over the splitting field and gives the stated degree bound. The finite divisor flow solving div(a)=sigma(div f)-div f is unique on each infinite Q-shift orbit. Because a is rational over ℚ(Q), its flow divisor is invariant under the Galois group of a finite splitting field. The product part is normalized to one at Y=0, so its multiplicative scalar is invariant as well. Thus the gauge descends to ℚ(Q,Y). The same argument works over K(Q). This completes the proof. ## 4. What the theorem does not remove The unramified branch hypothesis remains. It concerns zeros and poles as functions of the quantum parameter Q, not merely classical shape etaleness over M. No claim is made here that every rational comparison has that property, or that the actual unknown comparison line has been constructed. Nor does (3.3) itself preserve the ideal-meridian lattice. The gauge can carry a zero or pole on that divisor. The source, cut functional, and full ADO sign line must be transported in their specified lattices. A rational generic comparison fixes neither an arbitrary root-central scalar nor the nonzero coefficient of the selected regulator period. Those require the original pointing. This theorem is a new sufficient descent tool for that comparison problem, not the volume theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_q_parameter_curvature.py). [Results](../experiments/q_parameter_curvature_results.json).

title: Quantitative descent of the actual phase up to its boundary currents
text: # Quantitative descent of the actual phase up to its boundary currents 28 October 2026. Saturation gives more than a bound at exact critical points: on a slowly expanding regular window it gives a polynomial lower bound for the gradient everywhere above the volume level. Normalized gradient descent consequently costs only exp(o(N)) in that window. The full quantum dilogarithm has a uniform symbol estimate on the same slowly shrinking angular strips. This is a quantitative REGULAR-REGION statement for the actual full phase, at arbitrary fixed word width. It does not remove the original relative boundary currents. Descent can reach a shape/coordinate boundary, a logarithmic chart seam, or a quantum-pole exclusion before reaching the volume sublevel. Such exit currents must be retained. A claim of the full sharp knot bound still requires their estimate or exact cancellation. ## 1. The fixed phase and its algebraic critical equations Use the full logarithmic coordinates of [the marked critical-action calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md), including every Gaussian and cap coordinate. On a recorded local sheet, W(Z)=sum_a epsilon_a Li_2(A_a(Z)) +Z^t C Z/2+i kappa^t Z+c, A_a(Z)=sigma_a exp(v_a^t Z), phi=Im W, R=sum_a epsilon_a D(A_a), rho=Re Z. The actual signed monomial vectors v_a and quadratic form C have the integral/rational structure specified there; any required fixed algebraic coordinate cover is retained. Branches and their integer logarithmic marks are matched. In particular c has real imaginary-free normalization, and the exact off-critical identity is phi-R=rho^t Im(partial W). (1) Write x_i=exp Z_i. In these actual coordinates the exponentiated full critical equations are rational functions of the torus coordinates on the fixed cover: H_i(x)=exp(partial_i W), H_i(x)=1. (2) One can instead use a fixed nonsingular linear combination of the derivatives if a coordinate cover requires it; all norm comparisons then have fixed constants. It is necessary to use the original exponentiated equations, not powers that introduce additional solution components. Integer changes of the recorded flattening do not change (2). Clear denominators to obtain f_i(x). Let D(x) contain the torus coordinate factors, all cleared denominators, all singular graph factors, and the shape exclusions. The regular critical locus is the zero locus of the f_i in D!=0. Its JOINT shape-image closure Y in (P^1)^s is the saturated closure of [the critical compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md). The already proved input is |R|<=V on Y, V=Vol(S^3 minus K). (3) This is a statement about the actual full equations. Replacing them by an anchor-only, constrained endpoint, or unsaturated cleared system is not permitted in the following argument. ## 2. A finite saturation certificate separates high regulator values Take finitely many multihomogeneous equations G_l for Y in the product of projective lines. For their affine pullbacks g_l(x)=G_l(A(x),1), the localized radical ideal condition gives finite certificates D^(k_l) g_l^(s_l)=sum_i h_(li)(x) f_i(x), (4) after clearing any additional fixed rational denominators. Here k_l>=0 and s_l>=1 are fixed integers, and h_(li) are fixed polynomials. The power s_l cannot in general be omitted: the original critical ideal need not be radical. Formula (4) is an ordinary ideal-membership certificate. Its existence follows by taking the radical in the localized coordinate ring; it can also be produced and checked by polynomial arithmetic for a specified word. Normalize every G_l on unit homogeneous representatives, so |G_l|_norm is a continuous function on the compact product (P^1)^s. For any fixed eta>0 the compact set B_eta={shape tuples: R>=V+eta} is disjoint from Y. Therefore either B_eta is empty, or max_l |G_l|_norm >= mu_eta>0 on B_eta. (5) This uses compactness and the defining equations only, not an effective Lojasiewicz exponent or an assumption of isolated critical points. At finite shapes the affine value |G_l(A,1)| is at least its normalized value: the removed homogeneous normalization factor is a product of positive powers of sqrt(1+|A_a|^2), each at least one. ## 3. Polynomial gradient lower bound on a mild regular window Fix a finite analytic chart with its recorded logarithmic branches. For L>=2 let Omega_L impose |x_i|, |x_i|^(-1)<=L, |d_a(x)|^(-1)<=L for each individual excluded polynomial factor d_a of D. Further fixed chart restrictions, including selected-strip or quantum-pole exclusions, may be imposed. The upper bounds on all fixed polynomials on Omega_L are powers of L. Also |rho|<=sqrt(dim Z) log L. There are constants c_eta>0 and B<infinity, depending on the fixed word, chart and eta but not L, such that phi>=V+eta, Z in Omega_L ==> ||partial W(Z)||>=c_eta L^(-B). (6) Proof. If ||partial W||>=eta/(2 sqrt(dim Z) log L), this already implies (6), after increasing B and decreasing c_eta. Otherwise (1) gives R>=V+eta/2, so (5) supplies a g_l of modulus at least mu_(eta/2). For ||partial W||<=1, |exp(partial_i W)-1|<=e|partial_i W|. Clearing its denominator thus gives |f_i(x)|<=C L^a ||partial W||. The certificate (4), the denominator lower bounds and polynomial upper bounds give mu_(eta/2)^(s_l)<=C L^b ||partial W||. There are only finitely many certificates, so their largest exponent and smallest positive constant give (6). The case ||partial W||>1 is immediate. If B_(eta/2) is empty, the first alternative is the only one. This proves the claim uniformly even near nonisolated critical components and their genuine saturated degenerations. The same window gives a polynomial Hessian bound. Locally, partial^2 W=C+sum_a epsilon_a v_a v_a^t A_a/(1-A_a), ||partial^2 W||<=C L^a. (7) Higher fixed derivatives have the same type of bound. These bounds do not depend on the choice of an integer logarithmic mark, which changes only the linear part of W. Taking L=N^epsilon in (6)--(7) proves a quantitative exclusion of high-action approximate critical points in this window. The point is the exponent B*epsilon, which can be made smaller than any fixed positive number by choosing epsilon sufficiently small. This is stronger than merely excluding a convergent high-action critical sequence on a fixed compact set. ## 4. Subexponential cost of regular descent Regard the logarithmic chart as a real Euclidean domain. Holomorphy gives ||grad phi||=||partial W||. On phi>=V+eta use the vector field X=-grad phi/||grad phi||^2. (8) Then d phi(X)=-1 exactly. Equations (6)--(7) imply, for another fixed B, ||X||+||DX||<=C_eta L^B. (9) Extend it smoothly in a slightly larger regular chart as needed, with a cutoff which is one on the region being used; before a chart exit this does not change the flow. A cutoff over an inverse-power collar still has derivative bounded by a fixed power of L. Suppose the initial chain has mass exp(o(N)) and initial action at most O(log^2 N), as holds for bounded branches and logarithmic radii O(log N). Up to its first exit or its arrival at phi=V+eta, the available flow time is T_N=O(log^2 N). The usual variational equation, d(D F_t)/dt=DX(F_t) D F_t, and direct integration of its norm imply ||D F_t||<=exp(C_eta L^B T_N). (10) For L=N^epsilon, choose epsilon>0 so that B*epsilon<1. Every fixed dimensional fixed-time flow image, and the entire time-parametrized sweep before exit, then have mass exp(o(N)). The sweep gains only the additional factor T_N(1+sup||X||). No polynomial bound on this mass is needed for the exponential-rate problem. At the TARGET ACTION level the hitting-time map is also controlled: the time is exactly phi(Z)-V-eta, whose derivative has a polynomial bound in the recorded window. An arbitrary excluded-factor boundary is different. Its first-hit time can have an unbounded derivative at a grazing contact. Formula (10) must not be asserted for that first-hit map without an additional argument. A regular collar level chosen by coarea on the sweep controls the exit current; all such currents and any original chain boundary must remain in the period identity. More precisely, the [independent coarea construction](quantitative_regular_phase_descent_coarea_audit.md) uses H(u,z)=F_(u tau(z))(z), where tau=(phi(z)-V-eta)_+, and the running maximum m(u,z)=max_(v<=u) rho(H(v,z)) of a Lipschitz nested-window exhaustion. Coarea on the PARAMETER cylinder selects a legal level r in (1,2) such that its entire slice, pushed forward with multiplicity, has mass exp(o(N)). If the initial chain and its boundary have that mass bound, the exact period identity is integral_C omega = integral_C_low omega +integral_E_r omega-integral_B_r omega. (10a) Here B_r is the original-boundary sweep and E_r is the COMPLETE exit-associated slice. The latter can contain grazing curtains which have returned to the interior after touching the collar. It must not be relabeled as a current supported entirely on the collar hypersurface. All three currents have controlled mass; only C_low has the proved low-action support. The running maximum handles re-entry without a first-hit-time derivative or discarded curtain. Thus this statement bounds interior transport and its action-level endpoint. It is not a license to omit a boundary current or to cross an actual quantum pole. The latter is an excluded exit even if the classical shape is algebraically regular there. ## 5. The full quantum symbol on shrinking strips The defining-integral proof in [the literature-state audit](literature_state_volume.md#21-a-uniform-complex-remainder-on-an-entire-horizontal-strip) can be made quantitative in the strip width. For 0<b<=1 and |Im z|<=pi-delta, 0<delta<=1, log Phi_b(z/(2 pi b)) =Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i b^2)+R_b(z), |R_b(z)|<=C b^2 (delta^(-1)+log(2/delta)). (11) The constant is independent of Re z. Here are the bounds in that integral argument. With c=-b^2/24 and K_b(t)=[1/sinh(b^2 t)-1/(b^2 t)]/(4t sinh t), H_b(t)=K_b(t)-c exp(-t)/t, one has |H_b(t)|<=C b^2 for 0<t<=1 and |H_b(t)|<=C b^2 exp(-t) for t>=1. Consequently its weighted L1 norm with weight exp((1-delta/pi)t) is at most C b^2/delta. The remaining explicit arctan(z/pi) is bounded by C log(2/delta) on this strip, uniformly in Re z. Inserting these in the exact remainder integral proves (11). For the ACTUAL full function Psi_epsilon, substitute b^2=1/N and its recorded half-step shift. Taylor's formula uses |exp z/(1-exp z)|<=C/delta on the smaller angular strip. Hence, for 2pi/N<=delta<=1 and delta<=epsilon Im z<=2pi-delta, log Psi_epsilon(z) =Li_2(exp z)/(epsilon*2pi*i/N) +(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O(1/(N delta)). (12) All logarithms are the same selected-strip continuations as in the exact definition. For the derivative estimate use a disk of radius delta/4. At the threshold delta=2pi/N one must return to (11), rather than reapply (12) with an inadmissibly smaller delta: throughout that disk the shifted Phi argument has strip margin at least 3delta/4-pi/N>=delta/4. Its remainder and the half-step Taylor remainder are therefore still O(1/(N delta)) throughout the disk. Cauchy's formula gives, for every fixed k, |partial_z^k remainder|<=C_k/(N delta^(k+1)). (13) In particular delta=N^(-epsilon), with epsilon small, is allowed. A fixed product of these full functions, original monomial factors, Gaussian factors and rational source amplitudes has the actual W as its leading phase with subexponential amplitude on this window. This last assertion applies only where its rational denominators and selected logarithmic strips are retained. It does not analytically continue a finite cyclic atom across a Stokes boundary, and does not drop the full-function moment ray corrections. ## 6. Consequence and exact remaining task The final LOW-ACTION CHAIN obtained from an original scalar cycle by the controlled transport above, with the stated initial mass bound, has contribution bounded by exp(N(V+eta)/(2pi)+o(N)). (14) This follows from (10), (12) and the triangle inequality on that final chain. The exact Stokes identity expresses the original initial period as its low-action contribution PLUS the retained exit-associated and original-boundary sweep contributions. Even if every interior point of an initial chain reaches the target level, its own boundary sweep cannot be omitted. Estimate (14) by itself is not an estimate for that initial chain's complete period. It requires no assertion that the selected geometric saddle has nonzero coefficient, and is uniform over all fixed knot words to which the actual phase construction applies. The original period itself also contains the exit/boundary currents created or retained in that transport. Equation (14) becomes the desired whole-source bound ONLY after those currents have been controlled at the same rate. The entire all-transfer-endpoint corner has a separate subexponential estimate in [the total-transfer packet theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md). Mixed endpoint/bulk currents, simultaneous coordinate/shape exits, and source seams are not thereby estimated. They remain the concrete obstruction, rather than an unquantified cost of regular interior gradient descent. The shrinking-strip calculation, including both signs and the exact half-step normalization, has a separate [independent integral audit](shrinking_strip_full_psi_independent_audit.md). It corrected the displayed Hessian sign and supplied the derivative argument at the smallest permitted strip width; both are incorporated above. No computational sample is used to prove (6), (10) or (12).

title: A coarea audit of regular phase descent
text: # A coarea audit of regular phase descent 28 October 2026. This proves the boundary-mass assertion needed in Section 4 of [quantitative regular phase descent](quantitative_regular_phase_descent.md). It does not estimate the exponential size of the boundary periods. In particular, the boundary current below includes grazing curtains; its support need not be contained in a single physical collar hypersurface. ## 1. Precise transport statement Let C be a compact oriented piecewise smooth p-chain, with integer multiplicities, in a recorded logarithmic chart. The same argument applies to compact integral currents. Both M(C) and M(partial C) are assumed to be exp(o(N)). Let phi be the actual phase and a its target value. Suppose C lies in {rho<1}, where rho is a Lipschitz exhaustion and {rho<=2} is contained in a legal regular chart. All actual quantum poles and all chart seams which cannot be crossed are excluded from this chart. On {rho<=2, phi>=a}, let X satisfy d phi(X)=-1. Extend X to a globally defined smooth bounded vector field in a slightly larger real chart. The extension is only a device for defining a complete flow Phi_t; it must agree with X on the displayed region. Suppose, for the available time T_N, that sup |X| <= B_N, sup |DX| <= K_N, T_N=O(log^2 N), K_N T_N=o(N), and that B_N, Lip(rho), and the first derivatives of phi on the initial chain are exp(o(N)). In the application these are fixed powers of L=N^epsilon, with epsilon sufficiently small. Define tau(z)=max(phi(z)-a,0), 0<=tau<=T_N, H(u,z)=Phi_(u tau(z))(z), 0<=u<=1, m(u,z)=max_(0<=v<=u) rho(H(v,z)). (1) There is a level r in (1,2) for which the following currents are defined, have mass exp(o(N)), and satisfy partial T_r = C_low,r - C - B_r + E_r. (2) Here T_r is the transported truncated cylinder, C_low,r is supported in {phi<=a}, B_r is the transported side coming from the original boundary partial C, and E_r is the complete exit-associated current. The image of every term on the right lies in the legal closed window {rho<=r}. Thus a closed p-form omega on that window obeys the exact identity integral_C omega = integral_(C_low,r) omega + integral_(E_r) omega - integral_(B_r) omega. (3) The orientation of B_r is specified below. When C is closed it is absent. Formula (3) retains all relative boundary data; it is not a bound on the last two integrals by their mass alone. ## 2. Running maxima and quantitative slicing Orient S=[0,1] x C with du first. Then partial S = {1} x C - {0} x C - [0,1] x partial C. The variational equation and differentiation of u tau(z) give a local Lipschitz bound |DH| <= Lambda_N, Lambda_N <= const exp(K_N T_N) (1+B_N(T_N+Lip(tau))). (4) All fixed powers of Lambda_N are exp(o(N)). The positive-part definition of tau is Lipschitz and causes no difficulty. Bounds can equivalently be read in local parametrizations and integrated with their multiplicities. The running maximum in (1) is also Lipschitz. Indeed, write it as m(u,z)=max_(0<=v<=1) rho(H(vu,z)). Every function in this maximum has the same local Lipschitz bound, at most const Lip(rho) Lambda_N. The supremum inherits that bound. This argument does not differentiate a maximizing time or a first-hit time. Let Q_N be this bound. Coarea on the PARAMETER cylinder gives integral_1^2 M(<S,m,r>) dr <= Q_N M(S). (5) For almost every r, restriction to {m<r} is a finite-perimeter current and its boundary is partial(S restricted to {m<r}) = (partial S) restricted to {m<r} + <S,m,r>. (6) One may choose a common such r with M(<S,m,r>) <= 2 Q_N M(S). (7) The harmless factor 2 leaves a positive-measure choice of levels; the almost-everywhere current identities can therefore be imposed at the same time. A finite collection of chains or charts is handled by applying coarea to the sum of their unsigned slicing masses. Define T_r = H_#(S restricted to {m<r}), E_r = H_#<S,m,r>, C_low,r = H(1,.)_#(C restricted to {m(1,.)<r}), B_r = H_#(([0,1] x partial C) restricted to {m<r}). The u=0 face is all of C because rho(C)<1. Equations (6) and the product orientation give (2), including its minus sign on B_r. Pushforward commutes with boundary. In particular, (2) includes the boundary of the retained subset of the u=1 face; it is not permissible to discard it separately. For m(1,z)<r the entire trajectory up to tau(z) remains in the region where the extension is the actual normalized descent. Consequently its endpoint has phase a if phi(z)>a, and is unchanged with phase at most a otherwise. This proves the stated support of C_low,r. Monotonicity of m in u makes {m<r} an initial time interval in each fibre. There is no re-entry ambiguity, even if the physical trajectory later re-enters the window in the extended flow. Finally, mass pushforward and (7) give M(T_r) <= Lambda_N^(p+1) M(S), M(E_r) <= 2 Lambda_N^p Q_N M(S), M(C_low,r) <= Lambda_N^p M(C), M(B_r) <= Lambda_N^p M(partial C). (8) These are bounds on parametrized currents WITH their multiplicities. No inference from the size of an image set or from cancellation of its parametrization is used. All quantities in (8) are exp(o(N)). Stokes applied to the legal image of T_r proves (3). ## 3. Why the exit current includes curtains It is in general false that E_r is supported on {rho=r}. A local model is rho(H(t,z))=z-(t-t_0)^2. For t>=t_0 its running maximum is z. At z=r, the parameter slice {m=r} therefore includes the whole interval t>=t_0, although the physical value of rho is strictly less than r after t_0. These portions are grazing curtains in the boundary of the first-exit truncated cylinder. Coarea bounds their mass together with all other slice pieces. This distinction is essential. The construction proves controlled regular transport into a low-action chain PLUS an exit-associated current. It does not prove that this latter current has low action, or that its contribution is determined by data on one collar hypersurface. An additional estimate or an exact source cancellation is still required for a sharp full-period upper bound. ## 4. Audit verdict The saturation certificate and normalized-gradient estimates in Sections 2--4 of the root note support the interior transport assertion. Equations (1)--(8) supply the missing coarea argument without a first-hit derivative bound. They require a legal collar with the recorded derivative bounds, and retention of the complete exit-associated and original-boundary currents. No new general upper or lower volume bound follows from this boundary-mass result alone.

title: The actual quantum source at every bridge
text: # The actual quantum source at every bridge Research note, 27 October 2026. This continues the [arbitrary-bridge classical contraction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md) using the original finite quantum matrices. It computes all four balanced turns, a literal marked closure, their cyclic boundary sources and a flat completion under the actual meridian half-step. All formulas hold for arbitrary N and arbitrary bridge count. The completion needs two bulk channels: a single cap's bulk norm changes sign under the half-step. Keeping only the squared step would miss this. The explicit three-dimensional system below keeps that sign and the boundary source, including at the Kashaev color. This is finite quantum boundary transport. The selected knot period's comparison with the geometric regulator remains unproved. ## 1. The original caps lose their factorials exactly Fix q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2 and x=-M/q. Write F_a=(Q;Q)_a and w_a=v_a/F_a, both on V(x) and its standard dual color V(x^(-1)Q^(-1)). No unrolled weight lift is changed. The existing actual turn matrices have c_a=(-x)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2), g_b=x^(1-N) Q^(-b). (1.1) For 0<=a<N, cancellation in the full product F_(N-1)=N gives F_a F_(N-1-a)=N (-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2). (1.2) Indeed F_(N-1)/F_(N-1-a)=product_(r=1)^a(1-Q^(-r)) =(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)F_a. Thus the actual balanced left cap and cup are simply ev_L(w_a^dual tensor w_b) =x^a/N delta_(a+b,N-1), coev_L(1)=sum_a N x^(-a) w_(N-1-a) tensor w_a^dual. (1.3) The actual right cap and cup are ev_R(w_b tensor w_a^dual) =x^a g_b/N delta_(a+b,N-1), coev_R(1)=sum_a N x^(-a)g_(N-1-a)^(-1) w_a^dual tensor w_(N-1-a). (1.4) On their support the right-cap coefficient is (Q x^(1-N)/N)(Qx)^a. (1.5) The coefficients (1.3)--(1.4) are whole identities in the original finite matrices. The unbalanced J_x, its exact double dual g and all four snake identities were independently proved in [the pivotal duality note](relative_pivotal_duality.md).
