(2.1) For example the polynomial identity behind this calculation is product_(j=0)^(N-1)(z-qKQ^j-q^(-1)K^(-1)Q^(-j)) =C_N(z)+K^N+K^(-N), using q^N=-1. Both individual Casimirs are fixed by r. Ordered multiplication gives u^N=-rho^(2N)e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1. Retain the entire central divisor D_c=1-u^N=1+rho^(2N)e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1. (2.2) All factors 1-Q^j u become invertible after D_c is inverted: their product is D_c. No parity-dependent scalar is discarded. The center map of (1.2) is k'_1=k_1 D_c, k'_2=k_2/D_c, e'_1=e_1 k_2, f'_2=f_2/k_1, e'_2=k_1 e_2+e_1-e_1 k_2^2/D_c, f'_1=f_2+f_1/k_2-f_2/(k_1^2 D_c). (2.3) For the last two formulas, take the N-th powers of the coproduct intertwining equations. The mixed Gaussian-binomial coefficients vanish because Q has order N, including composite N. Use balanced center coordinates epsilon=rho^N E^N, varphi=-rho^N F^N. Then k+k^(-1)+epsilon*varphi=-C_N(Omega) and D_c=1-epsilon_1 varphi_2 k_2/k_1. Equations (2.3) have the same form in these balanced variables. For the checked algebra map Ad_(PR)=tau composed with r, its point map applies (2.3) to swapped inputs, by contravariance. For inputs (k,e,f),(l,g,h), with c=1-k g f/l, that point map is ((l c, k g, f+h/k-f/(l^2 c)), (k/c, l e+g-k^2 g/c, f/l)). (2.4) This is exactly the inverse holonomy map (4.7) in the [marked braid note](marked_braid_holonomy.md). The inverse is required by pullback; replacing it by the positive critical map changes the convention. The previously derived Borel-factorization/prefix change therefore identifies (2.4) with inverse Hurwitz transport. In those coordinates put G(k,e,f)=[[k,e],[kf,k^(-1)+ef]]. At the actual ideal color a=N-1, x_0=q^a, k_0=x_0^N=delta=(-1)^(N-1), Omega_0=-2, e=f=0. The marked meridian is mu=delta G. It is the identity at this augmentation. On the actual nilpotent color section x=x_0 M it has eigenvalues M^N,M^(-N); its squared eigenvalue coordinate is U=M^(2N), as in the [actual threading calculation](ado_threaded_shadow.md). This fixes the sign rather than silently changing the root character. ## 3. A regular three-parameter splitting module Work near (x,epsilon_0,phi_0)=(x_0,0,0), where epsilon_0 and phi_0 now denote the raw central powers E^N,F^N, not the balanced variables of Section 2. Choose the unique algebraic Hensel branch omega near -2 satisfying C_N(omega)=rho^(2N)epsilon_0 phi_0-x^N-x^(-N). It exists because C_N'(-2)=delta N^2 is a unit in characteristic zero. Thus the full center is smooth on this cover at the actual color; fixing omega=-2 first would instead produce a singular quadratic cone at the augmentation. For 1<=j<N define a_j=(omega-qxQ^(-j)-q^(-1)x^(-1)Q^j)/rho^2, P=product_(j=1)^(N-1)a_j. Every a_j specializes to [j]_q^2, a unit. On a basis v_0,...,v_(N-1) set K v_j=xQ^(-j)v_j, F v_j=v_(j+1) (j<N-1), F v_(N-1)=phi_0 v_0, E v_j=a_j v_(j-1) (j>0), E v_0=(epsilon_0/P)v_(N-1). (3.1) The product identity (2.1) gives the missing FE diagonal at j=0. The differences of the other diagonals give [E,F], and K gives the remaining relations. Thus (3.1) has the specified Casimir and central powers. At epsilon_0=phi_0=0 the chosen omega is qx+q^(-1)x^(-1), so these are exactly the actual nilpotent ADO E,F,K matrices. At x=x_0 they give the Kashaev color. General cyclic members have no H satisfying the unrolled weight rule; none is asserted. This is a splitting module, including at the nilpotent point. Indeed the distinct K eigenvalues give spectral projectors p_j. For adjacent nonwrapping indices, F and a_j^(-1)E give inverse matrix units. Their products give all matrix units. Conversely reduce any returning path using FE, EF and the specified full E and F cycles. Its p_0 corner is a scalar. Hence the central quotient on this chart is End of the free module (3.1). This proves the needed splitting directly, including the special fiber. ## 4. A concrete Hom line and its anchor For a pair of source modules use (2.3) for the target center and choose x'_1=x_1 D_c^(1/N), x'_2=x_2 D_c^(-1/N), with D_c^(1/N)=1 at the ideal pair. Keep the individual Casimirs. The target modules are again (3.1). Source matrices transformed by (1.2), and these target matrices, are two splitting representations with the same center. Their intertwiners form a rank-one Hom module. There is an explicit generator. For each transformed K'_i form P_i=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(K'_i/x'_i)^j. Let lambda_0=q^((N-1)^2/2), using the already specified square root of q, and v=P_1 P_2(lambda_0 v_0 tensor v_0). Define the columns of I by I(v_r tensor v_s)=(F'_1)^r(F'_2)^s v. (4.1) The matrix-unit description proves all six intertwining equations. At the ideal pair the transformed algebra is conjugated by the actual full R, and R(v_0 tensor v_0)=lambda_0(v_0 tensor v_0). Consequently (4.1) equals that actual R at this point. In particular I is invertible on the formal neighborhood. This constructs the Hom frame using the K cover and ordinary units; no roots of E^N or F^N are required. At the base det I=1. Set I_bar=(det I)^(-1/N^2) I, (4.2) using the root with value one there. This is a specified finite algebraic cover and a pointed line, not a free scalar choice. For a triple, the rational Yang--Baxter identity identifies the two target splitting modules. The two products of the framed intertwiners differ by a scalar. Each pair map has determinant one, so its embedding on a triple also has determinant one. Thus the scalar has N^3-th power one. It equals one at the ideal triple, where the actual finite R satisfies Yang--Baxter (the generic highest-weight identity specializes without denominators [N]_q). In the formal neighborhood a root of unity with this value is one. This proves strict local holonomy coherence on the specified cover. Global continuation must retain its root cover and phases; this argument alone gives no globally normalized tangle invariant. ## 5. Exact restriction to the original knot period For the same nilpotent color on both strands, write R^0 for the actual uncheck R with its common Cartan factor q^(alpha^2/2) removed. The formula (4.1) restricts to I=lambda_0 R^0. Its diagonal entries before the common factor are x^(-r-s)q^(2rs), whence det R^0=x^(-N^2 a)q^(N^2 a^2/2), a=N-1. Writing x=x_0 M, the root of det I selected above is M^(-a). Therefore I_bar=x^a q^(-a^2/2) R^0. (5.1) At M=1 this is the actual full R. For the residual normalization R^0 the actual same-color twist is theta_0=x^(-a). For (5.1) take theta_bar=q^(-a^2/2). Their ratio is exactly the crossing scalar x^a q^(-a^2/2). On a knot braid of writhe w, multiplying crossings contributes this scalar to the power w; the zero-framing twist correction contributes its inverse. The pivot and cut pairing are unchanged. Thus the reduced and full zero-framed knot periods are exactly the original ones throughout this nilpotent meridian germ. In particular F_N(1)=<K>_N still holds. This statement concerns the same-color cut evaluation. It does not assert that the constant theta_bar is a ribbon twist on every mixed cyclic object. Nor does it change the full ADO factor d_N(M)=i^(N+3) M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). The [rank-one meridian wall](marked_braid_holonomy.md) and its whole ratio at M=1 must still be retained in a global source construction. ## 6. What this contributes to the ideal-triangulation route The audited ideal-triangulation theorem supplies a complete positive geometric representative beta_T and its marked Bloch regulator. The [crossing fundamental-cycle calculation](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) already identifies the complete classical crossing class with beta_T. The construction here supplies actual local quantum holonomy data and a Hom line regular through the color used by the original invariant. It therefore provides a local object to transport when comparing a diagram decomposition and an ideal triangulation. It supplies neither the relative gluing source nor its chosen global contraction. In particular the actual root augmentation mu=I and the complete hyperbolic meridians are different central data. The [threaded separator](ado_threaded_shadow.md) rules out simply equating their homogeneous eigenlines while preserving the interior observables. A regular local family of crossing modules does not prove that the corresponding closed knot representations lie on one component, or identify their evaluations. The required comparison is of pointed relative source extensions, including their cut/cap data, full meridian wall, peripheral factors, and selected evaluation. It must also specify the trajectory between fixed semiclassical shapes and root-central coordinates. Positivity and local Yang--Baxter coherence alone do not prove nonzero geometric contribution, exclude cancellation, or bound the norm of the unknown comparison period. The volume identity (4/N)log|F_N(1)| -> log||P_hyp||=2Vol(M)/pi remains unproved. The subsequent [closed-braid note](closed_braid_period_line.md) constructs the admissible global braid Hom line and a literal scalar cut functional from these local data. A grading calculation identifies its entire upper triangular reducible period with the actual ADO meridian value. It also proves that the formal central augmentation neighborhood is abelian and identifies the Alexander attachment divisor. This advances the global braid construction; the relative triangulation source, opposite-weight geometric coupling and regulator norm remain unproved. ## 7. Independent exact diagnostics [The audit](../experiments/audit_regular_holonomy_braiding.py) checks 14 generic cyclic automorphism cases, including every commutator, the rational inverse, coproduct transport, Casimirs and central powers. Six three-factor tests check the quantum Yang--Baxter maps. Six tests construct the matrix-unit intertwiner and check all six generators. Fourteen actual nilpotent/ideal cases check exact conjugation, the anchored frame and determinant root; thirty knot cut evaluations check the compensating twist. Nine third-order deformation tests, through level 15, check the Hensel module and both central powers. The balanced-center sign and inverse holonomy convention are also checked symbolically. Even and composite levels are included. See [the results](../experiments/regular_holonomy_braiding_results.json). These diagnostics support the algebraic proofs, not a global period identification or volume estimate. ## 8. Literature coverage, not proof premises [Kashaev--Reshetikhin, math/0202212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202212) already constructs root-of-unity holonomy R-matrices. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, 2509.02354v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354v2) announces an explicit four-dilogarithm factorization and holonomy Yang--Baxter equation. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder, 2509.02365v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02365v3) announces invariants with flat-connection input and a phase-free geometric twist of Kashaev's invariant. These establish prior coverage of the general framework, not the selected original-state period comparison needed here. Their proofs, factorization and global normalization claims are not premises of Sections 1--6. The fixed-Casimir polynomial in the [older recoupling note](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) is a specialization/lattice lift; that note does not assert a generic braiding for it. Equations (1.2)--(2.3) use a different construction: the individual unrestricted central characters change by the holonomy map. The coherence proof here gives no generic Yang--Baxter identity for that fixed polynomial extension.

title: The regular meridian centralizer and the actual normalization line
text: # The regular meridian centralizer and the actual normalization line Research note, 26 October 2026. There is a smaller commutative group relevant to the framed geometric period: the centralizer of the regular marked meridian. It is multiplicative away from the parabolic fiber and additive on that fiber. Its framing torsor, invariant differential and power adapters can all be computed exactly. The actual ADO modified dimension is the inverse Lie factor of one such adapter, with its original phase. The group model G^(lambda) is an existing definition, already recorded in [the uniform source-base note](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md#3-the-deformation-group-is-an-existing-definition), from [Mezard--Romagny--Tossici, Section 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1104.2222v1#S1.SS2). Here its parameter is the meridian eigenvalue gap, rather than the quantum gap rho. The matrix calculations below supply the geometric application without importing a classification proof. This identifies the peripheral normalization line, not the selected global quantum period or its Bloch-regulator norm. ## 1. The centralizer is a smooth commutative group model On the marked meridian eigenvalue cover put kappa=M-M^(-1), mu_M=[M 1;0 M^(-1)]. This meridian is regular even at M=1, where it is a nontrivial unipotent. Commutation of a general invertible matrix with mu_M forces its lower-left entry to zero and a-d=kappa*b. Normalize the lower diagonal entry to one in PGL_2. The projective image of this GL_2 centralizer is J_M={C_b=[1+kappa*b b;0 1]:1+kappa*b!=0}, b*b'=b+b'+kappa*b*b', b^(-1)=-b/(1+kappa*b). (1.1) It is commutative. Its generic multiplicative coordinate is y=1+kappa*b; its kappa=0 fiber is the additive b-line. Its invariant relative differential is omega_J=db/(1+kappa*b). (1.2) These facts are identities of the smooth open affine-line group scheme. A limit of diagonalizing matrices is unnecessary. The PGL convention is explicit; fixed SL_2 sign characters remain separate marked data. On the open set M+M^(-1)!=0 this is also the full PGL_2 centralizer: a projectively commuting lift can only commute with mu_M, since conjugation preserves its nonzero trace. At trace zero there is an additional anticommuting component. For example, at M=i the invertible matrix [1 0;-2i -1] conjugates mu_i to -mu_i. All statements here use the commutative regular centralizer (1.1); near the complete meridian M=1 the distinction disappears. This geometric meridian centralizer is distinct from the large quantum commutant End_(U_q)(V^(tensor b)) computed in [the intrinsic cut atlas](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md). Its commutativity does not contradict the genuine SL_2 sector of the full actual braid transport. ## 2. The framing torsor has an explicit quotient by this group Use the same two framing coordinates as in the actual critical correspondence, with F_M(r,s)=[r 1-r;s -kappa-s], Delta=s+kappa*r !=0, F_M(1,1)^t=(1,-kappa)^t. The latter vector is the M^(-1) eigenvector of mu_M. Direct conjugation gives F_M^(-1) mu_M F_M =[M+s -kappa-s;s M^(-1)-s]=mu_s. (2.1) In particular this boundary meridian is independent of r. Left multiplication by C_b acts on the frame by r -> r+b Delta, s -> s, Delta -> Delta(1+kappa*b). (2.2) Where s!=0, r=0 is a section and b=r/s is the torsor coordinate. Thus r is the residual centralizer direction, while s records the boundary coadjoint coordinate. At completeness the action is r->r+bs. These statements hold for every representation in the marked chart, independently of its knot presentation. The initial position coordinate on the classical critical chart of the actual balanced state is A_cut=M/(M+s), (2.3) because x=-M and the raw K is -(M+s). At fixed M an invariant framing two-form adapted to this original cut coordinate is Omega_cut=(dr/Delta) wedge dlog A_cut =-dr wedge ds/[Delta(M+s)]. (2.4) Its fundamental centralizer vector is V_J=Delta partial_r. Direct differentiation gives Lie_(V_J) Omega_cut=0, contraction_(V_J) Omega_cut=dlog A_cut. (2.5) At M=1 this is -dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]. It is not an arbitrary choice of Haar measure on the two-dimensional framing group: it uses its one-dimensional centralizer and the specified cut coordinate. If t=r/s, then it is -dt wedge ds/(1+s). Equation (2.5) is a canonical algebraic reduction of this form. It does not yet prove that the actual selected finite period implements that contraction or divides out a group volume. ## 3. The marked A-curve supplies a second section of J_M Let ell be the centered longitude eigenvalue, with ell(1)=1; retain the original preferred-longitude sign separately. Any SL_2 longitude commuting with mu_M has the form lambda=[ell (ell-ell^(-1))/kappa;0 ell^(-1)]. (3.1) Normalize its lower diagonal entry in PGL_2. Its section of the same group (1.1) is b_lambda=(ell^2-1)/kappa, b_mu=M, 1+kappa*b_lambda=l=ell^2, 1+kappa*b_mu=m=M^2. (3.2) On the normalized smooth geometric branch, b_lambda|_(M=1)=dlog ell/dlog M=tau_cusp. (3.3) This is an ordinary value of a regular function: both numerator and denominator in (3.2) have simple first meridian terms. The positive cusp shape selects the geometric direction. The geometric A-equation in these coordinates is exactly A_geo(M^2,1+kappa*b_lambda)=0. (3.4) Its strict transform removes the common kappa power; the exceptional polynomial is its tangent-cone equation in b_lambda. Distinct slopes separate there. Normalization still retains the branch mark if several branches have the same tangent. The group model alone does not supply the marked central regulator constant or its volume. ## 4. Powers give the actual ADO normalization, including its phase Define the Laurent polynomial u_n(M)=(M^n-M^(-n))/(M-M^(-1)), u_0=0, u_1=1, u_(n+1)=(M+M^(-1))u_n-u_(n-1). Matrix multiplication gives exactly mu_M^n=[M^n u_n(M);0 M^(-n)]. (4.1) At M=1 the polynomial has value n, and at M=-1 it has value (-1)^(n-1)n. The original full ADO factor is therefore d_N(M)=eta_N/u_N(M), eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.2) This is precisely the previously fixed formula, since u_N=M^(1-N)(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). It is an exact algebraic evaluation, with its whole meridian germ and phase retained. For a power degree D, let H_D=diag(u_D(M),1). Wherever u_D!=0, it is the canonical meridian normalization adapter: H_D^(-1) mu_M^D H_D=mu_(M^D), H_D^(-1) C_b^(kappa) H_D =C_(b/u_D)^(kappa_D), kappa_D=M^D-M^(-D)=kappa*u_D(M). (4.3) Its map on the centralizer Lie coordinate is multiplication by 1/u_D. Thus the actual dimension line is eta_N times this determinant line for D=N. At the parabolic fiber the adapter is diag(D,1), so the original value eta_N/N follows without separately evaluating two zero factors. ### The same adapter is a determinant and residue map There is an intrinsic spectral-algebra version. Put B_M=R[T]/(T^2-(M+M^(-1))T+1). The regular matrix mu_M is cyclic: the vectors e_2,mu_M e_2 form a basis of determinant -1 at every M. An operator commuting with mu_M is therefore uniquely a+b mu_M. This identifies its GL_2 centralizer with B_M^times, including the nonreduced fiber B_1=R[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), epsilon=T-1. Its norm is Norm(a+bT)=a^2+(M+M^(-1))ab+b^2. The PGL normalization of (1.1) is the class of (1-b/M)+bT; its norm is 1+kappa*b. Adjoining the marked square root of that norm gives its SL_2 lift. This is a spectral unit torsor, with its quadratic root retained. For a degree D power define phi_D:B_(M^D)->B_M, T'->T^D. The Cayley--Hamilton relation gives, integrally, T^D=u_D(M)T-u_(D-1)(M), Mat(phi_D)=[1 -u_(D-1);0 u_D], det(phi_D)=u_D(M). (4.4) Use the canonical algebraic residue Res_M(a+bT)=b. Its Gram matrix in 1,T is [[0,1],[1,M+M^(-1)]], with determinant -1 even at the dual-number fiber. Equation (4.4) gives the exact comparison of these functionals: Res_M(phi_D(f))=u_D(M) Res_(M^D)(f), (d_D(M)/eta_D) Res_M(phi_D(f)) =Res_(M^D)(f). (4.5) The same map also preserves the spectral norm exactly: Norm_(B_M)(phi_D(a+bT')) =a^2+(M^D+M^(-D))ab+b^2 =Norm_(B_(M^D))(a+bT'). (4.6) Indeed mu_M^D has determinant one and the indicated trace, so the determinant of aI+b mu_M^D is that polynomial. The norm torsor and the residue co-source therefore have compatible cover maps, including at the dual-number fiber. Thus the normalization line and its residue co-source are compared together. At M=1, phi_D(epsilon')=D epsilon; the original 1/D factor is its exact dual correction. This does not identify B_M with the knot's entire quantum-A spectral algebra or its two-Casimir source: it proves the specified peripheral determinant and residue-line identity. The adapter becomes singular at a nontrivial torsion root where mu_M^D is scalar. The regularized lattices in [the resonant-source calculation](cyclic_source_connection_and_resonant_flags.md) must be retained there; a regular matrix conjugation through that point is not asserted. The actual root-central augmentation is still the identity representation in the earlier threaded-character test. We have not identified it with the nontrivial geometric parabolic mu_1 or with mu_M^N. Equations (4.2)--(4.3) identify the peripheral scalar line and its adapter only. ## 5. The source normalization composes exactly across cover degrees Taking powers in two orders gives u_(DN)(M)=u_D(M)u_N(M^D) =u_N(M)u_D(M^N). (5.1) The original phases satisfy eta_(DN)/(eta_D eta_N)=i^((D-1)(N-1)). Consequently the exact dimension tower is d_(DN)(M)=i^((D-1)(N-1)) d_D(M)d_N(M^D). (5.2) Its phase factors obey the associative three-degree cocycle identity, by expanding their integer exponents. This includes even and composite degrees. For example d_(2N)(M)/d_N(M) =i^N M^N/(1+M^(2N)). (5.3) The peripheral factor becomes i^N/2 only after M=1. This is a verified power-composition factor; identifying a move's multiplier still requires its actual source adapter. The paired actual source comparison has a simpler strict law. Its previously proved scalar is Gamma_N=gamma_N(M)gamma_N(M^(-1)) =d_N(M)/(N eta_N)=1/[N u_N(M)]. It therefore satisfies the exact identity Gamma_(DN)(M)=Gamma_D(M) Gamma_N(M^D). (5.4) This supplies a coherent peripheral paired line across power covers. It is not an identification of the tensor spaces or selected knot periods at levels D,N,DN. The actual root meridian step is compatible as well: d_N(q_N M)/d_N(M) =-kappa(q_N M)/kappa(M), (5.5) because (q_N M)^N=-M^N. Thus this line has exactly the original ADO difference cocycle, not a newly chosen gauge. ## 6. Covers also transform the framing coordinate For the connected meridional D-cover, the longitude is unchanged while M'=M^D. Equations (3.2) and (4.3) give b'_lambda=b_lambda/u_D, tau'_cusp=tau_cusp/D. The actual boundary coadjoint coordinate changes differently. The Cayley--Hamilton power formula in (2.1) gives mu_s^D=mu_(s'), evaluated at M'=M^D, s'=u_D(M)s. The normalized cover frame is F_(M^D)(r,u_D s)=u_D H_D^(-1) F_M(r,s). (6.1) In particular A'_cut=M^D/(M^D+u_D s), (6.2) which is generally different from A_cut^D. This distinguishes the internal position coordinate from the peripheral eigenvalue m, whose cover map really is m'=m^D. Pulling back the two-form (2.4) yields exactly Omega'_cut/Omega_cut=(M+s)/(M^D+u_D s). (6.3) Thus a cover comparison must keep both the Lie adapter and the specified cut-coordinate Jacobian. The regulator's degree-D law from the A-curve cover note does not replace this local source data. ## 7. Relation with the actual normal density The exact figure-eight calculation on the full two-variable framing chart now gives Omega_actual^2=-tau_cusp/[6 s^2(1+s)^2] (dr wedge ds)^2. It has precisely the dependence of Omega_cut^2 at M=1, with a representation-dependent scalar -tau_cusp/6. The old tests against dr ds/s and dr ds/s^2 did not test the centralizer/cut form (2.4). The [two-variable audit](../experiments/audit_full_framing_density.py) retains both free variables, the actual coefficient amplitude, the two Hessian null vectors and its transverse determinant in Q(sqrt(-3))(s,r). The exact identity proves independence of r; no interpolation or finite-field inference is used. [Results](../experiments/full_framing_density_results.json). The displayed density law is not asserted for every knot. The uniform conclusions proved here are the geometric centralizer, its framing quotient, its marked longitude section, and the exact original normalization and cover composition laws. Establishing that the actual source implements the reduction (2.5), and then transporting the selected period to its geometric regulator line, remains necessary for the original volume conjecture. ## 8. At the additive fiber the relative boundary is essential The quotient form specifies a sharper requirement on the source. On the chart s!=0 put t=r/s. At M=1 one has Omega_cut=dt wedge dlog A_cut =d(t dlog A_cut), A_cut=1/(1+s). (8.1) Thus its ordinary closed two-periods vanish on this chart. Commutativity of the centralizer does not give a nonzero absolute period by itself. Its relative boundary data cannot be discarded during the proposed reduction. For a concrete relative cycle let gamma be a closed curve in the s-plane avoiding 0,-1, and take the oriented chain Gamma=[t_0,t_1] times gamma. Stokes' theorem gives exactly integral_Gamma Omega_cut =(t_1-t_0) integral_gamma dlog A_cut. (8.2) For a positive small circle around s=-1 the last integral is -2 pi i; around s=0 it is zero. The endpoint separation is part of the relative source, rather than a consequence of the invariant two-form. Setting it to one specifies a normalization, which must be compared with the actual cut. The rectangular cycle here is a model relative class; it has not been identified with that selected quantum cut. Off the parabolic fiber the same chart has Omega_cut=db/(1+kappa*b) wedge dlog A_cut, b=r/s, kappa Omega_cut=dlog(1+kappa*b) wedge dlog A_cut. (8.3) The multiplicative fiber has an absolute logarithmic circle; the additive fiber does not. This elementary change is why one must transport a relative source or its regularized lattice, not just a class of ordinary closed cycles. It agrees with the earlier need to retain resonant normal jets, without identifying the different source constructions. The subsequent [actual cut-residue calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) now identifies beta=dlog A_cut in the original finite cut pairing, with its canonical representative, pole packet and normal carry retained. It also derives the principal crossing determinant and pivotal-volume factors uniformly. The remaining relative pushforward is not supplied by this exact boundary co-source identification. [The audit](../experiments/audit_regular_meridian_centralizer.py) checks the group, frame, longitude, invariant-density and cover identities, including the full normalization phases. [Results](../experiments/regular_meridian_centralizer_results.json).

title: The regular ADO period, its bounded source, and a cyclic trace
text: # The regular ADO period, its bounded source, and a cyclic trace Research note, 26 October 2026. This isolates a canonical regular period of the actual literature state. All its polar data come from ordinary colors and have polynomial size at the specified principal root. The regular period at completeness is exactly a weighted field trace on the squared-meridian cyclic algebra. Any specified actual all-level operator gives it a rootwise affine equation with a source in a fixed finite-dimensional Laurent space, with polynomially bounded coefficients. These statements hold for every knot. They neither prove that this source couples to the geometric branch nor establish the volume limit. They do not identify this rootwise source with a fixed generic rational source or import a published volume theorem. ## 1. The actual pointing and the statement Fix a b-strand braid closing to a zero-framed knot. The parameters and state are those of [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(Y) in C[Y,Y^(-1)], F_N(1)=K_N=<K>_N, F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. (1.1) The evenness and operator descent to Y were proved in [the squared-meridian note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md). The integer-color identities are the independently proved [quotient-color pointing](root_orbit_pointing.md). Here C_j has unknot value one; it is used to control exact polar data, not through a Jones asymptotic assumption. Put zeta_j=Q_N^j and S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1). There is a unique polynomial P_N of degree at most N-2 with P_N(zeta_j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. Define p_N(Y)=P_N(Y)/S_N(Y), R_N(Y)=(F_N(Y)-P_N(Y))/S_N(Y). (1.2) Then R_N is Laurent polynomial. With eta_N=i^(N+3), the exact full ADO state decomposes as N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1) R_N(M^2) +eta_N M^(N-1) p_N(M^2). (1.3) The second term has every polar principal part of the full state away from M=0 and infinity. The first term is regular there. This prescription is canonical in the marked Y-coordinate: p_N has precisely those simple principal parts, is regular at zero, and tends to zero at infinity. The main conclusions, proved below, are: * All C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N, satisfy the uniform bound |C_j(q_N)|<=[j]_(q_N)^(b-1)<=D_N, where D_N=sin(pi/N)^(1-b)<=(N/2)^(b-1). * |p_N(1)|<=D_N. Thus the regular full period and the full ADO value at completeness differ by a polynomially bounded quantity. * Exactly R_N(1)=(1/N) Tr_(C(Y)/C(U))(Y F_N(Y))|_(U=1), U=Y^N. (1.4) * A specified actual all-level operator, after a fixed rational gauge and denominator clearing, gives an affine equation for R_N. Its source has Laurent support in a fixed interval and coefficients O(D_N), independently of N. The last claim concerns meridian functions at each root. No corresponding bound on q-derivatives transverse to the root is inferred. ## 2. A positive trace bounds all the ordinary colors We reconstruct the finite algebra needed for the bound. Assume N>=3, theta=pi/N, and put delta=2cos(theta), mu_a=sin((a+1)theta)/sin(theta), 0<=a<=N-2. All mu_a are positive; with mu_(-1)=mu_(N-1)=0 they obey mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta*mu_a. Let H_m have the orthonormal basis of length-m walks on the chain 0,...,N-2 starting at zero. On a walk a, define U_i to be zero unless a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=c. Otherwise it replaces the middle height a_i by a neighbor a_i' of c, with matrix entry (U_i)_(a',a)=sqrt(mu_(a_i')mu_(a_i))/mu_c. (2.1) Direct multiplication gives U_i*=U_i, U_i^2=delta U_i, U_i U_(i+1) U_i=U_i, and commuting distant generators. For the square use the displayed neighbor sum. In the adjacent product the middle heights are forced at its two outer steps and the square-root ratios cancel, leaving the single U_i entry. Thus these are actual Temperley--Lieb matrices. The braid matrix B_i=q_N^(1/2) I-q_N^(-1/2) U_i (2.2) is unitary: its two eigenvalues are q_N^(1/2) and -q_N^(-3/2). The braid relation follows by expanding and using the three local Temperley--Lieb relations. The nonnormalized positive trace is tau_m(A)=sum_walks mu_(a_m) A_(a,a). (2.3) Endpoint preservation makes it tracial. The neighbor sum gives tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta*tau_m(A), and (2.1) gives tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). These identities determine the diagram trace: every Temperley--Lieb diagram at the next level is in the span of the included algebra and A U_m B, and cyclicity reduces the latter trace to the preceding level. In particular this trace agrees with the algebraic closure trace. Here is its connection with the fixed actual R. On the ordinary two-dimensional color, after retaining the common Cartan scalar, R_checked=q^(1/2) I-q^(-1/2) U, where U is zero on 00 and 11 and has block U|_(01,10)=[ q -1 ; -1 q^(-1) ]. (2.4) This follows by substituting E v_1=v_0 into the actual finite R. It obeys U^2=(q+q^(-1))U and the adjacent relation. With K=diag(q,q^(-1)), its partial quantum trace is I. Thus the actual quantum trace has precisely the two trace recursions above and equals (2.3), even though (2.4) itself is not Hermitian in the unmodified tensor basis. For completeness the j-color is represented by the idempotent p_(j-1). The recursion, within the requisite tensor power, is p_0=p_1=I, p_(m+1)=p_m tensor I -[m]/[m+1]*(p_m tensor I)U_m(p_m tensor I). (2.5) The Temperley--Lieb relations inductively give p_m U_i=U_i p_m=0 for i<m and (p_m U_m p_m)^2=([m+1]/[m])p_m U_m p_m; substituting this last identity in (2.5) verifies idempotence at the next step. All coefficients are real and denominators nonzero in the range used here. Hence these idempotents are orthogonal projections in (2.1). The trace recursion and delta*[m+1]-[m]=[m+2] give tau_m(p_m)=[m+1]. (2.6) This also verifies the actual color rather than assigning it by name. For generic q the common kernel of the U_i in V_1^(tensor m) has one vector at each weight: each adjacent exchange imposes the q-ratio read from (2.4), and adjacent exchanges connect all words of that weight. These m+1 vectors are F^r(v_0 tensor ... tensor v_0), with E F^r=[r][m-r+1]F^(r-1). Thus the image is exactly the ordinary (m+1)-dimensional highest-weight color. This identity specializes for m<=N-2, when all needed denominators remain nonzero. Cabling the actual finite R and restricting to these images gives its color R by the coproduct identity; equivalently expand the coproduct powers by the q-binomial formula. This is the same color comparison proved in [the degree note](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md#3-passing-from-parallel-strands-to-the-actual-color). For a b-strand braid colored by j<N, the tensor product P of these projections has positive trace [j]^b. The cabled braid is unitary, preserves P, and its framing correction has modulus one. On the image of P each diagonal entry of a unitary has modulus at most one. The positive trace therefore gives |C_j(q_N)|<=tau(P)/[j]=[j]^(b-1). (2.7) This is uniform in j,N. For N=2 only j=1 occurs and the statement is immediate. Since sin(pi/N)>=2/N, the D_N bound in Section 1 follows. At j=N the positive trace of the corresponding projection is zero; division by [N] is unavailable. Nothing here bounds the Kashaev color. ## 3. The exact principal parts and the regular remainder At a root zeta_j of S_N, S_N'(zeta_j)=N*zeta_j^(-1)/(zeta_j-1). Lagrange interpolation gives P_N(Y)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N) *S_N(Y)/((Y-zeta_j)S_N'(zeta_j)), p_N(Y)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N)*zeta_j*(zeta_j-1)/(N*(Y-zeta_j)). (3.1) The roots are simple and F_N-P_N vanishes at all of them. Since S_N(0)=1, division in the Laurent ring proves R_N is Laurent polynomial. It also gives the whole wall value R_N(zeta_j)=(F_N'(zeta_j)-P_N'(zeta_j))/S_N'(zeta_j). (3.2) The full state's phase, its monomial M^(N-1), and every divisor in S_N remain in (1.3). This is an identity of meridian germs, not a replacement of any factor by its numerical value at M=1. In particular both summands retain parity (-1)^(N-1) on the M-cover. Putting Y=1 in (3.1) gives P_N(1)=-sum_(j=1)^(N-1) zeta_j C_j(q_N), p_N(1)=-(1/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1) zeta_j C_j(q_N), |p_N(1)|<=D_N, K_N=N R_N(1)+P_N(1). (3.3) The interpolation coefficients themselves are [Y^r]P_N=(1/N)sum_j C_j(q_N)(zeta_j^(-r)-zeta_j), 0<=r<=N-2. (3.4) They have modulus at most 2D_N. More usefully, every Taylor coefficient of the proper polar function at zero satisfies [Y^r]p_N=(1/N)sum_j C_j(q_N)(1-zeta_j)zeta_j^(-r), |[Y^r]p_N|<=2D_N, r>=0. (3.5) This direct formula avoids estimating a growing Vandermonde inverse. The subsequent [actual Weyl-descent proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) now proves C_(N-j)=C_j for every knot in these conventions. It rewrites (3.5) as an exact sine-matrix moment and improves its bound to D_N. Thus the bounded Laurent source has an explicit Weyl structure, without a new quantum-state definition. Its geometric coupling and cross-level norm remain unproved. ## 4. Any actual operator supplies a bounded rootwise source Take the specified actual all-level reduced operator in squared-meridian coordinates, P_hat=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(q,Y)T^j, T Y=q^2Y T. Existence and descent were proved in the [finite-state](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and [even-meridian](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) notes. Let f=Y-1. Choose and retain a fixed nonzero clearing factor c(q,Y) so that A_hat=c*f*P_hat*f^(-1) belongs to C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)][T]. (4.1) At the actual root U=Y^N is shift-invariant, and F_N/S_N=f F_N/(U-1). Therefore exactly A_hat(F_N/S_N)=0, A_hat R_N=b_N, b_N=-A_hat p_N. (4.2) This is the full ADO normalization after extracting its explicitly known eta_N M^(N-1). Equivalently this extraction twists the full shift by kappa=-q^(-1), retaining its N-cyclic sign (-1)^(N-1). It is not a new chosen knot state. Write the Laurent support of all coefficients of A_hat as contained in [r_-,r_+]. The source b_N is Laurent polynomial: (4.2) also equals A_hat R_N, which has no finite nonzero poles. At zero every shifted p_N is O(1); at infinity every shifted p_N is O(Y^(-1)). Hence b_N in span{Y^r : r_-<=r<=r_+-1}. (4.3) This finite-dimensional space is independent of N. Empty intervals mean the source is zero; nonvanishing or geometric coupling is not being assumed. There is also a uniform bound on its coefficients. If a_(j,e)(q) is the coefficient of Y^e in A_hat's j-th term, the coefficient of Y^k in -A_hat p_N is a sum of -a_(j,e)(q_N)*Q_N^(j*(k-e))*[Y^(k-e)]p_N, k-e>=0. Equation (3.5) and |Q_N|=1 bound it by 2D_N sum_(j,e)|a_(j,e)(q_N)|=O_A(D_N). (4.4) The sum is bounded because A_hat is fixed and Laurent polynomial in q. The argument holds at all sufficiently large levels where the specified annihilation identity applies. Every fixed meridian jet of b_N at Y=1 has the same polynomial bound, since its Laurent support is fixed. Restoring the full monomial contributes only the corresponding fixed powers of N to such jets. This removes a rational-source-factorization hypothesis from this *rootwise* construction. It does not prove that the coefficients of b_N come from a single rational function b(q,Y), that its generic difference-extension class is the earlier one, or that q-jets of those coefficients are bounded. The latter are not controlled by principal-root unitarity. The individual rootwise affine equation has the rational particular solution R_N, so it splits over that root field. This does not split the generic all-level extension: the source coefficients and the selected sections have not been algebraized in q. The cross-level period and its regulator norm remain the issue. There is a useful pointed uniqueness statement under a separate rank hypothesis. Suppose the rational homogeneous solutions of A_hat form the one-dimensional C(U)-line generated by u_N=F_N/S_N. Then every rational solution of (4.2) regular at both Y=Q_N and Y=1 has the same value R_N(1). Indeed the difference of two such solutions is c(U)u_N. The anchor C_1=1 makes u_N have a nonzero simple pole at Y=Q_N, so regularity there forces c to vanish at U=1. Since u_N is regular at Y=1, the difference has value zero there. Thus this source and its two meridian lattices determine the complete period without a remaining central scalar. Rank one is sufficient, not asserted for every actual knot operator. ## 5. The complete regular period is an intrinsic cyclic trace Let E_N=C(Y), K_N^cent=C(U), U=Y^N. The extension is cyclic with sigma(Y)=Q_NY, and Tr_(E_N/K_N^cent)(Y F_N(Y)) =sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Q_N^j Y F_N(Q_N^jY). (5.1) It is Laurent polynomial in U; its whole value at U=1 is defined. Equations (1.1) and (3.3) give t_N:=R_N(1)=(1/N)Tr(Y F_N)|_(U=1). (5.2) Thus the regularized complete value is already an algebraic period pairing on the actual cyclic object. The functional uses the marked monomial Y, not a selected eigenvalue with largest modulus. An anchored central rescaling F_N->c(U)F_N, c regular and c(1)=1, preserves it. An unpointed Hilbert-90 module alone still does not supply F_N. More generally every Fourier coefficient t_(N,r)=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) zeta_j^(-r)F_N(zeta_j) satisfies |t_(N,r)-K_N/N|<=D_N. The particular r=N-1 is (5.2). If the target volume is positive, exponential growth with that rate for K_N is equivalent to the same growth for any of these coefficients: their differences from K_N/N are polynomial, and log N/N tends to zero. This is an equivalence of the conjecture, not a proof of either side. ## 6. A positive trace norm gives another exact formulation On S_1=C[Y]/(Y^N-1), define the involution by conjugating coefficients and sending Y to Y^(-1). At the actual principal root it preserves the cyclic structure. The pointed state has the positive squared trace norm H_N=(1/N)Tr_(S_1/C)(F_N^* F_N) =|K_N|^2/N+(1/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2, 0<=H_N-|K_N|^2/N<=D_N^2. (6.1) For a hyperbolic knot with volume V>0, the following statements are equivalent: (2pi/N)log|K_N| -> V, (2pi/N)log|t_N| -> V, (pi/N)log H_N -> V. (6.2) For example the first implication uses (3.3): a polynomial term is exponentially smaller than a sequence of positive exponential rate. The converse follows from the same identity. The norm equivalence follows directly from the positive identity (6.1). Equivalently the regulator target log||P_hyp||=2V/pi becomes (4/N)log|t_N|-log||P_hyp|| ->0, (2/N)log H_N-log||P_hyp|| ->0. (6.3) The positivity here controls the semisimple tail. It does not estimate the complete regular period or prove its geometric coefficient. ## 7. Why a regularized period is needed at the complete point The anchor and evenness give F_N(q_N)=F_N(-q_N)=1. Therefore a nonvanishing geometric WKB amplitude uniformly valid across both M=1 and M=q_N cannot directly describe the reduced state if it has positive volume growth. Indeed a holomorphic geometric action with a nonzero finite shift multiplier, and an amplitude whose ratio at those points tends to a nonzero number, would give a nonzero finite limit for F_N(q_N)/F_N(1). The anchor would then exclude positive exponential growth of F_N(1). The exact decomposition explains how such an inference fails: F_N(Y)=S_N(Y)R_N(Y)+P_N(Y). (7.1) The regular term is multiplied by a function with S_N(1)=N and S_N(zeta_j)=0 for every ordinary orbit color. The actual full ADO normalization precisely removes that function, leaving the regular period R_N and the controlled polar part. The zeros and poles occur at spacing O(1/N); a coefficientwise formal branch cannot erase their whole meridian germs. This uses the exact original factors, including the sign character, rather than an asymptotic replacement. The [geometric action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) and [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) now provide the marked regulator connection and norm to compare with t_N or H_N. What remains is proving that this specified regular quantum period has that norm. Bounded source coefficients alone do not prove its coupling, noncancellation, or the geometric factor's survival in the summed operator. No volume conjecture is claimed here. The subsequent [normal-period construction](peripheral_normal_period.md) keeps the factor Y-1 in the polynomial quantum module. Its complete full ADO value is the first normal derivative of (Y-1)F_N across U=1. A boundary-column argument gives a necessary factor condition for positive volume growth. Under the stated rank, or checked Weyl-sector invertibility, condition that derivative is an exact inverse-matrix period with known bounded source. It equals R_N(1) plus the controlled p_N(1), with the full phase retained. Its norm comparison is still additional work. ## 8. Coverage and independent verification Positive Temperley--Lieb path traces and unitary braid matrices are existing theory; [Aharonov--Jones--Landau](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0511096) is one explicit coverage source. The connection of root-of-unity nonsemisimple invariants with derivatives already has coverage in [Murakami](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287), while the ADO/integer-color unification is covered by [Willetts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854). No proof, completion theorem, or asymptotic result from those sources is a premise here. Partial-fraction interpolation and cyclic field traces are standard algebra; no novelty claim is made for them. [The audit](../experiments/audit_regularized_kashaev_period.py) compares 30 positive colored path traces with independently assembled actual highest-weight cut states, checks 62 principal-root color bounds including colors next to the truncation wall, and checks the ADO quotient-color identification at the small levels. Ten exact finite- field Laurent cut calculations verify all polar divisions, every ordinary-color value, the cancelled wall derivatives, and the weighted cyclic trace identity. All checks passed. The uniform arguments above, rather than these finite samples, prove the statements. Results are in [the audit output](../experiments/regularized_kashaev_period_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_regularized_kashaev_period.py

title: What cyclotomic descent can identify with the regulator connection
text: # What cyclotomic descent can identify with the regulator connection Focused applicability audit, 27 October 2026. The marked Bloch regulator has an algebraic logarithmic connection, but its exact finite quantum step is not thereby rational in Q,Y. An absolute rational unipotent family with identity cyclotomic curvature cannot supply that regulator connection in a regular Q->1 limit. This remains true even if its initial rational gauge has poles at Q=1. The appropriate possible use of zero-curvature descent is a relative comparison between two already specified period realizations, with their sources and markings. No construction of that actual comparison or volume theorem is asserted here. ## 1. A rational-coboundary confluence lemma Let k be an infinite characteristic-zero field and put h=Q-1, D=Y partial_Y. Suppose a rational matrix C(Q,Y) is regular at Q=1 as a matrix over k(Y)[[h]], with C(Q,Y)=I+h A(Y)+O(h^2). (1.1) Assume it is a generic rational coboundary in the column convention: C(Q,Y)=G(Q,QY)G(Q,Y)^(-1), G in GL_d(k(Q,Y)). (1.2) Then the differential equation D v=A(Y)v has a fundamental matrix in GL_d(k(Y)). A pole of the initial G at Q=1 does not evade this conclusion. **Proof.** Introduce an independent anchor Z, fixed by sigma and D, and normalize on the right: Ghat(Q,Y;Z)=G(Q,Y)G(Q,Z)^(-1). (1.3) It obeys the same transport and Ghat(Q,Z;Z)=I. Its Laurent expansion in h has finite principal part. Its coefficients are rational in Y,Z and regular at Y=Z over k(Z). To see the last point, take a common rational denominator before expanding. Its first nonzero h coefficient as a polynomial in Y is nonzero at the generic value Y=Z. The extra normalization denominator is independent of Y and has the same property at generic Z. Thus expansion and evaluation at Y=Z commute. If Ghat had a negative leading order -r, r>0, the coefficient G_(-r) would satisfy D G_(-r)=A G_(-r), G_(-r)(Z;Z)=0. (1.4) This follows by comparing order h^(1-r) in sigma(Ghat)=C Ghat. The coefficients of A(Y)/Y are regular at the generic anchor. Expanding at Y=Z, the formal differential equation uniquely determines all coefficients from the constant term, so the zero initial value makes G_(-r)=0. This contradicts its leading-order choice. Hence Ghat is regular at Q=1. Its constant matrix G_0(Y;Z) has G_0(Z;Z)=I and satisfies D G_0=A G_0. (1.5) It is generically invertible. Specialize Z to a value in k avoiding the finitely many rational denominator and determinant exceptions. This gives a fundamental matrix over k(Y), proving the lemma. The same argument can be expressed analytically at a generic complex anchor. The independent-anchor proof avoids an assumption of uniform Laurent expansion at an accidentally degenerate numeric anchor. The anchor condition matters. For the scalar G=Y-Q one has C=Q(Y-1)/(Y-Q)=1+h Y/(Y-1)+O(h^2). Normalization at the fixed anchor Y=1 gives Ghat=1-(Y-1)/h and remains singular. That anchor is a pole of the limiting connection; it is excluded by the generic construction. At an independent Z the normalized limit is (Y-1)/(Z-1), the required rational fundamental solution. ## 2. Consequence of full cyclotomic curvature identity The full rank-one and upper-triangular descent theorems construct a rational G satisfying (1.2) when the specified rational triangular transport has identity whole cyclotomic curvature. If that transport also has the regular form (1.1), the lemma shows that its entire classical differential limit is rationally gauge trivial. Here the coefficient-field and full-root hypotheses are those in [the descent theorem](additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.md): principal roots suffice for rational coefficients by Galois descent; over a number field one must supply the additional whole-root or coefficient-conjugate marking stated there. The statement is about the full differential module, not the residue of every displayed matrix entry in every gauge. A rational singular gauge can change individual residues and higher pole terms. What is excluded is a nontrivial marked logarithmic extension such as the regulator's first additive logarithm block below. There is an exact root-normal version as well. For every sufficiently large root where G is defined, take the module T=C^(-1)sigma_Q. The gauge v=G w changes it to sigma_Q. By the gauge law of [the first quantum-normal construction](first_quantum_normal_connection.md), the descended operator pi L_1/N^2 is therefore the trivial connection U partial_U in that invariant frame, U=Y^N. This assertion does not need a regular Q=1 gauge. It holds at each regular finite root. It does not make an arbitrary pointed source section horizontal. Nor does it identify generic kernels with special central-fiber kernels at rank jumps. Those remain source/lattice questions. ## 3. The marked regulator is not a rationally trivial connection On the normalized marked A-curve let m be the nonconstant meridian function and l the longitude function in the recorded conventions. The Heisenberg period equations are dU=dm/m, dV=dl/l, dH=U dl/l. (3.1) More precisely Pi=[1 U H;0 1 V;0 0 1] obeys the right equation dPi=Pi Omega, with Omega_12=dm/m, Omega_23=dl/l, and other entries zero. In the column convention the fundamental matrix is Pi^t and its connection matrix is Omega^t. These equations define an algebraic flat connection on the curve, with its fundamental-class mark fixing the central period. Already dm/m has no rational primitive on the curve: at a zero or pole of m its residue is ord_p(m)!=0, whereas an exact differential of a rational function has residue zero. A nonconstant meromorphic function on the compact normalized curve has such a divisor. The same obstruction survives every finite algebraic cover. The pullback residue is multiplied by the nonzero ramification index; it remains nonzero in characteristic zero. Thus Log m is not an algebraic function on any finite cover. Equivalently the rank-two additive block d(v_1)=v_2 dm/m, d(v_2)=0 (3.2) has no rational fundamental matrix, even on a finite cover. A horizontal rational vector with v_2!=0 would supply the forbidden primitive. This block obstructs rational triviality of the full marked Heisenberg connection. Directly in its recorded right convention, suppose K were a rational fundamental matrix for dK=K Omega. Its first column f_1 is a nonzero constant vector, and its second column obeys d f_2=f_1 dm/m. A constant row functional a with a f_1=1 would give the forbidden rational primitive a f_2. This avoids any choice of a splitting of the rank-three filtration. Consequently the regulator connection cannot be identified, preserving its flat structure and meridian marking, with an absolute rational triangular family satisfying both identity cyclotomic curvature and the regular confluence hypothesis (1.1). The finite-root normal connection of an absolute rational coboundary is likewise trivial and does not already give the marked regulator connection. These are global function-field obstructions. In a small analytic disk at m=1, or its formal completion, Log m is a perfectly valid primitive. Local formal triviality is not generic rational or finite-algebraic triviality. Algebraicity of the complete gluing shape does not remove this distinction. ## 4. A rational deformation can carry logarithms if curvature is retained The obstruction is not to a rational deformation of the differential connection. A simple Heisenberg example makes the missing condition explicit. On the torus chart take m=Y, l=Y^r for an integer r, and A=E_12+r E_23, A^3=0. The logarithmic connection is d v=A v dlog Y. The rational matrix C_rat(Q)=exp((Q-1)A) =I+(Q-1)A+(Q-1)^2 A^2/2 (4.1) has that regular differential limit. Its exact root curvature is C_rat(zeta_N)^N =exp(N(zeta_N-1)A), (4.2) which is not identity for N>=2 when A!=0. Its limit is exp(2pi*i A), the nontrivial logarithmic monodromy. All central Heisenberg terms are retained in this formula. The exact horizontal step of that same differential connection, on the chosen logarithmic sheet, is instead C_exact(Q)=exp((Log Q)A). (4.3) It contains Log Q and is not rational or algebraic in Q. Already its first superdiagonal is Log Q. This cannot be made a rational function by a rational additive gauge: such a change adds a rational function to that entry. The residue of dQ/Q on a finite cover also directly excludes an algebraic Log Q. Thus a rational algebraic connection does not furnish a rational exact q-step. Formula (4.1) gives a genuine confluence construction, while (4.3) gives exact connection transport; they are distinct whole objects. This torus example isolates the logarithmic issue and is not a replacement knot state or a hyperbolic volume model. ## 5. The precise possible use of comparison descent The zero-curvature theorems can be applied to a specified relative comparison whose own transport has identity curvature. They should not be applied to trivialize the absolute regulator period. Two period realizations may carry the same nontrivial logarithmic and central periods while their relative algebraic comparison descends. Its source, cut anchor and integral lattice still must be matched. Equality or conjugacy of the two absolute curvature matrices is insufficient. On a Hom module its curvature acts on a comparison matrix P by P |-> H_act P H_geo^(-1); even H_act=H_geo does not make this action identity on all matrices. One needs a specified comparison line or filtered subobject on which that relative action is identity, or an actual curvature-intertwining section together with the necessary descent data. Nor is the naive product C_geo^(-1) C_act in general the transport matrix of this Hom module. The descent theorem applies only after this relative zero-curvature object has been constructed. Likewise the actual geometric quantum action has an exponential scale exp(W/Log Q). It need not be a regular unipotent confluence of the form (1.1). Singular or derived limits outside the lemma's hypotheses require their own maps and normal source complexes; they are not justified by a scalar norm equation. The actual first-normal source constructed from the finite-sum central derivative and the Fourier--Mellin source are genuine data available for that comparison. No equality with the regulator source or its nonzero selected period is inferred here. [Exact confluence/gauge audit](../experiments/audit_regulator_curvature_obstruction.py). [Results](../experiments/regulator_curvature_obstruction_results.json).

title: Majorization, exact regulator conservation, and pointed energy
text: # Majorization, exact regulator conservation, and pointed energy 28 October 2026. Majorization gives a sharp general product inequality, but by itself it pays the pointwise singular-value envelope. There is a stronger, useful strict-convexity statement: a bistochastic mixing map which fixes the regulator observable can mix only equal-regulator channels. That property makes the exponential action weights telescope and gives an endpoint bound for the original source energy. The actual quantum connection has not been proved to possess this property. ## 1. The general log-majorization inequality For invertible d by d matrices A_j let s_1>=...>=s_d be their singular values and P=A_(m-1)...A_0. For every 1<=r<=d, sum_(i<=r)log s_i(P) <=sum_j sum_(i<=r)log s_i(A_j). (1) Indeed the product of the top r singular values is the operator norm of the r-th exterior power. Apply the elementary product-norm bound there. At r=d equality holds, by multiplicativity of the determinant. Thus log s(P) is majorized by the decreasing vector with entries sum_j log s_i(A_j). For completeness, the convex-function implication needs no imported inequality. The partial-sum inequalities imply sum_i (u_i-t)_+ <=sum_i (v_i-t)_+ for every t, because each side is the maximum over r of its top-r sum minus rt. Every convex piecewise linear function is a linear function plus a positive combination of these hinge functions. Approximation proves sum f(u_i)<=sum f(v_i) for every convex f. Taking f(t)=exp(pt), p>0, yields the corresponding Schatten bound. This is sharp with only the individual singular spectra specified: positive diagonal matrices whose decreasing singular directions are aligned attain equality. It cannot be generally improved by changing the convex function. On a regular slowly varying recurrence with a tame supplied instantaneous eigenbasis, the transformed steps are diag(lambda_i(x_j))+O(1/N). For eigenvalues bounded away from zero, their singular logarithms are the decreasing log|lambda_i|+O(1/N). Consequently (1) yields the integral of the POINTWISE sorted root moduli. It does not yield the maximum complete marked-branch action. For r=1 this is the safe classical spectral envelope already proved for the actual source. All exterior-power refinements retain the same limitation at r=1. The actual source costs are not part of a singular-spectrum list: |ell^*P s|<=||ell|| ||s|| s_1(P). In the actual macroscopic theorem, s is the entire ordinary-color packet on the denominator-avoiding complex circle and has proved polynomial norm. That fact makes (1) an original-source upper bound; it does not supply a new branch-selection inequality. ## 2. Strict convexity gives a stronger exact rigidity Let C be a nonnegative doubly stochastic matrix and r a real vector. One has the EXACT variance identity sum_(i,k) C_(ik)(r_i-r_k)^2 =2 r dot (r-Cr). (2) The two quadratic terms on expansion use the row and column sums. In particular, if Cr=r, every term on the left vanishes: C_(ik)>0 => r_i=r_k. (3) This is also the equality case of strict convexity of t^2 under doubly stochastic averaging. Merely preserving the TOTAL mean of r does not give (3); every doubly stochastic matrix preserves that mean. There is a noncommutative version directly suited to an energy. Let Phi(X)=sum_a K_a X K_a^* be a bistochastic Kraus channel: sum_a K_a^*K_a=I, sum_a K_aK_a^*=I. For a Hermitian regulator observable R, sum_a ||R K_a-K_a R||_HS^2 =2 Tr[R(R-Phi(R))] =2 Tr[R(R-Phi^*(R))]. (4) Expansion proves this identity: the two square terms each give Tr R^2, and the cross term is Tr[R Phi(R)]. Thus if either the Schroedinger or Heisenberg channel fixes R, EVERY Kraus operator commutes with R and with exp(tR). In an eigenbasis of R, all mixing is inside equal-regulator blocks. This is substantially stronger than conservation of one scalar mean in one selected state. For reference, a bistochastic channel also majorizes the eigenvalues of every positive input. For a rank-r projection Q, Tr[Q Phi(rho)]=Tr[Phi^*(Q)rho], where 0<=Phi^*(Q)<=I and Tr Phi^*(Q)=r. Diagonalizing rho bounds this trace by the sum of its top r eigenvalues; maximize over Q. This proves the usual convex energy inequalities directly. The NEW information required for (3) or (4) is the fixed regulator observable, not bistochasticity alone. ## 3. Exact telescoping with the original source retained Here is a concrete sufficient condition for endpoint control. It is an algebraic transport theorem, not a claim about an unverified knot connection. Let r_j be specified real diagonal action vectors and G_j=diag(exp(N r_(i,j))). Suppose the diagonal propagation is D_j=G_(j+1) A_j G_j^(-1), A_j diagonal, ||A_j||<=exp(epsilon_j), sum_j epsilon_j=o(N). (5) Unitary diagonal phases may be included in A_j. Suppose the ACTUAL energy evolution is rho_(j+1)=D_j Phi_j(rho_j)D_j^*, (6) where Phi_j is bistochastic and fixes diag(r_j) as in (4). These are conditions on specified local connection maps; no unknown terminal product or Kashaev value enters their definition. They imply Tr[G_m^(-1)rho_m G_m^(-1)] <=exp(2sum_j epsilon_j) Tr[G_0^(-1)rho_0 G_0^(-1)]. (7) Proof. By (4) each K_(a,j) commutes with G_j. Write rhohat_j=G_j^(-1)rho_j G_j^(-1). Then EXACTLY rhohat_(j+1)=A_j Phi_j(rhohat_j) A_j^*. Take the trace, use positivity and trace preservation, and iterate. This is the desired partial-sum telescoping: all intermediate action potentials cancel, including at equal-regulator mixing events. For a genuine amplitude recurrence the special case is one UNITARY Kraus operator U_j. If [U_j,diag(r_j)]=0 and A_j=I, the whole product is exactly P=G_m (U_(m-1)...U_0)G_0^(-1). (8) If the zero anchor gives G_0=I, the singular values of P are EXACTLY the endpoint exp(N r_(i,m)), up to ordering. Thus every top-r log-majorization bound telescopes to an endpoint sum, not an integral of separately sorted local increments. For the original pure input rho_0=s s^* and output ell, (7) gives ell^*rho_m ell <=exp(2sum epsilon_j) ||G_m ell||^2 ||G_0^(-1)s||^2. (9) When the actual evolution is coherent, rho_m=P s s^*P^*, its left side is exactly |ell^*P s|^2. No replacement of that evolution by an artificial mixture is implicit in (9). The general positive-output energy has the same bound with its specified output Gram matrix in place of ell ell^*. All actual external factors and original source normalizations remain outside this estimate unchanged. In particular a zero regulator anchor, polynomial original source and co-source norms, and r_(i,m)<=Vol(K)/(2pi) give the sharp desired UPPER rate. No nonzero overlap or lower rate follows. Introducing an artificial dephasing or a Kraus average does NOT establish premise (6). For the original coherent scalar one must prove its amplitude evolution or its exact selected Plancherel energy has that positive channel representation. Nor does regulator invariance under finite character-cover monodromy over a FIXED normalized peripheral point, or equality at a ramification point, imply invariance under the quantum connection. A meridian loop which ends on a different longitude sheet can have a different regulator. A bounded number of subexponentially bounded connection matrices supported only in equal-action blocks also suffices in (8), with a subexponential norm factor; more generally their summed logarithmic norm cost must be o(N). They need not be unitary. Genuine representation ramification supplies equality of the calibrated values on a colliding block. Proving that the actual quantum connection has only those blocks, with that bound, remains the analytic/source requirement. ## 4. Approximate conservation needs the right accuracy Formula (4) gives a quantitative diagnostic. If ||Phi^*(R)-R||_HS<=eta and ||R||_HS<=B, then sum_a ||[R,K_a]||_HS^2<=2B eta. (10) Across a pair of regulator eigenvalues separated by g, the total squared Kraus mass is at most 2B eta/g^2. Hence polynomial approximate conservation gives only polynomial off-block suppression. After conjugation by exp(NR), a transition from r_k to r_i carries exp[N(r_k-r_i)]. A polynomial error need not survive that factor. For example a bound from (10) alone would need eta exponentially smaller than exp[-2N(r_k-r_i)] for an upward weighted transition. The fixed point property or an actual action barrier is essential. The independently proved Gaussian model makes this quantitative: its off-diagonal coupling can be 1/N, its complete marked branch actions are zero, but its selected growth is a/4-theta^2/(4a)>0. Discarding coherent phases costs still more. If W_N(theta)=b_N sum_(k=0)^(N-1) exp[a k(N-k)/N+i k theta], exact finite Fourier orthogonality gives (1/N)sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)|W_N(2pi ell/N)|^2 =b_N^2 sum_(k=0)^(N-1)exp[2a k(N-k)/N]. (11) The square-root energy rate is a/4, exactly the scalar envelope, whereas fixed theta in (0,min(a,pi)) has the smaller coherent rate. Thus a positive phase-averaged energy can destroy the conversion penalty that one is trying to use. Equation (11) is a phase-variable example, NOT the actual root-color Plancherel energy: that actual identity retains its special ordinary-color polynomial remainder. ## 5. The knot-specific test suggested by majorization The useful test is stronger than convex ordering of root moduli: construct the ACTUAL connection on a calibrated representation packet and prove that its positive energy map is bistochastic and fixes the regulator observable, or prove directly that its entries are confined to equal-calibrated-action blocks with subexponential cost. The exact rigidity (2)--(4) then supplies the missing no-upward-action mixing statement and the source estimate (7)--(9). The [complex representation-path theorem](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md) already supplies calibrated equality at genuine normalized ramification and an absolute endpoint volume bound. The [two-bridge midpoint theorem](two_bridge_midpoint_regulator_anchor.md) supplies the zero anchor on every genuine component of that class. The finite quantum connection, its possible nodal jumps, and its exact selected energy are still to be identified and bounded. General log-majorization or Karamata does not manufacture those facts from eigenvalues alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_regulator_majorization.py): exterior-power partial sums, the bistochastic variance identity, regulator-fixed quantum channels, exact pointed action telescoping, and the finite Gaussian phase-Plancherel distinction. Coverage only: product log-majorization is established matrix theory; see [Tao, Jeong, and Gowda, Some log and weak majorization inequalities in Euclidean Jordan algebras](https://userpages.umbc.edu/~gowda/papers/trGOW20-02.pdf). The exterior-power, convexity, channel and source calculations used here are proved above independently.

title: Relative framing transgression and the literal finite cut projector
text: # Relative framing transgression and the literal finite cut projector Research note, 27 October 2026. This constructs an explicit relative boundary complex whose source and co-source are the original finite cut projector e and marked defect D. The marked meridian supplies the relative fiber endpoints; no Haar-volume division is introduced. There are two exact presentations: an intrinsic finite-root residue model and a smaller logarithmic residue model using the original canonical representatives. Their chain projection is literally e. This realizes the finite boundary source. It does not identify the internal quantum pushforward with the geometric Gaussian framing pushforward. In particular it does not prove survival of the geometric block in the selected global period or the volume conjecture. ## 1. The classical form needs a relative source At the complete meridian M=1, use the original framing chart Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], V=s partial_r, A=1/(1+s), t=r/s. Then V=partial_t and beta=dlog A=-ds/(1+s), Omega_cut=dt wedge beta, iota_V Omega_cut=beta. (1.1) The ordinary two-form is exact: Omega_cut=d(t beta). This primitive is not harmless for a relative source, because its endpoint values are different. The relative endpoints have a marked geometric meaning. The regular meridian centralizer in the existing note is C_b=[1+kappa*b b;0 1], with kappa=M-M^(-1), and its action at M=1 is r->r+b s. The meridian itself is the centralizer section b=M, so at M=1 it translates t to t+1. A choice of initial framing section therefore gives the relative pair t=0,t=1. Replacing that section by t_0(A) translates both endpoints together. Since (dt-dt_0) wedge beta=dt wedge beta, the transgressed source below is independent of this choice on its invariant forms whenever the section change is regular on the retained source chart. A section with a pole at an added root requires its own boundary lattice data; no extension through that pole is inferred here. The geometric invertible-framing chart has s!=0, so A!=1. For the finite cut source we use the explicit extension F_tilde=A^1_t times G_m,A. It agrees with the framing chart at A!=1. Its added A=1 divisor is boundary source data, not an assertion that the original geometric frame remains invertible there. The generic meridian has a further marked period which must not be silently replaced by one. At fixed M, t=r/s gives Omega_cut=[dt/(1+kappa*t)] wedge dlog A, A=M/(M+s), V=(1+kappa*t)partial_t. The meridian sends t=0 to t=M. On its specified local logarithmic branch its relative centralizer period is L(M)=integral_0^M dt/(1+kappa*t) =Log(M^2)/kappa, L(1)=1. (1.2) This is a marked regular period, not a rational function. The centralizer power adapter already proved in the existing note gives L(M^N)=[N/u_N(M)]L(M), u_N(M)=(M^N-M^(-N))/(M-M^(-1)). (1.3) Indeed the adapted power map is t'=[(1+kappa*t)^N-1]/(kappa*u_N), and it pulls back the invariant differential to (N/u_N)dt/(1+kappa*t). Formula (1.3) retains exactly the actual modified-dimension factor 1/u_N. The generic centralizer also has an absolute multiplicative cycle, absent in the additive fiber. We do not identify its entire generic relative de Rham group with the polynomial additive resolution below. The finite source coefficients themselves retain their full M dependence throughout. ## 2. A relative complex with an explicit contraction For any characteristic-zero vector space E define a two-term complex R(E)^1=E[t], R(E)^2=E[t] direct_sum E direct_sum E, delta h=(partial_t h,h(0),h(1)). (2.1) All other degrees are zero. Define L(a,b_0,b_1)=integral_0^1 a(t)dt-b_1+b_0, i(f)=(f,0,0). (2.2) The integral is polynomial antiderivation over a characteristic-zero field; no analytic convergence or contour choice is used. We have L delta=0 and L i=I. Moreover the explicit degree-minus-one map H(a,b_0,b_1)(t) =b_0+integral_0^t [a(u)-L(a,b_0,b_1)]du (2.3) satisfies delta H+H delta=I-iL. Therefore H^1 R(E)=0, H^2 R(E)=E, R(E) equivalent to E[-2]. (2.4) Every linear map E->E' acts coefficientwise on this complex and commutes with delta,L,i,H. This naturality will retain every actual finite quantum matrix, source and cut. Geometrically, (2.1) is the relative de Rham complex along t=0,1 after taking a residue quotient in the A direction. A pair of the form (a(t)dt wedge omega,b_0 omega,b_1 omega) represents its degree two element, where omega is the chosen logarithmic normal form. The relative differential is (d omega,restriction omega-d eta). It gives precisely (2.1). The transgression is (2.2). In particular (dt wedge beta,0,0) gives a nonzero relative class: its image is beta. The ordinary primitive t beta has endpoint pair (0,beta), so its relative coboundary is (dt wedge beta,0,beta), whose transgression vanishes. Ordinary exactness does not kill the sourced relative class. ## 3. The intrinsic finite-root residue realization Fix the actual N>=2 and Q primitive of order N, over a field k containing its roots. Let C_N=k[A,A^(-1)]/(A^N-1), D_N={A^N=1}, omega_N=A^(N-1)dA/(A^N-1) =(1/N)dlog(A^N-1). (3.1) On F_tilde take logarithmic forms along A^1_t times D_N modulo forms regular along that divisor, and take their relative cone for t=0,1. The quotient has terms C_N[t] omega_N in degree one and C_N[t] dt wedge omega_N in degree two; differentiation is partial_t. Its relative complex is exactly R(C_N). The actual state f in C_N is the class i(f). Its cut functional is Phi_N(a,b_0,b_1)=(1/N)Tr_(C_N/k) L(a,b_0,b_1). (3.2) To see its literal residue meaning, first transgress in t and then sum residues at the N points of D_N. At A=Q^j, Res_(A=Q^j) f omega_N=f(Q^j)/N. Thus for an actual boundary vector f, Phi_N i(f)=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) f(Q^j) =phi_N(f), (3.3) the original balanced co-source. This is intrinsic to the finite algebra: replacing a representative by (A^N-1)g changes its form by one regular at D_N, hence changes no residue class. For a whole normal family retain U and use C_U=k[U,U^(-1),A]/(A^N-U). If f is regular at U=1, then Tr_dR(f dlog A)=(Tr f/N)dlog U, Tr_dR(f omega_N)=(Tr f/N)dlog(U-1), Res_(U=1)Tr_dR(f omega_N)=phi_N(f|_(U=1)). (3.4) Here omega_N is pulled back as (1/N)dlog(U-1). The factor U-1 is retained before specialization. Equation (3.4) is also a direct trace/residue realization of the source's normal direction. ## 4. The logarithmic zero-residue source and the exact projector Let R(k) be the same relative complex with logarithmic normal form beta=dA/A along the added A=0 source boundary of the A-line. This added boundary is not a new geometric critical point. For a finite state use its original canonical representative f_tilde(A)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) f_j A^j. Transgression followed by Res_(A=0) sends (dt wedge f_tilde beta,0,0) to f_0. Root orthogonality gives f_0=phi_N(f). (4.1) Thus the original canonical representative defines a strict cochain map R(C_N)->R(k), applying phi_N to every coefficient. Its section R(k)->R(C_N) applies the constant vector psi=1. Their composition on R(C_N) is the coefficientwise chain map e=psi phi_N=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) S^j, S f(A)=f(QA). (4.2) This is the literal original finite cut projector, not just a map with the same scalar norm. In the evaluation basis A=Q^a, its matrix has every entry 1/N. It has rank one and e^2=e on H^2. The averaging identity and idempotence also hold strictly on the two-term resolution; rank one here refers to its finite H^2. The two residue presentations agree by (3.3)--(4.1). They are not an identification of their unweighted ambient differential forms. In the D_N residue model the appropriate normal source is omega_N=[A^N/(A^N-1)] beta. (4.3) The unweighted beta is regular along D_N and has zero image in that particular quotient. In the A=0 model beta already is its logarithmic source. The chain map in (4.2), with the prescribed canonical representatives, is the exact comparison between them. Neither formula permits evaluating the source's pole first and then discarding its normal class. ## 5. The original pivot and marked defect lift unchanged In the same balanced evaluation basis, the original pivot is g(A)=x^(1-N)A^(-1), x=-M/q. This section first works in C_N, where A^N=1, so the displayed formula equals the literal power K^(1-N) for K=xA^(-1). Multiplication by g and g^(-1) gives coefficientwise chain maps on R(C_N). Define D=g^(-1)e. (5.1) Then on H^2, identified with the original color space, and also coefficientwise on its resolution, gD=e, D^2=0, DgD=D, Tr_(H^2)(gD)=1. (5.2) Indeed phi_N(g^(-1))=x^(N-1)phi_N(A)=0 for N>=2. In the evaluation basis (5.1) has the original matrix D_(a,b)=x^(N-1)Q^a/N. For every finite cut matrix C, Tr_(H^2)(g D C)=Tr_(C_N)(e C) =phi_N(C psi). (5.3) Every such C lifts coefficientwise and commutes with the explicit relative contraction (2.3). Hence arbitrary finite internal matrix composition and contraction commute with this boundary realization. The same applies when tensoring the cut leg with the remaining finite color spaces. This is exact finite linear algebra at every level, not a semiclassical or knot-by-knot assertion. The marked defect is still not an ordinary Hopf-intertwining coupon. This lift does not authorize moving D unchanged through a crossing. The whole full-ADO factor d_N(M), with its phase, pole, residue and normal jet, remains a separate marked line multiplying (5.3). In particular the 1/N from the cut source and the value eta_N/N of the modified dimension at completeness are distinct normalizations. For a whole C_U normal extension, one must distinguish the reduced representative g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1) from the literal clock power g_lit=(xA^(-1))^(1-N)=U g_red. Their defects are respectively D_red=g_red^(-1)e and D_lit=U^(-1)D_red. Both products equal e, so the cut comparisons above remain exact. Their physical normal derivatives do differ: D_phys g_red=-g_red, while D_phys g_lit=(N-1)g_lit, with opposite rates for the two defects. Thus the U adapter is retained whenever a normal pivot jet is compared; a coefficientwise root representative is not relabeled as the literal clock power away from U=1. See the exact [Mellin lift comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), Section 2. ## 6. The representative carry and deleted-root obstruction remain The map (4.1) is linear and is not an algebra map. Canonical representatives satisfy the actual carry identity A f_tilde-(Af)_tilde=f_(N-1)(A^N-1). (6.1) In particular phi_N(Af)=f_(N-1), although Res_(A=0) A f_tilde beta is zero. Taking f=A^(N-1) gives phi_N(Af)=1 while phi_N(A)phi_N(f)=0. Thus the zero-residue source is compatible with multiplication only through the retained canonical carry. With U retained, its term is U f_(N-1); no normal source is removed. The open geometric framing chart A!=1 also cannot by itself carry the whole finite cut. The idempotent epsilon_1=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) A^j is killed by localization at A-1 but satisfies phi_N(epsilon_1)=1/N. Thus phi_N does not descend through C_N->C_N[(A-1)^(-1)]. This is a precise source obstruction to deleting the excluded framing point. It is distinct from the projector e in (4.2), although both involve a finite average. Epsilon_1 is multiplication by one root's idempotent; e is averaging the shift and has constant image. There is now a precise repair after adjoining the actual matrix Ward differential. The [source localization theorem](ward_source_localization.md) replaces the boundary representative by P=1-epsilon_1, e_S=[N/(N-1)]P e P. Its matrix cut row has the same Ward class as the original cut, while its color co-source factors through A-1 localization. An explicit chain retraction and homotopy extend this comparison to the combined relative-Ward complex. With U retained, the deleted branch is marked by alpha(U)^N=U, alpha(1)=1, and removed as a whole regular idempotent summand; every normal carry is retained. The original color co-source's obstruction above remains valid on R(C_N) alone. The repair uses Ward currents and changes its representative with the exact factor N/(N-1). This is a boundary comparison. Compressing two internal operators separately omits the excursion L C(I-P)D J, so the theorem does not authorize deletion inside crossings or an internal geometric Gaussian comparison without those additional currents. ## 7. What is still needed for the internal geometric pushforward This gives a concrete relative boundary object, explicit chain projection and contraction, and literal realizations of psi,phi,e,D. The marked meridian rather than an arbitrary group volume supplies its relative centralizer interval. Absolute exactness of the classical framing form is therefore not by itself a vanishing argument for a source-compatible relative period. The finite boundary resolution is natural for every actual matrix, so ordinary finite internal elimination respects it. Its auxiliary relative coordinate t is not thereby identified with the zero mode r/s produced by the internal semiclassical Gaussian pushforward. Constructing that comparison, including (6.1), the missing root idempotent, and the normal divisor (4.3), remains necessary. In particular a constant geometric principal density would have nonzero image under this relative functional if the internal pushforward were proved to give this class. The boundary model does not prove that premise or select a global thimble. It supplies the explicit cochain target and the exact source defects that the missing map must transport. ### Finite contraction and formal Gaussian reduction are different maps The exact naturality statement is the commuting finite diagram R(C_N) tensor V_rest --lift(C)--> R(C_N) tensor V_rest | L | L v v C_N tensor V_rest --C--> C_N tensor V_rest, with the analogous inclusion and explicit homotopy. Thus actual whole finite internal contraction really does induce a chain map on this boundary resolution.
