The result applies in particular to the full cleared resolvent numerator V_N(sigma) at every real or complex sigma, including repeated spectral nodes. ## 2. A regular finite-dimensional lift, not a generic ADO normalization Hold N fixed and introduce a variable q near q_N, on the original local square-root branch for the Cartan factors. On the ordinary highest-weight module of highest weight d use K v_a=q^(d-2a)v_a, F v_a=v_(a+1), E v_a=[a]_q[N-a]_q v_(a-1), 0<=a<=d. Endpoints are zero. The literal finite universal R has summation indices less than N; all factorial denominators [h]_q!, h<N, are units at q_N. Its inverse, the actual duality matrices, and all finite Casimir polynomials are therefore regular there. No denominator [N]_q is used in a matrix entry. For clarity the self-duality is regular too. In the standard basis set J(q)v_a=c_a(q)v_(d-a)^*, c_a(q)=(-1)^a q^(a(a-N)). (1) Using S(F)=-KF and S(E)=-EK^(-1), the F equation is c_(a+1)=-q^(-d+2a)c_a, and the E and K equations give the same intertwiner. At q_N, c_a=q_N^(a^2), the actual complete-color duality. Change to the literal balanced basis v_a/F_a(q), F_a(q)=prod_(h=1)^a(1-q^(2h)); every F_a with a<N is a unit at q_N. The actual cup and cap formulas are thus regular specializations of these generic finite matrices, with the root pivot correction below. Extend each fixed root polynomial f_e by keeping its coefficients fixed and replacing Omega by the generic pair Casimir Omega(q). Retained R_e^(epsilon_e) is extended by its ACTUAL finite universal crossing, not by a guessed generic interpolation of its root Hermite polynomial. These are Hopf intertwiners in the actual oriented/dual frames. For the cleared numerator an explicit choice avoids any inverse: f_sigma(z)=[chi_N(sigma)-chi_N(z)]/(sigma-z), chi_N(z)=2 T_N(z/2)+2. (2) Equation (2) is a polynomial in z and sigma. Only AFTER specializing q=q_N use chi_N(Omega)=0 to identify it with V_N(sigma). No generic meromorphic resolvent or cancellation at a repeated node is assumed. This construction is an auxiliary finite-dimensional polynomial specialization. It does not identify the generic standard pivot with the genuine-q ADO pivot or assert an equality of their transverse jets. ## 3. Scalar open caps and one generic closed contraction Use the standard generic pivot K and its actual oriented evaluation and coevaluation. After the boxes and all top caps except r, the network is a Hopf map from the unit object to V_d tensor V_d^* at that pair. Through the explicit cup identification this is an endomorphism C_r(q) of V_d commuting with the generators. It is scalar: K has distinct weights generically, and the consecutive nonzero F arrows force all diagonal entries equal. Write C_r(q)=a_r(q)I. Equivalently the remaining two-head vector is a_r(q) times its original cup. The scalar is regular at q_N: it is one matrix entry of the open network in the regular frames just constructed. This argument needs no ordinary quantum dimension at the root and introduces no new mark. Close the last pair with the ordinary K-pivotal cap. The result is the SAME fully closed tensor contraction Z(q), independent of which cap was temporarily left open. The explicit trace of K is Tr_(V_d)K=sum_(a=0)^d q^(d-2a)=[N]_q, Z(q)=[N]_q a_r(q) for every r. (3) The dual has the same trace, by reversing this finite weight sum. For generic q, [N]_q is nonzero, so all a_r(q) agree. They are regular at q_N, hence their equality specializes. The division in (3) occurs ONLY generically; no zero quantum dimension is divided at the root. This uses literal finite tensors and a finite weight sum, not an imported modified-trace cyclicity or ambidexterity theorem. ## 4. Return to the exact root pivot and unrestricted mark At q_N every main weight has parity d, so the ACTUAL pivot is g=K^(1-N)=(-1)^d K. (4) In the flat-plat convention all bottom turns are left cups and all ordinary top turns are right caps. The left cups are unchanged; each of the k-1 ordinary top caps therefore acquires the SAME factor (-1)^d relative to the K-pivotal network. This is independent of r. The balanced source formulas are, with x_0=q_N^d and Q=q_N^2, p_(i,j)=N x_0^(-j) delta_(i+j,d), ell_(i,j)=x_0^j g_i/N delta_(i+j,d), m_(i,j)=x_0^j/N^2. (5) The mark m is unrestricted. Equations (1) and F_a(q_N)F_(d-a)(q_N)=N(-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2) give the cup and ordinary cap in (5) directly. The original rank-one source e=psi phi, psi_a=1, phi_a=1/N, has Tr(e)=1, and its marked insertion is D=g^(-1)e. Thus Tr(gDC)=Tr(eC), and DIRECTLY mp=1. For the scalar open vector in section 3, the original marked evaluation is consequently S_r=(-1)^(d(k-1)) a_r(q_N), (6) with no additional N, quantum-dimension division or component-dependent factor. All full Cartan factors and retained half twists were already inside the same a_r. A fixed original framing/peripheral character multiplies both sides of (6) equally. This proves the stated equality for all permitted top caps, at either parity and composite levels. If the one-cut modified normalization is used, its complete-color factor i^(N+3)/N is the same on any such complete-colored cut. Deformed unequal main colors, unrestricted moves of the nonintertwining defect D, and generic-q ADO derivatives are NOT asserted to satisfy this identity. ## 5. Consequences and the remaining cap question The exact homogeneous face-source identity therefore gives equal marked coefficients for the different original top-cap targets, for EVERY choice of the full Casimir polynomials. In particular the full S_N(sigma) is identical as a polynomial in all spectral variables. This is stronger than merely equality of the final knot scalar at one twist vector. ### Corollary: a certificate at any permitted original top mark Fix a width $k\geq2$, an original ordered $2k$-strand flat-plat skeleton $D$, and fixed retained half twists $\epsilon_e\in\{0,\pm1\}$. Suppose the endpoint permutation gives a knot and that, at some original top mark $r$, the diagram has the actual labeled simple-white geometric certificate and satisfies **all** hypotheses of at least one of these proved full-source criteria: - [complete-radius balance](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md); - the [anchored shared-radius criterion](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md); - a [finite cover of the actual sectors](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md). The protected faces, complete packing, target extraction, and any finite shared-radius witnesses in the selected criterion are those for mark $r$. Choose this mark and certificate once, independently of the quantum level and filling vector. Then there is $T(D)<\infty$, with the chosen certificate included in the fixed data, such that for every independently signed integer vector $\mathbf p$ satisfying $|p_e|>T(D)$, fixed before $N\to\infty$, and for **every** original top mark $s$, $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|K_N^{(s)}\bigl(K_D(\mathbf p)\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_D(\mathbf p)\bigr). \tag{7} $$ Here the actual crossing powers are $n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e$ and $K_N^{(s)}$ uses the original full normalization, with only the permitted top mark changed. There is no comparability condition on the magnitudes of the independent twists. Both level parities and composite levels are included. The volume is that of the same actual filled knot exterior; no claim of exact bridge number $k$, a joint growing-twist/level limit, or a threshold uniform in different diagrams is made. **Proof.** Let $S_{N,r}(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ be the full marked numerator with the polynomial coupons (2), without an extra retained $R$ factor. Sections 1–4, applied with $\epsilon_e=0$, give the exact polynomial identity $S_{N,r}=S_{N,s}$ for every $N$. The original Fourier/Hermite transform is a linear functional of this full polynomial. Its sine factors, charge weights and parity, Gaussian powers $n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e$, and scalar $q_N^{d^2\sum_e n_e/4}(-i)^R$ are the same for both marks. Apply that same exact transform to the polynomial identity. Multiplying by the same recorded final-diagram framing/component character and complete-color normalization therefore gives $K_N^{(r)}=K_N^{(s)}$ at every level. The retained half twist appears exactly once, through $n_e$ in this Fourier description; the alternative direct coupon description retains its actual $R_e^{\epsilon_e}$ as in section 1. At mark $r$, the selected theorem supplies the full original invariant limit and a threshold depending on its fixed geometric and finite certificate data. The exact scalar equality transfers that conclusion to each $s$, with the same filled topology and threshold. In particular, we do not transport its all-CROSS summand or its remainder decomposition. This proves (7). The width-three [mark-dependence example](research_complete_balance_mark_dependence.md) separates two sufficient tests on the same literal diagram: one mark passes balance while another fails. With the present corollary the successful test suffices for either marked evaluation. This does **not** prove strict enlargement of the underlying unmarked knot classes, and does not show that every original diagram has a successful mark. The identity does NOT transport an individual cap window or a chosen LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT term. Those row projections are not arbitrary Casimir polynomials/intertwiners. Their absolute coefficient arrays, protected targets, signed-incidence cycles and envelope maxima change with the mark. Equality of the summed polynomial does not identify those maxima or guarantee that a new mark has no residual cap. The earlier finite- collar obstruction remains unchanged. A direct termwise mark-slide or an absolute cancellation estimate still needs its own proof. The source inputs are the [original all-coupon identity](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), [literal duality](relative_pivotal_duality.md), [turns and rank-one mark](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), and [root Casimir relation and regular highest-weight construction](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). The [mark-dependence example](research_complete_balance_mark_dependence.md) is separate geometry. The sufficient applications use the existing [complete-radius balance theorem](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md) or [anchored shared-radius theorem](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md). The [finite-collar obstruction](research_double_protected_cap_finite_collar_obstruction.md) is unchanged. No literature proof theorem is used here. ## 6. scope and finite verification The preserved [portable audit](../experiments/research_audit_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.py) and its [results](../experiments/research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport_results.json) check original physical coproduct matrices, complete divided-polynomial numerators at sigma=-2,2,0,3, arbitrary Casimir polynomials, and the actual positive and negative crossings. They verify the remaining two-head vector entrywise against its scalar times the original cup before comparing the original top marks. The exact fixtures use compatible finite fields and check the stated integer overflow bounds. They verify the full source identity at the tested levels, not projected-sector identities or an asymptotic theorem.

title: Every original MAIN edge gives the same full marked coefficient
text: # Every original MAIN edge gives the same full marked coefficient 31 October 2026. , unpublished finite source theorem. This extends the existing top-cap statement by an actual spherical rerouting and a general Morse compiler. It does not insert a newly reset mark into an internal head of the old presentation. No source sector or absolute envelope is transported. ## 1. Statement and exact scope Fix a connected complete-colored flat-plat source with R recorded boxes, N>=3, d=N-1, q_N=exp(pi i/N). Each original box carries its full matrix f_e(Omega) R_e^(epsilon_e), epsilon_e in {0,+1,-1}, in the original order, with the full Cartan/crossing scalar. The f_e are arbitrary finite polynomials; their coefficients may depend on N and on additional spectral parameters. Let H_e be their original homogeneous face polynomials, of degree d. Treat the crossing as its actual root polynomial only when forming H_e; its auxiliary generic lift below uses the actual finite universal crossing. Keep the actual labeled plane matching graph and its ordered quartet (x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e) at each box. Set P(L)=product_e H_e(L_xe,L_be,L_ce,L_ye), deg P=dR. For an original MAIN edge separating distinct faces a,b, put Z_(a,b)=[product_(f!=a,b)L_f^d] P |_(L_a=L_b=0). (1) Then Z_(a,b) equals the original top-cap-marked scalar, with the same full finite normalization. In particular it is independent of the MAIN edge, including edges on different complete-colored components. A fixed recorded exterior framing or component character multiplies both sides equally. No component-dependent normalization is introduced. The graph connectedness here is the projection connectedness already needed by the face compiler. MAIN edges have distinct adjacent faces in the intended certified simple-white class. More generally that property also follows by contracting each matching edge: the resulting connected 4-valent graph has no bridge, since every vertex degree is even. The theorem includes the full cleared numerator V_N(sigma), all its root Hermite data, both level parities and composite levels. It is not an equality for individual LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT projections, which are not the intertwiners used in the proof. Equation (1) does not claim that every choice of edge passes a geometric or absolute-source certificate. ## 2. A regular generic pivotal lift which matches the root exactly Hold N fixed and use a variable q on a neighborhood of q_N, with the same local square-root choice for Cartan factors. Work in the category generated by finite-dimensional integral highest-weight U_q(sl2) modules, tensor products, duals and direct sums. Write H for the integral weight operator and K=q^H. Define z=(-1)^H, g_tilde=zK. (2) E and F shift H by two, so z is central. It is group-like because the tensor-product weight is the sum, and z^2=1. Since the actual antipodes give S^2=Ad K, g_tilde implements the same S^2 and is a valid pivotal structure. On V_L and its dual, z=(-1)^L. At q=q_N, on EVERY integral weight, including tensor-product weights, q_N^(-NH)=(-1)^H, g_tilde=q_N^((1-N)H)=K^(1-N)=g. (3) Thus this auxiliary pivot specializes literally to the original pivot. It is not the generic ADO expression K^(1-N), which would not implement S^2 at generic q. No identity of their transverse derivatives is used. The regular complete-color lift is the ordinary highest-weight module V_d with K v_i=q^(d-2i)v_i, Fv_i=v_(i+1), Ev_i=[i]_q[N-i]_q v_(i-1), and endpoint arrows zero. Its self-duality is J(q)v_i=(-1)^i q^(i(i-N)) v_(d-i)^*. (4) Directly, the F equation is c_(i+1)=-q^(-d+2i)c_i, and the E,K equations agree. At the root c_i=q_N^(i^2), the specified actual duality. The balanced basis v_i/(q^2;q^2)_i is regular at q_N, since i<N. So are J, its inverse and all four g_tilde-pivotal turns. In the unbalanced self-dual frame one also checks directly J(q)^(-t)J(q)=(-1)^d K=g_tilde on V_d: its i-th diagonal entry is c_i/c_(d-i)=(-1)^d q^(d-2i). Thus the chosen generic double-dual frame already has the displayed pivot, not a missing sign. Extend each f_e by holding its coefficients fixed and using Omega(q). The actual R and R^(-1) have finite sums with factorial denominators [h]_q!, h<N, all units at q_N. Hence the original full box matrices are regular Hopf intertwiners in these exact local frames. For V_N one may use the polynomial [chi_N(sigma)-chi_N(z)]/(sigma-z), chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, and only at the root use chi_N(Omega)=0. No generic resolvent or simple-node interpolation replaces the numerator. ## 3. Sphericality for every generic endomorphism used here The two pivotal traces for any endomorphism A in this tensor-generated category are Tr(g_tilde A), Tr(g_tilde^(-1) A). (5) They agree, not only on one complete simple module. Here is an elementary proof that also specifies what is not specialized at the root. For real q>0, q!=1, use the involution K*=K, E*=KF, F*=EK^(-1). It is compatible with the actual coproducts Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. On V_L give consecutive basis vectors positive squared norms n_0=1, n_i=[i]_q[L-i+1]_q q^(-L+2i)n_(i-1). These make precisely E*=KF; the remaining adjoint identities follow. Tensor-product norms give finite-dimensional unitary representations. Duals are unitarizable as well: the regular generic J identifies the dual of V_L with the corresponding V_L, and the transported positive norm gives the same adjoint relations. Reversed tensor products of these duals therefore remain in the same finite unitary category. Every invariant subspace has invariant orthogonal complement, since the adjoints of the generators remain in the represented algebra. For completeness, every irreducible summand is V_L with L a nonnegative integer. Choose a highest-weight vector of weight L; the commutation relations give E F^i v=[i]_q[L-i+1]_q F^(i-1)v. If r is the first zero F^r v, then [r]_q[L-r+1]_q=0. For real q>0 this forces r=L+1. The preceding ladder has distinct weights and spans the irreducible summand. Thus an arbitrary intertwiner on a tensor-generated object has blocks A=direct_sum_L (I_(V_L) tensor A_L). On such a block, both traces in (5) equal (-1)^L [L+1]_q Tr(A_L), because the weights L,L-2,...,-L are symmetric. Summing proves (5) for every endomorphism, including non-scalar multiplicity blocks. The original matrix entries and any specified generic endomorphism are rational in q^(1/2), with fixed complex coefficients. Identity on an interval of positive real q therefore proves the generic rational identity. This is sphericality for the category and maps actually used. Only the original regular finite matrices are later specialized at q_N. Neither the irreducible decomposition nor its projections are specialized; they may be singular there. In particular this proof discards no root nilpotent or Jordan datum. ## 4. Rerouting with all coupon disks and frames fixed Regard the original source as a ribbon graph on the oriented sphere, with each actual box contained in a small parametrized closed disk. These disks include every retained crossing, its local ordered inputs and outputs and its blackboard ribbon framing. They are kept fixed pointwise throughout the following construction. Choose a point p in face a outside the disks. A path from p to the old point at infinity can be chosen outside all coupon disks and transverse to finitely many MAIN arcs, missing their endpoints. A smooth vector field in a thin neighborhood of this path moves p to the old point at infinity, while fixing every coupon disk. Its time maps are orientation-preserving sphere diffeomorphisms. The image graph misses the new infinity because p was not on the graph. Thus it gives a plane presentation with a as its exterior face and the SAME ordered local coupon frames. No crossing is created; the ribbon framing is transported inside the sphere, with no normal twist. Only MAIN arcs are crossed: the disjoint coupon disks contain the matching edges, and their complement in the sphere is connected. The selected edge is incident to this unbounded face. Take a short subarc of it and a simple path through that face to a region above all coupon disks and the rest of the compact drawing. A thin rectangular neighborhood of the path is disjoint from the graph except at the chosen subarc. Push that subarc along the rectangle, leaving two parallel sides joined by a semicircular tip. This is an ordinary planar finger isotopy of an arc, not a new cup/cap component or a crossing. Its tip is an exposed top cap. Outside it is a; inside it is the same face b, extended along the thin strip. The coupon disks stay fixed. A small perturbation of the remaining arcs makes the presentation Morse. It need not be a flat plat. These operations have a finite tensor description. Away from passages of the outside point across a MAIN arc, ordinary planar isotopy is generated by tensor interchange and the four actual snake identities; their J and g_tilde factors cancel exactly. When the outside point passes a MAIN arc, the two plane readings close the same correctly bent endomorphism by its two pivotal traces. Equation (5) makes them equal. The cut boundary is transported by these turns, not assigned a new matrix in its old internal basis. This proves that the rerouted generic CLOSED scalar is the original one. All R/Cartan factors remain inside the fixed coupon disks. Leave the exposed cap open. The remaining network is a Hopf map to V_d tensor V_d^* or its reversed order. Under the actual cup/duality it is an endomorphism of V_d (or its dual). Generically it is a scalar a_(a,b)(q)I: distinct K weights force a commuting endomorphism to be diagonal, and the nonzero F arrows force equal diagonal entries. This scalar is regular at q_N, being one entry of a regular open network after the regular cup identification. Closing it with the corresponding ordinary cap gives Z_closed(q)=(-1)^d[N]_q a_(a,b)(q). (6) The same generic closed scalar is obtained with any original top cap left open, and its dimension factor is the same. Since [N]_q!=0 generically, their regular open scalars agree. They agree at q_N by specialization. No root quantum dimension is divided by zero. For a right cap use the original reduced defect g_tilde^(-1)e; for a left cap use g_tilde e, where Tr(e)=1 in the actual boundary basis. Their marked evaluations of the scalar open map are both a_(a,b)(q). At q_N these are the actual root turns/marks by (3). Therefore the rerouted marked scalar equals the old top-cap-marked scalar exactly. There is no further root sign to insert: the auxiliary pivot already matches g. In the original flat presentation it reproduces the old standard-K conversion factor (-1)^(d(k-1)) automatically. ## 5. Exact ordered root turns in the new Morse presentation The whole face compiler can now be repeated; it is not inferred from the old flat-gap sweep. Put x0=q_N^d and Q=q_N^2. The original balanced left/right matrices are ev_L(a,b)=x0^a/N delta_(a+b,d), coev_L(b,a)=N x0^(-a) delta_(a+b,d), ev_R(b,a)=x0^a g_b/N delta_(a+b,d), coev_R(a,b)=N x0^(-a)g_b^(-1) delta_(a+b,d), g_b=q_N^(-d^2-2b). In their literal left-to-right ordered physical pair (i,j), ALL four are exactly cup(i,j)=N q_N^(-d^2+di) delta_(i+j,d), cap(i,j)=N^(-1) q_N^(di) delta_(i+j,d). (7) For the right cap the ratio to (7) is q_N^(-2Ni)=1; for the right cup it is q_N^(2N(d-i))=1. No local logarithmic lift is reset. The two marked arrays are genuinely different off support: mark_R(i,j)=x0^j/N^2, mark_L(i,j)=x0^i g_(d-i)/N^2. (8) Each contracts to one with its corresponding original cup. With one cap exposed, global unwrapped degree conservation forces i+j=d: all boxes preserve total head degree, each cup supplies d and every other cap consumes d. On this forced support the two arrays (8) both equal N^(-2)q_N^(dj). This is not an early restriction of the mark. ## 6. Winding gives the unchanged P and exactly the two missing targets At each fixed box the existing full homogeneous matrix adapter remains matrix_e=N^(-1) H_e(x,b,c,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (9) Its local ordered frame was never changed. In the centered face lift, a physical head along a vertical segment is i=d/2+N(Log L_left-Log L_right)/(2pi i). At a cup or cap the first head sees the outside face o and inside z, so q_N^(di)=q_N^(d^2/2)(L_o/L_z)^(d/2). Let M_f count the original input/output middle incidences in face f. Let T_f count +1 for the outside of every ordinary physical turn and -1 for its inside, including the cap to be marked at this stage. In this GENERAL Morse presentation one has M_f-T_f=2 for f!=a, M_a-T_a=-2. (10) Here is the turning proof. Traverse each face boundary with the face on its left, rounding repeated boundary passages by a thin regular neighborhood when necessary. Inside a fixed box, take the same local planar resolution as the original input/output matching pair. Its net boundary turn is +pi at each middle face and zero at each outer face: the two middle passages reverse the vertical tangent, while each outer passage continues it. Along a Morse arc, an inside U-turn contributes +pi and its outside passage -pi. All remaining arc segments have zero net turn after a vertical-tangent deformation; this can equally be read as the signed crossing count of the horizontal tangent direction. Thus total boundary turn is pi(M_f-T_f). The bounded-face boundary has winding +1, and the exterior boundary winding -1. This proves (10), including repeated face labels by counting each occurrence. It does not require every turn to lie above or below every coupon. Multiplying (7),(9), the ordinary face character is therefore product_f L_f^((d/2)(T_f-M_f)) =L_a^d product_(f!=a)L_f^(-d). (11) At the exposed marked cap the original second head gives mark/cap=N^(-1)(L_b/L_a)^d. (12) Both a,b characters cancel; every other face has exponent -d. If the new Morse presentation has k' cups, it also has k' caps. The turn constants are N^(k')N^(-(k'-1))N^(-2)=N^(-1). Their q_N^(d^2/2) head constants cancel the k' cup constants q_N^(-d^2), exactly. The whole literal marked summand is consequently N^(-R-1) P(L)/product_(f!=a,b)L_f^d. (13) All half powers have assembled into integer face exponents. This establishes the coefficient CHARACTER with the same polynomial P, not a rotated, smoothed or independently renormalized local coupon. ## 7. Primitive grids, actual support and the unique alias Adding degree-two bends changes neither the closed graph's cycle lattice nor its dimension. Centering a head by d/2 turns the support i+j=d at a bend into a sign reversal. At a fixed box, unwrapped total conservation gives the actual divergence equation. Hence the integral homogeneous source lattice is still the divergence-free lattice of the same connected graph. On a sphere it is integrally isomorphic to face-potential differences modulo one common constant: integrate an integer flow along dual paths; its sum around a dual face is precisely the original vertex divergence, and every closed dual walk is generated by these face boundaries. No finite-index Jacobian is introduced. There are R+2 white faces, so fixing L_a=1 leaves R+1 independent N-point grids. At odd N the centered heads have integral offsets and the grids are L_f=Q^(p_f). At even N use the original cocycle whose value is one on MAIN edges and zero on MATCHING edges. Each shaded triangle has two MAIN edges, so it integrates to face parities t_f; set t_a=0 and take L_f=q_N^(t_f)Q^(p_f), p_f in Z/N. (14) In particular t_b=1. These are the same actual half-index offsets in the rerouted frame, not new independent choices of local carries. Every grid point gives canonical physical heads in {0,...,d}. First apply the established canonical physical support of the full-polynomial adapter (9), including its original endpoint zeros; it kills any failure of unwrapped conservation. At a turn the congruence i+j=d modulo N already implies i+j=d in this physical range. Conversely a supported physical state determines one grid point by the primitive face-potential construction. Thus summing (13) over the N^(R+1) grid points is exactly the original finite source. For supported states, changing integrated face-log lifts coherently by 2pi i leaves the entire summand unchanged, since its final face exponents are integral. These coherent face changes induce the actual closed integral head-flow changes. Arbitrary independent single-head resets are not justified: recorded local carries cancel globally only after physical support and coherent face integration are established. Let a monomial of P have nonnegative degrees n_f and total dR. Its grid average can survive only if n_b=0 modulo N, n_f=d modulo N for f!=a,b. The latter degrees are at least d. There are R of them, so their minimum already exhausts dR. Consequently the only alias is n_a=n_b=0, n_f=d for f!=a,b. (15) The even coset phase is one at (15). The normalized grid average in (13) is therefore exactly (1), with no additional N factor. Together with section 4's equality of actual reduced scalars, this proves the statement. ## 8. What this changes, and what it does not The permitted marking is an actual cut exposed after the described rerouting. It carries the original cup/dual boundary transport and the auxiliary pivot specializes exactly to the original root pivot. It is not an identity obtained by moving the old nonintertwining D through the interior coupons or by replacing it with the same matrix on another old head. That incorrect operation already fails in a direct finite internal-head test; that separate operation is not used anywhere in this proof. The equality is for the full polynomial source and hence for any common linear spectral/Fourier functional applied to it, with the same retained twists and exterior framing scalar. A successful full-source certificate at any such MAIN edge would therefore suffice for the original marked scalar, provided all hypotheses of that certificate have independently been checked in that marked geometry. No universally successful mark, sectorwise transport, equality of envelope capacities, or general strictly-overloaded source bound is inferred. In particular the existing flat-plat certificate theorems may use their original top-cap position, gap forest, or specific Morse sweep. Those hypotheses have not been rechecked for every rerouted presentation here. The finite equality does not itself extend those certificate theorems to arbitrary MAIN marks. No generic-q ADO derivative, root semisimplicity, scalar orthogonality, or low-demand cap/CROSS inequality is part of this proof. Only the auxiliary generic finite tensor identities are continued to the root. ## 9. Source dependencies and internal verification The exact inputs are the [original top-cap transport proof](research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.md), [literal duality and snakes](relative_pivotal_duality.md), [all four balanced turns and the original mark](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), [full homogeneous polynomial adapter](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), [original face-character and grid theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md), and [primitive integral face-potential lattice](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md). The full fixed-coupon sphere rerouting is written in section 4; it does not require an unrecorded planar-frame transformation. The [focused audit](../experiments/research_audit_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport.py) and its [results](../experiments/research_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport_results.json) construct the original physical coproduct matrices, full divided-polynomial numerators and actual positive/negative crossings, including their Cartan scalars. They contract the old physical top mark independently of the homogeneous calculation, then compare every actual MAIN-pair two-zero coefficient. The exact fixtures comprise 20 sources, 160 MAIN-pair coefficients, 19 nonzero sources, and 10 cases at each level parity. They use widths two and three, with both full numerators and arbitrary polynomial coupons. Field agreement and conservative integer-overflow bounds are explicit. No optimization, projected-sector identity, numerical asymptotic, or geometric certificate is inferred from these finite checks. The general identity is proved in sections 2--7.

title: Original one-cap pressure: global real continuation and an algebraic boundary response
text: # Original one-cap pressure: global real continuation and an algebraic boundary response 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. The original source boundary curve has an atom-free, log-algebraic pressure-root density and an exact selected logarithmic period equal to the original **drilled** hyperbolic volume. No filled quantum limit or ordinary knot A-polynomial identification is asserted. The original simple matched sphere, protected MAIN edge uv and cap F=(u,A,v,C) remain fixed. Every other original port is CROSS. Assume a strict finite positive one-cap stationary exterior, with all ordinary incidences positive, L_A=L_C and 0<nu<1/2. The [one-cap geometric double](research_one_cap_geometric_double.md) gives the stronger nu>1/4, but that stronger inequality is not needed below. Work on the ODD-level original binary polynomial P_N(A,C), with every other ordinary face extracted to its original demand d=N-1. Inputs are the local complex pressure theorem, its root-measure reconstruction, the original half-triangle potential and compact flow duality. No signed coefficient lower asymptotic is assumed. This note does not prove chi_D >= M_cap-Phi_D. ## 1. The positive-real gluing branch exists for every finite boundary ratio Put A=exp(z), C=1; let I be the other ordinary faces, with weights exp(w_i). For the original exterior triangles define \[ \mathcal F(z,w)=\sum_tQ_t(L)-\sum_{i\in I}w_i.\tag{1} \] Each supported half-triangle has supply 1/2. Its entropy is continuous and bounded on its closed supported simplex; its weighted potential is the maximum of entropy plus its load/log-weight pairing. On positive weights Q_t is real analytic. A pure supported corner contributes a linear term and no Hessian; every other supported triangle has Hessian kernel precisely common scaling of its supported coordinates. The graph joining ordinary vertices that share an exterior triangle is connected. Deleting the cap triangles removes only the ordinary edge AC from those triangles, and the triangle on the other side of AC remains in the exterior. Thus no edge of the connected ordinary graph is lost. The grounded Hessian in the I variables is positive definite at EVERY finite positive weight assignment, not only at z=0. Here is the required global coercivity. Extend a vector v in R^I by v_A=v_C=0. Write alpha^0 for the actual strict exterior allocation at the given stationary point. Its I demands are one. The recession function in the extracted directions is \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{rec}(v) &=\sum_t\frac12\max_{f\in\operatorname{supp}t}v_f-\sum_{i\in I}v_i\\ &=\sum_t\left[\frac12\max_{f\in\operatorname{supp}t}v_f -\sum_{f\in\operatorname{supp}t}\alpha^0_{t,f}v_f\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{2} \] Every summand is nonnegative. Equality requires all supported v_f in each nonmonomial triangle to be equal, since all its supported alpha^0 are strictly positive. Connectedness and the two fixed anchors force v=0. Hence rec(v)>=c||v|| for some c>0, by compactness of the unit sphere. The pure-vertex choices in each local potential give \[ \mathcal F(z,w)\ge c\lVert w\rVert-C(1+|z|).\tag{3} \] uniformly for z in compact real intervals. This also covers the empty I case with its empty minimization convention. Entropy boundedness is enough here; no global coefficient asymptotic is being invoked. Consequently (1) has one finite minimizer w(z) for every real z. Its grounded Hessian is invertible, so the implicit-function theorem makes w(z) and \[ F_{\mathrm{cl}}(z)=\min_w\mathcal F(z,w).\tag{4} \] real analytic on the WHOLE real line. This is actual positive gluing with the original I demands. It is not an assertion that its planar developing map remains embedded for all z. Let mu_D be the probability measure reconstructed from the local pressure germ in [the original pressure/root-measure theorem](research_cap_root_measure_from_classical_pressure.md). The function \[ F_\mu(z)=M_{\mathrm{cap}}+\int_{[0,1]} \log(1-p+pe^z)\,d\mu_D(p).\tag{5} \] is real analytic on all R (locally the denominator is uniformly away from zero). The local theorem says F_cl=F_mu near zero. The identity theorem for real analytic functions therefore gives \[ F_{\mathrm{cl}}(z)=F_\mu(z)\qquad(z\in\mathbb R).\tag{6} \] This continuation uses coercivity and the finite positive gluing system, not a remote every-degree coefficient limit or an assumed global complex saddle. ## 2. The exact residual interval is [0,1] Let R(s) retain precisely the original residual targets A:s, C:1-s, all I demands one and both protected demands zero. Its full feasible interval is [0,1]. To see the endpoint assertion, multiply the transportation problem by two: each exterior triangle supplies one, each I face demands two, and A,C together demand two. This is an ordinary bipartite network-flow polytope with integral supplies and demands (one may route both A,C into a common final sink). Integral vertices attain the linear minimum and maximum of the A load. In the original normalization these two extrema lie in {0,1/2,1}. The strict cap exterior realizes s=nu<1/2. The original complete packing realizes a residual s>1/2: the restored cap's uAC triangle has A load alpha_A in (0,1/2), so its exterior A demand is 1-alpha_A in (1/2,1). Thus the two extrema are 0 and 1. Convexity supplies every intervening value. This uses the literal half-supply network and the original complete packing, not a new mark or source. Compact concave duality now gives, including both endpoints, \[ \begin{aligned} F_{\mathrm{cl}}(z)&=\max_{0\le s\le1}\{R(s)+sz\},\\ R(s)&=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R}\{F_{\mathrm{cl}}(z)-sz\}. \end{aligned}\tag{7} \] The second formula follows also by closed concave biconjugacy; R is upper semicontinuous and concave on its compact feasible interval. In particular R(s)=M_cap-I_mu(s), where I_mu is the Legendre transform of the normalized integral in (5). The limiting derivatives of (7) as z tends to minus/plus infinity are 0 and 1. Differentiating (5) and using dominated convergence gives \[ \begin{aligned} \mu_D(\{1\})&=\lim_{z\to-\infty}F_{\mathrm{cl}}'(z)=0,\\ 1-\mu_D(\{0\})&=\lim_{z\to+\infty}F_{\mathrm{cl}}'(z)=1. \end{aligned}\tag{8} \] Thus neither endpoint carries a root atom. This is stronger than merely knowing the stationary mean nu or the finite polynomial's nonzero endpoint coefficients. ## 3. The selected circle-star equations give an algebraic boundary phase Write w=exp(z)>0 and m_D(w)=F_cl'(log w). For each nonmonomial exterior triangle t on supported positive weights a,b,c put \[ \begin{gathered} T_t^2=ab+ac+bc,\qquad T_t>0,\\ Z_{t,f}=\frac{T_t+iL_f}{T_t-iL_f} =\exp(2\pi i\alpha_{t,f}). \end{gathered}\tag{9} \] The same formula applies with exactly two positive weights. A pure supported corner has alpha=1/2 and is represented separately by the constant factor -1; a zero corner contributes 1. No zero T is divided out. The exact extracted-face equations are \[ \prod_{t\ni f}Z_{t,f}=1\qquad(f\in I).\tag{10} \] The branch is specified by the original load equations sum_t alpha=1, the positive T_t, and the actual stationary weights at w=1. The algebraic equations alone need not specify those integer lifts. After denominators are cleared, (9)-(10), L_A=w, L_C=1 form a finite polynomial system with Gaussian-rational coefficients. The Jacobian in the extracted log weights of (10) is a nonzero diagonal factor times the grounded Hessian. The nonmonomial T equations have nonzero T derivatives. Hence the selected branch is a regular algebraic curve over the w line. Its weight coordinates and its boundary product \[ B_D(w)=\prod_{t\ni A}Z_{t,A} =\exp(2\pi i m_D(w)).\tag{11} \] are algebraic functions of w. Equivalently there is a nonzero source-boundary eliminant \[ \mathcal A_D(w,B_D(w))=0.\tag{12} \] It may be obtained by saturating by the nonzero denominators and Jacobian and selecting the regular component carrying the positive branch. Eliminating a higher-dimensional extraneous component without this selection is not the asserted construction. Gaussian-rational polynomial equations suffice; taking Galois conjugates if needed gives an eliminant over their ground field. This is an algebraic boundary ANGLE response of the original source disk. It is NOT identified here with the ordinary knot A-polynomial, nor with a primitive meridian/longitude pair of the drilled group. That additional peripheral dictionary has not been proved. The phase B alone forgets an integer; the actual lift m is fixed by its positive continuation and the endpoint values 0 and 1 from (8). ## 4. The root measure is absolutely continuous with a log-algebraic density Push mu_D forward by r=(1-p)/p to a probability measure sigma_D on (0,infty); (8) removes the endpoint masses. For w off the negative real axis the pressure derivative has the actual Stieltjes form \[ m_D(w)=\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{w}{w+r}\,d\sigma_D(r).\tag{13} \] This holomorphic function continues the positive-real m from (11). For Im w>0 it has strictly positive imaginary part, since Im[w/(w+r)]=r Im(w)/|w+r|^2. Thus \[ B_D(w)=\exp(2\pi i m_D(w)),\qquad 0<|B_D(w)|<1.\tag{14} \] in the upper half-plane. The algebraic relation (12), valid near the positive axis, holds throughout that half-plane by holomorphic continuation. It fixes one selected algebraic branch there. On the positive axis |B|=1; the reflected branch obeys B(conj w)=1/conj(B(w)). No branch is reset on the negative axis. There can be no atom at any finite r0>0. If an atom has mass a>0, then at w=-r0+i y, y>0, \[ \operatorname{Im}m_D(-r_0+iy)\ge\frac{ar_0}{y},\qquad |B_D(-r_0+iy)|\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{2\pi ar_0}{y}\right).\tag{15} \] A nonzero algebraic branch near a finite point has a Puiseux leading term c(w+r0)^beta and hence a power-law lower bound along this ray. It cannot satisfy (15). This contradiction excludes every interior atom, without assuming any smooth limiting density in advance. Away from a finite set of algebraic branch, zero and pole points on the negative axis, the upper branch B is analytic and nonzero in a neighborhood. There one can choose Log B and write m=Log B/(2pi i)+an integer, with the SAME continued integer lift. Stieltjes inversion applied to m(w)/w gives the real-analytic density \[ \frac{d\sigma_D(r)}{dr} =\frac{\operatorname{Im}m_D(-r+i0)}{\pi r} =-\frac{\log|B_D(-r+i0)|}{2\pi^2r}.\tag{16} \] Explicitly, -Im[m(x+i y)/(x+i y)]/pi is the convolution of sigma_D with y/[pi((x+r)^2+y^2)]. Integrate it over a compact negative interval and let y decrease to0. The elementary Poisson approximate-identity limit gives that interval's measure; the analytic boundary values there give exactly (16). Endpoint atoms have already been excluded. There is no singular continuous part: outside that finite set the measure has (16), while a measure supported on the remaining finite set is atomic and has already been excluded. Returning to p yields \[ \frac{d\mu_D(p)}{dp} =-\frac{\log\left|B_D\!\left(-\frac{1-p}{p}+i0\right)\right|} {2\pi^2p(1-p)},\qquad 0<p<1.\tag{17} \] The density is nonnegative, integrates to one, and is piecewise real analytic. At an interior exceptional point it has at worst a logarithmic singularity: a Puiseux zero of B becomes a multiple of log|r-r0| in (16). A boundary pole is incompatible with (14). For completeness, at r=0 and infinity, (8) gives m->0 and m->1, respectively, so B tends to the nonzero value1. Its nonconstant algebraic Puiseux expansion gives m=O(w^a) at0 and m-1=O(w^-b) at infinity for some a,b>0 on the selected branches. Consequently the endpoint density bounds are O(p^(b-1)) and O((1-p)^(a-1)). In particular both logarithmic endpoint moments are finite. These assertions concern the actual fixed disk; they give no uniform exponent over varying diagrams. ## 5. The same algebraic branch determines the exact missing comparison Let f_D(w)=int log(1-p+p w) dmu_D(p), continued from positive w. Then f_D(1)=0, and on the slit plane \[ df_D=m_D(w)\frac{dw}{w} =\left[\frac{\operatorname{Log}B_D(w)}{2\pi i} +\text{the retained integer}\right]\frac{dw}{w}.\tag{18} \] Thus the original pressure difference is a logarithmic integral on the selected algebraic boundary curve. Its normalization is fixed at w=1, not by an arbitrary integration constant. Calling (18) the volume of a knot representation would need a separate group and relative-chain proof. Put q(z)=Q(0,exp(z),1). Its original normalization is \[ \begin{gathered} q(z)=\frac2\pi\operatorname{Ti}_2(e^{z/2}),\qquad q'(z)=\frac{\arctan(e^{z/2})}{\pi},\\ \operatorname{Ti}_2(x)=\int_0^x\frac{\arctan t}{t}\,dt. \end{gathered}\tag{19} \] Restoring the two original cap triangles and their two target logs gives the exact full-capacity formula \[ \Phi_D-M_{\mathrm{cap}} =\inf_{z\in\mathbb R}\{f_D(e^z)+q(z)-z\}.\tag{20} \] It is equivalent to the original R(s)+2f(s-1/2) formula, by (7), and does not replace either face target. There is an exact algebraic critical-point and absolute-value statement here, beyond an unspecified minimization. Put \[ B_{\mathrm{cap}}(w)=\frac{1+i\sqrt w}{1-i\sqrt w},\qquad a_{\mathrm{cap}}(w)=\frac{\arctan\sqrt w}{\pi}.\tag{20a} \] The derivative of the potential in (20) with respect to log w is m_D(w)+a_cap(w)-1. It is strictly increasing: the first derivative has positive Bernoulli variance and the cap derivative is strictly positive. Its limits are -1 and 1/2 by (8). Therefore there is exactly one positive critical point w_*, and w_*>1 because m_D(1)+a_cap(1)-1=nu-3/4<0. At this point \[ B_D(w_*)B_{\mathrm{cap}}(w_*)=1,\qquad m_D(w_*)+a_{\mathrm{cap}}(w_*)=1.\tag{20b} \] The second equality is the retained lift: the sum lies in (0,3/2) for positive w, so the only possible integer at a solution is1. The selected positive solution is algebraic, since (12),(20a) are algebraic and the critical point is isolated (the derivative is strictly positive). Its finite exterior weights restore the original complete A and C demands; every other original demand was already imposed. Thus it is the original complete circle packing. With C0=q(0)=2G/pi, where q's argument here is the log weight z and G is Catalan's constant, the exact relative logarithmic period is \[ \Phi_D=M_{\mathrm{cap}}+C_0 +\int_1^{w_*}\bigl[m_D(w)+a_{\mathrm{cap}}(w)-1\bigr]\frac{dw}{w}. \tag{20c} \] Equivalently the integrand is Log_lift(B_D B_cap)/(2pi i), with lift 2pi i[m_D+a_cap-1], not independently reset principal logarithms. The value is the original drilled hyperbolic volume divided by2pi by the already proved complete packing/capacity theorem. This is an absolute geometric consequence of that theorem and the specified constant M_cap+C0; it does not require a new representation-volume identification of (18), identify a knot A-polynomial, or prove a filled quantum limit. For r>0 let U(r)=Re f_D(-r+i0). The finite original two negative-axis suprema correspond, in precisely the degree-one normalization, to \[ -\chi_D=\sup_{r>0}\{U(r)-\max(0,\log r)\}.\tag{21} \] with the continuous limiting values at r=0,infinity included. The endpoint power and interior logarithmic bounds after (17) justify these finite limits; the original supremum-rate theorem already handles them without needing this additional regularity. Equations (18)-(21) put the proposed universal comparison on ONE selected, source-normalized algebraic boundary branch: \[ \sup_{r>0}\{\operatorname{Re}f_D(-r+i0)-\log_+r\} \le\inf_{z\in\mathbb R}\{f_D(e^z)+q(z)-z\}.\tag{22} \] This note does not prove (22). It proves that the previously arbitrary root measure is constrained by the actual finite circle-star system, has no atoms, and is reconstructed by (17). The known one-cap original chain only bounds the right-hand deficit by W(nu)/pi minus its fixed peripheral gap. It does not identify the logarithmic curve integral on the left with that representation volume or pay that deficit. In particular no global embedding of the positive exterior for all real z, no analytic continuation of an individual complex saddle through every branch point, no knot A-polynomial identification, and no signed original coefficient lower rate is used or asserted. ## Inputs The [original effective-response theorem](research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md), sections 1–3, supplies the local complex pressure germ and the grounded ordinary graph. The [pressure/root-measure theorem](research_cap_root_measure_from_classical_pressure.md), sections 1–2 and 6, supplies the same original odd-level measure and the exact negative-axis supremum rates. The [constrained cap capacity](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md), sections 1–2, retains the original targets and compact concave duality. The [triangle entropy theorem](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) fixes the half-supply normalization and local Legendre potentials. The [complete packing capacity](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) identifies the selected complete value with the original drilled volume. The [one-cap original chain budget](research_one_cap_original_chain_volume_budget.md) supplies the still separate geometric upper bound discussed after (22). Preservation changes mathematical formatting and supplies durable links. No numerical audit, signed coefficient lower asymptotic, arbitrary complex saddle continuation, knot A-polynomial identification, or general filled volume theorem is claimed. Inequality (22) remains open.

title: Absolute cap-star comparison: exact constrained capacity and its missing budget
text:
# Absolute cap-star comparison: exact constrained capacity and its missing budget 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. The original ordinary targets are one, the original protected MAIN pair is u,v, and Phi_D is the complete capacity in the original normalization Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). No general absolute cap bound is asserted. The main conclusions are exact variational reductions. They explain why the leaf and spectral-star results do not yet prove an absolute cap-only gap. Section 5 gives a literal obstruction to the stronger inference from LOCAL star hypotheses alone; it is explicitly not a common-stationary counterexample. ## 1. The exact one-cap residual capacity Name one original cap F=(u,A,v,C), with triangles uAC,uvC and matching edge uC. Its original cap degrees are q_A=1-s,q_C=s, with 0<=s<=1/2; u,v remain zero. Every OTHER port in this section is CROSS. Delete only F. Let R(s) be the maximum remaining complete-triangle entropy with residual targets \[ r_A=s,\qquad r_C=1-s,\qquad r_f=1\ (f	ext{ other ordinary}),\qquad r_u=r_v=0.	ag{1} \] Put R(s)=-infinity when this fiber is empty. On its compact effective domain R is concave and upper semicontinuous, by the compact concave triangle-flow problem. The exact original cap-sector maximum is \[ M_{\mathrm{cap}}=\max_{0\le s\le1/2}R(s).	ag{2} \] The original complete capacity has a different interval and a local entropy term. In the complete row F, its first triangle has loads (0,t,1/2-t) and its second is the pure-C half-row. Hence q_A=t, q_C=1-t, 0<=t<=1/2, and its entropy is 2f(t). Restoring its original targets in (1) therefore gives \[ \Phi_D=\max_{1/2\le s\le1}\{R(s)+2f(s-	frac12)\}.	ag{3} \] We used f(1-s)=f(s-1/2) on this interval. There is no change of mark, vertex, source pairing or target in (2)-(3). In particular concavity of R alone does not compare these two maxima: they use opposite halves of its effective domain. No reflection symmetry R(s)=R(1-s) is known for an arbitrary prescribed exterior. At an actual finite-common-weight cap-only stationary point with 0<nu<1/2, the cap equation is L_A=L_C. The remaining CROSS allocations attain their local triangle Legendre formulas at these SAME weights. For every feasible s', their dual affine upper differs from its value at nu by (s'-nu)log(L_C/L_A)=0. Consequently \[ R(
u)=\max_{0\le s\le1}R(s)=M_{\mathrm{cap}}.	ag{4} \] This needs neither differentiability of R nor a separate local maximality assumption for a Green row: all remaining rows are complete concave triangle rows. It does not assert existence of such a stationary point, and does not classify arbitrary boundary maxima of the cap-restricted sector. ## 2. The cap-forest quotient preserves every target exactly Now allow the at most two residual caps of classified positive-value data. Their ordinary incidence edges form a forest, as proved in [the cap-component theorem](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md), section 2. Let p be the number of caps, and relax EACH cap row from its prescribed overloaded orientation to ANY nonnegative split of unit supply between its two ordinary vertices. Its entropy is still zero. All other ports remain CROSS. Call this relaxed maximum M_rel. For a tree component with n vertices and n-1 cap edges, deleting those edges leaves total residual target n-(n-1)=1. Every nonnegative residual vector (r_a) on that component with sum r_a=1 is realizable by the relaxed cap rows. To see this, first let r be concentrated at one root. Give each edge's full unit to the vertex farther from that root; every nonroot vertex receives one and the root receives zero. Take the convex combination of these allocations with coefficients r_a. The restored cap load at vertex a is exactly 1-r_a. Thus deleting the relaxed cap rows and merging each component is an EXACT identification of the classical flow problem. Every merged target is one; unmerged ordinary targets remain one; protected targets remain zero. This is a flow quotient only, not a triangulated-sphere edge contraction or an identity coupon. The true cap orientations impose additional inequalities and are NOT silently discarded from the definition of M_cap. Write the original complete weighted potential as \[  egin{aligned} F_D(L)&=\sum_{t	ext{ original triangle}}Q_t(L)-\sum_{a	ext{ ordinary}}\log L_a,\ \Phi_D&=\inf_{L>0}F_D(L),\qquad C_0=2f(	frac14)= rac{v_{\mathrm{oct}}}{2\pi}. \end{aligned}	ag{5} \] Let E_cap be the linear subspace of log weights constant on every cap-tree component. Each cap's two ordinary weights then equal a common B, and its COMPLETE weighted value is exactly \[ Q(0,B,B)+Q(0,0,B)=C_0+\log B.	ag{6} \] In a component with n vertices and n-1 caps, the n target logs and n-1 cap logs leave exactly one target log. Compact concave duality for the remaining CROSS rows therefore gives the exact relaxed identity \[  egin{aligned} M_{\mathrm{rel}}&=\inf_{\log L\in E_{\mathrm{cap}}}F_D(L)-pC_0 =\Phi_D+\Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}-pC_0,\ \Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}&:=\inf_{\log L\in E_{\mathrm{cap}}}F_D(L)-\Phi_D\ge0. \end{aligned}	ag{7} \] The relaxed fiber is nonempty: start with an original feasible complete flow, remove the cap rows, and merge their components. Each cap has unit ordinary supply, so the same component totals are one. This also verifies the normalization in (7). Compact hypograph separation proves the dual equality even if a boundary multiplier is not attained. For the actual closed cap sector one only has M_cap<=M_rel. However, at classified cap-only stationary data with all cap splits strict and finite common ordinary weights, equality DOES hold. The cap equations place these weights in E_cap, the complete rows attain Q, and the original demands cancel all logarithms. The actual feasible flow attains the dual value in (7), hence \[ M_{\mathrm{cap}}=M_{\mathrm{rel}}=\Phi_D+\Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}-pC_0.	ag{8} \] This is an exact identification of the classical stationary envelope, not a claim that Delta_cap<=p C0. The latter inequality is the missing unsigned absolute comparison in this formulation. ## 3. What the new leaf/star mechanism proves, and what it still needs If there are no Green ports, a nontrivial maximal-weight cap component has a nonroot leaf whose other incident ports are all CROSS. The star theorem therefore applies at ANY cap-child valence, with 0<nu<1/2 from the original demand. This removes the earlier degree-two limitation for a RELATIVE star improvement. At the common stationary weights in (8), its weighted block envelope touches the original sharp block action. Indeed the CROSS neighbors supply nu to the internal A face, while the cap supplies nu to boundary C. Their log-weight discrepancy is nu(log L_A-log L_C)=0. With the unchanged exterior included, the full weighted envelope is precisely the value in (8), not an unrelated independently optimized number. The star theorem gives some eta>0 below that envelope. Other cap rows at their equal ordinary weights have polynomial weighted size at +2, and only an arbitrarily small extra exponential cost on a sufficiently small complex +2 disk. Other CROSS rows have the global-real coefficientwise endpoint majorant and its thin-strip continuation. Thus, when using these common stationary weights and retaining the whole internal A^d contraction, the relevant source bound has rate at most \[ \Phi_D+\Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}-pC_0-\eta.	ag{9} \] after reducing eta to absorb those small strip costs. Shared boundary variables and original ordinary targets are retained by the ONE final Cauchy extraction. A second cap does not involve this leaf A, so it belongs legitimately to the unchanged exterior. Formula (9) is an absolute gap below Phi_D IF \[ \Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}-pC_0<\eta.	ag{10} \] In particular the nonstrict variational inequality Delta_cap<=p C0 would suffice, because the star gives a strict positive eta. But no current theorem compares eta to Delta_cap-p C0 in general. The leaf mechanism alone therefore has NOT closed cap-only high maxima. For localizations around a stationary datum inside a larger source, one must use the genuine boundary coefficients of the contracted star and exterior-array fibers. Cutting individual internal cap indices would destroy the sum controlled by the theorem. The [original block-contraction theorem](research_original_block_contraction_and_cap_budget.md) gives that precise localization interface. These statements make no claim about a full filling period: an absolute fixed-strip gap on the entire relevant source complement is still required before the existing whole-period theorem applies. ## 4. The tempting exterior packing contact is not present Deleting F removes BOTH triangles uAC,uvC and their common MATCHING edge uC. The remaining positive CROSS disk has boundary u-A-C-v-u. It gives contacts uA,AC,Cv and the marked parallel-line edge uv. It does NOT give a contact uC. Consequently L_A=L_C does not force A to touch v by copying C's radius: the assertion that C already touches both lines has used a missing cap contact. There is a direct boundary-coordinate check. Suppose a positive exterior disk development has the prescribed boundary fan loads nu and 1-nu. Put theta=2pi nu, equal circle radius r, centers A=(0,0), C=(2r,0), and n=(cos theta,sin theta). Let the two lines be \[ u:\ n\cdot z=r,\qquad v:\ n\cdot z=2r\cos	heta-r.	ag{11} \] They are parallel; A touches u, C touches v, and A,C are tangent. The counterclockwise fan from the AC ray at A to its u ray has angle theta. At C the fan from its v ray to the CA ray has angle 2pi-theta. Thus the normalized exterior loads are exactly nu,1-nu. The line separation is \[ H=2r(1-\cos	heta)=4r\sin^2(\pi
u),	ag{12} \] not the extra-contact value 2r. For 1/4<nu<1/2 both entire disks fit between the two lines, and neither has the other line contact. Their distance to that other line is r-2r cos theta>r. At nu=1/4 the extra contacts first occur. This is a literal local boundary configuration, not a claim that every such boundary has an embedded finite interior CROSS packing, or that an arbitrary stationary disk develops injectively. It is enough to identify the missing step in the proposed immediate extra-contact contradiction. A global disk theorem could impose further restrictions; none is inferred here from the unfilled cap triangle. ## 5. A literal warning: local star hypotheses do not bound its exterior The following fixed matched sphere proves that LOCAL star hypotheses alone cannot bound the full weighted envelope by Phi_D. Start with the five-vertex simple sphere having ports \[ (u,A,v,C),\qquad(A,u,C,Z),\qquad(v,C,u,Z). \] Stellar-subdivide the last port's triangle vCZ by a new ordinary W, retaining its vZ pairing and pairing the other new triangles across CW. The resulting FOUR original ports are \[ F=(u,A,v,C),\quad E=(A,u,C,Z),\quad G'=(v,u,W,Z),\quad G''=(C,v,Z,W).	ag{13} \] Their eight triangles are uAC,uvC,uAZ,ACZ,uvZ,vWZ,vCW,CZW. Each edge is in two triangles, the sphere is simple, and the displayed paired edges uC,AZ,vZ,CW are distinct. Deleting them leaves a simple bipartite MAIN quadrangulation with four distinct vertices per port. The general Morse realization therefore supplies actual sources for this recorded incidence; no flat-plat word or knot equivalence is asserted. Mark the original MAIN pair u,v. Use F as cap, all other ports CROSS, and choose ordinary weights \[ L_A=L_C=1,\qquad L_Z=4,\qquad L_W=W>0. \] The entire A-star consists of E. Its endpoint A-load is exactly \[ 
u= rac1\pi\left(\arctan rac12+\arctan rac13ight)= rac14.	ag{14} \] The last equality uses the positive tangent-addition branch. In particular the local star hypotheses and its positive loss constants do NOT depend on W. Let X_E=Q(1,0,4)+Q(1,1,4), a fixed finite number. The original full weighted cap-only envelope, including every target, is \[ \mathcal E(W)=X_E-	frac12\log4+Q(0,W,4)+Q(1,0,W)+Q(1,4,W)-\log W. \] Each of the last three triangle potentials admits its pure-W half-load. Hence \[ \mathcal E(W)\ge	frac12\log W+X_E-	frac12\log4\longrightarrow+\infty.	ag{15} \] The actual complete capacity Phi_D of this fixed finite sphere is finite. Thus an arbitrarily large excess of this weighted envelope over Phi_D is compatible with all LOCAL star hypotheses and a fixed positive relative loss. The exterior is NOT stationary in this example. It is therefore NOT a counterexample to Delta_cap<=p C0, to the cap-only maximum inequality, or to the volume conjecture. At W tending to infinity its original W demand plainly fails the stationarity equation. The example only rules out promoting a local relative estimate to an absolute theorem without using the global demands/stationarity or a genuine positive reference comparison. Equations (1)-(10), rather than this warning, are the main reduced absolute problem. ## Dependencies The [whole CROSS-star spectral theorem](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md) supplies the genuine relative loss and fixed spectral neighborhoods. The [cap-component and stellar theorem](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md) supplies the forest and leaf selection, and the exact refinement used in section 5. The [full-fiber stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) supplies the original finite common weights and strict residual caps. The [triangle entropy normalization](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) and [complete-capacity duality](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) fix the constants and the compact concave optimization convention. The [matched-sphere Morse construction](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) supplies actual sources for (13); it does not identify them with another filled knot. The cap flow quotient in section 2 is classical only and does not change any quantum tensor. The explicit divergent-envelope example is nonstationary. It is not a counterexample at a stationary cap-only maximum. No numerical audit or scan is needed or claimed. There is no constructed bad common-stationary maximum, coefficient lower-rate assertion, new finite-source rewiring, or general prescribed-diagram volume theorem.

title: The original cap/CROSS signed contraction at every demand and both parities
text: # The original cap/CROSS signed contraction at every demand and both parities 31 October 2026. This theorem does not assert stability for nearby spectra or a whole-source/filling estimate. ## 1. Exact statement and comparison source Keep the original overlapping pair \(E=(A,0,C,Z)\), \(F=(0,A,0,C)\), with A internal to these ports and its unchanged demand \(A^d\), \(d=N-1\). Put raw E at \(-2\), raw F at \(+2\), and retain E's CROSS and F's RIGHT parts. Write \[ M=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1,\qquad H=\lfloor d/2\rfloor, \qquad J_n=\{\max(0,n-H),\ldots,\min(M,n)\}. \] Then \(M+H=N-2\), and the original signed coefficient, apart from its common raw sign \((-1)^d\), is \[ T_{N,n}=\sum_{j\in J_n}(-1)^jU_j C_{j,n-j}, \qquad0\le n\le N-2. \tag{1} \] All original unused factors, source turns, and remaining exponents \(C^nZ^{d-n}\) are retained. For explicit normalization, put \(\theta=\pi/N\), \[ c_r=2\cos((2r+1)\theta),\quad a_r=2+c_r,\quad \gamma_r=2-c_r,\quad s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\quad B_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r^2,\quad B_0=1, \qquad U_j=\frac{4B_j}{\prod_{r=0}^j\gamma_r}. \] The original continuant and unused suffix are \[ \begin{aligned} K_0&=1,\qquad K_1=s_1^2(A+Z),\\ K_r&=s_r^2(A+Z)K_{r-1} +s_rs_{r-1}a_{r-1}AZK_{r-2},\\ C_{j,h}&=[A^jZ^{d-h-j}]K_{d-h}(A,Z) \prod_{r=d-h+1}^{d}a_r. \end{aligned} \] Set C to zero outside \(0\le h\le d,0\le j\le d-h\). These are the full literal coefficients from [the original-demand source](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md), sections 1–2, extended before applying the cutoffs in (1). At odd levels \(a_{(N-1)/2}=0\) is retained, never divided out. At even N the positive comparator is \(D_{N,n}=\sum_{j\in J_n}V_jC_{j,n-j}\). At odd N it is \(D_{N,n}^o=\sum_{j\in J_n}V_j^o\overline C_{j,n-j}\), from the actual fixed-root regularizer \(V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2)\) at both ports. Explicitly, on the original cap range, \[ V_j=\frac{4B_j}{\prod_{r=0}^j a_r}\quad(N\text{ even}), \qquad V_j^o=\frac{B_j}{\prod_{r=0}^j a_r}\quad(N\text{ odd}). \] The odd denominators contain no central zero. The actual coefficient \(\overline C_{j,h}\) is obtained from the CROSS part of \(H_{F_N}(A,0,C,Z)\), with the spectral derivative at the fixed root; its original normalization and positivity are proved in [odd regularization](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), sections 1–3. Let \(D_{N,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}\) denote the appropriate one. These are positive for every nonempty range in (1). **All-parity theorem.** \[ \boxed{\limsup_{N\to\infty} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le N-2} \frac{|T_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}} \le0.} \tag{2} \] This is a subexponential bound, not a claimed polynomial factor. The raw numerator is never replaced by its regularized reference. The [even](research_cap_cross_full_low_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) and [odd](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md) full-low theorems prove (2) for \(n\le M\) at both parities. The [high-demand theorem](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md), sections 1–7, proves it with explicit polynomial factors for \(n\ge n_H:=\lceil3N/4-3/2\rceil\). [The all-odd middle proof](research_cap_cross_all_odd_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) has separately closed every missing odd index. It remains to prove the even middle, without identifying it with an auxiliary full slice. ## 2. A genuine all-parity contiguity and both cutoff currents Use the [original Newton source dictionary](research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction.md), sections 2–3, with \[ \widehat B_j(z)=B_j^{-1}\prod_{r=0}^{j-1}(c_r-z), \qquad Z_Ne_j=c_je_j-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1} \] (the last off-diagonal term is zero). Its physical turn identity retains all repeated nodes and all original cup/mark factors. Use the nonnegative row \[ v_j=B_j\prod_{r=j+1}^d a_r,\qquad B_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r^2 . \] The physical three-port adapter with the monomial coupon \(\widehat B_j\) gives exactly \[ C_{j,h}=v^T\widehat B_j(Z_N)e_{d-n},\qquad n=j+h. \tag{3} \] This is the same literal source identity used to derive the full recurrence; the cap specialization of \(\widehat B_j\) is \(A^{d-j}C^j\). It holds before any truncation. The Newton relation \((c_j-Z)\widehat B_j=s_{j+1}^2\widehat B_{j+1}\), and \(Z_Ne_k=c_ke_k-s_{k+1}^2e_{k+1}\), yield \[ s_{j+1}^2 C_{j+1,h-1} =(c_j-c_n)C_{j,h}+s_n^2 C_{j,h-1}. \tag{4} \] Reflection \(c_{d-n}=c_n\), \(s_{d-n+1}=s_n\) is exact. Set \(t_j(n)=(-1)^jU_jC_{j,n-j}\). Using \(\gamma_{j+1}U_{j+1}=s_{j+1}^2U_j\), equation (4) becomes \[ \gamma_n t_j(n)+s_n^2t_j(n-1) =\gamma_jt_j(n)-\gamma_{j+1}t_{j+1}(n). \tag{5} \] For the middle indices \(n>H\), put \(L=n-H\), so \(J_n=[L,M]\) and \(J_{n-1}=[L-1,M]\). Sum (5) over the original range, then use (5) at \(j=L-1\) for the adjacent-projector difference. This proves \[ \boxed{\gamma_nT_{N,n}+s_n^2T_{N,n-1} =(\gamma_{L-1}-\gamma_n)t_{L-1}(n) -\gamma_{M+1}t_{M+1}(n).} \tag{6} \] Both boundary currents are explicit. No top coefficient or lower projector has been omitted. At odd \(N=2m+1\), the first coefficient has \(h=m+1\) and vanishes by the actual unused central zero. Equation (6) reduces to the odd flux. Its one transition index \(n=m=H\) was separately retained in that proof. At even \(N=2m\), \(H=M=m-1\), the two actual boundary coefficients are \[ C_{n-m,m},\qquad C_{m,n-m}. \tag{7} \] The first is a genuine one-sided boundary term just beyond the finite CROSS cutoff, not a CROSS coefficient silently inserted in it. ## 3. The actual even comparator has the same uniform rate J Put \(u=n/d\), \(t=u-1/2\), and \(f(t)=-\int_0^t\log\tan(\pi s)\,ds\). The comparator rate obtained in the odd proof is \[ J(u)=f(t)+\max_{t\le a\le1/2} [3f(a)+f(a-t)]. \tag{8} \] It is strictly concave and has a unique peak \(u_*\in(1/2,3/4)\). Those conclusions depend only on the displayed continuous entropy, not on level parity. Here is the genuine even LOWER input. The [closed half-block entropy theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) section 5, equation (15), proves coefficientwise \[ B_{\mathrm{cross}} =4(A+Z)\mathcal D(A,0,Z)\mathcal D(A,C,Z) \le P_{\mathrm{cross}}<3B_{\mathrm{cross}}, \tag{9} \] where \(\mathcal D(A,b,Z)=R_M^*(b)\) is exactly the modified lower-block path numerator of its equation (15). If one instead uses its determinant denoted \(D_M\), then \(\mathcal D=C_{\mathrm{front}}D_M\) with \(C_{\mathrm{front}}=N/[2\sin(\pi/N)]\). This scalar is retained in (9), not dropped from the exact inequality. The same theorem proves uniform CLOSED triangle coefficient upper and lower rates for these \(\mathcal D\)'s. Their total degree is M, so \(M/d=1/2-1/(2d)\); this shift vanishes uniformly by closed continuity. The forced outer factor in (9) must remain. In the actual \(j=M\) comparator term choose the forced outer Z. Then the genuine latent A-degree k has integer interval \[ n-M\le k\le M . \tag{10} \] On the middle interval the limiting maximizing a in (8) is interior; rounding it into (10) costs \(O(1/d)\). Thus the forced Z term in the exact positive block supplies a matching lower rate. This is not an inference from a weighted capacity or an upper-only theorem. For the upper estimate, all latent allocations have, up to \(O(1/d)\), the same objective as in the odd calculation: \[ 2f(a)+f(v-a)+f(u-v)+f(u-a)-2f(v), \qquad t\le a\le v\le1/2. \tag{11} \] Here \(v=j/d\), and the actual even cap product gives \(N^{-1}\log V_j=-2f(v)+o(1)\) uniformly. Its derivative in v is positive, so the maximum is \(v=1/2\) and equals (8). The polynomial number of positive terms, the two-sided closed theorem, and (10) prove \[ N^{-1}\log D_{N,n}=J(n/d)+o(1) \tag{12} \] uniformly for \(M<n\le n_H\), including \(n_H\). The adjacent starting index n=M has rate \(J(1/2)+o(1)\). All d-versus-N and forced-unit offsets are absorbed by closed continuity; no finite support is enlarged for the lower estimate. ## 4. Both even currents lie below that same rate The cap boundary \(C_{m,n-m}\) in (7) has normalized A-load \(m/d=1/2+O(1/d)\), C-load \(t+O(1/d)\), and input middle zero. Its limiting endpoint CROSS entropy is precisely J(u), as in the odd flux calculation. The original uniform closed coefficient upper theorem therefore bounds it by \(\exp\{N[J(u)+o(1)]\}\). The new lower-cutoff coefficient \(C_{n-m,m}\) approaches the actual endpoint seam \[ (q_x,q_b,q_c,q_y)=(t,0,1/2,1/2-t). \] The [uniform original closed upper theorem](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md), section 4, equation (12), at \(\delta=0\), and the [closed Green/seam formula](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md), sections 1 and 5, give its rate at most \(2f(t)\). This statement applies to the actual one-sided finite coefficient; it does not require a CROSS lower formula for that coefficient. Since choosing \(a=t\) in (8) gives \[ J(u)\ge4f(t)\ge2f(t), \tag{13} \] this additional current is also bounded at rate J. All prefactors in (6) are polynomial: the gammas are bounded, \(U_j\le C N^2\) for \(0\le j\le m\), and the relevant cap indices are \(j=n-m\) and \(j=m\). The U bound follows directly from its shifted sine-product formula: it decreases up to \(m-1\), and the next ratio is bounded, while \(U_0=O(N^2)\). Consequently the entire right side of (6) has the uniform bound \[ e^{N[J(n/d)+o(1)]}. \tag{14} \] ## 5. Two-sided propagation completes the even middle On all indices from M to \(n_H\), the raw recurrence coefficients \(s_n^2,\gamma_n\) are bounded away from zero, and \[ \left|\log\frac{s_n^2}{\gamma_n}\right|\le C/N . \tag{15} \] Every forward or backward subinterval product is therefore bounded. Propagate (6) forward from the low endpoint n=M up to the peak of J. Every encountered current has rate at most the current J because J is increasing there. The initial low estimate has rate \(J(1/2)\). The O(N) terms and bounded propagators give \[ |T_{N,n}|\le e^{N[J(n/d)+o(1)]}. \] For indices beyond the peak, propagate backward from \(n_H\), where the proved even high-demand estimate is \(|T_{N,n_H}|\le D_{N,n_H}\). Now J decreases, so every boundary/current rate is again at most the current J. The same estimate follows. Rounding around the single peak costs o(1) in rate. Divide by the actual lower estimate (12). This proves the subexponential ratio on the even middle, uniformly in n. Together with the low/high intervals and the odd middle proof, it proves (2). ## Scope Every degree in the original nonempty J_n has been covered, with both finite boundary currents retained. The proof asserts neither a polynomial all-demand factor nor estimates on a spectral neighborhood. It does not identify independent overlapping Casimirs, introduce a semisimple coupon adapter, or compare arbitrary exterior face targets. A whole-source or filling consequence would require its own assembly argument. The new ingredients in this draft are the exact general contiguity (3)--(6), the even forced-unit lower check (9)--(12), and the seam-current comparison (13)--(14). No numerical growth experiment is used as proof. ## scope and finite source verification No finite monotonicity of individual coefficients is assumed. The [portable exact-field audit](../experiments/audit_research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.py) with [recorded results](../experiments/research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction_results.json) checks N=3 through 10: 164 literal coefficient-contiguity identities and 52 original projected flux recurrences, including both parity cutoffs and empty terminal ranges. It separately checks 52 full raw physical three-port scalars, 52 full auxiliary recurrences, 24 actual low-cutoff identifications and 52 Newton resolvent entries. All calculations are exact in the chosen finite fields, with conservative integer-overflow bounds. These are finite source-identity checks, not an asymptotic proof. The subexponential estimates are established analytically above. Root completed a fresh redirected replay of this combined finite audit with identical recorded results.

title: All odd demands: the projected flux and a concave comparator rate
text: # All odd demands: the projected flux and a concave comparator rate 31 October 2026. The theorem concerns the fixed cap/CROSS spectral pair. It gives a subexponential comparison with the odd endpoint reference, not a polynomial bound or a uniform estimate for nearby spectra. ## 1. Statement and retained source Let \(N=2m+1\ge3\), \(d=2m\), \(M=m-1\). Keep the original pair \(E=(A,0,C,Z)\), \(F=(0,A,0,C)\), its \(A^d\) demand, raw spectral values \((-2,+2)\), and all unused factors. Define \[ T_n=\sum_{j=\max(0,n-m)}^{\min(M,n)} (-1)^jU_jC_{j,n-j},\qquad D_n^o=\sum_{j=\max(0,n-m)}^{\min(M,n)} V_j^o\overline C_{j,n-j}. \tag{1} \] Here \(\overline C,V^o\) are exactly the CROSS/RIGHT coefficients of the actual odd regularizer \(F_N=V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2)\). The scalar definitions and continuant are those of the [original-demand source](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md), sections 1–2; their odd extension, including the zero unused factor, is proved in the [odd raw-source theorem](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md), section 1. The numerator remains raw. The ranges in (1) are the original finite ranges, not complete sums introduced above the low cutoff. **Theorem.** \[ \limsup_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ \mathrm{odd}}} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le N-2} \frac{|T_n|}{D_n^o}\le0. \tag{2} \] All denominators are positive in this range. The empty degree \(n=d\) is not included in the ratio. The [odd low-demand theorem](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md) proves (2) for \(n\le M\). The original [all-parity high-demand theorem](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md) gives \(|T_n|\le4N D_n^o\) for \[ n\ge n_H:=\lceil3N/4-3/2\rceil . \] It remains to bridge \(m\le n<n_H\). ## 2. Exact recurrence of the projected source Use the genuine Newton polynomial \[ F^P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_j\widehat B_j(z). \] At the protected cap it has exactly its original RIGHT monomials. The literal Newton multiplication rule gives \[ (2-z)F^P(z)=4+K_N\widehat B_m(z),\qquad K_N=(-1)^M s_m^2U_M. \tag{3} \] Indeed all intermediate coefficients cancel using \(\gamma_jU_j=s_j^2U_{j-1}\), and the omitted top coefficient is exactly the second term of (3). At odd level the raw E coefficient \(C_{j,h}\) vanishes for \(h>m\) because its unused suffix contains \(a_m=0\). Thus using full raw E with \(F^P\) is precisely (1), including its moving lower cutoff. The exact physical three-port adapter identifies the \(\widehat B_m\) insertion with \(C_{m,n-m}\), and therefore \[ \boxed{\gamma_nT_n+s_n^2T_{n-1} =4C_{0,n}+K_N C_{m,n-m},} \quad T_{-1}=0, \tag{4} \] where out-of-range \(C\)'s are zero. The [literal Newton source adapter](research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction.md), section 2, and its [raw odd extension](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md), section 1, prove this with all original turns and demands: inserting \(\widehat B_m\) at the cap inserts exactly the monomial \(A^{d-m}C^m\), and hence gives the single coefficient \(C_{m,n-m}\). Multiplying the resulting Newton row by \(2I-Z_N\) proves (4). No projected tensor covariance is assumed. For \(n\ge m+1\), \(C_{0,n}=0\). At \(n=m\), \(C_{0,m}=N^2\). Also \(s_m^2U_M=4N\), by the exact odd endpoint products. Thus the forcing prefactors are polynomial and no central zero is divided out. For all indices between \(M\) and \(n_H\), both \(s_n^2\) and \(\gamma_n\) are bounded above and below by positive absolute constants for sufficiently large \(N\). Furthermore \[ r_n:=\frac{s_n^2}{\gamma_n} =\frac{\sin^2(n\theta)}{\sin^2((n+1/2)\theta)}, \qquad |\log r_n|\le C/N. \tag{5} \] Hence every forward or backward product over a subinterval of these indices is bounded by a fixed constant. This is the raw recurrence; the much larger normalized coefficient \(t_n\) is not used here. ## 3. Actual two-sided endpoint coefficient asymptotics Put \[ f(t)=-\int_0^t\log\tan(\pi s)\,ds,\quad0\le t\le1/2, \qquad u=n/d,\quad v=j/d. \] The genuine odd cap-reference product is \[ V_j^o=\frac{\prod_{r=1}^j s_r^2} {\prod_{r=0}^j a_r},\qquad j\le M. \tag{6} \] The exact noncentral product \(\prod_{r\ne m}a_r=N^2\) proves (6), without dividing by \(a_m\).
