Uniform sine/cosine logarithmic sums give \[ N^{-1}\log V_j^o=-2f(v)+o(1) \tag{7} \] uniformly up to both endpoints. The needed E estimate is a genuine CLOSED upper and lower theorem: [odd regularized full numerator](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), section 3, equations (8)--(11), proves the exact raw factorization \[ H_{V_N(-2)}=N^2D_m(A,0,Z)D_m(A,C,Z) \] on these protected inputs. Each positive \(D_m\) coefficient has uniform closed triangle entropy \(\mathcal C(\alpha)=\sum_i f(\alpha_i)\), with total load \(1/2\). Its proof retains the actual positive first term in its equation (9) and the trim/fill lower estimates; it is not the general upper-only sharp LIMSUP theorem. Equations (3),(7) of that reference also compare the actual regularized CROSS coefficient to this raw positive factorization by uniform constant factors. For \(C_{j,h}\), let \(k\) be the first triangle's A-degree. The original positive convolution has precisely the integer interval \[ \max(0,j+h-m)\le k\le\min(m,j). \tag{8} \] Its two normalized triangle loads are \[ (a,0,\tfrac12-a),\qquad (v-a,u-v,\tfrac12-u+a),\qquad a=k/d. \] Thus the E entropy is \[ \mathcal{H}_E(u,v)= \max_{\max(0,u-1/2)\le a\le\min(1/2,v)} \{2f(a)+f(v-a)+f(u-v)+f(u-a)\}. \tag{9} \] The third f in the second triangle was reflected using \(f(1/2-t)=f(t)\). The positive convolution, its polynomial number of terms, and rounding \(k\) within (8) prove uniform matching logarithmic upper and lower estimates for (9). This includes a zero middle load and the original central-row boundary. Replacing d-normalization by N-normalization changes every argument by \(O(1/N)\); uniform CLOSED continuity absorbs it. For \(u\ge1/2\), write \(t=u-1/2\). Combining (7),(9), the limiting reference objective is \[ E(a,v;u)=2f(a)+f(v-a)+f(u-v)+f(u-a)-2f(v), \qquad t\le a\le v\le1/2. \tag{10} \] In the interior, \[ \partial_v E= \log\frac{\tan(\pi(u-v))\tan^2(\pi v)} {\tan(\pi(v-a))}>0. \tag{11} \] Indeed \(u-v\ge1/2-v\), and \(v-a\le v\), with strictness except the harmless boundary \(u=1/2,a=0\). Therefore the closed maximum is attained at \(v=1/2\), and its value is \[ J(u)= f(t)+\max_{t\le a\le1/2} \{3f(a)+f(a-t)\}. \tag{12} \] For the ACTUAL finite comparator, \(j=M\) is allowed and has \(v=1/2-1/d\), tending to that maximizer. At this j, the genuine latent interval (8) is \(n-m\le k\le M\). Rounding the limiting maximizer into this interval moves a by at most \(O(1/d)\). This proves the required lower estimate, not just an upper capacity. Consequently, uniformly for \(m\le n\le n_H\), including the backward initial endpoint \(n_H\), \[ N^{-1}\log D_n^o=J(n/d)+o(1). \tag{13} \] The same statement extends to the adjacent low endpoint \(n=M\) by continuity, with value \(J(1/2)+o(1)\). The flux \(C_{m,n-m}\) has \(v=1/2\) exactly and no cap factor. Its limiting E action in (9) is precisely (12). In particular the uniform closed upper estimate gives \[ |4C_{0,n}+K_N C_{m,n-m}| \le\exp\{N[J(n/d)+o(1)]\} \tag{14} \] on the middle interval. At \(n=m\), its extra \(4N^2\) term also satisfies this estimate, since \(J(1/2)>0\). All errors in (13)--(14) are uniform over the actual finite indices. ## 4. Concavity supplies the two propagation directions The function \[ f(t)+3f(a)+f(a-t) \] is jointly concave on \(0\le t\le a\le1/2\). Maximizing over a preserves concavity in t. The strict concavity of \(f(t)\) makes J strictly concave on the open interval. The maximizing a is uniquely interior for \(0<t<1/2\); it obeys \(3f'(a)+f'(a-t)=0\). The envelope derivative is \[ J'(u)=f'(t)-f'(a-t). \tag{15} \] At \(t\downarrow0\), \(a\to1/4\) and this derivative tends to \(+\infty\). At \(t=1/4\), the maximizer lies strictly between \(1/4\) and \(1/2\), so (15) is negative. Thus J has one peak \(u_*\in(1/2,3/4)\), increasing before it and decreasing after it. Solve (4) forward from \(M\) for indices \(n/d\le u_*\). The initial low theorem bounds \(|T_M|\) by \(\exp\{N[J(1/2)+o(1)]\}\). Every forcing in the resulting finite sum has rate at most \(J(n/d)+o(1)\), by (14) and monotonicity. Equation (5) bounds the propagation factors and there are only O(N) terms. Hence \[ |T_n|\le e^{N[J(n/d)+o(1)]} \tag{16} \] uniformly on that side. On the other side, solve (4) BACKWARD from \(n_H\), using the proved high-demand inequality \(|T_{n_H}|\le4N D_{n_H}^o\). For all sufficiently large N, \(n_H/d>u_*\). Every encountered forcing and the boundary term now has rate at most \(J(n/d)+o(1)\), since J decreases on this side. The inverse propagation products are also bounded by (5). Thus (16) holds uniformly here as well. Integer rounding at the single peak costs \(o(1)\) in rate by continuity. Divide (16) by the actual lower estimate (13). This proves (2) on the missing middle interval; combine it with the low and high theorems to obtain every \(0\le n\le N-2\). ## Scope The proof uses the raw odd projected recurrence, a genuine positive endpoint coefficient LOWER theorem, and a uniform two-sided comparator rate. It does not replace the original cutoff sum by its full auxiliary slice above M, use a norm bound, or infer finite monotonicity of the individual comparator coefficients. The even source requires its own boundary term, which is not covered by this all-odd statement. Nearby spectra, the full source and filling asymptotics remain separate; the all-parity extension is cited above.

title: The entire even low-demand range: a subexponential signed contraction
text: # The entire even low-demand range: a subexponential signed contraction 31 October 2026. analytical theorem. This extends the low-quarter estimate using its exact original-source recurrence. It retains the original two half-block cutoffs. The conclusion is subexponential, not a polynomial estimate, and does not cover odd levels or the remaining projected middle-demand range. ## 1. Statement and exact scalar reduction Let \(N=2m\ge4\), \(M=m-1\), \(d=N-1\), and \(\theta=\pi/N\). Use the original fixed-pair cap/CROSS coefficient \(S_{N,n}\), endpoint comparator \(D_{N,n}\), and coefficient \(C_{0,n}>0\) of [the Newton source theorem](research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction.md). In particular the original \(A^d\) demand, unused products, raw signs, and actual spectral pair \((+2,-2)\) have not changed. **Theorem.** Uniformly over the whole original low range, \[ \limsup_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ {\mathrm{even}}}} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le M} \frac{|S_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}}\le0. \tag{1} \] Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), all sufficiently large even \(N\) obey \(|S_{N,n}|\le e^{\varepsilon N}D_{N,n}\) for every \(0\le n\le M\). The threshold may depend on \(\varepsilon\). The exact source theorem gives \[ R_n=\frac{\gamma_n S_{N,n}}{4C_{0,n}},\quad R_0=1,\quad R_n=1-t_nR_{n-1},\qquad t_n=\frac{4\sin^4(n\theta)}{\sin^2((2n-1)\theta)}, \quad\gamma_n=2-2\cos((2n+1)\theta). \tag{2} \] For this range the original cutoff is precisely \(J_n=\{\max(0,n-M),\ldots,\min(M,n)\}=\{0,\ldots,n\}\). The auxiliary full slice therefore equals the original projected sum. No such identification is used above \(M\). Write \[ P_0=1,\quad P_j=\prod_{r=1}^j t_r,\quad A_j=P_j^{-1}. \qquad R_n=(-1)^n P_n\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j A_j. \tag{3} \] The elementary sine products and monotonicity of \(t_r\) give \[ P_M=\frac{N^2\sin^2(\pi/N)}4,\qquad 0<P_j\le\pi^2/4\quad(0\le j\le M). \tag{4} \] Indeed \(\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}4\sin^2(r\theta)=m\), whereas \(\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}4\sin^2((2r-1)\theta)=1/\sin^2\theta\). Moreover \(\partial_v\log t(v)=4\theta[\cot(v\theta)-\cot((2v-1)\theta)] \ge0\) for \(1\le v\le M\). Thus \(\log P_j\) is convex and its maximum occurs at an endpoint. This alone does not bound the signed sum in (3). ## 2. Exact endpoint factors and an analytic interpolant Define the removable-value functions \[ g(t)=\frac{\sin(2\pi t)}{2\pi t(1-2t)},\qquad s(t)=\frac{\sin(\pi t)}{\pi t}. \] Both are positive on \([0,1/2]\). They have holomorphic logarithms \(L_g,L_s\), real there, throughout the vertical strip \(-1/2<\Re t<1\). For \(g\), the zeros at \(0,1/2\) have been removed and the next zeros are \(-1/2,1\); for \(s\), the next zeros are \(-1,1\). Direct factorization of every sine in \(A_j\) yields exactly \[ A_j= \left(\frac2\pi\right)^{2j} \frac{\Gamma(j+1/2)^2\Gamma(m+1/2)^2} {\pi\,\Gamma(j+1)^4\Gamma(m-j+1/2)^2} \exp\!\left\{ 2\sum_{r=1}^jL_g((r-1/2)/N) -4\sum_{r=1}^jL_s(r/N)\right\}. \tag{5} \] This retains both real endpoint singularities in exact Gamma factors. Fix any finite \(Y>0\), and use Cauchy radius \(\rho=1/5\). All derivatives of \(L_g,L_s\) on the rectangles needed below obey \[ |L^{(k)}(t)|\le M_Y\,k!\rho^{-k}, \tag{6} \] where \(M_Y\) is finite and independent of \(N\). One may obtain (6) by taking a slightly larger fixed rectangle inside the indicated zero-free vertical strip. Let \(p=\lfloor\pi\rho N\rfloor\). For all sufficiently large \(N\) define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{E}_{1/2,N}(L;u) &=N\int_0^uL(t)\,dt+ \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} \frac{B_{2k}(1/2)}{(2k)!\,N^{2k-1}} [L^{(2k-1)}(u)-L^{(2k-1)}(0)],\\ \mathcal{E}_{1,N}(L;u) &=N\int_0^uL(t)\,dt+\frac{L(u)-L(0)}2+ \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} \frac{B_{2k}}{(2k)!\,N^{2k-1}} [L^{(2k-1)}(u)-L^{(2k-1)}(0)]. \end{aligned} \tag{7} \] Here the integrals use the analytic primitive on that strip. At \(u=j/N\), the two formulas approximate respectively the midpoint and right-endpoint sums in (5). For precision, the shifted Euler--Maclaurin remainder, the bound \(\sup_x|B_{2p}(\{x\})|\le4(2p)!/(2\pi)^{2p}\), and (6) give \[ |{\mathrm{remainder}}| \le C_Y N\,\frac{(2p)!}{(2\pi\rho N)^{2p}} =\exp[-(2\pi\rho+o(1))N] \tag{8} \] uniformly for every real integer \(0\le j\le M\). The same bound holds for the translated periodic Bernoulli remainder of the midpoint sum. The omitted next endpoint correction, if the chosen remainder convention includes it, has the same exponential bound and is absorbed in (8). Since \(2\pi/5>6/5\), the combined error in the exponent of (5) is at most \(e^{-6N/5}\) for sufficiently large \(N\). Replace the two sums in (5) by (7), with \(u=z/N\), and call the resulting function \(\mathcal{A}_N(z)\). It is analytic on \[ -1/4\le\Re z\le M+1/4,\qquad |\Im z|\le NY \] and a neighborhood of that rectangle. The numerator Gamma poles start at \(z=-1/2\); the other numerator Gamma factor is constant. Reciprocal Gamma factors introduce no poles. All analytic logarithms in (7) remain in their stated strip. Equation (8) gives the nodal estimate \[ \mathcal{A}_N(j)=A_j\exp(e_{N,j}),\qquad |e_{N,j}|\le e^{-6N/5},\quad0\le j\le M. \tag{9} \] No guessed degree interpolation is used: the values are matched with an explicit exponentially controlled error. ## 3. Uniform complex growth, including the endpoint layers Put \[ f(u)=-\int_0^u\log\tan(\pi t)\,dt,\qquad0\le u\le1/2. \] Use its analytic continuation to \(0<\Re u<1/2,\Im u>0\), with the logarithm continued from the positive real tangent. Reflect by conjugation below the real axis. The primitive has continuous boundary values on both vertical edges of this strip. The derivative bound (6) also shows, uniformly for complex \(u\) in any fixed-height rectangle considered here, \[ \mathcal{E}_{1/2,N}(L;u)=N\int_0^uL+O_Y(N^{-1}),\qquad \mathcal{E}_{1,N}(L;u)=N\int_0^uL+\tfrac12[L(u)-L(0)] +O_Y(N^{-1}). \tag{10} \] For example the correction terms are bounded by constant multiples of \(N(2k-1)!/(2\pi\rho N)^{2k}\). Up to half the optimal truncation their successive ratios are bounded below one; the remaining terms are exponentially small. The differentiated corrections are bounded as well. No estimate uniform as \(Y\to\infty\) is asserted. Uniform Stirling estimates in the right half-plane, applied to the exact Gamma factors in (5), now give \[ \log|\mathcal{A}_N(x+iNy)| =N\Re[2f(x/N+iy)]+O_Y(\log N), \quad0\le x\le M,\quad |y|\le Y. \tag{11} \] Here and below the lower half-plane uses the conjugate branch. There is no unbounded-endpoint Stirling substitution: for \(\Re w\ge0, |w|\le C_YN\), \[ \log\Gamma(w+a)=w\log w-w+O_Y(\log N), \qquad a=1/2\text{ or }1, \] with \(w\log w=0\) at zero. For \(|w|\le1\) this follows directly from the analytic nonzero Gamma function; outside that disk it is the uniform sectorial Stirling formula. Apply this to \(w=z,m,m-z\). Their real parts are nonnegative on (11). One can also check the leading primitive without any Stirling constant ambiguity. The Gamma contribution has derivative \(2\log[(1-2u)/(\pi u)]\), while the smooth-product contribution has derivative \(2L_g(u)-4L_s(u)\). Their sum is exactly \(-2\log\tan(\pi u)\), and their value at \(u=0\) is zero. On the full slightly enlarged \(z\)-rectangle, \[ |\partial_z\log\mathcal{A}_N(z)|=O_Y(\log N). \tag{12} \] All Gamma arguments have real part at least \(1/4\), their digammas are \(O_Y(\log N)\), and (6)--(7) give the same bound for the smooth factor. Thus moving \(x\) by at most \(1/4\) in (11) changes its real logarithm by only \(O_Y(\log N)\). This handles the left vertical contour at \(-1/4\) without choosing a logarithm across the endpoint singularity of \(f\). The right contour is handled in the same way. At real nodes, (9)--(11) in particular give \[ \log A_j=2Nf(j/N)+O(\log N),\qquad \log P_j=-2Nf(j/N)+O(\log N), \tag{13} \] uniformly down to \(j=0\) and up to \(M\). For \(0\le u\le1/2\), \(y\ge0\), define \[ h(u,y)=\Re[2f(u+iy)]-\pi y . \] For \(0<u<1/2,y>0\), the tangent has positive real and imaginary parts. Hence \[ \partial_yh=2\arg\tan(\pi(u+iy))-\pi<0,\qquad h(u,y)\le2f(u). \tag{14} \] The boundary values satisfy \(h(0,y)=h(1/2,y)=0\). For \(y>0\) the absolutely convergent series is \[ h(u,y)=\frac2\pi \sum_{\substack{k\ge1\\ k\ {\mathrm{odd}}}} \frac{e^{-2\pi ky}\sin(2\pi ku)}{k^2}. \tag{15} \] It follows either by integrating \(-\log\tan(\pi z)=-i\pi/2+ 2\sum_{k\ {\mathrm{odd}}}e^{2\pi ikz}/k\), with its value at zero, or by differentiating and matching the boundary value. Consequently \[ \sup_{0\le u\le1/2}|h(u,Y)|\le \epsilon_Y:= \frac{2e^{-2\pi Y}}{\pi(1-e^{-4\pi Y})} \longrightarrow0. \tag{16} \] ## 4. Alternating residues and the uniform subexponential bound For each \(0\le n\le M\), take the rectangle with real edges \(-1/4,n+1/4\) and imaginary edges \(\pm NY\). The poles of \(\pi/\sin(\pi z)\) enclosed are exactly the integers \(0,\ldots,n\), with residues \((-1)^j\). Therefore \[ \sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j\mathcal{A}_N(j) =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint \frac{\pi\mathcal{A}_N(z)}{\sin(\pi z)}\,dz. \tag{17} \] There are no poles of the interpolant in this contour. On the vertical edges \(|\sin(\pi z)|^{-1}\le C e^{-\pi|\Im z|}\); the same holds on the horizontal edges for large \(N\). Multiply (17) by \(P_n\). On the left edge use (4), (11)--(12), and \(h(0,y)=0\). Its integral is at most a fixed \(Y\)-dependent power of \(N\). On the right edge use (13)--(14): the exponent is bounded by \[ N[h(n/N,|y|)-2f(n/N)]+O_Y(\log N)\le O_Y(\log N). \] The shift from \(n\) to \(n+1/4\) costs only (12). Thus this integral has the same polynomial bound. On either horizontal edge use (4), (11)--(12), and (16). The integral is bounded by \[ N^{C_Y}e^{N\epsilon_Y}. \tag{18} \] All estimates are uniform in \(n\), including \(n=0\). The nodal replacement error in (9) is exponentially negligible even after absolute values. Indeed \(f\) is maximal at \(1/4\), and \[ 2f(1/4)\le\frac{1+\log2}{2}<1 \] by \(\tan(\pi t)\ge2t\) on \(0<t\le1/4\). Equations (4), (9), and (13) imply \[ P_n\sum_{j=0}^n|\mathcal{A}_N(j)-A_j| \le e^{-N/5+O(\log N)}. \tag{19} \] Combining (3), (17)--(19) gives, for every fixed \(Y>0\), \[ \max_{0\le n\le M}|R_n| \le N^{C_Y}e^{N\epsilon_Y} +e^{-N/5+O(\log N)}. \tag{20} \] First let the even level tend to infinity with \(Y\) fixed, and only then let \(Y\to\infty\). Equation (16) proves \[ \limsup_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ {\mathrm{even}}}} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le M}|R_n|\le0. \tag{21} \] This does not require any \(Y\)-uniform Stirling or interpolation constant, nor a scaled contour height \(Y\) growing with \(N\). Finally the original positive comparator contains \(V_0C_{0,n}=4C_{0,n}/a_0\), where \(a_0=2+2\cos\theta\). Thus, exactly as in the quarter-range proof, \[ \frac{|S_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}} \le\frac{a_0}{\gamma_n}|R_n| \le N^2 |R_n| . \] This and (21) prove (1). The recorded raw common sign does not affect the modulus. No other face demand or power has been altered. ## 5. Scope This is a cancellation estimate for the actual fixed spectral pair and every original even low-demand coefficient \(0\le n\le M\). It is stronger than a coefficient-norm or residue-variation bound: those can be exponentially excessive in this same problem. The new argument retains the alternating sign through the contour. The low-quarter theorem still provides its sharper polynomial factor there. The present proof does not establish a polynomial bound on the whole low range. It also does not identify the auxiliary full slice with the original projected sum when \(n>M\), prove the analogous odd-level low bound, control nearby complex spectra, or give a whole source/filling theorem. Those are separate tasks. The source input is the exact Newton recurrence with its original cutoff. The analytical estimates are (5)–(20). The [odd extension](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md) proves the corresponding odd-source statement with its regularized positive comparator.

title: Exact signed cap/CROSS contraction in a macroscopic high-demand range
text: # Exact signed cap/CROSS contraction in a macroscopic high-demand range 31 October 2026. **, unpublished analytical theorem** for the exact two-port incidence in the [original-demand convolution](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). The original internal face demand, both remaining degrees, and both genuine source cutoffs are retained. This proves a nontrivial range of that note's proposed comparison. It is not a bound for its remaining degrees, arbitrary spectra, or the whole invariant. The same exact degree window is controlled at every level N>=3: the comparison factor is one at even levels and 4N at odd levels, using the actual odd regularized reference specified in section 7. ## 1. Statement with the original finite normalization Let N=2m>=4, d=N-1, M=m-1 and theta=pi/N. Keep the original ports E=(A,0,C,Z), F=(0,A,0,C), where A occurs only at these two ports. E is its genuine CROSS polynomial at -2; F is its genuine RIGHT polynomial at +2. Extract the actual A-degree d first. In the notation of the original reduction, S_(N,n)=sum_(j in J_n) (-1)^j U_j C_(j,n-j), D_(N,n)=sum_(j in J_n) V_j C_(j,n-j)>0, J_n=[max(0,n-M),min(M,n)] intersect Z, 0<=n<=2M. (1) The raw B_N coefficient is (-1)^d S_(N,n), and the positive endpoint coefficient B_N^0 is D_(N,n). No extra N factor occurs. **Theorem.** For every even N>=4 and every original remaining degree ceil(3N/4-3/2)<=n<=N-2, one has the exact inequality |S_(N,n)|<=U_M C_(M,n-M) =V_M C_(M,n-M)<=D_(N,n). (2) Thus the polynomial comparison holds in this entire range with constant one, not just with a polynomial loss. In terms of the other remaining degree k=d-n, the range is 1<=k<=floor(N/4+1/2). In particular it contains every macroscopic limit n/N->rho>3/4, and includes the stated exact threshold at rho=3/4. The comparison is at the fixed spectra of (1) and at even levels only. ## 2. A positive injection with every unused factor retained Recall the literal source recurrence and coefficients s_r=2 sin(r theta), a_r=4 cos^2((r+1/2)theta), K_0=1, K_1=s_1^2(A+Z), K_r=s_r^2(A+Z)K_(r-1) +s_r s_(r-1)a_(r-1)AZ K_(r-2), C_(j,h)=[A^j Z^(d-h-j)]K_(d-h) product_(r=d-h+1)^d a_r. (3) All these coefficients are positive on the indices below. Let h=n-j and r=d-h. For j in J_n with j<M, append the A-monomer at the next row of K. Its contribution to the coefficient of A^(j+1) Z^(d-n) is s_(r+1)^2 times the preceding coefficient; every other contribution is nonnegative. The unused suffix loses exactly the factor a_(r+1). Therefore C_(j+1,h-1)>=s_(r+1)^2/a_(r+1) C_(j,h) =s_h^2/a_(h-1) C_(j,h). (4) The last equality uses r+1=N-h, hence s_(r+1)=s_h and a_(r+1)=a_(h-1). The factor in (4) is not an approximation; it is the exact weight of this subset of original paths, divided by the single unused row removed from the suffix. In the range of the theorem n>M, so J_n=[L,M] with L=n-M. For j=L,...,M-1, both j and h remain within the actual cutoffs; h>=n-M+1>=1. No full-sum or endpoint extension is being used. ## 3. Monotonicity of the actual alternating summands The literal cap ratio is U_(j+1)/U_j =sin^2((j+1)theta)/sin^2((j+3/2)theta). Put T_j=U_j C_(j,n-j)>0, a=(j+1)theta, b=h theta, and epsilon=theta/2. Combining this ratio with (4) gives T_(j+1)/T_j >=[sin(a) sin(b)/(sin(a+epsilon)cos(b-epsilon))]^2. (5) The finite threshold in (2) is exactly n-M+1>=N/4+1/2. Consequently for every adjacent pair in J_n, pi/4+epsilon<=a,b<=pi/2-theta. All denominators in (5) are positive. On the relevant intervals, sin(a)/sin(a+epsilon) and sin(b)/cos(b-epsilon) are increasing functions of their arguments: their logarithmic derivatives are cot(a)-cot(a+epsilon)>0 and cot(b)+tan(b-epsilon)>0. Comparing the first ratio at a=pi/4 and the second at b=pi/4+epsilon gives [sin(pi/4)/sin(pi/4+epsilon)] [sin(pi/4+epsilon)/cos(pi/4)]=1. Thus (5) is at least one, and T_L<=T_(L+1)<=...<=T_M. (6) For a singleton J_n this assertion is vacuous and the next step holds directly. ## 4. Alternation uses the original cutoff endpoint For any nonnegative increasing finite sequence, its alternating sum has absolute value at most the final entry. This follows by pairing consecutive terms from the final end for nonnegativity and from the opposite end for the upper bound. Applying it to (6) gives |sum_(j=L)^M (-1)^j T_j|<=T_M. (7) The original cutoff is crucial: its final cap weight obeys U_M/V_M =product_(r=0)^M cot^2((r+1/2)theta)=1, (8) by pairing angles with their complements. In fact U_M=V_M=N: the product over integer sine angles 1,...,m-1 has square N/2^(N-1), while the product over half-integer angles 1/2,...,m-1/2 has square 2^(1-N); the prefactors in U_M and V_M cancel their respective omitted first angles. The term V_M C_(M,n-M) is present in the original positive sum D_(N,n). Equations (7)--(8) prove (2), with all raw and endpoint normalizations unchanged. ## 5. Exact scope and remaining issue Equivalently, restrict the two degree-d polynomials B_N(C,Z) and B_N^0(C,Z), after extracting A^d, to the C degrees in the theorem. The coefficientwise modulus of the restricted B_N is bounded by the same restriction of B_N^0. Every exterior face target and the remaining C,Z degrees are retained. No exterior coupon has been changed, and a signed exterior may only be bounded after its own absolute coefficients are explicitly retained. This argument uses cancellation in the original alternating sequence. It does not pass through the [disproved bare cap-Cauchy norm or absolute tensor coefficient mass](research_cap_moment_cauchy_norm_obstruction.md). It gives no estimate for lower macroscopic n, and does not identify the projected coupons with unprojected Casimir functions. The full uniform inequality in the original reduction and the general strictly overloaded source bound remain open. No numerical sampling is used in this proof. ## 6. At low remaining demand the two projections are redundant There is a separate exact source simplification for 0<=n<=M. This section gives an identity, not another estimate. The FULL original cap at F, before RIGHT projection, has H_F(A,C;2)=sum_(j=0)^d (-1)^j U_j A^(d-j)C^j. (9) To verify the full range, set gamma_r=2-2cos((2r+1)theta)>0. The protected output middle forces the actual stop to be d. For the start i=d-j, the original raw sign and magnitude are (-1)^d (-1)^(d-j)=(-1)^j, product_(r=0)^(d-j-1) gamma_r product_(r=d-j+1)^d s_r^2. Reflection gives gamma_(d-r)=gamma_r and s_(N-r)=s_r. Thus the magnitude equals product_(r=j+1)^d gamma_r times product_(r=1)^j s_r^2. The exact full product product_(r=0)^d gamma_r=4 identifies it with U_j, including both j=0 and j=d. No upper-half state, derivative datum, or unused row has been discarded. Likewise the FULL original E coupon at -2, before CROSS projection, is H_E(A,C,Z;-2)=(-1)^d sum_(h=0)^d sum_(a=0)^(d-h) C_(a,h) A^a C^h Z^(d-h-a), (10) where the same literal coefficient formula (3) defines C_(a,h) for all these h. The protected input middle forces start zero, so (10) retains every possible actual stop and its unused suffix. In the product of (9)--(10), extracting the original A^d forces a=j. The remaining C-degree n then forces j+h=n. All exponents are nonnegative. Hence if n<=M, necessarily j<=M and h<=M. These are exactly the genuine RIGHT and CROSS restrictions already imposed in (1). Consequently [A^d C^n Z^(d-n)] H_F(full;2) H_E(full;-2) =(-1)^d S_(N,n), 0<=n<=M. (11) This permits using a valid identity of the actual UNPROJECTED Casimir coupons before taking this low-degree coefficient. It does not make the projected coupons covariant operators and does not turn their overlapping pair Casimirs into functions of one commuting operator. Any further tensor identity must keep the original pair order and cup/turn frames. Equation (11) alone supplies no polynomial bound in the missing low- or intermediate-demand ranges. ## 7. Odd levels retain the same degree window The reference is the actual spectral regularization at the fixed original root, not the raw odd endpoint. The even statement in sections 1--5 and the even low-demand identity in section 6 remain unchanged. Let N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, M=m-1, theta=pi/N and keep the original quartets E=(A,0,C,Z), F=(0,A,0,C), with A internal to these two ports. The raw E coupon is V_N(-2), while the raw F coupon is V_N(2), restricted to RIGHT. The positive reference at each port is the ACTUAL polynomial coupon F_N=V_N(-2)-N^(-2) V_N'(-2), where the derivative is spectral at the fixed root. Use its CROSS part at E and RIGHT part at F. These are the original odd supports: E has C-middle degree h<=m, and F has A-middle degree d-j>=m+1, or j<=M. The same literal continuant K_r and suffix coefficients C_(j,h) as in the even theorem describe raw E, with a_m=0. The polynomial has no terms h>m, since those paths miss the central row. The full cap formula U_j is unchanged at every j=0,...,d. Consequently the original signed coefficient after extracting A^d and then C^n Z^(d-n) is S_(N,n)=sum_(j in J_n) (-1)^j U_j C_(j,n-j), J_n=[max(0,n-m),min(M,n)] intersect Z, 0<=n<=N-2. There is no extra raw sign here because d is even. Write V_j^o for the positive F-reference cap coefficient. Its path lies entirely ABOVE the central row when j<=M. Its raw endpoint coefficient therefore vanishes; the spectral derivative removes its one unused zero factor. The exact positive coefficient is V_j^o=N^(-2) product_(r=0,...,d-j-1; r!=m) a_r product_(r=d-j+1,...,d) s_r^2. (12) The minus sign in F_N converts the negative spectral derivative to the displayed positive product. Equivalently this follows from the positive u-derivative in H_(V_N(-2-u)), with its coefficient N^(-2). Let Cbar_(j,h) be the genuine CROSS coefficient of H_(F_N) at E. The odd positive path expansion proves Cbar_(j,h)>=C_(j,h)>=0. Define the actual positive comparator after the same demands by D^o_(N,n)=sum_(j in J_n) V_j^o Cbar_(j,n-j). For every odd N>=3 and ceil(3N/4-3/2)<=n<=N-2, we claim |S_(N,n)|<=4N D^o_(N,n). (13) For a singleton J_n the argument below reduces to its endpoint term. Otherwise n>=m and J_n=[L,M], L=n-m. The exact monomer injection is unchanged: for j=L,...,M-1 and h=n-j, C_(j+1,h-1)>=s_h^2/a_(h-1) C_(j,h). Its denominator is positive because h<=m and h-1<m; the unused row removed from the suffix is N-h>m. Thus the central zero is never divided out. With a=(j+1)theta, b=h theta, epsilon=theta/2 the original summands T_j=U_j C_(j,n-j) satisfy T_(j+1)/T_j >=[sin(a)sin(b)/(sin(a+epsilon)cos(b-epsilon))]^2. The stated threshold is n-m+1>=N/4. Hence a>=pi/4 and b>=pi/4+theta, which is stronger than b>=pi/4+epsilon. All denominator angles stay in the positive sine/cosine range, since j+1<=M and h<=m. The two increasing sine ratios, evaluated at a=pi/4 and b=pi/4+epsilon, have product one. Therefore T_j is increasing on the original J_n, and its alternating sum has modulus at most T_M. The endpoint normalization is exact, not merely asymptotic. The standard full sine products and reflection give product_(r=0)^(m-1) a_r=N, product_(r=1)^m s_r^2=N, s_m^2=4cos^2(theta/2). The first identity follows because the two noncentral halves have equal products and their total product is N^2. Formula (12) at j=M gives V_M^o=N^(-2) N [N/s_m^2]=1/[4cos^2(theta/2)]. For U_M, its numerator and denominator products are respectively product_(r=1)^(m-1) sin^2(r theta) =N/[2^(N-1) cos^2(theta/2)], product_(r=0)^(m-1) sin^2((r+1/2)theta)=2^(1-N). Thus U_M=N/cos^2(theta/2)=4N V_M^o. Combining monotone alternation with the original endpoint term yields |S_(N,n)|<=U_M C_(M,n-M) =4N V_M^o C_(M,n-M) <=4N D^o_(N,n), which is (13). For N=3 only the singleton case occurs, and the same exact products give U_0/V_0^o=12. No small-level exception is omitted. The original even theorem and (13) consequently cover the SAME degree range at all N>=3, with constant one at even levels and factor4N at odd levels. The odd reference and its different CROSS cutoff remain explicit. This is a signed two-port coefficient estimate at the stated spectra, not a whole-source bound or a general volume-conjecture conclusion. The source input is the [original odd regularized numerator](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), sections 1--2: the literal derivative sign, noncentral product N^2, genuine supports, and coefficientwise P0<=H_(F_N). The all-index cap formula follows by the same unused-row reflection as in section 6; its full gamma product is 4 at both parities. No new finite audit or numerical asymptotic experiment is used. ## 8. Low demand still detects the actual Casimir Jordan data This final section concerns an EVEN-level source obstruction to a coupon-uniform semisimple adapter. It does not obstruct the particular fixed-resolvent signed inequality or a non-intertwining positive realization. Use even N=2m>=4, d=N-1, M=m-1 and the original two-port incidence E=(A,0,C,Z), F=(0,A,0,C). For arbitrary polynomial Casimir coupons f,g define the actual low-demand functional Lambda_n(f,g)=[A^d C^n Z^(d-n)] H_f(0,A,0,C) H_g(A,0,C,Z), 0<=n<=M. (14) The full homogeneous source fixes every raw normalization in (14). It is legitimate to study unprojected coupons here. In the fixed pair f=V(2), g=V(-2), the original RIGHT/CROSS projections are automatically satisfied after these degrees are extracted, as section 6's low-demand identity proves. The following proposed stronger realization is impossible: a semisimple realization of the ACTUAL E Casimir on a space, satisfying its original annihilating polynomial chi_N, which computes (14) uniformly for polynomial g by replacing g(Omega_E) with that same polynomial of the semisimple operator. Boundary vectors/functionals and the other coupon may be arbitrary. A finite-dimensional self-adjoint restriction or quotient intertwining the actual Casimir and preserving all these polynomial-coupon observables would be a special case. No assumption about a particular choice of positive inner product is needed for the obstruction. ### A literal nonzero nilpotent coupon The actual annihilating polynomial at even levels is chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2=4T_m(z/2)^2. The original complete-circle polynomial is L_N(z)=(-1)^d U_d(z/2) =(-1)^d 2T_m(z/2) U_(m-1)(z/2). (15) Here T and U are the ordinary Chebyshev polynomials with their displayed arguments; U_d(z/2) is monic. Thus L_N vanishes at every distinct root of chi_N. Also L_N^2 is a multiple of chi_N, so its value on the actual pair Casimir is square-zero. It need not be zero because the actual source retains confluent data. For any semisimple operator X with chi_N(X)=0, one has L_N(X)=0. Therefore a coupon-uniform realization of the type in the preceding definition would force Lambda_n(1,L_N)=0. We now check the opposite statement in the original source at every low remaining degree. ### Every original low degree detects this coupon The identity at F specializes to H_1(0,A,0,C)=A^d. Consequently (14) becomes exactly Lambda_n(1,L_N)=[C^n Z^(d-n)]H_(L_N)(0,0,C,Z). (16) The [original complete-channel identity](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) is H_(L_N)(x,b,c,y) =N sum_(a=0)^M k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y) Ptilde_(d-2a)(x,y), (17) where k_a beta_a^2>0. Each D_a is the actual positive-definite determinant polynomial and every homogeneous degree-a coefficient in its three variables is strictly positive. The retained polynomial Ptilde_s has strictly positive coefficients; at a=M, s=1 and Ptilde_1(x,y)=x+y. The [positive determinant theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md) proves these exact finite source identities, not coefficient-entropy assertions. After the specialization in (16), the a=M summand in (17) contains N k_M beta_M^2 D_M(0,0,Z) D_M(0,C,Z) Z. The first determinant is a strictly positive multiple of Z^M, and the second has a strictly positive coefficient at every C^n Z^(M-n), 0<=n<=M. Their product therefore contributes positively to C^n Z^(d-n), since 2M+1=d. All other summands in (17) are nonnegative. It follows that Lambda_n(1,L_N)>0 for EVERY 0<=n<=M. (18) As a normalization check, Lambda_0(1,L_N)=N^2. The highest-degree term of L_N is (-1)^d z^d; producing the pure outer monomial Z^d from the actual face operator requires all d lowering steps and gives another (-1)^d times product_(r=1)^d s_r^2=N^2. Lower powers cannot produce that outer degree. The two signs cancel. Equations (15) and (18) contradict the proposed coupon-uniform semisimple realization. In particular the low original coefficient filtration has not annihilated the complete-circle nilpotent. This is an all-even-level/all-low-degree source statement, not a numerical example or an unconditioned coefficient obstruction. ### Scope of the obstruction The actual signed target uses the particular pair V(2),V(-2). The proof does not exclude an identity specialized to this pair, a positive representation that does not intertwine arbitrary Casimir polynomials, or a bound that retains explicit Jordan corrections. It does exclude calling such a construction an actual semisimple Casimir restriction while also claiming preservation of every polynomial-coupon observable in (14). No estimate for the signed coefficient, no hyperbolic-volume statement, and no obstruction to the original volume conjecture is inferred. The only inputs are the actual homogeneous source, its full complete polynomial with confluent data, and the exact positive determinant formula, all already . ## Inputs The exact normalization and local incidence are those of the [original two-port source reduction](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). The full-interval source used in section 6 is the [original four-state source identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md); its [homogeneous physical adapter](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) keeps the original pair order and all matrix data. The obstruction is to a coupon-uniform semisimple adapter. It does not rule out a special identity for the fixed coupon or an explicit treatment of confluent terms.

title: Exact incidence for a cap/CROSS contraction, and what planarity does not force
text: # Exact incidence for a cap/CROSS contraction, and what planarity does not force 31 October 2026. **analytical research lemma.** Unpublished. This concerns the original marked source and the fixed spectral pair (+2,-2). No general spectral-neighborhood estimate or filled-volume conclusion is asserted. ## 1. The literal two-port condition is quadrangulation degree two Let T be the original simple white triangulated sphere, with its recorded pairing of triangles across MATCHING edges. Deleting those edges gives the original simple MAIN quadrangulation Q, with four distinct vertices on every port disk. Fix the original protected MAIN pair u,v. Name one residual cap as \[ F=(u,A,v,C),\qquad (u,A,C),\ (u,v,C),\qquad \text{matching edge }uC. \tag{1} \] The ordinary middle A is overloaded; C is the ordinary outer. LEFT, RIGHT and outer-reflected conventions have the identical incidence statement after relabeling. The protected vertices are still u,v, not new zeros introduced by a contraction. For any vertex a, let d_T(a) be its triangle valence and let m_T(a) count matching edges incident to it. Then its number of original port incidences is \[ d_Q(a)=d_T(a)-m_T(a). \tag{2} \] Each incident matching spoke joins exactly two consecutive triangles into one port; all other incident triangles contribute their own port. The four-distinct-vertices condition means that a port is counted once at a, never twice. Formula (2) also follows by deleting the matching spokes from the cyclic link of a. The following are equivalent for the cap child A: * A occurs in no port other than F and one further port E; * d_Q(A)=2; * d_T(A)=3 and its unique matching spoke is AZ, where Z is the third vertex in the link of A besides u,C. In that case the two remaining triangles at A are \[ (A,C,Z),\qquad(A,u,Z), \] paired across AZ. Hence the other port is exactly \[ E=(A,u,C,Z). \tag{3} \] up to the original middle/outer reflection conventions. This is the source typing required by the all-demand theorem after u=v=0. For completeness, if A occurs at F and E only, F contains one triangle at A because A is its middle. E contains at most two. A vertex of a simple triangulated sphere has at least three triangles, so there are exactly three and E contains the other two, paired across AZ. The converse follows immediately from this full cyclic star. Equivalently, each matching spoke consumes two triangles and F consumes one unpaired triangle, so d_Q(A)=2 forces d_T(A)=3 and m_T(A)=1. Valence three ALONE is not sufficient. The other two triangles can instead pair separately across uZ and CZ. Then all three spokes at A are MAIN and A belongs to three ports. For example, take the triangular bipyramid with apices A,B and equator u,C,Z, match its three equator edges, and mark MAIN edge uB. Its cap candidate is (u,A,B,C), while the other ports are (u,A,B,Z) and (C,A,B,Z), with harmless frame reflections if needed. Here d_T(A)=3 but d_Q(A)=3. This is an exact combinatorial distinction, not an assertion that this candidate is a high-value stationary cap. ## 2. At the classified maximum, the degree-two neighbor is CROSS Assume the positive-value maximum classification: all ordinary incidences have positive load, ordinary demands are one, and ports are complete strict CROSS, strict straddling Green, or residual marked caps. At (1), its common positive weights satisfy L_A=L_C and the cap loads are q_A=1-nu, q_C=nu with 0<nu<1/2. If d_Q(A)=2, the neighboring port has (3). A protected middle cannot be overloaded. The only possible Green child at E is therefore C. But its strict Green relation would imply L_C>L_A+L_Z, contradicting L_C=L_A. Thus E cannot be Green. If Z is ordinary, E has only one protected vertex and cannot be a residual cap either. Consequently E is strict CROSS at spectrum -2, while F is the flat cap at +2, exactly the fixed pair of the signed contraction theorem. If Z=v is protected, the four displayed triangles are the whole tetrahedral sphere. E could then only be another cap or CROSS. Two caps saturate the two ordinary demands and have total sharp value zero; cap plus strict CROSS cannot supply the C demand. Neither occurs at the stated positive-value maximum. This also follows from the cap-cap exception in the odd MAIN-cycle theorem. For the algebraic assembly below it is harmless to allow Z=v: setting Z=0 selects the missing C^d coefficient, since M+H=N-2<d. Both projected pair polynomials are identically zero. We do not assume that every typed finite pair has an ordinary Z. There are at most two residual caps, corresponding to the two distinct triangles adjacent to the marked MAIN edge uv. If BOTH cap children have d_Q=2, their two-port patches are automatically port-disjoint at positive-value classified data. Each neighboring E is CROSS, so it cannot be the other cap. If the two E's were the same port, that port would have one protected middle and one ordinary middle C. Both caps would consequently have the same ordinary C in their (u,v,C) triangle. But the two triangles incident to uv have distinct third vertices in a simple sphere. This is impossible. Their internal child vertices are also distinct and have no incidence in the other patch. This conclusion is conditional on d_Q=2 for the cap children. The maximum classification itself has not proved that combinatorial condition. ## 3. Simultaneous replacement with arbitrary shared exterior variables Fix any finite collection of port-disjoint typed pairs (E_i,F_i), each with its own ordinary A_i internal exclusively to that pair. The two protected vertices remain the original ones. Allow C_i,Z_i to coincide with remaining variables of other patches or of the unchanged exterior; within an individual port its four actual vertices remain distinct. At the exact spectra E_i=-2, F_i=+2, retain the original CROSS and one-sided cap projections. Write \[ B_i(C_i,Z_i)=[A_i^d]\, H_{F_i,\mathrm{cap}}(+2)H_{E_i,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2). \] and B_i^ref for the positive paired reference after the SAME A_i^d extraction. At even levels this is the positive endpoint projection; at odd levels it is the actual fixed-root regularizer at both ports. The numerator is raw at both parities. The all-demand theorem supplies a factor kappa_N>=1 with log kappa_N=o(N), independent of the remaining degree n, such that \[ |B_i|_{\mathrm{coeff}}\le\kappa_N B_i^{\mathrm{ref}}. \tag{4} \] The common unit source signs do not affect (4). All remaining degree coefficients are included: n=0,...,N-2 are controlled by the theorem, and the n=d coefficient is zero on both sides. Both polynomials have degree d in their remaining two variables. The original unused factors and normalizations are part of B_i and B_i^ref. Let G_N be ANY complex polynomial in the remaining original face variables, with no A_i incidence; it can be the unchanged product of the other original spectral coupons at arbitrary fixed parameters. Denote coefficientwise absolute value by |.|_coeff, and let L^t be any remaining original target monomial. Exact extraction and the triangle inequality give \[ \left|[L^{\mathbf t}]\,G_N\prod_i B_i\right| \le\kappa_N^s[L^{\mathbf t}]\, |G_N|_{\mathrm{coeff}}\prod_i B_i^{\mathrm{ref}}, \qquad s=\#\{\text{pairs}\},\quad\log(\kappa_N^s)=o(N). \tag{5} \] Indeed the A_i extractions commute and see only their own pair. Coefficientwise absolute value is submultiplicative, and positive coefficient inequalities remain valid when remaining variables shared by different patches are identified. Thus disjoint VARIABLES C_i,Z_i are not required. The internal A_i's, however, really are exclusive: one cannot put an A_i-bearing exterior into this argument. Every target in (5) is the original target d at an ordinary face and zero at a protected face. Each extracted pair still has its original remaining degree d. This is a conditional original-sector replacement, not a topological smoothing, an identity coupon insertion, or a proof that the reference/exterior contraction is below hyperbolic volume. It also gives no open spectral neighborhood of the pair (+2,-2), so it is not by itself a whole Fourier-period bound. ## 4. A structural obstruction to a universal two-port elimination Neither spherical planarity nor the original matching forces a degree-two cap child. The family of bipyramids makes this failure explicit without a knot scan. Let T be the bipyramid over an n-cycle, n>=3, with apices A,B and equatorial vertices z_0,...,z_(n-1). Pair the two triangles on each equatorial edge. The MAIN quadrangulation is the embedded K_(2,n), with ports \[ (z_i,A,B,z_{i+1}) \] up to cyclic frame choice. All quadrilaterals have four distinct vertices, and T is simple. Every MAIN mark joins one apex and one equatorial vertex. For mark B z_0, either possible residual cap has overloaded child A, whose original port-incidence degree is n. For mark A z_0 the roles reverse. Hence for n>=3 NO possible residual cap at ANY allowed MAIN mark has the required internal face. For n=3 this is already the valence-three counterexample in section 1. There are also arbitrarily large simple spherical quadrangulations with minimum degree at least three: subdivide each face of a cube into an l by l square grid, consistently across cube edges. The eight old corners have degree three and all new vertices have degree four. There are 6l^2 port disks, each with four distinct vertices. The diagonalization theorem gives simple choices and the general Morse construction gives actual sources. In EVERY choice, Q and its vertex degrees are unchanged. Thus no marked cap can meet the two-port internal-face condition anywhere in this family, for any mark. Euler only forces some quadrangulation vertex to have degree at most three, since its average degree is 4-8/V. It does not force degree two, and it certainly does not place that degree at a cap's overloaded child. The cap-edge forest and demand-one inequalities concern a different graph; they cannot delete the other original port incidences of A. These are structural obstructions to proving universal elimination solely from planarity and the known local source theorem. They are NOT examples of dominant non-CROSS maxima, counterexamples to the original volume conjecture, or a proof that a different multi-port block cannot work. A theorem forcing an applicable pair at every actual high maximum would first need an additional exclusion of caps on these incidence patterns. That exclusion is not contained in the existing activation, stationary, or odd-cycle classification. ## 5. Why an exterior A load is a genuinely different finite problem At a classified maximum all ordinary incidences are positive. If d_Q(A)>2, any selected F plus one neighboring port leaves positive A-load in the exterior. At a fixed such maximum that load is a positive constant in normalized degree, not a one-unit endpoint error. Even in the typed pair (3), keeping an exterior A-degree r changes the required extraction to A^(d-r). In the even notation of the exact original-demand convolution, the actual coefficient then becomes \[ \begin{aligned} &[C^nZ^{d+r-n}][A^{d-r}]\,H_F(+2)H_E(-2) =\text{(common unit sign)}\sum_j(-1)^jU_jC_{j-r,n-j},\\ &\max(r,n-H,0)\le j\le\min(M,n). \end{aligned} \tag{6} \] The theorem controls r=0, not all these shifted diagonals. This is not the already covered variation of the remaining degree n. In fact an unconditional shifted analogue is false. Set n=r; then the sum in (6) has only j=r and C_(0,0)=N^2. Its ratio to the paired endpoint coefficient is exactly U_r/V_r. For N divisible by eight, N>=16, and r=N/8, the original sine products give \[ \frac{U_r}{V_r} =\prod_{j=0}^{r}\cot^2\!\left(\frac{(j+1/2)\pi}{N}\right) \ge3^{N/8+1}. \tag{7} \] This is precisely the uncontracted-pair obstruction, now expressed as the missing internal-demand shift. It uses a boundary CROSS monomial with zero ordinary incidences and therefore does NOT disprove a possible shifted estimate restricted to the positive-incidence stationary regime. It does show why (4) cannot simply be attached to an A-dependent exterior or promoted to an all-shifts identity. ## Dependencies The source bound is the [all-demand, both-parity signed contraction](research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.md), with the exact typing and coefficients in the [original-demand convolution](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). The maximum hypotheses come from the [finite-multiplier stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) and [odd MAIN-cycle theorem](research_stationary_noncross_main_cycle_obstruction.md). The actual general-source realization is the [matched-sphere Morse construction](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md); its simple-chart existence input is the [maximal-diagonalization theorem](research_maximal_diagonalization_source_gap.md). The assembly requires the stated degree-two internal faces and exact unshifted demands. It does not assert that every stationary cap has that incidence pattern. No numerical audit or purported global realization of a non-CROSS maximum is used. The false preliminary converse “valence three implies two ports” was corrected before preservation: the actual criterion is degree TWO in Q, with the matching condition retained. The conclusions are a conditional fixed-spectrum source replacement and an obstruction to a topology-only universal use of that replacement. They do not rule out an additional theorem restricting high-value stationary maxima, a larger-star contraction, or a spectral-neighborhood estimate.

title: A low-demand signed cap/CROSS contraction from the original Newton source
text: # A low-demand signed cap/CROSS contraction from the original Newton source 31 October 2026. The theorem concerns the fixed spectral pair at even levels. It retains the A-face demand, all unused factors and the genuine cutoff. It does not use a uniform-coupon semisimple model or a positive moment norm. ## 1. Original coefficients and an auxiliary full slice Let N=2m>=4, d=N-1, M=m-1, theta=pi/N. Write c_r=2cos((2r+1)theta), a_r=2+c_r, gamma_r=2-c_r, s_r=2sin(r theta), P_r=product_(j=1)^r s_j, P_0=1. Use the original C_(j,h), U_j and V_j from the [original-demand convolution](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md), extending their literal formulas to all 0<=j,h<=d where meaningful. In particular C_(j,h)=[A^j Z^(d-h-j)] K_(d-h)(A,Z) product_(r=d-h+1)^d a_r, U_j=4 P_j^2/product_(r=0)^j gamma_r, V_j=4 P_j^2/product_(r=0)^j a_r, C_(0,n)=N^2 product_(r=0)^(n-1)a_r/P_n^2 =V_(d-n). (1) For every 0<=n<=d define only as an algebraic auxiliary S_n^full=sum_(j=0)^n (-1)^j U_j C_(j,n-j). (2) For 0<=n<=M this is exactly the original projected cap/CROSS sum S_(N,n), because its J_n is 0..n. No equality with the projected sum is asserted for n>M. The new identity is gamma_n S_n^full+s_n^2 S_(n-1)^full=4 C_(0,n), 0<=n<=d, S_(-1)^full=0. (3) In particular it keeps the original top-boundary coefficient that was undetermined by the previous C_(j,h) recurrence. ## 2. Literal three-port completion and its turn dictionary Use the actual two-bridge slot word [1,0,1], with first top cap marked. Its ordered face quartets are E=(A,u,C,Z), F=(u,A,v,C), G=(v,C,u,Z), with protected faces u=v=0. At E put the actual V_N(-2), at F the actual V_N(2), and at G put g_n(Omega)=product_(r=0)^(n-1)(Omega-c_r). The specialization of G is (0,C,0,Z). In the original face operator, (-T-c_(d-r)) acting on C^(d-r) has only the monomer transition -s_(d-r)^2 Z C^(d-r-1). Since c_(d-r)=c_r and s_(d-r)=s_(r+1), successive factors give EXACTLY H_(g_n)(0,C,0,Z)=(-1)^n P_n^2 C^(d-n) Z^n. (4) Thus the unchanged targets A^d C^d Z^d select (2), and the raw marked scalar of this three-port completion is Z(E,F,g_n)=(-1)^(d+n) P_n^2 S_n^full =(-1)^(n+1) P_n^2 S_n^full. (5) Here the raw E(-2) source is (-1)^d times its positive endpoint polynomial. The full F(2) monomer coefficient is (-1)^j U_j. Equation (4) is a genuine polynomial coupon, not a sector projector. For completeness the exact rational-tangle dictionary needed below is Z(E,F,G)=phi(G R(F R(E))), (6) where R is the genuine UNSCALED original quarter-turn and phi(B)=N^-1 Tr[(I tensor g)B] is the original marked Frobenius functional. This identity includes all original turns and their scalar factors. It can be verified directly as follows. Put x=q^d. Label the bottom physical pairs (s,d-s),(b,d-b); the successive box entries are E_(t,v;d-s,b), F_(d-a,u;s,t), G_(a,b;u,v). The unwrapped conservation laws force the first top pair to be (d-a,a). Two original cups, the first marked cap and the remaining ordinary cap contribute N^-1 x^(s+a+2b-2d). On the right side of (6), expand R(B)_(a,b;c,e)=x^(a-e) B_(d-a,c;b,d-e), g_b=x^(2b-d). Expanding the right side of (6) in its literal matrix order first gives N^-1 sum x^(u+h+2b-2d) G_(a,b;u,v) F_(d-u,a;h,k) E_(d-h,v;k,b). The actual root pair Casimir, and hence every polynomial F in it, is symmetric and invariant under the simultaneous swap/complement J(a,b)=(d-b,d-a). Explicitly, F_(r,s;p,t)=F_(p,t;r,s) =F_(d-s,d-r;d-t,d-p). The latter identity can be checked directly on the original diagonal and two transition entries: under U->Q^-1 V^-1, V->Q^-1 U^-1, the diagonal and corresponding upward/downward transition coefficients are unchanged. It then holds for all powers and polynomials, including every Jordan component. Apply both identities to obtain F_(d-u,a;h,k)=F_(d-a,u;d-k,d-h). Set s=d-k, t=d-h. The E entry becomes exactly E_(t,v;d-s,b). Unwrapped conservation in this F entry gives d-a+u=s+t, so its phase becomes x^(u+h+2b-2d)=x^(s+a+2b-2d). Thus all three matrix entries and the original turn/mark factor agree term by term with the physical contraction above. This proves (6) before spectral evaluation or the Newton change of coordinates. No generic semisimple recoupling or reset mark is used. ## 3. Original Newton algebra gives the recurrence Use the [genuine Newton packet](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) Bhat_r(z)=product_(j=0)^(r-1)(c_j-z)/P_r^2, R Bhat_r=Bhat_(d-r), phi(Bhat_i Bhat_j)=1_(i+j=d). Multiplication by z in these coordinates is the full lower-bidiagonal matrix Z_N: (Z_N)_(r,r)=c_r, (Z_N)_(r,r-1)=-s_r^2, Z_N^T=P_rev Z_N P_rev. (7) All repeated roots and Jordan data remain. If alpha_E is the Newton coefficient column of E, then (6) and the displayed transpose relation imply Z(E,F,G)=alpha_E^T F(Z_N) P_rev alpha_G. (8) For E=V_N(-2) the divided-difference formula for the ACTUAL numerator gives (alpha_E)_r=-V_r. Indeed chi_N(-2)=4 at even levels, and the coefficient is 4(-1)^r P_r^2/product_(j=0)^r(-2-c_j)=-V_r. For G=g_n, alpha_G=(-1)^n P_n^2 e_n. For F=V_N(2), the FULL minimal-polynomial identity chi_N(Z_N)=0 gives F(Z_N)=4(2I-Z_N)^(-1), (9) because chi_N(2)=4 and every gamma_r>0. Combining (5),(8),(9) cancels the exact nonzero factor (-1)^(n+1)P_n^2 and yields S_n^full=V^T [4(2I-Z_N)^(-1)] e_(d-n). (10) Let w^T=V^T[4(2I-Z_N)^(-1)]. Its defining identity w^T(2I-Z_N)=4V^T gives gamma_j w_j+s_(j+1)^2 w_(j+1)=4V_j. Set j=d-n and use (1), c_(d-n)=c_n, and s_(d-n+1)=s_n. This is exactly (3). No norm estimate or total-variation bound for this inverse has been inserted. Equivalently, the explicit inverse of the bidiagonal matrix gives S_n^full=4 sum_(h=0)^n (-1)^(n-h) C_(0,h) product_(r=h+1)^n s_r^2 /product_(r=h)^n gamma_r. (11) This is an exact fixed-pair signed summation identity, with cancellation retained. ## 4. A macroscopic low-demand contraction Define the same normalized scalar as the fixed-resolvent reduction, R_n=gamma_n S_n^full/(4 C_(0,n)). Since C_(0,n)/C_(0,n-1)=a_(n-1)/s_n^2, (3) becomes the INHOMOGENEOUS scalar recurrence R_0=1, R_n=1-t_n R_(n-1), t_n=s_n^4/[a_(n-1)gamma_(n-1)] =4sin^4(n theta)/sin^2((2n-1)theta). (12) The n=0 convention agrees with the original R definition. This is not a scalar orthogonal-polynomial assertion. For every even N>=4, |R_n|<=1, 0<=n<=floor(N/4). (13) Here is a direct proof, including the small levels. The positive function t(v)=4sin^4(v theta)/sin^2((2v-1)theta) is increasing for 1<=v<=M: its logarithmic derivative is 4theta[cot(v theta)-cot((2v-1)theta)]>=0. If N=4k+2, then theta<=pi/6 and t_k=(1-sin theta)^2/cos^2(2theta)<=1, because sin theta<=1/2. Thus all k successive maps in (12) preserve [0,1]. If N=4k, every n<=k-1 has t_n<=1 by comparison with v=k-1/2 (for k>=2 the same preceding inequality applies). The final coefficient is t_k=sec^2 theta<=2. Therefore the first k-1 values lie in [0,1], and R_k belongs to [1-sec^2 theta,1] subset [-1,1]. At N=4 there is no preliminary step and R_1=-1 directly. At N=6, R_1=0. This proves (13). Throughout this range n<=M, the full slice is the genuine original projected sum. Its endpoint comparator D_(N,n) is a sum of positive terms and contains V_0 C_(0,n), where V_0=4/a_0. Hence |S_(N,n)| <=4 C_(0,n)/gamma_n <=[a_0/gamma_n] D_(N,n) <=N^2 D_(N,n), 0<=n<=floor(N/4). (14) The sharper factor a_0/gamma_n is bounded independently of N on every fixed macroscopic interval rho N<=n<=N/4, rho>0. The raw coefficient differs only by (-1)^d. The original A^d extraction and remaining C,Z exponents have not changed. ## 5. Exact scope and validation Equation (3) holds for the full auxiliary slices, while the bound (14) applies to the original projected cap/CROSS coefficient in the stated low-demand range at even levels. It is complementary to the separately proved [high-demand theorem](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md). It does not yet cover N/4<n<=M, the middle cutoffs n>M, or the odd-level source. The forward recurrence can be unstable when t_n>1, so (13) must not be extrapolated without a further argument. A simple uniform bound for the actual full inverse in (10) is neither proved nor required. The proof inputs are the original-demand convolution, the [full homogeneous face theorem](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), the literal root swap/complement symmetry, and the genuine Newton turn/Frobenius identities. The literal physical-index verification (6) supplies the source adapter. A focused independent direct calculation of the original K recurrence at 90 digits checked (3) for all full slices at N=4,6,8,10,12,16,20 (76 coefficients); maximum relative residual below 6e-81. This is a finite identity check, not the proof of the general estimate. A separate [portable exact-field audit](../experiments/audit_research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction_results.json), independently contracts the actual three-port physical tensors at four even levels. It verifies 28 original marked scalars, 28 full auxiliary recurrences, 14 original low-cutoff identifications and 28 Newton resolvent entries. These finite checks support the source dictionary; inequality (14) is proved analytically above. The stated low-demand range and parity restrictions remain essential. In particular, the omitted top coefficient belongs to the actual source and cannot be restored from an auxiliary recurrence. Additional source reference: [full physical pair commutant and genuine marked trace](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md), sections 2–4.

title: Odd raw source: the same low-demand recurrence and contour bound
text: # Odd raw source: the same low-demand recurrence and contour bound 31 October 2026. The even theorem is recorded separately. The regularized odd coupon is used only in the positive endpoint comparator; the signed numerator remains the raw pair \(V_N(-2),V_N(2)\). ## 1. Original odd supports and an all-parity Newton identity Let \(N=2m+1\ge3\), \(d=2m\), \(M=m-1\), and \(\theta=\pi/N\). Retain the actual quartets \(E=(A,0,C,Z)\), \(F=(0,A,0,C)\), with the same original \(A^d\) demand as in [the odd high-demand source](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md). Put \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta)\), \(a_j=2+c_j\), \(\gamma_j=2-c_j\), \(s_j=2\sin(j\theta)\), and \[ B_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r^2,\qquad v_j=B_j\prod_{h=j+1}^d a_h . \] The sole zero \(a_m=0\) is never replaced or divided out. There is an exact all-parity Newton coefficient formula \[ (\alpha_{V_N(\sigma)})_j =(-1)^j B_j\prod_{h=j+1}^d(\sigma-c_h). \tag{1} \] Indeed, first take \(\sigma\) off all nodes. The divided difference of \(V_N(\sigma;z)=(\chi_N(z)-\chi_N(\sigma))/(z-\sigma)\) at \(c_0,\ldots,c_j\) is \(\chi_N(\sigma)/\prod_{r=0}^j(\sigma-c_r)\), the displayed tail product. This is polynomial in \(\sigma\), so it extends to every node, retaining all confluent derivatives. Consequently \[ \alpha_{V_N(-2),j}=(-1)^d v_j. \tag{2} \] At odd level this is \(+v_j\); it vanishes for \(j<m\) and is strictly positive for \(j\ge m\). For every \(0\le n\le d\) define the auxiliary full slice \[ S_n^{\mathrm{full}}=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jU_j C_{j,n-j}, \qquad U_j=4B_j/\prod_{r=0}^j\gamma_r. \tag{3} \] The unused-product convention gives \(C_{j,h}=0\) if \(h>m\). The original odd projected sum uses \[ J_n=\{\max(0,n-m),\ldots,\min(M,n)\}. \tag{4} \] For \(0\le n\le M\), both sums have exactly \(0\le j\le n\). Thus the auxiliary equals the original raw sum in the needed low range. No above-\(M\) identification is asserted. The physical three-port completion and its swap/complement turn identity in [the Newton source proof](research_cap_cross_low_demand_newton_contraction.md) hold at every level. With \(g_n=\prod_{r<n}(\Omega-c_r)\), its raw marked scalar is \((-1)^{d+n}B_nS_n^{\mathrm{full}}\). The genuine Newton turn, (2), and \(\alpha_{g_n}=(-1)^nB_ne_n\) give the same sign times \(B_n v^T V_N(2;Z_N)e_{d-n}\). Since \(\chi_N(2)=4\) at every level and every \(\gamma_j>0\), this proves \[ S_n^{\mathrm{full}}=v^T[4(2I-Z_N)^{-1}]e_{d-n}. \tag{5} \] No division by the odd value \(\chi_N(-2)=0\) occurs. The bidiagonal resolvent equation and literal row reflection yield \[ \gamma_n S_n^{\mathrm{full}}+s_n^2S_{n-1}^{\mathrm{full}} =4v_{d-n}=4C_{0,n},\qquad S_{-1}^{\mathrm{full}}=0, \qquad C_{0,n}=\frac{N^2}{B_n}\prod_{h=0}^{n-1}a_h . \tag{6} \] Here \(B_nB_{d-n}=N^2\), and the reflected unused product is exactly the last product. This forcing is nonzero for \(n\le M\). Therefore the original raw odd coefficient obeys \[ R_n=\frac{\gamma_n S_{N,n}}{4C_{0,n}},\qquad R_0=1,\quad R_n=1-t_nR_{n-1},\quad t_n=\frac{4\sin^4(n\theta)}{\sin^2((2n-1)\theta)}. \tag{7} \] No extra regularization factor appears in this raw recurrence. ## 2. The contour proof permits half-integral \(N/2\) Apply [the even full-low contour proof](research_cap_cross_full_low_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) to \(P_j=\prod_{r=1}^jt_r\), \(A_j=P_j^{-1}\). In its Gamma factorization replace the parameter \(m\) by \(N/2\), now half-integral. Every exact factorization and shifted Euler--Maclaurin formula remains valid. The largest row here is \(M=N/2-3/2\), so all Gamma real-part bounds on the contour \([-1/4,n+1/4]\times[-NY,NY]\) are at least as strong. The relative nodal error remains at most \(e^{-6N/5}\), and the leading analytic action remains \(2f(z/N)\). Replace the parity-specific sine-product bound on \(P_j\) by the already proved uniform real-node estimate \[ \log P_j=-2Nf(j/N)+O(\log N). \tag{8} \] Its proof uses the explicit Gamma factors, smooth interpolation and uniform Stirling estimate, independently of any prior bound on \(P_j\). Since \(f\ge0\) on \([0,1/2]\), this gives \(P_j\le N^C\) uniformly. That polynomial bound suffices on the left/top/bottom contour and for the nodal replacement error. The right edge still has the exact rate cancellation supplied by (8). Thus the same fixed-\(Y\), then \(N\to\infty\), then \(Y\to\infty\) argument proves \[ \limsup_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ {\mathrm{odd}}}} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le (N-3)/2}|R_n|\le0. \tag{9} \] No row-interior coefficient lower theorem is used. ## 3. The actual regularized endpoint comparator Use exactly the original odd reference \[ F_N=V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2). \] Let \(\overline C_{j,h}\) be its CROSS coefficient at \(E\), and \(V_j^o\) its RIGHT coefficient at \(F\). The positive path expansion gives \(\overline C_{j,h}\ge C_{j,h}\ge0\). At \(j=0\), the unused-row derivative removes the sole central zero and yields \[ V_0^o=N^{-2}\prod_{\substack{0\le r\le d-1\\r\ne m}}a_r =\frac1{a_d}=\frac1{a_0}, \tag{10} \] since \(\prod_{r\ne m}a_r=N^2\). The actual positive comparator \[ D_{N,n}^o=\sum_{j\in J_n}V_j^o\overline C_{j,n-j} \] contains its \(j=0\) term for \(n\le M\). Hence \[ \frac{|S_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}^o} \le\frac{4a_0}{\gamma_n}|R_n| \le4N^2|R_n| . \tag{11} \] Combining (9) and (11) proves \[ \limsup_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ {\mathrm{odd}}}} \frac1N\log\max_{0\le n\le (N-3)/2} \frac{|S_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}^o}\le0. \tag{12} \] Regularization occurs only in the comparator. The numerator, its support, spectral pair, and all original face demands stay raw. ## Validation and open scope A private exact-field specialization of the physical three-port audit checked \(N=3,5,7,9\): 24 original physical scalars, 24 full auxiliary recurrences, 10 explicit low-cutoff identifications, and 24 Newton resolvent entries. It uses the literal tail product (1)--(2), never a division by \(a_m\). The [portable audit](../experiments/audit_research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.py) has [recorded results](../experiments/research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension_results.json). These checks support only the parity/source dictionary, not the analytic estimate (9). No polynomial full-low estimate, nearby-spectral bound, or projected middle-demand conclusion is inferred.

title: A full spectral-strip gap for an original cap and its whole CROSS star

# A full spectral-strip gap for an original cap and its whole CROSS star 31 October 2026. The cap varies in a small complex disk about +2; every neighboring CROSS spectrum may range over the entire real fold with a sufficiently thin fixed complex strip. This is a relative weighted-star theorem, not an absolute Phi_D bound. The face targets and both parity cutoffs are unchanged. ## 1. Original source and theorem Let F=(u,A,v,C) be an original marked cap, with u=v=0 and A,C ordinary. Include EVERY other original A-incident port in a product of k genuine CROSS coupons. The valence k is fixed with the original diagram but otherwise arbitrary. Remove the fixed common raw signs and write \[  egin{aligned} P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(A,Y)&=\prod_eP_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(A,Y;\sigma(\delta_e)),\ \sigma(\delta)&=-2\cos(2\pi\delta),\ P_N^0(A,Y)&=P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(A,Y) ig|_{ oldsymbol\delta=0}. \end{aligned}	ag{1} \] The endpoint product has nonnegative coefficients at both parities. All shared variables remain identified. The actual finite CROSS degree projections are unchanged as the spectra vary. Fix positive ordinary radii, protected variables exactly zero, with L_A=L_C. Write P_N^+(a)=P_N^0(a,L_Y). The actual endpoint weighted action has the locally uniform real limit \[  rac1N\log P_N^+(L_Ce^t)\longrightarrow F(t),\qquad F	ext{ differentiable at }0,\qquad0<
u:=F'(0)< rac12.	ag{2} \] The derivative condition is the substantive scalar hypothesis. At a classified stationary cap with only CROSS neighbors it follows from the SAME original demand: L_A=L_C and F'(0)=sum_(e!=F) q_(e,A)=1-q_(F,A)=nu in (0,1/2). Put d=N-1 and M=floor(N/2)-1. For cap spectrum sigma the original projected polynomial and the extracted star are \[  egin{aligned} H_{F,\mathrm{cap}}(A,C;\sigma)&=\sum_{j=0}^M(-1)^jb_j(\sigma)A^{d-j}C^j,\ B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)&=[A^d]H_{F,\mathrm{cap}}P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] **Theorem.** There are fixed epsilon_*>0, h_*>0, eta>0 and N_0 such that \[ \sup_{\substack{|\sigma-2|\le\varepsilon_*\,,\ |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le h_*\ \operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in\mathbb R\,,\ |Y_f|=L_f}} |B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)| \le e^{-\eta N}P_N^+(L_C),\qquad N\ge N_0.	ag{4} \] Both parities and every remaining face phase are included. This extracts exactly the original A^d against the WHOLE neighboring product; it is not a shifted demand or an independent allocation at each neighbor. ## 2. Root-safe cap factors and the exact global CROSS majorant Set theta=pi/N and \[  egin{aligned} c_j&=2\cos((2j+1)	heta),&s_j&=2\sin(j	heta),\ B_j&=\prod_{r=1}^js_r^2,&b_j(\sigma)&=B_j\prod_{r=j+1}^d(\sigma-c_r),\ U_j&=b_j(2),&\gamma_j&=2-c_j>0. \end{aligned} \] These are the full original unused-row products, also at repeated spectral roots. They satisfy the polynomial relation \[ (\sigma-c_{j+1})b_{j+1}(\sigma)=s_{j+1}^2b_j(\sigma).	ag{5} \] For j<=M, the explicit increasing-sine ratios give U_j<=U_0=csc^2(theta/2)<=C N^2. Since product gamma_j=4 and chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, for |sigma-2|<=epsilon_s, \[ |b_j(\sigma)|\le U_j\prod_{r>j}\left(1+ rac{\varepsilon_s}{\gamma_r}ight) \le CN^2e^{N\kappa_s},\qquad \kappa_s=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+\varepsilon_s/2).	ag{6} \] There is no division by b_j, chi_N, or a varying spectral factor. This polynomial estimate is used near every endpoint or sampled zero outside the strict row interval below. The original cofactor interpolation theorem supplies the stronger, GLOBAL coefficientwise CROSS bound, on any fixed strip |Im delta|<=T, \[ |P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(\sigma(\delta))|_{\mathrm{coeff}} \le C_T\log^2(N+1)e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|} P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2).	ag{7} \] This is equation (27) of [the original cofactor factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), section 8, not an inferred coefficient lower asymptotic. Its nodal positivity covers ALL j,a<=J: for j<=a it is the direct positive original recurrence; for j>a it is the retained physical tail adapter. Thus the plain coefficient majorant includes j=J-1 at all nodes. Its central coefficientwise comparisons use (x+y)^2>=2xy, with the original forced outer units retained. Taking products in (7), even when face variables are shared, yields \[ |P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}|_{\mathrm{coeff}} \le Q_N\exp\!\left(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|ight)P_N^0.	ag{8} \] where Q_N is a fixed polynomial upper bound in N on a fixed strip. For later rate estimates put \[ \omega=\kappa_s+2\pi\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|.	ag{9} \] ## 3. Actual MAIN-edge angular loss on the whole neighbor fold The triangle on the opposite side of original MAIN edge AC from (u,A,C) belongs to a different port in P_N^delta. It contains the two supported positive variables A,C. Fix phi_0 in (0,pi/8) and a small radial interval |t|<=T_0. The cofactor angular theorem gives gamma>0 and a FIXED strip height h_0>0 such that \[  egin{aligned} |P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^{t+i\phi},Y)| &\le CN^K\exp\!\left(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|-\gamma Night)P_N^+(L_Ce^t),\ \phi_0\le|\phi|\le\pi,\quad |t|&\le T_0,\quad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le h_0, \quad\operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in\mathbb R,\quad |Y_f|=L_f. \end{aligned}	ag{10} \] Here C on the left is the actual complex face value. Thus A and C have precisely the stated phase difference regardless of other face phases. No phase is assigned to a protected zero. To verify (10) against the actual source, put u=-4sin^2(pi delta). At even N=2m the central formula is \[  egin{gathered} s_m^2(x+y)D_bD_c+s_ms_{m-1}xy(D_bE_c+E_bD_c),\ D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u),\qquad E_b=(a_{m-1}+u)R_{m-2}(b;u). \end{gathered} \] At odd N=2m+1 it is \[ G_bG_c+u s_ms_{m+1}xyD_bD_c,\qquad G_b=R_m(b;u),\quad D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u).	ag{11} \] The skipped-central odd term is retained. Every central summand has a cofactor on the actual AC side, at index J or J-1. On that side the actual angular theorem gives C N^K exp(-gamma N)R_j(positive;0), uniformly on the entire real fold and its fixed thin strip. The J-1 case includes the theorem's omitted-node extra-factor/division argument and its polynomial cost; no logarithmic angular prefactor is being claimed. On the other side apply the exact coefficient interpolation/Bernstein bound. The remaining central factors are bounded on that strip. At positive radii use, at even levels, D_b(0)>=s_(m-1)^2(x+y)R_(m-2)(b;0) and (x+y)^2>=2xy; at odd levels use G_b(0)>=s_m^2(x+y)D_b(0) and G_b(0)G_c(0)>=2s_m^4 xyD_b(0)D_c(0). These compare every central term to the actual positive endpoint kernel without division by a small diagonal or central zero. This proves (10); the other star ports use (7). Shrinking the strip later preserves all these fixed constants. ## 4. Total-degree tails and fixed choices of radii Choose delta_j>0 such that \[ 0<
u-2\delta_j<
u+2\delta_j< rac12,\qquad l=\lceil N(
u-\delta_j)ceil,\quad r=\lfloor N(
u+\delta_j)floor. \] For sufficiently large N, 0<l<=r<r+1<=M. Differentiability in (2) gives fixed t_-<0<t_+, as small as desired, and beta>0 with \[  egin{aligned} F(t_-)-(
u-\delta_j)t_-&\le F(0)- eta,\ F(t_+)-(
u+\delta_j)t_+&\le F(0)- eta. \end{aligned}	ag{12} \] Choose them also within (-T_0,T_0), and so small that \[ F(t)-vt\le F(0)+\gamma/4, \] for t between 0 and either chosen radius, and v in {nu-delta_j,nu+delta_j}. Continuity gives this extra condition. The integer rounding of l/N and (r+1)/N costs only O(1) in logarithms. Write P_N^delta=sum_j p_j^delta(Y)A^j. Formula (3) gives the exact total-degree split j<l, l<=j<=r, and j>r, all with j<=M. Positivity of P_N^0, (6),(8), and the two Chernoff radii show that the exterior parts have bound \[ \left|\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le M\j<l\ \mathrm{or}\ j>r}} (-1)^jb_j(\sigma)C^jp_j^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Y)ight| \le\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F(0)- eta+\omega+o(1))}.	ag{13} \] For example, the lower positive tail is bounded by exp(-(l-1)t_-)P_N^+(L_C exp(t_-)); the upper one by exp(-(r+1)t_+)P_N^+(L_C exp(t_+)). No individual neighbor A allocation is restricted. Endpoint or zero spectral rows are controlled by (6), not by solving a divided recurrence there. ## 5. An exact finite analytic antidifference on the interior rows Put h=1/N. For a complex log-radius zeta set \[  egin{aligned} w_j(\zeta)&=(-1)^jb_j(\sigma)e^{-j\zeta},\ a_N(t,\zeta,\sigma)&=-e^{-\zeta}  rac{4\sin^2(\pi(t+h))}{\sigma-2\cos(2\pi(t+3h/2))}. \end{aligned}	ag{14} \] Then w_(j+1)=a_N(j/N)w_j EXACTLY by (5). On a fixed complex tube about the strict row interval and a fixed rectangle |Re zeta|<T_1, |Im zeta|<2phi_0 with T_1>T_0, the denominator stays away from zero for sigma in a sufficiently small complex disk about 2. At sigma=2, a_N converges uniformly there to -exp(-zeta). After shrinking these fixed neighborhoods if necessary, a_N-1 has a uniformly bounded analytic inverse. The original b_j can still be zero; it is never divided out. All divisions in this construction are confined to the stated bulk interval, where both the denominator in (14) and a_N-1 are uniformly nonzero. Here is the finite construction, including its error. Put \[  egin{aligned} K_N&=(a_N-1)^{-1},\ (\mathcal F_hH)(t)&=- rac{a_N(t)}{a_N(t)-1}\,[H(t+h)-H(t)],\ H_N&=\sum_{q=0}^{m_N-1}\mathcal F_h^qK_N. \end{aligned}	ag{15} \] Let rho be the row-tube radius, K a uniform bound on |a_N/(a_N-1)|, and K_0 a uniform bound on |K_N| on the larger tube and fixed parameter rectangle. Choose \[ m_N=\left\lfloor rac{ho N}{8(K+1)}ightfloor\ge1. \] Use m_N nested tubes from radius rho to rho/2. Cauchy's derivative bound makes each forward difference cost at most 2h/s, with s=rho/(2m_N), so each F_h costs at most 4Khm_N/rho<=1/2. All literal shifts stay in the preceding tube. The finite geometric identity now gives \[  egin{aligned} a_N(t)H_N(t+h)-H_N(t)&=1-e_N(t),\ e_N(t)&=(a_N(t)-1)\mathcal F_h^{m_N}K_N(t),\ |H_N|&\le2K_0,\qquad |e_N|\le Ce^{-cN}. \end{aligned}	ag{16} \] All functions are analytic in zeta and sigma on the fixed parameter rectangle; the bounds are uniform. This constructs an exact finite antidifference, not an asymptotic solution for a discrete coefficient. Consequently the original window kernel satisfies EXACTLY \[ \sum_{j=l}^rw_j =w_{r+1}H_N((r+1)/N)-w_lH_N(l/N) +\sum_{j=l}^re_N(j/N)w_j.	ag{17} \] BOTH endpoint terms remain. Each w_j retains the full b_j unused-row product, including every common sampled zero. ## 6. Exact A contour and both radial side currents The actual window coefficient is \[  rac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^{i\phi},Y) \sum_{j=l}^rw_j(i\phi)\,d\phi.	ag{18} \] This is a literal coefficient contour, not a finite grid. No alias or bound on the total degree of P_N relative to N is needed. For |phi|>=phi_0, (10) and (6) give rate at most F(0)+omega-gamma. For |phi|<=phi_0, insert (17). The residual contributes at most \[ \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F(0)+\omega-c+o(1))}.	ag{19} \] by (6),(8). No analytic interpolation of p_j has been used. Consider separately the boundary terms j=l and j=r+1. Apart from the actual scalar (-1)^j b_j(sigma), their integrand is \[ W_j(\zeta)=P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^\zeta,Y) e^{-j\zeta}H_N(j/N;\zeta,\sigma). \] It is holomorphic on the small rectangle of (14)-(16). Deform the segment zeta=i[-phi_0,phi_0] to Re zeta=t_- for j=l, and to Re zeta=t_+ for j=r+1. The exact contour identity retains BOTH joining segments, at Im zeta=+phi_0 and Im zeta=-phi_0. On the shifted vertical segment, bounded H_N, (6),(8),(12) give rate at most F(0)+omega-beta. On either joining segment, the actual A/C phase difference is exactly +/-phi_0, so (10) applies. The small-radius choice after (12) bounds the rate there by \[ F(0)+\omega-3\gamma/4.	ag{20} \] Thus BOTH endpoint terms have a strict rate improvement, and both original radial currents have been controlled, not discarded. All bounds are uniform in the other face phases. ## 7. Closing the fixed spectral neighborhoods The row interval, angular threshold, radii and positive losses beta,gamma,c were fixed using the endpoint profile before the final spectral neighborhoods were chosen. Take epsilon_* within the initial cap disk, and h_* within the initial CROSS strip, such that \[ \operatorname{arcosh}(1+\varepsilon_*/2)+2\pi k h_* < rac14\min\{ eta,\gamma/2,c\}.	ag{21} \] All these numbers are fixed before N tends to infinity. Equations (13),(18)-(20) give a uniform upper rate strictly below F(0). Since log P_N^+(L_C)=NF(0)+o(N), reducing the gap once more proves the actual finite comparison (4) at all sufficiently large levels. This includes arbitrary real parts of every CROSS fold parameter. No cap moment sequence at a varied spectrum, unknown degree interpolation, or finite-order adiabatic extrapolation has entered. The finite high-order construction (15)-(17) supplies the stated exponential residual, and all source cutoff endpoints remain. ## 8. Exterior attachment and precise remaining scope As the whole A-star was included, the unchanged exterior G_N has no A incidence. For the remaining original target monomial Y^t, (4) and Cauchy give \[  ig|[Y^{\mathbf t}]B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)G_N(Y) ig| \le e^{-\eta N}P_N^+(L_C)  rac{\sup_{|Y_f|=L_f}|G_N(Y)|}{\prod_fL_f^{t_f}}.	ag{22} \] Here ordinary t_f=d and protected exponents zero are unchanged. Boundary variables may be shared arbitrarily. All raw source scalar signs are fixed unit factors; there is no new N normalization. This is a genuine spectral-neighborhood RELATIVE star improvement. Its displayed weighted star/exterior envelope is not generally known to be at most exp(N Phi_D). The hypothesis that every other A-incident port is CROSS also remains explicit. Consequently no universal cap elimination, full source gap, or volume theorem is inferred. ## 9. A shorter fixed-spectrum proof using only finite positive moments At the fixed spectra cap +2 and all neighbors -2, there is a separate proof of the relative star gap that avoids analytic antidifferencing. It uses the [exact positive cap-moment law](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md), not its disproved squared-norm strengthening. Put \[ P_N^0(A,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}p_{N,j}(Y)A^j,\qquad R_N(x;Y)=\sum_{j=0}^Mp_{N,j}(Y)(-Cx)^j. \] There is a positive random variable \(X_N\) with \[ \mathbb E X_N^j=U_j/U_0\quad(0\le j\le d),\qquad B_N(Y;2,0)=U_0\mathbb E R_N(X_N;Y).	ag{23} \] Its support is unbounded. Only the displayed finite moments are used. The original full sine products give \(B_d=N^2\) and \(\prod_{r=0}^d\gamma_r=4\), hence \(U_d=N^2\) at both parities. Thus \[ m_d:=\mathbb E X_N^d=N^2\sin^2\! rac{\pi}{2N} \le rac{\pi^2}{4},\qquad U_0\le CN^2.	ag{24} \] Fix a small \(\delta_0>0\).
