At A, add the original cap load, the whole inside contributions and E's outer load. All other contributions are nonnegative. Consequently \[ q_{E,A}+q_{E,Z}\le
u,\qquad q_{E,W}=1-q_{E,A}-q_{E,Z}\ge1-
u>	frac12.	ag{3} \] In particular E is NOT CROSS. This proof never assigns half-supply to a Green triangle: only whole original port supplies and exclusive middle incidences are counted. Equivalently, if E were CROSS, its inside half supplies 1/2, forcing at least 1/2 A load from the disk and E together, contrary to (1). If E is Green, W is its child and the exact common-weight relation implies L_W>L_A (the other outer v is protected). Thus the cap has an outgoing strict increase in child weight. If E is another cap, its other zero incidence must be Z=u. Hence D is a single triangle and E is the other port adjacent to the original mark. Its split nu' satisfies nu'<=nu. The inequality is strict whenever an additional positive A incidence remains outside F and E. Equality can only occur when A belongs exclusively to those two ports; no classification of that residual topology is needed here. One immediate useful condition is therefore: \[ 	ext{Every }A	ext{-neighbor other than }F	ext{ is CROSS} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad Av
otin E(T).	ag{4} \] The converse is not asserted. Nor does absence of Av imply Q-degree two: the bipyramid/K_(2,n) examples have absent opposite apex edge and arbitrarily many original A incidences. ## 2. A maximal component containing a cap gives an applicable CROSS star Form the graph on ordinary faces whose edges are the residual caps, each joining its ordinary outer to its overloaded child. Orient each edge toward its child. All weights in a connected component agree. There are at most TWO cap edges, from the two original triangles adjacent to uv, and no loops because the port vertices are distinct. Thus the only possible graph cycle is a parallel two-edge pair. That parallel case forces the four actual triangles uAC,uvC,uAv,vAC. They exhaust the simple triangulated sphere. With both ports capped its total sharp value is zero. It is excluded at the positive-value classified data considered here. Consequently every cap component is a TREE. This uses the actual at-most-two-mark incidence; it is not an arbitrary cap-graph assumption. Demand one implies that every vertex has cap indegree at most one. A tree on n vertices has n-1 edges, so it has exactly one indegree-zero root, and all other vertices have indegree one. In a nontrivial tree choose a leaf other than the root. It is a cap child A and is incident to exactly one cap F. Suppose this component's common weight is maximal among ALL non-CROSS-child weights (both Green and cap children). The leaf A cannot also be a Green child because its cap load exceeds 1/2. Nor can it be any Green input: that Green's child would have strictly larger weight than L_A. The classification therefore implies that EVERY other original A-incident port is CROSS. In particular its opposite edge Av is absent by (4). Its original CROSS-star load is exactly nu in (0,1/2), as required by the [whole-star spectral estimate](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md). This proves the following structural alternative whenever caps exist: * if a nontrivial cap component (one containing a cap) attains the largest non-CROSS-child weight, an applicable single-cap / all-other-neighbors-CROSS star exists, without any restriction on Q-degree(A); * otherwise some Green child has weight strictly larger than EVERY component containing a cap. No CROSS-only cap star is asserted in this case. In particular ALL cap-only classified positive-value data have an applicable star, even when both residual caps occur and even when every cap child has Q-degree greater than two. The exact whole-star theorem applies to that selected star at its stated weighted radii. Its improvement is relative to that weighted envelope, not automatically relative to Phi or a whole Fourier period. The second alternative is real remaining scope. Selecting only the largest component CONTAINING A CAP does not eliminate an incident Green input whose child lies at larger weight outside every such component. The cut (3) gives a precise original-flow instance of such escalation. The argument does not prove that all cap-bearing maxima satisfy the first alternative, nor does it eliminate an isolated maximal Green. ## 3. An exactly solvable complete triangle refinement Use the original half-triangle entropy and its weighted potential \[  egin{aligned} \mathcal C(\alpha)&=\sum_{i=1}^3f(\alpha_i),\qquad \sum_i\alpha_i=	frac12,\ Q(a,b,c)&=\max_\alpha\left\{\mathcal C(\alpha)+\sum_i\alpha_i\log a_iight\},\ f'(s)&=\log\cot(\pi s),\qquad f(0)=f(	frac12)=0. \end{aligned}	ag{5} \] For positive a,b,c put D=sqrt(ab+bc+ca). Its maximizing angles are alpha_a=atan(a/D)/pi and cyclically. Subdivide the triangle by a new ordinary vertex of weight \[ w=a+b+c+2D.	ag{6} \] The three new triangle roots are \[ \sqrt{ab+(a+b)w}=a+b+D, \] and its cyclic versions. Tangent addition, with positive denominator and sum below pi/2, gives the UNSQUARED angle identity \[ \arctan rac{a}{a+b+D}+\arctan rac{a}{a+c+D} =\arctan rac aD.	ag{7} \] Indeed the tangent of the left side is a/D, and both individual angles are positive with their sum below pi/2. Thus old corner loads add exactly as before, and the new w load is 3/2-1/2=1. The derivative of sum Q(a,b,w)-log w with respect to log w is the new w load minus one. It is strictly increasing, going from -1 to 1/2. Its unique zero is (6). Differentiating its minimum in the three old log weights and using (7) shows that its difference from Q(a,b,c) is constant on the connected positive octant. The exact identity is \[  egin{aligned} \inf_{w>0}\{Q(a,b,w)+Q(b,c,w)+Q(c,a,w)-\log w\} &=Q(a,b,c)+\kappa_*,\ \kappa_*&=4f(	frac14)= rac{v_{\mathrm{oct}}}{\pi}. \end{aligned}	ag{8} \] Here is an absolute calibration, not only a differential assertion. At a=b=c=1 the old angles are all 1/6, w=3+2sqrt(3), and every new triangle has angles (1/12,1/12,1/3). Since f(1/3)=f(1/6), the entropy gain is 6f(1/12). The absolutely convergent Fourier expansion \[ f(t)= rac1\pi\sum_{\substack{n\ge1\n\ \mathrm{odd}}}  rac{\sin(2\pi nt)}{n^2}, \] has sum_(j=0)^2 f(t+j/3)=f(3t)/3. At t=1/12, using the same periodic extension and f(5/12)=f(1/12), f(3/4)=-f(1/4), this gives 6f(1/12)=4f(1/4), proving the constant in (8). Formula (8) extends to protected zero weights by the closed entropy convention. ## 4. Fixed-boundary identity, including every protected zero Fix ANY closed old triangle allocation alpha>=0 of total 1/2. In the three refined triangle simplexes, impose total new-vertex load one and the SAME three old aggregate boundary loads alpha. Then \[ \max\sum_{	ext{three new triangles}}\mathcal C =\mathcal C(\alpha)+\kappa_*.	ag{9} \] For clarity, this is a compact concave optimization identity. Its fiber is nonempty at every alpha: at a pure old boundary vertex place 1/4 there and 1/4 at w in each of its two incident rows, and put a pure 1/2 w load in the opposite row; convex combinations give every alpha. The resulting value function is concave and upper semicontinuous on the closed half-simplex. Its weighted conjugate is the left side of (8), by elementary finite-dimensional concave duality with the single w target. The conjugate of C+kappa_* is the right side. Equality of the conjugates proves (9), including its boundary. This argument does not require finite boundary multipliers. Protected old vertices remain exactly zero, because their total load is zero and every refined corner is nonnegative. Every other original face target remains unchanged. There is no redefinition of a mark. Consequently replacing one CROSS triangle by these three CROSS triangles, with one new ordinary demand, adds EXACTLY kappa_* to the maximum of any fixed classical source sector for which the replaced triangle is CROSS. It adds the SAME constant to complete capacity Phi. This holds with arbitrary unchanged outside rows, even signed Green entropy rows, since (9) is a pointwise fixed-boundary identity before the outside maximization. Conversely an ordinary degree-three vertex all of whose incident triangles are CROSS can be eliminated with this constant, provided none of its incidences belongs to a non-CROSS row and the relevant outside row bookkeeping is retained. At the purely triangle-flow level, removal gives the smaller simple sphere when there are more than four old vertices. The intermediate pairing need not itself be an actual coupon matching. Section 5 gives a particular refinement whose matching is actual; no arbitrary elimination is silently promoted to a physical tensor identity. ## 5. Actual matched refinements can raise cap-child degree indefinitely Suppose a cap has the degree-two patch \[ F=(u,A,v,C),\qquad E=(A,u,C,Z), \] with E CROSS. Its triangles are uAC,uvC and uAZ,ACZ, paired across uC and AZ respectively. Stellar-subdivide ONLY ACZ by an ordinary W. Keep the original pair across AZ but replace its ACZ half by AWZ. Pair the other two new triangles ACW,CZW across CW. The new actual ports, in harmless middle/outer frame conventions, are \[ F	ext{ unchanged},\qquad E'=(A,u,W,Z),\qquad E''=(C,A,Z,W).	ag{10} \] All four vertices of each port are distinct. The simple MAIN graph remains bipartite: W has the same color as C,u, while A,Z share the other color. Every old MAIN edge is retained. The old face weights and circle-packing disks, and the cap data, are retained. The original port E is REPLACED: its AZ-paired half ACZ becomes AWZ, and the other two new triangles form the additional port E''. This does not retain the old coupon disk or assert equality of old and new links. Q-degree(A) increases by one. Subdivide the new AZ-adjacent triangle AWZ and repeat: after m steps the SAME cap child has Q-degree 2+m. For the sector with the cap fixed as cap and all these neighbor rows CROSS, (9) gives, for each fixed cap split and then after maximizing that split, \[  egin{aligned} M_{\mathrm{cap}}(\mathrm{refined})&=M_{\mathrm{cap}}(\mathrm{old})+m\kappa_*,\ \Phi(\mathrm{refined})&=\Phi(\mathrm{old})+m\kappa_*. \end{aligned}	ag{11} \] Thus the sector's deficit or excess relative to complete volume is EXACTLY unchanged. Positive stationary data also lift explicitly: use (6) at each insertion. Every old total face load and weight is unchanged, the cap still has L_A=L_C and the same nu, and each new ordinary demand equals one. Newly introduced ordinary angles are positive unless an incident vertex was one of the original protected zeros; those zeros remain zero. A stationary cap-only datum is a sector maximum by concavity of the remaining CROSS entropy and linearity of the cap row. This proves a structural limitation of valence-only arguments: stationary cap-star data and their sector value relative to Phi can be transported to arbitrarily high cap-child incidence degree. It does NOT produce a high seed, assert that the refined datum is a maximum over every non-CROSS assignment, or preserve a particular flat plat word or filled knot. It constructs actual matched-sphere sources and an exact classical sector identity. In this particular refinable class, high degree is reducible back to the seed by (9). Most importantly, (9) does not transport the finite signed cap/CROSS contraction theorem. Replacing individual positive CROSS coefficients inside an alternating cap sum loses its cancellation. No inequality between those finite signed sums is inferred from entropy surgery. ## Dependencies - [Full-fiber stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md): original common weights, ordinary positivity, and residual cap classification. - [Exact Green spectral maximum](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md): strict Green weight order and the original closed sharp entropy. - [Triangle entropy and its weighted potential](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md): the half-triangle Q and f normalization. - [Exact cap/CROSS incidence](research_cap_cross_incidence_and_disjoint_assembly.md): the internal-face criterion and its matching requirement. - [Matched-sphere Morse sources](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md): actual sources for the simple matched spheres in (10), not equality of the different sources. The stellar refinement retains the old circle-packing data but replaces the coupon E and changes its matching as in (10). It is not a finite signed-source identity or an assertion that the original knot is unchanged. No numerical audit is needed or claimed. The results do not assert a coefficient lower rate, finite signed-source rewiring, a universal Green elimination, or a global spectral/filled-volume bound.

title: Complete-radius balance depends on the original marked cap
text: # Complete-radius balance depends on the original marked cap PRIVATE exact observation, 31 October 2026. This concerns the finite geometric sufficient condition, not invariance or failure of the actual knot invariant. It uses TWO legitimate original top-cap marks on the SAME literal source word. No arbitrary local re-framing or new quantum mark is introduced. Use the already proved width-three word D=(1,3,2,4,1,3). Its face labels are u,a0,a1,a2,e1,e2,b1,b2 =0,...,7, and its original quartets are (1,0,4,2),(2,0,5,3),(4,2,6,5), (5,3,7,0),(1,4,0,6),(6,5,0,7). (1) With the FIRST top cap marked the protected pair is(0,1). Its normalized packing is exactly a1=(sqrt2,1;1), a2=(2-sqrt2,r;r), e1=(0,3/2;1/2), e2=(0,1/2;1/2), b1=(-sqrt2,1;1), b2=(sqrt2-2,r;r), r=3-2sqrt2, between linesY=0,2. This original mark passes Q-balance at all six ports. The SECOND original top-cap mark has protected pair(0,6), as the literal Morse compiler confirms. Its contact on Y=0 is p=-sqrt2. The ONE global Möbius transformation w=-4/(z+sqrt2) (2) sends that contact to infinity, keeps the lower halfplane as u, and sends the b1 disk to the upper halfplaneY>=2. It maps the entire same packing, retaining all source labels and contact orders. Its actual curvatures are (u,a0,a1,a2,e1,e2,b1,b2) =(0,1,2,3+2sqrt2,2,1,0,1). (3) Indeed a circle(X,Y;R) not through p has transformed curvature [((X-p)^2+Y^2-R^2)/(4R)]; the old lineY=2 becomes curvature1. The original b1 disk becomes the zero-curvature upper line. Every other listed value follows directly. This formula is a common whole-packing mark change, not independent modification of triangle weights. At the fourth port(5,3,7,0), the new quartet is (x,b,c,y)=(1,3+2sqrt2,1,0). Let F(r)=Q(1,r,0)=(2/pi)Ti2(sqrt r), with the original source constant. Put t=sqrt2-1 and G=Ti2(1), Catalan's constant. The balance gap at this port is exactly F((1+sqrt2)^2)+F(1)-log((1+sqrt2)^2) =(2/pi)[Ti2(t)+G]-log(1+sqrt2). (4) It is strictly NEGATIVE, with an elementary rational certificate: Ti2(t)<t<29/70, G<1-1/9+1/25=209/225, pi>31/10, log(1+sqrt2)>log(12/5) >2[7/17+(7/17)^3/3+(7/17)^5/5]. (5) For completeness, sqrt2>140/99 and <99/70 follow by squaring rational bounds. Thus t>41/99, and pi=8atan(t)>8[41/99-(41/99)^3/3] =9092816/2910897>31/10. The Ti2 and Catalan estimates are their elementary integral/alternating series bounds; the logarithm bound is the positive atanh series. The exact difference of the lower logarithm and upper first term in(4) is 2[7/17+(7/17)^3/3+(7/17)^5/5] -(20/31)(209/225+29/70) =114290888/13864903605 >1/200. Therefore the second-cap marked source fails complete-radius balance by at least1/200 at this actual port, whereas the first-cap marked source is balanced. In particular a legitimate different protected edge CAN remove a failed balance test for the same literal diagram (choose the first cap instead of the second). The conclusion is only presentation/mark dependence of this sufficient geometric test. It does not show a failure of any source volume equality, and it does not assert that every failing diagram has a successful mark. Applying a quantum theorem after changing a mark must still retain that original cap's exact source conventions; no generic open-word regulator invariance is used here.

title: Complex third faces and near-opposite MAIN phases in the actual raw cofactor
text: # Complex third faces and near-opposite MAIN phases in the actual raw cofactor The raw cofactor theorem applies to the original levels with the specified complex phases. It does not give a shared-volume comparison. Inputs are the [exact nodal adapter](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md), section 1; the [uniform complex determinant prefix bound](research_opposite_equal_triangle_determinant_bound.md), (5a); and the [real integral identity and original interpolation](research_opposite_equal_raw_cofactor_bound.md). The [full raw cofactor source](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) fixes the finite recurrence, both parity conventions and every unused factor. ## 1. Statement Set theta=pi/N, J=floor((N-1)/2), j=J-k for a fixed k>=0. Use the original cleared cofactor \[ \begin{aligned} R_j&=b^j\prod_{r<j}(a_r+u)+s_j^2(x+y)R_{j-1} +s_js_{j-1}(a_{j-1}+u)xyR_{j-2},\\ a_r&=4\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta),\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\qquad R_0=1. \end{aligned}\tag{1} \] Absent negative indices are zero. Fix 0<c0<=C<=c1 and a compact set of COMPLEX third-face values z. Define \[ \mathcal J_C(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\pi \log\max\{|z+Ce^{it}|,|z+Ce^{-it}|\}\,dt.\tag{2} \] Then, uniformly on these compacts and both parities, \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{\substack{C,z\\-4\le u\le0}} \left\{\frac1N\log|R_{J-k}(-C,C,z;u)|-\mathcal J_C(z)\right\}\le0.\tag{3} \] The logarithm of a zero is -infinity. The same bound holds for a fixed finite collection of k. A degree-j Bernstein extension adds exactly 2pi j |Im delta| when u=-4sin^2(pi delta). There is also a near-opposite version. For complex x,b with |x+C|+|b-C|<=h, there is a modulus omega(h)->0 such that \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{\substack{C,z,x,b\\|x+C|+|b-C|\le h\\-4\le u\le0}} \left\{\frac1N\log|R_{J-k}(x,b,z;u)|-\mathcal J_C(z)\right\}\le\omega(h).\tag{4} \] Thus after a common homogeneous phase rotation, (4) applies on an actual torus whenever the two MAIN arguments have equal radii and relative phase sufficiently close to pi, with ARBITRARY third-face phase. No individual coefficient estimate is inferred. ## 2. The exact signed tail and its continuum roots At every retained lower node u_a=-a_a, 0<=a<=j, the literal identity is \[ R_j(-C,C,z;u_a)=S_{2a}D_a(-C,C,z)K_{a,j}(-C,z;u_a), \qquad S_r=\prod_{v=1}^r s_v.\tag{5} \] The initial tail vector is (K_(a,a),K_(a,a-1))=(1,0). Its exact transfer has coefficients \[ \begin{aligned} p_r&=s_r^2(z-C),&q_r&=s_rs_{r-1}(a_a-a_{r-1})Cz,\\ K_{a,r}&=p_rK_{a,r-1}+q_rK_{a,r-2}. \end{aligned}\tag{6} \] For complex z there is NO positive sign gauge. Instead, with alpha=a/N and alpha<=t<=1/2, the transfer converges uniformly on the ENTIRE closed parameter triangle to [[p,q],[1,0]], where \[ \begin{aligned} p&=4(z-C)\sin^2(\pi t),\\ q&=16Cz\sin^2(\pi t)\bigl[\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)\bigr]. \end{aligned}\tag{7} \] The convergence is O(1/N), uniformly on the stated C,z compacts. No denominator occurs here. Write rho(t;alpha,C,z) for the maximum modulus of the two roots of lambda^2-p lambda-q=0. We will prove the uniform upper \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{a,C,z} \left\{\frac1N\log|K_{a,J-k}|- \int_{a/N}^{1/2}\log\rho(t;a/N,C,z)\,dt\right\}\le0.\tag{8} \] This is an upper estimate, including zero tails. It does not choose one scalar phase across a collision or a modulus crossing. There is also an EXACT finite scalar Jacobi structure. For l=r-a, normalize k_l=K_(a,a+l)/prod_(v=a+1)^(a+l)s_v^2. Then \[ \begin{aligned} k_0&=1,\qquad k_1=z-C,\\ k_l&=(z-C)k_{l-1}+\gamma_lCz\,k_{l-2},\\ \gamma_l&=1-\frac{s_as_{a+1}}{s_{a+l}s_{a+l-1}}\in[0,1],\qquad l\ge2. \end{aligned} \] This is the actual trigonometric tail identity, not a new quantum level. Formally, or for z!=0 using either square root, set \[ k_l=(i\sqrt{Cz})^lP_l\!\left(\frac{z-C}{i\sqrt{Cz}}\right). \] The square roots cancel by parity. The P_l obey P_0=1,P_1=w,P_l=wP_(l-1)-gamma_l P_(l-2). Hence P_l is the characteristic polynomial of the REAL symmetric zero-diagonal Jacobi matrix with adjacent entries sqrt(gamma_2),...,sqrt(gamma_l). Its spectrum lies in [-2,2] by the row-sum bound. Pairing its opposite eigenvalues shows that every zero of k_l as a polynomial in z lies on |z|=C: each pair contributes (z-C)^2+lambda^2 C z, and an unpaired zero contributes z-C. At z=0 the polynomial identity holds by continuation. This proves a scalar tail structure only; it is NOT a semisimple realization of the original complete-colored Casimir or of arbitrary coupon observables. The uniform upper below does not require an empirical zero limit. ## 3. A uniform slow-transfer upper that permits Jordan points For a compact family of two-by-two matrices T with norm bounded by M, Cayley-Hamilton gives, for every integer l>=1 and epsilon>0, \[ \|T^l\|\le C_\varepsilon(l+1)\bigl(\rho(T)+\varepsilon\bigr)^l.\tag{9} \] Indeed, if its roots are lambda_1,lambda_2, the coefficient (lambda_1^l-lambda_2^l)/(lambda_1-lambda_2) is the sum of l monomials, and has modulus at most l rho^(l-1), also when the roots coincide. The other Cayley-Hamilton coefficient is bounded by (l-1)rho^l. Absorbing M/epsilon yields (9), including rho=0. Divide the actual product into blocks of a FIXED length l. On a block the factors converge uniformly to one frozen matrix as N grows, because (7) is uniformly continuous and the finite coefficients have uniform O(1/N) error. The difference of its block product and T^l is o(1), uniformly in every parameter and the moving initial row a. Since rho+epsilon>=epsilon, for fixed l it may be absorbed into the right side of (9). Multiplication of the block norms gives \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\left\|\prod_r T_{N,r}\right\| \le\int_\alpha^{1/2}\log\bigl(\rho(t)+\varepsilon\bigr)\,dt +\frac{\log(2C_\varepsilon(l+1))}{l}.\tag{10} \] The incomplete blocks have bounded length and bounded norm. The Riemann sums are uniform, since log(rho+epsilon) is continuous on the compact parameter triangle. First let N tend to infinity, then l tend to infinity. This proves (10) without its last term. The epsilon removal is uniform. The root sum and product imply \[ \begin{aligned} \rho&\ge\frac{|p|}{2}=2\sin^2(\pi t)|z-C|,\\ \rho&\ge\sqrt{|q|}=4\sqrt{C|z|}\sin(\pi t) \sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)}. \end{aligned}\tag{11} \] If |z-C|>=C/2 use the first inequality; otherwise |z|>=C/2 and use the second. Hence on every stated compact there is c>0 such that \[ \rho\ge c\sin(\pi t)\sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)}.\tag{12} \] Together with the uniform upper bound, this gives uniform integrability of log rho. Use sin^2(pi t)-sin^2(pi alpha) =sin(pi(t-alpha))sin(pi(t+alpha)); the moving logarithmic endpoints have uniformly vanishing integrals on intervals of vanishing length. Consequently the integral of log rho from alpha to 1/2 is continuous jointly in alpha,C,z, including alpha=0,1/2 and z=0,C. The continuous integrals of log(rho+epsilon) decrease uniformly to it by compact monotone convergence. This proves (8). The missing fixed k terminal rows change the integral by o(1) uniformly, by the same logarithmic integrability; the finite product was always stopped at J-k. ## 4. Exact complex cancellation with the SYMMETRIC determinant action Define \[ \begin{aligned} L(\alpha)&=\int_0^{2\alpha}\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt,\\ D_{\mathrm{sym}}(\alpha;z)&=\int_0^\alpha \left[\frac12\log|z+Ce^{2\pi it}|+\frac12\log|z+Ce^{-2\pi it}| -\log(4\cos^2(\pi t))\right]dt. \end{aligned} \] Then the exact identity is \[ L(\alpha)+D_{\mathrm{sym}}(\alpha;z) +\int_\alpha^{1/2}\log\rho(t;\alpha,C,z)\,dt =\frac12\log\max(C,|z|).\tag{13} \] Here all terms have their integrable endpoint values. We prove (13) by a HOLOMORPHIC identity, not by equality of harmonic functions on a real interval. For t>alpha put w=z/C and \[ \gamma=1-\frac{\sin^2(\pi\alpha)}{\sin^2(\pi t)},\qquad0\le\gamma\le1. \] After lambda=4Csin^2(pi t) r, the two roots satisfy \[ r^2-(w-1)r-\gamma w=0.\tag{14} \] The discriminant w^2+(4gamma-2)w+1 has all its zeros on |w|=1. When gamma>0 and the roots have equal modulus, their sum/product give (w-1)^2/(-gamma w) in [0,4]. Thus w+1/w belongs to [2-4gamma,2] subset [-2,2]. Off the unit circle, w+1/w can be real only for real w, where it is outside this interval. Equality of moduli is therefore impossible for |w|!=1. The case gamma=0 has roots w-1 and zero and has the same conclusion away from w=1. There is a holomorphic dominant root r_out on |w|>1, normalized by r_out/w->1 at infinity, and a holomorphic nonzero root r_in on |w|<1, with r_in(0)=-1. These are precisely the roots of largest modulus there. The ratios r_out/w and -r_in have holomorphic logarithms fixed to zero at infinity and at zero, respectively. For positive real w>1, r_out is positive; for 0<w<1, r_in is negative. These signs fix the imaginary constants that matter below. Inside the circle, define the analytic determinant action by replacing the pair of log moduli in D_sym with \[ \log C+\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1+we^{2\pi it}) +\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1+we^{-2\pi it}), \] where the logarithms vanish at w=0. Define the tail action using log(4Csin^2(pi t))+Log(-r_in). These expressions are holomorphic in the disk and REAL for 0<w<1. On that interval, they are exactly the real quantities in the real cancellation identity. Their sum with L(alpha) therefore equals .5 log C as a complex identity on a real interval. The identity theorem gives that equality on the entire disk. Taking real parts proves (13) for |z|<C. Outside the circle, the determinant action uses \[ \operatorname{Log}z+\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1+w^{-1}e^{2\pi it}) +\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1+w^{-1}e^{-2\pi it}). \] The tail uses Log z+log(4sin^2(pi t))+Log(r_out/w). The TOTAL coefficient of Log z is alpha+(1/2-alpha)=1/2. Subtracting .5 Log z therefore gives a single-valued holomorphic function on the exterior, including infinity. It is real and zero on w>1 by the same real identity. The identity theorem shows it is identically zero, proving (13) outside the circle. The endpoint cases in alpha and the circle |z|=C follow by continuity. For the tail use (12); for D_sym use uniform integrability of the translated circle logarithm. Thus no lower bound or nonvanishing of the finite determinants or tails has been introduced. ## 5. From the complex determinant upper to the SAME full envelope The proved determinant prefix upper uses D_max rather than D_sym: \[ D_{\max}(\alpha;z)=\int_0^\alpha \left[\log\max\{|z+Ce^{2\pi it}|,|z+Ce^{-2\pi it}|\} -\log(4\cos^2(\pi t))\right]dt. \] Their exact difference is \[ E_\alpha(z)=\frac12\int_0^\alpha \left|\log|z+Ce^{2\pi it}|-\log|z+Ce^{-2\pi it}|\right|dt.\tag{15} \] It is nonnegative and nondecreasing in alpha. Equation (13) therefore gives the nodal upper action \[ \begin{aligned} L(\alpha)+D_{\max}(\alpha;z)+I_{\mathrm{tail}}(\alpha;z) &=\frac12\log\max(C,|z|)+E_\alpha(z)\\ &\le\frac12\log\max(C,|z|)+E_{1/2}(z)=\mathcal J_C(z). \end{aligned}\tag{16} \] For the last identity, the full symmetric determinant integral is .5 log max(C,|z|), by the circle logarithmic mean, while its denominator integral is zero. All identities include z=0 and the integrable zeros on |z|=C. No real cancellation is continued after replacing an average by a maximum without keeping its explicit extra term. Combine (5), (8), the uniform determinant prefix upper and \[ \frac1N\log S_{2a}=L(a/N)+O\!\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right). \] This proves the uniform nodal upper J_C(z) for every 0<=a<=j. The cofactor has spectral degree at most j. To include the k omitted nodes of the full J+1-point Chebyshev/Radau grid, interpolate \[ Q(u)=R_j(u)\prod_{a=j+1}^J(u-u_a). \] Its values vanish at the omitted nodes, and its retained values differ by at most 4^k. The full-grid Lebesgue bound is O(log N). Successive Markov derivative division by the k factors costs at most a fixed power of N, also at the roots themselves. This proves (3). All interpolation is in the genuine degree-j cofactor, not the full degree-d Hermite numerator. ## 6. Uniform stability of the two MAIN arguments We give the details needed for (4). The exact nodal identity (5) holds for arbitrary x,b,z with the same S_(2a). The determinant remains det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(z/2)H_+], and the homogeneous tail has coefficients s_r^2(x+z), s_r s_(r-1)(a_(r-1)-a_a)xz. First the determinant. On eta<=t<=1/2-eta, conjugate the perturbed transfer by the BASE opposite-equal eigenvector matrices. Their gap iC tan(pi t), inverse norms and derivatives have the same uniform bulk control, including every compact complex z. The conjugated norm is at most \[ \rho_{D,\mathrm{base}}(t;C,z)+C_\eta h+O_\eta(N^{-1}). \] The base rho_D is bounded below on that interval. Hence the logarithmic cost relative to its base action is at most C'_eta h N+o_eta(N). The first and final eta N rows retain the same direct bound O(eta N log(2/eta)+log N), uniformly in the perturbed coefficients. For prefixes that stop in either endpoint portion, use the same truncated estimate; the base omitted integrals are uniformly O(eta log(2/eta)). Thus the perturbed determinant prefix has upper action D_max(alpha;z)+omega_D(h), uniformly in all alpha, where \[ \omega_D(h)\le\inf_{\eta>0}\{e(\eta)+C'_\eta h\}, \qquad e(\eta)\longrightarrow0,\qquad\omega_D(h)\longrightarrow0.\tag{17} \] Only sufficiently small eta are used; constants depend on the fixed parameter compacts. No perturbed branch is followed through a crossing. For the tail, its finite transfer again converges uniformly on the whole closed triangle. Its limiting coefficients differ from (7) by O(h). Roots of bounded monic quadratics move by at most O(sqrt h), so their maximum modulus is at most rho_base+C sqrt h. Apply the fixed-block argument (9)-(10) to the perturbed matrices, and keep the base regularization in the resulting upper bound. After epsilon->0, the tail upper action is at most \[ \int_\alpha^{1/2}\log(\rho_{\mathrm{base}}+C\sqrt h)\,dt \le I_{\mathrm{tail,base}}(\alpha)+\omega_K(h), \qquad\omega_K(h)\longrightarrow0\text{ uniformly}.\tag{18} \] The last uniform convergence follows from precisely the continuity, lower bound and compact monotone convergence proved after (12). There is no assumption that a perturbed tail is positive or that its own spectral radius has a uniform positive minimum. The nodal factors S_(2a) are unchanged. Combining (16)-(18) and the same exact spectral interpolation proves (4), with omega=omega_D+omega_K. At each transfer estimate auxiliary parameters are fixed before N tends to infinity and are then sent to their stated limits. No N-dependent vanishing neighborhood is substituted for a fixed face-phase neighborhood. The spectral Bernstein extension has the same additional 2pi j |Im delta| at these perturbed face arguments. ## 7. The correct full third-face torus envelope For r>=0 the explicit maximum of (2) on |z|=r is \[ U_C(r)=\max_\phi\mathcal J_C(re^{i\phi}) =\frac1\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\log|r+Ce^{it}|\,dt.\tag{19} \] For r>0,C>0, write g(t)=log|r+C exp(it)|. This is even and decreasing on [0,pi]. In the upper half-plane J_C(r exp(i phi)) is (1/(2pi)) integral_(-phi)^(pi-phi) g(t)dt for 0<=phi<=pi. Its derivative is [g(phi)-g(pi-phi)]/(2pi), so the maximum is at phi=pi/2. Reflection gives the lower half-plane and the same value. At r=0 the result follows directly. This proof includes r=C by integrable limits at the isolated logarithmic zero. Unlike the real-face formula, (19) generally exceeds .5 log max(C,r). For example \[ U_C(C)=\frac12\log C+\frac G\pi,\qquad G=-\int_0^{\pi/4}\log\tan t\,dt>0.\tag{20} \] Thus the correct proven complex envelope has a nonzero phase cost. Equation (20) is a property of this UPPER envelope; no matching lower growth for the actual finite cofactor is claimed. It does not prove that a sharper radial raw-cofactor upper is impossible. Combining (4) and (19) gives an actual near-opposite-MAIN / arbitrary third-phase torus estimate with rate U_C(r)+omega(h). All original targets must still be extracted when this cofactor is used inside a source. This note neither sums the other cofactor terms nor proves that the resulting star envelope is at most Phi_D. It also makes no claim that spectral interpolation preserves a local sector's matrix covariance: only the exact cofactor polynomial is interpolated. ## scope No numerical audit or asymptotic sampling is needed or claimed. This is an upper bound for the original raw cofactor on the stated face and spectral domains, not a coefficientwise source replacement, a lower asymptotic, an absolute star or Phi_D comparison, or a filling theorem.

title: Direct signed circle fans and the untwisted relative fundamental chain
text: # Direct signed circle fans and the untwisted relative fundamental chain The source-to-group sewing is conditional on the stated hypotheses. Contact polygons do not supply the incorrectly inferred complete-color symbol, and the construction is not established at every sharp maximum. ## 1. Critical local chart and actual contact coordinates Let x,y,b>0, 0<delta<1/2, s=sin(pi delta), k=cos(pi delta), and c=b+(x+y)/s^2, T^2=b(x+y)+xy+b^2 s^2=c^2 s^2-c(x+y)+xy. These are the free-spectral critical equations on the strict LEFT straddling chart. The input triangle has (q,T_q)=(b,T); the output triangle has (q,T_q)=(-c,-T). In particular c>max(x,y). Put D=(x+y)^2-4xy s^2 and use the following common Euclidean similarity of the actual circle configuration: L=D/(xy), a=(y+x cos(2pi delta))/x, O=a-2isk, Z_q=a+(y-x)/q+2ik T_q/q, p_x=q Z_q/(q+x), p_y=L+q(Z_q-L)/(q+y). (1) The outer circle centers are 0,L. Their radii in this chart are sqrt(D)/x and sqrt(D)/y. Z_q is the middle-circle center and its geometric radius is sqrt(D)/|q|. O is the selected lower intersection of the outer circles, the actual P:J flag, where J=-exp(-2pi i delta). The two p's are the MAIN tangent contacts. The normalization is a Euclidean similarity fixing the original cone apex infinity. There is no resetting of an independent Gauss reference flag. Define the four literal fan shapes w_x=p_x/O, w_q=(p_y-Z_q)/(p_x-Z_q), w_y=(O-L)/(p_y-L), z_q=(O-p_x)/(p_y-p_x), and let D_BW denote the Bloch--Wigner function. Set V(q,T_q)=D_BW(w_x)+D_BW(w_q)+D_BW(w_y)-2D_BW(z_q). (2) The source force angles and their Legendre normalization are retained: mu=atan(bk/T)/pi, nu=atan(ck/T)/pi, G=Q_b+log c-J_c, h=G-mu log b-(1-nu)log c-xi log x-eta log y, xi+eta=nu-mu. (3) Here G is the actual sharp real action, including the outside-row products; the retained scalar modes are pure imaginary on this real chart. The definition and absolute normalization of Q,J,G are those of the signed-straddling generating relation. **Local theorem.** On this connected physical critical chart, V(b,T)-V(-c,-T)=2pi h. (4) The reflected RIGHT identity follows by exchanging input/output and the original orientation. No mixed-color word identification is used in (4). ## 2. Orientation and the factor two For a white circle, an original directed polygon edge from contact p to p' contributes Lambda((arg(p'-Z)-arg(p-Z))/2) to the cone volume with apex infinity. This holds for the recorded polygon order, even when it folds or has winding zero: sum the oriented triangle fan, cancel its internal edges, and use the oddness and pi-periodicity of Lambda. Since D_BW(exp(i theta))=2 Lambda(theta/2), its contribution to TWICE the cut-ball volume is the D_BW of the contact-ray ratio. For the input triangle the recorded white boundary edges are O->p_x, p_x->p_y, p_y->O. Their three ray ratios are exactly the first three shapes in (2). The shaded boundary has the opposite edge orientation, hence is (O,p_y,p_x). A triangle (p_x,p_y,O) coned to infinity has volume D_BW((O-p_x)/(p_y-p_x)); thus the shaded face contributes -2D_BW(z_q) to twice the ball volume. This proves (2) directly from the actual boundary orientation. The output triangle has the opposite original white-triangle order. Its displayed contact coordinates may lie on the same side as the input after folding, but its combinatorial order is not changed. Its contribution is therefore -V(-c,-T). The two abstract cut balls have opposite orientations and are developed using one target reflection, so their equal volume contributions give exactly (4), with no additional factor two. Repeated nonadjacent contacts in a white face cause no ambiguity: the cyclic fan identity is applied in the original edge order on ONE circle. The normalized repeated-vertex chains have zero terms; one does not invoke continuity for arbitrary coalescing tetrahedra. ## 3. Exact differential and the absolute constant The identity is scale invariant, so set y=1. Write s=2v/(1+v^2), k=(1-v^2)/(1+v^2), x=(T^2-b-b^2 s^2)/(b+1), 0<v<1. For q=b,T_q=T or q=-c,T_q=-T, put co=1-2s^2 and N_x=x(1-x)+q(1+x co)+2ixkT_q, N_y=(x-1)+q(x+co)-2ikT_q, O_x=1+x co-2ixsk, O_y=x+co+2isk. The four shapes (1) simplify, without changing any flag, to w_x=N_x/((q+x)O_x), w_q=-(q+x)N_y/((q+1)N_x), w_y=(q+1)O_y/N_y, z_q=(q+1)[xk-i(T_q+s(q+x))] /[k(q(x+1)+2x)+iT_q(x-1)]. (5) Let p_in=(T-ibk)/(T+ibk), p_out=(T-ick)/(T+ick), and let N_x^b,N_x^c mean the preceding N_x evaluated at (b,T),(-c,-T). Direct differentiation of the source Legendre expression gives 2pi dh=log b dArg p_in-log c dArg p_out -log x dArg(N_x^b/N_x^c). (6) Substituting (5) into dD_BW(z)=log|z|dArg(1-z)-log|1-z|dArg z gives EXACTLY (6) for the eight-shape difference. The accompanying verifier factors the rational functions over Q(i)[b,T,v], retains Gaussian-rational unit log norms (in particular log 2), and expands every log|factor| dArg(factor) coefficient. All 49 tensor positions cancel against (6). Conjugate factors have the same norm and opposite argument derivative; only constant arguments have zero derivative. This is a finite rational identity, with no numerical derivative or unrecorded logarithm branch. There are no shape or 1-minus-shape divisors in the physical interior. Indeed Im O<0, while Im Z_q=2kT_q/q>0 and q/(q+x),q/(q+y)>0 imply Im p_x,Im p_y>0. Also Z_q,L-Z_q are nonzero and p_x-Z_q=-x Z_q/(q+x), p_y-Z_q=y(L-Z_q)/(q+y), p_y-L=q(Z_q-L)/(q+y). The numerator of p_y-p_x, apart from its nonzero real denominator, is Ly(q+x)+qZ_q(x-y). Its imaginary part is 2kT_q(x-y); if x=y its remaining real term is nonzero. Thus all three contacts are distinct and all eight shapes and their complements are finite and nonzero. The domain (b,x,delta)>0 with delta<1/2 is connected. Calibrate at b=1,x=2,y=1 and delta->1/2. Then c->4,T->sqrt(6); all six white ratios tend to 1, and the two shaded ratios tend respectively to -2(3+sqrt(6))/sqrt(6), 3(2+sqrt(6))/sqrt(6), (7) which are finite real numbers. Their Bloch--Wigner values tend to zero. The verifier checks the leading numerator and denominator separately at this anchor before taking their ratio. For clarity, the source side tends to zero as well, rather than being calibrated only by a derivative: put t=k tau in its retained row integral. With r_k=sin(pi k tau)/k, Lambda(k tau)=2k^2 r_k[(x+1)r_k+ sqrt((x-1)^2 r_k^2+4x)], alpha(k tau)=4k^2(1-r_k^2). The two endpoints tend to b/(pi T_1),c_1/(pi T_1), strictly on opposite sides of 1/pi. The scaled interval is compact; the numerator is uniformly positive and bounded, and the denominator has one uniformly simple zero. Thus the logarithmic integral is O(k), while mu,nu,xi,eta are O(k). Consequently h->0. The differential identity, connectedness, and (7) prove the absolute identity (4). ## 4. Literal marked-line limits The local assertion includes the nondegenerate single-line limits by the same contact formulas, in the original apex frame. Here are their explicit limits, with y=1 by the same harmless similarity. When b->0 with x>0, put T_0=sqrt(x) and F=1-x+2ik sqrt(x). The input contacts become p_x=F/x, p_y=L+F, w_x=F/(1+x co-2ixsk), w_q=1, w_y=-(x+co+2isk)/F, z_q=[xk-i(sqrt(x)+sx)]/[2kx+i sqrt(x)(x-1)]. (7a) The actual middle line is Re((z-a) conjugate(F))=2k^2(x+1). Both contacts have positive imaginary part and O has negative imaginary part; p_y-p_x=4k^2+2ik(x-1)/sqrt(x) is nonzero. Thus the limiting shaded triangle remains distinct, and only the middle white fan becomes flat. In the source, mu=bk/(pi sqrt(x))+O(b^2), so mu log b->0. Its interval endpoint approaches 0, where Lambda(t) has a simple zero and alpha(0)>0. The discarded small integral is O(mu |log mu|); all remaining integrals and loads converge. Hence h has the same literal limit. When x->0 with b>0, first translate every contact and center by -1/x (or -y/x before normalizing y). This is affine and fixes infinity. For q=b,T_q=T or q=-c,T_q=-T the limits are O*=co-2isk, Z_q*=co+1/q+2ikT_q/q, p_x*=co+2ikT_q/q, p_y*=[(q+2)co+1+2ikT_q]/(q+1), w_x=1, w_q=-(-1+q co-2ikT_q)/(q+1), w_y=(q+1)(co+2isk)/(-1+q co-2ikT_q), z_q=-i(q+1)(T_q+sq)/(kq-iT_q). (7b) Here T^2=b+b^2s^2 and c=b+1/s^2. The outer x-circle becomes the actual line Re z=co; its two contacts are distinct on that line. The affine map z->i(z-co) identifies it literally with the existing outer-line adapter: O maps to +2sk and the middle center maps to -2kT_q/q+i/q. Thus the same selected raw J flag is retained. Both p's have positive imaginary part, and p_y*-p_x*=2k(kq-iT_q)/(q(q+1)) is nonzero. Thus the shaded triangle remains distinct and only the x-white fan becomes flat. The source interval endpoints stay strictly inside (0,1/2), on opposite sides of its simple alpha zero. On this compact interval Lambda is smooth and nonzero even at x=0, and its x-logarithmic derivative is bounded; the alpha zero is independent of x. Therefore xi=x partial_x G=O(x), so xi log x->0, and all other terms of h converge. For completeness y->0 can also be taken without ANY outer-label reversal: in (1), with x fixed and no translation, the x-center stays 0 with limiting radius1, the y-circle tends to Re z=co, O->co-2isk, Z_q->co-x/q+2ikT_q/q, and p_x->(q co-x+2ikT_q)/(q+x), p_y->co+2ikT_q/q, w_y->1. This is the same selected lower-intersection family. The identical compact-interval estimate gives eta=O(y) and eta log y->0. These calculations prove continuity for this ONE explicit family and its literal line triangles, not for arbitrary colliding ideal vertices. The only flat white contribution is D_BW(1)=0. A strict straddling triangle with both x=b=0 (or y=b=0) is NOT added by this statement: T=0 and nu=1/2 there, a terminal/free boundary stratum. The global theorem below permits a forced two-line corner only when its actual local branch is the already proved complete CROSS line triangle. Any other double-zero or free boundary needs a separate adapter. ## 5. Conditional original untwisted group and chain Fix the original certified simple-white marked plat. Assume the actual signed source clocks, selected spectral flags and full face stationary equations satisfy the hypotheses of [the regular signed group-sewing lemma](research_regular_signed_spectral_group_sewing.md) and yield one global developed reflection family. Restrict the local branches to complete CROSS triangles and strict free-spectral LEFT/RIGHT triangles covered by (4), including only the line limits of section4. All original cups, caps, prefixes and the unrestricted original mark are retained. In particular this is not a construction from an absolute maximum for which the sign cocycle has not been solved. Use the UNTWISTED drilled exterior Y_D^0. Its literal first-ball shaded pair is S_0=(O,C_1,C_2), S_1=(O,C_3,C_0), paired by O->O,C_1->C_0,C_2->C_3 within that ball. These displayed tuples are the FIXED PAIRING-LABEL listings. They do not override the oriented boundary-chain orders of section2: the input shaded chain has order (O,p_y,p_x). In particular no orientation sign is inferred just from the listing S_0. At a strict critical port, the primitive collar C has projective eigenratio -1 on P's selected flag. Hence C is the half-turn about the axis joining the two outer-circle intersections. Each outer white plane contains that axis, so C preserves BOTH outer planes. Its proved simultaneous main-head conjugations then show that C carries the input middle plane to the output middle plane. It therefore carries precisely all three ordered contact flags in this original permutation, not only O. At complete CROSS ports use their established three-point collar, including the literal line cases. Keep ONE global white reflection r_u for the second ball. Its shaded map is r_u C r_u with the same original labels; white face f pairs second to first by r_f r_u. The latter fixes the whole white plane after removing r_u and identifies its complete recorded polygon chain. These are exactly the original UNTWISTED face permutations. No retained-half across-copy permutation is asserted here. Use the labeled convex complete certificate to fix a degree-one abstract triangulation of the original two balls: fan the incident white faces from the original marked vertex p and cone p to the nonincident boundary triangles. Change only its developed vertex images to the present contacts. The original combinatorial boundary identifications still hold, so this is the original equivariant relative fundamental chain, even when its image folds. No new interior vertex, replacement mark or image-degree assertion occurs. Section2 computes its signed volume by its original face order. ## 6. Whole peripheral groups, truncation and the uniform gap Every main peripheral subgroup contains its noncentral parabolic meridian and hence preserves all horospheres at its contact. At a strict critical auxiliary cusp, its actual two generators are the primitive C^{-1} and P, up to the recorded central lifts. They commute, fix the same two ideal flags, and have unit-modulus eigenvalues. Therefore the WHOLE peripheral subgroup preserves every horosphere at the selected flag. At a complete CROSS cusp the corresponding whole subgroup is parabolic and has the same property. Merely commuting with identity is not used. Choose a horosphere at one lift of each original cusp and propagate it equivariantly. Peripheral preservation makes this well defined. No orthogonality of the now-intersecting white/shaded planes is required. Truncate the finitely many incidence corners compatibly; the ideal-chain limit agrees with the horospherically adapted equivariant volume. For a compact critical peripheral group this is also the canonical normalization used in the published general volume bound: put its chosen flag at infinity and its other fixed flag at 0. The cusp group acts by rotations z->exp(i theta)z on a horosphere y=H. The equivariant homotopy (z,H)->((1-t)z,H) remains on this horosphere and has rank at most two, hence zero three-volume. Its endpoint is the finite axis point (0,H); the remaining axis tail has rank at most one. This is a proof for the CONSISTENT original horospherical boundary cycle, not a claim that an arbitrary rotating torus or open mixed-flag bridge has zero cone volume. Consequently the canonical representation volume is the computed original two-ball chain volume, and 2pi sum_e h_e=Vol(rho), |sum_e h_e| <= Vol(Y_D^0)/(2pi). (8) If at least one port is strict Green, its ACTUAL auxiliary meridian has trace zero: the raw matrix M_0 satisfies M_0^2=-I. The original complete auxiliary meridians have trace squared 4. Apply the proved fixed-peripheral-word gap to the finite list of original auxiliary meridians, with deviation 4. It gives a diagram-dependent g_D>0, uniform on this entire conditional stratum, such that sum_e h_e <= [Vol(Y_D^0)-g_D]/(2pi). (9) This does not need a lower bound on delta, nor compactness of the ordinary radius parameters beyond the existence of the stated representation and chain. The published gap theorem uses exactly the canonical peripheral volume just verified. The same bound holds for any finite action limit of a sequence of these coherent regular stationary configurations, each containing a Green port. The finite meridian list and g_D are fixed, so take the limsup in (9). Clocks, row endpoints and spectral parameters may degenerate along that sequence. This is closure of ACTUAL solutions, not a density assertion for an arbitrary KKT boundary datum. The common original resolvent numerator uses H_V and is independent of retained half-twist signs; those signs enter the outside Gaussian through n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e. Thus (9), if its source hypotheses are established for a relevant sharp remainder stratum, uses Y_D^0 with the same capacity Phi=2Vol(Q_D)/(2pi)=Vol(Y_D^epsilon)/(2pi). It is NOT an identification of the differently marked exteriors or their filling phases. The existing all-CROSS filling theorem retains the actual epsilon and framing separately. ## 7. Verification and remaining scope The [portable exact verifier](../experiments/research_audit_critical_circle_fan_fundamental_chain.py) and its [saved result](../experiments/research_critical_circle_fan_fundamental_chain_results.json) check four generic contact-coordinate identities, the eight actual fan shapes and 49-position differential tensor, eight real endpoint values and sixteen separately nonzero uncancelled leading anchor factors. The verifier imports only rational factor and differential utilities from the formal-word audit; no complete-color mixed-symbol claim is imported. The global chain uses the original combinatorics of [matching geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), the abstract-chain construction in the [endpoint signed cut-ball proof](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md), and the canonical normalization and uniform conclusion of the [fixed peripheral-word volume gap](general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md). Its new intersecting-circle fan calculation replaces the endpoint orthogonal-shaded-face formula; that old formula is not imported outside its tangent case. The global proof still assumes actual signed-clock compatibility, the full original face stationary equations, the stated regular branch list and flags, and the permitted marked-line limits. It does not prove that every sharp absolute coefficient maximum has these properties, handle free spectral/row/ordinary boundary strata, or give a contributing Fourier cycle. Those are the remaining source and compact-boundary questions. The retained-half global face adapter is separate and unnecessary for this common untwisted numerator upper-bound statement. An inconsistent phase assignment may have an exponential cancellation relative to its own positive envelope. That envelope can exceed Phi; such a relative loss alone does not bound it by Phi. No combination of that local phase exclusion with this conditional geometric theorem is being asserted to cover the missing global remainder. ## 8. Mixed complete Green ports in the same original chain The [shared-stationarity reduction](research_regular_shared_spectral_stationary_reduction.md) also checks the following extension for general stationary data. Some one-sided ports may have delta=0 while another is strict positive-spectral Green. Retain their original endpoint signed triangle fans from the tangent cut-ball theorem; do not replace their parabolic collars by identity. The exact old adapter is C=I+i r(P+I), where r=(eta_c T_c-eta_b T_b)/(2(x+y)) is real, including its literal one-line and two-line versions. Normalize the tangent outer planes to Re w=0,1. Their raw product is P=-[[1,2],[0,1]], so C acts by w->w-2ir. It therefore preserves BOTH outer planes. Its already proved simultaneous head conjugations carry the middle plane and all three original ordered contacts. This proves the same shaded pairing used in section5, without an inference from eigenratio1. Its whole peripheral subgroup is parabolic and preserves the chosen contact horosphere. Consequently these endpoint Green fans and the new intersecting critical fans sum in ONE developed family and the SAME original two-ball relative chain. The permitted branch list in section5 can be extended by these old endpoint branches, including their proved forced two-line corners. At least one strict positive- spectral Green port still supplies the uniform trace-zero gap. If all spectral parameters are0, the existing endpoint noncross entropy gap applies separately; no trace-zero conclusion is made. For MAXIMA of the sharp interval functional, the new reduction gives more: a positive- length nonterminal one-sided delta=0 port can be improved at fixed face loads, so such mixed endpoint ports cannot occur on that regular maximizing stratum. Diagonal and terminal strata are not removed by that argument.

title: A formal five-shape identity on the critical signed Gauss word

# A formal five-shape identity on the critical signed Gauss word > **Source-identification correction, 31 October 2026.** The exact algebra below uses the complete-color five-shape expression at every crossing, although the auxiliary raw meridian has trace zero and color \(\chi_{aux}=\pm i\), rather than \(-1\). The universal Gauss/Hurwitz MAP remains valid, but the actual mixed crossing symbol has color factors omitted here. Therefore the asserted identification with the original mixed source or its diagram regulator is withdrawn. The computed rational word closure, formal-symbol differential and calibrated formal-symbol identity remain valid algebraic results. The true mixed-color symbol, its monomial boundary term, and any actual relative-volume comparison are UNPROVED in this note. All occurrences of “actual” below referring to the twenty SYMBOLS must be read subject to this correction; the actual matrix maps are unaffected. This note is unpublished and quarantined from geometric or quantum conclusions. This section is a formal signed-Green identity. Its source and geometric interpretation require the additional hypotheses stated below. This is a FORMAL-symbol identity on the universal untwisted four-crossing word on its free-spectral critical straddling branch. Both auxiliary central lifts are included. It does not assert an off-critical identity, a global relative fundamental-cycle identity, or a contribution of any original finite-sum cycle. In fact the corresponding off-critical local identity is false. ## 1. The critical domain and the retained source primitive Use the calibrated action and physical conventions of [the signed straddling relation](research_signed_straddling_green_relation.md). Let \(x,y,b>0\), \(0<\delta<1/2\), and put \[ s=\sin(\pi\delta),\quad k=\cos(\pi\delta),\quad A=x+y,\qquad c=b+A/s^2,\qquad T=\sqrt{bA+xy+b^2s^2}. 	ag{1} \] Thus \(c>\max(x,y)\). The selected pre- and post-pole endpoints satisfy \[ \mu= rac1\pi\arctan rac{bk}{T},\qquad 
u= rac1\pi\arctan rac{ck}{T},\qquad 0<\mu<	frac12-\delta<
u<	frac12. 	ag{2} \] The output root is the negative one, \(T_{-c}=-T\). Equation (1) is exactly the free real-spectral stationarity equation for the retained absolute interval action \(G\): \[ G_\delta=0,\qquad E_b=H_c,\qquad R_0=-E_b/H_c=-1. 	ag{3} \] Here both unused spectral intervals and the omitted-half scalar modes are retained, as in the cited note. The original signed Green primitive is \(S_G=G-\pi i(1/2+\delta)\); the actual two scalar modes differ from it by \(\pi i/2\) and \(\pi i/2+2\pi i\delta\). Their real parts agree on this real chart. The primitive logarithm is \(U_0=\pm\pi i\), not zero. This distinction is essential to the auxiliary matrix below. Write the actual face derivatives as \[ \partial_{\log b}G=\mu,\quad \partial_{\log c}G=1-
u,\quad \partial_{\log x}G=\xi,\quad \partial_{\log y}G=\eta,\qquad \xi+\eta=
u-\mu. \] Define the critical Legendre value \[ h=G-\mu\log b-(1-
u)\log c-\xi\log x-\eta\log y. 	ag{4} \] This is the fixed-load value of the calibrated continuum source primitive. The present lemma does not prove a new coefficient asymptotic or a selected saddle contribution. Let \(\mathcal W_\pm\) denote the signed Bloch--Wigner sum of the actual four positive crossings below, with the two central choices of the auxiliary meridian. Then the local conclusion is \[  oxed{\mathcal W_+=\mathcal W_-=2\pi h.} 	ag{5} \] The source reference flag and physical head conventions are unchanged throughout the proof. ## 2. Rational original heads and the actual word All face weights may be divided by \(y\). This changes neither the physical ratios nor any head or shape below; it is not a change of Gauss reference. Hence set \(y=1\). A common nonzero head scale \(g\) rescales every \(E\) by \(g^{-1}\) and \(F\) by \(g\); every crossing shape uses only \(K\)'s and products \(EF\). Thus set \(g_{\mathrm{in}}=1\) without changing a shape. For rational calculation use independent real parameters \(b,T,v\): \[ s= rac{2v}{1+v^2},\quad k= rac{1-v^2}{1+v^2},\quad x= rac{T^2-b-b^2s^2}{b+1},\quad c=b+ rac{x+1}{s^2}. 	ag{6} \] The physical domain is \(b>0,\ 0<v<1,\ T>0,\ x>0\). It is diffeomorphic to the connected domain \(b,x>0,\ 0<v<1\), using \(T=\sqrt{x(b+1)+b+b^2s^2}\). In particular it is not legitimate to keep arbitrary \(b,T\) fixed all the way to \(v=1\). The actual head map is \[ K=-X^{-1},\quad F=S(1-X),\quad E=(X^{-1}-1)/S,\qquad G(K,E,F)=  egin{pmatrix}K&E\FK&FE+K^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\quad L^-= egin{pmatrix}1&0\-KF&K\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{7} \] Set \(p=(T-ibk)/(T+ibk)\), \(p'=(T-ick)/(T+ick)\). The input pairs \((X,S)\) are \((-x/b,-p)\) and \((-b,1)\). If their matrices are \(G_1,G_2,L_1^-,L_2^-\), the original based ordered product is \[ P=(L_1^-)^{-1}G_2L_1^-G_1,\qquad \operatorname{tr}P=\sigma=-2+4s^2. \] The critical auxiliary matrix and its other central lift are \[ M_\pm=\pm rac{2P-\sigma I}{4sk},\qquad \det M_\pm=1,\quad \operatorname{tr}M_\pm=0,\quad M_\pm^2=-I. 	ag{8} \] This is the physical lift \(-iC^{-1}\) and its negative for the already selected projective collar \(C\). The third head is the Gauss decomposition of \((L_2^-L_1^-)M_\pm(L_2^-L_1^-)^{-1}\). For two successive heads \((K,E,F)=(a,e,f)\) and \((d,g,j)\), put \(w=1-ej\). One actual positive crossing replaces them by \[  egin{split} &(dw,\ [wg+e(wd-d^{-1})]/a,\ aj/w),\ &(a/w,\ e/(dw),\ d[wf+j(w/a-a)]). \end{split} 	ag{9} \] Its five shapes, with their signs, are \[ +B,\quad +w^{-1},\quad +A^{-1},\quad -B/w,\quad -(wA)^{-1}, \qquad A=-a^{-1},\quad B=-d^{-1}. 	ag{10} \] The minus signs in (10) denote negative coefficients of \(D\), not negation of the shape. Apply (9)--(10) in the original order \([2,1,1,2]\), where the positions are one-based. This defines the twenty terms of \(\mathcal W_\pm\), with their actual crossing signs. For completeness put \[  egin{split} N_{yb}&=(x-1)+b(x+2k^2-1)+2ikT,\ N_{yc}&=(x-1)-c(x+2k^2-1)-2ikT,\qquad g'= rac{N_{yb}(1-c)}{N_{yc}(1+b)} . \end{split} \] The returned main pairs are exactly \((x/c,-g'p')\) and \((c,g')\); the auxiliary head is unchanged. The verifier proves all nine returned Gauss-coordinate identities for each lift as rational identities over \(\mathbb Q(i)(b,T,v)\). This word closure is checked separately from the regulator differential. ## 3. Differential identity, including rational constant norms From (4), stationarity and \(G_\delta=0\) give \(dh=-\log b\,d\mu+\log c\,d
u-\log x\,d\xi\), since \(y=1\). Define \[  egin{split} N_{xb}&=x(1-x)+b(1+x(2k^2-1))+2ixkT,\ N_{xc}&=x(1-x)-c(1+x(2k^2-1))-2ixkT. \end{split} \] The physical force formulas give \(d\arg p=-2\pi\,d\mu\), \(d\arg p'=-2\pi\,d
u\), and \(d\arg(N_{xb}/N_{xc})=2\pi\,d\xi\). The omitted denominators in the last ratio are real units, so only their argument DIFFERENTIAL vanishes. Consequently \[ 2\pi\,dh= \log b\,d\arg p-\log c\,d\arg p' -\log x\,d\arg(N_{xb}/N_{xc}). 	ag{11} \] Apply to every signed term of (10) the exact convention \[ dD(z)=\log|z|\,d\arg(1-z)-\log|1-z|\,d\arg z. 	ag{12} \] The following finite factor computation proves that the sum of (12) is precisely (11), for EACH auxiliary lift. Factor every numerator and denominator of \(z\) and \(1-z\) over \(\mathbb Q(i)\), make each polynomial factor monic, and place its leading coefficient in the Gaussian rational constant. Identify a factor with its complex conjugate in the log-norm vector. Identify their argument differentials with opposite signs. A real polynomial factor has zero argument differential on a regular real component. For a Gaussian rational constant \(a\), factor the positive rational \(a ar a\); the coefficient of each \(\log p\) is half the exponent of the rational prime \(p\). This retains, for example, ALL \(\log|2|\,d\arg f\) terms. The unit \(i\) has norm one and constant argument, so its contribution is zero for these two separate reasons. Expand (12) as a tensor of these log-norm and argument vectors, and subtract the three tensors on the right of (11). Every rational tensor coefficient is exactly zero. There are 81 expanded positions for each lift. No numerical evaluation, tolerance, use of a closed-orbit theorem, or omission of nonunit constants enters this certificate. Equations (6)--(10) and this factor algorithm specify every input to the accompanying exact verifier. ## 4. Actual chart divisors and the absolute constant The reduced rational shapes themselves extend throughout the positive critical domain as maps to \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\). Here is a finite factor check that avoids an assumption about arbitrary coalescing flags. Their polynomial factors consist of \(b,b+1,v,v\pm1,v\pm i\), four real factors, and one nonreal factor. After the physical substitution for \(T^2\), the four real factors, up to the explicitly nonzero factors recorded in the verifier, are \[ x+1-2s^2,\quad x,\quad x+1-2xs^2,\quad x+1+bs^2. 	ag{13} \] The nonreal factor has imaginary part \((b+1)T(v^4-1)/2
e0\). Only the first and third factors of (13) can vanish. They cannot both vanish: their equations imply \(x=1,s^2=1\), outside the domain. As the numerator and denominator of each shape were cancelled over \(\mathbb Q(i)\), no shape has a simultaneous zero numerator and denominator here. A Gauss-chart divisor can therefore produce only a definite zero or pole of the shape. The continuous extension \(D(0)=D(1)=D(\infty)=0\) extends the sum through these divisors. The verifier independently checks the factor registry and the five physical reductions. For the constant, keep \(b,x>0\) fixed, with \(x
e1\), and let \(v\uparrow1\), using \[ T(v)=\sqrt{x(b+1)+b+b^2s(v)^2}. 	ag{14} \] Then \(c	o c_1=b+x+1\), \(\mu,
u=O(k)\), and the interval in the definition of \(G\) shrinks to zero. Explicitly, with \(T_1=\sqrt{x(b+1)+b+b^2}\), \(\mu/k	o b/(\pi T_1)\) and \(
u/k	o c_1/(\pi T_1)\). These two positive limits lie strictly on either side of \(1/\pi\). Put \(r_k(	au)=\sin(\pi k	au)/k\). On this fixed compact \(	au\)-interval the actual cleared root and denominator are \[  egin{split} \Lambda(k	au)&=2k^2r_k \left[(x+1)r_k+\sqrt{(x-1)^2r_k^2+4x}ight],\ \alpha(k	au)&=4k^2(1-r_k^2). \end{split} \] The numerator of their ratio, after cancelling \(k^2\), is uniformly bounded above and below by positive constants. Moreover \(r_k'(	au)=\pi\cos(\pi k	au)\) stays bounded away from zero, so \(1-r_k^2\) has one uniformly simple zero. The integral of \(\left|\log(\Lambda/|\alpha|)ight|\) in \(	au\) is therefore uniformly bounded, and the original integral is \(O(k)\). Finally the positive-root homogeneous formula gives \(0\le x\partial_x\log\Lambda\le1\), so \(0\le\xi,\eta\le
u-\mu\). Thus (4) gives \(h	o0\). This uses the retained interval primitive, not a normalization of a geometric volume. Independently, the exact twenty rational shapes in (10) have, for each lift, four zeros, four poles, and twelve finite REAL limits as \(v\uparrow1\). The verifier records the valuation and leading coefficient of every term. Substituting the finite \(T(1)\) from (14) preserves those valuations for \(x
e1\); all their displayed leading denominators are then nonzero. Each Bloch--Wigner value tends to zero, hence \(\mathcal W_\pm	o0\). More explicitly, writing \(c_1=b+x+1\), the five SHAPE limits in their original crossing order are the same for both lifts: | Crossing position | First | Second | Third | Fourth | Fifth | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | \(0\) | \(-b\) | \(-1/b\) | \(0\) | \(1\) | | 1 | \(0\) | \(-x/b\) | \(-b/x\) | \(0\) | \(1\) | | 1 | \(1\) | \(x/c_1\) | \(\infty\) | \(x/c_1\) | \(\infty\) | | 2 | \(1\) | \(c_1\) | \(\infty\) | \(c_1\) | \(\infty\) | Each row retains the regulator coefficients \(+,+,+,-,-\). Equations (11)--(12) make \(\mathcal W_\pm-2\pi h\) locally constant away from the listed chart divisors. Both quantities extend continuously across each such divisor, and the physical domain is connected. The fixed-positive-\(b,x\) paths (14) fix the constant to zero. Continuity in \(x\) includes \(x=1\). This proves (5), without resetting the source reference flag. ## 5. What this identity does and does not settle The local primitive includes all source logarithms in (4); its Legendre subtraction is essential. The actual scalar modes have purely imaginary differences on this real critical chart. The auxiliary lift and its primitive logarithm are retained in (8), so the result does not silently replace \(U_0=\pm\pi i\) by zero. This calculation does not discard a global peripheral boundary term. To turn the sum of local identities into representation volume, one must still identify the original sewn relative fundamental chain, including cups, caps, the unrestricted mark and any retained half twist. The conditional group construction is stated separately in [the signed group-sewing note](research_regular_signed_spectral_group_sewing.md). It does not itself imply the needed chain identity. The present proof also does not extend to a free noncritical spectral parameter, arbitrary complex clocks, or an arbitrary absolute shared maximum. The sign-cocycle and regularity hypotheses remain independent issues. No global period bound or volume-conjecture conclusion is claimed. ## Verification artifact The [standalone exact verifier](../experiments/research_audit_critical_signed_green_word_regulator.py) has an optional \(	exttt{--output}\) argument and a portable same-directory default. It generates the word and its shapes from (7)--(10), proves the rational word closure and differential tensor, verifies the physical factor registry, and records all endpoint valuations. Its JSON output contains the actual forty signed rational shapes, not only a zero residual; the [recorded result](../experiments/research_critical_signed_green_word_regulator_results.json) is retained as an unpublished research artifact. No floating-point computation is used. Retained half twists, protected-line degenerations and a global relative fundamental chain are outside this local calculation.

title: Exact quantum polarization between diagonalizations of a MAIN quadrangulation
text: # Exact quantum polarization between diagonalizations of a MAIN quadrangulation 31 October 2026. research theorem; not published. The full spectral source polynomials of all diagonal choices form an exact Newton-reversal orbit. Sections 9--11 prove this identity and the corresponding change of the original filled functional. Sections 1--6 distinguish it from a transport of integer twist powers, and sections 7--8 give its full-Hermite kernel and the remaining cancellation problem. Original terminal labels, Cartan factors, and primitive disk framings are retained. ## 1. What the local change actually does Keep one quadrilateral of the original MAIN quadrangulation fixed, with cyclic white vertices \((x,b,y,c)\) and diagonal \(xy\). In the actual inverse cut, its four cyclic terminals \(0,1,2,3\) have shaded groups \((1,2),(3,0)\) and physical untwisted arcs \((0,1),(2,3)\). This is the dictionary in [general Morse source](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md), sections 1--2, and [original crossing-disk cut](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), sections 1--4. Choosing the other diagonal \(bc\) rotates the local roles by one cyclic step. With the SAME four exterior terminals, its physical untwisted arcs are \((1,2),(3,0)\). Thus the zero-twist tangles already have different boundary pairings. Their geometric quarter-turn is a permutation of the boundary data, not an isotopy relative that boundary. Write \(T(n)\) for the original two-strand box with full signed integer power \(R^n\), including its recorded ribbon framing. Let \(r\) be the genuine orientation-preserving quarter-turn, using the original turns. In the unchanged exterior frame the two filled choices are \(T(n)\) and \(r T(m)\). Reversing all convention signs together does not change the obstruction below. Our sign is calibrated by the exact original identity \(r T(-1)=T(1)\). ## 2. Exact fixed-boundary tangle obstruction The double cover of a ball branched over a trivial two-string tangle is a solid torus. Its boundary is the double cover of the sphere with four marked branch points. Choose primitive boundary classes \(\alpha,\beta\), with intersection one, so the meridian of \(T(0)\) is \(\alpha\) and the lift of one positive half twist acts by \(\alpha\mapsto \alpha+\beta\). The latter is the elementary annular picture: the lift of an arc joining the two exchanged branch points is a simple closed core, and the lifted half twist cuts and reglues its annulus by one full turn. Induction, including inverse twists, gives \[ \mu_n=\alpha+n\beta. \tag{1} \] Represent the four-point sphere as the pillowcase quotient of a square torus. A quarter-turn lifts, up to the deck involution, to \(\alpha\mapsto \beta\), \(\beta\mapsto -\alpha\). Thus the turned tangle has \[ \mu'_m=\beta-m\alpha, \qquad \det(\mu_n,\mu'_m)=1+nm. \tag{2} \] A homeomorphism of tangles equal to the identity on the original boundary lifts to a homeomorphism of their branched solid tori equal to the identity or deck involution on the boundary. It must preserve the rational line of the meridian. Equations (1)--(2) therefore give \[ T(n)\simeq_{\partial}rT(m)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad nm=-1. \tag{3} \] For integer \(n,m\), the only possibilities are \((1,-1)\) and \((-1,1)\); they are indeed the two original single-crossing turn identities. No classification theorem is needed for the obstruction: the kernel of boundary homology into the solid torus is enough. In the usual rational-tangle fraction convention this is the negative-reciprocal rule, also proved in Kauffman--Lambropoulou, [On the classification of rational tangles](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0311499), sections 2 and 6. Consequently there is no universal portwise substitution of long integer crossing powers that reverses a diagonal flip while leaving the exterior tangle fixed. This is a general local theorem, not a test of a particular closed knot. It does not say that two specially chosen exteriors can never have isotopic closures. ## 3. The two different peripheral tori must not be confused The torus in (1)--(2) is the branched cover of the four-point boundary sphere. It is NOT the crossing-circle cusp torus. The genuine spatial quarter-turn moves the auxiliary circle and its twice-punctured disk together. It preserves that disk's preferred zero-self-linking longitude and carries its meridian to the corresponding meridian. This is the actual turn statement of [original preferred disk longitude](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), section 5. One must not install the matrix of (2) as an unproved cusp basis change. For the original integer surgery coordinate, the primitive killed curve is \(\mu+p \lambda\), and the inserted exponent is \(n=\epsilon-2p\). In the flipped standard box, obtaining the old tangle would instead require the rational exponent \(m=-1/n\). Formally this would ask for \[ p'=\frac{\epsilon'+1/n}{2}. \tag{4} \] For \(|n|>1\) and \(\epsilon'\) in \(\{-1,0,1\}\), (4) is not an integer. This formal expression is not a valid replacement by the already proved integer Gaussian filling functional. Even allowing surgery on that same unknot with \(p'=a/b\) in lowest terms does not give the original local ball move. Its primitive filling curve is \(b \mu+a \lambda\). If the other components are ignored, the filled ambient manifold has first homology \(\mathbb Z/|b|\mathbb Z\), whereas the original integer full-twist fillings have \(|b|=1\) and ambient \(S^3\). The crossing circles in this construction bound mutually disjoint disks when the MAIN strands are ignored. For several such rational fillings the same homology calculation is the diagonal presentation with summands \(\mathbb Z/|b_e|\mathbb Z\). It supplies no cancellation of these ambient obstructions. A rational-tangle replacement in a ball is a different operation and would require additional tangle data, not the single original crossing-circle filling at that port. More generally a fixed integral peripheral matrix sends a slope \((1,p)\) to \((a+bp,c+dp)\), giving \(p'=(c+dp)/(a+bp)\) when the result can be normalized. If \(b\) is nonzero, \(p'\) stays bounded as \(|p|\) tends to infinity, and it cannot be integral for infinitely many such \(p\): a bounded integral subsequence would be constant, contradicting the nonzero determinant. Thus a fixed cusp map sending a cofinal integer long-filling family to another such family must preserve the longitude line and have affine slope action. This is only a necessary condition; (2) does not itself assert a map of the augmented exteriors. ## 4. A source-preserving finite cover does not erase this local kernel Suppose one proposes a common finite cover of the branched boundary torus, with the SAME fixed boundary identification used for the two solid tori. Let its integral inclusion be \(A:L'\longrightarrow H_1(T^2;\mathbb Z)\). Over the rationals, \(A\) is an isomorphism. The lifted meridian lines are \(A^{-1}(\mathbb Q\mu_n)\) and \(A^{-1}(\mathbb Q\mu'_m)\). They coincide only when the original lines coincide, hence only when \(nm=-1\). This excludes a repair by such a source-preserving pullback cover. It does not exclude unrelated covers with different boundary maps, branched covers of the full link, or changes of chamber/wiring. Those would need new peripheral and original quantum source adapters. There is no general Kashaev descent identity supplied by a cover. ## 5. An exact original nilpotent quantum obstruction This is a separate finite check with a proof for all integer exponents, not a numerical sample. At \(N=2\), put \(d=1\), \(q=i\), and \(\lambda=\exp(\pi i/4)\). The actual full pair algebra is \(\mathbb C[\Omega]/(\Omega^2)\). In the Newton basis put \[ B=\widehat B_1=-\Omega/4,\qquad B^2=0. \] The original crossing Hermite data give \(r_2(0)=1\), \(r'_2(0)=i/4\), and retain the Cartan scalar \(\lambda=q^{d^2/2}\). Consequently \[ R=\lambda(1-iB),\qquad R^n=\lambda^n(1-inB). \tag{5} \] The genuine unscaled original turn satisfies \(\mathscr R(1)=B\), \(\mathscr R(B)=1\); these are the \(N=2\) cases of the full physical Newton turn theorem, not an eigenvalue-only transform. Thus \[ \mathscr R(R^m)=\lambda^m(B-im). \tag{6} \] For any nonzero scalar \(a\), equality \(\mathscr R(R^m)=a R^n\) forces \(m\) nonzero and, by comparing the two coefficients, \(nm=-1\). In those two integer cases (5)--(6) give the original exact equalities with \(a=1\). In particular allowing an unknown normalization scalar cannot remove the local obstruction. Discarding the nilpotent coefficient would lose exactly this test. Equations (5)--(6) rule out a coupon-uniform all-level original tensor identity of the proposed power-substitution kind. The topological argument of section 2 is independent of this small-level witness and continues to rule out the relative-boundary move without any level restriction. We do not infer distinguishability of all closed knots from their level-two invariant. ## 6. A global long-filling obstruction when capacities differ Let \(T,T'\) be two simple choices on the same MAIN quadrangulation, with their actual complete hyperbolic augmented exteriors and knot parity patterns. Suppose \(\Phi(T)<\Phi(T')\). Their complete volumes are \(2\pi \Phi(T)\) and \(2\pi \Phi(T')\). The [proved independent long-filling geometry](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) makes the filled volumes converge to these respective values as the minimum absolute integer filling coordinate tends to infinity. Choose each geometric filling threshold so that the volume error is less than one-third of the positive difference between the two complete volumes. The two resulting volume intervals are disjoint. No pair of knots in these two cofinal all-long families can have homeomorphic complements, and in particular they cannot be the same knot. This obstructs ANY proposed global transport between these families that keeps all new coordinates independently long. It does not assume a local tangle substitution. It applies in particular to a strictly lower-capacity simple chart and a maximal chart. Equal-capacity ties, transports involving short slopes, and changed rational tangles are not settled by this argument. It is not an obstruction to representing the same knot by arbitrary turned coupons, as in the next section. ## 7. What does transport exactly: full turned coupons There is a useful positive finite statement. For any set of changed diagonals, put the genuine turned OLD coupon in every changed disk of the new chart, using the inverse of its local frame rotation. On the original Hopf polynomial algebra the two quarter-turn directions agree, since the genuine turn squares to the identity. Each physical local tangle is then exactly the old tangle in the original exterior frame. Outside arcs and the actual reduced marked closure stay fixed. Morse bends use the original snakes; no ribbon twist or Cartan scalar is discarded. Thus the whole contraction is the SAME original filled knot source, but the new local coupons at flipped ports are \(\mathscr R(R^n)\), not new integer powers \(R^m\). By the full pair-commutant theorem these turned coupons are polynomials in the new ordered pair Casimir, with all root Hermite data. Therefore the new general Morse coefficient compiler applies to them. This is not sector transport, multiplicativity of the turn, or transport of a Gaussian filling theorem. The original final knot-framing character must be retained; it is not reset using a fictitious new braid exponent. Here is the exact spectral kernel of that change of polarization. For all \(N\geq 2\), let \[ \begin{gathered} c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\quad \chi_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{d}(z-c_j)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\\ S_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N),\qquad B_r(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/S_r^2. \end{gathered} \] The original exact turn is \(\mathscr R\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{d-r}\). Newton division of the resolvent numerator, keeping repeated nodes, gives \[ V_N(\sigma;z)= \sum_{r=0}^{d}(-1)^rS_r^2 \prod_{j=r+1}^{d}(\sigma-c_j)\widehat B_r(z). \tag{7} \] This is a polynomial identity representing \(\chi_N(\sigma)/(\sigma-\Omega)\). Since \(c_{d-j}=c_j\) and \(S_r S_{d-r}=N\), applying the turn and changing \(k=d-r\) yields \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal K_N(\sigma,\zeta) :=(\mathscr R V_N(\sigma))(\zeta) =(-1)^dN^2\sum_{k=0}^{d} \widehat B_k(\sigma)\widehat B_k(\zeta). \quad} \tag{8} \] No simple-node interpolation or root-normal deletion was used. This is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in each variable, symmetric in them, and it is the exact Newton reproducing kernel times the displayed original factor. Let \(f_n(\sigma)=\exp[nN\operatorname{arccosh}(-\sigma/2)^2/(4\pi i)]\) in the original slit branch. Choose a contour enclosing every actual spectral node, within its analytic domain and avoiding the cut starting at \(+2\). The original full power is \(q^{n d^2/4} f_n(\Omega)\).
