Thus the turned power is exactly \(q^{n d^2/4} g_n(\Omega)\), where \[ g_n(\zeta)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint \frac{f_n(\sigma)}{\chi_N(\sigma)} \mathcal K_N(\sigma,\zeta)\,d\sigma. \tag{9} \] This is equivalent to the full confluent Newton formula \[ g_n(\zeta)=\sum_{r=0}^{d}(-1)^r S_r^2 f_n[c_0,\ldots,c_r]\widehat B_{d-r}(\zeta). \tag{10} \] Finally any polynomial \(g_n\) can itself be inserted against the SAME new-chart numerator by its Cauchy/Hermite functional \[ g_n(\Omega)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint \frac{g_n(\zeta)}{\chi_N(\zeta)} V_N(\zeta)\,d\zeta. \tag{11} \] Multilinearity makes (9)--(11) exact for the whole marked source and all its original face targets. Unchanged ports retain their ordinary Gaussian functional. These equations supply the promised actual transformed functional at changed ports; they do not make it Gaussian. ## 8. The known maximal-chart gap does not alone control this kernel Even its pointwise absolute size is not subexponential. At the real corner \(\sigma=\zeta=-2\), every square in (8) is nonnegative. Take \(k_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\). For both parities this index precedes any vanishing factor. The original sine products give \[ \widehat B_{k_N}(-2)= \prod_{j=0}^{k_N-1} \frac{\cos^2((j+1/2)\pi/N)}{\sin^2((j+1)\pi/N)}, \] \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log\widehat B_{k_N}(-2) =2\int_0^{1/4}\log\cot(\pi t)\,dt =\frac{2G}{\pi}>0, \tag{12} \] where \(G=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log\cot t\,dt\) is Catalan's constant. The logarithmic endpoint singularity is integrable; splitting off the first fixed small interval and comparing monotone log-sine sums to their integrals proves the displayed Riemann-sum limit. Consequently \[ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log|\mathcal K_N(-2,-2)|\geq\frac{4G}{\pi}. \tag{13} \] The maximal-chart non-CROSS estimate supplies a strict source gap, not a bound that automatically pays the exponential size in (13). Thus no inference of its preservation follows by taking absolute values of the transformed kernel. The large kernel is itself compatible with cancellations: at \(n=1\), (9) produces the exact opposite single crossing. We have not claimed the transformed period actually has excessive growth, or that a cancellation-aware estimate cannot use the maximal chart. The precise remaining problem is a uniform cancellation-aware estimate for (9)--(11) applied to the complete maximal-chart source, together with identification of its actual filled action. The former Gaussian H1/H2 period argument does not already supply that estimate. The exact topology says which old knot such a successful new argument would concern; no rational-power or sector equality is needed. ## 9. Exact local homogeneous covariance, with canonical physical lifts This strengthens section 7 to a polynomial identity before any shared coefficient is extracted. Denote the original complete root turn scalar by \(x_0=q^d\) to distinguish it from a face variable. For an arbitrary full Casimir polynomial \(f\), the actual unscaled turn has entries \[ (\mathscr R f)_{r,s;u,v} =q^{d(r-v)} f_{d-r,u;s,d-v}. \tag{14} \] At the new box let the homogeneous face tuple be \((X,B,C,Y)\). On canonical physical support the new input/output clocks are \[ Q^u=-q^{-1}X/B,\quad Q^v=-q^{-1}B/Y,\quad Q^r=-q^{-1}X/C,\quad Q^s=-q^{-1}C/Y. \] The old matrix entry on the right of (14) has the literal face tuple \((C,Y,X,B)\): its inputs are \(s,d-v\) and outputs \(d-r,u\). Use centered physical face-log differences \(\operatorname{Log}(L_{\mathrm{left}}/L_{\mathrm{right}})=2\pi i(i-d/2)/N\). They are the original clocks because \(-q=\exp(-\pi i d/N)\). Complementing a head is then literal log negation. In particular \[ \operatorname{Log}(XY/(BC))=2\pi i(r-v)/N. \] The actual old adapter has denominator \((XY)^{d/2}\), while the new one has denominator \((BC)^{d/2}\). Equation (14) cancels their ratio exactly. There is no extra scalar or parity sign: \[ \boxed{\quad H_{\mathscr R f}(X,B,C,Y)=H_f(C,Y,X,B). \quad} \tag{15} \] Here canonical physical support is imposed FIRST. On the remaining modular grids, a wrong unwrapped total makes both matrix entries zero; no individual head is reset by \(N\). For supported states the centered lift calculation just made applies. After fixing a common face scale, the original local Fourier adapter samples all three independent root grids (with the actual even-level cosets). Both homogeneous polynomials have degree \(d<N\), so the difference has degree below \(N\) in each normalized variable. Product-grid uniqueness proves the formal identity (15), not merely an equality on supported individual heads. For clarity the two reflection symmetries used in comparing cyclic frames are also exact. Outer symmetry follows from the source operator depending only on \(X+Y,XY\). For middle symmetry, its diagonal is \(c_j\) and its downward coefficients are \(-s_j^2(X+Y)\) and \(-s_j s_{j-1}XY\), where here \(s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N)\). With the bilinear pairing \([z^d]uv\), reflection gives \(c_j=c_{d-j}\), \(s_j^2=s_{N-j}^2\), and \(s_j s_{j-1}=s_{N+1-j}s_{N-j}\). Thus the source Casimir, and every polynomial in it, is selfadjoint for that pairing. Equivalently its entries obey \(F_{i,j}=F_{d-j,d-i}\), proving \(H_f(X,B,C,Y)=H_f(X,C,B,Y)\). In particular the flipped frame \((b,y,x,c)\) satisfies \[ H_f(b,y,x,c)=H_{\mathscr R f}(x,b,c,y),\qquad H_{\mathscr R f}(b,y,x,c)=H_f(x,b,c,y). \tag{16} \] All four variables in (16) are the same original labeled white faces. It is the coupon that changes. There is no assertion that \(H_f\) alone is invariant under a cyclic permutation. ## 10. The exact spectral action of all independent diagonal flips Fix the MAIN quadrangulation, one MAIN mark, and a reference choice \(D\) of all diagonals. For any choice let \(S_D(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_R)\) be its original full marked spectral polynomial, with \(V_N(\sigma_e)\) at every port and all ordinary face targets retained. Each spectral degree is at most \(d\). There is no geometric or simplicity hypothesis in the following finite statement; the general Morse realization retains any parallel diagonal edges as incidences. Let \(\mathscr R_e\) denote the full Newton reversal on the degree-at-most-\(d\) polynomial in its spectral variable \(\sigma_e\), fixing all other variables. The numerator itself has the useful symmetric form \[ V_N(\sigma;z) =(-1)^dN^2\sum_{r=0}^{d} \widehat B_{d-r}(\sigma)\widehat B_r(z). \tag{17} \] It follows directly from (7) and the same reflected products as (8). Hence \(\mathscr R_zV_N=\mathscr R_\sigma V_N=\mathcal K_N\). Applying (16) at one disk and then taking the unchanged full marked coefficient proves \[ \boxed{\qquad S_{D^e}=\mathscr R_e S_D, \qquad S_{D^A}=\left(\prod_{e\in A}\mathscr R_e\right)S_D \quad(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,R\}). \qquad} \tag{18} \] Indeed (16) holds already for the product of local face polynomials, and the spectral reversal commutes with the original shared coefficient extraction. Independent reversals commute and each squares to the identity. A second flip returns a local frame rotated by a half turn; the exact outer and middle reflection symmetries above return the same polynomial, with no newly chosen gauge. The diagonal choices form the ordinary binary cube with its free \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^R\) action. Equation (18) is an equivariant assignment into the tensor product of the FULL Hermite algebras. Its image need not be a free orbit: some polynomials may have stabilizers. Thus no stronger torsor or freeness assertion about quantum states is being made. If \[ S_D=\sum_{\mathbf r}\tau_D(\mathbf r) \prod_e\widehat B_{r_e}(\sigma_e), \] then flipping \(e\) replaces \(r_e\) by \(d-r_e\) in this same coefficient tensor. In particular the finite positive norm \[ \sum_{\mathbf r}|\tau_D(\mathbf r)|^2 \tag{19} \] is invariant under all choices. This is the already specified Newton tensor norm. It is not a bound of the complete geometric rate, and does not transport CROSS/LEFT/RIGHT restrictions or their positive envelopes. Such restrictions are not invariant under (15). ## 11. Filled functionals transform contragrediently Define the exact original single-port functional on spectral polynomials by \[ \mathfrak F_{n,N}(p) =\frac{q^{nd^2/4}}{2\pi i}\oint \frac{f_n(\sigma)}{\chi_N(\sigma)}p(\sigma)\,d\sigma. \tag{20} \] It is the original Gaussian/Hermite functional before its equivalent whole-interval Fourier deformation. Thus its usual sine, integer charges, and endpoint terms have not been altered or dropped. The original raw filled contraction is \(I_D(\mathbf n)=(\bigotimes_e\mathfrak F_{n_e,N})(S_D)\). For \(A\) the set of flipped disks, (18) gives the exact equality \[ I_D(\mathbf n) =\left(\bigotimes_e [\mathfrak F_{n_e,N}\circ\mathscr R_e^{\mathbf1_{e\in A}}] \right)S_{D^A}. \tag{21} \] The changed local functional is exactly (9)--(11), with the turned polynomial \(g_n\) and the same external Cartan scalar. To see its adjoint convention directly, the coefficient Cauchy pairing is \([z^d](uv\bmod\chi_N)\). On the normalized Newton basis it equals \((-1)^dN^{-2}\delta_{i+j,d}\). Newton reversal is selfadjoint for this pairing. Therefore \(\mathfrak F_{n,N}(\mathscr R p)\) is the Cauchy functional with \(\mathscr R f_n\) in its first slot, precisely \(g_n\), rather than a guessed reciprocal Gaussian. Equations (18)--(21) resolve the exact source relation between charts. They do not contradict the topology of sections 1--6: keeping the old knot on the new chart changes its filling functional. Applying the ordinary Gaussian functional on both sides would instead give the two different integer-twist diagrams. The complete and filled geometric actions of those two procedures must not be conflated. The preserved quantity (19) does not bypass the exponential kernel in (13). A proof of the general volume conjecture from a maximal chart still needs a cancellation-aware analysis of (21), with the actual old peripheral action and its full source normalization. ## Dependencies The finite source inputs are the notes [general Morse realization](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md), [full pair commutant and original turn](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md), [full Newton turn and metric](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md), [original signed crossing powers](actual_direct_long_power_source.md), and [original Gaussian/resolvent functional](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md) in the notes directory. The geometric obstruction uses only the already identified complete volumes and the proved long-filling convergence, not a Kashaev asymptotic for a lower-capacity chart.

title: The double-protected spectral cap does not admit the naive finite collar
text: # The double-protected spectral cap does not admit the naive finite collar The obstruction concerns finite continuation in the specified chart. It does not exclude other blowup coordinates or prove a global group, killed-meridian, or volume obstruction. ## 1. The original cap coefficient and the remaining parameter Use the original ordered face quartet (x,b,c,y), with protected x=b=0. For a positive-length LEFT row the limiting degrees are q=(0,0,1-nu,nu), 0<nu<=1/2. At delta=1/2, sigma=2, the sharp coefficient action is zero. Its free nu stationarity with finite positive ordinary multipliers gives c=y. It does not fix nu. The proposed full-fiber boundary reduction is a separate theorem; the present obstruction does not require it. In particular it applies to the interior range 0<nu<1/2 if subsequent reductions exclude the terminal value. The exact original scalar has not lost its phase. Put theta=pi/N, d=N-1 and take i=0, 0<=j<=floor(N/2)-1. The original source identity is (-1)^d H_V = sum b^i c^(d-j) (prod_(a<i)alpha_a)(prod_(a>j)alpha_a) K_(i,j), alpha_a=2cos((2a+1)theta)-sigma. At x=0, K_(0,j)=y^j prod_(a=1)^j 4sin^2(a theta). At sigma=2 every unused alpha_a=-4sin^2((a+1/2)theta)<0. Consequently the RAW coefficient of c^(d-j)y^j in H_V is (-1)^j A_j, where A_j=csc^2(theta/2) prod_(a=1)^j sin^2(a theta)/sin^2((a+1/2)theta)>0. (1) Indeed prod_(a=0)^d 4sin^2((a+1/2)theta)=4. This is valid at both parities and retains the original omitted half. The signed output clock c_tilde=-c makes (-1)^j c_tilde^(d-j)=(-1)^d c^(d-j), a common recorded sign; it is precisely the post-pole sign choice, not deletion of the j-dependent phase. Thus c=y corresponds to the signed middle q=-y in the existing reflection chart. This does not by itself impose a global face-sign solution. ## 2. Literal raw reflections at the cap Use the matrices in the [literal signed line flags](research_signed_spectral_line_flags.md), section1. An anti-Mobius reflection is represented by J with det J=-1; ordered products are J_2 conjugate(J_1). Put s=sin(pi delta), k=cos(pi delta). The protected outer line and ordinary outer circle are J_x=-i I, J_y=[[i cos(2pi delta),sin^2(2pi delta)/y], [y,i cos(2pi delta)]]. For signed middle q and its actual root T_q^2=qy+q^2 s^2, J_q=[[i-2kT_q/y,-4k^2(y+q s^2)/y^2], [q,i+2kT_q/y]]. (2) At the protected input b=0, T_b=0 and J_b=[[i,-4k^2/y],[0,i]]. These are the actual two marked line lifts; their height is 2k^2/y. Define, with the original head order, A_q=J_q conjugate(J_x), B_q=J_y conjugate(J_q), P=B_q A_q=J_y conjugate(J_x). (3) Now set delta=1/2, c=y, q=-y directly in the polynomial matrices (2). All entries are finite, without any division by T or k: J_x=-iI, J_b=iI, J_y=[[-i,0],[y,-i]], J_q=[[i,0],[-y,i]]=-J_y, P=[[1,0],[iy,1]]!=I. Direct multiplication in (3) gives (A_b,B_b)=(-I,-P), (A_q,B_q)=(-P,-I). (4) Thus there is NO finite invertible C with C A_b C^(-1)=A_q, C B_b C^(-1)=B_q. (5) The first equality would conjugate the central matrix -I to the noncentral matrix -P. This obstruction remains in PSL2: identity cannot be conjugated to a nontrivial parabolic. Changing central lifts or adding decorating flags does not alter that central/noncentral distinction. The coincident marked lines therefore do not give a finite specialization of the proved original collar. The negative output circle is the same projective circle as y, and the central MAIN head has moved to the other ordered leg. Merely listing matching traces or free fixed flags cannot repair the required simultaneous ordered conjugations. ## 3. An exact family exposes the singular collar There is a useful diagnostic family with the SAME protected faces, even though its terminal row need not be among the surviving global maxima. For 0<delta<1/2 set c=y/s^2 and take q=-c,T_q=0. The local endpoint equations then have nu=1/2, and the existing centralizer has R0=-1. Write h=sin(2pi delta)>0. In the original frame its projective matrix is C=[[0,-h/y],[-y/h,0]], C^2=I. (6) For example, A_b=[[-1,-4ik^2/y],[0,-1]], A_q=[[-1,0],[-iy/s^2,-1]], and (6) conjugates A_b to A_q since h^2=4s^2k^2. It commutes with the whole ordered P, so it conjugates B_b to B_q as well. Its projective determinant is -1; choosing a determinant-one central lift does not change any conclusion. As delta approaches1/2, (6) has no invertible projective limit: multiply by h/y to obtain a matrix tending to [[0,0],[-1,0]], of rank one. This is the explicit mechanism behind (4), not an arbitrary failure of continuity at collided ideal vertices. The marked-strip height collapses while the noncentral outer product remains noncentral in this frame. Imposing the free-spectral critical endpoint equations with x=b=0 forces nu=1/2, outside the strict nonterminal stratum. At the cap the exact monomer permits arbitrary nu. Hence (6) does not approximate arbitrary cap loads by actual regular marked critical data. In the direct cap circle matrices the parameter nu has disappeared; any recovery of it needs additional boundary data rather than an unproved assignment of angles to coincident centers. ## 4. Exact limitation This refutes only the naive finite-collar extension of the existing line/reflection chart, with its original ordered heads and retained signed clock. It does not refute a different blowup, a global block reduction, or cancellation of the original cap source. A parameter-dependent common conjugation may change which limiting heads remain noncentral, and needs its own whole-source flags and sewing analysis. No such operation is assumed here. In particular (4) is NOT a global group representation: its required local relation already fails. The central input therefore cannot be called a killed meridian in an established representation, and no representation-volume gap follows from it. The existing regular fundamental-chain theorem must not be applied at this cap merely because the local sharp action is zero or the marked lines coincide. Dependencies: the [original four-state source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) for the exact finite sign, the [literal signed line flags](research_signed_spectral_line_flags.md) for (2)--(3), and the [regular stationary reduction](research_regular_shared_spectral_stationary_reduction.md) for the terminal strict-critical restriction. The finite-collar calculation retains the stated chart and ordered pair. No global representation or volume conclusion follows.

title: A Fourier Hilbert representation of the local entropy defect
text:
# A Fourier Hilbert representation of the local entropy defect The entropy identity is not a quantum Plancherel theorem. A global application must impose the original shared face constraints. Put \(\ell=1/2\) and \[ f(t)= rac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}{\pi}, \qquad 0\le t\le\ell. \] Here \(\Lambda(a)=-\int_0^a\log|2\sin u|\,du\). We have \(f(0)=f(\ell)=0\), \(f(\ell-t)=f(t)\), \(f'(t)=\log\cot(\pi t)\), and \(f''(t)=-2\pi/\sin(2\pi t)<0\) in the interior. Extend \(f\) periodically to \(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z\). ## 1. Exact positive Fourier coefficients For \(n\ge1\) write \(H_n^{\mathrm{odd}}=\sum_{j=1}^n(2j-1)^{-1}\). Then the uniformly convergent identity is \[  oxed{\displaystyle f(t)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}  rac{H_n^{\mathrm{odd}}}{\pi^2n^2}  igl(1-\cos(4\pi nt) igr).} 	ag{1} \] To check all constants, the cosine coefficient for period \(1/2\) is \[ a_n=4\int_0^{1/2}f(t)\cos(4\pi nt)\,dt =- rac1{\pi^2n}\int_0^{\pi/2} \log\cot x\,\sin(4nx)\,dx. \] Use the primitive \((1-\cos(4nx))/(4n)\) of \(\sin(4nx)\). The logarithmic endpoint singularities have zero boundary product, so \[ I_n:=\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\cot x\,\sin(4nx)\,dx = rac1{4n}\int_0^\pi rac{1-\cos(2ny)}{\sin y}\,dy. \] If the last integral is \(J_n\), then \(J_0=0\) and \[ J_n-J_{n-1}=2\int_0^\pi\sin((2n-1)y)\,dy = rac4{2n-1}. \] Thus \(I_n=H_n^{\mathrm{odd}}/n\) and \(a_n=-H_n^{\mathrm{odd}}/(\pi^2n^2)\). Reflection makes the sine coefficients zero. These coefficients are absolutely summable; Fourier uniqueness and the value at zero fix the constant term and prove (1). No asymptotic of a quantum coefficient is used here. Let \(c_n=H_n^{\mathrm{odd}}/(\pi^2n^2)>0\). In the real Hilbert space \(\ell^2(\mathbb N;\mathbb R^2)\), define \[ u(t)=\left( \sqrt{c_n/2}\,[\cos(4\pi nt)-1],\quad \sqrt{c_n/2}\,\sin(4\pi nt) ight)_{n\ge1}. \] Absolute summability proves that this is well defined, and directly \[ \|u(t)\|^2=f(t),\qquad \|u(t)-u(s)\|^2=f(t-s). 	ag{2} \] In particular the periodic entropy kernel is conditionally negative definite: for finitely many real \(r_i\) with \(\sum_i r_i=0\), \[ \sum_{i,j}r_ir_jf(t_i-t_j) =-2\left\|\sum_i r_i u(t_i)ight\|^2\le0. \] ## 2. The actual one-sided score and the completion slack Use the original half-block triangle allocations from [the joint entropy identity](research_joint_entropy_triangle_decomposition.md): \[ \alpha=(a,\mu,\ell-\mu-a),\quad  eta=(b,
u,\ell-
u-b),\quad \xi=a-b,\quad w=
u-\mu, \quad\gamma=(\xi,\ell-w,w-\xi). \] All entries are nonnegative; \(0\le\xi\le w\) and every triangle has total \(\ell\). Set \(U(\alpha)= igoplus_{j=1}^3u(\alpha_j)\) and \(C(\alpha)=\sum_jf(\alpha_j)\). Equations (1)--(2), together with reflection of \(f\), give exactly \[ C(\alpha)=\|U(\alpha)\|^2,\quad C( eta)=\|U( eta)\|^2,\quad C(\gamma)=\|U(\alpha)-U( eta)\|^2. 	ag{3} \] The pure triangle vertices all map to zero; this is not an injective parameterization of the closed triangle simplex. For the reference entropy \(h=C(\alpha)-C( eta)\), local energy bound \(g=C(\gamma)\), and joint upper score \(\widetilde h=(h+g)/2\), we obtain \[  oxed{\displaystyle \widetilde h =\langle U(\alpha),U(\alpha)-U( eta)angle, \qquad 	au:=C(\alpha)-\widetilde h =\langle U(\alpha),U( eta)angle.} 	ag{4} \] This identifies the local completion slack as an exact inner product, not a guessed norm of a quantum state. For completeness the nonnegative sign follows independently from the elementary circular triangle inequality. Concavity and \(f(0)=0\) give \(f(r+s)\le f(r)+f(s)\) for \(r,s\ge0\), \(r+s\le\ell\). For \(0\le b\le a\le\ell\), reflection then gives \[ f(a-b)=f(\ell-a+b)\le f(\ell-a)+f(b)=f(a)+f(b). \] This proves the triangle inequality for the periodic kernel by choosing representatives in \([0,\ell]\). Sum it over the three coordinates in (3) to obtain \(	au\ge0\). Its other orientation gives \(\widetilde h\ge0\). Thus \[ 0\le\widetilde h\le C(\alpha). \] ## 3. An exact transported closure for the angle constraints Let \(R_s\) rotate the \(n\)-th real two-plane by \(4\pi ns\). These operators form an orthogonal representation of \(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z\). Directly from the definition, \[ u(s+t)=u(s)+R_su(t). 	ag{5} \] Consequently for any ordered list of real loads \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\), \[ u\left(\sum_{j=1}^m t_jight) =\sum_{j=1}^m R_{t_1+\cdots+t_{j-1}}u(t_j). 	ag{6} \] An original face target one, or a triangle target \(1/2\), therefore gives an exact zero on the right. The order may be the actual cyclic incidence order. This is a transported linear closure, with the rotations determined by the original partial angle sums. It is stronger information than an untransported sum of vectors, which need not vanish. This cocycle is explicitly a coboundary: with \(v=(\sqrt{c_n/2},0)_{n\ge1}\), we have \(u(t)=R_tv-v\). The vector \(v\) belongs to the Hilbert space. Thus the affine action \(z\mapsto R_tz+u(t)\) has the fixed point \(-v\). It would be incorrect to call this a nontrivial algebraic A-torsor or to infer a quantum period from it. Its precise use is to encode the original additive angle constraints by an explicit unitary transport, frequency by frequency. ## 4. Scope of the Fourier reformulation Equation (4) may organize the outer-transfer compensation in a Hilbert space. It does not make the original nonlinear gluing constraints linear. In particular, a face sum of angles does not make the untransported sum of vectors \(u(t)\) vanish. It controls a product of phases and the rotated sum in (6). Comparing those frames at different ports is an additional problem. No cross-port orthogonality or Plancherel contraction follows just from (4)--(6). The inequality comparing the global shared score with the complete hyperbolic volume is still open. This note records an exact representation of its local defect, with no novelty claim about the general theory of conditionally negative definite kernels. ## 5. A positive interval-cut realization of the same defect The kernel also has a realization in which the local slack is a positive intersection measure. Keep the circle length \(\ell=1/2\), and put \(d(t)=\min(t,\ell-t)\) for \(0\le t\le\ell\). On \(0<a<\ell/2\), define \[ w(a)=-f''(a)= rac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi a)}>0. \] Since \(f'(\ell/2)=0\), integration of the derivative gives \[ f(t)=f(d(t))=\int_0^{\ell/2}\min(d(t),a)w(a)\,da. 	ag{7} \] The integral converges because \(a w(a)\) is bounded near zero. For each \(a\), let \(A_t^a=t+[0,a)\) in \(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z\). Normalized angular units are not used: circle measure is the ordinary length \(ds\), with total \(\ell\). Direct interval geometry gives \[ |A_t^a\mathbin	riangle A_s^a|=2\min(d(t-s),a). \] On \((0,\ell/2)	imes(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z)\), use the positive measure \(d
u=	frac12w(a)\,da\,ds\), and set \[ v(a,s)=1_{A_0^a}(s),\qquad u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)(a,s)=1_{A_t^a}(s)-1_{A_0^a}(s). \] Both functions belong to \(L^2(
u)\): \(\|v\|^2=	frac12\int_0^{\ell/2}a w(a)\,da<\infty\). Equations (7) and the interval identity show \[ \|u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)\|^2=f(t),\qquad \|u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)-u_{\mathrm{cut}}(s)\|^2=f(t-s). 	ag{8} \] Translation of the circle variable gives the same unitary cocycle and transported closure (5)--(6). There is a useful pointwise feature beyond a generic Hilbert embedding. For fixed \((a,s)\), all nonzero \(u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)(a,s)\) have the SAME sign: they are \(-1\) inside \(A_0^a\), and \(+1\) outside it. Write \(E_t=\{(a,s):s\in A_t^a\mathbin	riangle A_0^a\}\). Then \[ u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)u_{\mathrm{cut}}(s)=1_{E_t\cap E_s},\qquad u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t) igl(u_{\mathrm{cut}}(t)-u_{\mathrm{cut}}(s) igr) =1_{E_t\setminus E_s}. \] For the original endpoint triples \(\alpha, eta\), equations (3)--(4) therefore have the exact positive forms \[  oxed{\displaystyle 	au=\sum_{j=1}^3
u(E_{\alpha_j}\cap E_{ eta_j}), \qquad \widetilde h=\sum_{j=1}^3
u(E_{\alpha_j}\setminus E_{ eta_j}).} 	ag{9} \] These are finite measures even though the ambient measure \(
u\) is infinite. No hyperbolic solid or manifold volume is being assigned to the sets \(E_t\). Equation (9) makes the local entropy defect a positive cut quantity. A global comparison must still respect the original face loads and the incidence-dependent transport frames; arbitrary independent cut choices would enlarge the source and are not justified.

title: The exact even CROSS endpoint is not real stable, and the remaining parity adapter
text: # The exact even CROSS endpoint is not real stable, and the remaining parity adapter 31 October 2026. Research result: exact-source reduction and obstruction. The local nonstability and stable-reference comparison are proved in the stated scope; the actual global even negative-axis adapter remains open. The finite counterexample uses the original even CROSS projection at sigma=-2. It is not a nearby complete-circle model. The obstruction is local; no failure of stability or of an absolute bound for a globally extracted original exterior is inferred from it. ## 1. Literal even source and an exact N=6 counterexample Use the central factorization in [actual cofactor factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), sections 1–2. For N=2m, theta=pi/N, put $$ \begin{aligned} a_j&=2+2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\qquad s_j=2\sin(j\theta),\qquad A=x+y,\\ R_0(b)&=1,\\ R_j(b)&=b^j\prod_{0\le r<j}a_r+s_j^2 A R_{j-1}(b) +s_js_{j-1}a_{j-1}xyR_{j-2}(b). \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ with absent negative-index terms zero. Set $$ D_b=R_{m-1}(b),\qquad E_b=a_{m-1}R_{m-2}(b). $$ The ACTUAL polynomial, with its fixed common raw sign removed, is $$ P_{\mathrm{cross}}=s_m^2 A D_bD_c +s_ms_{m-1}xy(D_bE_c+E_bD_c).\tag{2} $$ All three central path types remain. No unused factor, spectral derivative, or CROSS-support condition has been replaced. Take N=6, m=3 and x=y=1. Write r=sqrt3. Then $$ \begin{aligned} a_0&=2+r,\quad a_1=2,\quad a_2=2-r,\\ s_1&=1,\quad s_2=r,\quad s_3=2,\\ L(z)&=R_1(z)=(2+r)z+2,\\ D(z)&=R_2(z)=2(2+r)z^2+6(2+r)z+12+2r. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ Thus (2), exactly, is $$ \begin{aligned} P_{\mathrm{cross}}(1,b,c,1) &=4\bigl[2D(b)D(c)+k(D(b)L(c)+L(b)D(c))\bigr],\\ k&=\frac{2r-3}{2}>0. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ Specialize the remaining real variable c=-2. Since D(-2)=4-2r and L(-2)=-2-2r, the original source becomes $$ P_{\mathrm{cross}}(1,b,-2,1) =(8-8r)b^2+(12-16r)b+72-48r.\tag{5} $$ Its discriminant is $$ \Delta=-6000+3456\sqrt3<0.\tag{6} $$ For a fully rational sign certificate, sqrt3<125/72 because 3*72^2=15552<15625=125^2; multiplying gives (6). A real-stable polynomial remains stable or zero after real specializations. The nonzero quadratic (5) has one upper-half-plane zero, contradicting that condition. Equivalently, perturb x,y,c to 1+i epsilon,1+i epsilon,-2+i epsilon. The simple nonreal root b of (5) continues to an upper-half-plane root for all sufficiently small positive epsilon, providing a zero with ALL four imaginary parts positive. Therefore: $$ \begin{gathered} \text{The original even CROSS endpoint polynomial is not real stable}\\ \text{in its four face variables, already at }N=6. \end{gathered}\tag{7} $$ This is an exact source counterexample, not a numerical root plot. The symbolic expansion of (1)--(4) independently reproduces (5)--(6). ## 2. Why the simplest auxiliary-cofactor pencil cannot repair this The candidate joint pencil R_(m-1)(b)+t R_(m-2)(b) also fails at the same original level and the same positive x=y=1. Indeed $$ D(b)-4L(b)=2(2+\sqrt3)(b^2+b+1).\tag{8} $$ A real-stable polynomial in b,t could not have this nonstable specialization t=-4. Multiplying the t coefficient by the original positive a_(m-1) only rescales the real counterexample t and does not repair it. Thus a Hermitian PSD pencil realizing this exact auxiliary cofactor pair is impossible. This does not exclude a different source-level decomposition or a globally extracted stability theorem. For comparison, the operator (x+y)+kxy partial_t DOES preserve real stability when applied to a polynomial stable jointly in all its indicated variables: after division by xyP, both 1/x+1/y and partial_t log P have nonpositive imaginary part, with the first strictly negative. The failure here is the required actual input pencil, not that elementary operator fact. No substitute complete-node pencil is inserted. Even the proposal to treat the three central summands separately as stable products fails: an individual cofactor appearing in them need not be stable. At N=8, M=3, set x=y=1 and put $$ r=\sqrt2,\qquad u=\sqrt{2+\sqrt2},\qquad v=\sqrt{2-\sqrt2},\qquad uv=r. $$ The literal recurrence (1) gives $$ R_2(b)=(2+u)(2+v)b^2+4(2+u)b+v^2(8+2u+r).\tag{8a} $$ since s_1=v, s_2=r, a_0=2+u and a_1=2+v. Its discriminant is $$ \Delta_2=4(2+u)\bigl[4(2+u)-(2+v)v^2(8+2u+r)\bigr]<0.\tag{8b} $$ The sign requires no root computation: u<2, u>3/2, v>3/4 and r>1 give the bracket strictly less than 16-(11/4)(9/16)12=16-297/16<0. The bound v>3/4 follows from sqrt2<23/16, whose square is a rational inequality. Thus the ACTUAL E_b=a_3 R_2(b) in (2) is not stable. A constant-size stable decomposition does not follow by viewing the three displayed central terms as its components. This does not exclude a different decomposition of the original polynomial. ## 3. The exact stable even comparison polynomial survives globally There IS a genuine positive stable comparison, but its logical scope must be kept exact. The [original even half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), section 5, defines the actual nearest complete-channel lower cofactors $$ D_b^*=R_M(b;u_*),\qquad M=m-1,\qquad u_*=-2+2\cos(\pi/N). $$ and proves the coefficientwise inequalities $$ \begin{aligned} B_{\mathrm{cross}}&=4(x+y)D_b^*D_c^* \le_{\mathrm{coef}} P_{\mathrm{cross}}(-2)<_{\mathrm{coef}}3B_{\mathrm{cross}},\\ D_b^*&=C_{\mathrm{front}}D_M(x,b,y),\qquad C_{\mathrm{front}}=\frac{N}{2\sin(\pi/N)}. \end{aligned}\tag{9} $$ Here D_M is the original positive Hermitian determinant. The polynomials in (9) retain the original level N and the ONE forced x-or-y unit. The shift u_* is the actual closest complete folded node; (9) does not assert it equals the full endpoint coupon. Since x+y and both determinant factors are real stable, B_cross is real stable. For an original one-cap exterior with R-1 CROSS coupons, let Q_N(A,C) be obtained by using these B_cross coupons and performing the SAME protected specialization and EVERY same exterior face coefficient extraction as for P_N(A,C). Then $$ \begin{gathered} Q_N\text{ is zero or nonnegative real stable},\qquad \deg Q_N=d=N-1\quad\text{when }Q_N\ne0,\\ Q_N\le_{\mathrm{coef}}P_N\le_{\mathrm{coef}}3^{R-1}Q_N. \end{gathered}\tag{10} $$ The exact coefficient inequalities follow under products and extractions; no face target changes. Under the standing nonzero complete-source hypotheses Q_N is nonzero at all sufficiently large levels. Its degree is d because B_cross has the same exact degree d as P_cross, including the forced outer unit. Consequently P_N and Q_N have the SAME normalized pressure at every positive boundary fugacity, whenever either limit exists. In particular, using the original both-parity positive coefficient theorem near the strict stationary exterior, that common limit is the same classical F(z) used at odd levels. The compact-measure argument requires only convergence on a small REAL interval here. The root measures of Q_N have bounded mass on [0,1]. Any weak subsequential limit mu gives integral log(1+p(e^z-1)) dmu(p)=F(z)-F(0) for real z in that interval, since its kernel is bounded continuous in p. The integral is analytic near z=0; equality on the real interval determines all moments. Thus every subsequential limit is the SAME odd-level mu_D. It follows rigorously that the stable REFERENCE exterior has the same Mahler and negative-axis supremum rates as the odd original exterior: $$ \begin{aligned} \frac1N\log\operatorname{Mahler}(Q_N)&\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\ell_D,\\ \frac1N\log\sup_{0\le t\le1}|Q_N(-t,1)|&\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{cap}}+m^-,\\ \frac1N\log\sup_{0\le t\le1}|Q_N(-1,t)|&\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{cap}}+m^+. \end{aligned}\tag{11} $$ This uses the logarithmic-supremum continuity theorem. The passage from Q_N back to P_N at negative fugacity is NOT supplied by (10). ## 4. Even exponentially sharp positive comparison is insufficient Here is a concise general warning, not an original-source example. For d>=1, j=floor(d/2) and fixed 0<a<log2, set $$ Q_d(A,C)=(A+C)^d,\qquad P_d(A,C)=Q_d(A,C)+e^{ad}A^jC^{d-j}.\tag{12} $$ All coefficients are nonnegative. The central binomial coefficient is at least 2^d/(d+1), so even the coefficientwise comparison is $$ Q_d\le_{\mathrm{coef}}P_d \le_{\mathrm{coef}}\bigl[1+(d+1)e^{-(\log2-a)d}\bigr]Q_d.\tag{13} $$ The normalized positive pressure, and all coefficient exponential rates, are unchanged. On any fixed real z interval, the pressure also has the same locally uniform complex continuation in a small neighborhood, because the added term is exponentially smaller than (1+e^z)^d there. Nevertheless for BOTH negative-axis intervals, $$ \begin{aligned} e^{ad}&\le\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P_d(-t,1)|\le1+e^{ad},\\ e^{ad}&\le\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P_d(-1,t)|\le1+e^{ad}. \end{aligned}\tag{14} $$ by evaluation at t=1 and the triangle inequality. The corresponding two suprema of Q_d are exactly1. Thus neither positive pressure nor even an exponentially sharp coefficientwise comparison transfers negative-axis exponential rates. In particular the genuine constant-factor source comparison (10) cannot by itself do so. This example does not assert that the correction in (12) is realized by an original CROSS exterior. It identifies the precise extra signed/structural estimate that an even-parity adapter would need. ## 5. Current conclusion and remaining original-source question The direct all-parity local stability extension is false by (5)--(7). The stable nearest-fold comparison Q_N is an EXACT original-level, same-target reference and has the desired limiting root measure. What remains is a negative-axis/source contraction for the ACTUAL difference P_N-Q_N, or a different exact positive decomposition with controlled signed boundary values. A proof that the globally extracted P_N itself is stable remains possible despite the local failure; no such proof or counterexample is given here. The original even and odd signed-cap finite moment identities remain valid independently of stability. This note supplies no spectral neighborhood, no signed-source lower rate, and no general filled volume theorem. ## Inputs Actual three central terms: [actual cofactor factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), sections 1–2. Nearest-fold comparison and its exact scalar: [even half-block coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), section 5. Positive physical determinant: [positive physical determinant](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md), sections 1 and 3. Original global extraction and odd root measure: [original cap extraction and Mahler bound](research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md) and [root measure and negative-axis supremum rates](research_cap_root_measure_from_classical_pressure.md). The N=6 counterexample and N=8 individual-cofactor calculation are exact finite source obstructions. The nearest-fold positive comparison retains the same targets, but it does not control the actual negative-axis rate.

title: Fractional one-sided sectors: the forest and the missing reduction
text: # Fractional one-sided sectors: the forest and the missing reduction 31 October 2026. **Open research interface.** The structural lemmas below concern the convex weighted comparison for one fixed actual LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT pattern. They do not prove its universal capacity bound. The comparison perspective is distinct from the original Green coefficient entropy. The [finite-sector cover theorem](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md) explains the desired implication for the original invariant. The [certificate separation](actual_shared_radius_certificate_separation.md) shows why unrestricted spectator mixtures cannot be assumed harmless. ## 1. Exact network and perspective Use the original simple-white plat, ordinary demands one and protected demands zero. At a LEFT port put \(p=b,o=c\); at a RIGHT port put \(p=c,o=b\). The two outer faces are \(x,y\). Its exact comparison flow is $$ q_o=1-\frac{t}{2},\qquad(q_x,q_p,q_y)=t\alpha,\qquad 0\le t\le1,\quad\alpha\ge0,\quad\sum\alpha=\frac{1}{2}, \qquad h_{\mathrm{env}}=tC(\alpha).\tag{1} $$ Here \(C\) is the original half-degree triangle entropy. CROSS retains its two separate half-supply triangle rows. Equation (1) is equivalently a supply-one node on the four original faces whose arc to \(o\) has lower bound \(1/2\). Thus the fixed-sector feasible polytope is an ordinary bounded bipartite flow polytope, with protected arcs removed. Scaling by two makes its supplies, demands and lower bounds integral. The incidence matrix is totally unimodular, so all vertices are half-integral before scaling. Every one-sided vertex has \(t=0\) or \(t=1\). In particular the polytope is the convex hull of the feasible pure-atom patterns. This is a statement about flow vertices, **not** maximizers of a concave entropy. Concavity has the wrong direction for an atomwise maximization argument. ## 2. The strict-overload middle graph is an actual rooted forest Select the ports with \(t<1\), orient their original middle edges \(p\to o\), and retain their endpoints. Each selected child has \(q_o>1/2\). Two such edges therefore cannot enter one ordinary face, and none can enter a protected face. In the [literal gap presentation](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md), middle edges in an odd gap form a path. Those in an even gap form a cycle based at the protected exterior \(u\). Different gap paths meet only at \(u\). An undirected selected cycle would be one of these exterior cycles. Since its edges each have one head and every indegree is at most one, every cycle vertex would have indegree one, including \(u\), a contradiction. Hence every selected component is a tree. Its indegrees sum to one less than its vertex count, so it has exactly one root and all arrows point away from that root. If it contains a protected face, that face is the root. Gap parity makes a component monochromatic, so it contains at most one protected face and its outer \(x,y\) faces lie outside the component. For a component \(T\) with \(\kappa\in\{0,1\}\) protected roots, define $$ \ell_e=t_e(\alpha_{x,e}+\alpha_{y,e}). $$ The selected edges contribute \(|E(T)|-\sum_e\ell_e\) to its vertices. Their total demand is \(|V(T)|-\kappa\). Therefore all remaining original rows contribute exactly $$ 1-\kappa+\sum_{e\in E(T)}\ell_e.\tag{2} $$ A pure identity contraction would leave target \(1-\kappa\). The extra term in (2) is the outer-load compensation required by a fractional leaf elimination. It cannot be omitted or absorbed into a protected zero target. ## 3. Finite positive KKT equations Assume a relative-interior maximizer has finite positive ordinary dual weights \(L_f\). Protected coordinates remain zero. Each active retained triangle is the unique maximizer \(\alpha(L)\) in the original triangle Fenchel formula. A genuinely fractional row satisfies $$ Q(L_x,L_p,L_y)=\frac{1}{2}\log L_o, \qquad 0<t<1.\tag{3} $$ The [triangle entropy inequality](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) then gives $$ L_o=\exp\bigl(2Q(L_x,L_p,L_y)\bigr) \ge L_x+L_p+L_y.\tag{4} $$ This is strict when at least two input weights are positive. Thus every nonzero input curvature is strictly below the overloaded curvature, except for a monomial retained triangle. Such a triangle has one positive input face \(f\), zero entropy and \(L_o=L_f\). It can occur only in an original triangle containing both protected vertices. The endpoint inequalities have different directions: $$ \begin{array}{ll} t=0:&L_o\ge\exp(2Q_{\mathrm{input}}),\\ t=1:&L_o\le\exp(2Q_{\mathrm{input}}). \end{array}\tag{5} $$ Consequently a maximal-curvature fractional overload cannot be an input of another nonmonomial fractional row. It can nevertheless meet CROSS rows and terminal \(t=1\) fixed-triangle rows: (5) does not give an ascending-curvature conclusion for those terminal rows. Pure \(t=0\) rows carry no retained-triangle load. A claim that such a sink has only CROSS neighbors needs an additional argument. ## 4. The exact condition for lossless elimination Strict concavity of \(C\) gives an equality criterion for its perspective. Between two states of positive mass, equality in concavity of \(tC(\alpha)\) holds precisely when their normalized \(\alpha\)'s agree. For CROSS, both triangle allocations must agree. Along an affine path in the mass and weighted-allocation variables, its second variation is $$ \mathrm d^2[tC(\alpha)] =t\,(\mathrm d\alpha)^T D^2C(\alpha)(\mathrm d\alpha).\tag{6} $$ It is strictly negative when an allowed normalized allocation changes. A monomial allowed triangle has no normalized variable. The same equality criterion extends to a mass-zero endpoint by continuity. At a constrained maximizer, another feasible point of equal or greater entropy must therefore keep every positive-mass normalized triangle allocation fixed along their connecting segment. If all endpoint masses \(t=0,1\) are also kept fixed, the changes \(h_e=\mathrm dt_e\) at fractional rows must solve the exact original face system $$ \sum_e h_eD_e=0,\qquad D_e=\alpha_{x,e}e_x+\alpha_{p,e}e_p+\alpha_{y,e}e_y -\frac{1}{2}e_o.\tag{7} $$ Thus an angle-changing CROSS compensation incurs a strict entropy cost at this maximizer. This does not compare the maximizer's value with \(\Phi_D\); it identifies the condition a lossless same-sector argument would have to satisfy. The columns in (7) are usually independent. Their overloaded children are distinct. Restrict to those face rows and order by \(L_o\). A nonmonomial fractional column has diagonal entry \(-1/2\), while every off-diagonal positive entry lies at a strictly smaller curvature. Without monomial dependency cycles, triangular elimination gives full column rank. More generally the kernel can only come from directed cycles of monomial fractional rows with equal curvature. Indeed, interpret \(2\alpha\) as an input probability vector and reverse the arrows from child to inputs. Each nonmonomial step strictly decreases curvature; a monomial step preserves it and has a single successor. A recurrent class of the restricted substochastic matrix is therefore a deterministic equal-curvature cycle. Equivalently, eliminate the strict curvature blocks; the remaining equal-level blocks are deterministic partial transition matrices: several columns may enter one face. Pruning their transient trees leaves exactly the recurrent directed cycles. A cycle has zero entropy and allows a constant mass circulation until one mass reaches zero or one. After these harmless cycles are removed, (7) is injective. The rooted middle forest and KKT order therefore do not, by themselves, provide a lossless leaf reduction. Half-integrality of the flow vertices does not repair this issue. ## 5. The remaining sufficient lemma For a fixed sector write \(P_s\) for its original incidence-flow polytope and \(H_s\) for the sum of its perspectives and triangle entropies. The universal comparison sought is $$ \max_{q\in P_s}H_s(q)<\Phi_D \quad\text{for every nonempty one-sided pattern }s.\tag{8} $$ The existing pure-pattern, identity and [fixed-triangle boundary theorems](actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md) control atom patterns. The original endpoint Green theorem does not control the intervening perspective pointwise. A sufficient new step would map a fractional maximizer into the original complete or source-permitted smoothed flow spaces while comparing **total** entropy and preserving the original face demands. Equation (2) requires transport between actual opposite-parity outer components. Equations (6)--(7) show why this cannot simply be declared a feasible lossless motion inside the same strict sector. A direct quantitative upper inequality could also suffice, provided it retains the fractional masses and shared targets. The network, forest and leakage statements hold on the whole closed polytope. The KKT and curvature claims assume the stated finite positive multipliers; their existence is not asserted. This research note proves no new group representation, relative fundamental class, universal sector bound, or original-invariant asymptotic. ## Scope Deterministic transition blocks need not be permutation blocks. Transient monomial trees are pruned before recurrent cycles are identified. The reduction does not establish inequality (8).

title: A flat cap has no uniform local exponential angular mismatch bound
status: Exact flat-cap obstruction to a local exponential angular gap
text: # A flat cap has no uniform local exponential angular mismatch bound The flat-cap example is a local limitation on phase suppression. It is not a lower bound for the full source or a filling period. At the residual cap \(x=b=0\), \(\sigma=2\), the literal raw coefficient is \[ [c^{d-j}y^j]H_V=(-1)^j A_j,\qquad A_j=\csc^2\frac{\theta}{2}\prod_{r=1}^j \frac{\sin^2(r\theta)}{\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)}, \qquad \theta=\frac{\pi}{N},\quad d=N-1. \tag{1} \] This follows directly from the [full-interval source identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md). At \(x=b=0\), the only start is \(i=0\) and \[ K_{0,j}=y^j\prod_{r=1}^j4\sin^2(r\theta),\qquad \alpha_r=-4\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta). \] The exact product \[ \prod_{r=0}^{d}4\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)=4 \] then gives (1), including the sign from the original unused factors and the common raw sign. No factor is removed. For \(0\le j\le M=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\), the sequence \(A_j\) is positive and decreasing, because \(\sin(j\theta)\le\sin((j+\tfrac12)\theta)\) on this range. Also \[ A_j\le A_0=\csc^2(\theta/2)\le N^2. \tag{2} \] The monotonicity of sine gives the telescoping lower bound \[ \prod_{r=1}^j\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)} \ge\prod_{r=1}^j\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+1)\theta)} =\frac{\sin\theta}{\sin((j+1)\theta)}. \] Consequently, for \(N\ge3\), \[ A_j\ge\frac{4\cos^2(\theta/2)}{\sin^2((j+1)\theta)} \ge4\cos^2(\theta/2)\ge3. \tag{3} \] Fix \(0<a<b<1/2\) and choose integer endpoints \(L_N\sim aN\), \(U_N\sim bN\) with \(U_N-L_N\) even. They lie in the original LEFT range for all sufficiently large \(N\). At the ordinary positive radius and common phase \(c=y=1\), the sharp stop-window polynomial and its actual absolute envelope are \[ W_N=\sum_{j=L_N}^{U_N}(-1)^j A_j,\qquad E_N=\sum_{j=L_N}^{U_N}A_j. \] Pairing consecutive terms of the decreasing sequence and keeping the last term gives \[ |W_N|\ge A_{U_N}\ge3,\qquad E_N\le N^3,\qquad \frac{|W_N|}{E_N}\ge\frac3{N^3}. \tag{4} \] The actual cap character is aligned only when the \(c\) and \(y\) phases differ by \(\pi\). At the phases used in (4), they are equal, so their distance to that supported alignment is \(\pi/2\), measured by the smallest maximum circular distance after optimizing the common phase. Nevertheless no fixed constants \(C,\kappa>0\) can satisfy \(\lvert W_N\rvert\le C e^{-\kappa N}E_N\) on all these levels. The retained alternating terms leave endpoint currents of at least polynomial size; there is no strict local stop-action gap at the cap. Therefore the regular-window angular theorem cannot be extended to a flat cap merely by assigning it the same opposite-sign incidence labels. An odd MAIN cycle involving such a cap does not by itself supply the product-envelope exponential loss used by the regular cycle-packing argument. This does not exclude cancellation after original shared coefficient extraction, a combined analytic block estimate with other ports, or a different source-preserving treatment of the cap boundaries. It makes no assertion that \(W_N\) occurs uncoupled in the full invariant. The proof is exact for every \(N\ge3\) and window lying in the stated range. It uses no asymptotic coefficient formula or numerical experiment. The [stationary MAIN-cycle theorem](research_stationary_noncross_main_cycle_obstruction.md) uses the cap character while keeping this limitation explicit.

title: An exact positive moment form for the original flat-cap coefficients
text: # An exact positive moment form for the original flat-cap coefficients 31 October 2026. analytical research lemma. Root derived the proof; two independent readers checked it in full. This constructs a positive inner product from the original cap weights. It does not prove that the adjacent CROSS polynomial is a contraction for that form, or establish the open original-demand convolution bound. ## 1. The actual finite weights Fix an integer N>=3, d=N-1 and theta=pi/N. The raw protected cap coefficient is (-1)^j U_j, where U_j=csc^2(theta/2) product_(r=1)^j sin^2(r theta)/sin^2((r+1/2)theta), 0<=j<=d. Write m_j=U_j/U_0. The statement is that there is a positive random variable X_N such that E X_N^j=m_j, 0<=j<=d. (1) Its support is not confined to [0,1]. In particular no Hausdorff-moment or pointwise contraction conclusion follows from (1). ## 2. Exact Euler product and beta factors Euler's sine product gives, with positive factors for this whole range, m_j=[Gamma(j+1)Gamma(3/2)/Gamma(j+3/2)]^2 product_(k>=1) B_(kN)(j)^2, (2) where B_a(s)= Gamma(a)Gamma(a-s-1/2) /[Gamma(a-1/2)Gamma(a-s)] * Gamma(a+s+1)Gamma(a+3/2) /[Gamma(a+1)Gamma(a+s+3/2)]. (3) Indeed each k contributes, before squaring, product_(r=1)^j [(kN-r)/(kN-r-1/2)] [(kN+r)/(kN+r+1/2)], which is exactly (3). The remaining product r/(r+1/2) is the prefactor in (2). This derives the shifts and constants from the literal cap, not from a free choice of moment functional. Let T_1,T_2 be independent Beta(1,1/2) variables. For each k>=1 and i=1,2 let independently A_(k,i) ~ Beta(kN-1/2,1/2), B_(k,i) ~ Beta(kN+1,1/2), Z_(k,i)=B_(k,i)/A_(k,i). All variables mentioned are mutually independent. The elementary beta integral gives E T_i^s=Gamma(s+1)Gamma(3/2)/Gamma(s+3/2), E Z_(k,i)^s=B_(kN)(s), (4) for -1<s<N-1/2; these restrictions are sufficient simultaneously for the factors here. In particular all moments in (1) are finite. Define finite positive products X_(N,K)=T_1 T_2 product_(k=1)^K Z_(k,1)Z_(k,2). Equations (2)--(4) give the desired moments in the limit, once convergence and uniform integrability are checked. ## 3. Convergence with no formal infinite-product inference For fixed s in a compact subinterval of (-1,N-1/2), the gamma ratio expansion in (3) gives log B_a(s)=O_s(a^-2), a->infinity. (5) The a^-1 terms of the inverse-beta and beta factors are respectively s/(2a) and -s/(2a), and cancel. The expansion and its first two s derivatives are uniform on a small neighborhood of zero. Consequently E log Z_(k,i)=O((kN)^-2), Var(log Z_(k,i))=O((kN)^-2). (6) Also log T_i belongs to L2 by its beta density at zero and one. The means are absolutely summable. Independence makes the centered partial sums Cauchy in L2, since their tail variance is the sum of the tail variances. Thus log X_(N,K) converges in L2 to a finite real random variable Y_N. Set X_N=exp(Y_N)>0. The products converge in probability. Fix an integer 1<=j<=d. Choose epsilon>0 with j+epsilon<N-1/2. The beta moments at that exponent exist; (5) shows sup_K E X_(N,K)^(j+epsilon)<infinity. (7) Hence X_(N,K)^j are uniformly integrable. Convergence in probability and uniform integrability give convergence of their expectations to E X_N^j. Equations (2)--(4) identify the limit as m_j. The zero moment is one. This proves (1) with every original weight retained. Removing any one factor leaves the same convergent log series, measurable in the other independent variables. Thus the separated factor remains independent of the positive limiting remainder. The measure is non-atomic and has unbounded support. For non-atomicity, separate the independent T_1 factor, which has a continuous positive density on (0,1). For unbounded support, separate the independent 1/A_(1,1) factor, which is unbounded, from the remaining positive random product. The remainder is bounded below by some positive number on an event of positive probability. Independence then gives arbitrarily large X_N with positive probability. ## 4. Exact finite-dimensional Cauchy inequality For m with 2m<=d, put on polynomials of degree at most m <p,q>_N=U_0 E[p(X_N) conjugate(q(X_N))]. Its matrix in the monomial basis is EXACTLY (U_(i+j))_(0<=i,j<=m). It is positive definite: a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots, while X_N is non-atomic. Thus |<p,q>_N|^2 <= <p,p>_N <q,q>_N. (8) At the even levels N=2m0 of the original cap/CROSS problem, its cutoff M=m0-1 satisfies 2M=d-1. The entire original cutoff polynomial space therefore carries this positive Gram form. The alternating cap character is retained by evaluating p at -X_N, rather than deleting (-1)^j. To express the precise missing step, use the coefficients C_(j,h) and range J_n of the original-demand convolution. Define the literal projected polynomial F_(N,n)(t)=sum_(j in J_n) C_(j,n-j) t^j. Then its actual signed coefficient is exactly (-1)^d U_0 E F_(N,n)(-X_N). (9) For n>M the cutoff in J_n remains in F; (9) is not a full-sum replacement or an orthogonality claim. Formula (8) supplies a genuine positive inner product, but no bound here compares its quadratic norm of F_(N,n)(-t) with the endpoint convolution involving V_j. That comparison is the remaining issue. In particular unbounded support prevents replacing the expectation by a maximum on [0,1]. No numerical asymptotic test is needed for (1)--(9). They neither transport projected sectors through the full Casimir source nor prove the original invariant's volume conjecture. ## 5. The moment threshold and the original even-level cutoff The convergence argument also gives E X_N^s<infinity for EVERY real 0<=s<N-1/2: choose a slightly larger moment exponent still inside that interval and apply the same uniform-integrability argument. Conversely, separate the independent factor A_(1,1)^(-1) from the limiting product. The beta density gives E A_(1,1)^(-s)=infinity whenever s>=N-1/2. The remaining factor is strictly positive and independent. Tonelli's theorem therefore gives the sharp statement E X_N^s<infinity iff 0<=s<N-1/2. (10) Here the equivalence is restricted to nonnegative s. No assertion about negative moments is needed. A nonzero polynomial p of degree r satisfies |p(t)|^2>=c t^(2r) for all sufficiently large positive t, while the lower degree terms bound its squared modulus above by C(1+t^(2r)). Consequently its squared norm is finite exactly when 2r<N-1/2. At even N=2m0 this is r<=m0-1=M, precisely the original RIGHT cutoff. Thus that entire polynomial space has finite positive norm, while every polynomial of the next or a higher degree has infinite norm. At odd levels the maximal degree is floor((N-1)/2); its identification with an original one-sided sector is NOT asserted, since the odd central row belongs to CROSS. There is also an exact finite functional relation. Define L_N(p)=U_0 E p(X_N), and let D=t partial_t act diagonally on monomials. Sines of D mean the corresponding finite diagonal operators. The literal ratio U_(j+1)/U_j gives L_N( t sin^2(theta(D+3/2))p - sin^2(theta(D+1))p )=0, deg p<=d-1. (11) Indeed (11) on t^j is exactly sin^2((j+3/2)theta)U_(j+1)-sin^2((j+1)theta)U_j=0. The degree restriction is essential. At j=d the formal numerator sin^2(N theta) vanishes, but the other term would require the divergent Nth moment. Equation (11) is not an identity on all degree-d polynomials and does not authorize deleting that terminal contribution. It supplies no self-adjointness or contraction claim for the adjacent continuant. ## 6. A finite algebraic evaluation at even levels The beta product proves positivity, but the required finite functional also has an exact algebraic realization. Keep N=2m0 and M=m0-1, so d=2M+1. In this section L_N includes the original factor U_0. Gram--Schmidt on 1,t,...,t^M gives monic orthogonal polynomials p_r and positive squared norms h_r=L_N(p_r^2), 0<=r<=M. All these coefficients are real algebraic: the moments U_j are products of squared sines at rational multiples of pi, hence belong to a real cyclotomic field, and Gram--Schmidt uses only field operations. Define the (M+1)-by-(M+1) symmetric tridiagonal matrix J_cap by (J_cap)_(r,r)=L_N(t p_r^2)/h_r, 0<=r<=M, (J_cap)_(r-1,r)=(J_cap)_(r,r-1)=sqrt(h_r/h_(r-1)), 1<=r<=M. Every displayed moment is finite: the largest degree is 2M+1=d. For any vector v, let P_v=sum_r v_r p_r/sqrt(h_r). Orthogonality implies that multiplication by t has exactly the displayed entries, since t p_r has degree r+1. Thus v^* J_cap v=L_N(t |P_v(t)|^2)>0 for v!=0. The matrix is positive definite; its off-diagonal entries are positive. Its eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_(M+1) are therefore positive and simple, and every eigenvector has nonzero first coordinate (use the tridiagonal recurrence starting at that coordinate). Define w_a=U_0 |(unit eigenvector at lambda_a)_0|^2>0. The characteristic polynomial p_(M+1) is still orthogonal to every polynomial of degree at most M. To check this without asserting its squared norm, define it by the last tridiagonal recurrence: the t p_M term pairs to zero against p_s for s<=M-2 by symmetry, and the chosen last two recurrence coefficients cancel its pairings with p_(M-1) and p_M. Only moments through 2M+1 occur. Its square need not be integrable, and in fact is not. For any polynomial f of degree at most 2M+1, divide it by p_(M+1): f=p_(M+1) q+r, deg q<=M, deg r<=M. The first term has zero L_N value and vanishes at every eigenvalue. The spectral measure above reproduces L_N on degree<=M: by the tridiagonal recurrence, p_j(J_cap)e_0 is a multiple of e_j for j<=M, so both functionals vanish on p_j for 1<=j<=M and give U_0 on p_0. It follows that L_N(f)=sum_(a=1)^(M+1) w_a f(lambda_a), deg f<=d. (12) All nodes and weights are real algebraic in a finite algebraic extension of the moment field. In particular the original cap convolution (9) is an exact finite algebraic evaluation with positive weights. Its original cutoff remains in F_(N,n). Formula (12) does not extend to degree d+1: the original moment there diverges, while the finite quadrature would assign it a finite number. This constructs the cap's own positive Jacobi matrix. It does not identify it with the different Jacobi matrix obtained by normalizing the adjacent continuant. No norm comparison between those two metrics, or volume bound for the original source, follows from (12). ## Inputs The weights are those of the [exact protected cap](research_trace_one_mark_and_cap_turn_interface.md). The polynomial in (9) is precisely the [original-demand cap/CROSS convolution](research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). No triangle factor, unused spectral product or projected endpoint is changed by defining this inner product. The positive moment metric retains the stated degree cutoff. The endpoint norm comparison remains unproved, and the next square moment diverges.

title: Fractional rows and the obstruction to entropy-preserving covers
text: # Fractional rows and the obstruction to entropy-preserving covers 31 October 2026. **Open research interface.** The lemmas below concern the convex weighted LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT comparison on the original marked source. They disprove an automatic entropy-preserving cover construction. They do **not** disprove the desired strict fixed-sector capacity bound by complete volume, or any statement about the original quantum invariant. The [fractional forest reduction](research_fixed_sector_fractional_forest_reduction.md) gives the exact flow network and stationary equations. This note isolates what an unbranched cover would additionally have to achieve. The [finite-sector cover theorem](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md) uses “cover” in a different sense: a finite cover of label patterns by valid shared-radius estimates, not a topological covering space. ## 1. Projected flows and their entropy Every original ordinary face has demand one; the two protected faces have demand zero. CROSS retains its two original triangle rows, each with supply one half. For a triangle allocation \(a\ge0\), \(\sum a=1/2\), the exact entropy is $$ C(a)=\sum_j f(a_j),\qquad f(s)=\frac{\Lambda(\pi s)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi s)}{\pi}, \qquad f''(s)=-\frac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi s)}\le-2\pi.\tag{1} $$ Consequently, including closed boundary allocations by continuity, $$ C(\overline a)-\overline{C(a)} \ge \pi\,\overline{\|a-\overline a\|^2}.\tag{2} $$ This is the normalization of the [fixed-triangle capacity lemma](actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md). At a selected LEFT or RIGHT port let \(o\) be the overloaded ordinary middle, \(p\) the opposite middle, and \(x,y\) the original outer faces. The fractional comparison row is $$ q_o=1-\frac{t}{2},\qquad(q_x,q_p,q_y)=t\alpha, \qquad0\le t\le1,\quad\sum\alpha=\frac{1}{2}, \qquad h_{\mathrm{env}}=tC(\alpha).\tag{3} $$ At \(t=0\) this is the pure identity endpoint \(e_o\). At \(t=1\) it is one retained triangle \(\alpha\) and the pure-middle half triangle \(e_o/2\). All protected incidences remain zero; the four original faces are distinct, so \(o\notin\{x,p,y\}\). For a rational feasible flow choose \(q\) with all \(qt_e\) integral. Clearing denominators specifies \(qt_e\) retained half-triangle atoms and \(q(1-t_e)\) identity atoms at each selected port. It does not specify a cover with closed face stars. ## 2. A necessary cover-realization condition Allow \(q\) lifts of every face and \(q\) copies of every original coupon and triangle incidence. At each lifted face require exactly one copy of each original incident corner. Copies may be assigned to lifts by arbitrary permutations: no common sheet labeling or trivial monodromy is assumed. An actual unbranched source cover must also retain the cyclic order, but we do not impose that additional restriction here. Require the following conditions: - Each ordinary lifted face has total load one; every protected lift has load zero. - Every CROSS triangle copy and every retained triangle copy has supply one half. - The mean allocation of a CROSS row is its prescribed \(a_r\). Among the \(qt_e\) retained copies of a selected row, the mean is its prescribed normalized allocation \(\alpha_e\). - The two atom counts at every selected port are the prescribed counts above. These are necessary for an unbranched original-source cover representing the given projected flow. We permit more incidence permutations than a genuine geometric cover; a failure here cannot be repaired solely by choosing different source monodromy. Let \(H\) be the fractional entropy and \(H_{\mathrm{cov}}\) the sum of the triangle entropies on such a realization. Equation (2) gives $$ \begin{aligned} qH-H_{\mathrm{cov}}\ \ge{}& \pi\sum_{r\ \mathrm{CROSS}}\sum_{s=1}^q \|a_{r,s}-a_r\|^2\\ &+\pi\sum_e\sum_{s\ \mathrm{retained}} \|\alpha_{e,s}-\alpha_e\|^2. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ Therefore entropy preservation—or the entropy increase needed to deduce \(H\le\operatorname{Vol}/q\) from a cover-volume bound—requires every positive-mass triangle allocation to be identical on all its copies. Varying angles across sheets cannot increase entropy while preserving the projected flow. The original bounded bipartite flow becomes integral after scaling by two, so it can be decomposed into feasible pure-atom flows. This does not supply the desired entropy comparison: (4) has the opposite direction. Such a decomposition can strictly lose entropy. ## 3. Quantitative obstruction at a fractional sink Suppose a port \(e\) has \(0<t_e<1\), overloaded face \(o\), and no other fractional row uses \(o\) as a retained-triangle input. Distinct strict overloads have distinct children, because each contributes more than one half to a demand-one face. All other load at \(o\) therefore comes from CROSS triangles or retained triangles of terminal \(t=1\) rows. Let \(M\) be their number of corner incidences at \(o\). Feasibility forces \(M>0\). The prescribed mean of these corners sums to \(t_e/2\). At a lift whose selected atom has state \(s\in\{0,1\}\), exact face closure requires their sum to be \(s/2\). Their total deviation from their projected values is \((s-t_e)/2\). Cauchy–Schwarz on these \(M\) corners and (4) yield $$ \begin{aligned} qH-H_{\mathrm{cov}} &\ge\frac{\pi}{M}\sum_{\text{lifts of }o} \left(\frac{s-t_e}{2}\right)^2\\ &=q\,\frac{\pi t_e(1-t_e)}{4M}>0. \end{aligned}\tag{5} $$ There are exactly \(qt_e\) state-one copies. The estimate uses only each lifted star, and permits arbitrary permutations between different face lifts. Its loss per sheet is independent of \(q\); even asymptotically lossless atomization is unavailable under these hypotheses. In particular this applies to a single fractional row. More generally, draw a dependency arrow from a fractional child used as an input to the child of the row using it. An acyclic dependency graph has a sink to which (5) applies. At a finite positive stationary point, the [exact KKT equations](research_fixed_sector_fractional_forest_reduction.md) give, for every genuinely fractional row, $$ L_o=\exp\bigl(2Q(L_x,L_p,L_y)\bigr) \ge L_x+L_p+L_y.\tag{6} $$ The inequality is strict when the input has at least two positive weights. Nonmonomial dependency arrows strictly increase curvature. If there are no equal-curvature monomial cycles, the fractional dependency graph is acyclic and (5) applies. Terminal \(t=1\) rows need not obey this ordering; their triangle corners are already included among the \(M\) corners. This does not assert that a global sector maximizer is fractional or has value above complete volume. It shows that a fractional stationary point's forest and curvature order do not supply the proposed lossless cover. ## 4. An exact original five-port flow Use the literal width-three word, in the original compiler's zero-based slots, $$ [1,3,2,1,3],\qquad\text{marked top cap }0. $$ The protected faces are \(\{0,1\}\), the ordinary faces are \(\{2,3,4,5,6\}\), and the original quartets are $$ \begin{array}{c|c} 0&(1,0,4,2)\\ 1&(2,0,5,3)\\ 2&(4,2,6,5)\\ 3&(1,4,0,6)\\ 4&(6,5,0,3) \end{array}\tag{7} $$ The ten triangle rows are distinct, all fifteen edges occur twice, and the seven vertices form the original simple-white sphere. This is the exact reduced width-three source in the [shared-radius theorem](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md), not an abstract graph requiring a new plat adapter. Set only port 3 to RIGHT, with the other four CROSS. For \(0\le\beta\le1/2\), take \(t_3=2\beta\) and \(\alpha_3=e_6/2\). Its loads and entropy are $$ q_4=1-\beta,\qquad q_6=\beta,\qquad h_3=0.\tag{8} $$ The two CROSS rows of a port are its original \((x,b,y)\) and \((x,c,y)\), in that order. Their nonzero face loads are $$ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{port}&\text{first row}&\text{second row}\\ \hline 0&\{2:\tfrac12\}&\{4:\beta,\ 2:\tfrac12-\beta\}\\ 1&\{2:\beta,\ 3:\tfrac12-\beta\}&\{3:\tfrac12\}\\ 2&\{5:\tfrac12\}&\{6:\tfrac12\}\\ 4&\{5:\tfrac12\}&\{6:\tfrac12-\beta,\ 3:\beta\} \end{array}\tag{9} $$ Every row has supply one half and is supported on its original triangle. Equations (8)–(9) give load exactly one at each ordinary face and zero at both protected faces. Thus the full shared constraints hold. The entropy is $$ H(\beta)=3C(\beta,\tfrac12-\beta,0).\tag{10} $$ It is strictly concave, vanishes at both endpoints, and has a unique maximum on this particular feasible segment at \(\beta=1/4\). There, $$ t_3=\frac{1}{2},\qquad H(\tfrac14)=\frac{6G}{\pi}>0,\tag{11} $$ where \(G\) is Catalan's constant. This segment is not asserted to contain the full fixed-sector maximizer. At face 4 the other three incidences are the face-4 corners of port 0's second row and both rows of port 2. Their projected loads are \(1/4,0,0\). Equation (5) gives at least \(\pi/48\) entropy loss per sheet, for every cover degree and every incidence permutation. In this sparse example the loss is even stronger: every admissible pure-atom realization preserving the projected flow has **zero entropy**. A nonnegative corner with projected mean zero vanishes on every copy. Thus both port-2 face-4 corners stay zero, and face-4 closure forces port 0's second row to a triangle vertex. Face-2 closure then forces port 1's first row to a vertex; face-3 closure forces port 4's second row to a vertex. All other rows were already monomial. This reasoning is local at each lifted star and does not require global sheet labels. Atomization is not empty: the \(\beta=0\) and \(\beta=1/2\) flows form a feasible two-sheet atomization with average \(\beta=1/4\). Their total entropy is zero, rather than twice (11). Integral decomposition therefore exists, but loses entropy in exactly the direction that the proposed cover-volume comparison would need to preserve. ## 5. The remaining general question The desired universal statement is still $$ \max_{\text{original fixed-sector flow}} H_{\mathrm{env}}<\Phi_D. $$ The example has neither a certified fixed-sector capacity excess nor an original quantum asymptotic excess. It rules out automatic unbranched cover atomization that preserves the projected flow without entropy loss. A different construction must change the projected flow and prove a compensating global entropy inequality, or allow branching and prove an appropriate new volume comparison. Summed angles \(2\pi q\) alone do not provide either condition. The focused exact check used the original Morse compiler and rational arithmetic: ten triangle incidences, fifteen paired edges, five rational flows, forty row sums, thirty-five face targets, and the exact two-endpoint average. The coefficient \(1/48\) is exact. The entropy and covering inequalities are analytical; these finite checks are not a proof of a general covering topology or of the open universal sector bound. The universal capacity comparison remains open.

title: One-sided comparison atoms, their convex mixtures, and the missing geometric adapter
text: # One-sided comparison atoms, their convex mixtures, and the missing geometric adapter PRIVATE analytical audit, 31 October 2026. No workspace/public files are changed. This assesses the original LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT weighted comparison, not the phase-sensitive source itself. It gives an exact obstruction to reusing the existing hybrid circle-development proof without a new adapter; it does not prove that an optimized comparison capacity exceeds volume. ## 1. Exact source conventions and the two pure atoms For an original port (x,b,c,y), LEFT has the proved real-spectral weighted upper rate L(l)=max{ log c, Q(x,b,y)+(1/2)log c }. (1) Here every Q is the actual half-degree triangle action, with Q(w)=max_{alpha>=0, sum alpha=1/2} [ C(alpha)+sum_j alpha_j log w_j ], C(alpha)=sum_j f(alpha_j), f(s)=[Lambda(pi s)+Lambda(pi/2-pi s)]/pi. (2) There is no additive constant or change of original face targets. Each ordinary face has load one and the two protected faces load zero. All four incidences remain in their original positions. If c is protected, the finite LEFT sector is identically zero; it is not assigned a positive regularized geometric value here. The second atom forces the output $(0,1/2,0)$; the first pure-middle atom has the stated identity contribution. The linked triangle-capacity duality retains these boundary allocations. There is also a useful uniform statement for arbitrary pure atom patterns. Choose, at every selected LEFT/RIGHT port, either its identity endpoint or its fixed output/input half-triangle; leave other ports CROSS. At every such allocation the proposed entropy is EXACTLY the frozen full endpoint entropy h at the same original degree vector: at a pure middle endpoint h=0, and at the half seam h is the one retained triangle entropy. The whole source balance equations are unchanged. Every nonempty pure atom pattern therefore lies in the closed set with some middle load >=1/2. The unique geometric endpoint theorem gives the SAME fixed positive one-sided gap on that closed set. Empty polytopes have value -infinity. Thus the pure patterns themselves are not the unresolved comparison. Their strictness can be proved by the existing actual endpoint geometry, or by the fixed-triangle lemma and actual identity-smoothing bounds. ## 2. The exact convexified comparison problem For positive face weights, (1)--(2) give the identity L(l)=max_{0<=t<=1, alpha>=0, sum alpha=1/2} [ t C(alpha)+t alpha_x log x+t alpha_b log b +t alpha_y log y+(1-t/2)log c ]. (3) The corresponding original degree vector is q_x=t alpha_x, q_b=t alpha_b, q_y=t alpha_y, q_c=1-t/2. (4) It has total degree one and q_c>=1/2. For q_c<1 put t=2(1-q_c), h_env(q)=t C(q_x/t,q_b/t,q_y/t); (5) at q=e_c define h_env=0. This perspective is concave and continuous on its whole closed LEFT simplex: C is concave and bounded, and t C tends uniformly to zero as t tends to zero. RIGHT is its literal reflection. At CROSS ports keep the two original half-triangle allocations. For any fixed actual LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT sector, minimizing the sum of these weighted expressions minus the original ordinary log targets is exactly the maximum of the corresponding sum of h_env and triangle entropies on the original incidence-flow polytope. This follows from compact concave hypograph separation, including infeasible and nonattained cases, by the same proof as the fixed-triangle duality. This is a proved convex duality statement, not an interchange of infimum with the finitely many pure atom patterns. The variables t in (3) are independent continuous optimization variables. The pure patterns are t in {0,1}; restricting to them need not preserve the maximum of a concave objective. Therefore strict gaps for every pure pattern do not by themselves prove the fixed-sector envelope gap. ## 3. This is not the actual Green entropy The actual positive LEFT coefficient entropy is h(q)=E(q_b,1-q_c,q_x), (6) not (5). An exact source coefficient makes the distinction quantitative. At q=(1/4,0,3/4,0), the source's single-x path gives h(q)=2 integral_0^(1/4) log tan(pi s) ds =-2 Catalan/pi <0, whereas t=1/2 and alpha=(1/2,0,0) give h_env(q)=0. The frozen entropy-sign note proves this from the literal coefficient, with its scalar normalization retained. It is not a numerical example. By continuity the strict inequality persists at strictly positive local degree vectors. More explicitly, the previously proved diagonal expansion gives, as epsilon tends to zero through positive values, q=(epsilon,epsilon,1-3epsilon,epsilon), h(q)=E(epsilon,3epsilon,epsilon) =2epsilon log epsilon+O(epsilon)<0, h_env(q)=6epsilon C(1/6,1/6,1/6)>0. (7) Thus the actual full-h volume/unique-maximum theorem cannot be applied pointwise to replace h_env by h. This is a local comparison obstruction, not a counterexample to a shared capacity bound. ## 4. Why the geometric construction does not transfer At an interior fractional stationary row, 0<t<1, variation of alpha in (3) gives the actual triangle angles alpha at the shared positive curvatures (x,b,y). Variation of t gives Q(x,b,y)=(1/2)log c. (8) The actual normalized input center angles are alpha, however, while the source balance equations use t alpha. Attaching an ordinary positive input triangle and a collapsed output triangle with angle load e_c/2 would change the prescribed face loads by Delta q=(1-t)(alpha_x e_x+alpha_b e_b +alpha_y e_y-e_c/2). (9) For a single fractional port in an original simple sphere this vector is nonzero: the four labels are distinct and at least one allowed input corner has positive alpha. Its c component is -(1-t)/2. At ordinary faces the resulting center-star angles would be 2pi(1+Delta q_f), not the required multiples of 2pi. Thus even stationarity of the fractional comparison does not license that tangent-circle development. For several ports one would need to prove cancellation of the SUM of (9); it is not among the comparison's face equations. Even such cancellation would not alone construct the collapsed original contact triples or pairings. There is a second, independently precise failure of a hypothesis in the hybrid tight-cut theorem. Its GREEN modification merges two half-supply triangle rows into a unit-supply four-incidence row and can only INCREASE each Hall capacity. The fractional comparison instead has an input row of supply t/2 and a deterministic c row of supply 1-t/2. For a set S, its local capacity is (t/2) 1_{ {x,b,y} touches S } +(1-t/2) 1_{ c in S }. (10) For an ordinary singleton S={b}, this is t/2, whereas the original complete pair contributes 1/2. For an ordinary outer singleton not c, it is t/2 whereas the complete pair contributes one. Thus the monotone Hall comparison used to identify all tight sets with actual permitted digons fails. Artificially imposed zero corners need not come from those original cuts. The existing relative-interior and marked-piece geometry theorems consequently do not apply by relabeling this row as GREEN. Finally the actual signed relative-chain proof counts the original two cut balls with their prescribed face maps and integer oriented triangles. Replacing a triangle volume by t times its volume is not a constructed relative fundamental chain of the original group. The formula t C is therefore not itself a representation volume. A new construction would have to supply common ordered contact triples, all original shaded maps, the original peripheral decorations and an actual relative class. None of those follows from convex separation or the scalar envelope identity. These are failures of the proposed direct adapter, not a theorem that no different representation/capacity argument can control the mixtures. ## 5. Legitimate routes still available One may choose a different shared positive radius vector for each ACTUAL fixed LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT sector, since the finite source is first decomposed into those sectors. A strict weighted certificate for each such sector does not require its comparison atoms to have a geometric realization. Likewise an anchored finite certificate bounding one selected one-sided port and the full envelope at all spectators is legitimate. Cluster is independently developing and certifying this stronger sufficient route. For a general theorem without such certificates, the missing input is one of: a strict bound for the exact fractional problem (3)--(5); a source-preserving finite comparison that separates the pure atoms before extraction; or a direct shared bound retaining the actual oscillatory one-sided coefficients.
