Existing pure-atom, identity-forest and hybrid representation results alone do not furnish this input. ## Audit provenance Independently read the frozen hybrid piece, tight-cut, diagonal identity, full-kernel entropy and unique-max proofs, the LEFT weighted envelope, and the newly drafted fixed-triangle capacity lemma. Identities (3)--(5), (8)--(10) are direct finite-dimensional algebra; (7) uses the already proved original coefficient/closed-entropy identities. No numerical experiment or new public theorem is claimed, and no genuine-q normal is required in this fixed-root discussion.

title: Free spectral retuning removes the negative diagonal singularity
status: Free-spectrum diagonal retuning with a uniform cap lower bound
text: # Free spectral retuning removes the negative diagonal singularity Retuning applies to a global maximum with freely varying spectra. It is not a statement about fixed-spectrum local maxima or a uniform finite-$N$ estimate in a shrinking cap neighborhood. ## 1. A uniform lower bound from one exact word Put k=cos(pi delta), 0<delta<1/2, and alpha_k(t)=4[k^2-sin^2(pi t)], beta(t)=4sin^2(pi t), eta_k(t)=k^2/sin^2(pi t), rho_k(t;x)=[1+x+sqrt((1-x)^2+4eta_k(t)x)]/2. For 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2 and 0<=xi<=w=nu-mu, the exact sharp LEFT functional is h_delta=B_delta+int_mu^nu log beta+J^*, B_delta=int_0^mu log|alpha_k|+int_nu^(1/2) log|alpha_k|, J^*=inf_(x>0){int_mu^nu log rho_k(t;x)dt-xi log x}. (1) The [normalized positive-eta word](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) has, for EVERY outer degree, a monotone word x^K y^(r-K) with no y-to-x transition. Its coefficient is exactly one. This is why its coefficient entropy is nonnegative. Directly in (1), rho_k>=max(1,x), so, for 0<=xi<=w, int_mu^nu log rho_k-xi log x>=0, J^*>=0. (2) This includes both extreme outer loads and w=0. It uses the actual word normalization; no missing sine or outside-row factor is discarded. The full unused-row integral satisfies the exact identity int_0^(1/2) log|alpha_k(t)|dt=0. (3) Indeed alpha=4cos(pi(t+delta))cos(pi(t-delta)). The two translated log-cosine integrals have sum independent of delta, since their upper endpoint derivatives agree by reflection about 1/2; at delta=0 the sum is zero. The integrable endpoint and interior logarithms justify continuation to the closed delta interval. Consequently h_delta>=int_mu^nu g_k(t)dt, g_k(t)=log[sin^2(pi t)/|k^2-sin^2(pi t)|]. (4) There is an elementary UNIFORM bound for its negative part. The integrand is negative only when sin^2(pi t)<k^2/2. On [0,1/2], sin(pi t)>=2t, so this set lies inside [0,k/2], and there (-g_k(t))_+ <= 2 log[k/(2t)]. Extend this positive upper bound to [0,k/2] and integrate: int_0^(1/2) (-g_k)_+ dt <= int_0^(k/2) 2log[k/(2t)]dt=k. Thus, simultaneously for ALL closed degree vectors, h_delta(mu,nu,xi)>=-k=-cos(pi delta). (5) The reflected RIGHT functional has the same bound. For full-row intervals 0<=mu<=nu<=1, use both outside intervals on [0,1]. Reflection t->1-t doubles (3) and the negative-part estimate, yielding h_delta^full(mu,nu,xi)>=-2k. (6) The constants in (5)--(6) do not depend on the interval or outer proportion. In particular no strict outer-degree condition is hidden. For clarity, the continuous cap functional is identically zero: at k=0, alpha=-beta and rho_0=max(1,x), so h_(1/2)=0 at every degree. This also is a uniform limit of the open-spectral functional. For small k the L1 norm of g_k is O(k): set s=sin(pi t)/k near t=0; log[s^2/|1-s^2|] is integrable on bounded s intervals. Above s=2, |g_k|<=C k^2 csc^2(pi t), whose integral from arcsin(2k)/pi to 1/2 is O(k). The reflected endpoint is the same. Also 0<=J^*<=J(x=1) <=int_0^(1/2) log(1+k/(2t))dt =[(1+k)log(1+k)-k log k]/2 on a half interval, and at most twice this on a full interval. Thus |h_delta|<=C k log(1/k) uniformly as k decreases to zero. The main lower bound (5) is sharper in the direction needed below. ## 2. Retuning a diagonal along any admissible opening At a diagonal mu=nu=a, xi=0, (3) implies h_delta(a,a,0)=0 FOR EVERY delta. (7) Let q(eps) be any feasible opening, with the original face loads unchanged globally. At this port its interval and outer split may be arbitrary admissible functions of eps. Choose the open real spectrum delta_eps=arccos(eps^2)/pi. Then (5)--(7) give h_(delta_eps)(q(eps))-h_delta(q(0))>=-eps^2 (8) for LEFT/RIGHT, and >=-2eps^2 for full rows. This holds uniformly in all closed outer loads, including monomial openings, every diagonal center, and variable interval lengths. In particular there is no negative eps log(1/eps) contribution after this allowed retuning. Equation (8) compares different spectra at the perturbed point. It is not a continuity assertion at the old fixed delta. Because the initial diagonal value is independent of delta, this change incurs no baseline loss at a GLOBAL free-spectrum maximum. It need not remain in an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the old spectral parameter, so it does not exclude a local fixed-spectrum maximum. ## 3. Stronger gains for interior diagonal centers The uniform cap choice already suffices to neutralize every diagonal. For an affine opening at a fixed center a in (0,1), write mu_eps=a+eps B, nu_eps=a+eps C, w_eps=eps W, W=C-B>0, 0<=xi_eps<=eps W. If a!=1/2, place a simple alpha pole at the interval midpoint, using delta_eps=|1/2-(mu_eps+nu_eps)/2|. The chosen spectrum stays in a fixed strict real compact when a stays away from 0,1/2,1. Throughout the interval beta is bounded below, and |alpha_(delta_eps)(t)|<=C eps. By (2)--(4), h_(delta_eps)(q(eps))>= W eps log(1/eps)-C eps. (9) The pole's logarithm is integrable. No division by the sampled finite alpha factors is made. The lower bound is uniform in the entire closed outer split; it uses only J^*>=0, not a bounded minimizing tilt. At a=1/2, choose delta_eps=eps D with any fixed D>0. Then |alpha_(delta_eps)(t)|<=C eps^2 on the interval and beta stays bounded below. Therefore h_(delta_eps)(q(eps))>= 2W eps log(1/eps)-C eps. (10) No placement of both small poles inside the interval is necessary: their common quadratic scaling is enough. This covers a lower-half terminal diagonal by restricting its admissible opening to that half. At a=0 or1 the bound (8) is used instead; the fixed-spectrum negative monomer singularity from the [ordinary-zero barrier note](research_sharp_spectral_ordinary_zero_barrier.md) is not retained. If W=0, the port stays diagonal and (7) applies exactly. ## 4. A global activation lemma with diagonal ports allowed Consider the actual shared feasible flow fiber. Its face constraints do not involve the independently free real spectra. Let (q,delta) be a GLOBAL maximum of the sum of the specified sharp local entropies. Separate the ports into: * non-diagonal regular intervals covered by the [ordinary-zero barrier lemma](research_sharp_spectral_ordinary_zero_barrier.md), including its terminal-row calculus extension, at their fixed strict spectral parameters; * arbitrary diagonal intervals, at any initially allowed spectra; * any other terms whose change in the proposed common-target direction has no negative eps log(1/eps) term and an O(eps) remainder. Suppose an actual feasible segment q(eps) activates a removable ordinary zero at a regular port. Keep every regular spectrum fixed. Retune ONLY the diagonal-port spectra by (8), or by (9)--(10) if a positive interior opening is useful. The regular terms have a strictly positive total coefficient b of eps log(1/eps), all other regular singular coefficients are nonnegative, and every diagonal costs at most O(eps^2). For a fixed finite diagram, sum h_new - sum h_old >=b eps log(1/eps)-C eps-C'eps^2>0, contradicting global maximality. Thus diagonal ports do not obstruct the prior regular ordinary-zero exclusion when their spectra truly are free over the original real interval. Likewise, a feasible positive opening of an interior diagonal gives a strict gain by (9) or (10), provided all other affected terms satisfy the stated nonnegative-singularity conditions. Row-zero/row-one diagonals alone receive only the neutral bound; this does not exclude all such vertices or all structural identity strata. The finite Hall/residual-cycle test from the ordinary-zero barrier note still decides whether an incidence can be activated in the original fiber. No larger fractional network, projected cover, or independent local reassignment is substituted. Pole-touching non-diagonal rows can still have a negative singular term and remain outside this global lemma unless separately controlled. ## 5. Order of limits and source scope These are exact inequalities for the sharp continuum functional, with the original degree constraints and unused-product normalization. For each fixed eps>0, delta_eps is strictly between0 and1/2; only then is N sent to infinity. The subsequent eps->0 argument is a finite- dimensional variational contradiction. It asserts no uniform finite-N coefficient asymptotic when cos(pi delta) is comparable to N^-1, no nonzero lower bound through a sampled omitted-half zero, and no simultaneous eps_N or delta_N limit. Exact common scalar zeros and their spectral phases remain part of any later source reconstruction. As before, the argument is a calculus theorem for the sharp upper functional, and applies to a genuine source entropy only where its coefficient identification has been established. It does not identify the rate of a signed sum of central CROSS paths, construct a volume representation, or prove a universal complete-volume comparison. ## Scope Root and an independent reader checked the complete argument, including the exact half/full normalizations, the constants one and two in the uniform lower bound, closed outer loads, cap continuity, both interior diagonal gains, and the global feasible-direction consequence. The fixed-perturbation-before-level limit is essential. No finite-level cap asymptotic, source-period lower bound or universal volume comparison is claimed, and no numerical audit is used as a substitute for the proof.

title: Boundary reduction for a global full sharp-source maximum
status: Global full-fiber maxima: ordinary positivity and no diagonals
text: # Boundary reduction for a global full sharp-source maximum The variational theorem concerns the entire original flow fiber with freely varying spectra. It does not assert finite-coefficient asymptotics, phase alignment or a volume bound. ## 1. Original fiber and explicit hypotheses Fix an original simple-white certified plat. Its white sphere is a simple triangulation, the protected faces u,v are adjacent along the marked MAIN edge, and a port pairs two shaded triangles across a MATCHING edge. Keep every original incidence, including the protected zeros. Let P be the FULL nonnegative transport fiber: each port supplies1, each ordinary face demands1, and each protected face demands0. No LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT label inequalities are imposed on P. A local vector q=(X,B,C,Y) with sum1 is written mu=B, nu=1-C, xi=X, zeta=Y=nu-mu-xi. The actual complete geometric flow qG belongs to P. It has positive load on EVERY ordinary incidence, zero on protected incidences, and both middle loads strictly less than1/2. Its two literal triangle allocations are positive on every ordinary triangle corner. Each port has at least one ordinary outer incidence: the two protected faces are joined by a MAIN edge, not by its outer MATCHING edge. Therefore qG_x+qG_y>0 at every port. (1) For 0<=delta<=1/2 define h_delta on the FULL interval by the original [sharp functional](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) h_delta(q)=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta| +int_nu^1 log|alpha_delta| +inf_(x>0){int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;x,1)dt -xi log x}, (2) alpha_delta=4[cos^2(pi delta)-sin^2(pi t)]. Here Lambda=beta rho, with beta(t)=4 sin^2(pi t) and rho the exact [positive eta-word root](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md), eta=cos^2(pi delta)/sin^2(pi t). Endpoint values are the continuous ones. In particular h_(1/2)=0 for ALL q. At delta=0, h_0 is the [continuous full-kernel endpoint entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md). On CROSS (B,C<=1/2), h_0(q)=max_(a+b=q) [Ctri(a)+Ctri(b)], (3) where the two original triangle rows have supply1/2 and their indicated middle loads B,C. This is the exact latent split of the original port, not independently reassigned angles. The all-CROSS geometric allocation has [total endpoint entropy Phi_D>0](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md). Consider a GLOBAL maximum of sum_e h_(delta_e)(q_e), with q in P and independent real delta_e in[0,1/2]. Alternatively maximize over the closed non-CROSS union, but assume the maximum being studied has value at least Phi_D and at least one STRICT non-CROSS middle load greater than1/2. Such a port keeps the geometric segment below in that union for all sufficiently small perturbations. No analogous claim is made for a seam-only non-CROSS boundary maximum. The statements use the sharp continuum functional directly. Where it is used as an upper functional for the actual source, this theorem does not supply a new coefficient-identification or cap-uniform N limit. ## 2. Fixed-load spectral exclusions First, a positive-length port at strict 0<delta<1/2 cannot have an endpoint at either simple alpha pole. Write the poles as p=1/2-delta and p'=1/2+delta. Moving an endpoint pole into the active interval increases the two outside integrals by |s|log(1/|s|)+O(|s|). If both endpoints are poles, necessarily mu=p,nu=p'; decreasing delta moves both inside and gives twice this gain. All other outside-integral changes are O(|s|). The tilted tail changes only O(|s|), uniformly in the tilt: with eta=cos^2(pi delta)/sin^2(pi t), 0<=partial_(log eta)log rho_eta(x)<=1/2, and partial_delta log eta is bounded on every strict delta compact. Taking a common infimum preserves that Lipschitz estimate, also for closed outer loads. Thus an arbitrarily small feasible spectral change increases (2). This excludes positive-length pole endpoints without assuming face stationarity or concavity in the row variables. Second, at delta=0 a positive-length nonterminal one-sided interval cannot maximize in its free spectrum. For a lower interval nu<1/2, put z=sin^2(pi delta) and L_z=Lambda_z/alpha_z, with z small enough that alpha stays positive on the interval. Directly from the positive root, -partial_z log Lambda_z <=1/[2(1-z)], partial_z log L_z >=1/[2(1-z)]. The first inequality follows by bounding its square-root denominator below by 4xy(1-z); it remains valid at a monomial tilt. Hence, uniformly in every outer tilt and after the same infimum, h_delta(q)-h_0(q)>=-(nu-mu)log(1-z)/2>0. (4) Reflection proves the upper one-sided case. Thus every positive-length delta=0 port at a maximum lies in CROSS, allowing its seams for now. Finally classify a positive-length delta=1/2 port at fixed loads. The sharp entropy dominates its monomer action because J*>=0. If 0<mu<nu<1, choose a positive k=cos(pi delta) smaller than the minimum of sin(pi t) on that fixed interval. The entire active interval is then after the small lower pole and before its reflection, and its actual monomer action is int_mu^nu -log[1-k^2/sin^2(pi t)]dt>0. (5) Thus every interval with both endpoints strictly inside(0,1) is excluded at the cap, uniformly over its closed outer split. Write I_k(0,a) for the initial monomer integral of log[sin^2/|k^2-sin^2|]. If mu=0 and 1/2<nu<1, the exact total and reflection identities give I_k(0,nu)=-I_k(0,1-nu)>0 (6) for sufficiently small k, because the latter initial interval has negative monomer action by its regular positive suffix formula. Exact reflection treats nu=1 and 0<mu<1/2. For mu=0,0<nu<1/2 and BOTH outer loads positive, the [protected-middle cap lemma](research_protected_middle_spectral_cap_exclusion.md) gives, at small positive k=cos(pi delta), h_delta>=2 min(xi,nu-xi)log(1+k) -(2/pi)k^2 cot(pi nu)>0. (7) The half-terminal extension has no baseline cost, and a full interval [0,1] has the same positive chord bound for strict outer loads. Exact reflection covers the protected output. Consequently a cap maximum with positive length can only have a monomial outer split and be [0,nu], 0<nu<=1/2; its reflected interval; or the whole interval[0,1]. (8) Every other fixed-load cap candidate has an available positive value at another spectrum, while the cap value is zero. This classification does not yet eliminate the zeros at (8). ## 3. One geometric segment, with source spectra retained or retuned Use the EXACT full-fiber segment q(eps)=(1-eps)q+eps qG. (9) It preserves every ordinary target, protected zero and row supply. It activates every zero ORDINARY incidence. It is not required to preserve an old LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT label at a boundary: the full source fiber has no such imposed labels. If a strict non-CROSS port was specified, its strict inequality persists for small eps. For a non-diagonal strict-spectrum port, keep delta fixed. The [ordinary-zero barrier table](research_sharp_spectral_ordinary_zero_barrier.md) and exact reflection give nonnegative eps log(1/eps) coefficients, strictly positive if an ordinary zero incidence is activated. Upper rows equal1/2 are regular units at a strict spectrum; there is no half-label inequality in this full fiber. At the full two-terminal interval mu=0,nu=1, write mu=eps B and 1-nu=eps C. With strict base outer loads use xi=xi0+eps dot_xi, 0<xi0<1; the two-end calculation gives B+C. At the x-zero corner instead use xi=eps X, and its coefficient is 2(B+C+X). Outer reflection is identical. These exhaust the positive-length full-row zero patterns. All other changes are O(eps). For a delta=0 CROSS port choose an attaining split in (3), and mix its two triangle rows with the actual geometric triangle rows. Their sum is EXACTLY the local vector in (9). The optimized h_0 at that vector is at least the entropy of this mixed split. Each triangle has a nonnegative closed-corner singular coefficient, strictly positive at every activated zero ordinary corner. Thus an ordinary zero in the port gives a positive gain. At a seam nu=1/2 the output triangle is the pure-middle vertex, and its contribution is 2 dot_nu eps log(1/eps)+O(eps), dot_nu>0. (10) The input triangle has no negative singular contribution. The mu=1/2 seam is reflected and gives -2 dot_mu>0. This uses an actual latent complete split inside the FULL endpoint polynomial. It makes no infeasible fixed-pattern retagging or terminal KKT assertion. For a diagonal mu=nu=a, retune its spectrum. At a in(0,1), (1) opens a positive interval; placing a simple pole inside it gives W eps log(1/eps)+O(eps), or 2W at a=1/2, uniformly in the outer split. At a=0 or1 use cos(pi delta_eps)=eps^2; its cost is at worst O(eps^2). These are the [free-spectral retuning estimates](research_free_spectral_diagonal_retuning.md). For a cap port from (8), the [cap-corner lemma](research_spectral_cap_corner_activation.md) gives the needed ordinary-zero gain. At [0,nu0] with nu0<1/2 and x load zero, choose cos^2(pi delta_eps)=eps K. Its singular coefficient is B+X, where B=dot_mu and X=dot_xi. It is positive if either zero incidence is ordinary. At a flat half-terminal monomial interval [0,1/2], the base value is zero for EVERY spectrum. Retune its base to delta=0 and use the actual latent CROSS split above. Its output triangle is the pure-middle vertex, so (10) gives a strictly positive gain because qG_c<1/2. This remains true when the input middle and the zero outer incidence are both protected. Thus the half-terminal monomial is excluded at every initial spectrum, not only at the cap. Exact reflection excludes the upper half-terminal monomial as well. At the flat full terminal interval, retune to a fixed strict delta and use the corresponding corner table. A full [0,1] monomial interval has three zero incidences, at least one ordinary, so its gain is strict. If both zeros of a half-interval cap corner are protected, keep the cap value zero. That port has no ordinary zero to activate. Reflected and outer-exchanged cases use the same exact source symmetries. All spectra are independent, so these choices can be made simultaneously without altering (9). There are only finitely many ports. Every listed singular coefficient is nonnegative; every strict gain dominates all O(eps) terms. Thus global maximality implies: * every non-diagonal port has positive load on every ordinary incidence; * no interior diagonal remains; * no positive-length delta=0 port lies on a CROSS seam; * no half-terminal monomial remains at any spectrum; * every remaining positive-length cap port has its two zero incidences both protected, and is a monomial corner [0,nu] with 0<nu<1/2, or its exact reflection. This conclusion is for a global free-spectrum maximum. No such simultaneous retuning is inferred at a local fixed-spectrum maximum. ## 4. Endpoint diagonals form an impossible closed component Only diagonals at a=0 or1 can now remain. Let D be their ports and F their occupied middle faces. Such a row sends its entire supply1 to one ordinary face. Protected demand0 excludes a protected occupied face, and demand1 makes the map D->F injective. Therefore |D|=|F|. Every face in F is saturated by its diagonal row. By section3 every ordinary incidence of a non-diagonal row is positive. Thus no non-diagonal row can even be incident to F: N(F)=D in the full supported bipartite incidence graph B. Evaluate the same demands with qG. The faces F require |F|=|D|, and only D can supply them. All supplies of D are therefore used inside F. Because qG is strictly positive on every ordinary incidence, no D row has an arc to an ordinary face outside F. Hence D union F is a union of connected components of B. The original graph B is connected. Delete u,v from the simple white triangulated sphere: the remaining white graph is connected. The [elementary connectivity argument](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) reroutes a path through the cyclic link of u, and then through the link of v with u deleted, which is a connected path or cycle. Every remaining white edge belongs to an original port quartet, so it induces a two-step path through that port in B. Every port has an ordinary incidence. These facts connect all vertices of B without creating any new source adjacency. Consequently nonempty D would mean all ports are diagonal. Their total sharp entropy is zero. This contradicts the feasible geometric value Phi_D>0 for an unrestricted full-fiber maximum. In the strict non-CROSS variant, the comparison must instead assume the studied maximum has positive value (as is automatic for any candidate at or above Phi_D). The all-geometric point need not lie in that restricted set, so its value is not silently used as a feasible NC lower bound. Thus D is empty under these stated value hypotheses. No actual identity smoothing or cover is needed for this tight-cut argument. ## 5. What the reduction proves, and what remains An unrestricted global full sharp maximum on this original certified fiber has no diagonal and has positive load on every ordinary incidence. Positive-length strict-spectrum ports have no endpoint at a pole; delta=0 ports are strict CROSS. The only cap ports left by this argument are monomial intervals [0,nu], 0<nu<1/2, and their exact reflections, whose parent middle and one outer incidence are both the original protected faces. Half-terminal monomials at any spectrum have been excluded by their cost-free retuning to delta=0. Those two zero incidences form the actual marked MAIN edge uv in one shaded triangle. The edge has two incident triangles, and they belong to distinct ports since ports pair across MATCHING edges. Thus at most two such positive-length cap ports remain, adjacent to the mark. This count does not identify their geometry, phase, or contribution. The same boundary reduction holds for a competing maximum of value at least Phi_D over the closed non-CROSS union if at least one STRICT non-CROSS port is present. A seam-only constrained maximum requires its own documented argument; it is not covered by a feasible qG segment here. Ordinary positivity is not an all-boundary theorem. Protected zero faces remain, the possible marked cap corners remain, and the full spectral/filling phase still has to be controlled. No finite positive ordinary multipliers, terminal geometric interpretation at a cap, new developing representation, bound by Phi_D, or quantum period conclusion is asserted at those residual cap configurations. All arguments here concern the sharp continuum functional. They use the exact original row/face constraints, both unused products, the normalized eta word and the separately proved endpoint entropy. They do not replace a signed polynomial by a new positive model or interchange a shrinking spectral scale with N. Any later use for the original finite source must retain its exact scalar zeros and the independently proved coefficient upper/identification statements. ## Scope No lower coefficient limit or volume comparison follows from this activation argument. The finite-multiplier conclusion is proved in the separate stationary addendum.

Indeed \[ \partial_\ell^2\log\Lambda_\delta(t;e^\ell,1) = rac{\eta_\delta(t)\cosh(\ell/2)} {4 igl(\sinh^2(\ell/2)+\eta_\delta(t) igr)^{3/2}}>0, 	ag{4} \] and its first derivative ranges from zero to one. The integrated first derivative therefore ranges from zero to \(
u-\mu\). At a protected start zero or stop one, the first derivative is bounded by one and the second derivative is integrable; on compact tilt sets it is \(O(t)\) or \(O(1-t)\) at the corresponding endpoint. The implicit function theorem consequently gives a smooth finite tilt in the free degree coordinates. Every movable row is strictly inside \((0,1)\). At strict spectrum it also avoids the two alpha zeros, so differentiating the outside integrals in that row is regular. Their possible interior logarithmic zeros do not affect this degree smoothness. At \(\delta=0\), the strict CROSS inequalities keep both movable endpoints away from the central zero. A protected endpoint is fixed and is not differentiated. Thus (3) is \(C^1\) on the relevant relative open face. If an outer incidence is protected, specialize the exact monomer first: its forced outer degree leaves \(\Lambda_\delta(t;0,y)= eta(t)y\), or its reflection. The same row argument proves smoothness on this protected face without taking a finite tilt of a zero weight. Both outer incidences cannot be protected, because their MATCHING edge differs from the marked MAIN edge. Finally, at the cap the full sharp functional is identically zero for every degree vector. It is smooth on its protected-coordinate face as well. Let \(A\) be the original finite row/face constraint matrix after protected incidences are removed. The differential of the total fixed-spectrum entropy annihilates \(\ker A\): every sufficiently small positive and negative tangent displacement is admissible. Elementary row-space orthogonality gives finite real row and face multipliers. Redundant balance equations cause no difficulty. Choose the sign of the ordinary face multiplier \(\lambda_f\) so that \[ L_f=e^{-\lambda_f}>0,\qquad \mathcal F_e(q_e)=h_{\delta_e}(q_e) +\sum_{f	ext{ at }e}q_{ef}\log L_f. 	ag{5} \] Here \(\mathcal F_e\) is stationary on the local row simplex. The row multiplier drops out because the local supply is fixed. The same finite \(L_f\) occurs at every original incidence of \(f\). At protected faces use the literal value zero only after specializing their zero coordinates; no expression \(0\log0\) or infinite multiplier is used. This is equality stationarity in degree variables. It is not local maximality of an individual weighted coupon. In particular no independent optimization of local rows or interchange of a shared infimum and maximum has been used. ## 3. The exact row equations and branch derivatives At a port let \(x,b,c,y\) now denote its common face weights. A protected one is zero in the literal specialized formula. Therefore \[ \mathcal L_\delta(\mu)=b\quad(b>0),\qquad \mathcal L_\delta(

These constants are those of the original outside integrals, not an unfixed primitive. For example the post-pole derivative is fixed by \(r	o1/2\), where the half-alpha integral has derivative zero and \(T_q	o\sqrt D\). Its normalized recurrence is R_n=1-t_n R_(n-1); the quarter-demand bound is analytical, including N=4 and N=6. The [full lower-range contour proof](research_cap_cross_full_low_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) now strengthens this to |S_(N,n)|/D_(N,n)<=e^{o(N)}, uniformly for ALL 0<=n<=N/2-1 at even levels. The [odd raw-source extension](research_cap_cross_odd_low_demand_subexponential_extension.md) proves the analogous bound for 0<=n<=(N-3)/2 against the actual odd regularized positive comparator. The signed numerator remains raw. Exact endpoint Gamma factors, optimally truncated shifted Euler--Maclaurin interpolation, and an alternating-residue contour retain cancellation; the interpolation error is proved exponentially smaller than the amplified positive envelope. Both vertical edges are kept, and the scaled contour height is fixed before N tends to infinity. The [all-demand contraction theorem](research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) now closes the projected middle range as well, at BOTH parities: \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log \max_{0\le n\le N-2}  rac{|T_{N,n}|}{D_{N,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}}\le0. \] The exact Newton contiguity relation retains both finite cutoff currents. The actual positive comparator has a uniform matching upper AND lower rate \(J(u)\), strictly concave with one peak. The odd boundary current and both even currents have rate at most \(J(u)\). Forward propagation from the proved low range and backward propagation from the proved high range have bounded raw propagators, and together cover the middle. The lower estimate uses actual positive half-block coefficients and their forced outer unit, not an upper capacity. An exact finite-field replay also checks the source contiguity and cutoff identities; the asymptotic estimate is proved analytically. This closes the fixed spectral pair \((-2,+2)\) with its internal \(A^d\) demand and both original projections. The [two-spectrum continuation](research_cap_cross_two_spectrum_neighborhood_stability.md) now strengthens this to complex neighborhoods at BOTH ports: \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log \max_n\sup_{|\sigma-2|,\,|	au+2|\le\varepsilon}  rac{|T_{N,n}(\sigma,	au)|}{D_{N,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}} \le\omega(\varepsilon),\qquad\omega(\varepsilon)\longrightarrow0. \] Two exact shifted Gamma products remove the nearby endpoint zeros from the analytic interpolation. The original short rows and central rows are treated without dividing by vanishing spectral factors. The projected recurrence retains the returning odd lower current and the odd central transition. A genuine comparator lower bound now holds through the high corner. Thus arbitrary shrinking complex polydisks give a subexponential comparison, at all original demands and both parities. A polynomial all-demand factor and arbitrary exterior incidences at the internal A face remain open. The unrestricted coefficientwise replacement fails on exponents that the original demand excludes, so that failure is not a counterexample to this theorem. The [incidence and simultaneous assembly theorem](research_cap_cross_incidence_and_disjoint_assembly.md) identifies exactly when this estimate fits a residual cap: its overloaded ordinary child must have degree TWO in the original MAIN quadrangulation. Triangulation valence three alone is insufficient; the matching must be retained. At a classified positive maximum the unique neighboring port is CROSS, and if both residual caps qualify their patches are disjoint. For any fixed collection of disjoint qualifying pairs, the coefficientwise subexponential comparisons multiply, even when their remaining variables are shared and the untouched exterior has complex coefficients. This is a paired-reference sector replacement, not yet a whole-source volume bound. Bipyramid quadrangulations and refined cube quadrangulations show that planarity and ideal geometric realizability do not force the degree-two condition. These are combinatorial obstructions to this particular elimination rule, not examples of dominant non-CROSS maxima. Allowing an exterior load at the internal child gives a genuinely shifted convolution, and an unrestricted version has the already proved exponential boundary counterexample. There is now a different estimate for arbitrarily large fixed stars: the [whole-CROSS-star spectral gap](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md). Include EVERY other original A-incident port, all required to be CROSS, in its product P_N. At positive radii with A=C assume its endpoint weighted action satisfies 0<F'(0)<1/2 when A is varied as C exp(t). Then the original A^d extraction against the cap has a strict exponential loss relative to the actual positive star value P_N(C). The estimate is uniform in every remaining face phase, a fixed complex disk about the cap spectrum +2, and the ENTIRE real fold spectrum of each CROSS neighbor together with a fixed thin complex strip. This theorem has no valence-two restriction. It keeps one TOTAL A allocation, uses the actual cofactor angular gap on MAIN edge AC, and controls both window endpoints and both radial contour currents with a finite analytic antidifference. Its separate endpoint moment proof uses only the original finite d-th moment; it never integrates the full high-degree neighbor polynomial or takes its divergent square. The earlier Cauchy-norm obstruction therefore remains valid. The [cap-component and stellar reduction](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md) also supplies an applicable star whenever a globally maximal non-CROSS-child weight occurs in a component containing a cap: a nonroot leaf is a cap child with only CROSS neighbors. This includes every cap-only classified positive maximum. Otherwise a maximal Green child is strictly heavier than every component containing a cap. An exact triangle-disk count retains this possible outgoing Green dependency; it cannot be removed by choosing a maximal cap alone. The same structural note proves a closed fixed-boundary CROSS stellar identity with additive constant 4f(1/4). Actual matched refinements can raise a cap child's incidence degree indefinitely while preserving that classical sector's deficit or excess relative to complete volume. This does not transport finite signed sums or preserve a filled knot. The star gap is RELATIVE to a stated weighted star/exterior envelope. That envelope has not been proved at most exp(N Phi_D), and mixed Green dependencies remain. Those are the substantive global obstacles; neither the new spectral neighborhoods nor the arbitrary-valence star estimate alone proves the general filled-volume conjecture. For even levels and low remaining degree \(n\le N/2-1\), extracting the original demands automatically enforces both RIGHT/CROSS cutoffs. Thus the fixed two-port coefficient can legitimately be studied using its unprojected polynomial Casimir coupons in this range. This does not make it a positive or semisimple representation: the low-degree source still detects the original nilpotent complete-circle coupon. A special identity for the fixed resolvent pair remains possible. The [exact cap-moment form](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) now supplies a positive inner product from those original coefficients: \(U_j=U_0\mathbb E X_N^j\), with a proved positive beta-product measure. At even levels its maximal finite polynomial degree is precisely the original RIGHT cutoff \(M=N/2-1\); higher-degree squared norms diverge. The actual alternating convolution is its expectation of the literal projected polynomial at \(-X_N\), and weighted Cauchy applies. The specific proposal to bound that entire positive norm by the endpoint comparator is now DISPROVED, as described below. The signed expectation itself now satisfies the all-demand subexponential estimate above; its polynomial strengthening remains open. The [finite continuant and cap tensor calculation](research_cap_demand_continuant_jacobi_interface.md) also gives the actual source recurrence with its undetermined terminal coefficient, the two original cutoff commutators, and an explicit orthogonal basis for each factor of the cap measure. Its squared norms are \(g_a=\sin(\pi/(2N))/\sin((2a+1/2)\pi/N)\), with \(1/N\le g_a\le1\) on the original even-level degree range. Thus the product basis has polynomial normalization. The original source polynomial's nonconstant coefficients can nevertheless be exponentially large. The exact finite slices also fail the necessary three-term property of a single positive scalar orthogonal family; that excludes another proposed identification, without excluding a tensor or block construction. The [cap-moment norm obstruction](research_cap_moment_cauchy_norm_obstruction.md) proves this failure analytically for every fixed \(0<u\le1/4\) and even-level sequence \(n/N	o u\). The original endpoint comparator has rate \(2f(u)\), while a single orthogonal component forces the moment-Cauchy bound to exceed it by at least \[ \chi(u)=4f(u/2)-2f(u)-2\int_0^u\log(2\cos(\pi t))\,dt>0, \qquad f(u)=-\int_0^u\log	an(\pi t)\,dt. \] The exact derivative \(\chi'(u)=2\log[(1+\cos(\pi u))/(2\cos^2(\pi u))]>0\) proves positivity without a numerical growth test. Absolute coefficient mass in this tensor basis fails for the same reason. The large component is orthogonal to the constant component defining the signed expectation. Thus cancellation remains essential: this is an obstruction to the particular positive-norm route, not to the original convolution estimate or the volume conjecture. A separate [constrained Hessian reduction](research_sharp_source_constrained_hessian.md) computes the exact quadratic cost of restoring the shared face targets after varying the spectra. The forced odd cycle alone need not provide an increasing second-order direction. Its local counterexample to that inference does not realize a stable global maximum. This route still requires a general inequality for the original constraint matrix. The [response and MAIN-network theorem](research_sharp_source_response_forest_main_network.md) computes the preferred Green responses explicitly. Their columns remain independent after zero-cost cap contraction, so no nonzero spectral combination repairs the preferred face loads for free. A resistor network built from actual MAIN edges gives a sufficient global instability test, with a per-port conductance budget that prevents double-counting. Whether the original demands force that inequality is open. The maximal Green-child cap component is a tree, and every other noncap port incident to it is CROSS. Exact triangle compliance gives a lower bound on the cost of spectator-only repair. At the local datum \((x,b,c,y)=(1,1,3,0)\), that cost is at least \(9\), exceeding its preferred spectral gain \(4\pi/\sqrt3\), whenever the datum occurs as a maximal child. No global occurrence is asserted. This excludes a universal spectator-only shortcut; the full constrained Hessian, which also changes the chosen Green's own response, remains undecided. The [entire CROSS period](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) already has its nonzero original filled-volume asymptotic. To transfer that result to the general full invariant, the complementary sectors need a sufficient strict absolute gap and the original whole-charge control. A drilled-volume upper bound alone, or the compact number \(M_D\) alone, does not accomplish that transfer. No universal all-plat conclusion is claimed here. ## Current publication boundary The unconditional block theorem, its exact rational certificate, monotone response proof and isolated-three-leaf extension are unpublished workspace results. The guide source chapters are updated locally. The preceding leaf-certified theorem remains a valid historical special case. The new two-leaf tangle theorem, its three component proofs, the arborescent target, algebraic cap period, boundary composition, two-cap response estimate and even-level stability obstruction are unpublished workspace results. The guide's source chapters have been updated locally. No public checkout or deployment was changed in this research turn; its checked HEAD remains `667400a` and is clean. The general prescribed-diagram target remains open. The results above provide source bounds, boundary reductions and conditional geometric comparisons; they do not establish the missing global estimate for every prescribed diagram.

title: The actual CROSS geometric action on a general Morse source
text: # The actual CROSS geometric action on a general Morse source 31 October 2026. Independent analytical/source extension. The conclusion concerns the existing CROSS principal action, actual geometric marking, local packet, and global spectral gap. It does not restore the full numerator by the older Fejér/flat-forest argument. ## Hypotheses retained Use the actual augmented link and fixed coupon frames constructed in [general Morse source realization](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md). Assume its chosen white triangulation is simplicial and has the same labeled nondegenerate positive right-angled certificate required by the existing marked-circle and complete-source theorems. Choose adjacent MAIN faces u,v as the two protected faces. The original local cofactor estimates and complete coefficient anchor are the analytic inputs; section 4 checks their shared-source assembly independently of full-numerator restoration. An arbitrary multigraph diagonal choice without such a certificate is not included in this geometric audit. ## 1. The marked pattern has no constant-headcount hypothesis [marked deformed circle pattern](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md), sections 1–4, uses only the labeled simplicial sphere, its MAIN/matching edge types, the two adjacent protected lines, and the positive finite-face Hessian. Its equations for finite centers/radii and signed line sides are unchanged. The rank proof deletes the two triangles incident to uv and propagates one infinitesimal motion through the remaining triangulated disk. It does not use the flat-plat gap forest or the placement of cups/caps. Thus the same common analytic line-circle family realizes the stationary CROSS radii in the new diagram, including the common strip at the two protected triangles. All local selected eigenlines are retained. ## 2. Variable-headcount group sewing is literal At a regular horizontal level of the new Morse diagram let \(F_0,\ldots,F_{m(t)}\) be the actual region sequence from left to right. Here \(m(t)\) varies at extrema and is even; the exterior regions are \(F_0=F_{m(t)}=u\). With the same globally defined white reflections as the existing complete-core proof, set \[ Q_j=R_{F_j}^+R_u^-,\qquad H_j=R_{F_j}^+R_{F_{j-1}}^-. \] Since \(R_f^-R_f^+=I\), one has exactly \(H_j\cdots H_1=Q_j\). Inserting or deleting a cup/cap replaces one region occurrence F by F,G,F. Its two heads multiply to \(R_F^+R_G^-R_G^+R_F^-=I\). Every prefix after the pair is unchanged. Every unchanged physical wire retains its two ordered adjacent faces, so it retains its based head. No independent frame is introduced at a new level or at a change in the number of heads. At a coupon its exterior regions are unchanged; the two-head product is the same original \(P\) before and after it. The already proved primitive collar \(C\), in that fixed local frame, transports the ordered pair and commutes with \(P\). The local formula \[ M=mR_0(J^{-1}-1)^{-\epsilon} C^{-1}(P^{-1}-I)^\epsilon, \qquad \det M=m^2R_0(-J)^\epsilon \] therefore has exactly the same selected eigenvalue and threading word. No term in it depends on \(m(t)\). The original disk-framed longitude, half-twist shear, and the unit at \(J=-1\) are unchanged. These are all the van Kampen relations of this newly constructed link: identity wires, cups/caps, and each original crossing-disk box. The event-incidence proof in [actual Morse critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) already permits arbitrary cup/cap/coupon events and arbitrary graph cycles; its displayed fixed-width wording is not an extra algebraic hypothesis. The spanning-tree reconstruction of momenta and the inverse prefix chart depend on the actual event graph, not on all cups being below all boxes. Alternatively the reflection formulas above construct the needed representation directly without choosing a magnetic chart. ## 3. Local action, boundary characters, and the absolute anchor [absolutely normalized cofactor action](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md) proves locally that the actual full-V cofactor action equals the absolutely normalized triangle action \(Q_b\), including every allowed one-line/two-line specialization. Its full head gradients retain the physical factor \((bc)^{-d/2}\), so they give the same ordered product and primitive collar in section 2. These statements are port-local and unaffected by an outside Morse turn. The new source compiler proves the original face character exactly on the new network. Thus its principal stationary action is precisely \[ A_\epsilon(\delta)=\operatorname{crit}_{L_{\mathrm{ordinary}}} \left\{\sum_e(Q_{b_e}+Q_{c_e}) -\sum_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\operatorname{Log} L_f +\pi i\sum_e\epsilon_e\delta_e^2\right\}. \] No additional delta-dependent turn term appears: the four original turns have already combined by the general face-winding identity into the displayed ordinary target. The unrestricted mark was restricted only after whole-source degree conservation, as in the finite theorem. Spectral-independent framing and parity characters remain outside this principal action, with their original values. The primitive collar and selected longitude give, in the existing conventions, \[ J_e=-e^{-2\pi i\delta_e},\qquad U_e=-\operatorname{Log} R_{0,e}-\epsilon_e\operatorname{Log}(-J_e),\qquad V_e=2\operatorname{Log}(-J_e)=-4\pi i\delta_e, \quad \partial_{\delta_e}A_\epsilon=U_e. \] Hence \(d(2\pi iA_\epsilon)=-\frac12\sum U_e\,dV_e\), exactly the same longitude polarization. The complete positive coefficient anchor is \(2\pi\Re A_\epsilon(0)=\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\), with the actual two-ball geometry. This anchor and the actual marked geometric germ give the existing absolute regulator formula \[ 2\pi\Re A_\epsilon(\delta) =\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_\delta) -\frac12\sum_e\Im U_e\Re V_e. \] The geometric germ is identified by the same positive marked gluing rigidity, which depends on the complete hyperbolic certificate and peripheral marking, not on a constant number of heads. Finally the exact local Fourier functional of the new source has \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\). Its charge phase therefore gives \(U_e+p_eV_e=-2\pi i\ell_e\), without another half-twist contribution. At the original unit charge the already calibrated primitive smooth filling equation and critical-value regulator equality are unchanged. This is an identification of the geometric action and marking, not a statement that a charge contributes or that its complement is small. ## 4. The CROSS local packet and global spectral gap The following dependency extension concerns the **all-CROSS** coefficient. It does not use section 4 of the older full-numerator packet theorem, whose restoration argument had separate hypotheses. The graph and its Morse presentation are fixed before the level tends to infinity. Write \(C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}\) for the original all-CROSS marked coefficient, including its sign \((-1)^{dR}\), where \(d=N-1\). The new source has \(R+2\) faces and exactly \(R\) original degree-\(d\) ordinary targets. Simplicity and the protected MAIN edge imply that no matching edge has both protected endpoints. Hence every local outer sum \(x+y\) is positive. The remaining zero patterns, including a one-variable triangle, are precisely those already treated in the actual local cofactor proofs. The [local interpolant rigidity theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_interpolant_rigidity.md) and its [exactly anchored interpolation](actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) therefore apply to every unchanged local polynomial: \[ P_{\mathrm{cross},e} =N^2\mathcal B_{e,N} \bigl(1+O(e^{-\kappa N})\bigr). \tag{1} \] This is uniform on a fixed small complex spectral and face neighborhood. The original maximal-fold anchor, beta factors, forced products, half-index, and even/odd central formulas are retained. These theorems are local finite recurrences and interpolation statements; they have no hypothesis about the number or order of global Morse events. For the shared angular complement, deleting the two marked vertices from a simple triangulated sphere leaves a connected ordinary graph. The elementary link-rerouting argument in the [original rank theorem](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) proves this without a flat-plat assumption. Every surviving edge lies in an actual triangle with two nonzero face variables. The [global cofactor angular theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) then detects every nonconstant ordinary phase. A one-variable triangle is retained as a monomial and contributes no false angular constraint. All other cofactors have their global polynomial endpoint majorant; the exact central sums cost only polynomial factors. After fixing one ordinary phase, the common-phase point is the only angular zero. The active edge rows are primitive \(+1,-1\) differences, so no additional angular alias is introduced. The [positive coefficient saddle theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md), sections 2–4, uses this same ordinary graph, the exact determinant pair-trace bounds, and the complete circle angle-force equation. Its face Hessian is positive definite on the \(R-1\) dimensional common-scale quotient. The complete exponent is \(\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y)/(2\pi)\), with the exact source anchor. No flat gap forest or constant intermediate headcount enters that proof. Define the finite phase on that original quotient by \[ \Psi_N(z,\delta)=\frac1N\sum_e\operatorname{Log} \mathcal B_{e,N}(\delta_e;L(z)) -\frac dN\sum_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\operatorname{Log}L_f(z). \tag{2} \] Uniform local convergence and the positive complete Hessian give its holomorphic saddle, critical value \(A_N\), and face Hessian \(H_N\). The new finite compiler gives exactly the original Cauchy measure; the simultaneous phase integrates to one, leaving \((2\pi)^{-(R-1)}d\theta\). Deforming that actual torus in its annulus, with local side faces in the angular gap, gives \[ C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}(\delta)= \frac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{NA_N(\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\delta)}} \bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr). \tag{H1} \] This repeats only sections 1–3 of the [original shared packet proof](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md). All finite normalization factors remain in (2), and the determinant branch is continued from the positive real Hessian. The estimate is relative on one fixed complex polydisk and controls all fixed derivatives on smaller polydisks. It has a nonzero actual source amplitude. The finite actions are separately even and real on the real chart. Their limit is the untwisted action \(A_0\) of sections 1–3, with \[ A_0(0)=\Phi,\qquad A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_e),\qquad C_e=\frac{\pi(T_{b_e}+T_{c_e})}{x_e+y_e}>0. \tag{3} \] At least one triangle at every port is nonmonomial: either both outers are positive, or one protected outer leaves at least one positive middle. Thus (3) is strict at every port. Shrinking the fixed chart gives the uniform negative real Hessian required by the spectral Gaussian argument. Half twists are added only through the original \(n=\epsilon-2p\) functional, as in section 3 above. For the global spectral bound, sections 1–3 of the [global CROSS theorem](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) use the signed normalized transfer, all starting rows, and a uniform upper bound on the original unused logarithmic products. Their local upper action is \(\max\{Q_b(\delta),\tfrac12\log b\}\), omitting the second branch when \(b=0\). It decreases strictly away from \(\delta=0\) except for the stated exact monomial. Every separated spectral port therefore has a strict loss in the product of its two triangle cofactors. The even/odd central sums keep both triangles in each term. Outside the common ordinary phase neighborhood, the global cofactor angular bound supplies a gap uniformly for all real spectra. Inside that neighborhood, the signed transfer proof supplies its fixed complex face extension: one separated port gives a strict loss, while all others stay below their endpoint rates plus arbitrarily small errors. The graph has finitely many ports, so choose the errors and strip small enough that their total is less than that loss. This gives, for every \(\eta>0\), some \(\tau,\gamma>0\) such that \[ |C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}(\delta)|\le e^{N(\Phi-\gamma)} \quad\text{if}\quad \max_e|\operatorname{Re}\delta_e|\ge\eta, \qquad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le\tau, \tag{H2} \] on the centered real cube for all sufficiently large \(N\). Every fixed derivative has the same strict rate on a smaller strip. This is the shared Cauchy sewing of the global CROSS theorem, with one set of face radii and the original targets throughout. Thus H1 and H2 extend to the new certified simple-white general Morse source. Constants depend on the fixed graph, complete radii, and zero patterns; no prescribed flat-plat width is required. For a full-source filling conclusion, the **new** global non-CROSS gap must restore the full numerator. No old Fejér smoothing, pure-middle forest, or flat full-packet restoration was used here. ## Verdict The extension retains the original positive certificate and local analytic hypotheses. It supplies the general Morse action and the two stated spectral estimates. Restoring the full source requires the new non-CROSS gap, rather than the earlier flat-forest argument. The unchanged local collar and global regulator inputs are the [primitive collar](actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md), [complete-core group and regulator assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md), [marked gluing rigidity](general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md), and [peripheral action boundary correction](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md). This dependency extension does not assert full-numerator restoration or a global period bound for the full source.

title: Effective boundary response and the original global cap variance
text:
# Effective boundary response and the original global cap variance 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. This concerns the exact ONE-cap coefficient at cap spectrum +2 and all other original CROSS spectra -2, on ODD levels. It supplies a classical positive Hessian test for the variance criterion, not a spectral-neighborhood or filled-knot theorem. ## 1. The same exterior and the two boundary weights Retain the source and binary polynomial P_N(A,C) in [the global negative-axis reduction](research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md), including all actual ordinary coefficient targets. Suppose a strict one-cap stationary configuration exists, with all other ports CROSS, finite positive ordinary weights, and L_A=L_C. Normalize their common value to one. Let I be the set of ordinary faces other than A,C; write A=exp(z), C=1 and L_i=exp(w_i). The original protected variables u,v remain exactly zero. Let t run over the original triangles EXCLUDING the two cap triangles. Write Q_t for its actual endpoint half-triangle potential. Define \[ \mathcal F(z,w)=\sum_{t}Q_t(L)-\sum_{i\in I}w_i. 	ag{1} \] There is no target term in z: A has not been extracted in the binary polynomial. At the stationary exterior, w=w_* solves \(\partial_w\mathcal F(0,w_*)=0\). Its A-load is the original residual split nu, and the normalized value is M_cap: \[ \mathcal F(0,w_*)=M_{\mathrm{cap}},\qquad \partial_z\mathcal F(0,w_*)=
u. 	ag{2} \] These follow by the same finite-common-weight Legendre attainment used in the cap-capacity theorem. The target logs cancel at A=C=1. ## 2. Positive Hessian with the original boundary anchor Let H be the Hessian of (1) in the variables (z,w) at (0,w_*). It is positive definite. Here is the graph check needed for this claim. Delete the protected vertices u,v from the original simple triangulated sphere. Its remaining ordinary graph is connected. Removing the cap triangles removes no edge needed in that ordinary graph: their only ordinary edge is AC, and its triangle on the opposite side remains in the exterior. Every other ordinary edge was unaffected. Thus the graph of ordinary pairs occurring together in an exterior triangle is still connected. The face C fixes the common scaling direction. For a positive triangle the Hessian of Q is nonnegative, and its kernel on its nonzero coordinates is exactly the common-scaling direction. For a two-supported-corner triangle this also holds; a pure corner has zero Hessian and equates no two phases. This can be seen directly from the strictly concave triangle entropy and its Legendre dual, or from the actual positive determinant pair-trace identity and its positive limiting bulk traces. The connected pair graph therefore makes their sum strictly positive after C is fixed. Linear target terms in (1) change no Hessian. In particular H_II is invertible (the empty I case has the usual empty matrix convention). The implicit-function theorem gives a real analytic w(z) near zero, and the reduced exterior value \[ F(z)=\mathcal F(z,w(z)),\qquad \kappa_D:=F''(0)=H_{AA}-H_{AI}H_{II}^{-1}H_{IA}>0. 	ag{3} \] The letters A in H indicate the log-A coordinate z. This is the actual Schur complement for the original demands, not a separately optimized star or a replacement graph. ## 3. The exact original odd polynomial has this variance limit At N=2m+1 each original CROSS endpoint is exactly N^2 D_m(x,b,y)D_m(x,c,y), with the original Hermitian positive pencils. Put \[ \mathcal F_N(z,w)= rac1N\log\prod_{e
e F} P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2;L) - rac{N-1}{N}\sum_{i\in I}w_i. 	ag{4} \] The local logarithmic derivatives of these actual determinants converge to those of Q_t on a fixed complex neighborhood of the positive weights. Their higher normalized derivatives are uniformly bounded there. The retained N^2 factors are independent of z,w and cost O(log N/N) in value; they vanish from the derivatives. These are exactly the local positive-packet and curvature inputs already used in the original positive face-coefficient theorem. The same preconditioned implicit-function argument gives finite critical points w_N(z), analytic on a fixed small disk, with w_N(z) tending to w(z). Let $F_N(z)=\mathcal F_N(z,w_N(z))$. The coefficient extraction of EVERY i in I is an exact |I|-torus integral. Its only angular maximum at z=0 is the zero phase: the determinant contraction pairs every ordinary phase with its neighbors, and both A and C are fixed at zero phase. The same connected graph from section 2 rules out every other phase, including lattice aliases. Every edge character is the primitive +1,-1 character. Its finite Hessian in the extracted variables is N times a uniformly positive matrix. Gaussian evaluation, with the original coefficient measure retained, therefore gives \[ P_N(e^z,1)=  rac{e^{NF_N(z)}}{(2\pi N)^{|I|/2}\sqrt{\det H_{N,II}(z)}} \left(1+O(N^{-1})ight), 	ag{5} \] where $H_{N,II}(z)=\partial_w^2\mathcal F_N(z,w_N(z))$, and the square root continues from its positive value at zero. The estimate is relative and uniform on one fixed smaller complex z disk. For completeness, the complex extension in (5) uses the same finite contour argument as the complete coefficient theorem. The stationary radius and its local integration box move analytically with z. Outside that box the original positive angular gap persists under sufficiently small complex perturbations of the weights. The connecting contour faces stay in that gap. On the moving local box, normalized third and higher derivatives are bounded, so Gaussian scaling and its odd cubic cancellation give the uniform O(N^-1) remainder. The finite-dimensional positive Hessian and compact graph fix the neighborhood before N tends to infinity. This does not differentiate a merely pointwise coefficient asymptotic or assume an unknown contributing cycle. Equations (4)-(5) imply, by Cauchy estimates on that fixed disk, \[  rac1N\log P_N(1,1)\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{cap}},\qquad  rac1N\partial_z\log P_N(e^z,1) ig|_{z=0}\longrightarrow
u,\qquad  rac1N\partial_z^2\log P_N(e^z,1) ig|_{z=0}\longrightarrow\kappa_D. 	ag{6} \] The relative error is nonzero for all sufficiently large N, and the normalized Hessian determinant stays away from zero, so their analytic logarithms and the Cauchy differentiation are legitimate. The exact odd real-root factorization of the SAME P_N is \[ P_N(A,C)=P_N(1,1)\prod_{r=1}^{N-1} [(1-p_{N,r})C+p_{N,r}A],\quad 0\le p_{N,r}\le1. \] Thus the variance in the exact negative-axis estimate is \[ V_N=\sum_rp_{N,r}(1-p_{N,r}),\qquad V_N/N\longrightarrow\kappa_D. 	ag{7} \] ## 4. A classical sufficient inequality, with its exact scope The original finite cap reduction and its strict omitted-tail estimate now give, along odd levels, \[ \limsup rac1N\log|S_N| \le\max\{M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\kappa_D,\Phi_D-\gamma_D/2\}. 	ag{8} \] Consequently the explicit response condition \[ \kappa_D > M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\Phi_D. 	ag{9} \] implies a strict absolute cap-sector gap at these fixed spectra. The weaker nonstrict condition gives a weak absolute bound. The original one-cap chain theorem supplies the sufficient alternative \(\kappa_D>W(
u)/\pi-g/(2\pi)\), or the stronger easily stated \(\kappa_D\ge W(
u)/\pi\), using its positive fixed-meridian gap. None of those comparisons is automatic from positivity of kappa_D. The response can be computed directly from the original common weights: for a triangle with supported weights a,b,c, put T=sqrt(ab+ac+bc). When at least two weights are positive, its half-loads are alpha_j=atan(L_j/T)/pi, with literal protected zeros. A pure supported corner instead has load1/2 and zero Hessian; no 0/0 formula is used. For two distinct supported corners, direct differentiation gives \[ -\partial_{\log b}\alpha_a = rac{ab}{2\pi(a+b)\sqrt{ab+ac+bc}}=:g_{ab}>0. 	ag{10} \] The diagonal is the sum of the incident g values by homogeneity. A protected endpoint contributes no log variable and no such edge; when exactly two weights are supported, (10) still holds with the third weight zero. Sum these edge conductances over the original exterior triangles. Then H is their graph Laplacian with the boundary vertex C grounded, and \[ \kappa_D= \min_{v_A=1,\ v_C=0}\sum_{\{i,j\}}g_{ij}(v_i-v_j)^2. 	ag{11} \] This is the exact effective conductance between the two ordinary cap faces. Its minimization eliminates precisely the original interior log-weight variables. The entries are algebraic in the weights up to the common factor1/pi, and the Schur operations are finite. The test uses classical gluing/response and volume data; it is not a condition on roots of a growing quantum polynomial or a purely algebraic replacement for the volume comparison. There is also a useful upper bound which limits the proposed shortcut. The finite Bernoulli variance and mean satisfy V_N/d<=bar_p_N(1-bar_p_N). Equations (6)-(7), with d/N->1, give \[ 0<\kappa_D\le
u(1-
u). 	ag{12} \] Thus a positive effective conductance alone is not a universal lower bound large enough to pay the geometric W budget. Condition (9) must be checked against the actual excess. This theorem proves no uniform margin in (9), no even-level stable factorization, and no extension to varying spectra. Those are separate requirements for a filled-period theorem. The conclusion in (8) is only the stated original one-cap/all-CROSS endpoint sector, with every source normalization and target retained. ## Dependencies The local determinant and curvature inputs are [the actual determinant curvature theorem](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md) and [the original positive coefficient saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md). The original cap Legendre attainment is [the constrained-capacity theorem](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md). The odd real stability, exact root-variance bound, and strict finite omitted-tail gap are in [the global negative-axis reduction](research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md). The geometric alternative is [the original one-cap chain budget](research_one_cap_original_chain_volume_budget.md).

title: The original one-cap coefficient reduces to two negative-axis suprema
text:
# The original one-cap coefficient reduces to two negative-axis suprema 31 October 2026. **exact-source and analytic reduction.** Unpublished. The original diagram, mark, and every ordinary degree target remain fixed. All noncap coupons are at their actual CROSS endpoint sigma=-2; the cap is at +2. No spectral-neighborhood, arbitrary-spectator, or unconditional absolute volume estimate is asserted. The final two polynomial suprema are the remaining problem. ## 1. Extract the original exterior first Use a simple matched source with protected MAIN faces u,v, cap F=(u,A,v,C), and R-1 other original ports. At level N put d=N-1 and M=floor(N/2)-1. Remove the fixed common raw unit signs from each CROSS coupon. Define the genuine binary residual polynomial \[  egin{aligned} P_N(A,C)&=\left[\prod_{\substack{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}\f
e A,C}}L_f^dight] \prod_{e
e F}P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2;L),\ P_N(A,C)&=\sum_{j=0}^{d}p_{N,j}A^jC^{d-j}. \end{aligned}	ag{1} \] Protected variables are zero BEFORE this extraction. Every remaining ordinary variable is extracted to its original d target. Homogeneity gives degree d exactly: (R-1)d-(R-2)d=d. At both parities the actual endpoint CROSS polynomials have nonnegative coefficients, so \(p_{N,j}\ge0\). This is the entire exterior, not only the ports adjacent to A. Set theta=pi/N and \[ s_j=2\sin(j	heta),\qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)	heta),\qquad U_j=\left(\prod_{r=1}^{j}s_r^2ight)\prod_{r=j+1}^{d}(2-c_r). \] The actual protected cap at +2 has all-index polynomial sum_(j=0)^d (-1)^j U_j A^(d-j)C^j; its original RIGHT piece has exactly j<=M. Thus the original cap/CROSS sector coefficient, up to its fixed unit scalar, is \[ S_N=\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_jp_{N,j}.	ag{2} \] Both original A^d and C^d demands have been imposed in (2). No sign has been assigned independently to a face occurrence. ## 2. Complete the finite cap sum, with a strictly smaller omitted tail Let R(s) be the original residual complete-triangle capacity with A load s, C load 1-s, all other ordinary loads one, and the two original protected loads zero. It is upper semicontinuous on its compact feasible interval, with value minus infinity when the fiber is empty. The same complete coefficient entropy gives \[ \Phi_D=\max_{1/2\le s\le1} igl[R(s)+2f(s-	frac12) igr].	ag{3} \] There is a strict constant gamma_D>0, depending only on the fixed diagram and mark, such that \[ \max_{1/2\le s\le1}R(s)\le\Phi_D-\gamma_D.	ag{4} \] Indeed, if 1/2<s<1 and R(s) is finite, the added cap entropy in (3) is strictly positive. At s=1/2 or s=1 it vanishes, but the cap's complete half-triangle is a pure vertex. The original complete optimizer is unique and positive on every ordinary incidence. Neither endpoint can attain its value. Compactness and upper semicontinuity now give (4). This uses the original complete-flow theorem, not any full signed-source volume conclusion. The proved uniform CLOSED local CROSS coefficient upper, followed by the actual finite shared-array sum, implies \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log p_{N,j_N}\le R(s) \qquad	ext{whenever }j_N/d\longrightarrow s.	ag{5} \] The number of local-degree arrays is polynomial because the diagram is fixed. Their limits satisfy exactly the residual targets defining R(s). This argument needs only the upper coefficient theorem; no rounding or lower estimate is needed. It includes zero coefficients. For all 0<=j<=d, \[  egin{aligned}  rac{U_{j+1}}{U_j}&= rac{\sin^2((j+1)	heta)}{\sin^2((j+3/2)	heta)} \quad(0\le j<d),\ U_0&=\csc^2(	heta/2)\le N^2,\qquad U_d=N^2,\qquad 0<U_j\le N^2. \end{aligned}	ag{6} \] The ratio crosses one only once, from below to above, so the maximum is at an endpoint. Consequently the omitted actual tail satisfies \[ |T_N|:=\left|\sum_{j=M+1}^{d}(-1)^jU_jp_{N,j}ight| \le e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_D/2)}.	ag{7} \] for all sufficiently large N. At odd N=2m+1, its smallest j=m gives j/d=1/2 exactly; at even N=2m it gives m/(2m-1)>1/2. Thus no parity seam is lost in the compact upper argument. ## 3. Exact positive moment reduction of the completed sum The original positive cap moment law supplies X_N>0 with \[ \mathbb E X_N^j= rac{U_j}{U_0}\quad(0\le j\le d),\qquad m_d:=\mathbb E X_N^d=N^2\sin^2 rac{\pi}{2N}\le rac{\pi^2}{4}.	ag{8} \] Only these finite moments are used. In particular its unbounded support is retained; no integration of degree greater than d occurs. The completed finite sum is exactly \[ S_N+T_N=U_0\mathbb E P_N(-X_N,1).	ag{9} \] Define two actual negative-axis suprema \[ B_N^- =\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P_N(-t,1)|,\qquad B_N^+ =\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P_N(-1,t)|.	ag{10} \] At t=0 these use the actual polynomial endpoint values. For X>=1, homogeneity gives P_N(-X,1)=X^d P_N(-1,1/X). Split the expectation at X=1 and use (8). The following FINITE inequality is therefore exact: \[ |S_N|\le U_0 igl[B_N^-+m_dB_N^+ igr]+|T_N|.	ag{11} \] In particular \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|S_N| \le\max\left\{\limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log\max(B_N^-,B_N^+), \Phi_D- rac{\gamma_D}{2}ight\}.	ag{12} \] The weak bound B_N^pm<=exp[N(Phi_D+o(1))] would prove the weak absolute cap estimate at these fixed spectra. A strict bound for both suprema would prove strict cap suppression. The exterior cannot be replaced by its independent positive torus majorant in this reduction: the coefficient extraction in (1) has already retained all its phases and all original demands. ## 4. Genuine odd-level real stability At odd N=2m+1 the actual sigma=-2 CROSS coupon is exactly \[ N^2D_m(x,b,y)D_m(x,c,y),\qquad D_m(x,b,y)=\det\left[bI+ rac{x}{2}H_-+ rac{y}{2}H_+ight].	ag{13} \] with the original positive-definite Hermitian H_-,H_+. If x,b,y all have positive imaginary parts, the matrix's imaginary part is positive definite. Its determinant is nonzero. Thus each factor is real stable. Identifying shared face variables, multiplying, taking the indicated derivatives for the ordinary coefficient extractions, and specializing those variables and the two protected variables to zero preserve real stability or give the zero polynomial. These closure statements also follow directly from the one-variable Gauss--Lucas/Hurwitz argument applied successively to the variables. The actual P_N is nonzero whenever its original complete coefficient is nonzero, as holds for every sufficiently large level under the retained complete-source hypotheses. Hence P_N is a homogeneous binary real-stable polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. Equivalently, including possible roots at zero or infinity, \[ P_N(A,C)=P_N(1,1)\prod_{r=1}^{d}  igl[(1-\lambda_{N,r})C+\lambda_{N,r}A igr], \qquad 0\le\lambda_{N,r}\le1.	ag{14} \] This applies to the original globally extracted polynomial, not to a degree projection of an isolated coupon. We make no corresponding even-level stability assertion here; the exact reduction (1)-(12) holds at both parities. ## 5. The exact remaining negative-axis variational problem For odd levels (14) turns (10) into \[  egin{aligned} \log B_N^- -\log P_N(1,1) &=\max_{0\le t\le1}\sum_r\log|1-(1+t)\lambda_{N,r}|,\ \log B_N^+ -\log P_N(1,1) &=\max_{0\le t\le1}\sum_r\log|t-(1+t)\lambda_{N,r}|. \end{aligned}	ag{15} \] Zeros have logarithm minus infinity. These are genuine signed boundary potentials, with the SAME root parameters for both branches. There is no modulus replacement before the original face extraction. A mean condition \(N^{-1}\sum_r\lambda_{N,r}	o
u\) alone cannot bound these potentials by a universal positive loss. Products approaching A^(nu N) C^((1-nu)N) have that mean and almost no loss at t=1. Such abstract examples are NOT asserted to arise from an original stationary triangulated exterior. The original R(s), genuine circle packing and fixed exterior targets are additional necessary data. For a strict one-cap stationary exterior, the original-chain theorem supplies M_cap-Phi_D<=W(nu)/pi-g/(2pi). A sufficient next statement is a bound on both actual quantities in (15) that pays the actual positive normalization's excess over Phi_D; the whole-star phase gap alone does not quantify it. No such bound is proved here. In particular neither real stability, nor the formal identity of the mean with nu, is being used as a substitute for an original-disk variational inequality. ## 6. A finite global variance budget at odd levels The genuine factorization (14), unlike an arbitrary star majorant, also supplies an explicit finite loss. Set \[  egin{aligned} L_N&=-\sum_r\log\max(\lambda_{N,r},1-\lambda_{N,r}),\ V_N&=\sum_r\lambda_{N,r}(1-\lambda_{N,r}) =\left.\partial_z^2\log P_N(e^z,1)ight|_{z=0}. \end{aligned}	ag{16} \] For every p,t in [0,1], the two affine functions in (15) attain their largest absolute values at an endpoint of the t interval. The endpoint values are 1-p, |1-2p| and p, all at most max(p,1-p). Moreover \[ -\log\max(p,1-p)\ge\min(p,1-p)\ge p(1-p). \] Thus the following inequalities are exact, with no asymptotic coefficient or root-distribution assertion: \[  egin{aligned} \max(B_N^-,B_N^+)&\le P_N(1,1)e^{-L_N}\le P_N(1,1)e^{-V_N},\ |S_N|&\le N^2\left(1+ rac{\pi^2}{4}ight)P_N(1,1)e^{-L_N}+|T_N|. \end{aligned}	ag{17} \] Equivalently the first term uses the genuine logarithmic Mahler measure \[  egin{aligned} \operatorname{Mahler}(P_N) &=\exp\left[ rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log|P_N(e^{i	heta},1)|\,d	hetaight]\ &=P_N(1,1)e^{-L_N}. \end{aligned}	ag{17a} \] The equality follows factor by factor from the circle logarithmic mean; roots on the circle are integrable. This is a property of the exact globally extracted polynomial. It is not the Mahler measure of separate local coupons or an exchange of a coefficient and a norm. There is a simple additional sufficient condition. Let k_N be the number of factors in (14) with \(\lambda_{N,r}\ge1/2\), counting all ties. At a tied factor the two terms are equal, and here the A term is selected. The original positive coefficient \(p_{N,k_N}\) contains the product obtained by selecting the larger term from every factor. Therefore \[ \operatorname{Mahler}(P_N)\le p_{N,k_N}.	ag{17b} \] If liminf_(N odd) k_N/d>=1/2, (4)-(5) imply a strict gap for (17a) and hence for the actual cap sector. This is a root-count condition on the original extracted polynomial; it is not implied by its mean. In a genuine strict one-cap stationary configuration, finite common weights L_A=L_C give the SAME valid residual dual upper bound for every s, and attain that bound at the stationary nu. Therefore R(nu)=M_cap is its unrestricted maximum, including s>1/2. The same upper coefficient argument (5), summed over j, gives \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log P_N(1,1)\le M_{\mathrm{cap}}.	ag{18} \] No lower coefficient rate or convergence of the second derivative is needed here. Consequently a sufficient, explicitly quantitative condition for this fixed-spectrum odd subsequence is \[ \liminf_{\substack{N	o\infty\N\ \mathrm{odd}}} rac{L_N}{N} >M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\Phi_D.	ag{19} \] The same sufficient condition with V_N in place of L_N is weaker but uses only the finite positive residual variance. If either liminf is at least M_cap-Phi_D, the weak absolute rate bound follows. If it exceeds that value by delta>0, (7), (17), (18) give a strict rate loss at least min(delta,gamma_D/2), after an arbitrarily small limiting error. These are sufficient criteria, not conclusions about all original exteriors. The geometric W budget is one possible way to upper-bound the right side of (19), but it has NOT been compared with L_N or V_N. In fact the factorwise estimate itself has a definite limitation: \[  egin{aligned} 0\le L_N&\le2\log2\sum_r\lambda_{N,r},\ 0\le V_N&\le d\, ar\lambda_N(1- ar\lambda_N),\qquad  ar\lambda_N= rac1d\sum_r\lambda_{N,r}. \end{aligned}	ag{20} \] For the first inequality, -log(1-p)<=2p log2 on 0<=p<=1/2 by convexity and the endpoint chord, while for p>=1/2 one has -log p<=log2<=2p log2. The second is Jensen's inequality for p(1-p). Thus this factorwise method cannot automatically pay a larger proposed nu-only budget. Equation (15), which retains the common optimizing t across ALL factors, is potentially sharper. This section is a general exact-source extraction criterion. It does not iterate a local cancellation estimate, claim a stationary phase for the signed polynomial, or infer an inequality from the mean alone. ## Inputs and scope Exact cap support and the all-index formula are in [the original cap source interface](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md), section 6. The [positive cap moment law](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) supplies the finite moments, including the last moment used here. The [original residual capacity](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md) fixes every target and the complete-cap entropy in (3). The closed CROSS coefficient uppers are in the [even half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) and the [odd original-source theorem](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), with the literal original shared-array dictionary. The [odd determinant factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), section 3, and [positive physical pencils](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md) give (13). The [original one-cap chain budget](research_one_cap_original_chain_volume_budget.md) provides the geometric sufficient comparison discussed after (19). Common weights give the same upper bound for every boundary split and attain it at the stationary split $
u$. This is a sufficient criterion, not a universal absolute-volume comparison. This supplies no near-spectrum extension and no complete fixed-plat or filled-period theorem. No numerical scan or source lower asymptotic is used in (1)–(12). The inequality comparing the actual negative-axis or Mahler growth with Phi remains open without a sufficient condition such as (19) or the stated root-count test.

title: A global closed-domain coefficient majorant from the original full tail
status: Uniform original-source upper bound on the full closed domain
text: # A global closed-domain coefficient majorant from the original full tail The global majorant is an upper bound. It does not give a lower coefficient limit or select a phase or cycle. ## 1. Exact treatment of the final spectral cap Retain the original full interval 0<=i<=j<=d=N-1 and r=j-i. Write theta=pi/N, kappa=cos(pi delta), 0<=delta<=1/2, and lambda_N=cos(theta)+cos(2pi delta), eta_a=lambda_N/[cos(theta)-cos((2a-1)theta)]. The actual coefficient of x^k b^i c^(d-j)y^(r-k), 0<=k<=r, is a_N=(prod_(a<i)alpha_a(delta))(prod_(a>j)alpha_a(delta)) [x^k y^(r-k)]K_(i,j), up to the recorded common unit sign. Thus its total degree is d. In particular CROSS is one full-interval K, not a difference of separately estimated central cofactors. Put s_a=2sin(pi a/N). The exact recurrence is K_(i,i)=1, K_(i,i+1)=s_(i+1)^2(x+y), K_(i,a)=s_a^2(x+y)K_(i,a-1) +s_a s_(a-1)alpha_(a-1)xy K_(i,a-2), a>=i+2.
