Dividing by prod_(i<h<=a)s_h^2 gives second coefficient alpha_(a-1)/(s_a s_(a-1))=eta_a-1: the exact identity is alpha_(a-1)+s_a s_(a-1)=2lambda_N. The row range avoids s_0. Every used denominator, i+2<=a<=j<=d, is positive. The exact normalized tail Q=K_(i,j)/prod_(i<a<=j)s_a^2 has the two-letter word expansion: the coefficient of each x^k y^(r-k) is a polynomial in lambda_N with NONNEGATIVE coefficients. Thus, even on the last cap where lambda_N<0, |[x^k y^(r-k)]Q(lambda_N)| <=[x^k y^(r-k)]Q(|lambda_N|). (1) This is the actual eta-word expansion, not an absolute-value substitution in the original signed two-step recurrence. Define a real effective spectral parameter by cos(2pi delta_eff)=|lambda_N|-cos(theta). For N>=3 its right side lies in[-1,1], and its eta parameters are exactly the positive ones in (1). If k_eff=cos(pi delta_eff), then k_eff^2=kappa^2 if lambda_N>=0, k_eff^2=1-cos(theta)-kappa^2 if lambda_N<0. (2) The negative case implies kappa^2<(1-cos theta)/2. Hence uniformly |k_eff-kappa|<=sqrt(1-cos theta)=O(1/N). (3) The original unused alpha_r(delta) factors are NOT changed to delta_eff. If any of them, or the retained A_rest factor, vanishes, the coefficient is zero and automatically satisfies the upper bound. ## 2. Uniform fixed-tilt bounds on the full compact parameter set For any fixed T<infinity, all l in[-T,T], every original row interval, and all real delta in[0,1/2], the full-interval fixed-block proof gives N^(-1)log K_(i,j)(exp(l),1;delta_eff) <=int_(i/N)^(j/N) log Lambda_(delta_eff)(t;exp(l),1)dt+o(1), (4) uniformly. Here are the inputs that remain valid at the cap. Divide K by prod_(i<h<=a)s_h instead of its square. The exact signed transfer is T_a=[[s_a(x+y),alpha_(a-1)(delta_eff)xy],[1,0]], a>=i+2, with initial values 1 and s_(i+1)(x+y). Its entries are uniformly bounded on the whole row range and the fixed tilt interval. Its frozen limiting matrix has spectral radius rho=(x+y)sin(pi t) +sqrt((x-y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4xy k_eff^2), and both eigenvalue magnitudes are at most rho. On [eta,1-eta], rho has a uniform positive lower bound. Cayley--Hamilton therefore bounds the m-th power by C(m+1)rho^m with uniform C, INCLUDING the repeated-root case x=y,k_eff=0; no eigenbasis inverse is used. For each fixed m, an actual m-row block differs uniformly by o(1) from its frozen block. Multiply these block bounds, then let N grow, m grow, and eta decrease to zero in that order. The factor C(m+1) costs log(C(m+1))/m per row. The bounded transfers on the two endpoint intervals cost O(eta N), and their omitted logarithmic integrals cost O(eta log(1/eta)N). Restoring prod s_a by its uniform sine-log upper sum gives (4), with Lambda=2sin(pi t)rho. Uniformly in l and delta, c_T sin^2(pi t)<=Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)<=C_T, so the missing endpoint integrals are uniformly small. The proof includes the defective balanced root at the final spectral cap. The integral in (4) is jointly continuous on the full compact set of endpoints, delta and l in[-T,T]: on every interior t interval this is ordinary continuity, and the displayed integrable lower bound controls both endpoints uniformly. Equation (3) consequently allows delta_eff to be replaced by delta in that integral at cost o(1), uniformly in all these variables. Equivalently regard the integral as a continuous function of kappa in[0,1], so no inverse-cosine derivative near an endpoint is needed. The original unused products satisfy the full uniform UPPER Riemann estimate N^(-1)log |prod_(a<i)alpha_a(delta) prod_(a>j)alpha_a(delta)| <= B_delta(i/N,j/N)+o(1), B_delta(mu,nu)=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta(t)|dt +int_nu^1 log|alpha_delta(t)|dt. (5) The same truncation proof covers all real delta, including merging cosine zeros and every sampled zero. The two cosine logarithms have uniformly integrable singularities. Moving a mesh endpoint by one row changes the corresponding integral by o(1) uniformly; a missing sampled zero is never assigned a finite lower logarithm. For the exact original coefficient a_N(k,i,d-j,r-k), equations(1)--(5) and finite Cauchy extraction give, uniformly for l in[-T,T], N^(-1)log|a_N| <=B_delta(mu,nu)+Phi_delta(mu,nu,l)-xi l+o(1), (6) Phi_delta=int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt, mu=i/N, nu=j/N, xi=k/N. No coefficient positivity is asserted on the negative lambda_N cap; the exact domination (1) is what supplies (6) there. Both parities and all original scalar modes/zeros are retained in the coefficient. ## 3. Uniform truncation of the outer Legendre infimum Let w=nu-mu and 0<=xi<=w. Factor the limiting tail root as Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)=4sin^2(pi t) rho_eta(exp(l),1), rho_eta(x,y)=[x+y+sqrt((x-y)^2+4eta xy)]/2, eta=kappa^2/sin^2(pi t). With a=exp(-|l|), the elementary square-root inequality gives 1<=rho_eta(exp(l),1)/max(exp(l),1) =[1+a+sqrt((1-a)^2+4eta a)]/2 <=1+sqrt(eta a). (7) Thus log rho_eta=max(0,l)+r_delta(t,l), where 0<=r_delta(t,l) <=log(1+exp(-|l|/2)/sin(pi t)). (8) Set R_T=int_0^1 log(1+exp(-T/2)/sin(pi t))dt. It tends to0. An explicit bound, using sin(pi t)>=2min(t,1-t), is R_T <=(1+a_T)log(1+a_T)-a_T log a_T, a_T=exp(-T/2). (9) Subtract the l-independent sine integral from Phi-xi l. Its remaining value is (w-xi)l+int r for l>=0 and -xi l+int r for l<=0. If l>T, its value is at least(w-xi)T, while the value at T is at most (w-xi)T+R_T. The same comparison holds at -T for l<-T. Therefore 0<=inf_(|l|<=T)(Phi-xi l)-inf_(l in R)(Phi-xi l)<=R_T, (10) UNIFORMLY in every closed row interval, xi, and delta. It includes w=0, xi=0,w, delta=1/2 and exact protected endpoints. There is no uniform-minimizer assumption and no concavity in mu or nu. ## 4. Continuity and the global coefficient LIMSUP Define on the FULL closed parameter domain H_delta(mu,nu,xi)=B_delta(mu,nu) +inf_l[Phi_delta(mu,nu,l)-xi l]. (11) B is continuous, by the same uniform integrability as (5). For each finite T the truncated minimum is continuous: its integrand is jointly continuous on a compact parameter set, and the difference of two minima is bounded by the uniform difference of their functions. Equation(10) then makes H a uniform limit of continuous functions. In particular H is continuous and finite on the entire closed domain. Given epsilon>0 choose T with R_T<epsilon, use (6) uniformly on that fixed tilt interval, and minimize there. Equations(10)--(11) prove limsup_(N->infinity) sup_(all i,j,k,delta) [N^(-1)log|a_N|-H_delta(i/N,j/N,k/N)]<=0. (12) This is a GLOBAL uniform coefficient upper bound, including the final spectral cap, all closed outer degrees, diagonal and terminal intervals, both level parities, and sampled zeros. Zero coefficients have logarithm minus infinity. No lower rate or every-level equality is inferred. If normalized degrees are taken over d=N-1, they sum to1 exactly and give mu=q_b,nu=1-q_c,xi=q_x. The N-normalized parameters in (12) differ by O(1/N). Uniform continuity of H on its full compact domain absorbs that difference uniformly. No finite protected target or seam support is changed. ## 5. The original shared-source upper problem is now compact For a fixed actual diagram D with R ports, use the original incidence flow polytope: each port supplies1, each ordinary face demands1, and the two original protected faces demand0. Assume it is nonempty, as it is in the certified geometric class. If it is empty, every finite source coefficient is identically zero and no finite maximum is needed. Define M_D=max_(q in this polytope, delta in[0,1/2]^R) sum_e H_(delta_e)(q_b,1-q_c,q_x). (13) The maximum exists by continuity. The number of original finite degree arrays is polynomial in N at fixed R. Apply (12) to every local factor and the triangle inequality to the ONE original marked coefficient. For its actual raw full numerator S_N, sup_(delta in[0,1/2]^R)|S_N(delta)| <=exp{N[M_D+o(1)]}. (14) All signs and omitted-half phases are still in S_N; (14) bounds their absolute sum rather than asserting they align. Only the upper passage from finite arrays to limiting flows is used. There is no lattice lower approximation, equality of rates, or separate optimization of local weighted norms in place of the shared target. The former boundary-UNIFORM coefficient-majorant burden is removed by (12), but the boundary-GEOMETRY and global phase questions remain. In particular neither M_D<=Phi_D nor a contributing full period is proved here. The [full-fiber boundary reduction](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md) and [stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) apply to this compact upper problem at their stated scopes. The global phase comparison still needs its own quantitative estimate. This proof uses no numerical audit. ## Dependencies and internal verification scope The [original four-state source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) supplies the exact full-interval coefficient and unused-row factors. The [positive eta-word identity](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) gives the polynomial domination in section1. The [global CROSS proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) supplies the antecedent fixed-block argument; section2 extends it explicitly through the cap on the full row range. The [full-fiber stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) is a downstream consequence together with the separate boundary lemmas; it is not a premise of the coefficient upper bound. No coefficient lower bound, positivity at the cap, phase alignment, complete-volume comparison or full-period estimate follows from this upper bound.

title: A real-root preserving q-derivative on the original protected-Green degree range
text: # A real-root preserving q-derivative on the original protected-Green degree range 31 October 2026. analytical research theorem. The theorem below gives new positive structure for the FULL spectator polynomial. It does not claim that truncation preserves roots, that the full polynomial is integrable against the Green moment law, or that the original signed coefficient is bounded by \(\Phi_D\). ## 1. The exact finite operator Put \(N\ge3\), \(\theta=\pi/N\), \(q=e^{i\theta}\), \(s_j=2\sin(j\theta)\), and \(S_a=\prod_{j=1}^a s_j\). Let \(0\le a<N\) and \(D=N+a-1\). On polynomials define \[ \begin{gathered} E=z\frac{d}{dz},\qquad \partial_qP(z)=\frac{P(qz)-P(q^{-1}z)}{iz},\\ \partial_qz^k=s_kz^{k-1}. \end{gathered}\tag{1} \] The removable value at z=0 is understood polynomially. Thus \[ \partial_q^aP(z) =\sum_{k\ge a}p_k\left(\prod_{j=0}^{a-1}s_{k-j}\right)z^{k-a}. \tag{2} \] Terms with k<a are zero. Terms with N<=k<=N+a-1 are also EXACTLY zero, since their product contains s_N. No limiting sine quotient is used. For a<=k<=N-1 all factors in (2) are strictly positive. **Theorem.** If \(P\) is a real polynomial of degree at most \(D\) with nonnegative coefficients and all its zeros nonpositive real, then \(\partial_q^aP\) is either zero or has nonnegative coefficients and all its zeros nonpositive real. Its degree is at most \(N-a-1\). This theorem concerns the compound a-th derivative. The intermediate single q-derivatives need not preserve nonpositive roots once the degree exceeds N. A zero output is possible, for example P=z^D when a>0. ## 2. Elementary proof by Euler's sine product We first record two ordinary operations on the cone of nonnegative polynomials with nonpositive real zeros. * Ordinary differentiation, multiplication by z, and fixed-degree reversal \(\operatorname{Rev}_DP(z)=z^DP(1/z)\) preserve this cone, or give zero. Reversal is allowed when degree P<D, in which case it adds zeros at 0. * For r<0, E-r preserves this cone. For r>D, r-E also preserves it on degree-at-most-D polynomials. Here is a self-contained verification of the second assertion. For c>0 and a polynomial P whose d zeros are distinct and strictly negative, the derivative of t^c P(-t) has at least one positive zero between 0 and its first positive zero, and between each consecutive pair of its positive zeros. Its nontrivial polynomial factor is c P(-t)+t d/dt P(-t), of degree d. Thus cP+EP has all its d roots negative and has nonnegative coefficients. Repeated or zero roots follow by perturbing the roots and taking coefficient limits. Finally \[ \operatorname{Rev}_D(r-E)P =(r-D+E)\operatorname{Rev}_DP.\tag{3} \] which proves the assertion for r>D. This proof retains all polynomial degrees; there is no assumption about a quantum inner product. The bottom and top multiplier blocks are respectively \[ \begin{aligned} B_a(E)&=\prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(E-j)=z^a\partial_z^a,\\ T_a(E)&=\prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(N+j-E) =\operatorname{Rev}_D B_a(E)\operatorname{Rev}_D. \end{aligned}\tag{4} \] Each WHOLE block preserves the cone. Individual factors of T_a or B_a whose zero lies inside [0,D] are not being asserted to do so. The two blocks commute, being polynomials in E. For k in the finite set {0,...,D}, Euler's sine product gives \[ \begin{aligned} \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}s_{k-j} &=\left(\frac{2\pi}{N^2}\right)^a \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(k-j)(N+j-k) \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}\left(1+\frac{k-j}{N}\right)\\ &\quad\cdot \prod_{n=2}^{\infty}\prod_{j=0}^{a-1} \left(1-\frac{k-j}{nN}\right) \left(1+\frac{k-j}{nN}\right). \end{aligned}\tag{5} \] The identities at the zero coefficients hold by the same entire-function product, without division by those zero factors. All remaining linear factors have their roots OUTSIDE [0,D]: the n=1 root is j-N<0; for n>=2 the roots are j-nN<0 and j+nN>D. The last strict inequality uses a<N. Thus each finite product of the remaining factors, applied as a polynomial in E after the two blocks in (4), preserves the cone. Every coefficient multiplier in its nonzero range is positive. The paired infinite product converges for each k, hence uniformly on the finite coefficient set. The limit polynomial is therefore in the same closed cone, or zero. For completeness, its closedness follows by polynomial convergence and Hurwitz on each compact subset off the nonpositive real axis; degree loss can only send roots to infinity. Formula (5) says the limiting polynomial is exactly \[ z^a\partial_q^aP(z).\tag{6} \] Removing its forced z^a proves the theorem. The support and degree claims follow directly from (2). For a=0 the assertion is the identity operator and the empty products are one. No finite numerical sample, scalar orthogonal-polynomial identification, or external multiplier-sequence theorem is needed in this proof. ## 3. The original odd endpoint spectator really satisfies the hypotheses Consider an original simple marked source with R ports, R ordinary face variables and two protected variables. Let a selected Green coupon have ordered faces (x,b,c,y), with y protected and x,b,c distinct ordinary faces. Assume every other coupon is its actual CROSS endpoint at sigma=-2. We do not change any source diagram, matching, mark, or face demand. At odd N=2k+1, d=N-1 and M=k-1. The exact endpoint coupon is \[ \begin{aligned} P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2) &=N^2D_k(x_e,b_e,y_e)D_k(x_e,c_e,y_e),\\ D_k(x,b,y)&=\det\left[bI+\frac{x}{2}H_-+\frac{y}{2}H_+\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{7} \] after removal of its fixed common raw unit sign. The physical matrices H_-,H_+ are positive-definite Hermitian. For variables with positive imaginary parts, the imaginary part of the matrix in (7) is positive definite. Its determinant is nonzero, so each factor is real stable. It has nonnegative coefficients by its positive mixed-minor expansion. Products and identification of shared variables preserve real stability. Derivatives and specialization of variables to a real boundary value preserve it or give zero; these follow by the one-variable Gauss--Lucas argument, approximation from the upper half-plane and Hurwitz. In particular extraction of any fixed nonnegative power, performed as a derivative followed by specialization at 0, is allowed. All protected variables are specialized to0 before extraction. Let the exact residual spectator be \[ P(x,b,c)= \left[\prod_{\substack{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}\\f\notin\{x,b,c\}}}L_f^d\right] \prod_{e\ne\mathrm{Green}}P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2;L). \tag{8} \] It is zero or a nonnegative real-stable polynomial, homogeneous of degree 2d: (R-1)d-(R-3)d=2d. Its full coefficients retain every shared ordinary target already extracted in (8). There is no independent optimization of different occurrences of a face. At the original lower node a<=M the input determinant has expansion \[ D_a(x,b,0)=\sum_{v=0}^a d_{a,v}x^{a-v}b^v, \qquad d_{a,v}\ge0.\tag{9} \] For each v define the actual binary residual \[ P_v(x,c)=[b^{d-v}]P(x,b,c).\tag{10} \] It has degree d+v=N+v-1, not degree d in general. It is zero or nonnegative real stable. Consequently P_v(1,z) has only nonpositive real roots, including possible zero roots; this follows from real coefficients, upper-half-plane nonvanishing, and coefficient positivity. Since \(v\le a\), its degree is at most \(N+a-1\), exactly the range of the theorem. Thus each FULL polynomial \[ Q_v(z)=\partial_q^aP_v(1,z).\tag{11} \] is zero or nonnegative and negative-rooted, with degree at most \(N-a-1\). There is a stronger combined statement: include the ACTUAL input determinant before extracting the b target. Define \[ \begin{aligned} F_a(x,c)&=[b^d]D_a(x,b,0)P(x,b,c)\\ &=\sum_{v=0}^a d_{a,v}x^{a-v}P_v(x,c). \end{aligned}\tag{11a} \] Both factors before this extraction are real stable, so F_a is zero or a nonnegative real-stable binary polynomial. Its degree is exactly d+a=N+a-1 when it is nonzero. Therefore the SINGLE full polynomial \[ Q_a(z)=\partial_q^aF_a(1,z).\tag{11b} \] is zero or negative-rooted with nonnegative coefficients. This combines all input b-loads with their original weights; it is not an unsupported assertion that an arbitrary positive sum of stable polynomials stays stable. The multiplication and coefficient extraction in (11a) prove the required stability directly. This is a genuine original-source statement for arbitrary valence of the selected Green faces: no two-port internal-demand reduction is used. It does require the stated CROSS endpoint exterior. An unextracted fan can have larger c degree; adding arbitrary signed exterior coupons need not preserve real stability. No assertion about that broader maximal-component situation follows from (11). The same reasoning works whenever an actual protected-source extraction has the stated degree bound and stable exterior. If b is also protected, only v=0 remains and the direct two-variable degree count gives d; this optional specialization adds no new moment or spectral claim. ## 4. Exact Green pairing and the two surviving cutoff issues For the source variables and node above, keep the original Green law X=X_(N,a), m=M-a, and the original total cutoff in the parent degree c. Its exact moments are \[ \begin{gathered} \mathbb E X^r=A_r= \prod_{i=1}^r\frac{s_{a+i}}{s_{2a+i+1}}, \qquad r\in\{0,\ldots,m\},\\ \mathbb E X^t<\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -a-1<t<N-2a-1. \end{gathered}\tag{12} \] The real interval in (12) is the OPEN Mellin domain; integer moments used by the original source have 0<=r<=m. In the protected outer case, the original sine-binomial identity gives \[ H_r(W_a(x,0))=B_a(r)x^r,\qquad B_a(r)=\frac{S_{a+r}}{S_aS_r}. \] Here \(P_{v,\le M}\) truncates \(P_v(1,z)\) in \(z\); later \(F_{a,\le M}\) likewise truncates \(F_a(1,z)\). The normalized original pairing obeys exactly \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal L_a(P_v) &=\sum_{r=0}^m(-1)^rA_rB_a(r)[z^{a+r}]P_v(1,z)\\ &=\frac1{S_a}\mathbb E\!\left[ \partial_q^a(P_{v,\le M})(-X)\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{13} \] The b and x degree targets have not disappeared: after the term x^(a-v)b^v in (9), the b target is exactly (10); homogeneity of P_v makes every term in (13) have total x degree d. Thus, with all original ordinary demands imposed, the normalized nodal Green/CROSS coefficient is \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal B_{a,N}=(-1)^m\gamma_{N,a} \sum_{v=0}^a d_{a,v}\mathcal L_a(P_v),\\ \gamma_{N,a}=\frac{N}{s_{2a+1}s_{m+1}}, \qquad N\ \mathrm{odd}. \end{gathered}\tag{14} \] Equivalently, using the single actual stable polynomial (11a), \[ \mathcal B_{a,N} =\frac{(-1)^m\gamma_{N,a}}{S_a} \mathbb E\!\left[\partial_q^a(F_{a,\le M})(-X)\right]. \tag{14a} \] All input determinant coefficients have been included in F_a. The factor 1/S_a is exact and can have exponential size; it is not absorbed into the polynomially bounded gamma. This is the already fixed original nodal block normalization \(R_aD_{a,m}=\gamma_{N,a}D_a\). The common raw source sign and the UNUSED Green scalar \(\zeta_N(u)\), present when the nodal block is interpolated back into the original numerator, remain outside this displayed block. Equation (14) does not evaluate or cancel that scalar at a sampled zero. Although Q_v in (11) is negative-rooted, the polynomial in (13) is its initial degree segment: \[ \partial_q^a(P_{v,\le M})(z) =Q_v(z)-\sum_{s=M+1}^{N-1} \bigl([z^s]P_v(1,z)\bigr) \frac{S_s}{S_{s-a}}z^{s-a}. \tag{15} \] Terms absent from the actual P_v are zero. Thus the upper band N<=s<=N+a-1 vanishes for algebraic reasons, but the ACTUAL cutoff current M<s<N remains. Truncation can destroy negative-rootedness; no root claim is made for the left side of (15). Nor can (15) be integrated termwise after dropping the cutoff. Its full degree can be N-a-1, whereas the moment threshold in (12) is N-2a-1. Some currents therefore need unavailable moments, even though every term in the original truncated (13) is integrable. For a=0 the top degree N-1 is itself at the excluded threshold. The identity is a polynomial identity at finite X, not a license for subtracting divergent expectations. The same exact cutoff identity and moment warning apply to the combined F_a,Q_a in (11a)--(14a); this is the version retaining the entire input polynomial before any absolute value. ## 5. A genuine full-polynomial phase identity, with its exact limitation If the combined \(Q_a\) is nonzero, write \(Q_a(z)=Kz^\ell\prod_j(z+\lambda_j)\), where \(\lambda_j>0\) and \(K>0\). For any \(r>0\) put \(p_j=r/(r+\lambda_j)\). Then its actual phase ratio is exactly \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{|Q_a(re^{i\phi})|}{Q_a(r)} &=\prod_j\left[1-4p_j(1-p_j)\sin^2(\phi/2)\right]^{1/2}\\ &\le \exp\left[-2\sin^2(\phi/2)\sum_jp_j(1-p_j)\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{16} \] The zero-root monomial has modulus one in this ratio. The variance is also exactly \[ \left(r\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\right)^2\log Q_a(r) =\sum_jp_j(1-p_j).\tag{17} \] In particular the negative-axis value admits a genuine factor-by-factor cancellation formula, before any absolute value is taken on its coefficients. This uses the SAME actual fully extracted polynomial, not an independently chosen positive majorant. Equations (15) and (12) are the precise remaining obstacles to using (16) inside the original Green expectation. In addition, no uniform order-N lower bound on (17) has been proved from the original exterior constraints. Thus the theorem establishes a general actual-source positive structure, but neither an absolute \(\Phi_D\) bound nor a signed Green contraction. ## Inputs The [original odd endpoint product](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), sections 2–3, supplies (7). The [physical positive matrices](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md), sections 1 and 3, supply the determinant stability. The [original maximal-Green block](research_maximal_green_component_block_transport.md), sections 4–5, retains the unused scalar and exact targets. The [sine-binomial and moment theorem](research_green_tail_sine_binomial_moment_transform.md) supplies the finite signed kernel and exact Mellin domain. The [original algebraic period](research_green_tail_algebraic_period_and_mellin_rate.md), sections 2–3, supplies the complete scalar and coefficient pairing. The theorem concerns exact real-root structure with the stated zero bands, original targets, Mellin cutoff and phase. It does not assert an asymptotic coefficient theorem.

title: The original Green pairing as a finite algebraic period and its exact Mellin cost
text: # The original Green pairing as a finite algebraic period and its exact Mellin cost 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. The kernel below is the original nodal Green tail with its original face extraction. Its contour form is an exact reformulation, not a new quantum invariant. The final volume comparison remains unproved. ## 1. The finite source data Use the [exact sine-binomial and finite-moment theorem](research_green_tail_sine_binomial_moment_transform.md). Put \[ M=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1,\quad 0\le a\le M,\quad m=M-a,\quad h=a+1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r. \] Let W be the MULTISET of 2a+2 values \[ W=W_a(x,y)=\{xq^{a-2r},yq^{a-2r}:0\le r\le a\}. \tag{1} \] Keep all repeated nodes. Write H_r for the complete homogeneous polynomial on a multiset. The original tail identity is \[ T_{a,M}(x,c,y)=D_{a,m}\,\mathbb E H_m(\{c\}\cup XW), \qquad D_{a,m}=\prod_{i=1}^m s_i s_{2a+i+1}. \tag{2} \] Here $X=X_{N,a}>0$ is the independently constructed beta-product variable. Its actual Mellin transform $M_{N,a}(t)=\mathbb E X^t$ exists on \[ -h<t<N-2h+1, \qquad \frac{M_{N,a}(t+1)}{M_{N,a}(t)} =\frac{\sin(\pi(h+t)/N)}{\sin(\pi(2h+t)/N)} \tag{3} \] whenever both moments in the ratio exist. For nonnegative integer r this is exactly the retained sine product A_r. In particular all integer moments from -a to m exist. No moments beyond the actual domain in (3) will be used. In fact the integer h makes this transform FINITE: \[ M_{N,a}(t)=\prod_{j=h}^{2h-1} \frac{\sin(\pi j/N)}{\sin(\pi(j+t)/N)}. \tag{3a} \] One concrete choice is $X=\prod_{j=h}^{2h-1}Y_j^{1/N}$, with independent positive variables of density \[ \frac{\sin(\pi j/N)}\pi\, \frac{y^{j/N-1}}{1+y}\,dy,\qquad y>0. \tag{3b} \] The Euler beta integral gives each factor of (3a), with exactly the moment interval in (3). This agrees with the upstream infinite-product law: for integer h its gamma factors telescope to j/(j+t) and, for each k>=1, (kN+j)(kN-j)/((kN+j+t)(kN-j-t)); Euler's sine product then gives (3a). Thus no moment-interpolation uniqueness is assumed. Let P(c,Y)=sum_s p_s(Y)c^s be the actual CROSS spectator product, with its shared boundary variables still identified, and define P_<=M by truncating ONLY its c degree at M. The original nodal pairing is \[ Q_{a,N}(Y)=R_a(x,b,y;u_a) [c^M]T_{a,M}(x,-c,y)P(c,Y). \tag{4} \] Thus its untruncated original parent demand remains the one established in the [maximal-Green component theorem](research_maximal_green_component_block_transport.md). No extra sum or independent face radius is introduced. ## 2. An exact confluent divided difference For nodes zeta_1,...,zeta_n, define their confluent divided difference of a polynomial F by \[ [\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_n]F =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint \frac{F(t)}{\prod_{j=1}^n(t-\zeta_j)}\,dt, \tag{5} \] with a positive contour enclosing every node. This definition remains valid at collisions, including zero nodes. Expanding at infinity proves \[ [\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_n]t^d =\begin{cases}0,&d<n-1,\\H_{d-n+1}(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_n),&d\ge n-1. \end{cases} \tag{6} \] The signed version of (2), followed by the original coefficient extraction, therefore gives exactly \[ Q_{a,N} =(-1)^m R_a(x,b,y;u_a)D_{a,m}\, \mathbb E\,[ -XW ]\bigl(t^{a+1}P_{\le M}(t,Y)\bigr). \tag{7} \] Indeed n=2a+2, so the monomial p_s t^(a+1+s) gives H_(s-a)(-XW); only a<=s<=M survive. This recovers exactly the signed finite sum from the upstream kernel theorem. Every surviving power of X is between 0 and m. ## 3. A fixed contour, retaining all scalar factors There is a useful stronger form of (7). Define the finite diagonal Mellin operator on the truncated polynomial by \[ (\mathscr M_{N,a}P)(w,Y) =\sum_{s=0}^M M_{N,a}(s-a)\,p_s(Y)w^s. \tag{8} \] Choose a fixed circle |w|=R>max(|x|,|y|). For each X>0 take the contour t=Xw in (5). Homogeneity gives \[ \mathbb E\,[ -XW ]\bigl(t^{a+1}P_{\le M}(t,Y)\bigr) =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_{|w|=R} \frac{w^{a+1}(\mathscr M_{N,a}P)(w,Y)} {\prod_{v\in W}(w+v)}\,dw. \tag{9} \] The exchange of expectation and this FIXED contour is justified, not formal: before expectation its numerator is X^(-a)P_<=M(Xw,Y). Every absolute random power is X^(s-a), with -a<=s-a<=m strictly inside (3), and the fixed denominator is bounded away from zero on the circle. There are finitely many terms. This also explains why the untruncated spectator polynomial cannot simply be inserted. The exact original cofactor adapter is R_a=S_(2a)D_a(x,b,y), where D_a is the physical half-triangle determinant. Reflection S_(N-1-r)=N/S_r proves the FULL scalar simplification \[ R_aD_{a,m}=\gamma_{N,a}D_a(x,b,y),\qquad \gamma_{N,a}= \begin{cases} N/s_{2a+1},&N\text{ even},\\ N/(s_{2a+1}s_{m+1}),&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \tag{10} \] To check it, D_(a,m)=S_m S_(a+M+1)/S_(2a+1). In the even case S_m S_(a+M+1)=N; in the odd case it is N/s_(m+1). These identities include m=0. In particular gamma is nonzero and bounded above and below by powers of N, uniformly in a. It is retained explicitly. Combining (7), (9), and (10) is the exact original-source period: \[ Q_{a,N}(Y)= \frac{(-1)^m\gamma_{N,a}D_a(x,b,y)}{2\pi i} \oint_{|w|=R} \frac{w^{a+1}(\mathscr M_{N,a}P)(w,Y)} {\prod_{r=0}^a(w+xq^{a-2r})(w+yq^{a-2r})}\,dw. \tag{11} \] All integer Mellin entries in (8) are finite products of sine ratios by (3). Thus (11) is a finite algebraic functional over the original cyclotomic coefficient field. The positive probability law gives one representation and useful estimates for that functional; it does not change its definition. Repeated poles in (11) mean confluent residues, not factors to be divided out or discarded. The diagonal operator also has an exact finite q-differential description. On its actual coefficient range 0<=s<=M, \[ M_{N,a}(s-a)=\frac{S_{2a+1}S_s}{S_aS_{s+a+1}}. \tag{11a} \] Define the symmetric sine derivative on polynomials by \[ \partial_q f(w)=\frac{f(qw)-f(q^{-1}w)}{iw},\qquad \partial_q w^n=s_n w^{n-1}. \] For the actual numerator $F(w)=w^{a+1}(\mathscr M_{N,a}P)(w)$, \[ \partial_q^{a+1}F(w)=\frac{S_{2a+1}}{S_a}P_{\le M}(w). \tag{11b} \] Every sine division here has index at most M+a+1<=2M+1<N. Thus this is a literal root-safe polynomial identity. Moreover F is the unique solution divisible by w^(a+1) of degree at most M+a+1: the displayed diagonal derivative has no zero coefficient on that space. No root-of-unity resonance is silently inverted. This supplies a finite operator characterization of the same numerator in (11); it asserts no generic-q AJ equation or new topological invariance theorem. There is a precise affine freedom here. All solutions of (11b) of degree at most M+h form a torsor for the additive space of polynomials of degree below h. The full-node contour in (11) annihilates this space: its denominator has degree 2h, and a numerator of degree below h has no residue at infinity. The original period is therefore independent of those q-integration constants. This statement concerns the stated full-node cycle; it need not hold for a contour enclosing only a selected subset of poles. This freedom can remove one whole q-string without losing a residue. Put \[ P_x(w)=\prod_{r=0}^a(w+xq^{a-2r}),\qquad F(w)=P_x(w)B_x(w)+A_x(w),\quad \deg A_x<h. \] This is ordinary division by a MONIC polynomial; it is valid even at zero or colliding face arguments. The remainder does not contribute to the full period. Also $\partial_q^h A_x=0$. Thus B_x is exactly the unique polynomial of degree at most M solving \[ \partial_q^h\bigl(P_x(w)B_x(w)\bigr) =\frac{S_{2a+1}}{S_a}P_{\le M}(w). \tag{11c} \] Uniqueness follows from the same degree bound: a difference would make P_x times a polynomial lie in the degree-below-h kernel, hence vanish. Finally the symmetric q-string divided-difference identity is \[ [zq^a,zq^{a-2},\ldots,zq^{-a}]B =\frac{\partial_q^aB(z)}{S_a},\qquad \deg B\le M. \] Check it on w^s: both sides vanish for s<a, and for s>=a the finite sine-binomial identity gives S_s z^(s-a)/(S_a S_(s-a)). All required indices are below N. The exact same original nodal pairing is therefore \[ Q_{a,N}= \frac{(-1)^m\gamma_{N,a}D_a(x,b,y)}{S_a} (\partial_q^a B_x)(-y). \tag{11d} \] Confluent nodes cause no exception: monic division and the polynomial q-string identity include them. In particular x=y retains the repeated-pole information of the original contour. The additional factor 1/S_a in (11d) is explicit and can be exponential; it has not been declared harmless. The order h grows with the quantum node, so (11c) is not a fixed-order generic-q quantum A-polynomial assertion. For a genuine cap tree, first replace the spectator coefficients by their [proved finite signed path-dilation averages](research_maximal_green_component_block_transport.md). Its total component degree is truncated at M before that average. The independent Green variable X then gives the same (7)-(11) coefficientwise, retaining the original outside factor U_0^(number of cap edges). All moments used by each independent variable stay in its proved range. ## 4. The exact interior Mellin growth Consider ANY sequence of the original indices for which h/N -> alpha with 0<alpha<1/2. Put Y_N=log X_(N,a). For \[ -\alpha<s<1-2\alpha, \qquad \kappa_\alpha(s)=\int_0^s \log\frac{\sin(\pi(\alpha+t))}{\sin(\pi(2\alpha+t))}\,dt, \tag{12} \] the integral is oriented when s<0. Then \[ \frac1N\log\mathbb E e^{NsY_N}\longrightarrow\kappa_\alpha(s). \tag{13} \] Convergence is uniform on compact subsets of the admissible (alpha,s) region. This covers both parities without replacing N. Proof at integer t=Ns uses (3) and M(0)=1: log M(t) is the sum of the retained log sine ratios, oriented backward for negative t. On a compact subregion the two sine arguments stay uniformly away from their zeros. The Riemann sums therefore give (12) uniformly. For arbitrary real t between adjacent integers, convexity of log M(t) places it below the joining chord and above the extrapolated preceding chord. The successive integer differences are uniformly bounded on these compact sets, again by (3). Interpolating changes the logarithm by O(1), which proves (13). No derivative of an unproved asymptotic is used. There is also a direct proof from the finite product (3a), valid for real s without interpolation. Its normalized logarithm is the Riemann sum of log(sin(pi t)/sin(pi(t+s))) over h/N<=t<2h/N. The limit is the integral over alpha<=t<=2alpha. It equals (12): both vanish at s=0, and their s derivatives are the first expression in (14). All arguments remain in a fixed compact subset of (0,1) on the stated parameter compacts, so the convergence is uniform. The limit is strictly convex: \[ \begin{aligned} \kappa_\alpha'(s)&= \log\frac{\sin(\pi(\alpha+s))}{\sin(\pi(2\alpha+s))},\\ \kappa_\alpha''(s)&= \frac{\pi\sin(\pi\alpha)} {\sin(\pi(\alpha+s))\sin(\pi(2\alpha+s))}>0. \end{aligned}\tag{14} \] Its first derivative ranges from -infinity to +infinity on the open interval in (12). The typical positive value is exp(kappa_alpha'(0))=1/(2cos(pi alpha)). ## 5. A proved large-deviation cost, not a bounded-moment shortcut Define for y real \[ I_\alpha(y)=\sup_{-\alpha<s<1-2\alpha} \{sy-\kappa_\alpha(s)\}. \tag{15} \] The laws of Y_N satisfy the large-deviation bounds with speed N and this rate: the logarithmic probability of any open set is at least minus the infimum of I there, and that of any closed set is at most minus its infimum. The rate is good, finite and strictly convex, with its unique zero at log(1/(2cos(pi alpha))). Here is a direct proof sufficient for the stated claim. Fixed positive and negative s in (12), together with (13) and Markov's inequality, give exponential tightness. For a compact set, apply the same bound with a near-optimal s at each point and take a finite interval cover; letting interval widths decrease proves the closed-set upper bound. For the lower bound at y choose the unique s with kappa_alpha'(s)=y and tilt the probability law by exp(NsY_N)/M(Ns). Under this law, small positive and negative tilts, (13), and strict differentiability give exponentially small probabilities for Y_N outside (y-epsilon, y+epsilon). Undoing the tilt on that interval gives lower rate -I_alpha(y)-|s|epsilon. Let epsilon decrease to zero and then take the best y in the open set. Exponential tightness extends the upper bound from compact to closed sets. Finally I grows at least linearly at both infinities by choosing one fixed tilt of each sign, so its level sets are compact. These arguments establish the asserted bounds directly rather than importing a large-deviation theorem. The optimizing tilt has an explicit form. For xi=e^y>0 put \[ \vartheta=\operatorname{Arg}(1-\xi e^{-\pi i\alpha}) \in(0,\pi(1-\alpha)),\qquad s_\xi=\vartheta/\pi-\alpha. \tag{16} \] Indeed xi=sin(pi(alpha+s))/sin(pi(2alpha+s)) is equivalent to tan vartheta=xi sin(pi alpha)/(1-xi cos(pi alpha)), with precisely the displayed continuous argument branch. Equations (15)-(16) therefore evaluate the cost without a free saddle choice. At the upper endpoint, the continuous value of (12) is \[ \kappa_\alpha(1-2\alpha) =2\int_0^\alpha\log(2\cos(\pi t))\,dt>0. \tag{17} \] This agrees with the exact last-even-moment computation in the upstream theorem. It is the exponential cost missed by copying the bounded-last-moment cap argument. The large-deviation statement does not make that cost disappear. ## 6. Uniform multiplier rates at every node and the exact Plancherel norm The interior probability limit has an all-node algebraic counterpart. Define the continuous function \[ \ell(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi u))\,du,\qquad 0\le t\le1, \] with its integrable endpoint values, and put \[ K(\alpha,\beta)=\ell(2\alpha)+\ell(\beta) -\ell(\alpha)-\ell(\alpha+\beta), \qquad 0\le\alpha,\beta\le\tfrac12. \tag{18} \] Uniformly over ALL original integers $0\le a,s\le M$ and both parities, \[ \frac1N\log M_{N,a}(s-a) =K(a/N,s/N)+O(\log N/N). \tag{19} \] To prove it, split the log-sine sum at its midpoint, where its monotonicity changes. Comparison of each monotone part with its integral gives, uniformly for $0\le r\le N-1$, \[ \log S_r=N\ell(r/N)+O(\log N). \] The first and last intervals contribute $O(\log N)$ by integrating $\log t$ and $\log(1-t)$; away from them the monotone-sum error is bounded by the endpoint oscillation, also $O(\log N)$. Apply this to the four products in (11a). Replacing $(2a+1)/N$ and $(s+a+1)/N$ by $2a/N$ and $(s+a)/N$ changes $N\ell$ by at most $O(\log N)$, including at the endpoints. This proves (19). In the interior, $K(\alpha,\beta)=\kappa_\alpha(\beta-\alpha)$, either directly by changing the integral limits or by comparing the derivative in $\beta$ and the value at $\beta=\alpha$. Equation (19) remains valid when $\alpha$ approaches zero or $1/2$; it does not claim exponential tightness of the probability laws at those endpoints. The original period annihilates the spectator degrees below $a$. Write its surviving part as $P(c)=c^a p(c)$, where $p(c)=\sum_{r=0}^m d_rc^r$. On this quotient the exact diagonal operator is \[ (\mathcal T_{N,a}p)(c)=\sum_{r=0}^m A_r d_r c^r, \qquad A_r=M_{N,a}(r). \tag{20} \] For $1\le p\le\infty$ give coefficient vectors the weighted norm $\|d\|_{p,R}=\|(d_rR^r)_{r=0}^m\|_{\ell^p}$, with $R>0$. If $\rho=R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{in}}$, the EXACT operator norm is \[ \|\mathcal T_{N,a}\|_{p,R_{\mathrm{in}}\to p,R_{\mathrm{out}}} =\max\{1,A_m\rho^m\}. \tag{21} \] Indeed a diagonal positive multiplier has norm $\max_{0\le r\le m}A_r\rho^r$, attained on a monomial. The function $\log M_{N,a}(r)+r\log\rho$ is convex by Holder's inequality for the actual positive law, so its maximum on the interval is at an endpoint. This includes $m=0$. For $p=2$, Fourier orthogonality gives \[ \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|p(Re^{it})|^2\,dt =\sum_{r=0}^m|d_r|^2R^{2r}. \tag{22} \] Thus (21) is also the exact Plancherel operator norm on these finite Fourier polynomials. No unproved polynomial bound is needed for this step. It is a norm of the Mellin multiplier only, not yet of the full q-boundary solution or the original signed pairing. For any sequence $a/N\to\alpha\in[0,1/2]$, (19) implies \[ \frac1N\log A_m\longrightarrow\frac12\ell(2\alpha), \tag{23} \] and for fixed positive $\rho$, \[ \frac1N\log\|\mathcal T_{N,a}\| \longrightarrow \max\left\{0,\frac12\ell(2\alpha) +(\tfrac12-\alpha)\log\rho\right\}. \tag{24} \] For (23), the limiting coefficient index in (19) is $s=M$, hence $\beta=1/2$. The reflection identity $\ell(1-t)=-\ell(t)$, $\ell(1/2)=0$, and \[ \ell(2\alpha)=2\ell(\alpha) +2\int_0^\alpha\log(2\cos(\pi t))\,dt \] give $K(\alpha,1/2)=\ell(2\alpha)/2$. The same uniform estimates justify both endpoint values and both parities. At equal radii the multiplier has subexponential norm for $0\le\alpha\le1/4$ and at $\alpha=1/2$, and positive norm rate for $1/4<\alpha<1/2$. The rational denominator and the divided-difference functional in (11) still have to be estimated. Neither (21) nor (24) pays those additional costs or proves a whole-source volume bound. ## 7. What this resolves and what it does not The isolated Green/CROSS pairing is now one explicit cyclotomic rational period with a finite diagonal sine-ratio operator, and the positive representation of that operator has an explicit rate function. This retains the actual quantum jets, parent demand, odd scalar, and all confluent poles. Its derivation makes no appeal to equality with a different invariant or a generic A-polynomial. An absolute estimate on (11) is still required. Its denominator has O(N) factors and its input polynomial has degree O(N); a contour deformation, a residue expansion, or a Cauchy inequality can therefore carry exponential costs. The proved moment rate quantifies one such cost but does not bound the whole signed integrand by Phi_D. Nor does the positive law justify replacing the signed integral by its Laplace maximum. The original peripheral action is retained by the prior whole-source assembly, not newly identified by (11). The interior probability-rate proof assumes alpha stays away from zero and one half. Section 6 gives uniform algebraic multiplier rates at ALL endpoint indices; it does not assert a good probability large-deviation principle there. No general prescribed-diagram volume theorem is claimed here. ## Scope The q-boundary formula retains its integration constants, monic division, colliding strings and explicit $S_a^{-1}$ factor. Section 6 uses the exact surviving-degree normalization and both parity/endpoint limits. No numerical asymptotic scan substitutes for those estimates. The [block-contraction theorem](research_original_block_contraction_and_cap_budget.md) still governs any use of this kernel in the complete source. A mask that cuts an internal signed sum need not preserve the period. The [current critical path](research_general_long_twist_critical_path.md) records the remaining absolute comparison and the distinction between selected diagrams and arbitrary prescribed long-twist diagrams.

title: Exact sine-binomial coefficients and a positive finite-moment law for the original Green tail
text: # Exact sine-binomial coefficients and a positive finite-moment law for the original Green tail 31 October 2026. analytical research theorem. This starts from the original nodal tail T_(a,M) in the maximal-Green block transport. It provides an exact positive-moment representation of that signed kernel. It does not bound the signed pairing by an endpoint source or by Phi_D. Every moment and polynomial truncation is explicit. ## 1. Original node, tail, and normalization Let N>=3, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), M=floor(N/2)-1, and choose 0<=a<=M. Put \[ m=M-a,\qquad h=a+1,\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta), \qquad d_r=a_a-a_r=s_{r+a+1}s_{r-a}, \qquad a_r=2+2\cos((2r+1)\theta). \] The original positive nodal tail is precisely \[ T_{a,M}(x,c,y)= \sum_{r=0}^m c^{m-r}K_{a,a+r}(x,y;-a_a) \prod_{i=r+1}^m s_i s_{2a+i+1}. \tag{1} \] In particular its actual Green occurrence is T_(a,M)(x,-c,y). Nothing changes the original level, unused suffix, node a, or parent pairing [c^M]. Define, on the finite ranges used below, \[ \begin{aligned} B_a(l)&=\prod_{i=1}^l\frac{s_{a+i}}{s_i},&B_a(0)&=1,\\ A_r&=\prod_{i=1}^r\frac{s_{a+i}}{s_{2a+i+1}},&A_0&=1,\\ D_{a,m}&=\prod_{i=1}^m s_i s_{2a+i+1}. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \] All these factors are strictly positive for 0<=r,l<=2m. Indeed the largest denominator index in A_(2m) is N-1 at even N and N-2 at odd N. The largest numerator index in B_a(2m) is also strictly less than N. Empty products are one. ## 2. The exact nodal continuant coefficients Normalize the original interval continuant by \[ Q_r(x,y)= \frac{K_{a,a+r}(x,y;-a_a)}{\prod_{i=1}^r s_{a+i}^2}. \] The actual nodal recurrence is \[ \begin{gathered} Q_0=1,\qquad Q_1=x+y,\qquad Q_r=(x+y)Q_{r-1}-\gamma_rxyQ_{r-2},\\ \gamma_r=\frac{s_{r-1}s_{2a+r}}{s_{a+r}s_{a+r-1}}, \qquad r\ge2. \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] The gamma identity is the original cofactor identity, not a positivity assumption. The following explicit formula holds: \[ Q_r(x,y)=\sum_{l=0}^r \frac{B_a(l)B_a(r-l)}{B_a(r)}x^l y^{r-l}, \qquad 0\le r\le m. \tag{4} \] Proof. The endpoint coefficients are one. For an interior l, substitute B_a(n)/B_a(n-1)=s_(a+n)/s_n into the coefficient recurrence (3). After multiplication by the common denominator, the required identity is exactly \[ s_r s_{a+l}s_{a+r-l} =s_{a+r}\bigl[s_{r-l}s_{a+l}+s_l s_{a+r-l}\bigr] -s_{2a+r}s_l s_{r-l}. \tag{5} \] Expanding each sine into exponentials, or using the product-to-sum identity twice, proves (5). This proves (4) inductively from the literal original recurrence. No identification with an external orthogonality measure or quantum turn is needed. Insert (4) into (1). The scalar factors telescope: \[ \frac{\prod_{i=1}^r s_{a+i}^2}{B_a(r)} \prod_{i=r+1}^m s_i s_{2a+i+1} =D_{a,m}A_r. \] Consequently the FULL original tail is \[ \frac{T_{a,M}(x,c,y)}{D_{a,m}} =\sum_{\substack{l,k\ge0\\l+k\le m}} A_{l+k}B_a(l)B_a(k)x^l y^k c^{m-l-k}. \tag{6} \] The original negative child character is therefore retained by c->-c; it is not absorbed into an unknown normalization. ## 3. Exact unit-circle alphabet, on the required finite coefficient range Let \[ W_a(x,y)= \{xq^{a-2r}:0\le r\le a\} \uplus \{yq^{a-2r}:0\le r\le a\}. \tag{7} \] as a MULTISET, so repeated values are retained. For any finite multiset W, define H_r(W) by \[ \prod_{w\in W}(1-wt)^{-1} =\sum_{r\ge0}H_r(W)t^r. \] This is a formal rational identity, with no convergence claim. The finite sine-binomial identity is \[ \prod_{r=0}^a(1-q^{a-2r}t)^{-1} =\sum_{l\ge0}b_l t^l, \qquad b_l=B_a(l)\quad(0\le l\le2m). \tag{8} \] For clarity, the sine quotient is asserted ONLY before the denominator reaches a sine zero. The rational series defines b_l at all higher degrees; a literal sine quotient need not do so. One elementary proof of (8) is induction on a using the actual geometric progression of the variables: separating q^a gives b_l^(a)=q^a b_(l-1)^(a)+q^(-l)b_l^(a-1). The product sine expression in (2) satisfies this relation by the finite geometric-series identity. Equivalently, multiplying the rational series by its denominator verifies its coefficients up to degree 2m, where every sine division is legitimate. Thus on the required range, \[ H_r(W_a(x,y)) =\sum_{l=0}^r B_a(l)B_a(r-l)x^l y^{r-l}. \tag{9} \] The unit-circle phases in (7) are exact original-level phases. Their existence alone does not identify a positive inner product on the shared face coefficient or justify a physical turn. ## 4. A positive beta-product law with the exact moments There exists a positive random variable X_(N,a) such that \[ \mathbb E X_{N,a}^{\,r}=A_r,\qquad 0\le r\le2m. \tag{10} \] Its construction retains all original sine factors. Use h=a+1 and take mutually independent variables \[ B_0\sim\operatorname{Beta}(h,h),\qquad V_k\sim\operatorname{Beta}(kN+h,h),\qquad U_k\sim\operatorname{Beta}(kN-2h+1,h),\qquad k\ge1. \tag{11} \] All shape parameters are positive. Define the partial products \[ X_K=B_0\prod_{k=1}^K\frac{V_k}{U_k}. \] For real s in the open interval \[ -h<s<N-2h+1. \tag{12} \] the beta integral gives \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E B_0^s &=\frac{\Gamma(h+s)\Gamma(2h)} {\Gamma(h)\Gamma(2h+s)},\\ \mathbb E(V_k/U_k)^s &=\frac{\Gamma(kN+h+s)\Gamma(kN+2h)} {\Gamma(kN+h)\Gamma(kN+2h+s)}\\ &\quad\cdot \frac{\Gamma(kN-2h+1-s)\Gamma(kN-h+1)} {\Gamma(kN-2h+1)\Gamma(kN-h+1-s)}. \end{aligned} \tag{13} \] At an integer r, Euler's sine product yields \[ A_r=\frac{(h)_r}{(2h)_r} \prod_{k\ge1}\prod_{i=0}^{r-1} \frac{kN-h-i}{kN-2h-i} \frac{kN+h+i}{kN+2h+i}. \tag{14} \] Here (h)_r denotes the rising factorial. This is precisely the moment of X_K in the limit, with the two factors in (13). No square is present here; this is a different law from the [earlier protected-cap moment](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md). For completeness, convergence is not merely formal. For fixed N,a and s in a compact subinterval of (12), the logarithm of the k-th factor in (13) is O_s((kN)^(-2)); its first two derivatives in s obey the same bound. The two potential terms of order 1/(kN) cancel. Hence \[ \sum_k\left|\mathbb E\log(V_k/U_k)\right|<\infty, \qquad \sum_k\operatorname{Var}\bigl(\log(V_k/U_k)\bigr)<\infty. \] The centered log series converges in L2, and its means converge absolutely. Thus X_K converges in probability to a positive finite X_(N,a). For any integer 0<=r<=2m choose epsilon>0 with r+epsilon<N-2h+1. Formula (13) and its convergent product give sup_K E X_K^(r+epsilon)<infinity. Uniform integrability then gives E X_(N,a)^r=lim_K E X_K^r, proving (10). The same argument gives the EXACT Mellin transform for every real s in (12), not only the integers: \[ M_{N,a}(s):=\mathbb E X_{N,a}^{\,s} =\mathbb E B_0^s\prod_{k\ge1}\mathbb E(V_k/U_k)^s. \tag{14a} \] with the factors in (13). For s!=0 choose p>1 sufficiently close to 1 that ps is still in (12). The convergent gamma product at ps bounds E|(X_K)^s|^p uniformly. This proves uniform integrability also for negative s, since X_K converges in probability to a strictly positive X. The value at s=0 is one. Gamma recursion followed by Euler's sine product gives the exact successive-Mellin ratio \[ \frac{M_{N,a}(s+1)}{M_{N,a}(s)} =\frac{\sin((h+s)\theta)}{\sin((2h+s)\theta)}. \tag{14b} \] whenever both s and s+1 lie in (12). In this domain both sine arguments lie strictly between 0 and pi. This is a consequence of the explicit Mellin product (14a), not an assertion that a shift equation alone determines a measure. There is a stronger FINITE simplification because h=a+1 is an integer. Finite gamma recursion in each factor of (13), followed by Euler's sine product, gives \[ M_{N,a}(s)= \prod_{j=h}^{2h-1} \frac{\sin(j\theta)}{\sin((j+s)\theta)}. \tag{14c} \] for every real s in (12). Explicitly, the base gamma ratio becomes product_j j/(j+s), and the k-th pair becomes product_j [(kN+j)(kN-j)]/[(kN+j+s)(kN-j-s)]. These are exactly the Euler factors in (14c). For integer r the same identity is also immediate by telescoping the two length-r sine products. In particular an alternative exact realization needs only h independent variables: for h<=j<=2h-1 let Y_j have density \[ \frac{\sin(\pi j/N)}{\pi}\, \frac{y^{j/N-1}}{1+y}\,dy,\qquad y>0, \qquad X_{N,a}=\prod_{j=h}^{2h-1}Y_j^{1/N}. \tag{14d} \] Every j/N lies strictly between zero and one. The Euler beta integral proves that the density is normalized and that E Y_j^(s/N)=sin(j theta)/sin((j+s)theta) whenever -j<s<N-j. Intersecting these intervals gives exactly (12). Thus (14d) proves (14c) and all finite moments directly. It has the same law as the earlier construction, since their log-variable moment-generating functions agree on an interval about zero. Either realization may be used in the finite identities below. The available upper threshold is EXACTLY \[ N-2h+1= \begin{cases} 2m+1,&N\text{ even},\\ 2m+2,&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \tag{15} \] Thus every moment needed for the degree-m kernel, even its squared finite polynomial, is justified. No moment beyond this domain is asserted or used. ## 5. Exact signed kernel and original boundary pairing Combining (6), (9), and (10) gives the finite identity \[ T_{a,M}(x,c,y) =D_{a,m}\,\mathbb E H_m\bigl(\{c\}\uplus X_{N,a}W_a(x,y)\bigr). \tag{16} \] Here H_m is the complete homogeneous polynomial of degree m, not an untruncated rational function. The original signed tail is \[ T_{a,M}(x,-c,y) =D_{a,m}\,\mathbb E H_m\bigl(\{-c\}\uplus X_{N,a}W_a(x,y)\bigr). \tag{17} \] Let the actual CROSS spectator product retain its original shared variables and write \[ P_N(c,Y)=\sum_s p_s(Y)c^s,\qquad P_{\le M}(c,Y)=\sum_{s=0}^M p_s(Y)c^s. \] Then EXACTLY \[ [c^M]T_{a,M}(x,-c,y)P_N(c,Y) =D_{a,m}(-1)^m\,\mathbb E \sum_{r=0}^m H_r\bigl(-X_{N,a}W_a(x,y)\bigr)p_{a+r}(Y). \tag{18} \] The actual factor R_a(x,b,y;-a_a) is to be multiplied afterward, as in the original Q_(a,N). Equation (18) uses precisely the original face demand M in the reduced block, hence the original d demand before the already proved lower-block factorization. The only spectator coefficients used are a<=s<=M. Nothing here permits changing a, shifting a neighboring demand, or assigning independent radii to shared faces. Every random power in (16)-(18) is at most m. The sum is finite, so extraction and expectation may be interchanged. For a nontrivial cap component the existing independent signed path-dilation averages may be applied coefficientwise first; the same total-degree truncation remains mandatory. The formal generating representation behind (16) is useful but must remain a FINITE coefficient statement. The integral of product_(w in W)(1-Xwt)^(-1) is not automatically a holomorphic function near t=0, and may have actual poles for real t. For example if a is even, W contains x and y themselves; X has unbounded support, so positive real t can meet a denominator zero. No untruncated rational integral, missing moment, or absolute contraction is inferred from (16). ## 6. Exact limitation of copying the protected-cap tail argument Unlike the earlier cap law, this law does not have a uniformly bounded last available even moment. Put S_j=product_(r=1)^j s_r. The elementary reflection S_(N-1-r)=N/S_r gives \[ A_{2m}= \begin{cases} \dfrac{S_{2h-1}}{S_hS_{h-1}},&N\text{ even},\\[6pt] \dfrac{s_1S_{2h-1}}{S_{h+1}S_{h-1}},&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \tag{19} \] These are exact, including m=0. If h/N->alpha in (0,.5), uniform sine-product Riemann sums give \[ \begin{aligned} \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log A_{2m} &=\int_0^{2\alpha}\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt -2\int_0^\alpha\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt\\ &=2\int_0^\alpha\log(2\cos(\pi t))\,dt>0. \end{aligned} \tag{20} \] The final strict inequality is elementary: log(2cos(pi t)) decreases, crosses zero once at 1/3, and its integral from 0 to 1/2 is zero. Its partial integral is therefore strictly positive at every interior alpha. Thus the bounded-last-moment estimate used by the protected-cap [shared-star proof](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md) cannot simply be imported at a macroscopic Green node. This is an exact obstruction to that proposed proof step, not a counterexample to the signed pairing estimate. The signed expression (18), including its original source coefficients, can still be much smaller than any positive moment or norm estimate. ## Provenance and scope The original K, T, and lower-block factors are those of [the original maximal-Green block transport](research_maximal_green_component_block_transport.md) sections 4–6. Equation (3) is its original normalized nodal recurrence. The positive-product construction is derived explicitly here rather than identified with the previous cap metric. The result is an exact finite algebraic and moment identity. It supplies neither a polynomial bound for the remaining operator nor a shared capacity or filling estimate.

title: The joint one-sided score as three elementary concavity gaps
text:
# The joint one-sided score as three elementary concavity gaps 31 October 2026. Workspace research lemma, independently checked algebraically. This supplies an exact identity for the new joint score. It does not establish a global transport, a representation volume, or the universal inequality. Use the [actual closed half-block entropy](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md). For a LEFT degree vector write $\mu=q_b$, $
u=1-q_c$, $w=
u-\mu$, $\xi=q_x$, $q_y=w-\xi$. The original interval coefficient entropy is $$h=C(\alpha)-C( eta),$$ where the input/output triangle allocations share their actual outer tilt and $$ \alpha=(a,\mu,	frac12-\mu-a),\qquad  eta=(b,
u,	frac12-
u-b),\qquad a-b=\xi. $$ Here all triangle entries are nonnegative, $0\leq\xi\leq w$, and the limiting endpoint allocations are those of the original coefficient formula. The new local relative-energy bound has entropy $$g=C(\gamma),\qquad \gamma=(\xi,	frac12-w,w-\xi).$$ Let $f(s)=[\Lambda(\pi s)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi s)]/\pi$ on $[0,1/2]$ and define $$D_f(u,v)=f(u)+f(v)-f(u+v),\qquad u,v\geq0,\quad u+v\leq1/2.$$ Concavity and $f(0)=0$ imply $D_f\geq0$. The reflection identity is $f(1/2-s)=f(s)$. Direct substitution now proves $$  oxed{\displaystyle h+g=D_f(	frac12-a,\xi)+D_f(\mu,w) +D_f(\mu+a,w-\xi).} $$ Indeed, the three sums of arguments are $1/2-b$, $
u$, and $
u+b$; all lie in $[0,1/2]$. Expanding their three differences gives $$ f(a)-f(b)+f(\xi) +f(\mu)-f(
u)+f(w) +f(\mu+a)-f(
u+b)+f(w-\xi), $$ which is $C(\alpha)-C( eta)+C(\gamma)$ by reflection. Thus the joint upper score $(h+g)/2$ is a half-sum of three nonnegative concavity gaps. Each $D_f$ is also the sharp protected-outer spectral action from [the boundary theorem](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md). The elementary reassociation identity $$ D_f(u,v)+D_f(u+v,w)=D_f(v,w)+D_f(u,v+w) $$ holds whenever the arguments and total stay in the domain. More generally, any binary parenthesization of nonnegative leaves with total at most $1/2$ has total gap $\sum_i f(u_i)-f(\sum_i u_i)$. This is a telescoping identity, not a claimed move of the original knot source. A possible use is to reorganize interval pieces along the actual middle forest while retaining all face targets. That application is still missing: the identity does not itself prescribe the required reassignment of original corner loads, preserve the original marked line flags, or compare the total with the complete Casson--Rivin optimum. The prior obstruction to lossless cover atomization of a fixed projected flow remains valid. The local joint score is not concave in general. On a protected-outer row it is $D_f(\mu,w)$, with $w$ fixed and $
u=\mu+w$. Its second derivative in $\mu$ is $$ f''(\mu)-f''(
u) =- rac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi\mu)} + rac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi
u)}. $$ This is strictly positive when $0<\mu<
u<1/2$ and $\mu+
u>1/2$, for example at $(\mu,
u)=(3/10,2/5)$. Thus local concavity of $(h+g)/2$ cannot be used to infer the universal shared maximum. This is a local curvature obstruction, not a feasible global-flow excess. Its first $\mu$ derivative is always positive by strict concavity of $f$, which still records a useful direction for a possible global transport.

title: Exact leakage and the limitation of middle-only D reassociation
text: # Exact leakage and the limitation of middle-only D reassociation 31 October 2026. **Research limitation; no global score counterexample.** This preserves the actual shared incidence flow. It does not disprove the joint/min score inequality and does not claim that an uncrossed interval arrangement is an actual source flow. Orient each strict one-sided middle edge from its parent to its overloaded child. On a directed pair e1 -> v -> e2, write the corresponding LEFT coordinates after literal reflection as parent mass mu_i, child mass 1-nu_i, interval I_i=[mu_i,nu_i]. The ordinary target at v is exactly one. If ell_v is the sum of ALL other original incidences at that face, its exact balance is (1-nu_1)+mu_2+ell_v=1, nu_1=mu_2+ell_v, ell_v>=0. (1) The term ell_v includes outer corners and any remaining middle incidence; it is not licensed to vanish because the selected middle edges form a forest. Thus the middle intervals concatenate only if ell_v=0. Even an ordinary path may produce overlaps, containment, or a reversal of their starting order. No prescribed interval-tree parenthesization follows from middle incidence alone. For a proper overlap, write I1=[a,a+p+ell], I2=[a+p,a+p+ell+q], a,p,ell,q>=0, a+p+ell+q<=1/2. For D(u,v)=f(u)+f(v)-f(u+v), direct cancellation gives D(a,p+ell)+D(a+p,ell+q) -D(a,p+ell+q)-D(a+p,ell) = f(p+ell)+f(ell+q)-f(ell)-f(p+ell+q). (2) For p,q>0 the right side is strictly positive. Indeed it equals integral_0^p [f'(ell+t)-f'(ell+q+t)] dt >0, with endpoint cases understood by integrability and continuity. Therefore replacing overlapping intervals by their union and intersection preserves the coverage multiplicity but DECREASES their middle-D sum. This is the opposite of the upper-bound direction needed to dominate the original joint score. A valid proof must account for the other two D terms of every one-sided port, or for a distinct complete-triangle entropy gain. An exact original full-flow witness for nonzero leakage is retained in the [exact rational certificate](../experiments/research_joint_middle_interval_leakage_certificate.json), verified by the [portable audit](../experiments/audit_research_joint_middle_interval_leakage.py) and its [recorded results](../experiments/research_joint_middle_interval_leakage_results.json). It uses the literal17-port word [1,3,0,2,4,1,3,0,2,4,1,3,0,2,4,1,3], marks0,16. At ports5=(6,4,9,7) and10=(11,9,14,12), take quartet loads q5=(1/8,1/10,13/20,1/8), q10=(1/8,3/20,3/5,1/8). Both are actual strict LEFT loads, and the two equal outer loads select the symmetric coefficient tilt. Their middle intervals are I5=[1/10,7/20], I10=[3/20,2/5], with overlap ell=1/5. All remaining ports are retained as actual full four-incidence rows; the saved exact denominator40 allocation satisfies ALL17 ordinary targets and both protected zero targets. It is not claimed that the other ports are all CROSS. The actual source has full monomial support, so integer multiples of this flow are literal coefficient arrays at levels d divisible40 (and ordinary floor/ceil rounding also applies). For this pair the three-D identity itself remains exact. Formula(2) only rules out ignoring leakage and claiming entropy-nondecreasing middle-only uncrossing. It says nothing about whether the outer-D terms can compensate in a global face-preserving reorganization, nor whether the complete geometric capacity dominates the resulting joint score. The [outer-completion identity](research_joint_outer_completion_dual_work.md) keeps the two other D terms and gives a separate sufficient shared-flow criterion. The middle-only obstruction here does not refute that route. The verifier checks 17 literal ports, 17 ordinary and two protected targets, all 68 rational quartet coordinates, the actual symmetric coefficient endpoints and the symbolic uncrossing identity.

title: Positive outer completion and an exact shared dual-work identity
text: # Positive outer completion and an exact shared dual-work identity 31 October 2026. **Research reduction; the universal comparison is open.** The identities and sufficient criteria below retain every original face target and protected zero. They do not assert that the completed triangle array is globally feasible, or that the criteria hold for every certified diagram. ## 1. Local completion, slack, and equality Write an original LEFT degree vector as q=(xi,mu,1-nu,eta), w=nu-mu=xi+eta, 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2. Use the actual coefficient endpoint triangles alpha=(a,mu,c), beta=(b,nu,d), a-b=xi>=0, c-d=eta>=0, a+c=1/2-mu, b+d=1/2-nu. Thus h=C(alpha)-C(beta) and g=C(xi,1/2-w,eta). Set delta=1/2-nu. The letter d in beta is a corner load, not the finite degree N-1. The original f is symmetric about1/4, f(1/2-t)=f(t), strictly concave on(0,1/2), and f(0)=f(1/2)=0. For 0<=b<=a<=1/2, f(a-b)=f(1/2-a+b)<=f(1/2-a)+f(b)=f(a)+f(b). Apply this also to c,d and to the middle difference nu-mu. It gives C(gamma)<=C(alpha)+C(beta), gamma=(xi,1/2-w,eta), tilde h=(h+g)/2=C(alpha)-tau<=C(alpha), (1) with the EXACT nonnegative slack tau=1/2[D_f(1/2-a,b)+D_f(delta,mu)+D_f(1/2-c,d)]. (2) This is not the original three-D formula: it records its complementary triangle-inequality deficit. For D_f(u,v), strict concavity implies D_f(u,v)=0 iff u=0 or v=0. At a nonterminal port delta>0, equality tau=0 therefore forces mu=0 and alpha to be a pure OUTER vertex. Indeed if both a,c are positive, both are<1/2 and (2) forces b=d=0, contradicting b+d=delta>0. Conversely that pure-outer configuration has tau=0. Terminal nu=1/2 has beta=(0,1/2,0) and tau=0 for every alpha. In particular tau>0 at every nonterminal row with positive mu, or with both input outer corners positive. The zero-slack nonterminal cases are zero joint-entropy monomial degeneracies, not positive-area regular rows. Complete the local port by retaining alpha on its original input triangle (x,parent,y) and putting the original output triangle at its pure child vertex, with child load1/2. These are two genuine nonnegative half-supply triangle allocations. Their quartet load differs from q by exactly Delta_e=b e_x+d e_y-delta e_child. (3) The parent load mu does not change. This sends the overloaded child's excess to its two original OUTER faces. It does not transfer it to the parent or change the mark. Protected corners are still zero. At a protected outer face, the actual closed coefficient tilt has the corresponding alpha and beta corners zero. On a diagonal mu=nu the tilt is not determined by the coefficient; choose a limiting tilt that preserves any protected outer zero. The original certificate never has both matching outer faces protected. A protected parent has mu=0. The overloaded child is necessarily ordinary. RIGHT is the literal reflected construction. ## 2. Global identity with actual shared dual weights Let q be ANY original feasible flow with a chosen closed CROSS/LEFT/RIGHT assignment. At CROSS ports choose an entropy-maximizing split into the two original triangles. At one-sided ports use the completion in section1. Call the resulting triangle array A. Every row has supply1/2 and every protected corner is zero. Its ordinary face totals are 1+Delta_f, Delta=sum_(one-sided e)Delta_e. (4) It need not satisfy the desired target1. Nevertheless sum_triangles C(A_t)=sum_ports tilde h(q_e)+sum_e tau_e. (5) For ANY finite positive ordinary radii L, marks exactly0, set F_D(L)=sum_t Q(L_t)-sum_(ordinary f)log L_f, B(A;L)=sum_t[Q(L_t)-C(A_t)-sum_(ordinary corners f)A_tf log L_f]. Every term of B is nonnegative by the exact triangle Legendre formula. Using (4)--(5) gives the exact identity F_D(L)-sum_e tilde h(q_e) =B(A;L)+sum_e tau_e+sum_f Delta_f log L_f. (6) At the actual complete radii L*, F_D(L*)=Phi_D. Thus the universal joint comparison is precisely a compensation problem between the nonnegative B and tau terms and the possibly negative OUTER transfer work sum_f Delta_f log L_f =sum_e[b_e log(L_x/L_child)+d_e log(L_y/L_child)]. (7) Protected outer terms vanish rather than introducing log0. No face flow has been discarded or reassigned without the explicit defect(3). ## 3. A finite shared linear-program sufficient criterion This consequence needs no minimax exchange. Fix L as above and a genuine closed sector s, with nonempty one-sided port set J. For each e in J define zeta_e(L)=Q(L_x,L_child,L_y)-(1/2)log L_child>0, omega_e(L)=max(0, max_(ordinary outer f)log(L_child/L_f)). Strict positivity of zeta follows because the matching outer pair cannot be the two protected MAIN faces. The completed output row is pure-child, so its EXACT term in B is zeta_e. From beta_x+beta_y=delta_e, Delta dot log L >= -sum_e omega_e delta_e. Let P_s be the original shared-flow polytope: each port has total1, ordinary face targets1 and protected0; CROSS middles<=1/2; the selected one-sided child>=1/2. All these constraints are linear. Define kappa_s(L)=sum_(e in J)zeta_e(L) -max_(q in P_s) sum_(e in J)omega_e(L)(q_child-1/2). (8) This is an ordinary finite transportation LP with its original labels. For an empty P_s the sector is absent. Equations(6)--(8) prove max_(q in P_s)sum_e tilde h(q_e)<=F_D(L)-kappa_s(L). (9) Hence the condition kappa_s(L_s)>F_D(L_s)-Phi_D (10) for each nonempty noncross sector, allowing a different verified shared radius vector L_s for each ACTUAL sector, proves the global joint gap and therefore the full long-filling volume conclusion under the already proved source transfer theorem. All twists remain independently signed, fixed and sufficiently long. A finite radius/LP certificate is enough; attainment of a shared-radius minimizer is not assumed. Since there are finitely many sectors, strict inequalities give a common positive margin. At L* the right side of(10) is zero. With arbitrary rational positive radii one may use a rigorous upper bound for F_D(L_s) and an independent lower bound for Phi_D, together with feasible LP dual certificates. No optimizer output is itself a certificate. This criterion applies at any fixed bridge width and is a theorem about the original incidence graph. No strict enlargement of prior balanced or anchored classes is asserted without an actual certified example; (8) deliberately discards useful B and tau terms and can fail while the joint criterion remains true. ## 4. An explicit additional nonlinear slack The exact derivative f''(t)=-2pi/sin(2pi t)<=-2pi gives D_f(u,v)>=2pi uv, by integrating -f'' over the rectangle[0,u]x[0,v]. Thus(2) yields tau>=pi[(1/2-a)b+mu delta+(1/2-c)d] >=pi delta[2mu+min(xi,eta)]. (11) For the second inequality substitute a=xi+b,c=eta+d,b+d=delta. The convex expression xi b+eta d+b^2+d^2 has maximum max(xi,eta)delta+delta^2 on that segment, so the first two outer terms are at least delta(mu+min(xi,eta)). The source identities guarantee the endpoint choices satisfy the corner bounds. The displayed lower bound may vanish in the monomial directions; it is strictly positive when delta>0 and 2mu+min(xi,eta)>0. Keeping it in(8) gives a stronger explicit polynomial optimization criterion on the SAME feasible flow; no concavity of that optimization is assumed. The unresolved general issue is proving adequate compensation in(6) for all feasible original flows, potentially using the outer-transfer graph and the positive Fourier kernel of f. Neither the middle-only cocycle nor a lossless cover of the original projection supplies that compensation. No new diagram coverage is asserted without a certificate verifying the stated sufficient criterion. The local score is the one in the [joint source criterion](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md); its exact three-gap form is recorded in the [triangle decomposition](research_joint_entropy_triangle_decomposition.md). The [middle-interval leakage lemma](research_joint_middle_interval_leakage.md) explains why middle-only reassociation is insufficient.

title: Long filling from a spectral cover by original main-edge cuts
text: # Long filling from a spectral cover by original main-edge cuts 31 October 2026. , unpublished sufficient theorem. The conclusion is the original invariant's actual filled hyperbolic volume. The sufficient covering condition below is not yet proved for every eligible plat. ## 1. A full-source criterion that can change the cut Fix an eligible original simple-white plat D at arbitrary fixed width k>=2. Keep its ordered boxes, retained half twists, original peripheral markings and a fixed endpoint permutation giving a knot. Write R for its number of boxes and Phi=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi) for its drilled volume rate. The actual twists n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e are fixed before the quantum level N tends to infinity. Put d=N-1. For every original MAIN edge m with adjacent faces a_m,b_m, define the full polynomial coefficient S_(N,m)(delta)=[prod_(f!=a_m,b_m) L_f^d] prod_e H_(V_N(sigma_e))(L) |_(L_a_m=L_b_m=0), sigma_e=-2cos(2pi delta_e). All ordered local polynomials and the R original spectral variables are unchanged. The [all-MAIN marking theorem](research_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport.md) gives S_(N,m)=S_N, the original full numerator, identically as a polynomial in every spectrum. This is not an equality of projected sectors. In particular a different choice of m at a different real spectral point still bounds the same S_N. In this Fourier formulation the local source contains V_N alone; the retained half twists enter through n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e in the original Fourier functional. They are not inserted into H a second time. Let P_m be the compact original face-flow polytope for this coefficient: each port has supply one, each unmarked face has target one, and the two marked faces have target zero. For delta in the real torus T^R=(R/Z)^R put B_m(delta)=max_(q in P_m) sum_e H_(|delta_e|_T)(q_e), B_*(delta)=min_(original MAIN edges m) B_m(delta). (1) Here |delta_e|_T is its distance to the nearest integer and H is the original closed sharp local action from the [uniform coefficient upper theorem](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md). Every B_m, and hence B_*, is continuous. The flow polytopes are nonempty: the actual packing at the adjacent marked pair supplies a complete feasible flow. No new independent port radii occur in (1). Choose a fixed a>0 so the closed real cube |delta|_infinity<=2a lies inside the original full packet's strictly concave geometric chart. Suppose max_(|delta|_T,infinity>=a) B_*(delta) < Phi. (2) Then there is T(D)<infinity such that, for EVERY independently signed fixed integer vector p with min_e |p_e|>T(D), lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|K_N(K_D(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus K_D(p)). (3) Both level parities and composite levels are included. There is no slope-ratio restriction and no assertion of a threshold depending only on k. A supplied 2k-plat gives bridge number at most k; exact minimal bridge number needs its separate certificate. The order in (2) matters. It is max_delta min_m B_m(delta), not min_m max_delta B_m(delta). A single mark need not certify the whole spectral complement. A finite cover by neighborhoods with different marks is allowed, and all of them bound the same full numerator. ## 2. Uniform real bounds and a finite covering interpretation The local coefficient theorem is uniform in the entire closed degree and real spectral domain. For fixed D there are only polynomially many integer incidence arrays. Applying the triangle inequality AFTER the original face demands have been imposed gives, uniformly in delta, |S_N(delta)| <= exp{N[B_m(delta)+o(1)]}. (4) The integer supplies and targets are d; rescaling by d gives P_m. Replacing d/N by one changes the action uniformly by o(1), by its proved closed-domain continuity. Protected exponents remain exactly zero. Neither the local theorem nor this coefficient estimate uses a flat-gap forest: it uses the unchanged local polynomials and actual face incidence. There are finitely many original MAIN marks, so their errors can be replaced by one uniform o(1). Equality of the full sources then gives (4) with B_*. By compactness, (2) is equivalent to the following finite-certificate form: the closed spectral complement |delta|_T,infinity>=a has a finite cover U_j, and for each j there are a MAIN edge m_j and gamma_j>0 with sup_(delta in U_j) B_(m_j)(delta) <= Phi-gamma_j. (5) For necessity choose a minimizing mark at each point, retain a strict margin by continuity, and pass to a finite subcover. Sufficiency follows by taking the smallest margin. The sets in (5) need not partition the quantum sum or its Fourier integral. No derivatives of cutoffs or sharp window boundary currents are introduced. The [original full-source packet](general_full_spectral_numerator_geometric_packet.md) already gives a nonzero relative asymptotic on the small geometric complex chart, with the original action A_N, amplitude and primitive face measure. Its limiting real action satisfies A_0(0)=Phi and has negative definite Hessian there. After the fixed chart is shrunk, strict concavity supplies a strict real gap on each compact annulus eta<=|delta|_infinity<=a. The packet also bounds the entire small real cube by exp{N[Phi+o(1)]}. Together with (2),(4), this proves for every fixed eta>0 a gamma_eta>0 such that, at all sufficiently large N, sup_(real delta) |S_N(delta)| <= exp{N[Phi+o(1)]}, sup_(|delta|_T,infinity>=eta) |S_N(delta)| <= exp{N[Phi-gamma_eta]}. (6) Only the original full packet is used. A local packet at a newly chosen cut, or an identification of its projected geometric action, is unnecessary. ## 3. A real gap gives the needed complex strip Here is a direct polynomial argument, so (6) is not mistaken for a complex estimate. If F is a Laurent trigonometric polynomial of degree at most d in each coordinate, and b(t) is a bounded upper bound for log|F(t)| on the real torus, then log|F(x+iy)| <= 2pi d sum_j |y_j| + integral_(T^R) prod_j P_(|y_j|)(x_j-t_j) b(t) dt, (7) P_s(t)=sinh(2pi s)/(cosh(2pi s)-cos(2pi t)). At s=0 the kernel means the point mass. It has total mass one. To prove (7), write z=exp(2pi i delta_j). For y_j>=0, z^d F is a polynomial holomorphic in the unit disk. The subharmonic inequality for its log modulus bounds it by the Poisson integral of its boundary log modulus; removing z^d costs exactly 2pi d y_j. For y_j<0 use z^(-1) instead. Apply this one coordinate at a time, using the already bounded real boundary data in the next coordinate. Zeros cause no problem: use the subharmonic regularization log(|P|+epsilon) and let epsilon decrease. This also proves the bound for an identically zero slice. Apply (7) to S_N. Its separate polynomial degree in sigma is at most d, so its Laurent degree in each exp(2pi i delta_j) is at most d. In (6) use the real gap at eta/2 and the global upper bound Phi+epsilon. If |x|_T,infinity>=eta, choose j with |x_j|_T>=eta. The Poisson mass of |t_j|_T<eta/2 is at most C_eta |y_j| for |y_j|<=1: its circular distance from x_j is at least eta/2, and the displayed kernel is bounded there by C_eta |y_j|. Consequently, for |y_j|<=tau, N^(-1)log|S_N(x+iy)| <= Phi+epsilon-gamma_(eta/2) +gamma_(eta/2) C_eta tau+2pi R tau. (8) First make epsilon small, then choose a sufficiently small fixed tau. This gives a strict upper rate below Phi on the desired complex strip. Fixed spectral derivatives have the same strict gap on a smaller strip by Cauchy; use the real gap at eta/2 before shrinking so the derivative circles stay in the covered region. Equation (8) is uniform in N. It does not differentiate any spectral cover or change a mark at a complex point. ## 4. Apply the whole-period argument to the full source The proof of the [entire all-CROSS period theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) uses precisely its two stated inputs: the relative packet H1 near zero and the whole spectral strip gap H2 away from zero. All subsequent estimates concern that entire polynomial and the original Fourier functional. They also require separate evenness and period one, the cosine polynomial degree bound, and the specified sine/Gaussian factors. The full source S_N has all these properties. Its H1 is the old full packet, including the raw sign (-1)^(dR), the original powers of N and the same finite action A_N and determinant H_N. Its H2 is (8). Apply that proof with S_N in place of its raw all-CROSS coefficient. Endpoint values still vanish after the sine factor is included, first endpoint derivatives match, and the second derivative endpoint currents are retained in the three integrations by parts. The infinite charge tail is handled on whole intervals; only the same finite charge set is localized. Thus no new spectral-cycle assumption or missing charge estimate is required.
