The nonzero leading term is the old unit-charge packet, with the same finite saddle, branch choices and all original framing/peripheral factors. Its limiting critical value is the actual filled volume by the [original marked action theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md). In particular the right side of (3) is the FILLED knot's volume, not Vol(Y_D). Enlarge the existing geometric and analytic long-filling thresholds until their O_D(sum_e n_e^(-2)) loss is smaller than the fixed complementary gaps. This choice works for all independently signed fixed twists with sufficiently large minimum magnitude. This proves (3). ## 5. A finite algebraic certificate at any original MAIN cut There is also a directly checkable sufficient condition which does not require solving (1). Choose ANY original MAIN edge m. Send its actual packing contact to infinity; its two faces become the marked parallel lines, and all other face curvatures L_f remain positive. This changes the geometric normalization, not the ordered boxes or their peripheral markings. The adjacent-mark construction in the [absolute packing-capacity theorem](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) gives the same complete rate Phi. For each original ordered quartet (x,b,c,y) in this normalization, put A=x+y. Suppose (A+b)(A+c) >= max(b^2,c^2) at EVERY port. (9) Then the full original long-filling conclusion (3) holds. More generally, one may replace (9) by a finite cover of the actual non-CROSS sector strings with shared positive radius witnesses, as in the [finite-sector criterion](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md), with these SAME two protected faces and all original face targets. Here is the dependency check that extends those sufficient tests beyond top marks. Their local CROSS/LEFT/RIGHT weighted estimates concern only the unchanged ordered polynomials, including their protected-zero specializations. The face coefficient is now exactly the same S_N by the all-MAIN theorem. At the chosen complete packing, the endpoint cost minus its ordinary targets is Phi by adjacent-mark capacity invariance. The [triangle entropy inequality](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) turns (9) into strict local balance whenever a one-sided sector survives. Protected overloaded middles give exactly zero sectors. Thus the proof of the [balance criterion](general_complete_radius_balance_filling_volume.md), or the finite-sector argument using its separate shared witnesses, gives a uniform real gap for S_N-C_(N,m), where C_(N,m) is the newly marked raw all-CROSS coefficient. The [global CROSS spectral-gap proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) also applies to this coefficient: a MAIN pair cannot be the two protected outer faces of a MATCHING port, each port has a nonmonomial triangle, and the ordinary white graph remains connected. The last fact follows from the simple triangulated sphere's connectivity after deleting two vertices. These are precisely the zero-pattern and connectivity inputs of its local estimates and common-phase sewing. Its weighted endpoint exponent is again Phi. Consequently C_(N,m) has a real gap away from zero, and hence so does S_N. The product-Poisson argument supplies a complex strip if only real bounds have been used. Now use the OLD full-source local packet and the full-period proof in section 4. No projected-sector transport, new-cut regulator identity, or rerouted flat-gap forest is required. This proves the claimed any-MAIN version of the finite certificates. It does not assert that (9) holds at some cut of every simple-white plat, or that changing the cut strictly enlarges the underlying knot classes. ## 6. Scope of the remaining problem The finite mark freedom removes the need to insist on one unfavorable protected pair throughout an upper-bound argument. It does not assert that (2), or any simpler balance certificate, always succeeds. A uniform proof of that covering inequality for general eligible plats would finish the stated long-twist conjecture through this theorem. If its unsigned upper functional is too large, a cancellation-sensitive bound for the same full source is still an alternative. The exact local spectral maximization [sum f(inputs)-f(sum inputs)](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md) can simplify conservative bounds on (1). One must keep the maxima over the shared P_m and the order of the spectral/mark choices explicit. Neither a minimum of separately optimized port bounds nor transport of individual LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT contributions follows from the theorem. The original half twists occur exactly once in the Fourier exponents. The covering inequality remains a hypothesis; its universal validity is open.

title: A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source
text:
# A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source 31 October 2026. This is a finite topology/source extension, not a volume asymptotic and not a claim that a new presentation has a prescribed flat-plat width. ## 1. Input, conclusion, and the local ordering Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite connected triangular cellulation of the oriented sphere, with a perfect matching \(D\) of its cubic dual \(\Delta\). Assume every paired pair of triangles has a four-sided disk as its union, with four distinct white vertices. Equivalently, begin with a connected spherical quadrangulation \(\mathcal Q\), choose one embedded diagonal in each quadrilateral, and triangulate along those diagonals. Parallel edges produced by a choice of diagonals are not silently identified. They are allowed as cellulation data here. A positive geometric certificate, when needed, is a separate hypothesis. There are \(2R\) triangles, \(R\) matched pairs, and \(R+2\) white vertices. For each quadrilateral choose the oriented cyclic order \((x,b,y,c)\), with chosen diagonal \(xy\). The two triangles are \((x,b,y)\) and \((x,c,y)\). The local box frame is input middle \(b\), output middle \(c\), left outer \(x\), right outer \(y\). Reversing this frame later would require its actual duality adapter; no such unrecorded reversal is part of the construction. The construction below gives a genuine augmented link in \(S^3\), with \(R\) labeled twice-punctured crossing disks, whose original cut graph is \((\Delta,D)\). It has a general Morse diagram containing exactly these \(R\) recorded two-strand boxes and no other crossing. In the fixed frames, any full original coupons \(f_e(\Omega)R^{\epsilon_e}\) have exactly the homogeneous source \[ P(L)=\prod_{e=1}^R H_{f_eR^{\epsilon_e}} (L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e}). 	ag{1} \] For any MAIN edge between faces \(a,b\), the original raw one-mark contraction is exactly \[ I_N=[\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^{N-1}]\,P ig|_{L_a=L_b=0}. 	ag{2} \] It is independent of the selected MAIN edge. The formula uses the original turns, reduced mark, all full crossing scalars, and complete root Hermite data. No level factor is suppressed. ## 2. Inverting the actual crossing-disk cut Embed the cubic dual \(\Delta\) on the sphere. Choose disjoint small regular-neighborhood disks around the matched edges and their endpoint vertices. Because \(D\) is a perfect matching, these disks are disjoint and meet the other edges in four boundary terminals each. Contracting each disk gives a connected plane four-valent graph \(G\), with \(R\) vertices and \(2R\) edges. At one disk label the four terminals cyclically \(0,1,2,3\) so that the two original matched vertices group terminals \((1,2)\) and \((3,0)\). These are the two shaded half-disk sectors. Draw the **physical untwisted main strands** with the other planar pairing \[ (0,1),\qquad(2,3). 	ag{3} \] These arcs are disjoint. Join the terminals outside the disks along the original nonmatching dual edges. The result is a finite union of embedded circles in the projection sphere. Each circle meets a box, because every piece came from the finite four-terminal construction. One must not identify these circles with the abstract cycles of \(\Delta\setminus D\): the latter uses the shaded grouping \((1,2),(3,0)\), whereas the physical strands use (3). In a disjoint three-ball neighborhood of each disk put the standard perpendicular crossing circle and its twice-punctured spanning disk, meeting exactly the two strands in (3). All its labels and its collar orientation are inherited from the chosen local box frame. This is an explicit link embedded in \(S^3\); no abstract three-manifold realization theorem is needed. Cut it along the projection sphere and open each original upper and lower half disk. The two shaded triangles at the box have the original labels \[ S_0=(O,C_1,C_2),\qquad S_1=(O,C_3,C_0). \] The untwisted within-copy gluing fixes \(O\) and sends \(C_1\mapsto C_0\), \(C_2\mapsto C_3\). Thus the cut is literally the inverse of sections 1–4 of [original matching-graph cut](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Its medial boundary graph is the medial graph of the supplied \(\Delta\), with every original white face and matching edge retained. The proof there that opening the disjoint half disks gives two balls is local and does not use a plat sweep; it therefore applies to this construction. Insert a recorded half twist \(\epsilon_e\in\{0,1,-1\}\) in a box when desired. Its original shaded maps are precisely the cross-copy maps in that same cut theorem. Both nonzero signs have the same terminal permutation but retain their different disk-framed peripheral paths. The external graph and the local polynomial frame are unchanged. ## 3. A knot parity pattern exists, without a bridge-width assertion Start with the untwisted physical circles of section 2. Form a finite graph whose vertices are these circles and whose edge at a box joins the two circles passing through that box (a loop is allowed). This graph is connected: otherwise the union of boxes and outside arcs, and therefore the connected four-valent graph \(G\), would split. Choose a spanning tree. Give its boxes odd parity and all other boxes even parity. Switching a tree box from (3) to the odd pairing \((0,2),(1,3)\) joins two distinct current circles into one. Process the tree edges in any order: after any subset, its connected tree components are exactly the merged circles, so the next edge still joins two different circles. Thus the final main link has one component. Each odd sign may independently be chosen \(+1\) or \(-1\). Filling box \(e\) with any integer power \(n_e\) of that parity preserves this one-component property. The original convention is \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\), where \(p_e\) is the integer full-twist filling coordinate in the recorded local disk framing. Arbitrarily large independent positive or negative powers of the chosen parity are available. This says nothing about minimal bridge number or a specified original flat width. ## 4. Producing the original finite Morse tensor network Choose a point outside the disks as infinity. In each disk use its given orientation-preserving parametrization to draw two vertical strands, with terminals \(1,2\) at the input and \(0,3\) at the output. The local quadrilateral is then exactly \((x,b,y,c)\) in section 1. The finitely many disjoint disks can be placed in such plane charts independently; this fixes, rather than transports or resets, their ordered four-leg frames. More explicitly, straighten each chosen disk parametrization in its own disjoint collar, and extend those collar changes to an orientation-preserving plane isotopy. The remaining outside arcs are then drawn between the resulting boundary endpoints. Thus the local vertical charts belong to one global plane drawing; no ribbon normal twist or permutation of a coupon's legs is introduced. Smooth the outside arcs and perturb their height functions away from the disks. There are finitely many ordinary nondegenerate maxima and minima, all at distinct heights after another small perturbation. No new crossing or ribbon twist is required. This is a general Morse diagram, with arbitrary cups/caps between recorded box heights. It need not be a plat with all cups below and all caps above the boxes. Evaluate it using exactly the original complete module \(V_d\), its regular self-duality \(J\), all four original turns, the original checked crossings and Casimir coupons, and one exposed original reduced cap. Upward/downward arcs carry the corresponding actual module or dual; their physical frames are related by \(J\), not by an independently reset diagonal insertion. Since the complete object is self-dual, these are the same original finite matrices in the ordered balanced head frames. This is the usual original ribbon tangle evaluation on the explicitly constructed diagram. There is no new normalization ambiguity. For fixed \(N\), the regular generic lift uses \(\widetilde g=(-1)^HK\), with \(J^{-t}J=\widetilde g\), which specializes literally to \(g=K^{1-N}\). Its two traces agree on every endomorphism in the tensor-generated integral-weight category. The full proof, including duals and regular root specialization, is in sections 2–3 of [all-MAIN mark and general Morse compiler](research_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport.md); it is independent of a flat layout. Its snakes prove invariance under the Morse interchanges just used. Its spherical trace exchange exposes any selected MAIN edge as a top cap while keeping every coupon disk fixed. The cut network is a regular generic intertwiner on \(V_d\) or its dual. Its \(K\) weights are distinct and its internal \(F\) arrows nonzero, so it is scalar. Its ordinary closure is \((-1)^d[N]_q\) times that scalar. Equality of closed spherical readings, followed by regular specialization, proves independence of the reduced marked scalar from the MAIN edge. No root quantum dimension is divided by zero. This argument works on any component because all the complete colors agree. ## 5. General Morse winding and the full original coefficient Here the all-MAIN compiler is repeated on the new diagram itself; there is no assumed old flat diagram whose coefficient is being transported. Choose the marked edge's adjacent face \(a\) as exterior and expose a top cap, with \(b\) its inside face. A connected four-valent graph has no bridge (the parity of degrees in either component would contradict one crossing edge), so these two faces are distinct. The finger move preserves their labels. Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). In literal left-to-right head order \((i,j)\), both original left/right cups and both caps are \[ p_{ij}=Nq^{-d^2+di}\,1_{i+j=d},\qquad \ell_{ij}=N^{-1}q^{di}\,1_{i+j=d}. 	ag{4} \] The exposed original mark, after the whole-source conservation forces its two remaining heads to sum to \(d\), is \(m_{ij}=N^{-2}q^{dj}\). This is a consequence of the full source, not an early restriction of the unrestricted marked matrix. Its contraction with its original cup is exactly one. At every fixed coupon the original adapter is \[ N^{-1}H_e(x,b,c,y)/(bc)^{d/2}. 	ag{5} \] Let \(M_f\) count middle incidences at boxes and \(T_f\) count outside turns minus inside turns in face \(f\), temporarily including the ordinary cap that will be marked. Round each fixed local box in its actual frame. Each middle passage contributes \(+\pi\) to the boundary turning index and the two outer passages have net zero; inside turns contribute \(+\pi\) and outside turns \(-\pi\). The bounded face winding is \(+1\) and exterior winding \(-1\), counting repeated boundary occurrences. Therefore \[ M_f-T_f=2\ (f
e a),\qquad M_a-T_a=-2. 	ag{6} \] This is the face-boundary proof in section 6 of the all-MAIN theorem, which uses only the local boxes and Morse arcs, not their vertical ordering or a flat gap forest. All ordinary turns and (5) thus give \(L_a^d\prod_{f
e a}L_f^{-d}\). The exact mark/cap ratio is \(N^{-1}(L_b/L_a)^d\). If there are \(k'\) cups, there are \(k'\) caps; their complete powers of \(N\) give \(N^{k'}N^{-(k'-1)}N^{-2}=N^{-1}\). Their recorded \(q\)-constants cancel, just as in (4). The whole marked summand is consequently \[ N^{-R-1} rac{P(L)}{\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^d}. 	ag{7} \] The integral conserved-head lattice is the original cycle lattice of the connected spherical graph. Bending edges does not change it. Integration across dual paths identifies it primitively with face potentials modulo their common constant. There are \(R+2\) faces, thus \(R+1\) independent grids after \(L_a=1\). For odd \(N\) use \(L_f=Q^{p_f}\). For even \(N\), the cochain which is one on MAIN edges and zero on matching edges is closed: each triangle has two MAIN edges. Since the sphere is simply connected it integrates to \(t_f\in\mathbb F_2\), with \(t_a=0,t_b=1\); use \(L_f=q^{t_f}Q^{p_f}\). The local full-polynomial adapter first imposes the canonical physical head support, killing all wrong unwrapped totals. Supported states and primitive grids then correspond exactly. Only coherent integrated face-log lifts are varied; no arbitrary individual head reset is used. The \(N^{R+1}\) grid count cancels (7). Nonnegative exponents of total degree \(dR\) leave only the alias \(n_a=n_b=0\), \(n_f=d\) otherwise: those \(R\) ordinary minimum degrees already exhaust the total. The even coset character is one there. This proves exactly (2), with no additional factor of \(N\). ## 6. Original signed filling powers and their whole spectral functional Replace the \(e\)-th box by its actual \(R^{n_e}\), where the signed integer \(n_e
e0\) is fixed before \(N\). The exact local identity \[ R^{n_e}=q^{n_ed^2/4} \exp\!\left( rac{n_e K(\Omega)}{2\hbar}ight), \quad \hbar=2\pi i/N,\quad K(z)=\operatorname{arccosh}(-z/2)^2, 	ag{8} \] retains all Hermite derivatives and every crossing scalar. It is the fixed-root identity of [exact original signed crossing powers](actual_direct_long_power_source.md). The explicit Gaussian/resolvent numerator functional is also recorded in [exact Gaussian/resolvent functional](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md). Different boxes do not need to commute; their ordered tensor contraction is multilinear in the local matrices. Define the full spectral numerator using the newly constructed original source, \[ S_N( oldsymbol\sigma) =[\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^d] \left.\prod_e H_{V_N(\sigma_e)}ight|_{L_a=L_b=0}. 	ag{9} \] Applying the original matrix Fourier/Hermite functional separately at each box gives exactly \[  egin{split} I_{N,\mathbf n}={}&q^{ rac{d^2}{4}\sum_e n_e}(-i)^R \sum_{ oldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\ell_e\Bigr)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_e\ell_e}\ &\ 	imes\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_e)\Bigr) S_N(-2\cos(2\pi oldsymbol\delta))\ &\ 	imes\exp\!\left\{N\sum_e [\pi i n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\ell_e\delta_e]ight\} d oldsymbol\delta . \end{split}	ag{10} \] This is the same local source-independent finite functional as in section 1 of [original whole spectral period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). Its charge-zero absence and whole-domain absolute summability hold before any geometric estimate. The proof uses the local matrix identity, the entire finite-degree numerator, and its original sine endpoint factors; it does not use a plat sweep. All side currents in a subsequent contour deformation would still have to be retained. The raw scalar in (10) is the actual original reduced ribbon contraction of the filled link constructed above. Its conversion to the specified zero-framed enhanced Kashaev convention is the original recorded framing/component character. At complete color its modulus is one; for a knot the enhanced component sign is one. If instead using the full one-cut modified convention, retain its additional \(i^{N+3}/N\). These exact distinctions are proved in [complete source normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), using local crossing/duality identities and scalar cut maps; they do not depend on the bridge count. No extra quantum dimension, semicircle normalization, or exponential basis factor has appeared here. For the complete augmented link, the original local crossing-circle contraction is still its exact \(L_N\) coupon, with its one ordinary auxiliary trace and no extra modified dimension. Thus (1)–(2) apply to that source too. A geometric certificate identifies its two cut balls with the original right-angled polyhedron and gives the actual augmented exterior, as in section 2; a volume asymptotic requires its own verified analytic hypotheses. ## 7. Scope needed by a diagonal-choice argument This theorem constructs an actual source for **each** diagonal choice on the fixed quadrangulation. The constructed links for different choices need not be isotopic, their marked coefficient polytopes need not coincide, and no projected sector or physical operator is moved from one choice to another. The common quadrangulation supplies a common finite combinatorial indexing only. Every original target, half-index coset, retained half-twist and disk-framed signed filling coordinate has now been supplied for that choice. Consequently a proposed complete-capacity-maximizing choice can refer to a genuine original source rather than a formal entropy model. This does not by itself prove its global source estimate, local filling packet, nonzero period, hyperbolicity, or volume limit. Those hypotheses must be checked on the chosen diagram. In particular no old flat-plat gap forest or prescribed bridge width has been transported merely by constructing a general Morse source. ## scope All finite matrix ingredients are the original duality, homogeneous source, all-MAIN compiler, and local full-Hermite filling functional. No new numerical audit is asserted for this constructive proof. No global spectral comparison, filling asymptotic, prescribed plat width, or equality between sources from different diagonal choices is claimed.

title: A maximal diagonalization has a strict full-source entropy gap
text: # A maximal diagonalization has a strict full-source entropy gap 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. This is an exact local and global entropy transport on the original face targets. Sections 4--5 prove a structural selection theorem: every finite connected SIMPLE spherical quadrangulation with four distinct vertices on each of its R>=2 faces has a simple complete-capacity-maximizing diagonalization, and every maximizing diagonalization has a uniform sharp non-CROSS gap. No claim is made that an arbitrarily prescribed diagonalization is maximizing. Different choices need not give the same original link. ## 1. Literal local transport Use the original four cyclic faces (x,b,y,c) and its matching diagonal xy. A LEFT degree row is q=(q_x,q_b,q_c,q_y)=(a,b,c,d), nu=a+b+d=1-c<=1/2. Here a,b,c,d denote normalized degrees only. The original sharp spectral maximum is G(q)=f(a)+f(b)+f(d)-f(nu), where f(0)=f(1/2)=0, f'(t)=log cot(pi t), and f(1/2-t)=f(t). In particular f>=0 on [0,1/2]. Replace only the matching diagonal xy by bc, keeping the quadrilateral boundary and its ordered face labels. Its two new triangles are (b,x,c),(b,y,c); the new port has outer faces b,c and middle faces x,y. The SAME degrees lie in its closed CROSS domain because a,d<=1/2. The following explicit CROSS triangle rows preserve every face degree: alpha_(b,x,c)=(0,a,1/2-a), beta_(b,y,c)=(b,d,1/2-b-d). (1) All entries are nonnegative because nu<=1/2. Their sums are each 1/2, and their combined b,x,c,y loads are exactly b,a,c,d. No face degree is moved to another label. Their entropy is C(alpha)+C(beta) =2f(a)+f(b)+f(d)+f(b+d) =G(q)+f(a)+f(b+d)+f(nu). (2) Thus the genuine complete/CROSS entropy h_flip of the flipped port satisfies h_flip(q)>=G(q)+f(nu). (3) For 0<nu<1/2 the displayed gain is strictly positive. The alternative allocation assigning all original b-load to the first triangle gives the further valid gain f(d)+f(a+b)+f(nu). At nu=0 and nu=1/2, use the closed formulas directly; no strictness is asserted merely from (3). RIGHT is identical after exchanging its overloaded middle and the other middle. Protected zeros are retained in (1), not approximated. ## 2. Simultaneous flips and original targets In a diagonalized spherical quadrangulation every shaded triangle belongs to exactly one recorded port: the matching pairs its two triangles. Hence the interiors of the quadrilaterals for distinct ports are disjoint. Assume all quadrilateral faces have four distinct vertices, and flip any collection I of ports simultaneously. Every original MAIN edge and all four boundary incidences of each port are unchanged. The two protected vertices remain distinct and joined by the same MAIN edge. The new matching edge bc lies inside the old port disk. The resulting object is a spherical triangular cellulation. It can have parallel edges if bc was already an edge, and two resulting triangles can have the same label set. These are distinct cell incidences. No loop is introduced because the original port has four distinct white vertices. No actual flat-plat realization of the changed matching graph is asserted or needed for the following classical capacity bound. Take a feasible original shared flow q. Let I contain every port where q has a genuinely overloaded middle; assign either side at a closed seam consistently if desired. On each unflipped CROSS port, choose its entropy-maximizing original triangle split. On each flipped port, use (1), or its RIGHT version. This produces a feasible COMPLETE triangle flow on the changed cellulation, with the SAME unit ordinary targets, the SAME protected zeros, and the SAME total supply. Therefore sum_e barH(q_e)+sum_(e in I) f(1-q_(e,child)) <= Phi_complete(D_I; original marks). (4) One may retain the larger explicit gains in (2). The right side is the actual normalized complete angle capacity of the changed cellulation, not the original Phi_D. At seams, use their actual closed CROSS/Green agreement; no finite path label is reassigned in a quantum polynomial. The simple-block construction applies to this classical capacity, including parallel-edge splitting: if feasible, it is the sum of the new simple-block polyhedron volumes divided by pi, with zero from double-triangle blocks. The explicit transported flow already proves feasibility. Thus (4) is a geometric upper bound with fully preserved demands, not independent optimization at separate ports. ## 3. The missing comparison for a prescribed chart remains geometric Equation (4) is valid for every finite quadrangulation in the stated class and every fixed original MAIN mark. It does NOT prove sum barH<=Phi_D. The flipped cellulation has new matching edges, and its complete block-volume sum has not been compared with the original complete volume. The actual old circle packing does not supply tangency along a newly inserted bc edge. Nor is this an equality of original quantum sources, or a licensed change of the original knot/crossing-circle topology. Any claim that the changed block volume is bounded by Phi_D, or by Phi_D plus the explicit local gains in (2), requires an additional proof. The new point is the exact load-preserving, nonnegative entropy comparison; neither a minimum/maximum exchange nor a sign-cocycle assumption occurs. ## 4. Every nonsimple diagonalization lies strictly below the maximum Fix ANY finite connected SIMPLE spherical quadrangulation Q, with R>=2 faces and four distinct boundary vertices in each face. Its vertices will be white faces and its quadrilateral disks will be ports. Choose independently one diagonal in each of its R faces. This gives 2^R labeled triangular cellulations T. Choose any original MAIN edge uv as mark; it is retained in all of them. The MAIN graph is bipartite: assign alternating parities around each quadrilateral, which integrate globally because all facial cycles have even length. A diagonal joins equal parities; a MAIN edge joins opposite parities. Thus a repeated edge in any T consists entirely of diagonals. There are no loops and no repeated MAIN edge. There exists a simple diagonalization by a purely combinatorial argument, before any entropy is considered. If two selected diagonals are parallel, choose their embedded digon and either side. A boundary diagonal bc belongs to a quadrilateral whose adjacent third vertices x,y are strictly on opposite sides of the digon. Replacing bc by xy introduces no repeated edge: an old xy edge would cross the digon. It removes one repetition of bc. Thus the finite integer sum of max(0,edge multiplicity-1) strictly decreases. Iterate to obtain a simple triangulated sphere on the same vertices. This uses no angle feasibility or chosen radius. All faces still come from the original four-distinct-vertex quadrilaterals. Let Phi(T;u,v) denote each chart's complete angle capacity, allowing -infinity if its fiber is empty. Every nonempty fiber is compact and has a maximizer. The simple chart just constructed has finite positive capacity by the simple-sphere packing/angle theorem. Therefore the largest capacity among the finitely many charts is finite and attained. Suppose T has two parallel matching edges joining b,c. They form an embedded digon. Since the fixed marked vertices u,v are joined by a MAIN edge, one side of this digon has no marked vertex strictly inside. Choose that side. If it has v interior vertices, it contains 2v triangles. Their total supply v equals the total ordinary demand of those interior vertices, so every b- and c-corner on that side has load zero in EVERY feasible complete flow. Take one boundary matching edge e. Its inside triangle is (b,x,c) and its outside triangle is (b,y,c), where x is strictly inside the digon and y strictly outside. Both differ from b,c, and x!=y, as the quad has four distinct vertices. In any maximizing complete flow the inside triangle is pure x, with load 1/2. Consequently the local combined degree has q_x=1/2 and the local entropy is exactly the entropy of its outside triangle: this is the seam value G with child x. Flip e to xy and use the transport of section 1 at nu=1/2. It preserves all global demands and does not decrease entropy. Hence the capacity of the new chart is at least that of T. Strict increase is not needed. The edge xy did not already occur: an existing embedded edge from x strictly inside to y strictly outside would cross the digon boundary, whose only vertices are b,c. Thus this flip removes one occurrence of a repeated bc edge and introduces no repeated xy edge. The nonnegative integer sum over unordered vertex pairs of max(0,edge multiplicity-1) decreases by one. Iterating terminates at a SIMPLE chart, without decreasing capacity. In fact the LAST flip in this process increases capacity strictly. Write the maximizing outside triangle loads, in the order (b,y,c), as (a,t,d), where a+t+d=1/2. Its inside triangle is pure x. The explicit new rows in the final simple chart are (x,b,y)=(1/2-a,a,0), (x,c,y)=(a,d,t). (5) Their entropy minus the old two-triangle entropy is exactly 2f(a). If 0<a<1/2 this is positive. If a=0 or a=1/2, one of the two new triangles has a zero corner at x. The vertex x is ordinary: it lay strictly inside the mark-free digon. In a SIMPLE marked sphere the unique complete entropy maximizer is strictly positive at every allowed ordinary corner, apart from its already fixed singleton rows, where that ordinary load is 1/2, never zero. Thus the transported flow in (5) is not a maximizer of the final simple chart. Its capacity is strictly larger even in this endpoint case. Consequently every feasible nonsimple chart has capacity strictly smaller than some simple chart. An infeasible chart is harmless. EVERY global capacity-maximizing chart is therefore simple. This argument does not assert that each intermediate digon flip has a strict gain; strictness at the final simple chart is sufficient. In particular the maximum equals the maximum over simple charts. Their capacities are the actual labeled polyhedron volumes divided by pi and are independent of the adjacent marked pair, by the packing construction. It follows that the maximum over all diagonalizations is itself independent of which original main edge is marked. ## 5. A sharp global inequality for every maximizing diagonalization Choose a complete-capacity-maximizing diagonalization D of Q. Section 4 proves that D is simple. Define its sharp piecewise local barH and its original unit-target fiber exactly as in the exact-G note. Then max_(q in original closed NC fiber) sum_e barH(q_e)<Phi_D. (6) Here is a proof retaining every boundary case. If q has a genuinely overloaded port with 0<nu=1-q_child<1/2, flip all its overloaded ports. Equation (4) and flip maximality give sum_e barH(q_e)<=Phi_D-sum_(overloaded e)f(nu_e)<Phi_D. Otherwise all genuinely overloaded rows are pure-child vertices (nu=0), and every other row is in the closed CROSS domain. If at least one pure-child row occurs, flip precisely those ports. The transported complete triangle flow has entropy equal to the original sum barH. If the new chart is nonsimple, section 4 bounds its capacity strictly below Phi_D. If it is simple, at a flipped pure-child port BOTH new triangles are pure at the child. The child is ordinary; at least one of the other three distinct vertices is ordinary as well, since only two vertices are protected. Its corner load in the transported flow is zero. Thus this flow is not the strictly positive ordinary-corner complete maximizer of that simple chart, and its entropy is strictly below that chart's capacity, which is at most Phi_D. Finally suppose there is no genuinely overloaded row. Then every row is CROSS, and the original closed NC condition means some middle load equals 1/2. The simple chart's complete entropy optimizer has no such middle: a protected middle is zero, and an ordinary middle shares its triangle with at least one positive ordinary outer corner. Both outers cannot be the protected pair, since their edge is MATCHING while the protected edge is MAIN. Thus every ordinary middle is strictly below 1/2. Uniqueness of the complete triangle optimizer gives a strict loss for this seam datum as well. If the original closed NC fiber is empty, its gap assertion is vacuous. Otherwise that fiber is compact and barH is continuous, so the pointwise strict inequality has a uniform positive gap. This proves (6) using ONLY the complete angle-capacity geometry of simple spheres and the local exact G. No full-kernel endpoint forest theorem, physical pure-middle deletion or flat-gap assumption is used in this argument. For an ACTUAL eligible original flat-plat source D whose white chart is such a maximizing diagonalization, the conditional theorem in the exact-G note now gives the full original independently signed long-filling volume limit, for all fixed sufficiently long twist vectors, both level parities and the original normalization. No new spectral-cycle argument is needed for that stated source class. The geometric hypothesis can equivalently be checked using the actual block volumes of the finitely many parallel-edge charts. The existence theorem in section 4 proves that every eligible MAIN quadrangulation has an ABSTRACT simple maximizing diagonalization and the sharp gap (6). It does NOT prove that an arbitrarily prescribed source is maximizing, or that the new maximizing diagonalization has a literal flat-plat realization with the same fixed bridge width and independent original twist boxes. That source realization is a separate issue. No change of the original knot or equality between different diagonalized quantum sources is asserted. ## Dependencies The local inputs are the [exact sharp Green spectral maximum](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md), sections 1--5, and the [absolutely normalized triangle entropy](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md). The global classical inputs are the [complete angle-capacity and simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), sections 1--5: compact duality, strict positivity and uniqueness of the simple-sphere optimizer, and absolute polyhedron-volume normalization. That construction also proves independence of a simple chart's capacity from its adjacent marked pair. The stated corollary for an already eligible original flat source uses section 7 of the exact-G note and its original whole-period dependencies. The conclusion selects a maximizing diagonalization in a finite family. It does not assert that every prescribed diagonalization is maximizing, that different choices define the same link, or that an abstract choice has a prescribed flat-plat width. A separate actual-source construction and its analytic/geometric adapters are required to draw a knot-volume conclusion for the newly selected general diagram.

title: Exact cap-tree and lower-block transport at a maximal Green child
text: # Exact cap-tree and lower-block transport at a maximal Green child 31 October 2026. analytical research theorem. This preserves the original face targets and every finite LEFT/cap cutoff. It gives an exact mixed-block reduction, not an absolute bound by Phi_D. No numerical test or publication claim is used. ## 1. The actual maximal-child component Use the classified common-weight datum. Choose a strict LEFT Green port E with maximal child weight among all Green ports, and call its child c. RIGHT is handled by the literal row reflection. Let S be the connected component of actual residual cap edges containing c. The response/network theorem proves that S is a tree, c has cap indegree zero, every other vertex has cap indegree one, and every other noncap port incident to S is CROSS. The chosen Green has no input in S, since all its supported input weights are strictly smaller than its child weight. Orient every cap from parent to its overloaded child. These orientations are therefore precisely the rooted-tree orientation away from c. Let P_N((z_v)_(v in S),Y) be the product of ALL the other noncap coupons incident to S, retaining their genuine CROSS projections. They may share arbitrarily many face variables. At endpoint -2, after fixed raw signs, its coefficients are nonnegative. The finite identities below also hold for arbitrary spectra in these CROSS coupons: positivity is not used in their derivation. The unchanged outside source has no incidence to S. Put N>=3, d=N-1, M=floor(N/2)-1. Each residual cap is held at its actual stationary spectrum +2 and has exact polynomial F_v(z_v,z_parent)=sum_(j=0)^M (-1)^j U_j z_v^(d-j)z_parent^j, v!=c, (1) in the original cap conventions, or their literal reflections. Here U_j=csc^2(pi/(2N)) product_(r=1)^j sin^2(pi r/N)/sin^2(pi(r+1/2)/N). No regularized reference replaces this raw cap. Write the raw chosen Green LEFT polynomial, removing only its fixed sign (-1)^d, as P_(E,LEFT)(c,Y;sigma)=sum_(s=0)^M c^(d-s)G_s(Y;sigma). (2) Its genuine strict-child support is s<=M at BOTH parities. ## 2. Original target extraction solves every cap index Expand the CROSS product in its original component-face variables: P_N(z,Y)=sum_(k in Z_+^S) p_k(Y) product_v z_v^(k_v). For v!=c let S_v be its descendant subtree, including v, and put K_v(k)=sum_(w in S_v) k_w, |k|=sum_(w in S) k_w. Extract the original demand z_v^d at EVERY vertex of S. At a nonroot vertex the exponent equality is exactly (d-j_v)+sum_(w child of v) j_w+k_v=d. At the root it is (d-s)+sum_(w child of c)j_w+k_c=d. Starting from the leaves therefore gives, with no relaxed constraint, j_v=K_v(k), s=|k|. (3) Because k_w>=0 and s<=M, EVERY cap restriction j_v<=M is automatic. Conversely every k>=0 with |k|<=M gives exactly one set of all cap indices satisfying the original face targets. Thus, up to the one retained fixed Green/CROSS raw sign, the exact component contraction is B_N(Y;sigma) =sum_(|k|<=M) G_|k|(Y;sigma) p_k(Y) product_(v!=c) [(-1)^K_v(k) U_K_v(k)]. (4) All exterior face degrees remain explicit in G_s and p_k. This is not a new source on a quotient graph: (3) is the solution of the original unit demands, before any analytic estimate. The same count explains the classical quotient. At a stationary flow, each cap split is the total CROSS supply in its descendant subtree, and the total CROSS supply in S is 1-q_(E,c)<1/2. In (3) the exact integer version is s<=M, not a freely chosen residual demand. ## 3. A genuine positive-moment transport, with the total truncation first The proved cap moment law gives independent positive variables X_v, one per cap edge, with E X_v^j=U_j/U_0, 0<=j<=d. Define the signed path dilation T_c=1, T_w=product_(edges v on path c to w) (-X_v). Then product_w T_w^(k_w) =product_(v!=c)(-X_v)^K_v(k). Let P_(N,s)(z,Y) denote the part of P_N of TOTAL S-degree s. Equation (4) is equivalent to the exact finite formula B_N(Y;sigma) =U_0^(|S|-1) E sum_(s=0)^M G_s(Y;sigma) P_(N,s)(T,Y). (5) Equivalently, with one formal root variable z, B_N=U_0^(|S|-1) E [z^d] P_(E,LEFT)(z,Y;sigma) (Pi_(total S degree<=M) P_N)((zT_v)_v,Y). (6) The TOTAL-degree truncation in (6) is essential. For every monomial retained by it, the exponent of each independent X_v is K_v(k)<=M, so all absolute moments in (5)-(6) are finite. Coefficient extraction and expectation may be interchanged on this finite truncated space. One must NOT put the untruncated full P_N inside the expectation before extracting the coefficient. Its degree in a descendant subtree may exceed d; the cap law has no such general finite moment. This is the same exact finite-moment restriction as in the shared-star theorem, now applied to a real cap tree. The formula retains nontrivial quantum information beyond the classical component-sum quotient. Already the monomials z_c^s and z_v^s for a leaf v have the SAME total component degree but receive relative factors 1 and (-1)^(s distance(c,v)) product_(edges on path) U_s/U_0. Therefore replacing all component faces by one equal variable is not the actual finite cap elimination. This is a statement about the exact boundary polynomial operator, not a counterexample to a source estimate on a particular diagram. ## 4. Exact Green lower-block factorization, both parities The remaining single Green operation in (5) has a concrete finite spectral reduction. Set theta=pi/N, m=floor(N/2), M=m-1, and a_r=2+2cos((2r+1)theta), s_r=2sin(r theta), u=-(sigma+2), alpha_r(u)=a_r+u, A_-(u)=product_(r=0)^M alpha_r(u). Let R_j(x,b,y;u) be the original lower cleared cofactor: R_0=1, R_j=b^j product_(r<j)alpha_r +s_j^2(x+y)R_(j-1) +s_j s_(j-1)alpha_(j-1)xy R_(j-2), (7) where absent negative indices and the last term at j=1 are zero. It is homogeneous of FACE degree j. The original prefix/active/suffix path expansion gives exactly G_j(Y;sigma)=R_j(x,b,y;u) product_(r=j+1)^d alpha_r(u). (8) No unused row or initial-state sum has been omitted. Reflection alpha_(d-r)=alpha_r shows product_(r=j+1)^d alpha_r(u) =zeta_N(u) product_(r=j+1)^M alpha_r(u), j<=M, zeta_N(u)=A_-(u) if N=2m, u A_-(u) if N=2m+1. (9) Define the actual lower-block numerator L_M(x,b,c,y;u) =sum_(j=0)^M c^(M-j)R_j(x,b,y;u) product_(r=j+1)^M alpha_r(u). It has FACE degree M and SPECTRAL degree at most M. The exact original Green source is therefore P_(E,LEFT)(c,Y;sigma) =zeta_N(u)c^(d-M)L_M(x,b,c,y;u). (10) The raw source has the fixed sign (-1)^d restored afterward. The odd factor u is the UNUSED central row, not a cancelled zero. This is the original level-N lower block, not a quantum source at a different level. ## 5. A positive nodal tail, with the child character retained The m lower nodes u_a=-a_a, 0<=a<=M, are distinct. At u=u_a, all terms of L_M with j<a vanish because their retained suffix contains alpha_a=0. For j>=a, the exact cofactor identity is R_j(u_a)=K_(a,j)(u_a) R_a(u_a). Here K_(a,a)=1, and K is the original interval continuant. The coefficientwise nodal theorem proves R_a(x,b,y;u_a)>=0, K_(a,j)(x,y;u_a)>=0, j<=M. (11) For clarity, positivity of K is nontrivial: normalized by product s_r^2 it obeys q_r=(x+y)q_(r-1)-gamma_r xy q_(r-2), with 0<=gamma_r<=1. Induction on q_r-xq_(r-1) proves positivity and q_r<=(x+y)^r. No termwise positivity of the signed dimer weights has been assumed. For r>a one has a_a-a_r>0. Put T_(a,M)(x,c,y) =sum_(j=a)^M c^(M-j) K_(a,j)(x,y;u_a) product_(r=j+1)^M (a_a-a_r). (12) This is a nonnegative-coefficient polynomial of FACE degree M-a. The entire nodal source factors EXACTLY as L_M(x,b,c,y;u_a) =R_a(x,b,y;u_a) T_(a,M)(x,-c,y). (13) The sign on c in (13) is exactly the sign of the unused lower suffix: there are M-j negative alpha_r factors. It cannot be deleted. The first factor is the actual complete-node input cofactor R_a=S_(2a)D_a(x,b,y), where S_k=product_(r=1)^k s_r and D_a is the original complete-circle determinant. This exact normalization is the source adapter in [original complete-node cofactor adapter](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) section 1, equations (3)-(4). The second factor is the explicit positive tail (12); no covariance or different-level quantum interpretation of it is asserted. At the two extremes, B_M=product_(r=1)^M s_r^2, T_(M,M)=1, T_(0,M)=B_M s_(M+1) sum_(j=0)^M h_j(x,y)c^(M-j)/s_(j+1), h_j(x,y)=sum_(r=0)^j x^r y^(j-r). (14) Indeed at a=0 the normalized interval continuant is h_j, and a_0-a_r=s_(r+1)s_r makes the suffix product telescope. These formulas are exact finite source identities, not estimates. ## 6. Polynomial-cost interpolation reduces the remaining spectral variable Let ell_a(u) be the cardinal polynomials on the LOWER m nodes u_a. Since deg_u L_M<=M, (13) gives the exact identity L_M(u)=sum_(a=0)^M ell_a(u) R_a(x,b,y;u_a) T_(a,M)(x,-c,y). (15) At even levels the nodes are the shifted Chebyshev roots, with Lebesgue norm O(log N) on [-4,0]. At odd levels use the full physical Radau family including the central u=0 node. For any scalar polynomial p of degree <=M, interpolate u p(u), of degree <=m, on that full grid. Its value at zero is zero. The full-grid O(log N) bound and division by the ONE known endpoint factor cost at most a fixed polynomial in N: for instance |p(u)|<=sup|(u p(u))'| and the elementary degree-m derivative bound C m^3 sup|u p(u)| give sup_[-4,0]|p| <=C N^3 log(N+1) max_(0<=a<=M)|p(u_a)|. (16) This proof works for complex scalar values. It does not infer an angular nodal theorem at an unavailable index. A polynomial cost is all that is claimed. The original prefactor in (9) has a uniform REAL-spectral bound. With sigma=2cos phi, the exact Chebyshev products give |zeta_N(u)|<=2 (N even), |zeta_N(u)|=|4cos(phi/2)cos(N phi/2)|<=4 (N odd). (17) The limiting endpoint values are polynomial continuations; no zero is divided. In particular the odd unused central factor is included. For the ISOLATED component S={c}, put Q_(a,N)(Y)=R_a(x,b,y;u_a) [c^M] T_(a,M)(x,-c,y) P_N(c,Y). The original isolated Green-star coefficient is exactly B_N(Y;sigma)=zeta_N(u) sum_(a=0)^M ell_a(u) Q_(a,N)(Y), (18) and (16)-(17) yield, for all real sigma in [-2,2], |B_N(Y;sigma)|<=poly(N) max_a |Q_(a,N)(Y)|. (19) The unchanged outside face coefficient can be taken after this identity; it is linear and all original targets remain. One may also apply the scalar cosine-Bernstein bound to B_N as a degree-d polynomial in sigma to extend (19) to a fold strip with the explicit factor exp(2pi d |Im delta|). For a nontrivial cap component, replace the s-th root coefficient of P_N in (18) by the exact averaged coefficient from (5). Equivalently, apply (18) to the finite polynomial sum_(s=0)^M E P_(N,s)(T,Y)c^s and retain the outside factor U_0^(|S|-1). This is legitimate finite linear algebra by the moment cutoff check in section 3. ## 7. What is resolved, and the exact remaining signed pairing Equations (3)-(6) are a finite quantum counterpart of the actual cap quotient, retaining every descendant demand and its character. Equations (10)-(19) reduce the continuous Green spectrum at polynomial cost to explicit finite child-character pairings against the actual CROSS spectator product. No arbitrary matrix, new face target or coefficientwise comparison of an alternating sum has been introduced. The lower block has distinct nodes, but this does NOT discard the original Casimir Jordan data. The original LEFT numerator vanishes at physical nodes because of zeta_N. Its quotient values L_M(u_a) retain precisely the information lost by that vanishing factor. They are not substituted for full-numerator values at those nodes. What remains is a bound on the signed quantities Q_(a,N), or their exact cap-tree moment averages, relative to an endpoint/volume quantity on the SAME original fiber. The factors in (13) have nonnegative coefficients before c is changed to -c, but taking their absolute coefficients would remove the cancellation being sought. Their positive capacity need not equal the original Phi_D. The a=M term has no tail and lies at the retained half boundary; the smaller a terms retain the genuine signed tail. Thus (19) is a concrete finite spectral reduction, NOT an absolute Phi_D estimate, an instability theorem, or a proof of the prescribed long-twist volume statement. No globally feasible maximum or counterexample is manufactured by these identities. ## Exact input provenance and scope Inputs: [actual response network and maximal-child component](research_sharp_source_response_forest_main_network.md) section 5 for the maximal-child component; [original cap positive moment form](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) sections 1-3 for the all-level finite moments; the [original homogeneous face source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) and [actual cleared cofactors and nodal interpolation](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) sections 1-2 for (7)-(10), and section 8 equations (22)-(26) for nodal positivity and interpolation. Original cap/cutoff conventions agree with [original cap and cutoff conventions](research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.md). The exact transport retains finite moment cutoffs and original subtree demands; no asymptotic lower bound follows.

title: Mixed whole-CROSS and regular-window phase losses
status: Whole CROSS and supported windows in one cycle bound
text: # Mixed whole-CROSS and regular-window phase losses The cycle-packing conclusion is conditional on the stated hypotheses. A product formula for the complete capacity is not assumed. ## 1. The whole-CROSS polynomial, with both parities retained Put \(d=N-1\), \(\theta=\pi/N\), \(u=-4\sin^2(\pi\delta)\), and \[ a_r=4\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta),\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\qquad A=x+y,\quad P=xy. \] All variables are the original four face variables of a port. Fix their zero pattern, require \(A>0\), and let the positive entries range in a fixed positive compact set. A zero variable stays exactly zero. In particular this includes protected middle and protected outer patterns allowed by the original marked source. It excludes two zero outer faces. Write \[ P_N^\times(x,b,c,y;u)=(-1)^dH_{V_N,\mathrm{CROSS}}(x,b,c,y;u). \tag{1} \] The sign in (1) is part of the actual numerator convention; it has modulus one and is restored when taking products of raw coupons. The [exact factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md), at the same level \(N\), uses \[ \begin{aligned} R_0(b;u)&=1,\\ R_j(b;u)&=b^j\prod_{r<j}(a_r+u) +s_j^2 A R_{j-1}(b;u) +s_js_{j-1}(a_{j-1}+u)P R_{j-2}(b;u). \end{aligned}\tag{2} \] The last summand is omitted at \(j=1\). For even \(N=2m\), set \(D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u)\) and \(E_b=(a_{m-1}+u)R_{m-2}(b;u)\). Then \[ P_N^\times=s_m^2 A D_bD_c +s_ms_{m-1}P(D_bE_c+E_bD_c). \tag{3} \] For odd \(N=2m+1\), put \(G_b=R_m(b;u)\) and keep \(D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u)\). The formula is \[ P_N^\times=G_bG_c+u s_ms_{m+1}P D_bD_c. \tag{4} \] The second term of (4) is the original path which skips the central row; its unused factor \(u\) remains. These are polynomial identities, also when a diagonal or central factor vanishes. Every central summand contains one cofactor from each of the \(b\)- and \(c\)-sides. No decomposition into separately optimized face variables is made. Define the positive endpoint value \[ B_N(L)=P_N^\times(L;0)>0. \tag{5} \] The zero-spectral recurrence has nonnegative coefficients. Positivity in (5) follows from the first summand of (3), or from \(G_b(0)G_c(0)\) in (4), since \(A>0\). ## 2. A finite majorant and the whole-port angular loss The cofactor interpolation theorem gives, coefficient by coefficient, \[ |R_j(u)|_{\mathrm{coef}} \le C\log(N+1)R_j(0),\qquad -4\le u\le0, \quad 0\le j\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor. \tag{6} \] Together with the exact central comparisons in that theorem, it implies \[ |P_N^\times(L e^{i\vartheta};u)| \le M_N^\times(L):=C_0\log^2(N+1)B_N(L) \tag{7} \] for every face phase and every real \(\delta\). The constant can be chosen uniformly over the fixed radius compact and all sufficiently large levels of both parities. Protected zero variables need no assigned phase. Here are the central comparisons explicitly. At even levels, \[ D_b(0)\ge s_{m-1}^2 A R_{m-2}(b;0),\qquad P\le A^2/4. \tag{8} \] Thus \(P D_b(0)R_{m-2}(c;0)\), and its reflection, are bounded by a uniform multiple of \(A D_b(0)D_c(0)\), already a positive summand of \(B_N\). At odd levels, \[ G_b(0)\ge s_m^2 A D_b(0),\qquad P D_b(0)D_c(0)\le\frac{1}{4s_m^4}G_b(0)G_c(0). \tag{9} \] The factors \(s_m,s_{m-1},s_{m+1}\) used here are bounded away from zero at large \(N\). The remaining factors \(|u|\) and \(|a_{m-1}+u|\) in (3)–(4) are bounded on the real spectral interval. This proves (7) without discarding the odd skipped-central term or dividing by a possibly zero diagonal. For the supported incidences define the distance to common phase by \[ d_\times(\vartheta) =\min_{\varphi\in\mathbb T} \max_{f\in\operatorname{supp}(x,b,c,y)} |\vartheta_f-\varphi|_{\mathbb T}. \tag{10} \] Incidences are retained separately if two arguments happen to be the same original face. For every fixed \(\eta>0\), there are \(c>0\), \(C_1\ge1\), and \(N_0\) such that \[ |P_N^\times(L e^{i\vartheta};u)| \le C_1e^{-cN}M_N^\times(L) \quad\text{whenever }d_\times(\vartheta)\ge\eta, \tag{11} \] uniformly for all real \(\delta\) and \(N\ge N_0\). To prove this, choose any positive outer incidence \(p\), which exists because \(A>0\). Taking \(\varphi=\vartheta_p\) in (10) shows that some supported incidence has circular distance at least \(\eta\) from \(p\). If it is \(b\), the supported phases of \((x,b,y)\) are separated; if it is \(c\), those of \((x,c,y)\) are separated. If it is the other outer incidence, both sides are separated. The selected side therefore has at least two positive entries. The [actual cofactor angular theorem](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) gives \[ |R_j(\text{phased side};u)| \le C N^K e^{-\gamma N}R_j(\text{positive side};0) \tag{12} \] for each terminal cofactor on that side. Indeed all terminal indices in (3)–(4) equal \(J\) or \(J-1\), with \(J=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). Apply (6) to the other side and (8)–(9) to each of the finitely many central summands. This bounds the left side of (11) by \(CN^{K'}e^{-\gamma N}B_N(L)\); absorb the polynomial into, for example, \(e^{-\gamma N/2}\). A cofactor with one positive face is a monomial, but cannot be the selected mismatched side. It consequently causes no exception to this argument. If the whole port has only one supported phase, the condition in (11) is empty. Thus a whole CROSS port has alignment label zero at every supported incidence. This is a whole-port conclusion from the exact central factorization, not an assumption that the two cofactor phases can be chosen independently. ## 3. Endpoint normalization and its rate Let \(Q(x,b,y)\) denote the original absolute complete triangle potential at \(\delta=0\), with homogeneity degree \(1/2\). Then, on the fixed radius compact and fixed zero pattern, \[ \log B_N(L)=N\{Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y)\}+O(\log N). \tag{13} \] In particular the exact majorant in (7) has a polynomial upper bound \[ M_N^\times(L)\le C N^K \exp\!\left[N\{Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y)\}\right]. \tag{14} \] This polynomial normalization is not needed for (11), but identifies its source-rate interface without an unspecified exponential scalar. For completeness, (13) follows from the existing endpoint cofactor packets with a quantitative product estimate. For \(b>0\), including exactly one zero outer weight, the [interior-start packet](actual_cross_cofactor_interior_packet.md) has its starting saddle in a fixed compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). The finite prefix diagonal is bounded away from zero before that saddle, and the positive tail root is bounded away from zero from there to the terminal row. Their logarithms have uniform bounded derivatives on these intervals. The finite-row shift is bounded, and the finite tail root differs from its limiting root by \(O(N^{-1})\). Elementary Euler–Maclaurin estimates therefore give \(N\phi_N(t_N)=NQ(x,b,y)+O(1)\). The packet amplitude is a bounded unit times \(\sqrt N\); hence \(\log R_{J-k}(b;0)=NQ(x,b,y)+O(\log N)\), for fixed \(k\). For \(b=0\) and \(xy>0\), the [protected-middle packet](actual_cross_cofactor_protected_packet.md) is a bounded nonzero amplitude times \(\prod_{j=1}^n s_j\lambda_{j,+}\). The positive \(\lambda_{j,+}\) is uniformly bounded away from zero even at the lower endpoint and differs from a smooth limiting root by \(O(N^{-1})\). Its logarithmic sum has bounded Riemann error. The remaining sine product has only the endpoint logarithm: comparison with \(\log t\) gives Riemann error \(O(\log N)\). The [absolute marked-action identity](actual_cross_cofactor_marked_action.md) identifies the resulting integral with the same \(Q(0;x,y)\). Finally, if \(b=0\) and exactly one outer weight is positive, (2) is the literal monomial \[ R_n(0;0)=(x+y)^n\prod_{j=1}^n s_j^2, \qquad Q(x,0,y)=\tfrac12\log(x+y). \tag{15} \] The half-sine product again contributes only \(O(\log N)\). These cases exhaust the allowed support patterns on either cofactor side. Apply their estimates to (3) at \(u=0\), using (8) for the upper comparison and its positive first term for the lower comparison. At odd levels (4) at zero is exactly \(G_b(0)G_c(0)\). This proves (13). ## 4. Mixed cycles on the one original face torus Take a fixed original source and one radius \(L_f>0\) per ordinary face. Protected face variables are specialized to zero before coefficient extraction. Select a set \(J\) of ports consisting of either: - whole CROSS coupons satisfying the hypotheses above, with majorant \(\mathcal E_{e,N}=M_{e,N}^\times\) and zero incidence labels; - literal regular moving windows satisfying the [four-positive theorem](research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.md) or the [one-protected-outer theorem](research_protected_outer_window_phase_exclusion.md), with \(\mathcal E_{e,N}=E_{e,N}\) and their actual endpoint-sign labels. - fixed-start \(b=0\) or reflected fixed-stop \(c=0\) windows satisfying the [protected-middle theorem](research_protected_middle_window_phase_exclusion.md), again with their literal positive envelopes and only their three supported incidences. Their hypotheses require both outer weights and the other middle weight positive. Each selected port now has the two bounds \[ |P_{e,N}|\le\mathcal E_{e,N},\qquad |P_{e,N}|\le C_e e^{-c_eN}\mathcal E_{e,N} \quad\text{if }d_e\ge\eta, \tag{16} \] where \(d_e\) is distance to its supported alignment. For CROSS this is (10); for a window subtract its prescribed \(0/\pi\) incidence labels before minimizing over a common phase. All constants are obtained at the same fixed threshold \(\eta\). Use the original supported incidence multigraph, retaining repeated incidences. For a nonempty finite collection \(\mathcal C\) of odd-label cycles, put \(\eta=\pi/(4r_{\max})\) and let \[ \kappa_{\mathcal C}= \max\left\{\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C: \lambda_C\ge0,\quad \sum_{C\ni e}\lambda_C\le c_e\ \text{for every }e\in J\right\}. \tag{17} \] The [fractional cycle-packing proof](research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md) uses only (16), so applies unchanged. CROSS vertices can carry paths between moving-window vertices, including across a protected middle whose zero incidence is absent. A cycle containing only CROSS vertices has even label and supplies no such obstruction. At unselected ports let \(M_{e,N}\) be any certified phase-uniform majorants for their actual polynomials. For the unchanged original target exponents \(t_f(N)\), Cauchy extraction on the one shared torus gives \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \left|\left[\prod_f z_f^{t_f(N)}\right] \prod_e P_{e,N}(z)\right| \le C e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal C}N} \frac{\prod_{e\in J}\mathcal E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e\notin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\prod_f L_f^{t_f(N)}}.} \tag{18} \] Raw numerator signs, any external source character and all additional source prefactors retain their actual moduli. There is no new power of \(N\), a changed face target, or an independent radius per incidence in (18). ## 5. Scope of the rate criterion The whole-CROSS contribution to the logarithmic majorant in (18) is exactly \(Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y)\) by (13). The moving-window contribution is its own original positive envelope. They are not identified with each other. If the normalized logarithmic limsup of the entire positive quotient in (18) is \(B_L\), its actual shared coefficient has upper rate \(B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}\). Thus \[ B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}<\Phi_D, \tag{19} \] is a conditional strict source-rate certificate whenever the original complete rate \(\Phi_D\) is known. No uniform margin in (19), no exhaustive window cover, and no universal bound by \(\Phi_D\) have been proved here. A family of polynomially many pieces still needs the uniform finite-level errors and constants specified in the cycle-packing criterion. Compatible phase systems, uncovered irregular windows, and the remaining source sectors require their own estimates. The statement here is for real spectral variables; a complex-strip version must also budget the unconditional Bernstein growth of all noncontracting factors. The finite central identities and cofactor angular theorem used above have their own original-source audits. This note composes their proved estimates analytically; it makes no claim to a new physical-matrix or asymptotic numerical audit.

title: A complete geometric double of a one-cap stationary exterior
text: # A complete geometric double of a one-cap stationary exterior 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. This concerns ONE residual cap and complete CROSS rows at every other original port. The original MAIN mark, face targets and matching are retained until the explicitly defined doubling construction. No equality of the old and doubled quantum sources or links, and no universal absolute cap-volume comparison, is asserted. ## 1. The actual disk and its double Let T be the original simple matched triangulated sphere, with protected MAIN edge uv and cap \[ F=(u,A,v,C),\qquad (u,A,C),\ (u,v,C),\qquad \text{matching edge }uC. \] Suppose first that a strict cap-only stationary datum exists: its cap loads are (q_A,q_C)=(1-nu,nu), 0<nu<1/2, all ordinary incidences are positive, the remaining ports are CROSS, and their common finite weights satisfy L_A=L_C. The result in [the cap-cut theorem](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md), section 1, then proves that the opposite edge Av is absent. Delete the two triangles of F and their shared edge uC. The remaining triangulated closed disk D has boundary, in cyclic order, \[ u,A,C,v.\tag{1} \] It has NEITHER boundary diagonal: Av was absent and uC has been removed. All four boundary edges are MAIN. Therefore every remaining original triangle pair lies wholly in D. Removing F has not cut any other port. Take two labeled copies D_1,D_2, and identify their boundaries by \[ u_1=v_2,\quad A_1=C_2,\quad C_1=A_2,\quad v_1=u_2.\tag{2} \] This reverses the boundary cyclic order, so the result T^dbl is a triangulated sphere. It is SIMPLE. Indeed each copy embeds injectively; an edge from one copy could duplicate an edge from the other only if both endpoints were boundary vertices. In the disk all such edges are the four boundary edges, because both diagonals are absent. Those four edges are precisely the edges identified in the gluing. There is also no triangle with all three vertices on the boundary: such a triangle would contain a boundary diagonal. Thus the gluing creates neither a duplicate triangle nor any repeated nonboundary edge. The inherited triangle pairing is an actual matching: every port lies in one copy and its four vertices remain distinct. The four glued edges remain MAIN. In particular T^dbl has a simple MAIN quadrangulation and admits the complete packing/angle-capacity theorem, with mark uv. If T has R ports, T^dbl has 2(R-1) ports. This is a new matched sphere, not a re-presentation of the old filled knot. The same construction is defined without a stationary assumption for ANY disk of this form with neither boundary diagonal. The stationary assumption above is one exact original-source reason that Av is absent. ## 2. Exact capacity and the genuine complete optimizer Let R(s) be the original residual capacity, as in [the original constrained-capacity theorem](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md), section 1: interior ordinary targets are one, the boundary targets are A:s, C:1-s and u:v:0. No targets are changed in this definition. At the stationary datum the remaining CROSS allocations attain their triangle Legendre optima at the original finite weights. Duplicate these allocations into D_1 and D_2 using (2), and duplicate the weights. They agree at the glued vertices because L_A=L_C and L_u=L_v=0. Every interior demand is still one. At each of A,C the two boundary contributions add to nu+(1-nu)=1. The protected demands stay zero. Thus the duplicated flow is feasible for the COMPLETE problem on the simple sphere T^dbl and attains its global Legendre upper bound. Consequently \[ \Phi(T^{\mathrm{dbl}})=2R(\nu)=2M_{\mathrm{cap}}.\tag{3} \] Here the last equality is the exact stationary dual-attainment theorem for the original one-cap residual problem; it is not an asymptotic coefficient or a source-limit assertion. The complete optimizer on the double is positive at every ordinary incidence and unique. Its actual circle packing therefore develops each copy of D injectively. This supplies an embedded exterior in this construction; it is not an assumption about an arbitrary signed Green development. There is also a converse characterization of the relaxed residual maximum. The double has an involution exchanging its two copies and interchanging u with v and A with C. Uniqueness of the complete optimizer and of its positive weights up to common scale makes the optimizer invariant under this involution. The two A/C weights are equal. To see that no scale is hidden, normalize the marked line separation; the involution preserves that normalization, or apply it twice to the positive proportionality factor to obtain factor one. Restrict this complete optimizer to D_1. All its interior targets are one. The boundary loads have the form s_*,1-s_*: the other copy exchanges them and the doubled targets are one. The common equality L_A=L_C means that its dual affine upper bound is independent of s. Hence \[ R(s_*)=\max_{0\le s\le1}R(s)=\frac{\Phi(T^{\mathrm{dbl}})}2.\tag{4} \] Strict concavity in the actual triangle loads makes this residual maximizer unique. For example, if two distinct residual load vectors attained the same maximum, their midpoint would give a strict gain in at least one nonconstant triangle row. The usual protected monomial rows are fixed and cause no exception. Thus a strict original cap-only stationary point, when it exists, is precisely this single residual optimizer with s_*<1/2. If s_*>1/2, concavity instead places the maximum over the original cap interval [0,1/2] at its endpoint; s_*=1/2 is the terminal case, not a strict cap. Here 1/2 is indeed feasible. Completing D by either missing diagonal gives a simple matched sphere with the same mark. The original uC completion supplies a strictly feasible residual load s>1/2, while the Av completion supplies one with s<1/2. Their convex combination supplies s=1/2. These two completions are different sources, not an asserted isotopy or a coefficient transport. ## 3. A new geometric restriction on the original cap split In the genuine packing of T^dbl, normalize the marked u,v circles as parallel lines, and let their positive separation be H. The finite circles A,C have a common radius r, are tangent to each other, and respectively touch u and v. They do NOT touch the other line, because Av and uC are absent from the simple contact graph. Every ordinary disk lies in the strip between u and v. Thus \[ H>2r.\tag{5} \] This strict statement is justified by the complete simple-sphere packing, not merely by the formal four boundary contacts. For clarity, the fan-angle calculation is orientation-independent at the required cosine level. Put the A center at 0, the C center at 2re, where e is a unit vector. Let n be the unit normal from A toward its line u. The boundary fan of D_1 at A has central angle theta=2pi s_*; its two endpoint rays are n and e. Hence n dot e=cos(theta), irrespective of which oriented arc realizes this fan. The two line equations are \[ u:\ n\cdot z=r,\qquad v:\ n\cdot z=2r\cos\theta-r. \] Their separation is therefore \[ H=2r\bigl(1-\cos(2\pi s_*)\bigr)=4r\sin^2(\pi s_*).\tag{6} \] Combining (5) and (6), with the ordinary fan loads between zero and one, gives the genuine residual-disk restriction \[ \frac14<s_*<\frac34.\tag{7} \] In particular EVERY strict one-cap-only stationary datum in the original setting satisfies \[ \frac14<\nu<\frac12.\tag{8} \] The nonstationary four-port example with local A-star mean nu=1/4 in the earlier cap-budget note is therefore not a counterexample: it did not satisfy the common stationary demands of the entire exterior. Neither (7) nor this proof covers a disk with another cap left inside; the rows duplicated here are all complete CROSS rows. ## 4. The remaining absolute inequality is now geometric, but unproved Let C0=2f(1/4) and retain the original prescribed chart D_orig. At a strict stationary one-cap datum, the earlier exact constrained dual is \[ M_{\mathrm{cap}}=\Phi(D_{\mathrm{orig}})+\Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}-C_0. \] Together with (3) this yields \[ \Delta_{\mathrm{cap}}\le C_0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi(T^{\mathrm{dbl}})\le2\Phi(D_{\mathrm{orig}}).\tag{9} \] Thus the missing unsigned cap comparison is a specific complete-volume comparison between an original capped disk and its twisted double. The construction proves both sides are genuine complete packing capacities. It does NOT prove the inequality in (9). The graphs and actual matched sources differ; there is no source equality, filling identification, or admissible right-angled contraction implicit in the gluing. The exact residual formulas remain \[ \begin{aligned} M_{\mathrm{cap}}&=\max_{0\le s\le1/2}R(s),\\ \Phi(D_{\mathrm{orig}})&=\max_{1/2\le s\le1} \bigl[R(s)+2f(s-\tfrac12)\bigr]. \end{aligned}\tag{10} \] The new geometry restricts the unique unrestricted maximizer of R to (1/4,3/4). A concavity statement and this location alone do not bound how much R can decrease between s_* and 1/2; a quantitative boundary deformation or a genuine capped-disk/double volume comparison is still required. No abstract concave function is asserted to be realizable by an actual positive triangulated disk. If the geometric comparison in (9) is certified for a particular one-cap configuration, the [signed spectral-star theorem](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md) supplies the further strict loss below Phi(D_orig). More strongly, Phi(T^dbl)<2Phi(D_orig) already gives an unsigned cap-sector gap. These are scoped consequences for that sector, not the full non-CROSS remainder or a general prescribed-diagram filling theorem. ## Scope and dependencies The only external mathematical inputs used here are the already original cap cut, compact complete triangle duality, and the simple matched-sphere packing/capacity theorem in this project. Relevant durable sources are: * [cap-star cuts](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md), section 1; * [original cap capacity](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md), sections 1-2; * [simple-sphere complete capacity and packing](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), sections 1-5; * [matched-sphere source realization](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md), for the distinction between the newly constructed matched sphere and the old source. The statement is limited to one cap with all remaining original ports CROSS. The doubled matched sphere is not identified with the original source, and no universal volume comparison is claimed.

title: The one-cap exterior has an original group representation, with a positive pyramid deficit
text:
# The one-cap exterior has an original group representation, with a positive pyramid deficit 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. Hypotheses are the strict ONE-cap stationary configuration of the geometric-double theorem: the original simple matched sphere has protected MAIN edge uv, F=(u,A,v,C), all other original ports CROSS, all ordinary incidences positive and finite common weights. The cap split is 1/4<nu<1/2. This constructs a representation of the original UNTWISTED drilled group using the positive exterior packing. It is NOT the failed direct specialization of the signed sigma=+2 source chart. The latter's [raw central/noncentral obstruction](research_double_protected_cap_finite_collar_obstruction.md) is unchanged. The construction gives a quantified absolute budget, not the desired nonpositive cap deficit. ## 1. Boundary packing and the actual ordered collar Normalize the four boundary contacts as \[ uA=1,\qquad AC=0,\qquad Cv=-1,\qquad uv=\infty.	ag{1} \] Put k=cot(pi nu), phi=atan k, so 0<k<1 and phi=pi/2-pi nu in (0,pi/4). The actual white circles have centers \[  egin{aligned} \operatorname{center}(A)&= rac{1+ik}{2},& \operatorname{center}(C)&=- rac{1+ik}{2},\ \operatorname{radius}(A)&=\operatorname{radius}(C) = rac{\sqrt{1+k^2}}2,& u:&\ X-kY=1,\qquad v:\ X-kY=-1. \end{aligned}	ag{2} \] The recorded exterior D lies on the LOWER side of the real contact line. In particular the A fan is the minor arc from0 to1 below the line, with angle pi-2phi=2pi nu. This fixes the side and orientation; the circles alone would not select which complementary disk is D. Write d0=sqrt(1+k^2). The following anti-Mobius reflection matrices have determinant -1 and the original coorientations: \[  egin{aligned} J_A&=d_0^{-1} egin{pmatrix}1+ik&0\2&-1+ik\end{pmatrix},& J_C&=d_0^{-1} egin{pmatrix}-1-ik&0\2&1-ik\end{pmatrix},\ J_u&=d_0^{-1} egin{pmatrix}1-ik&-2\0&-1-ik\end{pmatrix},& J_v&=d_0^{-1} egin{pmatrix}-1+ik&-2\0&1+ik\end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] Thus every original MAIN product at this port has trace -2. Set \[  egin{aligned} A_b&=J_A\overline{J_u},& B_b&=J_C\overline{J_A},\ A_v&=J_v\overline{J_u},& B_v&=J_C\overline{J_v},\ P_{\mathrm{raw}}&=B_bA_b=B_vA_v=J_C\overline{J_u}. \end{aligned}	ag{4} \] Its raw trace is -2(3-k^2)/(1+k^2)<-2. The harmless central choice P=-P_raw has positive trace. Define the projective collar \[ \mathcal C= egin{pmatrix}a&-1\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad a= rac{-1+3ik}{1+ik}=1-2e^{-2i\phi}.	ag{5} \] Direct multiplication gives the literal ordered relations \[ \mathcal C A_b\mathcal C^{-1}=A_v,\qquad \mathcal C B_b\mathcal C^{-1}=B_v,\qquad \mathcal C P_{\mathrm{raw}}=P_{\mathrm{raw}}\mathcal C.	ag{6} \] It sends the recorded flags 1->infinity and0->-1. It preserves each of the two outer white planes: projectively \(\mathcal C\) J_u=J_u bar(\(\mathcal C\)) and \(\mathcal C\) J_C=J_C bar(\(\mathcal C\)). The scalar in both raw identities is (k+i)/(k-i), so no equality of unscaled anti-linear matrices is being asserted. The determinant is -2 exp(-2i phi). Hence \[ \widehat C= rac{\mathcal C}{i\sqrt2e^{-i\phi}},\qquad \det\widehat C=1,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}\widehat C=2\sqrt2\sin\phi=2\cos\psi, \qquad 0<\psi< rac\pi2.	ag{7} \] The actual untwisted auxiliary meridian is the projective \(\widehat C^{-1}\); the preferred longitude is P (up to the recorded central sign). There is no introduced framing, half twist or replacement peripheral word. Every other original coupon has its usual tangent-circle collar from the complete positive exterior packing. ## 2. Both auxiliary flags, with their side fixed The common fixed points of P and \(\mathcal C\) solve \[ O^2-2e^{-2i\phi}O-1=0. \] Write alpha=arcsin(sqrt(2)sin phi) in (0,pi/2), ell=asinh(cos alpha)>0. They are \[ O_{\mathrm{out}}=e^{\ell-i\alpha},\qquad O_{\mathrm{in}}=- rac1{O_{\mathrm{out}}} =e^{-\ell-i(\pi-\alpha)}.	ag{8} \] Both lie STRICTLY BELOW the real line, on the existing exterior side. For the explicit P=-P_raw in (4), O_in is the expanding flag and O_out the contracting flag. \(\widehat C\) has eigenvalues exp(-i psi), exp(+i psi) there respectively, with psi=pi/2-alpha. Thus the meridian eigenvalue at the expanding longitude flag is exp(+i psi). Using the other flag does not change the volume calculation below. Reflection r_u swaps these flags: r_u P_raw r_u=P_raw^-1 and P_raw is genuinely loxodromic. The original cap parameter is NOT a real spectral delta in the earlier intersecting/signed source chart. No identification with that chart's local source action or its regulator primitive is used here. ## 3. Original group sewing and its non-reflected auxiliary flag Use the single global white circle family supplied by the geometric double, restricted to D and its four boundary faces. At every original MAIN edge the two adjacent white circles are tangent, so its ordered head is the actual noncentral parabolic reflection product. The reflection prefixes at a Morse slice telescope exactly. A cup/cap inserts F,G,F and its two ordered heads multiply to identity. Every unchanged CROSS box has its original primitive collar. At F use (6). These are precisely the original untwisted van Kampen/Morse relations; no local spectral interpretation is required to construct the group representation. This is the algebraic part of the variable-headcount group dictionary, independent of its source-action application. Here is an explicit compatible ideal-chain decoration, which avoids the false assertion that the chosen cap flag lies on both outer white planes. On the first original cut ball assign all unchanged contact vertices their exterior packing contacts. Assign its matching uC vertex one selected O in (8). On the second ball reflect every OTHER contact vertex by the ONE global r_u, but assign the cap vertex the SAME O, not r_u(O). This exception is essential. The original white pairing for face f is r_f r_u. On white u this is identity, so it matches O to O. On white C it is P_raw, which also fixes O. These are the only white faces containing this cap vertex. All their other vertices match by the usual reflection argument. Every other white polygon remains exactly the reflected polygon. Therefore the entire triangulated white face chains pair correctly, although the two altered polygons need no longer lie in white planes. Use the existing original abstract fan triangulations, chosen compatibly across paired faces. Degree one comes from the original positive polyhedron's abstract domain certificate, not from convexity or planarity of these newly developed polygons. The first-ball shaded cap pairing is \(\mathcal C\) with its original permutation \[ (O,1,0)\longmapsto(O,\infty,-1). \] The second-ball pairing is r_u \(\mathcal C\) r_u. It fixes the SAME O because r_u swaps the two fixed flags and \(\mathcal C\) fixes both. It sends the other two reflected contacts in the same recorded order. All other shaded pairings are unchanged.
