Consequently these assignments give the original degree-one relative fundamental chain, with the original within-copy untwisted permutations and one common choice of all other flags. They are not the differently marked chain of the doubled link. The auxiliary peripheral subgroup is of axis type, generated by the elliptic \(\widehat C^{-1}\) and loxodromic P with common fixed flags. All other cusps remain boundary-parabolic. The already proved general-peripheral volume theorem, section 2, identifies the sum of the developed ideal tetrahedron volumes with the canonical representation volume also in this axis case. Its explicit cusp homotopy has boundary flux O(y^-2); no horosphere preservation is asserted for P, and no extra arbitrary peripheral constant can be added to this ideal-chain calculation. ## 4. The cap is a pyramid subtraction, not a zero-volume patch In the convex doubled polyhedron the four contacts (1) lie in the vertical geodesic plane over the real line. They form an ideal quadrilateral K. The intersections of this plane with the four boundary white planes are its four sides. Convexity shows the plane's intersection with the doubled polyhedron is EXACTLY K: K is contained by convexity of its four vertices, and the four white halfspaces cut out no larger region. The plane splits the doubled polyhedron into the two exterior pieces. In this normalization the copy involution is the orientation-preserving half-turn \(z\mapsto-z\), which exchanges their sides; it is not reflection in the real contact line. Thus equality of the two volumes does not presume a reflected packing. The recorded D side is the lower side: absence of the boundary diagonal uC forces an interior neighbor in the A fan, whose positive angle lies on the minor arc below the real line. This fixes which of the two components is D, consistently with (2). Each has volume \[ V_D=\pi M_{\mathrm{cap}}.	ag{9} \] The first original ball's boundary is obtained from the D piece by replacing K with the four-triangle cone to O. Two of these triangles are the original shaded cap faces; the other two are the additions to the white u and C faces. This is a statement about the oriented abstract boundary chain, not a convexity claim for its new image. Since O lies on the EXISTING D side of K, that oriented replacement SUBTRACTS the volume of the ideal pyramid with base K and apex O. Using Vol[infinity,0,1,z]=D(z), its positive volume is \[ W(O)=D(-O)-D(O)>0,\qquad \Im O<0.	ag{10} \] Here is a chain-level sign check in this tetrahedron convention. The outward cut face is \[ K=[\infty,-1,0]+[\infty,0,1]. \] The NEW-ball-minus-exterior chain is \[ S=[O,\infty,1,0]+[O,\infty,0,-1],\qquad \partial S=\operatorname{fan}_O(\partial K)-K. \] Its boundary is exactly fan_O(boundary K)-K, and its volume is D(O)-D(-O). This fixes the subtraction sign without identifying the orientation of a listed pairing tuple with an oriented face chain. This provides an absolute orientation/calibration, not a differential guess or a claim that the four flat contacts alone make the cap zero. Thus the first original ball has signed volume V_D-W(O). Reflecting the second ball back by r_u and reversing its abstract orientation gives the same exterior D piece but the OTHER auxiliary flag r_u(O). Formula (8) and D(1/z)=-D(z) imply \[ W(O_{\mathrm{in}})=W(O_{\mathrm{out}}). \] The exact two-ball canonical-chain identity is therefore \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho)=2\pi M_{\mathrm{cap}}-2W(O_{\mathrm{out}}). 	ag{11} \] Both the factor two and the sign come from the literal ball pairings. The original all-CROSS source, source spectral phase, and its possible cancellation have not been changed or identified with this representation. ## 5. Explicit positive budget and its sharp elementary range Put O=O_out from (8). One has \[ |O-1|^2=2,\qquad  rac{1+O}{1-O}=-\overline O. \] The Bloch--Wigner differential \[ dD(z)=\log|z|\,d\operatorname{Arg}(1-z) -\log|1-z|\,d\operatorname{Arg}z \] then gives dW=2ell d alpha. At alpha=0 the two tetrahedra are flat and W=0, fixing the absolute constant. Consequently \[  egin{aligned} W(
u)&=2\int_0^\alpha\operatorname{arsinh}(\cos t)\,dt, &\alpha&=\arcsin igl(\sqrt2\cos(\pi
u) igr),\  rac{dW}{d
u} &=-2\sqrt2\pi\sin(\pi
u)\,  rac{\operatorname{arsinh}\!\sqrt{-\cos(2\pi
u)}} {\sqrt{-\cos(2\pi
u)}}. \end{aligned}	ag{12} \] Equivalently W=integral_psi^(pi/2) 2asinh(sin t)dt. In particular W is strictly positive and strictly decreasing for 1/4<nu<1/2. Its endpoint values are \[ W(	frac12)=0,\qquad W(	frac14)=2G,\qquad 0<W<2G.	ag{13} \] where G=integral_0^1 atan(t)dt/t is Catalan's constant. To check the upper endpoint without a special-value import, differentiate I(a)=integral_0^(pi/2) asinh(a cos t)dt. The substitution u=sin t gives I'(a)=atan(a)/a and I(0)=0, hence I(1)=G. Apply the actual original representation-volume bound to (11): \[ M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\Phi_D \le rac{W(
u)}\pi< rac{2G}\pi=C_0.	ag{14} \] There is also a strict representation-theoretic improvement at any fixed configuration. The actual primitive auxiliary meridian has trace squared 4cos^2(psi)<4. The fixed-peripheral-word gap gives some g>0 for the fixed original exterior and meridian (uniform when nu ranges in a compact subset of (1/4,1/2) with those data fixed), with \[ M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\Phi_D \le rac{W(
u)}\pi- rac g{2\pi} < rac{W(
u)}\pi.	ag{15} \] No available estimate asserts g>=2W, so this still does not prove the desired nonpositive deficit. The word is the ONE fixed original auxiliary meridian; no level-dependent peripheral power is used. Equivalently the original constrained defect obeys Delta_cap<=C0+W(nu)/pi<2C0. This is a uniform complexity-independent bound for a strict ONE-cap-only stationary configuration. It is weaker than Delta_cap<=C0; it does not settle the desired absolute cap comparison. A signed-source loss exceeding W(nu)/pi would suffice to close that configuration's absolute budget, but no such loss is asserted here. In particular a positive local loss, or a single opposite-face cofactor estimate, need not pay this entire amount. ## Scope and proof dependencies The original source incidence, mark and unsigned cap action are those of [the original cap-capacity budget](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md). The genuine exterior and its exact capacity are supplied by [the one-cap geometric double](research_one_cap_geometric_double.md). The group sewing is the literal reflection-prefix/Morse relation from [the actual Morse group dictionary](research_general_morse_cross_action.md), section 2, used only as an algebraic group construction. The ordered within-copy shaded permutations and degree-one two-ball chain are those of [the original cut-ball chain](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md), section 3; its old all-reflected auxiliary-flag choice is explicitly REPLACED at this one cap. The canonical ideal-chain volume equality for an axis cusp is [canonical volume for general peripheral images](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), section 2. The optional strict inequality (15) uses [the fixed-peripheral-word volume gap](general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md). In particular the old finite-collar obstruction at the signed real spectral cap remains valid and is not overridden by this different positive exterior chart.

title: A triangle upper bound for every one-sided relative-energy coefficient
text:
# A triangle upper bound for every one-sided relative-energy coefficient 31 October 2026. The proof is local and retains the full spectral numerator and positive endpoint reference at both parities. A shared global energy bound is not proved here. ## 1. Positive dependence on a single spectral parameter Write $	heta=\pi/N$, $s_j=2\sin(j	heta)$, and normalize the original tail by $$ q_{i,j}=K_{i,j}/\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r^2. $$ It satisfies $q_{i,i}=1$, $q_{i,i+1}=x+y$, and $$ q_{i,j}=(x+y)q_{i,j-1}+(\eta_j-1)xyq_{i,j-2}, \quad \eta_j= rac{\lambda}{d_j}, \quad d_j=\cos	heta-\cos((2j-1)	heta)>0, \quad \lambda=\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta). 	ag{1} $$ The actual start has $j\geq i+2$ in the last term, so no zero sine denominator occurs. On $0\leq\delta\leq1/2-1/(2N)$, $\lambda\geq0$. For an interval of length $r=j-i$, expand the continuant in the parameters $\eta$. A chosen set of disjoint edges contributes $(xy)^{|S|}\prod_{e\in S}\eta_e$. The remaining vertex intervals contribute their baseline continuants $$ h_\ell(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}x^ky^{\ell-k}, $$ which solve (1) with $\eta=0$. Thus every outer coefficient $q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)=[x^ky^{r-k}]q_{i,j}$ is a polynomial in $\lambda$ with nonnegative coefficients. This expansion follows by grouping the selected $\eta$ terms in the usual matching expansion of a tridiagonal determinant; the deleted-edge complements are disjoint intervals. Let $\lambda_0=1+\cos	heta$. Cauchy applied to these nonnegative polynomial coefficients gives the exact finite inequality $$  rac{q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)^2}{q_{i,j,k}(\lambda_0)} \leq q_{i,j,k}\left( rac{\lambda^2}{\lambda_0}ight). 	ag{2} $$ It is a coefficient inequality for the actual tail. It does not assume real negative roots or a coefficient central-limit theorem. ## 2. The original prefix and suffix normalization For the actual LEFT exponent $v=(k,i,d-j,r-k)$, write $a_N(v;\sigma)=B_N(\delta)q_{i,j,k}(\lambda)$ with $\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)$. Here $B_N$ contains the exact omitted-half scalar, all unused lower prefix and suffix diagonals, and $\prod_{r=i+1}^j s_r^2$. The original endpoint reference is $p_N(v)=B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}q_{i,j,k}(\lambda_0)$, $B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}>0$. At even levels the reference is $-V_N(-2)$; at odd levels it is $V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2)$. For a one-sided odd path the central zero is unused, so the derivative removes precisely that zero; its remaining normalization has only polynomial size. Bare odd $V_N(-2)$ is not the reference. Consequently (2) implies $$ \sum_{k=0}^{r} rac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)}x^ky^{r-k} \leq rac{|B_N(\delta)|^2}{B_N^{\mathrm{ref}}} q_{i,j}\left(x,y;\lambda^2/\lambda_0ight). 	ag{3} $$ All exterior and marked factors remain in $B_N$. We will estimate (3) by the uniform tail upper bound and logarithmic prefix/suffix estimates in [the global CROSS proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md), also used for arbitrary tail intervals in [the LEFT theorem](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md). ## 3. The effective weighted kernel Put $\mu=i/N$, $
u=j/N$, $w=
u-\mu$, and, for $0<t<1/2$, $$ s=\sin(\pi t),\quad c=\cos(\pi t),\quad z=\sin^2(\pi\delta),\quad k_\delta^2=1-z, \quad A=x+y,\quad ho=4xy/A^2. $$ The effective parameter in (2) satisfies $\cos^2(\pi\delta_{\mathrm{eff}})	o k_\delta^4$ uniformly in $\delta$. The exact finite parameter stays in the original positive-tail range. Define $$ \Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)=2s\left[As+ \sqrt{(x-y)^2s^2+4xy k_\delta^4}ight], \qquad \alpha_\delta(t)=4(c^2-z). $$ The uniform transfer upper bound, the upper Riemann bounds for both unused products, and the uniform positive reference estimate yield the weighted upper action $$ \int_\mu^
u\log\mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\,dt, \qquad \mathcal L_\delta=  rac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}\alpha_0}{|\alpha_\delta|^2}. 	ag{4} $$ This rewriting uses $\int_0^{1/2}\log|\alpha_\delta|=0$ only AFTER estimating the actual unused products. No finite division at a spectral zero is made. The tail estimate is uniform in both endpoints and the real spectral parameter, including the repeated-root case. The logarithmic errors are $o(N)$ uniformly, at fixed positive $x,y$ in a compact set. Let $$ R_\delta(t)= rac{sc}{c^2-z} = rac{\sin(2\pi t)}{\cos(2\pi t)+\cos(2\pi\delta)}, \qquad B_ho(v)= rac{1+\sqrt{1-ho+ho v^2}}2. $$ A direct simplification of (4) gives $$ \mathcal L_\delta=A R_\delta^2 B_ho(k_\delta^2/s). 	ag{5} $$ The complete positive half-block root is $$ L_0(t;x,y)=A	an^2(\pi t)B_ho(1/\sin(\pi t)). 	ag{6} $$ It is strictly increasing in $t$ and its logarithm is integrable. ## 4. An elementary rearrangement Define $t'=\pi^{-1}\arctan|R_\delta(t)|\in[0,1/2]$. The algebraic identity $$ (c^2-z)^2+s^2c^2-k_\delta^4c^2=z^2s^2\geq0 	ag{7} $$ implies $k_\delta^2/s\leq1/\sin(\pi t')$. Since $B_ho$ is nondecreasing, $$ \mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\leq L_0(t';x,y). 	ag{8} $$ The map $t\mapsto t'$ preserves the uniform distribution on $[0,1/2]$. To prove this, set $\vartheta=2\pi t$, $a=\cos(2\pi\delta)$ and $\varphi=\arg(e^{i\vartheta}+a)$. For $|a|<1$ this angle increases from $0$ to $\pi$, and $$ \vartheta=\varphi+\arcsin(a\sin\varphi). $$ The set $|R_\delta|>r$ has endpoint angles $\varphi_1=\arctan r$ and $\varphi_2=\pi-\arctan r$. Their arcsine corrections agree. Its length in $t$ is therefore $1/2-\pi^{-1}\arctan r$, exactly the distribution of $	an(\pi t)$. The endpoint cases are $t'=t$ and $t'=1/2-t$. For any measurable set of length $w$, the integral of an increasing function of a uniformly distributed $t'$ is at most its upper-tail integral of length $w$. Apply this elementary rearrangement to the interval $[\mu,
u]$ and to $\log L_0$, using truncation for its integrable endpoint singularities. Equations (8) and the distribution identity prove $$  oxed{\displaystyle \int_\mu^
u\log\mathcal L_\delta(t;x,y)\,dt \leq\int_{1/2-w}^{1/2}\log L_0(t;x,y)\,dt.} 	ag{9} $$ ## 5. The coefficient consequence and its current scope Write $\xi=k/N$. Weighted coefficient extraction in (3), (9), and the original complete-triangle Legendre formula give $$ \limsup rac1N\log rac{\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} \leq C(\xi,w-\xi,1/2-w). 	ag{10} $$ The statement is uniform on the entire closed one-sided simplex. For this, first choose a finite outer tilt within any prescribed error at each limiting degree, use continuity of the triangle entropy to obtain a finite cover, and apply the uniform weighted estimates to these finitely many positive tilts. This includes outer degree zero and collapsing intervals. The omitted final spectral cap has width $O(N^{-2})$ in $\sigma$; the polynomial Bernstein bound for each actual coefficient adds only $O(1)$ to its logarithmic supremum. Both parity reference normalizations are kept. RIGHT follows by the original row reflection. If a protected outer is zero, only its exponent-zero coefficients survive, and the already derived sharp boundary formula attains (10). The middle degrees remain $\mu$ and $1-
u$ in the original shared flow. Although the entropy bound depends only on the two outer degrees, it is not permission to reassign middle loads independently. The global energy comparison still requires a proof using the original shared targets.

title: A uniform opposite-equal-face bound for the original cleared cofactor
text: # A uniform opposite-equal-face bound for the original cleared cofactor 31 October 2026. analytical research theorem. This concerns the original raw cleared cofactor R_j, not only its complete determinant. It is a signed evaluation at x=-C,b=C,y=Z>=0, uniform over every real spectral value. No original shared-source Phi_D bound or filled-invariant conclusion is asserted. ## 1. Statement and exact source Put theta=pi/N, J=floor((N-1)/2), and fix a nonnegative integer k. Set j=J-k, restricting to N large enough that j>=0. Use the original \[ a_r=2+2\cos((2r+1)\theta),\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta), \qquad u=-(\sigma+2). \] The cleared cofactor R_j is defined by R_0=1 and \[ R_j=b^j\prod_{r<j}(a_r+u) +s_j^2(x+y)R_{j-1} +s_js_{j-1}(a_{j-1}+u)xyR_{j-2}. \tag{1} \] with the last term absent at j=1. This is exactly the finite source in [original cleared cofactor source](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) section 1. Every original inhomogeneous term is retained. For C in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,infinity) and Z in a fixed compact subinterval of [0,infinity), the claim is \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{\substack{C,Z\\-4\le u\le0}} \left\{\frac1N\log|R_{J-k}(-C,C,Z;u)| -\frac12\log\max(C,Z)\right\}\le0. \tag{2} \] The logarithm at a zero is -infinity. Both level parities are included. Equivalently there is a uniform o(N) upper error in (2). A fixed finite set of k can be included uniformly. On the spectral fold u(delta)=-4sin^2(pi delta), polynomial Bernstein also gives \[ |R_{J-k}(-C,C,Z;u(\delta))| \le \exp\left[N\left(\frac12\log\max(C,Z)+o(1)\right) +2\pi j|\operatorname{Im}\delta|\right]. \tag{3} \] The zero third face is included; C stays bounded away from zero. The real estimate is the mathematical point; (3) is only its exact degree-j spectral extension. ## 2. Exact nodal adapter and a uniform positive tail estimate At the LOWER physical nodes u_a=-a_a, 0<=a<=j, the original source adapter gives \[ R_j(-C,C,Z;u_a)=S_{2a}D_a(-C,C,Z)K_{a,j}(-C,Z;u_a), \qquad S_r=\prod_{v=1}^r s_v. \tag{4} \] This is [original nodal cofactor adapter](actual_cross_cofactor_global_angular_gap.md) section 1, equations (3)-(4), specialized without taking coefficientwise absolute values. Here K_(a,a)=1, K_(a,a-1)=0 and the tail satisfies the original homogeneous two-step recurrence. Write B=|Z-C| and H=CZ. On the actual half-range a<r<=j<=J, a_a-a_(r-1)>=0. A fixed sign change by sign(Z-C)^(r-a), when Z!=C, therefore turns K into the nonnegative continuant \[ \begin{aligned} L_a&=1,\qquad L_{a-1}=0,\\ L_r&=p_rL_{r-1}+q_rL_{r-2},\\ p_r&=s_r^2B,\qquad q_r=s_rs_{r-1}(a_a-a_{r-1})H. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] Thus |K|=L. When Z=C the same statement follows directly: odd-length terms are zero, and even-length terms are nonnegative. In particular no absolute value has been inserted into an oscillatory sum of two different signs. Both p_r and q_r are nondecreasing in r on this ACTUAL range: s_r,s_(r-1) increase before the fold, and a_(r-1) decreases. The first q_(a+1) is zero. Add a FIXED epsilon>0 to B in p_r; this only increases every L_r. Let p_r^epsilon=s_r^2(B+epsilon) and define its local Perron root \[ \lambda_r^\epsilon =\frac{p_r^\epsilon+\sqrt{(p_r^\epsilon)^2+4q_r}}2>0. \] These roots increase with r. For T_r=[[p_r^epsilon,q_r],[1,0]], the vector v_r=(lambda_r^epsilon,1)^T is a positive right eigenvector. Since v_(r-1)<=v_r componentwise, induction from (1,0)^T gives \[ L_j\le \frac{\lambda_j^\epsilon}{\lambda_{a+1}^\epsilon} \prod_{r=a+1}^j\lambda_r^\epsilon \le C_\epsilon N^2\prod_{r=a+1}^j\lambda_r^\epsilon. \tag{6} \] For the empty interval K_(a,a)=1, no prefactor is needed. The bound uses lambda_(a+1)^epsilon =s_(a+1)^2(B+epsilon)>=c epsilon/N^2, while lambda_j^epsilon is bounded above on the parameter compact. It therefore includes a=0, a near the fold, and B=0. There is no hypothesis of distinct tail eigenvalue moduli or a nonzero asymptotic seed. For alpha in [0,.5] define the continuum root \[ \begin{aligned} \Lambda_\epsilon(t;\alpha) =2\sin(\pi t)\Bigl[ &(B+\epsilon)\sin(\pi t)\\ &+\sqrt{(B+\epsilon)^2\sin^2(\pi t) +4CZ\bigl(\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)\bigr)} \Bigr], \qquad \alpha\le t\le\tfrac12. \end{aligned} \tag{7} \] In fact the exact finite roots are bounded DIRECTLY by (7) at t=r/N, alpha=a/N. The p terms agree, while \[ \begin{aligned} q_r &=16CZ\sin(r\theta)\sin((r-1)\theta) \left[\sin^2((r-\tfrac12)\theta) -\sin^2((a+\tfrac12)\theta)\right]\\ &\le16CZ\sin^2(r\theta) \left[\sin^2(r\theta)-\sin^2(a\theta)\right]. \end{aligned} \] Every sine argument is in the increasing half-range; the exact bracket is nonnegative for r>=a+1. Increasing the nonnegative q increases the Perron root, proving the asserted upper bound. The positive addition epsilon also supplies the uniform lower bound Lambda_epsilon(t;alpha)>=4epsilon sin^2(pi t). Consequently monotone Riemann upper sums in (6) give \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{a,C,Z} \left\{ \frac1N\log|K_{a,J-k}(u_a)| -\int_{a/N}^{1/2}\log\Lambda_\epsilon(t;a/N)\,dt \right\}\le0. \tag{8} \] Here and below an empty tail has logarithm zero. For completeness, log Lambda_epsilon is increasing in t. Its right-Riemann sum at r/N differs from the integral by O_epsilon(log N), uniformly in a, before division by N: the first cell is controlled by 4epsilon sin^2(pi t)<=Lambda_epsilon<=C_epsilon, and all remaining cell discrepancies telescope. The fixed terminal defect k omits only O(1) fold cells, with the same bound. Thus no half-step or uncontrolled moving-alpha replacement is needed in (8). As epsilon decreases to zero, these tail integrals decrease to \[ I_{\mathrm{tail}}(\alpha;C,Z) =\int_\alpha^{1/2}\log\Lambda(t;\alpha)\,dt, \qquad \Lambda=\Lambda_0. \tag{9} \] Their limit is finite and continuous jointly on the compact parameter set and alpha in [0,.5], including Z=0. To see a uniform integrable lower bound, if B>=C/2 then Lambda>=2C sin^2(pi t); otherwise CZ>=C^2/2. These two cases give \[ \Lambda(t;\alpha)\ge c\sin(\pi t)\sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)}. \] with c>0 uniform on the stated compact. In particular B=0 has \[ \Lambda(t;\alpha) =4\sqrt{CZ}\sin(\pi t) \sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\alpha)}. \] whose moving endpoint logarithm is integrable; the identity sin^2(pi t)-sin^2(pi alpha) =sin(pi(t-alpha))sin(pi(t+alpha)) gives uniform integrable logarithmic bounds, including alpha=0,.5. Together with a uniform upper bound, these logarithmic bounds prove continuity also as B tends to zero or Z tends to zero. Compact monotone convergence of the continuous integrals therefore makes epsilon->0 UNIFORM. Equations (6)-(8) prove (8) with epsilon=0. This is an upper estimate only; a zero odd-length tail causes no difficulty. ## 3. The exact integral cancellation For C>0 and Z>=0 set \[ S=C+Z,\qquad \rho=\frac{4CZ}{S^2},\qquad \beta=\frac{|Z-C|}{S}=\sqrt{1-\rho}, \qquad \alpha\in[0,\tfrac12]. \] Define, with integrable endpoint values, \[ \begin{aligned} I(\alpha) ={}&\int_0^{2\alpha}\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt\\ &+\int_0^\alpha \log\frac{|Z+Ce^{2\pi it}|}{4\cos^2(\pi t)}\,dt +\int_\alpha^{1/2}\log\Lambda(t;\alpha)\,dt. \end{aligned} \tag{10} \] Then EXACTLY \[ I(\alpha)=\frac12\log\max(C,Z), \qquad 0\le\alpha\le\frac12. \tag{11} \] Here Lambda is (7) with epsilon=0 and its ACTUAL scale; no undetermined normalization constant remains. Proof first suppose 0<rho<1 and 0<alpha<.5. Put v=sin^2(pi alpha), h=sqrt(1-rho v), beta=sqrt(1-rho)>0. The derivatives of the first two integrals and the moving lower endpoint of the third add to \[ \log(h/\beta). \] Indeed Lambda(alpha;alpha)=4|Z-C|v, and |Z+C exp(2pi i alpha)|=S h. For the remaining derivative, first differentiate with respect to v and then put u=cot(pi t): \[ \begin{aligned} \int_\alpha^{1/2}\partial_v\log\Lambda(t;\alpha)\,dt &=-\frac{\rho}{2\pi} \int_0^{\cot(\pi\alpha)} \frac{du}{A(u)(\beta+A(u))},\\ A(u)&=\sqrt{1-\rho v-\rho v u^2}. \end{aligned} \tag{12} \] Substitute u=sqrt((1-rho v)/(rho v)) sin theta. At the upper endpoint cos theta_*=beta/h. The elementary tangent-half-angle integral is \[ \int_0^{\theta_*}\frac{d\theta}{\beta+h\cos\theta} =\frac{\log(h/\beta)}{\sqrt{\rho(1-v)}}. \] Thus (12), multiplied by dv/dalpha=2pi sqrt(v(1-v)), equals -log(h/beta). This cancels the moving-endpoint contribution exactly, so I'(alpha)=0. At alpha=0 the first two integrals vanish and \[ \Lambda(t;0)=4\max(C,Z)\sin^2(\pi t). \] Since integral_0^(.5)log(4sin^2(pi t))dt=0, this gives (11). The same uniform integrable logarithmic bounds as in section 2 justify alpha->0,.5, beta->0 and Z->0. In particular C=Z is included by continuity; the derivation does not divide beta at that limit. At Z=0 one may instead use Lambda=4C sin^2(pi t) directly. ## 4. Uniform nodal bound for the ACTUAL cofactor The separately proved original determinant prefix bound is \[ \frac1N\log|D_a(-C,C,Z)| \le \int_0^{a/N}\log\frac{|Z+Ce^{2\pi it}|} {4\cos^2(\pi t)}\,dt+o(1). \tag{13} \] UNIFORMLY for all 0<=a<=J and the stated parameter compact. Its exact source and proof are in [opposite-equal determinant prefix theorem](research_opposite_equal_triangle_determinant_bound.md) (5a): the original tridiagonal determinant roots are (Z+C exp(+-2pi i t))/(4cos^2(pi t)), both moduli retained. This input is a genuine determinant upper, not an inference from a coefficientwise positive comparison. The elementary sine-product estimate gives, also uniformly in a, \[ \frac1N\log S_{2a} =\int_0^{2a/N}\log(2\sin(\pi t))\,dt +O\!\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right). \tag{14} \] The products have no zero since 2a<=N-1. Splitting at the midpoint and bounding the endpoint harmonic sums proves (14). Combine the exact source (4), tail upper (8)-(9), determinant upper (13), and sine product (14). Identity (11) proves \[ \max_{0\le a\le j}|R_j(-C,C,Z;u_a)| \le \exp\left[N\left(\frac12\log\max(C,Z)+o(1)\right)\right]. \tag{15} \] The o(1) is uniform in a,C,Z and both parities. No coefficient lower asymptotic or nodal nonvanishing is used. ## 5. Interpolation with the omitted nodes retained correctly The polynomial R_j has degree at most j in u. The full physical distinct-node grid has J+1 points u_a,0<=a<=J. We know (15) only for a<=j=J-k. Define \[ Q(u)=R_j(u)\prod_{a=j+1}^J(u-u_a). \] Then deg Q<=J; at each omitted node Q=0 exactly. Interpolation on the original Chebyshev/Radau full grid has Lebesgue norm O(log N). At retained nodes, the added product is bounded by 4^k. Therefore \[ \sup_{[-4,0]}|Q| \le C_k\log(N+1) \exp\left[N\left(\frac12\log\max(C,Z)+o(1)\right)\right]. \] Recovering R_j costs only a fixed polynomial. If q(t0)=0 for t0 in [-4,0], then q(t)/(t-t0)=integral_0^1 q'(t0+s(t-t0))ds, so its interval supremum is at most sup|q'|. The ordinary polynomial derivative bound costs O(J^2) per removed factor (O(J^3) would also suffice). Repeat k times. This proves (2). It also shows why no uncontrolled value at an omitted node or division by a sampled zero enters the argument. Finally apply the degree-j cosine Bernstein bound to obtain (3). The nodal factorization, all scalar sine products and the odd central endpoint remain literal original-source quantities. ## 6. Scope and useful consequence The same actual positive cofactor has weighted rate Q(C,C,Z) at u=0, by the [original complete half-triangle theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md). Thus (2) gives the explicit strictly positive asymptotic loss \[ Q(C,C,Z)-\frac12\log\max(C,Z)>0. \] This is uniform on the stated compacts, including Z=0. The strict inequality follows by a small positive triangle-corner perturbation of the largest pure weight, retaining its entropy gain. At the protected third face Z=0 this loss is exactly \[ 2f(\tfrac14)>0,\qquad f(t)=-\int_0^t\log\tan(\pi s)\,ds. \] This upgrades the determinant-only result to the raw cleared cofactor for ALL real spectra and a sufficiently thin fixed spectral strip. It does NOT automatically give a coefficientwise bound, an all-face-phase bound, a Green-star endpoint comparison, or an absolute bound by the original complete source volume. Other shared face targets and other coupons remain to be controlled. This raw-cofactor bound is for the specified real-face specialization, including $Z=0$. It does not cover an arbitrary face-phase torus or prove a complete-volume comparison.

title: An explicit cancellation bound for an original half-triangle determinant
text: # An explicit cancellation bound for an original half-triangle determinant 31 October 2026. analytical research lemma. This concerns the actual positive half-determinant at two equal, opposite face arguments. It is not yet a theorem for a raw cleared cofactor, a whole cap star, or a filled invariant. In particular, coefficientwise positive comparisons cannot transfer this estimate to a signed evaluation. ## 1. The finite determinant and the bound Put theta=pi/N and J=floor((N-1)/2). For a=J-k, where k>=0 is fixed, use precisely the matrices in [the physical boundary model](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md), section 1. They are a by a, with diagonal and upper adjacent entries \[ d_n=\frac1{\cos(n\theta)\cos((n+1)\theta)},\qquad (H_\pm)_{n-1,n}=\sqrt{b_n}\,[\sin(n\theta)\pm i\cos(n\theta)], \] \[ b_n=\frac{\sin^2(n\theta)} {\cos^2(n\theta)\sin((2n-1)\theta)\sin((2n+1)\theta)}. \tag{1} \] Their lower entries are the conjugates of their upper entries. The original homogeneous half-determinant is \[ D_a(x,b,y)=\det\bigl(bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+\bigr). \tag{2} \] Fix C>0 and specialize x=-C,b=C,y=z, where z may be complex. Define \[ \mathcal J_C(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\pi \log\max\{|z+Ce^{it}|,|z+Ce^{-it}|\}\,dt. \tag{3} \] **Lemma.** Uniformly for C in any positive compact interval and z in any complex compact set, \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{C,z} \left\{\frac1N\log|D_{J-k}(-C,C,z)|-\mathcal J_C(z)\right\}\le0. \tag{4} \] The convention at a zero determinant is log 0=-infinity. In particular, for REAL z, including z=0 and z=+-C, \[ \mathcal J_C(z)=\frac12\log\max\{C,|z|\}. \tag{5} \] This is an upper bound. Zeros and oscillation preclude inferring a uniform lower asymptotic. Both parities of N are included. The same proof gives a prefix version needed by the actual nodal cofactor adapter. For EVERY 0<=a<=J define \[ I_{C,z}(\alpha)=\int_0^\alpha \log\frac{\max\{|z+Ce^{2\pi it}|,|z+Ce^{-2\pi it}|\}} {4\cos^2(\pi t)}\,dt. \] Uniformly over these indices and the same parameter compacts, \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{a,C,z} \left\{\frac1N\log|D_a(-C,C,z)|-I_{C,z}(a/N)\right\}\le0. \tag{5a} \] Here D_0=1. No lower bound for any prefix determinant is used. ## 2. Exact scalar recurrence and its bulk roots Let Delta_n be the determinant of the leading n by n submatrix of (2), after the stated specialization. Tridiagonal expansion gives Delta_0=1, Delta_1=C+(z-C)/(2cos theta), and, for n>=1, \[ \Delta_{n+1}=A_{N,n}\Delta_n-B_{N,n}\Delta_{n-1}, \] \[ \begin{aligned} A_{N,n}&=C+\frac{z-C}{2\cos(n\theta)\cos((n+1)\theta)},\\ B_{N,n}&=\frac{b_n}{4} \left[(z-C)^2\sin^2(n\theta)+(z+C)^2\cos^2(n\theta)\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{6} \] For complex z this uses the product of the actual upper and lower entries, not their absolute square. All scalar normalizations in (2) remain present. For t=n/N in a fixed closed subinterval of (0,1/2), the transfer matrix [[A,-B],[1,0]] converges, with error O(1/N), to the matrix with \[ A(t)=\frac{z+C\cos(2\pi t)}{2\cos^2(\pi t)},\qquad B(t)=\frac{z^2+C^2+2Cz\cos(2\pi t)}{16\cos^4(\pi t)}. \tag{7} \] The two roots are EXPLICIT: \[ \lambda_\pm(t)=\frac{z+Ce^{\pm2\pi it}}{4\cos^2(\pi t)}, \qquad \lambda_+(t)-\lambda_-(t)=iC\tan(\pi t). \tag{8} \] They never collide on that bulk interval, independently of z. The eigenvector matrix with columns (lambda_+,1) and (lambda_-,1), its inverse, and its first t derivative have uniform bounds on the stated compact sets. In particular \[ \rho(t):=\max(|\lambda_+(t)|,|\lambda_-(t)|) \ge\tfrac12 C\tan(\pi t)>0. \tag{9} \] ## 3. Product estimate, with both endpoint portions retained Fix eta>0 and work first on eta<=t<=1/2-eta. Conjugate each exact transfer matrix by the eigenvector matrices at its two adjacent mesh points. Equations (6)--(8) give \[ E((n+1)/N)^{-1}T_{N,n}E(n/N) =\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_+(n/N),\lambda_-(n/N))+O_\eta(N^{-1}). \tag{10} \] Thus its norm is at most rho(n/N)+O_eta(1/N). The positive lower bound (9) makes the accumulated logarithmic error O_eta(1), not order N. Taking products and using the endpoint bounds for E proves the bulk upper bound by the SUM of log rho, with o(N) error. This retains the larger modulus at each step. For real z the two moduli coincide, so there is no selection of one unproved action branch or neglect of a growing transfer mode. The omitted physical rows are controlled directly. From (1), for every actual n in the matrix, \[ |A_{N,n}|+|B_{N,n}|+1 \le C_K\bigl(1+\cos^{-4}((n+1)\theta)\bigr). \tag{11} \] For example, sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta) =sin^2(2n theta)-sin^2 theta; on the actual range 1<=n<=a-1 its ratio to sin^2(2n theta) is bounded below uniformly for large N. The first O(eta N) transfers therefore cost O(eta N), and the last O(eta N) cost at most \[ O\bigl(\eta N\log(2/\eta)+\log N\bigr). \tag{12} \] This follows by summing log(N/r) at the actual half-integer or integer distances from the fold. A fixed k changes only a bounded number of terminal rows. No inverse determinant, nonzero initial component, or cancellation assumption is needed for this upper bound. Uniformly on the compact parameter sets, log rho is integrable at both ends: (9) bounds it below by log t-O(1) near zero and by -log(1/2-t)-O(1) near the fold; (8) bounds it above by O(1)+2|log(1/2-t)|. Its omitted integrals are consequently O(eta log(2/eta)). First take N to infinity and then eta to zero. The bulk Riemann sums and (12) give \[ \limsup \frac1N\log|D_{J-k}(-C,C,z)| \le\int_0^{1/2}\log\rho(t)\,dt=\mathcal J_C(z), \tag{13} \] uniformly as asserted. The last equality uses integral_0^(1/2) log(4cos^2(pi t))dt=0. The same estimates prove continuity of (3), including its integrable boundary zeros. For (5a), stop the same transfer product at the actual index a. The retained bulk interval is eta<=t<=min(a/N,1/2-eta). If a/N<eta, the entire product is in the short initial portion. Every omitted integral and physical endpoint portion still has the bounds just proved, uniformly in a. This proves the asserted prefix upper bound, including sequences with a/N tending to either endpoint. ## 4. Real arguments and the positive comparison If Im z>=0, the first modulus in (3) is larger; if Im z<=0, the second is larger. For real z they are equal. The integral over a half circle is then half the full-circle logarithmic mean. Expanding log(1-w) for |w|<1 shows that this full-circle mean is log max(C,|z|). The boundary |z|=C follows by the elementary integrable logarithmic limit. This proves (5) without assuming an asymptotic lower bound for the finite determinant. For real z>0 the positive determinant D_{J-k}(C,C,z) has the known triangle rate Q(C,C,z), with Q normalized by the original half-triangle entropy. Consequently (4) proves the explicit rate loss \[ Q(C,C,z)-\tfrac12\log\max(C,z)>0. \tag{14} \] Strictness follows by perturbing the pure corner of the largest weight into another positive corner: the entropy gain is of order -epsilon log epsilon and dominates its finite linear weight cost. At z=0 the permitted two-corner triangle gives exactly \[ Q(C,C,0)-\tfrac12\log C=2f(1/4),\qquad f(s)=-\int_0^s\log\tan(\pi t)\,dt. \tag{15} \] The rate for the positive comparator is from the original determinant, [even half-block entropy normalization](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), section 5, and [the odd simple-fold determinant](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), sections 2–3. These identify the full J determinant. For fixed k, successive Schur pivots of the positive matrix C I+(C/2)H_-+(z/2)H_+ lie between C and their diagonal upper bounds O_K(N^2). Removing k terminal rows changes its logarithm by only O_K(k log N). This proves the same comparator rate at J-k, at both parities. Formula (14) quantifies one special angular loss; it does not say that this loss pays the whole cap budget in an arbitrary star. ## 5. The adapter still required for the original cap problem At even levels the original modified cofactor is R_M*=C_front D_M, C_front=N/(2sin(pi/N)). The actual unmodified cofactor R_M has a coefficientwise positive comparison with R_M*. That comparison does NOT bound R_M(-C,C,z) by R_M*(-C,C,z). It was proved before inserting signs. Likewise a finite spectral interpolation of the raw CROSS polynomial requires all its actual nodal cofactors and terminal terms. Therefore (4) applies directly to (2), its retained polynomial scalar multiples, and products for which that finite determinant adapter is already exact. A separate [raw-cofactor theorem](research_opposite_equal_raw_cofactor_bound.md) now supplies the missing finite-source argument when the third face is REAL and nonnegative: the exact nodal cofactor, its signed tail, and an absolutely normalized integral identity give the same bound for R_(J-k) on the entire real spectral interval. This uses no signed version of the invalid coefficientwise comparison above. The arbitrary complex third-face case for that raw cofactor, the full spectral star with all its shared phases, the absolute shared-volume comparison, and the maximal Green pairing remain separate. No general long-twist theorem follows from this determinant lemma alone. The opposite-equal determinant values are exploratory diagnostics, not lower asymptotic bounds.

title: Original coefficient blocks, stationary touching, and the absolute cap budget
text: # Original coefficient blocks, stationary touching, and the absolute cap budget 31 October 2026. **analytical research lemma.** Unpublished. No full-source or filling theorem is asserted. The purpose is to identify an exact usable closure statement and the two missing steps between the proved whole-star estimate and an absolute Phi_D bound. Inputs are the [whole-star spectral gap](research_cap_cross_shared_star_spectral_gap.md), [cap-leaf structural theorem](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md), [original stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md), [uniform sharp coefficient upper](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md), [closed endpoint coefficient entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md), and [unique endpoint maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md). Their local estimates, endpoint theorem and original source identities are inputs. The unproved prescribed-chart full-source theorem is not an input. ## 1. Exact contraction before localization Fix the original marked diagram. Every coupon has degree d=N-1; ordinary targets are d and protected targets are zero. Keep the actual finite LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT restrictions whenever a sector is specified. Let B be a collection of coupons and I a set of ordinary faces all of whose incidences belong to B. Define the original contracted polynomial B_N(Y;theta)=[prod_(a in I) A_a^d] prod_(e in B) P_e,N(A,Y;theta_e). The exterior G_N has no A_a incidence. Consequently [original target] prod_e P_e,N =[Y^t] B_N(Y) G_N(Y). (1) All shared boundary variables remain identified. The degree of B_N is d(|B|-|I|); no new target or normalization occurs. Expand the EXTERIOR into its original local coefficient arrays k. Its boundary demand left for B is a_N(k)_f=t_f-sum_(e outside B) k_(e,f). Only nonnegative a_N contribute. The exact identity is [Y^t]B_N G_N =sum_k [Y^(a_N(k))]B_N prod_(e outside B) p_e,N(k_e). (2) This is a sum over polynomially many arrays at a fixed diagram. In (2) all internal B allocations have ALREADY been summed with their original signs. In particular no restriction on one internal cap index is introduced by restricting k. Let a=a_N/d. Suppose, uniformly on a spectral compact K, the actual boundary coefficients have an upper rate b(a,theta), in the sequential sense that every convergent admissible (a_N/d,theta_N) has limsup N^-1 log |[Y^a_N]B_N| at most b(a,theta). Take b upper semicontinuous. The established uniform local coefficient upper for the exterior then gives limsup N^-1 log sup_(theta in K) |[Y^t]B_N G_N| <= max_(q_out,theta in K) {b(tbar-A_out q_out,theta)+sum_(e outside B) H_e(q_e,theta_e)}. (3) The maximum ranges only over limits of exact exterior arrays for which the boundary degree is supported. Enlarging this to the corresponding closed original incidence image is safe for an upper bound. If that image is empty, there is no term. Formula (3) uses compactness and the polynomial array count, not lower rounding or a minimax interchange. In particular a torus estimate sup_(|Y|=L) |B_N(Y;theta)| <= exp(N(W(L)-delta(L)+o(1))) implies the genuine boundary coefficient estimate b_L(a)=W(L)-delta(L)-a dot log L. (4) Any finite number of such bounds can be MINIMIZED for the SAME boundary coefficient. One may also include its direct sharp block upper, obtained by summing its actual internal arrays. Thus b(a,theta)=min{b_direct(a,theta),b_L1(a),...,b_Ls(a)} (5) is legitimate. For a local spectral domain, include b_L only there; one can work with closed smaller domains or continuous majorants to avoid a discontinuous convention at its boundary. The same proof works for a FIXED partition into port-disjoint blocks with disjoint exclusive internal faces. Boundary variables of distinct blocks may coincide. Sum their b's and the remaining local H's on the reduced original flow. This gives an explicit finite-dimensional upper bound for the same source, retaining all targets. ## 2. What a finite cover is allowed to cover A spectral cover is harmless: at a fixed theta, estimates from different block decompositions bound the SAME full coefficient. Thus one may take the minimum of their full capacities from (3), and use a finite spectral cover on which this minimum is below Phi_D by a uniform positive margin. That is the same logical operation as the mark-spectral cover. A cover in INDIVIDUAL INTERNAL INCIDENCE ARRAYS is different. A mask cutting (2) preserves B_N exactly if it is constant on each fiber of the map from full arrays to exterior arrays k. Equivalently the mask must depend only on data left outside the contracted block. This is an exact sufficient condition. It is also necessary for the proposed factorization with unchanged B_N and a mask depending only on exterior data, as a formal identity for arbitrary local coefficients. Assign an independent symbol to each local monomial coefficient of each coupon. Distinct original incidence arrays give distinct products of these symbols. For fixed exterior array k, comparison of these independent monomials forces the full-array mask to have the same value on every internal array over k. No cancellation between different symbolic products can repair a nonconstant mask. This formal coefficient test is a logical obstruction to an inference, not an actual-link counterexample. A special identity for the actual coupons could give additional cancellations, but it would be a new input beyond the unchanged whole-star theorem. For overlapping stars a priority partition into neighborhoods need not have this fiber property for the star assigned to each piece. For example, the exterior degrees of one star may include a coupon inside the other. A common-exterior degree partition is safe, as is a fixed disjoint-block contraction. Otherwise an additional projection or boundary-tensor identity is required. One cannot reuse the unchanged whole-star bound for an arbitrarily cut internal sum. Consequently (3)-(5), rather than a cover of individual saddle arrays, are a rigorous quantitative extraction theorem. An absolute criterion is that the right side of (3), or the minimum over finitely many valid full capacities, is less than Phi_D. This criterion still has a variational comparison to prove on a general prescribed diagram. ## 3. The star envelope actually touches the stationary sharp action There is a useful precise connection between the existing weighted star bound and the sharp maximum; the two are not unrelated envelopes. Take a classified stationary residual cap F=(u,A,v,C), u=v=0, q_F,A=1-nu, q_F,C=nu, 0<nu<1/2. Suppose every other A-incident coupon is CROSS. Let B consist of F and ALL these neighbors, and I={A}. The common positive multipliers give L_A=L_C. Let q* be the classified stationary assignment and let a* be its total B-boundary loads, with A omitted. Write W(L)=sum_(e in B minus F) X_e(L), X_e(L)=Q_e,input(L)+Q_e,output(L). At each stationary CROSS neighbor, the same ordinary positive weights attain its triangle Legendre formulas, including its protected zeros. Therefore X_e(L)=h_e(q*_e)+q*_e dot log L. This follows alternatively from concavity of the complete two-triangle entropy and the common first-order equations; it is not a weighted maximality assertion about a Green coupon. The total B load at A is one, and its cap weighted load equals (1-nu)log L_A+nu log L_C=log L_A. Since the cap sharp action is zero, exact cancellation of these two log L_A terms gives W(L)-a* dot log L = sum_(e in B) H_e(q*_e). (6) Thus the proved spectral-star estimate, with its actual gap delta>0, gives a boundary-coefficient upper at a* equal to the original sharp block action MINUS delta. After adjoining the unchanged exterior at q*_out, the expression in (3) is total sharp action(q*)-delta. (7) Continuity of the exterior H and of the affine term in (4) preserves a strict improvement in a neighborhood of the EXTERIOR data and spectra. The whole cap spectral disk and CROSS strips are genuine fixed neighborhoods, as required by the star theorem. Equation (7) also holds for a maximum restricted to closed NC once the independently proved strict overload margin permits the original stationary equations. Notice what is and is not localized: (7) bounds every internal star allocation compatible with that exterior coefficient, not just those near q*. This is exactly why (2) is the correct decomposition. As a useful conditional consequence, if all maximizers of a specified sharp sector capacity M are covered by exterior-fiber neighborhoods admitting (7) for ONE FIXED block, and the block direct sharp upper is at most M elsewhere, compactness of (3)-(5) gives an actual strict upper M-delta_0 for some delta_0>0. A compatible finite partition into blocks has the same consequence. This is a strict improvement relative to M; it does not assert M-delta_0<Phi_D. ## 4. The absolute cap deficit is exactly 2 f(nu) Let f(t)=-integral_0^t log tan(pi s) ds, f(0)=f(1/2)=0, f(t)>0 for 0<t<1/2. Use h_0 for the actual positive endpoint coefficient entropy (both parities, with the prescribed odd regularizer), and H for the sharp real spectral upper. The closed monomer formula proves on the cap degrees just used H_cap=0, h_0,cap=-2f(nu). (8) At a classified CROSS neighbor at spectrum -2, H=h_0. Hence for a cap-only classified datum, with caps indexed by F, F_sharp(q)=H_endpoint(q)+2 sum_F f(nu_F). (9) This is an identity on the original flow, not a smoothing or a changed triangle allocation. The endpoint theorem and unique geometric maximum give H_endpoint<=Phi_D. More quantitatively let g_D=Phi_D-max_(q in original closed NC) H_endpoint(q)>0. (10) The maximum exists on the compact original flow; it is strictly below Phi_D because the unique geometric optimizer is strictly CROSS. Empty NC is vacuous. Thus on the cap-only data F_sharp(q)-Phi_D <= 2 sum_F f(nu_F)-g_D. (11) In particular a cap-only datum of value at least Phi_D must satisfy 2 sum f(nu_F)>=g_D. With one cap its nu is in a compact subinterval of (0,1/2). With two caps at least one has a definite positive f; this does not place BOTH parameters away from their endpoints. Formula (11) identifies a quantitative sufficient budget for a VALID localization or disjoint-block extraction: a cancellation loss exceeding 2 sum f(nu_F)-g_D gives an absolute improvement below Phi_D at that datum. Loss at least 2 sum f(nu_F) is a simpler conservative sufficient budget, leaving the original endpoint gap untouched. A potentially sharper budget uses the actual endpoint value H_endpoint(q), not g_D. The star theorem currently provides delta>0, not an inequality between delta and this deficit. Equations (6)-(7) explain how to compare the quantities without confusing different weighted envelopes. They do not prove the missing comparison. For the actual contracted star an even more intrinsic target is its positive ENDPOINT REFERENCE with the SAME A^d and boundary degrees, including the actual odd regularizer and the same sector projections. Let its coefficients be r_N(a)>0 on the relevant support. An estimate |[Y^a]B_N| <= exp(o(N)) r_N(a) (12) uniformly over original admissible a, and in an appropriate spectral neighborhood, pays the entire boundary-optimized endpoint deficit. The [two-spectrum degree-two theorem](research_cap_cross_two_spectrum_neighborhood_stability.md) proves the endpoint version with exp(o(N)); on a fixed nearby spectral polydisk it gives exp(N omega(epsilon)+o(N)), with omega(epsilon) tending to zero, for its typed pair. The arbitrary valence star theorem has not proved (12). ## 5. The exact minimal replacement test for arbitrary exteriors Fix any contracted B_N and positive comparison R_N with the same boundary degree. Restrict to boundary exponents a which are compatible with the specified remaining original target t, namely 0<=a<=t and any additional genuine exterior support restrictions. For a family of arbitrary exterior coefficients supported on all such complements, the following are equivalent: (i) |[Y^a]B_N| <= kappa_N [Y^a]R_N for every such a; (ii) |[Y^t]B_N G_N| <= kappa_N [Y^t]R_N |G_N|_coeff for every polynomial G_N with that allowed exterior support. The implication (i)->(ii) is exact convolution and the triangle inequality. For (ii)->(i), choose the single monomial G_N=Y^(t-a). One may include its harmless unit phase. Unsupported comparison coefficients must then force the corresponding B coefficient to vanish. No statement about inadmissible exponents is needed. For the actual fixed exterior, (i) is a sufficient condition, not a claimed necessary condition: its special source correlations can provide more cancellation. This distinction leaves room for a genuine larger-source identity beyond (12). For port-disjoint exclusive blocks, (12) at every block combines by ordinary positive convolution while retaining shared boundary labels. For overlapping blocks it does not automatically iterate. Taking an absolute value after the first contraction can erase the second block's internal signs, and its factors are no longer the unchanged original block. Either a single larger-block comparison or a proved compatible replacement operator is needed. ## 6. Why strict loss at old maxima is not an iteration theorem Two logically distinct claims are sometimes conflated: A. every high maximum of the original sharp functional has a cancellation block giving some positive loss; B. the actual source has rate at most Phi_D. Even with completely compatible localization, A gives a strict reduction from the original maximum M. It does not say the reduction exceeds M-Phi_D. A one-dimensional logical test is H(x)=Phi_D+a-x^2 and an exactly known improved bound H(x)-b, where 0<b<a. The maximum is strictly reduced, all original maxima are covered, but the resulting upper remains Phi_D+a-b>Phi_D. This is not a diagram counterexample; it disproves the purported abstract implication. Nor can the SAME estimate simply be applied again to subtract another b. After replacing the original upper by the minimum of new bounds, its new maxima can occur on a switch between bounds and need not satisfy the original sharp stationary equations. The boundary activation and cap-leaf theorems classify maxima of the original functional on its original fiber. They have not been proved for these new contracted, often nonsmooth upper functionals. Reusing their conclusion there would be circular. A valid finite iteration must therefore supply, at each stage, an exact coefficient-preserving replacement and a proved decreasing potential with a quantitative budget, together with either termination at the positive endpoint source or an absolute terminal bound. Current cap-leaf selection proves existence of an applicable relative star at certain original maxima; it does not supply these iteration data. The stellar identity reinforces the distinction: it preserves M_cap-Phi while increasing the cap incidence degree. It transports a CLASSICAL sector optimization, not the finite signed boundary polynomial or its needed compensation (12). ## 7. Endpoint resolvent: exact identity, but no free positivity For the full original Casimir quotient, chi_N(Omega)=0 and chi_N(2)=4 give the exact polynomial resolvent identity (2-Omega)V_N(2)=4I. (13) Every unchanged linear original source functional Lambda therefore satisfies 2Lambda(V_N(2))-Lambda(Omega V_N(2))=4Lambda(1). The extra Omega coupon has not disappeared. Projecting to the cap range produces the already known boundary currents of the Newton contiguity; omitting them would alter the source. An ordinary self-adjoint Casimir model would bound the scalar inverse by its spectral distance, but cannot be assumed to preserve the complete-colored quotient. The even coupon L_N=(-1)^d U_d(z/2) has L_N^2=0 modulo chi_N and vanishes at every distinct spectral node, whereas the [actual conditioned coefficients](research_cap_cross_high_demand_signed_contraction.md#8-low-demand-still-detects-the-actual-casimir-jordan-data) Lambda_n(1,L_N) are strictly positive for every 0<=n<=M, where M=N/2-1; in particular Lambda_0(1,L_N)=N^2. Thus a coupon-uniform semisimple adapter preserving these observables is impossible. This does not exclude a special identity for the fixed resolvent, an explicit treatment of its confluent corrections, or a nonlinear bound not intertwining arbitrary coupons. ## 8. Current concrete missing lemma The precise new candidate is a cancellation-aware boundary comparison for a whole cap/CROSS star at original A^d, either (12), or a weaker weighted coefficient bound whose loss satisfies the explicit budget in (11) after a legitimate reduced-flow maximization (3). It must retain every boundary face degree and the actual parity reference. Such a theorem would be a real absolute input. A finite collection of compatible bounds satisfying (3)<Phi_D uniformly off the geometric spectral cube would feed the [existing entire-period criterion](research_mark_spectral_cover_filling_volume.md); its nonzero geometric packet and primitive filling action are separate already proved inputs. Neither a positive local gap by itself nor a classification of old maxima supplies that strict absolute premise. No global counterexample has been proved here. The existing shared-star and structural notes state their limitations correctly; the gap is in the unproved bridge one might try to infer from them. ## scope Block localization uses independent formal local coefficients. Its stationary touching identity retains the negative endpoint cap entropy and the non-iteration limitation; a relative block loss alone does not pay an absolute volume deficit. The all-parity original target, actual sector projections, protected zeros, and distinction between endpoint compensation and a positive relative gap are retained. No source lower bound, universal cap elimination, absolute prescribed-chart comparison, or filling theorem is inferred.

title: Exact original before, active and after transfer
status: Exact original four-state identity; both parities
text: # Exact original before, active and after transfer 31 October 2026. An exact source identity: no asymptotic branch is selected and no unused row is deleted. Put \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \(M=m-1\), and \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\). Define \[ c_r=2\cos\frac{(2r+1)\pi}{N},\qquad \alpha_r=c_r-\sigma,\qquad s_r=2\sin\frac{\pi r}{N}, \quad A=x+y,\quad P=xy, \] \[ \beta_r=s_r^2,\qquad \gamma_r=s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1},\qquad A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=m}^{d}\alpha_r. \] At \(r=0,1\), set \(\gamma_r=0\); these are the original absent negative-row term and the factor \(s_0=0\). All products retain level \(N\). ## 1. The exact original polynomial The [original one-sided coefficient expansion](actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.md) has the sign-adjusted form \[ (-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}} =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha \sum_{0\le i\le j\le M} b^i c^{d-j} \prod_{r<i}\alpha_r\prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r\,K_{i,j}, \tag{1} \] where \(K_{i,i}=1\), \(K_{i,i+1}=\beta_{i+1}A\), and \[ K_{i,j}=\beta_j A K_{i,j-1}+\gamma_jP K_{i,j-2}. \] The raw resolvent sign is independent of the endpoints. The path sign \((-1)^{j-i}\), followed by changing the \(d-j+i\) outside factors from \(\sigma-c_r\) to \(-\alpha_r\), gives exactly \((-1)^d\). Set \(B_{-1}=1\) and \(R_{-1}=R_{-2}=Z_{-1}=0\). For \(0\le r\le M\), let \[ \begin{aligned} B_r&=b\alpha_r B_{r-1},\\ R_r&=B_{r-1}+\beta_r A R_{r-1}+\gamma_r P R_{r-2},\\ Z_r&=R_r+c\alpha_rZ_{r-1}. \end{aligned}\tag{2} \] Induction, first on the last active step and then on the last inactive step, gives \[ B_r=\prod_{u=0}^{r}b\alpha_u,\qquad R_r=\sum_{i=0}^{r}b^i\prod_{u<i}\alpha_u\,K_{i,r}, \] \[ Z_r=\sum_{0\le i\le j\le r} b^ic^{r-j}\prod_{u<i}\alpha_u\prod_{j<u\le r}\alpha_u\,K_{i,j}. \] In particular the diagonal \(i=j\) is retained, and \[ \boxed{(-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}} =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M}Z_M.}\tag{3} \] For the full numerator, the original path expansion runs over \(0\le i\le j\le d\). Take \(M=d\) and the empty omitted-half product \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=1\). The same induction gives \((-1)^dH_V=Z_d\), with every unused diagonal factor still present. The half-grid scalar formula in §3 is specific to the half-row restriction. ## 2. Four literal states Equations (2) are the polynomial transfer \[ \begin{pmatrix}B_r\\R_r\\R_{r-1}\\Z_r\end{pmatrix} =T_r\begin{pmatrix}B_{r-1}\\R_{r-1}\\R_{r-2}\\Z_{r-1}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad T_r=\begin{pmatrix} b\alpha_r&0&0&0\\ 1&\beta_rA&\gamma_rP&0\\ 0&1&0&0\\ 1&\beta_rA&\gamma_rP&c\alpha_r \end{pmatrix}. \tag{4} \] The initial vector is \((1,0,0,0)^T\). The direct before-to-after entry \(1\) accounts for starting and ending at the same row. There is no denominator at the initial rows or a sampled spectral zero. The diagonal blocks are the before scalar \(b\alpha_r\), the original active companion \[ C_r=\begin{pmatrix}\beta_rA&\gamma_rP\\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \] and the after scalar \(c\alpha_r\). Reversing the block order makes (4) upper triangular. On a strict compact row and spectral chart its active eigenvalues have limits \[ \Lambda_\pm(t)=2s\left[As\pm \sqrt{s^2(x-y)^2+4xy\cos^2(\pi\delta)}\right], \qquad s=\sin(\pi t). \tag{5} \] For positive \(x,y\), \(0<t<1/2\), and \(0<\delta<1/2\), the positive root is separated from the other root. The latter can vanish at the pole and must not be inverted. On the post-pole side \(\alpha(t)<0\), the after scalar is negative for positive \(c\), so it is separated from \(\Lambda_+\) even where their moduli coincide. The phase change \(c\mapsto-c\) can restore resonance. This identifies a possible input to the [analytic switching theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md). It alone does not prove suppression where a genuine eigenvalue crossing remains, and separation from the secondary eigenvalue must also be checked. ## 3. The omitted-half scalar stays exact For the product convention \(\alpha_r=c_r-\sigma\), \[ A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha= \begin{cases} 2\cos(N\pi\delta),&N\text{ even},\\ -4\sin(\pi\delta)\sin(N\pi\delta),&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases}\tag{6} \] The exact product definition fixes the signs, which would differ in the alternative \(\sigma-c_r\) convention. The odd central factor is included. Neither scalar is assumed nonzero; its oscillatory modes stay in (3). RIGHT follows by the literal original row reflection and middle interchange. A full-source application must still retain the original shared targets, half-twist and framing characters, and Fourier endpoint currents. An absolute-switch maximum with no actual eigenvalue resonance is only a candidate for suppression: a boundary-branch gap and a uniform analytic gauge estimate are additional hypotheses. No global source bound is claimed. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_research_original_four_state_transfer.py) and its [results](../experiments/research_original_four_state_transfer_results.json) check the finite transfer against the independent start/end expansion at both parities and the exact scalar modes: 10 levels, 49 spectral values, 196 transfer/path comparisons and 85 scalar-mode identities. The original matrix interface is inherited from the local numerator formula; these checks are not advertised as a new independent audit of the physical matrix.

title: A positive two-state transfer for the actual spectral tail
status: Exact positive tail transfer; regular local saddle
text: # A positive two-state transfer for the actual spectral tail 31 October 2026. This exact model of the normalized tail includes the negative coefficients of its usual two-term recurrence. It gives compact-interior Perron and outer-angular estimates, not an exponentially accurate interpolation in both endpoint rows or a global sign-cancellation theorem. ## 1. Exact normalization and word expansion Use the original one-sided tail from the [relative-energy theorem](actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.md). For fixed actual rows \(0\le i\le j\), let \(r=j-i\), \(\theta=\pi/N\), and $$ s_a=2\sin(a\theta),\qquad \lambda=\cos\theta+\cos(2\pi\delta),\qquad \eta_a=\frac{\lambda}{\cos\theta-\cos((2a-1)\theta)}. $$ The denominator occurs only at \(a\ge i+2\), so no zero row denominator is used. Put $$ Q_r=\frac{K_{i,j}}{\prod_{a=i+1}^j s_a^2},\qquad Q_0=1,\quad Q_1=x+y,\quad Q_l=(x+y)Q_{l-1}+(\eta_{i+l}-1)xyQ_{l-2}.\tag{1} $$ For \(r\ge1\), initialize \((X_1,Y_1)=(x,y)\), and set $$ \begin{pmatrix}X_l\\Y_l\end{pmatrix} =M_l\begin{pmatrix}X_{l-1}\\Y_{l-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_l=\begin{pmatrix}x&\eta_{i+l}x\\y&y\end{pmatrix}, \qquad 2\le l\le r.\tag{2} $$ Then \(Q_l=X_l+Y_l\) exactly: \(Y_{l-1}=yQ_{l-2}\), and summing (2) gives (1). Equivalently, $$ Q_r=\sum_{w\in\{x,y\}^r}x^{\#x(w)}y^{\#y(w)} \prod_{l=2}^r\eta_{i+l}^{\mathbf1_{\{w_{l-1}=y,\ w_l=x\}}}. \tag{3} $$ The initial state contains no transition weight. The empty word gives \(Q_0=1\). This proof retains every actual row parameter. For real \(\lambda\ge0\), all word weights are nonnegative even if \(\eta_a-1<0\). No claim of positivity is made for the original unused prefix/suffix factors or for negative \(\lambda\) in the final spectral cap. The energy Cauchy theorem treats that cap separately without this positivity. ## 2. Uniform angular contraction in the relative outer phase Suppose every entry of the real matrices (2) lies in \([m,M]\), with \(0<m\le M<\infty\). This holds uniformly when \(x,y\) range in a compact positive set, \(\delta\) stays a fixed distance below \(1/2\), and all rows \((i+l)/N\) stay in a compact subinterval of \((0,1/2)\). For phases \(\vartheta_x,\vartheta_y\), the matrix is obtained by multiplying its two rows by their respective phases. In each entry of a two-step product, the two intermediate states contribute positive weights \(A,B\in[m^2,M^2]\) and relative phase \(\vartheta=\vartheta_x-\vartheta_y\). Therefore $$ \begin{aligned} |Ae^{i\vartheta}+B|^2 &=(A+B)^2-4AB\sin^2(\vartheta/2),\\ \frac{4AB}{(A+B)^2}&\ge(m/M)^4. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ Set \(\kappa=(m/M)^4\). Pair consecutive transfer matrices, apply (4) entrywise, and then multiply nonnegative majorants. The unpaired transfer and initial vector obey ordinary triangle inequalities. This gives the exact bound $$ |Q_r(xe^{i\vartheta_x},ye^{i\vartheta_y})| \le\exp\!\left[-\frac\kappa2 \left\lfloor\frac{r-1}{2}\right\rfloor \sin^2\!\frac{\vartheta_x-\vartheta_y}{2}\right]Q_r(x,y). \tag{5} $$ Thus a macroscopic interval has a uniform exponential outer-angular gap away from equal phases. Equal phases are an essential exception: \(Q_r(e^{i\vartheta}x,e^{i\vartheta}y)=e^{ir\vartheta}Q_r(x,y)\). There is no independent contraction in both frequencies. If either outer weight is zero, the surviving polynomial is a monomial and the relative angular statement is vacuous. At \(\lambda=0\) strict matrix positivity also fails; (5) is not extended there by assumption. ## 3. A compact-interior relative Perron product Fix a compact positive set of outer weights, a compact real spectral set with \(\delta<1/2\), and constants \(\epsilon>0\) such that $$ \epsilon\le i/N<j/N\le1/2-\epsilon,\qquad (j-i)/N\ge\epsilon. \tag{6} $$ For all sufficiently large \(N\), the matrices (2) are uniformly strictly positive, bounded, and vary by \(O(N^{-1})\) per row. Their Perron roots are $$ \rho_l=\frac{x+y+\sqrt{(x-y)^2+4\eta_{i+l}xy}}2.\tag{7} $$ The square root, \(\rho_l\), and the Perron eigenspaces extend analytically to one fixed small complex neighborhood of the compact parameter set. The second eigenvalue may vanish. Nevertheless the discriminant stays nonzero and the modulus of its ratio to \(\rho_l\) is bounded by some \(a<1\), also on a sufficiently small complex neighborhood. No division by the second eigenvalue is used. Choose right and left eigenvectors \(v_l,u_l\), normalized by \(\mathbf1^Tv_l=1\) and \(u_l^Tv_l=1\). With \(z=(x,y)^T\), define $$ A_{i,j,N}=(\mathbf1^Tv_r)(u_2^Tz) \prod_{l=3}^r(u_l^Tv_{l-1}).\tag{8} $$ The empty products retain their usual meanings. Uniformly under (6), $$ Q_r=A_{i,j,N}\prod_{l=2}^r\rho_l\,[1+O(N^{-1})].\tag{9} $$ Here \(A_{i,j,N}\) is a nonvanishing analytic factor bounded above and below uniformly, on a smaller fixed complex neighborhood. Indeed each \(u_l^Tv_{l-1}=1+O(N^{-1})\), while the initial and terminal factors are positive units on the real compact set. For a proof, use the two instantaneous eigenvectors as a moving basis. After dividing each matrix by \(\rho_l\), successive changes of basis have diagonal entries \(1+O(N^{-1})\) and off-diagonal entries \(O(N^{-1})\). The second coordinate contracts by at most \(a+O(N^{-1})\). Its initial contribution feeds the first coordinate by a geometric sum of size \(O(N^{-1})\). Thereafter the generated second coordinate is \(O(N^{-1})\) of the first, so its feedback is \(O(N^{-2})\) per step, with total \(O(N^{-1})\). The terminal second-coordinate error has the same size. The diagonal main factors are exactly those in (8). These estimates also hold uniformly for the complex neighborhood, and Cauchy gives the corresponding fixed-parameter derivative estimates on a smaller neighborhood. The original tail is still \(K_{i,j}=(\prod s_a^2)Q_r\). In the limit \(t=(i+l)/N\), multiplication of (7) by \(4\sin^2(\pi t)\) gives exactly $$ 2\sin(\pi t)\left[(x+y)\sin(\pi t)+ \sqrt{(x-y)^2\sin^2(\pi t)+4xy\cos^2(\pi\delta)}\right],\tag{10} $$ the original sharp weighted tail root. Thus no new scalar normalization or absolute recurrence has entered. ## 4. A regular outer-coefficient saddle In the regime (6), let \(k/r\) stay in a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\), and set \(y=1\). There is a unique positive tilt \(x=e^{\ell_N}\) with $$ \partial_\ell\log Q_r(e^\ell,1)\big|_{\ell_N}=k.\tag{11} $$ These tilts lie in a fixed compact interval. To see this directly from (3), condition on all states except one. The conditional ratio of an \(x\) state to a \(y\) state equals \(e^\ell\) times at most two transition ratios, which are uniformly bounded above and below. Small or large fixed \(\ell\) therefore puts the expected \(x\) fraction uniformly near zero or one. Positivity of every word makes the mean strictly increasing. At compact tilts the variance \(V_N=\partial_\ell^2\log Q_r\) satisfies \(cN\le V_N\le CN\). For the lower bound condition on all odd positions: the even states become independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities bounded away from zero and one. Conditional variance and the law of total variance give a constant times \(r\). For the upper bound and all higher fixed cumulants, (9) provides an analytic logarithm on a uniform complex tilt neighborhood, with derivatives \(O(N)\). Cauchy coefficient extraction, (5), and the Taylor expansion of that analytic logarithm now give $$ [x^ky^{r-k}]Q_r(x,y) =\frac{Q_r(e^{\ell_N},1)e^{-k\ell_N}} {\sqrt{2\pi V_N}}[1+O(N^{-1})].\tag{12} $$ For precision, outside a fixed small angular interval (5) is exponentially small. Inside it, the variance lower bound and bounded higher derivatives give Gaussian decay. On the shrinking central interval the cubic term is odd and imaginary and integrates to zero; the quartic and squared cubic terms contribute relative \(O(N^{-1})\). All constants are uniform on the stated strict compact sets. Formula (12) is a coefficient theorem for the actual tail, not for a separately chosen positive comparison polynomial. ## 5. Original factors and the remaining magnetic problem A complete original one-sided coefficient includes the omitted-half factor, all unused prefix and suffix rows, and \(\prod s_a^2\). They must multiply (9) or (12) exactly. On a strict sign chamber the unused-row signs form the recorded lattice character. The omitted-half factor retains its two oscillatory modes and can vanish densely; it is not a nonzero analytic amplitude that may be divided out on a fixed spectral disk. These results control the outer relative frequency and give a relative \(O(N^{-1})\) regular coefficient approximation. They do not give an exponentially accurate analytic interpolation in \(i/N,j/N,k/N\). The [literal four-state transfer](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) and [analytic switch theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md) now provide a separate route for the middle frequencies: the [regular-window theorem](research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.md) proves exponential loss outside the exact local alignment, retaining both gauge boundary terms and every unused factor. On an inconsistent shared sign system it improves the original Cauchy bound relative to the window envelope. Compatible phase systems, irregular windows and comparison of that envelope with complete volume remain open. Polynomial relative errors or smooth integration by parts alone would not prove that exponential loss. The exact recurrence/source interface is checked by the [finite original-coefficient audit](../experiments/audit_actual_one_sided_relative_spectral_energy.py). The new word, contraction and regular saddle arguments above are analytical; no large-level numerical profile is used as their proof.

title: A complete-angle penalty for a prescribed diagonalization
text: # A complete-angle penalty for a prescribed diagonalization 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. This is a quantitative sufficient condition for a prescribed simple chart. It does not assert that the condition holds for every prescribed chart, or that different diagonalizations define the same filled knot. ## 1. Data and the exact image restriction Fix the original simple spherical MAIN quadrangulation, a prescribed simple diagonalization D, and one retained MAIN mark uv. Every port disk has four distinct cyclic vertices (x,b,y,c). Ordinary vertices retain target one and u,v retain target zero. All norms below count actual triangle-corner incidences, even if two cells have the same vertex labels. Let f be the source-normalized triangle function, with f(0)=f(1/2)=0, f(1/2-t)=f(t), and f''(t)=-2pi/sin(2pi t). The complete entropy is the sum of f over the triangle corners. For a LEFT degree row write (q_x,q_b,q_c,q_y)=(a,b,1-nu,d), nu=a+b+d<=1/2. Here a,b,d are degrees, not face weights. A protected input has its corresponding coordinate fixed to zero. A protected child c gives no such row. The sharp Green value is G=f(a)+f(b)+f(d)-f(nu). Flip xy to bc inside this original disk and use the exact allocation T(a,b,d)=(0,a,1/2-a; b,d,1/2-b-d), (1) in the ordered new triangles (b,x,c),(b,y,c). Its exact entropy gain is C(T)-G=g(a,b,d):=f(a)+f(b+d)+f(nu). (2) Thus the image is not an unrestricted complete angle simplex. In addition to the forced zero at the first b-corner, it satisfies alpha_x<=beta_c, equivalently nu<=1/2. Equation (1) preserves every original vertex load, including the protected zeros. RIGHT is obtained by exchanging the middle labels before applying this formula. These triangle lists specify corner incidence orders, not oriented boundary-chain orders. An orientation-preserving physical flip can use the quartet (b,y,x,c). Its middle-reflected convention (b,x,y,c) has exactly the same full homogeneous Casimir polynomial, by the original middle-reflection identity, as well as the same complete capacity. For a set I of flipped disks, call the resulting triangular cellulation T_I. It may have parallel matching edges. Its complete capacity is Phi_I, with the same fixed mark and original vertex targets. If the complete fiber is empty, no original sector transported into it exists. Otherwise its compact fiber has a unique entropy optimizer theta^I, by strict concavity. In a simple T_I, its ordinary corners are strictly positive, with a supported singleton row having its one entry 1/2. Its capacity is the actual complete polyhedron volume divided by pi. For a nonsimple feasible chart, the complete block-capacity theorem supplies the corresponding sum over simple blocks. ## 2. A closed algebraic local penalty For any complete optimizer theta and any feasible complete flow z, closed strong concavity gives C(z)<=Phi-pi ||z-theta||^2. (3) This is the same normalization as the fixed-triangle boundary lemma; it uses a segment from the optimizer and no boundary derivative. Also the concavity of f(t)-pi*t*(1/2-t), which is zero at both endpoints, gives the closed scalar bound f(t)>=pi*t*(1/2-t). (4) Consider one flipped port of theta^I, and abbreviate its two rows as theta_e=(p_b,p_x,p_c; r_b,r_y,r_c). Both rows sum to 1/2, and their protected entries are zero. Define K=1/2+||theta_e||^2-p_c-r_c, v=(p_x-p_c, r_b-r_c, r_y-r_c), Delta_J={s>=0: sum s=1/2, s_i=0 for protected inputs i}. At least one of the three inputs is ordinary, because the quadrilateral has four distinct vertices, the child is ordinary, and only two vertices are protected. Hence Delta_J is nonempty. Let s*=Proj_(Delta_J)(v), the ordinary Euclidean projection, with protected coordinates fixed zero. Set beta_e(theta_e) =pi min{K, K-1/4+||s*-v||^2-||v||^2}. (5) This is an explicit nonnegative, piecewise quadratic function of the six complete corner loads. The projection requires only the scalar water-filling equation s_i*=max(v_i-tau,0) for allowed i, sum_allowed max(v_i-tau,0)=1/2; the other coordinates are zero. In particular no Green optimization or spectral variable appears in (5). For every closed LEFT row (including pure-child and seam endpoints), pi ||T(a,b,d)-theta_e||^2+g(a,b,d)>=beta_e(theta_e). (6) To verify the constants and the minimization, put s=(a,b,d). The quadratic minorant from (4), divided by pi, is Q_theta(s)=||T(s)-theta_e||^2 +a(1/2-a)+(b+d)(1/2-b-d)+nu(1/2-nu) =K-2 v.s-2(ab+ad+bd). (7) On each ray s=t p, sum p=1 and p>=0, this is concave in t on [0,1/2]. Its minimum is therefore at t=0 or t=1/2, also when only one coordinate is allowed and the expression is affine. The first value is K. At t=1/2, use 2(ab+ad+bd)=1/4-||s||^2; minimization is precisely the projection in (5). This proves (5)--(6) and its nonnegativity without any numerical minimization. If T_I is SIMPLE, beta_e is strictly positive for every allowed child. Indeed Q_theta is a sum of a squared distance and three nonnegative scalar terms. Their simultaneous vanishing forces either nu=0, or nu=1/2 with a=0 or a=1/2. At nu=0 the two transported rows are pure at c, so some other ordinary input corner is zero; such an input exists as noted above. At the seam with a=0 the second c-corner is zero, and with a=1/2 the first c-corner is zero. The child c is ordinary in both cases. None is the strictly positive allowed-corner optimizer of a simple chart. Compactness then proves that the minimum in (5) is strictly positive. This argument retains all protected and singleton rows explicitly. The other exact allocation (assigning the b-load to the first triangle) can be used as well. It gives the same argument after exchanging the two outer labels and the two new triangles. Taking the larger of the two resulting valid lower bounds is permitted. No pointwise choice of face radii or separate optimization of shared loads is involved. ## 3. A prescribed-chart geometric certificate For each nonempty flip set I whose complete fiber is feasible, compute theta^I and Phi_I. For every e in I, evaluate (5) separately for each allowed original overloaded middle. Let beta_(e,I) be the smaller of these values, or the sole value if only one child is allowed. One may use the improved outer-exchanged bound just described on each side. For nonsimple charts these formulas remain nonnegative but need not be strictly positive. It is also valid simply to set their penalties to zero if only their complete block capacities are available. For an original feasible flow whose genuinely overloaded ports are exactly I, use (1) on those ports and optimal complete splits on the remaining CROSS ports. Combining (2), (3), and (6), discarding only the nonnegative squared errors at unflipped ports, gives sum_e barH(q_e)<=Phi_I-sum_(e in I) beta_(e,I). (8) Every shared target in (8) is the original target. In particular this is not an independent maximization of local volume gains. Consequently the finite, entirely complete-geometric condition Phi_D > max_(nonempty feasible I) [Phi_I-sum_(e in I) beta_(e,I)] (9) implies a uniform strict sharp entropy gap on the original closed non-CROSS fiber. A maximum over no feasible flip sets is ignored. Indeed any genuinely overloaded datum has the uniform finite gap in (9). A datum with no genuine overload but in the closed non-CROSS set is a CROSS seam: at least one original middle equals 1/2. The original simple complete optimizer has every ordinary middle strictly below 1/2 and every protected middle zero. Uniqueness and compactness give the separate strict seam gap. Equivalently use the existing explicit seam constant pi*a_D^2/2 in original incidence norm. Combining the two gaps covers pure-child and all seam limits. All complete-capacity-maximizing prescribed charts pass (9): every simple flipped chart has Phi_I<=Phi_D and a positive sum of penalties; every nonsimple one has Phi_I<Phi_D by the last-flip theorem. Since there are finitely many charts, these inequalities give a positive margin. Condition (9) also permits Phi_I>Phi_D, provided its excess is smaller than the explicit boundary penalty. Section 5 gives one exact finite certificate of this phenomenon on an already recorded MAIN quadrangulation. We do not claim (9) for arbitrary prescribed charts. For an actual original source satisfying the simple-white packet/action hypotheses, the exact sharp-G conditional theorem now gives the full original long-filling volume limit under (9). The fixed diagram and half-twist data are retained; all filling parameters are chosen independently, with either sign, sufficiently long and fixed before N tends to infinity. The limiting volume is that of the original filled knot exterior. This uses the exact original numerator and its whole Fourier period, not a quantum equality between flips. ## 4. Why the boundary gain alone is not yet a universal comparison The formula above deliberately keeps a quantitative part of the forced boundary loss. There is a useful check against a hidden old minimax step. When a flipped chart is simple, let L^I be its complete face weights. The exact local Bregman divergence for its two triangle rows satisfies, for the same transport, D_e(T(q),theta_e)+g(q) =Q(b,x,c)+Q(b,y,c)-[G(q)+sum_f q_f log L_f]. (10) Here D_e includes the usual tangent linear term; row constants cancel. It is defined on the supported simplex: protected zero coordinates are omitted from logarithmic terms, and a singleton row has divergence zero. This is an identity, not the squared-distance lower estimate. Taking the local infimum on the closed LEFT simplex yields Q(b,x,c)+Q(b,y,c) -max{log c,Q(x,b,y)+(1/2)log c}. (11) Equation (11) is just the already known anchored LEFT weighted bound, evaluated at the flipped complete vector. Thus discarding the original shared coupling and minimizing each exact Bregman penalty separately does not prove a new universal volume inequality. Condition (9) is a checkable complete-angle sufficient certificate; proving that every prescribed chart satisfies a sufficient global comparison remains a separate task. No isotopy, filling transport, or marked target change is asserted here. ## 5. A certified nonmaximal prescribed chart on one existing graph This is a finite witness for the distinction between (9) and exact capacity maximality, not the proof strategy for arbitrary diagrams.
