Start with the already recorded reduced-width-three source whose literal original quartets are (1,0,4,2), (2,0,5,3), (4,2,6,5), (1,4,0,6), (6,5,0,3), with mark (0,1). Change only the first matching diagonal. The prescribed chart D has, in the middle-reflected incidence convention, quartets (0,1,2,4), (2,0,5,3), (4,2,6,5), (1,4,0,6), (6,5,0,3). For an orientation-preserving disk frame use (0,2,1,4) at the first port instead. The two differ only by the exact middle reflection of the full H_f, so the full source, CROSS degree closure, both one-sided orientations together, and the certificate are unchanged. The audit uses the displayed incidence convention and checks both allowed child sides; it makes no claim of a reflected physical disk isotopy. This is a simple matched sphere on the same five-port MAIN quadrangulation, with all original MAIN edges and the same marked pair. The new general Morse realization supplies its own actual augmented link. No flat-plat realization or isotopy with the old link is asserted. Its ordinary complete weights, ordered 2,...,6, are (1,1,3-2sqrt(2),4-2sqrt(2),3-2sqrt(2)). The independent flip set is encoded by a five-bit integer relative to THIS prescribed chart. There are eighteen simple choices, with the following exact ordinary complete weights; all other choices are nonsimple. This is the entire finite list, not a search over new knots. mask weights on vertices 2,3,4,5,6 0 1,1,3-2sqrt(2),4-2sqrt(2),3-2sqrt(2) 1 1,(3+sqrt(5))/2,(3+sqrt(5))/2,2+sqrt(5),1 2 1,1,1/9,4/9,1/9 3 1,3+2sqrt(2),2,2,1 4 1,9/4,1/4,7,1/4 5 1,4,4,12,1 6 1,4,1/4,9/4,1/4 7 1,9,4,4,1 9 1,3+2sqrt(2),1,4+2sqrt(2),3+2sqrt(2) 11 1,25,1,4,9 13 1,9,1,28,4 15 1,25,1,9,4 16 1,25/9,1/9,4/9,1/9 17 1,3+2sqrt(2),2,2,1 20 1,25/4,1/4,9/4,1/4 21 1,9,4,4,1 25 1,9,1,4,9 29 1,16,1,9,4. Here is a complete finite certificate method. For each triangle put T=sqrt(L_i L_j+L_i L_k+L_j L_k) and theta_i=atan(L_i/T)/pi, with exact zero and singleton conventions. For each of the ninety ordinary vertex equations, exact algebra proves product_(triangles containing f) (T+iL_f)/(T-iL_f)=1. An enclosing interval for the sum of its positive angles lies between 0.99 and 1.01. Thus its normalized sum is exactly one, not merely close to one. The local triangle sums are 1/2. The positive-weight triangle Legendre identity and these exact demands prove that the displayed angle flow is the unique complete optimizer. This uses no numerical root solving or assumption that a rounded critical point is exact. For a nonsimple choice, the audit enumerates all ordinary subsets S. Whenever exactly 2|S| triangle rows touch S, their total supply equals the entire demand of S. Consequently all their corners outside S are zero in every feasible flow. Intersect these exact forced supports. If n_t allowed corners remain in row t, concavity gives the capacity upper bound sum_t n_t f(1/(2n_t)). All fourteen nonsimple choices have such a bound less than 4.18. An infeasible fiber would be harmless; the bounds do not assert its feasibility or a new block decomposition. For the simple choices, (5) can be certified without choosing the exact active set of its projection. For ANY rational tau, completion of the square in the simplex Lagrangian gives min_(s in Delta_J) [||s||^2-2v.s] >= -tau-sum_(i allowed) max(v_i-tau,0)^2. (12) Use (12) in (5), and the better of the two outer allocations on each allowed child side. The audit supplies rational tau witnesses and encloses every resulting bound; correctness does not depend on their being minimizers. All entropy values are enclosed by the finite Fourier sum for the Lobachevsky function, with M=8192 and the explicit tail 1/(2M) per Lobachevsky term. Thus each f value has error at most 1/(pi M). The remaining operations use Arb at 192 bits, including square roots, arctangents, positive parts, minima, maxima, and the quadratic bounds. The author exact/interval replay gives 4.99985 < Phi_D < 5.00142, Phi_(mask 1)-Phi_D > 0.17855, min_(all 31 nonempty flip choices) [Phi_D-Phi_I+sum_e beta_(e,I)] > 0.01342 > 0.01. (13) For the nonsimple choices, replace Phi_I by the proved support upper bound and use zero penalties. Their certificate margins exceed 0.8. The second inequality in (13) proves that the prescribed chart is NOT capacity-maximizing. The third proves (9), with a uniform flip margin 0.01. Seam-only data retain the separate original seam gap. This proves a strict extension beyond the maximal-diagonalization hypothesis for prescribed matched charts, with the accompanying finite certificate. It does not claim that the resulting unmarked knot family is outside every older balance, sector, or differently presented family. Its actual long filled-knot conclusion uses the same source-realization and analytic inputs as section 3, with its own original half-twist pattern and framing normalization. The [portable exact/interval certificate](../experiments/research_audit_prescribed_diagonal_flip_penalty.py) and [its saved output](../experiments/research_prescribed_diagonal_flip_penalty_results.json) retain the full finite witness and its scope. The earlier floating diagnostic was used only to suggest these fixed algebraic weights. It is not invoked by the finite certificate or (13). ## Dependencies and status The geometric inputs are the [exact flip transport and nonsimple last-flip theorem](research_maximal_diagonalization_source_gap.md), [closed strong concavity](actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md), and [complete capacities with strict supported positivity on simple spheres](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md). The local source and original full-period consequence use the [sharp Green maximum and its conditional filling theorem](research_sharp_green_spectral_maximum.md). For the new actual prescribed chart, the [general Morse realization](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) and [CROSS action/packet adapter](research_general_morse_cross_action.md) provide the source and geometric inputs; the new non-CROSS gap restores the full source just as in the [integrated augmentation theorem](general_maximal_diagonal_augmentation_volume.md). The middle-reflection convention is the exact local source identity in [the diagonal-flip polarization theorem](research_diagonal_flip_quantum_polarization.md), section 9. The old five-port chart and its literal flat source are recorded in the [anchored shared-radius theorem](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md), sections 4--5. The quartet table is an incidence convention. Its exact middle reflection distinguishes it from the orientation-preserving physical frame, as explained above. The certificate covers exactly one existing five-face MAIN quadrangulation, its 32 diagonalizations, 18 algebraic complete charts with 90 exact ordinary-face equations, 14 nonsimple tight-Hall support bounds, and all 31 nonempty flip tests. It certifies a prescribed-chart extension beyond exact capacity maximality. It does not establish a universal prescribed-chart inequality or novelty of the unmarked knot families relative to every earlier presentation or criterion.

title: Regular stop-window exclusion with a protected input middle
status: Fixed-start protected-middle phase gap and exact reflection
text:
# Regular stop-window exclusion with a protected input middle 31 October 2026. **research local theorem.** This keeps the original specialization \(b=0\) exactly, hence the start row is \(i=0\). It assumes a strict regular maximum only for the stop. There is no regular start maximum, inverse zero-face weight, or inverse initial-row gauge. The conclusion is a phase loss relative to the original window envelope, not a comparison with complete volume. The reflected protected-output case is proved by an exact finite row reflection in §6. No double-zero specialization is included. ## 1. The exact fixed-start source Use \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(	heta=\pi/N\), \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\), and \[ s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\quad \alpha_r=2\cos((2r+1)	heta)-\sigma,\quad  eta_r=s_r^2,\quad \gamma_r=s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1}. \] Let \(A=x+y\), \(P=xy\), and retain the original continuant \[ K_{0,0}=1,\quad K_{0,1}= eta_1A,\qquad K_{0,r}= eta_rA K_{0,r-1}+\gamma_rP K_{0,r-2}. 	ag{1} \] The [literal source expansion](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) has the factor \(b^i\). Since every exponent is nonnegative, specializing \(b=0\) selects exactly \(i=0\): \[ (-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}}(x,0,c,y) =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha \sum_{j=0}^{M}c^{d-j} \prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r\,K_{0,j}(x,y), \quad M=\lfloor N/2floor-1,\quad A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=M+1}^{d}\alpha_r. 	ag{2} \] For the full numerator use \(M=d\), the empty omitted product, and \(H_V\) instead of \(H_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}}\). The start-at-zero diagonal term \(j=0\) is present in (2). It lies outside the regular stop window considered below; it has not been discarded from the full source. Let \(I=[
u_-,
u_+]\Subset(0,1)\) be a fixed stop window. In the half-row case take \(I\Subset(0,1/2)\). Write \(q_-\le j\le q_+\) for all integers in \(NI\). Restrict the sum in (2) to these rows and call the resulting raw polynomial \(W_N\). Let \(E_N\) be the same sum with positive face moduli and absolute values of every unused scalar factor. Throughout, \(x_0,y_0,c_0\) range over a fixed positive compact set, and \(\delta\) over a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). The window stays away from the two zeros \(1/2\pm\delta\) of \[ \alpha(t)=4[\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)]. \] All compactness assumptions are uniform on the chosen parameter chart. ## 2. An exact positive seed, including the initial singular rows For \(r\ge2\), put \[ \eta_r=1+ rac{\alpha_{r-1}}{s_rs_{r-1}} = rac{\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta)} {\cos	heta-\cos((2r-1)	heta)},\qquad M_r= egin{pmatrix}x&\eta_rx\y&y\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{3} \] For all sufficiently large \(N\), every \(\eta_r\), \(2\le r\le d\), is positive. They need not be uniformly bounded near the initial row. The following identities use them exactly: \[  egin{aligned} Z_1&= eta_1(x,y)^T,\ Z_r&= eta_rM_rZ_{r-1},\qquad r\ge2,\ Z_r&=G_r(K_{0,r},K_{0,r-1})^T,\qquad G_r= egin{pmatrix}1&- eta_ry\0& eta_ry\end{pmatrix},\ \mathbf1^TZ_r&=K_{0,r}. \end{aligned}	ag{4} \] At \(r=1\), (4) follows from \(K_{0,1}= eta_1(x+y)\). Thereafter it is the exact gauge identity \(G_rC_rG_{r-1}^{-1}= eta_rM_r\), where \[ C_r= egin{pmatrix} eta_r(x+y)&\gamma_rxy\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \] No \(G_0^{-1}\) occurs. Equivalently, (4) is the exact positive word expansion beginning with \((x,y)\), rather than an invented initial asymptotic amplitude. At complex face phases, entrywise absolute values satisfy \[ |Z_r(x_0e^{i\vartheta_x},y_0e^{i\vartheta_y})| \le Z_r(x_0,y_0). 	ag{5} \] This uses only positivity of the exact \(\eta_r\), not a bound on their size. In particular \(|K_{0,r}(x,y)|\le K_{0,r}(x_0,y_0)\). On any regular row interval, both \(G_r,G_r^{-1}\) are bounded, so the norm of the original active state is bounded by a constant times the positive \(K_{0,r}\). The same holds after further active propagation: it is still the exact state in (4), with the full initial seed retained. Choose once a macroscopic bulk interval strictly between \(0\) and the left endpoint of \(I\). On this interval the entries of \(M_r\) lie in one fixed positive compact set. Apply the [two-step word contraction](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) only there, and ordinary entrywise majorants before and after it. For any fixed separation of the outer relative phase, \[ |K_{0,j}(x,y)|\le e^{-\kappa_1N}K_{0,j}(x_0,y_0) \quad	ext{for every }j\in NI. 	ag{6} \] The early unbounded \(\eta_r\)'s introduce no loss: they occur identically in the positive majorant. Summation proves the window estimate in this outer-mismatch case. ## 3. Stop-action differences do not require a start-rate formula The limiting positive active root is \[ \Lambda_+(t)=2\sin(\pi t) \left[(x_0+y_0)\sin(\pi t) +\sqrt{(x_0-y_0)^2\sin^2(\pi t) +4x_0y_0\cos^2(\pi\delta)}ight], \quad L_\delta(t)=\Lambda_+(t)/|\alpha(t)|. 	ag{7} \] Choose a reference point \(
u_0\in I\) and define the stop primitive \[ F_{\mathrm{stop}}(
u) =(1-
u)\log c_0+\int_{

u_*\), with a fixed positive gap to both window boundaries. This is the only endpoint-maximum hypothesis. Here is a uniform relative estimate valid for the exact initial seed. Let \(u_r>0\) be positive left Perron vectors of \(M_r(x_0,y_0)\), chosen smoothly and with a fixed normalization on a regular neighborhood of \(I\), and let \(ho_r\) be their Perron roots. Their components are bounded above and below, and \(u_r/u_{r-1}=1+O(N^{-1})\) componentwise. Since the state \(Z_{r-1}\) is positive, (4) gives \[ u_r^TZ_r= eta_rho_r u_r^TZ_{r-1}. \] Comparing \(u_r^TZ_{r-1}\) with \(u_{r-1}^TZ_{r-1}\) and multiplying over any subinterval of that neighborhood yields \[ \log rac{K_{0,j}(x_0,y_0)}{K_{0,q}(x_0,y_0)} =\sum_{r=q+1}^{j}\log( eta_rho_r)+O(1). 	ag{9} \] For \(j<q\) use the reversed scalar ratio. The error is uniform for all such rows and all \(N\), independent of the magnitude or direction of the earlier positive seed. No matrix inverse or secondary-root inverse is used. Smooth Riemann comparison replaces the sum by \(N\int_{q/N}^{j/N}\log\Lambda_+(t)\,dt+O(1)\). Factor out the unused product above \(q_+\) and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\) exactly. If this common product vanishes, both \(W_N\) and \(E_N\) vanish. Otherwise, for positive summands \(T_j=c_0^{d-j}\prod_{j<r\le M}|\alpha_r|\,K_{0,j}(x_0,y_0)\), their nonzero ratios obey \[ \log(T_j/T_q) =N[F_{\mathrm{stop}}(j/N)-F_{\mathrm{stop}}(q/N)]+O(1). 	ag{10} \] Only the varying unused factors in the pole-free stop window enter this estimate. Thus each boundary summand is exponentially below the positive window sum. No absolute estimate for a potentially tiny common scalar, no regular starting row, and no start saddle has been assumed. ## 4. Only the stop switch is gauged Put \(A_{q_--1}=(K_{0,q_--1},K_{0,q_--2})^T\) and use the exact stop matrices \[ T_r^{\mathrm{stop}} = egin{pmatrix}c\alpha_r&w_r\0&C_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad w_r=e_1^TC_r=( eta_r(x+y),\gamma_rxy). 	ag{11} \] If \(V_N\) is the off-diagonal block of their ordered product over \(q_-\le r\le q_+\), the original window is exactly \[ W_N=(-1)^dA_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M} \left(\prod_{q_+<r\le M}c\alpha_right) V_N A_{q_--1}. 	ag{12} \] The stop at \(j\) includes \(C_j\), giving \(K_{0,j}\), not a shifted continuant. Equation (12) contains the complete original seed at row zero. Let \(s_
u=\arg\alpha(
u_*)\in\{0,\pi\}\). The supported alignment is \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_y=\vartheta_c+s_
u \pmod{2\pi}. 	ag{13} \] There is no phase for \(b=0\). At the maximum of (8), \(c_0|\alpha(
u_*)|=\Lambda_+(
u_*)\). The positive root is strictly larger in modulus than the secondary root on the strict compact chart. Shrink the window, retaining its interior maximum and boundary gap, so that \(c_0|\alpha(t)|\) stays strictly above that secondary modulus throughout it. Away from (13), either the outer relative phase has a fixed separation, already covered by (6), or it is small and the scalar phase \(\vartheta_c+s_
u\) is separated from the common outer phase. At exactly equal outer phases a constant unitary diagonal change of basis makes \(C_r\) that common phase times its real companion. The scalar therefore misses the Perron root by phase and the secondary root by modulus. A sufficiently small outer-phase perturbation preserves this full Sylvester separation. Analyticity in the scaled row variable extends it to one fixed complex neighborhood of the stop window. Apply the [analytic switch theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md) only to (11). It retains \[ V_N=H_{\mathrm{end}}(C_{q_+}\cdots C_{q_-}) -\left(\prod_{r=q_-}^{q_+}c\alpha_right)H_{\mathrm{start}} +\sum_j\left(\prod_{r=j+1}^{q_+}c\alpha_right) R_j(C_{j-1}\cdots C_{q_-}), \quad \|R_j\|\le Ce^{-\kappa_2N}. 	ag{14} \] Multiply each term by the actual seed in (12). Equation (5), the regular \(G\)-bounds, and (4) bound the first endpoint by a constant times \(K_{0,q_+}(x_0,y_0)\), and the second by a constant times \(K_{0,q_--1}(x_0,y_0)\), with their exact after-products. These are the two stop-boundary summands, within one mesh step. Their fixed loss follows from (10). For a residual insertion at \(j\), the same argument bounds its active input by \(CK_{0,j-1}(x_0,y_0)\). On the stop window the ratio \(K_{0,j}/K_{0,j-1}\) is bounded above and below by positive constants, directly from the positive matrix update in (4). Hence the residual is bounded by \(Ce^{-\kappa_2N}\) times the original positive stop summand at \(j\). There are only \(O(N)\) insertions. Both boundary terms and the residual are thus exponentially below the positive window envelope. Restoring all exact common factors gives, for every fixed distance \(\varepsilon>0\) from (13), \[  oxed{|W_N|\le C e^{-\kappa N}E_N.}	ag{15} \] Constants are uniform on the stated compact chart. Sampled zeros in common unused factors and either parity's raw prefactor remain exact. ## 5. The protected target and supported incidence graph The original \(b\)-face target is zero. Nonnegative polynomial exponents make the substitution \(b=0\) exactly its constant-term restriction, also when that face occurs at other ports. No new integration variable or phase is assigned to it. These ports supply the same two local inequalities used by the [cycle-packing criterion](research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md): the unconditional positive-envelope bound and (15). Use the three supported incidences \((x,y,c)\), with labels \((0,0,s_
u/\pi)\). All repeated incidences, shared ordinary radii, original targets, and external source characters remain as in that criterion. The local result itself gives no comparison with \(\Phi_D\). ## 6. Exact reflection and the protected output For every finite level and every spectral value, \[ \alpha_{d-r}=\alpha_r,\qquad  eta_{N-r}= eta_r,\qquad K_{i,j}(x,y)=K_{d-j,d-i}(x,y). 	ag{16} \] For the last identity reverse a monomer/dimer tiling of the interval \(i+1,\ldots,j\). A monomer at \(r\), of weight \( eta_r(x+y)\), goes to \(N-r\). A dimer ending at \(r\), of weight \(s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1}xy\), goes to one ending at \(N+1-r\); its weight is unchanged because \(s_{N-r}=s_r\) and \(\alpha_{N-r}=\alpha_{r-1}\). The reversed interval is \(d-j+1,\ldots,d-i\). This proves (16), including empty intervals, without a physical-turn or unrecorded duality. In the full original path expansion, the substitution \[ (i,j,b,c)\longmapsto(d-j,d-i,c,b) \] preserves every monomial, unused row factor and the raw sign. This is an internal local polynomial identity, not a relabeling of shared source faces. Hence the \(c=0\) specialization, which forces \(j=d\), is the exact reflection of the \(b=0\) specialization. A regular start window reflects to a regular stop window, with the explicit mesh shift \(j'/N=1-N^{-1}-i/N\). Such an \(O(N^{-1})\) boundary shift is covered by the same boundary-gap and one-row comparisons above. The genuine RIGHT half-row sector has \(i\ge\lceil N/2ceil\). Under reflection this is precisely \(j'\le\lfloor N/2floor-1=M\), at both parities. Thus (15) applies to protected-output FULL and RIGHT windows, with supported alignment \(\vartheta_x=\vartheta_y=\vartheta_b+\arg\alpha(\mu_*)\). The output-zero incidence is absent. This is an exact source reflection, not an assertion that a general turned operator is multiplicative. Both outer weights must remain positive, and the other middle must remain positive. No double-zero extension, irregular stop/start maximum, spectral cap, or pole-touching window is included. The theorem controls these specified source windows only; global window coverage and the complete-volume comparison remain separate. The conclusion retains every strict-window and positive-supported-weight hypothesis stated above.

title: Regular-window phase exclusion with one protected outer face
text:
# Regular-window phase exclusion with one protected outer face 31 October 2026. **research local theorem.** This is the exact scalar-active extension of the [regular-window phase theorem](research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.md). It treats \(y=0\) and \(x,b,c
e0\), with their moduli uniformly positive. It does not cover a zero middle weight or two zero outer weights. Its conclusion is relative to the original positive window envelope, not a comparison with hyperbolic volume. ## 1. The literal protected specialization has three states Use \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\), and \[ \alpha_r=2\cos rac{(2r+1)\pi}{N}-\sigma, \qquad  eta_r=4\sin^2 rac{\pi r}{N},\qquad a_r= eta_rx. 	ag{1} \] Setting the original outer variable \(y\) equal to zero removes exactly the dimer terms of the original continuant. Thus, for every \(i\le j\), \[ K_{i,j}(x,0)=x^{j-i}\prod_{r=i+1}^{j} eta_r, \qquad K_{i,i}=1. 	ag{2} \] This is a polynomial specialization, not a limiting estimate involving an inverse power of \(y\). Set \((B_{-1},R_{-1},Z_{-1})=(1,0,0)\). The exact recurrence is \[  egin{aligned} B_r&=b\alpha_rB_{r-1},\ R_r&=B_{r-1}+a_rR_{r-1},\ Z_r&=R_r+c\alpha_rZ_{r-1}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] Equivalently, \[  egin{pmatrix}B_r\R_r\Z_r\end{pmatrix} = egin{pmatrix} b\alpha_r&0&0\1&a_r&0\1&a_r&c\alpha_r \end{pmatrix}  egin{pmatrix}B_{r-1}\R_{r-1}\Z_{r-1}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{4} \] The direct before-to-after entry \(1\) retains the path \(i=j\). Induction gives \[ Z_M=\sum_{0\le i\le j\le M} b^ic^{M-j}\prod_{r<i}\alpha_r\prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r K_{i,j}(x,0). 	ag{5} \] For the original LEFT half-row source take \(M=\lfloor N/2floor-1\) and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=M+1}^{d}\alpha_r\). The raw source is \[ (-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}}(x,b,c,0) =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M}Z_M. 	ag{6} \] For the full numerator take \(M=d\) and the empty omitted product: \((-1)^dH_V(x,b,c,0)=Z_d\). These are the same source normalization and sign as in the [four-state identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md). All omitted-half modes and sampled zeros remain exact. ## 2. Strict regular windows and their three-phase alignment Let \(x_0,b_0,c_0\) range over a fixed positive compact set and \(\delta\) over a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). Put \[ \alpha(t)=4[\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)],\qquad L_\delta(t)= rac{4x_0\sin^2(\pi t)}{|\alpha(t)|}. \] Choose fixed disjoint row windows \(I_\mu<I_
u\) inside \((0,1)\), both staying away from \(1/2\pm\delta\). In the half-row case they lie inside \((0,1/2)\). Assume \[ F(\mu,
u)=\mu\log b_0+(1-
u)\log c_0 +\int_{\mu}^{
u}\log L_\delta(t)\,dt, 	ag{7} \] has a uniformly strict interior maximum \((\mu_*,
u_*)\) on those windows. The logarithmic poles in the integral are interpreted integrably. The maximum stays a fixed distance from each boundary, and the boundary values of each separated endpoint action have a fixed strict loss. This last formulation makes the required uniformity explicit. Restrict (5) to all integers \(i\in NI_\mu\), \(j\in NI_
u\), and multiply by the exact prefactor in (6). Call the resulting raw polynomial \(W_N\). Let \(E_N\) be the same window sum using \(x_0,b_0,c_0\), absolute values of unused \(\alpha\)'s and of the omitted product, and the positive monomer product (2). The windows are disjoint, so the diagonal path is outside this restricted piece, while (4) retains it in the full source. Write \(x=x_0e^{i\vartheta_x}\), and similarly for \(b,c\). Define \[ s_\mu=\arg\alpha(\mu_*),\qquad s_
u=\arg\alpha(
u_*),\qquad s_\mu,s_
u\in\{0,\pi\}. \] The exact local alignment is \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_b+s_\mu =\vartheta_c+s_
u\pmod{2\pi}. 	ag{8} \] There is no phase assigned to the zero variable \(y\). In a LEFT straddling window \(s_\mu=0\), \(s_
u=\pi\), so (8) is \(\vartheta_x=\vartheta_b=\vartheta_c-\pi\). For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), there are uniform \(C,\kappa>0\) and \(N_0\) such that \[  oxed{|W_N|\le Ce^{-\kappa N}E_N}	ag{9} \] whenever the supported phase triple stays at least \(\varepsilon\) from (8). The distance can be the minimum over the common phase of the maximum of the three circular errors, or the equivalent maximum of the two relative-phase errors. ## 3. Exact start and stop switches Write \(p_-\le i\le p_+<q_-\le j\le q_+\) for the integer windows. The start and stop matrices are the scalar-block matrices \[ T_r^{\mathrm{start}}=  egin{pmatrix}a_r&1\0&b\alpha_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad T_r^{\mathrm{stop}}=  egin{pmatrix}c\alpha_r&a_r\0&a_r\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{10} \] Let \(U_N,V_N\) be their respective off-diagonal product entries. Then \[  egin{aligned} W_N={}&(-1)^dA_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M} \left(\prod_{q_+<r\le M}c\alpha_right)V_N \left(\prod_{p_+<r<q_-}a_right)U_N \left(\prod_{r<p_-}b\alpha_right). \end{aligned}	ag{11} \] A start at \(i\) inserts \(1\), and the stop at \(j\) includes the active step \(a_j\). Thus (11) contains exactly (2), not a shifted path. There is no extra factor of \(N\) or auxiliary normalization. ## 4. Scalar separation and both boundary terms If (8) fails by a fixed amount, at least one supported middle phase mismatches \(\vartheta_x\) by a fixed amount. On its window, \(a_r\) and the relevant middle scalar have strictly positive moduli bounded above and below. For two such moduli \(u,v\ge m_*>0\), \[ |ue^{i\phi}-ve^{i\psi}| \ge2m_*\left|\sin rac{\phi-\psi}{2}ight|. 	ag{12} \] The exact coefficients are analytic in the scaled row variable, with \[ \alpha_h(t)=4\cos^2(\pi(t+h/2))-4\sin^2(\pi\delta), \qquad a(t)=4x\sin^2(\pi t),\qquad h=N^{-1}. \] The scalar gap (12) therefore extends to a fixed complex neighborhood of the selected window, uniformly for large \(N\). This is the full Sylvester hypothesis in the [analytic switching theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md). No secondary eigenvalue, positive two-state gauge or outer-relative-phase estimate is involved. Apply that theorem to the mismatched matrix in (10). Keep both pure endpoint terms and the residual switch sum. The residual coupling is \(O(e^{-cN})\); it remains multiplied by the original scalar products. Here those active products concatenate exactly: \[ K_{v,w}(x,0)K_{u,v}(x,0)=K_{u,w}(x,0). 	ag{13} \] Their absolute values are exactly the corresponding positive products. To compare with \(E_N\), first factor out all common unused products outside the two windows. These may include sampled zeros in the full-row case, and the omitted-half product may also vanish. If a common factor vanishes, both sides of (9) vanish. Otherwise the same estimate applies to the remaining variable products, with no bound on an inverse common factor. The variable \(\alpha\)'s stay away from zero, while \( eta\) stays positive on the active compact interval. Their logarithmic Riemann sums give uniform rate differences equal to the differences of (7), with \(O(\log N)\) errors. Each gauge endpoint term places the relevant start or stop at a window boundary, up to one mesh step. Strict endpoint maximality and separation of the two endpoint actions give a fixed exponential loss relative to the positive interior window sum. Both endpoint terms are retained. For the residual, (13) reassembles the active products exactly; the one-row factors and their reciprocals on the selected windows are uniformly bounded. Each insertion is therefore bounded by its \(e^{-cN}\) residual factor times a constant multiple of an original positive switch summand, up to one mesh shift. Summing polynomially many locations costs only a polynomial factor. Absorb it in a smaller exponential constant and restore all common factors. This proves (9). ## 5. Protected targets and the shared phase graph In the original marked coefficient the protected face has target zero. All polynomial exponents are nonnegative, so specializing that variable to zero is exactly the required constant-term restriction. No phase or Cauchy integration variable is supplied for that face. Consequently these ports may be combined with the four-positive ports in the [cycle-packing criterion](research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md). Use just the three supported incidences \((x,b,c)\), with labels \((0,s_\mu/\pi,s_
u/\pi)\). The local loss and the unconditional positive-envelope bound have exactly the forms needed there. The circular telescoping, fractional packing and original shared-target Cauchy arguments are unchanged. The case \(x=0\), \(y,b,c
e0\), follows by exchanging the two outer variables in the literal recurrence. Neither case permits a forced zero middle, two zero outers, a boundary maximum or a window touching a pole. No universal packing capacity, envelope margin or filled-volume theorem is inferred from this extension. The finite dictionary is an algebraic specialization of the already four-state and restricted-window identities, whose existing audits include a zero outer weight. The exponential estimate above is analytical; no additional finite-level test is claimed as its proof.

title: What a regular original shared stationary point actually implies
text: # What a regular original shared stationary point actually implies Unpublished workspace research reduction, 31 October 2026. This audits the hypotheses of the conditional signed-circle/group/fan theorem. No strong duality, concavity in the two rows, or separate weighted local maximality is assumed. The result is a first-order reduction on specified smooth strata of the original shared incidence problem, at every fixed width. ## 1. The exact functional being differentiated For a LEFT port write its original limiting degrees, in order (x,b,c,y), q=(xi,mu,1-nu,nu-mu-xi), 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu. (1) Let alpha_delta(t)=4[cos^2(pi delta)-sin^2(pi t)] and Lambda_delta(t;x,y) be the positive root of the original cleared tail recurrence. Define B_delta(mu,nu)=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta| dt +int_nu^(1/2) log|alpha_delta| dt, Phi_delta(mu,nu,l)=int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1) dt, h_delta=B_delta+inf_l[Phi_delta-xi l]. (2) This keeps BOTH unused intervals. The omitted-half scalar has zero exponential upper modulus, but its actual two phases are not discarded when reconstructing the source. Formula (2) is the sharp interval Legendre functional, not the fractional comparison t C(alpha). The fractional obstruction specifically prevents replacing (2) by that latter concave perspective and borrowing its duality. The [global closed-domain coefficient-majorant theorem](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) now proves a uniform coefficient LIMSUP upper bound for the original full-interval functional at both parities, including all closed degree boundaries, the final spectral cap and sampled zeros. The [regular theorem](research_sharp_regular_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) identifies (2) and its CROSS split with that full-interval functional. Thus the reduction applies to regular extrema of a proved compact original-source upper problem. An every-level remote coefficient limit or nonzero prefactor is NOT needed for this upper-bound route. No lower asymptotic or equality of a signed central sum with its upper rate is asserted. Uniform coefficient coverage does not imply regularity or geometric realizability of a boundary maximizer. On a strict ordinary chart, 0<mu<nu<1/2, 0<xi<nu-mu, 0<delta<1/2, and neither row equals t_c=1/2-delta. The minimizing tilt in (2) is unique and finite. Indeed, put eta=cos^2(pi delta)/sin^2(pi t)>0. Apart from a t-only constant, log Lambda(t;exp(l),1) =l/2+log[cosh(l/2)+sqrt(sinh^2(l/2)+eta)], partial_l^2 log Lambda =eta cosh(l/2)/[4(sinh^2(l/2)+eta)^(3/2)]>0. (3) Its first derivative ranges from 0 to 1. Thus Phi_ll>0 and its first derivative ranges from 0 to nu-mu, proving existence, uniqueness and smoothness of the tilt. The moving alpha zero has an integrable log; as long as neither endpoint meets it, B is smooth by its explicit logarithmic antiderivative. No convexity in mu or nu follows from (3). ## 2. Linear-target stationarity, without strong duality Use one original row supply1 and each original ordinary face target1; protected incidences have target0 and are removed, not regularized. For CROSS retain its two half-row allocations as separate local variables. Fix a smooth branch stratum in which every remaining local inequality is strict, apart from the explicitly forced protected zeros. At a relative-interior constrained local extremum of sum_e h_e, its differential annihilates the kernel of the LINEAR target map. Elementary finite-dimensional row-space orthogonality therefore gives face multipliers lambda_f, regardless of redundant target equations. All these multipliers are finite real numbers on this smooth finite- dimensional stratum, so L_f=exp(-lambda_f)>0 automatically. Then EACH local Lagrangian h_e+sum_(f at e) q_(e,f) log L_f (4) is STATIONARY in all its free local variables, with the same L_f at every occurrence of f. This is not an assertion that (4) is maximal over its full local polytope. A finite positive multiplier vector also does not imply that every local inequality is inactive; the preceding relative-interior hypothesis is substantive. At an ordinary LEFT port, xi stationarity and (3) give l=log(x/y), where x,y,b,c now denote these common positive weights. After this equality, (4) is exactly F=mu log b+(1-nu)log c+int_mu^nu log L_delta(t;x,y) dt, L_delta=Lambda_delta/|alpha_delta|. (5) The identity int_0^(1/2)log|alpha_delta|=0 is used only here, after retaining the actual outside products. The free row equations are L_delta(mu)=b, L_delta(nu)=c. (6) Since delta_e is independent of every shared target constraint, its first derivative at an interior spectral extremum is zero. This derivative is taken at FIXED (mu,nu,xi) in (2), before applying the tilt/envelope cancellation. At a solution of (6) it equals the partial_delta of (5). It is not differentiation along an already imposed equation c=b+(x+y)/sin^2(pi delta). ## 3. Classification of strict LEFT/RIGHT critical rows Write A=x+y, P=xy, z=sin^2(pi delta), D=A^2-4Pz. The proved L_delta is increasing before t_c and decreasing after t_c, from infinity down to L_end=(A+sqrt D)/(2z). For a pre-pole stationary row q>0 use E_q=A+2qz+2sqrt(z)*sqrt(qA+P+q^2z), Q_q'=-log(E_q/sqrt D). For a strict post-pole stationary row q>L_end use H_q=2qz-A+2sqrt(z)*sqrt(q^2z-qA+P), J_q'=-log(H_q/sqrt D). (7) These are the absolutely normalized primitives of the original cofactor. Both derivatives follow from the retained outside integrals; no maximum property of the chosen row is used to differentiate its stationary branch. There are three possibilities for mu<nu: * Pre/pre: (6) gives b<c. The weighted stationary action is Q_b-Q_c+log c, so its spectral derivative is log(E_c/E_b)>0. * Post/post: (6) gives b>c>L_end. The action is J_b-J_c+log c, and its spectral derivative is log(H_c/H_b)<0. * Pre/post: the action is Q_b-J_c+log c. Spectral stationarity is H_c=E_b. The two numbers are larger roots with the SAME product D, and their half-sums are A+2bz and 2cz-A. Strict monotonicity of that larger root gives exactly (c-b)z=A, R0=-E_b/H_c=-1. (8) Thus a strict interior free-spectral LEFT critical point MUST be the calibrated straddling branch. At this point the second row derivatives of (5) are -partial_t log L(mu)<0 and partial_t log L(nu)<0; the endpoint dependence is separable. The strict start/stop maxima at FIXED delta therefore follow from (6)--(8), rather than being assumed from the shared maximum. This checks the endpoint hypothesis of the regular switching-window theorem on compact subcharts. It does NOT make (5) a local maximum in delta: after following both stationary rows with fixed weights, this branch has a spectral minimum. Indeed sign(log(H_c/E_b))=sign((c-b)z-A) by the same larger-root comparison, and c>b at (8); as delta increases this changes from negative to positive. That row-following variation generally changes the original shared face loads and is not an admissible variation of the constrained problem. It cannot exclude a shared maximum. RIGHT is the exact original row reversal, exchanging b and c and the overloaded end. ## 4. CROSS and the exact protected exceptions A regular CROSS allocation has two actual half-cofactor rows, ending at 1/2, and their retained outer split. Its split stationarity gives the same shared tilt; each free starting row solves L_delta(mu)=q. Without assuming either start to be a weighted maximum, its branch is Q_q if pre-pole and J_q if post-pole. Every one of QQ,QJ,JQ,JJ therefore has strictly NEGATIVE free spectral derivative when all displayed weights are positive, by (7). A regular CROSS port cannot have 0<delta<1/2 at a free spectral critical point. Its remaining regular possibility is the complete boundary delta=0; delta=1/2 and terminal/pole rows remain separate boundary strata. Protected cases are specialized in the literal source BEFORE a tilt: * A protected LEFT overloaded c makes the whole finite sector zero. * If x=0 or y=0, the tail is its exact one-monomer product. Its outer degree is forced, so no finite log(x/y) tilt is used. Equations (5)--(8) still follow for the FREE rows by that monomer action, with P=0. These are the one-outer-line fan cases. * If b=0 with x,y>0, the start is exactly mu=0. Its sole-start primitive is Q_0, with E_0=A+2sqrt(zP). A pre-pole free stop c>0 has log(E_c/E_0)>0. A post-pole free stop is critical precisely when H_c=E_0, giving c=A/z. This is the middle-line case. * If b=0 and one outer is also protected, then P=0 and E_0=A=sqrt D. A strict pre-pole stop has E_c>A, and a strict post-pole stop has H_c>A. Its spectral derivative is positive in either case. Consequently there is NO free 0<delta<1/2 Green critical point with this double zero and nu<1/2. Equality forces the terminal nu=1/2, which is not covered by the regular argument. For a CROSS half with protected middle, use Q_0. Its derivative is negative if both outers are positive; it is zero only if the half is a genuine one-positive-weight monomial. In the actual simple-white plat an outer MATCHING pair cannot be the two protected MAIN faces. There are only two protected faces, and the four port labels are distinct. Thus BOTH CROSS halves cannot be monomial simultaneously: if one outer is protected, both would additionally need both middles protected. At least one half has strict loss. Hence the preceding CROSS exclusion survives every allowed protected pattern, provided its other local rows/splits are regular. No finite cross endpoint with a forbidden zero outer unit is silently inserted. At delta=0 a centralizer eigenratio tending to1 does NOT imply C=I: the outer product is parabolic and the collar's removable divided difference retains a nonzero limit. No kernel or identity assertion is made from that ratio. The existing endpoint entropy/chain theory is the relevant separate input there. ## 4a. A one-sided nonterminal maximum cannot have delta=0 There is a stronger statement for MAXIMA, without any local weighted maximum assertion. Fix any 0<=mu<nu<1/2 and any allowed closed outer degree 0<=xi<=nu-mu. Put z=sin^2(pi delta) and restrict 0<z<cos^2(pi nu), so the entire fixed interval remains pre-pole. At any positive outer weights, q=L_delta(t) is the positive solution of sin^2(pi t)=(1-z)q^2/(q^2+Aq+P). Differentiating gives partial_z log L_delta(t) =(q^2+Aq+P)/[(1-z)(Aq+2P)] >=1/[2(1-z)]. (8a) The inequality is exactly 2q^2+Aq>=0. It is UNIFORM in the outer tilt, not a claim restricted to the minimizing tilt. Integrating first in z and then in t yields int_mu^nu log L_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt >=int_mu^nu log L_0(t;exp(l),1)dt -(nu-mu)/2 log(1-z). Since the total half-alpha integral is zero, (2) is the infimum of these integrals minus xi l. Taking that infimum preserves the same uniform additive gain: h_delta(mu,nu,xi) >=h_0(mu,nu,xi)-(nu-mu)/2 log(1-z)>h_0. (8b) At mu=0 the logarithmic endpoint is integrable and (8a) is used on (0,nu] before taking its integral limit. At xi=0 or nu-mu the same tilt-uniform inequality applies to the limiting infimum. Alternatively the literal one-outer monomer has L=A sin^2(pi t)/(cos^2(pi t)-z), whose logarithmic z derivative is 1/(cos^2(pi t)-z)>0. Thus neither protected starts nor a closed outer-degree endpoint invalidate (8b). Changing only this port's delta leaves EVERY original face degree and target fixed. Consequently a maximum of the stated sharp shared functional cannot have a positive-length, nonterminal LEFT/RIGHT port at delta=0. Diagonal length0 and terminal nu=1/2 are deliberately excluded. For a fully regular maximum away from delta=1/2, every one-sided port is therefore a strict positive-spectral straddler, whereas every regular CROSS port is complete. Mixed endpoint Green ports are needed for general stationary data, but not for this regular MAXIMUM reduction. ## 5. Original face angles and the integer overload At any stationary local branch just classified, the ordinary weight derivatives of its stationary action are its original degrees q. This is the ordinary envelope rule at a stationary branch, not a strong-duality assertion. The physical triangle derivative gives alpha_(t,f)=theta_(t,f)/(2pi), with each triangle load sum1/2. The signed continuation retains the original output character: CROSS: q=alpha_input+alpha_output, LEFT: q=alpha_input-alpha_output+e_c, RIGHT: q=-alpha_input+alpha_output+e_b. (9) The signs and integer terms come from the actual local primitive, including Log c (respectively Log b), and its prescribed continued root. They are not the fractional t alpha loads of an envelope. At a protected line its alpha corner is exactly zero, by the literal line limit, so its zero target remains unchanged. Summing (9) at each original ordinary face yields exactly sum_(t incident f) sigma_t theta_(t,f) =2pi(1-o_f), (10) where o_f is the INTEGER number of incident LEFT/RIGHT overloaded middles. Every strict one-sided overload has q_f>1/2, so the target1 allows at most one, while a protected target0 allows none. Thus o_f in {0,1} on this regular stratum. Equation (10) is an automatic consequence of the original targets and first-order equations, with no independent maximization or source factorization. ## 6. Dependency audit: what is proved, what still is not For the smooth stratum described here, first-order shared stationarity automatically supplies common finite positive weights, all row and tilt equations, the straddling signed primitive and R0=-1 at every positive-spectral one-sided port, complete spectral parameters at every regular CROSS port, the literal allowed single-line adapters, and the integer face-angle equations (10). Global uniform coefficient-majorant coverage is now proved separately on the entire closed domain; neither that upper theorem nor an unnecessary remote coefficient LIMIT is a remaining hypothesis here. The following issues remain: 1. Relative-interior regularity: finite positive ordinary multipliers do not remove ordinary zero incidences, diagonal/terminal rows, spectral endpoints, or active structural flow facets. The separate [pole-endpoint exclusion](research_sharp_interval_pole_endpoint_exclusion.md) removes positive-length endpoint/pole contacts from genuine maxima, without asserting that every other boundary is regular. 2. The shared Z/2 face-character solution. The actual incidence signs must still satisfy epsilon_(e,f)=gamma_f+kappa_e on the original allowed incidence graph. The real target equations (10) do not impose these mod2 cycle conditions. 3. A proof that inconsistent-phase cancellation beats Phi. Its positive envelope may exceed Phi, so a relative exponential loss is not by itself the desired absolute comparison. Once the shared sign cocycle in2 is supplied on the stated regular real branches, the signed developing-disk/group dictionary uses (10) and the literal original marks to construct the comparison representation. Its original cup/cap/prefix and raw-line checks are still REQUIRED, but are supplied by that lemma rather than by an unproved new contributing-mode assertion. The new direct-fan theorem then supplies canonical volume and a uniform fixed peripheral-word gap on its stated regular branch list. Neither theorem needs local weighted strong duality. If some remaining ports instead lie at noncross delta=0, their correct endpoint tangent adapters must also be retained; one must not replace their collars by identity. Here is the explicit mixed endpoint adapter. At a tangent delta=0 Green port the frozen original reflection calculation gives C=I+i r(P+I), r=(eta_c T_c-eta_b T_b)/(2(x+y)) real, including its one-line and two-line formulas. Normalize the common tangent point to infinity and its two outer white planes to Re w=0,1. Their original raw product is P=-[[1,2],[0,1]]. Therefore C acts by w->w-2ir, preserving BOTH outer planes. The proved simultaneous head conjugations then carry the middle plane and all three ordered contacts. This establishes the same within-copy shaded pairing as the positive-spectral half-turn, with no inference from eigenratio1. Its entire peripheral image is parabolic and preserves the common horosphere. The old tangent signed local fan identity and new intersecting fan identity may therefore be summed in ONE developed family and the SAME original two-ball fundamental chain. At least one positive-spectral strict Green port still gives the fixed trace-zero meridian and uniform gap. If all spectral coordinates are0, use the existing endpoint noncross-mass gap, not a new trace-zero claim. The retained omitted-half modes give U0=+/-pi i at (8), not zero. Their corresponding central eigenvalue choices +/-i give the SAME order-two PSL collar. Reversing its selected eigenline also leaves that PSL collar unchanged. The compact-peripheral canonical volume is independent of which fixed endpoint is used, by the proved horosphere-to-axis contraction. Thus the real comparison does not require selecting a complex contributing mode or proving a nonzero intersection with the original Fourier cycle. Those questions belong to a lower-bound/contribution theorem, not this conditional upper bound. No retained finite scalar or original framing is being deleted; their convention is distinguished from a claimed contributing saddle. No arbitrary KKT datum is asserted to be a limit of these coherent regular solutions. This first-order classification removes a genuine local-maximality assumption but does not close the remaining global phase and compact-boundary problems. ## Dependencies and verification scope The original finite rows and retained scalars are in the [four-state source identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md). The weighted primitives and their derivative constants are in the [LEFT envelope proof](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md). The [fractional obstruction](research_fractional_one_sided_geometry_obstruction.md) is why no perspective concavity or local strong-duality claim is imported. The remaining [face-sign criterion](research_spectral_face_sign_cocycle.md), [regular group sewing](research_regular_signed_spectral_group_sewing.md), and [direct-fan fundamental chain](research_critical_circle_fan_fundamental_chain.md) retain the original source and canonical volume conventions. The tangent endpoint matrix is the literal formula in [marked signed development](actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md). The global coefficient-majorant theorem supplies only its stated upper bound. These reductions do not supply a lower coefficient limit, an incompatible-phase comparison with complete volume, or regularity and geometric control of every compact-boundary maximum.

title: Regular signed spectral circle development and original group sewing
text: # Regular signed spectral circle development and original group sewing 31 October 2026. This is a conditional group lemma on the regular stratum. It does not identify the globally sewn regulator with the sharp absolute rate and does not cover every compact maximum. ## 1. Exact hypotheses and the proposed conclusion Keep the actual labeled simple-white sphere of an original certified flat plat, its port matching, and its original adjacent protected MAIN faces u,v. At every ordinary face give a finite magnitude L_f>0. At the two protected faces keep the exact zero targets. Suppose the following data have genuinely been obtained from the selected local source phases: 1. The local incidence characters have a common solution epsilon_(e,f)=gamma_f+kappa_e. The signed ordinary clocks are (-1)^gamma_f L_f; no independent clock is used at another occurrence of f. Exact row scalars and the original framing remain recorded. 2. Every port has one of the calibrated two-triangle action branches: CROSS Q_b+Q_c, LEFT Q_b-Q_c+Log c, or the reflected RIGHT branch, with its actual spectral scalar modes retained. For a strict post-pole endpoint the signed triangle is the one proved in research_signed_straddling_green_relation.md. Each finite triangle lies on a REAL, nondegenerate circle branch described below. 3. All original ordinary face stationary equations hold. If sigma_t is the sign of a triangle in its local action and o_f is its overloaded-middle count, those equations are exactly sum_(t incident f) sigma_t theta_(t,f) =2pi(1-o_f). (1) Here theta_(t,f) is the ACTUAL center angle, with the prescribed oriented triangle branch. Protected incidences have zero load. No alternative target or quotient mark is used. 4. The two forced marked corners use the literal line adapters of research_signed_spectral_line_flags.md. No other ordinary circle collapses, no adjacent finite centers coincide, and no free row, pole, diagonal or spectral endpoint is being passed through. Then the proposed conclusion is that these data develop to ONE set of white circle/line reflections and their literal primitive collars, and hence to a representation of the original drilled group. The following proof explains why no convex embedding is needed and where the marked flags enter. It does not assert that hypotheses1--4 hold at an arbitrary maximum of an absolute envelope. ## 2. The real local metrics and their force angles An ordinary face has signed radius r_f=(-1)^gamma_f/L_f and geometric radius |r_f|. At a MAIN edge the center distance is |r_f+r_g|; equal signs give external tangency and opposite signs give internal tangency. On a matching edge with spectral parameter delta, the center distance squared is r_f²+r_g²+2r_f r_g cos(2pi delta). (2) The incidence character has zero outer entries. Hence the two finite outers have equal gamma, so (2) is a real circle intersection metric on the prescribed branch. To check the actual angle, normalize one port by its common row sign so x,y>0. Its middle is either q>0 with T_q>0 or a post-pole q=-c<-L_end with T_q<0. The latter satisfies c>max(x,y); its internal tangent distances are positive and nonzero. With D=(x+y)²-4xy sin²(pi delta), the law of cosines gives cos theta_y= [y(x-y)+q(x+y cos(2pi delta))]/[(y+q)sqrt D], sin theta_y= 2y cos(pi delta) T_q/[(y+q)sqrt D], (3) and exp(-i theta_q)=(T_q-iq cos(pi delta))/ (T_q+iq cos(pi delta)). (4) These are exactly the exponentiated source forces from the local generating relation. The signed q<0 does not invalidate the law of cosines: (q+y)/(qy)>0 is its actual internal-tangent distance. In the selected branch all three angles lie in (0,pi) and sum to pi. The input/output signs sigma_t in (1) orient their placement relative to the original white triangle order. At a line corner the same assertions use the explicit finite line matrices, not an inference from a vanished scalar root. The two finite angles use the directed normal of the cooriented line as the infinite center direction. Their sum is pi. At a two-line corner the finite angle is pi and both line angles are zero. Thus each local triangle is a rigid configuration up to an orientation-preserving Euclidean motion, including its coorientations and selected matching intersection flag. Adjacent triangles have the same actual edge data because every ordinary signed clock is shared. They need not place their disks disjointly. ## 3. Edge gluing, including the protected-line signs Along a finite/finite edge its two distinct ordered centers determine the Euclidean gluing. Along a MAIN line/finite edge the tangent line and the finite center determine it. Along a MATCHING line/finite edge the selected J intersection point is retained as well. This matters at cos(2pi delta)=0, when the finite center lies on the line: the selected intersection fixes the remaining possible half-turn. There is also a lift check. Normalize the reflection of each finite circle by its global signed curvature, the real lower-left entry of its determinant-minus-one matrix. An orientation-preserving Euclidean coordinate change preserves this normalization. Across a MAIN line/finite edge both local raw products have trace-2. Once the finite reflection is matched, the opposite central sign for the line would give trace+2, so it is excluded. Across a MATCHING edge the two triangles are the halves of the SAME original port; their common ordered product and selected J flag already fix the same line reflection, also at trace0. Thus the edge gluings propagate actual line reflections, not an unrecorded independent sign at each occurrence of a protected face. No positive sign is arbitrarily assigned to a zero clock. The marked line/line edge uv is unique in the original simple sphere. It will be a boundary edge in the developing disk and is never used as an underdetermined interior gluing. ## 4. The disk holonomy and the same two marked lines Remove one of the two triangles incident to uv. The remaining sphere is a triangulated disk, with u,v on its boundary. The other uv triangle supplies the initial two distinct parallel lines and its finite circle, using the exact two-line adapter. A marked triangle cannot be a negative Green triangle: one of its middle faces is protected, whereas a negative triangle would overload that face. Develop every local triangle by the unique edge gluing above. Around an interior finite vertex, the holonomy fixes its center. Its rotation is the signed center-angle sum (1), hence an integral multiple of2pi. The Euclidean holonomy is therefore identity, including its translation part. This remains true for a vertex incident to a marked line: the directed line normals are part of the same local angle data. Cycles of the disk dual are generated by these finite-vertex stars. Consequently development is independent of path. Both marked vertices are boundary vertices; no translation loop around an infinite vertex has been silently assumed trivial. Each boundary line fan is connected, so it propagates the SAME line reflection. The last finite vertex belongs to one developed circle and has its two prescribed incidences to those same lines. The selected line flags and coorientation, not an arbitrary choice of a parallel translate, determine its local two-line configuration. It therefore closes the omitted uv triangle. In particular the last corner must satisfy the exact height relation H=2cos²(pi delta)/L in its local normalized two-line chart; it is not an extra free strip parameter. Here is the raw-lift calculation that makes this last assertion explicit. Normalize the propagated lines by J_u=-iI and J_v=[[i,-2H],[0,i]], H>0, and write the last finite circle's signed curvature as q and center as X+iY. Its actual MATCHING product with u has trace -2qY=-2cos(2pi delta), while its MAIN product with v has trace 2q(Y-H)=-2. Subtraction gives qH=1+cos(2pi delta)=2cos²(pi delta). Thus q>0 and H=2cos²(pi delta)/q exactly. The retained selected J flag fixes the remaining ordered branch. Merely two unoriented incidences would not have supplied this conclusion. The result may overlap, contain internally tangent circles or have zero winding at an overloaded vertex. None of those properties invalidates the original reflection assignment. ## 5. Original Morse and peripheral relations Assign one resulting reflection to each original white face. At each matching port use its original ordered main heads A,B and product P=BA. The signed local action and line adapters prove that its primitive C transports BOTH heads and the chosen third spectral flag. It is therefore the actual three-point shaded pairing, not only a matrix with an appropriate trace. The original main prefix products telescope. The original cups and caps supply their based inverse pairs, with the same unrestricted mark. At each auxiliary circle the literal threading/Hurwitz word uses the recorded physical lift of C^(-1) and returns both heads. These are the actual Morse presentation relations used by the previous complete and signed-endpoint assembly. They are algebraic relations of the one reflection family; no embeddedness of its developed image is required. Thus the proposed regular data give an actual drilled-group representation. Its primitive peripheral ratio is the local one, including R0=-E_b/H_c on a straddling chart. The source scalar mode fixes the additive log branch; the retained half-twist uses the recorded change U_epsilon=U_0-epsilon V/2 exactly once. ## 6. The still-separate regulator and source questions This argument is deliberately GROUP-only. Matching white circles now intersect and the selected ideal flag is one of two intersection points; the endpoint tangent-face volume formula cannot simply be reused. The original two cut balls still provide a candidate abstract chain with their ordered contact polygons and shaded pairings, but its absolute Bloch-Wigner value must be compared to the actual signed spectral action, including the peripheral correction. Neither an arbitrary local Gauss-reference change nor agreement of action differentials proves that comparison. Likewise this regular lemma does not supply a sign-cocycle solution at every absolute maximum, a relative asymptotic for every remote coefficient, or a boundary reduction for escaping ordinary multipliers and free KKT strata. Those are necessary before it could yield a general quantum upper bound. The conditional group argument and exact two-line closure do not supply the source hypotheses or the separate regulator comparison.

# Phase exclusion for an original regular spectral window 31 October 2026. The straddling-window theorem in §§1–6 estimates a literal start/end window, retaining every unused row, omitted-half mode and raw sign. Its conclusion is an exponential loss relative to that window’s positive envelope, not a bound by hyperbolic volume. Sections 7–8 give the full-row extension and shared-torus consequence. ## 1. Literal window and hypotheses Put \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), \(M=m-1\), \(	heta=\pi/N\), \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\), and \[ \alpha_r=2\cos((2r+1)	heta)-\sigma,\qquad  eta_r=s_r^2,\quad \gamma_r=s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1}, \quad s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\qquad A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=m}^{d}\alpha_r. \] The active companion and its tail are \[ C_r= egin{pmatrix} eta_r(x+y)&\gamma_rxy\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad K_{i,j}=e_1^TC_j\cdots C_{i+1}e_1, \quad K_{i,i}=1.	ag{1} \] All face moduli \(x_0,y_0,b_0,c_0\) are strictly positive and range over a fixed compact set. The real spectral coordinate ranges over a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). Write \[  egin{aligned} \alpha(t)&=4[\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)],\ \Lambda_+(t)&=2\sin(\pi t)\left[(x_0+y_0)\sin(\pi t) +\sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)(x_0-y_0)^2+4x_0y_0\cos^2(\pi\delta)}ight],\ L_\delta(t)&=\Lambda_+(t)/|\alpha(t)|. \end{aligned} \] Assume the original positive weighted endpoint action \[ F(\mu,
u)=\mu\log b_0+(1-
u)\log c_0 +\int_{\mu}^{
u}\log L_\delta(t)\,dt, 	ag{2} \] has uniformly strict interior endpoint maxima \(\mu_*<t_c<
u_*\), where \(t_c=1/2-\delta\). The logarithmic pole in (2) is integrable. Choose disjoint closed row windows \(I_\mu,I_
u\Subset(0,1/2)\), away from \(t_c\), whose maxima are uniformly interior. Work on one compact parameter chart with fixed windows; a finite collection covers a compact family. The action separates into a function of the start and a function of the stop. Strict maximality therefore gives a fixed loss at either boundary of either window, uniformly in the other endpoint. Shrink the windows further so that the middle modulus \(b_0|\alpha(t)|\), respectively \(c_0|\alpha(t)|\), stays strictly above the active secondary eigenvalue's modulus. This is possible: at the maximum it equals \(\Lambda_+\), while \(|\Lambda_-|<\Lambda_+\) uniformly on the compact chart. Let \(i\) and \(j\) run over all integers in \(NI_\mu\) and \(NI_
u\). The exact raw window is \[ W_N=(-1)^dA_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\sum_{i,j} b^ic^{d-j}\prod_{r<i}\alpha_r\prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r K_{i,j}(x,y),	ag{3} \] where \(x=x_0e^{i\vartheta_x}\), and similarly for \(y,b,c\). Define \(E_N\) by taking the face moduli in each summand, the absolute values of both unused products and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\), and the positive tail \(K_{i,j}(x_0,y_0)\). This is the original positive window envelope. No division by \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\) is used. For each \(\varepsilon>0\), there are uniform constants \(c,C>0\) and \(N_0\) such that \[  oxed{|W_N|\le Ce^{-cN}E_N}	ag{4} \] whenever the phase quadruple is at distance at least \(\varepsilon\), modulo \(2\pi\), from \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_y=\vartheta_b=\vartheta_c-\pi. 	ag{5} \] One can use the maximum of these three relative phase distances. If the omitted-half scalar is zero, both sides of (4) are zero exactly. ## 2. Every active subproduct has a positive comparison Set \[ \eta_r=1+ rac{\alpha_{r-1}}{s_rs_{r-1}},\qquad G_r= egin{pmatrix}1&- eta_ry\0& eta_ry\end{pmatrix}. \] On the present row range, \(G_r\) and its inverse are uniformly bounded. Direct multiplication gives the exact identity \[ G_rC_rG_{r-1}^{-1} = eta_r egin{pmatrix}x&\eta_rx\y&y\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{6} \] The real \(\eta_r\) are bounded above and below by positive constants. The absolute entries on the right of (6), at arbitrary outer phases, are exactly their positive-modulus entries. Products inherit this bound. Moreover, the two columns of a nonempty positive product are uniformly comparable: compare the columns in its rightmost factor, then multiply on the left by positive matrices. Since \(G_ue_1=e_1\) and \(e_1^TG_v^{-1}=(1,1)\), the positive \(K_{u,v}\) is the product of the \( eta\)'s times the first-column sum of the positive word product. Column comparability and bounded gauge endpoints consequently give, for every active subinterval, \[ \|C_v(x,y)\cdots C_{u+1}(x,y)\| \le C_0K_{u,v}(x_0,y_0).	ag{7} \] The empty product uses \(K_{u,u}=1\). This does not replace the signed companion recurrence by its entrywise absolute value. Split products can also be reassembled at bounded cost. For consecutive positive word products \(P_1,P_2\), column comparability gives \[ (\mathbf1^TP_2e_1)(\mathbf1^TP_1e_1) \le C_1\mathbf1^TP_2P_1e_1. \] The empty cases are immediate. Restoring the \( eta\) factors yields \[ K_{v,w}(x_0,y_0)K_{u,v}(x_0,y_0) \le C_1K_{u,w}(x_0,y_0),\qquad u\le v\le w. 	ag{8} \] This is used for a fixed number of consecutive pieces, not with a fixed loss multiplied over \(O(N)\) pieces. The [exact positive-word angular estimate](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) implies \[ |K_{i,j}(x,y)|\le e^{-c_1N}K_{i,j}(x_0,y_0)	ag{9} \] when the outer relative phase is separated from zero. Each selected interval has macroscopic length. Summing (9) termwise proves (4) in this case, retaining all scalar factors and their zeros. ## 3. The two restricted switches are literal finite matrices Write \(p_-\le i\le p_+\), \(q_-\le j\le q_+\) for the integer windows, with \(p_+<q_-\). On the start window use \[ T_r^{\mathrm{start}}=  egin{pmatrix}C_r&u\0&b\alpha_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad u=e_1.	ag{10} \] Let \(U_N\) be its product's \(2\)-by-\(1\) off-diagonal block. On the stop window use \[ T_r^{\mathrm{stop}}=  egin{pmatrix}c\alpha_r&w_r\0&C_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad w_r=e_1^TC_r=( eta_r(x+y),\gamma_rxy). 	ag{11} \] Let \(V_N\) be its product's \(1\)-by-\(2\) off-diagonal block. Then \[  egin{aligned} W_N={}&(-1)^d A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M} \left(\prod_{q_+<r\le M}c\alpha_right) V_N(C_{q_--1}\cdots C_{p_++1})U_N \left(\prod_{r<p_-}b\alpha_right). \end{aligned}	ag{12} \] Empty products are identities. A start at \(i\) supplies the seed \(e_1\); a stop at \(j\) reads \(e_1^T\) after \(C_j\) acts. Thus its active factor is precisely (1). The disjoint windows exclude \(i=j\) because that path is outside their specified support. The [unrestricted four-state identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) retains that diagonal path. Formula (12) introduces no pivot, factor of \(N\), or source renormalization. ## 4. A mismatched middle separates the whole active block It remains to consider small outer relative phase. Remove the common outer phase \(\vartheta_o=\vartheta_y\). At exactly equal outer phases, a constant unitary diagonal change of basis makes the active companion \(e^{i\vartheta_o}\) times its real companion. Both active eigenvalues have this common phase relative to their real, signed values. On the start window \(\alpha>0\), so the scalar phase is \(\vartheta_b\). A mismatch from \(\vartheta_o\) separates it from the Perron eigenvalue; the window's modulus condition separates it from the secondary eigenvalue for every phase. On the stop window \(\alpha<0\), the scalar phase is \(\vartheta_c+\pi\), and the same argument applies. If the quadruple stays away from (5), either (9) applies or at least one of these middle mismatches stays uniformly nonzero. Taking the outer-phase threshold sufficiently small preserves the full Sylvester separation. The exact coefficients are analytic in \(t\) and \(h=1/N\): \[  egin{aligned} \alpha_h(t)&=4\cos^2(\pi(t+h/2))-4\sin^2(\pi\delta),\  eta(t)&=4\sin^2(\pi t),\ \gamma_h(t)&=4\sin(\pi t)\sin(\pi(t-h))\alpha_h(t-h). \end{aligned}	ag{13} \] The uniform real separation extends to a fixed complex neighborhood of the relevant window. The bounded analytic Sylvester inverse there checks all hypotheses of the [analytic discrete-switch theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md). There is no guessed interpolation of the discrete start or stop. Apply that theorem to (10) or (11), whichever has the mismatch. Its exact off-diagonal product consists of two pure endpoint terms and a sum with an exponentially small residual coupling. The scalar blocks remain \(b\alpha_r\) or \(c\alpha_r\). They do not occur in the same Sylvester equation, so no separation between them is required. ## 5. Both endpoints and the residual return to the original envelope Let \(T_{ij}\) be the positive summand of (3) without the common \(|A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha|\). The compact positive-transfer Perron bounds and the unused-interval Riemann products give uniformly \[ \log T_{ij}=NF(i/N,j/N)+O(\log N),\qquad \sum_{i,j}T_{ij}=\exp\{NF(\mu_*,
u_*)+O(\log N)\}. 	ag{14} \] The unused intervals stay away from the pole. The active interval crosses it, but the positive word matrix remains regular. The identity \(\int_0^{1/2}\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt=0\) is used only to rewrite the already bounded products into (2); it creates no finite division at a sampled zero. Use (7) to bound complex active subproducts and (8) to reassemble a fixed number of pieces into the original unsplit \(K_{i,j}\). Bounded gauge vectors can replace the endpoint \(e_1\)'s at bounded cost. Each of the two pure gauge terms fixes the relevant switch at a window boundary, within one mesh step, while all other starts or stops and exterior factors remain unchanged. Strict maximality and separability of (2) therefore give \[ 	ext{each endpoint term} \le \operatorname{poly}(N) \exp\{N[F(\mu_*,
u_*)-\gamma]\},\qquad \gamma>0. 	ag{15} \] Both terms are kept. Neither is assumed absent. For a residual insertion, (7)–(8) and bounded one-row couplings compare its weight with a constant times the original positive summand at that row, up to one mesh shift. The unused \(\alpha\)'s on the two windows are bounded away from zero, so these shifts cost bounded factors. Only polynomially many locations are summed. Thus \[ 	ext{residual contribution} \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{-c_2N}\sum_{i,j}T_{ij}. 	ag{16} \] Together (14)–(16) prove (4). Multiply the common omitted-half scalar back exactly, including its zeros; no nonvanishing scalar amplitude is asserted. ## 6. Limits of the local conclusion The proof requires positive ordinary face moduli and strict regular endpoint maxima. It does not cover spectral caps, row-endpoint or pole-touching windows, or a maximum on its window boundary. One zero outer weight reduces the active recurrence to first order and admits a scalar version under the same strict-window assumptions, but that case is not used here. A protected middle needs a different start specification. Incompatible local phase requirements may permit (4) at one port of a shared torus. They do not by themselves compare the resulting envelope with complete volume or show that these windows cover the full source. ## 7. Full-row regular windows The polynomial identity extends to the full numerator by taking \(M=d\) and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=1\) in (3) and (12). It is the same original path sum over \(0\le i\le j\le d\), with all outside diagonal factors retained. For \(2\le r\le d\), \[ \eta_r=  rac{\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta)} {\cos	heta-\cos((2r-1)	heta)}>0 	ag{17} \] for all sufficiently large \(N\) on the fixed interior spectral chart. On compact row intervals inside \((0,1)\), it is uniformly positive and bounded. Hence (6)–(9) apply unchanged. The limiting formulas for \(\alpha,\Lambda_+\) and \(L_\delta\) also hold throughout \((0,1)\). Choose two disjoint fixed windows inside \((0,1)\), staying away from the two zeros \(1/2\pm\delta\) of \(\alpha\). Assume (2) has strict interior maxima in those windows, and shrink them to satisfy the same secondary-modulus separation. The proof of (4) is then unchanged, with alignment \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_y =\vartheta_b+\arg\alpha(\mu_*) =\vartheta_c+\arg\alpha(
u_*), \qquad \arg\alpha\in\{0,\pi\}. 	ag{18} \] The signs are constant on the selected windows for large \(N\). The rate differences in (14) are still given by (2), with the continuous normalization \(\int_0^1\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt=0\). No absolute rate formula for a possibly zero common scalar factor is needed. The before and after unused intervals may contain a pole when a full-row window lies beyond it. Such a factor is common to every selected term; factor it out exactly before applying the estimates. Only the varying parts on the two windows need the smooth Riemann-product bounds. More explicitly, factoring the products below the first window and above the second window leaves (12), whose variable scalar products stay in the pole-free windows. The active middle interval is controlled by (6). The boundary gaps are differences of (2), so any factored common scalar has no effect. Its zeros again make both sides zero. This proves the full-row version with no assumed nonzero sampled factors. It covers the usual regular sign pairs \((+,+)\), \((+,-)\), and \((-,+)\) when the corresponding strict-window hypotheses hold; no classification of all critical or boundary configurations is required. The [finite window audit](../experiments/audit_research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.py) and its [recorded output](../experiments/research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion_results.json) check 402 exact half-row and full-row matrix/path identities, including sampled spectral zeros and zero outer weights. This checks the finite dictionary, not the analytical exponential estimate or a new physical-matrix interface. ## 8. An exact shared-torus consequence Fix the original incidence graph and protected-face specialization. Let \(J\) be a finite set of ports satisfying the full-row or half-row window theorem above, with all four incident weights positive. Other ports may have any certified absolute torus majorants \(M_{e,N}(L)\). Use one shared positive radius \(L_f\) for each ordinary face and the original coefficient target \(d\) there; protected variables remain zero. For each regular port impose (18) on its incident face phases. These are equations of the form \(\vartheta_f-\vartheta_g=0\) or \(\pi\). They have a simultaneous torus solution exactly when their signed incidence graph has even label sum around every cycle. Thus an inconsistent \(\mathbb F_2\) system has no torus solution. Compactness of the phase torus supplies \(\varepsilon>0\) such that at every phase point some port in \(J\) is at least \(\varepsilon\) from its alignment locus. Apply (4) at that port and the ordinary positive-envelope bound at all other selected ports. The original Cauchy coefficient formula gives \[ \left|[	ext{original targets}] \prod_{e\in J}W_{e,N}\prod_{e
otin J}P_{e,N}ight| \le Ce^{-cN}  rac{\displaystyle\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\displaystyle\prod_{f	ext{ ordinary}}L_f^d}. 	ag{19} \] There is no independent choice of radii at each incidence and no alteration of the original target. The homogeneous common phase is harmless. Any external source characters must be retained separately in their original normalization. Formula (19) is an exponential improvement on the specified shared window envelope, uniform for a fixed diagram and compact regular parameters. It does not show that this envelope is at most \(e^{N\Phi_D}\), exclude consistent phase systems, or control the omitted irregular windows.

title: Fractional odd-cycle packing for the original regular-window source
status: Fractional odd-cycle loss; conditional shared-source rate
text:
# Fractional odd-cycle packing for the original regular-window source This regular cycle-packing lemma has local hypotheses. It gives neither a covering statement nor equality of volume and source rates. ## 1. Original face phases and certified local losses Keep one positive radius \(L_f\) and one phase \(\vartheta_f\) per original ordinary face, with the unchanged target exponent \(t_f(N)\). For the original homogeneous source this is \(d=N-1\). Protected variables are specialized to zero as in that source. Let \(J\) consist of selected original ports whose literal start/stop windows satisfy either the four-positive regular-window theorem or the [one-protected-outer theorem](research_protected_outer_window_phase_exclusion.md). In the latter case exactly one outer weight is zero and the other three incident weights are positive. Write \(W_{e,N}\) for the actual window polynomial and \(E_{e,N}(L)\) for its positive envelope. Every unused row, scalar zero and raw sign stays in these definitions. At other ports use certified phase-uniform majorants \(M_{e,N}(L)\) for their actual factors. Index the supported incidences at a port separately, even if they meet the same face. A protected zero incidence is omitted and has no phase variable. The required alignment has the form \[ \vartheta_{f(a)}=\varphi_e+\pi\epsilon_a\pmod{2\pi}, \qquad a	ext{ incident to }e,\quad \epsilon_a\in\mathbb F_2, 	ag{1} \] with a free common phase \(\varphi_e\). A straddling LEFT window has labels \((0,0,1,0)\) in the order \((x,b,c,y)\); full-row windows use the actual signs at their two endpoints. In a one-protected-outer window delete the zero incidence from this list; the remaining three labels are exactly those in its scalar-active theorem. Let \(|\cdot|_{\mathbb T}\) be circular distance modulo \(2\pi\), and set \[ d_e(\vartheta)=\min_{\varphi\in\mathbb T} \max_{a	ext{ at }e} |\vartheta_{f(a)}-\varphi-\pi\epsilon_a|_{\mathbb T}. 	ag{2} \] The minimum exists by compactness. This is precisely distance from the local alignment in the product supremum metric. To compare with the relative-phase version of the local theorem, fix one incidence \(a_0\) and put \[ D_e=\max_{a	ext{ at }e} |(\vartheta_{f(a)}-\pi\epsilon_a) -(\vartheta_{f(a_0)}-\pi\epsilon_{a_0})|_{\mathbb T}. \] The circular triangle inequality and the choice of \(a_0\) give \(d_e\le D_e\le2d_e\). Hence, for each fixed \(\eta>0\), the local theorem supplies \(c_e>0\), \(C_e\ge1\), and \(N_e\) such that \[  egin{aligned} |W_{e,N}|&\le C_e e^{-c_eN}E_{e,N}(L) &&	ext{if }d_e\ge\eta,\ |W_{e,N}|&\le E_{e,N}(L)&&	ext{for every phase}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] The second inequality is the original positive-envelope bound. A zero common scalar makes both sides zero exactly; no local value is divided out. ## 2. Odd cycles force a collection of mismatched ports Form the bipartite incidence multigraph with ordinary-face vertices, selected-port vertices, and the labeled incidences (1). Repeated edges remain distinct. A simple cycle here has no repeated vertices except its initial/final vertex; two distinct parallel edges are allowed to form a length-two cycle. Protected zero incidences are absent. Choose a nonempty finite collection \(\mathcal C\) of cycles for which the sum of the incidence labels is odd. Let \(r_{\max}\) be the largest number of port vertices on one of these cycles. Fix \[ \eta= rac{\pi}{4r_{\max}},\qquad B(\vartheta)=\{e\in J:d_e(\vartheta)\ge\eta\}. 	ag{4} \] Then \(B(\vartheta)\) meets every cycle in \(\mathcal C\). Indeed, choose a minimizing \(\varphi_e\) at each port on the cycle and subtract its two incidence equations. Upon summing around the cycle, the face phases telescope, while the odd label sum leaves \(\pi\) modulo \(2\pi\). Applying the circular triangle inequality gives \[ \pi\le2\sum_{e	ext{ on }C}d_e(\vartheta). 	ag{5} \] If every port of \(C\) were outside \(B\), the right side would be strictly below \(2r_{\max}\eta=\pi/2\), a contradiction. This uses only the original incidence multigraph; no white-sphere topology is needed. ## 3. Fractional cycle capacities give an additive loss Take every \(c_e\) in (3) at the same threshold (4). Define \[ \kappa_{\mathcal C}=\max_{\lambda_C\ge0} \left\{\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C: \sum_{C
i e}\lambda_C\le c_e 	ext{ for all }e\in Jight\}. 	ag{6} \] This finite linear program has a finite attained positive value. Every cycle contains a port, so its variable is bounded by that port's finite capacity. The feasible set is therefore compact. A sufficiently small positive weight on any single odd cycle proves positivity. For any feasible packing, (5) implies \[  egin{aligned} \sum_{e\in B(\vartheta)}c_e &\ge\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C |B(\vartheta)\cap C|\ &\ge\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C. \end{aligned}	ag{7} \] Consequently every phase point has total certified loss at least \(\kappa_{\mathcal C}\). For a port-disjoint collection one obtains the simple lower bound \[ \kappa_{\mathcal C}\ge \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\min_{e\in C}c_e. 	ag{8} \] Overlapping cycles can improve the packing value; their phases are not assumed independent. The capacities are analytic inputs, not automatically known numerical constants. If a different cycle collection changes \(r_{\max}\), the threshold and its certified \(c_e\)'s must be checked again. Alternatively one may fix the smaller threshold \(\pi/(4|J|)\) once and then compare cycle collections using that common set of capacities. ## 4. The unchanged Cauchy coefficient At selected ports set \(P_{e,N}=W_{e,N}\). Multiply (3) over the bad ports, use the envelope bounds elsewhere, and then apply (7). Uniformly on the one original phase torus, for \(N\ge\max_eN_e\), \[ \left|\prod_eP_{e,N}ight| \le C e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal C}N} \prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L), \qquad C=\prod_{e\in J}C_e. 	ag{9} \] Use formal face variables \(z_f\), distinct from their radii \(L_f\). The original Cauchy formula gives \[  oxed{\displaystyle \left|\left[\prod_f z_f^{t_f(N)}ight]\prod_eP_{e,N}(z)ight| \le C e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal C}N}  rac{\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
