otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\prod_fL_f^{t_f(N)}}.} 	ag{10} \] All protected specializations, source target exponents and scalar modes remain unchanged. There is one radius per original face, not one per incidence. Any external source character or prefactor retains its actual modulus separately; no such factor is silently discarded in (10). ## 5. A conditional strict source-rate certificate Let \[ B_L=\limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log  rac{\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\prod_fL_f^{t_f(N)}}, 	ag{11} \] with \(\log0=-\infty\). Then (10) bounds the actual window coefficient's normalized logarithmic limsup by \(B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}\). For a diagram with certified complete rate \(\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\), \[ B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}<\Phi_D,	ag{12} \] is a sufficient strict-rate certificate for this original window piece. It strengthens merely recording that some positive phase loss exists. It does not establish (12) without quantitative envelope and local-loss inputs. A polynomial-size family of pieces can be summed only with uniform estimates. Precisely, it suffices that the positive quotient for each piece \(p\) be at most \(\exp\{N(B_p+\omega_N)\}\), where \(\omega_N	o0\) uniformly, that the multiplicative constants have uniformly subexponential growth, that the bounds apply from one common level onward, and that \(B_p-\kappa_p\le\Phi_D-\varepsilon\) with one \(\varepsilon>0\). The polynomial number of pieces then costs only \(o(N)\) in the logarithm. Uncovered source configurations require their own estimates. No claim is made that compatible phase systems are negligible, that arbitrary boundary windows satisfy (3), or that the packing capacities overcome every diagram's envelope excess. This is a general fixed-graph criterion available at arbitrary fixed width, not universal diagram coverage or the volume conjecture.

title: Research routes and preserved ideas
text: # Research routes and preserved ideas The new exceptional-period route retains the exact generic Casimir polynomial, its canonical scalar action and general local character relation, the actual continuant resolvent period, strict-support Green estimates, and separate endpoint controls. Finite-propagation windows and the universal marked rectangle bound are retained with their limitations. The coherent Fourier phase and global ordinary Legendre chart remain complementary tools. These results do not replace the cube, positive sewing or other earlier routes, and do not yet prove the general contributing source period. 29 October 2026. This is a navigation and scope record, not a new proof or a replacement for the underlying notes. No route below is abandoned because another has advanced. “Proved” refers to the repository's research arguments; broader statements remain open. Start with the [current frontier](general_equality_frontier.md) and [pretzel-to-general strategy](pretzel_to_general_source_strategy.md). The objective remains the broad original-source equality with the ACTUAL hyperbolic volume, retaining the mark, normal terms and peripheral normalizations. A projected sector, local volume formula or upper bound is not a substitute for that objective. ## 1. Pretzels, belt stacks and the general filling mechanism The [complete augmented pretzel proof](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) has an explicit sharp Fourier energy and a separate nonzero original period. The [width improvement](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) and [geometric equality proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) give the stated independently long fixed signed fillings: odd pretzel widths >=9, and the specified two-component even-width links >=10. Widths 3,5,7 are not covered by that alias estimate. The [signed belt-stack assembly](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) is another full-source equality family, with any subset of auxiliary circles independently sufficiently long-filled and no minimum stack width. Its actual diagrams, peripheral words and component counts are part of the theorem. The reusable [general source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) is CONDITIONAL on an actual nonzero even complex packet and an entire physical-color complement gap. The [general geometric theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) identifies a genuinely marked nearby representation with the actual filled geometry. Neither theorem supplies missing quantum hypotheses for an arbitrary new graph. ## 2. Cube, shared cores and projected chains — preserved with their scope The cube is a concrete primitive-core test, not the asserted general answer. Its [actual rectified-core geometry](actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md) has volume 16v8+2Vol(Q_cube); the extra shared-core term cannot be replaced by a product of local theta rates. The durable source chain of results is: * [Literal central cube reduction](actual_odd_central_cube_reflection_packet.md): exact original marked scalar N^12 S_N^8 phi(h^4), with all twelve channels fixed to the odd Steinberg channel and all phases retained. * [Positive cuboctahedral period](actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.md): the real positive sum has the actual Q_cube volume rate, identified by its explicit geometric tetrahedra. * [Four-rung packet](actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.md): all four rung labels are summed, including paired normals. Eight cycle labels remain fixed. Its odd-level partial source has the same actual augmented-cube volume rate and a strict unfrozen-color gap. * [Two-boundary transfer and projected chains](actual_three_port_cauchy_transport_and_cube_kernel.md): an explicit coupled weighted-Cauchy kernel has the sharp cube-minus- theta norm increment. Typed iterations retain every rung sum but still fix 2+6k cycle labels and use odd levels. Full cube color summation, cancellation/dominance after removing those cycle projections, even-level cube growth and arbitrary primitive-core graphs remain OPEN. The [full-cube diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_full_cube_complete_circle_source.py) and [its data](../experiments/actual_full_cube_complete_circle_diagnostic_results.json) are preserved as complex128 finite diagnostics, not proofs of positivity, error control or a limit. The scope cautions already appear in the cube proof notes, README and frontier. The projected-chain note is linked explicitly here so it is not lost behind the shorter cube summaries. ## 3. Positive Conway expressions and Karamata-style variational growth The [actual positive Newton algebra](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md) retains every root normal. Its genuine turn, multiplication and closures give a [whole-source positive Conway class](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md), without cube channel projections. The [variational limit theorem](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md) proves an all-level limit as a concave ideal-angle maximum for each fixed robust expression. Exact integer support supplies the lower bound at every level, including boundary maxima. Its angle triples still need identification with the actual complement's face/edge incidence. Some expressions have polynomial growth; positivity does not imply hyperbolicity or volume equality. This route is preserved alongside the cube's more explicitly calibrated but projected result. ## 4. Fourier, weighted Cauchy and the distinct Tauberian idea The [Cauchy checkpoint](cauchy_metric_route_checkpoint.md) and [source-preserving weighted Fourier energy](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md) record actual metrics and their boundary costs. The [whole-support Gram theorem](actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.md) now gives polynomial local source cost on every supported triple, both parities. Exact [three-port source sewing](actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) and its weighted packet retain correlated labels and the original mark. Sharp GLOBAL transported energy and nonzero geometric overlap are still separate requirements. The [turned-circle inertia obstruction](actual_turned_circle_reflection_inertia.md) shows why a positive face form does not automatically stay positive through a genuine change of pairing. The [Fourier-energy Tauberian criterion](actual_fourier_energy_tauberian_criterion.md) preserves a different use of the Karamata idea: a sharp positive Laplace singularity gives cumulative information, but a full every-level limit also requires cross-level control. That criterion is not silently assumed in the already proved direct pretzel asymptotic. ## 5. Pointed quantum A-structure and regulator torsors Keep the [A-polynomial/torsor status](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md), [intrinsic quantum norm torsor](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) and [actual regulator-weighted transfer](actual_regulator_weighted_a_transfer.md). They retain the original affine source, normal period, lattice and marked peripheral data. A classical A-curve or an unpointed module alone does not select the original period or its absolute regulator. The explicit transfer calculation also shows that small off-diagonal mixing can become exponentially large after branch-dependent weighting. The general selected-period/regulator norm comparison and geometric survival remain open. These constructions and obstructions remain available; the explicit-family source proofs do not replace them. ## 6. Generic four-port kernels and actual local volume The [all-port single Racah kernel](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) is an exact generic source identity with its row/column normalization. The [positive scalar/normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) and [hyperideal geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) give a local quantum-volume law, uniformly over supported low-fold sextuples, including moving boundary colors. The positive face metric is essential; the bare sum has a different action. Full partner germs carry nonzero [2N] currents and the actual channel gauges may have poles before confluence. A useful full marked transport metric and the actual GLOBAL edge constraints remain to be established. The four local face supports alone maximize at an octahedral boundary, not at an interior manifold saddle. Relevant prior coverage is recorded separately in [the literature scope note](literature_hyperideal_racah_volume_coverage.md). The [full source-volume certificate](source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md) explains the final geometric requirement shared by these routes: stationarity on the entire actual edge/peripheral angle slice, followed by the decoration, winding and end-completion checks. Local formulas, restricted stationarity and matching volume constants do not replace it. Preservation audit: the links above were checked against the current files and scope statements. No existing research note or diagnostic was deleted, rewritten or downgraded by this index. It adds navigation only; there is no new proof or change in the claimed knot/link families here. ## 7. Common frames, two exceptional factors, and original generic normals The [joint ordinary-column theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) and [finite selected-local certificate](actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) remain available with their domains and hypotheses. The [right-angled framing obstruction](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) rules out making every original factor central and selected in one frame. Its generic two-facet refinement localizes the weaker physical-support failure to exactly two factors at any bridge width. Continuation of those factors, control outside the central domain and coherent recoupling remain possible routes; none is asserted to be completed. The [small-channel derivative bound](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md) uses the original generic source. The [partner collision identity](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) retains its actual first normal and surviving tail, whose additional poles exclude an unrestricted individual-normal continuation. The accompanying [complex-growth exploration](../experiments/actual_partner_normal_complex_growth_exploration.json) is preserved as a diagnostic, not as a proved exponential lower bound. The subsequent [complex near-fold estimate](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on fixed complex compacts for (l-j) log N=o(N). The [matching-edge scalar](actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.md) and [marked four-port block](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) preserve another route: regroup the two exceptional factors at a crossing-circle edge, retain every target and the trace normal, and use the exact cancellation with the original complete-circle measure. Target/complement boundary estimates and the mixed-color/global cycle problem remain open. No existing route or diagnostic is removed. The [full physical ordinary packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) now removes the central-domain restriction on fixed compacts, with an explicit finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) puts every ordinary factor except one chosen matching-edge pair on that actual selected packet. The two failures and the exact block remain; target/complement estimates and the global period do not follow from local selection. The [all-physical generic-jet theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md) retains another complementary domain, with every fixed q derivative controlled on integer physical columns and divided pairs. The [completed target-projector identity](actual_matching_edge_completed_projector_block.md) removes the remaining target scalar factor and pairs the colliding channels generically. It retains the nilpotent term and the genuine first derivatives of the regular operators. Their native norms and the joint contraction remain separate estimates; the exact cancellation does not make those costs polynomial. The [native-energy theorem](actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md) makes the operator cost explicit and proves that every fixed derivative adds only a polynomial factor. Its simple midpoint example has positive exponential growth, so the energy must remain in any global estimate. The shared-variable variational route is preserved; separate local maxima cannot replace the actual network constraints. The [Plancherel profile](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) and [real shrinking-fold theorem](actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.md) now compute that full local cost. Its [local geometric interpretations](actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.md) include an octahedral degree block and a two-cube full cost, with the signed terms and phase conditions retained. The [shared-cycle source](actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md) makes the flow/Fourier route exact at arbitrary fixed width, and [coefficient duality](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md) supplies positive local variational data on its actual shared indices. The one exceptional geometric block and the global coherent route remain necessary subjects of study; a positive coefficient envelope alone has not resolved them. The [shared positive Fourier partition](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md) now gives that route an exact original-source Cauchy bound. The [radial reconstruction obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) records why one direct geometric interpretation fails under the right-angled certificate, without claiming a rate gap or discarding nonradial, boundary or exceptional-block approaches.

title: The shared spectral energy can exceed the complete volume rate
text: # The shared spectral energy can exceed the complete volume rate 31 October 2026. On one certified original seven-port source, the endpoint-conditioned energy exceeds the complete rate by more than 0.50, already at one fixed real spectral corner. This disproves the stronger proposed bound $$ \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}E_{\mathrm{NC},N} \le \exp\{N(\Phi_D+o(1))\}. $$ It does not refute the weaker endpoint-mass budget or the joint shared-flow criteria in the [energy theorem](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md). It is not a lower bound for the original oscillatory invariant. ## 1. An exact original shared flow Take the width-three word $$ [1,3,0,2,4,1,3] $$ with the first cap marked. The original compiler gives protected faces $0,6$, ordinary faces $1,2,3,4,5,7,8$, and the seven ordered quartets $$ \begin{split} &(1,0,4,2),\ (2,0,5,3),\ (0,1,6,4),\ (4,2,7,5),\\ &(5,3,8,0),\ (6,4,0,7),\ (7,5,0,8). \end{split}\tag{1} $$ Select only port $2$ as RIGHT; the other six ports are CROSS. At that port the outer $x=0$ and opposite middle $c=6$ are protected. Its normalized exponents have the form $$ q_x=q_c=0,\qquad q_y=w,\qquad q_b=1-w,\qquad 0<w<\tfrac12. \tag{2} $$ By the literal reflection of the [protected-outer coefficient theorem](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md), its actual coefficient and reference entropies satisfy $$ k^*(q)=0,\qquad h_0(q)=-2f(w),\qquad 2k^*(q)-h_0(q)=2f(w)=C(0,\tfrac12-w,w). \tag{3} $$ Here $C(\alpha)=\sum_j f(\alpha_j)$, $\sum_j\alpha_j=1/2$, and $$ f(t)=\frac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}\pi. $$ Equation (3) is an actual energy rate, not merely the general local upper bound. Its weighted energy potential is $$ \Psi_R=\tfrac12\log L_1+Q(0,L_1,L_4). \tag{4} $$ The flow therefore consists of the original input triangle $(0,1,4)$ of supply $1/2$, and a fixed half-unit at face $1$. This is entropy bookkeeping for (2); it introduces no new finite coupon or changed mark. The [registered certificate](../experiments/research_shared_energy_excess_obstruction_certificate.json) contains 30 exact rational corner values on the 13 original triangle rows other than port $2$'s output row $(0,6,4)$. Every row sums to $1/2$. With the fixed half-unit at face $1$, every ordinary face receives exactly one and both protected faces receive zero. At all six CROSS ports, both middle degrees are strictly less than $1/2$; at port $2$, the $b$-degree is strictly greater than $1/2$. All these assertions are checked over the rationals against the original compiler. Put $$ E_{\mathrm{cert}}=\sum_{\text{13 registered rows}}C(\alpha_{\mathrm{row}}). \tag{5} $$ At a CROSS port its two registered rows give one allowed split of the outer degrees, so their entropy is at most the actual coefficient entropy. At the selected port its one row gives exactly (3). No numerical optimizer is used to justify either assertion. ## 2. Actual integer arrays and a fixed spectral corner Let $q_{e,f}$ be the aggregated rational port-face flow above. For each even $N=2m$, set $d=N-1$. On the original port-face transportation network give each incidence the integer bounds $$ \lfloor d q_{e,f}\rfloor\le v_{e,f}\le\lceil d q_{e,f}\rceil. \tag{6} $$ The fractional flow $dq$ satisfies these bounds and all integer port supplies $d$ and ordinary face demands $d$. Integrality of the bipartite transportation network gives an integer flow $v_N$ between the bounds. All zero incidences, including the protected ones, remain exactly zero, and $v_N/d\to q$. The fixed strict middle slack gives $v_b,v_c\le m-1$ at each CROSS port for all sufficiently large even $N$, and $v_b\ge m$ at the RIGHT port. These are the actual finite supports with the true target $d=N-1$. The [full positive endpoint kernel](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) contains every degree-$d$ monomial, and its CROSS part has precisely these middle inequalities. Thus the original central factor is retained by classification of the actual coefficient. No separate rounding of formal half-triangle rows or removal of a forced outer factor is used. At the six CROSS ports choose $\sigma_e=-2$. At even levels the original reference is $p_N(v)=-a_N(v;-2)>0$, and hence $$ \frac{|a_N(v;-2)|^2}{p_N(v)}=p_N(v) \tag{7} $$ exactly. At the selected port use the fixed value $\sigma_2=+2$. After literal row reflection its monomer starts at $i=0$. Writing $\theta=\pi/N$, the exact unused-row formula and $\chi_N(2)=4$ give $$ |a_N(v;2)|= \csc^2(\theta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j} \left[\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+1/2)\theta)}\right]^2, \qquad j\le m-1. \tag{8} $$ Sine increases throughout these arguments. The unsquared product is between $\sin\theta/\sin((j+1)\theta)$ and $1$, including $j=0$. Consequently $$ 4\cos^2(\theta/2)\le |a_N(v;2)|\le\csc^2(\theta/2). \tag{9} $$ Its rate at this fixed spectral value is zero. The uniform endpoint entropy therefore yields the selected-port energy rate in (3), at the actual rounded exponents. Let $$ \boldsymbol\sigma^*=(-2,-2,+2,-2,-2,-2,-2). $$ The positive shared energy contains the summand indexed by $v_N$. The uniform closed endpoint coefficient theorem, (3), and (7)--(9) imply $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \liminf_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\ \mathrm{even}}} \frac1N\log E_{\mathrm{NC},N}(\boldsymbol\sigma^*) \ge E_{\mathrm{cert}}.} \tag{10} $$ All spectral coordinates belong to the same original shared numerator. No spectral optimization, limit/supremum exchange, or independent local face contraction is used. ## 3. A certified excess over the complete rate For an independent complete upper bound use the fixed ordinary radii $$ (L_0,\ldots,L_8)=(0,16,9,25,1,4,0,1,9). \tag{11} $$ The [actual complete capacity formula](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) gives, simply by evaluating one positive ordinary vector, $$ \Phi_D\le U= \sum_{\text{14 original triangles}}Q(L_{\mathrm{triangle}}) -\sum_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\log L_f. \tag{12} $$ This vector is also the original complete packing, but its optimality is unnecessary for the upper bound (12). The [verify-only audit](../experiments/audit_research_shared_energy_excess_obstruction.py) uses the fixed rational certificate and Arb arithmetic at 192 bits. Each Lobachevsky Fourier series has 8192 terms and the explicit absolute tail $1/(2M)$. The [registered results](../experiments/research_shared_energy_excess_obstruction_results.json) prove $$ E_{\mathrm{cert}}>7.51209890188,\qquad U<6.99858850313,\qquad E_{\mathrm{cert}}-\Phi_D>0.50. \tag{13} $$ The certified excess lower endpoint is greater than 0.51351039. Equations (10)--(13) refute the stronger energy-at-most-complete-rate proposal on an actual certified original source. The even subsequence already suffices to refute an all-level upper bound. ## 4. The weaker criteria are unaffected For a sector with endpoint mass rate $z_s$ and energy rate $e_s$, the weaker Cauchy condition is $z_s+e_s<2\Phi_D$. This certificate does not compare the energy excess with the endpoint mass loss and does not disprove that condition. The joint score must retain both terms on the same original flow. At the selected doubly protected port, (3) gives exactly $$ \frac{h_0(q)+g(q)}2=0=k^*(q). \tag{14} $$ The positive energy rate compensates an exponentially small reference coefficient; it is not positive growth of the original spectral coefficient. The universal joint-score and combined-envelope inequalities remain open. No lower bound for the original oscillatory source, no failure of its volume limit, and no obstruction to the weaker energy budget follows from this counterexample. ## 5. verification scope The portable verifier preserves the `verify` function's complete syntax tree and the registered certificate bytes; only imports and output/default paths were changed. It has no optional numerical builder or optimizer dependency. Its finite checks establish the original incidence, rational feasibility, support slack, and certified entropy inequalities. The asymptotic step uses the proved uniform coefficient theorems and integer transportation argument; no sampled large-level rate is presented as proof.

title: Sharp CROSS-degree domination and a uniform original seam gap
status: All-spectrum CROSS domination, explicit seam gap and filled-period negligibility
text: # Sharp CROSS-degree domination and a uniform original seam gap 31 October 2026. The comparison is between the explicitly defined sharp functionals. It does not turn a coefficient limsup into a coefficient limit. The global coefficient upper theorem supplies the finite source consequence at both parities and all spectral boundaries. ## 1. The full closed-domain functional Use the original local degree order q=(q_x,q_b,q_c,q_y), q>=0 and sum q=1, and put mu=q_b, nu=1-q_c, xi=q_x, 0<=xi<=nu-mu. The CROSS degree closure is 0<=mu<=1/2<=nu<=1. (1) This is a condition on the original four degrees. It does not assign a finite coefficient to a new path label at a seam. For 0<=delta<=1/2 use exactly the full sharp functional in the global coefficient theorem: alpha_delta(t)=2cos(2pi t)+2cos(2pi delta), Lambda_delta(t;x,y)=2sin(pi t) *[(x+y)sin(pi t) +sqrt((x-y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4xy cos^2(pi delta))], B_delta(mu,nu)=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta(t)|dt +int_nu^1 log|alpha_delta(t)|dt, H_delta(q)=B_delta(mu,nu) +inf_(l in R){int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt-xi*l}. (2) All integrals include their actual unused rows. The logarithmic singularities are integrable. H is continuous on the entire closed simplex and spectral interval by the proved uniform tilt-clipping argument, including xi=0,nu-mu, diagonal rows, protected coordinates, and delta=1/2. **Theorem.** On (1), for every real spectrum, H_delta(q)<=H_0(q)=h(q), (3) where h is the original continuous complete-endpoint coefficient entropy. In fact H_delta(q) is nonincreasing as delta goes from0 to1/2 for each fixed CROSS degree vector q. No sampled finite product is divided by a zero, and no coefficient lower asymptotic is used. ## 2. The unused products are maximized at the complete spectrum Set f(t)=log|2cos(pi t)|, as a locally integrable, even, one-periodic function. Its value is a decreasing function of dist(t,Z) in[0,1/2]. For 0<=a<=1/2 define J_delta(a)=int_0^a log|alpha_delta(t)|dt. The exact factorization alpha_delta(t)=4cos(pi(t+delta))cos(pi(t-delta)) and evenness of f give, with NO extra constant or factor two, J_delta(a)=int_(delta-a)^(delta+a) f(t)dt. (4) For fixed a this moving integral is absolutely continuous in delta, because f is locally L1. Almost everywhere, partial_delta J_delta(a)=f(delta+a)-f(delta-a). (5) If a,delta belong to[0,1/2], dist(delta+a,Z)=min(delta+a,1-delta-a) >=|delta-a|=dist(delta-a,Z). The first inequality follows separately from delta+a>=|delta-a| and 1-delta-a>=|delta-a|, the latter being equivalent to 1>=2max(delta,a). Thus (5)<=0 almost everywhere. Absolute continuity retains this sign through the logarithmic singularity at delta+a=1/2. Consequently J_delta(a)<=J_0(a), (6) and, more generally, J_delta(a) is nonincreasing in delta. If a=0 it is zero. If a=1/2 it is the full-period integral of f, also zero, independent of delta. For 0<a<1/2 the derivative is strictly negative almost everywhere in0<delta<1/2, but strictness is not needed below. On the CROSS domain, alpha_delta(1-t)=alpha_delta(t) and both unused endpoint lengths are at most1/2. Therefore B_delta(mu,nu)=J_delta(mu)+J_delta(1-nu) <=J_0(mu)+J_0(1-nu)=B_0(mu,nu). (7) This is where the CROSS degree hypothesis is used. A one-sided row instead gives a difference of two lower-half prefix integrals; (7) does not imply the same comparison there. ## 3. The tail comparison and the exact endpoint normalization For every finite real l and every0<t<1, the displayed positive root in (2) is nonincreasing in delta, since cos^2(pi delta) decreases. Thus log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)<=log Lambda_0(t;exp(l),1). Integrate over the same original interval and subtract xi*l. The inequality holds for EVERY finite tilt, so it also holds after the two infima over l. Combining with (7) proves H_delta<=H_0. The same argument between any two ordered spectra proves monotonicity. Integrable endpoint bounds justify each integral; alternatively the already proved closed continuity passes from interior row endpoints. No finite minimizing tilt is assumed when an outer degree is zero or at its full value. For completeness H_0 in (3) is the actual endpoint entropy, not another normalization. Put tau=1-nu. Symmetry about1/2 splits the tail integral into [mu,1/2] and [tau,1/2]. The identity int_0^(1/2)log alpha_0(t)dt=0 converts each corresponding prefix term J_0(a) into minus the alpha integral over its active half. Hence H_0(q)=inf_l{Phi_mu(l)+Phi_tau(l)-xi*l}, Phi_a(l)=int_a^(1/2) log[Lambda_0(t;exp(l),1)/alpha_0(t)]dt. (8) The integrand is exactly the source-normalized endpoint function l/2+log tan(pi t)+asinh(tan(pi t)cosh(l/2)). Its half-interval Legendre entropy is the proved triangle entropy Ctri(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi), with alpha summing to1/2. The infimum in (8) equals the maximum of the sum of the two such entropies over xi_1+xi_2=xi and 0<=xi_1<=1/2-mu,0<=xi_2<=1/2-tau. Indeed every split is bounded above by its value at a common tilt. At a finite minimizing tilt choose xi_a=Phi_a'(l); this attains equality in both half infima. The closed endpoint/outer cases follow by continuity of H_0 and of the triangle entropies and their closed split interval. This is only one-dimensional outer Legendre convolution, not concavity or duality in the row endpoints. It gives exactly the published h(q) on CROSS closure, including both terminal seams and the pure-middle corner. ## 4. A strict gap for all seam-only original shared data Fix an original simple-white certified marked plat D. Let Q_D be its actual compact incidence-flow polytope: each port supplies1, each ordinary face demands1, and both original protected faces demand0. Let Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). The proved endpoint theorem and unique geometric maximum give max_(q in Q_D) sum_e h(q_e)=Phi_D, q_geom is the unique maximizer, q_geom,e,b<1/2 and q_geom,e,c<1/2 at EVERY port. (9) These assertions retain the actual original marked packing and matching. They are not claims about a freely chosen incidence graph. Define the closed seam-only subset Sigma_D={q in Q_D: all q_e,b,q_e,c<=1/2, and at least one equals1/2}. (10) If it is empty, no seam-only candidate exists. There is an explicit fixed-diagram gap when it is nonempty. Put a_D=min_e{1/2-q_geom,e,b, 1/2-q_geom,e,c}>0, gamma_D=(pi/2) a_D^2. (11) Here and below ||q-q_geom|| is the Euclidean norm on ALL original incidence coordinates, namely the square root of sum_e sum_(f=x,b,c,y)(q_(e,f)-q_geom,(e,f))^2. A shared face's separate port incidences remain separate coordinates; protected coordinates are fixed at zero. No norm on the vector of distinct global face sums is used. To prove (11) is a valid gap, recall the exact triangle entropy Ctri(alpha)=sum_j f(alpha_j), sum_j alpha_j=1/2, where f(t)=[Lob(pi t)+Lob(pi/2-pi t)]/pi, f''(t)=-2pi/sin(2pi t)<=-2pi, 0<t<1/2. Here Lob is the Lobachevsky function in the endpoint triangle theorem. Its continuous endpoint values extend the resulting strong-concavity inequality to the CLOSED triangle simplex. The sum over both latent triangles of every CROSS port is therefore 2pi-strongly concave in the Euclidean latent incidence norm. The actual linear projection to q sums the two outer entries and retains each middle entry separately; its squared operator norm is at most2. Given two feasible q vectors, choose their maximizing latent allocations. Their convex mixture is feasible for the mixture of the original q vectors. Applying the latent strong-concavity inequality and ||P v||^2<=2||v||^2 shows that F(q)=sum_e h(q_e) is pi-strongly concave on the entire closed original CROSS fiber. This argument also covers a protected monomial half, which has no free latent coordinate. For any q in that fiber and0<t<1, maximality at q_geom gives Phi_D>=F((1-t)q_geom+t q) >=(1-t)Phi_D+t F(q)+(pi/2)t(1-t)||q-q_geom||^2. Divide by t and let t decrease to0. No boundary gradient is needed: F(q)<=Phi_D-(pi/2)||q-q_geom||^2. (11a) Every seam q has at least one middle coordinate equal to1/2, hence ||q-q_geom||>=a_D. Equations (11)--(11a) give its entropy gap directly, without an uncomputed seam maximization. The constant uses the exact normalization Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi), and is not uniform over diagrams. Apply (3) portwise. Uniformly over ALL original spectra, max_(q in Sigma_D, delta in[0,1/2]^R) sum_e H_(delta_e)(q_e)<=Phi_D-gamma_D. (12) In particular a maximum of the sharp functional on the closed non-CROSS union {q: some q_e,b>=1/2 or q_e,c>=1/2} with value at least Phi_D MUST have a strictly overloaded middle >1/2. Its possible seam-only alternative is excluded. This supplies that hypothesis for the existing restricted-non-CROSS activation and stationary reductions; it does not settle the remaining strictly overloaded, phase-inconsistent candidates. There is moreover a UNIFORM fixed-diagram overload margin eta_D>0: q in Q_D, max_middle(q)>=1/2, sum_e H_(delta_e)(q_e)>=Phi_D => max_middle(q)>=1/2+eta_D. (12a) To prove this, the set of pairs (q,delta) satisfying the two premises is closed in a compact space. If it is empty the conclusion is vacuous. Otherwise none of its points has max_middle(q)=1/2, since such a q lies in Sigma_D and contradicts (12). The continuous positive function max_middle(q)-1/2 therefore has a positive minimum on this set. This also handles an empty Sigma_D: then equality max_middle=1/2 is already excluded by the flow constraints themselves. Equivalently, a sequence of high-valued candidates whose maximal middle decreases to1/2 would have a seam-only limit, contradicting (12). No lower coefficient rate is used in this compactness argument. Thus the strict-overload qualifier in the existing high-value restricted non-CROSS reductions is automatic, with a margin uniform over their candidate maxima for this one fixed D. ## 5. Uniform finite-source consequence near the entire seam set Joint continuity of sum H on Q_D times the compact spectral cube makes (12) stable on a fixed neighborhood. There is rho_D>0 such that dist_infinity(q,Sigma_D)<=rho_D => sum_e H_(delta_e)(q_e)<=Phi_D-gamma_D/2 (13) for every q in Q_D and every real spectral vector. This neighborhood may include actual LEFT or RIGHT degree vectors slightly beyond the seams; no finite path label is changed. If Sigma_D is empty, compactness instead gives an empty sufficiently small neighborhood of the seam conditions, and there is no such contribution to bound. For each N let a_(e,N)(n_e;delta_e) be the ACTUAL local coefficient, with the original total degree d=N-1, unused products and raw phases. Sum over any set of original target arrays n whose EXACT normalized flow q=n/d lies in the neighborhood (13). The global uniform coefficient LIMSUP majorant and the polynomial number of arrays at fixed D give limsup_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log sup_(delta in[0,1/2]^R) sum_(such arrays n) prod_e |a_(e,N)(n_e;delta_e)| <=Phi_D-gamma_D/2. (14) Empty sums have logarithm minus infinity. In particular the actual signed sum over those arrays is eventually bounded by exp{N(Phi_D-gamma_D/3)}. This includes both parities, composite levels, all protected/row/spectral boundaries and sampled spectral zeros. The d-normalized target is unchanged; no lower approximation of a limiting flow or every-level coefficient limit is required. A degree-array restriction chosen independently of the spectral variables still produces an original spectral polynomial of degree at most d in each variable. Thus the existing cosine-Bernstein and whole-domain three-integration-by-parts transfer applies to this restricted source: its fixed thin-strip and entire weighted Fourier/Hermite period have a strict gap below Phi_D. All original scalar characters and endpoint currents remain. This concerns only the stated seam neighborhood; it is not a bound on the whole non-CROSS period. There is a direct interface with the actual filled volume. Denote this whole seam-neighborhood period by I_seam and the original whole all-CROSS period by I_cross, with the SAME original Fourier/Hermite normalization. After retaining a smaller fixed gap kappa_D>0, the transfer just used gives |I_seam|<=C_D prod_e(1+|n_e|)^3 exp{N(Phi_D-kappa_D)}, n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e. (15) The [entire all-CROSS theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) gives an eventually nonzero period and its relative asymptotic, with lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log|I_cross| =Vol(the actual smooth filled exterior)/(2pi) =Phi_D-O_D(sum_e |n_e|^(-2)). (16) The prescribed half twists, primitive fillings and actual final-diagram normalization are exactly those of that theorem. Choose a fixed-diagram threshold T(D) above its geometric and analytic thresholds and large enough that the loss in (16) is less than kappa_D/2 whenever every |p_e|>T(D). For each independently signed vector p fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity, equations (15)--(16) then imply I_seam/I_cross=O_p(exp(-c_D N)), c_D>0, (17) for example with any fixed c_D<kappa_D/2 after enlarging the vector-dependent starting level. Both level parities and composite levels are retained. No bound on ratios of the twist magnitudes is imposed, and no joint growing-twist/level estimate is asserted. Any common recorded framing/component character or common nonzero normalization factor cancels in (17); it has not been replaced by a new marked normalization. Equation (17) proves only negligibility of the specified seam remainder. It does not give equality of the FULL invariant with all-CROSS: the macroscopic, strictly overloaded non-CROSS contribution remains to be controlled. The nonzero all-CROSS contribution is the cited theorem, not a new lower-period claim from the present coefficient upper bound. ## 6. Dependencies The [global coefficient majorant](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) supplies (2), closed continuity and the uniform original coefficient upper bound. Section 3 above and the [closed half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) supply the normalized half/triangle identity. The [full endpoint entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) and [unique geometric maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) give the original endpoint function and (9). The [whole-domain Fourier lemma](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md), section 4, applies to the restricted polynomial in section 5. The [full-fiber activation](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md) and [stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) are downstream applications of the uniform overload statement (12a), not premises of the direct CROSS comparison or seam gap. No numerical audit or coefficient lower limit is used. The comparison covers only CROSS degrees and the resulting seam neighborhood; macroscopic strictly overloaded phase-inconsistent candidates remain outside the conclusion. In particular (17) is not a full-invariant volume theorem.

title: The exact spectral maximum of a full Green interval
text: # The exact spectral maximum of a full Green interval 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** This identifies the spectral maximum of the original sharp coefficient UPPER functional. It does not assert a coefficient lower limit, phase compatibility, representation volume, or a shared maximum bounded by Phi_D. ## 1. Statement on the original degree simplex Use the jointly continuous, absolutely normalized sharp action H_delta(q) of the [global closed sharp coefficient upper theorem](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md). Its row order is q=(q_x,q_b,q_c,q_y), with total one. On the closed LEFT domain q_c>=1/2 set s_x=q_x, s_b=q_b, s_y=q_y, nu=s_x+s_b+s_y=1-q_c. Let f be the actual triangle summand, f(0)=f(1/2)=0 and f'(s)=log cot(pi s), f''(s)=-2pi/sin(2pi s), 0<s<1/2. Then the exact calculus identity is max_(0<=delta<=1/2) H_delta(q) = G(q):=f(s_x)+f(s_b)+f(s_y)-f(nu). (1) For strictly positive s_x,s_b,s_y and nu<1/2, the maximizing spectrum is unique and lies in (0,1/2). It satisfies sin^2(pi delta_*) = cos(pi nu)cos(pi s_b)/[cos(pi s_x)cos(pi s_y)]. (2) The reflected statement holds on the closed RIGHT domain, with its original overloaded middle as child. On the closed CROSS domain the [closed CROSS comparison](research_sharp_cross_degree_domination_and_seam_gap.md) already gives max_delta H_delta=h_0. At the seams, (1) equals the actual complete triangle entropy, so these statements fit continuously. All spectra remain independent at the different original ports; this is a pointwise local identity, with no shared minimax exchange. ## 2. Construct the strict spectral stationary point from its degrees Assume the three input loads are positive and their sum nu is below 1/2. Define dimensionless positive common weights x=tan(pi s_x), b=tan(pi s_b), y=tan(pi s_y), A=x+y, P=xy, S=1-bA-P. The addition formula and nu<1/2 give S>0 and c=tan(pi nu)=(A+b-bP)/S, c-b=A(1+b^2)/S, c-b-A=A(b+x)(b+y)/S>0. (3) Put z=S/(1+b^2), k^2=1-z=(b+x)(b+y)/(1+b^2), delta=(1/pi)arcsin(sqrt(z)). (4) Both z and k^2 are strictly between zero and one. The last identity in (2) follows from cos(pi nu)=S cos(pi s_x)cos(pi s_b)cos(pi s_y). The original root is alpha_delta(t)=4[k^2-sin^2(pi t)], Lambda_delta(t;x,y) =2sin(pi t)[A sin(pi t) +sqrt((x-y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4k^2xy)], L_delta=Lambda_delta/|alpha_delta|. The exact pre-pole and post-pole row equations are sin^2(pi mu)=k^2 b^2/[(b+x)(b+y)], sin^2(pi nu)=k^2 c^2/[(c-x)(c-y)]. (5) Equations (3)--(4) give mu=s_b and the specified nu. For the second equation one may verify directly (c-x)(c-y)/(1+c^2)=(b+x)(b+y)/(1+b^2). The input is on the increasing pre-pole branch because k^2-sin^2(pi mu)=(bA+P)/(1+b^2)>0. The output is on the decreasing post-pole branch because k^2-sin^2(pi nu)=(P-Ac)/(1+c^2)<0. Thus this is a strict straddle, not a spurious squared solution. Its spectral stationary condition (c-b)z=A is exactly (3)--(4), with the [original normalized branch derivative](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md) log(T_c/E_b) equal to zero. ## 3. Verify the actual outer coefficient, not just its row equations The outer degree is the derivative of the literal integrated root at the minimizing tilt log(x/y). Write d=x-y and D=A^2-4Pz>0. Direct differentiation and integration give a(t)=partial_(log x) log Lambda_delta(t;x,y) =1/2+d sin(pi t)/[2sqrt(d^2 sin^2(pi t)+4k^2P)], int_mu^nu a(t)dt=(nu-mu)/2 +[asin(d cos(pi mu)/sqrt D) -asin(d cos(pi nu)/sqrt D)]/(2pi). (6) All inverse sines here are their real principal values. To check their difference without selecting an unproved sign, put B=bA+2P>0, V=sqrt(d^2+B^2), R=sqrt((1+x^2)(1+y^2)), theta=atan x-atan y. Then D=V^2/(1+b^2), and the two inverse-sine arguments in (6) are I_b=d/V, I_c=dS/(VR). For I_c use sqrt(1+c^2)=sqrt((1+x^2)(1+b^2)(1+y^2))/S. Furthermore sin theta=d/R, cos theta=(1+P)/R, sin(asin I_b-theta)=d(1+P-B)/(VR)=I_c. Since 1+P-B=S>0, tan(asin I_b)=d/B and tan theta=d/(1+P) have the same sign and |asin I_b|>=|theta|. Their difference remains in (-pi/2,pi/2), so asin I_b-asin I_c=theta=pi(s_x-s_y). The equality case d=0 is included directly. Equation (6) therefore equals s_x; its complementary outer degree is s_y. This verifies the original outer-coefficient Legendre equation and fixes the actual load vector q, not just a formal conic or two row roots. ## 4. Absolute action and uniqueness Let H_*(s) denote H_delta(q) at the smooth stationary data just constructed. Every degree is interior, the minimizing outer tilt is finite and unique, and the spectrum is a strict nonpole stationary point. The ordinary envelope rule therefore gives partial_(s_i) H_* = log(c/w_i), i=x,b,y. (7) This is also obtained by adding the original face-weight term to the local simplex action: its derivative is zero, and increasing an input decreases the child load by the same amount. No common scalar is dropped. Since w_i=tan(pi s_i) and c=tan(pi nu), the right side of (7) is f'(s_i)-f'(nu). On the connected domain s_i>0, sum s_i<1/2, H_*-G is consequently constant. Scale s_i toward zero in fixed positive ratios. Formula (2) gives delta_* ->1/2 and q tends to the pure-child vertex. Joint continuity of the original closed sharp action gives H_* ->0, as does G. Hence the constant is zero. This uses the proved continuous upper functional, not a coefficient limit or a collision claim about dilogarithms. Conversely any strict spectral stationary point at these degrees must be the one constructed above. At its actual finite outer tilt define x,y>0 and b=L_delta(mu), c=L_delta(nu). The normalized pre/pre and post/post branch derivatives cannot vanish, so the point straddles the pole and (c-b)z=A. In particular c>b+A. Set T^2=[Abc+P(c-b)]/[c-b-A]>0. The exact row equations imply tan(pi mu)=b/T and tan(pi nu)=c/T. Rescale all four weights by T. The tangent-addition identity now gives atan(x/T)+atan(b/T)+atan(y/T)=atan(c/T); the angle sum is below pi/2 because T^2-bA-P=A(b+x)(b+y)/(c-b-A)>0. Repeating the exact outer calculation (6) shows s_x=atan(x/T)/pi and s_y=atan(y/T)/pi. Thus all ratios w_i/T, and then z, are fixed by q and agree with (2). ## 5. Why the stationary value is the whole spectral maximum For fixed strict q, joint continuity makes the maximum on delta in [0,1/2] exist. The [fixed-degree small-delta perturbation](research_regular_shared_spectral_stationary_reduction.md#4a-a-one-sided-nonterminal-maximum-cannot-have-delta0) excludes delta=0 when the interval has positive length and nu<1/2. The cap value is zero, whereas strict concavity of f and f(0)=0 give G>0 for these three positive inputs. A spectral value at which an interval endpoint equals an alpha pole cannot maximize: the [original unused-log perturbation](research_sharp_interval_pole_endpoint_exclusion.md) into the interval has a positive epsilon log(1/epsilon) gain uniformly before the outer infimum. These are exactly the endpoint and pole exclusions for the same sharp functional and unchanged degree vector. At every remaining spectral value the original coefficient tilt is finite, unique and smooth. A maximum is therefore a strict spectral stationary point. Section 4 proves that there is exactly one, and its value is G. This proves (1)--(2) on the strict LEFT degree domain. The map q -> max_delta H_delta(q) is continuous on the entire closed simplex because H is jointly continuous and the spectral interval is compact. The right side of (1) is continuous as well. Approximation by the strict LEFT degrees thus proves (1) on the full closed LEFT domain, including zero ordinary inputs in the standalone local formula, protected specializations, diagonal intervals and the seam. No positivity or nonzero A_rest is inferred at any finite level. For nu=1/2, f(nu)=0 and (1) is precisely the complete input triangle entropy; the output is its actual pure-middle triangle. This agrees with the independently normalized CROSS formula at the shared seam. ## 6. Exact reduced row Hessian and the remaining global problem On the strict input simplex the Hessian of the optimized Green action is especially simple: D^2 G = -2pi diag(1/sin(2pi s_i)) +[2pi/sin(2pi nu)] 1 1^T. (8) There is exactly one positive eigenvalue and two negative eigenvalues. Indeed the positive rank-one update crosses zero precisely when sum_i sin(2pi s_i)>sin(2pi nu), which is strict for positive inputs whose total angle is below pi. A protected-zero input is removed before differentiation; with two positive inputs the signature is one positive and one negative. This recovers the prior monomer Hessian. Equivalently, for original local row displacements summing to zero, D^2 G[v,v] =-2pi sum_(input i) v_i^2/sin(2pi q_i) +2pi v_child^2/sin(2pi(1-q_child)). (9) The full original constrained second variation after optimizing the strict Green spectra is the sum of (9) and the actual negative CROSS row Hessians, restricted to the original row and face balances; cap rows retain their zero action. Formula (9) is a diagonal incidence form before imposing these constraints. It does not itself produce a positive feasible direction: the shared repair problem is still real. The general sharp upper variational problem can now maximize the explicit piecewise local function: actual CROSS entropy on CROSS degrees, and (1) on either overloaded-middle domain. Spectra optimize independently, so this elimination is legitimate; no face-weight infimum is exchanged with a shared maximum. A proof that this original shared maximum is at most Phi_D, or a cancellation-aware replacement when it exceeds Phi_D, remains separate. No universal full-Hessian instability or hyperbolic volume bound is claimed. ## 7. A general full-invariant criterion with no spectral variables This corollary keeps the original labeled simple-white geometric certificate and full-source conventions. It is a sufficient criterion, not an assertion that every such diagram satisfies its inequality. Fix an actual width k>=2 flat-plat skeleton D, its permitted mark and fixed retained half twists epsilon_e in {0,+1,-1}, whose endpoint permutation gives a knot. Let Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi) be its drilled volume rate. The common full-V source and Phi_D are the ones in the [whole all-CROSS filling theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md), including the actual full crossing scalars and final framing character. Define a continuous local function barH on the full degree simplex: barH(q)=h_0(q), q_b,q_c<=1/2; barH(q)=sum_(i=x,b,y) f(q_i)-f(1-q_c), q_c>=1/2; barH(q)=sum_(i=x,c,y) f(q_i)-f(1-q_b), q_b>=1/2. (10) The seam agreements proved above make (10) unambiguous. Let P_D be the original compact transport fiber: each port supplies one, every ordinary face demands one, and the two protected faces demand zero. Repeated incidences retain their original labels. Put P_NC={q in P_D : max_(e,middle b or c) q_(e,middle)>=1/2}, M_D^NC=max_(q in P_NC) sum_e barH(q_e). (11) If P_NC is empty the corresponding upper condition is vacuous and its asymptotic non-CROSS arrays are absent. Otherwise suppose the fixed diagram satisfies the explicit, purely degree-variable inequality M_D^NC < Phi_D. (12) Then there is a finite threshold T(D), including this certificate in the fixed data, such that for every independently signed integer twist vector p with all |p_e|>T(D), fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity, lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|K_N(K_D(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus K_D(p)). (13) Both level parities and composite levels are included. There is no comparability condition among the twist magnitudes, no growing-twist limit, and no threshold asserted uniformly over different diagrams. Equation (13) concerns the original filled knot invariant and its actual smooth filled exterior, not the drilled volume. Proof. Spectra optimize independently at the original ports. The closed CROSS comparison and (1) give the exact pointwise identity max_(delta_1,...,delta_R in [0,1/2]) sum_e H_(delta_e)(q_e)=sum_e barH(q_e). (14) Take the literal non-CROSS remainder, namely the full-V source minus its actual all-CROSS path sector. Every original coefficient array in this remainder has a one-sided or diagonal port. Its d=N-1 normalized limiting degree lies in P_NC; possible finite half-mesh conventions only give a uniformly vanishing distance from this closed set. The global uniform coefficient LIMSUP theorem applies through all row, outer-degree and spectral boundaries, including sampled zeros. There are polynomially many original arrays at fixed D. Equations (12)--(14) and uniform continuity therefore give a fixed gamma_D>0 and, uniformly on the entire real spectral cube and at both parities, |S_N^NC(-2cos(2pi delta))| <= exp[N(Phi_D-gamma_D)] (15) for all sufficiently large N. The estimate also bounds the sum of absolute values of these arrays; no phase alignment or lower coefficient limit is required. The remainder S_N^NC is still an actual polynomial of degree at most d in each sigma_e. Its degree/path projection is spectrum independent. Thus the cosine-Bernstein and whole-domain three-integration-by-parts argument of the [global sector theorem, section 4](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md) applies verbatim to (15). A sufficiently thin fixed complex spectral strip retains a positive loss. Source-only Cauchy estimates control the required derivatives; the original sine factors and Gaussian endpoint matching retain the second-derivative endpoint currents. The actual charge factors then leave the absolutely summable product of |ell_e|^(-2). Consequently some kappa_D>0 satisfies |I_N^NC(p)| <= C_(D,p) exp[N(Phi_D-kappa_D)] (16) for each fixed signed p. This is the entire original Fourier period, not an infinite sum of sharply cut local charge cubes. The polynomial dependence on N and on the fixed slopes n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e is absorbed by retaining a smaller positive loss. The proved all-CROSS whole period is eventually nonzero and has rate lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log|I_N^CROSS(p)| =Phi_fill(p) =Phi_D-O_D(sum_e |n_e|^(-2)). (17) Here Phi_fill(p)=Vol(S^3 minus K_D(p))/(2pi), with the same original normalization, half twists and framing. Choose T(D) large enough that this existing theorem applies and Phi_fill(p)>Phi_D-kappa_D/2 for all independent signed vectors in the stated range. Then (16)--(17) give I_N^NC/I_N^CROSS ->0 exponentially, at both parities. Adding the two literal sectors and retaining their common original normalization proves (13). The unproved general step is (12), not this conditional full-source implication. ## 8. Radial convexity and the exact local weighted transform Take positive face weights (x,b,c,y), and write the LEFT inputs as s_i=t p_i, where p_i>=0, sum p_i=1 and 0<=t<=1/2. For at least two positive p_i, differentiation on the open radial interval gives d^2/dt^2 G(t p) =2pi[1/sin(2pi t)-sum_(p_i>0) p_i^2/sin(2pi t p_i)] >0. (18) Indeed u/sin u is strictly increasing on (0,pi), so each term in the sum is at most p_i/sin(2pi t), strictly when 0<p_i<1. If only one p_i is positive, G is identically zero. Thus G is convex on every closed radial segment, by continuity at its endpoints. The added weight term is affine in t: sum_f q_f log L_f=(1-t)log c+t sum_i p_i log w_i. Its radial maximum is therefore attained at t=0 or t=1/2. At t=0 the value is log c. At t=1/2 the input has its actual triangle entropy, and maximizing its allocation gives sup_(closed LEFT q) [barH(q)+sum_f q_f log L_f] =max{log c, Q(x,b,y)+(1/2)log c}. (19) Here Q is the original weighted complete triangle action, with total triangle load 1/2; no degree normalization has changed. RIGHT has the reflected formula with b and c interchanged. On CROSS, the two genuine triangle allocations give the weighted supremum Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y). Since a pure-middle triangle is allowed in its closed degree simplex, Q(x,c,y)>=(1/2)log c and Q(x,b,y)>=(1/2)log b. Hence the exact full simplex transform is sup_q [barH(q)+sum_f q_f log L_f] =max{Q(x,b,y)+Q(x,c,y), log b, log c}. (20) All weights in (18)--(20) are positive; degree-boundary allocations are included by the established continuous extension. Formula (20) is exactly the local weighted transform of the original positive Fejer endpoint source in the [complete Cauchy-capacity theorem](actual_complete_source_cauchy_capacity_gap.md). Thus replacing that source by the spectrally optimized sharp action does not improve the bound obtained by reoptimizing a single shared positive radius vector. The original face constraints still couple the radial motions. No shared maximum and infimum have been exchanged, and (20) proves neither (12) nor the universal volume comparison. ## scope and dependencies The weighted radial transform does not exchange the shared minimum and maximum. The non-CROSS filling implication retains its stated strict entropy hypothesis and fixed-twist quantifiers. The dependencies are the closed global sharp upper functional; the strict stationary branch derivatives and outer tilt equation; the fixed-degree delta=0 exclusion; the pole-endpoint exclusion; and the proved closed CROSS comparison. All occur in the existing source notes. No numerical search is used in this proof.

title: A spectral-pole endpoint cannot maximize the sharp shared functional
text: # A spectral-pole endpoint cannot maximize the sharp shared functional The sharp-pole calculus does not establish a lower rate or nonvanishing at sampled zeros. ## 1. Statement with the exact gain Fix 0<=mu<nu<=1, w=nu-mu>0, and any closed outer degree 0<=xi<=w. Use the original sharp full-row functional H_delta=B_delta+inf_(l in R)[Phi_delta(l)-xi l], B_delta=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta(t)|dt +int_nu^1 log|alpha_delta(t)|dt, Phi_delta(l)=int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt, alpha_delta(t)=4[cos^2(pi delta)-sin^2(pi t)]. (1) The two simple spectral poles at 0<delta_0<1/2 are p_-=1/2-delta_0, p_+=1/2+delta_0. Assume at least one endpoint mu or nu equals one of these poles. Let m be the number of such endpoint contacts, so m=1 or2. There is a sign s in {+1,-1} such that delta_epsilon=delta_0+s epsilon moves every contacted pole INTO the fixed active interval [mu,nu]. For all sufficiently small epsilon>0, H_(delta_epsilon)-H_(delta_0) =m epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon). (2) The constant is independent of xi, including xi=0,w, and independent of the outer Cauchy tilt. It is locally uniform on a compact fixed- contact stratum: delta stays inside(0,1/2), w stays positive, and every noncontact endpoint-to-pole distance has a positive lower bound. No uniformity as w->0 or delta approaches0,1/2 is asserted. Thus no such positive-length datum can maximize H with a free real spectral coordinate. The same conclusion holds in the original shared-flow problem: varying only this delta changes none of its face degrees, protected targets or row supplies. ## 2. There is always a compatible inward direction The four single-contact choices are mu=p_- : s=-1, nu=p_- : s=+1, mu=p_+ : s=+1, nu=p_+ : s=-1. (3) Both endpoints cannot equal the same pole because mu<nu. The only possible two-contact case is mu=p_-, nu=p_+, where s=-1 moves the lower pole right and the upper pole left. Thus no two endpoint contacts demand conflicting directions. Choose epsilon smaller than the fixed interval length and the other indicated separations. Protected mu=0 or nu=1 cannot itself be a pole at interior delta, but it is permitted as the other endpoint throughout this proof. ## 3. The original unused products supply one logarithmic gain per contact The exact factorization is log|alpha_delta(t)|=log4 +log|sin(pi(t-p_-(delta)))| +log|sin(pi(t-p_+(delta)))|. (4) For delta in a compact subset of(0,1/2), write each sine logarithm as log|t-p| plus log(|sin(pi(t-p))|/|t-p|). The latter extends smoothly through t=p and has uniformly bounded first derivatives on t in[0,1]. Its variation in either outside integral is O(epsilon). Suppose first that p=mu and p moves to mu+epsilon. Its lower unused prefix changes by EXACTLY int_0^mu [log(mu+epsilon-t)-log(mu-t)]dt =(mu+epsilon)log(mu+epsilon)-mu log mu -epsilon log epsilon =epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon). (5) Here mu is bounded away from0 because it is an interior spectral pole. The same pole's upper unused suffix is separated by w>0 and changes by O(epsilon). If p=nu and moves to nu-epsilon, the upper unused suffix has the same expression with mu replaced by 1-nu, while the prefix changes by O(epsilon). Any other pole not at an outside endpoint contributes O(epsilon), even if it lies INSIDE an unused interval. To see this without differentiating an absolute singular integrand, use the exact primitive F(r)=r log|r|-r, F(0)=0, int_a^b log|t-p|dt=F(b-p)-F(a-p). Its p derivative is finite whenever neither fixed endpoint equals p. The stated noncontact separations give the uniform bound. In the two-contact case apply (5) once to each endpoint. Therefore B_(delta_epsilon)-B_(delta_0) =m epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon). (6) This retains BOTH actual unused intervals. For a lower-half LEFT presentation, the omitted upper-half integral is exactly zero, so (6) agrees with the retained A_rest normalization. It is not a claim that a sampled zero finite product has a nonzero logarithm. ## 4. Uniform control of the active tail, before taking any infimum Write a=sin(pi t), k=cos(pi delta), s=sin(pi delta), A=x+y, P=xy and R=sqrt((x-y)^2 a^2+4Pk^2). The original tail root is Lambda=2a(Aa+R). For x,y>0 and 0<t<1, partial_delta log Lambda =-4pi Pks/[R(Aa+R)], |partial_delta log Lambda|<=pi tan(pi delta), (7) because R(Aa+R)>=R^2>=4Pk^2. This bound is independent of x/y, hence holds on ALL outer tilts, including unbounded sequences of tilts used to approach a closed coefficient degree. If P=0 the literal monomer root has zero delta derivative and satisfies the same bound. At t=0,1 use the integrable sine endpoint limit; a single endpoint of integration has measure zero. On a small fixed spectral interval around delta_0, integration of (7) gives |Phi_(delta_epsilon)(l)-Phi_(delta_0)(l)| <=C w epsilon (8) for EVERY real l, with the same C. Subtract xi l and take infima in both directions. Since the Legendre values are finite for 0<=xi<=w, their difference is bounded by Cw epsilon. This requires neither a finite minimizing tilt nor differentiability in xi. Combining (6) and (8) proves (2), with its exact integer m. ## 5. Actual source and shared-maximum scope The original finite coefficient is its unused-row scalar product times one coefficient of the actual full-interval K_(i,j). No tail recurrence is replaced by its absolute matrix, and no omitted-half mode is differentiated away. The separately proved uniform upper coefficient estimate uses positivity of the actual eta-word and upper logarithmic Riemann sums, so sampled zeros only improve that upper bound. Its tail estimate remains regular when a row endpoint meets alpha=0; the unused-product estimate already allows such zeros. Thus on otherwise regular coefficient charts, this pole calculus does not require a new finite LOWER coefficient theorem. For CROSS one may use the single full interval directly. There is no need to choose a possibly singular latent half allocation; the uniform estimate (8) survives its equivalent outer Legendre split. For LEFT or RIGHT the same argument uses the corresponding half interval. Closed outer degrees and an exact protected start0 or stop1 are permitted in the calculus statement. Consequently a genuine maximum of the sharp shared upper functional cannot have a positive-length interval with an endpoint at a free interior spectral pole. This does not remove diagonal intervals, terminal row seams unrelated to a pole, spectral0 or1/2 corners, ordinary-radius escape, phase-cocycle obstructions, or the need for an absolute bound on inconsistent-phase contributions. It also does not assert that arbitrary remaining KKT data are limits of coherent regular solutions. No numerical audit is required for the elementary integral identity and the tilt-uniform bound proved here. ## Dependencies The [original full-interval source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) and [positive eta-word](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) supply the finite source normalization. The [regular coefficient upper bound](research_sharp_regular_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md) and [shared stationary reduction](research_regular_shared_spectral_stationary_reduction.md) state the upper-functional setting used here. No phase-density or boundary-maximizer conclusion follows from this local calculation.

title: The original sharp interval functional is a uniform regular coefficient majorant
text: # The original sharp interval functional is a uniform regular coefficient majorant This compact regular-stratum majorant is an upper bound only. The boundary extension is a separate theorem; no lower rate or regularity of maximizers is inferred here. ## 1. One exact coefficient, on the original full row range Put d=N-1 and retain the original alpha_r=c_r-sigma and s_r=2sin(pi r/N). For ANY 0<=i<=j<=d, r=j-i and 0<=k<=r, the coefficient of x^k b^i c^(d-j)y^(r-k) in the full homogeneous numerator is, up to its recorded common unit sign, a_N=(prod_(a<i) alpha_a)(prod_(a>j) alpha_a) [x^k y^(r-k)] K_(i,j). (1) This is the exact original start/end expansion, not a decomposition through separately signed central cofactors. In particular it covers CROSS directly and includes the odd central visited/skipped paths in the same K. Its total degree is exactly d. If j is in the lower half, the second outside product includes the original A_rest factor; equivalently retain A_rest separately and the unused lower suffix. No division by A_rest or by a sampled alpha is made. The normalized K has the positive eta-word expansion whenever lambda_N=cos(pi/N)+cos(2pi delta)>=0. On any fixed real spectral compact 0<=delta<=delta_max<1/2 this holds for all sufficiently large N. The word proof applies on the ENTIRE range i+2<=a<=j<=d: cos(pi/N)-cos((2a-1)pi/N)>0 there, and s_a,s_(a-1)>0. Thus its coefficients are nonnegative even across the central row. For every finite real tilt l, Cauchy's elementary coefficient bound is [x^k y^(r-k)]K <= exp(-k l) K_(i,j)(exp(l),1). (2) All signs of the original outside products remain outside K. A zero sampled factor makes a_N zero and automatically satisfies every upper bound below. Both parities are treated by (1); there is no odd bare- endpoint reference substituted for an actual coefficient. ## 2. Uniform weighted tails and outside products Write mu=i/N, nu=j/N, xi=k/N. On positive compact tilt sets the existing fixed-block transfer proof gives, uniformly in all interval endpoints, N^(-1)log K_(i,j)(exp(l),1) <=int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt+o(1). (3) For clarity the same proof genuinely covers full intervals, not just ones ending at1/2. After dividing K by prod s_a, its two-by-two transfer has bounded entries on [0,1] and limiting spectral radius rho=A sin(pi t)+sqrt((x-y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4xy cos^2(pi delta)). On [eta,1-eta] this is uniformly positive. Cayley--Hamilton bounds each fixed block by C(k+1)rho^k without an eigenbasis inverse; freezing a fixed large block and then letting N grow proves its integral upper bound. The endpoint intervals of length eta cost O(eta N), and their missing logarithmic integral costs O(eta log(1/eta)N). Restore prod s_a and send eta to0. This proves (3) with Lambda=2sin(pi t)rho. It also covers an exact protected start i=0 or stop j=d when such a chart is retained. The original outside products satisfy uniformly N^(-1)log |prod_(a<i)alpha_a prod_(a>j)alpha_a| <=int_0^mu log|alpha_delta(t)|dt +int_nu^1 log|alpha_delta(t)|dt+o(1). (4) Truncate log from below before the Riemann sum. The truncated function is jointly continuous; the translated cosine-log factors have uniformly integrable singularities. Their truncation errors tend uniformly to0. This proves an UPPER sum estimate even at arbitrarily close sampled zeros. A finite sum's value -infinity at an exact zero is harmless. For a lower-half presentation the exact A_rest has |A_rest|<=poly(N), including its zeros, and int_(1/2)^1 log|alpha_delta|=0. Thus (4) agrees with the retained omitted-half normalization, rather than deleting it. Combining (1)--(4), uniformly for l in a fixed compact interval, gives N^(-1)log|a_N| <= B_delta^full(mu,nu) +int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt-xi l+o(1), (5) where B^full denotes the two displayed outside integrals. The o(1) depends on the compact chart, not on the integer rows or spectral nodes. ## 3. Taking the actual finite Cauchy tilt Consider any compact regular chart with nu-mu>=w_*>0, xi/(nu-mu) in [epsilon,1-epsilon], and delta<=delta_max<1/2. Rows may be required a fixed distance from the endpoints for ordinary charts; fixed protected i=0 or j=d is also allowed. The continuum tilt minimizing the right side of (5) is unique and ranges over a FIXED compact real interval. Indeed the logarithmic root has the strictly positive second l derivative printed in the stationary reduction. Its first derivative lies in(0,1) and tends to0 and1 as l tends to negative and positive infinity. These limits are uniform on t in [eta,1-eta] and on the spectral compact. The omitted endpoint intervals have arbitrarily small length and the derivative is bounded by1 there. This proves uniform convergence of the integrated first derivative to0 and nu-mu and bounds the minimizing tilt. Strict positivity on an interior subinterval gives uniqueness. We may therefore choose THAT finite tilt in (5), with the SAME uniform error. Define H_delta(mu,nu,xi)=B_delta^full(mu,nu) +inf_l[int_mu^nu log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)dt-xi l]. (6) Then on every such compact regular chart, at BOTH parities, limsup_(N->infinity) sup_chart [N^(-1)log|a_N|-H_delta(mu,nu,xi)] <=0. (7) This is exactly the required uniform coefficient LIMSUP majorant. There is no lower asymptotic and no exclusion of A_rest zeros. If an outer face is protected, specialize the exact monomer first: K=x^r prod_(i<a<=j)s_a^2 or its y version. Its coefficient has the same upper formula with the corresponding closed outer-degree entropy, by the ordinary sine-log Riemann bound. No finite tilt of a zero outer weight is used. These fixed protected strata may be included; uniform approach through arbitrary additional vanishing ordinary loads is a separate assertion, not needed for (7). ## 4. LEFT and CROSS are precisely the sharp functionals For a LEFT interval nu<1/2, the identity int_(1/2)^1 log|alpha_delta|=0 makes (6) exactly h_delta in the stationary reduction, including both unused lower intervals. RIGHT is the actual reflected interval. For CROSS put tau=1-nu. Both alpha and Lambda are symmetric under t->1-t. Write B_a=int_0^a log|alpha_delta(t)|dt; then (6) is B_mu+B_tau+inf_l[Phi_(mu,1/2)(l)+Phi_(tau,1/2)(l)-xi l]. (8) This equals the MAXIMUM of the two half-cofactor Legendre entropies over the original outer split xi_1+xi_2=xi. One can prove this without any joint row concavity: each half entropy is bounded above by its weighted value at the common tilt, so their sum is at most (8). At the minimizing common tilt set xi_a=Phi_a'(l); then both half Legendre infima attain this tilt and equality follows. On regular charts these are strict positive splits; limiting splits require their separately stated boundary interpretation. Thus the latent CROSS split functional used in the stationary audit is a valid coefficient UPPER majorant. We never estimate a positive cofactor and then subtract a signed central correction: the original single K_(i,j) in (1) handles that correction before any bound. The physical degrees divided by d, rather than N, satisfy the original unit targets exactly. Their row/outer parameters differ by O(1/N). On the compact regular charts H and its split versions are uniformly continuous (including spectral delta=0 away from row/pole collisions), so this changes (7) by o(1). The upper reflected start is (d-j)/N rather than 1-j/N; its one-row difference is treated the same way. No finite support endpoint or protected target is reset. ## 5. The literal shared coefficient Fix the original diagram with finitely many ports. Restrict its degree sum to any product of the compact regular charts above, imposing the ONE original ordinary target d and the two protected targets0. There are at most (d+1)^(4R) incidence arrays. Apply (7) to each local coefficient, multiply, and use the triangle inequality on the actual coefficient sum. It is bounded by exp{N[sup_(original feasible flows in the charts) sum_e H_delta,e+o(1)]}. (9) The logarithm of the number of arrays is o(N) for fixed diagram. The same bound with the limiting closed feasible flow set follows by compactness and continuity; no lattice LOWER approximation is needed. For CROSS use its equal split representation (8). Each Cauchy tilt was allowed to depend on the LOCAL coefficient being bounded. This is legitimate before the original shared extraction; it is not replacing the original face constraints by independent weighted source maxima. Common face weights arise later from the linear-target stationary equations at an extremum of (9). Hence an every-level remote coefficient limit is NOT a remaining requirement for this upper-bound route on regular compacts. The stationary reduction may be applied to maxima of the proven majorant in (9). Its other restrictions remain: chart boundaries and phase incompatibility, and comparison of cancellation loss with Phi rather than only with a potentially larger positive envelope. No lower bound, nonzero quantum amplitude, or original-cycle contribution is asserted. ## 6. Separate checked maximum exclusion at the spectral cap For the full-row functional (6), the endpoint delta=1/2 has Lambda=4sin^2(pi t) max(x,y), |alpha|=4sin^2(pi t), and total alpha integral0. Thus H_cap=0 for every closed outer degree. Fix a positive-length interval [mu,nu] strictly inside(0,1). Put kappa=cos(pi delta)>0 and choose kappa<min_[mu,nu]sin(pi t). On that interval Lambda_delta>=4sin^2(pi t)max(x,y), |alpha_delta|=4[sin^2(pi t)-kappa^2]. Therefore, uniformly over ALL tilts, log L_delta>=log max(x,y) -log(1-kappa^2/sin^2(pi t)). Take the same Legendre infimum; the integral of the second term is strictly positive. Hence H_delta>H_cap=0 at fixed rows and outer degree, preserving every shared face load. Such an interval cannot maximize at the cap. The statement includes closed outer degrees but NOT a protected fixed start mu=0 or stop nu=1. It is a separate calculus exclusion for the majorant, not a boundary-uniform finite coefficient theorem. The protected-cap case remains open here. ## Source dependencies and verification scope The finite coefficient (1) is the path expansion of the [original four-state source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md). The [positive eta-word](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) gives the exact coefficient positivity; the [global CROSS proof](actual_global_cross_spectral_gap.md) gives the fixed-block upper estimate and unused-product logarithmic bounds. The [stationary reduction](research_regular_shared_spectral_stationary_reduction.md) uses the resulting sharp functional without claiming local strong duality. The protected-monomer comparison has the stated compact regular scope.

title: The constrained Hessian of the original sharp source
text: # The constrained Hessian of the original sharp source 31 October 2026. **analytical research reduction.** This derives an exact second-variation test on the original shared transport fiber. The local obstruction below shows why an odd MAIN four-cycle does not alone supply an unstable direction. It is not a globally realized stable maximum, an absolute source bound, or a volume theorem. ## 1. The actual fixed-spectrum row Hessian Use the [full-fiber activation](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md) and [stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md). Work at a classified datum with finite common positive ordinary weights, on its actual protected-coordinate face. All ordinary incidences are positive. For the restricted non-CROSS maximum, retain the hypothesis that its value is at least Phi_D and that some middle load is strictly greater than 1/2; then the small two-sided variations used below remain admissible. At a LEFT Green write q=(xi,mu,1-nu,nu-mu-xi), with actual common weights (x,b,c,y). Put g(t,l,delta)=log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1)-log|alpha_delta(t)|, a(t)=partial_l log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1), V=int_mu^nu partial_l^2 log Lambda_delta(t;exp(l),1) dt. The alpha and Lambda are exactly those of the full sharp functional; both unused intervals are retained. At the actual minimizing tilt, V>0 when both outer incidences are ordinary. Differentiation of that Legendre minimum gives, at fixed delta, d^2 h_delta = -g_t(mu) dmu^2 + g_t(nu) dnu^2 -[-a(mu)dmu+a(nu)dnu-dxi]^2/V. (1) There is no omitted scalar or spectral normalization in (1). The common weighted linear face terms have zero Hessian. A strict straddling Green has g_t(mu)>0 and g_t(nu)<0, so (1) is negative definite in the free local row coordinates. Protected middle coordinates are omitted, not varied. If one outer incidence is protected, specialize the exact monomer first: there is no independent xi coordinate or tilt, and only the two diagonal row terms remain. RIGHT is the literal row reflection. At a complete CROSS port the same argument at delta=0 applies: its start lies before 1/2 and its stop after 1/2, so the two row signs in (1) again give negative definiteness. Equivalently, write its entropy as the maximum of C(alpha)+C(beta) over the actual latent two-triangle split. On all free triangle coordinates, f''(t)=-2pi/sin(2pi t)<=-2pi. The projection to the four original loads has squared operator norm at most 2. Consequently d^2 h_CROSS(q)[v,v] <= -pi ||v||^2 (2) for every original row-tangent v, with protected coordinates removed. This follows either by differentiating the unique latent optimizer or directly from strong concavity and the same linear projection. The permitted protected monomial half contributes no independent coordinate; the other half supplies the remaining strict concavity. Thus the negative fixed-spectrum row Hessian K is positive definite on the product of the free noncap row-coordinate spaces. This does not say that the joint row/spectral Hessian is negative definite. ## 2. Exact original-target Schur complement Let v collect the noncap row displacements in any fixed linear row-simplex coordinates. Let s collect the spectral displacements of the strict Green ports. Hold the complete CROSS spectra at zero and cap spectra at 1/2 for this test. At the stationary datum write the second variation as Q(v,s)=-v^T K v+2v^T B s+s^T D s, (3) where B is the actual mixed row/spectral derivative and D is diagonal because spectra are local to the original coupons. No separate local maximum or local-to-global minimax exchange is asserted. If there are no residual caps, let T be the original ordinary-face balance map in these row coordinates: feasible v satisfy Tv=0. Redundant face equations are retained harmlessly. If residual caps are present, let T_0 be the noncap face map and T_cap the actual cap row map. A cap action is identically zero at its held spectrum. Its free row displacement w can compensate precisely T_0 v in im(T_cap). Hence set T=P T_0, where P is the orthogonal projection onto ker(T_cap^T). Then Tv=0 is exactly the condition that some actual cap displacement w makes the original face targets unchanged. All ordinary loads are positive, so these infinitesimal row displacements are realized by sufficiently small positive and negative displacements in the original fiber. This elimination is linear second-variation bookkeeping, not a change of the source or a new merged-face theorem. Define W=D+B^T K^(-1)B, R=T K^(-1)B, C=T K^(-1)T^T. The Moore--Penrose inverse C^dagger is needed only for redundant target equations. Since range(C)=range(T), every column of R is in range(C). Completing the square, or a constrained quadratic minimization, gives max_(Tv=0) Q(v,s)=s^T [W-R^T C^dagger R] s, (4) v_*=K^(-1)B s-K^(-1)T^T C^dagger R s. (5) Thus a positive eigenvalue of S=W-R^T C^dagger R (6) excludes the alleged sharp maximum. A genuine maximum necessarily has S<=0. Conversely S<=0 only passes this particular second-order test; it does not establish a local maximum or a global maximum. The matrix R^T C^dagger R is the exact nonnegative cost of repairing the row-optimal spectral displacement to the original face targets. The diagonal entries of W at a strict Green are positive. In fact the local row-optimal response at held common weights is K_e^(-1)B_e.
