The present result gives a checkable sign obstruction to one proposed real-to-complex reconstruction, and an exact polynomial normalization when that obstruction vanishes. It asserts neither that every global critical point has trivial sign obstruction nor that every soluble cocycle yields a contribution to the original cycle.

title: Every positive-value non-CROSS sharp maximum has an elementary odd MAIN cycle
status: Every non-CROSS maximum port forces an odd MAIN four-cycle
text:
# Every positive-value non-CROSS sharp maximum has an elementary odd MAIN cycle 31 October 2026. This source/combinatorial theorem uses full-fiber activation and stationary classification. It does not construct a representation or prove an absolute exponential phase gap, and uses no cap collar. ## 1. Exact hypotheses inherited from the original maximum Work with the actual certified simple-white marked plat and its original ordinary face targets \(1\), protected pair \(u,v\), and triangle pairing across MATCHING edges. Every MAIN edge has two incident triangles belonging to different ports. Let \(q\) and the common positive ordinary weights \(L\) be the data supplied by [finite-multiplier and stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md). In particular every ordinary incidence is positive, the supported port/ordinary-face graph is connected, and each port is one of: * strict CROSS at \(\delta=0\), whose incidence character is constant; * strict Green, with one negative half and overloaded ordinary middle \(o\), \(q_{e,o}>1/2\), and \[ L_o-L_p= rac{L_x+L_y}{\sin^2(\pi\delta)},\qquad 0<\delta<	frac12; 	ag{1} \] * a residual cap, with the two protected faces as one outer and the parent middle; its two ordinary incidences are outer \(a\) and overloaded middle \(o\), with \[ q_{e,a}=
u,\quad q_{e,o}=1-
u,\quad 0<
u<	frac12,\qquad L_o=L_a. 	ag{2} \] For a Green, the literal source character on its negative half is \(1\) at its overloaded middle and \(0\) at its outers; its other half has character \(0\). For a cap, the two supported ordinary characters differ by \(1\). This is the exact alternating monomer character, up to a constant row gauge. These statements are unchanged by original RIGHT reflection or outer exchange. No globally coherent signs are assumed. Here is a direct source derivation of the character table. In the [exact full-interval source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md), write \(\alpha_r=c_r-\sigma\) and retain every unused prefix and suffix factor. On a strict LEFT straddling window the prefix is positive and the lower-half suffix has sign \((-1)^{M-j}\). The [positive word expansion](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) makes the coefficients of \(K_{i,j}\) nonnegative for every sufficiently large level at a fixed strict spectrum. Thus, after retaining the common raw sign and omitted-half scalar, the varying sign is \((-1)^j\). The original middle monomial is \(c^{d-j}\), so this is exactly the character \(c\mapsto-c\), up to a degree-independent row sign. The common scalar is not divided out; at a sampled zero the source is zero. At the complete endpoint the same unused factors and tail coefficients are nonnegative, up to the common raw sign, giving the constant CROSS character. Literal row reflection gives RIGHT. The [flat-cap formula](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) gives the remaining character directly, including its raw sign at both parities. No geometric collar is needed for this table. A supported four-cycle \(e-f-e'-g-e\) has sign sum \[ \varepsilon_{e,f}+\varepsilon_{e',f} +\varepsilon_{e',g}+\varepsilon_{e,g}\quad	ext{in }\mathbf F_2. 	ag{3} \] It is odd precisely when the two ports' edge differences on \(f,g\) differ. The test retains actual incidences and is invariant under all row gauges and common face signs. ## 2. Every strict Green gives an odd MAIN four-cycle At a strict Green choose an ordinary outer \(a\). Such an outer exists: the two protected faces form a MAIN pair, whereas the two outers form a MATCHING pair. Write \(o\) for the overloaded middle of the negative half. Both endpoints of the MAIN edge \(oa\) are ordinary. Equation (1) gives \[ L_o>L_p+L_x+L_y\ge L_a.	ag{4} \] Thus \(L_o>L_a\) also when the other outer or parent is protected. The original edge \(oa\) has a second triangle at a different port \(e'\). The chosen Green has edge-character difference \(1\). We show that the second triangle has edge-character difference \(0\). A positive Green half or a CROSS half has that difference \(0\). If it is a negative Green half with difference \(1\), its overloaded middle must be \(o\) or \(a\): a MAIN edge joins a port middle to an outer. The two possibilities are impossible: * overload at \(o\) would put two distinct loads greater than \(1/2\) on the same original demand-one face; * overload at \(a\) would require \(L_a>L_o\) by its own version of (4). If the second triangle belongs to a residual cap and has both ordinary endpoints \(o,a\), it is the cap's ordinary output edge. Equation (2) would require \(L_o=L_a\), also impossible. These exhaust the classified ports. Thus the actual radial four-cycle \(e-o-e'-a-e\) is odd. The conclusion needs only (1), the exact sign table, original MAIN typing and face demands. It does not use a Green collar or representation volume. ## 3. Residual caps also give an odd MAIN four-cycle at positive value At a cap \(e\) let \(o,a\) be its ordinary output pair. They have equal positive weights and opposite incidence characters. Their MAIN edge has its other triangle at \(e'\). A noncap triangle cannot have opposite characters on this edge: a negative Green would require one of the equal weights to exceed the other strictly, while positive and CROSS halves have equal characters. Therefore the cycle is odd unless \(e'\) is itself a cap on the same pair. The latter case is incompatible with a positive-value maximum. Both caps have all their supply on the same two ordinary faces. The second cap cannot overload \(o\), since \(e\) already supplies more than \(1/2\) there; it must overload \(a\). Write the two parameters as \(
u\) and \(
u'\). Face demands imply \[ 1-
u+
u'\le1,\qquad 
u+1-
u'\le1, \] so \(
u'=
u\) and both demands are saturated by these two rows. Ordinary incidence positivity excludes every other port from both faces. The two cap ports have no other ordinary incidence. They and the two faces form a whole connected component of the supported graph. Connectedness then forces the entire source to consist of these two caps, whose sharp entropy is zero. This contradicts the positive-value hypothesis, in particular a global maximum at or above \(\Phi_D>0\). There is an independent literal sphere check of the exceptional geometry. After locally naming the protected pair \(u,v\), the first cap triangles are \((u,v,a)\) and \((u,o,a)\), paired across \(ua\). If the other triangle on \(oa\) is another cap output, its protected vertex must be \(v\). Its input must then be \((u,v,o)\): choosing ordinary outer \(a\) would repeat the first input triangle. The four triangles are exactly the boundary of a tetrahedron on \(u,v,o,a\). Every edge is already incident to two of them, so connectedness of the triangulated sphere leaves no other triangle. This is not a claim that the tetrahedral source cannot exist; its all-cap action is simply zero. Thus every residual cap at the positive-value data in §1 has its own explicit odd MAIN four-cycle as well. ## 4. Consequence and exact remaining limitation At every unrestricted global maximum, or competing strict-NC maximum of value at least \(\Phi_D\) under the stationary theorem's hypotheses, each non-CROSS port has an elementary odd supported four-cycle. In particular there is no common solution \[ \varepsilon_{e,f}=\gamma_f+\kappa_e \] unless every port is complete CROSS. In the restricted non-CROSS problem, this statement requires at least one middle load strictly greater than \(1/2\); it makes no assertion about a seam-only constrained maximum. A phase-coherent maximum therefore belongs entirely to the original complete endpoint problem. Its value is at most \(\Phi_D\), and the endpoint unique-max theorem identifies equality when that comparison is used. A competing non-CROSS maximum of high value is necessarily phase-inconsistent. An odd cycle alone is NOT an absolute upper bound for the oscillatory source. On regular windows the cycle-packing theorem subtracts an explicit local phase loss from a positive envelope; comparing that result to \(\Phi_D\) remains necessary. Residual flat caps do not automatically satisfy a regular-window exponential angular gap. The [exact flat-cap calculation](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) exhibits this limitation. No full invariant or volume theorem is inferred. Dependencies are the [full-fiber boundary reduction](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md), [stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md), [exact source expansion](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md), and [original MAIN/MATCHING dictionary](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). The [flat-cap companion](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) retains its exact raw coefficient and phase.

title: Composition of original matched-disk boundary data
text: # Composition of original matched-disk boundary data 31 October 2026. **exact-source and analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. This is an exact composition law for admissible disk modules built from WHOLE original matched ports. It concerns the actual positive CROSS source and its classical boundary response. It does not assert that every Conway/arborescent tangle admits this geometry, that arbitrary diagonal changes preserve a filled knot, or that signed quantum volume gaps follow from composing classical curves. ## 1. The compositional object retains weights, loads and the primitive A module is a finite union of original matched triangle pairs, with all its boundary edges MAIN. Its coupons retain their ordered frames. Protected face weights are set to zero before every extraction. Let I be its ordinary vertices whose original targets are internal to the module, and B its remaining ordinary boundary vertices. For every ordinary graph component require a vertex in B. Suppose the module has one finite positive weight assignment with all supported ordinary incidences positive and every I load equal to one. At the actual CROSS endpoint define, at either parity, \[ P_{\mathcal M,N}(L_B) =\left[\prod_{i\in I}L_i^d\right] \prod_{e\in\mathcal M}P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2;L), \qquad d=N-1.\tag{1} \] Every actual coupon scalar and fixed raw sign is retained, or a single declared product of its fixed raw unit signs is removed consistently. The degree in all boundary weights is \[ \deg P_{\mathcal M,N}=d\kappa_{\mathcal M},\qquad \kappa_{\mathcal M}=|\operatorname{ports}(\mathcal M)|-|I|.\tag{2} \] The object is this original coefficient module, not a separately closed tangle invariant with a guessed pivotal trace. No new cup/cap normalization is introduced along the cut. Let z_b=log L_b and put \[ F_{\mathcal M}(z_B) =\inf_{w_I}\left\{\sum_{t\in\mathcal M}Q_t(L)-\sum_{i\in I}w_i\right\}. \tag{3} \] The recession proof of the [algebraic boundary-pressure theorem](research_cap_algebraic_boundary_curve_and_volume_period.md) applies verbatim: the known strict allocation makes every recession summand nonnegative; equality forces a constant on every supported triangle and hence zero after the boundary anchors. The grounded Hessian is positive definite at every finite positive weight. Thus the minimizer is unique and finite for every finite real z_B, and F_M is real analytic there. Define the actual lifted boundary loads and phases \[ q_{\mathcal M,b}=\partial_{z_b}F_{\mathcal M},\qquad B_{\mathcal M,b}=\exp(2\pi i q_{\mathcal M,b}).\tag{4} \] They obey sum_B q_(M,b)=kappa_M by homogeneity. The phase tuple does not determine these integer lifts or the absolute value of F_M. As before, introduce positive square roots T_t^2=ab+ac+bc for every nonmonomial triangle, retain pure-corner factors -1, and impose the interior equations prod_t (T_t+iL_i)/(T_t-iL_i)=1 with their original load-one lifts. The invertible interior Jacobian makes the selected boundary phases algebraic functions of the boundary weights. Their graph defines an algebraic boundary correspondence on the selected regular component, with differential \[ dF_{\mathcal M}=\sum_{b\in B}q_{\mathcal M,b}\,d\log L_b, \qquad \sum_b d\log B_{\mathcal M,b}\wedge d\log L_b=0.\tag{5} \] The latter follows from Hessian symmetry. The graph has dimension |B| in the 2|B|-dimensional boundary weight/phase torus; locally it is Lagrangian for that displayed logarithmic symplectic form. Common scaling is retained, with its known linear primitive kappa_M log(scale). This is source boundary data, not an asserted knot character variety. At odd levels the actual stable positive determinants and the anchored ordinary phase graph give the same finite positive saddle as in the one-cap pressure theorem, now with several external z coordinates: the interior torus has one angular maximum, a positive grounded Hessian and an analytic critical point on a fixed small complex boundary neighborhood. Its normalized logarithm tends to F_M there. The determinant and original coefficient measures retain their polynomial N factors. This statement uses the actual positive source; it is not an assertion about a negative-axis or truncated signed sum. ## 2. Admissible disk gluing and exact finite coefficients Take two such modules with disjoint port interiors. Identify a specified MAIN boundary arc of the first with a specified MAIN boundary arc of the second, reversing boundary orientation and respecting the recorded vertex labels and bipartite colors. Alternatively glue their entire boundary circles to form a sphere. Within each old module the map on vertices is injective. All old matching edges and ordered port disks remain internal and unchanged. Identified vertices must agree in their protected/ordinary status. If a proposed new mark changes that status, first specialize the newly protected labels to zero in BOTH module definitions, then recheck their stated positivity and anchoring hypotheses. One cannot glue a positive ordinary boundary variable to a protected zero and silently keep the old positive pressure branch. This constructs the usual disk or sphere cellulation. For a geometric simple-white application it must additionally have no loops, repeated edges or repeated vertices in a port. The last condition follows from the injectivity just stated; repeated edges from two old diagonals are an actual possible obstruction and must be checked. These are explicit combinatorial admissibility conditions, not automatic facts about arbitrary Conway compositions. For an OPEN glued module impose an additional anchoring condition: EVERY resulting ordinary graph component must meet a retained ordinary boundary vertex. This does not follow merely because both child modules were anchored; gluing may consume their last anchors. If an unanchored component is instead a balanced closed component, treat its scalar coefficient factor separately and fix one common scale in that component for the classical minimization. A strict load-one solution requires its total triangle supply to equal its total ordinary demand; an unbalanced closed component has no such branch. For an eligible full sphere with connected ordinary graph, in particular with the original protected adjacent MAIN pair, one global scale is enough. Let S consist of the identified ORDINARY boundary vertices that become internal and acquire their original demand one. Shared vertices that remain on the external boundary keep a single common boundary weight. Protected vertices retain zero weight and are never assigned a d extraction. Under the literal source identification, \[ P_{\mathcal M_1\cup\mathcal M_2,N}(L_B) =\left[\prod_{s\in S}L_s^d\right] P_{\mathcal M_1,N}(L_{B_1})P_{\mathcal M_2,N}(L_{B_2}).\tag{6} \] This is simply the coefficient of the product of the same original coupons: the two sets of old internal variables are disjoint, and they are absent from the other module. Coefficient extractions therefore commute. Shared unextracted variables are identified before the last extraction. There is no independent variable for a repeated face occurrence, no shifted residual target, and no missing normalization. The degree check is kappa_glued=kappa_1+kappa_2-|S|. The right side of (6) is not claimed to preserve joint real stability under an arbitrary total-degree projection. It uses the precise individual original face extractions. If a different tangle operation requires a total degree or a linear combination of cut states, (6) does not silently replace that operation. ## 3. Classical pressures and algebraic boundary correspondences compose The exact classical law corresponding to (6) is \[ F_{\mathrm{glued}}(z_B) =\inf_{z_S}\left\{F_1(z_{B_1})+F_2(z_{B_2})-\sum_{s\in S}z_s\right\}. \tag{7} \] Indeed expanding (3) on the right gives the joint infimum over ALL old interior weights and the new shared interior weights of the sum of the unchanged triangle potentials with each interior target log subtracted exactly once. This is exactly the definition of the glued pressure. Infimum associativity proves (7) even at a boundary dual limit; no exchange with a shared entropy maximum is used. For a finite strict positive glued branch satisfying the resulting anchoring condition, the same coercivity and Hessian argument gives unique finite minimizers. Each balanced closed component is instead handled with its separate scalar factor and one scale fixed, as just specified. In an eligible full sphere with connected ordinary graph, in particular with the original protected adjacent MAIN pair, this is the single common scale. At each shared interior face the actual gluing condition is \[ q_{1,s}+q_{2,s}=1,\qquad B_{1,s}B_{2,s}=1.\tag{8} \] The SECOND equation alone loses the required integer. At a retained boundary face b the loads add over its actual old occurrences and the phases multiply: \[ q_{\mathrm{glued},b}=\sum_{i:\,b\in B_i}q_{i,b},\qquad B_{\mathrm{glued},b}=\prod_{i:\,b\in B_i}B_{i,b}.\tag{9} \] Thus the algebraic boundary correspondence composes by matching common weights, imposing the phase equations in (8), and eliminating the shared variables, while retaining the original load-one lift and the selected positive branch. Elimination without those choices may keep unrelated components or wrong integer loads. The pressure primitive composes with the explicit target correction: \[ F_{\mathrm{glued}}=F_1+F_2-\sum_{s\in S}\log L_s.\tag{10} \] evaluated at the shared critical weights. Differentiating (10), the shared-weight terms vanish by the FIRST equation in (8), leaving exactly the external differential in (5). Therefore the corresponding relative logarithmic periods add, with their original absolute base constants and the displayed target-log term. The eliminated curve alone does not retain those constants. Finite coefficient associativity, joint infimum associativity and the lifted equations prove associativity of these laws for any finite admissible assembly of modules. This is a closure theorem for actual source boundary data, not just a relabeling of a list of knot families. ## 4. What this supplies for a tangle formulation When a tangle decomposition is represented by such cuts of actual ordered matched-port disks, the original source coefficient and its positive boundary curve/period can be computed module by module using (6)-(10). If the resulting simple matched sphere carries the eligible original protected adjacent MAIN pair and the hypotheses of the original complete-packing theorem, that theorem identifies the full complete critical value with its original drilled hyperbolic volume. The inherited zero set and mark are part of this hypothesis, not consequences of simplicity alone. Nothing in the composition requires calling the whole diagram a bridge presentation. To apply this to a proposed Conway/algebraic tangle operation one must still verify its literal MAIN-arc boundary identification, original coupon frames and face targets, and the simplicity/packing hypotheses of the resulting source. This note does not identify every algebraic knot with such an assembly or transport integer long fillings through a rotated diagonal. The signed non-CROSS/cap cancellation inequality, even-parity negative-axis adapter, and filled-period estimates remain their separate original-source questions. ## Inputs The [original homogeneous source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md) and [matched-sphere Morse construction](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) retain the literal ordered port disks, face variables and target extractions used in (1) and (6). The [triangle entropy theorem](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) fixes the local half-supply potentials in (3). The [algebraic boundary-pressure theorem](research_cap_algebraic_boundary_curve_and_volume_period.md) supplies the coercivity, regular algebraic branch and retained-load arguments generalized to several boundary variables here. The [actual CROSS determinant factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) and [positive face-coefficient saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) supply the odd-level positive pressure identification. The [complete packing capacity](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) supplies the drilled-volume identification only under the original marked packing hypotheses stated in section 4. Every resulting ordinary component must satisfy the stated anchoring condition. Gluing also preserves protected versus ordinary status and the inherited marked pair. No numerical audit is used or claimed. This theorem composes actual admissible source boundary data. It does not prove that every Conway tangle operation preserves the required source geometry, identify a knot A-polynomial, transport arbitrary fillings, or supply an unsigned or signed non-CROSS volume bound.

title: Trace-one top marks and the exact protected cap-turn interface
text: # Trace-one top marks and the exact protected cap-turn interface 31 October 2026. These exact finite identities delimit two proposed cap simplifications. They neither rewire the diagram nor establish an absolute shared-source or volume bound. ## 1. Any trace-one matrix at the same original top cap Fix the original complete-colored polynomial-Casimir source and one top cap, with all full crossings and original turn conventions retained. Write d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and x0=q^d. In the balanced basis the ordinary cap and the original unrestricted marked cap are ell_(i,j)=x0^j g_i/N delta_(i+j,d), m_(i,j)=x0^j/N^2. For ANY matrix e, insert D_e=g^(-1)e on the same primal cap input. The literal contraction, before a support restriction, gives m^e_(i,j)=x0^j/N * e_(d-j,i). (1) Every polynomial Casimir coupon and the actual R/R^-1 preserves the unwrapped total of its two physical heads. The original bottom cups and other top caps therefore force i+j=d at the exposed top pair. On this actual whole-source support, m^e_(i,j)=N e_(i,i) m_(i,j). (2) Off-diagonal entries do not contribute. In particular e=E_aa gives m^a_(i,j)=x0^j/N delta_(i,a)delta_(j,d-a), m^a p=1, p_(i,j)=N x0^(-j)delta_(i+j,d). (3) The [scalar-open-cap proof](research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.md) shows that the remaining vector is a scalar times this original cup. Thus its evaluation by (1) is that scalar times Tr(e). Every e with Tr(e)=1 gives exactly the same full marked scalar, including e=E_aa. No positivity, idempotence or generic-q normalization is required for e. This is a statement for the full original source, not transport of e through a projected local sector. ## 2. Exact face-grid meaning: fixing a clock does not change the targets The original centered head formula at this top cap is q^(d i)=q^(d^2/2)(L_u/L_v)^(d/2). Its lifted clock equality, equivalently the explicit physical head assignment, is L_v/L_u=q^(d-2i)=x0 Q^(-i). (4) Therefore (3) fixes L_v/L_u=t_a=x0 Q^(-a). At odd N this is an ordinary Q-grid point; at even N it is on the original odd gap-parity coset. No half-power lift or head offset is changed. Let P=prod_e H_(f_e) be the original homogeneous numerator, of total degree dR. Fix L_u=1. The original marked source is the normalized N^(R+1)-point average of P(1,L_v,L_ordinary)/prod_ordinary L_f^d. Equation (2) multiplies by N and restricts the one v-grid coordinate to t_a. Thus the E_aa-marked source is EXACTLY N^(-R) sum_(original ordinary grid) P(1,t_a,L_ordinary)/prod_ordinary L_f^d. (5) All exponents of P are nonnegative. Each ordinary grid average requires an exponent congruent to d modulo N, whose least nonnegative value is d. There are R ordinary faces and total degree dR. Consequently EVERY ordinary exponent equals d and both u,v exponents equal zero. The remaining even-grid phases are one, because each exponent equals its target. It follows that (5) is [prod_ordinary L_f^d] P |_(L_u=L_v=0), (6) independently of a or the nonzero value t_a. More generally (2) gives Tr(e) times (6). All N factors have been accounted for: the factor N in (2) cancels the removed v average, and no extra mark scalar remains. In particular the alternate E_00 mark does NOT replace the protected-zero coefficient by a positive ordinary-radius coefficient or eliminate its cap corners. A physical marked head index a fixes a face clock; it is not the polynomial row-degree index j of a cap coefficient. Identifying these indices would require another actual source transform. ## 3. The cap comparison polynomial is an actual crossing corner modulus Now specialize the ordered local quartet to x=b=0. Put theta=pi/N. At sigma=+2 the literal full numerator has H_V(0,0,c,y)=sum_(j=0)^d (-1)^j A_j c^(d-j)y^j, A_j=csc^2(theta/2) prod_(r=1)^j sin^2(r theta)/sin^2((r+1/2)theta). (7) This follows from the exact full-interval expansion and the shifted sine product prod_(r=0)^d 4sin^2((r+1/2)theta)=4. It includes both parities and the omitted half. The ratios A_j/A_(j-1) are less than one up to the unique middle crossing of sin(j theta)=sin((j+1/2)theta), then greater than one. Hence the maximum occurs at an endpoint. A_0=csc^2(theta/2)<=N^2 by the elementary sine chord bound, and the ordinary sine product gives A_d=N^2. Thus 0<A_j<=N^2 for every j. Any original LEFT window is a subpolynomial of this coefficient modulus. The published exact normalized crossing coefficient on b^i x^k y^l c^t, i+k+l+t=d, is (-1)^(k+l+1) q^[kl-(i+1)(t+1)] N/(S_i S_k S_l S_t), S_a=prod_(r=1)^a 2sin(pi r/N). Set i=k=0,l=j,t=d-j and use S_j S_(d-j)=N. This gives H_(r_N)(0,0,c,y)=sum_(j=0)^d (-q)^j c^(d-j)y^j, H_(r_N^-1)(0,0,c,y)=sum_(j=0)^d (-q^-1)^j c^(d-j)y^j. (8) The inverse formula includes the confluent data, not just conjugate nodal eigenvalues. The actual face operator T has real monomial coefficients at this root: each displayed q/Q combination is invariant under q -> q^(-1). The [frozen signed-kernel theorem](actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md), section 1 and (6a), expresses r_N=sum_r(-q)^r Bhat_r and its ACTUAL Hermite inverse as sum_r(-q^(-1))^r Bhat_r, where Bhat_r has real spectral nodes and real sine-product normalization. Hence the inverse face kernel is coefficientwise complex conjugate in this real polynomial basis, including every repeated node derivative. This justifies using q^(-1) in (8). The ACTUAL crossing R^epsilon has the additional original scalar lambda0^epsilon, lambda0=q^(d^2/2), of unit modulus. Therefore |H_V(0,0,c,y)|_coeff <= N^2 H1(c,y), H1(c,y)=sum_(j=0)^d c^(d-j)y^j =|H_(R^epsilon)(0,0,c,y)|_coeff, epsilon=+/-1. (9) Here coefficient modulus is taken before evaluating positive c,y. The last equality retains the unit scalar's modulus; it does not delete its phase in a signed contraction. Crucially, the identity coupon on the original quartet instead has H_(identity)(0,0,c,y)=c^d, because its two middle variables are b,c. Thus (9) is not the standard identity-insertion polynomial on the original middle pair. ## 4. The exact boundary contraction, and what it does not identify Let P(c,y;Z) be any complementary polynomial in these two ordinary faces and all remaining variables Z. Then, with coefficient operators in Z retained unchanged, [c^d y^d] H1(c,y) P(c,y;Z)=[t^d] P(t,t;Z). (10) For epsilon=+/-1 let zeta=-q^epsilon. Equation (8) gives instead the SIGNED actual half-crossing corner identity [c^d y^d] H_(R^epsilon)(0,0,c,y) P(c,y;Z) =lambda0^epsilon [t^d]P(zeta t,t;Z). (11) So the actual turn carries a nontrivial shared-face phase, not the positive merge in (10). On the only relevant c-degree truncation, define D_A by D_A(c^j y^h)=A_j c^j y^h for 0<=j<=d. The raw cap identity is [c^d y^d] H_V(0,0,c,y)P(c,y;Z) =[t^d](D_A P)(-t,t;Z). (12) The coefficient bound gives a positive merged-polynomial upper bound via N^2[t^d]|P|(t,t;Z). It does not turn (12) into (11), nor show that the signed complementary contraction has the same bound or rate as a geometrically smoothed source. The merged pair c,y is an OUTPUT MAIN edge. Its two incident white triangles belong to two different original matching coupons. Removing the two triangles of the cap coupon is therefore not the same combinatorial operation as contracting that MAIN edge. A physical rewiring would have to retain the neighbor coupon, its boundary typing, and the phase/degree operator in (11)--(12). No such two-port turn or volume comparison is proved here. ## 5. Dependencies The exact inputs are the [homogeneous source](actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md), sections 1–4 and (10); the [signed kernel](actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md), section 1 and (6a); the [original marked cap](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), (2.1)–(2.4); and the [top-mark transport theorem](research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.md). The [finite-collar obstruction](research_double_protected_cap_finite_collar_obstruction.md) remains unchanged. The existing [mark audit](../experiments/research_audit_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.py) already verifies the scalar-cup identity entrywise and hence all E_aa evaluations in its fixtures. No new finite replay, physical rewiring, absolute shared-source estimate or volume assertion is claimed here.

title: Concave triangle radii and the overload obstacle projection
text: # Concave triangle radii and the overload obstacle projection 31 October 2026. The universal comparison remains open. The concavity, clipping and counterexample statements concern one fixed LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT sector and preserve its protected faces and targets. They do not establish a general filling theorem. The [finite-sector criterion](general_actual_sector_cover_filling_volume.md) explains the desired application. The [fractional forest analysis](research_fixed_sector_fractional_forest_reduction.md) records why a local completion cannot simply discard shared face loads. ## 1. An ordinary-radius concavity theorem For the original triangle entropy \(C(\alpha)\), with \(\sum\alpha_i=1/2\), put $$ \begin{aligned} p&=2\alpha,\qquad K(p)=2C(p/2),\qquad H(p)=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i,\\ G(p)&=K(p)-H(p),\\ F(w)&=\exp(2Q(w)) =\exp\max_{p\in\Delta}\left(K(p)+\sum_i p_i\log w_i\right). \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ The [triangle Shannon inequality](actual_triangle_entropy_algebraic_balance.md) gives \(G\ge0\). Its ambient diagonal second derivatives satisfy $$ \frac{\partial^2G}{\partial p_i^2} =\frac1{p_i}-\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi p_i)}<0.\tag{2} $$ Thus \(G\) is strictly concave and extends continuously to the closed simplex. A supporting plane at an interior point has the form \(G(p)\le a\cdot p+b\). The ordinary entropy variational formula gives $$ F(w)\le e^b\sum_i e^{a_i}w_i.\tag{3} $$ For any positive \(w^0\), choose the supporting point to be its optimizer in (1). Stationarity gives \(p_i^0\propto w_i^0e^{a_i}\), so equality holds in (3) at \(w^0\). Therefore \(F\) is the infimum of positive linear forms. In particular it is **concave in ordinary radii**, homogeneous of degree one and coordinate-monotone. Equivalently, $$ F(w)\le F(w^0)\sum_i p_i^0\frac{w_i}{w_i^0}.\tag{4} $$ Original zero-face continuity extends this to nonnegative coordinates, with \(F(0)=0\). The absolute normalization also gives $$ F(w)\ge\sum_iw_i\ge\max_iw_i,\tag{5} $$ strictly in the first inequality when at least two weights are positive. This is a stronger statement than convexity of \(Q\) in logarithmic radii; the two statements are compatible. ## 2. A convergent, order-independent clipping procedure At each surviving one-sided port let \(o_e\) be its overloaded ordinary middle and \(I_e=(x,p,y)\) its retained triangle. Its actual weighted bound is $$ A_e(L)=\max\left(\log L_o,Q(L_I)+\frac12\log L_o\right). \tag{6} $$ A protected overloaded middle makes the original sector zero and is omitted. The input triangle has three distinct vertices and at least one ordinary vertex. The child \(o\) is not an input vertex. The pure branch is active exactly when \(L_o\ge F(L_I)\). Starting with any finite positive ordinary vector, choose a selected port and perform $$ L_o\longleftarrow\min\{L_o,F(L_I)\}.\tag{7} $$ Both protected coordinates remain exactly zero. If \(m,M\) are the minimum and maximum starting ordinary radii, every iterate lies in \([m,M]\): an input has an ordinary coordinate at least \(m\), and (5) bounds its new child below by \(m\). No marked-radius regularization is needed. Let the full fixed-sector cost be $$ V_s(L)=\sum_{e\in C}X_e(L)+\sum_{e\notin C}A_e(L) -\sum_{f\text{ ordinary}}\log L_f. \tag{8} $$ Every update (7) makes \(V_s\) nonincreasing. Along a nontrivial update the chosen row stays on its pure branch down to the tie, so its \(\log L_o\) cancels the target \(-\log L_o\). Every other local term is coordinate-monotone, including through changes of its maximizing branch. Thus decreasing \(L_o\) cannot increase the remaining expression. This also handles repeated overloaded children and arbitrary interactions between branches; no differentiability is required. Visit each selected port infinitely often, in any fair asynchronous order. Every coordinate decreases to a limit \(L^\infty\in[m,M]\). Continuity along the update subsequence at a fixed port gives $$ L_o^\infty\le F(L_I^\infty)\quad\text{for every selected port}.\tag{9} $$ In fact this limit is independent of the fair order. If \(B\) is any feasible positive vector with \(B\le L^{\mathrm{start}}\), monotonicity of \(F\) preserves \(B\le L\) under every update. Hence \(B\le L^\infty\). The limit is the **greatest feasible vector below the starting vector**, uniquely characterized this way. The feasible domain is convex in ordinary radii, since each constraint in (9) is a hypograph of a concave function. It is also closed under coordinatewise maximum. At any coordinate that decreased, at least one constraint having it as child is tight: otherwise that coordinate could be raised slightly, improving input constraints and preserving its strict child constraints, contradicting greatestness. No uniform convergence rate is claimed. Define the half-triangle potential $$ V_{\mathrm{half}}(L)=\sum_{e\in C}X_e(L) +\sum_{e\notin C}\left(Q(L_{I_e})+\frac12\log L_{o_e}\right) -\sum_{f\text{ ordinary}}\log L_f.\tag{10} $$ At the clipped limit \(V_s=V_{\mathrm{half}}\). Therefore the exact variational restriction is $$ \boxed{\quad \inf_{L>0}V_s(L) =\inf_{\substack{L>0\\L_{o_e}\le F(L_{I_e})\ \forall e}} V_{\mathrm{half}}(L). \quad}\tag{11} $$ The clipping procedure gives a finite positive admissible vector of no larger full cost from every starting vector. Attainment of either infimum is unnecessary. ## 3. Half descent fails even from a complete packing The monotonicity in §2 applies to \(V_s\), not to \(V_{\mathrm{half}}\). An exact example uses the original reduced width-three word \((1,3,2,1,3)\), first cap mark, protected faces \(0,1\). Its actual [complete packing](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md) has $$ (L_2,L_3,L_4,L_5,L_6)=(1,\varphi^2,\varphi^2,\varphi^3,1), \qquad\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}. $$ Select only port \(0\) LEFT. Its retained triangle is monomial, so clipping changes only \(c=L_4\), from \(\varphi^2\) to \(1\). The exact derivative is $$ \frac{\partial V_{\mathrm{half}}}{\partial\log c} =-\frac12+\frac2\pi \arctan\frac{c}{\sqrt{c(1+\varphi^3)+\varphi^3}} +\frac1\pi\arctan\sqrt c.\tag{12} $$ At the starting packing it is \(1/2-\arctan(\varphi)/\pi>0\), using \(\varphi^2(1+\varphi^3)+\varphi^3=\varphi^6\). At the endpoint it is $$ -\frac14+\frac2\pi\arctan\frac1{\sqrt{1+2\varphi^3}}<0,\tag{13} $$ because \(1+2\varphi^3=5+2\sqrt5>(1+\sqrt2)^2\). Thus the half potential increases on a final subinterval of the clipping path, although the full sector cost continues to decrease. With one selected port there is no alternative update ordering that repairs this pointwise assertion. ## 4. The greatest geometric projection can end above volume A stronger example uses the literal width-three word $$ (1,3,0,2,4,1,3),\qquad\text{first cap mark, protected }(0,6), $$ with complete curvatures $$ (L_0,\ldots,L_8)=(0,16,9,25,1,4,0,1,9).\tag{14} $$ These are certified without a numerical packing solve. The original compiler gives seven ports, fourteen distinct triangles and twenty-one edges, each incident to two triangles. Every triangle discriminant \(D=\sqrt{\sum_{i<j}L_iL_j}\) is an integer. At ordinary face \(f\), multiply \(D+iL_f\) over its incident triangles, using \(i\) for a monomial triangle. In face order \(1,2,3,4,5,7,8\), the products are $$ -6800,\ -994500,\ -24650,\ -1700,\ -490100,\ -100,\ -1170. $$ Each angle is positive; elementary \(\pi/4\) or \(\pi/2\) bounds put each total below \(2\pi\) (in fact at most \(7\pi/4\)). The negative real products therefore make every total exactly \(\pi\). All original ordinary angle loads equal one. The convex complete potential is stationary and hence minimizes at (14), giving its actual complete rate \(\Phi_D\). Uniqueness modulo scale identifies the complete geometry. Select only port \(2\) RIGHT. Its quartet is \((0,1,6,4)\), with sole ordinary retained input \(L_4=1\). Greatest clipping changes only \(L_1:16\to1\). After cancelling unchanged original factors, the endpoint half potential minus the complete rate is exactly $$ \begin{aligned} \Delta={}&Q(1,0,9)+Q(1,1,9)-Q(16,0,9)-Q(16,1,9)\\ &-Q(0,16,1)+\log16. \end{aligned}\tag{15} $$ A 192-bit Arb evaluation with 2,048 Fourier terms for each Lobachevsky function and the explicit tail \(1/(2M)\) certifies $$ 0.22616591009<\Delta<0.22989612898,\qquad\Delta>0.22. \tag{16} $$ The finite check verifies the original chart, all seven exact angle products, the single clipping constraint and both the cancelled expression (15) and the full potential difference. Its inputs are exact integers; no optimized or rounded packing is used as proof. There is only one constraint, so simultaneous or reordered clipping gives the same endpoint. Consequently the greatest projection of the geometric vector need not pass the desired bound. Equation (11) remains valid: a different feasible vector, potentially smaller than the greatest one or obtained by changing other faces, may still pass. This is not a fixed-sector capacity excess or an original quantum-rate counterexample. ## 5. The remaining global inequality On the feasible domain, $$ V_{\mathrm{half}}(L)=V_{\mathrm{complete}}(L) -\sum_{e\text{ selected}} \left(Q(L_x,L_o,L_y)-\frac12\log L_o\right).\tag{17} $$ Every bracket is strictly positive: a surviving overloaded middle is ordinary, and the outer pair is MATCHING, so cannot be the two protected MAIN vertices. The deleted triangle has at least two positive coordinates. At the complete geometric vector this puts the half potential below \(\Phi_D\). Equations (13) and (16) show why clipping alone does not preserve that certificate. The open step is to find an appropriate feasible vector whose deleted-triangle defect exceeds the complete-potential excess. Equalizing middle radii also needs its original target correction. For one unprotected edge \(b=c=B\), the old cost is the identity-smoothed remaining potential **plus** $$ Q(x,B,y)-\frac12\log B\ge0.\tag{18} $$ These terms add over a selected forest. A protected component cannot impose middle equality at positive ordinary radii at all: equality with its root sets those radii to zero and requires a separate target adapter. Neither (18) nor concavity of \(F\) is an existing smoothing-volume upper bound. The exact source and interval calculations establish (11) and refute the proposed monotonicity and greatest-projection bounds. The universal optimized fixed-sector inequality remains open.

title: Two residual caps: exact topology, a complete flat cylinder, and the original volume budget

# Two residual caps: exact topology, a complete flat cylinder, and the original volume budget 31 October 2026. **analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. Assume classified finite-common-weight stationary data on the original simple matched sphere, positive at every ordinary incidence, with exactly TWO strict residual caps and CROSS at every other port. The original protected MAIN edge is uv. A cap child receives 1-nu>1/2 and its ordinary outer receives nu in (0,1/2); their positive weights agree. The positive-value hypothesis excludes the all-cap tetrahedral exception. No adjacent-mark sphere theorem is applied to nonadjacent zero vertices. The new construction below is a complete Euclidean CYLINDER. The resulting absolute budget is still positive: it does not prove M_cap<=Phi_D. ![Two cap-contact cuts between parallel marked lines; boundary schematic with interior packing omitted.](../book/figures/two-cap-cylindrical-boundary.svg) The figure illustrates the boundary geometry only; it does not assert that the omitted interior admits a packing for these chosen coordinates. Its [renderer](../experiments/render_two_cap_cylindrical_boundary.py) records the exact schematic parameters. ## 1. Literal two-cap topology The two protected triangles are uvC and uvD, with distinct ordinary C,D. After relabeling the first cap is \[ F_1=(u,A,v,C),\qquad (u,A,C),\ (u,v,C),\qquad 	ext{matching edge }uC. \] The second has either matching vD, with child B and quartet(v,B,u,D), or matching uD, with child B and quartet(u,B,v,D). MAIN bipartiteness and demand one leave the following possibilities: * Four distinct ordinary vertices A,C,B,D. The union of the two cap patches is a four-triangle disk sharing just uv, with hexagonal boundary u-A-C-v-B-D-u in the first type, or u-A-C-v-D-B-u in the second. * One shared ordinary vertex, necessarily the child of one cap and the outer of the other. Up to exchanging the two caps and protected labels, the pair is \[ F_1=(u,A,v,C),\qquad F_2=(v,B,u,A).	ag{1} \] Their patches share the TWO MAIN edges uv and uA. Their union is a four-triangle disk with protected u in its interior and boundary A-C-v-B-A. Indeed two distinct caps cannot have the same child (two loads>1/2), and the same outer would repeat an original uv triangle. A common child/outer is impossible in the same-protected-outer type by the MAIN bipartite colors. In the opposite type it gives exactly (1). If both ordinary vertices were shared, the previously proved parallel cap exception is the whole tetrahedron with zero action. All boundary edges of these cap unions are MAIN, so every remaining original port lies wholly in the complementary disk. No half-port is removed or supplied an invented half-demand. ## 2. A shared ordinary vertex is impossible in the cap-only stationary case For (1), write the two cap parameters nu1,nu2. The complementary disk has boundary A-C-v-B. All its rows are complete CROSS triangles. Its original residual loads and weights are \[  egin{gathered} r_A=
u_1-
u_2>0,\qquad r_B=
u_2<	frac12,\qquad r_C=1-
u_1>	frac12,\ r_v=0,\qquad L_A=L_B=L_C>0. \end{gathered}	ag{2} \] The strict first inequality follows from ordinary incidence positivity: A has an exterior incidence, since the simple four-boundary disk cannot triangulate its boundary neighborhood without an A corner. Interior ordinary demands remain one. Their triangle angles sum to 2pi. Here is a useful elementary boundary-development argument, requiring no assumed injectivity. Develop the complete positive center triangles in this disk. The zero boundary vertex v is represented by its ONE cooriented line. A one-line triangle is the actual infinite Euclidean strip triangle with two finite centers tangent to that line. Gluing across finite edges uses the common lengths r_f+r_g; gluing across a line/finite edge uses the same line and finite center. The full 2pi stars at interior ordinary vertices give trivial Euclidean holonomy. Such loops generate the punctured-disk continuation, so there is a global developing map. The v fan is connected, so it propagates the SAME cooriented line. Put that line horizontal and write rho_f=1/L_f for circle radii, distinct from the residual loads r_f in (2). Equal B,C radii put their centers at equal height on the same side of it. They are distinct: their intervening positive line fan has horizontal length sum 2sqrt(rho_i rho_(i+1))>0. The A center is equidistant from B,C since AB=AC=rho_A+rho_B. Thus it lies on their perpendicular bisector. Reflection in this perpendicular bisector exchanges the boundary rays BA and CA and fixes the directed line normal. The recorded boundary fans at B,C are consequently equal modulo 2pi. More explicitly, if beta=arg(A-B), then \[  egin{gathered} \arg(A-C)\equiv\pi- eta\pmod{2\pi},\qquad \arg(n_v)=- rac\pi2,\ 	heta_B\equiv- rac\pi2- eta\equiv	heta_C\pmod{2\pi}. \end{gathered} \] Both actual fan sums lie strictly between0 and2pi, so they are equal. This contradicts (2). It also excludes a degenerate collinear center triangle, where the same angular congruence still holds. Therefore \[  egin{gathered} 	ext{At strict cap-only finite stationary data,}\ 	ext{the two ordinary cap pairs are disjoint.} \end{gathered}	ag{3} \] This uses all-CROSS positivity outside the two caps. It is not a topology-only assertion about arbitrary marked diagrams or Green data. ## 3. The correct hexagon double We are now in the first case of section1. Let D be the remaining disk; its six boundary vertices are distinct. Define the involution of its boundary by \[ u\longleftrightarrow v,\qquad A\longleftrightarrow C,\qquad B\longleftrightarrow D.	ag{4} \] In either of the two cyclic orders above, (4) reverses the boundary orientation. Gluing two copies by (4) produces a triangular spherical CELLULATION T_cyl. Each original triangle retains three distinct vertices and each original port its four distinct vertices. The matching is inherited separately in each copy, because all boundary edges were MAIN. Parallel edges may arise from doubled boundary diagonals; we do NOT claim this cellulation is simple. Crucially u,v are NONADJACENT. Their sole original edge uv belonged to the removed cap union. No other uv edge existed in the original simple sphere. Thus every triangle of T_cyl has either three ordinary vertices or exactly one zero vertex. Duplicate the original finite weights and complete triangle allocations. They agree under (4) because L_A=L_C and L_B=L_D. Each boundary ordinary demand becomes nu_i+(1-nu_i)=1; interior ordinary demands remain one; u,v remain zero. Hence T_cyl carries an actual strictly positive complete angle assignment at its finite weights. This fact is all that is needed below; no nonadjacent-mark source or capacity theorem is used. ## 4. Complete flat-cylinder development, including properness and injectivity For each ordinary face f write its circle radius r_f=1/L_f. A triangle with three finite vertices is the Euclidean center triangle of side lengths r_i+r_j. Its angles are precisely the complete source angles. A triangle with zero vertex u and finite i,j is its exact one-line model: put the line at height0 and the finite centers at \[ (0,r_i),\qquad (2\sqrt{r_i r_j},r_j). \] Its carrier is the infinite half-strip triangle below their joining segment, with two parallel rays from the centers toward the ideal vertex. The finite side has length r_i+r_j and its finite angles are the original complete angles, summing to pi. The same construction applies at v. Glue these Euclidean triangles along their prescribed edges/rays. Every ordinary vertex has angle2pi, so the resulting metric on the topological sphere minus{u,v} is flat and has no cone point. This metric is COMPLETE. Beyond the finite heights of all centers in one zero-vertex star, its successive strips glue into an exact flat cylinder. Its circumference is \[ T_u=\sum_{\substack{i,j	ext{ successive}\	ext{in the }u	ext{ fan}}} 2\sqrt{r_i r_j}>0.	ag{5} \] and similarly at v. Vertical offsets telescope, so no longitudinal drift is hidden in this calculation. Truncating both cylindrical ends leaves a finite union of compact truncated triangles. A path escaping either end has unbounded height, which is 1-Lipschitz and therefore costs infinite length. This proves completeness rather than merely local flatness and nonzero holonomy. The simply connected metric cover is therefore the Euclidean plane. One direct proof develops a local Euclidean frame and extends every straight geodesic by completeness; path lifting makes this a covering of R^2, and simple connectedness makes it an isometry. Its deck generator is an orientation-preserving Euclidean isometry without a fixed point, hence a nonzero translation. A once-around end loop is a generator of the punctured sphere, so both (5) are the SAME translation length, not an unspecified multiple. This establishes the developing degree and injectivity that an arbitrary flat immersion would not supply. Place the finite circle of radius r_f at every lifted finite vertex. Its sector in each incident finite triangle stays inside that triangle, by the usual tangent-center-triangle proof. The one-line version is equally literal. For example the i-circle sector toward the infinite vertex cannot cross the opposite vertical ray: if r_i>=r_j its maximal horizontal projection in that sector is \[  rac{2r_i\sqrt{r_i r_j}}{r_i+r_j}<2\sqrt{r_i r_j}, \] while if r_i<r_j it is at most r_i<2sqrt(r_i r_j). The other edges are handled by the sector definition and the actual i/j tangency. The infinite-corner sectors tile the half-plane below their common line. Thus the finite disks, and the two zero-vertex half-planes, have disjoint interiors in the developed plane. There are no accidental nonedge contacts: the same strict sector-support argument applies locally, and the center triangulation is globally embedded. More explicitly, the opposite finite side is covered by the other two tangent disks, with their contact strictly outside the third positive disk; the opposite-ray estimates above are strict. Thus nonedge supports are strict, not merely disjoint in their interiors. Periodic local finiteness prevents an extra contact arising as an accumulation of nonincident sectors. This also separates a finite disk from its nontrivial deck translates. Consequently this is a genuine PERIODIC circle packing between two distinct parallel lines. The lines are preserved by the same nonzero deck translation, and their disjoint half-planes face opposite ways. Their separation H is positive because finite positive-radius disks fit between them. This completes the cylinder theorem, without an adjacent-mark spherical-packing hypothesis. ## 5. The original exterior and the two cap parameters The original disk D minus its two ideal boundary vertices is simply connected, so a copy lifts to the universal cover just constructed. Its lift is embedded because the covering development is an isometry. It supplies ONE circle for every original finite face and the SAME two parallel marked lines u,v. Every original exterior contact is retained. The [original cap-cut theorem](research_cap_star_cut_and_cross_stellar_reduction.md) excludes Av (and the analogous other-child/ opposite-line edge), because every other incidence of that child is CROSS. The matching edge uC was removed. In the double, a possible Av edge from the other copy would correspond under (4) to that removed uC edge, and conversely. Therefore neither cross-line contact exists even in the periodic packing. The same holds for the second pair. The one-cap fan calculation now applies to each pair in this actual strip: \[ H=4r_i\sin^2(\pi
u_i)>2r_i,\qquad  rac14<
u_i< rac12,\qquad i=1,2.	ag{6} \] This is a conclusion, not a premise used to establish completeness. Each equal-radius pair supplies three collinear finite cap contacts; the fourth original contact uv is infinity. Their ideal quadrilateral planes cut the infinite periodic right-angled polyhedron. Each section is exactly its quadrilateral, by convexity and the four incident white halfspaces, just as in the one-cap proof. The two cutting planes do not intersect inside the white strip. Their finite contact segments lie in disjoint pairs of packing disks (each segment consists of two chords meeting at the pair's tangency), and the line contacts are distinct. Thus the segments cannot cross. Intersection of the two vertical planes, if any, lies outside the strip. Cut between the consecutive planes corresponding to the chosen lift of D. This gives a finite convex ideal exterior polyhedron Q_D with the original exterior white/shaded faces and TWO new quadrilateral faces. Local shaded supports come from the same tangent-triangle incircles; periodicity and the two cuts leave only finitely many faces. In coordinates where the white strip is 0<=Y<=H, each cutting contact line is X=a_i+b_iY. The two segments do not cross in the closed strip, so the between-cut region has bounded X,Y projection. Periodic local finiteness leaves only finitely many finite contacts and faces there. The old marked point infinity is now an actual ideal vertex. No topology of an old/new filled link is inferred from this auxiliary polyhedron construction. Let M_2 denote the sharp cap-sector value at the actual stationary datum. Its caps have action zero, so it is the sum of the exterior complete triangle entropies. Coning Q_D to infinity gives \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Q_D)=\pi M_2.	ag{7} \] Here the normalization can be checked directly, without inventing a nonadjacent-mark capacity. The complete shaded/white triangle terms give pi times the exterior entropy. At a boundary ordinary circle the closing chord adds the Lobachevsky term of the complementary fan. Within each cap pair those terms cancel because its fan loads are nu_i and1-nu_i. Both line faces and both new quadrilateral faces contain the cone apex and contribute zero. These account for every boundary term. The [original finite-weight dual attainment](research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md) also identifies this stationary value with the original closed two-cap-sector maximum. ## 6. Original group and the correct second-ball flags Use this one positive exterior family to form the actual original reflection heads. The restored original MAIN edge uv is the contact at infinity of the two parallel lines. At each removed cap use the explicit ordered collar from the [one-cap chain theorem](research_one_cap_original_chain_volume_budget.md), with its original local frame and its own nu_i. Retain the original oriented exterior fan when choosing that local chart. Depending on the recorded disk order, this may be the conjugate of the displayed one-cap normalization; no single affine normalization is presumed to send both exterior sides to the lower half-plane. Conjugating the chart reverses the plane orientation together with the oriented local fan, and both collar fixed points still lie on its actual inward exterior side. This describes the actual local matrices in their recorded coordinates; no cap is independently reflected or reset in the global circle family. Conjugate every local formula back by its actual coordinate change before sewing. The tangent CROSS collars are unchanged. The same literal Morse prefix, cup/cap and ordered-conjugation relations therefore construct a representation of the original untwisted drilled group, not of a periodic quotient. There is a small generalization of the one-cap flag rule. Fix u as the ONE reference reflection. At cap e let x_e be its protected outer (either u or v), y_e its ordinary outer, and let O_e be a fixed flag of P_e=r_(y_e) r_(x_e). On the FIRST original ball use O_e. On the SECOND ball use \[ O_e^{(2)}=r_u r_{x_e}(O_e).	ag{8} \] while all other flags remain r_u-reflections of their first-ball values. The white x_e map r_(x_e)r_u sends (8) to O_e; the white y_e map sends it to P_e(O_e)=O_e. The second shaded map r_u C_e r_u also fixes (8), since r_(x_e) exchanges the two peripheral flags and C_e fixes both. Its other two vertices have the original reflected permutation. These checks hold independently at both cap vertices, even when both lie on the same protected white face. Keep the original compatible face fans and degree-one abstract ball chains. The actual full peripheral subgroup at each exceptional cap preserves its axis; all other cusps are parabolic. The [general-peripheral ideal-chain theorem](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) therefore computes the canonical original representation volume, with no extra boundary constant or source-action identification. ## 7. The two inward pyramids and the quantified remaining budget In each local normalization the two collar flags lie on the existing exterior side of its flat quadrilateral. The original-chain boundary identity replaces that face by the four-triangle inward cone, whose signed volume is -W(nu_i). In a conjugate local chart use the original oriented fan and tetrahedron orientation together; the same geometric inward subtraction is still -W, rather than assigning the Bloch sign from an unrecorded affine chart. The two replacements have distinct auxiliary vertices and add linearly, even on a shared white polygon. Reflecting the second ball back by r_u changes its cap flag to the other peripheral flag, with the same pyramid volume. Hence \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho) =2\pi M_2-2 igl[W(
u_1)+W(
u_2) igr].	ag{9} \] where the SAME absolutely calibrated function is \[  egin{gathered} W(
u)=2\int_0^{\arcsin(\sqrt2\cos(\pi
u))} \operatorname{arsinh}(\cos t)\,dt,\ 0<W(
u)<2G,\qquad  rac14<
u< rac12. \end{gathered}	ag{10} \] The original representation-volume bound yields \[ M_2-\Phi_D\le rac{W(
u_1)+W(
u_2)}\pi < rac{4G}\pi=2C_0.	ag{11} \] The [fixed-word peripheral gap](general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md) subtracts a further g/(2pi)>0 for the fixed original exterior (uniform on compact subsets of the two cap parameter ranges). There is no estimate here making that subtraction pay the entire right side. Equivalently the constrained cap defect satisfies Delta_cap<=2C0+sum_i W(nu_i)/pi<4C0. Together with the one-cap theorem this gives a common geometric budget for every strict finite-common-weight cap-only configuration with at most two caps. It neither proves M_cap<=Phi_D nor bounds an original signed source by this volume without its remaining phase compensation. No real-spectral cap is silently replaced by these different geometric collars. ## dependencies and exact open scope Inputs are the [original stationary cap classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md), the cap-cut/forest theorem linked above, the [complete triangle angles and strict sector support](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), the one-cap ordered collar and pyramid chain, and the [actual general-Morse group dictionary](research_general_morse_cross_action.md). The absolute volume normalization and fixed-word gap use the linked original general-peripheral theorems. The new topology, complete-cylinder development, two-cap flag rule and volume assembly are proved here; they are not applications of an adjacent-mark packing theorem to nonadjacent marked vertices. The two local cap charts must be returned to the same global coordinates. When a conjugate chart is required, its oriented fan is retained; one cannot choose the two cap sides independently. Completeness and developing injectivity are established before sector support and the finite exterior are used. No quantum sector transport, universal absolute cap inequality, or filled-volume theorem is asserted. In particular the one-cap signed source/stability argument is not automatically iterated to two caps; this note proves the geometric volume budget, not that separate contraction.

title: Actual two-cap extraction and an original-demand response certificate
text:
# Actual two-cap extraction and an original-demand response certificate 31 October 2026. **exact-source and analytical research theorem.** Unpublished. The response inequality below is a sufficient certificate; its universal passage is not claimed. The source is the original simple matched sphere with the original protected MAIN pair u,v. There are two strict residual caps, all other coupons are CROSS at their actual endpoint -2, and both caps are at +2. The geometric classification has already proved that the two ordinary cap pairs are disjoint. Label child/outer pairs (A,C) and (B,D). The finite common weights satisfy L_A=L_C=a>0 and L_B=L_D=b>0. The exterior ordinary incidences are positive. This note does NOT prove that the resulting certificate always passes, and gives no varying-spectrum or filled-period theorem. Inputs are the durable two-cap cylindrical-exterior theorem, the original one-cap negative-axis reduction and cap moment form, the actual odd CROSS determinant factorization, and the original positive determinant curvature. The [two-cap geometry](research_two_cap_cylindrical_exterior_volume_budget.md) and the [one-cap extraction](research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md) retain the same source. There is no changed-diagram identification. ## 1. Four boundary variables and the two separate degree targets Put d=N-1, M=floor(N/2)-1, H=M+1, and let I be the ordinary faces other than A,C,B,D. Protected variables are set to zero first. Remove the fixed common raw unit scalars and form the actual exterior polynomial \[  egin{aligned} E_N(L)&=\prod_{e\ \mathrm{not\ a\ cap}}P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2;L),\ P_N(A,C,B,D)&=\left[\prod_{i\in I}L_i^dight]E_N(L). \end{aligned} \] There are R-2 exterior ports and R-4 extracted ordinary faces, so P_N is homogeneous of degree 2d. Its coefficients are nonnegative at both parities. The cap contractions impose MORE than this total degree: \[  egin{aligned} Q_N(A,C,B,D)&=[z^d]P_N(zA,zC,B,D)\ &=\sum_{0\le j,k\le d}p_{N,jk}A^jC^{d-j}B^kD^{d-k}. \end{aligned}	ag{1} \] The second pair degree is d by total homogeneity. Neither the cylinder construction nor the stationary classical pair loads makes the first projection redundant at finite N. All cap formulas below apply to Q_N, not to unprojected P_N. With theta=pi/N and c_r=2cos((2r+1)theta), retain \[ U_j=\left(\prod_{r=1}^{j}4\sin^2(r	heta)ight) \prod_{r=j+1}^{d}(2-c_r),\qquad 0\le j\le d. \] After the literal reflected cap relabeling if necessary, the actual cap coefficient is (-1)^j U_j times child^(d-j) outer^j. Thus, up to ONE fixed unit scalar, the original two-cap sector coefficient is exactly \[ S_{LL}=\sum_{0\le j,k\le M}(-1)^{j+k}U_jU_kp_{N,jk}.	ag{2} \] Every original ordinary degree d is now imposed. No independent signs are assigned to repeated face occurrences. ## 2. Completion has two mixed strips, not only a harmless double tail Write S_** for the same sum over all 0<=j,k<=d, S_H* for j>=H and all k, S_*H for all j and k>=H, and S_HH for both indices >=H. Then \[ S_{LL}=S_{**}-S_{H*}-S_{*H}+S_{HH}.	ag{3} \] The exact cap moment law gives independent X,Y>0 with \[  egin{gathered} \mathbb E X^j=\mathbb E Y^j= rac{U_j}{U_0}\quad(0\le j\le d), \qquad 0<U_j\le N^2,\ m_d=\mathbb E X^d=N^2\sin^2 rac{\pi}{2N}\le rac{\pi^2}{4}. \end{gathered} \] Consequently \[ S_{**}=U_0^2\mathbb E Q_N(-X,1,-Y,1).	ag{4} \] This is absolutely integrable since Q_N has degree d in EACH pair. Interchanging an unprojected P_N, which can have individual degree 2d, with these moment integrals is not justified and is not done. For v_-(t)=(-t,1), v_+(t)=(-1,t), define four actual suprema \[ B_{\epsilon,\eta}=\sup_{0\le t,s\le1} |Q_N(v_\epsilon(t),v_\eta(s))|. \] Homogeneity and the four regions X<=1/X>=1, Y<=1/Y>=1 give \[ |S_{**}|\le U_0^2\left[B_{--}+m_d(B_{+-}+B_{-+})+m_d^2B_{++}ight].	ag{5} \] Let R(s,t) be the original exterior complete-triangle capacity with residual A,C loads s,1-s, B,D loads t,1-t, every i in I load one, and u,v load zero. Empty fibers have value minus infinity. The original complete capacity is exactly \[ \Phi_D=\max_{s,t\in[1/2,1]} \left[R(s,t)+2f(s-	frac12)+2f(t-	frac12)ight].	ag{6} \] This fills the two original cap half-triangles and leaves every other triangle and target unchanged. Therefore there is gamma_HH>0 with \[ \max_{s,t\in[1/2,1]}R(s,t)\le\Phi_D-\gamma_{HH}.	ag{7} \] For an interior coordinate its added entropy is positive. At the four remaining corners both added entropies vanish, but at least one original ordinary cap incidence is zero; the unique positive complete optimizer cannot occur there. Compactness and upper semicontinuity prove (7). The proved CLOSED local coefficient upper and polynomial shared-array count imply the corresponding uniform upper for p_(N,jk). Since U_j U_k are polynomially bounded, for all sufficiently large levels \[ |S_{HH}|\le e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_{HH}/2)}.	ag{8} \] The finite thresholds satisfy H/d>=1/2 at both parities. In contrast, neither S_H* nor S_*H has this argument: its other residual coordinate may be below 1/2. Dropping those mixed strips would be an actual error. Sections 5-6 give separate original-demand bounds for them. ## 3. What stability survives, and the exact determinant inequality On odd levels N=2m+1, every actual exterior CROSS coupon is \[  egin{gathered} N^2D_m(x,b,y)D_m(x,c,y),\ D_m(x,b,y)=\det\left[bI+ rac{x}{2}H_-+ rac{y}{2}H_+ight]. \end{gathered}	ag{9} \] with the original positive Hermitian H_-,H_+. Products, shared-variable identifications, individual coefficient extractions and zero specializations show that P_N is real stable or zero. We do NOT conclude that Q_N is jointly real stable. Two valid conditional statements remain. For fixed positive B,D, P_N(A,C,zB,zD) is stable in A,C,z; its coefficient [z^d] is precisely Q_N(A,C,B,D), so this binary homogeneous polynomial is stable or zero. Also every individual row \[ q_{N,j}(B,D)=[A^jC^{d-j}]P_N(A,C,B,D). \] is binary real stable or zero. These facts do not multiply conditional negative-axis losses, and do not identify the full joint polynomial with a product of Bernoulli factors. Here is a different exact inequality which DOES retain the projection. For each determinant t in (9), at arbitrary positive ordinary weights, write its pencil as M_t=sum_f L_f K_tf>0 and set \[ A_{tf}=M_t^{-1/2}L_fK_{tf}M_t^{-1/2},\qquad\sum_fA_{tf}=I. \] Protected zero terms are absent. For complex numbers |z_f|<=1, set Z_t=sum_f z_f A_tf. The unital completely positive map from diagonal scalars to sum_f z_f A_tf is contractive (equivalently insert the isometry v -> (sqrt(A_tf)v)_f), so Z_t^*Z_t<=I. Therefore \[  egin{aligned} \log|\det Z_t|&\le- rac12\operatorname{Tr}(I-Z_t^*Z_t)\ &=- rac12\sum_f(1-|z_f|^2)\operatorname{Tr}A_{tf} - rac12\sum_{f<g}|z_f-z_g|^2\operatorname{Tr}(A_{tf}A_{tg}). \end{aligned}	ag{10} \] The inequality includes singular Z_t by continuity. All pair traces are real and nonnegative. There is no commutativity assumption. Define the normalized original loads and conductances \[  egin{gathered} r_{N,f}= rac1N\sum_t\operatorname{Tr}A_{tf},\qquad g_{N,fg}= rac1N\sum_t\operatorname{Tr}(A_{tf}A_{tg})\quad(f
e g),\ H_N=\operatorname{Laplacian}(g_N) = rac1N\operatorname{Hess}_{\log L}\log E_N(L). \end{gathered}	ag{11} \] The scalar coupon factors N^2 remain in E_N and disappear only from these derivatives. The factor N, rather than d, in (11) agrees with the coefficient-rate normalization. The total loss in (10), divided by N, is \[ e_N(z)= rac12\sum_fr_{N,f}(1-|z_f|^2) + rac12\sum_{f<g}g_{N,fg}|z_f-z_g|^2.	ag{12} \] For each individual coordinate its quadratic coefficient is exactly -sum_t Tr(A_tf^2)/(2N)<=0. Thus, when z_f is constrained to a fixed ray and its modulus varies in [0,1], e_N is concave in that modulus. This finite identity will justify radial endpoint minimization BEFORE any Schur relaxation. The exterior ordinary-pair graph is connected. Deleting the two cap patches removes no ordinary edge from that graph: their only ordinary edges AC and BD each have the opposite triangle still in the CROSS exterior; the two pairs are disjoint. The original ordinary graph was connected. Hence H_N has only the common scaling kernel. Its grounded principal submatrices are positive definite. The actual determinant derivative theorem gives r_N -> r and H_N -> H at fixed positive weights, where H is the original complete-triangle conductance Laplacian. No signed or projected coefficient limit is used here. ## 4. The four joint negative boxes have a finite response loss Return to common cap weights A=C=a, B=D=b. Set \[ F_N(L)= rac1N\log E_N(L) - rac dN\left[\sum_{i\in I}\log L_i+\log a+\log bight].	ag{13} \] To bound B_(epsilon,eta), the exact coefficient contour for (1) has the phases \[ (z_A,z_C)=e^{i	heta}v_\epsilon(t),\qquad (z_B,z_D)=v_\eta(s),\qquad z_i=e^{i	heta_i}\quad(i\in I).	ag{14} \] The phase theta is the original PAIR-TOTAL projection [z^d]. Its Fourier multiplier has modulus one. It cannot be fixed independently or omitted. All measures are the original normalized torus measures. The positive prefactor after dividing by a^d b^d is exp[N F_N(L)]. For fixed theta and theta_i, separate concavity from (12) shows that the minimum over t,s occurs at their endpoints. Across all four boxes this leaves the three real vectors per pair \[ \mathcal V=\{(-1,1),(0,1),(-1,0)\}. \] For \(v,w\in\mathcal V\), all other moduli are one. Thus the radial part of (12) is half the sum of r_(N,f) over zero boundary coordinates, and its remaining part is half the ordinary complex Dirichlet energy. Let boundary order be (A,C | B,D), and take the exact Schur complement \[ K_N=H_{N,bb}-H_{N,bI}H_{N,II}^{-1}H_{N,Ib}. \] Relaxing the interior unit phases to arbitrary complex values lowers the Dirichlet energy, with minimum z_b^* K_N z_b. Write its pair blocks as K11,K12,K22. For z_b=(e^(i theta)v,w), the relative theta remains: \[ z_b^*K_Nz_b=v^TK_{11}v+w^TK_{22}w +2\cos	heta\,v^TK_{12}w. \] Consequently define the exact finite positive loss \[ \delta_{12,N}= rac12\min_{v,w\in\mathcal V} \left\{\sum_{f:(v,w)_f=0}r_{N,f} +v^TK_{11}v+w^TK_{22}w-2|v^TK_{12}w|ight\}.	ag{15} \] There are nine expressions. Connectedness and positive boundary loads make their minimum positive: if there is a zero coordinate its radial cost is positive, while with no zero the pairwise opposite boundary values cannot be one common constant. The same argument applies to the limiting matrix, so delta_(12,N)->delta_12>0. Equations (10)-(15) prove, uniformly over all four boxes, \[ B_{\epsilon,\eta}\le e^{N(F_N(L)-\delta_{12,N})}.	ag{16} \] Here Q_N in the definition of B is at unweighted coordinates. Its bihomogeneity is exactly what canceled a^d b^d. The interior and pair-phase integrations introduce no exponential or polynomial loss. At the genuine common stationary weights, F_N(L)->M_2. Hence \[ \limsup_{N\ \mathrm{odd}} rac1N\log|S_{**}| \le M_2-\delta_{12}.	ag{17} \] This is an explicit global simultaneous cancellation bound using the original pair targets. It is not a claim that its loss pays the full geometric budget. ## 5. Each mixed strip retains a one-pair loss and its high-degree cost Fix j and write q_j(B,D) as in section 3. Its degree is d. Completion of only the SECOND cap gives \[ \sum_{k=0}^{d}(-1)^kU_kp_{N,jk}=U_0\mathbb E q_j(-Y,1). \] Its two negative-axis suprema can again be bounded directly by (10), without appealing to binary roots. Use arbitrary positive weights \[ A=ae^z,\qquad C=a,\qquad B=D=b,\qquad z\ge0. \] and retain all original I targets. Now A and C are individually extracted, to j and d-j, so their two phases are independent unit phases. Only B,D have the negative-axis boundary constraint. Let kappa_(2,N)(L)>0 be the effective conductance between B,D in H_N, eliminating ALL other ordinary vertices. The same radial endpoint and Dirichlet argument gives \[ \delta_{2,N}(L)=\min\left\{2\kappa_{2,N},  rac{r_{N,B}+\kappa_{2,N}}2,  rac{r_{N,D}+\kappa_{2,N}}2ight\}.	ag{18} \] Indeed the two-terminal Schur matrix is kappa[[1,-1],[-1,1]]; the opposite pair (-1,1) has half-energy 2kappa, and each one-zero case adds its half-load to half-energy kappa/2. These are the exact normalizations. Use (13) with A=a exp(z) in the product E_N but keep its displayed subtractions log a+log b. Cauchy extraction of A^j C^(d-j) gives the ADDITIONAL factor exp(-zj). Both row negative-axis suprema obey \[ B_{j,\pm}\le e^{N(F_N(L)-\delta_{2,N}(L))-zj}.	ag{19} \] This is uniform in every actual j, including zero row polynomials. The original moments and U_j<=N^2 therefore prove \[ |S_{H*}|\le\operatorname{poly}(N) e^{N(F_N(L)-\delta_{2,N}(L))-zH}.	ag{20} \] The polynomial is uniform on fixed positive weight compacts; one may take the explicit factor (d+1)N^4(1+pi^2/4). No j-dependent saddle or lower coefficient asymptotic is required. Since H/N->1/2, \[ \limsup_{N\ \mathrm{odd}} rac1N\log|S_{H*}| \le F(L)- rac z2-\delta_2(L).	ag{21} \] The reflected statement for S_*H uses B=b exp(z), D=b, A=C=a, with delta_1 the effective A,C response. The mixed sums retain their original indices and signs throughout; taking their absolute values does not discard their other cap's cancellation. ## 6. A finite classical sufficient criterion, with a local tilt improvement The limiting positive functional in (13) is the original exterior triangle potential \[ F(L)=\sum_{t\ \mathrm{exterior}}Q_t(L) -\sum_{i\in I}\log L_i-\log a-\log b.	ag{22} \] At the stationary weights it is M_2. In fact the same weights give R(s,t)<=F(L)=M_2 for every residual pair split: the two boundary log-weight contributions are always log a+log b. Equality holds at the actual (nu_1,nu_2) allocation. For the first mixed strip one may choose ANY fixed positive weights with A/C=exp(z)>=1 and B=D; then (21) is a valid upper bound. Thus one needs no global real saddle continuation to state or verify the following certificate. Choose two such weight systems L^(1),L^(2), with respective z_1,z_2>=0, and compute their actual conductance matrices and loads. If \[ \max\left\{M_2-\delta_{12},\ F(L^{(1)})- rac{z_1}{2}-\delta_2(L^{(1)}),\ F(L^{(2)})- rac{z_2}{2}-\delta_1(L^{(2)})ight\}<\Phi_D.	ag{23} \] then the original two-cap sector at the specified endpoint spectra has a strict exponential gap below Phi_D along odd levels. This follows from (3),(8),(17),(21), with only four terms. Replacing < by <= gives the corresponding weak upper bound. No sector has been moved to a different marked source. There is a legitimate local optimization for these weights. Fix b=1, write A=a exp(z), C=a, B=D=1, and minimize (22) in log a and log L_I. At z=0 the common stationary weights solve these equations. Their Hessian is the restriction of the connected original conductance Laplacian, anchored at B,D, hence positive definite. The implicit function theorem gives an analytic local family L^(1)(z) and F_1(z), with \[ F_1(0)=M_2,\qquad F_1'(0)=
u_1< rac12.	ag{24} \] The derivative is the original residual A load. Thus the high-degree Chernoff part F_1(z)-z/2 itself strictly improves for small z>0. The response delta_2(z) is continuous (a minimum of three smooth expressions); its change must still be retained when checking (23). The second mixed strip has the analogous family and derivative nu_2. This local construction does not assume global saddle differentiability. The geometric theorem supplies \[ M_2-\Phi_D\le rac{W(
u_1)+W(
u_2)}{\pi}- rac{g_D}{2\pi}. \] One sufficient way to verify (23) is that all THREE explicit losses M_2 minus its entries exceed this available budget. No such universal comparison is claimed. In particular, a relative delta>0 alone does not give an absolute Phi_D bound. There is a simpler, possibly weaker, test requiring no tilt. At the common stationary weights one has \[ \delta_{12}\ge\max(\delta_1,\delta_2). \] For each state in (15), drop the other pair's nonnegative radial cost and relax its boundary values as well as the interior values. The resulting two-terminal minimum is exactly one of the three expressions in (18), for the retained pair. This proves the claim for either pair, before taking the minimum over states. Consequently \[ \min(\delta_1,\delta_2)>M_2-\Phi_D.	ag{23a} \] alone implies the strict odd endpoint two-cap bound. At stationarity the explicit two-terminal losses are \[ \delta_i=\min\left\{2\kappa_i, rac{
u_i+\kappa_i}{2},  rac{1-
u_i+\kappa_i}{2}ight\}. \] Condition (23) retains the potentially useful extra high-degree costs and does not require (23a). ## 7. Scope and precise remaining issue The exact extraction, moment completion and high-high tail statement hold at both parities. The determinant response certificate is proved for ODD N, where (9) is the actual endpoint source, not a positive comparison substituted after signs. It controls actual globally extracted coefficients, including the pair-total Fourier phase. The new finite algebraic inequality (10) and nine-state response bound do not require real stability of Q_N. Conditional binary stability is recorded only where valid. All normalizations use N in the exponential rate, d in the original finite degree targets, and actual odd matrices of size m. The source constants remain in F_N. No independent phase per occurrence, changed exterior target, omitted parity seam, or divergent Mellin integral is introduced. What remains is quantitative: prove that (23), a stronger exact joint negative-axis criterion, or another cancellation estimate always pays the summed original geometric budget for actual cylinder exteriors. Neither the cylinder topology nor abstract stable-polynomial closure establishes that inequality here. Even levels, spectral neighborhoods, and whole filled periods are additional tasks. ## 8. A source-specific obstruction to restoring joint real stability There is a stronger necessary condition than the abstract projection counterexample. Any nonzero nonnegative polynomial Q which is homogeneous of degree d in A,C and degree d in B,D, if jointly real stable, MUST factor across the two pairs: \[ Q(A,C,B,D)=Q_1(A,C)Q_2(B,D).	ag{25} \] Here is an elementary proof, including absent endpoint coefficients. Put q(r,s)=Q(r,1,s,1) and Omega=C\(-infty,0]. Every r in Omega is a ratio of two numbers in the upper half-plane, and the choices for r,s are independent. Bihomogeneity and stability therefore imply that q(r,s) never vanishes on Omega times Omega. Let l be its actual degree in r. Its leading coefficient a(s) is nonzero at every positive s, because its coefficients are nonnegative and not all zero. Near one positive s_0, a(s) stays nonzero. For EVERY complex s in this small disk, every root of the monic polynomial q(r,s)/a(s) lies on the nonpositive real axis, since no root can be in Omega. Its coefficients are consequently real. They are also holomorphic in s, so they are constant. Hence q(r,s)=a(s)p(r) there, and polynomial identity extends this to all r,s.
