Homogenizing to the specified degrees proves (25), with possible monomial factors retained. Both factors have their nonzero one-variable roots on the negative real axis. Conversely products of these binary stable factors are jointly stable. The actual exterior provides an exact classical test against (25). Use relative log variables z,w and define the positive coefficient pressure of the SAME Q_N by \[ G(z,w)=\min_{\log a,\log L_I} \left\{\sum_tQ_t(ae^z,a,e^w,1,L_I)-\log a-\sum_{i\in I}\log L_iight\}.	ag{26} \] The formula is needed only on one neighborhood of z=w=0. Its local minimizer is finite and analytic by the same grounded-Hessian argument as (24). The original coefficient contour extracts all I demands AND the pair-total a degree d. Its only positive angular maximum is the zero phase: A,C share the pair phase, B,D are anchored, and the connected ordinary graph propagates equality of phases. All characters are primitive incidence differences. Thus the already proved positive determinant packet argument, with this literal identified phase, gives a uniform local complex relative asymptotic and in particular \[ \left. rac1N\partial_z\partial_w\log Q_N(e^z,1,e^w,1)ight|_{(0,0)} \longrightarrow G_{zw}(0,0).	ag{27} \] This is a positive coefficient saddle, not a signed-sector lower. The actual N^2 source factors and d targets are the same as in (13). Let K be the four-terminal Schur matrix from section 4, at the actual stationary weights. Write its off-diagonal entries as -g_fg^eff, with g_fg^eff>=0, and put \[ T=g_{AB}^{\mathrm{eff}}+g_{AD}^{\mathrm{eff}} +g_{CB}^{\mathrm{eff}}+g_{CD}^{\mathrm{eff}}>0. \] After eliminating I, the remaining extracted direction is e_A+e_C. Taking this ONE further Schur complement gives exactly \[  egin{aligned} G_{zw}(0,0)&=K_{AB} - rac{(K_{AA}+K_{AC})(K_{AB}+K_{CB})}{T}\ &= rac{g_{AD}^{\mathrm{eff}}g_{BC}^{\mathrm{eff}} -g_{AB}^{\mathrm{eff}}g_{CD}^{\mathrm{eff}}}{T}. \end{aligned}	ag{28} \] Therefore, if the explicit determinant in the numerator of (28) is nonzero for the actual finite-common-weight exterior, its actual Q_N fails joint real stability at every sufficiently large odd level. Indeed (25) would make the mixed logarithmic derivative identically zero, contradicting (27). This criterion refers to the original gluing solution and its original conductances; it is not a freely chosen polynomial counterexample. No claim is made that (28) is always nonzero. A separating ordinary circle tangent to both protected lines can couple the boundary through a bottleneck; the cylinder theorem does not exclude that possibility. Nor does zero in (28) prove factorization. The response bound in sections 3-6 applies regardless of this diagnostic and never requires restoring joint stability. ## Dependencies - [Original two-cap geometry and summed volume budget](research_two_cap_cylindrical_exterior_volume_budget.md) - [Original negative-axis extraction and strict one-cap tail](research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md) - [Exact all-index cap moment form](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) - [Actual endpoint CROSS factorization](actual_cross_cofactor_factorization.md) - [Finite determinant curvature and positive matrices](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md) - [Original conductance and coefficient-response normalization](research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md) - [Closed endpoint coefficient entropy](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) - [Original positive coefficient saddle and torus measure](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) No numerical audit or asymptotic experiment is used as proof. Native MathML rendering and dependency-link checks validate the document, not its mathematical conclusions.

title: An exact cap/CROSS convolution with the original MAIN-face demand
text: # An exact cap/CROSS convolution with the original MAIN-face demand The proposed inequality (8) remains open. This note keeps the even-level, original-demand convolution; an unconstrained positive envelope is a different problem. **Later status, 31 October 2026.** The [all-demand contraction theorem](research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) proves the subexponential version of (8), uniformly over every original remaining degree, and supplies the actual odd-level regularized comparison. The polynomial factor proposed in (8) remains open. The [two-spectrum continuation](research_cap_cross_two_spectrum_neighborhood_stability.md) also controls complex neighborhoods of both endpoints, with a rate excess tending to zero with their radius. The original internal demand and incidence hypothesis remain essential to this paired-reference comparison; the counterexample in section 4 still rules out arbitrary exterior face demands. ## 1. The actual local source and the demand that must be extracted first Put \(N=2m\ge4\), \(d=N-1\), \(M=m-1\), and \(\theta=\pi/N\). Let \(H_N(\sigma)\) denote the original raw cleared numerator and put \(P_N=(-1)^dH_N(-2)\), its positive endpoint polynomial. Consider two actual adjacent ports whose specialized ordered quartets are \[ E=(A,0,C,Z),\qquad F=(0,A,0,C). \] The two zeros in \(F\) are the original distinct protected faces, specialized to zero. The output triangle \((A,C,Z)\) of \(E\) and input triangle of \(F\) meet on the ordinary MAIN edge \(AC\). Restrict \(E\) to its genuine CROSS support and \(F\) to its genuine RIGHT support. These projections are parts of the original homogeneous polynomials; they are not asserted to be covariant Casimir coupons. Assume the ordinary face \(A\) has no incidence outside these two ports. Its original demand is then exactly \(d\), and must be extracted before taking a local bound. The unchanged exterior tensor may depend on \(C,Z\) and other faces, but not on \(A\). This is a local incidence hypothesis at arbitrary fixed width. For an explicit check of its original-source typing, it occurs in the certified seven-port word \([1,3,0,2,4,1,3]\) with the first cap marked. The protected faces are \(0,6\); take \[ E=\text{port }0=(1,0,4,2),\qquad F=\text{port }2=(0,1,6,4), \qquad (A,C,Z)=(L_1,L_4,L_2). \] The [original seven-port dictionary](research_shared_energy_excess_obstruction.md) shows that face \(1\) belongs only to these ports. No other original face or target changes. ## 2. Exact coefficients with all unused factors Set \[ a_r=2+2\cos((2r+1)\theta) =4\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta),\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta). \] The [actual endpoint tail](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) is \[ \begin{aligned} K_0&=1,\qquad K_1=s_1^2(A+Z),\\ K_r&=s_r^2(A+Z)K_{r-1} +s_rs_{r-1}a_{r-1}AZK_{r-2}\qquad(r\ge2). \end{aligned} \] For \(0\le h\le M\), define \[ C_{j,h} =\left[A^jZ^{d-h-j}\right]K_{d-h} \prod_{r=d-h+1}^{d}a_r, \tag{1} \] with \(C_{j,h}=0\) unless \(0\le j\le d-h\). These are precisely the coefficients of the positive CROSS endpoint at \(E\): \[ P_{E,\mathrm{CROSS}}(A,0,C,Z) =\sum_{h=0}^{M}\sum_j C_{j,h}A^jC^hZ^{d-h-j}. \tag{2} \] Every unused row is included in (1). In particular \(C_{0,0}=N^2\), since \(\prod_{r=1}^{d}s_r^2=N^2\). The raw \(E\) coupon at \(-2\) is \((-1)^d\) times (2). At \(F\), literal row reflection gives \[ \begin{aligned} H_{F,\mathrm{RIGHT}}(0,A,0,C;2) &=\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_jA^{d-j}C^j,\\ P_{F,\mathrm{RIGHT}}(0,A,0,C) &=\sum_{j=0}^{M}V_jA^{d-j}C^j, \end{aligned} \tag{3} \] where \[ \begin{aligned} U_j&=\csc^2(\theta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j} \frac{\sin^2(r\theta)} {\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)},\\ V_j&=\sec^2(\theta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j} \frac{\sin^2(r\theta)} {\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)}. \end{aligned} \tag{4} \] Both are positive. The first is the [exact flat-cap raw formula](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md). The second follows by retaining all unused rows at \(-2\) and using \(\prod_{r=0}^{d}a_r=4\). There is no additional normalization factor. ## 3. The exact original-demand convolution Define \[ \begin{aligned} B_N(C,Z) &=[A^d]\,H_{F,\mathrm{RIGHT}}(2) H_{E,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2),\\ B_N^0(C,Z) &=[A^d]\,P_{F,\mathrm{RIGHT}}P_{E,\mathrm{CROSS}}. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] Both have degree \(d\) in \(C,Z\). Neither has a \(C^d\) term, because the two original middle degrees are each at most \(M\). For \(0\le n\le d-1\), put \[ J_n=\{j:\max(0,n-M)\le j\le\min(M,n)\}. \] Then \[ [C^nZ^{d-n}]B_N =(-1)^d\sum_{j\in J_n}(-1)^jU_jC_{j,n-j}, \tag{6} \] \[ [C^nZ^{d-n}]B_N^0 =\sum_{j\in J_n}V_jC_{j,n-j}. \tag{7} \] The equality of the two occurrences of \(j\) is forced by the original \(A\)-face demand \(d\). It is not a new state identification. Both remaining face degrees stay in the polynomial. Multiplying \(B_N\) by the untouched exterior tensor and extracting every remaining original target reproduces the chosen two-port contribution exactly. The concrete possible elimination lemma is the existence of constants \(C_0,\kappa<\infty\), independent of \(N,n\), such that \[ \boxed{\quad \lvert B_N\rvert_{\mathrm{coeff}} \le C_0N^\kappa B_N^0 \quad\text{coefficientwise.}\quad} \tag{8} \] **Equation (8) is not proved.** Even a proof would address this particular incidence and support pattern, not every odd MAIN cycle. It would not permit arbitrary other spectral coupons to be replaced by endpoints. The two extreme coefficients do admit direct polynomial comparisons. For \(n=0\), only \(j=h=0\) occurs and the absolute ratio in (6)–(7) is \(\cot^2(\theta/2)\le N^2\). For \(n=d-1=2M\), only \(j=h=M\) occurs. Pairing complementary angles gives \[ \frac{U_M}{V_M} =\prod_{r=0}^{m-1}\cot^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)=1, \] so the absolute ratio is exactly one. These endpoint checks do not control the interior alternating sums. ## 4. Relaxing the original face demand gives a false inequality A stronger comparison on every coefficient of the uncontracted product fails. Extract \(Z^d\) from \(E\): homogeneity forces its unique monomial \(N^2Z^d\), leaving \(F\) alone on \(A,C\). Thus the ratio of the absolute coefficient at \(A^{d-j}C^jZ^d\) to the paired endpoint coefficient is exactly \[ \frac{U_j}{V_j} =\prod_{r=0}^{j}\cot^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta). \tag{9} \] For \(N\) divisible by \(8\), \(N\ge16\), choose \(j=N/8\). Every angle in (9) is at most \(\pi/6\), so this ratio is at least \(3^{N/8+1}\). No fixed polynomial comparison holds for all coefficients of the uncontracted pair. But this exponent has \(A\)-degree \(d-j<d\), and the actual exterior has no \(A\) incidence. It is absent from the original full coefficient. Hence (9) is not a counterexample to (8), to an original shared-target inequality, or to the volume conjecture. ## 5. Exact remaining finite problem A proof of (8) must control the signed finite convolution (6), including both summation endpoints. A terminating orthogonality or continuant identity would have to be derived with the original cutoff and unused products intact. No such identity is currently established here. The [two-anchor minimax estimate](actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.md) and [blockwise source transport](actual_blockwise_sublevel_source_transport.md) concern unit-factor anchor cores with other clocks fixed. They do not identify these conditional two-port values with the complete volume. The [cycle-packing estimate](research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md) provides loss relative to an envelope and does not prove (8). A private 80-digit probe evaluated (1), (4), (6), and (7) at five even levels through \(128\). It is a diagnostic, not an audit or proof, and is not part of this note's supporting evidence. No rate, universal polynomial comparison, or theorem for the remaining skeletons is inferred from those values. Any proof of (8) must control the original finite constrained sum, not replace it by an unconstrained envelope.

title: Why an unbranched exterior cover does not repair the replicated incidence sign obstruction
text: # Why an unbranched exterior cover does not repair the replicated incidence sign obstruction 31 October 2026. This is an obstruction to a source-preserving cover, not a fractional atomization argument or a claim that every cover of a link exterior is trivial. ## 1. The proposed construction and the exact scope Let D be an actual certified marked simple-white plat. Keep its original white triangulated sphere, pairing of the two triangles at each port, and protected adjacent MAIN faces u,v. At a port e write the four original face labels as (x,b,c,y); its two actual shaded triangles have white incidence sets (x,b,y) and (x,c,y). Their common outer edge xy is MATCHING. The four labels are distinct. In particular the two outer faces cannot both be the protected MAIN pair, so at least one outer face is ordinary. Let B be the original supported bipartite incidence graph: one node for each port and each ordinary white face, and one edge for every supported port/face incidence. Write \(\varepsilon_{e,f}\in\mathbf F_2\) for the literal incidence sign character in the selected source chamber. All exact scalar modes remain separate. A row gauge and common face signs would solve \[ \varepsilon_{e,f}=\kappa_e+\gamma_f\quad\text{in }\mathbf F_2. \tag{1} \] For the strict straddling LEFT chamber the entries are (0,0,1,0), and RIGHT is reflected; the argument below allows any chamber whose two triangle copies of a common outer incidence have the SAME character. This includes the actual characters in the current regular-window route. The suggested repair is an actual finite unbranched cover of the original drilled exterior, with unchanged source chamber and q data on every copy of each port, followed by the original cut-ball fan construction. To make that construction source-preserving, it must assign one signed clock to each lifted white face and allow local row/triangle gauges, with each lifted incidence retaining its base character. We allow different gauges on the two triangle halves; this is weaker than requiring a single gauge on an entire lifted port. Magnitudes may vary between sheets. No averaging of q, no change of chamber between sheets, and no new incidence signs are permitted in this particular proposal. **Theorem.** Under these hypotheses, such a lifted sign assignment exists on an exterior cover only if (1) already has a solution on the original supported graph B. Conversely, if (1) is soluble, its signs pull back to every cover (and the identity cover suffices for this sign issue). Thus an unbranched cover cannot remove a nontrivial original incidence class within the proposed source-preserving construction, in any degree. This is only a necessary sign test for the original group/fan sewing. Solving it does not supply the other geometric, source-asymptotic, boundary, or regulator hypotheses of that construction. ## 2. Resolve ports before discussing topology Let H be the white--triangle incidence graph of ONE original cut ball. There is one node \(t_{e,+}\) for (x,b,y), one \(t_{e,-}\) for (x,c,y), and one node per original white face. There is one edge for each triangle corner. This is the radial graph of the actual white triangulated sphere, not an abstract replacement of its ribbon structure. Let H' remove only the two protected white nodes and their incident edges. No ordinary face is removed. Pull the source character to H' by \[ \varepsilon_H(t_{e,+},f)=\varepsilon_{e,f},\qquad \varepsilon_H(t_{e,-},f)=\varepsilon_{e,f}. \tag{2} \] The following elementary equivalence is the key algebraic point: \[ \varepsilon_H\text{ is a coboundary on }H' \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \varepsilon\text{ is a coboundary on }B. \tag{3} \] The forward implication is worth proving explicitly. If \[ \varepsilon_H(t,f)=\kappa_t+\gamma_f, \] choose an ordinary outer face o of port e. Both halves are incident to o and have the same prescribed character there. Hence \[ \kappa_{e,+}+\gamma_o=\varepsilon_{e,o} =\kappa_{e,-}+\gamma_o, \] so \(\kappa_{e,+}=\kappa_{e,-}\). Their common value defines \(\kappa_e\) in (1). The converse simply copies a row gauge to both halves. There is also an explicit cycle version. In any supported B cycle, replace a passage f--e--g by f--t--g if the two faces lie in one half. If it must pass from b to c, choose an ordinary outer o and use \[ b\;--\;t_{e,+}\;--\;o\;--\;t_{e,-}\;--\;c. \] The two added outer characters cancel in \(\mathbf F_2\). Each B cycle therefore gives a closed H' walk with the SAME sign sum. Thus every original nonzero cycle has a specific resolved witness; protected zero targets cannot hide it. ## 3. Why the resolved obstruction cannot survive inside a lifted ball The topological input is the ACTUAL cut described in [original cut-ball construction](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), §§1--4. Cut along the projection sphere and the original crossing half disks. Opening each specified half disk cancels its semicircle handle. Each resulting piece is a genuine ball with the original labeled white/shaded boundary. Compact truncation of its ideal vertices retains a genuine compact ball. The truncated rectangles at main and auxiliary contacts are boundary disks, not deleted holes in that ball. The graph H can be represented on this boundary by face centers and arcs through their actual common edges. The white--triangle adjacency is the dual radial adjacency of that labeled medial cellulation. In particular every H' loop is null-homotopic in the cut ball. Removing protected nodes from the graph does not remove the protected faces or the filling disks from the manifold. A small MAIN-contact radial four-cycle bounds a disk through the corresponding truncated cusp rectangle; larger supported cycles are no less contractible in the ball. The boundary of one such rectangle is not itself a main-cusp meridian: a genuine meridional curve on the assembled cusp torus traverses the appropriate identified rectangles. One cannot assign nontrivial meridional monodromy to the perimeter of a single retained rectangle. For example, the original six-port chart in [exact face-sign criterion](research_spectral_face_sign_cocycle.md) has triangles (5,7,0) at the output of port3 and (6,5,7) at the input of port5. Their shared edge (5,7) is MAIN. The nonzero sign cycle \[ \mathrm{port}_3\;--\;\mathrm{face}_7\;--\;\mathrm{port}_5 \;--\;\mathrm{face}_5\;--\;\mathrm{port}_3 \] is already the resolved four-cycle around that one contact. Its obstruction is a contractible disk relation, not a choice of a main component's meridional monodromy. The general proof does not depend on this example or assert that its chosen chamber is a full maximum. For any unbranched covering \(p:Y'\to Y\), pull back the characteristic map of this compact cut ball. Since the ball is simply connected, each lift is an actual copy of the entire ball with the same boundary incidence data. This statement does not require a regular, connected, or double cover. It remains true when the original shaded pairing sends a half to another copy, as in a retained half twist: that pairing changes which lifted balls are glued, not the incidence within a single lifted ball. Now examine just ONE lifted ball. The proposed common signed clocks give one \(\gamma\) for each of its ordinary white faces. Each shaded triangle has its allowed local gauge \(\kappa_t\), possibly coming from a different lifted port than the other half with the same base label. Because every port copy retains the base chamber, their incidence relations are exactly (2). Consequently \(\varepsilon_H\) MUST be a coboundary on H'. Equation (3) forces the original \(\varepsilon\) to be exact on B. This proves the theorem. Equivalently, if a graph voltage cover is being interpreted as actual sheet transition data, all of its resolved H' loop voltages must vanish because those loops bound disks in one original ball. A nonzero B cycle has the same-voltage H' witness from §2, violating this necessary extension relation. Such a graph cover does not extend over the original cut ball; it is not an exterior cover with the required source incidence dictionary. ## 4. Relation to more general covering criteria For an independently specified graph map \(i:G\to Y\), a binary voltage character extends to a double cover of Y precisely when its class lies in the image of \[ i^*:H^1(Y;\mathbf F_2)\longrightarrow H^1(G;\mathbf F_2). \] Equivalently it must annihilate the kernel of \(H_1(G;\mathbf F_2)\to H_1(Y;\mathbf F_2)\). At the presentation level one must also respect every attaching relation; for permutation-valued finite covers the product of the gluing permutations around each actual relation is the identity. Agreement of meridional monodromies along a component is one necessary check, not a substitute for the ball and edge relations. No canonical map of the already-collapsed source graph B to Y should be assumed without checking the two shaded halves and their repeated outer incidences. The resolved ball graph is what gives the decisive relation here. The theorem does not claim that every failure to extend a \(\mathbf Z/2\) character prevents every unrelated finite cover. It proves directly that ANY proposed exterior cover carrying the replicated original signs and common-face sewing would already solve (1) on one lifted ball. ## 5. What this rules out, and what it leaves open This obstruction is different from [fractional-cover obstruction](research_fractional_cover_star_obstruction.md). There is no atomization, no change of angle allocations between sheets, and no Jensen loss in this argument. Replicating q exactly avoids that earlier problem but does not avoid the contractible resolved sign loop. It rules out repairing an inconsistent real source sign chamber solely by passing to an unbranched cover while retaining the original two-ball white-face and port dictionary. Therefore dividing a hypothetical cover representation volume by its degree cannot bypass this sign obstruction under those hypotheses. It does not rule out a construction that changes the chamber or local generating function on different copies, changes the projected incidence data, inserts new defect surfaces, or uses a branched cover. Those would need their own exact source/action comparison and fundamental-chain proof. It also does not prove a source upper bound from the unresolved magnitude and phase-cancellation estimates. The proof uses [exact face-sign criterion](research_spectral_face_sign_cocycle.md), [conditional signed group sewing](research_regular_signed_spectral_group_sewing.md), [original cut-ball construction](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md) §§1--4, [original paired fundamental chain](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md) §3, and the fractional-cover obstruction above.

title: Complete volume added by a marked unit chain
text: # Complete volume added by a marked unit chain 31 October 2026. Preserved analytical consequence of the [unit-chain closure theorem](general_marked_unit_chain_filling_volume.md). No new quantum estimate is claimed. Let \(\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\) be the absolutely normalized complete source capacity. In the marked strip normalization of that theorem, all new curvatures are one, and every old curvature is unchanged. Consequently the ordinary face-target logarithms are unchanged. Set \(C_0=Q(0,1,1)=2G/\pi\), with \(G\) Catalan's constant. For \(m\geq1\), the first prefix port contributes \(C_0\); the other \(2m-1\) prefix ports each contribute \(2C_0\). The changed first core port contributes an additional \(C_0\). Every other core action stays fixed. Thus \[ \Phi_{D^{(m)}}-\Phi_D =C_0+(2m-1)2C_0+C_0=4mC_0. \] It follows from the actual complete-source volume calibration that \[ \operatorname{Vol}(Y_{D^{(m)}})-\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D) =16mG=4m\,v_{\mathrm{oct}}. \] Here \(v_{\mathrm{oct}}=4G\) is the regular ideal octahedron's volume: splitting it into four ideal tetrahedra with angles \((\pi/2,\pi/4,\pi/4)\) gives \(4[\Lambda(\pi/2)+2\Lambda(\pi/4)]=4G\). The same difference is zero at \(m=0\). This proves that the added complete source regions increase the actual drilled volume, and are not a redundant presentation of a fixed augmented exterior. It does not assert additivity of the filled volumes or a filling threshold uniform in depth.

title: Residual Gaussian Ward currents and the cyclotomic source resonance
text: # Residual Gaussian Ward currents and the cyclotomic source resonance Research proof and audit, 27 October 2026. At COMPLETE color, the literal local currents and explicitly computed cut boundary rows give an all-order transverse Gaussian Ward ideal on the geometric framing torsor. It is a flat rank-one ideal, with the actual Gaussian amplitude as its nonzero horizontal generator. The original cut co-source has precisely the leading covariance required by the uniform Gaussian density. These formal statements do not identify the global finite framing contraction. An explicit cyclotomic resonance obstructs a naive extension to that source; keeping the whole power normal gives a separate exact divided-current/source comparison. ## 1. An explicit operator on the actual transverse block Use the actual independent flow coordinates of [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). Keep two coordinates `chi=(chi_1,chi_2)` external, and contract the other `r=m-1` logarithmic coordinates `u` by the nondegenerate geometric Gaussian. Write `H=Log Q` and I=C_beta(H) exp(S/H) a(chi,u,H), Z(chi,H)=G_chi(I). All original characters, half-steps, pivots and base-only factors are kept. The normalized moment of a regular insertion is E_chi[h]=G_chi(h I)/Z(chi,H). (1) The denominator is a nonzero formal Gaussian block, not the selected finite knot scalar. After its recorded common exponential and base line are factored out, it is a formal unit. Thus every coefficient of (1) is recursively computable by Wick contraction and finite formal division, and is algebraic on the stated geometric/half-density cover. Compose the literal local currents in [the crossing-current note](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md), keeping their multiplication insertions. Use the same unimodular integral closure solver as for the actual flow coordinates. Every resulting interior term has the explicit form h_(gamma,beta)(chi,u,H) T_chi^gamma S_u^beta I, where the shifts translate logarithmic coordinates by `H` times their displayed integer vectors. Transverse translation gives its exact Gaussian image E_(chi+H gamma)[S_u^(-beta)h_(gamma,beta)(chi,u,H)] T_chi^gamma Z. (2) The proof is the literal substitution `y=u+H beta`, with the critical point recentered at the unique corresponding branch. The insertion is shifted in the opposite direction; it may not be replaced by its unshifted value. External base substitution commutes with the finite Wick recursion. Summing (2) defines an explicit all-order residual difference operator for each composed current. It annihilates `Z` whenever the corresponding interior current identity is zero. Finite endpoint indicators remain their separate source terms; they have not been given a fictitious value in this interior completion. For the two full-tensor Hopf-adjoint combinations 2(ad_K-I)+2 ad_Ecal, ad_F+ad_Ecal, the already proved moment-map calculation gives the two cut-Borel principal fields `A(h_sl+2f_sl)` and `A(e_sl+f_sl)`. Formula (2) transports each term of their interior current equations. The marked `e,D` coupon is not Hopf invariant, so its cut boundary insertions must also be written and transported. The next section does this explicitly at complete color. The generic-M endpoint terms are retained and are not covered by the homogeneous complete-color assertion. ## 2. Gaussian covariance supplies genuine quantum corrections The map (1) is linear, not multiplicative. This matters even in the coherent all-level interior model. If `H_perp=S_uu` is the critical Hessian, direct quadratic Wick contraction gives E[fg]-E[f]E[g] =-H (partial_u f)^t H_perp^(-1)(partial_u g)+O(H^2), (3) for H-independent regular insertions, evaluated at the critical point. The sign comes from covariance `-H H_perp^(-1)` for the phase convention `exp(S/H)`. Cubic-phase and amplitude-drift terms cancel from this covariance at first order. Consequently replacing each coefficient of a product or bracket of Ward currents separately by its scalar expectation is incorrect. Formula (2), applied to the whole ordered term with all insertions, retains these corrections. This is different from the impossible product-preserving fixed-root matrix-to-scalar map. ## 3. The actual complete cut co-source matches the principal density The missing cut terms can be calculated directly, without postulating a Haar form. For `Phi(C)=Tr(e C)`, cyclicity gives the exact dual Hopf rows e_K=K^(-1)eK-e, e_E=K^(-1)eEcal-Ecal K^(-1)e, e_F=eF-KFeK^(-1). Thus `Phi((ad_K-I)C)=Tr(e_K C)` and similarly for the other two generators. The actual one-cut operator has diagonal support term by term, before the remaining internal sums, by total-index conservation. Only the diagonals of these rows contribute. Use `A=Q^a`, `k_a=xQ^(-a)`, `epsilon_a=M Q^(-a)-M^(-1)` for `1<=a<N`, and actual endpoints `epsilon_0=epsilon_N=0`. Direct multiplication gives (e_K)_aa=0, (e_F)_aa=(1-Q)A/N, (e_E)_aa=(Q-1)A/(N M x) +kappa(1_(a=N-1)-1_(a=0))/(N x). (3a) For example the E diagonal is `[epsilon_a/k_a-epsilon_(a+1)/k_(a+1)]/N`; the displayed two endpoint corrections are exactly what replacing the actual truncated edges by their interior formula would miss. At complete color `M=1,x=-q^(-1)`, these simplify exactly to (e_E)_aa=q(1-Q)A/N, (e_F)_aa=(1-Q)A/N. (3b) If the original scalar summand already includes its `1/N`, the boundary multiplication coefficients of the two displayed cut-Borel combinations are therefore b_1=2q(1-Q)A, b_2=(1+q)(1-Q)A. Both have `b_i/H -> -2A` as `H=Log Q` tends to zero. These are literal co-source contributions, not guessed scalar connection terms. Choosing the external pair to contain the actual cut index is always possible: its differential is nonzero on the framing torsor, and one more actual coordinate completes it to an etale pair. The matching geometric divergence is equally explicit. At `M=1` right multiplication of `F(r,s)=[r,1-r;s,-s]` by a row-stochastic frame change has fields X_a=r partial_r+s partial_s, X_b=(1-r)partial_r-s partial_s. The conjugation convention `delta G=[xi,G]` gives xi_1=A(h_sl+2f_sl)=-2X_b, xi_2=A(e_sl+f_sl)=X_a-X_b. Explicitly both traceless matrices have eigenvalue one on `(1,1)`. Subtracting `I` gives the row-sum-zero matrices with parameters `(a,b)=(0,2)` and `(-1,1)`, respectively, and normalized frame variation is `delta F=-F(xi-I)`. This checks the projective normalization and the signs in the two fields. For the actual cut density Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], A_cut=1/(1+s), direct differentiation gives div_(Omega_cut)(xi_1)=div_(Omega_cut)(xi_2)=2 A_cut. Consequently the actual co-source terms satisfy the precise leading covariance identity Lie_(xi_i) Omega_cut+(b_i/H)|_(H=0) Omega_cut=0. (3c) The uniform Gaussian density is a nonzero base-only multiple of this form, so it obeys the same identity. This proves the principal source covariance with the original cut. It does not yet prove that all finite normal/endpoint insertions have the required all-order image. ## 4. The complete residual current ideal is a flat line ### The actual graph current and its first-order field Use the local current identities with the input/output operator order fixed in the crossing-current note. Pair adjacent edge insertions along the braid. Every reindexing is retained as its finite difference current. The elementary product rule is j T^v c-(T^(-v)j)c=(T^v-I)[(T^(-v)j)c]. It fixes the sign and placement of each resulting boundary multiplier. The actual pivotal caps cancel the matched Hopf-adjoint insertions; their remaining boundary is exactly the dual cut row computed in Section 3. The determinant-one flow solver expresses all translations in the independent actual flow coordinates. This gives scalar divergence identities with the boundary coefficients `b_i` included. A translation by an integer vector can be written as a sum of coordinate differences by telescoping its steps, so no nonintegral current is introduced. At COMPLETE color these are homogeneous equations on the original scalar array after the explicit boundary term is brought to the same side. Each multiplier is `N diag(e_h)`, since the scalar summand already contains `1/N`. At generic `M`, equation (3a) instead leaves the two specified kappa-endpoint currents. They must not be omitted by continuity from the complete value. Here is a direct principal-field proof, beyond just identifying the full End-space Hopf symbols. For a local observable h(q,T)=sum_v h_v(q,H) T^v, acting on a generating kernel `exp(S/H)a`, its first amplitude-derivative coefficient is sum_v h_v(q,0) exp(v dot p) v=partial_p h_cl. This follows by first-order Taylor expansion of each shifted amplitude. The right kernel action uses the opposite input translation; therefore its commutator gives the position velocities of the corresponding Hamiltonian field on the canonical graph. The zero-order first correction is carried by the current's amplitude and boundary terms; it is not used to determine these vector coefficients. At a crossing with actual update `q_out=P q_in+R k`, the transfer velocity is uniquely obtained from that crossing's two output velocities. For example, in the positive update `(a,b)->(b+k,a-k)` it is simultaneously `k_dot=c_dot-b_dot=a_dot-d_dot`; equality follows from conservation of the local total position. The negative update gives the same statement with the prescribed signs. Determine this velocity crossing by crossing, then compose. This avoids trying to solve an underdetermined whole-word position equation. Restrict to the complete critical germ. The exact critical-scheme correspondence identifies this propagated Hamiltonian variation with infinitesimal conjugation of the framed representation. For the two compensated cut-stabilizer combinations it is exactly `xi_1,xi_2` above. The `ad_K` part alone can have zero position projection; no independent field is inferred from it alone. The compensated fields are tangent to the full critical framing surface. Since the retained actual coordinates are etale there, their two projected velocities are independent. Transverse Gaussian pushforward evaluates the leading velocity coefficients at the critical point and kills the transverse total currents. Formula (2), together with the explicit complete boundary weights, therefore constructs two homogeneous residual operators with these independent first-order vector fields. Their scalar leading term agrees with (3c). All higher coefficients are given by the same actual normalized moments, with the boundary terms still included. No separate scalar Ward character was assumed. ### Exact operator-ideal reduction Here is the exact operator-algebra reduction, without assuming multiplicativity of (1). Factor the framing-independent action and base line from `Z`, leaving an algebraic formal amplitude z(chi,H) in K_geo[[H]]^times. The full critical action has zero derivatives along the framing torsor, so it cancels from external framing shifts. Let `Wbar_1,2` be the complete-color residual operators just constructed, normalized by their common `H`. Expand their external shifts as formal differential operators; each H coefficient has finite differential order. Conjugate by the computed actual amplitude: P_i=z^(-1) Wbar_i z. Then `P_i(1)=0`. Right-normal ordering in commuting etale framing derivations writes, exactly, P_i=sum_(a=1)^2 A_ia(H,partial_chi) partial_(chi_a), A_ia(0)=xi_i^a. The leading 2 by 2 matrix is invertible on the framing chart. Its inverse in the H-adically completed matrix algebra of differential operators is the convergent Neumann series. Hence partial_(chi_a)=sum_i (A^(-1))_ai P_i. Conversely every `P_i` is a left differential-operator combination of these derivatives. Thus the residual current left ideal is precisely the annihilator ideal of the constant line after this gauge. Ungauged it is the flat connection nabla_a=partial_(chi_a)-partial_(chi_a)Log z. (4) Its flatness follows by direct commutation of logarithmic derivatives. This identifies the resulting complete-color formal Ward **ideal** and its cyclic rank-one module. Every other residual current annihilates `z` and hence belongs to this same annihilator ideal. It does not assert that separately expectation-substituted generators obey an undeformed Borel bracket, or that their full relation complexes have already been identified with the finite-source Ward complex. The uniform principal-density theorem gives `Omega_perp^2=-(T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2`. With the recorded square-root mark, the leading framing density is a base-only nonzero multiple of `Omega_cut`. Consequently (4) has that canonical leading trivialization. Its higher gauge coefficients are the actual Gaussian coefficients, rather than freely chosen transport data. ## 5. Why this interior comparison does not extend coefficientwise to the source Even one frame direction detects the missing completion. For the Euler derivation `D=A partial_A`, ordinary formal shift-to-current comparison uses exp(H D)-1=H D B(H D), B(v)=(exp(v)-1)/v, B(0)=1. (5) On the local stationary formal completion, the corresponding operator has positive stationary degree, so the Bernoulli adapter `B` is a unit. On a cyclotomic carry sector `A^N`, with `H=2pi*i/N`, it instead has B(H D) A^N=B(2pi*i) A^N=0. (6) The ordinary Euler current there is nonzero. These sectors are not regular coefficients in the same WKB line: `A^N` is an extra exponential character when `N=2pi*i/H`. Thus the local formal current isomorphism cannot be extended by the same invertible adapter while preserving the literal finite carry source. Deleting `A=1` by the proved relative-Ward homotopy does not remove this resonance. The relation `A^N=U` and its whole normal remain on the retained source. Nor does the normalized moment (1) control spectral degree near `N`, endpoint currents, or exponentially small local functions with a different global cut pairing. ## 6. The divided Frobenius current gives the exact normal repair The necessary extra direction can be computed, rather than postulated. Retain C_U=k[U^+/-1,A]/(A^N-U). Unfold the shift coherently by sigma_Q(A)=Q A, sigma_Q(U)=Q^N U. It preserves the relation. At `Q=zeta` its `N`-th power is identity. Before specializing put `delta=1-Q^N`. Then sigma_Q^N(A)=(1-delta)A, sigma_Q^N(U)=(1-delta)^N U. Therefore on every Laurent polynomial, and hence every regular whole normal germ, the exact divided normal is [(sigma_Q^N-I)/(1-Q^N)]_(Q=zeta)=-D_phys, D_phys=A partial_A+N U partial_U. (7) The derivation preserves `A^N-U`. It does not descend to the fiber `U=1`: `D_phys(U-1)=N U` is nonzero there. This proves precisely which normal datum a fixed-fiber framing derivative would discard. Let `tau_N=Tr_(C_U/k[U^+/-1])/N`, the original averaged cut on this whole finite algebra. In the canonical basis `1,A,...,A^(N-1)`, `tau_N(f)=f_0(U)`, so direct coefficient differentiation gives tau_N D_phys=N U partial_U tau_N. (8) This is an actual source-current chain map with all carries retained. It also extends coefficientwise through the polynomial relative source resolution and its endpoint transgression. More explicitly mark `alpha(U)^N=U`, `alpha(1)=1`, and use the evaluation branches `A=alpha(U)zeta^a`. In this basis `D_phys` is `N U partial_U`. On matrix families it gives the induced connection on endomorphisms. The coefficientwise extension of the original head projector `e` is constant. The whole-normal pivot has two distinct marked lifts: K_U=x A^(-1), g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1), g_lit=K_U^(1-N)=U g_red, D_red=g_red^(-1)e, D_lit=U^(-1)D_red. Only g_lit is the literal clock power away from U=1. Their physical normal rates are D_phys(g_red)=-g_red, D_phys(D_red)=D_red, D_phys(g_lit)=(N-1)g_lit, D_phys(D_lit)=-(N-1)D_lit. Both products are exactly e, so their paired cut has the same normal covariance. Their separate pivot/source jets differ by the retained U adapter and must not be identified from the common root value. Thus for the **original** marked matrix cut, Phi_U(D_phys C)=N U partial_U Phi_U(C), Phi_U(C)=Tr(g_red D_red C) =Tr(g_lit D_lit C)=Tr(e C). (9) No Haar division or normalization replacement is used. This e is the coefficientwise whole-normal projector, not the finite-rank Verma coupon Gamma=i e pi_0. Under the explicit [Mellin comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), those act respectively as tau_N(f)1 and [tau_N(f)]_(U=1)1. The latter has the additional normal row [nabla,Gamma_U]f=-[tau_N(nabla f)]_(U=1)1, nabla=D_phys/N. Equation (9) does not discard that finite-vacuum cut derivative. The boundary split Ward complex can be carried along this normal connection as well. On degree zero use the displayed derivative; on its image degree one define `nabla^1(delta_W C)=delta_W(D_phys C)`. It is well defined because `ker delta_W` is the scalar line, which the derivative preserves. The explicit splitting makes this a strict normal current map on the relative-Ward boundary complex. Its degree-one action is not an uncorrected entrywise derivative of the varying K,F Ward rows. ## 7. Exact scope of the new comparison step Equations (1)--(2), the explicit complete dual rows, and the principal-field proof construct the complete-color all-order residual Ward ideal. Equation (3c) identifies the original cut's leading covariance with the Gaussian framing density. Equations (7)--(9) independently identify the divided Frobenius normal current with the literal whole cut source, including `g,D` and endpoint transgression. These are proved pieces of the needed comparison. They are not yet a map between those two completed modules. The interior connection is over a single geometric WKB sector; the whole source carries the resonant exponential characters and normal modes exposed by (6)--(7). A source-compatible extension must transport these sectors, not replace the adapter in (5) by a unit outside its domain. The explicit marked transgression therefore does not yet prove that this residual geometric class has nonzero image under the selected finite cut. No nonzero selected global cycle, Stokes coefficient, or volume limit follows. [Exact source audit](../experiments/audit_residual_ward_source_covariance.py) and [results](../experiments/residual_ward_source_covariance_results.json) check the actual complete/generic-M boundary rows, both geometric divergences and field independence, and whole-normal Euler/carry identities. The all-order current/ideal argument above is a proof, not inferred from these finite diagnostics.

title: Independent audit of the resolved framing and Gaussian boundary residue

# Independent audit of the resolved framing and Gaussian boundary residue Audit, 27 October 2026. Sections 2--4.1 of [springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md) and Sections 3--6 of [compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md) pass this independent global-transition, normalization and scope check. No tests were rerun. ## 1. The actual framing torsor and its nonextendible centralizer The printed sections conjugate \(E_{12}\) to the two Springer matrices. Their ratio is \[ g_N^{-1}g_S= rac1v  egin{pmatrix}1&-1/(v\eta)\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Thus equality of the right-centralizer framings gives \(b_S=b_N+1/(v\eta)\), with the printed sign. The fibre-degree argument proves a genuine obstruction. At degree \(-1\), a coboundary has powers \(v^{\ge0}\) and \(v^{\le-2}\); it cannot supply \(v^{-1}\). At every nonnegative fibre degree, the north and south powers cover all Laurent powers, so the whole line bundle has no corresponding additive extension class. The elementary affine additive-descent calculation supplies the stated chart trivializations. This proves nonextension as an ordinary algebraic additive torsor; no asymptotic argument is involved. Renormalization \(a=-\eta b\) gives exactly \(a_S=v-v^2a_N\). The invertible matrix \[ g= egin{pmatrix}\eta&-a\\eta v&1-va\end{pmatrix}, \qquad\det g=\eta, \] recovers every projective frame on \(\eta
e0\); its south representative is \(-v\) times its north representative. Hence \(Y\setminus E_{\mathrm{exc}}\) is all \(PGL_2\), not only a birational open chart. At the boundary the matrix has rank one, the second flag is transverse to the retained first-column direction, and the original constant centralizer action vanishes. The line-bundle-valued translated action remains free, as stated. The elementary-modification lattice keeps an abstract noncentral meridian. It does not give a regular raw irreducible representation with central meridian. The separate escape argument is correct: irreducibility gives \(C_0
e0\), while \(\operatorname{Tr}[\mu_0,ho(g)]=2+C_0^2\). A regular raw limit with \(\mu	o I\) would contradict this constant commutator trace. The two displayed escape matrices have the stated \(t_c^{-1/2}\) and \((1-t_c)^{-1/2}\) terms. ## 2. Global logarithmic form and the exact Haar adapter Substitution \(b=-a/\eta\) gives \[ d\eta\wedge dv\wedge db =-d\log\eta\wedge dv\wedge da. \] Under the south transition, \(d\log\eta'=d\log\eta+2\,dv/v\); its extra term wedges to zero. Both this logarithmic form and its residue are therefore global. Its residue is \(-dv\wedge da=2\pi i\,\omega_I\), with the correct compact trace normalization. The canonical-bundle identities \(K_Y=O(2)\), \(O(E_{\mathrm{exc}})=O(-2)\), and \(K_Y(E_{\mathrm{exc}})=O\) agree with the explicit form. The actual bridge, rather than a guessed Haar measure, fixes the interior scalar: \[ v=p^{-1},\quad\eta=-sp,\quad b=(1-r)/s,\quad a=p(1-r). \] Its Jacobian is exactly \[ d\eta\wedge dv\wedge db=- rac{dr\wedge ds\wedge dp}{sp}. \] Consequently \[ \Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}\wedge d\log p = rac{H_G}{1-\eta v}. \] The adapter cannot be discarded in the interior. Its boundary value is one, which proves the printed residue without an adjustable numerical multiplier. On the already marked Gaussian phase and common base line, \(\Omega_{ eta,0}=c_ eta\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}\) with \(c_ eta^2=-T_ eta/2
e0\). Keeping that recorded line gives \[  rac1{2\pi i}\operatorname{Res}_{E_{\mathrm{exc}}} (\Omega_{ eta,0}\wedge d\log p) =c_ eta\omega_I. \] Thus its principal associated-boundary class and compact residue period are nonzero. This uses the marked phase; it does not choose a sign from the identity of squares. ## 3. Physical and associated cycles remain distinct The logarithmic section \(r_*=1-\log A/(2\pi i)\) has the stated deck change \(-1\). Its relative centralizer jump is \(-1/s\), whose primitive co-source has residues \(+1\) at \(s=0\) and \(-1\) at \(s=-1\). The opposite sign of the absolute frame coordinate \((1-r)/s\) is explicitly retained. The exceptional divisor over all of \(X\) and the physical exponential section are different objects. On the latter, \(\eta=(1-e^{-2\pi iva})/v\); its intersections with the divisor are the integer \(va\) fibres, with the removable special rule at \(v=0\). The real compact physical cycle meets it at its two endpoint poles. This does not identify that physical cycle with the compact cycle used to pair the divisor residue. The notes correctly make no such identification. They also do not extend all higher Gaussian coefficients or unrestricted logarithmic Green currents. An unmarked \(\log\eta\) would make \(d\eta/\eta\) exact and erase the relative residue. The missing whole current/source pushforward, and its nonzero selected horizontal image, remain separate. The polynomial coherent clutch and its line weights are intrinsic source data; they are not asserted to be the actual quantum dressing of every geometric frame.

title: The resonant framing blowup and the actual peripheral line
text: # The resonant framing blowup and the actual peripheral line 27 October 2026. This note proves exact identities on the geometric framing chart of the original first-slot inverse-pair cut. The full ADO dimension cancels the chart's apparent first-order pole before specialization. The paired principal Gaussian line also extends. Neither statement constructs the required map from the actual finite source to a selected geometric period. One correction matters: the generic physical inverse-pair atom is `AC=M*b_h/b_(h+1)`. Its first boundary coefficient is `s*zeta`. The coefficient `s*zeta+a/2` belongs to the RAW prefix quotient `b_h/b_(h+1)`, which omits its physical factor M. Those expressions cannot be substituted for each other in a quantum-product boundary calculation. ## 1. Work on a geometric formal branch, before imposing level N Let R be a characteristic-zero formal discrete valuation ring with uniformizer epsilon, containing the marked geometric coefficients. Fix a meridian deformation with kappa=M-M^(-1)=epsilon*a, M(0)=1, p=1-epsilon*zeta, d=1-kappa*beta, t=r+beta*s=d/(epsilon*zeta). Here M is the unique formal root near one of M-M inverse=epsilon*a. The coefficients c,beta,s may vary regularly with epsilon; c and s are units at zero. All leading formulas below use their values at epsilon=0. We work where zeta and s*zeta+a are units. These are classical geometric coordinates, not a newly chosen finite source. The actual generic-M first-slot matrices, as fixed in [the checked meridian-germ appendix](universal_resonant_cut_word_audit.md), are F=[[r,1-r],[s,-kappa-s]], U=[[M-c*beta,kappa*beta-c*beta^2], [c,M^(-1)+c*beta]]. Set Delta=s+kappa*r. Exact substitution gives Delta=d*(s*zeta+a)/zeta. (1) In particular Delta is a unit on this chart, despite r having valuation minus one. Direct conjugation gives, for k=(F inverse U F)_11, k=M^(-1)+a*(epsilon*a+s)/(s*zeta+a) -c*d*p/[epsilon^2*zeta*(s*zeta+a)]. (2) For completeness, U-M inverse I is the rank-one product [kappa-c*beta;c]*(1,beta). Its conjugated (1,1) entry is [kappa*(kappa+s)+c*(d-t)]*t/Delta, which proves (2), without discarding any meridian term. The actual physical momentum is still -(F inverse U F)_12/(k-M^(-1))=p. The SECOND balanced physical position, denoted A_e to distinguish it from the reference cut coordinate A_cut, is A_e=M/k, epsilon^(-2)*A_e -> -zeta*(s*zeta+a)/c. (3) Thus its valuation is two on this unit chart. The reference coordinate remains A_cut=M/(M+s); the two coordinates must not be conflated. ## 2. The framing lattice extends although the scalar clock escapes The matrix F has determinant -Delta, a unit, and at least one entry of valuation minus one. Over R its Smith exponents are therefore (-1,+1). Equivalently Lambda=F^(-1)R^2 is a free rank-two lattice inside the framed representation space. For a geometric representation defined over R, every conjugated holonomy F inverse rho(g) F preserves Lambda. Also F*(1,1)^t=(1,-kappa)^t, so the marked inverse flag remains primitive. This proves flatness of the underlying geometric representation lattice, not a comparison with a quantum source lattice. There is a useful precise restriction on that comparison. The actual finite second position operator has relation B_e^N=1 on the complete root fiber. A multiplicative scalar specialization carrying B_e to the geometric A_e in (3) cannot preserve that relation: A_e^N has valuation 2N, whereas 1 has valuation zero. Multiplication by a unit does not change this discrepancy. Dividing A_e by epsilon squared changes the N-th-power relation by epsilon^(2N), which is precisely a factor that must be accounted for, rather than a harmless unit gauge. This excludes a regular scalar-clock substitution with the original norm relation. It does not exclude a linear period transform, a singular change of lattice with its determinant retained, or an irregular/nonlocal source comparison. Such a construction would still need to carry the actual word and selected source. ## 3. The actual dimension cancels the framing-form pole exactly At fixed M the invariant form already specified by the marked centralizer calculation is Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[Delta*(M+s)]. Treat epsilon and a as base parameters. Using (1) and dlog A_cut=-ds/(M+s), its exact expression is epsilon*Omega_cut =dlog A_cut wedge dzeta/[zeta*(s*zeta+a)]. (4) This is an algebraic identity, not a claim about a selected integration cycle or a uniform Gaussian expansion. Now retain the original dimension line, including its phase: d_N(M)=eta_N/u_N(M), eta_N=i^(N+3), u_N(M)=(M^N-M^(-N))/(M-M^(-1)). The quotient u_N is a Laurent polynomial with u_N(1)=N. With B=M^N its exact fraction-field expression is d_N/eta_N=kappa*B/(B^2-1). Consequently, before any limiting argument, (d_N/eta_N)*Omega_cut =a*B/(B^2-1) *dlog A_cut wedge dzeta/[zeta*(s*zeta+a)]. (5) The epsilon inverse pole in (4) cancels against the original peripheral line. The factor B squared minus one remains in (5). It cannot be deleted at a torsion value or used to replace the whole regular lattice by two separately undefined quotients. At M=1 the original polynomial formula gives d_N/eta_N=1/N. On the physical power graph epsilon=1/N and fixed a, the branch is M_N=exp(asinh(a/(2N))), B_N=exp(N*asinh(a/(2N))) -> exp(a/2). Thus the scalar in (5) tends to a/[2*sinh(a/2)] away from its remaining norm divisor. At a=0 its regular continuation is one, in agreement with the exact value (1/N)/epsilon=1. This verifies the peripheral normalization at this boundary. It does not identify the rest of a geometric density with the original quantum period. ## 4. Physical inverse-pair atoms and the first-order correction Let mu_M=[[M,1],[0,M inverse]] and u_h=(M^h-M^(-h))/kappa, a_h=(F inverse mu_M^h F)_11=M^h+s*u_h, b_h=(F inverse U*mu_M^h F)_11. The power identity gives (mu_M^h)'_21=s*u_h in the framed chart. Since U'_12=-p*(k-M inverse), we get the exact formula b_h=k*[M^h+(1-p)*s*u_h]+p*M^(-1)*s*u_h. (6) For the negative move carrying U left across the next reference meridian, the actual physical dictionary A_j=M*ell_previous/ell_next gives A=M*a_h/a_(h+1), B=M*a_(h+1)/b_(h+1), C=a_(h+1)*b_h/[b_(h+1)*a_h], AC=M*b_h/b_(h+1). (7) This is the generic-M extension of the complete formulas; the factors M in A,B and AC are forced by the signed Gauss/position dictionary. At the boundary M=1+epsilon*a/2+O(epsilon squared) and u_h=h+O(epsilon squared). Equation (2) has common leading coefficient `-c/[zeta*(s*zeta+a)]` at order epsilon minus two. From (6), b_h/b_(h+1)=1-epsilon*(s*zeta+a/2)+O(epsilon^2), AC=1-epsilon*s*zeta+O(epsilon^2). (8) The physical atom therefore has no additional a/2 term. Keeping only the raw prefix ratio would introduce a false half-shift into a proposed product or Gamma-profile normalization. No such quantum profile is established in this note. At completeness the five negative coefficient atoms A,C,1/B,AC,C/B have valuations (0,0,-2,0,-2). The same valuations hold on this generic blowup chart when their leading coefficients are units. The atom AC approaches one at order epsilon. Consequently the ordinary fixed-atom Gaussian expansion is not uniform here, even though the inverse-pair principal normal line below is regular. ## 5. The paired principal normal ratio extends The squared PRINCIPAL variable amplitudes from the actual balanced coefficients, with Y=M squared and all fixed phases retained separately, are a_-^2=C/(AB)*(1-AC)*(1-Y/B) /[(1-A)*(1-C)*(1-YC/B)], a_+^2=AB*(1-BC)*(1-Y/A) /[(1-B)*(1-C)*(1-YC/A)]. The inverse move uses (A',B',C')=(B/C,AC,1/C). Direct cancellation, valid before putting Y=1, proves a_-^2(A,B,C)*a_+^2(A',B',C')=-C^2/(1-C)^2. (9) The mixed Hessians are V_-=C/(1-C) and V_+(1/C)=-V_-. The added normal Hessian has determinant -V_- squared. Thus its squared principal amplitude divided by that determinant is EXACTLY one. On the unit chart C tends to A(0) inverse and V_- tends to 1/[A(0)-1], a unit. The inverse-pair PRINCIPAL normal line extends through this blowup after pairing. This does not say that the individual amplitudes, all higher coefficients, the open source, or the full quantum normal lattice extend in this Gaussian frame. Equation (8) explicitly shows an atom colliding with one. An all-order completed source transform would have to control that collision with its actual word data. ## 6. Critical-path implication and exact checks The actual full dimension supplies the precise first peripheral pole cancellation; no extra numerical normalization is available to choose here. The inverse-pair principal determinant also causes no additional unknown scalar. What remains is a source-compatible linear/irregular geometric period map at the resonance, proving that the original selected class has a nonzero geometric image, with subexponential coefficient and a sharp global norm estimate. The displayed cancellations do not prove those three assertions. [The symbolic audit](../experiments/audit_resonant_boundary_blowup.py) checks the raw conjugation, the whole dimension/form identity, the physical-versus-raw first-order correction, the generic inverse principal-amplitude identity, and the dimension polynomial through level twelve. Its [saved output](../experiments/resonant_boundary_blowup_results.json) is a verification of these identities, not evidence of a volume limit or a finite-source/geometric identification.

title: Rivin optimization, a regularized angle flow, and the quantum source
text: # Rivin optimization, a regularized angle flow, and the quantum source Research note, 26 October 2026, following the user's suggestion to use Rivin's geometrization and flow viewpoint. The classical geometric problem has a precise convex formulation. We give an exact constrained flow and prove global convergence when the triangulation is complete and positive geometric. We then identify the additional lift needed for the actual quantum period, retaining a newly computed paired source-normalization identity. The volume conjecture is not proved. This is not a replacement positive quantum state or a claim that real convexity determines the original finite period. Current source frontier (27 October): [exact complete Fourier localization](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) places the original period entirely at the resonant row; regular finite Fourier rows vanish exactly. The [all-strand Euler/Cauchy theorem](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md) now expresses that original period as a specified finite coefficient or endpoint divided difference, with the whole word retained. Its [physical-clock equation](actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.md) has a nilpotent apparent denominator. The [full peripheral boundary calculation](resonant_boundary_blowup_and_actual_peripheral_line.md) proves the required first pole cancellation and corrects a raw-prefix half-shift. These provide exact inputs for the geometric comparison; Rivin uniqueness still does not prove its selected nonzero image or the sharp norm. The [critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md) keeps those three final gates open. ## 1. Existing scope and the correct optimization problem [Rivin, Combinatorial optimization in geometry](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9907032) explicitly develops linear programming and network-flow methods; the [journal abstract](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0196-8858(03)00093-9) states that scope. The triangulated Casson--Rivin formulation is stated in [Futer--Gueritaud, 1004.0440](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440): linear angle equations define a convex polytope, and an interior critical point of volume gives the complete hyperbolic metric. [Luo--Yang, 1404.5365](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.5365) uses the Fenchel dual of volume for decorated ideal metrics and curvature. For coverage of extended convergent flows on cusped triangulations, see the abstract of [Feng--Ge--Hua, 2009.05842](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05842). No published flow or rigidity proof is used as a premise below. For t tetrahedra let theta_(j,0),theta_(j,1),theta_(j,2)>0 be the angles on the three opposite edge pairs. Write C for the edge-incidence matrix: a column counts the two local edges in that pair, including multiplicity if their global edges coincide. The exact angle domain is A={theta>0: sum_(a=0)^2 theta_(j,a)=pi, C theta=2pi*1}. (1.1) Volume is strictly concave on A. The convex objective is its negative, rather than volume itself. An ideal triangulation alone does not guarantee an interior critical point. The positive complete triangulation from [the audited geometric input](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md) does supply one; this is where that input is decisive. ## 2. An exact flow-network representation Use a bipartite incidence graph with one node for each tetrahedron, one node for each global edge, and one arc for each of the six local edge occurrences, directed from its tetrahedron to its global edge. Give the arc the corresponding dihedral angle. Every tetrahedron has total outgoing flux 2pi; every global edge has total incoming flux 2pi. Impose equality of the two arcs belonging to each local opposite edge pair. These flow constraints are exactly (1.1), in both directions. This graph is derived from the dual cell complex: tetrahedra are dual vertices and global edges are dual faces. The opposite-pair equalities are additional local constraints. Deleting them would give a different transportation problem. Likewise the bare dual one-skeleton does not by itself record which original edges are encircled or the peripheral holonomies. Let A_0 be the full integer matrix of (1.1), and let B have columns forming a real basis of ker A_0. This description requires no invertible face-matrix chart. For quantum lattice applications one must retain the integral kernel and its peripheral marking as well; a real change of coordinates is not an integral saturation theorem. ## 3. Strict concavity and the geometric maximizer Set Lambda'(a)=-log(2sin a), Lambda(0)=0, and V(theta)=sum_j [Lambda(theta_j0)+Lambda(theta_j1) +Lambda(theta_j2)]. For alpha+beta+gamma=pi the negative Hessian in alpha,beta is [[cot alpha+cot gamma, cot gamma], [cot gamma, cot beta+cot gamma]]. (3.1) Its determinant is one and its first diagonal entry is sin beta/(sin alpha sin gamma)>0. Thus it is positive definite. This proves strict concavity on every affine angle domain. The existing [positive-factorial note](quantum_a_volume.md) already gives the independent stationary-point argument. Choose compatible cusp horospheres in a complete geometric triangulation. The truncated length of each global edge agrees across its incident tetrahedra. Summing the ideal Schlaefli identity gives dV=-(1/2)sum_e length_e d(total angle_e)=0 on the angle domain; changes of decorations cancel at ideal vertices. Hence its geometric angle point theta_* is stationary. Strict concavity makes it the unique global maximizer, with V(theta_*)=Vol(M). (3.2) This argument proves the direction needed here from the supplied geometric point. It does not assume that an arbitrary nonempty angle polytope has an interior maximizer. ### The same optimization generates the marked A-curve This also gives a precise connection to the requested torsor formulation. Use logarithmic shape coordinates x=(u_j,v_j), with u_j=Log z_j, v_j=Log z_j'', and their already audited symplectic form Omega. Let E be the isotropic space of independent edge Hamiltonians. Tangential angle structures are E^perp. The marked peripheral functions identify E^perp/E with a two-dimensional symplectic space, with Omega_red=-(1/2)dU wedge dV, U=Log m, V=Log l, m=M^2, l=L_intr^2. All peripheral logs are centered at the chosen complete lift; its longitude character remains recorded separately. At a positive shape, the sine rule gives dV_volume(delta theta)=Omega(Re x,delta theta). (3.3) For example, in one tetrahedron with alpha=Im u, gamma=Im v, beta=pi-alpha-gamma, Re u=log(sin beta/sin gamma) and Re v=log(sin alpha/sin beta). Differentiating its Lobachevsky volume gives exactly Re u dgamma-Re v dalpha. Prescribe the two real boundary angles a=Im U,b=Im V, and maximize volume on that affine slice of A. Its tangent space is E: fixing both peripheral angles removes the entire quotient E^perp/E. By (3.3), an interior critical point is equivalent to Re x in E^perp, which is precisely the real part of the edge gluing equations. Their imaginary part was imposed already. Thus the constrained maximizer solves the full complex gluing. Without fixing a,b, stationarity requires Re x in E, which also makes Re U=Re V=0 and gives completeness at a=b=0. Near the complete geometric point define the value function V_boundary(a,b)=max_(theta in A, Im U=a,Im V=b) V(theta). The positive geometric gluing branch exists there by the earlier rigidity proof. Its map to (a,b) is locally invertible because Im(dV/dU)>0. Hence these maxima are interior, unique and smooth. Reduction of (3.3) gives their exact differential dV_boundary=(1/2)(Re V da-Re U db), Re U=-2 partial_b V_boundary, Re V= 2 partial_a V_boundary. (3.4) Consequently the marked geometric A-curve is locally the Legendre graph of this boundary volume function. This identifies the same regulator differential already used in the Heisenberg period space. It is a statement about the classical geometric branch, not a quantum-A symbol or selected-period theorem. For clarity its boundary Hessian can be computed explicitly. If tau=dV/dU=p+i q_c at the complete point, q_c>0, then Hess V_boundary=-(1/(2q_c)) [[|tau|^2,-p],[-p,1]], det(Hess V_boundary)=1/4. (3.5) Indeed Re U=(b-p a)/q_c and Re V=(p b-|tau|^2 a)/q_c to first order; insert them in (3.4). The negative Hessian is positive definite. The same constrained flow below applies to each nearby fixed-(a,b) slice, giving a variational construction of this marked A-curve germ. There is an intrinsic boundary formulation. The calculation of (3.5) is pointwise on the positive gluing branch, with its varying tau=dV/dU and Im tau>0. Hence the convex potential Phi(a,b)=-2 V_boundary(a,b) satisfies the real Monge--Ampere equation det(Hess Phi)=1, U=partial_b Phi+i a, V=-partial_a Phi+i b. (3.6) Conversely a smooth strictly convex Phi with this determinant gives a positive complex curve by the last two formulas. Indeed dU wedge dV=(det(Hess Phi)-1)da wedge db=0, and Phi_bb>0 makes U a local real coordinate pair. Therefore V is holomorphic in U, with dV/dU=-Phi_ab/Phi_bb+i/Phi_bb. This is a direct local equivalence of the convex boundary potential and the positive marked complex A-curve germ. The fundamental-class mark still fixes its volume constant and the regulator's central period. The Monge--Ampere equation alone does not specify that mark, a particular A-curve, or a quantum period. It makes the geometric target independent of a chosen tetrahedral coordinate chart. ## 4. A regularized flow with the exact same objective Use h(theta)=-sum_i log theta_i as a metric potential. In coordinates theta=theta_0+B y define the constrained flow by dot(theta)=B [B^T diag(theta_i^(-2)) B]^(-1) B^T grad V(theta). (4.1) The matrix is positive definite whenever B has independent columns and theta>0. All angle equations are preserved because A_0 B=0. Moreover dV/dt=(B^T grad V)^T [B^T diag(theta_i^(-2))B]^(-1)(B^T grad V)>=0. (4.2) The barrier changes the metric, not the objective or its critical point. There is no regularization parameter to send to zero. Here is a global convergence proof, given theta_*>0 from Section 3. Use the Bregman function with its arguments in the following order: D(theta_*,theta)=sum_i [theta_*i/theta_i-1 -log(theta_*i/theta_i)]. (4.3) Differentiating (4.3) and using theta_*-theta in im B gives dot D=-(theta_*-theta)^T grad V(theta) <=-[V(theta_*)-V(theta)]. (4.4) The inequality is the tangent inequality for a concave function. Thus D is nonincreasing. It tends to infinity if any theta_i tends to zero, because every theta_*i is positive. The angle closure is compact, so the solution stays in a compact subset of A. The smooth vector field therefore exists for all time. On a compact positive region containing this trajectory and its segments to theta_*, the restricted negative Hessian of V has a positive lower bound mu. Choose B orthonormal for this estimate. If theta_i>=delta there, the inverse metric in (4.2) is bounded below by delta^2. The strong-concavity inequality gives ||B^T grad V||^2>=2mu [V(theta_*)-V(theta)], d/dt[V(theta_*)-V(theta)] <=-2mu delta^2[V(theta_*)-V(theta)]. (4.5) Consequently the volume gap decays exponentially and theta(t) converges to theta_*. Neither theorem has yet identified the selected global framing cycle or its polar continuation. In relating geometric matrices to physical edge momenta, the actual developed-prefix conjugation remains necessary. ## 34. The whole quantum object retains its cyclotomic and period divisors The [actual atom theorem](unfolded_atom_cyclotomic_divisors_and_two_nome_source.md) now proves an exact source extension before taking quantum jets. For the original unfolded Ward factorial F(Q,z)=1/(z;Q)_infinity retain U independently and put R=F(Q,zU)/F(Q,z). At a fixed n-th root, Q=zeta_n exp(epsilon), the marked normal slope U=exp(t n epsilon) has the whole sectorial exceptional period R -> (1-z^n)^t. At the ACTUAL slope t=1 the exact finite Ward iteration already gives (z;Q)_n, whose root value is 1-z^n. First setting U=1 generically gives one and erases this source. Rational t gives the specified Kummer norm by an exact telescope, with all branch marks retained. This is fixed-level specialization, not a growing-level asymptotic interchange. The same proof constructs two-nome difference transports with multipliers 1-z and 1-y. Their exact root formula retains the actual norm-one cyclic source, its determinant half-power, and the continuous Heisenberg period. Both the original atom and this completion have accumulating singular data at the physical parameter origin, explicitly ruling out automatic meromorphic differential-line descent for these local objects. The [finite polar-character theorem](whole_selected_line_polar_character.md) remains sufficient if a WHOLE selected meromorphic line is separately constructed. Its pole primitive would give the volume rate directly. It is not a consequence of the local atoms; the actual program keeps their difference transports and cyclotomic/source divisors. Proving the corresponding global original-source descent and regulator norm remains necessary. The [whole finite transport realization](whole_two_period_transport_and_actual_coefficients.md) now places every actual crossing coefficient in this two-period object without replacing the knot state. Its first-period ratios are exactly the finite Pochhammer products, so the extra completion cancels. Finite contractions, every original cap/pivot/phase and all normal derivatives are preserved. The full peripheral factor is kept separately: its denominator 1-M^(2N) and the transport norm (M^2;Q)_N agree at a root but require the specified whole adapter before differentiation. Their logarithmic Q-normal difference is already -1/2 at N=2,M=1. The original power graph is not equated with the invariant dual-nome coordinate off the root. ## 35. The actual framing cover and cap have explicit whole source data The [prefix-adapted framing theorem](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md) uses signed developed prefixes U,V, not a substituted local meridian. On the rank-one projector quadric the physical second clock is k=ell_U/ell_V. Together with the original cut clock it gives a cover of degree at most two, independently of braid length. The complete framing form is Omega=ell_V/(B D) dlog A wedge dlog B. Its field trace is generally nonzero. The exact reciprocal momentum deck still holds at completeness, and an actual prefix clock with its full q/M adapter realizes the normalized orientation insertion. More strongly the [identity-cap theorem](identity_cut_orientation_cover_and_marked_source.md) preserves the original source by a whole rational-form identity. For eta the actual second-port band variable, u=eta+eta^(-1), v=eta-eta^(-1), the source form is exactly F(eta)deta/(N eta) = [v F(eta)]du/[N(u^2-4)]. The original mark is eta=0 over u=infinity. The full finite tail, its endpoint correction and whole clock connection are explicit; no new odd-state source has been chosen. The principal geometric measure agrees, after the actual prefix adapter and a rational Jacobian, with dlog A wedge deta/eta. The same principal boundary calculation is a useful GEOMETRIC test: the independent geometric coordinate eta_geo=p_e^(-1) has a boundary at B=1 where the bare framing density has zero logarithmic residue on a regular chart. This is not an image of the original Fourier-band cap eta_F=0. A principal incidence or an equality of rational forms alone did not transport that source. The finite band/clock theorem and the actual polarization below retain the two variables independently and repair that distinction. The [finite framing-density source theorem](cyclic_framing_density_source.md) also computes its root filter exactly as gamma N lambda^(N-1)/(1-lambda^N)^2. Both lambda and gamma are intrinsic trace-word functions on the marked character/A-cover. The retained cyclic norm is 1-lambda^N. This exact source can have an exponential character even though the starting density is rational. Its identification with the actual Gaussian/source pairing is not assumed. ## 36. The first correction is absolutely exact but retains relative data The [first actual Gaussian correction](figure_eight_first_loop_cap_residue.md) now gives a characteristic-zero test on the figure-eight coefficient model with the literal two external positions (a_0,a_2). It retains the actual three-dimensional transverse complement, every closed pivot, color half-step and all twenty compact atoms. On the stated s=1 framing slice the complete coefficient z_1 is regular at BOTH candidate geometric boundary points. Each of its six Wick contributions separately has a double pole; all such poles cancel in the sum. All finite poles of z_1 occur at the two ramification points of the actual two-position projection, with order four and zero simple residue. An explicit rational Hermite primitive G satisfies G'=z_1 as an identity in the Riley function field. The pole at infinity and the full base-only line are separately retained. Absolute exactness does not determine the marked relative period. The two cap-point difference and the classical centralizer-step difference of G are both nonzero. Their normalized difference is unchanged by any base-only first-order unit and equals (295t-138)/112 for t^2-t+1=0. Thus a source-preserving quantum framing change has to carry the endpoint values of its primitive; it cannot erase them by declaring an exact form irrelevant. This is an exact prototype calculation guiding the general source theory. Its geometric momentum coordinate is not the independent finite band variable, and the residue calculation is not a pushforward of the original cap. No all-s or all-order conclusion is inferred. ## 37. Actual Fourier polarization reduces the remaining source to one index The [whole Fourier polarization](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md) now makes an actual change of basis on the second identity wire. Its Vandermonde inverse is retained before taking normal jets, with the exact forced connection, both endpoint carries and every original phase/peripheral factor. The first source keeps its full output row. Its raw partial array is Jtilde_(a,j)=sum_c T^V_(c,j;a,j), original period=(1/N)sum_(a,j)Jtilde_(a,j). At a root the inverse Fourier contributes 1/N inside Jtilde. Old physical b and its output offset are now summed internally; j is a genuine new external source coordinate. A double diagonal at the first cut would have removed that coordinate and is not the chosen source. The finite Fourier/alias theorem preserves all independent power characters on unwrapped current tails. The [geometric Fourier theorem](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md) uses the original macroscopic open phase S_open+vt, not an unbounded extrapolation of bounded-band jets. The mixed Hessian along the old framing tangent is dLog p_e, so the enlarged transverse block is nondegenerate on the new chart. Complete discrete-faithful holonomy makes (A,p_e) birational on that framing torsor; generic old projection caustics disappear. The marked regulator action is unchanged. The [extended partial-support proof](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) applies finite proper-coefficient linear algebra and least-moment repair to this SAME actual root partial family. Its constructed operator has a geometric A-factor before the final source sum. The auxiliary proper root lift and whole inverse Fourier normal germs are explicitly distinguished. Finally the [fixed-column source theorem](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) uses actual scalar root closure to remove the a average exactly: original period=sum_j Jtilde_(a_N,j). A generic rational phase gives a good interior sequence a_N and a nonzero phase-specialized partial operator on each marked residue class of levels. The actual whole Ward defect of this source change has a polynomially bounded primitive and is kept before differentiation; root equality is not falsely promoted to equality of all quantum-normal jets. The last selected source problem now has ONE exterior Fourier index. Its geometric survival and regulator norm still have to be proved. ## 38. A whole rigid source frame, a Möbius fiber, and an actual cancellation test There is now a literal algebraic answer for the finite boundary frame before jets. For the actual clock B and cyclic repair P, with Z=Q^N and e=e_0 e_0^t, BPB inverse P inverse=Q[I+(Z inverse-1)e], original source matrix=e sum_(r=0)^(N-1)P^r. The [rank-one moment/source proof](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md) keeps its divided wall projector, the original orbit co-source and both actual endpoint deletions. The [aligned cyclic frame theorem](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md) classifies this whole source-cyclic chart directly: its endpoint-corrected function/shift algebra is Mat_N. Its unmarked frame ambiguity is a line bundle, removed by a vector marking. The defect must be aligned with the actual source; rank one and flatness alone do not impose that alignment. The scalar of a closed actual word is separate from the rigid frame. The geometric fiber also has a simpler global function. Factor U-V=u(a,b) and put (c,d)=(a,b)V inverse. With the original prefix sign sigma, the ACTUAL momentum is p=sigma[c(1-r)-ds]/[ar+bs]. The [Möbius theorem](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) gives its inverse and identifies r=infinity with the intrinsic pole lambda=-sigma c/a, independent of the cut s. The whole principal density retains the norm 1-lambda^N. For the figure-eight prefix this pole has order six, and principal sampling is singular when six divides N even though the actual finite tensor is regular. The independent wall divisors 1-Q^N and 1-lambda^N therefore cannot be equated or canceled without their actual word/source map. Finally, the [actual zero-source Fourier current](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) is not an abstract countermodel. For the original two-cut tensor, W=[(I tensor B)T(I tensor B inverse)-T]/(Q-1) has zero second partial trace WHOLE, preserves its index support, and at a root has raw partial array J_W,j=[J_(j+1)-J_j]/(Q_N-1). Its formal geometric block on the good-A chart is nonzero, with the same regulator action: the leading amplitude is the derivative of the actual Fourier amplitude. Nevertheless its final source sum is exactly zero. The cyclic difference D has a centered inverse of norm at most one on the zero-source subspace, and abs(sum_j J_j)=sqrt(N) dist(J,im D).
