(2.2) The second equality follows from U=(C_N(X)+delta)/2, U^(-1)=(C_N(X)-delta)/2 and delta^2=C_N(X)^2-4. Thus A[X]=R+delta R. For the conductor, write S_(N-1)(X) for the monic second-kind Chebyshev polynomial satisfying Y^N-Y^(-N)=(Y-Y^(-1))S_(N-1)(X). Then delta(1+Y)/(1-Y)=-(X+2)S_(N-1)(X) in R. Equation (2.1) now gives delta B subset L. Since U is a unit, delta B=(U^2-1)B. This proves both claimed statements: (U^2-1)B subset L, L={f in B:Jf-f in (U^2-1)B}. (2.3) No reduced-fiber dimension count or root interpolation is required. ## 3. The cut uses the physical derivative, not a fixed-U derivative For f=(1-Y)g in L define ell(f)=g|_(Y=1,U=1) =-[d/dY f(Y,U=Y^N)]_(Y=1). (3.1) This is intrinsic in B=k[Y,Y^(-1)]. In ambient A[Y] notation, the Euler derivation which descends to B is D_phys=Y partial_Y+N U partial_U, D_phys(Y^N-U)=N(Y^N-U). (3.2) Therefore ell=-D_phys evaluated at (Y,U)=(1,1). This proves representation independence and gives exactly ell(v_n)=P_n(2)=T_n(1). (3.3) For a in A, ell(af)=a(1)ell(f), since f vanishes at the physical point Y=1. Hence ell kills (U-1)L and induces a cut on L/(U-1)L. By contrast partial_Y with U held fixed does not descend to B: it sends the zero relation Y^N-U to NY^(N-1). Even differentiating a preferred A-basis representative with U held fixed gives a different functional. For example f=U^2-1 lies in L by (2.3), is zero in B/(U-1)B, and has ell(f)=-2N, whereas its canonical fixed-U derivative is zero. This does not contradict ell((U-1)L)=0: U+1 does not lie in L. ## 4. A weighted-J-fixed class invisible in the ambient fiber There is a sharper example using a single Newton generator. Put d=floor(N/2). At all roots Y^N=1, the prefactor 1-Y kills Y=1, and the P_d factors kill all other inverse pairs. Thus v_d maps to zero in B/(U-1)B. In fact the exact identities are N=2d+1: v_d=-Y^(-d)(U-1), N=2d: v_d=-Y^(-d)(Y+1)(U-1). (4.1) They follow by multiplying X-Q^r-Q^(-r)=Y^(-1)(Y-Q^r)(Y-Q^(-r)); in the even case the root -1 occurs twice in the paired product. Each v_d is globally weighted-J-fixed by construction, yet ell(v_d)=N if N is odd, ell(v_d)=2N if N is even. (4.2) For the principal complex root, this is also P_d(2)=product_(r=1)^d 4 sin^2(pi*r/N)>0. Thus even the weighted-fixed condition does not justify passing to the image of L in the ambient complete fiber. The source lives on L/(U-1)L and detects classes in the kernel of L/(U-1)L -> B/(U-1)B. This is genuine normal lattice data. The cut theorem is correct with the physical derivative and the retained lattice; replacing either by fixed-U differentiation or ambient-fiber evaluation would lose its nonzero source.

title: The actual source lattice, companion monodromy, and its normal cut
text: # The actual source lattice, companion monodromy, and its normal cut Research construction, 27 October 2026. This gives explicit maps from an actual scalar quantum equation and its pointed source to the root monodromy kernel, cokernel and first normal equation. It also identifies the distinguished cut as a normal lattice functional, rather than assuming it is a cyclic invariant line. No geometric-component or regulator comparison is asserted. ## 1. The scalar source complex maps exactly to companion monodromy Fix a primitive N-th root zeta, N>=2. Write E=k(Y), F=k(U), U=Y^N, sigma f(Y)=f(zeta Y). Start with a specified actual scalar operator P(Q)=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Y) sigma_Q^j, sigma_Q f(Y)=f(QY), regular at Q=zeta, with d>=1 and a_0 and a_d nonzero there. Laurent shift operators can first be put in this form by a fixed shift. These choices retain the actual source; they are not minimal-operator assumptions. All maps below are initially over E and F, so no regularity at U=1 is being silently imposed. Let A be the solution companion matrix, so its first d-1 rows shift coordinates and its last row is -(a_0,...,a_(d-1))/a_d. Put J(Q)f=(f,sigma_Q f,...,sigma_Q^(d-1)f)^t, T(Q)=A(Q,Y)^(-1) sigma_Q, r(Q)=A(Q,Y)^(-1)e_d/a_d(Q,Y), S_N(Q)=I+T(Q)+...+T(Q)^(N-1), M(Q)=T(Q)^N-I. The following are exact identities of operators before specializing Q: (T-I)J=rP, M J=S_N r P. (1.1) Indeed sigma_Q J-AJ has only its last entry nonzero, equal to Pf/a_d. The second identity is the geometric-series factorization. Thus the actual scalar two-term complex maps to the monodromy complex by J in degree zero and S_N r in degree one. The actual source is transported by the displayed operator, including every coefficient and shift. At the root write T_0,M_0,J_0,r_0,S_0 for these operators. They are F-linear on E or E^d. Set K=ker_E M_0, C=coker_E M_0, pi:E^d -> C. The operator T_0 acts on K and C, with N-th power identity. There are canonical F-linear isomorphisms J_0:ker_F P_0 -> K^(T_0), (1.2) kappa:coker_F P_0 -> C^(T_0), kappa([h])=pi(S_0 r_0 h)/N. (1.3) Here scalar kernels and cokernels are taken for P_0:E->E as an F-linear operator. Equation (1.2) is the usual exact companion reconstruction, with no loss of the scalar section. For (1.3), first (T_0-I)J_0=r_0P_0 shows that r_0 induces an isomorphism coker P_0 -> coker_F(T_0-I). To prove surjectivity, use the first d-1 rows of sigma-A to eliminate the first d-1 coordinates of any inhomogeneous equation; the remaining coordinate is e_d h/a_d. If e_d h/a_d=(sigma-A)v, those same rows force v=J_0 f, hence h=P_0 f. Multiplication by A^(-1) gives precisely r_0. For an arbitrary F-linear T_0 the remaining map is E^d/(T_0-I)E^d -> C^(T_0), [v] |-> pi(S_0v)/N. It is onto by averaging a lift of an invariant class. It is injective because S_0=N+(T_0-I)R(T_0) for a polynomial R: if S_0v=M_0w, then v=(T_0-I)(S_0w-R(T_0)v)/N. This proves the claimed source-cokernel identification, including its normalizing factor N. It requires no semisimplicity of M_0. ## 2. The first normal map commutes with this source identification Put Q=zeta(1+epsilon). For every Q-dependent operator write subscripts 0,1 for its constant and first epsilon coefficients. In particular P_1=sum_j (a_(j,1) sigma^j+j a_(j,0) sigma^j D), D=Y partial_Y. In ambient A[Y] notation the same physical derivation is D=Y partial_Y+N U partial_U; (2.1) it preserves Y^N-U. A derivative at fixed U cannot replace it. Differentiate (1.1), restrict to f in ker P_0, and project to C. The terms M_0 J_1 f and (S_Nr)_1P_0f disappear. Hence pi(M_1 J_0 f)=pi(S_0r_0P_1f). (2.2) Consequently the canonical first quantum-normal operator of [the monodromy construction](first_quantum_normal_connection.md) obeys D_N(J_0 f)=kappa([P_1 f])/N. (2.3) This is an exact scalar-to-companion normal-source map. In particular, if the supplied whole Q-germ has P(Q)f(Q)=epsilon h_1+O(epsilon^2), then [P_1f_0]=[h_1] in coker P_0 and D_N(J_0f_0)=kappa([h_1])/N, s=S_0r_0h_1. (2.4) The actual off-root section is not assumed P-horizontal. Its first coefficient f_1 is retained in P_0f_1+P_1f_0=h_1. The source class is independent of changing f_1; the selected section and cut are not replaced by this class alone. For example the central derivative of the actual finite-sum lift constructs h_1 in the cited first-normal note. Equations (2.3)--(2.4) transport that actual source, rather than positing an abstract one. There is also a useful scalar form of the connection symbol. Put W_P=sum_j j a_(j,0)sigma^j. For f in ker P_0, kappa([W_P f])=iota(J_0 f), (2.5) where iota:K->C is inclusion followed by quotient. To see this, apply (2.3) to g(U)f and subtract g times the equation for f. Since [P_1,g]=N U g'(U) W_P, comparison with the monodromy Leibniz rule gives (2.5), for instance by taking g=U. Thus the correct scalar symbol is the shift derivative W_P and not an assumed invertible scalar. Jordan degeneracies remain visible in iota. ## 3. Keeping the actual source lattice and the companion cut At the root put A_0=k[U,U^(-1)], B=k[Y,Y^(-1)] and use the lattice L=(1-Y)A_0[X], X=Y+Y^(-1), (U^2-1)B subset L subset B, from [whole-source Newton transport](whole_source_newton_transport.md). Actual reciprocity gives f_N=(1-Y)F_N in L, and an actual invariant annihilator acts on L by the banded matrices proved there. The map J_0 embeds L into the companion space by its literal shifted coordinates. It need not embed it into a preselected regular power lattice if a companion denominator vanishes at the cut. Keep the fractional lattice J_0(L) and the source image S_0r_0(L), or retain the undivided scalar complex. In particular, localization by a_d followed by evaluation at U=1 is not an integral comparison theorem. The original cut transfers without ambiguity to J_0(L): cut_comp(J_0f)=-[D(pr_0 J_0f)]_(Y=1) =cut(f), (3.1) because the first component of J_0f is exactly f. The derivative is the physical one (2.1). This is a normal co-source, not evaluation of the first component in the ambient reduced fiber. More intrinsically, localize A_0 at w=U-1. Then wB subset L, and the cut is a well-defined functional on the thickened module B/wL, ell_B([b])=-[Db]_(Y=1). (3.2) It kills wL because every element of L vanishes at Y=1. The source fiber L/wL injects into B/wL and (3.2) restricts to its actual cut. This retains precisely the extra normal classes lost by B/wB. The same construction in the first companion coordinate transports this normal co-source through (1.1); no inverse of a vanishing peripheral factor is used to define it. There is a canonical Bockstein description. If f in L has zero ambient fiber, write f=wb. The map ker(L/wL -> B/wB) -> (B/wB)/im(L/wL), [f] |-> [b] (3.3) is an isomorphism. Changing f by wL changes b by L. Surjectivity uses wB subset L. On this kernel the marked cut is cut(f)=-N b(1). (3.4) This is a normal-lattice source map, not an unproved invariant line in the actual monodromy kernel. ## 4. The distinguished X=2 normal sector On L/wL the characteristic and minimal polynomials of X are C_N(x)-2, where C_N(Y+Y^(-1))=Y^N+Y^(-N). The root x=2 is simple since C_N'(2)=N^2. Thus e_2(X)=(C_N(X)-2)/(N^2(X-2)) (4.1) is a canonical rank-one projector on this abstract fiber. The right side is a polynomial. The cut satisfies ell X=2ell and ell(v_0)=1, so ell e_2=ell and identifies this line with k. Its literal generator before specialization is e_2(X)v_0 =-Y(U-1)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)Y^j/(N^2 U). (4.2) It has zero ambient fiber. Its divided-normal value at Y=1 is -1/N, so (3.4) gives cut=1. The selected sector therefore sits in the normal defect, and disappears if L/wL is replaced by its ambient image. Over the completed central ring k[[w]], the marked branch Y=1 determines a canonical etale idempotent e_0 in Bhat. It satisfies e_0 Lhat=w e_0 Bhat. (4.3) Indeed every source vanishes on this branch at w=0, and wBhat is contained in Lhat. Thus this is a rank-one direct summand of the completed source lattice; its fiber is the line (4.1). The physical connection D/N preserves etale idempotents. On this summand its logarithmic residue is +1, and dividing by w identifies it with the regular trivial branch line. The cut is -N times the constant coefficient in this divided-normal trivialization. This supplies an exact local normal sector. It does not imply that an actual annihilator, companion connection, or crossing transport preserves it. Nor does it automatically extend to a rational line over the whole central U-curve: the generic algebra B tensor F is the field F(Y), Y^N=U, and has no nontrivial idempotents. The branch projector becomes algebraic after the marked Kummer splitting cover and exists canonically in the completion at U=1; cyclic deck shifts permute those generic branches. Descent of one chosen branch is additional data, rather than a consequence of its simple special eigenvalue. Already at N=3, writing zeta^2+zeta+1=0, ell(v_0)=1, ell(v_1)=3, S v_0=-zeta^2 v_0, S v_1=2zeta^2 v_1. Therefore ell S is not a scalar multiple of ell. The cut is not even a common quotient character of the full banded algebra. Transport over the actual A-curve still requires a proved map of the actual scalar/source complexes, not just this boundary projector. ## 5. The exact cyclic envelope has a parity defect Let L_cyc=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) sigma^j L inside B. This is stable under sigma. The exact result is N even: L_cyc=B, N odd: L_cyc=sum_(j != j_0) A_0 Y^j direct_sum (U-1)A_0Y^(j_0), j_0=(N+1)/2. (5.1) Thus cyclic saturation is not always the ordinary power lattice. For the proof use the Fourier projectors E_j=(1/N)sum_l zeta^(-jl)sigma^l. Each character coefficient ideal is generated by the coefficients of the v_n. For 1<=j<=floor(N/2), the highest term -Y^j of v_(j-1) has no other exponent congruent to j modulo N. It gives the unit generator. For j>(N+1)/2 the lowest term Y^(j-N) of v_(N-j) does the same. The constant character is present in v_0. These exhaust the even case and all but j_0 in the odd case. For N=2m+1 the highest and lowest terms of v_m are the only terms with residue j_0=m+1; their coefficient is U^(-1)-1. Conversely the congruence Jf=f modulo U^2-1 implies that the j_0 coefficient of every f in L vanishes at U=1: the weighted reflection acts by -1 on this character there. All its coefficients are therefore divisible by U-1. This proves (5.1). Neither enlargement makes the cut descend to an ordinary ambient fiber: the row (3.2) still retains the normal direction. Bare sigma does not preserve L, and the parity defect is an additional reason to avoid assuming a cyclic invariant cut line. ## 6. What the construction reduces, and what remains The actual scalar equation, its first-normal source and its cut now have explicit maps to companion monodromy, with the exact cyclic normalization (1.3), (2.3), and the normal co-source (3.1)--(3.4). Thus an actual-to-geometric comparison may be checked directly on these pointed two-term complexes. It is not necessary to guess a global quantum connection or discard the source in order to make that comparison. The remaining issue is substantive: construct a geometric complex and a map matching the actual scalar source class and this marked normal row, including its integral lattice at U=1. No general invariance of the X=2 sector, regulator identity, or selected norm formula follows from boundary algebra alone. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap.py). [Results](../experiments/source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap_results.json).

title: A source-preserving quadrature with an exponentially smaller error
text: # A source-preserving quadrature with an exponentially smaller error 28 October 2026. This proves a discrete-to-continuous comparison, including the selected finite endpoints. It is a theorem for the displayed finite factorial sum. The [finite whole-source transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) now proves that this is the original 5_2 invariant, including the whole fixed-root meridian family. That identification is an exact finite calculation, rather than an inference from finite checks. The comparison removes the inner summation without choosing a saddle or discarding a Fourier mode. Its TOTAL error is bounded by a logarithmic factor times the already proved original figure-eight invariant. This is useful because that error has a strictly smaller exponential rate than the proposed 5_2 geometric contribution. The outer sum and the nonzero geometric contribution of the remaining integral are not proved by this result. ## 1. Reflection gives an entire interpolant Write Q=exp(2 pi i/N), F_n=(Q;Q)_n, 0<=n<N, and m=N-1-n. Consider a_(n,j)=Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/(F_j F_(n-j)), 0<=j<=n. Let Fhat be the exactly normalized interpolation in [the factorial theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). The entire interpolation selected here is f_(N,n)(z)=Q^[-n(n+2)-z(n+1)] F_n^3/[Fhat(z) Fhat(n-z)] * exp(2 pi i z). (1) Initially this is defined on the overlapping factorial strips. Reflection and the integer shift m give the exact entire continuation f_(N,n)(z)=f_(N,n)(0) H_(N,n)(z)/F_m, H_(N,n)(z)=exp[-i pi z(z-N+1)/N] (Q^(z+1);Q)_m. (2) Here Q^z always denotes exp(2 pi i z/N). In fact 1/[Fhat(z) Fhat(n-z)] =exp[-i pi(n-z)(n-z-N+1)/N] (Q^(z+1);Q)_m/N. Substitution proves (2), including its constant by evaluation at z=0. There is no branch choice or asymptotic step in this calculation. In particular f(j)=a_(n,j) at EVERY allowed integer, and |f(0)|=|f(n)|=|F_n|^2. (3) The factor exp(2 pi i z) is essential to the bounds below. Its value is one on the actual summation lattice. Its use is legitimate here because the comparison is proved for the entire interpolant with the original finite sum and its explicit endpoint terms retained. ## 2. Uniform endpoint bounds in a late-index region Fix 0<delta<1/2 and assume (1/2+delta)N <= n <= N-1. (4) For a=0,n and real t, direct absolute values in (2) give |f(a+i t)|/|f(a)|=exp(pi lambda_a t) P_m(|t|), lambda_a=(2a+n-2N+2)/N, P_m(t)=product_(r=1)^m [1+sinh^2(pi t/N)/sin^2(pi r/N)]^(1/2). (5) At a=n the indices n+1,...,N-1 have the same sine magnitudes as 1,...,m. Thus (5) uses the same product at both original endpoints. Since m<(N-1)/2, the factors for r and N-r are disjoint equal pairs. The complete sine product gives P_m(t)^2 <= product_(r=1)^(N-1) [1+sinh^2(pi t/N)/sin^2(pi r/N)]^(1/2) =sinh(pi t)/[N sinh(pi t/N)] <= exp(pi t). (6) The identity follows by factoring w^N-1 at w=exp(-2 pi t/N), and extends continuously to t=0. The last bound also follows from sinh(Ns)/(N sinh s) =(1/N) sum_(r=0)^(N-1) exp((N-1-2r)s) <= exp((N-1)s). For the two endpoint lambdas, (4) implies |lambda_0| <= 3/2-delta-2/N, |lambda_n| <= 1. Consequently, uniformly in (4), |f(a+i t)| <= |F_n|^2 exp[(2 pi-pi delta)|t|]. (7) For |t|<=1 one also has |f'(a+i t)| <= C(1+log N)|F_n|^2. (8) To check (8), differentiate the Gaussian and the finite product in (2). Each logarithmic derivative in the latter is bounded by C/[N sin(pi r/N)] <= C/r, because r<=m<N/2 and |t|<=1. Their sum is O(1+log N); (7) bounds the undifferentiated factor. All constants in (8) can be absolute. No asymptotic estimate near a zero endpoint factorial is being used. ## 3. Exact finite summation formula and its error Contour integration gives the finite Abel--Plana identity sum_(j=0)^n f(j) =integral_0^n f(s) ds +(f(0)+f(n))/2 +i integral_0^infinity [f(i t)-f(-i t)-f(n+i t)+f(n-i t)] /(exp(2 pi t)-1) dt. (9) For clarity, its hypotheses are verified directly here. The function in (2) is entire. On every vertical line 0<=Re z<=n its upper growth rate as Im z tends to infinity is at most pi(2n-N+1)/N < pi. Its lower growth rate is at most pi(3N-3-2n)/N < 2 pi, by (4). The bound is uniform in this closed horizontal interval for each fixed N,n. Thus the horizontal edges disappear when the residue contour with kernels (exp(-2 pi i z)-1)^(-1) above the real axis and (exp(2 pi i z)-1)^(-1) below it is sent to infinity. The real edges combine into the integral in (9), the two vertical edges give its displayed differences, and half-circles at 0,n give the two half endpoint values. This proves (9) for this interpolant, rather than assuming a formal quadrature expansion. For 0<t<=1, (8) bounds the numerator by C t(1+log N)|F_n|^2. For t>=1, (7) and the denominator in (9) give an integrable bound C exp(-pi delta t)|F_n|^2. Including the two half endpoint terms proves |sum_(j=0)^n a_(n,j)-integral_0^n f_(N,n)(s) ds| <= C_delta (1+log N)|F_n|^2. (10) In particular the finite endpoint source has been bounded, not declared zero, and every Poisson contribution implicit in the original finite lattice sum is accounted for by the exact error. ## 4. The total error is controlled by the original figure-eight period Let I_(N,delta) be the sum of the integrals in (10) for all n satisfying (4), and let S_(N,delta) be the same range of the original double sum. The triangle inequality in (10) gives |S_(N,delta)-I_(N,delta)| <= C_delta(1+log N) sum_(n=0)^(N-1)|(Q;Q)_n|^2 = C_delta(1+log N) K_(4_1),N. (11) The final equality is the independently proved original-state [figure-eight source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md). Therefore limsup N^(-1) log|S_(N,delta)-I_(N,delta)| <= Vol(4_1)/(2 pi). (12) This is an actual global exponential comparison for the specified late-index sum. It does NOT assert that I_(N,delta) has a nonzero geometric contribution, or remove the outer discrete summation. The low-index part also requires its separate absolute bound. ## 5. A reusable criterion for other finite bridge convolutions The same proof applies to h(z)=C exp[-i pi z^2/N+i pi beta z/N] (Q^(z+1);Q)_m, n=N-1-m, m<=(N-1)/2, beta real. If, for some epsilon>0, max(|-beta-m|,|2n-beta-m|)/N + 1/2 <= 2-epsilon, (13) then its finite quadrature error is at most C_epsilon(1+log N)(|h(0)|+|h(n)|), (14) provided |beta|/N is bounded; this last bound in fact follows from (13) and 0<=m<N. Multiplication by exp(2 pi i k z), k integer, retains the exact lattice values and replaces beta by beta+2kN. Condition (13) decides when that choice gives the required bound. This criterion is checkable from the actual finite transfer rather than a conjectured geometric cycle. If a bridge convolution has this form and its endpoint sums have a smaller proven rate, it can be removed with a controlled error. No assertion is made that all knot diagrams admit such an ordering or such endpoint bounds. [Finite-sum, entire-interpolant and exact contour diagnostics](../experiments/audit_source_preserving_inner_quadrature.py).

title: Exact finite-height outer quadrature for the original five-crossing source
text: # Exact finite-height outer quadrature for the original five-crossing source 28 October 2026. The original double sum now has an exact outer contour formula with finite upper and lower heights. Its source edges, upper kernel and lower kernel are all explicit. A uniform factorial estimate includes BOTH inner endpoints, so a certified phase bound on the full inner polygon gives a polynomially sized outer error without an additional amplitude assumption. This establishes the applied quadrature criterion. The numerical phase bounds proposed for the geometric contour are not proved here, and no selected outer saddle or volume limit follows from the identity alone. ## 1. The actual holomorphic outer function Use `Q=exp(2pi*i/N)` and the EXACT marked interpolation `Fhat_N(z)` from [the factorial theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). Define K_N(z,w)=Q^[-z(z+2)-w(z+1)] Fhat_N(z)^3/[Fhat_N(w)Fhat_N(z-w)] exp(2pi*i*w), g_N(z)=exp(4pi*i*z) integral_0^z K_N(z,w)dw. (1) Both powers of Q use `Q^z=exp(2pi*i*z/N)`. The two exponential factors are integer-lattice gauges, with their full off-lattice values retained. For an actual integer `0<n<N`, g_N(n) is EXACTLY the selected inner integral of the original double sum in [the inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md). The function g_N is holomorphic on `0<Re z<N`. For a direct proof use `w=t z`, `0<=t<=1`: both `Re w` and `Re(z-w)` lie in `[0,Re z]`, where Fhat is holomorphic and nonzero. The parameter integral is locally uniformly holomorphic. For fixed z, any inner polygon from zero to z satisfying the same real-part constraints gives the identical integral, by Cauchy's theorem in its simply connected zero-free strip. In particular the selected polygon `0 -> i lambda -> Re z+i lambda -> z` is allowed, even when lambda is negative. No integer-n reflection formula is being applied at a noninteger outer z. ## 2. Uniform factorial amplitudes INCLUDING the endpoint zero Fix epsilon>0 and C<infinity. On D={zeta:0<=Re zeta<=1-epsilon, |Im zeta|<=C}, let `J(zeta)=integral_0^zeta Log(2sin(pi t))dt`, marked from `0<t<1` and extended continuously at zero from the right strip. Put Phi(zeta)=J(zeta)+(pi*i/2)(zeta^2-zeta). There are positive constants c,C_1, independent of N>=2, with c sqrt(1+N|zeta|) exp[N Re Phi(zeta)] <= |Fhat_N(N zeta)| <= C_1 sqrt(1+N|zeta|) exp[N Re Phi(zeta)] (2) uniformly on D. In particular its logarithmic error is `O(log N)` on this CLOSED domain, including zeta=0. The mark of Phi equals `[Li_2(1)-Li_2(exp(2pi*i*zeta))]/(2pi*i)` with the one-sided strip continuation; it is not reset on a dilogarithm cut. ### Proof directly from the original Gamma product In that product set z=N zeta. All kth-factor Gamma arguments `N(k+zeta)` and `N(k-zeta)` have real part at least `N(k-1+epsilon)`. Stirling's formula in a fixed right-half-plane sector therefore gives, uniformly and with a summable remainder, log kth_factor =N phi_k(zeta)+(1/2)Log(1-zeta^2/k^2)+O_(epsilon,C)(1/(N k^2)), phi_k=(k+zeta)Log(1+zeta/k) -(k-zeta)Log(1-zeta/k)-2zeta. The O bound may be enlarged for finitely many small k; it is uniform on D. The derivative of phi_k is `Log(1-zeta^2/k^2)`. The sine product thus combines their leading terms with the central Gamma term into N J(zeta). The sum of the half-log terms is `(1/2)Log[sin(pi*zeta)/(pi*zeta)]`, a bounded analytic function on D with its removable value at zero. The summed remainder is uniformly bounded (indeed O(1/N)). It remains to control the CENTRAL Gamma without assuming `|N zeta|` large. Put w=N zeta. Its difference from its leading primitive is exactly log Gamma(1+w)-w Log w+w. For `Re w>=0`, `|w|>=1`, uniform Stirling gives real part `(1/2)log|w|+O(1)`. For `|w|<=1`, Gamma(1+w) is nonzero and bounded above/below on the compact right half-disk, and `w Log w` has a bounded continuous extension at zero. Thus the same real part is `(1/2)log(1+|w|)+O(1)` everywhere. The explicit phase relating G_N and Fhat contributes only the bounded term `Re(pi*i*zeta/2)` after N Phi is removed. Exponentiation proves (2). A finite initial set of N is absorbed by compactness and nonvanishing, if needed. ## 3. A phase certificate suffices for the whole inner polygon Let `x=z/N`, `y=w/N`, with x in a fixed compact late strip `0<alpha<=Re x<=beta<1`, bounded imaginary part. Suppose the chosen inner polygon Gamma_x has a uniformly bounded number of straight segments and bounded total length, and `0<=Re y<=Re x` throughout. The action from the LITERAL (1) is S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +pi*i(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (3) It is exactly the marked action used by the selected-inner contour calculation. Equations (1)-(2), including the O(1) linear Gaussian factors, give uniformly |exp(4pi*i*Nx)K_N(Nx,Ny)| <= C sqrt(N) exp[N Re S(x,y)] /sqrt[(|y|+1/N)(|x-y|+1/N)]. (4) The endpoint factors in (4) are uniformly integrable on this polygon family. Since |x|>=alpha, y and x-y cannot both be small. Near either endpoint the only remaining singularity is distance to that endpoint to power -1/2. Its integral on a straight segment of bounded length is bounded independently of the segment's angle or distance from the endpoint. Summing the fixed number of segments gives a uniform bound. Consequently, with G(x)=sup_(y in Gamma_x) Re S(x,y), the ACTUAL outer function has the quantitative estimate |g_N(Nx)|<=C N^(3/2) exp[N G(x)]. (5) This controls the original inner endpoints rather than assuming the interior square-root expansion extends through them. For an interior compact subchart, the usual nonzero analytic amplitude is more explicitly sqrt(2N) [sin(pi*x)^3/(sin(pi*y)sin(pi*(x-y)))]^(1/2) exp[-pi*i(3x+2y)] exp[N S(x,y)](1+O(1/N)), with its inherited square-root mark. Only the bound (5) is needed for the outer error criterion below. ## 4. Exact finite-height residue formula with the original integers Let a<=b be integers in the allowed outer range. Set L=a-1/2, R=b+1/2. These half-integer source edges enclose exactly the original integers a,...,b. Let gamma_+ be any piecewise smooth upper curve from `L+iH_L` to `R+iH_R`, with positive height, and let gamma_- run from `L-iD` to `R-iD`, with D>0. Assume their enclosed domain lies in `0<Re z<N`. Define paths Gamma_+,Gamma_- from L to R by adjoining their vertical endpoint connectors. All orientations below run left to right on the upper and lower curves. For every function g holomorphic on this closed domain, sum_(n=a)^b g(n) =integral_L^R g(s)ds +integral_(Gamma_+) g(z)/(exp(-2pi*i*z)-1)dz +integral_(Gamma_-) g(z)/(exp(2pi*i*z)-1)dz. (6) Proof: the positive whole boundary is Gamma_- minus Gamma_+. Use the residue-one kernel pi cot(pi z) and the identities `pi cot(pi z)=-pi*i-2pi*i/(exp(-2pi*i*z)-1)` above, `pi cot(pi z)=pi*i+2pi*i/(exp(2pi*i*z)-1)` below. The unweighted halves are each `integral_L^R g/2` by holomorphy. This proves (6) with no endpoint half-residue convention or limit at infinite height. Deform the real integral in (6) through Gamma_+. Then sum_(n=a)^b g(n)=integral_(gamma_+) g(z)dz +T_+(g)+T_-(g)+E(g), (7) T_+(g)=integral_(gamma_+) g(z)/(exp(-2pi*i*z)-1)dz, T_-(g)=integral_(gamma_-) g(z)/(exp(2pi*i*z)-1)dz, E(g)= i integral_0^(H_L) g(L+it)/(1+exp(-2pi*t))dt -i integral_0^(H_R) g(R+it)/(1+exp(-2pi*t))dt +i integral_0^D g(L-it)/(1+exp(2pi*t))dt -i integral_0^D g(R-it)/(1+exp(2pi*t))dt. (8) The upper edge weights in (8) are at most one; the lower weights are at most exp(-2pi*t). In particular no endpoint derivative estimate for g is needed. The identity is still the original integer source. The half-grid edges specify its residue cycle rather than replacing its lattice values. ## 5. Applied geometric contour and its sufficient exponential bounds Choose a fixed window `alpha_0=.51`, `beta_0=.99`, and take `a=ceil(alpha_0 N+1/2)`, `b=floor(beta_0 N-1/2)` when nonempty. Then `ell=L/N`, `r=R/N` belong to this fixed window. All other original outer indices remain in the two real collars and retain their separate estimates. For fixed `u_g in (alpha_0,beta_0)`, `h_g>0`, put h(u)=min(h_g,h_g(1-u)/(1-u_g)), gamma_+: z=N[u+i h(u)], ell<=u<=r, gamma_-: z=N[u-.1i], ell<=u<=r. (9) The proposed marked geometric choices are approximately `u_g=.86919340003238`, `h_g=.09218763788516`. Formula (7) holds for any exact choices; taking the exact marked saddle values makes the upper curve pass through that point. Its kink is harmless because the curve is piecewise smooth. Since beta_0<1, h has a fixed positive minimum on the window. Suppose rigorous bounds on the FULL inner polygons establish G(u+i h(u))-2pi*h(u) <= Lambda_top, G(u-.1i)-.2pi <= Lambda_bottom, G(ell+i tau), G(r+i tau) <= Lambda_upperedge, G(ell-i tau)-2pi*tau, G(r-i tau)-2pi*tau <= Lambda_loweredge, (10) on the respective top, bottom and connector ranges. They must include the horizontal maximum AND both inner connector pieces, not just the selected inner saddle. By (5) and the exact kernel bounds, equations (7)-(10) give |sum_(n=a)^b g_N(n)-integral_(gamma_+)g_N(z)dz| <= C N^(5/2) exp[N Lambda], Lambda=max(Lambda_top,Lambda_bottom, Lambda_upperedge,Lambda_loweredge). (11) Indeed on the upper curve its kernel has modulus at most `exp(-2pi*N h)/(1-exp(-2pi*N h))`, uniformly at most twice the exponential for large N; the bottom has the analogous fixed-height bound. The connector weights are already bounded in (8). Their lengths are O(N), giving the stated polynomial. Thus any certified Lambda strictly below the proposed geometric rate proves that the OUTER discretization error is exponentially smaller. Add the already proved inner error and both actual real collars before inferring a statement about the full original double sum. This theorem does not supply the bounds (10), a nonzero outer Gaussian coefficient, or the geometric volume calibration; those are separate required steps. [Formula and endpoint-amplitude diagnostics](../experiments/audit_outer_finite_height_quadrature.py). The residue calculation and uniform Gamma-product estimates above, rather than numerical phase samples, prove (2), (6)-(11).

title: Source-symbol certificates and dependence on the presentation
text:
# Source-symbol certificates and dependence on the presentation Independent audit and direct proofs, 27 October 2026. A nonzero ordinary-color anchor does not imply simple root monodromy. The correct selected-source condition has an exact dual certificate, weaker than simplicity. The canonical actual Fourier--Mellin source supplies that certificate without deleting Jordan blocks. This complements [the source-corrected normal connection](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md). It does not identify the Mellin source line with the meridian regular-profile line or prove the selected regulator norm. ## 1. The exact source/dual certificate Let \(E=\mathbb C(Y)\), \(T_0=B_0\sigma_\zeta\) be invertible, \(H=T_0^N\), \(L=H-I\), and let \(0
e v\in\ker L\) be the selected root section. Then \[ \iota(v)
e0	ext{ in }\operatorname{coker}L \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{rank}[L\mid v]>\operatorname{rank}L \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists w:\ wL=0,\quad wv
e0. 	ag{1} \] These are equivalent elementary vector-space statements: \(\iota(v)=0\) means \(v\in\operatorname{im}L\), and the annihilator of \(\operatorname{im}L\) is the left kernel of \(L\). Thus the needed witness is a dual monodromy cocycle that sees the actual section. A physical cut with nonzero value need not be such a cocycle. There is a direct minors certificate at every rank. Choose a nonzero \(r\)-minor \(A=L_{I,J}\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}L\). For \(i
otin I\), put \[ w_i=e_i^t-L_{i,J}A^{-1}e_I^t . \] The rank assumption gives \(w_iL=0\), and \[ \det egin{pmatrix}A&v_I\L_{i,J}&v_i\end{pmatrix} =\det(A)\,w_iv. 	ag{2} \] At least one such minor is nonzero exactly when (1) holds. The rank-zero case uses the empty determinant convention: the certificate is simply a nonzero coordinate of \(v\). In corank one, any source cut \(\ell\) with \(\ell v
e0\) gives the single bordered certificate \[ \det egin{pmatrix}L&v\\ell&0\end{pmatrix} =-\ell\,\operatorname{adj}(L)v. 	ag{3} \] As \(\ker L=Ev\), the rank-one adjugate satisfies \(\operatorname{adj}(L)v=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}L)v\). Therefore (3) is nonzero exactly when \(\iota(v)
e0\). If \(\Delta(t)=\det(tI-H)\), its exact normalization is \[  rac{\det\left( egin{smallmatrix}L&v\\ell&0\end{smallmatrix}ight)} {\ell v} =(-1)^d\partial_t\Delta(1),\qquad d=\dim_E M. 	ag{4} \] This supplies the requested adjugate/source test. A simple norm root is sufficient, but (1) remains valid in higher corank, where an adjugate or a first characteristic derivative can vanish despite a visible selected section. There is also an exact splitting interpretation. If \(T_0v=v\), then (1) holds if and only if \(Ev\) has a \(T_0\)-equivariant retraction from \(E^d\). For a witness normalized by \(wv=1\), the projection \(p=vw\) commutes with \(H\). Average its conjugates: \[  ar p= rac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}T_0^jpT_0^{-j}. \] Since \(T_0^NpT_0^{-N}=HpH^{-1}=p\), this is a \(T_0\)-equivariant retraction onto \(Ev\). Conversely any such retraction has a row \(w\) with \(wL=0,wv=1\). Thus an invariant source line can fail to split even when it is an ordinary saturated vector subspace. ## 2. Actual polynomial pointing does not imply simplicity The actual unknot already distinguishes the statements. Its color functions are exactly \(C_j(Q)=1\), including their full polynomial pointing, and its minimal meridian operator is \(S-1\). Use instead the equally valid actual annihilator \[ P_2=(S-1)^2 . \] Its solution companion is \[ A= egin{pmatrix}0&1\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=I+J,\qquad J^2=0,\ J
e0 . \] For \(T=A^{-1}\sigma_\zeta\), \[ H=A^{-N}=I-NJ,\qquad \ker(H-I)=\operatorname{im}(H-I)=E(1,1)^t . \] The actual source \(v=(1,1)^t\) has \(\iota(v)=0\), even though its first-coordinate cut and every color anchor equal one. The cut \((1,0)\) does not annihilate \(H-I\). Thus neither explicit polynomial colors nor their nonzero anchor forces the source-symbol condition in an arbitrary actual presentation. Even failure of a simple norm root does not imply failure of the selected symbol. The actual unknot annihilator \[ (S-Q)(S-1) \] has a companion with distinct eigenvalues \(1,Q\) at every root of level \(N\ge2\). Its monodromy is \(H=I\); hence \(\iota\) is an isomorphism although \(\Delta(t)=(t-1)^2\) has zero derivative at one. The dual certificate (1), rather than simplicity alone, is the appropriate invariant for the selected direction. Removing a known extra left factor is legitimate only with its source comparison. Scalar-operator module quotients induce inclusions of solution modules, so left multiplication is not a regular gauge of the same normal module. In the squared example, the inclusion of the true rank-one source line into the enlarged Jordan module sends its cokernel symbol to zero. This explains exactly why the first-normal construction was not claimed invariant under arbitrary annihilator left multiples. ## 3. Root saturation does not choose the whole normal quotient The exact diagnostic \[ \mathcal A=(S-1)(S-Z),\qquad Z=Q^N,\qquad G_N=1+Y^N \] from the source-corrected note makes the issue explicit. The minimal scalar operator of its root section \(1+U\) is \(S-1\), but \[ (S-1)G_N=(Z-1)Y^N,\qquad (S-Z)G_N=1-Z. \] Neither whole factor annihilates this source. Replacing the whole problem by its minimal root factor loses the source-normal rule. Given the full actual source, one can make a rank-one whole quotient: \[ S- rac{1+Z\,Y^N}{1+Y^N}. \] But its first-normal source-corrected connection is \[ U\partial_U- rac{U}{1+U}, \] so the quotient has retained the chosen source ratio itself. For the other exact source \(A+B Y^N\), the corresponding quotient and connection instead contain \[  rac{A+B ZY^N}{A+B Y^N},\qquad U\partial_U- rac{BU}{A+BU}. \] All have the same minimal root factor \(S-1\). When \(A+B=2\), all root color values agree as well. Consequently a root source-generated or saturated quotient can restore a rank-one symbol but does not canonically determine its whole normal lift from the root operator and anchor. This does not deny the canonical quotient determined by a supplied full marked source. It prevents using that quotient as an operator-only proof of the very source comparison still needed. ## 4. The canonical actual Mellin source supplies a visible dual There is a constructive way to obtain the certificate for every knot, in the actual sourced Fourier--Mellin polarization. Retain [the canonical finite-color source](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md): \[ Z(Q,X)=\sum_{n\ge n_0}C_n(Q)X^n,\qquad A(Q,X,S)Z=B(Q,X),\qquad Sf(X)=f(QX). \] Here \(A=P^M\), and \(B
e0\) is a fixed Laurent polynomial built from finitely many fixed actual colors. Its nonzero lowest coefficient was proved in that construction. Assume positive S-order and retain the canonical homogenization \[ P_h=(S-\sigma_QB/B)A . 	ag{5} \] On its companion vector \(v=(f,\sigma f,\ldots)^t\), the literal observable source row is \[ \ell v=Af/B . \] The defining coefficient identity of (5) gives the quotient dynamics \(\sigma_Q(Af/B)=Af/B\). Equivalently its companion matrix satisfies \[ \sigma_Q(\ell)A_h=\ell . \] Thus, for its \(T=A_h^{-1}\sigma_Q\), the row intertwines \(T\) with the scalar shift. At a level-N root, \[ \ell H_0=\ell,\qquad \ell v_0=AZ_N/B=1. 	ag{6} \] Equations (1) and (6) prove \(\iota(v_0)
e0\), whether or not the rest of \(H_0\) is semisimple. This is an observable quotient of the same actual scalar state, not an unused adjoined unit. This construction is robust under the original operator presentation. If the original actual annihilator is replaced by a left multiple, one rebuilds its canonical Fourier--Mellin source \(B\) and the homogenization (5). The same finite-color construction makes that \(B\) nonzero and (6) holds again. No deletion of Jordan blocks and no minimal-annihilator assertion is needed. If the transformed S-order is zero, \(AZ=B\) is its exact rational algebraic equation; there is no need to manufacture a normal companion. ## 5. Formal first lifts suffice for the rational obstruction The root rationality of [the cyclotomic Mellin fiber](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives \(Z_N\in E=\mathbb C(X)\). The first derivative of the actual whole series is only asserted to lie in \(F=\mathbb C((X))\). This is enough. Each fixed \(C_n(Q)\) is Laurent polynomial and hence regular at the root. Coefficientwise differentiation gives a formal \(Z_1\) with the SAME fixed lower X bound \(n_0\). No common analytic q-neighborhood, derivative growth bound in \(n\), or convergent X-series is required. Rational coefficients of the fixed operator and of \(B^{-1}\) are regular over \(E[[\epsilon]]\) for every sufficiently large N: nonzero fixed rational Q-coefficients have only finitely many exceptional root values. A possible moving X-pole order in their epsilon expansion causes no problem in \(F[[\epsilon]]\). Therefore the homogeneous whole companion has a first lift \(v_1\in F^d\) satisfying \[ L_0v_1+L_1v_0=0 . \] Both \(L_0\) and \(L_1v_0\) are rational over \(E\). Solvability of this finite linear system over the field extension \(F/E\) implies solvability over \(E\), by equality of matrix and augmented ranks under field extension. Hence \[ D_N(v_0)=0\quad	ext{in the rational descended cokernel}. 	ag{7} \] If \(c(X^N)v_0\) also admits a first lift for the SAME whole homogenized operator, (6), (7), and the Leibniz rule imply \(U c'(U)\iota(v_0)=0\), and therefore \(c\) is constant. The marked nonzero source/prefix anchor fixes it to one. Negative Laurent S-powers must be normalized by a fixed left shift applied to BOTH \(A\) and \(B\); the observable source becomes its same shifted quotient. The proof then applies without changing its pointing. No pole coefficient is discarded before specialization. The retained scalar is still the actual residue \[ K_N=\operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty} Z_N(X)\,dX/X . \] The theorem removes central scalar freedom on this canonical selected Mellin line. It does not exclude arbitrary homogeneous source-kernel additions, identify another supplied module with that line, or estimate this residue. There is a necessary directional qualification for other affine objects. In the root regularization \(AR_N=b_N\), the earlier central transformation acts as \[ (R_N,1)\longmapsto(cR_N+(c-1)p_N,1), \] rather than multiplying the augmented vector by \(c\). Its change lies in the homogeneous source-kernel. A nonzero observable symbol of that augmented basepoint alone does not remove such an affine change. The Mellin argument above works because the tested comparison is a central scalar multiple of the SAME actual scalar \(Z_N\), whose observable quotient is then multiplied by that scalar.

title: From the selected source volume to hyperbolic volume
text: # From the selected source volume to hyperbolic volume 29 October 2026. The task here starts AFTER an original-source theorem has proved lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N| = V_src. It is to prove that this particular V_src is the hyperbolic volume of the actual complement. The argument below isolates a finite classical certificate for that equality. It does not assume that the displayed quantum limit has been proved for arbitrary knots. The existing [filled-source proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) already supplies this certificate for its selected long-filling branch. The [independent tangent-space audit](source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) checks the distinction between a source saddle and a critical point on the FULL angle domain. Sections 2--3 below give an elementary proof of the complete-cusp Casson--Rivin implication, including completeness. ## 1. The exact certificate Let T be an actual oriented ideal triangulation of a manifold with torus ends. Write theta for its three opposite-edge-pair angles in each tetrahedron. Let A impose the tetrahedral sums and E count the local edge occurrences at each global edge, with multiplicities. The positive angle domain is P={theta>0: A theta=pi*1, E theta=2pi*1}. Put V_T(theta)=sum_i Lambda(theta_i), Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt. For a complete cusped complement the certificate consists of: 1. A specified theta_src in P, on the actual triangulation and with every tetrahedron positive. 2. The absolutely normalized equality V_src=V_T(theta_src). 3. Full constrained stationarity: grad V_T(theta_src) in rowspace(A,E). (1) Equivalently, one exhibits real vectors mu,eta such that for each tetrahedral opposite edge pair i=(e,e'), -log(2sin theta_src,i)=mu_t+eta_e+eta_e'. (2) The conclusion is V_src=max_(closure P) V_T=Vol(M). (3) Row dependencies cause no problem: (1) is precisely annihilation of ker(A,E). A constrained source saddle proves (1) only if all omitted angle directions have also been accounted for. Section 4 explains two ways to do this without requiring the source variables themselves to parametrize every angle variation. For a filled manifold replace P by the actual filled-slope angle slice, and retain its primitive angular lifts and its end-completion certificate; see section 5. Imposing the unfilled boundary conditions would compute a different volume. ## 2. Strict concavity proves the maximum, including the boundary For one tetrahedron put beta=pi-alpha-gamma. Its negative volume Hessian, in independent coordinates alpha,gamma, is H=[[cot alpha+cot beta, cot beta], [cot beta, cot gamma+cot beta]]. (4) The first diagonal entry is sin gamma/(sin alpha sin beta)>0 and det H=1. Thus H is positive definite throughout the positive simplex. The sum over tetrahedra is strictly concave on every affine slice. If theta_src is an interior stationary point, follow the straight segment to any distinct point theta of the closure. This segment is positive except possibly at its final endpoint. Its volume derivative starts at zero and its second derivative is strictly negative. The continuous extension of Lambda to [0,pi] therefore gives V_T(theta)<V_T(theta_src) for theta!=theta_src. (5) The feasible domain is convex; V_T is concave. The convex function is -V_T. Neither nonemptiness of P nor strict concavity alone guarantees that its maximum lies in its interior. Positivity of theta_src in the certificate supplies the needed interior point directly. ## 3. Why the complete-cusp critical point is a complete metric This proves the geometric implication rather than merely naming the maximum a volume. It uses (2), not a presumed complete representation. Assign one real number to each global edge: l_e=-2 eta_e. (6) An ideal tetrahedron admits horospherical decorations whose six signed truncated edge lengths are exactly these numbers. Here is the explicit compatibility check. For any decorated ideal tetrahedron, the three opposite-pair length sums have differences (l_e+l_e')-(l_f+l_f') =2log(sin theta_i/sin theta_j). (7) For example normalize its vertices to infinity,0,1,z. If the three finite horospheres have Euclidean diameters d_0,d_1,d_z and the horosphere at infinity has height H, the six lengths are l_(infinity,a)=log(H/d_a), l_(a,b)=log(|a-b|^2/(d_a d_b)). The opposite sums are a common constant plus respectively 2log|1-z|, 2log|z|, 0. The sine rule proves (7) in the corresponding angle order. Equation (2) shows that the target lengths (6) have exactly these differences. Conversely those two independent differences are the ONLY restrictions. Changing the four horospheres adds r_v+r_w to the length of edge vw. A six-vector delta is of this form precisely when delta_01+delta_23=delta_02+delta_13 =delta_03+delta_12. For instance r_0=(delta_01+delta_02-delta_12)/2 determines the other three, and the displayed conditions check the remaining edges. Thus each tetrahedron has the required decoration. Glue the ideal faces according to T. The unique face isometry with the prescribed vertex matching preserves its three horocycles: the signed lengths on the three sides agree. Indeed a change of the three horocycles preserving all three side lengths would have r_0+r_1=r_1+r_2=r_2+r_0=0, hence all r_i=0. These decorations therefore match across EVERY face. Around an edge there is no residual dilation, since the horospheres at its ends return to themselves. Its total positive dihedral angle is exactly 2pi by E theta=2pi. Thus the edge has an ordinary hyperbolic neighborhood, with neither a cone angle nor a translation defect. There are no finite vertices to check. First shrink the compatible horospheres, by one common factor for each cusp, until they cut actual triangular corners and the finitely many corner neighborhoods are disjoint. Their matched triangles then form a nonsingular Euclidean metric on each compact link torus. It is complete; its universal development is the whole Euclidean plane. These corner neighborhoods give full complete horoball ends. The remaining core is compact. Hence the glued metric is complete, of curvature -1 and finite volume, on the ACTUAL M. Its volume is the sum of its tetrahedral volumes, V_T(theta_src). This proves (3). To compare with a separately specified complete metric, one can also apply the two marked representation-volume inequalities in opposite directions, as in the existing [geometric equality proof](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). No universal existence theorem for positive ideal triangulations is used in this implication. An actual positive theta_src is an input. ## 4. Eliminating internal variables is legitimate when they are optimized There are two sufficient ways to verify the full stationarity in (1). **Reduced optimization.** Choose affine coordinates (y,x) on the allowed angle domain, with y internal and x the retained source variables. Suppose the internal solution y(x) is an interior critical point in EVERY y direction, and define W(x)=V_T(y(x),x). Strict concavity makes each such internal point the unique fiber maximum. Its internal Hessian is invertible, so the implicit function theorem gives a smooth local y(x). The chain rule gives dW=partial_x V_T, because partial_y V_T=0. A critical point of W is therefore a critical point of the full V_T. This justifies coherent elimination if the eliminated action has been proved to be THIS fiber maximum. Naming an arbitrary reduced source action W is insufficient. **Full gluing and the boundary pairing.** The route already used by the actual source is more intrinsic. With x_t=Log z_t, y_t=Log(1-z_t^(-1)), a direct sine-rule calculation gives dV_T(delta theta) =sum_t[Re x_t delta Im y_t-Re y_t delta Im x_t]. At a full complex edge-gluing solution, the edge/peripheral symplectic reduction yields, for EVERY edge-angle tangent, dV_T=(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i]. (8) Here U_i,V_i are the actual small logarithms of the squared peripheral eigenvalues, in the fixed oriented marking of our notes. Full edge gluing kills the internal directions; the remaining quotient consists of these boundary directions. At a complete point U_i=V_i=0, (8) proves stationarity on all of P. The [tangent-space audit](source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) states the necessary full-rank edge/peripheral hypotheses and proves the analogous equivalence for arbitrary Lagrangian boundary slices. In particular this is stronger than differentiating volume merely along a family of already-glued representations. ## 5. The actual long-filling source passes the filled certificate For a filled cusp, take a primitive slope a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i and its actual log equation a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i, epsilon_i=+/-1. (9) The affine angle constraints fix a_i Im U_i+b_i Im V_i=2pi epsilon_i. The real part of (9) annihilates (8) on every tangent to that constraint. Retained cusps are complete. Thus a positive source point satisfying full complex edge gluing and (9) is stationary on the ENTIRE filled angle slice. Strict concavity again makes it the unique global maximum. For our selected source these inputs are established as follows: * The [literal port lift](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) is a representation of the actual augmented-link group, based at its explicitly constructed complete oriented geometry. The [direct positive ideal subdivision](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md) supplies a compatible ideal chart for these actual cells, with no general triangulation existence assumption. Transporting this fixed positive triangulation by its marked flags gives the positive source point for sufficiently long fixed fillings. * Its source equation is U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i on the selected unit-charge branch. The [primitive-period proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) fixes this as an actual period, not a congruence modulo 2pi i. * The [marked action calculation](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) proves V_src,s(p)=V_T(theta_p), including the actual filling quadratic and the absolute complete-volume anchor. There is no unidentified boundary constant left in this equality. * The [geometric completion](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) proves that these primitive periods close to smooth solid tori, with complete retained ends. This rules out a cone metric or a multiple covering at the core. Consequently V_src,s(p)=max_(closure P_p) V_T =Vol(S^3 minus K_p). (10) The complete augmented value V_s instead belongs to the unfilled boundary problem. It cannot simply be substituted for V_src,s(p). The [improved whole-source bound](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) gives the original quantum limit needed above for every fixed odd width s>=9 and independently sufficiently long fixed signed p_i. The same note records even widths s>=10 for the specified single-cut two-component link invariant. These are the current quantum scopes; the classical certificate itself has no pretzel-width restriction. For a new source, once its limit is proved, the next work is precisely to supply its positive angle point, full stationarity and absolutely normalized volume equality on the actual topology. No further asymptotic theorem is needed AFTER those certificates hold. The existence of an abstract source rate alone supplies none of them.

title: Sourced telescoping: a geometric-support criterion and the endpoint obstruction
text: # Sourced telescoping: a geometric-support criterion and the endpoint obstruction Research note, 27 October 2026. This audits the connection between the [finite-array annihilator proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and the [nonzero geometric normal block](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). It proves a conditional geometric-support criterion, an interior certificate lemma, and a precise obstruction to the naive integration map. It does **not** prove that the actual selected finite-state operator annihilates the geometric normal block. ## 1. Use the same auxiliary lift as the normal coefficient model The auxiliary lift in the finite-array proof takes the `(0,0)` entry of the off-root cut partial trace. The normal coefficient model instead uses the balanced constant vector and normalized-average covector. At the root these give the same reduced scalar by scalarity of the actual cut endomorphism. Off the root they need not agree, and their summands have different supports. For the present comparison use the off-root normalized-average lift Fbar_N(q,x)=(1/N) sum_(a=0)^(N-1) C_N(q,x)_(a,a), in the same factorial boundary frame as the normal model. The gauge is diagonal and invertible over generic `(q,x)`, so diagonal cut entries are unchanged by it. At the actual root `Fbar_N=F_N`. Every crossing, pivot and residual framing factor is retained. The common factor `1/N` is independent of all shifts used in the finite-span argument, so it does not affect that argument or any summand shift ratio. This lift has a full-dimensional interior in the `d=m+1` independent flow coordinates. Indeed, close strands `1,...,b-1` using the integral cofactor of the knot permutation, with determinant `+1` or `-1`. The initial positions are integral linear functions of the free cut position `a_0` and the `m` transfers. Put `a_0=N/2+O(1)` and every transfer near `epsilon*N`, with `epsilon>0` fixed and sufficiently small. At zero transfer all positions equal `a_0`. Hence all positions on the fixed word are `N/2+O(epsilon*N)`. Every transfer is positive, and all upper position and transfer inequalities are strict for sufficiently small `epsilon`. Small independent variations of all `m+1` coordinates preserve these strict inequalities. Thus the support contains the integer points in a nonempty open rational cone for large `N`. The old cut-zero lift need not have this property. For example, one positive two-strand crossing with cut position `a_0=0` has update `(a_0,a_1)->(a_1+k,a_0-k)`. Closing the second strand forces `a_1=-k`; nonnegativity then forces `a_1=k=0`. Consequently its summand array cannot silently replace the full normal flow array. ## 2. A global array certificate restricts to an interior rational identity Let `I_N(q,x;k)` be one of these proper, aligned summands and let P(x,z,T,S) I=0, z=q^N, be a global zero-extended certificate from the finite-span proof. For each fixed shift occurring in `P`, choose a smaller open cone in the interior from Section 1. For all sufficiently large integer points of this cone, every shifted term in `P` remains supported. Divide there by the nonzero reference summand. Proper alignment makes the result a rational function R(q,x,z,t_1,...,t_d), t_i=q^(k_i). Then `R=0` as a rational function in the independent variables. Here is the needed density argument. Clear the fixed rational denominator, then expand the numerator as a finite Laurent polynomial in `(q,x,z,t)`. If it is nonzero, precombine equal monomials and choose an integer point `(N,k)` in the open cone avoiding every affine hyperplane e-e' +(c-c')N +(alpha-alpha') dot k=0 arising from two distinct `(q,z,t)` exponent vectors. Such an integer point exists: an open rational cone contains arbitrarily large lattice boxes, while finitely many proper affine hyperplanes cannot cover them. Distinct exponent vectors then give distinct powers of `q` after `z=q^N,t_i=q^(k_i)`. The resulting Laurent polynomial in `(q,x)` cannot vanish, a contradiction. Thus the numerator was zero. This result imports no summation or cycle. It says that the **same global certificate** is an interior contiguity identity. Any formal realization of the exact actual shift ratios therefore satisfies that identity before its internal variables are pushed forward. In particular the local exact ratios in the normal-period note may be used; their half-step, pivot, residual framing and base factors may not be omitted. ## 3. The safe order of central specialization and moment extraction Clear denominators of the whole certificate, then divide its largest common central factor `(z+1)^r`, obtaining `P0`. The generic fixed-`N` array identity survives this division: `q^N+1` is a nonzero element of the rational function field in generic `q`. Thus P0(x,q^N,T,S) I_N=0. The finite summands are regular at `q_N=exp(pi*i/N)`; the crossing denominators have indices below `N`. Specialization gives P1(x,T,S)=P0(x,-1,T,S), which is nonzero as a fixed Ore polynomial and annihilates the root array for all but finitely many levels. If several direct-sum summand components are retained, use their common certificate throughout. Now expand P1=sum_alpha A_alpha(x,T)(S-1)^alpha. For a least nonzero total degree `h`, every nonzero `A_alpha` of degree `h` annihilates the actual summed root period. This is the finite moment argument: for `w_i=exp(v_i)`, translation of the entire finite zero-extended array is exact and P1(x,T,exp(-v)) F_N(x,v)=0. At degree `v^alpha`, all terms containing a positive moment of `F_N` have a lower-degree coefficient of `P1`, hence are zero. The surviving term is `(-1)^h A_alpha F_N(x,0)`. This order is useful for a formal comparison: remove the central factor of the **whole certificate**, specialize, then extract moments. Dividing a central factor from an individual moment coefficient only after specialization is not justified by a formal source defined solely at `z=-1`. ## 4. Conditional geometric-support theorem Suppose the actual root-specialized contiguity realization admits a linear weighted formal sourced pushforward `I_v` with all of the following properties: 1. `I_v(S_i f)=exp(-v_i) I_v(f)` for every internal shift appearing in `P1` and its iterates. 2. `I_v(Tf)=T I_v(f)`, and external scalar coefficients commute with `I_v`. 3. `Z(v)=I_v(I)` is regular as a formal power series in the independent `v_i` at zero, and `Z(0)` is nonzero. 4. The unweighted period has its marked geometric WKB form Z(0)=C(h) exp(S/h) a_0 (1+O(h)), a_0!=0, with `h=Log q`, the retained base-only line `C(h)`, and the actual meridian-step ratio having leading value equal to the marked geometric longitude `L`. All character and full-peripheral gauges are included in that statement. For regularity in item 3 one may use `exp(S/h)K((h))[[v]]`, allowing a different finite negative `h` order in each coefficient of `v`; no uniform lower bound in the `v` degree is needed. Then **one of the actual all-level operators constructed in Section 3 has a nonzero classical symbol vanishing on the geometric A-curve**. Proof: apply `I_v` to the interior certificate. Items 1 and 2 give P1(x,T,exp(-v)) Z(v)=0. The same least-degree coefficient argument as for the finite sum gives `A_alpha Z(0)=0`. Choose one nonzero such coefficient and divide only its common scalar `(q-1)` valuation, obtaining `Ahat`. This division preserves the actual all-level root annihilation and the formal annihilation. Let `a_cl(x,L)` be the first nonzero classical symbol of `Ahat`; clear its rational denominators if necessary. Leading WKB order of `Ahat Z(0)=0`, with `a_0!=0`, gives a_cl(x,L_geom(x))=0. On an irreducible geometric branch this says that its defining geometric A-factor divides the cleared classical polynomial, in the stated peripheral gauge. The operator came entirely from the actual global certificate and finite moment extraction. No known A-factor has been appended to it. This statement concerns that constructed annihilator; it does not assert that every annihilator, or the minimal operator, has that factor. A larger annihilator's symbol can contain factors absent from the minimal one. ## 5. Why the current relative source does not supply the hypotheses The existing [relative source realization](relative_framing_source_transgression.md) constructs a literal finite boundary projector, natural for all finite linear matrices. It does not identify its auxiliary relative coordinate with the two internal Gaussian framing modes. Consequently its coefficientwise naturality is not item 1 of Section 4. The failure of the naive replacement can be written exactly. At completeness write Omega_cut=dt wedge beta, beta=dlog A, with marked endpoints `t=0,1`. On a relative top form the functional is L(a,b_0,b_1)=integral_0^1 a(t)dt-b_1+b_0. For any polynomial `f(t,A)`, L(partial_t f,0,0)=[f(1,A)-f(0,A)] beta. It is generally nonzero. The relative coboundary is instead delta f=(partial_t f,f(0),f(1)), and only this complete triple has zero transgression. Thus replacing an internal summand divergence by an ordinary derivative on the geometric framing chart loses precisely the endpoint co-source. The finite-difference statement is equally explicit. For `S_eta f(t)=f(t+eta)` and J_v(f)=integral_0^1 exp(v*t/eta) f(t)dt, one has J_v(S_eta f)=exp(-v) J_v(f) +exp(-v) [integral_1^(1+eta) exp(v*t/eta)f(t)dt -integral_0^eta exp(v*t/eta)f(t)dt]. These endpoint series are well-defined coefficientwise for polynomial `f`, expanding in `v` with Laurent coefficients in `eta`. Already `f=1` contradicts the desired weighted covariance for the fixed relative interval: `S_eta f=f` and `J_0(f)=1`, whereas covariance would require `(1-exp(-v))J_v(f)=0`. The source endpoints must move or be compensated. Ordinary formal Gaussian integration in the transverse directions does not remove this defect. There is a second exact obstruction to replacing finite source data by ordinary functions before pushforward. In C_N=k[A,A^(-1)]/(A^N-1), the prescribed canonical representative satisfies A f_tilde - (Af)_tilde = f_(N-1)(A^N-1). For `f=A^(N-1)`, the actual cut gives `phi_N(Af)=phi_N(1)=1`, while the naive geometric operation gives `Res_(A=0) A^N dA/A=0`. The existing source comparison is linear, with this carry retained; it is not a ring map. Local interior contiguity identities do not encode that carry by themselves. ## 6. Exact remaining statement A sufficient next result is an explicit chain map from the actual whole internal finite contraction, with all endpoint/carry strata, to the relative geometric Gaussian pushforward, which sends every internal shift to its weighted source action and gives a nonzero unweighted geometric period. Section 4 would then force a geometric factor in a specifically constructed actual all-level annihilator. At present the normal block is nonzero before the remaining source pairing, and the literal finite relative source is nonzero in its own resolution. The map between these two pushforwards has not been constructed. The endpoint identity above is an explicit reason why their separate nonvanishing and ordinary integration by parts cannot substitute for it. No conclusion about the selected global geometric cycle or its volume growth follows from this note.

title: The compact source is the boundary of a resolved geometric framing torsor
text: # The compact source is the boundary of a resolved geometric framing torsor Research proof, 27 October 2026. The regular-unipotent meridian centralizer torsor has a canonical renormalized compactification. Its exceptional divisor is the actual compact coherent source X=(P1 times P1) minus the incidence divisor. This is an explicit matrix construction, not just an equality of dimensions or a local choice of framing coordinates. The principal Gaussian framing form, with its actual diagonal flag co-source retained, has a global nonzero logarithmic residue class on this divisor. The intrinsic coherent source line and all normal weights are determined as well. The logarithmic source/current complex is still required to use this class in the selected quantum period: allowing an unrestricted logarithm of the normal would make its logarithmic differential exact. The actual finite source geometry is proved in [the compact coherent calculus](compact_coherent_source_period.md). The explicit r,s,p gauge and physical-symbol section used below are independently calculated in [the compact framing and residue construction](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md). The principal Gaussian comparison is the general theorem of [the density-line calculation](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md). ## 1. The cut meridian has its literal Springer resolution Fix the physical meridian sign so the complete eigenvalue is +1. The unipotent cone is mu=I+N, where tr N=det N=0. Its resolution is L=Tot(O_P1(-2)), N(v,eta)=eta [[-v,1],[-v^2,v]], eigenflag=[1:v]. (1.1) The other chart has V=1/v, eta'=-v^2 eta, N=eta' [[V,-V^2],[1,-V]]. (1.2) Both formulas are verified by multiplication. Away from N=0 its unique kernel/image line recovers the retained flag. At N=0 the flag is the exceptional P1. Thus this resolves the cut meridian; it does not assert that a whole irreducible representation has a regular raw-matrix limit when this meridian approaches I. For the actual physical compact symbol, put a=z/(1+wz), v=w, T=v a, A=exp(c T), p=1/v, c=2pi*i. Its complete Gauss matrices give exactly eta_phys=(1-A^(-1))/v, mu-I=N(v,eta_phys). (1.3) At v=0 the quotient has the removable value c a. More explicitly eta_phys=(1-exp(-c v a))/v=c a+O(v a^2), partial_a eta_phys=c exp(-c v a), (1.4) so it is a local holomorphic change of coordinates at the compact north pole. In the south chart, a'=v-v^2a and T'=V a'=1-T; since exp(c)=1, eta'_phys=(exp(c V a')-1)/V=c a'+O(V(a')^2). (1.5) Both real compact poles therefore retain their limiting eigenflag. The exact form identity is dv wedge d eta_phys/(1-v eta_phys) =c dv wedge da =c dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^2. (1.6) This is an algebraic/logarithmic resolution of the physical symbol: one may retain A as a multiplicative coordinate with the marked relation Log A=c va. There is no N-dependent limit in (1.3)--(1.6). The clock is still a period of its exponential connection, not an algebraic function on a finite cover of X. Globally A=1 has every integer T fiber; the two poles above are the endpoints of the specified real compact cycle, not the entire analytic divisor. ## 2. The full geometric framing torsor has a nonextendible pole Choose the reference cut meridian I+E_12 of a fixed irreducible representation. The full projective conjugation torsor is G=PGL2. Its map to the nonzero cone is g -> g E_12 g^(-1), with fiber the additive regular-unipotent centralizer. On the Springer charts with eta!=0 take the projective sections g_N=[[1,0],[v,eta^(-1)]], g_S=[[V,(eta')^(-1)],[1,0]]. (2.1) Their conjugations of E_12 are precisely (1.1)--(1.2). Directly, g_N^(-1)g_S ~ [[1,-1/(v eta)],[0,1]], (2.2) where ~ means equality after a nonzero scalar. If b_N,b_S are the additive centralizer coordinates on the right, then b_S=b_N+1/(v eta). (2.3) This torsor cannot extend as an ordinary algebraic Ga torsor over the zero section of L. Here is an elementary proof. On the punctured line bundle the cocycle in (2.3) has fiber degree -1. A coboundary of that degree is a sum eta^(-1) f(v)+(eta')^(-1)g(V) =eta^(-1)[f(v)-v^(-2)g(1/v)]. (2.4) The Laurent powers available on the right are >=0 and <=-2. The required v^(-1) is missing. Thus (2.3) has nonzero Cech class. On the whole bundle only nonnegative fiber degrees occur. At degree j>=0, the north regular powers are >=0 and the south ones are <=2j; together they span every Laurent power. Hence every regular Ga torsor on this two-chart total space has zero class. Its restriction cannot equal (2.3). This proves the obstruction without a torsor-triviality citation. For the elementary additive-descent step used here, an additive torsor on an affine chart is trivial: on a finite principal-open trivializing cover, clear all cocycle denominators by powers f_j^k, write 1=sum_j h_j f_j^k, and take the weighted sums of its additive transition functions. The cocycle identity makes these sums a coboundary. Thus no affine-chart torsor has been omitted from the two-chart calculation. There is also a direct irreducible-representation obstruction. Conjugating by diag(r,r^(-1)) makes the chosen meridian I+r^2E_12 approach I. Some other group element has a nonzero lower-left coefficient, because otherwise the representation preserves the chosen line. That coefficient becomes r^(-2)c. The raw representation escapes. Resolving its cut eigenflag does not remove this pole of the full irreducible framing family. This obstruction is independent of the chosen degeneration: for U=I+E_12 and B=[[a,b],[c,d]] in SL2, direct multiplication gives tr[U,B]=2+c^2. Irreducibility supplies some c!=0. If a regular raw limit had its cut meridian equal to I, this trace would tend to 2, contradicting its conjugation-invariant value. Thus no different regular raw framing can evade the escape. ## 3. Renormalizing the centralizer produces the actual source X Use the determined rescaling a_N=-eta b_N, a_S=-eta' b_S. Equation (2.3) becomes exactly V=1/v, a_S=v-v^2 a_N. (3.1) This is the compact coherent-source torsor. Indeed with a_N=z/(1+vz), one has a_S=v/(1+vz), and its complement condition is the transversality of the two flags ell=[1:v], ell_other=[-z:1]. Thus the renormalized space is the threefold Y=Tot(O_P1(-2)) times_P1 X, E_exc={eta=0}=X. (3.2) Its open part eta!=0 is exactly PGL2 by (2.1)--(2.3), not merely birational to a new state. In north coordinates its actual projective conjugator has the polynomial representative g(v,eta,a)=[[eta,-a],[eta v,1-va]], det g=eta. (3.3) At eta=0 this is rank one. Its image is the second flag and its first-column direction is the retained flag; the two are transverse. Formula (3.3) displays the compact source as the exceptional data of a degenerating actual projective frame. The south representative is -v times (3.3), with the appropriate south row convention. Scalar transition does not change conjugation. The original constant Ga action b->b+c becomes a->a-eta c. It vanishes on E_exc. The rescaled additive group of the line O(-2), acting by translation in a, instead extends freely. This is the precise twisted-centralizer replacement at the shell; there is no global choice a=0 in the nontrivial affine torsor X. The full representation extends on its elementary-modification lattice g O^2, with its projective scalar clutch retained. In that lattice the representation matrices are the fixed reference ones. Its abstract cut meridian remains nontrivial; only its singular inclusion into the original raw trivialization has become I. This associated-bundle extension must not be mistaken for an ordinary regular deformation of the raw representation to the central identity color. ## 4. The global logarithmic volume has the compact source residue Define the invariant three-form on the actual frame torsor by H_G=d eta wedge dv wedge db. Its normalization is specified by this equation. To verify invariance, on the SL2 cover write g=n_-(v)diag(r,r^(-1))n_+(b), r^2=eta. The h,e,f components of its Maurer--Cartan form have wedge r dr wedge db wedge dv=-H_G/2; conjugation by n_+(b) has determinant one, so this calculation holds for all b. Thus the stated factor of -2 relative to that Maurer--Cartan convention is explicit. Substitution b=-a/eta gives its exact extension to Y: H_G=-(d eta/eta) wedge dv wedge da. (4.1) This is global: dv wedge da is unchanged by (3.1), while d eta'/eta'=d eta/eta+2dv/v, whose added term wedges to zero. Consequently Res_(E_exc) H_G=-dv wedge da=2pi*i omega_I, omega_I=-(1/(2pi*i))dv wedge da. (4.2) The compact coherent sphere Gamma has integral omega_I=1. Thus (4.2) is a nonzero global algebraic de Rham class on X. A small normal circle bundle over Gamma is a lens-space cycle with Chern number -2, the compact PGL2 framing cycle. No global normal-circle section is needed for the residue pairing. The line-bundle calculation agrees with the explicit form: K_Y=pi^*O(2), O(E_exc)=pi^*O(-2), K_Y(E_exc)=O, K_(E_exc)=K_X=O. (4.3) In particular the logarithmic volume and its residue have trivial torus weight even though the ordinary centralizer torsor did not extend. ### 4.1 The actual principal Gaussian has the same nonzero residue This comparison uses the actual diagonal Hopf scaling, not an assumed arbitrary classical source action. On the old inverse-flag cut chart at complete meridian, retain its centralizer coordinate r and scale s: F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]. Allow the exact common diagonal momentum gauge p, and take the source conjugator g=(F(r,s)diag(p^(-1),1))^(-1). The explicit comparison with (2.1) is v=1/p, eta=-s p, b=(1-r)/s, a=p(1-r), A_cut=(1+s)^(-1)=(1-eta v)^(-1). (4.4) These are the bridge note's full three-dimensional framing coordinates; r remains present and is not confused with the two-dimensional meridian leaf. Their Jacobian is d eta wedge dv wedge db =-dr wedge ds wedge dp/(s p). It follows exactly that Omega_cut wedge dLog p =A_cut H_G =-(d eta/eta) wedge dv wedge da/(1-eta v). (4.5) The missing Haar adapter is A_cut in the interior. Its restriction to E_exc is one, so the residue is fixed, not guessed from weights. For any nondegenerate geometric critical representation satisfying the general density theorem, retain its original square-root phase and set c_beta^2=-T_beta/2. The torsion T_beta is nonzero and is constant along this conjugation torsor. Hence the actual principal Gaussian density has Omega_beta=c_beta Omega_cut on that marked line. Equation (4.5) proves (1/(2pi*i))Res_(E_exc) (Omega_beta wedge dLog p)=c_beta omega_I. (4.6) Its compact period is c_beta!=0. This is a global nonzero leading geometric logarithmic-residue class for an arbitrary such knot braid. It strengthens nonzero local Gaussian density to a global class on the actual compact source domain. The co-source dLog p and the phase line in (4.6) are part of the assertion. Here the domain identification is the canonical isomorphism E_exc=X. It is not an assertion that the physical compact cycle has already been pushed onto this exceptional divisor. The original base-only quantum normalization line is tensored through unchanged. No isolated compact factorial or full modified-dimension factor is evaluated at a root or removed by this variable-density calculation. This does not yet state that the whole actual quantum network pushes its selected source to (4.6). In particular Green currents can contain Log eta. Once that coordinate is admitted without its relative endpoint data, d eta/eta is exact and an absolute argument can erase the residue. The actual relative source/current complex must be carried through this boundary construction; a nonzero principal residue is not itself the global selected-period theorem. ## 5. Source and Gaussian line weights are distinct and explicit Let h(alpha)=diag(alpha,alpha^(-1)). At the north and south fixed flags the tautological O(-1) fibers have characters alpha and alpha^(-1), respectively, meaning weights +1,-1. The relevant integer weights are therefore | Line | North weight | South weight | |---|---:|---:| | tautological O(-1) | +1 | -1 | | nilpotent normal O(-2) | +2 | -2 | | ordinary K_Y=O(2) | -2 | +2 | | ordinary half-canonical K_Y^(1/2)=O(1) | -1 | +1 | | logarithmic K_Y(E_exc) | 0 | 0 | | logarithmic half-canonical line, on its sign mark | 0 | 0 | | prequantum O(N) | -N | +N | | polarized half-form K_P1^(1/2)=O(-1) | +1 | -1 | | actual coherent wave line O(N-1) | -(N-1) | +(N-1) | | geometric torsion/Gaussian ratio c_beta | 0 | 0 | The half-form identity is the exact intrinsic source identity H_N=H^0(P1,O(N-1)) =H^0(P1,O(N) tensor K_P1^(1/2)). (5.1) The determinant-line accounting is also compatible with square roots: the ordinary half-canonical character and half-normal divisor character cancel on a compatible logarithmic half-density line. The actual density theorem fixes the weight-zero ratio c_beta after the original cut-density factors have been combined. It does not identify a separately normalized transverse Gaussian with K_Y^(1/2) alone. These line statements retain the original square-root phases and do not equate ordinary coherent clutch with quantum dressing. The coherent vector line is the dual O(-(N-1)); its coefficient wave line is O(N-1). Their distinction avoids a sign ambiguity in the table. Pairing the actual source and co-source and retaining the incidence denominator gives the globally defined compact kernel, whose normalized trace period is already exact. There is a useful representation-theoretic check of the boundary weight. On the SL2 sign cover, (3.3) lifts as eta^(-1/2)g, so for n=N-1, Sym^n(g_SL2)=eta^(-n/2)Sym^n(g). (5.2) Its leading coefficient is the rank-one coherent operator of the two boundary flags. At v=a=0 the eigenvalues are eta^(1/2), eta^(-1/2), and the powers are eta^((n-2j)/2). This yields precisely the source normal pole and torus weight in the table. For odd n the single source requires its SL2 sign mark; the End kernel and paired compact period descend to PGL2 for every N. Equation (5.2) is the standard polynomial coherent-line clutch. It is not proved here to be the actual unrestricted quantum-group dressing of a physical Gauss frame. Ordinary SL2 Möbius action on coherent coordinates and the actual quantum dressing are different constructions until a source-preserving network map has been supplied. The exact actual result in this note is (4.6), which uses the independently checked physical diagonal gauge and principal Gaussian density, not this unproved identification. ## 6. Physical-symbol and residue sections remain separately marked The compact source also has the physical map of Section 1. Under the actual bridge coordinates it is reached by the logarithmic centralizer section r_*(A)=1-Log A/(2pi*i), a=p(1-r_*)=p Log A/(2pi*i). (6.1) The mark at the north pole is r_*=1 and that at the south pole is r_*=0.
