A logarithm deck shift changes r_* by -1 and its old frame coordinate b=(1-r)/s by +1/s; the relative comparison coordinate (r_*-r)/s has the opposite jump. Thus the global source needs the logarithmic transition, not a single split B1 section. The r,s,p note retains its boundary primitive and sign. The associated boundary coordinate T=va=1-r and the physical symbol coordinate Log A/(2pi*i) agree on the marked section (6.1). They are not identical functions on the full three-dimensional framing family. In particular taking an arbitrary framing section or identifying the old two B1 coordinates with the two compact leaf coordinates would change the comparison. More precisely the physical section is the graph eta=(1-exp(-2pi*i va))/v inside Y; eta on Y is otherwise independent. This graph meets E_exc at the analytic identity locus, not along all of X. For finite v!=0 that locus has va in Z; at v=0 its removable condition is a=0. On the real compact sphere only the two poles occur. Therefore the nonzero residue class on E_exc is not yet the image of the actual physical compact-cycle pairing. A relative cycle or source-chain comparison is still necessary. Equivariant descent supplies the global principal class (4.6) and fixes its line weights. It does not fix the scalar of a whole actual quantum source or ensure that unrestricted logarithmic Green transgressions preserve that class. The remaining operation is a marked relative pushforward with the actual source, caps, Weyl transitions and normal jets retained, rather than another choice of a local geometric optimum. The [exact universal audit](../experiments/audit_springer_centralizer_boundary_source.py) checks the matrix transitions, compact flag and form maps, actual Gaussian adapter, normal weights and coherent rank-one boundary. The [independent resolved-boundary audit](resolved_framing_boundary_independent_audit.md) also verifies the centralizer nonextension, matrix compactification, line bundles and principal Gaussian residue with the physical-cycle and quantum-dressing qualifications retained. The [independent global boundary audit](resolved_framing_boundary_independent_audit.md) checks the torsor obstruction, compactification, exact Haar adapter and marked principal residue, including its selected-cycle limitation.

title: The actual pointed fusion map in the literature charged matrix frames
text: # The actual pointed fusion map in the literature charged matrix frames Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an exact local comparison between the pointed cyclic fusion map used in the actual source construction and the literature basic/charged matrix dilogarithm. It retains four face frames, the input permutation, the scalar fixed by the selected unit, and the full integer-charge multiplier. At the nilpotent source the same identity gives a regular standard kernel on the normal chart. The fractional face powers combine to the integer carry pole. The normal kernel shape is a ratio of normal directions; for recoupling it is their ordinary projective cross-ratio. These are algebraic evaluations at fixed N, not a volume limit. The definitions compared below are the displayed definitions in [Baseilhac--Benedetti, Section 2.1.2, equations (3) and the following kernel](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0306283v2#S2.SS1.SSS2). Only definitions and scope are used from that source. Its proofs of symmetrization, tetrahedral invariance and global state identification are not premises. This note proves local identities directly. It does not repair the failed full vertex-order test merely by naming the charged tensor, construct the required global charged source, or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. Definitions and compatible roots Let N=2m+1>=3, r=m+1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), so 2r=1 modulo N. The odd-level restriction is part of the literature definition being compared. Section 9 computes the same existing fusion map at even levels without claiming that this source defines an even charged tensor. For u^N+v^N=1, with uv!=0, put Omega(u,v|n)=product_(j=1)^n v/(1-uQ^j). It extends periodically to every integer n. Let g_N(u)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-uQ^(-j))^j, h(u)^N=g_N(u)/g_N(1). (1.1) Here h is the literature g(u)/g(1), with its compatible Nth roots retained; g_N is its unambiguous Nth-power product. The basic kernel without that scalar and the published normalized kernel are L0(u,v)_(k,l)^(i,j) =Q^(kj+r k^2) Omega(u,v|i-k) delta_(i+j,l), L(u,v)=h(u)L0(u,v). (1.2) All indices are modulo N. In this note (i,j) are output indices and (k,l) are input indices, in precisely the displayed order. For the pointed fusion C_(s,t) choose nonzero compatible roots alpha^N=s, beta^N=t, eta=alpha beta, a_s^N=1-s, a_t^N=1-t, a_st^N=1-st, gamma=a_st/a_t, v=a_s/a_st, u=alpha/gamma. (1.3) Assume s,t,1-s,1-t,1-st are nonzero. Then tau=gamma^N=(1-st)/(1-t), u^N=s/tau, v^N=(1-s)/(1-st), u^N+v^N=1. The relations a_st=gamma a_t and a_s=gamma v a_t are part of the marked cover. Arbitrarily independent roots would miss their face factors. The shape in (1.2) is w_0=u^N=s/tau. It is the reciprocal of the cross-ratio label tau/s used by the earlier recoupling note. The corresponding orientation and index conventions must be retained in a regulator comparison. ## 2. Exact four-face factorization For a variable z and norm root a, write phi_(z,a)(j)=(Qz;Q)_j/a^j, Phi_s=diag phi_(alpha,a_s), Phi_t=diag phi_(beta,a_t), Phi_st=diag phi_(eta,a_st). These are the existing pointed cyclic-factorial frames. Define the other input-face frame and the quadratic phase by D_tau(k)=(beta v)^k / product_(j=1)^k(1-gamma^(-1)Q^(-j)), Gamma_N(k)=Q^(-r k^2). (2.1) They are periodic: (beta v)^N=1-gamma^(-N). Each denominator is nonzero on the stated chart. Let P exchange the total and relative input factors. In evaluation bases at the marked roots, the exact pointed fusion identity is C_eval=kappa (Phi_s tensor Phi_t) L0(u,v) (D_tau Gamma_N tensor Phi_st^(-1))P, kappa=(1/N)sum_(b=0)^(N-1) gamma^(-b)(Q eta;Q)_b/(Q beta;Q)_b. (2.2) Thus the comparison with the normalized literature L has scalar kappa/h(u), not an unspecified proportionality. It is fixed by the original pointed fusion map. The Gaussian and input flip in (2.2) are essential. Each remaining matrix is a function on a single face with its specified norm root; no new local quantum function has been introduced. Here is a direct proof. The known pointed polynomial kernel is C_(s,t)(U^a V^b) =w^a (Qw;Q)_b/(Qz;Q)_b, w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. Passing to evaluation bases gives delta_(l,i+j) times f_k(i,j)=(1/N)sum_b gamma^(-b)Q^(-kb) (Q alpha beta Q^(i+j);Q)_b/(Q beta Q^j;Q)_b. (2.3) Set x=alpha Q^i, z=beta Q^j. The finite-product recurrence in b and its cyclic closure give f_k/f_(k-1)=z (gamma Q^k-Qx)/(gamma Q^k-1). (2.4) Every numerator and denominator here is a unit on the chart. Divide f_k by D_tau(k)Q^(jk)Omega(u,v|i-k). Equation (2.4) makes the result independent of k. The relative Y-intertwining equation next gives the row ratio B_(i-1,j+1)/B_(i,j) =gamma v (1-beta Q^(j+1))/(1-alpha Q^i). Consequently B_(i,j)=phi_s(i)phi_t(j)A_(i+j). The total Y-intertwining equation reduces to A_l/A_(l-1)=gamma a_t/(1-eta Q^l). It follows that A_l=kappa/phi_st(l). The value at i=j=k=0 is exactly the finite sum in (2.2). The chirp in (2.1) cancels the k^2 phase in (1.2), proving the formula entry by entry. Invertibility of the pointed fusion and its face frames proves kappa!=0; if its value were zero the same recurrences would make the whole matrix zero. ## 3. The published normalization has determinant one: a rigidity proof First L0 is invertible directly. At fixed l its block is a pair of diagonal matrices times the circulant with entries H_n=Q^(r n^2)Omega(u,v|n). For its finite Fourier coefficients Hhat_a, the defining recurrence gives Hhat_a=(u+vQ^(1-r-a))Hhat_(a-1). (3.1) The multipliers are nonzero, and their product is u^N+v^N=1. If one Fourier coefficient vanished they would all vanish, contradicting H_0=1. This proves invertibility at composite levels as well. The exact root translations of L0, proved in Section 5, imply that Delta(u,v)=det L0(u,v) [g_N(u)/g_N(1)]^N is invariant under independent u->Qu and v->Qv. The clock and shift determinants are one at odd N. Thus Delta belongs to C(z), z=u^N, the invariant field of the Fermat cover. It is a regular unit away from z=0,1,infinity. It is therefore of the form constant*z^a*(1-z)^b for integers a,b. At u=0,v=1 the Gaussian circulant remains invertible, so a=0. At u=1,v=0, Omega(n)=0 for 1<=n<N and Omega(0)=1. The kernel is the permutation (k,l)->(k,l-k) with coefficient Q^(kl+(r-1)k^2). Its determinant is one: the permutation sign is one at odd N and the sum of those exponents is divisible by N. Also h(1)=1. This gives b=0 and the constant one. Hence exactly det L(u,v)=1. (3.2) This proves the normalization by an explicit invariant-unit argument and boundary evaluation, rather than a borrowed matrix-dilogarithm theorem. ## 4. The remaining scalar is a specified normalization torsor Put S=N(N-1)/2=Nm, and let F_s,F_t,F_st,F_D be the products of the diagonal entries of Phi_s,Phi_t,Phi_st,D_tau. The already proved polynomial fusion determinant and the two Vandermonde changes give det C_eval=[t/(1-t)]^S. For example the Vandermonde ratio is gamma^(-NS), which converts the polynomial-basis determinant to this expression. The input flip has determinant (-1)^m. The chirp determinant raised to N is one, including when 3 divides N. Equation (3.2) therefore gives the exact scalar norm (kappa/h(u))^(N^2) =(-1)^m [t/(1-t)]^(Nm) [F_st/(F_s F_t F_D)]^N. (4.1) The source value (2.2) and the chosen branch of h fix its remaining phase. Equation (4.1) is not permission to discard the scalar or choose independent roots at different moves. It makes its modulus and normalization line explicit from the four face factors. For compatible roots with bounded fixed logarithms of s,t, 1-s,1-t,1-st as N varies, (4.1) also gives log|kappa/h(u)|=O(log N). (4.2) Indeed a cyclic-factorial product has log-modulus log|F_s|=N log|(1-s)/(1-alpha)| -N log|D_N(alpha)|-m log|1-s|, where D_N(alpha)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-alpha Q^j)^(j/N). The fixed-log root bound proved in [the triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md#4-keep-central-and-semiclassical-shapes-distinct) is log|D_N(exp(w/N))|=O(log N). It gives O(N log N) for each F; the inverse-Q input frame obeys the same estimate. Substitution in (4.1) proves (4.2), with upper and lower polynomial bounds. This concerns these marked trajectories. It does not bound an arbitrary moving root frame or the selected contraction of the knot state. ## 5. Charges act through the finite Heisenberg torsor Let Z e_j=Q^j e_j and S e_j=e_(j+1). Finite-product cancellation gives, for every a,b modulo N, Omega(uQ^a,vQ^b|n) =Q^(bn)Omega(u,v|n+a)/Omega(u,v|a). Substitution in (1.2) proves the full operator identity Omega(u,v|a)L0(uQ^a,vQ^b) =(Z^b S^(-a) tensor S^a)L0(u,v) (Z^(a-b) tensor I). (5.1) No scalar is suppressed. The scalar normalization obeys g_N(uQ^a)/g_N(u)=Omega(u,v|a)^N. Thus on the compatible cover h_a=Omega(u,v|a)h_0, (5.1) is the corresponding identity for normalized L. Other normalization-root lifts retain their finite phase. For the matrix operation W_(a,b) on the right of (5.1), W_(c,d) W_(a,b)=Q^(bc)W_(a+c,b+d). (5.2) This follows from S^(-c)Z^b=Q^(bc)Z^b S^(-c). In particular the two root generators have central commutator Q. The root transport is the finite Heisenberg extension, with its central root retained, rather than an unmarked pair of roots. Its Weyl matrices are unitary for complex Q on the unit circle. To apply the literature charged definition, let w_0=z, w_1=(1-z)^(-1), w_2=1-z^(-1). For a chosen log branch and flattening f, its root formula is w_j'=exp[(Log w_j+(f_j-epsilon c_j)(N+1)pi*i)/N], c_0+c_1+c_2=1, epsilon=+/-1. Relative to the unshifted roots of w_0 and w_1^(-1), put a=r(f_0-epsilon c_0), b=-r(f_1-epsilon c_1), u_c=uQ^a, v_c=vQ^b. The published charged tensor is exactly R_(epsilon,c)=sigma_(epsilon,c)L(u_c,v_c)^epsilon, sigma_(epsilon,c)=u_c^(-m c_1)v_c^(-m c_0). (5.3) Equation (5.1) expresses this definition in the original matrix frame by explicit four-leg Weyl operators. For a negative tensor their order and inverses are reversed; the prefactor in (5.3) is still retained as printed. No published symmetry proof is assumed in this calculation. The integral charges must not be reduced modulo N in the prefactor. A lift (c_0,c_1)->(c_0+N b_0,c_1+N b_1), with c_2 adjusted, leaves u_c,v_c unchanged but multiplies the full tensor by z^(-m b_1)(1-z)^(-m b_0). (5.4) These are central functions, not generally phases. For fixed integer charges and fixed z the exact modulus is log|sigma_c|=-m/N [c_1 log|z|+c_0 log|1-z|]. (5.5) It is bounded across N under that qualification. The Weyl root shifts preserve the local normalized kernel's singular values; (5.5) supplies its remaining scalar norm. This operator statement supplies no lower bound for an arbitrary selected global contraction. ## 6. The selected source is explicit in the standard frames The pointed fusion sends the product unit to the product unit. In evaluation coordinates these are constant vectors. Equation (2.2) consequently says L0(u,v)p_standard =kappa^(-1)(Phi_s tensor Phi_t)^(-1)1, p_standard=(D_tau Gamma_N tensor Phi_st^(-1))1. (6.1) The flip fixes that constant input. In general p_standard is not the constant vector. This gives the selected source in the standard matrix definition, rather than identifying two unpointed kernels and resetting their boundary vectors. For a positive charged tensor (5.3), substituting (5.1) in (2.2) gives the original map with four transported leg frames and scalar kappa/[h(u)sigma_c]. For the inverse original map the corresponding scalar is h(u)/[kappa sigma_c], with the inverted leg order. These formulas retain the complete peripheral functions before specialization. Any already specified finite recoupled actual network can make this substitution with its full source, covectors, caps and scalar lines. Its period is then unchanged exactly. This is a local equivalence with the literature definition. It is not a proof that the independently prescribed face pairings, charges and selected vector of a global geometric state are the transformed ones in (6.1). ## 7. The normal chart gives a nondegenerate standard tetrahedron At fixed N take alpha=1-epsilon a, beta=1-epsilon b, a b(a+b)!=0, s=alpha^N, t=beta^N. Algebraic evaluation of the ratios at epsilon=0 gives gamma^N=(a+b)/b, u^N=b/(a+b), v^N=a/(a+b), kappa_0=(1-u^N)/(N(1-u)). (7.1) The last formula is the finite geometric sum obtained from (2.2), since its Pochhammer quotient becomes one. All these standard kernel parameters are nondegenerate, and kappa_0 is nonzero. This is an evaluation on the normal chart, not an N->infinity calculation. The singular face roots in (2.2) recombine integrally. On its support l=i+j modulo N put kappa_carry=floor((i+j)/N). Writing p_i(alpha)=(Qalpha;Q)_i, exactly phi_s(i)phi_t(j)/phi_st(l) =[p_i(alpha)p_j(beta)/p_l(eta)] gamma^(l-i)v^(-i)(1-t)^(-kappa_carry). (7.2) Use a_st=gamma a_t, a_s=gamma v a_t and a_t^N=1-t to prove (7.2). Thus the fractional powers cancel to the integer carry. Every other displayed kernel factor is a unit at the normal point. Multiplying row (i,j) by (1-t)^kappa_carry gives a regular source frame. Its determinant is exactly t^(N(N-1)/2), hence one at t=1. Its actual normal matrix, for l=i+j modulo N, is C0_(ij,lk)=kappa_0 [(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j/(Q;Q)_l] gamma^(l-i)v^(-i)D_tau(k)Q^(jk) Omega(u,v|i-k). (7.3) There are N(N-1)/2 carry-one rows. They are the retained relative source directions of the two-lattice construction; evaluating only an ordinary unscaled image loses them. The independent valuation calculation in the audit checks (7.3) directly from the original finite-product Fourier sum, as well as its determinant and unit pointing. For three normal leaf directions a,b,c the standard recoupling shape is z_normal=(a+b+c)b/[(a+b)(b+c)]. (7.4) It is the cross-ratio in the literature convention of the four cumulative normal flags 0,a,a+b,a+b+c. This follows by substituting the first-order products in s/tau for the two recoupling trees. It explains how geometric flag coordinates can occur on the exceptional source chart even though the leaf central parameters coalesce. A global geometric developing configuration must still be matched to the actual equivariant source, its gluing and its marked cut. Arbitrary local normal ratios do not establish that comparison. In particular (7.4) does not turn a reducible root-central character into the complete hyperbolic one or prove the selected regulator norm. ## 8. Verification and scope [The independent audit](../experiments/audit_standard_matrix_dilog_comparison.py) compares the torus-defined fusion matrix and its evaluated four-face expression at N=2,3,...,12,15. At the six odd levels it is the literal literature kernel. All four frame factors, the flip, chirp, nonzero kappa, selected source and determinant norm agree. It checks 874 root translations, 108 odd-level positive/negative charged definitions, their full integer-charge lifts, the Heisenberg commutator and the compatible cyclic-g normalization. All twelve normal source frames also match the independent leading-valuation calculation with their exact determinant phases. [Results](../experiments/standard_matrix_dilog_comparison_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_standard_matrix_dilog_comparison.py The uniform proofs are finite products, intertwinings, Fourier recurrences and invariant-unit rigidity. Their coverage overlaps existing cyclic 6j and charged matrix dilogarithm theory; no novelty is claimed. The new role in these notes is the explicit actual source, full scalar and normal lattice in the published tensor coordinates. The failed bare vertex-order prescription still needs a global source-compatible charged replacement. Equality of the selected knot period with the marked Bloch-regulator period and its all-level norm remain unproved. ## 9. The same existing fusion map at even levels There is an all-level algebraic expression, without dividing by two modulo an even N. Put q=exp(pi*i/N), lambda_0=-q. Then lambda_0^2=Q, lambda_0^N=(-1)^(N-1), Gamma_N(k)=lambda_0^(-k^2). The quadratic phase is periodic in k modulo N. Replace Q^(r k^2) in L0 by lambda_0^(k^2), and the input chirp by this Gamma_N. Equations (2.2), (2.3)--(2.4), (5.1)--(5.2) and the full normal-source calculation then hold at every N. They are exact matrices of the already defined pointed quantum-group fusion, rather than a separately chosen invariant. At odd N, lambda_0=Q^r, so the expression is exactly the literature kernel already compared. The Gaussian Fourier recurrence is now Hhat_a=(u+v lambda_0^(-1)Q^(1-a))Hhat_(a-1). Its product is one because lambda_0^N=(-1)^(N-1), proving invertibility at all levels. The same invariant-unit proof gives the exact determinant det L^(lambda_0)=delta_N, delta_N=1 for odd N, delta_N=(-1)^(N/2) for even N. (9.1) For completeness, the clock and shift determinant signs cancel in their N-dimensional tensor extensions. At u=1,v=0 the remaining boundary permutation and phase have determinant Q^(S^2), S=N(N-1)/2, which is exactly delta_N. This proves (9.1) without dropping the even-level sign. The evaluated fusion and the normal carry frame similarly have det C_eval=delta_N[t/(1-t)]^S, det C_normal=delta_N at the source. (9.2) In the scalar norm formula (4.1), replace (-1)^m by chi_N, where chi_N=(-1)^((N-1)/2) for odd N and chi_N=1 for even N. The input flip and the chirp's tensor determinant cancel at even N. All the phase factors are thus accounted for in the existing source map. The charge prescription (5.3) was read from an odd-level definition and is not asserted at even N by this observation. In particular its flattening/charge parity cannot be extended by silently treating one half modulo an even level. The all-level source expression is available for the required comparison, while the global charged construction and its selected regulator norm still require proof. The subsequent [shared face proof](shared_standard_face_gluing.md) now makes the four-face expression compatible on one affine flag chart. Its frame depends only on the ordered triangle and shared edge roots. Actual face pairings and corrected cyclic maps become fixed Gaussian matrices with retained scalar functions; the full ordered kernel includes an explicit orientation clock/shift and pointing factor. This establishes local gluing data for a specified network, while its equivariant global charges, actual source/cut and selected regulator norm still require comparison.

title: What the present notes add, and what they do not
text: # What the present notes add, and what they do not Research comparison, 26 October 2026. The user's requested direction is to identify the intrinsic period torsor and prove a uniform structural statement. Individual knot certificates are validation, not the main mechanism. This comparison distinguishes independent verification from a new mathematical construction; no novelty claim is made. **Latest target clarification.** The intended route proves Kashaev's volume growth through the quantum A-module or torsor attached to the actual invariant. The classical A-polynomial should emerge as its appropriate geometric support, with source and peripheral factors retained. Relating it to Jones is separate. The comparison with the previous work in this repo is in [the primary status, Section 0](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md#0-comparison-with-the-previous-work-in-this-repo). The auxiliary [direct classical A-period construction](a_polynomial_volume_limits.md) now supplies such a marked-root limit under a connectedness criterion, independently verified for the hyperbolic twist family. Its finite samples are not canonical; it is not presented as a standard quantum A-state or a new classical regulator theorem. Coverage for exact polynomials and volume functions includes [Guilloux--Marche, 1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395). The integer-norm construction, rounding estimate, cover product law and twist-curve algebra are independently proved in the note. The later [doubled-phase proof](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) works directly with the normalized geometric and conjugate places. It makes the unique constrained Rivin optimizer algebraic in its two multiplicative boundary phases and writes its marked volume potential as the central period of one fixed two-step Heisenberg connection. This is a refinement of the repo's earlier meridian etaleness and boundary Monge--Ampere calculation. The one-dimensional evaluation theorem in 1411.6062 has not been promoted to a multidimensional theorem by citation. The intended advance is a triangulation-independent **pointed boundary splitting module with its Heisenberg/dilogarithm period torsor**, together with its regulator comparison. It must be built on the intrinsic decorated character space, identify the literature state, and prove the requested volume statement uniformly. The current notes do not yet prove this theorem. Neither renaming a known local cover nor adding more knot examples would do so. The [whole-period rigidity note](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) adds a finite reconstruction criterion to the existing source-base and sparse-multiplicity arguments. It keeps q^N as well as M^N and their relative logarithmic connection before specializing. The root-only slice q^N=-1 is not stable under a quantum-normal derivative. Two Vandermonde inversions and level interpolation reconstruct any fixed bounded algebraic residual from mixed cyclotomic jets; a finite algebra norm extends the criterion to a chosen etale shape branch. These are elementary algebraic arguments, with no novelty claim. They provide a certificate for an already specified pointed map; they do not construct the unknown global quantum period comparison or infer its existence from Rivin's classical optimizer. The [rank-one divisor-flow theorem](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md) then removes the assumed levelwise gauge bound for a fixed split-divisor class. The full norm character detects total charge in each q-shift orbit; finite cumulative sums construct a generic rational gauge. A direct analytic discreteness argument fixes its remaining q character. The closest coverage found is cyclotomic q-curvature and parameterized generic difference-Galois groups in [Di Vizio--Hardouin, 1205.1692](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1692) and [1205.1694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1694). Only their abstracts are used for this coverage statement; none of their proofs or theorems is a premise of our restricted descent proof. A comparison line satisfying its divisor and norm hypotheses has not yet been constructed for the actual selected knot period. The same note now proves an extension to moving algebraic zeros and poles, unramified near q=1 and satisfying a finite nonresonance condition on their limiting values. An elementary independence lemma for c^N times meromorphic functions of 1/N separates their power sums; Newton identities and analytic discreteness force integral q-shift pairings. Unique finite divisor flow gives rational descent from the splitting field. No general q-curvature proof is imported. An explicit coefficient with identity curvature at every selected half-root but no generic rational gauge prevents dropping the parameter and divisor hypotheses. The statewise even closed lift nevertheless gives a constructive nonzero actual annihilator over Q=q^2 by repeating the existing finite-sum proof with Q^N=1. This does not assert q-sign invariance of the old minimal ideal or identify the unknown geometric comparison line. The [full rank-one extension](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md) now removes both ramification and limiting-value assumptions for rational Q-coefficients. Its proof is written independently from finite-cover analytic root parametrization, weighted sequence uniqueness and finite orbit flows. The [additive/unipotent extension](additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.md) handles rational sources and upper triangular transport, including the Heisenberg central term. These are special cases of the broad q-curvature subject advertised by [Di Vizio--Hardouin](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1692); no novelty is claimed and no published proof is a premise of the arguments here. The abstract was checked again for coverage on 27 October 2026. Constructing and marking the actual knot/regulator comparison remains the knot-specific theorem. The [whole-source Newton transport](whole_source_newton_transport.md) also proves its weighted invariant quantum-torus algebra directly, including an exact finite-root lattice, its conductor, and the physical cut. For coverage, the torus skein/noncommutative-torus connection appears in [Frohman--Gelca](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9806107), and related Askey--Wilson, skein and R-matrix structures are surveyed in [Crampe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.14815). [Habiro's completion paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0209324) advertises cyclotomic functions determined by their root data. Only these abstracts were consulted for this coverage statement. The explicit weighted source lattice, normal cut and banded identities here are proved in the repo; no published theorem is invoked to infer their geometric support or volume norm. The [actual Newton canonical transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) adds the exact coefficient recurrence, finite actual pointing and selected whole-germ evaluation, together with an explicit quantum birational inverse. The basis and invariant-division-ring setting have existing coverage: cyclotomic expansions are discussed in [Berest--Gallagher--Samuelson](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04415), and [Fryer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5071) advertises fixed q-division rings for finite monomial automorphism groups. Only their abstracts were used for coverage here; the specific identities and source arguments are proved directly. Neither general quantum rationality nor cyclotomic interpolation by itself selects the volume branch. There is now a proved [partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) from the actual finite arrays: two framing indices remain external, and formal transverse-only contraction satisfies the same certificate and least-moment identity as the finite partial sum. This yields a certified operator with a geometric classical factor, rather than adding one to an annihilator. It does not prove the geometric factor survives the final selected framing contraction. The [independent audit](partial_geometric_support_independent_audit.md) checks that exact distinction. No Jones asymptotic or published creative-telescoping theorem is used as a premise. The subsequent [whole clock-current proof](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md) derives the Jackson difference directly from the original divided matrices and their two anchored inverse arrows. Its shifted function, endpoint polynomial, explicit head Ward correction and marked Green carry are retained before normal restriction. The [flat confluent endpoint tower](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) provides integral primitives and the exact Newton/Smith evaluation index; the [global P1/Serre construction](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md) gives a whole rational co-source comparison with the actual pairing density retained. These supply new explicit steps in this repo's source construction. Jackson calculus, confluent interpolation and Serre duality themselves are established mathematics; no novelty is claimed for them. For coverage, Kashaev's original [cyclic 6j-symbol paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147) already places the cyclic dilogarithm in the Weyl/Borel framework, and his [1995 crossing paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020) states its R-matrix link construction. Rivin's [optimization paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9907032) already connects optimization of geometric structures to hyperbolic three-manifolds. Their abstracts were checked on 27 October 2026 for this coverage statement. The new clock/source formulas are proved from the specified actual matrices; none of these abstracts or their advertised theorems proves the missing full network/current map or selected regulator norm.

title: A tame paired Fermat frame for the original whole source
text: # A tame paired Fermat frame for the original whole source 28 October 2026. Pairing the actual cap heads before changing frame removes the exponential factorial norm found in independent-head Fermat frames. The paired source, its marked dual, and a full invertible frame are explicit. The frame and inverse are uniformly bounded on one fixed central neighborhood, for every level. Conjugating the whole actual word and all currents gives a pointwise identity of the original invariant, including its full meridian family and scalar lines. This is a theorem about the selected boundary source. It does not factor the new crossing into a positive geometric tetrahedron kernel, or identify its Cartan charge with a new Pachner edge winding. ## 1. The actual charged channel and the paired source Fix N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N). On the original relative dual pair the actual Cartan is Q^(-1-D), D=a+b, 0<=a,b<=d. Its invariant channel is EXACTLY H_d=span{|j,d-j>:0<=j<=d}, D+1=N. (1) Indeed Q^(-1-D)=1 and 0<=D<=2N-2 force D=N-1. The projector onto this channel is the actual finite Cartan average, not a new positivity projection. The [original source reduction](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md) uses the input/marked corner e_+=|d,0> and ordinary output corner e_-=|0,d> in this channel. Put epsilon=a^N and delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), delta(0)=1. Take the original normalized cap frames from [the exact cap theorem](actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.md), using the SAME a on the two heads, and project their tensor product to (1). In the basis indexed by j this gives V_j(epsilon)= epsilon / [(1-Q)(Q^2 delta;Q)_j (Q delta;Q)_(d-j)], W_j(epsilon)= (Q delta;Q)_j (delta;Q)_(d-j)/N. (2) These are removable formulas at epsilon=0, with V(0)=e_+, W(0)=e_+^t, V_d=R=(1-Q delta)/(1-Q), W_d=A=epsilon/[N(1-delta)] =(1+delta+...+delta^(N-1))/N. (3) All j<d entries vanish at zero. Replacing j by d-j gives V_-,W_- with limits e_-,e_-^t. Write V_+=V,W_+=W. To derive (2), the normalized input factors are (P_hat_d)_j=a^(j+1)/[(1-Q)(Q^2 delta;Q)_j], (P_hat_0)_(d-j)=a^(d-j)/(Q delta;Q)_(d-j). Their powers multiply to a^N=epsilon. The normalized output factors have powers a^(d-j) and a^(-(d-j)), which cancel. This proves central descent directly, including the exact affine charge. It also proves equality with the original corners at zero. No assertion that epsilon is the actual semicyclic or meridian normal parameter is needed. In the fixed old current frame, F_rel V is generally nonzero away from zero. Section 4 transports that current as well as the source; it does not silently claim V is an invariant vector of the unchanged current. ## 2. Pairing cancels the exponential factorial profiles For |epsilon|<=rho<=1/16, one has |delta-1|<=2rho/N, |1-Q^r|>=4 dist(r,N Z)/N. (4) There is an EXACT symmetry before estimating any long product: V_j=V_(d-1-j), W_j=W_(d-1-j), 0<=j<d. (5) Indeed, writing A_l=(Q delta;Q)_l, the two expressions are V_j=epsilon R/[A_(j+1)A_(d-j)] and W_j=(1-delta)A_j A_(d-j-1)/N. The symmetry swaps their two factors. It lets us estimate only j=ell-1 with ell=min(j+1,N-j-1)<=N/2. The consecutive ratios in (2) are V_(j+1)/V_j=(1-delta Q^(-j-1))/(1-delta Q^(j+2)), W_(j+1)/W_j=(1-delta Q^(j+1))/(1-delta Q^(-j-2)). (6) Their unperturbed magnitudes telescope from j=0 to ell-1, giving |1-Q|/|1-Q^ell|<=pi/(2ell). Each normalized factor at root distance s<=ell has relative error at most rho/(2s), so its logarithmic magnitude changes by at most rho/s. The numerator and denominator errors therefore sum to at most 2rho(1+log ell), with NO log N loss. Moreover V_0=(1-delta)/(1-Q), W_0=epsilon/[N(1-delta Q^-1)], |V_0|,|W_0|<=|epsilon|/2. Combining these statements gives the uniform tail estimate |V_j|,|W_j| <= (pi |epsilon|/4) exp(2rho) ell_j^(-1+2rho), j<d. (7) At rho=1/16 the squared power is -7/4. Every ell occurs at most twice, and sum_(ell>=1)ell^(-7/4)<=1+4/3. Hence the total off-corner squared norm is less than .015. Together with |R|<=1+rho/2 and |A|<=1+rho, this proves sup_(|epsilon|<=1/16) ||V_+/-||_2,||W_+/-||_2<=3 (8) for EVERY N. In fact the displayed estimates give norms below 1.1. The simple bound 3 suffices for all subsequent constants. This fixed CENTRAL disc corresponds to |a|=(1/16)^(1/N), near one, rather than the individual-head micro-collar |a|<=1/(16N). The Cartan-charge pairing is essential to the cancellation. More precisely ||V-e_+|| and ||W-e_+^t|| are O(|epsilon|), uniformly in N on this disc. This includes the endpoints by (3). The same holds in the reversed orientation. ## 3. The exact paired normalizer is a known algebraic unit The full paired value is G(epsilon)=W V = R (2-epsilon)/(1+delta) = R (1+delta^N)/(1+delta). (9) For a direct proof, for j<d put r=j+1 and multiply (2): W_j V_j = epsilon(1-delta)R / [N(1-delta Q^r)(1-delta Q^-r)]. The missing endpoint is W_dV_d=RA. The finite root identity sum_(r=0)^(N-1) 1/[(1-delta Q^r)(1-delta Q^-r)] = N(1+delta^N)/[(1-delta^N)(1-delta^2)] (10) follows by multiplying the two convergent geometric series first for |delta|<1, taking the root sum, and then rational continuation. Subtract its r=0 term. Its contribution exactly cancels RA, giving (9). Removable values extend the calculation to zero. On |epsilon|<=1/16, R and G are bounded units: for example |R-1|<=rho/2 and |G-1|<1/8. In particular G(0)=1. This scalar is computed from the known source alone. It is NOT a normalization by an unknown knot period. Its entire factor (2-epsilon)/(1+delta) must be retained. Equation (9) also holds for W_-V_-. It does not normalize the cross-oriented pairing W_-V_+, which vanishes at zero. Dividing by that latter pairing would destroy the ordinary zero-dimensional cup-cap behavior and is not permitted here. For real 0<epsilon<1, there is also an exact positive Hermitian structure. Reflection of complementary root factors gives W=(A/conjugate(R)) V^*, W/G=V^*/||V||^2, ||V||^2=|R|^2(2-epsilon)/[(1+delta)A]. (9a) For j<d, use conjugate((Q delta;Q)_(j+1))= epsilon/[(1-delta)(Q delta;Q)_(d-j-1)] and the analogous identity for d-j. Substitution in (2) proves (9a); the endpoint follows from (3). Hence V W/G is an ORTHOGONAL rank-one projector on this real interval. Its diagonal is the explicit probability distribution pi_j=epsilon(1-delta^2) / [N(2-epsilon)|1-delta Q^(j+1)|^2]. (9b) This describes the paired boundary functional. Ordinary output caps have the other orientation, and the transformed word remains complex. No positivity or noncancellation of the knot scalar follows. The paired source also has a fixed-order exact cyclic equation. Let A_clk act by Q^j and let (Tf)_j=f_(j+1 mod N), so T A_clk=Q A_clk T. Direct ratios in (2), including the wrap, give [(1-delta Q^2 A_clk)T -(1-delta Q^-1 A_clk^-1)] V=0, W[(1-delta Q^-1 A_clk^-1)T^-1 -(1-delta Q A_clk)]=0. (9c) The two finite operators have different ordering, as the actual marked co-source requires. Their regular classical symbol is the Gaussian relation p=-A_clk^-1. The dilogarithmic factorial profiles cancel in this paired boundary relation. At A_clk=1 its factors cannot be divided out; the exact equations retain the cap wall. The [degree/cap audit](actual_degree_carry_and_cap_winding_obstruction.md) proves these ratios and their wrapped endpoint identities. ## 4. An explicit full invertible frame of uniformly bounded norm Use either matched orientation, with reference corner e and v=V_+/- , w=W_+/- /G. Then wv=1 and e^t v=R!=0. Define on H_d g=v e^t+(I-vw)(I-ee^t), g^-1=I-v e^t/R+e w. (11) Direct multiplication gives g e=v, e^t g^-1=w, det g=R, g(0)=I, rank(g-I)<=2, rank(g^-1-I)<=2. (12) For instance decompose an input as ae+z with e^t z=0. The output is z+v(a-wz), and e^t applied to it determines a-wz because R!=0. This gives precisely the inverse in (11). On the disc (8), the bounds above imply the uniform estimates ||g||<=15, ||g^-1||<=8. (13) Both matrices in fact differ from the identity by O(|epsilon|), uniformly in N. They are algebraic meromorphic functions of epsilon,delta,Q, regular on the stated marked disc. Extend g by the identity on all other total-degree channels in the two-head space. This retains its norm bounds and commutes with total degree and with the actual Cartan clock. This is a full matrix frame, not only an isomorphism of one line. The construction does not assert that g commutes with the old raising and lowering currents. They are transported by the same conjugation, which is necessary for a pointed network identity. These are bounds for whole algebraic functions on an N-independent disc. They do not require truncating the source to a fixed list of Taylor coefficients or shrinking its central neighborhood. The norm is the fixed Euclidean norm in the original relative-head basis of the exact Rogers presentation. Conjugating back by a physical fusion matrix C_x need not preserve these estimates; that separate matrix can be exponentially conditioned. The new source frame adds no exponential cost within this specified exact presentation, and the scalar equality in Section 5 is independent of the metric. ## 5. Pointwise transport of the whole original arbitrary-plat invariant Use the literal original fused word B_beta, with EVERY degree channel retained, and its known source formula P_(beta,N)=chi_beta N^(1-k) <e_out|B_beta|e_in>. (14) At each chosen horizontal slice form a tensor product Gamma of the paired frames (11), extended off H_d as above. For an actual letter or coupon O between consecutive slices use O'=Gamma_next O Gamma_previous^-1. (15) The actual currents, sewing maps, projectors, and any other insertions use the same prescription. Internal frames cancel exactly, giving B'_beta=Gamma_out B_beta Gamma_in^-1. At the boundary use the original input orientation e_+ on each pair, the ordinary output e_- on k-1 pairs, and the marked output e_+ on the remaining pair. Then, POINTWISE in every allowed auxiliary parameter, P_(beta,N)=chi_beta N^(1-k) (tensor_out W_sigma/G) B'_beta (tensor_in V_+). (16) This follows from (12), not from a limiting argument or a proposed triangulation invariant. The original full meridian dependence and original scalar lines remain those of B_beta and chi_beta. With unnormalized output rows W, retain the explicit additional factor product_out G^-1 in (16). No cross-oriented source pairing is divided out. No independent head coherent frame H or M is substituted for g. Those frames have the exponential norms proved in the four-line note; the present paired, charge-preserving frame has the different explicit bounds (13). For a fixed bridge number its tensor norms remain bounded independently of N. At an actual input dual pair, (15) carries F_rel to a current annihilating V_+ exactly, since F_rel e_+=0. For an ordinary OUTPUT the sided identity is (W_-/G)F'_rel=0, because e_-^t F_rel=0. The marked output is not an ordinary Hopf cap. Thus the relevant auxiliary completion's Ward defect is resolved by an explicit full current transport. This does not identify epsilon with a semicyclic normal parameter, nor turn intermediate non-dual pairs into dual ones. ## 6. Normal residue corrections have uniformly bounded source cost For completeness, the paired source also supplies an exact finite-jet regularization of singular terms. With one common central variable set J(epsilon)=V(epsilon)W(epsilon), or use its explicit normalized version J/G. These rank-one kernels have uniformly bounded trace norm on (8). Hence ||[epsilon^r]J||_1 <=9*16^r. (17) For an actual matrix expansion O(epsilon)=sum_(r=-p)^infinity O_r epsilon^r with fixed pole order, the paired constant-term functional is exactly CT tr(OJ)=sum_(r=0)^p tr(O_(-r) J_r), |CT tr(OJ)|<=9 sum_(r=0)^p 16^r ||O_(-r)||. (18) The normalized kernel has another absolute constant. Independent input and output central parameters, or a fixed number of pairs, give the corresponding product Cauchy bounds. Central descent of the paired source is proved in Section 1; descent or bounded deck support of a transformed operator must still be checked. Equations (17)--(18) specify a linear regularization which agrees with the original cap on every assembled holomorphic word. It preserves any exact meromorphic matrix identity to which it is applied on one common domain. They do not assert that every singular summand has the same value as an older independent-head residue prescription. Such a comparison retains its actual Ward/sewing corrections. The stronger pointwise identity (16) does not depend on making that termwise identification. ## 7. What remains on the main critical path The original paired source is now represented by a genuine tame pointed frame, with its affine charge, dual scalar and currents all explicit. This is the part of boundary transport proved here. The new crossing in (15) has not been identified with the positive geometric tetrahedron kernels. The three angular clocks of a Pachner edge have not been proved to represent the charge D+1. In particular (16) neither removes the certified oversized weak alias face nor proves that the geometric scalar survives. A nonzero bulk component of V can still cancel against the exact transformed kernel. The general volume conjecture remains open. The independent checks are in [the paired-source audit](../experiments/audit_paired_actual_cap_source_independent.py). They compare literal two-head cap products and the actual Cartan projector, source bounds, the full normalizer, and the full frame identities. The uniform assertions follow from the proofs above.

title: A general A-operator growth bound with the cyclic source retained
text: # A general A-operator growth bound with the cyclic source retained Research note, 27 October 2026. This gives a one-sided exponential estimate for the original pointed period, under explicit conditions on a specified actual quantum A-operator. The proof allows eigenvalue collisions, nonnormal matrices and exactly vanishing leading columns. It uses the finite jet source, rather than assuming a regular growing solution of a classical recurrence. There is no bridge-number bound. The estimate is an upper bound, not the volume conjecture. Its classical largest-root integral can be strictly larger than the selected period's rate. Sections 6--7 make that limitation explicit. ## 1. The Bloch boundary relation forces roots of unity at a leading edge This general algebraic property already follows from our marked Bloch relation; no published K-theory proof is needed here. On the function field of a geometric gluing curve, or a finite augmented cover of its peripheral curve, the existing calculation gives sum_j epsilon_j z_j wedge (1-z_j)=-2 M wedge L in wedge^2(F^* tensor Q). (1.1) For a discrete valuation v and units after uniformizer extraction, define the multiplicative residue tau_v(f,g)=(-1)^(v(f)v(g)) [f^v(g)/g^v(f)]_residue. (1.2) It is multiplicative in each input, and alternating after tensoring the target with Q. Directly tau_v(z,1-z)=1: when v(z)>0 the residue of 1-z is 1; when v(1-z)>0 that of z is 1; when v(z)<0 the quotient z/(1-z) has residue -1, and the two sign exponents sum to v(z)^2+v(z), which is even. The remaining unit case is immediate. Thus (1.2) applied to (1.1) makes tau_v(M,L) torsion. At a place where M has finite nonzero residue M_0 and L has a pole, this says that M_0^v(L) is a root of unity. Hence M_0 is a root of unity. If the valuation is first defined on the peripheral curve, extend it to the finite gluing field; the valuation order is multiplied by its positive ramification index and the same conclusion follows. This keeps the marked lifts. Every nonzero root of the leading L coefficient of a geometric A-factor gives a point (M_0,infinity) of its projective closure. A place on the normalization above that point has v(M)=0 and v(L)<0, so the preceding argument applies. The same conclusion holds in the squared meridian Y=M^2. Thus that leading coefficient has only roots of unity in C^*, apart from its Laurent monomial. This is the leading-edge part of the usual temperedness property. This proof concerns the geometric peripheral factor supported by (1.1). It does not identify a given actual quantum operator's classical symbol with that factor, remove additional operator factors, or prove a quantum deformation is unramified. ## 2. Conditions for a source-preserving growth estimate Use a specified even-meridian actual all-level annihilator A=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,Y) T^i, T Y=q^2 Y T, Y=M^2, a_i in C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. (2.1) Even descent for the original state was proved in [the signed norm note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md). Clear denominators and remove a common power of q-1. Assume: 1. a_0(1,Y) and p(1,Y), p=a_d, are nonzero Laurent polynomials. 2. Every zero of p(1,Y) on |Y|=1 is a root of unity. 3. Near each such zero zeta the zero divisor of p(q,Y) splits into analytic branches Y=lambda_r(q), lambda_r(1)=zeta, with multiplicity allowed. Its local remaining factor is a unit. The third condition holds for simple classical roots, and for products of the usual binomials 1-zeta q^a Y^b. It is a genuine condition: a ramified Puiseux branch is not silently treated as analytic. Roots away from the unit circle require no such condition. The theorem does not claim these conditions for every knot's unknown minimal operator. They are directly checkable operator data. Let A_cl(Y,L)=sum a_i(1,Y)L^i and, outside the finite leading-zero set, let R(theta)=max{|L|:A_cl(exp(i theta),L)=0}, E(A)=integral_0^(2pi) log R(theta) dtheta. (2.2) The logarithmic singularities at the excluded finite set are integrable, as shown in Section 5. No selected source is replaced by a choice of the largest root in the definition of the invariant. **Pointed growth theorem.** Under conditions 1--3, the original Kashaev value recovered from this actual operator satisfies limsup_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| <= E(A). (2.3) Zero values on the left are interpreted as log 0=-infinity. For the positive pointed Gram period of the previous note, limsup_(N->infinity) (pi/N)log G_N <= max(0,E(A)). (2.4) We prove these statements below. Neither is an equality assertion. ## 3. A fixed-size positive transport keeps every singular step Use the exact generic color recurrence and bounded q-jet budget B from [the pointed Gram construction](pointed_a_gram_period.md). Write V_j=(C_j,...,C_(j+d-1))^t. Before specializing any root, p(q,q^(2j)) V_(j+1)=N_j(q) V_j, (3.1) where N_j has p on its superdiagonal and last row (-a_0,...,-a_(d-1)), evaluated at Y=q^(2j). Put q=q_N(1+t) and use the scaled variable s=N t. Let K_(N,j) be the lower Toeplitz lift of N_j(q_N(1+s/N)) through s-degree B. Its size is d(B+1), independent of N, and its entries are uniformly bounded. Let m_j be the actual order of p(q,q^(2j)) at q_N and define eta_j=[s^m_j]p(q_N(1+s/N),q_N^(2j)(1+s/N)^(2j)), beta_N=sum_(j=j_*)^(N-d)m_j <= B. (3.2) The fixed small-color jet column u_N is bounded. Multiplying (3.1) in the generic field and only then taking the indicated coefficient gives the exact formula <K>_N=e_(beta_N,d)^t K_(N,N-d)...K_(N,j_*)u_N / product_j eta_j. (3.3) Indeed the unlifted numerator is (product_j p_j)V_(N-d+1). The product has first nonzero s-coefficient product_j eta_j in degree beta_N, and the color column is regular. Thus (3.3) does not divide by a vanishing specialized leading coefficient. There is an exact positive transport of its squared norm. With rho_0=u_N u_N^dagger propagate rho_(j+1)=K_(N,j) rho_j K_(N,j)^dagger, |<K>_N|^2=Tr(E_(beta_N,d)rho_final) /product_j |eta_j|^2. (3.4) The last effect is its specified rank-one coordinate projector. All phases and jet couplings remain in the matrices and source. This is a positive matrix transport, not an entrywise-positive recurrence or a license to drop the source. The denominator is the same whole leading germ used in the original A-period. ## 4. The leading germ has a controlled logarithmic product Under conditions 2--3 one has sum_j log|eta_j|=N I_p+O(log N), I_p=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi)log|p(1,exp(i theta))|dtheta. (4.1) Here is a proof retaining exact root zeros. Away from a fixed neighborhood of the classical unit-circle zeros, p(q_N,Y)/p(1,Y) is uniformly 1+O(1/N). Near a zero zeta, each analytic root branch moves by O(1/N). At grid points with distance at least K/N from zeta, choose K large enough so the root displacement is less than half that distance. Factoring locally gives a log-modulus error O(1/(N distance)). Summation over these points costs O(log N). Only a bounded number of points lie within K/N of zeta. Because zeta is a root of unity, write zeta=exp(2pi i a/r). On each residue class of N modulo r, every such point is j=aN/r+k, Y_j=zeta q_N^(2k), (4.2) where k is in a fixed finite set of rational numbers; use both endpoint representations a/r=0,1 when zeta=1. Its ordinary value is a fixed analytic germ p(q,zeta q^(2k)) at q=1. Unless identically zero, that germ has a finite order, so its nonzero value at q_N is bounded above and below by powers of N. For an exactly zero value use the q-jet along the actual color trajectory. A coefficient of fixed jet degree is a finite sum of terms c zeta^b q_N^(u+2bk) N^(-m) binom(u+2b(aN/r+k),m). (4.3) Here u is the q-exponent of the monomial and b its Y-exponent. Formula (4.3) is meromorphic in 1/N with a finite-order pole or zero. The finite-monomial Vandermonde bound from the jet theorem bounds the first nonzero degree m. For each of the finitely many residue classes and offsets, that leading coefficient is therefore bounded above and below by powers of N for all sufficiently large N. If all bounded-degree germs vanished identically, their evaluations would violate that Vandermonde bound on every large actual trajectory. Thus exact zeros, including coalescing analytic branches, cost only O(log N) at this bounded number of points. The fixed discarded initial and final colors have the same control. Finally the classical grid product itself has the claimed mean. Factor p(1,Y) over C. Off-circle roots contribute N times their circle mean plus O(1), by the identity product_(Y^N=1)(Y-lambda) =(-1)^N(lambda^N-1). A unit-circle root of unity either has zeta^N!=1, giving a nonzero value in a finite set, or is a grid root. In the latter case omitting its zero factor gives modulus N by differentiating Y^N-1 at zeta. Multiplicities and the fixed removed points add O(log N). Combining these facts proves (4.1). The analytic-branch condition is used exactly in the O(1/N) displacement above. Classical temperedness alone does not prove it. In particular, if p(1,Y) is a Laurent monomial times cyclotomic factors with leading scalar of modulus one, then I_p=0. The entire product of leading germs is then bounded above and below by powers of N. Individual factors may still vanish or become numerical multipliers at a root. Their complete germs, rather than those separate numerical values, give this conclusion. ## 5. A direct upper bound for slowly varying matrix products We need only the following elementary norm lemma. Suppose bounded matrices K_(N,j) tend uniformly to a continuous matrix K(x), x=j/N, of fixed dimension. If log rho(K(x)) is integrable, then limsup (1/N)log||product_j K_(N,j)|| <=integral_0^1 log rho(K(x)) dx. (5.1) For completeness first fix epsilon>0 and set a(x)=rho(K(x))+epsilon. The matrix H(x)=sum_(n>=0)(K(x)^dagger)^n K(x)^n/a(x)^(2n) converges uniformly, is continuous, satisfies H>=I and is bounded above on the compact interval. Uniform convergence follows, for example, by unitary triangularization: bounded upper triangular matrices of fixed size have power growth bounded by a fixed polynomial times (rho+epsilon/2)^n, uniformly with constants depending on epsilon and the dimension. Its induced norm obeys ||K(x)v||_(H(x))<=a(x)||v||_(H(x)). Uniform convergence of K_(N,j) and uniform continuity of H make each step cost at most a(j/N)+o(1), and the change between the two neighboring H norms costs 1+o(1), uniformly. Multiplying, taking logarithms, and dividing by N yields integral log(rho+epsilon). Let epsilon decrease to zero. In the present application integrability and the passage to that limit follow from the polynomial lower bound on rho stated below. No diagonalization through an eigenvalue collision and no spectral-gap hypothesis enters this upper bound. For our lifted matrices the limit K(x) is lower triangular in jet degree, with the same diagonal block at every degree: N_0(x)=[0 p 0 ...; ...; -a_0 -a_1 ... -a_(d-1)] at q=1,Y=exp(2pi i x). Therefore rho(K(x))=rho(N_0(x)). Where p!=0 its eigenvalues are p(1,Y)L_i(Y), so log rho(K(x))=log|p(1,Y)|+log R(2pi x). (5.2) Both sides are integrable. Indeed the characteristic coefficients of N_0 are a_i p^(d-1-i), and a_0 p^(d-1) is nonzero by condition 1. Their finite-order zeros give a polynomial lower bound on rho near its finitely many possible zeros. This justifies the limiting norm argument as well as the integral in (2.2). Apply (5.1) to (3.3). The input is bounded, the selected coordinate has norm one, and (4.1) subtracts I_p from the growth rate. Equation (5.2) gives (2.3). The polynomial ordinary-color remainder in the Gram theorem then gives (2.4). This proves the pointed upper bound. ## 6. The source prevents turning this bound into a volume formula An exact countercheck is the unknot with the actual annihilator (T-c)(T-1), c>1, C_j(q)=1 for every color. All conditions above hold. The entropy is E=2pi log c, but the selected period is identically one and has zero rate. Its source is entirely in the L=1 line; the positive evolution (3.4) retains this fact. The same left multiplication can be applied to an actual hyperbolic knot operator and can enlarge E arbitrarily without changing its pointed period. Thus source reachability and a sharp estimate cannot be inferred from root moduli alone. Even full classical temperedness does not fix this source issue. Let C(Y,L) be the figure-eight geometric polynomial displayed below, and form the dummy left factor C(Y,T). The operator C(Y,T)(T-1) is an actual annihilator of the unknot's constant period. Its classical symbol is (L-1)C(Y,L), whose edge polynomials are cyclotomic, yet its selected period is still one. This is not claimed to be a standard quantum figure-eight operator; it is an exact countercheck on any argument using only the tempered characteristic polynomial and omitting the actual source. There is also a useful geometric calibration. For the figure-eight geometric polynomial in Y,L, A_geo=L^2-(Y^2-Y-2-Y^(-1)+Y^(-2))L+1, put c(theta)=1+cos theta-cos(2theta). Then log R is arcosh c(theta) on (0,2pi/3) and (4pi/3,2pi), and is zero on the remaining arc. Hence E(A_geo)=2 integral_0^(2pi/3)arcosh c(theta)dtheta =2 Vol(4_1). (6.1) The last equality is the already calibrated [classical cone/regulator comparison (historical context omitted)](quantum_a_volume.md), not an identification of that note's custom transfer state with Kashaev. This factor of two shows why the full-circle largest-root integral is not the desired selected volume. The quantum boundary and resonance data must choose the appropriate action; (2.3) does not prove that selection or its lower bound. ## 7. Coverage and remaining scope The leading-edge root-of-unity statement has existing coverage in [Cooper--Culler--Gillet--Long--Shalen, Proposition 5.10](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~culler/papers/PlaneCurves/curves.pdf). The direct residue proof in Section 1 uses only our recorded Bloch boundary relation. Existing regular q-difference asymptotics include [Garoufalidis--Geronimo](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405331), whose abstract specifies noncollision and nonvanishing assumptions. Only their stated scope was used for coverage; none of their proofs is a premise for Sections 3--5. The new step relative to the previous repo notes is a one-sided estimate for the actual pointed A-period that retains the complete cyclic leading germ, a bounded number of singular jets, and its fixed source, while allowing eigenvalue collisions. It requires the explicit leading-divisor hypotheses in Section 2. It neither proves those hypotheses for every knot operator nor proves a sharp geometric rate. Identifying and estimating the source-selected geometric action is still the central unresolved part of the volume conjecture. [Audit](../experiments/audit_tempered_a_growth.py). [Results](../experiments/tempered_a_growth_results.json).

title: Tetrahedral order changes and a calibrated figure-eight move
text: # Tetrahedral order changes and a calibrated figure-eight move Research note, 25 October 2026. The definitions are the Gaussian kernels and charged operators of Andersen–Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), Sections 4–7. We reconstruct the needed symmetries from the independently proved Fourier formula, rather than assuming the source's Fundamental Lemma or its global invariance theorem. The phase conventions are those of `peripheral_phase_and_state.md`. This note calibrates an actual move between the three-tetrahedron twist-family realization of 4_1 and the two-tetrahedron realization used for its audited minimal annihilator. Its statement is for generic boundary x, before setting the complete value x=0. Throughout, b>0, h=(b+b^(-1))^(-2), and q=exp(2pi i b^2). ## 1. Coherent changes of triangle ordering Define the published kernels A(x,y)=delta(x+y)exp[pi i(x^2+1/12)], B(x,y)=exp[pi i(x-y)^2]. As operators, A is reflection followed by a unit-modulus chirp, and B=M_+ Fourier M_+, where M_+(x)=exp(pi i x^2) and Fourier has kernel exp(-2pi i xy). Thus A,B are unitary and preserve Schwartz space, with adjoints given by their conjugate symmetric kernels. These assertions do not require a quantum-dilogarithm identity. For a triangle whose orientation is reversed, identify its space with its conjugate dual using the antiunitary maps R_A=A conjugation and R_B=B conjugation. They represent its two adjacent vertex transpositions. Indeed R_A^2=R_B^2=1. Their product is the linear operator V=A B^*, V(x,y)=exp(pi i/12)exp(-pi i y^2-2pi i xy). Completing a square in the middle integral of V^2 supplies the Fresnel factor exp(-pi i/4). The third product leaves delta(x-y), with total scalar exp(3pi i/12-pi i/4)=1. Therefore V^3=1. The two involutions and this relation give an *exact* representation of S_3, with the odd permutations antiunitary because they reverse orientation. In particular, the triangle basis change is determined by its vertex permutation, independently of a chosen word. The pi/12 in A is essential to this scalar calculation. All Fresnel and plane-wave integrals here can be regularized by a positive Gaussian. Their limits are the ordinary Fourier delta and Fresnel integral with the displayed normalization, not unspecified projective equalities. ## 2. The three tetrahedral generators Use a,beta,c>0 with a+beta+c=1/2 for the charges, and write f_(a,c)(r)=exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c,beta)(r), K_(a,c)(x,y;u,v) =delta(x+y-u)f_(a,c)(v-y)exp[2pi i x(v-y)]. The Fourier and inversion identities in the pentagon audit give the following three exact kernel identities, where bars denote adjoints: integral Abar(v,s)K_(a,c)(x,s;u,t)A(t,y) dsdt =Kbar_(a,beta)(x,y;u,v), integral Abar(u,s)K_(a,c)(s,x;v,t)B(t,y) dsdt =Kbar_(beta,c)(x,y;u,v), integral Bbar(u,s)K_(a,c)(s,y;t,v)B(t,x) dsdt =Kbar_(a,beta)(x,y;u,v). (2.1) Here is a direct verification, including the possible convergence issue. Put r=v-y. In the first identity the two A delta functions set s=-v,t=-y. On x=u+v, its coefficient reduces to exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c,beta)(r)exp[pi i r(r+2u)]. In the second identity the A delta sets s=-u and the tetrahedron delta gives x=u+v. After shifting t by x, its remaining integral is precisely Fourier inversion of the Schwartz function psi_(a,c); its coefficient is the same expression with psi_(a,c) in place of psi_(c,beta). This integral is absolutely convergent. In the third identity the tetrahedron delta sets t=s+y. Its quadratic terms cancel and the last integral is integral exp[2pi i s(u+v-x)]ds=delta(u+v-x). With exp(-pi epsilon s^2) inserted, the left side is epsilon^(-1/2)exp[-pi(u+v-x)^2/epsilon], so the distributional limit has coefficient exactly 1. The remaining smooth coefficient is again the first displayed expression. The defining inversion and conjugation formula for psi identifies these three expressions with their claimed adjoint kernels. There is no extra phase in (2.1). These are precisely the adjacent tetrahedral vertex swaps (01),(12),(23). The charges transform respectively as (a,beta,c)->(a,c,beta), (beta,a,c), (a,c,beta). The first swap changes the first two vertices in its incident faces 2,3, so it uses A on both. The middle swap uses A on face 0 and B on face 3. The last uses B on faces 0,1. This identifies the operators with actual face vertex permutations. Section 1 makes their compositions coherent; their actions on opposite edge pairs and on face labels are the ordinary permutation actions of S_4. The identities for a negative tetrahedron are the adjoints of (2.1). ## 3. Gluing through these order changes For a face and its oppositely oriented copy, simultaneous changes of basis preserve the pairing. For an even permutation this is unitarity; for an odd one, the bra and ket are interchanged as well as conjugated. Internal face adapters therefore cancel. A non-order-preserving intermediate face gluing is represented by its unique S_3 adapter from Section 1, rather than being silently replaced by an increasing vertex map. For the proper contractions of the previous notes this cancellation has a direct regularized justification. A paired B and B^* integration gives integral exp(-pi epsilon x^2) B(x,t)Bbar(x,s) dx =exp[pi i(t^2-s^2)]epsilon^(-1/2) exp[-pi(t-s)^2/epsilon]. It tends to delta(t-s); paired A kernels give that delta directly. After the independent face constraints are eliminated, invertibility of the original full face matrix lets one use the N dynamical arguments and the adapter errors t-s as independent coordinates. The dynamical functions are Schwartz, and the errors have normalized Gaussian weights. Rescale each error by sqrt(epsilon). Translations of the dynamical coordinates preserve their L1 norms, and their Schwartz bounds justify dominated convergence. Quadratic chirps have modulus one. The same argument applies to the plane-wave delta in the third rule (2.1). Thus changing face frames inside a finite proper contraction preserves its value, with these prescribed limits. This argument does not claim that an arbitrary trace of a bounded operator is trace class. Properness and the explicit Gaussian resolution supply the needed finite-dimensional justification here. One may consequently put a positive bipyramid into the canonical pentagon ordering, apply the audited identity, and return to the desired boundary orders. When both endpoint face contractions are proper, this gives their tensor identity with its retained pentagon scalar. It is unnecessary to assume that the intermediate canonical vertex order extends to one global branching of the closed triangulation. ## 4. The actual figure-eight bipyramid Start with the p=0 even twist face family: U=(r,v,s,g), V=(s,g,e,u), W=(u,v,r,e), signs=(+,-,-). Its degree-three edge has local representatives U_02,V_03,W_02. The incident internal faces are v,g,e. Gluing only these faces, before any boundary identification, gives the following five-vertex bipyramid: | Tetrahedron | Global vertices at its local 0,1,2,3 | Canonical local order | Pentagon label | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | U | (1,0,3,4) | (1,0,2,3) | 2 | | V | (1,2,0,3) | (2,0,1,3) | 0 | | W | (1,2,3,4) | (0,1,2,3) | 4 | The apices are 1,3 and the equator vertices are 0,2,4. All three canonical signs are negative, so this is the *adjoint* pentagon, not the original all-positive operator word. The remaining boundary faces r,s,u retain their original vertex maps. Replace the three tetrahedra by canonical tetrahedra 1=(0,1,2,4) and 3=(0,2,3,4), sharing their equatorial face h. Their face tuples are (r,h,s,u), (u,r,h,s). To obtain increasing face maps, reorder their vertices by (0,1,3,2) and (0,3,1,2), respectively. The result is X_2: (r,h,u,s), (u,s,r,h), signs=(+,-). (4.1) The boundary maps, including the nontrivial intermediate one, are computed from the original pairings in the script. In the canonical ordering the u gluing has full permutation (3,1,2,0); its induced triangular permutation is a cyclic rotation. It must be carried by the corresponding V or V^2 adapter. The coherent triangle rules account for it exactly. After the two reorders above all four face maps are increasing. This is a 3–2 replacement of the embedded abstract ball before boundary pairing, so it identifies the same knot exterior. Optional Regina checks recognize (4.1) as the standard two-tetrahedron figure-eight triangulation; the homeomorphism argument does not rely on that finite recognition. ## 5. Full angle and peripheral transport Write the old physical triples as (a_U,b_U,c_U), and similarly for V,W. The old canonical charges are half the following angles divided by pi: a_0=b_V/(2pi), c_0=a_V/(2pi), a_2=a_U/(2pi), c_2=b_U/(2pi), a_4=a_W/(2pi), c_4=c_W/(2pi). The balanced edge equations give c_2=c_0+a_4+a_0+c_4. All five free charges are positive and 1/2-(a_0+a_2+a_4+c_0+c_4)=c_U/(2pi)>0. Thus the entire positive angle space lies in the convergent charged pentagon chamber; no continuation through a pole is being assumed. In the ordered triangulation (4.1), the new triples are a'_1=a_U+b_V, b'_1=a_V+a_W, c'_1=pi-a_U-b_V-a_V-a_W, a'_2=b_V+c_W, b'_2=a_U+a_W, c'_2=pi-a_U-a_W-b_V-c_W. (5.1) They are positive, and both new edge weights are 2pi. The new face and peripheral matrices are exactly Q_f=diag(1,-1), H=diag(1/2,-1), A=[[1,-2],[0,4]], B=[[-1,-1],[0,2]], nu/pi=(-1,2), c_0/pi=(1,-1), p=(-1,1). Here the standard peripheral holonomies are mu_2=a'_1-a'_2, lambda_2=2(a'_2-b'_2). Pulling back (5.1) gives, on the entire old balanced angle space, mu_2=-mu_3, lambda_2=-lambda_3. (5.2) The old meridian and preferred longitude are independently certified in the topological note. The bipyramid homeomorphism transports them; cusp angle holonomy is preserved by the corresponding diagonal changes on its vertex links. Identity (5.2), with zero constant branch correction, records the resulting orientation convention. Matching the old curves therefore uses the negative of the displayed new longitude row, giving p=(1,-1) and the same c_0=(pi,-pi). This reverses the fiber variable and changes the printed prefactor: the matched state is -J_2(h,-x). ## 6. The exact phase certificate and state identity Use K_X from the peripheral-phase note. The adjoint pentagon multiplier is exp(i rho/h), where rho=pi P/12, P=(a_V+a_U+c_W)/pi-1/2. Direct substitution of (5.1) into the two K polynomials gives K_2-K_3+rho=11pi/12. (6.1) This identity holds for every balanced angle vector. In particular its longitude slope is zero. The script checks all coefficients on the four-dimensional affine angle space, not one special geometric point. For matched peripheral orientations the two coarea orientation signs are both -1, and N_2-N_3=-1. Applying the exact transform formula and its uniqueness theorem consequently gives J_3(h,x)=-exp[-pi i/12+11pi i/(12h)]J_2(h,-x). (6.2) Here J_3,J_2 are the literal printed FAMED states with the chosen eliminated coordinates: U for J_3 and the first tetrahedron for J_2. Use the increasing lexicographic face-label orders of the scripts; the corresponding face determinants are +1 and -1. Their p_1^2 factors are both 1. The equality is on their common horizontal holomorphic band around the complete meridian. Positive angle chambers overlap under (5.1), so the Fourier–Laplace comparison has an open longitude interval and requires no extrapolation from a complete-point test. ## 7. Reflection and the same selected minimal operator There is also an orientation-preserving automorphism of (4.1): interchange its two tetrahedra, with vertex maps (1,3,0,2), (2,0,3,1). These commute with every actual face pairing. Their induced angle map interchanges the tetrahedra and swaps a,b in each. The peripheral action is (mu,lambda)->(-mu,-lambda), and direct substitution on the full balanced angle space gives K(alpha')=K(alpha). Tetrahedral equivariance and the same transform uniqueness therefore show J_2(h,x)=J_2(h,-x). (7.1) Thus (6.2) is also an exact scalar equivalence at the same boundary x. Both the reflection and its scalar normalization were proved for the selected integrals, not inferred from a reciprocal classical A-polynomial. For clarity the known minimal order-two operator of J_2, in the natural Andersen–Malusà b-shift convention, has coefficients R=q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-qQ+1, b_0=q^2 Q^2(q^3 Q^2-1), b_1=q^(1/2)(q^2 Q^2-1)R, b_2=q^3 Q^2(q Q^2-1). The previous Ore and minimality proofs concern this same literature state after its recorded scalar gauge. Reflection sends (Q,E) to (Q^(-1),E^(-1)). Left multiplication by E^2 returns nonnegative shift degrees; its exact coefficient identity is b_(2-k)(q^(-2)Q^(-1))=-q^(-6)Q^(-6)b_k(Q), k=0,1,2. Only this Laurent monomial unit is removed. All nonmonomial peripheral factors, including those vanishing at the complete value, remain. Equation (6.2) now proves that the three- and two-tetrahedron states have the same primitive minimal operator and the same volume law. No colored Jones polynomial or arbitrarily chosen recurrence solution enters this comparison. ## 8. Checks and remaining scope Run `.venv/bin/python experiments/audit_figure_eight_move.py --regina` for the exact combinatorial, entire-angle-space, phase, reflection and operator certificates and the optional independent triangulation recognition. Without Regina use `python3 experiments/audit_figure_eight_move.py`. The independent integral comparison is in `python3 experiments/compare_figure_eight_realizations.py`. The latter compares four generic/complete boundary cases at two b values, using tensor Hermite orders 256 and 384. Its maximum relative discrepancy from (6.2) is below 1.2e-12, with refinement difference below 3.3e-10. It also checks the evenness (7.1) independently. These are numerical diagnostics of the separately proved identities. The argument audits the ordering changes needed in this concrete positive move and provides reusable local rules for other proper positive moves. Together with the endpoint moment theorem in the peripheral-phase note, these rules give selected-state annihilator invariance along certified proper positive paths between compatible geometric endpoints. It does not supply connecting paths for arbitrary triangulations, justify every nonproper contraction, or prove geometric FAMED certificates for all alternating knots. The positive factorial comparison model still needs its own generic boundary move law; its factor-eight test is not resolved by a different model's calibrated identity.

title: One extra quantum region degree, with an exact original crossing port
text: # One extra quantum region degree, with an exact original crossing port 28 October 2026. The third classical certificate changes the region flag in the literal middle configuration. Its two projective coordinates do not form a quantum torus on the original two heads. This note constructs a genuine quantum-torus extension with one extra region degree whose **typed matrix elements** are exactly those physical coordinates. The extension has a fixed vacuum source. It also proves an exact vacuum-port formula for the other original crossing factor. A complete marked full-Phi pentagon can be applied BEFORE the auxiliary contraction; summing every intermediate index still gives that original factor and hence the original R. No knot value defines the auxiliary source. The complete developed geometric face-order table for the third certificate is not inferred from these two facts. In particular, different matrix elements are not multiplied as though compression were an algebra homomorphism. The subsequent [physical THIRD theorem](literal_third_full_phi_certificate.md) now supplies that literal face/source certificate by a different construction on the original two heads: inverse actual flag transport and opposite-root FIRST, with its full reflected input adapter. It also explains the forced degenerate clock in this auxiliary vacuum port. The auxiliary identities below remain valid; they are not used as the missing regular geometric face table. ## 1. The actual third-region coordinates Use complete original heads and marks Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1), k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1), Z=Z_1, Z_2, X=xS_2S_1^(-1), S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu, XZ=QZX, XZ_2=Q^(-1)Z_2X, X^N=Z^N=Z_2^N=1. The actual total lowering current gives the normalized last region flag in the middle configuration's homogeneous frame as R=1-n_R, n_R=(1-Z_2)X=x f_2 S_1^(-1). (1) The root binomial product gives n_R^N=0, so R is a unit. Normalizing this new region to one changes the two projective coordinates to X'=Z_2X R^(-1), Z'=1-R(1-Z). (2) Their failure to satisfy X'Z'=QZ'X' cannot be repaired by renaming them as a new quantum-torus pair. We instead retain the missing face degree explicitly. ## 2. An honest extended quantum torus Add an auxiliary head with W|j>=Q^j|j>, S|j>=|j+1>, S|d>=k|0>, WS=QSW, W^N=1, S^N=k. It commutes with the physical heads. Put a=Z_2X and A=a tensor S^(-1), B=1 tensor W-Q^(-1)1 tensor WS+Z tensor S. (3) Then exactly AB=QBA, A^N=B^N=1. (4) For the commutator, A has quantum degree one against each of the three displayed summands of B. For the central powers, a^N=k and S^N=k give A^N=1. In the displayed order the three summands of B pairwise Q-commute. Their root binomial powers give 1-S^N+Z^NS^N=1. These calculations include even and composite levels. The face normalization has a periodic quantum lift. Define U_j=P(Q^j n_R)^(-1)P(n_R) =product_(r=0)^(j-1)(1-Q^r n_R), U=sum_(j=0)^d U_j tensor |j><j|, (5) where P is the original finite Euler polynomial. Every factor is invertible since n_R is nilpotent. Moreover U_0=1, U_1=R, U_N=1. (6) Thus there is no omitted auxiliary wrap or independently chosen norm root. Let Atilde=UAU^(-1), Btilde=UBU^(-1). Its typed matrix elements are <0|Atilde|1>=Z_2X R^(-1)=X', (<0|+<1|)Btilde|0>=1-R+RZ=Z'. (7) The Q^(-1) coefficient in (3) is essential: WS sends |0> to Q|1>, so its off-diagonal contribution in (7) is exactly -R. For every physical operator O, <0|U(O tensor 1)U^(-1)|0>=O. (8) Hence this controlled face extension can be inserted with its fixed vacuum without changing an original physical operator or any of its external source conventions. The ports in (7) have different incoming/outgoing types. When words are composed one must sum every intermediate auxiliary index. Equation (4) applies before that sum. It does not assert that multiplying the two entries in (7) preserves the same commutator after compression. ## 3. An explicit quantum triangle source The simple B in (3) is not an unspecified similarity. Set L=(1-Q ZW^(-1))S, C_B=P(L). (9) Then L^N=0, B=C_B W C_B^(-1), [A,C_B]=0, <0|C_B|0>=1. (10) Indeed L W=Q^(-1)WL and the finite Euler shift gives P(L)W P(L)^(-1)=W(1-Q^(-1)L)=B. The product around its clock orbit is proportional to 1-Z^N=0. Direct commutation gives [A,L]=0. The last identity follows because fewer than N raises from input zero cannot return to zero. Thus this source has fixed augmentation one, not a normalization chosen from a knot invariant. For h<N its complete input column is <h|C_B|0>=p_h(Z;Q^(-1))_h, p_h=(-1)^hQ^(h(h-1)/2)/F_h. (11) All factors and endpoint zeros in this column remain part of the source. ## 4. The other original R factor is an exact coherent vacuum port The original crossing has R_0=D P(n_-)P(n), n=(Q-Z^(-1))X=e_1S_2, n_-=-(Q-Z^(-1))a=-e_1Z_2S_2. Set a_eff=Q a Z^(-1), e_aux=(Q-W^(-1))S^(-1), n_0=a_eff e_aux. (12) The auxiliary e_aux is a unit scalar times the literal complete nilpotent raising/lowering matrix. Then exactly P(n_-)=<0|P(n_0)C_B|0>. (13) Here the whole intermediate auxiliary sum has been performed, not suppressed. For a finite proof, the original Euler coefficient cancels the h-fold lowering matrix coefficient to give <0|P(n_0)|h>=a_eff^h. Together with (11), the right side of (13) is sum_h p_h a_eff^h(Z;Q^(-1))_h. The actual physical relations aZ=QZa imply n_-^h=a_eff^h(Z;Q^(-1))_h, which proves (13) term by term. This is an exact all-level finite q-binomial bridge from a genuine auxiliary source to the original crossing factor. The polarization factor a_eff=QaZ^(-1) is forced by this calculation and is retained explicitly. Equation (13) can be conjugated by the U of (5) on the full extended space without changing its vacuum port, since U_0=1. Thus the same source extension contains both the actual third-region coordinate ports (7) and an original-R operator port. ## 5. A full marked pentagon before the complete auxiliary contraction Use the marked full-Phi clock on the auxiliary head, with its fixed scalar and top lift: F_W=phi_N diag_j[1/F_j], phi_N=sqrt(N)exp{i pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. Let P_0=P(n_0), H_0=P_0^(-1)WP_0, and F_H0=P_0^(-1)F_WP_0. Exactly as in the literal middle identity, since n_0W=QWn_0 and its missing arrow is the actual input zero, P_0 F_H0^(-1) =F_H0^(-1)P_0 P(-n_0H_0).
