If rho(a) has eigenvalues i,-i, Cayley-Hamilton gives rho(a)^2=-I. The same is true of rho(b), since meridians are conjugate. In PSL2(C), write their images as A,B. Then A²=B²=1, and every sign in w disappears: A(BA)^m=(BA)^m B. (2) Set R=AB. Since BA=R^-1 and A R A=R^-1, (2) becomes R^m A=R^(-(m+1))A, hence R^p=1. (3) Every word in A,B reduces to R^j or R^j A. Thus the projective image has at most 2p elements. Its inverse image in SL2(C) has at most 4p elements. This applies to reducible representations as well as irreducible ones, and uses no unitarity assumption. The image is metabelian: its subgroup above <R> is cyclic (R^p=+/-I in a lift), and its commutator subgroup lies there. The preferred knot longitude lies in G'': choose a Seifert surface and express its boundary as a product of commutators of surface generators. Their push-offs have zero linking number with the knot, so each generator lies in G'. Hence rho(longitude)=I. (4) In particular all these midpoint peripheral points have L=1 in the original preferred-longitude eigenvalue convention. A changed framing must retain its meridian correction rather than reuse (4) unchanged. ## 2. The ABSOLUTE representation volume is zero A finite group of hyperbolic isometries fixes a point c in H3. One elementary construction is to sum its orbit of a future unit timelike vector in the hyperboloid model and normalize that timelike sum. Use the constant equivariant map c on a truncated core. On each cusp, choose a peripheral fixed ideal point xi and extend along the ray from c to xi, depending only on the cusp height. The ray is peripheral invariant because both endpoints are fixed. These choices extend equivariantly to all lifted cusps. Every cusp and its interpolating collar have rank at most one; the core has rank zero. The pullback of the hyperbolic volume form therefore vanishes everywhere. By the independently proved choice-independence of the [general peripheral volume](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), this is the SAME absolutely marked regulator used by the Bloch chain: R(rho)=Vol(rho)=0. (5) No additive shift of a primitive is used to arrange (5). ## 3. No character branch escapes at this meridian For an irreducible pair with M!=+/-1, put A_M=[M,1;0,M^-1], B_(M,z)=[M,0;-z,M^-1]. (6) To justify this form, choose the M-eigenline of the first meridian and the M^-1-eigenline of the second as the two coordinate lines. If they coincide the pair is reducible. Otherwise the first upper off-diagonal entry is nonzero for an irreducible pair and may be normalized to one. The remaining entry defines z. Let W be the word in (1). The top-right entry of A_M W-W B_(M,z) is P(M,z)=W_22+(M-M^-1)W_12. (7) It is a polynomial in z of degree m, with leading coefficient (-1)^m product_(j=1)^(2m) epsilon_j in {+1,-1}. (8) Here is a direct leading-term proof. Each pair B^epsilon A^delta has z-leading matrix -epsilon e_2 (M^delta,delta). Multiplying these rank-one matrices shows that W_22 has the coefficient (8), while W_12 has degree at most m-1. This proves (8), independently of M. Every actual irreducible representation satisfies P=0. On a compact M-neighborhood of +i or -i, the other coefficients are bounded Laurent polynomials in M. The elementary monic polynomial root bound then bounds z uniformly. Thus the matrices (6) have convergent subsequences at the midpoint and their limits still satisfy the full group relation. Their limits are the finite-image representations of Section 1. There is a stronger local check. At M=i, inverse meridians differ from positive meridians by -I, so W is a sign times (BA)^m. Put t=tr(AB)=-2-z and define U_0=1, U_1=t, U_(r+1)=t U_r-U_(r-1). Equation (7) becomes, up to that same sign, P(i,z)=U_m(t)-U_(m-1)(t). (9) The identity follows from the determinant-one matrix recurrence for BA, or directly from P_0=1, P_1=t-1. Its m roots are distinct: t=2 cos((2j-1)pi/p), j=1,...,m. (10) Indeed U_m(2cos theta)-U_(m-1)(2cos theta) =cos(p theta/2)/cos(theta/2), with endpoint values obtained by limits. This also follows from the finite sine-sum formula for U_m. At M=-i one obtains the same roots, since replacing M by -M negates both meridian matrices after a constant diagonal conjugation. Thus each actual local branch through the midpoint has an ordinary finite analytic representative (possibly after taking its character normalization), not an escaping Riley parameter. The monic equation is finite over C[M,M^-1]; every one-dimensional nonvertical component of the actual relation locus reaches M=i and M=-i. More explicitly, a dominating irreducible component is closed in this finite scheme, so its image is a closed dense subset of C*, hence all of C*. No assertion about a vertical component is needed for a meridian transport curve. The volume is continuous at these limits. One can check this without assuming cross-ratios stay nondegenerate: M remains away from +/-1, so the peripheral eigenlines and axis vary continuously on each local branch. Choose the axis cusp maps continuously; their volume forms vanish on the cusp. The equivariant interpolation over the fixed finite compact core varies continuously, so its finite volume integral does too. Hence every such branch has limiting marked regulator zero. Reducible representations have zero regulator throughout and cause no additional endpoint case. ## 4. Consequence for COMPLEX conversion paths Combine (5) and the finite-limit statement with the [complex peripheral action identity](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md). For any path which genuinely lifts to a connected representation/Bloch curve, starts at this midpoint and ends at unit meridian, |Im integral Log(L) dLog(M²)| <= Vol(S³ minus K). (11) Ramification points on the normalized lifted curve are allowed. For the quantum step h=2pi i/N, the corresponding exponential action has growth at most Vol/(2pi). This controls all such lifted paths for the entire hyperbolic two-bridge class, rather than selected twist examples. It does NOT prove that every contribution of the original quantum recurrence admits this path description, nor that the number and prefactors of those contributions are subexponential. Those are the remaining analytic/source requirements. ## 5. Coverage and checks The trace-free slice and binary-dihedral representations are established subjects; coverage includes [Nagasato--Yamaguchi](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.0714). No proof from that source is used here. The group reduction, monic matrix calculation, finite limit and zero-volume argument are supplied above; no novelty is claimed for the representation classification. [Audit](../experiments/audit_two_bridge_midpoint_anchor.py) checks the generic leading coefficients, actual two-bridge sign words, the trace-free polynomial recurrence, and the exact finite-order relation. The finite audit checks 84 generic sign words and 41 two-bridge midpoint sign words, including simple roots and the exact finite-order relation.

title: Two actual flow cuts give a strict matrix and coherent Green complex
text:
# Two actual flow cuts give a strict matrix and coherent Green complex Research construction, 27 October 2026. Once two actual physical edge positions a,b have been retained, their zero-extended array is one matrix with independent row and column clocks. Both finite Green currents, all boundary rows/columns/corners, and the original 1/N co-source have an exact Laurent/coherent realization. This does not identify a physical single-port Hopf action with matrix multiplication, and does not assume that the geometric Gaussian commutes with the construction. The physical existence, four-port ordering and integral flow-chart choice are supplied by [the actual two-cut reconstruction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). The second cut is an INTERNAL IDENTITY edge: no new pivot is inserted there. All original pivots, caps and scalar peripheral factors remain in the actual array. Only a diagonal transport ALREADY present on that edge may be absorbed in its definition. ## 1. The actual array, source and independent clocks Let f(a,b) be a finite zero-extended array on Z^2 over the original coefficient algebra, after the specified other finite sums. All flow constraints and their zero entries are retained. On the head window 0<=a,b<N put J_ab=f(a,b), and n=N-1. The actual selected state is head-supported, and its period is \[ \Phi(J)= rac1N\sum_{a,b=0}^{n}J_{ab}. 	ag{1} \] There is no second factor 1/N. In particular this is the original rank-one average matrix row Tr(eJ), e_ab=1/N, rather than Tr(J)/N. The matrix is a reshaped DOUBLE-DIAGONAL four-port array, not an ordinary open-knot endomorphism. No scalarity condition J=cI is imposed on it. Let A=diag(1,Q,...,Q^n). The two actual characters are exactly \[ A_1J=AJ,\qquad A_2J=JA. 	ag{2} \] Both remain independent before the final source pairing. Their whole q-germs, including Q^N, are retained before root evaluation. ## 2. Exact shifts and every boundary term Let Ue_j=e_(j+1), j<n, and Ue_n=0. Define endpoint rows and columns r_+(b)=f(N,b), r_-(b)=f(-1,b), c_+(a)=f(a,N), c_-(a)=f(a,-1), restricted to the other head index. Then literal coordinate translations have the matrix formulas \[  egin{split} \Pi S_a^+f&=U^tJ+e_n r_+,& \Pi S_a^-f&=UJ+e_0r_-,\ \Pi S_b^+f&=JU+c_+e_n^t,& \Pi S_b^-f&=JU^t+c_-e_0^t. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] Here Pi is head-window restriction; these are coordinate-array translations, not physical single-port raising/lowering actions. The endpoint rows themselves translate and have endpoints. For example \[ \Pi S_a^+S_b^+f=U^tJU+e_n r_+U+U^tc_+e_n^t +f(N,N)e_ne_n^t. 	ag{4} \] More generally choose L_+=U^t,L_-=U, R_+=U,R_-=U^t, e_+=e_n,e_-=e_0 and t_+=N,t_-=-1. Then \[ \Pi S_a^\epsilon S_b^\eta f =L_\epsilon JR_\eta+e_\epsilon r_\epsilon R_\eta +L_\epsilon c_\eta e_\eta^t +f(t_\epsilon,t_\eta)e_\epsilon e_\eta^t. 	ag{5} \] The corner term is required for the two translations to commute. Longer words keep the corresponding finite strips and corners; there is no fixed finite head matrix representation of all translations without this tail data. The co-source versions of (3) are equally explicit: \[ \Phi(\Pi(S_a^+-1)f)= rac1N\sum_{b=0}^n[f(N,b)-f(0,b)], \] \[ \Phi(\Pi(S_a^--1)f)= rac1N\sum_{b=0}^n[f(-1,b)-f(n,b)], 	ag{6} \] with the analogous two column formulas. A clock on an endpoint uses Q^N or Q^(-1), not one substituted from its root value. The exact Weyl relation S_a^+ A_1=Q A_1 S_a^+, and its three counterparts, includes these endpoint coefficients. ## 3. A whole Laurent kernel retains the tails strictly Define the finite Laurent polynomial \[ \mathscr F_f(x,y)=\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb Z}f(a,b)x^ay^b. 	ag{7} \] This map is injective and has the exact operator dictionary \[ S_a^+\leftrightarrow x^{-1},\quad S_a^-\leftrightarrow x, \quad S_b^+\leftrightarrow y^{-1},\quad S_b^-\leftrightarrow y, \] \[ A_1\leftrightarrow[x\mapsto Qx],\quad A_2\leftrightarrow[y\mapsto Qy],\quad a\leftrightarrow x\partial_x,\quad b\leftrightarrow y\partial_y. 	ag{8} \] Consequently arbitrary ordered clock/shift words and every retained polynomial Green moment are transported exactly. External meridian Ore operators act on the coefficient algebra with their original order. Q derivatives of a dilation include its Euler chain-rule term; the source's normal terms are not frozen before differentiation. If an external Ore shift changes a chosen source/basis frame L, its transported operator is L_after O sigma(L_before^(-1)), with the specified semilinear coefficient action. It is not ordinary conjugation by a frame which the Ore shift has changed. For head-supported states (1) is exactly \[ \Phi_{full}(f)= rac{\mathscr F_f(1,1)}N = rac1N\operatorname{Res}_{x=1}\operatorname{Res}_{y=1}  rac{\mathscr F_f(x,y)\,dx\,dy}{(x-1)(y-1)}. 	ag{9} \] The same expression on currents sums ALL their finite tails. It equals the head row plus the explicit outside-window sum divided by N. Thus it kills both full zero-extended differences, while (6) records exactly the boundary removed by restricting to the head. No cyclic interpretation of either actual coordinate is used. ## 4. Explicit two-current complex and its contraction Write d_x=x^(-1)-1,d_y=y^(-1)-1. The actual two-flow Green complex on finite Laurent kernels has \[ d_1(P,Q)=d_xP+d_yQ,\qquad d_2(H)=(d_yH,-d_xH),\qquad\Phi_{full}d_1=0. 	ag{10} \] All actual finite certificate identities map to this complex coefficientwise. Define P_xF=F(1,y), P_yF=F(x,1), and \[ H_xF= rac{F-P_xF}{x^{-1}-1},\qquad H_yF= rac{F-P_yF}{y^{-1}-1}. 	ag{11} \] The quotients are Laurent POLYNOMIALS: their numerator vanishes at the indicated source point. In the original array, for example, H_af(a,b)=-sum_(k>=a)[f(k,b)-delta_(k,0)sum_u f(u,b)]; this is a finite sequence. Put \[ h_0(F)=(H_xF,P_xH_yF),\qquad h_1(P,Q)=-H_xQ. 	ag{12} \] Direct substitution gives \[ d_1h_0F=F-F(1,1),\quad h_0d_1+d_2h_1=I,\quad h_1d_2=I. 	ag{13} \] Thus both currents and their common corner/syzygy have a specified finite contracting homotopy. There is no inferred Gaussian or Stokes operation in this identity. If the section is chosen as the literal matrix identity, let E_N(x,y)=sum_(a=0)^n(xy)^a, so Phi(E_N)=1, and let Gamma=h_0(E_N-N). Replace h_0 by \[ h_0^{I}(F)=h_0(F)-\Gamma\Phi_{full}(F). 	ag{14} \] Then d_1h_0^I=I-E_N Phi_full, while the other identities remain unchanged. The 1/N in the original source is therefore preserved by the pointed complex; it has not become 1/N^2. This section is a specified homotopy anchor, not a claim that every physical two-cut tangle has identity matrix. ## 5. Global P1 kernel and the literal source/co-source The core polynomial (7) has bidegree at most (n,n), hence is a section of O(n) external_tensor O(n) on P1_x times P1_y. A single matrix operator kernel uses the dual coordinate w=y^(-1): \[ \mathcal K_J(z,w)=\sum_{a,b=0}^nJ_{ab}z^a w^{-b-1}\,dw. 	ag{15} \] In the monomial identification of the actual head basis with H^0(P1,O(n)), its input factor is the explicit Serre-dual Cech class in H^1(P1,O(-n-2)). The ACTUAL head ket and row are psi(w)=sum_(b=0)^n w^b and evaluation at z=1 divided by N. Thus \[ \Phi(J)= rac1N\operatorname{Res}_{w=0} \mathcal K_J(1,w)\psi(w). 	ag{16} \] This keeps the original uniform ket/dual, rather than replacing them by binomial coherent weights or compact ordinary trace. If a binomial-normalized coherent frame is desired, its diagonal source and dual adapter must be carried explicitly. No positivity, metric isometry or asymptotic phase is inferred from this vector space identification. Both clocks and the shifts act on (15) as in (8); for the input clock its action is the ONE-FORM pullback w->w/Q, which includes the differential factor. This avoids a spurious factor Q in the right clock. On the coefficient of dw the input index b is -w partial_w-1; the missing -1 would give the wrong moment. Matrix composition, when it is actually used, is exactly \[ \mathcal K_{JH}(z,w)=\operatorname{Res}_{u=0} \mathcal K_J(z,u)\mathcal K_H(u,w), \] with the input/output differential factors retained. It is not pointwise multiplication of symbols, nor a claim that the physical four-port tangle composes by the reshaped matrix product. The full tails in (7) are meromorphic sections with possible poles only at zero and infinity in each coordinate. Keep them as such, or as the corresponding relative Cech cochains with their explicit boundary rows. Projecting them to the finite H^0/Serre quotient would discard the terms (3)--(6). The whole residue (9) is regular on these finite Laurent sections and preserves them. This gives one global meromorphic matrix/coherent Green complex for both actual coordinate currents, with no hypothetical extra Fr flag. Here is an explicit principal-part/Cech description of the tails. For O(n) on U_0 and U_infinity use the transition z^n and write every finite meromorphic section uniquely as \[ p(z)=p_{<0}(z)+p_{[0,n]}(z)+p_{>n}(z). \] The first and last summands are respectively the finite principal parts at zero and infinity; the middle one is H^0(O(n)). This is the global-section form of 0->O(n)->O(n)(*0+*infinity)->principal_parts->0. Exactness is immediate from the displayed Laurent splitting. Two coordinates give N-by-N core, four strips and four corner principal parts. The two one-step rules are, for a core polynomial, \[ \Pi(z^{-1}p)= rac{p-p(0)}z,\qquad \Pi(zp)=zp-p_nz^{n+1}. 	ag{16a} \] The discarded monomials are precisely the outgoing principal parts; the incoming ones give the last row or first row in (3). Tensoring these splits gives the explicit corner formula (5). Thus this is a strict global meromorphic/relative-Cech lift of the actual finite tail data, rather than an appeal to a different cohomology class with the same scalar value. Its source evaluates ALL nine regions at (1,1) with the one factor 1/N. ## 6. One-cut restriction and the physical Hopf distinction Closing the second identity cut gives the original one-cut array p_a=sum_b J_ab, hence C_one=diag(p_a) and \[ \Phi(J)=\operatorname{Tr}(C_{one})/N. 	ag{17} \] The second clock and current cannot in general be reconstructed from C_one: matrices with zero row sums can have nonzero weighted row sums after right multiplication by A. Keeping J avoids exactly that loss. Neither its two clocks nor its arbitrary off-diagonal entries are subject to an ordinary open-knot Schur condition. The ACTUAL physical single-port Hopf actions of the four-port tangle need not descend to J. They can create off-diagonal port bands, whose source uses the corresponding original cut pairing. Equations (2)--(8) concern simultaneous coordinate translations of the scalar/charge-zero flow array, not that separate Hopf diagram. The necessary port-band current extension is therefore retained as an additional map; it is not asserted by this matrix reshape. Their exact bands and current audit are recorded in [the physical port-band calculation](two_cut_port_band_current_audit.md). The finite two-flow certificate now has an exact global coherent and sourced relative complex. Establishing that the nondegenerate geometric Gaussian pushforward is a map into this complex, with the same marked endpoint/carry data, remains a theorem to prove. No such commutation, nonzero selected geometric contribution or volume limit is inferred here. ## 7. An exact band involution and the identity-cut residue sign A nontrivial geometric deck which fixes BOTH position clocks cannot be an exact source-preserving involution on the bare matrix J. Indeed the two operators L_A,R_A have jointly simple eigenvectors E_ab. A linear map commuting with both is a Schur multiplier E_ab->w_ab E_ab. Since Phi(E_ab)=1/N, preserving the original source forces every w_ab=1. An anti-source map similarly gives only -I. This is a fixed-level obstruction, not a prohibition on a transform with nontrivial internal/band multiplicity or only semiclassically fixed clocks. The retained PHYSICAL PORT BANDS have such multiplicity. In the actual band convention put \[ J^{\mu,
u}_{a,b}=T_{a+\mu,b+
u;a,b},\qquad (\mathcal I J)^{\mu,
u}_{a,b} =J^{-\mu,-
u}_{a+\mu,b+
u}. 	ag{18} \] This is simply input/output transpose of the full four-port tensor. It is exactly involutive and preserves the actual full source N^(-1) sum_(mu,a,b) J^(mu,0)_(a,b), with zero-extended bounds. It is not asserted to be a symmetry of the actual knot word. It exchanges input/output clocks; the CENTERED clocks Q^(a+mu/2), Q^(b+nu/2) are fixed exactly. Their square-root mark is the original q with q^2=Q. They restrict to the physical position clocks on the zero band. Simultaneous coordinate translations in a,b commute with this involution. The finite Laurent band kernel and its exact transformation are \[ F_T(x,y;\xi,\eta)=\sum J^{\mu,
u}_{a,b}x^ay^b\xi^\mu\eta^
u, \qquad F_{\mathcal IT}(x,y;\xi,\eta) =F_T(x,y;x/\xi,y/\eta). 	ag{19} \] The original second identity-cut co-source is the eta constant term of F_T(1,1;1,eta)/N. Its period form is \[ 	heta_T=F_T(1,1;1,\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta}. \] For inversion iota(eta)=eta^(-1) the natural ONE-FORM identity is \[ \iota^*	heta_T=-	heta_{\mathcal IT}. 	ag{20} \] Thus the scalar coefficient source is even, but its Cech residue orientation line is canonically odd: inversion exchanges zero and infinity, and Res_infinity(theta_T)=-Res_0(theta_T). This sign follows from the literal identity-cut residue, rather than from an assigned choice of geometric orientation. Equations (18)--(20) give a candidate source sign line for a geometric deck with anti-invariant density. To use it one must still prove that the geometric deck lifts to this actual port involution and transport the whole R/word and source frames. Transposition swaps left and right insertions and reverses operator order; no unchanged single-port Hopf row or unproved Weyl symmetry is inferred. The fixed-clock bare-matrix obstruction and the full-band candidate are distinct, exact statements. [Exact shifts, source, global-kernel and two-current audit](../experiments/audit_two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.py). The [results](../experiments/two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source_results.json) pass fourteen root/whole-Q families N=2,...,8 and 742 head-plus-tail matrix units. They check every signed shift/corner, whole boundary clock, literal 1/N source and both current homotopies. An additional 1956 physical four-port matrix units check the candidate band involution, centered clocks and source; the residue orientation sign is checked symbolically. These tests do not identify that involution with the geometric deck or establish a Gaussian map.

title: Independent audit of the two physical cuts, bands and selected source
text: # Independent audit of the two physical cuts, bands and selected source 27 October 2026. The two-cut route gives a genuine two-position source/current model. It escapes the one-cut diagonal obstruction, has a unimodular flow chart, and supplies canonical nonzero LOCAL Gaussian blocks for bounded port offsets. The global selected-class comparison still needs its specified endpoint/projector and sheet data. The assertions below distinguish these operations explicitly. ## 1. Integral physical coordinates and the original source The existence/lattice proof in [the actual two-cut construction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md) passes independently. Edge differentials here mean logarithmic physical-clock differentials on the classical critical scheme; integer labels define the underlying flow lattice. If all edge differentials lay in the span of the first cut differential, so would all transfer differentials, contradicting the two-dimensional critical framing tangent space. A second independent physical edge therefore exists on an open chart. For a connected graph G with circulation lattice L, the kernel of evaluating a set S of edge flows is the circulation lattice of G minus S. Incidence ranks give exactly \[ \operatorname{rank}\mathrm{ev}_S=|S|+1-c(G\setminus S). \] Rank two for the chosen pair implies that its complement is connected. A spanning tree avoiding both edges gives an integral fundamental-cycle basis with these two flows as literal coordinates. Thus there is no finite lattice index, congruence loss, extra cover or Jacobian factor. All zero-extension support conditions move with that integer change of variables. Opening the second identity wire means replacing it by the literal matrix unit E_bd. Summing E_bb restores its identity. Every original pivotal/turn/framing/peripheral tensor stays in its original place; no second pivotal weight is added. The reconstruction T_(a,b)^(c,d) and its double diagonal J_ab therefore have the exact source \[ F_N=\frac1N\sum_{a,b}J_{ab}. \tag{1} \] Use RAW coefficients for J. If the old Green array already includes 1/N, multiply its partial reshape by N before applying (1). There is no second normalization 1/N. J is a linear reshaping, not the two-leg operator algebra. For example diagonal extraction of the identity on H tensor H is the all-ones matrix, whose source value in (1) is N, while the actual two-cut unknot is the swap tensor and gives J=I, value one. A trace-center or multiplicative statement about J cannot silently be imported from the original four-port operator. ## 2. The whole two-flow Green/source complex passes The [matrix/Laurent/coherent construction](two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.md) passes independently. The four signed shift formulas retain the correct row/column tails, and their composition retains the common corner. Its Laurent kernel includes ALL finite tails. Consequently source evaluation F(1,1)/N kills full zero-extended differences, while window restriction has precisely its displayed boundary rows. For d_x=x^-1-1,d_y=y^-1-1 the displayed h_0,h_1 satisfy all three contraction identities with their printed signs. The identity-matrix anchor is correct too: Gamma=h_0(E_N-N) has differential E_N-N, so subtracting Gamma times the original source changes the section to E_N without changing the other identities. It does not introduce 1/N^2 or declare every physical tangle to have that anchor. The P1 kernel uses the literal uniform source and dual, not binomial coherent weights. Its input clock is a ONE-FORM pullback w to w/Q: the differential factor cancels the extra Q, giving exactly Q^b. The finite Laurent principal parts remain in their nine tensor regions; projecting to a finite Serre quotient would discard the tails and is not done. The generating variables are dual weights, not physical positions: \[ \mathscr F(x,y)=\sum J_{ab}x^ay^b,\qquad Q^a\leftrightarrow[x\mapsto Qx],\quad S_a^+\leftrightarrow x^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Rivin's physical coordinates are A=Q^a,B=Q^b. Identifying (x,y) with (A,B) would change the problem. Source evaluation at x=y=1 is the original zero-weight framing pairing. ## 3. Actual port currents have an exact band extension For fixed literal port order retain \[ J^{p,q}_{ab}=T_{a+p,b+q;a,b}, \] with zero values outside all four physical ranges. If E e_j=e_j^{E}e_(j-1) and F e_j=f_j e_(j+1), direct matrix multiplication gives the first-port commutator identities \[ \begin{split} [E_1,T]^{p,q}_{ab} &=e^E_{a+p+1}J^{p+1,q}_{ab} -e^E_aJ^{p+1,q}_{a-1,b},\\ [F_1,T]^{p,q}_{ab} &=f_{a+p-1}J^{p-1,q}_{ab} -f_aJ^{p-1,q}_{a+1,b}. \tag{3} \end{split} \] The second-port formulas interchange (a,p) and (b,q). Arbitrary port matrices have the stated sums of such shifted bands. This is a lossless finite current map, including the genuine endpoint coefficients and all original phase marks. For every current tensor the original source is \[ \Phi^{(2)}(T)=\sum_{p,a,b}(e_0)_{a,a+p}J^{p,0}_{ab}. \tag{4} \] In the balanced frame (e_0)_ij=1/N. A homogeneous cut degree d selects p=d; only a conserving scalar kernel selects p=q=0. Thus (1) may not be used as the source of every off-diagonal Hopf current. The actual two-cut unknot already proves that a single-port E action does not descend to ordinary left EJ: its diagonal extraction is zero, whereas EJ=E is nonzero. The actual insertion identity (3.1) in the main construction passes: A and B intertwine their ACTUAL intermediate coproducts, so the true adjoint of A X B is A(ad X)B, and the genuine pivotal cap is natural. Its E prefix terms and F cancellations have the correct order and weight k_X. For weighted words retain their extra crossing currents; for the frozen cap retain its exact moment-clock defect. A naive Delta on the reshaped J is not used. In a specified parallel two-leg Delta convention, the source of an ordinary E row needs only J^(0,0) and J^(-1,+1); F needs J^(0,0) and J^(+1,-1). This follows by (3) applied to the actual coproduct. A word of r ordinary E/F generators accesses exchange bands |p|<=r. For arbitrary boundary ordering this statement must first be transported by its actual opposite/dual/braided port dictionary. The literal cut tensor is NOT automatically an End(V tensor V) Delta-intertwiner. General divided-N rows and large bands are not covered by a fixed bounded-band assertion. ## 4. The bounded-band Gaussian construction is genuinely positive The interior theorem in Section5 of the main construction also passes independently. Removing both cuts leaves a connected internal graph. Any balanced fixed boundary offset has an integral tree particular flow. Every other solution differs by an internal cycle, with the same free transverse chords. For offsets fixed independently of N, each original local position/transfer changes by bounded integers. Actual proper factorial/Cartan ratios are therefore finite products of known rational shifts. Their principal symbols are units on the regular shape chart, with the original common compact, peripheral, phase and half-density lines retained. The two physical coordinates give a nondegenerate transverse Hessian. The original Gaussian of that proper-ratio insertion has the same marked action and a nonzero leading amplitude. Its value is independent of a FIXED bounded particular-flow choice by the exact transverse translation identity. An N-cycle is a finite logarithmic-deck move and needs its additional period mark. The explicit interior port/current identities consequently have a canonical LOCAL cochain pushforward, not merely a dimension count. Original support and endpoint rows remain their separate relative summand; this theorem does not evaluate them. The nearest-band principal ratios are also correct in the ACTUAL balanced/factorial frame. Its canonical boundary form uses p_new=(1-A)p_old. Holding inputs fixed and shifting outputs by (p,q) changes the principal action by p Log p_cut+q Log p_e. The cut value is one, giving \[ R_{(+1,-1),0}=p_e^{-1},\qquad R_{(-1,+1),0}=p_e. \tag{5} \] Internal tree contributions cancel by critical momentum matching. Using the old momentum without its frame factor would change (5). ## 5. A physical two-parabolic chart and its sign target In a common ACTUAL physical chart, take a normalized cut meridian g_0=[[1,1],[0,1]], a trace-two meridian g_e=[[a,b],[c,d]], h=a-d, and F=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]]. Then \[ P=F E_{11}F^{-1} =\begin{pmatrix}r&r(1-r)/s\\s&1-r\end{pmatrix},\quad k_e=\operatorname{Tr}(g_eP) =d+hr+bs+c r(1-r)/s. \] Let A=1/(1+s), B=1/k_e, tau=r/s and D=c+sh-2cr. Direct differentiation and trace/determinant identities give \[ D^2=c^2+4cs(1-B^{-1}),\qquad \Omega_{cut}=\frac{d\log A\wedge d\log B}{BD}. \tag{6} \] If c=0, trace2 and determinant1 force a=d=1, and B depends only on s, contradicting an independent pair. Thus a rank-two chart has c!=0. The quadratic discriminant is generically nonsquare (its pole at B=0 is simple), and the deck is r to 1+sh/c-r. It flips D and Omega. Ordinary field trace of the coefficient1/(BD) is consequently ZERO. The symmetric matrix Q=[[h/c,1],[1,0]] has determinant -1 and satisfies g_0Q=Qg_0^t, g_eQ=Qg_e^t. Thus the same deck is P to QP^tQ^-1. This is a bilinear transpose statement, not an assertion of a positive Hermitian structure or an already proved quantum-Weyl symmetry of the whole word. In the moving cut frame the ACTUAL factorial momentum form is \[ g_{cut}=\begin{pmatrix}1+s&-s\\s&1-s\end{pmatrix},\quad g_e^{cur}=\begin{pmatrix}k&(1-k)p_e\\(k-1)/p_e&2-k\end{pmatrix}. \] If these are the displayed matrices in that same physical frame, with c=Tr(g_cut g_e^cur)-2 fixed, put z=s(k-1). Then exactly \[ c=z(2-p_e-p_e^{-1}),\qquad D=-z(p_e-p_e^{-1}). \] One may also verify D=-Tr([g_0,g_e]P). On the regular z!=0, p_e!=0 chart, the deck is precisely p_e to p_e^-1. Formula (5) therefore gives a genuine actual LOCAL odd-band observable \[ R_{(+1,-1),0}-R_{(-1,+1),0}=D/z. \] Its product with (6) is the nonzero even density dlog A wedge dlog B/(Bz). This does not say the original q=0 identity-cap source inserts that observable or selects that sign cycle. That is a specified remaining source-parity test. The physical dictionary is essential: in the existing marked holonomy construction H_j=B_(minus,prefix)^-1 G_j B_(minus,prefix). A developed meridian cannot be substituted for a physical Gauss matrix solely because both have trace two. The conditional chart consequence above requires the actual prefix/port adapter. There is an alternative finite parity-moment test where a third physical meridian clock is available in the SAME frame. For g_f with entries a',b',c',d', h'=a'-d' and W=c'h-ch' nonzero, \[ r=\frac{c'k_e-c k_f-(c'd-cd')-(c'b-cb')s}{W}. \tag{7} \] Thus D is a rational combination of three actual clock observables; its moment can be inserted through the retained internal-edge coupling, with no extra pivot. If the descended quadratic field is F(D), Delta=D^2, and lambda=Tr((a_0+a_1D) times -), then \[ \lambda(1/(BD))=\lambda(D)/(B\Delta). \tag{8} \] The actual odd moment lambda(D), rather than a chosen field-trace normalization, is the coefficient to test. Formula (7) has the same physical-prefix qualification as (6). ## 6. The exact remaining selected-class square Two physical cuts now give both external difference directions and their complete finite matrix/source complex. The old one-cut obstruction does not apply. Local transverse Gaussian transport also has both physical base variables and the bounded band currents just proved. These are genuine improvements. The whole selected comparison still needs the original internal finite head projections. In the known relative/Rees diagram their actual maps are, with all head flags retained, \[ P_t^{rel}(\sigma) =e^{(\sigma-p/d)u}P_t. \tag{9} \] Opening a second identity edge does not remove the remaining internal projectors. A proposed whole geometric pushforward Gamma must intertwine (9) and both endpoints, in addition to the actual crossings and the selected two-cut tail/co-source. Its elementary defect is the specifically typed expression \[ E_O=\Gamma_{out}O_{act,rel} -O_{geo,rel}\Gamma_{in}. \] For a word its residual is the finite telescoping sum \[ \sum_t O_{geo,>t}\,E_{O_t}\,O_{act,<t}. \tag{10} \] The internal source equation (9), not a generic formal Morse assertion, is a concrete remaining test. Its irregular factor cannot be silently replaced by a regular vacuum. The exact whole Fermat-trace source is one available explicit function for this comparison, with its original norm, trace and power characters. Equations (9)--(10) do not assert an obstruction to constructing Gamma. They identify what the new external matrix/coherent map does not yet prove. Extending it through these specified internal maps and proving the selected sign/orientation would give the desired whole source-class comparison; neither selected survival nor volume growth follows just from local nonzero Gaussian bands. ## 7. The actual prefix correction passes, including the parity signs The later [prefix-adapted two-position proof](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md) passes independently. It resolves the physical-prefix qualification in Section 5. For U=mu_j...mu_1 and V=mu_(j-1)...mu_1, the actual second clock is k=ell_U/ell_V. With C=U-kV the correct density is \[ \Omega_{cut}=\frac{\ell_V}{BD}\,d\log A\wedge d\log B, \qquad D=\partial_\tau\ell_C. \tag{11} \] The Section 5 density with numerator one is a special chart, not a formula for every physical internal edge. Direct quadratic root summation gives \[ \operatorname{Tr}(\ell_V/D) =\frac{c_Vh_U-h_Vc_U}{(c_U-kc_V)^2}. \tag{12} \] It can be nonzero; the actual figure-eight prefix in the main note has c_Vh_U-h_Vc_U=2u+1 for u squared plus u plus one equal to zero. The claimed rational primitive of the resulting trace form also has the correct sign. A nonzero field trace is not a selected period. The signed triangular reconstruction gives exactly beta=(-1)^j e_j and gamma=(-1)^j K_j f_j, because both triangular prefix adapters cancel out of these off-diagonal entries. Thus \[ \beta=(-1)^j(k-M^{-1})p,\qquad \gamma=(-1)^{j+1}(k-M)/p. \] At M=1, Tr(JC) fixes beta-gamma and differentiation gives D=s(beta+gamma). Hence the deck sends beta,gamma to -gamma,-beta, and p to p inverse, with D=(-1)^j s(k-1)(p-p inverse). This independently checks the parity j in its nearest-band and density formulas. The generic-meridian twisted reciprocal formula follows by using the actual cut meridian entries M inverse minus k_0 and k_0 minus M in this same trace equation; it also passes. Finally the literal inverse signed prefix is (q/M)^(j-1) product_(i<j) Q^(J_i). It is an actual finite diagonal clock observable with its peripheral factor, not a postselected scalar. Its principal symbol removes ell_V from (11). The note correctly keeps its ordered crossing/current transport and does not claim that it commutes through the whole word. ## 8. The finite identity cap has a marked orientation presentation [The marked cap-cover identity](identity_cut_orientation_cover_and_marked_source.md) now supplies an exact positive source comparison before any Gaussian: \[ F(\eta)\frac{d\eta}{N\eta} =[(\eta-\eta^{-1})F(\eta)] \frac{d(\eta+\eta^{-1})} {N((\eta+\eta^{-1})^2-4)}. \tag{13} \] The original cap marks eta=0, equivalently the preimage of u=infinity with v/u tending to -1. Its exact residue has all finite negative odd-band tails, with partial-sum endpoint (F_0-F_(-2K-2))/N. The compensating measure and this endpoint prevent replacing the original state by an arbitrary odd observable. The total form has no new branch-point poles. No global tensor involution is assumed. The principal prefix formula identifies eta=p inverse and gives Omega_cut/ell_V=[(k-1)/(A_1-A_0)] dlog A wedge d eta/eta on its regular coordinate chart, where A_0=c_U+s Tr U and A_1=c_V+s Tr V. This checks the principal density and its full rational Jacobian. Transporting the entire marked residue through the actual internal projectors and transverse Gaussian remains the global comparison. The new independent exact audit passes 21 literal actual signed braid tensors, seven literal-unknot levels and all 8,771 port matrix units at those levels, including their whole clocks and finite endpoints. See the linked cap-cover note and its reproducible script/results. The same note now records an important exact GEOMETRIC boundary check. Its eta_geo=p inverse differs from the finite Fourier-band variable eta_F. The relation eta_F p=1 is principal Fourier incidence, not an ordinary source-coordinate change or a map of the cap cycle. In the geometric relation u=p+p inverse, eta_geo=0 forces k to one and selects D=A_0-A_1. If c_U-c_V is nonzero, the prefix root r and ell_V stay finite. The full density multiplier ell_V(k-1)/(A_1-A_0) is O(eta), so Omega_cut has zero logarithmic residue there. This does not identify that boundary with the image of the original eta_F cap. For the actual figure-eight prefix at s=1 the limiting data are r=-2 and ell_V=2+3u_shape, with c_U-c_V=1 and A_0-A_1=3+u_shape. If a proposed source transform assigns the cap to this geometric boundary, a nonzero image needs its retained polar, endpoint or escaping block amplitude; the geometric residue functional is equation (19) of the cap-cover note. The finite identity (13) does not by itself imply that an interior regular Gaussian density has the original nonzero cap. This is a concrete remaining source coefficient, rather than a choice of an odd cycle by hand.

title: Independent audit of the actual two-head cyclic sewing
text: # Independent audit of the actual two-head cyclic sewing 28 October 2026. The exact five-term resolvent and the two-sector SMALL-CIRCLE period reduction in [the sewing theorem](exact_quantum_quad_source_transport.md) are correct, including the coincident-wall fibre. A balancing gauge gives a useful local matrix estimate. It does not turn the original period into a positive pairing or license the old Hankel deformation term by term. There is an explicit source-visible pole witness in the original positive crossing: its two sewn cross pieces have nonzero double poles absent from the nilpotent resolvent. Their contributions must accompany any subsequent cut deformation. ## 1. Resolvent order and the coincident wall On a total-index residue fibre choose basis b_n, n=0,...,N-1. Let S be cyclic raising, A=aS, z=a/t, and h=k+1. For h<N the actual truncated transfer deletes the arrows N-1 to 0 and h-1 to h. With U=[b_0,b_h], its deleted operator is UU^t A. Woodbury therefore gives R_T=R_A-R_A U (I+U^t A R_A U)^-1 U^t A R_A. Direct cyclic summation gives (I+U^t A R_A U)^-1 =C_h(z)=[[1,-z^(N-h)],[-z^h,1]]. All orders in the displayed formula matter. At h=N the two columns of U coincide, so a rank-two Woodbury inverse is NOT available. Nevertheless the SAME compressed expression remains correct, because U C_N(z) U^t=(1-z^N)b_0 b_0^t. This is exactly the single-deleted-edge formula. Thus the global five-term expression and its two cross terms are valid for every fibre without double-counting the physical wall. R_A and the two diagonal sewing terms are holomorphic at t=0. Multiplying by the marked analytic inverse-D germ and integrating on rho<min(1,|a|) kills those three terms entrywise. Other word factors do not alter that conclusion, since they use different integration variables. Consequently the at most 2^(3m) surviving cross-sector networks retain the original source exactly on the original product of small circles. ## 2. The balancing gauge and its quantitative scope Retain a continuous Log z and put D_h=diag(1,z^(h-N/2)), w=z^(N/2). Then exactly D_h^-1 C_h D_h=[[1,-w],[-w,1]], det C_h=1-z^N. (1) The original physical scalar is a=x^-1 or Q^-1 x^-1. On an actual inverse-D cut t=Q^(-epsilon j)r and at M=1, z^N=(-1)^(N+1) r^(-N). (2) For odd N, w is one of the two real values +/-r^(-N/2). The balanced C has positive eigenvalues 1+/-r^(-N/2) for r>1. For even N, w is purely imaginary, and the Hermitian part of the balanced C is EXACTLY identity. Both statements retain the root phase; z^N has not been replaced by a positive number. The gauge condition number is kappa(D_h)=r^|h-N/2|. On the actual radial scale r=exp(s/N), it is bounded by exp(s/2), uniformly in h and N when s is bounded. This includes h=N, although U then has repeated columns. For odd N the smallest balanced eigenvalue is 1-exp(-s/2), which tends to zero at the radial endpoint. At fixed r>1 the gauge can instead have exponential condition number; the stated bound is a scaled local estimate, not a uniform estimate on the entire radial ray. Moreover the two-sector Cauchy reduction keeps only C's OFFDIAGONAL part. Its balanced version is [[0,-w],[-w,0]]: indefinite for odd N and with zero Hermitian part for even N. Thus the positive diagonal of full C belongs to terms whose original small-circle periods vanish. Positivity of full C does not itself prove a lower bound for their remaining cross-sector contraction. The actual co-source is also a pivotal linear pairing, not the positive quadratic form used by an accretivity estimate. ## 3. Added cyclic poles change the required relative cycle Every cyclic R_A has poles at t^N=a^N, while R_T has only its nilpotent pole at zero. The five-term formula cancels all added poles. Discarding its analytic-at-zero terms preserves the small circle period but does NOT preserve global holomorphy. At completeness a^N=(-1)^(N+1). Thus for odd N the added poles lie at N-th roots of unity: most hit D-cut endpoints, and t=1 is an added pole where D itself is regular. For even N they lie at the interlaced half-roots, off those cuts. Separate cross pieces can have double poles. Their old radial-cut integrals may be nonintegrable when the pole hits a branch endpoint. Pole residues or the corresponding marked finite-part chains must be retained. Matrix balancing in Section 2 does not remove this change of relative cycle. ## 4. An exact original positive-crossing source witness Take N=2, M=1, Q=-1, q=i, x=i. In the opposite-root realization of the actual U_+ factor, a=Q^-1 x^-1=i. Use the original fusion C and Gaussian D=I from the strict crossing factorization, and the original averaged first-cut functional Phi with pivotal entries (-i,i). Keep its common Cartan scalar and external line separately, unchanged. Let R_cross(t) be the sum of the two cross terms, and R_T the actual transfer resolvent. Exact source contraction gives Phi(C R_T(t) C^-1)=2i/t^2, Phi(C R_cross(t) C^-1) =-2i(t-1)(t+1)/[t^2(t^2+1)^2]. (3) The leading double-pole coefficient of the second expression at EACH of t=i and t=-i is i. These poles are source-visible inside an actual positive crossing, rather than only in an arbitrary matrix entry. The original inverse-D germ here is f(t)=(1+t)^(-1/2). Both small-circle periods are exactly -i. The uncorrected old D-cut integral for the sewn expression, on t=-r, would instead be (2i/pi) integral_1^infinity (r^2-1)/[r^2(r^2+1)^2] (r-1)^(-1/2)dr. It is purely POSITIVE imaginary and therefore cannot equal -i. The missing cyclic-pole contributions are essential, even in this smallest actual-source example. The original normalization multiplies both expressions by the same retained nonzero factor; it cannot correct the mismatch. The missing ordinary residues are explicitly Res_(t=i) f(t)B(t)dt=(-9-i)/(4sqrt(1+i)), Res_(t=-i) f(t)B(t)dt=(9-i)/(4sqrt(1-i)). Their sum is approximately 1.0596435755300515788i. The raw cut integral is approximately 0.0596435755300515788i. The correct contour identity is cut MINUS these pole residues, which gives the original value -i. ## 5. Audit conclusion The exact small-circle sewing is a real finite-sector reduction. The balanced 2-by-2 matrix has a controlled condition number on the natural radial scale and the stated parity-dependent sign. Neither statement supplies a convergent termwise old-cut sewing or a positive selected scalar. A usable geometric comparison must carry the new cyclic poles and the original cross-sector source through the transform, including its endpoint corrections. There is a canonical linear repair when cyclic poles have order at most two, as they do in each transfer variable. At a D-cut endpoint alpha, put x=r-1 and write the remaining cut integrand as x^(-u)f(x), where f(x)=b_-2 x^(-2)+b_-1 x^(-1)+O(1). Its finite part is integral_0^1 x^(-u)[f-b_-2 x^(-2)-b_-1 x^(-1)]dx +integral_1^infinity x^(-u)f dx -b_-2/(u+1)-b_-1/u. Use these marked finite parts on the branch cuts and subtract the ordinary residues at unbranched cyclic poles. This gives the original small-circle period exactly. The constants follow from analytic continuation of the two elementary power integrals. The small endpoint arcs cancel their fractional divergences and have no additional finite residue: on the normalized cover a residue exponent would require j to be a multiple of N. Coordinatewise finite parts commute for this word because its ordered matrix source is a finite sum of products of one-variable rational factors. The tensor prescription retains the required corner subtractions. It preserves the source, while still not making its resulting scalar a positive quadratic pairing. The [regularized cut theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md) has positive derivative factor 1/[u...(u+p-1)] for p=1,2. At every integration-by-parts step the boundary term at infinity is O(x^(-(N-1)/2)), and the zero-end finite constant vanishes because u is nonintegral. The final derivative integral converges at both ends. The whole-word tensor prescription is a finite sum of products of one-variable factors, with only coordinate pole loci. The unit-circle/completeness hypothesis excludes additional poles inside a radial cut. Geometric coupling remains separate. [Exact and quantitative audit](../experiments/audit_two_head_cyclic_sewing_independent.py) and [saved results](../experiments/two_head_cyclic_sewing_independent_results.json).

title: The actual unfolded atom requires its cyclotomic divisors and second nome
text: # The actual unfolded atom requires its cyclotomic divisors and second nome Research proof, 27 October 2026. The original unfolded Ward factorial is not horizontal in a rank-one meromorphic line at the physical parameter origin. Its cyclotomic singularities already accumulate there. A two-nome difference-period object cancels the local root pole and has an exact cyclic/source factorization, but it also does not become an ordinary meromorphic line at the origin. It has explicit accumulating zeros on another parameter ray. The positive result is a whole exceptional-slope evaluation of the actual Ward atom, including its Kummer norm character, and an exact two-nome root formula retaining the original cyclic gauge and Heisenberg period. No published analytic-continuation or quantum dilogarithm proof is a premise. Use H=Log Q throughout. The physical root is H_N=2pi i/N. The earlier ADO parameter h=Log q is H/2. A fixed-root normal epsilon=H-H_N is a different parameter from the varying H_N. ## 1. The function is fixed by the actual Ward jets The literal finite source has f_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) z^j/(Q_N;Q_N)_j. Its all-level rational-coefficient unfolding was proved uniquely to be \[ F(Q,z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{z^j}{(Q;Q)_j},\qquad F(Q,Qz)=(1-z)F(Q,z),\quad F(Q,0)=1. \] For |Q|<1, |z|<1, coefficient comparison or iteration gives \[ F(Q,z)=\frac1{(z;Q)_\infty},\qquad \log F(Q,z)=\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{z^m}{m(1-Q^m)}. \tag{1} \] These are the actual unfolded source functions of [the Ward construction](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md), not an unrelated function chosen for its growth. The finite nilpotent head itself only uses the first N coefficients; scalar root values with nonnilpotent z require the retained central/source data below. ## 2. Cyclotomic singularities exclude the strict meromorphic-line target Fix a primitive n-th root zeta and Q=zeta exp(epsilon). On a closed sector around the negative real epsilon ray, uniformly for |z|<=r<1 with n FIXED, \[ \log F(\zeta e^\epsilon,z) =-\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(z^n)}{n^2\epsilon} +\log D_n(z)-\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z^n)+O(\epsilon), \quad D_n(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1-\zeta^jz)^{j/n}. \tag{2} \] All marks start at z=0. Here is an analytic justification of the coefficient calculation already recorded in the Ward note. Separate m divisible by n in (1). Nonresonant denominators are uniformly bounded away from zero on the stated sector: for m|epsilon| small, use the distance of the finitely many nontrivial n-th roots from one; otherwise their radial modulus gives a uniform bound. Their termwise difference from epsilon=0 is O(m|epsilon|), so the z-series remainder is O(epsilon). For the resonant terms use \[ \frac1{1-e^u}=-\frac1u+\frac12+O(u) \] uniformly on the same negative sector. For large u the error bound O(|u|) still holds; summing against r^(kn) justifies the uniform remainder. The weighted finite-root sum gives the displayed D_n constant. Thus (2) is a genuine sectorial estimate, not merely a formal Laurent calculation. For fixed 0<z<1, every H_(m,n)=2pi i m/n, gcd(m,n)=1, has the nonzero polar logarithm in (2). Along epsilon=-t, log|F|=Li_2(z^n)/(n^2t)+O(1). These singularities accumulate at H=0. A nonzero horizontal frame of a meromorphic rank-one H-line would be holomorphic and nonzero at every sufficiently small H_(m,n)!=0, a contradiction. Finite ramification does not help. A fixed algebraic/Puiseux gauge has only finite-order behavior there and cannot cancel this exponential singularity. Removing only exp(-Li_2(z)/H) also leaves every nonzero cyclotomic point unchanged as a singularity. This disproves automatic applicability of the strict one-variable meromorphic-line criterion to the original UNFOLDED ATOM. It does not prove that singularities cannot cancel in a completed whole word or selected period; that cancellation would need its actual source theorem. ## 3. The actual norm is an exceptional normal-slope evaluation Retain U independently and form the WHOLE ratio \[ R(Q,z,U)=F(Q,zU)/F(Q,z). \tag{3} \] The bare generic restriction U=1 is one. Instead put Q=zeta_n exp(epsilon), U=exp(t n epsilon). For fixed n, t in a compact subset of C, and |z|<=r<1, the same sectorial argument gives \[ \log R(Q,z,U)=t\operatorname{Log}(1-z^n)+O(\epsilon), \qquad R\longrightarrow(1-z^n)^t. \tag{4} \] Proof. Nonresonant terms in the difference of (1) tend to zero uniformly. For m=kn the term is z^(kn)(exp(tkn^2 epsilon)-1)/[kn(1-exp(kn epsilon))], whose limit is -t z^(kn)/k. Uniform Taylor bounds near zero and exponential bounds away from zero, absorbed into a slightly larger r<1, justify the summed O(epsilon). This proves (4). At the ACTUAL slope t=1, U=Q^n and Ward iteration gives EXACTLY \[ R(Q,z,Q^n)=(z;Q)_n,\qquad R(Q_n,z,1)_{slope=1}=1-z^n. \tag{5} \] Thus the original finite cyclic norm is an exceptional normal-slope value, not the result of first imposing U=1 generically. It retains factors such as 1+M^n when they arise from the actual z substitution. For rational t=a/b, b>0, retain the telescope \[ \prod_{j=0}^{b-1}R(Q,zU^j,U)=F(Q,zU^b)/F(Q,z). \tag{6} \] Here U^b=Q^(an), so for a>=0 the right side is the finite product (z;Q)_(an), and negative a gives its specified reciprocal product. Its root value is (1-z^n)^a. The marked individual exceptional period nu therefore satisfies nu^b=(1-z^n)^a, with nu=1 at z=0. Equation (6) does NOT assert R^b equals that finite product away from the exceptional restriction: its arguments are different. This is a fixed-n sectorial exceptional period and Kummer norm statement. It is not a holomorphic regular extension across an entire complex blowup neighborhood, where other cyclotomic divisors still accumulate. No fixed-n limit is interchanged with a growing-n limit. ## 4. A two-nome flat difference object made from exact products Let z=e^x and define, for Re H<0, \[ Q=e^H,\quad \widetilde Q=e^{4\pi^2/H},\quad y=e^{2\pi i x/H},\quad w=\widetilde Q y, \] \[ \Psi(H,x)=\frac{(w;\widetilde Q)_\infty}{(z;Q)_\infty} =\frac{F(Q,z)}{F(\widetilde Q,w)}. \tag{7} \] Both nomes have modulus<1. The numerator product is entire in w; the log-series quotient is used on the smaller common chart |w|<1. Elementary product cancellation proves the exact two transports \[ \Psi(H,x+H)=(1-z)\Psi(H,x),\qquad \Psi(H,x+2\pi i)=(1-y)\Psi(H,x). \tag{8} \] The two shifts commute, since each multiplier is fixed by the other shift. In whole independent coordinates (Q,Qtilde,z,y), the automorphisms are z->Qz and y->Qtilde^(-1)y, respectively. Equations (8) are a rank-one flat algebraic DIFFERENCE presentation over that fixed finite-type base. The product (7) supplies one marked horizontal period. It is not thereby an algebraic section or an ordinary meromorphic differential line in H. The second factor is invariant under x->x+H. It is a genuine difference-constant for the original Ward equation. On the left upper H sector, x->-infinity along the real axis makes both z,w tend to zero, specifying the product mark Psi->1. That extra period/source datum must not be inferred from the first equation alone. ## 5. Exact physical-root value and the full source factor Now fix N and H=H_N+epsilon, H_N=2pi i/N. Write X=z^N and mark V=Log(1-X), nu=(1-X)^(1/N). The exact normal identities are \[ \widetilde H=4\pi^2/H+2\pi iN, \quad\frac1{\widetilde H} =\frac1{N^2\epsilon}+\frac1{2\pi iN}, \quad w=Xe^{\gamma\widetilde H},\quad \gamma=1-x/(2\pi i). \tag{9} \] For x in a compact marked subset of Re x<0, use (2) on the numerator atom and its n=1 case on the dual atom. The entire negative Laurent part of the two logarithms is the same simple pole -Li_2(X)/(N^2 epsilon), and cancels. Their exact constant difference gives the sectorial root value \[ \boxed{\ \Psi_N(x)=D_N(z) \exp\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(X)}{2\pi iN}\right) (1-X)^{x/(2\pi i)-1}.\ } \tag{10} \] For clarity the dual constant is -Li_2(X)/(2pi iN)+(gamma-1/2)V; subtracting it from log D_N- V/2 proves (10), including its sign. The estimate is O(epsilon) on the stated sector. This establishes the finite marked root value, not an unproved holomorphic H-extension around the whole root. Use the ACTUAL determinant-normalized cyclic source gauge \[ g_{D,N}=D_N/\nu^{(N-1)/2},\quad S(X)=\operatorname{Li}_2(X)+(Nx)V. \] Then the COMPLETE factorization is \[ \boxed{\ \Psi_N=g_{D,N}\, \exp(S(X)/(2\pi iN))\,\nu^{-(N+1)/2}.\ } \tag{11} \] Every determinant root, its half-power mark, and the logarithmic period is retained. In the actual cyclic Ward substitution z=-t e one has X=-kappa_N t^N, so 1-X=1+kappa_N t^N is exactly the original norm, not an arbitrarily dropped central factor. The source/transport check is decisive. Under x->x+H_N, g_D multiplies by (1-z)/nu, while S changes by 2pi i V. Their factors in (11) combine to 1-z, exactly (8). Under x->x+2pi i, g_D returns to itself and S changes by 2pi iN V, giving 1-X. Thus the n-step quotient is precisely the finite product (5), with its central norm and branch marks still present. The raw finite polynomial also retains its affine source: \[ f_N(Q_Nz)-(1-z)f_N(z)=z^N/N. \tag{12} \] On the nilpotent quotient z^N=0, (11) has central factor congruent to one and g_D reduces to f_N. This is a canonical projection in the logarithmic z-jet ring: the Log z terms first occur with z^N. It is not a literal evaluation of Log of a nilpotent matrix. For moving tensor sources or nonzero central norm, (11)--(12) must be retained. Nilpotent-jet agreement does not prove that the two-nome completion preserves the actual whole normal source. The formula has the established rational quantum-dilogarithm coverage described in [the existing finite/continuous torsor note](rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md). Its proof here is the exact original Ward product and the two normal identities (9), without adopting that literature's proof. ## 6. The completion still is not an ordinary meromorphic H-line Fix real x<0. The function (7) has exact SIMPLE zeros \[ H_k=(x-2\pi i)/k\longrightarrow0. \tag{13} \] Indeed Re H_k<0, both nomes have modulus<1, and w(H_k)=exp(2pi i k)=1. Only the numerator's first factor 1-w vanishes; the remaining product and the denominator are nonzero, since |Q|,|Qtilde|,|z|<1. Moreover w'(H_k)!=0. This proves simplicity directly. A nonzero horizontal frame of a rank-one meromorphic line at zero cannot have these accumulating interior zeros. A fixed algebraic Puiseux gauge cannot remove them. Thus the completion does NOT repair the strict one-parameter criterion globally either. This does not prevent a finite polar ASYMPTOTIC along the physical positive-imaginary sequence. On a fixed marked compact annulus 0<rho<=|z|<=r<1, the actual finite sum for log D_N and elementary trapezoid bounds give \[ \log D_N(z)=-\operatorname{Li}_2(z)/H_N -\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z)+O(1/N). \] The central factor in (10) is exponentially small in its logarithm on this chart, because X=z^N. Therefore \[ \log\Psi_N(x)=-\operatorname{Li}_2(z)/H_N -\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z)+O(1/N). \tag{14} \] For a direct proof of the leading integral, expand integral_0^1 t Log(1-z exp(2pi it))dt=-Li_2(z)/(2pi i); the endpoint correction is the displayed -Log(1-z)/2. Uniform derivative bounds on |z|<=r give the error. This is a statement about the specified root sequence and chart, not an ordinary meromorphic H-germ or a global geometric-knot norm. ## 7. The usable target for the whole-period program The strict selected meromorphic-line polar-character theorem remains a valid sufficient condition. It cannot be inferred from the actual local q-factorial atom: both its original and completed forms give explicit obstructions. The natural exact local target instead keeps the cyclotomic divisors, the independent power/normal direction of (3)--(6), the two-nome difference presentation (8), and the central Heisenberg/norm-root period (11). The completion is not permission to replace the already selected Kashaev source by a convenient periodic factor. It has the same finite nilpotent jets but additional difference-constant period data. A knot comparison must carry those data, every peripheral factor, the actual internal projectors and its selected contraction. No topological invariant, global source descent, or volume conjecture is proved by this local construction. [Exact source identities and high-precision root/zero audit](../experiments/audit_unfolded_atom_two_nome_source.py). The audit passes at 80 decimal digits: 21 fixed-root expansions, 24 exceptional-slope limits, nine exact rational-slope telescopes, four generic two-nome shift pairs, 14 physical-root constants with both marked source transports, 12 exact finite-field affine-source polynomials, six accumulating simple zeros, and 12 independently bounded physical-root sequence cases. The two normal-coordinate identities in (9) also pass symbolic verification. The [saved results](../experiments/unfolded_atom_two_nome_source_results.json) record every case. These finite checks support the proofs above; they do not assert uniformity in growing n for the fixed-n normal limits. [Independent proof audit](unfolded_atom_two_nome_independent_audit.md) checks the sectorial estimate, full root constant, norm-root power, two transports, accumulating simple zeros and trapezoid endpoint.

title: Independent audit of the whole Ward atom and its two-nome completion
text: # Independent audit of the whole Ward atom and its two-nome completion 27 October 2026. Detailed examination of [the cyclotomic-divisor and two-nome construction](unfolded_atom_cyclotomic_divisors_and_two_nome_source.md), especially Sections 2, 3, 5 and 6. The fixed-level sectorial nature of the assertions is necessary and is stated in that note. This audit does not promote its finite root formula to an ordinary meromorphic parameter germ, a whole selected-knot source, or a volume theorem. ## 1. Fixed-level sectorial expansions and the normal-slope norm For a fixed primitive n-th root, split the absolutely convergent logarithm sum into m divisible by n and its complement. In a closed negative-real epsilon sector the nonresonant denominators have a uniform positive bound: for m times absolute epsilon small this is the finite root separation, and for it large the radial modulus is bounded below. Their differences from the root value are bounded by a constant times m times absolute epsilon. For the resonant terms the bound \[ \left|\frac1{1-e^u}+\frac1u-\frac12\right|\leq C|u| \] holds on that sector, using its Taylor expansion near zero and radial bounds outside a disk. Geometric decay in z then sums the errors. This proves the displayed O(epsilon) estimate uniformly on |z| at most r less than one, with n fixed. Its constant may depend on n; it does not give an estimate for growing n. Putting U=exp(t n epsilon), each resonant term of the log ratio has limit -t z^(kn)/k. The nonresonant difference is O(epsilon). Uniformity for compact t follows after absorbing exp(C m absolute epsilon) into a slightly larger z disk. Thus the exceptional value is exactly (1-z^n)^t with its z=0 mark. At t=1 the actual identity F(Q,zQ^n)/F(Q,z)=(z;Q)_n proves its norm interpretation without an interchange of two limits. The rational-slope telescope uses its different shifted arguments; it is not an off-exceptional identity claiming that the first ratio raised to a power is that product. ## 2. The root completion constants, including the source half-power Write c=2 pi i, H=c/N+epsilon, X=exp(Nx), V=Log(1-X). Direct inversion, not an asymptotic approximation, gives \[ \widetilde H=4\pi^2/H+cN,\quad \frac1{\widetilde H}=\frac1{N^2\epsilon}+\frac1{cN},\quad w=X\exp(\gamma\widetilde H),\quad \gamma=1-x/c. \] The first-nome constant after its polar term is log D_N minus V/2. The dual n=1 atom has constant -Li_2(X)/(cN)+(gamma-1/2)V. Subtracting these two constants cancels their entire simple polar asymptotic term and gives \[ \Psi_N=D_N\exp(\operatorname{Li}_2(X)/(cN))(1-X)^{x/c-1}. \] With nu=(1-X)^(1/N), g_D=D_N/nu^((N-1)/2) and S=Li_2(X)+(Nx)V this is precisely \[ \Psi_N=g_D\exp(S/(cN))\nu^{-(N+1)/2}. \] Both half-power factors are required: their combined exponent is -N on nu, producing the factor (1-X) inverse in the preceding formula. The first shift x to x+c/N changes S by cV and changes g_D by (1-z)/nu, which combine to the original Ward multiplier 1-z. The second shift x to x+c gives the multiplier 1-X. The original central norm is 1-X. The stated conclusion is the radial/sectorial fixed-N value; the calculation alone does not prove holomorphic extension around a whole root neighborhood. ## 3. Exact accumulating zeros are a decisive parameter obstruction For fixed real x less than zero, put H_k=(x-c)/k. Its real part is negative, so both infinite products in the actual defining ratio converge. Since 4 pi squared plus 2 pi i x equals c(x-c), one has w(H_k)=exp(ck)=1. Only the numerator factor 1-w vanishes: every remaining numerator factor is 1-Qtilde^j with modulus of Qtilde less than one, and the denominator has modulus of z and Q less than one. The derivative of w at H_k is nonzero. These are therefore exact simple zeros, accumulating at H=0 inside its product domain. A nonzero horizontal solution of a meromorphic rank-one connection at zero is nonzero at every sufficiently small nonzero ordinary point, by uniqueness of its scalar differential equation. Such a solution cannot have these zeros. A finite algebraic ramification and a fixed nonzero Puiseux meromorphic gauge do not remove them. The uncompleted atom already has accumulating nonzero cyclotomic exponential singularities. These two explicit facts forbid an automatic ordinary meromorphic-line interpretation of either atom. They do not prohibit cancellations in a fully specified word/source. ## 4. The physical-root leading estimate has the stated sign For g(t)=t Log(1-z exp(ct)), elementary trapezoid summation gives sum_(j=1)^(N-1) g(j/N)=N integral_0^1 g-(g(0)+g(1))/2+O(1/N). Termwise integration on |z| less than one gives integral g=-Li_2(z)/c. Thus log D_N=-Li_2(z)/H_N-Log(1-z)/2+O(1/N), uniformly on a fixed marked compact z chart. The remaining logarithm in the exact completion formula is exponentially small there because X=z^N. The note's physical-root estimate follows with its negative one-half logarithmic term. It does not supply a selected geometric knot period or a uniform estimate across the accumulating divisors.

title: Unfolding the actual Ward jets gives a marked dilogarithm period
text: # Unfolding the actual Ward jets gives a marked dilogarithm period Research proof, 27 October 2026. A product-preserving fixed-N formalization with reduced scalar symbols is obstructed under the regularity hypotheses of [the fixed-root audit](fixed_root_formal_ward_obstruction.md). Their coherent all-level factorial jets do admit an unfolding. This note constructs it and identifies its cyclotomic pole, regular part, norm-root gauge, and local Heisenberg regulator by direct formulas. This is a theorem about the literal Ward factorial block. It does not identify the selected full knot contraction with a geometric period, or prove the volume conjecture. No published asymptotic or quantum-dilogarithm theorem is a premise of the proof. ## 1. The actual jets and a faithful all-level unfolding Let Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2. The actual nilpotent Ward block has the finite factorial gauge f_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) z^j/(Q_N;Q_N)_j, with z=-t e and e^N=0. Every denominator in this formula is nonzero. Its constant term is one. The literal relation is f_N(Q_N z)=(1-z)f_N(z) mod z^N. (1) Consider a proposed unfolding F(Q,z)=sum_j c_j(Q)z^j with each c_j rational in Q and regular at Q_N for all sufficiently large N. If its restrictions modulo z^N give these actual jets at every sufficiently large level, then necessarily c_j(Q)=1/(Q;Q)_j. (2) Indeed fix j and use every N>j outside the finite exceptional set. The rational function c_j(Q)-1/(Q;Q)_j vanishes at infinitely many distinct Q_N, so is zero. Existence is the displayed series F(Q,z)=sum_(j>=0) z^j/(Q;Q)_j. (3) Thus all-level rational coefficient data, rather than a chosen levelwise continuation, determine one formal function. No bound on the degrees of c_j as j grows was assumed. The same argument works for any specified family of nilpotent jets with such a rational coefficient unfolding; it proves uniqueness, not existence for an arbitrary family or for an unspecified whole knot period. Coefficient comparison gives the exact equation and normalization F(Q,Qz)=(1-z)F(Q,z), F(Q,0)=1. (4) Over Q(Q)[[z]], these conditions also determine F uniquely. For |Q|<1 it agrees with the ordinary convergent quantum factorial F(Q,z)=1/(z;Q)_infinity near z=0. This analytic statement follows directly by iterating (4), or from the coefficient identity below; it is not used to justify a root specialization of the infinite product. The nilpotent jets in (1) do not on their own define a value of F at a root for nonnilpotent z. The cyclotomic pole must first be retained. The rational coefficient hypothesis excludes arbitrary unrelated periodic factors at different levels; it is not a claim that any transseries or multivalued modular completion is thereby fixed without additional markings. ## 2. The formal logarithm and its exact cyclotomic pole Take the z-adic logarithm, with constant term zero. Equation (4) gives directly log F(Q,z)=sum_(m>=1) z^m/[m(1-Q^m)]. (5) There is no convergence assumption in (5). For fixed m it is a rational identity in Q. Fix a primitive root zeta of order N and write Q=zeta exp(h). The expansion is coefficientwise in z, with one possible h^(-1) term. Put X=z^N. Terms m not divisible by N are regular in h. For m=kN, 1/(1-exp(kN h))=-1/(kN h)+1/2+O(h). Consequently the polar coefficient is exactly A_(-1)(X)=[h^(-1)]log F=-Li_2(X)/N^2. (6) Here Li_2(X)=sum_(k>=1)X^k/k^2 is first a formal power series. On a marked punctured curve it has its usual analytic continuation fixed from this germ. Formula (6) is a coefficient evaluation, not a limiting assertion about a selected knot sequence. This gives a useful logarithmic-coordinate interpretation. Passing to the N-th cyclotomic resonance retains the terms with indices divisible by N. Their denominators supply a second factor kN, so the resonant logarithm coefficient is a dilogarithm. Keeping only a bare nilpotent special fiber would miss exactly this term. ## 3. The regular part is the marked cyclic dilogarithm Define, with the z=0 branch fixed, D_N(z)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta^j z)^(j/N). Its formal logarithm is well defined. The elementary weighted root sum is sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j zeta^(jm) =N/(zeta^m-1) for N not dividing m, =N(N-1)/2 for N dividing m. For the first equality, differentiate the finite geometric sum and evaluate at the nontrivial N-th root zeta^m. This identity and (5) give the entire constant coefficient: [h^0]log F=log D_N(z)-(1/2)Log(1-X). (7) Indeed the nonresonant terms give log D_N minus its resonant part, and the resonant constant term is Li_1(X)/(2N). Combining them gives precisely (7), with its sign and factor one half. In a formal exponential line the first two coefficients are therefore F(zeta exp(h),z) =exp(-Li_2(X)/(N^2 h)) D_N(z)(1-X)^(-1/2)(1+O(h)). (8) Equation (8) is a coefficientwise formal statement in z and h. It is not a uniform rootwise asymptotic estimate or a permission to evaluate a divergent infinite product first. All logarithmic and square-root branches are continued from z=0 together. ## 4. Identification with the actual normalized norm-root gauge Use the actual cyclic Ward order near M=1, kappa=M-M^(-1), kappa_N=M^N-M^(-N), A_N=R[e]/(e^N-(-1)^(N+1)kappa_N), sigma(e)=zeta e, z=-t e. Then X=z^N=-kappa_N t^N, and the full determinant character is 1-X=1+kappa_Nt^N=Norm(1+t e). (9) Mark nu=(1-X)^(1/N) by nu=1 at the nilpotent fiber. The cyclic product satisfies the exact transport and norm identities D_N(zeta z)/D_N(z)=(1-z)/nu, Norm D_N(z)=nu^(N(N-1)/2). (10) The first follows by subtracting its two logarithms using the weighted root sum; the second follows by multiplying all its deck translates. Both identities hold on the common marked root cover, not with independent fractional powers chosen per factor. Define g_D=D_N(z)/nu^((N-1)/2). (11) It has Norm g_D=1 and sigma g_D=((1+t e)/nu)g_D. At kappa=0 it has constant coefficient one and reduces exactly to the actual finite factorial gauge f_N(-t e): equation (1) determines that nilpotent unit coefficient by coefficient. The [norm-root transfer theorem](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) constructs a meridian-regular norm-one gauge with precisely these properties. Their ratio is sigma invariant, hence scalar in R; its N-th power is one and its identity mark is one. Thus the two gauges agree exactly on the completed marked cover. This identifies the actual normalized Ward gauge with the defined cyclic dilogarithm, rather than only comparing their norms. For even N the half power in (11) has its identity square-root mark. The disconnected phase sheets are retained, not equated. Formula (7) may now be written particularly simply as [h^0]log F=log g_D-(1/2)Log nu. (12) The meridian-regular unit interpretation of (10)--(12) is over the characteristic-zero cyclotomic coefficient field, retaining all factorial denominators. No arithmetic integrality at those denominators is asserted. ## 5. The local Heisenberg regulator is reconstructed On the marked logarithmic cover of X away from 0,1,infinity put U=Log X, V=Log(1-X), S=Li_2(X)+UV, R=Li_2(X)+(1/2)UV. Direct differentiation gives dS=U dV, dR=(1/2)(U dV-V dU). (13) Thus U/N, V/N and S/N^2 are the coordinates of the usual Heisenberg period matrix Pi_N=[1 U/N S/N^2; 0 1 V/N; 0 0 1]. The right connection Pi_N^(-1)dPi_N has entries dU/N and dV/N on the first superdiagonal and zero central entry, by (13); equivalently dPi_N=Pi_N Omega_N. More explicitly, U/N=Log z, V/N=Log nu, S/N^2=-A_(-1)+Log z Log nu, R/N^2=-A_(-1)+(1/2)Log z Log nu. (14) Equations (6), (9), and the actual norm-root mark therefore reconstruct the full local flat period from the unfolded Ward factorial and its source. Its real regulator is D(X)=Im Li_2(X)+Re(U) Im(V), dD=Re(U)d Im(V)-Re(V)d Im(U). (15) This is the Bloch--Wigner local regulator, with the same marked logs. Individual Li_2 pole coefficients alone omit the displayed logarithmic metric term. No knot fundamental-class constant or orientation is supplied merely by this local calculation. These logarithmic formulas live on the generic marked punctured cover. They do not assign Log(0) to the nilpotent special fiber; there the regular jet and its divided source are kept instead. The actual divided cyclic source is tied to the pole by an explicit first-normal identity. Since kappa_N=N kappa+O(kappa^2), formula (6), with X=-kappa_Nt^N, gives partial_kappa A_(-1)|_(kappa=0)=t^N/N. The literal polynomial source from the cyclic Ward block obeys [(sigma f_N(-t e)-(1+t e)f_N(-t e))/kappa]_(kappa=0) =-t^N=-N partial_kappa A_(-1)|_(kappa=0). (16) This directly compares the actual normal source with the unfolded cyclotomic period coefficient. The same scalar t^N is the first-normal group-transfer character B_0(1+t e). The source, norm-root transfer, and period pole are three specified realizations of this one local normal datum. ### 5.1 The resonant pole is an exact divided-power tensor correction There is also an operator realization of this pole on the genuine integral complete-color lift. It is important to use that lift here, rather than suppose that a fixed-root typical color is a generic-q quantum-group module. On b factors let C(Q) be the total actual raising operator. Its individual factors have N-th power zero for every generic Q. The q-multinomial formula then shows that J_b(Q)=C(Q)^N/(1-Q^N) is regular at Q_N. Denote its root value by J_b. It lowers total integer position by N, so J_b^b=0. The [divided Ward fusion proof](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md) gives the matrix definitions, all root characters, and arbitrary-block associativity. The following derivation identifies its correction directly with the whole function (3). Since C(Q) is nilpotent for generic Q, evaluating (5) at -t C(Q) involves only finitely many terms. For m<N its root value is the corresponding coefficient of log f_N(-t C). For m>=N not divisible by N, C(Q)^m has a factor 1-Q^N while its denominator is a unit, so the term vanishes at the root. For m=kN with k>=2 the numerator has k such factors and the denominator only one, so it also vanishes. The remaining term, m=N, is exactly (-t)^N J_b/N. Consequently [F(Q,-t C(Q))]_root =exp[(-t)^N J_b/N] f_N(-t C). (16a) Here the exponential terminates before its b-th power. Equivalently, if A_i are the individual raising operators dressed by all later K factors, q-binomial expansion gives product_(i=b,...,1) f_N(-t A_i) =exp[(-t)^N J_b/N] f_N(-t C). (16b) Thus the exact finite tensor defect is the evaluated resonant logarithm of the all-level function. In the coordinate of (6), C(Q)^N=(1-Q^N)J_b(Q)=-N h J_b+O(h^2). Substituting this into -Li_2((-t C(Q))^N)/(N^2 h) gives the same (-t)^N J_b/N; all its higher dilogarithm powers vanish after specialization. This comparison uses the moving representation and retains its first normal. Substituting C^N=0 before taking the quotient would delete the entire correction. This is a general tensor theorem, with a nilpotence bound independent of N for fixed b. It is not a scalar growth theorem. Ordinary pivotal closure kills a degree-N lowering insertion. A marked missing-edge insertion can compensate that degree, and its divided Hopf-adjoint pairing with the literal cut is computed in the fusion note. A source comparison must retain that relative pairing before contraction. ## 6. A controlled norm theorem on an actual cyclic gauge chart The local reconstruction also admits an analytic norm estimate. This is a different parameter direction from the fixed-root h in (6)--(8): now N varies, Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), and hbar_N=2pi*i/N. Fix 0<r<1 and use the branches continued from z=0. Uniformly for |z|<=r, Log g_(D,N)(z) =-Li_2(z)/hbar_N-(1/2)Log(1-z)+O_r(1/N). (17) To prove it, put f_z(x)=x Log(1-z exp(2pi*i*x)). The function and its first two x derivatives are uniformly bounded on this compact chart. The finite product is Log D_N(z)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) f_z(j/N). Trapezoidal Euler summation therefore gives Log D_N=N integral_0^1 f_z(x)dx -(1/2)Log(1-z)+O_r(1/N). Termwise integration of the absolutely convergent logarithmic series gives integral_0^1 f_z=-Li_2(z)/(2pi*i). The normalization in (11) changes this by O_r(r^N), since Log nu_N=Log(1-z^N)/N. This proves (17), with both upper and lower norm control. It is an estimate of the specific marked cyclic gauge already identified in Section 4, not a choice of a new quantum state. For example an explicit bound for the absolute remainder in (17) is B_r/(12N)+r^N/[2(1-r^N)], B_r=4pi r/(1-r)+4pi^2 r/(1-r)^2. The displayed B_r bounds |f_z''|. The ordinary composite trapezoidal remainder, multiplied by N, gives its first term; |Log(1-z^N)|<=r^N/(1-r^N) gives the second. Thus no interchange of a divergent infinite root product and a limit is used. In particular its inverse has rate (2pi/N)log|g_(D,N)(z)^(-1)| -> Im Li_2(z). (18) The full local regulator uses the logarithmic metric term in (15). On a marked chart define the metrized inverse gauge by ||g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)||_reg =|g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)| exp[(N/(2pi))Log|z| Arg(1-z)]. (19) Then (2pi/N)log||g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)||_reg -> D(z), (20) with O_r(1/N) error on fixed compact marked subcharts. At z=0 the metric extends by continuity if needed. Formula (19) is the explicit metric on the local Heisenberg period line determined by (15); it is not an additional factor inserted into the actual Kashaev invariant. A global knot comparison must still show that its quantum period carries this metric with the prescribed signs and logarithmic transition functions. ## 7.
