What the local identification does not imply globally This replaces the obstructed fixed-N multiplicative comparison by an explicit coherent all-level function and its marked cyclotomic period. It proves an exact local source/gauge/regulator identification for a block built from the actual quantum matrices. To use it for the knot, the local transfer currents and their inserted moments must still be transported through the full source-preserving contraction. The selected cycle and cross-level metric cannot be inferred from agreement of local factors. For example, ordinary finite factorial ratios are regular at their roots because their polar terms cancel; extracting a pole from an individual infinite factor and forgetting that cancellation would not be a valid knot-period argument. The actual Newton period, the partially summed geometric block, and its marked knot Bloch action already exist in the other notes. Their remaining comparison must use the unfolded source complex, retaining the normal edge and all peripheral factors. Neither global source survival nor the general volume conjecture is asserted here. [Exact coefficient audit](../experiments/audit_unfolded_ward_factorial_regulator.py). [Results](../experiments/unfolded_ward_factorial_regulator_results.json). [Independent proof audit](unfolded_ward_factorial_independent_audit.md). [Independent moving-representation and cut audit](divided_ward_bridge_independent_audit.md). The [global function/source audit](global_period_rigidity_function_audit.md) records the extra selected-period information still required beyond this exact local function reconstruction.

title: Independent audit of the unfolded Ward factorial
text: # Independent audit of the unfolded Ward factorial Research audit, 27 October 2026. The formulas in [the unfolding theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) pass an independent coefficientwise proof check. This audit does not assert a global network-period identity. ## 1. All-level uniqueness Fix a coefficient index `j`. For all sufficiently large `N>j`, the actual nilpotent jet prescribes the value `c_j(Q_N)=1/(Q_N;Q_N)_j`; neither denominator vanishes there. A nonzero rational function has finitely many zeros, while the `Q_N` are infinitely many distinct points. Thus the coefficient is uniquely `1/(Q;Q)_j`. The exceptional set can depend on `j`. No common bound in `j` on degrees or exceptional levels is required. This proves uniqueness in the specified rational coefficient class, and the displayed universal factorial supplies existence in this case. ## 2. Cyclotomic pole and constant The formal logarithm is log F(Q,z)=sum_(m>=1) z^m/[m(1-Q^m)]. Put `Q=zeta exp(h)`, with `zeta` primitive of order `N` and `X=z^N`. For `m=kN`, 1/[m(1-exp(mh))]=-1/(m^2 h)+1/(2m)+O(h). The pole is therefore `-Li_2(X)/N^2`. The resonant constant is `Li_1(X)/(2N)=-Log(1-X)/(2N)`. For `D_N=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta^j z)^(j/N)`, the coefficient of `z^m` in its logarithm is -1/(mN) sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j zeta^(jm). For nonresonant `m`, this equals `1/[m(1-zeta^m)]`, exactly the constant of `log F`. For `m=kN`, it is `-(N-1)/(2kN)`, so the whole resonant part of `log D_N` is `(N-1)Log(1-X)/(2N)`. Subtracting `Log(1-X)/2` leaves precisely the resonant constant of `log F`. This checks the sign and every factor of `N` in the pole and regular part. The parameter `h=Log(Q/zeta)` here is a fixed-root deformation parameter. It is not the earlier large-level parameter `Log q` with `q_N=exp(pi*i/N)`. ## 3. Norm-root gauge and its uniqueness The marked cyclic product satisfies D_N(zeta z)/D_N(z)=(1-z)/(1-X)^(1/N), product_(a=0)^(N-1) D_N(zeta^a z) =(1-X)^((N-1)/2). Both follow directly by rearranging the marked logarithms, hence hold for even and composite `N` as well. With `nu=(1-X)^(1/N)`, the gauge g_D=D_N/nu^((N-1)/2) has norm one and the required normalized cyclic transport. Its nilpotent specialization has constant one and solves the same coefficient recurrence as the literal actual factorial. It therefore equals that finite factorial modulo `e^N`. The ratio of this gauge and the previously constructed norm-root gauge is sigma invariant, hence scalar in the completed base: the basis `1,e,...,e^(N-1)` has distinct sigma eigenvalues. Its norm is its `N`-th power. The identity marking forces this scalar to be one. This proves equality on the completed common marked cover, rather than merely equality of norms. The even-`N` square root is fixed by the same identity mark. For the actual cyclic sign `e^N=(-1)^(N+1)kappa_N`, substitution `z=-te` gives `X=-kappa_N t^N` and `1-X=1+kappa_N t^N`, with no remaining parity sign. ## 4. Period and source conventions For `S=Li_2(X)+UV`, `U=Log X`, `V=Log(1-X)`, direct differentiation gives `dS=U dV`. Thus the stated Heisenberg matrix has `Pi^(-1)dPi` with zero central entry; equivalently its right equation is `dPi=Pi Omega`. The opposite Maurer--Cartan convention would require a different central coordinate. Since `d kappa_N/d kappa=N` at completion, partial_kappa[-Li_2(-kappa_N t^N)/N^2]_(kappa=0)=t^N/N. The actual divided affine source is `-t^N`, exactly minus `N` times this normal derivative. The local Bloch--Wigner logarithmic metric term is retained by the displayed regulator formula. ## 5. Identity-meridian formal rigidity is already available [The closed-braid period note](closed_braid_period_line.md), Section 4, already proves that an Artinian representation with every meridian congruent to identity factors through knot abelianization. Its induction is valid: if all meridians agree modulo `m^r` and lie in `I+m`, their pairwise commutators lie in `m^(r+1)`. A Wirtinger crossing then equates consecutive understrand meridians modulo `m^(r+1)`. A knot has one connected understrand cycle, so all agree at the next order. Nilpotence terminates the induction. For matrix groups this argument does not require characteristic zero. More generally it applies whenever the identity congruence filtration satisfies `[G_r,G_s] subset G_(r+s)`. For the present `SL_2` application it proves the stated Artin functor equality and the claimed formal inability to reach nonabelian geometry from the identity representation. It says nothing analogous about a noncentral parabolic meridian or a different residual representation.

title: A uniform Frobenius base for the source and its marked period
text: # A uniform Frobenius base for the source and its marked period Research note, 26 October 2026. This places the actual scalar source coefficients at all levels on one difference base, retaining the Frobenius coordinate and root phases. A standard multiplicative-to- additive group model resolves the quantum--meridian point. The normalized two-channel source algebra extends there. A second marked chart evaluates the original central-pole normalization as a whole. The resulting Frobenius period is explicit and regular in h^2. This is the universal root-center period, not the knot's selected Bloch period. The global source comparison and volume conjecture remain unproved. ## 1. Keep the Frobenius coordinate independent before restricting a root Use the fixed literature parameter q_N=exp(pi*i/N) and meridian M. Introduce independent coordinates q,M,w and the finite phase cover zeta^4=1, U=w^2, sigma(q)=q, sigma(M)=qM, sigma(w)=-w, sigma(zeta)=zeta. (1.1) The actual root graph is Gamma_N: q=q_N, w=M^N, zeta=i^(1-N). (1.2) It is sigma-stable because q_N^N=-1. The phases are exactly zeta_N=q_N^(N(1-N)/2), epsilon_N=(-1)^N=-zeta_N^2, eta_N=i^(N+3)=zeta_N^3. No phase is reset independently at a level. The coefficient field on each phase component is C(q,M,w), with constant field C(q,U). (1.3) For a proof, sigma^2 fixes w and scales M by q^2. A rational invariant in M cannot have a finite nonzero pole, since its infinite q^2 orbit would also be poles. It is therefore Laurent in M, and invariance forces all nonzero M exponents to vanish. The remaining sigma invariance is w->-w, giving C(q,w^2). Adjoining the shift T gives the exact relations TM=qMT, Tw=-wT. Under (1.2), the second is the ordinary root identity T M^N=q_N^N M^N T. Thus this base extends the literature coefficient algebra and recovers it at each specified root. It does not impose monodromy one on a quantum-A module. Here w is a half-Frobenius meridian coordinate; it is not the geometric longitude or the norm-torsor spectral variable. The original normalization functions are now fixed rational functions: rho=q-q^(-1), f=M-M^(-1), d=zeta^3 f/(w-w^(-1)), C_cut=-zeta U/[(U-1)(U+1)], epsilon=-zeta^2, delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), nu=epsilon rho^2, A=epsilon rho(M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(w+w^(-1)). (1.4) They restrict to the actual full ADO dimension, cut line and adjacent-source overlap. Direct substitution gives sigma(d)/d=-f(qM)/f(M), sigma(C_cut)=C_cut. The central divisor U=1 and the half-root sign of w are retained. ## 2. Root graphs give a genuine algebraic rigidity test On each fixed phase component, the union of Gamma_N for infinitely many N in its residue class modulo four is Zariski dense. Indeed clear denominators of a proposed identity and write P(q,M,w)=sum_(a,b) f_(a,b)(q)M^a w^b. Let D_M be the span of its finitely many M exponents. If N>D_M, the exponents a+Nb for distinct pairs (a,b) are distinct. Restriction to Gamma_N is therefore zero only if every f_(a,b)(q_N) is zero. Infinitely many distinct q_N force these fixed polynomials to vanish. This proves the density assertion, including complex coefficients and every phase component. There is a finite-degree version over a number field K. After clearing denominators let D_q be the q degree and D_M the M exponent span. If N>D_M, phi(2N)>[K:Q] D_q, (2.1) then an exact whole-graph identity at that one level proves the generic identity on that phase component. The algebraic degree of q_N over K is at least phi(2N)/[K:Q], so each polynomial f_(a,b) has degree too small to vanish at q_N unless it is zero. For K=Q(i), the sufficient bound is phi(2N)>2D_q. The graph must lie in the domain of the cleared comparison. The degree hypotheses are essential: w-M^N vanishes on a single graph, and a cyclotomic polynomial vanishes at its q_N. Neither satisfies the relevant strict bound. Checking only M=1,w=1, or a few unspecified meridian samples, is not a whole-graph certificate. The actual knot period is not assumed to have this fixed rational presentation or these degree bounds. The test concerns source coefficients and proposed algebraic comparison maps once their bounds have been established. ## 3. The deformation group is an existing definition The standard group scheme G^(lambda)=Spec R[t,1/(1+lambda t)] is recalled in [Mezard--Romagny--Tossici, Section 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1104.2222v1#S1.SS2). We use this definition with lambda=rho and M=1+rho*t. Its group law and inverse follow directly by multiplying M: t*tprime=t+tprime+rho*t*tprime, t^(-1)=-t/(1+rho*t). (3.1) For rho invertible it is G_m, while its rho=0 fiber is G_a. This is existing group-scheme theory. Only the abstract and this definition were consulted; no isogeny, extension, or classification proof from that source is assumed here. Symmetric source coordinates near M=1 are s=(M-M^(-1))/rho, c=M+M^(-1), c^2-rho^2 s^2=4, M=(c+rho*s)/2. (3.2) This is the selected c=2 chart of the same deformation, since s=t(2+rho*t)/(1+rho*t). Its group law is (s,c)*(sprime,cprime) =((s cprime+c sprime)/2, (c cprime+rho^2 s sprime)/2). (3.3) Multiplication preserves the displayed norm; associativity follows either by expansion or by the M multiplication law. On the exceptional identity fiber rho=0,c=2 it becomes addition of s. This resolves the ideal (rho,M-1) in the meridian chart. The original meridian step is multiplication by (1,q+q^(-1)): sigma(s)=((q+q^(-1))s+c)/2, sigma(c)=(rho^2 s+(q+q^(-1))c)/2. (3.4) It preserves c^2-rho^2s^2 and has determinant one. Meridian inversion is (s,c,w)->(-s,c,w^(-1)); direct multiplication gives the relation inversion*sigma*inversion=sigma^(-1). At the exceptional identity fiber the action is exactly sigma(s)=s+1, sigma(w)=-w. (3.5) Charge is the ordinary multiplication map of this group. For the cubic source it is (M,w)->(M^3,w^3), equivalently s->s(c^2-1), c->c^3-3c. It intertwines the original meridian step with the third source step, retaining the charge from the actual projective source construction. ## 4. The normalized adjacent source extends over the exceptional fiber Let p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2), r=sigma(p), and k=q+q^(-1). On (3.2), p/rho=(k s c-(c^2-2))/2=:p_hat, r/rho=(k s c+(c^2-2))/2=:r_hat. (4.1) Their difference is c^2-2, a unit near c=2. Thus the old point ideal (p,r) pulls back to the principal ideal (rho); its proper transform has no residual point. This resolves the nonfree rank-one factor (u,h) in the earlier cyclic source lattice. The exceptional factor rho remains a specified line and divisor; principalizing the ideal does not discard that source datum. Normalize the source numerators by their recorded factor nu: d_hat=delta/nu=epsilon*s*c, a_hat=A/nu=c*r_hat/(w+w^(-1)). (4.2) Here epsilon^2=1 on the phase cover. These are regular on the chosen chart with w+w^(-1) invertible. The two coefficient matrices from the actual source become t_1_hat=[d_hat a_hat;0 0], t_2_hat=[0 0;a_hat d_hat]. On the exceptional identity fiber, d_hat=2 epsilon*s, a_hat=2(2s+1)/(w+w^(-1)). (4.3) At s=0,w=1 their matrix-algebra generators have nonzero units: a_hat=1 and a_hat^2-d_hat^2=1. Thus their multiplicity algebra and local scalar comparison torsor extend over the joint quantum--meridian degeneration. This resolves the shrinking fixed-level unit in the preceding normal-form note. It is the two-channel coefficient algebra that extends; the N-dimensional color factor and full knot section have not been algebraized. The original numerator matrices are exactly nu*t_i_hat on every root graph. The original projectors are t_i_hat/d_hat, so this normalization retains their full germs and defines no new state. The full affine factor has the uniform expression (1+w^(-2))*a_hat/d_hat =epsilon*w^(-1)*r_hat/s. (4.4) Its exceptional value is epsilon*w^(-1)(2s+1)/s. The pole at s=0 and the central cap at w^2=1 stay in the relative model; normalizing the numerators has not discarded either of them. The earlier obstruction to a common lattice for both unscaled projectors is consequently still present. ## 5. One marked Frobenius period realizes every prescribed root Put h=Log q and retain the original Tate mark tau=pi*i, so N h_N=tau. On the identity chart let u(h,s)=arsinh(s sinh h), M=exp(u), log w_per=(tau/h)arsinh(s sinh h). (5.1) This is the selected solution of M-M^(-1)=rho*s with M=1 at s=0. The quotient in (5.1) is regular at h=0, since u is odd in h. More precisely log w_per=tau*s+tau*(s-s^3)h^2/6+O(h^4). It is analytic in h^2 locally for bounded s. At h=h_N it is exactly N Log M, so w_per=M^N as a whole germ. Translation by q gives u->u+h, hence w_per->exp(tau)w_per=-w_per. Thus this one period section respects the original meridian action and recovers (1.2), rather than choosing unrelated sections at different levels. At the exceptional fiber it is the horizontal period dlog w_per=tau ds, w_per(0)=1, w_per=exp(tau*s). (5.2) This is an algebraic line with connection and a marked horizontal period, not a rational function of s. A regular algebraic group homomorphism G_a->G_m is constant: its defining function is an invertible polynomial, hence constant, and its identity value is one. Thus the nonzero Tate marking cannot be replaced by an algebraic character on the exceptional additive fiber. Retaining the period comparison is necessary even though its coefficient group and connection are algebraic. All normalized scalar source formulas in (4.1)--(4.3), and the source step (3.4), are even in h after this period section is substituted on a fixed phase component. Indeed c=2sqrt(1+s^2 sinh^2 h), k=2cosh h, and w_per are all even in h. This parity does not assert parity or regularity of the knot's geometric exponential exp(S/h). ## 6. The pole normalization becomes a marked regular evaluation The point s=0,w=1 alone does not evaluate d/rho: its expression is zeta^3*s/(w-w^(-1)). Retain the second chart w=1+s*ell, ell invertible. (6.1) Then the whole normalized dimension and cap are regular: d/rho=zeta^3*w/[ell(w+1)], s*C_cut=-zeta*w^2/[ell(w+1)(w^2+1)]. (6.2) Their complete values are zeta^3/(2ell) and -zeta/(4ell). The actual graph fixes the slope, not only the point: ell_N=(dw/ds)|_(s=0)=N rho_N/2. (6.3) Combining (6.2)--(6.3) recovers exactly d_N(1)=zeta_N^3/N. On the uniform period section this slope is ell(h)=tau*sinh h/h, d(h,0)=zeta^3*h/tau. (6.4) Thus the central normalization is a regular evaluation on a marked chart, including its transverse root-graph direction. No separate zero or pole was evaluated. At the exceptional fiber ell=tau; the period marking fixes that value. The meridian translates this marked chart to the other cap charts. Its orbit is not a single invariant point; those arrows remain in the lattice/source groupoid. This construction does not make all adjacent projector arrows integral on one lattice. ## 7. Scope and verification This supplies a uniform difference base for the actual source coefficients, its standard group deformation, a regular normalized two-channel algebra, and one marked Frobenius period with exact root restrictions. It also gives an algebraic rigidity test for bounded comparisons. These replace levelwise coefficient choices by specified functions and period data. The horizontal section above is the universal Frobenius period. It is not the knot's marked Bloch regulator. An actual global source/section comparison with the positive triangulation still has to be constructed, with all matrix and lattice transitions. The root-graph density theorem does not apply to an unknown comparison without its fixed presentation and degree bounds. The source coefficient algebra does not determine the scalar coefficient of the geometric exponential in the selected period. The subsequent [whole-period reconstruction](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) extends this root-only base by an independent v=q^N and t=1/N. Its action is sigma(w)=vw, with commuting derivatives D_q=q partial_q+t^(-1)v partial_v and D_M=M partial_M+t^(-1)w partial_w. The slice v=-1 recovers the base here but is not preserved by D_q. Thus quantum-normal jets require this extension before specialization. Bounded mixed jets then reconstruct any proposed fixed algebraic comparison, including one on a marked etale shape cover. This does not algebraize the full knot state or construct the missing map. The [fixed central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) controls a comparison factor once its fixed finite algebraic presentation is proved. It does not supply that global comparison. The volume conjecture remains unproved. The subsequent [common Frobenius/regulator period space](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) now puts this Frobenius mark and the geometric regulator action over one explicit logarithmic Heisenberg connection. Its additional Tate period J recovers all four root phases; unlike a frozen phase sheet it carries the q-direction connection. The full complete cap is -i J h/(pi*i), and the geometric exponential retains its volume term. Adjoining the rational Frobenius coordinate preserves an existing nonsplit source class, by a Laurent-coefficient retraction. Thus the common period space does not by itself supply the missing actual source comparison. [The audit](../experiments/audit_uniform_source_base.py) verifies the group law, Weyl and meridian matrices, normalized source and cap identities, and period-section translation through h^6. Four phase sheets verify bounded-degree exponent separation and cyclotomic factor degrees. Fourteen root levels verify the original phases and marked complete normalization, with 28 generic scalar root-graph specializations. These are source-base checks, not quantum-volume experiments. [Results](../experiments/uniform_source_base_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_uniform_source_base.py

title: A uniform norm group and sourced relation complex for twist knots
text: # A uniform norm group and sourced relation complex for twist knots Research note, 27 October 2026. This proves the one-relator side of the determinant reduction suggested by the 4_1 and 5_2 prototypes. The twist parameter remains arbitrary throughout. The construction comes from the actual knot-group relation, with its return-map sign and matrix normal direction retained. It does not assign a replacement quantum state or establish the selected Kashaev period's volume growth. ## 1. Uniform statement Use the signed twist presentation G_k=<a,b | a w^k=w^k b>, w=ab^(-1)a^(-1)b, k in Z, k!=0. The hyperbolic members have k<=-1 or k>=2. Set A=[1 1;0 1], B=[1 0;t 1], W=AB^(-1)A^(-1)B, z=t^2+2, v=1+t, P_k(t)=S_(k-1)(z), f_k(t)=v S_(k-1)(z)-S_(k-2)(z), (1.1) where S_(-1)=0,S_0=1,S_(j+1)=z S_j-S_(j-1), extended to all integer indices. **Theorem.** For every k!=0: 1. The pair (f_k,P_k) is obtained by powers of one explicit norm-one unit in a quadratic algebra. Its norm identity is f_k^2+t(t-2)f_k P_k-t^3 P_k^2=1. 2. The matrix return relator has an exact quadratic normal form in f_k. On t!=0, its full matrix equation generates the scheme-theoretic ideal (f_k), retaining its first jet. 3. The polynomial f_k is monic with constant term one and is squarefree, even modulo 2. The classes of t and P_k are integral units in Z[t]/(f_k). 4. At every parabolic root, the sourced relation complex is acyclic. With the orbit-volume and matrix-source marks specified below, its torsion is exactly T_k^rel=-2/[P_k(t) f_k'(t)]. (1.2) 5. The weighted residue on the full integral Riley algebra is a perfect pairing. Its branch coefficient is 1/[P_k(t)f_k'(t)], including all conjugate places. This theorem is uniform in k. The comparison T_k^rel=T_beta with the braid complex is proved by the existing exact prototype calculations for k=-1,2; a general presentation and quantum-source comparison is still required. No general Gaussian-density or volume identity is inferred merely by giving the relation torsion the same name. ## 2. A single quadratic norm group solves the twist transport Put b=t(t-2) and introduce the quadratic algebra E=Q(t)[y]/(y^2-b y-t^3). The norm of F+P y is N(F+P y)=F^2+b F P-t^3 P^2. (2.1) Let u=1+t+y. Direct multiplication gives N(u)=1, and multiplication by u in the basis 1,y is U=[1+t t^3;1 t^2-t+1], det U=1, Tr U=t^2+2. (2.2) Consequently (f_k,P_k)^t=U^k(1,0)^t (2.3) for every integer k. This follows either from the Chebyshev recurrence or from U^2-z U+I=0 and the initial values (f_0,P_0)=(1,0), (f_1,P_1)=(1+t,1). Taking norms proves f_k^2+b f_k P_k-t^3 P_k^2=1. (2.4) This is transport in an existing quadratic norm-one group, with a specified unit and source point. It is not the root-of-unity norm torsor of the quantum A-operator. The generic splitting cover has discriminant t^2(t^2+4). Twisting the diagram is not a manifold cover; those operations are not being identified. The algebra has a literal matrix realization: Y=W^(-1)-vI, Tr Y=b, det Y=-t^3, u -> W^(-1), W^(-k)=f_k I+P_k Y. (2.5) Thus (2.3) is the spectral transport of the meridian commutator itself, rather than a chosen auxiliary recurrence. ## 3. Exact matrix relator and its normal direction The base identity A W-W B=v(A-B), followed by Cayley--Hamilton, gives A W^k-W^k B=f_k(A-B). (3.1) Define V=(A-B)B^(-1)=[-t 1;-t 0], Z=(A-B)B^(-1)Y=[-t^2 2t(t-1);0 t^2], V^#=Tr(V)I-V=[0 -1;t -t]. The inverse return relation is A W^k B^(-1)W^(-k)=I+P_k f_k Z+f_k^2 V. Its inverse, with the same output-minus-input convention as dF-I in the braid complex, is R_k=W^k B W^(-k)A^(-1) =I-P_k f_k Z+f_k^2 V^#. (3.2) These are exact identities. The first follows from (3.1) and (2.5). For the second use determinant one and adj(I+X)=I+Tr(X)I-X in dimension two. In particular Tr R_k=2-t f_k^2, R_k-I=-P_k f_k Z modulo f_k^2, Tr Z=0, det Z=-t^4. (3.3) The trace alone loses the first normal direction. The marked matrix equation retains it in the nonzero vector Z. For completeness, the full ideal of entries of R_k-I in Q[t,t^(-1)] is (f_k). The entries give P_k f_k and f_k^2, since t is a unit. Equation (2.4) gives (f_k,P_k)=(1), so these two generators generate f_k itself. The converse inclusion is immediate from (3.2). This is a statement about schemes, including nilpotent test rings. ## 4. All parabolic roots are simple; the source unit is integral For k>0, f_k has degree 2k-1 and leading coefficient one. For k=-h<0 it has degree 2h and leading coefficient one, using S_(-j-2)=-S_j. Since S_j(2)=j+1, f_k(0)=k-(k-1)=1. (4.1) To prove squarefreeness uniformly, work over F_2. Put P(t)=overline(S_(k-1)(t)), Q(t)=overline(S_(k-2)(t)). Frobenius and t^2+2=t^2 give overline(f_k)=(1+t)P(t)^2+Q(t)^2, overline(f_k')=P(t)^2. Consecutive Chebyshev polynomials are coprime over every field: their recurrence reduces a common divisor to the pair S_0=1,S_(-1)=0. Thus gcd(overline(f_k),overline(f_k'))=1. Since f_k is monic, its resultant with its derivative is an odd nonzero integer. All characteristic-zero roots are therefore simple, without a genericity hypothesis. Let B_k=Z[t]/(f_k). Equation (4.1) makes t an integral unit. Equation (2.4) gives, in this algebra, t^3 P_k^2=-1, P_k^(-1)=-t^3 P_k. (4.2) Thus the source factor is an integral unit, not a factor silently canceled only at generic complex points. ## 5. The sourced relation complex and its normalization Let O be the noncentral trace-two conjugacy class in SL_2. At a parabolic root, the pair (A,B) is irreducible because t!=0. PGL_2 conjugation has an injective three-dimensional tangent, and its quotient on O times O has coordinate t=Tr(AB)-2. Let L be the one-dimensional matrix normal line spanned by Z in (3.3), with the specified generator Z. Differentiating the return relation on the fixed-trace pair space gives the complex 0 -> sl_2 --a--> T_(A,B)(O times O) --dR_k--> L -> 0, a(xi)=([xi,A],[xi,B]), dR_k=-P_k f_k'(t) dt times Z. (5.1) The derivative kills conjugation because R_k=I. It is nonzero in the remaining direction by Sections 3--4. The complex is therefore acyclic at every root of f_k. The source normalization is explicit. Use the ordered sl_2 basis H=diag(1,-1), E=E_12, F=E_21. On a fixed trace class use nu=dK wedge de/e for the matrix entries K=G_11,e=G_12. At A use (A_11,A_12); at B use (B_11,B_21), so nu_B=-dB_11 wedge dB_21/t. Both forms are invariant under conjugation. In the four tangent coordinates (A_11,A_12,B_11,B_21), the conjugation columns and the normal vector partial_t are [a(H),a(E),a(F),partial_t] =[0 0 -1 0;2 0 0 0;0 t 0 0;-2t 0 0 1]. Its determinant is -2t. The product orbit volume has coefficient -1/t, so its value on these columns is 2. The last differential in (5.1), expressed in the marked Z basis, is -P_k f_k'. Therefore the torsion is exactly T_k^rel=2/(-P_k f_k')=-2/(P_k f_k'). (5.2) Changing the complement by a conjugation column changes neither determinant. Conjugating the pair transports all the stated volume and source marks, so the scalar is frame invariant. Reversing the return relation would reverse the sign; no unmarked sign is being ignored. ## 6. A perfect residue pairing on the entire integral algebra For a monic degree-d polynomial f define Res_f(h) to be the coefficient of t^(d-1) in the remainder of h modulo f. Set lambda_k(h)=Res_(f_k)(P_k^(-1)h). (6.1) The pairing (g,h)->Res_f(gh) on Z[t]/(f) is perfect: its matrix in 1,t,...,t^(d-1) has zeros below its anti-diagonal and ones on that diagonal. Its determinant is (-1)^(d(d-1)/2). Multiplication by the integral unit P_k^(-1) preserves perfection, proving the claim for lambda_k as well. No localization at a discriminant prime is needed for the whole algebra. After splitting into the distinct complex root lines, Lagrange interpolation gives lambda_k(h)=sum_(f_k(t_j)=0) h(t_j)/(P_k(t_j)f_k'(t_j)). (6.2) Hence the branch coefficient is exactly -T_k^rel/2. It is a canonical weighted residue in a finite integral algebra, with its conjugate branches retained. ## 7. What this settles and what it does not The denominator and the -2 source normalization are now proved uniformly on the actual twist relator side. The commutator transport, exact normal form, all-root regularity and integral residue pairing have proofs for arbitrary k. They are not conclusions inferred from the prototypes. The existing prototype computation proves T_k^rel=T_beta and Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2 for k=-1,2. For arbitrary k, the next required map is the determinant- and source-preserving reduction from the braid period complex to (5.1), including its quantum lattice. The classical group relation alone does not supply that map. Even after that map, the actual global quantum source must have its regulator norm controlled across levels. This note does not prove the original volume conjecture, or replace Kashaev by the classical residue (6.1). The general program now uses the [arbitrary-bridge sourced complex](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md), with unrestricted bridge number and crossing word. The calculation above is retained as a one-relator diagnostic. A separate executable uniform-twist audit is not attached to this proof text.

title: An actual cut with a universal complete framing pole
text: # An actual cut with a universal complete framing pole Research theorem, 27 October 2026. For every complete discrete-faithful knot representation, an exact inverse-pair insertion in the original braid places a noncommuting meridian on the first slot at a second physical cut. The actual prefix there is V=I. Its Fourier momentum is a Möbius coordinate whose inverse framing map and density have pole p=1, independent of the knot and first framing phase. The added crossings have a nonempty regular atom chart, so the existing nonzero geometric normal block persists. This is an actual source-preserving choice of presentation and cut. It does not replace the selected source by sampling its principal density. That density is resonant at EVERY level. Controlling its whole quantum completion and the original selected class remains the missing geometric-period theorem. Subsequent exact source calculation: the [complete first-slot localization theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) proves J_(a,j)=P_N delta_(j,0) for EVERY first input, and in fact L(X_j)=P_N X_j. Thus the original regular Fourier rows j!=0 vanish identically at completeness. The missing geometric-period comparison concerns the resonant row. An [actual all-strand Euler/Cauchy formula](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md) now supplies its finite source as an exact coefficient or two-point divided difference, with the entire word retained. ## 1. Choose a meridian that does not fix the reference cusp Fix a b-strand braid presenting the knot and the complete marked holonomy. Normalize the reference meridian to J=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Write its initial developed meridians as mu_1=J,...,mu_b, using the signed convention of [the actual prefix dictionary](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md). Some mu_i has nonzero lower-left entry, since otherwise the representation is reducible. Choose the first such i. Every preceding mu_j is J, not merely another upper triangular matrix. Indeed mu_j=g J g inverse. If mu_j has lower-left zero, its unique fixed point is infinity, hence g also fixes infinity. In a torsion-free discrete projective group containing J, every upper triangular word has diagonal ratio one. Otherwise suitable conjugates of J, or their commutators with J, tend nontrivially to the identity; a nontrivial finite-order ratio gives projective torsion. This is the elementary discreteness argument already proved in the Fourier framing theorem. Such a g commutes with J. Put U=mu_i. It is nontrivial trace-two unipotent, with c=U_21 nonzero, and has the unique form U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), beta=(U_22-1)/c. (1) The rows/columns in (1) have zero contraction, so this expression retains determinant one and the actual meridian orientation. ## 2. Move it with a literal inverse pair, preserving every source factor Use inverse Hurwitz moves (X,Y) -> (Y,YXY inverse). Let P be the braid whose ACTION order is sigma_(i-1) inverse,...,sigma_1 inverse. It moves U left unchanged past the preceding J's. Insert the action words P then P inverse before the original action word beta_braid. The matrix order is R_beta_braid R_P inverse R_P=R_beta_braid. (2) The second cut is the FIRST physical slot between P and P inverse. At that level its developed meridian is exactly U; its physical prefix products are therefore V=I, U=mu_i, prefix sign sigma=-1. (3) The original first cut and its reference J are untouched. Closing the second cut with its original identity gives (2). The first output row, fixed-input source, all original pivotal caps and full d_N(M) line remain the original ones. Strand number and writhe are unchanged; the presentation acquires at most 2(b-1) crossings, independently of N. At an actual root use the genuine signed crossing matrices and their inverses. For a whole auxiliary q-normal calculation use the specified whole inverse matrices BEFORE specialization, so (2) is still an exact matrix identity and preserves all its jets. No inverse is obtained by first deleting a central norm factor. The second cut is at slot ell=0. The EXACT open meridian insertion therefore has no endpoint q^(-ell nu) character, by [the actual horizontal transport theorem](actual_open_meridian_horizontal_source_transport.md). Its Fourier dilation and scaled-frame correction are identity. The original gamma_N, x=-M/q and full meridian ratio g_N are still retained; their absence is not implied by ell=0. ## 3. The added crossings have a nonempty regular geometric chart Use the actual complete framing matrix F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], s nonzero, t=r+beta s. For h preceding J's set a_h=ell_(J^h)=1+hs, b_h=ell_(U J^h) =a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). (4) One negative move carrying U left across J has actual physical positions A,B and transfer C A=a_h/a_(h+1), B=a_(h+1)/b_(h+1), C=a_(h+1)b_h/[b_(h+1)a_h]. (5) Its five balanced coefficient atoms at completeness are A, C, 1/B, AC, C/B =a_h/a_(h+1), C, b_(h+1)/a_(h+1), b_h/b_(h+1), b_h/a_h. (6) All are different from zero and one on a NONEMPTY Zariski open. For an explicit proof, in addition to their denominator factors exclude 1-t, t+hs, t+(h+1)s, s+c(1-t). The differences from one in (6) have these nonzero factors, and C-1=-c(1-t)^2/[b_(h+1)a_h]. (7) Every displayed factor is a nonzero rational function because c is nonzero. The finite intersection over h=0,...,i-2 is nonempty over the infinite marked representation field. It also intersects any existing nonempty regular framing open for the original word. Reversing a move has A'=B/C,B'=AC,C'=1/C. Its positive atoms are AC, 1/C, C/B, A, 1/B, so the inverse path introduces no new nondegeneracy condition. This verifies admissibility of the ACTUAL new crossings rather than assuming that an arbitrary identity insertion is regular. On this common open the added critical equations are the actual crossing graph followed by its inverse. Intermediate states eliminate uniquely over local Artin rings; the marked critical scheme is the original one. Thus its two framing tangent modes and regular Morse--Bott property are unchanged. Equivalently, each inverse pair is a generating-family stabilization: in regular input/output position coordinates its added normal block has form [[0,mu],[mu,*]] with mu a unit. Its determinant is -mu^2. The explicit local mixed coefficients are C/(1-C) for the negative move and 1/(1-C') for its positive inverse, C'=1/C; they are negatives of each other and are units on (6). The original nonzero normal Gaussian therefore persists. Fourier polarizing the new cut removes the remaining framing mode as in the proved bordered-Hessian theorem. This proves persistence, not equality of every old and new formal coefficient in arbitrary Gaussian frames. The marked fundamental cycle/action calibration remains the same, since the actual inverse path adds a cancelling relative cycle. All Gaussian phases and source lines must still be transported. ## 4. The complete momentum and leading density are universal Direct conjugation of (1) gives F inverse U F =I+(c/s)[1-t;-t] * (t,1-t). Its first diagonal is k=1+(c/s)t(1-t). With the ACTUAL slot-one prefix sign -1, the balanced momentum is p=-[(F inverse U F)_12]/(k-1) =1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s. (8) Consequently (A_cut,p), A_cut=1/(1+s), are birational framing coordinates, with partial_r p=1/t^2 nonzero. No new quadratic framing cover or arbitrary change of the finite band source is introduced. The actual Fourier stationary incidence is xi=p inverse because this second cut has ell=0. The original geometric framing density is exactly Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] =-p/[s(1-p)^2] dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. (9) Its only principal-density momentum pole is p=1, corresponding to r=infinity. At a root that point belongs to EVERY finite Fourier grid. This theorem is on the COMPLETE M=1 fiber; it does not assert a single generic-M double-pole model or freeze its normal splitting. ## 5. What has become universal, and what is still missing For the principal rational coefficient alone, the regular nodes p=Q_N^j, j=1,...,N-1, have the exact sum sum_(j=1)^(N-1) -Q_N^j/[s(1-Q_N^j)^2] =(N^2-1)/(12s). (10) This is the elementary inverse-sine-square identity already used in the source-current norm proof. It is NOT the original period: the omitted node p=1 is a pole of this coefficient, while the actual finite tensor and its raw Fourier array are regular. No principal sampling is justified at that node, and the local Gaussian expansion is not uniform near it. Higher coefficients and the full source can retain other shape-chart exclusions. Equation (8) specifies the escaping scale explicitly. If p=1-zeta/N, then r=N/zeta-beta s. (11) The fixed-label nodes near zero therefore leave every fixed compact framing chart as N grows. A fixed-r formal expansion cannot decide their selected contribution. The full quantum boundary layer, together with its actual word and current terms, must be retained. Equation (10) provides neither its missing value nor a no-cancellation theorem. More strongly, the exact actual localization just cited says the regular-node contribution of the original array is zero, even though the sum of this isolated PRINCIPAL coefficient is (10). That principal sum is therefore not a bulk approximation to the actual complete array. The geometric formal block can be nonzero while its exact regular-node source value vanishes. The critical-path gain is concrete: an actual source-preserving presentation now removes the prefix-dependent leading pole and the port meridian half-step for ANY complete discrete-faithful knot representation on its regular geometric branch. The chosen leading pole is the single fixed resonance p=1. This supplies a uniform location and scale for the next source comparison. It does not by itself reduce all remaining shape/global issues to a knot-independent cap or prove gate C, D or E of [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md). [Exact source, atom and normal-Hessian tests](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_cut.py) and [saved results](../experiments/universal_resonant_cut_results.json) support the direct proof. The [independent proof audit](universal_resonant_cut_independent_audit.md) checks the actual placement, admissible chart, prefix momentum and scope of the normal-block persistence. The separate [word/source audit](universal_resonant_cut_word_audit.md) also records the explicit mixed-Hessian stabilization and a carefully scoped meridian-germ calculation with its split poles.

title: Independent audit of the actual universal resonant cut
text: # Independent audit of the actual universal resonant cut 27 October 2026. The construction in [the universal-cut theorem](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) passes under its stated complete discrete-faithful and original regular geometric-chart hypotheses. It is an actual presentation/cut change, not only a conjugation of an abstract representation. The complete principal pole and port half-character become universal. The global selected-period comparison remains unproved. ## 1. The unchanged meridian can be moved by the specified actual word The initial braid meridians generate the knot group. If they all had lower-left entry zero, the representation would be reducible. Choose the first U with c=U_21 nonzero. A preceding upper parabolic is conjugate to J within the discrete faithful group. Its conjugator must fix infinity. An upper word with diagonal ratio not one either gives nontrivial translations tending to identity under conjugation, or has nontrivial finite projective order. Discreteness and torsion freeness exclude both. Its ratio is one, so it commutes with J and the preceding meridian is EXACTLY J. In the actual Hurwitz convention the NEGATIVE adjacent move is (J,U) -> (U,U J U^-1). Thus the indicated sequence carries U LEFT UNCHANGED. Placing this sequence P and then its inverse BEFORE the old action word means the literal operator R_beta R_P^-1 R_P. This order matters. Opening the first physical identity wire between the two words supplies the claimed prefix V=I and signed first-slot index -1. The original cut, its input/output source and all existing caps remain in place. Actual R inverses, including their full Cartan/scalar marks, give identity reclosure at every level. The added writhe is zero. The original d_N(M) line is unchanged as a rational map/lattice, not replaced by its complete value. The same inverse identity holds in the supplied whole finite auxiliary lift, hence with all its normal derivatives. None of these identities requires extending an auxiliary source-frame deformation to a knot representation. The cut is at slot ell=0, so the actual open meridian endpoint factor q^(-ell nu) is one. This removes that PORT character only. The original x=-M/q, gamma_N framing power, full g_N and every independent peripheral power remain, just as stated in the note. ## 2. Every added atom is regular on a nonempty common open Write U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), t=r+beta s, a_h=1+hs, b_h=a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). The displayed b_h equals (F^-1 U J^h F)_11 by direct multiplication. Before each negative move the prefixes are J^h,J^(h+1),U J^(h+1), so its actual clocks and transfer are exactly A=a_h/a_(h+1), B=a_(h+1)/b_(h+1), C=a_(h+1)b_h/[b_(h+1)a_h]. The five atoms are A,C,1/B,AC,C/B. Besides their nonzero numerator and denominator factors, their differences from one are controlled by 1-A=s/a_(h+1), 1-C=c(1-t)^2/[b_(h+1)a_h], b_h-a_h=(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs), b_(h+1)-a_(h+1)=(c/s)(1-t)(t+(h+1)s), b_(h+1)-b_h=s+c(1-t). Each excluded function is nonzero because c is nonzero and t,s are independent framing coordinates. Their finite product therefore defines a nonempty Zariski open. The framing surface is irreducible, so it intersects the original nonempty regular chart. This is a general nonemptiness proof, not inference from the figure-eight tests. For the inverse positive move, A'=B/C,B'=AC,C'=1/C. Its atoms are AC,1/C,C/B,A,1/B. Thus it adds no further conditions. All inverse paths are actual reversed graphs of these same moves. For a two-POSITION transverse chart also exclude 1-2t, since the new clock has r derivative (c/s)(1-2t). This is another nonzero factor and leaves a nonempty open. The Fourier (A,p) chart itself has derivative 1/t^2 and resolves that position caustic. ## 3. The Morse normal block persists on this open The existing actual phase/critical dictionary is an isomorphism of the exponentiated critical scheme with the framed representation germ on its unit-atom charts, including local Artin rings. Adding the crossing graphs and their inverses eliminates their intermediate states uniquely and recovers the OLD fixed representation equations. Thus the new critical germ still has precisely its two B_1 tangent modes. The added 2 length(P) flow variables increase the Hessian rank by that same number. Every VARIABLE principal amplitude is a unit on the constructed open, with its original base-only line retained separately, so its transverse formal Gaussian block remains nonzero. The generating-family stabilization wording has an explicit twist unit, not an additional unproved determinant hypothesis. In the original input/output position coordinates the exact mixed Hessians from the actual coefficients are V_-=C/(1-C), V_+=1/(1-C'). For C'=1/C these satisfy V_+=-V_-. They are units on the atom open C!=0,1. Consequently the extra cross block has the indicated form [[0,mu],[mu,*]], with mu a unit up to its unit coordinate factor, and determinant -mu^2. No additional excluded function or singular quantum-gap division is required here. More explicitly, the inverse-pair generating phase can be written F(y,q)-F(y,q+delta)+S_open(z,delta), with its actual inverse marks. The y equation forces delta=0 because F_yq is a unit; the delta equation then fixes y from the old momentum. Its reduced critical phase is S_open(z,0)=S_old(z), and the added (y,delta) Hessian has determinant -F_yq^2. The intermediate position and net displacement are unimodular integer coordinates in the two added transfers. This gives the direct stabilization proof recorded in the separate [word/source audit](universal_resonant_cut_word_audit.md). The original marked action calibration continues to apply to the new admissible diagram. The inverse path cancels its canonical graph and relative contribution, with the fixed phase/base line retained. This does NOT prove equality of every old/new formal coefficient in arbitrary frames, nor a global Gaussian/source pushforward. Finite matrix inversion alone would not justify those stronger statements. ## 4. The new complete prefix and density are genuinely universal Direct multiplication gives F^-1 U F=I+(c/s)[1-t;-t] * (t,1-t), k=1+(c/s)t(1-t). With the ACTUAL balanced/factorial momentum and first-slot sign, p=-(F^-1UF)_12/(k-1)=1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s. Thus at completeness the framing map is birational, without a new quadratic cover, and Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] =-p/[s(1-p)^2]dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. The pole p=1 belongs to the INVERSE framing map and density; the momentum p(r) itself has its pole at t=0. The universal density pole is at r=infinity and lies outside the proved fixed regular framing chart. At xi=p^-1 it is the fixed Fourier node xi=1, present at every N. This exact principal formula has not been promoted to a generic-M double-pole formula or a substitute for the full quantum source. The regular-node sum (N^2-1)/(12s) is correct. It excludes precisely the singular node and is not the selected knot period. Higher coefficients, original shape-chart exclusions and relative current endpoints still need their whole completion. The source-preserving word change therefore gives a useful uniform critical target, but does not close gates C, D or E. The main note's [exact actual audit](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_cut.py) checks its identities and normal examples. The proofs above supply the general admissibility and persistence arguments independently of those examples.

title: Independent word/source audit of the universal first-slot cut
text: # Independent word/source audit of the universal first-slot cut 27 October 2026. Detailed examination of [the universal resonant-cut theorem](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md). The inverse-pair insertion is an actual source-preserving presentation change. On the established regular geometric critical branch its added crossings have a nonempty regular chart and preserve a nonzero normal block. This is not a claim about the contribution of the resonant node to the final selected finite sum. ## 1. The chosen meridian really moves left unchanged At the complete faithful discrete representation all positively oriented meridians are conjugate to J. If such a conjugate fixes infinity, its conjugating group element also fixes infinity, since J has only that fixed point. An upper triangular group word has diagonal ratio one: a ratio of absolute value different from one contracts conjugates of J toward the identity; an infinite-order unit ratio gives nontrivial such commutators approaching identity; a nontrivial finite-order ratio gives projective torsion. These contradict discreteness/torsion-freeness. Hence that conjugator commutes with J and the meridian is exactly J, not a scaled translation. The first nonupper initial meridian U therefore has only J's before it. Negative Hurwitz moves (J,U) to (U,UJU inverse), so U passes left UNCHANGED at every step. The already crossed strands behind it do not change the prefixes before its next move. This proves the stated finite action word and V=I at the FIRST physical slot. The sign sigma=-1 is the first PREFIX index, while the physical slot for the endpoint half-character is ell=0. These are distinct index conventions with the correctly stated different values. These meridians describe the q-to-one geometric critical representation. They are not the identity Frobenius-central meridians at the actual fixed-root augmentation. No center-deformation identification is needed or implied by this presentation change. ## 2. The exact finite tensor and source are unchanged In action order insert the chosen braid P followed by P inverse before the old word. In matrix order the closed operator is R_old R_P inverse R_P=R_old. Opening the new edge gives the literal coupon tensor ptr[R_old R_P inverse E_bd^(0) R_P]. Summing E_bb restores that exact identity. This leaves the first input/output source and all original pivotal caps in their original places. There is no new pivot, color, trace normalization or source vector. The writhe and strand number are unchanged. The full twist, half-Cartan scalar lines and d_N(M) must be kept in both R_P and its inverse; their common factors cancel as a matrix identity, not as separately evaluated numerical norm values. The specified whole finite inverse exists on the auxiliary q/M lift as well, so the same presentation identity preserves its normal jets. Topological invariance of an unrelated off-root lift is unnecessary. The internal cut is at ell=0. The exact half-character q^(-ell nu) is therefore one, while the actual longitude insertion, gamma_N and complete peripheral ratio still remain. In particular opening BETWEEN inverse matrices prevents canceling their inserted path weights before the second edge is reclosed. The new partial array is a real changed partial family with the same final state. ## 3. Admissibility is verified on the actual coefficient atoms Write U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), c nonzero, and t=r+beta s. At the step with h left J's put \[ a_h=1+hs,\qquad b_h=a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). \] The four physical positions and negative transfer follow by the actual triangular prefix reconstruction, yielding exactly the five atoms in the main theorem. Their differences from one are controlled by the displayed finite list of factors. In particular \[ C-1=-c(1-t)^2/(b_{h+1}a_h),\quad b_{h+1}-b_h=s+c(1-t), \] \[ b_h-a_h=(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). \] All are nonzero rational functions on the two-dimensional framing torsor; for example b_h has nonzero quadratic r coefficient -c/s. Their finite product is nonzero in its function field. The common regular open therefore is nonempty and intersects the old regular geometric framing open. Inverse positive atoms are permutations/ inversions of the same regular atoms, so they introduce no new identical-zero condition. This is stronger than just assuming that an arbitrary Reidemeister-II insertion has a regular shape chart. The first/second physical position pair can fail at its ordinary projection caustic. This does not invalidate the Fourier block: on this regular chart p=1-1/t has p_r=1/t squared, so the pair (A_cut,p) is etale. The bordered-Hessian theorem needs that pair, not an everywhere invertible old two-position projection. ## 4. The inverse insertion is a genuine Morse stabilization The actual crossing generating phase has a UNIT mixed Hessian on the regular atom chart, by the previously proved generating-family calculation. Fix its conserved total position and denote that phase by F(y,q), with y the intermediate first output and q the input. The inverse phase is -F(y,q+delta), with its actual inverse marks; any recorded base phase is retained. The surrounding old network has its ordinary open extension S_open(z,delta), with S_open(z,0)=S_old(z). Thus the enlarged local phase is \[ F(y,q)-F(y,q+\delta)+S_{open}(z,\delta). \tag{1} \] At delta=0 the y equation is automatic. The delta equation fixes y uniquely by the old momentum because F_yq is a unit. Its (y,delta) Hessian is \[ \begin{pmatrix}0&-F_{yq}\\-F_{yq}&*\end{pmatrix}, \qquad\det=-F_{yq}^2\ne0. \tag{2} \] The reduced critical phase is precisely S_old. Schur elimination therefore makes the enlarged Hessian congruent to its old Hessian plus (2). The original two-dimensional framing kernel is unchanged; it is not a newly assumed Gaussian complement. The intermediate position and net displacement are integer coordinates with determinant plus or minus one in the two added transfers, so this stabilization does not introduce a lattice factor or fractional cover. For a longer P the inverse pairs cancel successively from the middle. The common regular chart from Section 3 allows this induction. Equivalently the exact canonical graph followed by its inverse eliminates uniquely over local Artin rings. The critical scheme remains the original framed representation germ. This proves the Morse--Bott and nonzero normal-block assertion in the main theorem. It does not assert equality of every formal coefficient in arbitrary Gaussian gauges. All inverse flattenings, density/base lines and fixed phases must still be transported. The positive statement is on the existing REGULAR geometric branch. It does not manufacture a regular branch for an arbitrary originally degenerate diagram or for unrelated representation components. ## 5. Universal pole and its precise source limitation The raw actual first-slot conjugation gives p=1-1/(r+beta s), r=1/(1-p)-beta s, and \[ \Omega_{cut}=-\frac p{s(1-p)^2} d\log A_{cut}\wedge d\log p. \] The orientation agrees directly with Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/ [s(1+s)]. The pole is exactly p=1, not a rescaling chosen after evaluating the state. The finite regular-node sum equals (N squared minus one)/(12s), with the main theorem's sign. This normalization places the escaping point at EVERY level's pointed Fourier node. It does not remove the resonance. The actual finite tensor is regular there, whereas the principal Gaussian density is not. Its full source, the nonuniform boundary layer and all higher shape-chart exclusions are still required. The exact presentation change and persistent nonzero partial block do not prove that this block survives the final selected source. ## Appendix: a checked first-slot meridian germ, with a split density pole This appendix does not extend the main complete Gaussian/source theorem to generic M. It computes the raw physical momentum and the explicitly defined invariant form in [the regular-centralizer chart](regular_meridian_centralizer.md), Section 2. Its normalization is A_cut=M/(M+s), Delta=s+(M-M inverse)r and Omega=-dr wedge ds/[Delta(M+s)]. The actual balanced symbol in the marked braid note has x=-M, e=(k-M inverse)p and physical mu=-G. Hence at the first slot p=-(F_M inverse U F_M)_12/(k-M inverse); its minus sign is fixed, not inferred by continuity. Let kappa=M-M inverse and \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}M-c\beta&\kappa\beta-c\beta^2\\ c&M^{-1}+c\beta\end{pmatrix},\quad F_M=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-\kappa-s\end{pmatrix}. \] Then D=U-M inverse I has rank one. Direct matrix calculation gives \[ p=1-\frac{1-\kappa\beta}{r+\beta s},\qquad r=\frac{1-\kappa\beta}{1-p}-\beta s, \tag{3} \] on the regular chart, and for THAT invariant form \[ \Omega=-\frac p{(1-p)[s(1-p)+\kappa]} d\log A_{cut}\wedge d\log p. \tag{4} \] The momentum Möbius pole stays p=1, but the density has two simple poles, p=1 and p=1+kappa/s. They coalesce to the main theorem's double pole at M=1. Thus even this special first-slot calculation does not justify retaining a generic single-double- pole filter. An additional Gaussian-density/source comparison, if needed away from completeness, has not been supplied by (3)-(4). [The exact symbolic check](../experiments/audit_first_slot_meridian_germ.py) and [its output](../experiments/first_slot_meridian_germ_results.json) verify the raw conjugated momentum, complete bubble atoms and the density's full meridian dependence. The root main theorem's actual R/source and Hessian tests are linked from that theorem.

title: Exact complete localization of the original first-slot Fourier source
text: # Exact complete localization of the original first-slot Fourier source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. At an actual root, the first-slot cut in the [universal resonant presentation](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) has the exact original finite Fourier array J_(a,j)(1)=P_N(1) delta_(j,0) (1) for EVERY physical first input a. This includes the original all-ones output row, the original pivotal caps, twists and full peripheral dimension line. No division by P_N and no nonvanishing assertion are used. The result is a consequence of the actual Hopf rows, rather than an approximation by the geometric principal density. In fact the entire channel obeys L(X_j)=P_N X_j at completeness, as proved below; this is stronger than the selected scalar rows. Consequently the regular Fourier labels j!=0 have zero selected finite value at completeness. A nonzero local geometric formal block at those labels does not establish that it contributes to the original period. The resonant value P_N remains to be evaluated. In particular, (1) supplies neither its volume exponent nor a new scalar formula independent of the original word. ## 1. The actual channel and its source Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and retain the original meridian M. In the balanced head put B=diag(Q^a), K=x B^-1, x=-M/q, F_(a+1,a)=1-Q^(a+1), Ecal_(a-1,a)=M Q^(-a)-M^-1. (2) All missing entries are zero. Ecal is the fixed scalar multiple of E used in the actual balanced crossing conventions. Its coproduct and antipode have the same form as those of E. Cut a braid at its FIRST physical slot between two actual words A and Bword; both words intertwine the true iterated coproduct. The original second-cut coupon X defines the actual linear channel L(X)=d_N theta^(-w) ptr_g[ A (X tensor I) Bword ]. (3) Here ptr_g closes every strand except the original first open strand using g=K^(1-N), in the original order. The displayed external factors may instead be recorded in their original external line; the SAME convention must then be used for P_N and J throughout. The universal presentation inserts a word P and its literal inverse, so A Bword is exactly the original braid operator. It changes none of the factors in (3), including their actual rational-map/lattice specializations. The [root scalar-closure proof](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md), Section 1, gives L(I)=P_N(M) I. (4) There is an elementary version of that proof: the cut commutes with K and F; the distinct K eigenvalues make it diagonal, and its F commutator makes successive diagonal entries equal because 1-Q^a!=0 for 0<a<N. Thus no generic irreducibility or division by an unknown scalar period is needed. With the full line in (3), P_N=d_N F_N; with that line recorded externally, P_N=F_N. At M=1, F_N(1) is the fixed original Kashaev invariant. Set ell=1^t, and use the actual root Fourier projectors X_j=V^-1 E_(j,j) V, (X_j)_(b,d)=Q^[j(d-b)]/N, V_(j,b)=Q^(jb), 0<=j<N. The original one-index Fourier source is EXACTLY Y_j=L(X_j), J_(a,j)=ell Y_j e_a. (5) This follows by expanding the second-wire conjugation and retaining the all-ones first output row. Since sum_j X_j=I, (4) gives sum_j J_(a,j)=P_N (6) for every a. The 1/N in X_j is the Fourier inverse. There is no additional exterior factor in (6). ## 2. Why the first-slot channel intertwines the actual Hopf adjoint For the actual coproduct convention, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^-1 tensor F, S(Ecal)=-Ecal K^-1, S(F)=-K F. The induced action on an endomorphism is ad_K X=K X K^-1, ad_Ecal X=(Ecal X-X Ecal)K^-1, ad_F X=F X-K^-1 X K F. (7) For the FIRST tensor factor, direct substitution in the coproduct gives ad_h^(total)(X tensor I)=(ad_h X) tensor I, h=K,Ecal,F. (8) For example the Ecal commutator is [Ecal,X] tensor K_other, which becomes [Ecal,X]K^-1 tensor I after multiplying by the total K^-1. For F the extra term cancels as K^-1 X tensor F_other -K^-1 X K K^-1 tensor F_other=0. This verifies the position requirement. An arbitrary later-slot embedding is not substituted for (8). Multiplication on either side by an actual braid intertwiner commutes with (7). The original pivotal partial trace is also an adjoint intertwiner. One can check the latter directly, without assuming scalarity: on the closed tensor factor write K_o,E_o,F_o for its total generators and g_o for its original product pivot. At the actual root, [g_o,K_o]=0, g_o E_o g_o^-1=K_o E_o K_o^-1, g_o F_o g_o^-1=K_o F_o K_o^-1. Weighted partial-trace cyclicity cancels the closed-factor terms in (7), using precisely these identities. The remaining terms are ad_h of the partial trace. Equivalently these are the direct evaluation/coevaluation identities checked in [the closed-braid construction](closed_braid_period_line.md), Section 2. Scalars d_N and theta^(-w) commute with this calculation. Consequently L(ad_h X)=ad_h L(X), h=K,Ecal,F. (9) Equations (8)--(9) apply to the literal cut of any word of the specified equal original color, not only to an inverse-pair example. The inverse-pair construction is what simultaneously provides this first slot and the desired noncommuting geometric meridian while preserving the original selected period. Everything so far is an ACTUAL root identity. It makes no off-root q scalarity or compressed auxiliary Hopf assertion. ## 3. Complete cyclic generator formulas Let S be the cyclic raising shift S e_a=e_(a+1 mod N). The Fourier projectors satisfy S X_j=X_j S=eta_j X_j, eta_j=Q^j, B^-1 X_j B=X_(j+1). (10) All Fourier labels in this note are cyclic. At M=1 the missing physical endpoints in (2) have zero coefficients. Therefore, as exact finite matrices, F=S(I-QB), Ecal=S^-1(B^-1-I). (11) There is no replacement of a nonzero endpoint by a cyclic arrow. Substituting (10)--(11) into (7) gives ad_K X_j=X_(j+1), ad_Ecal X_j=x^-1 eta_j^-1 (Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j), ad_F X_j=eta_j X_j-eta_(j-1) X_(j-1). (12) For instance [S^-1(B^-1-I),X_j]B has its two X_j B terms cancel; the remaining terms are eta_j^-1(Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j). For the F row, the two S B terms cancel by B X_j=X_(j-1)B. These prove all formulas in (12) within the original finite balanced head. The first row of (12) and (9) imply Y_(j+1)=B^-1 Y_j B. (13) In particular their diagonal entries are independent of j. Summing (13) and using (4) proves (Y_j)_(a,a)=P_N/N. This latter identity also holds for generic M and will retain the full scalar period in the endpoint equation below. ## 4. Highest-input localization, followed by all-input propagation First take the actual input a=0. Since Ecal e_0=0 and ell Ecal=ell(B^-1-I) at M=1, (13) gives ell (ad_Ecal Y_j)e_0 =x^-1[J_(0,j+1)-J_(0,j)]. Apply (9) to the Ecal row of (12) and compare the two expressions. The resulting exact scalar recurrence is (eta_j-Q^-1)J_(0,j+1) =(eta_j-1)J_(0,j). (14) At j=0 its right side is zero and 1-Q^-1 is a unit, so J_(0,1)=0. For j=1,...,N-2 the coefficient eta_j-Q^-1 is nonzero, and induction gives J_(0,j)=0 for every j!=0. Equation (6) then gives J_(0,0)=P_N. This proof never divides by P_N and remains valid when the original invariant vanishes. For every physical input a, use (13), the F row of (12), and F e_a=(1-Q^(a+1))e_(a+1). They give (1-eta_j)J_(a,j) =(Q^(a+1)-Q^-1 eta_j)J_(a,j-1) +(1-Q^(a+1))J_(a+1,j-1). (15) At a=N-1 the last term is zero; it is not an added cyclic physical-input column. The candidate P_N delta_(j,0), constant in a, satisfies (15). Subtract it and call the difference D. The result just proved is D_(0,j)=0 for all j. If D_(a,j)=0 for all j and a<N-1, (15) forces (1-Q^(a+1))D_(a+1,j-1)=0. Every coefficient is a unit. Induction in a proves D=0, which is the stated theorem (1). The proof also works at M=-1, since then Ecal=-S^-1(B^-1-I); its extra common sign cancels in (14). There is a useful full-matrix corollary. Define the Fourier rows r_k=ell B^-k, which form a basis of the dual head. By (13), r_k Y_j=ell Y_(j+k) B^-k =P_N delta_(j+k,0) r_k. Directly from (5), r_k X_j=delta_(j+k,0)r_k as well. Hence L(X_j)=P_N X_j, (19) L(h(S))=P_N h(S) for EVERY element h(S) of the finite cyclic-shift algebra. This identity also uses no nonzero-period assumption. It concerns this commutative subalgebra of coupons, not the full endomorphism algebra or the generic-M channel. ## 5. The meridian endpoint and word data are retained off completeness Keep the actual root Q but allow M to vary. Put kappa=M-M^-1, W=E_(N-1,0). The exact finite Ecal matrix is Ecal=S^-1(MB^-1-M^-1 I)-kappa W. (16) The last term subtracts the cyclic arrow at the original physical endpoint. It is nonzero off completeness. The F row, K row, (13), (15) and (Y_j)_(0,0)=P_N/N remain exact. Define the ACTUAL inserted endpoint source R_j=ell L([W,X_j]B)e_0. (17) Repeating the preceding Ecal calculation with (16) gives M(eta_j-Q^-1)J_(0,j+1) +(M-M^-1 eta_j)J_(0,j) =kappa eta_j(P_N/N-R_j). (18) Indeed the cyclic part of ad_Ecal X_j is x^-1 M eta_j^-1(Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j), while its missing-arrow correction is -x^-1 kappa[W,X_j]B. On the output side, ell Ecal=ell(MB^-1-M^-1 I)-kappa e_0^t. This proves (18), including both its original scalar source and its actual inserted endpoint source. Deleting (17) before differentiation would alter the original meridian normal equation. There is no universal generic-M profile determined by P_N alone for all original words. The exact finite-field audit includes the same first-slot inverse-pair cut on the one-positive-crossing unknot and positive trefoil. At N=3, M=3 over F_157, their highest rows divided by their respective NONZERO full periods are unknot: [117,62,136], trefoil: [52,122,141]. Both sums are one modulo 157. The different rows disprove such a universal rational identity across these original words; this is not a separate claim about all hyperbolic knots or about a particular complex asymptotic boundary profile. It records why the whole word/source in (17)--(18) cannot be replaced by a knot-independent cap simply because (1) holds on the complete fiber. ## 6. Critical-path consequence and verification On this actual source-preserving cut ALL of the selected complete finite period is at j=0. Thus the nonzero geometric normal block on a regular p!=1 chart is not yet a nonzero image of the final selected scalar source: the complete finite rows at j!=0 vanish exactly. Sampling their nonzero geometric principal coefficient and summing it is not an evaluation of the actual finite array. The remaining issue is a source-compatible geometric transform of the resonant row and its whole endpoint/peripheral completion, not proving that an unspecified regular Fourier row survives. Its regulator exponent, subexponential coefficient and global norm estimate are still unproved in general. The current theorem does not close C, D or E of [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md). The [exact original-matrix audit](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_fourier_source.py) checks every matrix unit against all three Hopf-adjoint generators, the generic-M endpoint equation (18), all-input equation (15), complete delta localization and full matrix projector identity (19). Its [saved results](../experiments/universal_resonant_fourier_source_results.json) record 36 signed-word/cut cases at N=2,...,6, comprising 598 matrix input units and three generator checks per unit. The full d_N, original pivots and twists are retained in every case. These finite tests support the direct proof above; they are not used as a proof for untested knots or as an asymptotic estimate.

title: Pointed tetrahedral transport of the Verma root period
text: # Pointed tetrahedral transport of the Verma root period Research note, 26 October 2026. This factors the actual untruncated Verma crossing into four compact quantum dilogarithms, derives a scalar-one algebraic tetrahedral pentagon, and proves that finite formal pentagon rewrites preserve its selected root period after compression to the Verma lattice. It retains the boundary frame, its entire norm character and its poles. Individual compact products are not evaluated at roots of unity. The resulting root period is still the one independently identified in the [Frobenius Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md): V_N(M)=F_N(M)/Delta_K(M^(2N)). This supplies local operator moves for the proposed triangulation comparison. It does not establish that an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation carries the required colored network and pointing, or identify its selected quantum period with the Bloch regulator. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. A pointed compact pentagon For generic Q put P_Q(t)=(t;Q)_infinity =sum_(n>=0)(-1)^n Q^(n(n-1)/2)t^n/(Q;Q)_n. Use it as a formal series. Its constant term is one and P_Q(Qt)=P_Q(t)/(1-t). If AB=QBA, Gaussian expansion gives P_Q(A+B)=P_Q(A)P_Q(B). (1.1) For XY=QYX, conjugation by P_Q(Y) sends X to X(1-Q^(-1)Y)=X-YX. The two summands X and -YX satisfy the commutation required in (1.1). Consequently P_Q(Y)P_Q(X)=P_Q(X)P_Q(-YX)P_Q(Y). (1.2) This proves the pentagon directly from the series and its shift equation. It is an equality with scalar one, fixed by the constant term. The ordered middle argument -YX, including its Q phase in an X-before-Y monomial basis, is part of the identity. To make completions unambiguous, attach formal variables u,v to X,Y. The middle argument has tag uv. Every coefficient is finite in the (u,v)-adic completion of the quantum Laurent algebra. Inverses of P are defined in the same completion. No analytic branch or root-level value of an individual infinite product is assumed. ## 2. A tetrahedral operator, including its shear and phase On Laurent monomials in z_1,...,z_b let Z_i multiply by z_i and S_i f(z)=f(...,Qz_i,...). Put x_i=Z_i, y_i=S_i^(-1), so x_i y_i=Q y_i x_i. Define a monomial shear (C_ij f)(z)=f(...,z_i z_j,...,z_j,...), a_ij=-Q x_i x_j^(-1)y_j, T_ij(t)=C_ij P_Q(t a_ij)^(-1). (2.1) The shear conjugates x_i to x_i x_j and y_j to y_i^(-1)y_j. Its exact monomial action gives C_12 C_13 C_23=C_23 C_12. Move the dilogarithms past these shears in the two products below. On the left their arguments become A,-AC,C; on the right they become C,A, where A=u a_12, C=v a_23, CA=QAC. Indeed the transformed a_13 has coefficient -Q uv, whereas AC has coefficient Q uv. Inverting (1.2) therefore proves T_12(u)T_13(uv)T_23(v)=T_23(v)T_12(u). (2.2) This is the algebraic three-to-two tetrahedral operator identity with its exact shear and scalar. It is not a claim that the uncolored geometric triangulation theorem supplies the extra tensor data needed to apply it globally. For a direct coefficient check, T_ij(t) sends a Laurent monomial of exponent vector n to vectors with n'_i=n_i+m, n'_j=n_j+n_i, coefficient=t^m(-1)^m Q^(m(m+1)/2-m n_j)/(Q;Q)_m, summed over m>=0. Tagged coefficients are finite. Omitting the Q in a_ij already violates (2.2); it is not a removable scalar normalization. ## 3. Four factors for the actual Verma crossing Use the same infinite Verma basis v_a=z^a, x=q^alpha, Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1). On one factor put S v_a=Q^a v_a and Z v_a=v_(a+1). Then K=xS^(-1), F=Z, rho^2 E=qx Z^(-1)(1-S^(-1))(1-Q^(-1)x^(-2)S). The right side kills v_0 and preserves the polynomial Verma module. Let G=P_Q(x^(-2)S), initially as a tagged formal diagonal operator. The functional equation gives rho^2 E=qx G[Z^(-1)(1-S^(-1))]G^(-1). (3.1) For a pair set A=Z_1^(-1)Z_2, S=S_1 and W=x^(-2)S, U=Qx A, V=-Qx A S^(-1). Here AS=QSA and VU=QUV. The formal universal uncheck R, with its common Cartan scalar removed, is D times its nilpotent series, where D(v_a tensor v_b)=x^(-a-b)Q^(ab)v_a tensor v_b. Using the independently derived R coefficients and (3.1) gives R^0=D P_Q(W)P_Q(V)P_Q(U)P_Q(W)^(-1). (3.2) Indeed the middle product is P_Q(U+V), with U+V=Qx A(1-S^(-1)); its action terminates on each polynomial input before the diagonal conjugation. Equation (3.2) is therefore the actual Verma operator, not a replacement cyclic crossing. Two applications of (1.2) remove the diagonal G: P_Q(W)P_Q(V)=P_Q(V)P_Q(-WV)P_Q(W), P_Q(W)P_Q(U)P_Q(W)^(-1)=P_Q(U)P_Q(-WU). Since -WV=x^(-1)A and -WU=-x^(-1)AS, the four-monomial formula is R^0=D P_Q(-Qx AS^(-1))P_Q(x^(-1)A) P_Q(Qx A)P_Q(-x^(-1)AS). (3.3) The checked crossing is the usual flip times (3.3). Its inverse is the inverse word, with the same external conventions. All Cartan, flip and zero-framing factors remain in the period. ## 4. Compression fixes the boundary lattice The individual factors in (3.3) can send a polynomial input to infinitely many negative powers of z_1. The complete product has an elementary cancellation. Introduce a color tag h and a transfer tag d in (3.2): replace W by hW and U,V by dU,dV. In (3.3) this tags the second and fourth arguments by hd, and the first and third by d. After grouping the whole product, the coefficient sending (a,b) to (a-n,b+n), before the checked flip, is exactly d^n x^(-a-b+n)Q^((a-n)b){a choose n}_Q (h x^(-2)Q^(a-n);Q)_n, 0<=n<=a, (4.1) and is zero for n>a. Here the Gaussian coefficient is a polynomial, not a divided-factorial value at a root. For a uniform proof, first expand P_Q(d(U+V)). Its n-th power acts by the factor product_(j=0)^(n-1)(1-Q^(-a+j)), which vanishes for n>a. Combining this factor with the Euler coefficient gives d^n x^n Q^(-n(a-n)){a choose n}_Q. The diagonal ratio from G is (h x^(-2)Q^(a-n);Q)_n. Applying D at the output gives (4.1). This is also the direct untruncated crossing coefficient of the preceding note at h=d=1. Every fixed homogeneous total-index sector of the combined operator is thus a finite matrix of Laurent polynomials in q,x and polynomials in h,d. The inverse has the same property, by the terminating inverse R series. Its determinant is the invertible Cartan monomial times that of a unipotent triangular matrix. The combined operator preserves the original polynomial Verma lattice. Neither this fact nor its root specialization is obtained by specializing its four compact factors separately. ## 5. A precise pointed transport theorem Start with the Verma braid operator and a fixed cut, pivot and grading insertion as in the [graded trace construction](frobenius_verma_period.md). Expand its crossings and inverses by (3.2) or (3.3), with independent auxiliary tags for the occurrences. Permit a finite sequence of the formal pentagon identities, their inverse identities, exact monomial/shear identities and cancellations of adjacent inverse factors, with their argument tags and external leg identifications transported throughout. These are equalities of the external operator, before taking its trace. Then compress the entire rewritten operator to the original Verma lattice, set its tags to one, and specialize q=q_N. The resulting graded cut period and its rational continuation at tau=1 are exactly the original ones: rewritten V_beta(q_N,x;tau)=V_beta(q_N,x;tau), rewritten V_N(M)=F_N(M)/Delta_K(M^(2N)). (5.1) Here is the proof, including the otherwise missing specialization step. All factors have positive auxiliary tag degree, so every rewrite is defined in a common formal completion of the Laurent module. The initial complete operator has the polynomial matrix entries of Section 4. Formal operator equality forces the rewritten complete entries to equal those polynomials, including the vanishing of every forbidden negative-index transfer. Thus setting the tags to one and specializing q use a known regular polynomial entry. No root limit of an individual factor is used. Each coefficient of the cut grading tau sums only finitely many input and intermediate indices after this compression. The coefficientwise period identity follows. At a root the initial period has the rational formula proved in the preceding note. Two rational functions with the same series at tau=0 are equal; hence their entire rational continuations, poles and regular whole specializations agree. This proves (5.1), including the Kashaev fiber and its marked normal coordinate. Multiplying by the full d_N(M) retains the full ADO normalization as before. This theorem transports the actual selected period under the specified formal operator moves. It does not assert that every Pachner or face-permutation operation on arbitrary ideal triangulations has already been assigned such an operator identity. For such an application the coloring, polarization, turns and boundary identifications must be constructed and checked. ## 6. The relative norm torsor at the Kashaev boundary Normalize the diagonal operator in (3.2) on v_0. Its finite ratio is g_a=P_Q(x^(-2)Q^a)/P_Q(x^(-2)) =1/(x^(-2);Q)_a, g_0=1. The finite expression specifies its meromorphic root frame even though the two infinite products individually have no such value. For q=q_N and U=M^(2N)=x^(2N), g_(a+1)/g_a=(1-x^(-2)Q^a)^(-1), g_(NA+r)=(1-U^(-1))^(-A)g_r, 0<=r<N. (6.1) This is an explicit rank-one cyclic norm character Norm((1-x^(-2)Q^a)^(-1))=(1-U^(-1))^(-1). It is invertible away from its divisor; at U=1 its meromorphic filtered lattice, with pole order A on the A-th polynomial block, must be retained. Every finite total-index filtration has finite pole order. At the actual Kashaev color x=q_N^(N-1), x^(-2)=Q, so the first N frame entries are g_r=1/(Q;Q)_r, 0<=r<N. They are exactly the factorial frame of the already fixed [actual cut boundary](marked_braid_holonomy.md). The next entry has a pole. The combined crossing is regular nevertheless by (4.1), and the complete rational trace is regular there because Delta_K(1)=1. Evaluating this diagonal frame separately at its pole would lose the prescribed boundary data. The middle arguments in pentagons also retain nontrivial central norms. If XY=QYX and Q has order N, direct ordered multiplication gives (-YX)^N=-X^N Y^N (6.2) at every parity. Thus its binomial norm factor is 1+X^N Y^N, which can specialize to a numerical multiplier. In the tetrahedral operator (2.1), a_ij^N=-Z_i^N Z_j^(-N)S_j^(-N), with the same sign. Such factors must be carried as functions before a whole boundary specialization. The strict formal identities above do not justify discarding them or repair a different numerical state model by fiat. The subsequent [factorial source-torsor calculation](factorial_source_torsor.md) identifies this frame directly with the literature cyclic primitive. For h=Q^(-1)x^(-2), write p_a(h)=(Qh;Q)_a=nu^a phi_a(h), nu^N=1-U^(-1). Then the exact Verma frame is g_a=1/p_a(h)=nu^(-a) phi_a(h)^(-1). Its block pole character in (6.1) is the N-step transport of this same singular cyclic frame. The new two-direction affine extension and cut-root adapters retain its source channel and the full endpoint factors. They do not supply the remaining global colored/polarized network or its selected regulator norm.
